0:
A notice has been hung on the wall.
Vig the Dwarven smelter stands here, overseeing his store.

This dim tunnel is unfinished and unadorned, the walls still scarred by the picks of Dwarven miners. Facing the entrance is a huge wooden worktable, made of a single huge slab of oak, which also serves as a counter. Behind it, in the distance, bright red and yellow coals glow fiercely under the great smelting pots. Wood smoke laced with the smells of melted rock and hot metal wafts over the counter whenever a current of air passes this way.
1: The lowest level of the city begins here, where the houses and parks of the upper areas give way to business and government. The walls rise up straight and proud to the ceiling, well above your head, which is covered with an intricate pattern of stonework. The lines weave in and out and over and under each other, leading your eyes down the hall until the tracery vanishes out of sight. The main passage to the upper levels rises upwards and westwards, while a short corridor going straight west leads to a doorway from which a warm blast of acrid fumes occasionally issues.
2:
A little note is nailed to the wall.
A dwarven potter is here sculpting clay.

Here all sorts of pottery is created. On the east wall sit several storage sheds containing various types of clays. In the centre sit two potter's wheels for forming plates and bowls and other useful objects. Finally the items are fired in the kilns along the west wall. To the south is arrayed a selection of toys made from wood and clay.
3:
A dwarf is here processing wool.
A dwarf is here processing wool.

Bales of wool are brought here from the upper levels where they are bought and sold. A host of dwarves works diligently to produce cloth for their people. First the wool is sifted through and all rocks and twigs removed. Next the shaggy clumps are loaded onto the distaff, and spun into long strands of yarn, spindles of which are brought to the back of the room.
4:
An apprentice scurries about the room.
A long-bearded weaver is busily making cloth.

This is a small, cramped chamber brightly lit by several wall-lanterns. The room is filled by several looms at each of which sits a nimble dwarf, weaving the yarn which is periodically brought from the front of the room. There is a continuous clickety-clattering as the wooden looms are opened and closed.
5:
A dwarven child wanders around.
A dwarven female is here walking around.

After a long but gentle decline from the west, the corridor here levels out. This is the commercial centre of the city, and on either side you see doorways to offices and workshops. The walls are lined with ornamental columns, and between each two a simple scene is carved into the wall.
6:
A female dwarf is here cutting a piece of leather.
A sergeant of the dwarven guard looks around alertly.
A dwarven cityguard is patrolling the streets.
A dwarven cityguard is patrolling the streets.

The smooth scent of leather fills the air. This room delves back far from the main passage. In the back are vats of soaking hides, being prepared for tanning. Nearby is a series of tanning vats slowly turning the hides into leather. There are also a few Dwarves pounding various oils into fresh hides, producing a soft chamois leather. Finally the leather is cut and shaped, sewn and decorated, at tables arrayed across the front of the chamber. All types of leather goods can be seen in various stages of production.
7:
A brass lantern has been set on the ground.
The dwarven engineer is here reading a report with a calculating look.

Here are the offices of those who direct the Dwarves' great work. This is a long, somewhat narrow room, filled with orderly desks, and more paper than tools. The light is bright and diffuse. All the tunnelling and digging and carving is overseen from this room. The design of the caves is a careful match of the needs of the growing population of the caves with the natural desires of the stone in which they live.
8: All around you busy Dwarves do the work which keep this city alive. You are completely surrounded by bustling activity, and the Dwarves pay your sloth no mind. The passage continues east and west as far as you can see, small cones of light dwindling off into the distance.
9:
An iron pick has been dropped here.
A coil of rope is lying here.
A dented pail has been carelessly left here.
A dwarven cityguard is patrolling the streets.
A dwarven cityguard is patrolling the streets.

Here is where the miners of the area leave and pick up various mining tools. Wooden ore buckets and picks of all sizes adorn both the walls and the floor. It seems messy, yet the workers you see coming and going seem to know exactly where everything is.
10: This dim tunnel leads deeper down into the mountain. Unlike those to the north it is unfinished and unadorned, the wall still scarred by the picks of Dwarven miners, whose activity you can faintly hear to the south.
11: The stolid hall stretches off before you. To the east the decor changes; the patterns of stonework end, and a wide variety of axes hang upon the walls. Around you are bearded Dwarves of every description and station. Nobility in their finery walk quickly east to the King's court, while labourers walk the same way for a pint of mead in the Khazad Kheled-Baruk. On one side of you a cart is pulled, stacked high with cloths and thread in a thousand colours, and behind that comes a mule loaded with pig iron. Anything your hands or stomach or head needs must surely be close at hand.
12: A cobbler is here mending a pair of sandals.

Here a master cobbler and several journeymen produce most of the footwear for the city. There is a variety of materials spread about the workbenches, but leather and cotton seem to predominate. The work here is quiet and relaxed, and a joking banter passes back and forth amongst the cobblers. You see that several guilds have set up their shop here. In the immediate area you notice that the woolworkers and a tailor have set up a table.
13: A dwarf stands here crafting children's toys.

This room is filled with a wide variety of toys, all beautiful and some obviously magical. You see puppets and soft cloth dolls, metal soldiers, wooden animals, hobbyhorses, small clay ducks on wheels, miniature boats, intricately carved tops, and all sorts of puzzles and tricks. A few Dwarves sit over cluttered workbenches, adding to the stocks.
14: The tunnel here is only dimly lit by lanterns along the wall. This seems to be a recent excavation, and is as yet unused. To the south you hear the sound of picks striking stone wafting up from a downward-sloping tunnel.
15:
A small bat is standing here.
A small rat runs about, oblivious to your presence.
From the pick marks on the walls around you, this passage was purposefully delved, but it seems to have been abandoned. Several dark lanterns hang from the walls.
17:
There is a decorative sign on the wall here.
Dori the armourer is here pounding on iron.

The alcove at first looks small and cluttered but as your eyes scan the cavern slowly you realise how deceptive it looks. The room is huge, but most of it is covered by assorted furnaces, forges, iron rods, and the like. Suits of completed armour line the far wall while bits and pieces seem to fly around the floor. The workers pay you no mind as they go about their work, banging and hammering, chipping and moulding.
18: All along this passage hang axes. From floor to ceiling, they hang majestically, testament to times of war and glory long since passed from these proud people. The axes are of all shapes and sizes, lengths and widths. You can spot legendary axes, from tales told of heroes long gone, their only link back to the living world. The axes line the way, separated only by white stones, carved bowl-like into the wall, emitting a faint glow like muted candle-light into the hall. Jutting out from the stone walls, two signs appear, one on the north wall and one on the south, their lettering clear and dark in the stone.
19:
A metal sign hangs by the door.
Ginnar the weaponsmith stands here pounding out a sword.

This cavern is filled with instruments of death. Swords and axes line the wall, maces and morningstars hang from bars running from the ceiling, while other weapons of all sorts simply lie in heaps along the floor. The heat of the room is oppressive, but the Dwarven smiths seem to pay it no mind. In fact, your presence is either noted with a scowl or not noted at all. The smiths simply go about their work, paying you no attention at all. A hastily scrawled note is attached to the counter.
20:
A large bulletin board, entitled "Free Peoples' Chronicles", is mounted here.
A circular stone well has been built here.
A large stone fireplace with a roaring fire warms the room.
A huge clock is standing here.
A dwarven innkeeper stands ready to rent a room to a fellow dwarf.

Though from the outside this alcove looks simple, from within it grows to a cavernous size, growing tall into the rock and furnished with many walkways and terraces. Here, dwarves who have travelled from abroad may claim lodging for the night, resting their backs on the gentle beds of the inn. The atmosphere is relaxed, as if the tension from without cannot penetrate its hallowed stone walls.
21:
A well-crafted white fountain is here, water pouring forth from it.
A traffic sign is here, giving directions.

All along this passage hang axes. From floor to ceiling, they hang majestically, testament to times of war and glory long since passed from these proud people. The axes are of all shapes and sizes, lengths and widths. You can spot legendary axes, from tales told of heroes long gone, their only link back to the living world. The axes line the way, separated only by white stones, carved bowl-like into the wall, emitting a faint glow like muted candle-light into the hall.
22: This giant natural cavern spreads out before you like the workplace of Aule. Stalactites hang down from the roof, bright gems glowing from their tips, projecting a kalidescopic light all around you, flickering and dancing on the walls. Giant stalagmites stand, carved masterfully into statues depicting Mahal in different poses. Many dwarves are here at all times, resting, standing or kneeling in prayer or reverence. An ornate altar stands here, dominating the centre of the hall with its presence.
23: A large bulletin board, entitled "News of Arda", is mounted here.

This small chamber slopes down into the mountain. Unlike the rest of the caverns it is only dimly lit here; some few smoky torches serve to cast a flickering light over the room. Sarcophagi line the floor. On the paths between them walk a few Dwarves with bowed heads. Here they remember their loved ones, who walk no more upon this earth, but sit with their fathers in the halls of waiting until Mahal calls to them again.
24:
A dwarven cityguard stands here looking scornfully at foreigners.
A dwarven cityguard stands here looking scornfully at foreigners.
A dwarven cityguard stands here looking scornfully at foreigners.
A sergeant of the dwarven guard looks around alertly.
An experienced dwarven captain stands here with an air of authority.
King Thorin II, Oakenshield, sits here on his throne (glowing).
Thurn, guide to Dwarvenhome, is standing here.

Here sits the Dwarven king, King Under the Mountain, upon his throne of black rock. His throne dominates the room, a large hall of black stone streaked with gold. Suits of armour, shining softly in the light, line the walls and regal carpets cover the floor. Many Dwarven courtiers move about, performing matters for the king, who sits here listless, his face thrust deep in thought.
25: A traffic sign is here, giving directions.

This giant natural cavern spreads out before you like the workplace of Aule. Stalactites hang down from the roof, bright gems glowing from their tips, projecting a kaleidoscopic light all around you, flickering and dancing on the walls. Giant stalagmites stand, carved masterfully into statues depicting Mahal in different poses. Many dwarves are here at all times, resting, standing or kneeling in prayer or reverence.
26: A large bulletin board, entitled "Board of the Free Peoples", is mounted here.

This small room is lined with shelves dug into the walls, and filled with cabinets, desks, and chests filled with all sorts of great tomes, old and yellowed, but still treasured for their store of knowledge. On every surface is some scroll or map, wall-hanging or book. Here the records of the Dwarves and their trials upon Arda are written and stored for future generations. Dwarves linger here for many an hour, simply sitting and pondering, absorbing the past as if to give them strength for the future. On a table sits a Khuzdul-Westron dictionary. On a poster on the wall is the Song of Durin. There is also a family tree of Durin's folk.
27:
A rusty pickaxe with a broken handle lies discarded here.
A dwarven cityguard is patrolling the streets.
A dwarven cityguard is patrolling the streets.

Light seems to shine from everywhere and nowhere here, illuminating the Dwarven cavern in an eerie glow. Statues line the way, a testimony to greatness gone, perhaps hinting at greatness to come. The walls are covered in tapestries of semi-precious stones, forming rock paintings of Dwarven lords and heros, their eyes shining rubies, looking at all those who pass beneath them. Their eyes seem almost living, their glint at once sad and accusing, cold and caring, as if the souls of the ancient Dwarves glimmered within them.
28: Light seems to shine from everywhere and nowhere here, illuminating the Dwarven cavern in an eerie glow. Statues line the way, a testimony to greatness gone, perhaps hinting at greatness to come. The walls are covered in tapestries of semi-precious stones, forming rock paintings of Dwarven lords and heros, their eyes shining rubies, looking at all those who pass beneath them. Their eyes seem almost living, their glint at once sad and accusing, cold and caring, as if the souls of the ancient Dwarves glimmered within them.
30: The great hall extends before you, an avenue lined by bright rubies, shining like subterranean roses in the light. The floor is smooth, polished by the wise and skilful hands of master Dwarven craftsmen. Carvings cover the walls, bas-reliefs of ages long since past, heros long dead, and glory long since faded from Durin's folk, remembered only in the scarlet glow of the rubies and the stonework of Dwarven artists. The grim faces of the Dwarves around seem to burn with determination. Perhaps the Hall of Rubies will ring again with the sounds of Dwarven triumph. To the south, a sign of black rock, lettered in bright ruby hangs above a lit alcove. From inside, the sounds of merriment can be heard.
31: The great hall extends before you, an avenue lined by bright rubies, shining like subterranean roses in the light. The floor is smooth, polished by the wise and skilful hands of master Dwarven craftsmen. Carvings cover the walls, bas-reliefs of ages long since past, heroes long dead, and glory long since faded from Durin's folk, remembered only in the scarlet glow of the rubies and the stonework of Dwarven artists. The grim faces of the Dwarves around seem to burn with determination. Perhaps the Hall of Rubies will ring again with the sounds of Dwarven triumph. To the south, the Hall of Dwarves can be seen, its sombre walls rising straight up into the ever-dusk recesses of the chamber.
32: The great hall continues before you, a dazzling crimson spectacle, lined by bright rubies, shining like subterranean roses in the light. The floor is smooth, polished by the wise and skilful hands of master Dwarven craftsmen. The grim faces of the Dwarves around seem to burn with determination. Perhaps the Hall of Rubies will ring again with the sounds of Dwarven triumph. All along this majestic path lie benches carved from dark stone where Dwarves sit and watch the world pass by the light of a thousand glittering eyes.
33: The great hall extends before you, an avenue lined by bright rubies, shining like subterranean roses in the light. The floor is smooth, polished by the wise and skilful hands of master Dwarven craftsmen. Perhaps the Hall of Rubies will ring again with the sounds of Dwarven triumph. Here the hall ends in a carved-out alcove with benches smoothed out of the hewn rock walls. By the light of the glittering gems, several Dwarves sit and read or just look around them in awe at the work of their forefathers.
34:
A mailbox stands here stuffed full of messages.
A big bottle is lying here.
A dwarven tavern-keeper tends bar.

The tavern is a high ceilinged room filled with the smoke of pipes and the laughter of Dwarves at ease. Oval tables, growing out of the stone like mushrooms, dot the floor, while a counter of pure marble marks the bar. Here, it seems, all cares are forgotten, and the Dwarves who sit around you seem only interested in a strong drink, a good meal, and the companionship of friends.
35: The vertical shaft embarks on a steep descent into the underground of the Blue Mountains. Broad ladders have been fastened into the rocky walls by thick iron eyebolts that grip around the legs. Far above, a wooden platform is barely visible in the dim light where the ladders seem to end. The sound of mining reaches up through the shaft echoing between the walls.
36: A large cavern hewn into the solid rock opens around a large shaft leading down into the mountain. A sturdy wooden fence encircles the shaft to prevent accidents. On the eastern side is an opening in the fence that leads onto a wooden platform leaning over the shaft. The platform is used to haul ore out of the mines with ropes; empty metal buckets used for this purpose have been stacked in the southern end of the cavern. An opening in the northern wall leads out of the mine area.
37:
A dwarven cityguard stands here looking scornfully at foreigners.
A dwarven cityguard stands here looking scornfully at foreigners.
A dwarven cityguard stands here looking scornfully at foreigners.
A dwarven surveyor is standing here.

Through great labour a dome-shaped cavern has been excavated in the mountain. The finely carved walls clearly show the remarkable skill given to the dwarves by Aule. The dwarven guards have set a guard-post here, outside the mines to the south. There is a table and four stools in the corner, a plank bed across the floor, and in the centre is placed a fair-sized hearth generously warming the cavern. To the south is a dark tunnel leading further into the mountain.
38: A great curved ceiling encloses a hall of remarkable workmanship. Runes and strange sigils decorate the flawless walls. Tall, wide pillars spun with glittering threads of metal stand at even intervals in two rows through the hall. Through rectangular openings in the rock above the hall flows a calm refreshing breeze carrying the cheerful sound of birds singing during the day. While the hall is richly ornamented, it is apparently not used for the purpose it was intended. At some time the southern wall was opened up, and that way now lies a dark tunnel peering right into the heart of the mountain.
39: This wide way has been modelled as an avenue, in the style of Elves and Men. To the sides are shops selling all sorts of goods, bustling with Dwarves and the occasional Man or Elf. Between the shops bright outdoor scenes are painted, and weary travellers may rest on benches along the way. On the ceiling high above can be seen a bright blue sky dotted with puffy white clouds. Here the passage bends slowly east and north. An arch in the southern wall leads into a large cavern.
40: This wide way has been modelled as an avenue, in the style of Elves and Men. To the sides are shops selling all sorts of goods, bustling with Dwarves and the occasional Man or Elf. Between the shops bright outdoor scenes are painted, and weary travellers may rest on benches along the way. On the ceiling high above can be seen a bright blue sky dotted with puffy white clouds.
41: A dwarven cityguard stands here looking scornfully at foreigners.

This wide way has been modelled as an avenue, in the style of Elves and Men. To the sides are shops selling all sorts of goods, bustling with Dwarves and the occasional Man or Elf. Between the shops bright outdoor scenes are painted and weary travellers may rest on benches along the way. On the ceiling high above can be seen a bright blue sky dotted with puffy white clouds. This part of the way is particularly busy, as it intersects the main path from the outside to the deeper parts of the Dwarven caves.
42: This wide way has been modelled as an avenue, in the style of Elves and Men. To the sides are shops selling all sorts of goods, bustling with Dwarves and the occasional Man or Elf. Between the shops bright outdoor scenes are painted, and weary travellers may rest on benches along the way. On the ceiling high above can be seen a bright blue sky dotted with puffy white clouds. To the north lies a prosperous-looking gem shop and to the west lies what looks like an inn.
43:
Nordri the shopkeeper stands here overseeing his store.
A dwarven cityguard is patrolling the streets.
A dwarven cityguard is patrolling the streets.

Dwarves are great lovers of precious metals and glittering gems, and their jewellery crafting is unsurpassed in Middle-earth. Even now, in the long decline of Durin's Folk, the finery on display is impressive. Though history has given Dwarves and Elves few reasons to love one another, still Elves sometimes come here to buy Dwarven handiwork.
44:
Traces of pale white tones form the aura of this place.
A dwarven cityguard stands here looking scornfully at foreigners.
A dwarven cityguard stands here looking scornfully at foreigners.
A dwarven cityguard stands here looking scornfully at foreigners.
A dwarven sergeant is here watching over his guards.
A sturdy pack horse is standing here.
A horse of the Rohirrim (ulo) is standing here.

A largely ceremonial hall, it was the first mineshaft that led down to what is now the second level of this Dwarven city. Dwarves hustle and bustle up and down the great staircase at whose top you now stand. Guards stand watch by the stairs, scowling at non-Dwarves, and a large sign is etched into the stone above them. It has been a long time since the eyes of Men or Elves have been welcome in the strongholds of the Dwarves, and this place is no exception.
48: A spiral staircase has been carved into the stone, winding its way around and around some fifty feet up and down. A single painting covers the outside wall, a broad overview of some distant battle which the Dwarves will never forget, and never forgive.
50: This passage leads east and west, delving its way through the mountains. This is a residential area, and the walls are pocketed with rows of doors, one after the other, each leading to an apartment where some solitary Dwarf resides. This area is boring, almost drab. The grey stone walls continue their monotonous march under the Ered Luin. There are no signs of decay or poor workmanship, but neither is there any ornamentation or beauty in the design. The main passage through this residential area turns east-to-south here, and a side passage enters from the west. The sides of the passageways are marked by rows of doors, one after the other, each leading to an apartment where some solitary Dwarf resides. Simple, utilitarian construction has been used here. The grey stone walls show no signs of decay or poor workmanship, but neither has much ornamentation or beauty been incorporated in the design.
51: A small line of houses extends off from the main route. The rock changes as the tunnel extends to the south, where it is no longer suitable for mining.
52: This sweltering room contains the Dwarven ironworks. Carts are wheeled up to the entrance, where they deposit their ore in large bins. In this part of the chamber sturdy Dwarves crush the ore into small pieces. Nothing is wasted; the iron dust is sintered into larger, more useful lumps. Carts bring the bits of iron ore south, where the heat intensifies.
53: A dwarf stands here sweating over the furnace.

Groups of sweating, bare-chested Dwarves labour in the heat to process the steady flow of iron ore. In the centre of this area is a cylindrical stone- built furnace. Into it the Dwarves feed a mixture of coal and iron ore. Around the furnace stand Dwarves pumping stolidly on tuyeres, feeding the flames within. After a time they remove a solid lump of malleable iron, adding it to the stacks on the side of the room. This cavern is near the top of the mountain, and several large ventilation shafts rise from the ceiling.
60: You are within an enormous cavern which extends beyond your vision and whose ceiling is lost in darkness. Though the floor is perfectly smooth, the walls are rough, filled with small niches and rocky knobs sticking into the hall. To your northeast, in the centre of this vast chamber, you can see what appear to be mountains rising up from the floor. Nearest you is a grey mount, rising up to a silver peak. Farther north stands one like a tooth tipped with snow; its walls glowing red in the cavern's light.
61: You are within an enormous cavern which extends beyond your vision and whose ceiling is lost in darkness. Though the floor is perfectly smooth, the walls are rough, filled with small niches and protrusions sticking into the hall. Directly to the north you see a miniature mountain rising high above your head, even here, deep within the Blue Mountains. It rises quickly, hard grey stone cunningly crafted by the Dwarves, with a silver peak gleaming in the cave's light.
62: You stand within an enormous cavern which extends beyond your vision and whose ceiling is lost in darkness. Though the floor is perfectly smooth, the walls are rough, filled with small niches and protrusions sticking into the hall. Arrayed to your northwest are three tall, broad towers, cleverly crafted to look like mountains. All three are made of hard grey stone, with snowy white peaks. The sheer sides of the furthest gleam a dull red in the light.
63: You stand at the corner of an enormous cavern. It opens to the west and north, and no end to its greatness can be seen. Just to the northwest there is a dark pool. Towering over it on three sides are mountainous towers, grey and red and snowy-capped. Fifty feet or so above you there is a large opening in the south wall.
64: You stand within an enormous cavern which extends beyond your vision and whose ceiling is lost in darkness. Though the floor is perfectly smooth, the walls are rough, filled with small niches and rocky knobs sticking into the hall. Just to the east a vast tower of rock rises from the floor, gleaming a snow- white silver at its peak. To the northeast stands a mountainous tower with sheer, dull-red sides. Peeking between them you can just see the white peak of a third tower.
66: The ground slopes gently down to a wide clear pool. The area around you is rough, except for a small flat surface near the pool, and several comfortable paths leading away. Several Dwarves peer into the pool, thinking of the twilight time when the first of their race awoke. They seem to be treating the water with great reverence, taking care not to touch its surface.
67: You are at the eastern edge of huge cavern deep within the earth. Just to your west is a small pool, around which stand several unusually contemplative Dwarves. Many other Dwarves walk quickly north or south.
68: A traffic sign is here, giving directions.

Many Dwarves pass by you here, at the northeastern corner of a gigantic opening in the mountain. This seems to be a major thoroughfare leading east and south. To your west are three mountains rising high up into the air. Two you see clearly, hard grey rock rising slowly up to white towers. Behind them you can glimpse the peak of a third.
69:
A dwarven child wanders around.
A dwarven female is here walking around.

This is a majestic entranceway to an enormous cavern to the west. From the east a wide corridor slopes slowly up, with constant width and height, until it approaches its end. There it abruptly widens, the ceiling rises into shadows and the path splits into two, separated by a massive statue. Dwarves walk quickly past you carrying all manner of provisions and crafts, paying little heed to the majestic sculpture.
70: A slender dwarf is here, tinkering with mechanical devices.

In the shelves that line the walls of this room lie countless devices. They all seem of a strange, mechanical nature. A great table fills the eastern portion of the room, and several lamps hang above it. On this table are scattered tumblers and strange instruments.
71: An aged and experienced dwarf is here, eager to share his wisdom.

Here within this tower in the shape of a mountain, the skills of survival are taught to those who would go out into the wild, mastering animals and facing the dangers of the elements. Even dwarven warriors, with faces hard as stone, know that their skin can be rent and torn, and that it is important to know how to bind one's wounds so that one may heal and return later on to battle.
72: Frag the dwarven warrior-master stands here drilling recruits.

Inside this tremendous tower of stone, the Dwarven war-masters teach the lessons of combat to their pupils. All around you, Dwarves spar with each other and with straw dummies, lunging, parrying and swinging their weapons in a synchronized dance of death. You are surprised at how crowded the sparring area is, and wonder if the Dwarven armies will once more march against evil in the lands of Arda.
73: You stand at the curved corner of an enormous cavern which extends beyond your vision to the south and east. Though the floor is perfectly smooth, the walls are rough, filled with small niches and knobby rocks jutting into the hall. To the east a great tower rises before you, a mighty peak tipped with snow like silver, but with sheer naked sides, dull red as if stained with blood. With your back to the cavern's wall, gazing up at the peak, you can almost believe that you are far away, and that the Dwarves still live in comfort and prosperity.
74:
A large bulletin board, entitled "Tales", is mounted here.
A huge clock is standing here.
A large fountain, made from grey stone, pours water from its centre.

To the east is the exit from the caves, but there is no hint here of sunlight. Still, the high ceilings, cheery lighting, and fresh air make this place seem almost like the outdoors. This seems to be something of a gathering place. There are many stone benches and tables arranged together so that small groups may sit and talk. Many Dwarves on their way in or out of the caves stop here to meet with friends awhile, and in a few groups you also see an occasional Elf.
75:
A sergeant of the dwarven guard looks around alertly.
A dwarven cityguard is patrolling the streets.
A dwarven cityguard is patrolling the streets.

This wide way has been modelled as an avenue, in the style of Elves and Men. To the sides are shops selling all sorts of goods, bustling with Dwarves and the occasional Man or Elf. Between the shops bright outdoor scenes are painted, and weary travellers may rest on benches along the way. On the ceiling high above can be seen a bright blue sky dotted with puffy white clouds. A general store is to the north.
76: Rekk the pipeweed trader is here, blowing smoke rings.

You are in a small, fragrant shop. All around you is the aroma of dried pipeweed. The source of the smell is obvious; pipeweed leaves and plants are hanging from strings and racks all over the shop. There is also a small case here displaying pipes and other objects. Small barrels are stacked around the side walls. At the back of the shop there is a small desk and a chair. To the west you can return to the main thoroughfare.
77:
A secretary is sitting at the desk.
A dwarven gateguard watches over the entranceway.
A dwarven gateguard watches over the entranceway.
A dwarven gateguard watches over the entranceway.

You stand at the very entrance of the Dwarven stronghold deep within the Ered Luin. To the east stand two huge iron doors. In times of peace they stand open, but should the warning horns blow they can be quickly closed and barred, and provide a formidable defence. The hall rises high above your head, its long lines drawing your eyes to the wide space above you. Far from a damp and dreary cave, this is a mansion - a grand hallway wrought of rich stone. Carved out of the living rock of its walls, busts of the great Dwarven kings stare into the hall. You can make out Dain I and Thror, watching over the entrance to the kingdom of the longbeards.
78:
A dwarven cityguard is patrolling the streets.
A dwarven cityguard is patrolling the streets.
A dwarven cityguard is patrolling the streets.
An experienced dwarven captain stands here with an air of authority.

Here are the simple barracks of the Dwarven home-guard. Wooden beds are bunked along the walls and a weapons-rack rests by the door. The home-guard is sworn to protect the city from all invaders, and their loyalty and ferocity have earned them much renown.
80: A dwarven cityguard is patrolling the streets.

Here are the simple barracks of the Dwarven home-guard. Wooden beds are bunked along the walls and a weapons-rack rests by the door. The home-guard is sworn to protect the city from all invaders, and their loyalty and ferocity have earned them much renown.
81:
A dwarven cityguard is patrolling the streets.
A dwarven cityguard is patrolling the streets.

This wide way has been modelled as an avenue, in the style of Elves and Men. To the sides are shops selling all sorts of goods, bustling with Dwarves and the occasional Man or Elf. Between the shops bright outdoor scenes are painted, and weary travellers may rest on benches along the way. On the ceiling high above can be seen a bright blue sky dotted with puffy white clouds. From the north come smells of baking. To the east Trader's Way opens to the outside.
82: Frar the baker is here, tending to his ovens.

The Dwarves make bread in their own image, short and hard. You see many Dwarves filter in and out of the bakery, chomping hardily on bread that looks like stone. From the look of the baker's wares, he very well may forge them rather than baking them in an oven.
83: A rumpled-looking dwarf walks around here.

The floor of this rather spartan room is covered in hay. A pungent, earthy smell fills the area. Various squeaks and growls can be heard from the cages and pens lining the wall. A battered wooden table stands in the middle of the room.
84:
A canoe has been left here.
A canoe has been left here.
A canoe has been left here.
A fat carp swims here.
A fat carp swims here.

This pond seems to have an underground source, as there is no visible inlet stream. It is not huge, just big enough for children to play in the water, and some animals to drink from. You could take a boat out on it, but you could not go very far at all.
85: The track you were on takes a turn for the better, as the loose gravel and rocks give way to tight fitting stones, inlaid with polished ore of various colours. The walkway ends in front of a smooth wall. It is so sharply defined that it might be a gate, but you see no breaks in it at all.
86: A very large stairway, carved from marble, leads up towards the surface and down into the Dwarven Halls in the heart of the Blue Mountains. The massive steps are flanked by a smooth paved road, which the Dwarves use to transport heavy items to and from their halls. The walls are covered with Dwarven runes and with carvings of important events of the history of the people of Durin. Torches are set in the walls and light the stairway efficiently; a light breeze from below keeps the air clear and breathable.
87: A worn trail ends here, at the foot of a high stone tower. An ornate archway to the east leads inside. To the north, beyond a large wooden building, lies the bank of the Nan Duin, while the trail continues to the south. To the west, a wide crack in a hill attracts your attention. The inside of the crack is lamplit, and you can see a very large marble staircase leading down.
88: You have arrived at a T junction. To the north the trail ends at the foot of a stone tower, near the Nan Duin. To the east you can see a dense forest in the distance, while to the south the winding trail climbs to the Blue Mountains, flanking the west side of the forest.
89: A prospector is walking around slowly, looking for a new ore vein to mine.

The trail runs east and west through some low, rocky hills. Not far to the north a stone tower attracts your curiosity. It is almost certainly inhabited, as you can guess from the smoke coming out of the chimney. The glittering waters of the Nan Duin flow from the west to the east behind the tower, mirroring the mountaintops. It is a fascinating sight.
90: The trail descends from the foothills to the west and plunges itself into the heart of a large forest to the south. North of here, the Nan Duin flows calmly to the east; you can follow its southern bank to the east, into the outskirts of the forest. Not far to the northwest, you can see a high stone tower.
91: The trail turns east into the heart of a dense forest; to the north the trees become sparser, and an area of rocky foothills begins. The woods to the southwest are unusually calm, while to the northwest a stone tower dominates the landscape.
92: The trail cuts the dense forest in a more or less east-west direction. On both sides, huge trees and tangled weeds flank the path, and prevent you from leaving it. Far to the northwest, the forest seems to grow thinner; right against the horizon, you barely manage to see the profile of a high tower.
93: You continue your journey along a trail in the middle of a dense forest. A nearly continuous wall of trees and greenery blocks your way north and east. Behind the thick trees, something seems to be growling at you. You feel that the ferocious creatures of the wood want to drink your blood.
94: The trail winds its way through a dense forest, turning to the north and east. A smaller trail leads west into the depths of the wood. On the trunk of a massive tree to the south, you can see the marks of many mighty axe blows. Some pieces of a fragmented skeleton lie at the foot of the tree. You can only try to guess what happened... Far to the northwest, you can barely see some smoke rising to the sky.
95: The trail stretches far away in an east-west direction, climbing gently to the west. A forest of huge trees flanks it on both sides. Miles behind the treetops, you can spot the snow capped peaks of the Blue Mountains.
96: The trail winds its way to the west and south through a dense forest. In this place, a hole in the otherwise impenetrable barrier of entangled greenery could allow you to enter the thick woods to the north, but something - perhaps the occasional high pitched howls and deep growls - might discourage the faint-hearted from venturing among the ancient trees.
97: You are on a dusty trail leading north and east through the woods. Some branches, which evidently obstructed passage, have been cut and now lay on the border of the trail. To the west, a seldom used path enters the forest. You can smell the presence of mushrooms in that direction, though you cannot figure out the species.
98: Huge trees, which seem to reach the sky, flank the trail on both sides here. You would rest for a while in their shadow, but your instinct tells you that danger awaits you in the forest. The trail turns to the west and south.
99: The trail winds its way north and east through the Blue Mountains. A small path, almost completely hidden by high grass, climbs the steep mountain side to the south. To the north a dense, gloomy forest flanks the trail. A thick wall of huge trees and entwined greenery prevents you from entering the woods here.
100: A woodpecker is here, tapping on a tree.

Maybe you should remain on this path as opposed to entering the forest to your north. Uncertainty settles on you at the thought of entering. Can you handle the threats and dangers of the dark gloomy place? Many glowing eyes darting in the blackness peer at you, and almost lure you in with their tempting gleam. The path continues to the south and west.
101: The trail continues to the north and east here. The presence of life is sparse, limited mostly to animals and birds. The treetops are alive with the songs of swallows and finch, and the grounds are occupied by squirrels, fox, and deer. The river provides a good source of water, and food from bushes is plentiful. Habitation by more humanoid creatures is not in evidence, except for the trail.
102: The trail continues to the east and west here, past heavy woodlands all around. To the north, nothing special attracts your attention besides the abnormally thick growth of vines and tree limbs. To your south however, there is a grassy field. A pile of stones that looks out of place makes you take notice. Should you investigate or write it off to coincidence?
103: The trail bends here, leading south or west. To the north lies a great forest containing massive trees overgrown with vines and bushes. A large fire in this woodland would surely be visible for many miles, and would burn for many a night. The gloomy blackness of the forest stares back at you, seeming to invite you in. You cannot be sure, but you think you see many glowing eyes peering out at you from behind the tree trunks.
104: The trail you are on is hard packed dirt. It leads through a dense forest, choked with vines and bushes amid the massive tree trunks. The trail leads north and east here, past a dark woodland. To the west is a small clearing, looking uninhabited at the moment, but signs of encampment mark the area in the form of an old fire pit. Should you investigate or leave it undisturbed?
105: A sharp-eyed hawk is here stalking some prey.

The path continues from the east to west here. Another trail leads into the south. Whoever makes their residence in these parts is a sturdy fellow for sure. The forest that spreads its breadth around you is dark and gloomy. Thick branches and vines grow everywhere, some even encroaching on the trail itself.
106: A roe deer is standing here, watching the terrain while chewing the vegetation.

The trail rises and falls slowly with the rolling plains. Bushes and tall grasses brush across the horizon. The dirt along the trail seems to have been disturbed by the passing of others. The land slowly rises to a mountain range in the northwest. The trail continues its motion to the north and south.
107: A roe deer is standing here, watching the terrain while chewing the vegetation.

The trail runs north, crossing a series of low hills heading towards a large range of mountains far to the north. The track slowly descends as it wanders through the plains towards the south. The path is well kept with small rocks marking its passage. The rest of the hill continues to the west, but slowly merges with a range of greyish-white hills far to the northwest.
108: Water trickles from many tiny gullies, meeting to form a small stream. The flow of water is not yet continuous. But the ground in the shallow ditch seems to stay wet. The trail continues to the north and west, crossing the dense carpet of grass. The plains continue far to the east and south.
109:
A brown fox is here, looking for some rabbits to chew up.
A roe deer is standing here, watching the terrain while chewing the vegetation.
A sparrow is flapping around on the ground.

Travelling this nicely kept mountain trail, zigzagging between and around boulders, fissures and rocky outcroppings. A majestic granite ridge rises into the sky a bit north of here. Streams and small hills mix in this relatively flat terrain, several smaller streams slowly descend to the east. A neatly kept trail continues to the west.
110: The trail is well kept and its borders are lined with small stones retrieved from the rocky ridge that lies to the north-west. The trail continues to the east and south. The land rises and falls to the north and south. The land rises to the northwest. Trees dot the plains and increase in frequency to the northwest.
111:
A low and wide-spread tree grows here.
On the tree's branches, there are two juicy plums.

The trail continues to the north and south. The terrain gradually rises to the west as the trees increase in number. Through the scraggly oak trees and tall underbrush, a tall hill can be seen reaching for the sky. A larch-wood glade with heavy underbrush covers the ground to the west. Various trails created by animals cross between the bushes.
112: A fallow deer is grazing peacefully here.

The trail follows the flow of the land and bends to the north and west. A few scattered oaks dot the plains, marking the beginning of a vast forest to the southwest. Gently rolling plains cover the horizon to the north and east. Tall grasses flow along with any breeze. Clumps of brush and an occasional tree break up the monotony.
113:
A sparrow is flapping around on the ground.
A large elk is standing here, chewing grass and leaves.

The trees beside the trail are tall and their leaves block out the light from the sun and the moon. The forest continues to get thicker to the south and west. But to the north the trees thin out and dense vegetation covers the ground. A vast plain stretches far to the east.
114: Although you feel safe on the path you are on, there is no saying what dwells within these dark woods. The beech grove to your south does not seem too threatening, but curious, some would say frightening, sounds can be heard from the thicket of ash trees north of here.
115: Here, as the path bends south and east, a tiny track strays from it, heading its own way through grassy slopes to the west. To the north the ground slants slowly upward into the forest, and from it you can from time to time hear the forest birds stir up a noisy symphony.
116: The forest path steers steadily on north and south between the trees. You may enter a grove of beeches to the east, but west the overlapping branches stubbornly denies you access. The gap in the forest seems to grow wider within sight to the north.
117: You stand on a modest forest path, the horizon on all sides veiled by a mist of trees. The forest seems less dense to the east, tall and bulky trees which from here look like beeches. Westward you can enter a more intimidating part of the forest, dense woods which seem to have the very darkness of the Pits of Utumno nestled within. To stay out of the forest, you can follow the path trailing north and south.
118: This path, being only a minor trail of the many roads stretched out between Mithlond and the Dwarven Homes, does not see much use. It follows a natural vein of open space through the forest, sometimes not more than a couple of pole lengths in width, but most often it measures up to a hundred feet across. While the path leads the way north and east, a gap in the deep, dark forest leers wickedly at you from the west.
119: You are moving on a path through the outer limits of a forest. Neither the forest to your east or north are as dense as the imposing forest surrounding the path going west, and south you clearly see the forest breaking up into open grassland.
120: You stand on the borderland between forest and fields. To the north the forest closes in on the beaten path, only letting out sounds of wildlife from its dark recesses. A southward gaze shows you the path making a zigzagging pattern through a rustic scene of fields and foothills.
121: This flimsy path lies along the edge of a forest. The fir trees and bushes form a thick wall to the west and south, seemingly as dense as the wild and mighty forests of Far Harad. The path continues north alongside the forest's edge, and east towards rich green fields.
122: A sparrow is flapping around on the ground.

The trail is well-used and easy to travel on. All around you the green grass bends softly in the wind and the chatter of many small birds can be heard. To the north and west a great forest begins and to the south and east vast plains and green hills dominate the landscape.
123: This trail seems to be frequently used, it is even and smooth, which makes travelling easy. It continues north and east, and further east you see some foothills, which rolls on for a long distance. To the west you notice a forested area, which seems to have rich animal life, just like the woods that lies southeast from here.
124: Here the trail curves gently through the landscape, it goes west and comes from the south. Smoothly rounded foothills can be seen in the east and the smoke from some fire is hanging in the air here. The smell of meat and wood suggests that someone is smoking freshly caught game and the scents seems to be coming from a building that can be seen to the southwest.
125: A Trail Going Past a Cabin

You see a cabin to your west and a barrel of water stands in front of it. There is smoke coming from the chimney, and the air smells of freshly cooked meat. The cabin is made of thick logs and has two small windows and a sturdy oakdoor. Several dead rabbits are hung to dry in the sun on a wooden rack. The trail you are standing on leads on north and east of here.
126: A tall elven trapper is walking around here.

This is a sparse but comfortably built cabin. Several hunting tools adorn the wooden walls and different kinds of bows are hung above the fireplace, where a nice fire could be built. A metal box used for smoking meat is hanging above the fire too, and often the smell of meat in the air. Some furs and pelts lie on a desk in the middle of the room, and a few stools are placed around it. On a shelf at the back of the room there is a partly finished longbow.
127: The trail bends here, going west and south. Further west you can see smoke coming from a small cabin, and to the north a small hill is visible. As a bird flies off to the east you see foothills in that direction. A multitude of tracks cover the trail, making individual tracks harder to distinguish.
128: The trail leaves north and east. It seems often travelled, although not often by large creatures or wagons. The area west of here is filled with small rises and inclines in the landscape. Another curve in the trail lies east of here.
129: A Trail Going West and South

The trail makes a sharp turn in the landscape here, turning south and west from the point you are standing. It continues west for a while and then bends again, and to the east some hills can be seen. Looking south you see that the trail bends around another corner and vanishes from sight. No trees grow here, only small bushes.
130: Looking north and east you see the trail heading onwards in those directions. A hilly terrain streches out to the west and to the south some bushy fields can be seen. Far to the north the trail bends again and east you notice a crossway far away.
131: A green frog is here, hopping around.

The trail comes to a crossing here, leaving in three directions. West, south and east the trail leads. To the north it twists through some hilly terrain. Looking further away in any direction yields little more information about the area, the only thing you notice is that the trail goes straight south. A small sign has been placed here.
132: The trail bends in a nice curve going north and west. Looking further north you notice that the trail bends again after a while and to the west the trail comes to a crossway. A deep forest surrounds the trail to the east and south, the forest seems to be very deep and also calm.
133: An Elf is here walking around.

A forest lies to the east, different animals can be seen and heard in the deep but calm forest. The trail itself goes north and south here, looking further south you see that it bends to the east and to the north it comes to a crossway of some sort. Westward several bushes grow on a plain.
134: A Bend in the Winding Trail
A young man in ranger's attire is here, travelling the roads.

Yet again the trail bends here on it way into the wilderness. It goes north and east here and to the south plains covered with bushes stretch out. Looking west you see more plains. The air is calm and not much wind ever disturbs this area. Small rocks lie beside and on the road.
135: A Bend in the Winding Trail

The forest surrounds the western and nothern border of this area. Sounds from different animals echoes out from the deep forest. The trail itself turns west and south here. Many small curves in the trail makes it a little bit tiring to walk on, and the small pebbles that lie on the trail makes it even harder to walk without slipping a little.
136: A curvy trail carves through the landscape here, going north and south. It is bordered to the east by a deep forest with tall and ancient looking trees. The trail is narrow and curves madly on its way into the wilderness. To the west a vast bush-covered area stretches out.
137: The trails makes a bend to the north here, coming from the east. Looking west you see some plains stretching out and to the south similar terrain can be seen. A dark and calm looking forest is visible to the northeast and the trail goes on for as far as you can see to the north.
138: The trail bends west and south here, while to the north a large forest is visible. It seems to be very deep and different bird calls echoes out from it. To the east you notice a large winegrape field that stretches out for as far as you can see. Pebbles litter the ground here, making it tricky to walk without slipping.
139: The curvy trail makes yet another bend on its way into the wilderness. Far to the southeast you know that Mithlond is located, home of Cirdan and the fair elves. In this area you see however, a river to the south that seems to be rather rapid. The trail itself goes north and east here and looking west you see some fields stretching out.
140: An Elf is here walking around.

Curving its way through the landscape the trail makes another bend here. This time it turns west and south. Looking north you see a well-tended winegrape field and beyond that you see the dark outline of a forest. Southward you hear the noise of running water.
141: A grey wolf is here, snarling aggressively.

The river runs west to the west of here, but to the east the trail continues for a while. Northward the trail also goes on in almost a straight line. Looking south you notice the river again, looking even wilder than to the west. Bushes and small trees grow along the trail.
142: The trail comes from the south and turns to the west here. A river can be heard far to the west while to the east you see fields stretching out. Directly north of the path you see winegrapes growing in straight rows, someone is caring well for them.
143: The trail makes a sudden turn here, from the east to the north. The river can be seen flowing far to the south, until you can just make out where it enters the Gulf of Lhun. The southern most slopes of Ered Luin can be seen far to the north.
145:
The corpse of an elven farmer is lying here.
The corpse of an elven farmer is lying here.
A pitchfork has been carelessly left lying here.
A pair of soft leather boots are on the ground.
A grey pair of pants are on the ground.
An ancient flat straw hat is lying here.
A grey shirt is on the ground.
The corpse of an elven farmer is lying here.

You are on a small dirt trail running north and south, along a rushing river. Just to the south you see can see Mithlond. Far to the north you can make out the southern peaks of Ered Luin. Beyond Mithlond you see the Gulf of Lhun extending to the horizon.
146: Before the North Gate of Forlond

Traces of fierce red tones form the aura of this place.
A small campfire is here, ready to be lit.

A small trail runs through the great fields north of Mithlond here. The path continues to the north, and a rushing river runs to the west of the trail, making its way to the Gulf of Lhun a few miles to the south. To the immediate south are the North Gates of Forlond. The great, white stone walls that surround the city break only here, and in that gap stands a huge, iron gate.
147: A Trail Bending East and South

The small trail bends here, going east and south. Looking west you notice a rocky area, covered with sharp stones and boulders. To the east the trails continues for a little bit, at least according to what you can see. A small slope can be seen north.
148: You have reached a crossing in the trail. The main trail leads north and west here, while a small path to the east, covered with weeds and grass, seems to lead across the bushy fields. South of you a large forest looms, its underbrush looking rather dense and thorny. A faint sound of some small animal can be heard in the distant.
149: The trail goes north for as far as you can see, but to the south it bends in a westward direction. Foothills are visible to your west, possibly containing some small game. The grassy fields east of here seems like a peaceful place with the tall grass gently swaying in the wind.
150: A brown fox is here, looking for some rabbits to chew up.

The trail leads south from here. Small foothills lie a small distance to the west from here, while some plains stretch out to the east. The trail seems to be well trodden upon. Looking south you can see how the trail cuts through the landscape in a snakelike manner.
151: The trail is cleared from brush and other plants, and it looks to be in a decent shape. Both sides are covered with dead trees and bushes. The landscape is turning hilly to the northwest. The hills to the west are still very small and can easily be travelled without any major hazards.
152: A sparrow is flapping around on the ground.

The trail rambles along in a north-south direction, almost hidden away within the foothills of this area. Smaller hills make the way west from here a bit harder to travel without mounts. A small stone on the side of the trail has some markings on it.
153: A large rabbit looks peacefully at you, ready to dart away.

Large hills cover the land both to the north and west. The uneven terrain hinders the view of the surrounding land. Two oaks hang over the trail, attempting to embrace and forming an arch above the trail heading to the north. The path continues to the south where the land seems to be more even.
154: A sparrow is flapping around on the ground.

A large hedge of blueberry bushes grows along the southern side of the trail. Birds and other animals seem to have made off with most of the fruit. The trail continues north along the broken hills of limestone to the northwest, and travels along the uneven ground leading into them to the west. Only a few trees can be seen along the top ridge of the hills.
155: Bushes, shrubs and high grass are threatening to overgrow this trail. Some big tree roots have already cracked it up. A lone oak is growing besides the trail is here and a manmade birds nest is nailed to the trunk about twelve feet from the ground. The hills stretch west as far as you can see.
156: The trail turns to the west and to the north here. To the north a tavern stands next to the trail, welcoming travellers. Trees grow more numerous around the trail here as well as bushes and other larger plants. Animal tracks are mixed with the tracks of humanoids and cart tracks on the ground.
157: In Front of a Wooden Building

An alehouse stands to the east. On the sign, a worn painting of an old axe can be seen. The building seems small compared to those of the great elven cities to the south. However, it is a welcome sight on the long trail. Shrubs and bushes decorate the western edge. The worn path continues to the north and south.
158: Large stones have been placed in various spots crossing the shallow stream. A few lie covered with moss. Thick brush and a few large oaks keep the crossing private. The trail leads north into a series of foothills, while to the south it crosses a vast plain. The foothills wind their way from the north, to the west, before continuing south again.
159: The trail appears to have been cut through the limestone between two valleys. Steep vertical cliff sides have been worn by water, which drips slowly even now. Rocks litter the sides of the trail. The valley to the east, and the one to the south, seems to open up to a land much smoother than the rocky hills here. An occasional crevice leads even deeper into the hills, many too small to enter.
160: Small shrubs and young trees line the trail, like heralds, waiting for the arrival of their king. Grass flows gently along the plains far to the east and south. A series of deep hills line the base of a high plateau to the north and west. The trail cuts follows a limestone valley to the west, hopefully, more easily travelled than the rest of the hills seem to be.
161: Trail along the Base of Low Hills

Various bushes grow beside the trail, and a line of young trees dot the plains nearby. A deep series of washed-out limestone valleys lead deep into a series of hills to the west, which eventually lead to a high plain to the west. The trail continues along the foothills to the north, while the trail leads around the hills to the south.
162: Trail along the Base of Low Hills

Grass grows thickly along the sides of the trail. Large bushes present hiding places to predators of all kinds. Flowers have taken root in the rich soil that has been washed down from the high plains to the west. Foothills begin the climb. The trail continues to follow the foot of the ridge to the north and south.
163: A narrow, worn trail snakes its way through the hilly countryside. All about, towering hills rise up in various shapes and sizes. The trail continues north and south, running parallel to the ridge west of here. Some tiny flowers grow beside the trail amidst the lush green grass.
164: A Faltering Trail in the Rising Mountains

A mountain goat is here, jumping from cliff to cliff.
A mountain goat is here, jumping from cliff to cliff.
A mountain goat is here, jumping from cliff to cliff.

The trail climbs a slope here, and to the west the land slopes upward into the foothills of this small mountain range, which whilst spectacular, is no match to the lofty peaks of Ered Luin, far west of here. To the south the trail winds between massive boulders and piles of rubble, travel both east and west is possible with little difficulty. To the north, the trail runs down a fairly steep slope.
165: Off to the west of here the trail narrows, and almost disappears, as it marches into the rising foothills of the mountains. The ground underfoot is quite rocky, but still numerous bushes and small shrubs line either side of the path, and the everpresent sound of birds and insects can be heard.
166: The trail here is only wide enough for one or two to ride or walk abreast. Underfoot, the ground is rocky, and the surface fairly uneven, and the path slopes upward as it marches to the southwest from here. To the north the footing appears to improve, as the path climbs steadily downward.
167: The trail grows narrower here than it is to the north, though the same small bushes and shrubs still line either side of it, and it has the appearance of a pathway wrought by mortal hand. It slopes steadily upward to the south, and becomes rockier in that direction, whereas to the north it widens out and grows steadily wider and smoother.
168: At a Branch in the Trail

Small bushes and trees line the trail and you can hear the sound of many birds singing within their boughs. The width of this trail could easily accomodate four or five horsemen abreast, but to the south it becomes narrower, steeper and more rocky. However, it allows easy access to the forest to the north.
169: The ground underfoot is quite poor and rocky, so that only a few small, sickly shrubs and some thin grasses cling to life here. And much of the vegetation has been worn away by the feet of passing travellers, using this route for their journey from the Blue Mountains to the lowlands to the east.
170: A woodpecker is here, tapping on a tree.

The rocky soil here is a pain to walk on for either mount or walker. A little thicket of bushes grows here next to a very large mountain standing to the south. Much life fills this thicket including snakes, rabbits, squirrels, and other small rodents. A journey to the south looks very tiresome, as the trail begins to climb up a steep slope.
171: Far to the west you see patches of green grass and hills of lush bushes. Here however, there seems to be only a cracked rocky soil that makes walking difficult for either mount or walker. Thanks to the white stones lying beside the trail here you can follow it. It must have been the dwarves that marked the trail this way in order to follow it even on such a rocky terrain. Northwards lie some more flat-lands, and to the south a small range of hills lead into the eastern Ered Luin. Somewhere in the north you hear the sound of flowing water, probably the Nan Duin.
172: A dove rests near one of the flowers.

You find yourself on the top of a small hill that gives you a view of the surroundings. You can see a huge forest to the west, tall and dark it seems to be, and also to your east you can spot a great forest. The trail is broad and wellmarked and is easy to follow. To the south west you can see a small farm in the distance. It is in fair shape, and is obviously inhabited. Flat land reveals itself on your east side, and you can barely see the swift Nan Duin flowing in the north.
173: You are in a wide expanse of plains now, with the path clearly followed in the middle. You can see two big forest to the east and west here. The one to the east seems rather large, but you are so far away from it that you really can't tell that much about it at all. The one to your west side however, looks dark and gloomy, with many large trees and snaking vines. What evils lurk in that section of woodland? You hear a river flowing to the north, and also spy a small bridge in that direction.
174: The path goes ever on, and now you are right outside a small farm. These fields have been somewhat cultivated. Not carefully tended and tilled as the farms in the Shire are, but worked on nonetheless. Rocks have been removed as has the annual grass. In its place grow a few green shoots indicating vegetables. A gate is to your south, probably the entry into a small farm, and you will reach a cosy home after crossing what appears to be a pasture.
175: The path makes a smooth bend here and turns east and south. However, the west holds a very dark forest. Also to the north is a forest, seeming to reach around and encompass you. This seems to be a transition area between the open hills and plains, where it merges with the dark gloominess of the forest. Small animals grace the plains, and similar creatures occupy the forest. These are not what concerns you however; the ones that hide within the bounds of the forest are of more concern. Should you enter?
176: Traversing the land between rolling hills, you can still follow the trail easily. It contains nothing of unusual properties, just wavy grass and small animals. The way runs north-south here, opening into more plains-type land in front and in back of you. Scrambling up the gentle forest would be easy, if not for a crumbling ridgeline that parallels the valley. It lies on your west side, and would be impossible to climb up without dislodging many rocks.
177: Small bushes and trees line the trail and you can hear the sound of many birds singing within their boughs. The width of this trail could easily accomodate four or five horsemen abreast, and was obviously created to allow easy access into the great forest. Off to the east lies a large clearing and looks like a perfect place to stop and rest.
178: Small bushes and trees line the trail and you can hear the sound of many birds singing within their boughs. To the east the trees become more frequent and the trail narrows.
179: The trail narrows and is almost completely engulfed by the forest. Great trees tower along either side of you as you carefully make your way through the forest. Wild animals can be heard from every direction which cautions you to navigate carefully. The trail leads west and east.

The bridge spans across the river and leads south into the great forest, and to the north there are open plains.
185: Unlike the terrain on the south side of the river, vast hilly plains cover the entire horizon. The small rolling hills are covered with long yellow-brown grasses, some even waist high. Bare spots of earth and stone top off the occasional hill accenting their variety of shapes and sizes. The trail continues to the west and to the south you can see a bridge.
186: Hills continue to stretch out as far as you can see. The grass on the hilly slopes hypnotically sways as strong breezes swirl around from multiple directions. To the south thick brambles makes it impossible to travel in that direction, but a steady murmur and the occasional splash confirm that the river is nearby. The trail continues to the east and west.
187:
A fierce boar is here, making grunting noises.
A robin is here, carrying small pieces of wood to its nest.

Hills continue to stretch out as far as you can see, yet the path is easy to follow here. The grass on the hilly slopes hypnotically sways as strong breezes swirl around from multiple directions. To the south thick brambles make it impossible to travel in that direction, but a steady murmur and the occasional splash confirm that the river is nearby.
188: Hills continue to stretch out in all directions. The grass on the hilly slopes hypnotically sways as strong breezes swirl around from multiple directions. The hills continue on to the south towards the river, and to the north towards higher ground. The path continues to the north and south.
189: Hills still stretch out in all directions, but their numbers decline and each hill seems to be the size of a small mountain. The land has much more definition here and it is no longer easy to keep watch in all directions. A high ridge to the distant north traces the horizon and several odd formations along its edge, not quite natural, catches your eye. The path bends to the east and south here.
190: Hills still stretch out in all directions, but their numbers decline and each hill seems to be the size of a small mountain. From this viewpoint they look to be outposts of some sort, but you cannot tell for sure.

A cold damp chill swells around you as you settle into a comfortable stride in the centre of the valley bed. Plains open up to the north and the valley continues on to the east.

A mountain lion eyes you closely and prepares to pounce for his next meal.

An assortment of different sized rocks blanket the entire floor of the valley, making footing difficult, and you take each step with care. A cold damp chill swells around you as you settle into a comfortable stride in the centre of the valley bed. The trail continues to the north and east.
193: You make your way past the loose scree and begin to climb the steep winding path that leads up the side of the mountain. In a few areas the rock face steepens and juts out, forcing you to make short vertical climbs to regain the path and continue onward. To the west lies a shallow valley while the worn trail continues upwards.
194: Although the trail is not nearly as steep as it is below, the grade is sufficient to keep you cautious as you search for solid footing. High grass grows all about and seems to be the only sign of any vegetation in the vicinity. The grass's brown edges and yellow stalks indicate the problem with the ground's impermability to water, and if it were not for the occasional overflow of the nearby river nothing could grow here at all.
195: These floodplains consist entirely of soft topsoil, silt, and other debris that the river deposits here when it overflows its banks. This combination of soil and river-life provides perfect fertile land allowing bushes, shrubs, and flowers to thrive and flourish along the plains' northern and western outskirts. The western side of the plains show deep linear gouges in the land, as if large heavy objects had been consistantly dragged across from the river. You try to come up with some way these could be naturally occuring, since the only obvious exit to the south is by no means a possible route to take heavy equipment, but you are unable to fathom any explanation. To the east you can see many rocks; it seems like you could cross the river without a boat here.
196: You carefully step on the boulders while the water trickles past you. Through the crystal clear water you can see the many different species of fish and other river life living within the shallows. Tiny ripples from the dew dripping off the surrounding plantlife are the only blemishes on the glassy surface of these tranquil waters.
197: Small rocks cover the ground all around you and make small crackling sounds as you move upon them. Small patches of ground quartz line the areas closer to the water, bubbling with moisture. To the east you see flat ground, covered with larger rocks and a few huge boulders which dominate your view. The trail ends here, but it looks like it continues on the other side of the river. To the west you can see a river, still you might be able to enter without a boat.
198: Massive boulders seem to be everywhere, making it difficult to move quickly around this terrain. An uneasiness comes over you as you feel that this place is much too quiet, seemingly void of life. You would not give it another thought if it were not for the strange scrapings you see on the lower portion of the rocks, and the faint scent of musk that fills the air. The trail is a pain to follow for you and you have to take it easy around here.
199: Massive boulders seem to be everywhere, making it difficult to move quickly around this terrain. You would not give it another thought if it were not for the strange scrapings you see on the lower portion of the rocks, and the faint scent of musk that fills the air. The trail branches here, with travel possible to the east, west and south.
200: Giant boulders tower over you blocking your passage to the south. Their masses cast shadows all about the ground and it is difficult to see if any evil lurks within them. Off to the west you see the edge of a sparse forest and you can hear the sound of many different animals rustling amongst the trees. It looks like the trail leads into an opening to the north here.
201: With predominantly younger trees spaced many meters apart, this section of the forest is quite bright and welcoming making you feel at ease as you stroll deeper into the forest. To the east the trees thin and then disappear completely, giving way to the a trail. To the south the trees grow much closer together, effectively sheltering the ground from the elements as well as blocking out much of the light, yet there seems to be a path you can follow here.

You stumble across what seems to be a small path meandering through the rows of trees. It seems to be very old but well used. It must be the main trail from the southern lands into the Blue mountains to the northwest. You seem to be able to distiguish the path as it leads south and west, continuing through the towering trees.

A brown fox is here, looking for some rabbits to chew up.

You try your best to keep sight of the signs of the old forest path. Giant trees surround you, towering and intimidating, forcing you to keep aware of their presence as well as the creatures that they might shelter. You seem to temporarily lose your way, but ahead to the south and north you can once again see small traces of the ancient byway.
207: The thick thorny bushes fade away, replaced by soft dark earth and small green and yellow bushes growing little red berries. Off to the west the trees once again are thick, and the murmer of rushing water can be heard. The byway continues over a small leaf-covered hill to the north and south.

209: A sturdy pack horse is standing here.

You find yourself on a shady path in the forest. The path is well-prepared and makes travel here easy. The forest is bordered to the north by hills and rocks, and you think you hear the sound of water running among the trees. The main path seems to continue east and west, and you can enter deeper into the forest to the south.

To the north you can see mostly mountainous terrain.

The trees are green, most of them tall pines, and the scent makes you feel like staying here for a while. The brushwood between the trees has been removed and set up at several places. You notice a small path in the bushes to the east, while you can stay on the main path by going north or south.

To the west and the east you see two paths, conveniently connected by the bridge.

The path continues to the north and south.

225: The path you follow is easy to follow. You wish all paths should be so easy to follow indeed. On all sides of the path you can see some thick grass growing. The path continues to the north and south.

This trail seems to be every step less defined, and you realise few come around here. It goes north and west.

You'd better use the road that goes south and east.

To the north the river can be reached from the bank, while to the west you can see a small island. Soft silt and shallow water make it impossible to reach from here though.
232: The lands both to the east, and to the west of the trail boast a natural, rugged beauty. The sound of grasshoppers can be heard from the grass nearby, and from somewhere to the west the croaking of frogs seems to originate. This is usually a peaceful spot, although the local wildlife are regularly disturbed by travellers. The river lies to the west, but to the east a sandstone rock cliff prevents movement in that direction, although it gets lower to the south where it eventually disappears.
233: The trail curves sharply to the west and north. East of you, you see a flat area. Sometimes you see a stag run by and a deer here and there. The plains seem to be filled with life and vegetation. It looks as if mother nature blessed this place.

The river flows from the west to the south, across a forest. The water is so clear that you can watch the fish swimming between the rocks on the bottom of the river.

You continue along the blue water of the of Nan Duin as it stretches far to the east and west beyond the horizon. A large beautiful rose bush is blooming here.
A buck runs swiftly from place to place, looking about warily as it grazes.

Several small bushes cover this part of the field. They lack flowers but make it up with plenty of nasty looking thorns. To the west high grass can be seen, but to the east the bushy fields continues. North of you grows a shorter kind of grass which seems to get deeper further north. Looking south you see a ruined shack that seems to have been the home of a farmer once, now long gone.
435: To the west a trail can be seen, leading north and south. Further east the fields continue all the way as far as the eye can see. Not a single tree can be spotted in that direction, but some bushes grow irregularly through the landscape.
436: Standing in the high grass with birds flying above your head you see more plains to the north. West of here is a trail leading north and south, while the grass looks just as high to the east. The grass is high enough to be the hiding place of dangerous animals ready to spring upon innocent victims.
437: A Path outside a Ruined Shack
