The small path ends in front of an old abandoned shack. It seems to have been an old farm building of some sort, but its state of decay suggests it has been a while since it was inhabited. Some movement can be seen inside however, though it is evident that it is an animal moving about. Outside the shack is a dried out well, with an unusual bucket barely hanging onto a piece of rope. No door is seen in the entrance - it has simply fallen off the hinges and lies next to the shack.
438:
The small fierce-looking bat is hanging from the ceiling, obviously sleeping.
The small fierce-looking bat is hanging from the ceiling, obviously sleeping.
A small bat is standing here.

You enter the small building. Looking around you, you notice a table that is falling apart and some abandoned kitchen wares. A old bed is standing in the corner of the room but it looks far from inviting. The wind blows in through large cracks between the wooden panels and the stove is completely ruined. Some strange droppings on the floor reveal that a small colony of bats have made this old building their home.
439: A large beautiful rose bush is blooming here.

North of here you see an old and partly ruined shack. It looks as if it once belonged to a farmer that used to work these fields a long time ago. The fields stretch out in all directions and small bushes litter the area. The bushes are small and most of them have thorns. Some of them might carry berries during the summer.
440: A large and very deep forest is visible south and west of here. Various animal cries can be heard echoing out between the trees. The wind here is calm and it smells sweet. To the north you see a small trail, possibly leading to the hut you can see northeast. The immidiate vincinity is covered with bushes and small trees.
441: Travelling westward means that you will go deeper and deeper into this ancient forest, looking east you see open plains of some sort stretching out. The trees are growing very tall here and they cover the sky completely with their large, old and knotted branches. The echoes of animals can be heard coming from deeper within the forest. You also notice that the wind is cut off by the protection of the trees, no matter how hard it blows on the plains, here it is always calm.
442: If you venture west you will enter a forest that seems to be deep and calm, while north of you some plains covered with bushes are visible. East and south of here more fields covered with grass stretch out. The air is humid and still, the forest must shield this area from the worst winds.
443: The air is very humid and still here. Not much light can filter down through the thick branchwork above you. Moss grows on everything and echoes of wild animals can be heard but you rarely see anything moving. Some boulders are strewn around the forest floor, many have the shape of living things but are only nature's work on stone. It is impossible to see far in any direction, the trees simply grow too thick here. A large boulder looking like a troll is lying here.
444: A swift and agile forest cat moves silently through the vegetation.

The trees grow bigger and bigger the deeper into the forest you travel and soon the sky is hidden from your sight by the large branches sprouting from the trees. A few birds can be heard calling deep in the forest, their sounds echo throughout the vicinity. Other living creatures move about, making noises but you have a hard time spotting any of them. Always present, always distant they move about in the own business.
445: You walk among ancient trees here, so tall that they completely blot out the sky above you. Boulders covered with moss can be seen here and there, resting as they have rested undisturbed for eons. Some take on the shape of trolls, some seem to be frozen forms of different animals. Moss dangles from the limbs of the trees and a soft fungi smell is hanging in the air. No matter what the weather is around this spot, the wind will never reach down here.
446: Rocks litter this area, varying in size, but all very sharp. Travelling is very awkward here and the trails seen in all directions but to the north must be easier to travel by. A great oaktree is looming north from here.
447: In the Middle of the Foothills
A woodpecker is here, tapping on a tree.

This area is completely surrounded by small, rocky hills and other rough terrain, making travelling here somewhat difficult but not too tiring. A single large oak tree decorates this area and birds can sometimes be seen flying in and out of the treetop. A hole in the trunk about halfway up seems to be the home of a squirrel, based on the litter of nutshells on the ground at the base of the tree.
448: A squirrel scampers around here, looking for nuts from the trees.

This area is with the exception of a few small rocks smooth, making travel a feat. To the east a trail can be seen, going north and south. Further west a large tree is growing among the foothills, and to the south you can once again make out the trail. A gentle foothill stretches north.
449: A tall stag is here, grazing peacefully.

A trail can be seen to the west while the foothills stretch out to the north and east. No trees grow here, but some bushes and rocks litter the area, making travel somewhat tricky. Rabbits and other small animals has made several tracks in a small puddle.
450: The foothills offer a nice bit of scenery with several animals darting between hiding places among the multitude of bushes and rocks. Travelling here is light although a trail would feel welcome for tired feet. To the north you can see some plains. The foothills continue in all other directions.
451:
A wolf cub happily plays here.
The mother wolf stands here, protecting her young cubs.

Grasses constrict the growth of other plants on the high plains. Few bushes manage to grow above the grass and even fewer trees manage to reach the sky. Sounds of wildlife can be heard, but the local flora hides their movement from sight. The plains continue to the west, but hills surround the field in all other directions.
452: A few loose rocks make travelling here slightly harder. The local fauna of the foothills offer no great surprises and the only thing that catches your eye is a trail far to the east. The air is crisp and fresh.
453: From this smooth hillside you can spot a trail to the east, some smoothly sloped hills to the north and foothills to the west. Travelling looks slightly harder in the foothills, albeit it does seem to offer an abundance of wildlife. To the south more hillsides can be seen.
454: You are standing on a small round hill, which lies among gently rolling foothills. To the west you can make out a trail, to the north you see plains and beyond them, more hills. Looking east you see hills that stretch around to the southeast. Quite a few bushes make out excellent hiding places for small animals and birdnests. You spot another trail directly south of here.
455: A fat rabbit is here, chewing on some grass.

You have entered a part of the plains that is covered in tall, lush grass. Northward the grassy plains becomes partly overcome by rocks and boulders of all sizes. Hills start to form, making the land harder to travel to the south and several miles to the east as well. Many smaller birds and even an occasional predator flies about in the air, concentrated to some area west of here.
456:
A brown fox is here, looking for some rabbits to chew up.
A rabbit is here eyeing your presence warily.
A sharp-eyed hawk is here stalking some prey.
A fat rabbit sits here, chewing on some grass.

Wild fields of wheat, unattended and overgrown with weeds dominate the landscape here. Birds are having a paradise. Small vermin scuttle across below the plants and birds of all sizes and variations fly above. A large monolithic boulder sits in the centre of the wheat field. The boulder makes an excellent watch point for large predators that are hunting smaller game.
457: A line of limestone streaks across the hillside, a mere twelve feet long and barely two feet across. Several small rocks have broken off and lie at the base of the hill. The hills continue to grow and more limestone can be seen to the north. Vast grasslands lead out of the hills to the west, while smooth hills can be seen to the east and south.
458: Varied bushes and trees dot the hillsides. Signs of wildlife abound. Tracks, trails, and chewed plants can easily be found. Sounds fill the air. These smaller hills slope down to a wide plain to the east. Hills rise to new heights to the northwest.
459: Intermittent streaks of limestone break up the grassy hillsides. Several rocks have split from the rock, tumbling into the gullies. Flowers sprout from the edges of the torn up ground, where the grass does not choke them off. Thick brush grows along the base of the hills. The ground rises to the northeast where a vast grassland begins.
460: A wolf cub happily plays here.

Large gaping wounds of limestone streak across the lush grass hills. Deep gashes have been made by rushing rain waters. Bushes have found the edges favourable for growth. Game trails meander through the brush, crisscrossing the hill sides. The hills continue to the east and south, and the land rises to the north.
461: A small termite is running around making strange sounds.

Many shallow ravines cross the hills, granting passage to the water that has eroded the hills to the north and west. Lush carpets of grass cover the hills between the crevasses. Varied flowers have managed to find their place in the sun. The hills become smoother to the south, which meet with a large plain to the east.
462: A robin is here, carrying small pieces of wood to its nest.

Various kinds of grass grow in clumps or near larger stones. Weeds are numerous among the collections of rocks. More plains covered with rocks can be travelled to the west. East and south the terrain consists of green grassy fields. A shallow dingle filled with swaying grass lies to the north.
463: Rocks, boulders and stones of all sizes dot these lush grasslands. Moss and grass partially conceals many of them. Small animal trails lie scattered across the ground. The rocky fields come to an abrupt end to the northeast. The rolling plains continue far to the east, south and west. A line of trees indicate the beginnings of a forest to the northwest.
464: In this high growing wild grass, many tall and thick spots can be seen, where the grass has grown together in clumps. A couple of trees are spread out in the grassland. A large forest grows to the north and west and a trail leads around the forest to the west as well as to the south. Rocks, boulders and smaller stones are strewn all over these grasslands.
465: A squirrel scampers around here, looking for nuts from the trees.

This is the border of a forest. The trees are randomly spread out, impairing movement. Most of the trees are old and are now stretching high into the sky. Bushes and other smaller plants grow in-between the scattered trees. A small trail leads off to the west, where the forest also seems to be denser.
466:
A small, dense tangle of roots covers the ground.
A large elk is standing here, chewing grass and leaves.

The old trees grow very dense here, the crowns almost blocking out all light from above. The underbrush is sparse and consists mainly of leaves, broken branches and dead fallen trees. Small game trails can be seen darting between the many trees. The forest continues all around, however, the trees seem to grow closer together to the west.
467: A stocky mountain mule is here, waiting to serve.

You stand in a mixed grove of chestnut and oak trees. A thin, whispering sound fills your ears, apparently just the wind stirring the upper twigs and branches of these tall beeches. The grove extends east and north, while a path can be seen curving around it to the south and west.
468: A robin is here, carrying small pieces of wood to its nest.

You stand in the northern part of a grove of beeches, tall oak trees with thick-set trunks and boughs with a multitude of branches. The undergrowth partially covers the many interlacing roots, making it easy to trip and fall if you are unwary. You spy a path though the trees to your north and west.
469: A large rabbit looks peacefully at you, ready to dart away.

The limbs of the giant oak trees interlace above, forming a canopy. Little underbrush manages to grow here, as the canopy of leaves blocks most of the sunlight. The ground is thickly covered with fallen leaves and an almost constant rustling fills the air as the forest wildlife goes about its business. The woods continue to the west and east but a trail lies to the north. Southward lies the oldest part of the forest.
470: A sparrow is flapping around on the ground.

The forest consists of oaks and many varieties of fir trees. Broad trunks reach far into the sky, their interlaced branches creating a thick canopy. Light seems to penetrate due to the fact that there still is plenty of undergrowth surviving along the ground. Travel is much easier along the base of the pine trees, where the fallen needles have made it difficult for other plants to grow. The forest seems to grow even deeper to the west. However, a wide plain can be seen through the trees to the north and east.
471: Ancient oak trees spread their branches in an almost grabbing fashion. They mark this forest as very old. Some underbrush is evident, but most of it has been eaten by animals. A big owl's nest is prominent in one of the trees. The forest grows thicker and darker the more west you go.
472: Lush grass grows all around with small area apparently having been grazed upon. Flowers reach skyward, long stems holding them up towards the sun. Game trails dart in and out of the many bushes growing upon the plains. A forested areas begins close to the north and west, while the grasslands continue far to the south and east.
473: A brown fox is here, looking for some rabbits to chew up.

Long grass covers the area, providing effective cover for the local fauna. Few trees have been able to take root and survive. One ancient oak spreads it branches over the plains. The grasses stretch across the ground between a series of hills to the southeast and a forest to the northwest. Grasslands can be seen stretching far to the north and south.
474: A large rabbit looks peacefully at you, ready to dart away.

Foot high wild grass covers the land for as far as the eye can see. These mainly flat grasslands continue in all directions except north. A dell between several hills hides a vast amount of young oak trees to the north. Smaller field animals roam the grass-covered lands at free will.
475: A fat rabbit is here, chewing on some grass.

In a shallow depression, weeds and bushes grow in a dense clump. The wind does not penetrate the thick brush. The occasional limestone rock breaks up the otherwise flat grasslands. Hilly terrain to the east and south begins a descent to the coastal plains of the gulf of Luhn. Grasslands continue to the north and west.
476: Deep crevasses cut through the hills, revealing the white limestone lying beneath the green hills. Trees grow sparsely, but flowers and bushes have found purchase along the newly exposed ground near the ravines. A lush carpet of grass covers the plains to the north and west, while a series of hills can be seen to the south. More hills can be seen to the east.
477: The broken limestone ridge separates the lowland plains to the east from the high plains to the northwest. Varied bushes provide cover for the various animals that inhabit the local area. Bare patches of solid limestone sit intermixed with areas covered with plant life. A trail circles around this rocky patch of ground from the south to the east.
478: A large rabbit looks peacefully at you, ready to dart away.

The land gently drifts up and down, slowly, gently. Grasses completely cover the ground, patches of large bushes and a few isolated trees manage to keep the view from becoming monotonous. Once in a while, a small mound of dirt stands alone, announcing the home of some burrowing animal. The plains seem endless and continue on far to the north and west.
479: An elk cow gazes coldly at you, chewing on a small branch.

An egg shaped bump of limestone has forced its way to the surface. A small strip of stone stretches across the plains, almost 100 yards long, creating an small area where the grass refuses to grow. A large patch of bushy vegetation has found a home, where the limestone has channelled the rain water. A single tree has found a place to plant its roots along this bald spot, providing shade during the afternoon. A few other trees can be spotted along the grass covered plains.
480: Thick, long, wavy grasses lead up to this sinkhole. Grasses continue growing along the sides. Thick brush grows amongst a tumble of boulders gathered at the bottom. The grasslands continue on in all directions. The plains are broken up by scattered trees and large clumps of brush.
481: A twisted pine stands writhing in pain. The trunk bends with unusual angles, the branches stretch from awkward angles. A few well-developed boughs seem to provide the tree with enough enrichment to survive. The grassy fields provide a comforting contrast to the ancient trees. The plains give way to a rocky limestone outcroppings to the south and east.
482: Fir-trees lie scattered throughout the limestone outcroppings. They have found cracks in the ground to plant their roots in. The roots of one large tree has split one of the larger boulders. Ferns, small berry bushes and many climbing vines cover the ground following the furrows of soil between the limestone rocks. This is a range of hills going from the south to the north, splitting the flat plains east and west of here in two parts.
483:
A huge, black wolf is here, ready to devour.
A black wolf pads restlessly, looking for its next prey.
A black wolf pads restlessly, looking for its next prey.

This valley splits the range of hills that goes from the south into the north. The stone bed floor of the valley completely covers up the once free flowing stream. Water still flows beneath the rocks and stones, having carved out a tiny new canyon of its own. The tracks of many small animals can be seen crossing through the light silt that has gathered on the stones all around. The land rises to the north and south, but hints of a vast plain can be seen through the jagged limestone peaks to the east and west.
484: A stream flows down from the foothills, the water splitting apart, with some flowing into the grasslands to the south. Most of the flow continues to the east. Large quantities of shrubs and bushes grow tightly together on the southern bank, nourished by the fresh stream water. A line of hills gathers around the quiet plains to the north and west.
485: All sorts of bushes, ferns and other low growing plants completely cover the ground. The ground is saturated with water flowing out of the hills to the northeast. Puddles of shallow water lie in shallow places upon the earth. A few large prints can be seen in the soft dirt. Some large animal has been chewing on the local foliage.
486: Deep gullies dig into the plains above, revealing many layers of limestone. Thick grass grows along the grooves cut into the stone, where eroded topsoil has settled. Limestone rocks litter the bottom making travel difficult. The hillside continues to the west, the way obscured by the rough terrain. A faint trail follows along the north-south ridge to the east.
487: The grasses flow gently with the passing winds, while the bushes bend towards the ground when the wind picks up. A few trees stand strong, but a groan can be heard on an occasion. The fields flow gently downhill to the southeast, where they quickly give way to an eroding hillside. A great view of the coastal plains of the Gulf of Lhun can be seen from the edge of the hills.
488: A large rabbit looks peacefully at you, ready to dart away.

Ancient furrows lie covered in weeds, while briars grow freely on the formerly bare earth. A pile of sod lies near a circle of stones protecting a circle of ashes. Wild grasses have begun to cover the clearing, similar to the way they have almost completely covered an ancient trail leading towards a series of hills in the south. The flatness of the plains continues on in all other directions, infrequently pierced by a lonely tree.
489: Vegetation has found few places to flourish within these limestone hills. A few bushes have found pooled topsoil to spread their roots. The thick grasses from the plains above grows in clumps. The slowly eroding plains abruptly end here, descending to coastal plains of the Gulf of Lhun. The limestone ridge continues to the south and east.
490: The smoothly flowing grasses of the highland plains end along the northern and eastern edges of this field. Erosion has cut many grooves through the rich dirt, revealing the crumbling limestone that decorates the hills along the edge of the plains. A few trees have managed to climb into the sky despite the constant battle with the winds. Bushes grow in large clumps all along the plains to the west and south.
491: Deep crevices slice through the limestone, created by torrents of water rushing down from the mountains far to the northwest. Small boulders and rocks lie scattered about, left there when the swiftly flowing waters finally subsided. Roots of many large bushes reach deep into the ground, the upper areas brazenly exposed to the elements.
493: The hills rise in height the further west you travel. Far off to the west you can see that the hills have turned into a small mountain peak. A trail made for easy travel has been made to the east of here. The lands are very fertile here making it a good place for wildlife.
495: Grass grows all over these hills, as do trees. The trees do not grow together in a forest but instead are randomly spread around in small groves. This gives the region a strange unfinished look. To the east the hills become a large stone plateau. More hills cover the land to the south.
496:
A roe deer is standing here, watching the terrain while chewing the vegetation.
A fat rabbit sits here, chewing on some grass.

Thick clumps of grass protected by briars lie scattered throughout the grazed plains. A few round brown platters can be seen sitting on the ground. Wild grasses grow thicker to the south and east. A few lonely trees stand against the cold wind gusts that comes swirling down from the heights of the Blue Mountains to the northwest. A trail can be seen west of here.
497: Blades of the long grass lie pointing to the south. The winds blow down from the Blue Mountains far to the northwest. The land gently rolls with the winds in all directions. A few trees stand alone facing the weather. Various bushes create the only true windbreaks along these highland plains.
498: A large rabbit looks peacefully at you, ready to dart away.

Small brown lumps of dirt pockmark the surface of the plains. Tiny dirt covered trails dart in and out of the clumps of grass. Large bushes lie gathered together against the winds. A few trees stand defiant, their branches dipping and rising with the winds. The plains continue on in all directions.
499: A large pool of mud occupies this small clearing in the bushes. A ancient oak sprouts from its banks, and in return provides protection from the sun. Holly bushes surrounds what must have been a pond at one time. The plains continue on towards the northwest, trees occasionally defying the winds. The lands slowly dip to the east, where a line of hill tops create a jagged horizon.
500: The tall grass lies along the ground in large gathered clumps. The blades point south towards the warmer climates. A few trees have managed to stand strong against the winds that buffet these high plains. The land slowly rises to the northwest and falls away to the southeast, where a line of hills break up the horizon.
501: A sparrow is flapping around on the ground.

A small patch of ground lies barren. The grasses grow thick around the edges, with bushes gathering around. Nothing grows in the centre and the dirt lies exposed. The rolling fields stretch far to the horizons, meeting a series of hills far to the east.
502: The corpse of a small termite is lying here.

The grass grows short and the bushes seem stunted, however, the soil appears to be very dark and rich. Grasses flow along the plains, quietly swept by the wind. A stream meanders its way through the grasses, having started somewhere to the east and quietly making its way to the hills in the southeast. Hills carved by this and other similar streams decorate the horizon to the east.
503: Limestone has melted away, creating a deep fissure in the plains above. The sides of the crevice are irregular, containing many pockets. Bushes try in vain to secure their roots to the crumbling rock. The canyon narrows to the west, but begins to reveal a pattern of rocky outcroppings to the east. Steep limestone walls make it difficult to discern the terrain to the north and south.
504: A huge boulder sits alone in a field of grass. No moss grows upon it, but there are some dark stains on the eastern edge. At six feet tall, the boulder demands noticing, but it seems out of place on these flat plains. A few trees stand taller than it, but most of the bushes do not even come close to the same height. It would be possible to roll it down hill to the east, but the ground slopes upwards to the north and west.
505: Several large bushes decorate the plains with a lush green, a perfect hiding place amongst the otherwise featureless plains. Tall grass leans against the base of the bushes sitting on the outer edge of this patch. Three trees sit near the middle providing a little shade. The plains are covered with fewer bushes in all directions, however, a small line of trees can be seen far to the west.
506: The plains ascend to the north, covered with cranberry bushes. Nests of birds can be seen sitting amongst the branches, cradled from the winds that sweep down off the Blue Mountains located to the northwest. The plains continue to rise in that direction. Grasses cover the land far to the east and south, but a deep forest can be seen to the southwest.
507: The magnificent scenery overwhelms you. Smooth hills descend below the tree- line to the southeast. Small yellow flowers grow in a small carpet-like patch. A trail zigzags its way to the north and west. The crest of the hill can be followed into a deep brush forest to the east.
508: A small trickle of water flows from the spring quietly to the east, following the contours of the high plains. The plains flow gently higher further to the north and west. They drop slowly until the meet a ridge of hills to the east. A few trees dot the horizon, their roots carpeted with the long grasses and varied bushes that grow freely along the plains.
509: A solitary tree stands in the middle of the plains, surrounded by a series of stumps jutting up through the tall grass. Many young saplings attempt to establish a grove of oaks, bravely standing against the highland winds. A stream, barely larger than a trickle weaves a path through the plains from east to west. The plains continue far to the north and west, covered with trees in an unorganised pattern. A dark line of hills can be seen cutting across the horizon far to the east.
510: A large rabbit looks peacefully at you, ready to dart away.

A small furrow of limestone lies exposed. Thick grasses grow right up to the edges, with some small grasses growing in the sandy soil between the ridges of stone. A small tree attempts to create roots through the southern point, while a large flowering bush occupies the other end, a scant six feet away. Gently rolling plains continue on to the east and west, but a small grove of trees can be seen far to the south.
511: This small dell is completely crowded by young oak saplings. Some short stubs of older oak trees can be seen poking through the brush all over the dell. It seems like someone may be caring for the cuttings, cutting down the old and replanting with new. The underbrush is heavy, but very little dead wood or brush can be found. Grassy plains seem to surround this small patch of oaks.
512:
A woodpecker is here, tapping on a tree.
A black snake, with red markings, is lying here.

The remnant stumps of an oak forest cover the ground. The wood breaks away freely, having been cut a long time ago. A few young saplings have taken root, but not enough to replace the forest. The forest still survives to the west. This land has become an extension of the vast grassy plains that extend far in all other directions.
513: A brown fox is here, looking for some rabbits to chew up.

Foot long grass sways back and forth in the wind. Simblemynde flowers grow in small patches scattered about. An occasional streak of limestone inhibit the growth of plants. The edge of a deep forest stretches across the horizon to the west, but the fairly flat grasslands continue in all other directions.
514:
A colourful butterfly is fluttering around here.
A prospector is walking around slowly, looking for a new ore vein to mine.

Rough, grassy hills fill the landscape in all directions. On the ground, more or less evenly distanced, you can see the entrances of a mole colony. From time to time some of the small animals poke their snout out of a hole, but immediately retreat as they perceive your presence.
515: Your journey has brought you to an area of rough, grassy hills. The wind blows through many small valleys, making strange whistling sounds. Not far to the north, you can see a large marble cliff, which seems to have been extensively mined by the Dwarves. A whiff of smoke rises into the sky from behind a hill to the northeast.
516:
A colourful butterfly is fluttering around here.
A pony is standing here, ridden by you.

The trail winds its way up into the Blue Mountains to the southwest, and descends into the valley of the Nan Duin east. Many rough foothills, which have been extensively mined by the Dwarves, surround you and block your vision of the horizon, except to the northeast, where, in the distance, you can see an isolated tower.
517: Here the trail, which runs between some foothills and a dark forest, turns north and west. Far to the north you can see a tower. The tangled greenery prevents you from entering the fear-inspiring woods to the south-east. As you try to peek inside the darkness, you suddenly see a glowing red pair of eyes. Then it is gone... or was it your imagination?
518: You are travelling through an area of rough, grassy hills at the feet of the Blue Mountains. The hills become higher to the west, while to the east the ground gently slopes down to a dense forest. You can barely see a worn, winding trail following the edge of the wood, and you wonder where it would lead you if you allowed your steps to follow it. A mine shaft descends into the darkness at your feet. You hear the noise of the Dwarven miners working below.
519: The trail countinues its long journey across the Blue Mountains to the south and to the east. The foothills to the north show extensive signs of mining operations. The Dwarves have dwelt in this region for thousands of years.
520: A pony is standing here, ridden by you.

The trail runs near the edge of a dark forest. To the south the huge trees become less dense, and you can leave the hills to enter the wood. North and west the trail continues its long journey across the Nan Duin valley. Far to the northeast, a whiff of smoke rises into the sky.
521:
A grey wolf is here, snarling aggressively.
A grey wolf is here, snarling aggressively.
A squirrel scampers around here, looking for nuts from the trees.

The huge trees here grow so thick that no light at all reaches the ground. Ominous howls echo through the woods, filling your heart with despair. You feel that some large, predatory beast wants to feed upon you. Here and there patches of grey, dead-smelling moss grow on the tree trunks. Warped, pale, almost skeletal bushes make your movement difficult.
522: The huge trees here grow so thick that no light at all reaches the ground. Ominous howls echo through the woods, filling your heart with despair. You feel that some large, predatory beast wants to feed upon you. Here and there patches of grey, dead-smelling moss grow on the tree trunks. Warped, pale, almost skeletal bushes make your movement difficult.
523: You find yourself at the edge of a large pine forest. The trees are very large, but in this place they are distanced enough to allow you to see the sky above you. Not far to the south, however, the forest becomes extremely thick and dark. Red eyes blink in the darkness, spying each move you make. To the east you can barely see a trail crossing the forest.
524: A grey wolf is here, snarling aggressively.

Small dried fallen branches and pine needles crackle as you travel through this dense forest of huge trees. Above you, a few squirrels jump from one tree to the next. You realise their presence more by hearing than by sight, as the branches are so entwined that nearly no light filters through them. To the west the forest becomes even more dense and gloomy.
525:
A squirrel scampers around here, looking for nuts from the trees.
A grey wolf is here, snarling aggressively.

You have reached a small clearing in the Narbrethil Forest. Huge pine trees surround you in all directions. As you look west and south, however, you realise that the forest is much thicker than to the east.
526: Small dried fallen branches and pine needles crackle as you travel through this dense forest of huge trees. Above you, a few squirrels jump from one tree to the next. You realise their presence more by hearing than by sight, as the branches are so entwined that nearly no light filters through them. To the north the forest becomes even more dense and gloomy.
527: You find yourself on the western corner of the huge Narbrethil Forest. Large pine trees grow here and there, and become thicker and thicker as you travel to the east. North and west of here, a worn trail flanks the forest and leads towards the Blue Mountains to the south. Some distant howls remind you that this is not a safe place to rest your tired bones.
528: A pony is standing here, ridden by you.

The trail climbs the steep slopes of the Blue Mountains to the west, and descends rapidly to the Nan Duin Valley to the north. To the east there is a light forest, while to the south you can see deer grazing in a field full of grass. Some tall pine trees grow in a double line along the trail.
529: A light, cool breeze descending from the Blue Mountains carries to your nostrils the scent of delicate flowers. Here and there you can see some deer grazing on the short grass, and a nightingale is singing from the branches of an isolated fir tree. You relax for a moment in this calm place, before climbing the mountains to the south or entering a long winding trail not far to the north.
530:
A well-fed cow stands here chewing her cud listlessly.
A well-fed cow stands here chewing her cud listlessly.
A fat rabbit sits here, chewing on some grass.
A thin, crippled deer looks around timidly.
A fallow deer is grazing peacefully here.

The plains begin to slope upwards to the south, where the Blue Mountains rise high towards the sky. A low wall of stones has been built to the east; beyond the wall the grass grows very high. To the northeast, behind the grass, you can spot a dark and forbidding forest of pine trees.
531: A thin, crippled deer looks around timidly.

You force your way through a sea of high grass, being careful not to put your foot inside one of the numerous rabbit holes that dot the ground. Some small animals run quickly among the grass, making a rustling noise. To the south the ground rises quickly towards the Blue Mountains, while to the northeast you can see a large, dense forest of pine trees.
532:
A fat rabbit is here, chewing on some grass.
A fat rabbit is here, chewing on some grass.
A fallow deer is grazing peacefully here.

You force your way through a sea of high grass, being careful not to put your foot inside one of the numerous rabbit holes that dot the ground. Some small animals run quickly among the grass, making a rustling noise. To the south the ground rises gently towards a small valley in the Blue Mountains, while to the northeast you can see a large, dense forest of pine trees. The grass becomes shorter to the east.
533: You find yourself in a dense forest of huge pine trees. The thick undergrowth hinders your movements, and the entwined branches above you cover nearly all the sky, making this a rather gloomy place. From time to time, a series of deep growls and excited howls echoes through the woods. You are not sure you wish to meet the source of the noises.
534:
A fat rabbit sits here, chewing on some grass.
A fallow deer is grazing peacefully here.
A brown fox is here, looking for some rabbits to chew up.
A colourful butterfly is fluttering around here.

You have reached the southern edge of a large pine forest. The trees are very high; squirrels jump among their branches, and hide as soon as they perceive your presence. To the west there is a field filled with very high grass; to the south, a barely visible path climbs the mountain side, bending and twisting to take advantage of the few places where the ascent is not too steep. Even so, you think it would be better to rest for a while before attempting to climb the path.
535:
A sprawling green bush of stinging nettle grows here.
An erect shrub with green pinnate leaves is growing here.
Inside the shrub, there are two piles of crimson raspberries.
A fallow deer is grazing peacefully here.

In this section of Narbrethil Forest, the huge pine trees grow far from each other, so that during daytime the light of the sun reaches the ground. Many bushes grow among the trees; a small, nearly invisible path leads east to west. The trees become much thicker to the north, where a barrier of living wood prevents you from reaching the heart of the forest, and to the west.
536: In this section of Narbrethil Forest, the huge pine trees grow far from each other, so that during daytime the light of the sun reaches the ground. Many bushes grow among the trees; a small, nearly invisible path leads east to west. The trees become much thicker to the north, where a barrier of living wood prevents you from reaching the heart of the forest.
537:
A rabbit is here eyeing your presence warily.
A rabbit is here eyeing your presence warily.
A rabbit is here eyeing your presence warily.

In this section of Narbrethil Forest, the huge pine trees grow far from each other, so that during daytime the light of the sun reaches the ground. Many bushes grow among the trees; a small, nearly invisible path leads east to west. The trees become much thicker to the north, where a barrier of living wood prevents you from reaching the heart of the forest.
538: In this section of Narbrethil Forest, the huge pine trees grow far from each other, so that during daytime the light of the sun reaches the ground. Many bushes grow among the trees; a small, nearly invisible path leads east to west. The trees become much thicker to the north, where a barrier of living wood prevents you from reaching the heart of the forest, and to the east.
539: You find yourself in a dense forest of huge pine trees. The thick undergrowth hinders your movements, and the entwined branches above you cover nearly all the sky, making this a rather gloomy place. A light breeze carries the scent of mushrooms from the north.
540:
There are two mushrooms here.
You see two bright red mushrooms on the ground.

This section of Narbrethil Forest is filled with mushrooms. Mushrooms of all sizes and descriptions grow everywhere: bright red or dull brown on the ground, small yellow-green mushrooms on the trunks and on the branches of the huge pine trees. Unfortunately, many of the fungi are poisonous. To the north and east a trail flanks the forest, while to the south the trees become thicker.
541:
A colourful butterfly is fluttering around here.
A fallow deer is grazing peacefully here.

A large pine forest grows northwest of here. The trees are not very thick, so that you can clearly see the sky, and amid the undergrowth you recognise many strawberry bushes. To the south the trees gradually become even less dense, until the forest gives way to the grassy slopes of the Blue Mountains.
542:
A beautiful and docile horse is standing here.
A rabbit is here eyeing your presence warily.

The ground here slopes steeply, forcing you to zigzag if you want to climb up to the mountains or down to the bottom of the Nan Duin Valley, where a grassy field flanks a large pine forest. You take a deep breath and continue your long journey.
543: A robin is here, carrying small pieces of wood to its nest.

You find yourself on the slopes of the Blue Mountains, south of the valley of the Nan Duin. A small twisting path leads east through the mountains, and north towards a large pine forest. To the west the ground slopes down to a grassy plain, while to the south you can see the entrance of a Dwarven mine. It seems to have been abandoned: you can see no miners around, and a deadly silence fills the place.
544: There are two short flowers, with purple blooms here.

The snow-capped peaks of the Blue Mountains surround you on all sides, except to the north, where a small, nearly invisible path leads towards a large pine forest. The flanks of the mountain are covered with grass and small bushes; some goats are grazing nearby.
545: You are at the entrance of a long tunnel, supported by strong-looking timbers of typical dwarven make. You immediately notice that something is amiss: the timbers and the granite walls bear black scorches, as if a searing flame had touched them for an instant. In one place the timbers have been so severely damaged that part of the ceiling has collapsed. On the ground, at your feet, lies the charred skeleton of a Dwarf. The tunnel continues to the east.
546:
An iron pick has been dropped here.
A dirty shovel is lying on the ground here.
A small bat is standing here.
A small bat is standing here.

You have reached the end of the abandoned mine. To the west, the tunnel climbs up towards the surface. Some fire-consumed mining gear lies here. As you inspect the walls of the tunnel, you realise that the iron ore vein which attracted the Dwarves to this place is far from being exhausted. The black scorches on the timbers are not likely to have been caused by an accident, otherwise the stubborn Dwarves would have returned.
547: Layers of lively grass fill out the landscape. A group of deer carefully meander along, chewing on the grass. Squirrels run up and down a tree branch playfully. You take a stretch and enjoy the beauty nature offers you. The grass grows tall and unhindered, as the breeze blows past, the stalks brush against each other in a symphony of rustling sounds. A trail is clearly marked to the north, while to the east there is more grass.
548:
A sturdy pack horse is standing here.
A small grasshopper clings to a blade of grass, ready to spring.

A small pile of logs and debris litter the centre of the clearing. A fire once burned here, but as you feel the cold ashes you realise, it must have been in the distant past. Nothing else is remarkable about the small clearing. To the north and east you can detect a hard dirt trail leading through the forest. To the south though, a pile of boulders interspersed with the trees make that direction not an option.
549: A rabbit is here eyeing your presence warily.

Short grass and colorful flowers grow all around you and make you feel at ease. You stop for a moment and relax, watching the beautiful butterflies flying between the flowers and some bouncing rabbits chewing the grass. Not far to the north you can see a large forest, while the mountains to the south are too steep to climb.
550:
A rabbit is here eyeing your presence warily.
A large eagle soars above you.
A fat rabbit sits here, chewing on some grass.

Short grass and colorful flowers grow all around you and make you feel at ease. You stop for a moment and relax, watching the beautiful butterflies flying between the flowers and some fat rabbits chewing the grass. Not far to the north you can see a large forest, while the mountains to the south are too steep to climb.
551:
There are two piles of wild strawberries here.
A fallow deer is grazing peacefully here.
A brown fox is here, looking for some rabbits to chew up.

You have reached the southern edge of a large pine forest. The trees are very high; squirrels jump among their branches, and hide as soon as they perceive your presence. The smell of resin and of wild berries fills the air. South of you the Blue Mountains ascend steeply; you stop for a while, contemplating their snow covered peaks.
552:
An albino fish is swimming here, looking for some food.
An albino fish is swimming here, looking for some food.

The cave is dimly lit with an eerie yellow-green light emitted by glowing mosses growing on the walls. Huge stalagmites rise from the cavern floor, forming a maze of pillars. Following the sound of dripping water, you find a large, dark pool beneath a cluster of lichen-encrusted stalactites.
553:
A fragrant smelling bag is lying here.
A large bundle of pale yellow fur is here.
A woodman's axe lies here.

You are squatting inside a small space which seems to be used as a storage chamber for a hunter. It might even be used as a hideaway, if such a thing should be needed in this quiet region. Pelts and hides from lions, wolves and bears lie stacked innermost, and some forestry and hunting equipment is heaped by your feet.
554:
A dense carpet of blue flowers dip their heads in the breeze.
A brown pond between old branches and roots is here.

In the midst of the grove stands an old and crooked rowan, shedding its leaves into a small pond by its feet. Also by the pond lies some crude, chalk-white slates covered with golden hair, the hair of mountain lions. Spread out around a huge uprooted stump to the east, is a circle of blue violets.
555: You are walking on the treshold of a green grove of rowan trees. A rocky ridge borders it to the south and east, and north of it lies a tall, bracken-covered hill. From here you can follow a valley westwards or move to the centre of the grove to the east.
556: A stocky mountain mule is here, waiting to serve.

This valley floor is draped with dense green shrubbery and sprinkled with a few thickets of maple shrubs. A path is swallowed by the shrubbery as it dives into it from the west. Following the valley east, you will reach a solitary grove of trees protected by the embrace of the ridge to the south.
557: You are on a faint path which here rounds the western edge of a jagged ridge. There is valley not far below you to the west, but far enough to make your fall a lethal one, should you get the notion to try descent. The path fades away as it cuts in between the ridge and hills eastwards.
558:
A small and well-kept fire lights and warms the room.
There are two mushrooms here.
A tall and hardened man sits here, whittling a piece of wood.

Someone has recently moved into this cave. The walls have been carven with a much more careful hand than the water that eroded this cavern long ago. The walls are bare of dirt and fungus, except for one corner in which several large, and apparently edible, mushrooms grow. Various shelves and drawers and chairs, all made skillfully from wood, adorn this chamber. On the ground, next to a bed of moss, lies a very large bear-skin carpet.
559: Moss covers the ground at your feet, and it grows thicker towards the entrance of a cave to the east. In this moss you see some heavy footprints, leading to a door of pine. North are the outskirts of a pine-forest.
560: A forest spider is here crawling around.

Your feet make crispy noises treading the brittle undergrowth in this narrow vale. Steep hillsides covered by moss and vines leads you in a north-south direction, and the convex shapes of hills to your north block all view of what might lie beyond. To the south the valley leads out into a light forest.
561: A narrow track leads through this uniform forest of birches. To the north, where the ground has an upward-sloping tendency, there is a thinning out of the black and white trunks. West of here a tangled web of shrubs blocks the way. You might follow the path north or south from here, or force your way through the dense foliage to the east.
562: Here stand slender, young birches, lesser trees which one day will grow as tall as those in the more robust forest east and south. Northward, the forest bows to tall hills through which a narrow vale cuts like a gaping wound. The opposite way lies a forest clearing, obviously man-made.
563: You are on the eastern fringe of a grassy field. Here trees surround you to your south and east. Tall birches stand as pale sentinels on both sides of a carved, wooden arch which marks the beginning of a track leading south into the forest.
564: A robin is here, carrying small pieces of wood to its nest.

A rough path leads you around the snow-capped peaks of the Blue Mountains, and west into a small valley. The ground is nearly barren: only a few patches of grass and some small bushes grow here and there.
565: You are at the bottom of a small grassy valley in the Blue Mountains. A narrow path, which has nearly been hidden by the vegetation, leads to the mountains around you. As you gaze around, you see that to the north, where the ground descends gently, the grass becomes very high; beyond the high grass there is a large pine forest. To the south, after a steep ascent, lies a small gap in the mountains.
566: Mountainous hills surround you, making the uneven track you are following invaluable in keeping a steady direction. The track crawls steadily on in in a north-south direction, with any sight of what lies ahead obscured by the wayside slopes.
567: Looking out across this peaceful farmland, you see herds of sheep grazing quietly and untended. A high fence runs east-west a small march to your north. You can also spot a small track between the hills in that direction.
568: A nightingale is here, chirping a sweet melody.

A rough path leads you around the snow-capped peaks of the Blue Mountains, and east into a small valley. The ground is nearly barren: only a few patches of grass and some small bushes grow here and there.
569:
A woody evergreen plant grows here, with many stems reaching upward.
A rabbit is here eyeing your presence warily.

A small path winds its way through the snow-capped peaks of the Blue Mountains. This place is nearly barren; only a few small patches of grass grow among the rocks. A high pitched whistle breaks the silence when you reach a turn in the path. Perhaps it is a marmot, fearing for the safety of its home.
570: A large ram guards his flock of sheep.
These sloping hills are covered with fences, probably used by farmers as pasture during summer. North of you the Blue Mountains rise above the hills, where dwarves are rumoured to have built a city.
571: A clear spring babbles as cool water trickles out of the ground.
Here lies a stretch of farmland wedged between the hills of the Blue Mountains. A high fence can be seen a couple of stone throws away in all directions except east, where more fields lie.
572: Apparently these fields are being used for grazing a local farmer's livestock, a small herd of sheep. A stout fence has been built to the north side of the pasture, perhaps to protect the animals from the large carnivores, which must live in the mountainous country beyond.
573:
A woolly sheep is grazing here.
A woolly sheep is grazing here.

You are on the southern boundary of a wide field of grass. A fence blocks the way west of you, but a slim gate, only wide enough for a man to pass through, has been put into the fence just here. Several oak branches are used to block the gate, and inspecting it closer, you see obvious strain in both the branches and the gate. A string of feathers, animal bones and bits of furs hang on top of the gate, out of your reach.
574: You are on a path which doesn't seem to be much in use. Southwards it leads into the hills of the Blue Mountains, while east it dissolves more or less at a solid-looking gate which doesn't seem openable from this side. A grisly wolf skull has been pinned to the top of the gate.
575: You stand on a hillside some way above a small path which is twisting and twining its way through the uneven terrain. Your feet wade through rugged brush, making sounds like the crackle of a cheery campfire. You can re-enter the path south or west, depending on which way you are bound.
576: The path winds through these morose hills spellbound by the shadows of huge mountains in the west. It is possible to ascend some way up in the hillsides to the east, or you may elect to follow the path north or south.
577:
A woolly sheep is grazing here.
A woolly sheep is grazing here.

You tread soft grass, seeing nothing but fields to your north and west. Likewise, east and south is nothing but a dense wall of trees. Gaining access to the forest from this spot is seemingly impossible, but you think you can spot a break in the forest a little further northeast.
578: You stand on a small avenue which has been cleared through a forest of tall birches. The avenue leads out of the gloomy forest light to you north, through a masterfully carved wooden arch. Going forth south into deeper forest will lead you who knows where, but the makers of this avenue must obviously be civilised creatures.
579: You stand in a field of tree trunks, some of them uprooted. Thick logs lie stacked in a pile, the stack being held in place by beams driven into the ground at the base of it. Movement north and south are your only alternatives, the forest in other directions being too dense.
580: The track ends on the threshold of a lone cabin. The small abode is completely surrounded by the forest on all sides except where the track you are on comes to meet it. The green door, inset with a tiny window not much bigger than a peephole, is standing half ajar, welcoming you to step inside.
581:
A wooden stool sits in the corner.
A simple wooden chest is here.
An elven woman of indeterminate age assesses you with a stern look.

This is a cosy living room, readily revealing the occupation of its inhabi- tants. In a corner there stands a spinning wheel and a stool, and on the floor beside the wheel lies a bundle of the finest wool. Different-colour yarns are stacked in another corner, above which hangs a shelf with cans containing strange substances. Among the other furniture you notice a chest containing wool sweaters and other knitwear. Oddly enough, the only window in this room is a big glass window put between two of the ceiling support beams, providing rich light on a sunny day.
582: This is a modest room, divided into two parts, kitchen and bedchamber. By the kitchen table stands a cabinet filled with various plates and cutlery. A bench and stove for food-preparation are also present. Should you feel tired, lay down and relax on the double bed at the other end of the room, and there is also a bathtub in one corner, which you could use to get that black grime off your body.
583: A nightingale is here, chirping a sweet melody.

The path climbs up to the top of a bluff hillside. Turning north, you see fields dotted white with flocks of what must be sheep. Eastward a forest rests its huge bulk, continuing almost out of eyesight. The path meanders west into the hills, and south it crosses a small valley stream on its way to the top of a rotund hill.
584: You walk on a small path between dreary hills, looking intently for life somewhere in the rippling landscape. Far away, you can hear a dulin sing, and unseen creatures scuttle through the dense undergrowth. East and west the path leads on.
585: At this point the craggy slopes to your west force the path to turn north and east. A scree has dispatched a jumble of rocks onto the path, making riding impossible. Below a small bush wedged between rocks to your west, you notice a faint discolouration on the stones.
586: You are following a rarely used path climbing up to a pale hill in the east. Southward the path descends to level terrain, grassy fields held captive by the forest in the east and the watchful hills in the north, west and south. Farther west, the Blue Mountains points its snowy fingers to the heavens.
587: On this rocky height nothing grows but stubbled grass. The ground is strewn with boulders and slabs of granite, huge rock relics unmoved since the ending of the second age of the sun. The grinning streak of a ravine lies some way to the north, while south the hill drops sharply down to lower slopes.
588: You stand on top of a hill, a good lookout point to the rural landscape surrounding you. The forest lies dense to the northeast, east and southeast, only broken by freckles of grassland. A strange sight in the lowlands to the south is a circle of monolithic stones. No descent to the forest or the plains is possible; you can only follow the path north or west through the hills.
589: You stand on a slope slowly ascending from the grasslands to the south. Up north, the path climbs steeper into rugged hills, while south you see the path curving to your left. You can also make your way east, along the sides of the hills to the north.
590: The hillside ends abruptly at a tall rockface which tilts slightly out the top. You spot several bird nests in small niches in the rock high above your head. Looking directly south across the fields, you see some upturned slabs of rock forming a circle; lowering your gaze you see two paths come together in the fields below.
591: You stand on a hillside some way above a plain. The ascending slopes to the north are too steep for climbing, forcing you either to follow the angled terrain west or retreat to a path down on the plain south of here. Looking east, you see a line of marshy grassland almost totally obscured by the surrounding forest.
592: The forest rim to the south follows this path east and west. Westward the forest vanishes in the face of a plain, and north lies an increasingly steep hillside. To the northeast the path, accompanied by an avenue of moist grass, climbs into a forest-dominated area.
593: You are on a green-gowned plain, ornamented with patches of golden flowers. A path barely visible in the high grass comes from the west, while another one enters the plain from the forest in the east. The two paths team up to make a trail south to a strange formation of stone.
594: A large eagle soars above you.

You are on the western edge of a fertile plain. To the west lies the domain of eagles and goats, brash mountains with peaks covered by eternal snow. The smaller shapes of hills spread out to the north. A small path here provides passage into the hills, while east it will take you towards the forest on the other side of the plain.
595: You have entered a valley secluded by vertical cliffsides in all directions but to the north. In the middle of this valley someone has created an eerie circular stone formation. Seven crude arches of grey rock are facing you, each covered with runes illuminated by a strange, internal light. Various scenes have been carved into the stones.
596: The walls of black rock in this corridor seems to absorb every ray of light coming from the outside. Every sound, however insignificant, echoes between the sheer black stone all around you. The floor is even and easy to walk on, and there seems to be a corridor leading south but it is impossible to tell what lies there.
597: Two smudged wall mirrors have been mounted on the west and south wall of this dark hallway. Broken glass lie scattered on the ground, although none of the mirrors appear to be damaged. The rough stone floor is warm to the touch, and a waft of hot air, reminiscent of a dry desert breeze, circulates the hallway. The corridor turns north and east from here.
598: Blocks of quartz have been used as building stones for the walls of this chamber. A red flame burns from a wall socket, its flickering light sending dark shadows dancing across the blue-black wall surfaces. A narrow stairwell leads down through a rectangular opening in the floor.
599: A dark intangible shadow turns to face you.

You have entered an ancient place of worship or sacrifice. In the centre of this clearing stands a huge stone bowl supported by four skull-shaped pedestals. Broken skulls and bones litter the bowl, and from a small round hole a strange black smoke emanates. A masked face is depicted on the rock- face to the south.
600:
Some thick writhing vines whip all around you.
A tree-snake lies wrapped around one of the tree branches.
A tree-snake lies wrapped around one of the tree branches.

This place looks like an abomination of nature, a chaotic parade of misshapen vegetation. Gnarled roots entangle your feet, stooping trees stretch bent limbs towards the ground, and thick, foul-scented vines cover the cliff wall to the south. Through a break in the trees to the west, you see something dark rising towards the sky.
601: You are in really rough forest now. The soil underfoot is dry, and in effect weary and bent trees appear to the south along with withered ash bushes, obstructing any advance in that direction. Going back north now seems to be your only alternative.
602:
A huge grizzly bear is here, roaming the wild.
A grizzly cub is here, snarling loudly.

The conical shapes of tall, elegant firs are all around you, and nothing else. It is not easy to keep directions, but you notice that the ground rises slightly southwards. You can hear crows and croons from several birds, but you see no signs of movement anywhere.
603: This east-west path trudges in the midst of wet-soiled grass, which in turn is surrounded by dense forest to the north and south. Looking downhill to the southwest, you see some plains in the distance, while east you see a tiny lake by the path.
604: Here the swampy terrain makes leaving the path a treacherous affair. A dry patch of moss gives you a chance to go north into the woods, but following the path east or west looks more inviting. North of east you see the muddy marsh envelop a tiny lake.
605: At this point the path rounds the southeastern corner of a baby lake, ovally shaped and not much larger than a pool. Some of its water is drained by a small brook running southeast into the forest. There being no possible entry into the forest here, your only choice is to follow the path north or west through the marsh.
606: On the Shore of a Lake

You are close to the northeastern shore of a very small lake. The ground is wet and spongy, and on the opposite side of the lake it looks even worse. To get there you must follow the path south, lest you wish to ascend the path northeast to drier land. As for the forest lying in all other directions, one visible entry point can be discerned to the north.
607:
A huge grizzly bear is here, roaming the wild.
A grizzly cub is here, snarling loudly.

You move along a forest slope, on mossgrown ground littered with rocks covered by lichen. The ground descends sharply to the north, and the forest seems lighter in that direction. To the south, trees cling to a small ridge too erect for safe ascent.
608: You are walking on the north side of a ridge in the forest. Near the top of it a huge uprooted tree lies rotting among the pebbles and stones of a scree. To the east, where the ridge fades to nothingness, the ground drops to a lower level, as it also does northwards.
609: You are wandering in deep, dark forest. The moist forest floor has caused a layer of humus to form around the base of the trees, nourishing mushrooms and fungi. You can move in any direction, but from here every way seems just as dark and uninviting.
610: Wandering on in the monotonous landscape of firs, you almost stumble into a crevice in the undergrowth. It is only a narrow gap cutting north and south, and you can see both of its terminations from where you stand. From somewhere comes a faint whisper of running water, but around here the quietness is supreme ruler.
611: You are in a forest dominated by tall, evergreen firs. It is possible to force your way west, deeper into the forest, but it might be hard to keep your bearing in that omnipotent darkness. Through the the many trees to the east, you can see the forest humbly making way for an old path.
612: This place seems like a fortress of trees. Wherever you stand, some needled branch is bound to touch your shoulder. You see nothing of your surroundings except heavily branched fir trunks, but you should be able to press south or east to get out of this place.
613: 'For east or west all woods must fail...' goes an old traveller song, but it might seem vain to tell the one who is lost in darkness about the beauty of sunlight. And right here the forest seems to have no end, two dark walls embracing the vein of grassland on which this east-west track runs.
614: The small track crosses a small mound from which you can look down on an oval basin to the southwest, which is centred in a strip of boggy grassland lying in between the trees. You can enter the dark forest by going north or south, and eastward the track leaves down through waves of tall grass.
615: It seems entering the forest here was a waste of time. The trees stand closely massed, forcing you to turn back in the same direction from whence you came, you only gain being loose branches tangling into you clothing and equipment.
616:
The corpse of a fallow deer is lying here.
The corpse of a marten is lying here.
A tall stag is here, grazing peacefully.

Blueberry bushes grow abundantly here, covering most of the soil between the trees. A rubble occupies the south side of a nearby mound. Two small holes between the rocks are probably fox-holes, or the dens of some other animal. The way north is blocked by a dense shrubbery, but any other way will carry you on through the forest.
617: A tall stag is here, grazing peacefully.

Pine trees dominate your surroundings, and the ground is specked with needles and cones. A squirrel notices you and scramble up the nearest tree, while a roused chattering of birds spreads the message of your arrival. To the west there seems to be an increasing growth of bushes and firs, and southwards the forest dwindles.
618: A tall stag is here, grazing peacefully.

The forest does not give you much space to work your way through, and in the spaces between the trees bushes grow, some as tall as waist-high. Many times you are forced to retrace your step and try some other route. The many birds in the trees make quite a fuss over your passage.
619:
A coloured game bird is visible in the vegetation, watching you warily.
A coloured game bird is visible in the vegetation, watching you warily.
A nightingale is here, chirping a sweet melody.
A fallow deer is grazing peacefully here.

You are dwarfed by these cloud-climbing giants among trees. These must be descendants of the mighty brethil which once grew lavishly in the forests of sunken Beleriand. A good climber would certainly be able to get a splendid view of the forest and its surroundings from one of these tree-tops.
620: You stand on the borderline between birches to the north and firs to the south. A thread of trampled undergrowth comes from the east and widens some- what as it enters the birch forest to the north. At times you spot shadowy figures moving at safe distance among the trees. To the southwest you see the tops of some trees as tall and slender as castle spires.
621: You are deep within the forest. A plentitude of firs surround a group of slim pines growing on an elevation in the terrain. The extreme density of the forest leaves you clueless as to what lies ahead, but a barely visible strip of downtrodden brush trails west.
622: You are wandering between a few of Yavanna's innumerable creations. To the west is an expanding section of birches, and southwards lie denser woods of conifers. In the brush around your feet bloom fragrant flowers from some broad-leafed herbs.
623: A domesticated pony, beast of burden to many, stands here.

You are in a dead and silent part of the forest. No wind stirs, and it is just as well, because there are no leaves to rustle, no pollen or spores to be spread. Only the dust and smothering smell of dehydrated and worm-eaten old wood can be carried on the breeze from here. Why this place has been cursed by a dry-spell you cannot tell, for most of the forest around you is in contrast luxuriously well-growing.
624: You move on into the thick forest, and soon you find yourself among maple shrubs. You cannot on your life figure out where you came from, but westish looks like the most comfortable going from here. You can spy the crest of a hill over the crowns of trees to the north.
625: North of you stands a cliff, its lower parts overgrown by the forest vege- tation, and to the west a group of stooping trees cling to the rockface. The ground is dry and dusty in place, more so to the south, where a stand of black trees can be seen.
626: The musty odour of rotten vegetation fills your nostrils. Decaying boughs and branches cover the emaciated soil. The remaining trees are just naked, blackish trunks with peeling bark or no bark at all. To the west you see more discomforting forest death, but anywhere else will take you to fresher parts of the forest.
627: A fallow deer is grazing peacefully here.

Many different sorts of trees are gathered around you. The greyish trunks of pines are the most prominent. Two young birches stand leaning against each other, and the occasional ash tree can also be spotted. Looking northeast, you see an immense oak tree, and to the south the forest opens up onto a path.
628: Here grows a lonely contingent of fragrant shrubs carrying white and blue flowers. All around it the thick forest dwells, mostly firs, but also some dry-barked pines with their few branches set high up on tall trunks. To the east the trees stand further apart than north and west. You decide it to be the easiest way out of the forest.
629: This place in the forest stands out for its ordinarity. Surrounded by a mass of trees which all looks exactly the same, you have completely lost all directional sense. You decide you can either use the sun and the moon as beacons, or just wander randomly on.
631: You stand on sloping ground, the many firs preventing a good uphill view. Looking north you get a fine view of a green vale in the forest, but the ridge across it prevents scrutiny further north or west. From a particularly crowded part of the forest, beneath a cliff to the west, you spy a spiralling band of ascending smoke.
632: You are standing in a small vale on the south side of a overgrown ridge continuing east and southwest. West of south the ridge joins a line of hills lying south of the forest. The forested hillsides to the south seems to offer a long but easy climb into those hills. You can also follow the vale east.
633: This small forest vale lies between a ridge to the north and growing hills which can be discerned some way to the south. A blanket of needles fallen from the many firs covers the stubby grass. You can follow the vale east and west from here, or ascend the fir-riddled slopes leading south.
634: The watery moss saps your strength as you move through the forest. The almost unfelt breeze sifting through the dense woods carries a faint reek of decay. To the south and west the forest seems heavier but not so troubled by dampness as here.
635: Some ugly blow-flies are buzzing around here.

You have waded into a sludgy mire. You sink knee-deep into the mud, making a sucking noise at every advancing step. A serpentine strip of muddy water rimmed by brown weeds crosses the mire, but it does not look deeper than would prevent you from crossing it to enter the forest lying eastwards.
636:
A colony of red ants is here. The ants seem to ignore you.
Some ugly blow-flies are buzzing around here.

You are standing in spacious forest by the eastern edge of a quagmire. As you study the darkening forest around you, it becomes obvious that the rough woods are impenetrable in all directions but south.
637: As you trudge along between the trees, a mound appears before you. In its side you see a round hole about four feet high, too big to be the entrance to the home of any ordinary forest animal. Peering into it you see nothing but complete darkness.
638: A mottled snake is sneaking here, ready to sink its fangs into flesh.

You have slid into what can be best described as a mud bath. Water from an underground stream must have mixed with sand and earth, and created this thick yellow-brown liquid. The slippery granite floor which caused you to fall leads up to the outside.
639: In this place the trees look to be in an ongoing battle for sunlight and space. All around, intertwining roots and branches hamper your movement. You stumble onward, trying to keep your bearings.
640: A stocky mountain mule is here, waiting to serve.

You move among prickly fir branches in the lower parts of a hillside, standing about level with the ridge crest on the other side of the vale to the north. The woodlands give way to the southwest, but still one or two fingers reach south into the hills from the giant palm of the forest.
641: The thick bushes which dominate the trail lower on the hill have completely given way here, on this steep slope. Higher up the trail, to the south of you, the path becomes a little more level, though the land there seems to slope upward from east to west, and in this rising land the track almost vanishes.
642: A large marmot is here, scurrying in between the rocks.

There is a gradual slope to these parts, leading into steeper mountains to your south. By no means as high as the mighty peaks of Ered Luin, but still formidable. Around you is flat land, some covered with grasses, other parts more sparse and rocky. The Nan Duin, or valley river, flows east-west through the region somewhere north of you. Small animals scurry around the place looking for food.
643: This large hill is not great in size, just high enough to stand above the surrounding plains. There is grass covering the mound, and some deer play happily off to one side. Just to your west, a shelf of rock has broken off, making travel down that slope impossible. Below the small cliff stands a lone farmhouse, looking neat and inhabited. You could get there by traveling northwards a bit, skirting the rocks. On the other sides of you are flat-lands.
644: A small flower grows here, with a purple bloom and wide leaves.

These are steeper slopes than other parts of the land around you, and take you high above the small hills to your north. Southwards the way is blocked by a sheet of granite rising vertically out of the ground. The chunks of rock that were part of the cliff face are littering the ground around your feet. Below you to the west, you spy a lone farmhouse, obviously inhabited as it seems to be well kept. Below you to the east, are flat fields of grass and weeds.
645: This small ridge is apparently serving the purpose of connecting two small mountain peaks. The term small is of course, in relation to the towering peaks of the Ered Luin in the west. Looking down a small path, you see below you some thin woods. By no means as thick as the forests in the northern parts of the area, it does however hold a fair number of trees. This ridge ends to your east, before plunging down a large cliff.
646:
A huge, poisonous spider is here.
A diamond-back rattlesnake is coiled here, ready to strike.
A huge, poisonous spider is here.

This pit was maybe a mine used by dwarves looking for gold or gemstones. Unfortunately, the walls of this cave do not appear any more than a reddish hardened clay. A scattering of broken tools and even a badly dented lantern litter the ground. The pit is cramped and the air still and stale.
647:
A sparrow is flapping around on the ground.
A tall stag is here, grazing peacefully.
A tall stag is here, grazing peacefully.

The path bends from north to west here. The trail looks fairly well used, and could probably lead you to some civilization. This looks like the main path used up here in Lhun for travellers. To the north-west you can see a huge gloomy forest rise, while to the east you can see plains.
648:
An apple tree with bright green leaves grows here.
On the tree's branches are three apples.
A brown donkey watches the surroundings, perhaps looking for a chance to graze.
A well-fed cow stands here chewing her cud listlessly.
A brown donkey watches the surroundings, perhaps looking for a chance to graze.
A brown donkey watches the surroundings, perhaps looking for a chance to graze.
A rooster is resting here.
A well-fed cow stands here chewing her cud listlessly.
A hen sits here, keeping her eggs warm.
A hen sits here, keeping her eggs warm.
A hen sits here, keeping her eggs warm.

The pasture is rich in grass. Perfect for the livestock the farmer keeps. A small farmhouse is to the south, neatly kept and sturdy. A little shed is attached to the west wall of the dwelling, probably for storage of farming supplies. Flowers grow next to the fence-posts, the only place a cow cannot stick its big head. Through the fence, flat lands of rolling hills and wavy grass can be seen.
649:
A small oaken table has been set here.
On the table, there are a butcher knife, a pan, and a spoon.
A peaceful farmer is here, whistling merrily.

This is a simple farmhouse, not heavy on the decoration. Opting instead for practical items to lay about, you sense a hardworking family lives here. A butterchurn stands in the corner, and several pairs of old worn-out boots lie just inside the door. Dishes are stacked on the table, and you can see food goods lining the pantry. There is a small shed out the door to the west, while to the north you can enter a pasture through another door.
650:
A large torch lies here among the dust.
A dented pail has been carelessly left here.
A dirty shovel is lying on the ground here.
The farmer's wife is bustling busily around.

Just a simple shed, used for storing farming supplies. Rakes and hoes are hanging on the wall, along with shovels of various sizes. A metal bucket sits unused in the corner. A narrow door leads out the east wall of the place, probably into the farmhouse you saw earlier.
651:
A huge, smoking campfire is burning here.
A placid pond is here, inviting you to take a refreshing drink.

A small clearing in the trees provides a perfect place for this camp to have been set up. A large circular site for campfires is located just off centre and is surrounded by ample area for travellers to set up camp. A small pond offers fresh water and a place to wash up and fill your skins.
652: Massive trees appear in every direction, their trunks dominating entire directions. For the most part you cannot see their tips, and are astounded at how long they must have been here. Forest murmurs in all directions keep you aware that you are not alone.
653: Massive trees appear in every direction, their trunks dominating entire directions. For the most part you cannot see their tips, and are astounded at how long they must have been here. Forest murmurs in all directions keep you aware that you are not alone.
