654: Massive trees appear in every direction, their trunks dominating entire directions. For the most part you cannot see their tips, and are astounded at how long they must have been here. Forest murmurs in all directions keep you aware that you are not alone.
655: Massive trees appear in every direction, their trunks dominating entire directions. For the most part you cannot see their tips, and are astounded at how long they must have been here. Forest murmurs in all directions keep you aware that you are not alone.
656:
A woodpecker is here, tapping on a tree.
A fallow deer is grazing peacefully here.

Massive trees appear in every direction, their trunks dominating entire directions. For the most part you cannot see their tips, and are astounded at how long they must have been here. Forest murmurs in all directions keep you aware that you are not alone.
657: Massive trees appear in every direction, their trunks dominating entire directions. For the most part you cannot see their tips, and are astounded at how long they must have been here. Forest murmurs in all directions keep you aware that you are not alone.
658: Hills still stretch out in all directions, but their numbers decline and each hill seems to be the size of a small mountain. The land has much more definition here and it is no longer easy to keep watch in all directions. A high ridge to the distant north traces the horizon and several odd formations along its edge, not quite natural, catches your eye. The path twists its way from the west to the south.
659: The hills slowly flatten out and the grass gives way to small bushes and shrubs. The familiar sounds of the river can still be heard to the south, but are somewhat muffled by a growing number of thick trees and bushes that line the riverbank.
660: Large maples grow randomly about this entire area, their huge limbs sheltering the sky from sight, and their bases still scarred from ancient milkings. A patch of small evergreens grow off to your west, huddled close together trying to survive amongst the much larger maples. Large multi-colored leaves are scattered across the ground, and the faint smell of pine is in the air.
661:
A woodpecker is here, tapping on a tree.
A robin is here, carrying small pieces of wood to its nest.
A boar cub is playing here, and exploring the wide world.

You are surrounded by tall bulky maple trees in all directions. The trees have grown so closely together and are so huge that it makes it almost impossible to see anything more than five meters away. To the south the number of trees dwindles, opening up into a beautiful orchard. To the west the land emerges into some flat-lands covered in grass and smaller bushes. You also see a small hill rise up in that direction.
662: The Bottom of a Dwarven Tomb
A pale ghost advances forward, shimmering with a pale light.

Surrounded on four sides by massive stone walls, the feeling is one of entombment. Examining the blocks reveals a much finer cut of stone than was used to make the staircase. This was obviously an important figure indeed to have such an elaborate tomb. The surprising thing about this place is, with so much treasure here, there is no sarcophagus. Perhaps it was looted by earlier grave-robbers.
663: A woodpecker is here, tapping on a tree.

To your north is a massive cliff of loose rocks. It prevents any travel in that direction and is very unstable. The land apparently chose this spot for a geologic upheaval that left this odd-looking mound of rock. Up above it, you think you see the beginnings of a flat range and hilly area. There is no access from here though, as the cliff is so unstable.
664: A large beaver is here, gnawing on a piece of wood.

You are on a sandy strip of soil that runs along the bank of the Nan Duin. Just to the north however, the clear space ends. After the few meters of beach, the land suddenly sprouts massive trees. Looking past the first few trees, you see a dark and gloomy forest. It looks spooky, but you hear the soft cry of birds in there, making you realise that the place has at least a few harmless creatures.
665: The Nan Duin stretches out before you, winding slowly down to its junction with the large river Luhn. Trees dot the area, as do grasses of various sizes. The riverbanks are almost crowded with animals trying to get their fill of water, and the birds wait anxiously in the tree for some bathing water. To your north, a wall of stone arises, but the way is clear to the east and west.
666: You are now on a small trail that seems to have very infrequent use. It is covered by gravel and pebbles of different sizes, interspersed with a brown hard soil. Just south, you see a sturdy bridge crossing over the Nan Duin. The path seems to continue to the north, towards distant lands. In the west you can see a massive forest that has a gloomy appearance. Perhaps getting closer to it would make it seem less threatening.
667: On the ground, there are two rafts.

From your vantage point on top of the bridge, you can see in every direction. Flowing east-west under the bridge, is the swift Nan Duin. To your north you can detect a small earth path leading towards distant lands. Only grassy plains are visible to the south, their wavy grasses blowing free in the wind.
668: You stand upon a grassy hill just south of a large bridge. A cool breeze blows through your hair. You observe insects hard at work buzzing around various wild flowers, and birds taking some of the long dry grass in their beaks. Looking to the south you see expanses of fields and farms spreading majestically. Rolling hills lead into thick forest-land to your west. While to the north is the river with a small bridge over it.
669:
The corpse of a centipede is lying here.
A colossal tree, its trunk as wide as a small cottage, stands here.
A small centipede is here scurrying about.

The lands around you are simple yet diverse. The barrage of colour comes not from green trees, or bright flowers, yet is still present in the form of golden stalks of grass, brown rocky soil, and pale gray rocks. Less friendly lands lie to your west, where a large forest begins. You cannot enter it here however, as the trees interspersed with vines makes passage impossible. In the north, you can hear the faint sound of running water. Looking to the south you see the trail used by the dwarven merchants, selling in the elven ports the iron goods produced in the Blue Mountains.
670:
A fallow deer is grazing peacefully here.
A fat rabbit is here, chewing on some grass.

The refreshing Nan Duin is to your north, flowing briskly along its east-west course through the mountains. The flat-land here is grassy and dry, except for where the water meets the land. Rocks dot the area in small clumps, and there are small trees grouped together. Southwards you spy more grassy plains, and to the west a large forest looms in the distance.
671:
An apple tree with bright green leaves grows here.
On the tree's branches is an apple.
A worm is here slithering around.
A snake slithers towards you.
A lonely goatherd stands here, watching his herd of goats.
A goat is here, grazing in the hills.
A goat is here, grazing in the hills.
A goat is here, grazing in the hills.

A line of apple trees borders the Nan Duin and offers quite a bit of shade. A squirrel has decided to take residence in one of the large trunks, apparently happy with the days search for food. The water flows just to your north, while southwards the terrain gets more rocky. Open plains are on both your east and west sides.
672:
A large marmot is here, scurrying in between the rocks.
A fallow deer is grazing peacefully here.

The land is less fertile here, due mostly to the many rocks and pebbles in the soil. Growing things here is not impossible however, as evidenced by the annual grass growing long and wavy. More flat land is on all sides of you, rising slightly to your west in the form of a small hill. The hill is round and would offer only a moderately better view. In the north you hear water.
673: A fallow deer is grazing peacefully here.

You are walking through wide plains south of the Nan Duin. The plains continue to the north and the terrain looks a bit rougher to the west. These rolling plains grow good grass, the kind that is long and brown.
674: A fallow deer is grazing peacefully here.

Vast stretches of plains surround you. The splashing of the Nan Duin comes from the north, where it flows west-east towards the Luhn. The plains continue to the south and the tops of hills can be spotted to the southwest. Movement here proves a little difficult as many rocks and piles of rubble clutter the ground. The rising Lhun Mountains can be seen to the south.
675: A large, loyal falcon is circling above.

The land here is bleak and empty save for the dark forest to the west. The plains in this area are different than the plains of southern Eriador, as their fertility is decreased due to the extreme rockiness of the soil. That has not hindered the wavy grass however, as it grows thick and long. More of the same grassy fields can be seen to the south and east. The Nan Duin flows swiftly to your north.
676: You see a small opening in the vegetation to the west and south. The darkness feels like a blanket suffocating you, as there is little light that can enter the forest because of the dense tree-tops. To the north, travel is inhibited by massive clumps of dead brush and trees. Even as so much dead vegetation covers the ground, the forest is full of life and fragrances. Animals scurry about in their daily quest for food.
677:
A forest spider is here crawling around.
A swallow flies high above the ground.

The forest to the west becomes increasingly tangled as you try to push your way through. The branches seem to have a mind of their own as they try to inhibit your progress. The ever-present darkness decreases your vision considerably. To the south there appears a break in the dense forest. It is only a small clearing, but perhaps it will lead to more open areas. The sounds of animals and birds fill the air. The way east is blocked by impassable mounds of dead vegetation and fallen trees.
678:
A black raven flies in the sky searching for flesh to prey upon.
A black raven flies in the sky searching for flesh to prey upon.

Thick branches and sharp thorns brush up against your legs and arms. You are constantly probed by the long vines and gnarled limbs of the trees. In every direction there is more of the same gloomy forest. It grows dense and choking all around you. Only towards the west does there seem to be any break in the growth. A small clearing is nestled there, amongst the foliage.
679:
A black wolf pads restlessly, looking for its next prey.
A black wolf pads restlessly, looking for its next prey.

The growth of trees, bushes, and vines is increasingly abundant here. So thick even, that you have to scramble under and over bushes to make any headway. Travel to the south is not just difficult, it is impossible. bushes mingled with the dense foliage makes traffic impossible in this direction. Cries of animals pierce the heavy silence in the forest, some crying for food, others echoing the last scream of death.
680:
A tree-snake lies wrapped around one of the tree branches.
A tree-snake lies wrapped around one of the tree branches.
A fierce wolverine is here, snarling at you.

Loud growls circle around you and you feel as if you are definitely not alone. The forest seems to surround you here, as it grows thick on your east, west, and south. Northwards the way is blocked by some abnormally large piles of deadfall. The west seems a bit more clear, and you hear the sound of running water from that direction. It is probably the mighty Nan Duin.
681:
An opossum stands here, sniffing around the ground.
A black raven flies in the sky searching for flesh to prey upon.

On three sides the forest surrounds you, with only north offering any other choice. In that direction you see the Nan Duin meandering throughout the Blue Mountains. Just south is a less wooded part of the forest, sort of a clearing. On the east and west sides of you however, there is a dark and threatening woodland, that seems to exude danger.
682:
Some thick writhing vines whip all around you.
An opossum stands here, sniffing around the ground.

The darkness in the forest overwhelms you, but you see glimpses of glowing eyes peering at you intently. For brief moments you can hear growls as packs of wolves begin to take hold of your scent. Will they leap out at you or slowly follow you until you bed down for the night? Any opening in the forest to the Nan Duin is covered by a very dense vegetation that is hard to push through, but manageable.
683: This part of the forest is covered in vegetation which makes it very difficult for you to tell the direction you are heading. Most of the sun's light is eliminated, due to the entanglement of greenery far above. Some natural light slips in however, whether it be the sun or moon, and from this light you can see that there is only more forest all around you.
684: A tree-snake lies wrapped around one of the tree branches.

Much to your relief you can make out a path to the south. The dense greenery and tangled foliage make orienting almost impossible. Every turn looks the same and the trees obscure any tell-tale landmarks. The air smells heavily of rot, as the shade of the ground keeps the bacteria in constant supply. A feast for the tiny creatures, the deadfall from the trees is quickly decomposed.
685:
A tree-snake lies wrapped around one of the tree branches.
A forest spider is here crawling around.

The forest grows thick and wild here. So much so that it slowly loses its forest-like appearance. Vines have covered some of the trees, making it seem as though the trunks around you are one entity. Light can barely be seen through the dense tree tops, and even if you are blessed with keen powers of sight in the darkness, visibility is of a short length. To the east however, the growth seems to thin slightly.
686: You have stepped into a small clearing in the forest. Around you on all sides are dense trees interspersed with vines and rockpiles. The thickest parts of the forest lie to the east, west, and south, with only the northern direction offering any variety in surroundings. To that direction, you hear the sound of running water, probably the mighty Nan Duin. Looking up in the trees, you see some rather large nests. Though a source of protection for the birds that inhabit them, they would not support your size and weight.
687: The forest here grows dense and dark. The high treetops are as thick as the branches towards the ground, making the penetration of sunlight or moonlight very difficult. The dim light afforded you allows detection of a small trail to the south. On all other sides however, only more gloomy forest awaits. The howl of wolves and the screech of birds punctuates the heavy silence.
688: A bright red mushroom is growing here.

Many trees cover this area, interfering with your sense of direction. You chop off branches and vines in hope of finding a way through this dense mess. Ground foliage is made primarily of mushrooms, fern-type plants, and hardy flowers. This is because all of them have a relatively low light necessity, and can grow in the shade that the treetops produce. A particularly large pile of dead branches catch your eye. Peering intently at the pile, you swear there is noise coming from it.
689: A woodpecker is here, tapping on a tree.

The area you are in gives plenty of variety now. All around you are samples of the various terrain to be found in this large region. To the south is the Nan Duin, which transects the mountains in an east-west direction. On your north and west sides, woodlands grow in varying densities, ranging from chokingly thick, to sparse and roomy. Tall grass grows on the ground when not smothered out by larger foliage. The eastward direction holds a small trail, leading to distant lands.
690:
A woodpecker is here, tapping on a tree.
A fallow deer is grazing peacefully here.
A grey wolf is here, snarling aggressively.
A grey wolf is here, snarling aggressively.
A squirrel scampers around here, looking for nuts from the trees.

The trees grow increasingly large as they grow closer to the Nan Duin, making travel more difficult. The river flows just to the south, but your chances of reaching it from here are small. Huge boulders interspersed with dense clumps of shrub prevent you from proceeding easily. Small birds peer down at you in wonder, and you hear the sound of a woodpecker busy at work.
691: A tall and sturdy oak tree towers over you.

The forest borders the mighty Nan Duin here. It is flowing merrily along just to your south. You cannot go northwards here, as a pile of boulders has mixed with the trees and vines, making travel impossible. The forest extends to your east and west, leading into more gloom and darkness. The sounds of forest animals reach your ears, mostly small animals, but occasionally a large thud or snap can be heard, signifying a larger beast.
692:
A shrub with maple-like leaves is growing here.
On the shrub, there are two handfuls of blackcurrant berries.
A fallow deer is grazing peacefully here.

The Nan Duin stretches before you and you take a deep breath and inhale the fresh air. Many frogs and toads leap around your feet as you observe a family of deer drink from the river. The scene is peaceful, much more peaceful than the sight of the dense forest to your north. Perhaps harmless, but heavily overgrown areas like that have often been the habitat of less-than-friendly beings. The river is to the south, flowing east-west over the Blue Mountains.
693: A woodpecker is here, tapping on a tree.

This part of the forest seems darker than the rest, probably due to the entanglement of the trees above you. Even in the dim light, you can detect a less thick region to your north, and a set of claw-like footprints that lead off to your east. Looking closer, you see an odd structure of some sort. Not exactly a building, but humanoid construction for certain. An owl's glowing eyes divert your attention for a moment as you continue to hear sounds of wildlife around you.
696: On the Side of the Trail
A tall and strong hunter is standing here.

If you are so inclined, this grassy space just off the trail seems like a nice place to take a rest. Ferns, long grass, and short trees scatter the area close at hand, while much taller and thicker woodlands lie to the south. Just east of here, that earthen trail continues, leading into lands many miles away.
697:
A mouse is here nosing around, looking for a safe place to hide.
A large, loyal falcon is circling above.

To the west the hill descends into the Narbrethil Forest. Recounting tales of the place, you are thoughtful of the stories of ghastly beasts and lost hunting parties. Rather than believe these stories, you look with an eye of wisdom at the place, and decide that instead of mighty creatures, the people got lost within the massive trees and gripping vines. The east reveals long stretches of grass leading to a small trail.
698:
A fat rabbit sits here, chewing on some grass.
A furry, striped raccoon is here, nosing around for some berries or roots.

To the west is the ominous Narbrethil Forest with trees peeking high amongst the clouds. The east brings in more grasslands and to the south a cliff begins to ascend to the top of a hill. In the north, rolling plains with some large canyons are in view. A particularly deep canyon prevents immediate travel in that direction.
699:
A robin is here, carrying small pieces of wood to its nest.
A nightingale is here, chirping a sweet melody.

You notice the forest appears to be a bit darker here, but you manage to uncover a small track that leads to the south. There are a few footprints on the ground, obviously old, but large and a bit intimidating nonetheless. Small caterpillars and other insects roam about casually, and sounds of small animals can be heard as they rustle about in the thick growth.
700:
The bee flies around here, collecting nectar from the flowers.
The bee flies around here, collecting nectar from the flowers.
A large, loyal falcon is circling above.

A lovely trail of flowers borders a group of bushes. To the north, a great canyon has opened up, leaving no option for travel to that direction. Southwards holds a bit more variety, as it forms a cliff of loose rock, about five meters high. There is a danger in climbing it, for the stones are unstable and could come down upon your head.
701:
A brown fox is here, looking for some rabbits to chew up.
A robin is here, carrying small pieces of wood to its nest.
A nightingale is here, chirping a sweet melody.

The grass blows in the wind and you come across an occasional group of bushes that seem out of place in these vast grasslands. What catches your attention most however, are the large roots rising out of the ground. They lead to the south, past trees that try to block your entry into the place. If one tries hard however, the tangles and roots can be overcome if one really wants to proceed into the dark woods.
702:
A fallow deer is grazing peacefully here.
A large elk is standing here, chewing grass and leaves.

A few rabbits hurry into the forest at the sight of you. The land here is rough, buckled and cracked in places as if something lives beneath you. As you examine the ground you come across large roots, enormous actually, that lead to the forest to the south and west. A couple of deer peer angrily at you as they nudge their fawn to the nearby pond. You may enter the forest to your south, or continue into the grass to your east.
703:
The corpse of a large elk is lying here.
A shrub with maple-like leaves is growing here.
On the shrub, there are two handfuls of blackcurrant berries.

The lush greenery is a refreshing sight. Rabbits, squirrels, and other small rodents scurry between the bushes, making use of the foliage to build shelters and attain food. Birds sing songs that fill the air with a gay melody. As they tend to their young in the trees that stretch far above, you hear high pitched cries signifying the newborn birds perpetual hungriness. You hear the familiar murmur of the Nan Duin to the south.
704:
A huge, black wolf is sleeping here.
A mother wolf is sleeping here.
A wolf cub happily plays here.
A wolf cub happily plays here.

The temperature in here is higher than that above ground. Perfect you decide, for a nesting place for animals. The bones on the floor are indicative that something else has had a similar idea. Scraps of flesh litter the floor, and the smell is dank and foetid. The only way out is back the way you came.
705:
A patch of moss grows here on a wet, flat stone.
A giant slug is here, oozing around.

The dark and gloomy hole is filled with whimpering sounds that seem to come from the south. The smell of rotten flesh invades your nostrils and almost makes you choke. The tree above seems to encroach here, as you see thick roots protruding below the surface into this narrow crawlspace. Another dark room is barely visible to your south.
706:
A small mushroom grows nearby.
A large potato is growing here.
A carrot is growing here.

A beautiful garden is here, comprised of wildflowers of captivating colors. The fragrance is lively, somewhere between fruity and spicy. Insects are drawn to the bright colours, and buzz happily about the many different kinds of growth. A thick green hedge, presumably to keep the local herbivores out, surrounds the garden and prohibits travel anywhere but back the way you came.
707:
A small oaken table has been set here.
On the table, there are a butcher knife, a pan, and a spoon.
A large stone chest is here.
A tall and strong hunter is standing here.

This is little more than a sprawling hut situated on the bank of a peaceful slow-moving river. Part stone, part sod, the hut leans drunkenly against a tall, thick tree. Its roof is equally haphazard, composed of large branches, wooden plates, and gaping holes. The view out the west window is vast, as it reveals the Nan Duin making its slow trek downstream. There are doors to both the west and north. Otherwise the decor is spartan.
708:
You see two slender plants on the ground.
A large shrub covered with dark violet berries grows here.
On the shrub, there are three piles of violet berries.
A placid pond is here, inviting you to take a refreshing drink.
A black catfish is here, lurking in the mud.
A crayfish is here, snapping its claws at you.

A little trickle of water filters into a pool bordering some rocks. A couple of fish dart around it, and you notice stepping stones placed evenly across the pond. A small dock lies to the south, accessible easily by the stones. Flowers of different colors grace the banks of the water, and birds sing in happy harmony. A high hedge to the east prevents you from going in that direction.
709:
A fishing rod has been left here.
A canoe has been left here.
A light boat made of reeds has been left here.

This dock appears to see little use. The familiar sounds of birds singing and the rustling of animals through the underbrush are curiously absent. A line of stepping stones extend from the dock across a small pond to the north, while the Nan Duin flows strongly past to the south. The only sign of habitation nearby is a ramshackle cabin to the east, which may house the builder of this dock.
710: You find yourself in the heart of a light forest. The trees and undergrowth are not dense, and you can move around easily. Many flowers grow here, where the Nan Duin crosses the forest. You can see some squirrels on the treetops, and you hear birds tweeting.
711: A woodpecker is here, tapping on a tree.

The huge trees overwhelm you as the diameter alone is bigger than the fattest troll in Arda. Their enormous branches make ideal homes for the local animal population. Squirrels scamper around the limbs, while a woodpecker concentrates on the trunk. The tree-tops are high, their leaves blocking out much of the natural light from above. In all directions you can see only more trees and dense vegetation.
712:
A colony of red ants is here. The ants seem to ignore you.
The garden snake slithers harmlessly here.

The huge trees of the Narbrethil Forest surround you in every direction. Their mighty roots delve deep into the earth. Small, colorful birds sing merrily all around, making you feel relaxed. An medium sized anthill stands near one of the trees.
713:
A fallow deer is grazing peacefully here.
A squirrel scampers around here, looking for nuts from the trees.

You are crossing a beautiful forest north of the Nan Duin. The trees must be very old, since their size is truly impressive. All around you, the rustling of the leaves and the birds chirping make you feel at ease. You can see a small hole on one of the trees, it is probably a squirrel's home.
714: A fallow deer is grazing peacefully here.

You find yourself in the heart of a light forest, on the northern side of the Nan Duin. Small birds are chirping amid the rustling leaves of the huge trees. A rivulet of warm water flows from the north towards the river. As you continue your journey across the greenery, you relax in this peaceful environment.
715:
Some delicious wild strawberries grow on the ground.
Some delicious wild strawberries grow on the ground.
A fallow deer is grazing peacefully here.
A prospector is walking around slowly, looking for a new ore vein to mine.
A prospector is walking around slowly, looking for a new ore vein to mine.

You find yourself in a light forest on the northern bank of the Nan Duin. The undergrowth is not at all entangled, and you can walk around with ease. Here and there, small yellow flowers and red berries grow among the huge trees. Their sweet smell fills your nostrils.
716:
A light boat made of reeds has been left here.
A prospector is walking around slowly, looking for a new ore vein to mine.

Worn steps, which the Dwarves carved into the relatively soft rock of the river bank, lead south and west to the calm water of the river. At the top of the steps, a small, seldom used trail begins its long journey towards the Blue Mountains to the north. Beyond the river, which enters a forest of huge trees not too far away, you spot a high stone tower. It probably was built to guard these lands against invaders and other dangers.
717:
A shrub with maple-like leaves is growing here.
A squirrel scampers around here, looking for nuts from the trees.

In a clearing of the Narbrethil Forest, fuming water flows from a crack in the ground and fills a small pool before finding its way to the river. The heat locks this place in an eternal summer. Bunches of small wild flowers grow around the spring; a deer, which was grazing here, flees silently into the woods as soon as you arrive.
718: A colourful butterfly is fluttering around here.

You are crossing a beautiful forest on the slopes of the Blue Mountains. The trees must be very old, since their size is truly impressive. All around you, the rustling of the leaves and the birds chirping make you feel at ease. A light breeze from the east carries the scent of flowers.
720: The huge trees of the forest far to the east could not grow here as well, due to the thick layer of stones above the soil. A few long striped snakes dart here and there between the rocks, in search of food.
721:
A snake slithers towards you.
A snake slithers towards you.
You are in the middle of a rocky plain, almost devoid of vegetation; a few patches of wild flowers, which somehow managed to find water below the thick layer of stones, are the only exception.
722: You are at the edge of a rocky plain, nearly devoid of vegetation. Only in the cracks of the large stones some moss has managed to grow. A few striped snakes are slithering between the rocks. To the south the plains are flanked by the Nan Duin.
723: At a small intersection now, you are offered two choices. The earthen trail still runs north and south here, but a small patch of grass is just to one side of it. To your east is an overgrown path, leading to a circle of stones atop a large hill in the north. A huge iron gate, wedged between two boulders, makes the way impassable unless you have the key to the gate.
724: The trail continues to the east and south here. On occasion you notice a few small animals run from one side of the path to the other to the safety of the forest. The forest may hold safety for them, but as you look into the dark shadows of the trees, you wonder if it will be dangerous to go in there. A bird's cry echoes from within the bounds of the woodlands.
725: A stocky mountain mule is here, waiting to serve.

The path bends from the west toward the north. On your east lies a large hill, with a circle of stones arranged in a ring on its top. The stones are obviously hand placed. You cannot scramble up the slope here, for this side of it has broken away, leaving only a crumbling cliff standing. To attempt a climb up this would be futile, as the rocks would surely tumble down upon you.
726: The trail stops here, mandated by the fact that a gorge has opened up to your north. Not having a bridge here, it is totally impossible to cross. On your east and west sides however, the plains of this region continue. A well-trodden earth path leads away southwards, heading back towards the river. Bunnies hop playfully close to the edge of the chasm, daring the loose rocks.
727: A sturdy pack horse is standing here.

The path seems to dead-end here, as it meets a dense hedgerow, which sweeps around the small hill, to the south, apparently enclosing it completely. Atop this hill, a circle of stones can be seen, which seem to have been laid out deliberately, to a careful design. Even at this distance, carvings can be seen on some of them.
728: A diamondback rattlesnake is coiled here, ready to strike.

You are standing on a small hill, made mostly of solid rocks and some sandy soil. Examining the stones around you, you see that they are placed about three metres apart, and are arranged in a ring. Each stone is about a metre high, and a metre wide. In the centre of the ring, a massive slab covers the ground. It is completely smooth, and has a short inscription on it. Around the base of the hill, a dense encircling hedgerow has been planted.
729: You are standing in some long wavy grass, just on the bend of an old path. It goes in a north-south direction, and lies to the east and south of where you are now. More rolling hills and grass seem to be the topography of this area, but forested areas lie south of the trail. The grass blows in the wind like a million dead arms.
730: The inky blackness embraces you as the stairs descend into the depths of Amon Othar. Rough hewn blocks of stone construct the walls, leading you to believe that it is Dwarven work. You cannot see the landing of the steps yet, leaving you only two options. Either back up the stairs into the outdoors, or down into the unknown.
731: The bare white walls of the small antechamber stand straight and tall, barring any passage except due east, where a small dark corridor can be seen, leading off into the darkness. The walls are void of decoration, but small structural features are present, that would create shallow shadows dancing upon the wall. The stone floor of the chamber is carefully laid, using different shades of coloured stones, thus creating streaks of colour and images.
732:
A huge statue made of stone suddenly turns to life.
A huge statue made of stone suddenly turns to life.
A guardian stone beast is here, protecting the grave.

Now behind one of the grey walls, you find yourself in a narrow room with a low ceiling. Used most likely as a second treasure room, the blocks of stone here are of the same fine cut. A strange thing about this room, as soon as you entered it, a feeling of great tension came over you. It was as if your presence awakened a long-dormant power.
733: A small campfire burns here, its low flames giving off only a little light.

The ancient corridor gently slopes down to the east, and climbs to the west, where it ends in a barely visible chamber. The white stone walls are smooth to the touch, with little sign of moisture. The only features that give a clear hint of progress while moving along the passage are the tiled floor and some small holes, regularly spaced at the top of the walls and along the ceiling.
734: The burnt and blackened skeletal remains of a human are here.

The corridor is an arched passage through the mountain, leading east, further into the ancient tomb, and west towards the entrance. The walls are burned and blackened by furious flames in several places and most of the white stonework has been cracked and has fallen to the ground in small splinters as a mockery of its former glory. High upon the walls there are small holes, placed with an even spacing, their rims black and ragged by the burning inferno that once raged unchecked here. Lining the ceiling, similar holes can be seen all along the passage. The floor of the corridor was once a tiled floor, the stones laid with great precision to form a beautiful hallway, but now they are encrusted with remnants of molten white stonework and blackened by blazing fires. Upon the floor lie charred and rusted remnants of old weapons, some of which are partly melted.
735:
The corpse of a stone statue is lying here.
The corpse of a stone statue is lying here.
The corpse of a stone statue is lying here.
A mountain mule is sleeping here.

Deep below the mountains lies this small and carved hallway. Carefully created by master craftsmen the chamber has a floor laid with stone tiles, and white walls that are polished smooth by caring hands. The white masonry of the walls is only broken by a heavy lever, placed in a dark crack on the eastern wall.
736: The small cubicle is shaped as a semicircle, the wall almost perfectly round. The white wall is smooth and polished, made by master craftsmen; the ceiling is flat, made of somewhat darker stone. Being a very small chamber, the cubicle more resembles a niche, created to place a statue in. Placed on the southern wall there is a small lever, fastened in a small, dark crack. Marring the white surface of the room are small streaks of red and upon the floor there are dark red spots covering the stone.
737:
A metal wall shield rests on the ground.
A quiver wrapped in gems and rubies lies here.
A beautiful longbow, embellished with lines of silver and mithril, lies here.
A fortune in gold lies in a heap.
An old axe lies half-buried here.
A fire opal catches the light.
A stone sarcophagus lies on the floor.

A large stone grave is standing on the floor in the middle of the room. The place is well kept and the tapestries on the wall remind you of the room you just came from. These tapestries and pictures however, seem to be centered on a particular individual. Although many dwarves are seen in the pictures, one dwarf is seen in them all. You conclude that he must be the resident of the tomb. As his picture depicts a large, battle scarred Dwarf, you wonder if disturbing his final resting spot is a wise decision. Upon the tomb are some words etched in the stone.
738: A fat rabbit is here, chewing on some grass.

Several boulders lie about the field, looking like they may have once been arranged in some meaningful pattern. Large bushes obscure the view of the surrounding fields. The land gently rises to the northwest until it meets a line of dark blue hills. The cool winds whistle through the boughs of the trees scattered along the plains.
739: This broad plateau is covered in prickly briar plants. Walking through the closely knit bushes is difficult, as well as somewhat painful. The numerous rabbits inhabiting the briar patch dart about with ease, well protected from hawks and other predators by the thorny branches. With some effort, you can make your way east to a trail through the hills, or travel south to the the crest of a hill.
740: A sparrow is flapping around on the ground.

The northern winds have swept the plains clean. Weeds grow up between the cracks formed between the boulders. One particularly large rock provides a good viewpoint of the surrounding terrain. The hill along the ridge continues to the east and west, but makes a gradual descent to the south. The plains continue to the north through a field of dark-green briars.
741: A brown fox is here, looking for some rabbits to chew up.

The constant winds blowing across these plains make the grasses and thick brush sway in the breeze. The bushes provide some protection from the winds. The land gently rolls on to the south and east. A small rise to the west overlooks a grove of ancient oaks. The foothills of the Blue Mountains rise above the horizon far to the northwest.
742: A brown fox is here, looking for some rabbits to chew up.

You are in the midst of a lightly wooded area. The woods are mainly composed of young pine trees, barely larger than saplings. Passage to the north is blocked by a steep rock face, which continues to the west. As the ground rises to the east, the trees thin and bare patches of stony terrain are visible. The woods extend downhill to the south, where the pines are gradually supplanted by larger and more numerous oaks.
743: There are few trees here under this sharp cliffwall bordering the forest. You can follow it west or head south towards a great oak which stands out among the lesser trees. The cliff is smooth with no obvious projections, so climbing it is clearly out of the question.
744: This steep slope is covered with bushes and small trees. Below you, to the north, there seems to be an entrance to a mine. The ground before it is grey and covered with pebbles. Further north the valley of the Nan Duin is meandering through the landscape like a giant snake.
745: The mountain slopes upwards to your north, small crooked birches cover the area, but below you the vegetation is flourishing. The hills that stretch out to the south seem to be a perfect place for shy animals to hide in.
746: You found a narrow tunnel leading down into the darkness. The granite walls are covered with a layer of encrusted smoke particles, and the air is very thick. The echo returns to you each noise that you make, amplified and distorted in a malignant way.
747: The tunnel here branches in a Y junction. To the south, this dreadful place is illuminated by a pale reddish glow. The tunnel also continues to the east, where it descends slowly, and north to the exit. Sudden gusts of wind bring a faint smell of brimstone to your nostrils.
748: A spirit floats towards you and howls with an evil laughter.

This part of the tunnel is hotter than the rest, and bathed in a reddish glow coming from a gaping hole in the floor. The air is difficult to breathe, as the smell of smoke and brimstone is overpowering. The walls here are even more blackened and scorched than elsewhere in the tunnel. The cavern steeply slopes down both to the east and to the north.
749: A spirit floats towards you and howls with an evil laughter.

You are standing in a narrow, dark tunnel. Its granite walls seem to have been blackened in some sort of conflagration. The atmosphere is thick, and a feeling of dread pervades the place. On the southern wall, a sort of shaft leads up. The walls of the shaft are extremely hard, and as smooth as glass, making the ascent impossible. The terrain ascends to the west, where, in the distance, you can see a pale reddish glow.
750: You are standing in a narrow, dark tunnel. Its granite walls seem to have been blackened in some sort of conflagration. The atmosphere is thick, and a feeling of dread pervades the place.
751:
A small, sickly green mushroom grows here.
A patch of moss grows here on a wet, flat stone.
A small pool of red-stained water lies here.

You barely manage to squeeze yourself through a narrow crack in the tunnel and you reach a dark, cold, damp room. Red-stained water drips on you from the ceiling and collects into a small pool at your feet. A pile of old bones lies on the bottom of the pool.
752:
A hungry-looking giant lizard is slithering towards you.
A hungry-looking giant lizard is slithering towards you.
A hungry-looking giant lizard is slithering towards you.

Perhaps climbing down from the hole above was not a very good idea. At the moment, you are standing on a frail-looking platform suspended above a large and deep pit. The area is illuminated by the red glow of the lava which fills the bottom of the pit, several yards below. You can barely breathe, since the heat and the billowing fumes of the lava make this a very uncomfortable place.
757:
A light boat made of reeds has been left here.
A slender plant, with white flowers at the top, grows here.
A large shrub covered with dark violet berries grows here.
On the shrub, there are three piles of violet berries.

You find yourself at the western edge of a dense, gloomy forest. Beyond the Nan Duin, which flows calmly north of here, you can barely see a path which winds its way far to the north. The trees are less dense to the west. East of here, however, the forest becomes VERY dark and dangerous. Ominous howls and cries filter from there; and the growth seems so tangled that it must be very difficult to find one's way.
758:
A dwarven soldier is here, watching for trouble.
A dwarven soldier is here, watching for trouble.
A short, muscular dwarven captain is giving orders to his soldiers.

The thick stone walls of this tower rise high all around you. The windows are very narrow, and the room is lit by a huge fireplace. Some hewn wood has been stacked near the fire. Opposite the entrance, a spiral staircase leads up.
759:
A huge hollow horn, of Dwarven make, has been placed here.
A dwarven soldier is here, watching for trouble.

You have reached the flat roof of the high Dwarven tower. A long spiral staircase leads inside. From here you can see the valley of the Nan Duin all around. The calm, clear river flows from the western mountains and it enters a large forest far to the east. A long, worn, winding trail descends from the Blue Mountains southwest; it reaches the foot of this tower and turns to the southeast, where it enters the forest. Another trail, leading north, begins on the other bank of Nan Duin, being flanked by barren plains on one side and by a light forest on the other. West of here there are many rough hills, which have been extensively mined by the Dwarves, while to the south you can see a dark, gloomy forest. This is an excellent place to guard the lands of the Dwarves: as you can realise, any movement on the river or the trail would be spotted quickly.
760:
A stocky mountain mule is here, waiting to serve.
A stocky mountain mule is here, waiting to serve.
A domesticated pony, beast of burden to many, stands here.
A domesticated pony, beast of burden to many, stands here.
A brown donkey watches the surroundings, perhaps looking for a chance to graze.
A young dwarven stable-hand checks on the horses.
A domesticated pony, beast of burden to many, stands here.

This building houses the mounts that travellers to the Ered Luin need for negotiating the miles. In the main, ponies fill the stalls: the favoured mount of the dwarves. However, larger mounts are also catered for, as well as exotic pets. A set of shuttered windows to the northern end of the building show a good view of the nearby Nan Duin.
761: A hungry-looking giant lizard is slithering towards you.

You have entered a groove in the forest undergrowth. Its slippery sides are about ten feet high, but luckily the southern edge slopes gently up to the forest proper. The bottom is layered with mushy moss, soaked by an artery of underground water surfacing for the length of this cut in the forest floor.
762: You had to climb quite high to get a good view, and standing with your feet cautiously balanced on one of the highest branches, you feel a slight swaying caused by your weight and the wind. Still, an excellent view of the lands of Lindon presents itself before your eyes.
763: A brown bear is sleeping here.

You enter a dark, moist cave about fifteen feet across. Rust-coloured water trickles down the far wall, forming a pool of unclean water covering half of the cave's floor. You can make out no other exit than the cramped tunnel through which you came.
764:
A black catfish is here, lurking in the mud.
A crayfish is here, snapping its claws at you.
A snake slithers towards you.

On the underside of the bridge a thick moss grows, obviously in response to the constant moisture supplied by the river. It is relatively dark under the bridge, as the space between the boards of the bridge and the river is quite small. You see many loose boards on the bridge, while others appear quite strong. The Nan Duin flows contentedly in its usual east-west direction.
765: The river banks here consist of solid stone; whether natural or otherwise they provide the perfect location for the construction of the wooden bridge you see overhead. The builders obviously knew that this stone would resist the river's ability to erode, and that this bridge would stand upright for many years to come. The river narrows here and the stone banks provide sturdy footing to rest and water ones horses. The river flows from west to east.
766: The darkness opens up into an old armoury, filled with several fireplaces, benches and anvils. This large abandoned cavern still seems to be in perfect order. Along the walls hangs an assortment of half complete weapons and armour, mostly comprised of axes, shields, swords and spears of all shapes and sizes. The cave continues to the east. Tunnels open in the southern and northern walls.
767:
Some roots lie here waiting to ensnare weary travellers.
Some roots lie here waiting to ensnare weary travellers.
Some roots lie here waiting to ensnare weary travellers.
Massive roots shift uneasily all around you.

The tunnel ends abruptly, only a few paces from the large cavern lying north of here, in a large pool of water. This is the armoury's water supply but it seems to have been left unused for a long period of time, as roots have grown in the wet tunnel, partly blocking access to the water. The water is dark but clear, showing few signs of the bottom below.
768: The tunnel continues in the darkness, extending east and west as far as the eye can see. The bare walls are totally smooth, showing signs of care and thoroughness in their construction. The floor slants away to the east, further into the dark rock. A smell of dust and coal pervades the air.
769: This large wooden crate has been crafted to look like a storage silo from the outside, complete with a stock of grain and a fully functional door assembly. The entire wall facing the storage cave easily swings out of the way with little effort. Its lock and hinges are crude and lack any kind of protective casing or housing. Wafts of damp air emanate from a narrow tunnel leading eastwards further into the mountain.
770: The tunnel widens up, almost like a small cavern. The floor is cold and the air dry, making this cavern a good place for long term storage. Several silos have been built against the walls, apparently for storing grain and crops. The wooden planks of the silo fronts line up by the walls, covering them totally. Small piles of grain lie spread across the smooth floor.
771: An underground tunnel through the black rock mountain. The walls are crude, as is the floor, but the grinding tear of feet and time has worn a smooth path in the rock, into the tunnel going north. The floor inclines steeply at the southern wall, allowing passage to the grid up in the roof.
772: The tunnel continues its course through the black rock, deep below the mountain peaks. The passage is almost as big as a cavern; the roof is several feet higher than the tallest of dwarves; the walls wide enough for half a dozen adventurers to walk abreast. Crates, boxes and piles of stored goods are stacked to one side of the tunnel, forming a narrow path along the other wall.
773: The underground tunnel lies in darkness. Built up by black rock walls and a slightly slanted floor it leads through the mountain. The walls are crude, dust dances in the air in front of you. The tunnel southwards widens as it leads deeper. A stair is built at the north end, leading up to a grid in the tunnel roof.
774: A huge stone platform, standing 2 or so meters high, has been placed at the centre of the niche. A massive rock table with 10 chiseled boulders for chairs sits in the middle of the platform. The area surrounding the platform is huge, and could easily support crowds in the hundreds, and possibly thousands. This was obviously a place of extreme importance, and you feel somewhat in awe as you gaze upon this ancient dwarven council site.
775: High ridges and peaks surround this small vale entirely blocking off any possibility that it may be seen from the outside. The north and west sides of the valley contain numerous small huts and cabins, so old that some are roofless and others have simply collapsed. Large outposts are located at the top of the mountain ridges to the south and southeast, used to survey the entire surrounding countryside. A large structure sits in the middle of a niche to the south and a small path leads off east.
776: This cabin seems to be the living quarters for leaders of the vale, as it is the well constructed and situated quite centrally and close to the auditorium. It is fairly large and seems to have room to sleep about 10 comfortably. A dusty old canvas map of the vale and surrounding country is still pinned to a long table in the centre of the room.
777: You seem to have stumbled onto a narrow hidden path that leads west through the mountains. Made up of mostly solid rock, the ground is much harder here and the gouges from the east are not nearly as deep, and in some places unnoticable. The path widens to the east and opens up into a small mountain vale.
778:
A large stone fireplace with a roaring fire warms the room.
An alert young dwarf is working here.

Large oak and pine furniture is placed in an orderly fashion all around the interior of the alehouse. A fire burns in the huge fireplace along the east wall. A bear fur covers the floor in front of the fire. Oak barrels cover the northern wall, containing the varied beverages sold here. A large oak bar covered with wood carvings keeps the customers away from the barrels.
779:
A roast haunch of boar sends up a fragrant aroma.
A large stone fireplace with a roaring fire warms the room.

A bright light emanates from the fireplace, generating enough heat to fill the room. A large table covers the centre of the room. Bowls, pitchers and cutlery lie scattered about, apparently in use by the kitchen staff. Several barrels sit in a rack along the eastern wall. The equipment seems sturdy, but lacks the detail to be of much value. A pair of double doors leads into the common room.
780: Carved limestone walls surround deep valleys. Much of the cliff sides have crumbled leaving their remains along the steep hillside. Small shrubs grow amongst the boulders and stones. The rocky lands continue to the north and south. A trail can be seen to the east, where the canyons open to a vast plain.
781: A bear is here, covered with coarse black fur.

Varied branches cover the vast floor of the hollow cave. The branches appear to have been torn from large shrubs. The leaves have been pressed down by a heavy weight. Wild berries add colour to the greys and browns of the surrounding walls. The cavern seems to have been enlarged by large claws. Light leaks through the thick vegetation covering the doorway.
782:
A tiny spider is here, eating a tiny bug.
A huge, venomous spider is here.
A tiny spider is here, eating a tiny bug.
A tiny spider is here, eating a tiny bug.

The tunnel walls are covered with tiny streams of water, trickling down to the floor. There they pool together and flow to the south. A patch of earth and roots hang from above. Small webs decorate the edges. The tunnel seems to have been carved into the limestone long ago. A cool breeze comes from the south.
783: Ancient lime stones have been carved and worn smooth by the passing of water that must have once flowed here. A few chunks have broken away from the walls since. Various cracks decorate the stone above. Some evidence of seepage can be seen. A soft glow from a larger cavern can be seen to the west.
784: Many glittering rocks, crystals and other loose minerals are scattered on the ground. Several of the glowing crystals appear to have been collected and placed in piles to give some concentrated light in special places. A completely rusted lantern lies on the ground giving evidence that sometime in the past someone has visited this place. Rushing water can be heard to the south.
785: Small crystals create a small amount of light. The swiftly moving underground stream rushes along, pushing all in its path to the east. Dark cubby holes and deep crevices line the walls and ceilings, but the water has worn the surface smooth. There seems to be no place to get a solid grip. A large cavern opens to the north, but the water wants to go down a chute to the east.
786:
A giant, strange looking green fungus is here, ready to devour you in seconds (red aura).
A giant slug is here, oozing around (red aura).
A giant slug is here, oozing around (red aura).

Ancient diggings line the caverns walls. Bones can be seen lying in many of the small alcoves. Small pieces of wood and rusted metal sharing their resting place. A cool mist seeps from the limestone in one corner, where most of the bones seem to be located. Lichens and moss grow in varied places around the cavern.
787:
A small termite is running around making strange sounds.
A small termite is running around making strange sounds.
A robin is here, carrying small pieces of wood to its nest.

The inside of the stump is damp and mildewed. Wood crumbles at the slightest touch, with piles of sawdust pile along the edges already. Hundreds of tiny holes pierce the inner side of the old tree. In the centre is a small burrow, which has been dug out by some creature. The outer casing of the trunk leans against what little remains of a once great oak.
788:
A great wolf with coal-black eyes stares intently at you, drooling saliva.
An ancient fungus smothers the boulders.

Varied molds completely cover the damp rock walls. Water slowly seeps down to form pools of liquid, which seem to lead deeper into the floor. The air is very musty, no evidence of a breeze can be felt. Small bones from squirrels or other rodents can be seen scattered about.
789: A partridge attempts to hide in the undergrowth.

The land slowly rises to the northeast. Trees cover the slope, making travel torturous. However unlikely, the trees seem to grow even more closely together to the west. A tall oak tree dominates the others. Its branches reach out far above the tops of all the other trees. The wooded area succumbs to the skies towards the south.
790: A sparrow is flapping around on the ground.

The forest thins here somewhat, allowing a patch of larch-wood to flourish. The wooded area allows easier passage than the dense forests closing in on the larch-wood. The local trees protect a varied growth of bushes and flowers from the mountains far to the north. The forest grows wilder and more entangled to the west. The forest continues up the rising hills to the north. Trees grow sparsely upon the plains further to the east.
791: You are in the forest, south of a huge oak and north of a thin forest path. A group of silver-grey ash trees have taken root here, some of the wearing clusters of green flowers. To the east and west the forest seems green and rich, but northwesterly it looks dark and squalid.
792: There are some acorns lying here.

You are standing beneath the lower boughs of a sublime oak tree. Overhead a swallow rides the wind, maybe it is protecting nestlings in the tree-top. An acorn falls to the ground, probably because of the harsh rapping of a wood- pecker. To the north you see the great wall of a cliff causing a sharp ending to the forest.
793: This is a small round antechamber, not more than ten feet across. It is dressed in red velvet and the air is very dry. The floor is made of black stones placed in circles. Above the centre stone a hatch leads upwards. A small doorway to the south leads into a chamber where a sarcophagus can be seen along the opposite wall.
794: You have entered a small chamber with walls of earth. Steel constructions keep the force of nature at bay, making sure the ceiling doesn't crash down upon you. Water is dripping off the walls and the smell of damp earth lingers in the air. The stone floor is covered with gravel and a small stream of water flows out through the stone door west of you since the floor is slightly sloping in that direction. Along the eastern wall a statue of a dwarf stands in full metal armour with a hideous mask covering his face.
795:
A guardian stone beast is here, protecting the grave.
A huge statue made of stone suddenly turns to life.

The corridor ends in this small chamber far below the ground. In the middle of the room a pedestal has been placed, upon which a statue of stone stands. On the eastern wall a huge dragonhead protrudes from the wall, its black eyes following every move you make. The northern wall pictures dwarves fighting dragons and the vaulted ceiling is painted black except where dragonfire illuminates the sky. A corridor leads to the south.
796: The corridor turns to the east here. The earthy smell is now tainted with a vague odour of stagnant water which seems to be concentrated to the middle of the room. The walls here show huge terrible dragons flying across a pale blue sky with a massive darkness looming behind. They almost look real.
797: An earthy smell is strong throughout the humid air in this tunnel. Water is dripping from the walls and algae are growing on the few stones that can be seen in the damp earth floor or protruding from the walls. The tunnel makes a turn to the north where it leads into a dark pool of water.

A large, engraved sarcophagus sits on a raised dais.

A tall statue of a dwarf, dressed in metal armour stands here.

The left one wielding a great axe and the right one a large hammer. The walls in here are made of black stone, as is the floor. A small arched doorway leads back north to the circular ante- chamber.
799: The walls and ceiling in this corridor are painted all in black, making the darkness very immense. On each wall, east and west, a square crucifix made of gold has been put. Every noise you make in here echoes between the walls a few times before it fades out. South of you it seems like the corridor ends in a large cave while north of you it enters a small chamber. The scratching of small feet against the stone floor can occasionally be heard.

801: This is the northeastern part of the large hall and the ceiling here is painted in a dark blue colour. The walls are made of a black stone, delicately put together. 802:

The corpse of a stone statue is lying here.

This is the southeastern part of the large hall. The ceiling fades into a light blue colour in the corner, which makes a sharp contrast to the black stones in the wall. The stone floor is cold to the touch and dust swirls as you move around. Many statues of different dwarves have been put against the walls. Some of them look like they could start moving any second.
803: A stocky mountain mule is here, waiting to serve.

This is the southwestern part of a large hall. The wall is made of black stones, delicately put together to form the picture of a dwarf on the south wall. The ceiling is painted in a dark blue colour that fades into a lighter colour to the east. There is dust in the corners and an faint earthy smell lingers in the air.

A weapons rack stands against the wall.
A weapons rack stands against the wall.

A small rat runs about, oblivious to your presence.

This room is full of chests and other valuable things. Several racks have been placed along the southern wall and the eastern wall pictures dwarves celebrating the victory after a long war. West of you a large hall can be seen through a stone door.
805: The air in here is dry and cold and there is a vague earthy smell. The dust in the corners swirl as you pass by, but the floor is clean except from that. Beautiful paintings covers the stonewall to the west, while the eastern wall looks grey and naked. A handle can be seen protruding from the grey wall.

A corridor leads deep into the darkness to the north.

The corpse of a mottled snake is lying here.
The corpse of a watersnake is lying here.

You have fallen into a dark and ominous pit and when you reach the bottom, the trapdoor snaps shut behind you with a loud thud. The floor is covered by water to your knees, dark and full of junk. Since it is impossible to see what you are stepping on it is really hard to move around fast. There seems to be a well built of stone in the middle of the room, it is only two feet across and has hardly been used very often since green lichen covers it almost completely. Walls of stone surround you in every direction, fifteen feet high, where they reach the trapdoor above.
808:
A sign hangs on one wall.
Althof the shopkeeper is here, examining his inventory.

In these unhappy days colonies of Dwarves are spread far across Middle-earth, and Dwarves must sometimes travel far from their homes. The walls are covered in sacks and bags, fishing rods and tackles, and everything else that a travelling Dwarf might require on the road.
809: This quiet inlet is almost completely surrounded by lush green forest. The water from the river slowly creeps in from the west, and there is a small rocky beach on its north side. The branches from the huge trees extend well out into the middle of the inlet, scattering multi-coloured leaves that float in slow rhythmic swirls.
810: Huge boulders are strewn all about, making the trail quite tiresome to follow. Rocky hills rear high to all sides, but the path picks a way between them, turning here from west to south. An eerie silence seems to fill the air in an all-enveloping gloom.
811: You barely make your way around the boulders here, trying to keep track of the so-called path, which seems to stumble haltingly through the hills. In all directions rugged hills climb away from you, their summits covered with rocks, their slopes with loose scree.
812: The path is hard to keep track of and after a little while you can get quite frustrated. The path seems to continue to the west into the hills. To the south some small hilltops appear.

The wind blows with a cold chill here. To your excitement you can see a tiny trail to the west and to the south you can see small hills rise.
814: The path you try to keep travel along, is extremely difficult to walk upon because of all the rocks and boulders here constantly obstructing your way all the time. To the north, a large gorge is blocking your way, making travel there impossible, while to the east you are happy to see an old house. Both to the west and south, the landscape is the same as here, barren, cold and hard to walk upon.

A grey-cloaked elf is here, looking for the tracks of evil creatures.

You are standing in front of an old inn, probably not used for several decades. Judging by the look of the house, it looks like it was abandoned a long time ago. The roof, or what's left of it looks really rotten and the nonexisting door and glasses in the window adds up the general look of an really old building. There's a little fireplace here, and you can see a few bushes growing nearby.
816: The dry cold wind lashing over the cold plains up here makes travelling here a bit uncomfortable. The grass covers your feet entirely and you can't see any special path to follow. To the west you can see an old house, while the plains continues to the north.
817: When you stand in the middle of this plain, you feel like being lost in the wilderness up here. The grass covers your feet entirely and you can't see any special path to follow. To your puzzlement you can see an old building to the southwest of you. What kind of people live up here in these desolate areas? More plains open up to the south and east.
818: When you stand in the middle of this plain, you feel like being lost in the wilderness up here. The grass covers your feet entirely and you can't see any special path to follow. You can see plains in all your directions.

The wind blows gently in your face making you feel somewhat refreshed. You can see more plains to the west and northwest, but you can also notice a little trail to the north and east of you.

The trail is well-kept and you start to wonder who uses it that regulary up here in this cold area of Arda. Here, the trail seems however to end and you can't find any special track to follow. To the south and west of you there are plains, but the path continues to the east.

You are walking on a small trail leading towards more plains. The wind blows more cold up here, making you move on faster towards your unknown destination. 823: There are not that many bushes and grass left around you, and the surrounding has become a bit more rocky. To the far north you can see big mountains rise up in the distance, and it make you feel small and unimportant. Still - you can catch the sight of some grassy fields to the west, but the path continues to the north.
824:
A colourful butterfly is fluttering around here.
A boar cub is playing here, and exploring the wide world.

The path seems to be little used and it's not easy to keep track of it all the time. On both sides of the trail, you can see grass growing and you can hear some birds singing around you. This must surely be an uninhabited land. You feel lonely up here and the endless plains and rocky terrain adds that up much.
825: A giant rat patters against you, squeaking maliciously.

It must have been a long time since this inn was populated and gave shelter to weary travellers. Some old rotten furniture, shelves, a cot and a broken stone fireplace are all you can spot at first sight. The floor is littered with dirt and dead leaves. There is a ventilation shaft over the fireplace, but of no need as half of the roof is missing. The only exit is back south.

The corpse of a thief is lying here.

The corpse of a giant rat is lying here.

The stairway gives out creaking noises when you step on it, still it seems to hold your weight. A little backroom opens up to you when your eyes get used to the darkness down here. The room is very narrow, and the loose planks on the walls make this a very dull place. It must have been used as a wine and maybe beer storage room when the inn was operative. Still you wonder who made all the footprints you can clearly see on the floor. On the eastern wall you can see huge beerbarrels.
827: The corpse of a mean brigand is lying here.

You have made your way into the secret hideout of the local robbers of the Blue Mountains. It must be here that they stay when they are not sneaking around the trails, robbing innocent travellers on their way. On the southern side of the room are some beds and you can also see a table. There is also an old sofa here, covered with blankets. The room is poorly lit, but you can see that there is a lot of garbage thrown around here.
828:
An old-looking ring, covered with runes, lies here.
An old-looking ring, covered with runes, lies here.
A large stone chest is here.

This is the inner sanctum of the Brigands. This must be the treasure room, since it is separated from the main room. This room is also dimly lit, making you feel uncomfortable about this whole place. The only exit is to the west.
829: A mountain lion eyes you closely and prepares to pounce for his next meal.

You are walking among some grassy hilltops. There is no special path to walk upon here, but you travel fast and easy here anyway. The air seems to carry a strange feeling to you. Your further exploration to the north is blocked by a huge gorge making it impossible to travel there, while to the south you can see more small hills.
830: You are walking up and down on several small hilltops. The landscape around you is changing. You notice that the country begins to stretch out and to the north you can see some plains, while south, east and west you can see more hilltops.

This mountainous terrain makes you pretty exhausted, as you put much effort in moving around, up and down all these small hilltops. The hills look higher to the south. To the far south you can see a forest.
832: The hills here have become much rougher and rockier. You have to move very slowly up here, twisting your way between large boulders and stones. The surrounding area looks quite wasted and dead, but to the north you notice more hills and some of them are even covered with green grass.
833: The hills here have become much rougher and rocky. The so-called path you tried to follow is impossible to keep track of due to all the rocks and boulders you constantly have to make your way around. To the south you can see a forest, and you can also see a river flowing lazily southwards. To the north however, you can only see more hills.
834: As you travel further out on the flat plains you get more and more annoyed by the rocks and stones making it a pain to travel here. Now and then you can hear little sounds as if the rocks and boulders are suddenly coming alive.
835: As you make your way out on the flat highlands of the hill you find yourself obstructed by huge rocks and boulders spread out everywhere. You can see more rough terrain to the west while you can enter a valley to the north.
836: Walking around in this valley seems to be an easy job. The ground is barren and you can see no bushes or other places giving shelter here. You feel very exposed up here. In all directions around you, you can see other hilltops except to the south where you can see some forest.
837: You are standing in the middle of some small hills stretching both to the north and to the south. The hills climb and fall endlessly, but you notice that you slightly move upwards. The surrounding area look rather wasted, cold and dead. The hills continue to the north and to the south, while the eastern exit is blocked by huge boulders.
838: You are walking on some rolling hills. All these small hilltops making you go up and down all the time nearly make you feel dizzy. The landscape is barren and seems to be lifeless. The hills continue to the north and to the south.
839: You are walking on some rolling hills. You can see much more hills to the north of you. The landscape around you consists of hilltops, some partly grassy and some rocky. You can barely see the peaks of some mountains far away to the north. The wind is coming strongly from the north here, you better move on.
840: A horse of the Rohirrim is standing here, ridden by you.

You have entered a valley stretching east-west from here. The ground is barren, making it easy to travel upon. You can't see any special path to follow here. To your northeast you can see a large hilltop, probably the biggest landmark around here. To the south there seems to be no exit, but maybe you can squeeze your way through the rocks.
841: You find yourself in the midst of many small hills. The landcape seems to be the same in all directions; mostly hills everywhere with some huge boulders and rocks lying spread among them. To the north you see a rock face, making the way further north impossible.
842: You leave the safety of the trail below you and climb up on this huge mountain plateau. Not much vegetation grows here, but you find a little bit of comfort in enjoying the great view you have towards the huge range of mountains you can see to the far north, with its snowy peaks it truly is a majestic view. The hills continue to the west.
843: A colourful butterfly is fluttering around here.

The landscape has indeed changed. All around you, you see boulders, rocks and stones. Not much grows here, in fact you can see nothing else than rocks. A cool breath of air blows in your face, refreshing you from these weary travels. You see some small hills open up in front of you, while to the west you can spot a clearing.
844: A clear spring babbles as cool water trickles out of the ground.

You are standing at the base of a hill. The hill is so steep and prevents you from further exploration that way. You can spot some patches of grass and flowers growing here. The only exit is back east.

A colourful butterfly is fluttering around here.

The landscape has indeed changed. All around you, you see boulders, rocks and stones. Not much grows here, in fact you can see nothing else than rocks. The surrounding area looks pretty wasted and dead.

Far north of here you can see a mountain range, while east and west you see small hilltops. To the northwest you can see a hilltop. Maybe you get a better overview over the surrounding area from the top? The path continues to the north.

You made your way to the top. From here you can see pretty far away in all directions. To the north you see some forest and hills, westwards you see a river, it must be a branch of river Lhun. South of here you can see mostly rocky terrain and some plains and small clumps of forest. The only exit is back east, but you notice a huge rock here, slightly loose.
850: A clear spring babbles as cool water trickles out of the ground.

The path you try to keep travel along is extremely difficult to walk upon because of all the rocks and boulders here constantly obstructing your way all the time. There is a large amount of small pebbles around here, in all sizes and shapes, but most of them are covered with moss. On your western side there are small hills, while to the north the plains seem to continue.
851: The small hills surround you completely. The air here is cold and chilly, and you get a strange feeling... Or maybe it is only the fresh wind blowing steadily on your face all the time that annoys you. The landscape seems to change here and to the north and east you can enter some rocky plains.
852: A fierce boar is here, making grunting noises.

You find yourself in the middle of some plains, following no special trail. The grass that grows here covers your legs. To the south you can hear the sound of water. The plains seems however to end here and you can spot a little trail to follow to the north. The plains continues to the south.
853: You are standing in some quiet plains. The grass that grow to your waist sways gently in the wind and a few small bushes grows nearby. As you try to find a path to follow, you notice there are plains in all directions, save to the south where the river is slowly making its way southwards.

You are in some quiet plains. A few small bushes grow among the grass. There is a big river to the southeast.

You are standing next to a barn. There's an old well here, probably fully functionable providing water for the animals around here. There's a river flowing gently southwards to the east, and to the north you can see some plains.
856: A peaceful farmer is here, whistling merrily.

When you enter the barn, you notice it is used and inhabitated by animals. The smell is not that bad. Looking around you see a neatly-kept barn. The walls seem solid and you don't have to watch where you step. This could be a nice place to stay over night if you have nowhere else to stay.
857: You are standing in a small clearing. There is a small fireplace here, and small rocks placed around it to contain it. This would indeed be a nice and peaceful place to stop by and cook a meal. All around you are some small bushes and the ground seems to be more fertile here. To the north you can see a barn, while east runs a river that you just cant reach because the bank. There's a path leading to the south.

The vegetation here is thick and lush, of the very deepest green, each blade of grass long and broad. The field stretches further north, and there seems to be a small building, possibly a barn, standing to the north-east.
859: A well-fed cow stands here chewing her cud listlessly.

When you stand in the middle of this field, you can see that the grass is more thick and juicy than other places around you. This would definitely be appetizing to a cow. However - to the north the land grows more wild and you can see huge boulders and rocks around. The only exit is to the south.
860: Through this hidden entrance you have managed to go inside; a small cavern dimly lit by some torches hanging on the wall. This must be the very entrance to a dwarven mine. The air is rather dusty here. You can go further into the cave complex to the east, or you can go up.
861: Further into the cave, the walls have become smoother to the touch of your hands. Dust seems to be rising from below to rest under your feet. Some metal tracks run along the floor with an empty mining cart left unattended.

This seems to be a blindway. The tunnel is very narrow and stops suddenly here. It looks like the work here has been abandoned. Maybe because they did not find any ore? You see a huge black chasm open up when you look down.
863: A dwarven miner is here, digging the hard rock with his pick.

You find yourself standing in a big room. This must be one of the dozens of mineshafts probably in this cave complex. You can go further into the caves to the north, and to the east you see a smaller room.
864: You find yourself standing in a big room. This must be one of the dozens of mineshafts probably in this cave complex. The air is dusty and not clean at all. To the east you can see a hollow shaft covered with a plank.
