870: You have ended up on a dead end. Below you the water rushes past you. Further down towards the south the river moves lazily at a steady rate. The water from up here has indeed a long journey towards the Grey Havens.

872: From here you can go north to a trail or enjoy your stay here by the river. The path you travel upon is broad and wide, making it a pleasure to travel. You just admire the river and you are appalled by its greatness. It mesmerizes you whispering about the tales of the old in your ear.
873: A nightingale is here, chirping a sweet melody.

The trail is wide and well-worn, making it a pleasure to walk upon. To both sides some grass and small trees grow. You can hear the birds singing around you, and you can hear the bubbeling sound of water not far away. The path continues to the south and east.

Some strange force regenerates you in some way. At least you think it is the case. Maybe it is just some kind of magic acting on your mind?

The rhythmical beat of axe to wood is in sharp contrast to the otherwise serene atmosphere.

Eastwards the track continues, and the entrance to the hut is just to your west.

It is a stone wheel, powered by a crank on one side. The double edged axe that hangs from the wall suggests that this a lumber-jack hut.
880: A robin is here, carrying small pieces of wood to its nest.

The forest is rather thick here, making you feel a tad uncomfortable. The trees are growing very close to each other. The thick vegetation here makes it hard to move on deeper into the forest. The place is shady because only a few sunbeams reach the soft ground here. To the south you can see some huge pawprints.

999: Small rock shards poke here and there among the sparse and sometimes mottled yellow grass, which is the only vegetation here. Dense sharp bushes prevent you from going east, and this natural wall continues further north.
1000: Under the somewhat underfed wild grass, the soil is mixed with some pebbles. A few weeds bring somber patches of colour in the landscape. The dense thicket that continues southwards blocks your way east. Similar obstacles can be seen in the distance, to the north and the south-west.
1001:
A brown snake watches you.
A brown snake watches you.
A sharp-eyed hawk is here stalking some prey.

The ground is covered by sharp weeds and strewn with small shrubs, making travel painful for anyone lacking boots or thick skin. To the north a great thicket of thorny bushes grows. Some kind of building lies west of this vegetal barrier.
1002: Grass and shrubs grow wild all around. The ground is broken making traveling difficult. Here and there among the grass large stones stick out like giant heads. To the south and northwest a large thicket of thorny bushes grow. An especially large rock stands here, perched on top of it, a vacant hawk's nest. East the grasslands opens south and north. Far behind them the hills grow tall.
1003: A small boar with big yellow tusks looks eager to fight.

This dense thicket is surrounded by man-high thorny bushes. The air is stale, as wind can not penetrate this far into the bushes. The branches that are reaching towards the sky forms a canopy, making this a natural shelter. A rough path coming from the east allows access to a slight depression of bare earth.
1004: Grass and shrubs grow wild all around. The ground is broken making traveling difficult. Here and there among the grass a large stone sticks out like a giant head. Some thorny bushes grow northwest. A small bird maybe a finch sings merrily somewhere among the shrubs.
1005: Grass and shrubs grow wild all around. The ground is broken making traveling difficult. Thick thorny bushes grow middle of some rocks and shrubs. In the south they become so thick that entering them is impossible. In the east rough grasses and shrubs continue. Little ways off in the northwest is another thicket.
1006: Many holes in the ground make footing treacherous. Many rocks and dense shrubs slow down progress through these desolate plains. Looking closer however the grasses and shrubs are teaming with insect life and many birds fly around catching them. Some bushes grow here and there, and behind them plains seem to continue every direction.
1007: Many holes in the ground make footing treacherous. Many rocks and dense shrubs slow down progress through these desolate plains. Looking closer however the grasses and shrubs are teaming with insect life and many birds fly around catching them. Some bushes grow here and there, and behind them plains seem to continue every direction.
1008: A sparrow is flapping around on the ground.

Many holes in the ground make footing treacherous. Many rocks and dense shrubs slow down progress through these desolate plains. Looking closer however the grasses and shrubs are teaming with insect life and many birds fly around catching them. Some bushes grow here and there, and behind them plains seem to continue every direction.
1009: A swallow flies high above the ground.

While the outer vegetation of this thicket is rather low and dense, the shrubs here in its centre grow much higher, reaching for the dim light above. The bare stems near the ground level allow an easy passage for any wildlife around here. Large patches of earth have been overturned, uprooting the vegetation that grew there and creating a clearing in the thicket.
1010: Some bushes to dodge and lots of rocks and holes to hop over. Those elements dominate these rough plains. In the northwest the bushes become impenetrable and to the southwest is a sinister-looking pile of boulders. However there is some open ground between the boulders and bush and with some determination one might be able to pass through. To the east the land is open until the hills start to rise taller and taller.
1012: Many holes in the ground make footing treacherous. Many rocks and dense shrubs slow down progress through these desolate plains. Looking closer however the grasses and shrubs are teaming with insect life and many birds fly around catching them. Some bushes grow here and there, and behind them plains seem to continue every direction.
1013: Some bushes grow here providing hiding places for small creatures that hide before you can see them. The hill side east of here is almost vertical. South, west and north the flat ground continues.
1014:
A sparrow is flapping around on the ground.
A rabbit is here eyeing your presence warily.
The garden snake slithers harmlessly here.
A sharp-eyed hawk is here stalking some prey.
Some bushes grow here. Square pieces of rock lie on the ground. The hill side east of here is almost vertical. South, west and north the flat ground continues.
1015: A swallow flies high above the ground.

Some bushes grow here. Square pieces of rock lie on the ground. The hill side east of here is almost vertical. South and west the flat ground continues. To the north a path winds its way through the rough plains.
1016: The ground is very broken here. Stones and grasses make traveling tiring and unpleasant. Some large boulders have rolled down the hill northeast long time ago.
1017: Many holes in the ground make footing treacherous. Many rocks and dense shrubs slow down progress through these desolate plains. Looking closer however the grasses and shrubs are teaming with insect life and many birds fly around catching them. Some bushes grow here and there, and behind them plains open to the north, east and west. South and southwest a small hill rises above the plains.
1018: Grass and shrubs grow wild all around. The ground is broken making traveling difficult. Here and there among the grass large stones stick out like giant heads. In the west an enormous pile of rock rises from the plains. It is almost size of a small hill. In the south is a small hill. Grasslands continue in other directions.
1019: The hill drops down steeply to the east and north. Small flowers dot the ground around an old twisted tree. The land to the north descend in gentle waves westward. Large thickets of some dark bushes stand out like islands middle of the golden sea. Many birds fly in flocks above the plains, and high above them almost out sight a lone hawk circles looking for his prey. In the east is another hill top. Down below the drop little ways to the north a large mound of some kind is built.
1020: There is a lot of water on the ground.

This appears to be the ruin of an old outpost. After examining the place you discover that this was a dwarven outpost, but nothing is left except from a few broken stone tables. The floor here is filled with rubble from the roof and the walls.
1021: There is a lot of water on the ground.

The plains in this area seem to change into a more desolate area as you look to the east and northeast. The plains continues south as far as your eyes can see. West of here a very tall and thick brush can be seen. While looking north you suddenly notice what appears to be some very old ruins.
1022:
There is a lot of water on the ground.
A brown fox is here, looking for some rabbits to chew up.

You bend down to peer at a small thorny bush. Its endurance in harsh conditions inspires you to hope that the harsh plains will offer you something to gain. The greens to the west seem to be the growths on the outside of a rock.
1023:
A brown fox is here, looking for some rabbits to chew up.
A brown fox is here, looking for some rabbits to chew up.
A brown fox is here, looking for some rabbits to chew up.

These plains seem to stretch on endlessly. The ground is hard, composed mainly of sand and rock, but this does not seem to deter the abundant grasses and weeds that grow everywhere. A few spots of colour are visible where wildflowers manage to survive.
1024:
A large rabbit looks peacefully at you, ready to dart away.
A large rabbit looks peacefully at you, ready to dart away.

Flat, treeless land continues in all directions with the exception of an extremely thorny section of bush to the west. Travel in that direction would result in the skin of the creature attempting the passage being ripped to shreds by the strong, sharp thorns sticking from the branches on the bushes.
1025:
An intact skeleton of a man is walking around here.
An intact skeleton of a man is walking around here.
An intact skeleton of a man is walking around here.

Certainly this was built for men of ages past. There is no entry to this structure. Tedious must have been the labor to build such housings. No doorway is visible anywhere. Some boulders larger than others stick out of the pile like spikes from a morningstar. There is an ominous feeling in the air, like a sudden thunderstorm that has been brewing from the beginning of time is about to strike. Stone black as night stands on the side of the mound. Strange whispers echo in the air. Tales of fear and terror beyond words come to mind to those who listen.
1026:
An erect shrub with green pinnate leaves is growing here.
A horse of the Rohirrim is standing here, ridden by you.

Large berry bushes grow wild here. To the north they become increasingly thicker, until a point where they are far to dense to allow one to see what lies behind. To the south the bushes have failed to grow as thickly. Going that way might make for easier travelling.
1027: A rabbit is here eyeing your presence warily.

The hill slopes down eastward. Grass grows tall upon its shoulders, and here and there small white and yellow flowers sway in the breeze. The lands to the north descend in gentle waves westward. Large thickets of some dark bushes stand out like islands in the middle of the golden sea. Many birds fly in flocks above the plains, and high above them almost out sight a lone hawk circles looking for his prey. West is another hill top.
1028: A badger is here, exploring for food.

The ground slopes a bit to the west and south. Grasses grow shorter here than to the north where the land is much rougher. A tall row of evergreen bushes grows to the south. West is a long low hill and east seems to be a small field of some kind.
1029:
Some delicious wild strawberries grow on the ground.
Some delicious wild strawberries grow on the ground.
Some delicious wild strawberries grow on the ground.
Some delicious wild strawberries grow on the ground.
Some delicious wild strawberries grow on the ground.
Some delicious wild strawberries grow on the ground.
Some delicious wild strawberries grow on the ground.
Some delicious wild strawberries grow on the ground.

The grass here is thick and healthy, but does not grow quite as high as in the surrounding areas. Finding oneself walking amongst thousands of small white flowers, which merrily bow in the breeze, ones heart becomes content and dark thoughts once so close vanish into thin air. Don't you wish, that this was the strawberry season, because that is what these little plants are. Ground slopes down from west to east. Northward the various bushes and shrubs make travel more difficult.
1030: A small tree grows here next to a strange shaped stone. To the south the Tower hills continue. To the west rough plains extend far and wide. And beyond, somewhere far in the distance, enveloped in the mists is the Blue Mountain range where rumor tells dwarves still dwell. To the north and east are many hills, which are covered by shrubs and stones. Down below to the north is a long narrow vale, which pokes like a finger from the open lands in the west into the hills in the east. The landscape has a rough and wild look.
1031: A finch flies low above the ground.
The hills start growing in the east. To the north and west the valley continues. In the south a steep hillside stops you from taking that course. West is also a path through the hills.
1032:
A sturdy billy goat stands here, proudly protecting his goats.
A goat is here, grazing in the hills.
The flowering shrubs sway gently in the wind. The hills begin to grow taller as you move to the north or west.
1033: Hill Covered with Shrubs and Stones

A lonely goatherd stands here, watching his herd of goats.
A goatherd's dog is here.

Rocks sizing from pebbles to large rocks make the slopes more difficult to descend or ascend. The brushwood spreads its fragrant smell all around you. To the north is a bit taller hill and to the west is a path, but the slope is too steep for a safe climb. In the south it is possible to descend into a narrow vale. In the east the hills continue far into the horizon.
1043: The hill slopes steadily down into a small glade, in the west, between the hills. The hills are coming to an end. A small mound is still to the west but main part of the hills are to the south and east. The ground is covered by many interesting rocks and shrubs.
1044: Large rocks lie on the ground. Wild bushes grow all around. The land is flat except to the north where a small arm of the hill extends towards the west. The birds and insects sing and buzz in the air, busily going about their business.
1045:
A squirrel scampers around here, looking for nuts from the trees.
A swallow flies high above the ground.

Numerous large rocks and rock piles in these grasslands provide shelter and hiding places for many small animals. Nearby is a very large one, thrice the height of a man. It has a pair of swallows' nests, built by swallows of course, under a small ledge.
1046: A swallow flies high above the ground.

The tall trees grow close together everywhere, and their branches high above cast dark shadows on the ground. Birds fly from tree to tree hunting for insects that are also here in swarms. The sound of water comes from the west. Some tree stumps among the thick layer of dry leaves indicate that men with axes visited these woods a long time ago. The underbrush is mainly of ferns, which grow here and there in the boggy depressions in the ground.
1047: The garden snake slithers harmlessly here.

The large trees block out the heat of the sun and provide shelter from the wind and rain. A small footpath runs from the east to west among the trees. Some birds fly high above within the dark green foliage. The ground is covered by some thick and wide leafed grasses, which grow in small patches from the rich muddy soil.
1048: A pleasant glen is formed between the embracing arms of the hills. Small berry bushes grow here and there. South, below a tall and steep hillside, a small hut is built. A path leads to it from the west, and other paths lead to small bushes to the east and to a fenced area apparently set up to keep sheep or goats.
1051: A finch flies low above the ground.

High above in the sky the branches of a huge oak tree swing back and forth in the wind. It stands alone by the thickets that grow over the stream to the south. The trunk is too smooth and slippery and the branches way too high for any save the squirrels to climb this tree. The ground gets muddier to the south. From the west comes the sound of water.
1052: The hill slopes eastward down into a small flat area between the hills. Soothing sounds of the wind moving in the grass surround you. A small berry bush grows here among the grass. The ground opens wider to the south.
1053:
A heron is stalking the area, looking for fish.
A swarm of mosquitoes is here, humming around you.
A colourful butterfly is fluttering around here.
A finch flies low above the ground.

Too shallow to swim in and too narrow for boating, this small stream makes its way from the thickets south and southeast to the more open water northwest. Some bushes grow on the banks. West bank is drier than that in the east. Weeping willow waves slowly in the wind on the east shore.
1054: Winding Waterway by a Small Hill

Here the stream sweeps gracefully past the base of a small hill, which seems to mark the end of the Tower Hills, which give way to the plains to the west. A narrow trail winds lazily along the banks of the stream, and small yellow flowers grow among the lush grass.
1055: A small plant grows here, with long, pointed leaves and flowers at its top.

Tall poplars grow here like green pillars supporting the sky. Bushy willows with silvery leaves sway in the wind. The stream flows in the east, but ground there is soft and willows form an impenetrable thicket. Going there is senseless. North a small hillock stands overlooking a stream.
1056:
A swarm of mosquitoes is here, humming around you.
A swarm of mosquitoes is here, humming around you.
The garden snake slithers harmlessly here.

The stream winds gently through the sprawling hills. Here it is very shallow, with a bed comprised of small stones, which create a multicoloured pathway, stable and secure for wading. To the north, the stream narrows somewhat, and becomes a little deeper and more turbulent, but upstream, to the southeast it appears to be smaller, suggesting that this area is located not far from the source of the waterway. The waterway east is blocked by a thicket of willows.
1057: The garden snake slithers harmlessly here.

The stream flows quietly east of here through thickets of willows and water plants. The ground here is very soft and your feet often sink deep into the mud. Southward the ground gets firmer and a row of tall poplars grow, from east to west. Behind them is a small trail among the hills. Insects swarm thick in the air and the area provides them with plenty of places to breed in.
1058: A swarm of mosquitoes is here, humming around you.

Numerous willow bushes grow in the stream which is quite narrow and shallow. To the north they form an unpassable thicket. The water is only knee high. Many aquatic weeds and grasses poke their leaves above the surface. The bottom of the stream is soft and muddy. The ground gets firmer eastward where a tall forest grows. In the south the water continues upstream towards its source. In the west willows grow on the streambank.
1059:
A brown bear is sleeping here.
A swallow flies high above the ground.

With the strength of ten men the bear has dug itself a small nest into the hills side. The ground is covered by a thick layer of dry leaves. The walls are round. The floor is flat and dry. This would be a pleasant little hole if the smell of the bear wasn't so thick in the air. Maybe it's better to leave quickly.
1060:
A heron is stalking the area, looking for fish.
A heron is stalking the area, looking for fish.
A swallow flies high above the ground.
A sparrow is flapping around on the ground.

The soft sandy bottom invites a weary adventurer to remove the sweaty boots and wade in the cool waters. A tall beech grows on the west shore. The river flows slowly from the southwest to the northeast. The river is too deep to cross without a boat or by swimming.
1061: A badger is here, exploring for food.

Tall grass stands on this small hill. The sun has dried the vegetation and it now blows in the wind making soothing sounds. The battle of good and evil seems far away. On the gentle slope a large pine tree grows alone surrounded by grasses and shrubs.
1062: The river flows gently through the rough wilderness. Small shrubs and trees grow on the banks. It is time to desert your boat if you want to continue upstream. The river shrinks to a small stream southeast, too overgrown for a boat.
1063: A swallow flies high above the ground.

Tall willows grow wild here, drinking the waters of the river. In the west they became impenetrable. To the north the river continues downstream. To the south is a small trail making its way through the wilderness.
1081: The large road runs from the east to the west. Occasional animal noises can be heard from the bushes that grow by the side of the road. To the north some water can be seen glimmering in the distance.
1082: An elf is here walking around.

The large road is cutting through the hills like a sharp knife; whoever it was that built it must have been very good at mining. Some tufts of grass grow on the road and some trees grow beside it. The road bends west and north here.
1083: There is a lot of water on the ground.

An offshoot of the small stream to the west covers much of the road here with a few inches of water that are easily waded through. Perhaps someday someone might build a bridge over this piece of land if the water level rises and it becomes a hinderance to passage along this often travelled road. Following the road will take you east or south.
1084:
A fierce boar is here, making grunting noises.
A boar cub is playing here, and exploring the wide world.
A boar cub is playing here, and exploring the wide world.

Along the road some small trees grow providing shade for the tired travellers that pass this way. In the north and south the great Tower Hills reach for the sky. The road continues to the north and west.
1104: There is some snow on the ground.

The Road to the Grey Havens bends south-west here. South of the road are plains and to the north and east is a group of trees. It's nothing like a forest but it is so big that you can't see how far it stretches to the north. There are tracks leading north-east into the trees.
1105: There is some snow on the ground.

The Road to the Grey Havens bend north-east here. The countryside to the south is pretty uninteresting. Just empty plains and occasionally some vegetation. The road shows signs of years of use, like tracks of horses and horse-wagons. There are ruts in the road which makes progress a bit annoying.
1106: The Road to the Grey Havens
There is some snow on the ground.

The Road to the Grey Havens goes east-west here. The road is in a good condition. To the north is an area with bushes and trees. You hear a humming coming from the north and you see bees flying around. You notice tracks on the ground leading northwards. South of the road are plains filled with bushes and other small plants.
1107: The Road to the Grey Havens
There is some snow on the ground.

The Road to the Grey Havens goes east-west here. Bushes are to north and south of the road and further northwest you see a group of trees. The bushes in the north look like someone is tending them, the ones in the south don't. Also there is more life in the area north-west of you than in the south.
1108: The Road to the Grey Havens
There is some snow on the ground.

The Road to the Grey Havens bends south-west here. The road is surrounded by boring looking plains. There isn't much vegetation growing in the plains just a few bushes and a tree every mile or so. A broken tent is scattered over the ground just south of the road.
1112: The Road to the Grey Havens bends south-west here. In the east you can see a a well-tended path leading into the dense vegetation. In the north the road is bordered by undergrowth that is too dense to enter. South of the road is the savanna - a place full of life.
1113: The Road to the Grey Havens bends north-east here. In the north-east the road is bordered by dense vegetation making it impossible to go there. To the south and west of the road lies the savanna. The road shows signs of years of use but is still in a quite good condition.
1115: There is a lot of water on the ground.

The road goes east and west, leading to lands full of mystery and adventure. Everything around you is quiet and still, and the soft hum in the air gives life to this place. To the west, you know you will find the legendary Grey Havens, a place where, it's said, the magic of the past ages can still be found.
1116: The road keeps going, leading to uncommon places. If you follow it westwards, it will lead you to the gates of the Grey Havens, just at the shore of the sea. South of the road, you see a very rough field and to the north, a grove so dense that it is impossible to walk through it.
1117: The road bends here, going south and west. Towards east and north, you can see very dense groves which makes passage in those directions extremely difficult. However, you can barely manage to get into the grove through a small passage in the north. To your south, you see empty lands, too uneven to allow passage.
1118: The road bends here, going north and east. To the east, you can see a field of tall, green grass. In the northeast, you see a very dense group of tall and dark trees standing silently. You get a strange, uneasy feeling just looking at those trees. To your west are some rough looking fields which grow too uneven in your south to pass through.
1119:
A tree-snake lies wrapped around one of the tree branches.
A tree-snake lies wrapped around one of the tree branches.

You have made your way up in the tree. There are many huge branches here, making you feel secure. Maybe this would be a good resting place. To the north you get a view of the forest. It seems to clear up not far to the north, and you see some mountainous terrain through the haze.
1122: You are standing right in front of the huge east gate of the legendary city of Grey Havens. High and marvellous, white marble-walls tower up above you. The gate in front of you is made from the finest wood and sheathed with silver and mithril. You are overwhelmed by the breathtaking eminence of this large Elven seaport. Beside the road there is a sign mounted on a post.
1124: A light boat made of reeds has been left here.

Most of this cave is underwater and continously fed by waves coming in from the north. The southern part of the cave slopes up gently until it reaches a dry rocky plateau. Green algae hang from the ceiling and off of rocky walls. The only visible exit lies in the north and leads out into the Gulf of Lhun.
1125: An arrow lies on the ground.

Salty air reaches here through a slime covered opening to the north while a tunnel leads off to the south into darkness. Green water runs down from the ceiling and along the walls making the ground here quite slippery. As waves hit against the outside of this enclosure, the walls vibrate, sending small sprays of slime through the air.
1126: The corpse of a giant rat is lying here.

The air in here is thick and not all of the odours can be attributed to originating from decaying plant matter. Green slime covers all sections of the tunnel with the exception of some solid pieces of matter that litter the ground. Off in the northern distance the rhythmic sounds of waves can be heard as they crash against obstructions.
1127:
A giant rat patters against you, squeaking maliciously.
A small rat runs about, oblivious to your presence.
A small rat runs about, oblivious to your presence.
A small vicious black rat squeaks at you for disturbing it.
A giant rat patters against you, squeaking maliciously.
A trained horse (Rood) is standing here.

Bits of grass has been tucked in under mud and slime making this area into a nest of sorts. It is not hard to tell what has been eaten here, bones litter the area along with a few smaller skulls. The nest reeks of rat faeces that has accumulated over many years. The only way to leave here is to the east.
1128: The corpse of a giant rat is lying here.

The ceiling, walls and floor of this long tunnel are covered in green slime. Long trails of slime run down from the ceiling making it difficult to pass through this tunnel without getting some of it on oneself. Peculiar designs on the floor suggest that something has recently disturbed the gooey mass. The tunnel ends abruptly to the south and bends westwards into the darkness.
1129: This passage is quite narrow and not very high. The ceiling has partially fallen down in a number of places leaving rocks and earth blocking parts of the passage. Slime covers the damp northern wall and occasional sounds of distant crashing waves can be heard.
1130: A huge black fungus is here, exuding a foul stench.

This hole is very cramped and dark with only a small opening upwards. The chamber consists simply of a hollowed out sand pit, though exactly how the pit was created is not evident. There are a few rotten wood planks visible along the sides of the pit suggesting that at one time it may have been used as a storage facility. Below some planks to the north, a small opening is visible.
1131:
There is a lot of water on the ground.
The corpse of a small brown snake is lying here.
An arrow lies on the ground.
The bushes here seem to irritate your lower legs but you continue further. You can continue north into the seemingly thickening bushes, or go back south where the bushes seem more open.
1132:
A small brown snake is slithering around here.
A small brown snake is slithering around here.
A small brown snake is slithering around here.

Here you can see the bushes thicken into a thorny thicket. You wonder what life could have once lived here in such a confining area, but you see that you can continue further, going east, or you can return to the trail south.
1133:
There is a lot of water on the ground.
The butchered corpse of a boar is lying here.

You can sense that the bushes get thicker here as you trudge on. That sense of adventure in you instinctively tells you that everything here is safe and friendly. The passage through these bushes runs north-south.
1134: It's nothing to be worried about, you explain to yourself, as you see that the thicket is really quite normal and harmless. You tediously make your way through the restrictive branches as you notice that you can go south and west.
1135:
There is a lot of water on the ground.
The corpse of a dreadful snake is lying here.
A large brown snake with black patches is coiled here.
You resist scratching a cut from the thorny thicket as you trudge further through. Something, you think, must be out there. But you can only accept your fate and continue on your way.
1139: There is a lot of water on the ground.

Indeed, your presaging thoughts prove to be trustworthy. The thicket seems to come alive at you, both irritating your skin and stinging your eyes. You worry that if you go further, you might not be able to return. Yet, you trust your instincts, and continue north.
1140: There is a lot of water on the ground.

You shiver as you hear strange animal noises about you, and you look quickly back only to be relieved that you can still retreat south. To the north you see that you could squeeze through the passage in the thicket, yet you are unsure that you really should.
1141: There is a lot of water on the ground.

After making your way through that tiny passageway, you wonder how it was possible for you to enter it. You hear the sound of water nearby. Maybe it's the great river of Lhun flowing thru here? To the east you can spot a exit further into the small bushes, while you can see a bit more dense bushes to the south.
1142: A huge, poisonous spider is here.

Some light shines in through the cracks above you, but that doesn't make it easier to perceive the surroundings since the air is full of a greyish mist. To the north a black cave opens up. There is a smell of wild animals here, and not unlikely it emanates from some big predator.
1143:
A great wolf with coal-black eyes stares intently at you, drooling saliva.
A fierce bat is here, lusting for your blood.

This cave would otherwise be completely dark if it were not for your light source. Travellers who successfully made their way past here have left their marks on the cave wall. You carefully step around the huge boulders in the cave, noticing a musty smell coming from the north, and what seems to be a light mist to the south.
1144:
A bloodthirsty bat is sleeping here.
A bloodthirsty bat is sleeping here.
A fierce bat is here, lusting for your blood.
A fierce bat is here, lusting for your blood.

You enter a cave covered in moss and light fungus growing on the sides. The musty smell is hardly bearable, and your boots squish on the slime underneath. To the south you see an impending continuation of the cave.
1145:
There is a lot of snow on the ground.
A pack horse is standing here, ridden by you.

It's very hard to find your way through this thick shrubbery. The bushes seem to grow thinner to the north, while to the west they thicken drastically. The way east is effectively blocked by a sheer rock, covered by thorny bushes. To the south the thicket seems somewhat yielding, almost elastic.
1146: There is a lot of water on the ground.

West and East of here the hazels grow high, making it impossible to journey in those directions. To the north one can barely hear the trickle of a small forest stream. Further south, the dark yet yielding bushes extend further. The ground is covered with brown vegetation. The only visible parts of the soil are the black rocks which stick up above the bushes.
1147: The trees get denser here, and the stream has become smaller and smaller. There is no undergrowth here, just the trees above you and some rotting materials on the ground. To the west the stream flows silently towards the Lhun. Travel north and east is blocked by some thick shrubbery, while the thicket looks less dense to the south.
1148: The trees around you loom overhead as the sky above suddenly disappears. The water here is shallow enough to easily wade through. There is almost no undergrowth around the stream, since the towering trees allow no sunlight to reach the ground. One can feel a smell of decay to the east, while to the west the air smells fresher.
1149: There is some snow on the ground.

A shallow stream flows lazily through the forest. Around it, the trees grow high and thick, casting a thick shade on the ground. The water itself flows from east to west in a steady pace. Eastward the trees grow thicker together, while to the west the path seems lighter.
1150: As you walk along the small path you cant help to notice a small and peaceful forest a little east of you. Maybe it would be a good place to enter while taking a rest. To the west you see the worn trail and beyond the trail is the river.
1151:
There is a lot of water on the ground.
A clear spring babbles as cool water trickles out of the ground.
A tall and strong hunter is standing here.

You have entered, what appears to be, a frequently used resting place. Quite a few trees surround this campsite giving you shelter from the wind. It would appear that quite a few adventures have found this the perfect place to make camp for the night. Between a few rocks you see a small spring flowing north. Several branches have been burned here. The plains continues in all directions from here. You can use this place to sleep and to refresh yourself at the spring.
1152: You delightfully look upon this small red wooden home, which might have once housed a hunter or another protector of the land. A makeshift table and bed once provided lodging, and can do so once again for your own choosing.
1153: A number of bushes have been able to find a hold within the sand that covers the ground here. Though the area is mostly sand, a number of small boulders have lodged themselves deep into the earth and would likely be difficult to move. Instead of the sand having been blown flat from the sea breeze reaching it from the west, it has landed in piles making this ground uneven. A predominately sandy region continues to the south while the bushes increase northwards.
1154: Luscious grass grows amongst small thorny bushes on the slopes that rise gradually to the north and south. A path of pressed down vegetation continues further east along the floor of the valley. Though you could scramble up the valley's edge to the south, northwards a high rock wall makes passage impossible.
1155: A variety of grasses grow here abundantly though some of them have been flattened by a heavy creature walking through here frequently. The valley ends by a cluster of thornbushes in the east. Southwards the valley walls are quite steep. A rock wall at the northern edge prevents you from travelling in that direction.
1156: Thorny bushes completely surround you on all sides except for a small path leading through them to the west. Pieces of brown fur have been caught on some of the thorns and sway gently back and forth in a light breeze. A small depression dug into the ground is covered with broken and gnawed bones.
1157:
A sparrow is flapping around on the ground.
A trained horse (my) is standing here, ridden by you.

Gently sloping ground northwards leads down into a small valley. Here the earth is covered with a thick blanket of dark green grass. A piece of driftwood has somehow ended up on this field. The grass becomes much thinner as it encounters less fertile ground westwards. Some fresh dug up earth lies on the ground near a small hill to the east.
1158: A sparrow is flapping around on the ground.

In sharp contrast to the rocky regions west of here, the ground is mostly covered in sand leaving it soft and hard to walk on. Interspersed among the sand are a few rockslabs that must stem from the cliffs to the west. The sand continues to the north and south and some of it has travelled east on the brisk wind. Sounds of the sea reach you from the distant west.
1159: A large rabbit looks peacefully at you, ready to dart away.

The ground here is covered mostly with rock plates and a number of giant boulders. Sand has found its way between every crack and crevice among the rocks. A strong breeze blows here from the west and carries with it the salty scent of a large body of water. Sounds of waves hitting shore and the cries of gulls fill the air.
1160: This region is neither all sand nor all rocks. A fast flowing stream cuts off the area to the south, its steep and muddy shores preventing descending into the water. Little vegetation grows here with the exception of a few hardy grasses. Northwards the sand increases while the soil becomes softer to the east. From the distant west you can make out the sounds of a sea.
1161:
Clusters of slender stems and tall leaves thrive in the mud and shallows.
A worm is here slithering around.

Thick growth of bulrushes cover this area completely hiding the moist ground from view. Sedges and cattails have somehow managed to find spots to grow alongside the bulrushes. A fast flowing river runs by to the south supplying this area with large amounts of water. A sandy region lies westwards and to the north bushier vegetation grows.
1162: A massive fire must have raged through here some time ago. Most of the original vegetation in this area has died and what little remained of it is black and dying. Some tiny light green grasses have begun pushing their way through the ash surface. The remains of a tall tree lie among the ashes. There is no sign as to how and why the fire started here.
1163: The wind must have carried some burning matter onto this field from elsewhere, as parts of this grass field have been scorched. There are only a few blackened spots, mostly ones surrounding burnt branches. The rest of the field is covered in a mixture of long green grass interspersed with a few golden grains.
1164: Long grass can be seen all around, gently swaying in a light breeze. Parts of the grass has been trampled down, creating small paths that branch off and take a number of headings. The height of the grass here could easily hide numerous creatures without them being detected. In the south the plains give way to a swampy region of land.
1165: The grass is fairly short here but quite thick. A thorny section of brush cuts off the landscape to the north. A large number of dandelions have taken over parts of the field, creating a sharp contrast between their brilliant yellow colours and various shades of green. The fields of grass continue towards the east and south.
1166: A large rabbit looks peacefully at you, ready to dart away.

Thick grass grows in this area, mostly due to a watery region to the south that nourishes these plains. Further north where water is less plentiful vegetation becomes drier and less diverse. Small paths are visible leading through the grass in various directions, their origins unknown. The uncut plains continue both to the east and west.
1167: A fast flowing river cuts through the landscape here as it spews to the surface from underground somewhere in the east and again dives down into a narrow underground tunnel in the west. The water here is remarkably clear, revealing a gravely bottom. Bullrushes cover a marshy ground above the tunnel westwards, making any travel above ground there impossible. Tall trees rise empore to the south indicating a foresty terrain. Towards the north a grassy field sways in a light breeze.
1168: The clear water flows at a fast pace to the west here. Along with small white stones, small tussocks of lush, green grass cover the riverbank to the south. In the north-east the highest peaks of the Tower Hills can be spotted.
1169: The cold waters of this wild river flow steadily on, indifferent to any change of scenery on the banks. North of here one can venture into the rubble of the beginnings of the Tower Hills. An old and proud pine forest grows on the river bank to the south. South-east you can catch a glimpse of a high tower.
1170:
An elf is here walking around.
An elf is here walking around.
A fierce boar is here, making grunting noises.
A boar cub is playing here, and exploring the wide world.

Large, impressive and infertile are the hills that fill the landscape. The only things that grow here are some small windswept bushes that somehow have managed to get a foothold in the rocky hills. To the north and west the land changes drastically, levelling out into vast grassy fields. A river can be seen to the south.
1171:
A well-fed cow stands here chewing her cud listlessly.
A well-fed cow stands here chewing her cud listlessly.

These fields are covered with short juicy grass that appears perfect for cattle to graze in. A few bushes are scattered across the fields and an occasional tree can be spotted here and there. To the north and west the fields spread out and to the south a river runs wildly. Looking east, large hills fill your vision.
1172: There is a lot of water on the ground.

Short juicy grass covers the ground, making travel easy and comfortable. Small animals play in the grass making all kinds of strange noises. To the south and east large hills are rising towards the sky and to the west the grassy fields spread out.
1173:
There is a lot of water on the ground.
A fierce boar is here, making grunting noises.
A boar cub is playing here, and exploring the wide world.
The wild ox seems ready to charge you.
A fierce boar is here, making grunting noises.
A boar cub is playing here, and exploring the wide world.

Lush green grass covers the ground here and among it a few delicate flowers grow. Though the area continues to be mostly grass to the east and south, west of here the ground becomes less fertile. In the far north-east a forest can be distinguished.
1174: Clusters of slender stems and tall leaves thrive in the mud and shallows.

The earth here has completely vanished and given way to a sticky, watery mud like substance. It is impossible to avoid sinking in here since the mud offers little resistance. The only dry land accessible is westwards or north. Though a bridge is present to the south any movements here only cause you to sink down further and the distant bridge would be too high to reach. Flowing water to the east contributes to the wetness here.
1175: From east to west, this wild and desolate river continues its journey. All around, peaks of cliffs and rocks block out any possible glimpse of an unbroken horizon - this is not the place for spectacular views! South of here there seems to be some sort of landing.
1176: The river meanders through the hills at a steady pace, slowly finding a route towards its ultimate goal. Between the hills to the south one can glimpse a large tower that seems to be the only sign of habitation within this area. The river flows on to the west, while the rocky hills that shade the water continue to the east.
1177: Here among the ancient Tower Hills the wild river flows steadily on. There seems to be little wildlife in this barren and rocky part of Arda. The river continues its journey south. Travelling upstream to your east could be a less tiring alternative compared to a trip into the hills themselves.
1178: The wild river flows steadily on, following the ancient riverbed carved deep into the softer soil between the unyielding cliffs. The water is clear and chilly. Travelling upstream to your east might be a less tiring alternative to a trip into the hills themselves.
1179: The cold, clear water flows in a westerly direction. The river is quite deep, but you can distinguish that the bottom consists of sharp rocks. To the east high cliffs lean to the river. On the south bank, a small mountain path twists its way among the rocky hills.
1180: The river takes a turn here, bending from east to south. Where the river turns, erosion has dug out large potholes in the rock. A few small bushes grow on the riverbed; tiny fishes can be seen floating though the greenery. High sharp cliffs tower to the west, making travelling in that direction quite hard even for a skilled climber.
1181: This section of the wild river seems especially barren and desolate. It would take a skilled climber to venture south through the sharp cliffs that tower on the riverbank. An easier option would be to follow the river downstream, which is due west in this case. In the meantime, one could always look at the very impressive rock formations on the bottom of the river.
1182:
There is a lot of snow on the ground.
A small rabbit glares angrily at you.

This dark river meanders slowly through the hills, cutting a path through the surrounding dark cliffs and rocks. The water here is very clear and fresh, yet it has a somewhat metallic taste. There are some signs of vegetation here: thick weeds grow on the dramatically sloping banks.
1183:
There is a lot of water on the ground.
An Elf is here walking around.

A few trees break the monotony of these hills. The trees are low and bent from the hard wind that lashes against them. To the east a trail can be seen and to the north a river cuts through the cliffs.
1184: Large thorny bushes are scattered among the high pointed cliffs. A strong wind blows here, making it hard to walk upright. To the north the cliffs come to an abrupt end as they fall steeply into a dark, wild river, while to the east the slope isn't that steep and you would easily be able to walk down to the water.
1185: There is a lot of water on the ground.

This precipitous hillside is filled with sharp rocks and large boulders. Among the rocks grow small tussocks of lush, green grass and small thorny bushes. To the north the terrain becomes even more rocky and to the west the hills become completely impassable. However, to the east, you can spot a small trail twisting and turning through the hills.
1186:
There is a lot of water on the ground.
A small brown snake is slithering around here.

A small path twists its way among the the rocky hills, speeding up travel. Large boulders are scattered across the landscape almost as if a giant had tossed them around. To the north you hear the roar of a wild river and to the east the hills are so steep that travel in that direction is completely impossible.
1187: At the Ruins of an Old Barn

On the top of the steep hill you can see the ruins of an old barn. It seems that it has been left to fall apart a very long time ago. Nothing remains of the walls except small stumps of wood pointing towards the sky, and the remains of the roof are scattered all over the place. Grass covers most of the planks, but some of the planks are remarkably fresh and seem to be newer than the rest of the ruin.
1188: Large, sharp rocks are scattered around the landscape. Between the boulders some large thorny bushes grow so close together that they completely block the sunlight from reaching the ground. Atop a high hilltop far to the west a tall tower can be seen, while huge rocks completely block your way to the south.
1189: There is a lot of water on the ground.
The magnificent Tower Hills stretch as far as the eye can see. There is little vegetation here, except a few thorny bushes and some dry grass. To the west a high, white tower reaches up to the sky.
1190:
There is a lot of water on the ground.
An Elf is here walking around.

Long dry grass and small thorny bushes cover the hilly terrain. To the west and north the hills fall down towards a river. The slopes are steep and rocky and going that way will take some effort. To the east the hills open up into a rocky wasteland. Far to the south-west you can see the contours of a high tower.
1191: At the Base of a White Tower

A colourful butterfly is fluttering around here.
A squirrel scampers around here, looking for nuts from the trees.

Of all the rocky hills that surround you, this appears to be the highest. On the top of this hill stands a high, white tower completely made of stone. It rises several hundred feet toward the sky and the view from the top must truly be magnificent. A zig-zagging trail, paved with small white stones, leads from the tower's entrance to the west. Dense, thorny bushes surround the base of the tower, making it hard to approach from anywhere but on the path.
1193: The dense forest completely surrounds you, hiding you from view on all sides. The trees stand close together, making any travel here slow and dull. Forming a thin but compact canopy above the branches block most light from reaching the ground, giving a shadowed and grey appearance to the area. Due to the lack of life-giving light the undergrowth here is sparse with the ground mostly covered by fallen pine needles.
1194: A brown fox is here, looking for some rabbits to chew up.

Here the forest opens up into a small clearing. The ground is covered with soft, green grass which makes this a perfect place to sit down and rest. To the north some water can be seen through the trees. To the south and east the forest continues.
1196: This probably does not even qualify to be named a bridge. Two medium sized logs have been pulled across the river below you and tied together. The logs are quite slippery from the water splashing up. Since the tree trunks are still rounded, one needs to have good balance to cross the river here. The water flows by southwards, but its origin is unknown. To the north, where there should be a river, a swampy area looks uninviting.
1197: Instead of the familiar green colours that are usually found in this region, most of this area is smothered by a blanket of colourful blossoms. The field is bordered by a fast flowing stream passing by in the south. Some logs allow crossing of part of the river to the east. Vegetation grows more coarsely north of here and the flowers give way a field of grass westwards.
1198: The riverbed widens here somewhat as water reaches it from both the south and the north. A slope climbs upwards in the east towards a wooden region. Murky water, likely due to the stir up created by the increased waterflow, prevents judging the depth of the water here. The river continues at a quick pace westwards.
1199: The river flows quickly westwards in a nearly straight fashion. Steep slopes rise upwards both to the north and south. It would be difficult to get a grip anywhere on the riverbank. The water is far from clear here, it seems to be carrying a lot of mud and sand with it from regions to the east.
1200: Water moves here at a leisurely pace northwards where sounds suggest an increase in the flow of the river. The stream arrives from the east and is redirected by a riverbank to the west. The riverbank is quite muddy and any attempts to climb it would be unsuccessful since there are no easy grips available. South a gaping hole might indicate the presence of a passage.
1201: There is hardly a current on this river as it slowly makes its way westwards. The river is quite clear here and a rock filled bottom is visible. To the north stands a small forest which is easily accessible from here. The southern slope however is muddy and would be impossible to climb.
1202: Clear and tranquil, this pond has a soothing impact on the environment. The only sound that can be heard is the chirping of small birds looking for food on the edge of the pond. Large bushes grow around the pond making it a quiet, isolated haven. Through the bushes to the south you can spot a large road passing by.
1203: A black bear is sleeping here.

Large pines grow here overshadowing your path. There seems to be almost no undergrowth as the sunlight never reaches the ground. The dense and dark forest continues to the east but to the north a small clearing can be seen. To the south a pond can be spotted through the trees.
1204:
A small mushroom grows nearby.
A squirrel scampers around here, looking for nuts from the trees.
A small grasshopper clings to a blade of grass, ready to spring.
A squirrel scampers around here, looking for nuts from the trees.

Light mist climbs up the western and southern riverbanks and gently blankets the ground here. Some colourful dried leaves might have fallen from the trees a while ago for they now cover the ground. The forest continues north and east. Near the southern riverbank a thick patch of mushrooms has found a suitable spot to grow.
1205: A brown fox is here, looking for some rabbits to chew up.

A small animal path is winding its way through this forest of tall pines. Some small bushes grow beside the path and the sounds of small animals can be heard from within them. The forest continues to the north and west but to the east the large Tower Hills can be seen rising towards the sky.
1206: The brook is quite wide here and its pace is therefore much slower than to the south where the brook narrows. The riverbanks consist of dark, moist soil covered with lush, green grass and small white flowers. To the north a dark pine forest can be seen. The brook flows west at a moderate pace.
1207: The brook forms a quite fast-paced stream here as it becomes even more narrow than before. High cliffs prevent you from going west or south, as the rock is so smooth that it is impossible to get a proper grip on them. The brook flows northward at a very high pace.
1209: There is some snow on the ground.

Coming from the north and smoothly turning west, the brook widens somewhat here as it is nourished by the waters of another stream that flows in from the south. It is hard to judge the depth of the brook as the water is murky due to the stir-up created by the increased water-flow. A high cliff rises towards the sky in the east.
1210: Filled with clear, cold water this small lake constitutes the border between the high hills to the north and the lower plains to the south. Some small fish can be seen swimming just above the rock-covered bottom. A small stream flows out of the lake to the north.
1211: This lake is filled with clear, cold water. Some small fish can be seen in the clear water near the bottom and many water insects assemble on the surface of the lake, attracting fish and occasional birds. Thick bushes and low trees cover the shores. A small river flows out of the lake to the east. A high and mighty cliff rises towards the sky to the north.
1212: A small river appears from a wide fissure in the ground, follows the bends of the rocky slope and continue in a fast pace due west. Just after the river comes out of the underground, a small stream leaves the rocky channel and continues east. The banks are filled with lush, green grass and small bushes. To the south a large road passes by and to the north the great Tower Hills can be seen.
1215:
There is a lot of water on the ground.
A black raven flies in the sky searching for flesh to prey upon.

Large hills surround you on all sides. A small path winds its way in a northerly direction. Some small thorny bushes are scattered around the path, making it hard to walk beside it. To the west the hills are so steep that even a skilled climber has no chance of going in that direction. In the far north a high, white tower can be distinguished.
1216:
A placid pond is here, inviting you to take a refreshing drink.
A squirrel scampers around here, looking for nuts from the trees.
An elf is here walking around.

A small brook flows in from the east and fills a hollow in the ground here, forming a pond. As the brook never ceases its flow, the excess of water is drained into a larger brook to the south. The pond is not very wide but so deep that it is hard to see the bottom. Around the pond the vegetation is lush and green, almost like an oasis in this harsh and infertile part of the Tower Hills.
1217: Large, sharp rocks are scattered across the hillside. The vegetation here consists of lush, green grass and small thorny bushes. To the east the hillside is so steep that any attempt to climb it would be futile. The rocky hills continue in all directions. In the north-west you see the contours of a high tower.
1218: A squirrel scampers around here, looking for nuts from the trees.

A small brook flows through lush greenery and sharp pointy rocks. The brook is not so deep and you can easily see the bottom which is filled with small white stones. The brook flows in a westerly direction and seems to end in a small pond just west of here. Looking south you see a very high cliff that points towards the sky.
1219: As if tossed around by a playful giant, many large rocks are scattered all across the slopes of the mighty hills. Large thorny bushes make travel somewhat painful as their sharp thorns get stuck in every exposed part of your body. The grass that grows here is quite high, almost reaching a normal man's waist.
1220: There is a lot of water on the ground.

A couple of large trees growing on the top of this hill distinguish it from the surrounding hills. Growing by the side of the trees are some small bushes which make this a quite comfortable spot to sit down and rest. The bushes grow in a half-circle around a large patch of soft green grass.
1221: A black raven flies in the sky searching for flesh to prey upon.

Large boulders are scattered across the landscape. Between the boulders, small trees and lush green bushes try to survive in the infertile soil. To the south you can catch a glimpse of water, but everywhere else you look, all you can see are hills and more hills.
1222: There is a lot of water on the ground.

Like a tower, this cliff stands tall and mighty between two bodies of water. The flat rock is smoothed by time and doesn't even have a single small crack that could make climbing on top of it a bit easier. However, the top of the cliff is flat and some soil has been able to get a grip somehow. The view from this vantage point is astonishing.
1223: An elf is here walking around.

The ground here is covered by a multitude of small, round stones. Some tufts of grass and a few bushes grow between the stones. Occasional animal sounds can be heard from within the bushes. To the east and south you can see a large road pass through the terrain. To the north and east however, you vision is completely filled with the mighty Tower Hills.
1224:
There is a lot of water on the ground.
An Elf is here walking around.

From this rocky hill, more rocky hills can be seen in all directions. There is a very limited set of wildlife and flora here. Despite the desolate appearance of the area, tough animals and hardy vegetation can make a living here. A steep hillside completely blocks your way to the north.
1225: A squirrel scampers around here, looking for nuts from the trees.

Stones of all sizes cover the hillsides. Many green bushes grow among the stones. From within the bushes various sounds, most likely made by birds and rodents, can be heard. To the south the hillside is so steep that it is impossible to travel that way.
1226: A Small Trail in the Hills

The trail runs here in a straight north-south direction. A large oak tree has somehow managed to get a grip in the infertile landscape, providing some shade on hot summer days. The only other vegetation are small bushes and occasional patches of grass.
1227: Large, spiked boulders cover the hills, forcing you to pick your way between them. The ground is covered with lush, green grass and low shrubs and bushes. The wind is quite harsh here, tugging at your clothes and making walking upright a hard task.
1229: Small, round stones cover the slopes of these hills. Occasional bushes and shrubs grow between the stones. To the south the hillside is so steep that it is impossible to travel that way. On the top of the hill to the north you can spot the remains of a small hut.
1230: A Small Trail in the Hills
An elf is here walking around.

The trail is bending north and west here. To the west you catch a glimpse of a high tower stretching towards the sky. The terrain beside the trail is rough and nothing except small bushes grows here. To the south the hills appear to become lower.
1231: A Small Trail in the Hills

A beautiful and docile horse is standing here.
A pony is standing here, ridden by you.

Here the trail is bending east and south. In the far south you see a large road that seems to be used on a regular basis by travellers. To the west you can distinguish a high tower rising towards the sky. The hills in the east do not seem as impassable as those in the west.
1232: The ruined remains of a small hut are the only thing that breaks the monotony of large boulders and stone blocks. The only vegetation that seems to be able to get a grip in the sparse soil are small, thorny bushes and occasional low pines. Looking west, a small trail can be seen, winding its way through the mighty Tower Hills.
1234: A Small Trail in the Hills

A small trail is winding its way through the Tower Hills. It seems relatively well used and travel is easy here. Large bushes grow along the path and sounds of small animals can be heard from within them. Looking around, you see that you are completely surrounded by the Tower Hills.
1237: A Small Trail in the Hills

A small trail runs here, making passage through the Tower Hills easier. A few small bushes grow beside the trail and some tufts of grass grow on its surface. To the south a large road passes by and to the east and west the Tower Hills stretch out.
1238: A Steep Hill beside the Road
A black raven flies in the sky searching for flesh to prey upon.

Small bushes grow on this steep hill, which lies just north of a large road. Among the bushes, many small rocks covered with green moss lie. An occasional tree can be spotted but the harsh wind prevents them from growing high and mighty. To the north you can distinguish a small trail winding its way through the hills.
1239: A Small Trail in the Hills

The small trail bends north and east here, winding its way through the mighty Tower Hills. Far off to the west a tower stretches towards the sky, making the hills around look small and insignificant. Steep hillsides make it hard, but not impossible, to leave the trail.
1240: A Small Trail in the Hills

The trail bends west and south here, following the steep hillsides. A few large bushes grow by the trail, but otherwise this landscape provides no place to hide, escaping the wild predators that roam these hills. In the south a large road can be discerned.
1304: Here the cavern comes to an abrupt end, the uneven stone walls blocking passage in every direction but west. An old rotten cupboard hangs on the wall, its doors attached by one hinge each. Someone apparently uses this place as a refuse dump as food leftovers are scattered all around the room. The stench here is almost unbearable.
1305: The cavern is filled with all types of junk. Broken furniture and rotten clothing are strewn all around. The floor is soft and damp from the water that trickles down the stone walls, assembling in small pools on the floor. A fragile ladder leads up to a higher level of the cavern and there are exits to the east and west.
1306: This part of the cavern is quite nice and tidy, as if somebody actually cares how it looks. Torches light the room with a flickering light, and a carpet covers the uneven floor. A table with some chairs placed around it stands in the middle of the room. To the north there is another lit room, but to the east the cavern extends into darkness.
1307: An experienced smuggler is here, conspiring with his cohorts.

Lit by the many torches hanging on the walls, this part of the cavern is actually quite comfortable. The air is dry and warm, and the floor is covered by a large grizzly bear fur, complete with head and paws. A large oaken table with five chairs around it stands along one of the walls. On the western wall you can see a crude oil painting of a high tower.
1308:
A sturdy bandit bodyguard stands here, eager to hack you to pieces.
A sturdy bandit bodyguard stands here, eager to hack you to pieces.
A sturdy bandit bodyguard stands here, eager to hack you to pieces.
A sturdy bandit bodyguard stands here, eager to hack you to pieces.

The air here is drier than in the cave to the south and permeated by the stale smell of old, rotten food supplies. In a corner of the cavern some coffins are stacked on top of each other. To the south the cavern continues. A fragile ladder leads down.
1309: The floor of this cave is covered with hard, sandy soil. Small rivulets of water trickle down the stone walls, forming pools of water on the floor. A narrow ladder leads up to the roof. To the north the cave continues further into the hill.
1310: The wind blows hard here high above the plains which spread far and wide toward the west. West behind the wall, a steep cliff prevents entry of all enemies without wings. North is the highest point on the hills and in the face of the rock entry way is hewn leading down into darkness. Many dry bushes grow here whistling in the wind. This place provides a perfect place to watch everything that moves upon it. A plaque hangs on the old ruined wall.
1311: The wall of stone extends from north to south. Every now and then some of the stones have fallen down. Some down the cliff on the plains below and some lay now beneath this side of the wall. To the south the wall turns east and would prevent entry down the hill, but a portion of it has collapsed into a large pile of rubble. Foundations of a building are buried in the ground. Maybe it was a stable or a lodging for men, you will never know. Ground is quite level, but in the east your view is prevented by a small mound. A juniper bush spreads its fragrant aroma on top of it.
1312:
A short evergreen plant, with slightly bluish needles, grows here.
A small animal, all covered in spines, snuffles amongst the undergrowth.
A swallow flies high above the ground.

The ground slopes down southward from a high hill to the north between a tall ridge west and a tall hill to the east. Many juniper bushes grow here and there. At the foot of the slope thick vegetation prevents entry to the grassy plains below.
1313:
A swallow flies high above the ground.
A finch flies low above the ground.
A badger is here, exploring for food.

Upon this large hill, a small campfire burns without creating much smoke. A small pile of firewood has been left next to the fire, while a few poles have been put into the ground, forming the pillars of a small tent. A felled tree seems to be being used as bench upon which, someone has left some fine carvings. It looks as if this camp has been in use for quite some time.
1314:
A woodpecker is here, tapping on a tree.
A colourful butterfly is fluttering around here.

Junipers grow wild on these hills and the aroma is most delightfull. Down below the trail winds like a snake around this very hill. It's not possible to enter it from here unfortunately. The drop down is at least 4 fathoms. The hill slopes steadily upwards to the north. The edge of the cliff turns westward in the south and there it drops down to a narrow vale. To the west a small ridge blocks the view, but it is not an obstacle for a hardy adventurer.
1315: A swallow flies high above the ground.

Junipers grow wild on these hills, and their aroma is most delightful. Down below, the trail winds like a snake around this very hill. Unfortunately it is not possible to descend to the trail from here, and the drop down to it is at least four fathoms. The hill slopes southward. West behind a small depression is another hilltop.
1316: The grass grows thick upon this hill top. It looks as if it was the highest hill. Though the hilltops to the west and east seem to be about the same level. An old well, now useless and blocked by some stones, stands amidst the vegetation. To the north the hillside is too steep even for a mountain goat to climb down. Southward the the hill slopes down and is covered by juniper bushes. Maybe there is a shelter from the wind.
1322: A narrow tunnel winds its way up and through the hillside. It is wide enough for three to walk abreast and high enough to lead a horse. Over the years flowing water has worn deep grooves into the ground making footing difficult for both horse and rider. The floor is covered by puddles, mud and slippery stones. The air humidity is perfect for the colorful fungus which grows on the walls. Yellow, red and dark brown patches cover them in many places. The roof of the tunnel is made from wedge-shaped stones that have been laid cleverly into an arch. Some of the sharp stones project below the others, and man or beast must bow humbly to pass them.
1323: Hill Overlooking the Road to the Grey Havens

This huge old hill stands here like a wedge, forcing the road to the Grey Havens to take a turn around it. East and south of here the ancient Tower Hills stretch out, while travelling north and west would take you down to the road.
1324:
A black wolf pads restlessly, looking for its next prey.
A black wolf pads restlessly, looking for its next prey.
A wild bull seems ready to charge you.

Large green bushes grow on the hilltops, breaking the monotony of the otherwise mostly grass and weed-covered hills. Some large boulders are scattered among the bushes. The hills continue in all directions, but an old road winds its way through the hills to the north and east.
1325: A black wolf pads restlessly, looking for its next prey.

These gentle rolling green hills are overlooking the Road to the Grey Havens that meanders through the landscape to your north and west. East of here the landscape gradually changes into a more dramatic view: that must be the famous Tower Hills.
1326: There is a lot of water on the ground.

These hills differ markedly from the grassy hills that can be seen to your west. There is virtually no vegetation here, only some thorny bushes and patches of high yellow grass. The hills themselves seem old and grey, naked rocks interspersed with eroded cliffs.
1327: From this rocky hill, more rocky hills can be seen in all directions. There is little wildlife and flora here. Despite the desolate appearance of the land, tough animals and hardy vegetation can obviously make a living in this area. To the west the landscape get more cultivated and easier to travel through.
1333: A wild bull seems ready to charge you.

Here one can find rock, stones, cliffs and more rocks. There is absolutely no vegetation here. The hills are completely naked and exposed to the erosive forces of sun, wind and rain. On one of the hills one can see the remains of a campfire.
1334:
There is a lot of water on the ground.
A quarrel has been set down on the ground.
A black wolf pads restlessly, looking for its next prey.
A black wolf pads restlessly, looking for its next prey.

These towering hills look very dramatic indeed. Comprised of black and dark-grey rocks, they loom threateningly over any mounted traveller. One of the hills looks particularly menacing, and it takes just about no imagination to make out a grinning face in the rock. Travelling west towards some greener hills seems easier than to venture further into the towering hills north and east of here.
1335:
There is a lot of water on the ground.
The butchered corpse of a black wolf is lying here.

The hills continue in all directions. Travel southwards from here is prevented by a sheer rock face, but one can venture out among the hills in all other directions. The hills north and west of here seem gentler and greener, while the hills to your east are naked rock.
1336: Various types of grasses cover these old hills. On the southern slopes one can see a type of herb that is unusual to find around these parts of Arda: a tough, grey-green plant with sticky yellowish leaves. Looking up from these flowery distractions one can discern the road to the Grey Havens to the north.
1337: Among these grass-covered hills stands a white weather-worn rock. Upon closer inspection one can see that it must have been erected here for some purpose, but it is unclear what this purpose might have been. In the shade of this rock grows a tough birch that seems to be older than the hill itself.
1338: A brown cow is here, contemplating a higher reality whilst chewing slowly.

Here lie the remains of what once must have been some sort of roadside hut. Decaying logs and patches of gravel tell a story of some sort, but there are few other signs of habitation here. It is possible to travel north to the road between the Grey Havens and the eastern lands. One can also venture among the hills east and west of here.
1339:
A black wolf pads restlessly, looking for its next prey.
A black wolf pads restlessly, looking for its next prey.

A plethora of different grasses covers these ancient hills. The dominant type seems to be a tough, low grey-green weed. However, what catches the eye are the patches of a tall red-leafed grass that reaches almost four feet here and there. North of here runs the road between the Grey Havens and the eastern lands.
1340: A large, loyal falcon is circling above.

This is a fairly large grass-covered hill. From this spot one has a fair view of the surrounding area. North of here is the road to Grey Havens. To the south and east a landscape of rolling hills stretches out. A vast grassy plain lies to the west. There is something solemn and untouched about this place.
1341:
A brown fox is here, looking for some rabbits to chew up.
A brown fox is here, looking for some rabbits to chew up.

The ground is covered by grass and small bushes with only an occasional tree sometimes breaking the monotony. To the east a large grassy hill rises above the land, but to the north and west the grassy plains continue.
1342:
A fat rabbit is here, chewing on some grass.
A brown fox is here, looking for some rabbits to chew up.

Vast grassy plains stretch out before you with small trees and thorny bushes scattered all across the open landscape. In the far east large hills fill the horizon and to the west cultivated land takes over.
1343: The landscape ripples with amber waves of grain. The wheat appears ripe and must be ready to be harvested soon. Gently swaying stalks continue towards the west. Further north the golden field gives way to a large area of corn. No trees are in sight and the landscape seems quite flat.
1344: Densely packed wheat grows here giving this whole area a rich golden colour. Some small paths lead through the field, probably the remnants of the farmers movements when this field was sown. Some of the stalks appear to have been nibbled on by a small creature. The field continues eastward but passage is blocked by a fence in the west.
1345: High stalks of corn rise all around, virtually blocking the view of the sky above. A strong odour originates from the west, but a tall dark pile in that direction blocks any investigation. The corn field continues towards the east, while uneven ground leads northwards. Further south of here the tall green stalks of corn give way to shorter yellow vegetation.
1346: Rows of corn grow here, their green stalks swaying in a gentle breeze. Though it is difficult to see anything other than corn, there appears to be a field of yellow foliage further south. North and east the corn gives way to shorter vegetation. Whoever planted this corn must have spent a large amount of time doing so, the rows are perfectly straight and evenly spaced.
1347:
A woodpecker is here, tapping on a tree.
A fat rabbit is here, chewing on some grass.
A brown fox is here, looking for some rabbits to chew up.

A small brook twists its way through the lush green fields here. Along the brook some large bushes and small trees grow. To the north a large road passes by and to the south the grassy plains continue while to the west cultivated land takes over the wild plains.
1348:
A fat rabbit is here, chewing on some grass.
A fat rabbit is here, chewing on some grass.
A colourful butterfly is fluttering around here.

Soft lush grass covers the level ground. Some small, thorny bushes provide shelter for the small animals that live in these fertile plains. To the east and north a large road passes by and to the west and south the plains continue.
1349: The uneven ground here makes travel difficult. The ground has been forcefully dug up everywhere and turned over so as to bring the nutrient rich dark earth to the surface. Only a few spots of grass are still visible, their numbers increasing further in the west. Southwards high stalks of corn grow while to the north flat, well-travelled land indicates the presence of a road.
1350: Little vegetation grows here, the ground has been recently turned over exposing some worms and dark earth. Hoofprints along with bootprints can be seen along the uneven ground. Directly north the flat earth indicates a more frequently travelled area. Turned over earth continues in a western direction while high stalks partially hinder your travel southwards.
1351:
Yellow flowers, with grey-green foliage, grow in clusters here.
The bee flies around here, collecting nectar from the flowers.
