Patches of vibrant yellow flowers cover the area, interspersed among a variety of long grasses. Cart tracks lead north towards a well travelled road and westwards. A continuous buzzing of numerous insects prevails and an occasional butterfly flutters past you.
1352: A high wooden fence closes this section of grass off from the areas around it. The only entrance and exit to this pasture exists in the form of a wooden gate in the north. The ground is covered by short grass that has given way to a patch of dirt just in front of the gate. A small wooden building stands to the east with part of its roof reaching into this pasture and providing some shelter.
1354:
A half wolf is here, loyally protecting his master.
An elven farmer is here surveying the land.

Indentations in the ground along with flattened vegetation indicate a path extending east and west. This area seems well travelled by heavy carts and the grass has recently been trimmed. South of here the rear side of a small structure is visible while to the north a high fence blocks off a section of field.
1355: A thorny bush grows on the northern side of heavy cart tracks leading towards a structure in the south. Similar tracks continue east along a path. Little grass can be found here, the ground is almost totally covered with deep grooves from heavy loads and frequent travel. A smaller less travelled path branches off from the main tracks and leads west.
1357: Yellow flowers, with grey-green foliage, grow in clusters here.

The small path bends here, leading north and eastwards. A high wall prevents passage to the south while a building stands directly to the west. The path is well worn but has been taken care of. No heavy animal tracks or machinery pass through here leaving the ground solid and covered in small flowers.
1358:
A goose waddles around here.
A goose waddles around here.

This area is sheltered on all sides except east. The ground is covered by small rocks and some straw and widens to the north. South a door blocks entrance to a hay-filled stable while a heavy wooden door leads west into a farmhouse. Iron rings embedded in the southern wall must serve as a place to tie up livestock. No roof covers this area and gusts of wind occasionally stir up a few haulms of corn. A covered passage can be entered east of here.
1359: A neat straw pallet is lying here.

Barn doors stand to the north and south. On the walls beside the doors hang various halters and leather pieces. The short passage continues west into an open courtyard and east to the outside of this barn. The roof is in need of repair as the sky can be seen through a gaping hole.
1361:
A small oaken table has been set here.
An elven farmer stands here partially hunched over.

Part of the iron hull of a stove reaches into this room from the kitchen, providing heat and a place to dry clothes when the stove is in operation. A wooden table along with three matching chairs stands next to a window by the northern wall. Shelves filled with pottery and keepsakes line the eastern wall. The only other furniture in this room is a large rocking chair near the oven.
1363: A placid pond is here, inviting you to take a refreshing drink.

A bench stands beneath a fairly large tree, next to a small pond. A few waterlilies float on the surface of the pond and occasionally small waves ripple across the waters clear surface. A road appears to bend around this area to the north and east. Long grass grows further west of here and the outline of a building lies to the southwest.
1364: Fairly long grass grows amongst bits of rock slabs, contrasting to the solid rock surface present north of here. A wooden building borders this grassy area to the south with a large window facing in this direction. Occasional sounds of splashing water can be heard from the not too distant east.
1365: A mass of dark green leaves clings to a wall.

High walls rise up in the north and continue both into the northwest and northeast. The ground is a mixture of sand and rocks and the only vegetation here are clusters of green ivy that cling to the solid walls and nearly reach the top. Sandier regions lie to the west and south while a well-travelled road is accessible to the east.
1366: By the Rear of a Building

From this vantage point it is impossible to determine where the entrance to the wooden structure to the south lies. The ground is fairly soft here and seems to consist mostly of sand and small rocks. A number of boulders and larger rocks have been piled up into a heap next to the building. The soft sand continues westwards while more solid ground lies to the north and east.
1367: Much of the ground here is covered by boulders of various sizes. The Gulf of Lhun lies to the west and it is quite calm in this area. Occasionally larger waves collide with some of the boulders further out, causing some sprays of salty water. Little vegetation grows here though some sand is visible amongst the large rocks. Further east and south the rocks diminish, giving way to more fertile land.
1368: The Gulf of Lhun looks almost inviting as its massive body of grey water stretches towards the western horizon. The ground here is covered mostly in sand along with a few hardy bushels of grass. A number of animal tracks can be seen imprinted in the soft sand. Only a few large boulders remain here, though their numbers increase in the north.
1370:
A king crab is crawling around in the sand here.
A seagull is soaring above you.
Artos the Man, wielding a longsword, is here, riding a pack horse.
A pack horse is standing here, ridden by Artos.

Sand has piled up in various areas here, creating an uneven ground. The sounds of a not too far off body of water reach here from the west. Aside from the mounds of sand, there is little change in the landscape. A small building can be entered directly east.
1372: A trained horse (ulo) is standing here, ridden by you.

Though most of this field consists of grass bushels, the sand underneath is quite visible. Trees have apparently found it difficult to establish themselves here due to the soft sand not providing much support. The field becomes sandier as it leads westwards to the sea. An enclosed section of sand lies to the east.
1375: The river seems to increase its flow here as it begins to slope even further into the earth. Directly west a large bridge is visible, but climbing up here anywhere to reach it would be impossible. The river is simply too fast and powerful to allow for any manuvering to the side. The only directions in which travel is possible are eastwards upstream or underneath the bridge in the west.
1376: The corpse of a shad is lying here.

This river flows by quite far below the lands to the north and south of it. Steep slopes rise up in those directions, their crumbling surfaces making climbing undesirable. Many boulders have fallen into the river forcing it to flow around them in some areas. These obstructions, combined with the high speed of the water present a dangerous obstacle course for anything trying to get through here alive. The current presses on westward leaving little time to ponder the consequences of false movements.
1377: The flow of this river is redirected here by solid rockwalls, forcing the water to travel westwards. The eastern rivers edge shows signs of erosion from the constant pressure of the water passing through here. Occasional sprays of water occur whenever the river flows over semi submerged boulders. The slope leading up on the northern side appears to present some spots that would allow for a somewhat safe climb.
1378: A massive lone oak tree grows in the middle of this field surrounded by long thick grass. A stream borders the field both to the south and west with steep slopes reaching down to the water. East the field continues along the stream towards a colourful patch of flowers. Bushy regions of land lie northwards.
1379:
A squirrel scampers around here, looking for nuts from the trees.
A squirrel scampers around here, looking for nuts from the trees.

Thick branches reach out to the east and west while the main trunk of this oak continues a short stretch upwards before it too splits into a number of smaller sections. The branches appear thick, but venturing away from the centre of this tree might not be a smart idea. The bark of the tree is rough and appears as if an animal or something has developed a liking for it.
1381: The river is quite high here, but still far from reaching the top of the riverbanks on the northern and southern sides. Steep slopes lead up on both sides, suggesting that at one time much more water was flowing through here. Nevertheless, the river is still quite substantial and is flowing at a high rate westwards. It is impossible to make out anything beneath the water surface here.
1382: The water here is quite turbulent as a small waterfall creates fairly high waves. The river bends quite abruptly northwards as it encounters a solid rockwall. Travelling upstream towards the east would be difficult due to the strong current coming from that direction. Occasionally grey shapes can be seen swimming passed beneath you.
1384: The bridge above blocks out any view of the sky. From this vantage point the bridge is situated quite high up from the river and appears to have been built very sturdily. The river flows through here at high speed and plummets towards the north into darkness.
1385: A pair of soft leather boots are on the ground.

The hallway is simply decorated with a worn rug on the wooden floor. There are doors to the east and west and open doorways north and south. A red candle sits upon a small cupboard and some dirty shoes have been left on the floor beside it. Rugged jackets hang on hooks by the southern wall.
1386:
Some cereals that look like wheat are lying here.
A small box has been left here.
A water barrel has been left here.

The air in this room is substantially colder than the temperature outside it. Solid rock forms the ground, out of which two steps have been carved to place the main floor of the room below ground level. A number of large barrels and boxes occupy the room. Scents of dried meat and rotting vegetables saturate the stagnant air.
1387: A sturdy bed made from solid oak lies here, covered in warm blankets.

A large wooden bed takes up most of the space in this room. It is covered with a number of blankets apparently made from sheep wool. Above the door leading east hangs a cowhorn stuffed with some dried flowers. Part of the floor is covered with the skin of a large brown animal. A drawer stands next to a window facing westwards.
1388: Though this room contains no bed, it is apparently used as a bedroom. Bushels of straw lie by the southern wall and are partially covered by a blanket. The floor is neither stone nor wood, it is earth that has been pressed flat by many years of being walked on. A single chair that looks too weak to hold anything, stands next to a makeshift bed. There are no windows in this room, nor is there a light source. The only light or airflow here originates from beyond the northern doorway.
1389: A mouse is here nosing around, looking for a safe place to hide.

The entire enclosure is filled with loose hay. A path has been created heading north and south between a door and the other end of the barn. Outside sounds are muffled in here except for occasional wind howling through cracks in the walls and stirring up pieces of hay.
1390:
A chunk of salt is here.
A domesticated pony, beast of burden to many, stands here.
A stocky mountain mule is here, waiting to serve.

The wood on the door leading into this stable has been chewed at by something with a lot of enthusiasm. In fact, much of the room has teeth marks on bits of the wood. The floor is covered with straw and a strong equine odour prevails.
1391:
A brown cow is here, contemplating a higher reality whilst chewing slowly.
A woolly sheep is grazing here.
A woolly sheep is grazing here.

A partial roof has been built here to allow for shelter from the elements. The ground is trampled and soiled by heavy livestock crowding in this area. A few helms of hay suggest this to be a feeding area as well. A wooden trough stands underneath the covering providing a source of water. A fence prevents animals from leaving in all directions save east.
1392:
A cow stands here, chewing her cud.
A bull stands here, calmly looking around.
A cow stands here, chewing her cud.

The grass here is short and in sharp contrast to some yellow flowers that remain untouched by the grazing of the livestock in this pasture. A fence prevents animals from escaping to the south or north. Circular patches cover the ground in spots and seem to attract a variety of insects.
1393: The earth has been dug up here by frequent passage of livestock and carts. A barn stands directly to the west with a small passage leading through it towards a farmhouse. Various farming equipment along with a battered cart have been left next to the southwestern barnwall. A gate blocks livestock from leaving their southern pasture and a very small building can be spotted to the east.
1394: A well-fed cow stands here chewing her cud listlessly.

A wooden fence consisting of a number of planks prevents animals from leaving this area to the east or south. An unmistakable odour drifts here from the north. Grass grows in a variety of shades and heights.
1395:
A hen is trying to pick some grains here.
A hen is trying to pick some grains here.
The rooster is here, strutting about.

Steaming piles of manure have been heaped almost to the height of a full grown elf. A path leads up through the juicy mess and a dirty bucket next to the manure pile suggests someone has the daily chore of adding more manure to the heap. Various insects can be seen scuttling among the mass enjoying their feast.
1396: This room is very small and seems to have been constructed for a single purpose. A long wooden box spans the entire eastern wall. The box is shaped strangely and appears to have been created out of two pieces. The pieces stand at different heights and both have a slab of wood covering a hole leading down into the hollow box. A small bucket of water stands next to the box and a number of cloth strips hang on the northern wall.
1397:
A brown fox is here, looking for some rabbits to chew up.
A sparrow is flapping around on the ground.

You find yourself within a dug-out hole in a hill. The only exit is through some long grass covering an opening to the west. Earth and some feathers line the ground. Strong animal odours along with the cramped space of this hollow make it quite difficult to breathe in this room.
1398: This cavern must exist deep within the earth for its walls are made out of hard rock. Though above you the water created a tunnel naturally, down here the cavern has somehow been hollowed out by tools. The water flow is almost non existent in complete contrast to the water rushing passed overhead. What could be a chamber lies to the east, but a strange bubble covers the entrance.
1399: The sounds of flowing water can be heard directly to the north. This tunnel would not allow any creature save one the size of a hobbit to walk upright. Some pieces of earth have come loose from the ceiling resulting in a partial blockage of the passage. A strange scent reaches you from the south.
1400: The bloated bodies of some frogs lie scattered in this tunnel, perhaps they were overcome by the strange smell blanketing this area. From somewhere the sound of water reaches you. Stagnant air combined with an inexplicable heat, apparently from decaying organic matter, make this place a great place for the growth of fungi. The tunnel continues to the west and north.
1401: A few larger pieces of earth have fallen to the ground here from the ceiling but travel remains relatively unobstructed. The tunnel consists mostly of a hollowed out earth passage that bends occasionally to avoid large boulders that are imbedded in the ground. Somewhere to the north the sound of running water can be heard while south of here the tunnel continues.
1402: A few dried out bits of seaweed suggest that at times this tunnel must be flooded with water. Small heaps of a dark mushy substance have piled up in the middle of the tunnel giving off a strong odour. The tunnel leads from here to the east and to the south where it seems to end.
1403: A black snake hurries towards you with sly intentions.

The walls and floor surrounding you are covered with some sort of dark sticky substance that gives off a powerful odour. Discoloured water drips from the ceiling and forms yellow puddles on the soggy ground. High above you there seems to be an opening, if you dare climb these walls. A low tunnel that must have been dug many years ago leads north.
1407:
There is some snow on the ground.
A brown fox is here, looking for some rabbits to chew up.

The trail gets wider to the east, running through the low hills. Despite the rich vegetation, not a single green shoot can be spotted on the well-travelled path. Standing water and mud cover the trail, keeping clear footprints for days.
1408: A brown fox is here, looking for some rabbits to chew up.

A narrow yet wet, earthy track suddenly disappears in a debris of wood on the eastern slope of a large hill. The trail winds its way around the several tiny trees, keeping a general west-east direction. Unlike the surrounding slopes, the path is not covered by vegetation and a lot of fresh tracks can be seen on it.
1409:
A malicious thug is here, threatening you.
A malicious thug is here, threatening you.
A stocky mountain mule is here, waiting to serve.

Several corpses of large wolf-like beasts lie on the floor, slowly decomposing. The blood, once fresh, has dried and seeped into the hard earthen floor. Corners of the low ceiling are covered with thick, dusty cobwebs.
1410: A barely noticeable footpath runs across the valley, bending around the large stones. Debris from rock and rotten trees blocks the passage to the grass- covered hill in the northern part of the valley. Grass and occasional wildflowers cover the soil, with a few rocks scattered around. A wall of high bushes grows between the two hills in the east.
1411: A thick, secluded grove surrounds the narrow passage between two hills. Signs of life are plentiful, a lot of animal tracks are leading in and out of the forest. Farther to the west, the view is almost blocked by a man-high wall of bushes.
1412:
There is some snow on the ground.
The corpse of a bandit is lying here.
The corpse of a bandit bodyguard is lying here.

This stone-covered slope slowly declines towards a small valley to the north. Some sharp rocks lie about the worn footpath, which bends here and continues to the east and to the south. A few small trees grow amongst the low, green bushes.
1413:
There is some snow on the ground.
The corpse of a bandit bodyguard is lying here.
The corpse of a bandit bodyguard is lying here.
The corpse of a bandit is lying here.
The corpse of a tall stag is lying here.

The ground is very soft and covered by some wild forest flowers. Pine trees loom above a narrow path, which crosses the low hills. A burned-out circle of grass marks a campfire which can be seen just west of a small trail junction nearby.
1414:
There is some snow on the ground.
The corpse of a huge, black wolf is lying here.
The butchered corpse of a fallow deer is lying here.
The corpse of a black wolf is lying here.

These hills were once sharp and high, yet wind and rain has smoothed them. Several trees grow on the rocky slopes, giving a perfect hideout to small animals. Northwards, the forest becomes more deep and gloomy. A small footpath cuts its way through several large stones.
1415: There is some snow on the ground.

A small, rocky path comes down from the hilltop to the north and continues its way to another group of hills to the south. The ground along the trail is quite smooth and even, with some occasional rocks lying around. Several low birch trees grow here and there along the footpath. The green grass of the plains grows high, undisturbed for years.
1416:
There is some snow on the ground.
A black wolf pads restlessly, looking for its next prey.
A huge, black wolf is here, ready to devour.
A squirrel scampers around here, looking for nuts from the trees.

A lot of tall pine trees grow nearby, dispersed along the slopes of the low hills. A worn footpath runs between the pines and enters a green valley between two large hills southwards. Moving to the east, the trees stand farther apart.
1417: There is some snow on the ground.

Two huge, mossy rocks mark the entrance to this small valley between high hills. A small, stone-paved trail heads north-south, avoiding the large rocks scattered everywhere. The deep, green moss seems to thrive at the lowest levels of the valley, leaving no room for other plants. Hill slopes to the east and west are dominated by majestic trees and dense bushes.
1418:
There is some snow on the ground.
A snake slithers towards you.

A stony path continues here, bordered by some small, moss-covered granite pillars which are obviously man-made. The forest becomes more dense, with high, ancient pines looming above the path. The surrounding hills and treetops block all the sunlight during the daytime.
1419: The corpse of a mean brigand is lying here.

The high grass, interspersed with occasional trees and bushes, covers the steep hill slopes to the north and south. A footpath, void of any footprints, was once much wider but now almost disappears amongst the plants. A huge oak tree stands a little off the path, giving refreshing shade from the hot summer sun.
1420: Rows of tall trees and high bushes surround this barely visible trail that runs in an west-east direction. Small, white stones are scattered all over the path, making it difficult to walk. Tracks of some small animals are crossing the footpath in many places, leading deep into brushwood. A valley opens out wider to the east.
1421: The dense pine forest covers both hillsides of this wide valley, making it impossible to leave the trail. The forest thins towards the bottom of the valley, giving more sunlight to other forms of vegetation. The trail is covered by a thin layer of earth, with some small stones raised here and there. A small junction can be seen a few miles to the east.
1422: The corpse of a mean brigand is lying here.

Two trails meet here forming a three-way passage between the surrounding hill ridges. Light pine forest covers the steep slopes, the trees growing more densely westwards. A small but obviously well-travelled path winds between tall pines going in an west-east direction and branching southwards. To the south, the trail disappears in the high bushes between the trees, but with a little effort and patience it would be possible to follow it.
1423: There is some snow on the ground.

Gently sloping hillsides fade into the small valley, protecting it from the wind. All kinds of colourful flowers bloom around the winding trail emitting a strange mixture of scents. Debris of rotten logs and stones rest in a small hollow near the road; being the last remains of a long abandoned watchtower, once overlooking the surrounding lands and the road to the Grey Havens.
1424: There is some snow on the ground.

Thick, thorny bushes are scattered over the northern and southern parts of the ridge, making it impossible for travellers to descend. Standing on top, one could see surrounding hills, forested valleys and the road to Grey Havens far in the north.
1425: There is some snow on the ground.

There are doors leading into other rooms of the building like the kitchen and the living rooms.

The narrow tunnel continues to the east, but seems to open up into a larger cave to the west. A large iron door is in the southern wall.

A spirit floats towards you and howls with an evil laughter.
A spirit floats towards you and howls with an evil laughter.

A few broken coffins lie by the western wall of the cavern. The coffins are empty, but many dry bones and skulls are scattered all over the floor as if somebody had strewn them around while scavenging for valuables. A large sturdy ladder leads up the southern wall. To the north and east the cavern extends into darkness.
1526: The tunnel is quite narrow here. Small pools of water are continuously forming on the ground, fed by tiny rivulets that trickle from the fine cracks in the walls. The narrow tunnel continues to the north, but to the south it opens up into a large cave.
1527: This tunnel is so narrow that any grown-up man would almost have to bow while proceeding to avoid bumping his head against the tunnel roof. The floor is covered with hard soil that is quite damp from the water that is pouring down the walls. The tunnel continues east and south.
1528:
A spirit floats towards you and howls with an evil laughter.
A spirit floats towards you and howls with an evil laughter.

Here the tunnel is very narrow and there is almost no room to manoeuvre. Sharp pointy rocks protrude from the walls, tearing at your clothes whenever you move. The air is moist from the many rivulets of water trickling down from the roof. The tunnel continues to the east and west.
1529: Sharp rocks cover the floor, making passage somewhat hazardous. Equally sharp rocks protrude from the walls which are covered with a net of cracks. Water is pouring down these cracks, forming a small stream that disappears in a hole by the base of the rocky wall to the east. The tunnel seems to be even narrower to the west but opens up a bit to the south.
1530: In one of the corners of the cave some animal droppings can be seen; apparently some animal uses this place as its resting quarters. The air is moist and hard to breathe. The cave is quite big, its roof almost the height of two men. A couple of torches hang on the walls, their flickering flames chasing away the shadows. There is a narrow opening in the northern wall and two somewhat wider openings in the eastern and the southern walls.
1531: A large eagle soars above you.

This tunnel is quite large, almost two men high and at least five men wide. The floor is very smooth and slippery. The tunnel bends from the west to the south. The walls are cracked and a smell of wet soil is prevalent in here.
1532:
A wooden chest stands in the corner.
A moaning ghost advances towards you, shimmering with a pale light.
A beautiful and docile horse is standing here.
A sparrow is flapping around on the ground.

This cave is more than four men in height, and almost circular. The floor is quite flat, as if it has been trodden under many feet. Large torches are placed on the walls a few feet apart from each other, lightening the room. In the middle of the room a marble altar with a shrine is placed, and along the western wall stand three large coffins.
1534: In Front of the Tower Hills

There is some snow on the ground.
A cute young hawk is sitting here waiting for his mother to feed him.

The landscape is slowly rising towards the south-west and it isn't as flat as it is in the north-east. Small hills alternate with gentle slopes and rich, green but flat valleys. The valleys are totally covered with high vegetation. A couple of miles in the south the Tower Hills are rise up high in the sky.
1535:
A nest is here.
A large mother hawk is here looking for a prey to feed her young.
A cute young hawk is sitting here waiting for his mother to feed him.
A cute young hawk is sitting here waiting for his mother to feed him.

The main part of the small plateau is covered by a large bird's nest. It is about three feet in diameter and made out of hundreds or thousands of bush- branches. The edge is covered with bird droppings. Bones and furs of small animals like rabbits are scattered all over the plateau.
1536:
There is some snow on the ground.
A sparrow is flapping around on the ground.
A sparrow is flapping around on the ground.

The landscape changes here. In the north, you can see a large hill where bushes grow. Towards the west, you can see the beginning of the tower hills. A large number of bushes are growing here. The grass here has a huge variety of colours and lengths, and the whole place is very pleasant looking.
1537: A waist-high evergreen shrub grows here, with thick, reaching branches.

This hill is a bit larger than the others on the rolling plains. It offers an excellent view over the plains. To the south-west are the Tower Hills and to the east are the Far Downs. To the north the road to the Grey Havens is a faint line against the horizon. In the south and south east the plains continue.
1538: A brown fox is here, looking for some rabbits to chew up.

Up and down small hills it goes here. The hills are covered with thick, rich grass. Bushes and trees grow on the hills and in the valleys between the hills. Mole-holes are under the bushes and broken off leaves indicate the presence of larger animals. To the south the steppe begins and to the east is a large hill from where one can get a splendid view over the plains.
1539:
A small grasshopper clings to a blade of grass, ready to spring.
A small grasshopper clings to a blade of grass, ready to spring.

An endless looking flat plain stretches south until it reaches the Tower Hills. North of the rocky land is a rolling plain. The only thing growing on the rocky land is grass. From the tracks on the ground it is possible to judge that not many living things travel through the rocky land.
1540: The land here is covered with soft, lush green grass which comes up to your ankles in height in most places. The plains continue to the east and to the south. The Tower Hills rise in the west and north and obstruct passage in these directions. Small, furry little animals rush by you in search of food and sometimes trying to get away from a predator.
1541: The landscape undergoes a swift change here. To the south small hills rise, covered with dense vegetation. In the west, the land gets rough as the plains contain small hillocks and big rocks leading towards the tower hills. In the east, you can see a small forest. Tulips and other bulbous flowers grow here. A few rabbit holes can be seen and there are tracks of foxes near the holes. The rough plains to the north appear hard to pass through, but the way is clear in all other directions.
1542: A beautiful and docile horse is standing here.

The brushwood is almost a small forest here consisting only of deciduous trees. Most of the trees are maple trees and occasionally there is a beech growing between them. The ground is covered with rich grass and the bushes are standing close together. A squirrel lair is built in an old tree stump.
1544:
A woodpecker is here, tapping on a tree.
A fallow deer is grazing peacefully here.
A fallow deer is grazing peacefully here.
A fallow deer is grazing peacefully here.

A dense hedge out of head-high bushes marks the eastern edge of the brushwood. Bird nests of small birds are built in the higher bushes and in the branches of maple trees. In the tree-trunk of one of the larger trees there is a woodpecker nest. Knee-high above the ground the bark of the trees shows signs of boar tusks.
1545: In the south, a group of very thorny bushes is growing. To the west, is a large hill and in the east, a lone tree. Many animal tracks are leading from a brushwood in the north past the large hill and then along the bushes to the lone tree. The ground is covered with soft, green grass. Parts of the grass are trampled into the ground by the hoofed animals which pass here.
1546: Oops, these bushes are really spiky!!! You are spiked with thorns from head to toe. The grass is shrivelled and you can see NO signs of animals here. The long thorns make your progress very difficult and thinking of the other unpleasant things that are maybe here gives you an urgent desire to leave this place head over heels.
1549: There is some snow on the ground.

An area of thorny bushes is in the west. In the east and the south, a huge rock rises up towards the sky. In the north, you can see a large tree standing in a sea of grass. The way east appears very difficult.
1551: There is some snow on the ground.

The grass grows knee-high here, caressing your legs when a soft breeze blows. The vegetation grows dense in the east, and looking far in the east, you see a dark grove of tall trees. To the west and north, you can see pleasant, lush green grassy plains.
1552: A large shrub grows here, filling the air with a heavy scent.

The vegetation is quite dense here and grows a lot denser towards east, where you can see a dark grove of tall trees that look gloomy. In the west, you can see a field with tall, green grass growing in it. The passage north is blocked by strange, poisonous looking weeds and bushes. To the south, you see grassy plains stretching endlessly leading nowhere.
1553: You are standing in front of a large oak tree. On the ground, you can see many animal tracks leading down to a water-hole. The water-hole is obviously the explanation for the many animals coming here. A rope ladder is leading up the tree to a tree house. Who lives in this forsaken area? The large shadow of the tree looks inviting to take a rest.
1554:
The butchered corpse of a large elk is lying here.
The butchered corpse of a tall stag is lying here.

The grassland stretches in every direction mile after mile. Occasionally, you can see groups of bushes and sometimes you can even get a glimpse of a tree or two. The beds of flowers here have an almost hypnotic fragrance and you have a sudden urge to sink into one of these beds and lie down and drift away on a sparkling cloud into the land of dreams.
1555:
An apple tree with bright green leaves grows here.
On the tree's branches are two apples.
A fallow deer is grazing peacefully here.

In the north, you can barely see the road to Grey Havens. Small rabbits are hopping through the grass. The innocent smell of the beautiful flowers makes you relax. A soft breeze is blowing over the grassy ocean perfectly suiting this peaceful area.
1556:
A small and tough weed grows here.
An elven hunter, fair and mighty, roams here warding against evil.
A tall stag is here, grazing peacefully.

The ground here is a little rough but it appears to get rougher in the east. To the south, the vegetation becomes quite dense and you snort as a whiff of foul odour comes from the south... no use going that way. In the west, the plains become even and covered with soft, lush green grass. The road is to the north.
1557: This field is certainly rough and hard to walk on. Stones, large and small, half-hidden in the tall and thick grass make every step a torture for your feet. To the north, you can see the road to the Grey Havens, and to the south, you can see a grove of tall trees but it is too dense for you to be able to get through.
1558: You are now standing in a rough field full of stones and thick grass that makes it very difficult to walk on it. To the north and the east, you can see the road leading to the Grey Havens. To your south, is a thick grove with large, tall trees. However, the path there is full of jagged rocks which make it impossible to reach that grove.
1559: There are two handfuls of clover here.

The grassland is very dry here, perhaps some local water supply problem. A hot wind is blowing tumbleweed over the ground and you can see a few dried out bushes. In the more sandy areas you can see the tracks of small animals, maybe rabbits or snakes?
1560:
There are two handfuls of clover here.
A restless rabbit bounces around.

The grassland ends to the north, marked by the road to the Grey Havens. The grassland spreads out like an endless meadow full of flowers. The grass is more than knee-high, and traces of many small animals can easily be discerned. To the east is a small path stamped through the grass, clearly produced by someone in boots, but the tracks appear to be rather old.
1561: A colourful butterfly is fluttering around here.

The grassland runs along the Road to the Grey Havens. Tall, shoulder-high bushes are growing here forming a hard-to-pass barrier in the south. You can see tracks of larger animals like boars and elks. There are for sure also predators here looking for prey.
1562: The grassland stretches west far beyond the horizon, maybe it covers even all the way to the Grey Havens. A small snake is sneaking through the grass trying to catch a rabbit or a mouse. You can hear the deep rutting call of a large elk trying to impress a female elk.
1563: There are two handfuls of clover here.

You are standing in a clearing in the midst of the grassland. An ideal place to rest. Small animals are bouncing around. You feel safe from predators. You can't be sure where you are but you can see a narrow path leading north- south. Following the path might lead you back to the road or maybe to a populated area.
1564: A group of twelve stout oak trees is growing here in a perfect circle. Inside of the circle is a small, chest high, grassy hill. This ancient relic is surrounded by endless miles of the savanna. To the north you can see the faint line of the road to the Grey Havens against the horizon.
1565: Looking south and east you see the endless grassland going on and on towards the horizon. A soft breeze blows over the grassland from the south. A couple of animals' tracks are leading west. Hmm, did you just see a shadow vanishing behind the bush? Maybe someone is here watching you!
1566: A narrow path leads north-south through the grassland. As your eyes follow the path southwards you can see a large tree. You also notice animal tracks leading towards that direction. Maybe something interesting is there? To the west the vegetation becomes denser and east you can see a couple of trees.
1569: The corpse of a tiny spider is lying here.

A small stream is coming from the north slowing down its pace towards the south as it is slowly widening. The tunnel walls are covered with mud and one can not say for sure if this tunnel was built by some living being or dug in the ground by the rushing water. A faint light is coming from the south and replacing the dim light of the fungi.
1570:
The corpse of a giant slug is lying here.
The corpse of a mottled snake is lying here.
The remains of a black fungus lie here in a heap of rotting compost.
A patch of moss grows here on a wet, flat stone.

This side part of the tunnel is leading north into a rotten room. The main part of the tunnel is to the west. The ground is covered with disgusting looking slime and a few bones are lying around. Many have entered here but only a few have made it out again alive, but the reason for the poisonous stench is not apparent here.
1571:
The remains of a giant fungus lie here in a heap of rotting compost.
The corpse of a bloodthirsty bat is lying here.
The corpse of a huge, poisonous spider is lying here.
Prasil, wielding a mighty dwarven axe, is standing here.
Kaniivel the Tarkhnarb Orc, wielding a steel claymore, is standing here.
A hungry warg stands here, sniffing around for flesh.

A series of small caverns that are connected through a narrow tunnel is leading from the north towards the east. The tunnel is partly collapsed so that the only way through it is to climb or crawl over piles of muddy earth. A dim light is radiating from fungi that grow all over here.

The tunnel is leading in a sharp bend from the west to the south. In the east wall is a large opening. What is behind the opening is covered in darkness. The only hint of what might be there is a poisonous stench coming from the east. Out of a crack in the ground, a stream of water is coming which rushes towards the south.
1573: Old and rotten wooden shores are stabilizing the muddy cavern. The cavern is the entrance to a tunnel leading south. A soft but cold draught is coming out of the tunnel. A small water-stream is coming from above rushing past the cavern and then vanishes in a crack. The cavern is barely lit by a pale light that comes from the south.
1574:
The corpse of a bloodthirsty bat is lying here.
The remains of a giant green fungus lie here in a heap of rotting compost.
The corpse of a giant slug is lying here.
A patch of moss grows here on a wet, flat stone.
Guano the Cave Troll is resting here.
Prasil, wielding a mighty dwarven axe, is standing here.

The cavern originally was a natural one but someone has widened it into a large room. It looks like it once was a smuggler hideout. Now, some of the most revolting living things inhabit this cavern. The ground has a strange green colour and doesn't look all that solid. The poisonous stench is coming up from the ground and the room is filled with piles of bones and skulls.
1575: Well-tended looking bushes are growing in straight rows, running in a north- south direction here. The bushes are waist-high and covered with thousands of flowers. From the north the soft babbling of a brook is coming. In the west is a large group of trees. East and north-east are empty plains.
1577: Between ancient trees, a lot of undergrowth is growing, and this makes moving in any direction very difficult. In the north, you see a high, wooden fence covered in ivy. The tops of large tents are visible over the fence. To the south you see the road, while a path leads through the undergrowth in the west. To your east a dense grove stands.
1578: The grove is not very dense here. Whichever direction you move in, you feel as if you are walking on a path. The ground is rough though, and you have to look down occasionally to avoid stumbling over some root or bush. The grove seems to be getting denser towards east and to the south. You can see the forest growing sparser in the west.
1579: There is a lot of water on the ground.

The grove gets very dense here but it's not very hard to walk through it. All around you, you can see a large number of trees with fat trunks that look so hard that you can imagine why no one ever bothers to cut wood out of them. It is strange, you reflect, how old things sometimes hide still older ones.
1580: There is a lot of water on the ground.

Around you, the trees seem to open up as if you were walking by a path, even though the ground is rough and the passage is not easy. You can see the road in the south through the branches. The grove gets a lot denser in the east and the north, thereby preventing you from going in those directions.
1581: Entrance to the Elven Hunting Camp

An elven guard is wandering here, keeping the peace.
An elven huntsman is standing here, watching for signs of evil.

In front of the gate to north leading inside an elven camp is a small clearing. Elven guards are guarding the gate from evil beings. The camp is surrounded by a wood-made fence that prevents wild animals from entering the camp. The gate is secured with a primitive bolt. Behind the gate is a fireplace, a couple of tents and a paddock.
1582:
A beer barrel has been left here.
A large stone fireplace with a roaring fire warms the room.
An elven huntsman is standing here, watching for signs of evil.
An elven guard is wandering here, keeping the peace.

There is a large, stone-made fireplace here. Next to the fireplace is a grill. The elves use this fireplace to roast meat for their meals. A delicious aroma is coming from the tent in the north, like there is a kitchen there. A bit west of the fireplace is a pond and to the east is a group of tents.
1583:
A placid pond is here, inviting you to take a refreshing drink.
A dented pail has been carelessly left here.
An elven huntsman is standing here, watching for signs of evil.
An elven guard is wandering here, keeping the peace.

There is a small pond next to the fence surrounding the camp. The pond is supplied with water by a small brook coming from the west. A couple of buckets are placed near the pond. To the west there is a fence and behind the gate a small, juicy meadow. The meadow is also surrounded by a wooden fence. To the north is the entrance of a tent.
1584: In the smoking chamber the elves smoke the meat they get from their hunts to keep it edible over a long period of time. They also store the already smoked meat in here to keep it dry. On the side of the chamber there is wood piled up that is used for smoking the meat. You can also see a big flue for directing the smoke into the open air.
1585:
An infusion of herbs gives out a nice scent.
A spoon is placed here.
A large bookshelf sits against the wall.
A elven cook is standing here, busy cooking meals.

Inside this large tent there is the kitchen of the camp. In here the elven cook boils the more delicate food. A large cooker is standing in the north and at the sides of the tent are cupboards. Above the cooker is a flue. Kitchen utensils are spread all over the kitchen table and some large pots and saucepans are placed in a corner of the tent.
1586: An elven huntsman is standing here, watching for signs of evil.

At the east and west side of the tent are elven beds. The pillows and the quilt covers are made out of soft but robust looking green cloth. In the north part of the tent stands a large wardrobe. The floor is covered with a brightly coloured carpet. One can see flowery patterns on the carpet.
1587:
A sticky honeycomb lies on the ground.
A large piece of cheese has been placed here.
A delicious looking apple tart has been placed here.
A bowl of salad has been placed here.
A small oaken table has been set here.

This simple tent is built out of a couple of wooden poles and a thick canopy made out of water-repellent cloth. The tent's purpose is to offer a meeting place sheltered from rain and snow or other forms of bad weather. The tent is also used for taking meals. A table with nicely placed dishes on it is here.
1588: An elven huntsman is standing here, watching for signs of evil.

On the west side of the tent there are two elven beds. The beds are decorated with beautiful ornaments. The bedding is made out of yellow silk. This tent belongs to the more important elves of the camp. In the south is a small facility for the morning washing. In the east part of the tent are big chests containing different sets of clothes for different occasions.
1589:
A sturdy pack horse is standing here.
A sturdy pack horse is standing here.

The elves of this elven camp keep their horses in this paddock. The ground is covered with a juicy meadow. A small brook is entering the meadow from the west and leaving it to the east. To the north there is smoke coming up out of the earth. Behind the wooden fence are green plains filled with bushes.
1590:
There is a water skin lying on the ground.
A sack of flour has been placed here.
A large piece of cheese has been placed here.
An elven guard is wandering here, keeping the peace.
An elven guard is wandering here, keeping the peace.

Inside the storage tent there are hunting weapons and other hunting utensils. stored. Spare parts for the tents are stacked in one corner and horse brass is lying on the floor in the west part of the tent. The cook stores the food he needs for cooking in this tent. You smell smoke coming up from a trapdoor.
1591:
An elven woman is here merrily walking along.
An Elf is here walking around.

This is the western end of the village. To the south can be heard the pleasant tinkling of many elven voices raised in a song. The houses, like the rest of this elven village, are built of a sturdy but amazingly light material which blends in with the local flora and fauna.
1592:
A barman watches you calmly, while skillfully mixing a drink.
A lovely elven maid is serving beverages here.

A sign hanging here draws your attention. Despite the sign, you get the feeling that you are at home here. This place appears to be full of people indulging in merry singing and laughter. Many shades of grey and brown fight for dominance here, but this enhances the natural wooden colour of the ambience. The tables appear to have been cut out of trees, parts of which still form the walls of this bar.
1593:
A small loyal cat is here.
A small loyal cat is here.
An Elven innkeeper stands ready to sign up his guests.
A lovely elven maid is serving beverages here.

The inn is lit by lanterns on the walls and furnished with a few round tables and some chairs. From the north, you can hear voices and laughter from the people in the bar. Towards east, there is a large mirror. The whole place is well kept and feels comfortable, just like most structures in this village.
1594:
There is a lot of water on the ground.
A large fountain, made from grey stone, pours water from its centre.
A beautiful and docile horse is standing here.
An elven guard is wandering here, keeping the peace.
An elven guard is wandering here, keeping the peace.

Hidden from prying eyes, you have stumbled upon a small Elven village nestled among the trees here. The main street runs east-west here and faint voices can be heard off to your left. You can barely pick out the Elven houses as they blend in with the forest, but here and there you catch a glimpse of a twinkling eye and a laughing face looking back at you. You can see buildings both to the east and to the west.
1595:
An elven boy is running about here.
A small, loyal beagle is here, eager to please.

As you walk on the main street in this village, you feel at peace and happy. Around you, you can pick out many houses, big and small, among the trees. To the north, you see a heavy wooden door with strange symbols drawn on it that seem mysterious. From under the door, you detect a faint blue light which moves your heart. To the south is a magnificent temple dedicated to the Valar. The people here like to lead simple and happy lives, it appears but are strong enough to withstand attacks on their lives or lifestyles.
1596: The village priest welcomes you to his simple church.

The place is calm and silent. This grand temple is dedicated to the All-Mighty Valar, Lords of Arda, and whose memory is almost lost for the common elf. An altar of fine marble can be seen, and in the walls ancient paintings revive for the observer forgotten ages.
1597:
An elven guard is standing here at his post.
An elven guard is standing here at his post.
An elven guard is standing here at his post.
A beautiful and docile horse is standing here.
An elven guard is wandering here, keeping the peace.

This path hidden in the grove is not used very often, as you can see. All around is silent, and the atmosphere is undisturbed by any sound of activity except your steps and one occasional bird singing somewhere in the trees. To the north, you think you see a village, but it is hard to say since it seems to be as quiet as everything in this place.
1598: A hooded brass lantern has been left here.

Steel doors and hard-wood furniture is what you see around you. The floor is hard and smooth. Some items of metal armour are hung on the walls which look well polished and strong. The size of the armour amazes you when you realise that men who wear these items are bound to be extra-ordinarily big and strong. To the north, you can see what looks like a place to eat for the guards. To the west, you can see beds implying a resting area for them.
1599:
A bowl of salad has been placed here.
A bowl of salad has been placed here.
A large piece of cheese has been placed here.
A small oaken table has been set here.

This is the village guards' mess hall. Long oaken tables polished and stained to a lustrous brown sheen occupy the centre of the room; benches of similar construction stand next to them. A savoury smell wafts into the room from the east.
1600:
A stove stands against one wall here.
An elven cook is standing here, busy cooking meals.
Taara the Mountain Troll (TT) is standing here.

This place is spacious and very tidy. You can walk in the broad aisles between the long kitchen counters. The stoves are all arranged in the centre of the room directly under the chimney. Shelves on the walls are all stacked with flour, spices and other kitchen material. The kitchen implements are arranged on the walls on hooks. A window opens to the north where you see a dark grove behind a small clear piece of land.
1601:
A sturdy peg for hanging armour is on the wall.
On the peg, there are a sabre, a large wooden shield, a cutlass, and a rapier.
A small oaken table has been set here.

As you enter this room, you find yourself in a large room with beds and couches neatly arranged near the walls. The meagre furnishings in the room illustrate the hard and simple lifestyle of the guards. There are lanterns hung on the walls at regular spacing between beds. Northwards are what look like bathing rooms. Some beds have small tables near them with a few books stacked up.
1602: This large hall has a huge round mahogany table in the centre with many sturdy, polished oak chairs placed around it. One of the chairs is decorated with intricately carved designs resembling the figures of the Valar. In one corner of the hall, there is a small table with water pitchers placed on it. The hall is lit with four large torches burning in each corner. The room is apparently designed to keep the outside noises from bothering people inside. Your senses tell you to try and keep yourself from disturbing the silence.
1603: An elf sits here delving into some old tomes of elven lore.

This is a small room artfully decorated and furnished to make it appear bigger. Tapestries, ancient beyond reckoning, line the walls. Many heroic figures stare out at you as if watching you and judging your worth. From the east comes a small steady glow, too steady to be a fire. The glow seems to be radiating goodness which blesses all that is good and instils horror in the evil hearts.
1604:
A large bookshelf sits against the wall.
On the bookshelf, there is a grey leather-bound book.
An elven guard is wandering here, keeping the peace.
An elven guard is wandering here, keeping the peace.
Aldereon the ancient Noldo stands here, gazing at a forgotten past (glowing).

This room is rather small, but the lighting gives off the illusion of magnificence. Tapestries adorn all four walls, as in the outer room. Vistas of vast lands long forgotten seem to draw the viewer into their splendour and hold them there. The entire decor is as a shrine to an age long past, with wondrous things that Arda will probably never witness again. The bright glow which provides a light as brilliant and beautiful as the distant stars comes from a small phial embedded in a stone in the centre of the room. The light is so brilliant and encompassing it casts no shadow, and the light enhances the effect of the tapestries. A feeling of importance emanates from this phial, and its removal from this room would most likely bring down the wrath of the elves on the thief.
1605:
An elven guard is wandering here, keeping the peace.
An elven woman is here merrily walking along.

Birds are chirping sweet melodies and small furry animals rush past you as they search for food among the dense trees to the north. A small grassy park has been fenced in for the little children to play in. To the south, you see a simple structure which houses the priest to the Valar. Far towards east, you observe that a small area has been cleared among the forest for growing crops.
1607:
A map has been dropped here.
There is an old street-lamp on the border of the street.
One of the strong town gatekeepers is standing here.
An elven guard is standing here at his post.

You are just inside the city walls of Harlond, the part of Grey Havens on the southern shore of the Gulf of Lhun. A main road heads west and a smaller gravel road leads north and south. Through the gate to the east lies outdoor adventure and possibly danger.
1608: There is an old street-lamp on the border of the street.

The gravel road leads north and south. To the west is what looks like a small barracks. A ladder with stone steps has been carved out of the city wall here. It leads to a small room that sits atop the city wall. Along the base of the wall are some small plants and bushes.
1609:
There is an old street-lamp on the border of the street.
A pretty elven girl is strolling around here.
An elven woman is here merrily walking along.
Rampart Road continues north and south here, and to the west you see a small cobblestone street. Along the base of the wall grow some small plants and bushes.
1610:
A large beautiful rose bush is blooming here.
There is an old street-lamp on the border of the street.

The road leads north-south, following the city wall that separates The Grey Havens from the wilderness. To the north a small watchtower rests on top of the city wall, looming high above this road. Some small plants and bushes grow along the base of the wall, seemingly undisturbed by the immense traffic.
1611: There is an old street-lamp on the border of the street.

The road stops here against the great city wall to the south. A number of bushes grow here along the base of the wall and you can see some roses. A circular staircase rises up to a tower on top of the city wall here.
1612:
There is an old street-lamp on the border of the street.
A large beautiful rose bush is blooming here.
Deep inside the bush, there are two red roses with leaves and thorny stems.
A pack horse is standing here, ridden by you.

A small trail runs between large rocks and wild rose bushes. To the west a path follows the city wall and continues towards the shore of the Gulf of Lhun. To the east the north-east corner of the city wall can be seen with a staircase leading up to the top of it.
1614:
There is a red, delicious-looking apple here.
There is a red, delicious-looking apple here.
An apple tree with bright green leaves grows here.
This large area has been planted with many fruit trees. You just might be able to find something to eat here. Off to the east is the city wall and a small cobblestone street lies west.
1615:
There is an old street-lamp on the border of the street.
The elven lamplighter is making his rounds through the streets.

You stand on a small street that does not look too heavily travelled. Small wooden houses line both sides of the street, and elven children play happily in the small yards. The street leads north and south from here and a pretty home to the west has a large sign above in front of it.
1616: There is an old street-lamp on the border of the street.

The street ends here with the shore directly ahead to the north. Off to the west is a dense collection of homes almost like a miniature village inside Harlond. A number of pretty flowers grow here likely planted by nearby residents. The city wall blocks travel east of here.
1617: This sandy area is covered with many large rocks. Moss is growing on many of the rocks and seaweed carried in by the tide lies everywhere. Many birds crawl around here looking for small fish unfortunate enough to have been washed ashore. Travel further east is restricted by the increasing number of large rocks and the nearby city wall. Off to the south are some elven homes.
1618:
An elf is sitting here, fishing for a catch.
An elven guard is standing here at his post.

This short wooden pier stretches about 200 feet out into the Gulf of Lhun. Many elven fishermen sit here for hours trying to catch something for dinner. The waves crash against the pier and it is not uncommon to get drenched as you fish here. The winds in the Gulf are strong and at times even the hardiest fisherman must head for cover.
1619:
A king crab is crawling around in the sand here.
A king crab is crawling around in the sand here.

The sandy shore ends here at the beginning of a small cliff. The cliff is not high but it is steep enough that you have no chance of climbing it. The rocky surface is smooth but bumpy. At one time it probably had sharp edges but erosion by water has taken its toll. The rock face is covered with bright green moss. Many strong waves crash against the rocks and water splashes in your direction. There are many crabs crawling around here. They seem to like the shade offered by the rock face.
1620: This short slightly sandy road heads north towards the shore. Rows of elm trees have been planted along it and it is quite pretty. Up ahead you can see the deep blue water of the Gulf of Lhun. Violent waves crash against the shore and many birds fly above you.
1621: Home of the Old Elven Mage

A large bulletin board, entitled "Mages' Guild", is mounted here.
Malindon the elven mage is here reading over some old texts.
An elven boy is running about here.

This is the house of an old elven sorcerer and his wife. The decor of the room leaves no question that he has been very successful. You can still see numerous magical tomes and small pouches likely filled with components needed for powerful magic. Perhaps you will be able to learn some minor skills here.
1622: There is an old street-lamp on the border of the street.

This gravel road leads north and south, following the great wall surrounding the city. Looking up, you see the top of the wall, some twenty feet high, and the blue sky above it. Some small plants and bushes grow against the base of the wall here. The road goes north towards the city gate and south towards a large park.
1623: This is a large park which seems very popular among the elven citizens. The trees are fairly dense here and you can see some small animals scurrying about. The park continues to the south and a small home lies to the west. The solid city wall lies directly to your east.
1624:
A low shrub with bright green, oblong leaves is growing here.
A seagull is soaring above you.
An elven boy is running about here.

You stand in a large, tranquil area of the park with many pretty trees and small bushes. This is definitely a great place to relax and many elves seem to be doing just that. The park continues to the west and north and the city wall lies to the south and east.
1625:
A placid pond is here, inviting you to take a refreshing drink.
A fat carp swims here.
A fat carp swims here.
An elven citizen is here enjoying the day.

You stand in a large, tranquil area of the park surrounded almost completely by trees. It is so peaceful here that you can easily forget that you are in the midst of a great city. Several elves lounge here and there, resting against the trunks of the great trees. The park seems to continue to the east and there is a small home to the north.
1626:
A brass lantern has been set on the ground.
A ranger stands quietly here, willing to teach his knowledge of woodcraft.

You have entered a small house situated among some small young trees. This peaceful place houses a ranger quite willing to teach you all his skills. With the park and some fairly dense areas of trees to the south, he easily has space to teach you skills like riding and tracking.
1627:
Hanging above the entrance is a sign.
An elven grocer is standing here, quietly humming to herself.
You are now in a decent sized building with many well-stocked shelves. Many people are moving around in here and the grocer's business seems to be doing pretty well.
1628:
There is an old street-lamp on the border of the street.
An elven boy is running about here.
The road runs north and south here. Off to the north is a large square which appears quite populated. The road here is lined with many buildings but none have entrances from here.
1629: There is an old street-lamp on the border of the street.

This is the busiest road in the city. It runs west and east from here, and people are hurrying along in both directions. From the north you can smell the aroma of fresh-baked bread, and to the south you see what looks like a small grocery.
1630: There is an old street-lamp on the border of the street.

You are on the busiest road in town, leading north and south. To the west you can see a grassy area, with several people walking here and there and children playing among the trees. You are barely able to avoid being pushed and shoved by the groups of passing people.
1631:
There is an old street-lamp on the border of the street.
A pretty elven girl is strolling around here.

You stand on the Main Road, which leads to the north and west. To the east, barely noticeable, is a small street heavily shaded by monstrous trees, and to the south you see a large grassy area. To the south is a beautiful house with a highly decorated door.
1632:
There is an old street-lamp on the border of the street.
A beautiful and docile horse is standing here.

You can walk in virtually every direction here. To the east and west the Main Road continues, and to the north you see a small grassy area. A much larger area of greenery is to the south and it seems to extend for quite some distance.
1633:
A mailbox stands here stuffed full of messages.
A heavy desk, made of solid oak, stands here.
A secretary is sitting here.
An elven boy is running about here.

This is a small courier post, much like a post office. This particular post serves Harlond. Elves in travelling clothes sprint here and there awaiting the daily rider to arrive. There is a small sign posted on the wall here.
1634:
On the centre of the back wall, you can see a big sign.
Kevlar the elven armourer is here polishing items he has on display.
A pretty elven girl is strolling around here.

You have entered Kevlar's armour shop which specializes in leather and chain mail. Although this is a small shop, the items are of fine elven quality. The wall behind the counter is covered by shiny pieces for sale and the heat from the forge can be felt coming from a back room.
1635:
A large bulletin board, entitled "Warriors' Guild Board", is mounted here.
A weapons rack stands against the wall.
An impressive elven knight stands watch here (glowing).

You have entered the yard dedicated to the teaching of warrior skills. Warriors of all types and ability fence and practice other skills all around the yard, and the smell of sweat is almost overwhelming.
1636:
A white-painted bench is here.
A large beautiful rose bush is blooming here.
Deep inside the bush, there are two red roses with leaves and thorny stems and two white roses with leaves and thorny stems.
This is a large pretty garden, seemingly moonlit even in the light of day. Pale white flowers tell you something sad but beautiful, and masterly grown trees offer shadow when the sun is too hot.
1637: There is an old street-lamp on the border of the street.

You are on a small street leading north and south. Small houses line the eastern side of the street, and to the west you see a white building with large pillars of stone standing beside the entrance. To the south you hear some splashing sounds.
1638:
A sign rests on the counter in front of you.
An elven baker is standing here, covered in flour.
This is probably the biggest bakery in the town of Harlond. The selection of fresh goods is enormous, and the prices seem quite reasonable.
1639: There is an old street-lamp on the border of the street.

The Road continues on to the south and to the west where it passes through a gate to the older part of the town. To the east you see a small grassy area, and to the north a smaller street leads to a row of buildings.
1640: There is an old street-lamp on the border of the street.

The older, but richly ornamented facades reveal that this is an older part of Grey Havens. To the east, newer houses can be seen through a gate, and this street continues to the west, sloping slightly downwards.
1641: There is an old street-lamp on the border of the street.

There is a small slope here and the old street continues to the east and west almost horizontally. To the west the street runs towards a tall watchtower made out of stone, standing near the tall city wall. The buildings around you are neatly and delicately built, the walls covered with colorful flowers in some spots.
1642: There is an old street-lamp on the border of the street.

The street is sloping east-west here. The old, ornamented buildings are well-maintained but slightly stained by the salt sea winds from the gulf of Lhun. Connected to the city wall to the south is a spiral staircase leading up to a tower.
1643:
There is an old street-lamp on the border of the street.
Cirdan the Shipwright is standing here (glowing).
The elven lieutenant is here looking for any sign of trouble.

This long and proud street is named after the Valar's domain which is now beyond the circles of the earth but was reachable when the city was founded. It ends in a flat, open place west of here and also leads east. A strong animal smell is coming from the north.
1644: There is an old street-lamp on the border of the street.

The Valinor Street ends here, not far from the Harlond quay. Only a few small buildings without any ornaments stand among the trees here. The street continues to the east, and to the west you can see the edge of the city quay with moored boats of many different types. The faint sound of water lapping against stone mixed with occasional shrieks from seagulls drifts in from the Gulf of Lhun.
1645:
There is an old street-lamp on the border of the street.
A pretty elven girl is strolling around here.

You are on a round part of the quay, paved with white, recently cleaned stones. In the centre, a slender tree has been planted. Its white flowers illuminate the surrounding facades without casting shadows anywhere. A long pier stretches out to the west, and a proud and wide street begins to the east. The quay, lined with boats of all sizes, begins to the south and continues further north.
1646: An elf is sitting here, fishing for a catch.

You are standing on a narrow jetty, no more than six feet across, which runs out towards a tall, ancient lighthouse to the west. The rocks are a bit slippery so you have to walk slowly. Boats lie on both sides and cold waves bounce them slowly up and down.
1647: A cold, salt wind blows across the jetty here, and some waves are big enough to wash your feet. A tall, stone-built lighthouse stands nearby, having withstood thousands of storms. Its entrance, through a wooden door, is to the north, and the way back is to the east.
1648: Built by the first elven settlers of Grey Havens in the beginning of the Second Age, this lighthouse stands as upright as ever. Its walls are of solid stone taken from the dwarven quarries of Ered Luin and they show little sign of erosion. A spiral staircase leads up, and there is a wooden trapdoor which presumably leads down.
1649: You have entered the main floor of a small tower. A large red banner hangs from the north wall, on which a resplendent crest has been depicted. On the eastern edge of the room, a large stairwell allows passage to the upper floor, while to the south a staircase has been carved out of the rough rock, leading down. The room is lit by sconces built into the walls, but is otherwise bare.
1650: There is an old street-lamp on the border of the street.

This is the main quay for ships coming from Pelargir, the port of Anduin and Minas Tirith. A few ships still travel that route, and the quay is far from empty despite the Shadow near Pelargir. You can walk north and south.
1651: There is an old street-lamp on the border of the street.

Large ships recently arrived from the cities of Belfalas and Lebennin are docked here. Some of them are in need of repair and you notice some Elves working on a few of them. South of here ships from Pelargir lie and the quay continues to the north. The Gulf of Lhun stretches out to the west, its salty water lapping against the grey quay.
1652:
There is an old street-lamp on the border of the street.
An elven guard is standing here at his post.
Several large ships, both the slender, elven ships and the sturdier-looking man-made vessels are moored here. The quay continues south and east.
1653: The Pier of the Grey Havens

A sign is attached to a post here.
There is an old street-lamp on the border of the street.

The great elven ships departing for Valinor leave from this pier. Many long farewells have occurred at this pier. As each month passes, more and more elves tire of Middle-earth and decide to sail back to Valinor in the west. You can go back to the quay to the east. A wooden barrier prevents you from reaching the western end of the pier.
1654: There is an old street-lamp on the border of the street.
This is the large market-place where goods arriving by ship are auctioned out, traded, and transported to distant kingdoms. Large quays go further north and west.
1655: There is an old street-lamp on the border of the street.

This is where the large ships enter Harlond. The huge white sails are fluttering in the salt breeze, and sailors are climbing around in the rigs. The quay continues north, and connects to a market south. A pier reaches out into the Gulf of Lhun to the west.
1656: The finest sails on this side of the ocean are made here. They are white as snow, light and strong enough to take advantage of fearsome gales. The exit to the quay is west.
1657: There is an old street-lamp on the border of the street.

The narrow street continues north-south between both small and large buildings, most of which are very basically built and seem robust. There are almost no shops here, and the buildings seem to be used as workshops and for storage. The wind carries the smells of fish and salt water from the Gulf of Lhun that lies to the north.
1658:
There is an old street-lamp on the border of the street.
An elven woman is here merrily walking along.

The strong smell of fish from the north blends into the rich atmosphere of a crowded street filled with many workshops and restaurants and a faint bitter-sweet scent of unknown origin from the west. An elaborate metal sign representing a shiny sword entangled in seaweed hangs outside a small shop to the east. The street goes north-south but is so narrow that a cat could easily jump from one balcony to another.
1659:
There is a large sign on the wall.
An elven herbalist is watching his merchandise here.
A sturdy pack horse is standing here.

The scent of a thousand rare herbs blend together in the air of this tiny but well stocked shop. Hundreds of small pots and jars with mystic inscriptions fill the shelves along with fresh herbs in water-filled vases and oddly-shaped containers filled with spices with remote, exotic and sometimes unknown origins. Your mind feels heavy, and you suspect that this is a subtle trick of the shopkeeper to make you pay more.
1660:
A small flask has been left here on the ground.
There is an old street-lamp on the border of the street.
A beautiful and docile horse is standing here.

From here, the fishing-boats go out before sunrise, and return many hours later, with hopefully a good load of fish to sell on the market. The quay is littered with wooden boxes, rope coils, buckets, and much else that the elven fishermen didn't bother to stuff away. The market is east, and the quay continues west.
1661:
A note has been posted on a pole here.
There is an old street-lamp on the border of the street.
An elven guard is standing here at his post.
This is where the ferry docks. Riding this can take you to Forlond on the other side of the Gulf of Lhun. The quay continues east and south.
1662:
A sign is nailed to a pole.
There is an old street-lamp on the border of the street.

From far away, the great ships arrive here, carrying a precious load of herbs and spices. A bitter-sweet scent almost makes you forget the intense smell of fish, and there is a small shop, striking in its insignificance, to the east. The quay continues north and south.
1663:
There is a sign hanging from a pole.
There is an old street-lamp on the border of the street.
A fishmonger is standing here, loudly advertising today's catch.

This is the famous market in Grey Havens where all the delicacies from the sea can be found at the high quality, needed to satisfy the demand of Elven gourmets. Fishmongers are loudly advertising their loot and prices, and the whole place smells not only of fish, but also of oysters, crabs, edible seaweed, and everything else. There are quays to the north and west, a street going south, and an inn to the east.
1664: There is an old street-lamp on the border of the street.
Ahh, what a lovely smell! Fishing-boats arrive with the gifts of the sea ready to be sold on the market or brought home to the fishermen's wives. The market is south and you can also go east.
1665: A fishing net has been left here.

This is where the fishermen of the Havens hang up their nets to let them dry. It makes the place look as if giant spiders lived here, hence the name. Old fishermen sit on wooden benches, mending a few meshes in their favourite nets. You can go east and west from here, and the Gulf of Lhun is directly north.
1666:
A tiny spider is here, eating a tiny bug.
A wolf spider is here, among the trees.

The nets here are not fishing-tackle, but real cobwebs. The elves have long appreciated the beauty in the skilfully woven webs glistening with morning dew and this is a garden where the not completely tame spiders have been encouraged to freely show their art. Less natural webs can be seen to the west.
1667:
There is an old street-lamp on the border of the street.
An elven boat-fisher is here hard at work on his boat.
Cirdan the Shipwright is standing here (glowing).
The elven lieutenant is here looking for any sign of trouble.

This is the main construction place for ships in Harlond. Half-built ships rest here like the ribcage of a dead animal. Singing ship-builders and woodworkers are here building the hull of the famous elven ships. They treat the wood with such care and love you would think it was alive. Cirdan himself often directs the building helping keep them as sea-worthy as they have been the last half-dozen millennia.
1668:
There is an old street-lamp on the border of the street.
A stocky mountain mule is here, waiting to serve.
A stocky mountain mule is here, waiting to serve.
A domesticated pony, beast of burden to many, stands here.

The street is crowded, and voices speaking many languages are mixed with the smells of newly caught fish from the market to the north, food from the nearby restaurants, and wood, stone, ivory, leather, cloth, and hemp from the elven craftsmen's workshops. The street goes north and south, and there is a shop of some kind to the west.
1669:
A map has been dropped here.
There is an old street-lamp on the border of the street.
The large Well of Osse is here, full of sparkling clear water.
Curifil the elven guide stands here carrying an old book.

You are standing in a narrow square surrounded by old buildings, a multitude of shops, restaurants, bars, ateliers, and many happy elven citizens. A large well dominates the scene. The well is always full of clear, fresh water and serves not only as a water source but also as the meeting place in the inner parts of Harlond. Passages lead off in all directions. In particular, the Seagull Inn is located to the west.
1670: There is an old street-lamp on the border of the street.

The narrow passage, named after the well in the inner town, goes north and south here. At its narrowest place, you can touch the house walls on both sides of the passage with your arms stretched out, but people pass each other elegantly anyway.
1671: A note is attached to the wall here.

Despite being a bit removed from the other shops in town, many customers are moving about in here. Many different pets are available. You can hear a multitude of different sounds in here. It really is a bit loud. If you would like a pet, you should probably decide quickly. A grey-haired elven shopkeeper is standing here, cleaning up after the animals.
1672:
A large bulletin board, entitled "Board of the Free Peoples", is mounted here.
A note is stuck to the wall.
A huge clock is standing here.
A white-painted bench is here.
