1865: You walk upon a venerable road. Stretching amongst rolling hills, leading you ever closer to the sea, and the home of the Shipwright. Your boots break the silence on gravel polished by endless generations of fellow travellers, and you breathe in the clear air, blown by breezes out of the downs. All is quiet here, though you cannot be sure if the silence is serene or threatening.
1866: 'Ever on, ever on,' they say of this road, which carries your weight effortlessly upon its back through the hills and vales that populate this land. You can almost hear the sea instead of the cobbles upon which you tread, and can almost hear Cirdan calling you to join him and follow him across the sea. But you shake away these dreams and see only hills around you.
1867: Veering around a particularly impassable hill, the road makes due by bending along its length, like the slither of a snake. Even this mighty road must bow down to the downs which surround it. The hills, like waves in an earthen sea, smother the road and bind it like a prisoner, forcing it to run like water in their cracks.
1868: The road makes a bend around a lesser hill with a single tree on its top and thereby run east and south. To the east the road goes straight through some low hills and the hillsides to your west blocks the way in that direction.
1869: Looking along this great road, you see a grassy flat begin to eat away at the hills, stretching to your south, and emerging to your north, farther east. You wonder if perhaps, the end of these hills is near, and if it is, what must lie beyond? But then in the distance, as if answering your silent question, you see more hills, as if the plains were a mere interlude in their parade.
1870: The road runs through the edge of the Shire, stretching westward through the far downs to the sea beyond. Constructed by men and elves, it cuts a straight line through a grassy prairie. A few flowers are scattered among the thick grass that lines the road, their scent barely discernible. Large shapes move from time to time through the prairie further off the road, but it is impossible to determine what they might be from here.
1871: The road to the sea goes ever and on right through a small grassy prairie, while steep hills stand like walls to its sides. The stones of the road carry the marks of many travellers and uncountable carts. The air is full of the smell of flowers which grow in the medium high grass.
1872: Looking along this great road, you see a grassy flat begin to eat away at the hills, stretching to your north, and emerging to your south, farther west. You wonder if perhaps, the end of these hills is near, and if it is, what must lie beyond? But then in the distance, as if answering your silent question, you see more hills, as if the plains were a mere interlude in their parade.
1873: The hills hammer this road, like iron out of a forge, to suit them, and here, such has the road been hammered, forced to bend itself around a mountainous hill which imposes itself upon you, almost regal, like the king of the downs. Even the road must pay its dues to the king, and contorts itself into a bow. The other hills rise up around, like courtiers in the king hill's court, and the road, his jester.
1875: The road bores onward through these downs like a blind mole, following some hidden logic that only it knows. You stand in a valley between two hills, on a road which seems to travel endlessly forward, you wonder if you will ever see the end of the road, or even of these downs, which tower everywhere about you, trapping you, enclosing you.
1876: 'Ever on, ever on,' they say of this road, which carries your weight effortlessly upon its back through the hills and vales that populate this land. You can almost hear the sea instead of the cobbles upon which you tread, and can almost hear Cirdan calling you to join him and follow him across the sea. But you shake away these dreams and see only hills around you.
1877:
A stocky Bounder is here safeguarding the Shire.
A stocky Bounder is here safeguarding the Shire.

The gravel road runs east and west through the rolling hills of the White Downs. The sides of the road are covered in closely cropped grass. Just to the south of the road, a long scar has cut itself a way through the hills. It might be possible to descend down into it, but climbing back up seems a lot harder.
1878: The road is made out of brown and grey cobblestone, and it runs in an east-west direction. Sloping slightly, it ascends into the White Downs to the west. A short distance to the east, the town of Michel Delving lies proudly, with several hobbit dwellings and gardens. Just off the road to the north stands a large tower.
1879:
A well-crafted white fountain is here, water pouring forth from it.
A stocky Bounder is here safeguarding the Shire.

A large gravel road runs in an east-west direction here, being crossed by a few smaller paths going north and south. Clustered around the roadside lies several hobbit dwellings, like small dents in the grassland. Most of the hobbit-holes have carefully tended gardens around them, with the scent of flowers filling the air. The hobbit village continues to the east, while the large road ascends slightly to the west, as it climbs the White Downs. A large, thorny hedge follows the path leading south.
1880: A Shirriff stands here, keeping a watchful eye on things.

The gravel road continues through a hobbit village. Several dwellings and houses stands on both sides of the road. Most of them are built in stone, but some others are carved out of the ground itself. The largest house is a whitewashed stone-building with a carved oak door, standing just south of the road. In the distance to the west, the White Downs rise up to meet the horizon.
1881: A smiling hobbit child is playing around here.

The gravel here is hard-packet and trampled. The road broadens a bit in the west. There lies the village of Michel Delving, scattered with hobbit dwellings. A small hobbit burrow lies just to the south, marking the outskirts of the village. Bordering the north side of the road stands an orchard, surrounded by green fields. To the east, the large road continues.
1882:
A trim Bounder is here, patrolling the Shire and watching for evil.
A cute rabbit is here.

The large road, made of hard-packed gravel, goes onward in an east-west direction. To the west it starts a slight ascension towards the White Downs. The village of Michel Delving can be seen resting there, at the foot of the downs. The southern side of the road harbours a large green field.
1883: A large gravel road runs through the fields here. It bends here to avoid a small hill, lying just to the east. Fields of strange plants cover the ground to the south. The road continues to the north, and to the west in a slight incline.
1884: The large road turns both south and eastward here, toward a small hill that shields whatever lies beyond. To the west a small gradient leads up to an orchard, while thick grasses cover the land to the northern side of the road extending out as far as the eye can see.
1885:
A trim Bounder is here, patrolling the Shire and watching for evil.
A hobbit is here walking around.

The gravel road bends its way around a small hill that lies just south. It looks like it would not be too hard for anyone to climb up and watch the surroundings. To the north lie vast plains, covered in tall grasses and a few bushes. The road goes onward to the east and west.
1886:
A hobbit is here walking around.
A trim Bounder is here, patrolling the Shire and watching for evil.

The road is made of hard-packed gravel worn over the course of many years. The road cuts through some grassy plains, while heading eastwards or to the west around a small hill. Just to the south of the road lies a large farmyard, where a wooden and a stone building surrounds it.
1887: Hard-packed and dirty, the gravel road runs east and west through the plain, dividing it in separate fields. To the north the grass grows quite tall and dense, while it becomes more of a desolate wasteland to the south. Standing out against the south-west fields is a building made of stone, lying just off the road.
1888: The gravel road runs through the landscape, going east and west from here. Frequently used, it has become hard-packed and worn. The fields to the south of the road are laid in waste, while the overgrown grasslands lie in stark contrast on the northern side.
1889: You are travelling along the East Road. It stretches to the east and the west here. To the south, you notice a small orchard. It looks like a good place to rest your weary feet.
1890: You are travelling along the East Road. It stretches to the east and the west here. To the south, you notice a small orchard. It looks like a good place to rest your weary feet.
1891: You travel onward on the East Road. To the north, you see a huge tree stretching its branches high into the sky. It looks like it might be fun to climb on it.
1893: The road bends to the north and west here. You can also enter the plains to the east and south.
1894: You travel along the East Road. Here the road bends from the east to the south. To the north, there is a low hill covered with some fields.
1895: You are travelling onward along the East Road. Looking south, you see a great expanse of plains stretching out to the horizon.
1896: The road runs east and west here. It is bordered on the south by a vast expanse of plains. The low hill to the north you realise is a hobbit hole. You see the front porch north of you.
1897: The road here bends from the north to the west. To the south, the plains stretch off into the distance. You see a low hill to the north-west.
1898: Here the East Road bends from east to south around a low hill. To the north is a small pond. You can see the plain stretching off to the south- east.
1899: You are travelling through plains along the East Road. Looking to either side, you see that you can leave the road and wander off into the plains.
1900: You are travelling through plains along the East Road. Looking to either side, you see that you can leave the road to the north and wander off into the plains there. While it is blocked to the south by a dense brush.
1901: Tree-covered hills lie to your southeast, Tuckborough and Tookbank nestled among them. Grassy plains lie to your north, and Michel Delving is somewhere to your west. The road continues to the east and west.
1902: A squirrel scampers around here, looking for nuts from the trees.

Tree-covered hills lie to your southeast, Tuckborough and Tookbank nestled among them. Grassy plains lie to your north, and Michel Delving is somewhere to your west. The road continues to the east and west.
1903: Tree-covered hills lie to your southeast, Tuckborough and Tookbank nestled among them. Grassy plains lie to your north, and Michel Delving is somewhere to your west. The road continues to the north and west. A path leaves the road, heading south. A sign is here.
1904: A hobbit is here walking around.

Tree-covered hills lie to your southeast, Tuckborough and Tookbank nestled among them. Fields lie to your north, and Michel Delving is somewhere to your west. The road continues south and east of you.
1905: A sparrow is flapping around on the ground.

Tree-covered hills lie to your southeast, Tuckborough and Tookbank nestled among them. Grassy plains lie to your north, and Michel Delving is somewhere to your west. The road continues to the north and west.
1906: A stocky Bounder is here safeguarding the Shire.

Here, in the meeting of the roads, a small village resides. An occasional hobbit strolls by, thinking of dinner most likely. To the west is the guard post that helps protect the village. A small unkept road leads north.
1907: The road continues west as always, leading to the small village of Waymeet. To the east the road bends towards the heart of the Shire.
1908: The road continues ever on westward. The surrounding lands are quiet and serene. Occasionally, the sounds of hobbit children playing break the calm silence.
1909: Here, a big stone has been set in the middle of the East Road to mark the meeting point of three of the four farthings in the Shire: the eastern, the southern and the western ones. To the north there are some meadows and two towns, but a large building prevents any step in that direction. To the south only fields can be seen.
1910: This crossroad lies in the middle of the plain. The East Road runs east and west, passing through the Shire. There is a small path to the south and a large road heads towards a village in the north. A sign can be seen at the northern side of the crossroad.
1911: Here the East Road passes through the farmed plains that cover the land. While there is a dark lane to the north, which leads to the bank of the river, the road is otherwise monotonously straight. The earthy ground is covered by innumerable tracks, made by passing hobbits, horses and carts.
1912: A sturdy pack horse is standing here.

To the north, the road is bordered by a river which runs east-west and to the south the road is bordered by some fields. Beyond the fields, a small green hill is visible along with a few lonely trees and some farms. The outline of a small town is barely discernible in the distant north-west.
1913: Here, the road is very muddy, making it easy to distinguish a set of footprints heading towards the southern field. To the north a small river can be heard and to the far south the plain slopes upwards forming a large hill.
1914: The road continues east-west across the Shire. It is evident from the well worn tracks that this road is used by many of the inhabitants of the Shire. Parallel to the road, at some distance to the north, a small river flows towards the east. To the far south, beyond the fields, there are some hills.
1915: Here, a fork in the road branches to the north and leads to the the town of Dwaling. Along this path, one can see the nearby river and fields. The East Road continues to the east and west across the Shire.
1916: This road, built across the Shire, heads in an east-west direction. To the north a small river overflows its bank and to the south there are some evenly spaced trees, blocking the view in that direction.
1917: Just east of here there is a small village and to the west, several miles down the road, there is a crossroad. To the north a small river has overflowed its bank and to the far south the fields slope upwards forming a green hill.
1918: Inside the Small Village of Frogmorton

A large fountain, made from grey stone, pours water from its centre.
A cute rabbit is here.
A pretty hobbit maiden is walking around here.

This small village is formed by some houses built on the sides of the East Road. It is also used for travellers and adventurers often to take a rest since it has a good inn. The Floating Log is just north of here, offering good food and beverages.
1919: Inside the Small Village of Frogmorton
A duck is here, quacking happily.

You are in a small village built on the sides of the East Road. Some houses and hobbits can be seen around. Although this place is not too populated, it has quite a good inn, since many travellers and adventurers use it to take a rest: The Floating Log Inn.
1920: The East Road continues, passing through the Shire now. This land is peaceful and its people friendly. You can count on a safe passage through it. To the south a hobbit farm is built, and to the north the Water goes silently to join with the Brandywine. To the west you see a small village.
1921: The East Road continues, passing through the Shire now. This land is peaceful and its people friendly. You can count on a safe passage through it. To the south a hobbit farm has been built, and to the north the Water goes silently to join with the Brandywine.
1922: A hobbit is here walking around.

The road, that has crossed the most strange lands, is now running through a quiet and peaceful region. One can follow the road east or west. To the north, a stand of reeds makes it impossible to go there. To the south you see furrowed fields behind a small fence. It seems easy to leap over it.
1923: The road, that is wandering through the most strange lands, is now crossing a quiet and peaceful region. You can follow the road east or west. To the north, a stand of reeds makes it impossible to go there. To the south you see furrowed fields behind a small fence. It is easy to leap over it.
1924: The road is quite easy here. Everything seems peaceful and one could hardly expect any hostility from the surroundings. To the north is a yard protected by a fence. You can follow the way to the west or east.
1925:
A duck is here, quacking happily.
A pretty hobbit maiden is walking around here.

The road continues to the west and east. The region you are crossing now seems very peaceful, and you can walk without being worried about danger. To the east you see a small village of really little houses.
1926:
A stocky Bounder is here safeguarding the Shire.
A duck is here, quacking happily.

The road now is crossing a small village formed by cute little houses of hobbits. They are really small. All around you, you see the people of the village doing their labors, walking from one place to another. The road goes to the west and the east. North of here a little street goes through the houses.
1927: The road goes on, taking you to strange places. This area, surrounded by green fields, seems quite peaceful though. The road continues to the west and east. Further in the west, you can see a small village of tiny houses.
1928: You are travelling on the Old East Road, with green fields all around you. To the north you can see the Bridgefields, and far in the west you see a small hobbit village. The road goes west-east here.
1929: The road is quiet and peaceful around here. A small fence is south of the road, preventing you from entering a huge garden. To the north you see a small hill, and the road continues west and east.
1930: The road goes on, leading to unknown and mysterious places. The road is now crossing a region of peaceful fields, where the air is clear and quite enjoyable. All around you, green fields extend into the distance. A small river is cutting the fields north of here, and a small farm is to the south.
1931: You now stand on the Old East Road...it looks well rutted from the many who have passed this way. The road continues on in an east-west direction. There is vegetation to the north of the road and traverse is possible there.
1932: You are standing on the Old East Road in the extreme east of the Shire. Northwest of here you see the Bridgefields, and south of here you can see a wide and heavily used path. The road leads on east and west, Brandywine bridge is just east of here.
1934: The road winds its way through a light forest. One might wonder where the this road leads, but for now there seems an odd sense of safety here at least compared to the forest.
1935: You are travelling along on the Old East Road, which winds its way through a light forest here. There seems to be some fields beyond the light forest to the north, but there is a shadow over the forest in the south.
1936: You are adventuring on a well travelled road going east-west. The road at this point is enclosed by woodland to the north and south. The forest, though light and young along the roadside, appears to age and thicken further to the south.
1937: You are adventuring on a well travelled road going east-west. The road at this point is enclosed by woodland to the north and south. The forest, though light and young along the roadside, appears to age and thicken further to the south.
1938: You are adventuring on the well travelled Old East Road. The road at this point turns southward. There is a light forest bordering the road to the north and west of here. Further to the southwest you see an old and wise forest.
1939: You are adventuring on a well travelled road going east-west. The road at this point is enclosed by woodland to the north and south. The forest, though light and young along the roadside, appears to age and thicken further to the southwest.
1940: Here the road runs east-west and is bordered by a high bank that leads to plains. The road is rutted and there are many pot-holes filled with water from the recent rains. Going east the road sinks down into a ravine.
1941: Here the road runs east-west and is bordered by a high bank that leads to plains. The road is rutted and there are many pot-holes filled with water from the recent rains. The road turns slightly but still heads mostly in the east-west direction.
1942: Here the road runs east-west and is bordered by a high bank that leads to plains. The road is rutted and there are many pot-holes filled with water from the recent rains. The road turns slightly but still heads mostly in the east-west direction.
1943: Here the road turns northward. You see that wagon wheels have dug deep ruts into the road and that they are filled with water from recent heavy rains. You feel that you are not too far from town.
1944: Here the road runs east-west. You see that wagon wheels have dug deep ruts into the road that are filled with water from recent heavy rains. There are many potholes, and the road is bordered by high plains to the south, and a light forest to the north.
1950: Turning and bending, the Old East Road leads around a few sudden depressions or rocky heights, which are covered with boulders. Small bushes have grown so near to the road that their branches already touch the ancient stones and a few roots have begun work apart the worn pavement.
1951: Many cracks cover the ancient road. The pavement is broken in many places and small patches of thin grass have taken root between the stones. The road itself climbs over a small hill, only to descend quite fast into a slight depression. Hills dug by moles can be spotted on the northern side of the road.
1952: The road runs between two ancient oaken trees. Their huge crowns span high above and cast a huge shadow on the ground. Countless days of sun have bleached all of the stones that seldom get touched by shadows. Fallen leaves, mixed with rain-water, have turned the stones below the trees darker over time, making the road seem to be made of a different kind of stone in that place.
1956: A pewter candlestick is standing here.

This place gives you an idea about the lifestyle of the priest. The room is barely furnished other than a few chairs and a table for occasions when the people need the priest's advice, perhaps. A small lamp in a niche in the west wall is the only light source. The floor is covered with a thin carpet which feels quite soft to the feet.
1957:
There is a lot of water on the ground.
An elven boy is running about here.
A small, loyal beagle is here, eager to please.
A beautiful and docile horse is standing here.

This area has been cut out of the dark forest that surrounds it for crops. It spreads about half a mile in each direction. When you look eastwards, you see what appears to be a large building right next to the forest boundary. To the west is the elven village. You are walking on a small muddy path that goes directly towards the structure in the east.
1958: A lonely, sad-looking elf is sitting here in deep thoughts.

This building serves as a refuge if you get caught in the rain while out in the fields, but its main purpose is to store the surplus food grains for use later. You can see storerooms sectioned off to hold different grains, but you are not able to access those piles. You also see large haystacks and piles of oat near the walls.
1959: You are in a large room which is filled with cereals and fodder for the farm animals. The roof looks sturdy and leak-proof. The barn is to the north and you can see the fields in the west through a small window. The walls of this room are thick and strong, and there are some strange weeds thrown about the room, probably to keep out the pests.
1960:
A shiny gold ring has been abandoned here.
A pair of rigid leather boots are on the ground.
Greater parts of a broken weapon are lying on the ground.

This room is dark and quiet and the shadows loom large. The walls are dry and hard. A layer of dust has settled on the floor, indicating that this place has not been used in a long time. Thick stone columns support the roof every twenty feet or so.
1962: You find yourself in a damp room with a low ceiling. The walls of solid but bare stone return an echo of every sound you make. The floor is covered with dust and mud, and there is fungus growing on the walls. As you look up, you see that the roof has cracks in it that allow water to seep in. You can sense something strange but no matter how hard you try, you cannot figure it out.
1963:
A restless rabbit bounces around.
A brown fox is here, looking for some rabbits to chew up.

You are standing in a field just north of the road that leads to and away from the Grey Havens. The field is covered with soft, green grass. All is quiet around here but you can hear high-pitched noises made by some insects that you cannot see or locate. This would be a good place to camp if you wanted to stay a while - since there is nothing here to disturb you.
1964: The road is just to the south of you. Soft, lush green grass covers the whole area. The sounds made by wind, as it passes over the grass, make you yearn for your home and your friends. Perhaps you should stay here a little while and let that feeling take its course. But if you have to ride on, you might just let the memory of this place take a hold in your mind.
1965: A fallow deer is grazing peacefully here.

The grass has grown much taller here, but it is still soft and green. This grassy field ends a little distance north from here, where a dense and gloomy looking grove begins. The branches of the trees in the grove are so inter- twined as to make it impossible to go in there. Besides, you have the distinct impression that going in there might not turn out to be very safe.

You have entered the home of a family of wolves. Perhaps it would be wise to retreat if you can. The walls of this place have scratch marks all over them. As soon as you entered, something began to move fast, and then they came into view as they made a lunge towards you.
1967: The grove is dense and almost impossible to walk through, here. Everywhere you look, the trees loom large over you, reducing your long range view. Now and then, everything becomes very quiet. You find however, that this place is not as quiet as it appeared from outside. Dim but sharp sounds of activity can be heard coming from every direction. Something dangerous and wild lives here, it appears.

Loud and wild noises are coming from all around you and this makes you want to leave this place quickly. Something unseen is definitely moving around out there.

You are surrounded by tall trees in every direction. This grove is a very strange one. One moment everything is quiet and still, and the next second, everything seems to come alive. You try your best to hide from all the wild animals here, but they say that the wild ones hunt by their noses as much as by their eyes and ears.

Wild animals are bound to be around. Once in a while, you hear a loud roar or a howl, and your blood freezes for a moment.

A very dense and dark grove with rather tall trees is visible as you look north. Upon careful observation, you notice a small gap between the trees which allows you to enter the grove if you so desire. Far to the south, you can see the road leading to the Grey Havens. The fields continue in the east and the west.
1978:

The grassy fields are very silent. Any movement or noise is merely the wind rustling the grass as it passes over the fields. The whole place appears to be safe and peaceful. The grass grows taller in the north and in the east. To the west, the fields continue.
1979: There is a lot of water on the ground.

The lush green grass rises up to your knees here. But the ground is firm and so you can walk here without too much trouble. The fields continue to the west, where the grass grows less high, and to the east. In the north you can see the vegetation growth become quite dense. The road to Grey Havens is to your south.
1980: The vegetation grows thick here, with tall and dark trees beginning to dominate the landscape. Towards the east, you see some grassy plains and in the west, there is a dark grove of trees which looks dangerous. There is a silence in these woods that is both eerie and soothing at the same time. In the south, you see large fields covered with lush green grass.
1981: A large variety of plants and undergrowth can be found here. The ground is quite soft and the vegetation is quite dense. In the west, you can see a dark grove of tall, dark trees, which appears quite frightening. In the south, you see some more trees. As you look east, you see vast, grassy fields covered with soft, green grass. To the north a single tree can be seen in the distance.
1982: A solitary tree can be seen in this small clearing among the woods. Its branches seem particularly robust and able to support a large amount of weight. Wooden beams have been attached to the trunk, allowing one to climb upwards.
1983: An Elven steward stands here, watching over the household.

Several wooden planks and walls have been erected to form a small house within this large tree. Branches and leaves cover you overhead, forming a natural barrier against the rain and weather, while letting the sunlight beam in during the day. To the east, a door leads out onto a rather thick branch.
1984: The wind whips across these plains with very little in the way of protection. If solitude is what you require then this is the right place to have come. The only sign of life is a trail, obviously regularly used, amongst the numerous animal tracks. To the east rise the Far Downs and far to the west, on a clear day, can be seen the Tower Hills beyond which lies Mithlond.

A small pile of stones has been piled here.

Numerous mosses and lichens cover the walls and stones of the place, the odd stunted bush hugging the remaining standing walls. It would appear that someone was here not too long ago... there is what looks like the remains of a fire and a crude shelter, which has collapsed into a heap of branches and matted grass.

Walking here is generally a pleasant and invigourating experience, provided the weather is good, otherwise it can be an extremely miserable, disheartening place. Numerous animal tracks criss-cross the area at regular intervals. To the south is a small stand of trees. A small pile of stones has been set here.

The trail you have been following has brought you to a junction, with a small, well-tended path leading off into the small wooded area to the south. The wind blows hard here seemingly all the time - maybe a quirk in the lie of the land... whatever the case, there is a hut visible in the woods which could provide a certain amount of shelter should you so desire it. A large pile of stones has been built here.

A wide counter stands just in front of the staircase that climbs its way to the upper level of the inn. A large sign hangs from the counter. There are some paintings of famous hobbits hanging on the walls.

Quite obviously, this warm building is the Inn of the Seven Stars. Many hobbits and weary travellers frequently drink themselves into oblivion within its lively walls. There is a huge bar on the far wall. Many kegs of fine ale run along the length of the shelf behind the bar. At one end of the bar is a huge fireplace, where a roaring fire heats the entire room. In the centre of the room and to the north are many tables and benches. A large staircase can just about be seen through the smoke coming from the hobbit pipes and the fire.
2019: The poor decoration of this house indicates it must be the home of a rather poor hobbit. There is a small bed in the corner and a rickety looking table and chairs in the centre of the room. A small window in the west wall looks over the downs.
2020: A small path leads from the road just north of here to the tiny village of Greenholm. It appears to be mainly used by the travellers on their way to either the Shire or the Grey Havens. The typically cautious hobbits who live in Greenholm to the south have probably rarely left their pleasant village. To the north is the road to the Grey Havens.
2021: You are in an empty room which was probably occupied by some poor hobbit family. It looks like this small building wasn't abandoned very long time ago, because there is only a thin dust layer on the floor and you can barely discern spider webs in the corners.
2022:
A smiling hobbit child is playing around here.
A busy hobbit female is here worrying about the home labours.

By hobbit standards, this is quite a plush living room of a house. You can see a small bedroom joining the room and also a small kitchen. The house was obviously not designed for many hobbits to live in, it might have been a first house for a pair of newlywed hobbits.
2023: Many hobbit houses surround the eastern end of Green Street. To the south is a very expensive looking house which must be the home of some important hobbit. It has been recently painted and looks very pretty with its flower garden around it. The houses to the north and east are less remarkable. Although they have gardens, none of them are quite as good as the one to the south.
2024: A well-crafted white fountain is here, water pouring forth from it.

The main street of the small village of Greenholm runs from east to west here. Many hobbits can be seen going about their daily business. To the south is a small shop, with a large sign over the doorway. The main street continues the east and to the west. To the north a path leads up a small rise towards the road to the Grey Havens.
2025: The main street of Greenholm ends at the Inn of the Seven Stars. There is a small pictured sign hanging from a tall post just outside the door. The inn looks warm and cosy and the smoke pouring out of the chimney indicates that there is a hot fire burning fiercely inside. Attached to the Inn just south of here is a small stable. There is a small hobbit house just to the north.

A shopkeeper stands here, eager to sell you his wares.
A drunk hobbit is sprawled on the the ground before you.

The shop is a surprisingly busy shop for a small village in the middle of the Far Downs. From the looks of the shelves, it sells nearly everything a hobbit might need for every day life. The shop was named in the memory of that legendary hobbit gardener Holman the Greenhanded whose descendants formed the Greenhand clan and settled this village many years ago.

Coralled by the road and the hills, the prairie is cut from its other half, and forced to submit to the will of the hills, and the feet of man.

Yet, an occasional stag seems to pass or stop for a mouthful of the green grass from time to time.

2137: Thin but high grass covers this prairie. While many higher hills can be seen in the distance, many smaller ones cover the plain. Over the time a population of moles seems to have done a good deal of digging and have left their low heaps of soft earth all around. Apart from the moles, many other animals of all sizes have left their marks by nibbling on or walking through the grass.
2138: The prairie stretches on in all directions, while low grass forms a dense carpet in the sections between the occasional low bushes. The bushes are sparse, their branches are brown and the leaves a very thin green.

You see no real pass through the dark depths of the downs.

The hills seem ominous, and you wonder, in their dark depths, just what secrets they are hiding.

2147: An altar is here, glowing with a bright light.

You are standing at the ruins of an ancient temple, now partly overgrown. The roof that once was made of stone lies shattered on the floor and the crumbled walls are full of holes. The altar at the end of the temple stands rather intact among the debris. You can tell that not only time has destroyed this once so beautiful temple but some sort of physical force as well.
2148: This pass runs through a valley between the downs. The ground is heavily littered with loose rocks, with tough, yellowish grass scattered among them. There is little sound to be heard here, beyond any that might be made by travellers. Steep hillsides rise up to the east and south, blocking movement in those directions, while to the west the hills rise more gradually.
2149: The windswept downs provide a bleak yet austere view. The only sounds to be heard are the rushing of the wind over the grass and the occasional cry of a falcon riding the air. Walking here is generally a pleasant and invigourating experience, provided the weather is good, otherwise it can be an extremely miserable, disheartening place. Numerous animal tracks criss-cross the area at regular intervals. To the south the downs appear to be ending, giving way to bleak, unwelcoming plains.
2150: South of the road the terrain becomes quite rough: long grasses blow in the wind, the gradual rise and fall of the downs broken by the occasional gully eroded by the action of the weather on the chalk. There is little sign of any form of habitation in the area - the road to the north being the only sign that anybody ever comes near here.
2151: You tread upon a gravelly pass which traverses the valleys between the downs. You walk, crunching upon hard stones and crab grass, among the shadows of silent hills, which lay like scales of a dragon long buried. Little noise besides your own, reaches your ears, and only an oppressive silence greets you. The hills, like watchmen, say nothing, but seem to glare at your every move.
2152:
An intact skeleton of a man is walking around here.
An intact skeleton of a man is walking around here.

You see row upon row of clay-made coffins, sarcophagus upon sarcophagus, lining the walls up to the ceiling. Yet, as you look closer, you notice the coffins have been vandalized. They are destroyed and broken-up in many places and strange marks have scratched out the runes which once covered the coffins and the walls. The smell is oppressively musty here, and you feel your pulse race as you begin to scan the room more and more quickly.
2153: This small cave looks like it was once the burial chamber of some priest. The walls, seemingly once lavishly decorated with symbols, are now just a collection of scratches. The large sarcophagus has been savagely broken into and thrown against the southern wall, while all the once beautiful pottery which once graced the floor has been destroyed. The entire southern wall has been knocked down from the outside, the walls being bent in and crumbled, and not able to save this chamber from being molested. A broken sarcophagus can be seen along that wall.
2154:
A pile of unidentifiable garbage is everywhere.
A strange white skull lies on the floor looking at you.
An old-looking ring, covered with runes, lies here.

This place might once have been a bunk room, but now is simply a mess. Nothing is in order. Things are simply strewn everywhere as if some chaotic whirlwind had blown through. A lack of dust upon anything might suggest that this happened quite recently. What reason someone may have had in tossing around this grouping of worthless junk is a mystery.
2155: This is small but surprisingly clean alcove, totally empty but for a pile of decaying coffins which line the western wall. A quick glance around reveals that this room has been abandoned for a long time. Dust covers all but the most recent tracks of small rodents. The walls are smooth, devoid of any design or fault, making one ponder what use this room might have once had.
2156:
The corpse of a small bat is lying here.
The corpse of a small bat is lying here.
A small bat is standing here (hidden).

Hollowed out by water, this cave is the shape of a huge overturned bowl, its ceiling lost in shadows. Water gathers in a dark pool in its centre, perhaps the remnants of an underground river, now, merely a dark pond. With every traveller's step the clatter of equipment echos wildly through the cave. A dark stream is here, trickling from under the western wall, terminating in a small pond.
2157: Whether it was carved out by the hands of men, or whether it was hollowed by some force of nature you know not. All you see is the bowl-shaped stone walls of the pit which seem to oppress you. The dripping of water from the rock is a torture to your hearing and the musty smell causes you to cough despite yourself. Was this where you were destined to end your travels?
2159: You find yourself on a soft earth trail running through a section of the white downs. So called for the chalk that covers them, they rise up to greet you like so many bleached skulls, as if they once all had faces which have eroded with time. You make little noise as you move through this graveyard of hills, but you always imagine you hear something, or see something, out of the corner of your eye, which always disappears.

2162: You climb up the rough slope and finally find yourself standing upon the King Hill. Standing tallest among the hills, it reigns regally over the downs that surround it. Cool winds sail through you, chilling your bones and causing you to involuntarily shiver. A green grass covers its summit, a living crown upon the King Hill. Though grass covers its top, its sides are covered in a skin of chalk, an immovable face, weathered and bleached by the ages. Looking about from this vantage point, you imagine seeing all of the lands bending out before you, and here, looking down at them, you imagine ruling it all, and you understand why they call it the King Hill.
2163: A sturdy bed made from solid oak lies here, covered in warm blankets.

You are standing in a small building of stone, which sits, like a watchtower upon this hill. There are windows on all sides, and a small bed in the corner. All that graces the rest of the room is a simple table. Though it looks deserted, everything is remarkably clean and dust-free, like it is still, perhaps, lived in. You feel at home here, at peace.
2164: You stand upon a hill so named for a small ranger outpost that graces its summit. Though the sides of the hill are covered in a skin of chalk, the path you took up its side was smoothly sloped and covered with grass. The outpost is small, but reasonably well-kept, and you can enter it by travelling farther up the hill. Looking out, you can see across the downs, and, looking west, you even think you see the spiralling towers of the Grey Havens.
2165: This massive dry trench has sunk well below the level of the surrounding hills. The sides of the gorge are steep, and white from exposed rocks strewn about by frequent small rockslides. The ground towards the northern end of the scar is rubble-strewn, and the slope to the north looks impossible to ascend.
2166:
A sturdy pack horse is standing here.
A sharp-eyed hawk is here stalking some prey.

The gorge runs in a north-south direction, like a scar in the surrounding countryside. Finding itself more than sixty feet below the surrounding hills, not much sunlight ever reaches the ground. Even so, there are a few stunted weeds growing in between the boulders that cover the dry valley-floor. A few broken animal bones lie scattered at places.
2167:
A cute rabbit is here.
A sharp-eyed hawk is here stalking some prey.

The narrow gorge turns eastward through the downs. The steep cliff-sides prevent any travel further to the south and west. In several places the cliff has collapsed, leaving shallow scree slopes. Large rocks and a great deal of rubble lie scattered all over the ground.
2168: The ground of this area is dry and rubble-strewn, from frequent small rock-falls. It is a narrow cleft, about sixty feet below the level of the surrounding hills. Carving its way through the White Downs, the gorge continues to the west, while a scree slope leads to the east.
2169: This old dirt path does not look to be used too often. The thorny hedge follows the path as it bends towards the east or north, too high to make out anything lying behind it. A scree slope leads down into a gorge, marring the White Downs to the west.

A large sack is on the ground.

You drop down into a large hole dug underneath an almost solid floor of garbage. Several roughly hewn shelves hold the things the Ratheads hold dear...junk. The cave itself is very musty and damp, water, and other liquids dripping from the garbage above the trap door. The smell of what you can only hope is excrement fills your nostrils, sending immense images of squalor and filth to your mind's eye.
2173: A smiling hobbit child is playing around here.

Green and healthy apple trees stand all around this grass-covered orchard. Just to the south of the orchard runs a large gravel road, while a smaller dirt path is seen to the west. There is a large sign next to the orchard, with a hand-written notice upon it.
2174: Closely cropped grass covers this field. It looks like a grazing land for cattle. Just to the west of the pasture there is a path running alongside the White Downs. The fields continue to the east and north, while several apple trees forming an orchard stand to the south.

A large piece of fresh, raw meat lies here.
The butchered corpse of a well-fed cow is lying here.
The butchered corpse of a well-fed cow is lying here.
A well-fed cow stands here chewing her cud listlessly.
A hobbit is here walking around.

This field is closely cropped grassland. It is most likely used as a pasture for cattle, judging by the amount of cow dung lying everywhere. To the north lies a small, wooden farmhouse. The grazing lands extend for miles to the south and east. To the west a dirty path runs in a north-south direction.
2176:
There is some pipe-weed here.
A hobbit is here walking around.

A large oaken table and the chairs arranged around it, dominate this small farmhouse. The floor is made out of several wooden planks. It is covered with dirt. Two small, round windows sit in the eastern wall, providing a view of the pasture lying there. Resting against the western wall are a couple of bunk-beds. A door leading out of the house is situated in the south wall.
2178: A Bounder is here, patrolling the Shire and watching for evil.

A small dirt-path runs at the base of the White Downs, lying protectively to the west. To the east of here lies a pasture of lush grass, and a small farmhouse can be seen to the north-east. The dirt-path continues up a hill to the north, and towards the road, several miles to the south. A few large footprints can be seen on the path.
2179: A hobbit is here walking around.

Following the eastern edge of the White Downs, this dirt-path runs in a north-south direction, slowly ascending towards a hill in the north. Just to the east of the path, green pastures stretch lazily. A larger gravel road can be seen a few miles to the south.
2180: This path goes northwards into the White Downs, following their eastern edge. To the west, the downs create leeward, sheltering the path from any wind. However, the abruptness of the cliffs also makes it impossible to travel in that direction. Just to the east of the path, an orchard can be seen, while a large road runs past to the south.
2181: A hobbit farmer is here, thinking about seeds and vegetables.

Cattle-hooves have churned the soil here, making it muddy. A few tufts of grass grow at uneven intervals. Imprinted in the mud are tracks of small animals, as well as those of cattle. Just to the west of the pasture stands a pleasant little farmhouse. Grassland of tall grasses lies to the east, while knee-high grass cover the pasturage to the south.
2182:
The butchered corpse of a well-fed cow is lying here.
A well-fed cow stands here chewing her cud listlessly.

This fallow field is covered in knee-high grasses and weeds. The pasture has not been ploughed for a few years. Grazing lands, looking better tended, lie to the north and west of here. To the east grassland stretches on for miles.

Knee-high grasses and weeds grow wildly covering this field. The soil beneath the unkempt grass is hard and having not been worked on for some time. There are similar looking lands to the north of here, whilst the pasture to the west look more recently tended. For several miles to the east tall grasses can be seen. Just to the south of this field, an orchard sits against the road.
2184: A pretty hobbit maiden is walking around here.

Several apple trees stand in this grass-covered orchard. A few rotting windfall-apples litter the ground below the trees. A thorny hedge has been planted in the south border of the orchard, shielding it from the road that runs there. The orchard continues a couple of miles to the west. To the north lies a fallow field.
2185: Thick, tall grass grows here, providing food and shelter for the animals in the area. The soil is a bit muddy, and tracks of many small creatures can be seen. The grassy lands extend far to the east and south. A pasture for grazing animals can be seen to the west.
2186:
A tall stag is here, grazing peacefully.
A fallow deer is grazing peacefully here.

Tall and thick grass covers the dry ground, rolling like waves of a green sea. Trampled straws form a narrow trail, leading to a pond in the east. The grasslands extend for miles to the south and west. Against the horizon in the west, the white downs can be seen.
2187:
A placid pond is here, inviting you to take a refreshing drink.
A trout swims here.
A trout swims here.

A large, shallow pond rests here. Its muddy perimeter is filled with animal tracks, as well as some growing rush dipping in the water. The water in the middle of the pond looks a bit cleaner, and can be reached by wading a few yards. Wildly growing shrubbery and thistle can be seen in the grasslands to the east. Less overgrown grasslands stretch far to the west and south.
2188: A sparrow is flapping around on the ground.

The grey-green grass that grows here sways lazily in the breeze. A few bushes and patches of clover also dot the plain here and there. The soil is dark and somewhat muddy, filled with prints from various animals. Just to the north lies a large, shallow pond. In every other direction, the grasslands continue, somewhat overgrown in the east.
2189: Tall grasses, grey-green in colour, cover the dark soil. A few bushes stand against a gravel road passing by in the south. Similar fields of grass lie to the north and west, while overgrown grasslands covered in shrubbery and thistle lie to the east.
2190: Thick, green grasses and a few bushes dot the land here. The soil is made of dark earth, and it is quite dry. Fields of grasses stretch for miles in all directions. South of here a large gravel road runs through the grassland. A small hill rises beyond it.
2191: Vast grasslands extend for miles to the north and east. The grasses are thick and tall, in a greyish shade of green. The soil is somewhat muddy, but still dry. A fallow field stretches to the west. Just to the south of here a large road passes by.
2192: A small cluster of clover grows here.

The ground is covered in gently swaying, tall grass. A few, large patches of clover break the monotony of the rolling grassland. These plains stretch further in all directions, except to the west, where a fallow pasture lies.
2193:
A small cluster of clover grows here.
A small cluster of clover grows here.
A fallow deer is grazing peacefully here.
A brown fox is here, looking for some rabbits to chew up.

Tall grass, swaying gently, grows in abundance upon these plains. Only a few patches of clover at scattered intervals break the monotone landscape. The grasslands stretch forever on, in all directions. Beyond them to the west, white downs rise against the skyline.
2194:
A small cluster of clover grows here.
A small cluster of clover grows here.

The land here is reverted to scrub, and covered in wildly growing shrubbery. Rough grasses grow beneath the bushes and a few patches of clover and thistle mar the landscape. Faint animal trails lead to the west, where a large, shallow pond resides. In all other directions, the grassland continues its wild growth.
2195: High stems of thistle reach up towards the sky, as well as overgrown scrub and bushes dotting the land everywhere. A few small trees and young saplings are also present among the bushes. Some animals have made faintly outlined trails on the ground. For miles to both the south and the west, these overgrown grasslands continue.
2196:
A small cluster of clover grows here.
A small cluster of clover grows here.

Stretching for miles in every direction, rough grasses extend among bushes of various sizes. There are stems of thistle, reaching high towards the sky, growing everywhere. Patches of clover also dot the grassland at several occasions.
2197: This plain is overgrown by thicket and high-stemmed thistles. Patches of clover and tufts of rough grasses also dot the landscape. These overgrown grasslands continue for miles in all directions, but they look somewhat less covered with scrub to the west. In the northwest a muddy pond can be seen.
2198: Rough, tall grasses grow densely upon the dry ground. Several high-stemmed thistles and a few thorny thickets also grow scattered around the grassland. The overgrown fields continue for miles to the north and to the east. In the south the scrub gives way to a large gravel road running by in an east-west direction.
2199: The rough grass here grows high and wild, looking to have been neither tended nor cropped in a while. Blotting the grasslands at several places are high stems of thistle, and a few small bushes. The overgrown lands continue to the north and west, while the East Road runs by just to the south.
2200: You are standing on the plains boarding the East Road. To the east you see the plains starting to become overgrown as you leave the cultivated areas. To the south is the East Road wandering mindlessly along its merry way.
2201: There are two piles of pine nuts here.
Squeezing your way down through the hole, you come out in a small chamber below, inside the tree. This must be where the squirrels are hiding their nuts for the cold winter months.
2202: At the Base of a Large Tree
A squirrel scampers around here, looking for nuts from the trees.
You stand at the base of a large tree. You can definitely climb it. Looking at it, you see plenty of easy hand holds and places to put your feet. Glancing down, you see a small hole going down.
2205: This is one end of this homes' main hall. Against the western wall is a closet and looking down the hall toward the north you can see many guest rooms and rooms belonging to the owner's children.
2206: A smiling hobbit child is playing around here.
You continue along the main hall. To the south is a simple hobbit study, to the north lies the pantry and the cellar. There are tapestries on the walls here.
2207:
A busy hobbit female is here worrying about the home labours.
A colourful butterfly is fluttering around here.
This is the main hall. To the north, you see the kitchen and the drawing room. To the south lies the dining room and the parlour.
2208: You are standing in the front hall of a hobbit hole. There are many pegs along the wall to hang cloaks and hoods to dry. There is a rug on the floor to dry boots or feet.
2209:
There is some pipe-weed here.
A smiling hobbit child is playing around here.
You are walking between rows and rows of pipeweed. They are neatly laid out and appear to be well cared for. The field is surrounded by what looks like a sturdy fence.
2210: You are walking between rows and rows of pipeweed. They are neatly laid out and appear to be well cared for. The field is surrounded by what looks like a sturdy fence.
2211: Standing on the edge of the pipeweed fields you see that it stretches west as far as you can see. These hobbits are definitely serious about their pipeweed.

A small mushroom grows nearby.
A small mushroom grows nearby.
A small mushroom grows nearby.
A small mushroom grows nearby.
A small mushroom grows nearby.
A hobbit farmer is here, thinking about seeds and vegetables.
A colourful butterfly is fluttering around here.

You are in a small garden. There are rows and rows of various types of vegetables. A fairly good sized portion of the garden is dedicated to mushrooms. It looks like these hobbits are able to grow enough here to keep their families well fed.
2213: A clear spring babbles as cool water trickles out of the ground.
Here a small spring bubbles up from below and flows off to the east. Right here is it shallow enough to wade in during hot days. It looks cool and refreshing, inviting you to take a drink.
2214: A placid pond is here, inviting you to take a refreshing drink.
You see a small pond. To the west you hear the sound of a small spring bubbling up from the ground. To the east lies a grassy plain, and south of you is a bend in the Old East Road.
2215: You are standing in a field of chest-deep swaying grass. Looking about, you notice the ground sloping slightly downward and the grass thinning a bit to the west. To the south, you can see the East Road.
2216: You are standing in a field of chest-deep swaying grass. To the south, you see the Old East Road winding lazily through this sea of grass.
2217:
A Shirriff stands here, keeping a watchful eye on things.
The Mayor is sitting in his huge chair, snoring loudly.
A secretary is sitting at the desk.

White walls surround this large room. Several portraits of well-fed hobbits, possibly past Shire Mayors, hang on the walls. A desk stands near the entrance. It is strewn with yellowing papers and scrolls. Two large windows are set in the western wall of this building, while a large cupboard covers the southern end of the room.
2219: This is a small and dingy room. A thick layer of dust has settled on the floor. Several shelves are attached to the south wall, holding thousands of old papers and ledgers. This room looks empty and is probably not used too often.
2220: This faint trail turns towards the south-east. The lands surrounding the trail seem to be desolate and dry. To the east, the path is even more faint and dusty. The White Downs obstruct any attempt at travelling to the west and south.
2221: The path here is very faint. It leads both to the west, below the towering White Downs, and the south among desolate fields. There is a hedge lining the northern and eastern sides of the trail. The area to the north looks to be covered in extremely dense vegetation. A hole can be spotted in the eastern hedge, providing a view of an old cottage.
2222: The faint path is overgrown by thorny bushes here, preventing any travel onwards to the south and east. It does not look like anyone has used this trail for a very long time. The White Downs can be seen some distance to the west.
2223: The dirt path continues its course towards the south-east. It does not seem to be used much. The back of an old, wooden building stands to the north. The surrounding area is very dry and barren, save a few bushes growing around the path, covering it at some places. The silhouette of a tall tree can be seen beyond the wastelands to the east.
2224: An old well stands outside an old, ruined cottage. However, it is filled with mud instead of water. The door of the building to the south seems solid enough, but the roof could collapse at any moment. A large, thorny hedge grows to the west. There is a hole in the hedge, revealing a path on the other side. To the north lies a field of hay, while a ploughed field lies just to the east of here.
2225: The scent of hay fills the air, emanating from a few heaps of hay that lie on the ground and a few haystacks standing here and there. Several dense bushes grow behind a hedge to the west, preventing any movement in that direction. To the south of the field the remains of a rather decayed old building stand. Fields of grasses and other plants are located to the north and east of here.
2226: Lush, green grasses sway lazily in the wind here. The vegetation grows denser to the west, preventing travel in that direction. A hobbit burrow can be seen to the north-west, marking the edge of the Michel Delving village. To the north lies the large gravel road called by many The East Road. Irregular patches of small fields lie to the south and east. They seem to be well cared for.
2227: The dank smell of decay hangs heavily in the air here. Several large holes in the roof have clearly been allowing in the rain for some considerable time. The tattered remains of some furniture lie scattered around the cottage. This ruined cottage has clearly been abandoned for quite some time.
2228: The barren ground here consists of dry dirt. There are a few thistles growing here and there, but otherwise this is a wasteland. Beyond the continuing wastelands to the east, a tall tree can be spotted. The fields to the north have been ploughed recently, but nothing grows there yet. A faint, dusty path lies to the west.
2229: Deep furrows have been ploughed into this field recently. It does not look like anything has been sowed here yet, and the ground is quite muddy. To the north and east, large grain-fields can be seen. The lands in the south however, are barren and waste. Just to the west of this field stands and old, ruined cottage.
2230: A worm is here slithering around.

Rich and fertile soil covers the ground of this field. Stout stems of grain grow upon it, supporting large heads of wheat. These fields continue for miles to the east, while the ploughed fields to the south do not seem to be sowed yet. In the north, patches of some strange plant covers the ground. A ruined cottage can be seen to the south-west, standing next to a field of hay.
