2360: You walk in a dense forest, up and around a seemingly infinite range of hills. There are signs of life all around you. You relax somewhat, and the journey is pleasant. However, you realise you could get lost, if not careful.
2361: You walk in a dense forest, up and around a seemingly infinite range of hills. There are signs of life all around you. You relax somewhat, and the journey is pleasant. However, you realise you could get lost, if not careful.
2362: You walk in a dense forest, up and around a seemingly infinite range of hills. There are signs of life all around you. You relax somewhat, and the journey is pleasant. However, you realise you could get lost, if not careful.
2363: A low shrub with bright green, oblong leaves is growing here.

You are walking along a trail, winding its way around some forest-covered hills. Although not very wide, it seem to be frequently used. There are signs of life everywhere. The trail goes east and west.
2364: A brown bear is sleeping here.
This hill is covered with trees, as are all of the hills in this area. What makes this hill stand out is the bare rock face along its side, in which there seems to be a cave.
2365: You walk in a dense forest, up and around a seemingly infinite range of hills. There are signs of life all around you. You relax somewhat, and the journey is pleasant. However, you realise you could get lost, if not careful.
2366: You walk in a dense forest, up and around a seemingly infinite range of hills. There are signs of life all around you. You relax somewhat, and the journey is pleasant. However, you realise you could get lost, if not careful.
2367: You are walking along a trail, winding its way around some forest-covered hills. Although not very wide, it seem to be frequently used. There are signs of life everywhere. The trail goes east and north.
2368: You walk in a dense forest, up and around a seemingly infinite range of hills. There are signs of life all around you. You relax somewhat, and the journey is pleasant. However, you realise you could get lost, if not careful.
2369: A sparrow is flapping around on the ground.

You walk in a dense forest, up and around a seemingly infinite range of hills. There are signs of life all around you. You relax somewhat, and the journey is pleasant. However, you realise you could get lost, if not careful.
2371:
A Hobbit shopkeeper stands here, eager to sell you his wares.
A domesticated pony, beast of burden to many, stands here.

The shelves of this small store are packed with various items, most of which no respectable hobbit would ever need. However, you are in Tookland. Some Tooks even leave the Shire! A small sign rests on the counter.
2372:
A heavy desk, made of solid oak, stands here.
A Shirriff stands here, keeping a watchful eye on things.
A Shirriff stands here, keeping a watchful eye on things.

This modest building houses the Shirriffs of Waymeet. The entrance is in proper order, and so is a nearby desk. However, next to the desk rests a wooden table with what appears to be an unfinished meal and a several personal belongings. At the far end of the room, an empty jail cell sits in silent meditation.
2373: A few sparse trees are scattered across these plains. Forest covers many small hills, south of you. You may reach the road by walking south or east.
2374: You are on a small north-south path heading from the border road to some fields to the south. There are many cart tracks running back and forth along this path, making it seem well used. Green grass and some small trees make up the border of the road here.
2375: The road bends to the north, or can be followed east towards Waymeet. The fields here are overgrown with weeds, and the road looks like it doesn't get travelled very often.
2376: A Bounder is here, patrolling the Shire and watching for evil.

The purpose of this road seems forgotten, as it ends suddenly. The road is in obvious disrepair, and the fields that lie around it look as if they've been more cared for than the road itself. To the south of you the road bends east, continuing on its journey towards Waymeet.
2377:
There are two potatoes here.
There are two turnips here.
There are two cabbages here.
There are two piles of wheat cereals here.

All around you are fields of corn, wheat, vegetables, and various other things that the hobbits grow. Every now and then you can see a busy hobbit running from field to field doing one of many tasks that are needed to keep these fields in their current condition. The Border Road passes through the fields to the south. To the east you can see a small pond.
2378: A tilled field lies before you, obviously not yet planted. The plough still lies in the corner of the field and everything is prepared for planting. It simply looks as if the farmer has not had the time to plant this area of his fields. There is a minor irrigation system laid out around the edges of the field. To the east you can see a large barn; thick bushes block passage to the north.
2379: Right in the middle of all this farmland, this little pond looks completely out of place. However, the hobbit who farms this land seems to have made the best of it. A rather complex irrigation system has been erected in the area, feeding most of the crops in this field and even some of the neighbouring fields. A small creek runs south from here. To the north you can see a large barn.
2380: Around you are acres of pastures in lightly rolling hills. This area seems to be well used, as patches of grass seem to have disappeared, leaving only mud and dirt where they used to be. However, there is still much grass left for the livestock to feed upon. To the north you can see the centre of the farm.
2381: Lush green grass grows here, this pasture seems not to have been used at any time in the near past. It looks as though the owners of the farm have this pasture off on rotation, although, with one look at the field to the west, it might be time they moved the cows back over to here. A fence separates this field from the field to the east. A small gate leads north to the farm.
2382: The fields around you must hold enough vegetables to supply the Arthedain army! Acres and acres of land around you, all covered in various vegetables. You can see a couple of hobbits tending to the crops in the far corner of the field. To the east, you can see a vegetable garden.
2383: Unharvested wheat is all the eye can see for many, many acres. It looks as though the wheat is ready for harvesting, yet no one has had the time or resources to finish the task. Tilled fields lie to the north and to the east. The Old East Road is to the south of you, running to Waymeet in the west.
2384: Coming from Waymeet, the road bends to the west. Around, you see the common fields of all the Shire. It appears that this road is not used very often.
2385: The fields around the road are cultivated, but the road itself seems forgotten. It looks as if it wasn't used very often and you wonder where it leads. The road continues west, or you can follow it back eastwards towards Waymeet.
2386: A small campfire burns here, its low flames giving off only a little light.

The fields here are covered in rows upon rows of lettuce. For miles, all that you can see are rows of perfect green heads of lettuce. The hobbit who farms these lands must really like his lettuce. To the south you can see the East Road as it continues on its way. Another road cuts through the fields to the north.
2387: A bulb of garlic with green stems is here.

The fields around you are completely covered with carrots, lettuce, tomato plants, radishes and various other vegetables. And in the middle of it all you can see a small creek running west-north towards a small pond just to the north. The hobbit who owns these lands must be truly proud of his fields. At some distance to the south you can see the Border Road cutting through the farmland.
2388: You are just north of the Border Road which leads from Waymeet to nowhere. Rye, barley and hops grow on the fields around the road. To the west you can see a small creek making its way through some more fields.
2389:
A dented pail has been carelessly left here.
A brown cow is here, contemplating a higher reality whilst chewing slowly.
A brown cow is here, contemplating a higher reality whilst chewing slowly.
A brown cow is here, contemplating a higher reality whilst chewing slowly.

You are in a large barn. To the east, you can see the centre of a large dairy farm, and all around you are cow stalls and troughs. The rafters hold much hay for the cows, and there are bottles, casks, and barrels of milk stored neatly against one wall. The barn itself is enormous, being approximately twenty-five yards wide, fifty yards long, and ten yards high.
2390: A small white fountain is here.

Around you is the workings of a decent sized dairy farm. You are not too far from the Shire's largest village, Hobbiton, and you can imagine that this dairy farm is the major source for milk and cheese in the area. The owners of this dairy farm must be quite prosperous, as the area seems clean and there is a small square where workers can stop and rest. In the middle of the square there is a small water fountain. To the south, you can see a rather large pasture. There is also a barn to the west, and the entrance to the farm is to the east. To the north behind a hedge you can see a path surrounded by trees.
2391: You are at the entrance to a small dairy farm just outside of Hobbiton. There are many cart and animal tracks here, and the ground is hard packed. You can smell manure all around you as it assaults your nostrils. To the south, there is a small pasture. To the east is a small path leading to the fields outside of Hobbiton.
2392: On the sides of the path, trees have been replaced by thick vegetation. The loud humming of insects gives evidence of a nearby bog. One may follow the path back east towards Hobbiton or continue along west.
2393: A hobbit is here walking around.
The path here is fairly moist due to its proximity to water to the north. It continues to the west while also leading east towards the village of Hobbiton.
2394: This path runs parallel to the water which can be faintly heard beyond a thick line of trees. The way leads west to Little Delving and east to Hobbiton, one of the largest towns in all the Shire.
2395: A Bounder is here, patrolling the Shire and watching for evil.

All around you are the sounds of many winged insects and mosquitoes. This trail is not used too often, making it difficult to advance through the sedges. You can go either north or south, but it is impossible to know what lies in either direction.
2396:
A swarm of mosquitoes is here, humming around you.
A swarm of mosquitoes is here, humming around you.

The ground is damp and boggy. Here and there you come upon pools and wide stretches of reeds and rushes filled with the warbling of little hidden birds. You must make your way carefully to avoid falling in and getting covered by the mud. The bog continues east while to the south a trail is discernible through a thick stand of sedges. One can see water to the north.
2397:
A frog is standing here.
A frog is standing here.
A swarm of mosquitoes is here, humming around you.

The ground is damp and boggy. Here and there you come upon pools and wide stretches of reeds and rushes filled with the warbling of little hidden birds. You must make your way carefully to avoid falling in and getting covered by the mud. The bog continues west while there is water to the north.
2398: The river here is murky. The water has a brownish tinge to it due to the effects of the nearby bog. Swampy plants and flowers float on the surface of the water. Except for the humming of the mosquitoes that live in the stagnant water, it is silent.
2399: The river here is murky. The water has a brownish tinge to it due to the effects of the nearby bog. Swampy plants and flowers float on the surface of the water. Except for the humming of the mosquitoes that live in the stagnant water, it is silent.
2400: The river here makes a soft bend to the south, leading to the Brandywine River to the east. The large trees are being slowly replaced by thick vegetation, and the water is slowly becoming more and more stagnant. Mosquitoes seem to be everywhere.
2401: The river here makes a soft bend to the north and east. Around the banks of the river trees are becoming sparse and more insects than normal are buzzing around.
2402: There is a bank to the south, where you can leave this gentle river. The flowing becomes dimmer as you get closer to the source, somewhere to the west. To the south-east, you see a large cabin hidden in the trees.
2403: The water flows gently here, cutting through the quiet plains of the Shire. With the soft rippling of the water and the calm wind in your face, you feel as if you could sail all the way down the Water to the Brandywine and beyond to the far sea.
2404: The river turns gently here flowing southeasterly, carrying you in its travel through the lands of the Shire. To the south, you think you see a large cabin half-hidden in the trees.
2405: The water flows gently here, cutting across the quiet plains of the Shire. With the wind at your back, you feel as if you could follow this river all the way to the Brandywine and then out to the great seas of the west.
2406: The water becomes more and more stagnant as you approach its source. To the north and south you can see the plains and fields of the Shire. Off to the north-east you see a large hill with a road near it.
2407: The river turns gently from the north back towards the east, carrying you in its travel through the lands of the Shire. To the south, you think you see a large cabin half-hidden in the trees.
2408: On the sides of the path, the fresh scent of the large trees makes your walk pleasant. To the north there is a big wooden cabin half-hidden in the trees. There must be water somewhere to the north as murmurs of a river can be heard. The path leads towards Little Delving to the west while leading to Hobbiton eastwards.
2409: This path runs parallel to the Water which turns west-south here. If you follow the road west, you will find Little Delving. At some distance to the east lies Hobbiton, the largest village in all the Shire.
2410: You have now entered a large wooden cabin. It is well equipped with camping supplies. Judging by the contents of the room, the inhabitant here must really have a passion for nature. A door leads eastward into another room.
2411: A ranger stands quietly here, willing to teach his knowledge of woodcraft.

This room is where Valindur the Ranger teaches woodcraft to pupils willing to learn. Many strange herbs are stored in pots and several bookshelves hold tomes on the various arts of riding, healing, and hunting.
2412:
An erect shrub with green pinnate leaves is growing here.
Inside the shrub, there are two piles of crimson raspberries.
A large thorny branched shrub is growing here.
On the shrub, there are two piles of blackberries.
A smiling hobbit child is playing around here.

Around you grows many small bushes. Gooseberries, currants and raspberries grow here in abundance. These fields seem to be treated much differently than the other fields in the area, as fruits do not need as much attention as vegetable fields or corn fields do. The fields suddenly end to the north as they come to a small path. To the west you can see a pasture behind a fence.
2413:
A large potato is growing here.
A carrot is lying here.
A large potato is growing here.
A smiling hobbit child is playing around here.

Many types of vegetables are growing here, although it looks like the main vegetable is potatoes, as you can see a rather large planting of them in the south-west corner of the fields. To the east, there is a small pasture, every other direction yields more fields.
2414: Before you are a few acres of fields. Many different types of plants and vegetation grow here in patches of different colours. The fields continue to the north and to the west; to the south and to the east you can see the Old East Road.
2415: Many acres of pasture lie before you. Lush green grass grows here, and there are many cows and horses around. Small gates and fences section the pasture into smaller areas which are used to hold the individual types of livestock. To the west you can see a large vegetable garden.
2416: A golden, firm onion is here.

Many different types of flowers grow here. Mainly golden poppies and mountain laurels, but there are a fair amount of roses and purple lilacs to one side as well. Some smaller plantings of various herbs and some onions also make up much of this area.
2417: This path follows the same general path as the water to the north. On the sides of the path are rows of trees which provide the traveller with ample shade. To the east lies the village of Hobbiton while to the west lies Little Delving.
2419:
A hobbit is here walking around.
A sparrow is flapping around on the ground.

This path follows along The Water westwards. A fairly busy village can be heard to the north-east, which could possibly have a place to rest after your long adventures. The path runs west towards the town of Little Delving.
2420: This path follows the same general path as the water to the north. On the sides of the path are rows of trees which provide the traveller with ample shade. To the east lies the village of Hobbiton while to the west lies Little Delving.
2422: A stocky Bounder is here safeguarding the Shire.

Lush fields stand between the East Road, and the village of Hobbiton. Well tended, and separated from the surrounding countryside by lush, and neatly trimmed hedgerows, these fields obviously see frequent use, and a narrow trail cuts north to south, where the people of the Shire use it as a short- cut from the main road to the numerous smials, which you can see a small distance to the north.
2423: A young man in ranger's attire is here, travelling the roads.

This is the village of Hobbiton, one of the most important places in the Shire. Many hobbits have their home here or in the surroundings, and the town has good stores where the people can find what they need. To the east is a well equipped General Store, and to the north you see the centre of the village.
2424: A Hobbit shopkeeper stands here, eager to sell you his wares.
In this large well equipped store, one can find almost anything. On the numerous shelves are every imaginable kind of supplies necessary for a long journey.
2425: A hobbit shopkeeper stands here, eager to sell you his wares.

As you enter, you are taken aback by the quality of the clothes here. The owner, Heldor, is not here currently. He must be out scouring the surrounding lands for the clothes he sells. A sign hangs above the entrance.
2426: The street progresses east and west through the heart of the village. To the south stands Heldor's Clothes Emporium, and to the north a private dwelling.
2427:
A Shirriff stands here, keeping a watchful eye on things.
A Shirriff stands here, keeping a watchful eye on things.

You are at the eastern border of Hobbiton. To the west you can hear the sounds of merchants selling their wares and of children playing in the streets. A cosy little hobbit hole lies to the north. The village ends here, and the Bywater Road begins in the east.
2428: To the west is the centre of the town. This street crosses east-west through the village. To the north resides the ever popular Tembur's Quality Pet Store, and more shops can be seen to the east. The centre of the town lies west.
2429:
A Hobbit shopkeeper stands here, eager to sell you his wares.
A hobbit is here walking around.

This is a modest shop of animals. Some of them are cute, just to be used as companions, and others are tough beasts of work. Their sounds fill the room. As you look in the cages, you see some little animals that would do real well as pets. Will you take one with you?
2430: Small round windows set into the front of the room offer a view of the Small Street to the south, and are framed by neat curtains of a jolly blue fabric, with bright yellow flowers. Like most hobbit holes, this is a neatly kept place, cleanly swept and with new paint on all the woodwork.
2431: A busy hobbit female is here worrying about the home labours.

You are now inside a comfortable hobbit hole. Many small windows provide a good view of the beautiful countryside while keeping the place well ventilated. A stone fireplace against a wall is ready to provide warmth in the winter when needed. A large pantry is visible, and, in classic hobbit tradition, very well stocked.
2432:
A large bulletin board, entitled "Free Peoples' Chronicles", is mounted here.
A large fountain, made from grey stone, pours water from its centre.
A Shirriff stands here, keeping a watchful eye on things.
A Shirriff stands here, keeping a watchful eye on things.
A Shirriff stands here, keeping a watchful eye on things.
A young man in ranger's attire is here, travelling the roads.

Built in the middle of the largest village in the Shire, this square is often used as a gathering place for reunions and parties. The square is very clean and appears to be well kept by the fine inhabitants of this village.
2433: This rather wide path leaves the village of Hobbiton towards the lands north. A bridge lies ahead, allowing you safe passage over the water. You can see a large hill farther up the road. To the west is a small dock used to launch boats onto the water.
2434: A bridge made of solid wood allows travellers to pass over the water without fear of getting wet. To the north, a rather large hill can be seen, while the village of Hobbiton can be spotted to the south.
2435: The road leading to the hill is wide and its sides are covered by flowers and soft grass. High and beautiful trees give the air purity and a sensation of calm, making the walk easier as the road becomes steep. To the east you can see a mill, working with the waters of the river.
2437: Here the road heading north from the village of Hobbiton begins to climb the tall green hill which overlooks all the surrounding countryside. A humble lane leads off to the west along The Hill's lower flanks. To the east is a large building, the door of which is partially obstructed by a pile of metal scraps.
2438: A huge glowing fire stands in the middle of the place, overheating the whole building. A large heap of coal is lying against the northern wall and a huge bellows is filling the eastern part of the forge. Against the southern wall several unfinished tools are standing: a few picks, some shovels and other common gardening tools.
2439: A large rabbit looks peacefully at you, ready to dart away.
This narrow lane travels along The Hill to the west. The slope of the hill above it to the north is terraced; lush garden plots and vineyards can be seen.
2440: This small and little-used lane (judging from the relative absence of ruts) extends east and west along the southern flank of The Hill. A few modest residential holes have been delved in the bank to the north of the road, each with its own front garden.
2441: This is the western end of Bagshot Row, a modest residential lane. Some hobbit-homes, each with its own garden before the round door, line the northern, hilly sides of the road. This last garden is an especially handsome, well-kept one.
2442:
Herb: thyme
Herb: rosemary
Herb: tarragon
Herb: marjoram

A small evergreen plant grows here, its woody stems reaching two feet.
A thin, hairy plant, with small, oval leaves, grows here.
A woody evergreen plant grows here, with many stems reaching upward.
A waist-high evergreen shrub grows here, with thick, reaching branches.
On the shrub, there are two piles of grey-green leaves.

You are now in the garden of Bagshot Row, home of the Gamgee family. The well maintained flowers and plants are amazing, and it is apparent that they are the work of an artist. Sam "The Uncle" Gamgee is famous for his secrets in the maintenance of a good garden, and looking around, it is easy to see why. A little path of stones leads west towards a door.
2443: Uncle Gamgee is here, thinking about the season.

This is the house of the family Gamgee. It is a nice place, though a little modest. There are tools for gardening kept in one corner. This is not surprising since the family has a long history as gardeners. In fact, many say that they are the best in the whole Shire.
2444: A small oaken table has been set here.

This hole is a typical low-class hobbit house. It is a poor hole, also very well maintained and arranged. The first sight announces clearly one of the major point of the hobbit life: food. Everything here seems to be designed to bring the most delight for meals: large table, comfortable chairs, large kitchen, huge cupboards, probably filled with food-stuff.
2445:
A golden, firm onion is here.
A bulb of garlic with green stems is here.
A hobbit is here walking around.

This garden is obviously maintained by a good gardener: it looks rather healthy and some appetizing scents are carried on the soft wind. The rows of vegetables are straight: one can recognise celery, garlic, onions, tomatoes, potatoes, leeks and even cauliflower.
2446: This is the well tended garden of Bag End. The plants and flowers have been cared for by an expert, judging by their quality and condition. A huge old tree stands in the middle of the garden.
2447: You are in the entrance garden of Bag End, reputed to be one of the finest smials in all the Shire. The plants are very well cared for, and the flowers here seem especially fragrant. To the north you see a round green door set in the side of the hill.
2448: You are in a rather large smial, probably one of the largest in the Shire. On the walls you can see beautiful paintings while many strange knick-knacks rest on the shelves and tabletops. Bag End used to be owned by Bilbo Baggins, but he has been gone from the area for a long time. The Sackvilles have taken residence here.
2449: This is the well tended garden of Bag End. The plants and flowers here have been taken care of by an expert, judging from the quality and condition of the foliage here.
2450: The road winds up The Hill and eastward around its green flank toward the village of Overhill. In the lush sides of The Hill, to the north, can be seen some windows and a round green door; the path leading to that door is barred by an iron gate.
2451: This wide path bends around the Hill and leads towards the small village of Overhill. There is an animal pen directly east and the hill, itself, stands to the west.
2452: This wide path wraps around the hill towards the small village of Overhill. To the east are large spans of green fields, and to the west is the hill itself. This area doesn't seem to be as densely populated as the rest of the Shire.
2453: In Front of a Purple Door

This is a scene of disorder, uncharacteristic of the Shire. In front of a dwelling dug into the hillside to the east, flowers have been tramped into the mud, and the grass is marked up by many footprints. A door to the east has been nailed firmly shut, its lock stopped up with lead, and a sign has been hung on it, written in black ink.
2455: This was formerly a goat pen, but some of the boards and rails which comprised it have been hastily taken down to be used for another purpose. Some of the windows have been broken out. The floor is covered with scattered hay.
2456: You have finally reached the village. To the west a few smials are clustered together, forming the nucleus of the village. This village seems even more peaceful than the others in the Shire.
2457: You are standing in the middle of a small group of houses that form this tiny little village. This place is very quiet, except for the wind rustling through the trees. The hobbit holes here do not seem to be as luxurious as those in Hobbiton. A path winds up the Hill to the south.
2458: A lean and well-travelled hobbit stands here, while resting his legs.
You are standing in the centre of a small group of smials that form this tiny village. The houses here are not quite as nice as those located in the rest of the Shire.
2459: A busy hobbit female is here worrying about the home labours.

This smial is almost comparable to a simple hole in the ground. The furniture is in disrepair, and the place seems fairly devoid of any signs of wealth. Even so, the hobbits who live here take pride in themselves and keep the place fairly clean.
2461: A Bounder is here, patrolling the Shire and watching for evil.

This is a large and comfortable smial, the dwelling of a well-off hobbit, or so it seems. Comfortable furniture rests on soft carpeting; polished molding lines the round doorways which lead off to the other sections of the home.
2462: You are in a charming place away from the hustle and bustle of the village. Small trees grow on the sides of the square, inviting you to take rest beneath their boughs. A large and beautiful smial lies to the north and to the south is the Post Office of Hobbiton. A small street leads eastward to the centre of the village, while to the west it turns into a placid lane heading through the fields towards Needlehole and Little Delving.
2463: This street goes east and west through Hobbiton. Here you can see small houses on each side of the road. It does not appear to be a very busy area. To the west the street ends at a charming square while to the east is the centre of the village.
2464: A mailbox stands here stuffed full of messages.

In this building can be found the local post office of the Shire. Many hobbit employees run around busily, organizing letters in order to get them to their destiny. You can check the desk to see if anything has arrived for you.
2465: The flowing of the water becomes more and more stagnant as you approach its source. Just to the east the river flows under a small bridge. To the south is a small wooden dock where you can leave the water.
2466: The Water flows quietly under the wooden planks of the bridge. To your sides, you can see the banks of the river covered by mud and reeds. You cannot leave the river here.
2467: The water becomes more and more stagnant as you approach its source. To the north and south you can see the plains and fields of the Shire. Off to the north-east you see a large hill with a road near it.
2468: The river floods toward the east. Far in the west there is some houses. It seems that the river is going forever straight east. The north bank is unreachable because of some sharp cliffs and on the south bank a small mill stands, powered by the waters of the river.
2469: This river flows calmly from its source somewhere in the west towards the east where it should mix its waters with those of the river Baranduin. A small bend can be seen in the east, where the river flows along a small town. To the north, there are some cultivated fields, also there are some sharp cliffs which prevent to entry to those northern lands. On the south bank is a small road that crosses the countryside.
2470:
A black catfish is here, lurking in the mud.
A fat carp swims here.
A frog is standing here.

This is a river bend. Southwards there is a small lake. On its south bank some buildings stand, indicating the place of a village. Otherwise the land, cultivated, is wholly flat. Its monotony is broken only by small waves of the ground, and some lonely trees.
2471: This small lake, north of the village of Bywater, is really quiet: only a few billows prevent the watery surface to be a perfect mirror. To the north there is the Water entering the small lake, and to east it flows away.
2472: A singing, happy drunk is staggering about here.

Just between the Bywater Road and the Water stands this busy mill yard. The loud sounds of the mill machinery can be heard from the eastern building, the property of Ted Sandyman the miller, a man not known to be fond of strangers prowling about his land.
2473:
A sack of flour has been placed here.
A sack of flour has been placed here.
Ted Sandyman is angry at seeing you on his property.

The sounds of the mill overpower all other noises. To the north there is the machinery working with the waters of the river, milling grain into meal for consumption by the hobbits who live in the Shire. Ted Sandyman, the owner of the place, must be nearby as he doesn't like to leave his building unsupervised.
2474:
A hobbit is here walking around.
A hobbit is here walking around.

The road makes a bend here: it comes from Hobbiton, a few miles away in the west, and goes to Bywater which lies on the southern bank of the small pool that lies just here. Before that pool there is a small bank with hundreds of small stones scattered about it. A small coppice of chestnut trees stands between the road and the northern river.
2475:
A tall, stately, dome-topped tree grows here.
On the plant, there is a green spiny capsule.

This road is made of earth as hard as stone. It is one of the most used way in the whole Shire as it binds the small town of Hobbiton, just west of here, and the big village of Bywater, a few miles in the south-east. The road goes east-west, parallel to the Water that flows just north of here, after a small mill. South of the road, there is some fields, divided by hedgerows, and not far the dark line of the East Road can be seen.
2476: This field, uncultivated, is a grazing field. Grass is the best food for the cows of Bywater's farmers. Just south of here a big road is running eastwards- westwards and there are two villages in the neighbourhood: Bywater in the east and Hobbiton far in the northwest. A large wooden building prevents walking eastwards.
2477: This is a quite small village. The streets are bordered by lots of chestnut trees. The houses are either little constructions on the ground with round doors and windows, or dug-in houses, which seem to be very comfortable excavations. The only building which seems to be interesting is called the Green Dragon Inn.
2478:
An old piece of paper lies on the ground.
A singing, happy drunk is staggering about here.

This is a quite small village. The streets are bordered by lots of chestnut trees. The houses are either little constructions on the ground with round doors and windows, or dug-in houses, which seem to be very comfortable excavations. To the south you see a street leading to a main road. To the north you see a large pool, and to the west a road leaves town and winds through the fields toward a distant hill.
2479: By an Inn on the Bywater Road

The Bywater Road bypasses the pool of the Water that lies, quiet, north of the famous village of Bywater. The first houses of it are less than one mile east of here. A lonely inn, in an old wooden house, stands on the west of the road; its stables are a large wooden building, south of the road. Some ponies' neighings can be heard.
2480:
A large bulletin board, entitled "Board of the Free Peoples", is mounted here.
A large stone fireplace with a roaring fire warms the room.
Jonty, the waiter, is attending to his duties.
A Bounder is here, patrolling the Shire and watching for evil.

This is one of the finest inns of the Shire, famous for its beer and food. It is usually a fairly busy place, with many hobbits relaxing here after a hard day's work. Many a fine story is spun here by the local storytellers. A wooden door leads south to the guest rooms, where an adventurer can rest his or her weary bones, for a small fee of course. A small sign is nailed upon the bar.
2481:
A large bulletin board, entitled "News of Arda", is mounted here.
A well-fed hobbit has set up an inn here, renting out rooms.
A Bounder is here, patrolling the Shire and watching for evil.

This room is very quiet: even the merry sounds of the northern inn do not make their way here. A big door stands open to the west and through it one can see the many other doors leading to the guest rooms of the reception.
2482:
A large stone fireplace with a roaring fire warms the room.
A huge clock is standing here.
A drunk hobbit is sprawled on the the ground before you.
A small hobbit bartender is here, bragging about the beer.
A trim Bounder is here, patrolling the Shire and watching for evil.

This large room is filled with lots of tables. The fire sparkles softly in the left corner. The old bar stands on the right side. Hobbits are chatting here, and all of them have some empty cups of beer laying on their table. A small sign stands upright on the bar.
2483: This small brisky river floods eastwards. The waters are clear and one can see the bottom of the river even if the current is strong. The dark lane of a road follows the river in the south, and the northern dam is filled by many sharp cliffs, blocking the passage.
2484:
A trout swims here.
A fat carp swims here.

This river is flooding eastwards. Parallel to it there is a dark line to the south, probably a path or a road. As much the south coast of the river is calm and covered of grass, the north coast is filled with many sharp cliffs, preventing every movements in that direction.
2485: This small river is flooding eastwards. The inhabitants of this country call it 'The Water'. South of here one can see a road and west is a small lake, but there are so many sharp cliffs along the north bank of this river that one cannot see any further.
2486:
There is a huge, pyramidal beehive here.
A bee flies around here, collecting nectar from the flowers.
A bee flies around here, collecting nectar from the flowers.

This field is on the south bank of a briskly flowing river. The ground is very muddy. Not far in the west there is a small village and just south of here there is the lane of a road. Far in the south, after lots of fields, some green hills are standing, breaking the monotony of the plain.
2487: Between the northly river and the southly road, the ground is very muddy. Just east of here there is a small construction and further some houses stand on the plain. The south part of it is covered by lots of rectangular fields.
2488: The river, which runs northly of here, should often become greater and flood a part of the plain. Here the ground is very muddy, indicating that great amount of water run here not so long ago. Southly there is a big road.
2489: This field is covered by a thick dark green grass. Nevertheless the ground is very spongious due to the amount of water the near river let periodically run here when some flooding occurs. A dark earth road lies just south of here, and a small bridge can be seen over the river northeast of here.
2490: This river floods cold from the west toward the east. There a small bridge stands over it. Not far in the south there is the dark line of a parallel road leading to the bridge. The north coast of the river is covered by sharp cliffs.
2491: This part of the dam of the Water is not cultivated. The ground is sandy and therefore any walk is harder here. Lots of bushes grow around this place, making the road difficult to reach. A big tree, an oak, can be seen west from here and the river floating just south of here makes a lot of noise.
2492: This place is not cultivated. There is only a huge tree growing here. It is so huge that its stems are covering the ground all around. Its canopy is so high and so dense, that daylight is filtered and the main colour one can see is dark green. The flat, smooth bark that covers this tree is too slippery for climbing.
2493: A sparrow is flapping around on the ground.

This northwest-southeast road goes along a river. It seems to disappear in the north in an endless somewhat hilly green plain. Not so far in the southeast there is a small bridge over a river. The north bank of the river is filled by sharp rocks.
2494: This field, lying among the other fields wholly covering this wide plain, is cultivated. Lots of furrows are covering it from the east to the west. At each corner stands a tree or a big stone, delineating the property of each hobbit farmer.
2495: A colossal tree, its trunk as wide as a small cottage, stands here.
This place, just westward of an important path, is the end of one of the fields of the Shire. The furrows stop suddenly and a big lonely tree marks the end of the field.
2496: This large dirty path connects Dwaling to the East Road. The path runs from the north-west to the south-east. This area of the Shire is very peaceful. By listening carefully one can hear a nearby river and some birds singing in the distance.
2497: The path here makes a gentle turn from the south-east to the north-east, heading towards the hills of Scary which rise in the distance and toward the village of Dwaling beyond. The countryside around is very serene and calm.
2498: This well-trod path slopes gently upwards as it heads north-east towards the hills of Scary. The surrounding countryside lies calmly around you, trees gently rustling in the soft breeze.
2499: This field is cultivated. The furrows leads north-south and some of the plants begin to grow : you see here and there some green twigs growing. South of here there are some trees and a medium-sized roads runs eastward of here.
2500: A sparrow is flapping around on the ground.

This dirty road, not much larger than a path, is connecting the hobbit village of Dwaling to the East Road. It mainly goes from the northwest to the southeast through a very peaceful land, only disturbed by some birds songs and a very faint noise of water.
2501:
A sparrow is flapping around on the ground.
A sparrow is flapping around on the ground.

This road is connecting Dwaling to the East Road. It is somewhat dirty and hundreds of tracks can be seen on it. It goes from the northwest to the southeast. The land around is very peaceful, silent except some birds and a very distant noise of water flooding.
2502: A sparrow is flapping around on the ground.

This is a large path that climbs gently into the hills of Scary which leads towards the village of Dwaling that lies unseen in the distance. All around roams the wildlife of the countryside, free of worry or care, amidst the renowned foliage of the Shire.
2503: A sparrow is flapping around on the ground.

This large path leads northwards and eastwards from the East Road towards the hills of Scary and the fishing village of Dwaling that lies beyond. The surrounding countryside is quiet and calm and the foliage is quite splendid, supporting the reputation of the Shire gardeners.
2504: A trim Bounder is here, patrolling the Shire and watching for evil.
The road narrows a bit here as it curves its way northwards into the hills of Scary. Less travelled than the path to Dwaling proper, the road still remains hard underfoot and is easy to travel on.
2505: To the north the road enters a crossroad at the foot of the hills of Scary. The countryside is as serene as ever, however, a more silent stillness seems to come from the hills to the east. Yet this is the peaceful Shire, and the grass around moves slowly under the light wind.
2506: Here a large path from the south, coming up from the old east road, joins a wide path from Scary to the east to form the path to Dwaling northwards that skirts the rising hills of Scary. The road seems to be well travelled and is comfortable underfoot.
2511: You have reached a flat hilltop on the north-western edge of a range of hills known in the Shire as the hills of Scary. The tall, untrampled grass and wild shrubbery tell tales of desertion and isolation. Gazing outwards, you see an endless expanse of grassland to the north and what looks like a village some way off to the north-west. A narrow trail winds down the northern slope here.
2517: You have climbed up on one of the higher ridges of the hills of Scary. Wild grass and shrubbery cover the ground as elsewhere. Gazing northwards, you see an endless expanse of grassland extending all the way to the horizon. The northern slope at this point is too steep to descend.
2518: You stand on a higher hilltop at the western end of a range of hills known in the Shire as the hills of Scary. Gazing outwards, you make out a village far to the north-west. The western slope is too steep to descend, but you can see that the hills end a short distance north and south.
2519: You have reached a flat hilltop on the south-western edge of a range of hills known in the Shire as the hills of Scary. The tall, untrampled grass and wild shrubbery tell tales of desertion and isolation. Gazing outwards, you see what looks like a village far to the north-west and a cluster of farmed lands a little way south. A narrow trail winds down the southern slope here.
2520: You travel on a wide path which winds along the foot of the hills of Scary. Old criss-cross tracks of wheels and hooves much like those seen on the path to Dwaling suggest some of the carts from Dwaling pass this way. A small trail leads up the slope on your north. You can follow the path east or west.
2521: This wide path narrows a bit as it winds along the hills here, joining a crossroads to the west. The hardened road seems to bear the burden of many Dwaling carts. To the east the road leads into the small village of Scary.
2522: A Bounder is here, patrolling the Shire and watching for evil.

You stand in an open field of grass bordered on the north and east by a wide path. Wild flowers growing haphazardly here and there lend their bright colours to the picturesque scene. A wooden fence blocks travel to the south.
2523: A pretty hobbit maiden is walking around here.

You travel on a wide path which winds along the foot of the hills of Scary. Old criss-cross tracks of wheels and hooves much like those seen on the path to Dwaling suggest some of the carts from Dwaling pass this way. The path makes a turn to the north and east here. A large field opens up to your west, while a wooden fence blocks passage south.
2524: You travel on a wide path which winds along the foot of the hills of Scary. Old criss-cross tracks of wheels and hooves much like those seen on the path to Dwaling suggest some of the carts from Dwaling pass this way. The path makes a turn to the south and west around the hills here.
2525:
A rabbit is here eyeing your presence warily.
A sparrow is flapping around on the ground.

You are on a southern ridge of the hills of Scary. Wild grass and shrubbery cover the ground as elsewhere. Gazing southwards, you see a cluster of farmed lands a little way off. Nearer at hand, a wide path winds its way to the village of Scary just at the foot of these hills, but there is no way down from here. A steep, unclimbable hill rises to your east.
2526:
A large thorny branched shrub is growing here.
On the shrub, there are two piles of blackberries.
A rabbit is here eyeing your presence warily.

Here the hills seem to envelope you entirely as they rise and fall all around. A sudden feeling of isolation and loneliness grips you, though you know you are still in the Shire and the exit from these hills is not far off. You look around, and are a little reassured by the familiar sight of grass and shrubs. Still, you start to wonder if the village of Scary got its name from these hills.
2527:
There are two piles of wheat cereals here.
A pitchfork has been carelessly left lying here.
A mouse is here nosing around, looking for a safe place to hide.
A mouse is here nosing around, looking for a safe place to hide.

This appears to be where the farmers of Scary store their crops after harvest. Some remnant stalks in one corner indicate where the unthreshed wheat is kept temporarily in rainy weather. Sacks of grain, potatoes and mushrooms stand neatly stacked against one wall, while dry hay is piled against another.
2528: You are at one end of a mushroom field. Narrow paths have been left between neat rows of mushrooms to allow for walking. A wooden fence on the northern edge of the field keeps out trespassers. You see a small wooden building on your left.
2529: You are at one end of a mushroom field. Narrow paths have been left between neat rows of mushrooms to allow for walking. A wooden fence wraps around the northern and eastern edges of the field to keep out trespassers.
2530: There are two piles of wheat cereals here.

You guess that this field is used for cultivating wheat. Harvesting seems to be just over, for the field is bare save for stray stalks of wheat lying here and there. On the south a wooden fence keeps out trespassers. A small wooden building stands to your west.
2531: A hobbit farmer, holding a shovel, is resting here.

You see various farming tools and implements neatly arranged in labelled wooden boxes stacked against the western wall. In the eastern wall, a small window looks out on the furrowed fields. A round wooden table and some chairs set beside the window suggest that the shed doubles as the farmers' rest area.
2532: A hobbit farmer is here, thinking about seeds and vegetables.

You guess that this field is used for cultivating wheat. Harvesting seems to be just over, for the field is bare save for stray stalks of wheat lying here and there. On the south a wooden fence keeps out trespassers.
2533: A hobbit is here walking around.

You travel on a wide path which winds along the foot of the hills of Scary. Old criss-cross tracks of wheels and hooves much like those seen on the path to Dwaling suggest some of the carts from Dwaling pass this way. The path leads east and west here. On your south a wooden fence borders the path.
2534: A smiling hobbit child is playing around here.

The path leaves the foot of the hills at this point and maps a straight course east to the village of Scary. This part of it appears to be kept in better repair, perhaps due to the proximity of the village. The same criss-cross tracks that are so plainly visible to the north are much fainter here. To the south and west, a wooden fence bends round the path.
2535: The village of Scary is now clearly visible to the east, and you can see that the path you are on runs right through its middle. This part of the path seems to be kept in constant repair, for old tracks can barely be seen. A wooden fence runs the length of the path to your south.
2536: Here neat rows of turnip shoots lie between equally neat furrows. The shoots look young, and you decide against digging up a few for supper. A wooden fence on the north and south keeps out trespassers.
2537: Potato tendrils run all over the field here, and you have to walk with extreme caution so as not to step on them. You see that some attempt has been made to impose order on the tendrils by the placement of furrows, but even the hobbits' propensity for neatness has to give way to nature. To the north and south a wooden fence keeps out trespassers.
2538:
A dark green cabbage is growing here.
A golden, firm onion is here.
A bulb of garlic with green stems is here.
A hobbit farmer is here, thinking about seeds and vegetables.

This part of the farmed fields is used for growing vegetables. The field is sub-divided into smaller plots by furrows and footpaths. In some plots, you see green shoots only poking their tips out of the soil, while in others, leafy, delicious-looking vegetables tempt you. Yet other plots are empty. A wooden fence surrounds the field on the north, east and south.
2539:
A circular stone well has been built here.
A smiling hobbit child is playing around here.

You are in a grassy field bordered by wooden fences west and south. A neat row of low hedges separates the field from the village of Scary on the north, and a wide path on the east. The hedges are low enough to jump over, but there is an opening in the northern end from which a small muddy path leads to the large well in the middle of the field.
2540: A Bounder is here safeguarding the Shire.

Like all hobbit villages, the village of Scary is well-ordered with its neat rows of houses on both sides of the wide path which runs right through its middle. This end of the village appears to be poorer than its neighbours to the west, for the houses are really small and some have no pretense of a garden even. A few old carts lean outside some of the houses.
2541:
A Shirriff stands here, keeping a watchful eye on things.
A Shirriff stands here, keeping a watchful eye on things.

Like all hobbit villages, the village of Scary is well-ordered with its neat rows of houses on both sides of the wide path which runs right through its middle. You can see that this is a poorer part of the Shire, as the houses are generally small and the gardens just bits of tended ground. On the south, a wooden fence has been erected around some farmland.
2542: A hobbit is here walking around.

You travel on a wide path which winds along the foot of the hills of Scary. Old criss-cross tracks of wheels and hooves much like those seen on the path to Dwaling suggest some of the carts from Dwaling pass this way. The path makes a turn to the west and south here. Large open fields are visible on your north and east.
2543: You are in an open field of grass bordered on the south and west by a wide path, and on the north by a sheer hillside. Wild flowers growing haphazardly here and there lend their bright colours to the picturesque scene.
2544: A smiling hobbit child is playing around here.

You are in a well-tended field which extends to the east. The grass here is of even height everywhere, the flowers and trees grow in neat little patches. You guess that this is the party field of Scary, where all important events are held. To your north and west are more fields, but they do not look as well-cared for.
2545: You are in a well-tended field which extends to the west. The grass here is of even height everywhere, the flowers and trees grow in neat little patches. You guess that this is the party field of Scary, where all important events are held. North and east the field ends at low hedges which surround some private gardens. Small lanes lead straight through these gardens to bright round doors set in the hillside.
2546: A busy hobbit female is here worrying about the home labours.

You have entered an extremely comfortable-looking hobbit hole. From the size and furnishing of this place, you guess that the owner is much wealthier than his neighbours in Scary. A small round window set in the western wall looks out on the garden, and a big fireplace sits against the eastern wall.
2547: A pretty hobbit maiden is walking around here.

You are in an unremarkable small field off a wide path to your south. On all other sides, the rising hills of Scary look imposing as they fence you in. You notice an uncovered hole in the northern hillside, which looks barely big enough for an average-sized hobbit to squeeze through.

A Bounder is here, patrolling the Shire and watching for evil.
A Bounder is here, patrolling the Shire and watching for evil.

You are struck by the contrast of this field against the one you just left south. The tall, uneven grass has apparently never been cut, and the flowers and trees have apparently been left to grow anywhere they please. On three sides the rising hills of Scary fence you in, so that your only exit is back south.
2549: You find yourself on a narrow ledge carved out of the side of a steep hill which looms high on your south. The ledge continues to the east, while a safer-looking plateau beckons to you from the west. North is a sheer drop down to something shiny. You wonder if there is water down below.
2550: From the shape of this terrain, you can almost imagine yourself to be on the bottom of a gigantic furrow. Sheer hillsides loom to your north and south, while the relatively level ground you are on dips slightly from west to east. The grass appears greener, the trees taller and more numerous, perhaps due to the little stream running its course through here.
2551:
A brown fox is here, looking for some rabbits to chew up.
A squirrel scampers around here, looking for nuts from the trees.

The feeling of insecurity heightens as you continue along the narrow ridge which remains level for some distance to the east and west. Here the hills of Scary end in a sharp incline on your north. Looking down the southern edge, you detect a faint glint as of a shiny surface below, but there is no way to descend from this point.

To the north you see what looks like a huge pit with a small spring in its centre, while on your south the hills end in a steep drop down to a large grassy field. A little further south from the field, you can see the village of Scary with smoke spiralling out of its numerous chimneys.

A clear spring babbles as cool water trickles out of the ground.

You have descended into what can only be described as a huge pit in the hills of Scary, for rising hills surround you on three sides. On your north, the hillside is so sheer that it forms an unscalable wall, though the slopes on your south and west are climbable. The grass here looks greener, and trees grow in place of the stunted shrubs elsewhere, perhaps due to the proximity of the small spring. To the east the ground seems to dip slightly, as water from the spring flows off in that direction in a little stream.

This is part of the River Brandywine which forms the east border of the Shire. The water is cool and clear, and seems to be home to a great variety of fishes. North of here, the River appears to constrict suddenly, causing the water flow upstream to be much more rapid than from this point onwards. Going further upstream is impossible, for it is all boaters on this water can do to keep small crafts from being carried back south by the current.

Even if you are just passing through, you should stop by Woodhall and sample the famous beer of the East Farthing. Stock Road continues to the north and west.
2821:
A small grasshopper clings to a blade of grass, ready to spring.
A hobbit is here walking around.
A smiling hobbit child is playing around here.

You decide that you should be more careful as you stumble and nearly fall in a rut in the road. Your boots continue to raise dust, making it hard to see. The road continues on to the south and to the east, where you can see a crossing.
2822: More stone than wood seems to make up these woods. Much of the wood present has stood untouched for so many ages it has petrified. There is a notable lack of animal movement or any evidence that animals even pass through this area in travels to more hospitable land.
2823: The main point of this oak forest is the silence. There is no bird songs that can be heared. The trees grow very close one from the other, building a grey wall in the east. To the west and the south, more space can be seen between them.
2824: A black crow flies low to the ground here, looking for carrion to eat.

This field is spongious. In fact, it is soaked by water. Therefore lots of tracks can be seen in the fresh furrowed earth, showing the intense wild life of this country: one can even recognise some foxes footprints among the numerous tracks.
2825: A Hobbit shopkeeper stands here, eager to sell you his wares.
You are in the general store of the village of Woodhall. A well-built counter displays the wares that the grocer has for sale today.
2826: To the east, one can often hear the joyous laughter of hobbits seemingly living their innocent lives unaware of the evils of the world. In that direction lies the small village of Woodhall while to the west one would find the Stock Road.
2827: The air is quiet, but you know the fields hereabouts must be full of life. Small creatures hide in the grasslands beside the trail, intent upon evading notice by those who might hunt them. And so unkempt is the land that one would not need to travel too far from the path before being lost from view.
2828: The road is surrounded by a grass that reaches your knees. Silently, this land is worthy of its fame of being a peaceful place. You hardly can see signs of life around you, excepting the road that far to the north you barely see. Anyway, you know that the fields are full of life. The small village of Stock rises not too far to the east.
2830: The small river flows down to the Baranduin. After this eastward bend of the brook the riverbad widens and the current slows down. The banks of the brook are to slippery to leave the water. The village of Stock is not far to the north.
2831: The brook bends from the west to the north. The riverbanks are steep and covered with wet and slippery moss, it is impossible to leave the waterway. The surrounding landscape is peaceful with a small village to the northeast.
2832: From the west, the bend of the brook opens up to the east and suddenly, it is all peaceful again between the wide banks. In the northeast direction, the outline of a town can be seen.
2833: The current grows faster as it rounds a bend to the east. The once calm brook has become much more turbulent, making navigation difficult.
2834: The brook flows faster here and makes a sharp bend northwards. Its bottom is narrow and its bed smaller, causing the current to quicken to a dangerous pace.
2835: The small gentle river flows towards the Baranduin. Its banks are steeper in this part of it and covered by thick patches of slippery moss making it impossible to climb on land. The current of the brook is moderate.
2836: The Stockbrook is a small gentle river. Its mossy banks are lined with tall alders and willows forming a green ceiling over the clear water. In this part of the brook, the current is moderate.
2837: A sparrow is flapping around on the ground.
The Stockbrook flows calmly and quietly between the two green banks on either side. Its crystal clear water allows one to see the bottom of the brook and all the creatures that dwell within.
2838: Here, the brook yields to the local terrain and curves from south to east. The current of the small river towards the Brandywine gains a little in strength and makes travelling upwards the brook difficult.
2839:

A black catfish is here, lurking in the mud.

The Stockbrook flows swifly between steep banks. The strong current looks as if it makes travel downstream very easy. The riverbanks are lined with alders and willow trees which often times cover the river in shade.

A large fountain, made from grey stone, pours water from its centre.
A Bounder is here, patrolling the Shire and watching for evil.

You are standing in the central square of a small Hobbit village named Woodhall. This village is not as famous as Stock, but it is no less merrier than any other village your travels have taken you to. To the east is a bar where you can sample some of the famous East Farthing beer. To the north is a general store where local Hobbits buy their supplies. A path leads west to Stock Road.
2841: The Taproom of the Tipsy Cat Tavern

A small hobbit bartender is here, bragging about the beer.
A Bounder is here, patrolling the Shire and watching for evil.

Though quite small, this bar seems to be one well patronised by the local folk, and rightly so too, for the ales of the Eastfarthing have a great reputation throughout the Shire. A short, sturdy wooden bar stands at one end of the room, and a cosy hearth is set into the wall across from the doorway, to warm the room on cold winter evenings.

A tiny spider is here, eating a tiny bug.
A mole is looking out of a mole-hill here.

Here is the beginning of the Stockbrook. Multiple small waterways come from the higher hills around to flow together to create the Stockbrook. It is an inspiring sight to see and hear nature hard at work. If your destination is the River Baranduin, also known as the Brandywine, this seems to be the correct brook to follow.

A restless rabbit bounces around.

There isn't any underbrush, but it is still very hard to travel because of the huge, twisted roots of the elm trees. Everywhere you turn, you see trees and more trees. You begin to wonder if it is true that shortcuts make long delays.

2855: Here the ground slopes up to the east, and you wonder if there is an exit in that direction. The tunnel seems to be slightly wider at this point, for the walls are not so threateningly close. Or is it just a trick of the mind?
2856: You walk warily on, following the twists and turns of the tiny tunnel. With every step, the smooth mud walls seem to edge ever closer, threatening to close in on you.
2857: You appear to have come to a dead end. As you stare at the walls they almost seem to come alive, as if trying to move toward you, closing in upon you. But that can only be the workings of your imagination. However, it remains clear that the only way out of this place is to the north.

A simple wooden chest is here.
A simple wooden chest is here.

Without warning, the tunnel walls suddenly part and retreat from you, and you find yourself in some kind of small cave with -- you gasp, and feel your heart thumping with excitement. Can it be that you have chanced upon an ancient treasure trove? Dust-covered chests are lined neatly against the walls, perhaps forgotten by whoever hid them here. You get closer to the chests, then notice the note pasted on one of them.
2865: You are under a wooden bridge, which is quite new... The Water is running under you from the west towards the east. The river is here quite under a wooden bridge, which is not very old, although some sign of moisture indicates it has been already flooded several times. The Water is running from the west towards the east, and it seems possible to climb on the bridge from here.
2866: This field lies near a small road which runs through the Shire, just north of here. The field is well-kept and divided in small parcels limited by a single stone at each end. In the south, there is a bigger field and the brown line of an earth path can be seen in the east.
2867: Some cereals that look like wheat are lying here.

This field, one among hundreds to be found on the plains of the Shire, which is bounded in part by the Old East Road and the woody hills far to the south, is farmed and harvested with great care. For only the best wheat can be used to make the bread that the Hobbits will eat.
2868: A large potato is growing here.

An important component of a hobbit's diet is the potato. This field, which the hobbits use to grow potatos, is the largest of all the hobbits' fields. The furrows run towards the south as far as the eye can see. Perhaps this field extends as far as the southern hills which are barely visible from here.
2869:
A dark green cabbage is growing here.
A round turnip is growing here.

Around you are many acres of lush farmland, rows upon rows of cabbages, turnips and parsnips. The heads of these vegetables cover the area like a perfect green carpet spreading out in front of you and into the horizon. To the west, the farmland continues.
2870: The soil here seems perfect for growing crops, and some hobbit farmer is already taking advantage of this. All around you grow rye, barley, hops, oats, flax and wheat. All seem ready for harvest. It also looks as though the farmer has taken the time to install a simple irrigation system in the area to keep his crops wet and well nourished. The fields continue to the east, and there is a small orchard to the south.
2872: Trees dot the countryside here, as a small orchard grows here. Apple trees seem to be the main production of this orchard, with some smaller berry bushes and some pear trees to the side. A small planting of parsnips and barley can also be found here.
2873: You are surrounded by beautiful hills that are being used as a pasture for many animals. Lush green grass grows all around. To the north, you can see some cultivated land, the west, an orchard, and to the south, the pasture continues.
2874: This field extends as far as the eye can see. It is evident from the evenly spaced furrows that the field is used to grow corn and other vegetables. While, there are no signs of the farmers, from the freshness of the furrows it is obvious that the farmers have not strayed far.
2875: A large potato is growing here.

This field is really quite large. While most of the fields in the Shire are of similar size and are relatively small, this one is so big that one can't see its northern end from here. There is another field towards the south, where some woody hills appear, limiting the cultivated plain you are standing on.
2876: A smiling hobbit child is playing around here.

Lush pastures and low rolling hills dot the countryside here. Several small animals, and some livestock has found a home here. The hills make great hiding spots for rabbits, and the pastures are great for the cows and horses. To the west, you can see a small farm.
2877:
A low and wide-spread tree grows here.
On the tree's branches, there are three juicy plums.

The lands around you are almost completely empty. Every now and then you can see a small animal run into or out of its hole and scurry off into the distance or down another hole. The ruins of a small house also lies here, almost buried under the long grass. You can see a small orchard to the north, and a small farm to the distant west.
2880: A worm is here slithering around.

Like most fields of the Shire, this one is cultivated. One can't determine what sort of plants the farmer intends to grow here, because the field was recently tilled. South of here a forest grows on the large hill which blocks the vision in that direction.
2881: A pack horse is standing here, ridden by you.

A path starts here at the core of the forest and seems to lead towards the north. All around trees can be seen announcing a large forest southwards. To the west furrowed ground can be found, marking the beginning of some fields.
2882: As you enter this pasture a calm and sense of peace beckons to you. Even though this place may be calming there is still an eerie surround to it, things may be at work here. You notice, in a southerly direction, some huge trees. A barely visible road lies also southerly from here.
2883: On the Side of the Road

To the north and east there is a little forest and another expanse of barren lands. Several trees are growing randomly within this vicinity. The trees are healthy looking and seems to be well taken care of. To the north is a small open forest with several types of trees in. Southerly there is a small trail leading from a much wider track.
2884: A hobbit is here walking around.

You walk in a forest, growing in and around a range of hills. All around you there are signs of life. Travel is rather peaceful. Here, the hills seem to be dying down, however, only a faint memory, not far east.
2885: A rabbit is here eyeing your presence warily.
You are walking through a range of low, sloping hills. Sparse trees cover the land. Wild flowers are in bloom. To the south and east, the forest gets much thicker.
2886: You are within a fine and well spaced forest. There are some scurrying animals sniffing along the ground and sniffing the berries which grow here. You can hear the birds singing on the birches of the trees, the edges of the forest are visible so you hope it is easier to get out of this forest than some others that are within this vicinity.
2887: Stock Road continues its journey through the forest, and enters Tuckborough, just west of you. The forest is calm, but not quiet. Rather, it is teeming with life.
2888: The road continues through the calm forests. The sides of the road are rustling with action. You wonder if it is wise to camp too close to the woods which border the road. As you walk on you notice the soft noises of the animals. The road continues easterly and westerly, to the north is a small expanse of grassland.
2889: You're not really sure where the forest gives way to Tuckborough, but you are now standing in this old halfling village. Many of the nearby hills have burrows, or smials as the hobbits call them, but it seems regular houses and shelters are becoming more and more popular. Some hobbits stop to see what you're doing.

This is a a small well-tended barn which contains a big stack of hay as well as a paddock. This would obviously be a good place to leave your horse.

The birch, maple, and pine all make an impression in these woods. Your foot crunches upon the leaves and needles which make up the forest floor. Shafts of sunlight break through the branches high above, and a soft breeze plays around you. A quiet, gentle, woods you think, until you hear a dark howl to the south, and then you wonder.

You stand in the town square of Tuckborough. Here, hobbits come out of their burrows to meet, exchanging pleasantries, and sitting down for a smoke. Not far from here is a large door, leading down into the ancestral home of the Tooks, Great Smials.

A Hobbit shopkeeper stands here, eager to sell you his wares.

The scent of pipeweed is, quite obviously, very strong in here. Behind the counter, Brenon Took smiles at you. He invites you to sample some of the new brands, and it is very tempting to do so. There are bags and cases of pipeweed in every corner, along with a small cabinet containing various pipes that are on display. A sign hangs near the entrance.

You walk in thick forest, over and around a large range of hills. There are signs of life, all around you. While travel is pleasant, it is slow, and you start to think you might get lost.

This is obviously a storage room. There are crates, sacks, and barrels all over the room. However, some wooden barrels catch your attention, the gentle smell of pipeweed wafting through the air. You stop to remember all those comfortable evenings in front of the fire, listening to tales near and far. Why the heck are you adventuring, anyways?
2908: The corpse of a hobbit smuggler is lying here.

You have entered a small, square room. This room is kept in fine condition when compared with the deserted room above. There is even a rug neatly covering the floor. Some clothes hang on a rack, against the western wall, and some boots lie underneath.

A long wooden table occupies nearly all the space within this room. Two long benches sit beside it. A meal was eaten here rather recently. The dirty silverware is clear evidence.

This small room contains a shelf with all the various tools and ingredients necessary for preparing a large meal. A big pot hangs over a blazing fire. A small hole in the ceiling allows the smoke to leave the room.
2911: Three beds stand in this room, one against each wall, save the northern. The beds are unmade, matching the floor, which is covered by clothes, bedding, and other litter. The residents are not as orderly as most of the hobbits of the Shire, that is certain.
2912: The corpse of a smuggler is lying here.
You pull the curtain aside, and enter what seems to be the living quarters of a single person. A bed rests alongside the east wall, and a desk is along the south. On the desk is a letter.

The ground is spongy and walking is difficult as it slightly shifts under the slightest weight. It is covered with wet vegetation, though in parts standing water can be seen. Marsh gases slowly escape the rotting vegetation, giving the area a very distinct smell. A trail lies to the east of this bog.
2914: The road you are on could not be more mundane than it already is. You notice a small bog to the west. As you move on your nose slowly starts to recognise the sweet odours of pipe-weed in the wind. There could be some hobbits close by.

A gorcrow is standing here.
A Bounder is here, patrolling the Shire and watching for evil.

You are standing on the ruins of a once great wooden building. The remains of the various rooms are scattered all over the area. There is very little left of the eastern side wall of the building which confuses you. You can return back to the clearing.

2921: You are walking on a stone paved path which must have been a larger road at times when people had affairs that required passing the forest of Woody End. From here following the path gets a bit nasty, the next step the way to go might not be exactly clear.

A brown pond between old branches and roots is here.
A grey wolf is here, snarling aggressively.

A wolf cub happily plays here.

You are standing on a small clearing in the southern side of the woods. The path comfortably leads you here, maybe too comfortably. You notice the prints of various animals on the path and around the pond here. The old stone paved path goes on toward east and is engulfed by the forest at some point.

A small barrel made of aged oak and strong iron hoops stands here.
A beer barrel has been left here.
A hobbit is here walking around.

You have found the secret hide-out of the infamous Woody End Brewers. They are a party of all races who seek huge profits by selling beers and wines to the people who cannot go to the cities to buy it. The floor is flooded with beer.
2925: A black crow flies low to the ground here, looking for carrion to eat.

You are walking around in the dense forest of Woody End. Your sense of direction has disappeared since you entered these woods. There is no way to tell which direction would be best to go to right now. It may be time to use your navigational skills.

The sticky, stinking muddy path seems alive with all manner of small insects. Mostly they slip by unseen, but they are felt and heard, lending a decidedly unappealing air to this place. To the north and west lie heavy woodland, where the ground appears to be firmer. The path stretches to the east. But south of here the trail peters out, the way blocked by a thick and slimy mire, which may well prove to be impassable.

A slender plant, with white flowers at the top, grows here.
A slender plant, with white flowers at the top, grows here.
A large shrub covered with dark violet berries grows here.
A tall stag is here, grazing peacefully.

You stand in the famous forest of Woody End, many trees around you blocking your view to few pathetic paces. Most of the trees are oaks and beeches, and heavy vegetation covers the ground. The humidity is so intense that you could almost touch it.

You've found the old lonesome tanner's hiding place deep within the woods. He doesn't seem aggressive; actually he might even be delighted to see other people, though he isn't going to allow you to stay around for too long. There are skins of different animals on the ground around him, he seems to be knitting something from one of them.

Bustling with life, this forest is very dense; filled with vines and shrubbery. More woods spread out in all directions, but through the undergrowth a small path can be glimpsed every now and then.

You have entered the woods from the northern section. The forests are full of life and of course the feelings of danger are very strong around you. Pairs of invisible eyes are glaring at you pondering to find the best possible place and time to make a dinner out of you.

The lands around you are extremely boggy. Many footprints can be seen, deep indentations in the soft soil. This wetland is difficult to travel, the mud and wet weeds clinging to your feet, and the road which lies to the south offers an easier route to follow.

Hanging on the walls of this small home, there are many magnificent paintings of a mighty ship being tossed about by raging waves. The pictures all show the same ship with the same stout captain at the wheel. The lone occupant of this home, a withered captain, occasionally glances up at the paintings, losing his thoughts seemingly for hours.

You walk through a narrow gate on a green path. You peer into an old-fashioned countrified house. It is long and low, with no upper storey; it has a roof of turf, round windows, and a large round door. This is Crickhollow, one of the houses of the Brandybucks.
