You have entered the luxuriously furnished office of the mayor of Newbury. A finely crafted oak desk occupies the centre of the room. Several lonely unfinished documents lie upon the desk as evidence of the mayor's frequent absence. The walls are paneled with a very fine light brown wood that almost seems to glow. A masterfully crafted suit of plate armour rests against the wall of the office. There is a colourful oil painting of the mayor hung upon the western wall.

You are standing at the edge of a ancient forest, it looks older than anything you've seen before. The trees look twisted strangely alive. To the south the forest looks even darker, and there is an unmistakable scent of evil in the air. You have the feeling that something is lurking for you in the depths of the forest. You'd better get out of here quickly!

You are standing in a light part of the forest bordering the road. To the southeast the forest seems to be much darker, and it almost seems to be alive. Some evil source must be in the centre of it, and you don't really want to go in there. The road is north and west of here.

This is a large kitchen, large enough to prepare food for the huge feasts hosted by the Brandybucks. It seems to be kept quite tidy, at least the room is clean and tidy right now. On some shelves a lot of dishes, cups, plates, pots and other kitchen utensils are stored.

The Master of Buckland is here, proud and important-looking.

You enter a large smial and find yourself in a large and almost cylindric hallway. You can enter several large rooms and halls. The size of the rooms in here surprises you. This is the largest hobbit dwelling you have ever seen. A large plaque is placed on one of the green walls. It can tell you about the history of this house.

This is a large hall, the largest room of the Brandy Hall. A large fireplace in one of the corners makes this room comfortable on cold winter days. Several round windows let light in from the outside. The wall is full of pictures of important looking members of the Brandybucks. Expensive furniture tells you that the Brandybucks are probably the most wealthy family in the Shire. Among the pictures on the wall, you notice a drawing of a family tree.

A patch of moss grows here on a wet, flat stone.

Judging by the sounds of ponies and cows above you, you must be under Farmer Maggot's barn. Everywhere you look is darkness. You can feel dirt and soil occasionally falling from the ceiling. You had better be careful because one of those ponies or cows may come crashing down on you.

There are several small stalls for the many ponies Farmer Maggot owns. Perhaps, with his permission, you would be able to borrow one of these stout ponies for your journey.

You are inside a cozy, dirt-floored barn. In the centre of the barn, there is a small, worn out wagon. To the north is a stable. Judging from the smells coming from the stable, you guess that there might be a pony in there.

This seems to be Farmer Maggot's secret cellar where he keeps his best beer. The smell of ale dominates this small room giving you reason to believe he often keeps this small room well stocked. There is also a barrel of wine, a rarity in the Shire.

You are in the living room of Farmer Maggot's house. The room is furnished with comfortable furniture that looks inviting to your weary legs. To the west, there is an archway that leads into a dining room dominated by a large elm table. Next to the front door to the east is a stairway leading up to a hallway.

This large, by Hobbit standards, room is dominated by a large, round elm dining table. The table is large enough to seat many Hobbits, and is surrounded by a like number of finely carved elm chairs.

Lining the rest of the walls, there are cupboards where various breads, mushrooms, and vegetables are kept. Your nose twitches as you catch the scent of a finely brewed beer.

You are in a bedroom. Judging by the size of the beds, this must be a room for Hobbit children. There are fourteen little beds arranged in an orderly manner about the room. A door leads east, out into the hallway.

You are standing in an upstairs hallway. To the south, there is a door that you guess leads to Mr. Maggot's bedroom. To the west, there is a door leading to another bedroom. A stairway along the north wall leads down to the living room.

You are in the master bedroom. A large, by Hobbit standards, double bed is against the north wall. Set in the eastern wall, is a window, giving a view of the whole Maggot farm. A door leading to a closet is on the west wall.

In this small closet, all you can see are some Hobbit clothes and a small wooden chest placed against the north wall. Although nothing seems to be out of the ordinary, you have a sense that there is more here than meets the eye.

You have found Old Maggot's secret hideaway. All around you is dark. The walls seem to be made of a strange material that seems to absorb light. You can just make out a stout chest set in the centre of the room. This must be where Old Maggot has stashed his fortune. Greed and morality war for control of your actions as you gaze upon it.

It may be your imagination, but there was a faint flicker of light from above. You think you can make out a small hole in the ceiling that leads up to an air filled space.

A small round cave opens up, its wall in some places made from packed earth, in others by naked stone. A rough straw pallet lies at the base of one wall, while a low wooden table bearing a single flickering candle sits near the centre of the cave. The cave extends further to the north.
3159: A tiny spider is here, eating a tiny bug.

East there is a long wall, that used to mark some sort of boundary. Travelling along this wall for a bit you find a hole big enough to walk through.
3242: You're walking through the thick wall that used to mark the boundaries to an old and almost forgotten about kingdom from long ago. You realise there must be a sad tale about why only the wall remains, but you think it's best to never ask someone to tell you the story.

3250: Wandering Path along the Ridge of a Hill

Out of breath from your climb up the slope of this hill, you are happy to have finally reached the top. Up here you can almost see forever. As you slowly catch your breath, you sadly realise there are many more hills to climb in these downs before you reach your destination. After a bit, you begin looking for a safe way down off this hill.
3251: Wandering Path along the Ridge of a Hill

This is the perfect place for viewing the trail you must follow to reach your destination. Up here you can see almost everything. Far off to the north you see a line going east west that from this distance looks like trees before the road. Both north and south there are many more ridges of hills left to traverse. These hills peep out at you through the fog that blankets the valleys between the hills.
3252: This hill is so steep you must travel the slope sideways. If you tried to walk straight up or down this hill you would gain too much momentum and would soon tumble over and roll down this hill. Half way during your travel you notice the faint grassy path you have been following splits into two different directions. One of the forks leads down into what looks like a small peaceful valley.
3253: You're standing in a valley on the foot of a what seems to be the tallest hill in the downs. To the north you see ridges of more hills that seem to fade off into the distance. Still no sign of the road as you begin your journey again with weary feet.
3254: On Top of a Small Hill

On top of this small hill you are able to see more clearly all the ridges you may have to climb to the north. Also you look around for the best path to take that might get you out of the downs a lot quicker. Clearly the best path seems to lie to the north-east, the hills seem a little less steep in this direction.
3255: A Tiny Valley hidden within the Hills

Steep grassy hills surround this small and secluded valley on all sides. The only exit is to climb back up the hill that brought you to this place. The grass under your feet is soft and lush green. The air smells so sweet from the scent of the grass, that you decide this is a nice place to sit and relax your tired, weary feet. On the horizon to the north you can see the rounded peaks of ridge after ridge of hills. You've still a long way to travel to the road, so a rest here in this beautiful valley might better prepare you physically as well as mentally for the journey ahead of you.
3256: A Grassy Path up a Steep Hill
The only way to traverse this hill is to weave slowly back and forth along the incline. This is such a labour to do and you quickly begin to run out of breath.
3257: A Grassy Path Heading up a Hill

Before you stands what must be one of the highest hills in the downs. The only way up the hill seems to be a faint path in the grass that wanders up the steep incline. To your east, is a smaller hill, but much more difficult to ascend because it's even steeper slope. South the path seems to wander to even more hills.

The hills are rolling steeply here, and you have reached the end of a well-tended path. The stone-border is sparse here, and the path goes up and down, across the hills and between them.

The entrance to Tom and Goldberry's house is humble. No great portal, just a simple little gate. Flowers of every shape and colour flourish here, carefully placed so as to best show the forms and hues of each. The clear and beautiful voice of a maiden sings above you.
3274: In Front of the Garden Gate

The entrance to Tom and Goldberry's house is humble. No great portal, just a simple little garden gate. You admire the work of Goldberry, the flowers are classified by their different species. But all are flourishing, showing you their multiple colours. You hear the clear voice of Golberry singing for the health of her plants and you listen with delight.
3275: You are on the threshold of Tom Bombadil's house. From the door to the east comes a golden light which envelopes you. Already, half of your fears and worries begin to disappear. From inside you can hear a clear voice, sweet as the sound of a healthy spring playfully cascading over some nearby rocks.
3276: A Creek in Front of Tom's House

The river carried you safely to this small creek. You see the river continue smoothly further down. As you have a quick look around you, you notice a small, well kept house. You can see some smoke coming out of the chimney. You feel that your will has returned and you pray that these people will help you.

All of the ground is covered with hay, but you ought to watch where you put your feet.

A small oaken table has been set here.
A busy hobbit female is here worrying about the home labours.

You have entered into a small hobbit hole without even knocking on the door! It seems that the hobbits that live here will eat soon, there is lots of good food on the table, and the kitchen looks like a mess. The man of the house seems to be out at the moment, but since the food seems almost to be finished he'll no doubt be home soon.
3306: This dark and musty tunnel seems to be used as a warehouse. There are bundles of coarse material and large wooden crates littering the floor. There are some barrels piled up against the eastern wall and stacks of boxes seem to be covering something to the north.
3307: This tunnel seems very old. The floor is covered with debris from the crumbling ceiling as well as in a thick layer of rubble. The walls of the tunnel are infested with mould, which thrives in the damp and humid tunnels. Strangely enough a footpath has been cleared through the rubble, as if this tunnel is often in use.
3308: This tunnel is a narrow passage between the rubble-filled tunnel in the north and a small cavern in the south. The rock-walls are range from pale yellow to dark grey in colour, at places covered with sickly, grey-green mould.
3309:
A brown bear is sleeping here.
A vicious little bandit advances towards you.

This small chamber has been deliberately carved out of the soft yellow rock. The ground of the cavern is made of cracked stone, and there is a large flat stone resting in the middle of it. Several alcoves have been cut into the sides of the chamber. A few reminders of the previous occupants lie scattered about the floor.
3310: The extent of this large underground chamber may only be determined by painstakingly following the wall all the way around. At several places, stalactites have merged with stalagmites, forming large pillars. The entrance of this cavern lies to the west, where the cavern ceiling is much lower.
3311: Carved by some long vanished, underground river, the roof of this cave is quite low. Small stalactites hang like daggers from the ceiling. In the middle of the cave, some of the stalactites have been broken off, to open the cave for exploration. The cave slopes gently upwards to the west, where large rocks rest unnaturally at the cave-entrance. The grotto becomes much wider, and somewhat higher to the east.
3373:
A great blade, long and sharp, cleaves the ground here.
The corpse of a young ranger is lying here.
A large WARNING SIGN is here.
A colourful butterfly is fluttering around here.

The road ends here outside the high, arched gateway that, if entered, would lead you through the walls and into the old city of Fornost. In ancient times this was the seat of mighty human warlords until it was besieged and taken by the Witch-king of Angmar. Although retaken shortly after, the city lay in ruins after the fierce battles. It remained in that state for many centuries to come, and only recently has it found new inhabitants. The Dunedain have started the slow process of restoring the city to its former importance and glory.
3406: The Old East Road runs east to west, bordering the outskirts of the Chetwood forest. To the south, the road is bounded by a hedge beyond which seems to be open fields, which are mostly covered with grass and dotted with the occasional small shrub.
3407: A pony is standing here, ridden by you.

Tucked between the hedge and the marsh, the Old East Road continues on from east to west here, skirting the Midgewater to the north on its journey between Breeland and rivendell. To the northwest the hardwood trees of the Chetwood begin to become thicker, indicating that the ground is probably drier in that direction.
3408: The road is muddy here as it passes through a low depression. To the north, wet grasses grow on a muddy plain -- a mere taste of the marshes that lie farther to the northeast. The Great Hedge to the south blocks the South Downs from view, but some distance to the southeast, a large hill peeks above it.
3409: The Old East Road passes through a low area here, right on the southern edge of the Midgewater Marshes. Somewhere to the east lie the Weather Hills -- the crown of Weathertop is clearly visible when the sky is clear -- beyond which the road passes on its long journey to Rivendell. To the west, the road bends north once the marshes end, and then passes through the Chetwood and thence to Bree. Alongside the southern edge of the road, the Great Hedge screens the empty hills of the Southern Downs from view.
3410: Just to the north of the road lie the treacherous fens of the Midgewater Marshes. A low mist -- a seemingly eternal feature -- hangs low over the dense vegetation, obscuring sight and hiding hordes of biting insects. Running alongside the road to the south is the Great Hedge. In places it looms as much as nine feet above the ground, and its tangled branches provide an unpassable barrier between the marshland and road to the north and the expanse of the South Downs to the south.
3411: The road bends here once more, turning west to south to avoid the wet marshes. To the east, a narrow strip of grassy ground provides a last chance of steady footing before the marshes themselves. To the north, the weed-choked pools of the Midgewater reach to the edge of the road itself.
3412: Water running from the Old East Road to the south collects here, pooling and collecting in little rivulets before running off into the Midgewater Marshes to the north. Just south of the road can be seen the great Hedge, its branches so intertwined that it is impossible to push through to the other side. Directly to the north a low hill rises, allowing one a good view of the marshes.
3413: The road bends east to north here, following the southern boundary of the Midgewater. Pressed right against the roadside to the south is the Hedge -- somewhat thinner here than elsewhere, but still a non-trivial obstacle. On the far side of the hedge, a large hill raises out of the landscape, and presumably one could see much of the surrounding territory from that vantage point.
3414: The road continues east and west, hemmed in by the Hedge to the south and the Midgewater marshes to the north. Through a break in the reeds to the north, the remnants of an ancient stone road can be seen, leading north into the marshes.
3415: A small lake of black water lies just to the north, its dark water almost lapping at the edge of the road. Another similar lake brushes the road a couple of miles to the east. The Great Hedge to the south seems extraordinarily thick here, as among the gnarled branches the straight trunks of many young oak trees can be found, having found purchase on a small patch of higher ground.
3416: To the north, a small lake of ominous black water encroaches to the fringe of the Old East Road. The lake is surrounded by the reeds and sedges typical of the Midgewater, and looks quite deep. To the south runs the Great Hedge, separated the road from the South Downs, while east and west the Old East road continues it journey.
3417: The reeds of the Midgewater grow right beside the north edge of the road, and the hard earth is muddy in several of the low-lying places. To the south, the Hedge hides from view the wide open expanse of the South Downs.
3418: The marshes to the north appear to end a short distance to the east, where the land becomes higher and much drier. The Old East Road continues east and west, and to the south lies the Hedge.
3419: The faint smell of dank water lingers here at all times. This part of the road is always pretty dark, as the hedge towers above it on the south and east sides. The road makes a turn north and west here, barely avoiding the thorns and the waters to the northwest. Deep ruts have been carved in the muddy earth, and this has caused some wagon to loose a wheel which now lies half buried in the mud just at the foot of the hedge.
3420: A pony is standing here, ridden by you.

This part of the road is in a bad shape. Muddy and deeply rutted it really could use some attention. A faint effort to dig a ditch towards the marshes west of here has proven a failure, and the ditch is full of black and still water. As the road turns south it enters a thin stretch of land that lies between the waters and the hedge. It continues in a fairly straight line east, eventually disappearing below Weathertop on the south side. North of here lies some bushy wetland, but beyond this the ground gets higher.
3421:
A small grasshopper clings to a blade of grass, ready to spring.
A pony is standing here, ridden by you.

The hedge grows fairly low here on the south side of the road, about twelve feet high only. Mounted people and trolls might attempt to peek over the edge and try to see what is on the other side. Large footprints indicate that this has been tried. The road is fairly bad shape, with ruts so deep as to make stones come forth, causing wagons and cart to jolt.
3422: Old East Road by a Rock

A small grasshopper clings to a blade of grass, ready to spring.
A pony is standing here, ridden by you.

As the road dodges a large rock north of here it pushes closer to the hedge. A semi-arc of thorns cover half of the road, providing some shadow on hot days. Now and then bypassers cut off twigs to keep the hedge at bay, and these litter the ground. A faint trail runs north of the rock also, as some people prefer to avoid this narrow passage.
3423: A pony is standing here, ridden by you.

As well as the hedge grows on the south side of the road, bushes grow on the north quite frequently. The road descends and rises fairly much for a few miles here, and you see wild red and yellow flowers hiding amongst the bushes in the dips. The road is in pretty good shape, and travelling is easy.
3424: A pony is standing here, ridden by you.

A few ashen trees form a grove on the north side of the road here. Someone has cut down some of them, and the logs and stumps are used for resting and eating on. A campfire has been assembled in the middle, and the place is littered by bones and horse manure. You also see dog-like tracks all over. The hedge grows thick south of here, and the road continues east and west.
3425: Thick wooden beams support an archway through the hedge here on the south side of the road. While burnt and battered, the beams still stand strong. The handicraft is excellent, and surely made by numenorean hands. A path leads through the opening to the plains south of the hedge. The brown Old East Road runs away far both to the east and west, but eventually disappear south behind the hedge in both directions. North of here lie vast grey plains beyond a small grove of ashen trees.
3426: The dusty road runs east-west here north of the thick hedge. To the north, vast grey plains stretch out as far as the eye can see. Little wildlife catches the eye, but you can hear birds and animals move inside the hedge.
3427: A grey wolf is here, snarling aggressively.

The road makes a turn here, leaving in the south and west directions. The hedge follows closely its path on the south side, being thorny and uncared for. It ends a few yards from the road though, and poses no threat to travellers who doesn't want to leave the road. All to the north and east scrubby plains stretch out, and here and there the dark shadow of an old watchtower rise from them.
3428: Around this bend the thorns grow very high, towering to heights above twelve yards. You can hear small animals play inside, and you spot a nest of some kind high up. Northeast of here lies a patch of earth devoid of any signs of life. You can follow the road north to another bend or east, where the road is stone- laiden and well kept.
3429: A small grasshopper clings to a blade of grass, ready to spring.

The hedge grows thick and pretty wild south of here, and the road turns and twists fairly much to avoid its whims and spurs. On the north side of the road the land is dead and brown, making a sharp contrast to the green and lively hedge. For some reason the road is laden with stones on this part and eastwards, while a mile further west it turns into a dustroad.
3430: The road is very well kept here, with grey stones fitting tight together. The slow murmur of the wind blowing through the high hedge can be heard below sounds of birds singing in some deciduous trees north of the road. The hedge is thin and dead in many places, even burnt. Nowhere can you find a way through it though, and it is still impassable.
3431: You are standing on the most frequented road of all Middle-earth. You can walk without any difficulties on this nice and smooth road. But be sure not to get off this road if you want no trouble.

3444: This is the great road which stretches east and west across Eriador. Built over two thousand years ago, the traffic along this road must have once been considerable to justify the expense. Nowadays, there are few travellers to marvel at this great feat of construction. The road cuts through the flat land here, shadowed by the impressive hedge of thorny bushes to the south and the thick expanse of bracken of the plains to the north.
3445: The road here curves northward to approach closer under the watchful eye of Weathertop. This great conical hill lies fully ten miles in a northwesterly direction, yet from this distance it is still striking.
3446: The road bends here slightly, the westerly stretch snaking southwards before continuing onwards to Bree. East, the road passes within a few miles of the southern flank of Weathertop, known as Amon Sul by the learned.
3447: This is a lonely countryside, flat for miles about, bar the north where lies the distinctive shape of Weathertop. Isolated as it is from the rest of the range of hills, it marks the southern end of the Emyn Sul. A trail in the flat terrain before the hill curves southwards, towards this road.
3448: Directly south of Weathertop, a meeting of ways occurs. The first is the great road built by Elendil's followers long ago, unbroken for many miles in either the east or west direction. The second route is a simple trail, with few stones to mark it. This trail crosses the passage of the road.
3449: You are standing on a small path, hills lying to the north. You almost can't see where the path leads to; this path doesn't seem to be used very often.
3450: You are standing on a small path, hills lying to the north. You almost can't see where the path leads to; this path doesn't seem to be used very often.
3451: This small trail winds its way amongst the hills which rise above you to the north of here. As it twists and turns through the rolling countryside, it is often quite impossible to make out where the path might lead, and it is perhaps for this reason that it is so seldom used. Thick weeds and long grasses grow among the stones of the trail, almost obscuring it from view in places.
3452: You are standing on a small path, surrounding the hills to the north. You almost can't see where the path leads to; this path doesn't seem to be used very often.

3455: The trail seems to have enlarged itself. You can now see through the dense vegetation. You can sense an unknown force, surrounding you. Its evil aura makes you shiver.
3456: The path seems to become smaller and smaller. You begin to doubt if this path was the right direction to take. The vegetation obscures the passage; you scratch yourself everywhere. What a nasty region ! You swear loudly; it was maybe a word too much : you have woken up all the strange animals hiding in the bushes...

3460: The trail continues, hard to distinguish among the grasses and small bushes that grow here. The land is flat here. Only the hills in the northern and eastern distances break the flat lands stand out from the plain.
3461: You find burrs sticking to you as you follow the trail through the grasses. You hear the sounds of insects and birds about you, but there is no sign of other people... even the trail might have been made by animals. Far off in the east, the rounded green shapes of the Weather Hills are the only sign that this plain has an end.
3462: A small grasshopper clings to a blade of grass, ready to spring.

Someone made a trail here among the barren plains. It is hard to pick out among the rocks and the short grass, but it goes west and south bypassing a small, seemingly deserted village to the north. From the north to the southeast a line of mighty hills dominates the horizon.
3463: A colourful butterfly is fluttering around here.

Someone has made a trail here among the treeless plains. It is hard to pick out among the short grass and the wildflowers, but it leads to the north and to the east, avoiding the walled town northeast of you. From the north to the southeast a line of hills dominates the horizon.
3464: Someone has made a trail here among the barren plains. It is hard to pick out among the rocks and the short grass, but it leads to the west and to the south, purposely avoiding the walled town to your east. No smoke comes from that town, nor are the plains about it cultivated. From the north to the southeast a line of mighty hills dominates the horizon.
3465: There is a lot of snow on the ground.

Grass grows on the trail, making it hard to distinguish from the grasslands all about. There are almost no trees here, and if people once grew crops or herded cattle on the plains, there are no longer any signs of it. Birds, beasts, and bugs are the only dwellers here.
3466: Hiking along this trail is quite quaint and lovely, there are few stubs of tree roots that make this path a little bumpy but not at all harsh. Parts of the trail look forgotten and deserted, while others look well kept. Most likely this is just from the natural abandonment of the area and not because of anything else. The lands around the trail seems to change quite often and there looks to be no real cabins around here, a few dead trails suggest that maybe there once were people living around here, but they are all gone now.
3467: This part of the trail is one of those parts that shows its little use. Grass grows along the trail and aside from the obvious cleared trail, if you were to just look to the sides you would swear to be in outlands, far from any people maybe though, this is best. Those lone travellers that seek isolation would be enchanted by this land. Walking here with the little animals of the land making their noises is so calm and peaceful that you could get used to it.
3468: There are few trees spread vast along this part of the trail. The grass looks to be new. Only small creatures seem to be living in this area. This part of the path seems to be slowly regrowing itself. It is like there once was a battle here. The trail goes onward and is fairly easy to travel along.
3469: This trail is all but forgotten. The trees around here look to be dying. The grass is brown, a few weeds survive. Dead animals lay along the trail. This looks to be where a battle once had been fought. It is hard to tell just how long ago it might have been, but judging from the corpses a couple years. This is not a place to put up camp. The ground is scorched and hard.
3470: The flowers along here are more like weeds. They have very little beauty in them. The trail is overgrown with grass and in some areas mushrooms. This part of the trail does not seem as well kept. Animals though can still be heard making there way through the land. A flock of birds can be seen flying overhead.
3471: This trail at times seem well kept, at others seems abandoned without any reason. Giving you a strange feeling. The flowers along the trail here are beautiful and seem to have been taken good care of. In other areas this does not seem to be the case. What reason for this though you do not know.
3472:
A canoe has been left here.
A canoe has been left here.
A domesticated pony, beast of burden to many, stands here.

The path seems to be leading towards a bridge, this may be a way to cross the river that can be heard in the distance. The land around here is level and seems to be a nice place to set up camp off the main trail. Animals can be heard moving towards the river, most likely to get a drink of water. Making your own mouth water at the thought of it.
3473: There is a lot of snow on the ground.

You are now over the river. Over to the east is the end of the bridge, and safety. You could head out further on the bridge it looks safe enough to go on forward. The wind is blowing slightly, causing the bridge to creak and rock in the wind. Either way you go you might want to think of going that way fast.
3474: Below you is a small calm river that is not that far down. If you look closely you can see what looks like bass and other things swimming. Moving on this bridge is difficult and one at a time is a good idea. To the west you see the end of the bridge and looking back east, you can see the far side swaying in the breeze. Large planks of wood have been made in some parts of the bridge, making it a whole lot more sturdy.
3475: A Path to an Old Rope Bridge
A hardened ranger is walking around, looking for tracks.

You look out east and see what looks like a bridge across the river. You test the bridge and it seems quite sturdy to support you. The river is quietly moving along. Down south you see a path along the river. To the west is a little overgrown trail it leads through the bushes. You can also go north along the river, maybe there is somewhere along the bank to wade across as well. There what looks like a path along the river to the north. You notice some extra support along the sides of the bridge.
3477: The trail borders some hills, the hills seem to go on for quite some ways to the north. The sounds of a small river can be heard not too far towards the east. The trail is quite level here and easy to move along. The best thing to do would be stay on the trail. The trees around the trail are small trees, easy to climb and see what might be in them. If you had the time, you could rest up there in one of the trees, the sun is nice fairly nice around this area.
3478: A boar cub is playing here, and exploring the wide world.

Hiking along here seems quite peaceful, a few birds sing in the trees around you. A couple rabbits jump and scurry off as you crunch down on a few fallen twigs. The ground is fairly even and only a few tree roots penetrate the ground as you walk calmly along this trail.
3479:
A grey wolf is here, snarling aggressively.
A ferocious warg is here, snarling angrily.

The path is very quiet, so quiet the air barely moves across the ground. The grass and shrubs along the path are green and living, filling the still air with their scent. There are few obstacles along the path, the ground is very level and has few rocks along it.
3480: This old trail runs along the bottom of a scarp that separates the plains to the north from the lower lands around the Midgewater Marshes. In many places, deep channels have been cut into the sandstone of the cliff and debris has been deposited across the trail in alluvial fans.
3481: Just to the north, a small but steep cliff rises alongside this trail, while to the southwest, the land slopes gently downward to the fens of the Midgewater Marshes. This trail is littered with debris that has washed down from the plateau above, and in places has been almost obliterated.
3482: This trail runs parallel to a small cliff that rises sharply to the level of the dry plains to the northeast. The rain that falls on the grassy plateau drains rapidly into the marshes to the west, for the scarp is cut in many places by severe channels and gullies.
3483: This trail runs at the foot of a small cliff that demarcates the boundary between the high plains to the northeast and the depression that houses the Midgewater Marshes to the southwest. The cliff is up to sixty feet high in places, and its steep wall is too crumbly to scale.
3484: Strewn with rocks that have washed down from the rocky plains above, this narrow trail takes advantage of a small dry area along the foot of the scarp to avoid the soggy plain to the west. The trail bends from east to north, hugging the cliff all the way.
3485: Following the contour dictated by the foot of the scarp to the north, the path turns from west to south here. The scarp is higher to the east, reaching in some places up to sixty feet above the level of the trail. The trail appears to begin sloping gently upward to the east, finally leaving the marshes behind.
3486: A green frog is here, hopping around.

A large gully cuts into the face of the scarp, leading sharply upward to the north. The trail passes between the gully's mouth and the marsh to the south. The gully itself is heavily vegetated with dense scrub, but it is possible to take advantage of it and climb to the plateau above.
3487: There is a lot of snow on the ground.

The trail is littered with debris that has washed off the scarp to the north. The scarp is cut with many small channels - too steep to climb - that indicate that rainfall quickly drains from the plains to the north into the marshes to the south.
3488: There is a lot of snow on the ground.

This trail of packed earth runs along the northern boundary of the Midge- water, closely following the foot of a scarp that forms the boundary for the high plains to the north. At this point, the trail bends from north to east, nestled in a small dry area between the scarp and marsh.
3489: This trail bends from the west to the south, following the contours of the land. It is bounded to the north and east by a steep scarp about thirty feet high that forms the boundary of the lowlands inhabited by the Midgewater that lies off the southern edge of the trail.
3490: Cutting a thin track through the bracken-carpeted plains is this trail that connects the Men Formen in the west, with the Men Romen to the south. Though no more than a road of packed earth, it is clear that travellers have been here recently, both by the mark of horseshoes and the print of boots. Animal tracks also cross the trail at intervals and droppings dot the trail. Obviously some beasts can survive amongst the indigestible vegetation.
3491: The trail leads through a wide flat area avoiding the hills. There's a little more plant growth here, a few tall bushes growing on a slight rise a few hundred yards east. To the south, bracken takes a stranglehold over the land. Thus there is at least some change to the monotony of a grassy terrain.
3492: The wide open expanse stretches for many miles around. It forms part of the great open wastes of the Lone-lands, only interrupted by the chain of hills to the north and east. The soil is of little use for growing and so has never been cultivated: only grasses and hardy shrubs grow in this wilderness. To the north a small hill breaks the flat view, but it is itself dwarfed by the shadow of Weathertop to the east. A depression has formed on that mighty hill's western flank where one could shelter from the wind. Else one must travel through the wastes.
3493: Though dwarfed by Weathertop to the east, being atop this hill commands a reasonable view of the surrounding area as the flint and chalky soil mean no trees or shrubs grow to obscure the vista.
3494: This is the southern end of the Weather Hills, where the wavy ridge of many miles falls away before the mighty rise of Weathertop. Though this trail often reaches many hundreds of feet above the surrounding flat land, it also dives down into lower passes which break the length of the ridge of hills. Though the trail is cunningly disguised for most parts, the fortifications which it once supplied are still evident to the keen observer from afar. While broken and overgrown, ancient stoneworks remain part of the landscape.
3495: The trail passes over the plain here, its travellers hidden from prying eyes by lines of moss-covered stones on either side of it. Peering between the stones, the traveller can see small hills to the west and south and a larger hill to the northeast. The greatest hill of them all, Weathertop, rises high above you close to the southeast.
3496: Here the trail runs north and south at the western foot of a steep hill. Two lines of boulders, higher than men, protect travellers from prying eyes. In the northwest there is a forest, and beyond it another great hill rises in the distance.
3497: The trail hugs the eaves of a dark wood. It would be difficult for any, even birds, to spy those moving upon it. To the east rise the steep, bare slopes of a great hill, but the trail continues north and south and the bold could venture into the trees to the west.
3498:
A sturdy pack horse is standing here.
A sturdy pack horse is standing here.
A hardened ranger is walking around, looking for tracks.

The trail takes cover under the eaves of a dark wood, following its edge west and south. To the north and the east, great hills rise towards the sky. Mighty Weathertop rises in the south, still some leagues off.
3499: The trail runs north and east, following the edge of the thick forest which grows to the southwest. Beyond the path, steep hillsides rise towards the sky, bereft of all cover save grass. On them you would be easily spied, but here even a bird couldn't spot you.
3500: Here, in a narrow space between the eaves of the dark wood southwest of you, the tall, steep sides of the great hill of you, and the barren, exposed plain stretching into the eastern distance, lies a small trail. It hugs the edge of the forest, taking shelter from unfriendly eyes under its boughs. The old trees grow thickly but the trail has somehow remained clear.
3501: The trail runs east-west, hugging the bottom of a steep, rocky slope at the base of the hill to the north, and following a small, clear space between the hillside and the dark eves of the thick wood which lies to the south. A small patch of sky is visible between the hillside and the treetops.
3502: The trail runs east-west, following the bottom of the hill to the north and keeping clear of the dark wood to the south. The northward slope is more gentle here than elsewhere, and you could walk up it onto the shoulder of the hill. The trail is lined on both sides by great boulders. The moss and lichen on their sides speaks of how long they have been here. From between them it is obvious that they were placed here with a purpose, by folk who wished to travel the line of the hills without being seen.
3503: The trail curves around north and east as it rounds the corner of the great hill. A foothill rises to the west. Southwards, flat plains stretch to the horizon their end marked by a dark line of trees to your southeast. Then you follow the trail into a small hollow in the plain, and your view of the lands about is blocked. A few small, thorny bushes grow here as well as the grass and weeds.
3504: The great hill in the east slopes downwards much more gently here than elsewhere, and its sides are covered with grass standing several feet tall. The trail takes advantage of this, climbing a little way up the hillside to follow a narrow north-south ravine. You could walk up the shoulder of the hill. To your west the great, flat plains begin, and a foothill rises, its rounded top level with the trail, to the southwest.
3505: A colourful butterfly is fluttering around here.

The trail runs west and south, close beneath the steep banks of two of the Weather Hills. A pass between them leads up, eastwards, towards the green- grown stones of an old wall. The slope of the pass is gentle, but its sides are steep and high. The green plains stretch off towards the southwest and a small foothill perhaps a league away.
3506: Here a hidden trail runs under the shoulder of the great hill to the north. People travelling on it are protected from the vision of travellers on the plains or inquisitive birds by a line of great boulders which look from the outside like simply more rocks on this barren, rocky stretch of hillside. The slope north of you is almost vertical: nothing could climb it, and someone one the hilltop above would have to come to the cliff-edge and look straight down to see you. Barren plains stretch into the distance to the west, but southwards a small hill rises from them a little more than a league away.
3507: Here the trail runs closely under the steep slope of the Weather Hills. Its builders placed a line of boulders along the trail where it rises into view of the plains, and they protect any travellers here from peering eyes. The trail continues north into a dell between the great hill to your northeast and a foothills to your northwest. Eastwards it follows the bottom of the hill.
3508: The old trail runs north-south through a desolate valley between one of the Weather Hills to the east and one of their foothills to the west. Thin grass grows here, and stones, and weeds, but nothing else. The eight hundred foot slope to your east is too steep to climb, but at least a watcher on the top of the hill would have to come to the edge and look straight down to see you. You could easily climb the much smaller hill to the west.
3509: The hidden valley between the Weather Hills and their foothill turns west-south here. At one place a faint trail leads to a narrow pass east through the Weather Hills. You can see fortifications at the top of the pass, although even at this distance the green of vines on the stone walls shows them to have been long abandoned. Perhaps this trail was built by the same people who built the fortress, for the trail would have been an excellent route to move men and supplies there swiftly and without the foe's knowledge.
3510: The trail travels east-west, along the bottom of a small valley between a foothill to the south and the main ridge of the Weather Hills to the north. There are a few bushes here, as well as the grass and rocks. You cannot see the tops of the hills because of the walls of the valley, but they also protect you from being seen by any watchers.
3511: A fat rabbit is here, chewing on some grass.

Here a hidden trail runs under the shoulder of the great hill to the northeast. People travelling on it are protected from the vision of travellers on the plains or inquisitive birds by a line of great boulders which look, from the outside, like a few more rocks on this barren, rocky stretch of hillside. To the south, great, barren plains recede into the distance, while a small hill rises to the west. The trail drops into a valley in the east and continues north into a small dell.
3512: The trail runs north-south at the foot of the great hill to your east. A line of great boulders protects travellers on the path from being spied upon by creatures on the plains to the west or birds in the air above them. The plains are stony, but support a thin growth of grass and thistles. They stretch to the western horizon. Another grey-green hill rises to the north.
3529: The grassy downs roll out of sight in all directions as they gradually emerge from the thick foliage in the east. Large stones and rocks naturally form a wall to the south. With sporadic pockets of tiny trees and dense undergrowth in certain low-lying regions, the grass is green and luxuriant.
3764: The entrance is leading to a courtyard northwards, and there are hallways both east and west of here. All the walls and the roof are made of stone, and some old weapons and shields are hanging on the walls above the hallways. Some strange sounds, like men moving around, can be heard above. The ground is covered with old cobblestones. Heavy usage of horses and men, have worn out the stones.
3765: The room is pretty dark because of the rather small opening westwards, and a door northwards that lets no light through. The roof is made of solid stone, as is the floor. The floor seems less used here than west of here, probably because no mounts and pets have been allowed here. Silence fills the room, as nothing can be heard in any direction due to the heavy door northwards, and the low opening westwards.
3766: This ancient hallway contains more luxury and the carvings are more detailed than the other rooms in the eastern parts of the castle. North of here an ancient door blocks the way. The door is solid and some carvings can be seen on it. In the south-western corner of the room a stair leads upwards to a tower seen above. Some lanterns hang on the walls around the room, and they give off enough light so that each corner of the room is lit.
3767: Rubb Grumm is standing here, watching you carefully as you enter.

This is a large room, which contains a big table with a dozen chairs around it. The table stands in one end of the room, while the rest of the room seems rather empty, besides some old maps and drawings on the walls. The walls are made of brick like stones, still the room is warm and comfortable. One of the reasons for that might be the wooden floor.
3768:
A Rhudaurian guard is here, patrolling the Castle.
A Rhudaurian guard is here, patrolling the Castle.
A Rhudaurian guard is here, patrolling the Castle.

This is where the guards of the castle live and spend their time when they have no assignment. When not on duty the guards occupy themselves with games or attending to their accoutrements. The men each have a bed and locker for their belongings including their armour weapons and uniforms, but precious little else. In addition to lodgings, it contains rooms for meals and training.
3769: A large fountain, made from grey stone, pours water from its centre.

A large squarelike area that clearly shows indications of heavy use. The sturdy cobblestones worn by both the weather and the frequent visits of many people. In the centre a large grey fountain can be seen. Its clear water flowing steadily. The massive front gates and their overgate structure loom above the southern portion. To the east lies the old and well used stables while north of here the exit to the Great Halls can be seen. West of here the lies a large brick building, housing the guards of the castle.
3770: Placed on the eastern portion of the Courtyard lies the wood building that houses the mounts and pets of the inhabitants. Made out of thick pines and with a thatched roof it makes a safe lodging. In connection to the stable a small paddock can be seen, where the mounts get their daily exercise. The keeper of this lodging is the Grumm family. A family that has outlasted many of the noble lines of Rhudaur.
3771: This hallway is light, as it is lit up by several lanterns on each wall. South of here a huge door blocks the entrance, while a hall appears to the north. The stones used to make the walls here are not as dark as in the rest of the castle, which indicates that this part was finished at a latter stage. A carpet covers the floor which is made of stone as in the rest of the castle. The temperature here is rather cold.
3773: Carved from an anomalous lobe of maroon-streaked crimson stone, the hall resembles a chapel of retrospection. Its walls, alcoves, pilasters, and arching vault are carved in mannish forms whose faces resembles the old rulers of Rhudaur. The floor is covered with a thick red carpet. Upon this carpet stands a large roundish oaktable. Here the valiant heroes of Rhudaur have their meetings, discussing different news from the world outside. Around on the walls different signs can be seen. The entrance is secured by a large oakdoor, covered with detailed carvings.
3774: A Rhudaurian guard is here, patrolling the Castle.

Like the western tower this one has the same openings high on the wall. The openings let some light in so the castle is fairly lit. In addition to this some lanterns are placed around in the tower so it can be lit at night. An opening westwards leads to the battlements above the gate, and a stairway, leading to the top of the tower, can be seen north of here.
3775: A large bulletin board, entitled "Mages' Guild Board", is mounted here.

The stairway leads upward, toward the top of the tower. Despite the long stairs this chamber seems rather empty. The only thing of interest that can be seen here is a board, mounted upon the wall. The walls themselves are constructed with brick-like stones, greyish in colour. To the south the main floor of the eastern tower can be seen, through an arched doorway, and through the small square window in the west wall, the castle grounds spread out below.
3776: A Rhudaurian guard is here, patrolling the Castle.

The cave contains several signs that tell about the background of the inhabitants. They tell about the place of roaring red gold, of its history, inhabitants, famous places, and more. The cave itself is cold, and nothing covers the floor. Lanterns are the only light source, giving out a dim light. Due to its round form, the cave has no corners. South of here a larger hall can be seen, and you notice some light from a fireplace.
3777: A large, dusty alcove sits in a wall, smelling of soot.

This huge hall has several lanterns mounted on the walls, and a fireplace gives off some light. The hall is about ten times thirty meters in size and made of stone. The fireplace provides necessary heating. Around on the walls several signs tells stories from battles the inhabitants participated in. Some pictures reconstructing the battles can also be seen on the western wall. North of here a small cave appears, while a hallway leads southwards.
3778:
A follower stands on vigilant guard here.
A follower stands on vigilant guard here.
A sorcerer is waiting here to teach his art.

The height between the floor and the roof is quite low here, not more than six feet at the most. The floor is made of wood, which squeaks as you move across the room. In one corner stands a desk and a chair, which have obviously been used recently, and small square windows set in each wall offer an excellent view of the castle and its surroundings. A narrow stairway leads to the main floor of the tower, below.
3779: A large eagle soars above you.

From here it's possible to see down on the path and the wooden bridge in front of the castle. Below on the other side lies the courtyard, and noise of people and horses can be heard. The battlements are made of huge brick like stones, while the floor is made of wood. Eagles are circling above, looking for small animals in the dense vegetation around the castle. Towers can be seen both east and west of here.
3780: A Rhudaurian guard is here, patrolling the Castle.

The tower contains a few small square-like openings high on the wall. They are high up on the wall so that it is impossible to see out through them. The walls are made of stones formed like bricks. East of here there is an opening that leads out on some battlements. Further east another tower like this one can be seen. North of here a stairway can be seen, leading upwards to the top of the tower. Stairs lead downwards to the lower parts of the castle.
3781: A large bulletin board, entitled "Clerics' Guild Board", is mounted here.

The stairway leads upward, offering access to the top floor of the tower. There is almost nothing in this chamber, save for a heavy board, which is mounted to one of the grey stone walls. Through an elegantly arched doorway, to the south, the main floor of the tower can be seen, and through the small square window in the east wall, the castle grounds can be spied below.
3782:
A disciple and follower of the priest stands here.
A disciple and follower of the priest stands here.
A haggard man dressed in tattered robes is here, willing to teach his art.

From this lofty room it is possible to see much of Fornost and Fornost Erain. Looking downward through the small square windows affords a view of the castle courtyard to the east, and of the castle surroundings. The chamber is low- roofed, such that anyone more than about six feet in height would have to stoop to avoid banging their head on the ceiling, and the only way out of here is via a narrow stairway, leading downward. The room contains only a simple bed, a small desk, and two old chairs.
3783:
A mailbox stands here stuffed full of messages.
Bura Grumm is here looking after the Castle.

This room has been built from sturdy dark stone. The rock has been cut out and brought here from the granite filled mountains of Rhudaur. Neatly fitted and polished with great care its difficult to see that the room has been made by seperate stones. From this hall several doors can be seen, leading to the private rooms of the castle inhabitants. No hangings or storied webs, nor any things of woven stuff or wood can be seen in this solemn room.
3851: Ruined Park under the High Cliff
A Dunadan soldier is here busily performing his duties.

You make your way through the increasingly dense vegetation and reach the foot of the cliff. Its face is sheer, as it runs about a hundred yards straight up. There is absolutely no way one could scale the cliff at this side. On its top lies the even taller tower of the citadel. For a very brief moment you get the sensation it is all falling down on you! No wonder the citizens of Fornost change the subject whenever the old castle is brought up! South of here you can spot a section of the city walls.
3852: A placid pond is here, inviting you to take a refreshing drink.

This pond lies just below the base of the cliff. A small, decorative stream of water flows through a hole in the side of the cliff a dozen or so feet above the surface, and gently plunges down into the pond.
3853:
A Dunadan soldier is here busily performing his duties.
A Dunadan soldier is here busily performing his duties.

You stand among some ruins, at the edge of what seems once to have been a magnificent park. But that was obviously long ago, and centuries of free growth have turned it into quite a wilderness. Westwards past this wilderness a high, black cliff thrusts into the sky.
3854:
There is an old street-lamp on the border of the street.
An old man is walking around, cleaning up.

You are just inside the gates of the town, with a wild park to the west and an irregular clump of buildings in the north and east. There seem to be no major roads here except for the one you're standing on, The King's Road, which leads north further into the city and south out through the main gates. To the east lies a building with thick walls, but you can't see any entrance on this side.
3855: Under the Wall, between the Gates

An experienced Dunadan officer is standing here, keeping things under control.
A Dunadan gateguard is standing here.
An experienced Dunadan officer is standing here, keeping things under control.
A Dunadan gateguard is standing here.

You are standing here between two portals in a cobblestone passage under the outer wall of the city of Fornost. The southern one is a portcullis, usually raised in times of peace. The gate to the north is iron-clad and looks extremely massive. Glancing up you notice machicolations through which hot oil or missiles can be rained down upon an invading enemy. A bronze plaque is fixed on the wall.
3856:
A sturdy target for arrows, made out of thatch, stands here.
A Dunadan soldier is here busily performing his duties.

The small cobbled yard is surrounded by walls on all sides. Some soldiers are perfecting their skills at swordplay under the supervision of a higher officer. An archery range has been constructed towards the south wall, for the Dunadan scouts and hunters to practice at. North is a gate leading out of the garrison, and east the headquarters of Fornost's forces.
3857:
A sturdy trained horse is standing here.
A sturdy pack horse is standing here.

You enter a fairly large yard, most of its cobblestones covered with dirt. The building that occupies the eastern and northern ends of the square is a two-story, red painted barn. Two double doors allow you to enter in any of those directions. Between the doors is a large stack of yellow hay. The northern entrance has the words 'Gordun's Fine Animals' painted over it in big letters. Now the building to the south has thick walls of stone, with very few and very small windows, almost like an extension of the city's wall. You see soldiers passing in and out of its doorway.
3858:
A rather dirty young boy is here, ready to tend to the stable.
A Dunadan soldier is here busily performing his duties.

Here you can turn over your mount to the care of the people at the stables. Although the building itself doesn't seem to be in a very good condition, with large parts of the ceiling and walls missing, you think your mount will do just fine here. His needs are obviously not as high as yours. A small note sits on one of the walls.
3859: You step out on the cranking wooden floor of this large, high barn. The big doors swung open easily since several of the planks making up the walls are missing. This makes the environment in here much the same as the one outside. For all sorts of animals, this is a temporary home. Their many different scents reach your nose and the combination is not a pleasant smell! There is a sign placed on one of the walls.
3860: An old tailor is sitting here, working with a piece of fabric.

This shop is filled with fabric of different colours and varying materials. The tailor sits on a stool in a corner, while his apprentices are busy measuring out the customers. There is a note on one of the walls.
3861: You walk among the trees and bushes, just below the high cliff harbouring the old citadel. Although large parts of the city have been rebuilt, the Dunedain rangers have yet to reach the castle. It sits high up there. Strong, dark and silent. It suddenly makes you feel VERY small. You release the castle from your thoughts as you turn your attention to the beauty of the surrounding wilderness instead. The King's road can be seen a bit east, through the trees.
3862: There is an old street-lamp on the border of the street.

This broad road looks very old, and it is clear that it has been patched up recently. This is also your general impression of the city and its walls. To the south you can see the main gates. Just east is a small square. A park lies to the west directly below the high cliff on which the old castle of Fornost is situated.
3863: This staircase leads in winding steps up the tower beside the main gate of the city. Although the steps are relatively wide, they are also quite old and worn out, which makes them slippery. There is nothing to hold on to, so watch your step!
3864: This is where many of the soldiers keep themselves occupied when they are not on duty. Some of them play cards, some read while others just chat. A huge wooden table dominates the room and several chairs are set around it. The room has no windows, but there are a couple of paintings of famous battles. On one of them you see the hordes of Angmar storming a city which might be Fornost. You can't be sure though, because all you can see is a part of a city wall.
3865: This is a huge sleeping room with 15 two story beds. Cupboards for the private possessions of the soldiers are along the walls and paintings of more or less dressed women are attached to them.
3870: A heavy desk, made of solid oak, stands here.

You enter a small but neat and luxuriously furnished room. A red carpet covers the floor, which creaks as you move over it. Small windows high on the northern wall allows light to slip in on sunny days. The largest part of the room is occupied by an old, heavy desk make of oak, covered with papers and maps. There are also some comfortable chairs and a small cabinet containing liqueur in fine bottles.
3871:
A Dunadan soldier is here busily performing his duties.
An experienced Dunadan officer is standing here, keeping things under control.
A secretary is sitting at the desk.

The corridor widens up a bit, and you see a small niche with a desk in it. To the east you see a very comfortably furnished office, and in contrast with this there is a solid metal door on the southern wall - obviously leading to the jail. A sign sits on the secretary's table, and a notice hangs beside it.
3872:
A Dunadan soldier is here busily performing his duties.
A Dunadan soldier is here busily performing his duties.

You walk through a plain, simple corridor that runs east and west. There are small windows high on the southern wall, but they don't let much light in, so there are burning torches attached to the wall every here and there. A door is in the northern wall.
3874:
A large bulletin board, entitled "Tales", is mounted here.
There is a lit street-lamp on the border of the street, illuminating the area.

As the street reaches the thick walls of Fornost's garrison, it makes a sharp turn to the east. A large canopy shelters the corner. The wild street-trade you encountered along this street becomes more specialized, as this seem to be the place where jesters, musicians, and artists demonstrate their skills, in hope of selling their services.
3875:
There is an old street-lamp on the border of the street.
A citizen-mercenary is here, waiting for a job.

Walking along this street of trade and commerce, you get the feeling that after a long struggle, good times are finally coming along for the inhabitants, with the promise of prosperity just around the corner. Craftsmen's alley continues east and west.
3876: There is a lit street-lamp on the border of the street, illuminating the area.

This must be one of the quieter places on Craftsmen's Alley. Not that it means this place is peaceful: the many voices of the street-mongers are replaced by the noise created as metal hits metal, coming from a smithy north of the street. Thick, black smoke rises from its chimney.
3877:
There is a lit street-lamp on the border of the street, illuminating the area.
A Dunadan soldier is here busily performing his duties.
An experienced Dunadan officer is standing here, keeping things under control.

You arrive this old and crumbling gateway, yet another monument of the city's past. It bridges the northern side of the street with the southern, where the city's garrison is nowadays. Wherever it once led, whatever building it once was the entrance to, is now long gone and forgotten.
3878:
There is an old street-lamp on the border of the street.
A man passes by, intent on his business.

This street shines out in contrast to its dingy neighbourhood, like a fire in a forest; and with its freshly painted shutters, well-polished brasses, and general cleanliness and gaiety, it instantly catches and pleases the eye of the beholder.
3879:
There is a lit street-lamp on the border of the street, illuminating the area.
An old man is walking around, cleaning up.
A woman is here, looking for someone to chat with.

The street runs north and south along the city's eastern wall. You can see rangers patrolling the battlements above you while narrow, high houses line the other side of the road. To the north lies the heart of the city, the Market Square.
3881:
There is an old street-lamp on the border of the street.
A rugged-looking man is standing here.
A citizen-mercenary is here, waiting for a job.

You are standing in the shadow of the high city walls, below one of the few sections that hasn't needed any rebuilding. The scent of freshly baked bread grabs hold of your head and turns it north, where you discover a tiny bakery.
3882:
The Baker looks at you calmly, wiping flour from his face with one hand.
An insolent scholar is here, pondering.

You are standing inside a small bakery. A sweet scent of freshly baked bread fills the room. You feel hungry as you look at all these fine breads well arranged on their shelves. A tidy sign is nailed to the wall.
3883: A mailbox stands here stuffed full of messages.

You have entered a big hall with a great deal of activity. People are constantly coming in, doing their business, and leaving thereafter. You can check here if somebody wrote a letter to you, or write one yourself to your friends in other cities far away.
3884: A large bulletin board, entitled "Board of the Free Peoples", is mounted here.

This is where Fornost's magistrates gather, debate, and sometimes even come to a decision! However they don't appear to be in session today, but there is a board on which you can read other peoples opinions, and perhaps express some of your own.
3885: There is an old street-lamp on the border of the street.

Although this place is called market square, you cannot see any signs of that particular activity going on here. Either the markets occur on special days, and this isn't one of them, or maybe the name just stuck from the old days. Here on the northern end of the square you can see the building which contain the city-council's meeting place and the post office. A large red sign can be seen hanging over the entrance to a house on the southern end of the square.
3887: Oh, what a display of shields and fine protective clothing! Shopping here is a must for every true warrior and all other people who have to fight for their living. Especially wonderful are the glittering chain mail clothes in bronze and silver.
3888: This is the place where you can buy excellent weapons, new or used, as you like, in every price range. The weaponsmith will also mend your old sword if you are a little low on cash right now. A large sign is pinned on the wall behind the counter.
3890:
A circular stone well has been built here.
There is an old street-lamp on the border of the street.
Fardur the guide is here, leaning on his walking-stick.
A citizen-mercenary is here, waiting for a job.

You stand at an old well, which apparently still serves its purpose, as people arrive to fill their barrels, pots or waterskins. You hear laughter and singing through a window in house to the south, but you cannot see a thing, for the curtains are closed, and the entrance is a bit west, under a bright red sign.
3892: A large bulletin board, entitled "News of Arda", is mounted here.

Fornost's citizens don't seem like a very religious lot to you, but of course they don't totally ignore their creators. This circular temple contain statues and portraits of the Valar and the Maiar, but also men and elves the citizens feel worthy of such an honour. A board here contains all known prophesies and commandments the creators have laid down on the shoulders of mankind.
3893:
There are three apples here.
There is an old street-lamp on the border of the street.

The footpath you are standing on takes you to a small, round sanctuary if you continue east on it. The city wall is just north and houses block your way south. Turning your attention to the gardens for a moment, it seems like the gardener is a true master of his profession. The lawns are all very green and neat, the various bushes well trimmed, and the flowers have just the right colours. Clearly a case of quality before quantity!
3894:
There is an old street-lamp on the border of the street.
A well-crafted white fountain is here, water pouring forth from it.

Judging from the state of the neighbouring buildings and streets this is one of the finest, if not the finest, areas in the city. There are no traces of trash or ruins, and while the buildings around the square might be old, they have all been restored to mint-condition. Pleasant vegetation can be seen to the east, and streets lead south and west. A massive rectangular pedestal bearing a bronze plaque occupies the centre of the square.
3895:
There is an old street-lamp on the border of the street.
A citizen-mercenary is here, waiting for a job.
An old man is walking around, cleaning up.

With the city wall at your back, you stand facing the south, contemplating the architecture of the large building in front of you. A short but wide flight of stairs leads up to its entrance, which lie past a row of massive columns. The building is rectangular with windows and ornaments on the walls. You realise you are standing outside the famous old Library.
3896: There is a lit street-lamp on the border of the street, illuminating the area.

You note yet another sign of the neighbourhoods prosperity; this street is the only one you've seen so far where the cobblestones are clean and free of the usual mud, dust or trash which can be seen everywhere else.
3897: There is a lit street-lamp on the border of the street, illuminating the area.

Guild Street runs east and west with the city wall on its northern side and a row of important-looking houses on its southern. This seem to be the place where all the various guild of the area are situated: the cooper, potter, mason and shoemaker guilds can be seen further down the street. Most notable though, the warrior-guild is just south of here.
3898:
A weapons rack stands against the wall.
Huor of Dor-lomin is standing here, ready to teach his arts.

This is the place where martial skills are learned and perfected. At the walls hang different kinds of weapons, mostly slashing, so you can practice all the associated fighting techniques. The teacher here is said to be a specialist of the parry skill, so he might show some new tricks even to experienced fighters. From here you can go back north to Guild Street. A staircase leads up to a room that seems suitable for a little break after the training or perhaps a chat with some fellow warriors.
3902:
An experienced Dunadan officer is standing here, keeping things under control.
A Dunadan gateguard is standing here.
A Dunadan gateguard is standing here.
Torbik the Hobbit is standing here.

You have arrived at the gateway which takes you through the wall to the old not yet reconstructed part of this ancient town. This wall was raised to shield the citizens of new Fornost from the shadows that still reign among the ruins of the city's western parts and the old castle. Every now and then soldiers open the gate to allow for rangers to pass through. Some of the returning ones are bleeding and have obviously been fighting quite recently. The words 'ENTER AT YOUR OWN RISK' are written in large letters on the gate.
3903:
A Dunadan soldier is here busily performing his duties.
An experienced Dunadan officer is standing here, keeping things under control.
A Dunadan soldier is here busily performing his duties.
You enter a small cabin which serves as shelter for the soldiers posted at the gate. The only furniture is a table and some chairs.
3904: The King's Road by the Palisade

A beggar is here, asking for a few coins.
A rugged-looking man is standing here.
A Dunadan soldier is here busily performing his duties.
An experienced Dunadan officer is standing here, keeping things under control.
A wealthy merchant is slowly strolling around here.
A simple servant quietly walks around, performing his duties.

You have come into the middle of the slums of Fornost. What a shabbiness! Bitter faces are looking out of half dilapidated houses, children are playing in the dirty gutters. You can see beggars here, starving. Give them a few coppers, they need it to survive. To the south you can see the poorhouse. A palisade runs from the northern city wall to the base of the cliff which lie a bit south, cutting the city in two parts.
3905:
A sturdy bed made from solid oak lies here, covered in warm blankets.
A beggar is here, asking for a few coins.
A beggar is here, asking for a few coins.
A Dunadan soldier is here busily performing his duties.

This is the place where the poor people of Fornost can get a blanket and a hard plank bed for the night. It's very depressing here, and you hope you won't end up in a place like this. From time to time a charitable woman comes to drop off some old breadcrumbs.
3906:
Olly is standing here, cleaning some cups.
A Dunadan soldier is here busily performing his duties.

This is a small, shabby place. The room is dimly lit and the customers all seem very mysterious, keeping low profiles at their tables. This also goes for the owner of the place. He glares suspiciously at you as you enter, and all conversation is halted. Then, as your eyes meet his, he quickly returns to cleaning some cups. Not a very hospitable place it would seem!
3907: A rugged-looking man is standing here.

The road runs through this part of the city, which seem more ruined than rebuilt. At some places evidence of on-going construction is visible; scaffolds and strange machinery, shovels and other tools can be seen. To the west, the road turns again as it reaches a wooden wall.
3909: This part of the King's Road is very solitary and in spite of the low growl of Fornost all around, very silent. Small sounds carry far. The domestic sounds present in houses on the east side of the street are clearly audible and the echoing footsteps of an approaching person precede him by a long time.
3910:
There is an old street-lamp on the border of the street.
A singing, happy drunk is staggering about here.
A Dunadan soldier is here busily performing his duties.
A singing, happy drunk is staggering about here.

Along the street you see the typical houses of Fornost, high but very narrow stone buildings, with roofs either flat, or slanted ones made of dried grass. There were probably wooden buildings once, but they have failed to stand the test of time and where they once stood there are now only hollow gaps.
3911: There is an old street-lamp on the border of the street.

This is the junction of the King's Road, which runs north to south, and the Short Street that leads eastward into the heart of Fornost where busy merchants and shoppers can be heard going about their business. Beyond that lies the Crown of Arnor Inn, where travellers and citizens alike tend to gather. Though the people of the city have a rough and ready look about them, for the most part the city is quite clean and well-maintained.
3912: There is an old street-lamp on the border of the street.
The road continues north and south. West, an overgrown park spreads out beneath a high cliff. East of the road lies the houses of the common Fornost citizen, in a somewhat shabby neighbourhood.
3913: There is an old street-lamp on the border of the street.

This street is exactly what its name says, short. It runs from the Kings Road in the west to Market Square at the centre of the city. Along the road on both sides narrow, tall houses can be seen. To the north, a large old building dominates the view because of a regal look that gives it an almost holy appearance.
3914:
A sign made of polished brass is on the wall.
A clerk sits here, lazily tending to the thermal baths.

You are standing in the reception area of the thermal baths. The air is warm and moist, carrying with it the scents of all sorts of perfumes and oils. A mosaic picture of Ulmo, lord of the waters, covers the floor.
3915: Aaaaahhhh! You slide into the warm water of this large, shallow pool and suddenly feel totally relaxed! The water comes from a natural warm spring. It has a light-yellowish colour, and smells slightly of sulphur. The warm water and the moist air make you feel very sleepy ...
3916: An insolent scholar is here, pondering.

As you enter the room, making some noise, you get angry looks from the scholars in here. They are all very silent with conversations held in whispering voices. Most of the people in the room are sitting at special writing-tables, copying the works of long dead masters.
3917: A huge clock is standing here.

You have entered the legendary Great Library of Fornost, which before its ruin nine hundred years ago held the largest collection of books and scrolls in this part of the world. Nowadays, it is not nearly as impressive, although once again the library has managed to gain a good reputation among human scholars. A massive staircase leads up to the collection itself.
3918:
There is an old street-lamp on the border of the street.
A little boy is here, running around.
A little dog is here.

This small passage is so narrow you can barely bring a horse through it. It connects two squares; Market in the south and Arnor just north. On either side of the alley, tall, gaunt houses shoot up against the sky, with time-stained fronts and windows that have grown dim with age.
3919: There is an old street-lamp on the border of the street.

This is the north-western corner of the square, where a very narrow alley leads north, away from the crowds, into quieter parts of the city. The city wall can be seen east of the square, giving a sudden and unwelcome reminder of the city's violent past. The entrance to 'The Traveller's Shop' is to the west.
3920: There is a lit street-lamp on the border of the street, illuminating the area.

This is the centre of the new, rebuilt Fornost. A few short years ago this place was abandoned and deserted like the rest of this ancient city, but it has already developed a thriving trade. The inhabitants are all doing well it seems, and hoping to do better still. Trays of fish and fruit indicate that the shop west of here is a grocery of some sort. A street leading south plunges a hole in the otherwise massive front of stores and houses that border the square.
3921: There is an old street-lamp on the border of the street.
