You walk in a narrow alley, bordered with two and three story houses, tightly packed together. The houses' ground floors are often used as shops or working areas for the craftsmen this street is so suitably named after, while the families live on the upper floors.
3922:
There is a lit street-lamp on the border of the street, illuminating the area.
An old man is walking around, cleaning up.

You have ended up in the chaotic circus of street-commerce. The loud voices of fishmongers, butchers, blacksmiths, carpenters, or just anybody with something to sell, makes normal conversation practically impossible. You try and quicken your pace, but it is useless; the street is just too crowded. You can escape the crowd west, into a small tailor's shop.
3923: There is an old street-lamp on the border of the street.

This short street runs in an east-west fashion. The town's gates lie to the west while the Market Square and the Crown of Arnor Inn can be found to the east, on either side of the street, houses line the road. Rows of laundry stretch between the houses and in some cases over the road, the larger items catching the wind and flapping noisily.
3924: A large grocer is here, waiting to buy or sell some goods.

This is a large, spacious shop with enough room for all sorts of goods. You see shelves full of food, partly ordinary, partly exotic, imported from foreign lands and grown and produced by other races. You see fruits and vegetables, spices and herbs. A small sign hangs over the counter.
3925:
A large grocer is here, waiting to buy or sell some goods.
A man passes by, intent on his business.

In this shop you can buy all that you might need on your travels or adventures. On the walls and shelves you see lanterns, sacks, ropes, bags, shovels and all kinds of gadgets and stuff that could prove to be useful out there on the roads or in the wilderness. There is a sign on the counter.
3926:
An old innkeeper stands here, talking to some guests.
A man passes by, intent on his business.

As you enter this large rectangular room, you remember hearing good words about 'The Crown' on your travels, and the first impressions are not disappointing. The room extends further east, where food and drinks are being served. In the middle of the room's southern wall a fire is sparkling on a hearth. A flight of stairs leads up to the customers' private chambers. It is clear however that the arrangements would be made down here, should you want to rent a room.
3928:
A small oaken table has been set here.
A Dunadan stands here, dressed in the garb of a woodsman.

This room is small, but the lack of clutter makes it appear more spacious. On the wall several maps of the nearby forests hang. A table stands in the centre of the room. A single door leads out to the south.
3929:
A large torch lies here among the dust.
A small, loyal beagle is here, eager to please.
A small, loyal beagle is here, eager to please.
A ranger stands quietly here, willing to teach his knowledge of woodcraft.

Here, people can learn much to help them survive the harsh wilderness. Skills such as tracking, riding and other useful skills are taught by experienced Dunadan rangers, who some consider to be the most knowledgeable in the ways of the wild in all of Arda.
3930: The people come here to watch and perhaps put some money on fighting animals. Often roosters, but not always. It could be a bear fighting some dogs, or maybe a captured orc, weakened by the sun. The winner lives to fight again another day. The loser of course isn't that lucky.
3932: Along the smooth granite walls, some small closets and a chest of drawers are situated. A large cavebear-fur covers most of the floor, complete with paws and head. Right in front of the entrance, a man-sized mirror hangs beside a large clothes hanger filled with worn cloaks and shirts.
3933: A rabbit is here eyeing your presence warily.

Having left the civilised part of Fornost, you now stand in front of something that looks more like a sparse forest, than a ruined city. Time has long since caught up with the old houses, and grass and bushes cover them. However, the road you are standing on still seems to be traversable westwards, among the ruins.
3934: Just to the east, the wooden palisade rises, to protect the inhabitants of Fornost from whatever lives on this side. To the north, you see the remains of the King's Road that once ran from the main gates to the castle that lies on the cliff that towers above you to the west and the south.
3935: The corpse of a bandit is lying here.

Here, just behind the wooden wall, that the citizens of "new" Fornost put up, the scene is quite different. Remains of old houses lie as piles of stone blocks on the ground, overgrown by grass and small trees. Nothing remains to remind you of the beautiful city that once stood here, except the old castle, that still stands on a high hill to the south-west. To the north, the old city wall still stands, protecting the world outside from the dangers that lie within.
3936: Moss clad stones are the only sign of this part of Arthedain's old capital. No man has lived here for over nine hundred years, and only small animals run around between the rocks these days.
3937: There is certainly nothing royal about this road any more. The square white stones that once formed an easily travelled road, slowly climbing up to the castle above, now are cracked and crooked.
3938:
The corpse of a tree-snake is lying here.
The corpse of a tree-snake is lying here.
A boar cub is playing here, and exploring the wide world.

Grass and bushes cover the ruins of Fornost Erain. Looking around you, you notice the ruined road to the south, the city wall to the north, and nothing but more ruins in the other directions. Further south, you see the dark castle, overlooking the once great city. A large tree stands here between the rocks.
3939: To the north you see the only real evidence of the old city that once stood here. It is a part of the outer walls of Fornost, that has survived the long years since the invasion of the Witch-king. To the south, there is a small, withered road, and beyond it, you see the ominous Royal Castle of Fornost.
3940: The road still runs straight from the east to the west, slowly climbing its way up on the hill that the western part of Fornost was once built upon. Grass, bushes and small trees stand everywhere around you in the ruined houses.
3941: It seems that you should be careful if you wish to travel in this area, for stones and rubble litter the ground, half-hidden among the grass and the tall weeds, ready to trip you. These broken fragments of larger stones are all that remains of the old city of Fornost, and now this place is home only to the unseen creatures who can be faintly heard, scurrying through the undergrowth.
3942: Once, houses bordered this road, but they all lie in ruins these days. The road is sort of intact though, and can take you north or west from here. Looking south, you see the old castle sitting silently on the hill, its high towers stretching high into the sky.
3943: A boar cub is playing here, and exploring the wide world.

The road bends here. To the east, it leads to the safety of the civilised parts of Fornost, and to the south, it slowly climbs around the hill from which the old castle looks down on the ruins that surround you.
3944: The high wall of Fornost still stands to the north, preventing you from any attempt to go that way. To the south you see an old road leading towards the large hill with the abandoned castle on top. Looking west, you see what might be an old house still standing against the wall.
3945: The Guild of the Black Dagger

A large bulletin board, entitled "Thieves' Guild", is mounted here.
A thief is waiting here to teach his art.
This is the place for thieves to learn their evil abilities. You see some assassins practising their skills, and in a few weeks they will be ready to go out and use their knowledge on the streets.
3946: Entrance to the Black Dagger Guild

A thief is here looking for some stranger to rob.
A thief is here looking for some stranger to rob.
A thief is here looking for some stranger to rob.
A thief is here looking for some stranger to rob.

You have found a secret room beneath the old ruin. There is very little light in here and you sense people hiding in the deep shadows around you. A black dagger with a neatly carved hilt is fastened to the door that leads east of here. Few men have seen this place and lived to tell about it.
3947: This must be one of the very few houses that have lasted since the city was virtually destroyed. Its northern wall is actually the old city wall, and you can leave the house through the empty doorway to the east. The floor is covered with dirt and grass, and as you look up, you see that the entire ceiling is gone.
3948:
A fallow deer is grazing peacefully here.
A vicious little bandit advances towards you.
All around you, you see grass-covered piles of stones, but to the north of you stands what appears to be a fairly intact house. To the south you can see the ruined remains of the King's Road.
3949: The road runs east and west here. Looking south, you can see a pile of many stones - obviously the remnants of a larger house. The remains of a wall prevents you from going very far in that direction. A small stone catches your eye.
3950: A dark intangible shadow turns to face you.

This small height once was a place of death. The Dunedain never penalized anyone with death, but orcs hung people in large numbers - a far more merciful fate than the one that could await you at their torturers in the dungeons of the old, ruined castle that towers south of here.
3951: This street once led to the gallows hill just east of here. Now, no one has used it for over eight hundred years, and it lies in ruins. The cobblestones that used to be perfectly lined up now lie in a mess, and most of them are overgrown by thick, brownish grass.
3952: Carefully looking around for traces of the civilisation that once stood here, you notice that the once great King's Road crosses another decayed road which leads from an old square to the north towards a small hill just south of here.
3953: Here, in the middle of what seems to have been a small square, you see a stone circle, that once was a well. Now, there is nothing left but a dark hole in the ground. To the west, you see some houses that seem to have withstood the test of time, with their walls still standing.
3954: There are many large white stones littering the area, obviously the common building material of that era. However, the layout of the stones bears no resemblance to the buildings of the great city that once stood here. Everything that consisted of wood must have rotted away centuries ago, leaving nothing but a hostile, scary sea of grass covered stones.
3955: Just to the north of here the city wall stretches some thirty feet into the air above you. The city that once lay within seems to be far away though, since the only thing you can spot around you are small birches and a few bushes.
3956: This rather small house must once have been the home of a medium sized family. The doors to the east and south have long since rotted, but the gaps have allowed animals to run in and out rather freely, which, from the faeces that lie all about you, they obviously have done.
3957: At the Corner of the City Wall

You have now reached the northwestern corner of the once mighty city. The high city wall turns from the east to the south here and to the east you see the back of a small house. The breach in the wall that you passed on your way here is clearly visible to the south.
3958: At the Breach in the Wall

In the year of 1974, when the foul orcs of Angmar attacked Fornost, they managed to break down the city wall at this very point. Looking through the wide hole, you see a green forest stretching in all directions. A few houses with their walls still standing can be seen to the east, but most of the city that once lay here seems to be gone.
3959: A fallow deer is grazing peacefully here.
A small grove of birches has taken root here in the ruins of the city. An occasional rock sticks up between the roots, but not much else is left to see here.
3960: Not much is left to see of the road that once led north from the King's Road towards the city wall. Looking west, you see the wall of a crooked house, with its empty windows gaping at the surroundings. To the south you can see the remains of the once busy Kings Road.
3961: The wide road that was once the King's Road crosses a smaller street that leads from the south to the north. The King's Road used to be over forty yards wide and easily travelled on the perfectly fitting white stones from the White Downs. Now, war and nature has slowly broken it down, and only a few broken stones peek out from the undergrowth reminding you of its former beauty.
3962: A small, once paved, street leads north and south. Passages to the east and west are blocked by the crumbled walls of old houses. To the north, you see the ruined King's Road, and to the south there is the remains of an old house.
3963: From the layout of this ruined building, you quickly decide that it must once have been one of the stables of Fornost. Arthedain never really used cavalry, but horses were widely used for transportation, and from the adorned walls, you see that the Dunedain cared a lot about their mounts.
3964: The road is getting rather steep, making motion rather slow. Just south of here, the road meets another, smaller road in a T-junction. To the east and west, steep slopes offer no grip for climbing.
3965: Looking around you, you see the remnants of a house that is now completely destroyed. Crumbled remnants of the buildings walls lie all about you, reminding you of how violent the war must have been.
3966: You can still see the remainder of some neat flower beds in this small backyard. It surely must have been the pride and joy of some skilled housewife several hundred years ago, before the orcs came here and mutilated everything.
3967: The roof of this small building is since long gone, lying rotted to dust somewhere on the floor probably. To the east is the large road that once was the King's Road, and to the south you see something that looks like a small backyard, perhaps used for herbs once long ago.
3968:
A fierce boar is here, making grunting noises.
A boar cub is playing here, and exploring the wide world.
A boar cub is playing here, and exploring the wide world.

The road turns here in a straight ninety degrees angle. To the south, it slowly begins to climb the hill towards the ruined castle, and to the east it can take you back towards the inhabited parts of Fornost Erain - the northern fortress of the kings.
3969: The wide road starts to narrow as it begins to wind its way towards the top of the hill with the castle on top. Thick tufts of grass have emerged between the crooked paving-stones that still lie here covered in moss and lichen.
3970: A rabbit is here eyeing your presence warily.

The road that led up here is nothing but a small path now. It turns here from the east to the south, where it climbs around the hill. Just north of here you see the crumbled walls of a house, destroyed ages ago.
3971:
A fierce boar is here, making grunting noises.
A rabbit is here eyeing your presence warily.
Here, the wide road meets a smaller street that leads east on a wide ledge around the hill that lies to the south east. To the west, the road leads up on the hill to the gates of the royal castle.
3972: This old street leads halfway up the castle hill that rises to the south. You cannot find any spot to climb the steep cliff between you and the castle and not far to the north is the edge of a steep cliff which would surely mean certain death for any climbers.
3973:
The corpse of a boar is lying here.
The corpse of a thief is lying here.

The small street ends here with a large house to the south. It has withstood wind and rain, and still stands as a memory of the beauty once seen throughout the city. The street leads halfway up the hill on which the Royal Castle still stands, sheer drops to the north and the east clearly indicate that there is no way to proceed.
3974: A dark intangible shadow turns to face you.

As you enter the old building, you can't help being impressed by the skill of the Dunedain masons that once built it. Beautiful ornaments surround the now empty door posts and a splendid mosaic on the south wall, now covered with dust, shows a picture of what must have been the city of Fornost at the peak of its beauty.
3975:
A dark intangible shadow turns to face you.
An ancient spirit, dressed in the arms of a soldier, challenges you.

Once these barracks must have offered lodging for hundreds of soldiers. However, there is very little left of this old building - most probably it was virtually destroyed when the thousands of orcs from Angmar poured in over the city.
3976: Sloping Path to the Old Castle

The path quickly climbs its way south and up, towards the outer gates of the castle that lies south east of here. At this point, it passes the ruins of a large house to the east, and to the west, you see a small path sloping down towards the foot of the hill.
3977: The small path you are standing on zigzags its way past boulders and trees, taking you either north to some kind of statue at the base of the hill or east to the path leading up to the castle.
3978: A boar cub is playing here, and exploring the wide world.

A large statue stands here in memory of the fallen elves and humans that lie buried behind the iron gate to the west. Looking through the bars of the gate, you see a large tree-covered burial mound surrounded by a soft mist. To the south, a small path winds its way up the foot of the hill.
3979: Many dark, silent, ancient oak trees stand on guard over the graves of the valiant elves of the Grey Havens and men of Gondor and Arthedain. The many gravestones tell of their valiant deeds and their heroic contribution to the liberation of Fornost. This place is certainly no place for a living man to linger.
3980: A shadowy haunt floats here, oblivious to your presence.

This is the top of the gloomy burial mound that contains the bodies of the men and elves that died trying to drive the orcs out of the city. Strange shadows mixed with a light mist drift between the black oaks that loom over the dead.
3981: A shade is here, shrouded in an inky blackness.

This room has been sealed off since the year of the great war. The air is anything but pleasant to breathe and you hold your nose in disgust as you slowly enter the dark room. A sudden sound from the darkness catches your attention and you quickly try to make out what caused it before something nasty jumps out at you...
3982: A rabbit is here eyeing your presence warily.

A small stairway leads up from this small, and empty basement to the slab of stone that has kept visitors out since the old days of the war. The dirt walls have begun to collapse, and you don't feel very safe in here as suddenly you hear even more dirt falling down from the eastern wall.
3983: Forest outside the Breach in the Wall

You are standing in a green forest growing at the foot of a high wall to the east. The wall is several paces high, and once contained the prospering city of Fornost Erain. Looking between the high trees, you see that there is a wide breach in the wall at this very spot, allowing anyone, who has the nerves it takes, to enter the abandoned city.
3984: Sloping Path to the Old Castle

You are standing on the remnants of the road that leads to the castle on the hill above, overlooking the ruined city behind you. To the east, there is a small path slowly climbing upwards, and you have to walk carefully not to trip over the old, crooked cobblestones.
3985: Sloping Path to the Old Castle

The path slowly takes you up the hill. Once, this was a road paved with cut stones from the White Downs far in the west of Arthedain. It has, however, not been in use since the big war with Angmar, when the city below you was ruined, leaving nothing but crumbled walls and the surprisingly intact castle that looms above you to the east.
3986: Finally, you have reached the end of the withered path. You are on a small drawbridge that can take you into the black gap where the gates of the castle once were. Looking downhill, to the west, you can only see traces of the road that used to lead up here. Looking over the edge of the bridge, you see the dike which was once used to stop the ferocious hordes of orcs that plundered Fornost a millennium ago.
3987: This room obviously once contained the sleeping-chambers of the gate guards. Looking around, you can see old pieces of rotten wood that were once the furnishings in this dark cellar. An old stone stairway leads to the floor above.
3988:
A black snake hurries towards you with sly intentions.
A black snake hurries towards you with sly intentions.

Jumping down from the drawbridge, you find yourself stuck in the steep dike that was once used to prevent any invasion attempts against the royal castle that towers above you. Unfortunately, you can't seem to find any way up from here.
3989: Looking up, you see a sturdy stone arch holding the battlements above on its shoulders. Examining the wall to the west closer, you see that the great hinges that once held the gates are nothing but rust, and the gates themselves are nothing but dust lying on the ground. You can either enter the outer yard of the castle to the east, go back on the drawbridge or go through the black hole that once was a door to the north.
3991: The road follows the high wall to the south. It can take you either uphill, to the east, where the citadel lies, or downhill to the silent ruins of Fornost below. High grass grows everywhere, making it obvious that no man has travelled here in a very long time.
3992: The road leaves the gates of the outer wall to the west, and slowly climbs the small slope that will take you to the main building of the castle in the north-east. South of here, the high battlements rises above you, overlooking the surroundings.
3996: Looking around you, you see the high outer wall to the east, and a large stone house to the west, its roof since long gone, but the walls still look intact. Behind it, you see the high towers of the citadel rising high into the air.
3997: This is the final part of the old road that leads from the outer gates to the citadel that lies west of here, on the other side of a small square. The road continues south, taking you downhill, past the remains of a rather large stone building.
3998:
A stocky mountain mule is here, waiting to serve.
A horse of the Rohirrim (my) is standing here.
A stocky mountain mule is here, waiting to serve.
A stocky mountain mule is here, waiting to serve.

This once was a place filled with people. Now, only a withered well standing in the middle of the square is left from those days. Looking west, you see the large gate to the citadel, with its towers stretching into the sky. A road leaves the square to the east, taking you downhill.
3999:
A dark intangible shadow turns to face you.
A dark intangible shadow turns to face you.
A spirit floats towards you and howls with an evil laughter.

Crumbling stone walls are the only remnants of a large house - once the home of the hundred soldiers that once was the Royal Guard of Arthedain. The roof has fallen in, and you see no traces of any living beings. You shiver as you look around and see the piles of human bones that reminds of the horrible slaughter that once took place within these walls.
4000:
A scimitar has been left here.
A scimitar has been left here.
A scimitar has been left here.
A scimitar has been left here.

A small room lies here, just behind the gate of the castles' main building. You can go back outside to the east or up a wide stone stair to the west. Stretching over twenty yards from the north to the south, this is truly a hallway worthy of a king.
4001: You have entered the impressive halls of the old kings. Once, great feasts were held here, but now, there is nothing that seems joyous about it. Where once great chandeliers lit the halls, tables now lie broken on the floor. The hall continues to the north and the west. A wide staircase leads down to the east, to the gate of the citadel.
4002: This is the north east part of the large hall. There are piles of dust and old cobwebs on the floor, and you feel very small as you walk through the dark halls of the Arthedain kings.
4004: An ancient spirit, dressed in the arms of a soldier, challenges you.

The south west corner of the hall lies in complete darkness, but you can make out some kind of tunnel or passage leading south of here. It certainly doesn't look very inviting. A broken stone table lies on the floor, covered with ugly marks made by foul orcs long ago.
4006: Darkness surrounds you as you try to make your way south through the passage. Your flickering light is not strong enough to give any signs of what awaits you in the pitch black tunnel.
4007: A Skeletal Warrior is staring angrily at the surroundings.

This room really gives you the creeps. The dungeons hidden way down in the ground below the citadel above haven't been used by living beings in nearly a thousand years. Rusted chains are fastened to the walls and in them, skeletons of tortured men still hang - the result from the cruelty of the horrid orcs that overtook Fornost in the year of 1974.
4008: You have now entered what seems to be the dungeons of the old castle. There are remains of since long dead prisoners, left to die in here by the foul orcs in a forgotten past. Metal doors are to the south and the north, and to the east the corridor leads into a small room.
4009:
A rotten corpse is hanging here.
An ancient spirit, dressed in the arms of a soldier, challenges you.
An ancient spirit, dressed in the arms of a soldier, challenges you.
Once, the prison keeper lived in this square chamber. Strange and abhorrent torturing tools lie rusting and withering on a bench. In one corner you see charred bits of a wooden bed.
4010:
An ancient spirit, dressed in the arms of a soldier, challenges you.
A dark intangible shadow turns to face you.

A small stone stair reaches down from the dark tunnel above and ends in this moist cellar. The air is very heavy to breathe, and you have much trouble trying to find your way through the small passages.
4011: This old cellar was obviously razed in the raging battles that once took place in the castle. The north and west walls lie in a pile of rubble, the south wall still stands, and you can go back to the rest of the cellar to the east.
4012: The air is getting heavier and heavier to breathe. It is very moist, and you feel your clothes clinging to your body as you carefully move around in the old cellar. In the flickering light of your lantern, you see no other way out, but back to the east. A sudden gust of air makes you aware of a terrible stench coming from somewhere in the darkness that surrounds you.
4013: Dark rock walls surround you, as you walk around in the cellar. The rooms are cut directly out of the high hill that the castle stands upon. However, from the perfectly smooth walls, you can easily tell that these cellars were made by skilled Dunedain.
4014:
A small campfire burns here, its low flames giving off only a little light.
Radikas the Dwarf (RR), wielding the Hammer of Belegost, is resting here.
Jeru the Dwarf, wielding an ornate, steel-shafted warhammer, is resting here.
Miltar the Half-Elf (MM), wielding an engraved broadsword, is resting here.
The stench in here is barely bearable. You find yourself standing on the beginning of some kind of marble quay that leads out in a pool with black, oily water.
4015: This is the end of the quay. To the east, the underground pool stretches into the darkness. Watching the water carefully, you see that small ripples keep coming in against the stones. Silently, you wonder what might be out there, in the black water of the pool.
4016:
The large kraken lies in the water, lashing at you with its tentacles.
A green, weaving tentacle rises out of the water, crawling towards you.
A green, weaving tentacle rises out of the water, crawling towards you.

Slowly you paddle your way through the black water. The oily surface lies silent, except for slow ripples that keep coming from the centre of the pool somewhere out there. You are amazed at how very how large this cave is and indeed, large is its inhabitant too...
4017: In the Quick Stream of Water
A wooden chest stands in the corner.

The water quickly rushes down the sloping tunnel, carrying you away from the horrible kraken that lies dead above. What is that? Suddenly you catch a glimpse of something standing on a small ledge next to the stream that carries you forward. If you hurry, you might have time to grab it...
4018:
A giant, strange looking green fungus is here, ready to devour you in seconds (red aura).
A giant, strange looking green fungus is here, ready to devour you in seconds (red aura).
A fierce bat is here, lusting for your blood.
A fierce bat is here, lusting for your blood.
A fierce bat is here, lusting for your blood.

You stand in a small cavern, with water up to your waist. A stream of water is coming down from above. As you investigate this further, you realise that the walls are too slippery and steep to climb, and perhaps it would be best to leave it at that.
4019:
A fierce bat is here, lusting for your blood (hidden).
A fierce bat is here, lusting for your blood.
You can hear, or rather feel, the sounds of the city. It all seems far away as you are now walking through this low, moist tunnel with water to your ankles.
4020: The small but steady stream of water at your feet flows through an old, rusted grating at the eastern end of the tunnel. Outside the grating, you can see trees, and a couple of feet down, a small pond.
4021: A Skeletal Warrior is staring angrily at the surroundings.

Terror creeps upon you as you look around in the chamber of death and violence. Here, many prisoners suffered a fate worse than death itself, under the supervision of the skilled orkish torturers. This room is no place for someone of the living world...
4022: The End of the Winding Staircase

Looking up, you see that the staircase ends here, and leads out in some kind of room above you. You cannot see anything of what the room contains, but a thick layer of dust tells you that no one has walked here in many, many years.
4023: A dark intangible shadow turns to face you.

The wide staircase leads you up, into a tower in the north-west side of the castle. Looking back down, you see the beginning of the great hall, but you can see nothing of what lies ahead of you as you gaze into the darkness of the stairs to the south.
4024: Still climbing upwards, progress is very hard. The staircase takes you in a spiral up the circular tower. You can go either down, to the north, or up to the east.
4025: A Skeletal Warrior is staring angrily at the surroundings.

The stairs slowly circle their way upwards in the tower to the north and down to the west. A small window in the thick stone wall lets some fresh air in here, and you see that the layer of dust is somewhat thinner ...
4026: The balcony you are standing on is large and robust. It is fifty feet wide and reaches some ten feet from the tower wall behind you. Turning your gaze to the south, you see a forest covered area, with the Iaur Men Formen, the Old North Road, reaching south, towards Bree.
4027: The Large Hall in the Tower

You push disgusting thick cobwebs to the side and try to make your way forward without falling on any hidden objects (or treasures?) on the floor. A rusty iron door leads out onto an old balcony to the south. The dark hall continues to the north and the west.
4028: The Large Hall in the Tower

You have reached the north-eastern corner of the large hall. A winding staircase can take you back down to the more inviting safety below you. The wind howls around the tower making you feel slightly frightened of entering this large cobweb filled room.
4029: The Large Hall in the Tower

A huge, poisonous spider is here.
A huge, poisonous spider is here.
A huge, poisonous spider is here.

This large hall is situated about half-way up the unusually well preserved northwestern tower of the citadel. Large cobwebs hang across the walls, and in each corner of this long since abandoned room, and an occasional strange creaking noise can be heard, as if something were crossing the uneven wooden floor behind you.
4030: The Large Hall in the Tower

A huge, poisonous tarantula extends her legs to you.
A huge, poisonous tarantula extends her legs to you.

Cobwebs cling to everything in this room, and you feel yourself entangled by their soft silk every time you move. The sticky strands seem to be stronger than any normal spider's web however. Faint scuffling and an occasional louder clattering can be heard from somewhere in the darkness nearby.
4031: Ah! You have found a secret staircase behind the curtain. You carefully peer up the stairs, but the darkness above is impenetrable by your weak eyes. A very thick layer of dust lies on the ground, with no traces of any being of flesh and blood having walked here in hundreds of years.
4033: A large, loyal falcon is circling above.

A breathtaking view lies below you, as you look over the walls that prevent you from falling down on the castle yard several hundred feet below. Looking around, you see all of Arthedain stretching into the horizon. Below you, the city of Fornost lies quietly, with the ruined western part and the rebuilt eastern part.
4034: You have reached the last room in the tower. In the middle of the room stands a sturdy stone pillar, with a perfect half sphere cut out of it. Recalling the old tales of the wise men at home, you realise that this must be the site of the Palantir that once was kept in Fornost Erain to communicate with the southern kingdom, Gondor. However, Arvedui, the last king of Arthedain, took it with him into the cold depths of the icy waters of Forochel.
4035: Sloping Path to the Old Castle

You are now standing just north of the point where the path starts turning east, around the hill. You can see the silhouette of the castle here as you turn your gaze to the east, where it lies silently on its hill.
4293: Cattails - some several feet high - obscure vision in every direction. The parts of the ground that are not submerged beneath the black water consist of large islands of mud that smell of rotting vegetation. The air is filled by the cacophony of buzzing insects and singing frogs, and sometimes seems to be just a solid wall of insect swarms.
4294:
A swarm of midges is here, humming around you.
A neekerbreeker is standing here.

The ground is slightly drier here than to the southeast, but still damp enough to support hordes of cattails. Their long stalks sprout everywhere and make it difficult to see more than a few feet in any direction. Clouds of bothersome insects rise at each footstep, eagerly seeking their next meal.
4295:
A swarm of mosquitoes is here, humming around you.
A neekerbreeker is standing here.

To the west lies a wall of cattails, marking the edge of the Midgewater Marshes. This area, although still damp, resembles the grassy plains found elsewhere on Arda. To the east and north a narrow path can be made out, hugging the foot of a tall scarp.
4296: To the west, the grasses of this area give way to growths of sedges and reeds that mark the Midgewater Marshes. The ground is very damp, and it seems to gently slope down toward the marsh. The grassland is cut to the east by a trail that runs along the bottom of an escarpment.
4297: To the east, the land rises slightly and the thick sedges and reeds give way to grasses. There is little open water here - mostly the ground is made of thick mud that smells of rotting vegetation. To the southwest, the Midgewater Marshes make travel an almost impossible chore, but to the northeast, there appears to be a trail that runs along the edge of the fens.
4298: A buzzing dumbledor is here, flying around you in close circles.

There is little open water anywhere in this area - thick plant-life erupts through the dark surface of the water, forming a veritable jungle of reeds and sedges. Nowhere is the water more than a foot in depth, but the mud beneath the surface sometimes seems bottomless.
4299: This area of the marsh is characterized by huge stands of cattails surrounding large open stretches of mucky black water. Most of the ponds are too deep for comfort, but there are enough shallow areas to travel further in any direction. To the north, the cattails take over completely, and their long stalks block any view of the areas in that direction.
4300: The clouds of insects that give these marshes their name are clearly in evidence, with mosquitoes, gnats, and midges filling the air and generally making nuisances of themselves. Where the water is shallow enough to allow passage, the bottom is a thick black mud that pulls downward at each footstep.
4301:
There is a lot of snow on the ice.
A green frog is here, hopping around.

This area is criss-crossed by several shallow ditches filled with muddy water. The water in the ditches is stagnant - if it flows at all it must drain into the marsh. A low and muddy ridge to the north is home to a stand of willows, but only sedges, reeds, and occasional cattails grow alongside the channels.
4302: A thick wall of reeds encircles this round pool of dark water. The lake does not have well-defined boundaries, for beneath the cover of the reeds, the water and thick mud seem to merge seamlessly, one into another.
4303: The ground is completely covered by a layer of water - mostly of depth less than six inches, but in other places there seems to be no bottom. It is impossible to travel consistently in a single direction, as the marshes seem to conspire to make travel as tortuous as possible.
4304:
A swarm of midges is here, humming around you.
A buzzing dumbledor is here, flying around you in close circles.
A buzzing dumbledor is here, flying around you in close circles.

The frequent stretches of deep mud and black ponds makes it impossible to travel in a given direction with any certainty. On all sides the marshes reign unchallenged, providing a home to ravenous hordes of biting and stinging insects, who in turn sustain a huge population of frogs and other less familiar predators.
4305: A swarm of mosquitoes is here, humming around you.

To the east, the thick vegetation of the marsh seems to abate slightly. Every square inch of mud that lies above the waterline is home to chaotic tangles of shrubs and reeds that intertwine in thick knots. The cover of the plant life hides hordes of insects that rise in great black clouds as soon as the plants are disturbed.
4306: To the west, the rampant vegetation of the marsh reigns unchallenged - from here it looks like a wall of tangled reeds and sedges. To the north and east grasses dominate the wet plain, while to the south the ground looks to be a huge flat expanse of mud.
4307: The ground here is very damp, and often small muddy puddles greet careless footsteps. Everything is overgrown with a variety of grass that is verdant green with long, wide blades - almost like sawgrass, except without the serrated edges.
4308: The ground beneath the thick grassy cover is actually quite dry, in stark contrast to the wet mires that lie to the south and east. To the north runs a small trail, hugging the bottom of the scarp that marks the northern boundary of this basin.
4309: A sluggish stream - bloated with mud - runs just south of here, emptying into the marsh. The stream's bank is basically just a ridge of mud that has been anchored by several small willow and alder trees. A few miles to the north, the land rises abruptly in a steep scarp that marks the northern edge of the basin occupied by the Midgewater Marshes.
4310: A sluggish stream - more of a wide ditch than anything - lies just south of this area, beyond a small stand of willow trees. Some distance to the north, a large scarp looms, marking the southern boundary of a region of stark plains. The vegetation here is thick, consisting mostly of many varieties of grass, but occasionally a small tree has found a niche in which to flourish.
4311: Running from east to west, this scarp overlooks a depression in the earth that is now filled by the Midgewater Marshes. The rock of the scarp is generally very crumbly, but there are patches of solid granite. The plains that extend far to the north are dotted with great boulders that seem to have been dropped at random. Farther to the east, it appears that the ground along the foot of the scarp rises, and consequently is much drier.
4312: To the north and east stretches an expanse of sparsely vegetated and rocky plains. South and west, the plains come to an abrupt ending at a small cliff that overlooks the marshlands below. The cliff is much higher to the west, where the plains rise up to form a hill, but for the most part it is around twenty feet high. Running at the bottom of the cliff is a small trail that can probably be accessed from here, but the crumbly texture of the scarp edge suggests that getting back up may be impossible without great effort.
4313: A black crow flies low to the ground here, looking for carrion to eat.

To the west, the land rises into a large hill, while in every other direction, nothing but more plains can be discerned. Frequently, boulders are scattered about, like they had been carelessly tossed away by a gigantic child. Besides the wiry grass that covers the hard soil, patches of thorny brush sometimes are seen.
4314: The plains here form a hill whose southern and western slopes appear to have been shorn off, leaving behind a sheer cliff about sixty feet from top to bottom. Along the base of the cliff runs a small trail that leads around the northern edge of the Midgewater, and then through the Chetwood into Bree-land.
4315: The hard plains come to an end quickly to the southwest at a small cliff that overlooks the Midgewater. Here on top of the scarp, the ground is mostly dry and the only signs of life are patches of brush and occasional rabbits who scamper into the open.
4316: There is a lot of snow on the ground.

To the north and east, the land slopes upward to a broad plateau. These bleak plains end immediately to the south at a small cliff that stands around thirty feet high. At the foot of the scarp, a small trail skirts the northern edge of the Midgewater, whose misty expanse makes up the landscape to the south. The cliff is too steep to negotiate safely here.
4317: The steep scarp immediately to the south is here cut by a deep and narrow gully. The bottom of the gully is choked with brush, and it appears to have been dry for years. Following the floor of the gully to the south will lead one to the narrow path that follows the foot of the scarp.
4318: The plains to the north and east come to an abrupt end here on top of a steep scarp. Beyond the foot of the scarp lies the wet expanse of the Midgewater Marshes, but it seems there is a narrow trail running flush against the bottom of the cliff. The drop is around thirty feet, and it looks to be possible to slide down it to the trail below, although getting back up may be a problem.
4319: The few trees that have survived the buffeting winds of these plains have had their growth stunted. The most successful plants are several varieties of tough brush and thorn bushes that frequently cluster in impenetrable clumps.
4320: There is a lot of snow on the ground.

Cold winds frequently buffet the hard ground, loudly rustling through the dense low brush. There are very few trees, and the few that have managed to survive have been twisted by the wind into squat and tortured shapes. The plain slopes downward to the south, until it reaches a steep scarp that marks the edge of the depression occupied by the Midgewater Marshes.
4321: Two huge fingers of granite thrust upward out of the unforgiving soil, towering twenty feet over the surrounding plateau. The edges of the rock are deeply scored with grooves that resemble claw marks made by some tremendous, impossible beast. Scattered about are large boulders of the same type of rock, also bearing the same type of grooves.
4322: A black crow flies low to the ground here, looking for carrion to eat.

The exposed rock that frequently emerges from the hard earth looks as if some gigantic claw had raked it in the distant past, as the granite has been furrowed in a consistently north-south fashion. The plains slope upward to the northeast to form a broad plateau, and somewhere to the southwest lie the Midgewater Marshes.
4323: The plains are dotted with huge boulders that look as if they have been carelessly strewn about. Dense brush grows on the hard soil that dominates the area, although periodically the soil gives way to bare and windswept granite.
4324: A thin, hairy plant, with small, oval leaves, grows here.

The land levels off here, forming a large plateau. To the southwest, it drops steadily, descending into the depression occupied by the Midgewater Marshes. There are little signs of life besides a few patches of brush and signs of rabbits, as nothing large could subsist on the harsh landscape.
4325: A thin, hairy plant, with small, oval leaves, grows here.

This plateau supports scraggly patches of grass that become thicker to the east, where water seems to be more plentiful. The landscape is dotted with large boulders that seem to have been randomly scattered by some gigantic hand. Occasional outcroppings of granite appears as well, mostly worn smooth and having the appearance of having been scraped by huge claws.
4326: The land is eternally grey here, with cold hard earth and occasional patches of exposed granite extending to the northeast all the way to the horizon. Sporadic patches of spiny scrub offer little to relieve the monotony of the landscape, but offer shelter from the wind for the small animals that survive out here.
4327:
There is a lot of snow on the ground.
A swarm of midges is here, humming around you.

The earth is dry and cold here, and very few plants manage to eke out an existence here. Frequent winds gust from the north, chilling the air and hinting of frigid wastes far to the north. To the west, a narrow and deep gully cuts across the land, and to the north and east the land slopes upward, presumably until the Weather Hills far to the east are reached.
4328: There is a lot of snow on the ground.

A deep gully knifes across the plain here, leading south into the expanses of marshes that lie some distance away. The bottom of the gully is completely choked with brush, and apparently it has been years since water consistently flowed through it. To the north and east, the bleak plains continue to the horizon, offering nothing to break the monotony of the landscape.
4331:
There is some snow on the ice.
A swarm of mosquitoes is here, humming around you.
A buzzing dumbledor is here, flying around you in close circles.
A citizen mercenary (VIIS), holding a longsword, is lying here, incapacitated.
A sturdy pack horse is standing here.
A swarm of mosquitoes is here, humming around you.

To the north, an open lake can be spied beyond a wall of reeds. Everything here is either wet or alive, making for a most uncomfortable journey. Each footstep is an effort, as the muddy ground seems to be trying to ingest those foolish enough to travel here.
4332: The frequent stretches of deep mud and black ponds make it impossible to travel in a given direction with any certainty. On all sides the marshes reign unchallenged, providing a home to ravenous hordes of biting and stinging insects, who in turn sustain a huge population of frogs and other less familiar predators.
4333:
A swarm of mosquitoes is here, humming around you.
A neekerbreeker is standing here.

The frequent stretches of deep mud and black ponds makes it impossible to travel in a given direction with any certainty. On all sides the marshes reign unchallenged, providing a home to ravenous hordes of biting and stinging insects, who in turn sustain a huge population of frogs and other less familiar predators.
4336:
A large bonfire is burning here.
A ruffian is sneaking around here, looking for some mischief to do.
A ruffian is sneaking around here, looking for some mischief to do.
A ruffian is sneaking around here, looking for some mischief to do.

This earthen mound rises a few feet above the level of the surrounding marsh. It is completely surrounded by a wall of impenetrable reeds - the only exit from the islet appears to be the trail leading west. A small shanty has been erected on the eastern portion of the islet.
4337:
A small oaken table has been set here.
A malicious thug is here, threatening you.
A malicious thug is here, threatening you.
Bill Ferny is watching you with suspicious eyes.

This ramshackle shanty has been carelessly thrown together out of spare scraps of wood. There are many small gaps between boards, so that very little shelter is provided from wind or rain. In the centre of the room, a small table sits on the earthen floor, and a few chairs have been set around it.
4338:
A small barrel made of aged oak and strong iron hoops stands here.
A small barrel made of aged oak and strong iron hoops stands here.
A water barrel has been left here.
A beer barrel has been left here.

Lots of junk has been haphazardly scattered around this storage room - no care at all has been taken, and much of the stuff is broken. The walls of this shabby room are crudely fashioned - glimpses of the outside are visible through cracks between the boards. The roof is in even worse shape, and this explains why a lot of the equipment in here has been severely water damaged.
4339:
A shield bearing the markings of Arthedain lies here.
A wooden chest stands in the corner.
A large dog curls his lips back and snarls.
A large dog curls his lips back and snarls.

This room has been hollowed out of the earth, and its walls are simply the damp soil. The place smells as if animals have been kept penned in here, further evidenced by the dung on the floor. Some old rags have been piled in one corner, and in the other corner is an old chest.
4349: Pools of water hide treacherous depths of soupy mud, so each step must be carefully planned before execution. Small flowering plants occasionally bloom amongst the reeds and sedges, adding a bit of contrasting colour to the green and black of the marshes.
4350: To the north and east, a large amount of mud has been deposited, burying all of the vegetation. Here at the edge of the muddy flats, the reeds and sedges still hold sway, though they are nowhere nearly as dense as in the depths of the Midgewater Marshes, which begin in earnest to the south and west.
4351: The sticky black mud of this area smells vaguely of rotting vegetation. The viscous sludge is in places over two feet in depth - it was probably deposited recently because the plants of the marsh to the southwest have yet to colonise here successfully.
4352: Hordes of biting and stinging insects swarm through the thick air, feasting mercilessly on every square inch of exposed flesh. Great care is required to navigate successfully here amongst the fens, as bottomless pits of mire can lurk beneath seemingly shallow pools.
4353: A noisy neekerbreeker is shrieking here.

The frequent stretches of deep mud and black ponds makes it impossible to travel in a given direction with any certainty. On all sides the marshes reign unchallenged, providing a home to ravenous hordes of biting and stinging insects, who in turn sustain a huge population of frogs and other less familiar predators.
4354: The frequent stretches of deep mud and black ponds makes it impossible to travel in a given direction with any certainty. On all sides the marshes reign unchallenged, providing a home to ravenous hordes of biting and stinging insects, who in turn sustain a huge population of frogs and other less familiar predators.
4355:
A green frog is here, hopping around.
A swarm of midges is here, humming around you.

This vast expanse of sticky black mud was probably once an open grassland similar to the landscape to the north, but apparently the stream to the east overspilled its banks and deposited all this sediment. Sporadic patches of grass poke their stems up through the muck, hinting that they will soon reclaim this land.
4356: A black catfish is here, lurking in the mud.

This silt-laden stream nears its end here -- all hint of its channel vanishes when it enters the marshes to the southwest. The stream's banks are low mounds of sticky black mud, cemented into place by many small willows and alders.
4357: The current of this sluggish stream is barely discernible as it lazily drains southwestward into the Midgewater Marshes. The banks on both sides are covered by young willows and small, stunted alder trees. The soupy bottom of the stream lies only a few feet down, but the mud below seems to have no bottom, forcing those who would cross to take care.
4358: This stream loses its coherence here, as all trace of a current disappears amid these muddy flats. To the south and west, the amount of mud that has been deposited hints that this stream recently flooded, leaving behind the thick viscous mud that coats the plain. To the east, a stand of alders is flourishing in the damp soil.
4359: A swarm of midges is here, humming around you.

Just to the north, a sluggish stream dumps its load of mud into the marshes. This area is almost devoid of vegetation -- it looks as if someone coated the landscape with a layer of sticky black mud. A few tentative tendrils of green have begun to show, and soon this plain will once again be home to the rampant vegetation of the marsh.
4360:
A blooming water-lily floats on the surface of the water.
A black catfish is here, lurking in the mud.

The murky water of this pond seems to be very deep. Occasionally great bubbles float to the surface and burst, smelling vaguely of rotting plants. The pond is choked with plant life, and its muddy banks are home to a dense wall of reeds.
4361: A blooming water-lily floats on the surface of the water.

Just to the east, a solid wall of reeds marks the edge of a stretch of open water. This area is home to many insects - most of which seem intent on feeding - that are a constant nuisance. The muddy ground is generally covered with sedges and tangled brambles, while the frequent pools of dark water sport a coat of water lilies and other aquatic plants.
4362: A large pike is lurking in the mud by the bottom.

The sedges briefly give way to a large area of open water. The water is deep brown and occasionally bubbles slowly work their way to the surface and burst -- probably gasses from decaying matter on the bottom. On all sides, the sedges quickly reassert themselves, completely choking any exposed ground with their tangled growths.
4363: A buzzing dumbledor is here, flying around you in close circles.

The dense reeds and rushes frequently hide pools of ominous-looking black water. Insects are the masters here - they fill the air in great buzzing clouds, eager for a meal. From time to time a splash of water can be heard, indicating that other, larger forms of life are around.
4364: This flat plain is totally coated in mud, as it is a miniature delta for the sluggish stream to the east. Small channels in the mud are filled with water that seems to be slowly draining into the marsh. Very little vegetation has grown here - perhaps the mud was deposited recently.
4365: These trees anchor the southern bank of the sluggish stream that flows just to the north - they have thrived here in the damp soil. The stand of alders continues to the south, while the stream bends so that it also lies to the west of here.
4366: These young alders have flourished here in the damp earth. They are common to the north as well, while to the south a small tongue of higher ground that protrudes into the marsh is home to a grove of young willows. To the west, all vegetation has been buried beneath a thick layer of sticky mud.
4367: This tongue of hardened earth protrudes out into the marsh, almost as if the plains to the east were attempting an invasion. Several young trees have taken advantage of the soil and taken root - they would be unable to survive in the saturated soil of the surrounding marshes.
4368: A clear spring babbles as cool water trickles out of the ground.

A small tongue of high ground protrudes westward -- its crest overgrown with young oak trees that have taken advantage of the dry ground and taken root. A small spring of clear water bursts from the ground here, and its runoff flows down the southern slope of the hill where it is quickly lost among the marshy grassland.
4369: To the west, a small tongue of higher ground protrudes into the marsh, providing a home to a small stand of trees. The marsh here is home to many varieties of sawgrass, and their serrated blades tend to cut anything with which they come in contact.
4375: This is a dense stand of sedges with sharp, cutting leaves. White mist floats in the air, lending an aura of mystery to the marsh. With each step, clouds of insects are stirred up from the vegetation, eager for a meal.
4376: Many varieties of saw-toothed grass make this area their home. The ground is saturated with water, and makes a squishing sound at each step. The monotonous buzzing of insects continues incessantly, broken only by the calls of frogs and occasional splashes of unknown origins.
4377: A swarm of mosquitoes is here, humming around you.
Beneath the grassy cover, many shallow pools of water are hidden. Most of them are fairly muddy, but there seems to be a source of fresh water to the north that keeps a few of them drinkable.
4378: The ground here is very damp -- in some places as much as an inch of water lies hidden under the waving grass. The terrain slopes slightly downward to the west, so this water must drain into the marshes in that direction. Occasionally, narrow rivulets wind through the grasses, their flow unconstrained by any channel.
4379: A big hummerhorn is here, flying around you.

To the west, the ground sinks and becomes gradually damper, until at last the grass of the plains is replaced with the rampant vegetation of the Midgewater Marshes. Eastward lies a land of low and grassy hills, rolling unchallenged, save for an occasional stand of trees, to the distant Weather Hills.
4380: To the north and east, the ground becomes much drier as it slopes upward to the Weather Hills many miles to the east. Westward, the ground descends into the depression that is home to the Midgewater Marshes and their hordes of gnats and midges. The ground here is damp, but there is very little standing water to be found.
4381: Each footstep is greeted by a soft squishing noise as the ground seems to be saturated, even though there is very little standing water. The grasses of the South Downs, which lie south beyond the Great Hedge, have here found a foothold and flourished on the wet plain. Directly to the south, the Old East Road runs along the north side of the Great Hedge.
4382: Bounded on the east by marshy grasslands and on the west by an ominous looking black pond, this strip of land is the transition from the plains that lie to the east, and the marshes that lie to the north and west. To the south, the Old East Road is tucked along the northern side of the Great Hedge as it skirts the southern end of the marshes on its journey between Bree and Rivendell.
4383:
A black catfish is here, lurking in the mud.
A black catfish is here, lurking in the mud.

This pond of foul black water is bordered by thick growths of reeds and cattails. When the bottom can be felt, it seems to be thick mud covered with layers of rotting plant debris. Just to the south, the Old East Road passes, and the water of this pond literally laps on the northern edge of the road.
4384:
A black catfish is here, lurking in the mud.
A black catfish is here, lurking in the mud.

This pond, and its twin lying a short distance to the east, are filled with foul-smelling black water. The unmistakeable odour of decomposing plants thickens the air, though the hordes of mosquitoes and other insects do not seem to mind. When the bottom of the pond can be felt, it seems to be made of thick mud covered with a layer of slimy rotting vegetation. To the north, the muddy shore marks the beginning of the Midgewater, while on the south side runs the Old East Road.
4385: A few scattered stone blocks are all that remain of an ancient causeway, the rest having been claimed by the marshes. It appears that a road once led north here, but there is no hint as to its eventual destination. The Old East Road bends around this wet area that is nestled between the Midgewater to the north and a murky black lake to the east.
4386: The insects of the Midgewater seem to be under the guidance of a malevolent intelligence, as they somehow seem able to find skin no matter how well covered. The ground -- where it rises above the shallow water -- is com- pletely saturated and the footing is often treacherous. To the south, the marshes seem less severe, but this in every other direction the terrain is much the same.
4387:
A buzzing dumbledor is here, flying around you in close circles.
A mewlip is here, faintly wailing at you.

Just to the south, beyond the edge of the marshes, the Old East Road con- tinues its journey between Bree and Rivendell. The wet marshes almost reach the road, which is sandwiched between them and the Great Hedge that lies a bit farther south. To the north, a low mist hangs over the marsh, hiding the hordes of insects whose buzzing can be heard even now.
4388: The air is filled with insects that bite, sting, and generally do their best to annoy. Each step farther into the marsh brings a chorus of sound from loud insects hidden among the vegetation. Sometimes the frogs begin to call back and forth, raising their voices to almost deafening levels.
4389:
A buzzing dumbledor is here, flying around you in close circles.
A swarm of mosquitoes is here, humming around you.

The maze of mud and vegetation of the heart of the marshes lies to the northwest. Here it is still possible to move fairly easily, as the sedges and reeds are not that dense. To the south, a pond of black water is nestled among the reeds, while to the east the ground becomes drier as the edge of the marsh nears.
4390: To the west, the marshes begin in earnest. This area consists of damp ground overgrown with many varieties of sawgrass. The serrated blades of grass, although not dangerous, are still capable of inflicting small stinging cuts on the careless -- cuts that are immediately sought out by hordes of blood-drinking insects.
4391:
There are two swamp irises here.
A big hummerhorn is here, flying around you.

A low mist hangs over this area of the marsh, as the air is completely saturated with water. Just to the south, right along the edge of the marshes, the Old East Road passes. To the west, the terrain gets slightly drier, but to the north and east, travel among the fens will be difficult.
4392: The marshes encroach from the north until the almost reach the Old East Road to the south. This fringe of damp grasslands dotted with open pools will certainly one day become part of the Midgewater Marshes to the north, but for now the land still sustains many of the grasses that are characteristic of the downs to the south of the Old East Road.
4393: The ground slopes steadily downward to the north, becoming steadily damper until the fens of the Midgewater Marsh are reached. The Old East Road runs a short distance to the south, skirting the southern end of the marshes.
4394: A noisy neekerbreeker is shrieking here.

The constant din of uncounted hordes of insects and amphibians at times seems loud enough to drown out speech. The ground here is mostly soft mud that is at times covered with up to a foot of brown water, making each step an uncomfortable chore. Directly to the west, a low bluff marks the end of the marsh in that direction at least.
4395: The soupy mud that greets each step makes travel an unpleasant experience. It is nearly impossible to travel in a generally straight line -- any progress at all is via circuitous and tortuous routes through the mazey mire.
4396:
A swarm of mosquitoes is here, humming around you.
A swarm of mosquitoes is here, humming around you.

The muddy bottom beneath the murky water makes each footstep an effort, as if the Midgewater were deliberately trying to devour prey. To the east, a damp mist lies low over the marsh, and to the north lies a dense growth of sedges. Westward the vegetation seems to thin a bit, though clouds of biting insects seem unphazed by the lack of cover.
4397: Considerable effort is required to successfully navigate amongst the many pools of black water, as the thick vegetation and grasping black mud seem to impede each step with a malevolent intent. To the east, the vegetation clears and reveals a large pool of what looks to be soupy mud, while in every other direction, the marshes continue.
4398: The mud here is very deep, and it seems keen on enveloping anyone foolish enough to tread here. Luckily, there are several twisting routes that avoid the deep muck, although any travel must be done slowly and carefully.
4399: A swarm of mosquitoes is here, humming around you.

To the west is what appears to be a lake of soupy mud. On every other side, the rampant vegetation of the marsh makes motion difficult. Clouds of insects and the frogs that feed on them can be seen everywhere, and they fill the air with noise.
4400:
The corpse of a buzzing dumbledor is lying here.
A buzzing dumbledor is here, flying around you in close circles.
A buzzing dumbledor is here, flying around you in close circles.
The spongy ground is saturated with water. A light mist caresses the marsh plants with wispy white tendrils, and all around the hum of insects and the songs of frogs can be heard.
4401: The ground is slightly drier here than to the west, and on the whole it appears to be rising slightly to the east, where the towering Weather Hills can be spied in the distance. The vegetation here runs from the sedges and reeds of the marshes to the grasses of the plains to the east.
4402: The spongy ground is saturated with water. A light mist caresses the marsh plants with wispy white tendrils, and all around the hum of insects and the songs of frogs can be heard.
4403: Like the hump of some great sea serpent, this islet of spongy black mud rises a short distance out of the murky mud. Completely overgrown with dense vegetation, it is difficult to push through to the marsh on the other side. The air is choked with gnats and midges, and the sonorous singing of the multitudes of frogs and insects drones on incessantly. The slope to the south appears to be very slick and steep, so it might be difficult climbing it back out of the swamp.
4404: The air is filled with the cacophony of millions of insects buzzing about, along with the calls of the animals that feed on them. Occasionally, a splash of water can be heard, as some unseen animal leaves the muddy shore. The air is tinged with the smell of rotting vegetation and marsh gas, which makes it unpleasant to breathe.
4405:
A blooming water-lily floats on the surface of the water.
A blooming water-lily floats on the surface of the water.
A frog is standing here.
A swarm of mosquitoes is here, humming around you.
A frog is standing here.

Strange insects buzz about, constantly seeking ways to find any exposed flesh. Their incessant buzzing is punctuated by loud calls of frogs and cries of birds. The pools of water tend to be shallow and still -- breeding grounds for the hordes of gnats and midges that give these marshes their name.
4406:
A blooming water-lily floats on the surface of the water.
A blooming water-lily floats on the surface of the water.
A big hummerhorn is here, flying around you.
A frog is standing here.

To the north, the tall vertical stalks of reeds form a wall of vegetation. Here, they are not nearly as dense, and it is possible to see a bit in each direction. Underfoot, there are about six inches of black mud mixed with rotting vegetation that grab and suck after each careful footstep.
4426: Eastern End of a Small Forest

This forest marks where the Downs that cover the lands to the southeast come to a stop. A large number of thorny bushes make travel through this forest almost impossible. Indeed the plentiful supply of sunlight and rain at the edges of the forest has made the bushes there so numerous it's only possible to reach the outside lands if a traveller heads west through the centre and leaves the forest there.
4460: A cluster of white star-shaped forget-me-nots flourish here in reminiscence.

A low mound covered with with short and springy grass rises above the surrounding plains. The earth beneath the grassy cover is not as tightly packed as in the flatter areas, suggesting that this mound may be of artificial origin. Some distance to the north, the dark green line of the dense hedge alongside the Old East Road can be discerned.
4470: The ever-present gale deters anything tree-like from growing up here on this high hill so the area is covered in spiny grasses and heather. On bright days, the red of the flowers blooming among the furze bushes across the fields to the north blaze against the darker green of their leaves.
4471: A swallow flies high above the ground.

The fields you are standing in are in a pretty bad shape. All around you are knee-high weeds, mostly red poppy. Nothing of worth seems to grow here. The soil is free of stones, some of which probably have been used to build a citadel that now lies in ruins east of here. Beyond this, you see wastelands as far as the eye can see. South of here, a high hill strives towards the skies.
4472: As the hedge is planted in an east-westwards fashion here, the trail you are upon takes you in the same directions. South of here lie old farmer fields, long since forgotten. A few poppies of the type that grow in the fields glow red here in the underbrush of the hedge, seeds blown here by southern winds.
4490: To the south a largish mound, too regularly shaped to be of natural origin, rises from a flat area among the downs. The grass here is soft and pleasant and small yellow flowers are interspersed among the green. Some distance to the north, the dark green line of the Great Hedge can be seen from the tops of most of the low hills.
4574: What once must have been a mighty citadel lies in ruins here. Large stoneblocks overgrown with moss and grass lie in a circle around a large hole. The hole is well ten yards deep and thirty yards wide. It must once have been the cellar or prison of the citadel, as the walls and floor are covered with stone. A path leads north from here towards the hedge, and it looks as if it has been traveled quite frequently lately.
4575: You are upon a battlefield of old, with rusted weapons and armours still lying half-buried in the grass. Here and there bones stick out of the ground, as if only a thin layer of soil was thrown upon the corpses in a vain attempt to protect them from animals.
4576: These are desolate lands. The forbidding earth that covers these plains will not allow more than low grass and writhing bushes to grow. You can spot some smoke to the north, and the light of a campfire catches your eye.
4577:
A small brown snake is slithering around here.
A snake slithers towards you.

Hard, dark earth covers the ground around here, turning more and more into sand further east. Grey grass grows in the cracks, as well as a few crooked bushes. These dusky plains continue both west and east, while the lands to the north are more travelled, and many paths seem to criss-cross over the terrain there.
4578: A worm is here slithering around.

The ground here is fairly sandy, with more hard earth to the west. A few hardened bushes grow in the vicinity, the last ones you can spot for a few miles when looking eastwards. Far to the north the hedge runs all along the horizon.
4579:
A small brown snake is slithering around here.
A snake slithers towards you.

Pale yellowish white sand covers these downs, with sparse tufts of grey grass. Except for snakes and worms, little wildlife care to live in these surroundings. The downs continue east and west, while the hedgetrail makes a turn north of here, following the hedge closely.
4580: A worm is here slithering around.

Travelling among these sandy downs is fairly strenuous. The ground slips away beneath the feet, leaving deep tracks. Both east and west these sandy hillplains continue, while the green outlining of the hedge can be seen a few miles north.
4584: Gaakt, wielding a black runed dagger, is standing here.

Many confusing paths and trails run in different directions around here. Some are manmade, other natural animal trails. It is hard to follow the hedgetrail at times, as you mix it up with sidetracks disappearing into the low brush. The hedge runs northwest though, and you can trust on the trail following it closely.
4585: You have reached something of a crossing of paths here in the middle of the plain, the widest leading through the grass northwards towards the hedgetrail. Where the others lead is hard to tell, as they seem to go in circles or lead straight out to empty plains.
4586: This is where the hedge turns south and east, and the hedgetrail follows it closely. This place is searingly hot on most sunny days, as the hedge deflects sun back south, and winds slow down among its leaves. The grass that grows here is dry and brittle at all times, growing to a feets height at most.
4587: Low grass and tiny clover grow on the sides of the one yard wide hedgetrail that leads almost all the way to bree to the west and a few miles past weather- top far east of here. You spot the old east road now and then on the other side of the hedge to the north, but thorns and thick branches block the way for many miles.
4588: Dry and compassionless ground starts here, swept clean by winds that gain speed over the barren plains south of here. To your north grows the hedge, and the hedgetrail quickly crosses this flat platform, leaving east and west.
4589: You are standing amongst small mounds lacking any vegetation. The hedgetrail winds east and west among these smooth brown heaps of earth. The northern horizon is obscured by the hedge which grows thick a few stones away. Desolate plains are to the south, divided in patches by small trails.
4590: Path to the Old East Road

The old east road lies north of here, and a path leads there through a wood-beamed archway in the hedge. Many trails lead in various directions over the plains to the south, the largest being the hedgetrail running east-west here just south of the hedge.
4591: Here the path runs southeast and westward, following the hedge closely. Many small leaves have assembled here in the corner of the hedge where the wind slows down. The ground is fairly hard and barren though, with only sparse patches of dirty grass.
4592: The hedge avoids the sandy south downs by turning north and east here, and the trail goes a few yards away from the thorny wall. A mile or two to the south and west the hard dark earth around here turns into bright sand, where nothing seems to grow.
4593:
A snake slithers towards you.
A finch flies low above the ground.

The trail is a few yards wide here, running upon hard dark brown earth. Looking south you see brighter plains, covered mostly with sand. The hedge north of you is high and thick, and you hear sounds of small animals from within.
4595:
A worm is here slithering around.
A small brown snake is slithering around here.
A worm is here slithering around.
A snake slithers towards you.

These are the south downs, empty, sandy and devoid of most wildlife. Sandworms and slithering snakes care to make a living here, feeding upon whatever small animals stray into the area. These sandy downs continue southwards, while more desolate land lies to the east and west, south of the hedge and the hedgetrail.
4596: Small paths leave in almost all directions here, carved in the grassland. Should you choose to follow one you would either end up in the sandy downs to the south, on the hedge trail north of here, or in the plains that continue both east and west.
4597:
A huge, smoking campfire is burning here.
A hunter, holding a broadsword, is resting here.

Someone has built a shelter from old logs and grass here, providing some protection from both sun and rain. The grass is fresh, and it is clear that it is constantly maintained. There is a huge campfire in the middle of this dry place. Remains of small animals lie in a heap behind the shelter, and a foul stench emerges from there.
4598: Old stone stairs lead down to this wrecked cellar, with pillars and partly razed walls still standing. Everything down here is covered in stone, overgrown with moss in places and with grass growing in cracks. An odd, cold feeling is over this site.
4599: Dank and narrow crypts wind here below the citadel and down under the plains. Graves full of bones lie in hollows at your sides, dug into the soft earth. Being only about one yard wide at their most narrow passages, wielding a weapon has its problems at times. Slowly winding eastwards, the tunnels get colder and the air gets thicker.
4600: A war-weary wight-warrior is standing here.

This is at the eastern end of the narrow tunnels dug beneath the citadel to serve as a final restingplace for its inhabitants. A small chamber is here, perhaps once serving as a room to mourn in and spend some time revering your ancestors. The room is simply dug out of the earth, with no decorations except for a few wooden benches along the soft earthen walls and a large stone slab with many delicate inscriptions firmly set in the north wall. Filled with old mourning and grief, the air here is thick and chilly.
4601: An old wight is standing here, ready to fight.

The deepest chamber of the crypts is large and paved with stone. Several mansized stone chests are lined upon slabs on the floor, and the walls are all covered with sealed graves as well. This must be the tomb where the commanders and rulers of the citadel were buried. A faint green glow lights up the place, but no such light source can be found.

In front of you stands an impressive cliff. It seems impossible to climb on it. You search for an exit but you must give up and return by the same way

4617: You notice the bushes define a quite perfect circle around you. At your right, you notice a small path. The bushes are so high that you can't see what is behind them. You hear some voices; you try to shout, but your voice is shallowed by the noise of the wind !
