4621: You are standing on a small plateau. You take a look around you, but notice nothing special except the small wood far west. The wind blows quite strongly here and you feel exposed to the wild nature elements ! You should find a better place to rest.
4622: You are on a small earth path leading down. You notice that this path must be used quite often because you see no grass on the middle of it. You can smell the fresh air coming up to you.
4623: You are at a sharp bend in the path. To the west you can see an extremely open area among the bushes, where no trees seem to grow. To the north the trail descends sharply, making its way between the dense green shrubs which cling tenaciously to life even on such a slope.
4624: You are standing on the top of the pile. You try to keep your balance. Maybe you should get down as fast as possible. The trunks may roll down...

4628: Amongst the low, undulating hills of the downs, the great hedge stretches into the west and the east, hugging the contours of the land. On its southern side, this ragged trail winds, keeping with a few score yards of the bushes. The grass has in many places overgrown the track but the trace of many former travellers has not been erased completely.
4629: This is a hilly region lying below the impressive face of the Milkfall Edge. This side of the down, the broken face of limestone is exposed, its pale colour giving the escarpment its name. Directly below the face, the terrain is littered with irregular blocks of rock which have fallen from the eroded cliff. These range from pebble size to the size of a house, making travel both treacherous and unpredictable. However, away from the Edge, most of the region is covered in grasses which thrive on the downs.
4630: Within a mile of the escarpment, the Milkfall Edge dominates the view east. Its pale stone creates a long chain of rock stretching south, but broken here by a deep cutting right through to the backslope.
4631: A ferocious warg is here, snarling angrily.

You are standing in a dense forest, just along the road. You see a small path to the north, but the forest seems to continue even further. The air is fresh and an agreeable scent of pine floats around you. You feel relaxed and walk joyfully in the forest singing some old songs.
4632: You are standing in a dense forest, just along the road. You see a small path to the north, but the forest seems to continue even further. The air is fresh. An agreeable scent of pine floats around you. You feel relaxed as you talk joyfully in the forest.
4633: You are standing in a dense forest, just along the road. You see a small path to the north, but the forest seems to continue even further. The air is fresh and an agreeable scent of pine floats around you. You feel relaxed and walk joyfully in the forest singing some old songs.
4634: You are standing on a wide path, on the top of the hills. But the forest is so dense, you can't see what really surrounds this forest. You guess the hills must continue to the north.
4635: You are standing on a wide path, on the top of the hills. But the forest is so dense, you can't see what really surrounds this forest. You guess the hills must continue to the north.
4636: You are standing in a dense forest, just along the road. You can see the forest continuing to the north, becoming higher and higher. The soil is so wet here that your shoes are all full of mud. Maybe you should take some time to wash them up ? You hear the soft sound of falling water just next to you. Time for a bath ? You look at your dirty equipment : really not presentable !
4637: A clear spring babbles as cool water trickles out of the ground.

You are in front of a steep cliff. It is impossible to go further. You notice a small brook. Some clear water springs out between the rocks; it runs down in an agreeable melody; you wish you could hear such music more often. The only exit is south.
4638:
A large brown snake with black patches is coiled here.
A black snake, with red markings, is lying here.

You are in a very small cavern; it is so small that you must bend over to enter it. After your pass, the dense vegetation which recovers the entry closes itself. You seem to be trapped; in the dark, you notice some living forms. You try to search for these moving shadows, but your light is really too weak.
4639: You are in small dark tunnel. You must bend over to advance further and you can feel the numerous rocks on the ground, scratching your poor legs. This passage seems very ancient, but well kept.
4641: You are in front of a dark chapel. You can't remember seeing such a strange architecture. It seems that the chapel was built not so long ago... You notice a perfect lack of beauty ! Should you really enter it ?
4642:
A small brown snake is slithering around here.
A small brown snake is slithering around here.
A small brown snake is slithering around here.

You are in a small hall. Some torches seem to be hanging on the side of the wall; they seem to have been just put off as you came in. You can't see through the darkness of the corridor; you fumble at nearly every step. Why is this room so unfriendly ? Obviously, you shouldn't stay here for long...
4643:
The corpse of an evil priest is lying here.
A pair of soft leather boots are on the ground.
A black pair of pants are on the ground.
An old-looking ring, covered with runes, lies here (glows blue).

This room was obviously built for one unique reason; they must use this room to hide themselves from the intruders. Maybe are you considered as an intruder. Maybe you will be punished in consequence...
4644: You've just entered the remains of a burned out hut once belonging to a human or possibly hobbit occupant. There are blackened orc arrows protruding from the wall along with other signs of battle. The fire which consumed this place has long since burned out. You can only make out the outlines of this once beautiful dwelling.
4646: There are some tracks here in the grass, leading to a small wooden lodge south of here on the plains. The smell of burned and charred wood reaches you from there. Thick brush among old pine trees growing in the north and east of here would slow down progress to a halt.
4647: This is a very dry, hard trail in the grass with some old footprints cast in it. The mud is so dry that there are cracks throughout the path. The trail ends behind a building to the north, and disappears in equally hard and dry land to the south.
4648: The ground here is very flat and soft, with lush green-grey grass in all directions. The air is fresh, carrying the scent of grass. North of here the plains are somewhat brushy, while the lands to the south and east become less vegetated. To the west the plains continue.
4649: A small grasshopper clings to a blade of grass, ready to spring.

The grass has a more brownish tone around here, but is still coarse and fairly high. Thin young plants of birch and aspen grow here, only a few yards high. The thin leaves they carry rattle in the wind, creating the sound of many hooves far away. The brush here continues to the north, while flatlands are to the west and south. A dark small building has been risen on the plains to the east.
4650: Thick bushes and tall grass make travelling difficult. To the north the bushes grow less dense, and high grass offering shelter to all sorts of wild creatures grows there instead. To the south, the open country seems safer.
4651: Bleak, fairly long grass grows here. Here and there you step into holes hidden beneath the grass, perhaps old graves or traps. These plains stretch out as far as you can see in all the regions to the south, and also a few miles northwards.
4652: A small grasshopper clings to a blade of grass, ready to spring.

The grass is mostly brown-red in this area. It is as if the blood that flowed here and the rust of hundreds of weapons has tainted it for centuries. A large barren circle where nothing grows is here in the middle of the plains, no doubt the site of a huge bonfire where corpses were burned.
4653: There is a lot of snow on the ground.

The grass here is tall, it waves along with the wind and makes some whistling noises. The sky is cloudy and it looks like it could possibly break out into rain. Though there are patches of blue up there. A few animals can be heard moving along in the grass. Most likely just some rabbits nothing that would pose a threat for anyone. However you never know with such tall grass.
4654: The plains are fairly uneven here, with slopes and mounds covered in the very common grey-green grass that grows all over these vast plains. You notice that a few mounds has been dug up, as if someone had been searching for something. The diggings are a few years old though, and grass is growing almost as thick as before in these places.
4655: This is an old round Arthedain watchtower. Five yards tall it is still intact a thousand years after it was raised, except that the stairs that once led up to the roof has collapsed and lie near the walls on the floor. No furniture remains here, if there ever has been any. The inside is empty and barren with packed earth. No arrow slits or windows adorn the walls, and the only light that enters here is through the door and the hole where the stairs entered the roof.
4656: These are the plains just north of a bend in the old east road. While grey-green grass covers most of the plains north and west of here, the landscape to the east is barren, and devoid of any visible wildlife. A few overgrown brooks are barely visible beneath the thick grass; they are only about a foot deep and seldom filled with water.

A sturdy bandit bodyguard stands here, eager to hack you to pieces.

For a few miles south and east are dead, barren plains, and the land here is also devoid of most vegetation. Dry, cracked earth with small tufts of grass cover this area. You notice that the mounds that cover this area very often are giant anthills, some of them over three yards in diameter. To the west and northwest the grassy plains continue.
4658: This is a few miles of barren land where nothing grows and nothing moves. Even the coarse grey grass that is so common in this region refuses to grow here. To the north and east the plains are more fertile and low scrubs are scattered about the land, while this desolate landscape continues eastward. South and west, the road makes a turn just in front of the Great Hedge.
4659: Although the earth is hard and dry, cracked up in deep fissures in many places, a few aspen trees manage to survive here north of the road. Birdsong can be heard from within the grove, and you catch a glimpse of a finch among the leaves and branches.
4660: A woody evergreen plant grows here, with many stems reaching upward.

Deep scars are cut in the dry earth here. Fissures and ravines have opened up the flatlands as if severe quakes have shook the area. You have no problem traversing these openings though, as they are only about a yard wide at most. The constant threat that the edges might collapse and trap you makes progress slow anyhow, and venturing further east would be very dangerous.
4661: The land here is cracked, and the further east you get the larger the fissures and ravines grow. Wherever you look, cracked land is before your eyes, but north and west grass grows with a grey tint. Far south you spot the hedge and the old east road.

To the north and west, the grass grows thicker and more colourful. On the plains west of here stands an old watchtower, with the door looking this way. South and east of here lie barren lands.
4663: A brass lantern has been set on the ground.

But the most impressive hill of all, thousand-foot Weathertop, rises to the east. The small hills themselves continue south.

Beyond them, to the southeast, you can see the conical top of Weathertop against the sky.

Further off, to the southeast, you can see the conical top of Weathertop against the sky.

To the south, the land rises and falls in much smaller hills and valleys. Beyond them, to the southeast, you can see the conical top of Weathertop against the sky.

The only simple entrance to the village is here, where an old battered gate still hangs on rusted hinges. No sounds can be heard from within; it's unlikely that anything would want to live in this place.

On the horizon a line of tall hills marches from the north to the southeast.

You emerge from yet another tangle to find yourself in a small clearing. After the thick forest, it is strange to see the sky clearly again. All around the clearing are more bushes, and above them the foliage of the trees.
4689: Trees grow thickly above you. Mosses and lichens grow on the trunks of hoary oak and ancient pine alike. Small plants and fungi grow in their shade. It is impossible to travel in a straight line, though you try. Only the sounds of the wind in the trees and of the activity of the forest life disturb the quiet.
4690: This forest is a tangle of small trees, some ancient, some young, and thick bushes. Small trails start and stop, without apparent purpose. Butterflies hover near wildflowers, and you can hear birds singing above.
4691: A woodpecker is here, tapping on a tree.

With effort, you make your way between the trees. Few are large, but they grow thickly. From time to time you think you have found a little path, and that makes travel easier for a little while, but always it ends nowhere.
4692: You are at the edge of a vast stretch of desolate plains. To the east, the thin grasses abruptly give way to large trees standing in a thick wood. To your north loom the Weather Hills, and one of their foothills rises out of the plains to the northwest. Over the tops of the trees you can see the flat head of Weathertop in the southeast.
4693: You are on a vast, desolate plain. The short grass could cover nothing larger than a bug. To the north a small hill rises out of the plains. It is as barren as they. 4694: You are on a vast, desolate plain. The short grass could cover nothing larger than a bug. A foothill lies to the northeast, and you can see a dark line of trees far off to the east. A line of great hills looms in the distance, forming a great arc from the north to the southeast.
4695: You are on a vast, desolate plain. Small stones and short thistles stick out among the thin grass. To your southwest stand the walls of a long-deserted town. A line of great hills looms in the distance, forming a great arc from the north to the southeast. But there is another feature much closer: to your southeast stand the walls of a human town. There are no signs of activity in or near it.

To the southeast a walled town still stands, the only sign of people on the plains. Much further off loom a line of great hills. They form a great arc from the north to the southeast.

4699: You are on a vast plain. Small stones stick out among the thin grass and thistles. The ground slopes gradually upwards towards a line of hills in the eastern distance. A small foothill rises but two leagues north. In the other directions, there are only flat plains.
4700: A colourful butterfly is fluttering around here.

You are near the northern edge of a vast stretch of desolate plains. The short grass could cover nothing larger than a bug. The Weather Hills loom in the distance in a line marching from the north to the southeast.
4701: You are at the northern edge of a vast stretch of desolate plains. The short grass could cover nothing larger than a bug. The line of the Weather Hills is still some leagues to the east, but one of their foothills rises directly to your north.
4702: You easily walk up the small hill's grassy sides. Looking about, you can see far and wide. A range of great hills, several times as tall as this one, recedes into the northern and southeastern distances. The closest of these hills is barely a league to the east. A forest grows northwest of the hill, and green plains stretch into the southern distance.
4703: This flat expanse of ground is dominated by the steep slope of a mighty hill in the east. To the south, the land rises, towards a much smaller hill, and it slopes gently westwards, towards a line of alders which marks the end of the plain. Around you, grasses and small plants grow. The plain continues northward.
4704:
A black crow flies low to the ground here, looking for carrion to eat.
A black crow flies low to the ground here, looking for carrion to eat.
A black crow flies low to the ground here, looking for carrion to eat.

Here, on a long stretch of flat land perhaps a league wide, the grasses and thistles of the the plains eke out a living among the stones. The grassland ends at a line of trees in the west and at the steep rise of a grey-green hill in the east. It extends south.
4705: You are standing on a gentle, grassy slope. It continues to your south, and slopes gradually westward up to the hilltop, where you can see some overgrown stone-works. But to the west the hillside falls away steeply towards a great grassy plain several hundred feet below you. The plains stretch into the distance. Beyond them the air is hazy.
4706: The peak of this hill is covered in stones and thin grass. A long stone wall has been built along the ridge where the land falls away to both east and west, and it comes from the south and passes over the hilltop. In many places it has fallen into grassy piles of stone during the long years since it was last maintained. The view is spectacular, and you can see far in all directions.
4707: An Old Stone Wall on a Hillside

The old wall follows the height of the land from the east and curves northward up to the top of the hill north of you. In many places it has fallen into mounds of grassy rubble over the long years, and vines grow on the parts which still stand. The stony ground about you supports only thin grasses and scattered wildflowers among the stones, but to your northwest a great shallow hollow in the centre of the hilltop is filled with bushes and tall grass. The hillside continues to the east, and only slopes down gently towards the southwest shoulder of the hill to your west, but in the south it ends abruptly in a great cliff beyond which grassy plains stretch far into the distance.
4708: You are standing on a gentle, grassy slope. It continues to your north, and slopes up gradually to the west, where you can see the ruins of a long stone wall To the west and to the south the hillside falls away in great cliffs. Beyond the cliffs lie great green plains. A small foothill interrupts them a league or so south of you, and in the western distance you can see a dark line of trees. Beyond that a haze in the air blocks your sight.
4709: You have reached the northeast-southwest ridge which forms the backbone of the Weather Hills. Someone long ago built a dike on its top. The hill slopes gently down to the west and the north, and a cliff blocks access to the woods that lie south. But for the dike there are no signs that speaking peoples ever came here, save perhaps a few places at its base where the grass grows more thickly.
4710: A colourful butterfly is fluttering around here.

Short grasses grow here, and there are many rocks of different sizes, but there are no trees. An earthen dike has been built along the highest part of the hill. The ground slopes gently downwards from the northeast to the west. It drops off abruptly to the south, and beyond you can see dark green treetops on the plain several hundred feet below you. Treeless green plains stretch into the distance beyond the western slope of the hill.
4711: The hillside is covered with short grasses and wildflowers. It slopes gently down to the plains to the west and the south. The view is spectacular. Other great hills rise northwest and southeast of you. Further southeast looms Weathertop, mightiest of all these hills. Closer, below you, lie a small hill to the southwest and the dark green treetops of a wood in the south. Beyond them flat green plains stretch towards the horizon.
4712: You are at the northeast corner of a vast stretch of desolate plains. The short grass could cover nothing larger than a bug. One of the Weather Hills rises steeply from the plain little more than a league to the northeast, and much smaller foothills lie to the east and to the northwest. You can see some old ruins on the Hill.
4713: In the lands to the west this would be a landmark, but here it is a mere foothill before the line of the Weather Hills. Its crown and slopes are treeless and rocky. To the west and south barren plains recede into the distance, while north and east stand two great hills.
4714: You are on a vast, desolate plain. Small stones stick out among the thin grass. To your east looms a line of great hills. You can barely discern ruined stone-works on their treeless sides. The pass between the nearest two is deep with steep sides, and in it you can see more ruined fortifications, green-grown with time. To the north a foothill rises from the plain and to the west and south there is only the plain, stretching into the distance.
4715: A colourful butterfly is fluttering around here.

You are on a vast, desolate plain. Small stones stick out among the thin grass. To your east a line of great hills looms. Like the plain they are barren and treeless. The pass between the nearest two is deep with steep sides. To the northeast a foothill rises, but to west and south there is only the plain, stretching into the distance.
4716: The garden snake slithers harmlessly here.

You are on a vast plain. The vegetation is sparse - grass, thistles, and other weeds - but during the summer it supports many insects and birds. A line of great hills looms in the distance, forming a great arc from the north to the southeast. In the other directions, there are only flat plains.
4717: You are on a vast, desolate plain. Small stones stick out among the thin grass. To your east looms a line of great hills. They are barren and treeless. Closer, small foothills rise from the plain about a league to the north and to the east. To the west and to the south, the plains stretch on until the sky meets the grass.
4718: You are at the eastern edge of a vast, desolate plain. Not far to the north, the steep slopes of a huge hill rise towards the sky. The plains continue a little less than a league eastwards, forming a bay between the northern hill, another giant in the east, and a much smaller hill which rises gently from the grass to the southeast. To the west and to the south there are only plains, stretching away to meet the sky at the horizon.
4719: The plains here wash up against the hills, forming a small inlet, with great hills of the main line of the Weather Hills some distance yet to the north and east and a relatively small foothill just to the south. The bottom of this valley is bare of any plant larger than the short grass.
4720: You can see far from the top of this small, grassy hill. Great hills rise steeply to the north, the northeast and far to the east. You can see a small tower on the top of the northern one. To the southeast a thick wood covers the ground in darkness. Beyond it, there is another hill in the distance. To the south, to the west, and to the northwest the green plains stretch on, featureless.
4721: You are in a vast, desolate plain. The short grass could cover nothing larger than a bug. To the east a small foothill rises out of the sea of grass. A line of great hills looms in a great arc from the north to the southeast.
4722: You are on a vast, desolate plain. Small stones stick out among the thin grass. A line of great hills looms in the distance, forming a great arc from the north to the southeast. Closer, but still a league to the east, a smaller hill rises gently. In the other directions, there are only the plains, stretching featurelessly into the distance.
4723: You are on a vast plain. A hobbit might call it desolate, for there are no signs of inhabitation, and no trees or food-bearing plants. An elf could sit here for hours with pleasure, watching the patterns of the clouds and the bumblebee methodically fertilising a small patch of yellow flowers nearby. A line of great hills looms in the distance, forming a great arc from the north to the southeast. To the west and to the south there are only the plains, stretching into the distance.
4724: This must have once been the village square. On each side are derelict buildings - houses and shops. The ground was once cobbled, probably creating a smooth but firm pavement, but time hasn't been kind to it. Here and there stones are missing, and those that remain are chipped and dirty. On one side of the square, a building still remains in a relatively good state. A sign hangs from an outstretching bar, squeaking in the breeze. The worn street continues eastwards.
4725: The name of this inn is now ironically suitable. Although it has stood far better than any of the other buildings in the village, it still couldn't be said it was in a good state. Rotting chairs are sprawled on the floor, rusty candlesticks still holding stubby candles beside them. What still remains intact, however, are the stairs leading up to the rooms. The rooms themselves haven't fared so well - only one still remains.
4726:
The ghostly form of a young woman stands here in despair.
A tall, thin ghost paces the room, looking about malevolently.

You shudder to think what kind of guests would now stay in this room. The roof has long since fallen in, collapsing on the torn and decaying beds. As you look over the beds, you're shocked to see beneath some rubble two skeletons large enough to be Human or Elven. A feeling of death surrounds the room, enough to place fear into the most evil heart.
4729: A circular stone well has been built here.

Here, the small village ends. This must have been where most of the villagers lived, as from what can still be made from the buildings, most look like places of dwelling. Also, a quaint stone well sits tidily in the centre of the road, likely placed to be most convenient to the inhabitants. None of the buildings are now safe to enter, and the village wall prevents any exit other than back west.
4730:
A beer bottle has been left here.
A large stone chest is here.
A beer barrel has been left here.
An ancient fungus smothers the boulders.
An ancient fungus smothers the boulders.

Down a few stone steps is this small chamber. The walls are made of stone, so it has managed to survive better than many of the wooden constructions outside. This may have been some kind of treasure room for the innkeeper, and also a storage room. Judging by the cool air and the cobwebs around the door, it looks like this room hasn't been disturbed in a long time.
4731: The land dips here, forming a little bowl on the top of the hill. The grasses grow taller here, and bushes stand out among them. Insects hum and chirp and buzz and birds sing. Some large animal has been digging among the ground. But there is still no surface water here.
4732: An Old Stone Wall on a Hillside

This hill's top forms a shallow bowl several miles across. You are standing on the bowl's southern rim. The rim is fairly flat, sloping down gently towards the hollow northwards and towards the shoulder of the hill in the east, and continuing westwards. To the south the hill slopes very steeply down into a narrow valley, beyond which another hill rises. An old stone wall is built along the top of the rim, running west-east. Vines grow on those parts of it which have not collapsed.
4733:
A tall stag is here, grazing peacefully.
A fallow deer is grazing peacefully here.
A fallow deer is grazing peacefully here.

The broad hillside is fairly flat. It slopes gently upwards to south and east. You can see another hilltop across a deep but narrow valley which lies north of here. In the west the hill ends abruptly.
4734: A large wall once blocked passage from the East here. Now many of its stones form grassy heaps on the hillside, and what yet stands could be climbed over in many places. The hillside slopes gently up to the wall. It ends at a rocky height in the southeast and follows the ridge down into the pass north of you. The pass is narrow and another hilltop is almost level with you on the other side. A tower has been built at the top of the height.
4735: You have come to a grassy field which seems to be at the top of the world. The ground falls steeply away from you in three directions. To the north, a steep climb leads down to a deep valley between this hill and the one north of it. In the west the hill ends at a great cliff. Grassy plains far below you stretch into a blue distance. To the south, the field slopes more gently down towards the hill's southwestern shoulder. Only to the east does the level field continue.
4736:
A nightingale is here, chirping a sweet melody.
A lone hawk soars high above you.
A finch flies low above the ground.

Flat plains with little else than grass growing upon them continue in all quarters from here. Slowly rolling past old battlefields to the northern edge of the plains, south towards the old east road, and west towards the midgewaters, these plains cover an area of about a fifty square leagues. Not much seems to be moving upon them, but you can spot birds of prey in the sky, perhaps hunting rabbits and fieldmice that might live in the vicinity.
4737: A lone hawk soars high above you.

The old east road runs south of here, and the thick hedge follows it close on the south side. This is on the edge of vast grasscovered plains that stretch out in all directions on the north side of the road. A carcass surrounded by flies and inhabited by worms lies rotting here, deceased a few days ago. The stench can be felt a hundred yards away to the sensitive nose.
4738: Prickly, white-stemmed plants, with blue flower heads grow in abundance.

Coarse grey-green grass grows in all directions here. Once the battlefields where the armies of Cardolan and Arthedain armies fought off the witchkings' blood must have flowed abundantly here. Small, shy blue flowers grow plentiful here, a strong contrast to the history of these plains.
4739: Dullish grey-green grass grow here on very white soil. Perhaps so many bones have been crushed here that the ground has changed colour. Plains stretch far away in all directions.
4740: Low bushes with black stems and fat green leaves grow sparsely here in the grey short grass. This is the northern reach of the battleplains, as the vegetation grows too dense to the north for any such activities. In all other directions these grass covered plains continue though.
4741:
A black and white cat is playing in the grass.
A small grasshopper clings to a blade of grass, ready to spring.
A small grasshopper clings to a blade of grass, ready to spring.

These plains are full of simple grass, a good resting place for your animals. The sun is beautiful here and the winds make the grass dance along the ground. A few rabbits scurry out of sight and some other squirrels roam around by their trees. The ground is nice and flat, easing your feet as you walk. The clouds fly by dancing in the blue skies.
4742: A smiling hobbit child is playing around here.

There is nothing but tall grass as far as you can see. Clouds make shadows along the ground as they are whisked around by the wind. Rabbits hop around here gnawing on the grass as you walk by. This is a very calm and peaceful place. The tranquility of the rustling grass and clear blue sky calls to you like the homes of your childhood.
4743: Here is another patch of shrubs along the trail. This part of the land though does not look like it is meant for traveling upon. Though there are quite a few berries along here, there isn't much in the way of anything else around here. It may be just a good idea to head back up towards the trail.
4744: Here is a little patch of land near a trail. The ground here is covered with weeds and it feels like some of them maybe making you to itch. This is not a pleasant place to spend any time. The trail looks more well tended and that would be a better place to spend your travels.
4745: The river makes its way along and you feel a breeze going up your back. The water is a murky-looking green, and even though this is a rather small river, you cannot really see the bottom of it. The currents change very suddenly, maybe you could catch some bass or something. There is for sure something in this river.
4746: A sharp-eyed hawk is here stalking some prey.

Insects buzz around your head as you slosh your way through the thick mud. The putrid smell of decomposition assaults your nostrils as you make your way around. Swatting the annoying insects away from your eyes, you cannot see much of anything else living here. Only a few dead trees break the monotony of the brown slush beneath your feet.
4747: A placid pond is here, inviting you to take a refreshing drink.
This is a small pond where whoever tends these fields most likely gets his water from. It looks quite safe to drink and from what you have seen of the farmer's work that is probably true.
4748:
A cow stands here, chewing her cud.
A sturdy pack horse is standing here.

You have entered a fenced in yard of some sort. From the looks of it, this seems to be part of a farm. To whom it might belong you are not at all certain. The grass is thick and lush here and, in the odd patches of sod, you detect tracks that could be from horses or cows. Perhaps this is an animal pen.
4749:
There is some snow on the ground.
A round turnip is growing here.
A small grasshopper clings to a blade of grass, ready to spring.

Half buried in the dirt, you notice bits of brightly colored wood that seem to resemble childrens' toys. The ground is flat and the grass smoothed over, as if trampled by many feet. In fact, as you listen, you can hear laughter coming from the north. Stumbling over the toys, you are able to make your way through this field.
4750:
A loaf of bread has been left here.
A loaf of bread has been left here.

You have entered the humble abode of a small farmer's family. The children are all out running around playing and the farmer can be found around here somewhere tending after his farm. The hut is a small building made of logs from the forests up north. It seems to be sturdy and the family seems to be a friendly one.
4751:
There is some snow on the ground.
A small grasshopper clings to a blade of grass, ready to spring.

Every where you look you see nothing but bushes and wild grass. Insects fly about, dancing and playing. The flowers smell wonderful as you tread on through the tall grass. The sounds in the air are quiet and peaceful. It is nice except for all the insects biting your arms and legs.
4752:
There is some snow on the ground.
A tiny, harmless centipede is here.
A tiny, harmless centipede is here.
A small grasshopper clings to a blade of grass, ready to spring.
A black and white cat is playing here.

Here is just a little grassy hideaway, a little pond is down in the centre. The sun reflects off the water. Animals can be heard relaxing in this nice cool spot. The flowers around here are blooming and beautiful. The land is covered in lush green grass. This is one spot that you could just relax and sleep in forever.
4754:
There is some snow on the ground.
A detached red rose is lying here.
A detached white rose is lying here.
A cute rabbit is here.

The flowers in this patch are all multicolored and smell a wonderful variety of smells. The patch is natural but has a well kept look to it. Running through here and just frolicking in the flowers sounds actually like a nice vacation from your long adventure.
4755: A smiling hobbit child is playing around here.

There is nothing but tall grass as far as you can see, clouds make shadows along the ground as they are whisked around by the wind. There are rabbits moving around here gnawing on the grass as you walk by. This is a very calm peaceful place. The rustling of the grass along with the blue sky makes it a place that you would want to make a home around here.
4757: A large Oak tree is here old and looking almost dead. It looks to be a fort for some children but they aren't around right now. The tree is large and black and roots are sticking out of the ground every where. Some flowers grow by the bottom of the tree and little grass near it as well. Very few animals seem to be moving around here.
4758: The plains around here seem to go on for ever and you could easily get lost in them. All the land you seem able to see is that of tall grass. The few trees in this area all look alike. A feeling of boredom strikes you as you look out over this plain looking landscape.
4759: A smiling hobbit child is playing around here.

The grass here is tall, it waves along with the wind and makes some whistling noises. The sky is cloudy and it looks like it could possibly break out into rain. Though there are patches of blue up there. A few animals can be heard moving along in the grass. Most likely just some rabbits nothing that would pose a threat for anyone. However you never know with such tall grass.
4760: The grass here is tall, it waves along with the wind and makes some whistling noises. The sky is cloudy and it looks like it could possibly break out into rain. Though there are patches of blue up there. A few animals can be heard moving along in the grass. Most likely just some rabbits nothing that would pose a threat for anyone. However you never know with such tall grass.
4761: The trees around here seem to be littered with bird's nests. This looks to be a form of sanctuary with them. They eye you closely as you enter their area. You can see all different kinds of birds here. Many of them are flying off. Feathers are floating everywhere and the birds' screeches are the only thing you are able to hear.
4762: There is nothing but tall grass as far as you can see, clouds make shadows along the ground as they are whisked around by the wind. There are rabbits moving around here gnawing on the grass as you walk by. This is a very calm peaceful place. The rustling of the grass along with the blue sky makes it a place that you would want to make a home around here.
4763: There is nothing but tall grass as far as you can see; clouds make shadows along the ground as they are whisked around by the wind. There are rabbits moving around here nibbling on the grass as you walk by. This is a very calm and peaceful place.
4764: You lie on a small hill, the grass is nice and green to the touch. The wind blows through the nearby trees. A squirrel moves close to you as you have invaded it's tree. The branches of the tree make creaking noises as the wind moves through them. The grass looks like an ocean with each wave another breath of the wind. The sun is setting over the hill casting red and orange rays dancing into the sky.
4765: Left Wing of a Dunadan Mansion

This is the room where the inhabitants of this mansion cook and sleep. While the iron bars in the old fireplace have been recently replaced, the beds are rudimentary and dirty. On the floor someone has drawn large intersecting circles in different colours and a mirror of polished steel is located next to the exit. Other than these features the room is unadorned.
4766: Low, dry and brittle grey-green grass covers this tableland. A few white flowers are hiding in the grass, sometimes forming small patches. The ground drops fastly off to the north, while it remains flat and easily travelled in the other directions.
4767:
A wild bull seems ready to charge you.
A small grasshopper clings to a blade of grass, ready to spring.

Low grey grass covers this plateau. While the ground inclines too sharply to be passable to the north, you could probably make it down to the marshes west of here. In the summer grasshoppers chirp in the grass, while during winter the occasional hole in the snow indicates some kind of subterranean animal. The plateau stretches out southeast for a few miles, flat and featureless all the way to the edges.
4768:
The wild ox seems ready to charge you.
The wild ox seems ready to charge you.
The wild ox seems ready to charge you.

This is just above the easternmost regions of Midgewater. You can see the swamps down below a sheer drop down to the west. You are about twenty yards up, and swallows circle at about this height catching mosquitoes over the murky waters. The grass grows thick here, and the plateau is green and flat for a long distance in all directions but the west.
4769: Very flat and featureless the plateau continues in all directions from here. Sparse bushes try to survive, begging for rain during hot summers. They have thin branches and seldom carry anything else than bitter, vaguely poisonous fruits.
4770: This is the eastern part of a very flat plateau, all covered in green-grey grass. Looking east, you see a few abandoned structures down on lower plains, and beyond that the ground rises towards the weather hills. Many bushes grow in an area near this eastern edge, which is very steep, and they intertwine in such a way as to make them impossible to penetrate.
4771: Thick brush covers the northern part of this plateau, and there is little hope of getting through them. You notice uprooted grass along a wide streak here, as if large animals had passed by in a horde lately. The ground slopes slowly down to the east.
4772: This is the southeastern peak of the plateau, rising to a height of about thirty yards above the plains to the south and east. A watchtower in wood has been raised here long ago, in order to overlook these plains. Nowadays nothing more than the basic structure is left standing, and the floor and roof lie in a rotting heap on the ground. You can see the thin line of the Old East Road far south and the hedge rising just beyond it. The ground slopes slowly downwards in that direction, while the cliff is far too steep to be climbable to the east.
4773: A black wolf pads restlessly, looking for its next prey.

A small brook starts here and leads down the southern side, carrying off some water down to the lower plains when it has rained heavily. Some heather grows nearby. The slope to the south should not be too hard to manage, even if it might take a while.
4774: The plateau has a very unsecure and steep slope down its western side. A few low pine trees grow on the edge. They have a hard time clinging on to the loose soil, and their roots are bared as rain erodes the plateau and washes it down into the marshes below. You notice small stubs hidden in the grass, so probably quite a forest grew here once. The plateau dips down to the south also, but less dramatic. Down there are wet bushy plains.
4775:
A cluster of dark green, feathery fronds flourishes in the shade.
A bullfrog is standing here.

This is probably the easternmost tongue of Midgewater. Lots of bushes and ferns grow on these soggy plains. There is no clear water here though, only the occasional feet-deep mudhole. You hear the quaking of frogs all around, and this is probably a perfect breedingplace for them. A sloping bank up to the north will take you to dryer grounds.
4776: A cluster of dark green, feathery fronds flourishes in the shade.

The tableland to the north has left quite a few large stones here at its base, as the earth has been eroded and washed away out on the plains during the centuries. Among them live many ferns, and for some reason there are moss- covered logs here also.
4777: You are amidst fairly thick and high grey grass which beckons in the wind. These plains slowly ascend a tableland to the north, and turn into bushland to the west. South of here is more of this rich grass, and beyond this you can outline the hedge following the whole southern horizon.
4778: You are on flat, grassy plains below the southeast corner of a plateau. This feaureless landscape continues to the east. West of here, where this tableland slopes down and enters the plains, they grow bushier and more vegetated. No signs of humans ever living in the near vicinity can be seen, but a few miles to the north you can outline the silhouette of a structure of sorts. The ground gets rougher to the south, more wrinkled with dips and small hills.
4779: The old ruin of a house stands here on the middle of these empty plains. Although the building probably is no more than a few hundred years old and therefore was built after the wars, it must have seen its share of misery. Any inhabitants are long gone, and the estate is in a state of permanent decay. The fields surrounding it grow weeds, the well is filled with soil, and the outhouses are probably burnt down. The only thing that remains and witnesses of a once very well-tended farm is the roof. Still supported by ten thick wooden beams, it defies storms, snow and heat. Covered with thick grass, it is still in such a good shape as to keep the ground below dry under even heavy rainfalls. During winter, though, snow will blow in through the sides and cover the rotting walls and the broken jars and pots that still lie decaying on the floor. A fence once surrounded this place, but now only a few poles remain standing a few hundred yards out on the plains.
4780: Bushes grow close to the sheer cliff of the plateau to the west here. Some cling as well to the cliffside that rises fifteen yards or more. A ravine seems to lead west, well hidden by these bushes. The entrance is only about two yards wide, and hard to spot. East, north and south are plains, and a mile or so south the skeleton of a building can be seen.
4781: The flats you are on stretch out seemingly endlessly towards the south and the east, while the plains slope gradually upwards to the west, and forms a plateau. The ground crepitates as you move, and you notice there are many old branches and twigs hidden in the thick grass. You pass many stumps, so this once must have been quite a forest.
4782:
A sharp-eyed hawk is here stalking some prey.
A cute rabbit is here.

You have entered a rather harsh patch of shrubs, the shrubs are really beginning to tear at your clothes. This is a rather difficult area to move through. However it doesn't seem to last very long and nice land is in sight not far away.
4783:
There is some snow on the ground.
A large thorny branched shrub is growing here.
On the shrub, there are six piles of blackberries.
A black and white cat is playing here.
A smiling hobbit child is playing around here.

There are some wild blackberries growing around here. The shrubs are wooded and covered in small pricklers that make picking their fruit hard to do. However there look to be some really ripe blue and black berries here along with a few other type of berries.
4784: A small grasshopper clings to a blade of grass, ready to spring.

The grass here is long and tall. Little trees dot the area forming a kind of a path. Underneath the trees, small plants, perhaps ferns, grow, forming a sort of hedge. The trees are small and just provide enough presence to unnerve you. The animals around here are small and they tend to stay hidden from you.
4785: On these plains, where once fierce battle stood between Arthedain forces and the hordes of the witchking, only small, barely visible mounds recognizable as graves witness of the bloodshed. The air seems thick and hard to breath however hard the wind blows. The spirits of the deceased perhaps feel disturbed by your presence.
4786: Grey-green grass covers these ancient battlegrounds. Some old stones mark the corners of an old house that once must have stood here. Living must have been poor, as armies probably ransacked this homestead on every passing by. Some clover still grows in the old fields where cattle once were kept. The only sign of a well is the ring of stones a few yards south of the building.
4787: These are the outskirts of the old battlefields. Thick, coarse grey-green grass cover the ground, and you trample in a hidden mound full of rusted metalpieces. The plain continues in all directions, with not much moving upon it.
4788:
A finch flies low above the ground.
A lone hawk soars high above you.

The grass is fairly heavy to walk in, as it is about two feet tall around here. The land is flat in all directions, and you notice very little around here that moves across the land, except for a few rabbit ears sticking up in the grass now and then.
4789:
A brown fox is here, looking for some rabbits to chew up.
A finch flies low above the ground.

This is flat land with grey-green grass, stretching out in all quarters except the southwest where the old east road runs past some ashen trees. Some kind of campsite has been set up there next to the road. You travel easily here, almost bouncing along, as the ground is soft and spongy.
4790: South of here the road goes in east- and westwardly directions. West is a bushy area with many small depressions, while the endless plains you are on continue to the north and east. The only thing that really stands out around here are a few higher bushsprouts, boldly declaring their right to live here in the thick grass.
4791: You are among the small dips north of the old east road. Bushes with brittle grey leaves grow in plentitude here. Tiny red and yellow flowers compete with the grass and the bushes about shadow in the deeper parts of the depressions. Although this is one of the lower parts of the plains you can find no water here except after a rain, when the ground becomes soggy.
4792: Tall, rich grass grows upon this soft ground. Walking is strenuous while at foot. Many bushes grow near the road south of here, with thick, moist leaves that will glisten on sunny days.
4793: A black pond of water is here.

A few small groves grow far apart here on the plains, mainly birch and alder trees.You have found one with a pool. Ten feet down it lies, with few fatbladed flowers floating on the surface. As the banks leading down to the pond are very slippery, you have to approach it with care so you do not fall into the water.
4794: A swarm of mosquitoes is here, humming around you.

These plains north of the old east road is fairly bushy, with moist ground. Someone has tried to dig a ditch, either to feed the plains with water or drain them, but the project must have been abandoned and the ditch is only about a mile or so. The road runs just south of here, making a bend towards the east and south.
4795: Grey and featureless plains seem to roll on forever here. No signs of water can be seen, and the air trembles from heat on hot days. In wintertime these plains are just as ruthless, with nowhere to hide from the biting frosty winds.
4796: A brown fox is here, looking for some rabbits to chew up.

This is far out on the plains, with little civilization in sight. A house can be seen far away to the west, but that is all. Grey-green coarse grass covers the land, rolling in the wind like waves at sea. A long way from here on the northeastern horizon you can discern the dark outlining of the Weather Hills. On the northern horizon lie more mountains, beyond what looks like a forest. South is the old east road and the hedge, while behind a plateau to the west lurk the dark and devious Midgewater marshes.
4797: A brown fox is here, looking for some rabbits to chew up.

Here lies the stone foundation of a keep or mansion of some sort. Complete with kitchen, stables, yard, and a diversity of rooms and halls this must have been the home of some quite prominent person. Unless the stones have been carried for use elsewhere, this building must used wood for walls and ceilings. No objects will be found here, as the place must have been abandoned about a thousand years ago, around the time of the witchking wars. Also you see no signs of any cellar or subterranean construction, except for the well which is filled with earth and overgrown with grass. A mountain ash grows where there once were household fields, carrying a few dark red fruits for any hungry birds.
4798: A brown fox is here, looking for some rabbits to chew up.

Once a probably very beautiful deciduous forest must have grown here as the land is flat and open. Stubs and a lot of old twigs and branches are hidden in the grass among the bushes. Grey grass covered plains stretch out towards the south and east, while the ground gets higher a few miles to the west. North are thick bushes, and you cannot hope to come far in that direction.
4799: The river has gotten rather shallow and the edges of the bank are rather muddy. To the west there looks to be a pond that you can possibly go into. The river is a really murky dark green. Highly unlikely anything lives in this area. You would be better off just leaving this area and heading on with your adventure. Heading towards the pond might be a good idea. To the east you can enter the river much better. The river seems to get a little wider as you go east.
4800: The River seems to be widening alittle. It is rather murky and muddy. Moving is not an easy feat to do with the current so slow. You find that putting your feet in here would not be a pleasant experience. It is best just to keep moving and find someplace to get off this river. The breeze in the air is rather chilling. The sun is heading off, this is not a good place to be spending a night. Better that you keep moving.
4801: The river is now wide and fairly slow, it is probably best to just let your craft float if you are headed down river, and just sit back and relax. A few bass can be seen swimming along in the river, and something else as well though the movements are hard to tell what they are, they look like twigs off a fallen log. Timber lays around the shore line, that is most likely the case.
4802: You are in the Green River. The river for some strange reason, has a green color to it, maybe this is why they named it the Green River? It is also cool and the bottom is too cloudy to see. Something greenish seems to move along the bottom of the river. You might be curious but you are not that curious to see what is down there. The breeze keeps you floating and daydreaming of past adventures. Best just to keep daydreaming and float on down the river.
4804: You are rafting through a nice calm river. Moving circles in the calm water with your hands, you slowly drift into thought. You could just let the raft take you anywhere it leads. The current seems to have some irregular movement in it though. The water is a murky greenish color and a few logs float along in here with you. Some insects can be seen dancing along the water, skimming from log to log.
4805:
There is a lot of snow on the ice.
A ferocious warg is here, snarling angrily.

The river is rather murky. You can not see the bottom of it even though you know it isn't all that deep. The sand in the river seems to be drifting about as if there is something moving along the bottom. Here it looks as if you could take a dive down, to see what it is that is under the water. The mud though looks rather bad near the bottom and the water is all too quiet to want to dive down there. It is probably best just to go on and forget about diving in here.
4806: There is a lot of snow on the ice.

The woods along the bank can be seen quite well from here. You notice that the water is getting darker as you head down river. The currents are erractic and they don't seem to ever move in a normal pattern. The insects along the side of the river move slightly along the top of the waters. The water moves ever so slow. Best that you keep yourself alert, you never know what might be lurking in the waters below....
4807: This area is darkened by the tall trees along the bank of the river. The cool breeze chills you. You can feel the waters coolness on your ankles when you dip your feet in. You could go for a swim in the clear green waters of the river. However, the moving of shapes in the water suggest that it would not be such a smart idea here to do.
4808: The river at this point is crisp and rather clear. It is still dark and green and shapes can be seen moving along in the waters. They look just like twigs or something but advice says not to just jump right into the waters. You can float down the river and just relax or paddle up it and see what is at its end. Right now though you can not help but sip the cool clear green water of this river. It refreshes you from your long days journey.
4809: A ferocious warg is here, snarling angrily.

The river is quite clear here. The rocks in the water along for a slightly swifter current than what looks like is headed down south. Headed north though the river doesn't look as if it is as peaceful and calm. Best here is just to get out and wade or swim through the river heading up north. The river looks to be turning more into a creek than a river as you head north. Then again with the sun moving down. You could be mistaken. In either case, right now you feel like you want to just take a nap with the sounds of the rushing water all around you.
4810: Surrounded by fifteen yards sheer rockwalls with only a two yards wide ravine leading out to the plains east of here, this valley is well hidden. Thick brush grows on the rim, hiding it also from detection from above. Pine trees cover most of the hundred yards wide space, while a large wooden mansion lies below the north valleyside. A faint path leads through the trees up to the stairs and the porch. The house lies silent like a large resting animal, hungrily awaiting foolhardy intruders to force its half-rotten frontdoor and go astray within its leaky wooden walls.
4811:
A guestbook lies here, its pages yellow and fragile.
Some delicate brass lamps are attached to the walls here.

Two red carpets lie across the blankpolished black floor in this large hallroom. The ceiling is white, with two unlit large lustres hanging in heavy chains. Straight ahead a large stairway leads up to the second floor, made of dark brown wood with sturdy banisters, and one of the carpets lead from the front door up the stairs. The other carpet runs between a doubledoor in the west wall and another more plain door in the east. Four lamps are attached to the wall, which also is adorned with masks and garments. A small bell is protruding from the wall beside a large curtain on the left side of the stairs, and just to the right of the frontdoor stands a small pulpet with an open book, a quill, and an inkjug.
4812:
Some delicate brass lamps are attached to the walls here.
A large, dusty alcove sits in a wall, smelling of soot.

Parquet floor covers this room, worn out between a brown drape in the north wall and the large table in the middle of the room. A white and brown wooly carpet is spread below the table, and one large seat is at each end. A fireplace is in the northeast corner, and fresh flowers spread a sweet scent throughout the room from their place in a vase in front of it. In the ceiling which is crisscrossed by many thick fillets of chestnut is an unlit lustre. Almost the whole southern wall is covered by a huge painting. Everything is in very good shape, and meticulously attended.
4813:
Some delicate brass lamps are attached to the walls here.
A stove stands against one wall here.
A circular stone well has been built here.

This kitchen has every utensil there is, with the wall covered with shelves full of pots, jars, sets of knives, spoons and forks, glassware, plates and all the other things a cook might need. The wooden floor has a patch of stone just in front of the stove to prevent fires from starting. A small well is actually drilled in the northeastern corner, near the sink.
4814: Some delicate brass lamps are attached to the walls here.

In this room dark wood has been used for floor, walls and furniture. Bright coloured cloth cover the sofas, armchairs, tables and walls though, lighting it up a little. This room must have been intended for recreation, relaxing, and learned discussions. A pair of large thick oaken doors lead north.
4815:
An old-looking ring, covered with runes, lies here.
A black and silver surcoat lies here.

This is a large room, almost thirty yards long and twenty yards wide. A trampled barren earthfloor and wooden walls that lean inwards on the eastern, western and northern sides surround a large platform made of stone near the northern end. Low wooden benches stand at both sides of a path leading up to the platform, so this must once have been some kind of meeting hall. The architecture here is different from the one used in the house itself, and this part is probably the older. A small balcony hangs out from the southern wall about ten yards up, and an archway seems to lead back into the building. A thick rope runs from this ledge over the platform and ends in the northern wall, and a basket of sorts hangs down from the rope above the platform.
4816: The darkened figure of a once noble being lingers here.

About five yards wide, this platform hovers in the air several yards up from the earth covered ground below supported by a single thin stone pillar. A dark dome with wooden walls surrounds this flat surface, and any words uttered reverberate strongly throughout the darkness.
4817:
Some delicate brass lamps are attached to the walls here.
A large, dusty alcove sits in a wall, smelling of soot.
A large bookshelf sits against the wall.

All the walls in this room are covered with bookshelves, except in the north- west where a clean fireplace occupies the corner, and on the southern wall is a painting resembling an old man sternly watching what goes on in this room. An inscription runs all along the top of the walls, just below the ceiling. The only furniture in this room is a pleasant armchair with a small table standing in the middle of the room upon the red, strangely patterned floor.
4818: You are standing in a small basket hanging from a rope attached to the southern and northern walls of this large dome. The basket jerks a little, and you cling to the ropes that support the wooden planks you are standing on.
4819: This hall is fairly empty and featureless. A blue shorthaired carpet covers the dark parquet floor, but no furniture except a pedestal with an empty pot has been placed here. All doors exiting this room has been barred shut with many thick planks, except for one leading north through an archway. Above the stairs leading down south hangs a dramatic painting on the wall, depicting a battlefield.
4820: When stepped upon, this balcony complains with a stern creak. However built with thick logs running into the south wall, the planks are thin and brittle and the whole structure leans slightly downwards. A slender railing runs along its edge, but there is reasonable doubt whether it would support the weight of more than a small dog. A large wooden dome lies northwards and beneath you, with a platform in the middle. A thick rope is fastened in a hook just above the archway to the south, and passes over the platform to the barely visible opposite wall. A basket hangs in a tackle from this thick rope. Another, thinner rope is attached to a small winch on the railing, with the other end attached to the basket. The point seems to be to make a sensational entrance to the platform by flying in the air standing in the basket.
4906: A brown fox is here, looking for some rabbits to chew up.

A forest shaded in by heavy trees blackening out the sunlight, creatures must use this area for an entrance to the river to get something to drink. A murky green river lurks towards the east from here. The shadows dance along the trees from your lantern, music can seem to be heard off in the distance. This very well could have been an ancient burial ground, the strangness of the land along with that cool breeze from the river, sends chills down your spine.
4908: The trees whistle with the wind, rustling can be heard all around you. This is still a dark and mysterious area. The trees are huge and move to block out all possibility of light. There are scurrying sounds all around you, looking about though you can not see anything. The ground is damp and is mucking at the feet. As far as you can see there are nothing but trees to look at.
4909: A sturdy plant grows to a height of almost a yard.

Claw marks litter the trees along here, this is some predator's territory and it seems you may have entered it. Exits out of here are difficult as that the trees blacken out any light from above. The soil is moist and soft to the touch making stepping cool and the breeze chills your body.
4913:
A ferocious warg is here, snarling angrily.
A brown fox is here, looking for some rabbits to chew up.

Here are the woods blackened by the high limbs of age old trees, this land is full of noises and night predators can be heard devouring their little day prey. This is not a good place to set up a camp. A few old relics seem to lie scattered about, as if a hunting party had been through here.
4914: The woods here shade you from the sunlight above. It is hard to tell if there is even any daylight. Night animals roam around here freely preying on poor travellers who are not well versed in forest life. Movements seem to be coming and going all around you. This does not seem like a very safe place to stay too long. Sounds of crunching can be heard all over the forest. The darkness and the dense trees make it hard to tell which way you should go.
4915: A ferocious warg is here, snarling angrily.

Along here there comes the sounds of a slow flowing river nearby. The woods are closed in by many trees blocking out the sunlight. The wind moves through the trees making whining sounds that seem to cover up a more real noise. The ground being soft and moist makes this not a comfortable place to rest.
4916: A Murky Forest along the River

Along here the soil is soggy and the trees are as black as the land itself. The woods are full of animals moving about, as you turn around quickly you see a small wolf devour a rabbit. The land is dominated by the night creatures. The river can be heard not too far away. There you will find something to drink and a place to rest.
4917: A Dark Forest along the River

Along here you can hear the gently moving waters, the ground before you is rough and hard to move along. The night give way to night predators, however, you realise that it is still day time. The trees are so close and huge that they black out any possibilities of seeing the sun. Night animals lurk around but every where you turn you see nothing but trees.
4918: As you look ahead to what you have just entered. You see many little hills. The possibility of Hobbits living here is a good one. Though there hasn't been any really seen yet. There could be still some in among those hills. As you know the hobbits like to live in the hills. This could be a good place to gain some more supplies. The hills are sloped gently and travel is easy on them. The grass is soft and green and walking here you can just relax and daydream as you move along.
4919: A grey wolf is here, snarling aggressively.

This hill is much higher than the rest of them and you can see for miles. A few trees cover the hills and down toward the south one giant tree seems to have provided shelter for old travlers and new adventurers. There could be a good place to rest. Here though is nothing but grass, while the flowers are pretty to look at, your attention can't be kept here for very long.
4920: A grey wolf is here, snarling aggressively.

This trail looks like very familiar. You seem to be heading towards what sounds like a river. Toward the east there looks to be a possible river. You could head back north, the trail near the hills is smooth and without much dangers. It seems to be a well traveled trail. With adventurers on it often going to and from many different parts of the world. You could take the somewhat old looking path that leads along the flatlands to the west. Towards the east there seems to be an old path leading down toward the river.
4921: Old armour lay strewn along this trail. Bones of dead warriors are scattered around. The charcoal remains of some of them can be seen near burnt ground. Once great swords lay broken in the rubble. The victors seem to have made a trail onward, though this one seems to have been laid to rest, an ancient burial ground. Along the trail lies a breast plate with an inscription.
4922: A ferocious warg is here, snarling angrily.

This hill is more of just a steep incline than a hill. The grass on here is a luscious green and the flowers are blooming. A few bees fly around here collecting nectar. The sound of birds can be heard playing amongst the tree. This is a lovely place for a rest. All around you you can see only more gentle hills and trees for shade.
4925: A Large Tree on Top of a Hill

A brown bear is sleeping here.
A brown bear is sleeping here.

A large tree stands here, of a size which can only be appreciated by walking all round its large base. Its wide canopy would surely provide some shelter from foul weather, or a welcome shade, on a hot sunny day, and the grass, which grows, thick and lush, among its tangled roots, would make a pleasant place to sit, or even take a nap.
4927: At the top of this hill you see nothing but more gentle hills, for some weary hobbits this could make a lovely place for a home. Around here is nothing but blue skies with few white clouds whisking around in the breeze. It is a place that is both relaxing and nice to explore, who knows what might be out there among the different hills.
4947: This is a narrow path which hugs the contour of the final hill of the chain of hills which are the Emyn Sul. The trail winds its way into the hills west from here, but cunningly it is disguised and also obscures any travellers. However on the further part of the trail south, climbers are not so fortunate. As the trail ascends the north-west slope of Weathertop, anyone becomes quite conspicuous, visible for miles around.
4948: Southern End of the Weather Hills
A grey hare stands alert, looking and listening for predators.

Wandering among the Weather Hills is fairly easy, as long as there is a path to follow, but here that is not the case. The surrounding area is so lush with grass and undergrowth that even a poorly-maintained trail would be a relief to the weary traveller.
4949: This is the western end of the valley, the ground rising in every direction bar the east. This place seems to act as a refuge for much of the wildlife in the area, due both to the shelter the valley gives, and to the spring on the southern slope. A stream trickles down into the valley floor.
4950: A small flower grows here, with a purple bloom and wide leaves.

There is a great view of the Emyn Sul stretching off northwest for many leagues. Except for the valley below, most of the countryside is barren and inhospitable. Down on the eastern slopes a pool of water and a gully lie.
4951: On the top of the great hill one sees the scant remains of the Tower of Amon Sul, the greatest fortress in Eriador in the Third Age. It was destroyed in the wars between the Dunedain of the North and the armies of Angmar, and little survives to this day. Marking the outer wall of the fortress, a wide ring of ancient stone-work stands, crumbled by the centuries or covered with age-long grass. By standing upon this ring, one is afforded an unparalleled view of the lands around. Within the centre of the circle, a cairn of broken stones is piled, a memorial to the lost by someone now long forgotten.
4952: The wind is harsh and forgiving on the slopes of Amon Sul and with such poor soil, there are no trees to offer shelter. As one seeks to maintain a purchase on the hill, the grasses whip around ones legs while the gorse and heather snag and tear. The only reward is that the vista of many lands is laid out. An even better view of these lands can be got by climbing to the top of the hill.
4953: The path cuts through the choking bracken, passing before the foot of Amon Sul, the conical shaped hill to the north. It was there, an age ago, that Elendil waited for a sign of the approach of Gil-galad's army. They marched into the east, many never to return this way again.
4956:
Uldor (UU), wielding a great warsword, is standing here trying to concentrate.
A black crow flies low to the ground here, looking for carrion to eat.

The wilderness is no longer so flat here as the ground begins to gently slope upwards onto the lower flanks of Amon Sul-the last and greatest of the Emyn Sul. A trail to the south-west crosses the bracken-covered plains, showing the way to the traveller who wants to cross the open land.
4957: A clear spring babbles as cool water trickles out of the ground.

This hollow sits sheltered on the western flank of Weathertop, where the slope of the hill becomes too steep to climb. Rocks that have fallen from higher up the hill, have at some stage been organised into a low wall by visitors to this place. From their shape it is clear that many were originally cut for a building, though no structure remains. The other sides of the dell slope up pleasantly, preventing the worst of the winds but allowing refreshing breezes. Beyond the grassy sides to the hollow lies the monotony of the flatlands which encircle Weathertop and the Weather Hills. As a result of this depression, water which soaks through Weathertop's porous rock comes to the surface.
4958: A grey hare stands alert, looking and listening for predators.

This path was built to supply the fortress which once stood on the top of Amon Sul-the highest point for many leagues. Climbing up from the lower slopes of the hill to the north-west, it winds its way slowly up the harsh ascent of the great hill. No trees or thick vegetation grow to hide one from spying eyes.
4959: A grey hare stands alert, looking and listening for predators.

This final slope to the summit of the hill is steep and rocky, drawing heavy breath from any climber up the trail. The trail winds its way down the slope, first moving west, then north, as it tries to minimise the gradient. To leave this path would invite more toil, whether going up or down. However, it is possible to manoeuvre across the west- or north-facing sides of the hill if one desires.
4960: Hard-work indeed, this flank of Amon Sul is both extremely steep and plagued by high winds. If one wants to climb further up, there are no easy means to except by striking out for the trail to the north or expending considerable energy and climbing directly up to the summit. The grass waves across the slope creating a featureless yellow-green sea of vegetation, while islands of heather break up the scenery.
4961: A dun-coloured grouse is sitting still in the heather.

This is part of the southwest side of conical Weathertop. By the standards of the surrounding plains, the soil here is quite fertile, sustaining a variety of short grasses and a few hardy flowers, but mainly gorse and heather. The elevation is sufficient to see many of the surrounding lands, but to gain an unparalleled vantage point only the very top of the hill will suffice.
4962:
A Dunadan ranger is crouched over the fire, cooking a meal.
A sturdy trained horse is standing here.

Here, in a small hollow, protected from the elements is a small shelter. The walls are merely the baked earth from which the shelter has been cut, but in some places pelts have been nailed up to provide a better backdrop. There seems to be adequate space and facilities for several men to survive: a water bowl and jug, a pile of kindling, some hares hanging from rafters to smoke, and some pallets for sleeping. A small chimney dug into the earth provides ventilation.
4963: Along this stretch of the northern border of the old kingdom of Cardolan, the great hedge which marked the divide is broken. The terrain this side of the East Road is flat and generally covered with grass. However, the carpeting is uneven as the soil deteriorates in quality, compared to the verdant green of the downs. The trail that shadows the southern side of the hedge, is joined by a wide path from the north which comes through the breach from the East Road a few miles distant.
4964: Compared to the green carpeting of the downs to the west, the thin, rocky soil here is a dramatic change in environment. It is the hardiest of grasses which grow in patches, while short bushes dot the landscape, most notably some spindle-trees. Exposed rocks coated in grey lichen are common, while slimy trails show that slugs and snails must roam at night. Occasional droppings show that large animals frequent the plains, while field pipers occasionally swoop low overhead.
4965: The trail obviously still has use, as the sparse grasses have been kept from overgrowing the meandering path by the scouring of hoof and foot. Due to this wear, the trail is some one foot lower than the surrounding plains. Stones, cleared from the trail long ago, still mark the width of the trail. However, much of the line of stones has been disturbed over the years.
4966: The trail heads southwest from the northeastern border of the South Downs, into the heart of the former Dunedain realm which these days is mainly deserted. Though commerce along this track is probably scarce, its route into the southern lands still makes it a minor artery in the network of roads and trails which were established many thousands of years ago.
4967:
A sturdy trained horse is standing here.
A sturdy trained horse is standing here.

Though there is no great hill to avoid or contour to follow, nevertheless the hedge and its attendant trail meanders here, producing a mild kink in the long thorny chain. The track is particularly obscure here as travellers have taken other routes across the plains. Little life disturbs the peace, except for a few birds who fly in and out of the briars.
4968: North-east of the Milkfall Edge, the great hedge of the former Dunedain realm bends here from its normal east-west course. The trail also follows the hedge's course, though the north-eastern leg has all but vanished due to lack of use.
4969: The wind murmurs as one crosses the endless miles of grass-covered prairie. The soil here is capable of sustaining quite a variety of docks and grasses, quite unlike the majority of the Lone-lands. The ground slopes upward to the west where the last of the escarpments of the South Downs breaks.
4970: East of the last escarpment of the Tyrn Hyarmen, the soil here is healthy enough to support lush grasses and flowering plants. Further east, this is no longer true: the plains of the Lone-lands start and with them a harsher environment.
4971: The trail and the hedge here pass a few miles to the north of the termination of the Milkfall edge, the last of the South Downs. The terrain at this point is elevated due to its proximity to the escarpment, providing a sloping gradient down to the north where the East Road crosses the land.
4972: A grey hare stands alert, looking and listening for predators.

This is the most easterly of the South Downs: the Milkfall Edge. West is the edge, the limestone exposed on the escarpment itself. Some three score yards below the edge lie many blocks which have broken away from the face. The slope is covered in grass, providing good grazing for sheep owned by any shepherd in these downs.
4973:
The corpse of a roe deer is lying here.
A small evergreen plant grows here, its woody stems reaching two feet.
A roe deer is standing here, watching the terrain while chewing the vegetation.

Cutting through the down, the valley is rugged and strewn with blocks of limestone that have tumbled from the steep sides. As to why the valley developed through the scarp, perhaps the reason is it originally was the site of a vein of rock less resistant to erosion. Whatever the reason though, this is a haven for plants and animals in the South Downs.
