5242: An Abandoned Path in the Broken Hills

Here a rocky spur juts out from the hills to the southeast and stabs northward at the road. The rocks are barren and cracked, and burned to a pale, dusty grey by the sun's heat. An ancient track can just be made out, winding along the flank of the spur and climbing to the south.
5243: Normally, a walk through grasslands like this would be quite pleasant. Under the brooding gaze of the hills to the south, however, make you feel more as if you're trying to sneak past a watchdog. To the north and west, the grasslands take you further from the brooding menace to the southeast. South and east of you is the Old East Road; beyond which, the land rises up into shattered hills.
5244: An intact skeleton of a man is walking around here.

You stand amid the broken hills of the Lone-lands. The hills drop off into sheer cliffs in all directions, except to the east. To the east, you can make out the remains of a path. To the northeast, your eyes are drawn to an ancient ruined tower on an overlook.
5245: An Abandoned Path in the Broken Hills
An intact skeleton of a man is walking around here.

What little of the path you see winds its ways through the tortured terrain of the hills, but it generally runs east-west. You are definitely going up into the hills, even though you can't see much. While looking around, you feel chill in the pit of your stomach as you glimpse the top of a tower beyond a hill to the northeast.
5246: An Abandoned Path in the Broken Hills

Although the path has been winding its way through the cliffs that make up these hills, it makes a definite turn from north to east here. The desolation of this place is only made worse by the impression that this path has not been used for ages.
5247: An Abandoned Path in the Broken Hills

You can just make out the path as it winds it way from the road to the north up into the hills to the south. This path does not appear to have been used for some time. The only reason you are able to follow it is because there is no other way to go in this broken terrain.
5248: You stand amid the waving grass of some gently rolling plains. Everything seems unnaturally silent. Casting a glance at the rocky hills to the northeast, you feel a shiver. Perhaps it is something in those hills. To the south, the land becomes more rocky and desolate.
5249: The silence of the Lone-lands surrounds you. Broken only by the buzz of insects and the rustle of the wind, you feel compelled to keep the silence. The rocky hills to the southeast make you feel afraid to be heard. The gently rolling plains continue in all directions, broken only by a stand of trees to the north.
5250: The occasional buzz of an insect and rustle of wind in the grass are the only things that break the monotony of these grasslands as they march off in all directions. Several miles northward, you can see the Old East Road as it winds its way through the Lone-lands. In the distance to the east, you can see the land rise up into some broken hills.

This old, forsaken path continues up into the broken hills of the Lone-lands from the west to the north. Beyond some hills to the north, you can see the battlements of a shattered tower. You have the eerie feeling that you are not alone in these shattered lands.
5279: A suspicious-looking man watches the area carefully.

At last! Some real shade. You have managed to find a hollow in the rock that is protected by a tangle of vegetation. Not only is it out of the elements, but there's also a small spring that provides a trickle of water for this natural shelter. You feel safe enough in here to rest and regain your strength before going back out and battling with the harsh terrain of the Lone-lands.
5280: A large, engraved sarcophagus sits on a raised dais.

You have entered a burial crypt. While it appears to have been hastily constructed, you can tell that it is of Dunedain, if not Numenorean, make. All about this dark chamber are carvings in the walls and on the raised dais upon which rests a stone sarcophagus. The presence of Evil hangs in the air, trying to suffocate all that is living.
5281: An Abandoned Path in the Broken Hills

The remains of this path lead from the broken hills to the south to a hill overlooking the lands to the north. Atop that overlook, you see the ruins of a tower. The hills of the Lone-lands surround you, the silence of which you expect to be shattered by a scream at any instant.
5282: You stand amid the broken hills of the Lone-lands. To the south and east, the land drops away in sheer cliffs to the broken plains below. To the west, you think you can make out a path. To the northwest, an ancient tower sits atop an overlook.
5283: An intact skeleton of a man is walking around here.

You stand at the northern most end of the broken hills of the Lone-lands. The land drops off in sheer cliffs to the north and east. To the north, beyond the broken plains below, you can make out the Old East Road. To the west, an ancient tower stands on an overlook.

A skeleton of some humanoid lies in the dust.

You are standing at the top of an overlook at the northern end of the broken hills that make up this part of the Lone-lands. The hills continue to the south and east, with the remains of a path leading south. Before you is the towering bulk of an ancient tower. Glancing down at the road below, you see the shadow of the tower, a shadow shaped like a cruel orkish dagger. You feel cold, a cold not from the breeze, but from the Shadow of the tower.

You feel a presence, like a vulture circling, waiting for your death.

Out of sight in the depths of the tangles, strange squeaks, rustles, and movements can barely be discerned.

Great bramble bushes the size of apple trees huddle together, merge, coalesce into a single monstrous brambly thicket. There is no telling where one bush ends and another begins; whether some ephemeral chink of vacant space is between or within. There is only a continuous mass of briars, of thorny creepers, of muddy thorns underfoot and tearing, ripping thorns at eye level. The air is dense and stagnant, yet there is movement in the depths of the bushes, and sounds: squeaking, rustling, gurgling.

A bedraggled man stumbles as best he can across the terrain.
A grey hare stands alert, looking and listening for predators.

Suddenly you find yourself in an area of burnt and damaged vegetation. The burnt grass and the ashes are signs of a recent brushfire raging these plains. Here and there fresh grass has sprung through the ashes on their way to once again cover the ground with tall green grass.
5350: There are two handfuls of clover here.

A casual chirp from a bird in the sky reaches your ears. The tall, dry grass strokes your waistline as you move. Scanning your surroundings yields nothing but plains in all directions except to the south, where the Old East Road is clearly visible.
5351: A bedraggled man stumbles as best he can across the terrain.

A few lonely trees border the road to the south. The dry grass cracks under your feet as you make your way forward. Sounds of animals can be heard from within the dense plains. Judging from the many tracks in the dirt this might be a good place to hunt for food.
5352: You are walking through the dry grass on some plains beside the Old East road. The vegetation is sparse and consists mostly of a few bushes and lonely trees besides the high grass. The silence is uncanny and you cannot see a single animal around, except for a casual bird flying high in the air.
5353: A bedraggled man stumbles as best he can across the terrain.

In the middle of these plains the grass is burnt and trampled. Someone obviously made a campfire here quite recently. You are surrounded by grassy plains in all directions, except to the south, where the road you left is visible. Staying in these plains might be a good way to elude followers.
5354: A raider is here, looking for plunder.

Here, just north of the Old East Road, vast plains of green grass dominates the surroundings. The grass appears trampled in some places indicating some larger creatures have walked here recently. It is possible to move in all directions from here.
5355: The tall grass growing here offers good protection from the eyes of predators and other evil-minded creatures. Sounds from small animals running around in the grass can be heard. Searching for tracks in the dirt also reveals that larger hoofed animals walked here quite recently.
5356: Vast green plains border the road that runs just south of you. Looking north you see tall green grass swaying in the wind. The ground shows signs of various types of creatures walking here. It is possible to explore the plains further to the north, east and west.
5357: As you walk through these silent plains beside the road you notice some strange clawed tracks in the ground leading northwards to an abandoned farm. Some large animal unknown to you must have made these tracks.
5358:
A black crow flies low to the ground here, looking for carrion to eat.
A black crow flies low to the ground here, looking for carrion to eat.

You are standing upon one of many plots of dry, broken earth which make up these plains. Around you grow evil looking shrubs and weeds that grow taller than you'd think possible. Small shoots of brown grass try to grow within the cracks of the dried earth which creaks like old floorboards when you walk on it. Here, the flats seem to end, disappearing into the weeds to the north and the brush to the south.
5359:
A raider is here, looking for plunder.
A raider is here, looking for plunder.
A raider is here, looking for plunder.
A raider is here, looking for plunder.

You are standing upon one of many plots of dry, broken earth which make up these plains. Around you grow evil looking shrubs and weeds that grow taller than you'd think possible. Small shoots of brown grass try to grow within the cracks of the dried earth which creaks like old floorboards when you walk on it. Here, this tract of flat land borders a clump of tall weeds to the north and spiney shrubs to the south, working its path east and west between them.
5360: You are on flat, dry ground, which is so overgrown with tall thornbushes that your surroundings are completely obscured from view. In every direction they rise up - perhaps a bit higher to the south and east, but, wherever you turn your gaze, unnaturally tall and fierce-looking. Their interlaced canes are covered with huge brown thorns.
5361: Great stands of thorny brush rise up around you in all directions. Their roots grasp at the earth like many-knuckled hands; like barbed whips, their creepers and branches, lined with huge thorns jutting in all directions, rise up all around, laced together in a sharp and potentially deadly net.
5363: A majestic brush-lion moves through the brush with deceptive lack of haste.

Thorny creepers tear at you as you pass, ripping and piercing. The largest thorns are the size of a large man's hand, and are coated with a stinging brown resin! The bushes coquettishly pull you in, it seems, first giving way, then rearing up like an impenetrable wall, forbidding and impassable.
5364: The ground seems stony and infertile; nothing green grows here. Nothing at all does, save these horrible great thornbushes which blot out the sun and wind in all directions. Their twisted roots seem to squeeze all the life out of the ground; their thorny creepers lash at you as you pass, ripping at the exposed surfaces of your body.
5365: The patch of weeds here shifts strangely in the breeze.

You push your way into a stand of gigantically tall grey weeds which stand like spears, pointing skywards. They rise to heights which dwarf even you and their stems grow as thick as your wrist. `These are not ordinary weeds', you think to yourself and you even imagine you hear a low humming noise among them.
5366: A giant rat patters against you, squeaking maliciously.

On every side, in every direction, tall thorny bushes block travel, view, even the wind. The air is musty and heavy, thick with the smell of rotting vegetation. There is no path, only occasional chinks in the walls of thorny brush which tower higher than a tall man. Beyond the lacework of the sharp-thorned canes, in the shadows, there may have been some movement.
5367: You are standing upon one of many plots of dry, broken earth which make up these plains. Around you grow evil looking shrubs and weeds that grow taller than you'd think possible. Small shoots of brown grass try to grow within the cracks of the dried earth which creaks like old floorboards when you walk on it. Walking among the plains, you spot a growth of many tall weeds a mile or so to the west in this otherwise lifeless expanse.
5368: The patch of weeds here shifts strangely in the breeze.

You push your way into a stand of gigantically tall grey weeds which stand like spears, pointing skywards. They rise to heights which dwarf even you and their stems grow as thick as your wrist. `These are not ordinary weeds', you think to yourself and you even imagine you hear a low humming noise among them.
5369:
The patch of weeds here shifts strangely in the breeze.
A black crow flies low to the ground here, looking for carrion to eat.

Tough weeds are thriving aggressively across the field, preventing the ground to breathe. All around can be seen ahead what was once a field of rye. The ground is flat on which islands of shrubs and thorny bushes have established themselves. Sharp rocks are scattered around making it difficult to walk here.
5370: A fallow deer is grazing peacefully here.

You are standing at an old, crumbled and overgrown farm. The main house can hardly be seen anymore as only the floor covered with debris remain. Near the old barn you notice some old man and horse bones.
5371: You push your way into a stand of gigantically tall grey weeds which stand like spears, pointing skywards. They rise to heights which dwarf even you and their stems grow as thick as your wrist. `These are not ordinary weeds', you think to yourself and you even imagine you hear a low humming noise among them.
5372: You are standing upon one of many plots of dry, broken earth which make up these plains. Around you grow evil looking shrubs and weeds that grow taller than you'd think possible. Small shoots of brown grass try to grow within the cracks of the dried earth which creaks like old floorboards when you walk on it. Here, the flats run into a patch of weeds to the east but continue unimpaired to the west and south.
5375: At this point, the river flows under a bridge which crosses a narrow point in the ravine in a single span. On the east bank of the river, the poplars grow about a steep set of stairs cut into the stone, leading up to a side of the bridge. Within the shadow of the bridge, plants that prefer the shade thrive.
5376: You are standing in a dense forest, just along the road. You can see the forest continuing to the north, becoming higher and higher. The soil is so wet here that your shoes are all full of mud. Maybe you should take some time to wash them up ? You hear the soft sound of falling water just next to you. Time for a bath ? You look at your dirty equipment : really not presentable !
5377: This is a dense forest, just along the road. You can see the forest continuing to the north, becoming higher and higher. You hear the soft sound of falling water just next to you.
5380: This hill is crowned with a great field. The grass grows thickly here. The field falls gently away east and west from a north-south ridge on which a grass-grown dike has been built. The field continues west, and descends into rougher, more rocky terrain to the east and south. In the north a path along the ridge leads down into a narrow valley between this hill and the one north of it.
5381: A clear spring babbles as cool water trickles out of the ground.

You find a small hollow in the hillside here. A spring bubbles in it, and a brook flows from it down the hillside towards the eastern plains. Someone has taken advantage of this water source to build a campsite: there is a firepit, and a stack of firewood, and the hollow itself provides shelter from the winds. There is a pass beyond the steep slope to the north, and beyond it are the eastern slopes of another great hill.
5382: The hillside slopes gently down towards plains in the east, and up towards the top of the hill in the northwest. It is covered with rocks, short grasses, and thistles. An old stone wall snakes up from the valley in the south and turns west towards the hilltop. Many of its stones have fallen loose, and in places it is little more than a tall, grassy pile of stone. Beyond the valley the top of another hill rises above you.
5383: This track in the wilderness is barely visible through lack of use. If it was not for the inhospitable soil, plants would have totally obliterated its path. As it is, one can walk on the track east or west amongst the weeds and grasses.
5384: A field vole has frozen to the spot, sensitive to your presence.
The route of this track bends though one sees this only through keen observation. Stumbling through these lands, a traveller would be forgiven for missing this nuance in a long-dead trail.
5385: This shallow ravine leads into the small basin to your west. It seems to have carried water many ages ago. As silent testimony to the long gone water, trees that once flourished are now dead and rotten. Some small trees, however, are still clinging to life, evidenced by a few tiny leaves on their branches. The draw continues to the east.
5386: A small brown snake is slithering around here.

The floor of the draw is covered with sand and smooth pebbles. Apparently the water that once flowed in this channel washed away all of the soil components leaving these remains behind. Small lizards occasionally appear through cracks in the riverbed, only to disappear in a blink of an eye.
5387: A small brown snake is slithering around here.

The water that was once here played a vital role in the growth of the surrounding trees. Judging from the size of the dead stumps and fallen branches, the trees must have been huge, full of leaves and life. That was long ago however, as all that remains is sandy soil and deadwood. Peering through the deadened trees to the south, you see an empty plateau which seems to end abruptly a stone's throw away.
5388: This ancient, dry streambed winds further back into the plateau. Sometimes it broadens to a flat basin, floored by red-brown sand; sometimes it is a barely passable stairway climbing up rock shelves over which the stream doubtless fell in merry cascades in ages past. Rock walls, eroded by the wind into fantastic shapes, rise on either side; clumps of ferns can be seen sprouting from the bare rock, high up, nourished by a moister layer of the stone.
5389: A black snake, with red markings, is lying here.

An ancient dry ravine cuts through the rocky plateau, sloping from its heights to the south downward toward the west. Here and there are old stone basins at the foot of waterless falls, filled with rounded pebbles, red, yellow, blue-grey, worn smooth by vanished cascades. Pools which once were filled with clear water are now flat sandy expanses, marked by the trails of snakes, by the marks of little clawed feet, and perhaps by other, subtler marks as well.
5390:
A black snake, with red markings, is lying here.
A black snake, with red markings, is lying here.

The gully continues on its miles-long path which it has cut through the soft rocks of this plateau. Here its floor is broad and sandy, and clumps of hardy grass eke out a living from the rainwater. Birds of prey can be glimpsed against the sky from time to time. Barring a few odd markings in the sand, there is no sign that anyone has ever lived in these parts.
5391: A narrow gully winds southward out of the highest parts of this plateau. Here it takes the form of a steep-walled ravine or canyon. The walls are unclimbable, having been smoothed flat by wind and rain to the height of many men. The floor of the gully is stony and broken into myriad shelves and stages, down which water plunged in the distant past. Now only snakes and spiders haunt the sand and stones, it seems.
5392: Making your way through a sea of straw, you see the grass concede to a squalid stand of shrivelled trees to your south. Eastward the ground slopes upward to richer grassland. A short walk north will bring you onto a road running east and west across the plains.
5393: Here the plains rise slightly from the Old East Road to the north. The many miles of plains stretch all around you. To the south is a small draw that looks as though it once carried water. The bank is too steep to negotiate travel to it from here, perhaps there is a way around. Across the draw is a cliff that looks like the rim of a deep canyon.
5394: Slackly the plains rise up, letting you look down on the road which lies north and east of here. To your south, a draw bordered by withered trees ends the plains' dominion. Gazing beyond the draw, you see a ridge rising up and spanning east. Turning east, you notice that the land becomes more hilly as it descends toward the ford across Mitheithel river.
5395: A large rabbit looks peacefully at you, ready to dart away.

Slackly the plains rise up, letting you look down on the road which lies north and east of here. To your south, a draw bordered by withered trees ends the plains' dominion. Gazing beyond the draw, you see a ridge rising up and spanning east. Turning east, you notice that the land becomes more hilly as it descends toward the ford across Mitheithel river.
5396: Slackly the plains rise up, letting you look down on the road which lies north and east of here. To your south, a draw bordered by withered trees ends the plains' dominion. Gazing beyond the draw, you see a ridge rising up and spanning east. Turning east, you notice that the land becomes more hilly as it descends toward the ford across Mitheithel river.
5397: There is no way to tell if this path has been used recently. The presence of fresh growth would indicate that the trail was old and forgotten. However, the lack of moisture makes the sprouting of anything almost impossible. The surface of the ground is rock hard, making it very difficult to track anything.
5398: There is no way to tell if this path has been used recently. The presence of fresh growth would indicate that the trail was old and forgotten. However, the lack of moisture makes the sprouting of anything almost impossible. The surface of the ground is rock hard, making it very difficult to track anything.
5399: This seems to be the dim head of a gully plunging down to the north. The walls of the gulch are a hundred feet high, and the sky is only a narrow slash high above; the direct rays of the sun never fall here. A dismal grey-green moss covers some of the dimly lit rocks. To the south is a dark cave-mouth from which the vanished stream once poured; a faint and musty breeze wafts from it.
5400: The cave is much bigger than it appeared to be from the outside. It has smooth stone walls, probably from the water that once flowed through on its course to the valley. A path leads east, but it is too dark to tell what lies in that direction.
5401: Here the breeze blows steadily toward the west, to what looks to be a small cavern. Around a slight bend, you see rays of light. It appears to be natural light, from the sun or moon, but you cannot be sure. Getting out of the twists and turns of the passages behind you is a very welcome thought.
5402: Moving on, you soon reach another nexus. Tunnels trail off in all directions from this place. All details of what might lie ahead are consumed by the oppressive darkness. A faint scent of urine and excrement tells you that something dwells inside these corridors of stone.
5403: You are at a four-way junction now. In every direction lie more of the same rocky passages. You try to remember which way is out, but each tunnel looks the same. Using the directional flow of the wind does not seem to work, as the faint breeze seems to be coming from every tunnel.
5404: The ridge splits three ways here. To the north and west, it joins more passages like the one you are in now. To the south however, it looks as though the tunnel dead-ends at a small cavern. The earth in here smells dry and old, but fresh air keeps the place well ventilated.
5405: Dipping slightly below the pool, is a hollowed ridge that once served as an aqueduct to bring water to the pool. It is bone dry now though, as the water has chosen alternate means to get to its destination. The air is fresh here, cool and dry. For the freshness, the tunnel must have another exit, shall you bravely attempt to find it?
5406:
A grey snake slides along the water.
A grey snake slides along the water.

Behind the tall rocks you have discovered a small pool of refreshing water. Sheltered on all sides by the relatively large boulders, you realise how it can exist in such a hot, dry landscape as it is comfortably shaded. Looking over the rocks to the west, you guess that this was once the site of a nice waterfall that cascaded down to the valley below. A smooth line of rocks, out of place in the jagged cliffs, marks the water's descent. But where did this water come from?
5407: Before you is a small depression that once was probably a nice watering hole. A sinking feeling overcomes you as you realise that it is totally dry now. The only derivation of moisture comes from a thin sheen of dew on one of the rocks at the north side of the basin. Any liquid that might escape however, is quickly sucked up by the dry earth.
5408: This broad, flat plateau extends for miles to the east and north (where the ground seems higher). The ground is stony and the vegetation is sparse - coarse grass, nettles, an occasional thorny bush. Nothing grows here that would be edible by respectable folk. It must rain here often enough, judging from the water-carved gullies here and there, but the water must drain quickly into the permeable stone. To the west there appears to be a fold or break in the otherwise seamless grey landscape.
5409: This is a broad shelf on the northwest face of a rocky hillside that rises to the south. The rock is flat and soil-less, and only a few scraggly bushes grow here. A fitful breeze blows the dust of the Lone-Lands across the stony surface. This location gives a good view of the ground far below to the north and west.
5410: The stony ground continues for miles in all directions - flattish, but covered with broken and worn boulders and fragments of rock. Brownish grass and weeds scrape out a miserable living in the crevices and around the intermittent rain puddles.
5411: The ground is flattish, the horizon is distant and unmarked by hills, but the uneven and stone-covered ground makes travel unpleasant and difficult for foot, hoof, or paw. Coarse-leafed thorny bushes huddle in brownish clumps. The quiet is almost absolute, with only an occasional slithering rustle from behind a stone.
5412: The ground here climbs toward the west in a maze of water- and wind-carved rocky outcroppings, pinnacles, blocks, and gullies. The going is difficult and the way hard to find. If there was ever a trail through this jumble, it has long since disappeared.
5413: The slope is a bit more steep here than in other parts of the area. To the west, the ground rises to what appears to be an overlook of some sort. Apart from that, the only thing breaking the monotony of the plains is a path leading in a northeasterly direction.
5414:
A fierce boar is here, making grunting noises.
A boar cub is playing here, and exploring the wide world.

Long, dry shoots of plains grass grows here. Adapted for the harsh, dry climate, this annual vegetation rises and falls with the seasons. You note that all seems peaceful here, the only break in the grass being sparse clumps of bushes and a few rocks. The plains seem to extend as far as the eye can see.
5415: The plains sprout thick wavy grass that reaches waist high to the average human. The dirt underlying the grass is loose and crumbly. The only life you detect is the small desert animals that scurry about looking for food. The grass waves to and fro with the wind, making endless waves where there is no water.
5416: A fierce boar is here, making grunting noises.

Pushing your way through the dry, ensnaring limbs gets to be a tedious process as you are constantly stopping to remove thorns, cobwebs, bugs, and twigs from your hair and clothes. The terrain is not treacherous, but the vine-like branches make it easy to slip and hurt yourself if not careful.
5417:
A fierce boar is here, making grunting noises.
A boar cub is playing here, and exploring the wide world.

Deciding that you have enough water for the moment, you push through the dense tangles of dead growth, roots, and thorns. This thicket seems to contain nothing of interest, especially not the hidden treasure you were hoping to find. Taking a deep breath, you notice that the strange smell detected earlier is now stronger.
5418: A small plant grows here, with long, pointed leaves and flowers at its top.

This must have been the site of a small campfire a long time ago. As you continue to peer past the masses of dead brush, you spy a strange looking plant. Smelling the air confirms that this is the source of the odour you detected earlier. You search the recesses of your mind trying to recall any mention of a plant of this nature.
5419: A large rabbit looks peacefully at you, ready to dart away.

Maintaining its north-south direction, the path still has no obvious endpoint. To the north is more open-space, broken only by the Old East Road. In the more immediate vicinity, you spy some dense thickets to your east, and a small ridge of earth to your west. The path continues to the south.
5420: Here the trail runs north-south while passing by some dense thickets. As you move along, you detect a fragrant odour. As there seems to be no blossoming flowers in the area, you find it most odd that a sweet scent could be here. Perhaps it is something unnatural.
5421: A fierce boar is here, making grunting noises.

Here the path slopes gradually upward to the west, ending at a small levee. Your steps quicken and your heart beats a little faster at the sight of the levee. After all, isn't one designed to hold back a body of water? To the north is the small ridge noticed earlier, from this angle however, it looks rather odd. There is something about it that you cannot seem to figure out. To the east the small path continues.
5422: Here the path goes two ways. North, past many miles of cheerless plains eventually crossing the Old East Road, and west continuing further into the expanses of rolling plains and empty lands. To the north-west is a natural ridge covered with tall, dry grass. It is not high, just evidence of where the earth has pushed upwards in rebellion of its constraint.
5423: There is no way to tell if this path has been used recently. The presence of fresh growth would indicate that the trail was old and forgotten. However, the lack of moisture makes the sprouting of anything almost impossible. The surface of the ground is rock hard, making it very difficult to track anything.
5424: Carved crudely out of the stone, this staircase descends precipitously. The cut stone is not smooth and shapely like dwarven work. Rather it is rough cut and functional. Whatever the case, it is not here by natural means, which only leaves one question; that of who built this.
5425: Traversing the narrow stair, you are careful with your movements. The bottom of the passage is still not visible, and it might be a long way to the landing. Glancing at the stone walls, you notice no artwork or other tell-tale signs as to the origin or function of this place. A quick check of your light source is comforting, as it is pitch-dark.
5426: You seem to be at the bottom of the large cliff. A narrow stone staircase leads upward further than you can see. The floor here is hard dirt, and the ceiling is relatively high. There seems to be a massive slab of rock blocking travel to the west, leaving only back up the stair as an obvious option.
5427: A Stoor child is playing peacefully here.

Emerging from the bottom of the cliff, this gate is not easily visible and in a place that would be easy to defend. The gate itself is two stone slabs placed together in a formation that would make opening from the other side all but impossible. Around you is the fertile beauty of the valley, green and lush. The river gurgles lazily in the background.
5428:
A low, many-branched shrub covers the ground here.
A domesticated pony, beast of burden to many, stands here.
A Stoor goes about his daily business.
A Stoor child is playing peacefully here.
A Stoor child is playing peacefully here.

Standing in front of the gate, you spy buildings and pathways that indicate a small village. You wonder who would locate their homes here, deep inside the valley. They must be a small race of people, as the homes and other structures around you are smaller than elven-kind. From somewhere inside the village you hear excited shouting, perhaps the villagers have spotted your arrival. Will you be welcomed?
5429: A Stoor goes about his daily business.

Proceeding into the heart of the village, you find yourself on a dirt track leading toward the small river. On either side are small dwellings used by the citizens of the village for various purposes. Glancing around, you try to discern the magnitude of the village. Spying no tall spires or towers, you guess that this is pretty much the extent of it. Alleyways branch off leading to small houses, but no other roads.
5430: A Stoor goes about his daily business.

Still proceeding east-west, you surmise that this is the main road of the village. As you explore, you notice that none of the citizens are anxious to approach you. No nods of greeting, no friendly waves. If this is the nature of all its citizens, then it's small wonder that the village is so secluded. Unfriendly as they seem to be, no outward signs of hostility are visible either.
5432: A huge clock is standing here.

This seems to be the museum of the village, containing various historical artefacts and memorabilia. Books line shelves, perhaps if you glanced at some, you could learn more about this village and its people.
5433:
A shortsword is on the ground.
A small vicious black rat squeaks at you for disturbing it.
A small vicious black rat squeaks at you for disturbing it.

The basement of the mathom is dark and musty. Moisture seeps in through cracks in the walls and makes the air heavy around you. This place is used as a dump for unwanted supplies and relics. A few broken weapons and worn out armour litter the floor.
5434:
A Stoor child is playing peacefully here.
A Stoor goes about his daily business.

Small houses with wooden walls and thatch roofs line the path. From small windows you catch glimpses of curious hobbits peering out at you. In the yards of others, frightened mothers usher their children into the safety of the buildings. You wonder about the frightened looks, and figure that these folk have some great tragedy of the past looming over them. Perhaps the house to your east can provide more answers, it looks different than the other homes.
5435:
A small evergreen plant grows here, its woody stems reaching two feet.
A small evergreen plant grows here, its woody stems reaching two feet.
A large beautiful rose bush is blooming here.
A clear spring babbles as cool water trickles out of the ground.

This seems to be the place where the Stoors gather for town meetings and other social events. It is small, but well suited for the populace of the Stoor community. You see fisherman swapping stories of monster sized fish that got away, and children laughing as they play.
5436:
A Stoor goes about his daily business.
A Stoor goes about his daily business.

The well-trodden dirt path runs east-west through the bulk of the village. Small alleys branch off into small homes and down to the river edge, but this seems to be the only major thoroughfare. Citizens stare at you in wide-eyed wonder as if you are the first outsider they have seen.
5437:
A Stoor goes about his daily business.
A Stoor goes about his daily business.
A Stoor goes about his daily business.

The dirt path turns into a nice cobblestone walkway, obviously leading to the house to the west. The house is not overly large, yet is much larger than the other structures in the village. It looks well kept and the doormen in front of the door imply that something important is inside.
5438: The foyer is large, seemingly able to hold the entire village populace at one time. On the walls are paintings of men and women attired in fancy halfling clothes. The floor is wooden and seems to be well taken care of. The only feature that catches you eye however, is the set of double oaken doors to your north.
5439:
A small pouch, made from leather, lies on the dust.
The Chief of the Stoor Village is here.

A simple office, one that defies the marvel of the rest of the house. The official that works here must mean business. Spartan furnishings scatter the office only for functional measure. A few wooden chairs, a wastebasket, a pair of lamps. The only elegant feature of the place is the massive desk scattered with papers. The desk is from a rich wood, and highly polished.
5440:
A raft has been left here.
A hobbit fishtrader loudly advertises his fresh fish here.

A simple shop, apparently here to serve the needs of the village fishermen. A few nice boats are being repaired, and a raft lies unused in the corner. Located by the bend of the river, it provides easy access to either direction. West, towards the mouth of the river, and south, leading eventually to the Hoarwell and beyond.
5441:
A fisherhobbit is cruising the River in his reed boat, looking for fish.
A trout swims here.

In the river, you get a chance to look up at the mighty canyon walls that tower over you. Their presence gives you a certain feeling of security and solidness. It is this feature of the land, you guess, that made the townsfolk pick this site for a village.
5442: The shallow river winds generally south and west through a gorge sixty feet deep. The cliffs rise sheerly, striated in shades of beige, grey, red-brown and gold. The water is clear and cool, and the shapes of fish can be seen darting against the coloured pebbles on the river bottom.
5443:
A salmon swims here.
A fisherhobbit is cruising the River in his reed boat, looking for fish.

The river winds into a series of curves here, slowly making its way to the Hoarwell and beyond. Rocks jut up from the bottom of the river bed at this point, making boat-travel an unwise choice. The fish swimming in the water look like a tantalizing lunch, or snack.
5444:
A trout swims here.
A salmon swims here.
A trout swims here.

The water of the river is clear enough to see the bottom. Fish swim by peacefully, avoiding the lures of the fishermen. Green grass lines the sides of the river, making several nice places to stop and have a spot of lunch. The river is relatively narrow and shallow, but obviously big enough to supply the village with fresh food to eat.
5445:
A trout swims here.
A fisherhobbit is cruising the River in his reed boat, looking for fish.

This is where the river originates, sprouting from the ground as it escapes the many miles of underground tunnels it must have passed through on its way here. The water is cold, having come from the mountains of the Weather Hills in the north-west. To the south, the river winds its way to join the Hoarwell, and eventually to end up in the waters of the River Bruinen.
5446: A large rabbit looks peacefully at you, ready to dart away.

Making your way through a sea of straw, you see the grass concede to a squalid stand of shrivelled trees to your south. Eastward the ground slopes upward to richer grassland. A short walk north will bring you onto a road running east and west across the plains.
5447: Here the plains rise slightly from the Old East Road to the north. The many miles of plains stretch all around you. To the south is a small draw that looks as though it once carried water. The bank is too steep to negotiate travel to it from here, perhaps there is a way around. Across the draw is a cliff that looks like the rim of a deep canyon.
5448: You stand on a plain that is somewhat elevated from the road, giving you a good view of the lay of the surrounding land. The Old East Road, which runs north of here, sweeps nonchalantly around the bushes, trees and small hills that lie on these plains. Looking southwest, you can barely make out a lone spire fighting for attention amongst the sullen hills.
5449: The thick grass continues, seeming never to end as you gaze across the open plain. Looking north, the road winds its way across the Lone-Lands. To the south and east, only more plains await. Nothing about this area is openly stimulating, in fact, quiet rolling plains like this might make for a nice place to take a nap.
5450: Slackly the plains rise up, letting you look down on the road which lies north and east of here. To your south, a draw bordered by withered trees ends the plains' dominion. Gazing beyond the draw, you see a ridge rising up and spanning east. Turning east, you notice that the land becomes more hilly as it descends toward the ford across Mitheithel river.
5451: Slackly the plains rise up, letting you look down on the road which lies north and east of here. To your south, a draw bordered by withered trees ends the plains' dominion. Gazing beyond the draw, you see a ridge rising up and spanning east. Turning east, you notice that the land becomes more hilly as it descends toward the ford across Mitheithel river.
5452: The reason for the sparse life here is apparent. Food, habitat, and water are obviously deficient. Any beast living in such a place must be a fierce forager indeed. These trees bear no fruit and give little cover or shade. It is so dry here, the slightest spark could set the place ablaze.
5453: A tree-snake lies wrapped around one of the tree branches.

The woods of this little forest are barely surviving the heat and drought. Many have already succumbed to the grim conditions and stand like silent sentries watching the road. Their leafless branches offer little shade and even less protection from the elements. The only perfect use of this wood, seems to be fuel for a fire.
5454:
A tree-snake lies wrapped around one of the tree branches.
A tree-snake lies wrapped around one of the tree branches.
A large rabbit looks peacefully at you, ready to dart away.

The ground is littered with dead bark and bleached wood. The small, scraggly trees are so dry that their branches snap in the slightest wind. Dropping a torch or a hot coal here would certainly have dire consequences, as you and the surrounding area would quickly be engulfed in flames.
5458: The trunks of this small forest are withered and cracking. Their bark is peeling off in dry strips, making funny corkscrew shapes as it breaks off and falls to the ground. The wood that remains is very dry and would catch fire quickly. It would be wise to keep a firm grip on any open flame here.
5459: This area just off the road is scattered with dried out bushes and stumps. Tumbleweeds that have rolled into the bushes make an impenetrable wall of growth. They lodge onto anything that will stop their momentum. However, in the middle of a storm, all those weeds might work to keep out the wind.
5460: The bleakness of the land around you makes you appreciate even the most ordinary things usually taken for granted. Your senses dull from lack of input as the land around you seems to swallow any sight, smell or noise of any redeeming quality.
5461: When the sun beats down on this road laid down long ago, every landmark is seen as if through a film of yellow-grey. Rubble and dirt whirls up from underneath your feet, indicating just how dry and unsustaining the soil of the surrounding plains must be.
5462: The worn road is surrounded by plains to the north and south. The grassy plains continue out of eyesight to your north, unperturbedly growing and expanding, as they have since the year 1409, when this land was burnt and pillaged by the armies of the Witch-king on their march to Amon Sul.
5463: There is little to be impressed with on this stretch of road. To the south and east lies more of the road, while the vast plains continue to surround you. You estimate that this is about the halfway point on the road between the town of Bree in the west and the Elven refuge of Rivendell in the east.
5464: Visible in the west is the massive Weathertop. As for the road you are on, its dust and grit seem to clog the very workings of your body. As you walk between the vast stretches of plains, you seem very small and insignificant.
5465: You seem to be in the heart of the Lone-Lands now. Crossing the vast plains in an east-west direction, the Old East Road marks the only break in the tall grass. On either side of the road, the familiar rolling hills stretch out for many a farthing. Far to the south you think you spot a canyon, but from this distance you cannot be sure.
5466: A lifeless forest accompanies the roadside view at this point. Westward you can see the Old East Road lying in a straight line, while the forest to your northeast forces the road toward the Last Bridge to bend south.
5467: As you continue down this lonesome road, all you can do is shuffle your feet. Even the dust you kick up seems more alive than the surrounding land. You strain to glimpse some sign of life, inwardly knowing it is futile.
5468: The road here is dusty and cracked from lack of moisture. With luck this area might get precipitation enough to offer some relief but this seems doubtful. Most days the sky remains clear sky and the drown still thirsts, conditions that often cause travellers to check that their precious water is securely tucked away before trudging onward. To the south you discern a small path.
5469: In the heyday of the Kingdom of the North, this road was widely used, as it was the main artery of traffic between the prosperous Dunedain settlements of Arnor. Now nothing remains to reminisce of its former glory. The road lies in disrepair, beaten and worn by the feet of the occasional traveller and adventurer.
5470: Draughts of warmer wind blow in your face from a northern direction. Looking to the source of the reassuring wind you discover an uncomfortable change, the once golden prairies you fondly recall being here have been scorched and blackened. It looks as though a mighty battle has just been waged. The road continues East-West.
5471: This small but relatively deep valley was created by the slopes of adjacent hills. It is shallow enough that you can climb out easily but deep enough to be invisible from the road to the South. The east slope is steeper and has a few loose planks neglectfully left there.
5472:
A brown fox is here, looking for some rabbits to chew up.
A brown fox is here, looking for some rabbits to chew up.

Crossing this vast stretch of grassy plain is going to take all the resolve you can muster. Even you may not have enough to cross this sea of grass. It is so endless that you wonder if, by crossing it, you will end up in the northern wastes of Arda.
5474: A brown fox is here, looking for some rabbits to chew up.

Following no pattern, heeding no laws, the long grass blows carefree in the wind. Rolling with the gentle contours of the land, you note little change in the surroundings. The grass goes on for as far as the eye can see. To venture into such lands, one must have brought plenty of provisions.
5475: The horizon seems to contain only more of the green-brown shoots of grass that you have seen bordering the road for the last few farthings. It goes on and on, farther than you think you can ride in a day or even a week.
5476: The rolling plains goes on and on, covered with a dry grass that the smallest fire would set to fire. The interspersion of brown thickets of growth and rocky soil, gives it only a tinge of variety. The ground is in several places littered by small but sharp stones, able to cut the leather of a boot or wound the hooves of a horse. Southward the slope of a low but rocky hill is covered by such stones.
5477: All around you is the same old grass. Even a solitary flower would seem out of place in these dull brown plains. Broken only occasionally by sparse patches of rocky soil and scraggly thickets, the monotony is overwhelming. Dropping a torch here would be most unwise, as the lack of water makes everything very dry.
5478: A wagon of unknown origin has been left here on the fringe of the forest. Obviously abandoned long ago, you wonder which cruel fate befell its owners. The wagon is in shambles, two of the four wheels broken, and the cloth top has all but disintegrated.
5479:
A wild dog bares his yellow fangs at you.
A wild dog bares his yellow fangs at you.
A wild dog bares his yellow fangs at you.

You seem to have found the home of some wild beasts. The earth has been carved out from around the wagon by the wear of the wind, making a perfectly hollow niche under the floorboards. It seems that whatever lives here is quite comfortable. You see scraps of meat and fur from rabbits on the ground. There is a pile of bones in the corner.
5480: The smell of smoke is still strong here, but the heat of the flames has dropped from such painful proportions. There is just enough relief to wipe the sweat from your brow and clear your eyes. The rest may be brief however, as fire can spread quickly in these open plains. Perhaps the rocks to your east may provide more stable shelter.
5481:
A diamond-back rattlesnake is coiled here, ready to strike.
A diamond-back rattlesnake is coiled here, ready to strike.

This is an area of the plains saved from the wrath of the fire. Spared only because the ground is littered with broken chunks of rock, left behind from a massive upheaval of the earth. Some of the rocks are too big to move, but poking around some of the little ones may unearth some treasure perhaps.
5482: Whether started by you or someone else, this fire is out of control. You cannot see farther than in front of your face. Your eyes sting from the billowing smoke and it is so hot it burns!
5483: Huddled in this dense growth of plants, you feel that this is a safe place to rest, hidden from any wild animals that might pass by. Peering out of the thicket, you can see that the plains continue to the east and west, and the Old East Road lies just to the south.
5484: You stand amid the rolling plains of the Lone-lands. All around you is the same knee-high grass. The plains continue to the east and west. The Old East Road makes its way to the south, beyond which the land grows rocky. To the southwest, in the distance, you can see forbidding cliff-like hills rising above the broken landscape.
5485: Before you lies farthing after farthing of waist-high wavy grass. As the wind blows the stalks to and fro, it rolls like waves of the distant sea. It makes a dry rustling sound as the shoots brush together.
5486: The area south of the road still contains remnants of wildlife, but to the north, the land grows continually paler. Black hills, scraped of all vegetation stand out bare against the sky, wisps of smoke and steam hang in the heavy air.
5487: Eastwards, thick smoky clouds obscure your sight. To the south, a small trodden path branches off this road. Both north and south offer little more than minor vegetation, small brush and weeds, atypical of the plains surrounding you. The only signs of life at all in fact, would be men who once toiled here to make this road.
5488: A rabbit is here eyeing your presence warily.

A feeling of dread enters into your heart and dampens your soul. You want nothing more than to leave this foul area behind you. You can no longer bare to look around at the bleak landscape. You grit your teeth and stare straight ahead.
5489: A rabbit is here eyeing your presence warily.

Black smoke and ash swirls around you, restricting your breathing and making you gag. Even the bleak landscape, no sight for sore eyes, has been blotted out by this thick foulness. You wipe the soot from your eyes and try to simply focus on the road ahead of you.
5490: The need for concentration is evident here. Dark swirling clouds of dirt and debris diminish your view and lash at your clothing. The road vanishes ahead into swirling clouds of evil winds, tread carefully and do not stray from the road.
5491: This path seems to have been carved by wild animals rather then by any civilized race. Winding back and forth across the coarse grass and small shrubs, it heads south and east, to an unknown destination.
5492:
A huge, black wolf is here, ready to devour.
A grey wolf is here, salivating profusely.

The sharp smell of clover and pine mixes sweetly in the air, contrasting sharply with that of the northern side of the Old East Road. There, poisoned by evil, the ground festers with foulness and stench. Yet even here amongst the vegetation you cannot hide, the thin scraggly weeds and thorny scrub offer little protection. The path continues north and south.
5493: A huge, black wolf is here, ready to devour.

Here the path meanders to the east, wandering into a small thatch of forested hills. Perhaps there, under the cover of nature, you can find protection from the evilness that permeates this area. Quickening your pace, you head towards the unknown, knowing that it must be better than here.
5494: A huge, black wolf is here, ready to devour.

You are standing in an open area, surrounded by small weeds and dirt. Up ahead a small dilapidated village of broken wood and stone can be seen. Perhaps this was the mining village that supported excavation of Turngurth, now it seems long deserted.
5496: Standing on broken bits of gravel and concrete, this was once a very sturdy road, expected to carry no doubt, the heavy loads of ore and metals gutted from mining Turngurth. All around you, a somber mist lay, the strength of Angmar is heavy here. Around you lie the battered remains of some houses.
5497: You have entered a simple building, intended to house the miners after a long day of work. It is scarcely more than your length and width. On the floor lies the remains of a small straw bed, now overgrown with weeds which have sprung through the wooden floorboards.
5498:
A vicious little bandit advances towards you.
A smuggler is here, angry at having been seen.

Here, underneath the cover of the ramshackled town, seems a perfect place to have an illicit smuggling headquarters. Apparently, you aren't the first to realise this, around you lie broken crates of wares and black market items. A large table stands squarely in the middle of this room.
5499: Twisting along the graded trail, ahead of you it bends back to the east, bringing you closer to the forest. Carefully searching the ground, you notice odd footsteps seeming to disappear into the brush.. or maybe it is just the scuffled footprints of a few wandering vagrants.
5500: Here the path tackles a sharp rise in the land, tacking back and forth like a ship sailing against the wind. As you near the forest the evilness around you seems to dissipate, perhaps you can finally find some peace in the forest ahead.
5501: The path that you were near seems to have disappeared in the brush and rocks around you. To the north, the Old East Road runs swiftly and sharply through this vile land. The forest ahead of you does seem less haunting than the surrounding area, but only by a little. Deep shadows loom ahead beckoning you to challenge their domain.
5502: The forest around you certainly is far from healthy. The trees bend and groan, trying valiantly to stand firm against the evilness surrounding them. Spaced widely and stunted, you can easily see through them and to the north, where the source of the evilness lies.
5503: The ground is hard and rocky here, rising and falling like a stormy sea. You fight to stand afoot, the small rocks threaten to constantly throw you off balance. Looking around you see evidence of many beasts, at least it isn't lifeless, something lives here.
5504: The rich smell of nature is stifled here, replacing it, an odor of sweaty skin and spit. The trees here are heavily scarred with teeth marks and gnashes. Around you rest the trampled remains of various decaying beasts. You appear to have stumbled upon the meeting place of a pack of wild animals.
5505:
A waist-high evergreen shrub grows here, with thick, reaching branches.
On the shrub, there are three piles of grey-green leaves.

Here the trees, while never thick, seem to wane out even more. Only a few lumps of vegetation can be seen. Most of the landscape consists of rocky barren hills, and stunted brown shrubs. Nothing here appears to be what you would consider alive, rather.. simply existing.
5506: A wild dog bares his yellow fangs at you.

Little shade is afforded by these sickly trees. You are actually thankful of this, the darkness here does not seem comforting or entirely without an evil presence. You laugh at yourself, aware of it or not, you find yourself hopping from sunbeam to sunbeam, avoiding the evil weight of the shadows.
5507: Twigs snap and crackle under your feet making stealthy movement impossible. Any animal that wasn't alerted to your presence certainly is now. You glance backwards, the eerie feeling that something is watching you constantly tugs on your mind. Looking about, bits of matted bloodied fur littered the area, some very vicious beasts have made their home nearby.
5508:
A placid pond is here, inviting you to take a refreshing drink.
A wild dog bares his yellow fangs at you.
A wild dog bares his yellow fangs at you.

The water here flows up from an underground aquifer. Cold and fresh, it is naturally filtered by the rocks and gravel below the surface. Looking deep in the water, you can clearly see the bottom, it even looks like a nice place to take a swim.
5509: A grey wolf is here, thin from starvation.

Hmm.. why do you always seem to do that? You always just have to look everywhere. Well, now your exploring spirit has gotten you lost.. again! Fighting your way deep in the thicket, you begin the agonizing and tedious search for a way out.
5510: Hmm.. why do you always seem to do that? You always just have to look everywhere. Well, now your exploring spirit has gotten you lost.. again! Fighting your way deep in the thicket, you begin the agonizing and tedious search for a way out.
5511:
A grey wolf is here, thin from starvation.
A grey wolf is here, thin from starvation.

Hmm.. why do you always seem to do that? You always just have to look everywhere. Well, now your exploring spirit has gotten you lost.. again! Fighting your way deep in the thicket, you begin the agonizing and tedious search for a way out.
5512: Hmm.. why do you always seem to do that? You always just have to look everywhere. Well, now your exploring spirit has gotten you lost.. again! Fighting in the deep thicket, you begin the agonizing and tedious search for a way out.
5513: Hmm.. why do you always seem to do that? You always just have to look everywhere. Well, now your exploring spirit has gotten you lost.. again! Fighting your way deep in the thicket, you begin the agonizing and tedious search for a way out.
5514: You have entered a simple building, intended to house the miners after a long day of work. It is scarcely more than your length and width. On the floor lies the remains of a small straw bed, now overgrown with weeds which have sprung through the wooden floorboards.
5515: The sharp smell of urine and dung cuts through the scented boughs of pine around you. The ground, carpeted by a bed of long thin needles, muffles your footsteps, and perhaps those of predators as well. The faint clatter of birds and squirrels returns to this part of the forest; perhaps all is not evil here.
5516: A large eagle soars above you.

The land here is wild and pathless, with bushes and stunted trees growing in dense patches containing wide barren spaces in between. The grass is scanty, coarse and grey, and the leaves in the thickets are fading and falling. Further to the north there is a high ridge raising up out of the fields and to the east the Mitheithel flows southward until it finally joins with the Bruinen and becomes the Greyflood.
5517: The forest here consists mostly of beeches, the bark of which has an unwholesome yellow tinge as if the trees were affected by some strange disease. The undergrowth is sparse, but there is a lot of bracken that crackles even when nothing seems to disturb it. To the east the forest becomes even thinner and eventually ends, giving way to a vast barren plain.
5518: A light forest begins to the west of you, but on all the other sides the landscape is barren. Desolate plains stretch all the way to the eastern horizon, but to the north they begin to rise slowly and eventually end at a vast ridge that stretches from the east to the west. The vegetation is sparse and colourless and almost no sounds of wildlife can be heard.
5519: The plains rise rather steeply towards the ridge which crests to the north. The ground here is rocky with large boulders scattered across the terrain. Not much grows here, and the little that does is bleak and grey. There is a whistling sound in the air as the wind finds its way between the boulders.
5520: Overlooking the Old East Road, this ridge lies a couple of miles south of the road. The ground slopes steeply down towards the road creating a steep cliff. At the bottom of the cliff lie rocks from countless rockslides and from this angle you can see that a pile of rocks to the east cover an opening in the cliff.
5521: A mother eagle flies high above, looking for prey.

The cliff wall that ends this ridge abruptly is full of cracks as it bends slightly outwards in the west. To the south-east, along the plains, the Mitheithel flows southward until it joins with the Bruinen and becomes the Greyflood.
5522: To the north a sheer cliff has formed before the rocky plains below. On the northern edge of the plain an old road winds towards an ancient stone bridge in the north-east. To the south-west, as far as the eye can see, the highlands of central Eriador spread out. To the east and south a precipice drops into the river far below.
5523: The ground falls away towards the plains in the south and the river in the east. It is quite rocky here and the most of the soil seems to have grown away. South of you some stunted trees still grow; but here, the largest vegetation are some bleak bushes with few leaves.
5524: The prominent fin of a silver-yellow fish breaks the surface of the water.

A sheer cliff to the north makes it impossible to leave the river in that direction and the western bank looks steep and difficult to ascend. The river seems to flow straight from here, towards the south, for many miles.
5525: The river lies nested between vast plains to the west and an old abandoned farmland to the east. The river flows south for many miles will it eventually merges with the Loudwater and becomes the Greyflood.
5526:
A bass swims here.
The prominent fin of a silver-yellow fish breaks the surface of the water.

The river flows south towards the vast unpopulated regions of central Eriador. On the riverbanks some vegetation slowly grows and a few birds fly high above the ground. The river will continue for many miles before it reaches Tharbad and after that the vast sea but to follow the river so far does not seem possible.
5527: A small and tough weed grows here.

To the east the rocky ground slopes steeply into a river that flows from the north. A large number of bushes and stunted trees grow here, feeding off the nearby water. In the gaps between the bushes and trees huge boulders can be seen. Further to the north the land begins to rise where it finally crests forming a high ridge five or six miles from here.
5528: Lying near the river to the east, this area seems to have been flooded many times. Some of the debris washed up by the river lie here and there, most of it being dead trees and bushes. The ground is quite rocky but small stunted trees and a few bushes manage to grow in the topsoil. Not much evidence of animal life can be seen here except for the birds flying high above.
5529: Here the river Mitheithel, or in the tongue of men the Hoarwell, turns to the west as it continues to flow southward. The riverbanks are steep and rocky and here and there on the banks some shrubs and bushes have managed grow.
5530: A sheer cliff that is impossible to climb looms above you to the north and west. The cliff is full of cracks which small birds have used when building their nests. As it does in many other places, the river once again bends and now it continues south.
5531: The Mitheithel twists and turns. The water flows swiftly between a pair of huge boulders, and anything swept along by the river risks being smashed against them. The riverbanks are quite steep and littered with stones.
5532: A large brown snake with black patches is coiled here.

On the floor of this cave lies the skeleton of some large biped creature. It probably got trapped here when some stones fell on top of the cave mouth to the east. The walls of this cave are cracked and there are some old and now almost completely faded paintings on them.
5533: A high cliff wall blocks the way to the west and south. The wall is several hundred feet high and grey, except for those places where bushes grow in the cracks. Close to the north is the old east road. The road is not in a good shape and it is quite hard to see the difference between it and the surrounding rocky plains.
5534: The Old East Road to the north-east and a high ridge to the south surround these bleak and barren fields. No animal life exists here but excrements and tracks from small creatures can be found on the ground. The ground is quite rocky and the only vegetation here are some scant patches of heather.
5535: These rocky plains lie nested between the Old East Road to the north and a high ridge line to the south that will transform into a grey hill to the east. Some heather grows between the rocks on the ground where a snake or two will sometimes hide.
5536: The river Mitheithel surrounds these hills on the southern and eastern side. North of the hills a steep and rocky slope leads down to a bridge that crosses the river in the north-east. Many of the bushes stand close to the river and between them the coarse grass grows tall.
5537: The river bends once again and flows south from here. Further downstream the river twist and turn causing much erosion to the riverbanks. On the rocks closest to the water green alga and moss grow uninhibited forming a slippery surface. Not many traces of animal life can be found around here but some bird droppings do appear on the rocks.
5538: The ravine cut by the river is more narrow and steep here. At the bottom of the ravine there are small ledges close to the water which contain coarse grass and stunted bushes. On the northern ledge lies a dead tree, which was uprooted somewhere upstream, as well as some loosely scattered gravel which has been washed away from the nearby road.
5539: Bend in the Old East Road

The gravel laden Old East Road curves to the north in order to avoid a rocky slope to the east. At the southern edge of the road patches of heather slowly give way to the rocks that lie scattered across the plains. The skyline in the far north is dotted by the blunt mountain peaks.
5540: Huge stone blocks lie close to the northern edge of the Old East Road and beyond the boulders the blunt peaks of some distant mountains can be seen against the horizon. The Old East Road has been poorly maintained, for large gaps and holes in the structure have formed making travel by wagon impossible. The only vegetation that can be seen from here are scant patches of heather mixed in with some weeds.
5541: Bend in the Old East Road
In the cracks of the road surface tough weeds grow, but apart from those little vegetation can be seen. On the south side of the road there is a large cliff rising sharply out of the rocky plains.
5542: Bend in the Old East Road

The Old East Road bends here, avoiding the huge boulders to the east. While you can move east, the boulders and rocks will make travel in that direction difficult. Along the side of the road there are some scant patches of heather and sharp rocks scattered about. The wildlife here is almost non-existent, with only small birds making an occasional venture.
5543: This stretch of the Old East Road is straight and narrow. It passes between two ridges that block the view to the north and south. The road is in poor condition due to lack of proper maintenance for many decades. On the side of the road some bushes grow, and scattered among the bushes various rocks can be found.
5544: A dark somber veil seems to pervade this area. The grassy fields and mountains fade from view and all that can be seen is the smoking embers of a torched and barren land. You search your memory for some news of a battle, waged near here, but recall no such event. What could have possibly have happened?
5545: Bend in the Old East Road

Here the Old East Road bends to the south as it bypasses several huge stone blocks which prevents easy passage the west. The heather, a few yards from the roadside, bows slightly in the wind that blows from the surrounding plains. The road slowly dips to the east as it traverses the lower lands besides the river Mitheithel.
5546: A grey hare stands alert, looking and listening for predators.

The sounds of a river swirling against its bank can be heard to the east, the same direction the road slopes steeply towards. On the southern side of the road the terrain turns rocky where several large boulders can be seen. There is an impressive bridge, made out of stone, a little ways towards the south- east and next to the bridge there are some partially standing buildings.
5547: Bend in the Old East Road

Part of the road near the river seems to have been washed away in a flooding, while other parts are slippery and undermined. The riverbank next to the road is steep and muddy as the road turns south towards more stable ground. The Last Bridge, which can be seen on the horizon, appears quite massive even from this distance. It is made out of stone, with three great arches that have withstood the ravages of time.
5548: Bend in the Old East Road

The Last Bridge can be seen to the east, at the bottom of a short steep slope. It was built by the men who once dwelt here, ages ago, but no longer remain. The Old East Road bends northward to bypass the steep and rocky slope to the west. Far away to the east, beyond the Mitheithel, another river lies. It is Loudwater, the Bruinen of Rivendell. The road runs along the edge of the hills for many miles from the bridge to the Ford of Bruinen which lies before the Loudwater.
5549: A big and sturdy structure, this is the last bridge, before Tharbad, crossing the river Mitheithel which flows from its sources in the Ettenmoors. It was built by the men of Rhudaur before they fell under the shadow of Angmar. The bridge is made of rectangular stone blocks, but some of them are missing and others have crumbled under the weight of time. From below comes the sound of water swirling against the bridge's three great arches. On the eastern side of the river, the decaying remains of a small cluster of buildings can be seen.
5550: A southern path leads towards a cluster of old and decaying ruins nestled in a grove of trees. To the west a large stone bridge spans the raging waters of the river Mitheithel and on the other side of the bridge a steep and rocky slope can be seen. While the foliage looks more lush on this side of the river, signs of wildlife are scarce.
5551: Bend in the Old East Road

The road bends sharply towards the south, avoiding a steep slope just east of here. At the northern edge of the road a sombre country of dark trees winding among sullen hills are visible, while to the west the road leads towards a large decaying stone bridge. The river Mitheithel can be seen to the west, flowing rapidly from its sources far north in the Ettenmoors.
5552: The western bank of the river is steep and littered with rocks from the Old East Road while the eastern bank is more benign and easier to ascend. Just south of here is the Last Bridge. From here, as the river flows under its three great arches, the bridge looks very large. Time has taken its toll on the bridge as some of its large stone blocks have crumbled and others have been washed away.
5553: The differences between the east and west riverbanks are startling. On the western bank very little vegetation grows while on the eastern bank a grove of trees, starting from the edge of the river, grows. A bit north the Mitheithel merges with one of its tributaries causing the river here to be wider than further upstream.
5554: Here the Mitheithel, flowing down north and east from the Ettenmoors, merges with one of its tributaries which originated in the harsh highlands to the north-west. North of the river lies an ancient fortress, protected on three sides by the water.
5555: A large eagle soars above you.

A sheer cliff, forming the northern bank, rises sharply from the water and atop this bluff stands a large tower. The upper levels of the structure are missing, but it is nevertheless an impressive building. Attacking the fortress from here would be quite impossible. On the southern shore of the river a light forest grows.
5556: The southern bank of the river is covered by trees but on the eastern bank the only thing that covers the ground is small sharp rocks. Beyond the sloping riverbank to the east a forest can be seen. It is difficult to tell what kind of trees predominate there, but they appear to be very large. The river is partially blocked by rubble fallen from the ruined stronghold to the north.
5557: To the west, well protected behind the river and by a steep cliff, lies an old ruined fortress. Once four towers marked the corners of this edifice. Now, only one tower remains and that one only partially intact, the rest having been reduced to rubble as has much of the fortress wall. Most of the debris has tumbled into the river leaving massive, angular, grey stone blocks everywhere. The waterway cuts a narrow path through the valley with its eastern bank covered by moss and rotting waterlogged trees which appear close to death.
5558: This ridge continues both to the east and west. A couple of miles to the east it curves northward where it eventually ends at the base of some barren hills. The view is spectacular up here on the ridge and down below, to the south, lies the Old East Road. Twisting and turning its way between Amon Sul to the west, and the river Bruinen to the east, the road stretches far into the distance.
5559: Here, heather covers much of the ground, except for those patches which are broken up by thickets and large boulders. To the south a ridge rises up and above it the shape of another, higher ridge, can be discerned against the sky.
5560: The most common form of vegetation growing on these rocky plains is heather, which is broken up into small patches by large rocks and an occasional bush. A ridge gently rises out of the surrounding plains in the distant south and con- tinues to the south-east where barren hills eventually take over.
5561: The plains stretch to the west as far as one can see and to the north until they reach a distant river. The vegetation here consists mostly of heather and brush, some of which appears to have been grazed upon. But no tracks remain to identify the species of the grazer.
5562: The rocky plains to the west gradually transform into these barren hills. Not much grows here, just some grey heather and a few stunted bushes, but further to the north lies lush vegetation and a forest. At the foot of the forest a tributary of the river Mitheithel flows gently down from the highlands until it finally joins the river in the east.
5563: North from here one of the river Mitheithel's tributaries flow towards the south-east. On the other side of the tributary, to the far north, lies the ruined town of Cameth Brin which was once the capital of the Rhudaur kingdom. Now almost nothing remains of that town as it was destroyed in one of the countless wars that plagued this region. The hills stretch far from here in all directions and they seem almost devoid of life.
5564: The hills stretch as far as can be seen to the south and west but to the north they end abruptly bounded by one of the tributaries to the river Mitheithel. The hills that are visible are bleak and barren and the only indication of wild life is an occasional bird searching for food.
5565: A grey hare stands alert, looking and listening for predators.

The remains of old wagon tracks lead east towards a ford in the river. Among the tracks some weeds and coarse, bleak grass have begun to grow. To the west the hills begin to rise gently and continue for several miles.
5566: A dark and ruined fortress lies on the east side of this tributary which feeds the river Mitheithel. While not much of the fortress is left, one of the towers has managed to remain standing. Here the river is rather shallow, thus there appears to be no problem crossing to either side.
5567: Squeezed between the river to the west and an impressively large fortress to the east, this small island provides little room to manoeuvre. The skill of the masons who built the fortress was superb for while the fortress looks truly ancient it will probably stand for many more years. The northern part of the stronghold is nothing but ruins, apparently destroyed by both siege machines many years ago and continual erosion from the river.
5568: The ground slopes steeply down towards the river which is just east of here. There, the river Mitheithel joins with one of its tributaries and together they rush to the sea in the distant south. The ground is littered with many small, sharp rocks between which grow a few stunted bushes.
5569: Steep hills surround you on all sides. Growing upon the slopes of the hills are a few patches of heather and coarse weeds but for the most part the ground is barren and grey. To the south the hills gradually recede and eventually give way to a flat plain.
5570:
A low shrub with bright green, oblong leaves is growing here.
Scattered in and on the shrub, there are a handful of blueberries.

The only way to avoid travelling through these steep hills is to use the Old East Road, some 3 miles to the south. The hillsides all about are littered with sharp rocks. While these rocks are all grey in colour, they can be found in a variety of different shapes and sizes. Between the rocks patches of heather and a few small blueberry bushes grow. Apart from those plants, little vegetation can be seen.
5571: A ridge, that formed to the far west, has transformed into these rolling hills. While not much vegetation grows here, a few weeds and some small patches of heather manage to thrive. Tracks from some kind of small animals criss-cross the ground. They seem rather old and worn making it hard to determine what kind of animal made them.
5572: The ridge that began far off to the west ends here. To the east, hills extend outwards for many miles. South of the ridge, down a short but steep slope, the grey plains are cut off by a road.
5573: A sheer-faced ridge lies just north of here, where it cuts across the land to the west, before turning northward.
