5782: A huge, black wolf is here, ready to devour.

This is the edge of a dark forest, which is cut by the Old East Road to the north and to the east. The trees around are mostly of an unfamiliar kind, with dark-grey boles and branches and dark-green leaves that resemble a clawed paw. The foliage of the trees does not seem to be very thick, yet it lets through almost no light, and no smaller plants seem to survive in the shade.
5783: A dark sombre veil seems to pervade this area. The grassy fields and mountains fade from view and all that can be seen is the smoking embers of a torched and barren land. You search your memory for some news of a battle, waged near here, but recall no such event. What could have possibly have happened here?
5784: A beautiful and docile horse is standing here.

The skyline is flat and unending along this stretch of the road. Westwards however, a violent storm whips dust swirls high into the air. Here however, the air is remarkably still, allowing the unpleasant odor of rotting flesh to permeate the dusty air.
5785: Black ash spills over the land and road, surrounding you in an unholy darkness. The plains around you exhibit no signs of life, just blackened stumps of bush and limp weeds. The road continues south and west here, but travels deeper into the blackness westwards.
5786: The road runs straight west and east into swirling clouds of evil winds. The dark swirling clouds are made of dirt and debris that diminish your view and lash at your clothing. Tread carefully and do not stray from the road.
5787: Evil winds stir dirt and loose weeds from these lifeless plains, obscuring your view and making the road difficult to follow. Surrounding you, black clouds of cruel design blow foul breath onto the scarred land. Leaving the road would be dangerous.
5788: Dirt rains down from the air upon you like a heavy spring shower. Accumulating in your pockets and folds, you can even feel its added weight upon your body. Squinting to shield your eyes, you try to scan for the road, but to no avail. Caught in this constant blowing wind, you lose all sense of orientation, only the thin strands of weeds blowing fiercely in the wind give you a sense of direction.
5789: The ground rises here, bringing you slowly out of the fierce winds preying on the lower lands. Once perhaps this was a grassy slope, covered with bushes and weeds. Now, broken wood and bits of metal zip through the air, threatening to pierce or bash you without warning. The ground, broken rocks and dirt, add dust to the air shrouding you in a fog of particles.
5790: The wind quiets here, ending its howling reign at the cusp of this rise. Below you and to the north, the brown grass waves in the wind, but it is of a more natural persuasion. The forced winds around you ebb back, gathering strength near the fissure, their source of power.
5791: Wizard spells are of course powerful, it is easy to remember seeing mages throwing herbs into the air as they sang words of spells, summoning clouds and rains upon once shining bright skies. Perhaps that is what the foul minions of Morgoth have done. Plagued this land with eternal winds of evil. Or perhaps this dying land suffers from nothing more than the fatal lick of Melkor's powers, songs of discord ruining Eru's vision, regardless, the land around you lies dead and miserable with no end in sight.
5792: Broken stumps and bits of wood are all that hint of this lands former life here. Once perhaps a green forest, now they stand as monuments and relics to a life long lost. Surely the winds could not have caused all this death? Rumors of the strength of Angmar trigger your thoughts. Perhaps this was engineered by the foul WitchKing, for the air around you blows with malevolence.
5793: A few patches of hearty vegitation struggle here to take root. Choked in dirt and debris, they lay bruised and pale, clinging to life. The majority of the area is nothing but broken dirt and rock, a true wasteland. Checking to find some sort of reference or orientation, your view is lost in the constant winds around you.
5794: The earth lies barren here. After years of fighting with constant winds, the land lies plucked clean, like a goose without a feather. All that remains is loose dirt and broken debris. Gnarled pieces of wood, tattered bits of clothing lay tossed apathetically, the victims of a powerful and hateful wind.
5795: A black snake, with red markings, is lying here.

The ground here rolls ever so slightly, once no doubt a waving lush plain of grass and flowers. Now, like a broken and battered enemy, all that remains is dust and rock. A few weeds dig into the lifeless land, the last remaining warriors of a beaten and dying land.
5796: Seemingly lost within this fog of dirt and particles, you look vainly for the reassuring road. Winds swirl around you, lifting your body with incredible force. A few more gusts like that, and you could find yourself flying through the air! Glancing around for some sort of reference, your gaze is broken by the endless view of brown.
5797: Tiny whirlwinds sprout around you, swirling dust into plumes and sending them spinning to the sky. The fiery glow of Arien or Stars is blotted by the blanket of dirt constant falling downwards upon you. Shaking the dirt from your body like a heavy snow, you scan for a way out of this wasteland.
5798: Like a crooked dagger into the heart of Ea, here an open fissure travels deep underground, perhaps even into the Eternal Flame. Waves of incredible heat belch from this opened wound, mixing into the cool air and creating turbelent winds. Dirt and debris kick up around you, obscuring your view and threatening to topple you without warning.
5799: A brigand, looking at your nice purse, is sneaking here.

This small passageway through the hills was created to ship materials easily to and from the under-construction mine in this vicinity. It's crudely crafted, with no support save the rock above it. It now appears to be abandoned.
5800: Crunch.. Crunch.. Crunch.. the sound of feet on the dry vegetation is the only audible sound you hear. Scanning for signs of life, the occasional snake or vulture are your only companions, and certainly not friendly ones. Opening into a vast plain of broken, seething, ashen ground, these hills gently roll for miles and miles, until your sight can perceive no more.
5801: The sound of crunching feet on the dry vegitation is the only audible sound you hear. Scanning for signs of life, the occasional snake or vulture are your only companions, and certainly not friendly ones. Opening into a vast plain of broken, seething, ashend ground, these hills roll onwards for many miles, until your sight can perceive no more.
5802:
A low, many-branched shrub covers the ground here.
A suspicious-looking man watches the area carefully.

Leaving the bitter winds behind, you feel no safer here. The burnt ground, as though touched by the fierce Anar, lies scarred and black. The charred bushes leave a bitter taste in your throat and mouth. Your body, covered in dried sweat and filth, begs for rest and sleep. Yet here, in this opened barren land visible for miles, rest would not be prudent.
5803: A grey wolf is here, salivating profusely.

Rising before you is a blackened slope, further to the west you see more of the same dreary, blackened ground. It is as if war were waged here from which the land never healed. Looking southward you glimpse part of the Old East Road, wishing desperately you could get back to it.
5804:
There are two stinging nettles here.
A brown snake watches you.

The ground, brown and parched lies gasping for life around you. Huge vicious nettles seem to be the only plant thriving here, pricking your skin and bringing blood to their sharp pointy spear-like petals. Searching for a sense of direction, you seem small and insignificant in the bleak area of the Lone-lands around you.
5805: A sprawling green bush of stinging nettle grows here.

You stumble out of those windy barren plains, thankful to have escaped with your life. Quickly scanning the area, it doesnt look much more pleasant. Surrounding your sight is dry, cracked, burnt grass and towering stinging nettles. Your body involuntarily shudders as the stinging nettles bite into your mottled and sweating flesh.
5806: A few hardy trees remain here, the last guardians of a once lush forest. But weathered after years of evilness, they now stand bent towards the ground, leaning on one another for support. The entire effect is haunting, you look up at a network of interwoven trees, blocking the heavens above.
5807: A black pond of water is here.

The pond before you appears relatively dried out and lifeless. Small pockets of water have collected in some of the deeper depressions of this uneven pond bed making drink possible. The water however, is dark and gritty.
5808: You peer closely at this mishapen hill trying to discover its secrets. Then it dawns on you, this is in fact not a hill at all, but a man made structure, conquered by the wild elements of nature. A small pock marked archway stands over the rubbled entrance, inscribed upon it the words: "TarnGurth", or rough westron translation, Gates of Death.
5809: From this vantage point you can see an outlay of the area. Westwardly, the ashen land continues, occasional vents of steam can be seen whistling out from under rocks. To the east, you are puzzled. It looks as though you see a brown grassy hill, but its odd shape makes you curious. Far to the south, the Old East Road is visible.
5810:
A brass lantern has been set on the ground.
A coil of rope is lying here.
A rusty pickaxe with a broken handle lies discarded here.

This small cut in the rock appears to have once held all the mining equipment used in excavation. Scattered about the floor lie broken lanterns, bits of metal and splintered ore carts. Along the wall, dirty but strong rope hangs from wooden pegs, a true essential for any miner.
5811: A brown bear is sleeping here.

Up ahead of you the sky peers through the domed cavern walls, cool air mixes with the hot dry heat from farther within creating a constant yet gentle breeze. From the far wall, rain water and moisture collects and leaks down a crevice in the ceiling, collecting in a small cool pool of water. The entire affect refreshes your sweat stained body.
5812: Your heart, so recently free and light, drops like a stone pit.. Yes, it is true you are standing outside among the sky and air, but towering walls surround you on all sides. The opening, is in fact, the bottom of a huge blackened sinkhole. There appears to be no access to the surface from here.
5813: You appear to be travelling along the main passageway of the mine. In between the wooden planked walls the wet earth sweats with warm water. The wood itself appears warped and compromised, its integrity lost after years of moisture and stress.
5814: The corridor here begins to descend further into the earth, the air takes on a musty mildew-like smell. Off to your right a wooden door prevents further access leaving you only further downwards into the dark, as your option.
5815: Here marks the entrance to the caverns of TarnGurth. The walls surrounding you perspire with underground warmed water, giving the entrance a humid misty atmosphere. Parts of the muddy walls have been smoothed away and arched with wooden supports, yet most of the cavern has been left in excavation form, with the walls gashed and gutted, the strikes of pickaxes still visible. It seems obvious that this mine was long abandoned before it was ever finished.
5816: A big cavebear is padding around here.

This part of the tunnel has partially caved in, but you notice a section of the roof still standing. Beneath it, the bones of foxes and rabbits lay cluttered on the floor. Along the farside of the wall, a large crack in the floor sends intense waves of heat lofting into the air. This looks like a nice warm spot for some animal to live.
5817: Is your imagination playing tricks on you or did you just feel the cool lick of a soft breeze upon your sweat stained forehead? You cautiously advance forward, the sound of trickling water echos from the walls ahead.
5818: Enough light is shining from ahead that you are finally able to see the walls again. To your surprise, the dirt sodden earth has been replaced by smooth worn rock, small veins of copper and gold streak through the wall, magnifying the light source, and sending it sparkling down the length of the tunnel.
5819: Warm currents of heat circulate in the air around you, yet deep inside you feel cold and afraid. It occurs to you, maybe this mine wasn't abandoned after all, maybe the workers left their merry homes fully expecting to return, and vanished in the depths of these mines, never returning... What would put such a thought in your mind?
5820: Fierce heat lashes at your face from farther ahead. The walls weep here with hot, scalding water. It appears as though this was to have been a side corridor, but digging was probably stopped when they realized they were dangerously close to an underground steam spring.
5821: AAAAAIIIIIYYYYEEEEEEEEEEE!!! Your body shudders in sharp unyielding pain as the hot steam from below sears the flesh from your body. Your eyes explode seconds later, sparing you the sight of a mist of red plume travelling up the vent.... the last remains of your mortal body.
5822: The rocks blast you with stored and active heat, nearby there must be a very hot flow of molten rock or steam. The tunnel twists and curves here making it difficult here to see what is ahead. A small door to the west is also noticeable.
5823: Here the tunnel breaks into two seperate directions, westards or eastwards. Both choices plunge you further down into the dark and intolerable heat. You cant help but have an eerie feeling about this place. Perhaps you should just turn back?
5824: A thick darkness hangs in the air, barely penetrable by your light. The sea of black around you makes you grasp for the moist earthen walls in reassurance. Only seconds later, a powerful wave of nausea sweeps over you, your nostrils are assailed with the smell of rotting flesh and stale blood.
5825:
An intact skeleton of a man is walking around here.
An intact skeleton of a man is walking around here.
An intact skeleton of a man is walking around here.
A moaning ghost advances forward, softly floating above the ground.
A small spirit floats around here, with despair in its eyes.

Turning the corner you are stunned and horrified by the sight that greets you. This large open cavern, that was probably a principle area of mineral extraction, has been turned into a decaying uncovered gravepit. The numerous small chutes that normally serve to probe for mineral content, have been stuffed full with broken limbs, decaying bodies, and tattered remains. The effect is quite sublime, the once open tubes now resemble a gruesomely improvised catacomb. A weathered board stands here, displaying a warning...
5826:
There are two musty loaves of bread here.
There are two beer bottles here.
A giant rat patters against you, squeaking maliciously.

Stepping down into the cellar you are shocked by the warm water surrounding your ankles... this area is flooded! Barrels that once probably held wine and drink now float empty along the debris strewn water. Upon the shelves, bits of moldy bread still remain untouched.
5827:
A hooded brass lantern has been left here.
A dark intangible shadow turns to face you.

A large oaken desk dominates this room, covered about it still lay the schematic drawings and blueprints for this mine. Above the chair a tattered and musty banner once displaying some proud crest, now is worm eaten and undistinguishable. The room looks alltogether undisturbed, yet you still feel a presence nearby.
5828: You stumble on the bones and corpses under foot. All around you the pale white faces of the dead stare blankly at you, some viciously mauled, others you would almost mistake for alive. You walk quietly, fearful that one loud noise might wake them out of their daze. A pale corpse stares directly at you.....
5829: The ground here is sticky to walk on, your feet making sucking noises with each step you take. A sense of danger washes over your body, you wish your feet would stop making so much noise! Cautiously glancing around you, you notice fine threads of silk swaying gently, only thing is, there is no wind.
5830:
The corpse of a huge tarantula is lying here.
The corpse of a huge tarantula is lying here.

Large rocks here lay covered with a thin glaze. Long sinewy threads of web spindle to the ceiling creating a huge tent in the centre of the room. Nestled underneath this moist shelter, HUGE spider eggs, easily the size of boulders, lay pressed up against the rocken walls. If these are the husks of infant spiders, you shudder to think of the adults....
5831:
The corpse of a huge tarantula is lying here.
The corpse of a huge, poisonous spider is lying here.
The corpse of a huge, poisonous spider is lying here.

Thick rope sized strands of web cut your path, hanging from the walls and and corridors around you. Navigating through these webs, and avoiding entanglement is becoming increasingly difficult. All around you, shadows spring and disappear from view. Perhaps it is time to turn around.
5832: A huge, poisonous spider is here.

That last step didn't seem too wise. Encircling you, thick ropey glue like webs greedily grab at your clothing. You try desperately to weave a path through the dense webs, but any second you could become totally trapped.
5833: Thick cobwebs cover the tunnel, ensnaring you in their sticky strands.

Attempting to navigate through this dense wall of web is proving very difficult. Tough thick web snare your clothing, forcing you deeper into their grasp. Can you escape? You lunge forward with every ounce of strength, I guess you shall soon find out.
5834: Up ahead you feel the familiar warmth and humidity associated with this entire cavern.. only, it somehow "feels" different. The hot current comes in regular timed pattern, followed by a faint, guttural noise. Whatever is ahead of you, it sounds large.
5835:
A sable pouch lies on the ground. (blue aura).
Thick cobwebs cover the tunnel, ensnaring you in their sticky strands.
A rotten corpse is hanging here.
A huge, poisonous spider is here.
Moving silently and adeptly along his webs, Mormaeg senses you.

Large spindles of webs drop from the high vaulted ceiling, travelling downwards into a large widening arc. Before you lies a macabre scene, mummified remains of Elves, Dwarves and other unlucky pests hang lifeless within the webs. You catch a glint of metal here, a bundle of something there, the whole area reminds you of a bunch of puppets, suspended by strings.
5836: The sweat rolls off your face in torrents, stinging your eyes and drenching your body. You wonder how anyone could have worked in these conditions. Up ahead however the darkness breaks, some bright light source further ahead is reflecting back off the shining rocks. It affords you minimal light.
5837: A water barrel has been left here.

As you push the planks aside, a draft of cool air wafts out in your face. Apparently you have wandered into some sort of dwelling. There is little to notice, just a table, chairs, and a few boxes scattered about. The spartan existence along with the isolated location makes you think that the inhabitants are either very poor, or on the run from something.
5838:
A sturdy bandit bodyguard stands here, eager to hack you to pieces.
A sturdy bandit bodyguard stands here, eager to hack you to pieces.
A wiry smuggler is here, attempting to avoid being seen.

Cleverly concealed from the road, this hollowed out slope is a perfect place to hide from the nearby travellers. The furnishings suggest that there is constant activity here. There are water barrels and clothes on the floor, while in a corner you see various weapons lying about. It occurs to you that this sort of place would be good for an ambush, or just to hide stolen goods.
5839: A hungry warg stands here, sniffing around for flesh.

Old pines loom far above you, blocking out any light the sky might provide. Some of the withered trees, rotten and ancient, have fallen apart and the splinters cover the mossy ground. In some places the trees are torn by mortal hands however, broken and scattered. The forest gives away to a barren plain in the north. South of here a huge barricade-like pile of old trunks and branches obstruct any further passage.
5840: Here the trees grow so tall, with crowns so thick, that there isn't a single place where the sky is visible. The ground is all mud and rocks, and it seems this part of the forest lacks all signs of animal activity. The smell of pines and dirt is ever present.
5841: This part of the forest is old, dark and murky. It smells of decay and half of the trees are probably dead. Except for the knocked down trees and huge, deep tracks of trolls there are no signs of living creatures. To the west the forest lightens some, but to the east and south the forest of Trollshaws stretches further on.
5842:
A buck runs swiftly from place to place, looking about warily as it grazes.
A small rat runs about, oblivious to your presence.

Tall pines with thick, huge crowns stretch towards the skies, preventing both sunshine and starlight to reach the forest floor. The ground is a strange mix of mud and moss, dead branches and thorny shrubbery. East and west of here, passage through the forest is possible.
5843: The trees here stand so thick that, combined with the multitude of thorny shrubbery on the ground and climbing the pines, almost any movement is a strain. There is no way of knowing if the faint glow from far above is the sun or the moon, or even the stars. It seems as if this old forest wittingly and in a clever way is blocking all light to reach any of its dwellers. The woods lighten up just a tad to the south and west. Travel in any direction is made impossible by the sheer mass of trees, both dead and alive.
5844: South and east of here, a dense and dark pine forest grows. The trees are old and tall, with huge, thick crowns. Here the ground is barren, covered only with rubble and an occasional sharp, jagged rock. To the west, the plains continue.
5845: Black and Murky Pool in the Pine Forest
A hairy black spider wraps up a silken package with her hind legs.

A still, almost dead-looking, black pool lies here in the midst of the forest. It smells of decay, and rotten branches and twigs break the surface in numerous places. To the south the forest looks to grow even thicker, but west of here passage is still possible without too much strain. The remnants of a wooden sign lies next to the pond, unreadable from years of decay and erosion.
5846: Small Hill in the Pine Forest
A brutish forest troll is hunting here, looking for some tasty flesh.

A small hill, covered by spruce and an occasional young pine, rises above the forest floor. Even though on higher ground, the dense forest still obstructs vision in all directions -- the pines standing taller than this hill. A mound made from smooth, round boulders stands here.
5847: A brutish forest troll is hunting here, looking for some tasty flesh.

Old, tall pines stand here in silence, reaching towards the sky. The ground is covered by a layer of twigs, pine-needles, moss and dead branches. At some places miniature spiderwebs hang between the twigs on the ground, and in a few of the webs an insect or pine-needle has been caught. The forest continues to the west and south, but to the north it rises somewhat to climb a small hill. East of here, a flat area lies -- devoid of trees.
5848: Skull-shaped Boulder in a Dreary Pine Forest
A forest spider is here crawling around.

A massive moss-clad boulder stands amidst the numerous pines, shaped almost like a skull -- the moss being its helmet. Between the trees to the west a forest trail can be seen. To the east, north and south the dense forest spreads out undisturbed. Small webs can be seen on some of the bushes, and between twigs on the ground.
5849: A Trail through the Dense Pine Forest

The forest grows dense here, letting only a few rays of sun reach the small white flowers and twigs on the ground. Some spruce and lots of pine trees grow here, of which several are very old and thick and a few have reached a great height, now towering high above the roof of the forest. A trail climbs up from the south, narrowing some as it turns west.
5850: A fierce boar is here, making grunting noises.

The ground slopes slowly to the south, now and then broken by boulders and big rocks. The forest mainly consists of pine trees, but also spruce can be seen growing here together with juniper and an occasional thorn bush. Not very broad but still clear, a trail can be discerned winding its way eastwards through the twigs and shrubberies under the trees.
5851: A thick, dense forest of old withered trees and strong pines extends in all directions. An occasional moss-covered boulder can be found, and on some of the dead trees some pale fungi are prospering. It seems birds are the only creatures who inhabit this area, since no signs of any ground-living beasts can be seen.
5852: Tall, strong pines stand close together here, thick and ever-green. The ground is covered by a layer of thick, soft, strong-smelling moss. To the west a hedge can be glimpsed through the trees and underbrush. In all other directions only forest can be seen.
5853: North of here, the vast forest stretches undisturbed for miles, but to the south the trees surrender to the plains. East and west of here the edge of the forest goes on towards the horizon. Bushes and even an occasional flower cover the ground here, and there are tracks of small animals everywhere. Tiny spiderwebs can be seen between the branches of some of the trees.
5854: Along the edge of the pine forest to the north, sturdy plants and patches of flowers can be found, as well as tracks of smaller woodland animals and birds. South of here the forest gives way to a bushy, flat plain but to the east, west and north the tall pines rule the land.
5855: A brutish forest troll is hunting here, looking for some tasty flesh.

Thorny bushes and tall pines would make travel in this part of the forest very taxing, were it not for the worn and wide trail that climbs up to the north and into the forest to the east. South of here the pines seem to stand a bit further apart, but in all direction the forest grows as dense and shady as ever.
5856: A brutish forest troll is hunting here, looking for some tasty flesh.

Winding its way through the dense forest, dodging boulders and small hedge-like clumps of shrubbery, the trail is the only reason travel is possible in this harsh environment. To the west and east, the trail plunges deeper into the forest. South of here the trees stand tall and silent. Passage north is impossible because of the severe undergrowth. In some trees tiny spiders have spun their thin webs.
5857: A brutish forest troll is hunting here, looking for some tasty flesh.

The ground being hard-packed earth, covered with a few pine-needles, twigs and a nut-shell once in a while, this trail makes travel through the old, dense pine forest less taxing. To the south the forest becomes a tad less dense, but in all other directions the heavy woods continue. The trail leads on to the west and east.
5858: East of here, the otherwise dense forest becomes lighter as the number of mighty pines decreases. A few old, rotting stumps can be seen in some places; like ancient but still bleeding wounds in the woods. The mossy ground is covered by twigs and pine cones. North of here a trail leads deeper into the dense underbrush.
5859: A buck runs swiftly from place to place, looking about warily as it grazes.

Dense bushes and trees shrouded in a multitude of tiny spiderwebs, glimmering in any light, flank this narrow trail. The pines cease growing to the south, but the forest maintains its grip on the landscape to the north and west. North of here however, it seems spruce is dominating the horizon. To the south a large, flat area lies. Here the trail sits clear, only partially covered with a thin layer of pine-needles.
5860: A thick layer of brown, dried spruce-needles cover the mossy ground in most places -- only broken by a few very low plants with blueish green, rounded leaves. Patches of pale, hard fungi grows on the trunks of some of the tall and old spruce. To the north the forest opens up to some rocky plains, but to the east the spruce forest grows as dense as ever. West and south of here the woods are a bit lighter, mainly consisting of pines.
5861: Rotting branches and small twigs cover the ground, in some places covered by moss and spiderwebs. The pines stand as tall as ever here, and the forest spreads out in all directions. To the south, a small trail can be glimpsed through the dense vegetation.
5862: Two huge pine trees have fallen here, their stumps being charred. Some time ago this part of the forest must have suffered from a lightning-strike, which resulted in the fallen trees forming a massive barrier to the west and south. North and east of here, further passage into the forest is possible.
5863: A Trail along a Sheer Rock Face

A small mushroom grows nearby.
A brutish forest troll is hunting here, looking for some tasty flesh.

East of here a sheer, tall and remarkably flat granite rockface blocks all passage. Only in a few places is the smooth surface disturbed by erosion or spidery carvings. A trail stretches through the dense forest just by the rockface, and it slowly climbs down to the north and south. To the west the silent forest lies thick and dark.
5864: A disgusting forest troll is searching for fresh meat here.

The trees grow so dense that passage through this part of the forest is very hard. Old, withered rocks break the ground in a few places, overgrown by fungi and covered in dead, brown spruce-needles. To the north a meadow can be glimpsed, but west of here the spruce forest lies undisturbed. Open fields lie to the south, and some rolling hills dominate the eastern sky.
5865: A Majestic Mound in a Spruce Forest

A short evergreen plant, with slightly bluish needles, grows here.
On the plant, there are two clusters of hard, round, black berries.
A disgusting forest troll is searching for fresh meat here.

A huge, mossy meadow dominates this part of the forest. In its middle a tall mound has been raised, possibly hundreds of years ago. The boulders are somewhat eroded and covered with fungi and moss. A broken circle of smaller, white, rocks surround it. The spruce forest stretches onwards to the east and south. To the north and west a rocky, barren plain lies.
5866: A disgusting forest troll is searching for fresh meat here.

Huge spruce trees grow very close together here, the ground being moist and mossy. In a few places small rocks show beneath the moss, covered by the cones and needles which have fallen from the trees. The air is thick, and the forest lets very little light in -- making this wood very dim. Some small webs spun by even smaller spiders hang between some branches. To the north and west the forest stretches onward. South of here a large, grass-clad hill stands. To the east a thorny hedge of brambles and young spruces form an impassable obstruction.
5867:
A forest spider is here crawling around.
A buck runs swiftly from place to place, looking about warily as it grazes.

Here the trees stand close together, forming a massive barrier of sharp needles and heavy branches. The ground is moist, black earth and very few plants grow below the spruce. Large spider webs form glimmering spans between the trees, tiny drops of dew stuck to them reflecting the small and thin rays of light which passes through the thick woods. To the south one can travel deeper into the forest. North of here the forest thins as an area of green hillocks begins. East and west of here, flat plains can be seen -- the eastern one being covered by tall grass and the western one rocky and barren.
5868: At some places the pines stand so close together there is no way of telling where the crown on one tree ends and where the next one starts. Dead branches, splinters and stumps cover the ground, only to be overgrown by brown bushes in a few places. Travel east from here is made impossible by a very thick hedge, composed by all sorts of thorn-bushes and young trees.
5869: The canyon dips to its lowest point here, with sheer rockfaces to the west and north. East and south of here the canyon continues, sloping upwards to the surrounding terrain. A few old and broken bones lie on the ground, and in some places small brown-green plants grows. In the north-west corner of this dip in the canyon four boulders stand in a square-like formation.
5870: A large pile of boulders is sitting here, probably debris from a rockslide.

The canyon floor slopes heavily downwards to the north, and upwards to the east -- towards the rocky hills. North of here the canyon seems to bend to the east, far away. The canyon floor is covered by rubble and earth, and some tiny and twisted plants grow here.
5871: Mainly composed by spruce, but also an occasional pine tree, the forest dips southwards into the plains here. East of here a thick, inpenetrable hedge makes any passage impossible, but to the west the bush-covered plains stretches on. To the north the vast, dense and shady forest of pines grows old and ever-silent.
5872: A fierce boar is here, making grunting noises.

Tall and steep these hills rise high above the Old East Road to the south. East of here a very deep and narrow canyon splits the hills apart, and it seems to be impossible to get to the bottom without risking life and limb. To the west however, quiet plains slope from the north down towards the road. North of here patches of trees form a forest, which grows thicker in that direction.
5873: The road is still rather level even though the terrain on both sides is quite rugged. This is due entirely to the presence of a notch cut through the hills like a dagger-wound. Whether this is a natural phenomena or the remnant of some ancient construction project cannot be determined, but travelers certainly benefit from its existence.
5874: A very steep ridge running from southwest to northeast meets the road here, but the road passes through a narrow cleft and manages to stay almost level. If this cleft is artificial, it was excavated centuries ago because the walls are well eroded.
5875: The road winds through an area of hills to the south and a plain sloping upwards to the north. East and west of here the road continues. To the north-east, a remarkably tall and steep hill can be seen.
5876: The road passes through a region of small hillocks, which grow larger as one moves to the east. The surrounding countryside supports a few sparse patches of forest, but for the most part the land is grassy. To the east, some of the larger hills begin to support some forested areas.
5877: Flat plains, with only a few shrubberies and even fewer flowers slope down to the south, where the Old East Road stretches from east to west. East of here steep, dangerous-looking hills stab at the sky, and far to the north the edges of a vast forest can be seen where the plains end. A small and somewhat demolished mound, overgrown with thorny bushes and grass stands here.
5878: A statue of a troll is posed in a moment of flight yet forever frozen in stone.

Dead bushes mix with living ones on this seemingly dead plain, which connects the forest to the north with the slopes to the south. East of here the forest dips southwards into the plains, but west of here the horizon is clear. To the south-east jagged, tall hills can be seen.
5879: Flat plains stretch from the slopes to the south to the pine forest to the north. West of here a mound can be seen in a distance, but to the east the plains goes on without any noticable landmarks. Small clumps of bushes and thorny shrubberies grow here, and even a tiny patch of young spruces has rooted here.
5880: The plains slope down from the north towards the Old East Road, south of here. Heather plants grow beside the road, and boulders of different sizes are spread out all over the slopes. Embedded in the grass are wooden splinters from what must have been several wagons many years ago. Far north of here, the border of a forest is visible.
5881: A very wide and tall hill stands here, its western side being a smooth and sheer granite rockface. A huge circle of mighty pines crown the hill, giving it a majestic look. East of here smaller hills, overgrown by pines, makes the landscape look like a forest-green sea of trees, the hilltops being the waves. To the south flat, rocky plains spread out.
5882: A large open area spreads east- and south-wards. Only rubble and small, ruined mounds and an occasional bush or patch of slender sillows cover the ground. To the west a small hill protrudes towards the horizon, it's top just above the crowns of the pines standing beneath it. North of here a round hill is topped by a symmetric circle of pines, making it resemble a head wearing a crown of trees.
5883: Rocky ground, devoid of all animal life, spreads out far to the north. The only signs of any life are the old, abandoned campsites and the broken and withered bones that can be spotted in a few places. To the south -- ranging through the south-east, to east of here -- a majestic forest of old and strong-looking spruce grows. To the west another forest begins, but that one consists mainly of pines -- them too being tall, old and strong.
5884: Numerous small hills, their sides covered by a large number of tall and ever-green pines, lie scattered here. To the east the range of hills is covered by grass, but west of here a huge hill -- crowned with pines -- can be spotted. South of here a plain lies, its face plagued by the brownish green, thorny bushes which grow there.
5885: Thorny Bushes Scattered on Rocky Plains

The rocky plains lead further on to the west, the ground here broken by tall, brown-green thorn bushes. A spruce forest can be seen to the south and east, the powerful trees making the woods look like a green inpenetrable wall. To the north wooded hills roll smoothly.
5886: Grass-covered hillocks grow into rolling hills to the west, where the trees dominate the plant-life. Here a large number of different flowers -- mainly white and light blue -- grow in patches. To the south a forest of mainly spruce, as well as some willows at the outskirts, grows in silence. The hilly area surrenders to the grassy plains east of here.
5887: Two feet tall, lush and green grass cover this wide plain. Very few flowers, mostly tiny pale ones, grow here. To the west the landscape elevates some as the grass climbs numerous hillocks. South of here the grass grows taller, it is also darker in colour. To the east a large area of tall hills stand, looking as if they are cloaked in a layer of dark green pines.
5888: Brownish green grass grow tall on this open plain. In some spots the grass disappears and only charred, cracked earth can be seen. The open area ranges from here both to the north and to the south, the grass looking as if it is a bit shorter to the north. Hills can be seen to the north-west and north-east, and east of here a trail can be seen winding through the wooded hills. To the west a very dark spruce forest stands.
5889: Yellow flowers, with grey-green foliage, grow in clusters here.

A narrow, worn earthen trail leads into the rolling hills to the south and further into the large fields of tall brown-green grass to the east. Small clumps of young sallow trees grow in the western end of this plain, and beyond them a thick and tall hedge-like formation of brambles and spruce blocks entrance to the dark forest. To the north the grassy plain meets the sky at the far horizon. A great hill pierces the skyline in the south-east.
5890: Narrow Trail by a Great Hill

An utterly great hill rises east of here, seemingly impossible to scale by any means. Here the wooded hills stand covered by animal-paths and a vast number of conifers -- growing dense in the dales between hill-crests. From the north a thin trail grows wider as it enters the hilly area. The trail leads further into the hills to the south, but to the west the elevated landscape looks undisturbed by any kind of civilization.
5891: A clear spring babbles as cool water trickles out of the ground.

A quite large, but yet ordinary-looking, hill stands here; green grass and moss covering its sides. On top of the hill a small spring bursts from the ground, the water forming a tiny pond. To the south a faint trail can be seen winding its way over the flat plains. North and west of here a large forest of spruce trees stand, dark and sinister-looking. To the east some smooth hills can be seen.
5892: Trail through Hills Shrouded in Conifers

Young, bright green spruce and pines climb the sides of the grassy, rolling hills. Some of the trees can not be more than a few years old, whereas some other are almost full-grown. A small trail winds its way through the lush dales between the crests. The path leads into the fields west of here and to the north the trail passes by a very tall hill which lies to the north-east. The floor of a dim valley can be espied far down to the east.
5893: A huge warg is here, moving in for the kill.

Here the hills stand in formations creating a multitude of small dales between the crests. Many of the hilltops looks as if they were cut off or hammered upon by the gods ages ago -- the round, rolling hills topped by very flat surfaces. A ridge of jagged hills is clearly visible against the eastern skyline, but to get there one would probably have to approach them from another direction. A plateau rises to the south, and west of here the ground lowers into the plains. This range of hills stretches further northwards, where a winding, serpentine trail can be seen circling the hills and dales.
5896: To the south, much of the forest has been cleared away. Perhaps there was once some sort of habitation there. To the west, the land rises to a low range of hills, although the road seems to stay somewhat level as it takes advantage of a notch cutting through the hills. The forests are not as prominent to the north, and often the hills have bald tops.
5897: On the south side of the road, a rich forest spreads out. East of here the road digs deeper into the hills, but to the west the ground flattens some. To the north, rugged hills make it impossible to leave the road.
5898: To the north, a set of extremely rugged hills prevents one from leaving the road, as the ground quickly deteriorated into eroded gullies choked with undergrowth. South of the road the hills aren't nearly as severe, and the pockets of forest are full of game.
5899: To the north, many rugged hills present a formidable challenge to anyone traveling off of the road. The hills are gentler to the south, but there is quite a lot of vegetation. To the west, a very steep (but narrow) ridge cuts across the road at an angle.
5900: All earth on the eastern side of this hill has eroded away, leaving a clean and sheer rockface. Beyond the rockface a range of smaller and not as rugged hills cover the landscape. The Old East Road lies south of here, but to get there one would have to go far west before it is possible to climb down from the tall hills. To the north, more hills lie scattered over the land.
5901: On top of this rugged hill, a clump of trees provides a natural wind-shelter as it surrounds a small dip in the hill-crown. To the south a majestic view of the Old East Road opens up, but climbing down the steep and rubble-covered hillside would be impossible. The hills slopes down to a number of smaller rocky hills to the west, but east of here another hill stands as tall and steep. Some smaller, smoother hills stand to the north.
5902: This area is covered with rocky hills and small hillocks between them. On the ground boulders, rocks and rubble makes travel hard. Strong-looking young spruces form small clumps on the tops of some of the hills. To the south the Old East Road stretches from east to west, and west of here the hills slopes downwards into a very narrow crevice-like canyon. East of here the hills grow taller, and there is no way of seeing past them.
5903: This narrow canyon, windling between the tall and rocky hills, gives no hint of any plant or animal life. All that can be seen is cracked earth and sheer rockfaces. The canyon slopes down to the west, and to the east it is possible to scale a steep hill. To the north the hills disappear as fields begin.
5904: Quite large, blackened boulders lie scattered across the flat lowlands. Brown and dried grass cover the ground. A narrow canyon begins south of here, digging its way between the tall hills. The lowlands spread further on east, and west and north of here a vast pine forest lies.
5905: This large area of flat land spreads further on towards the north, west and east. The ground is mainly covered by brown, tall grass and some smaller dark green bushes carrying black-blue berries. To the south a massive of sharp, rocky hills can be seen.
5906: Brown, dried grass everywhere -- only to be disturbed by the worn earthen trail which leads west, into the pine forest, and east, onwards through the lowlands. Row by row, the pointed spruce stabs at the sky north of here, forming a truly mighty-looking forest. A few hillocks rolls at the eastern horizon.
5907: A narrow trail cleaves the tall grass on the plain covered by tall, brown and green grass. North of here a large hill stands, the trail leads east into a hilly area and west further through the grass. South of here the brownish fields continue. The trail breaks a circle of white rocks on the ground.
5908: A small, dried-out and shallow pond is the only thing which interrupts the seemingly endless flat lands which spread further on to west and north. Tall, steep hills pierce the southern horizon, their tops looking a bit like teeth towards the sky. East of here lies another range of hills, lower and not as sharp.
5909: The entire area is covered by numerous rather tall hills -- sharp, steep and jagged. At some places the hillsides are so cracked and rocky that climbing them would be impossible. A few dried-out bushes stand on one of the hill tops. South of here stands a very large hill, tall and steep. Looking north, one can see a huge plain -- only disturbed by an occasional patch of young, slender trees.
5910: Climbing these hills makes it possible to see for long distances. West of here a deep and narrow canyon goes to the west, where it after a mile or so bends off to the south where it disappears behind the hills. To the north the hills get fewer and fewer as open fields spread out. East and south of here the hills grow taller, steeper and more jagged. This area is covered by smooth, low hills and scattered boulders.
5911: The ground gains altitude to the north, where a large plateau dominates the horizon completely. Here the hills are lower, their sides clad in grass, moss and young conifers. The eastern slopes of this ridge are too severely steep to allow and travel in that direction. South of here the Old East Road makes a fast descent into a bowl-like valley, the slope being sheer and impossible to climb.
5912: The road passes through a bowl-shaped depression. The drainage seems to be poor, since the ground at the bottom is quite muddy. Along the northern edge of the road, the imprints of several huge and booted feet are obvious, even to those without a modicum of skill in tracking. The tracks head west, up the road, but disappear soon after leaving the soft mud.
5913: Some delicious wild strawberries grow on the ground.

A small area of flat land extends from here to the north; to both the east and west the hills present a challenge to travelers. To the west, some of the slopes are so severe as to make progress impossible. South of this area, the Old East Road takes advantage of a break in the terrain to provide a means of moving westward.
5914: The road here is often cut with small gullies caused by water draining from the hills to the north and west. To the east, the road slopes down into a shallow valley from whence comes the sounds of a small stream. Further west, the hills become more severe, with bald crowns sticking high above the dark forests.
5915: An area of flat, and somewhat rocky, lands spread out towards the south. The barren ground is occasionally disturbed by a monolith-looking rock or small patches of spruce. To the north a very dense and dim forest with a few very tall trees jags the horizon, and east of here a more open area with some scattered clumps of trees lie. To the west a high plateau can be reached by walking a small trail which winds upwards.
5916: The trees grow very close here, creating a thick and moist atmosphere, almost giving substance to the air itself. Between some bushes large, thick spiderwebs glimmer with tiny drops of water. The forest expands to the north and east, but to the south open and flat lands stretch out. Rocky and jagged hills stab at the western skyline.
5917: Thick and thorny bushes grow heavy in the small gaps between the multitude of dark trees, the ceiling of tree-crowns being so dense only thin rifts of the sky can be glimpsed. The dense forest spreads out to the south, but in all other directions hills surround the woodlands. East of here a remarkably tall and wooded hill can be seen.
5918: A vast number of small hills -- shrouded in cloudy heather -- range from the dim forest to the south towards the northern horizon. Patches of soft, green grass cover the hillsides. The vague outlines of a trail winds far east of here, and to the west a very high hilltop dominates the skyline. Climbing it would be impossible from here, due to the jagged, sheer rockface to the west.
5919: Heather covers these soft-looking and tall hills. In a small meadow between two hills stands the stone ruins of an ancient building, moss-covered and decrepit. To the north it is possible to climb down a somewhat steep rockface and reach the bottom of a deep crevice, where a thin trail leads from east to west. East of here winds a serpentine trail.
5920: A great bustard strides over the grass.

A deep crevice splits the land between the wooded hills to the north and the heathery hills to the south. The narrow cleft looks almost like a deep wound in the ground, like a long and thin rift in the landscape. A rocky trail lies at the bottom of the crevice, leading both east and west. The northern side of the crevice is too sheer to climb, the rockface smooth, dark rock.
5921: These hills are covered with soft, black earth. On them pines grow -- both ancient ones and younger trees. To the east it is possible to climb a very tall hill-top. West of here the range of hills continue without any visible landmarks. In what looks like a broad crevice -- south of here -- a trail runs from east to west. Scaling the sides of the land-rift would surely be lethal.
5922: A great bustard strides over the grass.

In the thick layer of black, soft earth that covers these hills tall, strong pines have rooted ages ago. The mighty trees stand thick, but there is not much other plantlife, apart from the moss that covers the few round boulders on the ground. To the west, a small flat area is covered with grass -- beyond that a tall, wooded hill. To the south and east the wooded hills roll over the land.
5923: On a Trail through the Wooded Hills

A thin trail winds between the hills, leading east into a narrow crevice and south onto the plains. Spruce and an occasional pine cover most of the hillsides, and on top of one of the hills an old and unused campsite can be seen. North of here the pines grow more dense on the hills, making them look even taller. To the west a field with tall, brown grass goes on towards the horizon.
5924: Brown grass, more than five feet tall, grows on these fields. A small, worn trail leads west into the grassy fields and north, winding its way through heavily wooded hills. To the south a very tall hill stands, its northern side being a sheer, unclimbable rockface.
5925: Descending from this incredibly tall hilltop would only be possible to the south. The hillsides to the west, north and east are sheer and gives no support for climbing them. To the south however, lies a deep and dark valley. East of here a range of heather-shrouded hills can be spotted, and beyond them the vague outlining of a serpentine trail. The flat area to the north is also split by a thin trail, possibly the same one as far east of here. The northern trail bends off to the west into the jagged hills that pierce the western skyline.
5926: The burnt and blackened skeletal remains of a human are here.

This valley is quite deep, its floor covered by a thick mix of moss and dark green grass. Some lone spruce trees rise from the damp valley floor. The western side of this bowl in the terrain is steep, and climbing it would be hard. Moving to the east or south would be a much easier way of ascending from this silent and secluded place, the valley-sides in those directions not at all as steep as the western one. At the northern end of the valley, the ground rises far off towards the sky, forming a tall hill.
5927: Hills composed of brown-red rock form a massive of jagged, cracked hills devoid of any trees or flowers. The sheer hillsides and the harsh terrain to the west makes passage to the lower, flat hills there impossible. To the north the entrance to a valley can be guessed, and south of here highlands stretch further on, covered by low plants and bushes. East of here lies dim woodlands.
5928: Short, worn green grass covers this large elliptic plateau, as well as a few dark green bushes and an occasional young pine. The ground slopes downwards to the south, into an area of low hills. East of here a range of taller hills rolls over the landscape. To the east a swift descent upon the plains is possible.
5929: The landscape here is composed of many small hillocks. Their rounded tops are often completely free of vegetation, but in the shallow depressions between there are often small stand of trees. The Old East Road lies north of here, and some hills stand to the east. West of here a flat, grassy area resides.
5930: The ground is a bit rougher here than to the west, and hills begin to dominate the landscape. To the north, the ground becomes much gentler and glimpses of the Old East Road are visible from the northernmost of the hills. The range of hills continues to the northeast --- the road passes through a notch in the hills, so a traveler would not have an arduous journey through the region, provided he stays on the road.
5931: Right to the north, the Old East Road runs through a notch in this range of rugged hills. Travel is treacherous, as often steep slopes are hidden beneath thick brush, and in the vales between the hills the trees grow close and tangled.
5932: Immediately to the west, a tall and razor-like ridge precludes any movement in that direction. The ridge ends abruptly a short distance to the north; it almost looks as if it has been sliced to allow passage for the road which lies a short distance away. In general, the terrain here is hills, broken by occasional patches of dense forest. The forests seem to dominate more in the northern areas.
5933: The hills here are fairly rugged. From the crests of the taller ones, the brown ribbon of the Old East Road can be seen a few miles to the north. Some of the lower hills are covered with pine and spruce, and in the shaded dells, tangled masses of rhododendrons make movement a chore.
5934: The lower-lying areas in the region are generally havens for small patches of forest, while the tops of the hills (some with slopes quite severe) stick out above the trees like rocks from the sea. The terrain seems much the same in every direction, but to the north the Old East Road is visible from vantage points on top of the hills.
5935: To the east, the forest abruptly ends in a large clearing. The ground is fairly hilly, and in the small dales between hillcrests the forest is quite thick. Small game-trails crisscross the area, and the calling of ravens is heard quite often. To the north, at the bottom of a slope, the Old East Road can be espied.
5936: At some point in the recent past, many of the trees in this area were chopped down --- the remains of rotting stumps are scattered throughout. In the centre of the clearing is a bare patch of earth, with pieces of charred wood protruding from the ground in several places. Perhaps some foolhardy person decided to settle here, but whatever structure once stood has long since been destroyed.
5937: The land falls somewhat to the east - the forest there becomes thinner, but the undergrowth seems much more prominent. To the north winds the ribbon of the Old East Road. The road is clearly visible because it runs through a shallow valley. To the east, the trees give way almost completely in an abrupt transition.
5938: The undergrowth has almost choked out the forest here --- only a few ancient gnarled trees have survived amongst the sea of brambles and thorn- bushes that have taken root here. The ground is fairly low and damp, and seems to slope slightly to the east. To the west the forest again prevails, and the ground is much drier.
5939: Numerous rivulets feed the growing creek as it meanders southwards. Gravel glistens from the clear creekbed, shining golds, browns, and reds. Gnarled tree-roots protrude from the streambank; the water is shaded by the flanking copses of beech and willow. To the west is a chaotic tumbling of brush and brambles.
5940: A large meadow opens up amid the surrounding brush and heath. The road meanders along its merry way to the north, while south you note a number of dilapidated structures that appear to be uninhabited.
5941: The Road descends into a valley and crosses a small creek. While the Road has been eroded somewhat, the colourful streambed is easily forded. There is a glimmering to the north where the creek seems to originate, to the south the valley deepens and widens as the creek courses forward.
5942: The Road ascends from the valley to the west, curving alongside a large vale. A large field lies to the south, grassy with some large trees scattered about. A few tumbled and broken structures lie beyond the field, while in the other direction woods grow near unto the road, and tall ridges rise above the treeline.
5943: Here the Road clings close to the feet of the hills, rolling and winding its way among woods and heather-covered slopes. The land is somewhat pleasant, but there is an oppressive look to the uplands to the north--somehow an air of evil radiates from the frowning crags and peaks.
5944: Continuing ever onward, the Road runs straight and true momentarily before resuming the winding and rolling that renders it difficult to gauge the path ahead for any great distance. Stained and broken by weather and neglect, the Road nevertheless bears evidence of recent travel by horse, cart, and the padding paws of some unknown quadruped.
5945: Fractured and faded by time and neglect, this ancient road still provides a solid footing as it winds from west to north. Scattered trees line the roadside, although to the east there are only twisted boles bereft of vitality.
5946: Here the Road winds through an area of denser forest--the trees nestle closely looming above you, their branches extended attemping to grasp their brethren opposite the road. Illumination filters through their limbs, dappling the way with alternating spatterings of light and shadow. One may continue along the road to the east or south, or dare to enter the unknown forests bordering the wide path.
5947: The Road proceeds through a dark, ominous section of the lonelands; all about are the withered apparently fire-blasted stumps and skeletal boles of trees. A trail blasted into the landscape will allow an easy journey north where the land seems if anything more tortured and inimical to life. Perhaps though, one's return might not prove so simple...maybe it would be wise to leave this area hastily.
5948: The Old Road proceeds doggedly onward through the barren surroundings, running momentarily straight and true. A faint urge to hurry onward tingles in the back of your mind; the area above the road has an unwholesome cast, while egress to the south is thwarted by a natural hedge of hawthorn.
5950: Bend in the Old East Road

The Road bends to the south and east before continuing its long journey from Rivendell to Bree. The countryside is rather barren hereabouts with the notable exception of a prosperous arbour of unusually tall and vital larches on one side of the Road.
5951: The Road passes alongside a broad dale, with abundant trees and brush all about you. The brush is so overgrown to the south as to effectively impede all travel in that direction--only the dint of many hours chopping and hacking would allow even minor progess.
5952: The Road plods onward, its surface worn and effaced by the travails of time and the impact of many a foot, hoof, or wheel. On either side of the road are mounds and patches of brush and brambles, growing so hardily to the south as to discourage all attempts to breach them there.
5953: To the south a dense patch of weeds and brambles makes entry into the forest seem quite impossible. To the north, however, the woodland has rather a weak and sickly appearance, with only the most sparse undergrowth, and a scattering of thin conifers. The road itself seems rough and unkempt.
5954: An impenetrable natural hedgerow of gorse and brambles stands to the south of the road, whilst to the north lies a narrow band of hills. The road itself is rough and stony, and shows little sign of regular recent use for heavy haulage, although it might easily be more often utilised for foot or mounted traffic.
5955: Marching doggedly onward from east to west, the Old East Road here lies immediately to the south of a narrow band of hills. To the other side the carriageway is bounded by a vast tract of woodland. Some of the trees grow so close to the road that their lowest branches reach well over the path, and an unwary traveller on horseback might easily find himself tumbled to the ground by these limbs.
5956: With hilly country to the north, and a thick area of woodland to the south, a traveller along this part of the Old East Road might find it difficult should he seek a suitable campsite. However, judging by their appearance, the woods should offer good hunting for those at need, for they are thick and lush, and should support a good variety of wildlife.
5957: The road here is littered with stones and a few tumbled boulders, which appear to have originated in the rocky sward just north of the carriageway. To the south you can see a thin area of woodland, the outskirts of a large forest, which stretches away to the southeast.
5958: Turning from west to north, the road travels through a low point in the land, and is littered by rocks and a few scattered boulders, which have apparently tumbled from an open area of sloping land to the northwest. To the south of the road lies what might once have been a pasture.
5959: Rocks and stones, and even a few small boulders litter the road here, where it travels through a shallow dip, making its way from east to south, then on westward across the land. The ground both east and north stands a little bit above the elevation of the road, whilst to the south and east it levels out once more. A vast forest looms across your field of view to the north.
5960: A little way to the north of here, a rough and bloody trail beats a ragged path through the forest. Neither have the trees and undergrowth here wholly escaped the depredations of whatever creature rent the trampled the vegetation there. Everywhere you look there are broken saplings and down-trodden bushes and weeds.
5961: The elongated shape of a stoat can be seen darting across the terrain.

Here the trail is marked with many bloodstains some of them fresh. Bending to the north and to the west, the rough path continues through the thick woods, and it is apparent that only creatures of massive strength could have ploughed such a course through the forest.
5962: Bits of blood and gore of various ages lie everywhere here. It looks as if some giant hand tore something limb from limb. A strange place to call home, or a place to flee for your lives. Large, splayed feet marks lie all over the heavily trodden ground.
5963: The road ploughs a steady east to west furrow across the country, as it makes its way bewteen Rivendell and far distant Bree. To the south it is bounded by what must once have been the lands of a smallholding. But to the north the thoroughfare is bounded by an area which seems to have been cleared of trees much more rapidly, and without a thought to farming.
5964: With now fallow farmland to the south, and an area of woodland which has apparently been brutally and carelessly felled lying to the north, the road here takes on a bleak aspect. Every slight gust of wind bites hard, with no nearby hills or trees to reduce its force, and not a single weed manages to grow amid the rocks and stones of the surface of the thoroughfare.
5965: Some ugly blow-flies are buzzing around here.

Travelling as it does now through a bleak and unsheltered part of the land, the road takes on a windswept and unwelcoming aspect. Perhaps long ago it saw frequent travellers, but now it has an air of disuse. Judging by all of the rocks and stones which litter its surface, it seems unlikely that many carriages, carts or wagons follow this route.
5966: Sweeping from west to north, the road draws close to a small range of hills. Hard by to the east is a sprawling forest, whose dark-limbed trees seem to reach out toward the roadway. And to the south and northwest lie regions which appear to have been hastily deforested at some time not too far into the past.
5967: The road changes course here, from a due east-west route, taking a turn to the south for a time. A narrow band of hills rises above you to the north, offering a ready place from which to watch people as they progress along the carriageway. The lands to the west however offer no shelter or hiding place, for someone has stripped them of the trees which once flourished there.
5968: The road winds east and west through the forest. A group of tall, dark trees blocks the passage to the south, while the land opens slightly towards the hills of the north.
5969: The road continues onward, its surface worn from many a traveller. The lands to the north of the road rise quickly, blocking your view of the distant Ettenmoors. To the south, the trees open slightly, offering access to a sombre forest.
5970: The Road begins to slope downwards toward the east where you spot a small stream that crosses the path. The land to the south is thick with forest and impassable, making the only option to stick to the road.
5971: A winding waterway crosses right over the Old East Road here. It is brown and muddy, but no more than half a foot deep. The road travels to the east and west here, and the stream crosses the road from north to south.
5973: Erupting from the hillside, a large spring burbles as it feeds a small creek that winds along a valley to the south, bisecting the large road there. The grey hillsides are covered with patches of heather and bracken, pale grasses also cling along the hills. The surroundings seem unnaturally quiet.
5974: A swift and agile forest cat moves silently through the vegetation.

Scattered clumps of fir and pine coexist with small patches of beech and mountain oaks. The ground rises sharply to the east, climbing into a untold number of hills. To the north the woods become thick and gloomy, bearing an enigmatic menace. Silence and somnolence prevail, broken only by the distant cry of a dark bird of omen.
5975: A swift and agile forest cat moves silently through the vegetation.

The very air around you seems murky and substantial, so closely the trees grow here. Even in the daytime, twin pinpoints of light suggestive of eyes peer out from the dim black vegetation. The land rears up in saw-edge peaks and ridges dominating the eastern skyline.
5976: Suddenly rising from the surroundings is a rock-tumbled hillside thickly blanketed with evergreens. Peering through the trees, one can detect a small strip on a trail winding here and there to the northeast. Dense primeval forest lies all about, thick bundles of firs and pines.
5977: While in places faint and overgrown, or choked with fallen stones and trees, at one time this path seems to have been much used. It was a path made by strong arms and heavy feet. Here and there old trees have been cut or even broken down, and the larger rocks have been cloven or heaved aside to make a way.
5978: Undulating from side to side in harmony with the contours of the land, the trail skirts by a large collection of hills to the north, winding east towards rising forests. The wayside is fairly barren, grassy and dotted with small flowering plants; few trees are to be seen.
5979: The rabid raccoon stands here, frothing at the mouth.

Wide hills rise and fall above the winding trail at their feet. The hillsides are green with plentiful grasses and a sprinkling of flowers and other small clinging flora. A narrow but distinct way leads from the trail below winding upward to a particularly tall summit to your north.
5980: The high hilltop affords a superb view of the surrounding countryside. Most notably you see a thin ribbon of a trail that seems to originate far to the northeast, beyond the horizon, though you see it pass by a stone tower at the edge of your sight. Somewhere far to the southwest, it most likely reaches the road, although this is beyond your immediate view. Closer at hand, the land is rocky and windswept, bereft of trees. All that grows here are some short grasses and thorny bushes; if one plans to spend time observing the surroundings it would be wise to account for the weather as there is nothing to shelter you from wind, rain, or snow.
5981: Tall pines have put their roots deep in the soil, and now guard these hills from wind and rain. Yet in places water has cleared paths in the terrain, taking some of the ground with it.
5982: All is silent below the canopy, and no single leaf or branch moves. One could almost expect something happening, but nothing does. The air is still and smells of decaying fungus. The forest comes to an abrupt end at the sloping hills in the east, but in the north it descends down without changing its shape.
5983: The rocks that cover the field in the east are less common here, so there is more room for trees to put their feet on. Rather efficiently they have so done too, the trunks are big and the branches strong. Sky cannot be seen through the canopy, but some light enters the forest from the east.
5984: The forest is broken by a clearing in the north, and there are some deers there eating grass. One of them has met the end of his life here though, body ripped open and half-eaten. It has not yet started to decay though, but it very soon will due to number of worms and other little beings crawling around.
5985: Here in the south corner of the clearing the grass slowly turns into bushes and eventually to the dark trees that block your view to the south and east.
5986: Here the canopy is less thick, and some light throws shadows in the bushes and plants. Birds can be heard singing happy songs in the middle of this otherwise gloomy forest and that had to be a bouncing little rabbit that just jumped away from your sight, or maybe it was something utterly different.
5987: Once again the sky disappears from the sight and only dark coloured branches of the trees can be seen, like a ceiling held up by these mighty trunks that seem to be feeding some life. Indeed, some trunks are being eaten alive by worms, termites and whatever there might be crawling inside them.
5988: In the east lies a green sloping land rising to a ridge of small hills. To the west a set of tall trees hide the view with their grey barks that cast dark shadows upon the land.
5989: In the Shadow of Huge Trees
Only a few bushes of undergrowth have found space among the huge trunks and their roots, which at some places look like snakes circling in the soil. The sky remains unseen beyond the canopy.
5990: The mother wolf stands here, protecting her young cubs.
All around the view is blocked by darkened trunks of trees. Branches grow only in the upper parts of the trees, forming a natural ceiling over this temple of trees.
5991: For some reason there is no sign that any trees at all have ever grown here. Instead the field covered with grass, obviously feeding the few deers that live in the area. Here and there the grass has been bent, showing where the animals have been resting just recently.
5992: The trees grow close to each other, letting little light enter the undergrowth. Only a few tiny green bushes have found room to grow among the huge trunks, and their future does not look that bright either.
5993: The already dense trunks suddenly seem to grow together, but in fact it is the western wall of an old stone building. There are no windows on this side, bar a small closed hole in the upper part of the wall. At the roof level the canopy partly blocks your vision, but there definitely is something even taller than the trees up there.
5994: The cook that once might have dwelt here, has been long gone and it shows. Foul smell fills the air as if corpses were rotting somewhere near, and the floor is covered with dirt. Here and there there are marks of something still living here, but it is definitely not human. Through a broken door in the east wall a livingroom can be seen, and a little staircase leaves up near the door.
5995:
The corpse of a young rat is lying here.
A large piece of plain cloth is on the ground.
An old-looking ring, covered with runes, lies here.
A plain leather belt is lying here.
The corpse of a brown-skinned orc is lying here.
The corpse of an orc-soldier is lying here.
An old-looking ring, covered with runes, lies here.
A large piece of plain cloth is on the ground.
A plain leather belt is lying here.
A half-rotten corpse is hanging here.
A large stone fireplace with a roaring fire warms the room.
A young and vicious olog-hai eagerly awaits intruders.
A small rat runs about, oblivious to your presence.

The room has not been cleared in ages, it seems. Obviously the current owner of the tower does not mind living in a mess like this. A wooden table stands near the northern wall, surrounded by several chairs. On the west wall there hang at least two rabbit corpses and a bigger furry corpse on the floor below them. Next to the corpses a doorway leads to a smelly kitchen. The door out is in the east wall between two little windows.
5996: The path coming from the fields in the south turns to the east and disappears into the forest. A small footpath continues in north west where it disappears from the sight behind an ancient tower. West from here there is a wall with two windows and a wooden door between them, leading probably into the tower. A small plaque can be seen just to the left of the door.
5997: A circling old trail comes from the north and after a rise on a hill in the south, it disappear from the sight. Far in the north, where terrain is flat, it seems to turn sharply to the east.
5998: A little used trail climbs up to these hills from the north and continues far to the south. Down on the west side of the hill the fields are covered with grass and small bushes.
5999: Nothing has been done to keep this trail clear in ages, and trees are about to take it over. In the north there is a break in the forest, filled with old stumps. In the west a high tower rises high above the treetops.
6000: The forest gets more and more dense in the east. South of the road, where the terrain slopes sharply, the forest is mixed, but in the north it is dominated by tall and dark spruces.
6001: The trail turns north into a very dense part of forest. It looks impossible to ride that way. In the west the road continues directly as far as the forest allows you to see.
6002: Trees have almost filled the trail here. Some of the branches are so sturdy and low that one has to constantly keep dodging them. Dark coloured birds circle all around, looking suspiciously at weird visitors. The forest disappears in the east, making travelling easier that way.
6003: Following the trail further east, it makes a turn northwards before entering yet another forest like that in the west. Small hills can be seen in the south, and far away you can see some higher ones behind the forest.
6004: Trying to avoid the haunting trees, the trail turns north following the edge of the forest, only to be forced to enter it there. In the west the trail crosses a wide plain before disappearing again. The plain continues to the south all the way to a ridge of hills that block your vision further.
6005: A wolf cub happily plays here.

An old trail coming through the plain from south makes a sharp turn to the dark forest east of here. Several large footprints are visible in the undergrowth, following the trail both ways. Some of them look not that old at all.
6006: The trail twists and turns its way through the dense pine forest. The boughs of the trees crowd over the path leaving only a small clear gap through to the sky. A thick carpet of pine needles makes the trail soft and springy underfoot which eases the burden on tired legs. The trail continues to the north and the west. To the east and south the forest rises up a sharp incline from the trail.
6007: A coloured game bird is visible in the vegetation, watching you warily.

From your position amid the pines of the wooded slope, you can gaze down upon a trail twisting its way through the woods to the west. The creatures whose feet and hooves have beaten the path below have shied from climbing the sharp slope from which you now survey the land. The ground drops away to the west and the north. To the south and the east the forest thickens.
6008: The trail passes an ominous forest to the north, the fair lands far to the west. The trail drags on towards the east, creeping around the forest as a snake would wrap around it's victim.
6009: The trail seems to cringe away from the forest to the west and north. A skull hangs from a branch nearby, leering at you as you pass its vigil. One can only guess as to who placed the warning.
6010: Klaees (thedon), wielding a great warsword, is standing here.

Thick and gloomy, the forest envelops you. Little light filters down from the closely twined branches above your head, and the densely packed trunks deaden and distort sound. Now and then a furtive rustle and cracking of branches can be heard from somewhere deep within the trees.
6011: Thick boughs of dense pine block out all light from above, plunging the forest into perpetual night. The ground is soft and yielding underfoot, being composed of decayed needles and twigs fallen from the trees over the years. Any noise from your passage seems to cause answering rustles and shiftings from the undergrowth, too irregular to be mere echoes.
6012: The trail skirts the forest to the south here, separating it from the diseased land to the south. As you watch your step you notice the previous rain has not yet erased the foot prints of some large two legged creature.
6013: Some ugly blow-flies are buzzing around here.
