A strange combination of scents fills the air along this trail. The strong scent of pine from the forest to the north combined with the musty, putrid smell of fungi to the west. Perhaps it is best to leave this area to the beasts.
6014: This small east-west trail runs past a dark and foreboding forest to the south, and a field of tall grasses to the north. Much farther to the north can be seen the border of another forest. One can only wonder what beasts roam these woods, at least, one can hope they can only wonder.
6015: Some ugly blow-flies are buzzing around here.

The trail has almost been lost to the weeds growing north of you, and the underbrush at the border of the forest that lies to the south. Luckily a few large beasts must occasionally walk this path, as the earth has remained too packed for even the toughest weeds.
6016: North of you a large field of weeds and grasses can be seen, looking like a tempting spot to rest and take a break. East the trail can be seen cutting its way inbetween the two forests that have merged. It remains unknown what sinister eyes may be watching from the forests, readying themselves for the unwary traveller.
6017: This small trail winds it's way through the forest here, following the southern forest line to the west. The trees crouching in on the trail provide a few nice shady spots to shelter from the hot summer sun, but they are sure to also hide a few beasts of the forest.
6018: A disgusting forest troll is searching for fresh meat here.

The forest has thinned here, allowing tall grasses to invade the forest. An occasional shrub can be found, ready and willing to block your way, or provide a few vines full of sharp thorns to scratch at your flesh.
6019: The thinning forest here has led to a greater amount of underbrush. To the north the growth is so thick it seems to squeeze the life from the trees, while to the south the forest has fallen to disease.
6020: A brutish forest troll is hunting here, looking for some tasty flesh.

The forest opens to the south, to the scene of a broken shack. In all other directions the forest thickens, much to thick to be passable to north, but still thin enough to travel east or west. One noticable aspect of this area is all the uprooted trees, and those trees lacking branches.
6021:
A rotten corpse is hanging here.
A half-rotten corpse is hanging here.

They say that if you don't ask, the trees won't tell you. Here, it might be preferable if you do not ask, for the small animals stuck through like rotting shish kebabs on the tree limbs give off an odor bad enough to make you sick to your stomach already.
6022:
A disgusting forest troll is searching for fresh meat here.
Some ugly blow-flies are buzzing around here.

Within the heart of the forest things just seem gloomier. No normal forest sounds can be heard, perhaps it is just your passing, but the small animals that live here must have become accustomed to danger. Only the silent will survive.
6023: The earth here has been mauled on an almost continous basis. Or, perhaps it might be more accurate to say, nightly. It seems as if something has been eating the roots of the trees. Certainly something with a voracious appetite.
6024: The trees here seem old, and tired. Their large trunks support a wide and dense canopy, but the burden seems to have taken its toll. For under their branches roam those beings who prefer the dark, and survive only by the grace of night.
6025: You have entered the edge of a thick forest, which blankets the north with dark shadows and green and brown highlights. When it is overhead the yellow eye turns the canopy above a brighter green but its rays do not reach the forest floor, making the area the hunting ground of creatures of the dark.
6026: There is some snow on the ground.

Shattered trees mark the edge of the forest here. Apparently something has a habit of hiding here and charging out to the trail to surprise the unwary traveller. The clicking sounds of beetles can be heard from some of the broken trees, no doubt eating the tree from within.
6027: The remains of a mass of vines lie here in a heap of rotting compost.

Trees here give way to the south and east, forming the border to the forest of sorrow. East of the forest can be seen the remains of an old shack, and to the south a small trail leading it's way across the morbid landscape.
6028: The midst of the forest bespeaks ages of sorrow. Bent limbs seem to reach out to you, begging for your ability to move to more hospitable territory. Even the roots seem to reach out from the earth, eager to get away from whatever lurks below.
6029: A brutish forest troll is hunting here, looking for some tasty flesh.

The trees here hang their limbs low, seeming to hold the weight of Arda upon their broken and bent wood. You ask yourself what could be worse, to be a tree, forced to endure the sights and sounds within this grisly forest, or to be one of the victims.
6030: A brutish forest troll is hunting here, looking for some tasty flesh.

The underbrush has grown thick here, effectively blocking passage through the forest to the south and west. Many brambles and vines seem to have made a nice home for themselves here, tearing at your flesh as if they survived on your blood and not the sunshine they get so little of.
6031: Sorrow speaks loudly its name within these woods. No stars and no sun can be seen through the thick canopy, only the cool air as it rustles the branches above. No doubt because of the thick canopy overhead, the forest floor has very little brush, and can be navigated easily, with the exception a large stand of trees to the south that are thick enough to block travel southwards.
6032: The stand of trees has grown too thick to be passable to the south, but elsewhere the thick overhead canopy has prevented the extensive growth of underbrush that clogs the passage south.
6033:
The corpse of a brutish forest troll is lying here.
Some ugly blow-flies are buzzing around here.

Several large holes can be seen in the canopy overhead, letting through light from the sky above. During the daytime the nastiest beasts that inhabit the forest will surely be kept at bay, but at night this world belongs to different owners.
6034:
A bright red mushroom is growing here.
There are two mushrooms here.
A brown fox is here, looking for some rabbits to chew up.
A brutish forest troll is hunting here, looking for some tasty flesh.

Like many pillars reaching up to support a vast ceiling of green, the forest gives you the feel of a vast indoor arena. An arena that only the worms and fungi clean, and the fun begins at night. Prepare to be the next gladiator.
6035: A brutish forest troll is hunting here, looking for some tasty flesh.

Overhead the forest is thick, down below it is barren. The smell is unique however, a combination of evergreen, musty wet air, and odor of a rotting corpse. Probably the deer corpse up ahead, with the fungi sprouting around it.
6037: The forest darkens the horizon in all directions except north, where you can see a barren area filled with boulders. You can hear the wind whistling a tune of sorrow around the trees, begging for the future to bring happier times.
6038:
A disgusting forest troll is searching for fresh meat here.
A brutish forest troll is hunting here, looking for some tasty flesh.

A thick canopy blocks the sun from reaching the forest floor in this area. Mushrooms can be seen clinging to the trees, and a foul stench arrises from their rotting pussing caps. Probably wise to avoid mushrooms that thrive in decay.
6039: A brutish forest troll is hunting here, looking for some tasty flesh.

Horrid smells overtake you, and you notice the rotting remains of something at the base of a tree. Whatever it was, something took great joy in smashing it's skull against the trunk of a tree. Perhaps it is best to leave the trees to their fate and escape with your own life intact.
6040: A brown fox is here, looking for some rabbits to chew up.

Thick trees, bent trees, all of which seem to reach to the sky for some saviour. Although their foliage is thick enough to keep the yellow eye at bay, this hasn't helped their roots and trunks, as evidenced by many scratches and gashes in their bark.
6041: A brutish forest troll is hunting here, looking for some tasty flesh.

The forest can be seen thinning to the north, finally giving way to a field farther north. Eastwards a rocky slope stops the forest from spreading its depression any farther east. A few of the trees at the edge seem ready to fall down the rocks, their roots straining to hold them up.
6042: The edge of the forest, with its forlorn and bent trees has reached its end here. As the trees thin, the underbrush grows thick, and its thorny appendages constantly snag you, as if trying to drag you back. An occasional fungus can be seen pushing its bulbous top through the earth.
6043: All around this small clearing the trees and brush seem to reach towards you, anxious to cover more land. The land seems to have been trampled often by large beasts. What few plants remain have been crushed numerous times.
6044: Some ugly blow-flies are buzzing around here.

The forest has provided for its own here. There are many nice places to hide behind the bushes while keeping an eye on the clearing to the south. From the flattened bushes you can see that someone has been using this area recently.
6045: A disgusting forest troll is searching for fresh meat here.

The smell of putrid rot hangs in the air, as if someplace, hidden beneath the roots of a tree, may lie the corpse of an unlucky traveller. The woods have never been hospitable to humans or hobbits, and it has only grown worse with the passing of each day.
6046: A brown fox is here, looking for some rabbits to chew up.
The fertile soil of the forest gives way to the rocky ground of a gully to the west. Its steep sides look passable here, but certainly not as easy as the woods in all other directions.
6047: As if a bone was ripped from the earth here, this gully bares the rocks that make up the foundation of the land. Starting west of here a short ways, the gully bends to the north where it's sides are steeper and the rocks seem to have sharper points.
6048: This rocky terrain seems to funnel to the east, making moving in other directions possible albeit dangerous. Here and there can be seen an occasional bone, leftovers from someone's dinner. Someone very big.
6049: Grasses grow tall in this strange clearing. The trees seem to have avoided this area, their branches actually turned away, leaving naked trunks exposed to whatever menace might lurk unseen here.
6050: The remains of a twisted tree lie here in a heap of rotting compost.
The woods here have been twisted horribly, as if the evil of the east had shaped them to his desires, then froze them in that state to prevent any feeling but agony to enter their souls.
6051: The ravine heads north and south here, with forest high up to the east and west. The walls to the east and west, too steep to climb, seem perfect for the few vultures that sit in the trees high overhead, watching for a spare morsel. The crack in the earth deepens to the north.
6052: The remains of a twisted tree lie here in a heap of rotting compost.

Nefarious grins seem to be traced in the bark of the trees here, their branches reaching out as if to drag you into some hidden maw. Even their roots can be seen to wiggle, as if blowing gently in the wind.
6053: A twisted tree is here moving slowly with the wind.

These ghastly woods seem ready to charge you, each with a sinister face painted in the lines of it's bark, always looking, always watching you. Some short trees, almost midgets compared to their cousins can be seen to have roots lying mostly on top of the soil.
6054: A twisted tree is here moving slowly with the wind.
The trees here seem to move and bend, forcing you along a path of their choosing. Their trunks twisted, their leaves sprouting from bark, it would seem Morgoth himself had paid a visit to this place.
6055: A mass of wriggling vines drops on you from the trees.
The trees here bend as if they were dancing, frozen in impossible positions. Some stand with trunks arched as if doing somersaults, others bend as if they were a vine and not a tree.
6056: Some roots lie here waiting to ensnare weary travellers.

Branches delve into the ground here, only to spring forth with leaves a few feet away. Madness seems to have reached its peak here, with what seems to be roots climbing the trunks of other trees as if they were vines.
6057: While this may not be the most hospitable place around, the rocky walls of this chasm seem to offer some protection from the evil forces that warp the forest above. Of course, that may all be just an illusion.
6058: The ravine curves again here, leading to the north and west. The walls to the east and south may be climbable, and you can see the forest towering overhead. One can almost hear a faint thumping noise coming from below.
6059: The crevice bends again here, heading to the east and south. The walls here are not so steep as those to the south, and may be climbable, although the woods overlooking the crevice urge you to reconsider that direction.
6060: A forest spider is here crawling around.

The forest is sparse here, a few trees looking over a ravine to the west, and thick underbrush preventing movement anywhere but back south. This area seems a bit less weary than the rest of the forest, perhaps because some light actually warms the earth in places here.
6061: The weary forest looks out over a bend in a ravine situated to the west. North and south the forest continues to be traversable, but the easterly direction has been blocked by trees that seem to have been planted close together on purpose.
6062: No light reaches the forest floor here, the canopy above providing enough nourishment for the large trees to sustain them against the withering trials given to the by the evil beasts that roam the forest. It is said that trolls turn to stone at the touch of a ray of sun, and perhaps it is the trolls knowledge of this that keeps these trees unharmed in this dangerous area.
6063: The forest stops abruptly to the north, where a steep slope leads into a wide chasm. Going north may be unwise for those who wish to stay in the shelter of the forest. Not that these woods bring peace of mind, but at least any eyes that may be watching you must be skillful in keeping quiet as well.
6064: A half-rotten corpse is hanging here.

Westwards the underbrush has covered the forest floor making It impassable, and north the earthen ground gives way to large rocks and a steep slope. An entire body has been nailed to the trunk of a tree near the rocky slope - it appears to have been an unlucky dwarf and its feet dangle only inches from the ground.
6065:
A disgusting forest troll is searching for fresh meat here.
A brutish forest troll is hunting here, looking for some tasty flesh.

The forest here is a tangled mess of thorns and brush, you can probably move east or west, but traversing the forest in the northern or southernly directions would be impossible. On the brighter side, a few small animals can be seen in the area, making the forest a tad less sorrowful.
6066: The canopy overhead has begun to thin, letting through enough light to distinguish night from day, but not yet enough to permit a vigorous stand of underbrush. Northwards however, a large amount of brush has blocked travel, and southwards a robust group of vines does the same.
6067: Small amounts of underbrush can be seen to the north, suggesting more light than is usual for this portion of the forest. In all other directions the canopy overhead has kept the ground clear of vegetation, albeit a bit dark also.
6068: The forest here overlooks a small trail to the south, and fends off a field to the west. Underbrush is a common obstacle, but easily routed around. The canopy overhead is almost complete, providing just a little light to the plants that live closer to the earth.
6069:
A brutish forest troll is hunting here, looking for some tasty flesh.
A brutish forest troll is hunting here, looking for some tasty flesh.

As you travel under the grace of the trees you are reminded of your small stature in comparison with the rest of the world. Be you a legend among men you are still but an ant among the more fearsome creatures of the forest.
6070: A brutish forest troll is hunting here, looking for some tasty flesh.

Several small stands of mushrooms can be found along the forest floor in this area. Sprouting out from the matt of needles that form the forest floor they provide the housekeeping for the forest, decomposing the more protein rich substances that find their way here.
6071: This forest must be centuries old, its large trees raising towards the sky, each in its own space, meshing perfectly above with its neighbours. Gone however, are the protectors of the forest, as is evident by the various forms of desecration practiced against their woody skin.
6072: A disgusting forest troll is searching for fresh meat here.

A sense of evil pervades the forest here, as if something powerful and sinister was watching your every move. A few ravens can be heard screeching overhead, but the sky has been covered with a leafy replacement that readily conceals the birds.
6073: The buzz of insects can be heard, coming from a large bush near the southern edge of the forest. Closer inspection reveals a dead raccoon, beset upon by a horde of flies and be The insects have finished off too much of it to make any judgement on how it died.
6074: Large amounts of underbrush fill the space in-between the trees here, where the grass nearby fights for ground against the tall trees of the forest. It is questionable who will win this war, for both sides - the grass and the trees - look tired and unhealthy.
6075:
A large thorny branched shrub is growing here.
On the shrub, there are ten piles of blackberries.

A huge blackberry bush sits on the western edge of the forest here, separating the forest from a clearing to the west. It is certainly possible to manuever around the bush, and a few small animals can be seen using it as shelter.
6076: A disgusting forest troll is searching for fresh meat here.

Like so many pillars holding up the sky, the trees of this forest have created a vast hall. With the canopy overhead providing shelter from the light and heat of day, and some shelter from the rains and winds, the only thing missing is dinner. Of course, that may be your purpose here.
6077: A solid stand of trees blocks the way west. Hidden among them, and surely unreachable by you, one can just barely glimpse the large nests of some giant birds hidden at the base of the canopy. You cannot determine what kind of bird it is that dwells in the darkness under the canopy, but it surely must have good night-vision to feed its young.
6078: Thick vegetation and spiny creepers choke off any thoughts of passage to the west or north here. The trees continue to grow thick and support their tremendous canopy, but you can see faint hints of light northwards, where the forest may be thinning.
6079: The barren forest floor has been rudely interupted by large amounts of brush and creepers to the north and east, making those directions impassable. A few small animals can be seen scurrying around the vegetation, but none can be seen foraging any farther into the forest.
6080: Several large trees grow close together to the east, forming a natural barrier for travellers. Numerous choke creepers can be seen winding their way around the trees in this area, their thick thorns guarding the trunks of the trees.
6081:
A rotten corpse is hanging here.
A half-rotten corpse is hanging here.
A rotten corpse is hanging here.
A half-rotten corpse is hanging here.
A half-decayed corpse of a goblin lies rotting on the ground.

Something has made this part of the forest its very own trophy room. The heads of just about anything, from stags to elves and orcs, can be seen impaled on the branches here. It is odd that the heads have all been placed only 4 to 5 feet off the ground.
6082: Grasses and small bushes have taken this clearing for their own, fending off the forest that has encroached on them from all directions but south. The darkness hiding behind the trees can almost be felt, trying to press towards this clearing, only to be stopped by the open sky above.
6083: The opening in the forest here reminds you of a valley, with the grasses and bushes looking so small against the backdrop of large trees that guard their flanks. If fenced off this area would surely make a good corral or pasture.
6084: The tall grasses that populate this field seemed to have overgrown themselves without any farm animals to feed on them. The weeds have been the winners in this competition, leaving the weaker plants to shrivel and die.
6085: This grassy field separates the forest to the north from a small trail to the south. The grass itself is more a mixture of various weeds, all quite happy and healthy. A couple cows, or a herd of sheep would survive well here.
6086: This large field of grass, broken by the occasional lone tree, extends north and east until it meets the border of a large forest, and south until stopped by a trail that is situated between it and the southern forest.
6087: A stocky mountain mule is here, waiting to serve.

This rocky slope descends to the east, winding away from the forest to the south. It would almost seem that someone has purposefully placed the rocks here in unsteady positions, for even the largest rocks tip and move as you walk on them.
6088: The forest seems to have been split and pushed open here, with a massive collection of trees smashed to the sides, forming a natural barricade between the clearing and the rest of the forest. A few saplings have begun to return the area to the clutches of the forest, thus providing evidence that whatever trauma did this has not been back.
6089: Some ugly blow-flies are buzzing around here.

The forest here has been decimated. Many hundreds of logs have been uprooted and pushed aside, and the ground bears large ditches, as if two gigantic beasts had once fought here. Whatever it might have been seems to be gone now, as one can see the small plants and saplings that have begun to grow again.
6090: You have arrived at the base of a low cliff. Its walls much too steep for climbing, it appears to be used as a camp quite frequently. A small campfire can be seen, but it is currently extinguished.
6092:
A patch of short black fur lies on the ground.
A patch of short black fur lies on the ground.
A black wolf fur is here, lying on the ground.
A patch of short black fur lies on the ground.
A brown bear fur is here lying on the ground.
A brown fur is here lying on the ground.
A black wolf fur is here, lying on the ground.
A cloak mottled in green and brown, and stinking to high heaven lies here.
A hungry warg stands here, sniffing around for flesh.
A huge warg is here, moving in for the kill.

You have entered a small den, inhabited by two large wargs. The ceilings are low and the space cramped. In the centre of the room a large pile of furs is being used as bedding, undoubtably from the warg's previous meals. The exit is easy to notice from this side, a narrow opening just big enough to let the sun filter inside during the end of the day. The entrance does take some effort to squeeze through.
6093: The gloom of the forest has been stymied by a small trail that can be seen running to the north and west, providing a break from the trees, and thus the darkness that they hide below their branches. Further to the south, however, the gloom is abundant, threatening to fill your heart.
6094: Some sunlight can be seen creeping through the forest canopy, but even this close to the border of the forest the light is filtered through many leaves, producing a dusk-like environment even at the height of day.
6095: Any sensible person would desire to go north at this point, where a small trail might take them away from these woods and their black heart. Perhaps you are not sensible, perhaps even foolhardy, in which case a southernly route can assure you many more encounters with ferocious beasts.
6096: The trees grow close here, as if to ward off those who might wish to wander under their limbs. Their leaves are almost successful in warding off all the light, and appear to become even more competent to the south, where darkness is all that the eye can see.
6097: Finding yourself deep within the woods, it has become easy to lose your way, with the thick forest obscuring any landmarks that you might have used as a reference. Finding your way out may be a matter of luck.
6098: The thick forest here has replaced the sky with it's branches and leaves, removing all light from above. Dark shapes and shadows flirt with the large trees as you move around, keeping your eyes moving to and fro, but revealing little of what lies ahead.
6099: The forest is very efficient here, turning daytime into night beneath it's leaves. It is also rather quiet, all the small animals having departed from the vicinity long ago. The scent of evergreen is strong.
6100: Large knotted trees reach their branches upward here, supporting a massive canopy that filters the light from the air before it reaches the forest floor. While there is a lot of activity overhead, the bottom of the forest is barren.
6101: What once must have been a strong set of trees has begun to droop their branches, and an air of hopeless can be felt. West of here you can see a large number of dead and dying trees, being eaten by some pestilence that threatens to invade this forest.
6102: Deep and thick the forest blankets the land. All around you the firs stand straight and tall, their high branches casting a shadow over all beneath them. The dense forest has its own distinctive odour of bark and sap. Indeed a hunter would be better to rely on a good sense of smell in this dim underworld.
6103: Deep and dark, the forest holds you in its grasp. Tangled boughs clutch at your body and long finger-like twigs scratch and cling to exposed flesh. Strange murmerings and creakings emanate from the dense undergrowth, lending the forest a hostile and foreboding atmosphere.
6104:
A shallow pond is here, tinted green with algae.
A large rabbit looks peacefully at you, ready to dart away.

The damp, lichen covered boughs and trunks stand decades old, their leafy crowns covered in dark green foliage. Insects scurry away from areas of disturbed bark, scuttling back under cover as quickly as possible. The clammy, damp air catches in your throat and the odour of dank wood fills the air.
6105:
A forest spider is here crawling around.
A forest spider is here crawling around.
A forest spider is here crawling around.

A twisting and turning path is the best one can hope for in this dim and gloomy woods. Any sense of direction is quickly lost amid the trees and everywhere you look an indistinguishable trunk or branch or bough gazes back. The best you can hope for is to chose a path and stick to it as best you can.
6106:
A disgusting forest troll is searching for fresh meat here.
A disgusting forest troll is searching for fresh meat here.

Thicker than the surrounding forest, a stand of firs grows dense and close nearby. The trunks seem to form an almost impenetrable wall of wood and travel through the forest is only possible following a tortuous route around the trees. The cries of woodland birds can be heard from the foliage high overhead.
6107: A deep blanket of silence lies over the woodland. No cries of bird or mammal break the unnatural quiet. The silence emphasises the hostile aspect of the crooked trees, standing sentinel over the vale. No respite from the forest is obvious, the trees growing outward all around.
6108: The dark fir trees surround you, growing high above and cutting even the strong light of noon to a mere glimmer at the forest floor. Pine needles and cones shed from the boughs litter the ground, decaying to form a moist layer of nutrients for the trees from whence they came. The forest seems to thin toward the west.
6109:
A large toadstool grows nearby.
A large toadstool grows nearby.
A large toadstool grows nearby.

What used to be a part of the forest is now part of the grave. The majority of the trees that once stood here have withered and died, the remaining trees seem ready to share that fate. In the boughs of one of the trees can be seen a massive horde of webs, crawling with worms. No doubt the source of this pestilence.
6110: From the outside this broken down shack seemed rather mundane. Boards could be seen lying around, and the walls had been shortened a notch or two, scarcely tall enough to provide shelter for a hobbit. Upon closer inspection you can see the shack has a new purpose. In the centre stands a firepit, complete with spit for roasting. A humanoid skeleton remains tied to the spit.
6111: The trail bends to the north and west here, skirting a forest that sits to the south and east. Although you havn't heard of this trail being frequented by any of the fair races of arda, it has certainly been trampled down well by some large humanoids on a fairly frequent basis.
6112: If this trail gave you the creeps when it passed the forest, you should feel like running this stretch. All around the land has been overcome with disease, with many dead trees to the north, and to the south nothing but fungi eagerly devouring what has been left by the ravages of disease.
6113: The trail here splits, a short path leading north to the site of a broken down shack. Looking to the south you can see what may have been farmland at some point, now looking more like a fungi garden. Certainly the fate of the builders of the shack follow that of their old fields.
6114:
There are two toadstools here.
There are two mushrooms here.
A huge black fungus is here, exuding a foul stench.
An ancient fungus smothers the boulders.

This stark land bears nothing useful to the world. Tall fungi grow almost as tall as the withered trees, often feeding on the stumps of those trees fallen long ago. More than anything else however, it is the smell that drives you to leave this area, for fungi do not have the most pleasant smell.
6115:
An ancient fungus smothers the boulders.
A giant, strange looking green fungus is here, ready to devour you in seconds.
A huge black fungus is here, exuding a foul stench.

Withered trees, shrunken from disease and the torture of wind dot the landscape here. The fungi however seem to relish this place, growing in abundance. Their sweet and sickly smells are quite overpowering, and probably the reason no animal life can be seen either.
6116: An ancient fungus smothers the boulders.

All of the higher plant and animal forms seem to have left this place for more hospitable areas. A few dead and withered trees can be seen, along with the multitudes of mushrooms that litter the ground. Obviously some sort of disease has overtaken the plant-life here.
6117:
A statue of a troll is posed in a moment of flight yet forever frozen in stone.
A coloured game bird is visible in the vegetation, watching you warily.

The trail curves to the north here, avoiding the dead land to the east. Even an old bespectacled hobbit can see that some large humanoid has frequented this trail, the large footprints buried in the mud. It may be wise to pass this section of trail before night descends.
6118: You are amidst a curious gap in the forest. The soil seems thick but the air here has a strange tang to it and no plants or animal tracks can be seen. The forest crowds round the clearing on the north, south and west sides. The clearing continues to the east.
6120: Slender trees grow amidst brush and bramble in all directions. The thin forest is airy and light and chirpings and chitterings of small woodland animals sound from the undergrowth. To the south and west the trees peter out and to the east the forest becomes dark and foreboding.
6121: The ground rises steadily from the low forest in the north to a high ridge of hillside in the south. To the east and west forest climbs up the foothills toward your present location but peter out leaving this open back of high ground exposed to the elements. The ground underfoot is rocky and hard with a few divots of coarse grass growing amidst the boulders where they can.
6122: Shattered and splintered boughs and trunks lie bent and twisted all around. Mosses and lichens grow over the broken surfaces showing that whatever caused this gross damage did so in times long past. The forest recovers to the south as it climbs up the lower reaches of a large hill. A bare ridge of higher ground extends from the hillside to the east.
6123: Dim and dank, the dark trees stand silently watching you. In all directions, the forest continues. The uncanny quiet lends the place an uneasy air, any small sound being followed by a deep foreboding silence. Overhead the boughs of the trees reach down for you, their twigs and branches like long gnarled fingers.
6124: Sturdy firs rise thirty feet and more, their lofty upper branches waving in the breeze high above you. The soft earth underfoot is laced with roots and vines, growing down into the subsoil to suckle at the nutrients contained within. The sweet smell of pine sap hangs in the air.
6125: A few trees stand solitary amid a sea of brush. The dense shrubs, ferns and brambles grow to a height of several feet and form a uneven green surface over which you know gaze. Several of the bushes sport long thorns which are coated with an itchy, irritating moisture - a fact which becomes only too apparent as the thorns catch skin and pierce flesh.
6126: Dense and bushy, the forest springs forth from the soft ground of the trollshaws. The trees are surrounded by brush and undergrowth rising several feet high. Occasional thorns and brambles pull and tug at exposed skin and tear at clothing. Many small insects hover and skim over and through the undergrowth.
6127: Lit from above the high, thick branches of mixed cedar and oak cast angular shadows on the lower forest. Shapes become difficult to distinguish in the broken light providing perfect camouflage for any predatory creature abroad in the woods. The land begins to rise slightly to what you guess to be the south-west.
6128: A partridge attempts to hide in the undergrowth.

The ground here lies above the level of the surrounding forest to the north and east. To the west the land rises steeply up the flank of a ridge which protrudes from the large hill to the south-west. The firs and pines of the forest do not appear to grow well on the hard rock-strewn ground rising to only fifteen feet in many cases.
6129: This narrow ridge of high ground protrudes outward from the hill to the south and runs deep into the lowland forest to the north. The forests climb the sides of the spur to the east and the west but do not reach to the crest, leaving a narrow strip of bare land, covered only with hillside grass and heather.
6130: The tree cover on this north facing slope of hillside is sparse. Stunted pines grow across the face, struggling to find purchase on the thin and rocky soil. The slope continues upward to the south, climbing toward a summit. To the north, you can descend into the lower forest. To the east, a spur of hillside runs outward from the massive flank of the range.
6131: The ground rises slightly to the south, the trees leaning into the slope like massive balusters. The soil of the slope is friable and loose, making progress uphill tiring. To the north, east and west the forest continues. To the south the trees begin to thin out.
6132: The slope increases to the south as it climbs up the beginnings of a large hill. The trees grow tall in the fertile ground reaching upward to catch light on this north facing slope. Telltale droppings scattered on the ground beside small burrows show that woodland animals also make their home here.
6133:
A fat rabbit sits here, chewing on some grass.
A fat rabbit sits here, chewing on some grass.
A squirrel scampers around here, looking for nuts from the trees.

Tall pine trees cover this steep slope. The hillside to the south rises a foot in height for every two feet travelled making progress in that direction a tiring climb. High above your head, the pine branches from a canopy of needles through which dim light filters from above. The close spaced trunks deaden sound and the forest seems almost unnaturally still and silent.
6134: The slope rises steeply to the south gaining a foot in height for every two travelled. The forest clings tenaciously to the thin soil of the hillside, the trunks angling up toward the sky. The sweet smell of pine sap hangs in the air. To the east and west the forest continues across the slope. The hill rises to the south and drops away to the north.
6135: The field slopes gently to the south toward a ridge of undulating hills and disappears further behind a couple of higher tops. The ground is mostly filled with grass and short bushes.
6136: Trees here are not as tall as they are in the north, instead the older trees here seem to be birch. Obviously spruces are slowly overtaking the area though. A small trail circles at the plains northeast from here.
6137: The conifers of the woodland grow tall and straight across the face of the hillside. Over the years many pine needles have fallen to form a soft, thick blanket on the ground. The forest continues in all directions, though to the south, the trees begin to thin out as the slope increases.
6138: There are some acorns lying here.

The ground rises steeply to the south, climbing up the flanks of the range of hills cutting across the land. Tall and straight conifers grow all around, rising proudly from the springy bed of fallen pine needles which lies thick around their bases. Any disturbance of the pine needles releases the thick aroma of moist earth and wood sap into the air.
6139: A robin is here, carrying small pieces of wood to its nest.

Trees around you are so huge and tall that they seem to be disappearing in the clouds above you. Through the trunks you see a more open area in the north, but everywhere else the forest continues. Luckily the forest is not very dense, so moving here is not a problem.
6140: Here the tall trees that tower high above ground in the south have not blocked sun from warming the ground, letting some grass grow in the soil. Following the border of the forest to the east, there seems to be a path going towards a huge pine.
6141: The the path coming from the forest behind a tall pine in the east disappears here. If it ever continued west, it is now overgrown with grass. In the south there is a forest of tall trees.
6142: A ferocious warg is here, snarling angrily.

The trees have grown very straight here, and they have just a few branches in their lower part making climbing to them rather hard. A couple of squirrels run up and down the trees chasing each other. The soil is sandy here, only in some places grass grows on it.
6143: An about ten yards wide opening runs from north-west to south-east here between the two forests. While the forest far in the east is strictly spruce, the other forest right on the west side of the path is mainly pine. In the south there is a ruin of an old fortification, upon which a high tower rises.
6144: The path circles through the forest and right next to the wall of a tower south of here. It then seems to make a turn behind the corner in east and disappears from the sight. There is a thick spruce forest north of here.
6145: Southern Edge of a Spruce Forest

The forest is much lighter here than in north where you cannot see anything more than a few yards away. Small animals have also found this light forest better place to live in. South of here there is a wide opening in the forest and a crossroad of three paths.
6146: A statue of a troll is posed in a moment of flight yet forever frozen in stone.
All around you there are rotten stumps, now housing colonies of termites and small worms. The clearing continues further in the north and in the south it leads to a trail.
6147: The trees are young and short here, indicating that the area has not always been so densely forested. Indeed, the soil here is so good it might have been used as a field sometime in the past. But in the coming years it will become as dark as the older forest north of here.
6148:
A fallow deer is grazing peacefully here.
A grey wolf is here, salivating profusely.
A wide plain opens up here, bordered by a dark forest in the west and far in the east. A little trail runs over the plain in the southeast, only to yet again disappear in the frightening forest.
6149: Ant Hill in the Dreary Forest
A colony of red ants is here. The ants seem to ignore you.
The most visible landmark here is a gigantic ant hill, its top reaching high above. It must have taken centuries for the colony of ants to build this hill, even with the great number of them.
6150: The forest borders a small clearing west of you, surrounding it like tall city walls. Only some grass grows on the ground, most of the soil being covered by fallen spruce needles. A tiny path circles at your feet to the east, filled with busy ants.
6151: You are in a little clearing, surrounded by tall, dark green spruces in east and west. Some of the trees that have grown here in the past have been cut down, and the rather dry soil of this location has not allowed new trees to grow up.
6152: Sharp needles make moving in the forest difficult. The twigs almost seem to be reaching down for prey from the darkness above. The forest continues dark as ever in the west, where as in other directions it is not so thick.
6153: Deep in a Dark Spruce Forest

The trees allow no light to enter the undergrowth, causing an uninviting and eerie darkness. There grows nothing green in the soil, and only animals living here show nothing of themselves but an eye or two in the darkness around you.
6154: A pack horse (ulo) is standing here.

The ancient pine stands here like a king, surrounded by smaller trees. The path makes a sharp turn around the trunk of the tree and continues south and west. Up in the tree there is a bird nest between two branches.
6155:
Klaees (thedon), wielding a great warsword, is standing here.
Lhurank (brenny), wielding a darkened orkish axe, is standing here.

Probably the remains of an old building, huge stones have broken the forest into little clearings. No clear outline of the building can be seen, but it seems to have been rather big, since some of the stones are several feet in diameter.
6156: The trees are rather short here compared to rest of the forest. Up above the treetops a ruined tower rises to guard the woods around it. There is a slight decline in the terrain to the east, leading to a ruined field.
6157: Old moss covered stones around the field suggest that it was once protected from wild animals by a fence. Now, there seems to be nothing to protect. Thick undergrowth and little bushes have filled the field.
6158: A few trees have been just recently torn from their roots by god knows what. Beside the trunks there are tracks allright, but it is very hard to tell if this has been done by many large beings or one really big.
6159: Though fertile, the soil is too rocky for more than grass and small bushes to grow. In the south, where the terrain meets the root of a hill range, the rocks disappear and are replaced by thick bushes that seem to thrive in the slope. Through a strangely direct row of trees, a small trail can be seen in the east.
6160: These undulating hills are covered with thick bushes everywhere, and the slopes come as a surprise because they cannot be seen before getting to them. It is also just as hard to see what lurks in the undergrowth.
6161: A mass of dark green leaves clings to a wall.

Rimmed with ivy-covered walls of large stakes implanted in the ground, this enclosure is further shrouded by thick accumulations of bushes and brambles that render this area difficult to discern from the roadway. Large wooden stakes have been implanted in the ground to allow individuals to tether their mounts.
6162: These fields are devoted to the production of fodder for the many beasts of burden that frequent the caravan station. Bountiful rows of grains and fields of hay appear to be well tended. In one corner are a few rows of melilot and a small herb garden. The wooden fence, carpeted with ivy, surrounds and camouflages the area.
6163:
A roe deer is standing here, watching the terrain while chewing the vegetation.
A roe deer is standing here, watching the terrain while chewing the vegetation.

This meadow is pleasant and well-favoured, possessed of lush grasses and colourful blooms, complimented by a few scatterings of birch, aspen, and spruce. The road meanders along its long journey to your north; beyond it the land rises into jagged uplands. To the east the woods thicken somewhat.
6164: A hungry warg stands here, sniffing around for flesh.

This large room seems forsaken, but is less ruined than the exterior of the building would indicate. Debris is piled in the corners and cobwebs line the corners, but the walls are built of sturdy oak panels that seem to postdate the rest of the edifice. Perhaps some intrepid soul decided to refurbish the structure, but reconsidered staying in this lonesome wilderness.
6165: This hallway seems abandoned and disused, but the walls and rafters still seem sound. The floor is wooden and covered with a thin layer of dust while the walls are lined with cobwebs.
6166: A smaller room adjoining the main chamber has a confined, albeit cozy feel to it. Fine weavings emblazoned with bright colours line the walls, and some fine clothing hangs from wooden racks. Bundles and boxes of basic supplies are piled haphazardly in one corner. An open archway leads back into the common room, and there is a small wooden door to the south.
6167:
A huge clock is standing here.
A large stone fireplace with a roaring fire warms the room.
A tall woman in riding leathers is here.
A dwarf is here, bearing a grim and competent demeanour.
A wizened dwarf is busy at work.
A sturdy old dwarf wonders if you want something.
A young dwarf is here, attempting to look tough.
A hungry warg stands here, sniffing around for flesh.

You find yourself in a tavern of the most comfortable and inviting sort, brimming with the odours of tasty food and frosty ale. Someone has arrayed long trestle tables with accompanying high-backed chairs of darkened and well oiled hardwood. Above all sparkles a crystalline chandelier of coloured glass imbuing the surroundings with a soft relaxing ambience; evidently it is the product of some advanced dwarven handicraft. Lining the walls are oaken panels limned with the visages of patrons former and recent -- they are remarkably lifelike, infused with personality by some remarkably talented artisan.
6168: The room has a spartan quality, but yet retains all the integral trappings to make it a comfortable and cozy room of respite. A short bed with an oaken bedstand occupies one corner, with a matching nightstand close at hand. Woven rugs cover the floor, dyed bright and cheery colours. Hung on the wall are mementoes and a couple of oil paintings.
6169: This room is small in size, but what space there is has been crammed with supplies and sundries. Barrels, sacks, crates, bundles, casks, tools, spare weapons, and a plethora of other individual items have been stacked and arranged neatly to maximize the capacity of the area.
6170:
A low shrub with bright green, oblong leaves is growing here.
A roe deer is standing here, watching the terrain while chewing the vegetation.

New growth proliferates here, in a process of renewal not yet manifest in the scarred lands to your north. Young trees roughly uniform in size and age spread bright green needles towards the sky, and the ground is carpeted with fresh grasses and prolific wildflowers. A fresh crisp fragance whispers effervescently on the breeze, and small mammals and birds are seen occasionly gathering sustenance or merely enjoying the wonders of their fleeting existence.
6171: Perhaps this area was once lush and prolific, but at some point a dire force has shriveled and browned the entire landscape. Some twisted tree-boles and patches of dry brush and bramble dot the area, but otherwise it is completely barren. Rough hills rise behind the road to the north, whereas to the south the forest is green and growing, in sharp contrast to your current environ.
6172: The slow process of regrowth has begun in earnest here; a verdant carpet of wild grasses and flowers ripples underneath the fresh arboreal scions sending their new limbs questing towards the sun. The trampling of small trails in the grasses dotted with fresh spoor, and small nests of twigs and branches all attest to the existence of prospering fauna.
6173:
Some delicious wild strawberries grow on the ground.
Some delicious wild strawberries grow on the ground.

Rising above the surrounding environs, this lush and verdant plateau is well endowed with oaks and spindling pines. Underneath the trees flourish fields of strawberries and mountain lingons, their runners writhing and intermingling in a flurry of red and green. To the distant north, purple mountains rise contrasting the sky, the view opposite reveals a valley bespoken of healing and wonder.
6174: Thickly cluttered among themselves, whispering amidst the breeze, tall pines and spruce lie in secret conclave; their thoughts beyond the reckoning of even the elves. Cloaked in fiery green, the hillsides roll and dip with grassy dew-spotted rainbows glimmering in the light beneath the trees, descending to the north into a small rocky ravine that cleaves the highlands denying progress in that direction. To the east the pines grow sparse, southwards the land rises into a mighty plateau.
6175: A Patch of Thick Growing Hazels

Nestled in the midst of deep heather and bilberry brushwood is a patch of thick growing hazels. The prickly blanket of undergrowth effectively camouflages the area from the nearby road, nevertheless it is possible to observe any nearby travellers through the bushes.
6176: The land rises, slowly curving above the landscape, offering a good view of the surrounding environs. The forest is apparently in the process of rebirth to your northwest; evident are the low bright green tops of new trees. The land slides down into a valley east of you--the area looks rather peaceful and inviting for a fact. Closer upon you lie tall pines and a rich conglomeration of brush and heather.
6177: From each side of the deep valley a steep hillside clothed in thick pine woods rises from the bottom of the valley to the feet of twin escarpments. It is a large table of rock furrowed here and there from clefts that the wind and rain filled with dust, sand, and gravel. The hardy plants of the hills follow the lines of the furrows, forming miniature hedges, and in the larger crevasses cades and junipers, mixed with some twisted pines, have formed little dark green thickets.
6178: A long, wide terrace of rock stretches between two ravines, covered with small trees and herbs. Shielded from prevailing winds by a ledge of blue rock, it overlooks the bottom of a verdant valley above a sheer drop of fifty yards. On the hillside, slightly apart from the other trees, stands an ancient mountain ash, whose roots doubtless plunge into some invisible crevasse. Multilated by lightning, bristling with stumps like a parrot's comb, it stretches its long, leafy branches over a flat rock, smooth as a mirror and just perfect for a short respite.
6179: A fat rabbit sits here, chewing on some grass.

The woodlands prosper amid rolling stone hills and valleys. Rich, verdant undergrowth of rough yellowish grass, broom, and dogwood flourishes beneath a canopy of young pines and groups of turpentine trees. Here and there are plum trees prickly with black dead branches and a few old fig trees suffocated by their own suckers. A wall of large bare stones seems to be embedded in the base of a high rock face. A modest wooden door, flanked by small windows has been constructed in the bluish limestone wall. Beside it is a retaining wall brimming with rich soil that may at one time have housed a garden.
6180: A peaceful shady grove of tall thin pines grow here, not as robust as others nearby, but nonetheless gleaning a fragile beauty from the rocky earth. The trees' lithe appeal is accentuated by clusters of clematis, and a few wild carnations emerge from small fissures with a splash of colour.
6181: A small game trail dodges between clusters of elm and oak trees, together with a few grand old hazels. The earth is soft and moist, laden with rich humus, and supports a preponderance of broom and heather, mingled with vibrantly coloured wildflowers--clematis, honeysuckle, and larkspur. Fresh animal tracks attest to the constant use of this small pathway.
6182: A Turning Trail through the Trees

A preponderance of animal tracks cut between the trees, forging a path among the otherwise dense undergrowth. Tall and ancient oaks and elms grow proudly all about you, sheltering the area with their mighty limbs. And beneath their benevolent shelter all manner of shrubs and bushes thrive, competing with small wildflowers to cover the ground wherever the wildlife has not trodden all vegetation into the dirt.
6183: A small animal, all covered in spines, snuffles amongst the undergrowth.

Although this stretch of the woodland stands close by the road, the thick undergrowth forms an impenetrable hedge, which defeats any attempt to gain the thoroughfare. Great oaks lift their lofty heads above you, joining with the tangled brambles and gorse to shelter and protect this area, which must offer a home to innumerable small creatures. And, judging by the way the foliage has been cropped, these woods are also home to some larger game.
6184: A woodpecker is here, tapping on a tree.

Thick brambles and spiky gorse grow in a tangle beneath the tall trees. Great and ancient oaks and elms stand proudly all around you, their strong boughs forming a canopy overhead, and their lower limbs joining into the twisted snarl of undergrowth. To the north this foliage forms a natural hedge, which defeats any attempt at travel, but to the south and east the forest opens out somewhat. Progress westward is possible, but the forest appears to be no less forbidding in that direction.
6185: In the Forest along the Road
A swarm of midges is here, humming around you.

Tall trees and thick undergrowth run rampant just to the south of the road. Ancient oaks, elms and birch trees stand shoulder to shoulder with younger pines and firs. And all grows amid a proliferation of bushes and shrubs, the whole threatening to overrun the thoroughfare. Westward the undergrowth grows yet thicker, with thick brambles and gorse becoming predominant.
6186: In the Forest along the Road

A wild and healthy expanse of woodland stands sandwiched between the road and the old lands of a smallholding. Dry stone walls mark the border of the latter. Built to last, they are nevertheless beginning to submit to the test of time. Without repair, the constant pressure of the forest is beginning to breach the barrier. Even the road is not immune, for many trees have grown tall at its very edge, their branches and the dense undergrowth threatening to encroach upon the thoroughfare more with every passing day.
6187: The land here appears to have been denuded of trees long ago, perhaps to serve as a pasture or field for crops. But whatever purpose it once served, that is now in the past, and the area is now a fallow sea of weeds and scattered brushwood. Despite the stone wall, which is still largely intact, the forest to the west seems bent to reclaim what was once its own.
6188: The last remnants of a few rotten boards are scattered about the ground. A line of half-rotted posts stick out of the ground, showing where a fence must once have stood. These pales describe three sides of a rectangle, the fourth being comprised of an old stone wall, which stands at the forest border. To one end of the rectangular enclosure stands a rusted trough, its underside now pierced by rough holes. Below the trough the ground is marked by the russet stains of the iron-tainted water which has long run through the breaches in the bottom of the container.
6189: Thick heather and low-growing bushes are interspersed among the coarse, thin grasses which cover the gently rolling landscape. Though the ground shows signs that this was perhaps once a cultivated area, the land here has long since reverted to nature. Dreary and exposed to the elements, it has a chilly aspect. But it is in this wild and unkempt mien that its character originates.
6190: At the Edge of the Woods
A brown fox is here, looking for some rabbits to chew up.

An old stone wall once marked the boundary of the forest here. But it has now fallen to the tests of time, and to the constant pressure of the encroaching trees and undergrowth. At the edge of the woods new saplings are springing up, and though many are cropped and killed by the local wildlife, others thrive. So it is that the forest spreads once more into lands once taken from it by the diligent hand of hard-working crofters.
6191: The thick woodland opens into a wide glade where the trees stand further apart. Plant life flourishes here under the lighter canopy. The undergrowth of dense brambles and broom which predominate in these woods is supplemented by a thick carpet of lush, green grass and heather. Although the vegetation shows signs of frequent grazing, it remains in sound health.
6192: The game trail seems to falter here, splitting to take alternate tracks. To the west it marches decsisively through the trees, but east and south alike show signs of some use, both recent and regular. It is as if the creatures which have forged these paths have alternate destinations in mind, but the tall trees and heavy undergrowth make it hard to determine where each of the routes might take you.
6193: A Turning Trail through the Trees

A small mushroom grows nearby.
A small mushroom grows nearby.

Amid the tall trees and thick undergrowth of this verdant forest a game trail has sprung into being. Countless hooves and tiny paws must have stepped this way, for there is a distinct path among the trees, and upon it very little vegetation clings to life. The predominant trees in this area are deciduous, so no soft bed of needles marks the way. Rather the ground is covered with a thick leaf litter. Hard by the tree trunks, where fewer feet fall, this dense humus provides a rich environment where weeds and wildflowers can thrive. And in the more shaded patches a number of mushrooms grow.
6194: A roe deer is standing here, watching the terrain while chewing the vegetation.

Curving here from west to south, a high rock face crosses the land. Growing hard by this geographical feature the woodland thrives, with tall firs and pines almost choking out the older deciduous trees. A few small plum trees can be seen here and there, and among the thick undergrowth is a scattering of rhubarb plants.
6195:
A roe deer is standing here, watching the terrain while chewing the vegetation.
A roe deer is standing here, watching the terrain while chewing the vegetation.

A dirty, little pond sits in the shelter of the trees. Garbage and debris floats on its surface, making the water look rather murky, yet there is no odour of foulness or decay. Tall trees loom above you to all sides, and a variety of wildflowers, bushes and shrubs flourish here.
6196: At the Edge of the Woods

Young trees and stout shrubs grow all about you, reclaiming this land as part of the forest. A gated wall once stood here, dividing the wild woodland from the farmland beyond, but this has tumbled down completely. All that remains are irregular humps of stones and small boulders, upon which a variety of small plants and mosses have started to grow.
6197: Coarse grasses and thick tufts of heather grow all around. Here and there, a few low shrubs and bushes can be seen, as the gorse and brambles of the woodland spread out across the fields. Small saplings struggle valiantly to survive, but many have been cropped low to the ground by the local fauna. Neverthless, with the incursion of fast-growing species like pine, the woods will soon manage to reclaim this land.
6198: The elongated shape of a stoat can be seen darting across the terrain.

The ground dips and rolls gently in all directions. At some distance to the west a large forest rises out of the landscape, but here the only vegetation is coarse, thin grass, thick tufts of soft heather, and a scattering of stout bushes and tiny wildflowers. Unsheltered by hills or trees, this area is one which is bleak in aspect, yet it retains a certain austere beauty.
6199: Weeds and scattered brushwood grow all about, but a closer inspection of the area shows that this was once a crop field. Deep furrows cut across the land from north to south, but whatever was once planted here has now been choked out by the hardier wild plants.
6200: A small cottage and a number of smaller outbuildings once stood here. But all of the structures have been torn to the ground. Rough piles of stone show where the walls once rose, but of the contents of the buildings nothing now remains. Some charring on the stones suggests that the entire holding was fired, and there is nothing here to tell the tale of how or when this disaster fell.
6201: Clearly this land was once cared for and tended, for an extremely tall and broad dry stone wall protects it to both the south and east. The wall is one of quite heroic proportions for a simple farm, being built twice as thick as one would expect. And its height too is impressive. But apparently this was not enough to protect the owners of these fields. Judging by the weeds and rough shrubs which have overrun the area, something forced the farmers to leave the area some time ago.
6202: An extremely tall and stout dry stone wall has been constructed to the north of here. Although it shows signs of a prolonged period of disrepair, with no small number of stones having toppled from place, it remains in very sound shape, making it impossible to breach. But why it was built seems a mystery, for the land is here is nothing but barren, blustery plains, covered with nothing more threatening than coarse grasses, and small tufts of heather.
6203: The thick forest which rises to the north and east is steadily spreading out over the land. Already this area is partially covered by dense brambles and cruelly spiked briers. Tall, but strangely twisted saplings reach up through the choking grasp of the undergrowth. Coarse, yellow weeds and sickly, thin grasses grow everywhere there is any space between the tangled bushes.
6204: On a Wild and Open Plain

Though offered a little protection from the elements by a forest to the north, the land here remains blustery and windswept. Coarse, low-growing grasses and thick tufts of heather thrive in this environment, but only a few quite stunted bushes and shrubs rise above the ground. Closer to the forest, the vegetation seems to do better, rising to greater heights, but further south and west, the aspect becomes ever more bleak.
6205: In a Dark and Twisted Copse
A huge black fungus is here, exuding a foul stench.

Ancient and hoary trees crowd one upon another in this area of woodland. Part of a larger forest, which stretches out before you, both northeast and south- east of here, this coppice has a decidedly unwholesome air. Perhaps this is why the inhabitants of the smallholding which used to stand to the west took the time to construct such a tall and stout wall at its borders. The trees are all quite stunted, although large in girth, and their trunks seem to twist and writhe as they climb into the air. The branches tangle together above you, to make a thick canopy through which no natural light can pass.
6206: Blighted Land at a Forest Border

To the east and south a thick forest rises out of the land, its hoary, old trees dominating the landscape. But in this strip of land, just south of the road, someone has laid the woodland to waste. All that remains of the trees are charred and broken stumps, and the undergrowth has been cleared entirely. This must have been some considerable time ago, however, for now many weeds, clumps of thin grasses, and thick tufts of heather have begun to grow again.
6207: A dry stone wall once divided this land from the road to the north, suggesting that this was once part of a farm or smallholding. But now all that remains of the structure are tumbled rocks and small boulders, overgrown with grass and weeds. The size and number of rocks suggest that the wall was a tall one, and the wide area over which they have been scattered give rumour to a violent and malicious act of destruction.
6208: On a Rough and Broken Trail
Some ugly blow-flies are buzzing around here.

Though this entire area covered by weeds, thin grass, and a few small bushes, it is apparent that there was once a trail leading through here. Travelling from the Old East Road to the north, the scattered rocks and stones show the path which it must once have taken. Leading from the Old East Road to the north, they make their way directly to some ruined buildings, not far to the south of here.
6209: The last sad remains of a dry stone wall divide this land from the Old East Road, which sweeps past its western and northern borders. Now only scattered piles of tumbled rocks and stones remain, and a lot of these have rolled well within the borders of the field, suggesting that the walls were brought down by brute force. The ground itself is a sea of weeds and light brush, but the dirt below shows signs that it was once ploughed and tended, for even today long, deep furrows still scar the earth, though the crops once planted have been choked out by the wild vegetation.
6210: A path of trees, leading in from the north, comes to a sudden stop here, as if pointing to a lonely, broken tree. Surrounded by a small circle of bushes, the solitary giant stands just to the east of here, and overhead the canopy is higher and opens slightly around the solemn tree.
6211:
A tree-snake lies wrapped around one of the tree branches.
A tree-snake lies wrapped around one of the tree branches.

Tall trees loom above you now and seem to grow in a narrow line from north to south. The low branches cloud the top of the trees, and no outside noises can be heard from this part of the forest. Looking to the east and west, nothing can be seen beyond the trees that immediately surround you. Far to the south the forest is encompassed in darkness.
6212: A strange darkness fills the forest in every direction. The branches above seem to bend very low to the forest floor, and many vines crawl their way up to the canopy of the forest. A line of trees can be seen coming from the south leading to an unknown destination.
6213: The entangled branches overhead are so dark that it seems amazing that anything can live here. A small opening can be seen far away to the east. The trees to the south grow even closer together, and no light can penetrate their eerie darkness.
6214:
A mass of wriggling vines drops on you from the trees.
Some thick writhing vines whip all around you.

A barely discernible path twists its way to the south and east through the entangled underbrush of this dark forest. An unaware traveller could easily get stuck in the vines that cover the forest floor. The air is very heavy due to the overhanging branches and the sheer amount of trees standing beside you.
6215: The trees grow close together here and a small line of trees leads to an opening to the north. A small trail seems to be carved out of the trees, leading to either east or west. The forest canopy looms far above the floor here, making it possible to see the road to the north.
6216: Tall dark trees tower above the floor here seemingly unclimbable. The floor of the forest is open and filled with plants and bushes. The trees close around the outer edges of the clearing making all paths but the one to the west impassable.
6217: The water here begins to clear and grow in depth and small boulders seem to grow right out of the depths below. The shoulders on either side are steep and very slippery. The water flows from north to south.
6218: Small boulders rise out of the water creating ripples in the stream here. The shoulders of the stream are lined with large boulders and the banks are quite steep, but it should be possible to gain the shore.
6219: The water begins to shallow here and rocks can be seen amongst the bottom of the winding stream. The forest to the west opens just enough to allow entry into the darkness it conceals. The waterway turns east and south here.
6220: A small landing has been carved out of the surrounding trees giving easy access to the stream that flows here. Some tree roots can be seen through the crystal water of the stream keeping this forest richly nourished.
6221: The bank of the water opens to a small landing beside a forest in the north. Tree roots and rocks can be seen in the shallow section of the stream here. The streambed turns its course from east to south here.
6222: Boulders climb up from underneath the surface making travel difficult. Tree roots can also be seen nourishing in the shallows of the stream. The banks of the water wind their way from north to west along the forest.
6223: The water is wider here than at any other point. The bottom of the water can no longer be seen except along the very edge that leads to a high shoulder on the eastern and western shores. The stream continues to flow from north to south here, straightening slightly from its twisting passage through the lands to the north.
6224: Water begins to shallow here, making it easy to cross. The lands to the east are completely open, a contrast to the forest of the west. A strange tree dominates your view of the forest to the west, old and full of large knots.
6225: The land seems to once have been rich and full of life, yet lack of travel and concern has led to many tall bushes that grow out of control. Weeds dominate the ground. The ground is very soggy as though the stream overflowed here recently, filling the plain.
6226:
A low, many-branched shrub covers the ground here.
A wild bull seems ready to charge you.

The mud at the side of the river is deep and wide, forcing travellers to pass through it to reach the waters. Slowly to the east the ground becomes more firm and a lush countryside appears, whereas the land in the north seems untamed by comparison.
6227: The muddy shoulder of the river to the west becomes more firm, and sprouts grass a foot high. Groups of bushes and vegetation are scattered across the field. A large forest towers above the western lands, a harsh comparison to the seemingly endless land to the east.
6228: Grasses of many different yellow and green hues grow in abundance all around the floor of the plain. Most of the grass is short, with no one tuft standing any taller than its neighbours. A growth of wild weeds dominates the western land, where a winding waterway can be seen beyond a low wall of grass.
6229:
A roe deer is standing here, watching the terrain while chewing the vegetation.
A roe deer is standing here, watching the terrain while chewing the vegetation.

Grass of about half of a foot high dominates the land around you. The ground soft and moist, and though a wall of high grass and thin reeds blocks your view, the sound of running water betrays the presence of a nearby stream. The prairie opens to the south and east here.
6230: Tall bushels of brown and green grass flow in the breeze all around. A hint of a trail is here, trampled long ago by feet, leading to the east and west. The grass of the plains grow high here and to the west, whereas the land opens more to the east where a lush, colourful field can be seen. A thick clump of bushes blocks passage northward.
6231: A stocky mountain mule is here, waiting to serve.

Slowly the field sinks down and the ground becomes soft and moist. Tall, thorny bushes grow in a circle around the swampland with many small insects swarming any animal with blood that dares enter. The bushes become thick to the south, making the fields to the north, east and west the more desirable ways to travel.
6232: The ground beneath you is rich in a variety of brown and green hues. The foliage is diverse and grows in abundance in the absence of any large groups of trees. The land is open in all directions, as if only awaiting exploration.
6233: The rabid raccoon stands here, frothing at the mouth.

The ground is littered with remains of animal bones and campfires. The hill rises far enough to view the surrounding lands in all directions. The mountains of the north dominate the horizon, whereas an endless plain flows south of the road, seemingly melting its way into the sky.
6234: Only a small brown path can be seen here among the lush grass that surrounds the road that turns here north and east. A hill rises to the south, which overlooks the surrounding vegetation and seems an ideal place to rest.
6235: A few wagon marks are visible between the many horse tracks that lie in the road's soft shoulder. A steep, muddy hill rises to the north, and the road continues east and west.
6236: The dirt path of the road here is wide and soft, with little vegetation at the edges. A slippery rise to the north leads toward a steeper hillside. To the south a thick clump of trees prevents your progress. The road itself travels east and west from here.
6237: The dirt here of the road is firm and dry, with little vegetation growing along the banks of the turning trail. Trees start to populate the land to the east, which leads to the Trollshaws. The road bends south and west here.
6238: Bend in the Great East Road

The road bends from west to south, as it opens its way along a steep slope. Down the hillside, not further than a league away to the southeast, a wide expanse of flatland leads to the ford in the river Bruinen, the main pass from and towards the Misty Mountains. On the west, the trail disappears into the shadows of a narrow glen.
6239: The hills around meet here and a thin, winding path is formed by their joining. The slopes rise too quickly to climb up, forcing the use of this path. A few trees grow near the ridge, giving one another support when needed. A dense growth of cedar trees loom above the hills to the east, blocking the horizon.
6240:
A half-rotten corpse is hanging here.
A dark-skinned orc is here indifferent to your presence.
A large brown wolf stands here, its teeth partly bared.

The earth is littered with corpses and animal remains, leaving ants and flies a feast unlike any other. The stench is horrid and almost unbearable, the only exit is the narrow pass among the hills to the west.
6241: Tracks become more sparse as the winding trail slims to a few yards wide. A dark group of trees blocks passage to the west, but to the south the land opens out into a vast plain. Turning from north to east, the road travels onward across the countryside.
6242: The road opens wide here, and little blocks your immediate view of the lands around you. The Trollshaws begin to consume the land to the north. A green meadow fills the southern horizon, and the road goes east and west here.
6243: Straight and narrow, the road continues to plough through the countryside to the east and west here. A grassy green meadow grows to the south, filled with a variety of plants that contrast in colour to the brown path of the road.
6244: Straight as an arrow, the road stretches off into the distance to both the west and east. Its origins are not clear, but it may have been built when the Third Age of Arda was still young. By that time, the men had established the North-kingdom in Eriador, and the Old Road would greatly help them travel between their settlements.
6245: The old, dusty road continues to cut through the uneven landscape of the ancient realm of Rhudaur. The trail seems to run straight for the next few miles, opening into a small glen a bit further eastwards. Although well-worn indeed, it is still the easiest path through these inhospitable lands. It is therefore common to find marks of both travellers and steeds on its surface.
6246: Great East Road West of a Gully

The road continues to lead straight, as if ignoring the uneven terrain all around. No more than a mile further eastwards, it opens into a deep ravine with rocky, reddish walls. They stand so close to each other that one could think that the gully was slit open by the mighty blow of a giant sword. But even here, the rockfaces on both sides tower high above the road, leaving no other option than to progress along the path.
6247: Great East Road through a Rocky Gully

The road's width suddenly narrows as it runs through a deep cutting. Towering pines perched over moist walls of red stone cast shadows on the diminished path. The sheer, cliff-like rock faces rise upright, making any attempt to climb them pointless. The light rustle of a falling rock, or the faint patter of tiny feet echo through the shadowy, tunnel-like passage.
6248: West of the Ford in the Bruinen

A mile of flat, pebbly ground, dotted in shrubbery and weed, leads to the ford in the river Bruinen, where the foamy waters open their way noisily through the rocks. A path of compact earth cuts through the plain, showing obvious evidence of heavy use, yet bearing a surprisingly well-kept appearance. At the edge of the levelled riverside, it turns northwards and winds uphill. On the west, a dense forest carpets the southern face of that hillock with deep-green shades.
6249: A Ford in the River Bruinen

A few flat, smooth-edged, slippery-looking stones stick out of the shallow, yet troubled waters in this fordable section of the river. The stream dashes fiercely and noisily against them, like a tireless battering ram, but the rocks tear it to shreds of white, splashing foam. This is the only ford for many miles round about, and here is where the Great East Road crosses the Bruinen.
6250: Yellow flowers, with grey-green foliage, grow in clusters here.

The field opens to rows of trees and plants. Once, someone had taken great care in planting, now weeds sprout up among the plants and few leaves grow on the trees. Molehills show that the soil a few inches deep is rich and able to sustain life, but the top layer is loose and dry.
6251: Horse tracks dominate the ground beneath you. Grass and hay lie in abundance throughout the meadow, a perfect grazing land for horses. The ground is soft and many plants grow tall and colourful in the fertile ground. The meadow continues to the lands in the south and east.
6252: Piles of hay gathered in huge cubes fill the meadow for the grazing animals that pass through. The grass consists of many colours, shapes, and sizes, from tall, thin dark green needlelike grass to yellow leaf-like blades. The meadow stretches out before you to the east, west and south, but to the north the Old East Road cuts a scar across the land.
6253: White and grey stones litter the ground below you in no partictular order or pattern. Grass and weeds grow from among the stones, but the grass is short and even, unlike the meadow far to the west. A road traverses the countryside to the north along the southern border of a tall forest.
6254: A brown fox is here, looking for some rabbits to chew up.
