6476: A large landslide from the upper reaches of the hill to the south has formed this gully in the slope. The slip must have occurred several years past as the broken debris of rock and boulder is covered with lichens and moss. The sides of the gully to the south, east and west are steep and fragile with outcrops of loose rock and stone.
6477: The ground climbs upward to the south toward a split between two hill summits. To the north a large rockfall has created a precarious steep-sided gully down the north face of the slope. The land crosses the saddle and drops away to the south-east into a second valley in the hills.
6478: The narrow ridge from which you now gaze runs roughly south-west to north-east joining two high hill summits with a lower stretch of land, akin to a massive hammock of rock and stone slung between the peaks. To the south-east the hillside drops alarmingly downward into a steep river-cut valley.
6479: Bare hillside drops away on all sides of this lofty summit. The view of the surrounding land is panoramic. Several hundred feet below to the north, east and south, woods cover the land for miles around. To the west the range of hills continues, its bare mass stretching away in a massive curve to the south-west. This would be an excellent vantage point to behold any creatures travelling in the lands below.
6480: A small rat runs about, oblivious to your presence.

You are perched on the broad north facing slope. To the south, the hill climbs toward a peak and to the north, the ground drops away toward a dark green forest of pines. A brave adventurer could continue to the east and west across the rough rocky slope though walking would prove difficult on the damp uneven surface.
6481: The slope of the hillside reduces here with the ground almost level. To the south-east the hills appear to rise to a summit. To the north the land drops away from the plateau, becoming steep as it stretches down to the tree covered plains beyond. Yellow and gray grasses and tough heather grow around you harbouring a myriad of small flies and ticks.
6482: The land rises steadily upward to the south. The barren hillside provides a hard and unyielding footing with many boulders and rocks making progress slow and wearying. To the north, trees cover the lower slopes, stretching over the lowlands like a thick dark blanket.
6483: This hill provides a good view to the scenery. Though sparse in colours, the forms of hill ranges and huge blocks of rock cast interesting shadows in the terrain. One can almost see something big moving in the valleys.
6484: A black crow flies low to the ground here, looking for carrion to eat.

A few bush there and some grass here, that is all that grows on the hillsides. Tops of the hills have been cleared into blank rocky fields by the whining wind and rains. In the northwest there is a descend down to the forests.
6485: Forest by a Ridge of Hills

A little opening in the forest leads to the foot of a vast hill range in the south, where air is lighter, but life seems to be as hard as in the forests north of here. The wind carries a sad crying voice from that way.
6486: A tiny valley between two hills, one in the north and the other one in the south, where all the trees disappear and all you can see that way is a long ridge of hills. A little pond has formed here from the waters streaming down from the south.
6487: The hills seem to go on and on, without end. They are covered with little and large rocks and the terrain is hard to walk on. Sharp shadows dance on the close rock shapes as the wind sings in the cracks and valleys.
6488: The hills seem to go on and on, without end. They are covered with little and large rocks and the terrain is hard to walk on. Sharp shadows dance on the close rock shapes as the wind sings in the cracks and valleys.
6489: In skeleton: a dagger, a pair of smooth, black boots

A skeleton of some humanoid lies in the dust.
A black crow flies low to the ground here, looking for carrion to eat.
A black crow flies low to the ground here, looking for carrion to eat.

The hills seem to go on and on, without end. They are covered with little and large rocks and the terrain is hard to walk on. Sharp shadows dance on the close rock shapes as the wind sings in the cracks and valleys.
6490: A black crow flies low to the ground here, looking for carrion to eat.

The hills seem to go on and on, without end. They are covered with little and large rocks and the terrain is hard to walk on. Sharp shadows dance on the close rock shapes as the wind sings in the cracks and valleys.
6491: The ground levels out and dips slightly around you. This natural hollow provides shelter on the otherwise exposed hillside. The slight protection from the elements allows a few coarse shrubs and grasses to cling to life amid the had grey rocks and boulders. The hilly land continues all around with the summit of a large hill to the east.
6492: The shrubs and bushes of the lower slopes give way to hardy heathers and lichens growing where they can amidst the hard and unyielding ground. To the east, the land looks to rise several hundred feet to the summit among the hills. On this bleak hillside, your passage is obvious to any sharp eyed creature abroad.
6493: A swarm of midges is here, humming around you.

The rough boulder strewn hillside drops away alarmingly to the south and east. A steep sided valley cuts into the hillside to the south and you can discern a small stream tumbling down the vale. To the north the hill climbs upward toward its summit, hundreds of feet above you.
6494: The broad back of the hill lies flat here with several hundreds of yards of almost level ground stretching in all directions. Further to the east and north, the hillside climbs upward toward a summit. To the south the land drops toward the trollshaws. Few signs of wildlife are visible on this barren plateau.
6495: The rough hard ground descends to the south, leading down out of the high hills to the north. To the east and west the high ground continues along the range of hills. Gazing out over the lowland to the south, the trollshaws stretch far and wide, a blight upon the land.
6496: Down here in the valley the wind does not blow so cold, but the whine of it can still be heard above. The valley continues in the west, where it enters a dank misty area. Hills in north and south are steep, but easily climbable.
6497: A huge cliff rises high in the north and makes travelling that way impossible. The ascent in the south is much more friendly even if the hill that way is at least comparable to the one in north. The valley to the west looks cold and wet, and nothing can be seen through the fog.
6498: Just barely through the mist you can see the rising hills in the north, apparently a rather vast hill range starts there. To the east, toward a small pass going further east, the air gets lighter.
6499: A spirit floats towards you and howls with an evil laughter.

At least a little guidance out of this fog provides the rocky cliff that looks too hard to climb in the north. It might be possible to find cracks to put your feet on up there, but they cannot be seen from here.
6500: The hill range does not go any further south, instead there is a steady decline after which the terrain is swallowed under thick field of fog. The large valley in the south-east is all covered in fog and the smell of decaying wood is clear in the air.
6501: The frightening mist deepens east of here, flowing like a living being waiting for the unwary traveller. The birch grove in west looks totally out of place next to it.
6502: Apparently this is the southwest corner of the valley, at least the mist is not so thick in this direction. The terrain still descends a bit to the south, where it also gets wet and swampy.
6503: A slender plant grows here, with clusters of tiny pink flowers atop its stem.

The water from the surrounding forest seem to collect here, and disappear down through this little hole. Not much can be said about where it then goes, only distant plops can be heard down there. Only way to move here without soaking ones pants is to jump from tree root to another, hoping not to slip.
6504: Rising from the bogs and mire, these rounded knolls are densely blanketed with a multitude of fragrant evergreens, offsetting the suspect odour wafting from the swamplands. Under the protective boughs of firs and pines are a multitude of tiny flowers--white and lavender and violet. A sheer bluff dominates the eastern horizon, only a fool would attempt to ascend it. However, a small animal path winds upwards to the south.
6505: Luckily for you, the local fauna has established a faint trail along the hills, otherwise undoubtably you would have broken your neck ascending these bleak and treacherous uplands. Bare rocky slopes nuture but a few battered trees straining with life's tenacious will to survive in these infertile lands where the wind howls incessantly. Lichen and an odd reddish moss sprout from cracks or sheltered niches in the rocks, enlivening the otherwise gray and disenheartening surroundings. The trail spilts to the east or winds up and down the ascending ridgeface.
6506: A game trail winds from below, to a small saddle between the hills, then branches west and north, rising sharply to the west as it runs along a steep ridge of exposed rock. A few scattered trees nestle on the leeward slopes, firs and scrub pines, but otherwise the vegetation is scanty.
6507: The earth here is only semi-solid; a muddy mire that only barely supports ones weight. Nothing grows here, and the whole area smells of brimstone. To the east the mud grows soupy, and gas and water bubble from small fumaroles. A slippery, muddy slope rises to the north...it should be possible for an experienced climber to navigate the slope however.
6508: Cauldrons of boiling mud simmer sullenly, strange off-white plumes of mineral- laden steam rising in languid spirals to generate a strange mist that curls and cools, redissolving sulfurous compounds in a crusty rime that covers all available surfaces. The whole of the land lies choked in self-destroying paroxysms, rending itself, bleeding from crystalline pustules. A horrific malodourous stench of death and decay assaults the senses, an indescribable amalgamation of charnel putrefaction, fermenting offal, and plague-ridden purulence.
6509: A shelf of bluish-grey limestone rises above the immediate landscape, its surface well blanketed with tall pines and firs, and an occasional oak tree. Golden thistles bloom among rough grasses and small fragrant plants. The plateau drops off suddenly to the southwest, but you detect a small game trail to your north, that while best suited for goats, looks climbable.
6510: While more suited for goats than humanoids, a faint trail weaves its way along the side of a ridge then down to a shelf of bluish limestone a goodly distance below you. With care and paitence one might make their way through the hills northward, or follow the the goat-path along the course of the setting sun.
6511: Spindly windswept pines cling to the rocky surface, their vitality sapped by vines of broomrape curled vampirically about their trunks and limbs. The highlands fall away suddenly to the northwest, revealling a high cliff-face overlooking pine-dominated forests. The environ is quiet and desolate, and a sense of calm stillness pervades the air. Still, it does not feel like the calm of peace but rather that of grim expectation.
6512: As the result of a small rise in the terrain, the ground gets drier, and at the same time trees grow closer to each other. To the east the spruce forest slowly becomes dominated by straight pines. In the west, where the little streams seems to lead, the terrain becomes swampy.
6513: South Edge of a Misty Valley

A domesticated pony, beast of burden to many, stands here.
A moaning ghost advances towards you, shimmering with a pale light.
A horrifying darkness lies in the valley to the north. The air is still and wet, cold to the bones. The little one can see in other directions, there seems to be a little hill in the east.
6514:
A giant, strange looking green fungus is here, ready to devour you in seconds.
A moaning ghost advances towards you, shimmering with a pale light.
A moaning ghost advances towards you, shimmering with a pale light.
In middle of the fog you can only see a few yards away before everything is effectively blocked by the moist air flowing here.
6515: A beautiful and docile horse is standing here.

Only way one can tell the valley ends here is that the ground leaves up in the east, until it becomes too steep and rocky to continue. Moving carefully it could be possible to follow the edge of hills southwards without losing oneself in the fog.
6516: This hill provides excellent view over the misty valley opening in the west. It is very hard to say how far down there the ground really is, or if there is ground at all. The flowing air here is moisty and smells like rotten wood and fungi. In the north the hill slopes down to a small pass going east-west.
6517: The slope slowly makes it way up toward west, where it seems to become one of the highest points in the visible scenery. Ground here is covered with sharp edged rocks that make walking slow and dangerous, because each step must be thought up before proceeding.
6518: The hillside drops steeply to the south-west, leading down into a densely wooded valley. To the north and east the hillside rises upward, climbing the flanks of the range of hills. The view to the south encompasses the forest and plains of the trollshaws.
6519: The hillside rolls downward to the south and east. High on the slope, the vegetation is sparse and thin but as the land descends more tufts of grass and heathers appear on the rocky ground. The broad forests of the trollshaws lie spread out on the lowlands several miles to the south-east.
6520: The long spur of high ground from which you gaze, stretches out to the south- east like a massive finger. To the north-east a narrow valley cuts deeply into the hillside, its steep sides impassable to any creature without the power of flight. To the south and the east, the ridge continues.
6521: A long outcrop of hillside runs north-west to south-east, looming over the trollshaws. To the north, you can climb to the top of the ridge. To the south the slope becomes too steep to negotiate easily. The ridge continues to the east and west, its surface of loose rock and scree providing a slippery and dangerous footing.
6522:
Some ugly blow-flies are buzzing around here.
A roe deer is standing here, watching the terrain while chewing the vegetation.
Some ugly blow-flies are buzzing around here.

A rocky ridge rears above you to the north, cutting across the land from the northwest to the southeast. Its upper levels are denuded of trees, perhaps bearing too little soil to support such life. But here, on its lower slopes, a number of hardy pine trees seem to thrive, though further to the east, where the ground descends toward a deep gully, they again thin out and disappear.
6523:
A roe deer is standing here, watching the terrain while chewing the vegetation.
A roe deer is standing here, watching the terrain while chewing the vegetation.

You are in a thick wood composed mainly of dark, bushy trees. Interspersed in the forest every now and then are some small pine trees, spindly and weak. To the south and west the woodland continues, uninterrupted, but to the north it thins out a little, as it climbs a steep slope. Eastward the ground makes an abrupt plunge into a deep little gully, and there is a break in the trees.
6524: The thick woods continue here, the atmosphere dense and imposing. The trees here are not ordered and friendly, like in a pine forest, but seem to grasp at the sky with gnarled branches. To the west and north the dense forest continues, while to the east the ground plunges off into a deep gully, which provides a break in the trees.
6525: A roe deer is standing here, watching the terrain while chewing the vegetation.

Tall trees loom above you, their boughs spreading to form a lofty roof above your head. About their bases grow a variety of bushes and shrubs, wildflowers and weeds, forming a rich, varied and dense undergrowth, and scenting the air with sweet perfumes, which mingle with the redolent odour of pines. To the east the land slopes away from you, and the trees thin out towards a fairly deep depression.
6526: A Forest of Firs and Pines
A woodpecker is here, tapping on a tree.

The woods here are densely packed with thick bushy fir trees. Occasionally you see a thin spindly pine tree, fighting with the others for water and light. To the north, east and south the woods remain much the same, being quite dense and fairly dim. But to the west they seem to become lighter and rather more open.
6527: The thick forest surrounding you is made of densely packed fir trees. The trees have dark green foliage, and are growing closely together. To the north and east you can see nothing but more forest, while to the west you think you can make out some kind of clearing.
6528: You find yourself in a thick forest of dense, bushy trees. Only a little natural light can penetrate the foliage of the canopy overhead. The woodland stretches out in all directions, but to the north you can see that the ground climbs markedly, whilst to the east it begins a very gradual descent.
6529: A vast, rocky ridge runs from the northwest to the southeast in this area, looming high above the surrounding land. Here, toward its base, it still supports a good deal of vegetation, and even a few hardy pine trees, which thicken out as you descend to the south and west. Eastward the land remains quite sloped, climbing to the northeast, but descending in the opposite direction, toward a distant gully.
6530: With a nigh uncanny precision, the trees of the lower valley end in a straight line across the sloping hillside. Many small bushes and shrubs grow above the treeline and rise away from you for several hundred feet. From a bush near you comes a strange murmuring buzz.
6531: The ground drops away sharply to the west into the uppermost reach of a valley. The trees begin a few hundred yards below you though many small bushes and shrubs grow higher, almost to your vantage point. The hard rocky hillside climbs upward to the north and east and you can continue along the face of the slope to the south.
6532: The valley is sheltered on the north and east sides by the rising hillside beyond. This natural protection has allowed the wood and brush to proliferate and the thick undergrowth makes travel difficult. To the south and west the valley descends slightly.
6533: Less and less trees grow on the sloping hills, and in the north a vast region opens without a single tree bar a few puny bushes. Cold wind blows from that way, but the big pines quickly decay it into whine in the canopy.
6534: The terrain gets even higher in the north, rising to a tall hill. Clearly one of the most visible landmarks of the region, it effectively blocks your view further north. The lower parts of the trees here have been marked by some animal, an animal with big claws.
6535: The ground drops a few feet down in the west, where it steadily continues to descend until the fog hides it from the view. The trees are mainly pine here, with a few small birches in between.
6536: A few feet high cliff separates the two levels of the forest from each other, and a small waterwall brings the water from the upper level down to a stream that continues westward. It is possible to climb the cliff up, as long as you remember to choose the steps carefully.
6537: The pines grow close together, and the canopy does not let much light to the ground level. A little stream collects several tiny ones from the north, and turns the course of the water west toward a cliff edge.
6538: A brown fox is here, looking for some rabbits to chew up.
The ground is dry here, and only some grass grows on it. The pines seem to thrive in the sandy soil though, perhaps there is enough water underground for them to have a good life here.
6539: Many differing types of trees grow in this sheltered valley. The enclosing hillside and thick trees combine to cut down any wind to naught but a whisper. A few chitterings and squeaks of woodland creatures can be heard from beneath the foliage. The trees continue to the north and west. To the east and south, steep hillside rises up above you.
6540: Tall pines and firs grow all about you, and at their bases a variety of bushes and shrubs make up an equally healthy undergrowth. Westward the trees thin out markedly, giving way to an open area, and to the north another clearing can be seen. South and east the trees continue, if anything growing thicker.
6541: The forest parts and a large expanse of meadow is revealed. While trees do not grow here, there is a large variety of small plants, shrubs, and flowers that seem to enjoy the soil and sunlight. However, there is a large area in the centre of the meadow with no grass or vegetation at all, and there is a circle of blackened stones placed amidst it.
6542: A large glade opens amid the forest, with large areas of grassy meadows interspersed among the trees. Here and there are bunches of tiny white blossoms growing in low humps among the grass. The forest is shrouded with gloom to the northwest, but in the other direction the glade widens to form a large space open to the sun.
6543: The ravine contines to wind along to the west of this gloomy, darkened forest. Trees lock branches, preventing the light from penetrating to the earth where low broad-capped mushrooms and tiny white flowers spring from the moist soil.
6544: The forest opens up into a small clearing. Scattered about are rotting, splintered logs that were evidently at one time part of an old cabin. Now, however there is no sign of human inhabitants, just the silent pines standing vigilantly among patches of heather and bramble. Everywhere you look fragrant evergreens rise from the landscape, with the sharp crest of a ridge peeping from the treetops to your northwest.
6545: The ground arches upward towards the high ridge to your north. Grand, tall pines and blue spruces find a comfortable existence in the stony but fairly fertile soil. Small rounded bushes and tufts of grass grow between the trees, healthy if not prolific. A vaguely delineated trail weaves it way along the edge of the ridge, following the arching stone upwards.
6546: A wide ridge of hills arches above the landscape to your south, affording a view of spacious forested lands. Pines and an occasional fir or larch surround you, with small patches of brush, grass, and lichen underfoot. To the northeast the forest becomes dim and unappealing, below you espy a path winding down the cliff-face.
6547: Darkly twisted, knotted pines grow in large clusters on any available flat surfaces. Close around you brambles creep in and around the trees; the air is musty and conveys a sense of unease. Forest continues in all directions, south there is a sheer dropoff overlooking a wide band of forests.
6548: The forest begins to transition here, growing dense and dim to your north and thinning and sloping downward towards the rising sun. Pines rise prolifically all about you, giving the air a brisk clean smell.
6549: A fat rabbit sits here, chewing on some grass.

A fairly broad valley bottom is defined by the steep slopes to the east and to the west. Climbing gently northward, the vale gradually curves away to the east, in the far distance, but the only way to discern this is by spying the hilltops, for the entire area is populated by tall and healthy trees, which thrive in this sheltered and apparently well-watered area.
6550: The ground rises sharply to the east, and only a little less so to the west, defining a valley bottom, which itself climbs gently northwards. The entire area is densely packed with trees, pines and firs standing shoulder to shoulder with a variety of deciduous species, making a rich mixed woodland.
6551: A small animal, all covered in spines, snuffles amongst the undergrowth.

You have entered a small clearing in the woods. Covering the ground are small bushy shrubs with broad green leaves. Small animals scurry around beneath these bushes. On all sides the trees rise about you, but whilst to the north, the east and the west the woodland seems quite thick, to the south it remains rather open.
6552: A notable stand of tall firs and birches springs from a low rise, dominating the local skyline. Some dry brush and tinder are spread under the evergreens, which thin and disappear to your south, opening into a wide clearing.
6554: A pale mist redolent of rotting vegetation casts an unsettling pall about the forest. Indeed, the trees here seem rather unhealthy and discoloured somehow, with a strange greyish cast to their leaves and branches. Strange parasitic brambles curl up and down the trees to the exclusion of any other plant growth. A large impassable cliffwall rises to the north.
6555: Irregularly shaped clusters of trees grow amidst low grasses. Pines and firs predominate, with round mounds of brush scattered underfoot. A steeply sloped but not impassable trail twists up through the trees.
6556: A heron is stalking the area, looking for fish.

A very large space between two hills seems as if it has been cloven by some powerful force, be it natural or unnatural. A small path leads up to a shelf, where a small promontory offers a good view of the wetlands to the north, and evergreen woodlands to the west, beyond which you see a tiny ribbon that appears to be an established trail.
6557:
The corpse of a hill giant is lying here.
A rotten corpse is hanging here.

The ceiling and floor of the cave look like naturally formed, probably some of the ground has been carried away by rain but the thick network of tree roots has made new undergrowth grow on top of it, thus leaving this opening down here. Some trunks have been carried to make walls and give extra support to the ceiling.
6558: A little stone lies on the ground.

Some cataclysmic occurrence ripped the stones apart here. The ground is rutted and defiled by the shattered corpses of ancient stones. It appears that Morgoth himself walked through here wearing very heavy boots.
6559: You are standing on a rocky hill which you climbed by means of an old rough trail. The exertion has rendered you breathless but the sweat chills on your skin when you sense the aura of total evil that surrounds this place. Before you stands an old stone fortress, squat and sinister.
6560: The corpse of a starved grey wolf is lying here.

Again the sudden change takes you by surprise. The small disused trail has become an old road which arrows northward. The raised surface, the larger than normal width and the incredible straightness mark this as a military road. It appears to have been abandoned centuries ago yet still the surface holds good. To the west lies a rocky plain.
6561: A dark intangible shadow turns to face you.

All around you lie the remains of what was once an extensive military outpost. Long ago some great army marched here and you see the old decayed signs of their presence. The air is charged with evil and the walls seem to ring with the cadence of a long forgotten march. There is an old inscription on the wall and stairs leads upward.
6562: The room is dark and old and damp. You can hear the ancient stones groan as you move amongst them. The air feels chilled, and a slight draught disturbs it from time to time. On the walls you can make out some ancient carvings, but their substance has all but faded to nothing.
6563:
A dark intangible shadow turns to face you.
A dark intangible shadow turns to face you.

Here the whole region is visible, except for where in the south east the large mass of rock obscures the view. To the north the old road runs straight as an arrow towards Ettenmoors and distant Angmar.
6564: The trail turns northward here in an abrupt and unexpected fashion. All a around you there is a wasteland of shattered rock and barren plain. To the west you can see a rocky hill on which there appears to be some old fortifications. It is almost as if the trail recoils from this place, fleeing north and east at the first available opportunity.
6565: The trail curves southward into the fringes of the forest and descends gently among the trees.
6566: The trail bends a little to avoid the lonely pinnacle of rock which stands like a guardian at the forest's edge. No trees or large shrubs grow within twenty feet of the base.
6567: A ferocious warg is here, snarling angrily.

You hear the tinkle of running water to the south and heave a sigh of relief that the path has widened a little. The trail continues east-west and to the west you can see a tall crag standing like a sentinel at the forest edge.
6568: Along the edge of a deep canyon, the path wends its way, and clearly there is no way to travel to the north of the trail due to this obstruction. To the south however, you might choose to make your way into the rolling hills.
6569: The path here is extremely narrow, as it works its faltering way along the lip of a deep and treacherous canyon to the north; clearly there is no way to travel in that direction. To the south, however, stands a line of hills.
6570: Here the trail plods steadily from east to west across the land. At some distance to the south stands an old building. But even at this distance it is apparent that it has long been abandoned.
6571: A narrow trail cuts its way across the land here, proceeding almost perfectly east to west, with scarcely any diversion from its path. To the south of the trail stands an old yard, whilst to the north the way is blocked by a deep and dangerous canyon - clearly it would be impossible to travel that way.
6572: You are standing on a trail running from the east to the west. To the north is the edge of a vast and deep canyon. To the south, a huge forest dominates the landscape, rising high into the sky. The sight of the forest causes a bit of unease in your mind.
6573: You are standing on a trail that follows a huge canyon to the north. Though stable here, the trail quickly turns into a steep drop to the north and east. To the southwest and far south, a large forest rises high into the sky. This trail leads somewhere, but following it might require more than simply walking.
6574: Bending again around the canyon's rim, the trail leads you onwards to the unknown. A tall, impenetrable wall of trees blocks the south and west. The size of the forest piques your curiosity, but the sinister appearance daunts your courage. All that matters now is to avoid falling off the trail.
6575: Running parallel to the deep canyon to the north, the trail leads you along to your destination, known or unknown. The tall trees to your south, though draw your attention more and more. Your pace slows as you contemplate the dangers of exploration, but it will have to wait until you can glimpse a way in.
6576: Travelling along the only obvious path here, you follow your adventuresome spirit. To remind you of your mortality, the depths of the canyon and the towering trees mock whatever confidence you once had. Though it would be foolish to attempt to go north, a way into the forest might be found eventually.
6577: In the north, the canyon seems to rise into the rest of the landscape to the northeast. The trail itself bends to the south, entering part of the forest as it does so. Your choices might not include staying out of the forest if you move south.
6578: Standing at this part of the trail, the tall trees form a canopy over your head, blocking out most of the light from above. This part of the forest is rather peaceful, but the thick and dark trees to the south indicate that not all of the forest is of such silvan character.
6579: The trail narrows here, confined by the walls of trees lining both the north and south sides. To the north, though, a small path is discernible in between massive trunks. To the south, you believe you could slip into the dark depths, but the inherent dangers of such a place force you to reconsider. The canopy of trees even here is sufficient to block out enough light to put this place into dim twilight.
6580: At this point, no light escapes the thick green ceiling of tall branches and large leaves. Though smaller than before, the trail stubbornly moves onward defying the aggression of the trees. To the south, the forest is dark and impenetrable, curbing your adventuresome spirit. The trees to the north, though thick, leave sufficient room for you to explore there.
6581: Thin beams of light illuminate the trail, stubbornly working their way through the green ceiling above. Thick trees prevent any access into the forest around you, leaving you no choice but to remain on the trail. You console your spirit with the cold knowledge that ignorance can be at least healthy, if not blissful.
6582: The trail moves its way through the edges of the forest, offering a peaceful setting for your tired limbs. Maybe this would be a good place to rest, away from the landscape of danger in the distances. The healthy green leaves offer a balm to your eyes after the sights of past combat.
6583: You stand on a trail just moving its way into an immense forest to the west. The healthy green color of the trees raises your spirits. A small path leads off to the north, into an area of spread out trees.
6584: En route to the ground far below, your mind leaves your body, taking the time to admire the landscape in the few seconds before impact. Maybe the next opportunity, you will choose to respect the physical laws which govern Arda.
6587: En route to the ground far below, your mind leaves your body, taking the time to admire the landscape in the few seconds before impact. Maybe the next opportunity, you will choose to respect the physical laws which govern Arda.
6588: The ground here has been shattered and broken by some titanic force. There are no living creatures, no plants, no water. The splintered rocks lie like the discarded eggshells from some gigantic omelette. The recipe appears to have been a failure. To the south you can see a shattered mountain whose unclimbable scree strewn slopes rear steeply above the forest.
6589: Here the devastation is complete. Tortured shapes and twisted forms litter the ground. Polished skulls, stripped clean of flesh by carrion crows and other vermin, lie discarded amongst the detritus of battle. Rusted weapons, shattered sword hilts and broken shields leave no doubt as to what occurred here ages past.
6590: The forest peters out here, confronted on the north by a trail, the east by a blasted plain and the west by a spire of rock. To the south the trees thicken rapidly, but here they grow almost unwillingly.
6591: You are in a wasteland of broken rock. South and east the forest lies, patiently advancing northward. North of here you see an old trail all around you is devastation and ruin.
6592: Held between the shattered arms of the broken mountain the plain looks north and east. The south and west are impassable scree covered slopes, the north and east are barren wastelands.
6593: A tangle of stony ridges juts out from the plateau to the east. The ground generally slopes downward toward forested vales to the north and west, but deep ravines cut at seemingly random angles carve the ridges apart into great stony blocks. Low cliffs and sinkholes are everywhere. The rotten limestone is barely covered by scraggly bushes and a few ancient, twisted firs. There is no sign of civilisation.
6594: A tall stag is here, grazing peacefully.

The forested land drops sharply toward the west in a series of escarpments cut through with gullies and choked with rotten piles of collapsed stone. Spruces and firs jut from the slope at strange angles, greedily twisting toward the cold light of the sun. There is no water in the ravines, only dank moss and talus. Here and there are some harder blocks of stone which seem to have been worked by tools; but there is no obvious sense of what they used to be.
6595: The forest is sparse here, as the land rises slowly from the plateau to the west, becomes stony and barren, then plummets down to the west in a tangle of gullies and collapsed blocks of stone. The soil is thin here, and the rotten limestone underneath, cut through with joints and crevices, is exposed on every slope. The conifers are dwarfed, beaten down, twisted.
6596: You are in a dark, dense forest. All sounds of animals and the like have dissappeared. The light has grown very dim. Strange vegetation crowds about you. It has an unfamiliar odour and you find yourself becoming disoriented.
6597: A demon wolf lurks here, its dark form twisting and hiding its shape.

You are in a dark, dense forest. All sounds of animals and the like have dissappeared. The light has grown very dim. Strange vegetation crowds about you. It has an unfamiliar odour and you find yourself becoming disoriented.
6598:
A large brown wolf stands here, its teeth partly bared.
A large brown wolf stands here, its teeth partly bared.

You are in a dark, dense forest. All sounds of animals and the like have disappeared. No sunlight can reach the floor. Strange vegetation crowds about you. It has an unfamiliar odour and you find yourself becoming disoriented.
6599: You are in a very dense forest. All sounds of animals and the like have disappeared. The light has grown very dim. Strange vegetation crowds about you. It has an unfamiliar odour and you find yourself becoming disoriented.
6600: A steep-sided ravine slashes through the old rotten hills here. There is no water flowing in it; water drips from its sides, but is lost in the water-worn joints and crevices of the limestone. The floor of the ravine is covered with deep ferns on a surface of loose rubble. The ravine trends toward the southwest and plunges steeply downward. The wall of the ravine's south side is so steep that its floor must lie in perpetual shadow.
6601: Rough, steep-sided hillocks rise up here from the uneven forest floor, raggedly covered with low evergreen brush and crowned by clumps of twisted old pines. The rock of which they are formed is rotten, spongy limestone, honeycombed with crevices and gaping joints. The ground underfoot is full of potholes and stone blocks.
6602: Rising a hundred feet or so above the surrounding ground, the top of this small hillock looks out over the forests of the trollshaws. All around the ground drops away into forest though the north face of the hillock is more barren than the others, perhaps due to the lack of sun on its aspect. Underfoot the grass lies flattened by the wind scouring the top of the rise.
6603: Many types of tree grow together in a jumble of shape and colour. All around firs, cedar, oak and birch compete for ground and light. The trees shade much of the light from the ground and the forest floor lives in perpetual shade. Here and there a rabbit burrow gapes up blackly from the soft moist earth. Piles of small droppings suggest that the burrows have many inhabitants.
6604:
A huge black fungus is here, exuding a foul stench.
A wolf spider is here, among the trees.

Here the trees of the woodland are spaced wide and thin. Much shrub and brush cover the gaps between the firs in an untidy jumble of shapes and size. The area has an unkempt look to it as if nature herself has lost interest in the doleful place. A peculiar rotting odour hangs in the air, smearing itself across the back of your throat.
6605: A coloured game bird is visible in the vegetation, watching you warily.

The coarse ground of the forest floor climbs upward to the north, the trees appearing to lean over on the slope as they reach skyward. As the slope rises, the tree cover thins and the bare crest of the hillock can be seen some way off to the north. To the south, east and west the forest thickens as it descends to the lowlands of the trollshaws.
6606: Thick, dank forest, perpetually dark, grows here in a vale surrounded on the north and east sides by steep limestone escarpments. The stony ground is covered with deep moss, ferns, and fungus, and the air is damp and musty. Odd squawks and rustling sounds come from the dark boughs overhead.
6607: Crumbling limestone bluffs topped with unhealthy-looking conifers face west and overlook the dense forest below. There are no good trails up the escarpment, though there are a few hand-holds by means of which one might scramble down, if one wants to risk putting one's weight on rock which has been rotting for a thousand years. There are some chunks of granite which might once have been a fortification, in the days when men of the Dunedain ruled here.
6608: A huge warg is here, moving in for the kill.

The forest has grown suddenly dark and oppressive. There are no animal sounds just the cracking of twigs beneath your feet. The forest floor is a tangled mess. It is hard to find a path or even to decide which direction you are going in. You see that the forest is choked with fallen trees and undergrowth in some places.
6609: The forest has grown suddenly dark and oppressive. There are no animal sounds just the cracking of twigs beneath your feet. The forest floor is a tangled mess. It is hard to find a path or even to decide which direction you are going in. You see that the forest is choked with fallen trees and undergrowth in some places. You sense a looming presence adding to the darkness.
6610: The forest stretches out around you. The trees block sight of the horizon, constraining your world to several yards before the thick foliage shuts out sight of what lies beyond. Travel through the dense woodland is difficult, not least due to the difficulty of choosing and following a steady course.
6612: Brown and coarse, the trunks of the pine trees stand needle straight, raising their proud branches to the heavens. The evergreens cut down the light at the forest floor level to a permanent dusk and few other plants survive in the dim conditions. Only a few green ferns accompany the conifers.
6613:
A shrub with maple-like leaves is growing here.
On the shrub, there are two handfuls of blackcurrant berries.
A large thorny branched shrub is growing here.
On the shrub, there are a number of blackberries.

A dense forest of pines grows here; their boughs are very dark green, and seem almost black. Few indeed are the shafts of sunlight which ever pierce the thick canopy of needles above. The forest floor is a carpet of browned needles, packed thickly underfoot, and few are the plants which grow among the trees - some clumps of ferns, some stunted shrubs, and some berry bushes growing in the occasional clearing.
6614:
A black crow flies low to the ground here, looking for carrion to eat.
A cockroach is scuttling across the floor carrying some debris.

Here at the base of the hills to the east the ground is so thickly covered with rotten limestone boulders that little will grow here. The trees are few, and the stone is mostly covered with heather and with a kind of pale grey-green grass which seems half-dead, unable to support any life. The ground is empty and unhealthy. A few insects buzz about.
6615:
A disgusting forest troll is searching for fresh meat here.

6617: This small mound lies at least fifty feet higher than the surrounding area of forest. The trees of the forest do not quite cover the exposed crest of the mound. The break in the forest has allow thick bramble and briar bush to grow uninhibited. The buzz of insects visiting the wild bramble berries sounds out with the gentle rustle of wind in the trees.
6618: The ground rises slightly to the west, leading up from the surrounding forest. The pines are interspersed with birch trees, their silver bark contrasting with the deep brown of the evergreens. A few droppings and several small burrows dug into the slope show that you are not the only creature abroad in the woods.
6619: You are in a dark, dense forest. All sounds of animals and the like have disappeared. The light is dim here. To the east you see a large hill. Fallen trees and thick undergrowth prevent any further northward progress.
6620: The large hill rises high above the forest floor. Its sides are not very steep, but for some reason the forest has not covered the hill. Many rocks and boulders dot the slopes and the flat hilltop.

A disgusting forest troll is searching for fresh meat here.

6623: You are standing in a light, green softwood forest with trees full of life. There are some strange large footprints on the ground and to the east you can see that the forest gets thinner.
6624: Long slender pines let the light travel between their branches. The smell of an old forest fills your nostrils and relaxes you. There is a large hill to the northwest.
6625: A demon wolf lurks here, its dark form twisting and hiding its shape.
