6627: The woods around you grow so thickly as to make progress nigh impossible. Every step must be won from the undergrowth as it clings to limbs and catches at feet. The sounds of any movement through the brush echoes around the woodland before dying away to silence once again.
6628: The forest here has an illness upon it. The trees bear no leaves or needles and the grass is yellowed and dry. The ground slopes up a large hillock to the north and the forest deepens to the south and east. A strange odour curls up from the disturbed ground under you.
6629:
A grey wolf is here, thin from starvation.
A demon wolf lurks here, its dark form twisting and hiding its shape.
Long slender pines let the light travel between their branches. The smell of an old forest fills your nostrils and relaxes you. There is a large hill to the north.
6630: Long slender trees let the light travel between their branches. The smell of an old forest fills your nostrils and relaxes you.
6631: You are standing in a light, green softwood forest with trees full of life. There are some strange large footprints on the ground and to the east you can see that the forest gets thinner.
6632:
A roe deer is standing here, watching the terrain while chewing the vegetation.
A roe deer is standing here, watching the terrain while chewing the vegetation.

Small outcroppings of bushes and trees grow out all around the valley. Some small rocks are scattered about the valley floor, looking up you see the rock formation to the south that must have dropped the stones here. The hills rise around the valley in the south and west, and the field descends to a large valley in the east.
6634: The hills here are lower than the surrounding mounds and forest. Some trees begin to populate the western edge of the hill leading into the Trollshaws. The forest to the north dominates the horizon there, and not far to the south, at the bottom of the hill, the landscape is marked by the Old East Road.
6635: The trees quickly enclose and block further passage to the south. Some light filters through an opening in the hills to the west, and the Trollshaws continue overhanging the lands to the east.
6636: The land is soft and lush here, sustaining itself from the stream to the west. Many different types of plants grow in unorganized rows, some trampled from wanderers roaming from the road to the south. A large group of fir trees loom above and block the eastern lands.
6637: A rich mix of fir and pine trees scatter their way through the forest trail. A thick wall of cedar trees block passage to the west and south, seemingly impassable. Small circular stones lie on the forest floor, like eyes looking out from the ground at the branches above.
6638: Walls of thick cedar trees loom above you to the north and south preventing passage. The forest edge in the west is more open, like the east. No light filters into the passageway due to the dense canopy of leaves and limbs.
6639: Rows of tall fir trees lead to an intersection in the middle of the Trollshaws. The trees grow farther apart at the base but thick limbs and numerous fir needles still manage to block out both sun and moonlight. The trees of the forest open to all the surrounding directions here.
6640:
The corpse of an ugly forest troll is lying here.
A disgusting forest troll is searching for fresh meat here.

The forest here opens slightly, the trees being higher here than anywhere else in the Trollshaws. A wall of thick, dark trees lie to the south making that the only route impassable to travel from this part of the forest.
6641: A disgusting forest troll is searching for fresh meat here.

Strangely a group of tall pine trees block the passage north and south, a stark comparison to the open forest to the east and west. The forest here is rich in vines and ivy, with some bushes growing at the base of a stand of fir trees.
6642:
The corpse of an ugly forest troll is lying here.
The corpse of an ugly forest troll is lying here.

The trees give way to a small clearing here, with scattered boulders lying circular in formation around a pit filled with bones and tattered weapons of war. Large footprints are scattered throughout the clearing, all made by the same type of creature. The trees allow passage to the forest in the east, west, and south here.
6643: A tall stand of cedar, pine, and fir trees weave their way through the forest. The moist canopy is overgrown by branches making the air heavy in scent from the surrounding trees. The passage here is blocked in all directions except the east.
6644: Fir trees dominate the forest in this area. Thick branches and leaves block the sky from view keeping the air thick and scented. The forest opens slightly to the west here, and a row of trees leads east and south.
6645: The ground slowly rises to a ridge along the side of a tall hill. Trees line the passage below blocking the view of what lies there. A dark overgrowth of trees blocks your passage further to the east and south making the only route of travel to the north or west.
6646: Clumps of grass grow between stones and fallen trees along the base of the hills. The field's view of a distant horizon is blocked in all directions and the air is stagnant due to the hills blocking any wind. The hills rise to the east and south and a slightly higher field lies to the west.
6647: Trees clear away, broken rocks depart, and a lonely hill rises below your feet. The grass is plentiful here, kept low to the ground by many an animal treading through the land. The west lands open to a valley below the hills, whereas the east continues to rise.
6648: Many hills rise among one another making a twisting passage between them that continues to rise far to the east. The ground here is firm and makes for quick progress among the hills. A dark forest looms above the hills to the south.
6649:
A disgusting forest troll is searching for fresh meat here.
A demon wolf lurks here, its dark form twisting and hiding its shape.

Pine trees dominate the outer ring of the forest filling the air with a heavy scent from their needles. Some roots grow out from the soft ground, sometimes catching your feet. Two amply separated rows of cedars lead to the forest in the east and south.
6650: Cedar trees surround the ground forming a cover of leaves that prevents light from reaching the floor. Vines cower at the forest floor hanging on the lowest limbs, but the forest floor is clear of all other forms of life. Bones and animal remains litter the floor creating a heavy stench.
6651: A demon wolf lurks here, its dark form twisting and hiding its shape.

Trees and bushes start to protrude from the ground at the base of the hill leading to the Trollshaws to the southeast. The rising ground finally gives way to a densely vegetated field to the east, or continue to twist and rise to the west.
6652: A rich mix of cedar, pine, and fir trees grow out of the rich grassland and begin to block out the light from above. The lands to the east and west were more unfortunate, dominated by the massive trees and the darkness created.
6653: The grass that grows in the west quickly comes to a halt at a black shadow that signifies the entrance of the forest. Tall cedar trees grow all around you, their intermingling branches blocking the light from above. South and east the forest continues, whilst to the north the foliage becomes so dense that it forms an impenetrable natural hedge.
6654: You are now within the depths of the forest. The greyish, mouldy trunks of the knotted trees seem to bend over you as you walk by, their thin, dark branches hanging threateningly above your head. They even shift as you turn your back on them, or so you seem to glimpse from the corner of your eye. Occasionally, a branch drops noisily onto the rocky floor that lies hidden beneath the thick undergrowth.
6655: Tall trees tangle their limbs overhead, forming a solid canopy through which not a single ray of light passes, not even on the sunniest of days. With the winds blocked out, the air here is stale, and a dank odour of decay permeates the area. Thin, yet thorny bushes predominate amongst the undergrowth, and they grow with such wild proliferation that they make any attempt to progress further into the forest quite an arduous task.
6656: A few dispersed trees grow all over this wide area that, unlike the rugged terrain that is characteristic in these lands, seems rather level. Their look, although not wholesome, is still far from resembling the sinister appearance of the forest that looms challenging a bit westwards, if only because they stand alone. Turning to the east, the ground seems to descend abruptly into the lowlands, where a maze of hillocks, cracks, bluffs and gullies marks the landscape.
6657: The earth inclines to connect the high lands standing on the north and west to the stony plains that stretch out into the distance towards the southeast. Finding a path along the steep, craggy slope becomes harder and harder with every step, and so progress is slow and straining. A few thorny bushes grow among the rocks, littering the dull-grey, rugged landscape in brownish hues.
6658: A long, deep, natural fault cuts the countryside to the south, exposing the bowels of the earth to the light. Only a twisted, brownish brushwood clings to the cold, grey rock. If there ever grew anything higher, it was probably swept away by the frozen wind from the mountains, which shrouds the Bruinen valley in its icy breath.
6659: Countless crevices of all lengths and widths run through the ground, splitting it into patches of rock, like a stone floe breaking up little by little. And where the hard rock has hardly endured the harsh rains, winds, and frosts, no vegetation can grow, except a few stunted bushes with prickles all over. This shrubbery adds a faint touch of colour to the dull, desolate moors.
6660: A high, rocky plateau rises in the west. A large part of it seems to have come crashing down, forming a rough hillside along which one can climb to the top, among the sharp-edged rocks and the bare briars. When the wind blows from the mountains, it raises a cloud of dust and pebbles, and a deep shriek, like a loud moan, echoes throughout the plains as it slips among the rocks, as if it was being torn apart.
6661: Near the Eaves of a Pine Forest

The escarped ground here rises above the lowlands that form the valley of the Bruinen. The descent into the plains below looks feasible, though not without effort. An extensive, mournful-looking forest, shrouded in a deep blackness, seems to have taken possession of most of the terrain up here. Long, twisted branches hang defiantly from the huge, greyish trunks that mark out the boundaries of the woodland, not far to the west.
6662: A brutish forest troll is hunting here, looking for some tasty flesh.

Somehow the trees in this part of the forest appear to have been turned into stone. Their barks have an ashen, lifeless look. Thick moss and lichen hang from their trunks, exuding a penetrating smell. Even the air is dense and heavy, as if crushed under the weight of the endless night beneath the ceiling of dark leaves.
6663:
A brutish forest troll is here, fighting YOU.
Drazud (freshmeat), wielding a great warsword, is here, fighting a brutish forest troll.
Klaees (thedon), wielding a great warsword, is here, fighting a brutish forest troll.

If there is such a thing as the heart of this sinister-looking forest, you are probably close now. Huge, yellowish ferns, tall as standing men, conceal most of the ground. Nevertheless, it appears to be mostly uneven and earthy beneath your feet, but there are also sharp, moist, slippery stones and deep hollows filled with dark, crackling leaves.
6664: The darkness in this part of the forest is so dense that the ground at your feet seems lifeless. No plants, vines, or ivy grow here, just trees. Tall, towering pines to short, thick cedar trees, all their leaves and branches blocking any hope of sun or moon light. But the trees do open up enough at ground level to allow passage in all directions.
6665: A sharp-eyed hawk is here stalking some prey.

Vegetation in the field around you stands in ultimate contrast to the grass of the hills above. A diverse variety of plants and colour mix together in perfect harmony. The tranquillity of the field is broken to the south with the growth of the deadly Trollshaws, but continues to the east.
6666: A sharp-eyed hawk is here stalking some prey.

The pine trees begin to deplete and a green meadow grows from the ground in all directions. The air is clean and crisp, filled with the scents of the surrounding vegetation. The Trollshaws tower over the lands to the south seemingly impassable.
6667: Thick plants grow in an unhealthy tangle all about you. Above your head, the long limbs of a host of spindly evergreens knot together in an impenetrable canopy through which no natural light seems able to pass. Dense briars form a prickly barrier to travel north or west from here, but to the south and east the forest seems to open up just a little, perhaps offering the possibility of progress.
6668: A mass of wriggling vines drops on you from the trees.

A proliferation of pine trees grows all about you, tall, yet somehow sickly in appearance. Nevertheless, their many twisted branches form a dense canopy overhead, and no glimpse of the sky can be caught from beneath their leafy tops. The perpetual gloom has spawned an undergrowth of warped and tangled briars, among which dark, stunted ferns stand out here and there.
6669: A black crow flies low to the ground here, looking for carrion to eat.

You find yourself in an elevated area with abundance of small crags and rocky ridges. The ground is stony for the most part, with large, yellowish boulders. Heather and bushes grow scattered among the stones, as if sprouting from the many chinks and crevices. In the flattest areas, small groups of dark trees have gathered, like tiny outposts of the ominous-looking forest that extends to the west and north.
6670: Elevated Plains by a Dark Forest

An extensive mesa rises above the rough plains that spread to the southeast. Close to the north, a dark green wall marks the limits of a shadowy forest. Strangely, no branches seem to grow outwards, as if, scared of the light, they tried to hide in the darkness of the depths. To the east and south, the ground descends in a series of ridges and unevenness.
6671: Although the rough footing makes it difficult to notice, the ground descends gently, but steadily towards the river that can be partially glimpsed in the distance to the east. Somewhere behind those grey, rugged hillocks, the ford of the Bruinen must lie. That is undoubtedly the easiest path for those trying to reach the High Pass in the Misty Mountains, towering majestically in the background.
6672: Standing on a steep slope of some tall and brooding hills, you see the transition from grassy hills to lush forest. Tall oaks and pines grow high above you, providing shade to your eyes. Quickly though, to the west and north, the incline becomes a thick and dark forest, drawing you closer while promising only danger.
6673: Row upon row of trees grow over a hundred feet high, then branch out into countless branches all ending in leaves which fight for the sunlight unseen above. Leaves, twigs, and even large branches lie rotting on the ground, seemingly undisturbed by anything else. However, the occasional rustle can be heard from...somewhere forcing you to glance hurriedly everywhere to try and prevent an ambush.
6674: Moving further into this strange and massive forest, you ponder how such a forest could grow to such size. No smaller plants grow here, blocked out as they are by the incredible canopy of leaves and branches overhead. The soil itself is very rich, due to the leaves which have fallen from many feet above you. You peer into the blackness around you and wonder where to try and move to next.
6675: A brutish forest troll is hunting here, looking for some tasty flesh.

The trees grow as tall as ever, blocking even the tiniest ray of sunlight from penetrating that living ceiling. The darkness has a definite edge of danger to it. Who knows what evil might lie in these parts, away from any civilization. The air, clammy and still, forces you to breathe more heavily. The blood quickens with the anticipation of possible threats.
6676: A disgusting forest troll is searching for fresh meat here.

More and more trees stand implacably around this small glen, giving the impression of awe before this display of nature. The majesty of the trees masks a definitive danger, the danger of the wild. This must be home to many animals, most of whom are not amenable to intruders. Adjusting your shield, you consider which path to take.
6677: The thick pine trees form an unbroken canopy above you. Their smooth unbroken trunks rise to a great height and then spread out into thick crowns. The ground is covered with decaying pine needles and dark stones that have a slimy appearance. The usual fresh smell of pine needles seems to be lost in pervading climate of darkness and decay.
6678: The rabid rabbit is here, frothing at the mouth.

The thick pine trees form an unbroken canopy above you. Their smooth unbroken trunks rise to a great height and then spread out into thick crowns. The ground is covered with decaying pine needles and dark stones that have a slimy appearance. The usual fresh smell of pine needles seems to be lost in pervading climate of darkness and decay.
6679: A squirrel scampers around here, looking for nuts from the trees.

The forest is still quite thin here. The trees still admit a lot of sunlight to the forest floor where small plants grow thickly. The slope is much more gradual here and rises gently to the north and east. To the east and north the forest thickens rapidly.
6680: You are in a hilly field climbing steeply up from the stream. Only a few trees grow here, but you see the forest thickening rapidly within a couple of miles. The ground is rough; full of cracks and impassable high slopes. You see the end of the forest in the far south and hills covered with trees to the east and north.
6681: A black catfish is here, lurking in the mud.

A shallow and narrow gully marks what must once have been the bed of a small stream. Its waters now dried up, all that remains are a curious mixture of stones, twigs, rotting leaves and animal remains.
6682: You have come out of the forest where the land falls getly eastward toward a small, narrow gully, which might once have been a babbling stream bed.
6683: You are in a light, green softwood forest. Small juniper bushes grow under the shade of the pines. The ground slopes gently eastward toward a small, narrow gully, which might once have carried a gentle stream. To the north the trees thicken and the land slopes upward to a huge mass of rock that rears steeply above.
6684: A small stream once flowed through the forest here, but its waters have now run dry, leaving only a shallow gully. The trees and shrubs which used to thrive on its waters have begun to suffer from its loss, withering and dying, and giving way to the sturdier grasses of the open land to the east.
6685: You are in a grassy field. All around you you can see tree stumps some of which show signs of being new. The deforestation seems to have been accomplished by some animal. It is obvious that the forest once covered this entire area.
6686: A large, loyal falcon is circling above.

You are in a hilly field. Only a few trees grow here, but you see the forest thickening rapidly within a couple of miles. The ground is rough, full of cracks and impassable high slopes. You see a river in the west and the same terrain in the north and south.
6687: Some ugly blow-flies are buzzing around here.

The thick pine trees form an unbroken canopy above you. Their smooth unbroken trunks rise to a great height and then spread out into thick crowns. The ground is covered with decaying pine needles and dark stones that have a slimy appearance. The usual fresh smell of pine needles seems to be lost in pervading climate of darkness and decay. The forest looks impassable to the northeast.
6688: The thick pine trees form an unbroken canopy above you. Their smooth trunks rise to a great height and then spread out into thick crowns. The ground is covered with decaying pine needles and dark stones that have a slimy appearance. The usual fresh smell of pine needles seems to be lost in pervading climate of darkness and decay.
6689: Growing more closely than once thought possible, the trees provide a forbidding environment to try and explore. The pines, oaks, spruces, cedars, and others all serve to block out the sunlight and impede your progress. The danger from the wilds is very real here, and warrants caution.
6690: A sturdy plant grows to a height of almost a yard.

Within the thickness of the forest, the countless trees press around you, lending an vaguely evil feeling to this place. The amount of trees and high roots makes it difficult to walk many places, and you have to pick your way with care. The sounds of animals can heard from all directions, preventing you from concentrating on keeping your bearings.
6691: A brutish forest troll is hunting here, looking for some tasty flesh.

Onwards and inwards, you probe the depths of the vast plant life around and above. The smell of rotting leaves and thick soil fills your nose, and the damp, still air gives an unsettling feeling to the whole forest. What lives in such a deep forest, and what will it take to survive? To the north, the forest seems even darker, somehow possible despite the impenetrable canopy above.
6692: Entering the dominant part of the forest, the light quickly is shut out by the overhead plant life. Oak, pine, spruce, and cedar grow to their maximum heights, humbling all who stand under such ageless life. The smell of moist and rotting leaves forces you to take deep breaths, and random noises in the distance attract your attention away from your chosen path. This is not an area to take lightly, and woe to any who lack to strength to fight.
6693: A disgusting forest troll is searching for fresh meat here.

Moving further along among the immortal trees, you pause to try and track down those elusive sounds that prey upon your senses. There appears to be no end to the natural darkness caused by the immense ceiling of leaves and branches, forcing you to peer every direction to determine which way could even be travelled. Sometimes, caution is better than sheer valour in handling threats that cannot be immediately perceived...
6694:
A disgusting forest troll is searching for fresh meat here.
A brutish forest troll is hunting here, looking for some tasty flesh.
A young and vicious olog-hai eagerly awaits intruders.

Moving along the ominous paths within the primeval wood, you are beset by lingering doubts about you abilities. Winning your way further into the forest will not be easy. A small patch of ground not covered by leaves clearly displays the paw of some huge animal. You strain your eyes looking for possible threats as you consider your options.
6695:
Some pine nuts lie scattered upon the ground.
A clear spring babbles as cool water trickles out of the ground.

Moving to this cul-de-sac of the forest, the darkness continues to press upon your head. The canopy of leaves and branches is not there to protect, but to trap you within the home of the evil inhabitants. Blinking your eyes, you notice a spring of cool water, hopefully uncontaminated despite the reek that hangs in the clammy air.
6696: Efforts to probe into the deepest parts of the primeval forest are mocked by an impassable wall of roots and trees to the south. To the north, however, you believe you could squeeze through, and perhaps find a way in more to the north. Shaking some clinging leaves from your boots, you trudge onward.
6697: Standing in what you approximate as near the western border of the forest, you unfortunately cannot see any way to work yourself through the thick growth. Most of the time, you can pick several ways to go, and you can only pray that eventually you can find the way out. Kicking aside a rotting branch that flies apart from your boot, you press onwards.
6698: A demon wolf lurks here, its dark form twisting and hiding its shape.

The thick pine trees form an unbroken canopy above you. Their smooth unbroken trunks rise to a great height and then spread out into thick crowns. The ground is covered with decaying pine needles and dark stones that have a slimy appearance. The usual fresh smell of pine needles seems to be lost in pervading climate of darkness and decay. Eastward the forest is very thick.
6699: A squirrel scampers around here, looking for nuts from the trees.

The forest is quite thin here. The trees admit a lot of sunlight to the forest floor where small plants grow thickly. To the east and north the forest thickens rapidly and to the west you can see a dam and a lake.
6700: The forest is quite thin here. The trees admit a lot of sunlight to the forest floor where small plants grow thickly. To the east and north the forest thickens rapidly and to the west you can see a crude dam of tree trunks, behind which a stagnant pool of water has collected.
6701: A large jumble of old tree trunks has dammed the small stream, reducing its flow to a mere trickle here. The already sluggish waters, now slowed and stopped by the barrier have become stagnant, and a green scum floats upon the surface. To the west, this foetid pool is banked by a steep slope, above which the dark forest can be spied.
6702: You are in a dark, dense forest. All sounds of animals and the like have dissappeared. The light is dim here. To the east you see a steep slope which looks extremely treacherous. To the west the forest gets even darker and to the north a sheer rock face towers above you.
6703: The very ground of these lands seems old, worn, and faded, as if devoid of any sign of life. Long crevices like millennial wrinkles cross its surface, which looks chipped, crumbled up in a myriad of fragments of rock. This is certainly a wasted region, castigated by the wear of time, the harsh climate, and the fierce wars of the past.
6704: A cockroach is scuttling across the floor carrying some debris.

A few dun bushes with a scraggy look strew the discoloured surface of the stony ground. This has an utterly worn appearance, as though a horde of huge beasts had trampled over it, or it had been whittled away for countless years. Lots of pebbles lie scattered all about, but it is the large amount of dust and gravel that mainly command one's attention. A deep fissure cuts through the landscape to the north.
6705: With no nearby shelter to oppose the winds that sweep the wide valley of the Bruinen, nor the abundant rains of this harsh climate, this vast open area of plains stands buffeted by the elements. But the gentle stream of the river bathes the riverside, and thus the soil is humid and rich. Grass grows tall and healthy, and a variety of wildflowers abound.
6706: An ample plain extends by the riverside. Hardly any small rise stands out of the utterly level ground, as if the spates of the near river, or the copious rains had swept along any feature of the landscape. Contrarily, tiny, shallow pools abound, filling every small depression of the earth. A mixed vegetation of thick grass and high reeds sprouts all over the place, but especially by the river bank.
6707: You find yourself at the mouth of a wide dale going steeply downward towards the river on the east. Shielded by the solid valley walls of stone, and bathed in the pure waters of the Bruinen, vegetation grows lush, carpeting the ground in a deep green shade. Thus, the vale looks like a hidden garden amidst the stony moors lying all round, or maybe like a tiny green point among a greyish stain, in the eyes of the great eagles that ride the winds.
6708: Hillock after hillock and moor after moor, the mostly barren landscape rolls before your eyes. Here the ground undulates in a myriad of small, faded-grey, dull-looking hills. At times, one can hear the howling of the cold, northerly wind echoing through the dale, lashing the hillock summits and sweeping the dusty fields. On the north, the hills rise more tightly forming shadowy vales, their broken peaks outlined against the horizon.
6709: The low hills in this area block out the view of the broad landscape. All you can see are the greyish plants that somehow cover the hills here. Some lingering evil is near here, but you cannot seem to discover a particular source.
6710: Standing on one of the tall hills in the area, you force yourself to ignore the strange and disturbing vegetation and look around. To the east, more hills follow, with the River Bruinen barely visible far away. The huge forest to the north and west seems to be the best choice for your will to explore.
6711: A brutish forest troll is hunting here, looking for some tasty flesh.

Bordering the tall, brooding hills to the south, this section of the forest grows much shorter than most of the rest. The canopy is very thick, but seems much less alive. The leaves on the ground are all brittle and shiny, and you cannot find one leaf that is green. The trunks are somewhat twisted, as if some force has warped the will of this forest. A pang of fear stabs your heart as you consider this.
6712: This part of the forest, unlike most of the rest, is not nearly as healthy. The trees grow only to about half the height of the others, but still manage to block out all the sunlight. Picking up a leaf from the ground, it has a strange, almost metallic sheen to it, and crumbles quickly under your rough handling. Something is not right here, and your interests might be best served by not finding out why.
6713: Walking along the ridge of hills, you ponder about the depressing atmosphere that hangs around here. The large forest to the east and north rises almost to the height of these large hills. You consider the pros and cons of adventuring there while you rest a second.
6714: Looking over the rest of the landscape, these brooding hills provide a constant if troubling watch over the huge forest to the west and north. The health of the forest seems to mock the hills, as if the forest was responsible for the sad state of these hills. Greyish grass covers the sides, while turning your gaze to the south gives a view of rocky hillocks rising to bald, flat tops.
6715: A group of small, rounded hills rise close to each other in this area. Their gentle hillsides show green and brown hues, dotted in shrubbery and weeds. However, their flattened tops look bare, devoid of any sort of vegetation, offering only the dull, pale grey of the worn rock to the light. By their appearance, one can guess that they must certainly be old, perhaps as much as the imposing Hithaeglir, or even more.
6716:
A rock lizard is here, motionless as it observes you.
A black crow flies low to the ground here, looking for carrion to eat.

The ground drops down to the south, following the line of a wide crevice running from west to east, like a deep wound in the split terrain. As a result, a high wall of bare rock drops vertically down to the plains below. The gravelly stone has a yellowish look, as if sick from the sunlight. There are hardly any footholds in the rockface, and the few that exist seem unsafe and dangerous, hence the descent becomes impossible here.
6717: A large pile of boulders is sitting here, probably debris from a rockslide.

Wide and deep runs this crack, cutting through the battered ground, like a marked, millennial scar. It appears to be as old as the very Misty Mountains, raised by the Great Enemy in times as sinister as forgotten. Large heaps of stones crowd at the bottom, shrouded in thick shadows. To the south, it may be feasible to attempt the climb, but the northern face looks unassailable indeed.
6718: The thick pine trees form an unbroken canopy above you. Their smooth unbroken trunks rise to a great height and then spread out into thick crowns. The ground is covered with decaying pine needles and dark stones that have a slimy appearance. The usual fresh smell of pine needles seems to be lost in pervading climate of darkness and decay. Eastward the forest is very thick.
6719:
A huge olog-hai troll is here staring blankly at you.
A ferocious warg is here, snarling angrily.
A squirrel scampers around here, looking for nuts from the trees.

The thick pine trees form an unbroken canopy above you. Their smooth unbroken trunks rise to a great height and then spread out into thick crowns. The ground is covered with decaying pine needles and dark stones that have a slimy appearance. The usual fresh smell of pine needles seems to be lost in pervading climate of darkness and decay. Eastward the forest is very thick. It is very dark, the cliff westward shadows the forest deeply but to the north you see the forest grow lighter.
6720:
The corpse of a ferocious warg is lying here.
A horse of the Rohirrim (Rood) is standing here, ridden by you.

Long ago some industrious labourer cleared away a large swath of forest. The clearing is already well on the way to being reclaimed by its brooding neighbour. Scattered clumps of bushes and young trees are the early colonists Northward you can see a deserted habitation. To the west you can see the northeastern corner of the impressively sheer rock mass.
6721: The thick pine trees form an unbroken canopy above you. Their smooth unbroken trunks rise to a great height and then spread out into thick crowns. The ground is covered with decaying pine needles and dark stones that have a slimy appearance. The usual fresh smell of pine needles seems to be lost in pervading climate of darkness and decay. Southward the forest is very thick.
6722: The thick pine trees form an unbroken canopy above you. Their smooth unbroken trunks rise to a great height and then spread out into thick crowns. The ground is covered with decaying pine needles and dark stones that have a slimy appearance. The usual fresh smell of pine needles seems to be lost in pervading climate of darkness and decay. Eastward the forest is very thick. But westward and northward you can see that the forest gets thinner.
6723: The various trees growing here--pine, oak, spruce, cedar, reach incredible heights above. The multitude of their branches forms an impenetrable canopy that blocks out every bit of possible light, plunging the forest into eternal night. Even with light, the trunks seem to be of blackened wood, yet no fire has touched these immortal trees. The leaves on the ground are of large size, blanketing everything and muffling sounds. The cloying, sweet smell of leaves and pollen makes you slightly dizzy. Danger lurks in this forest, demanding your constant attention.
6724:
Some pine nuts lie scattered upon the ground.
A brutish forest troll is hunting here, looking for some tasty flesh.

This part of the forest is clearly back from the boarders. The trees dominate your sight, rising so high above. No light comes through, even in the brightest sunlight. Your pulse quickens with the anticipation of threats from all around, as nameless creatures pad quietly among the trunks. The smell of leaves and trees, usually reassuring, only threatens to distract you.
6725: A brutish forest troll is hunting here, looking for some tasty flesh.

You are standing at the northern edge of the forest, yet the thickness of the trees growing so closely together has not changed at all. Their verdant canopy still blocks out all of the sunlight. The only light you see are the occasional flickers to the north, but there is way you can work through the plant life growing that way. Instead, you must find another way, and brave whatever hazards lurk in this immense forest. Adjusting your equipment, you ponder where to go.
6726: Walking along the northern rim of the forest, you are amazed at how consistent the thickness of the forest is. Only brief and fleeting glimpses of light to the north tell you are standing near the edge. Frustration sets in because of the realization that despite being close to leaving here, no egress exists. The thick, cloying smell of old leaves and rich loam is lighter here, but is still quite strong. The options for exit are still limited, but a distant howl goads you on.
6727: Tracing the edge of the mighty forest, you stop to rest a second in this eerie place. Only the occasional rustle can be heard, with not even the singing of birds to reassure you. Finding a way might be the highest priority, as the sheer size of the wood unnerves even the coolest of adventurers. No animal tracks can be seen in the thick covering of leaves, and you hope that means that nothing could track you as well.
6728: Moving a bit deeper into the forest, the trees grow a bit closer together. The rich and bittersweet smell of fallen leaves is strong, masking anything else that might leave an odour. The choice between possible escape and further adventure wars in your mind, and you take a gut check to see where you stand.
6729:
A disgusting forest troll is searching for fresh meat here.
A mass of wriggling vines drops on you from the trees.

The search for a way out is becoming maddening. The forest continues on for miles, yet no way exists to leave. In your weary mind, you sense the forest laughing at you, mocking your feeble efforts to escape. A rustling of leaves quickly brings you back to your senses, and you look around for a path to follow.
6730: Damn! What looked to be a way out onto some sort of trail is blocked by an immense fallen tree. Even despite the loss of so great a trunk, no sunlight reaches down into these depths. Leaning up against the trunk a second, you wipe your sweating brow and take a second to relax. Better to be rested in combat than stumbling in exhaustion.
6731:
A disgusting forest troll is searching for fresh meat here.
A brutish forest troll is hunting here, looking for some tasty flesh.

Though away from the centre of the forest, this section is still as thick and daunting as the others. Maybe you will get lucky and find a way out to some brightly lit place, but hope can be deadly when the immediate threat is so close. Tripping on a root, you curse and vow to burn more wood next winter.
6732: A mass of wriggling vines drops on you from the trees.

The trees here, of pine, oak, spruce, and cedar, grow high above your head. Finally, the fallen leaves display the different colours they should. Though cheered by this sight, the threat obviously remains, and warrants your undivided attention. Why would anything voluntarily live so far away from the sun, and yet live in the living wild?
6733: Picking your way carefully among the thick trunks, you again ponder the significance of these strange trees. The leaves, though not as brittle, are still of that odd black colour, and you long for the sight of green, verdant trees and dappled sunlight. Adjusting your equipment, you sigh and continue to look for a path.
6734: A brutish forest troll is hunting here, looking for some tasty flesh.

Moving further into the inky depths, the trees grow a bit taller, but still have unnatural twists and turns to what should be tall and proud trunks. The pine and oak trees are alive, but not what is normally considered healthy. Your boots crunch noisily on the black, brittle leaves that cover the floor of the forest in massive amounts. You wish for sunlight to illuminate this place and perhaps drive the evil spirit that pervades here away.
6735: Some pine nuts lie scattered upon the ground.

The call of the adventurer, that which has claimed so many people, sings loudly in your heart. Taking on the obvious dangers here, you explore further into the depths of the forest. The canopy of thick branches and leaves gives the impression of being in a living cavern, with growing stalagmites holding up the ceiling. Combat skills honed to perfection, you brandish your weapon and continue inwards.
6736: Summoning all of your courage, you enter the centre of the forest. The darkness here is complete, smothering both light and mind in its evil embrace. Your feeble torches only bring out shadows and indistinct forms. Even more chilling, is that these forms are moving, seeking you out to destroy you. Readying your weapons, you prepare yourself for battle.
6738: Peering towards the east, all you see are countless trees growing high above you. No access to the interior is visible, despite the growing curiosity about what lies in there. In this deep wilderness, expect no mercy from the inhabitants, and you check you weapon's readiness to be sure of yourself.
6739: Moving along as best you can among the roots, you struggle from tree to tree. No real path seems to exist here, at least none you can tell. The thick ground covering only serves to confuse your dulled senses, and the unknown, unseen threat serves to fray your once steel nerves. One might consider leaving here while they can.
6740: A brutish forest troll is hunting here, looking for some tasty flesh.

Standing here, you see more of the same. Impressive trunks of ancient wood arching high above you, with their canopy of branches and leaves forming a ceiling as dark as stone. Strange sounds echo through the tree tops, even as the padding of many paws is muffled by the thick, spongy layer of dirt and wet leaves. By now, you can't tell which way might get you out of this incredible forest.
6741: A ferocious warg is here, snarling angrily.

Finally! A small path is visible to the east, leading to an even deeper section of this immense wood. The inky blackness lends no clues to what lies there, but you are tempted to brave the unknown anyway. For those of faint heart, access is open to the west, away from the beating heart of the canopied forest.
6742: A brutish forest troll is hunting here, looking for some tasty flesh.

Plunging into the depths, you step into part of the forest which throbs with a malevolent force. This is an evil forest, and you sense a desire to kill you and all your kind, and let the land be covered in living darkness. A rugged path is to the east, but you doubt you could manage to come back that way. The trees don't seem quite as vibrant, consumed by the driving power which preys on your sanity.
6743: A sturdy plant grows to a height of almost a yard.

Nearing the heart of the mighty wood, you sense the evil pulsing with around you. The canopy of leaves and branches holds in the darkness and spite, concentrating it more towards the centre. Indistinct sounds are heard from every and yet no direction. The atmosphere smothers your courage, and fear for your life.
6744:
A sturdy plant grows to a height of almost a yard.
A brutish forest troll is hunting here, looking for some tasty flesh.

Passage is difficult here, due to the thick, warped roots and massive trunks of hardwood trees. Pine and oak trees dominate the view, with the occasional spruce or even cedar tree breaking the pattern. The moist leaves on the ground mask your steps, as well as that of any possible predators. Perhaps a little exploration will yield the secrets of this dark wood, and with luck reap the rewards.
6745:
A brutish forest troll is hunting here, looking for some tasty flesh.
A disgusting forest troll is searching for fresh meat here.
A brutish forest troll is hunting here, looking for some tasty flesh.

Being here is an obvious decision to assuage your curiosity and probe further into the depths of this primeval landscape. Moving silently as possible, you scan the darkness around you for the telltale gleam of a predator's eye. The smell of leaves fills your head, causing your vision to blur slightly. To your hazy thoughts, combat would be a good way to clear your mind.
6746: This far into the forest, the trees become more than just towers of living wood. A faint feeling of awareness emanates around you, perhaps due to your jangled nerves. The network of trees and roots makes passage difficult, and you are afraid of losing your way if not careful. Several paths seem to lead away, but you cannot tell which is the best one to take.
6747: A clear spring babbles as cool water trickles out of the ground.

Moving carefully among the thick trunks of countless trees, you have reached a bit of a cul-de-sac. The forest is so thick you cannot seem to manage to go anywhere but the way you came. Maybe there is an advantage to that, since any threat would have to come from the south. Finding the way out might be your next goal.
6748: You stand in an old long abandoned courtyard that served the inn whose ruins you can see to the west. To the south and east the forest grows thickly. To the north you see what appears to be an old road.
6749: A fallow deer is grazing peacefully here.

Standing here, you pause to admire the tall latticework of leaves and branches that form a twinkling ceiling of lights above. A trail through the edge of the forest is to the north, and more scattered trees lie to the south. The western edge of the forest is quite thick, so thick as to prevent access.
6750: A ferocious warg is here, snarling angrily.

This trail bridges various landscapes around you. To the south, old and decrepit hills sweep onwards into the distance. A vast moor lies to the east, eventually leading to the mighty Bruinen river. A forest of astounding height dominates the western skies, filling you with awe at such natural majesty. To the north, endless plains stretch beyond your sight. The choice is yours to which path will suit you best.
6751: This edge of the forest is quite lovely, with the tall branches of the oak and pine trees rising high above you. Their leaves and needles block out most of the light, but allow a sparkling display of colours to light the fallen leaves that muffle your steps. Quickly though, the forest becomes a mass of thick trunks and roots that block access to the west.
6752: This slope is covered with tall and healthy trees, rising high above your head. Their thick branches block most of the immediate light, bathing the area in soothing shade. Jarring your senses, though, is the less healthy trees to your immediate west, with greyish leaves and branches. The trees to the north are more healthy looking, tempting you to forget your adventuresome instincts.
6753: The northern edge of these hills lies against the vast forest around you. Greyish grass and brush covers the sides, in sharp contrast to the verdant green of the treetops. However, you can't help but note that the two are somehow connected, and that appearances are not always true indicators.
6754: These hills, lower than the rest of the surrounding ones, force you to view only the greyish grass and bushes that grow here. All of your instincts tell you that something is very wrong here, and to leave as soon as possible.
6755: Northern Wall of a Green Valley

A wide, deep, green-covered valley descends southeastwards, to the encounter of the snaking waters of the Bruinen. A range of overlapping, small shoulders form this majestic, northern edge. Their worn peaks look like half-ruined battlements in a gigantic wall that cuts the icy, northerly wind off from the fertile valley floor. Further south, the other wall rises timidly above the plains that mark the landscape in the distance.
6756: A black crow flies low to the ground here, looking for carrion to eat.

Sheltered from the frozen, devastating wind from the mountains, the bottom of this deep vale looks in all its splendour. Here and there, small copses of leafy trees stand, surrounded by short, thick, wet grass growing all about. The murmur of running water mingles with the soft whisper of the fluttering, dark-green leaves, like an endless melody that repeats once and again. The dale opens as it draws closer to the riverbed, as if trying to embrace it.
6757: Near the Meeting of the Branches

The course of the river leads mostly straight here, and the flow hastens. On the eastern bank, a sheer cliff of bare rock raises above the waters, not that high yet vertically. And it seems to flank the stream, like a motionless bodyguard of cold stone. The waters pass by gently, almost noiselessly, along the grey wall, as if softly caressing it.
6758: Bend in the North Fork of the Bruinen

Looking through the limpid, crystalline water, one can clearly glimpse the rocky bottom of the riverbed, littered in boulders of all sizes. At dusk, when the westering sunlight falls aslant over the river, the mirror-like surface shines in bright orange shades. But when the nights are clear, the silvery gleam of the moon and the stars shimmers in the apparently asleep, whispering waters.
6759: Cold and quiet run the waters of the Bruinen, winding along the foothills of the Misty Mountains, and opening their way through the abrupt valleys and the stony crags. The elven people call this river Bruinen, but it was best known as Loudwater among the men that inhabited these lands long ago. And so it is still called by their descendants, although none of them dwell in this rough region any longer.
6760: A Bend in the North Fork of the Bruinen

Even in the sunniest summer days, the waters always remain icy to the touch. Upstream in the Misty Mountains, among recondite canyons, are the riverbasins of the Bruinen. And their waters come from the thawing snow that crowns the everlasting white peaks, that reach out towards the sky, like white fingers trying to touch it.
6761: The terrain undulates in this area, with large outcrops of rock that appear to spring forth out of the very ground, as if expelled by some unknown power. These stony protuberances are more numerous the closer to the river, like a levee built by the capricious forces of nature. In all other directions, the ridges give way to small hillocks, and those to old, worn hills, their smooth silhouettes outlined against the horizon.
6762: As the waters come down from the mountains, the flow becomes slower, although mightier too. The frequent waterfalls and rapids have been left behind, as well as the narrow gorges with upright walls of living rock. And so have the white waters embroidered with spray, rushing through the sharp-edged stones of capricious shapes. Here, among the foothills, the stream runs lazily and quietly, as if taking a break after the thrilling descent.
6763: North Branch by a Gravelly Riverbank

In this section, the high cliffs of stone draw back on the eastern bank, as they give way to a beach dotted with pebbles. Nevertheless, the tall stone walls do not disappear, but they stand equally sheer a bit further inland, maybe hinting a different course of the river in the past. With every gust of the wind, little waves go and fade at the gravelly beach with a soft rubbing sound.
6764: This lonely hill rises sharply into the sky, giving you a decent view of the rather uninspiring land. A huge forest attracts your attention to the north east, giving you an eventual path to go and explore. From here, the only way to go is back to the north, and follow the hills downwards to the lower area or south into a green valley.
6765: Though the hills all around are covered by tall grass and brush, the plants are all of an unhealthy grey hue. Northward, the hills diminish, worn by the endless passage of time. To the east, the hills rise and fall, like a sea of grey-green plants, all rolling in the same tide. Southwest of here, a green valley seems to beckon, offering perhaps a respite from these bleak hills, and to the west and northwest, a massive forest dominates the land.
6766: At this point, the hills are worn and aged. The same grey grass that covers the rugged and brooding hills to the south is here, but not as thick. The huge forest right to the west seems to wear down these hills, taking over the immediate land. The hills are even more worn to the north, but they seem safer than the overpowering forest.
6767: These hills are quite low, almost non-existent. The most prominent feature of them being a part of the larger ones to the south is the bleached grass that covers the ground here. The will of these hills is gone, destroyed by time and the more recent pressures of the vast and incredible forest to the west.
6768: A trail picks its way carefully through the sparse vegetation growing stubbornly from the rocky ground. The air is still and heavy, effectively sucking the life out of the already dreary landscape. In the distance to the west, a large forest lines the horizon. The trail effectively disappears to the east, leaving you to find your own path to walk on.
6769: The thick pine trees form an unbroken canopy above you. Their smooth unbroken trunks rise to a great height and then spread out into thick crowns. The ground is covered with decaying pine needles and dark stones that have a slimy appearance. The usual fresh smell of pine needles seems to be lost in pervading climate of darkness and decay. You hear the murmur of water to the west and you sense a towering presence to the north.
6770:
A large mean-looking troll is here.
A large mean-looking troll is here.

The thick pine trees form an unbroken canopy above you. Their smooth unbroken trunks rise to a great height and then spread out into thick crowns. The ground is covered with decaying pine needles and dark stones that have a slimy appearance. The usual fresh smell of pine needles seems to be lost in pervading climate of darkness and decay. You hear the murmur of water to the west and you sense a towering presence to the north.
6771:
A ferocious warg is here, snarling angrily.
A large earth troll is digging here, looking for some tasty morsels.
A small, mean earth troll is standing here, thinking of something hideous.
A large earth troll is digging here, looking for some tasty morsels.

The tunnel grows narrow and cramped as it squeezes through the bedrock, trying, apparently in vain, to ply its way east. To the west it opens out somewhat, and the air in that direction seems fresher, though hung with an overtaste of decay.
6772: Cramped and dark, this tunnel would be enough to strike terror into the mind of anyone with claustrophobia. The walls stand at a slight angle, leaning toward one another at the top, as if falling in upon you, and the uneven and pitted floor makes progress through the area quite perilsome. However, a soft but steady breeze from the east seems to promise relief in that direction.
6773: The large rock face to the south has deprived the trees here of sunlight. In the resulting shadow they have decayed and rotted, some with the sweet sickly odour of death, others with the gnarled withered contortion of lightless old age. From somewhere westward, the muted gurgle of water can be heard.
6774: Some ugly blow-flies are buzzing around here.

Here a slow stagnant stream laden with the detritus of the dead forest vanishes abruptly beneath the rock face. You can hear the echoing water in the spaces of the rock as it flows southward on its hidden journey. There is a glimpse of sky here which serves to depress rather than to cheer.
6775: A huge, poisonous spider is here.

The large rock face to the south has deprived the trees here of sunlight. In the resulting shadow they have decayed and rotted, some with the sweet sickly odour of death, others with the gnarled withered contortion of lightless old age. You sense evil. You shiver. East you hear the muted gurgle of water. North a large spire of rock pushes its way above the forest.
6776: A huge olog-hai troll is here staring blankly at you.

Before you is a branching of ways. In one direction a broad, though rough- hewn tunnel cuts into the cold, hard rock. To the north, however, the digging seems to have failed, for it appears that the tunnel does not proceed much further that way. Lastly, you might choose to follow a narrow and low-roofed passageway to the east, from whence a slight cool breeze drifts in.
6777: At the Slopes of a Rocky Outcropping

You find yourself at the northeastern edge of a massive rocky outcropping, which rears high and sombre above you. Leaving the area shadowed from the best of the sunlight, but exposed to the bitter northern winds of winter, the hill has rendered this part of the woodland stunted and sickly.
6778: The large rock face to the south has deprived the trees here of sunlight. In the resulting shadow they have decayed and rotted, some with the sweet sickly odour of death, others with the gnarled withered contortion of lightless old age. Somehow this place exudes an aura of evil.
6779:
The starving cow stands here looking for a patch of grass.
A demon wolf lurks here, its dark form twisting and hiding its shape.

You stand in a field behind an old deserted ruin. The forest grows densely to the east and west. South you see a clearing. The field is littered with decayed remnants of carriages and wine casks. Southwest of here you see the large mass of rock that dominates the landscape.
6780: You are inside an old abandoned inn. The walls have all decayed away and the chief remaining structure is the central chimney. You see the broken old fireplace which seems to contain some bones. All else is ruin and decay.
6781: A furry, striped raccoon is here, nosing around for some berries or roots.

Here on the elevated ground the vegetation grows sparsely in what light the huge rock mass to the south allows it to have. The slopes are riddled with huge depressions some filled with rocks and massive boulders. There is life here and on the breeze a faint odour of decay.
6782: Here on the elevated ground the vegetation grows sparsely in what light the huge rock mass to the south allows it to have. The slopes are riddled with huge depressions some filled with rocks and boulders. The air reeks of some nauseating stench and on the ground you see large bestial tracks.
6783: A clear spring babbles as cool water trickles out of the ground.

Here the stream is born. Between the hills on the east and the lonely sentinel of the rock spire on the right the water comes bubbling fresh and clean from the earth. Northward you see an old trail and to the south the shadows deepen.
6784: The tunnel has become smaller but still shows signs of having been used recently. The air is still foul and disgusting but the roof of the tunnel is cracked and broken. Here and there soil and water seeps through and drops onto the tunnel floor.
6785: A skeleton of some humanoid lies in the dust.

Though the cave is fairly small, its air feels fairly fresh and cool, with a slightly wet and metallic tang, presumably due to the mineral-rich waters of the underground stream, which makes its sluggish way across one end. It is not clear where the water originates, because it flows so slowly that it is almost stagnant.
6786:
There are two water lilies here.
A trout swims here.
A trout swims here.
A trout swims here.
A ferocious warg is here, snarling angrily.

A fairly large pond of water pools here, behind a roughly formed dam of heavy tree trunks. With its sluggish flow stopped entirely, the water has become quite stagnant here, and a thick scum of algae floats upon its dark surface.
6787: Here on the northern shore of the pond, a small shelf of dry land arcs around the waters, clinging to a sheer rockface, which rears above you to the north. The ground slopes sharply down into the pool, but here and there you can see large depressions.
6788:
A large earth troll is digging here, looking for some tasty morsels.
A large earth troll is digging here, looking for some tasty morsels.
A small, mean earth troll is standing here, thinking of something hideous.

Three tunnels meet here, branching off to the north, the east and the west. From the west can be heard a faint sound of running water, whilst from the north a slight yet perceptible breeze drifts in, carrying with it not only the promise of fresh air, but also an undercurrent of decay.
6789: Here a rough spartan quarters has been burrowed into the rock. There is filth and garbage everywhere. All around you the shattered possessions of the former occupants lie in untidy heaps. A single tunnel exits this area, and it appears that attempts to dig onward in the opposite direction met with failure, as the roof has crumbled in at that end of the chamber.
6790: This corner of the canyon bends to the north and east, forming a right angle with the incredibly high walls. The air is still and tense, making you jump at the slightest sound. This leads to the Trollshaws, tempting your will to fight with your instinct to survive.
6791:
A tall plant with a perfectly smooth stem gracefully marks the landscape.
A tall plant with a perfectly smooth stem gracefully marks the landscape.
A tall plant with a perfectly smooth stem gracefully marks the landscape.

From this vantage point, all you can see are sheets of rock rising a hundred feet above you. A sense of vertigo briefly distracts you due to the height. Jarring your observations is the constant danger that lurks here, since you are not in a land where the weak survive.
6792: Sloping downwards slightly, this valley of stone leads you onwards to the eventual bottom of the canyon. To get there, you would have to climb down a steep slope, but you think the trip would be safe enough. The faint smell of excrement hangs in the air, forcing you to cover your nose as you check the readiness of your weapons.
6793: This corner of the canyon bends from the east to the north. The sheer southern canyon wall gives you an idea just how far down you are, and you briefly contemplate what would happen if you had fallen off from the top. With a start, the realization sinks in that this is part of the dreaded Trollshaws, and as such a very real danger exists here. A faint smell of offal hangs in the air; a reminder to keep alert.
6794: This point is definitely at the bottom of the surrounding landscape. Up to the east is a large bowl of rock, and to the south is the massive stone wall of the canyon. To the north, the other side is too tall to allow climbing, allowing progress either onward down the valley or back to the crater.
6795: Despite the nearness to the rocky edge of the deep canyon, the forest is still quite thick. Tall and healthy oaks, pines, aspens, and other trees grow abundantly, blocking even most of the site of the terrain to the north. If you wish to explore down there, a rain trail to the east looks usable, but it is quite steep.
6796: North of the trail which winds its way by the canyon and forest, this edge is still very thick. The deep canyon forbids travel to the north, confounding your curiosity about what might lie down there. The forest stretches a bit further to the east, barely thin enough to allow travel.
6797: Forming a large rim, the bowl of rock here prevents you from looking out over the canyon basin that is to the west. A path can be picked out that way, so with a little effort, you can make your way there carefully. The centre of the bowl is damp from the frequent drainage from the large rain trail to the south, but the porous rock prevents you from taking a drink there.
6798: This trail plunges steeply downwards into the rocky valley below. The only reason you can travel here at all is because of the fact that the rains over the years have carved a workable path through the stone itself, as it drains from the fertile land to the south.
6799: A ferocious warg is here, snarling angrily.

On the northern edge of the forest, you notice the healthy if scattered trees around here. This is where the forest ends and the rocky canyon region begins to take over. Looking carefully, perhaps a trail exists to the north which is safe enough to travel down, if one wishes to explore to the north.
6800: A ferocious warg is here, snarling angrily.

This northern edge of the forest is comprised of tall and healthy spruce, oak, and pine trees. Though the trees themselves are loosely growing here, the fallen leaves are sufficient to provide a blanket that covers the ground and softens your footsteps.
6801: You are meandering through the moors of the Bruinen. The land is rough and hilly, covered with wildly sprawling vegetation and thick ground cover, dry as it is. There are no signs of wildlife. The air is still and sombre.
6802: On the western edge of the moor, you see the beginnings of a large canyon to the west. Everywhere else is just more of the same morose land. The air, calm and dry, hangs heavily over this uninspiring land.
6803: Exploring along the western edge of the moor, you walk along dry and infertile land. All that grows here is weeds and other rank plant life. The air, despite the presence of the Bruinen a bit to the east, is dry and calm, leaving a sense of despair in the land.
6804: Spreading out from the western side of the Bruinen, this western edge of the moor presents a depressing view. Occasional vegetation juts up from the rocky terrain, despite the size of the nearby river. To the east, you see more of the same land and vegetation. A large canyon lies far to the west.
6805: On and on, the plains lead northwards. Much further are the infamous Ettenmoors whose name has been known to fill many stout hearts with fear. No sounds of wildlife can be heard here, with not even a breeze to move the tall, dry grass that grows all around you.
6806: You are meandering through the high moors of the Bruinen. The land is rough but mostly flat in all directions, covered with wildly sprawling vegetation in earthen colours. The travelling is slow with no paths to follow, bounded by some impassable shrub to the north. You hear the sound of flowing water coming from the east.
6807: You are meandering through the high moors of the Bruinen. The land is rough, covered with wildly sprawling vegetation that makes the going difficult. Here the moors slope down to meet the river Bruinen to the east, making a passable ford to the fertile plains on the other side.
6808: You are meandering through the high moors of the Bruinen. The land is rough as it gradually slopes down from its heights to the level of the fertile plain across the river to the east. The travelling is difficult due to the sprawling brush and undergrowth.
6809: You are meandering through the high moors of the Bruinen. The land is rough but mostly flat in all directions, covered with wildly sprawling vegetation in earthen colours. The moors stretch northwards and eastwards to a spur of the river Bruinen.
6810: You are meandering through the high moors of the Bruinen. The land is rough but mostly flat in all directions but west, though the wildly sprawling vegetation makes travelling a bit difficult. The air is still and sombre except for a faint sound of rushing water from the east. To the west a sparse forest starts up, populated thinly by healthy spruce oak and pine trees.
6811: A fierce boar is here, making grunting noises.

You are meandering through the high moors of the Bruinen. The land is rough but mostly flat, towering over the river which bends its way north at the eastern edge of the moor. Across the river hills rise in response, but flatten out further to the north into a fertile plain.
6812: You are meandering through the high moors of the Bruinen. The land is rough but mostly flat in all directions, overgrown with wildly sprawling vegetation in earthen colours. The moors stretch northward bounded only by the gurgling Bruinen to the east.
6813: You are meandering through the high moors of the Bruinen. The land is rough but mostly flat in all directions, covered with wildly sprawling earthen vegetation. The going is hard and the only sounds are that of rushing water far to the east.

6815: You are meandering through the high moors of the Bruinen. The land is rough but mostly flat in all directions, hard to travel through due to the wild overgrowth. To the east the rushing of the river can be heard, the only sound in the sombre air.

6817: This lonely hill, covered with a small wood, stands between the dark forest and the river. Here stands a copse, comprised of obviously ancient oak trees, whose gnarled roots stand proud of the ground in places. Four miles east of here an archway can be seen soaring into the sky. It joins the moors on either side of the river. Far to the east, the towering Misty Mountains can be seen, with their many snow-covered peaks.
6818: This stretch of high moors is bounded to the east by the river Bruinen, which flows along a gorge several feet below. Though possible, it would be dangerous to leap into the rushing waters, and the current appears strong enough to sweep you several miles downstream. Northwards a small bluff overlooks the river, where a majestic rock arch soars high into the sky, bridging the moorland to either side of the watercourse.
6819: After walking past the archway through a rather flat area, you find yourself on the top of a small cliff. Looking down from the top there is the riverbed of the Bruinen. Onwards, the tunnel continues, a gaping maw carved in the very ground of Arda. Roots stick out from all directions, as well as the blind eyes of very large earthworms. The thick rancid smell of troll pervades the tunnel, leaving no doubts as to who carved this path.
6847: This tunnel is actually quite large for one beneath the ground. The thick dirt and debris indicate you are not far from the surface, yet you feel closed in by the dark, uneven surfaces.
6848: Pieces of dirt and rock filter down from the ceiling, covering your head or helmet in its filth. Large, splayed footprints lead both ways, and a rancid, metallic smell dominates your senses.
6849: A small, mean earth troll is standing here, thinking of something hideous.

This tall and narrow passage is dug out of hard, rich dirt. Aside from occasional pangs of claustrophobia, you manage to walk fairly easily through here. The air is full of the rich smell of fresh loam, mixed in with the bitter odor of troll excrement. Up ahead to the north, the passage becomes more of stone, with more dirt to the south.
6850: The corpse of an earth troll is lying here.

Bending from the south to the west, the tunnel is completely made of stone. The walls, floor, and ceiling appear to have been crudely mined from the application of more strength than skill or tools. The only things you know of with the will and strength to do this are the trolls that inhabit the lands around here. A foul smell of troll sweat hangs in the air and makes your eyes water. Time to move on.

This section of the tunnel ends abruptly into a smooth wall of stone. The tunnel has many rough sections along the ceiling and walls, and the air is heavy with the smell of some foul odor. Along the northern wall, there is a huge rock which might be moved with great strength.
6852: A large earth troll is digging here, looking for some tasty morsels.

Moving along this narrow and tall passage, you brush up against roots and other plant parts protruding from the hard-packed dirt. Fears about a cave in are not that high, as the roots themselves hold all the dirt in place. Obviously, trolls dug this passage out, and have been using it frequently. The acrid smell of troll fills your nose and makes your eyes water.
6853: Sloping slightly downwards, the tunnel makes its way further and further along from south to north. Strange sounds echo hollowly through here, mostly muffled by the earthy walls. You brush aside a large root with annoyance as you contemplate getting out of here as quickly as possible, before the stench of troll forces you to vomit.
6854: The corpse of an earth troll is lying here.

Onwards, this irregular tunnel moves along under the massive trunks above. It bends from the west to the north, seemingly ignoring any roots that might have been growing here. The marks of crude cuts line some of the bigger roots, testimony to the strength and purpose of the makers. Splayed footprints line the dirt floor, with the occasional bone or excrement as well. You hurry along to escape this foul place.
6855: The corpse of a large earth troll is lying here.

Your senses stay alert to the danger that lies down these parts.

The smell of troll droppings is enough by itself to warrant your departure, but the inhabitants have other ideas.

There are some crude steps cut into the wall to help one to climb out of here.

The downward slope of the tunnel has increased! You lose your footing here and there but manage to maintain your balance. You begin to wonder if the slope of the tunnel will continue to get steeper, and if it is wise to continue onward into the darkness.

6898: The sloping passageway continues on, sloping down from south to north. It's walls, ceiling and floor are made of rough, packed earth. It appears that these tunnels were dug out by great hands. The air in here is stale and damp, due to the lack of sunlight.

The walls of the passageway are much rougher here than farther south. It seems as if the packed earth leads into a rock to the north. This appears to be a crest in the passage - both north and south it begins to fall. The ceiling is low as well - the trolls that evidently inhabit this place surely must find it uncomfortable. There is a predominant stench in the air, making breathing very difficult.
