You enter a dark, smelly tunnel. A rank odor of rotting flesh is carried by a light breeze from somewhere inside the dark entrance.
6914:
The remains of a swarm of blow-flies lie here.
The corpse of a bloodthirsty bat is lying here.
Some ugly blow-flies are buzzing around here.
Travel on this little stairway is difficult. Assorted rocks have been thrown together to make a rough stairway. The light of a torch to the east shows a little, empty room.
6915: As you enter this room, the smell of decaying flesh hits you in the face. You see to the north and south what looks to be piles of dead bodies and stripped carcasses.
6916:
There are five half-rotten corpses here.
There are five rotten corpses here.
A bloodthirsty bat is sleeping here, hanging from the ceiling.
A bloodthirsty bat is sleeping here, hanging from the ceiling.
A demon wolf lurks here, its dark form twisting and hiding its shape.
You are now walking upon piles of dead bodies... Are you sick?
6917:
The corpse of an elven slave is lying here.
The corpse of an elven slave is lying here.
A prisoner is sitting here, looking at you with sad eyes.
You can hardly walk through this disgusting, reeking, little cave. Ragged people beg and claw at you as if there was no hope for life. Rats run rampant over decaying corpses and litter.
6918: You have no idea what you have climbed into. The tree has been eaten, is being eaten, by hordes of small worms. Each excretes a thin weblike strand behind it. The smell the creatures make is horrid, as if some airborne toxin was setting off alarms in your nose.
6919:
A small campfire burns here, its low flames giving off only a little light.
A pan is here, ready for use.
A half-rotten corpse is hanging here.
A beer barrel has been left here.
A water barrel has been left here.

The walls of this cave are blackened by soot from many fires and covered by crude carvings and dried blood. Bone splinters and small patches of cloth lie on the hard earthen floor, along with wads of partially digested hair and a broken wagon wheel. In the north-eastern corner of this cave stands a makeshift bed of straw and pieces of cloth.
6921:
A wooden chest stands in the corner.
A rotten corpse is hanging here.
A half-rotten corpse is hanging here.

The walls of this cave are jagged and cracked, as if somebody would have created with open space in the hill with sheer force. The granite is dark grey and spotted with dried blood-stains. The floor is rocky here, tiny streams of water trickle between the small rocks to the lower eastern cave.
6923:
A forest-green cloak lies here, concealing the ground beneath (glows blue).
A dagger lies on the ground.
A pool of thick, red liquid covers a section of the ground.
A skull is here, spiked to the end of a pole.

This small area looks like a valley within the valley. The ground dips into a rocky bowl, overgrown by thorny brambles and patches of moss. To the north an opening in the side of the huge hill can be seen, dark and sinister. All sounds are muffled here, and no birds can be heard. A few sets of huge footprints are set in the mossy ground, leading towards the stonedoor set in a rockface to the west.
6924: Troubled Waters South of a Ford

Even here, a mile downstream from the ford, there is still a lot of turbulence in the water. Strong underwater currents zigzag through the rock-strewn bottom, forming dangerous-looking whirlpools in the surface. But little by little the streambed deepens, and the flow slows down. Here the river takes a sharp turn to the west, avoiding the upright walls of a protruding ridge.
6925: Like all along the eastern shore of the Bruinen, the terrain ascends steeply as it goes away from the waters, among large, grey boulders darkened by the moisture. All sorts of weeds and bushes grow in the hollows of the rocks, and so do tangled brambles with prickles all over. The western face offers only a sheer drop down to the waters, as though these had thoroughly scratched the riverbed over the years. But on the north, it seems feasible to approach the stream, although the descent doesn't look easy at all.
6926: A sturdy pack horse is standing here.

A low ridge rises by the stream, overlooking its course for many miles. Its top looks mostly level, as if flattened by the abundant rains in the region throughout countless years. However, there are small hollows and holes in the rock, where dark water gathers in small ponds. Nevertheless, the crag bends over the waters to the northwest, like a half-built bridge, or maybe merely like a thick pillar of stone whose base has been thrashed by the troubled waters of the river.
6927: The terrain continues to ascend, from the valley floor through which the river flows up to some escarp bluffs towering in the distant east. The ground is mostly covered in patches of thick, tussocky grass. There are small copses of high firs as well, their pointy tops climbing up to the sky. Their dark-green leaves shake in the wind, filling the dale with a deep whisper. A faint scent emanates from those leaves, impregnating the air.
6928: Here too, the crystalline current of the Bruinen runs unapproachable along a deep cutting several feet below. The ground drops steeply in an uneven wall of rock dampened by the mists that hang over the water. Brambles and briars fill any tiny gap among the stones covered in thick, green moss. Below, the waters flow swiftly, singing loudly as they pass by the rock faces.
6929: A Path along a Steep, Brown Bank

A stony trail climbs this steep incline, the first one off the stream in these folded lands. The hillside shows the dun colour of matted earth, sprinkled with pebbles and boulders here and there, as if carried along and then left by a flood of the river. Perhaps for that same reason, only a few thorny brambles grow here, their yellowish hues half-camouflaged by the ground.
6930: The pebbled trail ascending from the ford goes on snaking uphill, apparently trying to climb to the high ridges that tower imposingly in the further side of the vale, to the east. The overhung limbs of an occasional lonely tree standing by the wayside cast thin shadows upon it, but the landscape is mostly wild-grown and marked by shrubbery. Here a small track branches southwards, rather faded and overgrown, and dwindles away into the rough lands.
6931: The faint trail marked with white pebbles treads untiringly along the endless, bushy incline that climbs to the high moors. Those bluffs show faces of bare rock, like outliers of the distant Misty Mountains. And away over them, the very Hithaeglir reach up defiantly towards the sky, their bulky bodies of stone crowned in white, snowy peaks shrouded in clouds.
6932: Bend in the Path to the Misty Mountains

The trail continues to wind uphill, trying to reach the majestic bluffs that loom apparently unapproachable ahead, as if rooted out of the earth. When the moon rises on clear nights, a bluish-silvery glint shimmers in the rims of those high moors. But here the path snakes though deep brakes and prickly heather, and through fields of high grass, always along the steep slope. Despite its sinuous course, however, it seems to lead from west to north.
6933: Bend in the Path to the Misty Mountains

Always snaking among the briars and thorns, the track goes on imperturbably along the slope. At some spots it is no more than a half-faded trail, hardly distinguishable among the weeds. But in other places it looks rather better marked, with small white stones lying on both waysides. The countless turns and the thick brushwood make it hard to figure the course, but here it seems to bend sharply from south to east.
6934: A fallow deer is grazing peacefully here.

This section of the trail skirts around a wide depression to the south, where the ground becomes steep and slippery. Eastwards the terrain, the colour of heather and crumbling rock, rises slowly toward the feet of the mountains. The long line of the Bruinen can be seen glittering among banks of grey stone away to the north.
6935: The track meanders lazily amongst ivy-clad hillocks, following an east-west route. A yawning fissure opens to the south, dark and deep, so that one could neither jump over nor climb down into it. Past the fissures a ridge of hills rise, its heights broken into many bare points almost like the teeth of a blunted saw.
6936: In all these moors there is no sign of any dwelling: wild and tangled vegetation is all that covers the slightly undulating ground which stretches unchanged for miles in all directions. Half covered with moss or heather, small white stones show now and then where little footpaths depart from the main track. Most of them lead only to a dead-end among the hillocks though.
6937: A small brown snake is slithering around here.

You are now in the southern side of a wide vale. At times, thick mists like clouds of greyish vapour spread all over from the river at the bottom. But when the days are clear, one can easily see the ground ascending steadily eastwards for several miles, climbing up to some high, imposing moors. And there, among the towering bluffs, the dale narrows slowly into a gorge through which the Bruinen river flows like a trickle of silvery water.
6938: As almost all along the southern fork of the Bruinen, the river flows between cliff-like walls of rock, as if confined within a moat many feet below. Here the bank appears to be only slightly less steep. However, it may be possible to attempt a risky descent among the dangerously slippery rocks that spring from the very waters, like bulky sentinels of stone flanking the stream.
6939: A flat shelf paved with bare stone slopes very steeply into the Bruinen here, bearing the marks of aeons of erosion. A cliff borders the river not far to the east, although further to the south it gradually lowers. Thick brush can be seen peeking over the clifftop, and creepers cling to the wall in cracks and holes.
6940: The loud rippling of the water opening its way through the rocks, and the numerous, small falls command one's attention in this mostly straight section of the river. Both banks look extraordinarily steep, like a little gorge with walls of damp, living rock. The current is fast and foamy, but one can easily make out the rock-sprinkled streambed. Lots of leaves, sticks, and even small stones float by, carried away with the waters.
6941: The river runs westward here, clear and chilly between steep banks of grey stone. A few miles to the east a cliff rises up to flank the water, and further upstream the river disappears, swallowed in a vast rift among the hills. A green meadow spreads northward, until the foot of a ridge of rocky, bare hills that loom far in the distance. Downstream the river is joined by the other fork of the Bruinen, which flows in from the north.
6942: A sheer cliff to the north flanks the south fork of the Bruinen, which flows steadily past a few dozen yards below. Crossing the area is difficult as matted undergrowth covers the ground - brambles and creepers growing to the height of a man's waist - and not a single footpath can be found in this corner of the moors.
6943: A few barely noticeable tracks tread the moors, twisting through the thick vegetation. Most of them lead only to a dead end though, or to the cliff edge which overhangs a bend of the Bruinen. The river comes down from out of a rocky gorge to the north, foaming and churning, then slows and turns westward.
6944: To the north grass and weeds grow on a muddy bank, while on the other side the water is bordered by a tall cliff, which gradually lowers to the west. It was carved by the river over thousands of years, and still the process is going on: deep hollows form at its base and roots hang at its top, being exposed by the crumbling terrain. A few miles east the river seems to spew from a gorge in the moors.
6945: The water flows at speed through the gorge, eddying around a few large boulders that lie on its bed. It comes down with some speed from the north, and turns west under the shadow of the high cliffs, losing speed as the river widens. A few pine trees cling to the gorge walls on unreachable shelves halfway up, their roots hanging out from the rock.
6946: The edge of a ridge of hills lies to the south of here, and the soil becomes rocky and cracked as it rises toward them. A deep gully, so narrow a deer could almost leap over, blocks your way westward. Its sheer flanks are made of dark stone, and the glittering of water can be glimpsed at its bottom.
6947: A few withered shrubs manage to sprout out of the rare cracks in the ground here. To the west a flat extent of bare rock paves a massive promontory, the last branch of a ridge of hills. A noisy brook, at the bottom of a narrow and rocky gorge, can be seen below here to the east and south.
6948: A brook leaves a deep gorge and flows southward in the middle of a widening, green valley here. The only real sign of life is a small group of beeches, which manage to find cover under the face of the huge spur of rock bulging from the hill to the north. Heavy round stones litter the ground, obviously carried by the water, and grass and weeds grow amongst them.
6949: The rocky shoulder of the hill to the north comes down in huge steps to the level ground at the bottom of the dale. A few lofty fir trees rise among the lush grass, their twigs arching toward the ground, filling the air all around with their scent. Not far to the east, a brook hurries in its rocky bed, under the shadow of a huge cliff.
6951: A long, deep-green dale opens to the east, protected from the chill, northerly wind by a rank of old, crumbling hills. Patches of thick, wet grass carpet the valley sides, dying them in an uniform, light-green colour that contrasts with the blurry, deep shades in the trembling leaves of the scattered trees. But at dawn, when the day breaks and the light slowly broadens, the whole vale shines in the bright grey hues of dew.
6952: A thick brushwood covers the ground that in this area looks mostly level. The tangled weeds make progress somewhat harder, but they don't hinder the quite splendid views of the near surroundings. To the north and west the earth goes quickly lower towards the river flowing several miles below. A bit closer, a half-faded path zigzags through the rising fields, leading roughly southwards. On the east a deep vale ploughs the ground like a huge dike. To the south the plains stretch, but high grass slowly replaces the shrubs.
6953: The landscape around the worn path changes slowly as the leagues roll beneath your feet. To the south, the ground looks more and more fertile, and all sort of grasses grow exuberantly on the high plains. Conversely, a rocky soil seems to prevail on the north, covered mostly in heather and shrubbery. Here the trail takes a wide bend from north to west, always following the line of the Bruinen down in the lowlands.
6954: Like a thin, blurry shadow, at times strengthened, at other times diminishing, the path imitates the bends of the river. But with every step, it seems to draw slightly closer to the stream, as both go away snaking to the southwest. A protruding ridge stands directly to the west, forcing the path to take a sharp turn from east to south here. Beyond that bend, it disappears into the grasslands.
6955: A small, flat-topped pinnacle of rock stands in the path of the Bruinen river, forcing the stream to detour it. The waters bathe the northern and western faces, that look heavily broken and dangerously slippery. The other hillsides, on the contrary, descend gently into the uneven plains that stretch out in the distance, blending with them. A trail can be glimpsed cutting through the fields down there. Overlooking the river, a deep-green wood spreads to the very edge of a high embankment above the flow.
6956: Large, wet boulders covered in thick moss seem to sprout out of the riverside, forming a stony fence that blocks any attempt to reach the stream. The ground goes sharply lower to the edge of that cliff-like rockface above the waters. Here and there a lonely oak stands atop the rocky wall, stretching its limbs out over the grey barrier, like long fingers willing to cool off in the river.
6957: This narrow path cuts through the high, wild lands, leading southwards off from the Bruinen Vale. The trail looks rather faltering, at times clearly laid, at other times barely distinguishable, and difficult to follow. All in all, it seems to follow roughly the course of the river that flows calmly several miles below, on the west.
6958: The landscape rolls on in a myriad of folds, as though a giant among giants had tried to press the valley walls together, perhaps willing to close it. Small clumps of trees abound, with leaves fluttering in the wind and lofty trunks growing closely. But especially there are fields of fresh grass, a thick, wet, short grass, fibrous and rough to the touch, capable of enduring the harsh climate of this region.
6959: Edge of a Range of Hills

A row of small shoulders stretches eastwards, crowning the southern wall of the Bruinen Vale that lies to the north. Their broken peaks stand out starkly against the horizon, especially at dusk, when the slanting light wanes and shadows spread. On the south, another dale cuts deeply through the country, much narrower but also richer in vegetation.
6961: All around here lies a folded and broken land. No trees grow on these bleak hills, but shrubs and some ivy grow where cover can be found against the wind. At this point the hills seems to have been cloven apart, and a small canyon falls to the north between sheer walls. Southwards the ground falls, in huge steps, towards a wide valley far below: from there comes the noise of water and the scent of trees.
6962: A tiny rivulet trickles among moss-covered stones at the bottom of this narrow cleft, so deep and dark that the lowest part is never enlightened by the sun. It comes from the south, where the ground rises steeply, and turns sharply to the west. Twenty yards of dark, smooth and slightly undercut stone tower on its sides: there is no way up.
6963: The ground here sinks well below the level of the surrounding area, forming a bowl-shaped depression. Water comes from a gully that opens in a low cliff on its eastern side, and collects in a muddy pool at the bottom. Surprisingly, grass, weeds and flowers grow bright and tall on the wet and spongy ground. On all sides the depression is surrounded by muddy, slippery banks.
6964: A patch of moss grows here on a wet, flat stone.

A deep and dark fissure begins here, flanked on either side by high walls, and descends northwards, widening slightly and getting deeper. Still it is possible to climb up out of the gully, as cracks in the walls provide good hand-holds. A small rill gushes out of a crack in the rock, and trickles slowly among dark slippery stones at the bottom.
6965: This is the western edge of the moors, surrounded by the river to the north, west, and south, like a last outpost of the elevated lands. In contrast, the bluffs extend eastwards in a long procession as far as the eye can reach. An abrupt cliff to the north and west frowns over the upper branch of the Bruinen, while the lower fork glitters below, directly to the south. The cliffs look crumbling and broken, towering upright above the unreachable waters.
6966: Although the moor isn't as high here as a bit further eastwards, there is still quite a drop down to the troubled waters of the Bruinen, to the south. Away over the river, a steep bank gives way to a markedly ascending ground. The raised flatlands stretch away in all other directions, but on the north and mainly the west they do so only for a couple miles, until they meet the bordering course of the river.
6967: A green meadow lies between the forks of the Bruinen to the south and west. Among the grass and flowers, a few tall fir trees rise near the stony banks, nourished by the river waters. The terrain becomes poor and dry at the top of the high moors that rise northward, and only a few heather plants manage to grow there.
6968: Yellow flowers, with grey-green foliage, grow in clusters here.

The terrain slopes gently to the south, down to the river where the tracks of small animals can be seen among the grass and weeds that grow in the soft mud. Eastwards the bank rises higher and the impetuous current foams in the rocky bed, pressed on by towering walls of stone. The river leaves your sight further up the valley, where it comes roaring in from the north.
6969: As the valley narrows again the river churns and hurdles over rocks, and you are flung and battered in almost every direction. Water is everywhere, and the force of it is irresistible. You are hurtled downstream at increasing speed. At one of the few points you are above water you catch a brief glimpse of the steep walls of the gorge, and realise that the only way out is downstream.
6970: Atop a Cliff in the Moors
The enchanting will-of-the-wisp beckons you with a blurred light.

The high moor comes to a sudden end in an escarp cliff above the river, as though the very water had cut it like a knife with a frozen, shifting blade. Here the ground shows an ashen grey colour, and pebbles abound. But hardly anything manages to grow here, except the occasional brownish heather. A bit off south, the elevated bluff extends westwards, like a long finger of cold, barren stone.
6971: A large rabbit looks peacefully at you, ready to dart away.

This is the western edge of a ridge of rocky hills that extends eastward in a long procession as far as your sight can reach. An abrupt cliff to the west frowns over the upper branch of the Bruinen, while the lower fork glitters far away to the south. The cliff is crumbling and broken to the north, falling towards a pebbled beach a many dozen yards below.
6972: All around here lies a rough and folded land; thick vegetation sprawls wildly and not a copse or a solitary tree rises to break the undulating line of the horizon. Southwards the Bruinen cleaves the country in a wide gorge, and near its banks, the land becomes less harsh - grass, weeds, and green bushes grow there on the sloping ground.
6973: A wide stretch of terrain lies between the river and the cliff that marks the western edge of the high moors. In ages past it was the bed of the river, when the rock was carved smooth and sheer by the water. Southwards the cliff is broken and crumbling, yet it seems not possible to find a way up.
6974: This is the bank of the Bruinen, which runs just to the west of here. The river is wide and deep, making it a formidable barrier. No plant life grows on the pebbled ground that is the river bank, but a few weeds can be seen at the base of a cliff that slopes very steeply up to the east. The bank proceed further southward.
6975: A mountain mule is standing here, ridden by you.

This elevated place provides a good view over the course of the river: it flows many hundred feet below between pebbled beaches, forming a wide arc from the north to the west. A huge fissure opens eastward in the rocky and barren soil, its flanks made of dark crumbling rock.
6976: The north fork of the Bruinen cleaves its way through the moors west of here, with high cliffs flanking its course northward for many miles. A few withered plants grow in this windswept place, while eastward, where the ground dips in a shallow dell, bushes and high grass cover the terrain.
6977: Small footpaths tread over the brush-covered hills that spread in almost every direction from here. Their journey is erratic and studded with forks though, and most of them lead only to a sheer cliff to the south. At the bottom of the gorge the Bruinen hurries along, sprinkling and foaming around the stones, and the rushing of water echoes up from the valley. Imposing spurs of rock thrust southwards from the cliff, screening the valley further upstream from your view.
6978: The ground dips to form a shallow depression, filled with roots, bushes, and rocks hidden among the high grass. Here and there some huge boulder sticks out of the vegetation, probably fallen from the crumbling flanks of a large cleft to the north. The rising ground blocks your sight in every direction; maybe there is a better view at the top of a hillock that rises east of here.
6979: You are in a huge cleft in the hills, well below the level of the surrounding land. To the east a scree climbs up to the moors, looking like a river of white stones. The bottom of the rift here is studded with broken rocks, fallen from the scree or the cleft walls. Still some vegetation, mainly whin and brambles, manages to grow in the dry soil.
6980: A sturdy pack horse is standing here.

You are meandering through the moors of the Bruinen. The land is rough and hilly, covered with wildly sprawling vegetation and thick ground cover, dry as it is. There are no signs of wildlife. The area here dips below the level of the hills and you cannot make out much of your surrounding area, although to the south you can see a crumbled rift in the moors.
6981: The river Bruinen runs northeasterly-southwesterly through the moors which rise up on the east side of the bank. To the west a sudden copse of trees appears. The air is still and quiet, punctuated only by an occasional low howl from the moors.
6982: The river Bruinen runs northeasterly-southwesterly through the moors which rise up to great heights on either side of the crystal waters. The air is still and quiet, punctuated only by an occasional low howl from the moors.
6983: The river Bruinen runs from the northeast to the southwest through the moors. The smooth, crystal water flows silently, the only sound being an occasional howl from beyond the shores of the moors.
6984: A small grove of trees has sprung up here fighting with the moors to the north and the river to the east for survival. The trees are densely packed and provide excellent protection from the elements. Huge, gnarled roots extend down and into the river to the east.
6985: The river Bruinen runs northeasterly-southwesterly through the moors, rising up on either side of the crystal waters. The air is still and quiet, punctuated only by an occasional low howl from the moors.
6986: You have reached a bluff overlooking the river Bruinen, at the foot of a majestic rock arch reaching skyward and spanning the running waters. The arch seems an easily crossable bridge; caution must be taken while crossing, however, since it is quite a height to the flowing river below... The river flows north-south, splitting into two branches north of here. On this side of the river sprawls more of the Bruinen moors.
6987: You are meandering through the high moors of the Bruinen. The land is rough but mostly flat, covered with wildly sprawling vegetation. The river lies to the east, many tree-heights below. Southwards a small bluff overlooks the river, where a majestic rock arch soars into the sky joining the moors on either side of the river.
6988: You are meandering through the high moors overlooking the Bruinen which flows southward many tree-heights below. The land is rough but mostly flat, covered with wildly sprawling vegetation and thick ground cover. Across the river matching cliffs rise out of the fertile plains.
6989: This spur of the Bruinen enters a turn here around some hills, flowing from the north to the east. The waters churn over the rocky streambed, carving their way through the limestone that form the walls of the moor and cliffs to either side of the river.
6990: This spur of the Bruinen flows gently from the north, past some hills to the east and the high moors to the west. The only sound is the gurgling of the river further to the south.
6991: This spur of the Bruinen flows gently from the north, bordering a fertile plain to the east and the moors to the west. The moors slope down to the water's edge and the river is fordable here as it flows over a gravel bed, thus making travel from the plain to the moors possible.
6992: This spur of the Bruinen flows gently from the north, bordering a fertile plain to the east and the high moors to the west. The air is muted and all around is silent, befitting the stark landscape around you.
6993: The fertile plain beneath your feet runs wildly into the distance, bounded only by the two spurs of the Bruinen to the southwest and southeast. Grass joyfully grows tall here, nourished by the waters of the river. Something seems to rise out of the flat earth to the east.
6994: The plain rises slightly here, forming some low hills terminating in a bluff overlooking the river south of here. From this height, you can see the plain stretching northwards to where the west spur of the North Bruinen curves back eastward.
6995: The plain rises slightly here, forming some low hills terminating in a bluff overlooking the river south of here. From this height, you can see the plain stretching endlessly northwards.
6996: This spur of the Bruinen turns around some northern hills, flowing from the west to the south. The waters churn over the rocky streambed, carving their way through the limestone that form the substrata of most of this region.
6997: A cluster of white star-shaped forget-me-nots flourish here in reminiscence.

Unexpectedly a mound rises here out of the earth. Covered with grass, you can nevertheless make out the unmistakable rusted relics of a hard-fought battle of a bygone era scattered here and there. You realise with a start that this must be the burial mound of the slain and shudder when you think that this plain is not only fertile by the waters of the Bruinen but also by these dead.
6998: The fertile plain sprouts joyfully growing grass beneath your feet, racing wildly into the distance, bounded only by the two spurs of the Bruinen to the southwest and southeast. To the west the landscape burps, for a small earthen mound rises out of the surrounding flatness.
6999: A tall stag is here, grazing peacefully.

The fertile plain beneath your feet runs wildly into the distance, bounded only by the two spurs of the Bruinen to the southwest and southeast. Grass joyfully grows tall here, nourished by the waters of the river. It is a wonder that this land has not been cultivated as you savor the richness of life and air.
7000: The fertile plain beneath your feet runs wildly into the distance, bounded only by the two spurs of the Bruinen to the southwest and southeast. Grass joyfully grows tall here, nourished by the waters of the river. This seems like a good place to have a picnic with the river gently flowing by.
7001: Flowing from its source in the Misty Mountains, the river Bruinen runs southeasterly toward the vale of Imladris. A fertile plain bounds the river to the north and a rolling heath lies to the south from which an occasional rustling and cluck startle the air.
7002: Flowing from its source in the Misty Mountains, the river Bruinen runs southeasterly toward the vale of Imladris. A fertile plain bounds the river to the north and a rolling heath lies to the south.
7003: Flowing from its source in the Misty Mountains, the river Bruinen runs southeasterly toward the vale of Imladris. A fertile plain bounds the river to the north and a rolling heath lies to the south, from which cluck-clucking may be heard.
7004: Flowing from its source in the Misty Mountains, the river Bruinen runs southeasterly toward the vale of Imladris. A fertile plain bounds the river to the north and a rolling heath lies to the south.
7005: The river skirts some cliffs to the west as it continues to meander southwest, passing the bleak Bruinen heath to the east. The air is still and quiet, though occasionally a cluck-cluck can be heard above the trickling waters.
7006: The river skirts some cliffs to the west as it continues to meander southwest, passing the bleak Bruinen heath to the east. The air is still and quiet, though occasionally a cluck-cluck can be heard above the trickling waters.
7007: The river skirts some cliffs to the west as it continues to meander southwest, passing the bleak Bruinen heath to the east. The air is still and quiet, though occasionally a cluck-cluck can be heard above the trickling waters.
7008: This spur of the Bruinen flows from the north toward a fork in the river. Cliffs overshadow the river to the east and you can make out the faint outline of what seems to be a bridge of some sort arching over the river further to the south.
7009: The river skirts some cliffs to the north as it continues to meander southwest, passing the bleak Bruinen heath to the east. The air is still and quiet, though occasionally a cluck-cluck can be heard above the trickling waters.
7010: Here two branches of the North Bruinen come together at the foot of some tall cliffs. One spur heads straight towards the north, while the other flows towards the northeast and the peaks of the Misty Mountains. Both join into a larger river as it flows south under a huge natural stone arch.
7011: Flowing from its source in the Misty Mountains, the river Bruinen runs to join a western spur to the south, where can also be seen the outline of a great rock arch or bridge spanning the moors on either side of the river.
7012: A majestic natural rock span arches overhead this stretch of the Bruinen, casting a pale shadow upon the rippling crystal waters. The span joins the eastern and western moors, both of which rise up on either side of the river.
7013: The river Bruinen takes a slow southwesterly course, from under an arching rock formation to the north. The waters cut through the moors here, etching and delving through the limestone.
7014: The river has carved a great stone arch. It looks quite sturdy and wide enough for safe travel. The arch itself seems to be one huge piece of rock carved by the relentless rushing of the Bruinen. Perhaps in the past some disturbance raised this temporary block to the river, which was soon remedied. Now it serves as an excellent path over the river.
7015: You have reached a northerly bluff overlooking the fork of the Bruinen where two spurs join into one and flow under a soaring natural rock arch to the south which spans the moors on either side of the river. To the north, the fertile plain stretches indefinitely, nourished by the flowing waters. To the east, you can enter the strong current of the Bruinen.
7016: The plain rises slightly here, forming some low hills terminating in a bluff overlooking the river south of here. From this height, you can see the plain stretching endlessly northwards.
7017: The fertile plain beneath your feet runs wildly into the distance, bounded only by the two spurs of the Bruinen to the southwest and southeast. Grass joyfully grows tall here, nourished by the waters of the river. A small mound of earth seems to rise a little further north but nothing compared to the low hills of the south.
7018: The fertile plain beneath your feet runs wildly into the distance, bounded only by the two spurs of the Bruinen to the southwest and southeast. Grass joyfully grows tall here, nourished by the waters of the river. Only some small hills to the northwest and southwest disturb the horizon.
7019: The fertile plain sprouts joyfully growing grass beneath your feet, racing wildly into the distance, bounded only by the two spurs of the Bruinen to the southwest and southeast. Unfortunately, the river bank is also full of grass, preventing fording the river to the brown heath on the other side.

A cute rabbit is here.
A pigeon is strutting around here.

You are wandering in the heath, a rolling expanse of country covered with earth yellow underbrush. The silence is broken only by an occasional cluck from somewhere in the dry ground cover. The heath stretches in all directions, shaped like an oval, bounded by what sounds like the river Bruinen in the west.
7021:
A gorcrow is standing here.
A cute rabbit is here.

The heath stretches in all directions, ovally shaped, bounded by what sounds like the river Bruinen in the west.
7022: You are wandering in the heath, a rolling expanse of country covered with earth yellow underbrush. The silence is broken only by an occasional cluck from somewhere in the dry ground cover. The heath stretches in all directions, seemingly blown by the west wind and moulded by the river Bruinen.

You are wandering in the heath, a rolling expanse of country covered with earth yellow underbrush. The silence is broken only by an occasional cluck from somewhere in the dry ground cover. The heath stretches from the branch of the Bruinen to the north, rippling land onward to the brooding moors which rise up against the horizon further south.

You are wandering in the heath, a rolling expanse of country covered with earth yellow underbrush. You feel unbounded by the constraints of space as you spread your arms to encompass the golden heath, and your mind roams freely over the gently rolling lay of the land.
7026: You are wandering in the heath, a rolling expanse of country covered with earth yellow underbrush. Only occasional clucking disturb the brooding atmosphere. The heath stretches in all directions, bounded by what sounds like the river Bruinen in the west and what seems to be even hillier moors to the south.
7027: This bluff overlooks the fork of the Bruinen where two tributaries merge into one. South of the fork a majestic rock formation arches into the sky, spanning the river. To the northeast you see the rolling lands of the heath and to the south sprawl the hilly moors, covered with scrub and pockmarked with dips and hollows.
7028: You are meandering through the moors of the Bruinen. The land is rough and hilly, covered with wildly sprawling vegetation and thick ground cover, dry as it is. The only visible landmark is the natural arch over the Bruinen to the northwest, for most of the moor is nondescript, pockmarked with little hollows.
7029: You are meandering through the moors of the Bruinen. The land is rough and hilly, covered with wildly sprawling vegetation and thick ground cover which makes passage difficult. The area here dips below the level of the hills around you and you cannot make out much of your surrounding area. The hill to your northwest seems to be taller than the rest, though.
7030: You are meandering through the moors of the Bruinen. The land is rough and hilly, covered with wildly sprawling vegetation and thick ground cover, even tougher than the brush of the heath. The air is clear and you can see the land dipping and rising around you, even northwards to that great span of rock that arches over the Bruinen.
7031: A narrow path leads you through the high, broken moors between the two branches of the Bruinen. It winds among the hills and descends slowly following a south- east course. A few patches of grass and small twisted bushes grow in the nearly barren ground.
7032: This is the edge of a long ridge of hills that extends westward rising and falling until the horizon. Southwards a sheer fall of many hundreds of feet frowns over a dark and wide gorge. On the other side of the ravine a ridge crowned with windswept firs rises against the sky. Eastward the land is broken - cliffs, crevices, and ravines block your way and your view.
7033: A footpath runs over a level strip of terrain, under the cover of the sheer cliff of dark rock which rises several hundred feet high to the west. The ground is encumbered with many boulders fallen from the cliff walls, dotting the green of the grass. The land ascends gently eastward, away from the cliff, and the meadow gradually gives ground to a forest of pine-trees.
7034: Coming from the elevated terrain in the west, the trail bends southward. It borders on the outskirts of a pine forest that climbs a slope to the east, where it grows thicker and darker. The vegetation is thick enough to partly hide the track; here and there roots hinder your walk.
7035: You are meandering through the moors of the Bruinen. The land is rough and hilly, covered with wildly sprawling vegetation. You are on a stretch of higher land, with dips and hollows here and there off to the side. The going is tough because of the undergrowth and perhaps that's why you see no signs of wildlife. The air here is still and sombre.
7036: You are meandering through the moors of the Bruinen. The land is rough and hilly, covered with wildly sprawling vegetation and thick ground cover that makes travelling difficult. There are little signs of wildlife. The visible landmark is the natural arch over the Bruinen to the northwest, though from here you can barely make it out, slender as it is.
7037: The small footpath you have been trying to follow disappears into a tangle of impenetrable brush here on the side of the hills. The land rises up sharply around you and there seems no way of climbing the steep sides to get a better view of the lay of the land.
7038: You are trying to follow a small footpath into the brooding moors. The path winds through the golden heath around and amongst the rolling hills. It seems but slightly used as none of the surrounding vegetation seems to be disturbed.
7039: A pigeon is strutting around here.

You are wandering in the heath, a rolling expanse of country covered with earth yellow underbrush. To the east there is a small rise and beyond that a small stretch of trail that winds upwards into the Misty Mountains. The heath, however, rolls unbounded northwards, as if the land were moved and rippled by the blowing wind.
7040: Standing on this rise you can see the golden heath stretching out before you to the north and to the west, with the Bruinen river at its furthest end. South sprawls the moors of the Bruinen, rough and hilly. A small footpath seems to lead downward and southwestward into its depths.
7041: You are trying to follow a small footpath into the moors. The path winds and snakes its way through the heath around and amongst the rolling hills. It seems but slightly used as little of the surrounding vegetation seems to be disturbed though you spot some telltale traces here and there of some woods- crafty wanderer.
7042: You are meandering through the moors of the Bruinen. The land is rough and hilly, covered with wildly sprawling vegetation and thick ground cover which makes the going rough. Somewhere to the south, you know, lies the vale of Imladris, or as men call it, Rivendell.
7043:
A huge, black wolf is here, ready to devour.
A black wolf pads restlessly, looking for its next prey.
A black wolf pads restlessly, looking for its next prey.

Some sparse young pine trees rise at the foot of a grassy slope, before a huge forest spreading eastward behind them as far as your sight can reach. Various bushes grow in hollows and among the few rocks that stick out of the grass. To the west a ridge of bleak hills looms in the distance.
7044: As the terrain slowly ascends eastward, the pines become thicker and thicker. Grass covers the terrain among the trees, and huge erratic stone blocks lie broken and half buried. To the west a small path runs at the foot of a sheer cliff wall before crossing the south fork of the Bruinen, where the stream spreads in stony shoals.
7045: For thousands of years the water carved the smooth walls that enclose and shelter this great bay. Now however, the ground is completely covered by pebbles and rocks, as the river takes a different route to the south. A few trees and some matted undergrowth manage to grow under the shadow of the east side, where some loam has fallen from the cliff. To the north the cliff has better endured the challenge of time, and is still smooth and impassable.
7046: Sparse patches of grass and heather plants strive for life in these bleak and broken hills; against the odds it would appear. A great bay enclosed by steep cliffs opens suddenly to the south, many hundreds of feet below. Carved long ago by the water which has long since departed for another route, these days only a stream of pebbles paves its bed. The cliff here falls smooth and sheer, allowing no descent, but elsewhere it is cracked and crumbled.
7047: You are meandering through the moors of the Bruinen. The land is rough and hilly, covered with wildly sprawling vegetation and thick ground cover, dry as it is. You are in a small dell, surrounded by higher moorland on all sides. Here, not a sound stirs the air... you feel you are almost a part of the silent, brooding moor.
7048: You are meandering through the moors of the Bruinen. The land is rough and hilly, covered with wildly sprawling vegetation and thick ground cover, dry as it is. The only visible landmark is the natural arch over the Bruinen to the northwest for most of moor is nondescript, pockmarked with little hollows.
7049:

You are meandering through the moors of the Bruinen. The land is rough and hilly, covered with wildly sprawling vegetation and thick ground cover that make travelling difficult. The land dips down sharply to the west and south though you can try to keep on the high land. You can espy the top of the natural arch over the Bruinen to the northwest from here, soaring even higher than you stand now.
7050: You are meandering through the moors of the Bruinen. The land is rough and hilly, covered with wildly sprawling vegetation and thick ground cover, dry and impassable as it is. The only visible landmark is the natural arch over the Bruinen to the west, though from here you can't really discern the sounds of the river. Northwards roll the gentler heath.
7051: Here the rolling heath from the north meet the more hilly moors to the south. There is no marked change in vegetation, the heath turning into more dense and more brownish brush. The land dips and rises more sharply in the moors though, and you are careful watching your step. The only sound in the air is the gurgling of running water close by.
7052: You have reached a bluff overlooking the river Bruinen, at the foot of a majestic rock arch reaching skyward and spanning the running waters. It seems an easily passable bridge. It is quite a height to the flowing river below... To the northeast sprawls the heath and to the south lie the moors from which you came.
7053: You are meandering through the moors of the Bruinen. The land is rough and hilly, covered with wildly sprawling vegetation and thick ground cover, dry as it is. The area here dips below the level of the hills and you cannot make out much of the lay of the land, but you think you can make out that great natural arch just northwest of here.
7054: You are meandering through the moors of the Bruinen. The land is rough and hilly, covered with wildly sprawling vegetation and thick ground cover, dry as it is. The only visible landmark is the natural arch over the Bruinen to the northwest for most of moor is nondescript, pockmarked with little hollows.
7055: You are meandering through the moors of the Bruinen. The land is rough and hilly, covered with wildly sprawling vegetation and thick ground cover, dry as it is. The only visible landmark is the natural arch over the Bruinen to the northwest for most of moor is nondescript, pockmarked with little hollows.
7056: Thick heather covers the low, rocky hills that spread for many miles to the south and east. Westwards a small scree descends steeply into a deep rift, enclosed between crumbling cliff walls. No visible path crosses this country, and in all the silent moors there is no sign of any dwelling.
7058: A great heel of rock thrusts outward from the cliffs, overhanging a lofty waterfall which rumbles in the deep gorge far below. Thin mist from the falls surrounds the place and veils the landscape all around you. Still, a wide bowl-shaped valley, as opposed to the gorge here, can be guessed westward. On the other side of the fall a cliff rises again, and a dark-green line of trees follows its edge.
7061: A large rabbit looks peacefully at you, ready to dart away.

At the bottom of a widening rift a white stream of rocks slopes steeply to the west, flanked to the south by a crumbling cliff wall. It is quite unstable, and even the fall of a small pebble could result in a landslide. It is very tiring to walk on the scree in any direction, as the stones give way at every step.
7062: You are meandering through the moors of the Bruinen. The land is rough and hilly, covered with wildly sprawling vegetation and thick ground cover, dry as it is. The brambles of the brush are tough and hinder your passage. The only visible landmarks are the natural arch over the Bruinen to the north, and the scree of white stones to the south.
7063: A sturdy pack horse is standing here.

You are meandering through the moors of the Bruinen. The land is rough and hilly, covered with wildly sprawling vegetation and thick ground cover, dry as it is. The area here dips below the level of the hills and you cannot make out much of your surrounding area, save the sound of gurgling water somewhere close by to the west.
7064: The great rocky sides of the ravine draw nearer, as the stream bends southward and becomes faster and deeper. From there a faint but distant rumbling sound can be heard. Over time the water eroded away the rock to the north, making a great bay, now dried up, that opens in the sheer northern walls.
7065: The stream flows shallow and broad on a wide expanse of pebbles, between two towering walls of rock knife-edged against the sky far above. Little light reaches the bottom, even on sunny days, and dark moss covers the lowest part of the walls. Midway to the top a few scrawny trees grow in crevices and fissures.
7066: The river widens to many hundreds of feet here in stony shoals, trickling and bubbling over a bed of shining pebbles. To the west it threads its way into a deep, wide gorge where tall cliffs rise like mighty towers on either side. A little trail climbs the grassy banks of the river, keeping close to the cliff.
7067: At the bottom of an open valley the river runs slowly, before gradually widening westward and dividing into many small streamlets as the river passes through a ford. To the north many sparse pines rise from the grass, and the forest becomes denser the further up the slopes you look. A green meadow lies on the southern bank - a small open area before further forest.
7068:
A trout swims here.
A trout swims here.

The stream flows under the shadow of a pine forest to the north, so that much of the river is overhung by their branches. The shoreline rises and falls as V-shaped gullies end by the river, their sides cut by the water. A gentle slope climbs to the south, and grass and weeds grow on its muddy bank.
7069: The ground slopes steeply southward, towards the south fork of the Bruinen which flows under the shadow of the trees. The land is cut by V-shaped gullies, created by the many small creeks that run down to the river. Some grey lichen clings to the pines, but no plant life or undergrowth manages to grow under the dark shadow of the trees.
7070:

The trees struggle silently for light in this thick forest, and the trunks rise tall and slender. Their bark has a fierce red-brown colour and are completely bare almost till the top, where they spread into a mushroom crown of twisted and gnarled boughs. A thick and soft carpet of pine needles conceals the sloping ground, and every now and then an uprooted old tree slowly rots on the ground.
7071: You are meandering through the moors of the Bruinen. The land is rough and hilly, covered with wildly sprawling vegetation and thick ground cover, dry and deader than usual. Around you rise the higher lands of the moor, almost brooding in their stillness and silence.
7072: You are meandering through the moors of the Bruinen. The land is rough and hilly, covered with wildly sprawling vegetation and thick ground cover, dry as it is. The edge of the moor is just northwards where it encounters the heath. From here, you can see a great forest dominating the skyline to the east, however, it is unreachable from here as the roughness of the moorland makes travelling difficult.
7073: Standing on this rise you can see the rolling heath stretching out before you to the north and to the west, with the Bruinen river at its furthest end. South sprawls the moors of the Bruinen, rough and hilly. A small footpath seems to lead downward and another can be seen to the east.
7074: The trail here bends south to east, clipping the golden Bruinen heath to the northwest, where occasional cluck-cluckings permeate the stillness of the air. A small footpath disappears westward into the hills.
7076: You are wandering in the heath, a rolling expanse of country covered with earth yellow underbrush. The heath stretches west and south, bounded only by what sounds like the river Bruinen to the north and rising land to the east upon which a trail to the Misty Mountains climbs ever upward.
7077: You are wandering in the heath, a rolling expanse of country covered with earth yellow underbrush. The silence is broken only by an occasional cluck from somewhere in the dry ground cover. The heath stretches southward toward the moors from the river flowing just north of here.
7078: Flowing from its source in the Misty Mountains, the river Bruinen runs southeasterly toward the vale of Imladris. A fertile plain bounds the river to the north and a rolling expanse of heath lies to the south.
7079: A rabbit is here eyeing your presence warily.

As you climb up the hills, a number of rocks fall free and roll down the hill. It's hard to keep a steady footing, and no tracks of your passage are left behind. You notice a small hole in the rocks to the south, but it is too small for one of your size.
7080: The path takes another turn here, turning from the east to the north. The hills surrounding the path are relatively small compared to the mountains that can be seen off in the distance. It seems hard to believe this path can take you all the way to those mountains.
7081: A brown fox is here, looking for some rabbits to chew up.
As the path continues on, so do the deep ruts. The path here takes a curve winding towards the east. To the north is a small patch of trees, but there is no obvious entrances from this side.
7082: The higher moor tapers away here, giving way to the gentler rolling heath northwards. This area seems to be frequented with travellers as it is close to the trail to the Misty Mountains and seems to be less wild than the rest of the moors. The air, however, is silent.
7083: You are standing in a small grove of trees that provide comfortable shade for a weary traveller. To the east is the main road, and you can hear the sound of a river nearby.
7084: As the Bruinen continues, you find yourself dozing off on your boat. The wide, steady river flows onward in a roundabout fashion. To the south is a clump of trees, and to the north are some plains. The river continues to the east and west.
7085: The path bends here, continuing upon its way to the west and to the north of you. And as far as you can see in both directions, it bears deep ruts. To the east of here the vast expanse of the Loudwater Plains opens up before you.
7086: The path continues onward, seemingly forever. It is easy to walk on the hard-packed dirt, as long as you avoid the deep ruts that can occasionally be found in the middle of the road. To the east are some hills, and the path continues to the west and the south.
7087: The dirt path takes another curve here, going both north and west. The plains are just opening up on the east, and you can spot many hills dotting them as they spread out over the land.
7088: A brown fox is here, looking for some rabbits to chew up.

As the hard-packed path continues, another curve from the south towards the east forms. The ruts here continue along the path, as if they follow it. To the west is a small clump of trees, and to the north is a river.
7089: The curve in the road turns again, going from the west to the north. To the east and south are the plains, and farther on you can see more of the hills. Farther north you can see the river again.
7090: The road here is getting a bit softer, as it nears the river. The path takes a turn from the south to the east, and to the north and west is the river. The deep ruts continue along the road.
7091: The road path here finally straightens out for a bit. The path continues west and east, and the river continues along the path to the north. To the south are the plains and the hills, and there is a wild patch of trees growing down there.
7092: As the path continues from the west to the east, so do the deep ruts. Some evidence to what made these ruts are finally seen along the sides of the road as there are a few wagon wheels stuck in the dirt, from when the river switched its course.
7093:
A fallow deer is grazing peacefully here.
A grey wolf is here, salivating profusely.

The tracks here seem more obvious, as the path gets slightly softer near the river. This path seems to be a major trade highway. The path continues to the west and east, with the river running alongside it to the north.
7094: The trade path starts winding again, as the river moves, and it follows the river. To the north and west the path continues, and to the east and south are some plains. Farther to the south you can see a wild forest.
7095: A small grasshopper clings to a blade of grass, ready to spring.
The path takes a bend here, heading both west and south. The path makes a slight turn here to avoid some of the hills to the north. Along the sides of the roads a few flowers grow by themselves.
7096: A small grasshopper clings to a blade of grass, ready to spring.

As you enter the hills, you find a small path that winds it's way through them, making it easy to go through them. The main road runs around the hills, as the bigger caravans cannot wind their way through these hills.
7097: A small and tough weed grows here.

You slowly trudge up this large hill. You look around and see that there are many large rocks resting on the sides of the small trail you are on. The trail leads from the west to the top of the hill to the north.
7098: The plains here become slightly hilly as they run into the hills to the north and the south. There are no paths visible that would allow passage into the hills. However, you see a break in the forest to the south, where the trees grow close together and the undergrowth sprawls over the floor of the forest in clumps and sheets of green vegetation.
7099: You are standing on the edge of some vast plains. There are a few trees growing here and there, with a large concentration of trees towards the south. You don't see any visible path into the forest to the south, as the trees are growing too close together. To the northwest you see a small concentration of hills, and there are also some hills to the northeast.
7100: The trees are starting to get thicker here, as you enter the forest. The air is filled with birds singing and the leaves of the oak trees rustling in the slight breeze. In some places, the trees are so close that you cannot continue moving. To the west the light grows brighter as you see the entrance of the forest, but to the east the forest grows darker.
7101: As you walk into the forest, the light grows dimmer, and the trees grow closer. Untamed by man or elf, these trees have been growing wildly, as free as they were designed to be. There seems to be quite a mixture of trees, including mostly evergreens and a few oaks and maples scattered around. To the north are the plains, and all around is more of the forest.
7102: A small grasshopper clings to a blade of grass, ready to spring.

The trees are starting to get thicker here, and are bunching together to block movements in many directions. With this many trees, and in this state of wildness, you have never felt closer to nature. To the east the light grows stronger, and the only other way that movement is possible is to the south, where the trees block out most of your vision.
7103: The trail in the hills starts here, and leads up to the peak of the hill to the west. The south is too littered with stones and rocks to be safe to travel into. The vast Loudwater Plains can be seen to the north and east.
7104: You have reached the peak of this small peak. After a moments break, you stop to take a look at the area surrounding you. To the east and south you can see a large wild forest, where the trees grow so close that it looks like a landscape made of green leaves. To the west you can see a small path that winds its way far to the south and off into the distance to the north. For a while it runs along the mighty river called the Bruinen.
7105: This small bit of grassland is isolated from most of the rest of the great Loudwater Plains.Surrounded on the east and west by gently rolling hills, and the north by the path, this bit of plains looks like a nice place to rest for a while. There are a few old campfires seen here and there, long cold.
7106: The grass here is thick, deep and luxuriant. You feel like you can fall down in the grass and sleep for eternity. A large hill rises up to the south, but you can see no safe path leading up it. The plains continue in all other directions, including north to the river Bruinen, also known as Loudwater.
7107: A small grasshopper clings to a blade of grass, ready to spring.

As you make your way through the plains, you can see a small path leading up into the hills to the south. This hill is the highest point around this area, so you think that it might have a good view of the surrounding area. In all other directions, the plains continue, as plains are often led to do.
7108: A fallow deer is grazing peacefully here.

The plains starting here are mostly flat, covered in a lush grass with a few other grasses and weeds interwoven into the pattern. The great river Bruinen can be seen a bit to the north, and the path that runs alongside it is to the north and west. There are a few old campfires in this area, from caravans that stopped here long ago. Now, weeds are growing amid the rocks and ashes.
7109: The grassy plains continue on here, going in all directions but north. The grass whispers against your legs as you make your way through it. To the north you can see the path that runs along the Bruinen.
7110: The plains here run into the road that runs with the river Bruinen. The grass fans out in all the other directions, into a few hills that dot the landscape. The grass is here is short, and looks like it has been grazed.
7111: The plains take a break here as they run up the small hills to the north and south. The bulk of the plains lie to the southwest, where a few small trees can be seen growing here and there. To the north lies the small path.
7112: Here are a couple of small hills that rise up out of the plains. They are soft, gentle hills with barely any height to them. The grass does not grow much up on the hills, as they are covered in small rocks and pebbles. The hills continue on to the south, and to the west are the Loudwater Plains.
7113: A couple of small hills stand here, giving you a better view of the surrounding area. To the west you see a hill that stands higher than any of the others, and you think the view would be better over there. The plains stretch out to the west, towards that hill.
7114: The dark forest starts to take turns now, as the trees grow in a seemingly random pattern. The trees form barriers that are impossible to pass, so you must travel in the few open spots. Travel is possible to the west and south.
7115:
A rabbit is here eyeing your presence warily.
A small grasshopper clings to a blade of grass, ready to spring.
A ferocious warg is here, snarling angrily.

As you come into this area of the forest, you can't help but seeing the squirrels bouncing around from tree to tree playing some game that only they understand. The forest here thins out a bit, and to the south you notice some kind of clearing, where there are no trees at all.
7116:
A small cluster of clover grows here.
A small cluster of clover grows here.
A grey wolf is here, snarling aggressively.

The trees here are becoming thicker as they merge into the large forest to the south and east. You begin to hear the calls of some of the animals in the forest, and you can hear the subtle rustling of movements deep within. There are a few ranges of hills around you, to the west and also to the northeast.
7117: Here in the plains grow a few trees, randomly placed every now and then. The trees grow much thicker to the south, as they grow into the wild forest that lies before you. The ground here rises up on a slow slope to the east as it leads up into the small hills.
7118: You here the gentle chirping of the small insects that inhabit this area of the plains. The grass becomes thinner here as it rises up the slope of the small hill to the east.
7119: You are now deep within the plains. Totally surrounded by them, you feel somewhat humbled by nature, and it's power. The grass is light, and easy to pass through, and is cool and moist to the touch. In the distance you can see mountains rising up above the horizon.
7120: Grassy plains surround you as you make your way through them, pushing aside the grass when it becomes too tall to walk over. A few trees grow in the plains here, and to the south you can see a great wall of trees. To the west the plains rise up to some small hills.
7121: The path here continues on, as paths tend to do. To the east the wild forest continues, and to the west is a small hill. The path continues to head in a north-south direction.
7122: A grey wolf is here, salivating profusely.
The road goes onwards and onwards, seeming to last forever. To the east is a large, wild forest, where the trees are growing so close together that it is hard to see much past the first tree.
7124: An old, overgrown path takes you north from here around a large forest extending to the east. Looking south, you see the path leading up a hill to a bridge over the river. You remember old tales of a large trade-route, leading between the dwarves in Erebor, the Lonely Mountain, and Imladris, the home of the proud Noldor.
7125: A wolf cub happily plays here.

You are standing on a path leading up a slope to the south. It turns north and east here. To the east, you see the northern end of an old bridge leading across the river Bruinen. You turn your eyes to the north-east and see a large forest spreading across the lands.
7126: This is high up on a cliff above the river. South of here, a stone bridge can take you across the river to the path that continues to the south. You follow the path to the west, leading you down from the cliff and then further north, eventually to the High Pass through the Misty Mountains. You can also enter a wild forest to the north.
7127: A ferocious warg is here, snarling angrily.

As you push your way through the scratchy pine needles, the forest gets thicker and thicker. Soon movement will not be possible any more. To the east and west, the trees are so close together that movement is not possible.
7128: A small grasshopper clings to a blade of grass, ready to spring.

As you struggle through the trees, earning a few scratches here and there, you realise that the trees here are just not worth fighting. The only direction that movement is possible is back to the north, from where you came.
7129: A grey wolf is here, snarling aggressively.

The forest that surrounds you brings you peace, but you can sense some other feeling underlying the peace, subverting it. The forest here is very thick, and the only direction that movement is possible is back to the east.
7130: A large elk is standing here, chewing grass and leaves.

This is the edge of a wild forest. It extends to the north, and you can hear the howling of rare beasts. Dare you really enter this old forest, forgot by all men a long time ago? You can get back out to the east, from where you also hear the splashing water of the south fork of the Bruinen.
7131: This bridge is considerably high above the River Bruinen which lies below. The stone arch carries that carries travellers safely across, stretches the width of the river, which continues upstream into the Misty Mountains. Downstream, is the northern bank. Beyond that, barely noticeable in the distance, is a large house, perhaps it is Imladris, the home of Elrond. The bridge bears the mark of the dwarves on a stone plaque that is fastened to its middle.
7132: You are on a high cliff at the Bruinen. A small path leads north, onto a bridge over to the north side of the river. You can go down a slope to the west, leading down to the riverside. The path continues to the east, and beyond it a plateau stretches east. When you raise your eyes, you see the grey mountains in the distance, and you wonder what foul creatures it hides.
7133: The South Fork of the Bruinen

The light is glittering in the surface beautifully as you slowly drift down the river. If it only could be like this forever... To the west, the river speeds up as it whirls around some rocks in the river.
7134: The South Fork of the Bruinen

Here, the river is flowing faster among some rocks in the river, carrying you downstream, eventually to reach the city that once was the capital of Cardolan - Tharbad. If you hurry, you might get ashore on the north bank, where a grassy field stretches north. The southern bank is full of scattered rocks. To the west the river flows under the pine forest on the northern bank, and is cloaked in shadow.

Its mighty roar reverberates between the walls, and although a rising cloud of mist veils the horizon behind the waterfall you can guess the valley widens further downstream. At the edge of the cliffs a line of firs stands out against the sky.
7136: Swept out into midair by the waterfall, you experience a moment of weightlessness while you plunge downwards at increasing speed. It doesn't last long though, as you soon reach the bottom of the gorge. The last thing you notice is the rocks just below the surface of the water, against which your bones are smashed to pieces.

You are standing in a grassy field just north of the southern fork of the great river Bruinen. Looking south, across the river, you see a rock-covered area before the large wilderness in the south. Just east of here, a path leads up a slope to the northern end of a bridge, high above the river.
7139: Looking down, you see nothing but green grass covering your feet. To the east, just in front of a large forest, a path leads north from a bridge over the Bruinen. The river itself with its splashing and sparkling water is a bit further south of here.

A brown bear is sleeping here.
A brown bear is sleeping here.

As you first enter the dank cave, a musty odour comes from the back. Around the room are a number of bones from small animals. There are a few worn spots and some tufts of fur here and there, making the room look very lived in.
7141: A large elk is standing here, chewing grass and leaves.

The edge of a fir forest peeks over the edge of a sheer cliff to the west, with one particularly huge tree spreading its branches well out over the edge. A small path follows the feet of the cliff wall, leading northwards to where the Bruinen flows over a shallow pebbled ford. To the south it sinks in a wooded V-shaped dell.
7142: A Wooded Dell of Silvery Firs

A forest of silvery firs spreads westward from the bottom of a V-shaped dell, while to the south a small footpath winds among the dense underbrush. To the east the ground rises more steeply, and prunes and brambles grow so thick and matted that there is no way to pass them. To get to the top of the slope, where the forest extends again, you would have to make a long detour.
7143: This section of the trail skirts around a deep dike to the south, where an ivy-clad wall bars the gap between two hills. It was built during the long siege by the Witch-king, as part of the ancient fortifications whose ruins still loom on the crest of the hills. A forest of silvery firs spread to the north.
7144: A large rabbit looks peacefully at you, ready to dart away.

This trail borders the southern edge of a wide forest. Huge firs spread their branches over the path at many points and, from below, the leaves appear to glitter as if threaded with silver. A ridge of hills, with sheer flanks, looms far to the south, and over their crest are a few ruined walls half covered by the vegetation.
7146: An easy track passes through the moors, and runs eastward under the shadow of a sheer cliff. It is the rocky shoulder of the last hill in a small range, and at its top can be spotted the overgrown ruins of an ancient fort. North of here the vegetation grows thicker, but now and then a small footpath departs from the main track and ventures into it.
7147: The trail here follows the edge of a black ravine to the south, occasionally marked by white stones. Now and then lesser tracks leave the main path and lead into the vegetation, but in the rocky soil it is not easy to tell whether boots or hooves trampled them. A small hillock rises from the thick vegetation to the north.
7148: The trail here becomes erratic, and though it appears to keep running east-west, many lesser tracks split off it which, if followed, soon disappear in a hollow or behind an hump. The landscape remain unchanged in every direction: tangled vegetation and small ivy-clad hillocks.
7150: A fallow deer is grazing peacefully here.

The track keeps a straight east to west course over open ground, but not far to the west it seems to run under the shadow of a forest. To the north a large finger of rock seems to stick out of nowhere in the middle of a field. A ridge of hills rises to the south, and over their rocky and steep sides lie the ruins of some ancient fortifications.
7151: Rocky grounds lie to the north, between you and the great river Bruinen in the distance. The path bends here, around the plains to the east, and continues towards the Misty Mountains. Straight east of here, a plateau rises high above the surrounding land. You see a small path leading up on it, heading towards a bridge over the river.
7152: The path bends north here, avoiding the hills to the west. To the east it winds its way towards the Misty Mountains, which dominate the horizon. The land all around the trail is barren, a legacy to the second age when the Witchking laid siege to Imladris. Nearby to the south-east lies some crumbling stone walls of a farm abandoned many years ago.
7153: You are standing on the path leading east-west. Just south of here is a small farm. It seems to have been deserted for quite a while. Its roof has fallen in, and there is not the slightest sign of any life. To the north, beyond the plains, the ground slowly turns very rocky.
7154: A hungry warg is standing here, ridden by you.

This is the intersection of two old roads. The path that leads east-south is actually the former Great East Road, but it no longer used, and neither is the path that leads north to the High Pass through the Misty Mountains. To the east, you see vast plains extending very far away into the unknown wasteland that lie west of the Misty Mountains.
7155: You are surrounded by plains to your east and your west. A path runs north and south from here. To the north, the path leads up a slope, and over a bridge over the river. South of here, there is a path intersection. You look around you, and you notice how very quiet it is around here... No animal, no nothing... Beware and watch your steps - you have a dangerous way ahead of you.
7156: A small path carries you north, up a rather steep slope. You cannot go anywhere but follow the path north or south. Looking east and a bit south, you see vast plains stretching very far into the distance. To the south, you see that the path meets another path in a T-crossing.
7157: Looking around, you see the path you are standing on continuing south, and west (where a bridge across the river is). North you see the river Bruinen flowing in a canyon below. To the east, there is a plateau, and in the distance, the towering Misty Mountains.
7158: A hungry warg is standing here, ridden by you.

The trail bends here, leading you north to the intersection of paths or east, towards the grey Misty Mountains. To the west, you see a small barn, but you find no way to enter it from this side. Vast plains extend to the north-east and to the south you see nothing but wasteland.
7159: A hungry warg is standing here, ridden by you.

The trail leads straight east, towards the mountains. It seems to have been out of use for many years, and it is sometimes hard to find it under the thick grass that covers it in many places. South of here, you can enter the wasteland, a hostile area with no sign of shelter against foul beasts and bad weather.
7160: Grass covers the small trail you are standing on. It runs straight from the west to the east, taking you into the Misty Mountains in the east. You can see it continuing in a very straight line, something due to the trails former status as a part of the Great East Road, built by the Numenoreans of Arnor.
7161: A hungry warg is standing here, ridden by you.

The trail leads past an old ruin of a house, that is set on a small hill to the south. The trail is running east-west, and can take you into the Hithaeglir, or back to the Old East Road and Rivendell to the west. Looking north, you see nothing but vast plains, and there, in the distance, you make out a high hill, or plateau to the north-west.
7162: A hungry warg is standing here, ridden by you.

The trail continues in the same old direction - east and west. Following it with your eyes, you see that it makes a sharp turn to the north a bit further east. The trail is nearly overgrown, making it obvious that it is not used very often these days.
7163: A hungry warg is standing here, ridden by you.

You are still on the trail taking you towards the waiting mountains in the east. To the north, you can enter some plains that seem to extend very far in all directions. Looking to the north-east, you see a small cave.
7164: Here, the grassy trail runs just south of a hill. Looking west, you see the trail continuing very far, but as you look east, you notice that the trail turns northwards.
7165: A hungry warg is standing here, ridden by you.

Just east of here the trail bends to the north, westwards however the trail continues very far. Northeast of here you see a hill, and further in the east you see an even higher hill, but they are nothing compared to the high mountains far in the east.
7166: A hungry warg is standing here, ridden by you.

You are standing on the trail to the mountains as it bends from west to north. South of here you see a slightly rocky plain, and to the west the trail continues over the flat landscape. In the east you see a high hill rising over the trees.

You are standing on the trail to the Misty Mountains. The trail runs in a north-south direction bordered by thick bushes on both sides. The trail looks as if it is not used now as much as it once was. To the east a high hill can clearly be seen high over the rest of the forest.
