7463: The spirit of a mighty warrior greets you with an evil laughter.
You are now in the chamber of a chieftain named 'Ghar-Gleh'. His name is carved into the northern wall. More than a thousand years ago, he was a chieftain of the Hill-men.
7464:
The spirit of a mighty warrior greets you with an evil laughter.
Ducaht (tooprettytodie), wielding a great warsword, is standing here.
This chamber contains the tomb of 'Ghar-Bledh', a chieftain among Hill-men in this area more than a thousand years ago. His name is written on the northern wall.
7465: The spirit of a mighty warrior greets you with an evil laughter.

This chamber contains the tomb of a chieftain named 'Ghar-Bidch'. That name is written on the northern wall. It is written with ordinary Tengwar, but the language is unknown. Most likely, it is written in the language the Hill-men spoke more than a thousand years ago.
7466: The air of this hidden staircase is musky and reeks of disuse. There are no tracks of the troll's clumsy feet in the dust on the floor. No offal or refuse from their inhabitation touches this place. Perhaps this will lead you to the chambers that were mentioned in the painting in the large chamber.
7467: The spirit of a mighty warrior greets you with an evil laughter.

This chamber contains the tomb of a chieftain named 'Ghar-Dehn'. His name is written on the southern wall. It is written with Tengwar, but you don't recognise the language. Most likely, it is written in the language spoken among the Hill-men in these areas more than thousand years ago.
7468:
The spirit of a mighty warrior greets you with an evil laughter.
Ducaht (tooprettytodie), wielding a great warsword, is standing here.

This is the chamber where the tomb of 'Ghar-Adje'. He was once a chieftain of the Hill-men, and probably slain fighting the Dunedain in a battle a long time ago. His name is written on the southern wall.
7469:
A shadow suddenly leaves its place on the wall, trying to reach your neck.
A shadow suddenly leaves its place on the wall, trying to reach your neck.
A shadow suddenly leaves its place on the wall, trying to reach your neck.
A sudden silence fills the cave as you enter. There is a lot of dust in the thick air. This is not a resting place for any creature who has some sanity left.
7470: Among the fallen stones you found a hole, and you entered it and reached the bottom of a narrow tunnel. From west a calm sound enters this humid place. It almost sounds like someone singing but it is ice in the voice.
7473: You are on the northern riverbank next to a bridge. The trail north of you bends and continues on the other side of the river. Behind the bridge, you see that the river is joined by a smaller river.
7474:
Lhurank (brenny), wielding a darkened orkish axe, is standing here searching for something.
A grey wolf is here, snarling aggressively.
Klaees (thedon), wielding a great warsword, is standing here.
A grey wolf is here, snarling aggressively.

You are on the northern side of a river running from the east to the west. The ground is covered with sand and it is obvious that the river is often much wider. Its source is up in the mountains. The borders of the bed indicate the river contains different amounts of water, probably more after rainy periods or during the snow-metling season.
7475: A grey wolf is here, snarling aggressively.
You walk on a sandy riverbank. The river flows silently to west, and far away, it appears to run into a deep valley. North of you is an old trail going into the Mountains.
7476:
A small cluster of clover grows here.
A small cluster of clover grows here.
A grey wolf is here, snarling aggressively.

A river is south of you. It runs silently to the west, and you see that it is joined by another small river far away. You also notice a bridge across the river. If you follow the trail north of you, it will take you there.
7477: Huge rocks cover the ground. It seems easier to travel on the trail to the north or on the river bank to the west. Steep mountains block your way east and south.
7478: In a distance to the east the trail bends slightly to the north. Now it is blocked by rocks torn down from the mountainsides by avalanches. The trail goes later into a deep valley. Westwards the trail seems to lead you towards a dark forest of pines. To the south are rocky flats.
7479:
A squirrel scampers around here, looking for nuts from the trees.
A grey wolf is here, snarling aggressively.

The foot of the mountains appear to be only a mile away. But it is the size of those mountains that plays you a trick. To the south is a riverbank. A branch of the river Bruinen is floating westwards and later south of the dark forest far west.
7480:
A grey wolf is here, snarling aggressively.
A squirrel scampers around here, looking for nuts from the trees.
A huge, black wolf is here, ready to devour.
A huge, black wolf is here, ready to devour.

The trail passes a flat an rocky area. A few birches grows by the trail and you are close to the mountains. The mountains in the horizon rise high up in the sky. They are partly covered with snow. Wind makes mountain sides almost free from snow throughout the year.
7487: A web of small, erratic footpaths leads through the brush-covered hills that spread to the south and east. Still, the vegetation is thick enough to hide many possible passages, and perhaps the half-hidden small white stones that stick out of the grass at points could be a clue to these. A sheer precipice opens a few steps to the north, but there is no way to climb down it.
7488: A sudden precipice frowns over a tall waterfall. Its roar reverberates between the sheer cliffs and a thin mist rises up to these elevated moors, veiling the gorge far below. A bush growing a few feet high in the form of a small recumbent pine tree has completely invaded the uneven ground, spreading a strong odour of resin. Eastwards the land falls for many yards, and down there a grove of silvery firs stretches for miles.
7489: The conical shapes of many firs surround you, spreading eastward from the base of a low cliff. The trees are not densely crowded, and high grass fills the ground between them where the light of the sun can reach. At the bottom of an abrupt fall to the north the southern fork of the Bruinen cleaves its way, fast and deep, through the moors.
7490: Crossing this undulating land is quite difficult, as much matted underbrush covers the ground. Still, a few half-covered footpaths can be found among the brambles and the bushes. To the south the soil is clearer and the pale line of a well-trodden path treads the moors. A small forest of silvery firs climbs a gentle slope to the north.
7491:
A large rabbit looks peacefully at you, ready to dart away.
A large rabbit looks peacefully at you, ready to dart away.

The ground rises here to form a small hillock. All around the landscape spreads unchanging as far as your sight can reach; heather and thick vegetation covering the undulating ground. Tiny, barely noticeable footpaths lead through the heather, apparently going in no particular direction. A faint odour of resin is carried by the breeze from the north, where a thick growth of bushes can be spotted.
7492: The ground dips below the level of the surrounding area, and the rising slopes all around block your sight. Probably the hillock to the east of here would provide a better view. The vegetation is thick enough to hide many of the small tracks, even though small piles of white stones often seem to mark them. They are encumbered with roots and bushes, and meander uncertainly through the undulating terrain.
7493: Small Glade among the Silvery Firs

A circle of lofty firs encloses the flat top of a small, grassy hillock, and behind them the wood extends in every direction. The large spreading boughs glitter with a silvery appearance when observed from below, and their bark has become roughened and darkened with age.
7494: A sheer drop encircles this lofty and exposed place from three sides, and the only way on foot leads south. Many of the trees suffer from the wind that must beat this outcrop harshly; still, some are very old and big indeed. To the north, at the bottom of a deep gorge, the shallow south fork of the Bruinen flows on a wide bed of pebbles.
7495: The western edge of a ridge of hills climbs east of here in a sheer wall of rock, with a few straggly weeds peeking over its edge. The cliff slowly lowers to the south, where a line of boulders makes a circle at the edge of a vast level area. In the middle of the plain rise two low, solitary mounds.
7496: The ground is littered with boulders fallen from a crumbling wall of dark grey stone that climbs northward, at least a dozen yards high. Tiny shrubs peek out of the chinks in the wall, and small animals hide in holes at its base. To the south the ground slopes gently toward a narrow valley, where heather gives way to grass and flowers.
7497: Low, gentle hillocks lie all around for miles, with thick heather growing on them. The terrain is covered with their roots, and their branches sway gently in the breeze. Southwards the land drops down sheer cliffs many yards to a deeply cut valley; a noisy brook flows down from the east in it, and turning around the last branch of a ridge of hills passes out of sight.
7498: A noisy brook runs swiftly among sheer stony banks, sprinkling and sparkling on a rocky bed. It flows in from the east and turns southward, where the sides of the valley draw near, leaving only a small gap between them and the green meadows that flank the water. Sheltered from the wind and fed by the water, a few thin beeches rise on a low, grassy foothill. A few large animal tracks can be seen around here, particularly nearby the bushes to the north.
7499: A spring bursts forth from a rock wall to the south, and forms a small pool at its base; the water feeds a small rivulet, which runs west in a sunken valley. All around the pool, besides short grass and colourful flowers, many boulders lie: they are the remnants of an ancient wall that still stretches eastward along the edge of a wide stretch of level terrain.
7500: A cluster of white star-shaped forget-me-nots flourish here in reminiscence.

Two mounds lie in the middle of a level stretch of terrain, one barren and covered with dark rocks, the other with grass among the darker ivy and little flowers growing on its top. All around in this landscape can be seen ancient and ruined fortifications: all that remain of a line of ramparts and quarters that used to stand here.
7501:
A rock lizard is here, motionless as it observes you.
A fallow deer is grazing peacefully here.

A long line of boulders, a few feet tall and partly hidden by thick vegetation, runs up and down the slopes of a ridge of hills from here. It fades in the distance shattered and broken in many places, bordering a wide stretch of level terrain a few miles wide to the north. In the middle of the plains two mounds rise from the heather.
7502: A few marred steps and piles of huge black boulders lie in this elevated place. Nothing else remains of the ancient temple that once stood here, at the corner of a rocky plateau, overlooking a deep valley to the north and west. Echoes of a dreary power still fill the place and no plant yet dares to grow among the ruins.
7504: A massive lion is here, baring its glistening fangs.

A low natural crack enters the cliff for a few yards, its entrance hidden by thick vegetation. The cave is obviously inhabited - there are some tufts of fur and a few piles of animal waste. In a corner lies a pile of bones, some of them still dark with blood.
7505: A few pines grow here on a small grassy shelf, halfway up a high cliff. From below the shelf would not be visible because of the overhang of the cliff, and even supposing it were, the climb up the sheer face would be near impossible. It is surrounded by sheer drops on every side, and gives a wide view of the land nearby. A path leads westward on a narrow ledge, descending towards the brushy base of the cliff, and would be the only way one could leave this place other than jumping off into the river below.
7506:
A copper penny lies on the ground.
A copper penny lies on the ground.
A copper penny lies on the ground.
A copper penny lies on the ground.

You are meandering through the moors of the Bruinen. The land is rough and hilly, covered with wildly sprawling vegetation and thick ground cover, dry as it is. You are in one of the many hollows that pockmark the moors and you can barely peek over the tops of the surrounding land.
7507: An orchid of light violet petals blossoms nearby.

You have stumbled upon what seems to be a campsite. The remains of a fire lie in the centre of a carefully trampled down heath floor. A shanty constructed of rearranged branches lies to your left. It seems to have been recently occupied but you cannot find a trace of the occupant or occupants, or a clue to their identity, or where they may have gone.
7508: The sharply rising moor tapers away here, giving way to the more gently rolling heath northwards. This area seems to be frequented with travellers and seems to be less wild than the rest of the moors. The air, however, is still and silent, brooding here where land meets sky.
7509: The river here takes a slow, easy turn, and you spot a few small fish down in the water swimming along happily, minding their own business. You can follow the river to the north or to the west or get out onto the shore.
7510: As you take another gentle curve in the river, you find yourself comforted by the peaceful flowing of the river. The bend in the river takes you either to the east or the south.
7511: The river here starts to straighten out heading both to the west and east. The gentle lapping of the water on the shores put you at ease, and to the south you see a worn trade path.
7512: As you flow down the river, letting the current guide you, you wonder just how much of Arda can be reached by rivers. The river continues onward, with a small trade path following it.
7513: The river continues onwards, ever onwards. The peaceful air and the knowledge of the protection of Rivendell make you feel very safe. In fact, you find yourself dozing off every now and then.
7514: The wide river takes another curve here, going to the north and to the west. To the east and south is that small trade path that keeps following the river.
7515: You are still on the river Bruinen. Below you, close to the bottom of the river, you see small fish moving away from you, scared by your presence. The river flows silently through another bend at this point. You can paddle the river going to the south, or to the east.
7516: The river bends east-west here. It slowly runs towards a bend in the west. Reeds grow on the northern riverbank and you see slippy animals wriggling through the mud. A lonesome tree-trunk with a beaver sitting on it is drifting in the river.
7517: The river bends north-west here. In the south-east part of the bend huge amounts of drift-wood have accumulated. Most of the drift-wood is rotten and you wonder how long it takes for wood to rot in this cold climate.
7518: As the river starts to wind around through the land, the path was made to follow it, probably for the easy landmark the river made. The wagon wheel tracks continue, and the road bends again to the south and east.
7519: The path continues on, winding along next to the river. The signs of a trade route are still around, and there some flowers growing alongside the road. Everything seems so peaceful around here.
7520: You stroll out into the plains, making your way through the grass and weeds. Most of the plains lie to the southwest, and beyond them you can see a dark, wildly growing forest. To the south are some gentle hills, and to the west is a well worn trail. Beyond the trail lies the Bruinen.
7521: A large shrub grows here, filling the air with a heavy scent.

As you move farther into the plains, the trail becomes more distant and the grass around you grows taller. There are many kinds of grasses and weeds growing out here, as well as a number of the smaller wild animals. You are in the northeast corner of the plains, as the plains stretch out to the southeast.
7522: The trail goes north-south here. To the west is the river Bruinen and to the east is a dense vegetation you can't enter. The trail is overgrown and for sure not often used these days. In the north is a crossing in the trail where you must decide if you want to go further north or maybe east.
7523: A small grasshopper clings to a blade of grass, ready to spring.

A few small bumps in the ground are beginning to form here, as the plains gently roll into the hills to the south. The hills are not very large, in fact they are barely hills, raising no more than a few feet off the ground. The plains continue on to the north and to the west.
7524:
A brown fox is here, looking for some rabbits to chew up.
A grey wolf is here, salivating profusely.

The plains flow onward here. The tall grasses wave gently in the breeze and small butterflies and dragonflies are flitting about oblivious to your presence. The hills to the south continue on for a while, gently rising above the rest of the plains.
7525: The plains start here, as the path winds it's way through them. The grasses here are less sparse, and grow thicker as you walk out into the plains. The trail is both to the north and the west, with some gentle hills rising to the the south. More plains can be seen to the southwest and to the east.
7526: The river bends north-south here. You see small tunnels in the eastern river- bank and can catch a glimpse of a muskrat. Fishes are swimming in the water and insects are flying about.
7527: The river bends south-east here. The water is ice cold and you can see small ice floes drifting in the river. In the north part of the bend the river flows very slowly. Water vegetation grows there and you see strange, little, green creatures jumping from leaf to leaf.
7528: The trail from the south splits here, with one fork leading north toward a cliff, and the other heading toward the Misty Mountains. The trail is quite overgrown and thick thorny bushes grow to either side.
7529: The ford leads north-south over the Bruinen. The river is wider and calmer here as in the east. The water is shallow enough to pass the river and reach the bank on the other side. The river-bed is muddy and from time to time you trip over rocks.
7530: The trail bends south-west here. It leads along a northern branch of the Bruinen towards a mountain range in the north. The ground is still muddy from the ford in the south and you discover tracks leading north. You can see the remains of an ancient, burned down guard-post or small fort. Someone must have guarded the ford against people or armies coming from the south.
7531: The trail leads east-west here and it leads slowly towards a cliff in the north. The cliff is pretty high and you feel icy winds coming down from it. The trail is leading through barren plains and the landscape is dreary. Under the cliff you will find shelter against the uncomfortable weather.
7532: The trail leads east-west here. Big rocks have fallen down from the cliff. The rocks in the middle of the trail were pushed aside so that horses and horse-drawn carts can pass here.
7533: The trail leads east-west here. Under some rocks you discover a hidden camp- fire. Considering the look of the ashes the fire is maybe two days old. You also find hidden rubbish and the remains of a meal. Finding tracks of people who used the campfire is very hard and you can only guess where they went.
7534: The trail leads east-west here. Broken off branches from trees and bushes are lying on the ground. You wonder where they came from since you can't see any trees or bushes here. Maybe they have fallen down the cliff and above you is a forest or another kind of vegetation? Unluckily you can't see any green leaves and your hope of finding living beings vanishes again.
7535: The trail leads east-west here. In the cliff to the north you can see the entrance to a larger cave. Big footprints lead to the cave. The footprints look like they were made by the paws of a gigantic bear.
7536: The trail leads east-west here. You can see strange paintings in small caves in the cliff. One of the upper caves contains a painting of a dragon and in the northern part of the cave you see a broken altar.
7537: A path is leading north up to a cliff. The trail leads east-west here and leads further east under a high cliff. You find signs of tracks here. The tracks lead from the east to the path north. The trails is used here at least sometimes.
7538: A large pile of boulders is sitting here, probably debris from a rockslide.

The trail leads east and west. East is a crossing of trails, while to the north and south lie just barren, endless plains only interrupted by sky- high cliffs. To the west the trail leads through a small canyon between two cliffs. The canyon is blocked by the remains of a rockslide.
7539: The path is leading north-south and fast up around a cliff. The path is very narrow here and it looks like it is very seldom used. To the east you can see overhanging rocks above your head, but none of them has fallen down yet!
7540: The path bends south-east here. The rocks above you look more unstable and you notice small ones on the ground. A weathered signpost is here, but the writing has long ago faded away. You get a first glimpse of the landscape ahead. It looks plain and empty.
7541: The path is gentle here passing a cliff to the south. To the north are endless empty plains. Rocks are falling down from the cliff and trying to avoid them you nearly fall over the ones in the path. The cliff isn't so high here anymore and you can climb up to its top. The path bends east-west here.
7542: The path leads west-east here. A dense fog is coming from the north what makes it impossible to even guess what comes next and where you really are.
7543: The path leads east-west. A dense fog is coming from the north what makes it impossible to even guess what comes next and where you really are. What evil may be hidden behind the fog, or is it maybe a hidden treasure? The path has reached the same altitude.
7544: The path leads east-west here and leads gently around a forest to the north. Footprints are leading to the forest in the north. Oops, they really look big! You see bones being thrown out of holes in the forest. Broken armour, weapons and other equipment lies around and you are for sure not the first careless traveller who has ended his life in a big cooking pot!
7545: The path leads east-west here and passes a forest to the north. Dark shadows lie over the path and a cold wind from the north blows icy air into your face. Human skeletons are pinned to stone stakes in front of the forest. It looks like evil creatures have eaten the poor ones alive!
7546: The path bends north-west here. It leads away from the cliff in the south to a mountain chain in the north. There is snow on top of the mountains. The path is surrounded by empty plains.
7547: The path bends east-south here. You can discover signs that the path is still inuse. Tracks of small groups passing swiftly are here. Barren plains surround the path. The plains stretch north until they reach another cliff.
7548: The path leads east-west here. Every once in a while you notice skeletons, bleached by the sun, beside the path. It becomes colder and colder and you are sure that many of the dead travellers were frozen to death.
7549: The path leads east-west here. Icy winds blow into your face as you walk on towards a branch of the river Bruinen. Further in the east you see that the path leads northwards into a long forgotten, evil land. The mountain-range in north therefore must be the Coldfells.
7550: This path, now merely a swath of trampled down vegetation, once was an often used route to the evil northern kingdom of Angmar. Now fallen, Angmar is rarely visited except by wicked and fell minions of the Enemy. The ground and grass beneath your feet is laden heavily with frost, numbing your toes as the wind numbs nearly all of the rest of you. The path continues to the north and west.
7551: Turning to the east and south, the path to Angmar heads northward, between the cliffs to the east and the terrain to the west. The chill wind blows strongly from the North, bringing with it a heavily-laden frost, telling a tale of woe for the evil of Angmar.
7552: Following the clear and cold river that laps upon the banks that border the east of the road, this path bends west and north. Farther to the south, a small patch of woods is nestled in a small nook between the river and the sheer cliff-face, refusing either to be swept away by the current or be pushed out by the stone.
7553: A strange man, dressed in black priestly-garb, walks here (glowing).

Straight north and south this path goes, directly itself un-erringly to the north, to the fallen ruins of Angmar. You feet trod on, leaving footprints where the frozen grass does not straighten. Surely easy to track, but you hope fervently that nothing would want to follow you.
7554: A sturdy pack horse is standing here.

The path to Angmar diverges from the cliff-faces to the east, fearing to stray from the fastest course. Why anything or anybody would want to explore further northward, you have little idea...only evil could await you there. Pulling your cloak tighter against the icy winds, you march onward, determined.
7555: The plain stretches in every direction. Stones cover the ground and from time to time you find bushes and small areas where grass and other vegetation grows. It looks like this barren landscape will go on forever. But wait! You find something like a path where the rocks were pushed aside, but you can't discover any tracks.
7556: You have entered an area of plain, barren plains. Spare vegetation grows here and the ground is covered with frost. In the north you can see a high mountain- range. The plain stretches from the east to the west as far as you can see.
7557: The progress here is very difficult. Large rocks are in your way and you have problems to discover paths between them. On the other hand the rocks also give you some shelter against the icy wind.
7558: You find tracks leading north here. The tracks are less hidden as you go northwards. You can't escape the icy wind that comes down the mountains in the north and you have just made it half the way to the mountains.
7559: You can barely see your own hands. The fog here is really unbelievably thick. It just cannot be natural fog! The plain is barren and empty here and you feel that there are no living beings near.
7560: Fog, fog, fog! You feel a soft wind coming from the north; maybe that's the direction where it comes from? The fog stops where the forest begins in the east. Small round stones can be found and the ground is covered with frost.
7561: A brutish forest troll is hunting here, looking for some tasty flesh.

The forest suddenly becomes very dark here. The trees build a solid top that blocks the sunlight totally. You notice broken off branches and small openings in the undergrowth. It looks like huge creatures walk through this forest. As you progress deeper into the forest you see smoke coming out of holes in the ground.
7562: A large earth troll is digging here, looking for some tasty morsels.

The forest is extremely dark here and the undergrowth is very thick. The trees are overgrown with moss and it even hangs down from their branches. Gigantic funguses grow on rotten tree stumps and thorny bushes are everywhere. Ouch! A hole is in the ground.
7563: You are going through an endless looking snow-field. The snow is driven away by the icy wind out of the north. Soon you tracks are blown away by the wind and you risk getting lost.
7564: It becomes colder and colder. Here is much snow that has build dunes and the snow reaches up to your hip. The high snow makes it possible for you to see your tracks at least for some minutes before they are covered under the snow again.
7566: The ground is slightly covered with snow and an ice-cold wind chills your bones. A few crippled bushes exist here, barely covered with dark-green needles.
7567: Snow over snow, here is so much snow that it makes you sick. The reflecting sunlight makes it harder and harder for you to see anything. You should leave here soon or you will slowly turn blind. To the south-west you can see a forest but large dunes of snow in front of it make it impossible for you to go there.
7568: The aren't so many rocks here as before and you feel the icy wind from the north again. In front of a rock you make a cruel discovery. Two frozen mummies inside of iron cages. Someone must have put them here that they froze to death.
7569: The tracks slowly lead west and you discover hidden signs on the rocks. It is so cold here that even the vegetation is completely frozen. Here it is where the icy winds from the north hit the plain.
7570: Finally you have reached the mountains. The mountains go vertically up for quite a while and build a cliff. Under the cliff you find shelter from the icy wind. Slowly recovering you look around and are surprised. The vegetation that grows here is dense and looks like someone has planted it. The tracks lead to the west.
7571:
A white wolf is here.
A white wolf is here.
A hungry warg is standing here, ridden by you.

Shadows lie over this plain and giving those not accustom to the lower light an uneasy feeling. In the sky one can often seen black crows circling above. The crow's eyes seem to pierce even the darkest shadows as if they are spying upon the land looking for intruders.
7572: A black crow flies low to the ground here, looking for carrion to eat.
You find areas which look like fields, even when you are not sure what plants grow here. The plants must be extremely resistant against frost. To the west is the entrance to a small village.
7573: Traces of pale white tones form the aura of this place.

You are standing in front of a wooden gate that blocks the entrance to the hillmen village. The village is surrounded by a wooden stockade. A small tower is built above the gate for the guards on watch. Evil signs are painted on the gate. It is pretty obvious that you will be hanged on the highest post available.
7574:
The corpse of a hillman-warrior is lying here.
The corpse of a hillman-warrior is lying here.

You are under the watch-tower. The tunnel you are in is leading north inside the village. Embrasures are in the wooden tunnel walls and you see a second, open gate at the exit inside the village. Wagon tracks are in the mud and horse-droppings cover the ground.
7576:
A hillmen warrior is here, ready to fight.
A hillmen-chief is here, ruling his village.

The town hall is the large wooden building that mainly consists of a single room. A long wooden table stretches from the south to the north end of the room. The table is surrounded by wooden chairs with odd looking patterns on them. At the northern end of the table stands a large throne-like chair. The floor is built completely out of wooden planks and the windows even have panes of glass. The town hall is used for sittings of the village council or for feasts when the weather is too cold outside, which it is most of the year of course.
7578:
A hillmen child is here, playing with his toys.
A hillmen woman is here, chatting about local news.

The house's furniture is plain and simple. You see a wardrobe, two chairs and a table. The floor consists out of stamped loam. Above you is the sleeping chamber and a small storage room, but there is no obvious way up. In the south part of the house is a fireplace which is also used as a hearth. The shutters are closed and can be made waterproof with oily fabrics.
7580: A huge stone-portal can be seen to the west. This must be the entrance to the grave of an Angmar Lord. Pictures of evil spirits are painted on the portal and you see a sign that tells you that this is the grave of an Angmar war-leader. You wonder again why this grave isn't guarded more. You can look through holes, in the portal and the walls, into the grave but you don't see any evil spirits or skeletons in the grave.
7581: A guardian stone beast is here, protecting the grave.

A stone made sarcophagus is in the west part of the room. It is simple and without carvings on its sides, just a smooth sarcophagus. There are no treasure chests here and no signs of hidden treasure rooms. Statues of warriors are standing around the sarcophagus building a small army.
7582: An intact skeleton of a man is walking around here.

You find yourself in a cold dank and dusty chamber. The ground underfoot is uneven and quite hard - closer inspection shows it to be made of solid rock, as are the walls. However, the uneven shape and unfinished textures suggest that this place was hewn by no mortal hand.
7584: This cramped passageway twists and turns, and in places it seems doubtful whether you will be able to proceed any further. Progress is hampered not only by the sharp changes of direction, but also by the small dimensions of the crawlspace, and by its rough and unfinished nature; sharp outcrops of hard stone keep tearing at you as you try to move on.
7585:
A skeleton of some humanoid lies in the dust.
An intact skeleton of a man is walking around here.
An intact skeleton of a man is walking around here.

The walls, floor and ceiling of this chamber appear to be rough-hewn, or perhaps they were not carved by mortal hand at all, but rather this is a natural cave. At one time somebody built a stone staircase out of this place, but that has long since collapsed to a pile of useless rubble, and it seems that to escape from this place one might need to be quite skilled at climbing.
7586: The tunnel is very dark and narrow. You realise that the walls in the rooms before were all softly glowing, spending light to light the rooms. Skeleton skulls can be seen in small niches in the wall. You feel the presence of evil spirits near.
7587:
A wooden statue of a guardian suddenly creaks, slowly turning to life.
A spirit floats towards you and howls with an evil laughter.

The room doesn't look special as you expected it to. It has the same paintings and runes on the wall as the room above. Statues are in the corners of the room, they look like guardian statues. You wonder who or what really guards this burial mound. A dark tunnel leads west.
7589:
Zee the Tarkhnarb Orc, wielding an ornate, steel-shafted warhammer, is standing here.
A hungry warg stands here, sniffing around for flesh.
Witchkin the Black Numenorean, wielding an ashen blade, is standing here.
A sturdy trained horse is standing here.

Now you have found the place where all this fog comes from. The hill is about twice as high as an average human and its surface is smooth and black. Strange red glowing runes are written on the hill. The hill doesn't look natural at all and you wonder how runes can glow. This hill is surely a magical construction.
7590: You really must be near now. The fog is so thick here that you can't even see your own hands. As you go further north-east you bump into rocks right and left of you. You are going through a narrow passage.
7591: The fog becomes thicker and thicker now, but you discover that the fog doesn't cover a big area. It comes from something in the north-east. The rocky ground is interrupted by small, dust covered areas. You see strange irregularities in the dust.
7592: This must be an old battlefield. You see frost-covered skeletons everywhere and you find rusty swords and armour here. There are two types of skeletons, one kind looks like human skeletons and the other kind is much smaller. Maybe orc- skeletons? You also discover that the armour is split into three different types. This looks like a battlefield of old Angmar. Orcs and hillmen fighting against other humans.
7593: The stench in this hole makes you vomit. Unidentifiable dirt is everywhere here on the ground. You can't see any furniture. The hole is barely lit with light that comes from the opening above. You feel a light wind coming out of the north-west corner.
7594: A powerful young troll stares at you.

The tunnel bends east-west here. Water is dropping from the ceiling and the ground is covered with a black, slimy mass. Shadows flit over the tunnel walls. You hear screams coming from the west where the tunnel widens into an inter- section. There is a hole in the east wall.
7595:
A stone troll is standing here, scowling about.
A powerful young troll stares at you.
A powerful young troll stares at you.

Two tunnels, one from the south and one from the east, are crossing each other here. They lead west into the main part of this underground area. Skull-headed staffs stick right and left of you in front of the tunnel walls. This is for sure no resting place for an exhausted traveller!
7596: As you enter the hole you see a small path leading north through piles of trash. The hole was dug out a long time ago and it looks like the entrance to a larger underground construction. Maybe it was built to give sun-shy creatures shelter in the day?
7597:
An old, strong cave troll is standing here.
A stone troll is standing here, scowling about.
A powerful young troll stares at you.
A powerful young troll stares at you.
A powerful young troll stares at you.

You are in a large room with a big fire in the centre. On top of the fire is a huge cooking pot. The pot is even big enough to put complete human beings in it! You see a screaming head looking over the edge of the cooking pot waving at you and begging for mercy and help. All kinds of eaten up body parts are scattered over the ground.
7598: A large mean-looking troll is here.

In this room there is a large grill. A corpse spit on a roasting spit slowly cooks over it. From the size of the corpse you can only guess that this poor creature once was a dwarf or hobbit. In the north-east corner you can see more corpses ready prepared for the fire. In the small pot next to the grill a sauce for the meat is boiling. You don't dare to think what the sauce is made of.
7599: Approaching the mighty joining, the river takes leave of the path and boldly and confidently flows south, its icy current allowing no argument from any that travel its course. The cold waters seem to rejoice and splash amongst themselves; soon they will have less to fear from Angmar.
7600: Faster and faster the current flows, coming closer and closer to the lands of the south that are not choked with the dust of ruin and evil. To the east, the cliff-sides turn from the river, and now broken and rough lands border the path. An eerie howl gives the impression that the river is not totally safe.
7601: Running along the little-used trail that goes north to where Angmar once stood, this branch of the Bruinen seems eager to join with its brothers. Flowing steadily and strongly to the south, its cold depths occasionally, and very briefly, reveal some silvery fish.
7602: The deep waters follow the bend of the path, turning briefly westward before, a bit away, they turn back to the south. Although the stone cliff to the south forces the river to abandon the hardy woods to the west, the river does not leave without battering the wall continuously, and in years to come the current may know victory. Although rushed to leave the north, it seems to be patiently trying to destroy the cliff.
7603: The clear, icy waters flow past the earthy banks of the forest to the east, granting the life-giving water to the pines that crave it. To the west, you can see a grassy path, and farther to the east, over the trees, a mighty cliff, red and brown and yellow, stands over the river and its surroundings.
7604: The path to Angmar and this river follow each other dedicatedly, perhaps together they feel safer from the fell fortune of the North. Nevertheless, both seem to go as fast as they can to leave that accursed realm. The cold current pushes your southward, eager to continue its journey.
7605: Directly east of the river stands a cliffside, directing even the strong current of this eager branch with an indifferent ease. But the red-brown sandy bottom of the river tell the tale of who really wins in this eternal struggle. To the south, a slight rising in the ground pushes the river westward, allowing a small grove of trees to survive.
7606: Directly east of the river stands a cliffside, directing even the strong current of this eager branch with an indifferent ease. But the red-brown sandy bottom of the river tell the tale of who really wins in this eternal struggle. The river flows to the south, fleeing the cold realm of Angmar and seeking safety with the other tributaries with which it will join.
7607: The plain is a continuation of the cliffs east and south. It is covered with large boulders which make it possible for you to avoid the worst of the cold blowing wind. In the north part of the plain, near a winding path, you find a weathered wooden cross.
7608: The cliff ends here and the surrounding areas all have the same altitude, but the landscape is still rising towards the north. Brown moss covers the cliff and little black creatures are running around. The spare vegetation is stooped to the south from the constant blowing wind.
7609: The river bends south-east here. The river is surrounded by high cliffs to the north-west and south-east. The cliffs channel the water and make the river very wild for a small section. You can see calmer parts near the riverbanks where you can progress further.
7610: Clear, deep and strong this cold river runs, flowing steadily over any rocks that may try to obstruct its path. It veers west, avoiding the rough ground of the steppes to the south. The current comes from the north, pushing to join with other tributaries to form the mighty Bruinen.
7611: A sturdy pack horse is standing here.

The cliff slowly turns northwards. To the east you can see a northern branch of the Bruinen flowing towards a crossing with another branch of the river. The cliff builds a canyon with a cliff further east. The trail down the cliff bends to the south and leads along the Bruinen towards a destination unknown.
7612: No vegetation and no rocks are here. Just a grey, empty plain. A path is leading through the plain, you wonder where it leads to. Going near the cliff looks pretty dangerous. Icy gusts of wind may blow you away and over the cliff.
7613: The vegetation is lighter here as in the forest to the west. The bushes are dried out and there are no trees here. Sand covers the rocky ground but you can't discover any tracks here. Down you can see a trail coming out of the west leading towards a ford in the Bruinen.
7614: A huge warg is here, moving in for the kill.

The forest looks rotten here and the trees are decaying. Trees are split in half and others look like someone with really big teeth was chewing on them. The undergrowth is trampled into the ground and no signs of living animals can be found. A cold wind comes from the north.
7615:
A white wolf is here, prowling for something to eat.
A huge warg is here, moving in for the kill.
A white wolf is here, prowling for something to eat.

You are in a dark forest. Dead, burned-out trees surround you and the ground glooms in a dark light. The trees look like they have turned to stone a long time ago and they have no leaves. You are not sure if they are alive or not! A couple of trees are broken off and you wonder who and what for they are used now.
7616: A dense fog is coming from the north and you can barely see your own hands. You can't see anything of the surrounding landscape and you are not sure where the cliff ends. It is very quiet here and the only living thing you can find is lichen on the rocks.
7617: The cliff is a break in the slowly rising landscape. Huge rocks are lying on the ground making it almost impossible for you to move on, but you have a perfect view over the surrounding landscape. Down the cliff you can see a trail bending from the east to the west. A path is leading north-east from the trail and you can see the Bruinen in the south.
7618:
A cavebear is sleeping here.
A hungry warg stands here, sniffing around for flesh.

Piles of bones lie around and you see torn apart clothes. The cave is only a small hole in the cliff. Cockroaches and rats run round trying to get their share of the leftovers. You notice that the cave was once clawed in the rock. Either these creatures have left or were driven out by the big, wild bear.
7619: Hastily Built Bridge over a River

The river bends north-south here. To the east are rocky steppes and to the west a riverbank that is too high and steep to climb up. However, roughly carved logs have been haphazardly thrown together to allow passage. The work looks quite recent. To the north a region of rapids begins and the white caps of fast moving water can be seen. You see fish jumping out of the water trying to avoid the rapids.
7620: Between the two tributaries, and just west of a cliff, these grounds seem rather out of place. The going is rough, as the footing is uneven and uncertain; a hasty step could result in a sprain--the very thought of being stranded here, unable to leave, makes you shiver...and not from the cold.
7621: Closer to the cliffs, the ground gets more broken and rockier, and your legs weary of their travels, but resting here seems to be the less desirable alternative. The freezing river is to the east and south, and north the cliffs begin.
7622: The ground rises, approaching the red-orange cliffs that stand to the north-east. The steep sides of the cliff might provide a windbreak, but surely any other creatures that frequent this land must know that too. Perhaps returning to the road would be best.
7623: Small and insignificant you appear at the base of these mighty cliffs, rising so far above you head and cutting through the clouds themselves. The colour of the rock of the cliff-face, reds and browns and oranges intermixed, remind you of a sunset, but no sunlight warms this cold land, only the dull-grey of the sky could provide any illumination.
7624: The ruddy cliff continues here, blocking any hope of going north. Any fancy to climb up the face ends quite quickly if the sheer side is gazed at. How could any puny human dare challenge the immortality of these ancient stone landmarks? The river, though swift and cold, would be much easier to travel on.
7625: Still the mountainside continues, and it seems to go on perpetually east and west. The rocky ground seems to have been, at one point, part of the cliff face; but over the centuries and ages the wind and rain and ice have pried from the wall any rock even slightly loose. You cover you head quickly, fearful of any latecoming rocks that may decide to join their brethen.
7626: A sharp-eyed hawk is here stalking some prey.

A hard ride either west or east would not bring you to the end of this cliff-face, so wide and broad is it. Its rich red-earth tones are only occasionally marred by the nests of various bird of prey that dot the rock with darker patches of brown and black. You wonder how a raptor could survive in this land, barren and lifeless, devoid of almost any prey, and living in a nest continually battered by the icy winds that blast the mountainside. They must be truly hardy beasts.
7627: As your legs grow weary of this rocky base, your eyes travels over to the southwest, where the river flows by at a brisk pace. You can see no feasible way to enter it, and content yourself with knowing that it is not that far off. This must truly be a savage place, you think to yourself, if the freezing waters of the tributary seem mild by comparison.
7628: A sharp-eyed hawk is here stalking some prey.

Stoney silence is all that you hear here, except for your own breathing and footsteps. Rarely, a piercing cry of a raptor is heard, shattering the silence with a chilling hunting cry. You pull your cloak closer to your body, and hurry on in your journey.
7629: Klaees (thedon), wielding a great warsword, is standing here.

Curses escape from your lips as these cliffs continue, and show no sign of ending anywhere soon. Your legs ask for a respite from the futile task of following the cliffs to their end, and your skin begs for warmth and shelter from the icy winds.
7630: Klaees (thedon), wielding a great warsword, is standing here.

The cliffs continue on, racing alongside the river and forcing any who pass to follow its course. However, the ground here seems to be made of smaller pieces of rock, allowing your legs a momentary rest before starting off again onto rougher terrains. The cliff is a majestic red-brown colour, and it almost seems warm in this cold clime.
7631: The cliffs continue along the river to the south. Erosion has eaten several feet from the outside of the road, but the grey rock has otherwise withstood the elements. Gazing south, a forest of pine stands haughtily. The Grey Mountains surround the pines almost engulfing them.
7632: Turning east with the river, the russet colour of the cliffs begins to be corrupted by the drab greys and blacks of harder stone. The rocky ground that forms the bank of the river has been worn away with time so that the river is an immediate drop from the edge of the path. Very little vegetation survives here, but what there is looks quite hardy. A bit north of the immediate cliffs, mighty mountains rise up, the first signs of Hithaeglir.
7633: Path at the Base of a Cliff

The soft whitewash from a single birds nest stands in glaring contrast to the grey slate that dominates the landscape. The path firms up here and shows signs of recent use and continues on to the east and west.
7634: The path widens out to a road here. Grey rock again forming the bed of the road. The ground swells upward slightly and continues in a definite upward grade to the east. The river dwindles into the distance and breaks away to the east. The summits of the stately cliffs still tower high above.
7635: There are two statues of trolls posed in a moment of flight here.

Steeper and steeper the incline becomes to the east. The road, while easier travelling than the path is definitely more taxing on the body. All the land seem grey now, barren and lifeless up to the whitecaps of the mountains. No natural animals can be found here, no matter how thoroughly you look. There doesn't appear to be any other way into the mountains but this way.
7636: The cliffs abruptly end as the river veers away for a time. The road winds its way slowly up a hill before heading west in the distance. The sinewy path of the road can be seen snaking in and out of jagged outcroppings of grey rock. The only way is up or back west.
7637: The road crests here and begins a slow jaunt to the north. The cliffs are no more. They have been engulphed by the dreadful mountains that rule this region, which seems to lie pale and weak below these terrible heights. One such peak you stand on now, yet instead of feeling mighty and above the world, you feel all, alone, and utterly helpless. With a simple shrug these mountains could end your existence -- but they deign not to notice your plight.
7638: All about you is mountains. The scrubby fauna doesn't seem to be able to survive at this altitude. The road is little more than broken stubble here, a grey steep slope that helps your legs little. The trail of rubble bends to the east again.
7639: Your legs tire of constantly ascending and descending these mountain slopes. The grey rock that forms the road is loose and jagged, and every step must be watched lest you injure yourself. Aside from several small scrubs and hardy grasses, you can find no life here. The road has fallen into heavy disrepair here, but heavy foot prints can still be seen. A smaller path descends northwards.
7640: A trail runs through here, covered with greenish moss and slightly slippery. It seems the path has not been used in some time. Both to the north and to the south it winds into the mountains, steeply to the south, more gently northwards.
7641: The grey slate once more resembles a road and seems to lead somewhere. A dark ominous tower, almost blending in with the mountains as backdrop can be glimpsed to the east. The road also heads west here.
7642: A Road through the Grey Mountains

The grey rock of the road comes to a halt before a massive tower made of the same slate grey rock of the road. Mountains abound on all sides, and any entrance further east becomes decidedly tougher. The tower itself seems to be in disrepair, but all signs also indicate recent occupants. The road continues to the west and the din of a river relentlessly punishing stone occasionally drifts from the south. More mountains stretch east, inhospitable as ever. A small metal plaque has been fixed to the tower wall, beside the door.
7643: The trail continues, dodging some large, dense bushes and particularly impressive pine. Here it is cool and quiet, with only a slight breeze disturbing the stillness. High above, patches in the canopy allow you to see some sky.
7644:
A very strong orkish leader is here on patrol.
An orc sentry is here on patrol.
An experienced orkish scout is looking for tracks on the ground.
An orc soldier is standing here.
An orc soldier is standing here.
An orc soldier is standing here.
An orc soldier is standing here.
An orc soldier is standing here.

The air about you is soothing; and far away indeed seem the cares and dangers of the Ettenmoors. The cold light of the sun is shaded by several old pine- trees that border the path, and these same pines shelter you from the chill wind; but the tops of the trees sway back and forth, paying that much homage to the icy blasts. The ground grows rockier to the north, and the moss that covers the ground begins to give way to tougher grasses.
7645: Strange tracks on the ground lead to the north. You have descended a bit in elevation from when you were east of here, and you are now surrounded completely by mountains. From just to your west, you can hear screams. Or maybe it's just wolves howling. How can you be sure though?
7646: Phew! You're finally there. Walking in the mountains, you can see all the lands around you. Far below you see the river, winding along from the eerie Misty Mountains in the far east to the safer parts of the world in the west. Next to the river you can see a small trail.
7647: Up and up you go. Soon you will be among the mountains themselves, but here you are only about halfway up. You are climbing up in a small ravine that was carved by a stream running down from the mountains, so you aren't able to see any of the surrounding lands yet. Just a little higher and you'll be there.
7648: The foothills are getting bigger and steeper. Soon you will be climbing up the eastern face of the Grey Mountains. To continue on, you must climb up the steep, darkly coloured stone. It looks quite dangerous from here, but the view might be worth it.
7649: Clambering up the boulders from the river below, you find yourself among some foothills made of dark stone that rise up sharply to the west. To your east, you can make out the river far below. The rock face to your north makes passage impossible. You can faintly hear strange noises coming from the mountains to your west.
7650: A Shallow Section of the River
A grey wolf is here, salivating profusely.

Here, the river is very wide and shallow, making a crossing without a boat possible. The water is clear and you can see what might be bones among the stones at the bottom of the river. To the south a path continues on, heading for the mountains to the east. To the north, boulders have fallen from the mountains all the way down to the banks of the river, and you can probably make your way among them if you are careful.
7651: Trail Meets a Tributary of the Bruinen

The trail is now at the same elevation as the river. To the north, the river looks peaceful and easy to ford. You can continue to follow the trail east or west. You can also enter some foothills to the south if you are feeling VERY brave.
7652: Maybe you should have headed into the foothills. You are almost overcome with dread and fear as you survey the barren lands around you. Shrill screams sink down to your alert ears from the mountains and hills around you. The calm and safety that you knew so well just to the west of here are just a memory now long gone...
7653: The trail splits in two and heads south and north. To the north, it continues along high above the river. To the south, it slowly disappears as it climbs up into the Misty Mountains. To the east, a cliff wall keeps you from being able to ascend to the mountain tops above you.
7654: It's never too late to turn back. It's beginning to look like it might be too late very soon. You know nothing has changed in the last few minutes, but every time you look up, the sky seems darker. The worn trail runs carelessly to the east and west. Your passage is hopelessly blocked to the north and south by dense growth.
7655: A furry, striped raccoon is here, nosing around for some berries or roots.

Far below you, you can see rough whitewater rapids in the river. It looks like a very dangerous place. The trail here is well-used. Along it, you see dark spots that look suspiciously like blood. A piece of skin and a clump of fur (or is it hair?) is lying on the ground.
7656: Your whole body suddenly feels cold and icy. The temperature has not fallen, but something dark and cold has overcome you. You can't help but feel wild and hopeless despair as you look to the east. It is hard to see very far in any direction. You aren't sure if it is foggy or if there is something wrong with you.
7657: A demon wolf lurks here, its dark form twisting and hiding its shape.

South of here you can see the Worn Foothills. They seem to curse this land with their barren loneliness. A cold wind blows from the east, making you shiver. The trail is worn into the ground here, and the steep hills to your south block your passage. To your north, you can see a river flowing steadily along. The river's bank is too steep to climb down.
7658: The trail has been partly washed away. It's still passable, but don't get too close to the edge. The trail goes east and south and the northwest edge has been completely washed down into the river far below. You can only pray that it doesn't rain again before you come back this way, because the trail might not be here much longer.
7659: If you continue east, you will be wandering in the foothills of the Misty Mountains. The trail you are on continues to the north. You hear strange sounds and cries rising out of the foothills. Panic begins to cloud your thinking. Maybe it would be best if you hurried on past this place.
7660: A grey wolf is here, salivating profusely.

Cutting through dense vegetation, the trail winds and twists and it rises up to the mountains in the east. Looking just to the east, you can see that you will soon be walking among some small foothills. What you can see of the trail takes a crazy path up through the foothills.
7661: Your legs burn from the steep rise. How much farther, you wonder, could this accursed trail rise? How many boulders could there be... never had you imagined so many of the big black things had existed. Each one blocks the trail, or is placed such as to confound attempts at travel. And all around, the grey dead lands brood vacantly.
7662: Now you travel up a rocky incline, and not as the crow flies. For each step to the east, another three is taken to the north, and a quick knee-scraping scramble up. Movement here is maddeningly slow, but not life-threatening. You couldn't fall more than a few feet in these harsh rocks. You almost wish for some danger, for some relief from the stifling, monotonous climb.
7663: Here the trail straightens out a bit, and you can see what lies ahead, finally. No forest, no city -- only a trail sprawls out to either side, for what seems miles. The very wind here seems dull and dead, the rocks seem less alive than granite could ever be. The only thing more repulsive than this roadway is the insanely dark and broken lands surrounding it.
7664: More and more trail lies in either direction. All there is, is the trail. Impassable badlands border the road on each side, and it is all you can do to cling to its rocky surface, the only remnant of civilisation for miles. And it climbs, higher and higher, to the east. Far in the distance the Misty Mountains rise before you threateningly.
7665: The road is hard and stony under your feet, and the sharp and bony rocks seem to penetrate hard leather boots. Slowly the path rises to the east, in a roundabout way. There are many obstacles to pass; many fallen trees to circumvent, splintering boulders to clamber over, and crumbling ledges to avoid. All around the land is wasted and dark, like an insiduous graying has overtaken it, sucking the life and vitality, and leaving only a pale carcass of shale and carbon.
7666: The trail has ascended enough to form a slight lookout. Peering around, you can see the pine forest falling away to the southwest, and in its place barren and broken badlands spread across the steppes of the Hithaeglir. To the north, across a frigid shining river, the vanguard of the Misty Mountains rises up grey and solemn, subjugating the majestic cliffs far to the west.
7667: Your wearying legs definitely detect an upward grade in this trail. Slowly it will climb up, ascending up the mountains to roll down to the forests below, on the other side. The miles between you and the path's completion are too numerous to even comprehend, many a day will you be travelling before you reach its end. A frantic thought enters your mind : IF you reach the end. You hear the crawling vermin that inhabit the Misty Mountains do not take kindly to travellers.
7668: Turning east and south, this trail has fully diverged from the forest. Now, however, the grey and drab landscape that slowly surrounds you seems to draw your life and vitality from your body. The dark and frightening forest seemed so alive and welcome in comparison. Soon there will be no more trees, only scraggly shrubs clingly desparately to the grey sides of the mountains.
7669: Leaving the forest to the south, the trail turns briefly north. The ground rises with this bend, and soon you are breathing heavily from the incline. A greyer shade covers the land here, darkening the cold, clear blue sky to the west with the grey, dead sky to the east. You remember stories of your childhood about fell trolls and orcs that inhabit the ettenmoors, and hope they were merely tales told to scare naughty children.
7670: A bit to the north, there lies a freezing river that rushes uncontrollably to the west. It cannot flood the trail in its panic, for it is bordered by a steep bank that would plunge any man into the icy depths. To the south, the forest borders the road and from it come some evil and foul grunts. But the trail continues east and west, straight as a blade.
7671: Travelling further east and west, this trail will eventually climb up the Hithaeglir Mountains. A chill and brutal wind flies from the sky, battering the trees in the forest to the south and the cliffs to the north. And you are no exception; every piece of your skin burns and stings, and your eyes water from the cold.
7672: Stretching east to west, this trail promises little but danger as it takes you towards the mountains. Going back is not necessarily safe either, as the trail is bordered by wilderness that only the strongest may survive in. A stiff wind whips your hair about, and your cloak avails you little to keep warm.
7673: Bending south and east, this trail promises little but danger as it takes you towards the mountains. Going back is not necessarily safe either, as the trail is bordered by wilderness that only the strongest may have any hope to live. You quicken your pace to avoid any encounter with the beasts that inhabit this icy realm.
7674: Turning west and north, this trail promises little but danger as it takes you towards the mountains. Going back is not necessarily safe either, as the trail is bordered by wilderness that only the strongest may survive in. To the south, you can see a dark forest, from which very little sound comes. It seems strangely quiet and almost too peaceful.
7675: Bending south and east, this trail promises little but danger as it takes you towards the mountains. Going back is not necessarily safe either, as the trail is bordered by wilderness that only the strongest may survive in. The Misty Mountains seems a bit closer here. You are not sure whether that is ill or good fortune.
7676: Turning west and north, this trail promises little but danger as it takes you towards the mountains. Going back is not necessarily safe either, as the trail is bordered by wilderness that only the strongest may survive in. To the south and east, you can see a dark forest, from which various snarls and howls greet you. The road seems endless, the miles stretch out before and behind you, and you feel so stranded...
7677: Bending south and east, this trail promises little but danger as it takes you towards the mountains. Going back is not necessarily safe either, as the trail is bordered by wilderness that only the strongest may survive in. The majestic peaks stand mightily to the north, proudly displaying their reddish colour to all that might watch.
7678: Turning west and north, this trail promises little but danger as it takes you towards the mountains. Going back is not necessarily safe either, as the trail is bordered by wilderness that only the strongest may survive in. To the south and east, you can see a dark forest, from which various snarls and howls greet you. Several pairs of eyes peer at you from that forest.
7679: Stretching east to west, this trail promises little but danger as it takes you towards the mountains. Going back is not necessarily safe either, as the trail is bordered by wilderness that only the strongest may survive in. To the south, you can see a gloomy forest, from which various snarls and howls greet you. Soft footfalls travel with you, emanating from the south.
7680: Stretching east to west, this trail promises little but danger as it takes you towards the mountains. Going back is not necessarily safe either, as the trail is bordered by wilderness that only the strongest may survive in. To the south, you can see a murky forest, from which various snarls and howls greet you. The sound of panting causes you to be alert. It must have come from the forest.
7681: Bending south and east, this trail promises little but danger as it takes you towards the Hithaeglir Mountains. You dare not venture from the road, as about this countryside there lies a wilderness that only the strongest or most cunning could survive in. A small animal--perhaps a squirrel--darts away from the trail.
7682: Turning west and north, this trail promises little but danger as it takes you towards the mountains. Going back is not necessarily safe either, as the trail is bordered by wilderness that only the strongest may survive in. To the east, you can see a murky forest, from which various snarls and howls greet you. The cries of birds can also be heard from the forest.
7683: Stretching east to west, this trail promises little but danger as it takes you towards the mountains. Going back is not necessarily safe either, as the trail is bordered by wilderness that only the strongest may survive in. The vegetation to the south is too thick to allow an egress that way, but to the north the river borders the road, inviting you for a refreshing, if freezing, boat ride. Your ears are soothed by the sound of water flowing past rocks, coming from the river to the north.
7684: Stretching east to west, this trail promises little but danger as it takes you towards the mountains. Going back is not necessarily safe either, as the trail is bordered by wilderness that only the strongest may survive in. The vegetation to the south is too thick to allow an egress that way, but to the north the river borders the road, inviting you for a refreshing, if freezing, boat ride. The whistle of the wind on the cliff-tops is shrill in your ears.
7685: Stretching east to west, this trail promises little but danger as it takes you towards the mountains. Going back is not necessarily safe either, as the trail is bordered by wilderness that only the strongest may survive in. The vegetation to the south is too thick to allow an egress that way, but to the north the river borders the road, inviting you for a refreshing, if freezing, boat ride. A stiff wind blows through, and no cloak can keep out the chill that it brings.
7686: The trail runs east-west here. Wilderness surrounds the trail and to north you can see a crossing in the Bruinen. The countryside is rough and wild and an icy wind from the north chills your bones.
7687: The main branch of the Bruinen meets here with a northern branch of the river. Due to temperature differences in the two different branches turbulence arises.
7688: In its last solitary moments, this river surges forward, past the broken lands to the north and the trail to the south. In mere moments it will be joined, removing its impurities and venturing to the healing lands of Elrond. This accursed land will soon be far behind you, if you follow the river's wise path.
7689: Navigating between the rocky steppes to the north and the broad trail to the south, the river relaxes, safe in the knowlege that soon it will be swimming with its brother. But still the water is cold and clear, and it has not rid itself of the bitter taint of the Hithaeglir. Perhaps it never will, and perhaps it will never forget the torment that it and the hills around it suffered from the orcs.
7690: Returning to face west, this river borders the seemingly well travelled trail to the south. Almost condolingly, the waters wave goodbye to the trail, fearing for its safety when it will trudge through the mountains, but glad that it will not have to face that horror again. The current picks up speed at it comes nearer to the warm lands of the south.
7691: Avoiding the frozen and broken grounds to the west, the river twists quickly before returning to its normal path. The steppes that the waters avoid are certainly unhospitable, and offer less solace than this river. The icy clumps of earth seem even colder than the freezing water.
7693: The river straightens out again, taking a more westward course. Over the roaring and splashing of the waves you are on, you can faintly hear the distant murmur of yet another tributary. Perhaps they will soon meet and join, forming a stronger river, safer from the terrors in both their birth- places.
7694: A small break in the steep bank to the southeast allows a glance at a small section of the road there, and the dark pine forest beyond. The gloomy forest seems more interesting than these frigid waters, the strange taste of which lingers for hours at the slightest sip or small splash on the lips. A long strange howl makes the forest perhaps too interesting.
7695: The cliff-sides to the north seem to glow with a majestic red-orange, and a lone hawk is briefly silouetted against the luminence, before it returns to its nest. You wonder where and what it hunts, for you have seen no small game or ground creatures in this debateable land. Even the river you are on holds no fish, for you doubt that any fish could survive the brackish impurities.
7696: A chill wind blows over the river, bringing a fine, frosted mist that coats your hands and face, causing uncontrollable shivers. The river flows steadily, secure in the knowlege that soon it will not be alone. No such promise is there for you, and a second set of shivers come unbidden -- these caused by a much more frightening source than just the clime.
7697: The branch of the river heads southwest here, navigating past the stately cliffs to the north, and staying faithfully beside the trail to the south-east. With the promise of finding its brethern, and forming the mighty Bruinen, the current continues at a hurried pace. Only by the strongest paddling could one keep even still in these frigid waters.
7698: The river is deflected back to its proper course by the steep bank that curves to the west, but after some minor turbulence the current runs strong and deep to the west again. The road can be seen, both to the south and east, but you are moving too fast for any chance to disembark from these chill rapids.
7699: The sandy bottom of the tributary has only a few rocks on it, and fewer still that surmont the freezing sprays, but those rare stones send the current into erratic swirls, and only the merciless battering of the huge volume of water that will not be hindered by such palsey means. The crests of the waves are a glistening white, and the foam coats you, drawing every ounce of heat from your heart.
7700: The current flows strongly west, running with all its strength from the tortured and orc-infested Misty Mountains that spawned it. Although clear, the waters are bitter, fouled with the impurities that it carries until it finally reaches the sea. There, perhaps, it will swim among the warm eddies and currents, bathe in the healthful saline waters, and rid itself of the horror of its past.
7701: The water of this clear river is, like almost everything for miles, cold and icy. Small droplets sting and numb your face and hands, and you desparately hope that you do not have to plunge into the numbing water. The river flows to the west, fleeing the mountains from which it sprang.
7702: With every second, the waters that surround you seek to place themselves as far from the east as they can. In their haste they abandon serenity and calm, and each wave clashes and battles with its neighbours to be away sooner. The cliffs to the north grow more and more stately to the west, and to the east they are overtaken by grim and colorless mountains.
7703: Twisting west and north, the waters crash about you with white-crested waves. When the misty spray coats you, you feel chilled; where the frigid water soaks you, you shiver convulsively. Quickly the river flows, leaving the grey landscape and greeting the cold and clear land to the west. In every crash and roar of the waves, you think you can discern a warning, a warning about the fell east.
7704: Veering south, so to avoid the impassive grey rock of the mountains, this river rushes onward to the west, eager to leave this accursed land. The air grows chiller and clearer to the west, giving relief to the dead grey mist that encompasses the realm about you. Far to the south, a dark pine forest threatens you, and a horrible cry greets you with its sight. North there is no solace either, with the grey and terrible mountains reigning above you.
7705: Although the river is less swift than to the east, it is still not to be trifled with. The current would make travel west very easy, yet not safe as you notice small tips of what must be large rocks just below the water's surface. Briefly you wonder what could be east to make this river hurry so.
7706: The current is strong, deep and swift. It carries you, and various other debris from the mountains, quickly to the east, flowing down the steepeing slope. Far to the west, a lone hawk soars far above the land, gracefully navigating the mountain tops and cliff sides. It gives no indication of coming further east, however.
7707: Your mind is lulled into a bored stat, briefly, from the lack of activity in this endless river. Yet, a dark howling sets your mind back on edge, warning you that nothing in this Ainur-forsaken land is safe. The current picks up slighty, as the ground falls to the west. The air is chill and foul, and breathing is far from pleasant.
7708: The water grows rougher here, running over large stones and boulders that have fallen from the mountains far above. No simple rock can divert this river, however, as it travels unwearying towards the east, far from its tortured youth. Over the growl of the water, you can hear a faint, yet distinguishable war-cry, borne on winds from the mountain-tops.
7710: For miles to the east and west this river is an unbroken straight blade, shining through the greyness of the mountains and badlands. But here, a small outcropping to the north forces the river to skirt the rock. Roiling and spraying, the water beats futiley against this stone protrusion, but to no avail. Dejectedly it still flows westward.
7711: Although the grey mountainsides to the north form a perfectly smooth and strong barrier for the water, slowly and patiently the rock is being eaten away, and carried far to the west and south. Alas, this labour is not without toll, and the water you are on grows bitter and unclean with the dust and lime.
7712: Gurgling and bubbling, the river flows guardedly west, backing away from the tortured and cruel mountains of the east. In the murmurs of the river, you imagine that the water is trying desparately to relate its tales of the east, tales filled with horror and evil to cause even the most stalwart hero to cringe like a craven slave.
7713: The water here is somewhat clearer than it was further to the east. The river is a bit wider but it is also more shallow. Logs stuck in the river and large rocks poking up make passage difficult. The banks of the river are covered with dense foliage that makes it impossible to see the surrounding lands, in in addition to preventing you from leaving the river.
7714: The river turns again to the east here, flowing along to the south of the Grey Mountains. Its colour has become quite dark due to all the debris being washed into it from small streams in the mountains. Through the murky water you can catch brief glimpses of dark moving shapes. Or is that just your imagination?
7715: The rapids that are further upstream have disappeared entirely. The river is calm and the water rushes along silently. You are in the shadow of the Grey Mountains that rise up high above you just to your north. The water is dark and dirty, and a feeling of hopelessness slowly settles on you.
7716: Ahhh, how refreshing. The soft sound of these peaceful rapids soothes your aching soul. Even though you are still worried by the evil you feel about you and the strange shapes you sometimes see moving along the banks, you are able to take a moment to appreciate this calm and peaceful place.
7717: Although there are a few rocks and other dangerous objects in the river, you momentarily lose yourself in the gentle undulating of these gentle rapids. Your worries and fears disappear for the time being in this enjoyable experience.
7718: Perhaps continuing to this point in the river was not such a great idea. You are barely able to keep control of your boat as you are bounced between hazardous rocks and boulders that have fallen from the heights. The river looks calmer both to the east and west. In fact, anything else looks better than this.
7719: The water gushes along, inexorably carving a path into a dark stone, forming a deep cleavage into the already tall mountains. To the west, you can hear the sounds of some rapids. On towards the east, the river widens and becomes more shallow. Fortunately to the west, the rapids do not seem too dangerous.
7720: Around and around swirls the water in the river, caught in numerous eddies created as the river twists and turns through the foothills of the mountains to the northwest. The river cuts through the dark stone that rises up to form the Grey Mountains high above you. You keep telling yourself you are not afraid of the wild mountains and the ominous river, but it does no good.
