This is the deepest part of the forest. It actually dips down into a sort of natural amphitheater of gigantic proportions; a coliseum of filled with tall, silent pines, thorny, tough bushes, and hidden deadfalls. You can barely make out what is around, and each half-hidden object becomes a possible foe. It seems that a collection of smooth, regularly shaped rocks are partially buried here, some covered by fallen trunks, and a few out in the open.
7757: In the midst of the huge, cold wood, stands a short wall of broken, ancient stones. The wall is unearthed and usurped by the trees in many places, and quickly disappears on both ends. Each stone is cracked and moss-encrusted, and partially smooth with age. Judging from the wall's construction, there might be more to the north.
7758: Without warning, the darkness suddenly penetrates your heart, and you feel fear--fear of the wild creatures half-seen in the periphery, fear of losing your way in this horrid wood, and fear of the next step. You maneouver through half-frozen pines as they look down impassively at your plight.
7759: A stocky mountain mule is here, waiting to serve.

You stand in the fringes of a deep, cold pine forest. The thick canopy envelopes the forest in an eternal twilight, with only small patches of illumination. The ground crunches softly under your feet as you step among the fallen brown needles.
7760: The forest's activity seems to be far away from here, but you know it is only an illusion. Though the trees are as uncaring as before, and the darkness as full of menace, this place is oddly quiet. It is like this eerie glade is forbidden to the denizens of this cold forest. Suddenly you notice a strange pattern in the undergrowth. Here is the outline of a small building, the stones still half-sunk into the ground. And here is the remnant of a wall, now broken and fallen. The scattered ruins direct you to the east, where you can see the forest thins, and buildings of a less-deteriorated nature hide among the trees.
7761: A brown pond between old branches and roots is here.

Hidden within the shelter of a small, overgrown knoll, is a tiny pool of cold and dark water. From a crack it falls into the pool, drop by drop. The footsteps of a pack of many large, clawed animals imprint the muddy bank of the water. Then, you notice it. Among the beasts' pawprints is the mark of a single, iron-shod boot.
7762: A huge, black wolf is here, ready to devour.
The climbing gets slightly harder here, and the rough slope continues to ascend to the south. The chill wind blows against your skin and hair, making you feel much colder than you should.
7763: The hills border a deep pine-forest to the north, and continue to the east. West lies a particularly large hill, overlooking the bleak countryside like an enormous turret, built long ago by the armies of men, and left to sink back into its basic elements.
7764: A particularly hardy variety of short, sparse grass covers the hills here, blasted by wind and sleet at least half of the year. The hills here are short and almost pleasant to traverse, but continuing east, they become high and broken. The edge of a huge pine forest lies to the north.
7765: Grey, rolling hills are all around, with only a few stunted trees to relieve the monotony. Here the winds seem to blow quite harshly, pressing the dry scratchy grass against the earth. The scene slowly flattens out and gives way to a pine forest.
7766: It seems these hills go on for miles and miles. The mounds are regular and boring, but in their lack of identity somehow threatening. Each one could hide a servant of evil, or cover a treasure or undead horror. So you travel with constant, nervous alertness, among the barren grey hills, seemingly empty, but haunted with shadows of danger.
7767: Here a path, almost obliterated by the harsh elements of the north, begins and heads through some hills, to the mountains of the east. These rising hills are gloomy and grey, and there is no movement or life that you can discern.
7768: You notice that these hills, ranging from tall to very short, all seem to flow in a common direction. The maze-like enclosure of their sometimes-rolling, sometimes-vertical walls zig-zags back and forth. But all the way across, the elevation increases quickly as you travel to the east.
7769: High, smooth hills undulate all around, and surge upward to meet a dismal range of mountains to the east. The ground is cold and ungiving, the few bushes small, hardy, unloved things. A scarcely-used path goes from east to west, following the rise and fall of the land.
7770: Further down you continue, sometimes in a gradual, almost boring fashion, but at other times in dangerous, precipitous descents. You pass a gargantuan boulder that is lodged into the side of the mountain, and wonder, like hundreds of travellers before, what on Arda could have put it there.
7771: The fog rises up along the sides of this cold, enormous slab of granite and shale, mingling with the steam of your exhalations, and confounding your vision. All is dark and grey, dead and unmoving. Here and there a hardy, gnarled little tree hangs from an unlikely perch, but besides that, all is lifeless. The rubble-strewn little trail leads down the mountainside, into some barren hills far below.
7772: This small trail grows very steep, climbing up into the mountains to the south. The ground gets rockier and more treacherous, as bits of loose shale and stone shift under your feet. A multitude of other footsteps have been here to pack down the rocky ground, but still it has not settled. A faint odour catches your attention, and draws your eyes to a small glimpse of white bones.
7773: You have travelled long and far to reach this mighty set of mountains, the Hithaeglir. The trail has been steep and cruel, yet you have persevered. Now, instead of a majestic panorama or scenic beauty, a greyish mist rises up from the cold, grey stone sides of the mountains and blocks the sights of the world beyond. And, as this is but the start of the Misty Mountains, your tribulations have only just begun.
7774: You wander aimlessly in these treacherous mountains. The mist is a bit thinner than it usually is and you can catch glimpses of the forsaken lands spread out to your north. To the east, your climb gets much steeper as the mountains rise up to a high pass.
7775:
An opossum stands here, sniffing around the ground.
An orkish warg-rider, wielding a lance, is here, riding a hungry warg.

The rocks on either side of this pass are wet and slimy to touch. The pass is a bit worn as if many animals have passed this way. There are blood stains on some of the rocks near you, making you wonder what kind of a fierce battle took place here. You can descend from this place to the east and the west.
7776: A darkness settles on your heart as you wander through these barren mountains. All around you is nothing but the cold stone that makes these mountains and the mist that gives them their name. West of here, the mountains rise up slightly into a high pass. It is too misty to see anything else.
7777: Terrible thoughts fill your mind as you linger in this terrible place. Thick cold mist is all around you. You can't tell which direction the mountains continue in. Will going north lead you to safety? Is there safety anywhere in these mountains? Something furry brushes your foot as you walk along but when you look down you see nothing. It seems that you are being watched from every direction.
7778: The mountains stretch out around you, rising majestically into the sky. Away to the north, the spur upon which you stand reaches an abrupt end, at a what appears from here to be a tall cliff. Perhaps from there you will be able to see the countryside far about.
7780: You are walking along the northern edge of this range of the Misty Mountains. For some odd reason, you are overcome with pride to be alive in an area where countless innocent creatures have doubtlessly suffered terrible deaths. What a shame it would be if you died in these distant and barren lands.
7781: The mountains suddenly get much steeper here. The climb looks easy but it will be hard. You should have a good view from up above if this fog around you clears up. Every once in a while, you imagine that you can hear screams in the distance and the fog sometimes seems to be alive.
7782: The fog that is south and east of you has thinned and you can peak out at the lands below you. To the north and west are steep cliffs. Looking out northwest from here, you can see the remains of a forest. Past the forest you think you can see more mountains. It's hard to tell because the air is still a bit misty.
7783: Walking across these raped plains is wearing you out. There is nothing to see but burned and dead land all around you. To your east, you can enter the charred hills...more raped land. The plains seem to continue endlessly to the north and the west. South of you, you can enter the forest.
7784: The plains have risen up in elevation, but you are not quite in the Burned Hills. This certainly is an evil place where many have died and none have cared. To your north and west, the Burned Plains spread out before you. Heading east will take you into the hills.
7785: This section of the hills is littered with burnt wood and corpses. An awful smell seeps from the ground and burns your nose when you breathe. Maybe this was a graveyard? From the way it smells, it certainly could have been. The ground here looks strange, like there is something buried in it...
7786: Simply calling these hills burned does not do them justice. You can't seem to think of the right word as you wander through this ruined place. The hills go east and west. To your north and south are the mighty Misty Mountains. You feel slightly claustrophobic as you hurry on.
7787: The trail has become steep here, forcing you to travel slowly lest you lose your footing. Letting your gaze travel south, further down the trail to the mountains, the sky seems so grey that the skyline is hardly discernible. The tracks seem fainter here, due to the increase of rock in the soil.
7788: Twisting west and north, the tracks start following a ridge that beings to rise above the surrounding lands. The grey of the rocks and earth grows dirtier and deader to the southwest, and the air gets chill from the altitude that its climbs to. A frigid wind blows through, whipping the loose tails of your clothing.
7789: Farther into the rocky badlands this trodden trail ventures. Huge foot-prints, not even slightly concealed, travel both to the south and north. Several of the tracks have freshly broken the soil. Far to the south and east the Misty Mountains form from smaller, fragmented hills.
7790: A half-decayed corpse of a goblin lies rotting on the ground.

Here, on a turn in the trail, the foot and paw prints increase, until the ground seems just layer after layer of prints. A hole, in the middle of the trail, has been dug out of the rocky ground. The stench about here reeks of old beasts and filth. Scattered about the hole are various corpses and skeletons, in various stages of decay. Suddenly, a startling growl is heard from under the soil.
7791: The trail lumbers east and north, trampling though the barren wastes that surround you. Jagged rocks and broken stones threaten your feet, yet you notice that whatever made the tracks on this trail seem to have been bothered little by the edges and splinters on the ground.
7792: South the trail continues, into a debatable land in which no life exists. North this trampled swath joins with the main trail, however that seems hardly more enticing to either your legs or your intuition. A rotten corpse, too frozen and dry to attract flies, stains the area with a horrible stench.
7793: A quiet little cleared space leads to more ruins. Although this site is overgrown with bushes and small trees, it is apparent that once a village huddled here beneath the pines. All that is left above-ground is a half- fallen wall of stone and a couple scattered white marble blocks.
7795:
A nasty troll female crouches here, with a feral look in her eyes.
A nasty troll female crouches here, with a feral look in her eyes.
A small, mean earth troll is standing here, thinking of something hideous.
A small, mean earth troll is standing here, thinking of something hideous.
A large earth troll is digging here, looking for some tasty morsels.

The smell of trolls is stronger here -- caused, perhaps, by the mats and heaps of filth that the trolls must sleep in. This part of the cave is as bad or worse than the previous, with bloody stains on the floor and walls at favourite eating spots, and bones littering the ground here and there. To the south, a large rusty door guards something the trolls must find valuable.
7796:
A large piece of fresh, raw meat lies here.
A large piece of fresh, raw meat lies here.
A large stone chest is here.
A half-rotten corpse is hanging here.

This room is surprisingly clean; perhaps the barbaric trolls have some sense of value after all. Still, it is but a small alcove carved out of the surrounding stone, and the trolls' treasures and valuables are scattered about randomly. There is a musty scent of disuse that pervades everything in this chamber.
7798: Once a short, sturdy rock gate guarded the entrance to the village, but it has long since deteriorated into rubble. The walls are broken and covered with dark lichens, and extend into the shadows of the forest on either side. Beyond the gate lie the ruins of a humble little village, bathed in the cold darkness of the pines.
7799: A narrow path runs along the forest floor, eternally shaded by the thick opaque canopy. A mostly-intact stone hut opens up to the path, but the darkened interior is hidden from casual inspection.
7800: The path continues through the remains of the village. Most of the buildings seem to have rotted away long ago, but several edifices still stand in stony defiance of the elements and the wind.
7801: This building, which seems to have once been a little guardshack, is one of the better-preserved in the village, and now serves as at least a part-time residence of a bevy of swallows. The roof is fairly solid, and three of the four walls still stand. The hut is dark inside.
7802: A cobblestone road is set in a track to the north. Some kind of change seems to have occurred in the last couple of decades, as the cobbles are sunk several feet from their original position, and partially covered with damp, cold loam. Off to the west a narrow, crumbly path ascends steeply up the mountain.
7803: There is some snow on the ground.
This bumpy alley runs between two overgrown lots, filled with knee-high grass and thick, short bushes. You step over a large, fallen tree trunk, broken open and rotten inside.
7804: You stand in an open alley that connects the two main sections of the village, or at least the parts that still stand. To either side is a scraggly field, that probably contained a bunch of huts at one time. A stone structure lies to the east.
7805: One stands in front of a smallish, round structure, constructed of dozens of head-sized stones fitted together into a dome-shape. Not a single building block has fallen, despite the obvious age of the building. In its youth it probably stood about three feet higher, because now it has sunken into the black earth and has covered part of the door which marked the front.
7806: You stand on a rocky, shallow hill. A narrow trail leads up the mountainside, where little rocks keep dislodging themselves and tumbling down. High above you can barely see a thick, squat tower of some sort, half-hidden by a moss-covered crag.
7807: This trail leads up and around the mountain, heading in a northerly direction. Shaded by the tops of the pines, and hidden by large granite outcroppings, it would be hard to spot from below.
7808: The mountain wall and the outcropping on the right almost meet on the top, throwing darkness between, and giving the impression of a long, tall tunnel. You can just barely see the sky above, cluttered with some silhouetted bushes that shudder in the wind.
7809: You stand before a rude, squat tower; round and built of rough stones, with earth heaped around the greater part of its circumference. The tower is about twenty feet high, and leans against the mountainside. A rusty old irondoor is sunk into the lime-kiln, like the door of a great oven. A path leads up around the side of the kiln, to the top of the structure.
7810: The inside of the kiln is wide and somewhat more expansive than it would seem. The stones here are blackened and melted from the great heat that once blasted them. Now, they are mossy and dark for a different reason. The wind whistles over the top of the kiln, but not overly loud. The interior is cool and sheltered from most exposure. Embedded in the south wall is a sturdy-looking iron door, but no handle is apparent on this side.
7811: You stand on top of the tower-like structure; from here you can see all around. To the southwest, a dark pine-forest covers the land like a heavy rug, and the Misty Mountains rise up everywhere else. Directly below you see the layout of an ancient, ruined village, long since decomposed into the earth. Only a few stone buildings remain to attest to its existence. But the old plots are still free of trees, and from up here the traces of the village are quite clear. Beyond the village proper you see some black caves dotting the rock face. Underfoot is the open top of the kiln, some eight feet across, and ten deep. Inside, it is dark and cool, and the stones are black with the lichens and mosses of years of long disuse.
7812: Piles of earth and stone embrace the kiln, covering it to the depth of a few feet. This path leads to the top of the kiln.
7813: You can go no further in this direction. As much as you don't want to, you must go back the way you came, through the Worn Foothills. To the north and west, the foothills become too rough to be passable. To the south, the Misty Mountains rise up so steeply that you don't even consider climbing them.
7814: Wandering through these foothills is beginning to wear on your soul. You long for the simple warmth and safety that you once knew. West of here, the hills get a bit smaller. They look more passable than the ones you are currently in. Heading east will bring you deeper into the Worn Foothills.
7815: Ick. These hills are a sorry sight. The hills are made of dense, wet, and black dirt. The whole place smells putrid, as if many creatures have died and decayed here. The hills continue to the east and rise up to some mountains south of here. In many places, blood seems to have been mixed in with the dirt on the ground.
7816: A mountain goat is here, jumping from cliff to cliff.

Why would anyone want to live out here? Well, it seems that someone did because just east of here you can see a small hut. From here, it looks abandoned. Looks can be deceiving. Better be careful. If you have to flee through these hills, it will be rough going.
7817: This hut is very old and had obviously been abandoned for a long time. In one corner is a pile of white dust that could have been a pile of bones many years ago. The hut itself is beginning to fall apart. It is made of a hard wood that you can't quite identify. Though the wood is strong, the walls are rotting. There are odd scrapes on the floor, but don't worry. They too look older than time...or so you think.
7818: What a terrible place to be lost in! You wander back and forth, your sense of direction lost. All you know is that the Misty Mountains seem to surround you no matter which way you look. Maybe if you head back west, if you can find it, you will find a way out..
7819:
A large mean-looking troll is here.
A hungry warg stands here, sniffing around for flesh.

It smells like something has been dead a long, long time here. The wooden beams that support the floor of the hut above you are rotting, and you don't feel very safe here. From the rotted remains of various items here, you postulate that this was once a wine cellar.
7820:
A valuable gold coin lies here.
A huge olog-hai troll is here staring blankly at you.
An old, strong cave troll is standing here.
A hungry warg stands here, sniffing around for flesh.

This room is nothing like the cellar you just came from. The walls are made of an odd polished stone and they look newly made. In some places, runes that you are unable to translate have been carefully carved. The room seems completely empty, which is odd because you certainly don't feel alone.
7821: A sharp-eyed hawk is here stalking some prey.

Now high up in the mountains, you would surely have a wonderful view if it weren't for the mist all around you. You can hear strange calls from below that make your blood run cold. A faint odour reminds you of trolls. Or is it just the smell that seems to live in these forsaken mountains?
7822: A grey wolf is here, snarling aggressively.

Back and forth, up and down you go as you make your way through the mountains. You have almost lost all sense of direction. There is a steep but climbable incline rising up to the west. The mountains are too steep to climb to the north and south.
7823: These mountains rise high above the hills below. You can follow the mountains as they rise up even further (is that possible?) to the west, or you can attempt to descend the east face of the mountain. Somehow you don't feel too luck as you look at the terrain around you.
7824: There must be nothing that these plains have not seen. From the looks of them, they have been swept with disease, fire, and even floods at one time. They have heard many screams and have watched many die in agony. Now you feel that they are watching you, and that you time is near.
7825: These terrible plains seem to continue forever to the west. North of you, high mountains rise up. Going to your east or your south won't get you off these plains, but at least you can see something in the distance in those directions. Nothing grows on this plains and, in places, deep scars have been cut into the ground.
7826: A mountain goat is here, jumping from cliff to cliff.

No longer lost in the Worn Foothills, you are climbing up into the Misty Mountains. 'Is this really a good idea?' you wonder as you push on. It looks like being lost in the hills might be a whole lot better than being lost in these mountains.
7827: Higher still rise the mountains! You are almost climbing straight up now. The rocky slopes are made of dark but smooth stone. The stone seems to simply absorb light and it is cold to touch. As you walk along, you pass the remains of some poor animal that made the mistake of exploring this place.
7828: A big, nasty vulture is sitting here, protecting its nest.

Phew. Finally among the high tops of the Misty Mountains. To the east, you see the Misty Mountains rising up from the scared hills and plains below them. The place you find yourself in is oddly quiet, and the dark stone mountains give you no comfort.
7829: Far below is a dangerous looking cliff. You can scale the mountain side down to it if you are careful. From this point, you are able to see the peaceful lands of Arda far to the west. You know that, somewhere out there, is the noble town of Rivendell, but right now it is hard for you to picture it.
7830: You have come down from the mountains as far as you can. If you continue on down, the mountain side turns into a cliff. Attempting to climb down the cliff wall will be the last mistake you ever make. Better turn back and pass through the desolate mountains again. At least you know they are safe...more or less...
7831: Oh no!! As you stupidly attempt to climb down the cliff wall, you lose your grip and fall. Down, down, down you go until finally you SPLAT on the hard rocks. Oh well, so much for your puny little life! Maybe next time you'll look first.
7832: A Way through the Burned Forest
A squirrel scampers around here, looking for nuts from the trees.

At last you are out of that wasted place. Where to go from here, though. It looks like your only options are to go back into the forest or to head north to some desolate looking plains. The plains look more inviting from here as you consider descending into the forest again.
7833:
A squirrel scampers around here, looking for nuts from the trees.
A disgusting forest troll is searching for fresh meat here.

Something lives here from the looks of this place. There are big footprints everywhere. Piles of ash-covered bones are scattered about. Whatever lives here must live off of unlucky wanderers like you. The only way out of here is west and you think you had better head in that direction right now.
7834: A disgusting forest troll is searching for fresh meat here.

Fear settles down on top of you, and you hardly notice it. You have suddenly become sure that someone or something is tracking you through this wasted land. You can escape to your south or head even deeper into the forest to the east. South looks like a better choice.
7835: A Hill above the Burned Forest

It's amazing how much good some fresh air does you. This hill rises out of the forest of burned trees below you. The hill itself is completely bare, but at least its not covered with the charred remains of trees and who knows what else. You had better get ready to brave the forest to your south because it is the only way out of here.
7836: Wow, you sure are getting sick of walking around this depressing place. If only you could get up away from the forest floor for just a moment. Wait, to the north it looks like there's a small hill. Maybe if you can clamber up it, your claustrophobia will be eased temporarily.
7837: A disgusting forest troll is searching for fresh meat here.

You are now deep in this awful forest. The dust and ashes that rise up as you trample through are beginning to choke you. All the blackness around you seems to suck up the sunlight. You don't think anything could live in this place, but you aren't so sure when you hear grunting noises nearby.
7838: A disgusting forest troll is searching for fresh meat here.

Tracks of some humanoid creature go through the ashes here, and they look fresh. Though the trees are the only things that obstruct your view, they are so thick that you can't see far. The ashes that you are kicking up also make it hard to see. It's strange, you think, that the ashes of a fire that seems to have happened so long ago have not been washed away yet.
7839: It seems that you have hit a dead end in your wanderings. The trees to the east and west of you, though burned, are still standing tall and strong. Sometimes it seems like they aren't really dead. South of you is a steep cliff wall that is obviously impassable.
7840: A disgusting forest troll is searching for fresh meat here.

The corpses of burnt trees are all around you. What could have started a fire powerful enough to clean this whole land? Everything around you looks more or less the same, but you think you might be able to get out of here by heading upwards. It looks like you can also head down and deeper into the forest.
7841:
An orkish warg-rider, wielding a short spear, is here, riding a hungry warg.
A hungry warg is standing here, ridden by an orkish warg-rider.

Somehow you have descended even further from the forest floor to reach this evil place. There are no burned trees here like there are where you just came from, but you almost wish there were. This place is dark and barren except for a few strange plants. It makes your skin crawl.
7842: A grey wolf is here, salivating profusely.

Here you are, all alone and wandering in these dangerous hills. There seems to be no logic to why you have come here. Even with a large group of adventurers, this place is by no means safe. Hopelessness clouds your thoughts as you begin to believe that sooner or later, something here will kill you. Gathering your courage, you think of a path to take.
7843: You are now in a small space between the rolling hills. You are still in the hills, but you are at a lower elevation than your were before. South of you are the Misty Mountains. The hills continue to the north and the west between the high mountains.
7844: At last you are nearing the end of these ugly hills. Just east of you are some steep hills. They don't look inviting, but they are certainly better than where you are now. To your south, you can see a ravine coming down from the mountains, but it is too steep to climb. South, past the ravine, and to the north, you see the ever-present Misty Mountains.
7845: A low, many-branched shrub covers the ground here.

The small trickle of water that runs down from the mountains must have been much larger at one time to have carved such a deep ravine. It is too puny to even drink from. The steep walls of the ravine and the crack that it becomes as it continues north make your only exit back the way you came. Yes, more climbing, more mountains, and more fear.
7846: Up into the mountains you go again. You have the strange feeling that you have been here before. The mountains continue to the east, west, and south of you. To the east they rise high into the mist until you can no longer see them. To the west and south, they go on into the distance.
7847: The mountains sink briefly down into steep hills. North and south of you are the Misty Mountains. To your west, you can enter the Burned Hills. Neither option looks good to you as you try to decide if you should hike into the mountains or risk it in the hills.
7848: The mountains drop a bit in elevation just to the west of here. You can easily climb down the mountain side to where the air is thinner and your head will spin less. You can see nothing in the other directions because of the thick fog that gave these mountains their name.
7849: Hiking in these mountains makes you wonder if there is good anywhere in the world. You are beginning to jump at shadows, and you can't help but wonder if the next corner you round will reveal a clan of trolls or a wolf pack. The mist is thick, keeping you from viewing the lands that surround you and making you paranoid.
7851: Picking a path carefully where none before existed, you are unable to tell if you are making any progress. The mountains continue to all look the same, covered as they are with a thick fog. The fog sticks to your clothes and the clamminess works its way to your soul.
7852: The crazy shape of these mountains at times leaves you in a place where the only way out is to go back the way you came. This is such a place. After countless hours wandering in the Misty Mountains, you have again hit a dead end. For some reason the word 'dead' seems to resonate in your mind and in your soul.
7853:
A big, nasty vulture is sitting here, protecting its nest.
A grey wolf is here, salivating profusely.

What terrible force of nature made this place? The mountains here are barren and colourless. In the distance, wolves can be heard howling wildly. How can even wolves survive in this lonely place? What do they live off of? What do they eat? What might they eat!?
7854:
A sharp-eyed hawk is here stalking some prey.
A sharp-eyed hawk is here stalking some prey.

Back within the mountains, this is clearly one of the many ranges of the Misty Mountains. The range continues to the west. This point is so high up here that attempting to climb down to the hills south of here would require great caution.
7855: You walk carefully among the mountains. The view of the surrounding lands is complete in every direction, but you don't dare take you eyes off your path for fear of losing your footing and falling to your death. The wind seems to whisper something to you as it whips around the mountains.
7856:
A sharp-eyed hawk is here stalking some prey.
A grey wolf is here, snarling aggressively.

These mountains certainly do deserve their name! A thick mist hangs in the air and keeps you from seeing more than a few yards in any direction. You can hear faint noises from all around you. You imagine you can see shapes moving in the fog.
7857: A demon wolf lurks here, its dark form twisting and hiding its shape.

Thick but strange grass grows on these plains. The grass is tall and things seem to be moving about in it. In the distance, you think you can see bears wandering across the plain, but they could be trolls. To the west, the plains seem to continue on forever. You exit to the south is blocked by steep mountains.
7858: Standing on this part of the barren plains, you follow along the mountains that line the southern horizon. A stiff, chilling wind wails through the mountain peaks and drives the heat from your bones. Though tired from trudging through the thick, brownish grass that covers the plains, intuition tells you that this is not a safe place to rest.
7859: You are now between two ranges of mountains. You can't see very far up the mountains because they are shrouded in a thick mist. East of you, you see a gap between the mountains where you might be safe from the weather and the wild animals that roam these plains.
7860: An ibex is watching you from afar.

Heading south from the mountains, you have ended up in a small space between two ranges. You can climb up into the mountain range south of here. In this small gap, you are safe from the wind and cold that were eating away your heart and body while you were hiking in the naked mountains.
7861: You start your climb up into the foothills, leaving the safety of the trail behind and below you. To the east, foothills rise into the Misty Mountains. South and southeast of you, you can see the wild plains between two ranges of mountains
7862:
A huge, black wolf is here, ready to devour.
A huge, black wolf is here, ready to devour.

Up and up go the foothills, leading to the Misty Mountains. To the east you can climb up into the mountains. The way looks rough and you aren't sure you'll be able to get down once you get up. The foothills to the south are too rough to be climbable.
7863: You have stepped off the trail and you suddenly discover that you are among the famous Misty Mountains. What a forsaken place this is! The evil here is thick and you begin to feel chilly even though you are not very high in the mountains yet.
7864: An ibex is watching you from afar.

You are now high up in the mountains. An icy wind blows from the east, whipping across the mountains tops. The lands of Eriador lie to the west far away. You can see nothing east because the mountains rise up steeply in that direction.
7865: A demon wolf lurks here, its dark form twisting and hiding its shape.

Steep mountain sides block your exit in all directions but south. You can only hope that none of the monsters you know to exist in these mountains come at this moment, because you could easily be cornered here. Looking at the high cliffs that surround you, you find it hard to control your panic. You'd better get down from here before you drive yourself crazy.
7866: Now high up in the mountains, you are walking along the bank of a river. The bank to the north is too steep to climb down. The trail is well worn and covered with animal tracks. There are also some tracks that you can't quite identify. How strange, you thought you could track anything...
7867: Still next to the river, the trail has become a bit wider. It is made of dirt and rock, and anything that used to grow on it has long since been killed off by the countless passing of unknown creatures. Due to the trail's good condition, you are able to pass by this area quickly.
7868: The trail continues alongside the river, bending here from west to north. The path is sometimes obstructed by large boulders that have been dislodged from the mountain to the south -- whether by natural forces or by the near-legendary stone giants may never be known. The river to the north is inaccessible from here because of the treacherous rocks that line its course.
7870:
A black metal shield has been left here.
A metal shield is on the ground.
A scimitar has been left here.
A butcher knife is lying here.
A pair of chain mail sleeves lies here.
A mace is on the ground.
A large stone chest is here.

This was clearly not in the original tower. In fact, you would be hard pressed to call this even a room, rather it is an alcove chopped into the rock walls surrounding the dungeon. Over the last few years, it has apparently served as a repository for any junk the orcs wished to get rid of, or even things of value they wished to store. There is so much clutter and junk in here it is hard to even start to search for anything worthwhile.
7871: Once this may have been a carefully constructed section of the tower; now it has been hacked and hewed until the original walls can barely be seen, and only the new, expanded walls enclose you. The air is filled with a dank, musky scent that reminds you of something...better not to dwell on that. A well fitted iron door is in the north wall, in a section of stone that was not butchered. To the south the wall was broken to form an archway, and another doorway is to the west.
7872:
A scuffed and worn leather satchel has been left here.
A large sack is on the ground.
A beer barrel has been left here.

Obviously this room was not part of the original tower. The walls are rough-hewn, and no thought was paid to them after the builders finished excavating a reasonable sized room. The ground is uneven, and littered with mats of cloth and straw beds. Loose equipment is scattered about, and several items, rusted away, stick out of various stench-ridden cloth heaps.
7873: Grachalg the Uruk-hai smith stands here, working his forge.

This chamber is dominated by the forge at its centre. Its walls are covered in soot and the smell of hot metal fills the air. Three narrow vents, too small for even a hobbit to climb through, are evenly spaced around the chamber's roof. They look cunningly-built, but most of the room is rough-hewn. There is little space here, just the bare minimum necessary for a smith to work, and nothing not immediately needed for the forge is stored here.
7874:
A tall brown-skinned orc, with wide arms, examines you harshly.
A tall brown-skinned orc, with wide arms, examines you harshly.
A tall brown-skinned orc, with wide arms, examines you harshly.
A tall brown-skinned orc, with wide arms, examines you harshly.

Once this tower may have been a proud fortress of the kingdom of Rhudaur, holding at bay the evil armies of the north. In the recent past, however, the murals of glorious battles and the walls they are on have been desecrated. The furniture that once would comfort an ever-vigilant sentry must have recently seen crueler occupants. There are some narrow slit windows high above the floor, through which some grey shafts of light can fall during what passes for daylight in these grim mountainous wastes.
7875:
An orc sentry is here on patrol.
An orc sentry is here on patrol.

With four windows, one in each cardinal direction, peering over the broken cold surroundings, this high tower is certainly an excellent look-out. The grey stone of the walls nearly blends in with the grey stone of the mountains, and the grey overcast sky gives everything a dead, grey shade.
7876: The scent of musk is most definitely at its peak here. The floor is littered with straw and filthy cloth, intermixed with bones and rotting meat. Small piles of offal and rotting scraps fill the air with a smell so thick and disgusting that you feel sick. The walls that surround you are scarred deeply with claw marks.
7877:
A tall brown-skinned orc, with wide arms, examines you harshly.
A tall brown-skinned orc, with wide arms, examines you harshly.
A demon wolf lurks here, its dark form twisting and hiding its shape.
A demon wolf lurks here, its dark form twisting and hiding its shape.
A hungry warg stands here, sniffing around for flesh.

The walls were not carved, rather they look as if they were hacked away by some large axe. The stone is a dead grey, but is covered in dried blood of some sort. The smell of iron is strong here, and floor is rocky and hard to walk on. A doorway was cleaved from the rock to the north, and in the inky shadows of the ceiling a faint trap-door can be seen.
7878:
A huge, smoking campfire is burning here.
A dark-skinned orc is dancing around the fire.
A dark-skinned orc is dancing around the fire.
A dark-skinned orc is dancing around the fire.
A female orc stands glaring at you.
A female orc stands glaring at you.

The grey stone of the mountains this hall was carved from seems dead and hard in the shadows cast by the fire in the centre of the hall. On the rough ground are scattered mats and beds of straw where most of the inhabitants of this tower spend the night.
7879:
A water barrel has been left here.
A water barrel has been left here.
A wooden chest stands in the corner.

This is merely an alcove carved out of the main hall, and the light from the fire does not reach you. The walls are overgrown with mould and fungus, and the musty smell fills your lungs. Various worthless items are scattered about, but in one corner a large chest lies, aged and open.
7880: You are in a hidden chamber buried deep below the rocky pinnacle of the tower. Once the personal sleeping chamber of the tower's commander, this room has now become the last safety measure should the garrison fall to an enemy army. Atop a small metal ladder, a passage, blocked by a metal grille, may allow the last survivors to flee and call reinforcements.
7881:
A mailbox stands here stuffed full of messages.
Karash, the Captain of the Tower, stands here alert for enemies.
A tall brown-skinned orc, with wide arms, examines you harshly.
A tall brown-skinned orc, with wide arms, examines you harshly.
A tall brown-skinned orc, with wide arms, examines you harshly.
A demon wolf lurks here, its dark form twisting and hiding its shape.
A demon wolf lurks here, its dark form twisting and hiding its shape.
A demon wolf lurks here, its dark form twisting and hiding its shape.

The stone walls of this room are circular, and carved with more skill or care than most in this tower. A large desk lies on the northern wall, on top of it are papers and maps. But a table stands in the centre of the room, flanked by a pair of chairs. A larger chair sits at the head, and on it are various weapons of war. A large map hangs on the southern wall.
7882: The path rises to the north, beginning a gentle climb up the mountainside. Southwards it bends gently, into a forested vale. The ground is littered by small rocks, haphazardly strewn about the path. The pine trees, common to the south, are sparser, and they no longer block the wind. Tough, dark- green grass grows out from under the stones.
7883: Though this is still perhaps one of the more pleasant and well-built trails you have travelled, time and the harsh clime have take their toll. Small boulders of every colour and make, granite to lime, litter the path, and you have to take care in stepping among them.
7884: The trail continues on, unchanging, still clinging closely to the dark mountainside. You notice a slight deterioration of the trail that continues on to the east; small patches of rubble are scattered here and there, and the southern edge of the trail seems not so sturdy. The way bends a bit to follow the curve of the mountain.
7886: This trail leads west-east along the mountains. Even though the countryside all around is dark and depressing, the trail is wide and flat, and not uncomfortable. It is easy on the feet, and secure and unthreatening.
7887: A small campfire burns here, its low flames giving off only a little light.

A dark rock path ends as it begins its climb up among the tall black mountain tops. As it follows around a bend, a cliff wall the route and the line of vision. However, you seem to catch a glimpse of something beyond the trail. A different land, perhaps.
7888: The mountain trail climbs up through a blind bend. The rock rises up on both sides like tall, dusky walls, and when you look up you lose your sense of equilibrium.
7890: A dusty little trail winds up between two ridges, towards the summit of a large, dark mountain. On the way, the rock face opens up, revealing a dense, forbidding forest, and a sprawling landscape. Beyond the woods are wide, grey marches and an endless expanse of bumpy hills. There is no sign of civilization from here to the frozen horizon.
7891: The mountain trail climbs ever upward, toward black cliffs and massive looming peaks. Closely hugging the mountain itself, the trail is flanked on the other side by a deep gorge, the bottom of which is shrouded in an eternal darkness.
7892: Continuing along its east-west path, the mountain trail disappears up ahead around a big, smooth, spur of rock, presumably leading back south. A great wide chasm opens up before you; this direction would not be a wise one to choose. However, the valley hundreds of feet below is quite beautiful and impressive to behold, truly a wonder of nature. You probably would not survive the trip.
7893: The trail dips down back into a sheltered nook, heading southwards. The mountains are all around, and you enter a small valley, hidden from exposure on all sides.
7894: Before you unfolds a small, hidden valley. The walls are sheer and unclimbable, and crumble unhealthily. It seems the wind and rain are forbidden from disturbing the eerie placidness, and have left the rock old and unpolished. All is quiet, but a tenebrous tension borne of unnatural stillness pervades the whole place.
7895: A large pile of boulders is sitting here, probably debris from a rockslide.

The mountainside angles here sharply, becoming more and more severe until a sheer western cliff is reached. The rock is flaky and weak, and pieces detach from the main mass to fall to a painful breaking far below. But as you ascend, reaching the impassable part, the stone undergoes a change in character. It becomes smoother and darker, and seems more healthy and solid.
7896: The ground underfoot is crumbling; the footing unsteady. Unclimbable valley walls rise ominously all around, cradling the canyon in a firm grasp that is almost suffocating. The rocky floor angles to the south, draining to a water-worn sinkhole. A brisk descent leads to another small ravine.
7897: The ravine is quiet and dark, the dizzyingly high walls throwing an eternal shadow over its worn stone features. The irregularity of the walls make a climb upwards possible, where the sky can be seen, and the ravine continues to the east. The floor is water-washed and covered with smooth pebbles and rocks, and a white line shows that this was once a stream bed.
7898: As you reach deeper and deeper into this dark valley, the tranquillity and silence seem to become more and more threatening. Though it looks deserted, there is no way to know if anything has passed this way recently. And the quiet is the quiet of watching eyes and motionless talons. You begin to feel like something hunted.
7899: By bracing your back and flexing your legs, you inch your way down a long, narrow chimney. The walls are fairly smooth, and there are few footholds, but as long as you are careful, there is no real danger. However as you descend it becomes darker and darker, very cool. The air down here seems to be of a different order--stagnant and ancient.
7900: This is a natural corridor. A straight, long, stone wall rises on the west, that extends upwards a hundred feet--there to meet the shale-grey sky. A fold in the northern edge reveals a small stone alcove, somewhat hidden from full view. The floor slopes gently to the east, where it meets up with a flat plateau, the first in a series of terraces.
7901:
A horse of the Rohirrim (ulo) is standing here.
A sturdy pack horse is standing here.
A stocky mountain mule is here, waiting to serve.

The floor here is sunk about a yard and a half lower than the floor outside. The room is square and small, obviously chiselled by skilled hands into such a shape. However, the edges are soft and weathered now, and the walls stained darkly by something. Some rusted clutter lies about, and a few rocks, but that is all that is left here.
7902: The sky overhead is dark, and barely visible. For the walls on the north and south are high and seem to lean inwards, so that only a narrow sliver of sky can be seen. The terrace surface is flat and wide, and composed of a hard, rough bedrock. You can hop down to another terrace to the east or with a little climb, traverse the slope to the west.
7903: The terrace is more like a ledge. The sides have begun to crumble, and the footing is a bit unsafe. A big crack bisects the ledge, leaving a hole about a yard wide that goes a long long way down.
7904: You have reached what must be the deepest part of the valley, an area so quiet and dark, that you almost disbelieve that you are outside. The floor is solid bedrock, and is inexplicably tainted black. High, high above, you can see the tops of the valley walls. They are mountain tops, blackened, and piercing the walls with sharp tips. It is hard to relate the open sky with this suffocating darkness down here. The valley continues to the east.
7905: The black tinge of the walls seems to become darker and darker, covering more and more of the stone, and you know that to credit it to the growing darkness would be a lie. But to lie to oneself doesn't seem like such a bad idea right now. A shiver runs down your spine as you suddenly realise that whatever inhabits this fell valley has perceived you!
7906: The valley is narrow but very tall. Great, blackened walls rise sharply on every side, and you almost have to bend backward to see the top, where the tips of ancient mountains are, surrounded by misty white clouds. The shade here is very deep, and you cannot see very much sky at all.
7907: A little canyon branches from the main valley floor here. Like the rest of this area, it is shady and cool, but the feeling of being watched abruptly disappears as soon as you turn the bend.
7908: The valley is narrow but very tall. Great, blackened walls rise sharply on every side, and you have to almost bend over backward to see the top, where the tips of ancient mountains are, surrounded by misty white clouds. The shade here is very deep, and you cannot see very much sky at all.
7909: The walls arch slightly overhead, tunnel-like, making this room even darker than the eternal dusk all around. To the north or south are large, open valleys.
7910: You duck your head to enter this small chamber. The walls are roughly hewn and shadows, conjured by your light's inadequate flame, dance wildly in the corners. Opposite from the entrance, a half dozen large oval holes stare blankly from the irregular rock wall.
7911: The air is completely still--almost stagnant--but thirty yards above the mountain bushes dance contortedly in heavy wind, to the accompaniment of a great howling. The ledge is itself high above the valley surface. and a quick glance down makes you clutch the security of the rock dizzily. A rough, natural path leads west to a small, dark hole in the stone.
7912: You squeeze through the narrow hole and emerge into a much larger cave. It is very dark in here, but what little light there is reveals a long, but thin chamber, natural and irregular. The northern wall is riddled with a series of dark holes, whose contents cannot be seen.
7913: Here the ceiling opens up, and a rocky route starts directly overhead. To the east, the ground slopes downward quite rapidly, into a deeper darkness that hides whatever lurks below.
7914: A patter of gravel tumbles down the slope as you stumble and almost take the quick way to the bottom. The footing here is slippery and dangerous, caused by the loose layer of small rocks. The passage is made easier by keeping in touch with the smooth northern wall. Down below, at the beginning of the incline, you can see the entrance to a large cave.
7915: The ground here crunches loudly as your boots sink into the gravelly ground with each step. Each footfall makes you more and more paranoid, and facing the empty, blank stare of cave entrance doesn't ease your nerves by any means. Unclimbable, smooth walls rise about on all sides, and a slippery climb up is your only alternative to the cave.
7916: The lower mountainside here has split open, as if great stony hands had grasped both sides and wrenched the rock apart. The ripped wall shows many layers of multicoloured stone, not at all like the blackened scab covering everywhere else. You waver momentarily before the gaping fissure, and your movement causes some gravel to scrape together. A great force pulls you forward, like the urge to jump from the edge of a height, or the call of the flame to the doomed moth.
7917: This endless tunnel burrows deep into the earth, seeming to penetrate the very heart of the ancient mountain. It seems like you are passing into a new world; one that is cold, lightless, and, but for the scuffle of your own feet, totally quiet. There seems to be an eerie hum permeating the tunnel, but you know it is merely the marks of your mind struggling to cope with the subterranean and alien environment.
7918:
A stocky mountain mule is here, waiting to serve.
A great dark-grey horse stamps restively.
A large warhorse is standing here, clad in mail.
A spirit floats towards you and howls with an evil laughter.

The tunnel looks as if it continues on what for seems like hours, before it ends and pulls up before a huge, grim iron portal. The door is ten feet tall and half as much in width, but seems to be very thick and sturdy. It swings to the left on ponderous, roughly-hewn iron hinges, and remarkably is almost silent. In the exact middle of the door is a massive keyhole, at least a foot in height.
7919: A huge, wild-eyed beast turns to you and roars ferociously.

You enter a huge room with high, vaulted ceilings fifty feet overhead. The flagstoned floor sprawls out before you, and your torch paints strange pictures on the plain walls. There is an unfinished quality to the chamber, like the seven empty niches cut out of the wall, and the unused tapestry knobs. High above you can see the beginnings of an elaborate scene painted with faded dyes on the ceiling, but the true colours and meaning of the diorama have passed from this world.
7920: You pass through a high, smooth stone arch into a tunnel-like room. The walls are sculpted strangely, and you are both disgusted and strangely fascinated by the grotesque patterns. Suddenly you realise in a horrible moment that what you are looking at is not carved rock, but the actual petrified bones and skulls of people, grafted somehow with the very walls.
7921: Cautiously inching your way into this room, you see four passages ahead of you. One or two of them are sealed or blocked off; intentionally or not, you can't be sure. You turn around and then back again, and then you realise that you're not sure from which way you came. The contorted bones hanging on the walls grin at you.
7922: A spirit floats towards you and howls with an evil laughter.

Cautiously inching your way into this room, you see four passages ahead of you. One or two of them are sealed or blocked off; intentionally or not, you can't be sure. You turn around and then back again, and then you realise that you're not sure from which way you came. The contorted bones hanging on the walls grin at you.
7923: Cautiously inching your way into this room, you see four passages ahead of you. One or two of them are sealed or blocked off; intentionally or not, you can't be sure. You turn around and then back again, and then you realise that you're not sure from which way you came. The contorted bones hanging on the walls grin at you.
7925:
A spirit floats towards you and howls with an evil laughter.
A spirit floats towards you and howls with an evil laughter.

The walls here seem to undergo a change from the ones before. These seem to be newer, more recent additions to the ancient resting place. And more oddly, the bones grafted into the stone are not wholly petrified, even though the process has begun. Ragged strips of fabric, desiccated and rotted, hang on some of the skeletons, and here and there you see the dull grey of iron or the glint of steel.
7926:
A dark intangible shadow turns to face you.
An ancient spirit, dressed in the arms of a soldier, challenges you.
An ancient spirit, dressed in the arms of a soldier, challenges you.

You enter a plain, square room with walls of clean smooth stone and a slightly rounded ceiling. Hanging on the walls are an assortment of martial tools, including crossed black swords and long steel spears. The weapons, as well as the two tapestries, are in surprisingly good condition, due perhaps to the preserving effect of the lack of water and outside contamination.
7927:
Traces of fierce white tones form the aura of this place.
A stocky mountain mule is here, waiting to serve.
A stocky mountain mule is here, waiting to serve.
A great dark-grey horse stamps restively.
Armscor the Woman, wielding an engraved broadsword, is standing here.
Mieldor the Half-Elf, holding a bejewelled oak staff, is resting here (glowing).
A great dark-grey horse stamps restively.

A set of wide, shallow stairs leads up to an open room. The room is raised up on a dais and is bathed in shadows. Still, a sort of unholy light emanates strongly from there, and you sense a great evil power.
7928:
Traces of rich white tones form the aura of this place.
A soft pouch, made from leather, has been left here.
A crimson leather belt is lying here.
An old-looking ring, covered with runes, lies here. (blue aura).
A short spear is lying on the ground.
A crimson leather belt is lying here.
A sabre is on the ground.
A pair of rigid leather sleeves lies here.
A sturdy pair of rigid leather boots are on the ground.
A cutlass is on the ground.
A pair of rigid leather sleeves lies here.
A sturdy pair of rigid leather boots are on the ground.
A short spear is lying on the ground.

When you enter this fell chamber you instantly know you have crossed into a place of great evil and danger. The walls here are rusted black, a scabrous lichen-substance covering the stone and fixtures. The flagstones are scratched and cut, as by the assault of fearsome sharp talons. Resting against the far wall is an immense throne of iron, sturdy as the mountain itself, and just as immovable. You are overcome by a wave of fear and feel that you are in a horribly precarious, dangerous place.
7929:
An elegant marble chest sits against the wall.
A large stone chest is here.

As you break the seal and open the door, a blast of dusty, stale air puffs into your face, momentarily blinding you. When you open your eyes, you see a small five foot square room, with several stone chests lying against the western side of the room.
7930: The enchanting will-of-the-wisp beckons you with a blurred light.

As the trail ends, a yawning indentation opens up to the south, where the rock has been hewn away in large, cracked pieces. Among the layer of smooth water-polished rubble is a collection of huge cube-shaped blocks of granite. The mountainside has been systematically chipped away, and the exposed insides are of the same, good rock as the blocks.
7931: At the crest of this particular slope, a wide, sturdy ledge of solid rock protrudes from the mountainside, and allows east-west travel. Though the wind is loud and powerful, if you stay close to the mountain there is little danger. But past the ledge it falls off steeply, into a rocky plain hundreds of yards below.
7932: A rudely carved channel in the rock here, perhaps an ancient streambed, allows passage up the side of the mountain, which slopes steeply. Except for the long rut, all else is smooth and impassable. Small, smooth stones tumble down periodically.
7933: You slip into a small niche--a jagged crack in the rock. Some geological forces have pulled and stretched the sheer cliff face until it split open, and now a dark cave looks out quietly.
7934: Soft, chalky hills undulate all about. It is hard on the eye, and you find yourself falling asleep even as you walk. It would be so nice to just lay down for a while and rest... to close heavy eyelids for just a moment. It seems like there is no end to this place.
7935: Dead, grey hills are heaped around the foot of the mountains like some dusty piles of chalk. Indeed, the mounds here are of a weird, uncomfortable character. The surface is loose and breaks easily, allowing little foothold for traveller or vegetation. No trees choose to remain here, no grass wreathes the bloodless hills.
7936: A large, steep promontory juts out into the hills, separating the hills on the west from the ones of the east. It is a subtle change. If possible, the eastern hills are less threatening, but also, less alive. The grey of the east is not the grey of dead grass; it is the grey of earth that has never had grass, of flat sheets of stone masquerading as hillsides. A quick clamber up the side of the promontory reveals this area in all its dark and dreary splendour. From way up here the sprawling expanse before you takes on a sort of beauty, like a cold goddess who disdains to smile.
7937: A short evergreen plant, with slightly bluish needles, grows here.

The land about rises higher and higher, affording a good view of a land perhaps not worthy to be seen. Westerly, a dark and thick forest of pines grows among the hills. Far to the east and south, past the grey hills, are the Misty Mountains. And again, far to the north are more of the same.
7938: Here begins--or ends--a rocky, rolling, terrain. Undulating hills, tall and grey, stand stolidly to block your way. The ground itself is hard and crunchy, frozen year-round. Perennially, the summer rains come with cool, soft caresses, to wake the earth, and all to no avail. For deep within the hills slumbers a icy heart that will forever lie dormant.
7939: The slender but massive pines rise all about, through a haunting luminescence that lends a subterranean character to the place, and a wispy fog that entwines and dances with the trunks. The cold of the forest begins to sink in, permeating clothes and chilling armour.
7940: A huge stone giant is here, glaring at you.

The darkness hides the edges of the cave, but you can see that though it is not too large, it is irregular, and dangerous. The ground, however, is fairly even, and matted down with dirt and dead grass.
7941: Cresting the rise of yet another round, grey, hill, a singular thought strikes you. Out here in this wilderness, many miles from civilization or the company of others--the loneliness, and savage, untamed nature of it all is overpowering. There are no footprints in the chalky earth, no burnt-out campfires or discarded horseshoes. Perhaps you are the first to ever venture here. Certainly there is no reason in sight to draw visitors, or even explorers. There is not a soul to be seen for miles and miles in this depressing wasteland.
7942: A wide, flat promontory intrudes shockingly into the heart of the grey hills, glowering ominously at the rest of the landscape. The ledge is shallow and not too high, but flat and composed of a hard, dark rock. It isn't too hard to scramble up the side and get to the other side... more hills.
7943: You have descended into a little flat dell between a very high hill, and a jutting, low escarpment of dark rock. Here is shaded and protected from the periodic winds, and the grass grows thickly. Some hardy bushes perch on the leeward side, and you even see some tough little wildflowers waving in the wind, their plain yellow and white colours a delight in this desolate land.
7944: The ravine continues along in an west-east direction, a great rut furrowed into the hard brown granite. The sides are too steep to see over into the surrounding lands, but to the south, a grim landscape of bleached white hills waits disinterestedly. Scratchy, dense thorn bushes throw thin, spiny claws in your way.
7945: The bush-filled canyon spills out into a rising area of rough, rocky ground, and you can see the solid, immense wall of the mountains rising before you. It is hard to tell exactly what dwells amongst the various dells and depressions here, covered as they are by concealing foliage.
7946: Your path draws up in a rocky little valley with no other exits. The sides are too high to climb, and there are no other paths leading out. The floor of the gulch is dry and strewn with all manner of polished little pebbles and stones. It seems that once there was a small pond here, but now all is dry and quiet. However, a second glance reveals a small shelter behind some bushes. A campfire has been used here not too long ago, and some tools are scattered about haphazardly.
7947: From here unfolds an impressive panorama of a dark wilderness, totally barren of man or his devices. There is no trace of human habitation, not a building or a road of any sort. All you can see are dark forests, white hills, grey marches, and mountains of solid granite. And a deep ancient cold touches all of them with icy fingers.
7948: A rocky ledge protrudes past the slope of the mountainside here, hiding the misty tops from view but offering somewhat of a shelter from the weather. A natural chimney, the sides rough and rocky, give easy access up.
7949: This is a long, smooth slope, covered with half-frozen grass. It is not hard to go east or west, and to the south a large ravine splits the earth. An old animal trail leads to the north, but then meanders off back west.
7950: A long, wide ravine opens to the south and west. The sides are tall and slant at a 45 degree angle to meet the grim, grey sky. The ravine floor is covered by a thick growth of tough bushes that make it hard to traverse. There is no sign of any human life, except for a rough, overgrown trail. You get the feeling that it was made by animals, perhaps wolves or some species of northern elk. However, far above, near the rim of the ravine, there is a long, white scratch of chalk.
7951: Here is a large hill that leans heavily against the mountain to the north. Some scraggly bushes and black, thin trees cling to the cold hard surface, making the way not too hard to climb or descend.
7952: It seems that under the chalky earth here are a pod of large, roundish boulders, for there are perhaps thirty or forty lumps rising from the ground. Some are bald, and some are covered with sparse grass or some bushes, but it is an eerie sight, reminding you of the pupae of insects, or maybe the eggs of an immense arachnid.
7953: A large pile of boulders is sitting here, probably debris from a rockslide.

Bridging the gap between a massive hill of black boulders and a steeply ascending granite terrace is a long, flat ledge, swept clean of debris by a wickedly howling wind. The edge drops away quickly to the south, but the path is wide and by keeping to the north wall is not too dangerous.
7954: Part of a six- or seven-tiered natural terrace, this ridge juts out over the surrounding rock, but is not too high to easily reach. Unfortunately, the ledges seem to be among the clouds, and cannot be accessed from here. This place affords a good view of the lands to the south; where a sprawling expanse of white hills seems to push against a thick, dark forest.
7955: A huge pile of gargantuan, black boulders clumped together, form this part of the mountainside. The rock is hard and smooth, as if weathered from eons of sleet, hail, and cold rain. It is also cold to the core, a deep and ancient cold that goes to your bone and makes you feel small and weak. In your ascent you can go west or east, or head back down to a dark, flat area of plains.
7956: The western side of the mountain has eroded away, leaving a precipitous drop of hundreds of feet. Far, far below, you can make out a shallow depression filled with water and boulders. It would behoove the traveller to watch his step here; a slip could lead to a messy death.
7957: A huge grizzly bear is here, roaming the wild.

The marches extend up to the base of the mountains, which rise rapidly from the surrounding flatlands. The ground is hard and unyielding under your boots. All slumbers dormant in an eternal, icy sleep.
7958: A huge grizzly bear is here, roaming the wild.

The borderlands are great and forbidding--dark and quiet. Here--approximately half the distance between the northern mountains and the southern pine-forest, it is easier to get a perspective of the land. Everything is ugly and unhappy and you wonder why anything would want to live here. But things do live here. You can hear them...
7959: The hills here are steeper and more treacherous. The ground has cracked open in places, the crumbling edges posing danger to those who venture near them. In some parts, the sides of the hills have fallen, leaving sheer cliffs with sharp boulders at the base.
7960: A scene of rolling, lightly wooded hills unfolds before you. The ground is hard with the frozen coldness of years without thawing, the trees sparse and thin. Long, golden grass blankets the solid earth, and hugs the slender black trees.
7961: The frozen tundra-like expanse of the marches extends miles and miles to the east and west, like a huge, league-wide brushstroke of dull black paint. The sun seems to never shine warmly here, though her pale yellow light is often present. Certainly there is never enough heat to melt the crunchy frozen grass and earth underfoot.
7962: A flat, frozen plain stretches out to the horizon, covered with short, dark grasses. Long, sloping hills emerge from the levelness of the marches, and every once in a while a thin, black tree, devoid of leaves or life, can be found standing silently on a hilltop.
7963: The monotonous, cold dark nature of these flatlands seems to sap your energy and vitality. Each step seems to take more and more of an effort, and your will to continue is taxed more and more with each footfall. But it is just as far to go back, so on you go.
7964: The edge of the woods is a strange place--on one side clumps an imposing set of hills, and on the other a dark and living forest. You get the impression that the two sides are different worlds. The inhabitants of one do not invade the territory of the other, and thus an unspoken, unsteady truce prevails. But the tension of the separation, perhaps desirable but certainly not natural, pervades the whole place.
7965: The path winds around an especially dense copse of trees, and you forget which way you were heading, and almost, why you were going that way at all. The darkened forest continues on, with no respite in view.
7966: You have long since lost your sense of direction, and it is all you can do to stumble forward, half blind. The path helps you along, but it gives no comfort. The wicked coldness of the place permeates your thickest cloak, and the darkness suppresses the exhilaration of danger and exploration.
7967: Unlike the other mounds this great hill is tall and flat, with sharp, steeply rising sides. It is bald, and the whitened platform of the top catches the glare the of the unkind distant sun. A precipitous cliff to the west descends into the depths of a dark pine forest, from whence emits a cacophony of imagined forest dangers. In all other directions are monotonous hills.
7968: The trees thin here a bit, as the pines, indisputable masters of their domain, bow to the mountainside, and allow a rocky little trail to lead off to the south.
7969: You tread softly among these gargantuan trees, untouched by man or dwarf since the time when Melkor walked the earth, and led his Balrogs to destroy and debase. A secret voice alerts you to the possibility that one of his fell demons has chosen this very forest as his realm and hiding-place, and your misgivings grow even deeper and more potent.
7970: The forest here is dark, but patches of weak light filter down through the canopy. The less dense nature of the woods must be the cause of the relative brightness. To the west the trees thicken malignantly, like the muscular contraction of a great serpent's coils. Off to the east can be seen large, grey hills, that you aren't sure are any more inviting.
7971: The bitter air that sluggishly wafts through the glades and openings of the forest is crisply frigid, and surprisingly fresh. But it is dark here, and if it weren't for the tiny light of your little lantern, you wouldn't have a chance of staying on the path. As it is, rocks and roots reach for your legs from the side, and ruts in the path open up to trip and hinder your passage.
7972:
There is some snow on the ground.
There are two piles of coins here.
There are two statues of trolls posed in a moment of flight here.
A dark intangible shadow turns to face you.
An ancient spirit, dressed in the arms of a soldier, challenges you.
An ancient spirit, dressed in the arms of a soldier, challenges you.
A dark intangible shadow turns to face you.
An ancient spirit, dressed in the arms of a soldier, challenges you.
An ancient spirit, dressed in the arms of a soldier, challenges you.

Here, just south of a sheer rock face, a small glade can be found amongst the thick vegetation of the vale. This same vegetation blocks any movement east, west, or south, and the rock to the north prevents any option there. Occasionally small pebbles clatter down from atop the face.
7973:
An arcane spirit floats around, making strange magical gestures (glowing).
A spirit floats towards you and howls with an evil laughter.
A spirit floats towards you and howls with an evil laughter.
An arcane spirit floats around, making strange magical gestures (glowing).

Outside, on the mountains, you were frozen by snow and icy winds. Here, the cold is a still, slowly invading entity. No amount of clothes can keep one comfortable. The bare stone walls and trodden floor give no indication of what may be causing the chill, although a small scrawled message catches the eye.
7974:
An ancient spirit, dressed in the arms of a soldier, challenges you.
An ancient spirit, dressed in the arms of a soldier, challenges you.

This room is in utter disarray. There seems to be no order to the clothes and various articles of personal belongings that are strewn about here. Under some of the larger piles several cots can be found, presumably once used to sleep in, when living things inhabited this lair.
7975: The hallway ends here, and leads only back to the south. However, a rough archway leads to the west where you smell something not altogether pleasant, and a crude door is fashioned to the east. Upon the door a small note, dry and crackled with age, is posted.
7976: Branching off to the north and west, this rougly constructed hallway feels too narrow to be comfortable in. The ground, once uneven, has been worn smooth by treadding that occurred in years long ago. The walls have a light coating of frost on them, and have been soild from filthy handprints and splashes of blood. Some mutterings drift in the stale air, originating from the west, while a strange scent finds you from the north.
7977:
Klaees (thedon), wielding a two-handed sword, is standing here.
Ogeron, wielding a black runed dagger, is standing here (hidden).
Drazud (freshmeat), wielding a great warsword, is standing here.

The air grows chill here, so cold that you shiver without control and to no avail. The darkness deepens, and to the west it grows inkier, so that a doorway can only barely be made out. Soft murmurs and ghostly whispers float to your ears, and every ounce of superstition in your body rebels, wanting only to flee as fast and as far from here as possible.
7978:
A musty loaf of bread has been left here.
A musty loaf of bread has been left here.
A musty loaf of bread has been left here.
A musty loaf of bread has been left here.
A musty loaf of bread has been left here.
A wooden chest stands in the corner.
A spirit floats towards you and howls with an evil laughter.

Once this room may have been used for food preparation and storage; now it contains only the remains of the store it once had. Strangely, the provisions do not seem to be spoiled; perhaps the spectral cold kept them preserved. Heaped in the corners are the broken and dusty eating utensils that may have once been used by a company of an army. There is a strong stench of poorly prepared meats here.
7979:
A bastard sword is on the ground.
A pair of chain mail sleeves are lying here.
A pair of ring mail leggings are lying here.
A chain mail coif is on the ground.
A chain mail hauberk is on the ground.
A small oaken table has been set here.
A dark wraith, wielding a broadsword, is here, fighting Tordol (t).
An ancient spirit, dressed in the arms of a soldier, challenges you.
Earubon the Elf (e), wielding a ceremonial dagger, is standing here trying to concentrate.
Tordol the Dwarf (t), wielding a blackened dwarven axe, is here, fighting a dark wraith.

In all corners of this room parchment and paper is piled up, cluttering the ground and housing a large quantity of dust. In the centre of the room, a single, rickety table stands, teetering from all the papers laid atop it. The ghastly glow that lights this chamber is maintained by a small, still candle, placed in the centre of the table. The intense chill seems coldest in this chamber, and the spectral forms draw your very life from you.
7980: There is some snow on the ground.

The top of this range of cliffs has a slight depression in the centre, perhaps this mountain was once an active volcano. In the very centre of this cold and barren plateau, where you stand now, there are frozen and dead stumps and trunks of trees. By the sheer volume of broken trunks, this must have once been a fertile vale, but now, twisted by some foul sorcery, it is a dead, oppressive forest. Once you have entered it, every direction seems the same, as the lifeless stumps crowd about you, confusing your mind.
