7987: Peaceful Stretch in the River Bruinen

The river slows to a near halt as it widens, near the centre of the valley. On the northern bank is a wooden pier overlooking the river, with a set of steps winding up the steep riverbank to a house above. To the south a few crop fields lie, interspersed with small huts where the elves store their farming tools. Downstream the river flows underneath a slender bridge of obviously elven make, and continues down the valley.
7988: A graceful and thin bridge spans the river here, as the river speeds up somewhat from its lazy pace upstream. To the west you can see the river become slightly turbulent, while further downstream the rapids become rather larger as the valley narrows. Swimming there would not be easy.
7989:
A canoe has been left here.
A graceful and slender tree grows here.
A retired Captain stands here, selling boats.

Formed of perfectly fitting stained oak planks, the pier provides a breathtaking view of the river and valley. To the north steps ascend the riverbank, leading up to the house. This is a popular place to hang out due to the moderate temperature here, and is obviously used often judging by the many boats tied up to the dock. A sign is shoved into the ground here.
7990: A lovely elven maid is serving beverages here.

This quaint, spacious room has many windows offering a spectacular view of the Bruinen River. There are many tables and chairs, and a fresh breeze seems to always be blowing through. This looks like a nice place to relax for a while. A sign is posted on the wall.
7991: An elven baker is standing here, covered in flour.
The talented baking staff of this shop makes fresh baked goods twice a day. The smell of delicious cake, and fruit pastries makes your mouth water. You see a sign on the display case.
7992:
An elven grocer is standing here, quietly humming to herself.
An Elf is here walking around.

Here the elves run a lively trade in supplies for adventurers. In addition to a wide selection of items made here in Rivendell, this store often has something exotic to offer. There is a sign posted behind the counter.
7993: The trail crosses the slope here, winding through the pine trees. Nearer the valley floor the pines give way to oaks and beeches, perhaps because of the shelter this deep ravine provides. Looking down you can see this path bridges the river and heads onto the northern bank, meeting two other trails just to the west of a large house. Above here the path climbs steeply to the top of the slope, and leaves the valley.
7994: An elven guard is wandering here, keeping the peace.

The path travels across the slope here, through a mixture of oak and beech trees. Further down it leaves the trees and descends steeply to the valley floor, where it meets another trail south of the river. To the east it levels off for a while, before taking a final steep turn upwards and leaving the valley altogether.
7995: To the west and east the cliff is sheer and impassable. Even here the path has to traverse across the slope, cutting into the rock face in parts. The track itself is solidly built and looks completely safe, with rocks cleared away and the sides shored up by wood at several points. Looking down you can see this path follows the river east for a while, then bridges it and heads towards a large house on the northern bank.
7996: Top of a Steeply Sloping Path

The Bruinen cuts across the moors, widening from the gorge it is to the east and west. Here it is a wide and deep valley, sheltered from the elements that make the moorland so barren. Looking down you see verdant greenery, and some signs of inhabitation: a large house lies on the northern bank of the river, surrounded by cultivated fields and gardens. A well built and obvious path leads down the valley wall, but does not continue into the moors in any noticeable form.
7997: The trail here follows the Bruinen on its southern bank. As the river flows towards the end of the valley it accelerates and passes over some rapids, gradually falling further below the level of the path. To the west, where the riverbanks disappear in the gorge, the path can go no further and begins climbing up the steep valley slopes. Eastwards it passes through some fields and then bridges the river, heading towards the house on the north bank.
7998: Three paths meet here, just south of the bridge. The main trail travels north and west from here, while a smaller and less well-used one climbs up the valley slopes and through some trees. On the other side of the Bruinen a large house can be seen, overlooking the river from atop the steep bank.
7999: Twisting Path above a Pine Forest

You are on a path winding across the fairly steep slopes in the northwest part of this valley. Below this point you can see the trail descend into a pine forest, and later emerge from it nearer the river that runs through the centre of the valley. To the west the path twists further as it seeks a way out of the valley.
8000: An Elf is here walking around.

This path is near the top of the valley walls, many hundreds of feet above the valley floor down below. The path has been worn by many footprints over the ages, and has become rather narrow and treacherous in parts. Although further to the east is not such a poor path, near the top of the valley walls certainly is. The final section requires any traveller to be extremely sure of foot.
8001: Here the moors are interrupted by a large valley, and it is down into this that the path leads. Looking down a verdant green valley can be seen, somewhat at odds with the rest of the landscape around here. A river runs through the centre of the valley, several hundred feet below, and it is perhaps this and the protection from harsh winds that allows the greenery to prosper down there.
8002: Path Winding through a Pine Forest

You are in the middle of a light pine forest, on a winding path. These trees have obviously stood for hundreds of years, as their weight and girth will attend to. Out to the east you can see the trail leave the forest and meet with several other trails near a large house. Further up the trail becomes steeper and leaves the tree-line behind.
8003: Track on the Outskirts of a Pine Forest

You are on a path overlooking a pine forest, in a sheltered valley. Westwards it leads across the slope towards the high moors above, while below it descends into the forest. It becomes extremely steep and difficult there, as the trail is little more than a stairway of tree roots and branches. You would have to be very careful with your footing to climb down that way.
8004:
A graceful and slender tree grows here.
An Elf is here walking around.

You feel a sense of comfort and well-being as you stroll along the paved courtyard. You notice the upper floors are built on top of this plaza, except in the centre where the sunlight warms this place by day, and the stars shine in by night. The courtyard as a whole is a popular meeting place for the residents of Rivendell, and you can see elves everywhere talking merrily or singing together. You see a magnificent fountain to the north- east and some shops along the perimeter of the yard.
8005: A graceful and slender tree grows here.

You notice the upper floors are built on top of this plaza, except in the centre where the sunlight warms this place by day, and the stars shine in by night. You see a magnificent fountain to the north and some shops along the perimeter of the yard.
8006: A large fountain, made from grey stone, pours water from its centre.

Here seems to be the central meeting place for the inhabitants of Rivendell. The mood is so jubilant that you can't help but smile broadly as you wait here. Unlike the rest of the courtyard, there is no roof above your head, allowing the sunlight to shine in by day and the stars to be visible by night. Before you stands a huge marble fountain with an awe-inspiring copper statue of Ulmo, the Vala of the Waters. In the centre of the fountain lies a clear crystal, filling the air with a soft radiance.
8007: A graceful and slender tree grows here.

A strip of leather with a buckle is lying here.

An elven tailor is standing here, tidying his selection.
A sturdy pack horse is standing here.

The back of this spacious room is dominated by four large worktables, upon which a variety of garments can be seen, each at a different stage of its creation. On the table to the left, huge bolts of fabric lie next to sharp shears, used to cut the material, whilst on the table furthest to the right, the clothing lies, neatly folded, awaiting only finishing touches. On the two remaining tables, the partially crafted garments lie, and at the front of the shop, the finished goods are displayed on shelves and pegs for your perusal. A large sign has been hung on the wall, beside the doorway, and a smaller piece of paper has been nailed beside it.
8012:
Angdil the elven smith is here, fashioning exquisite armour and weaponry.
An elven guard is wandering here, keeping the peace.

This huge room is dug partially underground to regulate the temperature produced by the many furnaces constantly in operation here. You can find smiths at work at almost any hour, producing high quality armour and weapons. A sign stands near the entrance.
8013:
A graceful and slender tree grows here.
Arwen Undomiel stands here in radiant beauty (glowing).

8015: A large bulletin board, entitled "News of Arda", is mounted here.

Here the inhabitants of Rivendell come to informally honour the Ainur and Eru Iluvatar. Especially dear to the elves is Varda, and for her the roof is opened on clear nights to allow the starlight in. Important messages from the Ainur, as interpreted by the Wise, are collected here for the enlightenment of all.
8020:
Some plump juicy grapes are growing here.
Some plump juicy grapes are growing here.
Some plump juicy grapes are growing here.

On a steep slope near the valley ridge, the elves have constructed a tiered, irrigated, vineyard here. You see rows and rows of vines with big delicious red grapes growing on them. Occasionally some workers will show up and take a bushel of grapes to the House. To the north, a short walkway leads to a cottage.
8021: These fertile fields draw irrigation from the river south of here and support a range of crops. The Misty Mountains appear in breathtaking majesty to the east, over the roof of a small house. To the north is the entrance to a small house.
8022:
A doorkeep stands here ready to obey his master's wishes.
A tall and strong guard is here.
A tall and strong guard is here.

The pleasant warmth of a bright fireplace welcomes all friendly visitors to the house of the Elven wizard, explorer and part-time orc hunter Galawon. A large wooden table, surrounded by chairs, stands in the middle of the room, upon a brightly coloured carpet. In the southwestern corner a sofa and a couple of armchairs offer a more comfortable way to rest. A mantelpiece, definitely unusual in its nature, stands beside the front door, on the southern side of the room; to the north, behind an arched passage, a smaller room can be seen. Wide windows on the eastern wall offer a staggering view of the Misty Mountains.
8026: On a Huge Outcrop of Rock

A massive spur of rock thrusts out into a narrow gorge here. To the east the Bruinen falls several hundred yards into a frothy cauldron of water, filling the air with a thin mist. The landscape in all directions is nothing but barren moorland, except to the west where the gorge opens up and becomes rather lush. The only way down into the valley you can see is a spiral staircase cut in the cliff, which descends to the bottom of the gorge.
8027:
An Elf is here walking around.
An Elf is here walking around.
An Elf is here walking around.
An Elf is here walking around.

The path is rather slippery in this narrow gorge due to the spray, and you will have to pick your footing extremely carefully. The path winds down from above in a set of stairs cut in the rock, and continues west in the small space between river and cliff wall. Down to the east the river foams and churns, after entering the gorge in a waterfall of several hundred yards.
8028: A Rocky Ledge by the River

The river passes over a small waterfall just downstream of here, and following it the path climbs down on a stairway that has been cut from the rock. Upriver the path hugs the cliff walls, and in parts becomes treacherously narrow. To the west the gorge widens, and becomes a lush valley.
8029: This narrow river track winds around outcrops in the rock, following the trail of the river. In parts it is not a path at all, merely rocks it is possible to walk on. To continue the path someone has cut a steep stairway in the cliff sides, which ascends into the gorge to the east. The river itself passes over a small fall south of here and winds on down the valley.
8030: Bottom of a Waterfall in the Bruinen

The Bruinen enters the vale of Rivendell in a great cataract, creating a thundering roar and a great cloud of mist, and then continues down in a series of cascades. At last the water plunges in a twenty-foot sheer arc, raising a gentle mist. Downstream you can see it wind through the valley, pass through some rapids and leave it as the cliff walls narrow again. Swiftly flowing as most mountain streams usually are, this one appears to lose some of its speed to the west of here, where it slows to a lethargic pace.
8031: Gleaming in the light of several torches, sharp and shining, are some of the finest swords ever created. Fastened to the plain marble walls, as memories of the past creations, the swords have been forged by the hands of Feanor, the greatest of all the elven smiths, and his son Curufin, and in turn those of his son, Celebrimbor the ring-maker. Not much else can be seen in this hall save the bright light that beckons you from the south.
8032: The light in this room comes from the walls themselves. Several gems, rubies, emeralds, opals and sapphires have been inlaid to create a pattern of light that beckons and calls, telling tales of the forgotten eras. The crystals on the walls almost seem in motion, always giving a new pattern to follow, a new story to learn. As the dazzling patterns and colours continue to swirl around you and in your mind you snap back to reality with a sense of loss, but still, a sense of joy and love.
8033: These fertile fields draw irrigation from the river south of here and support a range of crops. The Misty Mountains appear in breathtaking majesty to the east. You can enter the river here via the irrigation canals.
8034: These fertile fields draw irrigation from the river south of here and support a range of crops. The Misty Mountains appear in breathtaking majesty to the east. You can enter the river here via the irrigation canals.
8035: In a single curving span this bridge leaps twenty feet over the Bruinen, without rail or kerb. At first it would appear to be less than safe, but underfoot the off-white stone of which it is made proves to be of exceptional grip. Like all things of Elven manufacture it fits beautifully with nature - its simple and minimal profile does not blot the landscape, instead enhancing it with its own grace.
8036: Several trails meet here, in the centre of the northern river bank. Paths to the north and west lead into the large pine forest that dominates this side of the valley, while to the south another trail bridges the river. To the east a large house sits atop the steep bank, surrounded by gardens and some smaller buildings - perhaps this is the fabled Last Homely House of Elrond Half-Elven.
8037: Entrance to the Last Homely Home
A graceful and slender tree grows here.

A beautifully painted archway, with a silver plaque set above it, gives access to the House of Elrond. North of here a large field can be seen, while to the east the sound of singing and merriment can be heard in the courtyard. To the south you notice the Ranger's House, where the noble rangers are quartered.
8038:
An elven guard is wandering here, keeping the peace.
A noble Elf stands here, proudly displaying his valuable assets.

The Rivendell Jeweller has been recently restored and expanded, still containing the largest wealth of gems in all of Eriador, but now stocking smaller pieces of jewellery. Behind a finely carved desk stands a tall Elf, and in front of him the largest range of priceless items you might ever see; their value maybe matching that of the Arkenstone itself. A sign rests on the counter.
8039:
An elven herbalist is watching his merchandise here.
Elrond the Master of Rivendell is standing here (glowing).
On one wall, a window allows sight of the outside. Otherwise, this room is unremarkable. Your eye sees boxes and bags filled with herbs and dried plants. Spices seem to be this store's trade.
8040:
A graceful and slender tree grows here.
Elrohir, son of Elrond is here (glowing).
Elladan, son of Elrond is here (glowing).
A ranger stands quietly here, willing to teach his knowledge of woodcraft.
An elven guard is wandering here, keeping the peace.

The furnishings provided are nothing spectacular, just some comfortable beds against the west and east walls with a simple chest at the foot of each. No possessions are left here, and the room is usually empty, as most rangers spend extended periods in the wilderness far away from this sheltered vale. However, some of the most skilled ones work in shifts to provide around-the- clock training for young Dunedain and elves eager to learn. These instructors stress leadership skills and self-confidence, and this shows through in the excellence of the ranger organization.
8042:
A domesticated pony, beast of burden to many, stands here.
A sturdy pack horse is standing here.
A domesticated pony, beast of burden to many, stands here.
A sturdy pack horse is standing here.
A sturdy pack horse is standing here.
An elven youth is busy attending to the animals.
An elf is here walking around.

Guests of Elrond leave their horses and pets here in the care of professional stablehands where they are routinely fed, groomed, and exercised while their owners are enjoying a rest in Rivendell. In addition, fresh horses are always kept available for those in need of transport.
8043: At this simple stand a cheerful elf will arrange a pet for you from Rivendell's stock of excellent trained animals. There is a sign posted on the wall.
8044: The path winds through the pine forest, getting steeper the further up you look. There it gets so difficult that you would need to scramble up the slope, using the roots and branches as steps. Another path branches off to the north, where it suddenly levels out as it begins to travel along the slope towards the east. The trees themselves are gnarled and ancient, obviously having overlooked this valley for many hundreds of years. A low stone building stands east of here.
8045: This short path leads east to the agricultural fields that feed Rivendell. To the west there is a small archway that leads to the courtyard of the Last Homely House.
8046:
An elven guard is standing here at his post.
Erienal, the host to guests of Imladris is standing here.
A sturdy pack horse is standing here.
Weary travellers in need of rest may arrange for a private room here. Most guest chambers are small, yet comfortable, and offer a relaxing view of the Bruinen as it rolls past Rivendell.
8047:
A ticket has been forgotten here.
A ticket has been forgotten here.
A ticket has been forgotten here.
A ticket has been forgotten here.
A ticket has been forgotten here.
A ticket has been forgotten here.
A ticket has been forgotten here.
A ticket has been forgotten here.
A ticket has been forgotten here.
A ticket has been forgotten here.
A ticket has been forgotten here.
A ticket has been forgotten here.
A ticket has been forgotten here.
A ticket has been forgotten here.
A ticket has been forgotten here.
A large bulletin board, entitled "Clerics' Guild Board", is mounted here.
A venerable elven priest is here, willing to teach his art.
Silmariel, wielding a steel-tipped spear, is standing here.
You feel a spiritual growth within yourself as you enter. At this guild the master specializes in channeling the god's will towards healing, but also knows many other prayers.
8048:
A large bulletin board, entitled "Mages' Guild Board", is mounted here.
A grey haired elf is standing here, ready to share his knowledge.

The spell masters of Rivendell are here at all hours to keep up with the demand for magical knowledge. Here one can learn a broad selection of mage spells, from elves who have had centuries to hone their talents.
8050: The stairs continue up to the third floor and down to the ground floor. A carpeted hallway extends east from here, while a wide terrace of white stone, probably marble, opens to the south. A white, graceful archway leads towards another section of the Last Homely Home in the north.
8051:
An elven guard is wandering here, keeping the peace.
Elrond the Master of Rivendell is standing here (glowing).
The spacious hallway runs east to west. More portraits, this time of the Dunedain Kings, are in view on the walls; Elendil, and his remarkable son, Isildur.
8052:
Elrond the Master of Rivendell is standing here (glowing).
An elven guard is wandering here, keeping the peace.

The spacious hallway runs east to west. On the red velvet-covered walls you notice some portraits of great elves who still remain in Middle-earth today; Glorfindel, a warrior who survived countless battles and trials, Galadriel, queen of the elves of Lorien, and Elrond, master of Rivendell.
8053:
A huge clock is standing here.
A large bookshelf sits against the wall.
On the bookshelf, there is a Grey Havens map, an ancient parchment, a map of Rivendell and a silvery-green leaf.
Erestor the High Mage of Rivendell is studying here (glowing).
An Elf is here walking around.
You marvel at the vast collection of tomes, books, and scrolls in this room. You can often find the more studious inhabitants here absorbing lore. There is a large sign hanging on the south wall.
8054: An Elven steward stands here, watching over the household.

A large bed dominates the room. Two paintings of Mirkwood hang on the western wall. A window showing the forested valley of Rivendell is in the northern wall, and against the southern wall stands a large closet.
8055: A large bulletin board, entitled "Free Peoples' Chronicles", is mounted here.

This room is intended as a waiting room for persons who will meet with Elrond in the Council Chamber to the north. There are a lot of comfortable chairs, and desks to organise documents on. You see a wooden sign with large letters carved into it near the door.
8056:
A large bulletin board, entitled "Tales", is mounted here.
A fine marble chessboard with ivory and ebony pieces is set here.
A large stone fireplace with a roaring fire warms the room.
Quenaire, the Elven master of tales stands here, waiting for an audience.
Elrond the Master of Rivendell is standing here (glowing).

This room takes its name from a great hearth at the north end, in which a bright fire burns continuously. On either side, carven pillars extend along the length of the room. The cosy atmosphere makes this a favourite meeting place for guests of Elrond.
8057:
A seed-cake has been left here.
A wrapped piece of candy is here.
A large biscuit has been left here.
A loaf of bread has been left here.

This room is dominated by a long table that extends almost the entire length of the room. The table is covered with a scrumptious looking spread and there are many chairs to sit in. Every now and then someone will walk in and take some food to eat, and it is quickly replaced by the kitchen staff.
8058: This giant-sized room takes up most of the top floor of the house. The ceiling is formed into a dome of a glassy material which is impossible to break, yet perfectly clear to gaze through. Although there is not much to see of the landscape from here, the stars of the night sky come into full view, seemingly better than even under the clearest of weather conditions.
8059: The aroma of gourmet cooking wafts through the air. You see several ovens and huge kettles, along with an impressive collection of pots and utensils hanging from racks near the ceiling. Cooks work here almost incessantly to turn Rivendell's bountiful harvest into delicious food, and it looks like they truly enjoy their labours.
8060:
An elven guard is wandering here, keeping the peace.
An impressive elven knight stands watch here (glowing).
An Elf is here walking around.
This ornate staircase leads up to the Royal Suites, wherein reside Elrond and Arwen. A guard is usually posted here to politely guide guests to the public areas of Rivendell.
8061: A large bulletin board, entitled "Board of the Free Peoples", is mounted here.

This is the famous council room where the Istari and other important persons meet with Elrond to discuss pressing matters. A long table dominates the furniture along with a few chairs. When this room is not in use by the council, Elrond welcomes all who have need to use these facilities.
8062:
A well-crafted white fountain is here, water pouring forth from it.
An Elf is here walking around.

This is a nice place to take a breath of fresh air during extended council meetings. A lovely view opens from here to the valley, with the south fork of the Bruinen extending off into the Misty Mountains, which seem to loom right in front of you. You can see some very tall peaks that break through the clouds, and many that have snow and ice on them.
8063: Large bookshelves completly cover all walls, interrupted only by two small doorways, one leading east and the other west. Four large armchairs made of rugged leather stand around a low oaken table. As there are no windows, the light is provided by lanterns positioned in several locations around the library. The floor is covered by large carpets woven of wool.
8064: A doorkeep stands here ready to obey his master's wishes.

A large mirror covers the northern wall, exquistily carved in ebony. Some worn cloaks hang from a clothes hanger made from a large oakbranch. The floor is covered by a large cavebear fur and a window showing the valley outside is situated in the southern wall. Looking west you see a large library.
8065: A humble man stands here, ready to help you with your things.

There is a small chair standing infront of the fire. It looks like a nice chair to relax in and close enough to the fire so there wouldn't be any problem to keep warm. On the walls there is a lot of art hanging, it makes the room look friendly. Most of the art is hand made paintings of flowers. But one off the paintings looks different, it's something written all over the painting.
8066: You just reached the highest point in Rivendell the land of the elves. From this place you are able to gaze all the nice spots in Rivendell. On a cloudless day or a night with a high moon, you can glance over the ferocious battles around the vicious ford.
8067: A doorwarden stands here ready to obey his master's wishes.

You find yourself in an entrance to a building, here the floor is made of dirt. You have to brush of your shoes before you go any futher so you dont drag any dirt into the inner rooms of the house. In the south and north the house continues. A large warning sign stands here.
8068: You are now in the hallway to and old building, on the walls there are some picture of old people. The floor is tatterd from many years of hard use. On the floor an carpet is put, it has stripes in different colour.
8069: An Elven steward stands here, watching over the household.

Here is an bedchamber, there is only a bed in here. The room has no windows so the owner can sleep at anytime with out being botherd by the sun. Along the bed a small lamp stands giving a pleasent light in the room.
8070: This is a small library, that the owner has been collection books for in many years. The walls are coverd with bookshelf that contain many book, most of them are about the powers of magic. An small sofa is standing in the corner of the room, and it is ragged from many years of use.
8071:
A well-crafted white fountain is here, water pouring forth from it.
A large bookshelf sits against the wall.
A sturdy pack horse is standing here.

The ceiling and walls of this room are covered in a shimmering white stone of unknown origin, broken only by occasional paintings. The paintings seem old and fragile, depicting ancient events of Elven lore. High bookshelves follow the walls from east to west filled with tomes of days past. Near the northern wall a large cauldron is placed, suitable for experiments which have been known to billow thick plumes of harmless smoke out into the main hallways of Rivendell that lie to the west. A simple door leading to a bedchamber adorns the north wall.
8072: A doorwarden stands here ready to obey his master's wishes.

Separated by an oakdoor from the rest of Rivendell, this strange house is suffocated by smoke-filled air. To the east, further into the house, there is even more smoke. On the wall there are several pictures showing groups of people standing beneath a cloud-filled sky. Under one of these pictures there is a bronze sign. The sign is ancient and dirty making it nearly illegible. However, a few symbols on the sign, N^m'r C^st'd, can be discerned.
8073: A mailbox stands here stuffed full of messages.
This cubicle allows two individuals to engage in private discussion. The walls are plain wooden panels, void of any ornaments. The council chamber can be glimpsed south of here.
8074: A humble man stands here, ready to help you with your things.

In the right corner of this simple room there is a small fireplace emitting a warm glow. For some reason the dense smoke found in the adjacent room does not enter this room, perhaps because of the warm fire. A small table stands in the left corner and next to it there is a bed with white sheets. On the wall four hooks can be seen hanging while a red carpet lies across the floor looking rather clean and in good shape.
8076: The river rushes through the narrow gorge with a thundering tumult. The walls press closer together, causing the current to rush even faster. Threatening boulders that have managed somehow to resist the current loom as the current rushes past, promising certain death if struck.
8077: Huge stone walls border the river both north and south, imprisoning it though the river rages against its captors. The current is treacherously swift, threatening to dash any boats against the sharp rocks.
8078: The river is shallow here, but still swift enough to be a danger to the care- less traveller. To the west, the river enters a gorge -- steep rocky cliffs rise on both side -- and to the east it continues toward its source. The trail that follows the southern bank is accessible here -- sharp rocks prevent access farther upstream and downstream.
8079: The river grows smaller and shallower to the east as it approaches its head- waters. Several small streams join it here, and the volume of water is sig- nificantly greater to the west. Sharp rocks and treacherous eddies in the current prevent one from accessing the trail that still follows the river to the south.
8080: The river makes a hairpin turn from south to west here, following a natural gap between two mountains. The source of this water cannot lie too much far- ther upstream -- it hardly merits the designation river at this point. To the south, a gigantic natural bridge made of a single block of granite dis- lodged from the mountainside spans the river.
8081: The trail winds along the rim of a shallow gorge, through which the river to the north makes its way. Any slack in alertness may prove dangerous, for the trail is very narrow and in some places slick with spray rising from small cataracts in the river.
8082: A demon wolf lurks here, its dark form twisting and hiding its shape.

The trail forks here, with a small and faint spur leading down to the east into a canyon. The main trail turns north, following the path of the turbulent river. The only vegetation in this sombre landscape are bushes that possess wicked thorns, which grab and tear at all exposed clothing.
8083: The river to the north is passing through a shallow gorge, while the trail winds along on the rim. The trail turns from south to west here, following the river as best it can. To the east, a large ridge rises to the south of the trail, sealing it between the mountainside and the river.
8084: The trail is very precarious indeed, poised along a gorge to the north and a looming mountainside to the south. Sometimes boulders from frequent rock- slides almost completely block the path, forcing those who wish to pass into dangerously scrambling over the debris. To the east, the gorge seems to be nearing its head, and the trail begins to head down toward the edge of the river.
8085: The head of the gorge lies just to the east, and the sheer rock cliff that lies to the south of the trail seems to end there as well. The trail is often littered with debris from frequent rockslides, but at least it is much wider here than farther to the west.
8086: A demon wolf lurks here, its dark form twisting and hiding its shape.

The trail again runs right along the river here, and due to the caprice of nature, the sharp rocks that usually border the riverbed are not as frequent here, allowing access to the cold water. To the south is a smaller trail that leads down into a canyon that lies to the south of the ridge that begins just west of here. The trail itself continues east and west, leaving the river briefly in the latter direction.
8087: Just to the east, the river bends slightly, and the trail takes advantage of a magnificent natural granite bridge to cross the shallow gorge. To the west, the trail continues to follow every twist of the river, eventually leading out of the Misty Mountains and into the Ettenmoors.
8088: This massive rock slab has fortuitously formed a bridge across the river's gorge, a fact taken advantage of by the trail. Below runs the river, still daunting despite being so near to its source. A small ledge situated along the western cliff below the bridge might allow one access to the river, but the currents there are bound to be dangerous.
8089: A demon wolf lurks here, its dark form twisting and hiding its shape.

This trail cuts between two large peaks, leaving a river to the north and heading south deeper into the mountains. The air is permanently chilled here, and the rarefied atmosphere makes breathing laborious. To the south the road seems to head down slightly, before twisting out of sight.
8090: A demon wolf lurks here, its dark form twisting and hiding its shape.

The road takes a turn here to the west. It leads deeper south and maybe into some unknown regions of the mountains. When you look towards the top of the mountains, all you see is fog everywhere which hides most of the mountains. Occasionally you hear the sound of great big eagles high up in the sky. You wonder what kind of magic is hidden in the niches of these mountains.
8091: A half-decayed corpse of a goblin lies rotting on the ground.

The road passes through a narrow gully here, sharply turning from east to south. Piled in the middle of the trail are the bodies of two unfortunate travellers -- elven hunters perhaps -- who look to have succumbed to an ambush of some sort. The rocky sides of the gully could easily hide dozens of un- seen enemies. Whoever these travellers were, they gave a good accounting of themselves -- the presence of several goblin corpses attests to this.
8092: A demon wolf lurks here, its dark form twisting and hiding its shape.

To the south, the road slopes downward through a narrow gap between two large mountains. In that direction, the mountains look to give way eventually to rocky hills. To the north, the road slants upward, again following the only path between the two peaks, before it makes a sharp turn to the east and is lost from view.
8093: The road continues south from here. To your west you see a small cutout in the mountain side which allows you to step out of the road into comparative secrecy away from the eyes of other curious travellers. The cold is beginning to get to you and you wish you had more clothes and some ale to warm yourself with.
8094: The narrow road seemingly ends here, as its route south quickly becomes lost among some low hills. To the west is a deep valley filled with a dark pine forest. Occasional lonely howls echo up from the ominous forest, but the trees are too dense to locate their source.
8095: The hills are little more than jagged outcroppings of rock thrusting upward through the earth. On all sides, the high peaks of the Misty Mountains rise, enclosing this oasis of rocky hills. There is a road to the north that once led through this area, but its path has become lost so there is no indication of a correct direction to proceed.
8096: The rocky hills continue in all directions, until they eventually give way to mountains once more. These hills are like slanted rock tables, all tilted up from west to east at steep angles. The sharp rocks and rocky soil make walk- ing difficult, threatening to shred even the toughest of boots. Some distance to the east, there is a hill noticeably larger and of different appearance than the others.
8097: In every direction save east steep cliffs squelch all hope of movement. To the west, these rocky hills continue, bare except for occasional thorny plants that seem more dead than alive.
8098:
A huge warg is here, moving in for the kill.
A huge warg is here, moving in for the kill.

These hills are essentially large blocks of granite that have thrust upward through the tortured earth. On all sides, the high peaks of Hithaeglir rise, totally enclosing these barren hills. To the east, an especially large hill dominates the scenery.
8099: This hill, though smaller than the mountains to the east and south, is still very impressive. It is crowned by a small circle of stones, probably the remnant of some ancient tower -- perhaps a road or trail once led through this area. In every direction save west, the hillside is too steep and dangerous to attempt to negotiate, and any attempt to do so would surely send one sprawling to one's death on the jagged rocks below.
8100: These barren hills are formed by sharp rectangular blocks of granite that have been tilted at angles by geological forces. There is very little vegetation -- nothing larger than a few scraggly thornbushes has successfully found purchase in the scant soil. To the southeast, an especially large hill rises above the others.
8101: To the east is the the exit from this underground chamber. The walls of this place exude a sense of age -- perhaps even before the Witchking of Angmar first made his power felt and fell things gathered from all corners of Arda.
8102: The walls here are in better shape than elsewhere, and some faint carvings in an unknown language can be made out high on the western wall. This age of this place is an almost tangible force, seeming to mock those who dare invade with their own insignificance in the grand pageant of time.
8103: A hungry warg stands here, sniffing around for flesh.

The purpose behind this place is unclear. The walls are lined with ancient masonry that crumbles at the slightest touch, indicating great age. Perhaps this hill once housed a tower for guarding the dangerous road that led to these rocky hills, or perhaps this place is the tomb of some ancient and forgotten king.
8104: A hungry warg stands here, sniffing around for flesh.

This entire hill seems to be hollow, an amazing accomplishment considering the solid granite exterior. The purpose of this place has been lost in antiquity. Maybe this was once a watchtower of old Angmar, or perhaps this place predates even the Witchking's rule.
8105: The valley slopes steeply upward to the east, eventually meeting a trail that runs along the top of a ridge. The trees, mainly pine and fir, are old, perhaps old enough to remember the icy winters of the Witch-king's rule over Angmar to the north. The valley floor lies to the west, enclosed on three sides by steep mountain slopes.
8106: A rock cliff looms to the north, and the multitude of large boulders scattered among the ancient trees hints at frequent rockslides. The ground here is covered with old pine-needles and the tracks of many wolves. Howling and occasional sounds of padding feet just out of sight heightens the sense of danger here.
8107: There is a large notch in the cliff directly to the north, and many boulders have been piled there to obscure whatever lies within it. The ancient pines and firs are dense here, their black trunks giving this area a gloomy and foreboding atmosphere.
8108:
A grey wolf is here, thin from starvation.
A grey wolf is here, thin from starvation.
A grey wolf is here, thin from starvation.
A grey wolf is here, thin from starvation.
A great black and silver wolf is standing here, at the head of the pack.

The deep valley comes to an end here -- it is impossible to head farther west or north. To the south, more of the forest stretches, but in that direction as well a cliff is visible. The forest is dark -- very little sunlight can filter down through the thick canopy of pine needles -- and the howling of wolves indicates that this area may not be a good place to tarry.
8109: A hungry warg stands here, sniffing around for flesh.

There is an ominous cave to the south, nestled in this corner of the valley. The ground is littered with bones here -- mostly of elk and other large game, but there are a few of unmistakably humanoid origin. To the west and above the cave to the south rise sheer cliffs, inaccessible to those without wings.
8110: A hungry warg stands here, sniffing around for flesh.

The black trunks of the ancient pines press close together, forcing one to move via circuitous routes through this area. In a small clearing lies the carcass of a large elk -- almost completely stripped of meat, but obviously no more than a few days old. Its spine had been crushed and shattered by some mighty blow. Some of the smaller bones have been scattered about -- probably by scavenging wolves.
8111: The trees thin out a bit here, on the crest of a small hill in the valley floor. Immediately to the east and south, the hard grey granite of the moun- tains rises abruptly in a sheer rocky cliff. To the west and north the dense pine forest hides the ground, and also wolves judging by the occasional howls that can be heard in the wind.
8112: A hungry warg stands here, sniffing around for flesh.

This cave is fairly dry, and its floor is made of solid granite with a few old pine needles strewn about -- probably blown in from the forest to the north. The cave extends further into the rock to the east, and from that direction the smell of rotting meat can be detected.
8113:
A brutish forest troll is hunting here, looking for some tasty flesh.
A brutish forest troll is hunting here, looking for some tasty flesh.
A hungry warg stands here, sniffing around for flesh.

This dark cave smells of unwashed bodies and rotting meat. There are three piles of greasy pine needles and moss that look like crude beds, and scattered about are remnants of past meals. The cave continues to the south, but the darkness prevents any details from being espied.
8114:
A brutish forest troll is hunting here, looking for some tasty flesh.
A brutish forest troll is hunting here, looking for some tasty flesh.

The cave dead-ends here, becoming too narrow to pass any further. This part of the cave seems to be used as a refuse room -- with many gnawed bones, some still with clinging pieces of meat, tossed carelessly about. The smell also hints that this area is used as a sewer, as the trolls seem to be content to live in their own filth.
8115:
A nasty goblin is here walking around.
A goblin warrior is threatening to start a fight here.
A goblin warrior is threatening to start a fight here.
A nasty goblin is here walking around.

This area is the intersection of two major tunnels -- one passage leads to the west, while another slopes steeply down from north to south. This en- tire area is littered with the nasty leavings of goblins -- everything from feces to bones covered with clinging bits of rotting meat has been strewn haphazardly about the area.
8116: A goblin warrior is threatening to start a fight here.

This narrow tunnel is quite steep, going down as it goes north. Its walls are of black rock, and no time has been spared to finish their rough edges. Only the occasional gnawed bone litters the stone floor. The air is smoky and you feel a warm breeze coming from below.
8117:
A goblin warrior is threatening to start a fight here.
A goblin warrior is threatening to start a fight here.
A large, squat goblin gestures with a black knife.

Six flickering torches are mounted on one side of this roughly circular chamber, on either side of the passage entrance. Their baleful light reveals a scene from Hell. The walls and ceiling are made of dark, rough-hewn rock and the floor is covered with a stinking litter. In the deep gloom on the far side of the chamber, an altar to darkness rises among the smoke like a throne to Morgoth or a remembrance of long-fallen Thangorodrim.
8118:
A goblin warrior is threatening to start a fight here.
A goblin warrior is threatening to start a fight here.
A goblin warrior is threatening to start a fight here.

As you go deeper into these caves, signs of goblin habitat increase. There are a few faint carvings on the wall of the cavern, showing goblins worshipping their leaders. Other carvings show the leaders moving towards the interior followed by slaves carrying large chests.
8119:
A goblin warrior is threatening to start a fight here.
A goblin warrior is threatening to start a fight here.
A goblin warrior is threatening to start a fight here.
A huge fierce goblin is here, dark as evil itself.

This seems like the innermost cave. There is a huge goblin chair in the middle and several small chairs to the side. On the walls there are carvings showing previous goblin chieftains and innumerable others serving them. If one were to study the carvings carefully, it would become apparent that some of those displayed in the carvings are orcs.
8120:
There are two mushrooms here.
There are two bright red mushrooms here.
A patch of moss grows here on a wet, flat stone.
A small, sickly green mushroom grows here.

This chamber seems to be on the path of an occasional underground river as it is more damp than expected. The floor is largely buried in a soil made of gravel and foul refuse. The air is humid and heavy with the smell of waste. An opening in the ceiling shows where the waste comes from. The wall are covered by a thick layer of moss and mildew, and numerous mushrooms grow on the dirt.
8121: This cavern is very small and narrow. Those with claustrophobia will tend to flee through the only visible exit towards the east. The ground is littered with feces, some fresh, others old. There are bones and rotting carcasses at the rear of the cavern. The most disgusting of the carcasses bear fresh teeth marks.
8122: This is a very large cavern with carved benches and other man made features. It becomes apparent from the filthy clothes and other signs that these caves are the home of the Goblins and were recently occupied. No wonder these caves smell as they do.
8123: This portion of the inner caves is very cold and damp. The absence of all wild animals and an abundance of deer, elk, and elf bones on the floor of the cavern gives an appearance of someone's or something's feasting room. The dark corners of the cave hide all signs of life that may lurk to the north or east. If possible, a short rest before going ahead would be most advisable.
8124: This small chamber has oddly smooth and regular walls. They make the same precise angle at every corner. In the centre of the floor, a windlass has been set up over a large black hole. A rope disappears into the hole.
8125:
A goblin warrior is threatening to start a fight here.
A goblin warrior is threatening to start a fight here.

The inner caves are dark, cold and clammy, not at all comfortable for those who are used to living in valleys and mountains. But in this locale, this may be the best available dwelling. Shelter from curious eyes as well as the opportunity to light a fire without having to deal with fierce winds are definitely a plus. There are signs of local inhabitants, who have grown accustomed to living in damp caves.
8126: The tunnel here is much wider than those to the north. A boulder to the west has become a crude door that has been used from time to time to seal off the inner caverns. What is not obvious is if this door was meant to keep intruders out of the caverns or to keep something in the cavern.
8127: The tunnels go east to south here. The darkness prevents you from seeing too much of the tunnels. There might be hordes of goblins in them and yet you might not see them. You can't even see your own feet.
8128:
A nasty goblin is here walking around.
A nasty goblin is here walking around.

This seems to be the deepest part of the tunnel. There is a puddle of water in the middle of the room with a reddish tint. After examining the water it becomes clear that elves have recently been stewed here. Clearly this is not a place friendly to elves and their friends. No sound can be heard from the tunnels, so maybe the attackers are hiding in the darkness.
8129: A nasty goblin is here walking around.

The tunnels extend on and on. Though the wind can be felt, its origin can not be discerned. A strange whistling sound can be heard coming from above. At first, this sound could be mistaken as artificial, but after careful examination of the walls, it becomes obvious that the sound is merely the wind blowing through the little holes in the wall.
8130: The tunnel is very narrow. The sides are lined with jagged rocks that protrude from the side. Through a crack in the boulders, a valley can be seen to the south while the tunnel continues to the north. There is a powerful smell of goblin to the north.
8131:
A nasty goblin is here walking around.
A goblin warrior is threatening to start a fight here.
A goblin warrior is threatening to start a fight here.
A goblin warrior is threatening to start a fight here.
A goblin warrior is threatening to start a fight here.

This small and dusty chamber seems to be well used -- the floor is covered with the footprints of some type of humanoid. A small shelf in the north- ern wall about two metres above the ground gives access to a short tunnel that slopes steeply upward to a boulder that acts as a crude door. Another narrow tunnel leads down to the south, deeper in to the hidden recesses of the mountain.
8132:
A large bat is here, hanging in the darkness.
A large bat is here, hanging in the darkness.
A large bat is here, hanging in the darkness.
A small bat is standing here.
A small bat is standing here.

This is a sharply-slanted shaft whose floor is covered with loose scree. It does not appear to be a natural formation, but it certainly wasn't made as a passageway - at least not for feet such as yours. As you scramble down here you dislodge numerous rocks, which tumble below you with a series of small, soft echoes.
8133: This is a small tunnel, only five or six feet tall at the highest. You can see from the marks on the walls that it was hewn by picks from the hard grey stone surrounding you. The passageway is half filled with broken shards of rock, and the western end has completely collapsed. The passage slopes up to the east, where it also seems to expand.
8134: The passageway gets progressively larger as it ascends to the east, and here it is large enough for a group of three or four to walk abreast. The walls are rough and undecorated, but the floor is completely smooth and covered with a thin coat of a viscous, sulfurous slime.
8135: The large tunnel here slopes up to the east, where it gets taller and broader, and finally opens up into a spacious cavern. The floors and walls here are unadorned, but smooth and well-proportioned. They might once have been pleasant to walk upon, but are now covered with an acrid green slime which makes movement here a bit treacherous.
8136: A large domed chamber stretches off to the south. Cold rock is hard and savage, but here it has been crafted to a gentle, welcoming form. There are no edges here, no shadows; each facet of this place flows gently into another, drawing your eye slowly from floor to ceiling and wall to wall. A faint fresh breeze blows from the south.
8137: This elegant cavern adjoins a smaller chamber to the east. The arch of the entranceway is only half as tall as the dome above you, but their lines meet gently and form one graceful whole. The rock surrounding you has been carved and polished with such skill that even now it stands serenely unaffected by the passage of time. In daytime a diffuse light filters in through the opening to the east and through several shafts in the walls. The walls are unornamented, but the remnants of a mosaic around the edges of the floor can still be seen. A thin patina of slime makes the floor a bit slippery.
8138: The east end of this corridor merges seamlessly into a tall and well-proportioned cavern. As it extends to the west it descends noticeably, as well as slowly shrinking. This appears to have been an important passageway; unlike other corridors the walls here were once decorated, and dim remnants of frescoes are still visible. Ruined statues of Dwarven-lords line the walls, grim reminders of the transience of glory.
8139: Here the smooth floor of the cavern meets a wide road leading eastward. The way is wide and the arched ceiling rises high above, and large wagons or great companies of men could no doubt pass through unhindered. On the walls are carved broad scenes which, though weather-beaten, are clearly of a large host of Dwarves assembled in some company. On either side, near the walls, the floor once bore a mosaic; it has been all but destroyed by greedy fingers or lashing winds.
8141: The wind whistles through your hair, refreshing you after the time spent within the mountain. The cold air around you is invigorating, bracing, so fresh and clear you feel you could live here forever on it alone. Inexorable gravity, however, disagrees, and you plummet hundreds of feet down to the remnants of the road below, and to a particularly gruesome end.
8142: Slowly the corridor delves its way into the mountain. You begin to feel a slight increase in heat. The tunnel here is perfectly flat and smooth, and covered with a thin coat of mire, as if polished over decades by some hideous underground army.
8143: Deeper and deeper the passage makes its way, slowly bending here to the south. It gets hotter and hotter as you descend to the very root of the great mountain, and you seem to detect a faint red glow around the bend. The slime which covers much of these caverns continues here, if anything thickening as you go down. Wisps of fog flit across your face.
8144: Whatever it is that warms there caves must be quite close now; you can feel the heat radiating from the south. Light clouds of steam surround you, and an acrid reek assails your nostrils. Just south of here the tunnel opens into an enormous cavern, from which an ominous red glow can be seen.
8145: This shaft runs vertically for many feet; without the ladder running along its west side you would surely drop straight down to the bottom. As you descend it grows cooler, and a clammy dew settles on your skin. Finally the ladder ends, and with your feet you can feel no ledges or handholds further down. The only way to continue would be a blind leap of faith to the bottom of the shaft, however far down that may be.
8146: With no ladder on which to climb, you hurtle downwards through the dense dark air. The view remains unchanged as you fall, except for occasional corridors branching off from this shaft. As you gather speed the blood rushes to your head, your sight reddens and dims, and your consciousness slowly slips away. You will never know just where is it you finally land.
8147: You are at the entrance to an enormous cavern, carved deep into the living rock. This must once have been an important junction, as many passages open up along the walls. All are blocked now; the long toll of history has effortlessly undone what mortal hands struggled so hard to build. Or was the destruction purposeful? The cavern extends beyond the limits of your sight, but in a far off corner you can spy a faint red glow. The air is hotter in that direction.
8148: The western wall of this cavern slowly curves around to the east, where there is definitely a flickering hot red light. No sunshine from above could ever reach down here, through the curving corridors and cramped mineshafts, to the very roots of this great mountain. And yet, the eastern air, through veils of mist, glows red.
8149: Mithnaur the Dragon is sleeping here.
This seems to be the source of the heat, and the fog, and the muck which fouls these caves. Here, safe from daylight and stinging swords, far from meddling eyes, some great beast has made its lair.
8150: The northern wall of the cavern gently bends to the south. Various corridors branch off, but none progresses more than a few feet; all are collapsed, rubble-filled. The slime seems thicker here, and the stench more nauseating, than to the west. To the south, encased here with you, deep below the earth, you see a crimson glow, and hear a raspy, gurgling sound, like a teapot boiling on the stove. A huge boulder to the east seems to be blocking some kind of entrance.
8151: A vile stench lies over this room, where the dragon seems to have spent much of its time. The cave is smaller than the one to the west, but still large enough to hold the dragon.
8152: A mineshaft extends from the cavern like a small tentacle reaching outwards. From the cavern comes a fierce red heat and waves of steam. Near the entrance a ladder extends down into a pit. The mineshaft continues only a short while before your way is blocked by mounds of blasted rock.
8153: Slowly you climb upon a ladder leading into the inky deepness. You feel a dim heat radiate at you from above, and a dim fog drifts down around you, making your hands perilously slippery. Above you see a red glow; below you all is black.
8154: The passageway here gets progressively smaller as it descends to the west, and here it is large enough for a group of three or four to walk abreast. The walls are rough and undecorated, but the floor is completely smooth, and, because of the slime which covers it, rather slippery.
8155: The large tunnel here slopes down to the west, where it gets steadily smaller and rougher. The floors and walls here are unadorned, but smooth and well proportioned. They might once have been pleasant to walk through, but are now covered with an acrid green slime which has, in many places, hardened into dry flakes. To the north is a large opening into a spacious cavern.
8156: A pile of debris blocks the way, and you can go no further. Uncountable tons of stone surround you. You are deep within the mountain here, far from light and sky, far from the sun which Arien pulls endlessly above the distant heights of Middle-earth.
8157: Slowly rising, the tunnel follows the grain of the rock. The damp walls sparkle and glisten around you, reflecting the deep reds and burnt oranges which streak them. The air here is musty and stale, but cool and odourless, and not altogether unpleasant.
8158: This shaft is now several hundred feet below its top, and still it continues down. It is cooler here than it was above, and the rough-hewn walls surround you like a tomb. To the north a passage extends, slanting upwards. Some ways below the tunnel fills with water, and you can go no further down without submerging yourself.
8160:
A small leech is here, floating in the water.
A small leech is here, floating in the water.
A small leech is here, floating in the water.
A small leech is here, floating in the water.
You are in a small tube, perhaps ten feet high and 10 across, which is filled with water so icy cold that you have lost all bodily sensation. The water flows slowly to the west.
8161:
A small leech is here, floating in the water.
A small leech is here, floating in the water.
A small leech is here, floating in the water.
A small leech is here, floating in the water.
A small leech is here, floating in the water.
A small leech is here, floating in the water.

The tube steadily contracts as it goes west. Here it is no more than 6 feet high, and thin enough that you can touch both walls at the same time. It is still entirely filled with water, which is flowing ever faster to the west.
8162: The frigid water hurls you along to the west, propelling you through a narrow cleft barely big enough to hold you. You are dashed against the walls, and there is no hope of returning to the east. All you can do is hold your breath and hope against hope that you come out of this alive.
8163: The corridor which started out, far above and to the east, with giantish proportions, has shrunk here to a more Dwarven stature. It is quite rough now; though the floor is still comfortable to walk upon, the walls and ceilings are scarred as if by picks, and scattered rocks litter the floor. The slime which lines the floors to the east is absent here.
8165: This seems like the lowest point of the mountain ranges in the vicinity. For a change your lungs get a good supply of oxygen, making you feel lightheaded suddenly. You find that the only direction you can go from here is west.
8166: You see as you climb lower down the mountain that there is a small pass to your east. It does not seem like a well frequented one. Maybe going that way will get you to a road that does not go up dangerous mountain paths. There is what seems like the remnants of a campfire here. Maybe someone was here not so long back. You hope it is not one of the enemies.
8167: Going down the mountain, you feel a sense of gratitude towards the gods for having kept you from death's clammy grip. Here you see that you can take a variety of different routes. Your past experience in this land makes you wonder which way would be the safest. Also you hope that once you choose a path, you can retrace your steps easily in case of trouble.
8168: This narrow and rocky valley was once home to a mountain stream that has left an easily passable trail as its legacy. The valley floor is littered with debris from old rockslides -- one of which was probably responsible for the drying of the stream -- and the sides are too steep to be negotiated.
8169: Many years ago, a lively mountain stream flowed through here. Now all that remains is a narrow trail strewn with rocks. To the west, a narrow cleft cuts into the cliff face -- the stream obviously once issued from that direction. The sides of this narrow valley are far to steep to be scaled, so the only ways to proceed are to enter the cleft or turn back.
8170: The mountain path is nothing more than a mountain ledge here. The path continues to the south and to the west, being much wider there. It is very hard to move safely and impossible to ride a mount of any kind. Some strange tracks can be found going southwards. The path continues ahead leading to what seems like the abode of some unknown creatures.
8171: You can see a grand view from this summit; your eyes wander far to the west, over the foothills and the forests below; perhaps that is the Mitheithel on the horizon. There is no obvious path downwards, but it is possible to negotiate a ridge that leads toward the south.
8172: This is the southern most tip of the mountain top. From here you can climb down the mountain pretty easily. This side of the mountain seems much safer than the others. Farther south you see the range continuing as far as your eyes can see. The fog that envelopes the top seems to be pretty thin, though from far you thought it was dense.
8173:
A small, helpless eaglet screams for more food.
A small, helpless eaglet screams for more food.

This wide shelf houses an eyrie. The nest itself is foul, covered with filth and rotting meat, indicating that these eagles are not kin to the noble line of Thorondor. Perhaps when Morgoth held sway over Middle-earth while the Valar dwelt in Valinor, he bred such corrupt birds in mockery of the eagles of Manwe that dwell upon high Taniquetil.
8174: This path does not look too safe. Having the heart of a lion is not all that it takes to survive these parts. Especially since your mounts do not seem very happy with the rocky and treacherous route. Up ahead the path becomes even more dangerous and you pause and wonder if it is worth the risk.
8175: This narrow space cuts between two sheer rock faces that are separated by a mere ten metres. No vegetation grows here -- the ground is very rocky and strewn with boulders. To the east, the cliffs give way to an open space, while the cleft continues to the north, getting narrower with each step in that direction.
8176: The narrow cleft in the mountainside at last comes to an end. In every dir- ection save south rise steep rock faces -- seemingly impossible to scale. The ground here is shaded except during the middle of the day, and there are several large boulders lying strewn about, in fact, some of them appear to have been deliberately piled in front of a shallow recess in the rock.
8177: You seem to be at a bend in the path. You can't see more than a few dozen feet ahead of you. So you feel that there might be lots of hidden eyes staring at you from hidden places. The sooner you cross the mountains, the better. You keep whispering to yourself "Keep alert! Don't sleep!", over and over. The path to the north seems to lead to some shelter far away.
8178: On and on you go further into the mountains. You feel that these mountains are enchanted. You hope that the enchantment is good magic and not the filthy magic of the Enemy. This path seems to be not that well used and hence you feel it will be safe from the Lidless Eye's minions.
8179: You are on a path that is fairly wide here. East of here the path becomes very narrow and dangerous. Care should be taken while crossing it. To the west you can leave the path and get onto the mountain, but north seems to be the most interesting. From here, the mountain tops seem to be covered with fog, and the whole place looks very gloomy and sad.
8180: Directly to the east of here is a gravel-covered slope leading steeply down to the floor of a shallow canyon. The small trail comes to an end here, so the only alternative to returning to the south is to attempt the slope. Getting down should not be a problem, but it may be impossible to return up here.
8181: To the north a large and rocky ridge blocks the way, but the canyon wall to the south looks relatively easy to scale. To the west, the mouth of the canyon meets with the river, and presumably the trail as well. To the east the canyon widens and becomes shallower.
8182: The sheer rock face of a granite ridge forms the inpregnable northern wall of this canyon. To the south, the ground slopes gently upward for a while until the steep southern wall is reached. The ridge to the north appears to end a bit to the west, and the canyon also gets much shallower in that direction.
8183: Here you can enter the trail running east-west if you go north. To the west the canyon becomes very narrow. You feel as if there is danger to the south of you. You feel you really ought to investigate the region to the south though it would mean climbing a few rocks and boulders and even small hills.
8184: Having come south of the trail and the adjoining canyon, you see that the ground rises here in a gentle slope, and abruptly becomes a very high rocky wall preventing you from going south. You can go east though where the landscape is similar to around here.
8185: A demon wolf lurks here, its dark form twisting and hiding its shape.

This gentle slope ends abruptly to the south in a granite cliff. To the east it may be possible to scramble up the cliff as it is not as steep in that direction. To the north is the floor of a canyon carved many years ago by a river that has long since abandoned this channel. To the west the terrain looks very similar, though only for a short distance as another steep slope can be seen.
8186: You are at the northern edge of a wide canyon. You see that the canyon becomes narrower if you go north and west. To your south there are a few hills and boulders. In the distance you see a daunting mountain. Suddenly you feel that maybe it will not be as good an idea as you thought at first.
8187: This trail takes advantage of a narrow flat area between two towering peaks to the east and west. To the north, the trail rises higher while it leads to lower elevations to the south. The hard and rocky soil bears a few foot- prints -- someone has been here not long ago.
8188: Here again the steep slope continues. There seem to be a lot of nooks and perches in these slopes where an ambush party could be waiting to pounce on you when you least expect it. You also seem to hear the sounds of eagles nearby, though you don't see their homes. There does not seem to be a lot of places to go from here except west.
8189: This narrow ledge gives a brief respite to those attempting to climb the steep scree-covered slope. Below, the slope is too steep to descend, as the slightest misstep would send an unfortunate adventurer tumbling down to the canyon floor below. It is possible to manoeuvre east and west along the ledge, and one can probably climb up as well.
8190: The steep mountain side continues here from the east. There is not much of a hope of any way out of here but to continue the climb. The climb seems to get more and more dangerous as you take each step. You regret your decision to climb these slopes. You hope some of the great eagles of this region will take pity on you and take you to safety but they are nowhere to be seen now.
8191: Here the sounds of the great eagles sounds nearer. Maybe there is an eyrie nearby. You wonder if the evil of Sauron has touched their souls yet. The only hope for your mission to succeed is that they are still enemies of the one Enemy and will aid you. Without their help, the path through these mountains might be too difficult for you to overcome. If you do not find them, you will have to continue your trudge upwards and hope your shoes do not fail you.
8192: You find that at such heights, the air is very rare and your breathing has grown deeper. Stories of people dying of lack of air come to mind. You shudder. Hey what was that? An eagle. ... No, it is just an illusion of your frightened mind. Steep slopes all around, and lots of hidden nooks. Enough to drive your crazed mind out through the doors into the land of paranoia. Maybe you can rest nearby for a while.
8193: Aaaaaaahhhh. At last a place to rest your tired bones away from the eyes of danger. This seems like the ideal place to rest and recuperate from the arduous climb... or is it?! Your paranoia catches hold of you for a second but you decide to take a chance. Looking around you see that you can watch the whole of the road beneath you. This seems like the ideal spot to waylay travellers and loot them of their money and such.
8194: Directly overhead, a massive slab of granite forms a natural bridge over this rushing water, connecting the cliffs on either side of the river. The bridge is at least fifteen metres above the water, but it may be accessible due to a small ledge on the western cliff.
8195: The water here is shallow, but still swift enough to be dangerous, and its icy touch numbs the flesh almost instantly. The source of this stream must not be too much farther upstream -- the water is crystal clear. There is a trail running along the northern bank of the river, but it is impossible to reach due to the jagged rocks and swift currents.
8196: Here the river widens slightly, slowing down the strong flow of water. Sheer walls of stone block any attempt to get out of the river, forcing you to choose to follow the water west, or to try and follow it east. Perhaps you will soon be able to leave the water, and continue your journey...
8197: With a persistence beyond the powers of Morgoth, the water continues its journey westwards. The flume through which the water flows here is cut deep into the mountains, cutting off passage to the south. However, you can climb north on to a worn path running through the mountains. To the east, you can follow the river upstream up to a waterfall farther along.
8198: The river here is thin and shallow. Although very cold, the water appears very muddy. Almost red in hue, it flows towards the west. To the east, you see a waterfall. South of here, you see nothing but mountains. Perhaps, the trail north of here leads someplace interesting...
8199: The trail forks here, with one branch heading east and following the river to the south, while the other heads north deeper into the mountains. To the west, the trail crosses the river gorge via a natural bridge, formed by a single huge block of granite that, when shrugged off the side of the mountain, somehow landed to form a bridge.
8200: The river flows just to the south, about 10 metres below the level of this trail. Either the trail slopes down to the east, or the riverbed slopes up- ward, for the two seem to be much closer together to the east. West of this point there is a fork in the trail.
8201: A daunting cliff looms ominously to the north, dwarfing the small trail that winds along between its foot and the river to the south. The trail is wet with spray from the turbulent river, and often the footing is treacherous. To the east, the trail gets much closer to the river's edge -- perhaps it would be possible to enter the water there.
8202: To the east, the stream becomes more narrow as its source nears. The trail follows the northern bank, nestled between the icy water and a bleak cliff to the north. The cold peaks of the Misty Mountains rear up to the east - a seemingly impassable obstacle.
8203: This trail seems to go forever, with no end in sight. With the exception of the river flowing south of you, all you see is stone. Mountains and mountains of stone... Perhaps some ancient secret can be found in those mountains, but unless you have some means to cross the river, you'll have to travel farther until you find a break from the high walls of stone preventing you from leaving this trail.
8204:
A large pile of boulders is sitting here, probably debris from a rockslide.
An ibex is watching you from afar.

More and more in your journey, you begin to wish you never left home. Although a rock face might change, or a river might flow, the scenery is as bleak as could be. On this section of the path, you are fortunate enough to have the dreariness broken by the sound of a river to the south. Also, you hear a loud splashing noise to the southeast. Perhaps some vile creature of these mountains is playing in the water?
8205: Except for the loud roaring of the waterfall south of here, the mountains seem quiet and lifeless. Even the trail you're standing on seems devoid of life. Only the hardiest creatures could survive in this land for long, and you sense that you would prefer not to have the misfortune of meeting any of them. East and west, this trail continues, seeming to go deeper into the mountains in both directions.
8206:
A very strong orkish leader is here on patrol.
An orc soldier is standing here.
An orc soldier is standing here.
An orc soldier is standing here.
An orc soldier is standing here.

Passing through the lower mountains to the west, the trail follows the side of the mountain, just east of here, directly to the top. Glancing south, you notice what is perhaps a mirage of sorts. How could a pool form in these harsh mountains? Nevertheless, you are drawn to it, even if just to quench your thirst, and fill your skins. After all, this might be the last chance in these harsh, lifeless mountains.
8207: This narrow ledge is slick with spray spewn by the river as it rushes over the rocky streambed. Directly above is a large block of granite that has been sloughed off by the mountain -- it forms a natural bridge crossing the shallow gorge through which the river runs. The trail that has been following the river seems to cross here as well, so it has obviously been here for a long time.
8208: The High Pass turns south here, dipping down into the valley. To the north, you see a small, windy trail breaking off. The ground looks like it flattens out some to the north, but you can make out several peaks in the distance. There is a sign here, carved into one of the larger boulders.
8209: You continue to walk along the well-defined pass. Known by some as the High Pass, it is one of the primary trails for crossing these mountains. Though easy to walk along here, the land right off the path is quite dangerous. You realise you have to face the dangers of not just the terrain but whatever fell creatures reside here.
8210: Water falling from above splashes you, cleaning some of the dirt caked on your body. Dripping from your clothes, the water (and dirt) flows west, down through the mountains. A smile comes to your face when you consider just how far your dirt will travel before coming to rest at the bottom of the sea.
8211: A clear spring babbles as cool water trickles out of the ground.

So different from the rest of the scenery here, a large pool of water stands in the middle of this landing. It seems to be fed from underground, perhaps from somewhere beyond the sheer face of rock to the east... The water drains directly down in a thin, but quickly flowing, waterfall. The falling water flows west to form a thin river through the mountains. There appears to be a trail of sorts directly north of here, and to the east you spy a small camp.
8212: The river to the north must have dug this alcove in the side of the mountains. The only exit appears to be back to the river that you came from. However, this alcove does seem to offer protection from the creatures of the mountains. Perhaps this would be a good place to rest for a while.
8213: As you walk through the valley, you trip on a pile of rocks on the rocky ground. Looking around, you can see that this debris must have fallen from the mountain tops east of you. A rock slide must have occurred recently. Hopefully, this valley will be spared another while you are here. The valley begins to slope upwards south of here, while going down towards the north where you think you hear the sounds of splashing water.
8214:
A large marmot is here, scurrying in between the rocks.
A large marmot is here, scurrying in between the rocks.

You find yourself inside a U-shaped valley in the mountains. North of here, a thin river flows westwards, but there is no way to pass it without a boat of some sort. South, the valley tends to gain altitude. If you are unable to pass the river, perhaps your destiny lies to the south.
8215: The climb up the side of the mountain to the peak was more difficult than you thought at first. Luckily, you made it safely to the top. The humidity of the air here is quite high, and your vision is blurred in the mist. Looking back down the direction you came, the mountainside is littered with rubble.
8216: A mountain ibex is jumping from rock to rock.

Rising high from the ground below, the mountains tower over the land. Higher still, the peaks of the mountains look down upon the terrain with a view of all that can be seen.
