Unfortunately, there isn't much. Just north, you can see a large pool of water that falls into a river. East of that pool, a single peak rises high above the rest. In all other directions, you see nothing but the cold stone of the Misty Mountains.
8217: A mountain ibex is jumping from rock to rock.

Continuing up the slope, you find yourself near two mountain peaks rising above you. The southern one is inaccessible, but the one to the east is a fairly easy climb. Your mind ponders for a moment what might lie on the other side of that peak. Of course, there is only one way to find out.
8218: High on the top of this mountain, the lack of air causes you to become dizzy. You quickly lose your sense of direction for a brief moment, before becoming accustomed to the thinness of air. You shudder when you look south, as several of the peaks there are even higher. Perhaps you'll be able to avoid them in your journey...
8219: A slobbering giant greedily lumbers towards you.

As you look around at the vast reaches of grey mountains which surround you on all sides, and contemplate the sameness of it all, you can't help but wonder if you haven't been in this very spot already.
8220: High on the top of this mountain, the lack of air causes you to become dizzy. You quickly lose your sense of direction for a brief moment, before becoming accustomed to the thinness of air. You shudder when you look south, as several of the peaks there are even higher. Perhaps you'll be able to avoid them in your journey...
8221: As you look around at the vast reaches of grey mountains which surround you on all sides and contemplate the sameness of it all, you can't help but wonder if you haven't been in this very spot already.
8222: You wonder what force could have dug this alcove in the side of the mountains. The only exit appears to be back to the east where you came from. Leaving might be a good idea, as you are easy prey for anything that happens to wander in here, and it seems it would be too easy to trap you in here.
8223: This peak looks much the same as all the others you've climbed. The view is also much the same. The only thing really of any interest is the peak to the southwest. Higher than most of the others around here, it stands almost as a proud warrior of stone. Unfortunately, it appears that the slopes of it are much too steep to climb.
8224: Here there is a small hollow in the mountains, affording some protection from the snow and the constant, biting winds. The mountain walls around you are grey and ragged, and various rocks and protuberances look as if they could come crashing down at any time. Indeed, the ground around you contains the jagged remnants of many boulders which have done just that.
8225:
A mountain ibex is jumping from rock to rock.
An ibex is watching you from afar.

More and more, you dwell on the horror stories of large stone giants that wander deep in these mountains. The mountain peaks continue north and east of here. From your location low in the mountains, not much is visible here except for the endless ranges of stone and rock. With the trail lost, you might never find your way out of the mountains.
8227: As you pass by the never ending slopes and peaks of the mountains, you begin to lose hope of ever finding your way back to the trail you lost. While the mountains continue in their uninteresting fashion in all directions, you find that you are only able to climb up to a close mountain peak, or north, to more of the same mountainous terrain.
8228: A mountain ibex is jumping from rock to rock.

Ahead of you, a towering mountain rises steadily forward. Its peak, shrouded in wispy plumes of fog and mist readily fit into the monotonous scene, yet a single spur races towards you from which a thin curl of steam can most evidently be seen, causing your eye to pay attention to this behemoth mountain.
8229: Like the tail of a huge scorpion ready to strike, the towering mountain looms ahead. Its spur, reaches towards you guarding the higher mountain behind it. Up ahead, the ground increases in pitch, making you bite into the ground firmly.
8230: The ground pitches violently upwards here, as the mountain's spur, like a thick muscular root, digs into the rocky ground and shoots upwards. The thin plume of steam can be seen coming from directly ahead, no doubt the only warmth in an otherwise cold and lifeless climate.
8231: Even standing high on this peak of the mountains, you find yourself dwarfed compared to the yet higher mountain top just north of you. Utter confusion fills you when you look down. For some reason, the slope of the mountain looks different. More and more, you feel completely lost in these mountains.
8232: Even standing high on this peak of the mountains, you find yourself dwarfed compared to the yet higher mountain top just north of you. Utter confusion fills you when you look down. For some reason, the slope of the mountain looks different. More and more, you feel completely lost in these mountains.
8233: High on this mountain top, you find that the air is very thin. So thin, that you are unable to speak. Perhaps if the weather was ever good in this region, you would have a wonderous view of the surrounding mountains. As it is, however, all you can see are clouds, and more clouds.
8234: Both north and west of you, the mountains come to peaks. You can also see a wall of peaks going from the southwest to the northeast. Although you can climb up the western peak, the one to the north offers nothing but a vertical wall to its top. Perhaps it can be accessed from another side. A small cave-like alcove is south of you.
8235: You find yourself on a slope that rises higher into the mountains, coming to a peak above you. The slope flows south, falling into a lower part of the mountains. Sharp overhangs from the north and east taunt you. Passage in those directions is impossible.
8236:
There is a water skin lying on the ground.
A large torch lies here among the dust.
A large piece of fresh, raw meat lies here.
A brown fur is here lying on the ground.

Taking advantage of the sloping lands, a small camp has been erected here. Using the rising cusps as walls, the roof has been made of thatched branches and pelts. Inside, a small fireplace stands cold, a few bits of broken bones stand testament for its use. Off to one corner, a lantern glows dimly, giving enough light to illuminate the surroundings.
8237: Winding along the side of the mountains, the trail can be followed to a peak just north of here. As well, there is a very high, snowcapped peak towering above you. You notice signs of the trail also going south and east of here. Unfortunately, the blandness of the Misty Mountains hides from your eyes the true path.
8238: You are standing atop one of the lower peaks of the Misty Mountains. At this height, you can better see much of your surroundings. To the west, a trail seems to be following alongside a river. Another part of that trail seems to go southeast of here. Due east, more of the strong mountains of this region rise out of the ground. To the southwest, there is another peak higher than this one.
8239: Winding along the side of the mountain, the trail can be followed to the peak just east of here. However, to the west you can see a trail that flows next to a river far below. Although near a peak to the east, south of you is a sheer wall towards yet another, higher peak of the Misty Mountains.
8240: If you've become tired of wandering aimlessly through the mountains, perhaps you are in luck. East of here you notice a trail made in this treacherous quarry called the Misty Mountains. Of course, if exploration is on your mind, follow the slope down to the south. Perhaps you can find some lost treasure deep within the mountains.
8241: You find yourself wandering in a deep valley. All around you, the hard, grey stone walls of the mountains look down upon you. Both to your east and west you see the high peaks of mountains. Above you, you notice a shelf that you can reach. North and west, the valley slopes upwards, rising towards the high mountain tops.
8242: Fear strikes you as you recall horror stories of large stone giants that wander deep in these mountains. Sloping upwards from the east, the mountains continue north and west of here. From your location low in the mountains, not much is visible here except for the endless ranges of stone and rock. With the trail lost, you might never find your way out of the mountains.
8243: You wonder what force could have dug this alcove in the side of the mountains. The only exit appears to be back to the north where you came from. However, this alcove does seem to offer protection from the creatures of the mountains. Perhaps this would be a good place to rest for a while.
8244: The trail is stronger here, giving you a sense of confidence. A slope to the south appears to lead up to a mountain peak. However, your trail travels from the north, continuing east. The eastward path, which flanks the steep, bare, dangerous-looking flank of a mountain, goes up towards another peak in the Misty Mountains.
8245: With the path sloping upwards, you are able to reach another peak of the mountains to the east. To the north, you see a strong trail leading through the mountains. All other directions are blocked by high walls of stone which slant over you slightly, threatening to fall and crush you.
8246:
A very strong orkish leader is here on patrol.
An orc soldier is standing here.
An orc soldier is standing here.
An orc soldier is standing here.
An orc soldier is standing here.

From your perch on the top of this mountain, you can see that all but one side is very steep. To the south, you can see that the same holds true for most of the peaks in that direction. Far in the west, another row of mountain tops rises in the air. As there is nothing of interest here, you decide that you should go back the way you came, and continue your journey.
8247: As you climb down, you lose your footing and fall. Although you land comfortably, you find that you have no way of getting back up. Rising before you, a mountain peak stands high in the clouds. Climbing shouldn't be too difficult, and you quickly decide that standing here might not be very safe. Perhaps you can find a way down the other side of the mountain top.
8248: After a tough climb, you finally manage to reach the peak of this mountain. All around you, ageless snow rests. There is some fresh snow sifted on the very top of the snow cap. From this height, you can see that a long chain of mountains are strung from the north to south. Looking back down, you realize that your climb up must have dislodged some of the mountainside, as returning below is now impossible.
8249: As you follow the trail, the passage to the west is suddenly filled with large boulders! Luckily, you dodge the falling rocks. Unfortunately, passage that way is now hopelessly blocked. However, the trail appears to continue high up to a snow capped peak. Although it's a steep climb, you should be able to manage it without too much problem.
8250: As with the slope leading up here, the wind is stronger then you'd like. However, from this height, the threat of falling is much greater. You decide you should make haste and leave from this mountain top as soon as you can. Before you leave, however, you notice that the peak just south of you rises higher than most of the mountains in this area. Curiosity drives you to explore it further.
8251: The wind in this region of the mountains is much stronger than elsewhere. Whipping about you, it desperately tries to knock you off balance. Just south of you, you see a trail that travels through the mountains. Perhaps it leads to refuge of some sort. As well, you can climb to a mountain peak from here.
8252: A stocky mountain mule is here, waiting to serve.

You carefully pick your way between the rocks, knowing that one small slip could mean death. Looking up you can see the majestic peak of this mountain with the line of peaks snaking away to the south east like a worm glistening in the sun.
8253: You find that the trail runs through a valley at this point. You are able to make your way along the trail north and south. As well, you can follow a slope up towards the west. A large pile of rocks and boulders block any chance of passing to east.
8254: Here, the trail becomes faint and appears to continue in several directions. You can follow it up towards a mountain top, or east and south deeper into the mountains. If only you had a map of the region, things might be easier. Unfortunately, not even a map would help much, as by some evil magic, the true path seems to change occasionally. Or perhaps that's just a false rumour spread by those creatures who would rather have you as a dinner guest...
8255: A rather smooth trail begins here and heads off towards a ridge in the east. As well, you can follow a smaller path up to the peak of a mountain. Southeast of here, an extremely tall mountain rises high into the clouds. Perhaps if you could find your way to that peak, you could see the region better, and find your way out of here.
8256: From this peak, you have a clear view of a much higher peak rising to the south. The way to it, however, seems to be complicated. A trail continues east from here, as well as going down from the peak, and west. In the distance, you see a chain of more peaks in the west. To the north, the long chains all seem to come together.
8257: You are walking on a trail leading up the side of a mountain. A vast range of mountains spreads out to the west and south, with a magnificent line of peaks weaving down towards the south-east. To the east the path you are on leads straight as an arrow towards a tall pillar of rock, and to the north lies a dense forest, but no obvious way of getting there.
8258: A large sheet of rock from the south overhangs this area. As you stare at this overhang, your mind drifts into thoughts of its creation at the hands of the ancients. A picture comes into your mind of the massive upheaval Arda suffered when Morgoth was finally cast out. Even today, many ages later, signs of that battle remain throughout the lands.
8259: The thick dust of the mountains makes your way difficult. Both to your north and south, the way is impassable. However, it appears that you can climb to yet another peak of these mountains from here. Perhaps from there you can find your destination, and a way to get there...
8260: A long chain of mountain peaks are strung along the north and south. However, because of the gaps between them, none are accessible from here. From your perch, you notice two mountains with snow-capped peaks. One is south of here, while the other is somewhat east.
8264: You are standing at the bottom of a huge mountain. Far above you, some small, dark dots can be seen next to the white peak of the mountain. Probably birds flying high in the sky. North of you, the trail is leading west-east, through the snowy and cold Misty Mountains. It is probably possible to try to climb all the way up, though it seems to be harder the further you get, as the slope gets steeper.
8265:
There is some snow on the ground.
A mountain goat is here, jumping from cliff to cliff.

You are still on the trail, wondering where it will take you. You know that many of these trails far into the Mountains have bad ends. Still, you feel that you are on the track of the right way through these mountains. Walk on!
8266:
There is some snow on the ground.
A mountain goat is here, jumping from cliff to cliff.
A very strong orkish leader is here on patrol.
An orc soldier is standing here.
An orc soldier is standing here.
An orc soldier is standing here.
An orc soldier is standing here.

This may well be the High Pass, the most important trade route across this part of the Mountains. Few travel across now, however. Orcs lurk in this area, making all journeys very dangerous. Sometimes, you spot orkish corpses and other signs of combat.
8267: There is some snow on the ground.

The trail makes a few bends. You expect it to end behind every corner, but it goes on every time. You wonder if you soon reach the opposite side of these mountains. You have been walking quite some time now, but still you only see tall mountain-peaks in every direction.
8268: This trail takes a sharp turn to the south to avoid a high ridge, and then continues its steady climb toward a high pass to the west. Eastward, it continues its tortuous path - winding among the peaks and valleys of the Misty Mountains.
8269: The narrow trail makes a sharp bend from west to north here. To the west, it climbs steadily toward a high pass. The trail is in bad shape - frequently it is almost blocked by fallen rocks and small landslides. The high peaks that surround the area gleam with pristine white snow.
8270: You walk on a trail, well, whether it is a 'trail' or just a heap of stones is surely a matter suited for discussion. Anyway, you make a stop here. To the southeast, the trail is flooded. A stream flows rapidly downwards, and it will soon take that part of the trail down to the bottom of the valley north of you.
8271: A lone hawk soars high above you.

Well, you guess this can be called a trail. You have seen better ones, but it is obvious that someone has been here before you. The trail goes east-west. The mountain tops are far above you. The wind at the tops is strong: You see clouds of snow being formed up there.
8272: The trail runs north-south here, and the ground on both sides is relatively flat in comparison to the rest of the area. Further to the north, you can see the mountains rising up, and you can sometimes catch a glimpse of a rather large bird in the distance.
8273: Standing on top of one of the highest peaks in this range, you are overwhelmed by the power of the sight that greets you. In the north you catch a glimpse of a path leading east to west, and beyond that a dense forest. To the south east this line of peaks leads your eyes in a dazzling sinuous dance.
8274: The ground underfoot is somewhat rocky, but much easier going than travelling through the mountains. Obviously it was built by someone or something walking this way many times, for it is both relatively worn and wide. To the east the path seems to lead towards a pillar of rock, while several miles to the west the path starts to lead up the side of a mountain.
8275: Standing in the middle of this rocky trail, the magnificence of the surrounding mountains is obvious for anyone who would care to look. The wandering line of mountain-tops leads your eyes in a mesmerising dance, light glistening off the caps like sun on wet skin. The trail you are on leads west and east.
8276: Leading east and west, this trail seems to meet another at some short distance in the east. In the east there appears to be a large pillar of black stone, standing out in sharp contrast to the whiteness of the snow-clad mountains behind.
8277: Directly in the east the path you are on intersects another leading north and south. In the east stands a tall pillar of stone, contrasting with the snow- clad mountain tops behind it. The shape of the pillar is not obvious from this far away, but it definitely seems to have been carved, either by hand or by the weather. To the west the path leads up a mountain in the distance.
8278: This is the intersection of the well travelled path leading east-west, and an older but less used path leading north-south. The mountainside slopes steeply downwards in the north, and rises slightly to the south. In the east stands a black pillar which has obviously been shaped by something, but its precise form cannot be told from this distance.
8279: In the east the path seems to make a bend to the south, veering around a large, imposing pillar of black rock. In the south the cloud-wreathed tops of the mountains rear high, while in the west the path leads up the side of a steep mountain.
8280: The trail bends south and west here, around a large pillar of black rock standing at the side of the road. To the south the trail seems to make a sharp bend, and in the west the trail continues, rising up the side of a far off mountain. The pillar of rock here appears to have been crudely carved in the shape of a humanoid, wearing some sort of crown, but the ravages of the weather make further detail impossible to see.
8282: You can travel along this rocky path to the east and west, or you can rejoin the main road in the north. Underfoot you hear the crunch of fine rocks and gravel, and this path certainly looks like it has been built by someone or something. Further evidence of habitation is given by the smoke curling lazily from the chimney of the small hut to the south.
8283: The corpse of a black sorcerer is lying here.

The path leads north, south and east here. In the west the sheer size of the mountains rising above you makes you feel very inadequate, but the sight of the homely hut in the east cheers you up, with the small wisp of smoke curling from the chimney.
8285: The trail bends north and west here, around a small outcrop of rock. To the west, a mountain peak looms high above your head, but you can see no way of climbing up. In the east the mountains dip down to a valley before rising again to form some sightly less formidable hills.
8286: This rough trail leads south along a narrow ledge on the side of a mountain. The way both up and down is too steep for you to attempt to climb, so you must either follow this trail south, or go north onto the path leading east and west.
8287: The valley bottom is covered in rocks and debris which have broken from the mountain and come tumbling down to end up here. The valley bends here to the north and east, or you can climb the mountain to the west.
8288:
A very strong orkish leader is here on patrol.
An orc soldier is standing here.
An orc soldier is standing here.
An orc soldier is standing here.
An orc soldier is standing here.

Rocks from above lie strewn all over the floor, some large rocks, some small. Most look like they have been lying here for many years, ravaged by wind and rain. The valley bends west and south; to the east a smaller valley climbs up towards a narrow gap in the Hithaeglir.
8289: The trail you are following leads east and west here. Westwards you can see mountains rising to high peaks, while to the east you can see the wide valley of the Anduin. In the far north you spot an area of darkness which may herald a forest of some sort, but you can't be sure from this distance. Still in the north but rather closer you see a path winding its way east to west.
8290: Here is the lowest part of a slippery and steep path through the mountain. It is only possible to travel north. Some lichens grows here but else this place is deserted of any form of permanent life.
8291: Rocks and stones crunch happily under your feet as you travel along this path. In the west the Misty Mountains reach up to touch the clouds, while closer you can see a small wooden hut situated just south of here. You can go east and west along this trail.
8292: The trail leads east and west. In the west there stands an imposing black pillar of rock, that seems to have some sort of discernible shape, but it is too far away for its exact shape to be seen. To the east the path carries on further into the foothills, in the west the path bends to the north.
8293: The path is rocky, but not so rocky as to make it hard to walk. In the south you can hear the gurgling of water from a spring, in the east you see a small wooden hut, and to the west you see the large range of Misty Mountains rising far above your head.
8294: The trail leads east and west here, and in the west there stands a large pillar of black stone, silhouetted against the white background of the snow-capped misty mountains. North of you rises an impenetrable wall of rock, while in the south the mountains fall away into a valley before rising again to form a magnificent line of peaks.
8295: A black wolf pads restlessly, looking for its next prey.

To the north you can see a narrow valley between two high mountain peaks. The trail continues to the west, to the High Pass, and to the east, down the mountain slope. You notice a trampled path leading north into the small valley. Examining it closer, you understand that it is well-used.
8296: A black wolf pads restlessly, looking for its next prey.
The road takes you over a ridge. Occasional tufts of grass are spread along the road. There is no other vegetation in this very hostile environment.
8297: The path ends in the south at the entrance to that neat little hut which you have been admiring for so long. You can also follow the path to the west, where it rejoins the main road. Looking west you again stare in wonder at the great magnificence of those towering mountains.
8298:
A black wolf pads restlessly, looking for its next prey.
An experienced orkish scout is looking for tracks on the ground.
What used to be a road leading up the steep slope is almost completely gone. The remainders of it are sprinkled with fallen rocks, making movement very cumbersome.
8299: The terrain to the east is far too rough to travel, and you can only proceed by going up the mountain side, or further into the mountains to the west. To the north, a high mountain rises, and looking south you see another of the high peaks of the Hithaeglir.
8300: Entering through the mouth of the valley to the east, the road climbs steadily up the southern mountain slope, faithfully following all the bends of the mountainside.
8301: The road is quite intact here, making travel a lot easier. It runs along the southern side of the mountain, allowing you to climb the pass to the west or to leave the mountains and head to the Anduin vale somewhere east of here. The mountainside to the north looks very smooth.
8302: You are on a stony path winding downwards with a rocky wall to the north. To the south the ground slopes away and there is a dell below the level of the path overhung with bushes and low trees.
8303: You have now reached the bottom of the valley. To the north, a rather high cliff towers above you. From the south, you hear the splashing of water, and looking there, you see the source of a small stream, flowing slowly along the road to the east. To the west a narrow trail leads up to an even narrower gap in the Misty Mountains.
8304: The trail bends sharply here, rising higher to the west. East and south there is a small cliff, below which can be seen a rapidly moving mountain stream. Northward, the path continues its journey among the eastern foothills of the Misty Mountains.
8305: The road has now left the high mountains to the west and allows you to travel much more easily. To the east you see a road intersection in the middle of the wilderness. On the north side of the road pleasant green slopes invite you to come and visit.
8306:
A half broken rusted key has been left here.
A small metal key has been dropped here.
A clear spring babbles as cool water trickles out of the ground.
A sturdy trained horse is standing here.

The water bubbles merrily from a crack in the rocks and flows into a little pond. There must be an underground outlet for the water, because the pool never seems to get any fuller, yet the water doesn't leave here in any observable manner. This looks like a good place to rest your weary bones, or maybe the hut you can see in the east would be more comfortable?
8307: The valley continues north and south here. Picking your way carefully through shattered rocks, you wonder if you will ever find a way out of here.. when suddenly you spot a trail leading up the side of the mountain to the west. All around you can look up and see the magnificent snow-capped peaks towering high above you.
8308: A rock wall towers up on the east, casting its long shadow over the valley floor. In the west you can start to climb up the side of one of the tallest peaks in this range, or you can follow this barren valley either north or south.
8309: The valley ends here, dropping so sharply to the south that it would be folly to even try going down it. You can climb the mountains to the west, where you see the highest peak you have ever beheld rising far above your head, or you can follow the valley northwards. To the east a tall cliff blocks your way.
8310: Travel further south is curtailed by a large outcrop of rocks, which is almost impossible to pass. You can however descend into a valley to the east, or climb back up the mountain in the west.
8311: Standing on the loose rocks you wonder if this was a wise move, but the ground underfoot seems to be solid enough for the moment. You can traverse the side of the mountain to the north or south, descend to a valley in the east, or climb up to a ridge on the top of the mountain in the west.
8312: A small flower grows here, with a purple bloom and wide leaves.

The rocks on this side of the mountain are loose, but not loose enough to make you lose your balance and fall. You can descend further into the valley bottom, traverse the mountainside to the south, or climb back up to the ridge in the north or west.
8313: The rock underfoot is unstable, but you manage to keep your balance. The valley in the east seems to roughly follow the line of peaks to the south-east, or you can descend into the valley and then back up the side of another mountain.
8314: Small breaks in the snow here allow you to descend the side of the mountain if you wish, or you can continue along this ridge which leads to the south east. It is difficult to see clearly, but you think there is a traversable valley in the east.
8315: The mountain drops down to a valley in the east, or you can travel along this ridge to the south and west. On one of the highest peaks in this range, you can see for miles around, even spotting a dark forest many miles to the north.
8316: The mountains extend in a long sinuous chain to the north-west and south-east. Far to the north you spot a dark line which could only be a path leading east and west. Closer, you can see a valley in the east following this ridge of peaks which you are travelling on.
8317: A small trail leads up the mountain to the east allowing to climb back up to the ridge, or you can stay sheltered and travel west or south along the sides of this large mountain, being careful not to stand on any loose scree which may cause you to fall to your death hundreds of feet below.
8318: You can travel east or north, but you can see no way of climbing back up to the top of the mountain from here. Rising majestically above you to both the north and south, the snow covered peaks make you feel very small and insignificant in comparison.
8319: You can travel east or north, but you can see no way of climbing back up to the top of the mountain from here. Rising majestically above you to both the north and south, the snow covered peaks make you feel very small and insignificant in comparison.
8320: You can either climb back up the mountain to the east, or travel west along the mountainside. A large rock wall looms in the south, with a dark hole in the middle of it probably indicating the entrance to a cave.
8321: The wind here chills you to the bone, and the rocks move beneath your feet. Balancing precariously, you see that you can follow this ridge to the north and east, or you can go into the shelter of the mountainside to the west.
8322: A cowled sorcerer, in dark robes, gestures when he sees you (glowing).

Standing here you are dwarfed by the size of the peak which rises in the south. It looks impossibly steep for climbing, with many sharp rocks which could cut your hands to shreds. You can travel west and follow the ridge of smaller peaks which snakes out to the north-west, or you can descend the mountain to a valley in the east.
8323: This is one of the highest peaks in the area, and from here you can look all around and see the Misty Mountains in all their glorious splendour. To the north, the mountains slowly descend into a shallow valley, cut by a brown ribbon which must be a road, running east-west. To the south the mountains close ranks, forming an impassable barrier of rock, while to the east and west the mountains continue on for miles in their snow-capped, mist-wreathed splendour.
8324: This cave has been worn from the rock by the passage of many millions of quarts of water. This room is lit by the light streaming in from outside, but you can see that the cave extending further back into the mountain is shrouded in darkness. A foul odor avails your senses as you sniff around looking to see what might be living here.
8325: A grey-skinned mountain troll stands here.
Shrouded in darkness the gloom here is depressing. Peering around you, you can see that the cave extends to the west, or you can go back to the light in the north where the entrance is.
8326:
A large earth troll is digging here, looking for some tasty morsels.
A large mean-looking troll is here.
A large mean-looking troll is here.

A sulfurous stench comes from the water to the south, a lake which is wreathed in mist. Peering into the gloom you can see the cave extending east and west, and the ever present sound of dripping water un-nerves you in the darkness.
8327: The constant drip..drip..drip of water puts your nerves on edge. The darkness all around does nothing to allay any fears you may have about the inhabitants of this cave complex, and neither does the powdered bones on the floor.
8328:
A huge black fungus is here, exuding a foul stench.
A giant, strange looking green fungus is here, ready to devour you in seconds.
An ancient fungus smothers the boulders.

The light in here is eerie, and you see it comes from the luminous fungi growing all over the walls and roof, in many shades of green, orange, red and yellow. Obviously it is the decay of dead fungi that causes the awful stench in here. Or is it... unidentifiable remains lie scattered about the floor.
8329: A foul stench comes from the water to the south, and the steam rising from it has a sulfurous smell. You spot a glimmer of surreal light from the north, but to the east all you can see is the ever present, all pervading darkness.
8330: Ahh, at last, some shelter from the wind. Although the sides of this mountain are rather slippery, you don't have too much trouble keeping your footing. You can travel further south, or climb back up to the mountain top.
8331: Mountains, mountains and more mountains. If they weren't so beautiful, I guess you would be getting sick of them by now. Standing on the peak of this one, you have an excellent view all around. You can follow this trail along the peaks north or east. To the west you can descend a little to the side of the mountain to get some shelter from the harsh winds.
8332: The ridge of peaks along which you are walking extends further to the south and west. You can descend the mountain to the east, but then you would not be able to see these mountains in their full magnificence. You spot a valley in the east following roughly the same direction as the ridge you are on.
8333: The rocks underfoot are rather loose, but thankfully you managed to find a relatively compact patch on which to walk with safety. From here you can climb the mountain to the west, or traverse north along the side of the mountain.
8334: The trail is almost at an end here, dropping down into a valley which leads south-east. You can see mountains in the east and west, although those in the east don't seem to be so formidable.
8335: The trail bends south and east here, dipping down to a valley bottom in the south, leading along the side of a mountain in the east. To the west the peaks of this mountain chain rise majestically to their full height, glistening in the sun.
8336: Standing on the side of this mountain makes you feel slightly uneasy, since you realise that you could possibly lose your footing at any time and fall down the slope. To the west you can climb further up this magnificent mountain, or you can traverse the mountainside to the south.
8337: Standing on the top of this mountain gives you a commanding view of the area around you. This line of peaks weaves sinuously down to the south east, In the north a path leads east-west, and further north you can see a dense forest.
8338: The snow crunches underfoot as you travel precariously along a narrow ridge. The way down the west side of this mountain looks impossible, but in the apex of this peak and the one further east, you may be able to descend safely to the valley below.
8339: The mist-shrouded water moves gently around you. Strange sounds are echoed and amplified, distorted beyond recognition by the vast chamber in which this lake sits. The water smells foul, the stench of sulfur and decay ever-present in your poor nostrils. The lake extends to the south and west. You can also climb back to the cave in the north.
8340: You are gently rocked by ripples on the surface of this underground lake. Mist and foul-smelling gases rise from the surface of the water, seemingly reaching for your throat, trying to tear your lungs from your body. The lake extends to the north. In the west you see a low island jutting above the water.
8341: Ripples bounce backward and forward from the shore. The mist quickly rises up to wrap itself around your throat, and you can almost feel it trying to strangle you. The lake extends east, and to the south you spot a low island jutting above the surface.
8342: A wooden chest stands in the corner.

This rocky island must be where the inhabitants of the caves kept their most precious possessions, for in the middle of the island sits a very heavy stone chest with a very sturdy lock on it. The passage of many feet has worn the surface of the rock smooth, and the island is just high enough to prevent the mist covering it. Looking around, you see the lake to the east and north is covered with mist, making you feel truly isolated here.
8343:
A sturdy pack horse is standing here.
A pig is here, covered in mud.
A sturdy pack horse is standing here.

This small enclosed yard lies adjacent to a crude homestead, and obviously provides shelter to a few of the animals kept by whomever dwells in the cabin. The only fencing is along the northern edge of the pen - in every other direction natural granite forms the sides.
8344: The path ends here in a small, tidy garden, with most of the plants being in a rockery, surprisingly enough. The hut to the west looks solidly built from wood, which must have been hauled here from the forest you spotted way in the north, and smoke curls lazily away from the chimney on a light breeze.
8345: To the west of you is the Wolf Gate, the main entrance to the fabled Goblin-gate, home of the orcs of the Misty Mountains. A few steps are running down from the gate into a narrow valley between tall mountains.
8346: The stupid orc who used to live here got lost in the mountains years ago. His friends are still looking for him. If you don't like orcs, better not to be here when they show up. The walls and the floor of the room are bare; no objects can be seen, yet this place is obviously not totally forgotten. There are many cracks in the walls and the floor. In a big crack on the ground there is some water. Another big crack leads south.
8347: It is an extremely steep and slippery path leading southwards. An other option is to go through the big crack to the west. There is no sign of any life except for lichens on the dark rocks.
8348:
A shade is here, shrouded in an inky blackness.
A shade is here, shrouded in an inky blackness.

This small valley is nestled in the foothills of the Misty Mountains, and it has a quiet unspoiled demeanour. On either side steep walls guard its perimeter - the only means of egress appears to be a small tunnel behind a rock to the south.
8349: You have to move very carefully so you don't disturb the rocks on the unstable slope. The cliffs to the north and the south look impassable, but further to the east a gap between them allows a view of a forested landscape.
8350: A pile of rocks blocks your way to the east. Choked by the fallen rocks and boulders, the trail forces its way down the steep slope.
8352: Large rocks cover the western and the northern sides of this strange hill. Some hands must have put the rocks in their places. Hands belonging to living or undead creatures... who can tell?
8353:
A Skeletal Warrior is staring angrily at the surroundings.
A Skeletal Warrior is staring angrily at the surroundings.

The air is thick, making it hard to breathe. A weakhearted person or creature might have to fight feelings of terror. What happened to the poor soul buried here? This is not a burial place of anyone who was liked by his people. The head has been cut of from the body and turned upside down, and through the heart an iron spike has been driven.
8354: The pleasant grassy slope leads down from the small hill to the road. Looking east, you can see before you only ridges and slopes falling towards lowlands and plains glimpsed occasionally between the trees.
8355: The road can take you north, to the distant Eagle's Eyrie and the small trading centre Maethelburg that lies by the river Anduin. To the east you see the border of a dark forest, and south of here is a small crossing.
8356:
A very strong orkish leader is here on patrol.
An experienced orkish scout is looking for tracks on the ground.
An orc soldier is standing here.
An orc soldier is standing here.
An orc soldier is standing here.
An orc soldier is standing here.
The road from Maethelburg connects here to the road leading to the Lower Pass and to the Old Dwarven Road which starts to the east of here.
8357: A hungry warg stands here, sniffing around for flesh.

You are on the remnants of the Old Dwarven Road which connects Mount Erebor far in the east with Eriador to the west. Now only the fearless Beornings prevent the road from disappearing completely. A bit west the road splits into two parts, each leading through one branch of the High Pass.
8358: You are on the western border of a dark forest. The trees are standing very closely here, and the thick undergrowth makes it hard to move. West and south you can catch a glimpse of the road leading through the forested landscape. To the east the forest gets thicker.
8359:
A small evergreen plant grows here, its woody stems reaching two feet.
A small evergreen plant grows here, its woody stems reaching two feet.
A tall and majestic oak tree grows here, surveying the lands about it.
A large thorny branched shrub is growing here.
A brutish forest troll is hunting here, looking for some tasty flesh.

Pines, firs and other trees stand together in this quiet forest. You hear no birds and no animals. You watch carefully for any sign of life, knowing that something is here, waiting for its prey in the shadows.
8360:
A tall plant with a perfectly smooth stem gracefully marks the landscape.
A tall plant with a perfectly smooth stem gracefully marks the landscape.
A tall plant with a perfectly smooth stem gracefully marks the landscape.

The forest is here, quietly abiding its time. You keep turning around to check if anything has sneaked up on you from behind. From the treetops you hear the rattling of the leaves in the light breeze from the valley of the great river Anduin somewhere in the east.
8361: This is the east rim of the dark pine forest at the foot of the mountain range. Trees obscure your view to the west, and it seems to you that there is something moving in their shadow. To the south you can see a small forest river.
8362:
A brutish forest troll is hunting here, looking for some tasty flesh.
A brutish forest troll is hunting here, looking for some tasty flesh.

This mixed forest at the foot of the Misty Mountains consists of tall pines, old oaks and stout elms. Just south of here, you hear the sound of running water. It is a small stream carrying fresh water from the mountains to feed the Anduin somewhere in the south.
8363: A rabbit is here eyeing your presence warily.
Here the Old Dwarven Road leads across the little forest stream running east from the mountains towards the Anduin. The water looks cold, clear and quite safe to drink.
8364: To the north, the road winds its way into the lower branch of the High Pass, and to the south, it can take you down to the great river Anduin. To the east is a dark, green forest.
8365: This very old road was once built by dwarves to support trade between Arnor and the Lonely Mountain. Now it is mainly used by foul creatures of the night. The road leads north and south passing a slope you can see if you look west. On the east side is a green but very dark forest.
8366: Bend in the Old Dwarven Road

The old road turns north and east here. To the east of the road the forest is so thick that you can barely see two steps ahead. To the west the pine-forest rises almost to the top of the mountain slope.
8367: This is yet another turn in the twisting road, which is getting more and more overgrown. Obviously, travellers are not common guests here. Maybe the inhabitants of the surrounding forests do not need tracks or roads?
8368: The road bends north and east here. Green hills rise to the west of the road, their slopes covered by various trees and bushes. Some tall birches grow just to the south of the road. To the northeast you can see a dark forest.
8369: Zigzagging its way through a dark forest, this overgrown road can take you into the Misty Mountains, or south towards the Anduin. On all sides, high trees surrounds you.
8370: The road makes its way through a very dark forest. It is possible to continue on the road north and east. A thick forest to the south does not let anyone pass. The trees to the west are less dense.
8371:
A rabbit is here eyeing your presence warily.
A hungry warg stands here, sniffing around for flesh.

The road makes its way through a dark forest towards an unknown destiny in the east. Looking along the road, you can see that it leads down to the river Anduin, which it crosses by a ford, known to be rather dangerous. Beyond the river the road leads into Mirkwood and to the lands beyond.
8372: A very large tree branch has been ripped from a tree.

The trees that stand here are worn and scarred, like weary soldiers after a bloody battle. Many other trees lie on the ground; some have been cut, some broken, and some uprooted altogether. Smaller branches and twigs litter the area, with dead leaves and wood splinters covering the earth. As the wind blows by, it creates a low, resonating sound, with the pitch shifting up as the wind dies down. This place looks like a battlefield, as if the forces of nature had met in some sort of violent clash, only to have a tragic finale ending in sorrow and despair.
8373: A forest spider is here crawling around.

The forest here thins, allowing much more light to enter compared to the darker surrounding forest. Most of the trees seem to have been growing here a long while, although some are younger, about twice as tall as an adult human. The lower density of the forest gives room for some shrubs to grow. Some of the bushes have little round berries, although they do not look like they would be very tasty. The foliage all around has a medium green hue, but there is a great variety in the shapes of the leaves.
8374: The stream takes a sharp bend here, flowing beneath a small cliff to the north. The water is frigid, fed by snowmelt from the peaks to the far west. To the east, the stream widens a bit and becomes shallower before disappearing into a forest.
8375: This frigid mountain stream swifly plunges through a series of waterfalls and rapids on its journey to the Anduin. There is a hairpin turn here, and the banks are so steep that it is very hard to find purchase there. To the north the terrain becomes more gentle, but the current is still very fast.
8376: The stream plunges through a series of short waterfalls. The current is very swift, and the channel is full of sharp rocks. Northward there is a small cliff, above which runs a road. To the west, the land tilts sharply upwards, rising to the first peaks of the Mountains. You can climb the rocky bank to the south.
8377:
There are three water lilies here.
A tall plant grows here, with grey-green leaves and grey flowers.
A trout swims here.

The one who cups his hand for a sip and plunges it in the water might quickly pull it back. The water is freezing even during the summer. On the north and the south banks huge trees guard the river. Looking upstream, to the west, you see a small path crossing the stream.
8378: The small river cheerfully carries its waters through the sombre forest. The low mossy banks are covered with tall pine-trees which drop their cones, needles and branches into the clear water of the current.
8379: Here the small river leaves the surrounding forest and makes its way through the grassy plains west of the river Anduin. The water is clear and seems quite safe to drink.
8380: A brook trout is here, swimming in the current.

The river that flows from the west turns south here, trying to escape the clutches of the dark forest in the north. It rushes toward the grasslands to the south-east in its journey towards the great river Anduin. Sloping gently, the water carries some debris, but becomes ever more clear as it progresses downstream. Some gnarled logs create a maze for the water to run through, as if the logs were the arms of the forest, trying in vain to hinder the river's flow.
8381:
A trout swims here.
A brook trout is here, swimming in the current.
A brook trout is here, swimming in the current.

The river flows in from the north, abruptly changing course to head eastwards, as if it couldn't make up its mind about what to do. The southern edge of the river bank at the bend is rocky and the water swells and gurgles as it lashes against the rocks. A dark forest looms ominously to the south threatening to devour the river.
8382:
A brook trout is here, swimming in the current.
A brook trout is here, swimming in the current.
A brook trout is here, swimming in the current.

The stream continues its sinuous course in search of the mighty flow of the Anduin. In this area the river opens its way into a dark, sinister-looking forest. Lofty trees with greyish trunks and blackened leaves loom by the riverside. Leaning over the waters, they cast thick shadows on the darkened surface; even the gurgling of the stream can barely be heard here, as if the sickly-looking barks absorbed the lively sound of the running water.
8383: The river makes a bend here, turning east. Upstream to the north the river is cloaked in the darkness of the forest. On this new eastward course light can be seen; a refreshing change from the dreary forest. As the river turns against the bank it quickly picks up speed, the sound of the churning water drowns out any noise of wildlife; thunder is perhaps the only thing that might be heard over the water.
8384:
A brook trout is here, swimming in the current.
A brook trout is here, swimming in the current.
A brook trout is here, swimming in the current.
A brook trout is here, swimming in the current.
A very strong orkish leader is here on patrol.
An orc soldier is standing here.
An orc soldier is standing here.
An experienced orkish scout is looking for tracks on the ground.

Free of the dark forest, the river is wider and more approachable. From the grassy banks the slow trickle of water can be heard. At this point, the river turns southward. The rocks in the riverbed are worn smooth and round from decades of the water running slowly over them. The surrounding plains have been soaked by the rivers' runoff.
8385:
A crayfish is here, snapping its claws at you.
A salmon swims here.

As the river bends towards the south it widens slightly. Although slow flowing up until this point the slope of the ground to the south-east pulls the water downstream more forcefully. The current is increasingly stronger as it rushes to meet the much larger Anduin River in the distance. The shadow of the forest to the west is now just a memory, as this river heads toward brighter plains and pastures.
8386: As the river bends eastward the current begins to pick up speed. While the northern portion of this segment of river is relatively calm, the eastern section rushes at quite a quick pace. The fervent sounds of rushing water can be heard coming from that direction. Westward a dark forest looms, casting an ominous shadow upon the land.
8387: The river slows a bit here as it turns to the south, but it is not by any means tranquil. Looking upstream to the west there is a dark forest in the distance. Toward the east there are some ruins of what could have been a house, now reduced to rubble. Whatever destroyed that place is unknown. However, it was certainly not natural erosion.
8388: At this bend the river makes a quick turn backward to the east, part of a series of turns that serve to speed up the current even more. The loud roar of the rushing water is overwhelming and the banks of the river are under tremendous pressure as they force the strong river to turn at a sharp angle. Anyone travelling by boat here would have to keep their focus as they navigate these waters, lest they be dashed against the banks or capsized by the force of the water. A swimmer could do nothing but let the strongest current carry him where it may.
8389: As the river travels eastwards it roughly brushes against the riverbank, which serves to turn its course to the south. As it rubs against the bank the flow of the water begins to slow. Ahead in the distance the river is just a calm, smooth trickle.
8390: The river is calm as it moves slowly eastwards away from the shadow of the mountains in the west. Small water insects can be seen skimming the surface of the water along with broken bits of reeds that float gently past. A sense of peacefulness exudes from the small eddy pools formed by rocks in the current, and the soothing sound of the waters gentle flow.
8391: A fallow deer is grazing peacefully here.

This small forest at the foot of the mountains is full of green trees and colourful wild flowers. Listening to the singing birds and admiring the beauty of the forest makes you want to sit down and take a break from the dangerous world around you.
8392: You are now deep within the forest. Tall pines and sturdy oaks surround you, and you have trouble moving around due to the thick undergrowth. Listening carefully, you hear a grunting sound. Was it a boar, or something bigger sneaking around looking for fresh meat?
8393: You are now deep inside the forest. Old rotten logs, mixed with dead leaves and some brightly coloured flowers lie among the high trees. It is very dark in here. You unsuccessfully try to find the sources of the sounds that reach you. You can hear boars grunting, birds singing and an occasional branch breaking.
8394: A fallow deer is grazing peacefully here.

The forest surrounding you is very old. Ancient trees loom above you, forming an impenetrable ceiling between you and the sky. Moss-covered stones and the remnants of long dead trees make it very hard to move.
8395: A tree-snake lies wrapped around one of the tree branches.

The trees in this area of the forest seem younger than in other parts of it, but still have weathered many seasons. Their lush foliage blocks out any natural sunlight. The floor of the forest consists mostly of fallen leaves and twigs. Smaller plants and shrubs would be choked out by the massive roots of the towering trees, and would not receive the light they need to survive. The same might be true for other things that enter here.
8396:
A brutish forest troll is hunting here, looking for some tasty flesh.
A brutish forest troll is hunting here, looking for some tasty flesh.

The forest is thick as the trees crowd each other. The trees are an even mixture of old, wizened ones and younger, less hardened ones. With the passing wind the tree branches sway, looking as if they are talking to each other; it is almost possible to hear them whispering.
8397: Despite the great darkness covering much of this entire area, here some light from the sky manages to break through. The illumination is enough to see clearly during the day, or with a full moon at night. The stands of trees, while predominantly young, include some larger, older trees as well. The unusual quiet of this place, coupled with the uneven shafts of light entering from above, combine to create a very eerie feeling suggesting this would not make a good resting place.
8398: In this part of the forest there is a great variety among the trees. Some seem to be quite old, having weathered many winters, and grown tall with the light of the spring. Others are shorter, but still seem as if they have been here for ages. If only one could know what these trees have seen, for surely they must have been growing here since the beginning of time.
8399: Several large trees stand around this glade, providing a natural cloak. The ground is worn and packed, as if many large and heavy creatures had travelled through here. Some trees bear large scratches like scars, evidence that some of the visitors were quite fierce creatures with large, sharp claws. If those creatures were marking their territory it might be unwise to stay here for long lest they return.
8400:
A fallow deer is grazing peacefully here.
A fallow deer is grazing peacefully here.

The forest is more dense. High trees mixed with lower brush form a very hard terrain to move in. Looking around you, you see the tracks of wild animals such boars and deers. You also see tracks of something bigger - man or beast... Looking back, you get the comforting view of the road to the south and the west and realise that at least you are not hopelessly lost yet.
8401: This dark and gloomy forest covers some of the foothills of the Misty mountains. Somewhere to the east, the land gradually flattens into the Vale of Anduin, but here it is still quite rugged.
8402: The thick undergrowth is making it hard to walk. To the north the forest is so dense that you can barely see two steps ahead. The trees grow less dense south and west.
8403:
A fallow deer is grazing peacefully here.
A very large, hairy man is standing here, examining you carefully.
A very large, hairy man is standing here, examining you carefully.

Trees surround you on all the sides, hiding the sky above. The forest is dark and gloomy with thick undergrowth, making it very hard to move around. All around you, you hear the sounds of the forest, birds singing and boars grunting.
8404: To the north and to the east you can see nothing but tall green trees. West and south you can catch a glimpse of an overgrown road making its way through the forest.
8405: Under an overhanging cliff, there is a dirty, smelly, stinking orc camp among sharp rocks. Filthy piles of debris lies around it, and some unsanitary pots with black, oily stews can be seen hanging over fires.
8413: You have now reached the bottom of the valley. A few bushes and some grass cover the slopes, feeding the few animals that dwell here. The mountain slopes bear footmarks of humanoid beings.
8414: Rocks again... what a surprise. The rough path you are following along the side of this mountain makes a bend to the east and south here: to the east the path descends to the bottom of a valley, while to the south it enters a narrow canyon. Mountains rise up majestically in the north and west, but you can spot no way of climbing them from here.
8415: You are on the bottom of a rocky canyon, about two meters wide. High, smooth cliffs, with no handholds in sight, flank you on both sides, leaving almost no choice on where to proceed: you can either follow the canyon to the north, or squeeze through a crevice westwards.
8416:
A rabbit is here eyeing your presence warily.
A fat rabbit is here, chewing on some grass.

Wow! The view from here is breathtaking. You have reached one of the lower eastern ridges of the Misty Mountains. Looking east, you see a green forest and beyond it the mighty Anduin with its surrounding lowlands. Even further away lies a dark-green sea, the Mirkwood. To the west you see a deep valley far below.
8417: The ridge turns west-south here. To the west you can see its crest and the snow-capped peaks of the mountains beyond. To the east and the north you can try to make your way down the rocky slopes to the green valleys below.
8418: You are climbing up the steep rocky slope to the top of the mountain ridge. The rough path, which has been leading up the slope, has disappeared. The bushes and the long grasses between the boulders, the patches of rabbit-cropped turf and the bright flowers have all vanished. Pebbles, rubbish, rocks and boulders cover the slope in uneven piles, as if waiting for something or someone to start an avalanche.
8419: You are on the slope which leads to the top of a mountain ridge. A few bushes are the only larger growing things here. A small forest can be seen below the ridge to the east.
8420: A rabbit is here eyeing your presence warily.

You are on the top of a wide steep slope of fallen stones, the remains of a landslide. When you try to move down it, rubbish and small pebbles roll away from your feet. Soon larger bits of split stone go clattering down and start other pieces below them slithering and rolling, and you are forced to walk very carefully to avoid setting the whole slope above and below you on the move.
8421: A fat rabbit is here, chewing on some grass.

You have finally reached the eastern and lower side of the ridge. Looking around you, you see the Misty Mountains to the west, and a small forest below you to the northeast. A few dwarf birches are the only growing things up here except for the low grass that covers the ridge.
8422: You have stumbled across a small path among the rocks. It leads east, from where you can hear thick voices speaking a foul orkish dialect.
8423: Slender white birches rise all around you, a marvel in this dully coloured landscape. To the north and east you can see the old dwarven road running along the border of a dense forest. The ground is very wet. To the west there is an opening between the trees that does not look natural.
8424:
A fat rabbit sits here, chewing on some grass.
A rabbit is here eyeing your presence warily.

You have reached the crest of the ridge. The steep mountain slopes facing west, south and north make this place look like a fortress. The air is thin and clear, and even the smell of the pine trees does not reach so far up in the mountains. During the short and intense spring, the mountain flowers celebrate it with colours and smells.
8425:
Herb: tarragon
Herb: foxglove
Herb: belladonna

A small evergreen plant grows here, its woody stems reaching two feet.
A small evergreen plant grows here, its woody stems reaching two feet.
A small evergreen plant grows here, its woody stems reaching two feet.
A slender plant, with white flowers at the top, grows here.
A slender plant, with white flowers at the top, grows here.
A large shrub covered with dark violet berries grows here.
A rabbit is here eyeing your presence warily.

This forest, on the eastern foothills of the Misty Mountains consists mainly of high, strong pines, mixed with an occasional birch and some oaks. Every step you take brings you further up on the mountains, that rise to heights of over eighteen thousand feet above you.
8426:
A small mushroom grows nearby.
A bright red mushroom is growing here.
A brown fox is here, looking for some rabbits to chew up.

You are on the edge of a climbing wood of pines that stand here right up the mountain slope from the deeper darker forests of the valleys below. Looking west, you can see the rocky slope continue till it reaches the top of the mountain ridge. A path goes down the slope to the south.
8427: A brown fox is here, looking for some rabbits to chew up.

You are on the edge of a green pine forest at the eastern foothills of the largest mountain-range in all Arda - the Misty Mountains. Just east of here you can barely make out a small road. To the west the terrain starts to slope up. Some tracks lead south.
8428: The slope is covered with fir trees that provide some shelter from the wind. To the north you can see the top of a cliff and a series of waterfalls below. To the east, the trees give way to a road, and beyond the road there is a dense forest. To the west the ground becomes more rocky.
8429: Rocks of all possible shapes and sizes are strewn around you. A couple of fir trees decorate the monotonous landscape. To the east, the ground slopes up a little. To the north there is a steep drop to a small stream. To the south the slope rises all the way to the crest of the mountain ridge.
8430: A hungry warg stands here, sniffing around for flesh.

The path turns west-south here, rising up the rocky slope to the south. Pebbles and lumps of rock litter the path, making it hard to move. Some boulders rise on the sides of the path, giving a shelter from the wind and falling rocks to a few patches of grass and an occasional bright flower. To the north you can see a small stream.
8431: The path leaves the small dell to the north and winds its way up the green slope. Bushes and boulders seem to be all around you, both beside the path and almost directly under your feet, as if trying to make you stumble. You notice some plants and berries which look as if they might be edible.
8432: A tall stag is here, grazing peacefully.

Bushes and low trees overhang the dell which lies just below the level of the road through the Lower Pass. Long bright-green grasses cover the ground like a thick carpet with a couple of thinner patches where the grass has been cropped by rabbits. Two big boulders rise at the northern end of the dell as if keeping watch, the ground around them decorated with yellow rockroses. To the east you can see the source of the small stream, the waters of which feed the grasses around you. A small path leaves the dell to the south.
8433:
A clear spring babbles as cool water trickles out of the ground.
A rabbit is here eyeing your presence warily.
A small stream bubbles out of a little hole in the rocks to the west. It runs along the road to the north. Green grass and occasional flowers surround it, feeding on the nutritious fresh water.
8436: Narrow Part of the Broken Trail
The trail bends among the fallen rocks. To the south there is a sheer vertical drop into a dim valley far below. The walls of the chasm are too steep to try to climb down.
8437: You feel your knees wobbling as you try not to look down the steep cliff to the south. Keeping yourself close to the mountain wall, you press on your hazardous journey through the Misty Mountains. Looking behind a boulder that has fallen down on the trail, you see a dark cave.
8438: After the long journey that brought you here, this dry cave really looks like the ideal place to rest. A narrow arch, barely wide enough for an unloaded mount to pass, is the only connection to the outer world, making the cave an efficient shelter against bad weather and predator beasts.
8439:
The corpse of *an Orc* is lying here.
Figurski (FF), wielding an ornate, steel-shafted warhammer, is here, fighting *a Tarkhnarb Orc*.
*Laos the Tarkhnarb Orc*, wielding an ornate, steel-shafted warhammer, is here, fighting Figurski (FF).
*a Tarkhnarb Orc*, wielding a heavy morningstar, is here, fighting Figurski (FF).
A hungry warg stands here, sniffing around for flesh.
*a Tarkhnarb Orc*, wielding a bastard sword, is standing here.
A hungry warg stands here, sniffing around for flesh.

To the south, the rock is marred by a large crack, into which has been wedged a boulder that acts as a crude door. There is a small chink left free at the top, so it is possible to look into the chamber beyond. The air flowing through the crack is fresh, so the surface must be quite near. A narrow tunnel marked with the tracks of iron shod boots leads down into some type of hewn chamber.
8440: The Misty Mountains loom large and real in the south, overpowering your senses with their vast presence. The path on which you are travelling is rocky and hard to walk on, and the sun bleached bones of many animals lie by the wayside. The path leads east and west here.
8441: Snow capped mountains dominate the landscape here, and they distract your eyes from looking at what you are walking on, which is almost certainly not just broken rocks and gravel. The trail bends east and north here.
8442: This difficult trail winds through a rock-strewn col - not a valley, but merely a place lower than the mountains around it. Steep overhanging cliffs line the path to the northwest and southeast. But for a few low trailing creepers eking out a miserable existence among the rocks, the land seems completely barren.
8443: The Misty Mountains are lying before you like an enormous chain of mountains continuing in a circle. The path on which you are travelling is rocky and hard to walk on. The mountains around you force the trail to lead into a canyon here, this place would be perfect for an ambush. It is difficult to see anything that might be alive here, although, the bones of many animals are scattered by the wayside. The path leads north and east.
8444: The trail continues into a small canyon to your south, leading to the Misty Mountains. The trail is crooked and hard to walk on. Parts of dead animals are scattered all around. The snow-white tips of the mountains around you catch your eye. The trail turns east, or you can leave south.
8445: There are no more bushes or grass here. Only mountains and hilltops are left to surround you like enormous shadows. The path itself is crooked and hard to walk on, bones are covering the wayside.
8446:
A mountain goat is here, jumping from cliff to cliff.
A mountain goat is here, jumping from cliff to cliff.
Rocks and hilltops surround you in every direction. This trail is very desolate. Rocks and bones from dead animals surround you. Only a few scattered bushes can be seen. The path goes north-south.
8447: You are walking on a small trail, leading around the mountain. This trail is probably frequently used by travellers since it is well marked and easy to walk upon. You can hear birds singing in the distance. This place seems to be a good shelter from the wind. The trail continues in a west-north direction from here.
8448: You are walking on a small trail, leading around the mountain. This trail is probably frequently used by travellers since it is well marked and easy to walk upon. To the west, you see huge rising mountains, while on your east side you see small hills everywhere. The trail continues to the south, or you can enter some hills to the north. A small path is leading to another trail east of you.
8449: You notice the snow lying on the top of every mountain. A couple of birds are flying high in the sky. Sometimes you can spot bones and skulls of different animals lying beside the trail. You can either go north into some rocky hills, or leave south. A small path leads to another trail west of you.
8450: You are walking on a small trail, leading around the mountain. This trail is probably frequently used by travellers since it is well marked and easy to walk upon. Here, you will have to climb up to continue your way around the mountains. You can, however, spot a small trail leading between the mountains further west.
8451: You are walking on a small, but well-trodden path between the mountains. This path seems to have been an important fast connection between the east and west of this huge range of mountains. You are completely surrounded by mountains on all sides of you.
8452: You have left the lowlands behind you, and you notice the mountains which seemed far away, have indeed grown in size. You can see no trees here, only some small crooked bushes. A couple of crows are flying high up in the sky.
8453: This path is slowly ascending, making its way to the mountains you can see to the north. You can indeed see few trees here, making the landscape pretty desolate. The path continues to the east, or you can go down to the lowlands west of you.
8454: Lots of stones are lying here which make walking difficult. The mountains that seemed so small from afar have now risen and nearly cover your view in all directions. To the north you can enter a pebbled path, or you can follow this path east or west.
8455: The landscape changes as you move. There are big mountains in front of you with snow on their peaks. The only way to get further east is by passing through them. You can see a big cliff in the distance to the north. The main trail goes east-west.
8456: You have come to a small crossing of paths. To the north you barely notice an old twisted path. As with other paths in this area, it seems to lead nowhere. You hear howls in the distance, dangerous creatures might be near. The main path still goes east-west.
8457: You notice the land looks even wilder here. You can see mountains on all sides of you, and you begin to wonder what might live up here so far from civilisation. The vegetation is sparse, only a few crooked low trees around. The wind is cold and chilling, coming from the mountains. However, the path continues to the east, or you can turn back westwards.
8458:
There is some snow on the ground.
A ferocious warg is here, snarling angrily.
A hungry warg stands here, sniffing around for flesh.
A hungry warg stands here, sniffing around for flesh.

You make your way through a heap of stones, a result of an avalanche bringing lots of loose rocks with it. The side of the mountain is covered by small birches, except the area where the avalanche once flattened everything in its path. Once across the heap of stone, you see that the trail goes on.
8459:
There is some snow on the ground.
A ferocious warg is here, snarling angrily.
A ferocious warg is here, snarling angrily.
A hungry warg stands here, sniffing around for flesh.

Still walking on the trail, you study geological formations of this area. The mountains are grey, clad with scattered spots of snow. Snow tends to lie in areas well sheltered from wind. Sometimes, during a long winter, much snow is gathered, that it will stay throughout the summer. In areas also well hidden from the sun, large glaciers have formed. The path runs west to east, while a seemingly less used trail splits off to the south.
8461:
There is some snow on the ground.
A hungry warg stands here, sniffing around for flesh.

This might well be the famous High Pass. This part seems well trodden, although it may have been a while since people last wandered this route. You believe that a pile of stones caused by an avalanche or rock slide has been recently removed from the trail. It is said that Beornings from the Anduin valley east of these mountains keep the Pass open. You really hope that it was Beornings, not Orcs, that cleared the trail. You walk around a sharp bend in the trail and find it blocked by a large rock slide. No one has bothered to remove that pile, or the the rocks have slided down recently. You should be able climb to the other side, but you doubt you will be able to go the same way back.
8462:
A ferocious warg is here, snarling angrily.
A hungry warg stands here, sniffing around for flesh.
A ferocious warg is here, snarling angrily.
A hungry warg stands here, sniffing around for flesh.

This narrow and seldom used path winds its way through the passes of the Hithaeglir. Despite the frequent switchbacks and bends, you think that the trail is following on the average a north-south course. The surroundings are very cold and rocky, not even a blade of grass can grow here. Just after a bend, your way is blocked by a huge pile of boulders. You can only retrace your steps.
8463: A dirty shovel is lying on the ground here.

You have fallen down a long, long slope. The snow that made the fall so slippery cushioned you from any damage, although getting back up may be a pain. The air in this room is very cold, probably due to the vast amounts of snow around you.
8464: On the Side of a Mountain

This path winds treacherously along the side of the mountain. To the north the mountainside descends very steeply to the valley below. A cave mouth yawns darkly in the east. Maybe this could offer you some degree of shelter from the elements.
8466: The path hugs the contours of the mountain. The mountain rises steeply to the south, and falls down to a deep valley to the north. The path leads east and west. Directly west you catch a glint of reflected light.
8467: The noise here is deafening, you can hardly hear yourself think. The water is crashing down from above, collecting in a large pool, and flowing over the northern face of this mountain, to crash on another ledge farther below. Spray dances all around, reflecting the light in many colours, and soaking your clothes. Looking carefully you can see a path leading up the rocks on the south side of the waterfall, but it looks dangerous and you may not be able to climb back down this way.
8468: That last move was a mistake. Even though the handhold looked secure, the condensed water on its surface made it very slippery, so you lost your grip and fell. I think maybe you should listen to advice in future. Being adventurous is all very well, but that should be tempered with caution.
8469: The water runs into here from the West, then cascades over the edge of the rock ledge on which you are standing. Clouds of spray billow up from below and cast reflections all around. The water collects in tear-shaped droplets on your clothes, your ears..in fact, they collect on any surface. Climbing back down that steep path which you climbed up is probably not a good idea..the mist seriously reduces your vision, and makes the rock very slippery.
8470: A clear spring babbles as cool water trickles out of the ground.

Clear sparkling water runs cheerily from a crack in the rocks here. More than likely this water is a product of melting snows high on the mountain tops, and it is refreshingly cooling after your long climb. Gurgling happily the water flows to the east. In the south a short tunnel crosses one of the mountains, it seems to lead towards the main path.
8471: This short tunnel is lit by light coming from both ends and is only about twenty feet in length. High enough for the tallest elf to walk through unhindered, it must have been built by some pretty large creatures. The walls are smooth, although they show some marks of cutting tools where the passage was hacked out of the mountainside.
8474: You are standing on a rocky hilltop. There is nothing but solid rock around here. Not even a tiny little green bush is to be seen, making this place look very barren. Below you, a trail leads northwards. Further north, you see a lot of mountains, and to the west you can see rising mountains. There seems to be a trail to the west of you, and to the south is a very dark place.
8475: This is a really dark place. The trees block all light from the sun, even when the sun is at its brightest. This must be a perfect hiding place for creatures that prefer shady or dark places during sunlight. A narrow gap among the trees allows you to leave this place northwards.
8476: You are walking on a well-prepared mountain trail. A high chain of mountains, seemingly impassable, is west of you. You can see some grassy parts in the lowlands around you, but mostly this place consists of rocks and pebbles in all kind of different sizes and shapes. To the south the trail carefully slithers its way towards the mountains, climbing up and down narrow valleys. Eastwards you can see a hilltop.
8477: A large brown wolf stands here, its teeth partly bared.
