A large cave troll is here, staying close to his mother.
The ugly troll mother is roaming the cave, taking care of her loved ones.

Broken bones crunch loudly under your feet, and other things squish softly when you stand on them. Remains of many dead beings litter the floor, and it is most probably these remains which give rise to the awful stench which makes you want to take out your weapon and slice off your nose.
8771: A huge stone giant is here, glaring at you.

This chamber has a high stone ceiling, and is longer than it is wide, almost like a tunnel. The high walls are covered in minute cracks. The floor is covered with dust and debris, but it's origin must remain unknown, since most of it has decayed beyond recognition. To the south a natural archway leads into a smaller chamber.
8772: A hungry warg stands here, sniffing around for flesh.

The walls of this small chamber look like they have been carved from the rock by crude tools. Natural stone archways lead to the north and south, probably a continuation of the natural tunnel from which this chamber was hewn. To the east there is a boulder which could possibly be moved.
8773: Above your head sits millions of tons of rock, just waiting for the right time to come crashing down. The walls which arch up to the high stone ceiling are a maze of hairline cracks. Bones in various states of decay litter the floor, but most are so old that their origins are undeterminable.

However, on close inspection you see that there is something not quite right about the way the rocks are arranged against each other, and it looks like it may be possible to move the large rock on the western side without causing the rest to crash down and bury you in debris.

A forest spider is here crawling around.

At the centre of a large circle, formed by some old firs, stands an ancient oak tree. The knots on its trunk seem to form a face, as if it were grimly looking out at the world. Its boughs rise towards the sky, like an evil priest might raise his arms in chanting words of doom. Every now and then, as the wind blows, the other trees sway, like a great crowd in an uproar.

The surface of the road is somewhat bumpy with small patches of grass growing among the rough stones. If one looks carefully, traces of aged wagon tracks can still be seen in the hard clay. The road runs from the west, where a dark forest looms, southward to the dim outline of a mountain range on the horizon.
8778: The surface of the road is somewhat bumpy with small patches of grass growing among the rough stones. If one looks carefully aged wagon tracks can be seen in the sections covered by hard clay. The road runs from the north, where a small river is still visible, to the south, where a mountain stands.
8779: The craggy ground has a rugged surface littered with numerous small rocks. A few remaining bulky stumps are scattered across the ground giving the impression that a forest existed here a long time ago. The ground slopes gently to the east where the soil has fewer rocks. Bypassing this area to the south and west is an unused-looking road.
8780: Bend in the Old Forest Road

The road turns sharply here, skirting a gently rising slope to the south-west. The terrain towards the east and north, which holds numerous young saplings, contains the remains of an old forest. Further south-west a tremendous mountain overshadows the surrounding lands.
8781: West of the road the ground rises sharply towards a tall mountain while the ground slowly ascends to the south. East of the road there is a grove of young saplings growing among the rotten tree stumps of a former forest. The road continues both south and north.
8782: This area was once a vast forest but was cut down long ago. A large number of rotten tree stumps are visible, many of them now serving as homes for termites and grubs. Among the stumps a new forest of young saplings grows.
8783: Various kinds of slender young trees form a thick and exuberant grove here. The soil is dank and fertile with a lot of small undergrowth struggling beneath the trees. A few hoary stubs of large trees are scattered in sections, cut down by woodsmen long ago. An old forest road is visible southward, being rarely used now that the major woods have diminished.
8784: Bend in the Old Forest Road

The road makes a gentle turn here, continuing to the west and south. A grove with lush vegetation is located to the north. To the east there is a large strange-looking hollow, filled with bushes and covered by a soft mist. It appears that this road is infrequently travelled upon from the state of the roadbed.
8785: Thick bushes fill this large hollow which was formed long ago by some mystical event of the sky. The soil here is obviously saturated because groundwater easily rises when even the smallest of creatures walks upon it. The air is very humid and a deep mist forms from the ground. A clearing, cloaked in haze, opens to the north.
8786: Bend in the Old Forest Road

A strange-looking hollow covered with haze and thick bushes lies on the north side of the road and is the source of the mist that covers this region. East of here the ground descends to a large plain of rich soil. The road continues to the south and west.
8787: This vast plain has low vegetation that spreads out to the north. An extensive vale with the Anduin river at its centre can be seen from here when the light is right. The region to the north-west appears bushier than the valley while a road, probably used by the Woodmen of long ago, lies to the south and west.
8788:
A sad looking old farmer is standing here.
A squirrel scampers around here, looking for nuts from the trees.
A fat rabbit is here, chewing on some grass.

The old forest road runs to the east and north while a muddy trail joins it from the south. The trail has a rough surface and appears to be rarely used. To the east the road continues until it is out of sight. A tall grass covers the ground on the west side of the road.
8789: The surface of this trail has been formed by layers of mud that have hardened during the dry spells between rains. Depressions from wagons are barely detectable in the battered ground. The eastern edge of the trail is overlaid with large bushes, while the area to the west looks grassy. The trail continues both to the north and the south.
8790: Grass covers the land that borders this loam trail. Its infrequent usage seems to be only by wandering animals. The trail declines slightly to the south where it later turns westward. Far in the north the trail connects to a wider road that is in better condition.
8791: This plain seems very lively having an abundance of vegetation consisting of grass several feet high and various kinds of flowers. Several small bushes with small, green leaves have also managed to take root in the excellent soil. A mud-covered trail to the east and south bypasses this plain.
8792: A starving cow stands here, looking for a patch of grass.

A few burdock bushes are scattered among the clovers that cover this placid plain. A trail of matted grass and lumps of excrement marks the frequent passage of large animals across these plains. An entrance to a burned village is located southward.
8793: Grass, about a foot tall, covers this land which is next to an old road running along the south side of here. The land is low and continues a smooth descent eastwards where the fertile ground is filled with many different types of flowering plants. A wide valley, filled with various vegetation, opens to the north where the plant life seems to flourish.
8794: The land here has effectively been invaded by multicoloured blossoms growing among the opulent grass. An old forest road, that was used by the few Woodmen in this region until the forest became exhausted long ago, can be seen south of here. To the north is a small spring with very clear water. The flowers continue to the east and west, though to the west the terrain has fewer flowers.
8795: Fertile grass and large numbers of flowers of varying colours cover the ground creating a view of health. The surrounding land forms an extensive valley that gently slopes towards the flowing river Anduin in the far east. The flowers continue westward and in the south an ancient road can still be seen.
8796: A small animal, all covered in spines, snuffles amongst the undergrowth.

This area is entirely covered with densely packed, thick-branched bushes. The leaves of the bushes look very large with vigorous blossoms when the season is right. A wide valley opens to the north and is covered with bushes, while the land in the west appears grassy with an abundance of flowers. An old abandoned road runs beside this area to the south.
8797: Bend in the Old Forest Road

A huge, black wolf is here, ready to devour.
A black wolf pads restlessly, looking for its next prey.

The road makes a gentle turn here, continuing both south and west. Plump shrubbery intermixed with several thick clumps of bushes lies on the north side of the road. Short grass and rough spots make it appear as if the road has seen little usage for many years.
8798: These low, bushy fields are covered with grass and bushes of varying height. The bushes are low, but their branches spread out quite a bit. Thick clusters have been formed by many different species of brush - even an occasional tree can be spotted in a cluster. The bushes seem to stretch long tangles of branches towards the road, reaching for ground as yet uncovered by the thick brambles. To the south and west the road turns.
8799: These low, rolling fields stretch out unbroken by hill or woods under the skies above. The fields are mainly covered by grass, but many bushes and thickets of bramble grow here, almost creating a maze on the plain. In these thickets the sounds of small animals running around can be heard, as well as birds calling out to each other from their hiding spots in the foliage.
8800: This section of the road remains almost intact, with few bushes and other plants on it. The lack of plants is possibly a result of the quarry that lies to the east of here - the barren old rockface is not very fertile and no plant spores are sent onto this road from there. The road leads west to the Misty Mountains in the distance, and east through fields on its way to the Anduin River.
8801: A diamond-back rattlesnake is coiled here, ready to strike.

This is what seems to be an old abandoned quarry. The miners that once dug and broke stone here are long gone, but this place is like an old wound, inflicted by man and slow to heal. Some small, lonely flowers grow in pockets of earth among the otherwise barren stone. In all directions, except to the south, there stand fifteen-feet-high stonewalls that prevent travel by mounts but a skilled climber could ascend the western wall.
8802: North of the road lies a quarry, on whose west and south sides the road goes around. The road leads west to the mountains, and east to the ford in the Anduin River. It appears to be more like a wide, beaten earth path here with no stones in it. Perhaps the last visitors to the quarry took the last stones from the road instead of quarrying their own. The road appears to have seen little traffic for many years, and no care has been given to it for some time before that.
8803: These rocky plains are the western shore of the Anduin River. There, in the river, old ruins can be spotted, standing out strangely above the waterline. To the south lies an old ford, which allows passage across to the eastern lands of the Vale of Anduin.
8804: The clear water here reveals the destruction and waste that litters the riverbed. Ruins toward the east beside the river indicate the source of the large chunks of abandoned wood and metal, apparently thrown in by hand. Nevertheless, the river continues to flow south past all these obstacles to where it becomes very shallow. Some vegetation grows along the water's edge.
8805: A rock lizard is here, motionless as it observes you.

Ancient ruins of a long forgotten building stand here, with moss-covered stone blocks and broken logs standing from the ground. The surrounding grasslands are slowly reclaiming these ruins. To the south the old forest road can be seen and to the west the mighty Anduin river can be heard.
8806: Bend in the Old Forest Road

Debris from the old ruins to the north has fallen to cover part of the northern edge of the old forest road. Small elm and oak saplings grow along both sides of the road. To the west, a ford over the Anduin River is visible.
8807: The field is covered with lush, green grass that sways when the wind blows. Scattered about the grass are yellow and blue flowers. A pile of stones lies in the field, the stones grey with lichen. To the east a clump of trees can be seen and a bit to the west there appears to be a ford through the river.
8808:
A mass of wriggling vines drops on you from the trees.
A mass of wriggling vines drops on you from the trees.

Old elm trees and ancient oaks grow amongst each other here blocking much of the wind. The air is damp with moisture, the ground covered with dead, decaying logs and moss-covered rocks. Vines cling to the trees and climb up their trunks to reach for the light above the canopy. An animal track seems to lead to the old forest road that can be sighted through the trees to the south.
8809: Bend in the Old Forest Road

West of this road is a dark clump of trees around which the road bends. Eastwards the road continues straight for some distance. Saplings from the elms and oaks west of here grow along the edge of the road. To the southeast a small hill stands.
8810: A small rabbit glares angrily at you.

This grass-covered ridge declines towards the road in the south. A small trail runs along the top of the ridge to where it connects with the road. Some stones lie about the sloping sides and thorny bushes grow amongst them. To the north this ridge stands between two fields, and to the west there is an open vale. The road south of here has a bend in it.
8811: Foot-high yellow grass grows here, with the blades shaped like long, thin arrowheads. West of here there is a grassy ridge, while to the south an old road can be seen. A dark forest stands tall in the far east.
8812:
A garden snake slithers harmlessly here.
A garden snake slithers harmlessly here.

A small village can be seen halting the eastward journey of the Old Forest Road a few miles from here. The road takes a wide turn to the south before running up to the village walls. In the north, a collection of hills and levees form a semicircle, blocking in water-soaked plains sitting at a lower elevation.
8813: Off in the east, the tops of elm trees can be seen just above a village. The road leads up to the village but does not appear to continue past it. Immediately to the north, the ground slopes downwards into a low basin in the Anduin Vales. From this elevated vantage, travellers could make out the muddy lay of the lands in the north.
8814: A colourful butterfly is fluttering around here.

The road continues to the east and west for a few miles before bending away. This road lies in a state of disrepair as it is well-used here but ill cared for. To the south, weeds creep up to the road, crossing it and filling in potholes. In the north, the lands falls down into a large depression in the plains.
8815: The Old Forest Road stretches in an east-west direction here. To the east is a distant and huge, dark forest. Far to the west mist-covered mountains rise to the sky. The road does not appear to be used very often, if at all. Grass and tiny bushes grow in old ruts on the roadbed.
8816: The riverbed here is high enough to make it possible for people and creatures to cross. The water runs deep and swift in spots, with stones protruding from the surface in places. Anyone losing their footing might be dashed against some of those boulders. Both upriver and downriver the river is much deeper. The grass from the surrounding fields grows right to the water's edge, with some of it dangling in the water.
8817: The road broadens here into a large open area resembling a trampled square of earth more than a road. Small patches of grass grow in small clusters, along with an odd flower or two. To the east lies the Old Ford, one of the few places one can safely cross the Anduin River. To the west, a long unused road runs through the plains.
8818: From here the old road heads straight east to the ford across the Anduin River and north towards an abandoned quarry. The road seems to be slightly better repaired than farther to the northwest - why, one can only guess. To the west, dense brush covers the plain, and some vines have stretched out towards the road, longing for light and space to expand into. To the south lies an old farmstead.
8819: The main plants here are dense tangles of knee-high bushes with arrowhead-like leaves. The only undergrowth that lives beneath the bushes are thick, thorny weeds that cling to the ground. To the west stands the border of a forest. Eastwards a road makes its way through the uneven terrain.
8820: The birch forest that flourishes west of here is much thinner in this area. The birch trees grow farther apart here, making it easier to travel through this part of the forest. High grass and low bushes also grow here, enjoying the light that filters down through the treetops during the day.
8821:
A tree-snake lies wrapped around one of the tree branches.
A badger is here, exploring for food.

The luxuriant birch forest flourishes without restraint in this dank and vital terrain thereby inhibiting the growth of smaller plants. The trees grow very densely packed, making travel through this forest difficult. The forest becomes more mixed to the south but continues to be dominated by birches in the west.
8822: Large bushes with long green leaves cover this area along the road. A few tiny mountain ashes have managed to sprout here and struggle for nearly non-existent living space. The ground is teeming with roots of different sizes making travel unpleasant. The land declines gently northward.
8823: Great downy birches grow tall in this luxuriant terrain giving excellent protection and food for the animals that inhabit the area. The ground is very soft and there is a thick undergrowth with various small, decaying plants. This entirely birch forest continues to the east but becomes less purely birch in the south.
8824: Bend in the Old Forest Road

The corpse of a rabid, grey wolf is lying here.
A grey wolf is here, salivating profusely.

The road turns once again, snaking its way through the overgrown plains. The road was once broad and well looked-after, but only a wide cart-track remains. The edges and ditches of the road have already been taken over by creeping bushes. The road bends to the north and east, while to the south and west wild bushes cover the plain.
8825: A fat rabbit is here, chewing on some grass.

Sturdy bushes with wide, green leaves grow quite densely here. Both to the north and to the east of here is an old road. The bushes here spread out into the lands to the west. To the south appears to be the edge of a forest.
8826:
A wild bull seems ready to charge you.
A black and white skunk is scuttling about here, searching for food.

The hard packed soil, that was at one time a road, has lost its fight with nature. Several varieties of flowers, bushes and grass have loosened the soil enough so that they can flourish here. East and west the road runs from the ford in the mighty Anduin river to the mountains west of here.
8827: Bend in the Old Forest Road
A brown fox is here, looking for some rabbits to chew up.

Large bushes and a few mountain ashes grow along the south side of the road while along the western side grows a short grass, together with some flowers and a few small bushes. The road appears quite smooth and a couple of wagon tracks can be seen on the grass-covered surface.
8828: The land here is completely covered with short grass, many types of flowers, and a few small bushes scattered about. An old forest road passes by the north and east of here. The eastern road provides a well marked path to the river Anduin. The grassy plain continues to the west while the lands in the south are home to larger plants.
8829: The road is bordered by luxuriant vegetation consisting of various kinds of flowers and bushes that seem to flourish without restraint. The road descends to the east where the Anduin vale opens wide, with its river near the centre.
8830: A swallow flies high above the ground.

Fertile vegetation consisting of different types of flowers and several bushes border this ancient road which descends eastwards to where an extensive valley opens. The road appears quite unused and much of it has become covered by short grass.
8831: Bountiful grass and a few small bushes grow across this plain just south of the road. Tracks of animals are easily visible when some are passing through because of the soft soil. The land rises gently to the west where a bushy embankment rises. A small clearing opens out in the south.
8832:
A sharp-eyed hawk is here stalking some prey.
A sparrow is flapping around on the ground.

A small clearing covered only with short grass is here. The soft soil can easily show many tracks from various animals that sometimes pass this way. The lands to the north and west are nondescript but towards the east and south the terrain turns rugged and a number of small bushes appear.
8833: The land is overlaid by a large number of small bushes, many of which have had their leaves consumed by maggots. Meanwhile, a few birds fly overhead looking for small insects and maggots to feast upon. The bushy ground continues southward where the bushes grow more irregularly. A forest of green birches covers the land east of here.
8834: Thickets of holly bushes are scattered about, leaving fairly spacious routes between them. Spiky hawthorns unfold their nasty twigs and one must be careful in order to avoid being scratched. The passages between the bushes open into a small clearing to the west.
8835: This grassy land contains an even mix of hay and bushes with a few molehills scattered about. The surrounding lands look the same except to the east where the bushes grow more densely.
8836: A black snake hurries towards you with sly intentions.

The grassy land gently slopes down towards the west where a muddy-looking trail leads towards a village in the distant west. Hummocks of trefoil can be seen growing in several places forming a quilt-like pattern before you. The grassy land continues in all directions but the west.
8837: A brown fox is here, looking for some rabbits to chew up.

The rough trail bends here continuing to the north and the west where the remains of a burned village stand. It appears that the trail has not been used in a long time because of the rampant growth of hay which now covers it. The ground ascends slightly towards the east where a wide spread of grassland lies.
8838: Plains covered with grass and a few bushes surround this muddy trail which rises gently towards a burned village standing in the west. The mud on this trail could show the tracks of animals but the settling and flowing of the mud on this slope eventually removes them.
8839: Entrance to the Burned Down Village

This spot, where the land rises towards the ruined yard of a burned down village, marks the head of a muddy trail. The walls which once protected this village from its enemies are now crumbling and the wooden gateway which stood between the walls has been smashed. The remains of a burned out guard tower can be found southwards.
8840: A burned down village stands east of these dry plains. The plain appears very barren with only a small amount of vegetation, consisting mainly of a few small stunted bushes and some short grass. Traces of some animals can be seen on the softer spots of the ground when they pass through.
8841: Although the soil here is withered, small patches of grass and a few short bushes still manage to grow. It seems that the vegetation becomes more lush to the east, while the land to the north looks rocky and barren. Towards the south stands what was once a sturdy stone wall, but it is now falling apart.
8842: Numerous rocks of various sizes litter the ground, forming a patchy carpet of stone. A few parched branches squeeze their way through the rocks, reaching for light. To the north a mountain trail declines to here. The soil softens towards the east and south while the rocky land continues to the west.
8843:
A shallow pond is here, tinted green with algae.
A giant slug is here, oozing around.

The terrain slopes gently down towards a pond some twenty feet wide and filled with squalid-looking water. A few lily pads lie on the surface of the water, and various stones, covered with caustic phlegm, form a border around the pond. Tracks of various animals are embedded upon the muddy ground.
8844: The rich soil of this land is bountiful with dense hay. During the warm summer months various kinds of flowers burst with health, creating a richly-coloured environment. There are some smooth little stones scattered about and several small holes in the ground, most likely dug by moles.
8845: Large bushes, with thick leaves, grow on this sharp bank which borders a road to the north. Some of the bushes are missing leaves, having been consumed by insects and herbivores which occupy the luxuriant terrain. The ground descends gently southward where it is covered by grass and a few bushes. To the west there is a muddy trail which joins the road in the north-west.
8846: The ground here is covered with numerous bushes of various sizes and types. All of the bushes look healthy though some of the branches have been gnawed by animals feeding in this area. The bushy embankment continues westward and runs parallel to the road just north of here while the lands to the east and south are covered with grass.
8847: Short parched grass grows on this otherwise uninhabited plain. The once soft ground has become rather dried and broken due to long periods of sunshine and infrequent rain. The land rises gently northward where a bushy embankment stands. Grasslands continue to the south and west while a small clearing among the bushes is visible to the east.
8848: A muddy trail bypasses this grassy field to the west. Here, the ground is very rough and supports some divergent flowers and a few insignificant bushes. The ground gently rises northward where it forms an embankment covered with bushes. The grass continues to the east and south.
8849: Towards the east the road descends until it joins the mouth of a very large valley, while to the west the road continues until it branches north and south. On the south side of the road there is an embankment that is covered by large bushes. On the north side of the road lies a vast plain with short grass growing on it.
8850: An embankment, containing various types of bushes, lies to the south side of this infrequently used road. The road descends towards the east. North of the road is a grassy area. The road itself looks to be very old and in poor shape after having been deeply rutted by the passage of wagons many years ago.
8851: Short and dry grass covers this barren plain which contains only a few small bushes and some large rocks. Bones of some small animals are scattered around and other traces of different kinds of animals are imprinted on the surface.
8852: This barren land supports only a few stunted bushes and a couple of feeble pines. Very little grass has managed to take root in this poor soil. Towards the east the land becomes more hospitable to vegetation and more grass can be seen. A battered stonewall stands to the south-east, separating a burned down village from these barren lands. The region to the north appears very rugged.
8853: The ground here is rugged and lifeless, with a few broken stones littered across the top and an occasional dead root embedded in the surface. The bones of several small animals can still be seen though many of them have been crushed. To the south, where the soil appears moister, some stunted vegetation has begun to grow but to the east the rocky land continues.
8854: A swallow flies high above the ground.

Numerous rocks, both small and large, cover this arid ground as it nears the top of the mountain from the south, making travel difficult and the land inhospitable to vegetation. A small trail winds from the east on its way to the mountain's peak. To the south the terrain appears similar to here. Rising in the north is the peak of the mountain.
8855: From here, the top of the mountain, you can see much of the surrounding lands. The southern slope gently descends, while the other sides of the mountain are much steeper and more perilous. A small precipice is to the east, though it appears somewhat unstable and would be difficult to reach.
8856: This side of the mountain is very steep and even an experienced climber would find it nearly impossible to continue southward. The terrain is rough and barren with no vegetation. Towards the south a tall mountain looms, overshadowing the lands around.
8857: A large rabbit looks peacefully at you, ready to dart away.

The ground here is rough and hard with numerous small stones embedded into the surface although a few stunted, ancient junipers have managed to grow in the softer spots. The land rises gently towards the south where it eventually forms a steep mountain. To the north and east the remains of an old forest road can be found.
8858: Bend in the Old Forest Road
A small rabbit glares angrily at you.

The road bends sharply here, continuing north and east. Southwards the ground begins to rise towards some mountains. The surface of the road is hard packed, indicating that it was once frequently travelled, although the small patches of grass that are now growing make it doubtful the road has seen much use recently.
8859: A steep gloomy rock face rises to the south and west forcing the road to make a sharp turn east and north of here. The southern wall of the rock face is sheer and covered by some thick bushes while the west wall appears a bit gentler and has a few cracks which make passage that way possible for a skilful climber.
8860: A black crow flies low to the ground here, looking for carrion to eat.

This road is bordered by a gentle embankment of dirt and several small rocks to the south. A tangled logging area covered with young saplings is to the north. The road appears to be infrequently used since grass has managed to grow in many sections.
8861: Rocks of various sizes, as well as loose gravel, cover this embankment that follows the road just north of here. There is no vegetation growing in this austere ground for it is far too harsh to support plant life. A gloomy mountain with a sheer face stands west and is unreachable from this direction.
8862: A fat rabbit is here, chewing on some grass.

The ground here is particularly hard, and is unable to support much in the way of vegetation. Only a few scraggly trees have managed to take root among the stones that litter the ground. This rocky land rises northward and to the far south a small pond has formed. In the east the soil becomes more fertile.
8863: The grass here has prospered and grown to dominate this smooth region which gently declines eastward towards a crossing in the road. The soil becomes more barren in the west but seems to burst with health in the eastern lands where the river Anduin flows at its mightiest.
8864: Bend in the Old Forest Road

The road descends gently eastward where the terrain is more fertile and able to support its blooming vegetation. This poses a stark contrast with the land to the west where the soil is harsh and the terrain is mostly barren. The surface of the road is covered with short grass indicating it has seen little usage.
8865: The precipice is soft and brittle allowing many large fissures to form through the passage of time. Several of the fissures have caved in over the years making it apparent that they are both hollow and unstable. A few stunted pine trees have managed to grow in the less harsh portions of the slope. The western horizon is covered by a tremendous peak which obscures the view in that direction as it rises from the ground.
8866: The head of this trail originates at the foot of the soft mountain slope, and worms its way up to the precipice. The trail is tiled with small circular stones and seems of an ancient origin, possibly constructed by mountain dwellers. A short yellow grass traces the edge of the trail as it winds up towards the precipice.
8867: You find yourself in the outskirts of the vast mountain forest that carpets the valley side. The trees are more disperse in this area, opening room for a richer and more diverse undergrowth. Especially prevalent are the tall, leafy ferns that crowd around the thick trunks. Light filters in through the canopy of leaves, casting whimsical patterns on the ground. Only at dusk, however, does the forest show all its splendour when the waning light falls slanting over the treetops and orange glints shimmer on the rims of the leaves.
8868: The forest here thins, making way for some small bushes. The trees seem younger, about twice as tall as an adult human, and the bushes bear small red berries when in season. The foliage all around is thick and dark green in colour. Resilient branches and leaves that snap back when pushed aside, creating a confusing flurry, must slow travellers to these parts. A few hack marks made in the plants to clear a path seems to have had no effect. The leaves are ever growing and new leaves quickly replace the ones cut away.
8869: In these borderlands between the forest and the vast open plains there still grows an occasional tree among the small bushes and sturdy grasses. Westwards the trees grow denser, while in all other directions the forest completely vanishes.
8870: From the looks of it this field was once fertile and lush with wheat; now almost everything has withered away. Stalks of wheat lay clumped in piles on the ground, slowly decomposing into the earth. Not far to the north is a bend where the river turns and makes its way eastward. A dark forest looms across the field a ways to the west.
8871: A few solemn, scattered trees stand among the bushes and grasses in this area. Like silent sentinels they seem to keep an ever vigilant watch for some unknown menace, as if they were scouts or guardians of the forest that grows a short distance to the north-west. Eastwards the plains open up as the Vale of the Anduin gradually unfolds in front of you.
8872: The land declines gently towards the east where a healthy, leafy brushwood grows. The vegetation here is short, consisting mostly of grass with a few small shrubs. The rising terrain to the west appears quite harsh while the eastern and southern lands are more fertile.
8873: A brown fox is here, looking for some rabbits to chew up.

Young slender trees slowly grow here, replacing those that were cut down in the distant past. The soil is soft and nutritious offering a hospitable substratum for the growing vegetation. The terrain southward seems to also be a former habitat of trees and now contains many young saplings.
8874: Several bountiful bushes cover this smooth region which has many kinds of plants. The smaller plants, however, are left in the shadow of the bigger ones and thus they struggle for life. Most of the soil appears quite fertile.
8875: The ground here is filled with small bushes of a strange species. This type of bush seems to grow only in this area for some mysterious reason. There are no animal tracks in this area as if they shun these strange bushes and their slimy, long reaching leaves. In a few places near the bushes some bones of small animals are visible.
8876: The ambience of this clearing is very mysterious, with a strange mist rising from the hollow lying to the south. The ground here is muddy and provides uneven footing for travellers. A few puddles of water are scattered about. The horizon is largely obscured by a strange mist.
8877: This is the border of a tremendous vale which opens to the east. The ground here is covered with short grass and some bushes which are spread out across the grass. The edge of the valley continues to the north while to the south there is a vast plain covered by hay. A clearing lies cloaked in haze westward of here.
8878: The plain is covered with short grass and a few small bushes. The ground declines smoothly eastward where it joins a large valley filled with wildly growing plants. Westward a mysterious mist rises from a large, strange looking hollow that is covered with thick bushes.
8879:
A slender plant grows here, with clusters of tiny pink flowers atop its stem.
A small rabbit glares angrily at you.

The vegetation in this bountiful valley is very luxuriant and bears a rich growth of plants during the warm months of late spring and early summer. Land such as this forms the perfect environment for plant eaters and the animals that feed on them. The tracks of several animals are visible as well as a few small bones.
8880: A clear spring babbles as cool water trickles out of the ground.

The ground slopes gently around this tranquil spring where the crystal-clear water slowly trickles out of the ground. The water, no more than two feet deep, has collected around the spring forming a small pond. The bottom of the pond is covered with fine sand and a few snails. The lands surrounding the spring are flourishing with both plant and animal life and the singing of birds can be heard for many miles.
8881: Rampantly growing weeds and rotting crops have taken over this dormant land which was once cultivated but nowadays is untended. What became of the farmer that once farmed this land is unknown. A flimsy-looking hut stands along the northern edge of the field and apparently was the home of the farmer.
8882: Various sized bushes, most of them looking quite luxuriant, fill the valley. The soil is smooth and very soft, it readily absorbs the tracks of animals, both large and small, on its surface. An untended farm field is located westward next to a small hut. North of here the valley becomes lifeless.
8883: Bushes of various sizes cling to the steep slope that rises upwards to the east. Nearby to the west is a valley filled with bushes, beyond it are grasslands over which the Misty Mountains loom.
8884:
A slender plant grows here, with clusters of tiny pink flowers atop its stem.
A red-furred doe wanders peacefully among the grass.
A reddish fawn romps harmlessly among the tender grass shoots.

In this small valley the grass that dominates the lands to the east is broken up by large bushes growing in densely packed clumps. The clumps of bushes grow more numerous to the west and to the north a bush covered slope can be seen.
8885: A sharp incline rises up from the flat surface of the southern fields. East of here the slant is somewhat shallower, while to the north it appears more treacherous and steep. A few small plants sprout out of the incline among the generally uninterrupted blades of grass.
8886: Lush green grass grows lightly on this small slope. The slightest breeze makes the long grass sway in waves along the ground. A few sparse elms grow here, multiplying towards the north and northwest. The slant of the slope is equal in the easterly and westerly directions.
8887: Covering most of this small hill are bushes of various types. Solid rock shows through spots on the mainly grass-covered southern slope of this hill. To the south lies the edge of a drop into an old quarry.
8888: The earth here is gravelly, with matted-down grass growing on it. Clusters of foot-high bushes dot the surrounding area. To the east there is a steep embankment leading down to the river Anduin and to the north and west the terrain rises.
8889: A tall stag is here, grazing peacefully.

Rocks ranging in size from pebbles to fist-sized stones are scattered across the ground. The land declines into the Anduin River east of here where the stones continue and have been smoothed by the constant flow over them. To the west there is an old quarry, while south and north of here there are no distinctive landmarks.
8890: The water of the Anduin River is quite clear and the sandy bottom is visible although it is far below. It appears that the river begins to lose some of its depth as it flows south and deepens towards the north. There is short grass and small plants thriving on the river's edge but only trees grow on the eastern bank.
8891: Elms by a Bend in the Anduin River

Elm trees of various sizes grow away from the bank of the river. Closer by the trees give way to bushes of mixed varieties. The grass is high and deep- green in colour. Flowers of various colours grow around the base of the elm trees and in patches between them. South of here some ancient ruins can be seen.
8892: A colony of red ants is here. The ants seem to ignore you.

The remains of what appears to be a razed stone shed are lying about in the grass here. Grass and bushes grow amongst the old stones, with some moss growing on the stones. To the west, some trees can be seen and to the east there is a vale inside the fields.
8893: A detached white rose is lying here.

Small stone walls split the grassland here. The walls stand at several places in the field and saxifrages grow among the stones. Old hurdle poles covered with wild roses were placed in this grassland as well. To the west is an old ruined building.
8894:
A large beautiful rose bush is blooming here.
Deep inside the bush, there are two red roses with leaves and thorny stems.
This open vale spreads out north and west. To the east the land climbs up a grassy ridge, and a dark clump of trees can be seen to the south. Some wild roses grow in this vale.
8895: A lonely, large oak tree is standing here in this vale, surrounded by grass and purple flowers. To the north and south the vale continues. There appears to be a ridge rising from the fields to the east.
8896: The ridge stretches in a north-south direction and is covered by grass and rocks of different shapes and sizes. A few scattered elms grow on top of this ridge. To the south, the ridge appears to come to a gradual end, but it continues to the north. West of the ridge a vale sits in the middle of the fields. A trail runs along the length of the ridge.
8897:
A salmon swims here.
A bass swims here.

Flowing in from the east and curving back towards the south, the water here flows swiftly and at times overflows the riverbanks. Low shrubs and various greenery spreads in great masses along the sides of the river. Distant, but looming, in the west are the Misty Mountains.
8898: Throughout this small area bordering the Anduin River there is a thin, light grass growing; however, near the edges of the river, it sprouts somewhat thicker. Shorter plants and some small trees hang over the river. To the northwest some grassy fields rise.
8899: The current of the Anduin runs quickly here; the water is so deep and murky that the bottom is not visible. Branches, leaves, and roots hang limply from the trees and bushes into the water. Some longer, weed-like growths wave back and forth in the water, played with by the current.
8901: A Tributary Meets the Anduin River

A river from the west of here flows into the Anduin at this point, stirring up mud from the riverbed and causing the water to foam from the competing currents. The land to the north is constantly flooded by water from the rivers around it. There is a heavy concentration of rocks and boulders in the water here.
8902: A dun-coloured grouse is sitting still in the heather.

Out of the muddy ground here grows thick, dark-green grass. Short vegetation grows sparsely here, becoming denser towards the west, south, and east, where the sound of rushing water comes from. Towards the north, the grass begins to lengthen and it covers the ground completely.
8903: This portion of the river flows rapidly over its uneven bed of pebbles and larger rocks. As the water follows along its course here, it bends toward the south. Some of the water overflows the eastern bank to flood onto the grass east of here.
8904: The Anduin River flows calmly along, its current slow but steady on its way to the distant south. Grassy fields stretch from the river's edge outwards on both its east and west banks. The riverbed is littered with tiny pebbles and sand, colouring it beige and helping to camouflage its inhabitants.
8905: The river flows into here from the east and then turns southward. Long grass from the western side dips over the edge of the bank and hangs into the water where the current plays with it. The river depth appears constant along this stretch, but the pace slows as it curves southwards.
8906: Marshy Riverbank along the Anduin River

A restless rabbit bounces around.
Some ugly blow-flies are buzzing around here.

The riverbank here is mostly marshy, with expanses of lichens and moss lying scattered around. Many pebbles have been washed ashore by the rapid pace of the rushing waters as the Anduin River continues its journey, heading into the southern plains. A vast array of plains and fields lie settled over the western landscape and an endless quantity of grassland covers the land to the north-west.
8907: The river slowly finds its way between the sloping grounds both to the east and west, and can be seen bending to the right further ahead. Lush plains at the east bank seem to continue for a few miles before rising slopes hide the grassland beyond them from your view. Several willows lining the other shore are bent low over the flow.
8908: As the unstoppable flow of the Great River completes one more of its slow, countless bends, it takes up once again its main course towards the distant south, in its endless way through the green grasslands of the Anduin Vale. High and immutable tower the Misty Mountains to the west, like a row of heavy stone sentinels; but many brooks rise also in their snowy peaks, tributary of the greatest of Middle-earth's rivers.
8909:
A ferocious warg is here, snarling angrily.
A hungry warg stands here, sniffing around for flesh.

This narrow spit of earth, no more than a couple miles in width, stretches out between the courses of two water streams. On the one hand flows the mighty Anduin, taking a wide bend from east to south. On the other, a swift stream comes swirling down the mountains, and bathes the northern bank before rushing into the Great River. Soaked in water, the ground looks fertile indeed, and vegetation grows luxuriant.
8910: The Anduin bends between the plains on both sides of it. The flow is slowing down again, after having broken out of the narrow bed to the north, and once again the stream is taking up all its width. The river is still deep, but you can guess, more than actually see, a rock-strewn bottom from the many eddies. There is no sign of a fordable section anywhere nearby.
8912: A narrowing strip of land is squeezed between the River Anduin and a fast flowing stream to the south and west. A number of ancient-looking willows bend over the river, with their silvery leaves touching the waters. On the opposite bank, a lone high rock can be seen, towering menacingly above the flow.
8913: Here the stream takes its final turn, avoiding a low willow-lined peninsula, before joining the flow of the Anduin a few miles ahead. Northwards, the ground rises steeply to a promontory, the slope covered by low bushes and a few trees. Further south, the ground is perfectly flat and covered with tall grass that flows in the wind.
8914: The mighty Anduin continues its way towards the Great Sea. As the riverbed is becoming deeper, the flow strengthens. To the south, a lone high rock can be seen breaking the flow of waters. Overlooking the wide river, you can see a vast green prairie stretching out towards the horizon, with only a few low, lonely hillocks rising from the flat ground.
8915: A swallow flies high above the ground.

The flow of the waters to the west has been stopped by a steep slope, rising almost vertically for more than fifteen feet and forcing the river to bend southwards yet again. The other bank is lower and should lend itself to an easy landing. Grasslands seem to continue all the way to the horizon over there.
8916:
A fat rabbit sits here, chewing on some grass.
The rabid rabbit is here, frothing at the mouth.
A swallow flies high above the ground.

The western plains slowly descend until lining the Anduin with a narrow strip of white sand. On the other side of the river, barely visible from here, the flat ground stretches out all the way to the horizon, covered in lush green grasslands. Only a few lonely hillocks, no more than a few feet high, rise out of the seemingly endless plains there.
8917: The plateau narrows into a steep promontory overlooking the lush valley below, fed by a fast-flowing stream. To the west, the rocky ground drops vertically into a series of roaring rapids pounding its walls. Across the stream, south-west, a tall and lonely tree is standing atop the hill, its trunk split by lightning.
8918: The stream gets squeezed into a narrow canyon between towering stone walls on both sides, forcing its waters higher and faster. Several sharp cliffs are breaking the flow, the sound of water rushing past the boulders can be heard hundreds of yards away. Southwards, the stream can be seen bending left in a short while, looking a great deal more peaceful than here.
8919: The northern plateau comes to an abrupt stop here, with a vertical cliff-face dropping some twenty feet to a roaring chute below. The air is misty from droplets of water thrown all the way up here by the flow of water hitting boulders and canyon walls with abominable force. North-east, a battered stony ridge can be seen running through the land, splitting it into a higher barren plateau and lower sloping grasslands.
8920: The barren image of northern grasslands changes is it is slightly enlivened by a stream flowing south of here. Several bushes dot the landscape, and even the grass is a lot taller and greener than those that can be seen farther away. To the east, the stream has cut a gorge into a ridge running through the grasslands, a few miles away from here.
8921: The stream continues to travel calmly along the plains of the surrounding landscape. The water appears to get slightly deeper and an increase of the fish inhabitants is more noticeable near the centre of the stream. Plains can be seen to the east and west of you which seem very fertile given off by the presence of the lively green grasslands.
8922: The stream seems to get slightly larger as it travels southward heading into what one would predict to be a greater mass of water. The calmness of the stream allows one to easily navigate back and forth through the waters and onto the stream's shores. In the distance to the north lies many great plains in the endless landscape. Small fish can be seen trying to swim along with the small current of the stream water.
8923: The terrain here can be seen quickly ascending as it begins to stretch towards the stream nearby. A few yards away, it levels off into a small terrace that forms a viewpoint from which anyone could easily make simple observations. Heading towards the small terrace, you can overlook the stream and glance at the vast grasslands that encompass the surrounding land. A small crumbling building can be seen in the distance to the south.
8924:
A salmon swims here.
A large sturgeon swims slowly along the bottom.

As the stream continues to flow eastward the pace of the water ever so slightly speeds up as it bends to the south. As you go further along the small stream the water level seems to get deeper, contouring to the earth's natural sloping nature. An old crumbling building can be seen in the far distance to the south, but gives off the impression of vacancy set by its rotting wooden structure and its mossy covered walls.
8925: A tall pine tree grows here.

A lonely majestic pine tree dominates the landscape, looking over the sloping grassland spreading in all directions. West of here, the ground descends steeply towards the valley, at the bottom of which a shallow but moderately paced stream is flowing. The sandy ground is covered by many pine-needles and several cones shed from tall but growing trees.
8926: A Stream through a Lush Valley

As the ground starts rising steeply eastwards the stream bends to the right, finding its way to the bottom of the fertile valley. Few pines dot the landscape and the grass is tall here, unlike up on the plains where it is beaten and bent by a constant wind. Although the stream is rather narrow, the water is swift-flowing and fording it can prove more difficult than it might initially look.
8927: A small rabbit glares angrily at you.

The ground is rising eastwards, to form a small hillock just about a mile away from here. The vegetation seems to grow thicker in that direction, but here it is just an odd bush among the wind-beaten grass. A wide river can be seen flowing further to the east, with the opposite bank barely more than a line at the horizon. To the west, a steep incline climbs to a rocky plateau. In all other directions, sloping plains with a sea of tall grass flowing in the wind covering them continue as far as an eye can see.
8928:
A great black and silver wolf is standing here, at the head of the pack.
A huge, black wolf is here, ready to devour.
A grey wolf is here, salivating profusely.
A grey wolf is here, salivating profusely.
A large rabbit looks peacefully at you, ready to dart away.

Thick grass grows up to the waist-level of an average man here, flowing in eerie waves in the relentless winds. Several unmistakable signs indicate that this place has been a ground for a fierce battle sometime in the past. Occasional cracked skulls, both orkish and those of men, bleached white by sun and rains are lying around, half-hidden among the grass and the carcasses of horses and wargs. Broken spears and swords alongside battered pieces of armour dot the ground, slowly being overtaken by fast-growing grass which is well nourished by the blood that has been shed here.
8929: Some small rocks have been piled into a mound here.

Several sharp rocks and boulders rise from waist-tall grass here, with low and wind-bent bushes growing in their shadow, seeking a shelter from the wind. Southwards, the grass becomes lower, and in a couple of miles, the fields descend into a wide river, cutting through seemingly endless grass- lands that continue in every direction. Few rain-polished rib cages of horses, almost hidden in the tall grass, betoken a distant battle that has been fought here. A prominent mound of rocks, covered with moss and small bushes, suggests that someone important has fallen here.
8930: The River Anduin beside the Carrock
A swallow flies high above the ground.

The main branch of the river continues on its way south as it runs past a huge rock standing near the eastern bank. The flow is now faster, and the swirling waters give hint of the treacherous boulders that lie on the riverbed. A swift tributary stream comes from the west, leaving a small peninsula behind. On the east, a sheer wall of wet rock plummets down into the troubled waters.
8931: The river widens again after having run past the lone high rock to the north. The stream is still swift, and the air is filled with a vapour of water. Lush plains on the western bank slope upwards steeply, hiding the tops of the Misty Mountains from view. To the east, small hillocks rise out of the sloping ground, higher and higher the further from the river.
8932: Plains start to descend steeply towards the river, with the actual riverbank standing several feet high above the steadily flowing waters, making their way between some rather vicious-looking sharp rocks and boulders near the bank. Overlooking the river, sloping plains go on as far as the eye can see, and are framed by the snow-covered tops of the Misty Mountains beyond the western skyline.
8933: The plains start rising steeply, away from the Anduin Valley to the west. From here, you can see the river cutting through the landscape and grasslands, disappearing eventually between the hills of the southern plains. To the north you spot a lone rock standing tall above the flow of the Anduin a few miles away. Over the slopes and valleys to the west, the tops of the Misty Mountains frame the view.
8934: Grass grows among the scattered pebbles that dot the ground. A small but distinct animal trail cuts through the green grass here. It avoids the larger rocks which gives the trail a serpentine look. Far to the north a lone rock can be seen and rising to the southwest there appears to be a mound of stones.
8935: The wild ox seems ready to charge you.

The bushes here somewhat break the monotony of the grass that covers this land. The bushes are of various sizes, some with branches as thick as a hobbit's arm. There appear to be quite a few rabbits here considering all the piles of sand that rise from the ground among the bushes. To the west is a mound of stones.
8936: The plains here are completely overgrown with dense brush of all kinds, some short, some tall, some sporting colourful flowers between sharp thorns. Nature is thus - amidst the ugly one may find beauty. Among the top branches small birds have made their nests and can sometimes be seen trying to hide, looking for food or even singing now and then. To the south is a hillock amongst the fields.
8937: A small rabbit glares angrily at you.

Among the various bushes on the sides of this hill lie scattered moss-covered boulders. An animal track circumvents the rocks with the western end seeming to lead to a tarn that can be sighted through the bushes there.
8938: The tall grasses that grow here are of many varieties, some with thin and seemingly brittle blades, some more robust with deep, rich colour. To the south the fields seem to have been cultivated by man due to the rich earth there. To the east, the land dips into a slight depression.
8939: Here, on the eastern slope of a ridge, the people of the village have planted a field of turnips. The land appears to be quite well tended from the lack of weeds among the turnip crop. West of here stands a wooden palisade.
8940:
A well-fed cow stands here chewing her cud listlessly.
A well-fed cow stands here chewing her cud listlessly.
A small rabbit glares angrily at you.

Clover grows in huge patches here with lush, green grass covering the rest of the pasture. The pasture is a paradise for the cattle the men of the village are breeding. Northwest of here, in the plains, lies the village that owns this pasture. To the west is a grassy ridge amidst the fields.
8941: This semi-cultivated field lies directly north of the village palisade. All sorts of bushes and grasses and plants grow in this field. Deciding which have been planted by man and are edible, and which are wild is difficult at best, but clearly the inhabitants of this land would know.
8942: Embraced by green grass and small bushes a small tarn lies in the middle of this widespread field. The water of the tarn is brown but by the amount of animal tracks that can be seen in the mud bordering it this is a very well-used waterhole.
8943: On these bushy plains large rocks and boulders lie strewn about as if they had been thrown by giants. A more reasonable explanation would be that they fell or slid from the mound of stones that can be seen to the north, as the mound does not appear to have been tended for quite some time. Between the stones grows grass with many beautiful flowers peeping out from it, adding a colour to the otherwise green and grey landscape. To the far south one can spot a palisade, while to the west, in the distance, the Anduin River lies.
8944: Stones and boulders of different shapes and sizes have been piled into a large stone mound here. The stones, that are not covered with greyish moss, appear to be well weathered and give hints as to how ancient this mound is and how long ago it was created.
8945: The twisting Anduin River that rushes southwards to the west of here has flooded these grasslands, making the ground muddy with patches of water. Tracks can easily be seen in the mud when something passes through. South of here, stones of varying sizes have been piled into a high mound.
8946: A small animal, all covered in spines, snuffles amongst the undergrowth.

The plains are descending to the river, which is bending directly west of here and continuing towards the horizon through the southern plains as far as an eye can see. Eastwards, the ground is becoming more and more hilly as it rises slowly. Far beyond those hillocks, the outskirts of Mirkwood must lie.
8947: The river makes a gracious curve westwards, only to bend south again within a couple of miles further down the flow, and continue its endless journey through the borders of Rohan all the way to the salty waters of the Great Sea. On both banks, sloping grasslands roll on seemingly forever, with the snowy peaks of the Misty Mountains barely more than a thin white stripe at the western horizon.
8948: The Anduin River flows from the north and then curves toward the west. Dark- green, long grass grows from the edges of the south and east sides of the river into the distance. The water is clear as crystal, and the river bottom is far below the surface.
8949: The ground here is very sandy where not covered by grass or the large number of rocks and boulders here. Long, dark-green grass begins at the edge of the river, that flows west of here, and continues to the mound that sits to the east.
8950: The sandy shore gently declines into the Anduin river that flows to the west of here. Some lonely holly bushes are growing in the sand along with the occasional patch of long, dark grass.
8951: The soil is mainly of a sandy constitution, and thus only certain varieties of grass grow here - long, pale greyish-blue stalks that rattle stiffly when the wind blows. Among these grasses live small animals that scurry around looking for food and materials to build their nests and hollows. To the west the great Anduin river swiftly and strongly flows on its voyage to the sea.
8952: A large thorny branched shrub is growing here.

The grass does not dominate the landscape here like in many of the areas nearby. Blackberry bushes grow everywhere here, to the pleasure of the birds that come here for them. A small trail runs among the bushes giving a hint that not only birds travel to here for food, but that people from the village also come here for the berries.
8953: This grass-covered section of the vale extends into the south where a large lonely tree can be seen above the tall grass. A large wooden palisade made of long logs makes it impossible to go farther east here.
8954: A fishing rod has been left here.

A small boat ramp leads down into the mighty Anduin River flowing west of here. There are three small sheds built around a campfire site. The ground is trampled, giving a hint that this area is used frequently by some group of people in the Vale. A few elm trees grow along the bank of the river.
8955: The Anduin River flows smoothly from the north and abruptly bends to the west. Along the eastern edge of the river a few elm trees grow amongst tall and wavy grass. The river bottom is sandy and littered with small stones and pebbles, but their shapes and sizes are somewhat distorted by the water's depth.
8956: Oak trees of various sizes are growing on this side of the Anduin River. The branches of the bigger oaks that grow close to the shore hang over the river like long fingers. The ground is covered with old, dead leaves from the trees.
8957: Fields by a Bend in the River

The small oak saplings growing here are likely seedlings of the older oak trees that can be seen to the south. North and west of here the mighty Anduin river flows by. To the east there are no trees, only grasses.
8958: The water here flows smoothly as it comes from the north and bends towards the west. Long grass grows in patches to the east of the river, and thrives to the south. The slightly rocky and sandy river bottom does not appear to be far away, however the water is far too deep for one to stand in.
8959: A green frog is here, hopping around.

The ground here is rich with moist soil caused by the rushing water of the Anduin River, which lies to the east. Much of the land here has survived, rich with nutrients but poor in cultivation, with the help of the nearby water source. Pebbles have been washed up ashore with the rapid pace of the rushing waters as the Anduin River continues its journey heading in the south and seems endless from this view point.
8960: As the land approaches the course of two water streams, the grasslands of this area have become more dense and less sparse. To the east are many thick patches of grass and shrubs as you draw near the Anduin River. The land almost resembles a carpet of grassland similar to the terrain to the west. Further to the south lie more plains of small weeds that can be seen sprouting up where the ground has ruptured in many places.
8961:
A huge warg is here, moving in for the kill.
A huge warg is here, moving in for the kill.
A small grasshopper clings to a blade of grass, ready to spring.

The ground is higher here and provides a good vantage point for viewing the surrounding plains. A small but swiftly flowing stream runs at the bottom of the valley north and west of here, it's water seems to support the lush vegetation that contrasts with the otherwise barren lands around it. A tall and majestic lonely oak grows atop the hill, it's crown shattered by a strike of lightning. On closer examination, several very deep and scary-looking claw marks can be seen in the thick bark of the old tree.
8962: The stream leaves the valley bed here and flows eastward, towards the Anduin that can already be seen from here. An unusual-looking lonely rock towers on the other side of the river. A barely noticeable track follows the streamside through the plains and heads straight up the hill to the west, atop of which a lone lightning-struck oak tree stands.
8963: The stream follows the valley rim and bends sharply eastwards. To the south, at the top of the hill, a lonely and menacing, lightning-shattered tree towers above the plains and sloping hills around. Remnants of old campsites suggest that someone has been finding a shelter here in the not too distant past.
8964: The ridge sharply breaks right north of here into a steep-walled valley, at the bottom of which a narrow but turbulent stream flows its way eastwards, to eventually join the River Anduin in the distance. The ridge continues on the other side of it, separating the higher barren plateau from greener grasslands, as it runs in almost straight line north-east through the vast plains.
8965: A peaceful stream, almost the size of a small river, cuts east-west through the barren plain. The waterfront is lined with low bushes, about the only kind of vegetation around as far as the eye can see. The relative calm of the stream seems to be changing in a short distance to the east, where a cloud of vapour hangs above the foamy waters. A loud rumbling sound can be heard from there, as the water descends into a narrow gorge between steep cliff walls on both sides, towering more than twenty feet above the flow.
8966: As the grasslands reach to this area of the landscape, they scatter more sparsely if you continue in all directions. Walking further east will only lead you into a valley rich in vegetation and plant life. Looking further east is a flowing river large in length and abundant in water. The landscape here is rather uneven and has a definite slope down to the east.
8967: The surrounding land is occupied by open, steppe-like vegetation of perennial bunch grasses, with flowering culms that rise several yards high. Most growth and flowering occurs during late spring and early summer. The plants are dormant in winter and mostly dormant in late summer and fall. The Great River Anduin can be seen in the distance to the east. More fields of grass stretch outwards to the west and a large area of plains to the south.
8968: Distinct from the surrounding landscape to the north-west, you can notice the transition of widely dense grasslands to slowly disbursed plains of shrubs and patches of grass. This lively land can be seen to come to an end as you peer off into the easternmost direction, spotting the River Anduin. The great river continues to flow to the south in a rapid pace extending to the uttermost distance as far as the eye can see.
8969: The Anduin River has had a great impact on the surrounding land. The soil has become very marshy with its many shrubs, moss and lichens that grow out from the ruptured ground. The Great River extends in the far distance to the south and continues to flow as far as the eye can see. Large lily pads near the water's shore indicate a form of wildlife such as frogs or toads. Other forms of life can be observed such as the swarms of insects that can be seen on the edge near the riverbank of the river.
8970:
A dun-coloured grouse is sitting still in the heather.
A dun-coloured grouse is sitting still in the heather.

Small, misshapen pine trees are scattered about the quagmire. Among grass grows an occasional clump of bulrushes. There is a constant buzz from the insects that swarm here when conditions are right. To the east, the mighty Anduin River flows on its way south.
8971:
A swarm of mosquitoes is here, humming around you.
A swarm of mosquitoes is here, humming around you.

Stunted pine trees grow in this quagmire, which marks the edge of the river to the west. Along the water a compact wall of bullrushes sways with even the slightest of winds. On the ground some wood-grouse droppings can be seen among the cloud-berry bushes that stand above the grass.
8972: The river flowing along here from the west eventually reaches a bend and diverts toward the south. The bottom of the river is muddy, which provides nutrients for underwater plants, but clouds the water.
8973: A large beaver is here, gnawing on a piece of wood.

The river here deepens as it flows in from the north and slowly bends toward the east. The edges of the river are green with vegetation that lives off the river and the nutrients it carries. Moving eastwards the river begins to flow faster as it travels over a riverbed made of stones and rock.
8974: A small cluster of clover grows here.

Mixed with the thick green grass are many small white and pink clover flowers. The clover grows in dense clumps throughout the field giving the land a spotted appearance. In the eastern part of the field, there are some jagged rocks that stick up from the ground like sharp teeth. Both to north and east the sound of running water can be heard and to the south a gentle slope can be seen.
8975: A large beaver is here, gnawing on a piece of wood.

The river here runs a twisted route from the north into here, then flowing out to the east on its way to the Anduin River. The water churns and foams as a result of numerous mid-size rocks standing in the way of the rushing current of the river.
8976: A brown fox is here, looking for some rabbits to chew up.

Short grass grows here with a border of riverside plants along the banks of the Anduin River to the east. Little life appears in this sparsely covered area near the river. This region continues in much the same way towards the south. The field begins to incline upwards in the west.
8977: A fat rabbit is here, chewing on some grass.

The ground here continually rises towards the north, and declines southwards. The grass grows uniformly, hiding from view many small dips and ditches that litter the slope. Eastward the incline is gentler, while the decline to the west is the same as here.
8978: A small animal, all covered in spines, snuffles amongst the undergrowth.

This grassy slope is only slightly elevated from the grasslands to the east and north. Small flowers sprout in little patches throughout the soft, ankle-deep grass. In the westerly direction distant trees interrupt the normal horizon which is dominated in the other directions by low growing plants.
8979: Ancient willow trees, their trunks withered by age, grow here in a straight north-south line. They were planted like this a long time ago to act as a windbreak that would prevent fertile soil from being blown away by the wind. Amongst the green grasses are golden coloured wild oats which add a lush look to the field.
8980: Several towering elms grow widely spaced on this easy slope. However, aside from the immediate area around here, there are no trees to be seen in the distance. The entire slope is uniformly covered with thick grass, which continues in all directions.
8981: A large mother hawk is here looking for a prey to feed her young.

This slope, which is lightly covered by bushes, declines steeply to the west, and ascends to the east. Some sparse elm trees grow straight into the sky in spite of the steep slant to this hill. Many of the elms' huge, thick roots can be seen sticking from the soil. The slope is just as steep southwards as it is here, but to the slope to the north appears to be gentler.
8982: A brown fox is here, looking for some rabbits to chew up.

The land here appears to be quite dry and therefore it is hard for the larger plants to thrive. Grass and a few thorn bushes manage to grow here. In the dry grass an animal trail can been seen passing through to the north and south.
8983:
A fat rabbit sits here, chewing on some grass.
The wild ox seems ready to charge you.

This flat area is covered with two varieties of grasses. In the southern part of the field the grass is short and stumpy and has a yellowish colour, whereas along the northern edge the grass is green and tall. To the south the land rises up away from the sound of running water that comes from the north.
8984: A large beaver is here, gnawing on a piece of wood.

The flow of water over the underwater plants causes them to wave around and stir up the muddy bottom of this river, removing any transparency it might have had. Aside from the plant-life within the river itself, only plants on the surrounding edges drink from the water to support themselves. Beyond that margin of plants, larger plants cannot survive.
8985: Barren Plains along a Shallow Stream
A swarm of midges is here, humming around you.

Not much life is able to thrive here within the confined area dictated by the small stream and the dry path which you walk along. There are, however, a few trees and other forms of vegetation that can be seen within close distance. A small stream with muddy and shallow shores can be made out to the south and running waters can be observed heading in the eastern direction.
8986: The ground beneath you is somewhat hard and lifeless in this area. To the east are more plains like the one around you now and to the south is a small river, which from this distance looks rather brown and muddy. To the west is an old crop field which would have supported some bountiful crops but due to the lack of upkeep, it has just withered away like most of the land to the west.
8987:
A ferocious warg is here, snarling angrily.
A hungry warg stands here, sniffing around for flesh.

There are some small patches of grass extending from the northern fields. If you stare off to the west you can see the remains of a small hut. Everything else around is very lifeless and mostly plains. Travelling to the east or south would be more manageable due to the somewhat flat terrain heading off in that direction.
8988: Treacherous Cliff along a Steep Ridge

The ground here is very unstable and will give way at any time if one were to stand around for a long period of time. Navigating your way down the cliff will only lead to injury if not well experienced in climbing high cliffs. The narrow ridge seems to continue along in the north direction and looks less treacherous and more stable the further north you go.
8989: Grassy Fields along a Steep Ridge

An experienced orkish scout is looking for tracks on the ground.
An experienced orkish scout is looking for tracks on the ground.
A small grasshopper clings to a blade of grass, ready to spring.

The ground here is more stable than it is to the south. There is a thick carpet of grass all around you. To the west you can see more fields of wild plant life, while to the east drops a steep cliff followed by a vast expanse of plains. You can sense the grass shifting during every sudden movement, probably caused by the many insects jumping around within the fields. Looking to the far distance of the north you can spot an outline of a decaying house structure.
8990: Grazing Fields along a Ridge on a Low Hill

A small grasshopper clings to a blade of grass, ready to spring.
A huge grizzly bear is here, roaming the wild.
A grizzly cub is here, snarling loudly.
A grizzly cub is here, snarling loudly.

With the land more stable around here than further south, an endless amount of grassland has grown with the flourishing soil. Large carpets of flowers are noticeable in this area, along with tall weeds and short grass patches. To the north is a huge wooden fence, forming the shape of an animal pen, that surrounds an old and decaying barn. The only access for getting inside that pen would be to walk around to the front entrance which would take some effort considering the descending hill before the entrance.
8991:
The starving cow stands here looking for a patch of grass.
A brown cow is here, contemplating a higher reality whilst chewing slowly.

The large pasture stretches for a few miles along each side with an extensive and unbroken fence surrounding the pastured land. There is a gate to the north that opens and allows access out of the barn's fenced pasture. What would seem to have supported many cows once long ago is now home to only a few inhabiting cows that remain living throughout the many years of neglect by their previous owners. The soil still maintains some nutrients enabling some cow life to live day after day, yet given some time as the years pass by and if continuing at the same rate, will become lifeless and inanimate.
8992: Path Leading to a Ruined Farm House

Following the ground closely, a distinguished path can be recognized leading into what seems like a rundown old farm house to the east. Even though the size of the property might appear to be rather large, the inhabitants of this building have long since left the land to decay naturally. A cow pasture with a large and extensive fence can be viewed to the south that has restricted the movement of the remaining cattle, which survived throughout the years that have passed.
8993: Damp Plains along a Small Stream

Walking carefully on the damp terrain you notice your feet half submerged into the earth. Given the slight slope of the small stream's shore bank, one could easily slip and fall into the ever so peaceful water flow. Given time and age, the landscape here could very well become a marshy swampland inhabited by moss and fungi. The patches of grass beneath your feet are very limp and hung over, caused by the nearby water source.
8994:
A salmon swims here.
The prominent fin of a silver-yellow fish breaks the surface of the water.
The prominent fin of a silver-yellow fish breaks the surface of the water.
A bass swims here.
A large sturgeon swims slowly along the bottom.
A salmon swims here.
A trout swims here.
A bass swims here.

The hilly ground to the west gives way to sloping plains that seem to be rolling for miles and miles towards the Anduin in the east.
