The vegetation is becoming thinner, and only a few sparse pines remain from the forests further up the hills. A narrow but fast-flowing stream is coming from the mountains and finds its way towards the river, zigzagging through the grasslands.
8995:
A bass swims here.
The prominent fin of a silver-yellow fish breaks the surface of the water.

A small rivulet follows the bottom of the valley and heads away from the rising slope eastwards, atop of which an old decaying structure can be seen in the distance. The large structure to the south looks rundown as if not taken care of for several years. The south bank appears to have been cultivated in the past, but now it is fast overgrowing with tall grass and young bushes.
8996: Vegetation grows scarcely on the exposed surface of the plateau. Only stunted scrub and small, twisted bushes with prickles all over can survive here, half-hidden among the rocks. The ground is mostly ash-coloured, like the stone that forms it. Many cracks and chinks run along its surface, although not wide nor deep enough as to make a real obstacle to your advance. The plateau comes to a sudden end to the east, as a steep slope leads into the fields below.
8997: A large rabbit looks peacefully at you, ready to dart away.

The plains are slowly rising towards the west, from lush riverside meadows into higher and bleaker grasslands, exposed to cold winds from the Misty Mountains. The slope is seemingly growing steeper still further down south, for in a couple of miles it can be seen breaking into a ridge, separating the wide berth of Anduin from the first foothills of mountains far away.
8998:
A great black and silver wolf is standing here, at the head of the pack.
A huge, black wolf is here, ready to devour.
A grey wolf is here, salivating profusely.
A grey wolf is here, salivating profusely.

A ridge, almost fifteen feet high, rises from the sea of waist-high grass. It is crumbled in places, which makes it possible to ascend to the higher plateau behind its edge. Boulders, apparently broken lose from the stony wall, lie scattered around, surrounded by low and wind-bent bushes.
8999: The rabid rabbit is here, frothing at the mouth.

Western slopes begin to level here, with ground slowly descending towards a majestic wide river, a further few hours' walk away. Although still exposed to the elements, the landscape isn't quite as barren the closer one gets to the Anduin. In addition to low bushes, some trees dot the land, and several groves of trees that appear to be willows can be seen further east and south, lining this bank of the River Anduin.
9000: A swallow flies high above the ground.

The western grasslands come to an abrupt halt here, with the ground falling almost vertically for some fifteen feet towards the Anduin flowing directly east of here. Southwards, the ground declines more smoothly and leads to a small, willow-lined peninsula between the Anduin and a smaller river which is apparently fed by many small mountain streams from the Misty Mountains. Across the river, plains seem to go on forever.
9001: A fat rabbit is here, chewing on some grass.

A worn-out stony ridge runs through the grasslands, with rubble and broken boulders crumbling from its steep face, making it possible to climb it with a little care and some effort. Eastwards, gently sloping grasslands continue for several miles, and terminate by a wide river.
9002: A gravelly film of grey dust slides along the worn surface of the ground, pushed by a wind that seems to never stop blowing here. Particles of rock, and even small pebbles, are carried away, swept by the air, until they crush into a larger stone, or disappear into dark crevices. The sound of the grain grazing the earth spreads all over the plateau, merging with the howl of the wind.
9003: A Crag in the Middle of the Plateau

A diamond-back rattlesnake is coiled here, ready to strike.
A brown snake watches you.
A brown snake watches you.
A snake slithers towards you.
A grey wolf is here, thin from starvation.

A high, peculiar crag rises suddenly out of the uniform plateau. The softest areas of rock have mostly disappeared, devoured by the wind. Other surfaces, that seem harder, have somewhat withstood the erosion, and they show a better condition. Thus, the outline looks sharpened and irregular, as if serrated. All around the pinnacle, rocky fragments of all sizes lie scattered on the flat, grey ground.
9004: Small rises, standing a bit further north, partially shelter this area from the lashing, icy wind. The ground looks rocky and barren, and the landscape rather featureless, except for a number of little, weak trees, battered by the cold and elements, that grow scattered around. But even so, only a few blackened, pointed leaves still stick to their bare, greyish branches.
9005:
A nest is here.
A big, nasty vulture is sitting here, protecting its nest.
A big, nasty vulture is sitting here, protecting its nest.
A cockroach is scuttling across the floor carrying some debris.

Approaching the edge of the plateau a section of the ground seems to have given way, and melts into the lowland below. Observing along the split terrain, the inner rock can be seen exposed to the light giving notice to its faint grey surface deep within the crevice. The ground around you is absent of living plant life and is overpowered by the many small boulders and scattered rocks that have been naturally set by the earth's natural weather conditions.
9006: A Bare Incline to the Plateau

Walking towards the slight incline of the nearing plateau, the ground can be seen opening up its way to the top of an exposed landscape. The only sign of vegetation is the plant growth hidden behind the many rock formations across the plateau. Travelling further up the inclined land would give way to a lifeless earth only inhabited by the inanimate rocks that occupy the land at arm's reach.
9007: The land continues to rise creating a sloping ground, which makes walking more tedious if one were to travel farther east through the landscape. Noticeable from this distance is the large plateau to the east, which opens widely in the distance not far ahead. A small stream can be seen heading in a southerly fashion, but slightly hidden within the valley's edge.
9008: At the Foot of the Plateau

The terrain here can be seen ascending northward towards the dry plateau that lies in the distance. There are noticeable amounts of dotted grass formations buried on the surface of the many rocks that lie around in the surrounding area. Some of the rocks probably fell from the rocky wall to the east. The wall is mostly stone, but there are sections of earth from which vegetation sprouts. A small stream lies in the distance to the south and can be seen flowing further into the south.
9009: As bare as the ground may seem, many of the protruding rock formations rising from the ground beneath you could cause injury if a misplaced step was taken. The rocky walls of the empty plateau can be seen, plummeting down to the ground below. In rainy conditions small waterfalls can be seen forming, caused by the small brooks that slide down the cliff-face. In the nearby landscape, some form of grass formation can be seen but yet not abundant enough to create a field.
9010: The plateau comes to an end here, except for a ledge projecting southwards and westwards. The dry weather and lack of water has caused the ground to harden up and become extremely manageable to walk on. Overlooking in the westerly direction, the rock face descends steeply into the sloping terrain. The occasional cracking of a rock flying off the cliff to hit the ground breaks the sound of the winds that sometimes howl around this cliff. Further out into the distance, a large land of grasslands can be seen from above.
9011: The land is full of lush and lively grasses that the water has helped to grow for many years now. There are numerous rock formations in the surrounding landscape which have probably fallen from the nearby plateau over time. The impressive cliff-like face of the plateau stands majestically to the east, as if it had been rooted out of the ground. Dew is common in the mornings when the shadow of the plateau shrouds the land in darkness until the sun is high in the sky.
9012: Bend in a Stream through the Plains

The stream seems to bend here going eastwards cutting through the plains and flowing at a faster pace as it heads further east. Even though the current seems rather peaceful, you can feel the subtle nudges it gives off as the wind assists its rate of flow. This small river can be seen leading into a rather great river in the distance. Grassy plains can be seen to the western direction and to the south.
9013:
A fierce boar is here, making grunting noises.
A boar cub is playing here, and exploring the wide world.
A boar cub is playing here, and exploring the wide world.
A small boar with big yellow tusks looks eager to fight.

The earth is more fertile here since it is sitting next to a lively stream. If given the proper care some plant life can grow in these parts of the land. The stream to the east seems to be flowing in a south- easterly direction. A decaying barn surrounded by a large and high fence can be seen to the north western region.
9014: A decaying barn obstructs your passage to the west. The only means of passage is to go around the large fence surrounding the old barn to the south or by swimming through the nearby stream to the north. The land here is very fertile and gains its nutrients from the lively stream to the east and north.
9015:
A brook trout is here, swimming in the current.
A trout swims here.

The stream continues to travel in a southerly direction, bending to the east overflowing into a larger and slightly faster-paced stream. Small movements can be seen under the watery surface indicating signs of fish life up ahead. Continuing to journey along the stream's route will only lead you to greater and much faster flowing water, which only the most experienced swimmer could navigate through.
9016: A circular stone well has been built here.

An old building sits lonely on a flat plain overlooking the river, with its straw roof fallen in and crumbling chimney pointing to the sky above. Its decaying walls are slowly being overtaken by grass and vines. The last remaining doors and window shutters are still somewhat intact but the hinges squeak as the wind blows through them. The pasture behind the farm still contains what little life there is. Whoever once lived here must have left a long time ago.
9017:
The starving cow stands here looking for a patch of grass.
A brown cow is here, contemplating a higher reality whilst chewing slowly.

This slowly decaying cow pasture is contained by a large fence and has a broken down barn door in it. The fence blocks your path in more than one direction, which constrains your movement. There are only a few cows still left standing about that have been able to live off the still depleting nutrients that exist within the soil in the pasture. Given some time this pasture will be as lifeless and inanimate as the rest of the farm.
9018:
A ferocious warg is here, snarling angrily.
A hungry warg stands here, sniffing around for flesh.

The scenery along the landscape is very peaceful and soothing from this point of view. An old decaying farm house lies in front of you to the north, with a large wooden fence obstructing your passage. The only means of getting into the barn would be to walk around the wooden fence and through the front entrance. However, going for a closer look within the holding grounds of the barn and looking for any living inhabitants would prove a waste of time since they seem to have left it to decay many years ago.
9019: The area around you portrays a very quiet and calm place. The only thing which disturbs the silent plains is the sound of wind blowing by your ears. When you look around you all that can be seen are plains in most of the directions. To the west lie some fields. To the north can be seen a large fence surrounding a decaying barn.
9020: A small grasshopper clings to a blade of grass, ready to spring.

The soil around you is very poor in nutrients which makes the ground flat and rugged. It is very dull in the area about you and travelling further east would only lead you to more dull plains. The only presence of life is more to the west where fields of grasslands can be seen nearby. To the north is a subtle faint impression of a decaying barn surrounded by a large fence.
9021: A beautiful and docile horse is standing here.

Travelling through these lifeless plains is easier without the resistance of grass and plant life in your way. Walking in the western direction would only lead you into fields and fields of grass, whereas going in any other direction would only lead you to more plains.
9022:
A fierce boar is here, making grunting noises.
A boar cub is playing here, and exploring the wide world.
A boar cub is playing here, and exploring the wide world.
A small boar with big yellow tusks looks eager to fight.

The ground is unable to provide nutrients to any plant or grass life with the lack of water around here. There are more plains in all directions, but the vegetation seems just a bit more dense to the west. Looking further to the south is a flowing stream of muddy waters.
9023: Barren Plains along a Muddy Stream

Looking closer at the land around you there is not much change in the growing vegetation and plant life. The only sense of direction that can be of help is the muddy stream to the south of you. Looking far to the east, you can see a large body of water flowing rapidly. Everything else around you seems very motionless and inactive depicting the impression of a huge wasteland.
9024: A large beaver is here, gnawing on a piece of wood.

The river here is opaque from the stirring of mud caused by the movement of underwater plants within it. Dark green and brown protrusions of branches and leaves stick out of the water, causing ripples in the slowly flowing water.
9025: A large mother hawk is here looking for a prey to feed her young.

Not much remains of this old settlement; it appears to have been burnt to the ground a long time ago. The only thing still standing is an old battered chimney covered with ramblers and ivy. To the north, and the east, the sound of flowing water can be heard.
9026: Barren Plains near a Muddy Stream
A swarm of midges is here, humming around you.

Walking along these barren plains makes it easy to be confused as to whether you are going around in circles. The large expanse of green to the north gives off the impression that there is much grassland in that direction. Observing the route of the muddy stream it seems to head off into the southern direction. The sound of raging waters can be heard more clearly now, just as if you can almost distinguish you are getting closer to the source of the river.
9027: The earth is dead here with its lack of fields of flowers or any other sort of plant life. These plains extend in all directions except for the slight growth of grasslands to the northern direction. Looking closer to the south you can see a muddy river which stretches out in the eastern direction. A great river can also be seen from this point, heading into the east will only bring you closer.
9028: An experienced orkish scout is looking for tracks on the ground.

The grassland area that extends from the north and eastern direction seems to fade away as you glance farther south. More plains lie to the west and they seem to have their ability to grow plants. While a small river formation can be remotely seen in the southern distance, a greater river lies to the east.
9029: A beautiful and docile horse is standing here.

This area remains grassland, and is not taken over by woody shrubs and trees, because of seasonal drought, occasional fires, and grazing by large mammals. The soil of these grasslands is the deepest and most fertile in the surrounding area. To the east is a great river that is rich in colour and pleasant to more viewers.
9030: The grass here is a type of native grass, which is tough enough to withstand the strong dry winds of both summer and winter. The presence of these grasslands in this area allows for over wintering of large herds of elk. To the eastern direction lies a great river of tremendous power and strength. In every other direction lie more grasslands.
9031: The native grass here extends from the west and covers the ground beneath you. The cover of these grasslands is high enough to support different types of deer, elk and similar wildlife inhabitants. In the fescue grassland region further east though, the elk are generally absent due to the lack of nearby forest cover. Directly to the north of you is a bend in a stream heading in the eastern direction.
9032: An abundant amount of grass can be seen beneath your feet in all directions, continuing more densely in the north and east direction, and less sparse in the southern lands. As you stray farther to the north-east, the great Anduin River can be reached within arm's reach. Besides the grasses that grow here, wildflowers every spring provide a beautiful display of colour.
9033: The grass here is richer and can be seen more numerous as you peer to the north and to the east direction. A great river can be seen over in the east, which flows in a north and south route. Far to the west more plains cover the ground, similar to the view from the south.
9034: As the plains come to an end in this area, out come vast fields of grassland that encompass the surrounding land to the north and east. Short, shallow-rooted grasses, often growing in bunches covering large areas, can be seen nearby. To the south lie plains which form a desolate and lifeless landscape, giving off the impression of uninhabited lands.
9035:
Some ugly blow-flies are buzzing around here.
A swarm of midges is here, humming around you.

The landscape around here is very desolate and composed of dry land seemingly devoid of life. To the east of you lies a great river of enormous power which flows in a north and south direction. Further to the south of here is a muddy river which is rich in brown colours due to its vast amount of muddy water. Some fields of green can be seen to the north.
9036: No flowers or bushes grow in this land that is battered by winds that tend to blow from the west. In the shelter of some sharp rocks some patches of short, yellowish grass struggle to make this land appear a bit more fertile.
9037: A tall stag is here, grazing peacefully.

The ground here is nearly flat and very monotonous. Short, stumpy grass can be seen in all directions. There does not seem to be any memorable landmarks visible from here, but the sound of running water can be heard from the north.
9038: Water from the north flows through here and then towards the east. The water is deep enough to immerse many of the taller plants which grow in the water. Beyond the mixed types of plants growing along the edge of the river is a grassy field.
9039: A steep slope to the east blocks the flow of the stream and forces it to flow onward in the southern direction. The stream continues through the plains and lowlands towards the Anduin Vale. Lush vegetation and a couple of trees make this place look less barren than the surrounding plains.
9040: There are strong indications in this portion of land that once, long ago, someone or something took great care to cultivate it. All that remains are a few patches of wheat and corn which have survived through the ages on their own through the harsh seasons that have passed by, year after year. Towards the west an extension of this old field can be seen, along with an object which portrays the shape of a tombstone. The sound of rushing waters can be heard to the south.
9041: Immediately walking over the ground beneath you gives a sense that the land within arm's reach was manipulated by humanoid-like beings. Although no strong signs of cultivation are present, there is a noticeable trace of heavy movement throughout the ground around you. Whether this is an indication of life forms that once lived nearby long ago, it is too difficult to determine the exact details of these living forms.
9042: Bounteous Fields along a Steep Ridge

The endless fields of plants and flowers come to a complete stop here as the hill slopes downward at a rate which only an experienced climber would be able to navigate. The only way down this steep ridge is to the east and south where sharp protruding rocks can be seen sticking out of the sharply inclined hill. From this vantage point, fields of grasslands can be seen to the east and are continuous to the surrounding landscape.
9043: A sensation of life and activity comes from the boundless number of flowers growing within the grasslands all around you. A rainbow of colourful flowers can be seen within arm's reach and extends all around you creating a bright bed of flowers. Only time passing will stop the growth of these grasslands, as the hot season comes to an end and the cold season begins. The land descends and reaches the plains below further along the south and to the east.
9044: The land heading towards the southern and western directions seems to be more intact than any other of the ruined fields nearby. Most likely, the surrounding area to the south and west endured more maintenance, considering it was able to preserve the life that thrives to grow to this present day. Perhaps some manlike being assisted with the vegetation that flourishes in this area allowing small animals to feed off and run wild about.
9045: There are only small portions of loose grass remaining in the surrounding landscape. Observing more closely, signs of heavy passage can be seen crossing the ground beneath you in all directions. All that remains is the permanent damage done to the flourishing grasslands that once encompassed the land long ago. There is a large fence preventing your travel to the east and the only access to get inside that pen would be to walk around to the front entrance which would take some effort considering the descending hill before the entrance.
9046: Decaying Fields on a Low Hill

The landscape here descends down into the vast plains below. Travelling towards the plains below will only lead to a task that requires some work of a skilled climber. To the east is a ruined barn with a large wooden fence surrounding it. A small stream can be seen from the top of this hill and can be followed with the eye, flowing to the south-eastern direction. Further to the south the hills become more ridged and harder to travel along the terrain.
9047: Soggy Plains along a Small Stream

A mist of water can be felt coming from the northern direction. The ground beneath you seems to sink in about half an inch as the spray settles on the floor and becomes absorbed by the soil, turning into wet earth. Badly decaying fields of grassland can be seen from the horizon and a sense of warfare can be felt in the frigid wind blowing around you. Travelling in the south-westerly direction can only satisfy one's curiosity of the remains left behind of a battle taken place many years ago.
9048:
A large sturgeon swims slowly along the bottom.
The prominent fin of a silver-yellow fish breaks the surface of the water.
A trout swims here.

As the ground drops the rapids become a series of small falls and streams, throwing mist and vapour into the air as the water finds its way among the slopes and steps. A few of the falls are several feet high, but by being careful enough you can probably ford the stream with little or no trouble. Trees are becoming sparser when you move eastwards, where only vast sloping plains and grasslands extend as far as your eye can see.
9049: Although the stream through these parts is rather small, the water flows extremely fast. The current is strong enough to easily knock a man off his feet and carry him downstream. Flowing with determination towards the eastern rim of the large vale, it's clear to assume these rapids will result in a cascade of small waterfalls and streams farther away to the east. To the south is a vast expanse of battle-scarred plains.
9050: Greater parts of a broken weapon are lying on the ground.

The ravages of war are seldom more evident then they are upon this place. Soil rich with the blood of fallen warriors has only recently healed enough to allow new growth. A few weeds have sprouted up through the shallow graves of limbs lost by those who fell in battle.
9051: The sound of the wind sweeping across this old field could easily be mistaken for the howl of a dying man. Everything about this place conjures up the memory of death. Soil rich from soaking up the bloodshed of a great battle also holds the broken bones and mangled armour of those bodies left to rot without so much as being placed in a shallow grave. Since that time a few straggling weeds have managed to take seed and begin to heal this once fertile land.
9052: Despite the vast destruction of the surrounding areas, this flat parcel of land seems to have been for the most part spared. Bushes and even a few groups of young trees grow upon the sparsely grass-covered ground. However, this place is not without its scars. While it doesn't appear that armies clashed on this spot, the footfalls of troops passing by have left some patches of ground notably bare.
9053: The dark soil is rich with nutrients, allowing the plant life here to flourish. In the spring, beautiful wild flowers grow in abundance, displaying a dazzling variety of colours and scents. The grass grows thick and hardily, providing ample cushioning to anyone walking upon it. Small animals wander about, munching on berries or chewing on stalks.
9054: Despite the destruction that raged upon the land to the west, these plains are quite fertile and filled with life. Small animals dart around from time to time scavenging for food or nesting materials. Wild grasses and berry-bearing shrubs complete the scene of natural harmony.
9055: Before you lies a vast field of flowering plants. During the spring the flowers blossom, creating the perfect habitat for colourful butterflies and pollen bees. In the fall when the flowers are gone their seeds will take root, the beginning of the following year's floral display.
9056: A skeleton of some humanoid lies in the dust.

The remains of a small hut still stand here exposed to the elements. Looking at the front part of the ruined room the lack of life here is apparent. Even the spider's web high in one of the corners has been abandoned by its eight-legged owner. Further inside is a more startling sight; lying on the floor is what is left of what one can only assume was this hut's owner.
9057: The people who once tended this backyard are long gone. A half tilled patch of land leads one to believe that the caretakers departed suddenly. The plants are withered and dying. The land has dried up from a lack of watering and anything that might have once flourished is now in a state of decay. At the centre of the yard there is a small grave plot covered by a mound of loose soil with a large tombstone at the head.
9058: A crayfish is here, snapping its claws at you.

This small river is slowly but steadily working its way to the east. A few large stones line the bottom of the river along the northern edge, perhaps thrown into the water from the barren farmland there. The plain to the south seems to have a richer soil than the land to the north and its plants are thriving.
9059: This smooth plain is composed of dark nutritious soil which supports the many different kinds of bushes that thrive in this area. This plain is part of the wide vale that surrounds the river Anduin which flows east of here. The bushy plain continues westward while in the south there is an open valley covered in short grass.
9060:
A black snake hurries towards you with sly intentions.
A swallow flies high above the ground.

The vegetation here is biased towards short grasses that the cows often graze upon. The land north of here is covered with short bushes while the valley to the south seems quite austere, for no grass grows there. A dense-looking shrubbery that grows south-west of here forms a wall between the field and a small hut south of the shrubs.
9061: Open land to the north lets northern winds blow across this vale. While the soil is moist and soft there are no plants able to grow here for the strong winds sweep all living things away. The ground rises westwards where a small flimsy-looking hut stands and to the south the valley is covered with bushes.
9062: The fields have long since been abandoned, leaving the plants and grasses in a wild fight for survival. Old and rotting remains of low, wooden fences stand as silent relics of the former inhabitants of this area. Another reminder of the past is the flimsy hut located just north of here, slowly degrading and vanishing as the wild plants climb on it.
9063: Small bushes form a row of shrubbery growing next to a flimsy-looking hut that stands south of here. Some of the shrubs have unfolded their vines and firmly grasp the wall giving a sense of permanency. A field covered with weeds is visible to the west while to the north there is a bushy plain. A wide valley opens out eastward and declines smoothly towards the river Anduin.
9064: The soft soil is smooth and declines gently eastward where this bushy region continues. Several small shrubs grow here and there, thriving in this rich soil. The vegetation changes to the west where it becomes denser because there is more water available there. Shrubs grow to the south beside a small hut.
9065:
A trout swims here.
A trout swims here.

Barely reminiscent of its wide, fast-flowing source this small river is hardly more than a stream in these parts. The even ground gives little aid to propel the water further east and the riverbanks seem to soak up much of the moisture to feed the cravings of the surrounding plains. Despite these conditions the river does continue on eastward.
9066: The river gradually narrows here as it turns gently to the south. The current, not strong enough to widen its course, slowly pushes the water through the land. In time these river waters will mingle with those of the great Anduin River, which lies miles to the east. Some blades of grass float past and a few leaves drift along on the current.
9067: Even though these great fields appear to be quite an hospitable place for all kinds of animals, none that roam this land seem to be indigenous to this region. Closely examining the terrain one notices a small hut far to the east and a small river to the south slowly flowing west to east.
9068: This land has been clearly scorched by a horrible fire. Nothing escaped the searing heat. Those plants and grasses that were not completely consumed are withered from their proximity to the flames. Fine soot carried by the wind across the plains leaves a layer of black ash over everything. To the south one can catch a glimpse of fertile lands, but northward the destruction is even more widespread.
9069: Scorched by the deadly flames of what may have been a careless wildfire or one set in the ravages of war these plains are almost completely lifeless. Charred remains of what could have been a young tree lie as a lone sign that this area might once have been home to several varieties of vegetation.
9070: A few plants struggle to survive in this environment, crippled by a lack of direct sun and scorched earth. Some dusty grey flakes of ash, spread over a large portion of the desolate land, give evidence of perhaps a wild or intentionally set fire. Robbed of nutrients, not yet replaced by the natural order of things, the few plants present will soon fade.
9071: In the spring when the sun smiles upon this vast plain this fertile land bursts with flowers. A hardy variety of plant, the blooms last all through the summer months. In the fall, when all their petals have dried and fallen to the ground, this area gives off a sweet smell. In the winter, there is very little growth, while the bulbs of those flowering plants safely nestled in the soil are waiting for the cycle to begin again.
9072: The plants here have never recovered from the trampling of armies during what must have been a great battle. The once blood-stained earth still carries the broken bones and battered armour of the fallen warriors. In some places the fletching of an arrow or the hilt of a sword can be seen protruding from the ground.
9073: It is hard to imagine this quiet spot was once the site of a great battle. The soft soil, home to a variety of weeds and grasses, almost obscures the remnants of bones that lay as silent markers to those who died and were not even buried.
9074: The stream straightens out here and picks up speed on its journey eastward. Still quite calm, it emits a pleasant transparent sound as it passes the meadows that grace its shores. Some small birds flutter about bathing in the water and drinking from the cool, clear stream. Some other birds along the banks sing sweet songs, as if to thank the gods for placing this stream upon Arda.
9075: This small trickling stream winds through the plains. The water is crystal clear and flows quickly, inviting weary visitors to take a dip. As the stream slowly wanders back and forth on its way eastward towards the Anduin River it produces a small tinkling sound. Small animals come and go, stopping only to drink from the banks of the river.
9076:
A stocky mountain mule is here, waiting to serve.
A very strong orkish leader is here on patrol.
An orc soldier is standing here.
An orc soldier is standing here.
An experienced orkish scout is looking for tracks on the ground.

Almost utterly silent is the meadow that unfolds upon this land; the only sound to be heard is the whisper of a small stream. The stream speaks with nature's dulcet voice trying to maintain harmony, lest other less peaceful sounds would try to overwhelm this quiet place.
9077: The land gradually slopes to the west. At dusk when the wind blows it creates the illusion of these winsome grasses bending to pay homage to the setting sun. This entire area seems to carry an air of simplistic calm. Each morning these tranquil plains seem to awaken with life.
9078: Piles of stone and debris lie scattered across these barren plains. Just south of here all passage is blocked by the remnants of an old stone wall. Perhaps once quite sturdy, the wall is now slowly crumbling to dust, leaving only rocky fragments and boulders as a trace of its former glory.
9079:
A mass of dark green leaves clings to a wall.
A rabid rabbit is here, frothing at the mouth.

The vast plain stretches out in all directions except to the west. There the remains of an old stone wall blocks passage for animals as well as plants. The worn, broken rocks that make up the wall are covered in vines and ivy, which are slowly and inevitably choking the stone, assisting the elements in breaking the wall down into no more than rocky rubble.
9080: A dark green, foul-smelling shrub grows to about a foot in height.

The faint odour of rotten herbs lingers in the air. Almost all of the plants sticking up out of the ground are dead and decaying. Most of the leaves have fallen off, although a desperate few still cling to stalks and branches. Some small trees stand here, malnourished and slumping, their boughs touching the ground. Even the few blackened vines that once grew with vigour have given up their attempts to scale the ruins of the village walls.
9081: Set a bit lower than the surrounding plains land, this quiet old field has remained untouched by person or animal for what could have been an eternity. The ground is no more than dirt; not even weeds have laid seed. In fact, there is very little evidence anything ever grew upon this spot. Even the wind seems to overlook this place, blowing high above the ground.
9082: The river flows gently along to the east, having expended its energy closer to its source. All that seems to keep it flowing is the slight downward grade of the ground, leading it towards the Anduin vale. The surface of the water is unusually still, giving no hints as to the river's movement. An old dying tree stands at the southern bank.
9083: The plains spread out alongside this small river, accompanying it as it dances eastwards to join the powerful Anduin on its vast and arduous journey towards the distant southern lands. Not much grows here, even though the proximity to the water should create a suitable base for vegetation. A large old tree stands a few yards away from the southern bank of the river.
9084: Huge bushes with massive leaves create a gloomy atmosphere for this region. A few tall trees with wide spreading lush branches cast shadows upon the surrounding lands reinforcing the dark ambience. The vegetation to the east grows sparser since fewer and smaller bushes grow there.
9085: This field is almost entirely covered by the rampant growth of weeds. They now occupy the space of other plants which suffer from the strangling the weeds cause. The lands nearby look more fertile and the plant life in these areas flourish for they do not suffer from strangling weeds. The brush to the north differs from the other nearby areas in that it appears very shady with a couple of huge trees casting shadows about.
9086: This wide valley descends from the west towards a flimsy-looking hut in the east. The vegetation here is short of stature but very robust with various kinds of brightly coloured flowers all about. A small spring with crystal-clear water is located southward and several traces of animals can be seen leading through here towards the spring.
9087: The ground descends steeply from the west where the edge of the valley can be seen. The deep, dark brown soil is very nutritious and forms the basis for the many different kinds of plants growing here. The ground is mostly covered with grass but a few small bushes and a young birch grove full of thin saplings are also here.
9088: The grass, over a foot high, covers this flourishing vale between the lush shrubs and several young birches that grow here. The land rises towards the west where the edge of this valley is visible. This extensive vale continues to the distant east where the great Anduin river flows.
9089: The area is overshadowed by a pair of ancient trees with huge canopies that provide shade here and to some brush in the east. The land declines sharply from the west where the border of the vale is visible. Terrain similar to this region continues far to the east with various small types of vegetation, like grass and weeds, growing all around.
9090: From this point only a faint whispering sound can be heard from the river that lies to the north. A large oak tree dominates the area, emitting a rotten smell similar to that of unburied corpses. Some large trees far to the south cast dark shadows upon much of this bushy plain.
9091: The river slowly meanders ever onward to the east at a smooth, silent pace. Occasionally a small fish can be seen leaping out of the water creating a brief splash, breaking the serene silence. The usual water creatures go about their business; insects skim the surface, fish swim in the current, and birds swoop down to pluck a trout from the water. The river is bordered by plains to the north and south. The ruins of a village can be spotted nearby to the north.
9092: Damp and silent is the garment worn by this abandoned ground. No being of conscience could possibly desire to remain upon this dismal place for longer than necessity demands. All that can be seen across the barren landscape is land raped by fire. To the east the plains are far flourishing, yet from here they too are silent. To the south-west the grasping claws of a rushing river can be heard, seemingly yearning for someone or something to snatch from the riverbank.
9093: A cup has been set here.

The northern wall of this house is severely damaged, having buckled under the weight of the roof. The north section of the roof has completely collapsed leaving a sizeable hole above. Whatever caused the rampant destruction of the village moved north from here leaving a large breach in the wall. Shattered stones lie scattered all across the ground.
9094: The remnants of an old stone wall stand sentinel here, preventing travel southward from this point. In all other directions the plains stretch out toward the horizon from the base of the wall creating a smooth, billowing grassy expanse unbroken save for a tower far to the north-east.
9095: A black crow flies low to the ground here, looking for carrion to eat.

Like a fair maiden's long soft hair, these plains gently flow to the rhythm of the winds as they stretch out eastward. The subtle nature of their charm is not even diminished by areas of heavily burnt grass and an imposing dark tower.
9096: This entire area is filled with a remarkable stench. The pungent smell is inescapable; not even fragrant mauve petals could dispel this foetid odour. Progress through this area is impeded as one inhales this scent heavy air. The source of the odours, which seems to be some rotting meat, is combined with the stench of sulphur, creating an entire level of noxious vapours. Staying here for any period of time would be unwise as who knows the damage inhaling these fumes could cause.
9097: A long time ago, when the deadly breath of war raged through this area, a group of valiant warriors were surrounded and captured by an overwhelming force of the Dark Lord. Warriors were decapitated after loosing arms and legs and some of them were skinned alive. All that remains here now are piles of broken bones and perhaps a few lost souls looking for vengeance.
9098: Tortured by the plague of war, these fields have become a huge cemetery for the fallen soldiers who fought here. The plants here have been trampled by the many hordes who once walked over them; there is no new growth. The earth was once made muddy, drenched in the blood of soldiers who fell in battle. Now the only reminder is the dark colour and heavy consistency of the soil. Every so often the fletching of an arrow or the hilt of a sword can be seen protruding from the ground. As the wind sweeps across the field it creates a long, slow sound, like the moaning of someone on the verge of death.
9099: The vast grasslands seem to stretch out forever continuing on in every direction. To the south the ground becomes rocky, and there are some buildings far off in the distance. The fields to the east have a sombre look about them, and the earth there is dark as if there were a shadow emanating from the ground. An abandoned lodge lies in ruins just west of here.
9100:
A large pile of boulders is sitting here, probably debris from a rockslide.
A huge warg is here, moving in for the kill.

Large rocks seemingly sprung out of the ground make up this rocky landscape. This area appears to be an extension of the Misty Mountains; perhaps this is the very place at which they take root. The large boulders resemble a creature's jagged maw, with rough grey teeth in a huge open jaw that could snap shut at any moment. At times the light shining down from the sky creates a strange array of shadows, and one must wonder if there are some monstrous creatures around. An imaginative traveller might think of scenarios in which the boulders take on lives of their own.
9101: As this land gradually blends itself into the Misty Mountains more and more stones are visible in the soil. As one progresses from north to south the rocks gradually decrease in size, from huge boulders to small stones. Although the larger stones pose an obstacle to travellers who must traverse them, the medium sized chunks of rock prove to be the biggest nuisance. They jut out of the ground at the most inopportune times, and one could easily trip over them.
9102: This sprawling field sports an abundance of stout bushes and tall grasses, with many small rocks embedded in the soil. Occasionally some small trees reach up out of the bushes towards the sky. Small animals dart in and out of the bushes, creating little ruffles in the grass as they run through. At times a lone hawk or a flock of birds cross the sky.
9103: The remains of a large old wall still stand here, blocking passage to the south-east despite its crumbling state. The old wall follows a gentle curve, making a circle that continues on to the east and south. Traces of debris and piles of rock line its path.
9104: Tall stone columns on either side of the road are all that is left intact of this once lively village. The great gates, that once served as a border between this city of Woodmen and the wilderness beyond, fell long ago. The city walls are visibly weakened, with holes of varying sizes. Some of the holes are large enough to allow medium-sized creatures to pass through. The gates themselves appear to have taken quite a beating before they fell; there are large round impact marks at about waist height, possibly from a battering ram. Splintered fragments of the gate are scattered about the ground, and some larger chunks are still bolted to the columns. Whatever force laid siege to this city, it must have been quite massive.
9105: Just outside the old village walls this old field lies silently as a memory of the old inhabitants of this area. A few wooden poles rise out of the ground, the remains of a fence in a shape reminiscent of the grin of an old man that has lost almost all his teeth. The field itself is slowly being reclaimed by the surrounding plains, its man-sown crops fighting a valiant, but inevitably losing, battle.
9106: Silent and desolate best describe these plains that stretch out as far as the eye can see. Like a vast brown carpet they welcome travellers to take a leisurely stroll. However, this featureless area quickly becomes monotonous as the only break in this bleak landscape is a small collection of collapsed huts, probably the remains of an old farm slowly becoming as lifeless as the rest of the surroundings.
9107: This is the western edge of a wide valley which runs north and south. To the far east the mighty river Anduin flows in its centre. The lands to the east are covered with many different kinds of vegetation, most of them flourishing. The ground slopes sharply down from the edge to the centre of the Vale of Anduin. The plains to the north appear quite barren.
9108: The bushy terrain to the west ends here as the ground becomes flatter and the bushes slowly die out. Eastwards, an enormous valley opens out and spreads far to the east where it enfolds the river Anduin. Overall the vale is flourishing with a large variety of vegetation. A huge rock, some twenty feet high, stands at the edge of the valley.
9109: The vegetation here has a lower density when compared to the lands westward. A few medium-sized bushes grow here, leaving fairly wide routes between them. The ground is abundantly covered by animal tracks and even a few humanoid prints are visible on the surface. A wide valley opens out towards the east and continues into the far distance.
9110: Scattered on the vast plains are a few patches of low growing bushes along with some plants and creeping vines. Otherwise this area is dominated by weeds and grasses not strongly bound by the plants. Occasionally a light blowing wind stirs up some dust which slowly settles back to the ground covering the greenery.
9111: The proximity of this place to the river just north-east of here has created a rich and varied environment where various plants, weeds and grasses compete for the mineral rich space. A few single trees stand spread out along the bank of the river, throwing their small shadows across the otherwise open plains.
9112: The trail meanders along, slowly leading eastwards. There is little sign of wear on the ground leaving only a faint rut to indicate the path upon which grass is taking hold. A river rushing nearby to the south fills the air with the furious churning sound of fast-flowing water. The sound seems fainter to the north, where the quiet plains stretch out into the distance.
9113: The land here is barren, with a mixture of large boulders and gravel scattered about. The rocks are all that provides even a variety of colour. This area seems quite inhospitable to any kind of life, be it plants or animals. To the east there seem to be the ruins of a small village in the distance. To the south there is an old disused trail.
9114: The land is quite rocky, with huge stone shards jutting up out of the earth. Travelling across this area is quite difficult as each possible path is determined by the rocks which seem to create a confusing labyrinth. Someone on foot might have an easier time hopping across the tops of the large boulders; those with mounts, however, must travel on the ground.
9115: A small and tough weed grows here.

Bundles of thick weeds grow here. The tangles easily trip up those walking through. For young adventurers or those of short stature, travel here could be markedly slow. Although the earth is fertile, there is no space for anything of worth to grow; the weeds have overrun the field, choking out all other plants. Digging into the ground a bit one only finds a tangle of thin roots and masses of seedpods.
9116: The ground is quite uneven, riddled with large bumps and small rocks that could slow down weary travellers. These rough plains are filled with uneven grasses that grow in clumps of various sizes. A few wildflowers present small blotches of colour breaking up the monotony of the landscape.
9117: Standing out among the low and widely scattered patches of bushes there is a small cottage crouching beside a small and low hill. The back wall of the old and abandoned farmstead is built into the small earth-mound, and the remains of an old fence can be seen here and there.
9118: Small bushes are scattered all over this section of the plains, like small clouds spread throughout the sky on a midsummer day. Although this appears to be a very fertile area few animals can be seen. To the east a small ruined cottage stands out against the backdrop of this landscape. The grasslands slope upward toward a large forest which can be seen far off to the west.
9119: The plain slopes down to the south-east in a hardly perceptible manner. A number of large bushes crown the tops of long but low-lying bumps that sit like islands in the plain. The height of the bushes on top of the bumps almost makes the plain a living maze for travellers trying to navigate through it.
9120: The rhythmic undulating motion of these plains is reminiscent of a bunch of rabbits frolicking in the grass; every so often there is a stretch where the plains lie flat, as if taking a rest, before bounding off again into the distance. Standing on one of the higher points allows a good view of the flowing ripples of the surrounding land. As the wind blows the tips of the grass sway like waves in the ocean.
9121: This lush field sports an abundance of long sturdy grasses that wave with each passing wind. Interspersed with the grass are some hardy bushes and strong trees, spread out like big lumps of green dropped onto the landscape. Small animals dart in and out of the bushes creating little ruffles in the grass as they run through. Occasionally a lone hawk or a flock of birds will cross the sky.
9122:
Some pine nuts lie scattered upon the ground.
A tall pine tree grows here.

Several young pines grow on this vast field, shooting off from the older trees in the west. This is the perfect spot for new trees to grow, a large flourishing field with nourishment from the river that passes by to the west. Many full and round pinecones litter the ground, evidence that the trees are quite healthy. If even half of the cones sprout this field could grow to be forest.
9123: This small trail near the riverbank is covered in high grass indicating it hasn't seen much use in quite some time. The trail continues its journey eastwards for a while, before coming to an abrupt halt before the fallen gates of a ruined village. From the south the sound of rushing water can be heard, presumably the roaring river to the west.
9124: Crossing the swift waters of the river below an old and creaking rope-bridge passes the wild river here. Allowing safe passage for the worn and weary traveller, the bridge safely carries anyone across as it bypasses the strong and powerful currents and eddies that otherwise would be a harsh threat.
9125: This small path is almost completely covered up by thick, waist-high grass. The trail leads from a large river in the north and vanishes as it travels south. To the west is a withered field of wheat, and a rushing river can be seen south-east.
9126: Various plants battling for space mix here into one big tangled mass. It is hard to tell exactly what plants make up this entanglement since there is no way to separate them all. Clearly there are some wild grasses and herbs, along with some wildflowers, all corralled by several groups of shrubs. Far to the west a dense and dark mass of trees line the horizon, while to the east the plains stretch out to the horizon.
9127: These plains are a patchwork of varied vegetation. A single tree stands in a small cluster of bushes, while a dense group of brushwood is slowly creeping in from the south. To the northeast the vegetation slowly diminishes, giving way to vast open areas of grass.
9128: Large bushes with thick leaves grow more tightly-packed, forming a dense cluster, because of the excellent soil. The terrain south of here is made of the same soil and is covered in similar bushes. While eastwards the vegetation merely thins, to the west it appears scanty.
9129:
The rabid rabbit is here, frothing at the mouth.
The rabid rabbit is here, frothing at the mouth.

These swampy plains seem to have been created by a build up of runoff water from the river which lies to the south-east. Frequent rains cause the river to swell, flooding these plains over and over again. In the time it would take the ground to absorb the previous flooding, the rains return creating an endless cycle of watering. Due to this the grass here grows tall and wild, making shallow, miniature waterways and paths. Various seeds float along in these channels pushed along by the wind and the slope of the land leaving them to culminate in little pools.
9130: From this point one can see the beautiful vast plains that lie ahead. Interspersed between the majestic stalks of the tall grass that grows here lies a mixture of moss and weeds upon the ground. The mottled green and brown ground cover gives this place a dismal tone. Every now and then, the ground causes an uncomfortable squishing sensation, and if one stands still it feels as though the ground is sinking.
9131: These plains sport a sharp gradient as if they were leaning towards something far off to the south-east. The blowing wind across the tips of the grass creates the illusion of ripples which carry the eye in that direction. Seemingly out of place amidst these plains is a small group of pines jutting up straight out of the ground, only to be pushed and bent by the winds. Small bushes dot the landscape, providing shelter for rabbits and other small creatures.
9132: The vast sea of grass that lies here has slowly levelled off, with just a slight slant towards the great river to the east. To the south and west the slopes are much steeper, while to the east the plains are home to a wide variety of bushes. The grade of the slope allows for a quite good view clear to the eastern horizon.
9146: The river flows in from the east and then continues southward. Near the edges of the river one can see an occasional elm tree with its roots sticking into the water to drink. The water flowing over and around the roots causes eddies to stir up the silt on the riverbed which clouds the water. An occasional piece of root, or light piece of dirt, floats on the surface.
9147: A large sturgeon swims slowly along the bottom.

The swift water of the Anduin flows from the north and follows a curved route to the west. A good deal of water sometimes splashes onto the land by the river bend when the river is running high, making the grass wet and the ground muddy. The mud from the edges of the riverbank sometimes flows into the river, clouding up the water and making it impossible to see the bottom.
9156: A Wimple at the Edge of the Wildlands

The forest in the west changes its shape as it makes its way towards the great wilderness of the east. It slowly eases into a vast spread of grass and small bushes. Little else about the lore of this land can be gleaned by examining the surroundings. What hazardous creatures may live here is anyone's guess.
9157: An ocean of grass spreads from this point, in the shadow of the large forest to the west. The ground slopes gently down towards the east, where it eventually meets the mighty river, Anduin. To the west looming trees stand, blocking any further view. Far off east in the distance a little blue line, winding with sweeping turns through the land, must be the Anduin, despite how small it looks from this vantage point.
9158: These vast plains are covered with a brown cloak of grass, near death due to lack of nutrients. The ground is littered with small rocks lying scattered about. The plains slope down to the east, towards a large vale embracing the great river Anduin. To the west the plains lie veiled in shadows. Southwards, the large sloping plains continue for quite a distance until they meet the edge of a river by the forest.
9159: These plains stretch for many miles to the east. In the evenings they fall under the dark shadows of the Misty Mountains. Immediately south, a dark forest seems to be encroaching upon these plains, as if attempting a conquest. Although a small river can be seen to the west, the sounds of rushing water seem to be coming from the south.
9160:
A porcupine is waddling around here, its tail full of sharp quills.
A porcupine is waddling around here, its tail full of sharp quills.

The small river runs north-south here. A dark forest looms on its western bank. Vast plains stretch before you to the east. Turning around, you see the high peaks of the ominous Misty Mountains. The long mountain range stretches from Angrenost, also known as Isengard, in the south, to Carn Dum, the capital of Angmar, the land of the Witch-king, in the north. You have heard many frightening tales about these mountains - about Moria, where no man dares to travel, about Mount Gundabad, the orkish capital in the north, and about the horrid goblins of the Goblin-gate, somewhere in the High Pass just west of here. The river is less supported by water than it used to be and it slowly turns into land.
9161:
A porcupine is waddling around here, its tail full of sharp quills.
A porcupine is waddling around here, its tail full of sharp quills.

To the east of you is the dark pine forest which separates you from the foot of the Misty Mountains. The small river emerges from the forest here, starting its way east to the large river which eventually could bring you to Gondor and the ocean beyond. The river is less supported by water than it used to be and it slowly turns into land.
9162:
A tree-snake lies wrapped around one of the tree branches.
A tree-snake lies wrapped around one of the tree branches.
A tree-snake lies wrapped around one of the tree branches.

A sombre silence lies upon this forest. Almost every life form seems to have fled from the darkness that shrouds this place. The high, closely intertwined treetops ensure that little light makes its way down to the forest floor. However, there seems to be another, less obvious reason for the lingering darkness.
9163:
A cute little girl with tangled hair is standing here.
A small boy with a scared look is standing here.

A thin layer of slime covers the floor of this small pit beneath the dismal chamber above. A trickle of dirty water drips from the rusty grating in the ceiling of this pit. The ground here is soft and muddy with the water as it slowly soaks into the soil on its way into the groundwater beneath here.
9164:
The corpse of Nagash the Dark is lying here.
Klaees (donny), wielding a heavy morningstar, is standing here.
Bulg, wielding a great warsword, is standing here smiling.
Ducaht (tooprettytodie), wielding a great warsword, is standing here.

A powerful darkness fills this circular chamber, making it difficult to discern shadows. The floor descends slightly towards the centre of the room where a rusty grating is set in the floor. The water flows from the tunnel south of here in a small ditch then through the grating down into the filthy pit which sits under this chamber.
9165:
A raging bear is here, fighting Bulg.
A fierce bear, raging with insanity, is here.
Bulg, wielding a great warsword, is here, fighting a raging bear.

A small ditch has formed in the floor as water flows through this tunnel. The air is very humid here and the walls are covered with mould. The roof is made of many small bricks and has been shaped into the form of an arch. As the water flows north it passes through a circular chamber.
9166:
The corpse of a vicious rat is lying here.
Klaees (donny), wielding a heavy morningstar, is standing here.
Bulg, wielding a great warsword, is standing here.
Drazud, wielding a two-handed axe, is standing here.
Ducaht (tooprettytodie), wielding a great warsword, is standing here.

Humid air fills this large deserted cellar which was once used as a storage area for food. The scents of rotted food are present. The stone walls of the basement are covered with verdigris and water trickles from the roof. The floor seems to decline slightly northward where the flowing water has gathered. A couple of wooden barrels stand in the south-western corner.
9167: A small black vicious rat squeaks at you for disturbing it.

These huge stone stairs appear to be worn smooth except where many small cracks on their surface show. The cracks have been eroded from the trickle of water formed by the condensing of the humid air. However, the stairs seem quite firm and can probably support a person's weight.
9168:
The burnt and blackened skeletal remains of a human are here.
A small vicious black rat squeaks at you for disturbing it.

The entire ceiling of this great hall has collapsed, littering the floor with stones of various sizes. Sections of the walls have also been smashed in and several gaps are easily large enough to allow light into the room. Other rooms once led off this one, but nothing of those rooms remains. Numerous bones jut out from under the fallen rubble and a couple of shattered skeletons can be seen, making this room look like a mass grave. To the north there is another ruined hall.
9169: A skeleton of some humanoid lies in the dust.

From the scattered stones one can tell that this huge building once underwent some sort of large-scale catastrophe. The basic structure seems to have endured surprisingly well apart from the fallen mezzanine and the burned furniture. Many blocks of the former roof can be seen scattered among the skeletal remains on the ground. To the south there lies another hall which appears to have crumbled more extensively than this one.
9170: In the centre of this destroyed and ash-covered district stands a colossal well, some ten feet in diameter. The ring of the well is built of large granite blocks many of which have become loose or have fallen from the well ring. A large winch with a frail rope and wooden bucket stands above the well, seemingly still in workable condition.
9171: The extent of the mass destruction that was inflicted upon this village years ago is still easily visible when viewing the remains of the dwellings. However, time and the ravages of the weather have worked at the village and have softened some of the harshness of the destroyed structures. The strong stonewalls which surround the village are surprisingly well preserved. The only building that seems to have endured the ravage in some fashion is a large structure standing in the west. To the south there lies a massive but shattered well.
9172:
A battered warg fur has been left here.
A rotten corpse is hanging here.
A black pond is here, filled with putrid water.
A huge stone giant is here, glaring at you.

Hidden behind trees and bushes, a small shadowed cave has been dug into the slope. Twelve feet deep, its entrance is large enough to allow even the tallest creatures to pass. Scattered on the floor of the cave are the remnants of small animals, skeletal parts from larger prey and a few pieces of torn fur.
9173:
A neat straw pallet is lying here.
A large stone fireplace with a roaring fire warms the room.
A tall and strong hunter is standing here.

This hidden cavern offers excellent shelter for any traveller seeking cover from bad weather. The walls of the cave are craggy and a natural chimney rises high above, blackened from the use of a fireplace standing in the middle of the stony floor. Around the fireplace lie lumps of straw, offering a comfortable resting place for weary travellers. A dense thicket covers the cave's entrance.
9174: This poorly constructed cottage, made of splintery planks, has been severely beaten by the weather. The floor is covered with old filth, much of it in a decaying state, indicating a lack of recent usage. The roof has several holes which makes this place a poor shelter on rainy days. There are no windows in this hut and the only places for light to enter are through the cracks in the walls and through the doorway when the door is opened.
9175: A shadowy haunt floats here, oblivious to your presence.

This small cellar was once a storage area for food and other goods. While the cool air preserved the foodstuffs for many years they have long since decayed. Dust has settled deeply over the years this dwelling has been abandoned by its previous inhabitants. The walls of the cellar are made of clay and the floor is covered by a few planks.
9176:
A demon wolf lurks here, its dark form twisting and hiding its shape.
A hungry warg stands here, sniffing around for flesh.
A hungry warg stands here, sniffing around for flesh.

Not much light enters this room, if room is even the word to describe this place. It is more of a dingy pit, hastily carved out of the earth, as evidenced by the rough walls. Deep scratches and ruts along the earthen surfaces catch the shadows created by the dim light, giving the illusion of fresh wounds. The air is humid, suggesting that it might be a cellar of some sort, if it weren't for the well-worn bones that litter the ground. Judging from the pervasive odour, it is more likely a dungeon, or a holding pen for wild animals or pets.
9177:
A weapons rack stands against the wall.
In the rack is a longspear.
A tall brown-skinned orc, with wide arms, examines you harshly.
A tall brown-skinned orc, with wide arms, examines you harshly.
A demon wolf lurks here, its dark form twisting and hiding its shape.
A swallow flies high above the ground.

Looking around, it is evident that these are the barracks for the soldiers stationed at this outpost. The overwhelming stench of sweat and rotten meat hangs heavily in the air, seeming to emanate from no particular place. The odour is in everything. Two-high bunks are lined up against the walls; most are quite untidy, and the sheets hanging off of them are mottled with stains. The splotches have varying degrees of darkness; some look like blood, while others are more consistent with sweat and dirt. Old clothes are strewn about everywhere on the floor. Both the clothes and the floor are stained with spots similar to those on the sheets. It is evident that nothing here has been washed in a long while, if ever. A heavy wrought iron grid is embedded in the middle of the floor, with large hinges bolted to an adjacent floorboard. A large metal ring is attached to the side opposite the hinges, likely a handle allowing it to swing up, giving access to whatever lies below.
9178: Of all the places in this building this must be the most vital. Here the guardians of the tower can gather information about enemy or friendly movements from quite a distance so that they can send a messenger to prepare their chieftain for whatever is coming. The tower's importance is evidenced by its sturdy stone construction. Heavy blocks of stone hold the walls together by weight and placement. A domed roof protects the room from the elements, while small portals in the walls allow viewing of the surrounding lands.
9179:
A mailbox stands here stuffed full of messages.
A large bonfire is burning here.
A wooden chest stands in the corner.
A water barrel has been left here.
Murog, the Captain of the Fortress, stands here.
A tall brown-skinned orc, with wide arms, examines you harshly.
A tall brown-skinned orc, with wide arms, examines you harshly.
A tall brown-skinned orc, with wide arms, examines you harshly.
A demon wolf lurks here, its dark form twisting and hiding its shape.
A demon wolf lurks here, its dark form twisting and hiding its shape.

This is a dark and humid room at the heart of the outpost with a large door made of oak. The height of this room is approximately seven feet and like the rest of the outpost the walls are made of roughly cut stones that just as well might have been picked directly from the ground. It seems as if the guards of this outpost used this as a storage room. The smell of half-rotten meat tickles your senses.
9180:
A tall brown-skinned orc, with wide arms, examines you harshly.
A tall brown-skinned orc, with wide arms, examines you harshly.
A tall brown-skinned orc, with wide arms, examines you harshly.
A tall brown-skinned orc, with wide arms, examines you harshly.
A swallow flies high above the ground.

This seems to be the entrance hall of a small outpost. The walls are made of large, roughly cut stones. The craftsmanship is less than expert, and everything about this outpost leads one to believe it was built hastily. This particular building has not stood here long, judging from the age of its materials. The place lies in squalor, evidence that the most recent occupants may have been the orcs.
9181:
A small and well-kept fire lights and warms the room.
A female orc stands glaring at you.
A female orc stands glaring at you.

The ceiling of this tiny room is at most four feet high. The walls are made of heavy stones, which have been laid on top of one another, held in place only by weight. The only natural light in here enters through small cracks between the stones. This room does not appear to be a storage space, but rather some type of hidden escape route, should some enemy force come unexpectedly.
9182:
A large leech is moving close to you, searching for blood.
A small leech is here, floating in the water.

Completely water-filled, this small chamber was once part of the secret escape route that led from the old fortress into safety. The water is stale and dark as it is standing almost perfectly still. On the old floor of the chamber there are the remains of old barrels and stands of chests. However, their contents have long since become ruined and decayed.
9183: A small leech is here, floating in the water.

This old tunnel was once dry and carefully maintained, but since water from the nearby rivers has been eating away at the walls the entire route has been completely flooded. The water here is stale and dark since no movement helps to circulate it.
9184: A small leech is here, floating in the water.

The small tunnel turns sharply southwards here but the water continues to drag you slowly eastwards, towards the rocky walls. Small cracks in the wall allow the water to pass through as it strives to reach the large rivers that lie further to the east.
9185: This is apparently the end of a small tunnel that isn't more than about four or five feet high and not much wider. At one side of the tunnel there is a small hole leading upwards. On the other side there is deep, almost impenetrable darkness that is covering every sign of movement in the tunnel.
9186: This part of the tunnel is featureless and it runs from east to west. Despite being carved out of the ground the walls, floor, and ceiling are quite smooth. The dimensions here make the going quite tough for anyone either very tall or rotund.
9187: A large leech is moving close to you, searching for blood.

The tunnel here is wet and muddy. It seems as though this passage was dug as some sort of escape route, but perhaps a wall was dug too close to a stream, since the tunnel is now flooded. This particular section of the passageway is sloped upwards so the water is only about knee-deep. There is some sort of flat stone above you, supporting the ceiling, but the tunnel to the east is totally flooded. To proceed in that direction, one must plunge beneath the water, and hope that the exit is not too far away.
9188: A tiny spider is here, eating a tiny bug.

This cottage may once have been nice. Now, however, the roof and walls are shattered, fragmented remains of a home. The south wall is barely intact enough to support the broken oak door, with its gold-coloured handle. In the centre of this ruined place there is a small round table. A broken fireplace lies in what used to be the northern wall.
9189: A shade is here, shrouded in an inky blackness.

The walls of the mound are made out of large, rough stone blocks that were set into the walls of the mound with great care. Back when they were added the blocks were tightly fitted but now the cracks between the blocks have widened, revealing the soil behind. The floor was beaten down and then mixed with small pebbles. In the centre of the room stands a large, smooth, perfectly rectangular stone slab. There are no engravings to name who might once have lain on it so one can only speculate.
9190:
A pair of tongs lie on the ground.
A dented pail has been carelessly left here.
A well-muscled man stands here, covered in soot.

A big anvil dominates the centre of the room, while along the east wall stands a melting furnace which is fed by a pair of bellows. The furnace gives an orange gleam to the room. A variety of tools are hanging on the walls such as pinchers and fliers. In a corner some metal scrap is piled. A dented pail full with dark, oily water stands between the pile and the anvil. Both the walls and the roof have been turned dark with grime.
9191:
A circular stone well has been built here.
A young man stands here carefully guarding his village.
A young man stands here carefully guarding his village.
A woman stands here carefully guarding her village.
A Beorning captain is here, keeping the watch.
A young man stands here carefully guarding his village.

This square inside the small village has a well in its centre that has been made from stones of various sizes. Several posts support a small roof a few feet above the top of the well. A simple winch, with an attached rope and dented pail, is mounted on the well's posts. To the west stands the main building of the village. To the north there is a forge, and a gate east of here leads to a wooded pasture. A tall watchtower standing over the village square can be reached by the wooden ladder here.
9192:
A brown donkey watches the surroundings, perhaps looking for a chance to graze.
A pig is here, covered in mud.
A pig is here, covered in mud.
A duck is here, quacking happily.

The ground here appears quite trampled for a pasture field, not many plants remaining for the animals to eat. The areas around the gate to the west and the barn on the north side are especially bad due to all the animals herded through on a regular schedule. Perhaps one day if left to prosper the village will expand this pasture. Close to the gate there are two troughs, one for water and one for fodder. In the southeast corner there is a steaming dunghill.
9193:
A stocky mountain mule is here, waiting to serve.
A sturdy pack horse is standing here.
A sturdy pack horse is standing here.
A Beorning lad tends to the stables adjoining a large house.
A pack horse is standing here, ridden by you.

The walls of the barn are made of sturdy wooden planks and the roof is thatched. Along the walls are wide stalls for the animals. The barn was built with a hayloft and it is now full of hay. Standing from a crate just inside the entrance are several pitchforks, spades and a few other tools. A wooden wheelbarrow has been left carefully out of the way beside the crate. South of the barn stretches a wooded pasture.
9194: A duck is here, quacking happily.

This is the sleeping chamber of the men of the village. The northern and eastern walls of the room are lined with beds. A small table and a chair stands along the west wall. The beds are covered with well made quilts and lush furs.
9195:
A stove stands against one wall here.
A Beorning child stands here, craning his neck skywards.
A little girl runs around underfoot.
A dark woman moves with a determined look upon her face.

This is the main hall of the settlement; its walls are made from huge logs. A long wooden table, surrounded by chairs, takes up the majority of the space in this hall. In the western wall there is a huge stove built of thick irregular stones. The northern wall of the room is covered by some curtains.
9196: A young boy is here, bumping into things.

This small watchtower has been placed above the gates in the palisade. It has a thatched roof to protect the watchmen from sun and rain and its walls are made of thick planks. From up here it is possible to watch much of the surrounding land and easily keep track of people moving around.
9197:
Massive roots shift uneasily all around you.
Massive roots shift uneasily all around you.
A tiny spider is here, eating a tiny bug.
A giant earth beetle is standing here.

The air is damp and has an earthy smell to it. The walls and floor consist of dark, rich soil. Roots of different sizes penetrate through walls like long fingers as they try and find fresh soil for water and nutrients.
9198:
A very strong orkish leader is here on patrol.
An orc soldier is standing here.
An orc soldier is standing here.
An orc soldier is standing here.
An orc soldier is standing here.

This was once a tunnel in the earth, but the beams that once supported its ceiling eventually rotted too much to hold the weight of the earth above and collapsed. Small pieces of bone peek up from the pile of rubble, showing where a traveller was crushed. The room is filled with dirt, pieces of broken ceiling-beams, and small rocks. This passage way leads only to the east now.
9199:
An orc sentry is here on patrol.
An orc sentry is here on patrol.

Here the old escape route turns from south to east. The floor is covered with debris and rocks, showing where some of the ceiling caved in at one time. In the eastern wall is a small, dark opening from where a strong smell of decay emanates.
9200: This low and humid room must once have been a storage chamber judging from the debris and scraps of storage boxes that lie on the floor. The strong smell of rot and decay that fills the entire cave-like room comes from where things were once stored. The ceiling is low; what might have been an exit in it has been destroyed by the movement of the ground over time. To the west, an opening leads to a passage away from here.
9201: This is an old tunnel, dug through the earth from north to south. To the south, the faint sound of water moving about can be heard; northwards there is a deep and quiet darkness. The walls and ceiling are buttressed by heavy beams of some dark wood, which seem to have rotted in places, but they are still capable of supporting the roof.
9202:
