A half-decayed corpse of a goblin lies rotting on the ground.
Something cold and scaly slithers past your leg.
Something cold and scaly slithers past your leg.
A large leech is moving close to you, searching for blood.
A large leech is moving close to you, searching for blood.
A water moccasin slithers out of sight just below the surface of the water.
A water moccasin slithers out of sight just below the surface of the water.

This whole room inclines to the north where there is a large wooden door with metal fittings set in the wall. The room's slope leaves the southern half of the room flooded with water that at its deepest is only a few feet. The drier parts of the floor are covered with slightly damp soil. From what can be seen of the ceiling and walls, past massive spider webs, they appear to be formed of stone blocks with tangles of roots protruding through them.
9203:
A large leech is moving close to you, searching for blood.
A large leech is moving close to you, searching for blood.
A fierce-looking eel lurks in the darkness.
A long slender eel glides along the water, its body coiled to strike.

There appear to be walls in every direction except to the east. Vision is limited to a couple feet but it's possible to feel a small current in the water. The bottom seems to slope upwards to the east. The only roof that can be seen is water.
9204:
A large cockroach is crawling on the floor.
A giant, mean looking earth beetle is standing here.
A stocky mountain mule is here, waiting to serve.
A black, scaled reptile (two) is standing here.
A black, scaled reptile (one) is standing here.

The walls of this ancient cellar are made of huge, greyish stone blocks that were once perfectly joined. Some water trickles in between the blocks; no one has tried to plug the holes up and no other maintenance seems to have been done in quite a long time. At the far end there is a pool of water on the wooden floor. The floorboards are slippery with green moss and the ceiling beams are covered with spider webs.
9206: This is one of the few inns in this part of the land; unfortunately there is not much left of it. A large pile of broken wood scraps lies heaped in the middle of the floor. There is a staircase at the eastern side of the inn, suggesting that at some point there used to be a second floor to this building. The staircase does not lead anywhere now, as the walls have been demolished, with the roof collapsing in on top due to lack of support.
9207: A large bookshelf sits against the wall.

There are rumours of a great chieftain of the woodsmen, who lived in this area. His exact residence was not certain, but it may have been this village. This old lodge would most likely have been his dwelling. Not much is left intact, save a large wooden bookshelf against the northern wall. Next to the eastern wall the bed has taken heavy damage from an axe and now lies splintered and broken. A shattered desk has been left heaped at the western wall.
9208: In the middle of a large carpet of shattered limestone stands a large altar made of white marble, as evidence of the glorious chapel that once stood here. Now the altar is the only remaining vestige of that chapel, for those things that do not lie shattered on the ground among the limestone have probably been stolen or burnt.
9209: A circular stone well has been built here.

Apart from the surrounding ruins this old square has remained completely intact. A large white fountain containing two remarkable statues at its centre is the most noticeable of this courtyard's features. One of the statues depicts a huge bear standing upright. The other one is of a large man, in ranger's dress, wielding a beautifully carved longbow.
9210: Pieces of shattered and charred rock lie scattered all over the ground, mixed with piles of debris and burned wood. What was once a house is now a mere pile of rubble, all former markings and traces of architecture obliterated by some great force.
9211: Inside the Belly of an Old Tree

A small termite is running around making strange sounds.
A small termite is running around making strange sounds.
A small termite is running around making strange sounds.
A giant termite is here, crushing skulls and bones (red aura).
Some roots lie here waiting to ensnare weary travellers.

You are inside the belly of a very old tree that is almost completely rotten, the only thing that is fairly intact is its roots and parts of the branches. At the top of the tree you can see the sky lying above like a large carpet. You can also hear the whispers of a river that must be sneaking around somewhere nearby.
9212: The strong scent carried on the air is one of stagnancy and decay. It is similar to rotting flesh, although no bodies are evident here, or in the area below. This oak tree is obviously ancient, and these branches show signs of decay, greatly weakening their support. This part of the tree appears to have died long ago, and the rest of the tree is sure to follow. Looking down, the ground below seems incredibly far away; falling from this height could cause serious injury.
9213:
An albino fish is swimming here, looking for some food.
An albino fish is swimming here, looking for some food.
An albino fish is swimming here, looking for some food.
Dark water swarms around you. The sound of rushing water floods the room. Cracks and crevices along the edges of the cavern allow the water to slowly creep out towards other underground tributaries.
9214: A long slender eel glides along the water, its body coiled to strike.

The skeletal remains of various creatures float aimlessly atop the water's surface. Throughout the cave one can smell the stench of decay. Maggots cling to the rocks feasting on the slowly eroding remains. At times bits of rotting flesh form a layer of white debris lining the bottom of the water bed having been stripped from the bones by what must have been the force of powerful water creature.
9215:
An albino salamander is here, perched on some rocks.
An albino salamander is here, perched on some rocks.
An experienced orkish scout is looking for tracks on the ground.

This portion of the tunnels moves its way downward at a steady pace. Soon you realise that you have descended a significant distance. The sounds of booted feet echo around you, muffled in the damp air, giving you no clue as to their general direction. Pools of water swarm into the room at an even current from the south. Toward the northern section, the water level is as high as two or three feet in depth. Dark blurs blink in and out of sight in the murky water. Peering northward, the tunnels floor drops dramatically allowing the flowing water to find a home.
9216: An underground cavern splits off into smaller branches deep into the darkness. The broken stumps of stalactites and stalagmites suggest this deep traverse to be a naturally formed area into which the twisting tunnels converged. The air is moist and the walls breathe seeping water that trickles to small pools along the stoned floor. Eventually, the pools form some sort of convergence and begin to move downward to the north.
9217: From the east, the tunnel plunges sharply downwards into the darkness. The spikes here reach both the floor and the ceiling, forming fantastic columns of granite and limestone. The air here is damp, as if the weight of the stone has squeezed water from the rock itself.
9218: *a Morruhk Orc* (dead), wielding a heavy morningstar, is standing here.

From the intersection to the west, this passage takes a fairly straight plunge towards the east. Angled slightly downward, the gaping black hole presses down on the ceiling. The smooth nature of the floor in contrast to rough hewn sides suggests the passage to be well travelled. The unmistakable smell of orcs hangs in the air.
9219: This tunnel probes its way from the east to a small cave north, sloping steadily downward. The floor here is worn not from time, but from the heavy step of thousands of boots. The jagged and protruding stone leaking from its steady interior wall makes it unclear on how the tunnel was made.
9220: *a Morruhk Orc* (dead), wielding a heavy morningstar, is standing here.

This natural cave looks rather old. The air here is damp, and the northern and western walls bear no marks of any kind. To the east it looks as if somebody has, rather brutally, battered the rock into a hole and then fitted a large iron door there. To the south a small opening leads into a passage.
9221:
A studded leather belt has been left here.
A huge orc bodyguard looks at you suspiciously.
The dark presence of the Monitor stands at the stone door.
A huge orc bodyguard looks at you suspiciously.

This small chamber is evidently a guarded entrance to an Orkish lair, perhaps to the feared Goblin-town itself. A massive stone door lies to the south, hiding contorted tunnels infested by unknown fell beasts and cunning, evil Orcs. The walls are scarred with many blood-encrusted scratches, as if someone had used them to clean a sword. A half-hidden crack leads to a small natural cave connected to the outside, where Goblins can waylay hapless travellers. A sign has been scribbled near the crack.
9222: The large tunnel opens up and burrows its way downward into utter darkness. The hard stone floor is worn smooth by countless feet from the passage of orcs. The dark, oppressive atmosphere reeks of foul beings, beings to whom the sun is obsolete. Here, darkness reigns supreme, where goodness will only die. The tunnel travels to the east, and to the north a huge stone door lies heavily secured. A huge barricade of rocks, wood, boulders, and other debris covers the tunnel to the west.
9223: The tunnel continues to the east and west. The walls close in slightly so that two may not comfortably walk abreast anymore. That seems to be an even trade-off as the footing becomes surer and the ceiling height rises slightly.
9224: A demon wolf lurks here, its dark form twisting and hiding its shape.

Two tunnels intersect here, one dipping down to the east and the other leading up to the south. The tunnels are slightly disjointed, as one floor is about six inches higher than the other floor. The sloppily done work was never corrected and the sharp edge has been worn down to a dull nub.
9225: The tunnel bends sharply upwards and travel becomes quite difficult. Rough handholds and footholds have been carved into the rock itself. Iron rings occasionally still holding a piece of frayed rope appear on either side under the hand holds. It is obvious, the goblins opted for the less upkeep intensive handholds.
9226: The tunnel levels out here before continuing a more gradual descent to the east. The walls are rough but show signs of wear indicating heavy usage. The ceiling here is abruptly taller than either side of the tunnel. It appears there was supposed to be another level above this one, but it was never completed.
9227: The roughly carved tunnel delves downward to the east. Contrasting with the crude construction of the walls, the floor has been worn smooth, at times making footing difficult.
9228: A combination of jagged rock jutting out at odd angles and low ceilings make travelling rather difficult. The floor has been worn smooth however after countless iron shod feet have stamped it into submission. The tunnel continues its descent to the east.
9229: The rough-hewn tunnel makes a sharp bend here leading up to the west. There seems to be a draught of air coming from the south which can only be explained by either a larger opening to the south or some form of ventilation. Whichever it is, the draught carries smells only an Orc could produce.
9230: The tunnel is almost completely level here. The tunnel continues to the south apparently coming to a dead end or a turn. The ground sharply raises to the north while a different tunnel leads to a larger area to the east. The tramping of many iron-shod feet can be heard in every direction, but the draft still comes from the east.
9231: The tunnel joins the main tunnel to the west and becomes a full cavern to the east. The remains of stalactites with glittery deposits of minerals lie in a heap piled in one corner. It looks as though someone or something was infatuated with the pretty lights and got a little too rough.
9232: The tunnel from the west has opened up into a large cavern. The cavern, unlike the roughly carved tunnels, seems to be a natural occurrence. Stalactites hang pendulously from the ceiling, and the soft drip-drip of water can be heard echoing from the south. A crudely bored exit mars the beauty of the natural cavern to the north.
9233:
A blasted forge, built into the rear wall, warms the area.
Kormock the orkish armourer is working at his bench.
An elite orc-guard is on sentry here.
An elite orc-guard is on sentry here.

This is a square room that looks as if it was chiselled with a dull spoon. The air holds the crisp smell of burned wood and molten metal. Built into the rear wall is a forge and a small bellows accompanies it. The whole area is tinged with a thick layer of soot.
9234: The cavern flows to the south and west. The walls fluidly join floor and ceiling with stalactites peppering the ceiling. Iron-shod torch brackets have been thrust into the walls to provide light but they have an appearance of neglect.
9235: Streaks of minerals line the eastern wall of this great cavern. The roof of the cavern is peppered with short stalactites that have escaped the abuse of the orcs. The cavern continues in all directions but east.
9236: This appears to be just west of the centre of the cavern. The roof vaults up to dizzying heights and it is obvious that this cavern is a natural occurrence. The soft drip-drip of water can be heard echoing from the south.
9237: This is the south-western end of the cavern. The light of torches comes from an opening in the west wall. The roof is still beyond vision, and the drip of water is very loud to the east.
9238:
A large bulletin board, entitled "News from the Goblin Gate", is mounted here.
A brown pond between old branches and roots is here.
The orkish loremaster is standing here, looking for his audience.

The walls are irregularly shaped and sweep drunkenly from the west to the south. A small tunnel has been carved through the wall to the east. Iron brackets have been punched into the walls, with rust coloured marks marring the walls beneath them.
9239:
An elite orc-guard is on sentry here.
Gruksh, an orkish butcher is standing here.

Stacks of flour, and huge barrels marked in Orkish take up most of the room. In one corner is a huge cauldron with a shaft directly over it removing the smoke from the room. A pleasant scent of some kind of meat simmering in the cauldron assails the senses. To the east is a tunnel and to the south a room with a table can be glimpsed.
9240: A demon wolf lurks here, its dark form twisting and hiding its shape.

The overpowering stench of ripened flesh greets you with open arms. The room itself is squared off with a thick door that is barred from this side. The rock has taken on an uneven dark brown colour that seems darkest by a table that has been cut out of one wall. The table shows the scoring of a very sharp knife.
9241:
The corpse of a prisoner is lying here.
A prisoner is sitting here, looking at you with sad eyes.
A weary slave who has lost all hope sits here staring into space.
A weary slave who has lost all hope sits here staring into space.

A small room which is almost completely dark. In the corner is a candle made from the fat of some animal. The candle gives off a greasy light, casting shadows on the few possessions the room contains. Shackles adorn each wall, the metal dulled by the dried blood from a long catalogue of abused prisoners.
9242: The arch above blends into the wall to the east to form the corner of the great hall. Swirling winds, no doubt created by the oculus high above, have gathered small pieces of matted fur and other such sundries into a little pile in the corner. The hall continues to the south and west.
9243: A snaga is here, trying to sharpen a set of blood-encrusted needles.

The eastern wall of the great hall continues in both directions and becomes a corner a bit to the north. All around, the hall dwarfs everything in sight. Thin reeds of smoke, from the iron brackets on the walls and the fire in the middle, drunkenly stagger inexorably to the oculus in the centre of the hall.
9244: The eastern wall of the hall continues unabated with no break that can be seen. In every direction, the hall vaults to massive heights. Thin reeds of smoke from the iron brackets on the walls and the fire in the middle claw for freedom through the oculus in the centre of the dome.
9245: Two walls of the great hall coming crashing down from the lofty dome and form the south-eastern corner. The hall extends in every other direction, broken only by various tunnels and rooms breaking through the monotony of the walls.
9246: A huge and awesome dealer in black leather is here (glowing).

Crude stone tables play host to several decks of cards ready to be dealt. The cards themselves are ripped and bent and several look about to tear apart. The dealer's pit is arranged in such a way that he looks to stands taller than his actual height giving him an even more imposing presence than he already possesses. A few low hanging torches on the stone walls provide just enough illumination to see one's hand. The stench of spirits and the unwashed fill the air. A well-worn chest secured under a large and practically immobile boulder contains today's house winnings.
9247: A gnarled and crouching old orc is here, his head hung low.

This is the chamber of evil, where Harkz uses his spare time to come up with new ways of torturing elves and hobbits. In one corner there are a few machines standing in a circle that is used only for this purpose. Along another wall there is what looks like a bed, but instead of soft grass or something similar it is built upon bones of dead whities, with only a red blanket thrown on top of it.
9249: This small ledge widens out to the east and becomes another tunnel. A short drop down is another set of tunnels, the soft plink-plink of running water can be heard from there. It seems the two tunnels were meant to meet but were slightly off.
9250: This rather narrow and rough-hewn tunnel appears to have been carved as an afterthought. Sprouts of jutting rock reach up to trip the unwary passerby.
9251: Rough walls meet a rougher floor. The broken nubs of stalactites occasionally peak down from the roof, making it necessary to bend one's head to avoid a collision.
9253: A demon wolf lurks here, its dark form twisting and hiding its shape.
The crudely carved tunnel extends in either direction. More attention seems to have been paid to the floor here as the footing is sure, but it appears to get more tricky to the west.
9254:
A limping orc shuffles around here. He looks miserable.
An albino salamander is here, perched on some rocks.
An albino fish is swimming here, looking for some food.
An albino salamander is here, perched on some rocks.
An orc-guard is on patrol here.

Here, the cave dips lower into the bowels of the earth, collecting the moisture from the surrounding walls, and creating a shallow pool. About 6 centimeters deep, the polished surface is broken by many crooked rocks jutting above the surface. Littered in every direction are the bones of the small lizards that make up the staple food for the majority of the invalid orcs. This appears to be their main hunting ground.
9255:
An albino salamander is here, perched on some rocks.
An albino salamander is here, perched on some rocks.
A hungry warg stands here, sniffing around for flesh.

This area looks like the unlucky victim of an angry god's wrath. It looks only vaguely cave-like, as though a mighty fist punched violently upon these rocks, smashing an irregular and sunken hole into the hardened granite. The slick mossy walls drip beads of water into tiny pockets along the jagged floor. Combined with the heavy proliferation of broken rocks, this ground makes an excellent home for small little creatures. Faint clicking and buzzing can be heard amongst the rocks, and farther ahead into the darkness.
9256:
An orc is slinking around trying to look inconspicuous.
A limping orc shuffles around here. He looks miserable.

Stale, diseased air permeates your clothing and flares your nostrils. All around you, bits of bones and tattered cloth lay strewn in utter apathy. Here, in this cavernous underground, the refugees and unwanted orcs live out their dying days. Most are old and crippled, of no use to anyone and unable to survive if not for the abundance of slow, weak prey that inhabit the surrounding rocks. Some are perhaps younger, but none without ghastly deficiencies, making them miserable, weak, cowardly beasts.
9257:
A rather heavy clay jar stands here.
A female orc stands glaring at you.
A female orc stands glaring at you.

The hard uneven ground is padded here by thickly piled skins. Off to one corner, a medley of medications and salves lay haphazardly and carelessly stuffed in broken clay jars. Little comfort however can be taken in the surroundings. The smell of stale blood and infected flesh cuts sharply through the humid warm air. This is certainly a place to rest, but for many, their final rest. A broken clay jar rests in pieces here...
9258: A crippled orc (x) is standing here.

Altogether uncomfortable, even by orcs' standards, these pocked walls drip with a tepid moisture. Unsure if the moisture comes from the rocks, or the crowded breaths of so many orcs, the smell is quite pungent and stifling. Along the uneven floor, attempts at comfort have been made: piles of greasy warg fur lay bundled in heaps, partly negating the rocky surface beneath.
9259: Rusted weapons and broken shields lie hanging on pegs, or thrown casually down. This appears to have once been the main armourery for the forward gates, but is now deserted and unused. Since new passages were built closer to Wolf's Gate, the guard's armoury was relocated to a more suitable spot. The worn tunnel is a relic from a time when this area was constantly used, now, the most frequent visitors are little rodents scavenging for food.
9260: An orc is hobbling around on rudimentary crutches.

This small cramped cave was obviously built recently. Rough and irregular, the walls have no shape or pattern. The rock, a light porous limestone, burns at your skin and urges you to leave. Incredibly, someone or thing has made this a home; a light bed of pelts rests over most of the cave, barely enough room to lie asleep in. In the other corner, bones of fish and reptiles, a meager but forced diet.
9261: Rough and jagged, this tunnel is a crudely crafted extension of the natural fissure in the wall. Obviously not made by the skilled hands which carved the Burrow, this corridor was built quickly, and with little skill. As though travelling through a hallway of a sinking ship, this tunnel lists heavily downwards and pitched to the right. Faint motion and shuffling can be heard beyond the makeshift partition ahead.
9262: A cockroach is scuttling across the floor carrying some debris.

Over time, the constant beat of thousands of feet have softened and weakend these walls. Years of constant vibrations have caved in the softer rock, leaving a natural opening in this wall. The smooth marble-like walls of the Burrow roughly end here, slaking off into a mass of rubble underfoot. Venturing deeper inwards will lead you away from the safe footing of the smooth thoroughfare.
9263: Made by the same crude labour that built the tunnel to the east, work in this direction was apparently halted. Whether it was the resolve of the rock to prevent passage this way, or sheer laziness of the workers, the area lies unfinished and irregular. Shaped like a pear, the cavern grows thinner and abruptly stops about 2 meters from where you stand.
9264: You stand within the Burrow, a tube-like tunnel carved through the centre of the mountain above you. To the east and the west it stretches as if by the force of its own will, cleaving the mountain stone before it. Your feet step sure-footed upon the smooth floor of stone, smoother than any cobble or wooden floor. The walls arch above your head, a dome of grey rock above as the floor is a bowl before you as you follow the rock of the tunnel into the darkness.
9265: A warrior of Goblin Gate stands menacingly before you.

Ever onward this underground road travels, its course shaped eastern and western by the oppressing rock around it. Carved out of the mountain ore, it winds through the peak's bowels like a lonely worm, digging its way through the earth's darkest and hidden places, buried far beneath the fields of Bree or the evil desolation of Mordor. Here it is you stand, in a pocket of life beneath the mountain stone, within the embrace of this subterranean highway known as The Burrow.
9266: A hungry warg stands here, sniffing around for flesh.

Confident and straight in its eastern and western course, The Burrow extends from where you stand like a snake with two heads, each pulling in opposite directions, held taught in its course by rocky petrification. The smooth walls extend their curving embrace on all sides of you, the grey hewn and smooth like flesh. The bowled flooring slides you towards the centre, where your foot finds easy progress over stones as smooth as glass.
9267: Wide and spacious, this tunnel opening appears to be a main branch off the Burrow. Girded and supported by smooth granite arches, this junction could withstand the force of a legion of pounding trolls. Although cracked from years of neglect and stress, they still give you a sense of security, as though nothing from above could cave in these smooth walls.
9268: An orc-guard is on patrol here.

Arched like the back of a screeching cat, this tunnel angles upwards and then bows back at a downward slope. Torches line the walls at even intervals indicating that this is either a somewhat important, or well used, route. Up in the distance however, the yellow light fails to break the darkness, leaving you to wonder what lies in the deep pool of black ahead.
9269: The tunnel here is wide and smooth. Flames lick at the walls from torches lit along the sides. Crackling with a hiss of steam, the torches are the only sound you can hear, magnified and reverberated against the glass like surface. Here, the tunnel opens a new mouth to the east, and continues further into the darkness to the south.
9270: The tunnel sharply cuts to the west now, preventing you from seeing what lies there. Perhaps it is of some importance, as the area around you looks well worn and kept. A sagging and rotted door lies in your path. Why would those who maintained this area so well have failed to repair an obviously broken door?
9271:
A patch of moss grows here on a wet, flat stone.
A giant slug is here, oozing around.

The natural rock of this cave is made of some type of limestone. Pourous and fragile, it makes the perfect nesting ground for Slug larvae. The tiny holes seep and bubble a green slime, pulsing and oozing out of the rock's pores. You almost have difficulty moving, as your feet congeal to the sticky slug vomit below.
9272: The tunnel smoothens slightly here. The walls and ceiling still bulge and twist with stubborn wills of their own, but the floor here is smooth and passable. Faint tracks lay etched in the stone where at one point, ore laden carts once traversed. Now, filled with rusty-red water, they resemble small arteries travelling deeper into the mines.
9273: The walls bleed pasty red drop around you. Streaks of oxidized metal, turned bright red, resemble violent scars upon these hollowed walls. Far deeper, a bright streak of silver and copper catches your eyes, sparkling down the length of the vein, and disappearing into the darkness ahead. A weathered and sagging sign stands here.
9274:
A rusty pickaxe with a broken handle lies discarded here.
A huge orc bodyguard looks at you suspiciously.
A huge orc bodyguard looks at you suspiciously.
Guthblug the Foreman is here, scowling at you furiously.
An elite orc-guard is on sentry here.
An elite orc-guard is on sentry here.
An elite orc-guard is on sentry here.

The tunnels twist and turn as they lead down into the mines. Stone walls have been carved here by brute force, and timbers shore up the mine entrance to the south. From within you can hear the sounds of metal on stone and rock dust hangs in the air. An abandoned ore cart has been overturned here.
9276: Rusted tools lie scattered across the ground. The mark of chisel tools across the rock is apparent. A small hole along the rock-face was probably tampered with and forced open at one time or another. Whatever lies in there, the orcs seem to have purposely left behind.
9277: A dark and dreary cave leads south towards the unknown. Not a sound can be heard, and the usual boot prints are nowhere to be seen.
9278: The air here is colder than before, but there is no wind. The rock face is jagged and twisted, announcing its natural shape.
9279:
A newborn spider is here, hungrily crawling about.
A newborn spider is here, hungrily crawling about.

The passage makes a slow turn here from the north to the east. The air continues to be cold and stale. Your boots seems to stick to the floor, and cobwebs hang across the ceiling, some even reaching the floor.
9280:
The corpse of a huge, venomous spider is lying here.
The corpse of a huge, venomous spider is lying here.
The corpse of a huge, venomous spider is lying here.
Turning from west to the north, this passage narrows a bit as it continues. Strings of thick, sticky web connect from the walls to the floor and ceiling.
9281: A grey spider is stalking here, preparing to drain you of life.
Entering the round cavern, you notice hundreds of webs covering the walls, floor, and ceiling. Shadows of pitchy darkness hide much of the room.
9282:
A very strong orkish leader is here on patrol.
An orc soldier is standing here.
An orc soldier is standing here.

This portion of the tunnel plunges steeply into the depths, carrying you along in its dark embrace. The blackness before you invokes images of dreams and nightmares. The sounds of booted feet ring off the rough worn surfaces of this tunnel; a promise that something lives down here.
9283: Weaving from side to side, this tunnel moves at a downward slope. Despite the depths already travelled, there seem to be yet deeper places to explore.
9284: To the north, the tunnel narrows considerably. Cracks along the floor board indicate some sort of pounding, be it natural or man-made.
9285:
A demon wolf lurks here, its dark form twisting and hiding its shape.
A demon wolf lurks here, its dark form twisting and hiding its shape.
The tunnel continues straight, rising slightly in the northern direction. Prints of boots, aligned in double file, mark the dusted floor.
9286: The tunnel here is level, but slowly angles upwards to the south. Steady and heavy traffic occupies this area, and the sounds of orcs is very near. All along the floor, piles of refuse are scattered haphazardly. Cracks in the ground zigzag across the floor. And, to the western side of the tunnel, there is a wide pit, jagged and ripped from the stone.
9287: The section of tunnel here continues north and south, opening up into a rounded chamber to the south. Continued sounds of activity are heard in the distance. The floor is heavily littered with bits and pieces of recognizable and unknown items. A foetid smell of excrement and orc fills the stale air here.
9288: An orc is slinking around trying to look inconspicuous.

This area has been roughly carved into a round room which serves as a resting area for the wandering traveller or any guard on break from patrolling duty. The tunnel continues its descent to the north, and steadily rises to the east.
9289: Narrow and ill-wrought, this passage was roughly hewn from the stone of the mountain. The floor is worn away and smooth from its over use, but the ceiling is cracked and jagged, untouched by blunt tools. To the west, the twisting corridor widens dramatically revealing a small chamber.
9290: The passageway widens to the east, sloping upward ever so ruggedly. Then it ends abruptly in a huge cave-in. The stone is cracked and indented, looking like the rock itself moved at its leisure. To the north, the tunnel narrows considerably, allowing only double file formation.
9291: The tunnel apparently used to continue both east and west, following a rather crooked line. However it seems like somebody recently tore down the tunnel to the west, where fresh marks from picks and mattocks can be seen.
9292: Branching off from the main tunnel to the east, the tunnel continues for quite a distance to the west. The soft trickling of water can be heard from the larger junction to the east. The walls seem rougher, and the footing less sure, as if this tunnel received less traffic than the other.
9293: This is the former home of the representatives from the Zaugurz tribe. The cave was once quite comfortable, but it is now completely demolished and desecrated. Rubble and debris covers the floor. Remains of a door lies in the opening to the east.
9294: The tunnel abruptly ends in a mass of broken rock, the walls close in and the footing is quite tricky. A narrow opening in the heap of rubble and stones leads into the pile, supported by planks and the occational tree. A few dried out pools of a deep red colour line the cracks and sharper edges.
9295:
A shadowy and lithe orc stands here, half-hidden in the darkness.
A shadowy and lithe orc stands here, half-hidden in the darkness.
You catch sight of the lithe form of Kraksh, the Scoutmaster.

Cunningly hidden by the Goblin stonemasons, this small cave bears the marks of heavy weapon use. Deep marks and gouges line every wall but the entrance. Obviously, some form of weapons training went on here, but it remains a mystery why the cave would be hidden from prying eyes. The wall containing the entrance bears none of the abuse that the other three do. Someone assiduously avoided giving a clue as to what lay behind the door.
9296: The tunnel begins a slight decline to the north. It has that shabby look of neglect as telltale signs of age and forgotten remains of meals long past make for an unpleasant sight. The tunnel continues to the south.
9297: The walls of the tunnel seem to crush in temporarily as the tunnel narrows unexpectedly. Just as abruptly the tunnel turns to the south and east, seemingly on a whim.
9298: The tunnel appears to level off here. The rocky outcroppings make for excellent handholds and it seems many travellers have used them as such. The walls show the slightly slick feel of untold hands wearing down the sharp rock. There is a small cavern to the west but it appears to be empty.
9299: The tunnel widens as it goes south here. Thin rivulets of water flow from cracks in the otherwise sheer rock walls. The water collects in the centre of the tunnel in a shallow depression and slowly flows south. Wet footprints cover the floor and travel both north and south.
9300:
A demon wolf lurks here, its dark form twisting and hiding its shape.
A demon wolf lurks here, its dark form twisting and hiding its shape.

The tunnel becomes a small cavern here. Cracks in the vaulted roof let in several small trickles of water which join to form a small stream flowing softly to the south. Not more than half an inch deep at any point, silt and other refuse has piled up to form a sort of bank to one side.
9301: You have reached the westernmost part of a large room; a third iron gate lies directly to the south. The musty odour of animal seems to emanate from here. It is much heavier than before, and it is an almost palpable thing. Perhaps this is due to the lack of ventilation, or perhaps the source of the smell is nearby. The floor, like in front of the other two doors, shows a dark red liquid not quite dry puddling on the stone floor.
9302:
A demon wolf lurks here, its dark form twisting and hiding its shape.
A demon wolf lurks here, its dark form twisting and hiding its shape.
The stone has been worked into a rough cul-de-sac, serving as some sort of kennel. The stench of dung pervades even the solid rock, as the place has not been cleaned in a very long time.
9303:
A demon wolf lurks here, its dark form twisting and hiding its shape.
A demon wolf lurks here, its dark form twisting and hiding its shape.

Another stone cul-de-sac has been formed here, in a series of animal kennels throughout the complex. A thick layer of fur and dung covers the entire floor, marked by animal tracks dug deep into the accumulated filth.
9304:
A demon wolf lurks here, its dark form twisting and hiding its shape.
A demon wolf lurks here, its dark form twisting and hiding its shape.

Simply another alcove hewn out of the stone, the most remarkable feature is the foetid smell. The dung, both new and old, lays thick upon the ground. Barely large enough for one animal, the kennel serves to keep a multitude locked in.
9305:
A demon wolf lurks here, its dark form twisting and hiding its shape.
A demon wolf lurks here, its dark form twisting and hiding its shape.

This room bears the remains of many orcs staying in one spot. Gobbets of flesh and other dried spots dot the wall and floor of this place. In the corner is a small table with two shakey looking chairs around it.
9306:
A long water trough made of wood stands here.
A heavily scarred orc is standing here.
Nightbird the Morruhk Orc, wielding an engraved warhammer, is standing here.

The musty odour of animal is prominent here. The stone is blotchily stained dark red and some of it is still wet in places. A rusty iron gate occupies the south wall, but still looks serviceable. The area extends to the west and similar iron gates can be glimpsed.
9307: Nightbird the Morruhk Orc, wielding an engraved warhammer, is standing here.

This is the central part of a large room. A second iron gate closes off a chamber to the south. The overwhelming smell of animal is perhaps even stronger here. The floor is a mishmosh of stone and blotchy areas of a dark red liquid not yet dry in places.
9308:
A gnarled and crouching old orc is here, his head hung low.
A demon wolf lurks here, its dark form twisting and hiding its shape.

This small passage slants up from the Chamber of Combat, hewn from the surrounding stone with the same rough violence. Trickles of blood seep slowly down the floor, and a deliciously meaty smell wafts from the south.
9309: The entire hall vaults up to a cunningly crafted dome that seems to draw smoke away from any fires that may be lit here. The hall recedes everywhere except to the immediate west and south. An opening in the wall can be seen a bit to the east.
9310: The hall extends on every side except the south which is filled with a ornately carved gate rusted open. The distinctive smell of urine assails your senses from that direction.
9311: The hall continues unabated in every direction but south. To the south, the monotony of the wall is broken by a stout wooden door. The oddity of a wooden door amidst a mass of stone is something to remark upon.
9312: A demon wolf lurks here, its dark form twisting and hiding its shape.

Situated almost directly beneath the centre of the huge dome, smoky tendrils reach from various points of the hall and head directly for the oculus. They give the appearance of giving shadowy support to the huge dome.
9313: Almost straight up is the small hole drawing any smoke generated in the hall. All around the great hall extends, but to the west a gaping hole has been rent.
9314:
A shadowy and lithe orc stands here, half-hidden in the darkness.
A shadowy and lithe orc stands here, half-hidden in the darkness.
An orkish master-warrior torments his recruits here.

The room has been brutally carved from the rock. Not a straight plane or angle is evident and that seems to be the intended effect. Weakly flickering torchlight dances on the untamed walls making the rock seem a thing alive and dancing.
9315: The ceiling vaults to twice its normal height here as if to somehow indicate the importance of this junction. A great hall, with stalactites and stalagmites arranged to give the appearance of a great maw ready to devour unwitting travellers, opens to the east. The tunnel begins a slow descent to the north and travels on unhurriedly to the west.
9316: A demon wolf lurks here, its dark form twisting and hiding its shape.

This is a huge hall that extends to the east and south. The entire hall vaults up to a cunningly crafted dome that seems to also draw smoke away from any fires that may be lit here. The hall shows signs of habitation with strewn bones and mouldy pieces of something even an orc will not eat. To the west the hall narrows to a smaller, rougher-carved tunnel.
9317: A demon wolf lurks here, its dark form twisting and hiding its shape.

This is the northernmost part of the Great Hall of the Goblins. Above, the room makes an arch terminating to the east and west and vaulting to a dome to the south. Iron brackets fixed to the wall provide a murky light, and in some instances more smoke than light. The smoke can be seen lazily climbing to an oculus placed in the centre of the dome.
9318: This is the northernmost part of the great hall. The northeastern corner is not very far from here. The lowest part of the dome, which vaults to almost dizzying heights to the south, is almost directly above you.
9319: The hall rises to a crescendo on all sides. The sheer enormity of the construction of this hall is mind boggling. Small pieces of matted fur flow lazily across the floor, pushed by an unseen wind.
9320: The hall rises to a crescendo on all sides. The sheer enormity of the construction of this hall is mind boggling. Small pieces of matted fur flow lazily across the floor, pushed by an unseen wind.
9321:
A large WARNING SIGN has been posted by the Great Goblin here.
A large bulletin board, entitled "The Board of the Tarkhnarb", is mounted here.
A great throne, a grim blend of jagged iron and stone, looms over the cavern.
The Great Goblin is here, looking at you in disapproval.
A huge orc bodyguard looks at you suspiciously.
A huge orc bodyguard looks at you suspiciously.
A huge orc bodyguard looks at you suspiciously.
A demon wolf lurks here, its dark form twisting and hiding its shape.

The hall peaks at an oculus directly above. All around, the hall extends and smoke slowly filters from all directions seeking an exodus through the oculus. Through a trick of the acoustics, snippets of sounds from around the hall sometimes coalesce into something intelligible.
9322: A demon wolf lurks here, its dark form twisting and hiding its shape.
The hall extends about an equal distance to each side as it does to the ceiling. Small bits of detritus are scattered here and they are scattered by an occasional breeze.
9323: The tunnel begins a slight decline to the north. The rocky outcroppings make for excellent handholds and it seems many travellers have used them as such. The walls show the slightly slick feel of untold hands wearing down the sharp rock. Telltale signs of age and neglect, piled upon forgotten remains of meals long past, make an unpleasant sight.
9324: A demon wolf lurks here, its dark form twisting and hiding its shape.
The tunnel makes yet another bend here, this time to the west. Though the ceiling is quite low, adequate footing can be found. The tunnel is quite wide here but narrows either way.
9325:
An officer of the Uruk-tarkhnarb stands before you.
A dark-skinned orkish veteran guard is on sentry here.

The tunnel straightens out from a bend and heads east for a while. The low ceiling makes for slow going, but footing is sure here as the tramping feet of countless orcs have worn any inconsistencies out of the floor.
9326: A hungry warg stands here, sniffing around for flesh.

The tunnel makes a bend to the north and east here. To the east the tunnel drops slightly before levelling out, while continuing on placidly to the north. A slight breeze can be felt circling slowly to the east.
9327: The slope of the tunnel lessens a bit here but drops off again to the north. The way southward bends around a corner, and travelling that way looks easier on tired feet. Footholds, or perhaps crude attempts at steps have been carved into the rock but have been worn almost away and the footing looks tricky.
9328: Takhr the orkish warden is standing here, looking greedily at your stuff.

The larger area to the north has tapered off to a rather tall tunnel extending as far as can be seen in the gloom to the south. On each side of the tunnel are small niches about the size of an Orc with large padlocks on them.
9329:
There are two straw pallets here.
A large stone fireplace with a roaring fire warms the room.
A hungry warg stands here, sniffing around for flesh.
A large brown wolf stands here, its teeth partly bared.
A hungry warg stands here, sniffing around for flesh.
A hungry warg stands here, sniffing around for flesh.

A rather large sleeping cave, with thin streams of water trickling forth from hidden springs inside the mountain -- forming small pools of fresh water on the cave floor. A ladder leads up through a hole in the ceiling, and no other exits are visible.
9330: A mailbox stands here stuffed full of messages.

The grey walls of granite here are stained a dark brown colour. Pieces of what used to be a table are strewn here with what appear to be teeth marks. To the south, the hall tapers off to a small tunnel extending into the distance.
9331: A large bulletin board, entitled "The Board of the Tarkhnarb", is mounted here.
The tunnel widens out into a large area littered with debris. The ceiling is tall even for the tallest of trolls and would fit three across comfortably. The hall continues to the south.
9332: This is more a junction than a continuation of the tunnel. It widens out to the west into a much larger area. Contrasting with the rest of the tunnels, the height of the ceiling is enough for even the tallest of Sauron's minions to stand upright. The walls have been worn smooth as glass.
9333: The walls of this tunnel has been worn smooth with years of use. The roughly carved rock has been worn to a smoothness that makes it reminiscent of a small stream with eddying currents. The tunnel continues to the east and empties into a cavern to the west.
9334: The well worn rock of the tunnel resembles a small stream flowing on the walls. The many tramplings of iron-shod feet have beaten the floor into submission. The tunnel continues to the east and west.
9335: The tunnel bears the marking of heavy usage. The walls and floor have been worn down to an almost glass-like surface. The tunnel continues to the east and west.
9336: The tunnel makes a sharp bend to the north here. The worn rock abruptly changes directions, shattering the impression of a frozen river suspended on the wall. Dust and other debris has gathered in the tight corner, even with the heavy usage.
9337: The tunnel jogs slightly to the north here, before returning to an east/west path. The worn rock flows smoothly around the bend, the stone worked to a soft sheen. A thin layer of dust cowers in the corners waiting to be swept away.
9338: The tunnel completes the jog started to the south and once again heads east. The smoothness of the rock gives testimony to the heavy usage this tunnel receives. Many iron shod feet have tramped this way and it almost seems possible to pick out individual footprints in some locations.
9339: A gnarled and crouching old orc is here, his head hung low.
In this small dark cave, filled with swampy trees, small creatures are crawling around. One can spot a small opening among the tree's to the west which seems to lead into a clearing.
9340: The lack of ambient sound in this part of the forest is a fitting accompaniment to the lack of trees. What natural or unnatural force created this barren spot is unknown. A scattering of decaying scalps, twisted metal shards and torn leather, however, gives evidence of recent activity.
9341: The tunnel, showing the strain of extreme usage, runs in an easterly direction. The footing is sure and the walls are smooth. There are no protruding rock outcroppings or dangling fragments of rock to reach up and snare the unwary traveller.
9342: The Burrow continues to make its way east here, eternally pushing aside the thick stone to tunnel its lonely way through the depths of the mountain. On either side the tunnel walls rise up like a wave, as if to crash down upon you, arching up into the ceiling of this underground road. What little your sight can glean in the distance, the tunnel simply continues away from you, until the gloom of the dark and oppressive mountain closes around you and limits your sight.
9343: Once the backwater channels for a mighty subterranean river, these cavern walls lack the smooth countenance typical of most of these tunnels. Uneven and covered with dry silt, the slowly moving water never softend and smoothed these pitted walls. The cavern leads both east and north, to the south lies the Burrow.
9344:
An orc sentry is here on patrol.
An orc sentry is here on patrol.

Like the walls of an ornate tribe of beasts, the irregular walls here are decorated with the imprints of fossilized creatures. Perhaps shaped in random patterns to our civilized eyes, who knows what song they sing to an unknown entity.
9345: Branching off to the east, this long dead river continues along its north- south course. Scattered on the floor, bits of broken deadwood and dry silt are the only remaining contents of the river. Its history however, is clear enough to see. While not as fierce as the rivers that carved the Burrow, it was powerful enough to forge these caverns.
9346: Here, the wall's composition changes from shale and limestone back to heavy thick granite. The river, meeting this stubborn force, was not powerful enough to drive through the stone. Perhaps slicing 10 meters into the rock, it gave out and instead glanced back south and to the east, travelling along the path of least resistance.
9347: This area must of once been something similar to a pool. Accepting the pounding water from the south, which was sent up this direction by stubborn walls of granite, it collected here widening the natural crevice into a smoother, hollow bowl. Tunnels lead off to the west, east and south.
9348: The tunnel, like a crazed arrow bouncing off heavy targets, darts south here. A fierce battle with the thick granite to the east prevented any advance, and instead, the old river cut through the soluble sulphur to the south. Now, eons later, dry sulphur dust fills the air where once a mighty river raged.
9349: Allowing enough buffer between yourself and the Burrow, the airy tunnel continues north-south. Torches and lanterns are forbidden on the walls, assuring no peep of light could betray those travelling within this pass. Free of all obstacles and well maintained, even the need for personal light is shunned.
9350: An elite orc-guard is on sentry here.

Reaching a peak here, the walls bank smoothly into a gentle turn, tunneling back towards the Burrow. Scattered farther to the east are secret mechanical doors, built within these granite walls. Using goblin mechanisms, the doors swing one way, preventing any intruders from gaining access to this secret route.
9351: An orc-guard is on patrol here.

Arching like a smooth black serpent, these walls turn southerly and to the west. The smooth floor is hidden here, lined instead with matted furs of black wargs and brown bears. Your footsteps, muffled in the unnatural bedding barely reach your ears before being lost within the inescapable grasp of these tunneled walls.
9352: A wet, gilled reptile-like creature lurks in the water here.

Here the water becomes strangely more turbulent. Peering into it, swirls of motion can be seen from its unfathomable depths. Tiny faint bubbles float to the surface, indicating all that may be down there is not simple harmless plant life.
9353: The mild sounds of crashing waves bounce endlessly off these cavern walls, mixing and blending into a cacophony of echos. Large drops of mountain chilled water fall from the ceiling, splashing the icy lake water into your face and eyes. Never touched by the light of Anar, Eru only knows what could live here.
9354: An albino fish is swimming here, looking for some food.

The mild sounds of crashing waves bounce endlessly off these cavern walls, mixing and blending into a cacophony of echos. Large drops of mountain chilled water fall from the ceiling, splashing the icy lake water into your face and eyes. Never touched by the light of Arien, Eru only knows what could live here.
9355:
A water moccasin slithers out of sight just below the surface of the water.
A water moccasin slithers out of sight just below the surface of the water.
A water moccasin slithers out of sight just below the surface of the water.

Cold water bites into your legs and ankles, sending a quick shiver up your spine. Scanning ahead, you try to determine if this is simply an underground stream, or the beginning of a lake. If it is a lake, swimming it in seems most foolish, who knows what creatures could lurk within it.
9357: Built as a resting area for the Pass, Orcs and Goblins can assemble here without bottling up the thoroughfare. Large granite boulders offer support for those simply waiting, and a small trickle of cold mountain water from a underground mountain stream offers water to parched and sticky lips.
9358: Dark and obscure, the walls around you are not easily defined. Your footsteps announce your presence to anyone nearby, as they crunch and crack over the thin limestone spears jutting awkwardly from the floor beneath. The sound of water and cold slimy splash of stilled pools at your feet, indicate water must be nearby.
9359: Carrying you on without purpose or destination, these natural caverns bend west and south. Faintly pungent in the air, the smell of water and fish, perhaps resting ahead lies some of the same water that once forged these tunnels.
9360:
A large mean-looking troll is here.
A grey-skinned mountain troll stands here.
An orc soldier is standing here.

Naturally built by the forces of underground streams and time, these smooth porous walls are shaped in large elliptical passages. Massive natural archways lead into underground lairs, where beasts who've never seen the glow of Arien dwell.
9361: Here the secret trail comes to an end. Directly south, under the protection of a hidden granite goblin door, Wolf's Gate lies. From this vantage point, orcs and goblins can add a second attack or bypass enemies along the Burrow. Scanning the cool grey granite around you, you feel relieved that you are on this side of the wall, an upper hand over any enemy.
9362:
An orkish chieftain is here, controlling his guards.
An elite orc-guard is on sentry here.
An elite orc-guard is on sentry here.

Here the Burrow abruptly ends in a wall of stone broken only by a thick pair of metal studded doors. From underneath the portals, your feet pick up a light breeze, could this be a way out? The walls are wide and smooth, the floor bowed in the middle by the passing of many feet. Into the darkness, to the west, The Burrow begins, spread out before you like the bowels of a mighty snake. Your sight can only carry so far, the mighty tunnel sliding away before you into the darkness and subterranean gloom.
9363:
An orc sentry is here on patrol.
An orc sentry is here on patrol.
An elite orc-guard is on sentry here.

Carved out of the rocky granite, this tiny alcove serves as a guard post, protecting the Burrow from any intruders. Jagged and hastily made, it can hold a maximum of three guards at any one time. Further behind it, a large iron gate rests on rusty hinges. Its purpose, unknown.
9364: A cockroach is scuttling across the floor carrying some debris.

Cut from the same smooth granite as most of these tunnels, this deep grey passage leads along a north-south axis. To the west, an opened cavern reeks with the smell of dirt and decay, unabled to be contained within its vast openness the odor belches into this tunnel. Another cavern opens to the east, a growling noise can be heard coming from there.
9365: Carrying you firmly along these tunnels, the smooth granite floors carry the sound of your footsteps down the corridor in front of you. Built rather recently, this passage lacks the worn smoothness of the main passageways. A set of iron bars, a makeshift holding cell for enemies caught spying within this sector, blocks your movement to the south. The tunnel continues along its natural course with a sharp west-north turn.
9366:
A heavily-scarred orc stands here, begrudging your presence.
A cockroach is scuttling across the floor carrying some debris.

Dozens of ravenous, smelly wargs, locked in a big cage, fill this room with their blood-chilling growls and howls. This is where the Goblins of Wolf's Gate train their favourite mounts and where, between one raid and another, they feed them with raw meat - or with captured travellers, whenever possible. A smaller cage houses some evil-looking black birds.
9367: A prisoner is sitting here, looking at you with sad eyes.

Surrounded by smooth granite walls, this rock acts as a better barrier than most of the metals that could otherwise be used. Damp and cold, it offers little comfort, not even a fur or blanket to rest upon. In fact, this small cubicle is completly devoid of anything, just four blank walls staring at you. A set of iron manacles rest here.
9368: The ceiling is very low and sagging wooden beams support a large amount of dirt and stone above your head. A large spider scurries away at your approach, and to the south you can see some activity and hear the rattling of chains. Somewhere in the distance someone is screaming.
9369: The air is putrid and stale in the pits. From deeper in the mine you can hear the sound of steel striking rock, and the harsh cries of orkish overseers. Piles of slag line the corridor, and on one of the rubbish heaps lies the mutilated corpse of an elf. To the east, the corrider continues deeper into the mines, and to the north it leads back towards the Burrow.
9370: Carved quickly and without skill, these gnashed and uneven walls drip icy water from an underground stream nearby. The floor, slippery and wet, forces you to slow down and tread carefully. A slip in these jagged tunnels would be painful.
9371: Faint grumbling and wailing can be heard from the make-shift prison ahead. Having no desire to end up there yourself, it is probably not wise to investigate. You can simply continue on your way, by heading along the straight east-west passage.
9372: The walls bleed pasty red drops around you. Streaks of oxidized metal, turned bright red, resemble violent scars upon these hollowed walls. Once perhaps, this area was mined for precious metals. Now left in abandonment, the walls have turned red with rust, giving an eerie and life-like appearence to this crumbling tunnel. A weathered and sagging sign stands here.
9373: Digging your heels into the broken rock floor, you continue travelling through this poorly made tunnel. The fear of collapse is non-existent as you stare at the defiant rocks that resisted the strength of ravaging waters, erosion and orc-driven picks. It is equally obvious, that falling here wouldn't prevent those same defiant rocks from piercing your body and leaving you dead for the rodents to consume.
9374: Carved in a circular shape, the tunnel ahead of you looks quite unnatural. Off to one side, huge piles of dirt lay compressed with time, lending evidence to the suspicion that this tunnel was made by no miner's hands. Small tracks of slime and the moist sticky walls around seem more like remnants left by a burrowing creature. It seems evident that this tunnel was never part of any original design.
9375: The smooth walls are broken here by larger stubborn rocks that refused to yield to the passage of time. Though worn away by erosion in some distant age when this area was flooded, they yet break the uniformity of the tunnel walls, giving them a lumpy, sickly appearance. Passage to the east is blocked by a large wooden door.
9376: A hungry warg stands here, sniffing around for flesh.

The walls breathe a cool air, stored deep from with the mountain, upon your face. The walls, slightly moist, continue smoothly to the South and West. Faint cart tracks, etched into the stone floor from years of loaded ore carts, lead you towards the quarries where the orcs mined much of their metals. Rusted water, collected in the ruts, resemble red-blood arteries, guiding you to their destiny.
9377: Like a godly barrier, the rock to the east withstood the tunnelling of The Burrow, forcing it to angle north around it like a stream bending around a rock. From where you stand you can barely glimpse the grey and dusky face of the passage as it fades into blackness to the west. To the east, you can see no alteration of its straight and rigid course, disappearing beyond your sight in a sea of earthen haze.
9378: Perhaps the rock had been simply too tough to break, or perhaps because of some shuddering of the earth, whatever the origin, The Burrow, instead of continuing straight on its east to west course bends to the south. To the east, you peer along its length til it is lost in the veil of darkness that surrounds you on all sides. To the west, The Burrow slides south, curving like the back of a slithering serpent far beneath the skies and sun, under this dark and distant peak.
9379: Strewn about, bits of steel and cloth indicate this area to be some sort of gathering place. Most likely, this is where the warriors of the gate change shifts, a crude attempt at enforcing order amongst the relatively orderless hordes of orcs and goblins invading these hollowed walls.
9380: The grey walls curve gently here, racing to meet with the Burrow. Curving both to the north and east, your vision is obscured in this subterranean gloom. Guided only by the thick granite walls, you can continue north, breaking away from the Burrow, or east, speeding you closer with its twin roadway.
9381: Built for silence and stealth, the tunnel continues along a north-south axis. The walls, cooled by the immense mountain surrounding them, act as a cooling pump, mingling with the stale imprisoned air to create a mild refreshing breeze. The smooth curved walls around you reflect your footsteps and send them echoing down into the darkness ahead.
9382: A small, mean earth troll is standing here, thinking of something hideous.

Hard black granite stones form this small beach. Sheltered by the jagged rocks encircling it, it has been protected from most of the water, a main reason why it still exists. Crunching the stones beneath your feet, you search for any signs of activity here, but none can be found.
9383: The mild sounds of crashing waves bounce endlessly off these cavern walls, mixing and blending into a cacophony of echos. Large drops of mountain chilled water fall from the ceiling, splashing the icy lake water into your face and eyes. Never touched by the light of Anar, Eru only knows what could live here.
9384: The familiar sound of crashing waves is noticeable ahead. Looking downwards, the calcium-limestone floor abruptly ends, roughly 10 centimeters down from the lip along the rock, water laps against the impasse. Throwing your light in front of you, it is reflected along the tiny waves of this underground lake.
9385: Large craggy rocks hang from the ceiling and up through the floors. While made of a soft limestone, their jagged spears could easily disembowel anyone foolish, or unlucky enough to trip upon them. Collecting in small pockets around the scarred ground are dark pools of black water, you feel it wise not to drink from these shallow stagnant pools.
9386: A warrior of Goblin Gate stands menacingly before you.

The sharp smell of rotting fish flares your nostrils and constricts your throat. These walls, worn naturally by the erosion of underground streams, head further into the darkness, perhaps to the source that first shaped them.
9387: An orc soldier is standing here.

Narrowing the distance between the two twin roads, the passage cuts southwards again. Those travelling to the far end of the Burrow, a sharp westwards turn hastily adds further rock between the two serpentine tunnels.
9388: An orc soldier is standing here.

Nearing the secret junction with Wolf's Gate, the pass continues east-west. Here, the tunnel widens even more, pratically into an open cavern, allowing troops to assemble without impeding swift travel along the pass. The smooth granite walls are nicked and gnashed here, the victims of angry swords and shows of bravado.
9389: An orc-guard is on patrol here.

You stand within one of the many miles of The Burrow, a huge tunnel which seems to snake like a giant worm under the mountain. The walls have long been shorn to a smooth, almost slick surface. The floor curves like the bottom of a bowl, smooth and quick to carry you. To either side, to the east and to the west, The Burrow continues its tunnelling, unaware of the time or seasons passing far above, in the sky and heavens of Arda.
9390: The walls ring with the clatter of metal and commotion. Bootsteps can be heard clanging off the walls and the grumblings and murmurs of Orcs echo off the walls to your ears. To the south, a bright fire casts light into this room, bringing some heat to the cold smooth granite walls surrounding you.
9391:
An experienced orkish scout is looking for tracks on the ground.
A hungry warg stands here, sniffing around for flesh.

This stuffy cave serves as an all purpose resting-eating-sleeping ground for the Orc Guards. Piled in one corner, matted filthy furs lie, a small solace for the weary orc. Heaped in another corner, piles of bones and rotting flesh, the meals cast aside of busy or late guards.
9392: Dark and gloomy, even a brightly lit torch would fail to peel much darkness from this blackly painted darkness. Cold draughts of air whose origins lie deep in the mountain mix with icy water here and chill you to the bone. The wind whips in an almost regular pattern, as though you are caught in the giant breaths of the mountain.
9393: A hungry warg stands here, sniffing around for flesh.

The walls bleed pasty red drops around you. Streaks of oxidized metal, turned bright red, resemble violent scars upon these hollowed walls. Once perhaps, this area was mined for precious metals. Now left in abandonment, the walls have turned red with rust, giving an eerie and life-like appearance to this crumbling tunnel.
9394: Like the hallways of a tossing ship, this tunnel swerves to the right and left, pitching you forward and backwards. The rocks lay scarred here, bitten by the picks and axes of a legion of miners, and yet defiantly intact. Standing upright against the floor like a fanged snake, dangerously sharp rocks threaten to stumble and impale the unwary traveller.
9395: Continuing along this narrow and scarred tunnel, it becomes clear that it is not safe. Large polyps of huge stones bar you safe passage through most of the tunnel, forcing you to constantly climb and shift from side to side. Eru only knows why the miners felt a need to continue, but the passage continues to the south and north.
9396: This irregularly shaped entrance is narrowed and made dangerous by large rocky outcrops of unmeasurably hard and solid rock. Movement in here would be slow and tedious, as one must carefully step to avoid stumbling. Here, the miners battled with the very forces of Arda to tunnel a passageway, making it passable, but barely.
9397: Three men abreast could span this tunnel carved out of the dark rock of this mountain. One and a half men would it take to reach its roof. Standing within its centre, in either direction, east or west, it continues into the gloom. The curving walls arch above you oppressively, as if the entire weight of the mountain rested upon the back of its smooth arch. As you pad along it, step after step, as if you were stepping upon the coils of some long sleeping snake, your steps echo softly in your ears. You stand within The Burrow.
9398: This open cavern leads to the east, and southwards it connects to the Burrow. A natural cavern, large stalactites hang precariously from the eroded ceiling. Equally, jagged stalagmites rest dangerously along the floors. The entire effect is like walking into the mouth of a snake; one false misstep could send a hurling spear of rock piercing through your body.
9399: Heading sharply east-west, the passage shadows its twin, the Burrow. Sheltered by meters of hard, thick granite, not even a herd of stampeding Oliphaunts could send tremors into the Burrow. Lined against the walls, black warg furs lie draped to muffle any sounds, an added but unnecessary precaution.
9400: As smooth as worn glass, these fleshy grey walls bear you straight ahead. Travelling along an east-west axis, the worn floor carries you with ease. A passage leading to the north used to open here, heading towards a maze of natural caverns and tunnels; however, a massive, unmoveable boulder now seals the entrance, barring anything larger than a bat from entering.
9401: Checking against the Burrow, this secret route follows the curve of the Burrow, dipping to the south and west. Stretching your arm span from tip to fingertip, you cannot reach these walls, nor clearly see the ceiling. Focusing your gaze, your sight becomes lost in the sea of darkness surrounding you. The solid grey walls serve as your only guide.
9402: A hungry warg stands here, sniffing around for flesh.

Like a slithering snake, the passageway curves its way through this rocky mountain. Bending to the east and north, it continues to shadow the mighty Burrow, trailing it like an invisible predator. To the west, one of the goblin doors stands, protecting against entry. It serves as an exit for those traveling along Goblins' Pass.
9403: As if the hand of Eru himself had dug deep into the mountain to twist this underworldy road, The Burrow finds itself perverted from its straight course, bent by some will to go where it now flows. To the west, it exerts its inertial force. To the east, it is prevented, torn instead to the south, where it might flow to the song of its making. Standing within The Burrow's embrace, you can only wonder whether it was the hands of mortals that carved this place, or the hands of gods.
9404: An elite orc-guard is on sentry here.

As if the hand of Eru himself had dug deep into the mountain to twist this underworldy road, The Burrow finds itself perverted from its straight course, bent by some will to go where it now flows. To the east, it exerts its inertial force. To the west, it is stayed, turning instead to the north, where it might again fulfil the path chosen for it. From your standpoint, The Burrow flowing around you, its walls hugging you like the coils of a snake, you wonder at the simple marvel of its smooth hewn walls, its arched ceiling, and its foot-flattened floor.
9405: Here it is difficult to distinguish the black walls from the darkness around you. Squinting for exits, you make out a shadowy silhouette to the east and west, to the south, faint bootsteps and wailing can be heard.
9406: The granite walls around you make excellent sound conductors; voices and metal boots can be heard stomping and clattering off the jagged walls ahead. Attempting to discover where those sounds originate could prove a more difficult task however. The jagged angled walls spin echos into random patterns and directions, making them difficult to locate.
9407: Like a crack within the solid wall of stone, this small passage peters off into the darkness. The walls are oppressively close and jagged and the floor is rough and covered with rubble and dust. It is immediately apparent that, unlike The Burrow, this small tunnel is very rarely used, if it is used at all. A few broken weapons litter the floor, as well as strips of leather and splinters of wood, but nothing at all of value.
9408:
An elite orc-guard is on sentry here.
An orc assassin is hiding here, waiting for a victim to stab.

Like the home of some earth-wandering worm, the scope and the length of this passage dwarfs you. It stretches to the east and west in its unfathomable path through the mountain as if by the earth's will itself, this tunnel was made. Whatever created this hollow bowl of air submerged in earth and rock is anybody's guess. The orcs were known to have been skilled but this? The dwarves were masters, but this? Is there some higher hand at work within this dark and brooding mountain?
9409: A hungry warg stands here, sniffing around for flesh.

This dark tunnel serves to confuse those travelling along the Burrow. Seeming to start from no where, the only exit is westwards, to an opened cavern. Using an old miner's trick, you gently glide your fingers along the wall, allowing them to act as a guide while you travel along its curvy length.
9410: Crafted by the most highly skilled goblins, this pass secretly shadows the Burrow. Wide and smooth, insulated from the main throughfare by meters of heavy rock, legions of orcs and goblins could march from here to Wolf's Gate untraceable to those on the Burrow. Built to ambush and confuse intruders along the Burrow, this wide tunnel leads to the north and south.
9411: The sulphurous rocks and dust begin to irritate your lungs, stifling back a cough you rub your red, watering eyes. Every step you take worsens the air around you, safe if you cannot move, the constant trampling and motion stirs the long sleeping sulphur dust into the air, making you gag.
9412: The taste of spoiled eggs invades your mouth, and burns your nostrils. The sulphur is very heavy here, so much that the air begins to resemble a thick yellow fog. The passage may continue ahead, but you cannot see clearly enough to tell. For now, the only choice is back to the east.
9413: Here the main volume of the slow moving river flowed. Pounding through the soft limestone, it encountered thick stubborn granite checking its advance to the east. Splaying outwards with what little fury it possessed, it forged both to the north and south. Back to the west, lies its now lost source of origin.
9414: The ancient river must have been travelling with very little strength. Here, the walls and ceiling begin to close, shrinking in diameter and height. The limestone ends abruptly, replaced by noxious sulphur that tickles and constricts your throat. The passage continues along a north-south tangent.
9415: Putting more rock between you and the Burrow, this tunnel continues along a north-south line. Crafted by the most skilled goblins available, its smooth walls and wide berth allow the passage of companies of orcs simultaneously. Contained within these walls, could be the march of a thousands boots, echoing but inescapable along these walls.
9416: Opening into a wide mouth, this tunnel is smoothly crafted. The thick granite walls hurl you along its wide domain safely and sure-footedly.
9417: Swirls of sulphur lie in veins along the black skin of these granite rocks. The ancient river, unable or unwilling to head onwards, must have folded over on itself, forcing the water behind it into a turbulent loop, and thus widening this cavern. Immense by any standards, it would be a nice place to rest, if not for the itching noxious sulphur hanging heavily in the air.
9418: Once perhaps a quiet pool of water, this craggy cave pokes sharply at your feet. Made of razor-thin shale, walking on the ground is like walking on a roomful of blades. Luckily, made of weak shale and limestone, they break underfoot, sending up tiny plumes of fossilized dust and debris.
9419: Cold wet drops seep from the earthen walls here, immersing you to the waist in deep slimy water. Deciding quickly that this probably is not the safest spot, you grope for reassurance - what was that object that brushed against your leg? Piercing your look into the water, you can determine nothing, lost in the indomitable darkness around you.
9420:
A water barrel has been left here.
An orc slavemaster is here, looking for someone to abuse.

The corridor widens, and smoking torches obscure your vision. A series of iron rings are embedded in the wall here, presumably to chain slaves until overseers from deeper in the mines need them. Deeper into the mines you can hear the sounds of digging, whereas to the west is only darkness and cobwebs.
9421: As the ore ran out along this path, the digging was abandoned. Now slag rock is hauled in and stands in big piles waiting to be hauled away. A pale moth flutters by you, headed towards the light you can see to the east.
9422: This tunnel ends abruptly at a pile of rubble and broken timber. Jutting out from some stones you can see a dessicated thighbone. The beams overhead don't look very stable, and occasionally bits of stone and dust fall from the ceiling.
9425: A sign hangs above a door to the north, written in a vain attempt at Westron. The corridor branches off in several directions here and is beginning to get confusing. Written in soot on the walls seem to be some sort of directions.
9426: The floor shows marks of heavy carts being brought through from the south. That must be where the most heavy mining operations are now. From the west you can hear a miserable moaning.
9427:
A weary slave who has lost all hope sits here staring into space.
A weary slave who has lost all hope sits here staring into space.

The room is dominated by a central pit, in which large numbers of slaves are kept. Some try to sleep on thin mats, while others stare blankly and try to remember what the sky looks like. The smell coming from the pit is rank with sweat, decay, and fear.
9428: This shaft has not been used in some time. A stake with a length of chain attached is in the centre of the room. The sounds of the slave pits can be heard to the east, while to the south are strange tracks and marks as if something had been drug through the dust.
9430:
An albino salamander is here, perched on some rocks.
An albino salamander is here, perched on some rocks.

A sharp bend leaves one standing in a cold underground stream about ankle deep. Blind cave fish dart about in the water. Green algae line the rock, making it slick to walk on. The stream seems to come from somewhere higher up in the caves and is headed down towards the depths.
9431: The corridor tightens as it bends. The sound of running water comes from the west. Velvety moss grows on the walls to the west, and the air in that direction is more humid.
9432:
An orc slavemaster is here, looking for someone to abuse.
An elven slave, wielding a pick, is standing here.
An elven slave, wielding a pick, is standing here.

Moving through the quarry is quite treacherous. Open pits where the slaves dig ore from the ground line the walkway, and fires burn continuously, illuminating the high ceiling and making the shadows of stalactites dance. Bones are mixed in with the rubble heaps, and the clamor of digging assaults the ears.
9433: In the pits below are many slaves breaking rock and digging ore from the rock walls. The ledge is narrow, and nothing is between you and a treacherous fall to the quarry below. How the slaves get ore and rock up this ledge and back through the corridors, is anybody's guess. The ledge slopes downward into the quarry to the east.
