9434: The mining has broken through a wall and into another cavern at a deeper level. Looking down into the hole you can see where the orcs have placed wooden ladders. Jagged stalagmites line the hole and would prove dangerous if one were to slip. The clamour of the mines echoes down the corridor from the north.
9443:
A rotten corpse is hanging here.
A rotten corpse is hanging here.
A half-rotten corpse is hanging here.
A shadowy and lithe orc stands here, half-hidden in the darkness.
A shadowy and lithe orc stands here, half-hidden in the darkness.
An orc apprentice is here, going about his duties.
An orc apprentice is here, going about his duties.
Thrakghash of the Mordor Flame waits here, ready to teach his malevolent magic.

Tall pillars of smooth carved stone stretch upwards into the rock above you. Arcane runes are etched into the walls, illuminating the room in an eerie blue light. On the stone floor, a huge pentagram is painted in blood, with candles at each of the points.
9444:
An orc apprentice is here, going about his duties.
An experienced orkish scout is looking for tracks on the ground.

This strange room seems much older than everything around it. The ground rock is smooth and shaped with not a mark of any visible footprint. Stalactites still hang true, seeming much larger than ones seen in more elevated areas.
9445: This hidden vertical tunnel rises almost straight up from the area below. Natural handholds enable you to climb, though slowly.
9446: The corpse of an orc apprentice is lying here.
At this point, the river does end, emptying into a large, underground lake. The water looks somehow unhealthy, with not a ripple to signify any life.
9447: The stream widens considerably here, as well as picking up speed and volume. To avoid being swept away, you are forced to stay towards the sides of the tunnel, which continues onward towards the south.
9448: Widening slightly from the east, the stream makes a sharp bend to the east, sloping downward as well. The water is faster here, due to the increased slope of the floor. Moss and lichen grow in abundance along glistening rocks.
9449: Rising from some incredibly deep spring, a stream of clear water bubbles out from a hole in the rock floor, trickling its way downwards to the west. Peering above, this natural cavern's height is immense, reaching as high as the eye can see.
9450: The rock face remains irregular still, shaping itself any which way it chooses. Parts of the rock give off a silvery hue, lighting up the cavern, seeming almost majestic to the naked eye.
9451: Twisting in the same pattern, this long, probing passage turns from the east into another sharp drop into the pitch black depths.
9452: The rock and stone twist and turn into strange patterns and formations, defying the normal rock patterns seen above.
9453:
A large bat is here, hanging in the darkness.
A large bat is here, hanging in the darkness.
An experienced orkish scout is looking for tracks on the ground.

Twisting its way miles below the ground, the passage turns from the east into another plunge into the inky blackness. To continue now would mean exploring beneath the populated caves, to whatever lies hidden and undisturbed.
9454:
A large bat is here, hanging in the darkness.
A large bat is here, hanging in the darkness.
The tunnel bends from upwards towards the east. The rock here is basalt, granite, and veins of limestone. The weight of the caves themselves seems to rest on this rock.
9455:
A shadow suddenly leaves its place on the wall, trying to reach your neck.
A shadow suddenly leaves its place on the wall, trying to reach your neck.

Water drip-drops intermittently from the ceiling, adding to small, dark pools, cradled within the jagged stone. Corpses of all sizes are forced up against the western side of the cave, leaving a trail of blood and gore behind.
9456:
A spirit is here, fighting -a Tarkhnarb Orc-.
-a Tarkhnarb Orc-, wielding a steel claymore, is here, fighting a spirit.
A hungry warg stands here, sniffing around for flesh.
-a Tarkhnarb Orc-, wielding a halberd, is here, fighting a spirit.
A hungry warg stands here, sniffing around for flesh.

The natural stone twists and turns its way across the chasm. Oddly enough, boulders and rocks seem to be scattered across the floor, chiselled and dented. Blood stains mark the floor and parts of the stone wall, and the echo of the rushing water is no more.
9457: The rough stone arcs its way north and east, caring not for the weary traveller. The stale air is breathable, if somewhat distasteful. The distant rumbling of water is all that can be heard.
9458: The footing is hard to maintain, and small rocks and debris occasionally fall harmlessly to the ground. The floor and ceiling of this passage are so rugged and loose, that a clear path to travel is impossible. Cold air consistently blasts from below the precipice, eventually brushing off the southern rock face.
9459: The ground is tattered and rough, with cracks and crevices. The air is cold and musty, hinting that this passageway has not been frequently walked upon. As the tunnel twists to the west, the northern wall falls away, leaving a gaping precipice, and from far below, a faint sound of passing water is heard.
9460: The passage levels out more or less here, sloping downwards gently to the south. The rock here is rough, with stalactites and stalagmites jutting from the stone.
9461: Entering this tunnel, you find it difficult to stop from sliding downwards. With a little effort, you believe it may be possible to climb up. The angle and length of this area makes you wonder just how far down it goes.
9462: Entering this room, you notice that the sounds of your passage have faded to just whispers of what they were. The walls here are carved in a strange way, where the sounds just disappears into the odd contours. From the south, the tunnel continues straight and true. The scent of orc is clearly in the air.
9463: This odd tunnel bends at this point from the north to the west. Obscured alcoves strangely line the walls. The air here is stale, but the faint smell of orc can be detected. The inhabitants are no longer a mystery, but the purpose of the destination still is.
9464: Here the passageway abruptly ends. The floor is covered with dust and, every so often, dirt and rock debris fall through cracks on the ceiling. Not a sound can be heard but the dust falling to the floor.
9465: An orc assassin is hiding here, waiting for a victim to stab.

Darkness fills the room. The air is musty, and dirt litters the floor. Strong indentations of boot marks scatter the ground. In the far northwestern corner, sticks, fur, and other soft debris purposely merge together to form some sort of bed. Rusted and broken daggers carelessly lie on the ground in no particular order. Scraps of rotten meat, and what looks to be decaying flesh, add to the unpleasant aroma filling the room.
9466: The passage becomes even rougher here, as it bends from the north to the east. Jutting knobs of stone make travel difficult, requiring considerable dexterity to keep moving. No sounds or signs of activity can be heard here.
9467: Barely seen from the outskirts of the tunnel, this side passage narrowly works its way from west to east. Immediately, the ground becomes rougher, leading to the conclusion that this passage is rarely used, if at all, by humanoids.
9468: The tunnel ends abruptly here, eventually closing off into the rest of the stone. However, it looks possible to climb down some stalagmites that are in one corner, into a dark opening that leads downwards.
9469: From above, this passageway heads onwards towards the east. Compared to other tunnels, this one is quite narrow. The ceiling is so low, you often hit your head on the protruding stalactites.
9470: A small bat is standing here.
Surprisingly, the tunnel here becomes suddenly much higher, as it moves from east to west. It's amazing what natural rock formations can produce in such bleak environments.
9471:
A large bat is here, hanging in the darkness.
A large bat is here, hanging in the darkness.
A large bat is here, hanging in the darkness.
The queen bat is here, emitting piercing squeaks.
The tunnel ends leading into a murky cave. The floor is littered with carcasses. Screeching sounds can be heard off in the distance, and the air around you remains cold and still.
9472: Curving at a steeper rate, the passage makes a turn in its path. Massive gashes in the stone itself mark where the builders altered the course to fit their bizarre plan. The air is a little off, indicating that something either lived, or more importantly, died somewhere around here.
9473: A fierce bat is here, lusting for your blood.

Maintaining a steady curve from the sides and floor, this haphazardly hewn tunnel is indeed strange. Bits of rubble and debris litter the floor, indicating that the ones who constructed it don't bother to keep the area cleared.
9474:
A fierce bat is here, lusting for your blood.
A fierce bat is here, lusting for your blood.

Arriving at this point, you are in a wide and tall tunnel that runs along a gentle curve, both horizontally and vertically. The most notable feature here is the wall formation. The crude but long strokes indicate something of incredible strength carved this tunnel.
9475: The pit is definitely formed by someone or something. Natural rock does not produce open pits. Old bones lie scattered along the ground, with harmless maggots crawling in and out. To the west, the tunnel opens up dramatically.
9476: The passage ends suddenly, and as far as it is possible to tell, there is nothing special here except some deep smooth depressions carved on the rock face. They do not look like the random rock patterns commonly seen in natural formations.
9477:
A half-decayed corpse of a goblin lies rotting on the ground.
A mottled snake is sneaking here, ready to sink its fangs into flesh.
Underneath some broken boulders, lies a deep rocky hole. The walls are naturally shaped and form jagged crests and bridges.
9478: By this point, the occupants of this cave are obviously trolls. However, what kind of troll is strong enough to carve caverns out of the rock itself with only simple tools and brute strength? The size of the cavern also hints at trolls of massive height, far larger than any previous conceptions and sights you have seen before. The stench here is almost unbearable, with the amount of garbage lying around. The smell is not the primary concern though, dealing with the occupants is.
9479: Taking another sharp plunge downwards into its inward spiral, the passage is even dirtier than the previous section. Among the normal garbage are a few bones, testimony to the danger here.
9480:
A powerful young troll stares at you.
A powerful young troll stares at you.
A powerful young troll stares at you.
A powerful young troll stares at you.
A hungry warg stands here, sniffing around for flesh.

At this portion of the passageway, you notice a substantial amount of refuse, garbage, and dung. Evidently the powerful beings that built this tunnel have not paid much attention to keeping it clean. The quantity and state of the garbage indicates that the tunnel is still occupied.
9481: A half-decayed corpse of a goblin lies rotting on the ground.

From a steep curve from the west, the passage evens out a bit in its turn, but continues to slope downwards. The smell of decay hangs faintly in the air, alerting you to some possible hazard up ahead. Deeper and deeper this goes, leading to some unknown end.
9482:
A rotten corpse is hanging here.
A rotten corpse is hanging here.
A nasty troll female crouches here, with a feral look in her eyes.
A nasty troll female crouches here, with a feral look in her eyes.
An old, strong cave troll is standing here.

The trolls stopped digging here, instead carving a large cul-de-sac out of the granite itself. Filthy mats of hair and clothing serve as the beds for the massive occupants. Piles of discarded equipment lay in one corner, the only recognizable remains of the victims here. Dwarf, human, and elven armour is here, most of it ripped apart by brute strength.
9483:
An infant troll, baring its teeth, snarls here.
The ugly troll mother is roaming the cave, taking care of her loved ones.
An infant troll, baring its teeth, snarls here.
The ugly troll mother is roaming the cave, taking care of her loved ones.

Moving further into the trolls' lair, the cavern stretches yet higher above your head. Caked smears of blood decorate the walls in a gruesome crimson display. The remains of corpses line one side of the wall, in varying stages of decay.
9484: A small trickle of water flowing from the north makes a rather shallow pool here. The water seems to have worn away a corner of the tunnel and the water slowly collects there. A short climb up leads to a small ledge.
9485: The corpse of a vicious rat is lying here.

Here, in typical orc fashion, refuse and garbage has been carelessly thrown. Interspersed amongst the dirty cloth and piles of broken metal are decaying corpses and rotting flesh. Hastily thrown dirt makes a minor covering for this rotting cesspool, but the smell is still over-powering enough to roll your stomach. This is where the orcs with no honor or dignity are left to spend their eternal rest.
9486: Bend in the Old Forest Road

The Old Forest Road turns sharply, heading south and west. Immediately to the east, a wide path splits off from the road and heads north. It narrows as it goes. The Old Forest Road levee sits just north, protecting the road from the flooding that occurs in a large basin just beyond the road. In the near east, the gates of a village abruptly halt the road.
9487: A large rabbit looks peacefully at you, ready to dart away.

As the Old Forest Road bends from the east to the south, a footpath intersects the bend and widens. This blurs the edge of the road with the beginning of the path, making it difficult to distinguish one from the other. A large settlement has grown up where the Old Forest Road ends in the south, protecting itself within a wall of brush and trees.
9494: A colourful butterfly is fluttering around here.

The fertile soil of these plains give the lush, green grass its life and abundance. The plains continue to the north and east, it appears without end. However, several miles to the west, one could, if very observant, see the treetops of a small grove of trees and perhaps note the small village that lies just beyond.
9495:
A small grasshopper clings to a blade of grass, ready to spring.
An angry bee is here, collecting nectar from all the flowers of the garden.

The wild grass so prominent in these lands, is untainted by tree or bush for miles to the east and north. A vast sea of grass, as green as the ocean is blue, overwhelms the senses by its very size. In contrast, to the west lies a small man-made elm grove. And although it is obscured from view, even the most inept traveller can make out the signs of a large settlement just beyond the trees.
9496: Running from the southeast to the northwest, rows of young elm trees extend in perfect lines. Though not yet mature, the branches of these trees are wide enough to block most of the light from the sky, offering travellers a nice bit of shade or a cosy spot to camp. Just to the west, a large settlement obscures the horizon.
9497: Vast, green grasslands extend from here to the north and east for as far as the eye can see. These plains are home to many animals but dominated by horses. These wild, yet friendly animals can be seen throughout these grass-covered lands. Occasionally these noble creatures will bear a weary traveller on his or her way.
9498: Surrounded on all sides by the vast green land of the Anduin plains, a lone traveller would seem like a small ship adrift on the Great Sea. These plains, so beautiful and majestic to some, could become barren and life-threatening to others. These plains give no food and no water, only grass for farther to the east than mortal eyes can see.
9499: The plains continue to the east, with no end in sight. In every direction, a sea of green grass blankets the landscape. There is no sign of shelter or water for several miles. Off in the distant west, the ground rises, forming low hills. Occassionally, a wisp of smoke crosses the western sky.
9500: A large rabbit looks peacefully at you, ready to dart away.

The plains continue to the east, further than the eye can see. The grass stretches out for miles in every direction, offering no landscape to guide by; only your track heading off into the distance. However, soon the grass swallows even your tracks, repairing the perfect sea of green.
9501: The grass-covered plains stretch out for miles in every direction. The green grass blankets the land, turning the earth into a sea of green seemingly as vast as the sea of blue. Far in the west, even on the murkiest day, the shapes of large hills and levees form a line in the horizon.
9502: The grassy plains continue in every direction, a pure sea of green, uncontaminated by tree or bush. In the east however, the Grasslands seem to go on and on, farther than mortal eyes can see, seemingly forever. A few miles to the south, a small homestead can be seen lying just before a large village. To the east of the village, treetops offer an excellent feature for travellers to guide by for many miles.
9503: Moving through the Grasslands, it becomes apparent that large numbers of horses must graze in and wander these plains. Occasionally, large patches of grass will be eaten away and in their place, many hoof prints dot the earth. The appeal of this land for creatures that live off vegetation is clear. As long as the weather allows, the grass in these plains seems to continue forever.
9504:
A brown fox is here, looking for some rabbits to chew up.
A colourful butterfly is fluttering around here.

Everywhere there is grass and nothing more. As full of life as these fertile plains are, to a traveller without food or water, these plains would be as plentiful as dunes in a desert. For as far as mortal eyes can see in the east, the Grasslands continue onwards, without end. The more observant, experienced wanderer might catch a glimpse of the tops of a grove of trees, far in the south or even catch sight of smoke coming from a village just west of that grove.
9505: In the east, there is grass. In the west: grass. In the south: grass. In the north: even more grass. It hugs the land for miles in every direction. It offers no guidance. It gives travellers nothing to steer their course by. It goes on, seemingly without end, like a sea, a sea of green.
9506: A colourful butterfly is fluttering around here.

In this sea of green, there is little to catch the eye. In every direction, the grass flows like the waves on the ocean, small ripples that seem to go on forever. Occasionally, one might catch sight of a herd of horses, roaming and grazing in the Grasslands. The plains in the east continue for farther than the mortal eyes can see so finding these animals is a rare find indeed.
9507: Grass blankets the land in a seemingly unending sea of green. In the east, the tranquility of the grass threatens to draw travellers into the forever, into the beyond. Far in the west, what appear to be hills or levees form a line running north and south, as if they were constructed to block something in or out. But from this vantage, so far away, the purpose of those rises in the plains will remain a mystery.
9508: Moving along the western edge of the Grasslands, travellers in this region might note the line of levees and hills in the west that appear to form a retaining wall. However, from this elevation, it is not possible to see what lies beyond the natural and man-made hills. Several miles in the south, a small grove of trees can be seen on a clear day, while in the east, the Grasslands seem to continue forever.
9509: Natives of this land call the massive, green plains in the south The Grasslands. There really isn't a better way to describe the immense field of nothing but green, thick grass for more miles than mortal eyes can see. The Grasslands seem as peaceful and serene as a calm lake, but the ill-prepared will soon find that as rich and fertile as the soil is for the grass, the land offers little for creatures that subsist on more than grass. No bush, tree or water source is visible for miles.
9510: The Grasslands end abruptly here, as a small group of merchants have taken it upon themselves to start a settlement here. Passage in the north is blocked by a large fence with no gate on its southern side. The only way to continue northwards is to go around to the east or west. In the south, the Grasslands continue for many more miles than mortal eyes can see.
9511:
A small vicious black rat squeaks at you for disturbing it.
An angry bee is here, collecting nectar from all the flowers of the garden.

At the northern edge of a large grassy plain named the Grasslands by locals, a vast expanse of flat, green grass flows out to the southeast, apparently without end. Heading south would be very much like starting an ocean voyage. Without the proper planning and supplies, hunger and thirst would leave the unprepared traveller adrift in a sea of green, praying for rescue.
9512:
A fat rabbit sits here, chewing on some grass.
A brown fox is here, looking for some rabbits to chew up.

An adventurous farmer must own these lands, for a crop grows here that is rarely seen and never this far north: cotton. Healthy cotton plants are the only thing growing in this field and in the fall, if the weather permits, these plants will produce a plentiful bounty. Just beyond the field to the south, a vast sea of green grass engulfs the land.
9513:
Some delicious wild strawberries grow on the ground.
A fat rabbit sits here, chewing on some grass.
A brown fox is here, looking for some rabbits to chew up.

From atop this steep incline, any creature interested in watching the habits of Beorning merchants would be happy indeed to find this vantage point. From this elevation, one can clearly watch the comings and goings of the inhabitants of this tiny hamlet. A bee farmer has set up shop in the southern end of the Village and his hives sit just behind his shop. An animal trainer works with his horses in a paddock at the north end of town. Between the two, a run-down shack threatens to collapse on any who enter it.
9514: A small footpath widens as it approaches a small settlement to the east. There are a multitude of horse tracks leading to and from this tiny village along the path. Directly south, a large hill borders the road and may offer an excellent view of the surrounding lands. The strong, sweet scent of honey gets stronger in the direction of the village.
9515: This path runs to the east and south, following the base of a large hill. Grass taller than a man in the west and hills in the south block the horizon in those directions. In the north, a seemingly perfect sea of grass envelops the land. Under the protective shadow of a large hill in the east, a small settlement can be seen.
9516: At the base of a large hill to the east and a smaller one to the south, a path has been worn by the footfalls of man and beast. While the path crosses over the southern hill, it curves around the eastern one because going over that rise would be difficult, as steep as it is. Just off the path, to the west, a small campsite is nestled between hills to the south and west of it.
9517: The path is a bit wilder here than in the south, perhaps because the hill comes to a small plateau here before rising to the west and northeast. This plateau offers an excellent spot to take in the lay of the land before continuing onwards. To the north, this path becomes more pronounced as it winds to the east around a large hill.
9518: This small but distinct path continues running to the north and south, bisecting the grass-covered plains to the east and west. In the north, the plains give way to small hills, also covered by the grass that envelopes the land in every direction. This path crosses the hills in the north and seems to continue past them.
9519: Beneath a levee just to the west, a small, well-worn path continues to the north and south. To the east, vast grassy plains continue further than any mortal eye can see. This path is very easy to follow and must be travelled often to be as distinct as it is against the lush, green grass.
9520: An angry bee is here, collecting nectar from all the flowers of the garden.

A small footpath has been worn through the grass-covered lands, running north and west. Such a small path would have been overrun by the grass if it was not used regularly. Such trails usually mark trade routes between two villages. Perhaps the large village to the south has a sister village further north.
9521: A colourful butterfly is fluttering around here.

Weaving and winding its way around the levees and past smaller obstacles, this small foot path serves as a marker for travellers and traders from the large Beorning settlement in the south and the smaller one in the north. The path wildly wanders through the green grass in the fashion of paths only made by the footfalls of two-legged creatures. No animal tracks can be seen on this small walkway.
9522: An angry bee is here, collecting nectar from all the flowers of the garden.

The path eventually heads north-east, but in an indirect way. At times, the trail turns away from its intended direction, avoiding a rock here, a hole there. Despite its meandering, the path remains clear and easy to follow. Countless footfalls have worn away the vegetation and even in darkness it would be simple to keep on the trail.
9523: The earth has been worn bare by the footfalls of traders between the northern settlement and the village south of here. The path narrows and bends to the east. It winds in the erratic fashion most footpaths take. The unusual thing about this path is how narrow it becomes, much thinner than a path travelled with domesticated animals. The path also lacks wagon tracks. This must be a true footpath.
9528: Levee near the Old Forest Road

This levee was constructed just to the south of a large basin, too near the Old Forest Road. If not for this grass-covered hill, the water flooding that depression would have overtaken the road long ago. Riding north, into the basin, is not possible. The earth quickly becomes too wet for animals or men to find a stable foothold. From this elevation, on a clear day, one could easily see the hills that contain this basin to the north and west or watch the Old Forest Road in the south, as is winds east to west. A swarm of hornets is coming out of its nest.
9529: This levee is just one of many constructed to reign in the flooding of the basin in the west. Grass spreads from the eastern plains and blankets these man-made hills in a green wash of colour. As the western and northern slopes descend into the basin, riding quickly becomes impossible as the earth softens with moisture. Standing water and fields of mud can be seen covering the land for miles in the west.
9530: A cockroach is scuttling across the floor carrying some debris.

This obviously man-made levee serves a vital role in keeping the flood waters in the west at bay. If not for this steep, abrupt rise in the plains, the waters that sit stagnant would flow towards the plains in the south, washing away the Old Forest Road and the Beorning settlement directly south of here.
9531:
A small grasshopper clings to a blade of grass, ready to spring.
A small grasshopper clings to a blade of grass, ready to spring.
A cockroach is scuttling across the floor carrying some debris.

Down the northern slope, a secluded vale is nestled between the surrounding hills. Down the grass-covered southern and western slopes, the earth turns to a muddy mush as standing water on the plains creeps up this small outcropping. Travel southward or westwards is impossible mounted, for the muddy earth offers no solid footing for man or animal. Travel in that muddy basin would be difficult at best.
9534: The ground begins to dip down towards the southeast, forming a shallow depression in the plains between the hills and levees. The earth is soft here, undoubtedly because of the high moisture content of this soil. The ground gets softer and wetter as the earth drops off to the east. Travelling in that direction would be difficult at best, but impossible if one tried to ride there.
9535: A colourful butterfly is fluttering around here.

Small hills in the west give way to a shallow valley directly to the east of here. The earth softens as it slopes downhill towards a depression in the plains. The depression is contained on the east side by hills and man-made levees in the shape of a crescent moon. Riding towards the east would only be possible if the ground remained as solid as it is here, but that doesn't appear to be the case. The grass that is so characteristic of these plains is overcome by plants that survive in a wet environment further down the depression.
9540:
A stocky mountain mule is here, waiting to serve.
A vigorous man, hardened by the wilderness, patrols his beloved land.

The ground slopes down quickly here to the east. While the elevation change isn't very drastic, the sudden drop off still makes travel eastward difficult and impossible if mounted. From this position, a large pool of water a mile or so in the east can be seen spreading out and merging with the earth for many miles to the east and north. To the south, the levees that protect the Old Forest Road from water damage stand over the depression in the plains.
9541: Vibrant, green grass covers this area until it reaches the Old Forest Road directly to the south. The earth rises slightly to the south, elevating the road above the surrounding plains. In the northeast, a large basin stretches out for many miles and is filled with water. Travel in that direction could prove difficult.
9542: Just north of the Old Forest Road, the ground suddenly drops off towards a large field of stagnant water that is immediately to the north. The slope is traversable by unmounted travellers, but still very difficult. The water has made the earth soft and very likely to collapse under too much weight. From this vantage, plants and animals not common to the Vale can be seen in the water.
9543: Just north of the Old Forest Road, the earth drops off towards the north. It leads into what appears to be a flooded basin. Many miles to the northeast, hills and man-made levees have successfully trapped the water leaving it stagnant in that depression. Travel down the slope seems easy enough to do on foot but riding down would not be possible as the earth quickly becomes too saturated for mounts to keep their footing.
9544: At the base of this massive elm tree, it is almost impossible to see the watchtower directly overhead. Although it is the topmost part of a man-made structure, it uses the elm as its main support and uses the leaves as its camouflage. A careless traveller, attempting to sneak up on this village, would be in for a nasty surprise when passing this lookout point.
9545: The walls surrounding this settlement appear solid from a distance. But once closer, the true nature of this brush wall appears. Mature elm trees have been used as supports for an intricately woven wall of vines and brush. The skilled architects of this defence have constructed this wall so densely that no light from the inside village escapes.
9546:
There is a huge, pyramidal beehive here.
A bee flies around here, collecting nectar from the flowers.
A bee flies around here, collecting nectar from the flowers.
A bee flies around here, collecting nectar from the flowers.
A young goat playfully charges and hops away.
A young goat playfully charges and hops away.
A goat is here, grazing in the hills.

This unusually small plantation doesn't appear to produce any crops. Instead, the owner of this land has rows of beehives on one side of the path leading to the house and cows and goats grazing on the other. Several farmhands tend to the milling of the animals while others harvest the honey and wax from the hives. The master of this plantation however, is nowhere to be seen.
9547:
The corpse of a great, wild boar is lying here.
A small oaken table has been set here.
A stove stands against one wall here.

This simple abode exemplifies the typical Beorning home. Simplistic yet functional, nothing in this home is without its proper place. Nothing is too fancy but these people still manage to keep some of the finer things in life. A simple set of dishes is displayed on a shelf next to a polished set of metal utensils. In the oven, the smell of a pork-pie wafts onto the plantation.
9548:
A white-painted bench is here.
There is an old street-lamp on the border of the street.
The Gatekeeper stands here, leaning on his cane.
A young man stands here carefully guarding his village.
A woman stands here carefully guarding her village.

The fortified brush walls of this village have a distinctly different feel on the inside than they do on the exterior. What looks like an impenetrable wall of live wood and thorns from the outside takes on a total change of persona within. Flowers stick their heads out from the loosely intertwined vines which themselves are covered in moss and leaves. A green wall that thrives with life and vitality also protects the lives of the inhabitants of this village.
9549:
A mailbox stands here stuffed full of messages.
A Beorning captain is here, keeping the watch.

Hanging from the ceiling of this Spartan room is its only decoration, a large brass oil lamp. Even during the day, this lamp stays lit as a reminder to all who come here that like that lamp, the people of this small hamlet are always prepared for whatever darkness may fall.
9550: A young man stands here carefully guarding his village.

Climbing through the leaves and branches of this elm tree brings you to the northern watchtower of Ingrove. From this camouflaged vantage, guards can spot travellers to this area, miles before they come close enough to the city to be of any threat. Those standing guard on this tower do not fear attack from raiders, for even wood elves would have a difficult time spotting anyone through the watchtower's thick cover of leaves and branches.
9551: A dark woman moves with a determined look upon her face.

Underfoot, a carefully constructed stone road paves the main thoroughfare of Ingrove. Unlike most stone roads which use large, flat rocks, this road is composed of smaller, round stones. They have been driven into the underlying dirt with such force that the heaviest foot traffic could not disturb them. Small, flat coloured rocks have been embedded between the larger stones giving this road an almost smooth appearance. Directly north and south, the sounds of haggling merchants can be heard.
9552:
A small sign with fine handwriting was put here.
A well-muscled man stands here, covered in soot.
A young boy is here, bumping into things.
A young man stands here carefully guarding his village.

Standing in the centre of this modest home, a ten foot tall shining bronze sculpture scrapes the ceiling. Free form in its design and composition, this massive collage of swords, shields and armour has been forged into the shape of a massive bear, rearing up on its hind legs as if preparing to strike down anyone who comes here. After the initial shock of seeing a bear made of swords fades, one might notice the obsessively neat and ordered collection of small arms and light armour that hangs from perfect rows of hooks on the wall.
9553: In the Home of a Rotund Couple
A round little woman hurries to and fro.

On every bit of counter or cabinet or floor space in this home, some collection of goods sits covered in a light film of dust and what appears to be flour. Odds are, a traveller seeking goods for a journey would do well to inquire here. A small table by the wooden front door has dozens of tiny flasks resting upon it. Above and around the door frame, lanterns of every shape and size hang ready for use. Blankets hang from the walls like tapestries with racks of dried meat sitting nearby. Dozens of footprints have been left on the floor in the thick coating of white dust. A large door in the eastern wall leads into another room of the house.
9554:
A very fat man stands here, covered in a white powder.
A beautiful and docile horse is standing here.
A Beorning man hurries about his business.

The light coating of flour that sits in this couple's main room is multiplied one hundred fold in their kitchen. It is impossible to move without stirring up a cloud of flour. Every item in this room is a strange shade of white, from the floor to the clay jars that sit on the wide counters. A large stove, built into the southern wall, stays lit day and night. The smell of baking bread fills the room.
9555:
A large bulletin board, entitled "Tales", is mounted here.
A well-tanned woman watches you with caution.
A young boy is here, bumping into things.

A varied assortment of items line the shelves, haphazardly nailed to the wall. At first glance, the shelves appear to be full of mindless junk. But on closer inspection, it becomes clear that the items stored here are rare finds indeed. Old pieces of wall from the decimated city of Old Fornost, a scrap of wood from the original sign at the Prancing Pony Inn and a chunk of raw ore from the Blue Mountains are just a few of the items the owner of this home has collected. Most Beornings are wary of wandering too far from home but the resident of this abode must be an exception to the rule.
9556:
A well used clothes line is strung between two walls.
There is an old street-lamp on the border of the street.
A dark woman moves with a determined look upon her face.

This town's north-south thoroughfare ends here. Directly to the south, a massive wall of plant life stands as the village's protection. Small homes in the east and west contain the road, which heads north. The road stands in the shade of the wall and the homes most of the day. At night, small lanterns reflect light off the foliage, bathing this cove in a green glow.
9557:
A Beorning man hurries about his business.
A young boy is here, bumping into things.

This is a tiny house. As soon as leaving the doorway, the dining table blocks the path. Moving around that, a clothes line threatens to decapitate anyone taller than a hobbit. Once clear of those obstacles, a huge, brown stove takes up most of the room. There doesn't appear to be any room for a family to live here. But the clothes on the line clearly belong to children as well as adults.
9558:
A young man stands here carefully guarding his village.
A cockroach is scuttling across the floor carrying some debris.
A cockroach is scuttling across the floor carrying some debris.

The road narrows in the south and opens more to the north. Dominating the view in the north is the shape of a massive, unmoving bear. The sound of running water can also be heard in the north and in the east. But the most overwhelming assault on the senses comes from the west, where the smell of baking bread flows from the kitchen of a large home.
9559:
There is an old street-lamp on the border of the street.
A clear spring babbles as cool water trickles out of the ground.
A white-painted bench is here.
A small loyal cat is here.
A cockroach is scuttling across the floor carrying some debris.
A horse of the Rohirrim (ulo) is standing here, ridden by you.

A small, well-shaded area has been left undeveloped by the residents of this town. Small benches have been erected in this small park to give passers-by a dry, comfortable place to sit. Several mature elms give much needed shade from the sun and green, lush grass softens the earth underfoot.
9560:
A sturdy peg for hanging armour from is on the wall.
A small loyal dog is here.
A Beorning lad tends to the stables adjoining a large house.
A young boy is here, bumping into things.

These stables are arguably the cleanest ones ever seen. The light smell of hay is the only indicator that horses are even kept here. Saddles hang in neat and orderly rows on the southern wall, each with its own riding whip coiled around the saddle horn. Overhead, hanging from hooks in the rafters, many clean buckets with brushes sticking out over the rims wait for their next use. A small wooden sign hangs above the stable doors.
9561: Living Room of a Large Home

A large bulletin board, entitled "Free Peoples' Chronicles", is mounted here.
A huge clock is standing here.
A large stone fireplace with a roaring fire warms the room.
A fine marble chessboard with ivory and ebony pieces is set here.
A well dressed older gentleman greets visitors to his home.

This is the main room of a large, stately house. Many family portraits hang from the walls and plush couches and chairs are placed in every conceivable location. Thick, vibrant curtains hang from every window sill and large tapestries cover the walls. Above the fireplace, a life size portrait of a regal woman dominates the room.
9562:
A large bulletin board, entitled "News of Arda", is mounted here.
A small loyal cat is here.
A steward is here, ready to help you with your things.
A young boy is here, bumping into things.
A young man stands here carefully guarding his village.

At the top of a large staircase, many doors line a long, mirrored hallway. Each of these guest rooms has been offered to travellers and those who have no home. Each door in the hallway has been painted a different colour, perhaps to ease guests in identifying which rooms are theirs.
9563:
A sturdy target for arrows, made out of thatch, stands here.
A surprisingly tall Beorning woman stands here.
A young man stands here carefully guarding his village.

The earth is dry here, worn barren by the repeated footfalls of those individuals coming here for practice sessions. An experienced scout uses this yard as her training grounds for young Beornings she trains to be village guardians and someday, warriors. In the centre of this yard, a large training ring has been constructed. Along the northern wall a range for archery practice is fenced with poles every few yards as warning markers.
9564:
A large bulletin board, entitled "Warriors' Guild Board", is mounted here.
A battle-hardened man stands alert.

This is the home of a warrior, without a doubt. Hanging over the mantle are two crossed swords, both worn dull from repeated use in battle. Framing the swords on either side are two bronze shields, equally battered. Other than those items, the walls are bare. A small cot and a table with two chairs are the only furniture in the room. Out back, swords can be heard clanging against each other.
9565:
A tiny spider is here, eating a tiny bug.
An ancient hag sneers at all who look upon her.

The overwhelming stench of rotten food and mildew slams you in the face. How anyone could live in this overbearing smell of dirt and rot confounds the imagination. On a table, the only piece of furniture that any creature from this century could recognise, sits a totally green piece of bread. Rats scurry about underfoot and spiders spin their webs overhead.
9566:
A well used clothes line is strung between two walls.
There is an old street-lamp on the border of the street.
A cockroach is scuttling across the floor carrying some debris.

The stone-paved road comes to an end here as it reaches the northern wall of the village. On either side of the road the fronts of two small homes face the street. Overhead, the tops of mature elm trees provide shade for this quiet row. In the south, the busy hustle and bustle of the town can be heard.
9567:
A sturdy bed made from solid oak lies here, covered in warm blankets.
A small loyal cat is here.
A Beorning man hurries about his business.

Small and quaint, this cosy abode homes a happy couple who have recently become parents. Baby clothes and blankets are flung over the furniture and on the floor. Hanging in the back of the house are diapers, drying from a recent washing. But despite the mess created by the newborn and its less than prepared parents, this home still has a warm and welcoming feel.
9568:
A large bulletin board, entitled "Board of the Free Peoples", is mounted here.
A young man stands here carefully guarding his village.
A young man stands here carefully guarding his village.
A young man with dark, piercing eyes watches all who pass.
A stunning woman with flowing black hair pretends not to notice you.
A Beorning child stands here, craning his neck skywards.
A cockroach is scuttling across the floor carrying some debris.

The leader of this Beorning settlement oversees the village concerns from this humble abode. A small window with tattered curtains looks out onto the street. Upon large hooks bolted into the ceiling, several axes of various shapes and sizes hang ready to be used at a moment's notice. The east wall has a crude opening cut into it. Behind the opening, the gate of a massive metal cage can be seen. The cage appears to have been crafted to hold large animals, as the bars are extremely thick and spaced wide apart.
9569: A dark woman moves with a determined look upon her face.

This well-worn bit of road is the busiest in the village. Training grounds for the village guardians lie just to the east. A small, ill-kept house in the west has a constant stream of men entering and exiting with much haste. Traffic seems lighter in the south, though much noisier.
9570:
A massive bear-shaped fountain stands here.
There is an old street-lamp on the border of the street.
A huge cage is here, sitting by the side of a small house.

This is the central meeting place for Beornings living in these plains. A large fountain, sculpted from granite in the shape of a black bear, is the main source of water for this village, being constructed atop a fresh spring. To the east, the road runs up to the front door of a large house. Northwest, a large, iron cage sits next to a small, unimpressive hut. The cage appears to be covered in some sort of red, sticky goo and a few barrels stand near it, filled with rotten fruit of various kinds.
9571:
There is a lit street-lamp on the border of the street, illuminating the area.
A dark woman moves with a determined look upon her face.

The main thoroughfare of this village runs in a straight, east to west, line. It narrows in the east, leading to a large house and quickly widens westward, leading to the town square. Small flowers have been planted on both roadsides. The rows of flowers lead to the front door of the spacious home in the east. Just off the road in the south, a clump of trees offer shade to a secluded park.
9572: A young man stands here carefully guarding his village.

A stone road leads to a huge stone fountain in the east and a wall of green a bit farther west. Utilitarian in nature, this road also serves an aesthetic purpose. Using the stones as an artistic medium, the builder has crafted the image of a massive black bear in the road. The flat sculpture is so large that it would not be visible to those standing directly above it but would appear to be a dark patch in the stones. But viewed from the outer edges, a larger than life bear can be seen, looking towards the west with its head turned slightly upwards.
9573:
A large bulletin board, entitled "Jail", is mounted here.
A bowl of salad has been placed here.
A water barrel has been left here.

This square, metal cage sits adjacent to a small house. It measures about ten feet by ten feet and is capable of containing several men at a time, as its former use was as a trap for large game, bears in particular. Now, the authorities of this village have decided to put it to a more practical use, a holding cell for criminals. The lock on the side of the cage is a very strong and clever device. But even if it could be picked, the guards waiting on the other side of the bars would not take kindly to escaping criminals.
9574:
A sturdy pack horse is standing here.
A skilled horse trainer is here, watching his animals.

This paddock attaches to a small stable and one room house, all contained within the paddock fence. The trainer who calls this place his home truly lives with his animals because no doors separate the individual structures and man and animal alike can come and go through each as they please. So at best, the fence could be called the walls of this home with very little for a roof. In the middle of the paddock, large barrels sit in a spaced out row and are used to train horses how to be ridden and men how to ride.
9575: This small village is made up of only three buildings, constructed with their front doors facing in a semicircle to the west. Few would even refer to this collection of structures as a village if it were not for the large sign standing before you, proclaiming such. An odd mixture of smells and sounds fill the air here.
9576:
The bee flies around here, collecting nectar from the flowers.
A beekeeper is standing here, intent on his bees.

A small bed, a table and three chairs are the only furniture in this small home, however, every bit of wall space has been taken by shelves. It almost looks like the house has been built out of shelving. Sitting on the shelves, causing them to bow severely are jars and jars of honey. Every flat surface in the house is used to harvest honey out of its combs. With so much honey about, the occasional bee, buzzing around your head, is to be expected.
9577: Animal furs of all kinds line the walls of this large shack. Wolf and bear traps hang, uncleaned from last use, from hooks in the wall. A squarish hole in the wall serves as the only window. The door hangs haphazardly on its hinges but the lock is of the finest quality. This shack's owner does not seem to place much interest in appearances but pays a great deal of attention to security.
9578:
There is a huge, pyramidal beehive here.
The bee flies around here, collecting nectar from the flowers.
The bee flies around here, collecting nectar from the flowers.
The bee flies around here, collecting nectar from the flowers.
The bee flies around here, collecting nectar from the flowers.

The keeper of this farm has fenced in the land in the same way a horse breeder would fence in his paddock. However, there are no animals here, only insects and thousands of them. The large fences seem to be to keep animals out, rather than keeping anything trapped in. Within the fences are many rows of beehives, running from north to south. A few sit unused, but the vast majority are literally humming with working bees, producing honey and wax. The hives are constructed of wood so they can be easily opened by their owner.
9579:
A giant rat patters against you, squeaking maliciously.
A small vicious black rat squeaks at you for disturbing it.
A small vicious black rat squeaks at you for disturbing it.

Here under the floor of a run-down shack, a hunter has stashed a variety of trophies. Large bear furs, tanned deer skins and used animal traps cover the walls and floor. It is highly unusual for anyone to hunt bears in this part of Arda so it is clear why the owner of this shack hides the spoils of his hunts.
9580: The earth softly rises and falls underfoot as the plains attempt to reclaim the land taken by the hills long ago. From a distance however, this land would appear as flat as any plain to the casual observer, as the grass that grows here is tall enough to obscure the real lay of the land from view. Several miles to the south, a large hill gives travellers a landmark to guide by. Just east of that hill, a small settlement has grown up in the hill's shadow.
9581: The plant-life in this field has been eaten away by grazing animals, looking for a snack. Domestic animals are kept in the small settlement south of here and on any given day, several of the more tame and obedient animals are let out of the corral to graze. Many wander in this patchy, grass-covered area, nibbling at the grass and looking for treats from passers-by.
9582:
A well-fed cow stands here chewing her cud listlessly.
A well-fed cow stands here chewing her cud listlessly.

Adjacent to a fenced in pasture in the south, this piece of land is not owned by anyone, so domesticated animals have made it a grazing pasture. The grass only grows in patches that dwindle farther south. In the north, a sea of grass stretches for more miles than mortal eyes can see.
9583:
A domesticated pony, beast of burden to many, stands here.
A well-fed cow stands here chewing her cud listlessly.
A brown cow is here, contemplating a higher reality whilst chewing slowly.
A small grasshopper clings to a blade of grass, ready to spring.
A large rabbit looks peacefully at you, ready to dart away.

The overwhelming stench filling the air leaves little doubt that animals graze nearby. The grass only grows in patches in this corral as domesticated animals are kept here and the soil suffers the effects. Horses and cattle mill about near the west and south gates, waiting for the occasional treat from their owners or passers-by.
9584: In this messy tangle of thick, man-high stems, progress becomes troublesome, because of both the depth of the grass and its sharp, scratching edges. At times, you have trouble getting your bearings, as, no matter where you look, it's only grass all around, and there are no references to guide by. And sometimes, it even seems as if you were circling around. But fortunately, the sky is always above your head, and perhaps the sun or the stars may help.
9585: A Natural Viewpoint over a Sea of Grass

A rocky hill extends in this area. At the feet of its northern and eastern hillsides, the ground seems to have subsided into a deep hollow, the very steep slopes descending many yards downwards to the bottom. But near the top, a stone promontory extends out towards the sky, as if hanging on the air, and the sights there are impressive. A great expanse lies before you, covered in deep-green grass. And such grass! The stalks rise so high that they could easily conceal a standing man, and they swing in the wind forming waves that move up and down the plain, so that, from the viewpoint, it looks like a great green sea.
9586: Grass grows especially thick in this area, the tangled stems severely hindering your advance. Deep silence and intense stillness mysteriously surround this dense forest of grass stalks, as if no sound from outside, not even the howl of the wind, was able to come into the depths of this place, and no thing nor being dared to disturb its deep lethargy. Light is dim beneath the enclosing stem ceiling, and, in the half-darkness, the puzzling halo strengthens.
9587: Half-hidden among the high surrounding stalks, a clearer area suddenly comes into sight: not like a clearing, as grass still grows thick, but undoubtedly less dense. And this place seems to have a special meaning for the great red deer, as, during rut season, the large bucks come here to duel, their long antlers clashing in bloody fights to death. Strangely enough, there are no bones lying among the grass, nor any other signs of the defeated deer.
9588:
A huge tarantula (KAKS) is standing here.
A huge tarantula (YKS) is standing here.

In this messy tangle of thick, man-high stems, progress becomes troublesome, because of both the depth of the grass and its sharp, scratching edges. At times, you have trouble getting your bearings, as, no matter where you look, it's only grass all around, and there are no references to guide by. And sometimes, it even seems as if you were circling around. But fortunately, the sky is always above your head, and perhaps the sun or the stars may help.
9589: A small grasshopper clings to a blade of grass, ready to spring.

In this messy tangle of thick, man-high stems, progress becomes troublesome, because of both the depth of the grass and its sharp, scratching edges. At times, you have trouble getting your bearings, as, no matter where you look, it's only grass all around, and there are no references to guide by. And sometimes, it even seems as if you were circling around. But fortunately, the sky is always above your head, and perhaps the sun or the stars may help.
9590: A group of small hillocks with rounded tops rise slightly over the ground. Grass grows abundant on their hillsides, and only occasionally a smooth-edged stone shows among the stalks, as if forgotten long ago. Perhaps one day the proud tops of these hills towered above the grasslands, but nowadays they have become no more than a small unevenness of the ground, as if time and weather had slowly buried them in the earth, thus pushing them back to their source rock.
9591: The monotony of the plains breaks suddenly, as the grasslands run into a deep depression. To the east, the ground seems to have fallen down, forming a small cliff that rises over the bottom, and its bare, earthy wall stands almost upright, exposing the naked soil to the light. From the edge of the sheer drop, the ground looks a long way down, and covered by a great expanse where grass grows outstandingly high, as if trying to climb up to the top. The deep lowland spreads in the distance, but it rises slowly northwards till it levels up the plains.
9592: Outskirts of the Man-high Grass Fields

A great expanse of wild grass, spreading for many miles into the distance, starts in this almost forgotten spot beside the high thorny hedge that stands to the west. The ground descends noticeably towards the southeast, forming a deep depression where grass seems to grow even thicker, whereas, directly south from here, a steep embankment rises over the green grasslands, and behind it, you can distinguish the rounded tops of some ancient hills.
9593: A small grasshopper clings to a blade of grass, ready to spring.

You are now immersed amidst a vast green cloud of tangled vegetation. Advance becomes arduous, yet not impossible, as the weeds stick to you, and you can only set the thick blades aside with great difficulty. As you step onwards, the space you leave disappears as the immense mass of grass fills it, closing suffocatingly around you, reducing your vision to a few paces, and threatening to engulf you.
9594: A colourful butterfly is fluttering around here.

Time has turned these once mighty hills into little more than grass-covered anthills. Telltale pebbles, victims of time's harsh treatment, litter the landscape, giving travellers on foot something to kick up as they cross the hill. In the south, a small foot path takes a turn eastwards towards a small settlement. Farther south, the land rises as larger hills take prominence over the plains.
9597: A Path among the Flower-covered Hillocks

A belt of oaks, old and leafy, stands to the east, and two rows of trees start there, flanking a path that comes into the small hills in this area. The trail winds through flower plots covering the soft slopes amongst the shade of the tree tops. To the south and west, the rolling ground seems to stretch out, but the path bends northwards and disappears wandering into the flower expanses.
9598:
A small cluster of clover grows here.
A small grasshopper clings to a blade of grass, ready to spring.

The path runs through small, square flower patches that have been carefully planted around it, taking the shape of a large, tessellated expanse, that shines full of colour. The diverse scents of the many different flowers mix together forming a unique smell that is full of vaguely distinguishable, yet fine details. The path bends here, leading westwards into the grassy hills, and disappears into the flower plots to the south.
9599: Up the Slope and Down the Vale

In this land of countless vales, the miles seem to get longer under your feet, demanding an additional effort to cover them. From the top of a hill, the landscape around rolls in an endless series of hills and valleys, like the roughed ocean during the most terrible storm. But the path, unaware of whatever happens all around, continues its way winding through the hills, always flanked by the rows of elms and oaks.
9600: An east-west path is here, flanked by rows of tall oaks and leafy elms that have been carefully planted at the borders of the trail. To the west, it seems to head for a great rock that towers above the ground, silent and impressive, while, in the other direction, the path, always in the shade of the tree tops, goes into the hills and disappears among them. But you cannot discern any sign of where it may lead to.
9601: A Path Starting at the Foot of the Carrock

A ford of huge, flat stones leads to the foot of a great rock, almost a hill of stone. It crops out of the ground to the west, right in the path of the Great Anduin, like a last outpost of the distant Misty Mountains, or a huge piece cast miles into the plains by some giant among giants. At the base of the hill, a comfortable-looking cave opens into the rock, while some well worn steps, carved out of the stone, lead to the top. Certainly, this natural monument must have a special meaning for the inhabitants of these lands, for a path starts at the bank, and, flanked by rows of elms and oaks, disappears into the hills and vales to the east.
9603: A goat is here, grazing in the hills.

Even though countless vales and hills follow each other in this area, from time to time one draws your attention, as in this case. This particular dale appears to be much deeper than the rest, for, although the hillocks flanking it are not too high, it roams along a hollow in the ground. The hillsides tumble majestically downwards to a dried river bed, a long-forgotten tributary of the Anduin. To the south, the hillsides seem to lean towards each other, as if trying to conceal what lies through the gorge between their craggy summits.
9604: Low Hillocks near the River Shore

A fat rabbit is here, chewing on some grass.
Bulg (pukespy), wielding a great warsword, is standing here.

From the small hillocks that stand to the east, the ground comes tumbling down to this majestic river bank. Further east and south, it appears to roll more and more. There, at the top of a hill, an old wooden building seems to invite travellers to take a rest. In contrast, a huge green expanse spreads all over the countryside to the northeast, like a gigantic-sized grassy carpet that perhaps extends to the boundaries of the dark Mirkwood forest, far to the east. To the west, the river flows slowly southbound, with the imposing backdrop of the Misty Mountain peaks behind it.
9605: The flow of the Great Anduin, after detouring the huge rock that stands in its path to the northwest, runs into this bank. Through the years, it has broken the rock up into tiny stones, smooth and oval, that cover the ground by the riverside like a cold, stony carpet. The blow of the wind raises small waves that come to die on this fluvial beach, under the watchful look of the Misty Mountain peaks.
9606: A small, almost square flat area at the top of the stone provides a perfect vantage point for observing the surroundings. The path leading down to the foot of the hill appears very well trodden indeed, and leaves no doubt that this place has been visited often over the years.
9607: In this area of the eastern bank, the slow but unstoppable flow of the powerful Anduin has eroded the rocks that make up the ground. Through the centuries, the waters have sometimes smoothed their edges, at other times they have broken them up into small parts that lie scattered throughout the bank. The ground, although stony, is covered in rounded boulders, thus making your advance less arduous than might be expected.
9608: A low hillock stands to the east, with its slopes rising over the surface of the waters of the Great River. These waters detour the contours, glide past and then bend gently southwards towards the sea. The flow of the water is slow, but also restless and mighty, because of the width of the river, that, in this flat and uneven area, sometimes reaches the mile.
9609:
A swan swims gracefully on the surface of the water.
A salmon swims here.
A fat carp swims here.
A trout swims here.

The largest river in Middle-earth advances steadily southbound, to meet the salt waters of the still very distant Belfalas Bay. Its water, proceeding from the icy basins of the Grey Mountains, keeps cold to the touch for the whole year. Its surface is always limpid and clear, like a window through which the Great Vala Ulmo, Lord of the Sea, watches the land. For even here, many miles inland, among dense forests and high mountains, it is Ulmo who keeps control of every little pool and tiny brook.
9610: This low hill stands right in the path of the Great Anduin, forcing the waters to pass by on along its western side. Throughout the years, the stream has eroded the hillsides, shaping them into rocky upright walls, like small cliffs, that rise several tens of feet above the waters. On the northern side, where the stream falls directly upon the slope, the wear is more pronounced, and even from the very edge of the cliff you cannot see its base. Beyond the river, the view is excellent, as the landscape gradually ascends to the feet of the Misty Mountains.
9611:
A skull is here, spiked to the end of a pole.
A battered warg fur has been left here.

Countless rows of pikes exhibit the remains of unfortunate orkish heads and the dried furs of the mountain wargs, like a grotesque hunting-trophy museum in the open air. All sort of horrible grimaces show in the faces of those still preserved heads, and they are even more dreadful in those half-rotten ones, let alone the bare, sun-dried skulls, with their cadaverous eye sockets. Undoubtedly, these remnants have been placed here for the benefit of other dark minions. Grim warning of the destiny that awaits them, should they dare intrude further into these lands.
9612: Severally coloured flowers grow here and there among the grass. They add a dab of colour to the dazzling, deep green expanse that covers the ground like a huge carpet. To the east, the grass fields disappear, as small patches of carefully planted flowers take their place, whimsically disposed in a very colourful mosaic. A faint, yet clean buzzing seems to hover in that way.
9613: A small cluster of clover grows here.

Great patches of flowers, all the same kind growing together, cover these fields. Especially there is clover: cockstomb or purple clover with waving leaves, and small, white clover too, their little leaves swinging in the wind, as if in time to the background buzzing. An intense, sweet, honey-like smell impregnates the air, filling your senses.
9615:
A coloured game bird is visible in the vegetation, watching you warily.
A huge, black bear is here, proud heir to the great and ancient mountain bears (glowing).

A smooth, long slope rises gently towards a hill to the west that, small as it is, it still stands out of the plains around. The grass grows high and fresh on the hillside, almost wildly, as if it had remained undisturbed for years. Looking about, you can see the Great Anduin flow from the north. It flows past the remnants of an old pier, disappears briefly behind the small hill, and then continues its long way southbound.
9616: The wide river continues its way towards the sea, running through these vast grasslands that extend between the snowy peaks of the Hithaeglir and the dark and sinister Mirkwood forest. The flow avoids every little roughness of the ground in an endless series of gentle bends. Here, the river runs into a small hillock, and it turns westwards to detour it. But throughout the years, the stream has worn away the hillside, and now it towers vertically over the cold waters.
9617: The simple beauty of these lands shows clearly in this riverbank. A gentle, grass-covered embankment descends softly to the riverside, where the quiet and silent waters seem to caress the little round stones on the ground as they flow along. Now and again, a tiny wave comes to the shore, but it fades away before breaking, as if it dared not making any noise that might disturb the quietness of this spot.
9618: A small, lonely hill stands to the east, like a lump on the ground that stands out of the grassy plains around, and it is towards its top that this hillside rises, gradually but steadily. As it ascends, some weeds and scrubs begin to show among the grass, as if the latter ruled undisturbed in the low lands but the other plants challenged its reign on high. To the northwest, at the river- bank, you can see an old pier floating on the quiet waters of the Anduin.
9619:
Some cracked and splintered pieces of wood float here.
A swan swims gracefully on the surface of the water.
A trout swims here.
Bulg (pukespy), wielding a great warsword, is standing here.

The half-rotten but still recognizable remains of an old landing stage float mildly on the quiet waters of the river, along the eastern bank. Long ago, trade was intense and prolific in these lands, but the declining of Gondor and the strengthening of the orkish settlements in the mountains made an end of it. In those days, small barges sailed the river, light enough to allow portaging when they reached the Anduin rapids, to the south. But those were better times, and the fine goods from Gondor are now rarely seen this far north.
9620: A Mournful Section of the River
Bulg (pukespy), wielding a great warsword, is standing here.

For a moment, a heavy gloominess seems to engulf the river, as it runs along the withered western bank, where everything looks wasted and desolated. The waters seem to darken and turn cloudy and turbid, as if trying to conceal some ominous, forbidden secret that may lie hidden on the river floor. And they even seem to hasten, trying to leave this place behind as soon as possible.
9621: Bulg (pukespy), wielding a great warsword, is standing here.

Slowly but steadily, the waters of the Anduin continue their long travel southbound, having started many miles away at the icy springs in the Ered Mithrin, in the northern vales. Here, the stream has flooded the eastern bank, forming a small marsh where vegetation grows dense. On the contrary, a low hillock stands on the western riverside, silent and mysterious, and somehow it seems as if the own mighty Anduin avoided its slope.
9622: The river once again stretches out on its way far to the south, the water flowing slowly but purposefully towards the sea miles away. A cooling breeze runs over the surface of the river, creating ripples and dancing on the water. Along the shores can be seen small streams of rainwater adding to the might of the river in its journey south. To the east the bank rises unto great, rolling grasslands that stretch out as far as the eye can see. To the west the Misty Mountains can be seen looming in the distance.
9625: A Strong Eddy in the River Anduin

Pouring down over the ledge of black rock, the great river falls a short distance here. A cold wall of spray rises up from the chute. The seething current is coursing around everywhere, throwing forward everything and anything that gets in its way and pulling it back with a relentless force. If careless enough, one might not break the pull of the river, and end up in the deep and dark surface of the mighty flow.
9626: The great river rises here in a swell of foam and spray as it sweeps over the top of massive black rocks lying just beneath the surface of the water. The jagged edges of the rocks have been worn down with the eternal flow of the current, but they still churn the waters and make passage difficult, even for the experienced boat pilot. A quick glance reveals that the eastern bank of the river is lined with dark mud, while open grasslands hasten away in the distance.
9627: The waters of the River Anduin seem dark and forbidding and give away no hint of what lies deep beneath the surface. The river is vast, the large body of water flowing at a stately pace towards the distant south. Small fish can be seen just beneath the surface, trying to catch a glimpse of the sunlight. To the far west the peaks of the Misty Mountains loom, and to the east vast, rolling plains stretch out.
9628: The central channels of the River Anduin sweep by, silent and grey, leaving only subtle markings on the surface that belie the power of the swift under- current. Schools of fish can be seen feeding in the warmer currents near the surface, while the murky depths of the Anduin hide the passage of the larger predators. White against the distant sky, the lofty peaks of the Hithaeglir rise to the west, while to the east the rocky shore melts into an endless plain of rolling grasslands.
9629: The grey surface of the water slides by swiftly, a swirling pattern of whirls and ripples catching and reflecting the light. An occasional branch or bole of some mighty tree drifts by, soaked and half-submerged in the powerful flow. The distant shorelines are lined with tall and hoary willows, their grey roots twisting down the low banks. The western horizon is sharply dominated by the majestic peaks of the Misty Mountains, while rolling grasslands stretch away eastwards toward the distant and unseen eaves of Mirkwood.
9630: A sturdy pack horse is standing here.

This field of grass and wildflowers lies directly west of the great river Anduin. The shores are low and sandy, making a perfect place to launch a vessel into the river, should one attempt to cross. The great river would make any attempt to wade or ford it impossible because it is just too wide. Looking to the west, you spy in the distance the great Misty Mountains, while the eastern banks of the river are lined with stands of willows.
9631: A sturdy pack horse is standing here.

Long ago, after a glorious but painful victory against the dark minions, the men of the northern vales dug out a barrow for their fallen people. The Nenedain, as the elves call them, chose this small hill near the bank. It was hollowed out of the very earth, and a huge stone was set to block the way in. Nowadays, the tomb remains intact. The grass grows green and fresh over the hillock, but, strangely enough, there is no sign of animal life nearby, as if some unknown power scared the beasts. Perhaps it is the same power that has protected the place from plundering.
9632: The crudeness of an old battle, waged countless moons ago, has forever set its indelible mark in what once was a beautiful riverside. The ground is scrambled and spoiled; dense, black, dried stains fill the bottom of the holes among the wasted earth, and desolation extends wherever you look. Everything seems still and quiet, almost frozen, but sometimes the clashing of swords, the screams of fighting men and the howls of orcs and wargs seem to come back from the past like a soft, almost inaudible echo, rising from the ground itself.
9633: A huge, coal-black stain is all that remains of a one-time green and fresh riverbank. The grass, that once grew high and dense, has been burnt to the root and blackened ashes have taken its place in the ground. Now and again a slight glint catches your eye, perhaps some metal that didn't melt down, or maybe the dried remnants of orkish blood, for this desolation is the result of a huge pyre. The men of these lands, though kind and hospitable to their kin, hate orcs and wargs beyond imagination and they are cruel and merciless to their enemies.
9634: A Chamber Hollowed out of the Earth
The chilled spectre of a great Northmen leader seeks his eternal rest.

A short flight of narrow and dusty steps, crudely carved out of the very ground, descends into the hillock and opens into this square chamber with a low, rocky ceiling. A great niche draws your attention to the rear wall, surrounded by a coarsely-depicted but vivid battle picture. Below it, an inscription has been engraved on the gravelly stone. Along both side walls many other smaller niches fill most of the surfaces. The air is extremely dense and heavy inside the chamber, and stale when you breathe it, as if it had remained still, waiting for who knows how long.
9635: The garden snake slithers harmlessly here.

The ground is rocky and somewhat abrupt in this area, and it rolls more and more to the east, vale after hillock and hill after valley, while the earth beneath rises gradually as it moves away from the stony banks of the Anduin. At the top of one of the hills to the east, you can see an old wooden building, most probably a shelter for weary travellers.
9636: A small stream springs suddenly out of the rocks that make up the hillock, forming a tiny but clear reservoir in a little hollow, and then quickly disappears into the stones down the hillside. Brooks like this are common in these lands, and the vale's abundant rain filters through the rocky earth to then gush forth from a myriad of cracks and holes.
9637: These grassy hills are the worn remnants of sharp, rocky tears in the plains. Their history is told by the small pebbles that litter the grass, telltale signs of the erosion that has occurred here over the eons. Now grass creeps up from the nearby fields, covering the rock and blanketing the landscape in lush green.
9638: Lush, green grass blankets the landscape in all directions. Here the grass reaches so high that your tracks are quickly swallowed by the plains. On a closer inspection, small wildflowers can be seen popping up between the blades of grass. Anyone stopping long enough to notice the small flowers might also catch the stronger smell of flowers on a southerly breeze.
9639: The nearby Anduin River makes these plains rich and fertile. Thick green grass covers the plains for miles around but the occasional wildflower can be seen springing up between the blades of grass. A few miles south, the ground begins to slope downwards towards a large basin, a depression in the plains. In the distant south, a large road can be seen winding to the east and south.
9640: A small grasshopper clings to a blade of grass, ready to spring.

In the south and east, the ground begins a gradual slope downwards into a depression in the plains. Heading either east or farther west, a traveller would encounter impressive hills, much more taxing to ascend than the worn hills in the north. To the south, the ground slopes down into a shallow depression that extends for many miles. In that basin, stagnant water has collected and forms a treacherous, muddy mix that would be very difficult to traverse.
9641:
A small grasshopper clings to a blade of grass, ready to spring.
Drazud (freshmeat), wielding a great warsword, is standing here.

The ground slopes downward to the south from here. Underfoot, the earth gives a bit under the weight of its travellers, as it is saturated with water and softer than the ground to the north. Down the southward slope, the earth seems to get wetter and in the incline more treacherous. A group of hills and levees, in a crescent shape, stretch to the east and south and form a barrier for the depression directly to the south.
9642: The earth takes a subtle downward slide towards the south. The farther south one travels, the more saturated the earth becomes with water, and the more treacherous and difficult the southward descent becomes. Riding a mount down this seemingly gentle slope quickly becomes impossible. A group of hills and levees in a crescent shape stretch to the east and south and form a barrier for the depression directly to the south.
9643: A small grasshopper clings to a blade of grass, ready to spring.

This high, grassy hill offers an excellent view of this area's plains and vales.
