Immediately below, towards the south, brown wetlands stretch out until the land rises near the levees protecting the Old Forest Road. Travel in the south would not be possible mounted. Down the eastern slope, a small, secluded grove sits surrounded by hills in every direction.
9644: A cockroach is scuttling across the floor carrying some debris.

Small trees spring up under the protective branches of mature trees only to be snuffed out by lack of soil in this small vale. Life is plentiful here. Green moss covers the earth because the sun that grass would so desperately need does not penetrate the leaves of the trees. Wild flowers, accustomed to surviving in less than perfect conditions, grow abundantly in the vale, providing a soft cushion for weary travellers.
9645: A small hill grows westward, completing a circle of hills in the west. By far the smallest of the ring of hills, this grassy rise plays its role, just as well as its larger neighbours. In the west and down the slope, a small glen thrives inside the protective stance of the ring. Down the eastern slope, a foot path has formed where traders and travellers have worn the grass away.
9646:
A cockroach is scuttling across the floor carrying some debris.
A small grasshopper clings to a blade of grass, ready to spring.

As the land flattens out in the east, hills rise up in the west obscuring the lay of the western land from view. Grass covers the land in every direction, turning the rises and drops of the landscape into a rolling sea of green. Just a bit farther south, a large levee has been constructed to contain the flooding waters that cover the western plains.
9647: A small grasshopper clings to a blade of grass, ready to spring.

Just west of a worn foot path, travellers have used this spot so regularly to rest it resembles a permanent campsite. The grass has been worn flat, yet still grows. A small ring of stones marks the usual spot for the campfire. Poking sticks, used to keep a fire alive, lie strewn on the ground, in the hopes of future use. And two large logs, cut from mature elms, offer a place to rest weary legs, or lean against during a well-deserved sleep.
9648: Five foot tall grass completely obscures the ground and just about anything else moving upon it. Taller than a pony, a hobbit or even a short man, the thick grass gets even thicker in the west as it blends into a small grove of elms. All attempts to peer into the unyielding grass prove fruitless. All even the tallest elf could see from this elevation are the tops of trees, and blades of grass.
9649: A cockroach is scuttling across the floor carrying some debris.

In the south, grass as tall as a man reaches towards the sky. It sways gracefully when caught by the occasional breeze. The grass thins out a little the farther north it grows. It appears that something is pulling the life out of the soil in that direction. As the grass gets more sparse, no other plant life fills in the barren earth.
9650:
A small evergreen plant grows here, its woody stems reaching two feet.
A barn-owl is here, looking for easy prey.

A lonely oak-tree stands here, so huge that the base dwells in shadow beneath the enormous canopy - even on the most sunniest of days. The heavy branches bend under the weight of the mass of leaves on them, like an old stooping man. Over the years, its long roots have spread through the underground, so that no other tree grows nearby; and countless cracks run along its rough, hard, knotted bark, thoroughly carved by the years and the inclemency of the weather. The men of these lands call it Wisebark, and they are right, for this is one of the most ancient trees in Arda, and it has been here for more years than any man, orc, or even elf can count.
9651: A mighty brown bear, huge among his kin, growls threateningly.

The thick stumps of what once were large oaks dot the plain, their twisting roots still buried in the earth, as a great cemetery of trees. The oak-wood that extends to the north once stretched up to here, but now, all that still remains from those trees are the heavy wooden planks in the nearby buildings, and these bulky stumps. Long, concentric rings run along their wet, rough, upper surface, their number giving grave testimony to their great age.
9652: Old and worn, these hills seem to have been here since the creation of Arda, and to have endured every cataclysm in its history. The oak wood that grows over their rounded outlines seem to be almost as old, formed by great trees with thick, grey barks and broad and curved branches hanging from the trunks. Perhaps these very millennial oaks gave shade to the first Eldar while they rested before crossing the Misty Mountains, in their long trip to the Undying Lands.
9653: A large rock stands lonely at the top of this hill. Even though the features are coarse, and the surfaces smooth and worn by the effect of rain and wind, it unmistakably resembles the figure of a great bear, rising on its huge legs in a menacing attitude. Two knobs on the rock take the shape of the arms, and, in the upper part, the stone looks rounded, except for the projecting snout. Some cracks even vaguely recall the beast's ears and claws. Whether someone sculpted this statue, or it is only a miracle of nature, remains unknown.
9654: You are now at the southern border of an impressive dale, one that is not run of the mill, but that stands out of the many ones that give this land its name: the Anduin Vales. To the north, the valley gets wider, as if the hillsides had withdrawn respectfully from its path. But here, the vale dies at the mouth of what looks like a tight glen, that quickly disappears, wandering into the abrupt faces of two hills.
9655: An Old Refuge in the Hills

A mighty brown bear, huge among his kin, growls threateningly.
Klaees (thedon), wielding a great warsword, is standing here.
Bulg (pukespy), wielding a great warsword, is standing here.

A small wooden building, old and worn by the years, stands at the top of the hill. A short, earthy incline leads to the entrance, as if demanding a last effort from the traveller, and even further inside, for the door disappeared long ago, or perhaps the refuge never had one. All along the oaken planks, the grains of the wood mingle with the stains caused by the rain, forming a mosaic that covers the walls like a natural tapestry. The intense scent of wet wood fills the air, but all in all, the house has a comfortable look.
9656: A Hill over a Narrow Gully
A small grasshopper clings to a blade of grass, ready to spring.

In this land of hills and valleys, this is undoubtedly the roughest area. The ground is rocky and rugged, almost devoid of vegetation, except for some scrub that grows among the rocks. The eastern face of the hill looks particularly dangerous, as a narrow gully has formed along the bottom of the tight vale. There, the land falls away steeply downwards, wandering among large rocks and crags.
9657:
A large rabbit looks peacefully at you, ready to dart away.
An angry bee is here, collecting nectar from all the flowers of the garden.
Klaees (thedon), wielding a great warsword, is standing here.

These worn remnants of sharp, rocky tears in the plains have been smoothed by time and weather. Only the small pebbles underfoot give any sign of the mighty outcroppings that once stood here. Now grass from the nearby fields covers the rock and the land in a sea of green.
9658:
There are two piles of wild strawberries here.
A bee flies around here, collecting nectar from the flowers.
A bee flies around here, collecting nectar from the flowers.
Klaees (thedon), wielding a great warsword, is standing here.

Suddenly, wildflowers engulf the landscape, totally choking the life from the grass so abundant in these plains. The green, that so overwhelmed the landscape in every direction, has surrendered to the colour these wild weeds offer. In the midst of so many flowers, it might occur to one that the abrupt change in plant life was too sudden. This field may have been planted by someone.
9659:
An angry bee is here, collecting nectar from all the flowers of the garden.
Klaees (thedon), wielding a great warsword, is standing here.

The earth levels out here before rising to the east and dropping off to the south. Heading either east or farther west, a traveller would encounter impressive hills, much more taxing to ascend than the worn hills in the north. To the south, the ground slopes down into a shallow depression that spans for many miles. In that depression, stagnant water has collected and forms a treacherous, muddy mix that would be very difficult to traverse.
9660:
A fat rabbit sits here, chewing on some grass.
A brown fox is here, looking for some rabbits to chew up.
A colourful butterfly is fluttering around here.
A large rabbit looks peacefully at you, ready to dart away.

This small knoll leads to a large hill to the east and falls towards a depression in the south. Green grass covers this slight protrusion in the landscape, dotted with the occasional wild flower and errant bee. Northwards, the occurrences of wildflowers increase, heading towards what looks like a field of wildflowers.
9661: Two large hills, one to the east the other to the south, share this incline as their base. In either of those directions, travellers should prepare for a bit of a climb, as these hills are rather steep. But here, the soft, green grass eases tired feet. It offers a thick cushion over the hard ground. To the far north and west, the Anduin Vales sprawl for miles.
9662: In-between a small grove of trees and a wildflower field, a small brush thicket has sprung up, snuffing out the grass with its thick vines and bushes. Easily traversable on foot, mounted riders would not be able to navigate this stretch of land. In the north and south, hills rise above the plains, hiding vales between them.
9663:
Prickly, white-stemmed plants, with blue flower heads grow in abundance.
Some delicious wild strawberries grow on the ground.

Leading into a small brush thicket in the west, this elm grove offers excellent haven for those too weary from the sun to travel any further. Mature elms reach high enough to give small animals protection from land predators. But younger trees have low enough leaves that wandering plant-eaters could feed here, if needed.
9664: Above a small elm grove, this hill has done an excellent job of withstanding the punishment of time. Unlike smaller hills in the north, this one still bares jagged outcroppings and steep slopes. Grass covered, it is not barren of small bushes or wildflowers. Without doubt this is a large hill but not as large as the one that lies to the south-west. Immediately below this hill, a small glen has prospered in the valley.
9665: The earth smoothes and levels here for a short while. In every direction, small hills give rise to larger ones, hiding the vales this land is famous for in between them. Just to the south, a small, wild grove of trees sits protected by a steep hill further south. In the east, a faint path widens as it leads to a small settlement.
9666: Every now and then, as you look around, the landscape seems to blur for a brief instant. And then you feel carried to the distant ocean, far away westwards beyond the Lindon coasts. At times, the hills shape into huge, threatening waves that loom above you; at other times, the swinging of the grass in the wind turns into the scene of a calm, peaceful sea that quickly fades away. Perhaps Ulmo's influence is still powerful in the Great River, and it extends to the surrounding lands.
9667: A goat is here, grazing in the hills.

This abrupt hill seems to rise above the surrounding ones. The ground is rough and rocky, and the grass scarce, and in its place stones of different sizes lie everywhere. The earth is uneven, with steep slopes, and demands additional effort to walk, the scattered rocks only making it worse. But the western hillside commands your attention, descending almost vertically down to a narrow glen that makes its way through the feet of the hills. To the north, the figure of a bear stands at the top of a hill and, a bit further away, you can discern the hillsides of a majestic valley.
9668: The sunlight hardly reaches the bottom of this tight glen, along which some brook flowed long ago. Winding whimsically, it follows the narrow path between the abrupt walls of the hills surrounding it. Even though both walls are steep, the eastern one looks particularly sheer, as it plummets down from the top. The mouth of a cave appears here and there in the craggy hillside, most of the times too high to reach it. However, a shadowy cavern, deep black and mysterious, goes into the hill, only a few steps away.
9669: Between two unimpressive hills lies this small, brush-covered glen. In earlier days, the hills surrounding this tiny glade were mighty projections from the earth. In those days, venturing into this glen would have been a difficult task. But now, the gentle slopes offer an easy entrance to this valley and steeper ones to the north.
9670: Some delicious wild strawberries grow on the ground.

Flowers of every shape, size and colour surround you, some as tall as a man, others no taller than a rabbit. Most can be found throughout the land, but some are so unusual that they live nowhere but in these fertile plains. In the east, a small brush thicket has grown up in the shadow of a large hill in the south.
9671:
A red-furred doe wanders peacefully among the grass.
A reddish fawn romps harmlessly among the tender grass shoots.
A reddish fawn romps harmlessly among the tender grass shoots.

From this vantage, the lay of the southern lands is placed before you. Hills, worn smooth by time, frame the vast sea of green grass that covers the plains. A large depression in the southwest houses a swampy mud-filled plain, an area that most inhabitants of this land avoid. To the north, however, a very steep hill completely blocks the view, leaving travellers who wish to know what lies in that direction with only one choice: keep climbing.
9672: A duck is here, quacking happily.

A wide spread of flowers fills this area, up to some old oaks planted to the east, beyond which a high, thorny hedge hinders further advance. The bees flutter restlessly around the flowers, looking for the sweet nectar they need to produce their honey. The little ones make a faint buzzing sound, like a background humming that rises and lowers in tone; but the larger bees drone falteringly, as if joining every now and then up to the melody, and the whole sounds like a natural orchestra that never stops playing.
9673: All sort of shoots grow together in this area. Some look very old, and rough to the touch, standing as high as a man or even higher, and their colour is faded-green, almost ochre; some grow extremely long and thin, formed by many flexible and resistant fibres, and these ones have very sharp edges; others grow short and thick, and they seem to coil around the base of the higher ones; and there are even others that stand slender and light, with smooth borders and a deep-green colour. They all crowd around you in utter disorder, as if quarrelling for every inch of the ground.
9674: A swallow flies high above the ground.

The profuse grass here is crowded tightly together, as if fighting desperately for some living space in which to grow. To the west, it seems a bit lighter, and a sweet smell comes floating in the air from there, while north from here, a group of old trees stand dispersed along the plains. But to the east and south, the grass only becomes thicker and thicker, and the stalks grow higher, like an impenetrable grassy forest that threatens to swallow you.
9675: Walking through the grass dotted in flowers, the deep smell of honey emanates from the ground and blunts your senses, filling them up. This is a very strong and sickly-sweet smell, even suffocating, to the point that you can almost feel the sugary lumps sticking along your throat. For this is a land of marked features, from the penetrating odour of the sweet nectar, to the utterly intense green of the grasslands, everything here is on its purest, almost wildest state.
9676:
There is a huge, pyramidal beehive here.
The bee flies around here, collecting nectar from the flowers.
The bee flies around here, collecting nectar from the flowers.
The bee flies around here, collecting nectar from the flowers.

Huge hives, most of them fastened to wooden sticks shining with beeswax, line up row after row in this area of the grasslands. The smallest among them are dome-shaped, and they have broad, circling rings along their surface, as well as a little opening in their lower part, and there are a lot of this kind. But there are also others much bigger that have been hollowed out of the earth, and a huge hole opens into the inside, so large that it seems as if a giant tree had been rooted out of the soil. An intense and sweet smell fills the air, while a loud, unceasing drone hammers your ears.
9677: Border of the Red Deer Lands

You find yourself at the northern edge of a wide spread of grass, as dense and high as there probably doesn't grow anywhere else in Arda. Great deer with dark, ruddy furs find their perfect natural habitat in this area which is rich in food and hiding places. The roughness of the deer's coats protects them from cuts, scrapes and scratches, and their big, twisted antlers stick out over the shoots, half-hidden among the deep vegetation.
9678: Enormous shoots, shaking in the wind, wave to and fro heavily, harmlessly hitting you once and again as you walk by them. This huge tangle of sprigs appears to extend all over, but mainly southwards, where the giant blades crowd so densely that they threaten to engulf you. On the contrary, grass grows lower and lighter to the north, where a flat hill with wide slopes is silhouetted against the horizon.
9679: Boundaries of a Sea of Grass
A vigorous man, hardened by the wilderness, patrols his beloved land.

You are now at the northern border of an area where grass grows high and dense beyond imagination, forming a framework of rough, fibrous shoots intertwining in a mess. Further southwards, vegetation becomes even denser, if possible, taking the shape of a deep forest, like a little grassy copy of the sinister Mirkwood forest. Advance through the stems is slow and laborious, and somewhat frustrating, the grass closing immediately around you as soon as you put it aside.
9681:
A small grasshopper clings to a blade of grass, ready to spring.
A soft-skinned female deer wanders peacefully among the grass.
A reddish fawn romps harmlessly among the tender grass shoots.
A partridge attempts to hide in the undergrowth.

Lost in the middle of the great expanse of wild grass, this still spot is the perfect refuge for the red deer herds. In some places, they have rooted out the shortest sprigs with their powerful mandibles, opening holes in the lower part of the grassy tangle in which to shelter from the icy winters or the pouring spring rains. In other places, they have nibbled the weeds, clearing the thickness, or dug out shallow hollows with their strong hoofs, where they can lie to rest.
9683:
A red-furred doe wanders peacefully among the grass.
A reddish fawn romps harmlessly among the tender grass shoots.
A great male deer with reddish hair and twisted antlers stands here proudly.
A reddish fawn romps harmlessly among the tender grass shoots.
A red-furred doe wanders peacefully among the grass.
A small grasshopper clings to a blade of grass, ready to spring.

You are now immersed amidst a vast green cloud of tangled vegetation. Advance becomes arduous, yet not impossible, as the weeds stick to you, and you can only set the thick blades aside with great difficulty. As you step onwards, the space you leave disappears as the immense mass of grass fills it, closing suffocatingly around you, reducing your vision to a few paces, and threatening to engulf you.
9684: You are now immersed amidst a vast green cloud of tangled vegetation. Advance becomes arduous, yet not impossible, as the weeds stick to you, and you can only set the thick blades aside with great difficulty. As you step onwards, the space you leave disappears as the immense mass of grass fills it, closing suffocatingly around you, reducing your vision to a few paces, and threatening to engulf you.
9685: A thick layer of weeds have taken possession of what once was cultivated ground. Beneath the scrub, you can still catch a glimpse of the brown earth, and even figure out the lines of the furrows. The grass crowds around the plots, but only tufts and bushes grow inside them, thus making them look like unyielding bastions in the middle of the infinity of the grasslands.
9686: In Front of the Half-ruined Hobbit Mill
A mass of dark green leaves clings to a wall.

Situated in the middle of the eastern hillside, a small round building stands in front of you. Its circular wall is made out of irregular, many-sized, and roughly-cut stones, as if the structure had been hastily built, and they have hardly endured the weather and the years: some of them have fallen off and lie scattered on the ground or down the slope, while broad cracks and holes open their way through the wall. A tiny, worn out wooden door that stands with great difficulty on its hinges leads inside, whilst an earthy path, starting off at the entrance, goes away up the winding hillside.
9687: The Path to the Old Mill

A wide, wet, earthy track comes down from the top of the hill, taking a long way around along this southern hillside, and then setting out for the old half-ruined building that stands in the middle of the hillside eastwards. Weeds and other plants have partially covered it, a clear sign that the path has seen few travellers for years, but the route is still distinguishable. The way zigzags to detour every remotely steep incline; no slopes to climb for the hobbits that traced it long ago.
9688: A fat rabbit is here, chewing on some grass.

The monotonous flatness of the plains seems to be slightly altered by two small hills standing to the north, that are merely a little unevenness of the ground. Their gentle-sloping hillsides fade into the grassland, as if melting with it. But a swallow valley runs between them and, on its bottom, a group of houses gather around a small circle, forming a tiny village. Their inhabitants are well accustomed to the hard life in the Vales, the harsh climate and the constant threat from the Mountains. They are simple men and women, but proud and noble, and always loyal to their allies.
9689: A soft slope rises northwards to where an old, tumbledown-looking building with walls made out of rough logs and a thatched roof still stands rather precariously. A bit eastwards, in a small valley between two hills, thin columns of white smoke climb into the sky from a little village with hardly a dozen huts. Down the hillside, to the south, a group of ancient trees seem to withstand the advance of the vast grasslands that extend all around up to the horizon and beyond.
9690: In this section of the meadow, all kind of flora blooms among the grass stems. Large and small flowers of many different colours with intense scents abound, their petals taking every imaginable shape. But there are also other plants: thick, short, rough stalks, bulbous tubers, leaves sharp as blades or even thorny plants. They all grow dispersed among the green grassy background, as in a small vegetal sanctuary, or perhaps a garden for Yavanna's delight.
9692: The unmistakable marks of trampled grass show outstanding on the ground: they are certainly bear footprints, and, judging by their number, they belong to several different beasts. They all are large and deep, but some are really huge, and they slip a number of inches into the earth, the brutally squashed wisps crowding at their sticky, deep green bottom. There are footsteps all around, but they seem to lead north-south mainly.
9693: You are now in the middle of the vast expanse of grass that covers practically all the ground of these vales, like a great crowd of tiny, green-uniformed soldiers flanking the Great River as it marches past them towards the seas. Sometimes, when the wind rises - the soft inland wind, as icy in winter as torrid and dry in summer - the tall stalks swing all in harmony, taking the shape of wide waves running along the prairie, like a flag waving in the air, but a limitless one.
9694:
A low and wide-spread tree grows here.
On the tree's branches, there are two juicy plums.

A number of trees with worn, grey trunks and bent branches stand dispersed along the grassland. Perhaps one day the huge Mirkwood forest, still free from the Dark Shadow, extended up to this spot, and these few trees are the last trace of its presence. But nowadays, the grassy plains have totally surrounded and isolated them. When the wind rises and blows strong throughout the plains, and the undulating grass blades resemble the restless ocean, then the tree tops flutter heavily, like the canvas of the great vessels that sail the seas, and the trunks seem to stand straight like strong masts. But when the wind ceases to blow, everything becomes calm and the illusion fades.
9695: Although the soft swinging of the fresh, deep-green grassy stems gives them a fragile, delicate look, reality is way different. Winters are extremely tough and cold, frosts are common, and dew greets the sun every dawn as it rises over the shadowy Mirkwood forest. Summers, on the contrary, are really hot, almost torrid. Moreover, most of the animals depend on the juicy grass for their survival. Thus, behind their weak appearance, the sprigs grow strong and fibrous, with sharp edges and mighty, firm roots. From the most robust beorning to the smallest grasshopper, every inhabitant of these lands knows how tough life is over here.
9696: At the Foot of a Green Hill
A fat rabbit is here, chewing on some grass.

Some miles northwards, the top of a low hill rises heavily over the grasslands, its wide green slopes spreading all around, as if the hill had been wildly smashed by the hammer of a giant, or perhaps scattered under the march of a huge army. Here the hillsides incline shyly, almost imperceptibly, as if reluctant to leave the broad prairie. Only near the top do the slopes become slightly steeper.
9697: A thumb-long bee buzzes loudly as it flutters among the flowers.

A high and impenetrable hedge delimits this large farmhouse, whose only way in is apparently the broad wooden gate that breaks the hedge directly to the west. The ground seems to descend slightly southeastwards, where there stand a number of outbuildings and a long house a bit further. A shapely, wide, grassy track starts at the gate and sets out towards there, going down the meadow, which appears to be mostly covered with gardens full of lively- coloured flowers, and dotted with a few old oaks here and there.
9698: A well-groomed horse examines you with intelligent-looking eyes.

A bend in the high hedge that surrounds this great farmhouse suggests that you are now at its northwestern corner. The thorny wall towers quite high over a man's head. Small, dark leaves with pointed spikes along their edges, and what seem twisted stems with prickles all over, intertwine so densely that no little bit of light can get through the tangled barrier. In contrast with it, the vivid garden, that shines in a deep green background sprinkled with the many loud colours of the flowers, extends to the very foot of the wall, as if totally unaware of it.
9699:
There is a huge, pyramidal beehive here.
A thumb-long bee buzzes loudly as it flutters among the flowers.
A bearded man towers above you, the noble look of the First Edain in his face (glowing).
A well-groomed horse examines you with intelligent-looking eyes.

Tens and tens, or perhaps hundreds of huge beehives disposed in rows fill this part of the farmstead. They all seem exactly the same, with their golden bell-shaped tops made of straw. A deafening noise fills the air, due to the unceasing drone of the very many bees. And such bees! For their bulky size and extremely intense colours, it is clear that they are uncommon specimens, but they are not less hard-working because of that, and so they do their utmost to produce honey and wax for their master.
9700: A thumb-long bee buzzes loudly as it flutters among the flowers.

This wide path goes down through the hillside, across the green spreads and the flower patches, heading towards a group of small wooden buildings in the south, and, beyond them, down into a small courtyard in front of a low, long, wooden house. In the other direction, it bends softly westwards, leading to the broad gate in the hedge, but not entering the beehive fields that lie to the north, from where you can hear a loud noise. Animals seem to wander freely through pastures and gardens, but always alert to the presence of foreigners.
9702:
A large, long-bodied grey dog moves around swiftly.
A beautiful white pony with a long mane fixes you with a knowing gaze.

This little long building always seems fresh and in the shade. The light that comes in through the entrance hole is not enough to illuminate but the first few steps inside. Everything seems extraordinarily clean. There are large piles of straw, as golden as the sun, shining out in the dim light. Leaning against the side wall is a long watering trough, filled with clear, almost crystalline water. Beside it, lay several brushes and buckets. And despite their obvious residence here, the smell of the animals is remarkably faint.
9703:
A thumb-long bee buzzes loudly as it flutters among the flowers.
A thumb-long bee buzzes loudly as it flutters among the flowers.

The track runs across a group of several wooden buildings of different sizes. There are granaries, sheds and barns, and a few others whose purposes are not clear, and they all have walls made of thick, rough, oaken logs, and most of them are thatched-roofed, but some have wooden roofs instead. A great oak-wood extended all over this place way back, but a large part of it has been felled, and only the wide belt that surrounds the farmstead, and a few huge and lonely ancient trees, that grow scattered inside, are still standing. These few trees cast ample shadows, in which the animals can lie on the grass to rest.
9704:
A heavy chest of oak, banded with iron, stands here.
A water barrel has been left here.
Some curdled goats milk sits inside a cheese mould.
A sack of flour has been placed here.
A sticky honeycomb lies on the ground.

This high square building is divided into two floors. Supported by stout trunks that serve as pillars, a several-inches-thick platform rises a few feet over the floor, forming some sort of mezzanine that takes up most of the inner section. A heavy ramp made of thick planks ascends along the wall towards there, where large dark-brown sacks pile up. In the lower floor, many enormous barrels of reinforced wood are kept in store, together with big pots and jars of dark-red, rough earth.
9705:
A beautiful white pony with a long mane fixes you with a knowing gaze.
A well-groomed horse examines you with intelligent-looking eyes.

Located in front of the entrance to the long, U-shaped wooden house, the sides of this little courtyard are enclosed by the house wings, as its back side is by the front wall, where a small and dark door opens into the house. In the middle, there is a great oak trunk that shows evident signs of axe hacks. A number of lopped branches pile up in disorder beside it. To the north, a grassy track goes through the outbuildings, before continuing off into the distance.
9706: A large stone fireplace with a roaring fire warms the room.

A large hearth occupies the middle of this spacious, long hall, and it remains lit throughout the whole year, filling the room with the crackling of logs, the smell of burning wood, and the warmth of its fire. The smoke climbs lazily in search of the way out through an opening in the ceiling, past the heavy blackened rafters. Two rows of thick pillars, with what appear to be brackets for torches, support the roof that, like the walls and the floor, is made of wood. Slightly raised platforms run along both side walls, that are abutted by the wings, and so have no windows. Thus, the room is only dimly lit. On the north, a dark door leads outside, and so does a smaller one in the rear wall.
9708: A mighty brown bear, huge among his kin, growls threateningly.

Running through the wide gardens, this narrow little path heads northwards, parallel to the western wing of the house. Its outer wall is low and has no windows, and it is made of large, circular, hardly-worked trunks. Similarly, the roof ascends steeply towards the peak, right along the middle of the house. Flowers crowd around the track, and they seem to have been deliberately planted to grow facing it, offering their colour to whoever follows the way.
9709:
A tall plant with a perfectly smooth stem gracefully marks the landscape.
Yellow flowers, with grey-green foliage, grow in clusters here.
A thumb-long bee buzzes loudly as it flutters among the flowers.

These wide gardens, crammed with colour and liveliness, spread over most of the southern area of the farmhouse. A great assortment of flowers and plants are here, and some of them are so extremely rare that they may not be found anywhere else. Some have big crowns of silky petals; others are small and handbell-shaped; a few seem long and swaying; the variety is endless. And they shine in the most variegated colours, in deep and pale shades, and dark and light hues, like a great rainbow over the ground, but one with its stripes mixed and intermingled in a myriad of coloured blotches.
9710:
A sticky honeycomb lies on the ground.
A sticky honeycomb lies on the ground.
A sticky honeycomb lies on the ground.
An angry bee is working on a honeycomb here.
A three-foot-long queen bee is here, buzzing agitatedly.
A bee flies around here, collecting nectar from the flowers.
A bee flies around here, collecting nectar from the flowers.
A bee flies around here, collecting nectar from the flowers.
An angry bee is working on a honeycomb here.
An angry bee is working on a honeycomb here.
A drone bee flies around here, angrily buzzing.

The loud buzzing becomes deafening as one walks through the numerous huge honeycombs disposed in careful order, forming some kind of grid. They are big sheets of honey and wax, divided into perfect hexagons, and very sticky, thus hindering one's advance. The bees, on the contrary, come and go continuously, fluttering all about, and gathering in dense swarms. Here, inside the hive, nothing appears to be radically different from the bee pastures outside, but everything intensifies: from the thunderous drone to the utterly penetrating, almost wounding sickly-sweet smell.
9712:
A bear is here, covered with coarse black fur.
A bear is here, covered with coarse black fur.
A large rabbit looks peacefully at you, ready to dart away.

A wide, humid grotto opens inside this hill. You can hear the noise of running water coming from the northern wall. It flows in through the many cracks and clefts, and accumulates in large pools, like small subterranean lakes, that flood most of the cavern. At the back of the cave, to the south, the stones rise over the pond, forming a rocky platform, and a broad passageway with damp and earthy walls starts off there. Every now and then, large drops come down from the ceiling, breaking the silence with a deep sound as they fall into the dark-looking, shadowy lake.
9713: The gentle slope descends from the west levels to this area, forming a wide flat expanse, as if, long ago, a giant among giants had sat to rest on the hillside. A large pool fills the terrace, and its quiet waters look still, almost motionless, except for the shy and tiny waves that the wind raises occasionally. By the edge of the slope, several boulders have gathered; large, grey, rounded boulders with smooth surfaces, cold as ice and hard as steel.
9714: Despite the bleak look presented by the circular walls of this old building, and although nothing but rubble remains of the ceiling, the heart of the mill appears to be in good condition, as if the millstones were carved out of very hard stone. Both stones take up most of the room. The lower millstone, bigger and heavier, is placed below. Over it, the grindstone rotates when the mill is in motion. A very worn wooden chute deposits the grain between them, and, once milled, it can be collected in sacks through another hole.
9715: In this narrow cellar there is hardly any room to maneuver. A big waterwheel occupies most of it; the structure and the paddles are made of wood, which, in spite of their bad appearance don't seem shattered or broken. Two holes open through the stone ceiling, leading to the upper floor. A tight, circular one, right above the wheel; and another one similar to a trapdoor, but narrow and uncomfortable-looking. The whole revolving mechanism is placed over some sort of waterway, inclined along the hillside slope. The lack of space, and the fading light that filters from above, may force you to grope your way along, to avoid banging into something in the darkness.
9716:
An old page torn from a book is lying here.
A large bat is here, hanging in the darkness.
A large bat is here, hanging in the darkness.
A large bat is here, hanging in the darkness.
A huge bat is here, emitting piercing squeaks.

A carpet of thick dust covers all the surfaces, as everywhere else in the hole, but here it seems dotted with small black stains and filth of dubious source. The walls show dark marks of damp, and so does the ceiling, flat near the door but inclined in the rear end. A round dormer window leads outside there, although the dense vegetation conceals it partially. A wide stain spreads beneath it, exuding a piercing moisture smell. A broad bed, with legs worn away long ago and rotten bedding, and an old wardrobe, full of holes like a sieve, make up the furniture.
9717: A Dark and Silent Living Room
A large, dusty alcove sits in a wall, smelling of soot.

Shadows now dwell in what once was a bustling living hall. Wrapped in a deep darkness, an old hearth seems asleep, as if recalling ancient and innumerable stories, songs, and gossip, that certainly filled this room when hobbits still lived in Soakedfeet. One can still fancy the smell of the seed-cakes, or the shrill wheeze of the teapot on the heavy oaken table that occupies the centre of the room. The other furniture left with its owner, as well as the frills, profuse judging by the numerous holes and stains on the walls, and with them were gone the voices and tales, plunging the room into a deep silence.
9718: A one-finger-thick layer of grayish dust covers the ground of this small entrance hall, crowding about the borders, right where the walls stand. In spite of the prints of time, you can still distinguish their light yellow shade, and of course the smooth round section, that melts with the ceiling. On the northern wall, several marks reveal the positions that were once occupied by pictures, and perhaps wall lights, and even a chest of drawers. Close to the door, a long peg rack, darkened by the dust, still clings to the wall, and one can easily picture a row of coloured hoods hanging from it. The well-excavated corridor goes into the hill, but, to the south, it seems to open into a room.
9719: This short but carefully hollowed passage constitutes the hub of the hobbit hole. Leading into the hill, a few rooms open along its sides, approaching the hillsides in search of air and light. Its section is perfectly round, except, of course, for the thoroughly even floor, now covered with a thick layer of dense, grayish dust that gathers in piles, as if matted. The tunnel seems to come to an end here, but, to the north, a wide hole leads into a shadowy room, while, on the south, you can see a worn, green, oval-shaped door.
9720:
A small, rusty, broken cogwheel lies here.
A diamondback rattlesnake is coiled here, ready to strike.

The very air of this tiny room seems old and heavy. It is rancid and thick after years of stillness, and loaded with dust that scratches your throat and burns your lungs as you breathe it. The room is in utter disorder: high stacks of rusty tools and broken utensils, and heaps of old and useless junk intermingle following no pattern. Agricultural implements, pots, and crockery all appear to be in rather bad condition. Half-hidden among the rubbish at the foot of one of the walls, a little hole, only a few inches wide, disappears into the rock, its dark mouth wrapped in shadows.
9721: You are now in a small room with a lofted ceiling, that most probably follows the surface of the hillside. Opposite the entrance, where the ceiling is lower and more inclined, a half-rotten wooden shutter seems to have been closed for centuries. Below it, the wall has been carved in the shape of a stone table, with two holes for both a sink and a fireplace. The wall on the left seems dotted in numerous rusty nails, from which one day surely hung all kind of utensils and pots. On the contrary, a spacious larder opens to the right, inside which the smell of food still appears to float in the air.
9722: Many years ago, when the Third Age of Arda was still young, the first merry hobbits with their bare feet and loudly-coloured clothes moved into these dales, and they settled in this wide hill with gentle slopes, where the abundant grass grows always high and wet, and thus they called it Soakedfeet. It has been a long time since those little creatures migrated westwards beyond the Misty Mountains, but the hill is still honeycombed with passageways, even though most of the tunnels have collapsed and entrances are blocked. However, in the upper part of the hill, near the top, a small, round door still seems to be in good condition.
9723: Cultivated Fields in Front of a Farm

A large, though rough, wooden building, undoubtedly a farm, stands to the north. The surrounding fields have been cultivated and the ground divided into small raked plots. A small trail starts right at the farm door, and leads southwards zigzagging among the patches, seemingly bound for a small village with smoking huts that lies in a wide valley between two low hillocks. Every now and then, you hear a distant animal sound, but most of the times it is too faint to identify it.
9724: A well-fed cow stands here chewing her cud listlessly.

High and splendid, the tender, juicy blades of grass are the best possible food for the Beornings' animals. The soil must be extraordinarily fertile, for except for some nibbled wisps, there are no clearings in the grasslands, as if every night, new shoots of fresh grass would spring out to fill those areas where the beasts graze during the day, thus the prairie always looking deep green and radiant at each new dawn.
9725: A Tiny Stream through the Rich Grazing

You are now at the gentle slope of a broad hill covered in ever wet grass, its flat, smooth-edged top slightly outstanding to the southwest. A tiny brook with crystalline water comes down running through the fields from the south, and the grass blades on its surface look like diminutive boats competing in a weird race with no apparent goal, the sound of the flowing water encouraging them to rush. Down the hillside, the small stream seems to fade away suddenly, as if swallowed by the very earth.
9726: A tiny stream, clear and limpid, springs suddenly out of a group of rocks, as if, tired from being imprisoned in the underground, it wanted to feel the fresh air of the vales again. Slithering along the surface of the stones, the drops end up falling into a large flat rock, in an unceasing rattling, and forming a reservoir in a hollow of the stone, whose walls, soft and smooth, have been carved by the most skilled sculptor: Arda itself.
9727: Some delicious wild strawberries grow on the ground.

The grasslands roll out, covered with tall grass that dances and shifts in every thinkable nuance of grey, green and yellow. As the grass moves, strange but fascinating patterns are created, revealing sometimes the ground that is the home of small animals that scurry around in their search for food. In all directions the plains stretch out, as far as the eye can see.
9728:
There are two woody, stemmed plants here.
A red-furred doe wanders peacefully among the grass.
A robin is here, carrying small pieces of wood to its nest.

The grass here is almost three feet high, but bends easily and does not seem to hinder movement. The grass and several scattered bushes conceal the identities of some small wild animals, undoubtedly on a quest for food. The grasslands continue for almost as far as the eye can see.
9729: A colourful butterfly is fluttering around here.

Grassland spans here as far as the eye can see. The ground is a mix of dark green grass and hardy evergreen bushes. Far in the east, looms the shadow of a dark forest. In the distance to the west, great peaks of a distant mountain range can be seen.
9730: These fertile meadows are covered with tall, lush green grass that reaches a man's waist. Small, beautiful flowers of all colours grow here. Even some scattered bushes covered with flowers seem to have planted their roots here. To the east the land is covered with grass, while to the west there lie more meadowlands. Some trees grow tall and proud to the north.
9731: A sharp-eyed hawk is here stalking some prey.

These beautiful and lush meadows are of a deep, emerald-green colour. The high grass seems fresh where it stands in the fertile soil. Amidst the green, small flowers add touches of red, blue and yellow to the picture, only making the green of the grass appear even greener. In all directions but south the plains stretch out.
9732:
Yellow flowers, with grey-green foliage, grow in clusters here.
A bee flies around here, collecting nectar from the flowers.
A bee flies around here, collecting nectar from the flowers.
A bee flies around here, collecting nectar from the flowers.
A bee flies around here, collecting nectar from the flowers.

These vibrant meadows are the colour of emeralds, their lush, green grass covering most of the ground. In the small spots where the grass does not grow, beautiful flowers of red, blue and yellow grow in abundance. Surprisingly, the fertile soil has not been cultivated, but to the south one can spot signs of human hands: rows of beehives stand there. Some bees seem to have found their way here in their search for new, fresh flowers. In all other directions the plains stretch out.
9733:
A tree-snake lies wrapped around one of the tree branches.
A tree-snake lies wrapped around one of the tree branches.
A tree-snake lies wrapped around one of the tree branches.

Here stand, in small groups, a variety of different trees. One can spot birches, beeches and even a few lonely oaks. The grass that grows beneath the trees seems to be shorter than that covering the plains, but not much else grows in the shadow of the trees. To the south lie the more fertile vales of the Anduin, while to the north, east and west the vast plains stretch out.
9734: There are two handfuls of clover here.

These low, flat lands obviously hold better soil than the surrounding area, as lonely, great beech trees grow here, stretching their branches towards the distant skies. They look like great beings where they stand, keeping their distance between themselves. In their shadow, low grass and a variety of flowers and herbs grow. To the north and east, the great plains roll out, while to the west the bank of the Anduin rises. To the south the trees stand closer.
9735: This low rise is more exposed to the wind than the lands that lie about it, and yet a good place for the living. Small trees grow about, casting shadows over the grass and giving the rise a distinct air in comparison with the surroundings. To the east the great plains roll out under the sky, while to the west the great Anduin flows, like a tongue of steel in the green landscape.
9736: A Marshy Stand of Grey Willows

A shrub with maple-like leaves is growing here.
On the shrub, there are two handfuls of blackcurrant berries.
A brown toad is here, hunting flies.

Here the banks of the Anduin resemble a marsh more than anything. In this soft and moist soil some grey willows have placed their roots. Their long, thin branches stretch out and hang to the ground, giving the place a sad and almost ghost-like appearance. To the west lies the great Anduin, while to the east the land rises unto great, rolling plains.
9737: The waters of the Great Anduin have swamped the bank here, making use of the earthy, rockless ground. A small marsh has formed, where vegetation grows thick. The tall stalks of the reeds sprout out of the flooded ground, like a tiny but dense forest that sometimes hinders your advance. The marsh seems to spread southwards, and to the east, there is still vegetation to be seen, although much more sparse compared to the other areas.
9738:
A brown toad is here, hunting flies.
A green frog is here, hopping around.

The tall and strong stems of the reeds sprout out of the pools that cover the ground everywhere. At times, they form little clusters, at other times they grow in dense groups. The ground beneath your feet is soft, its solidity weakened by the water that has flooded it. And yet it doesn't seem unsafe, as the roots keep it compact. To the south, the earth becomes firmer and firmer, as high grass takes the place of the reeds, and you can see a wooden structure floating on the waters of the river.
9739: The remnants of an old loading bay sway gently over the waters. In olden times, this pier was used to unload goods that came from the northern vales, or even the valuable loads from the distant Gondor in the south. But those were other days, and now the quay has fallen into disuse. The wood is starting to rot away, and a few planks fell off long ago. Some loose threads are all that remains of the mooring ropes. A small outhouse, once used as storing area, crumbled long ago into a pile of broken planks. Only the dock itself looks relatively well-preserved, but even so, it doesn't give you any sort of confidence in its stability.
9740: A number of trees grow scattered on this gentle, grassy slope that rises very slowly towards the east away from the Anduin. Some of them stand lonely, as if they had been expelled from the very earth by some unknown force, while others group together in small clusters. The high, fresh grass crowds around their trunks, as if trying to challenge them, sometimes concealing them by several feet.
9741: The grasslands extend endlessly all around, and, from the distance, they seem to tinge the ground with a thick layer of intense green dye. However, a few features catch your eye: some trees grow scattered on the plain to the west, and there are some to the north too, but they stand together there with a somewhat dreadful look. In the opposite direction rises a small hillock with soft slopes, behind which the meadowlands spread.
9742: A Soft Slope to a Ruined Building
The garden snake slithers harmlessly here.

Rising slowly over the plains, this soft slope ascends towards the top of a small hillock to the east, where the old ruins of a wooden house still stand in a rather precarious condition. If there ever was a track leading up the hillside, it must have faded long ago, swallowed by the abundant grass that carpets the ground in deep green. The rear wall of what seems to be a building stands atop the hillock, a small door leading inside.
9743: In Front of a Ruined Tavern

A rickety old large wooden house crowns the top of this low hillock. The walls, made up of fat logs, are covered in thick moss and lichens, and exude a piercing smell of moisture, but the fineness of the oaken wood has preserved them from rotting. The roof seems to have borne worse fate - most of it caved in long ago - and only the broadest balks stay at their place. In the front wall, the door has tumbled down inwards, leaving a wide hole through which you can glimpse numerous broken planks and debris. Over the lintel, a half-rotten wooden sign seems about to fall off.
9744: Over the gentle slope that ascends gradually southwards, the deep green of the fresh grass mixes with the dark brown of the dug up earth, in small ploughed patches with deep furrows. The tender shoots of some unrecognizable vegetables spring up timidly out of the ground in some of them, but others already show well-grown plants that conceal the dun earth beneath them. The soil is rich in these lands, and the diverse crops feed their vigorous inhabitants throughout the year.
9745:
A small grasshopper clings to a blade of grass, ready to spring.
A small grasshopper clings to a blade of grass, ready to spring.
A small grasshopper clings to a blade of grass, ready to spring.
A small grasshopper clings to a blade of grass, ready to spring.
A small grasshopper clings to a blade of grass, ready to spring.

The tireless grasshoppers seem to have taken possession of this shallow, wet depression of the ground. Time and time again, they climb up the grass blades to jump from one shoot into another, often crashing in the air, but only to raise themselves and start climbing again, in an endless cycle. Sometimes many of them gather in a small area, and then the swarm appears as a dense mist that boils with activity.
9746: Certainly, water must be plentiful in this lands, because no matter what the weather is like, the stems of the grass are always fresh and wet, and look full of life. Sometimes, when the sun is shining high in the sky, the little water drops sliding along their edges mirror the light, adding a diamond-like sparkle to the deep green colour of the grass, and lightly tinting it with rainbow coloured reflections.
9747: A brown pond between old branches and roots is here.

A large pond has formed on this plain, surrounded by fresh mud soaked by the cold waters of the Anduin. The stalks of the reeds sprout everywhere, along with all sort of bushes and weeds that stick out of the mud and the pools. The pond looks full of life; the background croaking of the frogs and the restless singing of the crickets mix with the soft sound of the stems grazing in the wind, only disturbed by the occasional hollow sound of a little beast diving into the dark water.
9748: The ground has become muddy in this mire, and only the filtered water prevents it from drying. Even so, there are cracks and slits, and even furrow-like splits running straight as in a ploughed field. The reeds, though not as numerous as in the marsh to the west, line up along them like small, natural fences, as if delimiting their own domains. Grey, dense mud fills the widest cracks, forming small pools that seem to attract vegetation, as it sprouts thronging there.
9749: A group of trees with twisted branches grow in this area of the meadowlands, like a distant bastion of the dark and shadowy Mirkwood forest miles away to the east. Their knotted trunks tower above the grass stalks, over which long branches with dark, sharp-pointed leaves hang. Their dim, almost black tops form a contrast with the intense green grass on the ground, casting large and somewhat gloomy shadows upon it.
9750: In these lands, where water is abundant and grasslands extensive, the soil is rich in life, and, from the Old Days onward, men have inhabited these dales. As early as in the First Age, when the Great Enemy whose name shall not be mentioned had not still been defeated, some tribes of men, that came from the first Edain, settled in the northern vales. They were known as the Northmen, although the elves called them Nenedain, and they were related to the men of Rhovanion and to the ancestors of the Rohirrim. Nowadays, the main inhabitants of these lands are the Beornings, who protect the vales against the orkish threat from the mountains.
9751:
There is a huge, pyramidal beehive here.
A bee flies around here, collecting nectar from the flowers.
A bee flies around here, collecting nectar from the flowers.
A bee flies around here, collecting nectar from the flowers.
A small grasshopper clings to a blade of grass, ready to spring.

Lots of ochre-coloured beehives line up on the flower-dotted grass, and they impregnate the air with a strong sickly-sweet smell. The Beornings take care of the bees, and plant flower patches for them. And in exchange, the bees supply them with the honey they need to bake their honey pies, following the recipe from their forebears. Some people even affirm that these true-hearted, rude men can talk to their animals, by using a strange language based on sounds and gestures, and, judging by their relationship, they may be right.
9752: A well-fed cow stands here chewing her cud listlessly.

A small field of green grass, tall and dense, spreads out here. A coarse fence, made out of unequal oaken branches covered in moss, surrounds its borders, but not totally enclosing it. The Beornings look after and feed their animals, which in turn obey them of their own free will. In the western side, a rickety door leads into a thatched-roofed shed, from where you occasionally hear a loud neigh. Right behind it stands a larger wooden building, surrounded by cultivated fields; most likely a farm.
9753:
A small animal, all covered in spines, snuffles amongst the undergrowth.
A robin is here, carrying small pieces of wood to its nest.

Several insects, almost too small to be seen, fly between the blades of grass here. The dark green grass must contain some nutrients they crave. They leave no mark on the vegetation and seem to cause no problem for travellers or the small animals that can be heard to the north. Far off to the west, the high peaks of a mountain range scar the horizon. A good distance to the east, the tops of many tall trees mark the beginning of a great forest.
9754: Three foot tall grass grows through a mass of brown shrubbery. Some smaller bushes try to carve out a niche for themselves to grow in, but appear to be losing ground. Tracks of small animals, perhaps scampering for food, are abundant.
9755:
A large brown wolf stands here, its teeth partly bared.
A large brown wolf stands here, its teeth partly bared.
A colourful butterfly is fluttering around here.
A restless rabbit bounces around.

The flat grasslands are fairly featureless. The thick green grass grows in abundance. The ground is neither rocky nor rolling, instead it merely sits, holding the weight of things placed on top of it. Some animals can be heard and the occasional gust of wind rustles the blades of grass.
9756: The ground is a mix of dark-green grass and shrubs. Some small animals leave tracks in the ground as they go on with their daily routine of searching for food and shelter among the vegetation. In the northwest, a small hut can be seen. Far in the east lies a forest.
9757:
A loaf of bread has been left here.
A seed-cake has been left here.
A large piece of cheese has been placed here.

Everything seems mixed up and out of its place in this small, low-roofed kitchen. The sink is full of crockery, while the pantry is almost empty, the food scattered all over the most unlikely places. There are sacks lying on the ground, and jars standing on the table, together with full and empty pots and even an apron hanging from the back of a chair; all is in utter disorder. Several escape routes, rather than exits, flee out from this mess. To the south, a broad wooden door leads outside; to the east, a smaller one conducts into a small shed; and a winding staircase, with high, narrow steps, ascends into the upper floor through a trapdoor hole.
9758: A simple wooden chest is here.

This narrow and long room faces east, its axis following the line of the roof. Floor, walls and ceiling are all made of well polished, creaking, wooden boards, that shelter the inside from the winter cold, the persistent damp, and the annoying trickles. On the eastern wall, a round window lights the room. At dawn, it casts the light directly upon the bed, announcing the start of a new working day. A few planks, a mattress that is basically a heap of dry straw, and some thick wool blankets make up the double bed a tiny bedside table stands near its head. At the foot of the bed, beside the trapdoor hole, an old chest completes the furniture.
9759: A sturdy pack horse is standing here.

Without other purpose than giving the animals shelter and cover during the night, this shed isn't even distributed in sections. On the contrary, the different heaps of dry straw delimit the room, and the animals occupy their own without any trouble. By the rear wall, there are piles of still fresh and green hay, and a great stack of straw crowned by a large hoe. Several implements lean against the walls in one of the corners. Everything is somewhat in disorder, but clean and rather free of insects. A small door on the west links the shed to a large house in front of it, a waist-high gate leads into a meadow to the east.
9760: The grasslands abound in all directions. Some miles to the east some dark trees turn into a forest. The animal life seems prevalent by the scraps of food and the scarring of claws and teeth marks in the vegetation. On the western horizon, travellers can stare in awe at the snowy peaks of the great mountains.
9761: Thick grass grows in the shade of the tall young trees. Much of the light that would hit this area in the morning, is blotted out by the thick dark forest to the east. Only in the afternoon do the plants get the sunlight they need to live.
9762: This is the very edge of the eastern side of the Mirkwood Forest. Tall, old trees with dark leaves and black bark cast a gloomy shadow. A few small bushes try to carve out their place in the shaded ground. The view into the forest offers no clue to its contents and shows no sign of a clearing. To the west are the plains consisting of miles of flat land, a welcome change from Mirkwood.
9763:
The remains of a dark oak lie here in a heap of rotting compost.
The remains of a dark oak lie here in a heap of rotting compost.
The remains of a thick tangle of dark vines lie here in a heap of rotting compost.
The remains of a black tangle of roots lie here in a heap of rotting compost.
A black squirrel peers down from the branches of the trees.

Gloom fills the air, as the lack of light is discouraging. Visibility is poor and the trees all look very similar. They have bark so black it blends into the night and reflect any stream of light in the day. Rustling in the top branches can be heard. Who knows what creatures would find this dreary a setting a suitable habitat.
9764: Weeping Willows at the River's Edge

A large brown wolf stands here, its teeth partly bared.
A beautiful and docile horse is standing here.

In the moist soil at the river's edge stands a cluster of weeping willows, giving the landscape a beautiful, but also a sorrowful and desolate visage. As the wind rustles the long, thin branches of the trees a strange music is born, sounding as if the trees were impatient to move. Under the trees there is little vegetation - all sunlight is absorbed by the willows' hungry leaves. Directly to the west lies the river Anduin, and to the east, vast grassy plains.
9765: A seemingly ever-present wind rustles the grass of the wide plain, making it sway and shift in all imaginable nuances of green and yellow. Occasionally, a small cluster of flowers adds new colours to the landscape, breaking the monotony. To the east, north and south the vast plains continue seemingly unending, and to the west lies the great river Anduin. Beyond that, a hazy bluish grey wall looms - the Misty Mountains.
9766: A great sward of long, golden grass climbs up this low rise amidst the surrounding landscape of rolling plains. The few silhouettes of the lonely oak trees or the moving shadow of a distant herd of deer can be seen dotting the landscape and giving it life. An occasional breeze or gust of wind sweeps down from the Misty Mountains lying far to the west across the steel-grey surface of the mighty river Anduin. These open grasslands extend to the horizon in all other directions, with the ground sloping gradually upwards in the north.
9767: Green and yellow grass covers this even ground. The air is filled with a heavy silence, broken with the occasional singing of birds and the whisper of the wind. Broken blades of grass betray the presence of some animal activity.
9768: Amid the low grass grows a patch of colourful flowers. Apparently the flowers are resilient and appear to bloom all year round - when one wilts, another springs up. Some are dry already, some are just beginning to sprout.
9769: The soil in this fertile valley allows the grass to grow tall and strong. The unbroken horizon assures that this very landscape will continue for miles and miles ahead. The sound of water can be heard to the west.
9770: As older grass withers and dries up, the new shoots higher and higher. Entangling with each other, they create a thick curtain hiding the animals and perhaps the occasional traveller from sight. The grass grows lower to the east, and to the north a group of stately trees livens up the horizon.
9771: A small brown snake is slithering around here.

A cluster of low, but sturdy trees has settled on the plains. The oaks grow apart from each other, allowing the sun to reach the lower plants and the undergrowth. The ground is flat in all directions, and covered with grasses and herbs.
9772:
A fierce boar is here, making grunting noises.
A boar cub is playing here, and exploring the wide world.
A boar cub is playing here, and exploring the wide world.
A great male deer with reddish hair and twisted antlers stands here proudly.
A colourful butterfly is fluttering around here.
A soft-skinned female deer wanders peacefully among the grass.

Lying east of the river Anduin, these grasslands grow in a quiet dignity. The grass has a lustrous green colour and the land is smooth and gentle. In the south an outcropping of trees dot the horizon, and in the northeast another cluster of trees can be seen.
9773: A soft-skinned female deer wanders peacefully among the grass.

The river Anduin lies to the west, its ample waters providing nutrients for this gentle grassland. Tracks of different wild animals are imprinted in the soft soil. These plains extend in all other directions with a gentle slope to the north.
9774: A beautiful and docile horse is standing here.

The plains have risen and formed a small slope. The soil is fertile and the vegetation is thriving and healthy. The most common plants are grasses of several kinds, stretching about the landscape for many miles. Westward the flow of the river Anduin can be heard.
9775: The ground is slightly uneven with rocks scattered across the landscape. Occasional clumps of flowers break the monotony of these plains. The grass is very soft and flexes in the breeze. To the west the flow of the Anduin can be heard but tall grass blocks the view.
9776: A roe deer is standing here, watching the terrain while chewing the vegetation.

A solitary bed of flowers grows here, amongst the seemingly endless plains. Tufts of weeds grow between the rows of flowers, and many plants are in state of decay. The plains continue in all directions, rising slightly to the south.
9777: A colourful butterfly is fluttering around here.

The field here is covered with short grass with some flowers growing in it. The flowers have various colours ranging from yellow to blue. To the south one can spot a bed of flowers and in the east one can see the plains stretch out till the horizon.
9778: A bee flies around here, collecting nectar from the flowers.

Corn and different kinds of plants grow intermingled with the short dark green grass that thrives here. The trees growing here are very high, casting a shadow over the grass during the day. To the west the plains continue onwards to the horizon.
9779: A few trees with small plants growing below them grow in the short grass, that has a light green colour. To the west the plains continue until they reach the Anduin; in the far north is a small trail, and in the east is a clump of trees.
9780: The short grass that grows here is a bit brownish. Some flowers grow in between the grasses on the dark black soil. There is a trail to the north snaking through the vast grasslands and one can see the plains stretching out to the Anduin in the west.
9781: This trail is mostly made up of small pebbles and little stones and is becoming partly overgrown by weeds due to lack of use. The trail continues onwards to the west heading for the Anduin. To the east, the trail begins to be made less out of pebbles and more out of dirt.
9782: Some small vegetation like dandelions and buttercups have sprouted in between the dominant grass that grows here. A few trees are growing scattered around here, giving little refuge for small animals. To the south is a small trail, which bends and continues onwards far into the east.
9783: The plains in this area are covered by a lush green grass with beds of flowers here and there in them. There are some elevations in the plains with trees on them. To the northwest is a small hill with trees growing on top of it, and to the west the plains stretch out to the great river Anduin.
9784: In the grasslands there are some trees with bushes growing beneath their branches. The trees growing here are approximately sixteen feet tall. To the east is a small hill with a group of trees on top of it. The plains in the west continue onwards until they reach the river Anduin.
9785: The plains are covered by grass with a few trees scattered around. There are some small rises and dips in the plains due to erosion from the heavy rainfall in the past. In the lower spots, there is more vegetation. In the west the plains spread out to the Anduin, to the north the plains become almost empty. A small hill covered with trees can be seen to the southeast.
9786: These plains are almost completely empty in comparison to the ones surrounding them, save a few trees and weeds. There are stones of different sizes scattered around the plains. To the south and the east the plains begin to fill up with vegetation, to the west the plains continue onward to the Anduin, and in the north they stretch out towards the foothills of the Grey Mountains.
9787: The ground here is very flat with only a few dips and rises in it. In these dips grow some small bushes and different kinds of weeds. In the west the plains look rather empty and in the north the tops of the Grey Mountains can barely be seen.
9788: A few dandelions and some white flowers with yellow hearts can be found growing among the grass. A few trees are standing solemnly around. In the far north the plains stretch out to the foothills of the Grey Mountains.
9789: A garden snake slithers harmlessly here.

The grass in this area is about two inches high, with small flowers growing amongst it. There are some heaps on the ground supposedly made by some moles. A few solemn trees grow in these plains, giving shelter for small animals. In the north the peaks of the Grey Mountains can be seen. In the southeast one can see the edge of a small forest, which stands out against the plains surrounding it.
9790: Several kinds of herbs in different stages of growth grow amongst the grass. A variety of different mosses flourish in this area, thriving in the wet soil. There are some small groups of trees in the plains giving shelter and housing for small animals. A small forest is visible to the south, breaking the monotony of the continuous plains. In the far north the highest peaks of the Grey Mountains can barely be seen.
9791: A wild bull seems ready to charge you.

The grass is very short here with occasional patches of grass as high as someone's ankles, giving protection for small animals. There are some small fields of purple and white flowers growing between the grasses, just sticking out their petals above the grass. To the east the rim of the forest connected to Mirkwood can be seen, whereas in the southwest a small forest is growing.
9792: There are some flowers, small plants, and weeds growing interspersed with the very short grass. The trees begin to grow closer together as one approaches the border of the light forest in the east, which is part of the forest west of Mirkwood.
9793:
A woodpecker is here, tapping on a tree.
A swallow flies high above the ground.

The ground is covered by a thin layer of rotten leaves and twigs with some freshly fallen leaves on it. Some toadstools grow on the bark and foot of the trees in the forest. The canopy of the trees above is not fully blocking the sky above, so some light filters through it during the day. To the west are grasslands stretching out far to the west, to the southwest is a small depression.
9794: Fallen leaves and broken off twigs make up the cover of the ground. Some small shrubs grow here and there between the many trees, whose canopy almost blocks out all light from the sun during daytime. To the west and south the forest gets less dense, for the rest, the view is limited by the dense growth of trees.
9795: A thin layer of humus is covering the ground, being made up out of decomposed leaves and dead plants. The canopy of the trees is so dense that during the day barely any sunlight comes through it. Some strange species of toadstools thrive on the humus covered ground.

A forest spider is here crawling around.

A large brown snake with black patches is coiled here.

A soft-skinned female deer wanders peacefully among the grass.
A black snake hurries towards you with sly intentions.

The forest is composed of smaller, thinner trees to the east where the sky has broken through the canopy. Darkness is all that is encountered to the west, as the forest canopy closes in. A dense grassy field east of here can be seen through the trees. Bushes push themselves between the smaller trees, competing for the limited sunlight.
9797:
The corpse of a large red deer is lying here.
The corpse of a black snake is lying here.

The grass is little more than three feet tall and little else can grow here. The forests to the east and west encroach onto this field. The greater part of Mirkwood Forest can be seen to start in the east from here. The grass has grown wild, but would be ideal for cattle to graze upon, were it possible to lead them here. The field continues to the south.
9798:
A black moth flies towards the light.
A black moth flies towards the light.
Some dark, thick writhing vines whip all around you.
A huge, black wolf is here, ready to devour.

The large oak trees that grow here mark the beginning of Mirkwood forest. Forest humus litters the ground and small fungi are quick to take advantage of the detritus. Small bushes grow here but quickly disappear to the east where the forest becomes thick and very dark. During the day, the sun only shines through patches in the western part of this canopy. There is little noise here other than the breath of an occasional wind. There is a grassy field to the west and more forest to the south.

The sun does not exist here. The giant tree trunks in this part of Mirkwood are all that is visible. The forest humus smells of decay, the rotten trees that have fallen over are evidence of this. From behind every tree there seems to emerge strange and foreboding sounds.

Large oaks and beeches grow here, forming an impenetrable canopy through which the sun cannot be seen. The forest is enshrouded by a gloomy darkness, that is ever present. Massive tree stumps have become the home to small animals here, from the sounds that can be heard from this area. Whatever kind of strange creatures that have settled here remains a mystery.

Ancient stumps covered with moss stand here. Oak trees grow scattered but seem to cover this area with a thick canopy of branches and leaves blocking out the sky. Little else can be seen here, other than the occasional fallen branches. Bushes or other green flora cannot grow here, mostly because of the ever present shadow that looms overhead.

Giant branches far overhead grow out from huge oaks in this area of the forest. The forest floor is composed of huge rotten tree stumps, and the dark soil exudes a strong fungal odour. Rotten mushrooms, which have grown here and are now past their prime, add a fetid smell to the air. The smell of rot seems to continue off to the east.

Within this part of the dark forest, strange white fungi grow. There is a foetid odour present that hangs among the trees. The white fungi seem to be the origin of this smell, and the piles of bone strewn among them seem to give these fungi an ominous appearance.
