Dark and gloomy trees hang overhead within a shadowed canopy. Little can be seen here besides the gigantic tree trunks which seem to obstruct the view beyond a few meters. Large fungi grow here out of the duff layer, which is mainly composed of tree roots and fallen branches. A foul stench can be detected off to the west.
9805: A Dark Path in the Forest

The path through the forest continues on to the east through the dark and gloom but cannot be seen very clearly. Fallen logs to the north seal off any travel in this direction. It is dark and gloomy here, and the forest does not look inviting. The trees seem to close in on the path to the east, which may make it impossible to travel there.
9806: A Dark Path in the Forest

The path continues to the west and to the north. It is just a small footpath that traverses this part of Mirkwood. There are numerous fallen logs that have not decayed yet to the east, making that part of the forest impassable. The large trees in the south seem to grow towards this path in an attempt to disrupt it.
9807: Trees grow here in convoluted forms, spiraling up into the mists of the canopy above. Serpentine shapes entwine one another distorting visibility here. No further travel can be made east as the trees become impassable in that direction. The forest continues to the west and south, while the faint traces of a small clearing can be seen through the gloom to the north.
9808:
A silky, spidery web is here, spun into a spiralling wheel-shape.
A small mushroom grows nearby.

This area of the forest is composed mainly of the corpses of trees broken by some huge force. Stumps of gigantic trees stand here, as well as the logs that have fallen over. To the east, the forest becomes impassable, because of the sheer mass of timber that has decayed and been piled there. The smell of trolls is strong here, indicating a presence of several. The piles of bone and dung, indicate that this may be a home to these creatures. The forest still forms a tight canopy here, as the trees that have remained standing have grown to occupy the area that has been disrupted.
9809: Darkness engulfs everything here, as tall trees grow over head blocking off all light from the sky. The forest floor is a mass of fungi, large roots and other forest litter. Several large trees have fallen over in the east which prevents travel in this direction. Strange sounds emerge from the forest canopy as creatures that live in the top of the forest traverse it.
9810: The forest looks extremely ancient here. Old decaying trees are being replaced by larger trees, but even these are slowly being decayed by some wasting illness. Fallen logs here are quickly being taken under and decayed by fungi. This place reeks of decay and death. A skeleton of an animal, perhaps from some recent kill by a carnivore lies here under one of the logs.
9811:
Black roots shift uneasily all around you.
A tremendous black oak looms here.

Dark trees grow here, twisting and bending together creating nightmarish shapes. Several large trees grow around one very twisted shape. This large tree stands out because of its size and its shape. Twisting around, looking very old and hideously bent out of shape, it has large masses of stringy grey moss hanging from it. The smell of death is strong around this centre figure of a tree.
9812: The remains of a thick tangle of dark vines lie here in a heap of rotting compost.

Large trees have fallen here indicating the presence of something huge which moved through here some time ago, as evidenced by the fungi and moss that grow upon the logs. A disgusting odour emanates from the south, and noises of creatures can be detected. The forest in the west becomes very dark and still. The forest grows so thick in the east that it prevents any further travel in that direction.

The stink of death fills the air. Mounds of bone lie piled against the dark tree trunks of this forest. This area looks as if a slaughter took place as here are gashes into the trunks of trees. Steaming piles of dung lie to the north, indicating that something has moved through this area recently. There are no sounds that would indicate any ordinary forest life here.

Skylight no longer exists here, if ever it did. Large tracks of carnivorous creatures and bones of large herbivores are present on the ground. The large number of bones, and the stale scent of death make this place resemble a graveyard of sorts. Perhaps it is a feeding ground of a sort.

The trees have succeeded in tenting this area in darkness. Beeches and black oaks crowd together in this sombre forest. Dismal strands of silver-green moss hang low from tree limbs, creating a haunted garden of broad tree trunks emerging from layers of rotting leaves and fungi.

A round tangle with waxy leaves and white berries grows on a branch nearby.
Black roots shift uneasily all around you.

The dense trees branch out preventing easy travel. Barely enough light filters through the leafy canopy to sustain the growth of forest fern here. Beech and oak mass here in this still, sullen forest. The bark near the base of some of the trees in this area seems to have been shredded.

The darkness of this oak forest is enhanced by the growing number of black alder here. Shadows loom deeply, allowing only glimpses inside this tight mass of tree trunks and wispy trails of almost glowing, pale-green mosses and not much else. The deep layer of decay and mulch that cushions this black forest floor prevents noise from escaping.

A black moth flutters around.

A small break in the top branches lets a ray of light fall down illuminating the surroundings. The light reveals the forest to be even gloomier lit than when dark. The dirt is teeming with tiny bugs and some smelly unrecognisable bacteria. The remains of what was once a small squirrel is here decaying. Perhaps it is better that most of the forest is not well lit.
9819:
Black roots shift uneasily all around you.
A tremendous black oak looms here.

How the dense plants that make up the undergrowth survive without light is a mystery. They grow underneath and between the fallen limbs of the trees. A thin vine grows between two of the trees trying to reach beyond the tops in search of a bit of sunlight. The forest looks the same in every direction.
9820:
A huge black fungus is here, exuding a foul stench.
A huge black fungus is here, exuding a foul stench.
A colourful butterfly is fluttering around here.

One of the great trees of Mirkwood is here, lifeless. Obstructed by the other trees, it was unable to fall completely to the ground. What felled this monstrosity with it's 30 foot trunk, is a mystery but it must have happened long ago. Dead leaves still cling to its branches though they crumble to the touch.
9821:
Black roots shift uneasily all around you.
A tremendous black oak looms here.
A tremendous black oak looms here.
A black moth flies towards the light.

Whether it is the sun or the moon that shines above the tree-formed canopy is unknown. What little gleam of light enters here reflects on torn pieces of spider silk from what seems to have been a great web. The spider silk is old and no longer sticky to the touch. Instead it looks like thin hairs strewn carelessly over the dark branches.
9822:
A small mushroom grows nearby.
A giant, strange looking green fungus is here, ready to devour you in seconds.
A huge black fungus is here, exuding a foul stench.
A black moth flies towards the light.

Even though not far from the forest's border, there is no sign of a break in the trees in any direction. Little light reaches this place. The sound of scurrying animals above in the treetops alerts travellers they are not alone.
9823:
A huge black fungus is here, exuding a foul stench.
A giant, strange looking green fungus is here, ready to devour you in seconds.
Black roots shift uneasily all around you.
A tremendous black oak looms here.
A black moth flutters around.

During the day the small amount of light that reaches here makes the black sap leaking from some of the trees looks gelatinous. Small insects have been trapped and killed just by landing in a sticky spot. The leaking sap has also captured some small black pieces of fur.
9824:
A huge black fungus is here, exuding a foul stench.
A black moth flies towards the light.
A black squirrel peers down from the branches of the trees.

It's dark as dusk here even at noon. In a constant struggle for light it is amazing that any plant life on the ground survives. A few sturdy bushes have managed to grow and some shade grasses send straggle blades up through the mess of fallen branches on the ground.
9825:
Some dark, thick writhing vines whip all around you.
Some dark, thick writhing vines whip all around you.

A canopy of high tree limbs overhead signals that you are within the Mirkwood forest. The ancient dark trees are thick, but here at the edge of the forest they still let some light pass through to the undergrowth. There is almost no sign of animal life, though perhaps there are a few rabbits and squirrels nearby.
9826: Some young trees grow here just outside the forest to the south. They are a welcome change in the plant life from the deep dark gloom of Mirkwood. Their light brown bark has a sweet smell of sap. So pleasant are these trees that many birds have left nests within the branches.
9827: This forest fairway stretching from north-south is home to many woodland flowers. Purple blooms of delicate columbine tower above the multi-hued green mosses covering the soil here. Blue lupine and pale yellow daisies with brown eyes peek above the shorter grasses.
9828: A large dangerous looking green snake is coiled up here.

These shadowy plains only receive a short supply of sun as they are bordered on both sides by the gloomy Mirkwood forest. The woods have grown in such a dense formation that no entryway is found easily. Along the edges of the forest new saplings crowd competing for space. The fields continue both north and south.
9829: Plains continue here within these mighty forest walls. Travel is possible north or south as fields can be seen in these directions. The trees lining this area grow extremely dense and shut out light within their woody depths.
9830: The haunting and dark forest surrounds you in all directions except to the south. To the north the trees are less crowded than east or west where it is impossible to navigate. This forest plain is dotted with downed tree trunks, bracken and forest foliage. Not much light of day illuminates this field as the tall shadows of the surrounding forest prevent it.
9831: The corpse of a black moth is lying here.

The forest of darkness is bathed in a humid silence. Strong limbs and boughs of these strong trees hold up the leafy tent, preventing much light of any kind from entering. Moisture seeping up from the forest floor has created a boggy depression between these trees that almost prevents passage to the north. Tall beeches and oaks occupy most of the acreage here.
9832:
A silky, spidery web is here, spun into a spiralling wheel-shape.
A black moth flies towards the light.
A swallow flies high above the ground.

Darkness dwells here, as light is not common in the deep reaches of Mirkwood Forest. Broad tree trunks barricade the entry east as the woods take every foothold in that direction. The stillness and humidity in this part of the forest is strongly apparent. Strange sticky webbings of some kind connect many of the tree limbs.
9833:
A black moth flies towards the light.
A black moth flies towards the light.
A swallow flies high above the ground.

Stillness hushes these woods into an unnatural silence. Wisps of haunting green-grey mosses hang down from forest limbs. The one constant within this forest with its mature trees and dense canopy is the humidity. A strange humid heaviness fills this forest.
9834: The trees block out all the sun until late into the afternoon. There are no signs of animals here, just a few insects flying from leaf to leaf. One suspects the small plains animals do not venture into the woods and those animals native to Mirkwood Forest dare not show themselves this far west. The smell of rotten wood is in the air.
9835: Some dark, thick writhing vines whip all around you.

Interwoven groups of tall branches form a canopy blocking out the sky. It extends far to the east. Those travelling into the forest better get a good look at the sky while they can. Already the trees block out all the morning sun. Even at high noon not much light touches the ground.
9836:
A cluster of dark green, feathery fronds flourishes in the shade.
A black moth flutters around.
A black moth flutters around.
A robin is here, carrying small pieces of wood to its nest.

The vegetation is much thicker here than in the west. Rotten branches lay on the ground, catching and tearing at the skin of animals and travellers. Under the protection of these branches some small animals seem to move shielded from view. A careful listener can hear the sounds of dark squirrels moving in the live branches up above.
9838:
The remains of a thick tangle of dark vines lie here in a heap of rotting compost.
The remains of a black fungus lie here in a heap of rotting compost.
A black moth flies towards the light.

The forest is dark and hides all but the eyes of some small dark creatures living high within the branches of the trees. They don't seem to be aggressive but may distract travellers from more eminent dangers here. A sticky film, or perhaps just the leak of sap, almost black in colour, causes dead leaves to stick to the large trunks.
9839: Some dark, thick writhing vines whip all around you.

The leaves of the trees are very thick, and dark green in colour. The small amount of light that reaches the ground, must first pass through the thick leaves of the trees, then slip between the gaps in the crooked branches and hanging vines. The large bushes that grow here must thrive in shade. There are a lot of rotting branches and leaves lying on the ground.
9840:
A cluster of dark green, feathery fronds flourishes in the shade.
A black moth flies towards the light.

This is the very edge of the Mirkwood Forest. It lies just a few yards to the east. The trees within its boundaries are dark and foreboding. Almost no sun reaches the ground, blocked by a canopy of branches. The ground is covered with rotten branches and leaves.
9841:
A buck runs swiftly from place to place, looking about warily as it grazes.
A restless rabbit bounces around.

The plains in the west are slowly turning into the forest in the east. Some trees can be seen here and there, and bushes have become more common. Far in the west, the snow-capped Misty Mountains can be seen. To the east nothing can be seen but the gloominess of the edge of the Mirkwood Forest.
9842: Small animals too quick to be seen dart between the trees and bushes. From the scratches in the ground and the bite marks in some half eaten seeds, one could assume these are the same type of moles that roam the western plains, although few dare travel this far east.
9843: A brown furry gopher is here, ready to dive back underground.

Rich grains can be found in abundant supply here. The countryside sweeps gently in easy rises and rolls of the grassy terrain. The seasons have favoured this area and the rich bounty is appreciated by the wildlife. The tight formation of the grove of trees to the north does not offer any entry in that direction.
9844: Many of the tree-trunks here have been severely damaged. It looks like the bark has been deeply scratched leaving big gaping grooves in the trunks. This damage looks as if it has been done quite recently as fresh sticky resin is oozing from the wounds. To the east and south the vegetation is so thick that it is impossible to travel far in those directions.
9845: The forest intensifies both in the number of mature trees and in the looming darkness. These trees compete with each other for sky views by stretching limbs ever wider and higher and ultimately preventing any light from ever reaching the forest floor. Long hauntingly pale whisps of moss drape down from the branches above. The stands of mature trees block any passage to the east.
9846: A colourful butterfly is fluttering around here.

Whispers of light drizzle down, creating long shadows between the old timbers. Mosses grow up the north sides of the trunks here. To the east the trees have grown so densely as to seem almost fused at their trunks, making travel east impossible. The layers of leaves and other forest debris that cover the forest floor encourage fungi growth around the exposed tree roots.
9849:
A giant, strange looking green fungus is here, ready to devour you in seconds.
Black roots shift uneasily all around you.
A tremendous black oak looms here.
A tremendous black oak looms here.
A black moth flies towards the light.
A woodchuck is watching for enemies here.

The thick forest walls create a silent surrounding in all directions. The sullen shadows of these ancient trees hide in the darkness of the forest floor deep with countless layers of rotten leaves. Humidity hangs thickly in the air. Rough tree bark is softened by mosses creeping up the northern faces of the trunks.
9850:
Black roots shift uneasily all around you.
A tremendous black oak looms here.
A tremendous black oak looms here.

The trees here have such a thick canopy that very little sunlight penetrates through. It is difficult to tell whether it is day or night. The forest floor is quite roomy except for the space the trunks take up. Except for these trees, nothing seems to grow on the ground, due to the lack of daylight.
9851:
A black squirrel peers down from the branches of the trees.
Some dark, thick writhing vines whip all around you.

Darkness swallows all the moonlight and sunlight that sneaks into this black grove of oaks. Gnarled oaks link limbs forming an almost watertight umbrella preventing any measure of rain from reaching the forest floor. The conditions here may attribute to the stillness that hangs thick in this grove.
9852:
A huge black fungus is here, exuding a foul stench.
Black roots shift uneasily all around you.
A tremendous black oak looms here.
A tremendous black oak looms here.
A black squirrel peers down from the branches of the trees.

The dense grove of beech and oak tightens with branches and leaves covering the sky, preventing any light from intruding here. Glossy green-grey leaves and white berries drape from bare tree limbs as if they belong there. Old toppled logs and layers of rotting leaves carpet the forest floor.
9853: A giant, strange looking green fungus is here, ready to devour you in seconds.

Oppressive silence hangs here like the moss from the tree branches. Knotty tree roots emerge from the forest humus. Large coral shaped fungi poke out between the emergent roots, taking in the available moisture and nutrients. Some of these fungi are very large, having grown old in this darkness.
9854: Darkness consumes all light here, as trees of unimagined size curl and twist in all kinds of cruel shapes. Roots of all kinds bend and twirl through the forest floor. A gloomy oppressive silence hangs here, amid the forest canopy. Through the branches to the north a very pale light can be seen.
9855: The trees here grow in ordered rows heading to the north and east, except for one in particular tree. Most of the trees that grow here tangle with other trees, forming a matted canopy of mostly thick boughs and branches. There is a lack of a rotting smell which is common throughout most of the other forest except for the peculiar tree, which has small bones piled against its trunk. A strange eldritch light seems to appear faintly off to the northwest.
9857:
The remains of a black fungus lie here in a heap of rotting compost.
The remains of a black tangle of roots lie here in a heap of rotting compost.
The remains of a dark oak lie here in a heap of rotting compost.
The remains of a black fungus lie here in a heap of rotting compost.
The remains of a dark oak lie here in a heap of rotting compost.

The twisted trees that grow here do so in what could be described as rows. It looks as if these trees were planted in a special arrangement. Their boughs and branches intertwine and form a tight canopy. Gone are the smells typical of the forest. Gone are also the typical forest organisms of decay, such as fungi. A strange pale light can be detected off to the west.
9859: There is a swath of destruction running east to west. Large animal bones lie here scattered among those trees still standing. Stumps and uprooted trees lay strewn about the makeshift path of some large creature. There is a foul stench in the air of trolls, mingled with the smell of death. There is a deathly silent here.
9860: Oaks and beeches grow in distorted, almost nightmarish shapes here. Trunks of some of the trees stretch into one another merging to become one gigantic tree all the while rising into the darkened canopy above. The forest humus reeks of fungi, as mushrooms abound here, living off the decay and nutrients of the detritus.
9861: The path that meanders into the east and west from here is not well maintained as the forest has severely encroached upon it, covering it in places with large roots from the trees to the north and south. At times, rustling can be heard in the forest canopy above, as small forest creatures travel along.
9862: A Dark Path in the Forest

This part of the trail is particularly dark and gloomy, and the canopy overhead is seemingly endless. Large bulbous fungi grow on the sides of the path. Few weeds grow here, choked off by the ever present forest. The path continues to the east as well as leading off to the west. The forest grows to the south and in the north, a strong foetid odour emanates.
9863: Beech trees collide with oaks here as one glade overlaps another. Creeks and groans can be heard as the larger oaks rise above into a dark canopy. Huge branches can be seen intermingling between large oaks and beeches. The forest floor is covered with thin papery bark of the beeches and pale white mushrooms abound. A small trail can be seen to the north through the darkness.
9864: Some dark, thick writhing vines whip all around you.

The forest looks partially destroyed as something large has been moving to the east and to the west. The ground which is normally composed of mushrooms and rotting logs is smashed and upturned. Large tracks can be seen on the ground. The stink of decay pervades this area and grows ever worst to the east. Only darkness can be seen in all directions.
9865:
The remains of a black tangle of roots lie here in a heap of rotting compost.
The remains of a dark oak lie here in a heap of rotting compost.

This area of the forest is devoid of decay. These trees here grow in rows which seem to head in a southerly direction from here. The silence here is one of anticipation, as if the forest is holding its breath. Gone are the sounds that are common in other parts of the forest. The canopy overhead is composed of branches that grow tightly together. There is a strange pale light to the south.
9868:
The remains of a dark oak lie here in a heap of rotting compost.
The remains of a black tangle of roots lie here in a heap of rotting compost.
The remains of a dark oak lie here in a heap of rotting compost.
Black roots shift uneasily all around you.
A tremendous black oak looms here.
A tremendous black oak looms here.

Silence and darkness engulf this part of the forest. The trees seem to grow in ordered rows and show no signs of normal decay. Huge branches from each tree grow together in the canopy overhead making a thatched-like roof. A pale light can be seen to the north far off.
9870: Smells of rot and decay assail the senses. Fungi of all types grow here between the large tree roots which also poke themselves out of the ground. Massive tree trunks grow here, stretching up into the blackness above. No sounds can be heard around here, and this makes the silence of this part of the forest oppressive.
9871:
A bright red mushroom is growing here.
A black spider crawls here, a shiny red spot visible on its belly.

Neither the Sun, nor the Moon can easily find routes to give light to the dark forest floor. All the plant life that covers the ground seems dead or rotting, except for the fungi which aid in decomposition. Light green moss hangs from the tree limbs like decrepit bandages.
9872:
Black roots shift uneasily all around you.
A tremendous black oak looms here.
A tremendous black oak looms here.
A tremendous black oak looms here.
A large owl with small sharp horns looks cautiously around it.

The mature tree trunks in this part of the forest are as wide as two men. Deep humus littering the forest floor absorb sounds and with noticeable effect. Leafy vines with clinging discs creep up the tree trunks towards the sky. Several of the trees here have deep scars shredded into the bark.
9873: Long trails of green-grey mosses hang down from the leafy ceiling, creating a ghostly effect. The silence of the forest can be attributed to the thick spongy layers of spent vegetation cushioning the forest floor.
9874: A black moth flies towards the light.

Thick gnarled trunks of mature trees crowd this forest, embracing only still darkness. The ceiling is packed tight with the foliage of these old trees. Humongous roots reach up in tangled masses through the rot of the forest floor making passage to the south impossible. A few of the massive trunks have been ravaged by fire leaving only blackened charred hollows behind.
9875: A round tangle with waxy leaves and white berries grows on a branch nearby.

The different grasses in this meadow provide interesting hues of green and gold allowing views of subtle beauty in all directions. A few trees dot the softly rolling landscape, growing in greater numbers to the east and preventing travel to the north.
9876: The darkness of this forest is enhanced by the growing number of mature alder here. Shadows loom deep, allowing only glimpses inside this tight mass of tree-trunks and wispy trails of almost glowing, pale-green mosses and not much else. The thick layer of decay and mulch that cushions this dark forest floor prevents any noise from escaping. The immense trunks of these trees prevent passage to the west.
9877: The forest suddenly slopes somewhat upwards. It is not a steep slope but the incline seems fairly long and ongoing. Maybe it feels longer due to the severe density of the woods making it hard to walk with any speed here.
9878: There is a great mix of different trees here. Beeches, oaks and alder trees join the pines that dominate these woods. For some reason this part of the forest seems inhabited only by very young trees. There are no mature trees at all to be found here.
9879: Some roots lie here waiting to ensnare weary travellers.

Oaks and alder are common in this forest. It does not take long to notice the magnificent oaks with dense foliage towering majestically above. In the immediate area nothing else grows, aside from the fungi and mosses that grow rapidly. To the west and south the forest is so thick that there is no possible way to travel in either of those directions.
9880: These fields are overgrown with thatch. Grains grow in abundance, despite the assault of this fast growing pesky weed, which has travelled every which way. This terrain makes travel through these parts difficult and to the north the dense grove of trees prevents travel in that direction. Several large stones terrace the western corner.
9881: A small rabbit glares angrily at you.

A tree to the west, about a mile away, is the most noticeable feature here. The plains are otherwise flat and free from tall growth. The air has a calm serenity and it carries the smell of hay. These grasses have grown here for ages, green through the summers and brown in winter. In the east lies the great dark forest of Mirkwood.
9882: Seeds blown from nearby trees have taken root here. The barely two foot tall tree growths bend and break easily under the hoofs of animals. Dark green grass covers the land far to the north and west. These little trees might be a sign of the forest that is visible to the east.
9883: The plains here are dotted with young trees, spread from a nearby forest. The trees seem strong and sturdy. Their deep brown bark seems to resist the cut of animal claws or the whip of the wind. Gazing to the east you see more trees. They seem to be a great deal more seasoned.
9884:
A black moth flutters around.
A restless rabbit bounces around.

This is the very edge of the legendary Mirkwood forest. If there is a pathway through here it's not discernible. The trees grow tall and the lower plants sprawl through their roots without limits. Some almost invisible insects fly about annoying those trying to peer into the forest's depths.
9885:
A robin is here, carrying small pieces of wood to its nest.
A black squirrel peers down from the branches of the trees.

This is the edge of Mirkwood. Its trees, hundreds of years old, tower above the ground. What one can only assume is rich soil is covered with rotting branches and cumbersome tangles of low vines. Looking east it is impossible to see anything but more of these ancient trees.
9886:
A small mushroom grows nearby.
A sturdy pack horse is standing here.
A restless rabbit bounces around.
A restless rabbit bounces around.

The ground is covered with large dark-green bushes, many old and tall trees grow here. The vegetation is mostly coloured dark green, but the bark of the trees is dark brown. In the east, the forest gets even thicker, while in the west, grasslands grow ever thicker.
9887: A black moth flies towards the light.

This is the very edge of the huge Mirkwood forest. Large trees, hundreds of years old grow here, towering above some large thick bushes. The vegetation is mostly dark-green. Nothing beyond the forest can be seen in the east, while in the west, endless grasslands lie for miles.
9888: The ground is covered with large dark-green bushes, and old and tall trees grow here. The vegetation is mostly coloured dark green, but the bark of the trees is dark brown. In the east, the forest gets even thicker, while in the west, grasslands take over.
9889:
A great male deer with reddish hair and twisted antlers stands here proudly.
A restless rabbit bounces around.

Tall young trees grow here above a carpet of thick green grass. A few plants grow in the shade of the trees. This area gets little morning light, the sunlight blocked by the large dark forest to the east. The tracks of some small animals are scratched in the ground. On a hot day the shade of the trees and then softness of the grass beckons many a traveller to rest here.
9890: The ground is covered with three-feet high dark-green grass. Scattered bushes stake claim to the ground where the grass has not spread. Wild animals, moles and others, have marked the vegetation with their teeth and claws. To the east, a dark forest is a far contrast to these flatlands. Far in the west, a mountain range covers much of the horizon.
9891: The large elk gazes coldly at you, chewing on a small branch.

The grasslands continue westward for miles, but in the east clumps of trees turn into a forest. The empty holes left behind by moles ensnare the feet of careless travellers. The holes are hard to see through the three foot thick grass. A far distance to the west the peaks of the mountains are visible.
9892: There are several holes dug in the ground here, underneath the three-foot high grass. The grasslands go on for miles to the west. In the east scattered trees turn into a forest. The peaks of the great Misty Mountains are visible on the western horizon.
9893: A great male deer with reddish hair and twisted antlers stands here proudly.

Grasslands give way to trees as the lands turns into a forest. Bushes thrive in the tree shaded shadows. The ground is a haven for vine-like plants that form a thick undergrowth. It is impossible to see too far into the dark forest to the east.
9894: The garden snake slithers harmlessly here.

The low grass filling the western plains gradually give way to this land of larger bushes and trees. The trees have light brown bark, but to the east the trees are darker. From here, the trees in the forest, just two or three miles away, look black as night.
9895: The plains in the west are slowly turning into forest. To the east the trees blot out light. The young trees here easily leave enough light to nurture undergrowth. There are few animal markings perhaps they fear the proximity of this area to the dark forest.
9896:
A small rabbit glares angrily at you.
A small rabbit glares angrily at you.
A robin is here, carrying small pieces of wood to its nest.

The grass here is thin. Weeds grow quickly covering the bare space on the ground. The land is flat and featureless. Travellers find it is easily passable but the monotony of the area disheartens and visitors tend to meander. The remains of a past campsite, a stone circle where a fire must have burned long ago, almost encourages current travellers to rest here.
9897: The sprouts of small trees poke out above the grass. Perhaps the seeds from nearby trees blew here with the wind. They are rooted among the grass and only time will tell if they survive to grow into trees. If left untouched they might have grown high into the clouds.
9898: A lone tree stands here in the middle of the plains. Perhaps a seed from the group of trees to the west once drifted here. The tree casts a long shadow on the low grass below. A few small plants try to take advantage of the shade.
9899: Many different grains germinate freely here in abundance in all areas but one. There is a small hump in the field to the southeast. Around that swelling the grasses are meagre and matted down, well worn with activity and use.
9900: The meadows meet impassable forest walls of the Mirkwood here to the north and east. The tall woods shelter this area allowing dense foliage to prosper. The few trees dotting the fields have fallen victim to vines which hang from every limb. Flowering azalea and camellia reside over the ferns in the remainder of this forest dell.
9901: Some roots lie here waiting to ensnare weary travellers.

The edge of the forest curves widely here. The plains extend to the west and south, but the severely dense forested area prevents any access to these plains. Pine trees are the most dominant trees in this area along with black oaks.
9902: Strange trees with wide green leaves make the forest here very crowded. On the ground there is a thick layer of spent foliage. Travelling through these woods can be as difficult as travelling through thick snowdrifts. To the west the woody debris has piled high making travelling in that direction tiresome.
9903:
A woodpecker is here, tapping on a tree.
A quail stands motionless.

The trees in this area have very short trunks so they resemble gigantic bushes. These stunted trees make it difficult for a grown man to walk upright without hitting the lower branches. To the north and east extremely dense vegetation prevents access to the forest.
9904:
A small brown snake is slithering around here.
A quail stands motionless.

New young saplings of black oak, beech and black alder crowd this forest entrance with bright supple greenery. The soil is enriched with a dark brown mulch of rotting vegetation. Though many varieties of ferns can be found here, the dominant mother fern is especially abundant.
9905:
A black moth flies towards the light.
A black moth flies towards the light.

Stands of mature oak dominate this sparsely forested area. The forest floor is soft to the foot, covered in the mulch of many seasons debris. Sword fern sprout in bright green clumps amid the tall trunks and shadows.
9906:
A great horned owl looks cautiously around it.
A black moth flutters around.
A black moth flutters around.

Mature beech and black oak protect the forest floor from the glare of the sun and the curiosity of the moon. Only sharp slivers of light make it to the bottom of the forest, and then only when conditions are right. Drifts of forest refuse rots back into soil with the passing seasons.
9907: Beech trees reach their long limbs toward the sky, dappling this light forest in the day and shrouding it by night. Ivy grows rampant along the forest floor and up the trunks of these trees. The forest grows darker in all directions but west.
9908: Darkness pervades this area, where the trees grow so tall and thick as to block out any and all sky. Thick branches grow together above, while large roots poke out of the ground below which makes walking tricky at best. Trees seem to continue in all directions.
9909: Visibility is obscured here through the large trees. Looking past one massive trunk, all that can be seen is another tree. The trees grow in a chaotic mass of density, twirling and entwining one another sometimes more like vines than oaks. The stench of rot and death are prevalent here. Quiet rustling in the canopy above is from small creatures, as chirps and whistles can be heard. The forest seems to extend in all directions.
9910: The forest floor here has not seen sunlight for ages. Small white fungi of distorted shapes bend and twist, covering the humus. Huge roots from the dark gigantic trees jut out of the ground making this area very bumpy. The small areas make ideal holes for the small forest creatures that inhabit this forest. The forest becomes ominously dark to the east, but seems to lighten to the west.
9911:
The remains of a black fungus lie here in a heap of rotting compost.
A small mushroom grows nearby.
A huge black fungus is here, exuding a foul stench.

Colossal trees are swallowed up into the darkness above as they grow together to form a dense canopy of leaves and branches. Shrill whistles and chirps of woodland creatures that are common to Mirkwood can be heard all around. The smell of rot permeates the air here, as fallen logs are disintegrated by large fungi that grow here. The air is damp, and the ground moist which are perfect conditions for the fungi here.
9913:
The remains of a giant green fungus lie here in a heap of rotting compost.
The remains of a dark oak lie here in a heap of rotting compost.
A tremendous black oak looms here.
A giant, strange looking green fungus is here, ready to devour you in seconds.

The trees here grow in a strange semblance of rows. There is a lack of bones fungi or other things associated with the forest in other parts of the wood. Where the forest is quiet in other places, this area is deathly still. To the southeast a strange eldritch light can be seen.
9914: Large trees look as if they have been pushed aside here and uprooted, as some creature or group of creatures have moved through here. The forest continues on all sides. The smell of rot and decay is strong here, and continue to the east. Large tracks lead off to the east and to the west.
9915: This part of the dark forest contains a large concentration of beeches. The abnormally large white trees give the appearance of standing in a giants rib- cage. The forest canopy seems lighter in places, however no sky can be seen. Large white mushrooms grow here between the beeches, providing sharp contrast to the surrounding darkness. There is a sickly sweet aroma to this area, mixed in with the smell of forest rot.
9916: This trail is nothing more than a small dirt path. To the north and south the forest grows closely together. The trail here is exceedingly dusty and each step produces more clouds of dust, which adds to the lack of visibility. The smell of rot is strong along this section of the trail, coming from both sides of the forest. The path continues along heading both east and west.
9917: The path becomes increasingly dark both here and into the east. It lightens up and broadens somewhat to the south. Dark trees from the forest crowd the trail reducing it to nothing more than a small footpath. Travel is difficult at best. There is no sky visible, as the canopy grows closely together.
9918: Trail in the Forest of Mirkwood

The large dark trees of the forest seem to grow together in an attempt to block out this offending trail with some success. In places the trail becomes nothing more than a small line in between huge trunks. Strange chirps and rustlings of small forest creatures can be heard from the canopy above which lets in little sunlight. The trail becomes ever darker as it leads off in the north, while it also seems to disintegrate into the darkness to the west.
9919: Massive oaks grow here in a twisted manner, looking as though they had been tortured rather than grown naturally. Some trees have huge gashes in their sides, from claw marks of some unnatural beast that had passed here. Several trees have fallen over, and mushrooms and even the humus have been upturned by the passing of something large heading east. A trail of sorts can be seen to the north, while the forest continues to darken to the south.
9920: A skeleton of some humanoid lies in the dust.

Large trees grow here, strangling out the skylight with their mighty branches that tangle themselves together to form a ceiling of sorts. There are no large fungi or forest creatures which can normally be associated with this forest. Another strange thing is the lack of bones or smell of rot, except for a single humanoid skeleton.
9921: A black moth flies towards the light.

Trees of considerable size crowd out all skylight here. However one large branch hangs low enough to be reached. The tree roots here jut out from every corner of the humus creating tangles everywhere. Small mushrooms grow on every root feeding of the rich nutrients of the wood and surrounding humus. The stench of wood rot hangs in the air.
9922: Massive oaks grow here in a tangled mass of tree after tree. Branches grow together in a mass of wood that chokes out all light from above. Roots from underground poke out tangling much that grows here. Rot and decay are seen here as there are many different bones and skulls strewn about, particularly near the larger of the roots growing here.
9923: This is the outskirts of the large forest to the east of here. Trees here grow tall enough to block out most of the sky, though in patches, sunlight can pierce through the darkness. The smell of rot and decay is evident here, and seems to continue off to the east. To the west a large grassy field can be seen. On the forest ground, there are tracks of small forest creatures coming to and from this area. Faint rustlings all around can be heard as these small creatures move to and fro.
9924: The huge trees here become ever larger as they continue to grow eastwards merging into an increasingly darker canopy. Huge clumps of greenish-grey moss hang from the branches of these trees, and large bracket fungi grow from the trunks. These trees look like they have been here for a very long time. Huge tree roots extend from the ground, giving the forest floor a rough and bumpy appearance.
9925: A cluster of dark green, feathery fronds flourishes in the shade.

Tall majestic oak trees grow here blocking out most of the sun. Roots from these trees sprout from the ground intertwining themselves with one another making the soil uneven and travel difficult. Dark shelf fungi growing from the trunks seem to be one of the only things that can grow in this darkness. The forest continues to the north as well as to the south of here. To the east the tree trunks become darker and taller still. It seems lighter to the west.
9926:
A small mushroom grows nearby.
A large toadstool grows nearby.

The lofty trees here do not grow close enough to prevent the sun from shining through the tops. The forest floor is littered with the leaves of seasons past rotting timber and many varieties of fern. Leafy vines attach themselves to the tree trunks, in pursuit of daylight.
9927:
A cluster of dark green, feathery fronds flourishes in the shade.
A reddish fawn romps harmlessly among the tender grass shoots.

This sheltered meadow is protected by the forest in all directions but south. This location makes for longer nights with the long shadows of the forest close by. The northern facing tree trunks are awash with bright green moss. Shady forest flowers and ferns abound.
9928: A sprawling green bush of stinging nettle grows here.

The mature forest is close to the east across this meadow. Thorny thistle and stinging nettles hide within the wheat fields covering this area. Small flowers top stout stems dotting these grasses with texture and colour. The bothersome weeds can make passage by foot painful and slow-going.
9929: The broad mixture of mature trees diffuses the sky's offerings. Scrubby groundcover grows waist-high in some areas. To the south the woods open up to golden pastures.
9930: The trees give way to an open expanse of ferns and woody rhododendrons. Wild thorny hedges ramble into the glen to the west, beyond a well-tended garden. Soft mosses blanket the ground beneath the rich variety of forest vegetation.
9931: Fescue and other grasses grow shorter here, and wide stony patches of light brown earth are dotted with small shrubs and bushes. To the east the plains filter out and a loose glade of ferns thrives near the gloomy forest wall.
9932: A colourful butterfly is fluttering around here.

The dark forest to the east stretches to the north and south, thick as a castle wall, with few negotiable entryways. Dainty monkshood, velvety ground mosses and forest ferns grow here nourished by the moisture of daily dew and protected by the heavy shadows of the forest. Decaying logs lay haphazardly throughout these meadows, making travel cumbersome.
9933: The meadows meet the forest here with fallen trees and an array of ferns and forest flowers. Thin white stems topped by round white seed heads colour the green, looking like tiny magical wands. Clumps of dead foliage and leaves have accumulated in this sheltered meadow creating a natural haven for the wildlife here. There is no entryway into the forest to the east, it is too thick with trees.
9934: This area is covered with debris from seasons of dead foliage. It is overgrown with vines, creating a dense thicket. Bright purple blooms of thistles on pale prickly stems shoot up between the foliage of untamed, creeping, thorny vines. There are many large bushes, as tall as any man, with healthy green leaves above spent barren limbs.
9936: Several trees here grow close together. Their roots intertwine far below the surface. Above the ground, weeds have grown wildly into the size of small bushes. Marks on the tree trunks and damage to the flora give hint of a large animal or animals nearby. The thick vegetation tends to obstruct your view.
9937:
The garden snake slithers harmlessly here.
A small rabbit glares angrily at you.

The trees are denser here than to the north or west. Wild plants are plentiful within their shaded shelter. On the ground are the tracks of animals, some predators others prey. Low branches and tall plants have been trampled or broken forming animal paths.
9938: The clear views towards the horizon, becomes a thing of the past here. Trees close by begin to blot out the view. It is difficult to see much else than their many outstretched branches. Broken bones of a small mole are on the ground. The bones are badly decayed and would crumble to the touch. Whether this animal died of natural causes or was broken in two by the jaws of a larger beast is unknown.
9939: Bushes conceal small animals frightened by the presence of strangers. The grass is thinner here, it's roots not as strongly knit together. A few strands of onion grass poke out from the lower grass.
9940:
A restless rabbit bounces around.
A robin is here, carrying small pieces of wood to its nest.

The grass that grows here is coloured dark green, and some small bushes are growing about. The animals in the undergrowth are going on with their daily routine for food. In the east, the plains start turning into a light forest, but in the south and west, grasslands seem to take over.
9941: A great male deer with reddish hair and twisted antlers stands here proudly.

The ground and vegetation is slowly changing. To the south, the grass grows higher and becomes thicker. To the north, the grass thins and does not rise far off the ground. The white caps of the Misty Mountains can be seen far to the west.
9942: Thick green grass covers the ground here. Some of the taller blades show the signs of being trampled upon in the not too distant past. Perhaps by travellers on horseback or the carefree roaming of some animals. Toward the south the grass look like it may have once been under the care of some diligent gardener.
9943: The grass, while mostly wild, seems to have spread here from what may once have been a well-tended lawn. There are few bare spots and the grass seems to all be of a similar variety. Only a few bushes and the grass is only broken up by the recent growth of weeds.
9944: The garden snake slithers harmlessly here.

To the west is the front door of a small wooden building. An old path leads from an in-ground well to the door. From here you can see storm damage to the structure's roof. Whole pieces of roof are missing, presumably fallen into the house. Some neatly chopped wood rots south of the entrance.
9945:
A carrot is lying here.
A large potato is growing here.
A large potato is growing here.
A carrot is lying here.

Wild weeds invade this area. They leave little room for bushes or even a small tree to take root. The ground was once tilled and the remnants of what looks like a vegetable garden remain. Some ignored potatoes have sprouted into plants. There is a small wooden house to the east.
9946: The grass begins to thin a little, and various weeds have taken root. Rotting plants lay upended about the area, their sweet stench filling the air. Dirt has been thrown carelessly around, in no particular pattern.
9947: The vast plains and seamless grasslands end here giving way to more varied vegetation. Weeds that flower and less sturdy plants grow harmoniously in this dark soil. What enables this land to host this wide variety of life is yet to be seen. To the west a great mountain range looms on the horizon.
9948:
A small rabbit glares angrily at you.
A small rabbit glares angrily at you.

The northern plains become southern grasslands here. This in-between area has grasses of varying lengths and some sporadic shrubbery. A few moles live here but not as many as in other parts of the region. Other small grazing animals have left their hoof marks in the ground.
9949: To the south of this spot the plains gradually become grassier. One might suspect a change in the soil for the change to a hardier vegetation and taller grass. Some mole holes can be seen in the ground, but the moles keep to the underground.
9950: There is little break in the thick grass of these plains. This dark grass is so tightly rooted together that it would be next to impossible for any other vegetation to grow through. The odd sound of a mole tunnelling in the earth nearby seems unusually loud since it is the only thing audible.
9951: A robin is here, carrying small pieces of wood to its nest.

A few leaves from the trees to the north lay in the grass. Some carried by the wind others by the scurrying of animals. The trees offer a pleasant distraction to the monotony of dark green grass that carpets most of the plains. Some small flying bugs almost invisible to the naked eye jump from one blade of grass to another.
9952:
A tree-snake lies wrapped around one of the tree branches.
A tree-snake lies wrapped around one of the tree branches.
A tree-snake lies wrapped around one of the tree branches.
A tree-snake lies wrapped around one of the tree branches.

A group of tall trees grow here breaking up the monotony of the plains, here with bark so dark it's almost black. These trees have not grown to even half their potential yet. Some squirrels have left scratches in the trunk and branches. Nuts, cracked open and those just lying on the ground appear to have little hope of taking seed.
9953: A great male deer with reddish hair and twisted antlers stands here proudly.

This group of trees is a welcome contrast to the barrenness of the plains. These are middle-aged trees, stretching tall into the sky, but not so old as to cast a large shadow upon the land. Some bushes grow in the small amount of shade provided. An almost dead smell emanates from the trees that are most assuredly alive. The footprints of some large animals are embedded in the dirt.
9954:
*Eadrith the Rohirric Woman*, wielding a narrow runed awlpike, is here, riding a warhorse.
A colourful butterfly is fluttering around here.

Seedy grasses fill these fields with waist-high stems. Spurge blankets the rich soil below. The ideal growing conditions in these pastures yield enough grain to satisfy the wildlife here. There are trees north and south with the plains continuing to the east and west.
9955:
A brown furry gopher is here, ready to dive back underground.
A quail stands motionless.

A tight circle of chestnut trees stands together in these grassy wheat fields. Spent shells litter the ground below them. Mustard and fennel season this broad field with their presence. Far to the east the dark forest grows.
9956: The wild plains have fanned out here to form a tame plush carpet of seemingly uniform blue-green fescue. Slight depressions and gentle rolling meadows are softened by the thick cushioning of this luxuriant lawn. There is no shelter in this open sweep of green.
9957:
A lone hawk soars high above you.
A colourful butterfly is fluttering around here.

Wildflowers and flowering shrubs colour these meadows all year round. Hard red fruit speckle the woody stemmed, evergreen brambles that grow freely. Beautiful blooms including tulip, crocus, anemone and lilies are strongly represented with their colourful display. A few crab-apple trees dot these fields.
9958: Grasses including wheat, oat and fescue prosper in these fields. To the north tangled masses of prickly brambles prevent travel in that direction. Off to the far west not much can be seen aside from the Misty Mountains. The entrance to a forest is east of here.
9959:
An erect shrub with green pinnate leaves is growing here.
Inside the shrub, there are two piles of crimson raspberries.
A low shrub with bright green, oblong leaves is growing here.
Scattered in and on the shrub, there are three piles of blueberries.

Thorns and prickly leaves cover many bushes and broad vines. Many varieties of berries thrive in the rich soil provided by forest. There are short bushes with leathery dark green leaves and ground-hugging evergreen heathers. West of here a tall hedge does not allow travel in that direction.
9960: A small brown snake is slithering around here.

Long crowded rows of mature trees form a wide grassy alley. It stretches east- west and grows too densely to allow penetration through the trees to the north. The grasses growing here are of various species. The ryegrass and fescue are most dominant of the grasses and spurge is also quite plentiful.
9961:
A soft-skinned female deer wanders peacefully among the grass.
A reddish fawn romps harmlessly among the tender grass shoots.
A reddish fawn romps harmlessly among the tender grass shoots.
A reddish fawn romps harmlessly among the tender grass shoots.

The forest here is fairly open and the most common tree here seems to be oak. Hardy vines grow across the forest floor and up the large trunks. This finger of the forest is interspersed with small forest meadows and young saplings. To the south the trees grow too densely to travel in that direction.
9962: The dry earth is swathed in patches of sick-yellowed grasses. The many stones exposed above the ground look to be as promising a crop as possible here. The poor soil and the lack of water prevents further vegetation here. The shadows of the forest close in on the edges of this field.
9963: A huge, black wolf is here, ready to devour.

This field is formed of small bunch-grasses. To the east the grasses become intermingled with large bushes and further east, large dark trees can be seen. The sandy soil that these grasses sprout from is very dry and to the south becomes drier still. A small glade of trees can be seen to the west where moisture probably abounds.
9964: This grass field continues to the north and south. The sandy soil prevents much else from growing here besides the short bunch grasses. A few small boulders have come to rest here, with blue and white lichens growing on them. To the west a border of very large trees can be seen. The grass grows to this border and then stops forming a line between this field and the forest trees. To the west the grasses meet up with sedges and a few large boulders can be seen off in that direction.
9965: This field is surrounded by large trees to the north and east. These trees seem to be the start of some immense forest where light seldom penetrates. The grasses here meet these trees and stop at the forest border, not daring to grow further. A field to the west seems to have been abandoned a long time ago. The grass field here stretches into the south.
9966: Small saplings of beeches meet larger oaks to the east as the beginnings of Mirkwood forest takes shape. Bushes and grasses that grow here quickly disappear into the encroaching forest. A few large vines have taken up residence in this part of the forest. The canopy quickly becomes dark to the east, but here, the sun is able to pour through.
9967: This area of the forest looks as if it were damaged by a fire a long time ago. Many of the larger trees look scorched by fire. Some of them have even been hollowed out, making them home for small creatures. The darkness that is so common in the other parts of the forest is just as prevalent here. The forest continues in all directions.
9968: A bright red mushroom is growing here.

Gloomy darkness is all that is encountered here. Strange dark trees grow here blocking out all light and sky. The lowest branches of the trees are covered by strange looking stringy grey moss. The forest floor is home to several varieties of mushrooms. There is a stench of decay here.
9969: Gigantic branches, barren of leaves, reach down from the darkness of the canopy. Huge trunks, many laden with shelf fungi, grow scattered here. The forest floor is uneven at best with many roots having grown through the humus tearing it up. Strange pale plants have sprouted up here, alongside these large roots. The smell of decay is strong here, and it seems to emanate from the east and west. To the north, a small trail can barely be discerned through the gloom.
9970: Trail in the Forest of Mirkwood

This dusty trail seems seldom maintained given that many roots from the forest have found their way onto the path. So many gnarled roots make the road hard to follow in spots. The only way for one to realise this is even a road at times is to spot the clear areas between the trees. Large mushrooms grow on the sides of this trail. Through the gloomy darkness the trail can be seen to the east and west, while the forest trees tower above to the north and south.
9971:
A small mushroom grows nearby.
Black roots shift uneasily all around you.
A tremendous black oak looms here.
A tremendous black oak looms here.

Massive trees grow here, distorted in shapes unimaginable. Trees and branches twist and mesh together which completely obstruct any sign of skylight. Roots of massive sizes grow out of these large hideous looking trees. Several piles of bones are near some of the larger roots. A trail seems visible to the south, while a smaller path is visible to the east.
9972:
A tremendous black oak looms here.
A reddish fawn romps harmlessly among the tender grass shoots.

The trees become ever taller, disappearing into the darkness above. If a canopy exists it cannot be seen from here. Death and rot are all that exist on the forest floor. Large trees which have fallen over, resemble corpses with fungi growing over them. The occasional skeleton of a large herbivore lies here gazing absently into space with its hollow eye sockets.
9973: Trail in the Forest of Mirkwood
A small campfire burns here, its low flames giving off only a little light.

Stories are told of how dark and dreary this trail is, but they do it no justice. Hardly any light shines in during the day making the forest canopy overhead very oppressive. Strange noises can be heard from every corner of the wood. In some places this trail is little more than a footpath, overgrown with large roots jutting out of the ground.
9974: A distinct smell of decaying things taints this part of the forest. Skeletal remains of many animals and a few humanoid creatures lie strewn about the forest floor. Rot pervades this area as small, oddly shaped fungi decay fallen giant logs into the humus. Strange rustling sounds can be heard from all around, but no source can be determined. If there is a canopy it cannot be seen, as the darkness above reveals nothing. The darkness and smell of rot continue into the east. A faint clearing of what may be a path can be seen to the north.
9975: Large forbidding trees offer no sign of light from above. There is no noise from the usual forest creatures. The only life that lives here in the darkness besides the trees themselves are small fleshy fungi that make use of the forest litter.
9976: Huge towering oaks block out all light here. Menacing trees with huge branches grow here, giving this forest a dreadful appearance. Gone are the sights and sounds normally associated with forest life. This dark forest continues to the east and north. Through the dark haze present in this forest to the south and west grass fields can be seen.
9977: The grassy plain that exists here is overshadowed by large trees in the east and north, where an immense forest seems to begin. South of this field lies the remnants of a cultivated hay field. West of here the short grass from this field continue.
9978: A great male deer with reddish hair and twisted antlers stands here proudly.

An old hay field exists here. At one time this field was cultivated for hay or alfalfa, or some grass. The reasons for this field's existence have long since disappeared as has most of its cultivated appearance. Old fence posts dot the borders of this field, in a feeble effort it seems to keep out the dense grassy fields that surround it.
9979: Short bunch grasses abound here, not allowing growth for anything else. The only things that prevent this field from being flat are large rocks that jut out from the centre. The rocks seem somewhat out of place, but do not yield to the growing grasses that surround them. Lichens have taken residence upon these rocks, giving them a slightly bluish tinge. An old wheat field lies north of here while grassy fields can be seen to the east and west. A glade of small trees lies to the south.
9980:
A cluster of dark green, feathery fronds flourishes in the shade.
A shallow pond is here, tinted green with algae.

Small trees of oak and beech make up this glade, providing shade for a small pond in the centre of these woods. Tracks of small animals can be seen going to and from this waterhole. Small grasses abound here as these trees only provide shade and do not choke out the sky as the nearby forests seem to. Ferns and other fragile plants grow close to the pond, depending on it for much needed moisture.
9981:
A soft-skinned female deer wanders peacefully among the grass.
A reddish fawn romps harmlessly among the tender grass shoots.
A reddish fawn romps harmlessly among the tender grass shoots.

The forest here is mainly immature midsize trees with narrow trunks that are branchless until they form the crown of the tree. The treetops are widespread and form a roof which allows just a little sunlight to filter to the ground, even though the trees are not too close to each other. To the east there is an opening in the forest forming a wide river of grass.
9982: A dark iridescent dragonfly flies by.

Mature oaks and beech trees grow together in this quite open and sunny part of the forest. Several broad ancient trees with branches and boughs full of leaves stand above the rest. Young fiddlehead bracken prosper here in the seasons of dead leaves and vegetation strewn about the forest floor. To the west and south plains open up and the forest ends.
9983: Yellow flowers, with grey-green foliage, grow in clusters here.
Small rambling bushes and thick green grass make up most of the terrain here. A few withered oaks reach out with scraggly limbs. Not far to the north, the edges of the forest can be seen.
9984:
A red-furred doe wanders peacefully among the grass.
A reddish fawn romps harmlessly among the tender grass shoots.
A reddish fawn romps harmlessly among the tender grass shoots.

The green landscape is covered by a thick sod of ryegrass and fescue which is about the height of a man's boot. It slopes gently to the west where a small grove of peonies thrives. To the east a tall wide-stretched hedge grows wild and hinders access to what lies beyond.
9985: A sprawling green bush of stinging nettle grows here.

Brambles, stickers and sharp nettles have overtaken the plains grasses. Travel here is difficult even by mount. Underfoot, the rock-hewn soil is matted with prickly weeds that catch and snag everything passing through.
9986: Clumping ryegrass covers this plains. The ryegrass has choked out any other plants here, with the exception of a small grove of dwarf holly. To the west, the plains drop off into the depth of a ravine, making travel in that direction impossible.
9987: A large beautiful rose bush is blooming here.

The green grass is accompanied by evergreen shrubs and wild roses. The colours of these sweetly scented roses make this meadow as spectacular as any here in this vale. The scene can be dazzling with a bright blue sky behind white billowy clouds. A steep ravine to the west prevents travel in that direction.
9988: There is as much exposed bedrock as dirt in these fields of scrub grasses. Silver grey foliage of tough rock garden creeper circles the exposed stone. Bristles of dry stickers stand above the meagre crabgrass and weeds in these rough grounds. The plains continue to the north and south, while the hostile terrain seems to carry on west.
9989: Plain bent grass seems to dominate the other plants in these fields, growing low and stealthily across the plains. Tiny burrs covered in thin hairy barbs hide among these grasses awaiting passers-by to snag. Lesser grasses with thin delicate green stems are topped by lacy seed heads of pale gold.
9990: A robin is here, carrying small pieces of wood to its nest.

The hustle and bustle of a variety of small animal life dominates this area. Moles and other small animal scurry about their daily routine just out of sight. To the east is a small group of trees. In all other directions, the plains stretch onward for miles.
9991: The grass here grows higher than the surrounding plains. Perhaps something in the soil is causing it to thrive. What ever the cause, the tall grass has a strong sweet smell that lingers in the air. To the east are some trees. Far to the west, the caps of a mountain range loom in the distance.
9992:
The large elk gazes coldly at you, chewing on a small branch.
A robin is here, carrying small pieces of wood to its nest.

Animal tracks have worn down the thick green grass in several spots. The few bushes have been scoured for berries and small insects. These plains must be teeming with small animals. Yet, none can be seen. The plains continue in all directions for miles.
9993: The tall tops of onion grass rise above the dark green grass that covers most of this area. The bite marks of small animals into the onion greenery has let lose the sweet onion scent. A few other grass varieties also grow here. To support so much growth the soil must be rich in nutrients not found in other parts of these plains.
9994: The smell of wild onion overwhelms here bringing tears to the eyes of many a passer by. The grass grows meagrely in comparison to the thriving onions. Several small animals have left their teeth prints in these plants. Perhaps they were drawn to the rich smell and then surprised by the bitter taste.
9995: A large dangerous looking green snake is coiled up here.

The grass here is shorter than to the north or south. It is dark green in colour and the thick blades of grass cling together. A few wild onions have taken seed here. The plains to the north seem overrunning with strands of tall onion grass.
9996: Dark green grass, almost three feet high, covers the ground. Some moles have dug holes here, but rarely do they dare show themselves. In the north the grass is lower, perhaps due to changes in the soil. Far to the east lies a dark forest. In the distant west is a mountain range.
9997:
A small evergreen plant grows here, its woody stems reaching two feet.
A robin is here, carrying small pieces of wood to its nest.

The grasslands stretch out for miles in all directions. The grass is dark green, and almost three feet high. Some small wild animals are searching for food among the few small bushes that grow nearby.
9998: The scattered remains of nuts and berries lay here. Some small animal, probably a mole, appears to have had a feast. There are several dirt strewn mole holes dug into the grass. The thick grass is a dark green and thrives on the soil in these parts, spreading out in all directions.
9999: Animals scurry about faster than the time needed to make out their species. They hide within the dark green grass like thieves gathering berries and seeds before larger animals might have the opportunity to feed on them. The few bushes that grow here have been damaged by scratches and bite marks. To the north a few mole-holes can be seen.
10000: The vegetation nestled within the high grass here, has been scavenged for every last berry and seed. The small animals here devour the plant life in staggering amounts. The competition between moles, hiding deep in their holes must be fierce.
10001: A small animal, all covered in spines, snuffles amongst the undergrowth.

The odd wild plant breaks up the thick carpet of dark green grass. Sounds from below ground indicate that a mole colony is busy at work. The grass stretches for almost as far as the eye can see. The land is flat and monotonous. Travellers may find this area quite unremarkable, however the small animals thrive in the consistency of this easily passable land.
10002: A lone hawk soars high above you.

This is the home of several small animals. Moles have dug their homes down into the soil. The grass is dark green and covers much of the area. A careful observer would notice small bite marks in the blades of grass and the lower limbs of the few bushes. The rustling within the higher grass can only be the scurrying of the small mammals in their search for food.
10003: A robin is here, carrying small pieces of wood to its nest.

Some small round rocks are scattered randomly between the blades of grass. Though the soil here supports hardy dark green grass, the rocks indicate that this land was once barren. Few bushes or shrubs can survive here. The land is flat for miles and there is no shelter from the wind.
10004: The large elk gazes coldly at you, chewing on a small branch.

Thick blades of grass grow through the rocky soil. Their roots not well embedded in the ground give hint that this land was once barren. Very little other than the grass will even grow. Though the flat land is home to several sturdy shrubs and a few bushes.
10005: A large boulder sits here, breaking the monotony of the surrounding plains. It is the only noticeable landmark in the bleak and dreary land. Several small bushes have taken refuge on the lee side of the massive rock. The soil here is dusty and inhospitable to little more than the dark green grass that dominates much of these plains.
10006: The plains here continue on to the horizon in all directions. Caution is needed to avoid stepping in one of the many mole-holes dug into this land. Grasses in many shades, from dark to pale green, grow in clumps, perhaps concealing the moles who make this land their home.
10007: The flat lay of this land allows for a great deal of visibility. The dark grass continues for some distance without break of hill or valley. In the distance appears to be the mountains. The taller peaks almost seem to meet the clouds. Dense trees far to the east form a forest.
10008: Dull bent grass and weedy spurge cover these grounds. Several evergreen shrubs form a low bushy mound to the south. The plains continue on in every direction. A smattering of small hills indicates some rodent population uprising.
10009:
A white centipede is here.
A small centipede is here scurrying about.

A butte of seemingly solid grey-blue granite stands as tall as a Hobbit's knee The deep cracks along the rock protects the multitudes of insects that live within them. A deep vale to the north prevents travel in that direction. Voracious creeping vines find ideal conditions here as their foliage clings securely to the textured rock face.
10010:
A swallow flies high above the ground.
A swallow flies high above the ground.

The grassy plains drop off to the east as a steep ravine has left a deep cut in this lush vale. A few scrub oaks peer over the edges of the drop. This ravine can be seen running north to south - then cutting east to west. These fields lie at its junction. The severe cut of this ravine makes travel east or south unthinkable.
10011: A swallow flies high above the ground.

A deep ravine cuts through the fields to the east. The meadows are mostly weeds and grasses. A few dead trees can be seen lifting barren branches towards the sky. Lupine are scattered throughout the plains, adding ribbons of colour. Travel to the east is impossible as the north-south edges of the steep ravine cannot be traversed.
10012:
A tall pine tree grows here.
Some pine nuts lie scattered upon the ground.
