To the west low hills obstruct the view slightly, but in all other directions the view of the surrounding lands that stretch out gently beneath the great skies is unobstructed. To the south stands a lonely tree that seems to support the sky above you with its branches.
10103: A Large Tree in the Plains

A colourful butterfly is fluttering around here.
A colourful butterfly is fluttering around here.

Here, alone on the plains, stands a lonely tree. What kind of tree it is seems hard to tell, but whatever it may be, it must be a hard wood that can so defy the winds that constantly buffet these plains. It appears like a pillar of the sky, supporting the great vault of the heavens with its thick branches.
10104: A clear spring babbles as cool water trickles out of the ground.

These grasslands seem to be almost marshy, as they lie in a small dip in the plains. The ground is soft and moist with water that seems to be gushing up from some hidden underground source below. The grass grows in tufts, searching for drier place to take root. The stems that remain in the mucky soil grow yellow and soaked. To the south, the wet land continues, while in other directions the land seems to dry.
10105:
There are two woody, stemmed plants here.
A brown fox is here, looking for some rabbits to chew up.

Here the grasslands are turning marshy. Soggy footing makes the traveller search for drier spots, to avoid getting stuck in the mash of mixed plants and mud. Brown water trickles up from under ground, its trace yet unseen. To the north the moist plains continue, while in other directions the land seems to dry up.
10106: The grasslands roll out under the great skies above, forever shifting and dancing playfully with the wind. As the grass moves, it also shifts in colour, being of all thinkable nuances of green, yellow and grey. In all directions the plain stretches out, but to the north the ground seems to be marshy.
10107: The grass shifts and dances playfully as the wind rushes in from the north and west. Rustling and singing with the wind, the grass creates strange but beautiful patterns in the landscape that change constantly. In all directions the plain stretches out under the great skies overhead.
10108: The grass here seems higher and thicker than that which can be found on the plains surrounding it. It stands almost as tall as a man, the blades shifting and rustling gently in the wind. One can presume that this would be the perfect place for a predator of the plains to hide in, stalking its victim silently through the dense grass.
10109: A rabbit is here eyeing your presence warily.

The grass rolls out endlessly beneath the great vault of the sky above, evocating an image of emptiness. The fresh winds that come tumbling in from the northwest carry with them the scent of fresh herbs and grass. Into the east the ground grows moist underfoot, while to the west some bushes can be spotted in the plains.
10110: These empty plains lie like a great green carpet beneath the giant sky, that stretched from the one end of the horizon to another. Sounds of small birds and animals are mixed in with the constant whispering of the wind, creating a low drone, buzzing in the ears of the passerby. In all directions, the plains stretch out.
10111: These gently rolling grasslands have been blessed with large and healthy beeches that stand tall and proud. Their straight trunks extending high into the sky that looms above. Northwards the grasslands become covered with bushes, while to the south a fertile meadow catches the eye.
10112: An orchid of light violet petals blossoms nearby.

These grasslands are covered with all kinds of bushes, from low and thorny shrubs to larger bushes covered with tiny violet blooms. Between the bushes, small flowers and an occasional orchid seem to have found shelter from the wind. In all directions the plains stretch out under the great dome of the sky.
10113: These grasslands are covered with the tall, flowing grass of deep-green colour that is familiar for the fields around this landscape. No tree or even a small bush obstructs the view of the plains. To the south, the land becomes bushy, giving shelter for small flowers that dot the grass. In all other directions, the lush fields continue.
10114: The grassy plains roll out beneath the giant sky above in a never-ending dance with the land. To the west lies the only height visible: a small but rather high grassy mound that stands out sharply against the sky. Between the grass small patches of dirt are exposed, looking like some creature has just dug here. Animal droppings confirm the existence of some kind of wildlife. Higher grassland can be seen to the south, while these plains go on towards north and east.
10115: As the wind sweeps over the grass, it appears to be moving, rolling out in no particular direction. Still, it creates intriguing patterns as it flows out over the thick, green grass that covers this land like a smooth, soft green carpet. In all directions the plains stretch out beneath the skies.
10116: A brown fox is here, looking for some rabbits to chew up.

The flowing plains spread out like a grey and green carpet of thick and healthy grass. Small stones can be found here and there lying strewn about, almost hidden by the tall foliage. No trees or bushes disturb the view, for endless leagues the land stretches out, rising to the north and revealing another grassy field with animal tracks running through it.
10117: A brown fox is here, looking for some rabbits to chew up.

Small spots of tall, rustling grass randomly cut off by little patches of barren ground, cover these flatlands. Little trails are visible in the tall grass, evidence of a passing herd of grazing animals. The plains continue in all directions. To the south, the ground runs lazily downwards, opening the way to a thick carpet of flowing grass.
10118: Tall and dense grass covers the ground. Reaching a man's knee, it softly rustles when the wind blows among its dry stems, creating a music that is slightly different from that which is heard elsewhere on these plains. In all other directions the great plains continue, while to the north the land rises, and shows some low hills, which appear to be good spot for grazing animals to feast upon.
10119: The low hills rise from the immense plains, covered with a variety of grasses in all thinkable shades of green and yellow. Here and there, herbs, low bushes and other types of low vegetation grow, sheltered from the wind by the low hills. The grass seems to have been cropped off by herds of grazing animals. The plains stretch out in all directions.
10120: A brown fox is here, looking for some rabbits to chew up.

The top of the head of an average man would not reach the tips of the stalks here. The grass is tough and travelling through it is slightly strenuous, save for the many paths treaded by animals leading in almost every direction. The ground rises towards a hill to the south.
10121: Next to a stand of trees, smaller bushes and other plants grow in abundance. A few seedlings try to fight for the living space and the sunnier spots, but without success. To the north, something resembling a path can be recognized. Very high grass grows everywhere else, blocking large parts of the view, but a few trees can be seen reaching high towards the sky in the western direction.
10122: Yellowish in colour, this narrow track leads west-east among the grass. To the south, dense foliage obscures the view, and to the north, a few trees can be spotted. The grass has grown tall enough to hide even the least careful of small animals, and occasional animal sounds verify the existence of wild life underneath.
10123:
An apple tree with bright green leaves grows here.
On the tree's branches are four apples.

Planted here many years ago, this apple tree looks strangely out of place. Someone must have taken care of it, since the boughs have been purposely trimmed. There are no other fruit trees around, nor orchards, and if it were not for a path visible to the east and south, there would be no other sign of people.
10124: Located between a pond in the west and a path to the east, this meadow does not differ much from many other meadows that can be found in the Vale of Anduin. Green grass studded with white, red, blue and yellow flowers covers the area. A lonely tree may be spotted in the south.
10125:
A great male deer with reddish hair and twisted antlers stands here proudly.
A boar cub is playing here, and exploring the wide world.

This is an orchard with a few apple trees, a few pear trees, and some plum trees. It is not big nor in a very good condition, but it fulfills its role. The orchard is bordered by a small footpath to the north and east, and by meadows south and westward. In the southwestern direction a silvery pond can be seen.
10126: A colourful butterfly is fluttering around here.

The path leads west and east through different varieties of foliage, passing numerous colourful plants and bushes on its way. The ground descends in a slope continuing towards a gully to the north. What look like apple-trees can be seen a bit further south.
10127: The gully abruptly breaks the monotony of the fields surrounding it. Red flowers and small plants of different shades of yellow cover the northern parts, while pale green grass and blue flowers grow to the south. The gully widens to the east, but the slope is too steep to be reached from this direction.
10128: Tall Grass by the Edge of a Gully

The plain is covered with grass rising nearly one foot above ground, and not many other plants have managed to grow taller. Occasional bushes and stones break the monotony of the shifting grass. Very little foliage grows in the shade to the north, but it grows more densely in the other directions. A gully to the south makes the journey southwards somewhat hard but not impossible.
10129: The plains here are surrounded by forest in every direction but to the south. Shadows cover the plains most of the day. The grass is suffering from lack of sunlight and is dying in most places. The forest will most likely take over this area soon.
10130:
A bear is here, covered with coarse black fur.
A squirrel scampers around here, looking for nuts from the trees.
The forest floor is covered with a thin layer of humus in which some small bushes and shrubs grow. To the east and north the forest gets a lot darker, in the far west one can see grasslands.
10131:
A forest spider is here crawling around.
A forest spider is here crawling around.

The forest is all dark because of the thick canopy above blocking out all light. Some fungus grows on the ground, among the entangled roots of the trees around. To the south the forest becomes slightly less dense.
10132: The soil in the forest is made up of very dark organic material, originating from decayed branches and dead shrubs. Some small dark shrubs grow on the ground, where some mosses also grow. To the west the forest become less densely packed with trees.
10133: Some thick writhing vines whip all around you.

Due to the dense growth of trees, its canopy makes it all dark. Some small toadstools and fungus grow in the inky blackness on the rich dark soil. To the west one can barely see a plain stretching out very far into the west.
10135:
A tree-snake lies wrapped around one of the tree branches.
A tree-snake lies wrapped around one of the tree branches.

Because of the dense growth of trees, the ground is totally covered by the darkness. On the ground fallen leaves and dead shrubs are decaying, forming the nourishment for the tall trees. To the north the trail can be seen bending northwards.
10136: At a Bend in the Minor Trail

The trail bends to the north and west here. In the north the trail enters the forest west of Mirkwood. The trail is covered with dirt and gravel and is slightly overgrown by small plants and grass due to little use. In the east and south is a forest densely packed with oak and other kinds of trees.
10137: Trail through the Border of a Forest

The path in the forest is covered with a thin layer of rotten leaves and freshly fallen ones. To the north one can barely spot a path in the woods which has fallen into disuse and begun to grow over. In the south one can see the trail bend westwards, while in the east the trail continues on through the forest.
10138: Some small shrubs grow here, below the canopy of trees, where the rays of the sun shine during the day. To the south a barely visible path can be seen through the dense shrubs that grow there. To the west stretch grasslands with a dip in them to the far west.
10139: There are some flowerbeds with various kinds of colour scattered around in the grasslands. In the west the grasslands suddenly fall into a depression because of a dip in the plains. To the north and east the border of a forest can be seen and in the south is a small dark cave, that lies in a hill to the south.
10140: Near a Bend in the Trail

There are a lot of trees growing in the grass filled plains, bordering the forest to the east. To the northwest the treetops of the trees are lower than all around because of a dip in the plains there, to the south runs a trail through the grasslands and in the north is a wall of rocks standing against a hill.
10141: Bare soil makes up the most part of the trail in the west, with a few pebbles in it. To the east the trail becomes more made out of gravel with small stones. The grass growing beside the road has a healthy green colour, making a juicy treat for herbivores. To the far north a small hill can be spotted.
10142: A woodpecker is here, tapping on a tree.

There is some moss growing on the ground. Some small bushes grow below the trees, just there where they can catch a few rays of sunlight during day. The trees are somewhat apart from each other, letting the sun shine through the canopy during day. To the north is the trail that runs through the forest, heading into Mirkwood.
10143: In between the trees grow some shrubs and bushes barely able to catch a few sunrays. Through the canopy of the trees one can see the sky above. To the west a small pond can be seen in the outstretching plains. To the north the vague lining of a trail can be seen through the forest, to the south is a small meadow.
10144:
An apple tree with bright green leaves grows here.
On the tree's branches are two apples.

Amongst the small flowers like dandelion and passion flower grow small bushes in the meadow. The grass here has a healthy dark green colour. Also there grow some trees in the meadow, probably sprouted from seed from the forest around. In the west a plain can be seen spreading itself out, further around only forest can be seen almost enclosing the whole meadow.
10145: Small plants and bushes grow below the trees catching some sunrays that filter through the canopy above during daytime. To the west grows some very high grass with some trees in it, to the south and east the forest gets thicker packed with trees.
10146: A woodpecker is here, tapping on a tree.

Small bushes and shrubs grow below the canopy of the trees. The tall trees that grow here have some mosses growing on them. To the west one can see the plain with very high grasses stretching out to the horizon, to the east the forest becomes dark.
10147: During daytime some sunlight filters through the canopy of the trees, illuminating the forest floor. In between the trees grow some plants and bushes. To the northeast the forest gets dark, to the west the grasslands spread out in all directions to the horizon.
10148: At the Edge of a Forest

A grey wolf is here, snarling aggressively.
A grey wolf is here, snarling aggressively.
A wolf spider is here, among the trees.

The forest is very light in this area. In most places, where the forest gives way to the plains, the trees are spread apart from each other by at least ten feet. Travelling through here is, however, not very easy due to the large amount of vines that hang from tree to tree, and the slippery mosses and fungi underfoot.
10149: High grass and small plants grow on the plain, swaying softly in the wind. Few flowers grow here, and thick roots make it somewhat hard to traverse this plain. Close to the north, in the edge of a light forest, trees grow sparsely. Further northeast, however, the forest has grown denser and nothing is discernible, except the menacing trees. The grassy plains continue in every other direction and the foliage seems to have grown taller than usual to the west.
10150: The grass colours the plain in different shades of green as the never-ending wind shifts it softly. A few very large stones lie scattered about on the plain as if giants have been tossing them in random directions. A house rises to the southwest, and a gully leads down in the eastern direction, splitting the grasslands. The outskirts of a forest lie not too far to the north.
10151: A reddish fawn romps harmlessly among the tender grass shoots.

A small path can be discerned here, leading off to the east in a fairly straight line. It is lined by tall green grass and a few stones, and it has likely been tended by someone to prevent the grass on each side to merge.
10152: A patch of grassland has been carved out from the wilderness and turned for man's use. It is a pasture, and a good one for that. It lies just north of a little pond, so that the animals can have access to the water without having to cross large fields. The grass is lush and the plants seem very healthy. A line of trees border it on the east side. To the northwest stands a wooden building.
10153: A placid pond is here, inviting you to take a refreshing drink.

Among the grass, a placid pond reflects the sky. The water seems safe to drink, and indeed, tracks of domestic and wild animals prove that it is used for this purpose. In the reeds on the shore insects buzz busily. Green meadows lie all around, covered with grass.
10154: The terrain slopes a little, descending delicately to the pond in the north. The ground is wet, but not so much as to flood the plants. In fact, it is just perfect for water-thyme and other water-loving plants as well as animals.
10155: A small brown snake is slithering around here.

A footpath dissolves among the grass and the plants. It is small and overgrown in places, without many footprints evident. One barely discernible branch bends to the south, leading into a small clump of willows. The path is more pronounced to the east, whereas it leaves no trace to the west.
10156: Old, stocky trees clump together here, offering refreshing shade in summer, and some protection from the wind in winter. A characteristic bulge on top of the trunks attracts attention. It is evident that someone had tended these trees long ago.
10157: The grasslands continue here, with shrubs growing high, high enough to hide a large animal. West of here the plants are a little shorter. To the east the plants are even taller. Some trees can be seen in the northerly direction. The ground rises southwards, towards one of the grass-covered hills that is visible on the horizon.
10158:
A red-furred doe wanders peacefully among the grass.
A red-furred doe wanders peacefully among the grass.
A reddish fawn romps harmlessly among the tender grass shoots.

Here the land rolls out in bigger waves, creating small ridges and low hills that are covered with the same, tall grass that grows everywhere on the surrounding plains. The only signs showing that these hills might once have been taller are a few round boulders that lie strewn about. To the east and south these small hills continue, while to the north and west the land is flatter.
10159: The low grassy hills provide a welcome change in the otherwise flat landscape with their small, rolling ridges and sheltered valleys. In these valleys small bushes and trees grow, hidden away from the wind. To the south and east the land is flatter, while to the north and west these small hills continue in their rise.
10160: The small hills to the north once again spill out to become the low, rolling flatlands that cover most of this land. Sometimes the wind whispers in the grass, rustling the long blades and making them sing a strange but, in a way, beautiful song. The whole plain seems to dance to this tune. To the east and west the plains stretch out. To the south the land slides downward, giving view to another extent of grass-filled area.
10161: A great male deer with reddish hair and twisted antlers stands here proudly.

The vast grasslands stretch out beneath the giant dome of the sky as far as the eye can see. On this desolate plain, the sky seems to be the only companion, displaying a great game as the clouds seem to chase each other from horizon to horizon. The wind whispers its strange song over the plains, seemingly in search of an answer. The land rises northwards, allowing a view over these ever-moving fields.
10162: A colourful butterfly is fluttering around here.

This field lies here, like a giant green sea, with waves of shifting and rustling grass that roll out over the plains. As the tall grass swirls and moves, it creates strange and beautiful patterns, sometimes revealing the small animals that can be found beneath the surface of the grass. In all directions the plain stretches out, but to the south there is a small but rather high mound, standing out sharply against the sky.
10163: Some small rocks have been piled into a mound here.

Standing atop the small but tall mound the view is excellent, displaying in all directions the great plains that extend outwards from this place. To the south one can spot a giant, lonely oak-tree standing on the plains. And to the west, beyond even the steel-grey tongue of the Anduin, rise the Misty Mountains. To the east a small dark band on the horizon marks the Mirkwood. At the top of the mound, some withered stones stand in memory of some long forgotten hero or battle.
10164: Here, the wind seems to howl rather than whisper its strange song as it rushes in over the short grass. The flat land provides no shelter from the wind, and even the grass here seems to have suffered from the strong blasts. Not a single bush or flower has been able to plant its roots here. The plains stretch out in all directions, and to the north a small lonely mound stands out against the sky.
10165: The wind rushes in from the north and west here in great, stunning blasts, howling as it runs over the plains. The only thing able to withstand this seems to be the short, grey-green grass that covers the otherwise fertile ground. The plains stretch out in all directions from here.
10166: A brown fox is here, looking for some rabbits to chew up.

The plains roll gently out under the great vault of the sky that seems to stand on the pillars of the horizon. The only thing reaching out for this enormous roof above is a large oak-tree that completely dominates the plains to the west. To the south the land appears more fertile and lush, while to the east it is more forested.
10167: A giant tree looms here, towering above the surrounding plains. It seems to be older than the plains themselves, an ancient oak that has by sheer size survived the winds and hardships of the plains. The trunk is grizzled and the bark hardened by many centuries of exposure to the forces of nature, but the top branches seem young and fresh. At times, the shadow of the tree stretches out many hundred yards on the plains, that extend in all directions from here. A big and mossy rock sits here, flat to the ground.
10168: A black wolf pads restlessly, looking for its next prey.

In the grass of these fields grow many varieties of flowers, low and high, adding small touches of colour that stand in sharp contrast with the otherwise grey, yellow and green of the plains. Overhead, the sky forms a giant vault, stretching from the eastern horizon to the peaks of the Misty Mountains in the west. In all directions the plains stretch out, but to the south you can spot a big tree standing alone.
10169: The grassy fields that roll around and about, are filled with many kinds of grasses and flowers, making the ground look spotted. When the wind rustles the grass, these spots swirl in a strange but fascinating pattern. In all directions the plains stretch out under the great skies above. The ground enters a small rise to the north, showing more wind-blown grasslands.
10170: The grassy plains here turn from being very flat and low to the north, into a more rolling and twisting land to the east and south. To the east, a small but high mound can be spotted, standing out on the otherwise low, rolling plains. The sky above is a great dome of blue, white and grey, where the clouds play a constant game chasing each other back and forth. To the south the land reaches a small ridge, dotted with colourful flowers.
10171: A small grasshopper clings to a blade of grass, ready to spring.

The land here is absolutely flat. Standing on a small stool, one could probably see very far, as no ridges or hills obstruct the view. The grass here is of medium height, neither stretching towards the skies too much, nor hugging the ground too close, as if it were in some way conscious of its neighbour grass, not wanting to offend it by standing out in any way. The grasslands stretch out in every direction.
10172: Here the low, flat ridges that dominate the grasslands to the north seem to have been ironed out by nature in some strange way, and the land becomes more flat. Strangely, even the grass seems to have understood this, as no blade seems to reach higher than its neighbour. To the south the grasslands flatten even more.
10173: From the hill to the north the grasslands spill out again over the plains and once more resume the shape of the giant, green sea of rustling grass that covers these lands. The great sky above seems to be larger here than anywhere you have ever been, completely dominating all life here. To the east, south and west the grasslands roll on towards a distant horizon.
10174: Some delicious wild strawberries grow on the ground.

The carpet of grass that covers these lands makes a small bump here to create a small grassy hill that, despite being quite low, rises above the surrounding area. From up here the view is magnificent: the grasslands stretch out in all directions, and beyond them to the east, a small dark band on the horizon can be spotted - Mirkwood. To the far, far west a giant grey shape marks the Misty Mountains.
10175: A rabbit is here eyeing your presence warily.

The soft, rolling grasslands lie like a big, green blanket under the great dome of the sky above, moving and twisting constantly with the wind. As the grass moves, it displays itself in a great variety of colours - all thinkable nuances of green, yellow and grey are present, changing all the time. In all directions this sea of grass extends outwards to the horizon.
10176: The grass here seems higher than that covering the land to the west, the grass reaches even taller east of here. A deer could be seen in the grass, but smaller animals would remain completely hidden unless they were stumbled upon or thoroughly searched for. The grass tips are narrow, but quite tough. Very few flowers manage to get sunlight in this tall grass.
10177: The healthy grass, as well as the occasional patches of red flowers, sway gently in the wind, emitting a sweet fragrance. The grasslands continue, seemingly unchanged in all directions but to the east, where a cluster of trees stand.
10178: A bear is here, covered with coarse black fur.

Here the plains seem particularly lively. The grass reflects a deep green colour, unlike the dusty green that is usual on the steppes. The foliage has grown tall enough to reach the knees of a man, and small animals are likely to use it is as shelter. The plains continue in all directions. A patch of flowers can be seen to the west giving the grassland a slightly different nuance.
10179: A brown fox is here, looking for some rabbits to chew up.

The ground appears to slope a little here, and is soaked with water. Different kinds of plants thrive here, and all kinds of mud-loving animals. Even though the place looks very much like a mire, it is firm enough to support the weight of any animal that may pass by.
10180: The ground is soaked with water, forming small, shallow puddles here and there. The grass grows unhindered, except for the animals grazing on its sweetness. Meadows spread south, west and north. A whiff of moisture from the east betrays the presence of a small pond there.
10181: This meadow is covered with low, green grass. Many small paths cross it in all directions, with evident traces of wild life. The northern side is blocked by the wall the of a building, but all other directions are open and covered with more grass.
10182: Tall Grass North of a House

A red-furred doe wanders peacefully among the grass.
A reddish fawn romps harmlessly among the tender grass shoots.
A red-furred doe wanders peacefully among the grass.

The grass rises many inches above the ground and is of a yellow colour as well as many shades of green. Many small stones lie gathered in a pile in the middle of the plain and flowers have been placed on and around it. Ivy grows high along the house wall to the south, almost hiding it. The ground rises slightly to the west.
10183: High grass makes the journey through the plains slightly strenuous to accomplish. The grass has grown really tall, as far as the eye can see. A few flowers have managed to grow higher than the grass - those who have, stand proudly defying the wind while the grass shifts softly. A cluster of trees stands to the north-east and a long hedge has been planted to the west. The faint outline of a roof with a chimney can be glimpsed beyond the high grass, straight to the south.
10184: The grass grows high in this area, nearly to the armpits of an average man. To the east, the trees being to be take the plains over. Some holly bushes and wild flowers grow in patches where the grass isn't quite so high, taking away some of the monotony of the otherwise drab plains.
10185: Medium High Grass near a Forest

There are more trees growing in the grass nearer to the light forest in the east. Also some big shrubs grow in between the medium high grass. To the north the grass gets longer, while it diminishes in length in the south. In the east is a light forest and further east the forest becomes dark.
10186: The grassland beside the forest in the east is full of high grass with some lonely trees growing in it. A few plants are also growing here, which have succeeded to grow here. To the south the grass becomes shorter.
10187: The grass growing here is very long, making it difficult for other kinds of vegetation to grow here. A handful of trees have succeeded to sprout here, making a change in scenery besides grass. To the east one can see the rim of a light forest.
10188: A colourful butterfly is fluttering around here.

The grass that grows here seems to form a sea of grass. In between the grass grows some trees. Small paths are going in every direction here made by animals, which have trampled the grass when passing through here, foraging for food and water. To the north and east the grass becomes shorter, whereas it becomes longer in the west and south.
10189: At a Small Pond in the Grasslands

A blooming water-lily floats on the surface of the water.
A placid pond is here, inviting you to take a refreshing drink.
A colourful butterfly is fluttering around here.

The plain is mostly covered with grass, with some flowers and trees in it. In the middle of the plain is a small pond with reeds growing at its bank. To the east is the rim of a forest, to the north one can spot a small trail in the plain.
10190: The grass becomes taller here, making travel through it somewhat difficult. Some small trees are growing in between the grass with their branches waving softly in the wind. To the north and west is a trail, in the east the border of a forest can be seen.
10191: The trail here is mostly bare soil with only a few pebbles embedded into it. In the west the trail is more covered with pebbles and gravel. Beside the trail grows mostly grass and an occasional tree, casting their shadow during day over the plains.
10192: There are moss covered rocks scattered all around these grasslands. To the north, the plains slope into a small depression and to the south, a minor trail runs both east and west. A large forest is in the east, but the plains continue to stretch to the horizon in the west. To the northwest is a small hill.
10193: The plains here slope downward into a depression and are covered by numerous shrubs and trees. All around is elevated plains, in the east one can barely see the canopy of a forest. To the southeast is a small hill.
10194: There are some solitary trees growing on the plains, also some flowers grow here and there. To the east a dip in the plains can be seen, in the west is a small forest. A small trail runs through the vast plains in the south leading into the west and east.
10195: The grass that is growing here is all over an inch high, some small weeds and mosses grow in the grass. To the northwest a small forest can be seen which is a change in scenery in the ongoing plains. To the south a small trail runs through the grasslands, entering a forest at the east side of the trail. In the northeast the plains fall into a local depression of the plains.
10196: Through the grasslands runs a minor trail bending in the south to the west and continuing on towards the east. The trail is covered by some gravel. The grassland surrounding the trail is full of trees and small bushes.
10197: Small pebbles and gravel make up the most part of the trail, the remainder of it is bare rock. Here and there the trail is somewhat heightened by the roots of the trees growing beside the trail. Beside the trail the grasslands stretch out to the east and south, and to the north one can see the trail bending east.
10198: The grass is about twenty inches tall making moving through it pretty difficult. There are some solitary trees growing in the sea of grass. To the north is a minor trail bending eastwards in the far north.
10199: The grass here is extremely high, with a few trees in between it, surrounded by a seemingly endless sea of grass. Here and there are paths going criss- cross through the grass made by animals searching for food. To the north the grass becomes shorter, further north one can see a small trail.
10200: The trees growing in the high grass are sticking out above the grass only for three-quarter of their length. There are only a few plants which grow in between the grass. All around one can only see high grass save a few plants and trees.
10201: The trees that grow here solemnly in between the high grass is the only other sort of vegetation that grows here. To the south the height of the grass diminishes to a medium length.
10202: The grass here is as high as a rabbit standing upright. In the grass grow a few trees, casting their shadow over the grass during daytime. To the north one can see the grass become longer with only a few trees in it and in the east one can barely see the border of a forest.
10203: The grasslands on this even ground here have grown strong here, the grass being of a lustrous green colour. A few dandelions and other yellow flowers grow in small groups a bit to the west, looking very healthy as they have grown taller than the grass. Trees are seen towering towards the sky to the east. The grasslands continue in all directions and a long hedge stands to the south and south-west.
10204:
A great male deer with reddish hair and twisted antlers stands here proudly.
A soft-skinned female deer wanders peacefully among the grass.
A reddish fawn romps harmlessly among the tender grass shoots.
A reddish fawn romps harmlessly among the tender grass shoots.

The shrubs with red and white blossoms are covered with small berries and rise about three feet above the ground. The bushes are planted in a long row, leading off to the west and forming a hedge. Yellow grass surrounding the shrubs has grown taller than on the other parts of the plain, which likely means that someone has watered the hedge. The ground rises gently to the south, forming a slope, and the grasslands continue to the north and east. A light forest can be seen in a few miles away to the northeast.
10205: The slope leads downwards to the north. The many colours of different grasses and flowers shift in the blowing wind. The whining of the wind brings an occasional sound of animal activity as it passes through the plains. A long green hedge can be spotted in the western direction leading north. A wooden cabin has been built to the south-east. A tidily-grown row of bushes blocks the way to the south.
10206: Flat and grassy, this stretch of the ground shows signs of use. Here and there a small circle has been grazed out in the grass. In other places, some low ditches and barriers have been built out of pressed earth. A house stands to the northeast and a row of bushes has been planted to block the way north.
10207: This vegetation could be the dream for any animal that eats grass - tall, green, and juicy. A few flowers grow in a cluster but many more seem to have been eaten and only the stem remains. Apparently there is a water source not very far to the east since the soil looks even more wet in that direction. Tracks of all kinds confirm the presence of wild life.
10208: The ground seems a little wet, and the flowers use this moisture to the outmost. The grass is very thick, green and juicy. Herbivores would likely satisfy their hunger on these fields and indeed tracks criss-crossing the fields show sign of wild life.
10209: A boar cub is playing here, and exploring the wide world.

Here the plains are covered with flowers - bluebonnets and poppies. The climate allows them to bloom during most of the year, creating a colourful carpet on the face of the steppe. Plants here are thicker and greener than their cousins to the south and west, probably because they have more moisture and nutrition. The fields to the north and east seem to sport vegetation just as healthy. A few stones can be seen, around which different plants have taken root.
10210: A red-furred doe wanders peacefully among the grass.

The character of the grass cover differs from the surrounding fields - the plants are thicker, greener, and proudly displaying clusters of blue flowers, bluebonnets. These plants grow in such thick clumps that no ordinary grass can compete for space in-between them.
10211: A small brown snake is slithering around here.

The flat, even, grass-covered steppe leads on and on. A few stones lie scattered about randomly as if giants had thrown them. To the east a slight change in the colour of the plains suggests different kinds of plants - a welcoming change in the landscape. A barely visible, and long since dried-up waterbed leads towards that direction. The field to the north shimmers in a bluish colour and is seemingly covered with flowers.
10212: The plains roll out like a great sea of grass under the shifting skies above. Grasses, herbs and small flowers grow here, rustling and moving in the wind. In all directions, as far as the eye can see, the plains stretch out, seemingly endless.
10213: These grassy plains seem to stretch out forever and appear almost lifeless as they roll out under the skies. The only detectable movement is the grass that dances and shifts with the wind, but upon closer inspection small animals seem to be scurrying in the grass underfoot. The plains stretch out in every direction.
10214: These grasslands seem to stretch out forever, the horizon miles away being the only thing that meets the eye. The tall blades of grass that grow in this fertile plain, shift and dance in the wind. Flowing like an endless sea, these waves of grass roll out in all directions from here.
10215: A small grasshopper clings to a blade of grass, ready to spring.

These flat, grassy plains seem engaged with the wind in a never-ending dance. As the wind grabs hold of the long blades, they swirl and bend, creating long waves of grass that roll out over the sea of grass. The plains stretch out in all directions, with a slope descending west to the thick grassy field.
10216: A colourful butterfly is fluttering around here.

The flat, grassy plains lie like a calm, green water beneath the enormous dome of the sky above. The wind ripples these waters, creating small waves of grass that seem to follow a hidden and mysterious pattern. In most directions, these waters stretch out, with the small island of a lonely tree standing in defiance of the whispering wind. To the west, the ground begins to lower, giving space to yet another grassy field.
10217: A colourful butterfly is fluttering around here.

On these vast, slightly shifting grasslands no shadow falls. The flat lands seem completely unbroken by hills, heights or trees. The grass that at first seems to be a monotonous carpet appears, on closer inspection, to sport a variety of different plants and herbs. It may all look like one big sea, but it consists of small units of life. A small slope descends to the west while in other directions the plains stretch further out.
10218: No height, tree or valley seems to interrupt the vast, flowing grasslands that cover these plains. The grasses and herbs that grow here seem to forever stretch out playfully towards the skies, only to be grabbed by the wind and sent into a merry dance. The grasslands stretch out as far as the eye can see, with a ridge rising in the east and sloping on to the north.
10219: Under the great vault of the sky, these endless plains roll out in all directions, a playing ground where nature's forces put their might to play. The only thing surviving this game seems to be the tough grass that grows everywhere. Indeed, it seems to play some strange part in the game, dancing and creating patterns when moved by the wind.
10220: The tall trees that stand here cast long shadows over the flatlands, not making the plains look less desolate, but rather strengthening the impression of emptiness. The tall, straight trunks of the beech-trees make them look like pillars, stretching out for, and supporting, the high vault of the sky above. To the east stands a great oak-tree in solitude, while to the south the trees stand more closely together.
10221: The plains roll out endlessly under the great skies above you. With the great variety of grass and low herbs, they seem to somehow reflect what is above. As the wind reaches down and rustles the grass, the lands seem to wave in a strange dance. The ground descends roughly to the west, reaching out to a riverbank.
10222: The tall grass covering these lands seems to shift beneath the skies in a never ending dance with the wind. The colour of the grass is never constant as it shifts with weather and rain, being a dark, dull grey when the weather is bad, and a light, fresh green when blue skies are above. The grasslands stretch out in all directions.
10223: A shifting mass of grey, green and yellow grass lies all around, matching the sky that lies above. Vibrant and full with little rushing creatures in the summertime, dry and almost asleep in the colder months. Broken grass stems here and there indicate the presence of a bigger beast passing through this area, perhaps looking for smaller animals to chew on. The grasslands continue in all directions.
10224: A large, loyal falcon is circling above.

Rolling out under the skies, these vast grasslands seem to be unending. They are home to a variety of different grasses, high and low, green and grey, young and withered. Under the vault of the sky, the grasslands seem to match the heavens as they stretch out. To the east the ground enters a small rise, offering a bit higher view over the surrounding land.
10225: These flat grasslands seem vast and unending as they roll out under the skies. They sport a variety of different grasses, in all thinkable shades of green and grey. Some old, withered grasses add to the picture with their yellow, dried leaves and stems. To the east the land rises towards more open fields. In the other directions the plains stretch on, flowing like an endless sea.
10226: A brown fox is here, looking for some rabbits to chew up.

Thriving thick and healthy, the grass here grows high towards the sky. Thick stems and healthy leaves in all shades of green rustle in the passing breezes. Though quiet, the partly broken and stumped stems confirm the hiding wildlife in this area. These grasslands continue in every direction while rising in the east and revealing another endlessly waving plain.
10227: The tall, swaying grasses that stand here embrace all who enter this deep sea of green. Looking around is not possible, except over the tallest grass, which would reach to the shoulder of a grown man. To hide in these grasses would be easy - just lying down would make one all but invisible. A beast might use such an opportunity to stalk a traveller of the plains. To the north the ground rises, bringing more grasslands into the view.
10228: The grasslands roll out endlessly, low rolling lands covered only with grass that moves and shifts with the wind. As the grass moves, it shifts in colour, from a solid green to a pale yellow or dull grey. The skies above seem to reflect this as clouds come and go in an endless dance. The grasslands lower to the south into the tall grass.
10229: The low, rolling land is covered with high grass that reaches towards the sky, only to be grabbed by the wind and sent into a strange dance, creating mysterious patterns that change constantly. In the stillness, the only thing heard is the wind and the grass rustling. The plains stretch out in all directions.
10230: This small hollow in the ground must have retained some water in the past, allowing bigger plants to thrive. However, the bushes have dried out since then, and all that is left are dry roots and sticks entangled with each other. Travel becomes slightly difficult as the sharp ends of twigs catch both the clothes and skin.
10231: A great male deer with reddish hair and twisted antlers stands here proudly.

A lively patch of grass grows here, between the ruins of an old fire to the north, stony grounds to the west and dry bushes to the south. However, underneath the fresh, green grass covering the ground, black residues of old fire can be recognized. The even plains to the east seem to go on forever.
10232:
A small brown snake is slithering around here.
A roe deer is standing here, watching the terrain while chewing the vegetation.
A ferocious warg is here, snarling angrily.

The terrain swells a little, forming a very convenient place for a house. Indeed there are some remains of an unspecified structure here, though almost burned to the ground. A few charred beams stick up from the ground, wrapped with ivy-like plants. Seedlings of trees growing among the ruins show that the fire must have taken place many years ago.
10233: The view to the south reveals decaying remains of a homestead. When examining the ground, it appears to be partly burned and a few scattered trunks still lie rotten on the ground as in memory of an old fire. Gnarled and black trees cover the view to the west. Short grass covers the nutritious soil and leads on to the north. The foliage grows higher to the northeast and east, continuing like that all the way to the horizon.
10234: A red-furred doe wanders peacefully among the grass.

The plains are rolling on and on. The grass tall, but rather small, and yet nevertheless quite healthy and thick. The grass continues in all directions, with greener and higher plants to the east, smaller and drier to the west.
10235: An endless grassland extends in all directions, studded with clumps of taller plants and teeming with life. As the animals are shy and wary, they cannot always be seen, but the tracks and droppings testify that some animals have passed here recently. A house, breaking the monotony of the plains, is noticeable to the northeast.
10236: A roe deer is standing here, watching the terrain while chewing the vegetation.

Two varieties of green grass cover the plain, the darker kind dominating the northern parts. The wind shifts the grass softly, bringing a sweet fragrance with it. Small animals make occasional sounds on their way through the grass, but they remain unseen. The plains continue to the south and west, and a long hedge is seen to the north. A row of plants, which flowers show a bluish colour has been planted in the eastern direction. A house can be discerned behind it.
10237:
A bear is here, covered with coarse black fur.
A green frog is here, hopping around.

Thorny shrubs have grown nearly three feet above the ground, forming a hedge. Pink and white blossoms cover most of the hawthorns and red berries can be seen on some. The undergrowth is richer near the thorns than in the rest of the plain, indicating that someone has watered the bushes. The ground rises slightly to the east and faint shape of a building can be seen to the southeast.
10238: The thorny shrubs rise three feet above the ground and have been planted to form a long hedge. Some of the shrubs carry many small berries and they all carry blossoms, mostly white but an occasional red blossom can be seen. The undergrowth has grown rich near the hawthorns, which indicates that someone has watered them. The shrubs grow to the west, east and south. Grasslands extend to the north behind the hedge.
10239: Green and yellow grass covers the even ground, softly shifting in the occasional wind. Flowers with golden stems growing here and there fill the air with a soft, sweet scent. Every now and then there is a faint sound of some small animal scurrying between the grasses. The plains continue in all directions but to the south, where the planted thorns seem to form a hedge.
10240: Shrubs of different size and species grow amongst the medium long grass. One might have some difficulty moving through the tall grass growing in this area. To the north the length of the grass gets longer, but becomes slightly shorter to the south.
10241: Only a few trees manage to grow here in the long grass, standing far apart from each other. To the west and south one notices that the height of the grass diminishes and to the north and east, the grass stretches out in a continuous sea of green.
10242:
A red-furred doe wanders peacefully among the grass.
A reddish fawn romps harmlessly among the tender grass shoots.

The high grass makes it somewhat difficult to travel through. Small paths are in the high grass, probably by large animals who have trampled the grass, in search of water and food. To the west the grass gets shorter whereas all around here the grass is somewhat the same length.
10243: The grass grows very high here and all a hunter could see of a deer in the distant grass would be their antlers. Lone trees grow here and there, probably sprouted before the grass was so long. To the north and west one can see the height of the grass diminish, to the far north one can see the outlining of a trail.
10244: A colourful butterfly is fluttering around here.

The grass here is very high making movement through it somewhat difficult. The grass gives good protection as a hiding place for small animals. Some trees grow here and there, casting their shadow over the plain at day. To the south the grass becomes taller and to the north is a small trail.
10245: A magpie is flying around looking for some food.

The trail winds through the plains stretching to the east and west, covered by small pebbles and tiny stones. Beside the trail outstretching grasslands are visible, with a few trees and some wild corn growing in them. To the east the trail can be seen turning to the north.
10246: Near a Bend in the Minor Trail
A bee flies around here, collecting nectar from the flowers.

The grass growing here is competing with the bushes and shrubs for the best spots to sprout. The grass appears to win the competition, probably due to a low supply of nutrients. To the south and east is the minor trail that runs through the land between the Anduin and Mirkwood.
10247: The occasional tree can be found growing amongst the grass which covers the ground here, including the elevations and depressions in the grasslands. To the north the rim of a small forest can be seen, and to the south the outline of a small trail can be seen.
10248: The forest floor is covered with a thin layer of humus. Various sizes of ferns are growing where the sun shines on the forest floor. The oak trees are mostly covered by toadstools and looking up, a few nests are visible within the branches of the trees.
10249: The garden snake slithers harmlessly here.

The grass here is some two inches high, with a few flowers growing amongst it. On the ground are some small mounds made out of earth, supposedly made by moles. Scattered around are some cedar and oak trees. The plains look like they stretch out infinitely, except in the east where the rim of a small forest breaks the line of the horizon.
10250: Flowers grow here in the vast grasslands, a welcome change to the grass which covers the surrounding lands. A few trees are scattered around, standing solemnly in the vast plain. The trees are beginning to grow more closely to each other in the direction of the small forest in the northeast. To the far south is a small trail, which makes travel easier through these vast plains.
10251: A cluster of white star-shaped forget-me-nots flourish here in reminiscence.

The meadow is fully covered by dark green grass, with different kinds of flowers in it. A few small patches of the meadow are covered with bushes and shrubs, providing a good refuge for small animals. To the south one can see a tiny trail running through the grasslands.
10252: The trail is covered by a thin layer of gravel. A few branches of trees, that grow beside the trail, are hanging over the trail. The trail continues west for some distance and then begins to head south, while it continues in the east.
10253:
The garden snake slithers harmlessly here.
A green frog is here, hopping around.

Only a few trees grow here, with some big shrubs and bushes growing in small patches. To the west and north is a minor trail and in the northwest a bend can be seen in it. In the southeast the grass grows higher.
10254: In the grass grow a variety of plants, all barely sticking their heads over the grass. To the east the grass becomes even higher, whereas it becomes shorter in the west. In the northwest one can see a bend in a small trail.
10255: The grass that grows here is taller then in the west, whereas it is shorter then the grass that grows in the east. In between the grass grows some dandelions and some buttercups. In the west the grass is much shorter and one can see bushes growing in it. In the east the grass begins to grow taller and very thick.
10256: A green frog is here, hopping around.

Shrubs and bushes of different sizes grow on the dark brownish soil in between the tall grass. To the west one can barely see the outline of a structure of some kind in the short grass. In the east the grass becomes higher.
10257: Only a few flowers manage to grow tall enough to stretch their heads above the high grass that grows here. To the northeast the grass grows higher, whereas the grass grows shorter in the west and south.
10258: The plain is covered with several sorts of grass. The darker kind grows slightly higher and dominates the northern as well as the eastern parts of the plain. Occasional dandelions are seen wherever the grass has failed to reach more than a few inches in height. The plain continues in all directions.
10259: Thorny shrubs with white and red blossoms and small red berries seem to have been planted here to form a hedge. The hawthorns rise nearly three feet above the ground and continue in a fairly straight line to the east. Grass-covered plains continue in the other directions and a slope can be seen to the southwest.
10260: The dark grass stands almost two feet high and covers most of the ground, preventing the undergrowth to thrive. A few reddish flowers grow beside a large stone, around which the soil is dark and no grass grows. Thorns can be seen to the north and northeast, likely planted to form a hedge. The ground rises slightly to the west leading up to a slope.
10261: The grass is lustrously green and flowers of different colours have taken root amongst the hardy grass of this region. The ground rises quickly to the west, leading up to the top of a slope, behind which the colourful crowns of many trees can be seen. The shape of something that could possibly be a house, can be spotted far to the east.
10262: In the midst of these flat grasslands a patch of flowers springs to life. The stems are thick and green. The flowers, when they can be seen, are small, white and yellow. Grassland stretch from the southeast to the north. The ground rises to the northwest.
10263: A bear is here, covered with coarse black fur.

The plants on this stretch of the steppe are in dire need for nutrition: they look small, dry and withered. The ground is yellowish, and the soil seems to contain lots of sand. To the south stands a group of small, twisted trees. Flowers of different colours cover the ground to the north.
10264: A large owl with small sharp horns looks cautiously around it.

The trees here have undergone some unnatural change: they are low, gnarled and black. Their trunks are scarred, and their lower branches seem to have been clipped. This effect is most evident to the south. The northern parts of this coppice appear much healthier. Short grass grows to the north, along with green crowns of high trees.
10265: A cute young hawk is standing here.

Sparsely distributed trees form a small coppice here. The trees have a strange quality about them: the trunks are black, and all their lower branches are gone. Black coals lay on the ground, covered however by new foliage.
10266: The grass only grows sporadically here, forming small clumps among pebbles and rocks of different sizes. Since a steep rock wall towers to the west, it is not difficult to guess the origin of all these stones. On the north, there are some dark trees, and grasslands extend to the south and east.
10267: A large mother hawk is here looking for a prey to feed her young.

An immaculate cover of grass extends to the horizon except in the west, where a darker line may signify a change in the foliage. A careful observer might be able to spot some small animals around, hurrying in their search for food and shelter.
10268:
A rabbit is here eyeing your presence warily.
A cute rabbit is here.

On these vast grasslands the wind seems to be the only thing moving. But it also moves the very grass itself, making it dance a strange and unfathomable dance. Looking closer, one can notice small animals living in the tall grass that covers these lands. Life is hidden, but it is there. The plains stretch out in all directions.
10269: A sharp-eyed hawk is here stalking some prey.

The grass ripples when caressed by the wind, making strange patterns appear everywhere. It resembles a sea, and similarly the life that exists, is seen deep down and below the surface. Small animals scurry to and from their homes, feeding their siblings and securing their little lives. The plains continue in all directions, with an exception of a lowering slope to the south.
10270: Here the grass stands very tall, reaching a man's chest. It seems to be of another variety than the grass which covers most of these plains: the stems are thicker, the blades longer and broader. Hiding in these grasses would be easy since just lying down would make one all but invisible. The ground rises to the north, bringing more grasslands into the sight.
10271: The tall grass continues, coming in from the north. The blades are long and thick, reaching broadly out of the rich soil. As the wind comes in from the grey river of Anduin, the grass springs and rustles, bending downwards in the mighty breeze. Pawsteps of some bigger animal show that a beast of prey is stalking these lands for its next meal. The grasslands continue in every direction, rolling out like a giant colourful carpet.
10272: Some delicious wild strawberries grow on the ground.

The plains stretch out here under the open sky as far as the eye can see, the flat lands covered with high grass that shifts in the wind. Small animals scurry between the grasses on the ground, almost invisible in the underbrush. As the wind comes in from the north and west, the grasses shift and dance.
10273: The grasses that cover this open plain are high and strong, their slim, beautiful blades rustling and dancing in the wind. Below the grasses small animals live, running as you approach. The grassy plains roll out in all directions from here, stretching as far as the eye can see.
10274: A rabbit is here eyeing your presence warily.

The plains stretch out endlessly, covered with grass that seems to dance with the ever-present wind, creating strange and beautiful patterns. In this changing pattern small animals live, their lives dominated by the search for whatever food may be found here.
10275:
A colourful butterfly is fluttering around here.
A red-furred doe wanders peacefully among the grass.
A red-furred doe wanders peacefully among the grass.
A reddish fawn romps harmlessly among the tender grass shoots.

Here the grasslands rise faintly from west to east, spilling out into the great, rolling plains that lie between the Great River and Mirkwood. The rise is covered with low grass, the only vegetation that can survive here on the windswept rise. To the west flows the mighty Anduin.
10276: The riverbank rises sharply to the east, into the great plains that lie beyond. The rise is constantly whipped by the winds that come in from the north and west, over the grey waters of the Anduin, carrying cold moisture with them. The only thing that grows here is low grass, and even that seems to be on the brink of survival. To the south a group of small trees can be spotted, swinging their branches in the breeze.
10277: At the Bank of the River Anduin

A sharp-eyed hawk is here stalking some prey.
A rabbit is here eyeing your presence warily.
A cute rabbit is here.

The gentle slope of the eastern bank of the river is covered in lush grass and tall stands of cattails swaying in the breeze. The river begins to broaden out here in small, stagnant pools teeming with life. The marshy ground extends further to the south, where a large stand of grey willow trees overshadows the riverbank. Eastwards, the meadows sprawl out over gently rolling hilltops and broad valleys.
10278: A sharp-eyed hawk is here stalking some prey.

Here the land rises more steeply to the east, the slopes covered only with small clusters of grass. The soil is dry and loose here, a result of many years of slow erosion. The footing is unsafe, making it hard to climb the rise. To the north the land ascends less steeply, while to the east the grasslands stretch out beyond the rise.
10279:
A rabbit is here eyeing your presence warily.
A brown fox is here, looking for some rabbits to chew up.
A rabid rabbit is here, frothing at the mouth.
A rabid rabbit is here, frothing at the mouth.

This small, grassy meadow lies sheltered by low rises that ring this shallow dell, untouched by the relentless winds. As a result, the land is covered with small trees, lush rose bushes and herbs of all kinds. To the east the grasslands continue, while to the west lies the riverbed of the mighty Anduin.
10280:
A great black and silver wolf is standing here, at the head of the pack.
A ferocious warg is here, snarling angrily.

The grasslands begin here beyond the eastern bank of the river Anduin, stretching on to the east. The slopes are covered by tall grasses that shift as the wind comes in from the north and west, carrying with it a faint scent of water. To the west, a stony slope leads to the top of a small rise by the Anduin.
10281: A great male deer with reddish hair and twisted antlers stands here proudly.

Here the land rises from west to east, an extension of the riverbank of the Anduin. The rise is covered by a variety of grasses that shift in the wind, depicting at every time a new, unique pattern. Looking towards north, the grasslands stretch out and another open plain enters the view to the east.
10282: A ferocious warg is here, snarling angrily.

The wind whistles as it passes over these low, grassy lands, playing upon the grass as if it were an instrument. The sound created may not be called music, yet it is fitting for these lands in a way. Under the great vault of the sky the plains stretch out in all directions.
10283: The plains roll out under the great skies, covered with grass that dances in the wind, seeming almost a reflection of the skies. The colour of the grass shifts with that of the sky, being a beautiful green when the sky is blue, and turning a dull grey when the skies do. The plain stretches away from here in all directions.
10284: These low, rolling plains are covered with short grass that seems to shimmer as the wind grabs the blades, joining in a never ending dance. Here and there, ancient rocks lie about, smoothed over time by the caress of the wind. In all directions the plains stretch out, and in the distant west you can spot the great Anduin.
10285: A colourful butterfly is fluttering around here.

Silver blades of a foreign variety of grass grow tall on this rolling field. Light striking the blades causes the whole field to somewhat shimmer and dance in an almost magical fashion. The plains continue in all directions. Further to the west, a small grassy hillock can be spotted, rising in the plains.
10286: The ground evens out here; not even the slightest swelling can be seen. The grass changes its colour in different spots: brownish here, reddish there and yellowish at yet another part of the flat plain. A dark shape breaks the straight line of the northern horizon.
10287: A small animal, all covered in spines, snuffles amongst the undergrowth.

A massive rock rises from the surface of the surrounding grassland. It stands in solitude among the seemingly endless plains. Small cracks have been carved into the rock, looking somewhat like a natural stair. The grassy plains continue rather unchanged in all directions. A few stones can be seen scattered to the east.
10288: Open plains covered with grass - such is the landscape here. As far as one can see, the same kind of environment stretches all the way from southwest to north. Among the grass to the south, a huge lonely rock can be spotted. Dark, scattered trees grow to the east.
10289: A brown fox is here, looking for some rabbits to chew up.

The grass is low and weak, very distinct from the lush plains to the southwest. The northern parts are visibly sloping down, and are even more scattered, covered just with small clumps of grasses amidst pebbles and gravel. Low, dark line of trees meets the eye looking to the east.
10290: A colourful butterfly is fluttering around here.

The ground forms a slight depression here. It is filled with sand, gravel and pebbles. It is not quite a desert, plants are still growing here. It is just that the grass is sparse, low and delicate with long stretches of sandy ground in between.
10291:
A small brown snake is slithering around here.
A rabbit is here eyeing your presence warily.
A beautiful and docile horse is standing here.

The rocks and pebbles covering the ground hinder the growth of the grass. The area is sparsely covered with low, spiny bushes that are almost devoid of leaves and flowers. Their twigs are mostly dried and sharp, making it easy to prick one's skin here. To the south is a patch of smaller gravel and sand. To the north looms a low, dark ridge across the plains.
10292: A large elk is standing here, chewing grass and leaves.

You find yourself on the top of a slope where the grass bends slavishly with the breeze. It seems as if some animals have been here repeatedly, leaving a small trail of beaten grass leading off to the south. Tall oaks, proudly stretching up towards the sky, can be seen to the west.
