10540: A mountain mule is standing here, ridden by you.

This road must once have been well travelled, the ground is packed hard. Yet the weeds pushing their way through the soil signals the end of this road, dooming it to vanish in history. The road follows the contours of the land, running more or less straight east and west.
10541: The surface of the road is rather muddy here, although the reason for this is not readily apparent. However, the hedgerow to the south has taken on a different character, being comprised here mainly of tall, bright green ferns.
10542: You follow a small road through these dismal plains. The road bends west and south here, and you can barely discern a faint path diverging from the road, leading north to a small hill in the middle of a large plain.
10543: This is the beginning of the Road to Tharbad, a town known in rumours as the city of thieves and murderers. Even with its dark reputation, the road shows signs of regular use, with the indentions from merchant caravans and the tracks of shod horses. Just to the south you see a river, which travels beside the road for some distance, and to the northwest, stands a small hill, which is the highest point in this area.
10544: The road travels on straight to the east and the west. To the north, a great expanse of barren plains seems to stretch endlessly before you, and the road upon which you stand is scarred by many tracks, which speak of frequent, and recent, heavy use, by both vehicles and mounted travellers.
10545: You are travelling along a well-tended road, bordered to the south by some light woods, and from somewhere nearby, the sound of birdsong can be heard. The road stretches, seemingly without end, to both the east and west.
10546: The road turns sharply to the south here, before continuing its journey to the east, toward the city of Tharbad. A small dirt trail can be seen to the north, parting ways with the road, to descend a steep and stony embankment.
10939: Rocks and boulders are scattered all around, amongst the thin tufts of grass, and clumps of weeds. Little other vegetation seems able to grow here, though a few stunted bushes seem to cling stubbornly to life. To the north and south, these desolate plains stretch endlessly onward.
10940: A large boulder stands here, amid these desolate plains. Whichever way you turn, the plains stretch endlessly onward, dominating the landscape for many miles. The grass grows in thin, sickly tufts here, and only a few stunted bushes manage to survive in this barren region.
10941: These plains are the essence of desolation. The only vegetation surviving here is the occasional weed, except for a large group of bushes, which seem quite out of place here. Indeed, alone in all this are, this clump of bushes seems to be fairly healthy, even thriving.
10942: These desolate plains are almost featureless, save for an occasional rock, or a small stand of weeds. Whichever way you turn your gaze, this picture of devastation is mirrored, and nothing stands in the way of the cold, harsh winds, which whip across the landscape.
10943: Desolation is the only word for these plains. Even the weeds seems to have problems with surviving, but here and there you see an occasional flower or a bush, straining to make these plains fruitful, as they must once have been. Yet that seems to be a futile battle. The desolation can be seen in all directions.
10944: A black wolf pads restlessly, looking for its next prey.

Stiff blades of dead grass still stand here. Perhaps this ground was once rich and fertile, but it is now unable to sustain plant life. The earth is parched and cracked, hard underfoot, offering little bounce to your step.
10945: Standing in the middle of this dreary plain, the rare large boulder and the odd bush is all that can be seen in any direction. Gusts of wind whips at everything, wearing down what little that refuses to conform to flatness.
10946: Gazing eastward reveals a scene of utter desolation. In that direction, a vast expanse of barren and seemingly lifeless plains opens out before you. Westward, the Greenway cleaves a north to south path through the plain, as it journeys between Bree and Tharbad.
10947: These dreary plains would bring tears to the eyes of any farmer. Little but weeds could thrive here, yet you see the occasional dry bush striving to survive. All that can be seen, is nothing but these same plains unfolding.
10948: These flatlands are totally devoid of any plant life. The area appears never to have been cultivated, and the dirt is hard-packed and cracked, as if it had not seen water in years. Each footfall makes a peculiar crunching noise on the hard ground.
10949: The plain rises steeply to the east, ascending to a green hilltop. Little grows here, in stark contrast to the summit, which appears quite green, and it is a matter to wonder what past blight has led to the unwholesome nature of this land.
10950: What lies before you is nothing short of a wasteland, a wide expanse of dirt, where even the sturdiest weeds seem unable to gain a foothold. A few ragged and yellow clumps of dead grass lie, scattered about, long since desiccated by the cruel wind, which blows across this flat and featureless terrain.
10951: The tall grasses gently sway in the breeze, to create an almost hypnotic, rustling sound. A few stunted bushes grow here and there, and a lone tree reaches toward the sky. From here, it is possible to see far across the plains below.
10952: These devastated plains offer no hope for anything but solitude. Some weeds can be seen, and here and there a small bush strives for survival. The landscape to the north and northeast offers no relief from these plains, while to the west you see a road passing from north to south.
10953: Little vegetation and much dust makes these plains a desolate place, a sad place for the life loving, a place of recreation for those of darker persuasions. The only thing breaking the monotony are stones, pebbles and rocks.
10954: A grey wolf is here, salivating profusely.

Absolutely nothing grows here. The pale brown earth is completely bereft of even weeds or grass, suggestive of a long drought, or perhaps ground so poor in nutrients that it is quite unable to sustain even the hardiest plantlife.
10955: Barren Plains on the Side of a Road

A small scattering of sickly plants struggle to grow here, at the side of the road. Other than that, this place is a stark wasteland, bordered to one side by the road to Tharbad. To the north, this unappealing wasteland stretches onward, into the distance.
10956: A colony of red ants is here. The ants seem to ignore you.

The walls of this stone building have long since tumbled down and have become overgrown with grass. It is impossible to discern what purpose this building originally served, but perhaps it was a small home, or some sort of meeting hall.
10957: A tall, stately, dome-topped tree grows here.

Lush vegetation grows on this windy hill top. The view from here is scenic as you look out to the east. In the far distance, a large stone building can be seen, and to the south lie the ruins of a small stone building.
10958: Near the Top of a Hill

From here, parts of the top of the hill can be seen. The hill rises gently, but the climb is a long one. Reaching the top would be a strenuous exercise. Green hills climb away to the west and south of here, whilst to the north, an old and overgrown garden can be seen. All around, the grass grows tall and strong, so that even the tiny trail heading north is almost lost from sight.
10959:
A mass of dark green leaves clings to a wall.
The rabid rabbit is here, frothing at the mouth.

This garden must have been very beautiful before it fell into neglect. Now, weeds have sprouted and begun to strangle flowers and bushes. In the centre of the garden, it appears there once stood a statue, but it has been knocked over and is now broken into a few pieces.
10960: This small cottage might once have been a cosy home, but now it has fallen into a state of disrepair. The doorway stands empty, the hinges rusted and broken, and the roof is badly damaged. No furniture remains here but for a few scraps of wood, scattered about, which are all that is left of the room's former contents.
10961: The top of the hill jutts out here a little bit. On either side, the hill still slopes upward. To the west, some stone ruins can be seen. The wind howls up the hill and blows quite fiercely here.
10962: A grey wolf is here, salivating profusely.
In front of you, to the west, the hilltop jutts out further. However, the hill is steeper here. In the distance, to the east, you can see a stone fortress on top of another steep hill.
10963:
A huge, black wolf is here, ready to devour.
A garden snake slithers harmlessly here.

The ground slopes quite noticeably, and more grass buds are to be seen here than on the flatter, broken ground to the east. To the west, lies a long, grassy hill, which slopes upward toward a plateau.
10964: A large pile of boulders is sitting here, probably debris from a rockslide.

The ground here is riddled with stones of various sizes. The earth between the rocks is a mixture of weeds, dirt and moss. To the west the earth climbs gradually until it reaches a plateau in the far distance.
10965:
A rotten corpse is hanging here.
A black crow flies low to the ground here, looking for carrion to eat.

There is an almost discernible evil about this place, for here stands an old hangman's gallows, its wooden platform worn by age. A rotting noose still swings back and forth, menacingly, in the slightest breeze. But nowhere is there any indication who built this, or when.
10966: This seems to be a stronghold or a hideout of some kind. It has been hewn out of a large rock. The floor is paved with large stone slabs that are placed neatly against each other. From here a few people could defend this place from a large group of attackers.
10967:
A swarm of mosquitoes is here, humming around you.
A mountain mule is standing here, ridden by you.

The plateau comes to an abrupt end here. To the west, a large stone building can be seen, at a distance, on the next hill-top, but it seems that it would be impossible to travel in that direction, as a deep, and impassable gully lies between the two hills.
10968: A mountain mule is standing here, ridden by you.

You stand on a relatively narrow, but grassy plateau. The wind is strong here, blowing wildly in one direction and then abruptly changing directions. To the west the plateau goes on for a bit before it ends.
10969:
A black raven flies in the sky searching for flesh to prey upon.
A black raven flies in the sky searching for flesh to prey upon.
The garden snake slithers harmlessly here.
This hill is a gruelling climb. It leads up to a small stronghold that has been cut out of a few boulders on top on of the hill. At the foot of the hill is a small pond with grey water.
10970:
The rabid rabbit is here, frothing at the mouth.
A mountain mule is standing here, ridden by you.

Large rocks litter this steep incline, but a narrow, winding path seems to pick its way between the largest boulders. Twisting to the east somewhat, the trail leads up the hill to a large, wooded plateau.
10971: A mountain mule is standing here, ridden by you.

Numerous types of trees and bushes grow on this lush plateau. The high altitude provides an astonishing view of the surrounding country-side, and to the west, a narrow, winding path leads back down to the plains below.
10972: This would seem to be a gathering place for some sort of ritual. Small white stones are placed in a perfect circle, in the centre of which stands a statue. Who uses this place, and for what purpose, can only be imagined. The slope to the south is slightly hollowed, and to the west lies an unpleasant field.
10973: A Decayed Vale among the Hills

A swarm of mosquitoes is here, humming around you.
A nightingale is here, chirping a sweet melody.

This valley has a rancid and unwholesome smell. The ground is covered by a mixture of mud, dead grass and a strange red fungus, which seems to grow everywhere. To the northwest, a building can be seen atop a large hill.
10974:
A black raven flies in the sky searching for flesh to prey upon.
A garden snake slithers harmlessly here.

Here lies a small, sickly looking pond. The surface of the water is almost totally covered with a green slime. The parts of the surface that are not obscured appear to be grey. Obviously, this would not be the best place to fill your skins.
10975:
A nightingale is here, chirping a sweet melody.
A rabid rabbit is here, frothing at the mouth.

The earth is scarred by an assortment of stones that lay scattered about here. In among the cracks between the stones grow weeds and moss. This seems to the end of the plains that go out from here in the east.
10976: A mountain mule is standing here, ridden by you.

Huge boulders and dozens of large rocks stand among a littering of smaller stones, on these flat, and barren plains. It would seem that the blocks of stone and piles of dust and rubble are unnatural in origin, and their presence here has choked all life from this field.
10977:
A nightingale is here, chirping a sweet melody.
A black crow flies low to the ground here, looking for carrion to eat.
A mountain mule is standing here, ridden by you.

The ground here is quite flat, and littered with so many rocks and stones that even the crabgrass, so abundant to the west of here, seems unable to gain a toehold. To the north-east, atop a tall hill, a stone garrison can be seen.
10978: A mountain mule is standing here, ridden by you.
This field would be ideal farmland, but no sign of intelligent life can be seen for miles in any direction. An ugly, leafy type of grass grows wild here, coming up to the ankles of a full grown man.
10979: The hillside is so steep here, that it is all but impossible to go directly down it without tumbling out of control. Climbing it is sheer torture. To the east is a plain, which appears to be overgrown with long grasses.
10980: A faint trail through these hilly fields is all but completely hidden by the long, green grasses, which seem to flourish on this steep hillside. The air here seems particularly fresh and wholesome, and a cool breeze makes the lush green blades sway gently.
10981: The trail descends down to the floor of the ravine, winding sharply and then abruptly ending in front of what must be a very thick forest. Even in full daylight, the forest seems dark and ominous.
10982: Here the trail goes down for a bit and then rises again and turns east, where it leads down into the ravine. Looking down into the ravine from here, you can see only the tops of trees.
10983: A Narrow Trail above a Ravine

A nightingale is here, chirping a sweet melody.
A mugger lurks here, looking for a stranger to rob.

From here, you can look down into a ravine below. The trail is quite narrow, and it is necessary to proceed with extreme caution to avoid falling down the cliffside. The trees thin out somewhat, to the north, where the ridge becomes so narrow as to make passage on horseback seem somewhat risky.
10984: A mugger lurks here, looking for a stranger to rob.

A crude footpath winds through a light forest. The trees seem to thin out to the north as the trail narrows and seems to go along the top of a ridge. These woods are suspiciously quiet and there seems to be no sign of intelligent life.
10985: The trees here are so thick that they totally block out the sky and muffle any noise made. The wind blows the branches, causing a montage of shadows on the forest floor. It is hard to tell, but it seems that there could be something moving in the trees ahead.
10986: A Trail Down from the Road

It is a rather steep drop down from the road down to this dirt trail, which continues westward, narrowing markedly as it passes through a tall stand of trees. The pathway is littered with large numbers of stones of all sizes, which makes the way somewhat hard to travel.
10987: The trees are still dense as they grow right up to the wall of the ravine. This niche is particularly stagnant due to its isolation. Due to the closeness of the trees, it is impossible to move in a straight line for more than a few yards in any direction.
10988: A Forest on the Floor of a Ravine

Some thick writhing vines whip all around you.
A bear is here, covered with coarse black fur.

This dark forest is reminiscent of descriptions of Mirkwood. There is a stillness and a sense of forboding here that could chill a person to their very soul. It is hard to imagine that nature could be evil, but this forest seems very sinister.
10989: The valley floor comes to an abrupt end here, as you approach the base of a cliff. This part of the ravine is less densely wooded than the rest, but even so, this area remains quite dark and foreboding. Fragments of bone, charred and splintered pieces of wood, and twisted pieces of metal lie scattered about.
10990: A duck is here, quacking happily.

This cliff top overlooks a forest at the bottom of a ravine. So dense is the foliage that the floor of the canyon cannot be seen. What lives below must remain a matter for speculation, but the woodlands have a sinister air about them, which hints at all manner of evil.
10991:
A coil of rope is lying here.
There is a water skin lying on the ground.

Whoever lives here is not too concerned with cleanliness. Bits of rotten food are strewn about the floor and the fireplace has not been cleaned for a while. Even the planks in the walls are warped and cracked due to a lack of upkeep.
10992: The road upon which you stand seems a well-tended one, bordered, in places, by a light forest, from which the faint music of bird-songs can be heard. To the south, the Nen Kalthar makes its way through the countryside, but the bank of the river is too steep to scramble down here.
10993: The road continues its long journey, winding through the countryside on its way between Bree and Tharbad. To the south, it is bordered by a few trees, growing in an otherwise featureless flatland, and far in the distance, a small river can be seen.
10994: A nightingale is here, chirping a sweet melody.

The road comes to a four-way intersection here. The main route heads south and west, whilst to the north, there is a small pathway, created by heavy foot traffic through the grass. Eastward, a small, very stony, dirt path leads away from the road.
10995: A mountain mule is standing here, ridden by you.

A small dirt path turns off the road, and leads toward a ramshackle old cabin, which stands just west of here. Judging by the freshly disturbed soil, this trail has been used quite recently, and probably quite frequently.
10996: Yellow flowers, with grey-green foliage, grow in clusters here.

An old, dilapidated wooden fence runs east and west here and blocks the way to the north. Although it is rather run down, it is still too high to climb. The fence, in all likelihood, is designed to mark a property line, or to keep out trespassers.
10997: Yellow flowers, with grey-green foliage, grow in clusters here.

An old wooden fence stands here, obviously marking the boundary of somebody's property. It is too high to be jumped by a horse, and it is also quite clearly too unstable to be climbed, with planks hanging askew in many places.
10998:
A duck is here, quacking happily.
A brown toad is here, hunting flies.

In this section of this fence, some boards have rotted out and someone has made a hole large enough for one person on horseback to pass through. To the east, the fence ends and the grounds becomes more rocky. Through the hole you can see a vast expanse of plains before a hill.
10999: Nothing grows here anymore. Clumps of dead grass are everywhere here. For some reason the ground is not as fertile as the green land a few miles to the south. To the north, there is a hill with some sort of stone structure on top of it.
11000: A fat rabbit is here, chewing on some grass.
Lush amber grain grows across these fields, which are bordered, to the north, by a large wooden fence. To the south, the rich golden meadow continues, whilst east of here lie uncultivated fields.
11001: All around grows lush grain of a rich and vivid shade of gold. Plump ears grow atop long, slender stalks, which dance in the slightest breeze, making this look like an amber sea, which stretches into the distance, to the north. To the west lies a small pond, and south of here is a small, stony lane.
11002:
A clean fragrance drifts up from a thick clump of leaves.
A toad is standing here.

This small pond is ideal for fishing. It is crystal clear and beautiful. Its surface is placid and calm. Around the water's edge grow lovely tufts of green grass. To the east a vast expanse of golden grain opens out before you.
11003: A thin layer of small stones and gravel would make this a good path to tread, even in wet weather. However, a number of larger rocks, scattered here and there, could easily trip an incautious traveller. To the west the lane makes an intersection with the road to Tharbad, whilst to the north-east a small building can be seen.
11004: The road upon which you stand seems to be both well-tended and much-travelled. It is bordered to the west by an obviously ancient woodland, made up of a number of stout oaks. From somewhere in that direction, the sound of bird-song can be heard.
11005: The road makes its way south and west from here, as it journeys between Bree and Tharbad. The dirt and stones are hard-packed on this thoroughfare, a clear indication of the heavy use it has seen over the years, and no grass or weeds blemish its surface.
11006: The rustic lane heads out of the farm yard to the east and leads to the road to Tharbad in the distant west. On the north side of the lane, there is a lush field full of golden grain.
11007: This small field seems to overflow with healthy, green grass, making it a perfect place for livestock to graze. It is bounded on two sides by a neat wooden fence, separating it from the road to Tharbad, to the west, and from a small farm lane, to the north.
11008:
A hen is trying to pick some grains here.
A hen is trying to pick some grains here.
A pig is here, covered in mud.

Patches of wild grass and dirt are abundant in this run-farm yard, and the hedgerow to the east grows wild and unkempt. To the immediate north stands an old farmhouse, which appears to be in dire need of repairs, whilst south of here lies a green pasture.
11009: A peaceful farmer is here, whistling merrily.

This farmhouse is simple and rustic. It is lacking in maintenance though. The planks in the floor have faded in colour and are begining to rot. The furniture consists of a few wooden chairs, a table, and some shelves on the walls.
11010: A small animal, all covered in spines, snuffles amongst the undergrowth.
The foliage here grows wild and thick, and it almost seems that there is no way out of this undergrowth. To the north, south and west, the branches seem to be so tangled that no progress is possible.
11011: The shrubs here grow thick and tall, making progress quite difficult. To the east, the foliage is far too dense to force your way through, but to the west it seems to thin out somewhat. To the south, whilst the foliage is denser than ever, it does seem to become thinner, right at ground level.
11012:
A brown snake watches you (red aura).
A brown snake watches you (red aura).

A large, but simple, archway stands here. This must once have been a memorial of some sort, but now all, except the arch itself, stands in ruins. Huge piles of dust and shattered shards or stone lie all around, and the hedgerow to the south looks wild and overgrown.
11013: The Bottom of a Rocky Slope

A pile of rubble and dust has collected here, at the bottom of the slope, and a few large boulders lie here. Perhaps a path once passed this way, for a large and unnatural archway stands to the south, but a landslide has made it quite impossible to follow the trail back to the north.
11014: This slope seems to be far too steep and treacherous to travel upon, and it is quite impossible to scramble back up it, to the north. Many small rocks and stones roll down the hillside, underfoot, making it almost impossible to keep a steady footing, even without trying to attain the summit of the hill.
11015: A grave-digger is here, preparing to mend his shovel.

This cemetery is in bad need of repair. Weeds sprout up next to tombstones and the small wooden fence which runs along the perimeter of the graveyard is rotting and falling down. To the south, there seems to have been a landslide at some time past, and the scree-covered slope appears to be quite steep.
11016:
Yellow flowers, with grey-green foliage, grow in clusters here.
A duck is here, quacking happily.
A fat rabbit is here, chewing on some grass.

Tall, lush grasses cover these gentle, rolling hills, swaying in the lightest breeze, as if some small animal were moving through the dark blades. To the north stands a large wooden fence, whilst westward the flatlands continue.
11017: Yellow flowers, with grey-green foliage, grow in clusters here.

These plains roll gently, but for the most part, are fairly flat. Perhaps these fields belong to a farmer who uses them as pasture for his livestock. To the north, these fields are bordered by a large wooden fence, which seems to stretch endlessly, both to the east, and to the west.
11018:
There are three loaves of bread here.
A large pile of copper coins has been placed here.
A neat straw pallet is lying here.
A small barrel made of aged oak and strong iron hoops stands here.

Cold stone walls and a stony ceiling do not make this a cosy place, and yet this is evidently a living chamber of some sort. A large bed stands against one wall, and in the centre of the room is a stout table, with five sturdy chairs around it. A few rough straw pallets are also piled in one corner.
11019:
A small black vicious rat squeaks at you for disturbing it.
A small black vicious rat squeaks at you for disturbing it.
A small black vicious rat squeaks at you for disturbing it.

The corridor leads to the east and north here, though eastward it seems to come to an abrupt end after only a few strides. A small pile of bones leans against the southern wall, and above them an old, rusted pair of iron fetters hangs, ominously.
11020: The hallway ends rather suddenly here. Someone has recently left a large pile of rubbish here; scattered about the room are broken cups, fragments of wood, torn shreds of cloth and pieces of stone. The wooden beams supporting the ceiling appear to penetrate the eastern wall.
11021: All about the room are empty crates and jugs. This seems to be a storage room of some kind. On the floor, along the walls, there is a large number of rat droppings. Above, it seems that one of the rafters looks different from the others.
11022: The stone floor is hard and cool. From here, the corridor seems to extend forever to the north and the south. The rafters above cast shadows, obscuring the roof. Your footsteps echo resoundingly throughout the hallway.
11023: A short burly man stands here, looking around for something.

This cool, dry intersection has a musty odour to it. It consists of a series of cut bricks of stones placed next to each other. Scattered among them on the floor are fragments of rusted iron chains. The corridor bends here from the south to the east.
11024: The hallway comes to an abrupt end here. Judging from the iron doors on the north, south, and east walls, this appears to have once been a prison; who used it, and for what purpose, cannot be determined from here.
11025:
A musty loaf of bread has been left here.
A musty loaf of bread has been left here.
A prisoner is sitting here, looking at you with sad eyes.

Fungus grows on the walls of this unpleasant room, and the floor is covered by dirt and waste. The air hangs heavy with an unpleasant odour of death and decay, and no fresh breeze penetrates this place, to offer relief. The only apparent exit is the heavy iron door to the west.
11026: An intact skeleton of a man is walking around here.

The walls of this room tell a horrible story. The iron door has many scratches on it and the walls are stained red-brown from old caked blood. Some coarse straw has been left in one corner, perhaps to serve as a bed or even a latrine, and on one wall small scrapings in the stone appear to be an attempt to write a message.
11028: A domesticated pony, beast of burden to many, stands here.

Lush green grass grows strong and healthy in this lovely pasture, which would be an ideal spot for grazing cattle, sheep or horses. The fields extend to the south, east and west of here, whilst to the north lies a small, slightly unkempt farmyard.
11029:
A young farm-hand is here hard at work.
A cow stands here, chewing her cud.
A cow stands here, chewing her cud.

Clearly this portion of the pastureland has been badly overgrazed, with all of the grass bitten down to the ground, to leave only bare dirt. The endless passage of animals over this field has left it a quagmire.
11030:
A sturdy pack horse is standing here.
A mountain mule is standing here, ridden by you.

A few bales of hay are stacked in one corner of this ample building, and on the west wall a neat row of stalls has been built for the animals. In the north wall, a large opening lets out onto a muddy pasture.
11031: A cow stands here, chewing her cud.

Thick grass grows in abundance here, and trees stand at intervals over the field, with small clusters of flowers growing about their bases. You can catch a glimpse of a small house to the north, and just east of here stands an old wooden barn.
11032: A garden snake slithers harmlessly here.

This well grown grassland is located in a bend of the Road to Tharbad, which lies to the west and to the south of here. The fields are filled with thick and high grass, and a few small bushes grow here and there, punctuating the meadow, which stretches onward to the north and east.
11033: The bare hard soil of the road to Tharbad looks like a brown cut in the middle of the green grassy plains. The ground has many slashes in it from where merchant carriages once rode. Grass grows fairly tall within the neglected plains nearby, creating many homes for insects.
11034: A garden snake slithers harmlessly here.

The road to Tharbad winds from the north along to the east, and is bordered by the bank of a river on the southern and western side. The embankment slopes down fairly steeply, with soft red clay marking the surface of the bank. Around here and towards the north there is nothing except more fields and some burnt out carriages along the road.
11035: The road extends along the flat barren land towards the east and in the west. The hard dirt road winds and curves along the terrain like a snake moving in the desert. A small embankment slopes towards the south, leading to a fast flowing river. The road itself does not offer much to look at.
11036: Carriage tracks scar the ground in many different directions, making deep slicing gouges in the hardened surface of the road. Beside the lane, tall grass grows in dense clumps, which lean in the light breeze, and to the south, beyond the continuing roadway, the steep banks of the Nen Kalthar can be seen.
11037: A mountain mule is standing here, ridden by you.

Tall grass grows all over within this field, unlike the hard and bare land of the nearby road. Small holes lie here and there, in the ground, home to innumerable small beasts, and to the north, a large wooden building can be seen, hinting at the presence of a nearby farm.
11038: The edges of the road slope gently away, making its border that much more clearly defined. The nearby fields look unattractive and muddy, in contrast to the hard-packed dirt of the thoroughfare. A few trees grow beside the roadway, not too far distant.
11039:
The garden snake slithers harmlessly here.
A mountain mule is standing here, ridden by you.

The land rolls along in an endless sea of grass, with the wind lightly brushing the tips of the grass blades. A small column of smoke can be seen rising from the northwest. Some trees along the north mark the field of grass, and more woods can be seen in the distance.
11040:
A colony of red ants is here. The ants seem to ignore you.
A mountain mule is standing here, ridden by you.

Many dead and burnt out trees stand or lie here, their brown, blackish colour of death matching that of the grass around them. A recent rain has turned parts of the ground to a dark red-brown mud slurry, and a huge pile of dead logs blocks the way north and east. To the west stands an old wooden barn.
11041:
Yellow flowers, with grey-green foliage, grow in clusters here.
A mountain mule is standing here, ridden by you.

Green soft grass can be seen in the whole area, some small trees and bushes are also spread around it. There are small holes in the ground, too small to enter but big enough for a small animal. The country around looks a bit empty and to the south the road to Tharbad goes in a west-east direction.
11042: This stretch of wooded plains is bounded to the north and east by the road to Tharbad. To the west, it comes to an end on the banks of the Nen Kalthar. Here stands a small wood, comprised of obviously ancient oak trees, whose gnarled roots stand proud of the ground in places.
11043: A featureless grassy field stretches beside the roadway, and nearby the Nen Kalthar flows peacefully through the countryside. The ground here is moist and cool, the grass long and green, its roots fed by the water of the river. However, the road to the east is made of hard-packed earth, which somehow seems parched even in wet weather.
11044: A Large Tree beside the River

A tall and stately tree stands atop a steep river bank. Though quite ancient the tree is healthy and strong, and its base is surrounded by thick, green grass. The soft sound of the river babbling below lends a special music to the scene.
11045:
A brook trout is here, swimming in the current.
A brook trout is here, swimming in the current.

The riverbanks here are too steep to be scaled. Trees along each bank sway gently in the slightest breeze, dropping leaves into the gently rippling water, which laps against the land as it progresses south.
11046: A Calm Bend in the Nen Kalthar

The water slowly rolls across the land and takes a turn to the south here. To the east, a series of rolling plains can be seen. To the north, a road runs parallel to the river, marching off to the east, as the river bends southward.
11047: The cool water of the Nen Kalthar can be seen from atop the river bank. The path down to the water is steep and treacherous, as the shoreline is quite rocky, and slick with water, and to the east the road the Tharbad stretches into the distance, cutting a long scar through the countryside.
11048:
A cute rabbit is here.
A small bat is standing here.

The riverbank to the north is too steep to scale. Lazily the current moves downstream and ripples as it passes a large rock, which stands right in the middle of the waterway, its smooth surface moist and slightly mossy.
11049: A robin is here, carrying small pieces of wood to its nest.

Large, slightly slippery, rocks peep out above the surface of the water, which ripples and foams around them. The shallow shoreline is filled with tiny, multicoloured pebbles, and beneath the shimmering water, a riverbed of small rocks can be seen.
11050:
A robin is here, carrying small pieces of wood to its nest.
A cute rabbit is here.

This area is covered with thick green grass. The grass is well grown becasue of its never failing access to water. It is a sand bank to the east, which is bordering the Nen Kalthar, the sand shines with a soft yellow light. The field reaches further to the west as far as you can see.
11051: A small grasshopper clings to a blade of grass, ready to spring.

Nature demonstrates her power here, in this green billowing sea of grass. The field stretches eastward and to the south, amid the tall grasses, stands a lone tree, watching over the surrounding countryside.
11052:
A black crow flies low to the ground here, looking for carrion to eat.
A robin is here, carrying small pieces of wood to its nest.

A sad and lonely looking tree stands here, amid the tall grass, its branches stripped almost bare by the hard winds which blow so often over these open plains. The few remaining leaves have a sickly brown look, as if scarcely clinging to life. Around the tree stand a few short bushes, with dense foliage, better able to withstand the harsh winds.
11053:
A fisherman is sitting here in a boat in the middle of the water.
A bass swims here.

The serenity of this small river is remarkable. The clear waters gently flow onward, to the east, as they pass through a small grove of trees. In the distance, an old road can be seen, running alongside the river, on its endless journey through the surrounding country.
11054: A Shallow Bend in the Nen Kalthar
Of all the rivers on Arda, this one must be the most picturesque. The trickling it makes as it flows is music to a weary person's ears. The Nen Kalthar bends and flows to the east here.
11055:
A large toadstool grows nearby.
A hungry warg (Rood) is standing here, ridden by you.
A few trees grow along the road here. To the west and the south, the trees end as one gets close to the bank of the Nen Kalthar. To the north and the east, the road can be seen through the trees.
11056: A brown fox is here, looking for some rabbits to chew up.

You wander amid a tranquil, grassy plain, made fertile by the small river, which flows just north and east of here. The plain reaches, unbound, to the horizon, like an endless sea of waving green grass, with small wildflowers and numerous thick bushes to be seen among the greenery.
11057:
A grey wolf is here, snarling aggressively.
A brown fox is here, looking for some rabbits to chew up.

The grass here is long, and grows with a healthy green lustre. These plains, which stretch to the east and west, as far as the eye can see, have been made fertile, by their proximity to the small river, which flows eastward across the land, just north of here.
11058:
A small campfire burns here, its low flames giving off only a little light.
Yellow flowers, with grey-green foliage, grow in clusters here.
Klaees (thedon), holding a two-handed sword, is sleeping here.
Lhurank (brenny), wielding an ornamented sabre, is standing here searching for something.

These plains are rich and green, owing much of their health to the rich water supply from the small river just north of here. The plains stretch out to the horizon both east and west. The river is small, but looks rather deep, so it would be difficult to cross here.
11059:
A brown fox is here, looking for some rabbits to chew up.
A mountain mule is standing here, ridden by you.

The plain is lush and green, the grass rich and healthy. The babble of a small river to the north, and the sweet sound of birdsong make music in the air, unbroken except by an occasional gust of wind, which rolls across these endless flatlands.
11060:
Yellow flowers, with grey-green foliage, grow in clusters here.
A brown fox is here, looking for some rabbits to chew up.
A mountain mule is standing here, ridden by you.

The grassy plain unfolds before you, rich and lush with vegetation. Green grass covers your ankles as you stride along. The plain stretches as far as you can see both east and west, although you glimpse rising treetops to the west. A river cleaves the plain to the north, running east and west. Although not too wide, it seems rather deep, so crossing here could be difficult.
11061: Yellow flowers, with grey-green foliage, grow in clusters here.

The plains look rich and fertile here, propably owing a lot of its health to the rich watersupply from the river to the north. The plain stretches as far as you can see along the river to the east, while the view west is obscured by the growing vegetation and the rising trees of a small forest.
11062: A small animal, all covered in spines, snuffles amongst the undergrowth.

The vegetation is dense here, but not tall enough to be called a forest. Yet it grows tight, and you have to force your way through here. Looking west, you see the trees growing larger and larger, while to the east it thins down to a grassy plain.
11063: Some large trees among the thick undergrowth makes this place more or less a forest. Yet passage is slow, the bushes whipping at your face as you pass. The vegetation grows denser to the west. Somewhere to the north you hear the tinkling of a river.
11064: An ancient oak stands, quite alone, at the centre of a circle of smaller trees. Far past its prime, this enormous tree shows signs of rot, and many termites have consumed and eroded its once sturdy trunk. However, it still stands, its broad branches making a wide canopy above your head.
11065: You find yourself atop the tallest tree in the forest, with a panoramic view of the surrounding countryside. Beyond the forest to the north you see a river and a road side by side, leading eastwards. Further on you see a flat and rather large plain unfolding, the flatness broken by a hill and some buildings.
11067:
A bass swims here.
A bass swims here.

The river is quite deep here, but its waters are clear, and a number of small shapes can be seen, darting about above the stony bed. To the south, a wide grassy plain stretches into the distance, whilst to the north of the river, a wide roadway marches from east to west.
11068: A Shallow Part of the Nen Kalthar
A mountain mule is standing here, ridden by you.

The river is wide and quite shallow here, with numerous broad, flat rocks, peeping above the surface of the slow-flowing water. Grassy plains fringe the south bank, stretching off into the distance, whilst to the north, three roadways meet.
11069: The river is very deep here, but not at all wide. Through the clear water, small glimmering shapes can be seen darting hither and thither. The flow here is quite serene, progressing gently toward the east, whilst beyond the banks of the river, to the north, a road can be seen, tracing a similar route.
11070: The river is deeper here than it seemed, flowing slowly eastward. Small glimmering shapes down in the river scatters as you pass. A road seems to follow the river to the north, while a grassy plain unfolds to the south.
11071: Flowing west and east, the river is here too deep to cross without swimming. Just north you see a road following the river, while grassy plains can be found to the south. Gazing into the depths of the water, you glimpse small shapes, darting around.
11072: The river is quite deep here, but some large flat rocks, only partially covered by moss and weeds, provide a fairly safe footing. The Nen Kalthar bends east and north here, and is bordered to the south by gently rolling plains. To the northeast, a steep cliff rises out of the water, and peering downwards, it can be seen that this stretches far below the surface, even though it only rises some four feet above the waterline.
11073: The stream bends west and south here, counterpointing the road to the north. Although not wide, the river seems to be quite deep here. You see twinkles of light reflected in small, darting shapes near the bottom of the river.
11074: The river is deep and clear here, in fact much deeper than it seemed from afar. Looking down, you see glimmering shapes by the stony bottom, quickly darting here and there. To the north a small road follows the river, while to the southeast you see some trees.
11075: A Shallow Part of the Nen Kalthar

Clusters of slender stems and tall leaves thrive in the mud and shallows.
Clusters of slender stems and tall leaves thrive in the mud and shallows.

The river is very shallow here, propably because much of the water has found its way into the marsh to the north. To the south small trees can be seen, growing taller further south and west. The river gets deeper further east.
11076: Clusters of slender stems and tall leaves thrive in the mud and shallows.

You stand in the middle of a rather shallow river. Its hard to say where the river ends and the marsh to the north begins, since much of the water flows freely there. The cluttered forest to the south seems comfortable compared to the soggy mire to the north.
11077:
A large leech is moving close to you, searching for blood.
A large leech is moving close to you, searching for blood.
An angry bee is here, collecting nectar from all the flowers of the garden.
A swarm of mosquitoes is here, humming around you.
An angry bee is here, collecting nectar from all the flowers of the garden.

The mud is sticky and deep, and the air alive with the buzzing of countless small insects, most of which seem intent on making you their dinner. A faint rotting smell assails your nostrils, and even the ferns and small, stunted bushes seem to struggle to grow here.
11078: The ground is slightly elevated here, making the soil dry. No ferns or trees obscure the ground, making this place a haven in this mire. Even the buzzing of the insects have faded.
11079:
A swarm of mosquitoes is here, humming around you.
A swarm of mosquitoes is here, humming around you.
A swarm of mosquitoes is here, humming around you.

This wet mire dooms any boot passing through to instant sogginess. The marsh is deep and dense enough to force anyone to struggle to get through, and a few small animal bones peep up through the surface of the foetid mud. The air all around is filled, not only by a rotting stench, but also by the insistent buzz of innumerable insects.
11080:
A large leech is moving close to you, searching for blood.
A large leech is moving close to you, searching for blood.
An angry bee is here, collecting nectar from all the flowers of the garden.

Stunted bushes and large ferns occupy any traces of dry land in this soggy mire, leaving any attempt to pass through the area without getting soaked assured to fail. All around, the air is filled by the insistent buzzing of innumerable small insects.
11081: A swarm of mosquitoes is here, humming around you.

The air seems alive with small insects, which buzz incessantly about you, and is filled too with a faint rotting stench. Dark green ferns and small, stunted bushes cling to life in the quagmire, occupying any small island of dryness in the mud, and forcing any traveller to move through the deepest parts of the mire.
11082: Yellow flowers, with grey-green foliage, grow in clusters here.

The river gently separates the forest to the south from the mire to the north. Where the river becomes mire is hard to tell, but crossing the river will cause no problem. The river is shallow, and flows serenely from east to west.
11083: Brambles and briars grow thick among the trees, and to the south, they grow so densely as to obscure the trail completely, making progress that way quite impossible. To the west, too, the undergrowth is choking and no clear pathway can be seen. The soil here is moist, and the air thick with a faint musty odour, and from somewhere to the north, the sound of a river can be heard.
11084: Even though you stand in the outskirts of the forest, the trees grow close together here, and a thick underbrush of briars and brambles makes progress through this area quite difficult. An occasional howl pierces the air, obscuring the tranquil sound of flowing water, somewhere to the north.
11085: You force your way through this brush. Small, intertwined trees and bushes makes the passage very tiresome. The tops of larger trees can be seen to the south and west, while to the north a small river passes eastward.
11086:
A squirrel scampers around here, looking for nuts from the trees.
A huge, black wolf is here, ready to devour.
A black wolf pads restlessly, looking for its next prey.
A black wolf pads restlessly, looking for its next prey.
A black wolf pads restlessly, looking for its next prey.

Small trees and dense bushes are entwined to form what can only be called a brush. The trees are too small to be a true forest, but seem to be striving to grow into one. To the southwest the top of taller trees can be seen.
11087:
A large leech is moving close to you, searching for blood.
A large leech is moving close to you, searching for blood.
A swarm of mosquitoes is here, humming around you.
A swarm of midges is here, humming around you.

The air around you is damp and foul, filled with a faint rotting stench, and all about the incessant buzzing of countless small insects can be heard. Far to the south, beyond a small river, a forest can be seen, but to the north, east and west the marshland stretches into the distance.
11088:
An angry bee is here, collecting nectar from all the flowers of the garden.
An angry bee is here, collecting nectar from all the flowers of the garden.
An angry bee is here, collecting nectar from all the flowers of the garden.
An angry bee is here, collecting nectar from all the flowers of the garden.
An angry bee is here, collecting nectar from all the flowers of the garden.
A huge, bulky queen bee is here.

The ground seems firmer here, the mire less evident. You find yourself before an ancient willow, worn by rot and age, and cleft in half by some wild strike of a lightning bolt long ago. A loud buzzing is heard, louder the closer you get to the willow.
11089: You are on an ancient road, small of stature, yet with a dignity born from ancient use. Your passage disturbs some weeds breaking through the hard-packed ground. The road leads in a straight east to west direction, but the way westward has been blocked by the fallen bough of a tree.
11090: A rusty iron pick has been discarded here.

The light from the entrance to the south is strangely magnified here, perhaps due to multitudes of crystals, embedded in the walls, which reflect and enhance the light, making it possible to discern some of the details in this cave. Searching around, you find little of interest, not even a pocket of air. The only thing worth a closer look are some boulders and rocks blocking the way further north. Now and then something unknown touches your feet fleetingly.
11091:
A trout swims here.
A trout swims here.

You are diving into the river. Small fish scatter from your prescence as you explore the watery depths. The river is unexpectedly deep here, and due to the turbulent and muddy water, your vision is limited. At the southern edge of the river, you see an uneven cliff plunging into the depths. The cliff has many rather wide cracks in it, some of which seems to be human-sized too.
11092: You stand on what seems to be the highest point in the area. Turning slowly, you see that if nothing else, this is a place of contrasts. To the north you see mostly desolated fields and some ruined buildings. To the south you see a river flowing eastward along a road, while far to the southwest you see a small forest. Just southeast is the junction of three roads, Greenway, the Road to Tharbad, and a less used road leading towards Sarn Ford.
11093: Unwholesome plains surrounds you. The soil is cluttered with stones and rocks, yet a little greenery can still be seen, though most of this is merely weeds and a little choked, unhealthy grass. The plains ascend a little to the east, as they climb a small hillock.
11094: A rabbit is here eyeing your presence warily.

These dreary plains offer little solace for a weary traveller. Rocks of various sizes, from pebbles to large boulders, are found in multitudes here. Just east you see a large road cutting through the plains, running straight north.
11095: These dry and desolate plains offer little peace for a traveller. Rocks and weeds stain the earth. The soil is cracked and hard, the weeds are obviously the only thing able to survive.
11096:
A worm is here slithering around.
A spirit floats towards you and howls with an evil laughter.

These plains are desolated, in dire need of vegetation. The ground is rather flat, but, here and there, small crevices in the earth can be seen. An occasional boulder stands tall, defiant in the face of erosion.
11097: A worm is here slithering around.

These fields were once rich, yet now only the weeds survive. A faint rotten smell permeates this area. The soil is hard and cracked. An abandoned building can be seen to the northeast, torn by age and weather.
11098: A worm is here slithering around.

The furrows and the rotten remains of fences are all that remains of these fields of old. Whatever crop was growing here, it has now been replaced by weeds. Just north you see a partly collapsed building.
11099: This building is partly collapsed, the fireplace by one wall now nothing but loose stones and bricks from the collapsed chimney. Evil thoughts and evil deeds seems strangely manifest in the cold air. A door leads out east, with a mouldy rug lying in front of it.
11100: Rotten fences have long ago crumbled, yet still outline what once must have been a crop field. The weeds have long since replaced the crops, being able to survive in these inhospitable surroundings. The remains of a ruined building can be seen to the east.
11101: The soil here seems nutritious, at least when compared to the land further west, where the grasses grow yellow and weak. To the east, a small building stands in the distance, beyond a wide open field, and in the far distance, a roadway can be seen.
11102: A mountain mule is standing here, ridden by you.

The weeds seem dominant here, yet large tuffs of grass sprout here and there, giving this region a ragged appearance. The ground is uneven, rising and sinking, occasionally breaking into small clefts in the landscape.
11103:
A sparrow is flapping around on the ground.
A mountain mule is standing here, ridden by you.

The plain is flat, the grass a sickly pale green colour. There is little to attract anyone here, save perhaps some starved animal. Just east of here you see a faint path, partly overgrown, yet obviously leading north to a small hill.
11104: A mountain mule is standing here, ridden by you.

Green grass competes with weeds for survival on these plains. A sense of despair is somehow present here, tugging at your awareness, yet somehow beyond your perceptions. To the northwest, the plains rises to a small hill.
11105: A nauseating stench fills the air. The grass grows high, but it has a faint yellowish tinge to it, breaking the illusion of health. A partly overgrown path cleaves through the grassland, leading north to a tiny hill. The feeble chittering of grasshoppers is the only sound to be heard.
11106: One side of the barn has collapsed long ago, and what remains looks rather unstable too. Moving around here requires care. All you seem to find here are the yellowed bones of a cow-sized animal.
11107: Only a pale shadow of the activity of old remains here now. Once neat, the furrows which line the ground are now choked by intruding weeds. A crumbling fence runs along the road to the east, and also stands between this field and the plains, which lie to the south.
11108: An old, stony trail, laid to waste by ages of disuse, and exposure to the wind and weather, leads westward, toward a ruined farm. Crumbling fences border the trail, outlining ancient fields, to the north and south, whilst the pathway itself, leads east, to the Greenway.
11109:
A tall, stately, dome-topped tree grows here.
On the plant, there are three green spiny capsules.
A starving cow stands here, looking for a patch of grass.

Only a pale memory remains of these once rich and fertile pastures. The grass here seems to be fighting a losing battle against the encroaching weeds, and the fence, which once bordered these fields on three sides, now lies in ruins to the north, leaving the way open to a blighted and desolate plain. To the east, the fence, though decayed still bars the way to a wide road, which carves a bold north to south route through the countryside.
11110: The interior of the farmhouse is a complete mess. A thick layer of grime coats the floor, and the broken remains of the furniture lie scattered all around, themselves blanketed in a thick covering of dust and cobwebs. It would appear that this place was abandoned long ago.
11111: A mass of dark green leaves clings to a wall.

The farmyard is covered by flagstones, crumbled by age and the weeds which have forced their way up to the sun. A dry stone wall marks the margin of the land to the west, and a small pig pen, outlined by a rotting wooden fence, stands just before the barn to the south. To the north stands an old farm house.
11112: Though the grass grows quite tall here, it has an unhealthy, yellow hue. A few small bushes seem barely able to cling to life here, and the overall feeling of the area is one of decay and disease. These sickly plains stretch onward to the north and south, but to the west, a small hill rises out of the flat landscape.
11113: The yellow grass grows about ankle-high here, and a faint, pungent, rotting smell permeates the air. Though a few small flowers strive to survive, they seem to face a hopeless battle in this obviously unhealthy region. All that can be seen to the north and the south is a continuing expanse of barren plains, much like these.
11119: A sparrow is flapping around on the ground.

Standing alone in the middle of the grassy plains, this hill provides a decent place to scout the surrounding area. Covered by grass, this hill is crowned by a large cluster of bushes, cradling a rather unusual indentation in the side of the hill.
11136: A small spirit floats around here, with despair in its eyes.

The shaft seems to have collapsed here, with a large heap of boulders making passage further to the north impossible. Each movement stirs up clouds of age-old dust, and in the whirling eddies of small particles, something sticking out of the heap of rocks catches your eye.
11137: The shaft bends quite sharply east here, after having angled to the right a while. The air here is dry and dusty, making it hard to breathe. Some broken logs can be seen lying on the floor. These must once have supported the ceiling here. Strangely, the ceiling is still where it ought to be.
11138: A small spirit floats around here, with despair in its eyes.

You stand at the bottom of a hole. The shaft leads north, its ceiling hanging low above your head, and its walls, at times, growing quite close together. A ladder is propped against the wall here, but most of its rungs have long ago rotted away, rendering it useless to climb upward from here.
11139: The shaft takes a sudden stop here. You see some sort of mechanism over a large hole in the ground. The rotten logs and the ropes must once have been used to haul heavy loads up from the hole. Looking closer at the hole, you see a ladder leading down.
11141: You find yourself in an abandoned hole. Dust covers everything, and yet the furniture appears surprisingly whole. However, closer examination reveals centuries of rot. Judging by its size, and the rusty and useless remains of pickaxes and other mining tools, this must once have been the home of a group of dwarves. You find the torn remainders of a journal, yet little of it is now intact. It would seem that though this was once a natural cave, it was later enlarged as a living area; the room extends further north, sloping downward slightly, and ending in a rough door of wooden planks, which cover a wide opening. The walls seem to be sturdy and well built, save for the east wall, which has either collapsed over the course of time, or was perhaps constructed with some haste, and little skill.
11142:
The corpse of a slithering snake is lying here.
The corpse of a slithering snake is lying here.
The corpse of a slithering snake is lying here.
The corpse of a slithering snake is lying here.
The corpse of a green snake is lying here.
The corpse of a green snake is lying here.
The corpse of a green snake is lying here.

The corpse of a slithering snake is lying here.
The corpse of a slithering snake is lying here.
The corpse of a slithering snake is lying here.
The corpse of a slithering snake is lying here.
The corpse of a slithering snake is lying here.
The corpse of a green snake is lying here.

You enter a large cavernous area. A multitude of holes can be seen in the walls and the ceiling. Hundreds of slithering creatures can be seen, fleeing as they sense your presence. You see the room ending in an alcove just to the east, but the floor looks rather unstable.
11143: In a Hole beneath the Alcove

A small spirit floats around here, with despair in its eyes.
A small spirit floats around here, with despair in its eyes.
A small spirit floats around here, with despair in its eyes.
An evil Spirit Knight is here, feeding on your fear.
A sturdy pack horse is standing here.
A domesticated pony, beast of burden to many, stands here.
Staub the Dwarf (SS), wielding an engraved broadsword, is standing here.

A putrid stench fills the air. The ground in this small burial chamber is covered with an ankle-deep layer of blood-encrusted mud. A pedestal, crowned with a large casket, stands in the middle of the room, its lid lying on the ground beside it. Many bones litter the floor, jutting out of the stinking mud, yellowed by age. To the south, a small tunnel leads into the darkness.
11144:
Tordol the Dwarf (t), wielding a blackened dwarven axe, is resting here.
Agarnon the Man (a), wielding a broadsword, is standing here trying to concentrate.

The tunnel stops quite abruptly, as the ceiling further on has collapsed. The walls, floor and ceiling are rough and uneven, as if hewn in great haste, perhaps neglecting the use of timber props, and so precipitating the later cave-in. Small rivulets of water run down the walls, and pool in small indentations on the floor.
11145: A shadowy haunt floats here, oblivious to your presence.

This cellar shows signs of decades of abandonment. A thick layer of dust covers the room like a shroud. Some of the walls have crumbled with time, showing the bare earth behind. Judging from the broken barrels and rotten remains hanging from the ceiling, this must once have been a food store.
11146:
A spirit floats towards you and howls with an evil laughter.
A spirit floats towards you and howls with an evil laughter.

As you entered the abandoned inn, a portion of the floor gave way underfoot, plunging you into this dark cellar. The air has a musty and rotten odour, seemingly quite unhealthy to breath, and the ground is covered with broken shards of bone, which crumble beneath your feet.
11147: The current of the water is moving slowly, though, heading down south, it appears to be picking up some speed. Rocks can be seen on the bottom of the river, they are becoming more and more noticeable drifting downstream. The river's course heads south, and also leads back towards the north.
11148: A robin is here, carrying small pieces of wood to its nest.

The stream flows peacefully here, the gentle current creating multitudinous ripples and eddies on the surface of the water. Sand covers the entire bed of the river, and piles upward at the banks as well, left by the flow of the water. Every so often a light breeze blows across the surface of the water, making criss-cross patterns in the ripples.
11149: More rocks accumulate towards the east, making the river begin to roar loudly. Further upstream, to the west, the stream widens, and the banks become quite sandy, the waters more murky, and the current more languid. But here, the grassy banks are covered with trees and bushes, whose leaves fall into the water, and drift downstream.
11150: Two different waterways meet here, a small stream, flowing from the west, joining the Nen Kalthar in its eastward flow here. The current picks up pace, becoming swifter to the east, where more rocks can be seen, peaking through the surface of the water. Westward, the stream is more peaceful, with a sandy bottom, which swirls up, making the waters murky, as small fish swim about, raising the sand.
11151: The current gently moves the water towards the east, softly stirring up the sandy bottom. There is a greenish tint to the surface of the stream, which obscures the true depth, but a few old branches poke through the water, creating small waves, and suggesting that perhaps this waterway is quite shallow.
11152: Slowly and quietly the stream drifts onward to the east. Tiny tracks in the soft mud of the shoreline hint at the presence of small unseen creatures, and faint noises interrupt the tranquility of the scene. Trees, standing on the shore, bow down, dipping their branches toward the water, in a gentle breeze, and the blue-green water laps in small waves, toward the banks of the river.
11153: The riverbank has worn away to reveal this small, mossy niche. The ground is soft, earthy and moist, and the curving walls on all sides are covered in a thick blanket of dark green moss. The sound of the river to the north is all that is to be heard.
11154: A nightingale is here, chirping a sweet melody.

White foam forms all over the rocks as the current becomes more and more rapid. The water is cool as it quickly drifts by, with the air moving across the top of the surface. Very small rocks along the beach of the river swirl the water into tiny little whirlpools.
11155: The swift waters of the river are becoming more and more rough as the current heads off to slash the water against rocks breaking the surface. Mist fills this place as the water is splashed high into the air when it collides with the rocks.
11156: The river current has become swift and rough, slashing out over the rocks that break the water's surface. Creating a loud roar, which masks any sounds coming anywhere away from there, the river quickly and violently rolls on towards the east, with many white bubbles forming on its surface.
11157: A crayfish is here, snapping its claws at you.

The rocks in the river are becoming rounder in shape, breaking the water over them much softer than before. The sound of rough water from up the river is still extremely loud, and a reminder of how swift and treacherous it once was. A crisp, cool breeze waves over the surface of the water, chilling it slightly.
11158:
A brook trout is here, swimming in the current.
A brook trout is here, swimming in the current.

The blue waters flow slowly and peacefully here, the wide but shallow river bordered by banks full of flowers and bushes. In places, rocks peep out from beneath the surface of the water, forcing it to foam and splash as it makes its way slowly eastward, and the entire riverbed here is comprised of small stones, in all shades of grey and black.
11159:
A trout swims here.
A sparrow is flapping around on the ground.
A bass swims here.
A fat carp swims here.
A sparrow is flapping around on the ground.

The Nen Kalthar flows over many rocks and stones here, splishing and splashing as it makes its way eastward across the countryside. A gentle breeze blows from the east, cutting up the surface of the water even where the rocks do not make it foam.
11160:
A brook trout is here, swimming in the current.
A bass swims here.

The river bends here, flowing round the deep roots of a tall, old tree, which you can see to your east. Pebbles bump about the bottom of the river, bouncing against rocks, jumping happily away, and continuing to follow the flow of the river, which bends south then east again.
11161:
A trout swims here.
A bass swims here.

Gurgling contentedly, the river bends gently around the roots of a solitary tree which stands just north-east of here, drinking a deep draught of the wholesome waters of the Nen Kalthar. The river flows again to the east, carrying you towards the City of Thieves.
11162:
A bass swims here.
A fat carp swims here.
A fat carp swims here.

The river here is bordered to the north by high banks, apparently built up by the hand of man to protect the road to the north from flooding. To the south however, a large, square building stands low on the riverbank. It is apparent that this structure is a mill, though whether it is still in service is not possible to tell from here.
11163: Many old and burnt out carriages lie scattered along the roadside, which meanders from the east and towards the west. The ground underfoot is hard and bare, from the wear of many years of travel.
11164: Grassy fields border along the road to Tharbad towards the north, creating an endless sea of light green blades. The soft sounds of a river can be heard nearby, its bank sloping slightly towards the south. The grass around here is a nice shade of dark green, a contrast to its kin in the fields.
11165: A rabbit is here eyeing your presence warily.

You are walking along a well-tended road, which borders the Nen Kalthar. You can hear the sounds of happy birds singing nearby, and you feel untroubled by your journey. The road runs due east-west here.
11166: You are walking along a well-tended road, with the Nen Kalthar drifting past to the south. Birds are singing happily from the trees alongside the road, and all your cares seem to melt away to nothing. The road continues to the east and west.
11167: The wide roadway seems to be quite well tended in this part of the country, probably owing to the number of farms in the area. Just south of the road, at the bottom of an extremely steep and muddy bank, the river Nen Kalthar flows lazily from the west.
11168: A rabbit is here eyeing your presence warily.

The road is raised slightly above the level of the surrounding countryside, on a causeway. To the north, you can join a small path, which leads to a barn, in the northwest, or you could follow the path further north, towards a small farmhouse. Directly to the south stands a large, solitary tree, and the road sweeps on past this, heading from east to west.
11169: The road bends here, curving gracefully from the south to the west. In the north, a thin forest can be seen, and nestling, almost in its eaves, is a small farmhouse. To the southwest, a solitary tree stands, as if sundered from its kin by this wide roadway.
11170:
A squirrel scampers around here, looking for nuts from the trees.
A mountain mule is standing here, ridden by you.

The bank of the river bends along it, towards the east and in the north. The ground is very moist from the water splashing against the rocks and landing on the soil above. Many rocks can be seen breaking the surface of the river, creating little side currents within the water.
11171: A mountain mule is standing here, ridden by you.

Up along the bank, the water appears to have a blue greenish tint to it. The river bends around the bank, and a large tree stands over the river, its leaves slightly dipping into the water from their drooping branches. A few brightly coloured leaves float softly into the mainstream current, getting transported briskly down along the river.
11172: A robin is here, carrying small pieces of wood to its nest.

The rocky riverbank peters out to the east, where the road to Tharbad draws closer to the waters of the Nen Kalthar. Large, flat slabs of rock rise steeply upward from the rippling water, too steep and slick to climb; most seem flat and featureless, but one particularly large slab seems oddly scratched and notched.
11173: The water here has become so shallow that it is possible for even someone the size of a halfling to wade through it. The bed of the river has very few rocks that lie on the bottom here, exposing a muddy surface that appears to have been disturbed many times. Wind dances along the top of the water creating ripples on the surface.
11175: There are two piles of acorns here.

A solitary tree stands here, isolated from its fellows in the north by the line of the road to Tharbad. On the bole of the tree there is an elaborate carving which needs a closer inspection to be seen properly. To the west, the river Nen Kalthar flows by, diverted from its eastward course by the sturdy roots of this tree, which make the riverbank firm and strong here.
11176: The road here is raised slightly, on a broad earthen causeway. To the south there is a gentle slope down to a low wooden bridge, which spans the waters of the Nen Kalthar. The road itself curves around a solitary tree, which stands on the bank of the river, just to the west.
11177: A wiry smuggler is here, attempting to avoid being seen.

The road here runs east-west, straight as an arrow. In the north you can hear the noise of birds singing happily in the trees, and you fancy that you can actually hear the trees sighing with contentment. Looking south, you can see the sparkling, clear waters of the Nen Kalthar, flowing lazily toward the east.
11178: The noise of birdsong drifts on the air from the north, where a thin forest stands, separated from the road here by thick, thorny undergrowth. To the south, a small wooden building can be seen, standing right on the bank of the Nen Kalthar, and the musical murmur of flowing water can be heard even from the road.
11179: The road here bends from the south to the west, running parallel to the light forest in the north. The roadway itself is built on a raised earthen causeway, and at the bottom of the slope, under the boughs of the trees, there is a thick underbrush, which prevents entry into the woodland from this location.
11180: A sparrow is flapping around on the ground.

This wide road roughly traces the line of the Nen Kalthar, which flows from the west, toward the city of thieves. Here, a small hut stands beside the road, right on the banks of the river, and to the north, the roadway is bordered by a light forest.
11181: The road here follows the route chosen by the Nen Kalthar, which meanders lazily from the west, toward Tharbad, in the southeast, where it meets the mighty River Greyflood. To the north, a small, stony path leads into the outskirts of a thin forest, whose trees seem alive with birdsong.
11182: The road bends here, curving from the north to the east. Directly east you can see a ford, which crosses a small, but fast-flowing tributary, before it joins with the Nen Kalthar. Far north you can see a thin forest, with trees which do not grow very close together.
11183: A Ford on the Way to Tharbad

You have come to a well-built ford. Layers of rock have been placed here, to provide safe passage across a wide and fast-flowing stream. Although a few reeds have grown through the rocky base, the footing is still firm and only slightly slippery. The waters of the smaller tributary race and chase across the flat stones, then tumble over a slight drop, to meet the larger river to the south. Eastward the road climbs a slight rise, away from the ford.
11184: The road runs east to west here, along the edge of a grassy ridge. Standing by the roadside, you can see a treacherous drop to the south that plunges down into a steep gully. North, a muddy trail runs along the edge of a small river.
11185: Standing atop the brow of the hill, the road stretches west into the distance as it follows the contours of the river. Looking south, the road starts on a gentle downhill turn, flattening out as it approaches the bend at the bottom. Just north from here, a pleasant glade provides an ideal resting-place.
11187:
A fat carp swims here.
A bass swims here.
A fat carp swims here.

To the north stands a well-built but ancient ford, across which many generations of men must have passed. Here, a wide, fast-flowing stream joins the waters of the Nen Kalthar, as it makes its way east across the countryside.
11188: A short incline leads north towards a blind summit on the road, bordered by the trees on either side. Looking east, the road levels out as it winds into the distance. South of the road, a short drop leads down to the river's edge.
11189: The road here is pitted with holes and cracks in the soft ground, most likely due to the heavy coaches which frequently traverse the turnpike. A narrow trail departs the road to the east, heading off into the grassy fields. To the north a light forest shadows the road as it bends around to the west.
11190: The road twists through the scenic landscape, following a rough north to east direction. To the south and west, a muddy embankment leads down to the leisurely flowing river, winding its way through the countryside.
11191: Standing in the middle of the road you look around, surveying the surroundings. To the north, vast fields and plains spread out across the horizon, as far as the eye can see. South and west, the road continues its path through the countryside, while to the east, a gravel path leads up to a nearby tavern.
11192:
A rabbit is here eyeing your presence warily.
A hungry warg (Rood) is standing here, ridden by you.

A scattering of trees marks the edge of the road as it turns north and east, mirroring the path of the Nen Kalthar. Splashes of colour from the surrounding countryside, set against the vibrant river to the west, create a picturesque landscape.
11194: A clear spring babbles as cool water trickles out of the ground.

The road here is cracked and broken in places, partly due to the expansive roots from the surrounding trees, but also to the erosion caused by a small trickle of water that flows across the road from a nearby spring. The trees looming overhead cast long shadows across the road and the only sound to be heard is the constant burble of water into the spring.
11195: Partially sheltered by the bordering trees, the road bends around to the south and west. The road itself is very worn here, and rutted tracks filled with rainwater run along the roadside. Several large rocks have been recently placed in the middle of the road making an effective roadblock for any passing coaches.
11196: A Long Straight Stretch of the Road

The road here has fallen into disrepair, despite the fact that it is obviously used quite frequently. Perhaps as people grow closer to the city of thieves, they also grow less willing to tarry on the open road, where unseen eyes could easily spy upon their movements. The thoroughfare continues north and south from here.
11197: The hard-packed dirt road is rutted and a few rocks and stones litter the way, making it rather a perilous track to follow in any wheeled vehicle. Where further north, and closer to Bree, the road had been well-maintained, here it has been neglected for quite some time, judging by its appearance.
11198: A hungry warg (Rood) is standing here, ridden by you.

The road turns here, from west to south, as if trying to draw closer to the river. To the east it is bordered by a vast expanse of flatlands, but to the north a rough hedgerow of wild-looking bushes blocks the way, and the view, hiding whatever lies beyond from your sight.
11199: Just south of here a small stony path diverges from the road, then itself splits to lead both south and west. The main thoroughfare continues north and east, following its seemingly endless route between Tharbad, southeast of here, and the distant village of Bree, far to the north.
11200: Deep holes and ruts scar the road, as it scars the countryside in turn, cutting a path between Bree and Tharbad. Northward and eastward, the road is bordered by an open plain, affording no relief from the wind and weather.
11201: A hungry warg (Rood) is standing here, ridden by you.

The road journeys north and east from here, and is bordered to the west by a wild and unkempt hedgerow of thick and thorny shrubs. The surface of the roadway is in poor condition, ill-suited to travel in any wheeled vehicle, due to innumerable potholes and deep ruts, which now criss-cross the hard- packed dirt.
11202: The road here moves east-west, bordered on the north by grassy plains and by a stony bank in the south.
