Neither provide shelter or any form of relief from the summer sun, or from winter storms. The road itself is made of hard-packed dirt, and has fallen into some disrepair in this part of the country.
11203: A hungry warg (Rood) is standing here, ridden by you.

This rough dirt road filled with assorted loose stones seems to be in a sad state of repair. Though its ruts are shallow, its more numerous and much deeper pits make the road very bumpy. Any wheeled vehicle would be in for quite a ride as the road curves from west to south. Curiously, many tracks lead off the road into a narrow ditch east of here that catches your eye, maybe because it is a change in the bleak scenery of grassy plains that span out to the north.
11204: Not much distinguishes this section of road from the rest of the packed dirt, mixed stones and random pits that you see on the road that leads from Bree to Tharbad. A rocky bank to the west of here obstructs any clear view of the lands lying beyond in that direction, but to the south an expanse of fields and grassy lowlands can be seen.
11205: Yet again, the road changes its heading, now going west-south. From the north to the south-east, a plain stretches seemingly unobstructed as far as the eye can see, with the exception of a great forest occupying the lands several miles north of here.
11206: The old road gradually bends, evading the rough terrain to the west by taking a northern heading. East of here, the road continues towards Tharbad while going through vast plains. To the south the sound of rushing water can be heard as steep cliffs plunge into the river far below.
11207: A wiry smuggler is here, attempting to avoid being seen.

Going west and south, the road slowly descends an elevation in the terrain, eventually reaching the banks of the Nen Kalthar river some distance to the south. Although not in prime condition, the quality of the road seems to have improved somewhat compared to its state further north, suggesting that one might be getting closer to its destination, the infamous city of Tharbad.
11208: Twisting and turning, the road struggles on. To the south a strip of lush grassland lies between the road and the river, whilst to the west a light woodland borders the thoroughfare. The countryside here is quite flat, and in the distance to the southeast the walls of the city of Tharbad loom up above the land.
11209: The old road goes on, along the crest of a long slope which gradually descends to meet the churning waters of the Nen Kalthar south-west of here. The road itself shows evidence of frequent use - the heavy wagons travelling along it have left deep tracks, in some spots reducing the road into a muddy pool. Some half-hearted attempts to repair the worst sections have been made, yet it seems like the city is considered to be located too far from here to motivate any major effort.
11210: The road bends in a north-east curve, following the lines of a steep and grassy escarpment. To the west, the ground slopes down to the banks of the Nen Kalthar. Frequent use has taken its toll on the road, yet apparently some effort has been made at makeshift repairs, from time to time, as the thoroughfare remains good enough for travel on foot, on horseback, or in a coach or wagon.
11211: A steep escarpment to the north forces the road to turn from south to west as it makes its way between Tharbad and the far distant village of Bree. To the east, you can see a vast area of marshland, and the ground slowly begins its slope down towards the banks of the Nen Kalthar in the west.
11212: The roads sweeps from the north to the east, turning away from the nearby river. Loose cobblestones can be seen here and there, but the thoroughfare is in a fairly good state of repair. To the south, a thick natural hedgerow of shrubs and grasses borders the roadway, and offers a home to a variety of birds and small creatures, who are heard more often than seen.
11213: A Large Sign is standing here.

The road here stands slightly above the surrounding land, raised on a small causeway, presumably to protect it from floodwaters from the nearby rivers. At the bottom of a small incline, a narrow path meets the road then heads north and east, skirting the border of the marshes. To the south, the road approaches the gates to the city of Tharbad.
11214: Approaching the North Gate of Tharbad
A beggar is here, asking for a few coins.

Not far to the south, the forbidding gates of Tharbad can be seen, tall and imposing. The road here is made of interlocking granite slabs mortared with hard-packed dirt, and to either side of the road tall smooth walls climb high, as if funneling travellers toward the city gates. A heavy door of stout oak planks is set into the eastern wall, presumably leading to some sort of guard hut. Any traveller trapped here would be at the mercy of the denizens of Tharbad.
11215: Outside the North Gate of Tharbad
You are in front of a huge wooden gate. On the city wall, beside the gate, you notice a big sign. To the north, the road leads to the Shire, far away.
11216: A Small Bridge over the Nen Kalthar

A rickety wooden bridge crosses the river here. Built low and almost flat, this structure is so close to the surface of the water that in a heavy rain, a boat might be unable to pass beneath it, and indeed the entire construct could easily be washed away. With no rail, and much rot, the safety of this bridge must be open to question.
11217:
A brook trout is here, swimming in the current.
A bass swims here.
A fat carp swims here.

Southwest of here, a large square building can be seen, standing on the bank of the river. Just to the east, the course of the waterway has been diverted by the construction of a small, wooden boathouse, which forces the water to turn south, before regaining its eastward path.
11218:
A bass swims here.
A fat carp swims here.
A fat carp swims here.
A fat carp swims here.

West of here a large flat rock offers a low and easy landing place for small boats, and leads towards a large square building, which stands on the bank of the river. A small bridge leads from the road to this landing, suggesting that the building once saw trade of some sort, but now the area appears to be deserted.
11219: A wooden jetty projects onto the Nen Kalthar from the boathouse which stands just to the north. This old wooden construction has clearly seen better days, as is apparent from the rotting timbers, which occasionally break free, and float into the water here.
11220:
A fat carp swims here.
A bass swims here.

The river bends here, but it is not a natural bend. Rather, it is a curve made by men, engineered so that the banks will still hold firm, and resist erosion, so that the road to the east of here does not become flooded during heavy rains or other periods of high waters.
11221: The stony path makes a bend to the west here. It is a nice area around and the grass is wealthy and well grown. The bushes on the side of the path are small and with nice green leaves upon them. The sound of running water can be heard, it comes from the north, from the Nen Kalthar. The small bridge is to the north of here.
11222: The stony path makes a sharp bend here, continuing to the east and the south. Next to the path, the vegetation grows thick and lush, with many different flowers growing amid the long grass. The pathway itself is comprised of large flat stones, which were perhaps taken from the bed of the Nen Kalthar, which flows lazily through the countryside, just north of here.
11223: A colony of red ants is here. The ants seem to ignore you.

Thick bushes border the path to the east. High and thorny, they make travel in that direction quite impossible. A clump of trees stands to the south, where a small trail leads through a gap in the hedgerow, whilst the main path bends from north to west here. Far to the east, a mill can be seen.
11224: A dense carpet of blue flowers dip their heads in the breeze.

The path travels here through a small and peaceful glade, whose tall trees would offer welcome shade on a hot and sunny day. To the west the woodland becomes more dense, and thick undergrowth prevents you from leaving the path to travel in that direction. To the east, however, a gap in the tall hedgerow offers access to a well-tended garden.
11225: You are walking along a narrow, flower-lined path. To the north you can enter a peaceful glade, full of sweet-scented flowers and plants. To the east you can see a large green hedge enclosing a fairly large area, but you can't see what it is protecting from here. To the south-east you can see a wooden hut outlined against some green hills in the background.
11226: A brown fox is here, looking for some rabbits to chew up.

The path here is narrow and lined with flowers. It runs from the north to the south, where it then bends to the east. To the east of here you can see some wisps of smoke coming from the chimney of a small wooden hut, and beyond that you can see some small hills. Far to the north you can see a sparkle of water, and right at the range of vision there seems to be a green smudge which could be a forest of some description.
11227: From here you can clearly see that the path is leading to the wooden hut just east of here, and then it continues on up the gentle slopes of the hills beyond it. To the north-east you see a green hedge fencing something in, but you cant see through it. Small boulders line the path here, interspersed with flowers and coloured pebbles. To the west a smaller path leads toward a towering, and seemingly quite ancient, forest.
11228: The path here leads east and west. The path is lined by borders of dark, rich soil which has a fresh peaty smell. Far north of here you can see a sparkle of water, and beyond that the dark green of a forest. Close at hand you can smell the heady scent of many flowers, and also the faint aroma of cooking.
11229: A Path in Front of a Hut
A cluster of white star-shaped forget-me-nots flourish here in reminiscence.

The path here leads past a small wooden hut. The construction does not seem to be sophisticated, and yet the building seems quite sound. Flowering ivy climbs the walls, neatly framing the two windows which look out over this pathway, and roses border the structure, many different varieties blooming and growing in a harmony of colours, giving off a sweet perfume. To the right of the stout wooden door, a small golden plaque has been attached to the wall.
11230:
A raft has been left here.
On the ground, there are two canoes.

The interior of this small shed is dusty, and cobwebs seem to fill every nook and cranny. The large windows, set high in each wall, are so dirty that they let in no natural light, and the small landing to the south is built from timbers now so rotten that it is a wonder the jetty can still remain intact.
11231:
A fat carp swims here.
A bass swims here.
A trout swims here.

The banks of the river rise high here, to either side, confining it to a course chosen not by nature, but by the hand of man. Here the waters of the Nen Kalthar flow from the north, to the east, but to the south a small rocky creek diverts some of the waters into the rolling hills.
11232: The river here is confined by steep earthen banks, altering its natural course so that the roadway to the north might be pretected from rising waters in a flood. To the northeast, a well-built, yet ancient ford offers travellers a route across the fast-flowing tributary, which joins the Nen Kalthar just east of here.
11233:
A bass swims here.
A bass swims here.
A bass swims here.
A bass swims here.
A bass swims here.

The river bends around from the west to south here, where it flows into a steep walled gully. The deep, dark water carries you along with some vigour and it takes all you effort to avoid being tossed against the rockface.
11234:
A fat carp swims here.
A fat carp swims here.

Flowing from north to south, the river spills out into a wide channel as it emerges from the shadow of the gully. The high rocky banking on the western side prevents any progress in that direction, but it should be possible to pull yourself up to the muddy banking on the eastern side.
11235:
A fat carp swims here.
A fat carp swims here.
A bass swims here.

The river bends around a pebbled shoreline, widening out as it flows eastwards. The ice cold water is quite turbulent here as it flows over the rocky seabed, accompanied by a low roar. Through the crystal clear water, you can see many silvery fish darting about.
11236:
A swan swims gracefully on the surface of the water.
A swan swims gracefully on the surface of the water.

The river is quite shallow here as its path widens out to the soft, muddy banks that flank it on either side. Meandering slowly south, the undertowing current is nevertheless quite strong. The low embankment to the north and east provide a muddy scramble to the dry land.
11237:
A fat carp swims here.
A bass swims here.
A fat carp swims here.
A salmon swims here.

Coursing from north to east here, the river flows ever onward, its waters cutting into the low banks to the south, as they meander past. To the west, a pebbly shoreline reaches down to the water's edge, and gentle waves lap against the land, tossing some of the tiny stones back and forth. A fat carp swims here.
11238:
A bass swims here.
A fat carp swims here.
A bass swims here.

The river takes another twist here on its endless journey south. As the current swirls around, broken roots and stones are washed onto the northern bank. Looking downstream, the smashed remains of a small rowing boat lie beached at the river's edge.
11240: At a Bend in the River

A fat carp swims here.
A bass swims here.
A bass swims here.

The river makes a turn from north to east here. Although quite calm, the waters are deep, and too wide to jump across, so that the only way to get from one side to the other without a boat would be to swim. Small, silvery fish dart here and there, but somehow always manage to vanish from sight before they can be seen closely.
11241:
A bass swims here.
A bass swims here.

Here the river turns from the west to the south, and the current picks up a little pace. Small animals scurry along the shores, but the banks are high and steep, so these creatures quickly vanish from sight. Even the flat moss- covered rock, which dips its leading edge into the water, further to the north, now stands at some height above the river, as the channel cuts deeper into the land.
11243: The prominent fin of a silver-yellow fish breaks the surface of the water.

Turning from west to south, the swift river flows past the steep riverbanks covered with grass and leafy weeds that hang over the banks into the stream. The channel is growing wider here, and a number of massive boulders break the surface of the water.
11244: The prominent fin of a silver-yellow fish breaks the surface of the water.

The river flows from the north to the east. The current is stronger here, but it is still not so strong as to force you to follow the direction of flow, if you do not choose to do so. The banks to the south and west are steep and slippery - quite impossible to scale - and the view in those directions is all but obscured by the river bank. However, a tall and ancient stone tower can just be seen above the river bank.
11245: At a Bend in the River

The river continues its twisting, turning course across the countryside, here bending from the west to the south. The water seems to be quite deep. Luckily the eastern bank is low enough to climb. Far in the distance, the top of an old stone building can be seen above the tree-tops of the forest.
11246: A water moccasin slithers out of sight just below the surface of the water.

The water is deep here, but so clear that the riverbed can still be seen. As the river flows onwards through the countryside, it makes another sharp turn, this time from the north to the east. The low banks of the river south of here allow the river to flood the low grasslands there.
11247: A brook trout is here, swimming in the current.

The river travels onward across the countryside, turning here from west to south. Its banks are low, and the land slopes gently down toward the water, which has cut a wide channel over the years, so that the current is almost too slow to be observed.
11248: A brook trout is here, swimming in the current.

As the river flows onward toward Tharbad, it also draws closer to the tall, stone tower, which looms above the tree-tops to the south-west of here. The banks of the water are steep, muddy and slippery, and quite impossible to scale, so the only apparent option is to continue to follow the course of the waterway.
11249: The prominent fin of a silver-yellow fish breaks the surface of the water.

As the river flows south from here, it enters a wide pool. However, the water still flows onward, and remains fresh and clear, so the riverbed below is still quite visible. The banks here are low, and in the distance to the west, an old stone tower looms into view.
11250:
A swan swims gracefully on the surface of the water.
A swan swims gracefully on the surface of the water.
A brook trout is here, swimming in the current.
A bass swims here.
The prominent fin of a silver-yellow fish breaks the surface of the water.

The river widens out into a deep and massive pool here, and looking to the east it is easy to understand why, for there a sturdy dam has been built across the path of the waterway. The water spills and splashes across the top of it, to allow the river to continue its journey eastward, but the pool behind the dam seems calm and very deep.
11251: A surprisingly sturdy dam blocks the course of the river here, forcing the waters to pool behind it. Lazily the river spills over the top of the many timbers from which the dam has been constructed, continuing their journey eastward toward Tharbad.
11252: A brook trout is here, swimming in the current.

A steady flow of water splashes over the top of the dam to the west, kicking up sediment, and making this part of the river quite murky. The shorelines to either side of the waterway are steep and slick with mud, making these banks extremely difficult to negotiate.
11253: The Nen Kalthar is slowly flowing to the south. A wooden dam, which can be seen to the west, is stoping up the water and makes it calm and gentle. Steep shore- lines prevent you from climbing out of the water, so the only exits are west towards the dam, or to the south by following the river downstream.
11254: A brook trout is here, swimming in the current.

There is a sharp turn in the waterway here, as the Nen Kalthar turns to the east, from its previous southerly course. The riverbank to the south is quite steep, but stony, and numerous tree roots can be seen poking through, which might make it possible to climb to land, in the small woods to the south of the river.
11255:
A brook trout is here, swimming in the current.
A brook trout is here, swimming in the current.
A finch flies low above the ground.
A nightingale is here, chirping a sweet melody.
A robin is here, carrying small pieces of wood to its nest.

The turbulent waters of the river flow south from here, and the riverbanks to the north and west are steep and muddy. Sweeping onward, the river makes its way inexorably toward the mighty Greyflood, which can be seen to the southeast, near to the looming walls of the city of Tharbad.
11256: Strong currents often sweep any trespassers along, allowing little time to get a glimpse of the surroundings. Woods stretch to the very border of the river to the west, however, allowing a strong swimmer to reach the relative safety of solid ground.
11257: A brook trout is here, swimming in the current.

As the river cuts its way through the flat countryside, toward the south, its banks become lower and gentler. Further upstream the banks become steep and muddy as the land rises above the river. To the north, by climbing a low and sandy bank, an area of lush grassland lies between the river and an old road. To the east, the riverbank is topped by a thick, natural hedgerow so dense as to prevent travel in that direction.
11258: The current here is more intense than in the northern parts of the Nen Kalthar since you are close to the river Greyflood. You see flat land to your west and south. A little further downstream is the ancient city of Tharbad, but the area around here does not seem very populous.
11259: The river winds southward here through flat, muddy land, strewn with branches and leafless trunks from earlier floods. To the east is the ancient city of Tharbad, raised up on its mounds of debris and its old and rotting pilings.
11260: The river winds south across a muddy floodplain. On the west bank are some poorly drained but fertile enough fields. Eastward can be seen the ancient Port of Tharbad, and the broad River Greyflood flowing unhurriedly toward the distant sea.
11261: Here the comparatively clear waters of the Nen Kalthar, flowing south from the plains of Minhiriath, are absorbed by the great muddy torrent of the Gwathlo, or Greyflood. Its water is murky, and, having taken unto itself the wastes of the city of Tharbad just upstream, rather smelly as well; unpleasant lumps float upon the flood. There are few fish here, and the banks are covered with debris.
11262: The broad river forms a great, almost stagnant pool here as it struggles to absorb the waters of the Nen Kalthar to the west. The water is not terribly deep, but is extraordinarily dirty and not very healthy looking either. There are some dead fish rotting along the banks.
11263: A hungry warg stands here, sniffing around for flesh.

The broad, grey-brown river flows slowly toward the distant sea. The bank to the south and east is low, muddy, but easily climbable. Occasionally a bird will flap down from above and attempt to snatch a fish from the water. A few miles to the north is the old city of Tharbad, of which so many stories have been told.
11264: There is not much happening here and it's quiet except for the lapping sound of the water. Water is all around you, serving as a nice place for fish to dwell in. However, you think you can see some land far northwest and southeast.
11265:
A salmon swims here.
A sparrow is flapping around on the ground.

The brown water of the Greyflood, pungent with the 'gifts' bestowed on it by the population of Tharbad, flows slowly southwestward. Broad and slow here, miles wide, it seems placid and unthreatening at the moment; but when it floods, it must threaten disaster to anyone living or farming along its banks.
11266:
A salmon swims here.
A salmon swims here.
A salmon swims here.
Looking down in the water you see some fish, swimming fast away, frightened by your presence. You see more of the river looking north, east and south. To the west you can see some very high grass.
11267: In the river Greyflood, the water reflects the images you see before you like a large blurry mirror. Looking north, west and south you can see more of this mirror-like water. East there are some kind of plains.
11268: You must be in the middle of the river Gwathlo, as it is also called. Water is in every direction you look. Peering down you see fish swimming in the clear water. The current will soon take you south or west.
11269: The great brown river flows lazily towards the southwest. It is shallow here; the main channel is to the south. The banks here are grassy and fertile. To the southwest, a sort of mound or bluff can be seen.
11270: You're in the middle of the river Greyflood. In all directions you see water and more water. However, looking around you, you can see something rising above the surface to the northwest.
11271: This part of the Greyflood runs slowly past the southern bank. The shore is flat and entangled with thick brush, reeds, and cattails. A few sunken bridges lie rotting just below the surface in the reeds. The occasional splash of a fish interrupts the solemn sound of the river flowing.
11272: The river flows south here below a steeply cut bank. Above it is a rocky hill or pile of stones, whose bare surface can be seen above the tops of the foliage of the steep shore. To the south the water foams downward over great boulders; droplets of spray rise up, and there is a booming sound.
11273: This is where the main channel of Greyflood flows over some rocky outcroppings in fierce and dangerous rapids. A thick mist limits visibility, and you can barely outline the silhouette of a cliff far south, and the shores on the northern and southeastern sides. Everywhere whirlpools and undertows lurk between the rocks, ready to drag you down into the dark water.
11274: The water flows quickly here past a brushy riverbank to the south. East of here the bank is flat and muddy. To the west the surface of the river looks strange and uneven; a rushing sound comes from that way, and a mist obscures your view.
11275: The Greyflood makes a sharp turn west here and disappears below a rocky ledge. The water is foamy and wild, creating a haze in the air. To the north the water is even more upset, passing some heavy rapids. East of here is some marshy, brush-covered ground, and to the south a bluff rises from the riverside.
11276: A colony of red ants is here. The ants seem to ignore you.

The field slopes gently down toward the river, and is covered by waves of lush green grass. Here and there, clusters of beautifully coloured flowers can be seen, scattered among the grass, their heads bobbing in the light breeze.
11277:
A large thorny branched shrub is growing here.
On the shrub, there are five piles of blackberries.
A nightingale is here, chirping a sweet melody.

A few green berry bushes are growing here, and there is a pattern to their growth that aligns with a nearby white fence. The stems of the bushes have small, sharp thorns on them, becoming a minor annoyance to walk through. An old wooden fence borders the patch on three sides, leaving it open only to the east. However several of its planks seem to be quite loose.
11278: In the Outskirts of the Forest

Thick vegetation fills this area, which is bounded to the north by an old wooden fence. To the south and the east, the vegetation is so thick that it is impossible to force a way through the thorny bushes, but to the west, it might be possible to find a way deeper into the woodland.
11279: Some thick writhing vines whip all around you.

There are thick roots and vines spread all over the ground, which makes it almost impossible to pass through this area, and tall trees form a canopy overhead. Large bushes and shrubs choke the whole area, and it is quite impossible to tell what lies very far ahead.
11280: At the Edge of the Forest

A tree-snake lies wrapped around one of the tree branches.
A tree-snake lies wrapped around one of the tree branches.

The forest is thinning a little here, and it is finally possible to struggle into the thick undergrowth to the north. A lone tree here seems to rustle and creek more than those deep in the heart of the forest, with many of its leaves fluttering to the ground below.
11281: A woodpecker is here, tapping on a tree.

Most of the trees in this forest are extremely large, however, the one that stands here does not seem to be like the others. It has not grown very tall, and its trunk seems to have grown around itself, making it look extremely twisted. At the base of the tree, the tangled roots and rotten leaves seem to obscure a small hole.
11282: There are three piles of wheat cereals here.

Wheat grows in abundance in this field, some of which seems ready to be harvested. A fence borders the fields, with berry bushes climbing up the fence in the west. Another field, filled with corn, stands in the north, with a small house nearby.
11283: Like the wheat field, there is nothing more than a field of corn. A tall scarecrow stands in the middle of the field, fending off crows to no avail. Much of the corn in the field has been eaten, or knocked onto the ground. Corn stalks lie everywhere around the ground, and along the fence. To the north, the babbling river can be heard.
11284:
A brown cow is here, contemplating a higher reality whilst chewing slowly.
A brown cow is here, contemplating a higher reality whilst chewing slowly.
A black crow flies low to the ground here, looking for carrion to eat.

Some hay is piled up against the fence, covering part of it from view. The ground here is muddy and there are many hoof prints embedded in it. A sound of clanking bells can be heard coming from somewhere around here. The farm house can be easily seen now, as smoke rises from a small chimney atop the slate roof.
11285: A black crow flies low to the ground here, looking for carrion to eat.

Smoke can be seen curling up from the chimney atop a farm house, slowly drifting over and across the top of a large barn nearby. A small path leads back through the fields, toward the river, with tall grass marking the boundary of the trail. The wind blows across the grassy field making it look like an endless sea on land.
11286: This well worn trail runs through an endless field of grass, stretching off into the distance. To the north you can see a large pile of grey, moss- covered rocks, which block the route to the Nen Kalthar.
11287: A black crow flies low to the ground here, looking for carrion to eat.

Lush grasses grow tall throughout the area, and a few small trees stand to the west, overshadowing some small bushes. The soft, almost musical sound of the river hangs in the air, accompanying the freshness of the water. To the south, the rooftop of a small house can be spied.
11288:
There are three loaves of bread here.
Farmer Rushlight's wife screams about people interrupting her work.
Farmer Rushlight is standing here, taking a break from his tedious work.
A small bat is standing here.

A tiny square window is set above an old kitchen sink along one wall of the room. The kitchen cabinets end in the back corner of the house, where a large box, filled with firewood, stands. A large fireplace dominates the middle of the room, its hot coals spewing smoke, which rises and curls, seeming to caress an antique sword, hanging high above the mantle. Small chairs, with seats woven of straw, stand in the centre of the floor.
11289:
A stocky mountain mule is here, waiting to serve.
A mouse is here nosing around, looking for a safe place to hide.
A brown donkey watches the surroundings, perhaps looking for a chance to graze.
A sturdy pack horse is standing here.
A mouse is here nosing around, looking for a safe place to hide.
A domesticated pony, beast of burden to many, stands here.

Stalls line the sides of the barn, with a huge loft looming overhead. Bales of hay lie stacked in lines and rows along the edge of the loft up above. The smells of a farm are very evident here, with many different animal droppings littering the ground. An old lantern hangs from a nail in a rail overhead, at about the right height for a human farmer.
11290:
There are two turnips here.
A large beautiful rose bush is blooming here.
Deep inside the bush, there are two red roses with leaves and thorny stems.
A hen is trying to pick some grains here.
A hen is trying to pick some grains here.
A hen is trying to pick some grains here.
A garden snake slithers harmlessly here.

This stony farmyard must once have been quite pretty, with borders of rose bushes set along the fence to the south. But now all is overgrown and the red painted boards of the house, and its white eaves are now chipped and peeling. One window stands broken in its frame. To the north lies the bank of the Nen Kalthar, whilst a stony pathway leads eastward.
11291: A black crow flies low to the ground here, looking for carrion to eat.

A neat path of small stones makes it easy to travel here. To the north and south, beyond tall hedges, endless plains, covered with thick green grass, can be seen, and the hedgerow itself is made up of thick bushes, with soft green leaves and tiny red berries. The path stretches east and west.
11292: On the Bank of the Nen Kalthar

A robin is here, carrying small pieces of wood to its nest.
A robin is here, carrying small pieces of wood to its nest.

This is a well grown sandy bank which is bordering the Nen Kalthar. There are some small bushes on one side of the bank, they are green with thick leaves and they have some small red berries on them. Further up on the bank there is nice soft green grass, a perfect spot to lay down and feel the air from the river.
11293:
A bright red mushroom is growing here.
There are three mushrooms here.
A domesticated pony, beast of burden to many, stands here.

A small field lies fallow before an old barn, bordered on the south and west by a rotting wooden fence. The grass underfoot has an unwholesome appearance, which has probably resulted from the encroaching trees of the ancient woodland, which stands to the south. There lies a dense and unpassable underbrush, above which the massive trees loom.
11294: A woodpecker is here, tapping on a tree.

Of the many tall trees that fill these woods, one stands particularly high. It has a huge base with the size of a large cabin, the branches themselves are the size of small trees. Further within the forest, towards the west, trees identical to this one loom in abundance. The sky is masked from sight with the large branches and leaves.
11295: A tall pine tree grows here.

The trees around here have grown closer to the ground than they do in other areas within the forest. Their branches almost touch the ground, and in some spots there are marks from where they have scraped the ground, pushed by the wind. The grass has grown a little higher here, from the water that is trapped on the forest floor during rainy seasons.
11296:
A tall pine tree grows here.
A grey wolf is here, thin from starvation.

The ground here is cooled by both the air that caresses it, and the lush green grass that catches each morning's dew. There is little to see here, other than a variety of trees, with every branch, twig, and leaf looking exactly like all the others.
11297: A tall pine tree grows here.

A small hill slopes up here, covered with grass and the roots of trees that grow at an angle along the hill. There is a small hole at the base of the incline, almost covered by two tree trunks growing near each other. A few wild flowers grow across the side of the hill, their purple petals and long green stems blending beautifully with the colour of the leaves on the trees.
11298:
A tall pine tree grows here.
A cute rabbit is here.

The few scattered trees of the pathway have now closed in to form a giant forest. The air seems almost still, but for a gentle breeze, which rustles amongst the branches. Where once the path was grassy, now you stand upon ground littered with dead twigs, and decaying leaves, and interrupted in places by large, twisted roots, which protrude from the earth.
11299: A tall pine tree grows here.

A haunting chime can be heard as a breeze slowly picks up through the branches of the trees. The sign at the entrance of this forest may have some truth in it as a definite sound seems to emanate from nowhere. Branches from many different trees also have grown closer and closer towards the ground, almost touching it.
11300: One tree stands out among the rest in this area of the forest, it has large branches with many different kinds of coloured leaves. The ground below it is covered with the large seeds of its making. Foliage from the tree covers the area completely, obscuring any sight of the sky, and the roots of the tree are almost as thick as its branches, spreading out to some distance, to soak up every drop of available water. No bush or sapling can compete with this giant, which stands alone, and majestic.
11301:
A small plant grows here, with long, pointed leaves and flowers at its top.
A grey wolf is here, thin from starvation.
A black wolf pads restlessly, looking for its next prey.

Woods that once were so close, it was difficult to distinguish which branch grew from which tree, now have opened up to reveal the sky. The forest has formed a circle where no foliage dare enter. Grass closely hugs the border of the circle, making the boundary even more defined. All living beings within this forest avoid this area, as if it were somehow held sacred.
11302: The path within the woods ends at the base of a large tree, or so it would seem. The forest is so closely knitted that it is difficult to determine where the path may actually have gone. The sky is blocked slightly from view by the large trees and their branches with beautiful green and brown leaves.
11303: A woodpecker is here, tapping on a tree.

A large tree stands almost as a silhoutte here, with large green and brown leaves covering it entirely. The woodland behind grows even denser, the deeper one penetrates the forest, and a number of large branches lie on the ground here, perhaps brought down by some heavy wind.
11304: A woman stands here carefully guarding her village.

The woods continue to grow close together and crowd in on each other. This, and the dense foliage, make it difficult to tell what is up within the trees. A few notches have been carved here in the bark of the tree, like an ancient hand hold in a mountainside.
11305: A woman stands here carefully guarding her village.

The woodland is filled with trees, that are extremely close to one another. This forest has the look of being long left untouched, except for some marks on the trees. A sound is present that resembles a moan caused by wind rustling through branches.
11306: There seems to be no light entering this part of the woods. Trees have covered all the land here with their large branches and their many leaves. The grass on the ground is moist with the water that is trapped from evaporating with a morning sun.
11307: A woodpecker is here, tapping on a tree.

A couple of trees stand here close together, with their branches so interwined that they look like they are hugging. Another tree stands alone however, with its dead leaves and dead trunk. The other parts of the woodland keep a fair distance from this dead and strangely large tree.
11308: Parts of the interior of this tree are dead and decaying, giving off a rank odour. However, there is sufficient living wood remaining to maintain a strong structure, despite the rotting leaf litter and dead limbs, which lie all over the floor.
11309: A tall pine tree grows here.

The branches high up in the trees are rustling around much more than they did before, with the growing wind slapping them. Sounds can be heard coming from way up within the trees, however it is difficult to distinguish what the noises are. Many leaves lie on the ground, yet, there are many more up in the trees that make it impossible to see what is up there.
11310: Many noises can be heard coming from above, within the large foliage of the forest. Dangling from a branch, there appear to be some wooden pipes tied together, with holes in them. The small breeze that moves through them creates the most eerie noises. It is nothing more than a child's wind chime toy.
11311:
A dented pail has been carelessly left here.
A large grocer is here, waiting to buy or sell some goods.
A little boy is here, running around.
A woman is here, looking for someone to chat with.

Many different items sit in this room on shelves supported by branches of the tree. There are a few larger items that rest on the floor beside a large counter that stands in the middle of the room. There is a board on the counter that lists many prices of different things, however, they have been erased and rewritten so many times, it is difficult to tell what may be written on them.
11312: A woman stands here carefully guarding her village.

The bridge is well tied, with many thick and well made ropes wrapped around the different trees of the village. The rather narrow bridge makes passage tricky, though it does not wobble in the wind. One board, in the middle, creaks softly when pressure is upon it.
11313: There are a lot of wooden planks transformed into a platform in these huge crowded trees. The ground is far below, and small forest animals go about the trees unaware of the village above. A rope bridge connects the trees to small homes made of wood. The branches and leaves of the tree conceal it from below. The wooden rail along the platform disappears as three rope bridges begin to the north, south and west.
11314: A woman stands here carefully guarding her village.

Aloft high in the tree, constructed of a few small boards, stands a small perch. Like a bird's nest, the entire village can be seen from this height, including some of the houses that from below cannot be found. Branches criss and cross below here, making a natural ladder, with a square made out of rope as the only guard rail for an experienced tree climber. The entire forest, and most of the village can be seen and watched from up within this high tree.
11315:
A coil of rope is lying here.
A dented pail has been carelessly left here.
A grey wolf fur is here lying on the ground.

Animal furs hang along the walls of the home, their fur now only a decoration. A large bear skin lies on the floor near the entrance, its mouth grimly shut and facing the door. A window along the north side exposes the ground below, however the branches and leaves provide excellent cover.
11316: The bridge has many boards tied together tightly, creating a very sturdy, and well made bridge. The wood is painted a greenish and brownish colour, most likely to make it nearly invisibile to the ground below. There are many ropes tied to different branches to keep it very sturdy. The rail is a thick rope wrapped around the trunk of two trees.
11317: A small loyal cat is here.

A large bed made of furs lies in one of the corners of the room, with a large goose down pillow and many smaller ones piled up on top of it. A large bow and quiver rests neatly in the opposite corner of the house, with arrows that have beautifully coloured feathers within them. Branches run up along the back wall, providing more evidence that the house is supported solely by the trees.
11318:
A dented pail has been carelessly left here.
The baker looks at you calmly, wiping flour from his face with one hand.
A woman is here, looking for someone to chat with.

A large oven is embedded in the side of possibly the largest tree in this forest. Its bricks have decayed from a bright red colour, to one of blackened grey. There are pastries, wrapped delicately, sitting on shelves. A small chair and table sit beside the door of the house. The smells coming from the house have a taste in the mouth like that of fresh bread, pies, and cakes.
11319: There are wooden floors of different sizes, heights, and shapes all over this tree. A small building is supported among the massive branches to the north, whilst to the south and east, rope bridges reach out toward the nearby trees. Along the platform and the bridges are rails of soft wood, supported by interlocking branches, and tightly bound ropes.
11320: An intersection stands within the trees, made with tightly bound ropes and sturdy wood for the bridge. Buildings clutter all the trees nearby, with many rope bridges connecting them. The ground seems a far cry down below, with the branches of trees around it concealing it almost totally from sight. A large tree looms towards the west, its massive dead branches appear to be barely hanging onto it.
11321: A woman stands here carefully guarding her village.

Unlike most of the others in this part of the forest, this tree is quite unhealthy. Much of the wood is dead and some decaying, yet enough of the living heartwood remains, to maintain a strong platform, among the sagging branches. Nevertheless, much of the coarse bark on the trunk is peeling as if diseased.
11322: The platform is wide enough for many people to stand upon, with wooden rails enclosing it. This wooden structure is attached to an extremely large tree, and nearby, in another large oak, a building nestles among the branches. The leaves all around rustle in the soft wind, and the ground below cannot be seen through the thick foliage. Indeed, this place must be well hidden from the forest floor.
11323:
An old tailor is sitting here, working with a piece of fabric.
A woman is here, looking for someone to chat with.

Furs of many different animals hang from hooks in the wall, while, along the opposite wall, animal skins and leather lie on shelves. A large counter, with a wooden board hanging on the front, sits in the middle of the room. The board lists many prices of different items for sale, however, prices have been crossed out and new ones put in their place so many times, that it is difficult to read them.
11324: A woman is here, looking for someone to chat with.

The rope bridge makes a turn in mid air, creating an artwork of tied rope to keep it sturdy. It links a couple of different trees together, and with the extremely intricate rope pattern, allows for the bridge to change its course without having to find yet another tree. Even in fairly strong winds, the bridge hardly sways at all.
11325: The bridge has many boards tied together tightly, creating a very sturdy, and well made bridge. The wood is painted a greenish and brownish colour, most likely to make it nearly invisibile to the ground below. There are many ropes tied to different branches to keep it very sturdy. The rail is a thick rope wrapped around the trunk of two trees.
11326: A dented pail has been carelessly left here.

A few chairs stand in the middle of the room, facing some paintings that hang along the wall depicting the building of the village. A wolf skin covers the floor, greeting people as they walk in. Hanging in a corner is a lit lantern, with a small bucket of water sitting beneath it. The light from the lantern flickers on the wall, making the most beautiful dances.
11327:
A brown fox is here, looking for some rabbits to chew up.
A sturdy pack horse is standing here.
A grey wolf is here, thin from starvation.

The hole does not go back very far, but the rear seems to be a small fox den. Tiny bones clutter the corners, with a few pieces of fur left almong them, and tiny claw marks can be seen all over the ground, among the stout roots, which break through the soil and stretch up to the roof of the chamber. It would seem that the tree roots are the only thing which maintains the roof of this tiny earthy hollow.
11328:
A bear is here, covered with coarse black fur.
A robin is here, carrying small pieces of wood to its nest.

The ground above has rotted away from beside the tree to reveal this small hole. The carcass of a rotting animal along with the smell of rotten tree limbs and leaves, makes the overall smell of the hole very pungent. A few wild flowers grow along the sides near the top of the hole, hiding the outside from view.
11329: The End of the Garden Path

Herb: red rose x 2
Herb: violet orchid
Herb: ivory rose
Herb: white rose x 2

A large beautiful rose bush is blooming here.
Deep inside the bush, there is a red rose with leaves and thorny stem.
An orchid of light violet petals blossoms nearby.
A beautiful, ivory coloured rose with a tint of crimson is blossoming here.
A large beautiful rose bush is blooming here.
Deep inside the bush, there are a red rose with leaves and thorny stem and two white roses with leaves and thorny stems.

The path has led you to the most exquisite rose garden you have ever seen, where roses of all kinds grow and flower in abundance, creating an impression both natural and yet carefully planned. The different scents mingle into a heavy perfume, which has an almost relaxing effect, and all around, delicate trellises support climbing flowers, whose heads nod in the gentle breeze.
11330: A Path in a Well-tended Garden

The smells of many different flowers and shrubs peacefully assail you. The sharp tang of sap reminds you of the trees offering shade to both plants and the weary traveller. The path here leads north east or south. In the south it seems to end under a wooden trellis archway hung with roses and other climbing plants.
11331:
On the ground, there are two mince-pies.
You see two pork-pies on the ground.
A stove stands against one wall here.
There are two loaves of bread here.
A large stone fireplace with a roaring fire warms the room.

You are standing in the middle of a cosy and well-proportioned room. The furnishings are simple, but tasteful, and crafted skillfully, to enhance the beauty of their surroundings. To your right is a fireplace, with a simple stove, which must be the source of the smoke that could be seen from afar, and a half-circle of comfortable chairs have been set in front of this, as if to welcome visitors at any time.
11332: A Path in a Well-tended Garden

A small white fountain is here.
A cluster of white star-shaped forget-me-nots flourish here in reminiscence.
A cute rabbit is here.
A colourful butterfly is fluttering around here.

The flowers here are mostly shades of purple and yellow, and seem to be planted in shapes and patterns which look vaguely familiar. The path leads in all directions except south, where a large green hedge signifies the end of the garden. Beyond the hedge you catch a glimpse of a wooden hut. You can hear the sounds of someone working nearby.
11333: A Path in a Well-tended Garden

An apple tree with bright green leaves grows here.
On the tree's branches are four apples.
An apple tree with bright green leaves grows here.

The path here leads south and west, winding among many beds of flowers and small stands of trees. Some of the flower beds have been artfully arranged so as to make patterns, with one immediately adjacent to the path a perfect resemblance of a small white cat, lazing in a grassy carpet.
11334: A Path in a Well-tended Garden
A nightingale is here, chirping a sweet melody.

The tall hedge enclosing this marvellous garden surrounds you on three sides here. Thick and lush, there is no way through this barrier and so you are obliged to tread the gravel pathway, which leads north from here. However, to the west, a curl of smoke can be seen riding from a small building which stands beyond the hedgerow.
11335: The hills undulate gently here, rising to the north and dropping to the east and south. From the west a faint breeze blows, bringing with it the scent of flowers and freshly cut grass. In the east you can see the hills dropping down to the bank of a small creek, and beyond this you can see the sparkle of water. Far in the north you think you can see a dark smudge of green.
11336: A large rabbit looks peacefully at you, ready to dart away.

The hills here stretch east and south, a rocky slope to the north and to the west prevent further travel in those directions. However, beyond this slope, to the west, a high hedge can be seen, beyond which a well-tended garden has been laid out. Just south of this, a wisp of smoke can be seen, rising from the chimney of a small wooden hut.
11337: The hills spread south and west here, a steep rock-strewn slope preventing you from making a descent to the east or north. To the east, a small rocky creek can be seen, and further distant still, this meets with the Nen Kalthar, which flows from west to east, across the countryside. Far to the north, beyond a wide roadway, a large woodland can be seen.
11338: A large rabbit looks peacefully at you, ready to dart away.

The hills here dip down to a pebbled bank in the east. To the north and west you can climb the slight slope up the hills, to see what lies beyond. The grass underfoot is lush and green, and smells as fresh as morning dew. Pretty flowers grow all around, peeping from under rocks or standing, proud and alone in the field of green.
11339:
On the ground, there are two slender-stemmed plants, with brown heads.
A light boat made of reeds has been left here.
A robin is here, carrying small pieces of wood to its nest.

Brightly coloured pebbles and small rocks comprise the shoreline of a narrow inlet, whose calm waters seem fresh and clear. To the west, a small trail leads into some low, rolling hills, whilst east of here a range of high hills climb far above you.
11340: To the north, the Nen Kalthar makes its way aross the countryside, flowing ever eastward. However, the waters of this small, rocky inlet are all but motionless, and yet still fresh and clear. The footing is made somewhat treacherous by the large rocks and small pebbles which cover the bed of this creek.
11341:
A trout swims here.
A bass swims here.
A fat carp swims here.
A fat carp swims here.

The tranquil waters of this small, rocky creek are clear and fresh, despite the fact that there is almost no current here. To the south, a sandy pebbly shore gently upward, offering easy access to the rolling hills beyond, whilst to the northeast, this tiny inlet joins the waters of the Nen Kalthar.
11342: A Path in a Well-tended Garden
A colourful butterfly is fluttering around here.

The size of this garden never ceases to amaze. Nor does the wide variety of flora growing here quite contentedly. Surely the person in charge of this garden is a master of his craft, for no other could coax plants from all the different areas of Arda to grow together in perfect complement to each other. The hedge bounds the garden on the north and east, so you can only follow the path to the south and west.
11343: A Path in a Well-tended Garden

A robin is here, carrying small pieces of wood to its nest.
A nightingale is here, chirping a sweet melody.

You look around you, and everywhere you look all you can see is trees, flowers and shrubs of many different sizes shapes and colours. This garden is surely one of the most beautiful you are ever likely to see. The soil looks rich, dark and moist, willing to lend succour to any plant which may be placed here. There is a marked path leading through the garden, and you should be careful not to stray from it, so as not to anger anyone by trampling the plants.
11344:
A huge, hungry-looking rat is here.
A tiny spider is here, eating a tiny bug.
A tiny spider is here, eating a tiny bug.

In the middle of the north wall of the room stands a large waterwheel, made of aged oak, with fourteen hefty spokes. Flour has gathered in the corners and along the walls, and also in small gaps in the floorboards. Close to the west wall, a wooden stairway once led to the upper level of the mill, but this has long since decayed beyond use.
11345: A raft has been left here.

A large, flat rock makes a stable landing place and a useful roadway to the mill, which stands just to the west of here. To the north, a small, rickety bridge links this area to the roadway, which cuts from east to west across the land. Beyond the road, a small farm can be seen far in the distance, nestling in the eaves of a large woodland.
11346: A large flat rock protrudes from the riverbank just south of here, forcing the waters to continue eastward, though a little further downstream they turn again to the south. A small, wooden bridge spans the river here, reaching from the wide road to the north, toward the rocky prominence, barely rising high enough above the waters to permit passage of even a small boat.
11347:
A water moccasin slithers out of sight just below the surface of the water.
A water moccasin slithers out of sight just below the surface of the water.
A water moccasin slithers out of sight just below the surface of the water.

A stout, but narrow bridge, made of smooth blue-grey stones, arches smoothly above your head here, spanning the river. Grey-green moss peppers the surface of the stones, which have been dampened by the splashing water, as the Nen Kalthar progresses eastward, toward the city of Tharbad.
11348:
A large rabbit looks peacefully at you, ready to dart away.
A brown fox is here, looking for some rabbits to chew up.
A large rabbit looks peacefully at you, ready to dart away.

You are walking along some softly sloping hills. The grass underfoot is lush and green, and pretty flowers grow in abundance. The slope goes down to the west, leading to a small path, which goes past a wooden hut and then splits into two parts. To the east, the hill gets steeper, affording a good view all around.
11349: A sparrow is flapping around on the ground.

Low hills rise and fall, to the north and west of here, whilst to the east a range of higher hills looms above you. The hillside here is carpeted in lush, green grass, and a few small flowers, scattered here and there, add a splash of colour to the scene.
11350:
A wooden chest stands in the corner.
A small bat is standing here.

The boards in the attic creak heavily with each step taken up the stairs. The attic has very little light coming in from its one small window. There are many boxes piled up in the corner of the attic, and a few small rats can be heard squeaking around in the darkness. The air smells of the staleness this room has to offer.
11351: The air has been standing still in here for ages and smells rotten. This room is very small and dust lies towards the walls and all over the floor. A wooden bench stands towards the southern wall, one of its sides has broken and it has only 3 legs left. A small square hole can be seen in the ceiling but it is not big enough to light up the attic.
11352:
A large stone chest is here.
An experienced husky smuggler is here, plotting his illicit ventures.
An experienced husky smuggler is here, plotting his illicit ventures.
An experienced husky smuggler is here, plotting his illicit ventures.

A large cavern lies hidden here, hacked painstakingly out of the solid rock which makes up the riverbank. The digging was obviously done with little sophistication or skill, for the walls and ceiling are rough and unfinished, and only the floor is smooth. The dim light of a torch flickers from a high recess in one of the walls.
11356: A woolly sheep is grazing here.

Far to the north, you can glimpse the sparkling waters of the Nen Kalthar, as it meanders across the land, on its endless journey toward the ocean, but from here, no sound of its splashing waters can be heard. The howl of the wind is dominant on this high hillside, where a faint trail leads onward, east and south.
11357: A woolly sheep is grazing here.

You stand here in the shadow of the highest hill in the vicinity. Rising tall behind you it looks as though it could afford a good view of your surroundings. Even from here, you can see the silver ribbon of the Nen Kalthar stretching from the north-east to several leagues east of here. A faint path goes east and west here, leading upwards towards the peak of the hill behind you.
11358: The ground here is grassy and firm, but rocks are strewn about, making it rather risky to walk here without paying attention to your path. However, a clear trail can be seen, which hugs the lower slopes of one of the tallest hills, as it makes its way west and south across the countryside from here.
11360:
A neat straw pallet is lying here.
A wooden chest stands in the corner.

The interior of this small building is as dilapidated as it seemed from the outside. Small chinks in the wooden walls let the cold air stream in, and a few stained patches on the aging floorboards show where water has leaked in through the roughly thatched roof. But, despite the slight disrepair, it would seem that this place still sees frequent use, judging by the lack of dust or cobwebs.
11361: On a Winding Path to the Hills

Although the ground here is grassy and firm, it slopes rather severely in some places, and is littered with small rocks and stones. A narrow path can be seen, winding up into the hills to the north, and descending east toward the banks of a sparkling river.
11362: A pebbled shoreline stretches down from the grassy fields, where it meets the river's edge, lapping gently against the slope. The damp shingle slides about underfoot, leaving skewed footprints behind. Looking across the river, you can see the Road to Tharbad in the distance, a narrow ribbon running across the lowlands.
11363: Yellow flowers, with grey-green foliage, grow in clusters here.

Long lush grasses cover this gentle slope, which streches down towards the shoreline of a small, but lively river. Further north and west from here, the land rises more steeply, entering a narrow band of hills, but to the east lie only lowlands, the sprawling delta where the Swanfleet and the mighty river Hoarwell meet at the city of Tharbad.
11364: A Low Bank on the Nen Kalthar

A small cluster of clover grows here.
A cute rabbit is here.

The low banks of the river are covered in deep, thick grass and many wild flowers, fed by the ever-present waters, which sweep from north to east. Further south, the land rises slightly, climbing above the level of the water, but to the north and east all that can be seen are endless lowlands.
11365:
A hunter, holding a handaxe, is resting here.
A restless rabbit bounces around.

The banks here stand at quite some height above the flowing waters of the shining river, which feeds the rich grasslands of this area. Looking across the waterway, the road to Tharbad looms in the distance, cutting a dark scar across the countryside, which stretches low and flat as far as the eye can see. Not far from the shoreline the thick grass has been trampled down, as it approaches the entrance to a small shack. It would appear that this humble building still sees regular use.
11368:
A cluster of dark green, feathery fronds flourishes in the shade.
A forest spider is here crawling around.
A forest spider is here crawling around.

This small path leads toward a small, but dark forest to the south. From a distance the woods did not look dense, but here the trees loom above you, with an almost threatening air. As it heads south, the path is soon lost from sight amongst the undergrowth, and it seems that it would be all too easy to lose ones way among those ancient trees. However, a fainter trail can be seen travelling north through a lush green hollow.
11369: A large rabbit looks peacefully at you, ready to dart away.

Travelling from east to west, this small stony path leads from the river towards the border of a small woodland. Some way to the northwest an old building can be seen, and to the south, at the edge of the woods, many massive tree stumps litter the land.
11370: The gravel path coming from the west meets an incredibly large felled tree that spans the river to the east of here. You can see the old washed-out stone ford at the bottom of the steep slope beneath you. To the north, the river bank is steep and muddy, probably impossible to scale from the waters below.
11372: On a Path to the River

This trail is pleasant to travel upon, and you can see many small, tiny footprints on the ground. To the north you can see a well-travelled road beyond a weedy field. The path continues east, and west you can see a large tree bridge across the Nen Kalthar. The ground slopes down toward the river.
11373: Thick dark green weeds grow in abundance here in a wide field that gently slopes from the road north and east of here toward the river where the banks abruptly change to a very steep slope. In the south, a path leads toward an old river crossing.
11374:
A tall plant grows here, with grey-green leaves and grey flowers.
A tall plant grows here, with grey-green leaves and grey flowers.

At some height above the river, the soil on the banks here is nonetheless quite moist, and the grass and weeds grow thick and strong. Leafy weeds and small shrubs hang into the river, their branches trailing in the waters that flow inexorably by, as the river makes its way southeast.
11375: Sitting inside the turn of the road from north to east of here, these fields bear many a footpath, presumably from travellers preferring to travel through the fields than the road itself. Indeed, the fields are pleasant. The grass grows thick and healthy in spite of all the wear and abuse it's taken. The sound of running water south and west of here indicates you're near the river.
11376: The riverbank here is surprisingly gentle and leads up to grasslands east and north. Looking down the river south of here, you can tell that the banks are much steeper. At the river's edge, almost flush with the level of the water, lies a large, flat stone, which is almost completely covered with soft, thick, green moss.
11377: The ground here forms a steep slope between the river and road above. Thick clods of earth covered in damp grass make the ground difficult to negotiate and indeed, several of the smaller trees here are broken and doubled over. No doubt having served as someone's climbing aid.
11378: As you near the river's edge, the muddy embankment becomes more precarious. Eroded overhangs skirt the edge of the riverbank, threatening to give way at any moment. Gazing down, the river looks cool and refreshing.
11379: A mixture of soft mud and pebbles makes the ground quite slippery by the rivers edge. Most of the banking has collapsed into the river and a solitary tree remains rooted to the embankment, leaning over the river at an acute angle.
11380:
A sparrow is flapping around on the ground.
A brook trout is here, swimming in the current.

The river here is flanked by a forest to the west, but the bank is so steep that it would seem impossible to scale. To the east the bank is a little lower, but still appears to be quite steep, muddy and slippery. Apparently the only choice is to follow the fast-flowing waters, which bubble merrily toward the Nen Kalthar, to the south.
11382: A black catfish is here, lurking in the mud.

Rising high around you, the earthen banks of the river afford little view of the land about, but you can see atop the bank in the west a thin forest, from whence comes the sounds of many birds singing, and of animals scuffling about in the undergrowth. The water flows rapidly to the south here, and it is no easy feat to beat the current, despite the fact that this is such a small and seemingly insignificant tributary.
11383: A brook trout is here, swimming in the current.

The stream is decidedly rough here as it tumbles forth from a very rocky and narrow ravine to the north, and flows swiftly onward to the south, with a violence which belies its relatively small size. Indeed travel further up- stream would seem to be made impossible by the angry waters, and the origins of this waterway would seem to have to remain enshrouded in mystery. To the west, atop a steep bank, the trees of a thin forest look down upon the water- way, whilst to the east the bank appears too steep and muddy to scale, and its height obscures any view of what lies beyond.
11384: On the Fringes of the Light Forest

The pathway, upon which you tread, stands amid the eaves of an old woodland. Soft and grassy underfoot, the trail leads from the Road to Tharbad, which lies just south of here, to the north, deeper into the forest. From somewhere to the east the sound of fast-running water can be heard.
11385:
A fierce boar is here, making grunting noises.
A boar cub is playing here, and exploring the wide world.

Soft grass, springy underfoot, makes this pathway through the woodland. Here the trail diverges, heading westward, or to the north, winding off between the tall trees. To the south, a wider path leads out of the forest, toward the Road to Tharbad, whilst from somewhere to the east, the sound of fast-running water can be heard.
11386: A Pleasant Trail in the Light Forest

A squirrel scampers around here, looking for nuts from the trees.
A rabbit is here eyeing your presence warily.

Leaves and small twigs flutter down beside you, dislodged from up above by the many animals and birds who make this forest their home. The grass under your feet smells fresh, and feels damp, as though still wet with the first dew of the morning. The trail you are on leads under arched boughs to the north and south, or you can enter a large clearing in the middle of the forest to the west.
11387:
A mass of dark green leaves clings to a wall.
A colony of red ants is here. The ants seem to ignore you.

Right in the middle of the forest there is a small ruin. It is hard to tell what it was before, but it was something made of stone. It was probably a small house with four rooms from what remains of the walls. There is a stair going down to something that could have been a cellar. Near the ruin, the trees are old or dead. They are pale and grey, and have no leaves on them.
11388: A Pleasant Trail in the Light Forest
A woodpecker is here, tapping on a tree.

You are walking along the forest floor, under an archway high above, formed from interlaced branches. Leaves rustle softly all around, and small animals scamper into the undergrowth just ahead of you. The pathway continues through the trees, both east and west, whilst to the north a large clearing opens up.
11389:
A dense carpet of blue flowers dip their heads in the breeze.
A squirrel scampers around here, looking for nuts from the trees.
A squirrel scampers around here, looking for nuts from the trees.

The trees here form an almost perfect circle around this clearing. Trails lead out from here in all directions, passing under the stout green boughs of the ancient trees. In the centre of the clearing, a few small mushrooms grow, and all around, small animals scamper away, almost unseen, at the edge of your vision.
11390: A Pleasant Trail in the Light Forest
A squirrel scampers around here, looking for nuts from the trees.

The trail you are on leads east and west here, or you can enter a clearing in the middle of the forest to the south. Overhead you can hear the flapping of wings and the scratching noises of many small feet trying to gain purchase on the bark of the trees, as animals of the forest hurry about, packing as much happiness and industry into their short life spans as they can possibly manage.
11391: A Pleasant Trail in the Light Forest

A squirrel scampers around here, looking for nuts from the trees.
A squirrel scampers around here, looking for nuts from the trees.

The sound of birdsong is to be heard in the branches far above your head, whilst at your feet small animals scurry, unseen among the undergrowth which partially obscures the pathway here. The woodland stretches in all directions, though, to the south, through some thick bushes, a glimpse of the road to Tharbad can be seen.
11392: A Pleasant Trail in the Light Forest
A squirrel scampers around here, looking for nuts from the trees.

The grassy path is springy underfoot, and the sound of birdsong fills the air. The trees rustle in the wind, and all around are signs of abundant wildlife, which must fill this forest. To the east, a large clearing opens out before you, whilst westward, through the trees and bushes, it is possible to glimpse some well tended pasture fields.
11393: At the End of the Trail

A forest spider is here crawling around.
A forest spider is here crawling around.
A fierce boar is here, making grunting noises.
A boar cub is playing here, and exploring the wide world.
A boar cub is playing here, and exploring the wide world.

The trail seems to peter out here, as the trees grow closer together near the edge of the forest, almost as though someone has deliberately planted them so close together, to make a barrier. Through the thick undergrowth, a small building can be seen to the west, with dark smoke curling out of its chimney, but it is impossible to reach it, due to the dense vegetation.
11394:
On the ground, there are four loaves of bread.
A round turnip is growing here.
A map has been dropped here.
A peaceful farmer is here, whistling merrily.
An opossum stands here, sniffing around the ground.
A boar cub is playing here, and exploring the wide world.

The smell of freshly baked bread fills this small and cosy little home. A sturdy wooden table, surrounded by six simple chairs, stands at the centre of the room, and cheerful curtains cover the windows. The floor is made of stout boards, and the walls are painted neatly with bright white paint.
11395:
Yellow flowers, with grey-green foliage, grow in clusters here.
A well-fed cow stands here chewing her cud listlessly.

You are standing at the edge of the fields here, but the grass is still as thick as before. The fields continue to the west, but to the east, the thick undergrowth of a small forest blocks your way. To the south, a grassy path leads towards the forest.
11396: A Pleasant Trail in the Light Forest

The grass springs under your step, making your walk through this forest quite an enjoyable one. Birds sing sweet songs to serenade you, and little animals scurry here and there, at the edge of your vision. The trail leads north from here, into an open field, or east, deeper into the woodland.
11397:
A well-fed cow stands here chewing her cud listlessly.
A well-fed cow stands here chewing her cud listlessly.

You are standing in the middle of some lush fields, a sea of lush, green grass which makes an ideal pastureland for cattle. The fields continue to the north, where a small farmhouse can be seen, dark smoke curling from its chimney, and to the east, where they draw close to the borders of a thin forest. Westward, a small path leads through the fields, toward a huge wooden barn.
11398:
Yellow flowers, with grey-green foliage, grow in clusters here.
A well-fed cow stands here chewing her cud listlessly.

You are standing here in the middle of some fields, surrounded by grass which is thick green and healthy - ideal pastureland. The fields stretch into the distance, both to the south and to the west, whilst to the east a small and simple farmhouse stands.
11399: Yellow flowers, with grey-green foliage, grow in clusters here.

You are standing in the middle of some pastures, which stretch eastward from here, leading eventually to a simple farmhouse, beyond which a thin forest can be seen. To the south, a small pathway leads toward the Road to Tharbad, which runs east-west in this part of the country. Birds occassionally fly by, overhead, chirping and singing happily.
11400: This section of the path is fairly barren, as it seems to be a fairly often- used intersection, and the passage of many men and beasts has made the path dusty and worn. To the south you can see a road leading east-west, while fields extend to the north and east. To the west the dirt path continues, leading towards a barn in the northwest, but you can also see the rooftop of a house in the opposite direction, across the fields.
11401: On a Dirt Path in Front of a Barn

You stand on a packed-earth path that runs from the west to the east. Directly north of here there is a huge wooden barn which, although simply designed, looks clean and freshly painted. From inside you can hear the sounds of peaceful clucking, scritching, scratching and flapping. The path makes a bend in the west, or runs east to join an intersection.
11402: A Turn in the Dirt Path

A brown fox is here, looking for some rabbits to chew up.
A rabbit is here eyeing your presence warily.

The earthy path bends here around the corner of the barn, curving from the east to the north. An odd, and not necessarily pleasant smell drifts from that direction, but for now, you are quite unable to place its source. To the south, a thin ribbon of road can be seen through the trees.
11403: A cluster of dark green, feathery fronds flourishes in the shade.

You are standing at the end of the path, behind a large barn. A wheelbarrow is parked here, filled with fresh manure, which smells fairly strongly, and from inside the barn you can hear some clucking noises, along with scratching and flapping.
11404:
A young farm-hand is here hard at work.
A hen is standing here.
A hen is standing here.
A hen is standing here.
The rooster is here, strutting about.

You are standing in a neat barn, with freshly-dried hay for the horses sitting in the feed-boxes, and several hen roosts placed along the walls. There are stalls for cows here, lined with clean straw, but the stalls are empty right now. The smell in here is distinct in its nature, but it is a wholesome smell, not a sickly one.
11405: A nightingale is here, chirping a sweet melody.

This small stony path, leading from the roadway to the north, splits in two, the main trail heading west toward the river. Petering out not far to the south, the lesser track leads towards a grassy meadow.
11406: At a Resting Place by the River

This gently sloped, grassy beach along the shore of the Nen Kalthar seems a perfect spot to recover after taking a swim in the river that flows west to south here. The path to cross the river lies just north, and grass grows along the bank of the road to Tharbad for a few miles east of here.
11407: On a Grassy Bank by the Road

A tall, stately, dome-topped tree grows here.
On the plant, there are five green spiny capsules.
A fat rabbit is here, chewing on some grass.

Slightly higher than the path of the road north of here, this grassy bank gives a good view of the river a few miles to the west and the castle beyond. The bank becomes rather rocky to the east, but no stones litter the gentle slope south toward the meadow.
11408: A Stony Bank beside the Road

Overlooking a turn in the road from north to east, this stony bank provides a decent view of the surrounding lands. Off in the distance southwest of here, you can make out a tall tower that peeks above a line of trees to the north of the tower. Looking south, you see a trail of rocks leading down to a river dam.
11409: Yellow flowers, with grey-green foliage, grow in clusters here.

Overlooking the running water of the river west and south, this cozy little meadow full of short, thin-bladed grass sits in a slight depression behind a bank to the north. A few scattered stones litter the steep banks above the Nen Kalthar, and the ground starts to get a little stoney towards the east.
11410: Though some are small and flat, and others larger and more irregular, the myriad rocks which can be seen peeking up through the grass here seem to have been gathered together deliberately to form a crude path leading from north to south. The land itself lies in a slight depression, formed by a bank to the north, and the meadows lying south, east and west of here.
11411: This wide, grassy field sits by the bend in the road to Tharbad northeast of here. Though some rocks have been kicked off the road, there are more stones west of here than to the north or east. South the land becomes grassier, as it draws closer to a small river.
11412: To the south, the ground slopes down as it meets the Nen Kalthar, the pleasant waterway, which cuts its way across the countryside. At this point, the river has been dammed, creating a wide pool, and a small, gently splashing waterfall, which makes a musical sound, to be heard even at some distance.
11413: The river bank here is quite high, and has been eroded and undercut by the flow of the water, making it inadvisable to attempt to enter the water at this point. At some distance both north and east, a wide road snakes its way across the countryside, almost tracing the path of the nearby watercourse.
11414:
A tall, stately, dome-topped tree grows here.
A squirrel scampers around here, looking for nuts from the trees.

A sparse woodland of tall, slender trees rises to the west of here, and to the east and north, a wide road sweeps by. The land here stands at some height above the course of the Nen Kalthar, and the turbulent waters of the river flow from west to south, at the bottom of a steep, muddy bank. Whilst slithering down the bank to the water seems easy enough, returning to this point might prove to be impossible.
11415:
A fat rabbit sits here, chewing on some grass.
