A fat rabbit sits here, chewing on some grass.

The Nen Kalthar flows parallel to the road here. At the bottom of a steep and muddy bank, the waters tumble past, but the river has left its mark here. The land is lush, the grass green and thick, and flowers and shrubs grow in abundance. The sound of songbirds and the splash of the river fill the air.
11416: A small animal, all covered in spines, snuffles amongst the undergrowth.

A wide ribbon of grassland lies between the Road to Tharbad and the Nen Kalthar. The waters of this small river have fed the land well, and the grass here grows tall and healthy. Shrubs and small trees abound, forming a natural hedgerow, which starts here, and winds beside the road to the east, and the waterway to the south.
11417: In a Thick Hedgerow at the Meeting of Two Waterways
A nightingale is here, chirping a sweet melody.

The swirling waters of the Greyflood and the smaller river Nen Kalthar meet just a little to the south of here, outside the imposing walls of the city of Tharbad. The soil here is dark and rich, and a thick tangle of thorny bushes and shrubs flourishes on these low banks, and nestles up against the rough stone wall which can be seen to the east.
11418: A small cluster of clover grows here.

Water flows lazily past north and east of here. You hear the soothing sound of water splashing over the dam in the northwest. Both to the south and across the river to the north, you see some sparse woodland. The light green grass here seems to get less moisture than the healthier pasture in the west.
11419:
A dense carpet of blue flowers dip their heads in the breeze.
A small animal, all covered in spines, snuffles amongst the undergrowth.

Thin, but tall and healthy, the trees that grow here provide some shade for the thin carpet of water-starved grass and various sorts of bushes to hide under. Flanked to the south and west by a steep escarpment, the woods give shelter from the winds on plains beyond the ridge. The woods continue eastward.
11420: In the Sparse Woodland beside the River

A dense carpet of blue flowers dip their heads in the breeze.
A squirrel scampers around here, looking for nuts from the trees.

Tall trees grow all around, in a light, airy, scattered woodland. The trees are healthy, and the undergrowth made up of lush, green vegetation. To both the north and east a river sweeps by, supplying the woods with life-giving water, and further east a wide road can be seen, cutting a swath across the lowlands, and leading inexorably toward the city of Tharbad.
11421: Grassy Fields South of the Dam
A small cluster of clover grows here.

Since the water from the river continuously feed its soil, the grass here grows healthy and has a deep green colour to it. Northwest, you can see a wide pool that collects behind the dam. As a result of the pool, the fields west of here begin to get a little muddy in their lower lying areas. South, a steep escarpment resists your advance. The grass continues east, lightening in hue.
11422: In the Muddy Fields by the Pool

A clean fragrance drifts up from a thick clump of leaves.
A large bullfrog croaks loudly.

Because of their position adjacent to the pool north of here that collects water by the dam and also their low banks, the fields here have become very wet and muddy. From what you can see, the fields east of here look to be wet also, but the grasslands west remain dry. A steep escarpment south prevents travel in that direction.
11423: Yellow flowers, with grey-green foliage, grow in clusters here.

The vegetation here is flat, green and very pleasant to walk through. Aside from the weeds in the north and the fact that the ground begins to get a little soggy in the east, there is nothing unpleasant about this pasture nestled in the bend of a steep escarpment west and south of here.
11424: Yellow flowers, with grey-green foliage, grow in clusters here.

Thick green grass and scattered bushes and shrubs cover these gently rolling plains. The land here is rich and fertile, and must once have been home to many, but now the only sign of habitation is a massive castle, standing to the northwest.
11425:
Yellow flowers, with grey-green foliage, grow in clusters here.
A restless rabbit bounces around.

Verdant lowland plains stretch in all directions as far as the eye can see, carpeted in thick green grass, and occasional patches of shrubs. To the northwest, standing amid the grasslands, is a mighty castle, its high stone walls and massive tower dominating the view in that direction.
11426: A mass of dark green leaves clings to a wall.

The castle walls loom high above you, their crumbling stones and sheer height forbidding any attempt to scale them. Dense tangles of thorny brambles grow right up to the walls, and the grass and weeds here seem little disturbed by any traveller, and indeed this makes sense, for the huge building appears to offer no entrance to this side.
11427: A large rabbit looks peacefully at you, ready to dart away.

The grass grows thick and healthy here, right up to the castle walls, and an occasional gutteral croak can be heard, seemingly answered by a shrill insect-like chirping from deep in the vegetation. Peering upward, it is possible to see the castle battlements far above, but the crumbling stone walls appear to offer only the most tenuous of foot and handholds, so that it would seem that attempting to scale them may not be a wise plan.
11428: A large rabbit looks peacefully at you, ready to dart away.

The land dips down to the north, so low that the river has breeched its banks there, but here the land is comparitively dry, but nonetheless rich due to the ever-present waters of the Nen Kalthar. Westward, the plains continue until they meet the walls of a large castle, clearly visible in the distance, and to the east they fail only at the river edge.
11429:
A clean fragrance drifts up from a thick clump of leaves.
A large rabbit looks peacefully at you, ready to dart away.

Tromping through these dense weeds, you hear the melodic sounds of thousands of unseen insects performing beautiful symphony for anyone who will listen. These mesmerizing sounds, barely audible above the rush of the river north of here, become more noticable by the wide pool in front of the dam in the east. The weeds thin out south and west, as does the wonderful music.
11430:
Clusters of slender stems and tall leaves thrive in the mud and shallows.
A bullfrog is standing here.

The surrounding lowlands are filled with splashing noises, for the the river has overrun its banks in the north. The grass south of here becomes less damp and more healthy, and the knee-high grass west of here looks almost like a body of water as it ripples in the breeze.
11431: Wading in a Sea of Tall Grass

The grasses here are deeper than they might have appeared at a distance, and travelling through the thick growth is actually quite an arduous task. The long, delicate stalks of grass bob and sway gently in the breeze, and look like the rippling waves of a vast green lake. Further to the north the vegetation is less luxurient, as the terrain climbs somewhat, rising well above the level of the river to the east.
11432: The plains here are carpeted in a thick growth of tall grasses, which thrive in the deep rich soil. Sheltered from the elements by the castle and woodland to the west, but afforded plenty of sunlight by the otherwise open location, this area would make a splendid pasture, or fertile farmland.
11433: Though the embankment may be inaccessable from the river to the north and east, nothing prevents you from jumping into the water but your own will. The tall grass south of here looks like a body of water rippling in the wind, and the vegetation here is nice and green, but the fields to the west are dry because they lack the constant watering of the river.
11434:
A restless rabbit bounces around.
A large rabbit looks peacefully at you, ready to dart away.

The land here is cut off from the river to the east, by an embankment, which rises gently from here, then falls off sharply at the water's edge. Sloping downward gently to the south, the land regains the level of the waterway, and the grass there is more luxurient, but here the ground is quite parched, and the vegetation weak and more sparse.
11435: Though a swift river cuts across the land some way to the east of here, this part of the countryside lies too far from its nourishing waters, and all that manages to grow here are a few sparse patches of coarse grass. Further west, a gloomy woodland rises above the plain, its thorny and tangled undergrowth choking out even the thin grass, and contributing to an unwholesome air, which hangs heavily over the entire area.
11436: A small animal, all covered in spines, snuffles amongst the undergrowth.

A single massive stump stands almost alone, at a distance from the numerous smaller stumps which can be seen in the surrounding area. This must once have been a magnificent tree, dominating the land here, and thick sinuous roots break the surface of the ground all around you. To the west a small tract of woodland has apparently been spared from the woodsman's axe, and the thick undergrowth between the trees impedes progress in that direction.
11437: The banks of the river stand high here, and the ever-flowing waters seem to undercut the land somewhat. However, the earth is stabilised by a massive network of thick tree roots, which break the surface of the ground all about you, offering to trick and trip you with every step. These roots are all that remain here of a once mighty woodland, but further west numerous huge stumps litter the countryside.
11446:
A strong bulldog, with sharp teeth, growls at strangers.
The garden snake slithers harmlessly here.

The old gate rises up in front of you. This was the main entrance to the main castle of Minhiriath, and here all the soldiers marched to battle to fight off the evil minions of the Witchking. You notice that the castle seems to be surrounded by a huge and tall wall, guarding it from wild animals and unwanted visitors. The ground in front of the entrance is covered with huge tiles, but due to weather and erosion over hundreds of year, they have been broken and the ground is uneven. To the south you can see an old watchtower, while west you can see a small path leading up to a small mound.
11447:
A large round whetstone rests on the ground.
A strong bulldog, with sharp teeth, growls at strangers.
A strong bulldog, with sharp teeth, growls at strangers.
A strong bulldog, with sharp teeth, growls at strangers.
A strong bulldog, with sharp teeth, growls at strangers.

You find yourself inside the outer gate of the castle, standing upon a broad path, which leads directly to the castle keep. The entrance to the main part of the castle is set into a massive stone wall, which stands at the far side of a large, square yard, which opens up before you.
11448:
The corpse of a bulldog is lying here.
A small black vicious rat squeaks at you for disturbing it.
A bulldog is here, fighting Lhurank (brenny).
A bulldog is here, fighting Lhurank (brenny).
A small rat runs about, oblivious to your presence.
Lhurank (brenny), wielding a darkened orkish axe, is here, fighting a bulldog.
Klaees (thedon), wielding a two-handed sword, is standing here.

Elegant marble steps lead up to two huge black irondoors with alternating spirals of silver and gold that mark the entrance of the castle. Each door is four feet wide and seven feet high. The doors slide sideways into the castlerock along metal tracks, making the doors impossible to force open. The entrance is built halfway inside the sturdy castle walls, and you notice several murderholes in the ceiling above you. To the north stands a small guard house, and to the south the castle forges and armoury can be seen.
11449:
A domesticated pony, beast of burden to many, stands here.
A beautiful and docile horse is standing here.
A sturdy pack horse is standing here.

The south and west walls of this large but low-roofed building are divided into pens and stalls, most of which are piled with filth and refuse. However a few of those nearest to the doors have been kept reasonably clean and seem to be in daily use. To the east, an arched entryway leads into another part of the building.
11450:
The corpse of a diminutive rogue is lying here.
A slim young woman glares at you suspiciously.

The top of the tower is not enclosed, but a turretted wall stands on all sides, at once protecting, and yet offering a clear view in all directions. To the west, a small path leads down into a valley, whilst eastward, the castle stands in view.
11451:
A slim young woman glares at you suspiciously.
A slim young woman glares at you suspiciously.

This tower once served as an old watchpost and its main job was to stand vigil over the castle gate, checking anyone who claimed to have business to do inside. When you step in, you realise that not many guards could stay inside here at the same time. The room is simple, only a massive table made of stone has survived all the years of desolation here. The guards who sat here had a good overview over the gate to the north via a couple of huge windows on the northern wall. On the southern wall you can see a small staircase made of iron.
11452:
A wide bar of iron, coated in black dust, lies here.
A wide bar of iron, coated in black dust, lies here.
A weapons rack stands against the wall.
A light leather sling lies in the dust.
A small vicious black rat squeaks at you for disturbing it.
A small vicious black rat squeaks at you for disturbing it.

This chamber once served as the castle forges, ringing with the clash of metal upon cold metal, in the smithying of new weapons, and stout armours. But now, all lies cold and still, and no labours continue here today. Indeed, all the room is coated in a layer of dust, grease and grime, bespeaking of many years of disuse, and the racks which once held shiny plate and bright weapons have long ago been ransacked, leaving nothing of any value.
11453:
A large piece of fresh, raw meat lies here.
A large piece of fresh, raw meat lies here.
A delicate and beautiful crystal glass sits on the ground.
A large sack containing pepper lies on the ground.
A chunk of salt is here.
A tough strip of dried meat lies here.
A tough strip of dried meat lies here.
A small barrel made of aged oak and strong iron hoops stands here.
A small rat runs about, oblivious to your presence.

Entering this room, you become aware of the unstable and rotten foundation upon which this castle has been built. Small spots stain the walls, where water has constantly dripped into the room, and the floor beneath your feet is damp and muddy. The air is heavy and stinks of rotting wood and sackcloth. Looted, and damaged by both time and water, this chamber is useless now.
11454:
A small oaken table has been set here.
A simple servant goes quietly about her duties.
A cook is standing here, busy with her pots and pans.
A small vicious black rat squeaks at you for disturbing it.

This commodious room must once have been home to almost frenzied activity, in the preparation of great feasts for the lords of Minhiriath. Now most of the fireplaces, ranges, and massive stone tables are thick with the grime of years of disuse. Racks which once held pots and pans, spoons and knives, now hang askew, and the windows set high in the north and south walls are covered in so much filth that no natural light can enter.
11455:
A small rat runs about, oblivious to your presence.
A small vicious black rat squeaks at you for disturbing it.
The garden snake slithers harmlessly here.

This massive hall serves as the main entrance to the castle of Minhiriath. It is a long oval chamber, which runs from north to south, and is furnished in a combination of pastels and paisleys, slightly faded by age, yet still in much better condition than the exterior of the castle would suggest. The floor is comprised of white marble octagons circumscribed with black marble. On both walls are huge windows with partly coloured glass.
11456: This is the shadowy Hall of Heroes. The long walls bear many attachments for lanterns, which cast multiple shadows, dancing all around you, and the entire passageway is lined with the slashed portraits of the original inhabitants of the castle, which at first glance appear pretty grim. High on the eastern wall are a row of tiny square windows, but these are so dirty that even bright sun- light no longer reaches this place. Far to the southern end of the hall, a massive stone stair spirals upward, whilst a smaller iron stair can be seen leading downward, at the opposite end of the corridor.
11457:
A sturdy guardsman is here, his weapon at the ready.
A sturdy guardsman is here, his weapon at the ready.
An old, yet beautiful woman looks piercingly at you.
A strong bulldog, with sharp teeth, growls at strangers.
A tall, lean man follows your every move with his eyes.

The chamber in which you find yourself is both grand and tasteful, and must once have served both as a meeting hall and a place for feasting and great celebrations. At one end of the hall, upon a great dais, stands a throne, and behind this, the walls are hung with heavy tapestries, depicting the lords of Minhiriath. A long table of polished white marble stands at the centre of the room, hinting at the opulent banquets, which must once have been served here.
11458:
A sturdy guardsman is here, his weapon at the ready.
A sturdy guardsman is here, his weapon at the ready.

This is the old guard barracks used by the lord to maintain safety around the castle. The barracks was built here to provide a fast way to aid and protect their master. The barracks seem somewhat desolate now, however you can see a narrow staircase leading down. You see many small windows here facing in all directions, offering a good view of the castle and its surroundings.
11459:
A small rat runs about, oblivious to your presence.
A small rat runs about, oblivious to your presence.
A small rat runs about, oblivious to your presence.
A small vicious black rat squeaks at you for disturbing it.
A small vicious black rat squeaks at you for disturbing it.
A small vicious black rat squeaks at you for disturbing it.
A prisoner is sitting here, looking at you with sad eyes.

Though not large, this room nevertheless holds five cage-like prison cells. Time has taken its toll here, as in other parts of the castle, for all of the cell doors are broken, and hanging askew on their rusty hinges. The floor is littered with old chains, and manacles, left behind when the castle was long ago abandoned. No natural light can enter this place, for the two small windows, set high in the southern wall, are quite obscured by grass and weeds, which grow in the yard outside.
11460: The first thing you notice when you enter is the mosaic floor. The rest of the room is covered with grey granite, softened by grey velvet hangings. The walls are made smooth and on the western wall you can see a map carved in depicting a complete overview map of Numenor, the island who is now lost in the Great Sea. It seems like nothing has been touched here for years. You can see dust swirling up at your feet when you walk around.
11461: The corpse of a vicious rat is lying here.

As all lords in Cardolan, so the lords of Minhiriath relied upon a number of bodyguards, who would gladly lay down their lives for their masters. This small, and unadorned, chamber was their place of rest, while they guarded the master through the night, ready to spring to his aid, at but a moment's notice. To this end, the simple cots, cut into niches in the southern wall, were built not for comfort, but for utility.
11462: At the Top of a Spiral Stair

A massive stone stair spirals downward, and odd sounds echo up the stairs from below. To the west the passageway leads towards the private chambers of the castle, and it is clear that this narrow corridor was built more for utility than to impress the many guests to the castle. Yet the cold stone walls are quite smooth to the touch, and decorated with elaborate carvings, on which traces of gilding remain, in silent testimony to the great skill and artistry of the builders.
11463: A simple servant goes quietly about her duties.

The ceiling is arched gracefully above you and delicately painted in blue. A soft and warm light fills the room and dances off the pale indigo and azure tiles forming a simple yet elegant mosaic on the walls. The floor is covered in large tiles, of two shades of blue, arranged in a simple checkerboard pattern, and at the very centre of the room a large, perfectly spherical crystal sits atop a round oak pedestal. A low light emanates from the crystal, and it seems to be secured so as to be impossible to move.
11464: The room is small, and only one little window to the north, making the room dimly lit even at daytime, just like a bedroom should be like. It is here the lord of Minhiriath commonly rested, sleeping on a raised platform bed in the middle of the room.
11465:
A large bookshelf sits against the wall.
On the bookshelf, there is a small book, bound in maroon leather.

This tiny chamber nestles in the rafters of the castle roof, and has a low ceiling. The walls on three sides of the room are sloped, but the third stands tall and straight, and is lined with an old wooden bookshelf. Alas, no books, or other items of interest remain upon it. The only exits from this attic are to return down to the corridor below, or to investigate the room, which lies through an opening in the straight wall, to the west.
11466:
A coil of rope is lying here.
A case, made for quarrels, lies on the ground.

Thirty feet above the plains by the river, these battlements serve as a lookout tower for the castle. Scanning north, you can see the Road to Tharbad on the other side of the Nen Kalthar. To the east, you can barely make out the pool and the dam beyond. You see nothing but miles of grassy, rolling plains south of here. There is a small iron loop by the eastern edge of the battlements.
11467: The wild ox seems ready to charge you.

This outcropping is covered in brush and high grass. North and below the river makes its way southwest through harsh rapids. Looking east, you see the flat plains of Dunland stretching out beyond some more brushy land. South, the lands of Enedwaith lie before your eyes. The brush grows thicker though, eventually prohibiting travel in that direction.
11468: This flat, muddy land is watered by the Greyflood a few miles north. Brush and thick bushes grow here in the rich, black soil. A steep bank, seeming to have been cut by water, rises up to the south. To the west is dryer, higher ground; to the east, the vegetation thins out and the plains of Enedwaith begin.
11469: This low riverbank is entangled in thick brush. The ground is muddy, as water escapes the fast flowing river to the north and east, forming small pools. Some higher ground is to the south and east, where the plains begin. You hear the river pass some heavy rapids to the northwest, but all you can see is a thick haze covering the surface.
11470: A low swale of grass and reeds extends around you. The ground here is sandy, and heaps or bars of round, water-worn pebbles can be seen everywhere. To the south, the ground rises abruptly, and water-worn bluffs can be seen. Here and there is an ancient trunk, its bark stripped clean, half-buried in the mud and sand.
11471: A long-necked bird, with a fairly short spear-like bill stands here.

The shore here is flat, muddy, and full of bushes and vines. North and west the Greyflood flows slowly past, while fields and flatlands await to the east and south. The bank is covered with reeds and cattails, giving home to several species of insects and fish. The foundation stones of a house and some outbuildings, long abandoned, and what seems to be the capstone of a well, lie here, sinking year by year deeper into the mud.
11472:
The wild ox seems ready to charge you.
The wild ox seems ready to charge you.
This is rolling grassland. To the west it drops off rather sharply, and the ground there is low, damp, and overgrown. The flat grassland continues to the north and east, rolling towards Eregion.
11473: A wild bull seems ready to charge you.

The grass grows thick and dense in these fields, hiding a trail which turns into a small road as it approaches a little cottage to the west. If you follow it east you will enter some other grassy fields.
11474: The grass here is thick and dense. You hear the sound of small insects hiding in the grass. There is a high fence to the southwest enclosing some kind of lawn. North, east and south you see more flat land, while the Greyflood can be seen flowing southward beyond some muddy ground west of here.
11475: From these plains you can watch the water flowing in the river to your north and west. Southwest you barely discern a small building in the distance. Moving east and south you will take you to some more plains.
11476: You are near some plains which force the water to make a turn and flow from the north to west. A few insects have flown from the land and are now circling around you, trying to find a place to land. You see plain land east and south.
11477: This is a low, flat-topped bluff whose steep sides overlook the Greyflood on the east and south. On the west and north there are thick, tangled bushes, and the surface is very uneven, composed of big blocks of grey stone with deep black crevices between them. Shrubs and small trees growing out of the cracks have covered the stones with a tangle of roots.
11478:
A small animal, all covered in spines, snuffles amongst the undergrowth.
A wild dog bares his yellow fangs at you.

Bushes grow very dense and thick here. They have small thorns which lightly scratch your skin, but don't really hurt you. There are a lot of clusters of some sort of berries hanging here and there. The bushes are so dense you can only go to the plains north or east.
11479:
A fallow deer is grazing peacefully here.
A sparrow is flapping around on the ground.

The grass has grown very high here. When you turn around you can clearly see where you came from. Butterflies and other insects can be seen in the air. There are less grassy plains around you, except to the south, where you see lots of large bushes of some kind.
11480: The grass is thick and surrounds a few young trees. The ground here must be very fertile, because the vegetation is dense, but still short. You see more plains everywhere you look.
11481: An apple tree with bright green leaves grows here.

What you see is clearly the remainders of what was once a forest. There are some trees left which at the time the others were cut down probably were too small to be of any use. You see more plains everywhere you look.
11482:
A fallow deer is grazing peacefully here.
A restless rabbit bounces around.
Stumps, old and rotten, can be seen everywhere. Once this piece of land was a part of the forest which can be seen to the north. You can see more plains with stumps to your east and south.
11483: A fallow deer is grazing peacefully here.

The ground beneath your feet makes a squishy sound when you walk on it. It is far from marshy, but still you see water here and there. You notice some rotten stumps here and there, indicating that this was once a forest. You see more plains west and south. To the north and east you see the reason to why the ground is wet, the Nen Kalthar.
11484: This is a flat piece of land with old stumps here and there. Some small trees grow here, left to stand while others had to fall long ago. You see more plains in all directions.
11485:
A slender, wooden key is lying here.
A sturdy pack horse is standing here.
A restless rabbit bounces around.
A wild dog bares his yellow fangs at you.
A partridge attempts to hide in the undergrowth.

The thick grass here almost makes it feel like you're walking on pillows. This is a peaceful place. The plains stretch out in all directions, but looking further east you think you see something that looks like a riverbank.
11486:
A beautiful and docile horse is standing here.
A partridge attempts to hide in the undergrowth.

The grass is thick and soft. A cow could probably live all its life grazing on these plains. The only animals you see here are not that big though. The river to the east and south supplies the plains with fresh water. You see more plains north, and west you see some thick bushes.
11487: A colourful butterfly is fluttering around here.

The grass here is very high, housing many small animals and insects. You see a river beyond the grass to the east and south. Less grassy plains can be seen looking north and some very dense bushes are to the west.
11488: You are standing on the beach by the Greyflood. The soil here must be very fertile, judging by the vegetation. Various plants grow here and there in the thick grass. You see plains north and west and the river east and south.
11489:
A restless rabbit bounces around.
A fallow deer is grazing peacefully here.

The land here is as flat as a board; the soil is lush and rich, with thick grass and small shrubs growing wildly everywhere. Here and there are tilled fields, but there is no sign of the houses of the farmers. Possibly they live in Tharbad, across the river, working their fields by day, and at night retreating into the dubious safety of the city's walls.
11491: One of the citizens of Tharbad looks at you from the corner of his eye.

You enter an old watching tower. Parts of the walls are missing and a lot of fissures run about in the remaining parts. Stairs lead up to what was the first floor but look decidedly dangerous. Should you really venture on up?
11492: A black snake hurries towards you with sly intentions.

All looks moist down here and a lot of disgusting mud covers the floor. On the wall, you notice some big iron rings. Against the south wall, some worm-eaten planks are lying in the mud. As you look to the north you see some tracks on the floor.
11493: You enter what seems to be the house of a wealthy person. Looking to the south you see a huge fireplace with paintings hanging above it. A bookcase covering most of the eastern wall is filled with books and scrolls of a somewhat antique nature. Stairs lead up in the north-eastern corner of the room and a door leads outside to the west.
11494:
A middle-aged woman, the illusionist looks defiantly at you.
A little boy is here, running around.
A woman is here, looking for someone to chat with.

You are standing in a well lit room, but you can't seem to find the source of this ambience. There are open books and flasks bubbling with different coloured liquids everywhere you look around you. As you look around yourself, you begin to realise how unlearned you really are in the Arcane arts. A small wooden door leads to the south and behind it you can hear voices chattering away. There are also stairs leading back down.
11495:
A small intelligent looking mage is standing here.
A small intelligent looking mage is standing here.
A sturdy pack horse is standing here.

You enter a small library full of books and scrolls written in long forgotten languages. Apart from that the room is very bare with the only furniture being a table and two chairs in the centre of the room. A single candle sits on this table casting shadows on the walls which seem to threaten you in a very uncanny way.
11496: A valuable gold coin lies here.

This tiny room is lined with shelves containing books, scrolls, and parchments from bygone ages - writings considered too valuable, too irreplaceable, or - too powerful? - to be left out in public view. Perhaps looking at some of these books will provide information not commonly known..
11497:
An armourer stands here.
A little boy is here, running around.

You stand in the armoury with all kinds of armours on the wall behind the counter. You see helmets, shields and chain mails. To the north is a small yard. There is a sign tucked in between the items on display.
11498: The street ends here in a small yard. The air here is thick and rank making it difficult to breathe. All around you can feel people watching your every move, plotting their criminal activities. The house to the east makes the hair on the back of your neck stand on end without even having to look at it. An evil aura seems to emanate from it in all directions out of its dark and narrow windows.
11499:
A citizen-mercenary is here, waiting for a job.
An assassin is here looking for fresh blood and shining coins.

You stand on a small path between two old houses. Children use it when playing together. It connects the two black streets of Tharbad. These being Black Moon Street to the north and Black Blood Alley to the south.
11500: A guard is here looking for someone to abuse.

The road bends east and south here. A narrow, dark building to the east is trying to look inconspicuous which only draws your attention to it. There is a door at the front but who can tell what lies behind it. There are streaks of blood across the walls of the buildings and a small, dark path leading north.
11501:
A large bulletin board, entitled "Tales", is mounted here.
A huge and awesome dealer in black leather is here ( glowing ).

You enter a medium sized room. The air is filled with the acrid smell of stale and fresh smoke. Around you are many tables with gamblers sitting playing cards and many other games of chance. Thoughts enter your mind of maybe joining in on a game but you soon realise that you probably lose all of your hard earned money very quickly. A door leads back out to the west.
11502: The high city wall to your east closely hugs this dark alleyway. All around you are splatters of blood where the unfortunate denizens of this city have met their end. This must be one of the seedier parts of town. There is a gate to your west and the alley continues north and south.
11503: A guard is here looking for someone to abuse.

The high, grey city wall blocks further passage to the east as you travel along this alleyway. The alleyway bends north and west here. There are lots of small and squalid houses lining the alley as this definitely must be the poorer part of the city.
11504: You walk in the shadow of the high wall in the north. Behind the houses falling in ruins you can see the city walls in the south. There is a crossing to the west and you can go further to the east.
11505: A guard is here looking for someone to abuse.

You arrive at a crossroad. In the centre are the City's Gallows, where the seedier elements of town meet their end. Main Street continues north. To the south you can see a small marketplace, and there is a small alleyway to the east.
11506:
A woman is here, looking for someone to chat with.
A dirty bandit waits here looking for an easy mark.
A trained horse is standing here, ridden by you.

You walk along a large paved street, among the hustle and bustle of everyday life you catch glimpses of black clad bodies darting around in and out of buildings and around the crowds. From here you can see the Southern Gate rising above the heads of passers by to the west and the street continues to the east.
11507: Inside the South Gate of Tharbad

A guard is here looking suspiciously at everyone passing.
A guard is here looking suspiciously at everyone passing.
A guard is here looking suspiciously at everyone passing.
A guard is here looking suspiciously at everyone passing.
A dirty bandit waits here looking for an easy mark.

A huge wooden gate looms up before you as you enter the Southern gate of the city. To the west you can see a small hut which must be the guard post. On the wall beside you, you notice a small placard with some writing on it. Main Street continues to the east of here hugging the city walls as it goes.
11508: Instinctively you check your purse hanging from your belt. What a relief when you realise that it is still full. You can't feel safe in this street and you keep on looking right and left. The road is going west and you see main street in the north.
11509: The road narrows to the west, most likely to a lesser used or prestigious road. To the north, however, a dominating white archway boasts of the importance of what must lay beyond. Beneath the intricate column designs and ornate imbedded metal swords lies a bronzed sign of warning.
11510: The alley gets darker and narrower to the north. On the wall to the east you notice some splatters of blood which drip down to the ground. Obviously someone met a particularly grisly and unfortunate end here quite recently, probably best not to hang around here too long in case you meet up with the same fate. To the east you can see Master Road.
11511: The alley continues north and south from here. Visions of murder most foul begin to assault your senses and you have a great urge to press on to your destination.
11512: A little boy is here, running around.
You try to walk silently along the wall on the west but your steps are making a lot of noise on this paved road. Master road is south of here. Main street is bending north and east.
11513: You stand on the large paved road of Tharbad. You notice a small grey building to the north and a large house with white walls and freshly repainted shutters to the south. You can go further east and west.
11514: The road bends west and south here and a small alleyway leads off to the east. The houses are fairly well kept here and the walls have been freshly painted in stark contrast to the alley off to the east. The richer citizens walk around with their mean looking bodyguards in tow, some stop and look down their noses at you in disgust.
11515: The alley continues east and west here. To the west you can see Main Street. Large, dark buildings loom above you and make you feel like they are about to pounce on you. You realise why this alley got its name as you pick out the blackened blood streaking across the walls.
11516: You stand on a wide, and well paved road running north and south. Around you Tharbad city life continues on as normal without paying any heed to you it would seem. To the east of you a large, impressive, white building rises above your head. The building has an air of importance to it, in stark contrast to the grubby grey of the city walls.
11517: You are standing on a large road going south and north. There is a high wall to the west.
11518: The alley goes on north and south from here. You notice red marks on the wall to the east.
11519: You are walking along a very dark alley, the perfect place to be mugged or even brutally slain at night. The alley follows on to the south and leads to Main Street to the east.
11520: You are walking on a very dark alley, the perfect place to be held to ransom at night. Main street is east of here. The alley leads west and a small yard is north of here.
11521: The main road is going further east and south. A small alley is leading west of here. At the corner of main street and the alley there are some letters written on the wall.
11522: You are standing on a large, paved road. As you consider the street sweepings lying almost everywhere, you ask yourself if they have streets' cleaners here and if they do, how much do they pay them? The road is going further west and north. On the sides of the road you see old stone houses with heavy doors and dark windows.
11523: You are standing on a large, paved road. As you consider the street sweepings lying almost everywhere, you ask yourself if they have streets' cleaners here and if they do, how much do they pay them? The road is going on south and north. A small and dark alley leads east.
11524: The alley is dark and narrow. The houses to the north and the south seem to grin evilly at you and make you shiver uncomfortably. Main street is west of here and the alley continues to the east from where an awful smell is coming. South of here you see some burned down ruins, and a small note on the ground.
11525: A guard is here looking for someone to abuse.
A disgusting smell is coming from the stable in the north and you have to concentrate to not puke in the middle of the street. The alley goes further east and west.
11526: You find yourself on a small bridge of rotten planks crossing a muddy street section. The planks, half-way sunken in the mud, bounce with an unreasuring plop as you step onto them. North lie the Old Tower Street following the city walls and south the bridge leads into the Black Moon Street. A track of foot- prints leads off to the east through the mud.
11527: At first glance it seems that you have entered a cul-de-sac. Dark and foreboding houses surround you. A sign is hanging above a door to the west. The street leads back north, but maybe you could force your way down a small path between the houses to the south.
11528: The street continues north and south. Lots of rubbish is littered about seeming to fill up every nook and cranny. To the east you see a large and impressive house.
11529:
A little boy is here, running around.
A woman is here, looking for someone to chat with.

The city walls are quite old here and are promptly falling to pieces. You notice some clefts in it which some birds have made their homes. The street continues west and south from here and to the east an old watching tower rises up.
11530: You are walking on a large and strong stone bridge. Under it, you can see the Greyflood running slowly. It looks dark and polluted from the filth of the city.
11531: A guard is here looking for someone to abuse.

Filthy scraps line the edges and occasionally overflow into centre of this large, paved road lined with dull stone houses. Shut tight with heavy doors, these dingy, lifeless homes seem to peer out uninvitingly from behind their darkened glass windows and closed shutters. In the south, the sound of the Greyflood is barely audible as it gurgles beneath a narrow stone bridge.
11532:
A thief is here looking for some stranger to rob.
A simple servant goes quietly about her duties.
A bartender watches you calmly, while he skilfully mixes a drink.
A thief is here looking for some stranger to rob (hidden).

You stand in the middle of a large room. Light is coming from the fire on your left and from several oil lamps hanging from the ceiling. As you enter, all the customers turn suspiciously at you but they soon return to their drink. A lot of smoke is floating above the tables in front of you. On your right you notice a bar with a man behind it, waiting for your orders. There is a door in the north and an exit east. There is a sign above the bar.
11533: Entrance of the Thirsty Ranger's Inn
A brown donkey watches the surroundings, perhaps looking for a chance to graze.
You are standing in a poorly lit passage. To the west you can hear voices and music. A door leads east back to the street.
11534:
A sturdy pack horse is standing here.
A domesticated pony, beast of burden to many, stands here.
A sturdy pack horse is standing here.

You are standing in a big stable with many small stalls. The smell coming from the hay lying on the floor makes you feel sick. Several people are working in here and you think you can trust them with your mounts or other pets. A stable man is waiting here to serve you.
11535: A little boy is here, running around.

You are standing on a wide, paved road. The rubbish continues to pile up on either side of you. The road leads north and south amidst the drab stone houses which adorn it on either side. You also notice a small side street to the west.
11537: A large grocer is here, waiting to buy or sell some goods.

You are standing in a small room weakly illuminated. A counter is facing you but there is no stuff to buy around. On the wall, behind a strong shopkeeper looking suspiciously at you, a note is hanging. The exit is west.
11539: A beautiful and docile horse is standing here.

You are standing on a wide, paved road. Looking about you and seeing rubbish lying almost everywhere, you begin to ask yourself if there are any street cleaners in this town, if there are any, do they ever do their job? The road leads north and south with either side lined with dark and dreary stone houses.
11540: Before the North Gate of Tharbad
You are standing south of the northern gate of the city. The main street is south of here. To the east and to the west, a small alley is going next to the city walls.
11541: The alley runs west and east past huge city walls. Some bricks at the top of the wall crumble, but overall it is in good condition. Rubbish is littering the ground and a faint smell of putrification lies in the air. Not far to the east an old tower connects to the city walls and reaches far into the sky, while westwards an intersection of streets is visible.
11542:
The corpse of a bandit is lying here.
A woman is here, looking for someone to chat with.

The street hugs the city walls here. The north gate is just west of here. To the south you see a strange small house with dark and gloomy windows. They seem to look back at you. The street leads east and west.
11543: Inside the North Gate of Tharbad

A guard is here looking suspiciously at everyone passing.
A guard is here looking suspiciously at everyone passing.
A guard is here looking suspiciously at everyone passing.
A guard is here looking suspiciously at everyone passing.
A surly secretary is sitting at the desk.

You are just inside the northern gate of the city. Overhead a crudely shaped but sturdy-looking ledge joins the two sections of the city wall on your east and west. A guard post has been set up here to screen all who enter the city.
11544: A sturdy pack horse is standing here.
You are walking next to the northern city wall. A disgusting smell is coming from the west where the street continues further. To the east you see the north gate of the city.
11545: A guard is here looking for someone to abuse.

The smell is really awful here. Big piles of rubbish have been thrown against the wall to the north. To the south the houses are looking so old and abandoned that you are afraid to see them falling on you when you step along them. The street is going on further to the west and to the east.
11546: A little boy is here, running around.
You are standing on a small street following the wall surrounding Tharbad. South of here is West Alley and to the east the street is leading to the north gate of the city.
11547: The corpse of a bandit is lying here.
The alley is next to the western city wall. There are some marks on it. You can go north and south.
11548: You continue along this small and dark alley with its littered and broken surface feeling very uneasy, watching your back continuously as if someone were about to stick a knife in it. To the south you can make out a small square and the alley continues east.
11549:
One of the citizens of Tharbad looks at you from the corner of his eye.
One of the citizens of Tharbad looks at you from the corner of his eye.

You are walking on a small and dark alley. The paved street is quite broken and covered with mud and rubbish. You don't like the idea of being alone here at night without any weapon to defend your purse or even your life. The street is going west and south. A delicious smell of warm bread is coming from the east.
11550: The Baker looks at you calmly, wiping flour from his face with one hand.

You are standing inside a small bakery. A sweet scent of freshly baked bread fills the room. You feel hungry as you look at all these fine breads well arranged on their shelves. A tidy note is nailed to the wall.
11552: One of the citizens of Tharbad looks at you from the corner of his eye.
You are standing on a small alley next to the city wall. It goes further to the north. To the south you see the riverside.
11553: A little boy is here, running around.
The river bank is dirty and pools with stale, muddy water spreads a rotten stench in the air. Just south of here some ships lies docked at the quay. To the north lies the West Alley of Tharbad.
11555: You are standing in a small yard. There is a small pile of rusty and broken weapons in the north-east corner. To the south you see Shadows' street and there is a small shop to the east.
11556: You are inside a small weapon shop. The room is completely empty. All you see is a big counter to the east with an iron door behind it. The exit is west. There is a sturdy iron sign standing on the counter.
11557: A large bulletin board, entitled "Thieves' Guild", is mounted here.

Even though this building is housed away from the major traffic of the city, it is one of the biggest and most frequented buildings in Tharbad. Some people are milling about, hiding in shadows as they warily watch you, others practice some secret skill under the watchful eye of the masters. Looking around, on the walls you see racks of weapons designed with only one purpose in mind. The mere sight of these implements of pain and death send shivers down your spine.
11558:
A large bulletin board, entitled "News of Arda", is mounted here.
A sturdy bed made from solid oak lies here, covered in warm blankets.
A fine marble chessboard with ivory and ebony pieces is set here.
A little boy is here, running around.
You enter a small but well lit room, in fact this is the only room in Tharbad where one may rest and recuperate minding always to close the door behind him.
11559: The shady innkeeper is here looking you over with shifty eyes.

This is the reception in Tharbad. The desk is a mess, with papers and things scattered all over it. It has two drawers, one is locked and barred. A single window in the northern wall lets in enough light to see what you're doing, but the corners of the room are still very dark. A small door leads into a room just south of here and a narrow stair leads to the bottom floor of this building.
11560:
A large bulletin board, entitled "Board of the Free Peoples", is mounted here.
A barman watches you calmly, while skillfully mixing a drink.

You are standing in a long and smoky room. A bar is set against the western wall and you see a few tables beside the fireplace on your right. The room is sparsely furnished and the bar looks antique with many carvings covering its top. There is a small sign above the bar.
11561:
A huge clock is standing here.
A sturdy pack horse is standing here.
You are standing in the entrance hall of the Golden Knife Bar. A stair leads up to the Inn's rooms and the sound of many conversations comes from the south.
11562: A large grocer is here, waiting to buy or sell some goods.

You enter a small shop full of racks and shelves. Most of them are empty but behind the counter, far away from the hands of customers you see all sorts of trinkets stuffed into a big box. There is an exit to the north leading back onto Snake's Alley. A carelessly written note lies on the counter.
11563: You are walking along a small and dark alley. The paved street is badly cracked in many places with mud and rubbish littered all about. You begin to become uncomfortable with the idea of being along here at night without a weapon to defend your purse or even your life ! The street follows on to the west with Main Street to the east.
11564: The alley continues, with the state of the road getting worse and worse and still covered with mud and rubbish. The alley leads north and east.
11565: A well-crafted white fountain is here, water pouring forth from it.

You are standing in the centre of a small square with people jostling around you, a few children play their street games as well. This place is cleaner than most of the rest of city and you begin to wonder why. To the south you can hear voices, Snake Alley is north of here and to the west you can see West Alley and the coach shed.
11566:
A mailbox stands here stuffed full of messages.
A secretary is sitting at the desk.

You enter a small office with all four walls filled with pigeon holes from floor to ceiling. Looking closer at these boxes you notice that many are stuffed full with messages and small packages. Maybe there is something here for you? A door leads back out to the west.
11567: A well-crafted white fountain is here, water pouring forth from it.

You step into a large paved square. The ground here is fit with thick marble slabs and decorated with bright green ferns. In the centre of the Yard, a fountain sprays a fine mist into the air, falling softly into a large concrete pool. To the east, you see an entrance to the Chief of Tharbad's mansion. Master road is south of here, beyond the Arch.
11568: Around you, polished oak panelling travels the length of the walls to the floor, only giving way to a thick lush carpeting at your feet. Truly regal, this is where guests of the Chief wait until they can be seen. A few wide stout chairs stand firmly beneath a deep blue tapestry, inviting you to take a seat. A small sign hangs over the doorknob.
11569: Heavy grey stones cool this room, creating a small breeze as you enter. Thick tapestries of blue and white line the walls, acting as an insulator for the cold wintry months. The room is dominated by a long pine table, around which noble guests might enjoy a feast put on by the Chief. Thick bees-wax candles flicker from the tables, as if expecting guests to enter at any moment. A cold draft comes from the eastern wall.
11570: This abandoned cistern once held rainwater for the inhabitants of this small palace to drink. Now, plugged to prevent water and chiselled into from the Dining Hall, it is more a hiding spot for a smart assassin or wary Chief. It is often said the Chief, like a rabbit, always likes to have an escape or hiding place, for when things might go awry. Such is the life of a Leader of Thieves.
11571:
Traces of fierce red and fierce white tones form the aura of this place.
The corpse of a grim bodyguard is lying here.
The corpse of a grim bodyguard is lying here.
The corpse of a grim bodyguard is lying here.
The corpse of a grim bodyguard is lying here.
The corpse of a grim bodyguard is lying here.
The Chief of Tharbad is standing here (glowing).
A figure, cloaked indiscernibly in the corner, looks at you piercingly (glowing).
The shadow of a grim bodyguard is floating here.

The room you are standing in is spacious and expensively furnished. There is a big desk in front of you and a comfortable looking armchair behind it. A picture of the Chief of Tharbad is hanging slightly crooked on the wall behind the armchair.
11572: A wooden chest stands in the corner.

Lit with oily torches, this acrid black-sooted room is filled with papers and loan notes. A smaller table groans and bends under the strain of books and piles of papers in the centre of this walk-in vault.
11573: One of the citizens of Tharbad looks at you from the corner of his eye.

Here the block of buildings along the east side of the Old Tower Street comes to an abrupt end. Stone stairs, built into the city wall itself, lead down as the steep slope descends. From down there the sound of flowing water can be heard. Westwards a small bridge can be seen, made of some wooden planks, it connects the Old Tower Street with the Black Moon Street, which strolls through southern Tharbad.
11574: A small rat runs about, oblivious to your presence.

This is the eastern end of Chapman's lane. The massive city wall just a few steps to the east, prevents further movement in that direction. Southwards the East Gate of Tharbad can be seen. A long stretched arch spans across the River Greyflood, which noisily flows westwards. Built into the city wall, some stairs, made of stone, lead upwards.
11575: The Greyflood flows to the south here and Chapman's Lane runs parallel to it. Seagulls and rats are the most common inhabitant of this stinking, polluted riverside. They can be seen squawking and scurrying along the steep slope, foraging for whatever they can find. Close to the west several wooden docks lead into the river, providing landing spots for merchant ships.
11576:
A retired Captain stands here, selling boats.
A small rat runs about, oblivious to your presence.

Several small wooden docks provide spots for merchant ships to moor while they stop to load and unload goods. Looking up the slope the Old Tower Street to the west and the Thirsty Rangers' Inn to the north is in plain view. To the south-east, a small wooden bridge spans the Greyflood.
11577: A small rat runs about, oblivious to your presence.

This narrow way twists and turns between the high stone walls of the buildings. Piles of refuse and rubbish litter the ground, and emit a putrid stench of rot and decay. Eastwards some small wooden docks provide landing spots for ships, while Chapman's Lane continues its stroll northwards.
11578: A seagull is soaring above you.

The narrow lane makes its way between the buildings facing onto Main Street and the Old Tower Road. The buildings' stout back doors carry heavy padlocks. Piles of garbage decay beside the doors. A huge, green vine is crawling its way up the wall on the side of the street and it might be possible to climb it to get up to the roof.
11579: A seagull is soaring above you.

Here you have a very good view over the street below. People are walking up and down the street minding their own business and not paying attention to what happens above them. A huge vine grows on the back wall of this building extending downward.
11580:
An old gentleman is here, watching you.
A large cockroach is crawling on the ground.
A warhorse (ulo) is standing here.

You have entered a small, dimly lit room. In the vague light from a lantern you see all kinds of knives gleaming on the northern wall. A fully dressed mannequin stands in the middle of the room and a complete black silk dress hangs over a chair in the northeast corner. A very small ladder on the western wall leads up to the roof, where it abruptly ends.
11581: Here, high above the city, birds are circling around trying to find something to eat or simply to stretch their wings. Below you the city is buzzing with life and from here it looks quite harmless, however, it is easy to watch who walks on the street below. The sheer walls fall steeply to the street and it would be extremely difficult to try to climb down.
11582: From here you have a good view over the city. To the east an old tower can be seen reaching high above the city. Seagulls and some other birds are circling around it, squawking loudly. Massive city walls surround the city and you can see the northern gates from here. It is possible to climb up the roof west of you to reach even higher above the city.
11583: Balancing atop the high roofs, it is possible to overlook the city, which stretches out below your feet. Looking down, the course of the Old Tower Street running west and south is clearly visible, while the massive stone wall of an old tower is just some yards to the east.
11584: Above the roof birds circle and chirp trying to spot food or a good place to build a nest. The roof is made of wooden planks and a small hatch opens to a ladder leading below. To the northeast, the old tower of Tharbad reaches up into the sky.
11586: The cylindrical roof is built of reddish bricks, while the very top is a small flat area of wooden, cracked planks. This is the highest place in Tharbad and from here it is easy to overlook the whole city. To the east the River Greyflood begins its journey; first a huge irregular area of branching rivulets, then getting smaller and smaller, it vanishes into the horizon.
11589: Here in the narrow corridor, the tapestries on the walls are old and withered. Bits and pieces of them lie on the floor where cockroaches have taken to hiding under them. At one end of the corridor, a small door opens to a dimly lit room from which no details can be seen. Light comes from the bottom of the stairs where the noise of the common patrons in the inn can be heard.
11590:
A Guard is here looking suspiciously at everyone passing.
A Guard is here looking suspiciously at everyone passing.
A Guard is here looking suspiciously at everyone passing.

Protected from the elements under the city's wide stone wall, this area serves as a checkpoint for watercraft entering and exiting Tharbad. Three torches hang from metal chains fastened to the high, arched walls on either side of a narrow channel. A constant trickle of sewage pours into the crystal clear water from a narrow pipe on the southern wall.
11591: Outside the East Gate of Tharbad

Klaees (thedon), wielding a heavy morningstar, is standing here.
Drazud (freshmeat), wielding a great warsword, is standing here.
Sza (smurfette), wielding a great warsword, is standing here.
Ducaht (tooprettytodie), wielding a great warsword, is standing here.
Bulg (pukespy), wielding a great warsword, is standing here.

Sparkling water pushes its way into the city through a large, rusted metal gate made of closely-spaced iron bars. Noises from the city come through unhindered, giving an aural glimpse of what lies beyond the high stone wall that looms high overhead. The Greyflood flows from the northeast.
11592: Situated just west of the city walls and beneath a small wooden bridge, this stretch of river is exceptionally calm. The murky water that collects here from the slow current smells of raw sewage. To the northwest, a narrow channel leads to a set of wooden docks.
11593: The water from the river mixes with a constant flow of rotten sewage pouring out of thin metal pipes protruding from nearby buildings. These houses and shops are built right up to the bank of the Greyflood. There are two bridges off in the distance to the west and east.
11594: Dirty water flows westwards towards a wide stone bridge off in the distance. Several pipes dump an abundance of russet coloured sewage into the river from the buildings on the north and south banks, producing a ripe smell of sewage. Notably, a wide path cuts between a few of the houses on the south bank.
11595: The wide stone bridge overhead provides little shelter from the elements. The wind still whistles as it slips under the bridge and past the rocks at the river's edge. As putrid water laps against the rocks, a faint sound of running water can be heard coming from the northern bank.
11596: A pungent odour rises from the river. The water is a concoction of sewage, garbage, slime and unknown muck as it collects on the bank. The main part of the river runs swiftly here, from the stone bridge towards the city gates in the west.
11597: The current slows and fragments momentarily as the river becomes choked with weed and debris, its force dispersed into small eddies and backwaters. Low banks patched with small clumps of hardy dun-coloured grasses border the polluted waterway as it flows towards the gated entrance to the west. A resident occasionally adds to the current a helping of garbage or perhaps the contents of a chamber-pot.
11598:
A Guard is here looking suspiciously at everyone passing.
A Guard is here looking suspiciously at everyone passing.
A Guard is here looking suspiciously at everyone passing.

Sheltered from the elements under the city's wide stone wall, this area serves as a checkpoint for watercraft coming into and out of Tharbad. On each side of the narrow waterway three large torches chained to the high arch of the walls sway in the light breeze. Barely audible above the noise from the city echoing in the arch, the dirty Greyflood murmurs and gurgles past a rusted metal gate.
11599: Outside the West Gate of Tharbad

Discoloured water and debris slowly pour out from the large, rusted metal gate just behind Tharbad's high stone wall, creating an opaque brown plume several hundred yards long. Occasionally a mutilated corpse surfaces for a second or two before diving beneath the murky waves to the unseen depths of the river.
11600: The water is polluted and murky. Half-disintegrated garbage litters the bottom along with slimy moss which collects on the loamy riverbed. Vision is obscured by the murkiness, and only the slight bumps from what feel like fishes can be discerned.
11601:
There are two solid oak desks here.
There are five wooden crates here.
A wealthy merchant is slowly strolling around here.

The entire building seems to be a large warehouse. Narrow aisles wind between shelves piled to the rafters with crates and boxes. The only large spaces are at the south and north ends of the room. To the south, two desks are facing a doorway, and in the north there is a set of iron gates.
11602: Outside the South Gate of Tharbad

Before you stands a huge wooden gate with great spars of iron traversing it. You have come before the southern gate of the City of Thieves, Tharbad. Who knows what adventures will befall you once inside this famous city.
11603: This is an ancient stone road built atop a causeway which rises high above the low and muddy landscape on either side. Here it bends from the east toward the north, where a city wall can be seen in the distance.
11605:
There are two gold coins here.
A large cockroach is crawling on the ground.
A large cockroach is crawling on the ground.

This room is rather large, but nevertheless appears cramped due to the sheer number of objects in it. Cabinets with open drawers are located to the far left. Stacked just beside is a random collection of boxes, barrels, and other miscellaneous valuables of such various types that you wonder, if they belong to the owner or represent illicitly garnered booty. On the opposite side of the chamber a large opening is broken into the wall.
11606: You stand in a small quiet tunnel. In the distance you can hear running water. Your light throws ugly shadows all over the walls behind you. Looking at the walls you can see that they have been carved out of the rock and there is water trickling down the tunnel sides. The tunnel runs east from here.
11607: The tunnel here is only maybe three feet across at the most. The tunnel being this narrow forces you to almost walk sideways like a crab as you sidle your way through the gloom. Off in the distance voices can be heard chattering away, but you are too far to make out what they are saying. From this point the tunnel continues east and west.
11608: The tunnel bends south and west here. Far in the distance you can hear the sound of running water and some faint voices chattering away. The water is running down the sides of the tunnel with more vigour than before and it is quite damp underfoot.
11609: There is a slight movement in the air here suggesting that you may be heading out. From here you can see that the tunnel continues north and south, off into the darkness. The sound of running water is getting steadily louder as you continue your journey.
11610:
The corpse of a mugger is lying here.
The corpse of a mugger is lying here.

You arrive a T-junction in the tunnel. To the east a side tunnel disappears off into the darkness. As you peer in that direction you realise that you can only see a few feet in front of your nose. The main tunnel continues north and south. To the south you can see a small landing lit by a few torches.
11611: The corpse of a vicious rat is lying here.

This tunnel is very narrow and very quiet. Looking at the dust and dirt on the ground you can only see a few sets of footprints giving the impression that this tunnel is not used a lot. Looking to the east you can see the tunnel disappearing off into the gloom.
11612: The tunnel walls seem to close in around you here. Further to the east the ceiling arches down to meet the wall, and a small round opening is set into the very centre. Closer inspection suggests that the only way that hole leads is down. The footprints in the dust stop leading east, and turn to the south here.
11613: You enter a small room with the main feature being a set of stairs spiralling up in the centre. Looking at these stairs you can see that they have been worn smooth by years of feet climbing up and down them. The only exit is back to north.
11614: A small vicious black rat squeaks at you for disturbing it.

A cramped and roughly formed chamber, this room has apparently not been made with any long-term use in mind. Its floor, walls and ceiling are uneven, and in places the marks of whatever tool was used to carve this niche still scar the cold stone. Only around the door is there any sign of precision, and the small round slab fits perfectly into the hole it has been created to fill. It would seem that secrecy is the main aim of this place.
11615:
A small vicious black rat squeaks at you for disturbing it.
A small vicious black rat squeaks at you for disturbing it.

The tunnel is cramped, with its rough-hewn walls making close approach to one another in many places. The floor is uneven, with sharp rocks sticking up here and there, and despite a number of twisted timbers, the roof above you bulges in several spots, as if on the verge of falling in. A foul, putrescent stench wafts in from the east, reminiscent of rotting flesh and human waste.
11616: A foul smell permeates the entire pit, and the floor underfoot is covered in some sort of thick, soft, moist, rotting matter. Far above your head a rough opening can be seen, and it would seem that perhaps this hole was made with a marked lack of care and skill, for occasionally a small stone or a flurry of dust will tumble down. However, as crude as it may have been, the effort was sufficient to create a functional refuse pit.
11617: A small vicious black rat squeaks at you for disturbing it.

This long tunnel has curved walls and such a low ceiling that it almost looks like a hobbit hole in its shape. But no halfling would live in such a dank and gloomy location. Water drips down the walls to form small, murky puddles on the floor, and slimy mould grows everywhere. A foul stench pervades the entire area, and the faint whisper of fresh air, which emanates from a shaft above your head, does little to freshen the atmosphere.
11618: A small vicious black rat squeaks at you for disturbing it.

Here the tunnel turns from west to north. Its smooth, curved walls are almost covered by a thick coating of green-grey mould, made slick by the chilly water, which seeps in through hairline cracks near the roof. A slightly rotten odour emanates from the slime, filling the air around you, but a faint, cool breeze drifting down from above offers a little relief.
11619: The tunnel stretches east from here, before making an abrupt turn to the north, but to the west it seems to reach a dead-end, with cold, dripping walls to every side. In places, the brickwork seems to bulge, as if it were straining to withstand the weight of ground and water beyond, which seem ever to be striving to reclaim this area as their own.
11620: A tall shaft opens up above your head, and high on the western wall what appears to be a small opening can be seen. Of course, it is hard to tell whether it is indeed so small, or just very far above you. The walls are made of old bricks, crumbling in places, and slick with a blanket of green-brown moss.
11621: The darkness here is all-engulfing, almost tangible, and to the north and south the progress of this narrow tunnel rapidly disappears from sight. The air is so still and damp that it feels suffocating, but from a narrow shaft, set at the very centre of the ceiling, a faint breath of fresh air can be felt. From somewhere in the distance the repetitive noise of dripping water can be heard.
11622: End of a Long, Low-Roofed Tunnel

The tunnel comes to an end here, blocked to the north by a rough brick wall. To the south, it stretches off into the darkness, and from somewhere in the distance the incessant plop of dripping water can be heard. Though the roof of the passage is quite low, a narrow shaft can be seen at its centre, and from far above comes a rumour of fresh cool air.
11623: Dank Chamber at the Tunnel's End

A shadow suddenly leaves its place on the wall, trying to reach your neck.
A shadow suddenly leaves its place on the wall, trying to reach your neck.
A dark intangible shadow turns to face you.

A chill air pervades the chamber, and a musty odour assails your nostrils. The room is small and rectangular, with a high ceiling and a perfectly even floor. Three of the walls are made up of smooth blocks of stone, precisely placed, and mortared with such care that even the seeping water has not done much damage over the years. However, the fourth wall appears to have been constructed in haste, with rough bricks and no mortar.
11636:
A heavy desk, made of solid oak, stands here.
A large bookshelf sits against the wall.
On the bookshelf, there are a map of Bree, a map of Tharbad, and a map of Fornost.
A burly bodyguard stands here, a dour expression on his face.
A burly bodyguard stands here, a dour expression on his face.
The Master Assassin gazes at you with the cold eyes of a killer.

This large, square chamber is rather ostentatious. The walls are draped with heavy tapestries whose sombre hues seem to swallow light. A large midnight- blue carpet covers much of the floor, and the centre of the room is dominated by an imposing oak desk. Wrought iron brackets of eleborate design secure torches to each wall, casting a soft, dim light throughout the area, and to one end of the room, a thick velvet curtain is drawn back to reveal a massive oak bed covered with fine linens. Half-hidden by a corner of the carpet, a fairly small square hole has been cut into the floor against the left wall of the room, not far from the bed.
11637: The entire area is little larger than the small arched opening which leads into it from the chamber to the north. The roof is low, barely allowing a grown man to stand upright, and the floorspace is dominated by a rough hole, leaving little room to move about. From somewhere below, a slightly rank odour wafts upwards.
11638: A slender but well-muscled man seems to melt into the shadows.

The walls of this large chamber are made from huge blocks of stone. They have aged well, but here and there hairline cracks can be seen, and through these chilly water seeps slowly in, dripping to the flagstone floor, where it forms tiny puddles. Stout oak beams support the roof of the room, but toward one end the ceiling seems to sag, as if the weight of earth above were finally winning its battle to bury this construction.
11639:
The corpse of an experienced assassin is lying here.
A small oaken table has been set here.

Though uneven in places and obviously very old, the flagstone floor of this commodious hall has stood the test of time well. The walls are showing some signs of their age however, and in places water seeps in slowly through hairline cracks. The roof of the chamber is supported by stout oak beams, and only such a hard wood could have continued to brace such a heavy burden despite the damp and mould.
11640:
A canoe has been left here.
A canoe has been left here.
A sturdy trained horse is standing here.
A sturdy trained horse is standing here.

You arrive at a small landing where a couple of boats have been tethered to a small dock. The landing is lit by a couple of torches mounted on the wall by some metal brackets. There are quite a few footprints in the dirt on the ground suggesting this place is used quite frequently by the criminal elements of Tharbad.
11641: Tall pillars rise up out of the water. The air here is dark and gloomy with a hint of death encompassing it like a shroud. Your lights reflect off the water giving everything around you an evil, eerie feel. Looking at the pillars you see that they have been carved with letters that have been worn away and you are unable to read them.

A weary slave who has lost all hope sits here staring into space.
A weary slave who has lost all hope sits here staring into space.
A weary slave who has lost all hope sits here staring into space.

You arrive out of the water at quite a large landing with a couple of piers extending out into the water. All around you there are slaves loading up small boats with what must be contraband of some sort or other. To the east you can see a passage lit by torches on the walls.
11654: This passage is well lit and there seems to be a lot of traffic heading up and down the passage. Along the walls at regular intervals are torches mounted on stout iron brackets. The passage continues east and west.
11655: A smuggler is here, angry at having been seen.

The passage widens a bit here and to the south you can see a large warehouse filled with crates and boxes. Along the passage trudge slaves laden with crates and other sundry items. There seems to be a lot of liquor and pipe-weed passing through this area. The warehouse is to the south and the passage continues west.
11656: The smell here makes you want to vomit. All around you lies death and decay. There are bits of rotting food lying about as well as bits of rotting slaves. Whoever the slaver is he certainly has no care about his slaves.
11657: Tordol the Dwarf (t), wielding a mighty dwarven axe, is standing here.

This room has been well furnished by its owners with soft and comfortable looking chairs. In the centre of the room stands a large table with the remains of what must have been quite a lavish meal. Gaudy lamps light the room, giving it a sense of misplaced wealth. To the west is a large and strong-looking door, while to the south is the smugglers' bunk room.
11658: A large cavern opens up before you, in it all around you are crates and boxes of merchandise. Some of the crates are stacked neatly into columns which reach up almost to the ceiling, while some of the others lie littered around you. The warehouse continues east and south from here, but you notice a small door to the west.
11659:
An experienced smuggler is here, conspiring with his cohorts.
A weary slave who has lost all hope sits here staring into space.
A weary slave who has lost all hope sits here staring into space.

As you proceed through the warehouse you notice signs of an active slave trade here. Amongst the boxes and crates lie some empty manacles and chains probably used by some slave who has outlived his usefulness. From here the cavern continues east, south, and west
11660: The walls of the cavern loom up to the east and north here blocking off any further passage in those directions. There are many boxes and crates stacked very close together making your life very difficult as you try to squeeze between them. All around you can hear echoes of screams as the slaves are beaten on with their work.
11661: A smuggler is here, angry at having been seen.

You have reached the far corner of the cavern and the heart of the Smuggler's domain. To the east you notice a small inconspicuous door. From behind the door you can hear some heated arguments on various topics of smuggling. The cavern continues north and west.
11662:
The chief of smugglers is here, planning his next move.
An experienced smuggler is here, conspiring with his cohorts.
An experienced smuggler is here, conspiring with his cohorts.
The chief of smugglers is here, planning his next move.

This is a small room with a large table in the centre of it. Across the table are littered some large maps an drawings. Across the walls are more maps, there are also many timetables and plans crudely hanging on it. The room is lit by a solitary lantern standing on the table.
11663:
An experienced smuggler is here, conspiring with his cohorts.
A weary slave who has lost all hope sits here staring into space.
A weary slave who has lost all hope sits here staring into space.
