The cavern widens out a bit here and the crates and boxes aren't packed so close together, making your progress easier. Around you slaves and smugglers run about their business. You receive agonising looks from the slaves and evil glares from the smugglers. The Warehouse continues north, east and west.
11664: A smuggler is here, angry at having been seen.

The cavern sides rise up to your south and west here, blocking all further passage in those directions. You have to breathe in deeply in order to squeeze through the gaps in the columns of crates and boxes. The warehouse continues to the east and to the north.
11665:
An experienced smuggler is here, conspiring with his cohorts.
An experienced smuggler is here, conspiring with his cohorts.

This room is quite lavishly furnished, there are some soft and comfortable looking beds against the eastern wand western walls. The room is lit by some expensive looking lanterns. Across the southern wall is a large tapestry depicting events from Arda's history. The only exit is back to the north.
11666:
A musty loaf of bread has been left here.
A musty loaf of bread has been left here.
A musty loaf of bread has been left here.
A weary slave who has lost all hope sits here staring into space.
A weary slave who has lost all hope sits here staring into space.

The room is very bare and spartan apart from a few shackles chained to the wall the room has no other fixtures at all. A few straw beds lie in the corners of the room. All the slaves seem to have to eat is a few rotting morsels littered about the room.
11667:
A wooden chest stands in the corner.
A spirit floats towards you and howls with an evil laughter.
A spirit floats towards you and howls with an evil laughter.

This is a small cave that seems to have been used as a treasure chamber since it is filled with old coffins, chests and the like. But it is obvious that the treasure is history. Nearly all the chests are empty and most are broken or rotten. The smell of death hangs heavily in the air and some bones and skulls can be spotted between the coffins. The only exit is up through a small niche.
11668:
A longsword is on the ground.
A rusty pickaxe with a broken handle lies discarded here.
A giant rat patters against you, squeaking maliciously.
A giant rat patters against you, squeaking maliciously.
A giant rat patters against you, squeaking maliciously.

This cave is quite large and appears to have been set aside for the storage of weapons sometime in the past. Judging by the racks of rusting swords and axes, the people who built these tunnels had some other pastime apart from tunnelling. The cave extends to the north where it seems to be more narrow.
11669:
A greenish slime mould is here, smelling badly.
A rather heavy clay jar stands here.
A musty loaf of bread has been left here.

This place seems to be some kind of a storage cave. Around you are many jars and casks, most of which are cracked or broken into pieces. At some point this had probably been a food store for the many workers digging these tunnels. The cave continues to the south, where it seems to widen. Water is dripping from the stone ceiling.
11670:
A water moccasin slithers out of sight just below the surface of the water.
A water moccasin slithers out of sight just below the surface of the water.

The cavern walls here are dark, cold and moist, obviously due to the cold and foully smelling black and brown water that fills this pool from wall to wall. The smell from the water seems to be stronger in the larger cavern to the west. A small stream of bubbles rises to the surface from the cold stone below.
11671: The landing in the middle of the intersection is surrounded by dark, dirty water that seems to be the source of the awful smell that is filling this place. The squeaking noises all around make the darkness seem even deeper than it is. On all sides of the landing a shallow pool extends, except to the south where a narrow dark tunnel can be seen.
11672: The narrow tunnel is dark and filled with foully smelling, dirty water. The stench seems to grow to the north. The tunnel ceiling is quite low here, making it impossible to move without crawling. The walls are cold and moist. The tunnel continues west and north, where it leads into a large cavern.
11673:
A patch of moss grows here on a wet, flat stone.
A giant slug is here, oozing around.
A giant slug is here, oozing around.

This part of the pool reaches a small platform on the northern wall, which is covered with an oozing slime which makes your feet stick to the ground. The entire north wall is also covered in the slime, and the water here is dark-brown and foully smelling. To the south you can see a wooden landing.
11674:
A giant rat patters against you, squeaking maliciously.
A giant rat patters against you, squeaking maliciously.

This passage is quite dry and is climbing upwards to the north, possibly on a way out of the sewers. The walls are jagged, with shards of rock sticking out as if to catch at the clothing of anybody who passes too close to them. The southern wall is different from the rest in that it is covered in slime.
11675: A giant rat patters against you, squeaking maliciously.

This appears to be the end of a southward passage. To the north is a dark and sombre-looking door with a heavy iron lock on it. The air here is reasonably clean and there is a slight breeze coming from the direction of the door, indicating that this might be the way out.
11676: A black snake hurries towards you with sly intentions.

In this small enclosed room with an opening in the ceiling the walls are covered with old gobelins depicting various scenes of death and murder. Skulls and bones, apparently the remains of unlucky adventurers, lie all around. Two doors lead out of the room: a small wooden door in the eastern wall and a heavy iron door in the southern wall. A set of wooden stairs leads to the opening in the low ceiling.
11677: Looking around would lead you to believe that no one has ventured into these sewers for centuries. The walls of the tube are all rusted and sections of the tube have collapsed completely. Though the damage is not bad enough to stop you from travelling in either the easterly or westerly directions.
11678:
The corpse of an assassin is lying here.
The corpse of a vicious rat is lying here.
The corpse of a bandit is lying here.

If you look carefully you can see thin wisps of steam or smoke rising up from the sludge at your feet as it winds its way down to some outlet far beyond this point. As you trudge along in the dark bits of the sewer walls and ceiling flake off and land on you soiling your clothes and body. From this point the tube continues east and west.
11679: A small vicious black rat squeaks at you for disturbing it.

You drop down into a large, cylindrical tube. The first thing that hits you is the awful stench coming from whatever is crawling its way through the tube. The walls are almost perfectly smooth and made of some metal that has rusted away long ago. The tube continues east and west here with a room above you through a small hole in the ceiling.
11680:
A vicious little bandit advances towards you.
A vicious little bandit advances towards you.
A small vicious black rat squeaks at you for disturbing it.

This part of the tube has been destroyed by an earthquake or a cave-in. It is impossible to continue your journey any further west because large boulders block the way. There is a small niche in the wall.
11681: You are down the main pit of the old sewers, but you are not sure that the first use of all this part is to carry out sewage from the city! You can go up or south.
11682: A vicious little bandit advances towards you.
You are in a passage leading north and west. You feel that you are not the only one down here. As you look at the ground you notice some footsteps in the dust.
11683: You are in a small, dank cave and a lot of broken bottles lie on the floor. The walls are covered by some sort of moisture. There are stairs leading up and a way west.
11684: The ceiling of the passage is low and drips with moisture. Set deeply in the brick walls there are three doors: a red one to the north, a green one to the west and a black one to the south. To the east the passage opens up a little.
11685:
A giant rat patters against you, squeaking maliciously.
A giant rat patters against you, squeaking maliciously.

As you peer into the darkness all about you all you can see are the dark and gloomy walls of the tunnel. On closer inspection it becomes apparent that this tunnel was built in a great hurry. The surrounding air is damp and musty, which altogether makes it very unpleasant to breathe. To the south the tunnel continues.
11686: You begin to wonder if any type of light could penetrate this darkness. The air is also getting staler and staler as you continue your journey. On the wall to your left you notice some crude scribblings. Looking around you notice an old beam across the ceiling with a rope dangling from it providing a way down. Otherwise the tunnel runs west.
11687: This small cave contains a pool of water. The water here is stale and not fit for drinking and one can only wonder if anything could survive in it. The cave walls are dark grey, with water running down them making them look even darker. Darkness conceals the sources of many noises, some of them apparently made by something living. A tunnel begins to the south.
11688: A patch of moss grows here on a wet, flat stone.

This part of the tunnel is filled with dirty, brown water from wall to wall, the uneven floor muddy and making it very hard to move. Water drips from the ceiling soaking you right through as if attempting to make you thoroughly miserable. The stench from the water is extreme. The tunnel leads north and east. To the east, the tunnel seems to climb upwards.
11689: The tunnel runs east-west, brown and foul-smelling water filling it from wall to wall. Water is running down the walls in small streams, and the level of water in the tunnel seems to rise. The water level appears to be lower in the eastern part of the tunnel and higher in the western part.
11690: The water is shallow here and not so hard to wade through, but it is very dirty, murky and foul-smelling. The impenetrable darkness makes it hard to figure out where the different noises are coming from, but it is apparent that something living is causing most of them. To the east, a bridge looms out of the darkness and with it maybe a spot where you could dry yourself off a bit. The tunnel continues to the west here.
11691: This old bridge looks as if it had seen better days and doesn't look as if it could now support much weight. The ropes attaching it to either side of the dark chasm are old and frayed. It might be a good idea to hurry across and not dally here.
11692: A patch of moss grows here on a wet, flat stone.

The long narrow tunnel is filled with dark brown water from wall to wall. The water exudes a foul smell, which somehow appears very fitting for the surroundings. The ceiling of the tunnel is so low that only a hobbit could pass here without stooping. The tunnel continues to the east, while to the west it crosses an old bridge.
11693:
A giant rat patters against you, squeaking maliciously.
A giant rat patters against you, squeaking maliciously.
A giant rat patters against you, squeaking maliciously.

As you trudge along this tunnel it dawns on you that it was built very quickly and abandoned soon after that. Bits of ceiling keep falling on your head along with the odd drop of water. The tunnel continues east and west.
11694:
A giant rat patters against you, squeaking maliciously.
A giant rat patters against you, squeaking maliciously.

The tunnel is very wet and slippery here because of the water dripping from the ceiling and running down the walls. The state of the tunnel is also much worse than the one you entered into. The tunnel continues east and west.
11695: The floor cracks and groans, suddenly giving way beneath your feet. Sailing down a chute of water, swirling around you faster and faster it is clear why this tunnel was abandoned. Looking sharply for something to grab a hold of, fragments of torn clothing on jagged rocks dance around your view.
11696:
A large brown snake with black patches is coiled here.
A large brown snake with black patches is coiled here.

As you come round after your fall the first thing you notice is the taste of blood in your mouth. After that you realise you must have fallen into this cave. Looking around in the gloom you can see lots of skeletons. On closer inspection you notice that these are of many different races. You sit yourself down and wonder if you shall have the same fate as them.
11697:
A water moccasin slithers out of sight just below the surface of the water.
A water moccasin slithers out of sight just below the surface of the water.
A water moccasin slithers out of sight just below the surface of the water.

Water fills a narrow passage that opens into a larger cavern to the east. A disgusting smell flows from the direction of the large cavern. The walls here are dark, cold and moist, and there is no ledge or landing onto which one could climb out of the cold water. It is hard to see anything in the murky pool, but one thing is certain: something else lives here.
11698: A thief lurks here, looking for a stranger to rob (hidden).

The smell rising up from the sewage starts to remove the linings from your nose and throat. The tube you are standing in is about six feet in diameter and his half filled with sewage which seems to crawl its way instead of run. The dark side of this cylinder loom up as the tube bends south and west here.
11699: You are at the end of the tube, here the sewage forms a small pool before slowly seeping away through some hidden exit. From the ceiling another small tube enters this one, but you seem to be too large to enter it. The southern wall has been finished by a wall of bricks making it impossible to carry on.
11700: Here the thieves come together to plan their dastardly deeds, raids on other towns and villages, smuggling goods up and down the Greenway. On a large table some tankards have been forgotten. There are a few chairs set casually around the table. On the east wall there is a map. The only exit is north.
11701: A thief is here looking for some stranger to rob.

It seems you are in a cul-de-sac! There are red paintings on the walls describing a bloody fight. This is a warrior fighting an awful monster that you can't recognise. The only exit is west in a red room.
11702: You enter a room which has been painted completely in red. Across the walls there are many paintings of men clad in black and in various poses. There is a corridor leading north and another room to the west.
11703: The walls of this room are covered in paintings too but, these paintings depict scenes of horrific mass murder. The paintings begin to make you wonder how they got the walls of this room so red.
11704: You are in a corridor leading north and south. The walls are all painted red and on them hang many paintings of foul beasts being slain by men clad in black from head to toe wielding some magical looking daggers.
11705: End of the Corridor Daubed in Red

It seems that all of this part of the sewers has been painted red, the reason for this escapes you. In this room, a painting describing a beautiful landscape coves all the available wall space. You don't recognise this area of Arda but you feel very oppressed by these paintings.
11706: A large bulletin board, entitled "Assassins'", is mounted here.

After having gone through a small tunnel, you arrive in a small dark room. The tables are barrels, the chairs were cut from trunks. Some candles on the tables glow with a yellow shadowed light. Some people are here, all the conversation has stopped and a couple of brightening eyes have frozen your soul. This place could be the meeting point of some pirates. Some of the people have a patch on one eye, and all have a sharpened knife worn at belt. After a moment the conversation starts again...in whispers.
11707:
The corpse of a bandit is lying here.
A man dressed in dark clothes eyes his surroundings warily.
This is the secret guild of Tharbad. The walls are painted in red with torches fastened on them. The exit is west.
11709:
The corpse of an assassin is lying here.
Tsunami the Mountain Troll is standing here.
Malibu the Cave Troll, wielding an ornate, steel-shafted warhammer, is standing here.
Bunk the Cave Troll is standing here.
Olrome the Black Numenorean, wielding a steel claymore, is standing here.
Bos the Cave Troll is standing here.

You descend down a flight of old and rickety stairs to arrive at this point. Looking up you can see some faint light coming from the bar above. To the north a tunnel leads off into the darkness. The sides of the tunnel are smooth and a small stream of dirty water flows at your feet.
11710: You are in a tunnel that is going right north. The passage seems to be very ancient. You see some light coming from the south, but to the north it is dark.
11711: A thief lurks here, looking for a stranger to rob.

You are in a junction that allows you to go in four directions. To the west, you hear something like falling water. To the east is a corridor which seems to be in a very bad shape. The tunnel continues north and south.
11712:
A domesticated pony, beast of burden to many, stands here.
A domesticated pony, beast of burden to many, stands here.

You are in a tunnel leading north and south. The air is fresh here as well as cold. Looking on the walls around, you see splatters of dried blood. The blood probably belongs to some long forgotten adventurer who dared to come down here to make his fortune.
11713: You are standing over a large, gaping hole, it's very dark down there. If you listen closely your can hear screams rising out of the darkness. There are stairs to your left leading down into the darkness.
11714: You stand in a small kitchen. There is table on the corner and chairs nearby. Many tracks can be seen in the dust on the stone floor. There is an exit to the east and a door to the south.
11715: You are in a sleeping room. There are some beds made of wood and a table. Everything is so quiet here, you start to shiver and feel like going away. You can go west to the kitchen.
11716: A simple wooden chest is here.
You enter a small room which is filled with what must be all the Chief's loot from all of the dodgy dealings that he must of had up until now.
11717: You are in an old secret sector! You see a table and chairs around it. There is a bed on the corner of the room and a lot of dust is covering everything. You notice some tracks leading north and stairs leading down.
11718: A thief lurks here, looking for a stranger to rob (hidden).

You stand in a corridor, which is in poor condition. Rocks are scattered on the floor, making it hazardous to move about. Along with cracks lining the walls are some scratches, which catch your attention.
11719:
A large torch lies here among the dust.
A small campfire burns here, its low flames giving off only a little light.
The corpse of an assassin is lying here.
As you advance down this corridor, you can see the state of the tunnel get steadily worse and worse. It would not be a good idea to continue your journey east.
11720: This corridor has collapsed. You can go no further, due to the stones, earth, and wooden beams that block your path. A pool of blood seeps out from the pile of rocks...
11721: Big blocks of rock are blocking your way further west. A noise of water is coming from behind the stones. The only exit seems to be east.
11722:
The wild ox seems ready to charge you.
The wild ox seems ready to charge you.

You constantly hear the sound of grasshoppers around you. Larger plants seem to be rare in this area. To the north you see some field with green grass, but the land seems to become even more dry to the east.
11723: The grass is not as green as maybe it should be. The landscape is beginning to seem dry, allowing only a few plants to grow. You can see that the great Dunland Flats stretch out in all directions around you.
11724: The grass grows sparsely here. Some small bugs crawl between the blades on the ground. Here you see the distinct tracks of many hooved animals. North and west you see more flat land, but east you see the silhouette of a very large tree against the horizon.
11725: A long-necked bird, with a fairly short spear-like bill stands here.

A gigantic tree, at least a hundred feet high is standing here. It doesn't have any leaves, but can still give protection from the sun or the rain if you stand on the right side of it. North and west you see flat, dry land. However, east you see a small waterhole.
11726:
A black pond of water is here.
A snowy-white egret stands here alertly.

Some green bushes grow near this waterhole, almost hiding the remains of some large animal. It is only the skeleton that is left. Obviously it has been lying here for a very long time. The water in the waterhole is somewhat dark and perfectly still. Some flies are swarming near the bushes. This waterhole must be what's supplying the huge tree to the west with water. North and east the land is flat and dry.
11727: Thin grass covers the ground here along with some small plants. Once this land probably was a fine grazing field. Small insects fly around here. There is a hill to the north and some flat land to the east. West you see a pool of water.
11728:
A swarm of midges is here, humming around you.
A fat rabbit sits here, chewing on some grass.
A swarm of midges is here, humming around you.

Gradually the land becomes more and more fertile to the south. Large areas of grassy plains and fields stretch southward far into the skyline. Here the rich soil supports plenty of plant life and is carpeted by a layer of lush green grass. Vegetation becomes more sparse to the north while the fertile land con- tinues to the east.
11729: A fat rabbit sits here, chewing on some grass.

The southern region of this region is fertile and lush with a thick carpet of green grass. Numerous patches of mid-length wild grass provide ample shelter and food for various small-sized wild animals. Rabbits especially seem to be the predominant wild-life. Vegetation becomes sparse north of here while the fertile land continues both east and west of here.
11730:
Yellow flowers, with grey-green foliage, grow in clusters here.
A snake slithers towards you.

Here the Old South Road turns southward and disappears into the thick grassy layers that stretch out to the south. It is impossible to make out the road around the bend. Small clusters of flower and brush are scattered around the large field. Northwards the land becomes more fertile and the flora more rich. Eastward the road continues on its way.
11731: A well preserved road here can be seen clearly running through the grass field. That is probably because the road overlays the field by a few inches and no plants have been able to take root among the closely spaced cracks. Fertile grassy plains and fields surround the road. A barren plain lies to the east while the road continues north and westwards.
11732: Yellow flowers, with grey-green foliage, grow in clusters here.

As it steadily continues towards the lands of Gondor, the Old South Road runs in an almost straight line. Scattered along the sides of the almost invisible road lie the remnants of the old stone markers that indicated the road. Otherwise the area is covered by a thick grass layer dotted with small groups of flowers. Along the eastern side the remnants of an old stone fence can be seen while westward lies a more fertile land. South and north of here the road continues.
11733: The once well used road from Gondor to Fornost can barely be seen amidst the rich flora here. More or less broken and hidden beneath the grass lie the remnants of the old stonework that once was laid here near the intersection. Flowers of many kinds and colours coming from different places of the area have made their roots here. Along the the eastern side of the road what was once a stone fence now lies in a heap of crumbled rock. The road continues to the south while north it enters an intersection. West of here lies a flat plain.
11734: A crumbling fountain is in the middle of the place.

Here the road runs into an intersection. Scattered around it are several old ruins. Perhaps remnants of the houses of those that once inhabited these lands. There seem to have been several buildings, on both sides of the road. Maybe it once was a small village. What seems to once have been a fountain of some kind can still be seen at the south side of the road. Westward and southward the Old South Road runs, while the ruins continue to the east along the Road of the Smiths. The way north of here is blocked by the ruins of a fallen house.
11735: Here the road is broader and higher compared to other parts of the road. Mostly due to the frequent flooding by the bordering swamps and the resulting muddy residue. North of here are the swamps that are so typical for this area. West of here the road becomes narrower while east of here some sort of ruins lie along the road. South lie the remnants of what was once a cultivated area.
11736:
A wild bull seems ready to charge you.
A brown fox is here, looking for some rabbits to chew up.

Encouraged by the moist and fertile soil, massive looking weeds flourish and dominate the northern part of this field. The exit to the road is almost barred by the intertwining high growth. Southwards the weeds give over to a turf of short sturdy wild grass. Here and there various kind of wild flowers spot the land among small thickets of bushes. East of here is a road of some kind while west of here the plains continue. South of here the grass seems to merge into a flowery field.
11737: This is the road that will take you to the south gates of Tharbad. But it will also take you far south if you follow it in that direction. The road is built on a long causeway. From here you see the river Greyflood is to your north and you see some marshy ground down the slope to your east.
11738: The road goes north and east here. From the road you can travel straight west without going down a slope and get to a small hill. Down the southern slope you can barely notice a small trail leading down and in through the grassy field, where it seems to disappear.
11739: The road bends here and goes west and south, built on a causeway. What catches your eye is a massive pile of dead trees to the east. It seems to block your way to the Swanfleet swamp, but you also see swamp to the north.
11740: A wiry smuggler is here, attempting to avoid being seen.

The elevated road twists here and goes north to east. Down the slope to the northeast there is a swamp named Nen-in-Eilph, but the view is blocked by black, rotten, dead trees. You see plains to the south and some extraordinarily grassy field to the west.
11741: You're on the Old south road, leading from Tharbad in the northwest through the Dunland in the south. The road will take you west or south here. There is a swamp down a gentle slope to your east, but north some huge, black trees have fallen and are blocking the way.
11743: This is a bend in the Old South Road leading west and south. The road slopes slightly on its northern and eastern sides, which border a swamp of some sort.
11744: Here the Old South Road bends and goes from the east to the north. To the east the road slopes downwards and levels out with the ground level. You get the feeling that you're not too far away from a city, mostly because there is a small tower visible to the northwest. South you only see plains.
11745: The old broken road continues its way through the deserted land. Overgrown with grass and littered with rubble, the road is in bad shape from lack of use. Endless swamps stretch out northward and eastward across the flat landscape. Far in the east faint outlines of a structure of some kind are barely visible. South and west of here the road stretches on.
11746: Severely cracked and full of holes and bumps, the dull road winds itself in a north and easterly direction. A sort of thick brown weed is the only plantlife visible. The border of the road is partly immersed in water that has overflowed from the swamp area that lies just northeast of here. To the south and west the land stretches out into barren plains.
11747: Although old and decaying due to lack of use, the road here is still sturdy and compact. Healthy vegetation crowds alongside and sometimes onto the old road. North of here a swampy area stretches out. West and eastward the road continues while south of here lies a large flat plain.
11748: The grassy field here is awash with a rainbow carpet of blooming wild flowers. Countless species vie for attention from nectar seeking insects with bright hues of red, white, yellow, purple and pink. East of here the faint outline of the Old South Road can be seen while west of here lies a rather dry looking plain.
11749: A fat rabbit sits here, chewing on some grass.

Dotted across the plain are thickets of various sizes and shapes. Here the ground is fertile and sustains a thick carpet of sturdy short wild grass. Winding its way slowly southwards is a small rivulet. The water carries with it an unpleasant stench. Plains stretch in all directions.
11750:
A woody evergreen plant grows here, with many stems reaching upward.
A fat rabbit is here, chewing on some grass.
A fat rabbit is here, chewing on some grass.
A fat rabbit is here, chewing on some grass.
The wild ox seems ready to charge you.
A snake slithers towards you.

Here the land is dry and a bit sandy compared to the areas north of here. The thin topsoil makes it hard for anything to grow here, but a few thorny thickets have managed to take root. The whole region is rather flat and dreary. Far to the northeast a structure of some sort is barely visible. The plains continue in all directions.
11751: A squirrel scampers around here, looking for nuts from the trees.

A slight wind seems to blow perpetually around this bluff, setting loose a little topsoil, which is readily blown away, as there is little grass here to anchor it. The view is excellent, letting you see the endless plains to the south and east. There is flat land in all directions, but far southwest you see something that looks like a small pond.
11752: Dry and dusty, only allowing thin blades of grass grow in small turfs, this steppe also shows signs of hoofed animals moving around. North and west there is more flat landscape. East you see a bluff of some kind and there is a waterhole to the south.
11753: A wild bull seems ready to charge you.

These plains are arid and dry. Very little grass is growing here. The top layer of the soil is not bound to the ground by roots and lots of grass thus it's loose. East and west you see flat land. North the land seems a bit more vegetated, and south you see something resembling to a huge tree.
11754: A wild bull seems ready to charge you.

Small piles of dirt and soil lay here and there, violently torn up from the ground by what seems to be some hoofed animals. The grass has been torn away, revealing the soil upon which it used to grow. In every direction you look there is plain, flat land.
11755: A small brown snake is slithering around here.

Short, dry grass on the ground an occasional bush can be seen here. A small snake hurries for cover and disappears. The vegetation seems to increase in the north west direction and decrease to the south east.
11756: The grass is low, but still quite thick. There are some small holes in the ground which probably serve as entrance to some small animal dwelling. Where the trail is the grass is flat against the ground and it leads north and west. East and south you see some flat grassland.
11757: This is a field with thick, high grass which hides a small trail. The trail makes a turn here and goes in an east-south direction. When you look around you there is only more flat land to be seen in all directions.
11758: Standing on the small trail, which cuts through the dense grass, you see flat land all around you. East you see some low-grass plains and it seems as the landscape is getting kind of arid the more south you move. You can follow the path north or west through some more fields.
11759: The ground is not very capable of providing plants and grass with nutrition and water it seems, as it is sparsely covered. There are more plains in all directions, but the vegetation seems just a bit more dense to the west.
11760: A wild bull seems ready to charge you.

Flat land with thin, low grass is all around you. Some insects fly by as you turn your head around and watch the vast plains. The plains to the north seem to have more dense grass while the ones south seems to show signs of lack of water. West and east you also see more plains.
11761:
A young colt is frolicking playfully.
A wild bull seems ready to charge you.

Apparently this area is favoured by bugs and insects. They seem to like crawling on the blades of the grass and jumping to another one. The grass is short and here and there you see a small plant. Wherever you look you see more plains, but the southern ones seem a bit arid.
11762: A wild bull seems ready to charge you.

The grass shifts and ripples as insects jump out of your path just before you catch a clear look at them. There is no sign of civilisation on these seemingly endless plains, and it has perhaps been a long time since anyone chose to walk across these lands.
11763:
A fat rabbit is here, chewing on some grass.
A fat rabbit is here, chewing on some grass.

A large wasteland marks the beginning of the flat plains that continue to the south towards the area known as Enedhwaith. Here the plains are rather muddy due to the murky swamp that fills the area north of the road. No vegetation flourishes here except for a few blades of yellow sickly grass. The plains continue to the east, west and south.
11764: Thick dark mud occupies the plains here alongside the road. South of here the plain becomes more dry and green with grass. North of here is a large swampy area that dominates the region. Grassy rolling plains gradually flatten out to the south. The plains continue both east and west and to the south.
11765: A wild bull seems ready to charge you.
You are on some grassy plains which are bordered by the Old South Road to the north and east. The plains continue south and west from here.
11766:
A starving cow stands here, looking for a patch of grass.
A starving cow stands here, looking for a patch of grass.
A wild bull seems ready to charge you.
A wild bull seems ready to charge you.
A wild bull seems ready to charge you.

The grass seems to grow badly here. The ground does not seem to be able to nourish the grass and the plants that once grew here. Looking north you can see a high tower, but you see no entrance from this direction.
11767: Grass beneath your feet and grasshoppers jumping around you. Yes this is the plains of the south. An enormous area of plains stretches out before you. It is a very calm place you're in and the fresh wind gently fans your face.
11768:
A squirrel scampers around here, looking for nuts from the trees.
A wild bull seems ready to charge you.

A light breeze sets some tall blades swaying slowly. This is a very quiet and tranquil place. The only thing which disturbs the silence is the sound of the wind in your ears. When you look around you all you can see is plains in all directions.
11769: This is a small trail leading north and south. The blades of the grass have been bent at the ground, trampled. The trail is barely noticeable when you're just a few feet off it. Someone is using this regularly, but for what and where does it lead?
11770: Grass and small plants grow around you. Walking through the grass you hear something moving behind you. When you turn around you only see the furry tail of some animal disappearing behind some small bush. Looking around you, you see plains in all directions.
11771: A few small animals are dashing from one small shrubbery to another on these plains which lay by the side of some river you see to your west. In the other directions you just see more plains.
11772: You are by the riverside of the Greyflood, which is to your west and also to the north. The water is gently flowing along the shore line south-west. To the east and south you see plains stretching out before you.
11773: The wild ox seems ready to charge you.

Walking on the small trail, made by trampling feet only, you see plains all around you, except for a wedge-shaped hill to the east. You can't seem to climb it from this direction, but the south side seems to have a nice slope.
11774: This is an odd-looking hill. Having its slope to the south and all other sides of it unclimbable makes it look like a wedge. However, something that cannot be seen from anywhere but here is a hole in the hill, leading down. Right by the hole there are a few bones of some creature. The hill is surrounded by plains, but there is a road to the north-east.
11775: These plains are surrounded by a bending road to the north and east. Looking west you see there's a hill that looks like a wedge, its slope in the southly direction. Some more plains can be seen to the south.
11776:
A wild bull seems ready to charge you.
A squirrel scampers around here, looking for nuts from the trees.

The grass here is about a foot in height, and looking around you you see more plains of this kind in all directions but east. There you see a thin, but quite high tower. It looks like a watch tower of some kind. You can see no entrance on this side, but a few black windows stare at you from the top.
11778: Grass surrounds you. A few insects are humming around you as you notice there is a slope to the north which could be a hill of some kind. South, north and west you see more plains.
11779: The wild ox seems ready to charge you.

Hidden in the grass is this trail. You figure it's been used not too long ago, or the grass would have covered it rather quickly. There is a hill visible far to the north-east. Otherwise the only thing you see around you is plains.
11780:
A squirrel scampers around here, looking for nuts from the trees.
A colourful butterfly is fluttering around here.

This trail is barely noticeable in the grass. Apparently it's not being used too often. The trail makes a bend here, leading south from the east. A small hill can be seen to the north, while you see a shore of a river to the west.
11781: From here you can see the city of Tharbad not far north of here. You also see water when you look down the hill to the west. You see a road to the east and to the south you see a plain with a small trail cutting through it.
11782: The trail is almost hidden in the high grass. It's not even a trail, it looks more like the tall grass is bent in a certain direction, indicating someone has been walking here. The Old South Road can be seen here to the north and east. To the south you can see a high hill which is too steep to climb. The trail continues westwards from here.
11792: The grass is short and well-tended. There are many different plants and flowers growing in the flower-bed which borders the lawn. On the other side of the flower-bed the vegetation becomes quite tangled, and going that way is inconvenient; but there is a path which leaves the garden to the west and plunges abruptly down a muddy bank into the dense brush.
11793: This is a small cabin which has been packed with seemingly hundreds of trophies, bones, artefacts, "treasures", pieces of driftwood, skulls, polished stones, and pieces of nautical equipment of known and unknown functions. Most of these things seem water-worn, chipped, cracked, or rusted, and none of it has any apparent value; but it has all been carefully sorted, cleaned, and securely mounted on every available inch of wall space, with the overflow nailed to the rafters overhead. The owner of this cabin has apparently hauled this entire trove out of the river, piece by piece, through years of proud, if pointless, industry.
11794: The vegetation here is mostly reeds and grass, with some clumps of bushes near muddy sloughs. North and west of here it grows even dense, suggesting a river or lake lies in that direction. A path rises up a steep bank to the east, coming from there. Looking south you see more of this bushy, wet land.
11795: Once a large burial chamber, this place holds several mansized caskets. The caskets are opened and mostly emptied nowadays, their human remains scattered all about the room. Whether this has been done by looters or animals is hard to tell. Bones lie everywhere in disarray, disarticulated and gnawed. In the middle of the room the floor has collapsed, giving way for a great dark crevice.
11796: A heavy stench lies here, originating from animal droppings all over the floor. Filthy twisting cracks and natural passages lead in most directions from this cave. Only one leads further than a few yards before it becomes impassable though, heading north. The walls are of brittle rock, and a large mound of it is up against the southern end. The roof seems to have collapsed there, leaving a huge dark hole.
11798: A grey snake slides along the water.

Pillars and columns suggest this cave was once above water level but has been drowned since. The floor is covered with mud and slime, as it is too dark for any real vegetation to grow here. A slow current plays with you and the debris floating around. Sometimes it is pushing you further into the cave, sometimes dragging you out.
11799: This is a rather large underwater cave in the north bank of the Greyflood. A few small fish have found respite here, hiding in the cracks and among the seaweed that grows near the entrance. The water is black and stagnant, full of specks and lumps of dirt and debris that float slowly about, obscuring your vision.
11800: This is a rather deep section of the river. The water is dirty and blocks most of the light from the surface off. The seaweed covered bottom slopes downward to the south. The north bank rises abruptly in a rotten bluff of crumbling limestone.
11806: A large beaver is here, gnawing on a piece of wood.

Stretching out wide in all directions are the deserted fields and plains of the once so great Eregion. But now there is little left that beholds the life and culture that once was. The fields continue to the east while to the west the Old South Road can barely be seen. North of here is a more fertile land.
11807: Yellow flowers, with grey-green foliage, grow in clusters here.

The thick green carpet of grass here is evidence of the rich fertile soil of this region. Scattered around are flowers, bushes and even some trees. North and east of here the fertile grass covered fields continue while the vegetation thins out into a barren plain to the south. To the west remains of the Old South Road are barely visible. Remnants of the once surrounding stonefence lie to the south and west.
11808:
A small cluster of clover grows here.
Some cereals that look like wheat are lying here.

Here among the grass and flowers grow small patches of tall wild wheat. Maybe the only testimony to the long gone inhabitants who used to plant wheat fields in this area. An old ruin lies to the north while the fields continue to the south and east. The remains of the Old South Road can be reached to the west.
11809: Sitting along the road here are the remnants of buildings long ago abandoned. One of the ruins seems to stand out among the rest. It is the largest of the structures and has not decayed as much as the others. The only exit you can see is through a large arch. Westwards the ruins continue along the road, while eastward the Road of the Smiths continues.
11810: The road begins to narrow as it continues on towards the east. Old ruins intercept the road westwards. Crickets can be heard chirping in the fields to the south. The ground to the north is wet and muddy, indicating an area of swamps may lead ahead in that direction.
11811: This is the remnant of a once cultivated field. Where once various crops used to grow, many wild flowers and weeds have sprung up. The field carries on to the south. The field slowly turns into a grassy plain as it starts to creep on towards the east. To the north an old elven road, leading to Ost-in-Edhil, can be spotted.
11812: A thick, green layer of grass stretches out in all directions before you. West and northward the grassy field merges into fertile areas filled with various flowers and wild weeds. To the south and east the grassy field begins to change into rolling plains.
11813: This is the beginning of the great plains that start to stretch themselves out southwards towards Dunfearan and Enedhwaith. Grass covered hills and thickets can be spotted decorating the rolling landscape. The plains continue onwards towards both the east and west, while to the north fertile fields can be seen. Off to the east is a tiny hill.
11814:
A dove rests near one of the flowers.
A dove rests near one of the flowers.

Through half erect arches a large room becomes visible. The room is filled with litter and bricks from the walls and roof that once stood here. The only sign of any activity around here are some animal tracks on the floor and some bird nests on top of the walls. In the northeast corner lies a decayed stone altar covered with dirt. The only exit out of here seems to be an arch leading south.
11815: Here the swamp borders the side of an old road. The soft ground and numerous surrounding large muddy holes makes it a bit difficult to move about. The passage east of here is blocked by the ruins of what once was a large stone building. Westward the swampy area continues while north of here is the bank of a mud filled lake.
11816: Here the outskirts of a gloomy swamp border the side of an old road. Large muddy holes and soft ground make for difficult passage for travellers. North and northeast of here awaits the swamp with all its secrets. Far northeast, the faint outlines of something can be seen rising toward the skies.
11817: A small and tough weed grows here.

Here the pools of dark murky water are sparse and thin. The area is mostly covered with a thick layer of brownish weed and magnolia bushes. A few old branchy pine trees hovers precariously with their exposed knotty roots by the murky pools. South, north and west of here the swamp continues while eastward it is blocked by a mud-filled lake.
11818: A small and tough weed grows here.

The outskirts of the swamp loom quietly on the northern border of the Old South Road. The swampy area seems to stretch out endlessly in the northeastern and northwestern directions. Large muddy pools of dark, murky water forewarns of danger and difficult passage for the daring travellers. The Old South Road continues to the south.
11819: Here the swamp consists more or less of pure mud. Some brown weed grows here in squarelike formations, giving the impression of borders and boundaries in this formless swamp. There seems to be no other plant life around. The swamp con- tinues in all directions.
11820: Here deep within the swamp there are no signs of paths or passages in any form. Large dark pools of mud converge and diverge wherever the curvature of land leads them. The vegetation consists mostly of a thick brownish weed and some heather. Far to the north a river winds its way toward the sea, while to the northeast a building of some sort rises toward the skies. The swamp continues in all directions.
11821:
A swarm of mosquitoes is here, humming around you.
A swarm of mosquitoes is here, humming around you.
A small leech is here, floating in the water.
This is an edge of the swamp. You can see a road that has to be the Old South Road to your west and south. Moving north or east here will take you deeper into the Nen-in-Eilph.
11822: Spreading out in all directions the slimy mud seem to cover the whole swampy area. The only vegetation around here is some sturdy flooding swamp weed and one or two sickly pine trees with their crippled branches. North, east and west of here the swamp continues with its endlessness.
11823:
A black pond of water is here.
A swarm of mosquitoes is here, humming around you.

Due to all the pools and mudholes around here it is not always easy to find a safe path around. The thick brown weeds that dominate this area cover all the rest of the vacant land. East of here the weeds seem to become thin and more sparse, while north and west of here the swamp continues. South of here the passage is blocked by a large muddy pool.
11824: A swarm of mosquitoes is here, humming around you.

Here the vegetation is almost lifeless. Even the weeds are sickly and limp. The air hangs thick with a foul repelling odor originating from the bubbling pools that lie scattered here. To the south the vegetation seems to be more vibrant while north of here the lifeless area continues. The swamp stretches to the east and west of here.
11825: Not too overflooded with water the vegetation here is a bit healthier and colourful. Beside the brown weed and the crippled trees the are here is also covered by heather and some blueberries. South of here faint outlines of some buildings can be seen, but the way is blocked by a lake of bubbling mud. The same lake also blocks the passage westward. The swamp continues to the north and east.
11826: Large, muddy pools dotted with tufts of heather mark the beginning of the swampy area that lies north of here. Westward the passage is blocked by an old moss covered stone wall. North of here the swamp continues on, while to the east and south you can see an old road.
11827: A black pond of water is here.

The region is filled with pools of different sizes. Little appears to grow here, except for the thick weeds common throughout the swamp and a few crippled pine trees. Occasionally, a small animal can be heard off in the distance. The pools drain slowly into a larger pool towards the east. This pool looks stagnant and unsafe. The swamp continues on in all directions.
11828:
A small leech is here, floating in the water.
A swarm of mosquitoes is here, humming around you.

The thick, choking vegetation and soft, wet ground makes the journey here very difficult. A great host of insects gives the air a strange, hazy look to it. The swamp continues on in all directions, the sun and moon the only recogniz- able landmarks for directions in this desolate area.
11829:
A large leech is moving close to you, searching for blood.
A large leech is moving close to you, searching for blood.
A small leech is here, floating in the water.
A small leech is here, floating in the water.

Black, huge, rotten trees surround you. They look like skeletons of large creatures as they have no leaves, but are still dense enough to keep the sun- light out. Some trees have fallen and are now decaying on the ground. A cold shiver runs down your spine as you feel you are being watched. You cannot see anything special, but you hear a faint gurgling sound.
11830:
A swarm of mosquitoes is here, humming around you.
A swarm of midges is here, humming around you.

More swamp. You see swamp north, east and south. Looking west you can see some dark trees which leave you staring at them, thinking of what's there. Strangely enough there are very few insects here. Something seems to keep them away from this place. Whatever it is it probably isn't dangerous.
11831: The ground here is marshy and swampy. Insects already start to irritate you although you're just on the edge of this swamp, called the Swanfleet. The swamp stretches out north and east. You see a road to the west and south.
11832:
A slender plant grows here, with clusters of tiny pink flowers atop its stem.
A large leech is moving close to you, searching for blood.
A small leech is here, floating in the water.
A small leech is here, floating in the water.
A small leech is here, floating in the water.
A swarm of mosquitoes is here, humming around you.

The humidity is high here and you can feel it when you breathe. Mosquitoes are swarming around you and your feet stick to the marshy ground. Everywhere you look you see nothing but swamp. However, looking south you see a clump of trees in the marsh.
11833: A small leech is here, floating in the water.

Your skin is sticky from the high humidity. As you smack another mosquito its remains smeared on your skin and it takes great effort to get rid of it. The swamp surrounds you, leaving you all directions available for travel.
11834: The ground here gives the illusion of firmness and solidity. One wrong step in the wrong direction however, will land unsuspecting travellers head over heels into slushy muddy pools. Dense floating vegetation provides camouflage for the wicked awaiting pools. North of here lies the river Glanduin, while the swamp continues to the north, south, and west.
11835: Here amidst all the mud and water lies a tiny island of rock. Surrounded on all sides by the slimy green of the lurking swamp, the island's rocky surface shows a surprising red-brownish tint. An indication to the possible iron ore contents of the island perhaps. The centre of the island shows faint traces of a forge that once was here. From here the swamp continues in all directions.
11836: Most of the swamp here is overgrown with dense thickets consisting of large thornbushes. Thinly spread out are some crippled pine trees and some brownish looking weed. North of here the thicket becomes more dense and ends at the shore of a dark pool of mud. The swamp continues to the east, west and south.
11837: Thick wet mud covers the ground here. Some small bushes can be seen in small lumps here and there. Clouds of mosquitoes hover above the bushes for prolonged periods of time, forming ever-changing shapeless crown of grey over the plants. The vegetation becomes more dense to the north and the bushes grow larger and thicker. The swamp continues to the west, east and south.
11838: A swarm of mosquitoes is here, humming around you.

A few crippled pine trees grow here among thick growth of a thick brown weed of some sort. The weed seems to be the main inhabitant here and covers most of the region. To the east the weeds thin out and take on a yellowish looking colour. North of here the swamp runs into the river while south, east and west the swamp continues.
11839:
A large leech is moving close to you, searching for blood.

The only sound heard around here is of running water. Otherwise the area is more or less dead. Thick bunches of half-rotten weed emit an unmistakeable smell. To the south of here the lifeless area continues while to the east and west the swamp continues. To the north of here the swamp runs into the river Glanduin.
11840: A large beaver is here, gnawing on a piece of wood.

The swampland here appears to have been split between the barren ground to the west and the numerous bushes to the east. Scattered among the weeds are small tufts of heather. A bit to the northeast you can spy a large tower. The river Glanduin can be heard to the north. The swamp continues on to the south.
11841: A swarm of midges is here, humming around you.

Here the swampy area merges with some wetlands to the east. Soft mud melts together with earth and water making the grounds treacherous. The bubbling of the Glanduin can be heard to the north, while the swamp expands to the south and west.
11842: The swamps bordering the river here make for a very poor riverbank. Soft mud parts and gives away to the slightest pressure. South of here the swamp grows denser while the muddy riverbank continues to the west and east along the river. North of here the river flows by complacently.
11843: A colourful butterfly is fluttering around here.

The swamp here borders a fast running river. Soft wet mud serves as a bank for the river and a border between the two bodies. Continuing southwards the swamp grows more dense with reeds and bushes of various kinds. Eastwards the sparsly covered and muddy riverbank continues. North of here the river rapidly flows past while a dense thorny thicket grows to the west.
11844: Here the thorn-bush becomes an unlikely sanctuary from the wet soggy grounds of the swamp. Despite prickly thorny branches, the ground is at least solid and dry. North and south of here natural passages through the thicket lead back into the swamp. West of here the thicket becomes too thick and forms a deadend while east of here the bush thins out.
11845: The river is bordered to the south by a somewhat elevated road which leads to Tharbad's south gates. A swamp, taking over where the Sirannon splits up to join the Greyflood can be seen to the east. North and west you see the water of the river flow southwest towards Tharbad.

A swan swims gracefully on the surface of the water.
A trout swims here.

One stage of its long journey to the coast completed, the Greyflood has reached the walls of the city of Tharbad. The wide and majestic river carries vast quantities of through the land each day, and as it travels through the city it presents an ever-present threat of flood and destruction. Yet also, it is this river which gave the city its life.
11847: The watercourse is particularly wide here, with a large area of shallows to east, and extremely low shores to either side. Clear and sparkling, the waters of the Glanduin and Hoarwell, combined and known now as the Greyflood, amble sluggishly through the lowlands. Frequently breaching its banks, the river has created an expanse of muddy fens, which extend much of the way around the walls of the city of Tharbad.
11848:
A trout swims here.
A salmon swims here.

Flowing steadily southwest, the wide river makes its way through the marshes and wetlands of the river basin. Though the waters seem quite torpid here, it would be foolish to ignore their potential, for this is the very agent which has so often wreaked havoc on the city of Tharbad, with angry floods, which tear at the very foundations of the city.
11849: At a Meeting of Two Waterways

The River Hoarwell continues westward, joined by the Glanduin from the east, and the combined waters flow on toward Tharbad. All about, the flat countryside has been flooded often by the seasonal rise and fall of the waters of these two mighty rivers, and now they find themselves travelling through a wide area of marshes, as they continue their journey to the distant coast at Lond Daer.
11850: On a River amid the Marshland

The Greyflood flows to the south here, but it is apparent that it has often broken its banks and flooded the ground to the west, feeding the broad expanse of marshland beyond. Though still sluggish, except in times of flood, the waters seem to gain a little life here, creating a light mist and patches of snow-white foam atop the silvery surface as the river travels over an area of massive, rounded boulders which rest in its path.
11851: The river meanders onward through the wetlands. Though the river is wide and slow-flowing, it is also fairly shallow here, and white foam dances amid the clear blue water as it splashes against large rocks on the riverbed. Flowing from the north, the water courses westward from here, making its way towards the city of Tharbad.

Here the waters of the River Mitheithel flow westwards, where they meet the River Greyflood to continue their journey southward towards the sea, past the city of Tharbad.

The river here is broad and shallow as it winds its way throught the flat countryside. To the east and south, you can see a wide delta formed by the waters of the River Glanduin.

To the southeast lies a great delta, mingled with a peaceful, wildlife-laden marsh. The waters swirl slowly as the swift Glanduin river intersects the proud path of the Mitheithel. West of here these great waterways merge to become the Greyflood.

The patches of grass rise from the water. The sound of small animals who live in the marshy surroundings of the delta reaches your ears. To the south a small marshy island rises from the crystal water.

Far to the southwest the Glanduin and Mitheithel come together to form the mighty Gwathlo River, beyond which it is rumoured the proud towers of Tharbad loom, a shadow of evil in this otherwise peaceful environment.

The air is filled with the sounds of life as many species of birds fly about, attracted to the area by the abundant food and opportunity for nesting. To the west peaceful marshes open before you, their delicate foliage shining in the sun.

To the north lies the faint slope of a large hill and east of here a tower rises above the swamp overlooking the river. East and west of here the river continues while south of here lies the outskirt of a large swamp.

North and south of here the swamps of this region stretch out and there are no signs of humanoid life. East and west of here the river continues. Somewhat far to the north the slope of a large hill is barely visible while southeast of here a tall building of some sort rises above the swamp.

The water is dark because of the large amount of mud influx from the swamps into the river. East of here the river continues while south and west are the outskirts of a swampy delta.

Sprouting from the cold, clean waters of the Glanduin, the grassy foliage around you ranges in shade from green to golden. It sways gently in the shallow water, providing food and cover for many varieties of wetland creatures. The elegant marsh spreads westward, surrounded in all other directions by the depths of the river.

Here is an island of shallow wetlands that rises from the clear surface of the Glanduin supporting an abundance of plant and animal life. To the south and north from here the river encounters a marshy delta, where the waters of the Glanduin strengthen its current and join it for the final trip to the sea.

Rising above the water of the Glanduin Delta, this piece of land is covered with short green grass. The grass appears trampled in certain places, perhaps by some of the fishermen from Tharbad, who occasionally use these waters to make a living.
11875: Here the ground is extremely soft and saturated. East of here the river takes a sharp northward turn, constantly flooding the delta with rapid overflowing currents. South of here is a large and dense thicket of thorny bushes. West and north of here the swamp continues.
11876: Here the ground is more solid than other parts of the swamp. This has caused the topsoil to be more fertile. The main inhabitant here is some short sturdy wild grass. Dotted around this green layer are a few crippled pine trees and some short magnolia bushes. North of here the swamp enters the river Glanduin while east and west the swamp continues. South of here the way is blocked by a muddy pool.

Here the swamp is rather wet. Large muddy pools cover almost everything north towards the river, while south and west of here the ground looks more dry. The numerous deep pools make it difficult to find safe passage but there should be enough enough dry land in all directions for a foothold. East of here the wet area seems to end, while north of here the river Glanduin passes by. West of here the swamp continues.

Looking north, south, east and west you see nothing but swamp. The air is a bit humid and has the odd, sour smell that only swamps have. You can hear the flapping of wings nearby, but you also hear some strange sounds that definitely doesn't sound like swans.
11879: A swan swims gracefully on the surface of the water.
This is the Nen-in-Eilph, where numerous swans dwell. You see swamp in all directions, but you can tell by the low humidity in the air that you're near the edge of the swamp.

A small leech is here, floating in the water.
A small leech is here, floating in the water.

This is the western edge of the Wasteland of the Swans. You see the large swamp before you and you can hear the distant sound of swans calling. The swamp lays to the south and east. You see the flowing water of the river Greyflood to your north and west.
11881:
A blooming water-lily floats on the surface of the water.
A swan swims gracefully on the surface of the water.
A guard is here looking for someone to abuse.

As the river flows languidly by, its waters lap gently over this patch of rocky ground. The mud of marshland gives way here, washed clean by the persistent waters, and a clear, stony riverbed is revealed in these shallows. Further west, the watercourse becomes too deep to ford, though the current remains unhurried.
11882: A swarm of mosquitoes is here, humming around you.

The terrain here is extremely muddy, but does not have the same unhealthy feeling as do the marshes northwest of the Greyflood, perhaps due to the fact that here the ground is washed and renewed by the wandering waters of the Glanduin, which form a massive delta here, as they cross the flat land so near to the city of Tharbad.
11883: The river Glanduin continues to spread out here as it mingles with the great Mitheithel. To the north and south the clear, cold water flows through delicate grass and wetland foliage. The sound of wildlife is also loudest in those two directions, although many birds fly above the river unthreatened by your presence.
11884: The clear, cold waters of the Glanduin flow slowly amongst islands of golden grass, supporting a diverse collection of wildlife. To the east a grassy riverbank, spotted with a few young trees, shows evidence of drier ground. To the north the elegant Swanfleet marshes rise gently from the clean water, and to the west the river continues its leisurely journey.

The river now flows swiftly against the banks, pulling you towards a worn wooden bridge directly to the south. What lies beneath the structure is hidden in shadows, and remains a mystery to the curious eye. In the distance to the east you can make out the form of a small wooden shack.

To the south-west, across the vast fields, is the city of Tharbad. Although its grey-stone walls are not visible from this distance, the well-tended fields to the west serve as a reminder of its existence. To the north the fields are green and lush, having a plentiful supply of water from the river Hoarwell. The current continues in a southerly direction.

The river surrounds you in almost every direction, moving westwards at a slow, deliberate pace. The current quickens slightly as the river narrows and approaches a simple wooden bridge in the distance.

Flowing gently to the southwest the Hoarwell river extends into the murky lands towards Tharbad.

The calm waters of the Hoarwell bend to the west as they flow against the grassy riverbanks to the east and south. Peering eastward, you are confronted with dense, fertile wetlands as far as the eye can see.

The current seems to change direction here, as the Hoarwell wraps around a grassy riverbank and flows to the southwest. To the north lush wetlands emerge from the calm waters and spread westward.

Bordered by the big river to the south and east, and a small stream to the west, this piece of land is drenched with water. Each time you take a step you have to struggle to lift your foot from the sucking ground. This would probably not be a good place to replenish your water supply.

As it flows southwards, the river widens significantly. To the west the calm waters lap peacefully against the grassy riverbank. This insignificant waterway is actually a small branch from the powerful Hoarwell river, which can be heard to the south.

The calm waters of the Hoarwell seem to be in no hurry as they meander south- wards, rolling by the lush green grass to the west. To the east the river grows wider, and in the distance you can spot a beautiful, secluded riverbank.

Thick green grass grows in a patchwork, interspersed with coarse sedge. Fed by the waters of the river Hoarwell to the east of here, the land is rich, the soil thick and loamy. Westward it seems that the wetlands begin to recede, but to the east and south they stretch out before you.
11919: A long-necked bird, with a fairly short spear-like bill stands here.

Thick green grass, heather and tall sedges all grow here, seeming to battle one another for dominance in this wetland area. To the north, the more lush grass seems triumphant, but further south the land seems to become a little more marshy, and the heather is more dominant. To the west, a tall wall of old, weathered stones blocks the way, and marks the boundary of a farm whose large barn can be seen across the fields to the southwest.
