A duck is here, quacking happily.

Closer to the city these wetlands show evidence of frequent use. Contrary to popular belief, the entire city is not of a cut-throat nature and some of its citizens feel more comfortable trying to survive on the land rather than stolen goods and plunder. This is evident by the remains of a tattered fishing net that lies at your feet.
11921: At a Breach in the Wall

As the river Hoarwell flows southwest across the land, the ground begins to surrender to its influence, becoming peaty and marshy. Soft heather and tall sedges thrive here and dominate the landscape. A tall stone wall seems to have fallen into disrepair in the west, and a wide breach now gives access to the fields and farm beyond.
11922: A long-necked bird, with a fairly short spear-like bill stands here.

On the edge of the marshland, long deep cuttings can be seen scarring the landscape. However, it appears that these are no recent work, as rough sedge has already covered the vertical walls of the trenches. Not far to the west stands a rather dilapidated stone building, and to the south a narrow trail can be seen picking its way through the mire toward an old wooden bridge. To the east, the fens are bordered by a wide river.
11923: A long-necked bird, with a fairly short spear-like bill stands here.

The faltering path branches north into the peaty marshland. This narrow trail is almost non-existent, but the track looks more often used where it leads to a small wooden bridge that spans the Hoarwell to the east. The waters flow past lazily, but the broad expanse of boggy ground suggests that sometimes nature rules as the waters breach the banks and flood the land beyond.
11924:
Klaees (thedon), wielding a great warsword, is standing here searching for tracks.
Drazud (freshmeat), wielding a great warsword, is standing here.

A model of functionality, this simple bridge is constructed of several giant weathered timbers lashed together with thick rope and covered with sturdy planks. Although weathered with age, it appears able to support a fair weight. To the east lies a damp path through the spongy grass and to the west you see vast fields, carefully tended by an unknown hand.
11926: A long-necked bird, with a fairly short spear-like bill stands here.

The soft green grass that flourishes to the west of here gradually gives way to coarser patches of sedge. To the south an old stone wall can be seen, separating this grassland from the fields beyond. Tall, and made only from cleverly interlocking boulders, the wall is surprisingly intact, and the many patches of soft, green moss make it too slick to scale.
11927: At the Eaves of a Small Woodland

There are some acorns lying here.
A swarm of mosquitoes is here, humming around you.

A short distance to the west a small, scattered woodland can be seen, its tall trees offering some shelter from the winds which can howl across the flat plains which dominate the countryside here. Small shrubs have sprung up here, fed by the wetlands to the east, and the ground is made soft by grasses, heather and small clumps of bracken. To the south an old stone wall apparently marks the margin of some private land.
11928:
The starving cow stands here looking for a patch of grass.
A long-necked bird, with a fairly short spear-like bill stands here.

A yellow and dying field stretches out before you. The green grass, and healthy crops which once grew here were apparently destroyed by blight several seasons ago, and no seed has been planted to replenish the land. Small holes can be seen in the dirt, the hard labour of some unseen animal, but it is apparent that no other has toiled here in a long time. Immediately to the south, a large wooden barn looms up before you.
11929:
The starving cow stands here looking for a patch of grass.
The starving cow stands here looking for a patch of grass.
The starving cow stands here looking for a patch of grass.
A skinny young man stands here, a blade of grass in his mouth.
A long-necked bird, with a fairly short spear-like bill stands here.

Bounded on the east and north by a tall wall of dull grey stones, this land may once have been a rich and fertile pasture. Now, however it stands spoiled. Seasons of alternating rain, frost, and summer sun have transformed the ground into a rock-hard crust, useless for any form of farming, and even the most tenacious plants seem unable to gain a footing here.
11930: The starving cow stands here looking for a patch of grass.

A wide breach in the grey stone wall offers access to the marshes beyond. In marked contrast to the blighted acreage which characterises the farm, the wetlands seen from here are rich in plantlife. To the north, the ruined fields stretch for some distance, whilst just west of here a small cottage can be seen, its once smartly white-washed wooden walls now soiled and rotting.
11931: On a Trail through the Marshland

South of here the trail disappears completely, as it heads into the marshes, but to the east it seems to have found a patch of fairly solid ground. Beyond a broken gate to the north, a stony track overgrown with weeds leads leads toward a wooden cottage and a large old barn.
11932: Picking a Trail through the Marshes
A nightingale is here, chirping a sweet melody.

Running from east to west here, the trail has found fairly solid ground, as it passes by an old cottage, standing to the north. Though perhaps at one time the building was a pleasant one, it now has a run-down air about it, and the roses which once climbed its southern wall have been allowed to wither and die.
11933: A long-necked bird, with a fairly short spear-like bill stands here.

Meandering idly through these lowlands, the Hoarwell sweeps past from north to west here, its waters rising and falling with the passing seasons to feed the mashes. To the north the ground appears to be a little more firm, and a narrow path makes its way around the edge of the fens. Beyond this, a small stone building can be seen, with a thin whisp of black smoked twisting up from its chimney.
11934:
A long-necked bird, with a fairly short spear-like bill stands here.
A swarm of mosquitoes is here, humming around you.

West and north the dismal marshland stretches into the distance, but it is possible to travel in those directions by picking a route carefully between the worst patches of mire. The same cannot be said of the land to the south, which is so boggy as to be impassable. Eastward the ground meets a slight rise, and becomes comparatively dry.
11935:
A sturdy pack horse is standing here.
The rooster is here, strutting about.
A hen is trying to pick some grains here.
A hen is trying to pick some grains here.
A hen is trying to pick some grains here.
Farmer Black is standing here, looking very angry and crazed.
A small, loyal beagle is here, eager to please.

An old wooden ladder, most of its rungs now missing, is still fastened to the wall of the barn, but now it climbs without purpose. The floor of the hayloft lies scattered, haphazard piles of fallen planks covering the dusty floor of the building, the walls of the animal stalls seem to have been demolished on purpose, and someone has shattered the water troughs into smithereens.
11936:
A bright red mushroom is growing here.
A small mushroom grows nearby.
A bright red mushroom is growing here.
A huge black fungus is here, exuding a foul stench.

Though the woodland is sparse, the trees scattered quite far apart, this place still has a slightly unwholesome and gloomy air. The timbers are tall, but somehow sickly, their bark peeling and scarred with patches of black fungus. Stunted gorse bushes and thin bracken seem to struggle for life, and even the thin clumps of coarse grass seems unable to thrive.
11939:
A dense carpet of blue flowers dip their heads in the breeze.
Some delicious wild strawberries grow on the ground.
Some delicious wild strawberries grow on the ground.
Some delicious wild strawberries grow on the ground.
A small animal, all covered in spines, snuffles amongst the undergrowth.

A small ring of stones stands in the centre of a small clearing, which has obviously served as an encampment at some time in the past. South and west the woodland rapidly thins, giving way to open plains, but to the east and north huge, gnarled trees close in around the smaller, younger trees at the edge of the woods. To the north the undergrowth is thick and completely impassable. Eastward it seems less dense, though it is hard to see a path through it toward the centre of the woods.
11940: In the Eaves of a Small Wood

Some delicious wild strawberries grow on the ground.
Some delicious wild strawberries grow on the ground.
A clear spring babbles as cool water trickles out of the ground.
A brown fox is here, looking for some rabbits to chew up.

Small, thick gorse bushes grow all about, with dark green bracken, coarse grasses, and patches of heather carpeting the ground between them. In the lee of a small, scattered wood, and fed by the bubbling spring, this part of the plain is much richer in vegetation than the bleak, stony land just south of here.
11941:
A large thorny branched shrub is growing here.
A small animal, all covered in spines, snuffles amongst the undergrowth.

The bleak and stony plain opens out to the south, with only a few sparse, yellowing clumps of grass to cover the thin soil. But to the east, west and north, stubby gorse bushes grow in abundance, their thick and twining roots clinging tenaciously to the rocky ground.
11942:
A large thorny branched shrub is growing here.
A brown fox is here, looking for some rabbits to chew up.
A brown fox is here, looking for some rabbits to chew up.

Though still quite stony, the ground here seems a little more rich than it is to the south. Covering the area in a thick tangle of branches, small yet dense gorse bushes abound, with dark green leaves and sharp thorns. East and north the brush thickens considerably.
11945: Dark, dry clumps of earth make the ground uneven and awkward to move over. The area is totally dominated by tall, thorny bushes growing so close together in places that it looks like a thorny wall. Inbetween the bushes dry grass covers the ground. This uninviting terrain goes on in all directions, and passage east and south is impossible due to the density of the shrubs and bushes.
11946: The dreary brush goes on in all directions consisting of short green grass and three feet high bushes. The shrubbery is so dense to the east that passage is impossible. The leaves have sharp needle-like thorns that tear your skin even through clothes and thin leather.
11947: The only vegetation that has found room to grow here is short green grass and three feet high bushes. The ground seems fertile enough but this plant life is able to totally dominate. The brush is so dense to the east that passage is impossible while it is possible to go north and south with difficulty.
11948: The bushes make movement difficult but it is possible to travel farther into the brush to the north and south while movement to the east is impossible. The ground is covered with short grass in between the bushes. The area seems quite desolate showing no signs of civilised inhabitants.
11949: The dry ground is covered with a foot high green grass where the thorny bushes covering the area in all directions have yielded. It seems impossible to get farther east while travel in other directions will take you into other parts of the brush. To the south the grass is getting shorter but also less coarse as the soil contains more accessible water.
11950: The dry ground is covered with an equal mixture of a foot high green grass that seems to be able to draw enough water to thrive and coarse bushes. The bushes scattered over the area are getting taller and denser to the north where they seem to be weeding most other vegetation but it might still be possible to find a way through. The brush continues to the west and south.
11951: The dry ground covered with short, parched brown grass is hard and lumpy. Here, tall gorse bushes provide a little protection from the wind, but they also stop passage in most directions. It might be possible to clear a way to the west, while to the south the coarse bushes give up control to the flourishing green grass.
11952: A swarm of hornets is coming out of its nest.

The hard ground is lumpy and covered with short and parched brown grass. The only form of shelter is provided by the tall gorse bushes covering most of the area and keeping all other vegetation at bay. Passage is blocked by the bushes in all directions except south where it might be possible to clear a way through the bushes.
11953:
Zigurun the Black Numenorean (ZZ), wielding an engraved broadsword, is standing here.
A sturdy pack horse is standing here.
Uldor (UU), wielding a great warsword, is standing here.
A hungry warg stands here, sniffing around for flesh.

Choked by all the tall, dense gorse that consumes the landscape, small patches of parched, brown grass dot the cracked and lifeless dirt. Shrouded with their dark green leaves and menacingly sharp thorns, the bushes seem content as they flourish at the expense of all other vegetation. These proud, almost arrogant plants grow ever taller and wider, making passage difficult in all directions.
11954: Almost tall as trees, huge thorny bushes and shrubs grow close together forming an unrelenting spiky wall. Small patches of dry, dark grass grow subdued on the few areas the brush have not claimed yet. All around the horizon the brush goes on with discouraging density. There is very little life here as there is hardly any edible plants to give any nourishment.
11955: Short Grass on the Side of the Road

This short, dark green grass gives stark contrast to the packed dirt road that runs west and south of here. The vegetation feels soft and pleasant compared to the hard road, and the ambient temperature here is a few degrees cooler, too. Eastward, you begin to see some bushes, and a tiny hill rises up to the north.
11956:
A large, dangerous-looking green snake is coiled up here.
A large rabbit looks peacefully at you, ready to dart away.
A trained horse (Rood) is standing here, ridden by you.

The occasional thorny bushes that dot the land are surrounded by a thin carpet of dark green grass. The grass finally begins to yield to the bushes where they grow thicker east and north of here, but to the west and south not a single shrub is to be seen.
11957: In a Shallow Ditch beside the Road

This wide earthy trench does not seem to be a naturally formed gully, for neither the road to the west, nor the tiny hill east of here seem likely to produce sufficient runoff to create such a channel. More likely, but less savoury, is the possibility that some of the less honourable among the denizens of the city of Tharbad have created it for their own nefarious purposes.
11958: On Top of a Small Hill

Though this tiny mound of grass covered dirt hardly qualifies as a hill, it does give a view of the road a few miles to the west and south across a ditch and a field of grass, respectively. The light brush rising up north of here does not look so pleasant, but the rough bushes to the east look particularly uninviting.
11959: A large dangerous looking green snake is coiled up here.

Between a hill and a thicket, you find yourself wandering in the rough. Dense bushes stand so close together you hardly notice the long, thin grass growing at your feet. While the bushes thin toward the south, north doesn't seem any more inviting than where you stand.
11960: Dense thickets of thorny bushes dominate the landscape with short grass being the only other dominant vegetation. This brush seems to stretch on forever in all directions. The bushes make it difficult to move with their pointed thorns and sandpaper-like leaves tearing at your clothes.
11961: The land is mainly flat with bushes and short grass as the only vegetation. The bushes are mostly white thorn and thorny bushes. A small hill rises up to the south while the brush goes on in all other directions. The area seems quite desolate but the road to Tharbad probably lies somewhere to the southwest.
11962: Short stubby grass grows everywhere with only an occasional bush to break the harmony. Looking towards the east the bushes suddenly grow bigger. The Road to Tharbad runs close by to the west and can be accessed from here without any problems. A shallow ditch starts here and runs towards the south.
11963: A few bushes are scattered all over the area but besides those the only plants that grow here are various short grasses. Looking around the horizon the landscape looks like this in every direction except to the east where the bushes are larger and grow closer together. A trail can be seen to the west.
11964: The trail bends in a south-west arch connecting the stables to the west with the big roadway running to the south. The stables are housed in a tall wooden building in two storeys. Grassy fields offering grazing to the mounts of the people visiting flank the trail. Very little other vegetation can be seen.
11965: Tall bushes and shrubbery grow close together and make movement very difficult. Razor-sharp leaves and thorns rip through clothes and leather and bruise the skin. The brush seems to go on in all directions except to the west where the bushes grow shorter and farther apart.
11966: Short green grass grows in between the dreary-looking thorny bushes. The bushes have sharp leaves and needle like thorns making you want to avoid getting too close to them. The bushes grow in every direction as far as the eye can see. The area seems quite desolate with no signs of civilisation.
11967: A small trail leading north-south passes by Jasper's tavern to the west. The trail is flanked by plains on the east side with short green grass making a dense green carpet. A few bushes grow in spots, but little other vegetation thrives here. The tavern is built with sturdy stonewalls and a wooden roof.
11968: Thick grasses grow in abundance all over the area giving room for very little other vegetation. A small worn trail makes its way towards the west and south. The land seems endlessly flat and covered with grass in all directions except to the southwest where a building can be discerned.
11969: A scruffy-looking sign is mounted on the wall.

A large wooden sign painted with red letters clearly informs you that the stone building to the east is known as Jasper's Tavern. A wide, pebbled path comes in from the south, meandering towards the door of the tavern then continues north, where it presumably goes to the back entrance. The short grass here is trampled and patchy, with numerous footpaths leading east towards the tavern.
11970: Short green grass is the dominant plant life that abundantly covers the ground. Little other vegetation is present, but small, dry bushes grow all around here as well. The grass becomes taller to the north, and the bushes grow more dense to the east. Due west, smoke rises from the chimney of a small stone building.
11971: Small dry bushes and short green grass cover the ground in all directions. The grass gets longer yet drier to the north, and the bushes become more scarce to the west. The notable lack of trees makes the horizon seem empty. The dry land seems quiet and rustic, as if it has not ever been touched by civilised hands.
11972: A trained horse (Rood) is standing here, ridden by you.

Dry coarse bushes grow in patches in the grassy fields. They have stiff, sharp leaves covered with needle-like thorns giving them a natural defence against plant eaters. This pattern goes on in all directions save north where the grass seems to be getting taller and the ground drier.
11973:
The mother wolf stands here, protecting her young cubs.
A wolf cub happily plays here.

A wolf cub happily plays here.
A wolf cub happily plays here.

The animal den has recently been dug into the hard, dry soil. The earthen walls still show fresh traces of medium sized clawmarks. The first six to seven yards being a rather narrow tunnel opening up into a large den. Recent footprints on the dusty floor bears witness of wolves having used the den recently.
11974: A swarm of hornets is coming out of its nest.

Thin, dry grass carpets the ground. The carpet is only broken by large patches of white thorn and other bushes. These bushes grow into brush to the east, and the grass grows shorter towards the south. To the west and north, the dry land remains the same. Very few animals inhabit this barren and desolate area.
11975: The dry ground supports only grass and stiff coarse bushes with razor-sharp leaves. The grass is getting shorter towards the south while the bushes get more rare towards the west. Upon closer inspection the bushes turn out to be mainly white thorn but also some brambles.
11976: A dense carpet of grass covers the ground in all directions almost unbroken by other vegetation. There is some low shrubbery towards the east. The landscape has not been touched by civilised hands though it would make great grazing grounds for domesticated animals like cows. There is a hint of a trail to the west.
11977:
A cute rabbit is here.
A small black bird with red markings on its beak is here.

A trail makes its way from west to east, branching to the south where a large building can be seen. Long grass covers the ground in all directions north of the trail, with little other vegetation growing there. The trail is worn, showing signs of being used often by travellers to and from the building.
11978: The grass grows as high as a mans waist and totally dominates the area leaving no room for other plant life to thrive. The grassy plains go on towards the north while a small trail can be seen to the east. Glancing south and west the familiar lines of the Road to Tharbad can be discerned.
11979: The plains seem to stretch on forever in all directions with only the odd bush to break the monotony of the grass. A gentle breeze from the north carries a sweet scent in the air and the faint sound of songbirds can be heard in the distance. This would make a perfect grazing ground for cattle.
11980: The long grass dominates the open landscape looking towards the east and north. No other plant life has been able to gain space to grow. To the south and to the west a big roadway can be seen and it is possible to enter it from here.
11981: Long lush grass grows everywhere making the few rough bushes look like small islands in a grassy ocean. Panning the horizon the grass seems to go on forever like this in all directions. Looking south there seem to be a small trail cutting a line through the long grass.
11982: Long grass covers the ground in all directions with a few bushes as the only other vegetation. There is no place to take cover if the sky was to open its floodgates. A small trail cuts its way through the grass towards the south. Besides that, there is no hint of human presence.
11983: A few bushes grow in small clumps all over the land, but several kinds of tall grasses grow in abundance, making the ground appear as if it is covered with a thick, green carpet. East, the ground becomes drier, and the taller vegetation turns more dominant as the lack of moisture prohibits the grass from thriving.
11984: A trained horse (Rood) is standing here, ridden by you.

The dry ground supports mainly thin coarse grass and patches of bushes. Looking around the horizon the landscape is similar in all directions save west where the bushes are more scarce and the grass more dominant possibly due to more nourishment in the soil.
11985: A small grasshopper clings to a blade of grass, ready to spring.

Only thin coarse grass and patches of bushes have survived on this dry ground. This dreary land extends to the west and south while the shrubbery grows into brush to the east and north. Not many animals can be found here since the land offers so little nourishment.
11986: The plant life here is all brittle and twisted, finding little nutrients in the parched ground. As you force through the dense undergrowth, thorny fingers grip to your clothing and you can feel dry roots and branches breaking under your weight. This dreary landscape goes on in all directions.
11987: A badger is here, exploring for food.

The land is evenly covered with dry grasses and bushy undergrowth striving to draw nourishment from the dry soil. The brush gets denser looking north and east while the terrain looks the same to the south. To the west the grass is the dominant plant life.
11988: Grass and small bushes dominate the landscape. Panning the horizon the terrain looks the same to the north and south while to the north and east the landscape is being taken over by bushes. This land has never been cultivated by civilised hands.
11989: Thin grasses that cover the ground like a carpet dominate the landscape with a variety of other plants and small bushes striving to live here as well. To the north the grass is giving room to more bushes while the terrain looks the same in all other directions.
11990: A trained horse (Rood) is standing here, ridden by you.

Low shrubbery scattered among the plains gives a little shelter from the wind, but long grass seems to dominate the open landscape. Some small, thorny plants that look like thistles grow in clusters among the grass. The plains continue in all directions, but the patches of shrubbery seem taller in the north.
11991: Other plants grow here but the grass is dominant and covers the ground in all directions. The grass is rigid and makes movement tiresome. To the east the grass slowly gives room for low bushes and other vegetation while the grass grows even higher to the north.
11992: Looking around, the lush grassland extends out north and east as far as the eye can see. The thriving grass covering the area is the tallest vegetation and is only broken by patches of wild growing flowers. The plains continue to the south. Farther into the distance, the familiar lines of the road to Tharbad can be seen. A tall wooden building can be discerned in the northwest.
11993:
A fierce boar is here, making grunting noises.
A small boar with big yellow tusks looks eager to fight.

Lush green grass dominates this area leaving no room for bushes or trees. Small patches are cultivated by the owner of the nearby farm. A tall wooden building rises to the north with a wooden door facing this direction. Looking south the familiar lines of the road to Tharbad can be seen and it easily accessible from here.
11995: Thick tall patches of grass grow over the soft, fertile ground that borders the river here. North and south the narrow trail weaves its way along the riverbank flowing south towards the Nen Kalthar. To the east lies a rectangular building, it is a small farm building made with stone walls and a roof made from wood. A small wooden door is facing in this direction.
11996: A high riverbank sweeps down to the turbulent river on your west. From here, it looks like the climb back up will be very difficult. The trail winds it way north and south along the riverbank passing a small building on its way south. The tall green grass is covering the ground except at the few places at the riverbank where trees are taking advantage of the water supply.
11997: Overlooking a torrid and noisy river flowing southwards the riverbank appears quite steep and treacherous along the edge, and indeed it would appear to be in decline. The semblance of a narrow trail through the grass can be seen leading north and south while open grassland spans across the eastern horizon.
11998: A small black bird with red markings on its beak is here.

A steep riverbank quickly descends towards a fast flowing, turbulent river west of the trail. A few trees have managed to root themselves in the riverbank but there is very little other vegetation to hold the soil in place and it would be quite hazardous to attempt the descent. East of the trail the rich grasslands stretch as far as the eye can see.
11999: The ground is almost soggy making the various grasses thrive. The most plentiful species has long, thick, bladelike leaves with a very distinct yellow colouring at the tip. The plains seems to go on in all directions with no features of the landscape breaking the monotony of the grass.
12000: Going on in all directions the open country is covered with diverse grasses. The most dominant kind has big, yellow leaves while others exhibit different shades of red and tan. The soil is wet and almost mud-like giving ample nourishment to the thriving grasses.
12001: Long, slender grass covers the land almost as a giant green sea, bowing to the air currents to maintain the illusion of water. There is almost no other plant life managing to gain a foothold. The plains seem on go on in all directions with no distinct terrain features to catch the eye.
12002: A rabbit is here eyeing your presence warily.

The vast expanse of plains goes on unbroken by tree or other tall vegetation in all directions except to the east where some bushes can be discerned. The most dominating plant here by far is tall grass with broad, yellow leaves but other grasses mix in.
12003: A small black bird with red markings on its beak is here.

The area is covered with patches of thorny gorse bushes. A few stands of grass still hold their own ground but will eventually be strangled by the unforgiving brush. The bushes grow denser to the east while they give room for other plants to the south. To the west vast grasslands go as far as the horizon.
12004: Giving little room for other vegetation, dark-leaved green gorse bushes take up most of the growing space. It creates a not impassable wall of thorns but any movement further east will be difficult. A few patches of thin grass defiantly struggle to keep alive at the foot of the smallest of the bushes but it is a battle hard to win.
12005: Protected by large prickly thorns, the huge bushes and shrubs totally dominate the landscape in all directions. Movement is difficult as the dense vegetation leaves little room to manoeuvre. A few patches of short coarse grass manage to thrive at the foot of the bushes but are ever in danger of being choked should the bushes expand.
12006: Like an impassable wall of thorns the big bushes grow all over with interwoven branches and roots making movement very difficult. Even the leaves have pointed thorns at the edges making them look sawlike. Very little other vegetation can survive the dominance of the brush but a few strands of grass can be seen.
12007: Strained and weary, the short, dry undergrowth cannot compete with the massive gorse bushes that dominate the land. Armed with thousands of dangerous, needle like thorns, the bushes threaten to leech all remaining life from the parched ground. In a seemingly unrelenting conquest, the gorse grows higher and closer together as they attempt to capture the land, yet their formation begins to break in the west. Perhaps these bushes have only limited ambition.
12008:
The mother wolf stands here, protecting her young cubs.
The mother wolf stands here, protecting her young cubs.
A black wolf pads restlessly, looking for its next prey.
A black wolf pads restlessly, looking for its next prey.
A huge, black wolf is here, ready to devour.
A great black and silver wolf is standing here, at the head of the pack.
A colourful butterfly is fluttering around here.

An abundance of overgrown gorse bushes makes movement extremely difficult. They try to tear at anything they can grab with their needle-like thorns. Passage north and east is all but impossible, and the chance of going either south or west seems even worse. The gorse has sucked all the life from the hard, dusty ground that is void of any other vegetation.
12009:
A fierce boar is here, making grunting noises.
A small boar with big yellow tusks looks eager to fight.

Dry gorse bushes grow to a mans height all around the horizon making it hard to move around. It is impossible to work your way farther to the north while it might be possible to find a path in between the bushes farther east. Little other vegetation grows here except the dry brown grass striving to survive.
12010:
A badger is here, exploring for food.
A huge, black wolf is here, ready to devour.
A black wolf pads restlessly, looking for its next prey.

Tall dry bushes totally dominate the landscape only allowing short brown grass to share what little nourishment the soil offers. The bushes have razor-sharp leaves and stiff pointed thorns making them look extremely nasty. The bushes are loosing space to the grass to the west and south while the brush goes on to the north and west.
12011: A partridge attempts to hide in the undergrowth.

Tall green grass covers the ground everywhere outside the patches of bushes and shrubbery. The bushes are getting more numerous to the north and east making movement harder whereas they are getting more rare towards the south. The area looks quite desolate with no signs of human presence.
12012:
A small black bird with red markings on its beak is here.
A fierce boar is here, making grunting noises.

Long lush grass creates a sea of green with wavelike movement created by the wind. Dry bushes grow in large clumps looking like islands in the green ocean. The land looks like this in all directions except to the south where the bushes are notably smaller and grow farther apart.
12013: Wading through the tall grass, long green blades wave hypnotically in the breeze, accompanied by a gentle swishing sound. The sea of green continues west, while scanning the horizon north and east, the terrain becomes more barren. Large patches of bushes make dents in the green carpet.
12014: A small black bird with red markings on its beak is here.

Long, spindly grass covers the ground nearly as far as the eye can see. A stout wooden fence southwest of here marks the edge of a farm. The rich, fertile soil offers plenty of nourishment for the local flora, and the grass might serve as food for nearby fauna. A large plateau gently rises up to the west.
12015: The flat ground is uninterrupted by bush or tree, giving a clear view of the horizon. The tall grasses make room for wild flowers that splash the fields with vivid colours and fill the air with a sweet perfume. The whole landscape looks like a scene from a watercolour.
12016:
A fierce boar is here, making grunting noises.
A small boar with big yellow tusks looks eager to fight.
A boar cub is playing here, and exploring the wide world.
A boar cub is playing here, and exploring the wide world.

If surveying the surroundings, the extension of damp grasslands can be observed north and south. The ground seems fertile but sports mostly grass and weeds, in contrast to the plant life on the rich plateau east of here. A small wooden building can be discerned to the southwest.
12017: The fertile ground leaks water as due pressure is applied, and old footprints left by the natural inhabitants are well-preserved in the mud-like soil. East and south the scenery seems much the same, but a short distance west the steady sound of a fast flowing river can be heard. Tall grass is flourishing in the waterladen soil.
12018: Thick blades of grass, yellowing at the top, cover the saturated ground. The footprints left on the ground by the natural inhabitants are filled with water proving the ground to be extremely waterladen. Looking around, the grassland extends to the west and north while to the south and east drier plains cover the open landscape.
12019: A coloured game bird is visible in the vegetation, watching you warily.

Studying the surrounding landscape, one can see plains sweeping out all across the horizon, unbroken by tree or bush. The only sound to be heard is that of the long, dry grass as it blows gently to-and-fro in the breeze. There is no telling what kind of animals could be living here, hidden from the eye in the sea of grass.
12020: Across the horizon, rich grassland spreads out north, west and south, while to the east dense brush starts to take over control of the land. The grass becomes taller towards the west while scattered gorse bushes are cluttering the scenery towards the east.
12021: Tall patches of thin, healthy grass are strewn about amidst isolated stands of thorny gorse bushes. Although the gorse owns the terrain to the north and east, the bushes here are but young settlers. Their small, dark green leaves and short thorns do little to compete with the established colonies of grasses and weeds. Perhaps one day they will attempt a coup; but presently they just lie and wait.
12022: Dense but not impassable gorse covers the land, trying to snuff the struggling grasses that grow defiantly at their feet. The proud bushes reach out towards one another, displaying their thorns and darker green leaves. Yet the grasses here are not as easily overcome as their allies to the northeast; they seem to thrive despite the apparent adversity.
12023: As if responding to a cry for mercy, the taller, healthier grass from the west surges in to rescue the withered native undergrowth. Clinging defiantly to the broken soil while being choked by larger gorse bushes, the thin grass battles for its right to live in this bitter landscape but the thorny bushes show no mercy.
12024: Covered by coarse gorse bushes, the land has little hope of ever being released from their iron grip. Short, parched brown grass grows in small clumps in spots not yet conquered by the gorse bushes. Movement is difficult, since the prickly thorns grab hold of anything they touch. The brush continues in all directions.
12025: At the Edge of the Brush

Harsh moorland covered with thick, twisted bushes dominates the surrounding landscape here, which offers little protection from the elements. Long grass grows in between the bushes making the undergrowth a natural hideout for various critters avoiding detection by predators.
12026:
A badger is here, exploring for food.
A fierce boar is here, making grunting noises.
A partridge attempts to hide in the undergrowth.

Beaten down by the strong winds, the dried grasses lie flat on the plains here. Dense thickets of thorny bushes offer a little protection from the weather. The loose grass and various twigs and branches that make up the terrain floor provide perfect building materials for the birds that choose to nest here.
12027:
A small grasshopper clings to a blade of grass, ready to spring.
A partridge attempts to hide in the undergrowth.

Long dry grasses, combed to one side by the prevailing eastern wind, cover the gently rolling landscape where the bush does not prevail. Looking around, there is little sign of any distinguishing features that could act as a bearing, as you move through this featureless landscape.
12028: The plains stretch out north and east from here, undulating into the distance. One can hear the occasional rustling sound as small animals run through the long grass, trying to stay out of sight of any predators. West and south, the terrain takes on a more fertile look.
12029:
Some delicious wild strawberries grow on the ground.
Some delicious wild strawberries grow on the ground.
Some delicious wild strawberries grow on the ground.

The long green plains stretch out before you in all directions. Often the fair stroke of a pleasant breeze blows across the plains and the soft scented grass creates a relaxing ambience about the place. Wild strawberry bushes grow all around, inviting you to have a taste.
12030:
A sturdy pack horse is standing here.
A hen sits here, keeping her eggs warm.
A hen sits here, keeping her eggs warm.
A stocky mountain mule is here, waiting to serve.

A musty smell of hay, manure and rotting boards lingers throughout this small wooden barn. With its southern door boarded shut, the building is fairly dark and humid. It seems to get little ventilation from the wide, sliding barndoor on the north wall, but it's enough to keep the stench bearable. Cobwebs cling to the rafters of the low wooden ceiling above a couple of the pens, in spite of an abundance of bird droppings.
12031:
A well-fed cow stands here chewing her cud listlessly.
A well-fed cow stands here chewing her cud listlessly.

A small pen hosts the farmer's cows keeping them safe from wolves at night. Small patches of soil are used by the farmer for various crops including wheat and vegetables. The patches make a nice pattern cutting squares in the tall grass. To the south a tall wooden building can be seen, while a lower stone building lies to the west.
12032:
A small oaken table has been set here.
A stove stands against one wall here.
A peaceful farmer is here, whistling merrily.
A young girl is smiling at life.
The farmer's wife is bustling busily around.

Built of smooth white stones speckled with brown and grey, this quaint little structure seems to serve as a home to a small family. There is a wood-burning stove standing tall in the centre of the room, possibly giving support to the low wooden ceiling. Next to the stove, a table set for three waits to serve a future meal, and three small beds line the northern wall, only a couple paces farther away. A narrow glass window near the back door provides a glimpse of the outside world, and several shelves and cabinets on the south wall appear to obscure another window.
12033:
A patch of moss grows here on a wet, flat stone.
A giant slug is here, oozing around.

A small, black cave lies beneath the ruins, the stairs from above bending so sharply that this place never sees the light of day. The air is humid, and big drops of water can be seen on the walls. To the east, the wall has at some time collapsed, but it is difficult to tell what lies beyond. However, the air seems stale and has a distinctly musty odour.
12034:
A large bullfrog croaks loudly.
A crayfish is here, snapping its claws at you.
A crayfish is here, snapping its claws at you.

Though the water appears to be quite deep here, a number of large, fairly flat boulders make it possible to walk around without wading or swimming. As the river flows onward, the water laps and splashes against the rocks, making them quite slippery, and a thin layer of moss can be seen growing on a few of the tallest stones. Notably, the western part of this crossing has been washed out by flood, and the tree above is too high to reach. However, you notice that the the eastern bank looks easy enough to climb, as this was originally part of that path.
12035:
A small campfire burns here, its low flames giving off only a little light.
A wooden chest stands in the corner.
A water barrel has been left here.

The small hut looks cozy and comfortable. A small bed, table and some chairs are all that furnishes the room, and a small window faces north. On one wall you can see some of the ranger's small trophies, hung to either side of the plain, wooden door, which is the only exit from this place.
12036: A brook trout is here, swimming in the current.

The pool is wide and deep, and its silty bottom still lies some way below you. The waters swirl lazily around, kicking up only a little of the sticky sediment, and so they remain quite clear. Thick weeds grow throughout the pond, in places so tall as to obstruct your view even this far from the bottom, but to the east, at the wall of the dam, the area is surprisingly free from the tangle of vegetation.
12037: A river otter splashes playfully here.

Although this chamber is deep within the dam, over which the waters of the Nen Kalthar flow constantly, it is quite dry, and the air is fresh and sweet. In one corner a small nest has been built, mainly from soft brown fur.
12038: A brown fox is here, looking for some rabbits to chew up.

Covered with thick green grass, these plains continue far to the east of here. To the south a wide road traverses the countryside, taking advantage of the easily travelled terrain in this region. Further in the distance, in the west, a sparkling river chooses its own meandering course through these comparatively flat lands.
12039: These grassy plains continue east and west for many miles into the distance, becoming more rugged in the east. South, you can see the old hard-packed dirt road that runs from Bree to Tharbad. The plains continue north, getting more and more brushy.
12040: A lone hawk soars high above you.

Harsh weather has eroded this flat, exposed land and depleted most of its topsoil over the years. Now all that remains is a thin covering of stony dirt unable to support more than the most feeble of plant life. A few rough patches of grass cling hopelessly to the rough ground, but no plant any more substantial seems able to survive here.
12041: In a Ditch beside the Road

A black raven flies in the sky searching for flesh to prey upon.
A black raven flies in the sky searching for flesh to prey upon.

A long, narrow ditch runs parallel to the road, which is just south of here. For most of its length, it is filled with brambles. The ground is quite muddy, and the sides of the ditch fairly steep, but roots poke through the soft, damp earth, making it easy enough to scramble out, and just west of here it becomes increasingly shallow, as it approaches a sharp turn in the thoroughfare.
12042:
A brown snake watches you.
A small brown snake is slithering around here.
A small brown snake is slithering around here.
A robin is here, carrying small pieces of wood to its nest.

Bending from south to west, this culvert faithfully tracks the rambling route followed by the road to Tharbad. At its deepest here, the bottom of the trench is extremely muddy, making each step treacherously slippery, and threatening to tumble travellers into the sharp, thorny brambles.
12043:
A powerful ram stands here, poised and alert.
A wild sheep with a short, greyish coat grazes here.
A wild sheep with a short, greyish coat grazes here.
A wild sheep with a short, greyish coat grazes here.

Not far to the east, a faint gravelly trail can be seen, crossing this low plateau, and turning north, toward a thin tract of scattered wooland. At the edge of the plateau, to the west, the ground dips down into a deep ditch, before rising again to meet the roadway, which cuts a massive scar across the countryside.
12044: Near the Border of a Small Wood

There is a fine line between the woodland to the northeast and the plains to the south and west. The vegetation here is sparse, but the grasses and flowers grow richer than they do on the more exposed portions of the plateau, where the thin, stony ground seems unable to support much life. The Road to Tharbad can be seen, cutting a scar across the countryside, to the southwest.
12045:
A black raven flies in the sky searching for flesh to prey upon.
A black raven flies in the sky searching for flesh to prey upon.

Only a sparse covering of limp grasses and a few stunted briers seem able to survive in this harsh environment, depleted as it is of all but a thin layer of gravelly dirt. However, approaching the slight shelter offered by a thin tract of woodland the vegetation becomes more abundant further east.
12046: On the Edge of a Small Woodland

A faint trail across the plateau deadends here, as it meets the borders of a small, but surprisingly dense woodland. In the shelter of trees which stand to the north, the vegetation here is denser then it is on those parts of the plateau lying further to the south, and the soil deeper and richer.
12047: At the Eaves of a Gloomy Woodland

An old stone wall stands to the east. Whilst crumbling, and in need of repair in many places, it is nevertheless too tall to be scaled with any ease. North and westward a brooding woodland rears up, casting quite an unwholesome air over the surrounding land. Although not extensive, it is dense and dark, and indeed progress west into its heart is made impossible by its tangled undergrowth.
12048: A large, loyal falcon is circling above.

This tiny hill is nevertheless one of the highest points for many miles. Most of the surrounding countryside is comprised of plains and marshland, though a low plateau clims away from the river basin, to the southwest, and just not far in the distance, to the north a small, but dense wood can be spied.
12049:
A dense carpet of blue flowers dip their heads in the breeze.
A rabbit is here eyeing your presence warily.
A rabbit is here eyeing your presence warily.
A large rabbit looks peacefully at you, ready to dart away.
A large rabbit looks peacefully at you, ready to dart away.

In the lee of a small, scattered woodland, this small hollow offers a surprisingly sheltered location. It is nestled between a low hill to the east, and the gentle slope westward, which rises toward a massive plateau, standing just a little above the level of the surrounding countryside. Fed by drainage from the higher plateau, this hollow is lush. Thick grass and wildflowers grow in profusion, in a niche whose beauty and peace liken it to a high mountain meadow.
12050: At the Edge of the Plateau

The plateau reaches an end here, almost imperceptibly, as the land begins to fall off gently toward a soft grassy hollow to the east. Westward, a faint stony trail cuts its way across the flat lands, often almost losing itself amid the stubby grasses, short weeds, and rough, stony terrain.
12051: Travelling a Faint Trail across the Plateau

A faint trail can be seen crossing the thin grasses of the plateau, and making its way toward a small woodland north of here. Rapid drainage from this area, toward the rivers and marshes below, means that the land can only support weak vegetation, and much of the soil has washed away over the years, leaving only a thin covering of stony dirt.
12052: A large dangerous looking green snake is coiled up here.

A shallow but extremely muddy ditch extends to the north, but it comes to an abrupt end just south of here where the roadway makes another turn. Tough brambles make progress along the trench painfully difficult, and the sludgy ground offers little purchase. However, here there is less risk of exposure to unfriendly eyes than on the road or open plains.
12053:
A powerful ram stands here, poised and alert.
A wild sheep with a short, greyish coat grazes here.
A wild sheep with a short, greyish coat grazes here.
A wild sheep with a short, greyish coat grazes here.

The wide plains stretch on, spreading out to cover most of the landscape east of here. Not far to the north the grasses give way, and eventually surrender their claim of the terrain to a small woodland. To the south, at the bottom of a grassy bank, the Road to Tharbad meanders across the countryside.
12054: A faint path tracks its way across the plateau here, sweeping from the east to the north, approaching a small, but dense woodland. To the south and west a wide road cuts through the countryside. A few small wildflowers, and a thin blanket of yellowing grasses borders the path, but this part of the plateau is not at all rich in vegetation, and the ground is quite stony.
12055:
A wild sheep with a short, greyish coat grazes here.
A wild sheep with a short, greyish coat grazes here.

A faint, stony trail cuts its way through the thin grasses, heading from the west, towards the edge of the plateau, just east of here. Below lies a wide river basin, extending eastward across marshes and wetland, towards the mighty rivers Hoarwell and Glanduin, which come to a confluence in this region, and flow on, southwest toward Lond Daer and the coast.
12056: The escarpment becomes quite steep here, but the rise is fairly short, and the plateau is still not much higher than the plains below. Lush grass grows on this embankment, and is fed by drainage from the upland in the lowlands to the east and also from the waters of the river, further east.
12057: Richly watered by the runoff from the low plateau to the west and the small hill just north of here, this area of the plains is particularly verdant. The grass grows long and thick, but even so, wildflowers and small shrubs abound. To the east a small cottage can be seen, and south from this spot the plain stretches onward until it meets the fens.
12058: At the Edge of the Lush Plains

A narrow path plods through the marshes to the east and south, but here the land is characterized by long, lush green grass. This rich meadow is bordered some distance to the north by a gently sloping hill, and far to the west a low plateau watches over the grassland.
12059: Amid the Grasses of a Lush Plain
A fat rabbit sits here, chewing on some grass.

North and west a steep grassy escarpment rears up toward a low-lying plateau. To the east, the flourishing grassland stretches off into the distance and eventually meets the creeping marshland, whose borders seem to crawl further into the plains each year. Thick, dark green grass sways in a light breeze, stretching south as far as the eye can see.
12060: This steep bank is covered with thick grass, enriched by the drainage of water from the low plateau above. West and north you may reach the top of the slope, and the escarpment stretches on to the south, before sweeping westward toward a wide road.
12061: A wild sheep with a short, greyish coat grazes here.

A wide plain opens out to the north, covered by sparse grass and a scattering of tiny wildflowers. Though the lands to the east are lush, the plains atop the plateau show much poorer vegatation, as the waters required for life are rapidly drained from here, toward the rivers and marshes below.
12062: A finch flies low above the ground.

Only a short distance from the road to Tharbad, the land begins to climb gently, a long grassy slope, rising toward a low plateau. The bank is pock- marked by innumerable small burrows, many of which are at least partially hidden by the long, dark green blades, and tiny flowers are scattered like jewels among the lush vegetation.
12063: On a Path by the Marshes

A fat rabbit is here, chewing on some grass.
A fat rabbit is here, chewing on some grass.
A fat rabbit is here, chewing on some grass.
A restless rabbit bounces around.
A restless rabbit bounces around.

The road travels here on a slightly raised causeway. A little below the road, a narrow path stumbles around the western edge of the fen, in places totally consumed by oozing mud. Marshland stretches all the way to the slow-moving river in the east and extends to the city wall in the south.
12064:
A large leech is moving close to you, searching for blood.
A large leech is moving close to you, searching for blood.
A swarm of mosquitoes is here, humming around you.
A long-necked bird, with a fairly short spear-like bill stands here.

Stretching onward to the north, flat as far as the eye can see, the marshes make a singularly uninviting prospect. Brown, murky water puddles here and there, and the ground has a spongy feel underfoot. To the east and south the Hoarwell meanders lazily by, feeding the fens with its burgeoning waters,but to the west a narrow path struggles for existence, against the ever-widening quagmire.
12065: A robin is here, carrying small pieces of wood to its nest.

The River Greyflood, which flows not far to the east of here, makes its presence felt by creeping across the flat, low-lying land, making it into a wide marsh. A narrow trail used to pass through this area, but now it is almost lost in the thick, oozing mud and foetid pools of murky brown water.
12066:
A large leech is moving close to you, searching for blood.
A large leech is moving close to you, searching for blood.
A long-necked bird, with a fairly short spear-like bill stands here.
A swarm of mosquitoes is here, humming around you.

A stench of rotting matter fills the air here, and the insistent drone of insects buzzes all around. The ground feels spongy and wet underfoot, and small pools of murky water collect here and there. The only vegetation which seems able to survive in this festering marshland is an occasional tuft of coarse, yellowing sedge.
12067: On a Path by the Marshes
A fat rabbit is here, chewing on some grass.

Standing on comparatively solid ground here, the path draws close to the remains of a huge and solitary tree. Now but a lifeless husk, it was split asunder, apparently long ago, perhaps by a bolt of lightning. Nevertheless its colossal roots anchor this patch of ground against the encroaching marsh.
12068: Soft green grass thickly covers the ground all around, and tiny wildflowers grow amid this lush vegetation. But not far to the east, a wide marshland is slowly encroaching on these low-lying plains, which stand at the borders of the Road to Tharbad.
12069: This tall, grassy bank climbs toward a low plateau, which overlooks the river basin. Steepening, and growing taller to the north, the escarpment becomes little more than a grassy bank as it sweeps west, towards the road. To the east lie lush plains, fed by the waters draining from the upland, and bordering a wide marshland, which extends toward the distant river.
12070: Sweeping round to the east, the grassy bank is swiftly becoming rather taller, and longer, but maintaining a gentle slope, as the plateau seems to climb ever higher above the elevation of the plains below. However, this effect is only an illusion, and this remains predominantly a lowland area, with the plains actually dipping down toward the river, rather than the plateau rising.
12071: Amid the Grasses of a Lush Plain

A fat rabbit sits here, chewing on some grass.
A restless rabbit bounces around.

Tall, dark green grass sways in the lightest breeze, looking like nothing so much as a rolling green ocean. This verdant land is fed by the waters of the Hoarwell and Glanduin, which often break their banks and flood vast areas of the river basin. To the west an escarpment climbs to a low, exposed plain.
12072: On a Path at the Edge of the Marshes

The marshes are slowly encroaching on on this narrow path, which seems to be little used. East and south the mire seems fairly passable, albeit only with care. Nevertheless, this seems to be the direction taken by this trail. The ground slopes gently upward to the west and north, and this slightly higher elevation has spared the grassland there, at least for now, from the creeping waters of the river.
12075:
A forest spider is here crawling around.
A forest spider is here crawling around.
A woodpecker is here, tapping on a tree.

At the centre of a huge clearing in the woods stands a massive tree, which reaches high into the sky, its branches forming a living roof above your head. The trunk of the tree is more than eight feet in diameter, and covered with thick, dark brown bark. Small flowers of red, blue and yellow fill the clearing and dance and sway in a light breeze.
12076: At the Edge of a Clearing

South and west the undergrowth forms a dense tangle beneath the trees, and is quite impenetrable. At the centre of the clearing stands a massive tree, with a trunk whose girth is as large as a small building. Northward, the clearing stretches toward a more open part of the woods, and yet the trees there seem gloomy and brooding, unwholesome, and somehow tainted.
12077: A mass of dark green leaves clings to a wall.

A small wooden cottage, its once white facade now stained with dust and dirt, stands just east of here. A gravelly path, quite overgrown with weeds, leads from the threshold, and heads south, toward a trail, which skirts along the edge of a broad expanse of marshland. To the north a large barn can be seen, its old wooden doors warped and twisted by the ravages of the weather, and a lack of maintenance. However, despite all these signs of apparent ruin and abandonment, a thin wisp of smoke tails from the chimney of the cottage, suggesting that someone must still occupy the building.
12079: Heavy with the scents of mold and rot, stale air fills this small room. The floorboards have broken in several locations from years of strain, creating gaping, black holes in the floor. A small table and a chair, both of which seem to be about to collapse, stand where the holes in the floor are less numerous. You can see little else in the room, apart from a small fireplace occupying the north-west corner of the room. A simple door in the west wall leads to the fresh air outside, and a doorway leads north into another room.
12080:
A wooden chest stands in the corner.
A black spider crawls here, a shiny red spot visible on its belly.

This claustrophobically small bedroom is shrouded in constant gloom, as the windows have been barricaded many years ago. A small couch stands by the northern wall, its sheets grey with dirt, while in the middle of the room, an aged bottle with a candle stuck into it stands, apparently used to chase away at least a fraction of the shadows that fill the room. Animal bones and shreds of cloth litter the floor, adding to the general mess.
12081:
A swan swims gracefully on the surface of the water.
A toad is standing here.
Some remains of a few fish lie scattered in the shallow water. Apparently some animal had lunch here. Maybe this would be a good place for a hungry hunter to catch a meal.
12082:
A swan swims gracefully on the surface of the water.
A swan swims gracefully on the surface of the water.

Bordered by a grassy bank to the east, and a spongy path to the north, this small bit of the marshes is isolated from most of the rest of the Swanfleet Marshes. Looking southwards you see islands of golden foliage amidst the crystal clear waters of the river Glanduin.
12083: The ground here is damp and covered with spongy, green grass. To the east a slight crest rises noticeably out of the surrounding marshland, its peak hidden by a crown of dense, tangled foliage. You catch a glimpse of some sort of metal structure on the hill, but cannot reach it from this direction. To the west a peaceful marsh exists where the Glanduin and Mitheithel meet, and to the north you see a junction of paths. To the southeast, a faint odour of must and decay breaks the otherwise tranquil environment.
12084:
A green frog is here, hopping around.
A small leech is here, floating in the water.

Rising here and there from the shallow water are thick, brownish straws of grass. The water runs calmly here, filling your ears with a soothing refreshing sound. The Glanduin continues to the west and south.
12085: Here someone has dug out a rather large room. The roof and walls are supported by stone pillars which seem to have withstood the passage of time remarkably well. Thick layers of earth and dust cover the floor, evidence of the long vacancy of this room. Scattered on the floor are the remnants of what were once shining armours and well forged swords. Westwards lies a dark corridor.
12086: It is dark here inside the old ancient corridor. Supporting the roof here are some large marble pillars which seem remarkably well-kept. All the pillars have been decorated by old elven runes and strange carvings. The air is rather heavy and almost tinged with the presence of the old noldorian power. East of here lies a rather large room dug out of the earth while west of here the corridor continues.
12087: Here the corridor makes a rather sharp bend from the east to the north. The supporting pillars lining the corridor shows signs of decaying but the runes and carvings are still visible. The black and moist earthen floor seems to consume the light. East and north of here the corridor continues.
12088: A filthy looking man stares back at you from the shadows.

Here the corridor has come to an end. You are now standing in a small square room, the walls and floor covered with damp. The damp has to come from the swamps that lie many feet above you. Examining the room you notice it has one marble pillar in each corner and at the western wall you can see something that resembles a fireplace.
12089: A solid ironbound chest is here.

Neatly carved into the wall is a small and narrow niche. Just like the other rooms, here the floor is also covered with thick layers of dirt and dust. The only thing of interest here is a large dust-covered chest. The chest is made out of richly decorated iron. Much of the decor is intricately carved elven runes known as Cirth.
12090: A narrow trail, surrounded by reeds, leads away from the shady riverbank to the east, its path marked by the trampled grass that lies around you. The damp soil makes it hard to continue on your way. A small hill is visible in the south.
12091: A finch flies low above the ground.

In another time, this must have been a frequently used path, but somehow it came to be abandoned. The ground here is more dry, and continues into the golden plains to the east. The path leads onward to the south.
12092: The grass here is tall and golden, and sways gently in the breeze. This vast ocean of moving colour seems to continue endlessly to the south and east. To the west you spot a small path trampled into the thick grass, and a barely noticeable sound of rushing water comes from that direction.
12093: The slope slants down sharply to the west into a deep unforgiving looking canyon. Along the exposed slope lie clay, rocks, and shale which do not offer any adequate footing. To the east the ground is more level with some stones dotting the surface while to the south lies a level area covered with thick and tall vines.
12094: Some small rocks have been piled into a mound here.

The land begins to gradually slope downwards to the west and appears to become much steeper farther west. Many stones, large and small, smooth and sharp, and all manner in between create very unsure footing. To the east the ground smooths out into a small clear area while the area to the south becomes very rocky.
12095: The ground becomes clearer as it rises up from the forest and other lands to the east and south. A few scattered rocks make the terrain a bit tricky as it continues to rise to the west. But as the ground continues to rise further to the west, the number and size of the rocks begins to get bigger.
12096: A brown fox is here, looking for some rabbits to chew up.

This area appears to have once been a tall and mighty forest. However, all that is left now are the fallen and decayed trunks of this forest. Many of the trees seem to have been felled outward, almost in a circular pattern, as if by a giant windstorm. The splintered and burnt remains of other trees indicate that this devastation was also caused by lightning.
12097: A holly bush with dark green leaves is growing here.

Perhaps at one time this area may have been thickly wooded, but now, only a few lonely trees stand as a reminder of what this area once was. Fallen trunks and decayed branches lie scattered among the broken stumps. Long grasses cover much of the rest of the ground.
12098: The landscape levels out into a smooth sea of tall grasses. Save for the tops of the grasses swaying to the whims of the wind, little else can be seen. The plain continues far into the east while the ground to the west rises a little, and numerous tree stumps can be seen. To the south the grasses become very high and visibility in that direction is limited.
12099:
A fallow deer is grazing peacefully here.
A trained horse (Rood) is standing here, ridden by you.

Broad grasslands extend far into the eastern and western horizon. Millions of grass blades softly swish and sway, appearing as if they were trying to keep from falling down. To the south, the wide flat expanse of the grasslands gives way to barren and uneven ground.
12100: A fallow deer is grazing peacefully here.

The thick grasses create a solid green plain that sprawls into the horizon. The flat expanse of the prairie, however, is dominated overhead by the wide open sky. To the south the solid green of the grasses abruptly changes to a charred blackness.
12101: You are surrounded by low, evergreen bushes growing in the thin soil on these rocky hills. Outcroppings of white stone give the land an ancient, exhausted appearance. Here, in a swale between two hills, the bedrock has been completely denuded in an oval patch about a third of a mile long, and the white stone has been discolored as if a fire raged here long ago. Even where mud and soggy old leaves have collected, nothing grows in this patch. There is no sign of human life, and little evidence of large game. The land slopes upward to the north and east.
12102: A large rabbit looks peacefully at you, ready to dart away.

The treeless land slopes upward to the north and east. The hard, stony ground is covered by a carpet of heath and heathery plants about six inches tall. Underneath it the soil is very thin and barely covers the rotten and crumbling limestone that lies beneath. They say this land was once forested. That must have been very long ago.
12103: The flat land here is maybe two hundred feet higher than the valley of the Glanduin a few miles to the south. The soil is very thin here, and the rock underneath it is old crumbling limestone, which protrudes through holes in its purplish-green blanket of heath here and there, like exposed bones in an eroded graveyard. There is no sign that this land has ever been inhabited. It is silent and empty.
12104: A fierce boar is here, making grunting noises.

The ground here seems generally flat, but travelling over it one discovers numerous irritating crevices, holes, depressions, and stony obstructions, all more or less hidden by an eight-inch blanket of grey-green heath. The bone- coloured limestone of these hills is overlain here by a thin layer of harder greyish rock. Millennia of erosion have undercut the harder stone and caused it to crack apart and crumble into sharp-edged chunks, which lie scattered about here under the vegetation ready to turn the ankles of the passer-by or cause his horse to stumble and rear. But there is no sign of anyone having passed this way since the creation of the world.
12105: The rocky heath-covered land slopes gently downward to the south here. The ground is strewn with sharp-sided chunks of stone the size of a man's head, which are largely concealed by the foot-high heather which grows everywhere here. The soil is very thin; the heath seems to be rooted in the cracks of the stone itself. There are no obvious watercourses here - it seems as if the rainwater washes evenly off the old rock of the slope, or sinks into the rotten limestone and disappears.
12106: The land slopes evenly downward from west to east. The ground is stone, liberally covered with an evergreen carpet, a tangle of deep-green leaves, woody stems, and tiny white and lavender flowers. A few large rocky fragments are buried in the heath, lying where they have rolled down from the higher ground to the west.
12107: Bushes and small trees, many with fragrant wood and flowers, and most with nasty thorns, cover the rocky land here; mud and sand from a recent flood form a flat surface which readily reveals tracks. The rustling of small animals, and the fluid calls of songbirds, are heard frequently from the brush - generally, at some distance from you.
12108: This is a broad north-south valley choked with sand and pebbles. A very shallow stream meanders southward through it. Its course is convoluted, being more like a network of connected pools than a single stream. Other shallow pools lie as far as two hundred yards from the main course of the stream. It is clear that most of the flow of water through this valley is of ground water seeping southward through the porous sand and gravel, and that the stream and pools observed on the surface are only a small fraction of the total. The valley is bounded by brushy banks about six feet high, undercut here and there by flood waters; but gravel bars abound, and it is not hard to find a place to climb the banks.
12109: The topsoil here is thin, supporting only small and scattered clumps of rough grass. Deep rills running north and west cut the surface, exposing shards of bone-white limestone to the elements. To the west the plateau dips sharply, dropping to a brush filled valley roughly eighty feet wide.
12110: The ground here is flat enough, though it drops off very sharply toward the river valley to the west. The topsoil is very thin, and only sparse clumps of coarse grass can be found here. It looks as if most of the rain that falls here runs off rapidly, sinking into the porous rock or pouring down into the valley through normally dry washes.
12111: A large rabbit looks peacefully at you, ready to dart away.

Low, thorny brush and stiff brown clumps of grass cover a rocky landscape. The land is generally flat, dropping off sharply toward the river to the west, but it is cut by narrow, steep-walled ravines where floods have washed away the rotten underlying rock, and travelling is difficult. A barely perceptible footpath runs through the uninviting landscape from north to south along the lip of the embankment which falls toward the river.
12112: This is an area of brush on an earthen bluff overlooking a river to the east. Much of the brush has been trampled down or dug up, though. To the south you can clearly see some structures, which have been covered with mud and thorny branches, and walled around by the same, to the point where they are almost impossible to make out from any direction but your own. The mud here seems exhausted, barely fertile.
12113:
A tortoise creeps slowly through the mud.
A bee is sleeping here.
A bee is sleeping here.
A bee is sleeping here.

A rocky stream splashes downward to the west, meandering across the bottom of a canyon fifty feet deep and a hundred feet wide. The water is low, and the stream can be forded or crossed on stones at many points. Occasionally you may hear a fish splashing in one of the deeper pools.
12114: Low hills extend southward and eastward from here, with no visible sign of habitation. It seems certain that animals do graze on this short grass - their hoofprints are all around - but there is no sign of crofter or herdsman. Flies buzz, the wind sighs, and far overhead a bird gives a mournful squawk. This is a silent land.
12115:
A wild sheep with a short, greyish coat grazes here.
A wild sheep with a short, greyish coat grazes here.
A wild sheep with a short, greyish coat grazes here.
A wild sheep with a short, greyish coat grazes here.

A stony bluff overlooks the flat terrain below from an elevation of sixty feet or so. It is composed mainly of stone which the rain has not yet worn away; what little soil is left supports a coarse, scraggly growth of short grass. Signs that grazing animals have been here are abundant.
12116: These are low hills, nearly barren, covered by a tenuous coating of poor soil and short grass. They rise only a hundred feet or so above the wetlands to the west, and have been heavily eroded by rain and wind. They seem tired, old, as if waiting for a new change of the world to wash them away.
12118: The low ground here has been flooded by the water of the river, and tall reeds grow in the shallow water. Some old, rotten tree trunks lie among them, evidence that this has not always been a wetland. They are rapidly decaying, though; and frogs splash, blue flies buzz, watersnakes slither through the reeds as if this had been a marsh since the creation of the world.
12119: A compromise between the river to the north and the great reed-beds to the south, this area of shallow water is dotted with clumps of vegetation and water plants, laying their purple-dotted leaves gently on the surface. Water- loving insects dart about, barely rippling the surface as their featherweight bodies alight on the water, seeking some tiny morsel of food.
12120: The Forglanduin meanders south and west toward its junction with the Glanduin, its shallow waters placid and brown. Along its banks small animals peek out from the brush and reeds, watching for fish or water birds. Travel is slow due to the mud and wet sand of the broad riverbed.
12121: Here the Forglanduin is freshened by a tributary which joins it from the east. The flow of the combined streams, however, is not so great as to pose a serious obstacle to travel; the water is easily forded on any of numerous gravel bars and rock shelves. Piles of matted brush and branches line the edges of the floodplain.
12122:
A grey snake slides along the water.
A frog is standing here.

The river winds southward through a flat floodplain about two miles wide. In its present low-water state it is in effect a series of pools linked by an easily wadeable brownish flow. There seem to be few fish; birds of prey circle overhead but find nothing to stoop upon. The land is silent and empty.
12123: The shallow, muddy river trickles southward through low, apparently uninhabited brush-covered terrain, winding back and forth across a level flood plain about a mile and a half wide. Steep, undercut banks bound that plain, and driftwood, debris, and mud have been deposited here and there in cluttered heaps.
12124:
A tortoise creeps slowly through the mud.
A mother eagle is sleeping here.

Here the Forglanduin is a shallow, brown stream meandering southward across a broad valley. In time of flood the water probably fills the entire valley, undercutting the tall brushy banks you see to the east and west. Now the water is low, and the exposed sand and mud banks are speckled with green weeds.
12125: A large rabbit looks peacefully at you, ready to dart away.

Close-knit thorny shrubs and bushes make it tough going on this gentle slope leading down to a watercourse. Exotic orange-and-white flowers grow on some of the fragrant boughs. A stand of briars attracts your attention.
12126: Thorny branches and spiny canes are woven together into a solid mass which makes free movement all but impossible, exept where someone or some group of game animals has left narrow trails through and among the shrubs. Sounds of small scurrying animals and flapping birds can be heard down under the branches.
12127: This is the western edge of the silt-covered floodplain of the Forglanduin, and because (in contrast with the land eastward) there is actually some soil overlying the bedrock, some thick vegetation has sprung up. The bushes are covered with waxy green leaves, and in the summertime they bloom with colourful blossoms an inch or more across.
12128: A large rabbit looks peacefully at you, ready to dart away.

Shrubs bearing thick, deep-green leaves and nasty spines grow thickly here, but travel is possible where the foliage and canes have been trampled by wild game. The ground is soggy mud dotted with hard rocky protrusions.
12129: The shallow waters of the Forglanduin spread out here over a wide plain, seemingly as flat as a tabletop. Reeds hide the contours of the river's bank; the river is braided into several channels separated by pristine tan sand bars. Fish splash in the deeper pools, and the gargling cries of game birds are heard from the marshlands.
12130: A heron is stalking the area, looking for fish.

The brown waters of the Forglanduin have pooled here and spread over a broad expanse of the countryside, too deep to touch bottom. There is little current here. To the south the river is overshadowed by a great stone structure marching east and west - the ancient dwarven causeway, carrying the road that once linked the ancient centres of wealth and power in Middle-earth.
12131: The great dwarven road follows the course of the Glanduin here as it meanders west and north. Downstream, far to the west, is the city of Tharbad, once a great Numenorean seaport and the recipient of the commerce of Eregion and Moria. Since then the coasts have been changed, and Tharbad lies far inland; Numenor, Eregion, and Moria have all been ruined, and the road is nearly deserted.
