12132: The great elevated structure marches north and south, following the River Glanduin curve for curve. Built to carry the commerce of Eregion when that land was Middle-earth's most glorious realm, today it bestrides the empty mud flats in this silent and deserted landscape.
12133: You are on a monumental structure of stone, a great causeway elevated upon columns of black marble and carrying an ancient highway over the floodplains of the Glanduin and Forglanduin. Built by the dwarves five thousand years ago and more to carry the commerce of Eregion, it stands today, battered but strong, a monument to the vanished power of the dwarves of Khazad-dum, to the departed wealth of the elven lords of now-ruined Ost-in-Edhil. The road curves from the west toward the south here.
12134: The road follows the bend of the river from east to north as it has for thousands of years, but recent years have been unkind and the few paving stones which show through the grass and weeds are worn and cracked by the elements. To the west, the Glanduin flows steadily onward towards its meeting with the Mitheithel near Tharbad. The south bank is covered with holly and bushes, but in the distance you can see the plains of Enedwaith stretching as far as the eye can see.
12135: Here the road has been reduced to about two thirds of its former width by the encroachment of the river and the southern side may not be very stable for more than a man on foot. To the east the road continues, more or less safe from the inexorable flow of the river to the west. There are a few bushes along the side of the bank there and thus the road is holding up much better. The south bank of the river appears to be covered with a dense bushy growth which is mostly holly.
12136: The road rises slightly towards the east as it approaches a cliff. It appears not to have been in serious use for a very long time as evidenced by the copious grass growing up through missing stones. The fact that the road is still discernable after so long is evidence that it was once a major trade route. To the west, the road is being undercut by the river. To the south, the Glanduin continues its trek westward.
12137: This ancient path leads away to the south and west, hugging the soft, green banks of the powerful river Glanduin. Although many stones are missing from the road, the masterful pattern of interlocking cobblestones which remains indicates that this road was once a major thoroughfare. A tall cliff rises out of the swaying grass to the east, and grassy plains continue far into the south.
12138: A large rabbit looks peacefully at you, ready to dart away.

Here, where great piers carry the ancient Road of the Smiths over the main channel of the Forglanduin, the structure shows unusual signs of wear and damage. The stone columns have largely collapsed on the north side of the pavement; although the great slabs upholding the pavement have not collapsed, they are tilted dangerously at crazy angles. A great mound of heavy debris - willow trunks, great roots, and mud - has been piled against and under the span; from below you, you hear a booming sound, a sound of falling, churning water.
12139: Sixty feet above the mud flats of the Forglanduin the great old dwarven road marches on columns of stone, defying time and the river's waters alike. On either side of the road the land is flat as a sheet of paper, an expanse of marshes and standing water, scoured by the flood water which rolls off the almost soilless heath. On the north side of the causeway debris lies thick where the floods have hurled it.
12140: The road continues east and west atop its levee, twice the height of a man above the flat land to the north of the road and the riverbank to the south. The dark stones set here by the dwarves five thousand years ago are still firmly in place and mostly smooth. This road was once packed with trade to and from the dwarven dwellings at faraway Khazad-dum; but the collapse of the North-kingdom and the awakening of Durin's Bane have left the road desolate.
12141: The ancient dwarven road continues east and west, elevated above the surround- ing floodplain country on an earthen levee. Here, however, the road is covered with a thin layer of wet clay. Water has frequently overflowed the road from the north side, running over the pavement, eroding the levee on the south side, and leaving a deposit of sediment behind.
12142: The elevated stone road continues east and west, straight as an arrow. Grass and small weeds grow from the dirt which has collected between the stones. Still, it seems nearly as sound as when it was built thousands of years ago. There is very little sign that anyone still uses this road, however.
12143: You are on a smooth, straight, and ancient road. Tightly-fitted stones make up the pavement, which is raised above the surrounding plain on an embankment the height of a man. East and west it proceeds, parallel to the River Glanduin which meanders south of the road, now a mile distant, now lapping just below you at the foot of a breakwater. Once this was a busy highway; today the road and the land around it are desolate.
12144: The road appears to be solid and well engineered despite its obvious lack of use and maintenance. A noticeable layer of dust has settled over the large cobbles of the road and the stone blocks lining its sides. The rocks comprising the surface of the road appear smoothed and flattened from age and wear. The route continues east and west running parallel to the river in the south.
12145: The road slopes downwards as it dips closer to the river in the south. The large stones which fit together to comprise this road seem to have buckled a bit, possibly indicating that this area may have sunk somewhat since the road's construction.
12146: As the road follows the river on its course, a natural steep ledge forms between the road and the river to the south. Apparently the river has eroded its bed deep into the ground causing a cliff like wall to form from the road down to its banks. The large stones lining the road provide a nice overlook onto the river's waters as well as helping to prevent any careless falls down into the water.
12147: The solid and hard route continues to the east and the west. The road, itself, does not show any ill effects from the ages of wear it probably has endured. Each stone on the road seems to have been laid with great care, and together they all fit perfectly with one another. Despite their apparent age, no cracks have formed between the stone blocks and the wear over the years only seems to help smooth it out.
12148: The large flat stones of the road pave the way east and west through the wild lands of Eregion. A small grassy clearing by the side of the road to the south allows a spectacular view of the rushing river. A short distance to the north, a large ironwood tree stands, offering shelter underneath its branches. A large headstone can be seen under the thick boughs of the tree.
12149: A hungry warg (Rood) is standing here, ridden by you.

The rows of the stones lining the road bend causing the route to run east and south. The surface of the road, though dusty and hard, remains flat and consistent. To the west a path can be seen leading from the road into a large formation of rock cliffs while thick bushes hide the area to the north.
12150: A hungry warg (Rood) is standing here, ridden by you.

The flat dusty road continues north and south. Despite the dust and natural debris collecting on its sides, the roadway remains in good shape, its rocks seeming solid and firm on the ground. The river can be seen flowing to the east while a glint coming from the surface of a lake can be seen in the southwest.
12151: The Road of the Smiths crosses the River Glanduin. The bridge looks very old and sturdy. In the middle of the bridge, there is a trapdoor that must lead down to the river below the bridge. The river flows under the bridge from east to west. The distance from the bridge down to the water is too far for anyone to risk jumping into the water. The road continues north and south from the bridge.
12152: A long bend in the river leads it from north to west. To the west an old bridge made of wood and stone lets the river pass beneath a road going from north to south. On the southern side of the river bend plains filled with grass and flowers lie just above the riverbank, while on the eastern side lots of small bushes grow close together. Further east some trees can be seen in the distant horizon.
12153: This shallow part of the lake is at the north-eastern end. At the northern side sand cover the shore, while at the eastern side the lake ends in a river running beneath a bridge. The river Glanduin exits into the lake here. The bottom of the lake here is soft, as it is mostly sand covering it. A small current runs westwards from here because of the water entering the lake from Glanduin.
12154: From here the road continues north and south. Further south it bends westwards, while north of here it crosses a bridge. The ground is covered with dirt, and hardly no stones at all. A few, old footprints of horses and men can be noticed as the ground is searched thoroughly. Westwards a large lake covers the area north of the road, while to the east a grassy plain appears.
12155: The road bends north and west from here. To the west the road seems to continue on forever, while northwards a bridge appears in the distance. Below the bridge a river flows out into the lake that lies north-west of here. South of the road lies a small stream that also runs out into the wide lake in the north-east. A small path leaves the road eastwards from here, leading down to the stream.
12156: A sturdy stone bridge makes crossing the stream comfortable. Below the bridge, a trickling stream flows from the south to the north, ending up in the wide lake to the north. The Road of the Smiths continues to the east and west. There is a trapdoor on the middle of the bridge that seems to lead down under the bridge.
12157:
A trout swims here.
A bass swims here.
A bass swims here.

At the south-eastern end of this lake the water is clear and light blue. The ground at the bottom of the lake is filled with small stones which makes it rather pleasant to move around. Along the shore a road runs over a bridge to the south and continues northwards along the eastern shore. A small stream runs southwards beneath the bridge and on into the distance.
12158: This path leads southwards down to the bank of a small stream, and westwards to a road that bends north and west. East and north from the path plains cover the area as far as the eye can see. The plains are filled with medium long grass, that is quite dense. In between the grass tall flowers grow, and some trees lie scattered about.
12159: A tall stag is here, grazing peacefully.

The small path winds it way south along the side of the stream that flows west of here. Short grass covers the middle of the path, while longer grass grows on the sides of the path and down towards the water. This path leads to a road north-west from here. To the south-east lies a hill, and beyond the hill a large, beautiful lake appears into the view.
12160: The small path continues along the stream on the eastern bank. The stream continues south, while the path ends here. There is a small strip of grass between the path and the water. South of the path a tall hill rises above the ground. East of the path the land is very flat, covered with spots of tall, yellow grass. Apart from these spots, nothing seems to grow there at all.
12161: The road continues along the bank of the lake east and west. A bridge can be seen letting the road pass over a small stream east of here. The bridge is old, but sturdy, and made of wood and stone. Southwards small, but dense, bushes cover the area with their long thorns, while to the north a huge lake lies with its cold dark blue water.
12162: This part of the road seems to have sunk a bit lower than the rest. Water from several stagnant pools makes travel on the road treacherous. A flooded field lies to the south, while eastwards the land begins to dry up into grassy plains. The road continues on to the north and west.
12163: The feature that draws the most attention in this area is a dark, ominous pool. It does not appear to be very deep, but the muddy water makes the approximate depth hard to tell. Murky water pours into the pool from the swamps to both the north and west. A stretch of an old road can be seen from here to the south.
12164: Bushes and small thickets of magnolias grow out of the wet ground. The bushes become much thicker to the north and east. Behind these bushes, some sort of tower can be seen. A horrible stench draws attention to an ominous, murky pool to the south.
12165: This stretch of the road is pitted with potholes filled with muddy water. West and north of here are more of the swamps that dominate the region. A large pool of water to the north collects water from the surrounding area. The road continues on to the east and south.
12166: This section of the road seems fairly firm and stable, as compared to the west where the swamp has begun to overtake the roadway. To the north is the beginning of a swampy area. To the south of the road some plains can be seen. The road continues on to the east and west.
12167: The road is slighty damp and muddy, with occasional stones poking out of the ground. Beds of magnolias mark the outlines of the road, which continues on towards the north and west. To the south and east the flowers and grasses begin to merge with thicker vegetation.
12168: The road is barely visible because of the weeds and thick grass that have grown over it. Small pine trees and beds of magnolias barely outline the edges of the road. The road appears to continue to the south and east. Dense thickets block passage to the north, while to the west the weeds and grasses begin to merge with the outskirts of a swamp.
12169:
A holly bush with dark green leaves is growing here.
Partly covered by the bush's green leaves, there are a few inkberries.

Continuing in a rather straight line from east to west the old road winds its way through the wasted landscape. While the road gets more and more overgrown as you move west, it becomes more visible to the east. Scattered along the road you notice some holly bushes. North of here a dense thicket prevents you from continuing that way, while south of here lies a dusty plain. East of here the road continues.
12170: The Road of the Smiths bends here, and continues to the north and west. This part of the road seems seldom used. The area is covered with patches of weeds. The bushes to the east are too dense to allow passage through them. The only way through must be to avoid the nasty looking thorns. To the south plains stretch out in every direction.
12171: Dense bushes cover the area east of the road. To the north beyond the road a lake can be seen in the horizon. The road continues north and south from here, rocky and bumpy. This part of the road seems to be seldom used, but some footprints of people, and a few tracks of horses can be noticed as the ground is searched thouroughly.
12172: The Road of Smiths continue south and east from here, while an old, seldom used road continues westwards. The Road of Smiths, wide with the ground consisting mostly of dirt, seems to have been used recently. To the north a large lake covers most of the horizon from north to north-east. Rocks and deep water makes it hard to access the water from here, although the lake is almost level with the road.
12173: This road shows signs of decaying. It is mostly overgrown by high grass and large bushes. Some of them have big thorns and you have to walk carefully to protect your clothes and skin. The road was once paved with flat stones, but now they are mostly broken and scattered but they still show the course of the road. To the east this road meets the Road of the Smiths which is in a much better condition. You see the remains of a high building to the north along the road. To the west and south the ground becomes softer and you can see small pools of smelly water.
12174:
A snake slithers towards you.
A swarm of midges is here, humming around you.

Here the road ends at the edge of a river. The river is rather wide here and it looks like it has a strong current. At the riverbank you can see the broken remains of pillars that once supported a bridge, but now there seems to be no way across it. Looking northwards you can also see a large high hill. To the west lies a decayed stone building with a large tower attached to it. It seems to be very old. Southwards the old road continues while east of here lies a lake.
12175: The road continues west and east from here, while to the north a vast lake covers the horizon. This road mostly consists of dirt and small stones. A few tracks can be seen on the ground, as some people on horses passed the area lately. South of the road lies an area with dense, thorny bushes that looks unpleasant to move around in.
12176: The land here slopes gently southward into the Glanduin Valley - if the word 'gently' can be used of land looking so tired and uninviting. The rocky ground is covered with clumps of brownish grass and thistles. There are no trees anywhere in view, nor can many birds or small animals be heard. The landscape seems dull, drab, and empty.
12177: With struggling patches of thistle and coarse grass scattered amongst out- croppings of rotten limestone and patches of broken shale the rocky ground here slopes slightly to the south towards the Glanduin. Rising from numerous points in the cracked bedrock little trickles of water gather together and run down small channels to form a small stream flowing down to the west.
12178: A grey wolf is here, thin from starvation.

These overgrazed hills surround you for miles on every side. Clumps of coarse brown grass with a hint of green near the roots cling mechanically to life in the thin clay between the outcroppings of rock. Some larger rocks lie in a line across a hills flank, too straight to be natural, but otherwise barely distinguishable from their surroundings.
12179: Low, stony hillocks covered with sparse clumps of grass extend around you. There are a few broad-leaved plants around the bases of the larger rocks, but the more exposed ones have been nibbled down and pawed over. Nettles and thistles grow in the swales.
12180: These low and nearly barren hills extend southward to the horizon. Rainfall must wash off them in an instant, for there is scarcely any soil or humus to hold it here. Is it possible that great forests grew here once? That is what the stories say...
12181: A cluster of dark green, feathery fronds flourishes in the shade.

This is a canyon forty feet deep and eighty feet wide which has been carved by a meandering stream descending to the west. The water is muddy, shallow, and easily forded; perhaps in the rainier seasons the flow is stronger. Broad pools filling the entire canyon are interspersed with long stretches where the stream is comparatively narrow. Grass, green weeds, and ferns grow at the base of the canyon walls, and a few hardy shrubs cling to rocky shelves part way up.
12182:
The starving cow stands here looking for a patch of grass.
The starving cow stands here looking for a patch of grass.

These scraggly fields and pastures can barely be enough to support life. The soil is dried mud; the cattle have eaten whatever forage was here, and have broken down the rickety fences; the vegetation is rotting and untended. A wooden palisade about ten feet in height encircles the fields on the south and east sides.
12183: Here and there the thin soil of this rocky plateau has washed or blown away completely, exposing a surface of thin-leaved shale which peels apart readily into grey, sharp-edged flakes of talus. Where there is any topsoil, there is not enough to support more than a few thorny bushes and some scraggly grass and nettles. The land seems desolate and empty.
12184: The flat ground - composed of sheets of limestone and shale covered with a paper-thin layer of soil and some scrubby clumps of grass - is broken up by deep washes running downhill to the north and west. The land is all but desolate. It does not have an evil feel, but seems very tired and old. In ages past, deep green forest covered all this land - or so say the wise. Nothing remains of them or of the men who cut them.
12185: Sheets of broken limestone exposed by the sparse soil give this area the look of an abandoned graveyard. The topsoil looks very thin and worn, as if the land were tired and drawn out past its time. With little on the ground to hold water deep washes have been cut running west down the slight slope of the plateau.
12186: The land slopes evenly south and west toward the Glanduin. The soil is thin and infertile, and the vegetation consists of coarse grass and prickly plants, growing in drab clumps. The ground seems tired, ruined, worn out. There are no trees in sight, no bushes, no plants higher than a man's boot-tops.
12187: The hills here slope slightly to the south and west. Rising about eighty feet above the surrounding wetlands, the top of these hills is on a level with the stand of oak trees to the west. Trickling busily around, between and over rocks and patches of sand and shale a small stream cuts its way down towards these trees. The soil here seems to be worn out; spread thinly and looking tired it supports very little vegetation.
12189: The water of the Forglanduin has collected here in a deep lake two miles across. This is because its free passage under the main span of the ancient causeway to the south has been obstructed by a great pile of debris which has collected against the columns - tree trunks, brush, mud, even the carcasses of boar and sheep. Although the surface of the water seems calm, there is a slow current coaxing you in the direction of the causeway, where you can see twigs and leaves on the surface swirl in a powerful eddy.
12190: The ground here is soggy, and your footprints fill with standing water; the brush here is sickly and in danger of rotting, while plants more typical of wet ground have sprung up everywhere. Frogs can be heard croaking, screeching, and splashing in every direction.
12191: A fierce boar is here, making grunting noises.
Thick bushes covers the ground making it hard to travel through. It slopes down to the west, towards a flooded valley. Small flowers hides under the bushes, they grow in blue and purple.
12192: Here a shallow swale, the valley of a small stream which runs down from the low hills to the north here, has been filled with murky water, forming a broad lake. There do not seem to be any fish living in it. Around its edges the vegetation is soggy and rotten.
12193: Tall, thorny bushes with thick leaves and aromatic twigs grow densely here, and passage is difficult. It is impossible to see very far in any direction. Occasionally you hear the scampering of a small animal running for safety in the brush.
12194: A brown fox is here, looking for some rabbits to chew up.

Thick heath grows the height of a man here, mixed with dense thorny shrubs and briars whose interlaced shoots make travel difficult and unpleasant. Small animals can be heard scurrying for cover as you pass through. Here and there are signs that someone has come this way on a horse, with most of the hoofprints pointing north or south. There is no sign that anyone lives in this land, though. Occasionally you see a wheeling hawk abruptly stoop and then soar away with a tiny squirming shape in its talons.
12195:
A holly bush with dark green leaves is growing here.
Partly covered by the bush's green leaves, there are two piles of inkberries.
A bright green holly bush is growing here.
Partly covered by the bush's green leaves, there are two piles of hollyberries.
A porcupine is waddling around here, its tail full of sharp quills.

The ground slopes up to form a slight and broad rise. The soil here is ingrained with jagged rocks which appear to have sunk into the ground over time. The rise leaves the area exposed to the elements which keep the rise bare of growth. To the north, the ground levels out into a vast grassland while a road can be seen to the south.
12196: A few pines grow on the rocky ground here. A faint trail running north and south is imprinted on the hard plain soil. The rock strewn ground spreads all about, but is met by a large distinct looking road to the south. It appears that the trail connects to the road and runs north, far into the flat sparse woods to the north.
12197: A horse of the Rohirrim (Rood) is standing here, ridden by you.

Thick bristling pines stand tall on the level ground, occupying much of the landscape. Sparse grasses cover the ground while decaying pine needles darken the ground beneath the pine branches. To the north, a stone building can been seen nestled among the trees.
12198: A large bookshelf sits against the wall.

This house appears to have been standing for a long time from the look of the walls which show much wear. Nonetheless, the walls remain very sturdy due to their design which included hefty stones. The carpentry does not look dwarvish as there are no chiselled nor hammered features within the house, which, itself, has a much more natural look. The stones are round and smooth, and vines climb up the walls near the windows. The light making its way inside grants a calm, tranquil effect to the room. A large table spans the entire northern wall with some miscellaneous items still remaining on its surface. Even the wooden planked floor looks solid despite the significant layer of dust and a few pronounced scratches.
12199: The plain of grass shimmers as the tips of the grass blades sway and bend back and forth. The grass is dense, making passage a difficult and tiring task. To the west, a large chunk of rock can be seen standing in the distance. To the east the monotony of the green plains abruptly changes into a multitude of colourful flowers sprouting in an open field. To the south there appears to be a small dwelling, made of stone and wood.
12200:
A pool of darkish water has formed in a depression of the stone.
A trained horse (Rood) is standing here, ridden by you.

The flat even ground of the plains sinks down into a wide though very slight depression. A few dark green bushes are situated near the centre of the basin and seem to be encircling a small pool of water. Except to the north, tall grasses on higher ground prevent any view of the surrounding area. In the north, the ground appears to be very rocky and little grass grows there.
12201: This stretch of ground is, for the most part, barren. The soil is coarse and uneven, giving the area a rough and rocky appearance. Sharp dips and steep hills warp and pockmark the ground in sharp contrast to the flat grassy plains to the north. Here and there, hostile looking brownish thornbushes dot the bare ground.
12202: In comparison to the flourishing plains to north and south, the ground here seems to be dead. Burnt ashes cover much of the ground, darkening the land and giving it a somber aspect. Though there is no smell on the ashes, the overall lack of any resumed growth in the ground seems to indicate that fire swept through this area not too long ago.
12203: A trained horse (Rood) is standing here, ridden by you.

The clay soil here is very thin; in many places the white, chalky rock beneath pokes through like an elbow through a threadbare sleeve. The vegetation consists of low, evergreen, flowering bushes growing amid scraggly clumps of coarse grass. The land is uneven, rising and falling in abrupt little steps, like a thin silken sheet spread over scattered bricks.
12204: The land here slopes downward toward the west. The thin soil and the low, evergreen bushes that grow in it cover the hillside like old, worn burlap; the underlying limestone can be seen poking through it in little outcroppings everywhere.
12205: This heath-covered hill rises about a hundred feet above the valleys to the southeast and southwest, and provides a good view of the landscape. It extends below you like a purplish-green blanket thrown on the ground for a picnic: low, green heath on low, stream-worn hillocks. Once great old trees grew here in lush, rich earth; now the trees, and most of the soil, are gone perhaps forever.
12206: A short evergreen plant, with slightly bluish needles, grows here.

All around you are miles of treeless heath-covered moorland. The soil is thin to nonexistent; large rocks, forced to the surface by a thousand freezes and thaws, lie about everywhere and are being covered in turn by lichens and the omnipresent heath and heather. The land slopes gently down to the east here.
12207: Spring at the Head of a Stream

A clear spring babbles as cool water trickles out of the ground.
Yellow flowers, with grey-green foliage, grow in clusters here.
Yellow flowers, with grey-green foliage, grow in clusters here.

This is a broad, shallow bowl-shaped depression in the treeless, heath-covered landscape. A little north of its centre, a spring burbles out from under a rocky shelf, forming a small clear puddle. The stream that begins here meanders off toward the south and west; at the moment there is not enough flow from the spring, however, to maintain the stream's flow.
12208: The rounded crest of a ridge runs from north to south here, covered in a seamless blanket of heath; it resembles a gentle fold in a drapery of deep green cloth. Tiny lavender flowers speckle the landscape, blending at a distance with the pine-green hue of the heath and giving it a shadowy tint. The rock of the ridge is near the surface, but has been smoothed by years, and centuries of rain and wind. Little animals move here and there - a snake, a field mouse - but overall the land seems very quiet, as if it were exhausted.
12209:
A black snake, with red markings, is lying here.
A snake slithers towards you.

A heavily eroded ridge curving from the north to the southwest rises above the more level heathlands on either side. A few fragments of rock, almost buried in the thick tangle of woody stems and foliage, mark the rounded crest. To the east, the land drops more steeply toward a tangle of brush. There are no trees, signs of large game, or relics of the days gone by when men came here in great numbers to fell the seemingly inexhaustible forests.
12210: The land is rather even here, sloping very gently eastward toward a line of brush. The ground is essentially bare stone, covered with a sprinkling of humus and a seamless carpet of heath. The dark green leaves and pale pink and purple flowers are the only things saving the landscape from complete dreariness.
12211: The brush-covered ground slopes southward here, and the lower ground is wetter and almost marshy. Bushes and thorny shrubs grow thickly here, their leaves thick, deep green, and glossy, their roots gnarled and heavy, and their thorns sharp and waxy. Fragrant flowers bloom on the trees. Birds wheel overhead, then stoop on their unseen prey.
12212: This wetland extends eastward across a flat floodplain. At best you are wading in a foot of water, surrounded by reeds higher than a man. There are also numerous deeper holes, open pools, and mires, and you must watch your steps carefully. Dragonflies dart soundlessly among the tall blades, and wading birds stalk through the water, standing still, then plunging their long beaks below the surface after a frog or a minnow.
12213:
A snowy-white egret stands here alertly.
A fierce boar is here, making grunting noises.

Shrubs and trees grow here, low and spreading, few taller than a tall man. Their resinous thorny twigs interlace and make a mass of brush and briars, difficult to penetrate. Their leaves are grey-green and the flowers are aromatic. The soil is thin muddy sand over an uneven rocky layer which protrudes here and there in outcroppings crowned with scraggly bushes. Small, swift animals and birds scurry through the undergrowth.
12214: The heath-covered landscape slopes gently downward to the west here. Around you is a colony of white-flowered plants; the hills around you are covered with the more common purple-flowered variety. A few stones the size of a man lie here.
12215:
A clean fragrance drifts up from a thick clump of leaves.
A partridge attempts to hide in the undergrowth.

You are in the valley of a tiny stream which runs down from the higher ground to the north. There is not much water in its bed, but it is enough to give life to a dense tangle of bushes with thick aromatic leaves and thorny canes. Small animals scurry away from your noisy passage. To the south the ground is moister.
12216: The heath-covered, soil-poor land slopes gently southward toward the distant Glanduin. Small streambeds, which probably contain water only during the spring rains, cut the surface of the rocky hills.
12217: The land is flat here, and the soil fertile, and tall grass grows all around you in a green wavy sea. Its tops ripple with each breath of air. Tall stalks covered by gay conical heads of blue flowers poke up among the grass, competing for the attention of the bees. Your passage stirs up rustling movements in the grass as small, unseen creatures fast scurry away from you. Occasionally you tread upon stone or rotten wood and, looking down between the stalks, you can discern the remnants of a foundation, a fence rail, a cart - memories of the time when the farmers of Cardolan made this place a granary, before that kingdom was desolated by war and plague centuries ago. Here and there the grass has been beaten down more recently, and you can see hoofprints - sometimes headed south, sometimes headed east.
12218: Wild healthy grasses grow all around, rising high and thick. Occasional breaks in the tall grasses provide glimpses of more grassland to the north while the tops of some trees can be seen in the western horizon. The grass is especially thick to the south, preventing any view in that direction. A trampled narrow trail leads south through the grass.
12219: Hiding any trace of the solid ground, a layer of tall grass shimmers silently, creating the appearance of a soft green surface. The grass plain extends into the distance all about, completely encompassing the landscape, only finally giving way to the open sky in the horizon. To the west there appears to be a small dwelling, made of stone and wood.
12220:
Prickly, white-stemmed plants, with blue flower heads grow in abundance.
A fallow deer is grazing peacefully here.

This is the southern slope of a low hill which is covered by thick clumps of heather. Its myriad minute bell-shaped flowers dance as you pass. The soil is thin and poor, and outcroppings of the underlying white limestone can be seen everywhere.
12221: A grey wolf is here, thin from starvation.

You are on a rocky slope facing generally eastward, covered with the low, green, tough brush characteristic of the heathland. The soil is poor, but small animals and game birds can be seen if you look carefully, hiding from you and from any great birds of prey that might fly overhead in this open country.
12222:
A small brown snake is slithering around here.
A partridge attempts to hide in the undergrowth.
A badger is here, exploring for food.

Two tiny stream beds, one from the northeast and one from the northwest, meet here creating a single stream with a visible trickle of water in it. The stream is almost obscured by the thick thorny brush which has grown up around it. The shrubs have thick leaves and aromatic stems which produce a pungent, spicy odour as you laboriously force your way through them.
12223: A partridge attempts to hide in the undergrowth.

Low evergreen woody plants cover an expanse of very low rocky hummocks here, sloping upward imperceptibly toward the southeast. The squeaks and chatters of rabbits, grouse, and other small animals can be heard, but the animals do their best to stay out of your sight. A hawk wheels high overhead, surveying the empty landscape. Elves, men, and dwarves have lived in this land or travelled through it, but you see little evidence of their presence.
12224: Here low shrubs with waxy green leaves interlace their thorny branches into a dense mass, making travel very difficult! The twigs which break off as you pass exude a pleasant fragrance. The ground is flat, and stony outcroppings can be seen among the roots of the brushy plants.
12225: A small brown snake is slithering around here.

You are on a low north-south ridge, barren of trees, poor in soil, and covered by thick clumps of woody-stemmed evergreen plants with tiny purple flowers. A flat stone shelf is at the summit of one of the stony hummocks, and may once have been the foundation of a building of some kind, hundreds or thousands of years ago; this is the only sign that people have ever lived in this land.
12226: A streambed runs southward here, a waterless furrow in the centre of a shallow valley; perhaps after heavy rains there is even water in it. Near the streams course the heath is taller and bushier, and there are even a few shrubs of alder and juniper, their roots straggling over the rocks and grasping for purchase.
12227: A small and tough weed grows here.

This is actually not so much a ridge as an uneroded tongue of rock between two small stream beds. Low evergreen leafy bushes cover the gentle slope, ankle-high where the soil is particularly thin, knee-high elsewhere. The deep green heath is bedecked with tiny purple and white flowers, and bees and hummingbirds can be glimpsed as bright flashes of colour which dance about and then vanish.
12228: You are surrounded by heath, lush but tough bushes with small, evergreen leaves and tiny pink flowers that rise up taller than a man in the densest clumps. Occasionally a thorny briar tears at you. The land is generally flat and a small, waterless streambed winds eastward, lined with denser brush and an occasional willow tree.
12229: A large rabbit looks peacefully at you, ready to dart away.

This is the northern slope of a broad, low hill. It is a mass of cracked white stone, broken apart by fissures which radiate from the point where you stand. Little grows on the exposed stone, and where the wind has blown leaves and debris into the cracks, rain has washed them out again, so the land has not recovered well from whatever event took place here.
12230:
A dense carpet of blue flowers dip their heads in the breeze.
Yellow flowers, with grey-green foliage, grow in clusters here.
A fallow deer is grazing peacefully here.

Bright hues and deep tints catch the eye, a welcome break from the solid green of the endless plains. Scatterings of white, blue, red, yellow, and even purple in the form of flowers grow all about. The ground appears as if a rainbow had collided with Arda at this very spot and had penetrated the soil, causing this sweet confusion.
12231: A black raven flies in the sky searching for flesh to prey upon.

Lush grass carpets the land, creating a solid green surface over the ground. The long thin blades of the wild grass rise up several hands high, easily obscuring anything shorter than a hobbit. To the north, the green grass of the plains quickly turns into dark ashes of burnt ground.
12232:
There is a bright green, spiny capsule here.
A tall, stately, dome-topped tree grows here.
A fallow deer is grazing peacefully here.
A large rabbit looks peacefully at you, ready to dart away.

This is a broad, shallow valley with a faint watercourse draining to the south- east. There is more soil here than on the hills to the north but it is a heavy clay, not terribly fertile, and the tough grass grows in thick clumps. The watercourse is marked by a line of thick bushes and some low, thick-boled oak trees. From time to time you see a bird of prey wheeling silently high above you.
12233: A cluster of dark green, feathery fronds flourishes in the shade.

The land here slopes generally downward to the southwest, and is covered by tough, scrubby evergreen bushes which in places are as tall as a horse. Riding through the heath must be an odd experience, almost like swimming in a grey-green sea. Although the land seems completely deserted now, it was once productive farmland, and a few stones of an old farmhouse foundation can be seen providing shade for those plants that need it. To the west of it are some plants with lacy, dissected leaves and broad heads of tiny white flowers. You may have even heard that this land was all forest once, but that seems hardly credible.
12234:
A small brown snake is slithering around here.
A brown fox is here, looking for some rabbits to chew up.

The land here slopes very gently southward. Exposed stones are everywhere, but a thick carpet of heath and bracken covers the rocky shelves and softens their outlines. The dartings of small birds and game among the ground cover can be perceived from the corner of your eye.
12235: A trained horse (Rood) is standing here, ridden by you.

A treeless landscape surrounds you on all sides. The bedrock has been all but denuded of soil, and thousands of years of runoff have worn steep-sided furrows in the low rocky hillocks. Yet the thick blanket of heath which covers hill and valley alike has softened the edges of this otherwise harsh terrain. When the sun is low and red, its rays arouse splashes of gaiety and life from the flowers of the heath, bringing a few minutes of beauty to this most ancient and abused land.
12236: Prickly, white-stemmed plants, with blue flower heads grow in abundance.

Great, large clumps of pink-flowered heather have sprung up here on a gently undulating westward-trending slope. There is not a tree to be seen for miles. The ground is hard; the bedrock is only a few inches below the surface.
12237: Tall golden grass sways around you, almost caressing your legs as it bends to and fro, moved by the very slightest of winds. The vast sea of grass continues to the west and south, while to the east the golden grass starts to give way to brambles and hardier plants, which can grow happily in the rougher ground to be found in this direction.
12238: Here there appear to be the faint remains of a trail - evidenced only by there being slightly less bramble bushes in one area than another. Broken rocks and uprooted vegetation lie all about. To the south the trail appears to become more defined, while to the west the brush gives way to golden plains of luscious grass. In the east lies a large chasm, effectively blocking any travel in that direction.
12239: Decay has enveloped this road to such an extent that its destination is no longer apparent. The ground is rough and great boulders sprawl out on the terrain. Sharp brambles cover the ground, spreading from the large thicket to the south, and making passage very difficult. The smell of rot and decay permeates the air and casts a gloom over the land.
12240: The elements seem to have taken their toll on this path. A few boulders appear to have been split and blackened by lightning while numerous cracks and uprisings in the ground give evidence to some seismic activity. Tall weeds force their way up among the cracks and brambles dot the uneven ground. The way bends about, leading westwards, as a gaping chasm lies directly to the north.
12241: The trail meanders among the plants, heading roughly north and south. Here and there wild grasses obscure portions of the trail while a few scattered trees offer nearby shelter from the elements. To the east, the ground rises up into a flat plateau, while to the west a thick stand of brush and brambles prevents easy travel in that direction.
12242: The trail runs north and south, weaving about through the even terrain. A few bushes and small trees here and there comprise the sparse plant life in the area. The path contains numerous pockmarks which have been somewhat smoothed over by time and weather. By the side of the path a small sign is posted pointing to the east.
12243: The trail is wide here, leading north and south over dry grassland which is sparsely populated with trees. At this point the trail bends around a large black pillar of roughly hewn stone which abruptly stands in the middle of the path. Few trees grow in this area making the pillar easily visible from a significant distance.
12244: To the sides of the trail, the remnants of many fires and camps attest to the fact that this path was, at one time, a well travelled one. A stretch of the hardened trail here contains a few discarded horseshoes, a broken wagon wheel, a broken crate, and discarded lanterns, which all together are evidence of the high rate of travel, if not messiness, that occurred along this trail.
12245: A finch flies low above the ground.

The grass here is greener and the soil damper than that of the golden brown fields to your west. To the north the path leads away in the marshes. In the distance the faint sound of rushing water drifts on the breeze.
12246: As the hard dirt trail heads north and south through the sparse land, small signs of past civilisation can be seen about the road. A decayed wooden wall stands to the side of the road, bravely remaining upright while its three other partners lie at its base, broken and rotten. To the east of the road, a dark patch of trees and bushes can be seen.
12247: The surface of the roadway becomes soft and wet as wild green grass overruns part of the roadway. Ferns growing on both sides of the trail expand high into the air, overhanging some parts of the trail. To the east, thick ferns comprise a dark green clump of vegetation.
12248: Cool air wafts in from the east as the sound of splashing water emanates from the same direction. Looking east, the river can be seen running near the trail, its banks only several meters from the trail. Between the river and the trail, trees line the river's banks.
12249: The trail continues north and south. Parts of the path have been deepened with ruts while other sections are littered with debris such as broken crates and miscellaneous parts of wagons. Though there is much debris, the rusted and decayed condition of much of the litter is an indication that it has been a long time since this way was regularly used.
12250: The trail fades here, at the shores of the lake to the south. Trees stand just beyond the shores of the lake which extends to the southwest and southeast. The hard packed dusty ground of the trail is a sharp contrast to the soft wet shore of the lake. To the east, a river can be seen emptying into the lake.
12251:
A rabbit is here eyeing your presence warily.
A duck is here, quacking happily.
A robin is here, carrying small pieces of wood to its nest.

This part of the path is very overgrown with some grass and flowers. It is hard to see any signs of humans passing this way for quite some time. The path continues to the west and becomes hardly outlined in the south, while to the east a very dense patch of brambles creates an impassable barrier.
12252: This wet path heads to the west, slightly covered with grass and twigs. The golden grass surrounds it to the north and south. The cold wind would make the way very uncomfortable, lashing the dress of some weary traveller in this open flat.
12253: A finch flies low above the ground.

Here the path leads west, deeper into the marshes. The soil seems to be less damp to the east, and indeed some green healthy grass is visible in that direction. The thick vegetation here makes it hard to continue on your way.
12254:
A brown toad is here, hunting flies.
A large rabbit looks peacefully at you, ready to dart away.
The ground here is extremely moist, and the thick foliage surrounding you grows taller than a man. A traveller's feet would sink deeply into the murky water, chilling his skin and slowing his pace.
12255: The trail of trampled weeds and marsh-grass continues to the east. To the west the trail is bordered by a wet field, which runs up to a grassy riverbank, beyond which the regal Hoarwell can be seen. To your south the path leads into an exceedingly wet section of marshland.
12256: The path here bends westward, towards some grassy wetlands. The ever present sound of running water is stronger from that direction. To the south, the dense vegetation is too thick and tangled to continue.
12257: The path here runs in a north-south direction, bordered on the west by a slope, and on the east by a vast expanse of rolling fields. The westward hill looks as if it would be an ideal place to take in the surroundings from.
12258: You are at the top of a small hill, surrounded by flat, grassy land to the east and the river Hoarwell to the west. The high altitude offers a panoramic view of the region. To the south-west two rivers seem to come together. Beyond that the magnificent towers and steep walls of Tharbad loom on the horizon.
12259: A large rabbit looks peacefully at you, ready to dart away.

The golden, rolling fields spread out in all directions but west, where you can see a small path beaten into the thick grass. You can barely make out the sound of rushing water from that direction, although a steep hill prevents you from seeing its source.
12260: The ground here is relatively dry, and covered with thick golden grass. The rolling fields continue in all directions, as far as the eyes can see. From the west the faint sound of rushing water reaches your ears.
12261:
A nightingale is here, chirping a sweet melody.
A large rabbit looks peacefully at you, ready to dart away.

The ground here is solid, covered by a golden species of grass that glows in the sunlight and sways peacefully in the breeze. The grasslands seem to continue in the west. To the south the ground becomes slightly more green in hue, while to the east stands a very dense patch of brambles and thorns.
12262: A large rabbit looks peacefully at you, ready to dart away.

The vast golden plains seem to roll endlessly into the eastern horizon. The ground here is dry but fertile, supporting a healthy crop of thick ground foliage. To the west and south a small path leads away, and to the north and east the fields continue with no landmarks, so that a traveller could easily get lost.
12263: Dark and gloomy, large bramble bushes surround you, reaching out with their thorns to grab at your clothes and rip your flesh. Weaving to and fro in the slightest breeze, it almost seems as if the bushes resent the intrusion into their private sanctuary. Closing in all around you, the only ways out are back the way you came, or to fight your way through another patch of tangled, sharp branches.
12264: The thick thorns and brambles here make progress painstakingly difficult. Sharp and thorny growth chokes out all other life, strangling the grasses and the trees of light and room in the soil. The dense bramble thicket creates an almost impassable barrier to the north, even forcing the trail in the east to curve round it.
12265:
A small and tough weed grows here.
A large thorny branched shrub is growing here.

Tall weeds push their way up through the cracked soil, some rising high enough to obscure a fully grown man or possibly even an elf. Some vines armed with small thorns grow in the scattered bushes. Small black berries hang from them but appear too little to be of any nourishment. Holes dug into the rough ground signal the presence of some animal life.
12266: A robin is here, carrying small pieces of wood to its nest.

After a moderate rise, the ground becomes very level, allowing a grand view of the surrounding land. There is little growth here aside from a few scrubby trees which ruggedly survive on this unwelcoming ground. A thick layer of light brown dust covers the ground, sometimes swirling around at a puff of the wind.
12267:
A large owl with small sharp horns looks cautiously around it.
A robin is here, carrying small pieces of wood to its nest.

This is a very small peak, if one at all, for it only rises thirty or forty feet above the ground. Nevertheless, it provides a clear and broad view of the surrounding area. An examination of the lands to the south reveals the presence of a river and a trail. Brambles and bushes can be seen to the north and west while some trees can be seen in the eastern distance.
12268:
A large thorny branched shrub is growing here.
On the shrub, there are two piles of blackberries.
A bright green holly bush is growing here.
Partly covered by the bush's green leaves, there are three piles of hollyberries.

Large bushes with long thorns crowd the terrain. Progress through here is delicate and slow due to the sharp nature of the thorns. Though the ground is relatively flat here, footing is still treacherous and rightly demands much attention as fallen thorns are a lurking danger.
12269: In contrast to the thick and thorny bushes to the north and west, the plants here are lush, green, and leafy. The river bank is here, and the glimmering waters can be seen flowing to the east and south side of the clearing. The ground is soft and damp, making passage very comfortable.
12270: Some thick writhing vines whip all around you.

Short trees, no taller than six or seven yards, spread outwards, rather than up, bearing thick wide leaves, covering up the sky above. The effect is made more dismal from the climbers and vines that snake through the branches. A sweet smell mixed with the scent of decay wafts through the area, in a mysterious fashion. Certain areas of branches are broken as if something large had passed through.
12271:
A cluster of dark green, feathery fronds flourishes in the shade.
A swarm of mosquitoes is here, humming around you.
A swarm of mosquitoes is here, humming around you.
A swarm of mosquitoes is here, humming around you.
A swarm of mosquitoes is here, humming around you.
A swarm of mosquitoes is here, humming around you.
A swarm of mosquitoes is here, humming around you.

The area is quiet and calm as a cool mist hovers above the vegetation. The wet and soft soil gives under the slightest weight, only becoming firm some six inches below the surface of the ground. Thick ferns comprise much of the plantlife here and seem to thrive in the wet ground and moist air. A fresh and earthy smell from the greenery permeates the thick air. Clear drops of water can be seen hanging under the fern leaves.
12272: Thick sheltering branches lean over the banks, extending their boughs over the bend in the river. The river appears smooth and all is quiet, at least for the moment. The fresh and vibrant smell of wet leaves drift by as fallen vegatation accelerates downstream.
12273: The water is cold and rapid as the river flows southward. Despite much debris floating on and carried in the current, the river does not seem to be hindered or slowed by it at all. Little shallow pools form on the banks of the river where the current is not so strong. To the east many trees can be seen.
12274:
A bass swims here.
A bass swims here.
A bass swims here.
A bass swims here.
A bass swims here.

The river flows slightly slower in this section, allowing a decent view of the muddy bank to the south. Past the bank the land appears to gradually fade into swamps and fens. The Glanduin River continues its way east and west. Every once in awhile a small fish can be seen swimming along the murky riverbed.
12275:
A bass swims here.
A bass swims here.
A trout swims here.
A bass swims here.
A trout swims here.

The current of the river is markedly slower here, as it widens and enters an area of majestic marshland. The Glanduin continues to the north, and to the east the water is shallow enough for a man to stand. The peaceful sounds of wildlife drift on the gentle breeze, as small wetland birds and creatures go about their business.
12276:
A blooming water-lily floats on the surface of the water.
A blooming water-lily floats on the surface of the water.
A blooming water-lily floats on the surface of the water.
A bass swims here.
A salmon swims here.

The current of the Glanduin is more relaxed as the river opens into the Swanfleet marshes, also known as Nin-in-Eilph. To the north the marshes seem to be darker and thicker than anywhere else, restricting any further progress in that direction. Beyond these dim waters a densely vegetated hillock rises, a curious site amidst the otherwise flat landscape.
12277:
A salmon swims here.
A fat carp swims here.
A fat carp swims here.

The river Glanduin flows all around you, moving slowly off to the west where it forms a large delta in the distance. The water is brown and unclear, making it hard to discern the bottom, despite the water being quite shallow. To the north the Swanfleet marshes begin.
12278:
A fat carp swims here.
A bass swims here.
A trout swims here.
A snake with brown stripes is sliding along the water.

The river flows swiftly here, fed by icy springs deep within the distant Misty Mountains. To the northeast you see a thick, dim marsh that makes travel in this direction almost impossible, beyond which you can vaguely discern rolling grassland. To the west the current slows and the river appears to branch into a broad delta.
12279:
A swan swims gracefully on the surface of the water.
A swan swims gracefully on the surface of the water.
A salmon swims here.
A bass swims here.
A brook trout is here, swimming in the current.

The current here almost slows down to a standstill. The water to the south becomes murky as it thickens into a vast, swampy area. The other edge of the Glanduin can be seen to the north. The river continues on towards the east and west in almost a perfect line.
12280:
A swan swims gracefully on the surface of the water.
A swan swims gracefully on the surface of the water.
A salmon swims here.

The river flows swiftly as it flows from the west towards a lake towards the east. To the southeast, past the muddy banks, a tower can be seen above the foliage of the swamps. An occasional fish can be seen swimming along the bottom of the river, and several swans have taken refuge by the south river bank. The water has a brownish tinge as mud from the swamps to the south merge with the river.
12281:
A snake with brown stripes is sliding along the water.
A bass swims here.
A trout swims here.
A nightingale is here, chirping a sweet melody.
A fat carp swims here.
The river flows lazily toward the west. The Glanduin is not known especially for its strong current. It is wide enough to make travel uncomfortable without a boat.
12282: The river Glanduin runs westwards through the marshes which rise up on the north side of the bank. The air is still and quiet, punctuated only by an occasional low howl from the marshes.
12283:
A trout swims here.
A salmon swims here.
A trout swims here.
A fat carp swims here.

So close to the outlet of a lake the river is very wide here, and the current is so strong that it takes effort to overcome it. To the northwest you can see a large hill and scouting southwards you can see a tower which overlooks the surrounding lands. North of here lies a path of some sort. The river continues to the west, and south of here lies an old road.
12284:
A salmon swims here.
A bass swims here.

The lake is narrow here, and it continues westwards into the River Glanduin. The water is light blue, but shallow here in the north-western corner of the lake. Water lilies are growing along the banks, and a trail can be seen following the northern shore. West and southwards the lake continues as far as the eye can see.
12285:
A salmon swims here.
A bass swims here.
A salmon swims here.

The south-western shore of the lake is surrounded by roads both on the western and southern shore. The lake seems to be very deep, and the colour of the water is deep blue. Not much seems to grow along the shores, but the area seems to be an ideal place to fish. North and eastwards the lake continues as far as the eye can see.
12286:
A bass swims here.
A trout swims here.
A bass swims here.
A bass swims here.

The southern side of the lake is deep, and the water is green. A current coming from the north is the reason for the ice-cold water. The shore consists mostly of rocks, and access to and from the water is hard. A road runs along the southern shore from east to west. No land can be seen north, east or west of here
12287: Along the southern shore a road stretches from east to west. To the south-east a bridge can be seen. The water here is dark and cold, and the shore is filled with rocks which makes it hard to exit the water. At the bottom of the lake the ground is also filled with rocks, making it uncomfortable to move compared to the sandy shores at the northern side of the lake.
12288: The lake is at its widest here, and only the northern shore can be seen in the distant horizon. Some trees can be noticed beyond the northern shore. In these parts of the lake the water is dark blue and it seems like this is the deepest part. In every direction besides north the lake seems to be without an end.
12289:
A red-breasted mallard swims about, periodically upending to look for food.
A salmon swims here.
A bass swims here.
A red-breasted mallard swims about, periodically upending to look for food.

Fresh water from a tributary pours into the lake from the north. Sand and gravel from the outwash have collected in shifting bars and shoals. Solid ground is far from here, however. The wind creates ruffles in the water, and longer swells wash towards the distant ends of the lake. A slow current is set to the west. Waterfowl wheel very high overhead, out of bowshot.
12290: Some cracked and splintered pieces of wood float here.

The river widens and the rushing waters from the north slow from their crowded and frenzied rush downstream as they begin to enter the lake. A shallow and soft delta forms at the entrance of the river to the lake and many particles of dirt can be seen swirling in the delta's waters. In the east and west the lake retreats to the south a bit leaving broad sandy shores bordered by many trees behind them.
12291: The fields are in good condition here, fertile and moist, yet not soggy or overgrazed. To the north the grasslands seem to continue in an ocean of swaying green foliage, while to the south an old stone path leads down towards the river.
12292: An ancient road lies before you, carefully crafted of individual stones woven together in a solid, intricate pattern. The skill and labour obviously put into the construction of this road has paid off, for it remains straight and flat even after many obvious years of ageing.
12293: Small pebbles and dark wet sand line the shores of the southern lake, which from this distance looks very calm and inviting. The air is fresh and the sound of birds carry across from the other side of the lake. To the north a grove of trees can be seen growing on the banks of a river which flows into the lake just to the west.
12294: The shore stretches westwards along the northern coast of the lake which appears to be fed by a river emptying into it to the west. Grasses and some weeds encroach on the shore from the north, some patches reaching all the way to the waters edge. In the distance to the north, a tall rock cliff can be seen.
12295: The river bends and twists as it makes its way downstream, following its course passionately, frothing and tumbling on itself. The water flows with a power that easily sweeps any debris with it as the large logs and branches in the current attest to. A slight rumble can be heard from the river as its strength begins to increase as it makes its way west.
12296: A robin is here, carrying small pieces of wood to its nest.

The river's waters speed along, splashing, swirling, and overflowing over anything in its path, as it hurries along downstream. The river bends around to the south, curving around a small sandy peninsula. As the river swings to the south, its inertia causes some of its waters to overflow westwards, creating a swampy area inhabited by lush ferns to the west. The river becomes a little muddled to the southwest as swamp waters rejoin the river there.
12297:
Gaakt, wielding a nimble blade, is standing here.
Von (twitter), wielding an ornate, steel-shafted warhammer, is standing here.

The river deepens, as the water becomes darker and the bottom is no longer visible. Apparently the current of the river has also picked up as the edges have become brown as the rapid water has picked up more and more dirt from the banks. A few leaves speedily floating down the river are another indication of the increased velocity of the water.
12298: The river bends here, becoming shallow at the same time but now flowing southwards. At the banks of the river reeds and tall grasses sprout up through the water's surface, creating a strip of marshy ground. The water itself is very clear and the bottom of the river is distinctly visible at the shallow parts of the river.
12299: A black snake, with red markings, is lying here.

A few small and slender forms can be seen darting to and fro under the shaded surface of the river along the banks. An assortment of rocks and cobbles decorate the river bed as the crystal clear water advances westwards. Far upstream to the east, the river is shallow and narrow as a patchwork dam, apparently made of timbers and branches, can be seen far in the eastern horizon.
12300:
An iron pick has been dropped here.
Some small rocks have been piled into a mound here.

Tall rocky cliffs rise up all about. Broken rocks lie strewn all over the ground. Here and there are rocks which appear to have been shaped by hands rather than nature. At the base of several of the cliffs, portions of rock have been gouged out leaving small alcoves in the cliffs.
12301: The ground here is elevated some twenty to thirty feet above the level terrain. The ground is rocky but firm and a few hardy trees grow upon this gusty mound. To the north and west the ground abruptly erodes straight down into the banks of a rushing river. Slowly, the high ground slopes down to the east while to the south it becomes rocky.
12302:
An apple tree with bright green leaves grows here.
An apple tree with bright green leaves grows here.

Lush healthy apple trees grow on this small peninsula which is surrounded by the River Glanduin. It appears this was once a cultivated orchard as the orderly rows of trees attest to. Still the enriching river with its alluvial soil and clear waters has taken over the task of nourishing this grove of trees. A large rock cliff stands to the east, preventing any passage in that direction.
12303:
A holly bush with dark green leaves is growing here.
Partly covered by the bush's green leaves, there are two piles of inkberries.

Prickly leaved bushes encompass much of the area, making passage a scratchy experience. Brambles overrun much of the open ground making the terrain even more treacherous. To the west the land rises sharply while to the north, the thick bushes gradually thin out.
12304: Some trees have grown together here into a small bushy island with the river on one side, and flatter land on the other. A thin carpet of grass covers the ground underneath the trees. The ground slopes down to the north as it reaches towards the banks of a river.
12305:
A holly bush with dark green leaves is growing here.
Partly covered by the bush's green leaves, there are two piles of inkberries.
A diamondback rattlesnake is coiled here, ready to strike.
A small brown snake is slithering around here.

A few sparsely leaved saplings and some thorny bushes dot the rocky and hilly terrain. Other smaller and thornier bushes cover much of the ground, leaving very little room to manoeuvre through. Here and there holes bore into the ground, betraying the existence of some wildlife.
12306: A tall pine tree grows here.

Here, the ground begins to dip significantly, angling down towards the river to the south. Colourful mosses, lichens, and wildflowers blossom and sprout inbetween and out from under boulders and their damp and soily undersides. The moisture on the rock surface of the ground makes footing treacherous and the prospect of a fall into the river more apparent, if not more likely.
12307:
A bright green holly bush is growing here.
Partly covered by the bush's green leaves, there are some hollyberries.
A bright green holly bush is growing here.
Partly covered by the bush's green leaves, there are some hollyberries.

The slope of the valley begins to level out as the valley starts to give way to flat terrain again. Bushes and tall weeds have a larger presence here, yet numerous colorful flowers still sprout up occasionally. On a few rockfaces near the river, moss and lichen can be seen thriving. The moisture and the hard rock surfaces add much danger and difficulty to the footing throughout this area.
12308:
A holly bush with dark green leaves is growing here.
A small brown snake is slithering around here.

The area is populated by low trees whose branches hang so low that the trees look like large bushes. The terrain is comprised of a series of small mounds which make passage somewhat tougher than usual. The ground itself is dusty and rocky with little else growing save for the grove of low trees which are rooted in between some of the mounds.
12309: An opossum stands here, sniffing around the ground.

A hard packed stretch of ground is the only remaining semblance of a trail which is intermittently overrun and covered by weeds and other plant life. The path heads roughly east and west, however it disappears on hard dry ground to the east and ends at the foot of a small mesa to the west. Small loose rocks on the trail make footing uncertain at times.
12310: A large marmot is here, scurrying in between the rocks.

The ground is ripped and torn asunder as if a series of tremors had ravaged the land, or as if some huge creature had awoken from the depths and angrily made its way up through the surface. It is not certain if either may be the case, however the small sharp hills and the trees now growing out at odd angles from the uprooted ground are an indication that this area has undergone a violent change.
12311: A brown fox is here, looking for some rabbits to chew up.

The bushes and small plants here are very sickly. The grass blades and leaves on other plants are yellow, instead of healthy green, and dark brown spots can be seen clustering on some leaves. The soil itself does not appear rich and lively but rather pale and sandy. The terrain changes into a flat and smooth plain to the east while it turns very rocky to the west.
12312: The land relaxes and flattens out into a gentle plain. Compared to the tall grasses and thick scrub growing to the west and the east, this low plain seems very silent and peaceful. Small grasses on the ground only reach as high as a handspan and traces of animal life are either well hidden or, more likely, nonexistent.
12313:
A holly bush with dark green leaves is growing here.
Partly covered by the bush's green leaves, there are two piles of inkberries.
A small brown snake is slithering around here.

The terrain is uneven with small thorny bushes clustering in low areas. Cracks in the soil are testimony of the severe lack of adequate water here. To the south the land seems much the same while a small patch of grassland can be seen to the east.
12314: A short and sturdy stick lies here.

The tall grass here does not have the usual solid green colour typical of most grasses. The blades are of a light brown tint and appear to be much thinner than normal wild grasses. The dried out remains of grasses on the ground give evidence to the harshness of life here.
12315:
A holly bush with dark green leaves is growing here.
A small brown snake is slithering around here.

Many leafy bushes and small trees cover the ground, giving the area a distinctly green and fresh aura. The soil is rich and dark under the lush tree branches which sprout out in all directions from the tree trunks. The thickness of the brush prevents any decent view of the areas in the distance.
12316:
A tall pine tree grows here.
A bear is here, covered with coarse black fur.

Many tall trees are rooted here upon the grassy slopes of what is a slight valley among mostly even terrain. The ground slopes down from the east as the valley sprawls westward. A thick soft layer of needles on the ground makes progress through the valley more comfortable if not easier. Far to the south, a glint of water can be seen at times.
12317: A clear spring babbles as cool water trickles out of the ground.

A large deep pond has formed here as a dam of timbers and twigs holds up its western end. Water wells up from some underground source, possibly a natural spring, and distrurbs the otherwise flat surface of the pond, creating little expanding wavelets. Water seeps over the dam and flows down westward as more continues to gush forth from under the pond. On the grassy shores of the pond, gnawed stumps of trees testify to the constitution of the dam, and the ingenuity of indigenous wildlife.
12318:
A tall pine tree grows here.
A robin is here, carrying small pieces of wood to its nest.

The landscape is dotted with young saplings and a few young trees whose trunks still bend at every breath of the wind. Among the trees stand numerous large gnawed stumps. The ground is somewhat open as a few bushes encroach on the open woodland. To the north is a large pond, the western edge of which appears to be held up by a dam made of logs and mud.
12319:
A bright green holly bush is growing here.
A bright green holly bush is growing here.
A holly bush with dark green leaves is growing here.

Round holly bushes seem to thrive in this area. The ground is spotted with numerous fallen holly berries, which give it a bloody appearance. Curly leaves, armed with small needles on their edges, on the holly bushes hamper progress through the area while the fallen berries make footing very slippery. A large road can be seen to the south.
12320: The terrain here is level and dry. Short brown grass covers the ground, looking much like hay ready to be baled. Dust swirls up from the grassland, here and there exposing the roots and runners of the grasses. The dry ground is interrupted by bushes to the west and a road to the south.
12321:
An erect shrub with green pinnate leaves is growing here.
Inside the shrub, there are two piles of crimson raspberries.
A bright green holly bush is growing here.
Partly covered by the bush's green leaves, there are some hollyberries.

Large leafy bushes cover the dark moist ground here. The prickly leaves of the bushes make progress slow as there is very little room between any of the bushes. Many berries grow on each bush though not all of the bushes bear the same berries. The smell of the berries gives the air a strong sweet flavor.
12322:
A black raven flies in the sky searching for flesh to prey upon.
A horse of the Rohirrim (Rood) is standing here, ridden by you.

A faint trail, which in reality is just a slight way through the bushes, heads east and west. A few old small prints in the ground seem to indicate that this trail is used by animals, which apparently are heading to and from a water source in the west as the glint of water can be seen far off in that direction.
12323: A tall pine tree grows here.

Trees populate this plain, giving it the look of a light forest. Tall pines stand in small clusters, their needles scattered about to form an uneven blanket over the grass. The grasses thrive among many of the trees, making the most of the open ground and the dead needles on the ground. To the west, the frequency of trees increases to form a wood.
12324:
A holly bush with dark green leaves is growing here.
A small brown snake is slithering around here.

Small bushes armed with many thorns carpet the rocky and otherwise barren ground. The ground itself slopes up and down in an uneven fashion, leaving many different sized mounds and depressions. To the east a large rock can be seen in the distance while to the south the ground becomes lush and lively with thick bushes and trees.
12326:
A holly bush with dark green leaves is growing here.
A small brown snake is slithering around here.

Small trees, bushes, and thorny vines comprise the bleak landscape. The thick plantlife covering the area makes it very difficult to traverse as there is little open ground to step on. Muffled rustling among the plants seems to indicate the presence of small wildlife.
12327:
A black raven flies in the sky searching for flesh to prey upon.
An opossum stands here, sniffing around the ground.

Wild tall grasses populate the area. The density and height of the grasses make it hard to move through the area. Visibility is also hampered and it is compounded by the fact that much attention must be paid to the tricky footing among the grasses. The blades of the grasses are sharp and firm, making a trip through the area an unpleasant, if not painful, one.
12328:
Yellow flowers, with grey-green foliage, grow in clusters here.
A dense carpet of blue flowers dip their heads in the breeze.

Thick grass is joined by ragged weeds and white and yellow wildflowers. Each weed and wildflower grows as high if not higher than the tall grasses. To the north the grassland continues while a large rock looms over the flat plains to the south.
12329: A large boulder is here, it must be heavy.

A huge mass of rock pushes its way up from the ground here. It probably stands some twenty feet high and is at least forty feet long. The rock itself appears to be of hard granite. Sturdy pines growing on the even ground nearby offer a sharp contrast to the unusual rock formation. Small patches of weeds and grasses grow among the pines.
12330: Blackened stumps of what once apparently were great thick trees are strewn all about. Dark ash covers much of the level ground, giving it a dead and rotting appearance. A patch or two of grass can be seen here and there, however, no saplings can be seen which would herald a possible rebirth of this wood.
12331:
A mass of wriggling vines drops on you from the trees.
A mass of wriggling vines drops on you from the trees.
A robin is here, carrying small pieces of wood to its nest.
A horse of the Rohirrim (Rood) is standing here, ridden by you.

Weeds, thorns, and brambles are interspersed among the wild grasses, clumping into small thickets. Also intermingled among the grasses are patches of wild honeysuckle and berry bushes, which enrich the dull green of the grasses with dark and bright colours. The honeysuckle and berries give the air a natural sweet scent. Trampled ground running east and west is the only indication of a trail.
12332:
A tall, stately, dome-topped tree grows here.
A tree-snake lies wrapped around one of the tree branches.

The land is flat all around and is sparsely covered with parched brown grasses. A great tree stands here with its thick tall trunk making it appear as if it were the only connection between the ground and the heavens. A large circular area underneath the overhanging branches of the tree is sheltered from much of the natural elements.
12333: A pack horse (Rood) is standing here, ridden by you.

The ground rises up into a small plateau, giving limited view of the surrounding area. Dust covers the ground and swirls up at every puff of the wind. The soil is barren and devoid of any rich topsoil to support any plantlife. To the south lies a road running east and west. A lone tree can be seen standing alone far into the northen horizon.
12334: This is a structure, or group of structures, walled with sheaves of grey-brown brush and thatched over with mud and canes.
