The walls, or partitions, are not solid or built up everywhere as high as the roof; essentially it is one continuous room broken up into numerous connected passages and cubicles. The possessions of the dwellers are few and not worth taking; the atmosphere is one of hunger, poverty, and neglect.
12335: A fishing rod has been left here.

This room, or area, is depressed far below the dwellings north of here; the earthen walls seem solid, and the air is cool and damp. Torches flicker and snap. The floor of thin wooden boards is old and cracked, and emits a hollow sound when trodden on; below it can be heard a lapping and gurgling noise. There is a fishy smell, and fish scales litter the floor and cling to your feet.
12336: A large, dusty alcove sits in a wall, smelling of soot.

This dim, open area is clearly below the surface of the ground; walls of dried earth enclose it on the east and south. A stone hearth filled with cold, thin ashes is here; around it are some wicker stools with symbols woven in them, the only ornamental things you have seen in this part of the village. There is little to dispel the impression of hunger, apathy, and poverty.
12337: Walls of dried and hard-packed earth surround you on three sides. Leaning against the northern wall is an empty weapons rack, made of rough, unfinished timbers and wooden pegs. Mouldering, dirty straw gives scant covering to the bare earthen floor, with rotten scraps of food scattered about near a wooden table in the centre of the room. To the west the room opens up into a larger common room.
12338: A dozen small bedchambers, the size of storage bins, are connected here by a narrow passage cluttered by roof-poles and partly obstructed by incomplete walls. Each has a shabby grass pallet and little else. You see nothing in the way of clothing, food, or weapons; each villager must be carrying all his or her possessions around for safekeeping. The outside walls are windowless and the light is dim.
12339: You are floating in a dark, roughly rectangular chamber, apparently under- ground. The stone walls are completely sheer, and clearly artificial. Water pours in from a sluice high in one of the walls and crashes down with a thunderous booming roar. An undertow attempts to tug you downward, but it is not so strong that you cannot resist it.
12340: A strong current pulls you quickly through an underwater passage. It is pitch black. The walls are smooth and flat, but you can make out nothing else.
12341: There are two prickly plants with blue flower heads here.

Dry grass is shining with its yellow colour all around this area. It is almost one foot high and grows dense. To the north these plains are surrounded by high hills. To the east the plains become withered and cracked. The road follows its course to the south and the west.
12342: A colony of red ants is here. The ants seem to ignore you.

Scattered grasses struggle to grow here from within the hard packed earth. Large cracks in the soil caused by wind and rain make life impossible save for a few hardy species of vegetation. Ants and other small insects roam among the cracked fissures as if living within miniature valleys. The Eregion plains look healthier to the west and south. To the north numerous hills forbid passage.
12343: A huge granite precipice juts out into the sky here over the cliff face. Resplendent alabaster columns rise up from the broken stone to defy the wind that seems ceaselessly to whip out from beneath the cliff. A quiet and cold power from within the cracked white walls seems to chill the air around the structure. Standing silent and aged, the temple still seems to be well kept. A massive exquisitely carved set of marble doors to the north lead within the temple. To the south a faint trail leads back to the grassy Eregion plains.
12344:
A somber elf moves about here, listening for the dead.
A somber elf moves about here, listening for the dead.
A somber elf moves about here, listening for the dead.
A somber elf moves about here, listening for the dead.

A long hall leads beneath the towering white marble columns to a stone pedestal standing at the base of the northern wall. Although kept very clean, the finely chiselled floor is shattered in places where some ancient tremor forced the temple to crack. A sacred quiet fills this vast hall and gives the air here an eerie chill. To the south huge marble doors open upon the Eregion plains. A small door opens into a private alcove to the west.
12345:
A neat straw pallet is lying here.
A heavy desk, made of solid oak, stands here.
Amanrandil the High Daedeltir stands here resplendent in tranquility (glowing).

This spartan cubicle is carved out of the western wall of the temple. A narrow window looks out upon the precipitous drop to the floor of the cliff. A bare desk and a straw pallet are the only items of note within this tidy white room. A peaceful aura emanates from patterns of elven runes carved upon the walls.
12346: Yellow flowers, with grey-green foliage, grow in clusters here.

Looking westward, the terrain is mainly grassy with the occasional small wood or hill breaking the fairly flat view. To the north there is a peculiar temple resting on the edge of a windy cliff. A grassy slope rises up to a hilltop in the east.
12347: A black marble monolith has been erected at the top of this hill. It seems to have some runes printed on it, although the lettering has faded over time. A marvellous view of the surrounding countryside can be seen from here. To the north and the east a dark forest covers the land, while to the west and south, grassy, undulating plains cover the leagues to the horizon.
12348: A tormented spirit engulfed in grief and despair advances.

Darkness engulfs the tunnel that leads deeper into the hillside to the north. A slight breeze can be felt in the tunnel, suggesting that it is not just a dead end. Someone very skilled must have dug this tunnel, for the walls are carefully hewn and stone pillar supports have been inserted in places. The floor is still rough, but has been carefully cut to remove most of the rough edges. A dry wooden ladder leads back up to the surface.
12349: Hewn by dwarven hands, this tunnel is a relic from the ancient elven kingdom of Ost-in-Edhil. A short way ahead the roof of the tunnel has caved in, and no further progress is possible. The smooth stone pillars look sturdy enough to hold the tunnel roof, which suggests that they may have been forcibly removed to seal the tunnel. An old metal plaque stands on a stone pedestal in the centre of this part of the passage. A cool breeze blowing from the north relieves the stuffiness of the tunnel.
12350: Covered by thick, green grass, this wide plain extends far into the southern horizon. Not far to the east, a river seems to have cut its way into a rocky hill, leaving a sharp cliff face in its wake.
12351: You stand upon an ancient road, masterfully crafted of interlocking stones which seem to have withstood the passage of time for countless years. In places the stones lie broken or missing and weeds shoot up between them, betraying the mortality of this impressive work. To the northeast a foreboding cliff juts sharply up from the grassy plains, breaking the monotony of your surroundings.
12352: A robin is here, carrying small pieces of wood to its nest.

Cracked stones pave the ancient road that led from Tharbad to Moria. Most of the stones are missing now, and the ones that are left are cracked and badly worn. The road follows the cliff to the northeast, with the river just south of the road.
12353: At the Bottom of the Falls

A black catfish is here, lurking in the mud.
A salmon swims here.

Gallons of cold water plummet down from a high ledge some thirty feet above. As the water falls through the air and crashes down onto the bottom, thick white foam is formed at the surface and a dense mist spreads through the air. The river bends southwards and the channel of the river widens, giving the waters enough room to calm and slow. Slimy green moss coats many of the rocks lining the sides of the river. A few trees can be seen bathing in the cool mist behind the rocks.
12354: A robin is here, carrying small pieces of wood to its nest.

The sparkling water speeds along, seeming to gather momentum as it continues westward towards a large drop of some thirty feet straight down. At the edge of the waterfall, the water level decreases and smoothed rocks can be seen on the riverbed and jutting up and out of the river's surface. Large boughs from a few sturdy trees growing near the ledge on the banks of the river extend out over the waterfall.
12355:
A bass swims here.
A salmon swims here.
A fat carp swims here.
A salmon swims here.

Shade-bearing green leafy trees cloak the river from both sides, their thick branches drooping over the clear water. Occasional leaves and bits of bark are bourne along near the turbulent surface of the river, bobbing and dipping up and down all the while. The river swings to the west, slowing a bit as it rounds the bend.
12356:
A salmon swims here.
A salmon swims here.
A fat carp swims here.

Water rushes around the beginnings of a wooden dam which extends out from the banks of the river. The water, itself, is cold and clear, and offers a good view of the shallow bottom of the river. A few fallen trees remain lodged near an eroding slope of clay, dirt, and rocks. Grass covers much of both banks, almost up to the water's edge.
12357:
A salmon swims here.
A bass swims here.
A salmon swims here.
A fat carp swims here.

Cold clean water sparkles with purity, allowing unobscured views of the smooth stones on the river bottom below, and of the schools of large fish that swim along. The river swirls and whirls over a few rocks that jut up above the surface, foaming a bit as it continues its journey west.
12358:
A salmon swims here.
A salmon swims here.
A salmon swims here.
A fat carp swims here.
A bass swims here.
A fat carp swims here.

The swirling current bends to the south, churning and foaming with increasing fury. The waters of the river crash against the steep shores in the west as the current attempts to turn southwards. At the top of the shores, stones line the side of what appears to be a road which runs along the river to the west and north.
12359: The swirling brown water of the river sweeps powerfully along to the west, accelerating here as if preparing to leap over some obstacle. Where it meanders northward, a long, level embankment can be clearly seen, protected from the river where necessary by stone breakwaters: the Road of the Smiths. Reeds grow in the shallows and oaks, willows, and leafy shrubs line the banks.
12360: A river otter splashes playfully here.

The broad river flows westward through an untenanted land. Along its banks are willow trees, thick bushes, and reeds in which wading birds look for fish to grab up. To the north, beyond the ancient road which parallels the river, low, heath-covered hills rise somberly.
12361: The Glanduin flows westward toward distant Tharbad and its appointment with the Mitheithel; its waters are brown, strong, deep, and powerful. For centuries wayfarers plied this river in boats laden with grain and fruits for the dwarven city of Khazad-dum; with logs for the building of the great Numenorean fleets, longer ago, with the works of the elven-smiths of Eregion. Now there is no one between here and the mountains to buy or sell; the forests have been cut, and the fields abandoned.
12362: A snowy-white egret stands here alertly.

The great river flows westward here, joined by the inconstant waters of the Forglanduin coming from the east and north. The valley of the river is flat and moist, fertilized by soil washed from upstream; but the uneven land round about, once covered by great and deep forests, is now rocky and soilless, and covered with treeless brush and heath. A ruined jetty extends from the north bank.
12363: The channel of the Glanduin meanders through a flat floodplain, a land of reeds, shallow water, mud flats and sand bars. But here in the main channel the water is always deep and strong, nourished by the snow that falls in the Hithaeglir to the east, deep brown with the soil and ash of Eregion that wash off its once-forested hills.
12364: The Glanduin flows westward here, parallel to the channel of the Forglanduin which lies to the north. To the south is fertile land nourished by the rivers' annual floods. At one time the Glanduin may have been a well-travelled waterway, but there is nothing along the banks to indicate that people have ever passed this way.
12365:
A fat carp swims here.
A fat carp swims here.

The broad Glanduin meanders north and west here through a flat floodplain surrounding its meeting with the Forglanduin. Its waters are brown and deep, and its flow is powerful. Gulls sail overhead looking for fish; along the banks you may see an otter sliding down a mud bank, or a carp splashing in the shallows.
12366: The river continues towards it's meeting with the Mitheithel at a steady pace as if worried about being late but pacing itself for the miles ahead. This section of the river flows in from the east and bends to the north. The bank along the northern side of the river is closely followed by a road that is thousands of years old, and showing the signs of it's millennia of neglect. The southern bank, which at the moment is more west than south, is lined by trees, but you catch glimpses of a vast plain beyond them.
12367: Flowing swiftly to the west from the south, the river Glanduin hurries on its journey to the west. On the northeast bank runs the road of the smiths, and on the southwest bank trees overhang the water shading the shallows. The rivers current threatens to pull you west.
12368: Here the river turns north as it flows from the east. The swift current passes over boulders creating eddies and ripples along the water's surface. To the west, there are trees along the bank and the road of the smiths runs along the oposite side. South of here, the trees fade into a thorny combination of holly and other bushes.
12369: The fast, swirling waters of the Glanduin flows from east to west, bubbling and gurgling past the holly bushes covering the southern bank. To the north the Road of the Smiths continues to shadow the course of the river, while past the holly bushes in the south grassy plains can be seen stretching off into the distance.
12370: The flowing water of the river sparkles, reflecting the sky in a hundred small places as the current pulls you to the west. On the south bank you see thick clumps of holly and to the north the road of the smiths is slowly being eroded by the river.
12371: As you gaze down through the water, you see myriads of pebbles and perfectly rounded stones along the bottom. They appear to wave back and forth as the surface of the water ripples from the current. To the north and east, the road of the smiths follows the river. The river turns from south to west here, and the southwest bank is choked thick with holly but gives way to tall grass further south.
12372: The fast paced current in this section of the river races over boulders and under logs, making for a dangerous if passable way. On the north bank, you see the Road of the Smiths, and a steep cliff rising behind it. To the south, the endless grasses of the Enedwaith strech out before you.
12373: The cold waters of the Glanduin continue on their journey towards the sea, lapping at the tall, lush grass that grows on its moist banks. To the north and west an ancient trail follows the river, beyond which lies a steep, formidable cliff. The faint shadow of mountains can be seen far to the north and east.
12374: The waters of the mighty Glanduin flow briskly northwards, bordered on the south by some sparse woodlands. To the east a steep cliff rises towards the sky from the grassy fields, towering over a weathered trail.
12375: A low cliff borders the river to the north and east, leaving just enough room for an ancient road to wind its path between these obstacles. To the southeast a vast, grassy plain spreads out into the distance, with the Glanduin acting as its northern border. Directly south of here, beyond the river, is a small wood.
12376: An ancient roadway, its well-crafted paving stones now broken, follows the banks of the river. A low, rocky cliff prevents any travel to the northeast beyond this roadway. Shrubs and bushes grows amongst the nooks and cracks of the rocky cliff face. To the southeast, a vast, grassy plain spreads before you as far as the eyes can see.
12377: This ancient roadway leads southeast and northwest from here, obediently following the banks of the mighty Glanduin. The craftsmanship evident in the broken stones beneath your feet indicate that this was once a great highway of some long-lost kingdom. A tall cliff to the northeast blocks any movement in that direction, and the river makes travel to the southwest awkward without a boat.
12379: A green frog is here, hopping around.

The water of the Forglanduin river which pours down from the north collects here in a shallow, brown pool draining westward. Around you, birds settle on the exposed gravel bars and mud flats; here and there are deeper pools, possibly hiding treacherous quicksand.
12380: These dense, thorny bushes end at the river to the west. The brush continuess right to the bank of the river. The ground here is covered with thin branches that have, probably poisoned, sharp thorns. Further to the west a road passes the river with the help of an old, sturdy bridge. To the east the brush continue into some woods while to the south lies a grassy plain.
12381: A black wolf pads restlessly, looking for its next prey.

All the trees here seem to be young and widely spread out. Further east the trees become taller and thicker, and they grow much more dense than here. Because of this the forest seems to become darker and darker eastwards. A river flows along the edge of the forest in the north. Westwards the forest fades, and turn into small, dense and thorny bushes. The young, light forest continues southwards.
12382: The forest is dark and damp here. The dense leaves of the trees above shut out virtually all light. On the ground the grass is short and wet. Some mushrooms grow around the base of the trees, but apart from these and some scattered weeds nothing much seems to grow here. Further east the forest seems even darker and more dense than here. Westards the trees are younger, and much less dense. The forest ends up near a river in the north while to the south it continues dark and damp.
12383: The trees are very tall and old here, with moss covering them entirely. Every exit from this place is alike, which makes it hard to decide where to go. The only exception is to the north where there is a green, mossy valley leading northwards. All around, the only sight to be seen is that of tall, dark trees, through which no light seems to pass. There are a lot of rocks and boulders on the ground.
12384:
A mass of wriggling vines drops on you from the trees.
Some thick writhing vines whip all around you.
A large elk is standing here, chewing grass and leaves.

This part of the forest is full of old and tall trees. The leaves seem to block out all the light. Moss grows all along the sides of the trees. On the ground the grass and moss is damp, and nothing but a few mushrooms grow here. No tracks can be seen on the ground. It would seem that not many people have dared to venture into these woods. The forest seems to end east of here, while it continues in any other direction.
12385: A black wolf pads restlessly, looking for its next prey.

The large, old trees cover the area from any light that the sun may provide. The ground is damp, and hardly anything seems to grow here beside mushrooms and some scattered weeds. The dark forest continues north and east from here, while to the west the forest seems to become lighter as the trees are younger and not as dense. At the southern edge of the forest the area is open, covered by small, thorny bushes.
12386: A black wolf pads restlessly, looking for its next prey.

This seems to be the south-eastern end of the forest. It's very dark and damp. The trees are all old, with long branches filled with leaves. They block out any light coming from the sun. Westwards the forest fades, and small, thorny bushes cover the area. To the south the forest turns into a flat area, with virtually nothing but dirt, sand and scattered grass. Beyond the eastern end of the forest lies an area filled with long grass.
12387:
A woodpecker is here, tapping on a tree.
A mass of wriggling vines drops on you from the trees.

Young trees spread out over a wide area here. Green, short grass grows in between the trees, and makes the ground soft and comfortable. Eastwards the trees grow denser and denser, and the forest becomes dark and damp. The young forest continues northwards. To the south and west the forest fades and large grassy plains, filled with tall grass, cover the area.
12388: The plains are very flat and they continue westwards. All over the plains long, uniform grass grows. The grass is dense and thick which makes it hard to notice small animals living in the grass. Some scattered trees grow into a light forest northwards. To the south-east a large, old tree appears in the otherwise flat area. Southwards the grass becomes less and less dense, and the area is nothing but flat land, consisting of dirt, sand and some grass scattered around.
12389:
A bright green holly bush is growing here.
A tall stag is here, grazing peacefully.

Dense, thorny bushes grow here. The bushes are low and they create a carpet of thorns as their branches spread out all over the ground. These brushy areas fade southwards, and turn into a flat, wide area. To the west the thorny bushes become scattered, and a grassy plain appears. North and east from here lies a forest with large, old trees that block the sun.
12390: The knee-high, dense grass covers the whole area, from the north and eastwards. To the west there is a small stream running northwards, with a path running by its eastern bank. Further south the area is all flat, and in the distance there is a beautiful lake. These plains continue north and eastwards, and further north-east lies a forest.
12391: The plains are covered with knee-high, dense grass. To the south and west these grassy plains continue, while to the east the plains end up in some light woods. Over the trees, far to the east, lies some high mountains with their tops nearly invisible due to the mist. Northwards the plains are covered by bushes, with slowly increasing density.
12392: These plains are filled with medium long, green grass. A few trees are scattered about at the eastern parts of the plain. West of the plains a road bends from north to west. At the northern end a river flows from the east, and disappears beneath a bridge north-west of here. Southwards a path winds its way along a small stream. The plains continue eastwards leading into a distant forest.
12393:
An orchid of light violet petals blossoms nearby.
A large elk is standing here, chewing grass and leaves.
A small termite is running around making strange sounds.

The slope is filled with niches and little irregularities, and what is most noticeable about the area is the sheer greenery that can be seen all around. Tall weeping willow trees shelter the ground from the open sky. Green moss carpets the smooth rocks resting on the ground, which is covered by lush grasses and clover. The ground, itself, is soft from moisture, which is in full supply and collects in small pools on the ground.
12394: Willows and alders grow thickly here in the fertile soil by the River Glanduin. Tall reeds grow in the muddy shallows, and you can occasionally hear a splash, either of a fish or of something trying to catch it.
12395: The forest around you is dead silent and very little light filters in through the canopy of the trees above. There is a slightly ominous feel here, but you can see nothing specifically alarming about the place. To the west the forest continues and you can just barely make out the form of a large boulder among the trees. To the south and east the forest gets less gloomy, but to the north you really can't pick out any details.
12396: The Outskirts of a Dark Forest

As you enter this wooded area, you notice that this is just the beginning of a much older and deeper forest, perhaps a section of the great forest that once covered much of this area in times now mostly forgotten. As you gaze north and west you realise that the forest is darker and more forbidding. In addition to being older and deeper, maybe it wouldn't be such a bad idea to head out onto the plains to the south and east.
12397:
A colourful butterfly is fluttering around here.
A small termite is running around making strange sounds.

Swaying to and fro, the grass around you shows the motion of the wind much like the ripples on water. Gazing to the south, east and west the grasslands continue as far as the eye can see. To the north and west is the edge of a dark and forbidding forest.
12398: The plains roll away in all directions, the tall stalks of grass swaying gently as if in a dance. Far to the north-east a small copse of trees stands out against the monotony, while north and west of here the grass gradually gives way to a large forest, several miles across.
12399: The flat land continues to the west and south from here. The area consists of nothing but dirt and sand, with some scattered grass in between. To the south-west lies a very large tree. The tree appears to be quite menacing in size, with its long branches casting shadows over the base of the tree. East from here the grass becomes less scarce.
12400: The land here is very flat and wide. Not much seems to grow here, as the ground mostly consists of dirt and some sand with some grass scattered around. This flat land seems to encircle a very large tree to the south. The tree is old, with dry bark and some cracks running along its side. North from here the area is covered by dense, thorny bushes, while the flat land continues to the east and west.
12401: A brown fox is here, looking for some rabbits to chew up.

The land here is very flat and wide. Some grass grows scattered around, while most of the area consists of dirt and sand. Not much seems to grow here, besides a few old, dried out, bushes that all seem dead. This flat land seems to encircle a very large tree to the south-east. The flat lands continue east and westwards. To the north the grass become denser, and a large grassy plain appears.
12402: The land here is flat and wide. It stretches out east and south, covered in long, uniform grass. The flat area seems to encircle a very large tree to the southeast. To the north you can see some grassy plains stretching eastwards. To the west there is a small path following the course of a stream which runs northwards, leading from a lake which you can just glimpse far in the south.
12403:
A mass of dark green leaves clings to a wall.
A grey wolf is here, thin from starvation.

You have arrived at the ruins of a group of buildings which were built against a low bluff to the north. They are very old indeed and for the most part only the foundations remain, completely overgrown with brush and creepers. The walls and ceilings may have been made of wood, as they have completely vanished. An inscribed block survives, which may be the cornerstone of the main structure.
12404: A nobleman stands here in antique costume.

A fell silence pervades this dark, sunken courtyard. You tread upon ancient ashes. A smell of burned meat and fat comes up from the ground; charred bones lie about. Yet this is no recent pyre. The air is heavy with timeless sorrow and rage, and a red flickering light seems to bathe the sunken courtyard. The walls are steep, and scorched black.
12405: The Outskirts of a Dark Forest

A few birds and animals seem to be about their business here, but they seem furtive, as if there was something dangerous nearby. It could be your imagination, but to the north and west the trees seem bigger and the interior of the forest is unusually dark. Maybe the holly scrub to the east or the grasslands south of here would be safer.
12406: Here, close to the Glanduin, its annual floods have built up a layer of fertile soil. Willows, alders, and leafy bushes grow thickly here. There is no sign that anyone has lived here for hundreds of years, although here and there you see a stone that might once have been part of the foundation of a house or barn. War and plague have left little trace of the farms of Cardolan.
12407: A river otter splashes playfully here.

You are in a wetland, where muddy ground covered with tall reeds slopes imperceptibly northward and eastward into the shallows of the Glanduin. The great river loops westward here, and when the water is high this low ground must all be completely submerged.
12408:
A holly bush with dark green leaves is growing here.
Partly covered by the bush's green leaves, there are two piles of inkberries.

Bushes and thorns mixed with holly pull at your clothing every time you try to move here. To the north and west you see the edge of some forests, though the west looks a bit more gloomy. To the east there is more holly scrub before a thin strip of trees. All points south however are open grassland stretching to the horizon, with the exception of a small copse of trees standing by itself.
12409:
A holly bush with dark green leaves is growing here.
Partly covered by the bush's green leaves, there are a few inkberries.

It is really hard to move here on account of the thick bushes and holly laced with thorns. To the west the way is similar, though you can see that the line of the trees to your north eventually curves around to the south in the distance. The sound of flowing water lapping a bank reaches you through the trees to the east. To the south, the endless plains of the Enedwaith stretch as far as the eye can see, interrupted only by a small copse of trees which stands alone to the southwest.
12410: A stand of trees has taken advantage of the sustenance provided by the Glanduin and thrives on this bank of the river. Beyond this narrow fringe, the prairie again dominates the landscape -- only along the river is there enough moisture to support such life.
12411: A holly bush with dark green leaves is growing here.

A mix of holly, thistle and thorns grow here making your going somewhat difficult and leaving hundreds of little red scratches on any exposed skin below about three feet. The way looks easier among the trees to the north and east or in the tall grasses to the south and west.
12412: The trees here sway gently in the breeze and whisper softly to the wind. To the north and east, the river Glanduin flows westward quickly and quietly. The thorny looking scrub to the south and west is rather uninviting but there appears to be open grassland beyond that.
12413: A small grasshopper clings to a blade of grass, ready to spring.

The grass here is about four feet high and your ankles are getting slightly wet from the water that has not yet evaporated at the base of the grass. Down near the roots there is almost no breeze and the sun is blocked by the grass stems. To the north and east is holly scrub and to the south and west the grasslands stretch away in the distance. To the southwest is a small group of trees that seems to stand alone in the middle of the grass.
12414: Small insects jump away as you wade through the grass here. To the north the grass gives way to a scrubby combination of holly and other bushes. To the east and west the grass gets taller and to the south is a stand of trees that seems to stand alone as if an oasis in the middle of this flat grassy land.
12415: A small grasshopper clings to a blade of grass, ready to spring.

The tall grass plays around you swaying and bopping against you in the wind. To the north and west you see trees looming up, apparently the beginning of a substantial forest, and to the south and east the grass gets somewhat shorter, only about three feet tall instead of the four to five foot stalks found here. To the southeast there appears to be a small copse of trees in the distance, standing on its own in a sea of grass.
12416: The green sea of grass to the south and west that is the Enedwaith stretches as far as the eye can see. There is a small island of trees standing to the east. To the north and northwest the edge of a forest is barely apparent on the horizon.
12417: Inside the Small Copse of Trees
A clear spring babbles as cool water trickles out of the ground.

A cool quiet pervades this small copse of trees, giving the impression that this simple place is far more significant than it looks. The area has a certain aura about it. The trees, plants and flowers growing naturally here are no different from all the others throughout Arda, yet their beauty far exceeds that of any grove cared for by men or elves.
12418: Waist high grass is all around you waving in a gentle to and fro movement. To the north and east the grass becomes somewhat taller and thicker. To the west, a small stand of trees rises up out of the plains. South of here you see nothing but empty grasslands stretching for miles.
12419: The grass is so tall here that you can barely see over the top of it! You should be on your guard since almost anything could hide around here. To the north and east is a prickly looking holly scrub. To the south and west the grass becomes a bit shorter. Far to the south you can see a huge, solitary tree and there appears to be a small copse of trees near the horizon to the west.
12420:
A holly bush with dark green leaves is growing here.
Partly covered by the bush's green leaves, there are four piles of inkberries.

Prickly and painful, this brushy area is filled with holly, thistle and a long almost vine like plant with round green leaves and very sharp thorns. This is a most unpleasant place to be. To the east, the flora is only slightly friendlier, dominated by holly with fewer thorns. To the north is a wooded area consisting of relatively young trees. West and south of here is grass so tall that it is hard to see over.
12421:
A bright green holly bush is growing here.
Partly covered by the bush's green leaves, there are two piles of hollyberries.

Here on the south bank of the river Glanduin you are surrounded by thick clumps of holly bushes. Despite the beauty of all those shiny green leaves and bright berries, the pointed tips of the leaves are sharp and quite painful to the touch. To the north, the river flows quietly. East and west of here also appears to be dominated by hollies, but to the south very tall grass takes over the landscape.
12422: The grass here is amazingly tall. You can only barely make out what might lie in each direction, and certainly anything or anyone could be hiding just a few paces away. Unfortunately, this grass seems to harbor several types of insects whose annoyance factor is inversely proportional to their size.
12423: Tall, thick grass surrounds you, about waist high, and extends in every direction. The land is very flat, and it seems almost impossible for any place to be this uniform. There is one break in the monotony however - a lone, dead, leafless and barkless tree to the east.
12424: A small grasshopper clings to a blade of grass, ready to spring.

Dry stalks of grass tickle you as you walk through the waist high grass here. The landscape is almost entirely flat allowing you to see for great distances in all directions. You notice an old snag standing all alone to the northeast.
12425: The grass here is tall and dry coming nearly to your waist. Oddly enough, to the south and east the grass is both shorter and greener. Other than the colour and height of the grass there are no visible landmarks.
12426: The grass here is short and dry, criss-crossed with the tracks of what appear to be small rodents. The short grass continues on into the south and east, with a splash of white appearing near the horizon. To the north the grass grows taller and greener, extending for as far as the eye can see.
12427: A small cluster of clover grows here.

Short green grass grows here. Some places appear to have been cropped and the only flowers that grow are short. There is a little clover and a few wild violets. To the west the grass is taller and drier, while to the east you see that the landscape is dotted with more clover.
12428: A small grasshopper clings to a blade of grass, ready to spring.
You are standing among the tall, brittle-dry stalks of grass that seem to be most common in this part of the Enedwaithe. The grass to the east is shorter but greener, with occasional flowers.
12429: The grass here is tall and has dried out to a golden brown. The wind ripples its surface and the motion reminds you of wind on the surface of a pond only much, much bigger. The grass appears to be shorter to the east and greener.
12430: The vast expanse of the Enedwaith spreads out all around you, the grass whispering softly in the wind, dancing to its own music. Small insects can be heard chirping in the grass, otherwise the fauna is quiet. In all directions all that can be seen is green grass, with no prominent features to mark the landscape.
12431: Dry stalks of grass scratch against your legs as you force your way along. The landscape all around is almost entirely flat allowing you to see for great distances in all directions, not that there is much to see. To the northwest a massive tree stands all alone, reaching into the sky, while in all other directions the major feature is grass.
12432: The grass here is a mixture of green and brown, apparently in the process of drying out. You can hear the occasional cricket chirping, and the occasional call of a meadowlark or nightingale. Other than the lone tree to the west, you can see nothing but acres of grass, green to the north and brown to the south.
12433: The grass here is tall and coarse, scratching and exposed skin as you attempt to force your way through it. Swaying slightly to and fro, it quickly covers the tracks of your passage, making the grass a good place in which to hide. To the north the grass gives way to a dense scattering of holly bushes, while to the south and west the grass thins out and becomes shorter.
12434: Rippling before the wind, the grass around you is about waist high, much shorter than it is to the north and east, but otherwise much the same. The land is so flat that it seems like you can see to the edge of the world. One massive tree with high spreading branches is the only thing taller than you.
12435:
A wild mare is watching you warily.
A young filly is just learning to walk.
A wild mare is watching you warily.
A young colt is frolicking playfully.
A wild mare is watching you warily.
A small grasshopper clings to a blade of grass, ready to spring.
A rabbit is here eyeing your presence warily.

Tall and magnificent this tree has a trunk that is so thick two men couldn't wrap their arms around it. The branches spread out many feet from the tree providing ample shade. Unfortunately there are no branches low enough to reach for climbing. In all directions you can see nothing except green, grassy plains rolling on towards the horizon.
12436:
A bee flies around here, collecting nectar from the flowers.
A bee flies around here, collecting nectar from the flowers.

Grass and small purplish flowers dominate the landscape here. Small insects dart between flowers gathering nectar and pollen. A closer look reveals that the tips of the grass have begun to dry out and turn brown. To the north, there is a large, lonely tree standing all alone in the vast grasslands.
12437: The land becomes drier to the southwest -- the green seen to the northeast is gradually replaced by amber. The slightest whisper of wind causes the entire landscape to rustle as the drying stalks sway in unison.
12438: Tall, dry, brown grass waves back and forth, prickling your skin where it hits. The land is similar in all directions, but perhaps there is some green in the far distant north or east.
12439: This area appears to have burned some time ago, among the grass you see occasional charred stubble, and once in a while a gleaming white animal skull. Nearby sits a blackened stump which barely rises above the sea of grass around you.
12440:
A small cluster of clover grows here.
A small cluster of clover grows here.
A small cluster of clover grows here.

Most of the ground here is covered with pink and white clover, thinning out towards the west. Where the clover thins out, short green grass can be seen, continuing on to the north and west. Further to the north the grass appears to dry out, appearing to have a brownish colour.
12441:
There are three handfuls of clover here.
A bee flies around here, collecting nectar from the flowers.
A bee flies around here, collecting nectar from the flowers.

Many hundreds of white and pink flowers dot the landscape all around you. Bees and butterflies move from flower to flower, minding their own business. The flowers thin out to the north and east but continue on to the west.
12442: Short, green grass generously sprinkled with daisies, chicory and other flowers stretches out around you. The occasional bushy plant can be seen to the east. To the west you see that the land is carpeted with pink and white flowers.
12443: Small, bushy plants sprout from the vast plains, their boughs covered with dangerous looking thistles. The leaves of these plants resemble those of the familiar holly bush, yet seem to have a slightly lighter hue.
12444: The grasses which sprout unevenly from the rolling plains are unlike those found anywhere else in Arda. Small bushes and trees lie scattered amidst this strange, knee-high ground-covering. The horizon is enshrouded in tangled vegetation and it is difficult to see beyond a few feet. Towards the east there is an occasional glimmer, as of light reflecting from water.
12445: A robin is here, carrying small pieces of wood to its nest.

You are on a slight rise in the grass-covered plain, which offers an excellent view of the surrounding territory. To the northeast lies the crystal blue waters of the Glanduin, a striking contrast to the endless green ocean of grass which makes up these plains. An occasional thistle bush makes travelling across this vast open expanse difficult and painful if the wrong path is chosen.
12446:
A large ram guards his flock of sheep.
A woolly sheep is grazing here.
A woolly sheep is grazing here.
A woolly sheep is grazing here.
Tall, thick grass grows all about you, towering six feet above the dense turf. A clump of strange trees stands to the north, while from the east comes the sound of swiftly running water.
12447:
A bright green holly bush is growing here.
A brown fox is here, looking for some rabbits to chew up.

Lush, green grass laps at the trunks of the thin, scrawny trees which dot the vast plain. Under the twisted boughs of these dried out trees, some odd plants seem to have taken root. Every so often there lies the great charred corpse of some ancient plant, struck down by lightning years ago.
12448:
The garden snake slithers harmlessly here.
A badger is here, exploring for food.

Scrawny, weather-beaten trees have clumped together over the years, making progress through the thick foliage difficult at best. The great expanse of the Glanduin lies to the north and east, betrayed by the brisk sound which echoes amidst the twisted tree-tops.
12449: Waist high grass mixed with tall yellow plumes of goldenrod dominate the landscape here. To the north, the grass becomes taller and denser, to the south and west, it just continues without the goldenrods. To the east, some trees and brush grow thickly along the edge of a large river.
12450: The grass here is simply too tall to be sure of what lies more than a few feet in any direction. It seems that nearly anything could hide around here simply by laying down. To the north, you catch glimpses of a large river, and to the south, the grass appears to be a bit shorter.
12451: The tall grass all around you seems to have reduced visibility to near zero, and it it is nearly impossible to tell what might lie in wait here. The small biting insects that live in these grasses, however, seem to have abolutely no trouble finding you.
12452:
A bright green holly bush is growing here.
Partly covered by the bush's green leaves, there are two piles of hollyberries.

Though the holly lining this side of the bank is quite pretty, you have to be quite careful to keep from getting stuck by the sharp points on its leaves. To the north and east, the Glanduin flows by the bank. To the south lies very tall grass. West of here the vegetation is very similar. Further to the north you can see that the river is begining to undercut an ancient road.
12453: A bright green holly bush is growing here.

Holly bushes line the river bank here. Thick and prickly, these plants make travel quite painful, but not impossible. East and west of here the vegetation is similar. To the south tall grass takes over and to the north the river Glanduin flows quietly westward.
12454: The ground here is moist and the grass seems like it is growing out of control. You can only just barely see over it. If you stand on the tips of your toes you can tell that there is some sort of lone, dead tree to the south.
12455: A woodpecker is here, tapping on a tree.

Here stands a tall, dead tree with no bark. The only signs of life it bears now are the holes drilled in its side by flickers and other woodpeckers in their search for grubs. The only thing along the horizon in all directions is endless flat grasslands, the Enedwaith.
12456: Little voles and mice seem to be common here and are continually scurrying past your feet. They appear to have built their own little network of tunnels in the grass. To the north, you see an old dead barkless tree. To the south and east the grass gets shorter and drier.
12457: A small grasshopper clings to a blade of grass, ready to spring.

Short, dry grasses interspersed with thistle and burdock are all around you here. You also notice bare spots with dried out rocky soil here and there. To the east there is a large outcropping of rock that seems to jut out of the ground.
12458: The grass appears to be split into two regions here. The eastern side is quite green, but to the northwest of where you stand it becomes first drier then taller. The land is slightly lower to the southeast.
12459: A small cluster of clover grows here.

Short green grass mixed with clover and dandelions seems to be growing well here. Some areas, especially those south of here, seem to have been cropped close to the ground. To the north, you see a large spike of rock projecting out of the ground like a giant's finger.
12460: Green and about knee high, the grass here is soft and mixed with various flowers, including daisies and black-eyed-susans. Butterflies fly back and forth from flower to flower drinking nectar. Things seem quite peaceful.
12461: Prickly, white-stemmed plants, with blue flower heads grow in abundance.

The grass here is dry and short. Many areas are not even covered with grass at all, showing the rocky soil and allowing the wind to stir up little clouds of dust. To the west you see a large finger of rock jutting up out of the plains. To the east the land is lower and closer to the river with much taller and greener grass. To the south you see short green grass and flowers as far as the eye can see.
12462: The grass here is drying out. The tops of most blades are dry and brown, but the base of each plant is still barely alive. To the east there are trees, also drying out, but oddly the bushes at their base are bright green with many shiny leaves. To the south the land rises and dries even further.
12463: The grass is shorter here and no longer covers every inch of the ground. Through the breaks you see a stony, dusty, dry soil clearly in need of a good rainshower. Small weeds and the occasional hardy thistle also grow here. To the south you can see a large outcrop of rock.
12464: A clear spring babbles as cool water trickles out of the ground.

A massive jagged finger of rock rises out of the ground here. Smaller boulders surround its base. The south side seems to be seeping water from a small spring. As the water flows south it seems to spread out and seep into the thirsty soil. As you would expect, the grass is notably greener to the south.
12465: The grass here seems to be taller to the north and shorter to the south. This is apparently the result of water availability since it also changes from green to brown along the same gradient. Other than grass, the only thing you can see is an old dead snag to the west and the land seems to rise slightly to the south.
12466: Tinder dry and brittle, the grass here crunches underfoot as you travel across it. Use of fire here is probably not a good idea. The blackened tree to the northwest is a stark reminder of this.
12467: The burnt and blackened skeletal remains of a human are here.
All around you the grass is dry and brown. Several areas look as if they may have burned recently, especially to the west. In the distance to the west stands the stark form of a burnt tree.
12468: A small grasshopper clings to a blade of grass, ready to spring.

The grass here has gone to seed, the tops have completely dried out, and the occasional animal or bird can be seen gathering seeds from the large tufts on top of each stalk. Only a little green is left here. To the south there is even less. To the north the grass still has some green to it.
12469: The grass here once grew thickly, and is tall, but now the leaves have turned brown at the top, and the stalks are releasing their seed, as they dry. Further south and west the grass is even dryer, while north and east it is still green, and growing.
12470: A badger is here, exploring for food.

The grass here is about waist high, but it has dried out and turned a light yellow color. The stalks are dry and brittle, conditions that are just right for a grassfire. As you look along the horizon you notice a very large tree standing all by itself to the east.
12471: The golden fields of swaying grass extend for miles in every direction from here, only interrupted by one small copse of trees off to the north west. The vast extent of the plains of the Enedwaith begins to weigh on your mind, but for some reason your attention is continually drawn back to those trees.
12472: A rabbit is here eyeing your presence warily.

The mixed brown and green grass here is clearly of two types. One has a tufted head like wheat and the other has a rounded head, and is probably timothy. To the north is a small stand of trees and bushes growing thickly together. The view in all other directions is uninterrupted, endless fields of grass.
12473: A colourful butterfly is fluttering around here.
Golden, dry grass waves back and forth around your waist with a gentle swishing sound. The gently undulating landscape is uninterrupted in all directions.
12474: The grass here is a mixture of brown and green. The brown tops of the seed stalks are releasing their seeds at the slightest touch, they are getting into all your clothing, making you itch. To the south and west the grass is about the same, but to the north and east it is greener.
12475: Although these plains are home to hundreds of varieties of grasses, the lack of moisture means that the stalks are often dry and brittle. To the south, the blackened remnants of a once mighty tree reach toward the sky like a withered claw.
12476: Stark and bleak, the charred remains of a tree which has been hit by lightning stand here in the middle of brittle, dried out grass. Between the split caused by lightning, and the fire damage it is clear that this tree will become a dead snag standing alone in this sea of grass.
12477: A colourful butterfly is fluttering around here.

Blackened by a fire that passed through here, the grass has been burnt to a stubble all around you. The first shoots of new fire weed and grass are struggling to re-establish themselves in the dry soil. To the west and north you see the golden brown of dry, unburned grass, though the eerie shape of a burnt tree is also evident to the north.
12478: The landscape here is quite flat and monotonous. Dried out golden grass stands all around you. There doesn't seem to be any good landmarks that you can see from here. To the north and east the land is darker for some reason.
12479: Occasional tufts of dry grass and dead, dried up weeds dot the land here. The ground is mostly covered with dark gravel and rocks though many appear to only be dark on one side.
12480: A rabbit is here eyeing your presence warily.

Crunchy, dry grass surrounds you. This area is badly in need of a long soaking rain. Even cricket calls and vole tunnels through the grass are scarce. The landscape is much the same in all directions, tinder-dry and featureless.
12481: The grass here is almost dead. Only the bottoms of the stalks have any green left in them at all. Tracks and trails of large animals can be seen where the grass is pushed down and flattened. Some appear to be made by hooves, others are less distinct.
12482: The grasslands around you stretch on towards all horizons. There is nothing remarkable in any direction. Aside from the occasional bird song, things seem pretty quiet.
12483:
*Lumpin the Fallohide Hobbit*, wielding a black runed dagger, is here, riding a pack horse.
A pack horse is standing here, ridden by *Lumpin the Fallohide Hobbit*.

Tall golden brown stalks of grass sway in the breeze here and there and essentially everywhere for as far as the eye can see. The lone exception to this is a small copse of trees to the northeast. Something about those trees feels different, but you can't be sure what from this distance.
12484: Vast endless stretches of grassy plain roll gently away in all directions. Far in the distance to the west you see a tree standing alone on the plain. To be visible at this distance it must be bigger than any tree for many miles around.
12485: The grass around you appears to be dry and brittle from lack of water. It crunches as you walk through it and you can see your backtrail clearly. The horizon is flat and featureless in all directions.
12486: Dry, brown grass ripples in the wind around you swaying too and fro. The plains are brittle and dry for as far as you can see in all directions. To the west the grassland starts to become rockier, the ground studded with stones and cracks where the bare earth has dried up.
12487: Endless flat plains of grass stretch on for miles in every direction. There are few landmarks here at all, and it would be quite easy to lose your bearings here. To the east you see that the grass has been burned by a grassfire, while to the west the plains become rockier before meeting a cliff which can just be made out on the western horizon.
12488: A rabbit is here eyeing your presence warily.

Stretching out in all directions, the grassy plains march on towards the horizon. Swaying gently in the wind, the grass almost seems to be dancing to some unheard tune of a time long gone. To the north-east the grass seems to be darker and shorter, looking burned in paces, while to the west you can make out a small path leading up towards a cliff.
12489: The path bends west and north here, along the slopes up to the cliffs to the north-west. The path winds its way between the rocks and boulders lying around. Dirt and some scattered grass cover the path. To the north the path continues along the wall of the cliffs, and ends up in a rocky plain further north. To the west the path runs along the grassy slopes that descends from the cliffs above.
12490: This path seems to appear out of nothing. In among the rocks and boulders this path suddenly appears. The area around the path is totally covered with rocky plains. Nothing seems to grow here at all besides a few scattered, dried out bushes. To the west tall cliffs rise above the ground, impossible to access from here with their vertical walls. The path continues southwards.
12491: A brown fox is here, looking for some rabbits to chew up.

Covered with rocks and boulders the area lies beneath the cliffs to the west. The sides of the cliffs to the west are almost vertical, and there is no way someone could climb up there without being an experienced climber. The plains continue north of here, while to the south a small path appears from in between the rocks and boulders.
12492: The area is covered with rocks and scattered boulders. Between the rocks and boulders the ground consists of dirt and short grass, making it an ideal place for small animals like rabbits and foxes. Small, scattered holes can be seen around on the ground. To the north a flat area opens up, less rocky but even more deserted than here. Further west some cliffs rise above the ground and block the passage and view.
12493: Northwest from here a large tree grows, with its enormous branches casting long shadows around its base. Apart from the tree nothing much else seems to grow in this flat area. The area is covered with dirt and sand, with some scattered grass inbetween. To the east the lank grass is less scarce and turns into tall, green grass while the flat area continues north and west from here.
12494: This flat area consists mostly of dirt and sand, besides some scattered grass. To the west a large tree blocks passage. Its branches span out wide, and cast long shadows around the base of the tree. The flat, wide open areas continue south and westwards, while eastward lies an area with tall grass. In the eastern horizon high mountains rise above the ground, covered with mist.
12495:
A small termite is running around making strange sounds.
A small termite is running around making strange sounds.
A small termite is running around making strange sounds.
A small termite is running around making strange sounds.

Huge on the outside, the tree is totally hollow from the inside. The walls of the inner side of the tree are remarkably smooth. Great care must have been taken at carving the inside of the tree. Although it appears to be abandoned now, some noise appears to be coming from below. The bottom of the tree, as well as the northern wall, has some cracks in it, probably made by ants.
12496: The flat land continues to the east and west from here. The area consists mostly of dirt and sand, with some grass growing scattered in between. To the north lies a very large tree that blocks the view and passage. The tree appears to be quite menacing in size, with branches that span out, casting long shadows near its base. To the south some cliffs block the way.
12497: The cave is dry and warm. It has clearly not been formed by nature, but made by people long ago. Ancient the cave has been left abandoned for a long time. The walls are made of huge blocks of stone. Some cracks can be seen on the western wall. It's a long way up to the roof. Far up on the eastern wall there seems to be a large crack that lets in some air.
12498: Old cliffs cover the area to the west. Cracks and slits cover the ground, and without being careful it's easy to tumble and fall. Small weeds and scattered grass grow in between the slits and cracks. West from here there are more cliffs while to the east the cliffs abruptly come to an end and down below to the east a small path continues northwards through a rocky area. Southwards a slope descends, leading to a path going west and east along the slopes. To the north some cliffs block the passage.
12499: The slope gently rises up towards the cliffs in the north. The ground is filled with semi-long, wet grass, which makes it slippery. Further up the slope the ground is covered with less and less grass, and consists of mostly stones and rocks instead. Down below a path runs from west to east along the slope. Further east the slope descends down to some rocky plains.
12500: Slopes surround the path northwards, leading up to the top of some cliffs in the north. The slopes are covered with grass, nearly down to the side of the path, only parted by some small bushes at the side of the path. At the southern side of the path a large plain stretches out from west to east. This path continues east and west from here.
12502: A sturdy pack horse is standing here.

The slopes of this hill are very steep, and climbing here offers quite a few challenges. There are a lot of boulders and cliffs all around. Close to the west lies the top of this green and steep hill. A path runs north from here, along the cliffs lying to the north. In the eastern horizon lies some high mountains covered by mist.
12503: This path runs along the cliffs from north to south. The cliffs are littered with small weeds and patches of grass of uneven lengths. The path winds on to the top of the cliffs in the north, while to the south it passes the foot of a hill which rises above the cliffs. Westwards a large flat area can be seen, consisting mostly of dirt and sand with some scattered areas of grass.
12504: Some grass is spread out in between the rocks. The cliff consist of rocky ground, with some boulders and smaller stones lying around. To the east a wall of stone blocks the passage. Some cracks can be seen in the wall, as it seems old and worn out by the weather. Some of the cracks are large enough for small animals to enter. West and northwards the cliffs fade out, and a large flat area appears, while to the south a path runs along the cliffs.
12505: The flat lands continue to the east and west from here. To the northwest of you there is a very large tree growing. The tree appears to be quite menacing in size. Never before have you encountered such a tree. The branches of the tree span out, shading a large area at its base. To the south you can see a path climbing up the hills.
12506: A tall stag is here, grazing peacefully.

This flat land stretches out in every direction. Besides some scattered grass and a few dried out bushes in between the sand and dirt, nothing much grows here. This flat area seems to encircle a very large tree to the east. The tree blocks the passage in that direction with its long, thick branches. Far to the north some grassy plains appear, while further south the flat area ends up in several cliffs rising above the ground.
12507:
The corpse of a cavebear is lying here.
The corpse of a cavebear is lying here.
The corpse of a cavebear is lying here.

This warm cave is large and dry, besides a damp area around the opening leading upwards. The inner parts of the cave are dry and warm, with their dark grey stony walls. A small plateau is carved out a foot or so above the ground in the back of the cave. The floor is filled with a small layer of dust and dirt, with solid rock beneath. The only exit from the cave seems to be upwards through a hole high up on the wall.
12508: The beautiful lake spreads out to the south and west, calm and peaceful. The water here is light blue, and warm. It is possible to see the bottom of the lake if one looks closely. North from here a steep hill rises from the shore of the lake and blocks any escape in that direction. To the east a flat area seems to go on forever.
12509: A swan swims gracefully on the surface of the water.

The lake continues to the north and west. The water looks clear and deep. The cliffs surround lake to the south. There does not appear to be any way to climb those cliffs, as they rise up from the banks of the lake. To the east a flat area seems to go on forever. Far to the north a stream flows out from the lake.
12510: This is the south-western part of the lake. Nothing much grows along the shores here. The water is cold and deep in this area. To the east and south, all that can be seen are cliff walls towering high above the lake. The only way to continue is over the lake to the north or east. Far to the east, above the lake lies a barren hilltop.
12511: A swan swims gracefully on the surface of the water.

This is the western end of the beautiful lake. The lake continues east and south from here. Around the lake flowers grow close to the shore, together with short, green grass. Beyond the western shore of the lake a group of tall cliffs rise into the air. They seem impossible to access from here, with the steep slopes leading up to the top. A small stream flows north away from the lake.
12512: Many tall cliffs cover this area, as they lie close together. They lie so close together that it is possible to jump from one to another without risking much. Some dirt and some small bushes cover the stony ground. There is a path winding southwards down the steep hill. South, along the cliffs, there is a narrow path leading eastwards, while to the north lies a beautiful lake stretching out from north to east.
12513: The path winds its way between rocks and boulders leading eastwards. A few small bushes and some scattered grass grow on each side of the path. Steep slopes lead up to the cliffs north of here. In between the rocks and boulders a small path can be seen winding upwards along the side of the cliff. The areas south and west from here are totally blocked from view by rocks and stones, and are inaccessible from here.
12514: The path bends its way down to the west and gradually up the cliffs to the north. The path is wide, flat and easy to follow here, although it is mostly covered with stones. Large boulders and rocks make it impossible to move both south and eastwards. North-west from here green plains cover the horizon as they stretch out as far as the eye can see in that direction.
12515:
A mountain goat is here, jumping from cliff to cliff.
A mountain goat is here, jumping from cliff to cliff.

Plains cover the path as it winds down to the level of the area below the cliffs. The path is wide and easy to follow here, as the area is not as steep as it seems to be further north closer to the cliffs. The area eastwards is blocked from view due to large boulders and rocks that are in the way. To the south the path bends westwards.
12516: A brown fox is here, looking for some rabbits to chew up.

Rocks and boulders cover the path on the southern side, and to the north a tall cliff rises above the ground. A small track leads north from this path, and winds its way up towards the top of the cliff. It seems impossible to reach the top without any climbing experience. This path continues east and west from here. To the east the path ends up in an area filled with hills and grassy plains.
12517: A brown fox is here, looking for some rabbits to chew up.

The path is surrounded by plains and slopes filled with long green grass. The grass is short along the path, as many people and animals have travelled here. Slopes slowly climb up towards the top of a hill north of the path. South of the path there is nothing but endless plains. To the west the path enters a rocky area with cliffs on the north side and large boulders on the southern side.
12518: Tall cliffs lie westwards from here, while to the east the cliffs end and turn into an area of hills. The ground is rocky with a few small bushes growing in the small cracks in the cliff. The southern side of the slope is very steep, and the small path that winds its way down the side seems impossible to follow without some kind of climbing experience. Down below a path runs along the cliffs from west to east, and to the north lies a large, beautiful lake.
12519: Before the Top of the Hill

The ground here quickly turns into a steep slope. A lot of huge boulders are lying around. The path leads up and eastwards, leading to the top of the hill. Judging by the steep slopes it might be needed to be an experienced climber to be sure to reach the top of this hill. Northwards the slopes fade, and the land becomes flat.
12520: This flat area, covered with short, dense grass, appears to be stuck between some high cliffs rising in the east, and the lake that lies to the west. The lake stretches out to the west and by the edge of the lake the short, soft grass is filled with flowers of all kinds. Along the shore several water lilies slowly flows by in the clear blue water. Southwards a hill starts to rise into the air with its long, rather steep, slopes.
12521: This area is covered with short grass that becomes more sparse in the northern parts. To the east the ground increasingly consists of rocks as it approaches some high cliffs rising in the distance. To the west of here a beautiful lake appears, with different kinds of plants and flowers growing in the short, soft grass on the shores. The flat lands continue southwards along the edge of the lake.
12522: The flat land continues to the north and south from here. The area is covered with scattered grass, growing in between the spots that are covered with sand. To the north-east there is a very large tree growing. The tree appears to be quite menacing in size. The branches of the tree span out, casting shadows over a large area at its base. West from here a large hill rises far above the ground.
12523: The area here is very grassy, but in some places there are some rocks lying scattered around within the grass. They have probably been broken off the cliffs nearby. A tall, old and very large tree grows to the east. The branches of the tree cast shadows all around its base. To the north and south the flat lands continue, while in the west a small path runs along the bank of a small stream.
12524: A large hill looms above. There is a small path leading upwards to the top. The path is very steep, and it seems impossible to proceed in that direction without any knowledge of climbing. West from here a stream flows by, leading into a lake to the south. Northwards a path starts and continues along the bank of the stream. Past the hill eastwards there is nothing but wide flat plains as far as the eye can see.
12525: A river otter splashes playfully here.

To the south lies a small but beautiful lake. The stream flows out from the lake and heads northwards. Westwards tall cliffs rise up from the side of the stream. The cliffs seem impossible to access from here, as they are steep and slippery. East of the stream a steep hill rises into the air. The sides of the hill are filled with fairly short grass.
12526: The cliffs are hard and slippery, which makes it hard to move. They got a beautiful white colour. To the east, far below, a small stream leading into a lake appear. It seems hard to continue east from here, down the steep side of the cliffs. Plains reach out to the west, covered with tall, green grass. On the southern side a path starts, leading down from the cliffs.
12527: The path winds its way down the cliffs to the south and gradually up the cliffs to the north. The ground is hard and slippery, something that requires full concentration to avoid falling. There are a lot of big boulders and rocks that keep diverting the path from its intended straight line. Along the east side of the path lies a beautiful lake, while to the west plains reach out.
12528: The path winds its way down the cliffs to the south and gradually up the cliffs to the north. Large rocks and boulders makes it difficult to move east or west from here. To the east lies a beautiful lake, while westwards plains filled with tall, green grass cover the view. The path is slippery as its covered with hard, and partly wet stones.
12529:
A cute young hawk is sitting here waiting for his mother to feed him.
A mountain goat is here, jumping from cliff to cliff.

A stream running north and east from here surrounds the cliffs. Further north lies a large, dark blue lake. Its hard to move here, as the ground is hard, rocky and hardly ever flat. The cliffs continue south from here, while to the west a small forest starts at the base of the cliff. The forest is filled with thin, young pine trees, and beyond it green plains stretch as far as the eye can see.
12530: The stream continues east and north from here. The water is cold, and the current makes it difficult to move. To the north the stream passes a bridge, while on the western bank thorny bushes grow close to the water. The dense bushes, full of thorns, make it impossible to climb out of the water without being hurt. South from here high cliffs rise up from the banks of the stream, and into the air.
12531: The stream flows from the south to the west. It's shallow, and the bottom is covered with sand, except for a few stones that are spread out on the bottom. The water is cold, and a small current makes it harder than normal to move. Beyond the northern bank of the stream a road runs north and west past the stream with the help of a bridge. East from here a small path leads up to the side of the road.
12532: A blooming water-lily floats on the surface of the water.

The small stream passes east of some tall, white cliffs. It seems impossible to access the cliffs from here, due to steep walls leading up to the top. A path follows the stream on the eastern side, apparently leading to a road that lies north of here. To the south the stream exits into a beautiful lake, while it continues to the north.
12533: The small passage below the bridge is damp and cold. Pieces of wood and timber brought here by the stream lie stranded along the banks. The bridge is made of stone and wood, and a hatch can be seen up between the archways. The water is shallow, but a strong current makes it difficult to move. The stream continues southwards, while to the north a large, wide lake continues as far as the eye can see.
12534:
A trout swims here.
A bass swims here.

From beneath the bridge looks like it's made of stone and wood. It appears as an old, sturdy bridge, with plants growing on its walls. On one of the walls a ladder is running up to the archway of the bridge, and a small hatch leads to the top of the bridge. East of here the river widens and continues northwards, while to the west a large lake continues as far as the eye can see.
12535: The view is amazing from up here, with the possibility of seeing far in every direction. To the north lies the river, with a road shadowing it along its length. To the east flat lands stretch into the distance, with the tall peaks of the Misty Mountains rising into the sky on the horizon. Westwards lies grassy plains, punctuated by rocky cliffs. Down below, to the south, lies a small stream with a path running alongside.
12536:
A small termite is running around making strange sounds.
A small termite is running around making strange sounds.
A small termite is running around making strange sounds.
A giant termite is here, crushing skulls and bones.

Deep underground, this lair looks like it was carved out by a creature to secure it and its family. Inside this tree the walls are made of wood, but some dirt and small branches cover the floor. The lair is filled with the smell of rotting flesh and damp wood. The floor, slimy and slippery, is filled with decapitated remains of the poor victims of this foul creature.
12537: This path seems to lead to the cliffs east of here. The path is rocky, and it is hard to move without the risk of tumbling and falling. North and north-west of here there are enormous plains, covered with tall green grass. Movements can be seen in the grass as animals move about. To the west the path climbs slowly up to a rocky plateau providing an excellent view of the surrounding area.
12538:
A mountain goat is here, jumping from cliff to cliff.
Dreux the Hobbit, wielding a nasty orkish fang, is standing here.
A stocky mountain mule is here, waiting to serve.

This plateau overlooks the plains in the north and north-west. About the only thing that can be seen is long tall grass, but some movements and sounds can be seen and heard as animals move around in the tall grass below. There are mostly rocks lying around here, and slghtly to the north a small, smooth rock with grass growing round it covers the ground. East of here a path leads down from the plateau.
12539: This is the end of the plains. Rocky areas lie south of here, while plains covered in tall, thick grass cover the horizon in the north. The grass is thinner here, as the ground consists of mostly rocks which makes it harder for plants to grow. East of here a rocky plateau rises above the tall grass. It seems hard to access from here due to a steep wall of large rocks leading up to the plateau.
12540: A fat rabbit is here, chewing on some grass.

Tall grass as far as the eye can see in every direction is the only thing that can be seen from here. The grass is so dense it's hard to make out the ground, which leaves it hard to move around in this area. The ground seems to be covered with small rocks. When there is total silence animals can be heard moving around in the grass.
12541: South of here a rocky plateau rises up and covers the view in that direction, while plains continue as far as the eye can see in all the other directions. The tall grass makes it hard to see anything further than a few hundred meters in any of those directions. The ground is rocky here, and the grass is not as thick as it is further north.
12542: This seems to be the south-eastern corner of the plains. The grass is thinner here, as the ground is rocky and less fertile than other parts of these plains. A path leading the way in between the cliffs runs along the border of the plain to the south and east. The cliffs lie further east, with their beautiful white colour. South west from here lies a plateau, about as tall above the ground as the green grass in the plains north of it.
12543: A stocky mountain mule is here, waiting to serve.

This appears to be the beginning of an underground tunnel. The roof and walls are made out of stone. In the eastern corner of the tunnel the roof seems to have some cracks that let some light through. The tunnel is very wide, and judging by the smoothness of the walls must have made by someone. The tunnel continues southwards.
12544: The tunnel bends to the west and north here. The tunnel inclines down to the west and it gets wider northwards. The walls of the tunnel are damp, with some water dripping from the stones. While the walls are made of stone the floor is covered with dirt, which makes it rather slippery due to the water dripping slowly from the walls.
12545: As the tunnel continues westwards, more and more water seems to cover the floor of the tunnel. The floor is filled with mud here which makes it hard to move around without falling. The tunnel seems to widen out a bit again westwards, and the sound of water can be heard from the same direction. Still the tunnel slopes downwards to the west, while it's a struggle to move in the opposite direction.
12546: As the tunnel widens out a small underground lake appears. The lake is shallow here, but it seems to become deeper further west. Further west the lake slips out of vision due to the dark and the roof becomes lower and lower. The water is cold as ice although it's not too deep just here. Everything is made of stone here, the walls, roof and also the bottom of the lake. Eastwards a tunnel leads on into the dark.
12547:
A long slender eel glides along the water, its body coiled to strike.
A long slender eel glides along the water, its body coiled to strike.

The lake is filled with dark, deep and ice cold water here. It is extremely dark here, and the distance between the water and the roof is not much at all. The distance is just enough for a person to catch his breath without knocking his head against the roof. Water drips from the roof into the lake, and the walls are damp and slimy.
