12548: The lake bends north and west from here. To the north the lake becomes shallow and seems to end up in a tunnel leading north. Eastwards the lake becomes deeper and the distance between the roof and the water is very short. Water drips from the roof, and the walls are damp and slimy. A cold draft blows here, which makes the water ice cold.
12549: On this small plateau, a few feet above the water, the ground is cold but dry. The water below seems dark and cold, but rather shallow as it continues southwards from here. Damp, cold walls and a roof made of stone fill this place with darkness. There are some cracks in the walls, but still the smoothness of them indicate that it was people who made this place rather than wild animals or the passage of water. The tunnel continues northwards into the darkness.
12550: The tunnel comes to an end here. This place seems to be rather dry, and some dirt can be seen on the ground. It's very dark here and the distance between the roof and the floor is not even high enough for a normal human to stand up properly. The tunnel slopes downwards to the south, and the sound of water can be heard in the distance.
12551: The walls are dry here as well as the floor. A damp and rotting smell fills the air and a few drops of water are dripping from the roof. Some marks and cracks can be seen on the southern and eastern walls. On the eastern wall there is a large slit that a person, with some effort, could possibly squeeze out through.
12552:
A stone sarcophagus lies on the floor.
A guardian stone beast is here, protecting the grave.
A guardian stone beast is here, protecting the grave.

This room appears to be abandoned. All the furniture is made of rotting wood, and a damp fleshy smell fills the air. The dark tomb, with its floor and walls covered in dirt looks like it was abandoned years ago. The smooth walls and the furniture indicates that this place was made by cunning people. On the northern wall there is a door made of stone, covered with spiderwebs.
12553: Here the vegetation seems to shift a bit. The pines that grow around to the north and west have almost gone completely. As far south as you can see the grassy plains are the only thing visible. West of here the plains also continue while north of here you can see a field of some kind.
12554: The thick, soft grass which grows here makes travel very difficult. In many places the grass has grown to several feet in height. An occasional pine tree can be seen sprouting from the ground. The plains continue in every direction.
12555: The outlines of a faint path are marked with small weathered stones. The path is easy to follow despite the weeds and small bushes covering it as the trail travels in a fairly straight line towards the north and south. Large plains span out from the trail to the east and west.
12556: Small weathered stones mark the faint outlines of a path. Small bushes and weeds grow throughout the area, making the path of the trail difficult to follow. The trail continues to both the north and south. Barren plains span outwards towards both the east and west.
12557: Thick underbrush has been planted on both sides of the path, making the trail easily visible. The trail begins to decay some as it heads towards the north as the underbrush recedes. A small hill rises above the plains to the west. The trail continues onwards to the east in the direction of some ruined buildings.
12558: A simple wooden chest is here.

This old shelter sure has seen better times. The walls have fallen in and all the woodwork has rotted away. Only the northern wall seems to still be going strong. Here someone has cleared away the rubble, and the remains of a campfire can be seen. Left in the corner is some dry wood covered with a brown looking fur. From here you can go west. Obviously hidden with great haste, you can also see an old chest among the stone rubble.
12559: A swarm of midges is here, humming around you.

The plains rise towards a tiny hill, covered in lush, green grass. Clusters of flowers and brushwood dot the landscape. A ring of small stones once used for a fire pit can be spied to the south. The plains continue onwards towards the north and west. The outline of a faint path is to the east.
12560: Many grasses, weeds, and flowers grow in the fertile earth. A few young pine trees and an occasional bush also dot the landscape. The land begins to slope downward towards a ruined field to the north. Water marks in the ground seem to indicate that excess water from these fields have drained to the ruined field below. The land continues to rise gradually towards a tiny hill to the south. The grassy fields stretch out to the west. The faint outline of an old path lies to the east.
12561: The fields in this area are submerged under a thin layer of water, making it very difficult for most types of vegetation to grow. Only a few brown weeds and gray reeds can be seen above the water line. The lands to the west and south begin to slope upwards towards drier ground. A seldom used path can be spied to the east, leading away from the fields. An old road passes by to the north, muddy from excess water from the fields draining on to it.
12562: The faint outlines of an overgrown path can be seen here leading to the south. Old weathered stones serve as markers for the path. An old elven road passes by to the north and west. To the east is a grass covered plain. An occasional bird can be seen flying overhead.
12563: Thick grass muffles the sounds of the area, making the place very silent. Only some occasional rocks and thickets break up the rolling landscape of the plains. A road can be spied to the north, but otherwise the plains seem to spread out in all directions.
12564: The green ocean of grass that engulfs the area is only broken up by occasional dense thickets of thornbushes and several pine trees. The plains continue on in all directions except for to the west, where the faint outline of an old path can be spied.
12565: A bright green holly bush is growing here.

You are in a large field, which is covered with grass and flowers. It is more or less completely flat while the land seems to rise a bit to the north. East of here the flat plains-like area continues and also west of here. South of here lie some plains while to the north the fields seem to continue.
12566: Besides some fields west of here, nothing can be seen in any direction except plains. Tall grass, reaching up to a mans lower stomach, covers the area and makes it hard to look in any direction. This area must be the perfect hiding place for animals shy of people, and provide enough food for them with all the small animals living on these plains.
12567: This seems to be the middle of the plains. It seems like there is nothing else but tall, thick grass as far as the eye can see. It's hard to move around in this grass, partly due to the fact that it is so thick and tall and partly because the ground below is filled with rocks of all sizes. Animals can be heard moving around, but they cannot be seen except for some movements in the grass.
12568: Dark green, tall grass covers the area like a dense carpet. Some noises can be heard as animals are hunting in the long, tall grass and some movements can be seen in the distance. These plains stretch out in every direction but east. To the east a path appears to be leading in between some tall, white cliffs. The cliffs seem old and rugged, being formed by the weather and wind during many decades.
12569: These plains are filled with long, thick grass that can let a man or animal disappear with ease. Only movements in the grass can reveal someone trying to hide. East of here a small path appears in between the tall, thick grass. To the north-east some tall white cliffs rise high above the green grass, while the plains continue south and west from here.
12570: The grass here is long and thick, but still the ground is soft due to short grass growing in between the long grass. The long grass is tall, and would reach up to the middle of a normal sized mans stomach. Sounds can be heard, and movements can be seen as animals move around in the grass. Grassy plains extend in all directions, as far as the eye can see.
12571: Plains stretch out in every direction from here, although to the west the plains are more like fields, with shorter grass and a greater variety of other plants and flowers. In this area the only thing growing is the long grass which is as thick as a finger, and so tall that it steals the sunlight from any other plant trying to live in between the grass
12572:
A bright green holly bush is growing here.
Partly covered by the bush's green leaves, there are some hollyberries.

You are in a large field covered with grass and flowers. Southwards it makes a slight slope, while east and west it remains rather flat. West of here you can see a large plain while east of here the plains-like area continues. South of here the fertile land seems to continue. To the north you can see a dusty plain that borders a road.
12573: Much of the northern area of this field is covered by rubble from the once proud road that runs both north and west of here. Large rocks and rotten wood lie scattered about. South and east of here the large and colourful plains continue. Looking northwards you can see in the distance a tower rising towards the sky.
12574: From here the plains stretch out in all directions except north. To the north a road runs ewst and northwards. Long grass, reaching nearly up to the belly of a normal sized horse, grows here. Not much else is able to grow in the grass which dominates the area. The only exceptions are the small patches of rugged plants and flowers which have forced their way through the grass.
12575: These plains continue in every direction but north. To the north thick bushes and brushwood cover the area. The grass here is thick and long. It's hard to move around in, as it reaches the waist of a man. It's the same type of grass as can be seen all over these plains. Far east in the horizon some cliffs obscure the view, as they rise above the tall grass.
12576: A tall stag is here, grazing peacefully.

Endless plains can be seen westwards from here. Tall, thick grass dominates these plains and makes it impossible to see anything on the ground, or to notice the animals that move around in the grass. North from here a forest covered with young pine trees begins, while eastwards white cliffs glow in the light as they rise above the ground.
12577:
A bright green holly bush is growing here.
Partly covered by the bush's green leaves, there are two piles of hollyberries.
A brown fox is here, looking for some rabbits to chew up.

The area is totally covered with thick bushes with long sharp thorns. Any attempt to move results in an unpleasant and painful experience. Westwards the bushes seem to be extremely dense, and almost impossible to pass. The bushy area continues to the north, while eastwards a forest appears. The forest seems to consist of young pine trees. Beyond the forest to the east some white cliffs appear in the distant horizon.
12580:
A dun-coloured grouse is sitting still in the heather.
A squirrel scampers around here, looking for nuts from the trees.

Young pine trees grow here. They are not as tall and thick as the ones often seen in larger forests. It's possible to see through this forest, as the trees are not too dense. To the north and west small bushes grow as dense as a wall. Their thorns don't look too inviting. East beyond the forest white cliffs rise above the ground, and to the south plains cover the horizon.
12581: A large swampy area inhabits most of this area. Most of the land is covered by thick, soft mud or watery pools. Sprouting from the mud are various brown grasses and tall weeds. The vegetation becomes too thick towards the north, making passage in that direction impossible.
12582: The ground is soft here. It is covered by hard earth with thin, brown grass and high bushes. The bushes grows way over your knees. To the north the bushes become more scarce and you can see a high building far away. To the south and to the east the bushes become too dense and entangled for anyone to force their way through.
12583:
A black pond of water is here.
A large beaver is here, gnawing on a piece of wood.

The bushes in this area have grown together very close. The vegetation becomes extremely thick to the north and west, making travel in those directions quite impossible. The ground is very soft and wet, often ankle deep mud in places. Brackish water collects in pools, attracting many flying insects.
12584: This area is dominated by muddy soil covered in thick brown grass. The ground is very unstable, making travel difficult. An old road can be spied rising above the land to the east. The grasses merge with dense bushes as the plains continue to the south and west. Far off in the distance to the north is the river Glanduin. A tower overlooks the surrounding area to the north east.
12585: A black pond is here, filled with putrid water.

The ground is soft and wet, with occasionally pools of murky water. There are many bushes growing in the area. Many are harmless, but some have sharp leaves or thorns that could slash unprotected skin. The bushes continue on towards the west, but begin to fade towards the north and east. Passage to the south becomes difficult as the vegetation becomes even thicker in that direction, making travel hard at best.
12586: A black pond of water is here.

While an occasional scraggly bush pushes itself out of the tough soil, most of the ground is covered with pools of stagnant, muddy water. The pools gradually merge to the north into a wide river. The pools continue on to the west, but the ground becomes somewhat firmer to the south. Dense bushes hamper travels to the east.
12587:
A small leech is here, floating in the water.
A small leech is here, floating in the water.
A snake slithers towards you.

The vegetation is very scarce here. Tufts of hard, short grass grow out of the river banks. The river continues to flow past to the north. The grounds to the west and southwest slowly turn into a wasteland of bubbling mud, slender reeds, and buzzing insects.
12588: The ground here is quite treacherous, consisting of both hard and soft mud. Sinkholes threaten to capture unwary travellers, making the journey through this region slow and tedious. The ground between these mudholes is overgrown by dense grass and small bushes. The mud and grass continues on to the west. The rustling of the river Glanduin can be heard to the north. The ground hardens to the south, making travelling easier. Some ruins can be spied to the east through the vegetation.
12589: The swamps here are full of murky pools and mudholes. Tall reeds grow out of the ground. The pools begin to increase in size and finally merge into a river to the north. The swamps continue on towards the south and west. A large building is to the east, but cannot be reached from this side.
12590: You have entered a decaying building. It has obviously not been inhabited for a very long time. The wooden parts are mostly gone and there is no sign of furniture. There is a big arch in the east wall, the only thing left of the doors that once were. The floor is made of stones and is littered by broken stone blocks and dirt from the outside which the wind has brought with it. At the west side of the room stands an old staircase made of a dark coloured wood. It once led up to the crumbling tower that rises above you. The staircase is in really bad shape and the top part is missing.
12591: Your steps are very insecure here, but the tower seems more stable than it looked like from below. It is only about twenty feet high, but there are no big obstacles around to obstruct the view. Just north of here the river Glanduin flows from east to west. Further to the east lies a wide lake. On the other bank of the river there is a hill and to the west a swamp stretches as far as you can see. The horizon is flat to the south but far to the east, veiled in mists you more guess than see the outline of a mountain range. This is an ideal place for watching the traffic on the river.
12592: A duck is here, quacking happily.
You see a beautiful natural vale hidden from its surroundings by the sheer sides of the crater that it lies in. Due to frequent flooding of the Glanduin this vale turned into a small lake.
12593:
A great bustard strides over the grass.
A large rabbit looks peacefully at you, ready to dart away.
The vegetation around you becomes denser as you approach the end of the Swanfleet marshes. To the west a path is barely visible, and a small lake is situated to the north.
12594:
A large leech is moving close to you, searching for blood.
A large leech is moving close to you, searching for blood.

The soil is damp here, it seems like it is often flooded by the waters of the Glanduin. The Swanfleet marshes continue to the north and east. To the south is a marshy rise beyond which you can hear the gentle flow of the River Glanduin.
12595:
A heron is stalking the area, looking for fish.
A cute rabbit is here.

Rising above the calm surface of the surrounding water, this small island is covered with thick, green grass. It is evident from the myriad nests and scattered remains that this isolated crest is home for many species of wetland bird.
12596: The thick and dim marsh of the Swanfleet surrounds you on all sides. The soil looks brown, damp and ugly, with little sign of wildlife. To the south the river Glanduin flows on into the west, where it forms a large delta several miles distant.
12597: Much of the open water here is covered with green aquatic plants that hide the murky depths beneath. The wet and soft soil gives under the slightest weight. To the south the waters of the Glanduin flow slowly to the west, where they join the other mighty river, the Hoarwell.
12598: The fields grow green all around, some in better shape than others. The soil is damp, yet not waterlogged as those closer to the river appear to be. The walls of the city of Tharbad lie to the southwest, beyond the wide waters of the Greyflood.
12599: You are in the middle of a wide field, filled with short grass. The soil beneath the grass is fertile and damp, and only just solid enough to give a slight possibility of walking over it. To the south-west the sound of rushing water reaches your ears.
12600:
A rabbit is here eyeing your presence warily.
Klaees (thedon), wielding a great warsword, is standing here.
Drazud (freshmeat), wielding a great warsword, is standing here.

This small bit of grassland is not that damp and moist like most of the area around. The grass continues to the south while the Swanfleet marshes can be seen to the west. The outline of the path is visible in the north.
12601:
Klaees (thedon), wielding a great warsword, is standing here.
Drazud (freshmeat), wielding a great warsword, is standing here.

This part of the marshes looks a bit more peaceful. One can hear the sounds of wildlife here and there, but always in the distance, never close by. The marshes continue to the west and south, and to the east and north the wind roams in the open plains, covered by the green and golden grass.
12602: The ground here is moist and fertile, sprouting many grasses and small flowers. The sounds of marshy fauna reach your ears from the south, but otherwise not a sound of life comes from the marsh in the west.
12603: Stepping away from the path into the dense reeds, your feet sink quickly into the thick mud. Grasping for a handhold, you find only tangled foliage that tears easily from the ground, offering no support. You are overcome by the smell of rotting plant life and stagnant mud.
12604:
A small brown snake is slithering around here.
A brown toad is here, hunting flies.
Stretching out to the horizon in all directions, you can only see these marshes. It looks especially thick and dangerous to the north. The dank smell of decay comes from that direction.
12605:
A large leech is moving close to you, searching for blood.
A large leech is moving close to you, searching for blood.
A duck is here, quacking happily.

Stretching out to the horizon in all directions, you can only see these marshes. For the inexperienced traveller it would be hard not to get lost in here. The smell of rotten vegetation is thick in the air.
12606: A slender plant grows here, with clusters of tiny pink flowers atop its stem.

The odour of marsh gas and rotten vegetation is prominent, and the smell seems to cling to everything. In all directions you can see these mighty marshes, except east where you can barely make out the distinct smell of sweet, fresh air blowing gently towards you.
12607: The course of this ancient thoroughfare is guided by the sheer cliff that arises to the southwest and the river Glanduin. Beyond these majestic waters lie plains of tall grass as far as the eye can see. Looking east, you can see in the distance some ruins which lie on the northern side of the river.
12608: The ancient paving stones beneath your feet are covered with thick, dark moss, fed by the moisture of the nearby river Glanduin. Just to the north of the road lies a steep cliff, covered liberally with cracks that might allow a skilled climber to scale its considerable height.
12609: A steep rocky cliff guides the river Glanduin to the west. This ancient road has been built between the two. Old cracked paving stones indicate that the road was once a major route from east to west. A dark shadow from the cliff above is cast across the road here.
12610: An ancient fungus smothers the boulders.

Moss and fungus grows amongst the ancient paving stones that form this path, cast into shadow by the sheer cliff above. Despite the threatening overhang of this vertical rise, it appears the cliff has stood solid for many years. To the south the Glanduin flows alongside the ancient roadway, beyond which lies vast plains of tall grass.
12611:
A sparrow is flapping around on the ground.
A badger is here, exploring for food.

Green moss covers the ancient flagstones that pave the road beneath your feet, which rumour says once led from Tharbad to the dwarven kingdom of Khazad-dum. The path is in complete disrepair, yet is still used, judging by the recent wear and upturned earth around you. Beside the road to the southeast lie some crumbled ruins.
12612: Some ruined buildings can be seen not far to the south on this ancient road. Its paving stones are cracked and broken, and obviously misused over the years. The river runs to the southwest, and a tall cliff makes travel difficult to the north or east.
12613: Crumbling walls and fallen roofing are all that is left of this once fair village on the edge of the Glanduin. The stonework looks distinctly dwarven, although most of it has crumbled past recognition over the many years. A small path leads to the quay that juts out into the river just to the south of here. One of the ruins right next to the path looks distinctly like an old inn, although it is very hard to tell with the dereliction about you. The ancient road obviously passed through the centre of the village, and over a bridge to the west of here.
12614: Road of the Smiths at the Entrance to a Valley

To the west, a wide flat grassy plain can be seen. The Glanduin runs along the northern edge, where it has cut its way into the rocky hillside over the years. In the east, the river disappears around a bend in a rocky valley. The old road that you stand on follows the edge of the river both east and west.
12615: Although the rocky cliff to the northwest is slightly less steep here, the many bushes and plants covering the slope make it a very dangerous looking climb. Broken flagstones marking an ancient road run north and west, along the banks of the Glanduin. Just to the other side of the Glanduin, a steep rocky side of the valley climbs about fifteen yards, and you can see some woodlands on the top of the cliff.
12616: Following the course of the Glanduin, the road leads north or south. The river flows continually southwards towards its eventual destination, the Greyflood many leagues west of here. This road looks a little overgrown in some parts, especially where its paving stones have become misplaced or damaged over the years. Occasional footprints or horse tracks in the mud indicates some people still use the path.
12617: Shadows from the cliff above cast an eerie feel over this broken road which runs alongside the Glanduin. Although the cliff is not high, the dense bushes growing up the side stop all but the most foolhardy from climbing it. On the other side of the Glanduin, another cliff rises. A rock fall to the east seems to have blocked the road, but a trail can be seen going over the rock fall.
12618: Boulders dot the area between the cliff and the river Glanduin to the south. The cliff face has collapsed some time in the past partially covering the road that leads off to the west. To the east, the road continues up a steep slope.
12619: Jagged Bend in the Road of the Smiths

The road winds along the south and eastern wall of a towering sandstone cliff. To the south, the road leads down along the fertile riverbed. Tiny rocks dislodged from the cliff are strewn all across the old road and pieces of brick have broken away to clutter the surface of this ancient pass.
12620: Between the dense brush to the north and the sandstone cliff to the south, this broken road seems to run on without end. To the east the road descends sharply down towards the bank of the Glanduin. To the west it cuts deep into the walls of the jagged cliff. The bushes to the north seem very thick and almost impassable.
12621: Dense underbrush blocks any way into the forest to the north of here. Not far to the south there is a sheer drop, and from the dull roar coming from that direction a river must run along the base of the cliff. The road looks like it used to bend slightly to the south here, but a rockslide has terminated it abruptly. To the west the road continues to run between the forest and the cliff.
12622: The ancient road continues to cut its way between the cliff to the south and the dark forest to the north. Grass and weeds grow between the broken stones littering the ground where the once well-built road must have run, and animal tracks can be seen imprinted in the earth.
12623: Cutting through the forest, the ancient road is a little overgrown in places. To the south there is a thin band of trees, and the sound of swiftly running water can be heard from just behind them. Some of the animals of the forest chirp eerily, the alien sounds echoing from treetop to treetop. To the north a narrow trail leads off into the forest.
12624: The sound of running water rises from the gorge to the south of the road here, while to the north there lies a dense forest of holly bushes. Many old, broken paving stones indicate that this once major thouroughfare has been neglected for many years.
12625: A badger is here, exploring for food.

Broken stones pave the once great road between Tharbad and Ost-in-Edhil. Many centuries of neglect have made the road difficult to travel, with lots of loose or missing stones. The Glanduin follows the line of the road.
12626: The cracked and broken road follows the banks of the Glanduin. The many paving stones that lie about indicate that this was once a very major route, but it has obviously fallen into a state of disrepair.
12627: The road winds on to the east and the west following the northern bank of the River Glanduin. The paving stones are cracked and damaged now, but the road was once wide enough for two carts to pass side by side with plenty of room for pedestrians too.
12628: The ancient road bends from west to the south here, following the line of the Glanduin river. The lands to the east and north appear to have been partitioned off into fields and farm animals dwell therein.
12629: The road continues to wind its way through the countryside, but parts briefly from the river here as it turns to the east. A copse of trees forms a buffer between the river and the road to the south while the river itself continues its path to the west.
12630: A hungry warg (Rood) is standing here, ridden by you.

Small stone dykes border the road to the east and north here. Beyond these walls lie farmlands occupied by farm animals. The road continues to the west and south while some trees lie to the south-west.
12631: Klaees (thedon), wielding a great warsword, is standing here.

The ancient road travels steadily onwards to the north and east, tufts of grass growing between the cracked stones. To the west, a thin copse of trees can be entered which appears to lead to a ford over the river to the south-west. The river to the south appears much to deep to be forded, but its bed seems to widen towards the west.
12632:
A large rabbit looks peacefully at you, ready to dart away.
Klaees (thedon), wielding a great warsword, is standing here.

Twisting around the southerly bend quickly, the river drives ahead to the west. Even from here, some kind of structures are evident there. They seem to be very old, but there is little else that can be detected. A rough track of flattened earth rises to the north.
12633: An ancient road follows the river to the east and west. A short stretch of grass separates the road from the river, and a recently repaired dry stone wall to the north stops animals straying from the fields onto the road. A reasonably new looking wooden gate allows access to the fields without having to climb over the wall, and even the road here looks in reasonable repair.
12634: A big cliff begins here. The road follows its top to the east, and to the west, it continues along the bank of the Estelin River. To the north there is a small field, which seems to be abandoned and some tents can be seen at the edge of a small copse.
12635: The road runs from the east to the west on the top of a sharp cliff. The sight towards the south is expansive and you can see the whole Estelin Valley. To the north, after some fields there is a small copse, and at its edge there are some tents. You spot a small path leading down to a landing near the water.
12636: The road is on the top of a high cliff. There is a small path that goes north, towards the edge of a small forest, and to the east a very old bridge stands between the two sides of a deep gorge. The bridge is very old and seems to be a bit dangerous, especially if you try to travel across it with a mount.
12637: This bridge is extremely old, and has been partially destroyed both by the rigours of time, and by the deleterious ways of the armies of Sauron. The first part of the bridge, near to this side of the gorge, seems still to be solid, but further across it appears that it may be less able to support much weight.
12638: This is the main entrance gate to the once magnificent elven city called Ost-in-Edhil. Most of the city is in ruins now after a fierce battle and many years of decay. The Hollin Road itself continues to the west and to the north of here. It is pretty silent up here on this big cliff that the fallen city rests on except for some birds here and there, and the rivers that are joining below you. The Sirannon joins the Glanduin, who just a bit further away gets even more strengthend by the Sir Lantalaith. They all join their forces and continue their flow westwards.
12639: The roads bends here. It runs to the south where it enter a big crumbled city. West and north, there is a deep gorge from where the noise of flowing waters can be heard. The road seems to continue for forever towards the east, and some strange building can be seen on the other side of the gorge, to the west.
12640: The road runs east-west here at the top of sharp cliff. The vacuum opens just south of here and one can hear the slow flow of a large river. South-west of here there are the ruins of a big city, and north of here, a small strange decaying building blocks any movement in that direction.
12641: The road leads westward to a big, old city; eastwards, one can not see its end. South of here there is a deep precipice in which a slow river flows North of here there are plenty of old fields, now no more cultivated. A strange building is north-west of here and far in the north-east one can see a small black hill.
12642: On the top of a high cliff, the Hollin Road leads east-west. From here, there is a wonderful sight on all the south bank of the Sirannon, and the remains of a small dunlending village which seems to have been burnt down recently can be seen there. West of here, there is a big city, and far to the north one can see a small black hill.
12643: The cliff is now too high to let someone go to the south, towards the Sirannon River. The road leads east-west on the top of this cliff and far in the west a big city appears in the mist. North of the road there is some field, and the plain that lies in the south is inaccessible from here.
12644: Von (twitter), wielding an ornate, steel-shafted warhammer, is standing here.

The track follows the riverbed of the Sirannon. Many tracks leading up and down the track can be seen. The mountains to the east, with their eternal snows, are rising up. Just south of here the cold Sirannon flows westwards.
12645: This broad track, which is now known as the Hollin Road, continues to the west and east, forming a natural border between the northern wetlands and the river Sirannon to the south. While travel through the wetlands, to the north, is possible, not only does the soft land make it cumbersome, the faint baying of nearby wolf-packs makes it less than inviting.
12646: This rough road, which was onced used by the Elves of Eregion and the Dwarves of Moria in their travels from Ost-in-Edhil to Moria still runs alongside the river of Sirannon. While old and decayed, the road is still the quickest path for traveling across the harsh countryside. From here, the road continues to the south and east. In the west there are some fields, damp with moisture, and covered by yellowing vegetation.
12647: The track continues east and west across the sparse wetlands. To the south and east the mighty river Sirannon borders the track. Even from here, the water which forms the river Sirannon looks clear and refreshing. Small animals can be seen taking advantage of the river, some to wash their food, others to quench their thirst and still more to take a relaxing swim.
12648: The flow of the mighty river Sirannon, which is to the immediate south, can be heard along this decaying road. Further to the east the track bends slightly to the north, but to the west it continues in a straight line. To the south, down the steep bank and across the river, a small stone building of some sort can be seen and to the north a small pond blocks movement in that direction.
12649: The road continues to the west and northeast of here. To the south you can see an area of flat riverbank where, at one time, the mighty river Sirannon must have overflowed causing the banks to erode to the extent that the river has become wide and shallow, making crossing easy, though somewhat tedious. To the far north an area of burnt ground can be seen. A strange smell comes from that direction.
12650: The Hollin road, a wide well-trodden track, leads across the wetland from the southeast to the northwest. Farther to the south flows the clear water of the river Sirannon as it passes through a narrow ravine. On the other bank, some sort of stone building has been erected. It would have been difficult to cross the river here, but since numerous stepping stones has been placed across the ravine, it is no problem.
12651: In this region the decaying road is quite stony as it continues to the north and west. The moorland can be seen bordering the road to the north and, again, further to the south beyond the nearby river. While at one time the river was quite high, right now there is only an average flow of water.
12652: The road bends to the south and east of here as the road winds its way through the bleak wetland that extends far to the north and west. Even further to the southeast, across the far bank of the riverbed, you see patches of the misty land enveloped in some low-lying mist.
12653: A bend in the track leads to the north and west of here, carrying you across the bleak moorland and its cold, damp atmosphere. The riverbed to the south runs parallel to the track, seeming to hug it at every bend and corner, and once sent a mighty spray onto unwary travelers when it was full which is no longer the case.
12654: The Hollin moor lies to the north and east of this rough stony road which seems to continue forever towards the south-west and north-east. To the far east the peaks of the Misty mountains are visible, and nearer, just across the river to the south, a small building can be seen.
12655: Grassy Plains at the Cliff Top
Some small rocks have been piled into a mound here.

Balanced precariously near the edge of the cliff is a huge boulder. The only purpose for the rock must be to block the valley where the Glanduin flows to the south of here. However, it would take an incredibly strong force to move it. From the look of the vegetation that grows up to its base, it has stood in the same spot for many years. Westwards, beyond the cliff edge, only grassy plains and small hills can be seen.
12656: Prickly, white-stemmed plants, with blue flower heads grow in abundance.

The ground can be seen through the tall dry grass, where small animals can be seen moving about. The plateau begins a descent into a valley to the north and west. However, the plateau extends far to the east bordered by the valley along the southern edge.
12657: A sheer cliff drops down about fifteen yards into the valley to the south where the river Glanduin flows. To the southwest, grassy plains slope gently up towards the horizon. A ruined village of some kind can be seen just to the south of here, bordering the steady waters of the river. A grassy plateau extends northwards.
12658: The grassy plains extend from far in the north to a point immediately to the south of here, where there is a steep drop to the river valley below. Over the edge of the bluff, several buildings can be seen lying next to the Glanduin. A finger of land juts out into the valley to the east.
12659:
A large, loyal falcon is circling above.
A fallow deer is grazing peacefully here.
A fallow deer is grazing peacefully here.

An astounding view greets the eye from this high point, high above the river Glanduin. The river can be seen flowing through a narrow canyon to the north- east, around the base of this rocky spur and following the cliff edge to the northwest. Alongside the river there appears to be an old paved trail. Grassy plains cover the ground between the Glanduin and the horizon.
12660: You are on a poorly paved pathway which follows the base of a sheer, formidable cliff. The handholds which you are forced to rely upon are of questionable reliability, and the likelihood of a fall is high. Not far above your head lies a grassy patch of soil, marking the crest of this path.
12661: The ground is covered with a fine soot. Small fingers of grass have begun to find their way back to the surface. Several mounds can be seen breaking up the otherwise monotonously flat surface of the plateau. The burned ground continues to the north and east. A finger of land juts out into the valley to the south.
12662: The tall grass completely covers the ground. Occasionally, movements by small animals catch your attention. To the south and west the land continues on, but disappears before it meets the horizon. The plateau also continues to the north, where a few trees can be seen. The land to the east appears to be completely covered in black.
12663: The grass thins out here and you can finally see the ground. To the east a large dark area can be seen. The grassy plateau continues to the south and west. To the north several trees can be distinguished from the rest of the horizon.
12664: Northern Slope of a Grassy Hill

There is a huge, pyramidal beehive here.
A bee flies around here, collecting nectar from the flowers.
A bee flies around here, collecting nectar from the flowers.
A drone bee flies around here, angrily buzzing.
A drone bee flies around here, angrily buzzing.

Green grasses grow all over the northern side of this hill. The numerous rabbit droppings indicate that this is a favourite site for the local rabbit population. At the top of the hill, a black stone monolith can be seen. To the north the ground drops off suddenly into a gorge, while to the west a promontory extends over the gorge, carrying an ancient temple.
12665: A giant, mean looking earth beetle is standing here.

Young saplings grow profusely in the shelter of the hill to the west and the impenetrable forest stands as a border to the north. The strange lack of older trees is very disturbing, it is as if no trees had ever grown here until recently. To the east are the older trees towering together in a choked mass.
12666: A robin is here, carrying small pieces of wood to its nest.

A forest of massive twisted trees shrouds the earth with a canopy of black branches. This old forest keeps its world in darkness and forces the plants below to starve for the warmth of the sun. The silence is uneasily broken by the sound of the wind swaying through ponderous branches. The forest is impenetrable to the north but thins out to the west. To the east the forest becomes sick and unhealthy. From the south can be smelled the scent of dry grass and the Eregion plains.
12667: The verdant forest becomes sick and withered here. A stand of dead trees jut from the marshy ground like wooden claws reaching from the earth in fury. The ground is almost entirely made up of black mud with hard little rocks peeking out. Very sparse grass grows here and bloodsucking insects fly through the air, hovering over scattered puddles of grimy water. A huge black forest grows to the west, while the forest to the east looks healthier. A broad plateau stretches out to the south. Dense clumps of broken trees and rotten vegetation prevent movement northward.
12668: Trees grow all around you in this leafy forest. Many small patches of the sky can be seen through the leafy canopy above. Some unusually dark green plants grow under the protection of the trees, and many small forest creatures can be heard making noises in the undergrowth all around.
12669: A tree-snake lies wrapped around one of the tree branches.

A large smelly lake breaks the continuity of the forest here. All around the trees grow up to the lakes edge. Rushes and other water plants grow on the surface, and many insects buzz all over the wide expanse of water. It is far too murky to see what grows within the lake. A trail in the forest leads off to the east.
12670: A woodpecker is here, tapping on a tree.

Bushes grow thickly between the dense coverage of leafy branches above you. The high trees seem to dwarf every living thing, and the thick canopy of leaves blocks out virtually all the sky. Strange insects can be heard making weird chirping noises in the undergrowth. From their height and the girth of their trunks, it looks as if the trees have stood here for centuries.
12671: Trees tower high above you and their dense foliage blocks out most of the light entering this part of the forest. Small bushes cover the ground, and they thicken to the south. The forest is very dry however, and the slightly decomposing leaves and twigs on the ground may make a comfortable bed.
12672:
A fallow deer is grazing peacefully here.
A fallow deer is grazing peacefully here.

Blades of grass can be seen growing up out of the black soot, seemingly left behind by a recent fire which seems to have burned off the grass from the top of the plateau. The area scarred by the fire continues to the south and west. The plains on top of the plateau continue to the east. The way north is tangled with sickly trees.
12673: The charred corpse of a tree, struck by lightning, marks the northwestern edge of large burned out area of the plateau. The fire travelled far to the south and east. Young blades of grass can be seen just starting to poke their way through the surface. To the north is an ancient black forest.
12674: The ground is covered with black soot through which some young grass can be seen poking its way back to the surface. The fire stops at the edge of the cliffs which abruptly drop off to the south and east. The fire has revealed several mounds that the tall grass would have hidden. The burned out area stretches far to the north and east. A road can be seen running alongside the river in the valley below.
12675: Dense holly bushes grow all about, even overhead. They block out all the light of day. The occasional tree competes with the holly for space to grow. The twigs and leaves that cover the ground make it seem very spongy and soft. To the west there is an occasional glimpse, as of light reflecting on a body of water, while to the east the trail continues.
12676: The holly trees surround you almost completely, but yet you can still find a route through them. The trees have nearly driven all other life away, but still some other plants cling on tenaciously. Small animals scurry past, out of sight but not out of earshot. The branches above you interweave to form an impenetrable cloak from the light above and beyond making the forest a place of shadow and darkness.
12677: A large rabbit looks peacefully at you, ready to dart away.

The trail comes to an end here. The bushes and trees simply do not allow any progress to the north. The trail is visible for a way to the south, but its route is hardly visible as it wends its way around and under trees. Above you, the dense boughs of the trees and bushes block out all light, making the forest extremely dark. Although the trail ends here, you can still push your way to the east or west if you wish.
12678: A fallen log partly blocks the trail here, but it can be bypassed without much trouble. All around, the dead tree's old siblings rise tall and strong. The forest is thick and healthy, and there is nothing to suggest even that it was ever not so. The trail runs north and south, as straight as an elven spear.
12679: A mass of wriggling vines drops on you from the trees.

The trees are dense here but seem to thin out to the south and east. The sky cannot be seen from here, blocked from view by the tree crowns above. To the west, the trees form an impenetrable barrier and the branches resist all attempts at cutting a way through. To the east, the trees thin and grassy fields can be seen beyond the boundary of the forest. To the south, a road seems to travel east to west once you leave the forest.
12680: A large rabbit looks peacefully at you, ready to dart away.

Holly trees pervade the nearby area having banished most other plants long ago. The boughs far above block the sky from your view and prevent all light from entering the forest from above. The density of the trees blocks any possibility of travelling to your north or east, forcing you to move south or west.
12681: A badger is here, exploring for food.

The grassy field grows right up to the edge of a dense holly forest. Some kind of animal has grazed here recently, maybe cows or sheep. The occasional dry stone wall breaks the monotony of the plains to the east. To the south an ancient road follows the line of the River Glanduin.
12682: Dry stone walls cover this part of a vast grassy plain that stretches as far as the eye can see to the north and east. The walls segregate the plain into lots of smaller areas. Some kind of animal has been kept in these fields, maybe sheep or cows.
12683: A dark holly forest grows vigorously to the west. However it seems to be kept in place by some stone walls, and this area seems to be used to graze sheep or similar kinds of animals. To the east the land rises gently. A few leagues south a large river crosses the plains.
12684: Grasslands stretch out in all directions. Towards the south, the grass seems to have been laid out in fields with small stone dykes partitioning off the land. To the immediate south, a small building can be seen.
12685: The grass underfoot makes for easy travel in this area. The grass grows wild here and there appears to be little sign of any large animals. The grass continues for some distance to the south, seemingly partitioned by stone dykes.
12686: A peaceful farmer is here, whistling merrily.

This small building has been placed on a small hillock, seemingly to give a view of the surrounding countryside. It is a simple building and has only minimal cover against the elements. A small hearth has been built against one wall with a basic chimney to allow smoke to escape. A small pile of logs lies next to it along with flint, steel and some tinder.
12687: A peaceful farmer is here, whistling merrily.

Sheep and goats must have been in this field quite recently, from the look of the droppings on the ground. Short cropped grass grows all over the ground, except for some muddy tracks which appear to have been made by the sheep.
12688: Moss covered stone walls segregate this great plain into many smaller fields. The plain rises slightly to the northeast, and a forest covers it to the north- west. Just to the south is an ancient road, beyond which is a fast flowing river and then yet more plains.
12689: Above your head is a sparse covering of leaves, through which the sky can be seen in several places. The leaves rustle as the wind blows through them. The sparse undergrowth here has many small animal trails which zigzag all over the place. Many small creatures must use these paths regularly. A river flows westwards just to the north and east of here.
12690:
A dirty bandit waits here looking for an easy mark.
A dirty bandit waits here looking for an easy mark.
A sturdy bandit bodyguard stands here, eager to hack you to pieces.

This tower appears odd and unconventional from the first glance. It has a noticeably sloping floor, and the stark, stone blocks that make up the walls seem to have been defiled by crude drawings, particularly of elves being tortured and killed. The lack of finesse in these primordial inscriptions seems to indicate that they were produced by some dark foul beast of Morgoth, who may have manned this tower long ago. This perch affords an excellent view of the surrounding country-side.
12691: Dangling from the top of the cliff to the northeast, high above your head, are thick, stringy roots. Below the sheer vertical rise, the river continues on towards the northwest. The stone looks very unstable, and there are numerous chunks of rock near the edge of the river that must have fallen from the cliff.
12692: Running alongside a sheer cliff, the mighty Glanduin continues towards the northwest in its relentless journey to join the Greyflood in distant lands. A trail follows the northern bank of the river, sandwiched between the broad waters and the vertical rock face. Tall grass covers the fields which lead up to the southern bank of the river.
12693: The river becomes very wide and shallow at this point, making it an ideal place to cross to the other side. At its deepest, the river comes to about a depth of waist height. To the south and west, grassy plains cover all of the land, and a high cliff runs from the south to the northwest, with the river emerging from a steep valley just to the east of here.
12694:
A badger is here, exploring for food.
A goat is here, grazing in the hills.

A sandy beach runs along the inner edge of this bend in the river Glanduin. The dark, dirty looking sand turns into grassy dunes and then a grassy plain to the south. The Glanduin flows ever westward bordering the rather uncomfortable, hard beach to the north and the east. Many small plants and shrubs have found a place to grow in the sand, but their growth has obviously been hindered by the infertile soil.
12695: Small rocks and pebbles cover this steep hillside, which becomes flatter to the south. To the northeast a steep cliff seems to sprout from this rise, and to the south vast, grassy plains extend as far as the eye can see. A strange tower has been erected to the centre of the plains in the northwest.
12696: Verdant, green grass covers this hillside, which offers an excellent view of the vast plains to the west and the broad river Glanduin to the north, beyond which lies a steep, rocky slope.
12697: You stand amidst a dense patch of thorny bushes, which tear mercilessly at your skin. Just to the east lies a grassy hillside, which becomes quite steep to the northeast, until melding into a sheer cliff face. To the west the air seems to take on a sickly, brownish hue, accompanied by a disgusting stench.
12698: A black pond of water is here.

Foul fumes permeate the air around these dark looking waters, which seem to release a visibly brown gas. The foliage and grass surrounding this area seems to have taken on this repulsive colour and stench. The occasional bubble of some strange slimy substance breaks the surface of the pond.
12699:
A badger is here, exploring for food.
A brown fox is here, looking for some rabbits to chew up.

Several varieties of grass sprout from the earth here, increasing in height and colour as the sloping plain approaches a river to the northeast. In all other directions the rolling grasslands continue as far as the eye can see.
12700:
A dense carpet of blue flowers dip their heads in the breeze.
A squirrel scampers around here, looking for nuts from the trees.

The dense earth beneath your feet supports only a short, dense type of grass. Your view to the north is blocked by a copse of trees, beyond which you can make out the sound of briskly flowing water. A simple, stone tower rises from the bleak plains to the northeast.
12701: To the south and west of you lie vast plains of tall, thick grass. This ocean of green also extends to the east, beyond which you hear the faint sound of running water. Far away to the east you can barely make out the outline of some kind of tower.
12702: A sturdy pack horse is standing here.

A strange, ugly looking watchtower stands on a small rise in this part of the grassy plains. The way it leans slightly eastwards seems to indicate that the stone construction was hastily erected and it is surprising that the tower is still standing. At the base of the tower are wide arches, allowing you to see the marsh on the other side of the tower quite easily. A stone stairway leads upwards into the belly of the stone beast.
12703: Yellow flowers, with grey-green foliage, grow in clusters here.

The ground in this natural dip in the plains is very soft and boggy, and only seems to increase in moisture content as it approaches the river. One of the few pathways that traverses these wet fields splits here, with spurs going west south and east. To the west and south the earth seems to dry out slightly.
12704: A badger is here, exploring for food.

Sharp thistles and thorny bushes cover the rocky, dense earth beneath your feet. To the east lies a steep hillside which leads up to an unscaleable vertical rise, and to the north lies a swiftly flowing river.
12705: A squirrel scampers around here, looking for nuts from the trees.

Tall grasses cover this side of the hill. The peak is just to the south of here, although it is not a lot higher than this slope. To the west the slope gets steeper and there seems to be a way down onto the plains. To the east some trees grow. Just to the north of here there is a cliff edge.
12706: A great view of the countryside can be seen in all directions. To the north there is some kind of steep valley or causeway separating this hillside from the slightly higher one beyond. To the east there is a woods. To the west a vast grassy plain stretches as far as the eye can see. The river Glanduin crosses the plain, presumably it flows along the causeway to the north.
12707:
A large sturgeon swims slowly along the bottom.
A large sturgeon swims slowly along the bottom.

Water from the river Glanduin to the north has flooded into an oval pond cut into the stone of this hill. Slow eddies drive suds in circular patterns across this pool's surface. Just below the foam some large fish are swimming about an old wooden palette searching for a meal. To the north you see some very old quays. The cliff rises up very steeply to the south preventing movement.
12708: Some ruined stone quays jut out into the river as it flows slowly westwards. Many years of neglect have taken their toll on the old docks that once served the ruined village on the river bank. The stone is now cracked and crumbling, which makes the quays look very dangerous to use. Westward the grassy plains roll as far as the eye can see. The Glanduin is guided along to the west by a thirty-foot-high rocky cliff at its southern bank.
12709: Lichen and the occasional small plant clings to the rocky cliff that guides the Glanduin on its trek westward. Although the cliff is not particularly high, it looks virtually unclimbable. A road follows the river at the base of the cliff, and some wide plains can be seen to the southwest.
12710: The river bends from the southeast to the west here. An ancient paved road runs along the base of a cliff just to the north, and some ruins can be seen along the road to the east. The river seems to widen out to the west.
12711: Wispy looking grass sprouts from the ground here, dotted by the occasional odd-looking bush. Directly to the northeast, a large river emerges from a rocky valley, bordered by a sheer cliff, and turns to run along the northern edge of the plain. A small trail seems to follow the river.
12712: Short Grass at the Base of a Cliff
A squirrel scampers around here, looking for nuts from the trees.

Short, stiff grasses cover this plain that slopes down from a rocky cliff towards the Glanduin just north of here. There is a road following the opposite bank of the river, and just beyond that the cliff continues. To the south there is an impassable gorge. Occasional bushes and shrubs grow among the grasses.
12713: A bright green holly bush is growing here.

Tall straight trees grow all about this part of the hillside. The foliage is not too heavy and grasses grow between the trees. The hillside slopes down to the northeast where the woods seem to get thicker. To the north there is a gorge, but thick holly bushes block the way to the northeast along the edge of the gorge.
12714:
A bright green holly bush is growing here.
A cute rabbit is here.
A squirrel scampers around here, looking for nuts from the trees.

Tall, leafy trees cover this east facing slope. To the east, at the bottom of the slope, the trees and undergrowth are extremely dense. Only a very small animal could penetrate the tangled brush. The top of the slope is bare of trees but has sparse bits of plains grass growing upon it.
12715:
A grizzly bear is sleeping here.
A grizzly bear is sleeping here.

Some animal has excavated a round burrow within the densely packed brush here. Sharp thorns and a twisty narrow tunnel leading from the brush to the north make this refuge defendable against most intruders.
12716: Thick brush grows densely in this secluded valley. The valley walls slope up to the north and far to the south. A maze of packed brush makes travel difficult to the south. Holly grows profusely in this valley, especially to the east where the bushes get thick and almost impenetrable.
12717: Towering canyon walls block every direction except to the west. The high walls keep this canyon very dark and some shade can be found at any time during the day. A few scrub bushes grow in the rocky ground and a small trickle of water from the top of the canyon suggests at how it was carved. At the base of the canyon to the west you see a frothy pool.
12718: Creeping forever westwards, the Glanduin flows from the east to the west here. The river is quite wide and flows quite slowly towards some derelict quays just visible to the west. The river emerges from the canyon and crosses some wide grassy plains just beyond the quays. Upriver, the valley twists a little to the north. To the south the high valley walls rise high above the river.
12719: The river flows steadily to the west alongside a trail at the bottom of a narrow valley. The steep rocky walls of the valley must have been carved by the river over thousands of years. The occasional bush or plant can be seen clinging to the rocks, as well as many mosses. A few small trickles of water can be seen cascading down from the heights above.
12720: Bending slightly from the north to the west, the Glanduin flows forever westwards towards the sea. The sides of the rocky valley rise at least fifteen yards on either side, allowing just enough room for the road and river on the floor of the canyon. To the south and east the slope of the canyon is covered with brush and loose stones that forbid passage.
12721: A grey snake slides along the water.

Flowing steadily along the base of a rocky cliff, the Glanduin heads slowly towards the Greyflood far west of here. The cliff guides the course of the river from the north and a few leagues south of here, the canyon once again bends westwards. A black patch half way up the cliff side suggests that there may be a cave extending into the cliff face.
12722: A small muddy beach borders the east side of the Glanduin. It seems the river has dug its way through the hills over the years, leaving a flat bottomed valley with steep rocky sides. The Glanduin flows from the east to the south here. There appears to be some kind of road to the west of the river, however as it follows the bend in the waterway, it gets progressively harder to see.
12723: Widening a little, the river flows from north to west. There is a steep rocky cliff on the southern side, and some small waterfalls cascade down parts of this cliff into the river. A dark patch deep in the river at the base of the cliff seems to warrant investigation. On the northern side is a sandy beach with rocky cliffs beyond it. None of the cliffs that you can see from here are particularly high, they do, however, all look very difficult to climb.
12724: A grey snake slides along the water.

Steep rocky walls rise on either side of this natural causeway in which the river Glanduin flows. The top of the cliffs are not far up but the moss and lichen growing on the slippery surface of the rocks make the climb look very dangerous indeed. The river flows ever onwards along the causeway.
12725: The River Glanduin flows swiftly and eternally to the west, passing between towering clifftops to the north and south. Many small plants and the occasional straggling holly bush can be seen growing on the sides of the cliffs, but there is no suitable landing place here, and the only way to go is to follow the course of the river.
12726: The way guides the river westwards. The steep rocky sides, covered in plant life, block movement to the north or the south. To the east, the causeway seems to become far shallower.
12727: Following a narrow causeway to the west, the river Glanduin flows tirelessly onwards. The rocky wall to the south looks just about climbable, although there is no way to tell what is at the top of the cliff. On the clifftop to the north there seems to be the beginnings of a forest, but there is no way up the cliff at this point.
12728: The river bends a little from the south to the west as it travels through a rocky gorge. Although the river has descended below the level of the road already, it should still be possible to scramble up the northern rockface to reach the ancient path.
12729: Swiftly, the river Glanduin bends to the north to avoid a steep rise in the land to the west. The river has eroded its own gorge over the years to pass this shallow ridge. To the northeast a road follows the river, beyond it lies a grassy plain.
12730: The river is a little bit wider here than it is either to the east or the west, causing it to flow westwards at a slower pace than the rest of the waterway. A road to the north follows the river both ways. A sheer cliff-face to the south prevents you from travelling in that direction, its smooth walls offering no purchase for a climber.
12731: The cool water of the Glanduin washes up on the sandy river shore. Waterlogged debris has been thrown aside by the river, and mingles with smooth pebbles and dark soil. Startlingly green grass sprouts from the fringe. Just beyond the grass on the north and east bank lie the remains of an ancient road. To the south-west, the river has cut away at a sheer slope which defies climbing.
12732: *a Man*, wielding an orkish shortbow, is standing here.

Rocky protrusions break through the grasses that grow on this hilltop, making travelling somewhat awkward at times. However, this hillside looks far easier to traverse than some of those further to the west. A road can be seen not far to the north, but a steep gorge separates these hills from the road. A dull roaring sound can be heard from within the gorge.
12733: The west bank of the river is very steep and smooth, defying any attempts at climbing the steep walls. The river begins to travel faster here as it winds its way through the countryside. You can leave the river to the east where a small copse of trees can be seen.
12734: The bottom here is too deep to see, but it doesn't help that the water is dark and cold. Grasses grow all about the river, although far to the south on the horizon there is a dark line, maybe a forest of some kind. Just to the north- east a thick copse of trees grows.
12735: The waterway is broad and swift, but not overpoweringly so. The cool river flows continually west, leading from its origins in the Misty Mountains. Thick and healthy foliage hangs down from the scrublands to the south and the river bank gently slopes up to the road just to the north.
12736: The Glanduin continues its swift path through the lands, flanked as ever by the ancient road to the north. Beyond the road lies grassland with several low stone dykes marking off fields. The south bank is made up of grasslands with holly bushes growing at various intervals on the scrub.
12737: The sinuous river flows around some boulders here. But on closer examination, the rocks seem to be cylindrical and possibly made of marble. The Glanduin's course is unaffected by these boulders as it flows to the west. A healthy green forest can be seen beyond an open grassy area to the south.
12738: The road following the riverbed just north of here begins to raise slowly, letting a beautiful wall of carved stone appears at the north bank of the river. The wall continues far in the east where it seems to joins an old ruined city, perched on a high rock. Some fields can be seen south of here.
12739: The Estelin flows here gently towards the west. The flow is very calm here and some aquatic vegetation can be seen in the shallow water along the south bank. The big wall of carved stones to the north lowers slowly and seems to vanish some distance to the west.
12740: The river flows here between a high carved wall to the north and a low riverbank to the south. The Estelin is a good-sized river at this point - the mountains wherein its source lies can barely be made out against the horizon.
12741: Confluence of the Sir Lantalaith and Estelin

The two rivers mix seamlessly, one current smoothly merges with the other. The crystalline water of the Sir Lantalaith lightens the water of the green Estelin only slightly. South of here fields can be made out. The gorge to the north is spanned by two bridges - one made of planks, and the other, higher bridge made of carved stones.
12742: The lazy waves of the Estelin run along big carved rocks, on whose summit the ruins of an ancient city can be spied. The city is probably very badly decayed, as portions of it seem to have collapsed into the river over the years.
12743: Confluence of the Sirannon and Glanduin

The waters of these two rivers mixed here. Lots of eddies makes any boating or swimming dangerous : it is like the two rivers are fighting together. The Estelin continues its flow toward the west and north of here is the Sirannon River.
12744: A blooming water-lily floats on the surface of the water.

The waters wash against the base of a small cliff to the west. Atop the slope, the crumbling walls of a ruined city can be seen. North of here, there is another cliff, and there appears to be a road running along its summit. To the south, the Sirannon joins forces with another much larger river.
12745: A garden snake slithers harmlessly here.

A wide open field slopes slightly downhill towards the river to the south. Although there are the remains of many dry stone walls all over the field, to the south, just before the road, is one of the few still intact walls. With a wooden gate hanging in a gap in the wall to the south, it looks like someone has repaired it fairly recently.
12746: The river is not far from an old city, which seems to block the riverbed at some miles in the east. A big wall comes out of the city, supporting what should be a very important road, as the wall - partially destroyed - is several yards high.
12747: The waters are doing some eddies here, but they do not seem to be dangerous. Except for that, the Sirannon is a very calm river flowing toward the east. North of here a very big wall, partially destroyed, seems to support a road.
12748: An artificial wall, constructed long ago by the Noldor or Dwarves, prevents one from leaving the river to the north. The south bank is covered with burnt hulls of what were once huts. The flow of the river runs slowly toward the west, where some imposing ruins can be seen.
12749: The lazy flow of the Sirannon runs to the west here. An old road, following the bed of the river to the north, begins to rise letting an artificial wall building an unclimbable slope at some distance of the north. Small burned down huts are visible on the south bank of the river.
12750: The river Sirannon continues its east-west flow, bringing life to the lands of Hollin. The river has a brisk pace, but is not so fast that it cannot be navigated in safety. To the north of the river lies a well-trodden road which runs parallel to the river for as far as you can see, and beyond the road the northern wetlands of Hollin. To the south, the wetlands continue interspersed by a few nearby hills.
12751:
A tall plant with a perfectly smooth stem gracefully marks the landscape.
A swarm of mosquitoes is here, humming around you.
A trout swims here.
A frog is standing here.

The river continues its east-west flow, the current slow and calm, as the river widens. A bit of spray can be seen where the clear water cascades over some rocks. To the north you can see an old and decayed road that was once well used by people traveling through the Hollin. The foliage of the area is typical of this region; fields of vegetation dotted by numerous holly bushes and small trees. To the south, the rise of small hills can be seen.
12752: The river continues to the east and west of here, shaping the land as it flows. The Hollin road, to the north, can be seen matching the river's every bend and turn. To the south however, you can see the wetlands which cover the area south of the river. To the southeast you can see the corner of a stone building which is adjacent to the bank of the river. The building does not look sturdy, and appears as if it may fall into the river at any moment.
12753:
A frog is standing here.
A trout swims here.

The old river flows from the west, swiftly past the riverbank, towards the east, past a shallow area before turning to the north. While it is possible to climb up the steep northern bank, it will take much effort to do so. To the southeast and southwest a few small huts can be seen. The hills to the far south obstruct your vision in that direction while to the far north you can see the wetlands which are typical of this region.
12754:
A bright green holly bush is growing here.
Partly covered by the bush's green leaves, there are two piles of hollyberries.
A forest spider is here crawling around.

Darkness engulfs the entire area beneath the thick bushes. The holly bushes prevent travel in most directions, but there appears to be a few small animal tracks through them. Many webs can be seen spanning the branches of some of the bushes. To the north and the south the land rises a little.
12755:
A holly bush with dark green leaves is growing here.
Partly covered by the bush's green leaves, there are a few inkberries.
A huge, poisonous tarantula extends her legs to you.
A black spider crawls here, a shiny red spot visible on its belly.

Sticky webs hang from branch to branch of the densely packed brush. The bushes grow so high and thick that no light reaches the ground. There are no obvious paths to follow that lead out of the undergrowth, apart from the path which brought you here in the first place.
12756: A holly bush with dark green leaves is growing here.

To the north the holly bushes end abruptly at the edge of a sheer cliff. This cliff marks the southern edge of a narrow gorge through which the river Glanduin flows. To the south the holly undergrowth is thick and hard to penetrate. A grassy area at the edge of the cliff can be seen just to the east.
12757: The holly bushes give way to an open grassy area at the edge of a cliff. There is a deep gorge just to the northwest which guides the course of the Glanduin. Far to the northwest a tall hill can be seen, with some strange black object on top. To the east a maze of twisted holly blocks passage.
12758:
A bright green holly bush is growing here.
Partly covered by the bush's green leaves, there are some hollyberries.
A mass of wriggling vines drops on you from the trees.
Some thick writhing vines whip all around you.
A black snake hurries towards you with sly intentions.

Bright green holly bushes grow to an incredible height here, blocking out any light from above. To the north and south the ground rises sharply, but there does not appear to be any way out of the bushes. To the east and west, the shallow valley is still choked with holly.
12759: At the top of this small rise, the holly bushes still grow to an amazing height, blocking out nearly all the sky. To the north the ground appear to dip down into a densely vegetated valley running from east to west. East of here the holly seems to become slightly less dense, while to the west a dark clump of bushes seems to effectively block travel in this direction.
12760:
A holly bush with dark green leaves is growing here.
Partly covered by the bush's green leaves, there are a few inkberries.
A large brown snake with black patches is coiled here.

Dense holly bushes grow on this north facing slope of a secured valley. Although they grow quite high, it is possible to see the sky occasionally. However, at the few places that offer any kind of view across the valley, the only thing that can be seen is holly.
12761: Growing straight and tall, the trees here block all light from the sky above. Thick bushes make any kind of movement both painful and difficult. The occasional movement of a bush or chirp of a bird reminds you of the many small animals that inhabit this forest.
12762: Tall trees grow profusely in this dark forest, blocking out all sight of the sky above. Bushes grow thickly at ground level, making travel in any direction difficult. There are, however, occasional animal pathways which aid movement through the bushes.
12763: Thickly packed trees and overgrown bushes make passage very difficult through this part of the forest. The dense foliage overhead blocks out all sign of the sky, making the forest very dark and gloomy.
12764:
A holly bush with dark green leaves is growing here.
A black snake hurries towards you with sly intentions.

The thick holly bushes grow very high in this part of the valley, blocking out the sky completely. They also block travel in most directions quite well, some small animal paths seem to lead off to the west and south. To the east a thick tangle of holly bushes clusters around the stump of an old tree.
12765: A holly bush with dark green leaves is growing here.

A foul stench permeates the air all around here. It smells as if some kind of swamp is nearby, but the ground feels firm enough here. Dense foliage covers the sky, making the forest very dark. Unusually, fewer bushes seem to be growing in this part of the forest, although a thick tangle of holly bushes is concentrated on the western side of the forest.
12766:
A holly bush with dark green leaves is growing here.
A forest spider is here crawling around.
A forest spider is here crawling around.

Twisting about each other, the trees block many routes through the forest. Progress is slow, and backtracking is often required to find a path big enough to allow passage. The bushes growing all over the area hamper movement even further.
12767: Dense holly bushes block most of the pathways through the forest. However, progress can be made, albeit very slowly. The branches of the trees far above entwine in an intricate pattern, blocking nearly all the light from above, so it is difficult to tell if it is night or day above the treetops.
12768: This path has been cleverly hidden amidst the tangles of holly and thistles which grow densely packed all around. Though this path seems seldom trodden, it is kept in fair condition. To the north the path ascends up the gentle rise of the cliff's southern flank.
12769: Damp rotting logs line the edge of this sheltered glade in the dark forest. Tall trees block the view in all directions, but the ground seems to slope up to the northeast.
12770: The forest here is dark and gloomy. The trees grow tall here, blocking out any light from above. Lots of dense foliage makes travel awkward, although the numerous animal paths that criss-cross the area help a little.
12771: The path slopes gently along the cliff's western wall and nears a summit. Far below you to the west you can see the River Glanduin easily flowing against the sheer wall of the cliff. To the east several breaks in the cliff's flank make travel treacherous. To the north is a promontory which overlooks the Eregion valley.
12772: A black snake hurries towards you with sly intentions.

This lofty promontory extends out from the cliff to survey the Eregion valley beneath. The River Glanduin can be seen extending to the east and west along the base of the cliff wall far below. Deep within the valley to the west you can see the remains of a shattered village. Far to the north you can see a green forest extending along the top of the other side of the valley. To the east across a small chasm you can see where the cliff continues on. Southward leads you down a gentle slope towards an area dense with brush.
12773: A tall column of rock rises here with sheer faces in all directions. Peering over the edge, you can see the Glanduin River bending round the north and west while hills form the border to the east and south. From here, you are able to see for several miles in all directions.
12774: A large rabbit looks peacefully at you, ready to dart away.

Bare craggy hilltops block the view very far in any direction. Sparse grasses grow on the shallower slopes. Frequent rocky outcroppings break the grassy areas. Movement is possible to the south and the east.
12775: Little is able to grow on these rocky, inhospitable hillsides. Small tufts of grasses cling tenaciously to any small area of soil that exists with an occasional stunted bush growing in places.
