To the south, the hills disappear and a dense forest grows there, while to the west some breaks in the steep hillside seem to offer passage in that direction.
12776: Treetops cover the land for miles and miles south of this hillside. The forest starts a short distance down the south facing slope. To the north, the slope rises towards the sky. In the east, grassy plains cover the area between the Glanduin and these hills.
12777: Very little grass grows on this barren hillside. Grey rocks protrude from the ground making travel difficult. A forest can be seen to the south and a wide expanse of plains to the southeast.
12778:
A bright green holly bush is growing here.
Partly covered by the bush's green leaves, there are three piles of hollyberries.

From the top of this hill, yet more hills can be seen all about. Those to the north and west seem far more barren with many rocky outcrops. Those to the south and east seem far more verdant, some even completely covered with grass and holly bushes.
12779: Gently rolling grasslands cover the ground to the south of here while dense holly bushes grow to the east. Some large trees seem to form a copse just to the east. The density of the bushes to the immediate east makes it impossible to travel in that direction. However, to the north the river Glanduin breaks the continuity of the plains. There is a road running along the opposite bank of the river, with plains beyond it. Some rugged hills to the west look difficult to cross.
12780: Grassy hills rise skywards to the west of this flat grassy field. A fast flowing river travelling from east to west borders the fields northern edge. To the south the far edge of the field is hard to make out, but a dim forest seems to grow at the extent of your vision. Some footprints seem to lead northwards, but stop abruptly at a particularly dense area of holly bushes.
12781: A ruined wooden hut is perched on the hillside under the shelter of a large holly bush. It looks as if it was deserted for years, the door swings slowly on rusty hinges creaking loudly on every swing. Most of the windows are broken and there are some gaping holes in the roof.
12782: Tall, dry grasses grow up the sides of this hill, broken occasionally by a rugged holly bush. Ironically, a holly bush is growing right at the top of the hill. It looks a little windswept, but it seems to be flourishing. The river Glanduin can be seen to the north and east.
12783: Grey rocky slopes surround the faint animal trails that cross the area. The slopes to the south and the west are very steep, and climbing them would be dangerous. However, shallower slopes allow passage to the east and the north. In the far southwest some grassy plains cover the area down to a major river.
12784:
A bright green holly bush is growing here.
Partly covered by the bush's green leaves, there are two piles of hollyberries.
The garden snake slithers harmlessly here.

Small holly bushes cover this grassy clearing. It is, however, quite easy to avoid them whilst crossing the grass. To the south, east and west the bushes get thicker, possibly even impassable. The river Glanduin can be seen clearly a few leagues to the north.
12785: A holly bush with dark green leaves is growing here.

Holly bushes grow in abundance here and their red berries stand out on the backdrop of the green leaves. The bushes grow most densely to the east and south and prevent any form of passage in those directions. Far to the west a dense forest can be made out.
12786: Rugged grasses cover this slight slope. Many holly bushes dot the area, some have grown quite large on the windy plain. To the north, grasslands continue to dominate the scene, bordered on the east by the Glanduin. To the west, a dense forest can be seen.
12788: Holly bushes can be seen growing all over this low lying area just south of the Glanduin. Between the bushes, small paths can be made out, allowing comfortable travel through this area. All these paths seem to follow an east- west route. Upon close examination, these paths appear to have been made by some humanoid being.
12789: A well used muddy path extends from the shallow part of the Glanduin in the north and turns westwards. As the trail leaves the muddy shores of the river, the trail peters out and becomes increasingly difficult to follow. Grasslands and holly bushes stretch out to the east, making up the southern banks of the river.
12790: Here the river runs wide and shallow, allowing passage across the river. To the north, a small copse of trees obstructs your view of what lies beyond, although a river seems to travel behind it. To the south lie grasslands, with holly bushes interspersed over it.
12791: A small copse of trees stands here, forming a small break between the road to the north and east and the river to the west and south. Short pines stand here braving the open land here and flourishing against all the odds. Trails criss- cross the area, made by small game and some larger beings.
12792: Sparse holly bushes grow all over this plain beside the River Glanduin. Beyond the river the ground rises upwards, and from the straight lines that crisscross the surface, it looks as if it has been segregated into fields.
12793: Prickly-leafed holly bushes wreath this small clearing, hugging it on all sides and hiding it from view. Beyond the bushes to the south, some tall, slender trees rise up, fighting for position in the sunlight. The sky is directly overhead, unhidden by branches or leaves. The grass here is soft and downy, and the earth gives just enough to be comfortable.
12794: A bright green holly bush is growing here.

The holly bushes make passage difficult here, their thorns hindering any movement. Small animal trails criss-cross the undergrowth and travel through small natural tunnels formed by the holly bushes. The holly bushes continue to the north, but peter out to the east and give way to grasslands. The density of the bushes to the west denies any passage in that direction.
12795: Short grasses grow here and continue to the north. To the west, holly bushes take over the landscape, painting it a distinctive colour. To the north, beyond more grassland, you can see the line of a river snaking its way east to west with a road clinging to its northern bank.
12796: Grasses grow in abundance here, irrigated by the river to the north. The grasses continue to the south, while holly bushes begin to take over to the west and south-west. Across the river, you can see what remains of an ancient road following the river's path.
12797: On the South Bank of the Estelin

The water gently laps against the shore here. Among the reeds at the edge of the water insects hover looking for food. The slope of the bank here makes for a possible entrance to the water, but the waters look cold and unforgiving so maybe this would not be such a good place for a swim.
12798: On the South Bank of the Estelin
A river otter splashes playfully here.

The field bends slowly down to the edge of the water here. Around the shore some insects are fleeting about, every now and again a fish will surface and snatch an insect from the air. It seems possible to enter the river to the east.
12799: On the South Bank of the Estelin

The field here slopes gently down towards the water forming a small muddy bank. Around the edge of the water there are some reeds with a few insects buzzing around them. A small path leads off along the bank to the east. From here the river looks very cold and probably is as it has come from the frozen mountains far in the east.
12800: The South Bank of the Estelin

A small muddy path leads from here to the west, but this place is mostly filled by big brambles. It is difficult for big animals to move here. A slow river flows in the north and some fields seem to begin in the east.
12801: The South Bank of the Estelin
A sturdy pack horse is standing here.

The vegetation grows dense here, near the river. Some reeds are growing in the water. The river runs north of here and an old city can be seen on top of big carved stone wall on the other bank. Some fields can be seen in the south.
12802: This field used to be cultivated long ago. Some sparse wheat can still be seen, among the hundred of stinging weeds growing here. Also a few old walls, separating the old small fragments, still exist, but they are mostly crumbled. Such fields can be seen to the north and the east. The weeds are too dense to go to the south or the west.
12803: This field, with a dense vegetation, is surrounded by a bow of the Glanduin which receives the waters of the Sirannon River not far in the north. The plants here are growing well, as the sun is hot and the water is brought regularly by the river. The river is north and east of here and others fields can be seen west and south of here.
12804: This field has probably gone centuries since being used for crops - only a few hints remain to show it was once cultivated. The remnants of many small walls crisscross the fields - probably once they represented boundary markers.
12805:
A fierce boar is here, making grunting noises.
A boar cub is playing here, and exploring the wide world.
A boar cub is playing here, and exploring the wide world.

Lots of light green plants grow here. The ground should be quite fertile and, as the Glanduin River flows just east of here, enough water should be found by the vegetation. West of here there is a field divided by some crumbled walls.
12806: The river flows slowly here. It is quite large, but not too much deep, as one can see the grit on its bed. The dam to the east looks like it is somewhat damaged and some water seems to escape by this way, creating probably a bog on the neighbouring fields. A big river joins this one far in the north-west.
12807: The dark green water slowly runs to the west. Upon peering into the depths of the stream, small fish can be seen darting around small rocks and pebbles on the stream floor. To the north the remains of some small huts can be seen.
12808: This large river runs slowly to the north. The stream is not very deep but the green color of the water makes it look deeper as it is. Some small fish are swimming in it and lots of small rocks and pebbles can be seen on the stream floor.
12809: The flow runs slowly towards the north-west where a big tributary, the Sirannon River meets this large river. On the east bank, one can see a small village which seems to have been attacked and burnt down recently. Far in the north there is a big city standing on the top of a sharp cliff.
12810: The river here makes a small bend toward the north just before mixing its waters with the ones of the Sirannon north of here. The river comes from the east and to the west some vegetation grows on the bank of the Glanduin. Far in the north two bridges can be seen, connecting the two sides of a deep gorge.
12811:
The corpse of a bandit scout is lying here.
The village priest welcomes you to his simple temple.

This small building appears to be some sort of small temple for the inhabitants of the village. A few rough benches make the pews and a table at the back of building forms a pulpit. The building appears to be in a sorry state of repairs, with holes in the walls and roof which let in the rain.
12812:
The corpse of a bandit scout is lying here.
The corpse of a bandit leader is lying here.
The corpse of a bandit bodyguard is lying here.
The corpse of a thug is lying here.
The corpse of a robber is lying here.
The corpse of a bandit bodyguard is lying here.
The corpse of a bandit bodyguard is lying here.

Here lies a village, hidden from outside view by the surrounding bushes and trees. Apparently, someone doesn't want to be found. To the north, a small wooden hut has been built and the village continues to the west.
12813: A sturdy bandit bodyguard stands here, eager to hack you to pieces.

A wide open field seems to be the site of many recent skirmishes, although it isn't obvious what creatures the skirmishes are between. However, a closer inspection of some of the constructions that litter the area suggests that the field is used to practice battle. A small wooden hut lies to the north, a thin column of smoke rising from a small chimney on its roof.
12814:
The corpse of a woman slave is lying here.
A stove stands against one wall here.
A man moves cautiously around here.

This hut appears sturdy, but the inside is messy. Dirty cutlery and clothes lie haphazardly about the room suggesting that cleanliness is not a high priority for the inhabitants of this building. Several rough beds lie along one side of the hut.
12815: The underground stream ends here and flows out the northern wall through a small hole near the floor. Only very small animals could travel through the small hole, leaving only two obvious ways out, either the cave to the west or the ladder leading up to a trapdoor.
12816: This area seems to have been dug out of the softer earth here, but bare stone can be seen forming the walls and roof here, so no supports are required. This area seems to have little traffic, as there are few tracks here on the dirt floor. Those tracks that are here lead towards a rough door in the south wall.
12817: This apparently makes up a store room. Shelves line the walls and hold various mundane items required for a small village like salt, food and utensils. The room continues to the west.
12818: A dirty shovel is lying on the ground here.
The store room continues on here but ends at a stone wall to the west. More shelves line the walls filled with yet more supplies for the village. You can leave this part of the store to the east.
12819:
A long, smooth, steel-tipped lance is lying on the ground.
A long, single-edged sword lies on the ground.
A full metal shield is on the ground.
This room is apparently an armoury for someone. Various racks on the walls seem made to hold various weapons, mostly shortswords, bows and daggers. Small pieces of broken weapons litter the floor.
12821: The cavern makes a sharp turn here, leading from the south to the east. The water travels slowly round the bend, creating small whirlpools as it goes.
12822: The water continues its underground passage here, leading northwards. The water travels along a wider part of the floor here and so runs a little slower. The cavern walls are smooth here, apparently hewn out of the rock by centuries of water flow.
12823: A small black vicious rat squeaks at you for disturbing it.

The water makes a turn here, travelling from west to north down a gradual slope in the cave. The water flow is fast but kept to a narrow ditch in the centre of the cavern, a ditch which can easily be crossed by even the shortest legs.
12824: Water pours out of a hole in the western end of this cave. The water has none of the power that must have carved this cavern out of the solid rock from which it is made. The water travels down a small channel to the east.
12825: This small landing is surrounded by rocky walls. The rocky ground, partly wet and the slippering stones here, makes it difficult to walk around here. No sound is heard here, except from the constant flow of a river to the east of you. You can spot a tiny trail winding its way up from here.
12826: The river is shallow here; you can stand quite steady on your feet. Looking up, you can see an old bridge, but it seems like an impossible task to climb back up, as you find yourself in a gorge. However, to the west you can spot a little landing. Perhaps you can climb up from there? To the south you can see this river joining another one, making it bigger and stronger.
12827: The waters flows slowly from the north towards the south where the river goes under two bridges. The higher one seems partially destroyed, but the lower one, made of some wooden planks, seems more recently built and, therefore safer. The sides of the gorge are carved, and were also painted, also the colors have mostly disappeared.
12828: This tiny path comes out from the Hollin Road which runs east-west just south of here. It leads north along a small river to the east. The river lies far below the path and a small barrier prevents anybody from falling down. Plains lie beyond the river, as well as far to the north, where the path seems to be blocked by some kind of a building.
12829: The sight from this vantage point is an unusual one - the river flows between the carved walls of the gorge to the south, where it is crossed by two bridges. The higher bridge is made of stone, while the other bridge is situated only a few yards above the waters.
12830: The river flows calmly here. It seems to have some rapids in the north where some blocks have fallen in the river, but here the river is very quiet: one can even see the ground through the clear water. The river bends here toward the east; the sides of the gorge, always carved, seem unclimbable.
12831: A Bend in a Narrow Track

The path makes a small bend here. It leads westward to some small huts that are visible in the distance, and to the south it rejoins a larger road. Eastward there is a river, but the water lies several yards below the lip of the bank. To the north there appears to be an ancient cemetery.
12832:
The small fierce-looking bat is hanging from the ceiling, obviously sleeping.
The small fierce-looking bat is hanging from the ceiling, obviously sleeping.
A large bat is here, hanging in the darkness.

A stair was excavated in the carved cliff letting thieves reaching the Hollin Road that runs up there. To the east there is a small wooden plank bridge which seems not to be very solid. On the other side of the valley there is a same stair letting the people go inside Ost-in-Edhil. The decaying mass of the old bridge hides half of the sky.
12833: This bridge is neither solid, neither broad. The river flows quickly a few feet under the planks. On both side of the river, there are cliffs with stairs excavated in the stone. The big mass of the old stone bridge fill the sky.
12834: This is the base of a stairs leading up inside Ost-in-Edhil, the old Noldorin city which was ruined by Sauron's armies during the Second Age. This stair, like the plank bridge thrown across the river, was made by thieves who wanted to enter the elven city.
12835:
A domesticated pony, beast of burden to many, stands here.
A Dunlending hunter is here, stalking his prey.

This bog was probably created during the war between the Noldor and Sauron, long time ago. The waters of the Glanduin River came here and submerged all the vegetation. Since then, the vegetation decayed and slowly turned into peat. Some muddy holes can be seen, indicating that some people used to come here to find some fuel for their fires.
12836: Here, the mist is grey and dense, diffusing and absorbing all sources of light. While it is not known how long the mist has covered this land, the muddy ground has become bare, except for a few strands of yellow vegetation that struggle in their growth. Without much vegetation, the peaceful herbivores have become scarce.
12837:
The starving cow stands here looking for a patch of grass.
A black crow flies low to the ground here, looking for carrion to eat.
A black crow flies low to the ground here, looking for carrion to eat.

A small creek passes through the valley from east to west. That and the small protection from the elements given by the valley walls have pleased some farmer who seem to have settled down here. Vegetables grow in a churned strip of earth and further west you see more plants arranged in an orderly fashion.
12838:
A young colt is frolicking playfully.
A sturdy pack horse is standing here.

High grass grows on the barely undulated terrain in these desolate lands. Winds make the whole grassy landscape undulate even more, almost giving a sensation of sea-sickness. Beside the slight irregularity the plain is very flat and there is nothing to hide the horison in the distance.
12839: A black crow flies low to the ground here, looking for carrion to eat.

Endless green plains extend in every direction leaving you the most outstanding break in the general flatness. All kinds of animals eat from the grass and with them there are many sneaking predators looking for easy prey.
12840: The grass grows green here, grazing the legs of passing creatures as it slowly sways in the wind. The landscape surrounding you is also very fertile and the land between you and the horizon is coloured in various shades of green.
12841: A black crow flies low to the ground here, looking for carrion to eat.

The grasslands start sloping upward to the south where some hills can be seen. The plains stretch out in the north and east, and continue without end all the way to the horizon far away in the distance. The grass around you is scattered with small stones and pebbles.
12842: The grasslands stretch out in all directions away from you on this elevated terrain, save the hill that blocks your view to the east. The colour of the grasses change shade to a darker hue of brownish green in the south, melting into the horizon. Half-hidden in the grass here are some white stones arranged in a circle.
12843: This small track was used by the inhabitants of the small village which can be seen just north of here to go to the peat bog, which is just south of here, in order to take some peat for their fires. The village itself lies in ruins now. The village looks like it has been burnt down and molested very recently. A large river, the Glanduin, is flowing just west of here.
12844: The burnt and blackened skeletal remains of a human are here.

This hut is more or less completely burned down to the ground. The remains of a table and some burnt pieces of a bed are all that is left in this room. A small hearth is placed where the eastern wall used to lie. The room has a poor air to it, and there are no signs of any wealth at all. Across the floor lie some painted skins depicting battles fought long ago, but they are more or less completely destroyed.
12845:
A waist-high evergreen shrub grows here, with thick, reaching branches.
On the shrub, there are some grey-green leaves.

As soon the outskirts of this village are passed, you notice the smell of something recently burned down. It looks like this village has been plundered and destroyed not long ago. There are no signs of any villagers left alive. The village was made up of very small sod huts which now are more or less wrecked. The village path continues to the west from here and there are plains east of here.
12846: A horse of the Rohirrim (Rood) is standing here, ridden by you.

On arrival at the centre of the village you notice no signs of any living creatures whatsoever. Everybody seems to have either died or abandoned the remains of this village. The house to the west seems to have been somewhat of a regal air to it and is certainly grander looking than the rest of the houses. To the south is a the remains of a small sod hut.
12847: A half-rotten corpse is hanging here.

The inside of this once big hut is quite small but considerably more spacious than the others of this village. The ceiling has been completely perforated and someone has dug holes in the floor obviously looking for something. Most of the walls have been razed. The remains of a large fireplace lie in the centre of this annihilated hut.
12848: These Dunlendings who inhabited this village are not very wealthy as all the furniture seems to have been very inexpensive and meagre looking. In the south wall a fireplace stands with a few embers glowing away in the grate. The remains of a small bed takes up most of the north wall and a small table lies in pieces in the centre of the room. The only exit is back to the north.
12849: A cow stands here, chewing her cud.

Green grass covers the land around here and the pollen in the air makes you feel quite drowsy. Farm animals graze quietly around without it would seem paying much attention to you. Every now and again something will raise its head and give you a discerning look before going back to whatever it was doing originally. To the south the leftovers of a burnt down small sod hut sit quietly. Grassy plains open up to the east and to the west is the once lively village.
12850:
A clean fragrance drifts up from a thick clump of leaves.
A holly bush with dark green leaves is growing here.
Partly covered by the bush's green leaves, there are a few inkberries.
A grey wolf is here, snarling aggressively.
A grey wolf is here, snarling aggressively.
A large brown wolf stands here, its teeth partly bared.

This muddy region of the riverbank has eroded, leaving only a few tufts of bright green vegetation. You can enter the river by going north down a shallow slope and just beyond the river you can make out the broad Hollin road. To the south the northern reaches of Dunland can be found. However - to the west you can see the landscape shifts into more farmland.
12851: The presense of decomposing organic matter is strong, causing a layer of mist to cover the surrounding areas. Here, the mist is thin and wispy, but to the south it quickly thickens. Strange sound seem to originate from within the thickening mist, for evil growls and wolf-like howls echo loudly from that region.
12852: A slender plant grows here, with clusters of tiny pink flowers atop its stem.

Here, the mist has thickened, preventing most, if not all, sunlight from reaching the ground during the brightest of days. The ground, soft and spongy, is bare except for a few strands of yellowing vegetation. The damp air settles upon your face, with droplets of water rolling into your eyes. The mist distorts the nearby howls making it difficult to determine their directions.
12853:
A light boat made of reeds has been left here.
A fishing net has been left here.
A Dunlending hunter is here, stalking his prey.
A small child is here playing happily.
A small child is here playing happily.
A Dunlending woman is here tending to her children.

Standing at the entrance of the building, you notice foot prints in the wet mud which covers the floor, indicating that someone has been here recently. Several worn out pairs of boots stand adjacent to the northern wall, while a pile of logs destined for someone's fire are stacked in the southwest corner. A small fireplace runs along the southern wall. Even though the hut is very old, it seems to have only begun to decayed recently due to lack of care. On the west wall there is a small window from which you can see a small encampment consisting of several huts and a small corral. Further to the west, beyond the encampment you can make out a small decaying hut.
12854:
A swarthy Dunlending warrior is here, guarding his village against intruders.
A Dunlending woman is here tending to her children.
A Dunlending woman is here tending to her children.
A Dunlending woman is here tending to her children.

The single room hut, cramp and decaying, is crudely furnished with a wooden table, a small bed and a few unstable stools. The previous inhabitant obviously had little means or care for material comfort. Next to the cold fire place there is a large half empty cooking pot covered with mould and mildew.
12855: You stand at the edge of a small encampment. The entrances to two small huts are to the north and east while to the west you can enter a hastily constructed corral. The only obvious exit from the camp is to the south, along the path taken to the camp. From here the faint howl of a wolf can be heard as can the wind rustling through the holly bushes on the moor.
12856:
A brown donkey watches the surroundings, perhaps looking for a chance to graze.
A brown donkey watches the surroundings, perhaps looking for a chance to graze.
A brown cow is here, contemplating a higher reality whilst chewing slowly.
A cow stands here, chewing her cud.
A half wolf is here, loyally protecting his master.
An old Dunlending man is standing here.

Straw covers the ground here, keeping the ground soft and warm for the animals that are kept here. The stalls seem too small for horses, but just right for sturdy ponies. The low wooden kennels were certainly designed for dogs, unless, of course, wolves have been domesticated in these parts. A rickety gate is on the west side of the corral, held shut by a small strand of wire. Past the gate you can see the Dunland.
12857:
You see four eggs on the ground.
A rooster is here, strutting about.
A hen sits here, keeping her eggs warm.
A hen sits here, keeping her eggs warm.
A hen sits here, keeping her eggs warm.

In the dim light you can see the laying boxes for the hens and the patched wooden walls which keeps the predators away from the prized poultry. The thought of a few fresh eggs makes you linger for a while even though mounds and mounds of decaying feces fill the bottom of the cages and spread out onto the floor.
12858:
A swarthy Dunlending warrior is here, guarding his village against intruders.
A swarthy Dunlending warrior is here, guarding his village against intruders.
Wuda, wielding a woodsman's axe, is standing here.
A grey wolf is here, snarling aggressively.

The low glow coming from the embers of a dying fire does little more than enhance the dark shadows within this shelter. The rank odour of treated animal hides, which the walls of the shelter are made from, is quite oppressive. The faint smell of cooked meat is also evident, but no evidence of roasting meat can be found. Metal discs and ring shaped charms hanging from an overhead pole suggest that an important person lives in this dwelling.
12859:
There are two pieces of cheese here.
You see three loaves of bread on the ground.
On the ground, there are two fine lion pelts.
On the ground, there are two large skins.
A canoe has been left here.
A swarthy Dunlending warrior is here, guarding his village against intruders.

This small room was carefully added to the side of the main building in a fashion to make it difficult to detect. The shelves are covered with dust, implying that the room was seldom used. Noting the meager provisions, you surmise that the folk who inhabit this place are not wealthy.
12860: Here, the river has become rather shallow making it easy to cross. To the south you can barely make out a track that seems to lead towards a stone building. The side of the river bank indicates that you are not the first person to have forded the river here in order to enter the northern reaches of the Dunland. The river flows east and west from here.
12861:
A large beautiful rose bush is blooming here.
Deep inside the bush, there are two red roses with leaves and thorny stems.
A holly bush with dark green leaves is growing here.
Partly covered by the bush's green leaves, there are a few inkberries.
A bright green holly bush is growing here.
Partly covered by the bush's green leaves, there are some hollyberries.

This area of the moor is overgrown with young holly bushes, but beneath the young branches of the bushes the track is well defined. It is hard to tell whether the track was made by man or animals. To the north lies the Sirannon, forever flowing to the west. From here you can make out the faint outlines of a structure to the south, though the swaying branches of the young holly bushes obscure your vision. If you were to remove the branches from the bushes, you would have a clear view of a poorly constructed stone building. The doorway of the building would look worn and in need of repair, and you would be able to see recent tracks upon the path that leads to the building's entrance that would imply that the building was still in use. While the building would not appear to be in good condition, it would appear to provide better shelter than the branches of the bushes that obscure your vision.
12862: A rough overgrown track leads away from the dark entrance to the wooden hut just north of here. The track bends to the southeast, leading towards a nearby area shaded by some trees. The moorland opens up to the east but looks very bleak, cold and unhospital from here. Just south of here there is a small hill.
12863: This area is quite rough and gets rougher to the south as a small hill rises above the landscape. To the west, the wetlands are shrouded in a light mist that grows darker farther to the west. To the east the end of a narrow path can be seen which leads away from a small camp that lies somewhat to the northeast. This track seems to pass through an area overgrown with short shrubs and holly bushes.
12864: A fat rabbit is here, chewing on some grass.

This place, a few miles south of the River Sirannon is just west of some primitive huts which are constructed of branches and dry mud. The huts are surrounded by a large irregular wooden fence which makes access to them difficult. However, just outside the fence perimeter is a small corral, which can be easily entered through a rickety gate. To the west lies an unusual building that is constructed of rough stone walls, and covered with dew.
12865: Standing at the edge of a large stone building, you can see a doorway set in the wall further to the east. The riverbed of the Sirannon, which is to the north, flows from west to east carrying its life giving water as it shadows the decaying road which lies beyond the northern bank. To the west a small decaying hut can be seen and to the south a few hills dot the landscape.
12866:
A clean fragrance drifts up from a thick clump of leaves.
A swallow flies high above the ground.

To the north the River Sirannon can be heard flowing, while to the west a stone dwelling has been built upon the riverbank, making it somewhat difficult for you to approach the front of the building. You can, however, follow a small track which leads to the building entrance. The rough stone walls of the building are covered with dew, and to the west, beyond the building wetlands are visible.
12867:
A porcupine is waddling around here, its tail full of sharp quills.
A grey wolf is here, snarling aggressively.
A swallow flies high above the ground.

To the southwest, you can see the beginning narrow track which runs east-west from a dark dell in the east to the doorway of a building towards the west. More wetlands lie to the east, and seem to continue forever, yet, to the far east you can catch a glimpse of the far away Misty Mountains. To the south a few hills obscure your vision.
12868: A swallow flies high above the ground.

A moorland opens up to the north but it looks very bleak and cold from here, not the least bit inviting to those who seek a comfortable life. However the smoke which comes from a camp shows that primitive people choose to settle in that land. The short bushy vegetation is present everywhere, making any potential trail impossible to spot from a distance. A wall of dense vegetation grows eastward, blocking any attempt to move that way. To the far east, you can catch a glimpse of the mighty Misty Mountains, with its cruel snow-covered peaks.
12869: A tall plant with a perfectly smooth stem gracefully marks the landscape.

The mist begins to thicken as droplets of water form on your face as you pass through it. While sun light can still pass through the mist, it becomes difficult to see clearly. Strange howls seem to originate from the darker mists of the south and west.
12870: The thick mist seem to absorb and diffuse all light making it difficult to see clearly. The shapes around you are oddly blurred by the thick veil of water in the air. Something seems to be moving at the edge of your vision but you can't quite make it out before it moves away from you.
12871: A thin mist begins to form as water from the nearby river can be heard as it collides with some submerged rocks. While the mist clears to the east, where the back of a small hut blocks movement in that direction, it gets heavier towards the southwest as it rides an odor of decaying matter.
12872: A fat rabbit is here, chewing on some grass.

This corner of the grassy wetland, bordered by the river Sirannon to the north and west and a small building to the east, seems to be well tended for the vegetation is green and healthy, ready for harvest. A line of holly bushes are growing at the edge of the field forming a natural fence between the field and the nearby dwelling. A strong odor comes from the building, indicating a lack of hygiene by the current inhabitant.
12873: The holly bushes growing upon this section of the moor seem to be very hearty. The branches are well formed and are heavy with inkberries. An odor of decaying feces comes the nearby dwelling which is likely to be the home of whomever tends to these somewhat groomed plants.
12874: The ground becomes damp underfoot here and a light mist can be seen covering the lands to the south and west. Further north you can see the banks of the river Sirannon which once flow past the brown building standing directly west. The odor of decaying feces and rotting eggs issues from the entrance of the hut which can be entered through a low door.
12875: A light mist covers the ground here, making it hard to see your feet as you travel slowly across the barren wetlands. The mist seems to darken to the southwest but a comforting light issues from the building to the northeast. A trickle of water can just be made out to the north.
12876: A damp atmosphere blurs your vision as a light mist flows across the ground. You feel chilled as the water condenses on your clothes and begins to seep through to your skin. The mist becomes much darker towards the west but seems to clear slightly towards the east. The chill upon your body grows as you hear a strangled cry from deep within the mists but it is impossible to tell from which direction the cry comes.
12877: A grey wolf is here, snarling aggressively.

The beginning of a shallow valley to the west, and a hill to the east, break the monotony of the empty plains surrounding you. The grass grows a thriving green here, kept low only by wandering animals. Mingling with the blades of grass are small white flowers, growing in clusters.
12878: An old weathered scarecrow is planted firmly in the ground here.

There is a small creek running east to west through the centre of these very fertile plains, surrounded by all types of vegetation. Some of the plants seem to have been planted in rows, a sign that someone has been taking care of the land. To the north a thick mist can be seen clinging tightly to the ground.
12879:
A small child is here playing happily.
A small child is here playing happily.
A Dunlending woman is here tending to her children.

A drapery made of roughly cured animal hides covers the only entrance to this small hut. The walls are round and made of clay, daubed onto a wooden frame. A small hole in the roof serves to let out the smoke which rises from a little cooking fire, and also allows the light of sun or moon to enter the dusky room.
12880: Grasslands stretch out to the east and north. You can see that the grass seems to have been partitioned off into fields by means of some low stone dykes. Domestic animals roam the fields as well as some smaller wild animals.
12881:
A fallow deer is grazing peacefully here.
A powerful ram stands here, poised and alert.
A woolly sheep is grazing here.
A woolly sheep is grazing here.
A woolly sheep is grazing here.

Grasslands stretch out in all directions, punctuated by low stone walls. The fields stretch as far as the eye can see to the north, but beyond some fields to the south an old, disused road can be seen as it follows the path of the ancient Glanduin River.
12883: Cows and sheep have been roaming this field quite frequently, making muddy trails in the gaps between the dry stone walls. A large water trough towards the centre of the field suggests why they come here so much. The fields slope upwards to the northeast.
12884: Many tracks criss-cross here, as if it were the scene of much activity. Several animal trails lead through the mud to the south. You can see a small, low building to the west, but you cannot make out what may have built or what may stay there. To the south-west, you can see a road following closely the route of an old road.
12885:
A powerful ram stands here, poised and alert.
A woolly sheep is grazing here.
A woolly sheep is grazing here.
A woolly sheep is grazing here.

Grasslands continue to the south and west for a long way. Weeds intermingle with the grass and no signs can be seen of anything larger than a rabbit. Far, far to the south, a road can just be made out.
12886: Tall grasses obscure the view in any direction here. The occasional thistle makes wading through the grasses very uncomfortable. An occasional animal trail can be seen winding its way across the plain.
12887: Grasses grow quite tall on this part of the grassy plain. From here there is a great view of the land to the southwest. The plain has been broken up into many fields by some stone walls, and animals can be seen grazing in them. Further away the Glanduin traces its way from east to west. A path seems to follow the river.
12888: A starving cow stands here, looking for a patch of grass.

A large pond lies in the middle of this field, and many animal tracks lead up to it. It looks as if sheep and cows are the most frequent users, but there could be other animals too. Dry stone walls denote the edges of fields, although in places the wall has collapsed, allowing the animals to roam free.
12889: High stone walls have been built around this part of the plain. However, many sections have fallen down allowing access from most of the nearby fields. Not far to the south a road follows the river Glanduin from east to west.
12890: Roughly built stone dykes mark the boundaries of fields on these grassy plains. The tracks in the ground seem to suggest that some animals are kept here by someone, possibly sheep, judging by the droppings. Most of the tracks seem to follow an east-west route, but you can see no sign of why. Far to the south-west, a road can barely be made out, with a river just beyond.
12891: The grasslands here have been partitioned off with rough stone dykes. Evidence of the fields' inhabitants are obvious as you can see the spoor and tracks all around you. The fields spread all around, but expand furthest to the south- west. Beyond the fields, you can barely make out a road following the line of the ancient Glanduin River. Further to the west, a small building is visible.
12892:
A wooden chest stands in the corner.
Klaees (thedon), wielding a great warsword, is standing here.

The chief of the thieves should hide the treasures in that room. But, at the moment, it is quite empty. The walls are only plain earth and a ladder leads up. The air is a little moisty. Some empty chests can be seen along the northern wall.
12893:
A thief is here looking for some stranger to rob.
A mugger lurks here, looking for a stranger to rob.
Cinard the Master Thief is here looking furious.
The thief who lives here will surely not be a small robber. This tent is filled with lots of costly furniture. A fine carpet lies on the ground, covering most of it.
12894: Tall thorns seem to throw their sharp spikes and spears at you as you progress up this path. From here the path continues north and south, and from a dark wood in the east some spine-chilling shrieks and howls can be heard from time to time.
12895:
A forest spider is here crawling around.
A forest spider is here crawling around.
A swallow flies high above the ground.

Huge, impenetrable walls of thorns blockade all further passage in any direction except from where you came. To the east, a tall wall of thorny bushes blocks the way, like in the north and the west. The only exit is back to the south onto the trail.
12896:
A thief is here looking for some stranger to rob.
A mugger lurks here, looking for a stranger to rob.

This encampment consists of a few tents. A big fireplace stands in the middle of them. Some trunks were thrown all around it, letting people sit comfortably around the fire. The huts themselves are without interest, except one, just north of here which is much bigger than the other.
12897: A squirrel scampers around here, looking for nuts from the trees.

A tall wall of thorns blocks any further passage to the north and the west. Even though trying and keeping the thorns as far away as possible from you, it is not possible to pass through it, even by scratching your body on the sharp points. The only possible exits are east or south.
12898: The trail here peters out, with a few tracks continuing to the dark path that leads north of here. To the east a huge wall of thornbushes blocks your way over which you can barely make out a massive dark looking building. The trail continues north and south here.
12899: This cemetery has been abandoned for a long time. All of the tombs - and there are plenty of them - are covered with moist moss. Some of them have collapsed into piles of stone with weeds growing among the rubble. It seems that someone has been here not long ago, for there are recent tracks and the remnants of quite a few fires. A few of the tombs look to have been pried open - apparently by thieves in search of treasure.
12900: Small shafts of light that penetrate through the woody canopy above you give you just enough light to navigate by. From time to time small woodland creatures run past you on their daily business of hunting or being hunted. From here the wood continues east and north and a large hedgerow blocks any sight, and any walk, to the south.
12901: A small, well-worn path leads east and west here, and some old tracks lead to the north as well. To the west in the distance some small buildings can be made out. Northeast is a small copse hiding the rest of the valley. All around, the grass has been cropped short by grazing animals.
12902: From here the plains seem to stretch on to eternity, like a sea of green the grass slowly waves back and forth with calm undulations under a light breeze that blows across the plains.
12903: All around are small herds of animals quietly grazing away and seemingly oblivious to your presence. The grass has been cropped short here by the animals grazing, but the ground is still very soft underfoot, with patches of mud about where too many animals have stood for too long. To the south only the waters of the Sirannon can be seen coming out of an artificial gorge.
12904: This part of the cemetery seems older than the rest. There are no traces of thieves or graverobbers here - all the tombs appear intact. Most of them are engulfed in high weeds and brambles. A tall hedge blocks movement in every direction save west.
12905: Several large rocks have fallen down from the two carved walls that form the gorge in which the Ringnen flows. Lots of foam floats on the water, which rushes at a furious pace. The river flows onward to the south.
12906: The Sir Lantalaith flows here between two carved walls, making a deep gorge. These walls are very old and partially destroyed. The waters flows quite quickly, but it should not be too dangerous to boat or to swim around here. Due to some foam, it is not possible to see the bed of the river.
12907: A squirrel scampers around here, looking for nuts from the trees.

In that small copse, you can hear birds singing above you in the tree canopy. Around you lie a few rotting tree trunks amongst other foliage. From here the wood seems to continues to the west getting slightly darker as further you look. The plains are east of here.
12908: In the distance to the east there is a small copse, although from here it looks quite dark and gloomy. The local wildlife seems to enjoy an idyllic existence, and there is lots of evidence of small mammals who must make their homes in the grass. The plains continue to the north and west. A large unscalable wall blocks access to the river, which flows beneath in a deep gorge.
12909: The river flows towards the southwest and enters a deep gorge just south of here. The waters steadily gain speed, and some froth begins to be visible. The sharp cliffs loom ominously over the river to the south.
12910: Along some fields in the east and the west, the waters of the Sir Lantalaith begins here to become wilder. The two banks are narrower than in the north, and the speed of the river is thus increased. The river continues south-west from here between two stone walls, and one can see a small copse far in the west and a strange black hill not far in the south-east.
12911: The quiet waters of the Sir Lantalaith bend here toward the south where they disappear in a deep gorge. Some fields can be seen on the west bank and far there is a small wood. The east bank is also covered by some fields and very far in the east one can see the barrier of the Misty Mountains.
12912: The water has a clear blue hue of purity as it flows from the rocks. Fish swim about, darting among the shallow pools. From this point, the river flows to the west, winding away to join the Glanduin. To the south, some old fields can be seen.
12913: In the near distance there is a small copse. Every now and again a slight movement catches your eye making you glance over in that direction. For some reason unknow to you the grass is slightly shorter here almost as if it had been grazed by some herd animal. The wood is at some distance west of here and a small river stands in the east.
12914: In the distance to the west there is a small, dark wood. From here it looks very unfriendly and foreboding, although here in the plains all is calm and peaceful. Small animals dart past your feet and disappear into the undergrowth. The plains stretch out to the south and the east.
12915: A grey wolf is here, snarling aggressively.

The wood is quite dense here, but the ground can still be seen. The ground is quite moist and you leave footprints where your feet have been. All around can be seen the tracks of other woodland creatures as they criss-crossed your path. The wood continues west and south, there is a plain to the east.
12916: This small room has some carved walls with ugly paintings and sculptures on them. There is also the rest of eight columns in the centre of it, which seem to be much older than the rest of the temple. They should have each a figure on it, but all are destroyed and only some writing can still be seen on them.
12917: A dove rests near one of the flowers.

Some wheat can sparsely be seen in that field, indicating that this was a previouly cultivated area. North of here stretch some vast plains. A strange temple stands just west of here and the Hollin Road is south of here, running east-west. A small hill, completely black, can be seen in the north-east.
12918: This tomb is quite big, it seems that its builders constructed it carefully, in order to let it last for ages. The walls are carved, but no painting can be seen on it. The tomb continues to the the north and to the west where the tomb seems to be in a worse state of preservation.
12919: This room was originally the place where the corpse of a dwarf was deposited in order to wait for the end of the time, until the soul will come back from the Halls of Mandos. The corpse was originally lying in a wooden sarcophage, but was thrown away from it by some grave looter who then pillaged it. The walls, slightly carved, remain untouched. The only obvious exit leads to the south.
12920: A shade is here, shrouded in an inky blackness.

This part of the tomb is crumbling, and even small animals like rats fear it. As soon as you enter, the noise you make create some vibrations that make some parts of the already broken ceiling to fall down, hitting you some. Nothing can be seen in this section, either it is gone since very long ago, or it has been destroyed by falling rocks during all these years.
12921:
A spirit floats around, making strange magical gestures (glowing).
A shade is here, shrouded in an inky blackness.

The marble tunnel ends here. It is not a wall that blocks your way, but a huge pile of bones from molested skeletons. Skulls and pieces of bones lie scattered in the shallow water. The scent of dead tissue is intense but lots of worms and maggots seem to like the atmosphere since they cover the marble walls.
12922: The water covering the ground is dark and cold. The marble walls are wet from the humidity of the air in the tunnel. A dead bat is floating in the water. Some reflections in the water indicate that there is an open room just up of here. The tunnel also continues southwards.
12923: Moisture covers the marble walls in this corridor. The muddy ground is sloping downwards to your south. To the north the corridor expands in a larger room. The humid air carries a scent of death and decay. The ribcage of a human is lying on the ground along with some fragments of an arm.
12924: The smell is very strange here, the air must be a little bit different than above ground. It means that this tomb is probably very old and rarely, perhaps never, visited by living creatures. No corpse can be seen here and the floor goes slowly down towards the south.
12925: The grass is not very high here and some tufts of yellow, some wheat, can be seen. Just west of here is a deep gorge where a small river flows and east of here a bare mound of earth stands in a field, hiding most part of the mountains that are very far in the east. North of here there is a small river and the field continues in the south.
12926: In the middle of this field lies a slightly mounded patch of barren earth. The area around the mound appears to be infertile - the few clumps of vegetation that have managed to grow are yellowed and have a sickly appear- ance. The fields themselves have lain fallow for centuries - no one has cultivated here for more than a millennium.
12927:
A fierce boar is here, making grunting noises.
A boar cub is playing here, and exploring the wide world.
A boar cub is playing here, and exploring the wide world.
A finch flies low above the ground.

This field stands in a bend of the river which disappears into a deep gorge just south-west of here. Some sparse wheat grows here and there, but the field is no longer cultivated. The Misty Mountains can be seen very far in the east, and the middle of the field south seems to be barren.
12928: A brown fox is here, looking for some rabbits to chew up.

This field stands just north of the Hollin Road. The weeds are high, and some yellow spots can be seen, it is some wheat that still grows here after years of fallow. A strange black hill stands just north of here.
12929: A skeleton of some humanoid lies in the dust.

Stairs carved in the soil lead to the muddy bottom of a rather large burrow. It extends in all directions allowing you to move around freely. The chilly water covering the mud emits a penetrating scent of decay. An almost completely intact skeleton of a fallen minion of Sauron lies before you.
12930: This section is rather narrow and is not as well-excavated at the rest. You have to force your way through the roots and the mounds of earth on the floor. There are no parts of skeletons here. This area of the grave was never used.
12931: The burrow is very irregular. The walls are covered with marks from the fingers of its builders. The chilly green water still cover the soft and muddy ground. Clods of earth hang in the roots that grow through the ceiling.
12932:
A Skeletal Warrior is staring angrily at the surroundings.
An intact skeleton of a man is walking around here.
An intact skeleton of a man is walking around here.

The roots hanging in the ceiling whip you face as you enter a narrower section of the burrow. Bones that once were arms or legs stick up from the mud. The stench is so intense is almost completely absorbs your attention. The burrow continues westwards.
12933: This is the southernmost part of this underground burrow. A huge root grows straight from the ceiling to the muddy floor. It seems extremely solid and was probably not worth the effort to chop off. There are marks from the hands of the builders in the wall. Workers with large hands built this part of the burrow.
12934: Some sparse wheat grows here, indicating that this field was cultivated long ago. In every direction, there is such field, except south, where a decaying road can be seen. Very far in the west, a city seems to come out of the ground.
12935: This field was cultivated long time ago by the Noldor. During the Second Age, a big war happened and the followers of Sauron destroyed the area. Now only sparse wheat can be seen, and the Hollin road, which leads east-west just south of here, is partially destroyed.
12936:
A small rabbit glares angrily at you.
A fallow deer is grazing peacefully here.

While the wetlands continue to the north, they are separated from the river Sirannon to the south, by the wide Hollin road. Looking carefully at the ground, the remains of the bones of those who were either too weak or too slow to leave this area can be seen. The northern edge of the Dunland lies just beyond of the river Sirannon and offers shelter to those that come in friendship.
12937: A small cluster of clover grows here.

To the north and south lay the Hollin wetlands making movement in those directions difficult. However, in the distant south a track across the wetlands is faintly visible. To the west a thick tangle of holly bushes makes movement in that direction difficult if not impossible. Upon the soft ground the prints of those who have passed before you are embedded.
12938: A beautiful and docile horse is standing here.

A tangle of prickly holly bushes makes passage to the north and west impossible, but to the south and east, passage is possible. Further to the southeast a smooth track, which forms the Hollin road, can be seen, beckoning for travel. You can hear the baying of wolves in the distance, but are unable to tell which direction the sound originates from.
12939: Tall, green grass cushions your feat as you stroll idly across these plains. The plains gently roll and undulate, stretching off into the horizon to the north and the east. The wind softly sways the grass in gentle eddies, cooling your face and giving you crisp, fresh air to breath. There is a small river just west of here.
12940: The grass is green and very lush here, gently brushing past your knees as you wade through it. The grass is very soft and has the calming effect of soothing your feet. Around you there are animals grazing and insects buzzing around flowers in search of nectar. The plains disappear off the horizon. Far in the west there is a small river.
12941:
A beautiful and docile horse is standing here.
A beautiful and docile horse is standing here.

The path towards the south is blocked by a thick hedge of holly bushes. However, you can easily move across the lightly wooded area to the west and the plains to the east. To the north, you can see a large flat plain sparsely populated with trees and overrun by oxen and horses.
12942: A beautiful and docile horse is standing here.

The luxuriant fields of Hollin extend north and west from where you stand. The former Elven cultivators are gone. Wild herds of oxen, horses and deers now roam the fields which were once used to feed Ost-in-Edhil some 4500 years ago. A large pond, formed from a shallow depression and filled by the recent rains, is east of here. The mark of hooves show that animals use the pond as a source of water. Southwards a line of birch trees mark the bank of the river Sirannon.
12943:
A tall, stately, dome-topped tree grows here.
On the plant, there are two green spiny capsules.

To the south of here a thin plume of smoke can be seen, curling slowly upward in the wind. The wetland becomes very damp to the west while a smooth track lies directly to the south. You can see the remains of some small animals decaying on the rough grass.
12944:
A sturdy pack horse is standing here.
A sturdy pack horse is standing here.

Dank and rotten undergrowth abounds here, the decomposing organics emits a strong odor and makes the ground soft and mushy. Your feet are sucked into the deep mud, which continues more towards the north than towards the west, making it difficult if not impossible to move in those directions. Drier land, however, can be found to the east and south making it much easier to move in those directions. A smooth track lies towards the southeast of here.
12945:
A bright green holly bush is growing here.
Partly covered by the bush's green leaves, there are some hollyberries.
A beautiful and docile horse is standing here.

There are many small holly bushes here, some dotted with a few sickly red berries, but the majority of them barren. Other than the bushes, there are a few strands of yellow vegetation, much of it dead, the rest dying. In the distant east and south, beyond the wetlands, the track of the Hollin Road is faintly visible. Unseen from here, to the far south, lies the Dunland and to the north and west drier land can be found.
12946:
The wild ox seems ready to charge you.
The wild ox seems ready to charge you.
The wild ox seems ready to charge you.
The wild ox seems ready to charge you.
The starving cow stands here looking for a patch of grass.
A swallow flies high above the ground.

The plain slowly slopes towards the south and extends as far as one can see in all directions. The only clear landmark that can be seen from here is a line of dense vegetation to the distant south, where the river Sirannon is known to flow. The vegetation growing here is a mixture of wild grains such as oat and wheat. Wild grapes can be seen growing at the foot of a low fallen stonewall, indicating that this plain was once a part of the fertile fields of Hollin which was first cultivated by the elves of Eregion and later by the men of Arnor.
12947:
A bright green holly bush is growing here.
Partly covered by the bush's green leaves, there are a torch and some hollyberries.
A fallow deer is grazing peacefully here.
A fallow deer is grazing peacefully here.
A grey wolf is here, snarling aggressively.
A grey wolf is here, snarling aggressively.
A large brown wolf stands here, its teeth partly bared.

You can tell that this corner of grassy wetland was carefully tended to by someone, for some small holly bushes grow in a neat row along the edge of a low stone wall forming a fence which blocks movement towards the south. The stone wall are the only remaining debris of an old farm. To the east the river Sirannon can be heard, but a flooded plain blocks the direct path.
12948: Things are very quiet here, almost unnaturally quiet, causing a sense of unease which warns you that danger may be nearby. A campsite, which appears to be abandoned, lies towards the east. To the distant south lies a track which would ease your travel along this hilly ground. While the wetlands continue to the west, a dense row of small bushes prevents movement in that direction.
12949:
The corpse of a vulture is lying here.
The corpse of a vulture is lying here.
An arrow lies on the ground.
There are two rotten corpses here.
A small black vicious rat squeaks at you for disturbing it.
A big, nasty vulture is sitting here, protecting its nest.
A black crow flies low to the ground here, looking for carrion to eat.
A black crow flies low to the ground here, looking for carrion to eat.
A black crow flies low to the ground here, looking for carrion to eat.

This camp has obviously been raided by a group of marauding nomads recently. Fresh blood covers the ground around a burnt-out fire, and discarded arrows still litter the place. When you get near the burnt-out fire, you can still feel some heat coming from it. Maybe the nomads are still near? From the feathers on the arrows one would suspect that the attackers might have been one of the infamous tribes from the northern Dunland.
12950: An unusual smell from the west pervades the air here. The moorland seems the same as those surrounding you but a faint smell of blood suggests that some deed of violence has been committed nearby. The moor continues to the east and a decaying road crosses the hilly lands to the south.
12951: Here, the moorland has sparse vegetation, enough to keep the top soil from washing away but little more. The lack of vegetation is due to the rocky soil, which is unusual for this region of the Eregion which is known for its great fertility. To the south, a rough track which forms the Hollin Road, can be seen. Further to the west a thin column of smoke can be seen as it slowly drifts in the wind.
12952:
A bright green holly bush is growing here.
Partly covered by the bush's green leaves, there are a torch and some hollyberries.

The rolling hills abound here are covered with vegetation of all shapes and sizes, most of it in the form of low-lying holly bushes and heather. Across the moorland to the south you can just make out a wide track which winds across the land. Just south of the track, a depression in the earth is seen. Probably the small ravine which forms the river Sirannon.
12953: The road continues straight, running east and west of here, as the clear waters of the River Sirannon flow swiftly past. On the opposite bank there seems to be some sort of cairn which can be seen quite clearly against the dark moorland background. To the south a small area of the bank seems to slope gently down to the edge of the water.
12954: Years of usage has caused deep ruts to form, making the track very rough. Even though, travel upon the track is far faster than moving across the damp moorlands which surrounds the track. The track bends to the north and west here, as it passes north of a flat section of land which is the bank to the river Sirannon, and leads toward the mountains to the far east.
12955: A broad road crosses the land and continues south and east of here. To the south of here the river Sirannon can be heard and beyond the river a large cairn can be seen, standing proud in the bleak surroundings of the moors.
12956: From here the track continues to the south and east, while towards the west the moorland stretches out before you. Deep ruts in the track suggest that it has been poorly maintained, but since the nearby cities have long since been destroyed this is not surprising. The faint howls of wolves can be heard further westwards, upon the moors. Past the flow of the Sirannon, to the south, a range of small hills can be seen. The sight of these hills should bring forth old and forgotten tales of the tribes of fierce hillmen that once lived upon these lands.
12957: You are travelling upon the seemingly endless track that was once, very long ago, used by dwarves and elves when they carried goods between Moria and Ost-in-Edhil. Today, the track is no longer used by dwarves and elves in their search of trade, for the areas along this path are no longer inhabited. To the north, some hills can be seen while to the south what remains of the once mighty river Sirannon can be heard.
12958: A sturdy pack horse is standing here.

The old road continues east and west, as it provides a path between the Misty Mountains and Tharbad. Wind-blown leaves, holly berries, and rugged stones blanket the road as if they are trying to hide the lack of usage of the barren tracks. To the south, beyond the river Sirannon, the Hollin Hills can be seen, while, to the north, more hills hover on the horizon.
12959: The old road, once favoured by the wagons of long dead rich merchants, con- tinues to the East and West. To the south, the streambed of the Sirannon runs quietly and solemnly parallel to the road. All sorts of different types of terrain surrounds the area. Grassy hills and bleak forests hugs the road to the north.
12960: A boar cub is playing here, and exploring the wide world.

Great rolling plains of tall green grass open up.. The grass is very lush and green, a welcome change for your feet as well. Horses could easily graze here. The side of the road seems to be reachable to the east.
12961: A mean looking robber is here, demanding money from you.

The track continues east and south here through the countryside. To your north the wood continues and you can enter it from here. The track is hot and dusty, and the cool shade of the wood seems very inviting.
12962: The road bends to the north here and you can see the river bank to the east. Looking east you can see the Sirannon winding its way up towards Caradhras and the Misty Mountains. You can see many prints that have been set in the mud before you travelled along this track.
12963: A porcupine is waddling around here, its tail full of sharp quills.

This is a peaceful woodland, and all around the wood's population is at work or play. The sun glistens through the leaves and casts friendly shadows on the ground. From here one can see the track to the south and the wood continues north and east.
12964:
A clear spring babbles as cool water trickles out of the ground.
A sturdy pack horse is standing here.
A porcupine is waddling around here, its tail full of sharp quills.

This is a glade with a small pool in the centre of it. Around the pool there are many of the woodland creatures quietly drinking its refreshing waters. Everything seems so peaceful here, but scorch marks on the trunks of some of the older trees lets you know that it was not always like this. The wood continues east and south.
12965:
A cute rabbit is here.
A fallow deer is grazing peacefully here.

The wood is probably at its thickest here, but there are still small clearings here and there. Looking into them you can see some deer quietly grazing. There are many tracks of animals on the ground but none really to raise alarm. The wood continues to the east, south, and west.
12966:
A sturdy pack horse is standing here.
A fallow deer is grazing peacefully here.
A porcupine is waddling around here, its tail full of sharp quills.

The wood thickens slightly here making progress more difficult. The birds are still singing in the trees and animals still play around you. Even though the animals seem friendly, they always seem to keep a distance, never letting you get too close. The wood continues north and west.
12967: The track bends east and south here as it follows the path of the riverbed of the old Sirannon. Looking to the east you can see the mountains rising up, but those are many leagues away from here and of no concern at the moment. The track is criss-crossed with many footprints and tracks of animals.
12968: A fallow deer is grazing peacefully here.
This is a thinly populated wood. Still, there are many small animals scurrying around your feet. The trees here are mainly deciduous. The wood continues to the west and the decaying road to the east.
12969: You enter the remains of what must have been the town's watchtower. From here you can see a short way along the track. There are a couple of broken chairs and tables, but apart from that the room is completely bare, stripped by bandits long ago. The only exit is to head back down the way you came.
12970: You enter a small guard house. Looking around the room you can see it was built only for a couple of guards. When this area was used for trading that's all that would have been needed as the temporary markets would have been heaving with Dwarvern miners and Elven farmers. The Dwarves would have been enough to keep the peace as they guarded their gems and ores very carefully. In the north-west corner there is a flight of stairs leading up and there is an old gate back outside to the east.
12971: A porcupine is waddling around here, its tail full of sharp quills.

The wood is sparsly populated with small clearings here and many animals are seen to be grazing in them. Generally the wood goes about its daily business without a second thought to you, or so it would seem. The wood continues to the east.
12972: A Track in a Clear Forest

Looking at the ground here there seems to be a great many tracks arriving from the north and leaving either east or west. Looking north you can see a gate which is now an orange colour with the rust that has built up on it over the centuries. Above you, you can see a watch tower that has seen better days. The track disappears in the west and joins with a biggest road in the east.
12973: The old road continues east and west following the path of the Sirannon. There is a small wood some distance away. The wind picks up and blows the dust around you making you cough and splutter. To the west you can see the road winding its way down into the valley.
12974: The road continues east and west following the riverbed of the Sirannon. There is a small wood some distance off to the north. The wind picks up and blows the dust around you making you cough and splutter. To the west you can see the old road winding its way into the valley.
12975: The bed of the river is not what it used to be. All that is left is a stream not nearly as wide as the original Sirannon. This river was much bigger as it is now, but some climatics modifications, perhaps, have changed the facts. The stream floods east-west.
12976:
A bass swims here.
A bass swims here.
A bass swims here.

The small stream flooding in a bed too large for him, residue of its past importance, bends here. It is flooding from the east, as far as you can see, but will, from here, floods southward. A small decaying road follows the bed of the Sirannon to the north and the west.
12977: The riverbed continues north and south from this point. A small stream runs through the centre of the riverbed, over a layer of smooth round pebbles. The walls of the riverbed are wrinkled with dry cracks and fissures, due to the lack of water which once formed roaring Sirannon. An occasional weed protrudes from the muddy cracks, determined to take root in all but the most unlikely places.
12978:
A black catfish is here, lurking in the mud.
A large beaver is here, gnawing on a piece of wood.
A beaver is sleeping here.
A bass swims here.
A bass swims here.

Here the riverbed curves to the north and west, around the base of a small berry-covered hill. A beaver dam has been built through the great riverbed, to regulate the level of the water during the seasons in the pool it created. The top of a large beaver hut emerges from the water. To the east and south, more holly-covered hills are visible beyond the riverbed, splashing the landscape with a flurry of pinkish hue.
12979: A lonely hill stands here, overlooking the Sirannon streambed to the east and south. Low hollyberry bushes cover the ground in abundance, laden with heavy bunches of ripe hollyberries. A shabby old road can be seen to the west while far to the east, the towering Misty Mountains loom gracefully with the three giant snow-covered peaks.
12980: The Sirannon flows from east to west here, occupying a small portion of its ancient streambed. The water is cold and clear, and a reasonable effort is needed to hold position in the low but swift stream as it gathers pace, fed from the surrounding hills. Reeds and other marsh plants have colonised the wet riverbed, while the slopes are covered by grass. Far to the east, behind several lush hills, the towering Misty Mountains can be seen.
12981: The low river flows swiftly from east to west from here. The water is crystal clear and very cold, coming directly from the different tributaries which flow through the hills. It is difficult to navigate the river as the current drags you towards the west, making for a very bumpy ride. To the south the green hills, which are dotted red by berry laden holly bushes, can be safely reached from here. To the north you can see the Hollin Road.
12982: The river Sirannon flows swiftly here, from east to west. The water is clear and cold, being composed of melting snow from the nearby mountains. The current is rather strong and carries debris which has collected along the river's route. To the south, hills dotted with red, by hovering holly plants, seem safe and beckoning.
12983: A swarm of mosquitoes is here, humming around you.

The river leads directly to the of south here, the water moving with considerable speed as it flows over the pebbles which litter the riverbed. A broad track, that runs across the northern areas of this land, can be reached by climbing the riverbank to the north or west. In the south, a few small hills can be seen. The water here is clear and bright, and several species of aquatic life be seen.
12984: The river flows from the north, around a small bend, the channel then forces the water to the west, bending once again further on. A spray of water hits you in the face as it flies upwards from a nearby rock. To the south of you the wetlands, typical of this region, can be seen covered with foliage such as holly bushes and heather. There is also a track paralleling the river on its northern bank, that looks well used.
12985: Here, the river continues straight east and west as it winds through the wetlands. The river runs parallel to a wide track which crosses the land north of here, and leads on into the distance. When looking further to the south you notice some sort of a stone cairn that has been built near the bank of the river. A few hills can be spotted in the far reaches of the area, both south and north, but they are a ways off.
12986:
A toad is standing here.
A crayfish is here, snapping its claws at you.
A crayfish is here, snapping its claws at you.

Here, the river flows swiftly, being fed continually by mountain snowmelt and rainfall. The bottom of the river is covered with smooth stones, worn down by years of moving water. The channel that bears the current is not overly deep, making it easy to clamber up to the north where a small track runs. To the south, some hills can be seen, covered in the typical foliage of this region.
12987:
A trout swims here.
A trout swims here.

Directly to the north of here, you notice a shallow sloping bank which provides easy access to the road. The river flows swiftly on to the south-west and north-east, though not with the force of larger rivers such as the Bruinin. A stone structure and some small huts are visible to the south of the river.
12988: The torrent water flows swiftly over the boulders, which are pounded by the full might of the River Sirannon. The great abundance of fishes and other water creatures makes for a lively scene, darting around and amongst various aquatic plants. You can continue along the channel to the north and west, but the erosion has chopped the banks at a steep angle, making travel to the east and south difficult.
12989: Here, the flow of the Sirannon bends slightly to the north and west, as it runs parallel to the Hollin road which is just north of here. The shallow slope on the northern bank seems an ideal way to leave the riverbed. A bit to the south, you spy a series of small dwellings that are obviously very old. To get a better view however, you will have to go beyond the ravine formed by the river.
12990: You notice that the moorland in the distant northwest are quite overgrown, but to the southwest they are more sparse as they become enshrouded by a dense mist. A small stone hut of some kind lies to the southwest and adjacent to the stone building is a small hut. The bed of the river, itself, continues to the north and east. Though the land is fairly flat here, it seems to be but a small plateau as the region to the southeast becomes hilly. The water flows swiftly but peacefully along the river.
12991: The river Sirannon continues west and bends north at this point, in its ever winding path. A rough road can be seen to the north, running adjacent to the river, leading through the wetlands. Small hills are visible to the east, both north and south of here. The southern Misty Mountains, with it's three peaks - Caradhras, Celebdil and Fanuidhol - loom in the very distant east.
12992:
Clusters of slender stems and tall leaves thrive in the mud and shallows.
