A heron is stalking the area, looking for fish.

The Sirannon continues its path through the Hollin Hills from east to west here. The remnants of the once-mighty river lie across the entire width of the flat riverbed, allowing you to cross here with ease. To the west, however, the river gathers strength and pace as it is fed by rivulets and tributaries from the pink-red hills which pervade this area.
12993: A large beaver is here, gnawing on a piece of wood.

A well used trail winds its way through the foothills, leading from a ford in the Sirannon just north, to the south will it continues through a thin forest. To the east and west, the plains begin to rise as they form the Hollin hills. In the distant east, the crowns of the Misty Mountains can barely be seen above the hill-tops.
12994:
A woodpecker is here, tapping on a tree.
A partridge attempts to hide in the undergrowth.

The trail travels through a sparse forest here. Many deciduous trees grow here, interspersed with some smaller holly bushes. The trail itself continues from north to south, leading out of the forest into the hills to the south. The trail does not appear to be very busy, but it seems to have been used lately.
12995: A huge, black wolf is here, ready to devour.

The trail bends from east to north here as it travels through the pink-red hued hills. The hills lie in all directions, but a small forest intercedes between here and the hills to the north and east. To the south, the holly bushes thin out and grass becomes more predominate, although an occasional bush can still be seen.
12996:
A partridge attempts to hide in the undergrowth.
A partridge attempts to hide in the undergrowth.

The trail travels from east to west of here, journeying through as small forest as it does so. To the west, the trail enters some hills. The forest continues to the north and north-west, but the southernmost point of it lies here. The forest is sparse and seems lucky to have manged to exist in this area.
12997: Here, the trail bends from west to south, avoiding the grassy plain which extend east. To the west, beyond some low hills, the beginning of a forested valley is faintly visible. The trail is evidently used often, apparently by men, or man-like beings. To the north, the Hollin Hills stretch out for miles.
12998: The trail comes to a sudden end where it meets a crudely made palisade gate. Blackened tree trunks extend sharpened ends well above the ground, hiding and shielding from view whatever might be stirring inside. Several skulls have been fixed on the palisade as warning for the foreigners. The fields surrounding the palisade are covered with cow dung and show obvious signs of grazing -- whoever dwells behide the palisade surely depends on herds for their sustenance. The trail continues north through the grasslands, giving way to a sparse growth of trees.
12999:
A shallow pond is here, tinted green with algae.
A well-fed cow stands here chewing her cud listlessly.
A well-fed cow stands here chewing her cud listlessly.
A well-fed cow stands here chewing her cud listlessly.
A well-fed cow stands here chewing her cud listlessly.
A bull stands here, calmly looking around.
A large beaver is here, gnawing on a piece of wood.

These grasslands are fertile, and obviously well-grazed. The palisade visible to the southeast seems to indicate that whatever grazes here is probably domesticated. To the north, the low hills begin to show some woody growth, while the grassy hills to the west become slightly more rugged. To the east is a trail leading up to the front gate of the walled village.
13000: A goat is here, grazing in the hills.

This area of low rolling hills is carpeted with grass -- parts obviously well- grazed by some sort of herd animal. To the east, a sturdy palisade of logs forms a barrier, which, one might assume, protects the nearby villagers who use these grasslands for grazing live stock.
13001: From here, you can clearly see a small village some two miles north and east. This region, unlike the area to the west is level making it suitable land for the village to come. To the north or east you can move towards the village, while south and west leads you further away.
13002: From here, directly behind a small village, you can see a number of small huts. One hut appears to be larger than the others and the bright paintings on its exterior seems to indicate that the hut holds some significance within the village. A large fenced in corral blocks direct movement towards the north. The plains continue to the west, south and east.
13003: The thick long grass forms a blanket of green stretching for many miles in all directions. While it appears that an occasional elk or deer has wandered this way, the grass is thick and hardy and covers their passing leaving little in the way of a trail. An open region to the south can be seen where a water hole has formed and beyond it and to the west a single tall tree helps to maintain your orientation upon these plains. To the north and west some four miles a small village takes shape.
13004: The grassy hills have been closely cropped by grazing. To the west, an imposing log palisade rears up among the low hills - probably protecting a village. To the south, the hills continue, hiding the course of the River Glanduin somewhere among them. To the east, the grasslands continue unabated.
13005: A small evergreen plant grows here, its woody stems reaching two feet.

To the southwest, a log palisade is visible among the low grass-covered hills. The landscape looks heavily grazed - perhaps the people on the other side of the wall depend on cattle. To the west, a well-worn trail leads to what looks like a gate in the palisade.
13006: These low hills are carpeted with a tough grass that helps them resist erosion. To the east, the landscape becomes much flatter, and there is a village of some sort. In every other direction the hills continue - becoming more forested to the northwest.
13007:
A squirrel scampers around here, looking for nuts from the trees.
A buck runs swiftly from place to place, looking about warily as it grazes.

These lands were apparently once much more forested than now. In the small valleys tucked between the high points, only stumps remain. There hasn't been much regrowth, so the trees were probably cut fairly recently. To the west, woods again become visible among the hills.
13008:
A tall, stately, dome-topped tree grows here.
On the plant, there are two green spiny capsules.
A placid pond is here, inviting you to take a refreshing drink.
A small child is here playing happily.
A goat is here, grazing in the hills.
A goat is here, grazing in the hills.
A goat is here, grazing in the hills.

Nestled among the surrounding hillsides, this small well-watered valley is the home to a dense but young forest. You can tell animal life is plentiful for there are signs of small mammals everywhere. To the north, the hills are much more rugged while in the other directions they are characterised by gentle slopes.
13009: This terrain is dominated by gentle well-worn hills and lightly wooded vales. To the east there is a valley filled by what could almost be described as a forest. Holly bushes are not as prevalent here as in Hollin to the northeast, but it still lingers.
13010: To the northwest you can see a pile of stones which must be near the bank of the river Sirannon. The ground, further north of here, seems to get very wet and may not be able to support your weight. The moors to the south of here are lightly wooded by stunted trees which strive to survive the battering winds.
13011: Just to the north of here, a large pile of stones forms a cairn on the south bank of the Sirannon. The moorland stretches to the south, but to the west a rough shelter has been constructed. Getting inside the shelter from here will require a bit of travel for it is still a few miles away. The moorlands have been cleared of vegetation, and rough trenches have been dug into the soil. Perhaps someone is attempting to cultivate some crops.
13012:
A woody evergreen plant grows here, with many stems reaching upward.
A bright green holly bush is growing here.
Partly covered by the bush's green leaves, there are some hollyberries.
A Dunlending trapper is here searching for animals.
A Dunlending hunter is here, stalking his prey.

A small hut made of animal hides seems to stand guard against the wilderness on this sandy hill. The smell of roasting meat comes from within the hut to the south and some movement can be heard from there. The ground all around here has been trodden down by the passage of many people and the mud sticks to your feet as you pass over it. North-east of here there is an odd pile of stones.
13013: A swallow flies high above the ground.

A building to the south-west of here was constructed of rough stone, with little skill or attention to details. The gaps between the rough-hewn rocks leave the rooms inside the building almost as cold as the moorland out here. There is no entrance to the building on this side however, there must be an entrance to the building to the west or south of here. To the east, a tent, constructed with animal skins, stands upon a sandy hill.
13014: Moorland on the Bank of the Riverbed

This area of moorland lies between a strange Cairn to the east, a small building to the west, and the riverbed of the Sirannon to the north. These moorland seem wet, having soaked up the excess water that overflow the banks of the nearby river. Some faint animal tracks are barely visible in the wet mud, leading around a tent-like hut to the southeast.
13015: To the north the moors continues until it reaches the river Sirannon, but to the south there is a small hut which seems like a suitable resting place before you contine your journey. The wind carries the faint sound of flowing water in the north and you can just make out an irregularity in the northern reaches of Dunland to the east. The nature of the irregularity seems to be a pile of rocks, next to a small village.
13016: A large stone cairn stands in front of you, crudely constructed with stones from the surrounding moorlands. From the rough stones you can deduce that the cairn is very old, but it is not apparent why it was built outside the boundary of the nearby village. To the north the river Sirannon flows swiftly by, causing a pleasant spray to be thrown across the banks. Around the cairn, you notice that vegetation is strangely lacking, almost as if the plants are scared to grow there.
13017: While the moor is quite dry here a few heather plants, which cover the ground, seem to be growing very well. Scruff marks and a series of small holes on the plants suggest that wildlife around here is not as dead as in the surrounding moorlands. You are a long ways from the river, which lies to the north, and there are signs of human habitation to the west, as you can just make out a building in the distance.
13018: The hills extend in all directions from here. To the east, they are somewhat more rugged, but do not form much of an obstacle. To the north, the faint glimmer of what must be the river Sirannon can be seen. Somewhere among the hills to the south must lie the river Glanduin, and beyond that an expanse of land known as the Dunland.
13019: These hills are particularly rugged for this region - the land looking as if it had been pushed back and folded unto itself. Eastward the hills begin to fail, while to the south and west they continue unchanged. Some distance to the north, the river Sirannon can be spotted winding along the northern edge of the hills.
13020: The hills become much more rugged to the west, while to the east the hills seem to fade somewhat. Mostly covered with wiry grass, these hills are well-worn by the passage of time. To the southwest, it appears that some small areas of forest have managed to thrive in the little valleys.
13021: Yellow flowers, with grey-green foliage, grow in clusters here.

This appears to be the eastern edge of an expanse of hilly land. To the east, the land flattens significantly, becoming essentially a plain. The grassy hillsides appear well-grazed, so there must be a human habitation near. To the north, a trail winds among the shallow depressions between the high points of the land.
13022: A bright green holly bush is growing here.

The pink-red hills stretch out far to the west, holly bushes dominating the landscape. Few plants have been able to survive on these harsh hills. A trail can be seen, travelling through the hills and continuing into a forest northward. Several miles behind this forest, you can see a river flanked by an overgrown road.
13023:
A sturdy pack horse is standing here.
A boar cub is playing here, and exploring the wide world.

All around you terrain appears to be hills, covered by holly bushes, that stretch for miles and miles. Far to the north you can see an overgrown road hugging the northern bank of a narrow river as they travel together from east to west. To the east, the hills are punctuated by a small forest as they lead to the foothills of the Misty Mountains, many miles from here.
13024: The hills continue in every direction - somewhat steeper to the east - and are covered with the growths of holly bushes that are common in this region. To the north, the Sirannon winds among the hills leading westward to its junction with the Glanduin.
13025:
A fallow deer is grazing peacefully here.
A fallow deer is grazing peacefully here.

Although you are a long ways south of the river Sirannon, you can just make out the steep banks through the overhanging tree branches in this area of woodland. Your sight to the northwest is completely blocked by the overgrown trees and bushes, but off to the southwest you can see some sort of structures built on a small hill.
13026:
A slender plant grows here, with clusters of tiny pink flowers atop its stem.
Clusters of slender stems and tall leaves thrive in the mud and shallows.

You find the ground here unsound as as you sink to your knees in the damp mud. Passage through here is very slow as your attempts to get out of this damp area of moorland are nearly futile. The thought of being attacked here while ensnared by the mud makes getting out seem even more imperative.
13027: Winding past you to the north is the swift flowing Sirannon. A stone building, which is to the distant south-west of here, can be seen. An overgrown track leads away from that doorway towards the north. Another, closer, hut lies to the south.
13028: Clusters of slender stems and tall leaves thrive in the mud and shallows.

Here you can see the clear water flowing swiftly past you as the moorland meets the bank of the river. The water carries leaves and small twigs from nearby trees down stream as it flows towards the sea. The moorland itself continues to the south, seemingly featureless except for a strange nearby pile of stones.
13029: The moorland, sloping gently down to the nearby river, continues to the west, where in the far distance there are a few signs of civilization. The vegetation here is hardy, able to withstand the rocky soil of the hills, as well as the harsh weather that comes frequently. A sharp howl of a wolf makes you realise you are truly far from home.
13030: The hills, dotted with berry laden holly bushes, stretch in all directions, painting the landscape with their red berries. To the north, you can barely make out a river which winds its way across the countryside as a road hugs the northern bank. To the south-east, you can see a forest in the distance and far, far in the distant east the Misty Mountains can be seen as they reach towards the sky.
13031:
A bright green holly bush is growing here.
A great black and silver wolf is standing here, at the head of the pack.
A large brown wolf stands here, its teeth partly bared.
A grey wolf is here, snarling aggressively.
A huge, black wolf is here, ready to devour.
A large brown wolf stands here, its teeth partly bared.
A huge, black wolf is here, ready to devour.
A grey wolf is here, snarling aggressively.

The hills, covered with berry laden holly bushes, continue here, as they do in all directions. To the east, while the hills become smaller, the holly bushes do not thin and the ever present red berries continue to cover the bushes. To the distant north, you can see a road which follows the route of a river as they wind their way through the countryside.
13032: Small hills lie in the shadow of their larger counterparts to the west. In any case, your view to the north, west and south is blocked. To the east, however, you can see a forest. Far beyond the forest, the Misty Mountains can still be seen, towering above all else.
13033: Holly bushes litter the countryside, their rich pink-red berries adding colour to the region. Dots of pink-red continue far to the east, spreading also to the south-east. The berries are also visible, but for a shorter distance, to the west. The Sirannon flows through its wide riverbed to the north, skirted by the Hollin Road to its north. To the south, the land begin to transform as the pink-red colour of berries is replaced by lush green. The Misty Mountains caress the sky, dominating the horizon far to the east.
13034: A clean fragrance drifts up from a thick clump of leaves.

The Hollin Hills stretch south of here, flanked to the north by the remains of the river Sirannon and dozens of miles south by the mighty Glanduin. Beyond and adjacent to the river Sirannon, the Hollin Road winds its way east-west, joining the once great settlements of Moria and Ost-in-Edhil. Even from here, you can see that the road has suffered from a lack of use. Obviously, not many in current times have need of the road. The holly bushes of this region, as always, cling to the side of the hills adding a touch of read to the lush green background with their many berries.
13035: From this vantage point over the river, you can see, clearly, the southern hills. They are all covered by red dots which cling to the holly bushes growing upon them. To the north, the river Sirannon picks up speed and power, as it is fed by small rivulets and tributaries from this watered land. Clinging to the north bank of the river lies the Hollin Road, overgrown due to lack of use. Far to the east, beyond the holly-covered hills, are the Misty Mountains, visible even from this distance.
13036:
A weapons rack stands against the wall.
In the rack are a heavy warhammer and a bastard sword.
A spirit floats towards you and howls with an evil laughter.

A small unlit chamber has been carefully carved into the rocks underneath the somber crypt above. The chamber is very cramped and much of the space is occupied by the decayed remains of humans who are now eternally at rest free from the struggles of daily life. The rusted and worthless chain mail garments which once adorn their bodies mark them as warriors, the crumbling weapons of their lively hood still clasped in skeletal hands. A scripture has been carved upon the shield of one of the warriors.
13037: A diamondback rattlesnake is coiled here, ready to strike.

A bright radiance seems to issue forth from various coffins within this crypt, reflecting off the dust stirred by your movements. The air gives the whole room an ethereal quality, seeming to lull you gently, but your sharp senses detect an evil intent which continues to lurk in the dimmest corners. A dusty stone plaque is carved into the eastern wall.
13038: This large natural cavern seems to have been enlarged by skilled masons in order to fit a slab across the above entrance. Climbing down was easy, once you could see the rough ladder carved into the wall, but now a feeling of unease washes over you as you examine the surroundings. Was that a wolf howling outside, or the cry of a tortured soul from within the cavern ?
13039: The branches of prickly holly bushes, and the trunks of short trees block movement to the south. The moors surround you in every other direction but a small stone building, just west of here, catches your attention. Near the middle of the moors stands another dwelling, a little east of the stone building. The howling of the wolves seems to come closer all the time.
13040: A brown fox is here, looking for some rabbits to chew up.

To the southwest of here, you can see a dark area of trees and thick bushes. However, the thick vegetation prevents direct movement to that area. Leading away from the dark area, a faint track, that leads to a small stone building, is visible. Off to the distant northeast, you can see some sort of stone object next to a rough hut on the side of the river. The moors are featureless to the south and east of here. Less forested than other areas of Eregion, this place must have been hard-hit by many storms. The rolling hills around you seem to extend forever.
13041:
A grey wolf is here, snarling aggressively.
A grey wolf is here, snarling aggressively.
A grey wolf is here, snarling aggressively.
A large brown wolf stands here, its teeth partly bared.

The rough moor, completely surrounding this area, look particularly damp and uninviting towards the south. To the north, however, you can see some sort of cairn and a rough tent adjacent and west of the cairn. Further, west of the tent is a building constructed of stone and of poor quality. Beyond the tent and stone building are a few small hills, and beyond the hills are some flat lands similar to these moors. From here, the howling wolves sound very near.
13042:
A bright green holly bush is growing here.
Partly covered by the bush's green leaves, there are some hollyberries.
A brown fox is here, looking for some rabbits to chew up.

This small hill slopes gently down to the west where it meets the surrounding moors. To the northwest a stone pile stands near the river bank. A few small holly bushes have sprung up from the dark rocky ground here, but they seem to be struggling against the harsh conditions of this land.
13043:
A bright green holly bush is growing here.
Partly covered by the bush's green leaves, there are two piles of hollyberries.

This hill is almost bare of the holly bushes and much greener than the adjacent hills. The reason for the sudden change in vegetation is the proximity of the hill to a nearby forested valley, which is directly east. The valley, as seen from here, is a sparse forest, with varying hues of green vegetation. It continues to the east and northeast, becoming denser in those directions.
13044: Here, the hills have considerably less vegetation than they do further north, where they are dotted pink-red by the abundance of berry bearing holly bushes. Looking outwards from here, hills can be seen to extend in all directions. To the east, beyond the next hill, the beginning of a forested valley is faintly visible.
13045:
A large brown wolf stands here, its teeth partly bared.
A large brown wolf stands here, its teeth partly bared.
A large brown wolf stands here, its teeth partly bared.

The hills are more rugged here than farther east, and they continue both north and west. Small patches of woods are fairly common - although hardly a forest, there is plenty of wood available should the need arise. At one point, a small cave is visible in one of the hillsides.
13046:
A coloured game bird is visible in the vegetation, watching you warily.
A squirrel scampers around here, looking for nuts from the trees.

These low hills are well-worn, with few sharp faces or gulleys around to thwart a traveller. Several of the small valleys tucked among the hills are home to small patches of woods. Game seems plentiful, judging by myriad trails leading through the underbrush.
13047: A large water hole provides a place for wildlife to gather during times of thirst. While the source of the water is not clear, it is probable that this is a low point in the plains; and therefore water collects after each heavy rain fall. Alternatively, there could be an underground stream which provides a steady source of clean water. On occasion a deer or elk appears to be licking the soft mud but is more likely feasting upon a natural deposit of salt. While the plains continue in all directions, the region is well marked with a village some five miles to the north and a bit west, a large singular tree to the southeast, and the waves of a rolling hills in the distant west.
13048: An endless expanse of grass continues in all directions. While an occasional elk or deer can be spotted, the land is mostly barren of wildlife. From here, the faint outline of a small village can be seen towards the north, while rolls of some distant hills slowly take shape some four to eight miles west of here. For the thirsty, a water hole can be reached by travelling due east.
13049: A beautiful and docile horse is standing here.

This plain contains countless blades of tall, green grass. While a few trampled blades indicate that wildlife or men have passed this way previously, little else indicates their passage. While the land continues to be level in the north, east, and south, to the west a hill slowly forms.
13050: A sturdy pack horse is standing here.

As the hills before and after, this hill has been well-worn by the countless years upon which it has braved the onslaught of rain, snow and wind and contains few sharp faces or gullys to thwart a traveller. While there is not much to distinguish this hill from the others, a single graceful tree continues to thrive as it has for many years before this one.
13051: A low point upon the Eregion hills the view of the village further north and east is blocked. A soft upward slope continues to the south while the terrain levels off to the north. The backside of a cave blocks immediate movement towards the north but it can be circumvented to the west and east.
13052:
A badger is here, exploring for food.
A grey wolf is here, snarling aggressively.

While from a distance this dip is quite visible, here, in the shallow valley, the only immediate visible difference between this region and those to the north, south, west and east is that the village to the north and east is no longer visible. The upward slopes are so shallow that they would be barely distinguishable to someone walking through these hills. The grass and bushes are slightly richer in colour from the additional water that has seeped through the ground.
13053:
A great black and silver wolf is standing here, at the head of the pack.
A huge, black wolf is here, ready to devour.
A huge, black wolf is here, ready to devour.
The mother wolf stands here, protecting her young cubs.
A large brown wolf stands here, its teeth partly bared.
A grey wolf is here, snarling aggressively.

This hill is barren of the holly bushes which paint much of the landscape with their pink-red berries. To the east there is a small dip in the hill, which, from here would be barely visible to a traveller, but from a distance helps create an illusion of rolling hills. To the south there is a small cave, little more than a crevice in a small boulder deposited many years before this region became a grassy hill.
13054: The track continues through the dark dell that is surrounded by short trees and small holly bushes. The beginning of the track is just west of here, and is the perfect size to allow a human to pass though the dense bushes unscathed. It seems that a nearby grove of bushes has been well tended by someone, possibly the person who inhabits one of the dwellings to the north. There are no other directions to enter the dell, as it seems to be enclosed by a rambling hedge of prickly thorns.
13055:
A cluster of dark green, feathery fronds flourishes in the shade.
A placid pond is here, inviting you to take a refreshing drink.
A black bear is sleeping here.
A swarm of midges is here, humming around you.

The tightly packed bushes and trees of this region block the sun completely, making it difficult to see the shallow pool in the centre. The area has obviously been often visited by someone, as human sized footprints cover the ground, especially near the pool. The dell seems safe because the tightly packed bright holly bushes form a barrier against the outside world.
13056: A large brown snake with black patches is coiled here.

A large boulder, once the width and height of many men, appears to have split from the bottom upwards as nature pulled the large rock apart. Over the years, from freezing rain and natural erosion, this crevice slowly evolved into a small cave, not much larger than a small elf. The bottom of the cave is composed of the soft soil which forms the base of the Eregion hills, while the top is the sharp edge of splitting granite.
13057:
A bass swims here.
A bass swims here.

A calm serenity fills the quiet repose under the green banks of the Glanduin river. A joyful gurgle rises from the water where a green-leafed bush at the southern riverbank stirs the flow of the river. The current gathers up speed as the stream rushes over a shallow section near a bend that sends the river further west. A sudden squirt of water followed by a darting movement that glistens through the water suggests the presence of fish.
13058:
A river otter splashes playfully here.
A large pike is lurking in the mud by the bottom.

Calm flows the purling Glanduin as its ever bending course shifts through the grass-covered plains. Every now and then, the water slips over a stone or a boulder protruding the muddy riverbed creating a gentle fall, behind which the bubbles make a lustrous gurgling sound. Just south of the river a twisting trail darts along the riverside. The foreshore is buzzing with insects playing in the rich and varied plantlife whilst enjoying the comfortable access to water.
13059:
A water moccasin slithers out of sight just below the surface of the water.
A water moccasin slithers out of sight just below the surface of the water.
A green frog is here, hopping around.

The river slowly flows northwards through the green plains. The water is very calm, especially here in the middle. The water is more turbulent near the strands where rocks are hidden beneath the surface. A small trail follows the south shore of the river.
13060: The hills continue as before sprinkled with short grass and a few holly bushes. From this vantage point, a small village can be seen many miles to the north and east. While movement to the east, north and south is not impeded, a large boulder inhibits direct movement towards the west.
13061:
A shrub with maple-like leaves is growing here.
On the shrub, there are two handfuls of blackcurrant berries.

The trail follows the slowly flowing waters of the river Glanduin closely, as it dwindles through the Dunland plains. The grass is brilliantly green, and some willow trees extend slim branches over the water. In the south-west you see a hill rising from the grassy plains, and west there are some thick bushes hiding whatever lies behind them.
13062:
A small campfire burns here, its low flames giving off only a little light.
A lonely man tries to hide in the grass.

Hidden in a little bushy hollow there is a small campfire. Glowing coals spread a little light, and no smoke rises toward the sky. Someone must have lit it recently, but now the place is deserted. Some bushes between the fire and the trail would hide it completely from that direction, but the light would likely be spotted from the hill in the south-west.
13063: The grass grows very high here completely covering the soft ground it rests upon. The green carpet continues up on the hills directly south west giving them a soft appearance. On the hill in the west you see an old tower that overlooks the surrounding plains.
13064: On the Slope to the Hill
A grey wolf is here, salivating profusely.

Rocks and boulders are scattered on the slope making movement slow and a little treacherous. The grass that grows here seems to wither away further up, on the exposed hilltop, but is deeply green near the base of the hill. A little tower crowns the hill west, overlooking the flats around. A small chain of hills runs out southeast from here, rolling across the plains for many miles.
13065: You are a few steps south of an ancient wooden tower, its doors lying broken on the ground before you. The hill and the tower atop dominate the flat grasslands below, giving a magnificent view, but climbing the stairs could reward you with an even better one.
13066: A beautiful and docile horse is standing here.

The trail runs north and south through the great plains of Dunland. It has been here a long time, never overgrown even though it is now little used. The stony route it takes does not yield well to undergrowth, and little but small hardy shrubs grow here. To the west are grass-covered plains as far as the eye can see, while up the hillside east is an old dilapidated tower.
13067: The vision of the wetland fades to the west as it becomes enshrouded by a deep mist. To the northwest you can see the shape of some sort of stone building, and to the northeast you can see a secluded area with a dense population of trees. From all around you, the loud cries of wolves can be heard. The low howl, which is more of a soft growl, should advise you to proceed with caution. The hills continue to the east, while a faint trail leads off to the south.
13068: Rough land lies all around you; bleak silence interrupted only by the distant cries of wolves. The wetlands are crossed by narrow faint tracks leading to the north-east and north-west where there are a few old huts. To the east there is a dark enclosure of trees. The stillness of those trees to the east should make you feel uneasy. To the south a broken wooden tower sits atop a low hill.
13069: The land, rich and fertile, has grown wildly and unconstrained, covering every part of the ground. The layer of vegetation cushions your footfalls, but makes it easy to trip over the thin stems and tree roots that litter the ground. A few stunted trees have grown here, striving against the wind and rocky hills to survive. To the north a narrow path leads to the east and west, straight into a dark dell of the east. However, here, movement to the east is blocked by the thick vegetation.
13070: Grass and weeds cover the lands besides the Glanduin river in bright green. A purling sound reaches you from the river to the south and west, but north and east the quiet plains expand far into the horizon. Grubs and beetles enjoy the moist soil and the cool shadow under the vegetation. On the south side of the river rise the ruins of an old village, which is accessible via a ford.
13071: Fields of grass, weeds and flowers span far into the northern horizon, waving and bowing to the wind the green vision turns into a distant memory of the sea. A sound of purling water, coming from the south, completes the image and for a little while one may dream of the ocean shores so far away. Clusters of blue violets spring forth as comforting waypoints on the journey through the intriguing flora. The joyful gurgle of the river accompanies you mile after mile as your travel continues.
13072: Green fields span across the horizon with waving grass and a few scattered bushes. A small hill stands solemnly a few feet off the level of the plains, its gently slanting side covered in coarse grass that rattles in the wind. The view from the top is excellent and allows you to see far north across the open plains of southern Eregion. Far to the east lie the mountains in their stunning glory with snow-capped peaks. A few miles to the south the Glanduin river can be seen running west towards the Sea far away.
13073: The plains slope gently in every direction without any significant landmarks in the immediate vicinity. Green grass, nourished by the fertile soil, grows in dense banks everywhere, and in some places reaching heights of more than two feet. A hawk soars high in the sky, its keen eyes searching for small rodents to catch. Although the country is mainly flat, you observe a small elevation to the south.
13074: The downs are vegetated mainly by grass and weeds. Only occasional bushes break the monotone and endless sea of grass, and while rare there are also small flowers to be found whenever the grass retreats. While fairly level, the fields appears more hilly to the south where a ridge rise a couple of miles away.
13075:
There is a huge, pyramidal beehive here.
The bee flies around here, collecting nectar from the flowers.
The bee flies around here, collecting nectar from the flowers.

Wild green grass vegetates the downs in southern Eregion. Sloping gently the downs continues in all directions seemingly endlessly. Among the grass you spot many different types of wild flowers and berries, especially the holly bushes thrive well. A buzzing and humming rise from among the grass, bees are busy gathering nectar.
13076: Waist-high grass with intermittent wild flowers chracterizes the vegetation in the green downs. Although the grass is dominant, the fecund soil provides excellent conditions for other plants as well. Various sedges and club moss are quite common too, especially the shorter kinds. The otherwise level ground begins a slow climb to the east where a slope leads up a small mound.
13077: A mound rises from the fertile soil. Elevated about fifteen feet from the level of the surrounding plains it provides an excellent view of the lands north of the Glanduin river. In the east the misty mountains rise in clear silouette against the sky. Further south the river is seen as a clear dark line before the plains turns into a thick forest. North and west the grass- laden plains continue, seemingly forever.
13078: A fishing rod has been left here.

This small, grass-covered ridge rises gently out of the countryside. Many small bushes cover the area, making progress to the west difficult. Though there is a sporadic covering of grass, few animals appear to frequent the area. The ridge continues off to the south and west before melting back into the plains of Dunland.
13079: The ground slowly slopes upwards to the south and east where a narrow ridge forms. From here a burned hut can be seen some three miles to the northwest and another ten miles beyond the hut a small village. The ground is covered with coarse thick grass that easily masks the passage of wildlife.
13081:
An apple tree with bright green leaves grows here.
On the tree's branches are three apples.

Upon these plains, which are littered with grass and small bushes, this singular tree has managed to grow. Even though the tree flourishes and is often laden with fruit, not only is this tree the only one to be seen, it appears that not even a sapling has managed to sprout for many years. To the west and north of here a small water hole can be seen while to the east a hill begins to form.
13082: The grass has gradually become shorter and more dense then the regions to the north, west and east. In areas, the rough ground peaks through the grass forming a harsh contrast between the bright green blades and the dark brown soil. While a path does not exist, there are various small trails headed north towards a large water hole and towards the east a single large tree has placed its mark upon these plains.
13083: For unknown reasons, life avoids this section of the plains. The grass appears normal, though the tips are strangely browned and the stalks tougher then one would expect. Nothing but empty plains can be seen in all directions, the tall grass blocking the view for many miles. Though, to the distant west some rolling hills begin to take shape.
13084: An elk cow gazes coldly at you, chewing on a small branch.

The plains here continue unblemished. The grass is long and straight, every blade unbroken, free to swirl in the wind. To the west the plains continue as they do to the north and south. However, towards the east, while the land continues to be level, the region becomes barren.
13085:
A small child is here playing happily.
A goat is here, grazing in the hills.
A goat is here, grazing in the hills.
A goat is here, grazing in the hills.

The flat plains form a sharp contrast to the more hilly terrain north and west. The plains continue to the south and east but nothing of interest seems to mark those regions. From here, little can be seen of a small village to the north.
13086: Upon a slope, the terrain climbs slightly to the south and west while it falls to the north. East, the region flattens out forming a level plain. A few bushes are loosely scattered across the hill side interwined with short grass and a few clovers. A few scattered footprints of elks can be seen in soft ground but none are recent.
13087:
A large beautiful rose bush is blooming here.
Deep inside the bush, there are two red roses with leaves and thorny stems.
A brown fox is here, looking for some rabbits to chew up.

The land here is a series of low swells, rising just above the level of the surrounding plains. Ankle-deep grass covers the ground underfoot, but the land is hidden more by the plentiful bushes and shrubs in the area than the grass. The ground slopes gently upwards to the north, cresting a ridge.
13088:
The garden snake slithers harmlessly here.
A robin is here, carrying small pieces of wood to its nest.

The ground here is generally flat, though there are small swells to the land. A high covering of tall grasses covers the land, rising above knee level. Goldenrod is mixed in with the grass, creating a mixture of green and bright yellow. Slight breezes cause the entire landscape to shudder and move, creating a hypnotic wave-like pattern.
13089:
Some cereals that look like wheat are lying here.
The garden snake slithers harmlessly here.

While the majority of the land here is flat, the ground slopes upwards to the north, forming a hill. The ground is covered with a mixture of hay and tall grasses, growing to waist height. While no flowers can compete for sunlight against this tall vegetation, goldenrod grows in profusion, showering the area with a shimmering layer of yellow.
13090:
A small cluster of clover grows here.
A robin is here, carrying small pieces of wood to its nest.

This low and long hill runs from the east to the west, creating a large ridge in the plains. The lower slopes are covered by hay, which thins out as the hill rises. The remainder of this knoll has a green layer of grass across its entire length, with patches of clover growing in places. This raised vantage allows for a fairly good view of the surrounding land.
13091: Some cereals that look like wheat are lying here.

This area is completely covered by tall hay which rises more than waist-high. There is an occasional sign of animal life, from meandering paths in the vegetation to droppings. Despite the thriving growth, many rocks litter the ground. A slope rises above the plains to the south, getting progressively more steep.
13092:
Some cereals that look like wheat are lying here.
A restless rabbit bounces around.
A goat is here, grazing in the hills.
A young goat playfully charges and hops away.
A young goat playfully charges and hops away.

A high layer of hay and wild grains covers the ground, which swells slightly at intermittent intervals. The dips in the ground shelter clusters of bushes, which grow huddled together. There are a series of small holes dug into the ground, with little mounds of excavated dirt marking their openings.
13093: There are two piles of wheat cereals here.

Some bushes dot the area to the north, thinning out and stopping as the ground becomes level. A thin strip of grass lies between the end of the bushes and the wild hay that grows to the chest height of a man. This area seems to be seldom visited by animals, for the hay is strangely undisturbed. To the west, down a steep bank, flows a clear river.
13094: The Riverbed leads to the north and west here, seeming to become slightly more clear as if some fresh source of water added to its flow from somewhere to the north. The clearer flow still contains little life though as it continues its slow movement across the land. You may climb onto the riverbank to the north or follow the bed to the east or west.
13095: As you move along the riverbed of the once mighty Sirannon all your cares and worries just seem to vanish. The stream flowing north and west is very comforting and you may follow it in both directions.
13096: This place on the riverbank of the once proud river Sirannon is very tranquil indeed. There are birds in the trees, and the insects enjoying the muddy waters to the north. The riverbed lies to the north and the riverbank continues to the west.
13097: The banks of the riverbed move apart here where the flow of the river must once have been very wide. There is not much movement below the surface of the small stream the river has become now, the lack of water causing most of the waterbourne life to die or move long ago. The river continues east and south.
13098: A small breeze keeps the smell of the muddy riverbed away from you here. The riverbed leads east and west. A small tributary comes from the south, joining forces with the once very mighty Sirannon.
13099: Still the river twists and turns, having shaped the surrounding land to it's will. This particular bend in the river is to the west and north, and is still bordered by hills to the south, which are not quite accessible from here. To the north-west is an ancient track, and it seems that the streambed is shallow enough that you can clamber up onto it as well.
13100: A black catfish is here, lurking in the mud.

The clear river, cutting through the Hollin Hills, brings more water to the sandy riverbed north. The water, flowing from the sprinkled hills to the south, is a trickle of clear water running down the middle of this riverbed. To the south, the Hollin hills can be reached and to the west, some faint animal tracks can be seen. Far in the east, the Misty Mountains can be seen with their menacing snow-covered peaks.
13101: The river flows north and south, coming from the luxuriant forested hills to the east. The clear water mirrors the various lush vegetation growing along the riverbanks. To the south and west, peculiar-looking, red dotted hills can be seen. Far to the east, the Misty Mountains, which appears purple as they rise to meet the sky in the distance, are capped by glistening white.
13102: A black catfish is here, lurking in the mud.

The river flows north, coming from the luxuriant forested hills east. The clear water sprays a lush vegetation growing on the banks. To the south and west, peculiar-looking, hills can be seen, while to the far east, the Misty Mountains can be seen, with their awe-inspiring peaks looming above the land.
13103: In this bed the Sirannon continues on its neverending trek to find the sea. The land does not seem to have suffered at all, still looking well-watered. From here it is possible to continue along the meandering streambed. To the north seems to be an old overgrown road that might be worth exploring.
13104: The streambed makes a slow bend here, continuing to the north and west. The landscape surrounding the waterway is quite breathtaking, with the lush hills and forest to the north, and the majesty of the snow-capped mountains looming far in the east. Dwarf and Elf alike chose their homes of old well indeed.
13105: Here the shallow bed makes yet another bend, this time to the south and east. There is lush greenery all around, particularly to the north of the river, where lie hills adorned with wildflowers of various shapes, sizes, and colours. Even the slightly more desolate lands visible to the south have more than their share of the vibrant Hollinish flora.
13106: What a picturesque scene this must have been before the stream was slowed down, with the vibrant colours and the mountains in the hazy distance. Even now that the Sirannon has decreased its flow, the landscape is still lovely indeed. It is no wonder the Elves of ages past chose this to be their home on this side of the sea.
13107: There is some snow on the ground.

On and on the shallow bed continues. All of the flora greets your eye with vibrant colour, except for a few dead plants. Up to the north is an ancient track, and is seems that the streambed is shallow enough that you clamber onto it.
13108: A fierce boar is here, making grunting noises.

The land here its in a slight depression, seeming even lower because of the high ridge to the east. The soil is thick and slightly damp, due to the river running to the west of here. Patches of moss and weeds grow between the heavy layers of bushes that abound here. There is a definite slope to the east, which rises to form a high ridge. The land rises gently to the north and south to become level with the plains.
13109:
A large dangerous looking green snake is coiled up here.
A dun-coloured grouse is sitting still in the heather.

This land rests in a small hollow, shaped by a ridge to the east and a vertical wall of rock to the north. Small coniferous trees dot the area, mostly by the cliff-face in the north. These trees give way to smaller bushes and shrubs to the south. Little grows under the heavy layer of needles underneath the trees, but a constant and green layer of grass covers the rest of the area.
13110:
A holly bush with dark green leaves is growing here.
Partly covered by the bush's green leaves, there are a few inkberries.

You walk easily on a wide track, which runs alongside the dried Sirannon. This once may have been a well-kept and well-travelled thoroughfare, but since the fall of Ost-in-Edhil it has become somewhat overgrown with low grasses. You can't help but smile as you look at your peaceful surroundings, with the shallow streambed continuing to the south of you, and some rugged hills further north. As you look to the east your eyes linger for a moment on the mighty mountains of Moria: Caradhras, Celebdil, and Fanuidhol.
13111:
A bright green holly bush is growing here.
Partly covered by the bush's green leaves, there are some hollyberries.

The track bends here, seemingly at the mercy of the streambed winding to the east and south. The local flora here is lush and well-watered, thanks to the generous rainfall this area must recieve. Even the rugged hills to the north are not lacking in foliage of vibrant green and various wildflowers of all colours and hues. You see also a number of animals, but nothing you immediately discern as being threatening to your presence here. To the north your way is blocked by some bushes overgrown with thick holly and thistles.
13112: The old road continues south and east following the path of the dried-up Sirannon. There is some small hills just north of here. The wind picks up blows the dust around you making you cough and splutter. To the west you can see the road winding its way down into the valley.
13113: The road here is quite dusty and the wind continually picks up the dust and whips it around you, making you cough and splutter. There are some hills to the north with the path leading off towards them.
13114: Looking north from here you can see a path leading off alongside the stream. The track still continues east and west and seems to be used a bit more on this side as there are many tracks leading in both directions.
13116: The road bends east and south here as it follows the banks of the riverbed of the Sirannon. Looking to the east you can see the mountains rising up, but those are many leagues away at the moment. The road is crisscrossed with many footprints and tracks of animals. A small track enters the woods to the west.
13117: The road bends to the north here and you can see the river bank to the east. Looking east you can see the bed of the old Sirannon river winding its way up towards Caradhras and the Misty Mountains. You can see many prints that have been set in the mud before you travelled along this track.
13118: A swarm of mosquitoes is here, humming around you.

The hedgerow is quite dense here and the animals cross your path contimually. You can see the track to the north, and plains open up to your east. Looking at the ground, you can see many tracks in the dirt. There seems to be an old tributary of the Sirannon here.
13119: The river must once have been much wider here but now the water flows as three different narrow streams, all being easily crossed by foot. This must once have been a very peaceful stretch of the river, but now the mud and decomposing insects make the smell almost unbearable. The riverbed continues east and west.
13120: The road continues as far as you can see, running parallel to the riverbed of the Sirannon. There is a vibracy and life in the air here, heightened by the presence of the local wildlife, and the singing of the many types of birds that inhabit the land. However you realise that you are not terribly far now from Moria, the once great dwarven home of Khazad-dum. Indeed, the shadows of Caradhras, Celebdil, and Fanuidhol already lie across these lands, dampening the carefree feeling in the air, and making the atmosphere more somber.
13121: You are on an old track that was once a major thoroughfare for travellers to and from Ost-in-Edhil, the achitectural wonder built by the Gwaith- i-Mirdain. The road has since fallen into somewhat of a state of disrepair, and is overgrown in several spots. The track runs on the north side of the Sirannon, and to the south of the riverbed you see the Dunlandish wilderness. The mountains of Moria, known to humans as Redhorn, Silvertine, and Cloudyhead, dominate the landscape to the east, towering above you even though they are still quite a distance off.
13122: These green hills start to rise up around you and you can see them rising higher to the north. Looking south you can see the small hills as they head down towards the road. The grass is very lush here and was probably used for grazing some time ago. You can follow the hills to the north and south, or go onto a path to the west.
13123:
A Dunlending outrider, wielding a short spear, is here, riding a trained horse.
A Dunlending outrider, wielding a broad spear, is here, riding a trained horse.
A Dunlending outrider, wielding a broad spear, is here, riding a trained horse.

You are well into the hills now, and on either side the lush, green hills rise above you. To the south you can see the road and the riverbed of the Sirannon winding its way through this region. The air is fresh and clean, but you seem to sense an uneasiness in the land itself, as if it is still not at peace with itself. You can go north and south through the hills, or west onto a path.
13124: The hills begin to rise quite steeply around you here. To the east is a small cabin with smoke rising in a column from the chimney. There are footprints leading in and out of the cabin suggesting that it is used quite frequently. The air is clean, the grass green, and all is at peace. The exits are east, north, and south.
13125:
A large stone fireplace with a roaring fire warms the room.
A tall and strong hunter is standing here.

This is a small, well kept cabin used by the areas hunters. In the centre of the room there is a table with chairs sitting around it. Along the walls are shelves stocked with provisions for those who did not hunt well and have returned empty handed. A fireplace dominates the eastern wall.
13126: The hills in this country are very quiet. Most of them are covered with dense grass. The others are covered by a clear wood. The area is very quiet and should be a good hunting area.
13127: The hills rise up all around you, and you notice a small path leading west. Looking along this path as it twists its way round the hills, you notice that there are very few tracks of any kind on it. You are quite content as the lush grass is soft underfoot. You can go south and north.
13128: A fallow deer is grazing peacefully here.

The grass here is very green and very juicy looking. There are some animals grazing around you, and you feel completely at ease. Then again you should always be on the lookout for trouble as it could lie round every bend. The hills continue south and west.
13129: The hills rise up all around you, and you notice a small path leading west. Looking along this path as it twists its way round the hills, you notice that there are very few tracks of any kind on it. You are quite content as the lush grass is soft underfoot. You can go east and west.
13130: The hills rise up all around you, and you notice a path leading west. Looking along this path as it twists its way around the hills, you notice that there are very few tracks of any kind on it. You are quite content as the lush grass is soft underfoot.
13131: A fallow deer is grazing peacefully here.

The hills still rise up around you, but the path has become more defined and begins to head down a gentle slope into a valley. The tracks on the path have become more numerous and it seems to be leading to a watering hole of some kind. You can go south and east.
13132: You follow this path down, and the further you go the steeper it gets. Small streams trickle down beside you and the sound of falling water can be heard ahead of you, although not very loud over the sound of the wind. There are many other tracks on the path, but they are unrecognisable as they are all one on top of the other. You can go east and north.
13133: You enter the remains of a farmhouse which by the looks of things was destroyed long ago. Only a few walls remain along with the chimney stack. Looking around you find only the odd remnant of furniture, a carved table and chairs along with a few pieces of cutlery. The only exit is back to the west.
13134: A giant rat patters against you, squeaking maliciously.

A long time ago this field must have been used for grazing, but looking at the dead clumps of grass you can see this is not so now. There is an air of emptiness surrounding you and you feel very open and vulnerable. Looking to the east you can see a ruined farmhouse, and the foothills rise up to the south.
13135: A cockroach is scuttling across the floor carrying some debris.

The hills rise up all around you, and you soon begin to lose your sense of direction. The lush grass that grows around your feet is criss-crossed by many small trails. On examining these trails you see that small trails don't always mean small creatures as there are some rather large footprints in the mud. Caution may be best advised here until you can work out where you are.
13136: The green grass grows all around you. In and amongst this greenary you notice several large droppings and begin to wonder what could have made anything that large. The area seems very naturally lush here though, and little danger is apparent.
13137: The hills are smaller here and the grass all around has a trampled look to it. There are some footprints leading to the north but then they just seem to disappear. Some of the grass has been cut up and there are bits of turf and sod lying all around. The hills continue east and south.
13138: The hills rise up very steeply to the south and west blocking all passage in those directions. The lush grass that grows all around has some large footprints in it. The hills continue east and north.
13139: The hills rise up all around you, and you soon begin to lose your sense of direction. The lush grass that grows around your feet is criss-crossed by many small trails. On examining these trails you see that small trails don't always mean small creatures as there are some rather large footprints in the mud. Caution may be best advised here until you can work out where you are.
13140: The hills begin to rise up and your path has many animal tracks crossing it, as well as some very large footprints. You begin to lose your sense of direction but can still see a few buildings to your east. The ground tremors slightly in what seems to be all directions. The hills continue north and west.
13141: This is the western end of a small range of low hills lying to the north of an area of open plains. The hill range rises up higher to the north, into an area of rolling hills where the vegetation seems to be more abundant than the low shrubs on this hillside.
13142: A sharp-eyed hawk is here stalking some prey.

This area of open plain is bounded by thick bushes to the west and south. A low range of hills rise up to the north and continue eastwards, but the ground to the immediate east is much flatter. The vegetation in this area probably contains plenty of wildlife that could provide a skilled hunter with some to eat.
13143:
A brown fox is here, looking for some rabbits to chew up.
A brown fox is here, looking for some rabbits to chew up.

This piece of open ground before the old wooden gate may once have been a cultivated field or part of a rough marketplace set up beside the river. A dock of some kind lies to the east and and small tower has been built to the west. Looking northwards you can see the ground slowly rising up into some rolling hills in the distance.
13144: You pick your way over the rotten planks that used to make up this jetty. It certainly doesn't look safe and it would be a good idea to leave as soon as possible. Looking around you can see the remains of a few boats and looking out into the dried-up riverbed you can see the half-sunken remains of a barge, buried in the silt. Somebody was leaving in a hurry and didn't make it.
13145: The riverbanks widen here as they lead towards an area of the riverbed which must once have been some type of ford. The smell of rotting vegetation is not quite as strong now, but the swift flow of this stream must have once been much more comforting than what it has become. To the west an old landing platform for barges is perched on the riverbank, but you can't climb onto it from here.
13146: It's along the riverbank that this path runs. Looking down at your feet you can see many animal and human tracks. There are insects flying over the muddy riverbed to the west and everything is at peace. The track is south from here and the path continues north.
13147: This gentle path rambles on northward with an area leading down to the dry riverbed to the west. Around you the birds are singing and small animals scurry here and there, mindless of your presence. To the east you can see some hills rise up into the sky. You can go north and south along the path, with the riverbed to the west, and some hills to the east.
13148: This gentle path runs along parallel to the stream. Along the riverbank can be seen the local wildlife going about their daily business. Everything seems to be at peace here; there is little movement along the dried-up river now. The desperate spawning attempts of the salmon long ago ceased on this stretch of river. The path continues north and south.
13149: The path arrives at an old building of a small size which seems to come out of nowhere. The building itself seems to be in a very bad state of repair, with many cracks in the walls. To the west the path drops down to a small landing where a few small boats could have been tethered had the river not dried-up long ago. The path continues to the south.
13150: The wooden walls of this tavern are beginning to rot away leaving cracks for the wind to howl through. The old casks that served this place smell of their foul and rotted contents. A few old stools still stand by the bar, a simple thing made of some tan coloured wood. You may go back through the door to the south or north onto the deck.
13152: A clear spring babbles as cool water trickles out of the ground.

You enter a peaceful glade, and everything seems to be so calm - not even a ripple on the pond before you. Huge old willows gently dip their branches into the still waters. This must be the source of one of the streams that add to the trickle that the once great river Sirannon has become. You can go west and north to the hills, and south to the riverbed itself.
13153: A trickle of water coming from the north makes the muddy stream slightly clearer here, but it is still only a meagre flow compared to the mighty river that once carried sail-barges. The teeming waterlife of the stream has also died, leaving behind little but a muddy ravine in the lands.
13154: The loss of the waters in this once fast-flowing river must have had an awful impact on the surrounding peoples who would have relied on the supply of fish it provided for food and income. The trickle of muddy water can do little to support any life now, in fact the only movement you can see is that of mosquitos breeding above the foetid waters.
13155: A swarm of mosquitoes is here, humming around you.

The pathetic flow of the Sirannon's tributary continues along the riverbed between the riverbanks here. There is no wildlife to see in the ravine at this point, the fish having died long ago when the waters began to run low. The riverbed leads to the north and south.
13156: A swarm of mosquitoes is here, humming around you.

A breeze brings the foul smell of the rotting matter on the riverbed to your nostrils as you wander along the damp riverbed. The decaying vegetation, brought downstream from far away makes the stream take on a rusty-brown colour as it continues it slow flow southwards.
13157: A brown fox is here, looking for some rabbits to chew up.

This flat area is covered in rough grasses and small patches of low vegetation. To the north the land begins to rise up into an area of more hilly terrain, and to the east you can enter a dried-up riverbed of some kind. To the west the flat ground continues, but southwest of you somewhere you can make out a short tower.
13158: A boar cub is playing here, and exploring the wide world.

The land becomes slightly hilly here, rising up from the flat ground to the south and west, and towering above the dried-up riverbed of some stream to the east. You may move onto the riverbank itself to the north, or between the banks to the east. There is little wildlife apparent here, but the area is obviously not devoid of life as some animal tracks of some kind cross this area of the hills.
13159: On the Bank of the Dried-up River

This place seems to be very peaceful and you feel you could spend the rest of your life here absorbing the tranquil atmosphere, but in the dark recesses of your mind you feel the urge to press on. As you prepare to leave you wonder why the once mighty river Sirannon and its tributary has now dried-up to become the small trickle it is.
13160: As you leave the lower ground to the south of you, the foothills begin to rise up around you. The country is gently rolling and seems to be at peace as you move higher. The grass grows up around your knees and gently sways in the breeze. It must have been a long time after the Dark Lord laid waste to this area, for the land has regenerated itself and is now calm. To the west you can see the rolling hills rise up and lead off into the distance, to the north is an abandoned farm, to the east you can see the river bank and to the south the lower lying ground.
13161: You are standing in the middle of a small range of low hills that rise up further to the north. The hills also continue to the east and west, or you may move onto the lower ground to the south. The sparse vegetation on this hillside would not support many animals and there is little wildlife apparent here.
13162: This flat area of land is quite dry and would be very suitable to set up a place to rest. The plain lies just to the south of some hills that rise up further to the north. A dried-up stream is somewhere to the east of you, but more noticeable is a short tower to the southwest.
13163: A stone key with some strange runes lies here.

The smell down here is awful! Peering around in the gloom you can see that this room must be the cellar of the ruined farmhouse, but no one seems to use it now. A few broken barrels and casks lie here as well as the droppings of rats. The only exit is back up.
13164:
A big cavebear is padding around here.
A black spider crawls here, a shiny red spot visible on its belly.

This small, shallow cave is quite dry and sheltered, but not enough to prevent daylight to enter. Looking around, one notices some smoke marks on the walls where fires have been. Against the northern wall is a large flat slab of stone. The only exit seems to be south, but some etchings are on the wall, appearing to be runes of some sort.
13165:
The corpse of a crazed dwarf is lying here.
The corpse of a crazed dwarf is lying here.
The shadow of a crazed dwarf is floating here.
Norbert the Dwarf (NN), wielding a mighty dwarven axe, is resting here.
A strong and agile dales-pony is standing here.

This dark only sparsely lit by a few torches. The stone of the ground has been worn smooth by thousands of feet walking over it. Looking at the walls one can see that they have been painted and sculpted, but this must have been a long time ago as the plaster is crumbling and the paint peeling. The only exit is to the north.
13166: This is a dark hallway that is sparsely lit on either side by crude torches attached to the pillars. Eastwards and westwards the hall disappear into the darkness. This room was carved out of the rock with the great skill of the Dwarves from past ages. Most of this skill has long been forgotten along with this hallway as it would seem. The hallway runs north and south.
13167: The darkness here seems to be all consuming. You can hardly see past your own nose let alone the other side of the room. As you examine the walls you begin to realise how skilled the Dwarves really are. The walls are covered with cracked murals of events long ago. The darkness is impenetrable but you can see the hallway to the west.
13168: The darkness here seems to be all consuming. You can hardly see past your own nose let alone the other side of the room. As you examine the walls you begin to realise how skilled the Dwarves really are. The walls are covered with cracked murals of events long ago. The darkness is impenetrable but you can make out the torches in the hallway to the east.
13169: It is very dark here but you can still make out vague paintings on the walls as you near the sides of the room. The paintings have been done by an elven hand, because the artistry involved could never have been achieved by any Dwarf. You can still make out torches to the east.
13170:
The corpse of a black widow is lying here.
The corpse of a black widow is lying here.

The hallway continues its way, sparsely lit on either side by torches. The halls continues east and west disappearing off into the darkness. To the north a ring of torches and a large circular room can be seen. The hallway continues north and south.
13171: The walls of the hall seem to stretch on forever. All over the walls are paintings depicting battles from some time in the past. The hall seems to continue to the south and one can just make out a hallway to the east.
13172: You arrive in a room with a large shaft drilled into the floor in front of you. Set around this shaft is a steep spiral staircase. Following the staircase down are torches hung from the wall. The murals continue depicting battles and other occasions from the distant past. The exits are south and down.
13173:
The corpse of a black widow is lying here.
The corpse of a black widow is lying here.
Water drips slowly into a grey, still pool.

A depression in the rocks has collected a fair amount of a cool, clear water. Made possible by the constant seepage through the rock, the water seems to have a constant source. It looks and smells clean, naturally filtered by the sedimentary rock above. This must be where the Dwarves get their water needs every day. You wonder how people can stay down here for so long, but this seems to provide some explanation.
13174:
The corpse of a giant rat is lying here.
A greenish slime mould is here, smelling badly.
A greenish slime mould is here, smelling badly.
An iron pick has been dropped here.
A greenish slime mould is here, smelling badly.
A dwarven female is here walking around.

This seems to be the area where the dwarves who live in the mines congregate to eat their small snacks. The boulders lying on the caverns floor are worn smooth were they have been sat upon, and strange luminous slime covers parts of the walls where they have fed on discarded crumbs. The smell of vegetation comes from the south and to the east a cool damp breeze is felt.
13175:
A small mushroom grows nearby.
A small mushroom grows nearby.
A bright red mushroom is growing here.
A small mushroom grows nearby.
A small mushroom grows nearby.
A small mushroom grows nearby.
A small mushroom grows nearby.

The ground around you is covered in decaying vegetable matter that feeds the growth of the small white mushrooms of various sizes. The warmth generated by this decomposition keeps the chill of a breeze from the north to a minimum. The poor miners who are forced to survive on such food might just kill intruders just to steal their food for themselves.
13176:
Water drips slowly into a grey, still pool.
A dwarven miner is here, digging the hard rock with his pick.

As you enter the blackness you have to keep one hand on the wall so as you don't stray too far from something solid. The wall suddenly opens up to the east and you can smell some sort of vegetation from that direction. A cool draft of air suggests the caverns further to the east contain more water than the small pool on the floor beside the rock-face here.
13177: The passage continues north and south; there is also a tunnel to the east. It is very dark here, but one can see some light coming from the south. To the east there is the start of a tunnel, but it soon disappears into the darkness. The walls of the passage are smooth and have been well mined.
13178: This is the base of a ladder. The area surrounding the ladder is lit by torches hung on the walls but looking into the passage to the south, you are soon overwhelmed by the darkness. The ladder has been well crafted out of some hardwood and looks well cared for. The only exits are back up the ladder or the mine passage to the south.
13179:
The corpse of a crazed dwarf is lying here.
The corpse of a crazed dwarf is lying here.

The main thing here is the large round hole in the centre of the floor. Leaning against one side of the wall is a stout wooden ladder. Down into the darkness the base of the ladder is surrounded by lit torches. The ladder itself is well-done, with some hardwood and seems to be well cared for.
13180: This seems to be the end of the passage. In the southern wall is a large and sturdy looking door made out of some dark metal. Around the door, some torches hang illuminating the whole passage. The passage continues to the north.
13181:
Traces of fierce white tones form the aura of this place.
The corpse of a dwarven overseer is lying here.
A giant brick forge sits in the center of the room.
A horse of the Rohirrim (ulo) is standing here.
Staub the Dwarf (ST), wielding a mighty dwarven axe, is standing here.

This room is filled with maps and other papers. The dwarves who are working in this mine have carefully planned their operation in order to maximize the discovery and extraction of hidden jewels and precious metals from the foothills of the Misty Mountains. Some of the maps have fallen down and are covering most of an old tattered carpet.
13182:
The corpse of a black widow is lying here.
The corpse of a black widow is lying here.

You seemed to have reached a nexus in the tunnels. Most of the traffic travels north and west. The walls are covered in, what presumably are names, in a language that you can't read. The ways south and west are partially blocked off with barriers.
13183: The tunnel bends south and west here. To the south one can see another ring of torches. The ground also slopes down towards the south. There are no paintings on the walls here and this tunnel looks newer than the rest, as the walls aren't as smooth as the others.
13184: An iron pick has been dropped here.

There is something not quite right about the darkness here, it seems to have a gradient quality to it, sometimes darker in places than others. The walls of the passage are well finished and the craftsmanship involved hasn't been seen for many years. There is also another tunnel leading off in that direction, otherwise the tunnel continues south.
13185: You enter a small side tunnel. It's very dark in here and the air is full of dust, making it very difficult to breathe. A few dwarves scurry back and forth past you, carrying armfulls of rock and ore. The tunnel continues to the west, and the main tunnel is to the east.
13186:
A dwarven miner is here, digging the hard rock with his pick.
A dwarven miner is here, digging the hard rock with his pick.

You arrive at what must be the rock face. There are few miners busy digging and smashing the rock up; they seem to take no notice of you. The air here is very stale and full of dust making it hard to breathe; you wonder how anyone could work under these conditions. The tunnel runs back to the east.
13187: At the Base of the Stairs

This part of the mine is very old : the walls are all very smooth and polished. The passageway disappears off intho the darkness to the south. The stairs, that lead up, are made of strong wood. Some torches are firmly fixed onto the wall.
13188: A wooden chest stands in the corner.

This is obviously a treasure chamber. All around the walls take on a golden hue. The large chamber contains little wealth now but empty chests line the walls. A faint glow issues from one of these which perhaps contains the remnants of the dwarves' wealth. The only exit is back up into what looks like an operations room.
13189: The trail, bounded by the Hollin hills to the west and north and a river to the east seems to lead in only one direction, south. The ground is covered with a low growing foliage, mostly grass, and a few fallen twigs. The hills to the west and north are covered with holly bushes while the river, to the east, is crystal clear.
13190: The trail, formed by animal tracks, continues in a northern-southern direction from here. The trail is hard to discern, as its infrequent usage has allowed the vegetation to grow freely over it. To the west are the Hollin hills, covered by berry producing holly bushes, to the east is a small river.
13191: Here, the tracks vanish under the lush vegetation, making it impossible to follow the trail to the south. It seems that a much older trail, one used by men, used to head eastwards, but has been engulfed by the nearby river when its changed course. All around you, to the south and west, are the Hollin hills as they stretch for miles. You can follow the trail to the north as it separates the hills to the west and the river to the east.
13192:
A wild bull seems ready to charge you.
A wild bull is sleeping here.

The Hollin plain continue equally in all direction, and to the east a line of trampled grass can be seen. Near to the north, the river Sirannon can be heard, and just beyond the river, even from here, the remains of an ancient road can be seen.
13193: These plains, lush indeed, are veiled by an abundance of low growing but hardy holly bushes. Only a moderate amount of rainfall is required for these thorny, colourful plants to flourish. To the south-west, more of the ruddy hills of Hollin continue. To the north, the Sirannon - by now a small river - makes its way steadily toward the west.
13194:
A clean fragrance drifts up from a thick clump of leaves.
A beautiful and docile horse is standing here.
