Tattered and frayed, it appears to have once cushioned visitors' knees as they paid homage to the elven smiths. The walls are adorned with many finely engraved murals and designs depicting the history of the Noldor.
13356: A long rectangular stone table takes up much of the area of this small room. A large hand-blown glass chandelier casts a pattern of soft circular lights on the tabletop. Five carved stone chairs are carefully tucked under each side of the table ready to seat the elves long ago gone from this place. A tall chair at the southern end of the table commands a great presence over the rest of the table. Unlike the other rooms in these halls, the walls here are barren, giving evidence this was a place for serious discussions and distractions, even those of the simplest kind, were unwarranted. To the north lie two large metal doors; when closed their smooth surfaces line up perfectly with this chambers walls.
13357: This spiral staircase made of iron is so well constructed that even under the weight of those using it, it makes no creaking sounds. The forty steps follow a precise and equidistant cascading arrangement. A slightly tarnished silver handrail, made from one piece of precisely curved metal, follows the steps from top to bottom. This stairway was clearly designed to take up very little room, entirely contained in a five-foot wide cylindrical space. This hides it well behind the wall of water a bit to the south. From the other side of the water the staircase is completely concealed. Several people could use these steps at the same time single file in the same direction, however passage up and down simultaneously would be impossible.
13358:
A shiny gold ring has been abandoned here.
A longsword is on the ground.

From this short curved hall one can see the spiral staircase to the west and the wall of water just inside the room to the south. Along the carved granite walls are several square shaped insets about a foot deep. Inside one of the showcases are hooks and fasteners about the right size to have held swords and knives on display. Another looks as if a shield could have been displayed in its recess. The third inset is much smaller then the other two, seemingly to display jewellery, judging by its size and some narrow platforms set within.
13359:
A malevolent bat hangs from the ceiling.
A malevolent bat hangs from the ceiling.
A malevolent bat hangs from the ceiling.

This spacious, carved granite workshop once housed all that was necessary to take raw materials and craft them into works of art. A small, extinguished forge extrudes from the west wall. Row upon row of miniature pegs line the sides of the room securing detailing tools needed for the task of smithing. Wooden workbenches lie splintered about in ruins. The great treasures that were undoubtedly housed here vanished long ago, still there might be some small items that were overlooked.
13360: The air is humid in this place far below the great elven city. The only light sources are the dim blue flames from tiny iron lanterns that hang just below where the west wall meets the domed ceiling. The eastern edge of this wide granite platform shows a bit of wear from the rush of the natural water forcefully redirected through this channel of elven make. Carved out of the western wall is an elegantly arched doorway. Deeply etched runes provide a decorative border around the frame of this doorway.
13361: This delicate looking bridge is a work of art as well as function. Suspended above the watery channel it hangs from several woven chains. Each piece consisting of six finely crafted silver chains around an iron support rod. The walkway of the bridge is made of slats of heavy iron ore with fine silver folded over them several times. The entire presentation makes the bridge appear entirely made of silver. Adding to the illusion is the silvery reflection it casts on the water below. The fast flowing current stirs up a gentle breeze heading southward.
13362: From this dimly lit hall one can see straight across the elven-made channel to the west. The fast flowing water shoots through the circular conduit with such intensity that the western edge of this platform's granite floor has been forever smoothed by erosion. One of the tiles has broken loose, giving evidence that through neglect even the most well made of structures can fall prey to the elements. Two of the small iron lamps that run the course of the eastern wall are lacking their magical blue flames. A doorway carved out of the eastern wall is replete with runes surrounded by a decorative design.
13363:
A bloodthirsty bat is sleeping here.
A malevolent bat hangs from the ceiling.
A malevolent bat hangs from the ceiling.
A malevolent bat hangs from the ceiling.

The absence of tools and artifacts from this workshop might lead one to believe that any wealth once contained here has now departed. Whoever looted this shop seems to have been exceedingly interested in the detailing of gemstones. Several fractured bookshelves lie irreparable on the ground, stripped of any books they may have contained. Perhaps upon close examination some small setting of gold or silver might be found.
13364: A silver-scaled guardian stands poised for attack, exhaling a fiery breath.

Several wide granite steps lead from this hall down into the water filled channel to the west. Looking closer however, one can see that unlike the steps on the western side of the channel these are merely decorative, stopping just under the water level. The water rushes past this point with great intensity, yet very little of it ever escapes the conduit. The light from small blue flames in tiny lanterns lining the eastern wall casts a cool glow on the granite floor.
13365: This wide hall is bordered by a granite wall to the east and a water filled channel to the west. The air is humid and the rushing water creates a soft, cool wind through this enormous open area. The hall here matches the one west of the channel. The entire area shares the same curved ceiling that arches above the channel. It must have taken years for teams of elves to carve this conduit that diverts the water from a geyser north of here through this level of the underground. Cut right through the east wall is a doorway surrounded by deeply carved elven runes.
13366:
Several shards of broken glass lie scattered about the ground.
A malevolent bat hangs from the ceiling.
A malevolent bat hangs from the ceiling.
A malevolent bat hangs from the ceiling.
A bloodthirsty bat is sleeping here.

Glass globes, in two rows, line the ceiling of this intricate workshop giving off a soft white light. Along the back wall two furnaces used in the art of glassblowing lie dormant. Detailing tools are arranged haphazardly about the room amid the splintered remains of workbenches. Shards of multicoloured glass lie strewn about the shop causing the floor to sparkle.
13367: Beautiful silver chains shine above the mist as they support the swaying bridge of metal slats across the fast flowing water. The rush of water creates a cool wind blowing through this carved channel causing the metal bridge to clink from time to time like the ringing of tiny bells. Each section of chain is in actuality made up of six finely crafted silver chains around an iron support rod. The flat wide slats that make up the floor of the bridge are heavy iron ore with fine silver folded over them several times to feign the appearance of solid silver yet with the strength to support the elves as they crossed. A bridge of stone would surely have been sturdier but clearly the elves went to great lengths to practice their craft in constructing this work of art with function.
13368: Water flows through a channel just east of this wide platform. To the west is a large arched doorway cut into the granite wall. All down the sides and across the arch of the doorway are deeply carved elven runes. Small cast iron lamps, lining the space between the wall and ceiling, give off a soft light. Amazingly, their tiny blue flames show no source of being fed by oil or wood. Less than five of the lamps that line both of these great halls along the channel do not burn; they now are home to a few small spider webs. The ceiling curves upward to an arch above the channelled water and looks to curve back downward above a parallel ledge to this one far across the bridge to the east.
13369:
A large round whetstone rests on the ground.
A tarnished arrowhead lies discarded on the ground.
A bloodthirsty bat is sleeping here.
A malevolent bat hangs from the ceiling.
A malevolent bat hangs from the ceiling.
A malevolent bat hangs from the ceiling.

The dominating structure in this hollowed out workshop is a massive forge embedded into the western wall. Now dormant, this forge seems to have once been used to heat metals of varying sizes, before being hammered into shape on black anvils, arranged in a row down the centre of the shop. Looking upward, small air vents can been seen drawing air out from the chamber, providing a slight breeze. A fine layer of charcoal coloured soot covers the walls and floor.
13370: A silver-scaled guardian stands poised for attack, exhaling a fiery breath.

The small iron lanterns along the west wall provide light enough to see the cascade of granite steps that lead into the channel of water to the east. The tiny blue flames illuminate the water as it rushes over all but the top two steps. Looking over the edge of this platform it is clear to see the steps continue down, narrowing as they reach the bottom of the channel. Across the channel one can see identical steps leading down to the same underwater spot. Surely these stairs are not simply decorative and the water rushes too quickly for swimming. A long metal chain with a looping harness extends from the base of the first step.
13371:
A black snake hurries towards you with sly intentions.
A black snake hurries towards you with sly intentions.

This round concourse connecting the long halls at its north and south ends seems to have little other purpose than to create a more open environment than is common to places deep underground. A painted domed ceiling contributes to the illusion. Looking up one can see a pale blue sky with soft white clouds, so beautifully detailed only the absence of sunlight reveals the deception. Carvings in the walls resemble large mellyrn with pure gold leaf forming their delicate leaves. The moulding where the walls meet the floor has been shaped into small flowers, their petals kissed with shimmering silver leaf. Several park benches made of the palest granite line the walls. The sound of running water can be heard, accompanied by a cool draft emanating from the south.
13372: Two granite columns, smaller versions of the ones that line the hall above, mark the entrance to this lower level from the stairway to the north. The columns span the height of this corridor from the worn granite tile floor to the slightly arched ceiling. The stone walls, which one would expect to be cold this far underground, instead seems to carry a resonating warmth. Runes carved deep into the walls seem to have been burned into the stone rather than merely carved. Each letter is replete with black scoring making the letters stand out in colour from the wall itself. An arched doorway has been carved out of the solid granite of the western wall.
13373:
A black snake hurries towards you with sly intentions.
A sturdy pack horse is standing here.
A black snake hurries towards you with sly intentions.

Carved rectangular holes in the granite walls form compartments set into every wall in this room. Silver gates hang on hinges as doors to some of the larger sections. Other compartments have solid metal doors several inches thick. The doors however, were not strong enough to protect the safes' valuable contents from whomever ransacked this room. The floor is covered in broken bits of finely crafted objects made from silver, gold, and glass. Inside one of these gated cabinets is a thin metal blade, the metal has been folded over heat several times but it is nowhere near the thickness needed to do any damage. Clearly a useless unfinished work long ago abandoned.
13374: This small space is dominated by a long cylindrical stairway leading upward step by step in a spiral design. Made of iron, this well constructed stairway is firmly planted in the granite flooring, its only point of attachment at this level. The north wall behind the stairs has been carved at the same rate of curvature and polished smooth. The wall and the stair coexist without ever touching and are just far enough apart that an outstretched arm from the stair could not touch the wall.
13375: A stream of water several feet wide flows quickly down from an opening in the granite bluff just a short distance above. The cascade of water arches through the air about arms length from the side of the bluff to the north before crashing into the river at this point with tremendous force.
13376: Although this place is not far below the river surface, managing to get one's head above the water proves very difficult. The downward current created by the infusion of the water above continues to push anything floating here deeper and deeper. Looking north through clearer waters, a small natural lip extending just over the water's crest can be seen cut into the wall of the river bluff.
13377: This narrow channel leads north under the granite bluff upon which the old elven city stands. Natural in origin, it is just large enough for two people to swim side by side. Possibly a pocket of breathable air might exist further northward.
13378: The water is calm and clear yet gazing down through it there is no way to judge the depth. Looking upward, however, notably absent is the close granite roof that covered this passage to the south. What lies above is uncertain but it is the only option other than turning back southward.
13379: There is no air above the fast flowing water. Stretching out one's limbs, both the top and bottom of this chute can be touched. There is nothing, however, to grab hold of as...
13380: Water exits here through a hole carved out of the southern face of the granite bluff. Above is the old elven city of Ost-in-Edhil. Below a confluence of rivers and rocky outcroppings. A vertical stream of white frothy water carries everything flowing from the channel inside the bluff straight down to the waters below.
13381: The crystal clear water pushes southward without hesitation. About fifteen feet deep at its centre this conduit appears to redirect an underground geyser to a venting point close by. The granite channel walls are nicked in many places by what looks to have been metal weapons or perhaps even hooks, giving evidence that something or someone knew better than to let the current carry them any further.
13384: Only a finite amount of stale air fills the space between this pool of water and the mile of granite bluff bearing down on this cavern's roof. Once that air is gone it would take more time then one could survive waiting to replenish it. This perhaps may have been the fate of others who found this clandestine cave and faced the choice between running out of breathable air and drowning in the water below. A natural ledge, just wide enough to stand upon, surrounds this small underground pool of water to the south, east and west. Northward the cavern extends several yards.
13385: A skeleton of some humanoid lies in the dust.

This cavern seems to have been thoroughly searched by someone or something. Deep gashes in the walls indicate that the searchers were looking for some hidden entrance from here to the city of Ost-in-Edhil which lies more miles above. It is possible they believed this to be a secret place dug up into the granite bluff, however, looking closely one can see this whole cavern is a natural formation. Perhaps once there was a way for air to freely reach here. Now because of the channelled water above feeding the rivers to a higher water stage, this place is secluded from all others with only the one watery entrance to the south. The air is stale and with each breath there is less of it.
13386: Under the phosphorescent foamy crest of the waters rushing through this elven-made conduit the water is crystal clear. Holding one's breath while floating in about fifteen feet and looking downward through the rushing water one can see a solid metal door made of an unusual alloy; a mix of silver, iron and other metals. The current is very strong.
13387: Tordol the Dwarf (t), wielding a black waraxe, is standing here.

Encased in a chamber with four smooth granite walls, a squat ceiling and a grooved metallic floor, there is little to attract attention save for the reinforced metal door, with no apparent knob or handle, providing exit to the west. If examined closely tiny holes can be seen in the flooring, perhaps allowing water escaping in from the sliding metal panel above to flow out down below.
13388: Two slender polished handrails, reflecting the soft blue glow of lanterns running the length of this dimly lit corridor, assist travellers as they labour the sixty-three steps between two carved granite archways. This long passageway descends gradually from east to west. The smooth granite steps contain a continual etched pattern along the area where they meet the smooth stone walls. Other than these few decorative accents the stairway is rather simplistic.
13389:
A roughly stitched piece of green-grey cloth lies here.
An arrow lies on the ground.
An arrow lies on the ground.
A white marble statue stands silently guarding the threshold to the forge.
A white marble statue stands silently guarding the threshold to the forge.
Tarabaran the Dwarf (ta), wielding the Hammer of Belegost, is standing here.
Tordol the Dwarf (t), wielding a black waraxe, is standing here.

Strikingly, this chamber appears to have been untouched by the passage of time. Carved out of the granite and polished smooth the walls, floor, and ceiling are perfectly symmetrical. Skylight pours into the centre of the room through a large duct appearing to rise all the way up to the surface. Two tall archways, one leading north the other east, exit the room.
13390: Carved out of the granite rock this room is quite extraordinary. Where most rooms are filled with furniture and tools here the benches, the tool shelves and the forge itself are all part of the room, as if the creators sculpted out of the rock the area in which they would work and move. From the recess of the circular forge emanates a cool blue flame. It flickers just slightly, keeping an elegant shape, its tip white hot and its length reflecting its enchanted blue light on the walls.
13392: A stream of water several feet wide flows quickly down from an opening in the granite bluff just a short distance above. The cascade of water arches through the air about arms length from the side of the bluff to the north before crashing into the river at this point with tremendous force.
13393: A Dunlending woman is here tending to her children.

Leather skins line the inside walls of the small hut, keeping out drafts and other elements of bad weather. Through thin cracks formed between the outter plank lining of the hut, a small amount of daylight is allowed to penetrate inside. Several beds made of leather padding and furs are crowded together, taking up most of the room.
13394: This is the entrance of a seldom visited holly cave. The room is poorly lit by torches which are placed along the walls every few meters. The walls, blackened by the burning torches, have taken a dark grey hue, while the floor resembles a cobbled walkway. To the east, a cell door, which contains a small peephole, can be seen. The corridor continues to the north where it widens out and forms a larger cave.
13395: This is the entrance of a seldom used magic cave. The walls of this place are also dark grey in colour, but in several places painted motives have been drawn in red pigments. A faint breeze can be felt coming from another room to the south. The corridor continues to the north where it widens out and forms a cave, from which a strange religious feeling and an atmosphere of respect originates.
13396: An old Dunlending man is standing here.

Crude paintings cover the walls of the cave. They show the wild beasts hunted by the Dunlendings for either glory or food. Most of the paintings show the hunts of oxen, but they also show hunts of wolves, deer and bears. The main figure in one of the paintings is a large dark bear. The paintings are drawn using pigments such as coal and red argillite, taking advantage of the relief of the wall's surface. Following the lines of a protuberance in the wall, the mark of red hands can be seen just above some scattered human bones. At the foot of the wall, next to the bones, is a stone bowl which still contains the blood of a sacrificed prisoner.
13397: This is the prison cell where the Dunlendings keep those unfortunate travelers which have been captured. It is a dark and musky room, poorly light by a single torch provided near the door. There is a crude bed against one of the walls, and scattered litter across the floor, probably from former prisoners.
13398:
A large, dusty alcove sits in a wall, smelling of soot.
A rusty pickaxe with a broken handle lies discarded here.
A cockroach is sleeping here.
A cockroach is sleeping here.

Water basins, broken clay jars and empty bowls are scattered on the dirty floor, along with a stone anvil that was once used to crush wheat. This room, which used to be the kitchen of the palace, was designed to feed dozens of people at the same time. However, the kitchen has been pillaged and now looks as if a storm passed through it. The western wall, above the fireplace, is darkened by the huge fire which burned all the wooden furniture that once decorated this room.
13399: The main element of the room is this huge stone table, nearly 100 feet long, broken in its middle by a strong blow. In this place the former inhabitants of these halls had great banquets, and daily meals too. Four water bowls are at the four corners of the piece, dry now that the tubes have been filled up by the mud.
13400: A spirit floats towards you and howls with an evil laughter.

This immense Hall extends so far in every direction that it seems endless, for no walls are visible from here. The domed ceiling is supported by an seemingly infinite range of white pillars. Bas-reliefs were sculpted on them, but most have been scrupulously destroyed by heavy hammer blows. On those carvings that remain a fleet of four large ships can be recognised, each ship having a white tree figured on every sail.
13401: Lines after lines, dozens of carved pillars create an atmosphere of geometric beauty. Several of these columns are indeed sculptures representing the wise personalities who once walked in this hostel. Among those that can be recognised are Celebrimbor, builder of the palace, Galadriel and Celeborn who lived in Eregion for several centuries, and Aldarion with his captains, who first crossed the sea to visit the Noldor. While many of the statues have been hammered, they still stand. Now the elves are gone, cheated and hunted by Annatar, and only the lost souls of his fallen soldiers haunt these halls.
13402: In the middle of this colossal room stands an enormous pillar, which seems to enlarge the already large hall. The pillar is circled by a ring of stone tables, most of which have been destroyed. This hall, which must be more than 30 feet high, and no less than 3 furlongs long, has an extension east to a similar but somewhat smaller hall. The room continues north through through a narrow but extremely long tunnel.
13403: You stand in what is still a beautifully painted hall, with arched pillars to support the sculpted ceiling and marble benches around them. A high chair of pink marble dominates the room, before a wall of white stone streaked with silver. The ruin that fell on the place centuries ago was not sufficient to destroy the throne, but all the other stone furniture lay half broken on the floor.
13404: Greater parts of a broken weapon are lying on the ground.

This room, while big is empty, except for some garbage which litter the floor. It is a very long and wide hall, several dozens feet in each direction. The floor is marked by perpendicular lines, dug an inch into the ground. These lines are all that remains of wooden panels which once split this hall in separate apartments. Now the inhabitants are gone, and the place is haunted by the souls of the evil humans who died here under Sauron's leadership.
13405:
A rusty pickaxe with a broken handle lies discarded here.
A large round whetstone rests on the ground.

You stand in what used to be a workshop of the palace. Here, tools were mended and weapons were forged, and maybe even rings created. This room, now blackened from the fire which destroyed everything, once had a burning forge which emitted smoke through the chimney, while fresh air flowed through the small conduits. Both the conduits and the chimney are now filled with earth preventing exits through either one.
13406:
A large flat rock lies here, its surface etched with markings.
A black bear is sleeping here.

The long tunnel comes to a sudden end here, as the ceiling has collapsed under the weight of wet earth. Tiny bits of dirt fall on your head from spots in the unsupported ceiling, but roots seem to be holding together most of the ceiling preventing a total collapse. The passage east is blocked by a mass of earth and loose rocks.
13407: This tunnel, a dozen feet wide and high enough for a rider and his horse, is obviously artificial in construction, as the walls are straight and the floor level. However, the tunnel is partially filled with earth and moss is growing on the side indicating the tunnel is very old and probably abandoned. The tunnel extends to the north and west.
13408:
A bear is here, covered with coarse black fur.
A bear is here, covered with coarse black fur.

Threadbare stairs connect the surface with a deep passage. These stairs are enshrouded by earth and vegetation, and are recognisable as stairs only because recent rains have washed away some of the debris. They appear to be made of white marble, polished by many years of use.
13409: Little parts of a broken weapon are lying on the ground.

A long tunnel extends before you, dug in the calcarian rocks under the hills of Eregion. The floor had been expensively decorated by a mosaic, which displays the opulence of the former landlords. But in many places it has been mangled by evil hands, and muddy water flowing from the demolished ceiling partially covers it.
13410:
A rusty pickaxe with a broken handle lies discarded here.
A giant, mean looking earth beetle is standing here.
A cockroach is scuttling across the floor carrying some debris.

While to the south an extremely long corridor extends, you stand now in the crushed portal leading in a white Hall. The gate is more than five meters high, and was closed by two huge copper doors. They have been smashed by a outstanding force, and only one is still sadly suspended to the gate.
13411:
A giant, mean looking earth beetle is standing here.
A cockroach is scuttling across the floor carrying some debris.

Before you is a very wide Hall, dug in the hard rocks under Eregion. The walls are decorated with panels of white marble, and portentous sculptures have been carved in tablets of obsidian. On either side, carved pillars extend along the length of the room. Most of the inscriptions can still be read on tablets.
13412: A lovely small tin ring has been left here.

You are standing in the white Friendship Hall, where Tar-Aldarion met Galadriel and Celeborn five thousands years ago. Magnificent sculptures have been carved in tablets of obsidian and carved pillars extend along the central alley. The hall has been devastated by Sauron's armies, and several broken marble tables lay here and there, scattered around the floor. The place is empty, as all the valuables items have been looted, and the wooden or silken furniture decayed.
13413: This southern end of the large hall looks much the same as the rest of it, all inlaid with the same black rock. An eerie feeling hangs in the whole throne room, seemingly thick enough to cut if you chose to. A few statues line the walls here, all of them of mighty warriors wielding strange weapons.
13414:
A demon wolf lurks here, its dark form twisting and hiding its shape.
A demon wolf lurks here, its dark form twisting and hiding its shape.

The entire room is inlaid in obsidian, giving the room a beautiful yet ominous sparkle. One can't help but gasp in astonishment at the sight, the curiosity about these people heightened even more. There is however some debris which is most certainly out of place here, along with a smell that says this room is still frequented.
13415: The tunnel ends abruptly here, the obsidian walls glistening gently. The dank smell is still present, making your nose wrinkle somewhat. Mostly one can wonder why the passage ends here in such an illogical spot. Perhaps this tunnel was made for a more covert and clandestine purpose.
13416:
A tall orc of the White Hand glares through squinted eyes.
An uruk-hai orc growls at the sight of you.
An uruk-hai orc growls at the sight of you.
An uruk-hai orc growls at the sight of you.
An uruk-hai orc growls at the sight of you.
An uruk-hai orc growls at the sight of you.

Glistening slightly from the moisture condensing on the walls, this tunnel is not quite as dark as some of the others here. The walls and floor are made of a very smooth, shiny kind of rock, unlike anything you've seen before. There are small pools of standing water here and there, causing a stagnant smell to permeate the environment.
13417: This crossing is largely dominated by the huge mural that is on the north wall. It must be very ancient indeed, as certain scenes are missing, or are simply no longer able to be seen. While it is indeed beautiful, it also serves to add an extremely eerie feeling to this whole place. More than ever, one cannot stop wondering who made this place, and why they are apparently no longer here.
13418: A musty loaf of bread has been left here.

This room is not lit by any ambient light, so if your eyes are not suited to darkness, you had better light an artificial source. It is somewhat cool in here, as the room itself is carved into the very hillside. This seems to have been the conversing room of the dwelling, being fairly large and open. A cracked tabletop lies on the floor, as well as the charred remains of a chair. The floor is naturally hard-packed dirt, and a layer of dust covers everything.
13419: A diamondback rattlesnake is coiled here, ready to strike.

This crude shelter seems very sturdy. It is larger than it appeared from outside, as a second room has been cut into the hillside next to it. The roof you saw from the outside only covers about half of the area. The place seems to be uninhabited at the moment, as you see no tell-tale signs of life. It was probably used by the Dwarves of Moria as a resting spot on their long treks to the city of Ost-in-Edhil in the west. Another room is to the east.
13420:
A large brown wolf stands here, its teeth partly bared.
A large brown wolf stands here, its teeth partly bared.
A furry, striped raccoon is here, nosing around for some berries or roots.

Abruptly the trail ends here. You are standing before a simple stone dwelling, that looks abandoned at this time. No windows are present, so you may not peek inside from here. Only going in the place will give you a clue as to its purpose. Around you are dark trees looming high above. Since the stone that constructs the house is so natural looking, it blends well with the hill that borders it to the east. It would be difficult to spot the house from far away.
13421: Darkness prevails as the trail continues to the east and west. The shadows that obscure much of the area make it difficult to see, but it is possible to discern some strange tracks on the ground, although its hard to tell just who, or what, made them. To the west the path seems to end abruptly, and you seem to be able to make out some sort of old shelter there as well.
13422: Here the stone passage makes a corner, branching off in different directions. The utter darkness makes it too difficult to tell anything else as it seems to literally eat up any light source that enters its domain. One could easily get lost in here it seems, but the general layout seems simple enough. Rough hewn walls are all that is here, along with a few old torch brackets, now empty. Nothing extraordinary adorns the place.
13423: This small dark pathway lies just off the road to the south. It looks well trampled, but the growth of new grass, and the encroachment of nearby bushes, makes you unsure as to recent travel along it. No footprints can be easily seen, but it has definitely been well-used at some point. Going west is made somewhat difficult by a massive jumble of leaves, twigs, and other intertwining brushwood. To the north lies more of this seemingly deserted path.
13424: Here the stone passage makes a corner, branching off in different directions. The utter darkness makes it too difficult to tell anything else as it seems to literally eat up any light source that enters its domain. One could easily get lost in here it seems, but the general layout seems simple enough. Rough hewn walls are all that is here, along with a few old torch brackets, now empty. Nothing extraordinary adorns the place.
13425: Both the river and the trail avoid a huge boulder and diverge temporarily but as far as you can see further up and down the stream the trail follows the river closely. The land rises slowly in the west, eventually forming grass-covered, round hills.
13426: The trail follows the river closely, through the fertile grass on the riverbank. Some large bushes grow alongside with reeds by the river and a very old willow tree extend its branches over the water. Tracks in the damp earth near the river edge suggest that this becomes a crowded place when animals become thirsty.
13427: Fields coloured in green and yellow border to the banks of the Glanduin River. A little east of here the river makes a slow turn north and the low banks are partially flooded. Reeds, bulrush and bog moss grow in the aqueous soil. Many insects live in the moist environment, and a steady buzzing and humming can be heard. A cosy trail bends along the riverside on a small rise of worn earth.
13428: The clear water, that began its journey many miles away in the snow-covered mountain peaks to the east, trickles gently along, slowly gathering up speed to reach the Sea. The green banks along the river are filled with plenty of wildlife; insects buzzing, birds chirping with joy and silver fins carving through the water below.
13429: Following the contours of the river the trail continues through the grass covered plains. The trail bends and slopes a little, yet always manages to find its way back to the river. It often takes a minor sway away from the river to avoid the soggy and muddy area close to the banks. The path is clear and small pebbles makes it easy to follow.
13430: A pebbled trail snakes through the waist-high grass along the banks of the Glanduin river. Once the fields south of the river were fallow, tended by the hard-working and diligent citizens of Cillien. The rural plains are now overgrown with wild grass, and only the trail remains to indicate the amount of traffic that once passed south of the river. To the east can be seen the silent ruins of the village of Cillien.
13431: Located on a small rise on the western bank of the Glanduin lies the ruins of a once prosperous village. Standing in the old village square that allows a good view east, it's possible to see far upstreams the Glanduin. Around the square stand the ruined masonry of the houses that once formed the village. Although crude, a decent shelter from the elements can be found among the lichen-covered stone walls. A dusty trail runs through the village going west into the wilderness or south into Dunland. From the north comes the babbling sound of a ford in the river.
13432: A dusty trail runs along the western shore of the Glanduin. The river goes north-south here as it passes on the eastern side of a ruined village to the north. A richly vegetated slope lies between the trail and the river. The slope is fairly steep and the plants grow too dense to see if the ground is stable enough not to make the descend dangerous.
13433: In the regions south of the Glanduin river begins the vast plains of Dunland, through which this small path runs. Located near the Misty Mountains the region prospers from the melting water brought down from the snowcapped heights by the many brooks and streams. Green grass grows dense and in some places unrivalled by plants and trees. The view of the swaying grass would be unbroken, if not for the rising mountain about a half day's march to the south.
13434: Halfway hidden among knee-high grass and green bushes a trail snakes its way across the Dunland plains. Once sighted, gravel and stamped dirt makes following the trail easy. However it's not uncommon to see the vegetation overtaking the trail trying to confuse weary travelers.
13435: Stones and pebbles mark a trail well hidden among the waist-high grass that dominates the open plains. The trail, worn and bumpy, is a welcome guide through the monotonous landscape, where the variation in the vegetation relies only on the shifting colour of the grass. Yet a keen eye might spot the unexpected appearance of trefoil and crowfoot hiding among the thick grass along the side of the trail.
13436: Green grass grows on both sides of a trail that cross the flat plain. The small bump of a hill in the north-west is the only thing breaking the straight line formed by the border of the green grass and the colour of the sky far away near the horizon.
13437: The plain is completely flat here and covered with green grass. Different kinds of bushes and flowers grow in the fertile soil between grassy patches. The trail bends around brushy spots but is otherwise very straight. The dry carcass of a horse lies beside the trail spreading an odour of decomposing flesh.
13438: The trail passes north of a clump of bushes but everywhere else green grass covers the flat earth of Dunland. The bushes are constantly rustled by what must be small animals or birds. Small white and yellow flowers grow in the grass beside the trail.
13439: Partially hidden in the grass the trail wriggles its way through the plains. It fades away behind tall grass not far to the east and approaches some hills in the south. Everywhere the grass is green and undulates softly in the wind.
13440: A beautiful and docile horse is standing here.

The water rushes forth over stones and rocks stirred by a sudden shallowness of the river. The banks have grown further apart making the river expand to more than a hundred feet across. Nevertheless the shallow waters are easily passed if wet feet are no concern. On either side of the ford grows green grass and frail bracken in comfortable distance to the cold gushing water. A bit upstream, to the east, the river can be seen turning south around a small rise.
13441: The mighty Glanduin makes a narrow bend around a cliff to the southwest. While the plains in the borderland of Eregion and Dunland are generally void of obstacles, this cliff is large enough to have altered the course of the river significantly. On the low riverbanks to the north and the east is a dense growth of bracken and weeds, obviously thriving in the moist soil. Behind the cliff the river widens, and makes a gushing sound as the water rushes over a ford.
13443: Turning north the river continues along a densely vegetated slope to the west. Green bushes grow on the slope, and at the point where the slope makes a last steep descent grows a thick foliage of vines that hang into the water. In the clear water it's possible to spot many details of the hydrophytes that grow beneath the surface, especially the comb-shaped leaves of the water-yarrow is seen clearly. South lies a quiet meadow with soft grass.
13444: On its west bound journey, through the borderland between Eregion and Dunland, the river has reached more open land after many miles of company from a forest on the southernly side. Now grassy fields open on either side while the banks grow ever more green with goutweed and bracken. A small stream joins the river from the south, and after a hectic but uneventful merging, the river flows on as if nothing happened.
13445: As the gently flowing river passes north of a coniferous forest the current is slowly increasing. Dangerous boulders just beneath or above the water surface create local gushes and strong currents as the river is forced around them. The low banks on either side of the river are coloured in green by tall grass and sporadic brackens. On the north side of the river lie open plains as far as the eye can see.
13446: The soft flow of the clear water takes the Glanduin river further west on its journey towards its outlet in the great sea far away. The low banks of the river are vegetated by green grass and soft brackens and many insects enjoy the moist conditions close to the water. South of the river is a pine forest and north the vast plains of Dunland disappear into the horizon.
13447: The waters of the Glanduin river continues its mellow flow towards the great sea far in the west. Passing north of a dead pine forest the river marks the transition from plains to softwood. The sad sight of the withering conifers to the south is lessened by a green light in the distance suggesting a more healthy forest further south.
13448: Purling west the river passes south of what looks to be a small settlement in the plains north of the river. A small landing, in strong brown oak-timber, creates a good spot for landing fish and other waterborne goods. Near the bank the landing is elevated almost ten feet from the water surface, and it's possible to manoeuvre a vessel under the landing. South of the river lies a coniferous forest, which from a distance looks healthy, but a closer look reveals that many of the trees are withered and almost dead.
13449: While heading west the river comes upon a section where a low island of sharp rocks makes the water foam as it gushes over the stones. The situation becomes suddenly dangerous as the current steers you right towards the sharp teeth, but at the very last moment a strong side current shifts you north and out of danger. Once in safety you notice how the passing landscape is much different north of the river compared to south of the river. Wide open fields, almost as level as a dinner table, stretch far into the north, while a tired and dead looking forest raises its crowns despondently to the south.
13450: Coarse grass covers the fields north of the river in green. The country slopes slightly upward to the north, but is otherwise quite level. The Glanduin river can be heard clearly from the south, as a steady sound of water whisked to foam by sharp rocks. Across the river lies a forest, but the feature in the landscape is some buildings to the west.
13451: A small hillock covered with green grass and dandelions provides a good view of the surrounding areas. Beneath the delicate grass and flowers the soil is moist and fecund, yet stones lie scattered just beneath the surface as if a stone structure once stood here. Far to the south a dark forest can be seen on the other side of a river running west.
13452: A fierce boar is here, making grunting noises.

Broad oak planks creaks beneath your feet as you step unto the wooden landing. The landing is about ten feet wide and long enough to reach waters so deep that a small boat may dock without running ashore. Resting on thick wooden stakes the landing can support a heavy weight and in previous days it provided the halflings villagers with an easy access to the river. A hatch appears in the middle of the walkway, presumably used when unloading heavy cargo from boats able to sail beneath the dock.
13453: Where the plains of Eregion meet the banks of the Glanduin was once a small village. Halflings proficient with the use of dinghys made a home here close to the river. Fish and crayfish were plenty and provided food to support a fairly large population. Now the halflings are gone, and only the rundown ruins of the village remain as evidence of their presence. A dock at the bank of the river, once used to land the fishermens catch, is still useable.
13454: In southern Eregion the fauna is reigned by green grass and wild flowers. A tempestuous wind roams unhindered in the shelterless downs. While the vegetation appears unvaried and dull, a careful exploration reveals that beneath the grass grows numerous kinds of flowers; butterworth, scabious and broad-leafed cotton grass grows quite well in these conditions.
13455: Wild grass and heather dominate the open plains north the Glanduin river. Contrary to the unconstrained trek across the downs, the terrain south of the river would appear less manageable as a dense forest can be spotted even from here. Far beyond the forest lies the mountains with snow-capped peaks.
13456: The ridge, that runs for half a dozen miles along the northern banks of the Glanduin river, is vegetated from top to toe by thick grass, coarse as hay. Walking along the top of the ridge is easy, as the grass becomes thinner at the top and the top itself being fairly wide. Beneath a ridge to the north lie open plains that reach far into the horizon and from the south your eye catches the gleaming reflections of a river.
13457: Some small rocks have been piled into a mound here.

This grass-covered ridge gives a good view of the river that runs by to the south. The green vegetation almost reaches your hip, and passing through the country is not an easy task. A sudden opening in the vegetation turns out to be a dry spot with sharp stones and rubble, and in the centre stands a big grey stone. Standing on the ridge the whole river delta, the plains, a forest to the east and the mountain seems to become apparent and clear as if some magic of old clinged to this place refusing to let go.
13458: A fierce boar is here, making grunting noises.

A small hill rises from the fertile soil. On the slanting hillsides is a dense growth of coarse grass that rustles with life. Undoubtedly there are many small animals living among the grass, right now eyeing the visitor on the hilltop. The southern hillside is steeper than the other, and it leads right down to the bank of the river. To the north you spot another small hill only a few miles away, but otherwise the country is flat right up to the mountains that lie far in the east.
13459: The green fields to the north of the river slope gently into the distance. There are no trees or bushes to hinder the journey, yet the green grass and weeds grow dense enough to encumber a tired traveler. Hiding among the vegetion are small clusters of hogweed, easily identified by the saw-tooth patterned leaves and thumb-thick green stems. Both to the north and the south the ground climbs a little to reach the top of two small hills in each direction. To the west the river flows gently by, while making a turn that takes it further west.
13460: A mixture of wild grass and weeds grows throughout the sloping plains. Small grasstops dot the country and travelling the slanting inclines is a moderate strain to your endurance. A grass-covered ridge lies to the south obstructing the view, but to the north are open plains that continue seemingly endless into the far north.
13461: The terrain in the grass-covered plains of southern Eregion is mainly flat, but you have come upon a region where the land is somewhat hilly. Travelling up and down the slopes is a tiresome exercise, but as chances are there are plenty of suitable spots in the shelter of the small hills to make a camp. The vegetation is uniform, consisting mainly of grass, that varies only a little in thickness and in colour.
13462:
A bright green holly bush is growing here.
A boar cub is playing here, and exploring the wide world.

A perpetual view of green grass is offered to travellers passing through the plains of southern Eregion. The vegetation is mainly unvaried, yet erratic clusters of wild flowers can be found here and there. In the far east and south the lies the misty mountains, and before the mountains lies a dark forest.
13463:
A large cabinet capable of storing goods is here.
A wooden chest stands in the corner.
A small rat runs about, oblivious to your presence.
A small rat runs about, oblivious to your presence.
A huge, hungry-looking rat is here.

Once serving as food storage, the old cellar is well-equipped with shelves and cabinets lined along the walls. However, the cellar must have been sealed off long ago judging by the thick dust layer on the floor and the grey cobwebs spun in every corner. Rusted screw eyes in the eastern wall hold in place the remains of a rottened staircase. Rainwater has entered the cellar through the tiny chinks of a hole blocked by a large and very heavy stone slab. A narrow corridor leads to the south.
13464: A grey wolf is here, snarling aggressively.

A quiet meadow, with soft grass and a wide variety of wild flowers in the peak of their bloom, lies well-hidden just south of a scenic river. Slowly slanting the ground makes a casual descent down to the riverside, through a gradually thickening foliage. Almost beckoning for a swim, the clear river lies calmly ahead, stirred only by a gentle flow among the bracken dipping their roots in the shallow water. To the west a narrow trail can be seen winding its way through the grass up a cliff.
13465: A small gurgling stream is heading north along the border of an old forest. The stream is rich in fresh water weeds, and there are several boulders on the bottom which look promising should you decide to dip cork, string and hook with the prospect of catching tonight's dinner. Not far off to the north, the stream joins the Glanduin river, and together they journey for many miles west to the sea. The open landscape to the west of the stream is coloured mainly in green, and it continues as far as you can see.
13466: Bushy pines with gnarled branches and sturdy stems stand closer than arm's reach. Though the forest floor is mainly flat and easily travelled, there are places where thorny bushes and tall grass form nasty barriers between the trees and crossing puts heavy strain on both gear and limbs. From the north can be heard the incessant sound of purling water.
13467: A forest of weary and intertwined pine trees forms dense thickets in a maze- like fashion. Between the pine hedgerows green grass grows mixed with old spruce needles from last year's fall. The trees are thinning to the north where they are cut off by a river, and near the river grass and bushes take up more and more space.
13468: Previously green with beautiful pine trees the forest has now turned dull and grey. Most of the trees are dead and the few trees that remain alive struggle to keep what's left of their green needles. The dead forest floor is covered in brown needles that crunch and bounce with every step. North the vegetation slowly comes to life, as dead trees give way to bracken and green grass that grows effortlessly in the moist environment along the Glanduin riverbanks.
13469: A squirrel scampers around here, looking for nuts from the trees.

South of the Glanduin river is a softwood forest. A handful of different tree sorts can be seen, most of them have curly and crude branches, and are not very tall. The forest floor of spruce needles is soft and there is little underbrush to slacken the pace. Towards the riverbank to the north the trees are slowly dispersed as millet grass and wild flowers claim ground.
13470: Old yew trees and twisted scotch pines grow amongst each other on the southern bank of the Glanduin River. The bank slopes gently down to the riverside, where the trees gradually disappear in favour of bracken and grass. The river, not far away beyond the trees, can be heard as a clear purling sound of bubbles and foam.
13476: In an area densly vegetated with pine trees and bracken, travelling has to be done by foot. Even though the brackens are soft, clearing a way through the undergrowth soon turns arms and body weary. The south is cast is shadows by an ancient forest of tall trees with wide crowns blocking out most light.
13477: A squirrel scampers around here, looking for nuts from the trees.

The untamed forest consist mainly of tall trees with bushes and shrubs tangled about their stems. The ground present little elevation but nevertheless the vegetation offers many difficulties for a journey through the forest. Birds and rodents hide among the bushes in relative safety from predators. The vegetation to the west prevents any further travel in that direction.
13480: A brutish forest troll is hunting here, looking for some tasty flesh.

Bracken and heather covers the ground in a ancient forest of mixed trees. The fertile earth is soft and fairly level. Bracken are easily pushed aside, but sometimes the undergrowth changes into thick entangled bushes that cannot be passed without much cutting and cursing. Trees and brushwood, both green and bright, are in appearance so varied that it's hard to imagine any forestation ever to have taken place; an observation also supported by the thick roof of leaves formed by the tree-crowns above.
13481: Swaying with majestic grace in the wind, the slender trees of the old forest rustle a roof of dark-green leaves some twenty feet above. Between the trees grows a dense underwood that makes a mounted attempt to travel the forest impossible. A shallow stream trickles north along the forest floor, sometimes disappearing under dense bushes. Although the vegetation is very dense you catch a glimpse of a stone-structure to the west.
13482: The forest of tall trees standing only a few feet apart is not easily travelled as the brushwood of bushes and shrubs grows dense with thorns and constricting vines that entangle legs and arms. The ground, covered in brown leaves, is dry and provides a good hiding space for the many animals that live in the forest. Looking up the view is blocked by a landscape of dark green leaves that makes it impossible to determine whether it's night or day.
13485: A brutish forest troll is hunting here, looking for some tasty flesh.

Consisting mainly of tall deciduous trees and thickets of low bushes the green woodland is somewhat easily travelled. The soft forest floor is cast in brown and orange by withered leaves and bone-dry branches that crack on impact. The dark shadow from the dense tree-crowns above, plays mysteriously on the ground that is cold and never lit by the sun. To the south the forest is gradually thickening with dark bushes, and visibility in that direction is poor.
13486: The old hardwood forest rustle its dry branches in the wind shaking of dust and cobwebs. The forest floor, beneath the slender stems that surround you on all sides, is dry, and with each step you hear the crunching sounds of old leaves and twigs snapping. Above hovers a dense foliage of dark-green leaves which cloakes the underwood in dark cold shadow. A small stream takes its begining here, gentle clucks and purls sends it northward at a slow pace.
13487: A dense undergrowth among the tall trees in the forest hinders travel through this region. Bushes and shrubs, with thorny and torpid twigs, tangle gear and legs as were they insects caught in a spiders web. A line of trees with thick thornbushes at their feet grow on an escarpment to the south, passing that way is impossible. Above the tree tops form a dense layer of leaves blocking out light.
13488: Dark Opening in the Ancient Forest
A disgusting forest troll is searching for fresh meat here.

No wind moves through the quiet forest. A low wood-embosomed clearing enjoys the indisturbed tranquillity in the midst of a ancient forest. The clearing, created by a felling long time ago, is more than fifty feet across and covered with soft moss and heather. The otherwise anxious birds elsewhere in these woods seem to have settled with your presence in this clearing. A log of a fallen tree, now almost withered away, rests heavily on a dirt surface in the middle of the clearing where grass and heather are less dominant. In an odd way the trees surrounding the clearing bend inwards making the clearing very dark.
13489:
A brutish forest troll is hunting here, looking for some tasty flesh.
A brutish forest troll is hunting here, looking for some tasty flesh.
A disgusting forest troll is searching for fresh meat here.
A disgusting forest troll is searching for fresh meat here.
A disgusting forest troll is searching for fresh meat here.

Among tall trees of mixed sort exists a multifarious plantlife. Unhindered by the trees, that steal most of the light in the forest, the lower forest has developed into a fertile habitat supporting plants not normally found growing together. Groundsel, Corydalis and Goldenrod seems to grow especially well in these conditions. It's hard to find a way around the plantbeds that often blocks the way between the trees. East the plants are gradually dispersed as the forest opens into a clearing.
13490: Thick bushes with dark-green leaves makes the area very difficult to travel. Branches and vines twists together in a messy bungle quite impossible to open up. Nasty thorns makes it even worse, and there is no option but to find a way around the worst of the thickets. The darkness created in the shadow of the tree-crowns above makes navigation the forest even harder. North the bushes thin out while more and more trees rises. To the west both trees and bushes diminish as the forest seems to take an end there.
13491: Wild thorny bushes tangled into dense thickets hinders any traveller wishing to make way through the vegetation. In the thickets can be seen hawthorn and holly bushes with red berries. The clucking sound of trickling water reaches you from the west, a stream must be near. To the east the brushwood continues and also tall trees are begining to show.
13492: A dense undergrowth among mixed tree sorts slows movement through this region. The vegetation is varied and rich, although bracken has taken up most space. On the trees grow different types lichen, some green and curly other grey-brown with round bodily knobs; the seem to thrive in the dark shadows of a roof of dark-green leaves above. From the northeast falls a brighter light suggesting clearing.
13494: The trees stand only a few feet apart in the ancient forest, and interspersed between the tall stems grows a brushwood thick and thorny. Forcing a way through the underbrush has mostly bruises and scratches as result, and often a different route must be found. A dense and intertwined roof of dark-green leaves effectively cuts off most light from the forest. To the north an upwards slope with dense vegetation at the top prohibits any travel.
13495: Crude earthwalls, slanting and uneven, forms this dark earthen burrow beneath an ancient forest. Roots and boulders left in the walls underlines the sloopy work that lead to the construction of the burrow. The muddy floor is a mix of dirt, filthy rags and bones crushed into a state where their origin can no longer be determined. The smell is nauseating to say the least, and it is clear that this is the insanitary home of very filthy creatures. The trail of bones and rags points south, further into the ground.
13496:
The corpse of a gnarled forest troll is lying here.
The corpse of a gnarled forest troll is lying here.
The corpse of Urgorl is lying here.
A small campfire burns here, its low flames giving off only a little light.
A simple wooden chest is here.
A noticeable crack runs down one of the walls.

Slanting earthen walls lean inward forming a dome-shaped burrow about twenty feet wide. Twisting roots and large rocks protruding from the surface of the walls hinder movement, but judging by the size of the footprints left in the wet mud on the ground, a mere root would not be a problem for one of the inhabitants. Cracked bones and torn fabric litter the floor, and the remains of weapons and armour, enough to equip a small army, have been dropped to rust in a corner. A fireplace in the centre of the burrow, large enough to roast a cow or a bear, has a convenient outlet in the roof.
13497: A scattered population of pine trees stand dormantly around you shaking their branches in the howling wind. The forest floor is covered in green grass. To the east the forest silently claims more space, and the visibility in that direction is low compared the the west where the forest gives way to open plains. In the southwest a mountain ridge rises above the forest border.
13498:
The corpse of a wild dog is lying here.
The corpse of a wild dog is lying here.

Located at the foot of an inaccesible mountain ridge is a richly vegetated area. Man-sized bushes and bracken grow in green clusters in the soft soil. The purling sound of a shallow stream coming from the south is echoed against the tall cliff to the west. East the vegetation becomes more compact as the bracken is forced back by thornbushes and trees that mark the begining of a forest. A small trail around the mountain ridge winds through the vegetation while following closely the contours of the stream.
13499: Beneath the tall peaks of a mountain ridge the ground slopes upward until it meets a steep mountain side. On the sloping hillside vegetation is scarce, partly due to the permanent shadow of the mountains. The ground is rocky, yet stable enough to allow mounted travellers passage over the slanting hillside beneath the mountains. North the terrain flattens as the endless plains of Dunland begin.
13500: In a corner, between the mountains to the south and an old forest to the east, lies a peaceful meadow vegetated by grass, small bushes and dense banks of weeds. Tiny buttercups with yellow eyes shine from the western part of the meadow, where the ground becomes more rocky and hilly. To the east, under the shadow of a tall old forest, delicious mushrooms can be found growing wild.
13501: Out of the waist-high grass rise the ruined stone walls of a decayed manor. The remaining walls, now partially overgrown with lichen and grass, are thick and strong, capable of withstanding the rough weather in the open country. The ground between the ruins is soft and the plantlife along the walls is rich and varied. Among lush green bracken, that covers the walls almost three feet from the ground, grows a dense layer of goutweed and dandelions; could the bracken be hiding something else? To the east lies the border of an ancient forest of tall slender trees.
13502:
A small vicious black rat squeaks at you for disturbing it.
A small vicious black rat squeaks at you for disturbing it.
A spirit floats towards you and howls with an evil laughter.

In what was previously a prison cell in the basement of a manor, the ceiling has collapsed bringing down with it much earth and timber from the structure that once housed many men above. The fate of the prisoners trapped beneath the wreck is obvious, and a feeling of anger over the prolonged imprisonment or early death fills the air. A large gaping hole in the ceiling is partially covered by the vegetation that grows above the hole.
13503: A quiet stream purls gently as it flows north on the western side of an old forest. Lush green grass grows on the banks on either side of the stream, and further to the east bordering up the to the forest begins a dense growth of hogweed and stinging nettles. The grey ruins of a manor can be seen among the grass further south.
13504: A mixture of different pine trees, mingled in hedgerows with thornbushes and tall grass, surrounds you on all sides. The forest floor is covered with spruce needles and old withering twigs and branches that creak beneath your feet. Under brushwood and trees grows a multitude of flowers, herb and fungi. A small stream coming from the south darts through the forest heading west.
13505: Trees of two origins meet here. Low, but sturdy, conifers from the north are suddenly overtaken by a tall deciduous forest from the south. The trees have mixed over the years and recently a dense brushwood has joined to make any passage through the forest both difficult and tiresome. A sad view of dying trees meets you to the east.
13506: The once thriving pine forest is now dead and withering away. The trees were once green and healthy, but some disease must have caused the early quietus of the forest. The trees that still bear needles are scarce and ready to submit to their fate at any time, the ones already dead now host lichen and fungi. To the south the dead pine trees stop as a hardwood forest of taller trees begins.
13507:
A squirrel scampers around here, looking for nuts from the trees.
A squirrel scampers around here, looking for nuts from the trees.

Old and withered are the trees in the coniferous forest located south of the Glanduin river. A thick bouncing layer of dry spruce needles covers the forest floor. Some of the pine trees are long since dead, only lichen and fungi are left to find a last use of the wounded branches. South the flora changes to taller trees and a dense undergrowth, and from the north is heard the faint sound of the river flowing slowly through the landscape.
13508: Despite an overwhelming presence of lush green grass, the flora in the plains of Dunland is varied and breathtakingly beautiful. Dandelions, violets and poppy bloom with a stunning palette of colours and scents in the fecund soil, that provides a nutritious environment for the healthy vegetation. A myriad of insects and creepie-crawlers live among the roots and in the soil, only disturbed by the gentle gurgle of a small stream to the east.
13509: A woodpecker is here, tapping on a tree.

The plains of Dunland hosts a wide range of different plants among which the various types of green grass are the most dominant. But among the green grass one might stumble onto a meadow like this where, for a while, the grass plays a lesser role in the flora and wild flowers stand pretty and tall among a green covering of weeds. To the north a small trail is barely visible among the grass.
13510: The windswept plains of Dunland fill the horizon with a scenic view of green grass thriving in the fertile soil. Besides a few dirt- and rubble- filled holes the ground is even; low bushes and shubbery combat the almost waist-heigh grass for space, and even wild flowers make a lonely mark here and there. A thin dark line a few miles to the north denotes the presence of some kind of trail.
13511: The wide open plains of Dunland sweep across the horizon creating a scenic yet monotone view. Green grass flourish in the moist and fertile soil, and between turfs and grassy banks is found a variety of different wild flowers; some bear red crowns of bitter-smelling leaves. In the distance the waveing sway of the green grass blends into the horizon in a orange-yellow haze.
13512:
A black crow flies low to the ground here, looking for carrion to eat.
A large rabbit looks peacefully at you, ready to dart away.

From this position on the mostly flat plain you see the Misty Mountains rising from the flats, creating a jagged landscape on the southern horizon. A high peak reaches for the sky in the south-east, and further east the hills grow even higher. Some, at least in comparison flat, grass-covered hills bulge in the west. The yellow but mostly green plains lie to the north.
13513: The plain slopes discreetly upwards in the west until the steep slope of a hill blocks the way. In the south-west you can't but notice a spur from the Misty Mountains reaching out in the plains. Some quite large boulders have rolled down from the hill in the west, now offering dark shelter for snakes and other reptiles.
13514: From halfway up the slope to a hill in the south you can see the contours of quite a few hills bulging in the west. In the east you see the rounded and grassy hilltops being overtaken by the rough tops of the Misty Mountains. Drying grass dominates the immediate surroundings but as if they wanted to alleviate the dullness there some soft flowers growing by your feet.
13515: Grass-covered plains rise into low hills and slopes at the foot of a western spur in the Misty Mountains. The surface of the wasteland ground is hard and doesn't breed life to much else but the endless sea of green grass and a few clusters of wild flowers. Yet patches of thin bushes have settled in the shelter of a low depression to the southeast, where the hills begin their climb towards the peaks of the mountains.
13516: A trail of boulders leads the way through a steep climb in the mountains. A recent rock-slide sent boulders tumbling down the rugged mountain side and now the climb, that leads between jagged peaks, has become dangerous and not to be challenged by unskilled climbers. The slope bends upwards to the south, and to the west the terrain becomes less rocky as it gradually turns into hills.
13517: A grey wolf is here, snarling aggressively.

The craggy mountains provide only meager living conditions for the unvaried flora consisting mainly of scruffy moss and dry flowers. Here an escarpment connects the plains below the mountain range to a small plateau beneath the rocky peaks to the southeast. Slim crevices braid together a path of strong handholds suitable for traversing the southern part of the slope. North the rock takes a sudden dive, creating a vertical drop of several fathoms to the plains below.
13518: A grey mountain range to the south forms a high wall overlooking the foothills which unfold into a bumpy terrain of grass and bushes further on a few miles into the north. The ground is cold, confined to rest in shadow under the misty peaks of the mountains. In a quiet hollow between two neighbouring hills grows a small thicket of green bushes.
13519: Mile after mile the sea of grass and weeds continues in all directions. Besides the always common variants of grass, there are also thick beds of goutweed and stinging needles. The terrain is flat and unchallenging travel, but a mile or two to the south the land turns into foothills before a mountain range. Far to the east lies a dark and secret forest.
13520: An endless view of thick-nestled grass fills the horizon in every direction. Mixed with occasional wild flowers and wind-beaten bushes, the grassy plains form a gracious contour to the mountain peaks far in the east. The terrain is mostly flat, besides a series of low trenches that surround what appears to be a formerly farmed area. Barren since many years, the field has merged with the wasteland plains.
13521: The barren plains compose an endless view of grass bending and swaying in the wind. Only occasional bumps of soil and ruffled grass rise up, in a futile rejection to submit to the endless beating from the the rough conditions in weather found in the Dunland Plains. Besides a few low bushes seeking refuge in scarce depressions, all other vegetation is outnumbered by the always dominant thickets of stifled grass.
13522: Little shelter can be found in the open plains of Dunland. Here the weather sets the agenda; often, with fierce determination and force, the wind sweeps across the open land, gnawing its chilly teeth through any barrier in its way. The soil, being partly rubble and fist-sized stones, is little comfort to the scattered and unvaried vegetation of grass and low bushes.
13523: Beneath the widespread fingers of the Misty Mountains, that take shape far into the east, lies a small strip of rough and weatherbeaten turf. Grass and bushes struggle in the unforgiving conditions where the only shelter can be found to the south where a dormant mountain range with spiked towers of grey rock glitters through a thin cover of mist. The ground slopes steadily upward to the south, and gradually grass and bushes give way to stones and dull green moss.
13524: A fallow deer is grazing peacefully here.

A thin mountain ridge reaches out from a mountain range going east-west south of here. Moving across the ridge is a dangerous climb with many loose rocks on the way. Vegetation here is sparse, limited to dry grass and tiny bushes tugging their roots into the soil and rubble found infrequently throughout the many cracks and scars in the rock. The ridge provides an excellent view over the plains of Dunland to the north and over the treetops of a mixed forest to the east.
13525: The mountain terrain is challenging even for a skilled climber. Yet a rough ledge, beneath the the mountain peaks, provides as much comfort as is needed to endure the hardship of travelling through the misty cliffs. Beneath the mountain wall lie gaping gorges with sharp splintered rock-teeth waiting only to bite. Descending slightly, yet determined, a lower ridge bends away from the mountain to the north; it might be possible to leave the dangerous mountains that way.
13526: Overlooking the Dunland Plains is an exposed cliff-side under the great peaks of the Misty Mountains. The cliff is formed of the rough stone, that extends further west before it begins its steady decent into the plains. In the high mountains vegetation is scarce, limited to only a few patches of moss and the occasional wild flower. A thin mist swirls over the peaks to the east, limiting the view of further travel into the mountains.
13527:
A beautiful and docile horse is standing here.
A boar cub is playing here, and exploring the wide world.

Steep sloping hills strive to overlook each other as one after another they spread out beneath the overwhelming mountain peaks of the Misty Mountains to the east. Sturdy bushes and thick grass, struggle in the unforgiving wind that sweeps through the foothills. Boulders and mountain siplings pierce through the soil at many a hilltop and slope, exposed to the weather by the retreating vegetation.
13528: A large rabbit looks peacefully at you, ready to dart away.

This hill forms the westernmost outpost of the great Misty Mountains. The grasses grow sparse on the slopes down to the plain below but dwindle even more in the east leaving only a few bushes to protect the earth from stones and boulders tearing and ripping on their way toward the plain below.
13531: The rocky ground inhibits substantial vegetation growth, though a few small bushes and a sapling or two struggle to take root. Loose rocks and a few leaves lie dormant upon the ground, covering an ancient trail which traverses the terrain from north to south, providing passage from the valley to the Misty Mountains.
13532: These rough hills descend to the south and west while to the north and east they lead towards the mountains. Directly east there is a small chamber beneath a rough stone arch that crosses from one mountain peak to another. The arch, clearly visible from here, is a magnificent work of nature. It is more than one hundred feet long and over three feet wide and often coated by a thin layer of ice. To the east, beneath the arch, you can see the skeletal remains of those who lost their footing while crossing the bridge.
13533: Against the side of the mountain, to the east, the plains suffer from the lack of water and harsh winds. Once a long time ago a few hardy plants took root, but now all have withered and died leaving their crusty remains. There are no signs of animals on the ground or in the air for this place is truly barren.
13538:
A pack horse is sleeping here.
A pack horse is sleeping here.
A little dog is here.

Bounded by the Misty Mountains to the south and an ancient forest to the north little vegetation has managed to grow here. The soil consists mostly of small chunks of granite mixed with dirt and a few brittle leaves from the nearby forest. While a few blades of grass have managed to take root, as in previous attempts, they are likely to soon wither and die. To the north the forest begins to grow in earnest.
13539: To the north an ancient forest rises above you contrasting starkly with the mountains to the south. While the forest is densely packed with ancient trees and shallow shrubs, this region is only lightly foliaged. The ground, mostly a thin layer of soil upon a rocky substrate, is hard and unyielding to the roots of the few small shrubs that manage to grow here.
13540: This lightly forested area forms a transition between the Misty Mountains to the north and an ancient forest to the south. Grass can be seen growing at the base of the mountains and slowly giving way to some small ferns and coarse bushes. Here and there a small tree can be seen sprouting.
13541:
A sturdy pack horse is standing here.
A large mother hawk is here looking for prey to feed her young.

Only light vegetation and small trees have managed to survive the rocky conditions of this area, boxed in by the Misty Mountains to the south and a vast ancient forest to the north. While little can be seen to the south where the mountains rise before you, sounds and cries of wild animals can be heard from the north.
13546: Years of erosion as a small underground mountain stream flowed through the granite rock have caused the ceiling to collapse, forming this overhang some fifteen feet above the stream. While the sides are wet, making climbing somewhat difficult, the water below ensures a soft landing if you should fall. To the west, a difficult trip across the mountain leads towards a barren plain.
13547: West Side of the Misty Mountains

High above plains to the west and south you can see that much of the land has become barren. Long ago these were fruitful farmlands, but years of fighting followed by prolonged drought and isolation have left this land barren. To the north and east the mountains continue, blocking much of your vision. You can continue west and south onto the plains or, with great effort, east into the mountains.
13548: A black and white skunk is scuttling about here, searching for food.

Here, these plains form a stark contrast as the flat land ceases to the north and east where the Misty Mountains rise from the earth. While the plains are barren and consist mostly of brittle soil, little more than sand, the mountains are composed of a near vertical wall of rugged granite, which nature inadvertently provided as protection from all but the most invasive of intruders.
13549: Sparse barren plains surround you in all directions. To the south the plains, while still dry and barren, begin to show some signs of life. To the east, even from this distance, the mountains are clearly visible with the harsh features of the rough granite sides making their presence known.
13550: Often a sharp wind blows across the land producing a shrill whistle as it comes off the mountains to the north and east. A long time ago, a few hardy plants managed to survive these harsh conditions but a prolonged drought brought an end to their life. With their removal the wind quickly laid waste to the top soil making the return of plant life unlikely.
13551: These hills, a precursor to the Misty Mountains, contain an abundance of ragged boulders. While some of the rocks are little more than stones, many of them are larger than the largest troll. The gaps between the boulders make travel slow and difficult. To the north and east the Misty Mountains can be found, while to the west and south a vast barren plain stretches across the landscape.
