13552: A large rabbit looks peacefully at you, ready to dart away.

These plains are barren, void of both plant and animal life. Often a cloud of dust hangs overhead greatly reducing visibility. A soft shrill can be heard from time to time as the wind races through the gaps in the mountains to the north and east. Sheltered by the mountains, little water reaches this area leaving the soil brittle, hard and dry.
13553: These plains have been barren for many years. After the few plants that grew in this region lost life, the harsh wind removed the fertile top soil. With little water and poor soil, plants have been unable to regain a foothold in this region, leaving these plains barren. Little in the way of landmarks distinguishes this area from those nearby, and only the Misty Mountains to the east provide a meaningful landmark.
13554: Much of northern Dunland lies under the Misty Mountains, their ominous presence dominating the eastern skyline. Here is no different - they are under 10 miles away from these plains. Most of the rest of the horizon is flat however, miles upon miles of the same landscape. Here the winds have stripped the flat topsoil of all its nutrients, leaving it barren and rocky. No plants grow here in the dusty earth.
13555: Cutting its way through the plains, this trail is mainly used by Dunlending hunters to mark the route between the best hunting grounds. Here the ground is rather mixed - somewhat arid further to the east, and in better bloom to the west. The trail continues southeast from here, towards the Misties, and west towards a solitary hill.
13556: The path runs along the brush edge here, in the wind-battered plains. Both the brush and plains appear devoid of water, the arid soil little more than dust on the ground. Far to the east the Misties stand tall, dominating the landscape even from this great distance. The path continues west towards a lone hill in the plains, and east along the brushland's border.
13557: This trail runs down from the long-ruined hilltop town to the west, and into the plains. Along its southern edge it touches a large patch of brush, which you cannot see more than a few feet into. Out north stretch the flats, grassy and never-ending. East the path continues along the border of the brush, and turns southeast.
13558: A mass of dark green leaves clings to a wall.

These ruins are spread across the top of a solitary hill, rotting wooden and stone structures of all types. Making out what they once were is difficult, as most are little more than a collection of stone remnants covered by moss and reams of undergrowth. It must once have been a fairly important place, standing as it does at the junction of four trails. The Dunlendings who once occupied it have long since left for better pastures, like most of their kind in northern Dunland.
13559: A pack horse (Rood) is standing here, ridden by you.

Having seen much use in years past, this trail now looks abandoned. Deep ruts formed by travellers carrying heavy loads now only serve to trip up the rare careless wanderer. The path clearly leads to the west, and seems to widen further in that direction. What lies there surely is no longer the destination it once was, judging by the lack of traffic on this trail.
13560: A pack horse (Rood) is standing here, ridden by you.

Flat and packed hard by the wind and sun that beat upon it, the dirt here makes a path that must stretch for miles. Miles upon miles of high grasses stretch in all directions, except to the south. There a decaying wooden fence surrounds an untended field of crops, the countless stalks wild and intermingled.
13561: A pack horse (Rood) is standing here, ridden by you.

Loosely packed dirt is all this trail consists of, little more than a farm trail originally. Since northern Dunland was largely abandoned it is now used by the solitary hunters as the quickest route between two points. It shows signs of decay in places, where plants have taken hold. Not a soul has made an attempt to clear the path, and it grows steadily more difficult to pass every year.
13562: The ground grows slightly arid here, reflecting the difference in height. Not so much a hill as an elevation, the land here is exposed and wind-beaten. The soil is a light brown in most spots, mostly a thin layer on the rock. Under the shalter of the many boulders here small reptiles can be found scurrying around, the only wildlife visible except the birds circling above.
13563: Patches of grass are scattered along the ground. In places, the blades of grass grows long and rippling. In other areas, they have been cut short by the tearing winds. The soil is dry on the top of the hills while the soil in the valleys are moist. A trail is visible to the south.
13564: The plains continue on as far as the eye can see. Thick grasses gradually give way to rocky soil. In some areas, the rocks have been used as a boundary for the occasional campfire. A few shrubs grow here, large round bushes with lush foliage.
13565: Tall grasses grow here, and in every direction around you. In some areas signs of animal life are apparent, but mostly the height of the grass stops any sign showing. However the sounds of wildlife are constant, rustling around in the undergrowth without ever showing themselves.
13566: The plains roll on in gentle waves of grass and shrub looking to the north and east. The grasses sway in the prairie like winds that blow along the area, miles of plains rippling as one. The land is home to much wildlife under the grassy surface, many burrows visible all around. Above ground the population of small creatures teems, with rabbits and foxes visible all over.
13567: The plains roll like waves on a pond here, the constant rise and fall of the land all that is visible to the horizon. The grasslands are home to countless creatures - undisturbed by man the flora and fauna have prospered. Just south of here runs a trail across the lands, bordering an old field of crops on the other side.
13568: Wind-battered but relatively verdant, the land here appears to have benefitted from the rains that flow down from the hill southeast of here. The grass is lush and teeming with wildlife, despite the fairly rocky soil underneath. A trail is just visible to the east, travelling north-south through the billowing grass.
13569: The plains surrounding the path spread out into miles and miles of grass and small shrubs, with the occasional rock formation large enough to peek above the earth. To the south a ruined settlement stands its ground atop a hill, the path climbing to meet it.
13570: This flat land shows wear. Wind has blown the dusty dry soil over what little plant life dares try to grow here. The few shrubs are scarred with the scratches and bite marks of small animals trying to gleam some nourishment or perhaps to suck a tiny bit of moisture from a green leaf.
13571: A fallow deer is grazing peacefully here.

Scattered parennial shrubs litter the landscape here, their thin bare branches waving in the wind like skeletal arms. Not much else is able to survive in this poor dry soil, although a few blades of grass here and there attempt to draw what little nutrients from the soil they can. South a path is visible, cutting through the flatlands.
13572: A boar cub is playing here, and exploring the wide world.

Opening up on all sides from here are the plains, a wide open expanse from the Misties in the east to the western horizon. It is somewhat arid here, the wind battering any plant that grows much above the earth. A flat cropped layer of grass covers most areas, but little else grows. To the south a trail cuts its way through the land.
13573: Withered and dusty like most of the surrounding plains, these windswept lands are near completely barren of life. The occasional hardy shrub manages to poke through the rocky earth, but little more does so. To the north and northeast a hilly spur of the Misty Mountains thrusts outwards into the plains, its steep side facing you.
13574: Across the plains little can be seen. The air is choked full of soil and the ground is littered by the long dead remains of plants. To the north the ground begins to slope upwards as a hill forms a buffer between these barren plains and more fruitful places. To the east the Misty Mountains begin to take shape some six miles away.
13575: The steep hill rises sharply to the north and to the south it quickly falls as it merges into a vast barren plain. Often the region to the south is covered by dust as the wind lifts the barren soil into the air where it remains for days. While the taller hills to the north often block the airborne soil, here much of it collects both in the air and upon the ground making the ground silky and slick. To the east some six miles away, even when conditions are harsh, the rising slopes of the Misty Mountains are visible.
13576: A fierce boar is here, making grunting noises.

This hill is the last in a range running out from the Misties. Although nowhere near as high as the main mountain range, it is still a fair high climb to its height. Its southern flank is the steepest, and would require climbing to get down to the plains. North and east the hills continue, while to the south and west the plains continue endlessly.
13577: A sharp-eyed hawk is here stalking some prey.

At the base of a spur from the Misties, these plains are constantly battered from the winds that sweep down from its hilly reaches. The dusty soil here does not provide much nourishment for plants - only the hardiest of shrub takes root here.
13578: Scattered patches of grass cover the ground, soaking up what little moisture can be found in this arid land. The dry dirt seems to be inhospitable to much else other than these hardy grasses and the few small shrubs. Wind has kicked up the dusty top soil, covering what does grow with a layer of dust.
13579: Arid and dry, the ground cracked from lack of moisture, these flats produce little vegetation, save for the occasional shrub growing around a few sprigs of short-cropped grass. A worn path, clearly visible from this location, lies just to the west.
13580: A large rabbit looks peacefully at you, ready to dart away.

Cutting through the plains here is a hunting path, little used now as northern Dunland is mostly abandoned. Occasionally an old campsite can be spotted just off the path, the remnants of a trapper's camp, but generally there are few inhabitants around here. The path continues north into more plains and south towards a prominent hill in the plains.
13581: A rock lizard is here, motionless as it observes you.

It is apparent that the land here is healthy underneath - the earth is soft and the low grass healthy. However the windblown plains suffer growth to no major height, numbing and beating the vegetation constantly. Rodents and reptiles run amok here, the rocky ground much to their liking.
13582: Small rodents scurry between the rocks littering the ground here, underneath the surface of the grass. Pebbles are found lying all around, a rocky underbed to the soft grass. Northwards several hills can be seen rising above the land, rolling out from the Misties in the east like a wave in the land.
13583: Prickly, white-stemmed plants, with blue flower heads grow in abundance.

Dry, cracked earth with scattered low, wilted shrubs struggle to grow around here, even in the shade of the countless large rocks dotting the land. The landscape gently rises to the west, wind erosion slowly eating away at in places, leaving smooth rock-hard soil. In the distance you can make out a large hill to the southeast, alone in the plains.
13584: A boar cub is playing here, and exploring the wide world.

The land here becomes gently sloped towards the north, where a hill is visible rising out of the plains. Apart from that solitary landmark the immediate land is all flat grasslands, the same dry parched growth everywhere you look. East the presence of the Misty Mountains dominates the skyline, even at this huge distance.
13585: A diamondback rattlesnake is coiled here, ready to strike.

Dry and sun-scorched earth marks these seemingly endless plains. The immediate area is mainly flatlands, but you can see the land east of you rising to the north. Large stones litter the area, giving shade to the few surviving animals, mainly snakes, that try to survive here.
13586: Directly east a hill rises from the dry plains, but here and everywhere else between you and the horizon the land is completely flat. The yellow grass and the sparsely growing bushes barely covers the crackled earth. Here and there are cracks wide enough to trap an incautious wanderer's foot.
13587: A pack horse (Rood) is standing here, ridden by you.

From the top of this hill you can see far into the dry plains in the south and over the crests of some hills in the north. On the top of the hill there seems to be the remains of a huge log fire. Blackened earth and partly charred bushes suggest that it burned vividly not so long ago.
13588: Cromdreath the Mountain Troll (CC) is standing here.

Dust flies around in the air as the wind caresses the crackled earth. An occasional bush and the sparsely growing grass doesn't stop dust from forming unpleasant clouds. Despite the rough environment animals, mostly reptiles, leave tracks on the ground while running from one hiding place to another.
13589: You are south of some hills, on a plain that continues all the way to the south horizon and beyond. Some bushes are dispersed in the vicinity. Most of them are dead from drought. Also dead, are the remains of a large stag-like animal.
13590: A black crow flies low to the ground here, looking for carrion to eat.

A lot of dry bushes grow here, sending out spiny branches. In the south you see a straight line where the earth meets the sky which becomes jagged as you turn your head towards the hills in the north.
13591: The trail forms an imperfect line from south to north as it wriggles its way through the plains leading to a hilly area in the north and through desolate grasslands in the other direction. The grass is mostly dry here and green in only a few sheltered spots.
13592: Dried grasslands start at the southern foot of this hill stretching out all the way to the horizon somewhere far in the south. To the north you catch a glimpse of some more hills behind the crest of this one. Directly west you can see a narrow trail entering the hills.
13593: Crackled earth is clearly visible below the dried grass and sparsely growing bushes. Although everything is calm you can sense hidden life forms sneaking behind your back. Only the rustling of some leaves here and a branch swaying there speak of any other presence. Some hills rise in the north while the flat and dry plains dominate the lands in the south.
13594: A fallow deer is grazing peacefully here.

The vegetation is very dry here, by the foot of the westernmost outpost of the Misty Mountains. Rocks and boulders scramble down forming a wall between you and the rising hills in the east. Some evergreen bushes with oily leaves grow between the boulders giving little colour to the otherwise dull atmosphere.
13595: The few green grass blades are overwhelmed by yellow and dried grass that in the distance assume shades of brown. All around you there are grass covered hills, except for a stretch of land in the south that seems to lie flat all the way to the horizon, and beyond.
13596: As the hills diminish in height further east the valley opens up to the plains. The grass grows higher in the shelter of the hills while it is drying and yellow further south and east. Growing between grassy patches are bushes, and here and there, a small tree reaching up for the sky.
13597: Protected by hills the vegetation in the valley has grown high and dense and is obviously flourishing. Flowering bushes, trees and green grass struggle against each other rather than against the rough climate as everywhere else around. Small animals and birds are in constant motion rustling leaves and squeaking at each other.
13598: The trail bends along the foot of a hill in the west while in the north more hills block your view. You can see the vast plains extend all the way to the horizon far away in the south. There is a lot of grass on the ground, along with a few rocks and some dry bushes.
13599: This hill looks no different from the other hills. In the south you can see a small trail coming closer through the plains, rounding the east flank of this hill and disappearing behind another hill close to the north.
13600: From the top of a hill you can see far in the distance. Flat plains dominate the view south of you, and in the north you see hills bulging like a tormented sea. The hill is covered with dry grass with only a few green spots.
13601: A black crow flies low to the ground here, looking for carrion to eat.

Low and dry bushes are widely dispersed between grassy spots along with rocks and pebbles of all sizes. The whole land slants upward toward some hills to the north. Despite the drought of the surroundings you can sense life around you. The bushes rustle as small hidden animals fight for their survival.
13602: The landscape here forms soft weaves frozen in motion covered by dry grass and sporadic bushes. In the north the weaves become higher forming hills, while they calm down in the south forming a brown and yellowish grassy ocean. Directly south a lonely hill rises from the flats.
13603: The plains south of the hills are very dry, yellow blades of grass breaking at each step. The dry lands seem to continue in the south except for a lonely hill in the south-east. The spiny branches and dried bushes reach out toward your legs as if they were trying to tear you.
13604: The ground forms a large bowl here and assembled water has made the ground soft and swampy. You can hear the squeaking of some animal somewhere in the grass. Around you green hills form soft waves of grass, as if the ground once was made of floating matter and then suddenly froze.
13605: The hills in this area form soft waves of earth covered by grass. Continuously tormented by the wind, the grass grows sparsely and only a few spots remain green. Below the slope in the south you can see a green valley between the hills.
13606: Cromdreath the Mountain Troll (CC) is standing here.

The hills here form soft waves of grass-covered earth. An endless wind has browned the grass, and brings the fragrance of the earth from somewhere far away. A green spot of grass marks the birth of a small rivulet of water that makes its way down the hillside and down to a valley in the south.
13607: Cromdreath the Mountain Troll (CC) is standing here.

Here, close to the top of a rather tall hill you see can far in the distance. Some hills covered with dried grass are in the west, and vast plains stretch out as far as you can see beyond some more hills in the north. A small trail wriggles its way through the hills in the east.
13608: Many feet have chosen to walk around the large hill to the south as the trail takes a turn. To the north the trail continues into the flats of Dunland where nothing but grass can be seen. The trail bends in the east entering the hills.
13609: A grey wolf is here, salivating profusely.

The trails forks here, leading down to the plains in the west and into the hills in the south. In the east the trail passes some trees and something that looks like small buildings. A large stone has been erected in the grass near the crossing, with some kind of message inscribed on it.
13610: In the shelter of this valley some old civilisation has erected some kind of buildings from grass and clay. However that must have been a long time ago, as most of the huts have collapsed and there is no indication of any recent activity. Around the huts some bushes have grown high adding to the abandoned atmosphere.
13611: A circular stone well has been built here.

From in between them the crumbling buildings look even more abandoned than from the outside. The huts are in a very bad shape. Some of them are only remains on the ground, and of those with roofs all have holes of different sizes. You see the branches of a tree reaching out from a hole in the roof in one of the huts.
13612: Rocky Slope up to a Hill

Here and there, small rocks lie embedded amidst the gravelly slope. Climbing up the large hill to the east, the land appears to be very unstable. Venturing that way could easily result in the unleashing of an avalanche of rocks and stones. Only a few patches of grass, and a lone, rather stunted bush have managed to take root here. Westward stand the ruins of what might once have been a small village.
13613:
A cute rabbit is here.
A brown fox is here, looking for some rabbits to chew up.

From this point you can see very far into the plains in the north, but a hill blocks your view to the south. You catch a glimpse of something glittering on the very top of the hill. You can also see a small trail that plunges into the hills in the west and dwindles on the north-east horizon.
13614: The trail approaches some hills in the south as it stretches over the plains from east to west, but turning somewhat to the south. In the north the flat grasslands continue, gently bulging their way to the horizon. The grass grows high on both sides of the trail and here and there a traveller would have to force his way through the high grass bending over the trail.
13615: A brown fox is here, looking for some rabbits to chew up.

A small trail is here making traveling easier from the east to south-west. Far in the east the trail fades away near the horizon, while it passes between some hills close in the south vanishing out of sight behind something that looks like green foliage.
13616: The incline up to the hill in the south is not very steep but quite a few rocks have rolled down leaving scars in the earth where spiny bushes have found a suitable environment. The grass grows green and high, hiding all kinds of creatures.
13617: A large rabbit looks peacefully at you, ready to dart away.

While still on the vast plains of Dunland you can see how the trail in the south enters some hills disappearing between two of them instead of dwindling away in the distance as in the north. Some windswept trees, hardly more than bushes, struggle to survive beside the path.
13618: The grass grows very abundant here on a slope upwards toward a small hill in the south. A valley emerges from the hills in the west showing a few trees. The plains continue to the south while the flats of Dunland go on and on in the north and in the east.
13619: The valley is confined by hills in the north and south and it narrows to the west as the hills grow larger. The valley widens to the east and the grass grows higher. A few trees grow in the southern most part of the valley, sheltered from the wind by the hills.
13620: The valley narrows to the west and ends at the foot of a steep slope that could be negotiated with some effort. The hillsides confining the valley are almost vertical, but they give way to a wider valley in the east where grass replaces the rocks and dirt.
13621: The hillside slants heavily here leading to the east where a rocky, steep slope down to a narrow valley exists. Rocks and boulders are scattered all over the hillside making it difficult to manoeuvre.
13622: Here on the northernmost hill of the area you see the plains stretch out to the north, no end of it to be seen anywhere before the horizon far in the distance. Higher hills are to the east, and a narrow valley could be reached by climbing down a steep, rocky to the south.
13623: The grassland slants upward toward a hill to the south. The plains go on and on in all other directions, brown and green grass blurring into gray far in the distance. Some small pebbles and a few larger stones mingle with the grass around you.
13624:
A grey wolf is here, snarling aggressively.
A brown fox is here, looking for some rabbits to chew up.

You see myriads of small holes in the ground around you. Every now and then a small rabbit head surveys the surroundings only to notice you and return to the safety of the underground. Passing through would require some attention not to get stuck in a rabbit home.
13625:
A grey wolf is here, snarling aggressively.
A cute rabbit is here.

From the middle of a large green ocean you see the sharp line formed by the horizon in all directions. The land is slightly undulated and covered with green grass around you. A wide variety of animals live off the fertile soil and only move away far enough from you to feel safe enough to continue eating.
13626: The high grass bulges as the wind caresses it playfully on its way over the fertile plains of Dunland. The whole landscape conveys a feeling of solitude, as if the land echoed loneliness. There are traces of life despite that, kites soaring in the sky implies that at least some signs of life - and death - are present.
13627:
A grey wolf is here, snarling aggressively.
A large rabbit looks peacefully at you, ready to dart away.

The green plains of Dunland sway softly under the breeze. Feeding from the rich plantlife there are various herds of large animals along with smaller and more timid creatures. Ultimately these animals support a wide variety of predators that stalk the plains searching for weakened prey.
13628: The path runs north to south, through the plains of Dunland. It has been here a long time, made mostly of trampled grass and stone. All around are more plains covered with grass as far as the eye can see. You catch a glimpse of the Misty Mountains far to the east, imposing even from this distance.
13629: A variety of plants and grasses grow on these plains. Stiff stems with yellow flowers stand against the wind, while the grass bows deeply with the breeze. A bit west there is a small stream followed by what seems to be a narrow trail.
13630:
A brown fox is here, looking for some rabbits to chew up.
A black crow flies low to the ground here, looking for carrion to eat.

The grass is deeply green here, almost shading in blue in some spots. Reaching up between the grass blades beautiful blue flowers with long narrow stems arise. A hill climbs in the east, and another in the north, but south you see nothing but grass covered plains.
13631: The hill barely rises from the plain but its north side is almost vertical and forms a precipice down to the grass below. A tree stretches long branches up in the air in the south, reaching higher than this hill. The grass up here bulges and bows as the wind caresses it gently.
13632: Large bushes grow on the hillsides and green grass on the relatively flat ground between the hills. Stretching from east to north the great river Glanduin flows through, cutting a path in the plains. Between you and the river you can see the faint line of a small trail lying on the banks.
13633: The hill splits into two near the top. From here, you can see far into the surrounding plains and you can follow the gentle flowing of the Glanduin river far to the north where it eventually flows past the ruins of Ost-in-Edhil and to the east where it emerges from dense woods.
13634:
A fallow deer is grazing peacefully here.
A cute rabbit is here.

The grass on the plains is green and grows very high. Pebbles and interlaced grass blades makes it hard to move, but only for larger creatures. You can see how small animals could run about well hidden below the dense vegetation. The whole plain slopes toward a small hill in the west.
13635: Green grass waves slowly as the wind caresses the broken ground around you. Long grass blades extend towards the sky and some of them seem to make a serious attempt of actually reaching it. Some hilly ridges confine the other bank of the slowly flowing river in the north.
13636: A very large, mossy stone is firmly grounded in the earth surrounded with miles of grass in all directions. Except for the stone, there are only some tiny irregularities in the horizon to break the monotony of green grass with dried yellow blades here and there.
13637: A boar cub is playing here, and exploring the wide world.

A vast open field of mossy banks and turfs dominates every inch in range of sight. Buttercup mixed with crowfoot in tight clusters makes a picturesque view as they fade from bright yellow into lush green where the ever imposing beds of grass prevail over the minuscule occurrence of low green-stemmed bushes. The flat land is loose and forgiving to the feet or hooves that might travel through the fields of Dunland.
13638: Wild flowers and waist-high grass intermingle on the open plains. There is little variation in the green surroundings which seem to go on forever if not for the grey shadow of several ruins to the northeast where the plains are abruptly halted by a river. To the north and the east is a trail that appear to be passing through the ruins.
13639: The immense fields of Dunland stretch out around you with grass in various shades of green dominating the landscape. Northwest you see the ground sloping up toward a small and rounded hill. Small yellow flowers struggle to break through the dense grass at your feet to get some sunlight.
13640: The grass is very green and soft in this spot and it grows ankle-high. Faint tracks suggest that many animals live here. The grassy plains continue in all directions and far away you see the sharp border between blue sky and green earth.
13641: The grass is very dense growing waist-high here. The grass blades are somehow interwoven making it very straining to move. The wind makes the world around you wave like an ocean, but in shades of green instead of blue. Everything is flat except for the outlining of some hills far south and north.
13642: Rank weeds and grassy turf cover the almost completely flat plain. Plants with sprouting flowers reach toward the sky and a very large, flowering bush grows in the middle. A large herd of grass-eating animals must have passed recently grazing a wide track grass through the otherwise very high vegetation.
13643:
A sturdy pack horse is standing here.
A large rabbit looks peacefully at you, ready to dart away.

The grass sways in the wind, giving the sensation of being in a green and rather agitated ocean. High grass blades with sharp edges sting the legs of unfortunate wanderers resulting in a brief moment of pain along with a red and itching bump on the skin.
13644: A fallow deer is grazing peacefully here.

A large old tree rests on the steep hillside to the north littering the surrounding grounds with dead leaves. However there is still much foliage on the old branches and the atmosphere under the tree is rather dark and mysterious even during the brightest summer day.
13645: Grass grows abundant here, and along with it there are a few bushes and what could be called a tree, but in fact is not much taller than the bushes. Every movement results in rustling from the bushes.
13646: Long green grass blades reach toward the sky swaying gently in the wind. The vegetation cover the land everywhere around you, on the flat plains of Dunland, and on the small hills in the north. You hear the sounds of a shallow stream somewhere to the west, but it is hidden from this position.
13647: A brown fox is here, looking for some rabbits to chew up.

The Dunland Trail runs north to south through the great plains of Dunland. This trail has been here a long time, made mostly of trampled grass and stone. To the west are plains covered with grass as far as the eye can see, and to the east more plains. You catch a glimpse of the mountains far to the east.
13648:
A grey wolf is here, snarling aggressively.
A brown fox is here, looking for some rabbits to chew up.

These plains form the western border of Dunland. There is green grass as far as the eye can see to the west and south. A cool breeze passes over the plains adding to the relaxing atmosphere. To the east you see a small break in the plains and to the west green grass as far as the eye can see.
13649: A fallow deer is grazing peacefully here.

The plains stretch out around you from the this lonely spot in the vast plains of Dunland. A bit farther to the south you make out rising hills breaking the dullness of flat plains, but in the north the plain looks no different.
13650:
A black crow flies low to the ground here, looking for carrion to eat.
A grey wolf is here, snarling aggressively.
Cromdreath the Mountain Troll (CC) is standing here.

The Dunland Trail runs north to south through the great plains of Dunland. This trail has been here a long time, made mostly of trampled grass and stone. To the west are plains covered with grass as far as the eye can see, and to the east more plains. You catch a glimpse of the mountains far to the east.
13651: A fallow deer is grazing peacefully here.

The plains of Dunland look particularly flat here. The grass looks as flat as a board as each blade becomes blurred and melts into the surroundings. Some hills to the the north break the monotony of these otherwise level plains.
13652: In the middle of the plain there is a depression with a shallow hollow and, in the lowest part, a small pond with murky water. The grass appears to turn a darker and darker shade of brown as it nears the pond and the earth immediately around it is bared.
13653: The green and very fertile grasslands of Dunland slope gently upwards in all directions. Swampy and browned grass grow in the deepest part of the depression along with some swaying reeds, and an odour of putrefied grass and mud tickle your nostrils.
13654: Green grass undulates softly as the wind caresses the lands bringing the fresh scent of growing grass. In the east you can see the faint line of a trail that goes out of sight behind a hill in the south behind which more hills tower up. Only some kind of depression in the north breaks the monotony of grass as you look there.
13655: A large rabbit looks peacefully at you, ready to dart away.

Far away in the south you can spot the contour of some hills, but here the land is very flat and mostly covered with grass. Some spiny and very low bushes grow here and there, underlining rather than breaking the monotony of grass everywhere.
13656: The flat plains stretch out in all directions for as far as you can see. Brown, green and yellow grass melts into gray close to the horizon. Not many animals live here on the windswept plains. In fact, not much lives here at all.
13657: Animals and possibly a few boots have worn the ground away, leaving a stretch of grass that can barely be called a trail. However the grassland around it is full of rocks and pebbles and it's much easier to move about. The plain north of you continues unhindered while hills are visible in the south.
13658:
A cute rabbit is here.
A cute rabbit is here.
A large rabbit looks peacefully at you, ready to dart away.

The trail takes you around a few rocks and bushes, but it mainly travels straight from north to south on the plains. In distance the trail is only a dark line in the grass and at your feet it is not much more. It looks like the terrain becomes more hilly in the south.
13659: The grasslands slant upward toward a hill in the west. To the south you can see more hills while the plains of Dunland go on and on forever in the north. Some small pebbles and a few larger stones mingle with the browned grass making it hard to move.
13660: A large rabbit looks peacefully at you, ready to dart away.

The trail through the wide flats of Dunland is not much more than a trampled line of grass. To the north and east the trail continues through the plains, and dwindles far in the distance. Southwest and far in the south you see the contours of some billowing hills.
13661: A fallow deer is grazing peacefully here.

The grasslands that stretch out far to the north continue up a slope to the south. A few large boulders litter the soil, firmly lodged in the loose soil. Between the rocks the grass grows high as everywhere else on the plain.
13662:
A sturdy billy goat stands here, proudly protecting his goats.
A goat is here, grazing in the hills.
A goat is here, grazing in the hills.

Here on top of a hill you can see far away in every direction. The plains seem to stretch out to the north, a small trail interweaves into the horizon and disappears behind a hill in the east. To the south you see a valley and beyond that more hills. And beyond that, more hills.
13663: On Top of a Crumbling Tower

Your gaze can penetrate deeply into the surrounding plains from the top of the tower. It was built on top of a hill making it the perfect watchtower, but now it lies abandoned. The stone walls are soft and crumbled away from the top, and the floorboards creak under-foot at every step.
13664:
A grizzly cub is here, snarling loudly.
A grizzly cub is here, snarling loudly.
A huge grizzly bear is here, roaming the wild.
A grizzly cub is here, snarling loudly.
A grizzly cub is here, snarling loudly.
A huge grizzly bear is here, roaming the wild.

Not far from the entrance the cave narrows making it imopssible to proceed that way. The soft earthy ground is scarred by the fresh tracks of a large, clawed animal. The cave opening, to the south, reveals only the steep hillside which climbs from the bottom of the narrow valley below.
13665: Travelling the green fields of Dunland would soon become a tiring experience, if not the for varied flora and buzzing insectlife. Everywhere there is a new plant or rock to admire and explore, and butterflies are flapping their colourful wings in the breeze is a constant distraction from the road ahead. Suddenly a shadow becomes apparent to the east, a dense forest rises its tall crowns high in the air a few miles away. Just before the forest stand the walls of a ruined manor.
13666: A beautiful and docile horse is standing here.

The country rises with gentle hills in a region mainly vegetated by grass and weeds. Some areas have been scorched by the sun to form little brown islands among the green grass; there the ground is dry and the withered grass crumbles beneath your feet. A few miles to the south stands a tall mountain ridge with majestic snow-capped peaks. To the east lies a hardwood forest with tall green crowns casting a deep shadow among the stems.
13667: A strip of stiff-grassed fairway is wedged between the bulging foothills that spread out in front of the steep slopes of a mountain range to the south. The green grass flourishes in the fecund soil, beneath the protective cliffs of the mountain. The elevation progresses in the hills nigh the mountains until in the end it begins climbing steadily upwards. East the hills fade out before the dark shadow of a forest.
13668:
A beautiful and docile horse is standing here.
A fierce boar is here, making grunting noises.

Beneath a short overhang a comfortable plateau spans across two cliffs. The southern cliff quickly makes a climbable descent further into the mountain range, but to the north the cliff rises towards the most notable peak in sight. The suddenly level cliff is well protected between the cliffs, yet accessible from all sides, except to the north. Under a low scoop in the northern cliff is a small pile of fist-sized rocks.
13669: You are upon a narrow icy bridge, near the mountain's boundary with the plains, which extends across an enormous chasm. The bridge is nearly three feet wide and some thirty feet above the ground. While the ground below is composed of soft sand, a few sharp rocks make any sort of decent chancy at best.
13670: Midway up the side the mountain you can see across the naked plains to the west and south. To the east a steep, near vertical, incline makes it unlikely that you will be able to proceed in that direction. However, a gap to the north does allow passage.
13671:
A skeleton of some humanoid lies in the dust.
A skeleton of some humanoid lies in the dust.
A burly giant is here, covered with thick fur and snow.
A burly giant is here, covered with thick fur and snow.
A pack horse (polde) is standing here, ridden by you.

Below the arches, the colourful bands of rock which form the mountain pass above are clearly visible. There are at least a dozen bands of rock, each a unique shade ranging from deep brown to rusty orange. While some sunlight can creep in during early morning, this place for the most part is left in the shadows during the day. The ground is soft and silky, composed of very fine grains of dust that the wind and rain slowly chiselled from the rock which forms the basis of the giant arches.
13672: The remnants of plants that have lost their battle with this dry land lay here crumbling into nothing. A few weeds, that seem to need less moisture, continue to struggle between the occasional rains. The rain, which rarely falls, is never enough to satisfy all. North and east, the Misty Mountains loom ominously overhead.
13673: Towering above the plains the Misty Mountains cast enormous shadows onto the barren ground below. Wind cascades down the slopes, blowing dust into the eyes of travellers. The mountains rise sheer to the north, prohibiting access in that direction. The base of the mountains continues eastward, while dry barren plains stretch to the west and south.
13674: Rising up from the plains is the base of the Misty Mountains yawning precariously overhead. Large broken boulders lie strewn about the landscape, warning the traveller to be wary of potential landslides. A chill dry wind blows down the mountainsides, causing dust to swirl about in small but rapid whirlwinds. The steep rise in the mountains to the north prevent any passage in that direction. To the east the Misty Mountains begin in earnest. and south dry plains begin to take hold.
13675:
A white wolf is here, prowling for something to eat.
A white wolf is here, prowling for something to eat.

The Misty Mountains climb high, on reaching their peak somewhere north of here. Their height provides an excellent view of the countryside south and west, which is mostly dry flatlands. Southward the mountains begin to give way to a wooded grove of trees. There appears to be no way to travel further north. East, the mountains continue ever onward.
13676: A mountain goat is here, jumping from cliff to cliff.

Tall grey snow-capped mountains prevent any further journey to the east and north. The Misty Mountains continue to the south and west, lessening as they fall to the plains. Fallen broken boulders litter the ground, an indication of the threat that rockslides occur frequently here.
13677: A field vole has frozen to the spot, sensitive to your presence.

These drying and decayed plains bear witness to the difficult conditions of this area. The severe and unforgiving winds that blow down from the Misty Mountains have stripped away the fertile soil, leaving these plains barren. Only a few sparse bushes provide distinguishing landmarks in the nearby vicinity. Off in the distance, to the northeast, the Misty Mountains rise up with their snow-capped peaks.
13678: A large rabbit looks peacefully at you, ready to dart away.

Strewn about the landscape, large rocks and boulders begin to form the base of the Misty Mountains. The ground here is rocky and very little grows except perhaps the occasional shrub. To the west, barren plains begin to take hold of the landscape, while a wooded grove starts up to the south.
13679:
A bloodthirsty orc stands here, hell-bent on battle.
A bloodthirsty orc stands here, hell-bent on battle.

Death, decay and decadence are this cave's decor. Stains of blood mixed with orkish draught create ugly patterns on the floor and walls. A musty odour hangs in the air like a heavy fog. Rotten bones of an old kill lie under a bench, badly decomposing.
13680:
A bloodthirsty orc stands here, hell-bent on battle.
A bloodthirsty orc stands here, hell-bent on battle.

The musty smell of rotten meat lingers in the air. Two piles of torn human clothes have been arranged to soften the floor for sleeping. The clothes seem to harbour several parasitic organisms which feed on the ripped fibres. No light or fresh air enters here, and one can assume these clothes may have belonged to the same victims as the bones in the nearby lair.
13681: A mountain goat is here, jumping from cliff to cliff.

The Misty Mountains continue their climb north, reaching their summit somewhere far to the north of here. From this vantage point, one is afforded an excellent view of the surrounding lands south and west of this location. To the southwest the mountains begin to give way to a wooded grove of trees.
13682: Growing in the shade of the Misty Mountains plains take hold, although somewhat sparse and dry. They provide little shelter however, from the strong winds that blow down from high up in the snow-capped mountains. Rocky rubble, from the nearby mountain base, has fallen here, littering the landscape with countless boulders. To the south trees begin to take hold, and thicken into a grove.
13683: A wolf cub happily plays here.

The plants here grow in the shade of the great Misty Mountains looming overhead to the north. Their shelter breaks down many a strong wind and protects from what can be a burning sun. Rocky rubble, from the nearby mountain's base, has been tracked here.
13684: A group of young pines try to take seed in this place. Not much taller than ten feet they provide little shade nor shelter from occasional winds. Whether they will survive to tower above is doubtful given the lack of any such woods in the nearby lands. The arid nature of the land has perhaps already sealed their fates. The plains continue in all directions, only stopped eastward by the towering mountains.
13685:
A rabid raccoon stands here, frothing at the mouth.
A wolf cub happily plays here.

Not as dry here as to the north, this land is bit more hospitable. A cluster of prickly weeds catches dirt and the dried up leaves of some nearby plants that have died from lack of nourishment. Some rocks too heavy to lift are embedded here in the dirt.
13686: The plain is rather dry and desolate. Little vegetation can be seen, save for an occasional patch of grass here and there. Rocks and stones, however, can be found in a multitude. To the west and south, you see a trail bending around the plains.
13687:
Prickly, white-stemmed plants, with blue flower heads grow in abundance.
A boar cub is playing here, and exploring the wide world.

What vegetation lies here is sadly withering. Lack of moisture in the air and the soil condemns these few small plants and shrubs to a short life, if one at all. Many of the smaller growths have already succumbed. To the east more plant life struggles to survive. Further east, the Misty Mountains provide an ominous backdrop to these plains.
13688: Mountain peaks loom high above the base of these Misty Mountains blocking any view one might have to the east. Glancing eastward, one can see the entrance to a mine under an overhang in the rock. To the west, a wooded grove of trees takes hold and flourishes. Looking southward, a cliff face falls away before your feet. At its base a small stream tumbles along, on its journey to the sea.
13690: Rows upon rows of slow rolling hills, covered in a thick carpet of grass, stretch ever outward in all directions, save north - where the running of water over rocks can be faintly heard, out of the steep rocky mountains. A rich woodland grove sprouts up to the west. The hills flatten out into plains as they stretch south.
13691: The golden hue of short-cropped grass, rolling over wave upon wave of hill after hill, continues outward in all directions. A grove of trees stands to the north-west, while rolling plains and foothills continue north and east, until the Misty Mountains. The hills flatten out southwards, joining the grassland.
13692:
A rather heavy-looking steel key lies on the ground.
A sturdy pack horse is standing here.
A sturdy pack horse is standing here.

The trail moves alongside the tiny brook to the south, paralleling the line of the towering Misties to the north. All around lies the giant expanse of plains, broken only occasionally by small groves of trees and some solitary hills. The path continues through the plains, the link between the Dunnish villages.
13693: Passing from east to west across lightly wooded plains, this faint trail is sometimes impossible to find due to lack of use. However, it appears to widen to the west, showing signs of recent activity there at least. Grassy plains dominate the landscape here, with a large copse of trees to the north forming the exception.
13694: Constant winds, drifting down from the Misty Mountains, blow across this trail kicking up dust into the eyes of travellers. The trail bends here, heading north and east. The confluence of two streams lies to the west, passing by a Dunlending settlement on its north bank.
13695: Gurgling as it runs by the village, the stream is joined by a small tributary from under the bridge northward. The water of this stream runs slow and deep, widening also. Aside from the sound of water lapping against stones, and the wind drifting across the water, this place can be rather quiet. A trail lies to the east, along the water's edge. South of here a large forest rises up, stretching south for many miles.
13696: A Faint Trail beside a Narrowing Stream

A small trail leading east from a Dunlending village bends southward, narrowing here due to infrequent use. A gently flowing stream lies beside the trail, but it bends to the north into a wooded grove of trees. Trees can be seen in all directions, threatening to join the larger forest to the southwest and consume these plains.
13697: Standing in the midst of a large copse of trees, little can be discerned about the outlying areas. Large conifers rise up around you, dropping their cones onto travellers as a gentle breeze blows through the forest. Animals of all shapes and sizes can be seen darting back and forth among the trees.
13698: The hills here are relatively small compared to the massive peaks of the Misty Mountains in the northeast, but are high enough to provide a good view of the land. A rich woodland grove sprouts up to the west, while rolling plains and foothills continue east, until they reach the base of the mountains. The sound of running water echoes to the north.
13699: A tall plant with a perfectly smooth stem gracefully marks the landscape.

Small pine trees line the edges of a swift flowing brook. The water's edge, lined with algae and water lilies, teems with insect life. To the east and west the stream continues. The trees begin to fade to the south, where rolling plains pick up and dominate the landscape.
13700:
A fallow deer is grazing peacefully here.
A buck runs swiftly from place to place, looking about warily as it grazes.
A fallow deer is grazing peacefully here.

Lofty conifer trees rise high up high into the air, while a thick web of foliage blankets the ground, leaving little to no trace of visitors. The base of the Misty Mountains can just be seen peaking out from the trees north and east of this grove. The faint sound of rushing water can be heard to the south and the thinning grove continues west.
13701: Tall pine trees stretch overhead and a thick mesh of foliage carpets the ground. The conifers densely begin to crowd together to the south. North and west, the trees abruptly stop and give way to a vast expanse of open plains. The grove continues east, just before the mountains.
13702: Wide, open plains immediately surround and encompass you. A little distance to the north, the plains begin to thin out. Further north, the Misty Mountains rise high up into the sky. To the east and south, a woodland grove springs up and continues south. The fertile plains continue westward.
13703: The grass grows low and is cropped short by strong winds, which persistently blow down from somewhere high up in the Misty Mountains. Trees begin to spring up south and east of here, forming a small woodland to the southeast. A trail, making a slow bend around these plains, lies to the south and west.
13704: Bending back and forth across the open plains, the trail continues west and south from here. To the northeast, the plains dry out as they approach the base of the Misty Mountains. Southwest, however, the plains are green and lush with life.
13705: Following the bend, this trail makes its way east and south alongside a great distance of plains, both to the north and to the south. However, the plains to the north appear more dry and arid. A steady wind sweeps across the ground, cracking and hardening the exposed soil.
13706: A meadowed plain of short lush green grass lies here and stretches north, whilst the northern horizon is dominated by the Misty Mountains. The grass grows higher to the west, while a well worn trail lies north and east of here, curving along the outside of the plains.
13707:
The rabid raccoon stands here, frothing at the mouth.
A lone hawk soars high above you.

A lush, green plain of short green grass grows here and stretches far north into the endless plains. Far to the north and east the horizon is dominated completely by the vastness of the Misty Mountains. The grass grows higher to the west, while a well-worn trail lies south of here running east to west.
13708:
A sturdy pack horse is standing here.
A large rabbit looks peacefully at you, ready to dart away.
A lone hawk soars high above you.
A sparrow is flapping around on the ground.

A never-ending expanse of fertile green plains unfolds before you. This grassland meadow stretches far to the west and north, where it appears to stop at the base of the Misty Mountains. The plains continue to the west, while a well-worn trail lies to the south, bending north.
13709: A grove of towering conifer trees yawns over you to the east, while a lush green meadow lies to the west, this well travelled trail slicing down the middle. The pathway runs north from here, where it bends west, and to the south where it appears to intersect another path.
13710:
A tree-snake lies wrapped around one of the tree branches.
A tree-snake lies wrapped around one of the tree branches.
A tree-snake lies wrapped around one of the tree branches.

Large, looming conifer trees push close together, slowing progress in every direction. A carpet of lush green vegetation clings to the earth. The trees appear to thin out toward the west, while densely continuing east and north. A low stone wall prevents progress any further south.
13711: Standing amid a towering grove of pine trees, one might feel rather small in comparison. Water, cascading through tree roots and rocks can be heard throughout this grove, as the brook makes its way north. The trees appear to thin to the east and south, while densely continuing west and north.
13712: A rabbit is here eyeing your presence warily.

The running of water cascading through rocks and tree roots can be heard, and a small brook can be seen flowing through this grove of towering pine trees. The trees appear to thin to the east and north, while densely continuing west and south.
13713:
A brown snake watches you.
A rabbit is here eyeing your presence warily.

Tall close-knit pine trees crowd in from all directions, impeding but not altogether halting travel through this grove. A lush mat of green foliage carpets the ground, hiding the footprints of past travellers. The trees appear to thin out toward the north and west, while densely continuing south and east.
13714: Rocks and pebbles, deeply embedded into the roadway, give evidence of heavy use. The trail continues south, bending around a grove of towering pines, and west across a wide expanse of open plains. Far in the distance to the southeast faint wisps of smoke can be seen rising into the sky.
13715: Constant winds drift down from high up in the Misty Mountains, sweeping across these plains. The path that lies before you is at no risk of becoming obscured as signs of recent use have packed down the soil into an easily recognisable trail. Far off in the east, faint wisps of smoke can be seen rising into the sky.
13716: An elk cow gazes coldly at you, chewing on a small branch.

Two well-trodden trails meet here, one moving in an east to west fashion, the other coming from the north and dead-ending to form a three-way intersection. Southward, the edge of a large forest can be seen and before it a stream, fragmenting into several tributaries as it winds its way west across the plains. To the east, a small Dunlending village lies by the river.
13717:
A squirrel scampers around here, looking for nuts from the trees.
A swallow flies high above the ground.

A stream running near the forest edge continues its path west, flowing in from the Misties to the east. South of the stream an enormous forest takes root and continues south as far as the eye can see. The stream appears to fork to the east. A settlement can be seen to the northeast, surrounded by a primitive wall of wooden stakes.
13718: Standing on the forest edge, large conifer trees loom over you, threatening to consume travellers who head south into the heart of the woods. Pinecones lie strewn about the ground near the edge of a stream, which runs just north of here. A trail runs on the other side, west to east, and looks fairly well used. Both east and west of this location, the forest border continues.
13719: This well-trodden trail, tracing next to a stream running east and west, winds its way alongside a great expanse of plains to the north and a large forest to the south. To the east it appears another trail crosses this one. Beyond that smoke rises from a village.
13720: A sparrow is flapping around on the ground.

Signs of recent use are evident everywhere along this trail, as footprints have packed down the fertile soil into a well-worn path. A gently flowing stream follows alongside the trail. Far to the east, faint wisps of smoke can be seen rising up into the sky. To the north, expansive plains open before you while a large forest begins to take hold to the south.
13721: A woodpecker is here, tapping on a tree.

The forest begins to thicken immediately to the south, making travel difficult. On the other hand, to the north a well-worn trail moves east to west beside a gently flowing stream. Otherwise, the forest dominates the scene, its huge conifer trees intimidating the inexperienced traveller. The forest border continues both to the east and the west.
13722:
A brown snake watches you.
A brown snake watches you.

Tall and mighty conifer trees surround you near the forest edge. Pinecones lie scattered about as squirrels scurry along gathering food and storing it in tree trunks. The forest immediately thickens southward, while the wooded border continues east. To the north a well-worn path travels east and west beside a stream.
13723:
A large elk is standing here, chewing grass and leaves.
An elk cow gazes coldly at you, chewing on a small branch.

Standing at the forest's edge, the inexperienced traveller might reconsider entering such a densely populated gathering of pine trees for fear of becoming lost. The forest immediately begins to thicken to the south, while the forest border continues eastward. To the north a well-worn path travels east and west beside a stream, which bends west before heading south again.
13724: Curving gently from the north to the west, the current of this slow moving forest stream begins to quicken as other rivulets and tributaries join the flow. The stream gives way to fertile plains to the north, while an enormous forest begins to take hold south of here, stretching as far as the eye can see.
13725: Following a quiet stream south and east, this trail is hardly discernible, even while being travelled. The stream appears to gather speed as it widens, south of here. An endless sea of lush green plains unfolds to the north and a gentle breeze coming from the Misty Mountains far to the northeast creates waves across the waist high grasses.
13726: A strong wind blows down from the mountains most of the time, across waves of waist high grass, rippling across the plains. A worn path lies to the south beside a stream, making its way east. An endless sea of lush, green plains stretch out in all other directions. Far off to the northeast, the Misty Mountains provide a backdrop to the plains.
13727: Waves of waist high grass ripple as the wind blows across these plains. A endless sea of lush green plains stretch out in all other directions, the grass growing taller to the south and thinning out a bit as one travels to the north.
13728: A field vole has frozen to the spot, sensitive to your presence.

An immense, open grassland broadens before you in all directions. A few sparsely interspersed trees rise up from the carpet of grass, dotting the landscape. To the north a small path meanders from east to west. East and south the vast green plains continue.
13729: This path shows signs of more age then use. Only a few brave blades of nearby grass dare cross into the dirt marked for travel. A few stones, more the size of pebbles, have been ground into the dirt. The trail continues east and west from here. Plains lie on both sides of the path, the south being lush and green with life, while dry and arid to the north.
13730: A large rabbit looks peacefully at you, ready to dart away.

The arid soil here barely manages to accommodate even the wild weeds, which thicken to the south. Those that do grow siphon every bit of water out of the soil and leave the surrounding ground dry and dusty. To the south and west, a worn trail bends around the plains.
13731: The wind, when it blows, lifts the layer of fine dust-like topsoil that covers this land. The dirt has completely infiltrated all of the few grassy weeds and bushes growing in this dry domain, making everything a near uniform grey-green colour. Rain is always welcome here, although it soaks into the dry land almost as quickly as it falls to the ground. South of here, a faint trail cuts through the plains, seeking a more hospitable landscape.
13732: The path continues to guide the way across wide-open plains. Looking down, one can see the trail's recent use, marked by scores of footprints. To the north the plains appear to dry out, leaving brown stunted grass. Southward, the grasslands become thick and lush with green growth. The faint trail continues west and east, where it begins to widen.
13733: A vast sea of lush grassland stretches west and south from here. Several lone trees rise up from the waves of green grass, dotting the landscape. To the north and east a trail bends around these open plains. Far off to the northeast, the Misty Mountains provide a backdrop to the plains.
13734: A brown furry gopher is here, ready to dive back underground.

A tall, luxuriant sea of waist high grass ripples as the wind gusts across this prairie. Plains stretch out in every direction as far as the eye can see, the grass growing higher to the south and shorter as one makes their way further north.
13735:
A brown furry gopher is here, ready to dive back underground.
A finch flies low above the ground.
A large rabbit looks peacefully at you, ready to dart away.

Waist-high grass covers the plains, a deep lush carpet for the land. A worn path lies to the south beside a stream, making its way west. An endless expanse of fertile, green plains stretch out in all directions as far as the eye can see. Far off to the northeast, the Misty Mountains provide a backdrop to the flatlands.
13736: Moving east and west, a worn path, closely following a gently flowing stream, advances across a great span of plains to the north and an immense forest to the south. A steady wind sweeps the ground at all times, kicking up dust into the traveller's eyes.
13737: A pack horse (Rood) is standing here, ridden by you.

Passing from east to west along a stream, the worn path widens as it moves eastward. Vast open plains stretch far to the north, right up to the foot of the Misty Mountains. A huge forest begins to take root to the south of the trail, the towering trees drawing nourishment from the stream.
13738: An endless sea of green grass stretches as far as the eye can see. Waves of it, lush and thick, ripple as the wind blows across these plains. The grass grows slightly higher and wilder to the west, intermingling with the occasional bush and thick shrub. A worn path lies to the south beside a stream, making its way west to the sea.
13739: A field vole has frozen to the spot, sensitive to your presence.

A ceaseless expanse of plains stretches before you, a light wind rippling across the grasslands and causing ripples in the undergrowth. The lush sea of green plains continues in all directions as far as the eye can see, growing taller to the southwest and cropped shorter to the northeast. A trail can be seen to the north, bending south and heading east.
13740: Paved firmly into the ground by thousands of footprints, this trail begins a winding descent from north to south. As the path bends east, looking south, one can see an endless see of lush plains. Wildlife can be seen scurrying through the plains, their heads dipping in and out of the tall grasses.
13741: The path begins to widen here, as signs of recent use increase. The trail continues west and south. Plains lie on both sides of the path, but appear green and lush to the southwest, while dry and arid to the north. Far off to the northeast, the Misty Mountains rise high into the sky.
13742:
A wolf cub happily plays here.
A wolf cub happily plays here.
The mother wolf stands here, protecting her young cubs.

Sparse, barren plains unfold in all directions, becoming withered and decayed to the north and east. The barren flatness continue west, while a small faint path burrows its way through the dry-lands south of here. To the northeast, the Misty Mountains rise up before you.
13743: At the Bottom of a Long Shaft
A simple wooden chest is here.

Deeply embedded scars mar the walls and roof, caused by the clawing of picks over time. Some cuts are as deep as a dwarf's arm from elbow to wrist. The treacherous slope would be near suicide to ascend except for the most expert of climbers, being an almost vertical natural fissure. East is a junction in the mines, with four tunnels running from it.
13744: The corpse of a large bat is lying here.

Cobwebs hang from the top of this intersection, covering all but the door to the east. The tiny spiders who spun them are not readily apparent, probably hiding in the many small cracks in the stone. The web fragments are so frail now they almost disintegrate when touched. South the tunnel dips downwards towards a dead-end, while west and north the mining tunnels continue.
13745: Clumps of recently moved rock and dirt are carelessly strewn about the floor of this passage, in sharp contrast to some neater piles that seem to have laid untouched for years. Deep chops made by a sharp pick are visible on both sides of this tunnel. Clearly these random marks were not made by the mine's diligent dwarven creators.
13748: A pool of darkish water has formed in a depression of the stone.

Much of the dirt floor has turned to mud here. The walls, while keeping drier than the floor, also have a moist muddy quality. The wooden posts that hold this earthen tunnel in place have been weakened by the water seeping through from the ceiling above. It seems to be a constant drip, gathering into a muddy pool near the southern wall.
13749: Although the roof and walls of this tunnel are normal for a Dwarven mine, being of unpolished stone and wooden props, the floor has been smoothed into complete flatness. West an iron door leads into the main mines, while east the tunnel turns into a small chamber.
13750:
A large stone chest is here.
A small oaken table has been set here.
A large bookshelf sits against the wall.
An aged man with a cadaverous appearance is here.

Cut to a smooth chamber, this cavern originally belonged to the Dwarven miners who worked the caves. Certainly whoever now occupies it is no Dwarf, judging by the paintings hanging here. There is various furniture around the room, and many old scrolls and books. A table on the eastern wall holds various flasks, although what is inside is not clear.
13752: A low cliff overhang hides a dark opening in the side of the mountain where the ground has been artificially levelled. The rock surrounding the entrance is grey and dull, aiding little support or shelter to the flora that battles to survive in the windswept heights. Towering above the overhang loom the desolate peaks of the Misty Mountains, like giant stone sentinels watching over the lands beneath them.
13753: Three tunnels meet at an intersection that was once a busy distribution centre for goods and tools going about in the mine. A stone ceiling curves gracefully overhead, the craftsmanship of its constructor well-preserved over time. Even the finely chiselled corners of the granite that meet in the centre are still sharp and unspoiled. As the mine was abandoned years ago, the tunnel has now been filled with dust and cobwebs, and each step taken whirls up the dust that hangs silent in the air until caught in the webs.
13754: The dusty tunnel comes to a sudden stop on a ledge, looking down a fissure in the stone. The smooth walls of the fissure are near vertical and very narrow, making any climb very dangerous. It might be possible to find enough hand-holds to descend, but there is no route up. The fissure narrows above, too thin for even the smallest dwarf.
13755: This tunnel, once crafted with skill and persistence by the Dwarves, is now abandoned. Once the tunnel was swarming with busy miners transporting minerals found on the lower levels. The air is thick with dust and cobwebs here, making breathing tiresome and your throat dry. In a corner you see a heap of broken tools and oily rags, presumably left when the mine was abandoned.
13756: The corpse of *a Half-Elf* is lying here.

This wooden lift is no work of great craftsmanship. The maker of the lift can not have had much skill with wood, and the well-worn planks forming the floor have not been maintained in years. The sound of creaking beneath your weight is not enough to cause alarm though, as the planks are made of oak strong and thick enough to last. On the western and southern sides of the lift are openings in the six foot fence through which to leave the lift. On its eastern side is a small but noticeable metal socket.
13757: Cobwebs hang from the walls and ceiling, however even the small spiders that once spun them have abandoned the mines. Piles of stone and ore are all around as if the mine had been suddenly abandoned. The glint of valuable ore sticking out through gashes in the walls beckons travellers to collect some of these riches.
13758: The cracked dirt in the roof of this tunnel does not inspire confidence that it will not collapse. However, taking into consideration that it has stood the test of so much time already, it will most likely continue to bear the weight of the earth above. Carved places in the walls show this mine to be still laden with minerals. As with the connecting corridors, this place appears to be long abandoned.
13759: This nook has been undisturbed for many years. A few badly aged tools lay propped against the wall. Should someone use a pick or shovel on the ancient wooden supports, the twine that connects the wood to rock would no longer hold the stone's weight. The wood itself is aged, but having once been well-carved it still maintains its strength. The mine itself is still rich with ore, with small side passages leading into the lode.
13761:
A malevolent bat hangs from the ceiling.
A malevolent bat hangs from the ceiling.
A malevolent bat hangs from the ceiling.
A malevolent bat hangs from the ceiling.
A malevolent bat hangs from the ceiling.
A malevolent bat hangs from the ceiling.
A large bat is here, hanging in the darkness.

A tunnel hewed with great precision and skill runs through the dark mountain. It was clearly devised, crafted and used by dwarves, to gain access to the deep core of the mountain. The cold black stone on the floor is smooth, and would be perfectly level if not for the marks rendered by the countless feet that once worked in the mine. The tunnels have been abandoned for many years now, and a layer of dust has settled on the surface of the stonework.
13762:
A sturdy pack horse is standing here.
A sturdy pack horse is standing here.

The smell of horse manure, mixed with a musty earthen smell, assails the senses. Feet cannot help but track this mixture with them wherever they go. Bits of hay and feed lie strewn about the ground. The only exit appears to be south, through a wooden gate.
13763:
A large stone fireplace with a roaring fire warms the room.
A Dunlending hunter is here, stalking his prey.
A Dunlending hunter is here, stalking his prey.
A Dunlending Captain is here, overseeing his men.

Mounted on the walls are the heads of game, the chieftain's kills from nearby areas. Crude maps painted with dye made from local flowers are hung on the east wall, and several lie strewn about on a dark wood table, the dye being so faded they are unreadable. In the northern corner is a hearth made of stone, filled with wooden faggots. The only apparent exit lies to the south through a carved wooden door.
13764:
chest (here) :
a gold coin
a longbow
A wooden chest stands in the corner.

Hollowed out behind the map lies this small musty room, perhaps used to store the captain's trophies or treasures. The earthen floor is smooth and flat, showing signs of little or no use. The only exit from this room appears to be back west, through the map hung on the wall.
13765:
A small campfire burns here, its low flames giving off only a little light.
An old man is resting here.
*a Man* , wielding a broadsword, is sleeping here (shrouded).
A sturdy pack horse is standing here.

This tent show signs of being well used. A tanned hide drapes over the entrance flap to the north. The crude wooden furniture laying about the room is carved and simple. The focus of the room is a stone kiln, along the south wall, in which many pieces of pottery have been fired. It is aglow with light, casting shadows around the room.
13767: A domesticated pony, beast of burden to many, stands here.

A ramshackle wooden construction bridges the stream, allowing access to the village's eastern half. Simplicity of design makes this bridge of wood beams, knitted together with rope, very sturdy and functional. The beams show the wear of heavy hoof marks, worn in over many years. The craftsmanship of the bridge is not the most sophisticated, but still it is a source of pride for the inhabitants of the small settlement.
13768:
A clear spring babbles as cool water trickles out of the ground.
A pack horse is standing here, ridden by you.

An underground stream rolls through the plains nearby, and some of its waters are collected into a large pool here. Surrounding the pool a cart-worn dirt road leads east and west. An impressive lodge stands due north, while small tents lie to the south.
13769: A sturdy pack horse is standing here.

A set of sturdy wooded guard posts mark the entrance to this village. The hoof prints of many horses over time have made uneven dents in the ground. Bushels of hay stacked near the posts lie half-eaten. Several cow-hide tents lie to the south, the homes of this hillman people. A pinned horse corral lies due north, little used by a people unused to riding.
13770: A glittering stream runs gently westwards over a green field along the ridged side of a forest. The ice cold water murmurs as it changes direction around boulders and sunken logs sticking up above the surface of the water. The river bank to the south is isolated on both sides, bordered on one side by this river, the other by a large boulder.
13771: The forest kneels down to the stream here, creating a rocky outcrop just above the water. The scraggled bushes form a thick wall just before the steep bank, while east an enormous fallen boulder blocks the way. Strangely, no other boulders are anywhere in the vicinity. Far to the east the Misty Mountains can be seen rising like titans above the forest.
13772:
A bass swims here.
A fat carp swims here.

The gently flowing stream makes a sudden turn to the south and increases its speed as it hits the steep face of a rocky bank. Impressive stone walls of a stronghold rest high upon the steep river bank to the west. Far to the south a large forest can be seen beyond the river.
13773: A large rocky outcrop in the steep river banks forces the stream to bend here, creating much turbulence. The water is icy cold and fresh, and tastes like the crisp snow from which it melted. Fish beneath you can be seen struggling with the currents, many just managing to remain in the same spot without any headway. To the south a ridge climbs up into the forest, along which the river flows for many miles westward.
13774:
A large beaver is here, gnawing on a piece of wood.
A large beaver is here, gnawing on a piece of wood.

The waters become troubled and turbulent here, with some rocks jutting out from the streambed creating powerful flows and eddies. Salmon can be seen leaping over natural weirs and waterfalls, in an effort to return to their spawning grounds. From the north bank a pier protrudes out of a small village, ten feet into the river.
13775:
A blooming water-lily floats on the surface of the water.
A blooming water-lily floats on the surface of the water.

A wide pool of water with small mounds of sticks and branches dominates your view, with the trees sloping down to banks on each side. On the southern bank the trees extend out into the water, where the beaver's dam has caused the stream to burst its banks. Many of the small creatures can be seen scurrying about, along the dam and on the piles of wood in the water. The dam blocks further travel downstream, unless you clamber onto the banks to walk around it.
13776: A small dam blocks passage further upstream from here, beavers scurrying about its top. The dam is made from a variety of small sticks and branches, carefully managed into place by these industrious little creatures. Southwards the trees dip down to the stream, making progress in that direction possible, although the land looks quite marshy there. Westwards a stand of great willows can be seen, overhanging the river.
13777: A grove of willows gently bends over the stream, almost providing a roof above you. Boats of leaves float gently on the water, intermingled with the floating branches. The beds of reeds on the southern bank seem to be a hive of activity, providing a cacophony of sound. Behind the reeds the forest climbs up the very steep bank. Eastwards a dam can be seen clearly, a construction of countless branches and mulched leaves. Westwards the stream continues drifting along, downstream towards the sea.
13778:
A salmon swims here.
A brook trout is here, swimming in the current.

Floating logs gently bump and push you around, making it difficult to move in any direction. The river is full of wildlife - frogs can be seen sitting on the logs, croaking away looking for a mate. Other wildlife can be seen walking on the banks, or diving into the river. Fish can be seen idly swimming underneath you, carrying on with their lives oblivious to your presence. A small dam made from sticks is visible upstream from here.
13779:
A salmon swims here.
A brook trout is here, swimming in the current.

Flies and other water insects buzz over the river. Its flat calm surface is only interrupted by the occasional fish, giving off ripples that echo across the water.
