Every now and again a log or branch drifts past you on its voyage downstream. The river itself marks the boundary between plains and the woods, perched above you on a steep slope.
13780: The stream is a slow calm flow at this point, with the water clear enough to see the bottom a few feet away. Small fish can be seen darting under sunken timbers. The stream can be seen upriver, nearer to its mountain source, and westwards, where it lessens to trickling shallows. A trail fords the river there, continuing north into the plains and south into the woods.
13781:
Clusters of slender stems and tall leaves thrive in the mud and shallows.
A pack horse (Rood) is standing here, ridden by you.

The trail crosses a small stream here, the water shallow but very cold. The stream runs westward, away from its mountain source, its headway prevented by a small weir just west of here. On the south bank the forest continues, with a long overgrown trail barely visible. Constant woodland chirpings emanate from the trees, with fleeting glances at local fauna the only clue to their source.
13782:
A fallow deer is grazing peacefully here.
A beautiful and docile horse is standing here.
A pack horse (Rood) is standing here, ridden by you.

The worn path makes a long turn from west to north along a high, dark stone wall with small loopholes and stones projecting from its coping. The once partially cultivated ground is now overtaken by wild grass and small bushes giving it a deserted look.
13783:
A beautiful and docile horse is standing here.
A pack horse (Rood) is standing here, ridden by you.

The worn path forks in three as it approaches the wooden stakes of what looks like a village. One of the branches of the path heads straight east towards a large open area in front of the gate, while another travels north across a natural bridge over a fissure. To the west grasslands take hold, stretching far into the distance.
13784:
A mass of dark green leaves clings to a wall.
A pack horse (Rood) is standing here, ridden by you.

A worn path ends in a large flat area in front of a gate. Behind the clinging vines that grow on it, a glimpse of a small village can be seen. To the north a deep fissure breaks the line of the plains, but soon after the fissure the plains continue to dominate the landscape.
13785: A large rabbit looks peacefully at you, ready to dart away.

The grassy field changes into a muddy slope covered with ferns and osier as it gets closer to the stream. Large willows lines the stream where the ground is less damp. Some of the great trees have been cut down leaving only the stump to moulder away. North a deep crack in the earth blocks any passage.
13786: The ground gently slopes downward torwards a glittering stream to the south where ferns and osier grow luxuriant on the damp ground, attracting swarms of insects. A fresh wind coming from the open fields to the north makes the old willows sway to the beat of the wind.
13787:
A large stone fireplace with a roaring fire warms the room.
A swarthy Dunlending warrior is here, guarding his village against intruders.
A swarthy Dunlending warrior is here, guarding his village against intruders.
A Dunlending Captain is here, overseeing his men.

This is the tent of the village chief, a large dwelling with several small curtained rooms. It is barely furnished, with thick piles of furs providing the only seating. In the centre hang a few hunting trophies of the chief's younger days - deer antlers, boar tusks and even the skull of an orc. To the west a large tent flap leads out into the village.
13788: A swarthy Dunlending warrior is here, guarding his village against intruders.

The village centre is nothing special, merely a rounded area marked out with white stones around a central fire. To the east lies the largest tent in the settlement, an impressive dwelling of much wood and cow hide. South a tiny pier ventures out over the river, allowing the natives to fish and clean themselves.
13789:
A swarthy Dunlending warrior is here, guarding his village against intruders.
A Dunlending warrior stands here, guarding the gates.

You are behind the only gate, a flimsy construction of many wooden stakes roped together, of a small Dunlending settlement. A few tents stand on either side of the track, homes to these people. The track leads to the south where the centre of the village lies. Beyond it a river can be seen, where a small pier stands poking out through town walls.
13790: A rabbit is here eyeing your presence warily.

A small path leading through a once partly cultivated field makes a sudden turn by a small clump of rowans, heading down a slight slope to the south. Further down the slope, the ground is covered by ferns and brushwood where the sounds of water can be heard, streaming across the wide ford.
13791: The plains are covered with short, dry grass and gently slopes downwards to the south. In some spots, flat rocks lay bare due to the influence of erosion on the land. To the east the ground climbs abruptly down into a steep ridge, making travel difficult.
13792: Dry, billowing grass makes a rustling sound as the wind catches it for as far as the eye can see. The lack of anything but plains makes this area quiet and desolate. A large boulder is here providing shelter from the wind that rushes through the plains off the Misty Mountains.
13793: A very old and apparently dying tree stands here in solitude casting long, dreary shadows on the billowing grass that covers the vast plains. This part of the plains changes little, with nothing but rolling plains as far as the eye can see. The brown-green grass sways gently in the breeze all around you.
13794:
A rabbit is here eyeing your presence warily.
Cromdreath the Mountain Troll (CC) is standing here.

The lush green grass forms an endless carpet over these lands. Several rocks are wedged deep into the ground partially concealed by high grass. Some of the blades of grass have been scarred by the wind pusing them against the jagged rocks. To the south the silhouette of a large tree stands out against the horizon.
13795: A myriad grasses and shrubs mixed with some colourful flowering plants spring from the ground here. In all directions the land is surrounded by healthy and blooming plantlife. Every now and then a number of small animals scurry along the ground, soon disappearing into the dense undergrowth.
13796: A pack horse (Rood) is standing here, ridden by you.

At one time, this trail might have seen quite a lot of use, possibly leading to another of the network of Dunlending villages. Now all that is left is an untrodden path, quickly being eaten away at by weeds and grasses. Occasionally the feet of a lone hunter will beat this track, but most of the footprints left are those of migrating widlife.
13797: A pack horse (Rood) is standing here, ridden by you.

Few feet have worn down this path in recent years. The hard packed soil of ages past is beginning to crack under the sun and rain that fall upon it, and is overgrown heavily. The grass grows almost to a man's height in parts, limiting visibility north and south.
13798: A pack horse (Rood) is standing here, ridden by you.

It is impossible to see farther than a few feet into the healthy grasses that surround the southern side of this trail. The vigour of growth there is strong, that of a well-watered land. Eastwards the trail bends around the borders of a field of crops, one tended but now left to grow wild.
13799: The crops of the long-gone Dunlendings still grow here, thick and healthy in the verdant Dunland plains. Over to the east is a ruined farmhouse, now filled with the crops it was once built to tend. Round the north and west borders of the crops runs an old Dunlending trail, now little used.
13800: From the large hill to the northeast much water is gathered, and it makes its way in tiny streamlets into this brook, where it continues through the plains south. The water is clear and cold, bubbling over the rocky stonebed. The river banks have been invigorated by a source of water in this windswept plains, and on both sides the lands teem with wildlife. Above you, on the western bank, is the remaining wall of a long-ruined farmhouse.
13801: The trail runs north, into the ruins of a hilltop settlement, and south along the edge of an enormous patch of brushland. The hill, solitary in the plains, gathers much of the rainwater from around here, and west a small stream begins as a result. East is the edge of the brush - thick, black and extremely dense.
13802: Like withered arms the thin branches of these haggard bushes have intermingled, making movement through this area a real difficulty. The undergrowth grabs onto you at every opportunity, and it takes a real effort to move. Underfoot lies a dusty but hard topsoil, the brush sucking up most of the water that falls to earth. North and west the brush ends, small trails running along the borders.
13803: While normally little seems to grow in these arid windswept lands, the brush here is an exception. It is a hardy growth with little leaves and thin but strong black branches, which grow in all directions it seems. They mingle with each other, creating something not short of a wall in some directions. To the south the land falls away steeply into a depression, filled with more of the same dense black brush.
13804: Shrubs and bushes lie scattered about these plains, soaking up every last drop of moisture the frequent rain brings. To the west, the bushes cluster together forming a thick mesh, perhaps hindering travel. Far off to the east, the Misty Mountains rise up from the hills, their tops piercing the clouds. The trail continues north and east from here.
13805: Prickly, white-stemmed plants, with blue flower heads grow in abundance.

One of many connecting the small villages of northern Dunland, this path is not frequently trodden these days. The undergrowth on both sides has encroached on it in parts, the thick overhanging bushes making movement tiring. To the west and south the trail continues, winding its way through the plains.
13806: A worn path guides the way through high grass covering the vast plains. Small rocks scattered alongside the path looks like they have been thrown aside to make a clear passage on the trail. To the south are some small bushes growing reluctantly in a shallow depression.
13807: A rabbit is here eyeing your presence warily.
Wide open grasslands reach as far as the eye can see. The tough, green grass bends gently in a light breeze. Some small bushes grow reluctantly in a small depression to the north.
13808: A sharp-eyed hawk is here stalking some prey.

Flatlands covered with thick grass and small green bushes extend for miles in every direction. Through the tough, green grass that waves lazily in the wind, scattered rocks can be seen on the floor making travel difficult. The grasslands continue to the north, while the plains open up in all other directions.
13809: A brown furry gopher is here, ready to dive back underground.

The plains gently slope downwards to the south where the ground is covered with billowing grass. Sharp rocks and large boulders lie scattered on the ground, impeding any movement. To the west a steep valley breaks the line of the plains, but it is impossible to get down there from here due to the steep valley walls.
13810: A large depression cuts deep into the billowing grasslands where the view over the surrounding plains is blocked on all sides by the high edge. From here only the face of the depression and the sky are able to be seen. The bottom of the depression is covered with large rocks, and the ground is like clay between the boulders. It is possible to move north from here up into the plains, and west into a deep fissure.
13811: Cut clean into the plains like an axe mark on a tree, this crevice is deep and narrow. At its base the light is weak, and movement tricky due to the countless rocks littering the ground. Eastwards the crevice gives way to a depression in the plains, and easier ground. West the light is too weak to distinguish any features.
13812: Above you the sides of the fissure join and form a natural bridge several dozen feet wide. Here, well below the level of the plains, light does not reach, and it is dank and tepid. Debris, fallen from above, is strewn about the ground, requiring some effort to clamber over. The fissure lightens to the east and west slightly, but still the towering rock walls loom above.
13813: Not much more than twenty feet wide, the fissure in the plains runs for many miles. Here, some hundred feet down, the light is very weak and it is easy to stumble over the countless pieces of fallen rock. West the fissure opens up slightly, while east it darkens further. A strong breeze whistles through here constantly, making it hard to hear anything.
13814: A swallow flies high above the ground.

A depression forms here, well below the level of the plains. Little grows at its base, except for the occasional hardy shrub or thistle. South the valley towers unclimbable above you, while north the slope climbs gently enough to move with little difficulty. West is a more gentle route up to the flatlands above, while the valley narrows and becomes a fissure to the east.
13815: Vast and mundane grasslands, unsheltered from wind and rain, extend in every direction but east, where the earth gently drops down into a valley where only a few small bushes have managed to get a foothold on the barren land. Close to a large rock lie the scattered, charred remains of a campfire, used fairly recently. Northwards a hill lies in the plains, where a gloomy cave can be seen on its steepest side.
13816: A steep ridge in the west breaks the monotony of the grassy fields that are covered with high, billowing grass. The surroundings make the ridge look rather majestic as it climbs high into the sky. Running along the edge of the ridge is a small glittering brook lined with ferns.
13817: A very steep ridge running in a curve from east to south creates a windy turbulence as the wind whirls up off the face of the ridge. Small rocks are scattered in the high grass and the lack of vegetation keeps the surroundings barren.
13818: Vast, desolate plains covered with tall grass billowing in the wind extend in all four cardinal points. In certain spots some wasted and weather-beaten bushes have gathered in clumps providing shelter to small animals and birds. To the east, a brook can be seen winding its way across the green grasslands.
13819: Large, scattered bushes dominate this part of the otherwise grassy plains, providing shelter for the surrounding wildlife. A small, murmuring brook lined with ferns runs gently around the base of a hill from the east to the south.
13820: A large hill rises above the expanse of the plains, providing an unobstructed view of the horizon. A strong wind blows off the face of the hill, constantly changing direction, causing little vegetation to gain a foothold on the hill. To the south the hill steeply descends to the plains, too difficult to climb. A mound of stones forms a pattern on the floor of the hill, indicating this hill has some strategic importance.
13821: A boar cub is playing here, and exploring the wide world.

These are very fertile plains covered with tough, green grass. The same scenery stretches monotonously in most directions, interrupted only by the depression to the south. Rocks are scattered on the ground here, mostly buried under grassy mounds.
13822: A fallow deer is grazing peacefully here.

Tough, green grass stretches across these plains as far as the eye can see leaving little room for other species of vegetation to thrive. In some places various herbs and richly coloured flowers have rooted, making the plains more coulorful than the rest of the plains. To the south a narrow fissure blocks movement, beyond which the grasslands restart.
13823: A rough trail cuts through the grassy plains from north to south. Holes and bumps made from years of rain and horses makes travelling less then ideal. The worst parts of the trail have been temporarily repaired to make it passable, but none the more smooth. South the trail continues over a fissure in the plains, where the walls draw close and join for about twenty feet, creating a natural bridge.
13824: A tough, green grass covers the fertile plain about you. Even though little else grows here, one can easily find numerous herbs and flowers among the dominating, rough green grass. To the west a well worn trail can bee seen winding its way through the plains, while to the south a deep fissure blocks movement.
13825: The plains here slope steeply downwards to the south into a deep depression. Landslides caused from heavy rains have removed most of the dirt from the slopes, revealing the naked cliff that lies underneath. Vast, wide open grasslands lie to the east, where the Misty Mountains can be seen far on the horizon.
13826: While passable, the tall bushes certainly pose a threat for travellers. Their thin twisty branches keep all visitors at a safe distance, except perhaps those small enough to crawl through the bare patches. Leaves and other foliage carried on the wind seem to catch in these large plants and stick within the branches, never to be carried free again.
13827: The skin and fur of small animals lay ensnared in the thin scratchy branches of many large shrubs. Passage through these plants is cumbersome at best. Some of the four-foot tall bushes have formed a jagged hedge several yards long and almost three feet wide.
13828:
A boar cub is playing here, and exploring the wide world.
A pack horse (Rood) is standing here, ridden by you.

A tiny worn trail through the flatlands borders the brush here, which runs for many miles north and east. It looks well trodden, used often as the brush is fairly impenetrable. Indeed to the north it grows so tangled and interwoven it would be impossible to enter there. The trail continues south and west, along the edge of the brush.
13829: The trail runs between the brushlands and the grasslands, the easiest route through the plains due to the difficulty of passing the brush. Dunlending trappers occasionally use this trail to move between their village and the best hunting grounds, and this keeps the undergrowth from encroaching totally.
13830: A boar cub is playing here, and exploring the wide world.

The plant life here flourishes whether in bloom or just teeming with green. The moist dark soil is rich with nutrients making this a haven for many different varieties of flora. The sweet smell of nectar lingers in the air emanating from what is left of fruit that proceed the blossoms.
13831:
A frog is standing here.
A frog is standing here.
A brook trout is here, swimming in the current.

Green shrubs and small sandy areas cover the area around the banks of the water. Taller grasses grow along the bank leaning their way over the flowing waters. The roots of trees along the bank give the ground support against the erosions the waters would bring.
13832: The waters that glide along the rocks here make a very low trickling sound. Plant growth here is healthy and thick. Several trees have begun to grow along the edges of the brook adding strength to the soil along the banks.
13833: The grasslands spread in every direction on and on without a visible end. Rocks make their place known jutting out of the ground and rising above the countless species of plants. You can see some of the rocks have been chipped away at, possibly in an attempt a travelling ranger made at giving directions toward a trail or secret cache.
13834: A boar cub is playing here, and exploring the wide world.

Flowers blooming into purples, oranges, and reds shimmer here, as the wind blows through them. It looks as though the very ground is bursting with life and vigour. The rich well-watered soil allows a huge variety of species to grow and live here, as witnessed by the countless animals rustling around you. Few are visible though, hidden in the lush undergrowth.
13835: A clean fragrance drifts up from a thick clump of leaves.

The well watered soil here is healthy enough to grow an unbelievable amount of varying flowers and shrub. Among the grasses flowers of purple and yellow and orange give a depth to the grasses that flow around them in the wind.
13836: The roots of a large old tree extend out into the water exposed in areas along the bottom of the brook where the water has washed the overlaying soil away. Shrubs of various size find their place around this tree. Birds often perch high in the tree making their presence known with their incessant chirping.
13837: Flowing slowly through the plains, the brook is still not that deep. Downstream it gathers more waters from around though, and becomes deeper and swifter. To the south the plains run for many miles, flat and uninterrupted. A path runs through them to the east, bordering a stretch of dense brush. Both sides of the stream seem to benefit from the water, for they bloom with vigour.
13838: Between the black brush and a small stream, this path makes its way north to south. It cuts a line between utterly different terrain - on one side the arid and impenetrable bushes, and on the other the verdant and well watered river banks. To the north it continues, making its way towards a large and solitary hill in the plains.
13839: A black pond of water is here.

The black brush here is utterly unyielding - it would take an army of strong axe-wielders to cut their way through it. Only east, back into the centre of the brushlands, is it even possible to move. It is wet here also, with at least a foot of mud in the bottom, making movement even slower. Above you the sides of the bowl-shaped depression slope steeply in, cutting off the skyline.
13840: A large dangerous looking green snake is coiled up here.

This long valley is well below the level of the surrounding land, and it is impossible to see anything beyond the lip. It is replete with the same grasping brush as elsewhere, combining with the muddy earth to make movement tricky. To the east and north the valley slopes are steep, and would require a fair effort to ascend. South the valley opens up to the brushlands, while west it plunges into a dark defile.
13841: The growth is far sparser here than further into the brush, where it becomes dense and impenetrable. Still it hinders movement, and a twisting route is needed to travel at any pace. East and north the plains open up, a trail of the Dunlending hunters running through them.
13842: The rocky ground and the constant wind make the plains rather arid and bare on the higher ground, with grass growing reluctantly elsewhere. A poor area for the local wild life, but it seems they have adapted as the area is filled with many small creatures. North the land drops into a sheer crack in the earth, while southwards a trail runs from west to east.
13843:
A finch flies low above the ground.
A pack horse (Rood) is standing here, ridden by you.

The trail continues uninterrupted through the plains from the east to the west. Only scattered rocks and sparsly growing brushwood prevent the worn route from making a perfectly straight line through the plains. The ground gently slopes downwards to the south where a glittering river runs at the edge of a luxurious green forest.
13844: A small trail stretches through the vast plains in an east-westerly direction. Small rocks and hollows makes the trail twist and turn in an unpredictable way across the grass covered plains. A gentle slope to the south ends in a clump of densly packed willow trees where the sound of streaming water can be heard.
13845: A fierce boar is here, making grunting noises.

A small worn trail winds through the damp plains covered with brushwood and osier. The vegetation makes the trail hard to access on foot and in some places a new path has been worn to avoid the roughest parts of the terrain. A large stack of recently cut logs lies on the bank of a river to the south.
13846: A pack horse (Rood) is standing here, ridden by you.

A worn trail winds through plains covered with osier and brushwood. Parts of the ground are particulary damp, making the clay path hard to access. The way to the south is hampered by some large, tightly packed willows, with the sound of rushing water prominent beyond.
13847: Small Stone Bridge over the Brook

A large rabbit looks peacefully at you, ready to dart away.
A pack horse (Rood) is standing here, ridden by you.

The remains of an old farm left in ruins for years lies here, divided in two by a brook. A stone bridge that once linked the two parcels of land still stands even now, long after the farm has fallen into disuse. The small brook flows past the farmyard and under the bridge, out into a larger river to the south. A small worn path, that shows signs of recent use, runs west to east through the middle of the farmyard.
13848: A small brook murmurs as it twists and turns out of the east into the small rocks and boulders that are scattered over the grassy plains. A steep ridge blocks passabe to the west and north, forcing the brook to take a turn to the south.
13849: A brook trout is here, swimming in the current.

A winding brook runs west, cutting through the flat grasslands. The water cuts deeper into the humus and is stagnant, bringing a scent of mire to the air. Eastwards the plains are verdant, full of teeming wildlife and billowing grass, while a trail travels across the land to the south.
13850: A fallow deer is grazing peacefully here.

High, billowing grass covers the monotonous field that extends through the plain. The only other vegetation that has managed to get a foothold on the unsheltered flat are a few windswept bushes struggeling to survive. A path lies south of here, while the plains continue to grow in all other directions.
13851: The everlasting plain is particulary rocky in this area, making travel risky and tiring. The only vegetation that manages to grow here is high grass that looks surprisingly lush for such a barren place like this. A path lies south of here, and grasslands continue in all other directions.
13852:
A fierce wolverine is here, snarling at you.
Cromdreath the Mountain Troll (CC) is standing here.

Various shrubs and bushes almost cover the trail at this point, but a path can still be inferred from the line in the trees. Two large oaks dominate the view eastwards, strangely solitary in the forest. Still, there does seem to be a gap large enough for a man or animal to squeeze through. Peering between the gap, trees stretch off into the distance. The trail continues south and the sound of water can be heard from the north.
13853: A rabbit is here eyeing your presence warily.

Moving between these two huge oak trees, ancient beyond compare, isn't easy due to the thick undergrowth. To the west the forest thins out some and the calls of wildlife can be heard. The sound of a river bubble away to the north, but a sheer cliff prevents access to it. A trail cuts through the forest to the south, with a large fallen tree in the way.
13854: The undergrowth is fairly sparse here, making progress a bit of a trial. Bright flowers form a carpet on the forest floor. and the sounds of the forest seem oblivious to your presence. A small anthill lies at the base of one of these majestic trees, the tiny creatures carrying on their daily scurrying without knowing or caring of the world outside their own. The trees continue to the east, while west two large oaks almost block the way. The river is visible below, although the bank is far too steep to descend down, and south the bushes grow so closely movement there would be impossible.
13855: Forest flowers provide a colorful carpet for the forest floor here, overlooking a river a long way down. The scent coming from the flowers is all pervasive, near intoxicating in its intensity. The trees here are fairly sparse, making progress through the forest not particularly strenuous. To the south the trees are covered in ivy and other climbing vines, and the undergrowth grows thicker there.
13856: The ground becomes soft and spongy underfoot, with a green moss covering the forest floor. Due to the boggy ground the trees are smaller here, maybe only six foot in height at the most. The moss when squeezed gives off a trickle of murky water, which runs down your thumb. The lay of the land rises to the west and the forest dries out, while eastwards it becomes even more waterlogged and marshy.
13857: The stream to the north has burst its banks, flooding the forest here. The ground has become so waterlogged that only a few trees can actually manage to grow to any height, the result being a natural split in the forest. The forest to the west looks slightly drier, though to the east the near marshland is continued. The area next to the stream has been trampled into mud by animals coming down to the stream for a drink, almost two feet of sticky bog to sink into.
13858: A blooming water-lily floats on the surface of the water.

The stream has fully burst its banks here and flooded the forest here, due to the beaver dam blocking it. A bank in the east lifts the forest away out of the water, while the trees get quite boggy to the west. Dense forest to the south prevents you from getting out of this water, full of fish darting between the underwater tree trunks.
13859: Drooping branches of the willow trees give some good shelter here. The grass underneath is lush and green, and makes a good resting spot. The forest begins to ascend a ridge to the south, passable but steep, but to the north the steep drop blocks access to the river. Eastwards dozens of yards of briars provide an effective barrier.
13860: A small clearing opens in this glade, lined with countless small delicate flowers. A small column of wispy white smoke rises up through the trees to the east, soon disappearing into the sky. Tightly packed trees and briars form a complete barrier to the west, while the steep cliff northwards looks impossible to climb down. At its base runs a river, following the line of the ridge for many miles.
13861:
A huge, smoking campfire is burning here.
A gnarled old man is standing here.

A camp isolated by the thick forest lies here. Animal skins are stretched on racks, and in the centre of the camp sits a small fire with a blackened pot suspended above it. Around the fire some logs have been laid as a primitive seat. Even though bits and pieces of equipment lie around you the site still seems to be organised after a fashion. A rocky scree to the east prevents access to the forest beyond, and in the south thick brambles prevent travel.
13862: The ground here rises to the south, lifting the forest away and up from the waterlogged riverbanks. Even though the slope is by no means sheer, it is still steep enough that if you lost your footing the possibility of tumbling down the hill becomes very real. The trees here are mostly conifers, pines and spruces for the most part, their fallen needles providing a spiky carpet for the forest floor. To the west a cliff falls sheer into a forested defile.
13863: Through a Break in the Forest

The trees form a dense semi-circle in front of you, wildlife in abundance as if protected by someone or something. They seem to have no fear of anybody and go about their business totally ignoring your presence. The trees are tall pines, pools of water scattered about in the gaps between their massive roots. The trunks of these trees are solid and look as hard as stone, weathered over many years.
13864: A large overhang of rock creates a secluded area in the cliff, providing the needed shelter for the forest's more delicate blooms to grow, and they thrive in this environment. The forest floor is awash with colour. Bees buzz from flower to flower ensuring this little garden's survival. The other reason for its thriving flora and fauna is the seclusion - enormous fallen tree trunks block the route to the south.
13865: A great wall of pines surround you to the north and east, their spindly needles covering the ground like a carpet of mottled green and brown. The trees are massive, at least one hundred feet high. If you could manage to climb one of these it would give a view of the forest for miles around. The trees are thinner in the south, eventually opening up into a small clearing.
13866: A small clearing opens up in front of you. The clearing cannot be more than twenty feet across at its widest point but the lush grass does offer a place to rest your weary feet or maybe set up camp. Tall thick conifers line the eastern and western border of the clearing and are too thick to penetrate. In the south a thick mass of bushes and briars are interwoven in a way that none save the small woodland creatures may pass.
13867: A rabbit is here eyeing your presence warily.

Birch trees dominate the forest here, fairly far apart and obstructing movement little. Westwards the forest climbs a small ridge, which runs for several miles north and south. About you small pools of water can be seen in small hollows, where rain water collects running off the ridge. In the east the undergrowth takes over again, a large section of briars preventing movement there. North grow the viciously thick brambles native to this area, utterly impassable.
13868: Thick patches of brambles sit amongst the trees to the south and west, utterly impassable unless you have months spare to cut through. Small insects and birds can be seen flitting from bush to bush. The insects go after the nectar of the flowers, and the birds go after the insects. To the east a dense grove of pines stands offering shelter to the animals and plants that live in the forest. North a great wall of pines almost encloses a large area of grass. A trickle of a stream runs along the ground and sometimes under it.
13869:
A tall and majestic oak tree grows here, surveying the lands about it.
On the tree, there is a perfect oak branch.

From this point above the trees on a huge outcrop of rock most of the forest is visible. To the east the Misty Mountains can be seen, their spine arching away to the north towards the haven of Rivendell. To the south the forest can be seen stretching to the plains. To the west, beyond the forest, the plains stretch out towards the horizon. The forest continues in all directions from this point, with hundreds of yards of brambles preventing access to the east.
13870: A small ridge rises out of the forest here, reaching a peak to the north. The trees thin towards the top, but in the south the forest resumes its typically dense nature. A massive solitary oak dominates the west, overhanging the steep ridge side. Down the ridge to the east a small stand of birch trees provide a brighter part of the forest. Flowers bloom in the cracks of the rock filling this area with a wealth of colour.
13871: The forest rises up a slope to the east here and a large chunk of rock can be seen jutting out from the forest. The trees surrounding you are mainly oaks and the ground is littered with acorns. To the west the ground is covered with a thick layer of briars and thornbushes, while to the north it falls away steeply into a gloomy defile. Squirrels can be seen scurrying up and down these mighty trees collecting acorns and carrying on in a way that makes no sense to you.
13872:
A roe deer is standing here, watching the terrain while chewing the vegetation.
A Dunlending forester is here gazing up at the tree tops.

The only way to move in these briars is to fight your way through, tearing your clothing to shreds in the process. The only route that can be taken from here is to keep heading east to a spot which doesn't look quite so thick. Berries adorn some of the bushes surrounding you, but getting to them is quite tricky as it would involve putting your hand into some of the densest thorns.
13873: At a Corner in the Forest
A roe deer is standing here, watching the terrain while chewing the vegetation.

A thick wall of briars and thornbushes prevents heading any further east, so dense you cannot see more than a yard into it. The trail seems to pick up again to the south and west on its meandering course through the trees. Wild berries cover the bushes to the east, although they are unfamiliar. A shiny hard purple colour, they might not be safe to eat. North the trees hang over the edge of a deep valley, whose depths are dark.
13874: A pack horse (Rood) is standing here, ridden by you.

The trail has almost completely disappeared here, leaving only a small gap in the trees to give its direction. A small rabbit looks up at you inquisitively before turning tail and darting back into its burrow. Birds can be seen around, fluttering between nests in the trees above you, their chirping relieving the eeriness that seems to fill the woods. A tall stand of trees is visible to the west, high on the horizon.
13875: A pack horse (Rood) is standing here, ridden by you.

The trail is almost unrecognizable here as the forest has almost completely encroached on it. Wild brambles and other shrubs and bushes nestle neatly beside the trees. To the south impenetrable thorns completely cover the land, while to the north lies the side of an old wooden cabin. Closer to the trail wild strawberries grow with prolific gusto in their hundreds. The trail can barely be made out heading in an east-west direction, overgrown so heavily as it is.
13876: A pack horse (Rood) is standing here, ridden by you.

The trail swings north and east here in a wide sweeping bend. The forest fauna pauses to look at you as you approach, before darting away into the undergrowth. To the south the trees take on a strange glossy sheen, from this distance exactly what is covering them cannot be made out. Moss-covered stumps are the only sign of man's intervention in this forest, although the fallen trunks have been removed.
13877:
A tall stag is here, grazing peacefully.
A swift and agile forest cat moves silently through the vegetation.

Near the trail the light is far less, the ground beginning to blend into the trees. Small woodland creatures can be seen darting away from the noise that you make, disappearing into the gloom. There are so many dead and dried twigs and branches on the forest floor that even the most skilled of stalkers would have trouble creeping up on their quarry.
13878: The trail makes a wide sweeping turn north and east here leading through the forest. Southwards it would be possible to leave the trail and enter the forest, but it looks very dark and dense - getting lost seems like a real possibility should you decide to enter. Birds can be heard singing in the trees around you but southwards seems devoid of life altogether.
13879: The trail bends south and west here. Set slightly back from it is an old and dilapidated cabin. The owners of the cabin are nowhere to be seen and it looks like none have been through here in a while, as many of the tracks left on the trail are those of animals. Shrubs surround the path towards the door in what looks like an overgrown garden. Small animals can be heard snuffling about in the vegetation, but are not visible under the thick bushes.
13880:
A wooden chest stands in the corner.
A heavy desk, made of solid oak, stands here.
A large cockroach is crawling over the floor.
A large cockroach is crawling over the floor.

The inside of the cabin is run-down badly, with holes in the roof and rotted walls of wood. Around are littered the remnants of this long abandoned abode. Several bits and pieces lie about giving some clues to the previous owners - a small wood-burning stove still stands in the corner of the room, and bare shelves line the walls.
13881:
Some roots lie here waiting to ensnare weary travellers.
Some roots lie here waiting to ensnare weary travellers.

Thick roots from the surrounding trees have covered the forest floor here, causing you to keep stumbling and lose your footing. Strangely the forest is silent, as there seems to be no animal or plant life here at all apart from these wandering roots. The trees to the east are different as their leaves have patches of brown running through them.
13882:
Some thick writhing vines whip all around you.
Some thick writhing vines whip all around you.

The trees here are covered in vines and ivy, slowly suffocating the life out of the forest. On closer inspection there seem to be small animal skeletons trapped between layers of these vines. The dark green leaves of the ivy almost give the appearance of leaves on the trees, but is betrayed by the barren or brown patches where the host tree is visible.
13883:
A forest spider is here crawling around.
A forest spider is here crawling around.
A mass of wriggling vines drops on you from the trees.

Tall and barren trees surround you, not encumbered with the ivy or vines of the nearby woods. The forest floor is still covered with vines and creepers, but all the trees are dead, their bark stripped away and their life essence sucked out by these aggressive, marauding creepers. Strange though, there are trees to the east which look quite healthy.
13884:
Massive roots shift uneasily all around you.
Massive roots shift uneasily all around you.
A mass of wriggling vines drops on you from the trees.

The trees seem to loom over you here, a definite threatening presence filling the valley. There are no vines or bushes here, just some roots stretching off to the west. These trees are huge and form a wide semi-circle. Out the corner of your eye you glimpse flickers of movement as if the trees were closing in.
13885:
A Dunlending forester is here gazing up at the tree tops.
A porcupine is waddling around here, its tail full of sharp quills.

Fallen leaves form a brown mushy carpet here. High above you a thick green canopy plunges the forest into a green tinted twilight. The trees here are deciduous oaks and chestnuts, growing fairly close together. Amidst the chaos of forest life the local fauna carries on, wary of your presence but not perturbed by it. The forest grows thicker to the south, while to the east an unclimbable ridge looms.
13886: The tall pines to the west and east are sparser here, allowing a whole new flora to thrive. Small shrubs and bushes clamour for room on the forest floor for the shafts of available sunlight, while under them many species of animal snuffle around the earth. Eastwards tall deciduous trees form a thick canopy above you and these small shrubs and bushes stop abruptly. Westwards a break in the trees can be seen, possibly indicating a trail of some sort. A huge ring of hewn stone blocks the exit to the south, while thick impenetrable briars block the route north.
13887: The forest takes on a sharp slant here and the trail has little option but to follow it. The sharp colour of flowers on bushes and atop thin stems serves to give a sense of depth to the deepening gloom of the forest on either side of you. There is a cluster of small shrubs to the west, powerfully scented. The trail continues north and south of you, disappearing into the forest in both directions.
13888: Waist high bushes surround you here, many of them adorned with succulent fruit and berries. To the north there is a break in the forest. Most of the bushes here are evergreens like holly, covered with bright red berries. From the west a strong sweet smell of forest flowers wafts in on the wind. Eastwards the forest drops down a steep bank.
13889: Small shrubs of varying size are littered about on the forest floor. Some of them have green leaves, but this is in no way a majority. They vary in size, shape and colour, almost as many as there are snowflakes on the mountains to the east. A tall wall of thorns almost secludes this place, as it prevents access to the north, south, and west. Indeed the only way to leave this place is to return to the bushes, to the east.
13890: The tall trees surrounding you seem to be covered in a sort of slime. It is a pale green in colour, and seems to be choking the life out of all surrounding trees. All is quiet here, no small animals nosing around in the undergrowth, no birds singing in the trees. This area seems as if it has fallen under some evil curse. The effect is more prominent in the south, while the trail can barely be seen to the north. An enormous bank of thorns prevents movement east.
13891:
A large beautiful rose bush is blooming here.
A rabbit is here eyeing your presence warily.

An abundance of rose bushes fill this small clearing, their fragrance wafting on the breeze. There are many different colours and varieties, each with a distinct shape and smell. Butterflies and bees flit from flower to flower, ensuring nature's cycle and the propagation of the species. The forest looms to the north and east, while above you to the south and west a rocky ridge side blocks movement.
13892:
A huge black fungus is here, exuding a foul stench.
A giant, strange looking green fungus is here, ready to devour you in seconds.
A huge black fungus is here, exuding a foul stench.
A black wolf pads restlessly, looking for its next prey.
A bear is here, covered with coarse black fur.
A roe deer is standing here, watching the terrain while chewing the vegetation.
A brown fox is here, looking for some rabbits to chew up.

Trees lie littered around you like fallen warriors, each of them encrusted with numerous types of fungi and mould. The stench here is overpowering. Any life that was here would have been consumed by whatever desecrated the forest. Small pools of foetid water lie around you, as if nature was actively fighting the cancerous onslaught.
13893:
A small animal, all covered in spines, snuffles amongst the undergrowth.
A small animal, all covered in spines, snuffles amongst the undergrowth.

This area is in stark contrast to the rest of the forest, where the flora and fauna thrive. All around you is the musty smell of rotting wood. The trees themselves have been twisted and deformed, almost as though they have been frozen whilst writhing in pain. If there could be a visual sign of pain and suffering, their growth would be it. To the south the twisted branches mingle completely, forming an impassable wall of bark.
13894: A cluster of dark green, feathery fronds flourishes in the shade.

Tall and mighty conifers surround you here. These trees are so tall that they seem to touch the clouds in the sky above. Pine cones litter the forest floor here and squirrels can be seen running along branches. The forest thickens to the south, but to the east it seems to wither and die. To the north it thickens completely, making passage in that direction impossible.
13895: The sound you make while moving through this area of the forest must be heard for a long way around. The natural debris littered on the ground and the dry branches make any silent progress near impossible. Any quarry hunted here will almost certainly hear your approach. To the west a tall stand of pine trees can be seen silhouetted against the sky. Eastwards the forest thins slightly, maybe indicating a track or trail.
13896: A pack horse (Rood) is standing here, ridden by you.

The forest opens up into a wide glade. To your west the forest resumes its deep gloom and foreboding air. Eastwards a great ring of stone can be seen, possibly an ancient temple, but from here it is tricky to make out. The trail follows its course on a north-south line, winding constantly in the dense woods. Access to the forest would be possible but hard going, and might entail a round-about route.
13898: Deep inside a Cluster of Pines

Tall pines dominate your view here, the trees growing so close together that the small spindly branches around trunk level keep snagging on your clothing and poking you in the eye. Eastwards the grove thins out somewhat and in the west a tall ring of hewn rock blocks movement. South a dell of trees lies well below you, inaccessable from here.
13899: The forest begins to thin out here, but to the south the vegetation underneath them is far too thick to force any sort of entry through. A small ridge rises off to the north. The forest thins out to the west again but quickly grows very dense. The forest to the east is moderately dense, but the mix of trees means that passage is still possible.
13900: The forest is very dense here, shadows long and black as pitch in the limited light. Nothing grows on the forest floor, which is a mish-mash of rotted leaves and timber. Insects and small animals can be seen clambering over the decay, gathering food for themselves. To the south the land drops violently, into a steep depression.
13901: The forest is thinner here than in other places but these huge trees still manage to keep the forest floor in some sort of twilight. Small creatures such as rabbits and squirrels can be seen giving you a wary look before darting away into the undergrowth. Shrubs and bushes that live on the forest floor scramble for any light that the canopy above them misses, which is very little light indeed. A sheer wall of briars in the east blocks your venturing further that way, while to the south a high cliff stops you exploring into the mountains.
13902:
A large bat is here, hanging in the darkness.
A large bat is here, hanging in the darkness.
A big cavebear is padding around here.

This place is undoubtedly the lair of some large animal, judging by the large footprints and strewn skeletons of rabbits and deer. In its northern half many branches, leaves and furs have been gathered together as bedding, the gigantic size giving some idea of the girth of the lair's owner.
13903:
A mouse is here nosing around, looking for a safe place to hide.
A mouse is here nosing around, looking for a safe place to hide.
A finch flies low above the ground.

Nothing more than three crumbled walls now, this place was once the home of a Dunlending farmer. They are a nomadic people however, often moving on to new pastures, and the farm is long since abandoned. The crops of the surrounding fields have entered here, growing amidst the rotten wooden furniture. West leads out to the fields, through what was once a door. Now it is merely a lone doorframe, standing still where the wall around it has fallen.
13904:
A hungry warg stands here, sniffing around for flesh.
A large brown wolf stands here, its teeth partly bared.

A small cave excavated roughly from the stone has been made here to pen the orkish mounts. It has lain uncleansed for many years, and every surface is now utterly clad in filth. South a wooden gate to the pen swings on rusty hinges, leading out into the main tunnel. The pen is built close to that entrance for a good reason - so the orcs can flee speedily whenever the trolls come up from the deeper caves for food.
13905:
A bloodthirsty orc stands here, hell-bent on battle.
A bloodthirsty orc stands here, hell-bent on battle.

The crude and foul-smelling tunnel has been build recently and the many notches and scars in the walls suggest the work was done by orcs. Little attention was payed to decorations or finish; the construction was hurried and careless. The tunnel contains no installations to make it suitable for living, yet a strong smell of orcs, spiced with the unmistakeable stench of rotting meat, pervades the air, sugesting the tunnel has other purposes. A hatchway made of bones, fur and lack of skill covers an opening above the tunnel. West the smell of orcs increases.
13906: This roughly fashioned passageway has been cut without thought of direction or ease of movement. Anyone taller than the average orc would have to stoop or risk banging their head against the rock. The tunnel continues east, from which direction a faint breeze of air comes, and south through a curtain of hanging furs and skeletons. Both ways are too dark to see much further.
13907:
A snaga orc stares at you with interest.
A snaga orc stares at you with interest.

A large cavern, excavated recently without much skill, extends north and east here. Little attention has been payed to smoothening either the walls or the floor, and the ceiling has many sharp edges that often hang dangerously low. A dank and pressing stench penetrates the air, a natural and comfortable smell to the inhabitants. Crude beds, made of tattered furs and branches, have been clumsily arranged along the southern wall to serve as sleeping quarters for the orcs living here.
13908:
The corpse of a bloodthirsty orc is lying here.
The corpse of a bloodthirsty orc is lying here.
The corpse of a bloodthirsty orc is lying here.
The corpse of a bloodthirsty orc is lying here.
A large, dusty alcove sits in a wall, smelling of soot.
A wooden chest stands in the corner.
A sturdy crate made of nailed wooden planks sits on the floor.

Roughly hewn walls to the south and the east marks the end of a large cavern. Excavated with an apparent lack of skill, the cavern would make a poor resort even for a brief stay. Sharp edges and rocks in the floor don't promise a good rest should you decide to make a stop here. This corner of the cavern appears to have other use than resting; barrels and crates stacked against the eastern wall together with a large alcove to the south makes the cavern a good spot to store goods and loot. Unfortunately this collection of stores makes the cave a frequent raiding point for trolls, who burrow tunnels through the rock to reach it. Mostly these old tunnels have been collapsed or sealed up by the orcs, but there is no way to stop newer tunnels being built.
13909:
A half-decayed corpse of a goblin lies rotting on the ground.
A half-decayed corpse of a goblin lies rotting on the ground.

Burrowing upwards the trolls found orkish caves above them, and have taken to raiding them for food. Mostly the orcs find these tunnels and seal them off, but this one they have not noticed. It has been dug in a winding fashion, up and crossing a natural fissure in the rock. Above you it ends in a heavy but movable slab of rock, while below it winds down to the fissure's base.
13910:
A half-decayed corpse of a goblin lies rotting on the ground.
An infant troll, baring its teeth, snarls here.
An infant troll, baring its teeth, snarls here.
A nasty troll female crouches here, with a feral look in her eyes.
An old, strong cave troll is standing here.

This tunnel was originally the base of a huge natural fissure, which still extends high above you. It was widened by the huge power of the cave trolls, burrowing through the rock and earth with their bare hands. East and above you the tunnel starts to wind upwards, while west it feeds into a large natural cavern. At the moment this end of the tunnel is used by the troll bitches to keep their young, and consequently it is extremely dirty.
13911:
The corpse of a cave troll is lying here.
The corpse of a troll mother is lying here.
The corpse of a cave troll is lying here.
The shadow of a troll mother is floating here.
Cunh the Dwarf, wielding an ornate, steel-shafted warhammer, is here, fighting *Beat the Hill Troll*.
*Beat the Hill Troll* is here, fighting Cunh.

Hidden in one of many caves that riddle the Misties, a small band of trolls attempt to survive. The original cavern, naturally made, has been expanded with tunnels running west and east of here, while huge thorn bushes have been dragged over the entrance to obscure it. Most of the cave is rather filthy, the only exception being a few fresh skins of bears and other large creatures.
13912:
An infant troll, baring its teeth, snarls here.
A large cave troll is here, staying close to his mother.
An infant troll, baring its teeth, snarls here.
An infant troll, baring its teeth, snarls here.
A large cave troll is here, staying close to his mother.
An infant troll, baring its teeth, snarls here.
The ugly troll mother is roaming the cave, taking care of her loved ones.

In this small side cave the young trolls are kept, those that are too young to kill food for themselves. It is a round cavern, with every surface caked in a thick layer of dirt. Countless animal skeletons, from rabbit up to bear sized, litter the cave, remnants of the vast meals these creatures need. East is the main cavern, a high natural expanse much bigger than this burrowed one.
13913: The mountain climbs high above the forest here, giving an unobstructed view for leagues around. To the north the Misty Mountains dominate the horizon, to the west they drop down to lush plains and forests. Eastwards the mountains steepen, a mass of near-vertical rock, and in the south large forests and vast plains open up before you.
13914: Anyone on this ridge is constantly buffeted by the wind crossing over the lip of the corrie. To the east the ground falls away sharply before rising again to another peak miles off in the distance. The ridge continues on to the north, culminating in a large outcrop of rock forming the highest peak for leagues around. To the south and west the land descends to mountain pasture.
13915:
A huge grizzly bear is here, roaming the wild.
A grizzly cub is here, snarling loudly.
A grizzly cub is here, snarling loudly.
A boar cub is playing here, and exploring the wide world.

The grass becomes patchy at this altitude, giving way to patches of shingle and rock. The tallest form of plant life barely reaches a few centimetres in the sparse air. A narrow ridge to the north leads up to one of the peaks, standing ominously over the trees. To the west the plains descend down to the forest.
13916: A bear is here, covered with coarse black fur.

The grassy plains are high above the forest here. The air is quite thin, making every action more of a toil than routine. The plains continue to climb in the north, where a steep ridge begins some distance away. Small flowers that thrive in the clean, fresh air are in abundance, their coloured blooms poking above the light grass. The Misty Mountains in the east and north form a sawtooth across the horizon, tall and impassable.
13917: These flat, high plains are somewhat grassier than those to the south and several kinds of wildflowers flourish in the lush, fertile soil. The sound of small animals running through the grass reaches your ears and you spy the occasional bird from time to time, looking for grasshoppers hiding within the vegetation. Fields begin to stretch off to the east and the outskirts of a forest are directly to your west.
13918: These high plains are covered by broad-leaved plants, and quite a few delicate flowers. Low bushes and trees are scattered across the fertile soil, providing shelter from the winds that often sweep across. A small campfire has been laid here, surrounded by log-seats. Not far to the east the Misty Mountains can be seen, towering high above the otherwise flat lands.
13919: The trail becomes a ford here at the borderline of the forest. The stream continues from the east to the west. To the north the trail enters a big forest, while plains dominate the lands south of this ford. An old ruined tower can be seen just southeast of here, broken down by natural elements and time.
13920:
A roe deer is standing here, watching the terrain while chewing the vegetation.
A pack horse (Rood) is standing here, ridden by you.

The trail continues south and north through the forest. Many animal tracks lead off to the east into the trees, disappearing into thick undergrowth. Some of them are quite large, possibly a bear or bigger, but most are the small tracks of foxes and the like. Mountain peaks jut out above the forest far to the east, their snow-capped peaks dipping in and out of the clouds.
13921: The trail takes a sharp incline here and the forest follows. Large pine trees dominate the skyline to the east and the trail seems to follow them. Birds can be heard singing in the shrubs and small trees to the north, but none can be seen. Delicate flowers are visible among the grasses and bushes that line the trail.
13922: A large beautiful rose bush is blooming here.

Just off the trail here, the immensity of this forest is clear. It seems to stretch for leagues around with no end in sight. To the east the distant peaks of the Misty Mountains can be made out against the sky, at night blacking out the stars and by day hanging over the surrounding plains like ominous watching giants.
13923: The bushes surrounding you all have the same sickly yellow hue. On closer examination it is obvious the disease has entered these shrubs by the roots. and worked its way to every leaf and shoot, slowly killing as it went. Even the light here has a gangrenous hue, almost as if the poison in the ground has infected it too. South the twisted undergrowth grows very dense, utterly impassable without an army of axe-wielders, while east it lessens. It might be possible to clear away the dead sticks there, and leave this poisoned part of the forest.
13924:
A porcupine is waddling around here, its tail full of sharp quills.
A tall stag is here, grazing peacefully.

Small shrubs seem to dance all around, their flowers and branches waving in the slight breeze. There is something strange about the smell here - it reeks of decay, and seems to be coming from the west. Even the fragrance of the flowers is not enough to block it out. Small animals can be seen darting between bushes, disappearing into the densely twisted vegetation to the north.
13925: A fierce boar is here, making grunting noises.

The trail bends to the south and east here. Small shrubs line the trail on both sides, and a few animal tracks can be seen. A cluster of shrubs off the path to the west provides a relief of colour, compared to the constant greenery of the surrounding vegetation. Dense forest prohibits any progress to the north, as the growth is so tightly packed there is no way to get through.
13926:
A roe deer is standing here, watching the terrain while chewing the vegetation.
A boar cub is playing here, and exploring the wide world.

The trail passes through a dense patch of conifers, their brown straggly twigs brushing against your arms and face. Looking above the canopy you see a thick mass of dark green needles, letting no more than a minimal amount of light fall to ground. Rustlings can be heard either side of you, but the forest is much too thick to see what makes them. Small shrubs give off a pleasant scent to the south, where the vegetation grows less dense.
13927: A pack horse (Rood) is standing here, ridden by you.

The trail makes a sweeping bend north and west here. To the west the forest thickens considerably and comes right down to the trail. Tiny flowers can be seen poking their heads through the grass and small shrubs that line the trail, their smell quite noticeable in air. A tall stand of trees can be seen to the east, with patches of brown in the dark green canopy.
13928:
A Dunlending forester is here gazing up at the tree tops.
A pack horse (Rood) is standing here, ridden by you.

The trees surrounding you have been mauled here, all stripped of their bark and left to die. The score marks of knives and axes can be seen in the trunks, the marks of man not beast. In the south a tall palisade can be seen rising out of the trees, the trail to the west of it. In the east a mass of fallen trunks and tangled growth prevents further movement in that direction.
13929: The forest drops into a small dell here, the trees growing so closely together that they wall you in on all sides. The ground underfoot is soft and spongy. with small puddles of water nestled between the roots of the great trees. Tiny, delicate flowers are dotted all around, a carpet of colour in this isolated spot.
13930: The rolling foothills of the mountains to the east are covered in trees, mostly hardy conifers. There are a few small deciduous trees dotted about, in small groves like islands amongst the pines. Small creatures can be heard snuffling about between the trees constantly, often hidden by the dense growth. There are some small birds flitting from tree to tree, oblivious to your presence and carrying on with their daily life. The hills continue to the east and south, while the forest thickens and becomes impassable west and north.
13931: High cliffs surround this hill on three sides, leaving west as the only way to leave. The trees themselves are very sparse and the forest becomes disjointed here. In the quiet of the forest howls and growls can be heard ringing around the hills in the distance. Some of the trees have huge gouges in their bark, as if they had been mauled by a large animal.
13932: Scree and shingle dominate the plains here, providing very little grazing for the animals that usually inhabit the plains. The ground is very hard, with only a thin layer of topsoil. A consequence of this is the very small plants that can grow here, making the plains themselves very bleak. East the ground rises up onto a sharp ridge, some way above the forest.
13933:
Oni the Orc, wielding a barbed fang, is here, riding a hungry warg.
A hungry warg is standing here, ridden by Oni.

The forest begins to climb rapidly to the east, the trees mainly small conifers with large spaces between them. The trampled undergrowth below them suggests that this part of the forest is frequented by some heavy herd of animals. To the north there are large tree-covered hills, while to the east the forest gives way to vast plains.
13934: A rabbit is here eyeing your presence warily.

Many of the trees here have been cut down recently, their thick trunks still lain on the earth. Some have been dragged off, with the tracks in the earth leading west. Off to the east the forest begins to climb up into the mountains that dominate the skyline, while northwards the forest heads into the twilight made by the thick canopy of leaves.
13935:
A bear is here, covered with coarse black fur.
A pack horse (Rood) is standing here, ridden by you.

A large wooden gate stands before you, made from the massive hardwood trunks of the forest around this area. The ground here has been ripped and trampled into a thick mud from the constant traffic in and out of the camp. It clings and sucks at anything that walks into it, making walking all the more tiresome. The gate forms a break in a tall palisade, extending east and west.
13936: Moving through the briars and bushes that adorn the side of the trail is very tiring and energy sapping. Small flowers grow about your feet and colourful berries cling to the surrounding bushes as they sway in the breeze, mingling freely in the briar patches. To the south-east a tall palisade rises between the trees, probably a settlement of sorts. The wall runs from east to west, over ten feet high.
13937:
A boar cub is playing here, and exploring the wide world.
A fierce boar is here, making grunting noises.

Small shrubs, maybe six inches high, litter the forest floor with a riotous cacophony of colour and fragrance. The smell alone is potent enough, but with the countless colours it forms an extremely distinctive brew. East and south a hedge of briars block movement, as impassable and strong as brick wall.
13938: A pack horse (Rood) is standing here, ridden by you.

Staggered trees force the trail to meander in and out between them. These trees are huge, at least six feet in diameter. Underneath their prodigious boughs it seems as if they are standing as tall as the clouds themselves - even the Misty Mountains to the east cannot be seen due to their height. They lead off into the horizon in all directions, a sea of trees without any visible landmarks.
13939: A pack horse (Rood) is standing here, ridden by you.

The trail meanders through the huge trees, each one with a trunk of immense girth. Small birds can be heard squawking and chirping high in the canopy above you, but it is dense enough they cannot be seen. Small woodland critters can also be heard snuffling around in the undergrowth. Countless many flowers and weeds decorate the forest floor on either side of you, growing onto the path in many places.
13940:
A brown fox is here, looking for some rabbits to chew up.
A pack horse (Rood) is standing here, ridden by you.

The trail winds in and about the trees here and it is all to easy to lose it in the undergrowth. Small forest animals scurry across the trail in front and behind you, ignoring your presence. The trees look ancient and have an old gnarled appearance to them, towering over the path. Small shrubs and vines scramble for any light that gets through that overhanging natural wall.
13941:
A brown bear is sleeping here.
A brown bear is sleeping here.

Animal skeletons litter the floor of the den. In one corner a pile of droppings fills whole area with its pungent odour. The bushes surrounding this clearing are broken, their mangled branches forming a carpet on the forest floor. The trees surrounding this spot form a secluded area in the forest, making it safe for the mother bear to leave her cubs when she ventures out to hunt.
13942: Between these large and battered bushes an open clearing in the undergrowth has been made, the vegetation seemingly crushed by the passage of some large animal footprints. There are no berries or flowers on the bushes, only the the town branches where they once grew. Large padded footprints lead towards the bushes to the west. To the north and east a barrier of completely tangled bushes and vines block all movement.
13943: A high palisade of wood rises up before you. The palisade made from the stout and strong forest trees rises up about twenty-five feet to be topped with large wooden spikes making it totally unclimbable. The forest continues on to the west and some smaller bushes can be seen to the north. Beyond the palisade to the east and south the sound of animals can be heard along with the occasional voice.
13944: A mass of dark green leaves clings to a wall.

A tall wall of wooden stakes rises out of the ground to the west. The tops of have been sharpened for added defense, making the wall unscalable. An animal path lies to the south, cut out of the thick forest vegetation by massive paws and constant movement. The local forest creatures take no notice of this wall, scurrying around right up at its base.
13945: The ground next to the pool of water in front of you has been trampled into a thick mud by the repeated visits of forest animals. Its proximity to the nearby plains means that the grazing animals that live there also use this place to drink. Predators too must frequent this spot, for trails of blood lie streaked on the ground.
13946: A sharp ridge rises out of the plains and heads east, climbing steadily up into the mountains beyond. Small mountain blooms litter the grass about your feet, a burst of colour in the bleak hillside plateau. A couple of shrubs sit lonely by themselves here and there, breaking up the otherwise unchanging height of the swaying grass.
13947: A bear is here, covered with coarse black fur.

Vast plains of grass open up before you, climbing towards the east where the Misty Mountains sit overlooking this country. A ridge climbs above the plains to the north, with a steep drop to the forest, while south the forest begins again. In places around here the grass has been cropped short by the grazing of animals, heavy beasts judging by the pulped earth in parts.
13948: In the foothills of the mountains here, the trees are sparser than in the main forest. Most of the trees are conifers, stunted by the altitude. A flat and barren plateau lies to the east, before the snow-tipped peaks which dominate the skyline and landscape for miles around.
13949: A rabbit is here eyeing your presence warily.

Birds can be heard chirping in the trees above you, while many small animals are visible all around. This is an especially well populated area of the woods, perhaps because of the soil's well-watered fertility. Large, wide trees grow close together to the north, while to the south the land begins to be rather water-logged.
13950: This is obviously a path frequented by large game, judging by the four legged footprints that litter it. The tracks head east and west, while to the north a large wall of sharp wooden stakes looms out of the forest. A small track leads round its outer base, northeast of here, and out of your sight.
13951: Large footprints weave in an out of the trees, following the hoof tracks of the herbivores that live in the forest. Underfoot crushed flowers and plants lie everywhere. The trees here are entirely deciduous - oaks and birches. Their fallen leaves litter the ground below, adding a soft layer to the earth.
13952: Sparsely growing trees stand in isolated groves here, not impeding movement much. To the north there is a mass of bushes, many bruised and bashed by the animals that continually pad through them. The trees themselves are mainly deciduous oaks and birches, an almost watertight roof overhead. The forest floor itself still seems to be rather muddy though, perhaps due to the river nearby to the south.
13953: Masses of animal tracks seem to congregate here, making any attempt at tracking a particular animal impossible. Even your own footprints seem to be lost in the miasma that lies before you. Some of the larger tracks disappear in the bushes to the north, perhaps where some hidden lair lies. No flowers grow here, all have been long trampled before they could grow to any size.
13954:
The corpse of a weasel is lying here.
The corpse of a weasel is lying here.

Hundreds of animal tracks criss-cross in front of you, darting in front and behind trees. The tracks are a mish-mash of various animals, from the hooves of deer to the big pads of bears. In the north thick bushes prevent block all movement, unless you wish to spend weeks cutting through the undergrowth.
13955: The stream widens at this point, forcing the water to flow slowly westwards. It seems like the depth of the water grows shallow in the west direction but it is still deep enough to allow any small craft to flow through. The banks of the stream are quite steep at most places but several small beaches make it possible to climb up the bank easily. An old tower is visible through the trees on the south bank.
13956: As the stream bends westward it seems to get wider and deeper. The north-eastern bank seem flat and easy to climb, but the south-western bank looks much steeper and is covered with thorny bushes in most places. Some large trees can be spotted towards north and east, and on the south-western side of the stream an old tower can been seen through the vegetation.
13957: The forest comes to an end to the south and west, where a small stream cuts through the landscape. Even though a few large trees can be seen, the forest is made up primarily of small, thin trees and dense bushes. It appears that the forest gets more dense towards the northeast.
13958: A bushy tangle of vegetation grows thick in the outskirts of a light forest which lies to both the east and the west. Young saplings and grass thrive with abandon and cover the ground in a confusion of growth and foliage. A stream flows to the south and it looks as though a number of tracks from the plentiful wildlife in this area can be seen to the north.
13959: A sturdy pack horse is standing here.

A healthy mixture of smaller trees and undergrowth make up this wooded forest, giving some protection against the elements and large predators that roam the area, looking for smaller prey. Soft, green grass and a few stray branches cover the floor of the forest and the animal path to the north suggest that wildlife is abundant in this area. The forest begins to grow boggy to the east.
13960:
A tall plant grows here, with grey-green leaves and grey flowers.
Some thick writhing vines whip all around you.
Some thick writhing vines whip all around you.
A tree-snake lies wrapped around one of the tree branches.

Water spilling over the stream bank to the south makes this part of the forest almost impassable even on foot. The ground is muddy and boggy to the point that a traveller should be careful not to linger too long in one spot, for fear of being stuck permanently. The trees here are very healthy and excessively tall, due to the abundant supply of water. Dark green moss covers the trunks of the trees and a good portion of the ground as well. All the moisture in the area probably makes for a good breeding ground for small insects.
13961: A dense carpet of blue flowers dip their heads in the breeze.

All around the trees grow dense and thick in this area of the forest, their trunks wide in girth and their branches rising proudly to the sky. There are signs everywhere that this forest is thick with small game and the vegetation is flourishing green and healthy. The trees seem to thin out to the south and a path is visible to the north. Towards the west, the ground grows decidedly more boggy.
13962:
A fallow deer is grazing peacefully here.
A squirrel scampers around here, looking for nuts from the trees.

Both plains vegetation and young seedlings fight to exist here in the outskirts of the forest rising up to the west. Tall grains and short grasses flourish alongside the half-grown trees, creating a wild mixture of foliage and ground cover. One would imagine small game would especially favour this area, using the woods as protection against the larger predators and the grains and seeds providing ample food.
13963:
A large stone fireplace with a roaring fire warms the room.
A pan is here, ready for use.
A weapons rack stands against the wall.
A small oaken table has been set here.
A swarthy Dunlending warrior is here, guarding his village against intruders.
A Dunlending Captain is here, overseeing his men.

This is a small wooden building, seemingly inhabited by several people. There are a few beds on the southern wall covered by brown blankets. A wooden table stands by the eastern wall, just beneath a small window. Just inside the door several tools and even a few a weapons lie on a rack mounted on the wall. There is a small fire crackling in the stone chimney, with a few pots and cooking tools beside it.
13964:
A swarthy Dunlending warrior is here, guarding his village against intruders.
A Dunlending farmer is here, watching over the work in his fields.
A Dunlending farmer is here, watching over the work in his fields.
A pack horse (Rood) is standing here, ridden by you.

A high palisade surrounds this small village, seemingly put here to defend the area against wild animals and any other creatures that might try attack the settlement. The village lies on the very slopes of the Misty Mountains, just beneath the steep rock faces. Northeast of here a stone well marks the centre of the village, while west a trail goes through the palisade.
13965:
A small child is here playing happily.
A pack horse (Rood) is standing here, ridden by you.

A few small animals are running freely, looking for food. A few houses lie scattered within the wooden palisade that surrounds the village, built just beneath the steep stone walls of the Misty Mountains. Just south of here a door leads into one of them, a small thatched construction made of wooden logs. A stone well can be seen to the north, at the very centre of the village.
13966:
A swarthy Dunlending warrior is here, guarding his village against intruders.
A pack horse (Rood) is standing here, ridden by you.

This is a small village lying just below the steep slopes of the Misty Mountains to the south. A high palisade has been built around it to keep wild animals and the mountain orcs out. Just north of here the northeast part of the village has been fenced in for cattle, while west lie a few wooden homes.
13967:
A sturdy pack horse is standing here.
A brown cow is here, contemplating a higher reality whilst chewing slowly.
A brown cow is here, contemplating a higher reality whilst chewing slowly.
