A small part of the village has been put aside for cattle. A low fence against the palisade pens them in, while they are not out grazing on the pastures near the village. The ground here is crushed and muddy, without much grass. One can see where the villagers have been feeding the animals, as the southern part of the pen has the look of much-trampled hay.
13968:
An arrow lies on the ground.
An arrow lies on the ground.
An arrow lies on the ground.
An arrow lies on the ground.
An arrow lies on the ground.
An arrow lies on the ground.
A circular stone well has been built here.
A Dunlending hunter is here, stalking his prey.
A pack horse (Rood) is standing here, ridden by you.

A well marks the centre of this small village. The few wooden houses around here are built of wood, with stone base to make them more stable. They are encircled by a tall wooden palisade in all directions but south, where the Misty Mountains provide an impassable barrier. The northeast corner has been fenced in, to keep cattle in one place. There are a few hens running around here, scrutinising the ground for anything edible.
13969:
A hen is trying to pick some grains here.
A Dunlending woman is here tending to her children.
A pack horse (Rood) is standing here, ridden by you.

Here, inside a small Dunlending village, a few hens are slowly walking around looking for food. There are quite a few wooden houses spread out inside the palisade, small puffs of smoke coming from a few chimneys. The wall surrounding the village is about three yards high and seems very sturdy. Just east of here the centre of the village is marked by a stone well.
13970:
A rather heavy clay jar stands here.
A large stone fireplace with a roaring fire warms the room.
A rather heavy clay jar stands here.
A small oaken table has been set here.
A small child is here playing happily.
A Dunlending woman is here tending to her children.

Here, inside a simple wooden house, there isn't much to see. A few wooden pieces of furniture are placed around the room to make it more comfortable and many pelts and blankets are lain on the beds. A tiny wooden chimney has been built in the northeast corner, a fire crackling in its hearth. Several pots and jars stand on a shelf on the western wall, and a wooden door leads out to the south.
13972: The tunnel is narrow here, with broad shelves cut into the rock on either side of you. Upon closer inspection these are found to be graves. Many disjointed skeletons lie on each shelf, filled from floor to ceiling. A faint but eerie wind emanates from the east, down the deathly dark aisle. To the east lies a smaller chamber, but it is too dark to see any more.
13973: Shelves line this room from floor to ceiling in this seemingly long unused mausoleum. A thick dust has settled on almost every surface, and even the motion of your feet puffs up great clouds of it. In each shelf there lie the bones of a man, some have decayed weapons lying beside them, but most just lie with their arms folded across their chests.
13974:
The corpse of a stone statue is lying here.
A stone sarcophagus lies on the floor.

Inside this tomb, there are no burial shelves on the walls as elsewhere, only paintings depicting the life and conquests of its owner. In the centre of the room stands a large, stone coffin with a heavy stone lid. The shadows seem to move in the gloom, shifting from wall to wall. This seems to be an important room as colour has been incorporated into the wall paintings.
13975:
The corpse of a guardian stone beast is lying here.
A stone sarcophagus lies on the floor.
A stocky mountain mule is here, waiting to serve.
A great dark-grey horse stamps restively.
A stocky mountain mule is here, waiting to serve.

Inside this tomb are no burial shelves, only paintings depicting the owner's life and conquests. The exception is to the north, where the is a single empty shelf. In the centre stands a large coffin with a heavy stone lid. The shadows seem to move in the gloom, shifting from wall to wall. This seems to have been an important room, as colour has been incorporated into the wall paintings.
13976:
Tordol the Dwarf (t), wielding the fine silvery morningstar, is standing here.
A stocky mountain mule is here, waiting to serve.
Tarabaran the Dwarf (ta), wielding a blackened dwarven axe, is standing here.
A stocky mountain mule is here, waiting to serve.

The room is a perfect rectangle cut out of the surrounding rock. Many strange runes and glyphs cover the walls almost as though they convey some sort of story. They are arranged in neat columns running from floor to ceiling covering each of the four walls. On closer inspection of the glyphs the figure of a huge lidless eye appears frequently. In the centre of the room is a huge sacrificial altar, hewn from a strange, black stone - it seems to absorb all the available light. In its very centre is a prominent small hole, with many small grooves leading out from it.
13977: A large stone chest is here.

You have entered a small chamber, covering the walls from floor to ceiling are many more of the hieroglyphs that cover the rest of this temple. The only difference with these is that the glyphs and symbols here seem to have a much darker and grisly nature. Frequently there are symbols depicting a lidless eye and wars with extreme bloodshed.
13978: Low, thick grass covers the ground, with small trails made by horses, cows or some other kind of large creature here and there. The land has obviously been used for feeding cattle; however there is no village to be seen nearby. A watering hole has been dug in the shadows of a clump of aspen trees, partly hidden by low bushes, but easily found due to the number of tracks leading into it. The Misty Mountains are looming east of here, their foothills climbing swiftly into vast peaks.
13979: Lower Slopes of the Misty Mountains

Here, just southwest of the Misty Mountains, the grass is verdantly green and the low vegetation flourishing. There seems to be an abundance of small game living among the low shrubs and wind-whipped trees. Several tracks can be seen in the dark soil and a number of small farms can be seen just south of here.
13980: Lower Slopes of the Misty Mountains

The wild vegetation flourishes to a degree here, but seldom grows higher than a few feet above ground due to the biting winds. The white peaks of the Misties curve around north and east of here, like blinking bejewelled crystals just out of reach. South of here the contours of a few farmhouses can be seen on a small knoll.
13981: Lower Slopes of the Misty Mountains
An arrow lies on the ground.

Rising high above the flat prairie of Dunland, the Misty Mountains are an impenetrable obstacle for any normal creatures to cross. Their white tops glimmer in the clouds far away, and an occasional bird can barely be discerned as a spot circling them. Here, on the lower slopes of the Misties, the low vegetation is flourishing. It is possible to go south or west from here.
13982:
A rather heavy clay jar stands here.
A rather heavy clay jar stands here.
A small oaken table has been set here.

You are inside a primitive farmhouse made of logs. A number of wooden benches have been put along the eastern wall, partly covered by colourfully-patterned blankets. There are windows in every wall, and a wooden door in the southern side leading outside. The floor is made of oak planks, which crack quietly as you move around. There are many jars and pots around the small fireplace in the northwest corner of the building, containing food and plants.
13983: These green and fertile plains are covered by a broad-leaved grass, with many small trails going in all directions. By the crushed swathes of grass the land is probably being used for feeding cattle. The slow murmur of a stream working its way downstream can be heard from the south, and some buildings can be seen in the east. The small hills seem to grow west of here, making the land rise a bit.
13984: A Few Farmhouses on the Grassy Plains

A well-fed cow stands here chewing her cud listlessly.
A brown cow is here, contemplating a higher reality whilst chewing slowly.

Here, in the middle of the Dunland plains, a few small farmsteads have been built. Surrounding them are wind-beaten oak trees, and just south a small stream running from east to west. Beyond the stream a high palisade can just be discerned, with a few houses and farms visible within. The ground here has been laid bare in several places, perhaps caused by the cattle on their way to the water. A small knoll rises east of here, and the shapes of a few buildings can be seen on it.
13985: A Hill with Tents and Ruins

Many large tents have been raised on this grassy knoll, amidst the ruins of a farmhouse. In the centre of the tents there is a large fireplace, probably the meeting spot for these farmers. A small herd of cattle is fenced inside on the slopes of the hill, and many farming tools lie scattered all around. It is possible to see for miles from this place, all around the giant swept arc of the Misties that encloses these plains.
13986: Several deep tracks of animals can be seen in the soft soil here, probably made by cattle from the farms on a small hill to the west. This seems to be part of a large valley cutting east into the Misty Mountains, while west of here the vastness of Enedwaith stretches out seemingly forever. Just visible beneath a layer of overhanging vegetation is the small line of a stream, coming from the east and turning south.
13987: Lower Slopes of the Misty Mountains

A small stream gurgles by here, its waters nourishing the bushes and trees that spring up on both banks. The Misty Mountains rise high in all directions but west, where the plains of Dunland run to the horizon. Here and there lie large stone blocks, littering the ground as if some giant had cast them down from the mountains. There are many signs of this area being used for cattle, with trails of crushed grass crossing the grassy knolls.
13988: Here, at the base of the Misty Mountains, the soil is sandy and the vegetation sparse. Some low trees and bushes are scattered around in patches, growing a bit more dense around the stone blocks that spot the area. North the Misties tower high, while south lies a small hill covered by ruins. The only real spark of life here comes from a cold line of water, running down a creek in the cliff wall some distance to the east, and continuing through the plains.
13989: The craggy peaks of the mountains begin north and east of here, turning from faint foothills into an utterly unclimbable cliff in the space of a hundred yards. From the rocks to the east comes tumbling down a small line of water, sparkling against the dark mountain rock. On hitting the plains it pools for a moment, then swiftly disappears into the undergrowth.
13990: These plains lie slightly higher than the surroundings, making it possible to get a decent view of the nearby landscape. A small stream meanders through the landscape a mile south of here, surrounded by a corridor of bushes and fairly tall trees. Further south the Misty Mountains rise into the sky, impassable even for the most daring traveller. The ground slopes mildly downwards to the east and south, providing an easy descent.
13991: Yellow flowers, with grey-green foliage, grow in clusters here.

The high, flat plains spread out before you and continue on to the north, fertile and teeming with small wildlife. A mixture of short grass and tall grains grows in abundance here, providing the perfect hiding place for rabbits and small birds. The plains themselves are very level and higher than the surrounding fields and forest, allowing a clear view for several miles in all directions.
13992:
A squirrel scampers around here, looking for nuts from the trees.
A fallow deer is grazing peacefully here.

The vegetation is varied on the outskirts of this forest, but it is obvious that the forest is winning over the plains grass in the competition for survival and will soon take over completely. A stream can be seen running to the south and a lightly wooded forest begins to the west. High plains rise up directly to your east.
13993: Various types of wildlife abound in this lightly wooded portion of the land. Deer especially seem to favor this spot, perhaps drawn by the protection offered by the forest from predators that inhabit the nearby plains. The trees grow straight and tall, nourished by the rich, fertile soil and plentiful supply of water. A small stream runs to the west and south of the forest, but it seems the bank is too steep in either direction to enter it.
13994: Winding through a quiet forest, the stream bends here from the south to the west. It appears that the north bank of the stream floods frequently, overflowing into the forest in that direction. The light forest to the east is probably home to some small game but for now you might want to just follow the stream where it chooses to lead you.
13995: This stream flows quiet and gentle next to the lightly wooded forest bordering it to the north. Layers of think, green moss trail down the side of the bank and the occasional water lily floats delicately along the edge of the stream. The stream floats from the east to the west and a path is visible to the south.
13996: Bordering the footpath that raises to the south, the stream here is very wide and the current strong, flowing from the east to the west with speed and fervour. The outskirts of a forest are visible to the north.
13997: The water flows gently westwards through the almost flat landscape. On the south bank of the stream a small trail can be seen following the stream closely. The banks of the stream are quite low and would make it easy to leave the stream in that direction.
13998: A horse of the Rohirrim (Rood) is standing here, ridden by you.

Two small streams coming from the south and east join together and form a bigger stream flowing northwards. Where the two streams meet the water gets turbulent, forming small waves and eddies. The western bank is quite steep and covered with many small bushes that make progress in that direction quite impossible. At the crest of the western bank the top of an old tower can be seen rising over the bushes.
13999: Passing a ruined tower the trail passes a stream to the north, and to the south the trail continues among the plains. Further north you can see a big forest branching out over the plains. The tower just east of you is worn down by time, wind and perhaps even battles. On this western side of the tower there are some windows, but no entrance can be seen this way.
14000: Following alongside a footpath that lies to the south, the stream travels from the east to the west. The water is very clear here and is full of tiny fish and other small creatures. A forest rising to the north casts a gloomy shadow in that direction.
14001:
A bass swims here.
A fat carp swims here.

The current of the stream picks up speed here, rushing over small rocks and branches in its way. The bank to the south seems to be decaying from the constant wear of the water but the bank to the north is still quite solid. A light forest borders the stream in that direction.
14002:
A fat carp swims here.
A bass swims here.

The stream makes a lazy bend here, flowing from the east to the north. A tilted footpath can be seen to the south, runnning parallel to the stream. The gentle flow of the current and quiet sound of the water combine to make a traveller wonder if it might not be better to stay among these hills and follow the stream wherever it may lead.
14003: This flat, dirt footpath makes its way through the countryside, allowing for easy travel through the plains and hills. It is very narrow and large groups would be most comfortable travelling single file along the path. A stream borders the path to the north and east and the path itself bends here, continuing on both to the south and west.
14004: The footpath comes across a small stream flowing slowly northwards. The stream is quite shallow and the sandy bottom makes crossing easy - even the shortest of hobbits would not get his ears wet crossing this stream. The banks of the stream are covered with bushes and small trees. While the land north of here looks fairly flat, a slight rise in the landscape is clearly visible towards the southeast.
14005:
A black catfish is here, lurking in the mud.
A salmon swims here.

A quiet stream makes its way through the land, flowing from the south and crossing a footpath at the ford to the north. A portion of grainy lowlands is visible to the east and a trails cuts a brown swath through the land to the west.
14006:
A salmon swims here.
A salmon swims here.

Travelling parallel to the footpath to the west, this gentle stream runs from the south to the north in direction through a series of hills. A watery portion of elevated land rises to the east, creating a bank which looks to be too steep and slippery to climb from this side.
14007: The gentle stream bends from the east to the north, running its slow course through the plains and nourishing both land and animals with its abundant supply of water. It continues on north through a range of hills and runs close to the ford that is visible to the east. Although, as you examine the banks of the stream, it is clear that it would be just as easy to leave the stream at this point and step onto the trail that lies directly to the west.
14008: Quiet and soft, the gentle current of the stream flows westwards through the plains. A ford to the south gives one the opportunity to step onto a trail which appears to run east-west. Uneven plains cut away to the east or you can climb up onto a watery elevation rising up to the north.
14009: The stream from the south meets the one flowing from the east. and merge into one river heading north. A small trail fords the stream in that direction, or you could step onto dry land to the west. A trail runs parallel to the water there, from north to south.
14010: Soft and quiet, the stream makes its way between a bluff that slopes away to the east and a trail that runs through the plains to the west. The current is slow and mild, coming from the south and joining another stream to the north.
14011: A silvery fish quickly darts through the water.

The stream is rather narrow here, with its banks very high and its current gentle and smooth. The water is very clear and cool to the touch and there is an abundance of small fishes swimming in the water below. Plains stretch out to the east and a trail runs to the west and south. The stream itself continues north.
14012: Quite large and wide, the stream flows swiftly from the east to the west, joining another stream in the western direction. Moss grows thick along the bottom of the bluff that rises to the south, making it too slick to climb and casting a greenish tint into the water when the sun shines brightly on it.
14013: A small rivulet begins to expand here and turns into a full stream, flowing from the east to the west. A bridle path follows the stream to the north and a rocky bluff rises high in the air to the south, its sides too smooth and steep to climb. Looking farther to the north, one can see the outline of jagged hills rising above the horizon.
14014: A tiny rivulet makes its way from the brook to the east and begins to widen to the west. A bridle path is visible to the north and further on you can see plains beginning in that direction. A large range of hills raises up to the south.
14015: The quiet brook that flows from the south begins to expand in width and depth here and actually becomes a small rivulet to the west. It cuts a path though the plains with its strong current and is bordered by a path to the north. A sturdy, wooden fence surrounding what looks to be grazing plains for the settlement visible to the east prohibits travel in that direction.
14016: Slow and gentle, the brook bends softly from the east to the north. Its current seems to gradually be getting stronger, probably due to the excess run-off of water from the surrounding hills, and the width of the brook definitly widens as the brook continues on. The large hill range looms to both the east and south.
14017:
A crayfish is here, snapping its claws at you.
A brook trout is here, swimming in the current.
A brook trout is here, swimming in the current.
A brook trout is here, swimming in the current.

The current of this brook is extremely slow and gentle and an abundance of fish and other small water creatures take advantage of the barely flowing deep waters, hiding in small crevices and under stones in the nearly still waters. Lush plains lie to the north and the brook itself runs from the east to the west.
14018: This small brook flows into the plains here, from the forest to the east. The settlers to the north evidently appreciate the constant water source for there are signs everywhere of people and animals coming to the brook for its supply of fresh, clear mountain water. The brook flows to the west, while lush plains spread out to the south.
14019: A broken down tower looms just to the north, while the trail itself forms a t-crossing. Westwards it turns towards the forest that lies to the north, south it follows a stream while to the east there is a ford allowing you to safely pass the stream and continue on.
14020: A rabbit is here eyeing your presence warily.

Running side by side with the stream to the east, this wide trail continues on straight to both the north and south. A junction of this trail and another is directly to the north and you can spy flat grasslands opening up to the east. A tower is visible not far in the distance to the north.
14021: Wide and well-beaten down, this trail makes travel through the plains and hills easy whether one is on foot or is mounted. It leads both north and south for some distance, running between the stream to the east and the open grasslands to the west.
14022: The well worn trail cuts a brown swath through the grasslands, extending north and south for several miles in direction. A small stream bends away from the trail to the east and very far to the north, one can see the top of a tower rising up high above the plains.
14023: This trail is evidently quite popular among travellers, judging by how firmly the earth is packed down underneath you from countless feet and hooves. A small campsite appears to have been constructed to the south for those weary from the journey. The trail begins to bend, travelling both north and east in direction.
14024: Two trails cross here, one running east and west and the other extending straight south as far as the eye can see. A shallow place to ford the stream is visible to the east and a large stream runs to the north.
14025: A pack horse (Rood) is standing here, ridden by you.

Travelling through the plains, this trail is flat and wide, making travel upon it very comfortable and allowing a traveller to survey the surrounding lands without fear of stumbling. Looking to the west, an old campsite is visible and two streams merge to form one to the east. The trail itself meets another trail running crosswise to the north.
14026: This narrow trail makes its way between the smooth plains stretching away to the west and a gentle stream that runs quietly to the east. The bank leading into the stream is very slight and the water probably floods the path during the rainier seasons of the year. The trail continues on straight north and south in direction.
14027: A wild bull seems ready to charge you.

Running parallel to the quiet stream which flows to the east, a small trail begins here and travels on north through the fertile plains. A soft, grassy field stretches out to the south and an area of smooth, unbroken plains begins to the west.
14028: This trail runs through soft, bulging grass, which is slowly growing thinner and sparser in all directions save east, where the trail continues. Like a great brown shadow, a large patch of brushwood stains the fields to the south- west.
14030: A pack horse (Rood) is standing here, ridden by you.

Running alongside a small stream, the trail cuts a passage south across the grasslands. As it runs north it becomes noticeably soggy and wet, but still remains in good enough condition to support travel. Grasslands reach far to the east, and desolate and barren fields lie to the west.
14031: Soft underfoot, this worn trail offers comfortable passage along the border of the wilderness and the grasslands. Although primitive in its fashioning, it seems to be well-used and might serve as a trading route between the people who inhabit these lands. Its southern expanse grows ever wider, whereas to the north the trail remains narrow and primitive. The soft trickling of the stream running along the trail mixes with the sounds of wildlife, a serene oasis of nature amongst the plains.
14032: A pack horse (Rood) is standing here, ridden by you.

The trail acts as a border between barren and brushy fields to the west and soft, rolling grasslands to the east. The trail grows ever wider southwards as it approaches a seemingly abandoned guardpost. A gentle stream runs by the trail-side, accompanying it on its journey across this land.
14033: A mass of dark green leaves clings to a wall.

The remnants of an old guardpost lie here in foreboding solitude. Debris of collapsed barricades have been strewn across the trail, blocking it partially. A broad, paved path leads east, past the greater of the barricades, into a clearing among the mountain forest.
14034: The stone walls of this circular building are cold and most items are covered with dust and debris. A wooden staircase follows along the wall leading upwards towards the roof where an opening can be seen. The floor has marks in the dust from the feet of minor animals and in some places human footprints can also be seen. Other than a few broken chairs lying on the floor, most of the furniture left is still in pretty decent shape.
14035: The top of this tower appears to be stable, despite obvious damage caused by the wear of wind and rain upon the wood and stone. The scars of battles long past show in the broken battlements that line the top of the tower and the gaping holes visible in several places along the tower floor. To the north, one can see a large forest stretching itself along a stream, and plains continue to the west and south. Eastwards the forest continues alongside a trail, and even further east you can see the Misty Mountains.
14036:
A small vicious black rat squeaks at you for disturbing it.
A shadow suddenly leaves its place on the wall, trying to reach your neck.
A spirit floats towards you and howls with an evil laughter.

This dark and dusty cellar has little life left except for a few small rats hiding among the rubble. The wine racks lie empty and broken bottles lie on the floor in testimony to the wear of time and neglect upon this tower. The air is rather damp and it is hard to see clearly but it almost seems as though the shadows move behind you as you turn to head back up the stairs.
14037: This trail slowly bends north and east from this point, but as you look east you see that the trail continues south and east. South of here the plains unfolds into a great flat landscape. Looking north you see a ruined tower to the northeast, and behind it a stream flanks a big forest.
14038: A large expanse of level grasslands begins here and spreads south as far as the eye can see. The land itself is thick and green with a short, lush grass and a few wildflowers dot the landscape with their bright colors. A trail can be seen to both the north and east and there is a stream close by a little ways to the east.
14039: Flat and monotonous, these grasslands continue to the north and south and a broad trail runs directly to the east. The ground is covered primarily by a short, bright green grass but one can see the occasional wildflower or patch of taller grass flourishing brightly.
14040: These level grasslands expand lush and green to both the north and south for some distance. The soil is evidently quite fertile and both short and tall wild grasses take advantage of the good conditions, growing thick and abundantly. Looking to the east, you see a broad trail.
14041: A thick carpet of lush grass covers the ground in this area of the land. Occasionally you might catch a glimpse of a rabbit hiding in the tall grass or larger animals grazing off the healthy vegetation. The flat grasslands extend both north and south and a trail runs directly to the east.
14042:
You see two handfuls of clover on the ground.
A wild bull seems ready to charge you.

This extremely level portion of the land is blanketed by a healthy mix of grass and wildflowers. Clover in particular grows especially well, flourishing in the rich, fertile soil and filling the air with its heavy scent. Smooth plains stretch out to the south and grasslands continue to the north. It seems a campsite has been constructed to the east but it is hard to tell from this direction whether or not it is still in use.
14043: Evidently once a favorite place for travellers to stop and rest on their journeys, this old campsite appears to get little, if any, use now. Grass is just beginning to grow again after being trampelled down by so many feet and tents. A circle of stones surrounding the remains of a burnt-out fire conveniently sits directly in the middle of the campsite. A trail is visible to both the north and the east, flat grassland begins to the west, and smooth plains expand out to the south.
14044: Some cereals that look like wheat are lying here.

These smooth plains give a wide view of the surrounding lands, with little vegetation except some short grass to get in the way. An old campsite lies directly to the north and the plains themselves continue to the south. To the east, a trail runs through the plains.
14045: Growing thick and plentiful, short plains grass covers every inch of ground, creating a vast sea of green vegetation that flows to the north for quite some ways. Brush-filled plains begin to the south and a trail winds through the plains to the east.
14046: Long patches of brushwood stretch out from the dense undergrowth south, but they quickly thin out and fade into the bulging grass of the fields. Travelling south seems not only uncomfortable but also unwise since the fields to the east offer a far better route of passage.
14047: A large brown snake with black patches is coiled here.

Rough brushwood surrounds you, blotting out the ground with its thick branches. Rattling noises, the crunching of twigs underfoot and the rustling of leaves can be heard from all around. Many small creatures must be scuttling about nearby, or maybe the brush is just shifting around in the wind. It stretches even further west and north, while to the south and east lie barren and wild lands.
14048: Brown-stained grass and twisted shrubs blend together to form a truly hostile environment. The northern horizon is stained by large patches of brushwood amidst the plains. The southern fields seem even more desolate, but the vegetation that does exist there looks greener, and healthier in a way.
14049: A swallow flies high above the ground.

The harsh and barren wilderness stretches north into rough brushwood. Desolate fields lie all around you, but far to the south, past a bleak trail, the grass grows thick and full. Faint slithering impressions lead in all directions, bearing evidence of existing wildlife in this infertile surrounding.
14050: A pack horse (Rood) is standing here, ridden by you.

The trail's condition worsens as it strays into the brushwood westward - a real forsaken wilderness. This is clearly not a path often taken by the people of Dunland; seeing the hostile brushwood sway and rattle in the wind shows why. A more pleasant path can be seen to the east, at a crossing of trails.
14051: A pack horse (Rood) is standing here, ridden by you.

Three trails intertwine to form a crossing outside an old guardpost. A bleak trail leads west into the wilderness and shows little promise of comfortable travelling. The southern trail seems to widen as it cuts through the plains, perhaps a sign of more frequent use.
14052: Sparsely vegetated fields turn even more barren as they stretch westwards. A trail running along the south and east borders of the fields seems to lead to lands less wasted and lifeless, sheltered somewhat by the Misty Mountains. Far to the east you see that great mountain range tower into the skies.
14053: Dusty fields lie at the eastern border of widespread wildlands. Just east of here a trail takes a north-south route across the grasslands, running alongside a small stream. The fields, growing richer as they draw north and more desolate in the south, continue along the outskirts of the vast windswept plains to the west.
14054: Small patches of brushwood stretch out from the west, where the ground is completely covered by the thick undergrowth. Gazing across the western horizon you see naught which would justify passage through the dense vegetation. A far easier and more comfortable route of travel lies east, in the form of a trail running north-south.
14055: A pack horse (Rood) is standing here, ridden by you.

The trail struggles to make its way through the surrounding wilderness, here faltering and making an abrupt turn to the north. Southwards lie the wide open grasslands of Enedwaith, with sporadic patches of brushwood and shrubbery. To the east the trail grows slightly stronger, with less vegetation to overwhelm it.
14056: A pack horse (Rood) is standing here, ridden by you.

The trail finally succumbs to the wilderness and decay which surrounds it and becomes nothing but a faint outline and vanishes. The wilderness spreads out in every direction, save the trail leading south. East is a spur from the main mountain range, vast in its own right.
14057: Little hope resides here. The wind plagues the open wildlands, and nowhere is shelter to be found. Large patches of thick brushwood lie to the north, like great brown stains on the barren fields. Faint, but still discernible, a trail runs to the south.
14058: The ground itself becomes impossible to see as the thick brushwood rolls out across the plains. The brush rattles and sways in the wind, their naked twiggy fingers stretching out towards you. Northwards part of the brush yields and opens up, letting the ground show once again. To the south it borders the wild plains of Enedwaith, stretching endlessly.
14059: Spots of brushwood cover the plains, but as they draw north the spots grow fewer and further apart. In the south the brush grows very dense and completely smoulders the ground it has sprung out of. Eastward lie rolling grasslands, and beyond them a huge mountain range on the horizon.
14060: A short, tough grass flourishes in the fertile soil of these plains, clinging low to the ground and creating the appearance of an unbroken sea of green grass that continues both north and east. The plains to the south seem to break up and become bushier.
14061: Smooth, unbroken plains extend to both the south and east, covered with a mixture of dense, tough grass and short, wild grains. Flat grasslands open up to the north as far as the eye can see.
14062: A small footpath runs straight and narrow between a stream to the north and the grainy lowlands that lie directly to the south. It fords a small stream to the west and continues on to the east as well. The air is very fresh and clear and the dirt of the footpath below is level and smooth.
14063: Built at a steep angle into the land, this footpath is elevated enough to run slightly above the stream to the north and the lowlands that are thick with grain to the south. Looking farther north, you can see a forest rising up in that direction. The footpath continues straight on both east and west.
14064: Tall grains thrive in this low, moist portion of land. A few tufts of grass are visible among the thick, brown grains, flourishing in the fertile soil and a plentiful supply of the water from the stream to the west. A footpath can be seen to the north and to the south, a steep bank leads up to an elevated piece of land.
14065: Some cereals that look like wheat are lying here.

A wild variety of brown and gold grains sprout up across the lowlands here and to the west. A footpath borders the lowlands to the north and looking south, you can see the beginnings of a jagged range of hills.
14066: Jagged hills to the south and fields of grain shining gold to the west border this footpath which runs from the east and makes its way north. The path has a pronounced slope which makes walking or riding somewhat difficult.
14067: The natural erosion of the land has caused this portion of the footpath to tilt from the north to the south, making travel on any kind of mount impossible and even travel on foot is somewhat hindered. The footpath continues on, running west-east in direction.
14068: Numerous potholes make travelling on the path here difficult. You resort to picking your way around them carefully and can only guess the condition of the path deteriorates due to flooding from the stream to the north. This section of the path lies in a low area of the land and it is probably under water during the rainier seasons of the year.
14069: Probably a hunting path at one time, constant travel has made this an actual path which follows the stream to the north closely. Still, patches of grass and weeds can be seen sprouting up, threatening to take over the path and return it to wild grass again. A flat area of grass is thriving to the south and you can enter the stream flowing to the north of the path. The path itself continues on, running straight west-east.
14070: A pack horse (Rood) is standing here, ridden by you.

Still following side by side with the stream to the north, the path continues on west-east. Flat and well beaten down in this area, one finds travel on the path here very easy and comfortable. A large expanse of plains begins to open up further to the east and a flat track is clearly visible to the south.
14071: Stream at a Turn of the Footpath
A silvery fish quickly darts through the water.

Continuing on in a east-west fashion, the stream flows between a footpath that turns to the south and an expanse of high plains that rise to the north, They seem to be quite level and could probably offer a good view of the surrounding land.
14072: Almost hidden among the tall plains grasses to the east, this tiny trail becomes an real track here to continue on south. A settlement is barely visible in that direction and this flat track appears to lead straight to it. An area of grassy flatland opens up to the west and another larger footpath can be seen when you look north.
14073: Blanketed by an abundance of taller grass and flowers, this flatland seems to be a popular grazing area for all types of animals. Paths corner the land to the north and east and grassy hills are visible to the south.
14074: Barely hills at all, the soft, subtle inclines of this hill range are covered with a short, green grass. Travel through these hills is by no means difficult and the crest of the hills merely gives a traveller the chance to survey the lands that surround. The hills flatten out into a grassy level area of land to the north and a path is visible to both the east and the south. The hills themselves continue on to the west.
14075: A small rabbit glares angrily at you.

This small, level path runs straight to both the east and west, providing and easy way to make one's journey through the plains and hills that dominate this land to the north and south. It appears that another trail meets this one to the east and looking further south-east, one can see a settlement has been established.
14076: A pack horse (Rood) is standing here, ridden by you.

A track leading from the settlement to the south and heading north crosses the path that heads west through the plains and hills in that direction. Judging by the marks alongside the road, this intersection is in constant use. The settlement that is visible to the south seems to be quite large and well-established for such a remote area and one gets the idea its inhabitants must be quite tough to survive so far out from civilization.
14077:
A large elk is standing here, chewing grass and leaves.
The large elk gazes coldly at you, chewing on a small branch.

Here, on the slopes of the Misty Mountains, a low birch forest has managed to grow. Most of the trees are covered in lichen, starting a few feet up the trunks. Their tiny branches create a dense patchwork of a canopy, making this a haven for small birds. Just beneath the slopes to the west there seems to be a camp of some kind, behind a wall of wooden stakes.
14078: A pack horse (Rood) is standing here, ridden by you.

A gently sloping path runs from the east to the west and is bordered by the brook to the south and the hills that begin to the north. The angle of the path, although not quite even, is barely enough to notice and allows one to concentrate on the journey ahead.
14079:
A huge, black wolf is here, ready to devour.
A huge, black wolf is here, ready to devour.

Judging by the numerous hoofprints and footpints on this path, it is frequented quite often, probably by the settlers in this area wishing to cross the stream at the ford some distance to the west. Plains stretch out to the north and the path itself continues on to the east and west.
14080: A pack horse (Rood) is standing here, ridden by you.

A makeshift bridle path runs from the settlement that is visible to the far east all the way to the ford that crosses the stream a little ways to the west. The path is rather wide and well beaten down from all the travel of men and horses. Jagged plains stretch out to the north and a small rivulet trickles through the hills to the south.
14081: Bridle Path next to a Ford

This path was probably established as a way to lead the horses to the ford from the settlement visible further to the east. Numerous footprints are apparent all over the ground and one can imagine that it would be easy to ford the stream to the west on foot or mounted. Plains extend to the north and a stream flows swiftly to the south.
14082: A pack horse (Rood) is standing here, ridden by you.

The water is just low enough here to allow travellers to ford the stream running from the south to the north and continue on the trail east and west. The bottom of the stream is very soft and mushy and small stones and pebbles crunch underneath as you cross. Two streams merge to the south and this trail joins another to the west.
14083: A cluster of white star-shaped forget-me-nots flourish here in reminiscence.

A series of gentle hills rise softly and continue on east. Bright wildflowers and green grass cover the hills and help keep the land firm and soft to travel upon. A grassy scarp rises up to the north and a path makes its way through the hills to the south.
14084: A high, sharp uprising of rock forms a scarp facing the edge of the hills to the south. It is covered with a soft, green grass and gives a good view of the surrounding lands. A footpath is directly north and the land levels out to a grassy flatland to the east.
14085: A sharp outcropping of earth and rock creates a jagged ridge which turns into a grassy scarp to the east. The footpath to the north tilts in this direction and a range of hills rises up to the west. Looking south, you can see grass covered plains begin to stretch out all the way to the horizon in a sea of green and brown grasses.
14086: Rough plains covered with a short brownish grass cut a jagged edge between the hills to the east and the ridge to the north. The plains continue to the west and a bridle path runs east-west to the south. Not far in the distance, there is a large settlement visible to the south-east.
14087: Cutting their way into the hills, these jagged plains extend to the east and west with an expanse of brownish grass. One would guess that these plains do not get much water as they are very dry and the grass is very poor due to constant exposure to the unfriendly combination of wind, lack of rain, and poor soil. A bridle path runs to the south and a hill range begins to the north.
14088: A grey wolf is here, snarling aggressively.

Travel through the range of jagged hills that rise up before you is difficult but not impossible. The hills themselves continue on to the east but seem to flatten out into plains to the south. An area of grainy lowlands is visible to the north and a watery elevation of land can be entered to the west.
14089: These jagged plains slope sharply into small crests that could almost be termed hills if they were any steeper. A soft, thick grass covers the ground, mixed with a few stray grains. A hill range looms to the north and a bridle path is visible to the south. One could enter the stream directly west.
14090: A large eagle soars above you.

An elevated piece of land allows a clear view of the surrounding areas, revealing a series of low, jagged hills to the east and a section of grainy lowlands which lie to the north. Due to a natural spring bubbling up cool, clear water continuously, the ground in this area is quite soggy and water is standing in some areas. During the spring and summer months, there is probably a good deal of mud to contend with.
14091: A jagged set of hills rises up here and to the west. Loose stones and unstable rocks makes travelling through them somewhat treacherous but not impossible. One is forced to choose a path through them with care. Plains back up to the hills to the south and a footpath curves away to the north.
14092: A pack horse (Rood) is standing here, ridden by you.

The thin trail meanders through the grassy hills, surrounded by low trees and green-grey bushes. The trail itself is so worn down by frequent cattle movement that it lies half a foot below the soft surrounding soil. Many stones have been laid bare in the light brown soil, making it somewhat troublesome to travel on the route. South of here the Misty Mountains create an impassable barrier, even for the most daring climber.
14093: A pack horse (Rood) is standing here, ridden by you.

A well-travelled trail leads through the flat plains, a couple of feet wide, going in a straight west-east direction. Another path, small and thin, branches off to the south, where the plains rise up and become hillier. The grass which surrounds it is lush and broad-leaved, with a few flowers giving some colour. A quiet trickling sound can be heard to the north, a small stream flowing through the grass. South-east are the Misty Mountains, the greatest mountain range in all of Middle-earth.
14094: A Wide Footpath through the Plains
There is a lot of water on the ground.

The trail goes in an east-west direction. It is a few feet wide here, and seems to become even larger to the east. The surroundings are quite flat, with a few hills scattered around you. Here and there traces of farming can be seen - near the trail the grass has been gnawed on by creatures and an occasional pile of dung can be seen. The murmuring sounds of a small stream can be heard north of here, bubbling and chortling over a stony bed.
14095: A small trail comes through the palisade west of here and runs due east. It is a couple of feet wide, and frequent travel has bared the earth of its green grass covering. Above the palisade west of here a few chimneys can be seen, smoke coming out of some of them. To the south the vast Misty Mountains hinder anyone from travelling in that direction, while to the north the silent murmur of water can be heard.
14096: This little line of a stream is running from east to west, surrounded by bushes and trees. Birds can be heard all around, but are very hard to actually see in the abundant undergrowth. Many tracks of crushed vegetation can be seen leading down to the water, the trails of large animals coming to drink at the water. A few farm houses have been built on a knoll just north of here, their contours visible against the sky.
14097: A pack horse (Rood) is standing here, ridden by you.

A small trail that comes from the east turns quickly south here, following the mountain base. The grass is thick and green, and there seem to be many animals living in the small bushes. Just east of here it is a small stream falls from the cliffs and flows through here, joining an overgrown brook from the north. East lie some long abandoned ruins, simple farm buildings not used in many a year.
14098: Ruins near the Emergence of an Underground Stream
A pack horse (Rood) is standing here, ridden by you.

A small stream appears out of the cliffs to the south a few yards up, and falls to earth, before pooling and slowly flowing west to join with another stream. Alongside the water are the last remnants of some buildings. There must have been four houses here, clustered together in the shelter of the Misty Mountains. To the east a small hill can be seen before the base of the main range of mountains, a giant and never-ending series of white peaks.
14099: Ruins cover this low hill lies just beneath the main Misty Mountains. There seems to have been a large number of small farms here at some point in the past, before they were consumed by fire. There also seem to have been some kind of stone palisade around the farmhouses, now only a crumbled yard or two high. The remains of a recently used campfire are near the eastern wall.
14100: Other than a pronounced slope from north to south, this track is quite wide and comfortable to travel upon, leading straight into the settlement that lies a little ways to the south. Running straight north-south, the track meets another trail directly to the south and runs past the soft, grassy hills that rise and fall gently to the west.
14101: The brightly white peaks of the Misty Mountains tower south and east. The vegetation here is sparse, but near the base of the mountains low bushes and trees take advantage of the shelter. An old campfire lies in a circle of small stones, laid in a tight circle to prevent it from spreading. It is evident that it is long since it was used last, the ashes almost erased by wind and rain.
14102: A pack horse (Rood) is standing here, ridden by you.

A small trail runs through the fields, along the base of the Misty Mountains, turning west and north here to avoid the peaks. Even the best climber would be defeated by those sheer cliffs which rise up several hundred feet. There are many low bushes and small trees scattered in this area, providing shelter from wind and snow. A slight murmuring sound can be heard north of here.
14103: Fields on the Lower Misty Mountains

The fields here are partly burnt and the soil is bared in several places, showing the light, sandy soil that covers the lower parts of the Misty Mountains. The mountains tower up quickly in all directions but west, where a small hill is raised like an outpost of the mountains. South many bushes grow on the steep slope, crawling up the mountainsides and making passage difficult. They seem oddly placed, almost as if someone has grown them to block the route.
14104: A small stream rolls through the grassy plains here. A few large stones and boulders have been bared by the force of nature and lie in its centre, the waters cutting around them. Just south of here a palisade has been raised, many feet high and with a few roofs visible behind it. The palisade lies before one side of a spur of the Misty Mountains, casting a powerful shadow over the settlement. North of here a few small farms can be seen, seemingly abandoned but for a few animals standing amidst them.
14105: Surrounded by flat land this trickling stream breaks the monotony of sparse vegetation and scattered hills. It is bordered by flourishing plant life and a few tall trees. The sandy soil is slowly being flushed westwards as the stream gnaws on the land, meandering its way downstream. It is by no means hard to cross the stream, since it is well under ten feet wide. South of here a giant spur thrusts out from the Misty Mountains, towering over Dunland.
14106: A small stream is rushing downstream through the plains here. It is not even a few feet deep yet, with the riverbed of smooth pebbles still visible. The water itself is not hard to traverse, but will probably be less forgiving a few miles west of here, as it gathers tributaries.
14107: Southern Slopes of the Misty Mountains

You are on the slopes of a steep range of hills, a spur thrust out from the main Misty Mountains to the east. Just north of here is the end of that spur, a rocky outcrop like a pointing finger. Some way south, where the land drops to the plains, is a large forest, and running from its western borders is a river.
14108: To the north a steep peak rises sharply above you, towering high into the sky and dominating the landscape. A few small, sturdy bushes have managed to take root in the rocky and barren soil, but otherwise only a low covering of grass clings to the harsh surface. The rocky foothills of the mountains recede out to the south and west, while the area becomes more hilly to the east as the ground climbs slowly.
14109: A colourful butterfly is fluttering around here.

The steep granite heights of the Misty Mountains are gradually transforming into undulating foothills here, covered with rocks and boulders. Nevertheless it is still a tiring route to travel, with long falls and sudden crevices at every turn. The ground becomes flatter as the the slopes recede west and south of here, reaching out into the plains of Dunland.
14110: Except for the low, hardy bushes little can grow here, the wind and cold making it a hostile environment to wildlife. West the slopes lessen and first brush then trees are visible. There is a whole forest there, some rare shelter for the vegetation underneath. The mountains provide an impassable wall not far to the north, their towering faces of rock giving no hand-holds to climb.
14111: Southern Slopes of the Misty Mountains

Nothing much can grow here in the infertile earth, high above the plains. The bare land slopes up towards the giant peaks, impassable obstacles with gleaming white caps high in the clouds. A few rocks and boulders have fallen down from the cliffs, breaking the sandy soil.
14112: Lower Slopes of the Misty Mountains
A colourful butterfly is fluttering around here.

A high grey wall of rock rises above you, a large spur of the Misty Mountains reaching into the plains of Dunland. The grey granite blocks all passage north, stretching for many miles east and west. The ground slopes slightly down to the south-west, but the terrain does not change much from the rocky and infertile soil here.
14113: A fierce boar is here, making grunting noises.

Here, under the shadow of the towering rockface east, are some elevated and isolated lands. A few bushes manage to grow, trying to cover the rocky ground as they take advantage of the shelter. The grass is low and brown, conditioned by the hard weather. East the grey stone of the Misty Mountains rises high into the sky, blocking all further passage.
14114: A Spur of Hills from the Mountains

Thrown out from the mountains like a rippling arm in the plains, this range of hills is no more than mere foothills to the heights you can see east of here. Still, they take you quite a distance above the plains, giving a fair view of the land for several miles. Climbing down to the west or north is quite tricky, and would require care to avoid falling.
14115: A sturdy pack horse is standing here.

Low bushes crawl across the wind-whipped plains. Among the shrubs are a few low trees with bent and crooked branches, tortured by the constant wind from the mountains. Sometimes sounds can be heard from within the bushes, an indication of wildlife in this desolate part of Dunland. From the steep hills to the east falls a mountain stream, which trickles its way towards a forest visible miles to the west.
14116: A fierce boar is here, making grunting noises.

Thick grass seems to flourish here among the low, creeping bushes that cover the dusty mountain soil. A few birches and pines stand lonely against the harsh winds, the ground beneath them bare and hard-packed soil. North of here the ground starts to slope upwards towards the Misty Mountains, providing a seemingly easy start on an impossible journey in that direction. In amongst the brush is a brook, twisting its way through the plains but always ending up going westward.
14117:
A forest giant is here, fighting Cromdreath (CC).
Cromdreath the Mountain Troll (CC) is here, fighting a forest giant.

In this mixed pine and birch forest travelling is not very easy. There is much dense underbrush to fight, the branches a few feet above the ground. The dark brown soil is covered with needles, leaves and a few branches, a soft lair that makes it hard to move around silently. Barely audible is the tinkling of a line of water, hidden in the undergrowth.
14118: A Mixed Birch and Pine Forest

A shrub with maple-like leaves is growing here.
A robin is here, carrying small pieces of wood to its nest.
A long-tailed bird watches you from the vegetation.
A robin is here, carrying small pieces of wood to its nest.

Several different kinds of pines have managed to grow here, well nourished by the waters of a mountain stream which passes nearby. It flows in from the east, all the time gathering in water from small brooks, and continues north through the trees. Traces of larger wild animals can be found scattered around - large footprints and crushed undergrowth showing their route to the water.
14119: A long-tailed bird watches you from the vegetation.

Many birches grow here in these wooded uplands. The vegetation is sparse, mostly consisting of moss clinging to the exposed rock and various kinds of small hardy bushes. Most of it grows near a stream, flourishing in its clear water. There are quite a few hunting paths, their well-worn condition showing recent use. West of here the forest grows less dense and eventually finds itself defeated by the plains of Dunland.
14120:
A forest spider is here crawling around.
A woodchuck is watching for enemies here.
A long-tailed bird watches you from the vegetation.
A robin is here, carrying small pieces of wood to its nest.

Birches dominate this part of the forest, before the tremendous heights just north-east of here. The branches reach outwards from the stems a couple of feet above the brushy ground, making it quite hard to travel. Broken twigs and all sorts of different tracks can be found in the hard soil, with small screes a common obstacle. Just south of here a few pines and spruces have managed to get a foothold among the crowded birches, making movement there very tiring.
14121: Sloping gently upwards to the north-east, these plains are battered constantly by the winds which funnel down from the mountains. East the mountains edge ever closer together, until in the distance the arc closes. Immediately west of here lies a large forest of birches, stretching for several miles. It would seem to be the only place around here that cover from the winds could be found.
14122:
A small and tough weed grows here.
A restless rabbit bounces around.

These plains are in a huge three-sided basin, surrounded by mountains on all sides but west. Two giant spurs of mountains thrown out from the main range create this isolation, dominating the horizon. However wildlife cannot thrive in it, due to the winds that sweep down from the east. Funnelled by the narrow valley where the two spurs meet, they streak down the valley almost constantly, stripping the earth to a rocky soil.
14123: Bush-covered Slopes of the Misty Mountains

These lower slopes of the Misty Mountains are covered in low bushes and a few sparsely placed birches. To the west and south the trees grow in larger numbers to form a small forest. To your east the lack of taller growth allows the cold winds to howl fiercely across the open slopes, stopping anything but the very sturdiest of plants from surviving.
14124: Tall, lush grass is the predominant vegetation on these plains, thriving in the fertile soil and well nourished by the constant water supply to the north. Grasslands extend further to the south and a series of uneven plains begin to the west. A large birch and pine forest looms above you to the east.
14125: Sharp rocks and large boulders bulge out from the soft bed of grass, making the ground craggy and far from comfortable for travellers. A wide range of hills runs across the western grasslands, like an outstretched arm from the mountain.
14126: The spur of hills protrudes from the grasslands, in contrast to the flat plains which surround them. As they draw closer to their parent mountain range, their height grows and the land become barren and cold. Elevated above the great plain of Enedwaith, the hills give a good view over the grassy lands. However that wide and somewhat monotonous landscape makes it hard to focus attention on anything in particular, as the swathe of green merges into a whole.
14127: Rough, uneven plains stretch out here, covered by a short, tough grass which seems to grow lusher and more fertile to the east. A large hill range extends to both the south and west and a brook is flowing slowly through the plains and hills to the north.
14128: Extremely rough hills make travel arduous with loose stone and sharp inclines taking all of one's time and energy. The ground is practically bare of all vegetation except a few clumps of short grass here and there along the hillsides. The hills continue on to both the south and west and plains begin to the east.
14129: A waist-high evergreen shrub grows here, with thick, reaching branches.

As the hills stretch further north, the western spur-ends of the range slump swiftly. They come to an abrupt ending west of here, the grasslands taking over dominance of the landscape. East and south the foothills grow, as they run nearer to the vast mountains. Still, they remain accessible, mere lumps in the ground compared to those snow-tipped behemoths.
14130: A range of hills resides east of here. The grasslands themselves are riddled with sharp, pointy rocks and bleak slabs of stone. Further to the south the grasslands are unscathed by the cold, hard rocks, becoming lusher in stark contrast to the mountains.
14131: The steep incline and uneven ground of these hills conspire to give a traveller difficulty passing through them. The range continues heading on to the north or you could make your way through the plains to the west or the grasslands to the south.
14132: This hill range is wedged between the bluff to the west, a small rivulet to the north, and the brook that flows to the east. The hills seem to extend to the south for miles and are covered with a short, tough grass. Many loose rocks make travel in this area somewhat treacherous.
14133: Bluff in Front of the Rivulet

A mother eagle flies high above, looking for prey.
A small, helpless eaglet screams for more food.
A small, helpless eaglet screams for more food.

From the top of this bluff you can see for miles in every direction, the land stretching out before you in a sea of colour and variety. Looking north, one can see a small rivulet below heading east, the sound of its water echoing off the side of the bluff. Directly to the east, a series of hills rises up but you would have to climb back down the bluff and enter them from the south-west. Far to the north, a large forest is visible and a watch tower can be seen quite clearly in the north-west from this height. A large nest has been built into a crevice in the rocks of this bluff.
14134: Sloping from a southern angle, this rocky bluff overlooks a stream running at its base to the north and is bordered to the south by a series of rugged plains. One could climb higher onto the bluff to the east and get a better view of the land from there. It looks too difficult to scramble down the side of the bluff to either the west or north.
14135: Clods of earth and short tufts of grass break up the land in these plains. It looks as though a herd of animals find this a popular grazing spot and the ground certainly shows signs of being torn up by their hooves as they make their way across the plains. A bluff slopes upwards to the north and more plains continue to the south.
14136: Broken plains covered with a thick blanket of short grass and tall grains stretch from here on to the west. Loose stone and clods of dirt make passage across these plains difficult and time consuming. You can climb up to the top of the bluff to the north or enter the rocky grasslands that stretch out to the south.
14137: Tufts of soft, lush grass blend with sharp-edged rocks and stones to form a craggy and harsh landscape. As the lands stretch south, the rocks become sparse until finally all that remains is the soft and gentle grass. The western grounds are partially drenched in water, making the soil soft and slippery.
14138: A nearby stream fills the air with its soft trickling sounds. To the west you can espy a trail travelling in a north-south direction across the plains. Vast, unkempt grasslands stretch far southeast, running up to the very foothills of a grand range of mountain.
14139:
A Dunlending herdsman, in ragged leather stands here watching over his herd.
A domesticated pony, beast of burden to many, stands here.
A beautiful and docile horse is standing here.
A sturdy pack horse is standing here.
A young colt is frolicking playfully.

Smooth plains thick with a healthy covering of lush green grasses and clover lie here, making this an excellent place to graze horses and other livestock from the settlement to the east. A waist-high, solid wooden fence surrounds all sides of the grazing plains, with a large gate to the east. A brook borders the plains to the south and west and a path is visible to the north.
14140: A large cabinet capable of storing goods is here.

Built so well it is nearly draftproof, this storage lodge holds most of the food and skins that the settlers save up in reserve for those months in which food might be scarce. Piles of skins line the wall up to the ceiling in the back of the lodge and smoked meat hangs in strips from the ceiling along with strings of dried herbs and small vegetables. A few women of the village are busy reworking some of the skins into garments and blankets for the village and others can be seen braiding the various herbs into strands to dry.
14141:
A small oaken table has been set here.
A small child is here playing happily.
A small child is here playing happily.
A Dunlending woman is here tending to her children.

The inside of this lodge is small and rather dim, but the owners have done the best they could to create the illusion of space with the placement of the few simple pieces of furniture they have managed to collect. A small bed is pushed against the wall to the right and looking under it, you can see a trundle bed that can easily be pulled out at night for an extra sleeping place. A circle in the middle of the room has been reserved as a place to build a cooking fire, and above one can see a small hole near the top of the roof which draws the smoke up and out of the lodge. Sturdy, wooden chairs surround the small oaken table.
14142: A swarthy Dunlending warrior is here, guarding his village against intruders.

Standing in the heart of the settlement, there is a definite decrease of noise and activity. Things are much calmer here and it looks as if most of the lodges surrounding you are probably the homes of the settlers. A path leads away from the village towards the brook to the south, which borders the settlement. You could enter one of the smaller lodges to the east but the size of the lodge directly to the west catches your attention. It is much larger than any other building you have seen in the settlement so far, and judging by how well it is built, it is an important part of their village.
14143:
A huge, smoking campfire is burning here.
A swarthy Dunlending warrior is here, guarding his village against intruders.
A swarthy Dunlending warrior is here, guarding his village against intruders.

This large settlement seems to be in an ideal location, with its combination of shelter from the forest to the east and its constant supply of water from the brook to the south. The wooden lodges these people built for homes look solid and snug against the elements, and the sides of the lodges are covered with skins stretched across them to dry. There is an air of constant alertness for enemies and predators that keeps these people looking suspiciously at your intrusion into the safety of their village.
14144: This building seems to be more important than the others. There is only one bed in the corner and shelves on the wall have various jars and other implements on them. Against the western wall a small fireplace sits providing some warmth in the bitter winters that are commonplace in this country. On the south wall hangs a large tapestry depicting the life of the foresters, and the settlements they hail from.
14145:
A soldier dressed in polished equipment eyes you warily.
A soldier dressed in polished equipment eyes you warily.
A soldier dressed in polished equipment eyes you warily.
A Dunlending Captain is here, overseeing his men.
A sturdy pack horse is standing here.

You have entered a small encampment surrounded by a tall wooden palisade. A fire dominates the centre of the camp with a couple of huts on either side. The huts themselves are old but have been made with some craftsmanship from the surrounding forest. To the north a large, reinforced wooden gate stands and looks like it would keep out the most determined hordes. Around you people go about their business always keeping one eye on you, the strangers.
14146: Upon entering this austere hut, there seems to be very little in the way of creature comfort. Bunks line the northern and southern walls. Another door in the eastern wall leads back outside. The bunks themselves are made of plain planks. A thin blanket on each, which are so thin, they can only supply very little protection and almost none during the winter months. A few possessions are littered around and the only light and a little warmth is provided by a lam on a small and simple table.
14147:
A sturdy pack horse is standing here.
A stocky mountain mule is here, waiting to serve.

Many mounts mill around in this paddock. Here the beasts are kept, used by the loggers to drag the huge trees they fall to the camp, where they can be cut and then moved on to the Dunlending villages further south. Apart from the animals, watering and feeding troughs, also here is a small area used for storing a few of the great trunks.
14148: On the Lower Slopes of the Misty Mountains

Surrounded by the sheer slopes of the Misty Mountains on all sides but west, you find yourself in a small valley. It is partly covered with low bushes and filled with fallen rocks fallen from the heights. It would be near insanity to climb these mountains, the rocky walls stretching forever above your head. To the west you can see the valley open into a huge basin between two spurs of the mountains, gradually lowering in altitude as it heads out to the flat plains.
14150:
A sturdy rope has been tied here and descends below.
A rock lizard is here, motionless as it observes you.

The steep mountain side is extremely hard to scale. A white peak looms above you to the east while a deep valley, dotted with large rocks, can be seen far beneath you to the west. A small hole, leading down into the darkness, can be seen.
14152: A pack horse (Rood) is standing here, ridden by you.

The tiny path twists through the bare landscape. These are the mighty Misty Mountains, an almost dead place where nothing much lives. It seems very hard to survive here, as the vegetation is sparse and there is no obvious evidence of animals. Several peaks, their white tops glistening, rise high above this spot. West of here the path winds between more peaks, slowly descending.
14153: A pack horse (Rood) is standing here, ridden by you.

A rocky defile between two cliffs opens up here, one of many such small valleys in the Misty Mountains. It is barren, cold enough to deprive it of vegetation but not high enough to be snowed over most of the year. Through it runs a small path, obviously barely used, which leads north out of the defile. It ends at a metal gate, crusted with flaking orange rust, in the mountainside. There does not appear to be any other route out of here, the exposed cliffs being far too steep to climb.
14154:
A veteran Urughash orc paces around angrily.
A veteran Urughash orc paces around angrily.
A warrior of the Urughash is here, guarding the gates.
A warrior of the Urughash is here, guarding the gates.

The walls of this natural cave have been carelessly hewn, giving the impression of a poorly skilled mason. The grey tiles covering the floor are decorated with barely noticeable patterns, their crudity not diminished through the layers of muck that cover them. There is a strong oaken table and some stools in one corner of the cavern, where the guards gamble and arm-wrestle. A set of stairs climbs up in the eastern wall, while west is a strong metal gate. Prominent on the eastern wall is a drawing in gaudy colours: a large spiked club, dripping with blood.
14155:
The corpse of an orkish gate-guard is lying here.
The corpse of an orkish gate-guard is lying here.
A pair of chain mail sleeves lies here.
A rigid leather helmet lies here.
A rigid leather breastplate is on the ground.
A weapons rack stands against the wall.
In the rack are a black metal shield and a scimitar.

The room is filled with the scent of leather, rising from the many battle-worn pieces of armour and clothing that litter the ground. Weapons stand in racks and shields hang on the wall, where they can be swiftly grabbed and taken into use against any enemy. There is a narrow slit in the western wall, from where a path outside can be seen.
14156: The only pieces of furniture in this room are shaky tables and creaking, rotten wooden beds, covered with dark-brown stains and fresh blood. As the numerous raiding parties leaving these caves do not always return in best health, the severely wounded receive basic medical treatment here, although to many it proves to be as deadly as any final blow in the battle.
14159: The corpse of the orkish undertaker is lying here.

Roaring flames occasionally burst out of the huge fireplace and lick the ceiling of this ominous cavern. The heat is searing, hitting anyone who enters the room like a physical blow. The reek of burning flesh hangs heavily in the air, combining with the heat into a vicious stink. Several corpses lie piled carelessly on a table, their bodies shattered in battle, waiting for their turn to be consumed in fire.
14160: Passages from the east and south meet here, forming a spacious cavern. As the walls are not decorated nor finished, it is possible to make out the different layers of rock that make up these mountains. It would be hard to spot the door that stands at the far western side of the cavern, if not for the crude orkish graffiti that surrounds and emphasises it.
14161:
The corpse of an Urughash soldier is lying here.
The corpse of an Urughash soldier is lying here.
The corpse of an Urughash soldier is lying here.
The corpse of a veteran Urughash guard is lying here.
The corpse of an Urughash officer is lying here.
Cromdreath (CC) is standing here.
Umbe the Cave Troll is standing here.
Taara (TT) is standing here.

This corridor seems to have been carved by some underground torrent, now long dried up or directed elsewhere, and later retouched by tools of workmen. The passage continues to twist onwards west, and opens into a small cavern to the south. The floor is covered with dirt and small rocks, making walking at any speed treacherous.
14162: A pool of darkish water has formed in a depression of the stone.

This small cavern continues west, and narrows northwards to a tunnel, showing signs of the long-calmed fury of an underground stream. Water drips from the sharp stalagmites, forming clear pools on the floor. The sound of every drip is amplified and echoed by the smooth walls, a soft cacophony of noise almost like that of many people whispering.
14164: A stone wall quite unexpectedly appears from the shadows, yet it is not a dead end, but a sharp turn in the tunnel that continues northwards and grows into a small room to the east. Unlike other corridors this seems to be carved by hard work and effort from scratch, and is therefore much cruder.
14165:
A newborn spider is here.
A newborn spider is here.
A newborn spider is here.
A huge, poisonous spider is here.
A huge, poisonous spider is here.
A grey spider is stalking here, preparing to drain you of life.

This is probably the first room built in this labyrinth of caves and tunnels, now long abandoned and partly collapsed in one corner. The rotten remains of a table are scattered on the floor with various rusty tools, and on the walls some signs of faded drawings can be seen. The door that was once the entrance has been torn off its hinges and is probably now used elsewhere.

The corpse of an Urughash soldier is lying here.
