The corpse of an Urughash soldier is lying here.
The orkish instructor, wielding a broad scimitar, is here, fighting Mandara (m).
The shadow of an Urughash officer is floating here.
Mandara the Elf (m), wielding the black sword, is here, fighting the orkish instructor.

Several racks and poles have been erected in this eastern part of the hall, where slaves and prisoners caught in the surrounding lands are tied up and used as models for target practice. Receiving advice from their instructor, undoubtedly proficient in the skills of pain and torture, the snaga leaving this hall will know how to hit their enemy where it hurts most.
14167:
The corpse of an Urughash officer is lying here.
The corpse of an Urughash soldier is lying here.
The corpse of an orkish drudge is lying here.
The corpse of an Urughash officer is lying here.
A veteran Urughash guard, wielding a spiked war club, is here, fighting Mandara (m).
Mandara the Elf (m), wielding the black sword, is here, fighting a veteran Urughash guard.

In this corner of the vast hall fresh warriors are taught their basic tasks, whom they should obey and whom they should kill on sight. Part of the wall has been scraped clean of dirt and is now decorated with a vague and barely legible map. Where the faint drawing ends, shackles await disobedient snaga. They are tied up here and whipped to teach others some manners and to satisfy the blood lust of their instructor.
14168:
A veteran Urughash orc paces around angrily.
A veteran Urughash orc paces around angrily.
Gsharakh is here, working at his forge.

The deafening clatter of metal on metal and the thick forge smoke is the daily working environment in this corner of the huge hall. The ever increasing ranks of orcs need a constant supply of weapons and armour and the local blacksmith, familiar with the harsh conditions of the battleground, makes sure no fellow orc goes to combat bare-handed.
14169:
The corpse of a snaga orc is lying here.
A small oaken table has been set here.

After the tiring, tedious and often painful lessons the snaga come here to eat, sleep and quarrel. A huge steaming cauldron here looks like the mockery of an altar, for some orcs just as significant in sacredness. The walls of the rooms are covered in beds, hewn out of the rock.
14170:
A wooden chest stands in the corner.
A wooden chest stands in the corner.
A small barrel stands on the ground.
A small barrel made of aged oak and strong iron hoops stands here.
A beer barrel has been left here.
A water barrel has been left here.

Various goods have been piled in this room, hung on the walls or piled onto shelves. As each war party returns from pillaging and looting, the supplies of the merchant are refreshed, and it is here that the freshly recruited soldiers and scouts can equip for their blood-curdling task. The desk between the customers and the owner of the shop seems to be a line of chalk drawn on the floor, the crossing of which would cost an intruder dearly.
14171: This is the central guardroom of the caves. Rickety wooden beds stand along the walls and the table is littered with food and drink. As the guards are not allowed to bring any entertainment into their quarters, most spend their spare time elsewhere watching the torture of captured slaves and prisoners.
14172: A circular stone well has been built here.

This medium-sized cavern is home to a central guardpoint, meant to prevent any intruder from getting any further into the caves. A grotesquely carved doorway lies to the north, while weapon racks seem to be placed for soldiers storming in through the southern door. The few pieces of furniture here have been positioned to enable effortless guarding of the tunnels east, although the ramshackle wooden tables would not prove much defence against a strong foe.
14173: An orc is hurrying to fulfill his errand.

Stone steps once joined the lower and upper levels, but now the linking passage consists only of a cracked and pitted slope. The lack of any stonecraft has undoubtedly cost many orcs broken bones and wrenched limbs, for there is a good chance of tumbling down into darkness from here.
14174:
A weapons rack stands against the wall.
A simple wooden chest is here.
A small oaken table has been set here.
Tordol the Dwarf (t), wielding a mighty dwarven axe, is standing here.
Calarion the Elf, wielding a broadsword, is standing here.
Jabez the Elf, wielding an iron-shod mace, is standing here.
Krecek, wielding an engraved broadsword, is standing here.
Nimur the Dwarf, wielding an ornate, steel-shafted warhammer, is standing here.

A rectangular chamber of cut rock, this is the sleeping chambers of the clan's chieftain. The floor is littered with thick animal furs, some of them still with the head attached. Some basic pieces of furniture complete the quarters, some of obviously orkish make, others by a more skilled craftsman. Like many of the items in these caves, they were probably looted from the Dunlendings, or from some passing caravan.

The corpse of a veteran Urughash guard is lying here.
The corpse of an Urughash soldier is lying here.

The corpse of a veteran Urughash guard is lying here.
The corpse of an Urughash soldier is lying here.

Scarcely decorated stone pillars have been erected on both sides of a robust stone throne that stands in the middle of this large cavern. The uneven walls are decorated with various colours of carpets, probably looted from vanquished foes, and other trophies of war. West a small passageway leads into sleeping chambers, while south a badly-carved portal leads into a spacious cavern.
14176: It is impossible to tell whether these are rough stairs or just natural bumps and depressions that allow passage between the lower and upper levels. The side of the tunnel has been hewn and smoothed, so heavier cargoes can be hoisted down the slope.
14177:
The corpse of a veteran Urughash guard is lying here.
The corpse of an Urughash officer is lying here.
The corpse of an Urughash soldier is lying here.
The corpse of an Urughash soldier is lying here.
The corpse of an Urughash soldier is lying here.
The corpse of a snaga orc is lying here.
Mandara the Elf (m), wielding the black sword, is standing here.

This is a central intersection of many tunnels, a well used passageway. The clatter of shields and weapons echo from the east, with the occasional cry of pain. The grey tiles that cover the floor are worn bare by the constant trudging of heavy metal boots, but a vague pattern can still be made out in them, now long defaced.
14178: A rusty pickaxe with a broken handle lies discarded here.

This shaft has been cut at an extremely steep angle, following the line of a natural lode of iron. A frayed rope is the only means of support for the slave miners. Every now and then a rumbling can be heard in the tunnel, as large rocks dislodge themselves, crashing down the shaft and out of your sight.
14179:
A prisoner is standing here.
A prisoner is standing here.

This is a completely new tunnel dug into the mountains. It hasn't been fully widened yet, and the floor is still covered with gravel and rubble, making passage tiresome. Water trickles down from between iron hooks attached to the wall, that holds a strong rope offering support. Occasional natural depressions in the ceiling indicate that this is by no means a safe room to linger in.
14181: Although only recently dug, this passage is already taken into use, its ceiling supported with rickety wooden props. A cavity on the southern wall bears marks of pickaxes and other tools, as if someone had tried to dig another tunnel there, but abandoned the idea. To the west the passage continues and opens into a larger cavern.
14182: This cave was dug for the female orcs and their offspring, who are viewed by the rest of the orcs as an unhealthy nuisance. Some robust toys are scattered about the floor, while a large fire with a pot swinging over it functions as a primitive kitchen. Barely recognisable scenes of battle have been scratched on the walls with a dark-brown matter, perhaps the mother orcs trying to teach their young.
14183:
The corpse of an orkish outcast is lying here.
The corpse of a snaga orc is lying here.

Robust beds stand along the walls of this cavern, while a large stone rock in the centre acts as a table. No warrior uruk with any pride would spend a moment here - it is the sleeping quarters of the tribe's females and their children that don't have the strength to wield a weapon yet. The reek of filth is heavy in the air, the quarters never having been cleaned.
14184: The tunnels meeting here are natural, perhaps cut by some underground stream long since diverted elsewhere. Now they have become part of the warrens of tunnels inhabited by orcs. The western branch opens into a large cavern, while the northern one seems to be paved with small grey tiles. On the eastern wall there is some kind of rope-mechanism for hoisting various goods up the slope, to the upper part of the caves.
14185: What first catches the eye in this tunnel is the grey tiling that paves the floor. Although less than expertly laid, it is still a noticeable difference on the rough and unpolished passageways and tunnels through the rest of this cave system. Some scalps and other mutilated body parts hang on the wall at regular intervals, becoming more skeletal to the east. The tunnel continues south also, where the tiling ends, and opens into an intersection.
14186: The neatly paved passage continues west and north, where it becomes an junction with a passage going west. In addition to the ominous trophies hanging on the wall, several poles have been erected here, where victims of some arcane magic hang - no normal weapon would rip its target apart with such ferocious strength and explosive manner. Although sturdily built, the tunnel's ceiling has still needed to be later supported with wooden beams. It appears that this part of the passage is prone to forces that might tear it apart.
14187: Tordol the Dwarf (t), wielding a mighty dwarven axe, is standing here trying to concentrate.

This intersection has been decorated with a great amount of morbid care. There is an eye-catchingly intricate carving on the eastern wall, and a pyramid of skulls in the centre of the junction. The passage leading west is covered with a narrow carpet woven of nothing else but pale and tender-looking skin. Various ritualistic patterns have been drawn on the ceiling with soot and some other dried dark matter, flaking away in most parts.
14188: A Ledge above an Underground River
A patch of moss grows here on a wet, flat stone.

The tunnel makes a sharp turn and bends west and south. The grey tiles end abruptly and a rocky surface extends from there on. Several cracks have formed on the smooth walls, leaving the impression of forgotten care. A strong draft of underground wind blows from the west, where the water flows towards.
14189: The ledge ends here, the last fragments long since crumbled away. Below, the fast-flowing water creates a strong draft of wind in the tunnel as it speeds on westward. The only ways on from here are east along the ledge, or down into the water and wherever it may carry you.
14190: The smell of death hangs heavy in the air of this cavern. The chamber has many different levels linked by rickety wooden staircases, and is rich in niches and depressions. Torches high on the cavern walls cast an eerie flickering light, placed deliberately to leave some areas in the shade. A dark pool lies steaming and seething in the northern half of the cavern, the walls above it covered with indecipherable symbols and drawings. Next to it is a black altar, cut from marble-smooth black stone.
14191:
The corpse of a veteran Urughash guard is lying here.
A soft pouch, made from leather, has been left here.
The corpse of a veteran Urughash guard is lying here.
The corpse of a veteran Urughash guard is lying here.
The corpse of Mordrath the Uroth-Ghash is lying here.
The corpse of a veteran Urughash guard is lying here.
Calarion the Elf, wielding a broadsword, is standing here.
Jabez the Elf, wielding an iron-shod mace, is standing here.
Krecek, wielding an engraved broadsword, is resting here.
Nimur the Dwarf, wielding an ornate, steel-shafted warhammer, is standing here.

The chamber is drowned in utter darkness - a darkness that seems somehow to be more than a lack of light. The tiny fire in the middle of the room burns with a bluish tinge, but casts no light. The symmetrical domed chamber above looks as if it were burnt into solid rock - the surface is pitch black and completely smooth. There are absolutely no furniture or decorations, only a circle of leaves and fragile twigs around the fire. This is where the tribe's shaman spends most of his time, drawing strength from some malevolent source.
14192: A swift underground stream comes swiftly through a crack east of here, forcing itself down a narrow passage. The water is extremely cold, drawn as it is from the high snows the mountains above. It flows westward from here, hurdling rocks and squeezing around natural rock formations, before dropping off in a sudden fall into a northbound current. Above you can climb out of the stream, and onto the end of a ledge.
14193: A continuous breeze of fresh air from a wide aperture in the north wall keeps this part of the caves clean of cobwebs and dust, unlike most of the areas deeper inside. Looking out you can discern some of the terrain outside, mainly the steep valley walls. Undoubtedly you would be able to see more if you were to lean closer to the aperture.
14194: A sumptuous chamber harbours the entrance gate and provides passage to a tunnel leading east, further into the mountain. A small, broken staircase runs along the western wall. Originally it led to a guardpost above but now it is of little use, due to years of neglect. Protruding from the floor, a large lever sets a stark contrast to the surrounding smooth walls and well-cut floor.
14195:
Tordol the Dwarf (t), wielding a mighty dwarven axe, is standing here.
A stocky mountain mule is here, waiting to serve.

A clearing has been made here through the forested valley, the woods giving way to a broad, paved path leading up to the very face of the rock. The trail does not end there however, for a grand gate has been crafted and set to guard an entrance into the mountain itself. Grim carvings mar the enormous gate and the surrounding rock, as if to give a premonition of what lies beyond.
14196:
A large bat is lying here, mortally wounded.
Tordol the Dwarf (t), wielding a mighty dwarven axe, is here, fighting a large bat.
A stocky mountain mule is here, waiting to serve.

A smooth, finely wrought tunnel cuts a passage through the mountain. Due west it widens and reaches a large chamber. A faint roaring sound echoes in the gloomy darkness of a tunnel running east, deeper into the mountain.
14197: The corpse of a black-furred bat is lying here.

Great pillars tower before you, reaching ever upwards into the darkness above. A roaring sound emanates from intricate shafts at the base of each pillar as fresh air is channelled into the tunnels. The turbulent winds lash out at you and send dust dancing through the air, making it hard for you to see clearly.
14198: Beds of various sizes have been lined up along the walls. Although of different shapes and sizes, they all share one property - all are considerably small. Not even the larger of the beds would suit an average sized man. A few cradles by the western wall tell tales of children playing here at one time, but they are long gone now, and nothing remains save a few scattered, discarded belongings.
14199: Several short beds have been arrayed in some form of barrack condition. The chamber itself is rather crude and unornamented, as if to house only the less prominent of the dwellers. A thick layer of dust has settled upon all of the furniture, giving it a hazy grey hue.
14200:
Tordol the Dwarf (t), wielding a mighty dwarven axe, is standing here.
A stocky mountain mule is here, waiting to serve.

A pale silvery light illuminates the eastern end of this narrow, domed hallway. The western end seems less beckoning, with its roaring sounds of turmoil, but a constant flow of fresh and invigorating air originates from it.
14201:
The corpse of the dwarven statue is lying here.
A skeleton of some humanoid lies in the dust.
Calarion the Elf, wielding a broadsword, is standing here (glowing).
Jabez the Elf, wielding an iron-shod mace, is standing here trying to concentrate (glowing).
Nimur the Dwarf, wielding an ornate, steel-shafted warhammer, is standing here (glowing).
Tordol the Dwarf (t), wielding a mighty dwarven axe, is standing here (glowing).
Krecek, wielding an engraved broadsword, is standing here (glowing).

Set with large stone tables and many seats, this hall can harbour a large host of warriors and the like. Dwarven statues with proud and stern faces stand guard at a brightly shining door of silver in the eastern wall. The door emits faint gleams of silvery light that beam throughout the hall, dispelling the darkness where they fall.
14202: A swallow flies high above the ground.

The chamber is filled with empty trays, dust-covered tables and old barrels. A large, but long since burned out, fireplace in the centre of the chamber tells of grand, festive meals being prepared here.
14203: The silvery door shines with a pale light, illuminating the emptiness of this old corridor. A dusty carpet runs through here, following it east into a large room. Two smaller chambers lie just north and south of here.
14204: Wide, comfortable beds have been arranged along the walls. A supple drapery hangs in the doorway, providing a way to seal out unwanted light or any other interference that might disturb a much needed nights rest.
14205: Faint silvery light from the western corridor falls upon a splendid throne made out of dark, slate-blue stone. A thick, red carpet runs up to its very base, still in good condition despite it being many years since Thrain's folk left these halls. Lesser seats made out of the same stone rest on both sides of the throne, and although not as grand as the throne itself any prominent Lord would take pride in having such a seat.
14206:
A Dwarven battering ram stands here.
Tordol the Dwarf (t), wielding a mighty dwarven axe, is standing here (glowing).
Calarion the Elf, wielding a broadsword, is standing here (glowing).
Jabez the Elf, wielding an iron-shod mace, is standing here (glowing).
Krecek, wielding an engraved broadsword, is standing here (glowing).
Nimur the Dwarf, wielding an ornate, steel-shafted warhammer, is standing here (glowing).

You have come across an old weapons and armament storage. Broken hilts and old weapon sheaths lie scattered across the floor. Spider webs cling between empty weapon racks and a thick layer of dust has settled upon the entire chamber.
14207: Steep Hillside Rising to Join the Mountains

Like ripples in the plains, these hills roll out from the main range of the Misty Mountains to the east. Although incomparable to those vast snow-tipped peaks, they are more than substantial themselves. From here there is a good view out over the flatlands below. North the hills continue along the base of the Misties, while south a cave opens in the hillside.
14208: A massive lion is here, baring its glistening fangs.

A pitch-black crack in the hillside serves as an entrance, hollowing out to a wider cavern inside. Many skeletons, the bones gnawed by some ferocious beast, lie scattered all around, some still with flaps of meat hanging on them. A trail of gore leads through the dusty soil, into the darkest reaches of the cave. There a pile of furs and branches have been gathered, forming a giant bed.
14209: A small grasshopper clings to a blade of grass, ready to spring.

The grass grows thick and rich here, nestled at the base of the mountains and flanked in the north by an expanse of hills. The mountainside makes a steep climb and quickly rises into the sky. Vast grasslands stretch onwards to the north and west.
14210: A small grasshopper clings to a blade of grass, ready to spring.

As the towering mountains become more of a noticeable presence in the south, the grasslands finally yield their dominance of the landscape and give way to a forest running along the base of the mountain range. Far to the north and west the rich, green grass still remains the predominant feature of the landscape, to the edge of your vision.
14211: A light forest runs along the southern border of the grasslands, out of place with the monotony of the surrounding plains. The snow-capped heights of the mountains to the south thrust high into the sky, their presence overwhelming the surrounding landscape. Somehow, when this close everything else appears quite insignificant when faced with these grand giants of nature.
14212: A small grasshopper clings to a blade of grass, ready to spring.

As the grasslands draw nearer to the southern forest, the grass grows thicker and darker, and sporadic shrubbery helps the transition from fields into woodland. Past the hilly forest lie the rising mountains, their broken angles and sharp edges making them appear impossible to scale.
14213:
A very large lion with a dark mane watches you lazily.
A powerful lioness is barely visible in the grass.
A small grasshopper clings to a blade of grass, ready to spring.

Like a monotonous green blanket, smothering all shape and variation, the vast grasslands roll out across the eastern landscape. Here and there the grass forms low banks, which look like small ripples on this vast and serene ocean of greenery.
14214: Just west of here a trail barrels its way south across the plains, closely accompanied by the gentle trickle of a small stream. The entire landscape to the east blends into a monotonous green carpet of grass, occasionally varied by the odd bank or slope. The lowlands take an abrupt end in the southeast, where a small forest guards the base of the vast mountain range.
14215: A small grasshopper clings to a blade of grass, ready to spring.

The grass rolls out all around you, endlessly. The monotony of the featureless green landscape would make it hard not to lose your bearings, if not for the massive hulking mountain range east of here. A landmark of that size, so close, is impossible to overlook.
14216: A small grasshopper clings to a blade of grass, ready to spring.

The thick blanket of soft grass stretches across the landscape, bathing the surroundings in a lush green hue. Far across the southern expanse of the grasslands great mountains stand tall and proud, breaking the monotony of the grassy lowlands.
14217:
A lion cub is here hunting grasshoppers.
A small grasshopper clings to a blade of grass, ready to spring.

The lush green grasslands roll out towards the western horizon, flanked by a wide range of hills to the east. The sharp and slumped hillside looks fairly impossible to scale, the side of the bluff being sheer if not particularly high.
14218: An expanse of hills stretch out from the mountains across the grasslands. The steep inclines and rocky hillsides make this terrain cumbersome to travel in, and not at all appeasing to the eye with its cold and craggy landscape. West the cliff is too steep to descend.
14219: A beautiful and docile horse is standing here.

A crude chamber has been recklessly wrought out of the mountain. The broken texture of the walls shows lack of craftsmanship, but tells of great force being used in the construction. A tunnel cuts south through the mountain like a fresh wound and a huge hole punctures the westernmost wall.
14220:
The corpse of a trained horse is lying here.
A bloodthirsty orc, wielding a scimitar, is here, fighting Mandara (m).
A bloodthirsty orc, wielding a scimitar, is here, fighting Mandara (m).
Mandara the Elf (m) is here, fighting a bloodthirsty orc.
A sturdy trained horse is standing here.

The core of the mountain has been ripped apart to provide passage through it. Claw-like markings mar the walls of the tunnel like lacerations, and blood in the form of subsoil water gently trickles out of them. The smell of smoke drifts in from the south, mixed with some other rank odour.
14221:
The corpse of a bloodthirsty orc is lying here.
A large stone fireplace with a roaring fire warms the room.

A broad smoke-filled cavern harbours a large fireplace and acts as dining- hall of sorts. A slanting passage offers access to a small chamber just over- head, albeit it would take a good bit of scrambling to make it up there. The southern part of the cavern narrows considerably and forms into a small opening whereas both the northern and western parts form into tunnels.
14222:
The corpse of a snaga orc is lying here.
The corpse of a snaga orc is lying here.

A small dugout lies nestled deep inside the mountain, secluded from the rest of mountain dwelling by its draped doorway. Large animal hides have been strewn across the cold floor to serve as mattresses. Daunting remains of fallen prey lie stacked in piles along the walls of the chamber, perhaps kept as trophies or just proof of lack of tidiness.
14223:
The corpse of a bloodthirsty orc is lying here.
A bloodthirsty orc, wielding a scimitar, is here, fighting Mandara (m).
A sturdy trained horse is standing here.
Mandara the Elf (m), wielding the black sword, is here, fighting a bloodthirsty orc.

A seemingly unfinished tunnel grinds its way west into the mountain until finally coming to a halt. The walls are serrated by bulging protrusions and sharp broken angles. The westernmost part of the tunnel is cluttered with rocks and other debris from the ongoing construction work. The crude state of the tunnel raises the question of whether it's actually intentionally wrought or just the result of unbridled rage.
14224:
A piece of meat has been left here.
A tough strip of dried meat lies here.
A tough strip of dried meat lies here.
A tough strip of dried meat lies here.
A cooked and smoked piece of meat lies here.
A tough strip of dried meat lies here.
A piece of meat has been left here.
A cooked and smoked piece of meat lies here.
A tough strip of dried meat lies here.
A tough strip of dried meat lies here.
A fierce bat is here, lusting for your blood.
A fierce bat is here, lusting for your blood.
A bloodthirsty bat is sleeping here.
A bloodthirsty bat is sleeping here.
A bloodthirsty bat is sleeping here.

Smoke filters in from below making the air hazy and hard to breathe in this chamber which appears to serve as a food storage. A strong scent of cooked meat blends with the smothering smoke but doesn't help to make the air any less suffocating. A slanting passage leads down into a broad cavern which is lit by the flames of a large fire.
14225: Grassy Fields Nestled at the Mountainbase

The mountainside draws up into the sky near vertically, surpassing by far the skill of even the bravest climbers. Soft, grassy fields run along the base of the mountainside, and the grass takes on a greyish hue from the soil below, almost as if blending in with the mountain itself.
14226: Grassy Fields below the Vast Mountain Range

Green fields cower at the base of the overwhelming mountains, basked in a faint grey shadow. Further south, moving away from the mountains, the fields grow to be exceptionally lush, the wildlife flourishing to a point where the landscape seems absolutely riddled with small animals.
14227: A bulky overhang blots out the sky above, casting a thick, grey shadow onto the ground below. Every now and then small pebbles tumble down from above, as if the mountainside above was being stirred by something. The protrusion of the overhang is so great that one would question the stability of the rock, and indeed one could speculate about one's personal safety standing under it.
14228: A vast array of rocks of all different sizes and shapes impale the ground, making it craggy and cumbersome to travel upon. Rich grasslands riddled with waist-high grass roll out across the southern plateau, as far as the eye can tell. Northwards the gloomy mountains reach high into the sky above your head, impossible to climb and vast to behold.
14229:
A rock lizard is here, motionless as it observes you.
A sturdy trained horse is standing here.

Large chunks of rock impale the ground, as if they had been thrust down by a great force. The sharp boulders prove quite a hindrance for travellers trying to cross this field, slowing the pace of safe travel considerably. To the north the cliff side is impassable, towering immeasurably above you. West the ground breaks off sharply, the drop too steep to descend.
14230: The face of the mountain is almost unnaturally smooth as if it indeed had been wrought into such a shape, but who is to say what shapes nature decides to take? Thrust high into the sky a lone ledge protrudes slightly from the mountainside, making it a long drop for anyone unfortunate enough to stray over its edge. A plateau rising to the east is more rugged and uneven-looking than the mountain to the north; perhaps this land settled downwards at some time in the past.
14231: A large brown snake with black patches is coiled here.

A huge boulder cleaves the ground here, lying almost lopsidedly as it balances on its edge. Nevertheless it seems firmly implanted into the rocky soil, as if fallen from a great height. A steep hillside rises north and west of you, while east all is passage is blocked by a small spur of solid rock. Southwards the landscape changes shape into a rocky heath with a sharp and harsh texture.
14232: Rocky Plains at the Base of the Mountain

The ground is serrated by sharp-edged rocks and large, bulky boulders. The mountainside slowly makes its way up into the sky to the east, but although not that steep, its harsh and broken surface makes it virtually impossible to scale. The ground falls off sharply to the south creating a valley, near hidden within the undulating and rocky expanse of plains. To your north there lies an old guard-post, its barricades broken and seemingly abandoned.
14233: A pack horse (Rood) is standing here, ridden by you.

The trail traverses across the wide plains, a small hunting trail that is not much used. The ground falls away sharply to the east, creating a sheltered valley in the otherwise open plains, and south into a narrow crevice. As the trail continues south-west it widens continuously, and almost seems to gain pace as it swiftly cuts a passage through the lands.
14234: Flanked by brushy grasslands to the west and rocky, undulating plains in the east, the trail accesses a crossing of trails which lies north, but also cuts a passage south across the wide lands. East of here lies a towering spur of the Misties, a solemn and massive impression on the eastern skyline.
14235: A small brown snake is slithering around here.

The thick grass struggles to ward off the growth of brushwood, which seems to originate from the south. A bleak trail makes its presence duly noticed in the north, but it doesn't seem quite as comfortable as the much wider trail running along the eastern border of the grassland.
14236: Long patches of brush reach northwards towards a faint trail, but falter and fade away into the soft grass. Further to the east the brush remains sparse, succumbing there to the denser waving undergrowth. Southwards it gains strength and grows ominously dense.
14237: Thick brushwood blots out the ground entirely, save a few bald spots where the brown-stained grass manages to break through. In the south a dense thicket stands tall, a rare sight in these lowlands, but it does not look as healthy as the surrounding landscape. The grim bulk of the tall trees quench all light, making it a dark and dreary place. A trail runs swiftly across the plains in the east, a welcome sight amidst the harsh brushwood.
14238: A pack horse (Rood) is standing here, ridden by you.

Patches of brush stretch out towards the western border of the trail, like long arms trying to snatch unwary travellers and drag them into the thick brushwood in the west. The southern route of the trail runs unhindered across the smooth plains, making very few turns. Northwards the trail bends slightly as it struggles to avoid the outstretched patches of brush.
14239: In the Shadow of Some Trees

A forest spider is here crawling around.
A forest spider is here crawling around.

Large, bulky trees cast their shadows upon you, surrounding you with darkness. The air in this murky thicket grows suffocatingly thick, weighing upon you like a heavy burden on your travels. Sudden gusts of fresh air send mournful shivers through the dark tree-tops, filling the thicket with a welcome breeze.
14240: Trail Stretching across the Wide Plains

A dense thicket of trees lies nestled on the western border of the trail, a rarity indeed in these almost shapeless grasslands. The trail swiftly travels south, bending slightly as it passes some undulations in the grasslands, barely missing a deep crevice in ground just east of here. The northern route from here slowly but steadily runs across the lowlands, heading towards the end of a vast mountain spur.
14241: A big cavebear is padding around here.

A narrow crevice runs for some way into the valley's side, only to narrow and end abruptly. The steep sides of the crevice rise up above your head, almost touching in parts and ensuring no sunlight can reach to the base. Echoes of subsoil water dripping down from the broken angles of the crevice walls break the ominous silence.
14242: The wide stretch of grassy land in the valley gives way here, succumbing to its craggy surroundings. A low range of hills lies south, past a small cluster of rocky fields, creating a natural rift valley reaching out further north and south. To the west a dark crevice lies below the rising plains and outstretched fields.
14243: A rock lizard is here, motionless as it observes you.

The soft peat here draws to an end to the west, opening into a rocky valley floor. East of here, atop the higher plains, the grasslands have grown wild and unkempt, with thick waist-high grass and flourishing wildlife. The northern mountain range rests majestically at the end of the grasslands, surveying the lands solemnly.
14244: A stretch of waist-high grass runs like a border between the rocky plains to the north and the grasslands. Beyond the grass, at the edge of your vision, a gentle heath traverses across the landscape, edging along below a low range of hills. To your west the ground falls off rapidly, forming a natural valley, and to the north, silent and ominous mountains break the skyline with their high, snow-clad peaks.
14245: Waist-high, rich grass softly sways in gentle gusts of wind here. The serene setting is occasionally disturbed as animals scurry about and stir up rattling noises within the thick grass beds. A vast mountain range lies not far to the north, its gargantuan presence dominating the landscape.
14246: Small well-trodden trails, barely noticeable in the rich grass, run south over the tiny rocky spur there, and east through some meadows. The richness of the wildlife and the many trails lead to the conclusion that these fields serve as hunting grounds. The northern horizon is completely dominated by great peaks of the mountain-range, itself only a spur from the main body of the vastness that is the Misty Mountains.
14247: The wildlife thrives and flourishes amidst the rich fields, sheltered slightly from the great plateau winds by the Misty Mountains to the east. North of here the ground is less fertile, becoming increasingly rocky as it draws closer to a spur of those mountains. Gentle meadows run playfully across the southern landscape, filling the air with a faint heathery scent.
14248: A slumped landscape, marred by broken rocks and covered with tufts of thick grass, lies at the border of gentle meadows and fields. The ominous presence of the great mountains to the north and east becomes more and more overwhelming as the landscape draws closer to them, their vast peaks rising above the clouds in places. A small spur runs along the south edge of this field, small compared to the mountains but still preventing travel in that direction.
14249: The gentle fields playfully spread across to the south and west, vast open spaces you can see for miles. The craggy peaks of the Misty Mountains and the tiny spur of them to the north set a cold and harsh contrast to the heathery meadows, over which the mountains tower imperiously.
14250: The heathery meadows draw further east, flanked by fields on their northern side. The peat continues to the west, like a vast belt across the landscape. A grand spur of mountains to the north, thrusting out from the main range, ends the expanse of fields in that direction, although doubtless they continue on the other side.
14251: An arrow lies on the ground.

An ingenuously camouflaged windbreak, covered with turf and grass, offers shelter and comfort for the weary. A peculiar fireplace wrought in front of the windbreak draws attention. Stones have been stacked in intricate ways to channel its smoke, thus avoiding a large column rising up and attracting unwanted attention.
14252: An arrow lies on the ground.

A long stretch of fields blaze a passage through the surrounding high grass and peat. As it draws further east the terrain turns into a blend of heathery meadows and grassy fields, which runs all the way to the base of the towering mountain range in the east.
14253:
An arrow lies on the ground.
An arrow lies on the ground.
An arrow lies on the ground.
An arrow lies on the ground.

Banks of grass gently swoop down from the hills to the south, like rolling waves. Further to the north the grass grows thick and high, perfect for the hunting of prey. A long belt of heath rolls in from the north and trails away to the south-east, only ended by the cliff-side of a hilly spur.
14254: A low range of hills bulges out from the grasslands in the south, where the stretching peat turns slightly northwards into. West and north the land falls down sharply into a valley, while east it rises further. The route up there is slightly slippery, with many loose stones ready to trip the climber.
14255: Rocky plains stretch out towards the west, where the craggy soil becomes soft and wholesome. A low range of hills rise and fall to create a small valley to the north, offering seclusion from the open lowlands. Soft peat stretches like a long tail across the valley mouth here, a strange and extremely noticeable exception in the landscape.
14256: The plains incline slightly as they rise to meet a low range of hills in the south. The ground becomes craggy and barren in the east as it falls into a valley, while further east the terrain becomes boggy and sloped. Far beyond all that is a vast mountain range, dominating the horizon. A swift trail gently runs over slopes and banks west of here, while north the land falls into a sudden crevice.
14257: A pack horse (Rood) is standing here, ridden by you.

The trail disappears around the corner of a murky forest southwest of here, but runs steadily onwards north without any hindrance, towards the end of a grand range of mountains. Those are but a spur of the Misty Mountains, but still they tower into the skyline, a stark contrast to the surrounding lowlands and grassy fields.
14258: A pack horse (Rood) is standing here, ridden by you.

A murky thicket, drenched in darkness, stands like a persistent obstacle in the north. The trail is forced to bend eastwards to avoid the bulk of the trees as it travels north. Southwards the trail runs freely across the plains, offering safe passage through the lands.
14259: Climbing further into the mountains seems undoable as they rise up into the sky. The ledge you have reached offers little protection from the tormenting winds that lash out at you as you cling to the rock, and as you grope around for a better grip you notice a wide shaft in the face of the mountain.
14260: The trees nestle among rocks and crevices at the base of the mountains. Swiftly the Misties rise into the sky, making it a seemingly impossible climb, although a relatively smooth part of rock lies just to the south. An experienced climber might be able to gain some footing there, but the chances of reaching the peaks look meagre.
14261: Wide and unkempt grasslands roll out before you, reaching far to the north and east. Great mountains rise into the southern skyline, and a thick forest runs along their base. To the west a trail cuts across the plains, like a borderline between the rich grasslands and wide-stretched wilderness.
14262: A clear spring babbles as cool water trickles out of the ground.

Clear water springs out from the mountainside and softly trickles down into a clearing in the forest. The steep rise of the mountainside makes travel south or east impossible. The forestline continues west but halts at the border of the wide grasslands.
14263: The treeline grows thin as it travels north to meet the grasslands but thickens in the opposite direction. The rocky forest floor is slightly inclined, and doesn't provide easy footing for travellers taking a southbound turn. A small clearing lies east, and a soft, trickling sound beckons you thither.
14264: A large shrub grows here, its branches loosely spreading.

A light forest borders the rolling grasslands but as it draws closer to the mountains in the south it thickens, outlining the base of the thrusting spur. The range of peaks mountains rise high into the skyline, creating an impassable hindrance to travel in that direction.
14265: Forest at the Base of the Mountains
A giant form rustles among the trees.

The forestline runs up to the very base of the mountains, and some trees even sprout out in odd angles from the rockface itself. Far north, through the bulk of the trees, vast grasslands roll out across the horizon. The forestline continues both east and west, grabbing all available land between the rocks.
14266: A small animal, all covered in spines, snuffles amongst the undergrowth.

The forestline runs up to the very base of the mountains, and some trees even sprout out in odd angles from the rockface itself. Far north, through the bulk of the trees, vast grasslands roll out across the horizon. The forestline continues both east and west.
14267: As the trail travels south it seems to grow ever wider, winding its way south to approach the remnants of a long since forgotten road. Here and there gravel has been strewn across the trail, but it does not in any way hinder travel, nor does it affect the difficulty of movement.
14268: The field is riddled with loose gravel, which shifts as it is trodden upon, making the footing unsteady and tiresome. A widening trail lies nearby to the west, where it offers comfortable passage north or south across the lands. A low range of hills rises at the eastern border of the field and stretches further east across the heath.
14269: A low range of slumped hills bulge out from the soft plains. To the northeast the hills drop and form a small valley which lies sheltered by its flanking hillsides. Gazing out from the raised hills you see a swift trail traversing across the north-western plains.
14270: Small Camp Sheltered by the Hills

The surrounding hills make this campsite ideal, sheltering travellers not only from harsh winds but also providing cover from onlooking eyes, properties which are hard to find amidst the wide open plains. The resources of the campsite itself are meagre - all that remain are a burnt out fire and a few aged logs suitable for resting on.
14271: A low range of hills rise from the surrounding heath and boggy grounds, but swiftly fall into a small depression to the west. On the far side the hills continue. Far away to the east a vast mountain range makes its presence well noted, a giant presence on the horizon. To the north runs a stretch of flat plains, surrounded to the west and north by steep drops, and on the east by a high slope.
14272: The hillside, with its moss-covered protrusions and soft coating of grass and bog, becomes increasingly steep to the west. To the north it slants downwards along a grassy plateau before the Misty Mountains. The bog diminishes along the sides of the hill, until it disappears in the grasslands below.
14273: Soft peat rolls out like a warm blanket, or a coating, over the eastern lands. The western ground swiftly rises into a boggy hillside, whereas the northern lands are flat as can be, with wholesome, green grass. East and north is a rich plateau in the arms of two gigantic spurs from the Misty Mountains.
14274: Like a belt, the peat stretches east and west but in the north it gives way to grassy fields full of wildlife. A tower stands like a lone sentry to the south-east, on the end of a hilly spur thrust from the main range, while just south of here a valley falls away. Along the horizon the vast mountains curve around, dominating all the landscape to the north and east.
14275: The constant scent of heather is here, across the soft peat. Alluring meadows lie to the north-east, and when the wind comes from that direction the scent of heather becomes even more noticeable. A grim tower high above you breaks the southern skyline, silently surveying the lands from its hilly outcrop.
14276:
A large, loyal falcon is circling above.
A fallow deer is grazing peacefully here.

A range of hills rise into the southern sky, and the meadow halts promptly, giving way to a rocky slope. Soft peat rolls out like a smothering blanket west of here, but in the north the meadows thrive and flourish. Like a faint, grey shadow on the horizon, a tower can be seen to the south-west.
14277: The towering mountain range to the east throws out an arm here, making a low and rugged spur of hills. It is covered in waist-high grass, a few small shrubs and, here and there, stands of trees. To the west there is a ruined watchtower, overlooking the lands below. North, there are some broken plains, and foothills below the snow-capped peaks of the Misty Mountains. South the land below this ridge of hills is mainly rolling plains and, to the south-west wetlands. There is some building far off to the south of here, a farm judging by the fields all around it.
14278: The terrain continues to slowly rise here toward the Misty Mountains in the northeast. There is a good view over the fields and plains-land bordering the mountains, thus the tower to the north. It is now partially ruined and covered in moss, but would probably offer some protection to those defending it.
14279: A brown bear is sleeping here.

This lush valley is as isolated as they come, with the only entrance being through a narrow ravine to the south. A sheer crescent-shaped cliff bars all other directions. The valley is teeming with wildlife, the undergrowth about waist-height. In a few places there is soft, short grass with patches of wild flowers, gentle pastels with bright purple and blues thrown in for a colourful combination. Scattered about the valley a few trees have taken root, mostly oak but with a few maples and some apple trees.
14280: A High Plain Bordering a Cliff

This is a vast plain of waist high wild wheat, tips swaying in unison with the gentle breeze. In the near distance the wheat give off a heather-grey hue, while further away the fields appear almost black. On the eastern edge of this field there are some trees bordering a crescent-shaped cliff, below which is a secluded valley. On the far side of this gap, a ridge of hills rise, with an old tower visible atop their edge.
14281: The hills have smoothed out to this level expanse of land, covered in a light waist-high field of wild wheat mixed with some tall grass. Besides the grass the land is mostly without growth, except for a few oak trees. Looking about from the edges of this plain, the grasslands continue on to the south, but north give away to broken rocky lands.
14282: Clustered together like a bunch of grapes, these small foothills rise higher above the plains than the rolling plains you can discern to the west. Upon the slopes the grass becomes short and sparse, as the roots have a difficult time taking hold in the soft earth. On the steepest parts there is no vegetation, just dry brown earth. North the hills grow above the plains, like an arm from the Misty Mountains.
14283: The earth flows over some mild downs. These gentle mounds, tiny foothills to the rougher land to the north, are teeming with wild grass about the height of a man's knee. To the east there is a faint outline of more hills leading into the main range of mountains. South, the hills mellow out into a vast prairie, a windswept and open land.
14284: The land, which is virtually flat here, rises upwards to the north into a range of exposed hills. Almost like a line extending from the Misty Mountains, the land is split between the ragged and broken plateau to the north, and the flat lands stretching down to the Gap of Rohan.
14285: Here there are small clumps of grass, interspersed with beds of gravel to the south and west. The gravel comes from years of erosion on the unmaintained road there. To the east the grass becomes thick underfoot, with a few solitary trees breaking up the monotonous skyline. In the distance rise the ends of two great mountain ranges: to the northeast the Misty Mountains, and to the southeast the White Mountains.
14286: A pack horse (Rood) is standing here, ridden by you.

The cracked paving stones are few and far between here, barely recognisable as the remains of a once great road. The stones, which it seems were once smoothly cut and joined together, are now uneven and broken into bits of gravel. There are some jagged little edges sticking up from the dirt of the remaining larger stones, making the route a slow one. East the end of the Misty Mountains can be seen rising on the horizon, their snowy peaks overlooking the Gap of Rohan.
14287: A Few Stones Resembling a Road
A pack horse (Rood) is standing here, ridden by you.

The large meadows come to an abrupt halt here as a barely noticeable trail of stone debris makes its way through them. Though in very poor shape, there are still hints that a larger road formerly passed through here. What remains now is almost completely overgrown by grass and vegetation.
14288: A pack horse (Rood) is standing here, ridden by you.

Almost completely hidden by the grass is an ancient road. It is being taken back by nature gradually, although a few large paving stones remain. They are covered in a light moss, due to the non-use of this route. Between some of them coarse grass and unruly weeds have grown, breaking the slabs into loose pieces of gravel.
14289: The ground here is covered in short green grass, interspersed with patches of white daisies. There are a few trees here and there - mostly oak, with a few birch. These grasslands continue all around, interrupted to the south and west by the remnants of an ancient road.
14290: Here the land is mostly flat, and is covered in soft, bright green grass. There are patches of colourful wildflowers, breaking up the monotony of the land for a short while. Around these flowers are fresh mounds of dirt, pushed up by some busy animal digging. North the flat plains flow into some rolling grasslands, while elsewhere the flat plains continue.
14291: Yellow flowers, with grey-green foliage, grow in clusters here.

The waist-high grass is beginning to merge into fields of wild wheat here, the natural crops becoming more prevalent the further east you look. There are some periodic piles of rubble, the remains of abandoned Dunlending homesteads. They built their farms far from the great Numenorean road, avoiding the travellers that used that route.
14292: The lush grass merges into fields of wild wheat on this long, gradual, slope, some of it dry and brittle from the poor soil. It seems the cutting winds have stripped the earth of its topsoil, leaving bare a mostly rocky ground. East the grass grows strongly again, before falling away into a valley.
14293: This faint slope is covered with wild wheat and patches of wild flowers. In some spots the slope is barren, and the earth is visible. There are several mounds of fresh dirt and some other holes dug into the hillside by the animal life that inhabits this region. Natural rock formations block the way not far east of here, rising above the surrounding plains. South, the ground levels out into a vast prairie of wild wheat.
14294: This rocky valley floor twists and turns in various different directions and is extremely narrow, which makes travel through here tedious. Green moss grows on the cliff walls, which rear up to the east. The southern side of the ravine is not steep, eventually disappearing into the grassy fields. The ground is mostly bare rock, with short grass in patches. The ravine continues on to the north, with the walls increasing into sheer unclimbable cliffs.
14295: A Narrow Trail up a Ridge

The trail starts to slowly zigzag its way up the ridge to the decayed watch tower visible above. The track sometimes wanders around gigantic rock outcrops, sticking out from the hillside like knife edges. The ledge here is at times so narrow that it would be almost impossible for a wagon to make its way up. Yet it has been done at some time, since wagon ruts are still evident in the soil.
14296: Footholds and handholds are plentiful here, most of which are unstable. There are several small ledges to rest upon, luckily so as climbing this slope is tedious and exhausting. The view of the land below is astounding; however soaking up the view, and resting here for long might prove fatal. Loose stones abound, and if one of them dislodged from above you could be flattened.
14297: An arrow lies on the ground.

The ground is covered in rocks of varying shapes and sizes, dislodged from the cliff above. It appears to be unstable up there, with several large boulders that could tumble down at any moment. Here and there are large impressions in the earth, sobering reminders of the danger. The cliff itself looks climbable, but there is a much safer passage to the west. East the Misty Mountains are visible not too far away, an immense presence dominating the landscape.
14298: The ground is littered with rocks here. A track from the west meanders around various detours, making its way onto a trail that goes up the steep ridge to the north. There are places where the track used to be, but large boulders now cover. Where the ground is not covered with rocks there is short, sparse grass and in places craters of varying sizes. Above, a long distance to the north there is a tower of some sort visible on the end of the spur of hills. South of here the ground slopes downward to the outskirts of some farm.
14299: The prairies to the west give way to gravel and large rocks here, with only tufts of greenery here and there. To the north the land drops away slightly, forming a valley and then a ravine. South a line in the ground continues on, the remains of a dried-up riverbed. Also meandering through here is an old forgotten track that seems to be headed to the tower visible on a hilltop to the northeast.
14300: An old trail is faintly visible here, with wagon ruts in parts. Near this track is huge swathes of wild wheat, dry and brittle. South of here there are many stray bushes taking root in amongst the brambles and vines, making it a near impenetrable tangle. There are several small tunnels into the thorny mess, but only for small creatures. North, the terrain breaks into a gentle slope leading up to a high plain. East and west the prairieland continues.
14301: This prairie continues in every direction, except to the north where it rises on a gentle slope. The area is abundant with wildlife, with patches of bright wild flowers and a few trees scattered about. To the south-west a road is just visible cutting through wetlands on a raised causeway.
14302: A brown furry gopher is here, ready to dive back underground.

This continuos flat land is teeming with grass and small wildlife. Most of the animals can be seen and not heard, rustling about the undergrowth. The grass grows abundantly, about waist high in most places, hiding the creatures from view. This vast expanse of land continues as far as the eye can see, the huge expanse of the Misty Mountains in full view on the horizon.
14303: The lush, abundant plains are constant all around here, varying from bushes and undergrowth nearer the road to open grasslands further away. Just before the old road to the south, the land falls into a natural depression, filled with thick brush. Beyond it is a raised causeway, the road originally built above the lands to protect it from flooding.
14304: The land here is bordered by an old road, which cuts across the grasslands. The ground is covered with lush but short grass, beaten down by the powerful winds that can sweep across the land. To the north, the ground steadily rises towards a series of small rolling hills. The flat plains continue all around from here, becoming more vibrant to the east.
14305: A pack horse (Rood) is standing here, ridden by you.

Crumbled away over the ages since the route was last maintained, the road is now nothing more than loose gravel and countless cracked paving stones. The line it follows is unmistakable though: from south-east to north-west it goes, across the plains of Enedwaith.
14306: The gentle, rolling plains have levelled out into this meadow of very thick, soft grass. Herds of heavy beasts must graze here at some time in the year, judging by the swathes of trampled grass. To the east are the last remnants of a road, which originally travelled north-west to south-east. Further still is the outline of a mountain range, dominating the horizon.
14307: The land steadily rises here to the south. The grass is short, soft and lush, a natural place for the animal herds that have trampled it. To the east are the remains of a road, originally wide and proud but now reduced to rubble. It runs north to south there, built slightly above the surrounding fields.
14308:
An arrow lies on the ground.
An arrow lies on the ground.
A large wild horse is here, protecting his herd.
A pack horse (Rood) is standing here, ridden by you.

The road here has been almost completely overgrown with grass, soon to be forgotten and lost in history. It was once maintained by the armies of Gondor and Arnor, but no mason has mended it for many centuries now. Southeast it rises up onto an earthen causeway, carrying it above the soggy wetlands, and continues on towards Rohan.
14309: A pack horse (Rood) is standing here, ridden by you.

A wide flat area opens up to the south, covered in soft grasslands. The road to the south-east begins to gradually rise up onto a causeway, making its way through the wetlands. This old route used to travel for hundreds of miles over these lands, but it is now almost completely forgotten. To the east there is a natural depression in the meadowland, the steep slope blocking movement in that direction.
14310: A Deep Hollow in the Plains
A brown furry gopher is here, ready to dive back underground.

This depression is swift and sudden, almost invisible from most sides because of the tall grass. The base of the hollow is covered with thick brush in parts, extremely troublesome to move through. Goldenrod and other wild flowers grow on the steeper sides, most likely where the sun hits during the day. To the west and south, a road runs on a raised causeway well above you. The slope is steep and full of loose gravel, making it impossible to climb.
14311: The prairie slopes faintly downward to the south, a faint decline only visible from a distance. There the land becomes wetter, with the poor natural drainage making for a permanent semi-wetlands. Many wildflowers grow here on the grassy slope, the land being fertile and well watered. West the plains dip away into a natural bowl in the plains, while east the plains continue until they meet the southern end of the Misty Mountains.
14312:
A brown furry gopher is here, ready to dive back underground.
A horse of the Rohirrim is standing here, ridden by you.

A few stray arms of the blackberry bushes are invading these grasslands. The vines grow very densely, creating a tangled web of thorns near impossible to cut your way through. An easier route would be to walk around them to the south. Here the signs of birds and other animal life are heard and often seen, these lands being a fertile home for them. There is a faint trail here, headed south. It appears to be made by wildlife, judging by the hoof prints.
14313:
There is a huge, pyramidal beehive here.
A bee flies around here, collecting nectar from the flowers.
A bee flies around here, collecting nectar from the flowers.

This clearing is surrounded by thick impenetrable brambles and brush on all sides but south, where a path cuts its way through. A single cherry tree stands in the centre of the clearing, a solitary place giving a good view over the nearby brush. The ground is covered in grass, cherry pits, and various animal tracks.
14314:
Some plump juicy grapes are growing here.
Some plump juicy grapes are growing here.
A black-haired farmhand is here.

Lush vines with ripe grapes are plentiful here. The rolls of vines are well groomed and taken care of. The ground below is covered in a light brown dirt, and there is not a weed to be seen. There are several breaks in the rolls of vines, but not in the same place on each roll. Thus a bit of a maze is created to travel through, but never enough to get lost in. The ground flows gently downward in steps, lower to the south. West beyond the vines is a huge expanse of brush and brambles, with razor sharp thorns that block the way.
14315: The wheat is having trouble taking root in this bare rocky ground, which is littered with small grey stones. There are a few large boulders to the north, where they must have rolled down from the hillside. There is a dark tower on top of the hill, looking out from its western end. To the east the outline of a building can be seen, while west there is a stone wall enclosing a vineyard.
14316: A lonely, forgotten house stands in this field of overgrown wheat. Only the rock walls and a rotten door remains. Since the wheat crop had trouble taking root, the farm was abandoned for the better fields in the south. The soil here is just a fine layer of dirt, with a lot of little grey rocks - not the ideal planting conditions for any crop.
14317: An apple tree with bright green leaves grows here.

These trees are planted in such an orderly manner. Each row is perfectly straight. The ground is covered in a rich, dark dirt with a few grey rocks interspersed. Since the trees are planted in such wide, even rows, this grove doesn't offer much cover from the elements. Bordering this grove to the south and west are some farmlands, while only monotonous fields of wild wheat are to the east.
14318: Apparently these fields were abandoned for some reason. The grain is not at all healthy, or as well-tended as those in nearby fields. It may be that there is too much wheat growing, and the farmer decided it wasn't worth the effort to grow more. There are more abandoned fields in the north, and beyond them on the distant horizon a hilly range sticks out west from the Misty Mountains.
14319: Some of the fields here have stalks of corn that are at least seven feet high, waving with a life of their own in the wind. There are other fields where the corn is on a different rotation, and the ears are far from harvestable. The stalks of corn do not grow in even rolls, and are so tightly planted together that manoeuvring around them is somewhat impeded. The corn closer to harvest seems to be in the northern fields, and they block the view of what lies beyond them. Bordering these fields on the west is a thorny mess of brambles and brush that don't offer any path or route through.
14320: Twisting Path through the Blackberry Bushes

A large thorny branched shrub is growing here.
The bee flies around here, collecting nectar from the flowers.
The bee flies around here, collecting nectar from the flowers.

The tunnel between the bushes twists and turns wildly here, but always seeming to return to the same direction. There are several different natural tunnels that lead off into the brush, but none run for any great distance. This path appears to hold true to course though, leading somewhere through this maze.
14321: A black and white skunk is scuttling about here, searching for food.

Directly to the east is a mess of twisted blackberry bushes, their razor-like thorns sharp enough to cut on contact. Some brave animal has tunnelled its way through the brambles to some unknown place deep inside. Intertwined inside the vicious thorns are various low trees, which seem to have had their life almost completely choked out of them. Southwards the lands are covered in stagnant water in parts, with a raised causeway running through them just visible on the horizon.
14322: Just below the surface of the grass is about a half-inch of water. The earth, already saturated, is too soaked to take in this last bit of water from the recent rains. Always the water drains too slowly, the plains too flat and the soil not absorbent enough to lose its watery cover. An ancient road borders these wetlands to the south, built on a raised platform with small dikes under it to drain the water. The Numenoreans built the causeway straight through the wetlands, their engineering skill avoiding a large detour around the water.
14323: The road continues along on a built-up causeway, well above the wetlands to the south. There is a deep depression to the north, with some thick, tangled brush congesting its base. Part of the old road has fallen away into it, leaving the route barely passable. The surviving whole slabs on this road are few - most broken into gravel by the weather long ago. Westwards the causeway gradually disappears as the wetlands recede, the road inclining down to the plains.
14324: To avoid flooding from the wet grasslands, this ancient trail continues along its path on a causeway to the east of here. The rise is gradual, the line of the road as straight as it was centuries ago. Still, the surface has suffered from the lack of maintenance, becoming little more than a muddy track filled with rough stone fragments. Here and there the road disappears from sight as it dips into the undergrowth. Around the road the land is mainly flat grassy fields, although a wide depression dips down to the north-east.
14325: A Gentle Slope near a Road
A horse of the Rohirrim is standing here, ridden by you.

The meadow here slopes upwards towards the old road to the east. The ground is covered in thick grass mainly, with a few spots of wildflowers growing nearer the road. A route to the south leads over a hillside, while further south a small stand of trees is discernible on the horizon.
14326: A Slight Rise in the Meadow

This slight rise gives a good view of the ruined road, which it overlooks to the north-east. Surrounding here is a rich meadowland, verdant and flourishing with thick, waving grass. To the southeast there is a stand of trees, barely visible in the distance, bordering the wetlands. To the south is a steep and slippery bank that looks unsafe to traverse.
14327: A Steep Bluff in the Plains

This bluff is extremely difficult to traverse because of the countless small screes. Going around it might be a better alternative than trying to climb, and probably fall, down it. South looks the safest route down, with north and east being more of a cliff than anything else.
14328: The path here leads around the steep eastern slope of a bluff. The grass is trampled quite heavily, and in parts there is nothing but dirt. By examination of the tracks, it seems to be a trail made by a wild herd of animals. East and south the hillside gradually flattens down onto the plains, which is mostly lush green meadows stretching for miles. South, a long dotted line of trees stretches for miles.
14329: Bordering the remains of an ancient road, these fields are lush if somewhat uniform. There are some small bushes and clusters of blackberry bushes, but mostly the waving grass grows to the exclusion of all other undergrowth. The land rises to the west up a gradual slope, the side of a steep bluff visible in the distance.
14330: The platform that this road sits on is rapidly eroding along its edges, leaving it slippery and dangerous. Where half-upended flagstones do not threaten to tip you over, the overgrown weeds may trip you up. The causeway itself has started to seriously decay, and it will not be long before this part of the Great South Road is only a memory as well. The lands surrounding it are open grasslands to the north, with semi-swampland to the south.
14331: This is the highest place in the nearby lands, and visibility is good in every direction. The ruined road runs on a bed of stone and earth for miles through the wetlands, several yards above the water. Its age shows clearly, with large parts having fallen away. Far to the north-east the Misty Mountains can be seen rising in the sky with snow capped peaks, their stony might utterly dominating the horizon.
14332: The blades of grass are slick with water here, the soil below almost completely saturated. Poor natural drainage results in it pooling after the rains, making almost a marsh in the grasslands. South and west of here runs an ancient road atop a causeway, built to be safe from the frequent flooding. Its earthen sides are covered in loose stones, and would be easy to slip on.
14333:
Yellow flowers, with grey-green foliage, grow in clusters here.
Yellow flowers, with grey-green foliage, grow in clusters here.

The ground is covered in thick, short green grass. There are some bright spots of yellow scattered among the grass which, upon closer examination, are tiny buttercups. The calls of birds and the snuffling of animals can be heard to the north, where some dense brambles block the way. A small, but well travelled path is directly south of here, and some fields of grain directly east.
14334: These well-cultivated fields are in various rotations of growth, some closer to harvest than others. Each field is about an acre in size and they rotate between amber fields of wheat and the dark green plants of rye. Soon those closest to harvest will make their way to the nearby Dunlending town. A farm house is visible to the south-east, where several well-rutted paths lead.
14335:
A pitchfork has been carelessly left lying here.
A gardening tool that looks like a sickle lies here.

This field is covered in black dirt - it appears to have been burnt. Not even a bright green leaf of any weed has sprouted here yet. Even though the dirt is black, it is noticeable that the ground has been freshly ploughed. East and west of here the fields have some crops in full growth. North-east there are some trees, planted in even lines. The back wall of the farm house is south of here, with several pieces of farm equipment near it.
14336:
A carrot is lying here.
A large potato is growing here.
Some delicious wild strawberries grow on the ground.
A carrot is lying here.
A large potato is growing here.
Some delicious wild strawberries grow on the ground.
A carrot is lying here.
A large potato is growing here.
A black-haired farmhand is here.

Rows of various crops are planted here, which are well tended. The land between the crops is covered in fine well-ploughed dirt, with not a weed in sight. The field directly west of here has no signs of plant life on it, and tall hay is visible to the south. North, through the trees an outline of an old ruin can be seen. A farmhouse is visible to the south-west, with numerous other small buildings around it.
14337: Fields of Hay, Barley and Oats

These parcels of land are about an acre in size each and grow three crops for feeding the various farm animals. There are fields of hay, oats and barley, in different stages of being harvested. There are several bales on the ground, ready for storage. The main part of the farm lies west of here, the side of a building with no door there. To the east the plains stretch until the base of the mountains.
14339: A hungry warg (Rood) is standing here, ridden by you.

There are fields of tall wheat blocking the views south and north of here, waving in the wind together like waves in the sea. The field grows shorter to the east, revealing a fenced area. There are several animals grazing in this enclosed field, near to a farmhouse. The entrance to the farmyard is just east of here, surrounded by several buildings.
14340: A barely noticeable path comes down from the old main road which lies directly to the west, and leads eastward to a small farm. North of here there are fields of short grasslands which are obviously tended, and beyond them some very thick brush. South the causeway of the old road runs by, eroded over time but still passable.
14341: The Tattered Remains of a Junction

This ancient road carries on to the north-west on a raised causeway, but a smaller path runs off to the east and leads to an old farm. Along the track there are some farm fields which appear to be tended. On each side of the road here is wetlands, perhaps the reason why the road is on a causeway. To the south and east it dries out though, and the road levels to the plains.
14342: The abandoned road, so eroded it is almost dangerous, leads slightly downwards to the south-east, where the ground seems to become less wet. Here the road is surrounded by stagnant wetlands, but the causeway keeps the road from flooding. The soggy grasslands stretch for some distance to the south, the terrain being nothing but endless reeds and water.
14343: The ground here is saturated with water, and it squishes out underfoot like a wet sponge. The only grass that has taken root is a brittle, soft green; but it is sparse. An ancient road skirts by to the north-east, avoiding flooding on its raised causeway. Tiny dikes are built into it, draining rainwater off the road. There is a stand of trees some way to the south-west, along the border of the wetlands.
14344: The ground here is covered in thick grass, turning as one in the wind. Patches of wildflowers and daisies are interspersed here and there, but not in great numbers. The grassland is bordered to the south by a stand of alder trees, beyond which the terrain turns to wetlands. North-east an old road cuts through the fields, rising up above the soggy terrain on an earthen causeway.
14345: The land begins to rise here, towards a raised bluff in the north-west. The ground is covered in lush green grass, flattened in parts as if by a rampaging herd of animals. It seems to be especially so to the north, where a trail made by animal hooves is clearly visible on the hillside. South and east the ground flattens out into open meadows.
14346: The meadow here surrounds the small hill to the north. It would make excellent farm land, the ground being very fertile. Indeed the grass looks to be a bit trampled in places, as if a herd or pack of animals had recently come through here. To the south, the meadows continue, while to the north they rise up on the sides of a bluff.
14347:
A large stone fireplace with a roaring fire warms the room.
A Rohir outrider roams about, seeking out invaders.
A foot-soldier of Rohan is here.
A soldier of Rohan is here, guarding the tower.
A foot-soldier of Rohan is here.

Under the tower a natural cave has been widened, and converted into sleeping quarters. There are three beds cut from the rock walls, with thick animal furs the only bedding. North the cave continues, narrower than here, and above a slightly rickety wooden ladder leads to a hatch in the ceiling. Underfoot the rock is covered with a dusty layer of soil, damp in patches where water has seeped in from above.
14348: A soldier of Rohan is here, guarding the tower.

This is the northern part of a cavern; the rocky lower half that has remained unused. The reason is the pooling water, unable to drain away here because of the bare stone. South the cave has been made into sleeping quarters, widened into a habitable place. Above the rock ceiling is hidden in the dark, far above you.
14349:
A sturdy pack horse is standing here.
A sturdy trained horse is standing here.
A sturdy trained horse is standing here.

Surrounded by tall stone walls on three sides and the tower to the east, this open-air pen is used to keep the inhabitants' mounts. A modicum of shelter is provided from the elements by two wooden stalls on the southern well, where a rusted metal feeding trough stands. On the northern side the stone wall has crumbled over the cliff edge at one point, giving a view of the long drop down.
14350:
A Rohir outrider, wielding a longsword, is here, fighting Starbuck (SS).
A soldier of Rohan is here, guarding the tower.
A Rohir outrider, wielding a longsword, is here, fighting Starbuck (SS).
A sturdy pack horse is standing here.
Starbuck (SS), wielding an engraved broadsword, is here, fighting a Rohir outrider.

The base of the tower is earthen, the soil damp from lack of light. The walls are circular, about thirty feet in diameter, and made of large and rough stone blocks. Around the inside edge of the tower winds a staircase of protruding stone blocks, leading to the level above. Two doors exit from this level of the tower: a small western door leading to an animal pen, and the larger main door to the south, made of thick oak wood. Barely visible in the dark northern corner is a hatch, leading down.
14351:
An archer of the Mark is here.
A Rohir outrider roams about, seeking out invaders.
An archer of the Mark is here.

This is the highest accessible point in the tower. Above there used to be one more level, but it has long since crumbled away. The stair that once led up is no longer there, and its floor is nothing but rotten wood. Even here the planks are splintered and cracking in places, the neglect of ages apparent. However, even from this lesser height the view is panoramic - no movement within miles would go unnoticed by those watching from here.
14352: This lone tree gives an excellent view over the land nearby, although there is little to see but brush for a good distance. The branches themselves are strong and easily bear weight, with some of the limbs looking sturdy enough to venture out and gather some cherries.
14353:
An arrow lies on the ground.
An arrow lies on the ground.
An arrow lies on the ground.
An arrow lies on the ground.

The fields continue here, full of the same lush green grass as most of the nearby land. Mostly it seems flat all around, except to the north where the fields rise up into a sudden bluff. To the south a line of sparse alder trees cut across the land, their sinuous canopies waving in the wind.
14354: Among a Stand of Alder Trees
An arrow lies on the ground.

These white-trunked trees are located widely apart, thus manoeuvring through the grove is fairly easy. North of this stand of trees are miles of lush green meadowland, with a small rise in the distance the only break in the horizon. To the south, the bases of the trees are immersed in small pools of water.
14355: The trees here are sparse, their canopies little more than a bush-like tangle of sinuous branches and leaves. The ground below is covered in an ankle-high layer of grass, with the occasional shrub here and there. North of this grove are lush fields, stretching for miles. The trees to the south are in parts surrounded by water, their roots dipping into the pools.
