The landscape quite lovely indeed, although words do not seem to do it proper justice. The vibrant flora and colourful wildflowers dotting the hills only add to the already impressive spectacle. Even the Misty Mountains are beautiful from here, as long as you are far away so as not to be affected by the shadow they cast on this land at times.
14539: This is nothing but the continuation of the tiny tributary that continues on to the east and west. Little more than a trickle it is. The only sound here is the gurgling of the water, sounding its harmony with the winds that blow softly across all of Arda.
14540:
A tall plant grows here, with grey-green leaves and grey flowers.
A tall plant grows here, with grey-green leaves and grey flowers.

The small stream makes a bend here to the west and south, turning away from its ancient parent, the Sirannon, which lies further to the north. As it turns its back on the once-great river, the tributary heads deeper into the lands once known by elves as Eregion.
14541:
A tall stag is here, grazing peacefully.
A fat rabbit is here, chewing on some grass.

Lush indeed are these hills, supported by the endless supply of water from the large amounts of rainfall which grace this land with its kiss of life. All of the local terrain looks much the same, in fact, and everything seems full of floral life. Oddly enough however, there is an absolute silence in these parts, although you can plainly see a variety of wildlife that you would expect to make more noise.
14542:
A fat rabbit is here, chewing on some grass.
A brown fox is here, looking for some rabbits to chew up.

You walk lightly through these hills, with tall grasses and wildflowers all around you. The flora is so healthy in fact, that the grass springs immediately upright following your footfalls, leaving barely any sign of recent travel. The hills are well above most of the nearby terrain, but the grass is so high in places that it is sometimes hard to even see a foot ahead. East is a higher unclimbable rocky hill.
14543: You are on a fairly high mountain ridge layered with course rocks and tiny pebbles. To the east is a valley that winds its way northward. At the end of that valley you see a large stone formation resembling a crown.
14544: You are walking on a small path at the bottom of a valley with steep slopes. The valley seems to wind its way northwards, like a great serpent between the mountain ridges. Resembling the skin of the serpent, showing all the differnt hues of brown and green on its scales, lie the valley slopes, clad with occasional trees and bushes.
14545:
A small flower grows here, with a purple bloom and wide leaves.
A small flower grows here, with a purple bloom and wide leaves.
Covered with a tall, green blanket of grass, your stroll along this ridge is quite enjoyable. Hot and sweaty from the climb, you enjoy the light breeze that sweeps across this mountain ridge.
14546: These plains are tucked between a stream to the north and east and a ridge to the south. The plains overlook a deep valley to the west - a deep furrow in the earth that has a somewhat unnatural look.
14547: Still the valley goes on, and now a chilly wind starts to blow, blowing right through your clothes and freezing your skin. You bite your teeth together as a sign of resilience. Still, the cold is a strange kind of cleaning feeling; much like the beauty of this place is a cold beauty; as lifeless and hard as rocks.
14548: As you turn a hill sticking far out from the western side of the valley, a huge stone formation comes to view. It resembles a crown, seven peaks rising at the end of the valley. You quickly decide to go nearer and study the crown up close.
14549: At the Base of the Natural Crown

Before you is the most impressive stone formation you have ever seen; a great crown of rock seems to have been set at the end of the valley, leaving you standing at the king's throne. A steep climb it is, but you could probably make it. You're eager to see what hides in the middle of those peaks.
14550: You are in the middle of a giant stone-basin, its floor gently sloping into walls, smooth and flawless except for a single stair spiraling out from where you stand. At perfect intervals around the rim of the basin, seven peaks rise, giving you the impression of standing in the middle of a king's crown. This must indeed be the work of Aule himself, a gift to the people whose father he is.
14551:
A porcupine is waddling around here, its tail full of sharp quills.
A fat rabbit is here, chewing on some grass.
A bear is here, covered with coarse black fur.

Everything is peaceful in these hills, and you walk easily through them with the wind blowing lightly through your hair. The landscape is the very picture of serenity, with vibrant colour nearly everywhere you look, from the sky above to the wildflowers on the ground. The only unsettling element of this otherwise perfect setting the a shadow which seems to be on this land, perhaps cast by the rocky peak to the east.
14552: A brown fox is here, looking for some rabbits to chew up.

The hills stretch far in any direction, and in fact you cannot see much else. There are several forested areas however, and the glimmering silvery strip of a tributary of the Sirannon, long dried. Naturally you can't help but notice to the east the mighty mountains of Moria, known in the elven-tongue as Caradhras, Celebdil, and Fanuidhol.
14553:
A cloak mottled in green and brown, and stinking to high heaven lies here.
A fang, an orkish piercing sword, has been planted in the ground.
A large pile of copper coins has been placed here.
A half-decayed corpse of a goblin lies rotting on the ground.
A big cavebear is padding around here.
A large bat is here, hanging in the darkness.
A fierce bat is here, lusting for your blood.
A fierce bat is here, lusting for your blood.

The downward sloping passage opens into this large cave, beneath the peaceful hills of Hollin. The entire cavern has the smell of animal excrement, which is in large heaps at various parts of the cave. Also scattered about are numerous bones, mostly of fish and small animals. You can also discern, however, some seemingly human bones. Whatever lives here would probably not appreciate any company.
14554:
The small fierce-looking bat is hanging from the ceiling, obviously sleeping.
A bloodthirsty bat is sleeping here, hanging from the ceiling.
A bloodthirsty bat is sleeping here, hanging from the ceiling.

Darkness prevails in this cave, the only illumination coming from whatever light sources you've brought with you. Something rather large appears to frequent this cave, as can be told from the tracks here. Also evidence of this are some tufts of fur that can be seen on the walls of the cave, as if the inhabitant of this place has been rubbing against them in an attempt to get the lice and vermin out of its fur. The cave slopes downward, going further beneath the hill.
14555: A large mother hawk is here looking for prey to feed her young.

This cliff stands high above the once smoothly-flowing Sirannon. It is a good distance down, but the cliff is wide enough as to not be at all threatening, except for those with vertigo. It might once have been possible to dive down into the water, if you had been an expert swimmer, but now of course that is unwise at best, seeing as there is no longer any water to dive into.
14556: This small woodland gives you an opportunity to get off the grass for a while. Behind the riverbed to the north and west is the Hollin Road, used for many years by the Dwarves of Moria, and the Elves of Ost-in-Edhil. It has long since fallen into ruin, as there is noone to undertake the repair process. Just to the north-west is the dry riverbed of the Sirannon. It has long been the fairest river of the Eregion, but is now filled with earth and sand.
14557:
A bright green holly bush is growing here.
A porcupine is waddling around here, its tail full of sharp quills.

The hills here stand above a tributary of the perished Sirannon, ever watching over it while protecting it from the elements. It is possible to see for miles in any direction here, and the surroundings are essentially unchanging - nothing but vibrant greenery in every direction, be it grasses and fields, or forest. The one notable exception is the impressive mountain range far to the east, where lies the ancient Dwarven home of Khazad-dum.
14558: A fat rabbit sits here, chewing on some grass.

The hills here stand above a tributary of the dried Sirannon, offering a good view of the essentially unchanging surroundings. It is possible to see for miles in any direction, and as far as the eye can see everything is covered with vibrant greenery, be it grasses and plains, or forest. Even the range of mountains to the east manage to fit somehow into the picturesque scene.
14559:
A porcupine is waddling around here, its tail full of sharp quills.
A brown fox is here, looking for some rabbits to chew up.

A good vantage point is to be found here, as can be seen immediately. The hills here are high enough to peek over the tops of other hills nearby, while at the same time allowing one to vigilantly watch over a tributary winding below them. The terrain is for miles essentially the same, with large amounts of vibrant greenery and colourful flowers, along with a forest further north. The only very notable exception, of course, is the large mountain range far to the east.
14560: The tributary winds along through the hilly Hollinish landscape, seemingly very carefree. In fact, almost everything here is quite cheerful indeed, what with the mostly lush flora and variety of a animals present. Counterbalancing the gaity, unfortunately, are the imposing mountains of Moria off to the east, which cast their shadow on the land. In particular the hills in the distance to the north are darkened by the darkness cast by Celebdil, Caradhras, and Fanuidhol.
14561:
There are three water lilies here.
A crayfish is here, snapping its claws at you.

This is a small tributary that at one point joined with the Sirannon to the north, adding its own flow to that of the larger stream. The rivulet itself continues to the east, while we have hill rising on the western side.
14562: In this particular spot, the rough hills rise up to overlook the streambed of the Sirannon on its seemingly neverending search for the sea. Your vantage point is quite good, giving you a good estimation of the lie of the land in the surrounding areas, which mostly consists of grassy hills, and some forested areas as well, particularly to the north.
14563:
A bright green holly bush is growing here.
Partly covered by the bush's green leaves, there are some hollyberries.
A large marmot is here, scurrying in between the rocks.
A fallow deer is grazing peacefully here.

Here you stand quite near the river, on almost a landing of sorts, which leads into some rugged looking hills. Looking around at them, you can see that there is not nearly as much grass and foliage as on some of the other hills near, for some odd reason that you can't begin to guess. You can keep walking in these hills or enter the streambed of the Sirannon to the north.
14565:
A sturdy pack horse is standing here.
A sturdy pack horse is standing here.
A tall stag is here, grazing peacefully.
A tall stag is here, grazing peacefully.

The hills here are noticeably higher than the natural landing to the west, yet they ascend still further to the south. Throughout these hills you find small trails here and there, evidently created by the indigenous wildlife that lives here. Some of the tracks you find are quite small, while some are large enough for you to fit both of your feet in together. Perhaps you should pay a bit more attention to your surroundings.
14566: A swarm of mosquitoes is here, humming around you.

The riverbed continues ever on to the north and west, looking as though it might make a northward bend somewhere further east. The Sirannon now runs betwixt some hills on either side, leaving it in a small valley of sorts, so that parts of the banks are rather obscured in shadow. The road that faithfully follows the streambed is still to the north.
14567: The shallow bed of the Sirannon makes a bend here, winding to the north and to the west. Several wilting plants and grasses struggle for survival in and around the bed, in addition to many dead ones, having long since given up the fight to live. They are the exception, not the rule, however, as the rest of the landscape here is covered with vibrantly hued flora.
14568: Yet again the track bends to the will of the Sirannon, this time to the east and south. Across the perished stream, off in the distance, is Dunland. It is hard to make out any details from this distance, but it seems the Dunlandish hills are somewhat more desolate than those of Eregion. To the north are some lush hills, and there are signs of a forest further north. Naturally it is possible to clamber down into the shallow bed of the Sirannon, once the smoothly-flowing jewel of Hollin, but since dammed up, ceasing its flow.
14569: You trudge still upon the seemingly endless track. Once, very long ago, this journey might have been very exciting, meeting and talking with any number of interesting people from all walks of life. Unfortunately, you're many years too late, and the area is now uninhabited and the track is untravelled. To the north you can make out a way to get into some hills, and east and south is the hollin road.
14570: The wide trail bends here once again, winding alongside the river bed. The landscape here is even more in the shadow of the mountains of Moria than those to the west, even though you still appear to be a considerable distance away from them. The lands here are still fertile however, and you wonder if perhaps the beauty of this land once known as Nan-Eregdos is a remnant of the beauty once fostered by both Dwarf and Elf in their alliance of ages past. You may go east and west on the overgrown road from here.
14571: This was apparently a branching point of the Sirannon, back when its silvery ribbon stretched across the land on its journey towards the sea. The bed continues to the north, while the tributary is to the south. Also, it seems you can venture onto a small peninsula, which looks like it leads into some of the gorgeous hills that grace this land called Eregion.
14572: Here what had been the strong-flowing Sirannon was flowing directly to the sea, in an area marked by the various twistings of the river. The fast flow of the river here has once washed enough of both banks away so that to even attempt to climb up either one could be a potentially dangerous endeavour. An adventurer of calibre could certainly make it with no problem, however.
14573: This is a tributary of the Sirannon, bringing at some water to the waterbed north. The shallow bed left behind by the waterway runs east towards the mountains, and is lost on the western horizon. To the west is a cliff over the river, and hills lie in all other directions.
14574: Still the river twists and turns, having shaped the surrounding land to it's will. This particular bend in the river is to the west and north, and is still bordered by hills to the south, which are not quite accessible from here. Coming from the mountains to the south-east, a river adds quite some water to the streambed, which makes a bit more alive than it was further east of here.
14575: A crayfish is here, snapping its claws at you.

The sound of the local wildlife fills your ears and you stroll lazily along this everlasting waterway. In addition, you hear the whisper of the wind blowing through the thick grasses that blanket the surrounding hills, particularly to the north. The river is split in streams channels here, making the crossing easy. It twists more to the east, bending south. From here it is possible to continue along the meandering streambed, or to venture into some of the lovely hills that grace this land to the south.
14576: Winding lazily along, Sirannon bends yet again, seemingly on a whim, to the south and east. The river is still in somewhat of a valley, yet not so much as to totally obscure the sun, which is visible enough to highlight the vibrant colours of the local flora, and the dew glistening off of it. A little ways off to the north is an old overgrown road, practically the only sign that this gorgeous place has ever been touched by civilization.
14577: To the east and south the bed continues on, endlessly searching for its source. Also you can climb out of the riverbed north or west, to reach the road. It would be best to go that way, as the hills to the south look rather ominous, despite their lushness, and it may be a good idea to get as far from them as possible.
14578: You're still on this wide grassy track, once travelled by the natives of both Eregion and Dunland. That was a long time ago, and now there is hardly any sign of use remaining, in that you see no footprints, no cart tracks, only the knowledge that long ago this was a major thoroughfare indeed. To the south you see an old streambed, and to the north are some rugged hills.
14579:
A holly bush with dark green leaves is growing here.
Partly covered by the bush's green leaves, there are a torch and two piles of inkberries.

You warily move around another bend in this trail, stepping lightly so as not to make a single sound. Occasionally you come across a mangled animal carcass rotting on the ground, torn apart by something not terribly friendly. After stopping for a moment, you press on, ready for whatever may come. This path seems to take you between some high banks of earth, eroding and not safe to climb.
14580: Here the trail makes a smooth bend to the north and west. On the ground here and there are fragments of what appear to be broken tiles that may have once paved this path. It must have been a long time ago however, since the entire area is completely overgrown now. To the east you may enter some lightly forested hills.
14581: There seems to be some sort of path through these hills, judging from the way the foliage is bent towards the ground in places. To the south lies an old track, which once may have been well-used, but has since become overgrown with grass. Northward, however, the hills continue as the trees thicken to become the forest that lies even further in that direction.
14582: The neverending track runs still along the equally eternal Sirannon streambed. You feel at peace, looking at the lush flora of Hollin, which is apparently supported by a generous amount of rain. In addition you see plenty of small creatures playing or eating in the grass, and a number of birds soaring in the skies above. This place would be perfect, you think to yourself, if it were not so close to the mountains of Moria that they cast their shadow across the land.
14583: This is a small, yet apparently well-travelled path, running amongst some fairly large hills. The hills are tall enough, in fact, as to totally enshroud the trail in shadows, creating a seemingly evil shroud on the landscape. It would be wise to be careful.
14584: A large marmot is here, scurrying in between the rocks.

The trees thin out quite a bit here, as the predominantly wooded land meets an imposing cliff face to the west. Numerous rocks seem to have fallen from the cliff, as can be seem by simply looking around, and more rocks are falling all the time. From here you can follow the base of the cliff up a short slope, or head into better forested terrain to the east. To the south appears to be some sort of path, but it is too obscured in shadow to be able to tell anything more.
14585:
A squirrel scampers around here, looking for nuts from the trees.
A fallow deer is grazing peacefully here.

This small valley abruply pinches off, leaving you in a kind of natural bowl. The place is rather small in area, and is very nicely adorned with trees and lush green growth. In contrast to the rocky hills around you, that do not support such rich green foliage, the sight is definitely different. The reason the growth is so plentiful here is apparent, as a small spring bubbles up from the ground. Behind you the valley continues, or you may go up to the north to walk along a wooded ridge.
14586: You stand now in the summit of a small cliff, excavated by the erosion in this rocky hill. From this point you can see the landscape in every direction, hilly and covered by the forest. To the south a dusty line marks the dry streambed of the Sirannon. Far east you can see the white misty mountains. There is a definite shortage of the lush vegetation that covers most of the landscape here, what foliage there is comprised mostly of small scrub bushes. Rocks of various sizes cover the ground in place of the plants and trees.
14587: A fallow deer is grazing peacefully here.

This sparse slope seems devoid of most of the vegetation that inhabits other parts of this area. Probably due to the numerous falling rocks from the cliffside to your west, and from the heavy shade that seems to come from it. Loose rocks are constantly falling off the eroded hillside, and climbing up that way seems far too hazardous. To the west you can see the familiar trees of the forest, and what looks like a climbable ridge. In the south are some more rocky grounds like these.
14588:
A robin is here, carrying small pieces of wood to its nest.
A fallow deer is grazing peacefully here.
A woodchuck is watching for enemies here.

There is a definite shortage of the lush vegetation that covers most of the landscape here, what foliage there is comprised mostly of small scrub bushes. Rocks of various sizes cover the ground in place of the plants and trees, probably coming from an old eroded cliff that rises above some distance to the west. You can continue on these rockier grounds to the west and south, or enter some more fertile areas to the east.
14589: A robin is here, carrying small pieces of wood to its nest.

The gentle hills support a beautiful deciduous forest and a wide variety of small animals can be spotted among the trees by the patient. The land becomes a bit more rocky to the west, while to the east and south the hills continue.
14590: Sounds of animal life fill your ears as you walk through these hills. Trees grow fairly thickly here, and to the north and east the hills flatten out while the landscape becomes even more forested. You can travel in any direction here, be it into the forest, south into more of the hills that grace the land, or west, into some rockier and less foliated areas.
14591: A woodpecker is here, tapping on a tree.

The tall trees stand sentinel above, watchful yet beautiful as well, with their many hued leaves and wildflowers adorning their trunks. Small birds and animals are common here, paying more mind to their own business, ignoring you completely. It is possible to continue on in the forest to the north, or to some wooded hills which rise up to the east. To the south appears to be a small hollow.
14592:
A tree-snake lies wrapped around one of the tree branches.
A porcupine is waddling around here, its tail full of sharp quills.

Like old friends, the hills here stand alongside a lush forest in all their vibrant splendour for all the world to marvel at. Truly this is one of the most gorgeous lands you have ever seen, despite the unsettling feelings that arrise from the mountains. The beauty itself is very nearly enough to push all fear from an adventurer heart as he reveals in this majestic work of nature.
14593: A squirrel scampers around here, looking for nuts from the trees.

If you look slowly around, it is possible to see for miles and miles in any direction here. Looking to the west trying to take in every single detail, you could strain your eyes and hope for a glimpse of the ancient city of Ost-in-Edhil, which has lain in ruin for thousands of years. Try as you might, however, you cannot find it. Probably it is too far away to be seen from here.
14594: Seemingly neverending are these hills which grace the land known to Elves of old as Eregion. Various colourful flowers and bushes crown the green landscape in full bloom, as you witness some of Eru's finest work on display in front of you. The hills continue smoothly to both the north and west, and off to the south and east you can make out an old track.
14595: You stand here among these lush hills breathing in the refreshing Hollinish air, which feels clean and pure in your lungs. From this height, the view is breathtaking indeed, with lovely green countryside as far as the eye can see in nearly any direction. Added to all of that is the majesty of the mighty mountains to the east. Few things are so lovely as nature unblemished by the works of man.
14596: There is a very narrow trail of sorts here, running between the thick wall of vegetation to the north and some hills to the south. Certainly this place would make anyone who is claustrophobic most uncomfortable indeed. The trail is as maddeningly silent as the hills it serves to connect, which is enough to make anybody wary, claustrophobic or not. An ancient overgrown road runs its course to the south of here.
14597: Colourful grasses and wildflowers surround you here, among other types of flora, all of which is very well-watered thanks to the large amounts of rainfall this area must get. The hills here are substantially lower than those to the south, becoming flatter to the west.
14598:
A small evergreen plant grows here, its woody stems reaching two feet.
A woodpecker is here, tapping on a tree.

The hills flatten out here, as the landscape changes to accomodate the well- watered forest to the north. Gradually the tall grasses change to low bushes, which grow thickly together. There are several types of animal easily seen in these parts, from the small squirrels scampering about, to the birds resting in the trees singing a sweet melody for all of Arda to hear.
14599:
A robin is here, carrying small pieces of wood to its nest.
Wrinkletoe the Hobbit (WT), wielding the Axe of Durin, is here, riding a mountain mule.

Rocks dot the landscape here, managing to quell some of the smaller plants and bushes that might once have grown here. Most of the larger ferns and trees continue to live however, although they are perhaps not as tall or as vibrantly green as those which grow on more fertile soil. To the west and north it is possible to continue through these rocky grounds, while other directions maintain the same lush flora that the land of Eregion is known for.
14600: A woodpecker is here, tapping on a tree.

Utter silence prevails, making you wary as you follow this unclear trail. The shadow of the distant mountains of Moria is cast heavily in these parts, obscuring any light in some places, while letting it through in others, causing shadows of the foliage to dance and flicker ominously. The Dark One's arm reaches far indeed in these days. Hills lie an all directions, though to the west seems to be a small trail.
14601: Here the hills open up slightly, allowing an adventurous traveller to explore them more thoroughly. The landscape is really quite lovely, with vibrant green grasses everywhere, speckled generously with all sorts of wildflowers. Oddly, there aren't any animals present to enjoy the spectacle, despite the fact that there does not seem to be anything present which might disrupt their natural habitat.
14602: As this particular spot, the hills overlook the old track that runs alongside the streambed of the Sirannon. Your position offers a view of several miles in any direction, the lush landscape reaching the western horizon, to the imposing mountains of Moria to the east. Perhaps this very place was used to watch these lands in the days of old, when the friendship of the Elves and Dwarves brought this land to its greatest glories.
14603: There are two handfuls of clover here.

Below you, the Sirannon riverbed runs its course, having carved a path through these hills thousands of years ago. Even if this land has increased in age, its beauty remains untarnished by the long years. It is hard to imagine it more beautiful than it is now, even in the days of old, when Elf and Dwarf fostered their unique friendship, the likes of which may never be seen again.
14604:
A bright green holly bush is growing here.
Partly covered by the bush's green leaves, there are two piles of hollyberries and a torch.

This track continues along with no end to it in sight. To the east though, it seems to make a turn to the north, separating from its long-time travelling partner, the Sirannon. You notice all sorts of different types of terrain in these parts, from the grassy hills and forest to the north of the road, to the slightly more desolate hills to the south of it. For some reason however, the more desolate hills look somewhat more hospitable.
14605: A sparrow is flapping around on the ground.

The ancient track stretches ever on alongside its old friend, the river Sirannon. Even with the stream dried, the land seems not to suffer at all, as is evidenced by the lush greenery and vibrant colours present in the local flora, which consists of everything from grasses and wildflowers to a healthy looking forest to the north. The trees are so large, in fact, as to cast somewhat of a shadow on the hills surrounding it, causing them to look rather foreboding.
14606: Yet again, the grassy track bends along beside the Sirannon. The scenery here is most picturesque indeed, and looks like something out of a faerie tale; complete with the wild animals, the grassy hills and the ominous looking mountains to the east. Despite the gorgeous surroundings and the air of happiness and tranquility, some sort of shadow seems to be over this land, perhaps a remnant of days long forgotten.
14607: The track here winds lazily along with the will of the indominable Sirannon. Grass covers most of the track here, but is still worn in spots, probably the work of some animals that frequent the area. Signs of the civilizations that once stretched across the lands are quite absent however, and you wonder how all traces of the kingdoms of Eregion and Dunland could appear to have simply vanished. Perhaps the land itself remembers its former inhabitants, but you see no signs of them as you continue your journey through Hollin.
14608: The track bends here to the west and north, matching the curve of the Sirannon, whose bed runs its course just to the south of road. Far north are some lush hills that look high enough as to be somewhat difficult to get through. To the north of those lie some forested land, although you cannot immediately tell just how dense the forest gets. There are all sorts of animals about, playing in the grass or searching for food.
14609: A green frog is here, hopping around.

You wander now in the uneven bed of the Sirannon, a stream which once made its path known across Arda, but has long since decreased its flow. From here you can continue in the streambed, or enter some of the lovely hills which grace the land of Nan-Eregdos. To the north, you can even climb up onto an ancient road, and see where that may take you.
14610: The trail still goes on before you, and though it is comfortable, it constantly has you watching out for roots or brambles to stumble in. To truly enjoy the scenery, you have to stop and watch for a while.
14611: The path continues to wind its way from the gates of Moria to Ost-in-Edhil. Walking is comfortable, and you start to hum softly to yourself as you skip along.
14612:
A bright green holly bush is growing here.
Partly covered by the bush's green leaves, there are three piles of hollyberries.

A long time ago, this was a great road, the main route between the elven city Ost-in-Edhil, and the dwarven dwellings of Khazad-dum. Now it is little more than a trail, overgrown with bushes and brambles.
14613: At this point, the path bends in a long, smooth curve. Knowing the dangers of straying from the road, you decide to follow the path; either east towards Moria, or south towards the city of Ost-in-Edhil.
14614: The road continues to stretch for as far as the eye can see. You let out a heavy sigh as you realise the long journey ahead. To the south you can see the dry riverbed of the Sirannon.
14615: A fairly straight trail lies before you; east towards Moria, and west towards Ost-in-Edhil. You relax and begin to enjoy the comfortable stroll, as you realise the long journey ahead.
14616: The trail bends again here, winding its way north towards the gates of Moria. From here you can barely see the high peaks of the Misty Mountains to your east. To the south lies the once flowing river Sirannon.
14617: Still heading north and south, the road enters a terrain of much diversity. Hills, forests, river water, and open flat-lands all grace Eregion in this sector. The rise of a large hill of rock just north of you catches your eye. A barely visible path seems to skirt it at the near side, seeming to go around it, to where the water flows quietly by. You can still see the riverbed from here, carrying the small stream westwards toward Ost-in-Edhil.
14618: Still heading north-south here, the road begins to pass a large rock mound to your east. Not a small mound, more like a small hill of barren boulders, it stands firm, unyielding. Hills lie on your west, with trees and holly growing in abundance. The air is pure, and the sound of water running close by is comforting. The water you surmise, is that of the diminished River Sirannon, winding from the West gate of Moria to its destination of Ost-in-Edhil, far to the west.
14619: Leading north-south now, the wide dirt track passes out of view of the riverbed. As it was a comforting sight and sound, you hope to see it again on your trek down this road. The rock formation is unclimbable from this spot, yet you think there is an easier slope on the far side of it. Some small hills lie just west of you, looking gentle and rolling. Trees adorn the hills, though smaller and less dense than the trees of the forest to your north. The now familiar holly bush still grows in plentiful proportions.
14620: You walk on through this channel-like riverbed finding at every turn mud, mud, and more mud. The riverbed is making its final turn around the forest to your southeast, making a smooth curve around it. To the north you can see the road that connects Ost-in-Edhil to Moria.
14621: The Sirannon is still far from full capacity, and the small stream seems dwarfed by the riverbed in which it is flowing. The Hollin Road still runs alongside the northern bank, while to the south is a lush and dense forest.
14622: A green frog is here, hopping around.

You try to avoid the mud in the bottom of the riverbed, but you find it quite strenuous to keep walking on the rather steep slopes. Your boots are already muddy all over, and you rapidly tire of that annoying splish-splosh sound.
14623: In every direction save north, trees have taken root in the rich soil. To the north, the channel that now houses the shrunken Sirannon can be made out through a gap in the trees. The land is quiet - the stream's burble is practically the only sound.
14624: You are walking leisurely along the shrunken Sirannon to the north. Here, on top of the river slopes, the birds sing and the squirrels scamper around, harvesting nuts for the winter. You take care not to move to close to the bank, as you might fall down the rather steep slopes.
14625: The riverbed takes a great swing around the forest to your south, before it continues on eastwards. When the river was more active, it dug itself deep into the ground, so following the riverbed is like walking a small valley.
14626: To the east, the riverbed takes a turn toward the north, passing beyond view. On the northern bank, the ancient Hollin Road runs - a testament to the skill of the Noldor and Dwarves at working stone, for it is still in fair shape after the passage of four millenia.
14627: Up ahead, the riverbed takes another bend to the north. Colourful rocks are strewn about, smoothened by the river's passage. Occasionally, the rocks reflect the sunlight, making them especially beautiful.
14628: A squirrel scampers around here, looking for nuts from the trees.

You are wandering along the edge of a lush, dense forest. The trees towering above you prevent most of the sunlight from reaching you, shielding you from the hot summer sun. To the north you can see the almost dry riverbed of the Sirannon; to the south you can barely see the peaks of the Misty Mountains.
14629: The forest stretches on all around you, and huge trees prevent you from seeing very far. Not that you need to see far; the forest is beautiful enough, if a bit too quiet. Long ago the elves abode in this land; but the trees do not remember them, nor do the animals; but the rocks do, singing their quiet songs.
14630: You enjoy your stroll along this forest because the trees provide much needed shade from the cruel, hot rays of the sun. Always aware that you may not be the only inhabitants in this forest, you remain quite cautious.
14631: You've dared the tree, but will you dare the jump? It might be your only chance of getting to the other side of the crevice, but it's well over two yards, and you haven't exactly got much running space.
14632:
A burly giant is here, covered with thick fur and snow.
A burly giant is here, covered with thick fur and snow.

You are carefully walking along the edge of the Misty Mountains making sure each step has a firm footing; one slip and you may end up falling into the deep crevice to your west. To the east the mountains become steeper and steeper.
14633: You are on a very steep, rocky incline. Unable to head back south, you can either head north towards the Misty Mountains or west to a small knoll along the river.
14634: The water creates a tumult of icy spray as it speeds along its course, fish can be seen jumping to avoid crashing against the rocks. To the north lies a steep slope; going up would be rough, coming down would be impossible.
14635: The river bends here, curving its way from the east to the north eating its way through the rocks. As the water changes course, a large, calm pool is formed.
14636: The water beats itself against the rocks, polishing their surfaces to a glistening slipperiness. The sound of churning water echos through the crisp air.
14637: A small waterfall tickling down the Misty Mountains is the source of this river. From here the water flows westward down the rocky mountain side, carrying with it fallen leaves from the nearby forest.
14638: A brown fox is here, looking for some rabbits to chew up.

The ground slopes down again, and you walk into an ocean of mist. You can see your nearest surroundings, which suprisingly enough, consist mainly of trees. The trees are dead and black as ebon, though, their branches writhing tentacles that seem ready to trap anyone who comes near them. You try to keep your distance to the trees, and that leads you eastwards, deeper into the forest.
14639:
A brown fox is here, looking for some rabbits to chew up.
An opossum stands here, sniffing around the ground.

Due to some unknown reason, you have walked deeper inside this forest. The trees almost seem to spread in various patterns, leading you to where they want you to go. Suddenly, you are looking out over a round lake somewhere deep in this forest, the lake giving away a pale reflection of the sunlight.
14640: Floating on the pale surface of this shadowy lake, it is easy to see this lake lies within the middle of a misty forest. The trees surround this place in all directions. Only to the south does there seem to be way ashore. Elsewhere the brambles and trees simply stand too thick. Perhaps this lake is hiding a secret beneath its surface.
14641:
A dirty key of stone has been dropped here.
A mass of tattered fabric lies here in a heap.
A large arrow lies on the ground.
A large arrow lies on the ground.
A large arrow lies on the ground.
A large arrow lies on the ground.
A large arrow lies on the ground.
A large arrow lies on the ground.
A large arrow lies on the ground.
A large arrow lies on the ground.
A large arrow lies on the ground.

The trail abruptly ends here, leaving you quite disappointed. For there seems to only be one choice left, and that is to head back. Realizing that a fall from this elevation would be fatal, you are careful not to stand too close to the edge of the trail.
14642: The carved-out path slowly slopes downard along the side of the mountain. As you drag your tired feet along the rocky, dust-ridden trail, dust flies in your face, stinging your eyes, and leaving a mouthful of dust granules.
14643:
A small and well-kept fire lights and warms the room.
A simple wooden chest is here.
A small oaken table has been set here.
A musty loaf of bread has been left here.
A musty loaf of bread has been left here.
A musty loaf of bread has been left here.

A crackling fire is burning in the middle of this fairly large cave, giving faint light, and making flickering shadows on the smooth walls. The cave is warm and well isolated; it seems like the dwarves' work. One wall is stacked with fire-wood, by the other there are many chests, probably for food. At the far wall stand a table and some chairs, and in the inner corner are some improvised beds.
14644:
In the sarcophagus (here):
a two-handed axe (worn)

A stone sarcophagus lies on the floor.
A dark intangible shadow turns to face you.
A dark intangible shadow turns to face you.

Awe strikes you as you slowly proceed into this dully lit chamber, the light coming from two candles situated at either side of the square room. In the exact middle of it lies a short stone coffin, its sides and top beautifully ornamented with elaborate carvings. A slab is raised on one of the coffin's ends, like a tombstone, with writings on it.
14645: A snow covered slope leads up towards even thinner air; air that is flowing down the slope like an invisible glacier freezing your body. As your mind pushes your body forward, your body rebels threatening not to take another step.
14646: Footprints in the ice signal that a large biped has passed through this area since the last snowfall. The tracks lead to the eastern cliff face, and appear to ascend the impossible surface.
14647: The snow here is more ice then snow, revealing to those who use a little thought that it has not snowed here for years. What was it so long ago that lifted these mountains?
14648: Ironically, even though you sit upon one of the tallest mountains of Arda, your view is very dull, merely a few ice covered rocks. In an effort to keep warm, you try to imagine the warmth of your homeland.
14649: A sharp-eyed hawk is here stalking some prey.
The last of the trees lie far below you now. What greets you is the dismal sight of rock and ice blending into a glassy grey. You begin to dream of days filled with better greetings.
14650: The familiar sight of ice and rock fills your view, jagged slopes and icy pitfalls. Far to the east a large chunk of ice rises above the other mountain tops.
14651: Here, the ground rises sharply as if to stop you from venturing further into the Misty Mountains; though the climb is quite steep and treacherous, you decide to attempt this feat due to your sense of adventure.
14652:
A burly giant is here, covered with thick fur and snow.
A burly giant is here, covered with thick fur and snow.
You continue to make your way up the mountain; you are careful not to lose your footing, one slip may be fatal. To the east lies the heart of the Misty Mountains.
14653:
A forest spider is here crawling around.
A squirrel scampers around here, looking for nuts from the trees.
The forest suddenly changes character; the growth is so wild that it becomes nearly impenetrable. The rest of the forest is very pleasant, and so are the inhabitants, at least most of them.
14654: You stand in a bowl-shaped hollow in the moors, a rather distinct element in the terrain; and that is exactly why you picked walking here. Yet you are back to where you started; from here every direction seems the same. You stare cheerlessly at the slopes around you, hoping to find a path or some other landmark.
14655: A lush layer of grass blankets the moors, leaving an impressive image in your mind. Relaxed and at peace, you feel as if you could stay here forever; but as a true adventurer, you decide to continue your journey.
14656: The path disappears altogether, and you are at the point of returning when you suddenly spot some kind of strange stone portal set between two ridges. An arm of mist seems to be reaching out of that portal, but the mist dissolves in the air when it gets any distance away from the portal.
14657: Still the path winds on, leading you deeper and deeper into the moors. When the path is at its higher points, you can catch a glimpse of the mountains to the south. Suddenly, you lose sight of it again, and you start to wonder whether it was all just a trick of the eye.
14658: The stream bends from the east to the north here. To the south lie the moors. Stories tell that the moors are haunted, and children and grown-ups alike are loath to go there. If you're lost on the moors, it's said, you have lost yourself.
14659: A small stream pours forth through a crack in the cliff to the east, merrily cascading downward about twenty feet. The water is frigid - it must originate somewhere in the Misty Mountains to the east. The stream flows away westward into the lands of Eregion.
14660: This small stream flows out of the mountains to the east - its water still pristine. To the west, it joins with another stream that is flowing down the middle of a wide streambed. To the south, the stream continues.
14661: At this point the riverbed splits; you are left with the choice of either heading west, along a path soiled with footprints, or east, along a path not often traveled.
14662: The riverbed abruptly bends east, and you bang your head against the stone as you try to change directions yourself as well. You look up towards the sun and delight in having the few beams that can reach you warm you up a bit, until you hit your head against the stone again. Ouch.
14663: The riverbed bends here, curving downwards from the north to the west. Further down, the riverbed begins to run parallel with the Hollin road, the main path that connects Moria to Ost-in-Edhil.
14664: A worm is here slithering around.

A thin layer of soft grass covers most of the rolling ground, except for some large rocks clad with moss. Aside from these, the moors contain few or no landmarks to speak of. Animal life is scarce here, maybe a worm or two slithering on through the grass, or some strange bird flying high above you.
14665: The slopes of the moors get steeper, and the vegetation scarcer, as it turns into a more hilly landscape. Chilly, but refreshing winds blow upon the hilltops, bearing in them the legacy of the mountains far east. Somewhat north runs the riverpath of the now dry Sirannon river, carrying that same legacy.
14666: You dug out enough mud to slide down into a hole, and now you can slide further into what seems to be a large natural cavern. The fall is steep though, and you would probably not get up again this way. You are stuck in a rather awkward position at this point, so you better decide whether to get down or get out quickly.
14667:
A large bat is here, hanging in the darkness.
A large bat is here, hanging in the darkness.
A huge bat is here, emitting piercing squeaks.
A fierce bat is here, lusting for your blood.

The darkness here is all-consuming, so that even a bright light can seem to fail at times, leaving you using your hands to find your way. Occasionally an unfamiliar noise breaks through the gloomy silence, echoing eerily all around you, its source impossible to locate.
14668: Around every corner is nothing but darkness. Your sense of direction almost fails you (while your sense of time is long lost), but you think you are walking in a fairly straight southwest direction. You start to wonder about how many passages and side tunnels must have eluded you; but you won't let it distract you as you walk on, determined to find...what?
14669: With each passing moment you find it harder to keep calm in this consuming darkness, which only becomes worse when your feeble light tries to penetrate it, casting flickering shadows on the walls. An inner voice reminds you that a cavern such as this is crowded with silent hunters, and that a probable aim for those hunters would be you.
14670: A small bat is standing here.

You have never heard of this place, let alone heard its name; but it comes creeping upon you as you step into a system of caverns, each cave entrance is like a giant fiend's gaping maw, each stalactite and stalagmite ready to strike at you. The flickering light of your torch does not reveal much. As for your sense of smell, something foul has left a thick and stale stench; and it's not far away. The only reason why you didn't run back out is that the way behind you is blocked.
14671: The crudely wrought walls reach out to touch you, and when you bend away from them, they eat your light instead. You start to tremble as you hear footsteps coming from every direction; or perhaps these noises are the result of your overactive imagination.
14672:
A big, nasty vulture is sitting here, protecting its nest.
A big, nasty vulture is sitting here, protecting its nest.

A narrow walkway winds its way westward towards the edge of the mountain; you can see it split into two paths up ahead, making way for a pile of twigs, branches, and sticks oddly placed neatly in a circular fashion.
14673: Climbing up this tall peak was a great accomplishment on your part; you are quite tired from the exhausting climb so you decide to rest here for a while. While enjoying the scenery, you notice that the southern river in the valley below originates from here.
14674: You are swimming around in the clear but dark, and, of course, extremely cold (and wet!) waters of this lake. The rock bottom seems nothing out of the ordinary to you, neither are any mermaids paddling around here. If this won't get you a cold, what will?
14675:
A large stone chest is here.
A shade is here, shrouded in an inky blackness.
A shadow suddenly leaves its place on the wall, trying to reach your neck.

This natural cave must be some kind of an air pocket, at least you can breathe freely. But the air won't last too long, though, and you suddenly wonder how that shape deep in the cave could have survived here. Then you realise that it may not have a life to lose...
14676: w or d may fall to bears (-100hp)

You are perched on a tiny ledge in a deep crevice. The sides of the crevice are nearly vertical with few to none hand holds. While it might be possible to climb out, the extremely sharp rocks which litter the floor of the crevice will make it quite painful if you fail. Some fifty yards below you lies the bottom of the crevice.
14677: A holly bush with dark green leaves is growing here.

The river bends around this small knoll. Though it looked steep, you have decided to climb it. Among the few stout trees that grow here are patches of flowers and berries. Especially the holly bush, giving this region its name, Hollin, dominates the undergrowth.
14678: At the Bottom of the Crevice

A big cavebear is padding around here.
A big cavebear is padding around here.
You are standing at the bottom of a very deep crevice. Fear envelops you as you see sharp rocks along the edge. Those who foolishly tried to descend the crevice met their fate.
14679: The sides of the mountains rise up to the east and west, cleverly hiding this path. Even the snow has not found this place and the ground can be seen to be undisturbed.
14680: A buzz in your ear reminds you that there are other fauna besides fish that lives near the river. An itch reminds you how annoying they can be, as you glance around looking for the culprit.
14682: Floating down the river with you is a rather disconcerting sight; a dead fish with its belly upturned is attracting flies and crawdads. As you get closer the smell pierces your nose.
14683: On the side of the river the water flows backwards making movement upstream much easier for those using boats. Tiny fish can be seen moving within the weeds that cover the bottom.
14684: You brace youself as you prepare to meet the little waterfall that the water drags you towards. A two foot drop may not seem like much when on land but to see the water foam as it heads over the drop brings fear to your heart.
14685: A swarm of mosquitoes is here, humming around you.
The canyon walls loom to the south and west, a possible source of falling boulders. You note the presence of many large rocks near the bottom of the cliff-side.
14686: To the east lies a gloomy shore, the sight of which chills your soul and yet beckons you with a promise of solid ground. You ponder as images of the beast which may roam the area fill your mind.
14687: The smell of rotten vegetation fills the air combining with the strong smell of fish and mud. On the bank can be seen cakes of dry mud forming a mosaic of fissures along the edge.
14688: Your way eastwards is blocked by a deep crevice, over which once spanned a stone bridge. The bridge must have fallen into the crevice a long time ago; now only the remnants of its ends remain. You are glad to find evidence of inhabitants, however ancient, but the whole place also gives a spooky feeling.
14689: This tall ridge towers high above this region, casting a dark shadow to the west. Here, you can see a river flowing from the base of the Misty Mountains westward. The trail along this ridge heads north and east.
14690: You carefully follow a game trail along this ridge deeper and deeper into the mountains. You are very careful not to stray far from the path because of the loose shale slopes; a rock avalanche could start if disturbed.
14691: The forest seems to thicken to your immediate east; on the other hand, to the west seems to be a clearing before the river. Otherwise, this forest dominates the scene, its huge trees and pleasant flowers give it a tranquil feel. The terrain becomes steeper as you approach the mountain ridge to your south.
14692: Suddenly, you are out of the forest, and standing on a little clearing, bordering on the dried out riverbed that the Sirannon has become. Still, even with the absence of the stream, this place radiates peace and beauty. Patches of flowers in the hues of red and blue and yellow create a soft and lush carpet for you to lie down on. On the southern side of the clearing is a huge boulder, creating cool shade for the hot summer days.
14693: Large rocks are placed on regular intervals here, creating a ford across the small river. The stones are huge, and you wonder what party of stout men or dwarves or elves could have put them there. Anyway, there's not much need for them now, only perhaps as a place for children to play.
14694: The riverbed continues to wind its way westward towards Ost-in-Edhil. To the east lies a now pretty useless ford, only a fairly impressive stone formation remain in its place. To the north lies the Hollin Road, a trail leading to Moria.
14695: The game trail ends here; your only choice is to climb back down towards a clearing in the Sirannon Forest to the north or a river to the south. You let out a heavy sigh of relief as you realise that your journey down would be much easier than your journey up.
14696: On the Banks of a River
A holly bush with dark green leaves is growing here.

Shadows of the mountains darken this place, and their slopes echo and amplify the few sounds to be heard. Now, each footstep splashing in the water is almost comforting in its familiarity. Yet even here a few small bushes cling to the banks of the river, growing despite the shadow.
14697:
A small vicious black rat squeaks at you for disturbing it.
A huge, hungry-looking rat is here.

A gigantic fireplace in the southeastern corner dominates this room. The floor in front of the fireplace is now black with ash, piled up through years of decay. The rest of the room is only gray with the thick dust- layer lying as a carpet over the broken and rotted furniture.
14700:
A wooden statue of a guardian suddenly creaks, slowly turning to life.
A black spider crawls here, a shiny red spot visible on its belly.

Much smaller than the last one, this room contains almost nothing but a desk with a book spread out upon it. The air is stale, and a thick layer of dust covers every inch of the room; it seems like centuries since anyone has set their foot here.
14701:
The corpse of a young rat is lying here.
The corpse of a giant rat is lying here.
The corpse of a young rat is lying here.
The corpse of a young rat is lying here.

This room is very simple and sparsely equipped, yet it gives you the feeling that many a great dwarf has spent his hours here. A wash basin still stands on a nearly crumbled wooden table beside a long since rotted bed. A thick layer of dust covers the entire room. A book lies on the bed, and suprisingly enough, it still contains some readable passages.
14702: Standing on this fairly high ridge, you have a wonderful view of the area; to the north lies a dense forest and to the south lies a deep crevice, preventing you from going higher up the Misty Mountains. You notice a tall tree on the southern edge of the ridge.
14703: As you walk further south you notice the terrain getting steeper and steeper; you start to make your transition from a comfortable stroll in the lush, shady forest to a grueling climb up the mountain ridges ahead.
14704: There are two woody, stemmed plants here.

For some reason, this feels like the exact middle of this forest, its very essence seems to hide here. The huge trees forming the grove give a feeling of tranquility combined with respectfulness, not to mention some strange kind of watchfulness.
14705: This small rise separates the riverbed of the Sirannon and the Hollin Road. Sloping upwards only a few meters above the small stream, it is just high enough to give a scenic view down the length of the river. Holly bushes cover the hill with the same lush green leaves that adorn most other parts of the region. Looking north, you see a large rock formation. Looking like a table, it seems to have been there for many many years.
14706: The flat area you are in is very scenic and peaceful. The riverbed can be seen to your east and south, giving the field an island-like atmosphere. Just northwards, the flats continue, but turning more rocky and sandy. A massive rock pile to the north, almost a small hill, makes its presence known by jutting many meters in the air. Green grass and small flowers sprinkle the field, as well as some bushes of holly. Fresh tracks in the grass alert you that this is where the local animals come to graze, forage, and get water.
14707: This is the bed where once the Sirannon flowed on its journey from the gates of Moria to Belegaer, the Great Sea. Something has cut off most of the water supply farther upstream, for the volume of flow is significantly less than the size of the streambed would indicate.
14708: A brook trout is here, swimming in the current.

The river takes a more southernly course here, bordering some hills to the southeast. The Hollin Road at this point leaves the riverbed for a bit, making a swing to the north, and rejoining the river again later. The water is still cold, bearing its legacy from the great mountains. The swift flowing stream that was once here, is now represented by only the tiniest of trickles.
14709: A pebble strewn beach lies before you, gently leading down to the riverbed of the Sirannon. The small trickle of water is bending south and east here, flowing downstream toward its inevitable meeting with the Glanduin. Just to the north, the rocky mound rises up, making a large table-top formation. A large crack has opened in the rock face, and water running through it has carved a fair sized niche out of it.
14710: Just east of the Hollin Road, this path is little more than a dirty, matted-down grass trail. Used by travellers as a quick way to the edge of the river, the track also leads around the side of the rocks unseen from the main road. Not terribly high, only about twenty feet, the jutting rock looks plain and made of granite. A few sparkles glinting off its surface make you wonder if it contains any mithril, the precious silver metal mined by Dwarves.
14711: You are in the forest of East Eregion. Many elm trees tower above your head, blocking out the light. Although there is no underbrush, it is still very hard to travel because of the huge, twisted roots of the elm trees. East the forested hills are interupted by a strip of earth, the Hollin Road.
14712:
A woodpecker is here, tapping on a tree.
A tall stag is here, grazing peacefully.
A furry, striped raccoon is here, nosing around for some berries or roots.

You have reach the limit of the forest as it skirts a large mound of rock. This side of the rock-face is almost vertical, making climbing it unwise. There does however, seem to be a gentler slope up the far side of it. You hear the sound of water trickling to the west, though the rocks momentarily block your view of it. Eastwards the forest continues toward the Hollin Road in the distance.
14713:
A brown pond between old branches and roots is here.
A holly bush with dark green leaves is growing here.

Paralelling the dense forest to the east, this grassy hill runs north-south between rough mounts. Lush vegetation is all around you, made possible by both the fertile soil in the area, and also by the plentiful amount of water here. Animals are using the pool to bathe in, clean their food in, and to drink from. The hills to your west are inaccessible from here, as the decay of rocks forming the hillside have made unstable cliffs.
14714: A bright green holly bush is growing here.

You are walking in a most fertile hill. It passes between two higher ranges of hills, and winds down to meet the Hollin Road to the south. It goes further north as well, leading into northern Eregion and eventually into the lands of Rhudaur. A small stream is winding in tandem with the trail you are on, and gives the air a fresh smell as it tumbles along. The stream backs up in places, thanks to the industrious work of the local beavers. Their dams have created a series of pools along the stretch of the stream.
14715:
A forest spider is here crawling around.
A tree-snake lies wrapped around one of the tree branches.
A tree-snake lies wrapped around one of the tree branches.

This thinly wooded forest lies miles off the Hollin Road, which is located to both the south and east. More of the same terrain is to your north, leading into a thicker woodland. The ground is soft due to the fallen leaves, and rustles softly under your feet. Holly bushes grow wherever they are given a chance, bright green in some places, darker in others. Rocks are scattered among the foliage, forcing you to either climb over them or go around.
14717: The forest is growing thick here, and is even denser to the east, where it is bathed by a river flowing from the mountains. You hear some birds singing, probably talking about the marvel of the past. Celebrimbor is gone, but the land did not forget him.
14718:
A tiny spider is here, eating a tiny bug.
A squirrel scampers around here, looking for nuts from the trees.

You are in a forested hill, three miles west of the tallest hill in the area. As you get closer to the hill, you see that fallen trees cover the hill side. A storm has recently hit the mound, destroying the vegetation in its path. From the top of that hill you will have the opportunity to examine the whole area.
14719:
A holly bush with dark green leaves is growing here.
A large marmot is here, scurrying in between the rocks.

After the easy climb up from the niche, you find yourself atop a flat plateau of solid rock. Though not very high, the view of surrounding lands is incredible. Almost every aspect of Eregion presents itself to you from this vantage point. Below you to the south and east, the riverbed and the Hollin Road wind in tandem to destinations afar. The north contains holly covered hills and orchards, along with thick forests that wind eastward.
14720: Not big enough to be considered a full-fledged cave, this niche is only about three feet wide and is enclosed by a small overhang from the top of the pile. One side of the crevice makes for easy access to the peak of the rocks summit. Just to the south is a grassy area off the side of the riverbed. The surface of the rock around you is unremarkable, only growing a thin stringy moss called lichen.
14721:
A swarm of mosquitoes is here, humming around you.
A green frog is here, hopping around.

The river is not flowing with any significant volume, you can see from the marks on the banks that it has been much greater in earlier times. Around the river grow many Holly trees, giving the ancient Sindarin name to this region, Hollin. Now it is called Eregion, and is still a peaceful, comfortable land, in strong contrast to the looming Hithaeglir, The Misty Mountains.
14722:
A bright green holly bush is growing here.
Partly covered by the bush's green leaves, there are some hollyberries.

Lush indeed are these hills, supported by the endless supply of water from the large amounts of rainfall which grace this land with its kiss of life. All of the local terrain looks much the same, in fact, and everything seems full of floral life. Oddly enough however, there is an absolute silence in these parts, although you can plainly see a variety of wildlife that you would expect to make more noise.
14723: Lush indeed are these hills, supported by the endless supply of water from the large amounts of rainfall which grace this land with its kiss of life. All of the local terrain looks much the same, in fact, and everything seems full of floral life. Oddly enough however, there is an absolute silence in these parts, although you can plainly see a variety of wildlife that you would expect to make more noise.
14724: You are travelling among lower hills in an area called Eregion. The lands have become greener and warmer. Far in the west you see some vast plains, while the misty mountains block your view to the east. To the north and the south you see a region of heavy foliage block your way.
14725: The ground has mostly dried up, but there are still a few bog plants left growing here. To the west the ground becomes much firmer and the land rises. East the mountain begins.
14726: This section is quite well intact. The trail looks as though it has been built by professionals with a high standard of work. Perhaps the Dwarves or Elves of old are responsible for it. It is known that there were ancient trading routes which passed this way.
14727: You struggle past the nasty knee-high bracken and occasionally stumble over the boulders that it conceals. Cursing every single painful step you might begin to wonder what you are doing in this cold, inhospitable place.
14728: The trail is level and contours round slightly to the south. With each mile it turns southward the shadow of Caradhras slowly retreats and the true size of Celebdil is noticed.
14729:
A small flower grows here, with a purple bloom and wide leaves.
A small flower grows here, with a purple bloom and wide leaves.

You are shadowed by the towering peaks of Caradhras and Celebdil. The trail looks as though in the past a great deal of work has been put into it. But now the stones and boulders that once made a smooth travelling surface have been ripped up and are difficult to negotiate. The wind howls through the valley as if accelerated somehow by the forces of the mountains.
14730:
A large marmot is here, scurrying in between the rocks.
A mountain goat is here, jumping from cliff to cliff.
A mountain goat is here, jumping from cliff to cliff.

You are travelling along a region of very rough high ground. Everything else in this area is the same. There are just hills, outcrops and more countryside. A shrill chatter breaks the monotony from time to time, making you wonder what caused it. Looking around the clumps of rock, you see a small mammal about the size of a beaver. It seems to like darting among the rocks, calling its unique cry.
14731: You are climbing along a ledge high up on one of the cliff faces of a peak. On your west side there is a large rock face. Looking down over the east side of the ledge you see the Great Walls of Moria. The drop is vast and the walls look very spectacular from this angle. Far below you there have been many ancient battles fought over the Gates of Moria and many brave warriors have died.
14732: The climb takes a sharp turn south and west and becomes very exposed. The plant life is getting less and less the higher you climb. The ridge looks like it may have been travelled recently.
14733: You are at the start of a long steep ridge. The footing is good and the plant life is interspersed with patches of rocks. It would be to your advantage not to stray from the path as the drops either side might be hazardous for your health.
14734: This is the highest point in this area. You have a clear view of the three highest mountains in this range. Celebdil is the closest and lies to your east. It is overshadowed by the mighty Caradhras to its north. To your north-east you can see the mighty Redhorn Valley climbing up over Caradhras.
14735: This is a tricky little bit to negotiate. You have to climb down a few feet past a small outcrop then traverse along a ridge with a scary drop below. Let's face it though you are probably used to the mountains by now.
14736:
A big, nasty vulture is sitting here, protecting its nest.
A big, nasty vulture is sitting here, protecting its nest.
A mountain goat is here, jumping from cliff to cliff.
A mountain goat is here, jumping from cliff to cliff.

You are on the east side of the mountain and as far as you can see there is scree. In the wet scree such as this could be trecherous. The summit of the mountain is to your west. The rest of Celebdil can be seen to the east where on the summit a tower stands.
14737: This narrow ledge has a dizzying view of the cirque to the north. The valley contains a dark lake that almost totally fills the bottom of the bowl-shaped area. To the west the ledge quickly peters out, but to the south it is possible to maneuver among the rocky formations.
14738: To the north, this narrow trail descends to a relatively wide ledge over- looking a bowl-shaped valley. The valley below contains a dark lake - only a narrow stretch of land along the northern edge allows access to the head of the valley. To the south, the trail climbs upward to the crest of a ridge, while to the west a narrow ledge clings to the cliff wall.
14739: A mountain goat is here, jumping from cliff to cliff.

It is not unusual to find goats this high up in the mountains and you can follow the muddy goats trail around the back of the pinnacle. The trail is still climbing high onto the back of Celebdil. There is snow on the ground.
14740: To the north-east there is a large stack of rock extending to the sky for several hundreds of feet. There is no way over it, you will have to go around one way or the other.
14741: You sense the water is deep, with something sinister lurking below. Every now and then a few bubbles will cause dark ripples on the otherwise still surface of the water. The stone cliffs tower high above you and look as featureless as ever. To your east you can see where a trail has been drowned as the lake emerges. It leads straight into the walls. You are veiled by the eerie shadow of Celebdil.
14742: You are at the south end of a festering lake. The water is thick and stagnant which also makes it very smelly. All around you is barred with mountains except to the north. You cannot tell how far the lake extends. You are veiled by the eerie shadow of Celebdil.
14743: A narrow, grey boat has been left here.

You are at the south end of a long festering lake. The water is dark and smells evil. You cannot see the southern edge of the lake, but to your east you can see some tall grey-stone cliffs. In the north a clean mountain river joins the lake but is soon swallowed up into the blackness. You are veiled by the eerie shadow of Celebdil.
14852:
A woodpecker is here, tapping on a tree.
A woodpecker is here, tapping on a tree.

Miles west of the Hollin Road, this thin forest is green and spacious. Thicker woodlands lie to the north, the dense trees dwarfing the ones on this rocky slope. Holly grows abundantly, as it does in many areas of Eregion. To the north-east a ways, the hills rise steeper and less woody. To the south-east, you can see the riverbed of the Sirannon cutting across the land. Though the hills are rocky and close to the road, animals still roam leisurely searching for food.
14853:
A bright green holly bush is growing here.
Partly covered by the bush's green leaves, there are some hollyberries.
A woodpecker is here, tapping on a tree.
A squirrel scampers around here, looking for nuts from the trees.
A sparrow is flapping around on the ground.

On the edge of a large forest that stretches northwards, you look around for possible danger. As the trees do not grow chokingly thick, you can see that the forest is quiet and peaceful, though one can never be instantly aware of hidden danger. Various types of trees grow in the woods, and they are complemented by a large number of holly bushes and other plants. To the south-east, the Hollin Road winds alongside the riverbed of the Sirannon as it cuts east-west across Eregion.
14854:
A holly bush with dark green leaves is growing here.
Partly covered by the bush's green leaves, there are a few inkberries.
A restless rabbit bounces around.
A squirrel scampers around here, looking for nuts from the trees.

Standing in a small clearing, you are surrounded by trees of pine, fir, and aspen. The ground you are standing on is carpeted by a thick layer of fallen pine needles and leaves, making travelling here easy on the feet of both mount and foot traveller. Looking around for landmarks, you spy holly covered hills to your north-east, and more of this forest continuing to the south. Just to your east however, there is something strange about the woods. They seem to be hiding a wood-walled dwelling beneath their thick boughs.
14855: A bright green holly bush is growing here.

The trees in this forest are large and healthy. Adequate water and space make for an ideal growth environment. The trees in turn provide nourishment and shelter to the local animal population. Squirrels find the pine cones a tasty treat, and the deer nibble on the ends of green boughs. On the sides of some of the larger trees, you see spots where more mature deer have rubbed the bark with their antlers, trying to rid them of the annual velvet-like covering.
14856:
A bright green holly bush is growing here.
Partly covered by the bush's green leaves, there are some hollyberries.
A holly bush with dark green leaves is growing here.
Partly covered by the bush's green leaves, there are a few inkberries.

Covering the ground almost as a carpet, the bushes of holly grow thick and plentiful. Dotted with berries of red and purple, the name Hollin seems appropriate. The name was given to the area by the men of Eriador, but the elves of Ost-in-Edhil call the land Eregion. Grass attempts to grow in patches where the holly is lacking, and chunks of broken rock complete the terrain. The air is clear and cool, with only a slight breeze blowing.
14857: The moderately flat ground of this area is completely overgrown by holly - both squat bushes and larger trees. Their red berries stand in stark contrast against the bright green background of the thick waxy leaves. Many species of birds and small mammals live amongst the thorny leaves.
14858:
A holly bush with dark green leaves is growing here.
Partly covered by the bush's green leaves, there are a few inkberries.
A bright green holly bush is growing here.
Partly covered by the bush's green leaves, there are some hollyberries.
A tall stag is here, grazing peacefully.
A grey wolf is here, snarling aggressively.
A grey wolf is here, snarling aggressively.

The field you are standing in is almost choked with bushes of holly. As thick as it grows here, it is no wonder the men of Eriador called the place Hollin. The bushes grow bright green all year long, as it is designed to withstand very low temperature. The bushes are dotted with shiny red berries that look like a nice snack. Birds chirp in happy harmony around you and seem unperturbed by your presence.
14859: A tiny spider is here, eating a tiny bug.

Under the relatively large overhang, you find the place makes a good windbreak and heat trap. Nothing but thin moss is growing in this niche of rock, making it free of the annoying pricks of the holly leaves. There are remains of an old campfire here, evidence that someone else has used this shelter before. On the ground you notice sheets of spider webs, as if they go directly down into the rocks. You wonder why they did not use the walls to build a web. Perhaps it is their way of conserving heat.
14860:
A diamondback rattlesnake is coiled here, ready to strike.
A diamondback rattlesnake is coiled here, ready to strike.
A grey spider is stalking here, preparing to drain you of life.

Deep down inside the hill, away from the lights and sounds you are accustomed to, the spiders have existed for ages. Feasting on wandering bugs they bide their time. Waiting for a warm-blooded animal such as yourself to come into the lair. Bones on the floor are your first clue as evidence of these spiders tenacity. The next thing you notice, which gives an origin to the bones, is the various pieces of discarded equipment on the floor. As the beasts have no use for such devices, they must have come from wandering adventurers like you.
14861:
A huge, poisonous spider is here.
A huge, poisonous spider is here.
A newborn spider is here.

As you come to another wall of the cave, you are dismayed to find that the only exit is back the way you came. Groping through the amalgam of webs and corpses is not what you wanted to do. In a corner of the room, there is a stack of corpses, apparently drained of their blood as food for the resident spiders. Poking at the pile, you feel little resistance. Perhaps the spiders ate the bones and flesh as well.
14862:
A huge, poisonous spider is here.
A huge, poisonous spider is here.
A brown snake watches you.

You hack, push, and flail at the dense tangle of webs. Trying to get through all of them is indeed a chore. It must have taken dozens of spiders to construct all of the silky fibers. Among the strands are the now-familiar corpses that are woven into the webs. Looking like small sacks of flour, they bump into your face as you move by. Feasting on such things does not appeal to you at all.
14863:
A huge, poisonous spider is here.
A large, dangerous-looking green snake is coiled up here.
A brown snake watches you.
A black snake hurries towards you with sly intentions.

This pit is filled with bugs ans snakes; it must be one of the few dry, out of the way places around here, as so many things have come in to get out of the open. Small snakes slither around in the dust, while higher up, spiders of all sizes have made their webs.
14864:
A huge, poisonous spider is here.
A huge, poisonous spider is here.

As you push through the web covering, darkness embraces you. Even with a light source, the inky blackness seems overwhelming.
