Webs brush against your face, interspersed with soft objects that you assume to be web-enshrouded corpses of the resident spider's victims. Small clicking sounds can be heard from not too far away. The smell can only be described as stifling, as the odour is most unpleasant. By the dim glow of light here, you see the small cavern continuing to the east.
14865: Sloping slightly upward, the wide range of low hills abandons the dense holly groves. The terrain here is more rocky, and piles of stacked boulders lie here and there. From the hillside, you have a great view of the vast expanse of Eregion. Fields of holly lie close at the foot of the hills, while further away to the west, there are more heavily forested areas. Looking north, you see a rock overhang jutting out, and at first glimpse it looks like a good temporary shelter.
14866:
The corpse of a hunter is lying here.
A holly bush with dark green leaves is growing here.
A tall and strong hunter is standing here.
A tall stag is here, grazing peacefully.
A grey wolf is here, snarling aggressively.

The forests of Eregion grow fertile and thick. Containing a rich diversity of plants and animal life, the area is in a most stable existence. Trees of pine and aspen type are the most numerous, but scatterings of fir complement the place nicely. Vegetation other than tree-type is mostly limited to the familiar holly bush, though ferns and other ground plants grow in places. Thick tree boughs shade the territory, making the atmosphere dusky, yet not gloomy. Small hills arise to the north, where the trees thin considerably.
14867:
A bright green holly bush is growing here.
A woodpecker is here, tapping on a tree.

At the base of a small hill range, this forest is roomy and fertile. Trees of various species flourish in abundance; while lower to the ground, holly grows thick and strong. The floor of the area is scattered with rocks from the adjoining hills to your east. Some of the rocks are large, while others are mere stones. Peering through the forest to the south, you see what looks like logs stacked up neatly. Resembling a wall of some sorts, you wonder if there is actually someone living around here.
14868: A squirrel scampers around here, looking for nuts from the trees.

In an apparent area of transition, these small hills join thick forest on the west, with rolling hills on the east. The trees are spaced apart widely, barely giving the place shade during the day. Holly grows abundantly around the trees, its green leaves spattered with the red berries common to it. Animals find this a nice place to roam, and are seemingly unconcerned with your presence. To the north lie impassable cliffs jutting upward.
14869:
A holly bush with dark green leaves is growing here.
Partly covered by the bush's green leaves, there are a few inkberries.
A fat rabbit is here, chewing on some grass.

Not yet able to descend onto the small track down to the east, you look out across the valley that the trail runs through. Being relatively flat, the valley is a wetland, yet drains enough to avoid swampiness. Animals are there, taking in their daily requirement of water before moving along in the endless search for food. The rocky hills you are in border a large and thick forest to the west. Through the woods to the northwest, high hills rise up, looking very rocky and lacking the rich growth found here.
14870: In this section of the hill range, the ground to your east has completely crumbled, leaving a gentle slope leading down to the track below. Following a small stream, the trail runs north-south in direction. On other sides, the hills continue. More of the same geography lies northwards, while on the west, much larger hills rise up. These larger hills are composed of broken slabs of rock, and coarse gravel. Passage up the steep west slope is impossible, as an unstable cliff has formed.
14871: The hills here are rock strewn and relatively barren when compared to the rich growth of the forests. So many shards of rock and loose boulders litter the area that it is easy to get your foot caught in the spaces between them. The rocks come from above, by way of a steep slope to your west. In times of rain or high winds, unstable rocks break free and tumble down. Since the rock face is so unpredictable, you would be wise not to attempt a climb in this direction. Safer passages of travel lie to your north and south.
14872:
A holly bush with dark green leaves is growing here.
Partly covered by the bush's green leaves, there are a few inkberries.
A bright green holly bush is growing here.
Partly covered by the bush's green leaves, there are some hollyberries.

This slope in the hills faces to the east, catching the morning sun. The holly on this hillside grows well in these conditions. Boulders and broken rock still adorn the area, but the resilient holly bushes have managed to crop up wherever they can. Taking in the view, you see a small stream in the valley below, winding its way southward towards the Sirannon. A small path follows the stream, leading to an unknown destination.
14873: Just to the west is a large cliff, to the north is a range of quiet looking hills. The hills in the north are covered with thick growing holly bushes, but not choked like the more dense regions of Eriador. To the south, the old road continues towards Ost-in-Edhil. Many Elves and Dwarves once used this route in the days of peace. The riverbed of the Sirannon is slowly vanishing in the south-east.
14874:
A bright green holly bush is growing here.
Partly covered by the bush's green leaves, there are some hollyberries.

Separated from the riverbed here, the road winds northwards a bit, skirting a large rock formation to your south. Westwards the Redhorn Way continues into the heart of Eregion, past more holly covered hills and plains. Animals scurry about in abundance, looking just for the daily food and water they require. Far in the east you see the towering peaks of the Hithaeglir, tall and forbidding.
14875:
A bright green holly bush is growing here.
Partly covered by the bush's green leaves, there are some hollyberries.

Still skirting the large rock formation, the road bends from north to west here. The woodlands to the north are rich with wildlife. This land was once trekked across by many hundreds of Elves and Dwarves, yet little evidence of their existence remains. The lands seem undisturbed, yet history tells of when Sauron and his armies razed this place to the ground.
14876:
A bright green holly bush is growing here.
Partly covered by the bush's green leaves, there are some hollyberries.

The Road to Moria bends yet again, this time leading either south or east. The large rock mound is to your southeast, standing tall and unyielding. Just northwards, you can enter some of Eregion's flat-lands. Holly-filled and fertile, this area seems unspoiled. Animals engaged in their instinctive behaviours seem unmoved by your presence. Due mainly to the fact that in comparison to the days when Elves and Dwarves travelled this route in large numbers, recent travel has been light.
14877: Just west of the Hollin Road, your walk takes you through some muddy ground. The wet ground results from the many small streams flowing at the foot of the mountains, originating as snow-melt from the tall peaks of the Hithaeglir in the east. In all directions other than the road, the trees seem to grow together to form an thick green wall. Westwards the forest continues, and leads toward some small hills.
14878: These hills are covered by a dense forest which slow your walk. The trunks and branches have become tangled over the years, hopelessly difficult to separate them again. Many strange plants cover the ground, growing particularly tall in the shadow of the odd walls created by the higher trees.
14880:
A fallow deer is grazing peacefully here.
A restless rabbit bounces around.
A fallow deer is grazing peacefully here.

Rising above the road to the south, these hills are green and fertile, like most other parts of Eregion. Passing through the many trees and plants, along with the many species of animals, it is hard to believe that this land was once laid to total waste by the dark forces. Looking beyond the road, you see the semi-deep channel of the riverbed, winding east-west towards far away lands. Northwards, breakups of the rock have caused the formation of small cliffs. Though not extremely high, it is too unstable to safely negotiate.
14881:
A low, many-branched shrub covers the ground here.
A bright green holly bush is growing here.
A brown fox is here, looking for some rabbits to chew up.
A sparrow is flapping around on the ground.
A squirrel scampers around here, looking for nuts from the trees.

A long wooden building stretches before you to the east. Rectangular in shape, the brown log structure looks very old. The mortar in the cracks between logs is all but vanished. Only the solid construction from which it was made has saved it from becoming splinters of timber. Examining the logs, you see that they are remarkably strong despite the ancient design. The forest around you grows thick, providing a natural camouflage for the ruined lodge. It would take much effort to detect this place from most anywhere besides right in front of it.
14882:
A holly bush with dark green leaves is growing here.
Partly covered by the bush's green leaves, there are a few inkberries.

Thinning here, the trees still grow in large numbers, but more spacious as a result of the rocky terrain. Large clumps of boulders litter the ground, having fallen from a slope north-east of here. Looking towards the hills, you see that they incline gently and are growing thick with bushes of holly. More directly north lie some flat-lands of Eregion, adorned with holly and an occasional flower. To the south however, the forest thickens, and you discern a log dwelling hidden in the trees.
14883:
A holly bush with dark green leaves is growing here.
Partly covered by the bush's green leaves, there are a few inkberries.
A bright green holly bush is growing here.
Partly covered by the bush's green leaves, there are some hollyberries.
A fallow deer is grazing peacefully here.
A tall stag is here, grazing peacefully.

The holly grows thick here, its bright green leaves contrasting with the dark fertile earth it grows in. Piles of rock adorn the area, obviously falling down the slopes of the hills just east of you. Small spiders crawl over the leaves, some carrying whole berries as testimony to their huge proportionate strength. The air is clean here, and the gurgle of a small stream catches your ear.
14884: A fat rabbit sits here, chewing on some grass.

Still above the Hollin Road below, you cannot make it directly down because of the unstable cliffs. In the north, the hills seem to become less steep, perhaps opening a way for you to get down. Not heavily forested here, the main plant life seems to be the holly bush, giving more evidence as to why the men of Eriador called the region "Hollin".
14885: A woodpecker is here, tapping on a tree.

The hills you are in are relatively small compared to the massive peaks of the Misty Mountains in the east, but are high enough to provide a good view of the land. Geologic shifts have caused the rocks to break to your east, forming unstable cliffs. Looking down the cliffs to the east you see the Hollin Road below and the riverbed of the Sirannon further in the east. Rocks dot the hills, and holly grows wherever it can. To your north and west are more hills of this type, with rich woodlands beyond. To the south it is possible to reach the Hollin Road.
14886:
A bright red mushroom is growing here.
A beautiful and docile horse is standing here.
A grey wolf is here, snarling aggressively.

This particular section of forest has grown incredibly dense. On your east, the Redhorn Way runs east-west through the area. Originating at the massive west gate of Moria, it runs westwards toward the ruined city of Ost-in-Edhil, and beyond that, Tharbad. Around you are more forested hills, except to the north where a pile of boulders has found a place to accrue. Faint lines are evident in one of the large rocks, but you cannot find a way to open it no matter how hard you try.
14887: Just off the Road to Moria, or Hollin Road as it is called, these hills overlook a rich forest to the north. You can hear birds chirping happily, and larger animals foraging for food among the woods. Almost directly below you, at the base of some cliffs, is what appears to be an abandoned wooden dwelling of some sort. Though not able to traverse the unstable cliffs, the woodlands that lie further westward look passable. Further south, past the road, is the riverbed of the Sirannon, leading towards Ost-in-Edhil, the ruined city of the Noldor.
14888:
A bright green holly bush is growing here.
Partly covered by the bush's green leaves, there are some hollyberries.

You stand on a low hill, which has been pierced by the former Sirannon. A vertical slope leads east down the dry stream. The cliff is not extremely high, and a few bushes are growing, in its side. To the west the grassy slope of the hill leads to the Hollin Road, where many merchants were walking four thousands years ago but which is now deserted and covered by a thick layer of grass and bushes.
14889:
A brook trout is here, swimming in the current.
A brook trout is here, swimming in the current.

On and on the dried, cracked ground of the shallow bed continues. The absence of the stream is really the only flaw you can find, as you look around at the lovely Hollinish landscape. All of the flora greets your eye with vibrant colour, except for a few dead plants in and around the perished waterway.
14892:
A brown fox is here, looking for some rabbits to chew up.
A brown fox is here, looking for some rabbits to chew up.

You are in a wide clearing, at the junction of two paths. Running east- west is the legendary Hollin Road, traversing the vast expanses of Eregion. The road leads from the once-great kingdom of Ost-in-Edhil, to the mighty gates of Moria. The smaller track to the north is of unknown name, but seems to follow a small stream coming from that direction. The trees at the border of the clearing are surrounded by holly, a familiar plant of Eregion.
14893: The bridge is made of stone, and is well crafted. Peeling away the moss layer that covers it, you can hardly detect the intersection of stones. Judging this to be Dwarven work, you think about the mines of Moria, and the evils that lurk there now. The purpose of the bridge is to negotiate travel over a small stream that merges with the River Sirannon. The large river flows just to the south, as the small stream winds in from the north.
14894: Going east and west here, the track takes you through some muddy ground. The wet ground results from the meeting of the river and a small stream just west of here. At the junction, a small bridge of good construction makes the way easily passable. The larger river being the famed River Sirannon, and the smaller stream most likely just snow-melt from the high mountain peaks to the east. Looking up the small stream, you see a rugged track following its course.
14895: Winding ever-onwards towards the peaks of the Hithaeglir, the road is rough and rocky. The track continues to the west, leading into more of the same terrain and eventually to where Ost-in-Edhil once stood. Looking eastwards, you wonder if this path was used by Galadriel in her flight to Moria. Around you stretches vast Eregion, fertile and green.
14896: The Hollin Road bends from north to west here, connecting the foothills of the Misty Mountains to the plains of Eregion. Westward lies a land of holly-covered hills, while across the shrunken Sirannon to the east, the becomes more severe as the mountains approach.
14897: A huge warg is here, moving in for the kill.

This ancient road bends from east to south here. Westward the land becomes much gentler as the mountains become more distant. To the north, a deep valley has been scooped out of the surrounding land - it looks to be almost choked with vegetation.
14898:
A huge warg is here, moving in for the kill.
A huge warg is here, moving in for the kill.

This road was once a monument to the friendship between the dwarves of Moria and the Noldor of Eregion, but over the millenia since Sauron overran Eriador, the road has fallen into a state of great disrepair. Even though the dwarves lived in Khazad-dum for centuries after the elves left Hollin, the west gate of Moria was kept shut, leaving the quiet lands of Hollin to the beasts and birds.
14899: The Hollin road continues east and west, following the path of the shrunken Sirannon. The Hollin road is here joined by another equally ancient road, leading from the empty lands to the north. East of here lies the valley from whence the Sirannon originates - presumably the Gates of Durin lie at its head.
14900:
A huge warg is here, moving in for the kill.
A huge warg is here, moving in for the kill.

This ancient road is in great disrepair - it has seen little traffic in the thousands of years since Sauron drove the Noldor from Eregion. Little remains of the precisely fitted pavement - the frequent frosts and thaws of the region wave wreaked havoc with the stone, slowly wearing it away into dust. To the south, the road meets another ancient thoroughfare.
14901: The road is cut here by a swift-flowing stream. On either bank can be seen the crumbling remnants of a stone bridge that long ago collapsed. The stream is shallow enough that the debris from the old bridge protrudes from the water, forming a series of stepping stones. To the south, the stream joins a tiny trickle of water that flows out of the valley to the east -- judging from the size of the streambed, something farther up in the valley must have staunched the flow of water.
14902: The road continues to parallel the Sirannon to the south, leading down from the mountains to the east out into the hills of Eregion to the west. To the north, a large ridge rises abruptly, blocking the land to the north from view. To the west, the remnants of an ancient stone bridge form a series of stepping stones across a mountain stream that flows in from the north, adding its water to the trickle of the Sirannon.
14903: The ancient road is dampened by a small waterfall that flows from the top of the steep slope to the north. The water cascades down in a narrow stream, and then flows across the remnants of the road into the streambed of the Sirranon to the south. Eastward, the road parallels the Sirannon, leading farther into the vee-shaped valley.
14904: Sharp Bend in the Hollin Road
A beautiful and docile horse is standing here.

The road bends sharply from west to south here, passing between the streambed of the Sirannon and the steep valley wall. The Sirannon has been reduced to a trickle - in many places barely enough to dampen the rocks. The valley continues a good distance to the southeast, and at its head the ancient Gates of Moria should be found.
14905: The road follows the course where the Sirannon once flowed. The land rises steeply to the east, and the road climbs through a series of loops to the level of the top of the Stair Falls, which once merrily cascaded down a rock cliff to the southeast. The Sirannon is almost non-existent, so it is safe to walk out to the foot of the falls.
14906: The Hollin Road to the west descends in a series of loops to the level of the lower valley floor. To the south, it approaches the area around the top of the Stair Falls, and the presumably continues onward towards Durin's Gate. The road here is littered with debris that has washed down from the steep ridge to the north over the long years, but it is still in fairly good shape after long centuries of neglect.
14907:
A ferocious warg is here, snarling angrily.
A ferocious warg is here, snarling angrily.
A ferocious warg is here, snarling angrily.

The ancient stones of the Hollin Road march into the depths of the dark lake to the south - the water has risen to cover it completely. A narrow strip of dry land hugs the northern shore of the lake, nestled between the dark water and the steep cliffs of the northern edge of the valley. It appears that the dry land continues for quite awhile - perhaps even to the grey cliffs of the Walls of Moria.
14908:
A huge warg is here, moving in for the kill.
A huge warg is here, moving in for the kill.

Little remains of this ancient road - only occasional stretches where the climate has spared the pavement indicate that this was once more than a simple trail through the foothills of the Misty Mountains. To the east flows a babbling mountain stream, and to the west the land drops sharply into a deep valley - the slope is too steep to negotiate from here.
14909: A stream passes alongside the road to the east, continuing to the south out of sight. The road is decrepit - often there are great stretches where nothing except a few flat stones indicates its course. To the southeast, the great peak of Celebdil dominates the horizon.
14910: A stream passes alongside the road to the east, continuing to the south out of sight; it seems to depart from the road and choose its own path across the land the the northeast. The road itself does not seem well maintained, or well travelled; instead it seems abandoned and forgotten.
14911: The mere existence of this road is testimony that at one time this area was inhabited, at least enough to have two places to travel between. However, its current state seems to deny the idea that anybody dwells here now. The road continues its lonely journey to the north and south.
14912: While barren and rough, with few details to distract the eye, this area does possess a form of beauty, with its broken stones and untilled soil; some might see the elegance of the undisturbed lands of Arda, while others see an area with unlimited potential. The road crossing this place continues to the north and south.
14913: A Bend in the Ancient Road

Making an easy bend to the west and south, this road continues its long trek across these plains. At one time this road may have been paved, and might have been well kept by careful hands, but now it is little more than a blemish on the land; remaining visible only because its soil has been packed too much to let plants take root.
14914: A Bend in the Ancient Road

With no trees near the road to offer shade, the ground is brutally scorched between dawn and dusk when the skies are clear; pools of water vanish quickly, and all but the most stubborn grasses wither and die in the heat. It seems apparent why the land is so abandoned; there is little here for grazing or farming, so even a simple town would find life here difficult.
14915: Easily traversing the flat plains that surround it, this road maintains its simple course from north to south. Winds blow easily through this area, with little to hamper them; rains fall hard on the ground with few plants to lessen the blow. Indeed this place shows the damage done by natural forces, in the form of weathered stone and trenches formed by escaping water.
14916: This road is little more than a thin thread passing across vast lands that remain somewhat barren and uninhabited. Plains stretch out from either side of the road, while mountain peaks dominate the horizon beyond. The road follows a simple path to the north and south.
14917: Seldom used and even less maintained, this ancient road is little more than an interruption of the plains and mountains nearby. Alternately covered with a thin layer of dirt and washed clean by unhindered winds and rain, the surface of this road is constantly in a state of transition.
14918: Continuing easily to the north and south, the road begins to climb into the mountains to the north. Rivulets have formed in and alongside the road, allowing rains and melting snow to flow to lower ground, while scoring and eating away at the road.
14919: Loose boulders lie scattered across the road, fallen from the unstable slopes above. Broken shards of rock have gathered in piles, where they came to rest; shifting at times as the forces on them change. The road continues to the north and south between two mountain peaks, ignoring the stones that may eventually bury it.
14922:
A giant, mean looking earth beetle is standing here.
A giant, mean looking earth beetle is standing here.

The slopes of these hills are loose and rocky; there is little vegetation to hold the soil in place, so the ground is always shifting and sliding. An old road passes around from the east to the north through the otherwise uninterrupted terrain.
14923: This hill forms the western extreme of a narrow valley that passes just below it; a small, rubble covered road struggles its way through that valley as it presses north into the mountains. To the south lies a flat and featureless plain that follows the road out of sight.
14924:
The starving cow stands here looking for a patch of grass.
A squirrel scampers around here, looking for nuts from the trees.

As the mountains nearby flatten and spread into these plains, an old road passes just to the east on its lonely journey from north to south. The road itself has seen little use in recent years, as these plains begin to engulf and erase it.
14925: The starving cow stands here looking for a patch of grass.

Perhaps once covered by lush, green grasses, or leafy trees planted to offer shade to those travelling the weathered road to the east, this place is now barren and lifeless. A dry wind constantly washes over the land, free to wander in any direction, while all signs that this place was once travelled continue to fade.
14926:
The starving cow stands here looking for a patch of grass.
The wild ox seems ready to charge you.
The only things passing across the dark and hard soil is a forgotten road that crosses to the east, and the winds that find no leaves to caress or water to stir.
14927: Judging by the road to the east, this area was once populated, and supported enough trade to justify building such a road; perhaps once this land was used for crops or grazing livestock. All that lies here now is dirt, dust, wind, and stiff brown grasses which have buried any history that may have once been here.
14928: Flat and uninhabited plains spread around this place, with little standing between here and the great mountain ranges to the east and northeast. The soil is dark and nearly lifeless, too poor to support leafy plants, while a constant wind sweeps past.
14929:
A small brown snake is slithering around here.
The starving cow stands here looking for a patch of grass.
The wild ox seems ready to charge you.

Small holes are scattered across the ground here, many continuing into dark tunnels that lead an unknown distance into the ground. Perhaps the only shelter an animal might have here from predators or the elements, many have collapsed either partially or completely, but many more seem to be intact.
14930:
The wild ox seems ready to charge you.
A giant earth beetle is standing here.

Short, dry grasses have managed to grow in this infertile soil despite the harsh climate and lack of a reliable source of water. Otherwise devoid of vegetation, the surrounding plains offer little to distract the eye or hold one's attention.
14931: The ground is damp beneath the heather, as water does not appear to drain from this bowl scooped out of the foothills. To the west, the land rises to form a plateau, while to the south the valley continues. East of here is a gully - dry now, but surely filled with torrents of water after a heavy rain.
14932: This deep valley is choked with low vegetation. There seems to be no place for water to drain - it collects in the valley like a bowl. To the south, the valley wall can be climbed, leading up to relatively flat land. To the west lies a land of rocky hills, while north and east the valley continues.
14933: There are two woody, stemmed plants here.
You are in a valley with knee high heather. There are no real paths only narrow trails trodden in by local wild life.You are not sure what could be lurking below the heather ready to trap you.
14934: The gully walls are cut very steep and are made from a crumbly reddish rock - it would be impossible to climb out from here. To the west, the gully opens into an area of dense foliage, while to the north the gully narrows considerably, forming a dark area in which nothing can be seen.
14935: A huge stone troll looms overhead, ready to crush your body.

The rock up above is overhanging so much that it almost forms a cave. The sunlight can only penetrate a slight north-south crack. There is no other way to go except the way you came. This would be the perfect spot for an ambush.
14936:
A black crow flies low to the ground here, looking for carrion to eat.
A black crow flies low to the ground here, looking for carrion to eat.
A black crow flies low to the ground here, looking for carrion to eat.

Long distances of plains accented by even more distant mountains lie to the north, and a road just east of here works its way across the plains to the south and north. Farther to the east, more mountains arise from the ground, and block the view of anything beyond.
14937: A pack horse (Rood) is standing here, ridden by you.

As it follows an old roadway that cuts across the area to the east, these plains are nearly as flat and solid as the surface of that road. The ground has been stripped away by winds, leaving only patches of prickly grasses to hide an occasional rodent or reptile.
14938:
An arrow lies on the ground.
The starving cow stands here looking for a patch of grass.
A black crow flies low to the ground here, looking for carrion to eat.
A ferocious warg is here, snarling angrily.

An old and weathered road makes a bend to the east and north, circumventing a small outcropping of rock that protrudes from the ground here. Worn nearly smooth by the elements, its surface is brittle and loose. By certain stains that mark it, it could be guessed that birds may find this a suitable perch.
14939: Entering into the cave, you are met by a blast of foetid air coming from the back of the cave, which lies straight north. The crevice is fairly large, as you can stand easily in its main cavern. Noticing the bones of animals small and large, you are convinced someone or something has made this place its home. The place is sheltered from the elements, making it a nice dry refuge. The sun cannot penetrate more than a few meters inside the cave, and thus is always dark.
14940: A large marmot is here, scurrying in between the rocks.

This relatively flat plateau sits atop a ridge of rolling hills. The hills differ from those across the valley to the west, in that they are much rockier. Thin grass covers the ground here, making it much softer and quieter to walk over. There is a scattering of trees about, but they are few and far from each other. The foliage of choice here is the holly bush, along with some hardy moss clinging to some of the rocks. The table of rock seems to extend deep into a cave to your north. You lift your nose and detect a bit of foul air from it.
14941: A large marmot is here, scurrying in between the rocks.

Rocky soil covers the ground here, not wanting to sustain the rich growth like other parts of the region. The slope is steep here, yet not dangerously so. The danger comes from the falling rocks around you. Several loose boulders about the size of a medium Dwarf lie close by. Careening down from the higher slopes above, the hillside is littered with rock shards. More of the same rocky slopes continue to the west, but dropping off soon after to form a valley. A short distance to the east, another valley can be seen among the hills.
14942: Small groves of trees complement this grassy slope. Looking south you catch a good view of the Hollin Road, the chief thoroughfare in Eregion. It winds east and west across the land, and connects Moria to the ruined Noldor city of Ost-in-Edhil. To the north, the trees and foliage give way to more harsh hills. Ones adorned with rocks of all sizes, along with steep slopes. Holly grows here also, as it does in much of the area, dotted with berries of red and purple.
14943: A fallow deer is grazing peacefully here.

Crossing into an area composed of thin woods and rolling hills, you seem to be in a transition zone. The Hollin Road lies to your south, just over a small ridge. The east holds some of the same thin woodlands scattered with mossy rock. At the northern base of this small slope, woods give way to much rockier hills, ones that appear far more steep as well. If you travel down to your west, you will be in a green valley with a stream running through it. In places, the stream backs up to form quiet pools.
14944: A green frog is here, hopping around.

Clear, shallow, and cool - the stream babbles its way southward toward the River Sirannon. The junction of the two waterways comes just to the south, past a small bridge built over the brook. Long ago, the much larger river would have whisked the smaller current away, towards another river in the west, the Glanduin. Now however, the little stream seems to dwarf the Sirannon, as the flow has been dammed up. Northwards towards the origin of the small stream, green plants and trees cover hillsides and fill orchards. Animal life is abundant all around, but signs of humanoid creatures are minimal.
14945: Narrower and rougher than the Hollin Road, this rugged earthen track is running north-south, parallelling a small stream to the east. It wanders past some holly covered hills typical of the area, and leads into the heart of Eregion. In the west a cliff is blocking the way into a hill covered countryside. To the south, the trail merges with the wider, more frequently used Road to Moria.
14946: Passing by a small gurgling brook, the narrow path you are on runs north-south here. Its destination is unclear for the moment, but up ahead you see a bend in the path. Perhaps that will offer you more clues. The stream is located just to the east of the path, and appears to be only run-off from the tall mountains to the far east. The stream backs up in places, thanks to the industrious work of the local beavers. Their dams have created a series of pools along the stretch of the stream. In the west is a broken cliff.
14947:
A beaver is sleeping here.
A brook trout is here, swimming in the current.
A beaver is sleeping here.

Dammed up by the work of industrious beavers, the stream forms a relatively large pool here. Not terribly deep, but too deep to wade, you can swim or boat easily in the quiet water. Past the dam to your south, the brook continues its course toward the river in the distance. Green hills and forest still border the valley, and the path to your west still parallels the water. Small fish swim around happily in the pond, nipping bugs off the waters surface.
14948: Rising up from the valley eastwards, these hills are rocky and less vegetated than their counterparts on the western side. The trees are lacking in the less-fertile soil, and the rock piles are much larger here. Holly still grows, as it is a hardy plant, able to take the unfavorable conditions. A small stream flows to your west, continuing down the valley in a north-south direction. The hills continue to rise eastwards, and you think you spy a cave of sorts to the north-east.
14949:
There is some snow on the ground.
A tall stag is here, grazing peacefully.
A tall stag is here, grazing peacefully.

Standing on a western facing slope, you overlook a series of beaver ponds in a lush green valley. The trek to the valley is easy, as the hills slope gently into it from here. The plentiful water there makes the vegetation thick and rich, unlike these hills which are rocky and contain little foliage. The hills are not barren however. Ferns and holly grow around the place in frequent clumps. To your south are more hills, getting thicker with trees and flora as you head that way. The rise of the slope stops a bit to your east where it has formed sort of a rocky plateau.
14950: A brook trout is here, swimming in the current.

Flowing gently over rocks and sand, the little brook winds snake-like through the valley you are in. Bordered by green hills and forest, the area is full of life in the form of rabbits, deer, and other local creatures. Looking into the deeper portions of the water, you see fish swimming peacefully toward a small pond to your south. The track beside the stream is still following faithfully on the west side of you. Far in the distance, you see a larger river cutting east-west across the land.
14951:
The bee flies around here, collecting nectar from the flowers.
The bee flies around here, collecting nectar from the flowers.

The track bends here, still following the small stream on your east. Occasional mosquito swarms brush against your face, due to the inevitable stagnation of a few pools of water cut off from the rest of the flow. Otherwise this area is quiet and peaceful, containing green grass growing almost knee-high in some places. Stands of woody bushes line the stream in places, but the trail is clear of these as it follows at a distance. You can continue on the trail by turning north-east, or you may climb up a small range of hills to your north.
14952:
A bright green holly bush is growing here.
A holly bush with dark green leaves is growing here.
A fallow deer is grazing peacefully here.

Sloping eastwards here, the hills merge together at a gap where the stream flows through. Since the slopes of the hills are a bit higher than the running water, a small waterfall has formed on your east. Running south-westwards from there, the little brook flows a great distance into Eregion. Alongside this stream, a narrow, rugged path follows faithfully. Looking down the length of the stream, you see pools where the flow is being obstructed. You are prevented from going north by cliffs of unstable rock, but can head south on the small trail.
14953:
A crayfish is here, snapping its claws at you.
A crayfish is here, snapping its claws at you.

A small creek of shallow water flows between this rocky terrain. The water is pretty cold, as it originates as snowmelt from beyond a ridge seen in the north. The creek is shallow enough to be easily waded by all beasts, and many animals here are doing just that. Deer, small mammals, and birds all take advantage of the clear water. Some bathing, others drinking, it makes a pretty sight. The stream bends to the south-west, and the small path with it.
14954:
A tall stag is here, grazing peacefully.
A brook trout is here, swimming in the current.

From a ridge, water splashes merrily down a small waterfall and forms a stream westwards. The mountain water looks very clear and fresh, and is cool, almost chilly to the touch. The ridge is not very tall, but it is steep and slippery, making it impossible to climb up on it. Westwards, the small stream runs on through the land of Eregion. A narrow track begins to follow the stream further west.
14955: Entering into the cave, you are met by a blast of foetid air coming from the back of the cave, which lies straight north. The crevice is fairly large, as you can stand easily in its main cavern. Noticing the bones of animals small and large, you are convinced someone or something has made this place its home. The place is sheltered from the elements, making it a nice dry refuge. The sun cannot penetrate more than a few meters inside the cave, and thus is always dark.
14956: Moving further into the cave, all remnants of sunlight have disappeared. As something brushes against your face, you hear the flap of wings and small screeches. Thinking that this is a perfect dwelling for bats, you surmise that they are sleeping in the daytime, waiting for night to come. A covering of bat-droppings carpet the floor, making you wonder if this is the source of the rank air you smelled earlier.
14957:
A large bat is here, hanging in the darkness.
A cavebear is sleeping here.

The back of the cave is definitely the source of the rancid smell you detected earlier. It is caused by numerous corpses of different animals in various stages of decay. Some have flesh still attached while others are bare to the bone. Shreds of clothing and rusted equipment dot the floor, testimony of the failure of others who have tried to conquer this savage beast. It may be out for a moment, but when it returns will you be another bone on the floor, or will you succeed in ridding Eregion of this menace?
14958: This high on the slopes of Celebdil, the world is encased in a permanent blanket of snow and ice. The air grows thinner and more difficult to breathe. Each step upward is more and more of an exertion, and the narrow trail still climbs above.
14959: The footing on this trail is treacherous, as the rocks are covered in a thin casing of ice. Only a few hardy lichens subsist on the occasional patches of exposed rocky soil, and even the mountain goats seem to shun this harsh area. The trail continues leading steadily upward, toward an unknown destination, while below it passes into a milder clime.
14960: High on the shoulder of a spur of Celebdil, this ice-covered ledge is buffeted by high winds. A small cavern to the east offers a modicum of shelter from the harsh climate. A narrow trail leads down the side of the mountain, but it appears to be impossible to scale the cliffs above. Far below to the west, the hills of Eregion can be seen in the distance.
14961:
A small and well-kept fire lights and warms the room.
A wooden longbow is lying here.
A crazed dwarf is here, drooling down his beard.

This cave, high on the flank of Celebdil, is apparently the home of some intelligent creature, for there is a small fire burning here in a small circle of stones. There is no hint as to what would motivate someone to live in such a harsh locale, and whoever does dwell here must have a difficult life.
14962:
A quiver lies on the ground.
A sturdy leather backpack has been left here.
There are two large pieces of raw meat here.
There are three stout barrels here.

The room is essentially a natural cavern - it has had little if any work done to improve upon its natural state. The walls are cold stone that is encrusted in many places by a thin layer of ice. The temperature here is just below freezing, and this place is apparently used as cold storage for perishable food by whoever inhabits this place.
14963:
A shrub with maple-like leaves is growing here.
On the shrub, there are a handful of blackcurrant berries.

The wide area atop the cliffs over Durin's Gate narrows quickly to the south. Directly below is the cirque that forms the head of the valley of the Sirannon - except for a narrow strip of land along the northeast portion, it is flooded with dark water. The ground is littered with droppings of goats and elk, and their frequent wanderings have worn a trail leading up to the southwest.
14964: The narrow strip of dry land along the northern rim of the lake is cut here by a green and stagnant creek. The creek extends a short way into the northern wall of the valley, but it's source must be underground, for there is no water flowing from the high ridges above. The creek is shallow where it enters the lake - no more than ankle-deep at its edges, so it presents no serious obstacle.
14965: A Narrow Stretch of Dry Land

If the water level in the lake to the south and west were just a few inches higher, this narrow strip of dry land would not exist at all. As it is, the ground is often soggy, and in many places debris from the deteriorating cliffs of the northern edge of the valley almost blocks it. The Walls of Moria are quite close - their smooth, featureless cliffs clearly visible throughout the day.
14966: A Narrow Stretch of Dry Land

This narrow stretch of dry land is hemmed between tall grey cliffs to the east and an ominously dark lake to the west. The ground is littered with fallen rocks and boulders, making it difficult to traverse. In the shallows of the lake, rotting stumps and boughs are all that remain of a once regal grove of holly trees.
14967: A pair of tall, slender holly trees stand by the grey walls.

Dark and silent, the smooth grey cliffs rise from the water of the lake, looming overhead with a forbidding solemnity. The cliffside to the east is smooth and unbroken by any seam or crack. A narrow strip of dry land clings to the base of the cliff - cluttered with fallen rock and rubble, it provides a means of skirting the dark lake to the west.
14968: To the west there is an abrupt drop of several hundred feet. At the foot of the cliff is a narrow strip of dry land that skirts the fringes of the dark lake that fills the circular valley to the west. The cliff - and this shelf atop it - is unnaturally flat. There are cracks or footholds apparent at all in the sheer rockface. To the east, the mountains begin in earnest, and the peak of Celebdil Silvertine stands among them like an emperor.
14969:
A shrub with maple-like leaves is growing here.
A ferocious warg is here, snarling angrily.

This wide shelf runs to the south where it forms the top of a steep cliff that forms the eastern end of a round valley. The valley is almost complete- ly filled with an ominous-looking lake - apparently there is some obstruction at the head of the valley that prevents the water from draining. To the west, one may proceed along the crest of the ridge that forms the northern edge of the valley.
14970: From the crest of this ridge, there is a clear view to the south of a dark lake that fills the head of a valley. There is no trail leading down to the lake - the south side of the ridge is much to steep - but there does appear to be a narrow strip of land along the northeastern shore. To the east, the ridge climbs to meet a wide shelf that sits above the western end of the valley below.
14971: To the north is a steep slope that descends to a landscape of rocky hills. The ridge continues to the west, descending rapidly as it goes. To the southeast, ridge meets a flat shelf that sits atop a large grey cliff that marks the end of the valley to the south. At the foot of the ridge, a small strip of land along the northern fringe of lake can be made out, but the descent would be too perilous to attempt.
14972: This ridge forms the northern edge of the valley where the Sirannon once flowed. Directly below can be seen the old Hollin Road that leads from Durin's Gate westward into the holly-covered hills of Hollin. To the north the land is very rugged, but there is an exposed rock formation in that direction that should allow you to survey the terrain in that direction. To the west, the ridge begins to be cut by many crevices, and much of the rock seems unstable, so it is impossible to proceed that way.
14973: A sturdy pack horse is standing here.

The water is dark and has an evil presence about it. Ripples occasionally disturb the lakes stillness and puts shivers up your back. The whole area just smells of evil. The grey stone cliffs extend skyward to your east and the mountain casts cold shadows everywhere. You are veiled by the eerie shadow of Celebdil.
14974: To the west lies the dam at the head of the valley that has caused this lake to form. The water is deep here and extremely dark, hiding whatever may be lurking in its depths. The water smells as well, as if the floor of the lake were covered in rotting matter that has contaminated the water with the odour of decay.
14975: Directly to the east is a low cliff, some five fathoms high. The top is jagged and broken, and through a wide cleft at the top a small trickle of water flows, dampening the rocks. Clearly, this was at some time a large and magnificent cascade, but now the flow has been diminished to almost nothing. A series of stone steps have been cut into the cliff, allowing one to climb to the top.
14976: The Sirannon once babbled forcefully through this channel, but now the streambed is little more than a rocky trail with a trickle of water flowing from the higher portions of the valley. Occasionally enough water gathers in a single place to form stagnant pools, but these are little more than breeding places for variegated species of algae.
14977: You are on the side of a mountain with a few sparse plants. To the north you can climb down into a valley in which the vegetation seems to have taken root. To the south you can climb up to a mountain trail.
14978: A ferocious warg is here, snarling angrily.

A number of small stones have been gathered and piled into a small cairn. There is nothing but rock underfoot so this is certainly not a gravesite - perhaps it serves some other purpose. At the very least, it indicates that someone besides the mountain fauna has been here.
14979:
A mountain goat is here, jumping from cliff to cliff.
A mountain goat is here, jumping from cliff to cliff.

You can travel along a small track east-west made by mountain goats. It is easier to walk upon than scree or heather. As you travel east you are climbing further up the spurs and outcrops of Celebdil. You can see the great walls of Moria down in a valley to your north east. They look grand and probably have many stories to tell about wars of old.
14982:
A huge warg is here, moving in for the kill.
A huge warg is here, moving in for the kill.
A ferocious warg is here, snarling angrily.

To the east one of the first high peaks of the Misty Mountains begins. To the north and west, the landscape is a monotonous collection of dry hills whose reddish slopes are littered with boulders. It is possible to ascend a spur of the mountain to the south - it is a difficult climb of several hundred feet, but certainly not deadly.
14983: A huge warg is here, moving in for the kill.

The hills here are almost barren, with little vegetation around to conceal the reddish hue of the rocks. The land rises sharply to the south, forming a high ridge, while in every other direction the hills continue. Farther east, the Misty Mountains begin, and the triumvirate of Caradhras, Celebdil, and Fanuidhol tower above the surrounding peaks.
14984: To the south is a sharp and high ridge, while in every other direction the same reddish and dry hills extend. The hillsides are often strewn with boulders and cut with deep gullies that make travel difficult. To the northwest, the land becomes slightly more gentle - giving way to a sparse forest of pines.
14985: The hills end almost abruptly, coming to a halt at a steep slope overlooking a valley to the south. There is a road - apparently an ancient one - running alongside a streambed upward toward the head of the valley among the hills to the east. To the northwest, a few gnarled pine trees have managed to take root, and they form the outskirts of a sparse forest.
14986: The small stream that flows here gathers speed and runs down a boulder-strewn slope to the south, where it forms a small waterfall and tumbles onto the ancient road to the south. There isn't much soil here, but a few holly bushes and rhododendrons have managed to survive. To the west, the hills subside and the landscape becomes gentler, while to the north a sparse forest of pines provides a little shelter from the chilly winds.
14987: The hills here are more gentle than those to the east, and in general the land here and farther west seems to be well-watered, in sharp contrast to the dry and jagged slopes closer to the mountains in the east. To the west, a fair-sized stream is flowing, while to the south an ancient road passes, running parallel to an almost empty streambed.
14988: This small but swift stream flows to the south, through a maze of boulders. There is a high cliff to the east, while the land is fairly flat to the west, and there appears to be a paved road a short distance away in that direction. To the north, scraggly pine and fir trees form a thin forest on the eastern bank.
14989: The river trickles over the large rocks, creating a good habitat for mosses and lichen. The flow of the stream is not even close to what it was in years past, now bearing only a trickle of muddy water. When the river was at its fullest, only the stout of heart would have attempted to negotiate it. Now though, you can safely walk over the damp channel. The Misty Mountains can be seen in the east reaching far into the north. To the west are the lower, warmer lands of Eregion.
14990: You can still see the tide marks from when the Sirannon used to roar down this valley in its full might, but now it barely trickles downstream. The evil work of Sauron has dammed up the stream, pinching off the life giving substance to the lands in the west. The riverbed heads west, leaving the evilness of Moria far behind. There seems to be some sort of track to the north.
14991: The Sirannon is joined here by a swift-flowing stream from the north. To the east, barely a trickle of water is draining from the valley leading to the gates of Khazad-dum. The old road leading to Durin's Gate lies just to the north, following the streambed farther up into the valley.
14992: This small trickle of water twists its way down the centre of the streambed. The stream once carried much more water, but apparently something upstream has stopped much of the flow. To the west, another stream flows in from the north, and beyond lie the holly-covered lands of Eregion. On the southern side of the streambed, a narrow trail - probably made by animals - leads up the steep valley side.
14993: The small rivulet that was once the Sirannon is strengthened here by water flowing in from the north. The rocks of the streambed are damp and slick with algae, so walking tends to be a chore. To the north, the Hollin Road runs parallel to the stream, climbing steadily eastward into the higher land at the head of the valley.
14995: The foot of this valley lies a bit to the north, and in that direction the sounds of a mountain stream can be heard. The head of the valley is at a fairly high elevation, nestled amongst a spur of the Misty Mountains. East and west, the valley walls are too steep to climb.
14996: The bed of the Sirannon turns to the north here, bounded to the south and east by sheer cliffs. To the northwest, the ancient Hollin Road can be seen - paralleling the Sirannon as they both wind away westward into the hills of Eregion.
14997: The streambed now takes a strong westward turn. The slope of the bed steepens slightly as the water trickles down to warmer lands. Far to your east you can see the ruins of an old building. To your north you can see far enough up the bank to see part of the broken path. The stream no longer carries enough water to require a boat, only enough to dampen your feet as you trod along.
14998: The riverbed of the Sirannon is now heading westwards after a smooth curve in the north-east towards a bend in the far west. The water used to gurgle along swiftly, but no longer praises the green land. The area seems especially attractive when compared to the cold mountains in the east. From the forest land around you, birds and other small animals can be seen and heard, busily going about their daily search for food.
14999:
A swarm of mosquitoes is here, humming around you.
A large beaver is here, gnawing on a piece of wood.

A little west of here, the riverbed joins a smaller river coming from the north. The water seems impatient at the meeting, as most of its own water has ceased to flow. Any new addition would surely be welcomed. It is not deep enough here for fish to swim, but the higher waterlines on the rocks tell you that it once was a swift flowing volume of water. At least these surroundings seem more friendly than the mountains to the east.
15000:
A stone sarcophagus lies on the floor.
A granite chest is here, its sides inlaid with wood.
A huge statue made of stone suddenly turns to life.
A huge statue made of stone suddenly turns to life.
A spirit floats around, making strange magical gestures (glowing).

Amazed at the clever concealment, you proceed into a small room hidden from view by the tapestry. As you enter, a feeling of dread washes over you like a wave. Perhaps some ancient magic has left guardians to watch over the area. The single room differs from the tunnels in both height and width, being on the smaller side of both aspects. Only a single torch bracket adorns the walls of the place. The floor is hard dirt and the walls are the same cold stone.
15001: A shadowy haunt floats here, oblivious to your presence.

Walking further along the dim passage, no signs of life are yet apparent. This is not surprising as the folk that inhabited this land are long gone. The Dwarves long ago shut the mighty gates of Moria in fear of the dark lord. And the kingdom of Noldor Elves, in the city of Ost-in-Edhil, is nothing but ruin now. Yet evidence of their existence is here in this tunnel today. Discarded weapons and decaying leather lie scattered about the floor. Even a ragged tapestry is still clinging to the hooks that hold it to the wall.
15002: Pushing past the small opening you discovered, you find yourself in a dark tunnel that at first glance, appears to be empty. Although there is no obvious sign of inhabitants at this time, torch brackets on the wall as well as a few broken barrels indicate that this once was a place used by humanoids. The walls are cold and grey, made of simple stone blocks erected to keep dirt from collapsing and blocking the tunnel. You quickly surmise that this must have been an underground refuge for the Noldor Elves and Moria Dwarves that shared the dwelling above.
15003:
A little stone lies on the ground.
A giant, strange looking green fungus is here, ready to devour you in seconds.

The steps down from the kitchen are smooth and steep. At the bottom you find yourself in a neat storage area, long since empty of goods. As the temperature down here is much colder, caused by being surrounded on all sides by the cool damp earth, you feel this area was used for cold storage. As evidence of this, a wine barrel sits unused in the corner. Hard earth makes up the floor, while grey blocks of stone form the walls of the cellar. The only exit appears to be back up into the kitchen.
15004:
A pan is here, ready for use.
A cup has been set here.
A musty loaf of bread has been left here.
A musty loaf of bread has been left here.
A sparrow is flapping around on the ground.

Cutting this room out of the hill around it must have been no easy chore. Though not solid rock, the earth around here is hard packed, with trees and roots to inhibit excavation. The task was done however, and a small kitchen was the result of the work. Leading upwards to the outside, a small vent ascends from the ceiling. The great brick ovens used so many years ago, are smashed into barely recognisable rubble. A massive fire pit sunk into the middle of the floor is the most notable attraction. Being at least a square yard in area, it must have held a vast amount of wood.
15005: Moving further into the spacious meeting hall, you are not surprised to see it in shambles. Where once a large table stood, probably holding up to fifty guests, now only holds a pile of ashes and one of the table's wooden legs. A couple of chairs are overturned on the far side of the room, gathering much dust as the wood structure slowly decays around them. Off to the south is another room, though not half as large as this one. A bit of ripped cloth on the wall suggests there were a few tapestries covering the logs.
15006: A small black vicious rat squeaks at you for disturbing it.

Stepping inside the abandoned building, you wonder why it was built. Since this place is located west of the Misty Mountains, and east of old Ost-in-Edhil, you correctly surmise that this was a central meeting point for the Noldor Elves and the Dwarves of Moria. When business had to be discussed, or trade to be accomplished, it could have easily taken place here, as it would serve as equidistant from the two remote places. Of course, if the meeting was of great importance, it would undoubtedly have been held in either of the two more principal locations.
15007:
A large marmot is here, scurrying in between the rocks.
A sharp-eyed hawk is here stalking some prey.

You are on the western-most point of a small ridge. The view is nice form this point, as you have little to obstruct it. The familiar holly bushes dot the area, along with trees of various types. To the east, a small trail wanders further along the ridge-top. Looking downslope to the west, fields of holly and scrub trees catch your eye. Since the slope is not great, you feel certain you can negotiate your way down. A slab of rock has broken off to the south, forming a small cliff, and going in this direction would be unsafe.
15008: A robin is here, carrying small pieces of wood to its nest.

Walking the small path along the top of the crest, you catch the upslope winds from both directions. The ridge you are walking is not of great height, just enough to offer a fine view of the surrounding lands and give you a bit of security. The vegetation here is abundant, as is the wildlife. A semi-deep depression in the rocks has caught a smattering of rainfall, and formed a small pool of drinkable water.
15009: A woody evergreen plant grows here, with many stems reaching upward.

The hills you have been walking in have formed a walkable ridge here. The top of this ridge is graced by a two-foot wide path that leads east-west in direction. Though not overly high, this ridge affords a great view in all directions. To the north lies the meeting of the River Bruinen and Mitheithel, and the river valley stretching all the way to Imladris. Eastwards holds the mighty mountains, the Hithaeglir, and inside them - Moria. The south and west regions are the vast lands of Eregion.
15010:
A bright green holly bush is growing here.
Partly covered by the bush's green leaves, there are some hollyberries.
A holly bush with dark green leaves is growing here.
Partly covered by the bush's green leaves, there are a few inkberries.
A fallow deer is grazing peacefully here.

Rising up before a small valley to the south, this green and fertile hill range is a scenic spot. Growing around you is a multitude of plants and trees. Most of the plants are holly derivatives, but you can see where ferns and other foliage has made an appearance. Winding through the valley are two prominent features. One, a small stream, snakes east-south while running alongside the second feature, a track of earth and grass. To the south, you can directly climb down to this path.
15011: You are high up in the Misty Mountains and the view is still dominated by the mountains Caradhras and Celedbil. From this spot you cannot see the tops of these mountains but you can be sure enough that there is permanent snow cover not far above you.
15012: The wind buffets you about and the only place that might allow shelter is a narrow crevice cut deep into the north face of the mountain. To the east you can see many of the Misty Mountain Peaks.
15013: The trail changes direction here to negotiate a large spur that protrudes from the mountain side. The spur climbs high up the back of Celebdil before disapearing into the clouds. Little knolls and boulders are causing you problems on the ground.
15017: This stream flows to the south, curving slightly to avoid the end of a high ridge that lies to the southeast. To the east a sparse forest of pines and firs grows in the rocky soil, while to the west an ancient road of some sort can be made out.
15018: The stream flowing just to the west provides enough water to support a thin evergreen forest. To the northeast, the land becomes much drier and rockier, and the vegetation quickly peters out. North of here the forest continues, while to the south the land rises sharply to form a steep arrete.
15019: The rocky soil provides a home for a few scraggly pines and firs. To the south and east the land rises steeply, while the thin forest continues north and west. The trees are ancient, and their trunks have been twisted into strange gnarled shapes. A small trickle of water flows in from the east - its soft murmur almost inaudible - and then turns to the south.
15020: A few hardy pines have managed to take root in the rocky soil. The ground is still littered with large hunks of reddish rock that appears to have washed down from the rugged landscape to the northeast. A small rivulet of water winds out of the hills to the east, and flows almost unnoticed through the rocks until it drains away to the west. To the northwest, the thin forest continues.
15021: The landscape is dominated by rugged hills that are almost bare of vegetation. The land is extremely folded, and often cut by deep channels that have been carved by the rapid runoff of whatever rain falls here. Tucked among the hills - confined to a small channel - a tiny stream winds its way from the lands to the north, almost unnoticed as it flows to the southeast.
15022: A tiny rivulet of water flows in from the north - winding its way among the boulders that litter the slopes of these hills. It eventually finds a course leading westward. Other than that tiny bit of moisture, the hills are dry and almost barren. For the most part any soil has been blown away by the strong winds that blow from the mountains to the east, and only the scoured red rock remains.
15023: A beautiful and docile horse is standing here.

To the east, the terrain becomes much harsher as the Misty Mountains begin. Towering over the lower peaks to the east, Celebdil Silvertine reaches for the sky - its summit gleaming white throughout the year. To the northeast the peak of cruel Caradhras glowers, and in that direction lies the Redhorn Pass. Farther west, the dry hills continue - almost a wasteland of barren red rock.
15024: The hills here are very jagged, making travel extremely difficult. The rocks are predominantly the colour of rust, and the apparent lack of water makes this a forbidding landscape indeed. To the east, the high peaks of the Misty Mountains rear up - dominated by the lofty heights of Caradhras, with Celebdil lying a bit farther to the south.
15025: The landscape is covered with sharp boulders that may washed down from the surrounding hills during a flash flood. The faint sound of trickling water can be made out, as there is a small rivulet winding among the reddish rocks - barely enough to moisten one's lips. The source of the water appears to be somewhere in the hills to the north, and it flows onward to the south.
15026: This rocky plain is littered with reddish-tinged boulders. Little vegetation survives here, as whatever precipitation falls here seems to quickly drain into the valleys to the northwest. North of here lie some low mountains, little more than diminuitive copies of the high peaks of the Misty Mountains to the east.
15027: The land on this plateau is littered with reddish boulders, with very little vegetation having gained a foothold. The area seems quite dry - whatever rain falls here must quickly drain away from the rocky hillsides.
15028: The fierce winds that often blow here on the edge of the Misty Mountains have wreaked havoc with the trees of this thin forest. The evergreen trees have been twisted into strange shapes - their gnarled trunks assuming a variety of tortured poses.
15029: For no apparent reason, the twisted pines of the surrounding forest have suddenly given way to a circular clearing of packed earth. To the north and west, the sound of flowing water can be heard. In the centre of the clearing is a large boulder that brings to mind a pedestal set in the centre of an amphitheatre. The tracks of many animals can be seen in the earth.
15030: As this stream winds out of the mountains to the east, it passes between a sparse forest to the east and an ancient road to the west. The water is icy cold, and even though the stream is shallow, the current is strong enough to cause problems for those fording it.
15031: The smooth stream that flows in from the northeast makes a bend to the south here, as it encounters an old roadway to the west. The road is rather vacant, and seldom maintained; spanning the distance between forgotten places out of sight to the north and south.
15032: A crayfish is here, snapping its claws at you.

Curving smoothly from the north to the west, this stream curves around a small formation of stone to the northwest that has proven too hard to erode by the constant flow of water. A narrow beach follows the eastern shore of the stream, and small pools of still water filled with trapped debris have formed along the waterline.
15033: Occasionally washed clean of flotsam when the stream to the west floods, this place tends to accumuate whatever happens to fall into the water upstream. The water makes a curve nearby that creates various eddies and pools, which gather branches and floating weeds; the smell of composting leaves a bitter fragrance in the air. A steep bluff rises to the east, marking the edge of a family of mountains.
15034: From these low peaks, which mark the southwestern corner of a small group of hills, a short stretch of a a stream lies within view to the west. A small plain extends to the south, and rising mountains dominate the view to the east.
15035: These low mountains are covered by a thin blanket of tough grasses, which seem fairly healthy by their green hue. The grass becomes more dense to the east, as the ground descends into a small valley. Plains lie to the south and southwest, while mountains reach to the north.
15036: A clear spring babbles as cool water trickles out of the ground.

Large tufts of thick, green grasses grow scattered around a large mountain spring that has formed here. No trees stand here, perhaps hindered by the loose soil, but an abundance of small flowering plants, grasses, and reeds have sprouted and survived. The waters of the spring flow to the south.
15037: Overlooking a trail or road to the east, whose details cannot be clearly seen from here, this low hill seems to be almost a sentinel above the road as well as the plains to the south. Taller mountain peaks rise to the northwest, and some waving green grasses have grown to the west.
15038: Guided by your luck you struck a good path. It looks like the remains of an ancient road, that had once been broad and well planned, from Hollin to the mountain-pass. The moon, now at the full, rise over the mountains, and casts a pale light in which the shadows of stone are black. Many of them look to have been worked by hands, though now they lay tumbled and ruinous in a bleak, barren land.
15044: Some small and unhealthy trees have managed to grow here, taking what little water that they can and trying to hold their roots and leaves as the wind tries to blow them over. The source of their water is a quiet stream to the east, whose water is dark and swift.
15045: Curving gently to the south from the east, the current of this swift stream slows a bit as the ground flattens and the water spreads into a wider, more shallow channel. Taking advantage of the calm water, some reeds have taken root and offer a little colour to the otherwise bland landscape.
15046: A crayfish is here, snapping its claws at you.

Channeling down into a narrow and steeply banked streambed, where at one time the flowing water found a soft spot in the underlying sediment, the dark current moves silently south. A small clearing extends to the east, marked by some old and twisted trees, but the western bank is too steep to climb.
15047: The distant mountain peaks to the north and east are all that hinders sight or the winds in this area; the bleak plains that lie between offer no shelter or obstacle. Small cyclones of dust stir up from time to time, and dance around playfully until the winds change and the dust settles back to the ground.
15048: As the thin layer of silt along the ground is periodically whipped into a frenzy by gusting winds, and large clouds of dust turn the air into a dark and choking shroud, this place becomes even more unwelcoming than it had been. With no tall plants to slow the winds, the land remains barren; and while it is barren, it will remain uninhabited.
15049: Flat and somewhat featureless, baked solid by the scorching sun over many years, the ground is totally bare in places where the wind has swept unrelentingly across it. Patches of stubborn grasses still cling to the earth, drawing water that lies sheltered below the shell of hardened soil; sometimes eaten by roaming animals in need of moisture.
15050: A faint trail leads from west to east here, but the places that it connects are not easily distinguished. To the west, a band of colour that contrasts the darker soils here runs through the plains, while to the east, at some distance, a twinkle of green and brown catches the eye.
15051:
A large rabbit looks peacefully at you, ready to dart away.
A restless rabbit bounces around.
A small rabbit glares angrily at you.

Heavily laden with sorted dust and silt, the ground along these plains is soft and giving, at least as far down as the harder clays below. The occasional gust of wind will stir up bits of sand and hurl them to pelt whomever is standing in their way.
15052:
A holly bush with dark green leaves is growing here.
Partly covered by the bush's green leaves, there are two piles of inkberries and a torch.

Aiding the smooth transition from low plains to the spectacular mountain peaks on either side, these hills offer a decent view of the surrounding landscape. To the north and east extends a great mountain range, while to the south and southeast lie featureless plains. A road passes to the immediate west.
15053:
A big, nasty vulture is sitting here, protecting its nest.
A large marmot is here, scurrying in between the rocks.

As it is worn away with the rest of these mountains, this particular peak's destruction also takes its toll on the road below. As boulders dislodge and mudslides move down the western slope, the unkept path is slowly but steadily buried beneath the earth. Given time, no sign of that road will remain here.
15056: Winds blowing along this mountain area are often cold and dry; small patches of shaded ground seem to draw away the life and energy of the wind. What remains is a chill breeze that seems content to make travel harder by filling the air with choking dust and stripping away moisture to inspire thirst.
15057: Marking the southern edge of a vast range of mountains, the peaks here are a bit lower than the ones to the north. Despite the fact that the view to the north is blocked in this way, the slopes of these mountains offer a magnificent view of the moon in the night skies to the south, as it travels slowly over wide and undisturbed plains.
15058: At the Foot of the Mountains

Thrust upwards by some great cataclysm, or perhaps molded by the very hands of the gods, large and magnificent mountains rise out of the ground to the north and gaze out over the flat plains to the south. Winds passing freely over the otherwise flat land seem troubled by these great obstacles, and whip around as they are forced to change course.
15059: Inhabited only by wild animals, and marked by occasional tufts of grass that have managed to survive the elements, these plains are essentially barren and dead. The soil itself may not be infertile, and might be tilled to raise crops, but the area is so desolate that perhaps this will never happen.
15062: A shallow pond is here, tinted green with algae.

This particular patch of land is a bit different from the lifeless plains nearby, primarily because there is a small dip in the land which has filled with water. Thick, green grasses blanket the ground around the pond, thinning and shriveling as they spread away.
15063: The shadows cast towards the north by the noon sun, or even a bright moon watching from the south, pale in comparison to the ominous and dominating mountains to the north which seem to gather shadows to them. Plains reach to the south and west, to the horizon, while the eastern view is marked by more distant mountain peaks.
15064:
A mountain goat is here, jumping from cliff to cliff.
A mountain goat is here, jumping from cliff to cliff.
