A large rabbit looks peacefully at you, ready to dart away.
A restless rabbit bounces around.
A small rabbit glares angrily at you.

Dark and sometimes unstable slopes mark these low mountains; occasional scars where soft mud or loose gravel shifted and slid are all that break the continuity of the landscape. No trails or signs of settlement exist here; either they were long since buried by moving dirt, or never created to begin with.
15065: Great and rough mountains spread in all directions, blocking the view of any distant features or obstacles, as well as the sun or moon if possible. This place has always been somewhat remote and alone; its special feeling of sanctuary is hardly disturbed by a visitor who is not only mortal, but also otherwise insignificant.
15069: These mountains grow steadily larger and more magnificent towards the north, where they extend out of sight; to the south, they descend into wide and rather featureless plains. Little sign of animal life can be seen here, and even less evidence of civilisation exists. To the east and west, the rising mountains continue.
15070: As the landscape makes its slow transition between the plains to the southwest and the mountains to the northeast, a narrow and dry streambed meanders toward lower ground. While sometimes found to carry water, during the thawing of the snows from the mountain peaks, it is now dry and empty.
15071: Carved from the soft soil of the plains, as water lifted the lighter bits of dirt and sand and carried them with it, this place is now left empty and dry. The walls, too hard to be dissolved by the moving water, seem stable and secure; only when waters fill this small pit is it unsafe.
15072: This place is completely surrounded by vast distances of plains, with mountains to the north and east, and at some great distance to the south. Little can be seen to the west, as the plains roll out of sight, except for an occasional glimmer of green and brown against the stark skyline.
15084:
A crayfish is here, snapping its claws at you.
A crayfish is here, snapping its claws at you.

The way is wet and difficult as pebbles and icy water tumble their way westwards through the hills. Looking upstream, to the east, the snowy peaks of the Misty Mountains can be seen rising to the sky far into the horizon. Thick vegetation flourishes on the northern banks of the river while a faint trail is noticeable on the sparse southern banks.
15085: Far off to the east, a thin stream of water makes its way through a gap between the mountains and collects into a wide and dark pool. The mountains that the water divides spread like sweeping arms in an arc to the north and south, some distance away. These plains extend out of sight to the west.
15086: These hills fare the worst in all kinds of weather. The sun, when overhead, will scorch the ground and bake the soil. Newly fallen snow will fall between stones and wedge them apart as it refreezes. Rain strikes the rocks as it falls unhindered, then washes gouges into the mountain slopes as the water flees downhill. Even the winds push stone against stone, as natural forces work to change the terrain.
15087: Far beyond the view or influence of any civilisation, surrounded only by more mountains, barren of life, devoid of vegetation, uninviting, and impersonal are these ancient mountains. Older than life, more weathered than any gnarled tree, and as lonely as any widower, these mountains continue to watch the rising of the sun and the setting of the moon as they have for many mortal lifetimes.
15088: The ground throughout these mountains is rather dark, when not capped by a blanket of snow. Thick soil covers the slopes of the mountains, washed down by rains and wind, while the peaks themselves are exposed rock and weathered boulders. The mountains extend in all directions.
15097:
A mountain goat is here, jumping from cliff to cliff.
A mountain goat is here, jumping from cliff to cliff.
A ferocious warg is here, snarling angrily.

Huge piles of splintered and broken rock, hewn apart by the force of it striking the ground, lie at the bottom of this slope, marking the end result of some major landslide that occurred in this area. While it is difficult to judge how long ago this took place, it seems fairly recent, geologically speaking.
15098: Low grasses have sprouted at the bottom of this slope, sheltered from falling debris by a large formation of rock standing in the path of sliding dirt. Mountains seem to spread out in all directions, each blocking the view of what lies just beyond.
15099:
A bright red mushroom is growing here.
A small mushroom grows nearby.

A small mushroom grows nearby.
A clear spring babbles as cool water trickles out of the ground.

Nestled and hidden in the mountains, a small clear spring of water has formed, as water trickles down the mossy rocks of this slope. Well shaded by the looming peaks overhead, the water has collected in narrow pools, each accented by mosses or mushrooms.
15100: A small flower grows here, with a purple bloom and wide leaves.

This mountain is encircled by countless others that roll across the land to each horizon. Travel through this area can be dangerous, as loose rocks and dirt tend to shift unexpectedly, sometimes causing an even greater slide of the nearby slope.
15101: Sharp stones jut out of the sides of these hills, hanging dangerously onto the unstable slopes. Exposed by a constant battering of the elements, these rocks have little left to support them, and will likely become part of any rockslide that takes place.
15102: Large piles of fallen rock and mud accumulate at the base of these hills, either too massive to be carried away by flowing water, or allowed no exit to lower lands. Passage between peaks is thus a difficult affair, as the loose gravel and dirt is prone to shift under any additional weight.
15103:
A mountain goat is here, jumping from cliff to cliff.
A black raven flies in the sky searching for flesh to prey upon.
A black raven flies in the sky searching for flesh to prey upon.
A black raven flies in the sky searching for flesh to prey upon.

Long scars run down the side of this hill, as flowing water, either from heavy rains or melting snow, cut its way through the loosely packed soil as it moved downhill. In many places along these marks large areas of the slope have shifted, as the weight of the water soaking into the dirt became too much for the slope to bear.
15104: There is some snow on the ground.

The first thing you notice is the pile of severed heads which have been collected into a great pit in the middle of the camp. Dead orc bodies which those heads belonged to lay scattered all over the ground. The servants of Sauron are apparently brutal to their friends as well as their enemies. A huge building rises up to the south, overlooking the smashed burnt huts.

This appears to have been a very impressive camp at one time or another. Destroyed huts and burnt fences attest to its past vitality. However, it seems that this area has been pillaged and overrun by the armies of the Dark One. Surprisingly, there are no indications of battle. Evidently, such chaos is not rare among the forsaken servants of Melkor.

An encampment covers the land to the west. The Misty Mountains rise to the north, and hills wander east and south.
15107: There is some snow on the ground.

Corpses and skeletons are strewn across the ground. Some are pierced by strange, small arrows which seem to have killed them without warning. You recognize some of the skeletons as that of humans and dwarves. Strange, twisted trees torture the earth with their existence, forming a ring about the area which allows very little light with which to see by. Gnarled roots infest the ground and you feel you would not like to touch them!
15108: There is some snow on the ground.

Corpses and skeletons are strewn across the ground. Some are pierced by strange, small arrows which seem to have killed them without warning. You recognise some of the skeletons as that of humans and dwarves. Strange, twisted trees torture the earth with their existence, forming a ring about the area which allows very little light with which to see by. Gnarled roots infest the ground, and you feel you would not like to touch them!
15109: There is some snow on the ground.

You are standing at the base of a beautiful peak in the mountains. A cool and refreshing wind blows here. You find yourself understanding the dwarven love for these cold, rocky mountains. To the south however, the land takes on very ominous undertones.
15110:
There is some snow on the ground.
A burly giant is here, covered with thick fur and snow.
A mountain ibex is jumping from rock to rock.

No folk dwell in these lands now, but many other creature live here at all time, especially birds. Yet now all things but you are silent. You can feel it. There is no sounds for miles about you, and your voices seems to make the ground echo. You do not understand it.
15111: Climbing ever higher, you stand high atop a range in the Misty Mountains. Impressive, snow-capped peaks rise up all around you, providing a majestic view of the surroundings. To the north, the mountains sink down into a range of hills, dwarfed by the larger peaks. The air here is thin and cold forcing you to keep moving to stay warm.
15112: There is some snow on the ground.

Trudging along this huge mountain range you can only take the time to notice the countless peaks around you. A range of hills lies to the north but you cannot head that way, as a small river is flowing in a deep canyon just between you and these friendly hills. The mountains block your way south and east.
15113: You are walking in a plain covered by bushes, at the foothills of the Hithaeglir. A smooth path has been delineated in a small ravine, partially hidden beyond the high bushes. To the near south are hills, tall in themselves but dwarfed by the mountains a bit more south. The dangerous tales you have heard all seem true as you look upon that huge range. The peaks lie near the clouds and you can hear the screaming winds that echo through the mountains.
15114: You are walking in a trail among the first hills of Hollin. You have reached the foot of the Hithaeglir proper. Looking south you can see them standing proud and mighty. You remember the tales of your youth and your grandmother telling you that these mighty peaks were thrown up in the path of the elves by Morgoth in order that he might stop them reaching the West.
15116: There is some snow on the ground.
A pleasant trail runs through the hills here. Although it does not appear to be used often, it still has not become overgrown. You can continue on the trail to the east or south.
15117: You feel something ancient and great here. A warm and peaceful feeling fills your body. You feel that this is perhaps the only place among these hills that the servants of Sauron have not defiled with their presence.
15119: Little grows on these hills except grass. There are several small bushes trying to survive but they are not doing so well. Apparently, the cold harsh weather is too much for them. The sides of the Caradhras are now dark and sullen, and its head is in grey cloud.
15120: The complex is large, extending a fair distance to the east. Some equipment and debris in the corner seems to indicate that this may be a headquarters for Orkish captains. However, the room seems to have been used more as a shelter from the sun than as a base of operations since the room appears very disorganized and, for the most part, empty.
15121:
A mailbox stands here stuffed full of messages.
A coil of rope is lying here.
A wooden chest stands in the corner.
A large, dusty alcove sits in a wall, smelling of soot.

You can see that at one time this building had many rooms. But now, all the walls have been torn down to create one huge hall. You can see a rotten corpse hanging from the ceiling. A great deal of debris lies about here and it smells fairly musty.
15122: A water moccasin is sleeping here.

This flooded plain is very wide and somewhat musty, but the water is shallow enough to be easily crossed. This ford continues to the south and east, as it loosely follows the path of the river that created it; mountains and plains dominate the surrounding area.
15123:
A crayfish is here, snapping its claws at you.
A grey snake slides along the water.

As the shallow stream to the east enters this wide plain, it spreads out across the ground and covers the land with slow moving and very shallow water. Some small plants have taken root here, thriving on the lull in the stream, helping to hinder its progress further. The water continues to slowly flow to the south and west.
15124: A large brown wolf stands here, its teeth partly bared.

The place has served as a dumping-ground and graveyard. There are many half-rotten corpses and bits of trash which you don't want to guess the source of. The stench is awful!!! The hills stretch to the south and east and the ominous building looms over you to the north. A small stream flows here, its water poisoned by the garbage dropped in it.
15125: You stand at the back of the ugly, wooden building. The plain continue south, east and north. A small stream, coming from a marish that you can smell at the foot of the mountains, flows next the building. It is used obviously used as a sewer by the inhabitants of the house, and garbage has been thrown into the clear water, poisoning it.
15126: You are walking in a flat prairie, smoothed by a glacier many generations ago. The grass grows high, watered by several small streams flowing from the high summits around. You clearly see the great Misty Mountains guarding this land from the east, south, and north. You also notice some smoke rising from a strange structure to the west.
15127: The East Wall of the Strange Building

The wooden building looks very quickly (and very poorly) built. But it's too big to serve any mundane purpose and somehow it makes you shiver in disgust. The ominous structure makes you want to leave as soon as possible.
15128: You see some grassy hills surrounding you. Some withering trees are feebly attempting to grow in this cold, harsh climate. Regiments of black crows are flying over all the land between the Mountains and the Greyflood, and they have passed over Hollin. They are not native here; they are "crebain" out of Fangorn and Dunland. You do not know what they are about: possibly there is some trouble away south from which they are fleeing; but you think they are spying out the land. You also glimpse many hawks flying high up in the sky. Hollin is being watched.
15129: This is the last part of flat prairie. The plains end here, cedeing the place to the barren mountains. A cold wind blows from the east. Several small bushes and a tree or two are trying to grow here but the climate is not cooperating. Only the spruces and firs look healthy.
15130: It is strange how these hills confuse you. They all look very similar. Essentially there is nothing distinct in any of them. At least you can use the sun and the stars to figure out which direction you are heading but you definitely can not tell one hill from another.
15131: This path seems seldom used. There is something great and powerful here. It seems so ancient and beautiful. You surprise yourself by thinking that the plants adorn the path as if they were honouring it.
15133:
A bright green holly bush is growing here.
Partly covered by the bush's green leaves, there are two piles of hollyberries.

You climb to the top of the small hill under which you had been sheltering. It is crowned with a knot of old and twisted trees, about which lay a broken circle of boulder-stones. In the midst of this is a good place to light a fire, for there is no hope that darkness and silence would keep your trail from discovery by the wild beasts who live here. You are surrounded by high snow-covered peaks. The cold air and the strong winds here give you good reason to light a fire or leave.
15134:
A bright green holly bush is growing here.
Partly covered by the bush's green leaves, there are two piles of hollyberries.

You walk through the northern hollin plains, where Elves and Dwarves once built a rich kingdom. East you can see great mountain peaks covered with snow. They look beautiful and noble, lurking above you. The giant mountains seem to tower into the heavens. Mother nature can be so lovely and at the same time so threatening.
15135: The grass grows high in these plains, watered by a clear stream which flows from a valley east. It is not easy to walk through the muddy prairie, but it is the only way to reach the road south.
15136: Descending to the east very gradually, these mountains overlook a wide plain in that direction through which a thin thread of a road travels. Other, taller mountains stand to the west and south, while they taper and flatten to the north.
15137: Hardly a hospitable place, with hard, rocky soil, no shelter from the sun or winds, much less the occasional rain, and unsettled by any, these mountains do not even offer a vantage point or tactical advantage. So they remain as they always have: unused, unwanted, and undisturbed.
15138: The various peaks of hills, all different in height and breadth, are scattered in all directions across the terrain. The soil is rocky and rough, as the hills themselves are slowly weathered down by winds and rain; few if any plants have managed to take root in the poor dirt.
15139: Rising above a narrow beach to the west as a steep cliff face, down which an occasional rock is prone to fall, this mount looks down on a stream that flows by silently below to the north and west. Other mountains reach off to the south and east, while the distant north is flat and plain.
15140: A ferocious warg is here, snarling angrily.

Overhung with the sparse or dead branches of some knarled trees, with a dark stream passing to the north and west, this place is the closest this area has to a relaxing beach. The trees have grown close to the water, so at times when the water has risen, the soil around their roots has washed away, leaving some of them perched above the ground in an eerie fashion.
15141: Gurgling quietly as it encounters a barrier to the south, the stream makes an abrupt turn from the north to the west. A small, clear beach has formed to the south, with some small trees clinging to life along the water's edge. The beach also extends to the east, following this curve in the stream.
15142: A crayfish is here, snapping its claws at you.

Curving from the east to the south, following some unseen features of the surrounding terrain, this quiet stream scarcely makes any sound of its own. There are no thundering waterfalls, nor turbulent rapids, nor babbling shallows along the course of the water; it seems content for now to simply drift.
15143: A crayfish is here, snapping its claws at you.

The water of this stream runs cool and slow, but it is somewhat deep. Flowing with the curvature of the land to the southwest, the water is cloudy with silt and mud which is blown into the water from the surrounding plains. Aside from the sound of water lapping against stones, and the wind drifting across the area, this place can be rather quiet.
15144: As it drains the flooded land to the northeast, this stream runs deep and narrow, as though forged in what was once a natural dam. The water itself continues downstream to the west, making almost no sound as it moves.

The land here is flat, and broad, and covered almost completely by a shallow water. The water, which seems to enter this place from the northeast at some distance, is cloudy from the soil that is blown into the air nearby, yet it is refreshed and washed away before it can become muddy.

15294: Here the tunnel is running straight east-west through the mountain. It is clearly not natural, walls and the floor bearing the clear marks of orkish tools used in carving it through the red rock. The air stands still and the silence seems to become even denser to the west, while from the east some distant orkish voices can be heard.
15295: The tunnel divides into three separate branches here. The main passage runs east to west while another small cavern lies to the north, its entrance carved carefully from the red rocks of the mountain. The tunnel floor is even and smooth here, looking almost polished.
15296:
A sturdy trained horse is standing here.
Oslicek, wielding a steel-shafted mattock, is standing here.
A stocky mountain mule is here, waiting to serve.
Chanis the Man, wielding an engraved warhammer, is standing here.
A large warhorse is standing here, clad in mail.
A stocky mountain mule is here, waiting to serve.

The tunnel comes to an abrupt end here, stopping at the piles of loose rocks and debris along the west wall. Obviously the expanding of the caves has been halted here for the time being. The only exit is back to the east.
15297:
The sage's bodyguard is here, watching the entrance.
The sage's bodyguard is here, watching the entrance.

You are standing in a cavern with a perfectly even floor. The stone walls are of the red rock of Caradhras, but carefully smoothed. To the east there is a doorway, covered with a silvery grey warghide. A single torch has been attached to the wall, illuminating the room with a low yellow flame.
15298:
A small round stone lies in the dust.
A small round stone lies in the dust.
A small round stone lies in the dust.
A small round stone lies in the dust.
A small round stone lies in the dust.
A small round stone lies in the dust.
A small round stone lies in the dust.
A small round stone lies in the dust.
A little stone lies on the ground.
A small round stone lies in the dust.
A small round stone lies in the dust.
A little stone lies on the ground.
A small round stone lies in the dust.
A small round stone lies in the dust.
A little stone lies on the ground.
A small round stone lies in the dust.
A small round stone lies in the dust.
A little stone lies on the ground.
A small round stone lies in the dust.
A small round stone lies in the dust.
A little stone lies on the ground.

You have entered a surprisingly comfortable room. Although hewn into the red rock of Caradhras, the walls are smooth and the ground is even, covered with a carpet. The cosy bed is by the east wall and a golden plaque with ancient runes has been attached to the wall right above it. The heavy wooden shelf with different books and few parchment scrolls is standing next to the bed. There is a low black door in the north wall. A half-burned candle is standing atop of the heavy oaken table, dimly illuminating the room.
15299: A cockroach is scuttling across the floor carrying some debris.

Here the passage bends yet again. Running through the red rock mountain base, it twists to the north and east, rising slightly in that direction. The deadly silence surrounds you and no light can be seen anywhere.
15300:
An uruk of the Morgundul tribe is here commanding his soldiers.
An uruk of the Morgundul tribe is here commanding his soldiers.
An orc-guard of the Morgundul is on patrol here.
The narrow tunnel is coming from the south and bends sharply to the west. On the eastern wall there is an opening, leading to the smaller cave. Litter and smaller rocks cover the ground everywhere.
15301: The stone tunnel runs north-south here, apparently widening to the south. Some flickering lights can also be seen in that direction. It has slightly descending slope towards north and the passage can be seen twisting left shortly there.
15302: Long shadows cast from a dimly lit cavern to the east illuminate the red stone typical to Caradhras. This worn tunnel slopes gently to the north and continues a winding path southwards.
15303: A dark oaken chest, embellished with silver, stands by the wall.

A small, totally isolated room has been carved into the solid mountain, no voice from outside can reach here. The austere stone walls and low ceiling further emphasizes the isolation, and it is obvious that this room is not visited very often. The stacks of books by the walls are covered by a thin layer of dust. A low door leaves back to the sage's chamber to the south.
15304: The tunnel seems to be twisting every short while, making it hard to keep track on what direction you are moving to. Its appearance is clearly natural, although the marks of occasional artificial widening can be seen here and there on the walls and the ceiling.
15305: The tunnel bends to the north-west, having a steeply descending slope towards the north. The floor is covered with some dust and debris and is apparently not very often walked upon.
15306: The tunnel floor is steeply descending to the north here and quite a few footholds have been hewn into the stone ground to offer some support. You notice a few cracks in the otherwise smooth rock walls. The tunnel continues to the south, where it can be seen rising slightly and taking a left turn.
15307: Here the tunnel splits into the three separate branches. The western one seems to lead into the small dry cave, while the main tunnel continues to the east and south. Towards south it can be seen rising steeply.
15308:
A wooden chest stands in the corner.
A water barrel has been left here.

You are in a small dry cave with a few shelves by the walls. Steep cracks run over most of the floor and ceiling which only a few rough wooden beams support. Dust and debris are everywhere and the whole place looks rather deserted. A tunnel is to the east, enshrouded in darkness.
15309: The stone tunnel runs east-west here. The air is somehow damp and there are few stalagmites hanging from the ceiling. Tunnel walls are glistening because of the small drops of condensed water and the floor has a slight downward slope towards the east. The sound of tinkling water can be heard from there.
15310: A grey snake slides along the water.

A great underground lake stretches out in the cavern, its smooth surface is black and undisturbed. Stalagmites can be seen in the ceiling and occasional waterdrops break the silence with quiet plops when hitting the water surface. The rising tunnel leaves to the west and neither light nor sound exist.
15311: A wiry and furtive-looking orc crouches here, eyeing your belongings.

This is a spacious cavern with reddish stone walls. The air is somewhat warmer here and loud snoring can be heard everywhere. Bundles of blankets and rugs are lying all around, as well as the remnants of food. The only apparent exit from this place is through a tunnel to the south.
15312: Here the passage becomes slightly narrower and bends yet again, this time to the north and east. It has a slight downward slope towards the north and the air seems to get warmer there.
15313:
An uruk of the Morgundul tribe is here commanding his soldiers.
An uruk of the Morgundul tribe is here commanding his soldiers.
An orc-guard of the Morgundul is on patrol here.
An orc-guard of the Morgundul is on patrol here.

The passage bends to the southwest, running deeper into the heart of the Caradhras. Far away to the south, one might see something that looks like a faint light. However, whether it is daylight or firelight or even a mirage tricking the weary cannot be known.
15315: A small cave leaves the main tunnel to the west here. The floor is covered with debris and the walls are roughly hewn into the solid rock of the mountain. The obvious intention has been to expand the main tunnel eastwards but for some reason the work has stopped.
15316:
The corpse of a small suspicious orc is lying here.
Radikas the Dwarf (rd), wielding an ornate, steel-shafted warhammer, is standing here.
Gata, wielding a mighty dwarven axe, is standing here.
Dan the Half-Elf, wielding a Dunadan blade, is standing here.

Here the small grotto leaves the passage running west of here. The ceiling and walls are blackened by the soot. A few wooden benches are by the walls and a cauldron of stew is bubbling on a low fire here. A mound of bones and guts is towering in the corner.
15317: You have entered a high majestic cavehall. The torches on the walls are burning with a yellow flame, emitting a dim light and smoke. The walls are of the red stone of Caradhras and the soil below has been trampled hard by countless feet. East of you, a tunnel leaves upwards into the mountain.
15318: The red rock walls of the cavehall disappear into the darkness high above. The torches on the wall emit a faint yellow light. West of here, the tunnel intersection can be seen in the eerie darkness. The cavehall continues to the north and east.
15319: A mailbox stands here stuffed full of messages.

You are standing at the north-west corner of the dimly lit cavehall, which continues to the east and south. The red rock walls, blackened by the smoke from the torches beam high above your head, the ground has been worn perfectly even by many feet. The faint sounds of yelling and growling seem to be coming from the east.
15320: In its north-east corner, the cavehall seems to become considerably lower, the faint outline of the ceiling can be guessed through the darkness. To the east you notice a small niche and a passage with a slight downward slope leaves to the north. Sounds of metal pounding against metal are coming from the east.
15321: You are standing on a wooden ladder, descending into the darkness below on a stairwell which has been hewn into the grey rock of the mountain. Above, you barely notice a trapdoor in the ceiling and north of here, occasional strange snarling can be heard.
15322: The narrow tunnel comes from the south and abruptly ends at the heavy metal grid in the west wall and you notice a heavy lock hanging through the metal loops. The smell of animals is filling the air and its origin seems to be coming from this direction.
15323:
A half-decayed corpse of a goblin lies rotting on the ground.
An emaciated warg, half-mad with hunger, is here.
An emaciated warg, half-mad with hunger, is here.

You have found out the origin of the growls you heard. It's a dark sullen cave, with the deep claw marks all over the stone walls. Above you can be seen a trap covering the opening, while to the east you notice a metal grid. There are also quite a lot of separate bones lying strewn about the cave floor.
15327: The trail seems to fade out into the mountain side as it comes downslope from the west. South, the ground dips down into a small space of rock below an overhange visible even from here. The many tall trees are more abundant here than farther up the mountain, and look to continue to grow more numerous to the south.
15328: There is a lot of snow on the ground.

A tall outcropping of rock forms the western wall of this place; the slope down remains unclimbable. Only to the south and north would you be able to get up out of this bit of sheltered rock. Although they can be seen in the distance in almost all directions, there is an absence of trees here. Small tufts of rough grass show in the short summer, but at all other times no life seems to live here.
15329: Nestled between tall mountain ridges, stony ledges and rocky overhangs, this extremely narrow trail would be almost invisible even from directly above, as it makes its way from a wider gully to the west into a craggy and inhospitable area to the east.
15330:
A mountain ibex is jumping from rock to rock.
A mountain ibex is jumping from rock to rock.
A mountain ibex is jumping from rock to rock.

To the south of you the trail begins to emerge from its hidden route, as it slowly makes its ascent toward the top of the ridgeline. To the east the mountainside ends in a dizzying drop into a snow-filled valley sheltered between two mountains.
15331: The serpentine ridgeline continues writhing and curving through the mountains. The path is treacherous as no foothold is safe, and if you trust your eyes, what appears to be firm may send you plunging to your death.
15332:
A cockroach is scuttling across the floor carrying some debris.
A hungry warg stands here, sniffing around for flesh.

Here the stairs have been carved into the rock, rising sharply upwards. On the wall, a thick rope is running through the metal loops fastened to the stone wall, offering some support. Here and there, the steps are rather worn out. Occasional breezes of fresh air are coming from above and darkness seems to get less dense in this direction.
15333: This is a low room with grey rock walls, dimly lit by six narrow windows, through which the icy wind is lashing in. Looking out of those you can see the Misty Mountains stretching far and wide to all directions, with the Redhorn Pass winding between the snow-capped peaks and dark crevices. To the north, Caradhras is rising to the sky in its splendour. A stone stairway descends into the darkness below.
15334: You are in an ancient tunnel that winds east. It has not been used in centuries. It slopes downward at an alarming rate and you have trouble keeping your balance.
15335: You are in an ancient tunnel that goes south and west. It appears it has not been used in centuries. The tunnel is very steep and you must be careful not to fall.
15336: You are an ancient tunnel that heads north. It does not seem to have been used in ages. It is very steep and you had best be careful walking here.
15337: A giant rat patters against you, squeaking maliciously.
You find yourself shivering in a dark, smelly cave. Strange sounds echo in the darkness. Great wooden doors lie against the north and east walls.
15338:
A powerful young troll stares at you.
An old, strong cave troll is standing here.
A powerful young troll stares at you.

The awful stench here is very unnerving. If that is not enough of a reason to leave there are several trolls here. They are currently resting on what you might call cots but they probably will not be resting for too long. You can see that numerous bones lie on the floor, perhaps the remains of adventurers like yourself.
15339:
A grey-skinned mountain troll stands here.
A grey-skinned mountain troll stands here.
A powerful young troll stares at you.

You can think of only one thing and that is how to rid your nose of the awful smell. You eyes glance around the cave and you determine that this is the sleeping cave for large, very cruel, and probably quite nasty mountain trolls. The floor is littered with bones, trash, and broken weapons and armour.
15340:
A cloak mottled in green and brown, and stinking to high heaven lies here (glows blue).
A little stone lies on the ground.
A rotten corpse is hanging here.
A powerful young troll stares at you.
A grey-skinned mountain troll stands here.
A grey-skinned mountain troll stands here.
A giant rat patters against you, squeaking maliciously.

This room has served the trolls as both a prison and treasure room. Many dwarves have sat in this very place awaiting dinner at the hands of the mountain trolls. You notice 'treasures' lie upon the shelves. Bones, dead lizards and other trash are heaped with care upon the racks.
15545: A pack horse is standing here, ridden by you.

Running in-between the thick thorns, the trail is hard to follow, disappearing almost completely from time to time. It is almost as if there was a wall of living bushes, moving around, trying to make the passage as hard as possible. The trail itself is old and obviously used rarely.
15546: An orkish warg-rider is here, riding a hungry warg.

The trail has become rather obscured and seemingly hidden from view, as the thorns tower over it on both sides. Strange echoes and weird glimpses of movement can be seen from within as they sway in the wind, like living walls all around you. The thorns are immensely thick and impassable, except to the north where a path has been cleared through them.
15547: This path has been hacked through the great thick thorns that seem eager to swallow the trail and cover every trace of it with their branches. Not much can be seen or heard, except the rustle of the thorns in the wind and an occasional bird. It should be possible to enter the dense thorns to the west, but to the east some bushes obstruct the way.
15548: Just south of the old stone bridge the path cuts through a small area of dense thornbushes, which tower over the trail and block any view of the surroundings. Judging by the dead branches lying on the trailside the thorns are pruned regularly, keeping the trail passable. The only other thing that catches the eye is a stone tower rising from a ruined keep, some distance to the southeast.
15549:
A orc patrol-leader of the Ohurk-uai is looking for enemies here.
An Ohurk-uai warg-rider, wielding a lance, is here, riding a hungry warg.
An Ohurk-uai warg-rider, wielding a lance, is here, riding a hungry warg.
An experienced orc scout is looking for tracks on the ground.

This old stone bridge stretches across a yawning crevice, from which the rumbling sound of fast flowing water can be heard. Remarkably well preserved, there is not a single sign that the elements have marred it in any way. The stone is still as smooth and finely chiselled as the day the bridge was built, with several different carvings still visible on the railings. The trail continues on both sides of the bridge, disappearing into some huge thorny bushes to the south. Further to the southeast a tower can be seen, but at this distance no details can be discerned.
15550: This old trail used to be well trodden, but nowadays it is abandoned and empty, used only by villains and those who want to stay out of sight. The trail itself is covered by gravel, the remains of the smooth stone that paved it in ancient days. Surrounded by plains trying to recover the area stolen from it, the trail fights an unfair and losing battle against nature.
15551: This section of the road seems to be a transition from a larger trail to the south into a more defined road, somewhat elevated from the surrounding plains. It runs in a roughly north-south line, dividing a large plain into a bushier section to the west, and a greener section to the east that looks as if it may have once been cultivated.
15552: The road bends east and south here, curving past a meadow located just to the north. Although the area does not seem to be farmed, the soil and climate both seem hospitable. Animal tracks can be seen leading north towards the green grass, as well as west towards the bushes. The plains seem to continue on northward for miles.
15553: The road runs north and west, curving beyond a large grassy area to the east and forming the northern edge of a large plain to the south of here. The surface is hard-packed dirt with a few scattered rocks on the ground here and there. The edges of the road are lined with rocks that may have once been placed there deliberately, but now have a haphazard appearance, having been knocked about over the years by patrols and other large groups moving through the area.
15554: The road runs a straight north-south course here, diving between two grassy fields that could be plots of farmland were they not still and quiet, except for the occasional traveller or animals passing through. The entire region seems to have been neglected over time, as if it were somehow unfit for habitation by anyone.
15555: The road continues on a north-south path, almost as straight as an arrow. The landscape to the west is rather barren, with only a few patches of grass growing here and there near the road. Off in the distance in that direction, one can barely see a large outcropping or some sort of cliff that seems to grow up out of the surrounding plains.
15556: The road travels from a large junction to the north straight south for several miles. To the east the road slopes downward into a thick, grassy field, quite a stark contrast from the barren, rocky landscape visible to the west. The terrain to the west offers little to the traveller, whereas the east seems to be a good resting place for mounts, or to take a break from the road.
15557: This large junction of the north-south road and a narrow trail running west and east seems to be a meeting place of some sort. Large rocks have been erected to offer some small respite from the elements, but years of weather have worn them down, making them all but useless as shelter. The narrow trail runs west along the river and east into an overgrown section, seemingly the less travelled of the two directions. The road itself continues on as a hard-packed dirt surface moving steadily north towards the rapids, and south towards grassy plains.
15558: The road bends here from east to south, winding along the high ground above the River Bruinen. The River flows rapidly southward, hitting the wall below and creating a small whirlpool from the backwash. To the west of here the river has slowed down quite a bit as it pours into a deeper course. A small junction lies just to the south of here.
15559: The road runs along a straight course here as hard, packed dirt. A few pebbles and small rocks break up the otherwise solid reddish brown surface. Towards the east grass seems to spring up out of nowhere, and small flowers grow alongside the road, leading towards a full field of bright flowers. The southern section of the road leads onto an old trail that has been overgrown with bushes.
15560:
A restless rabbit bounces around.
A hungry warg (Rood) is standing here, ridden by you.

This section of road seems to have been formed out of a high river bluff that has slowly eroded away over the centuries. The road runs east and south here, following the Bruinen river as it picks up speed and depth on its southward course. The ground slopes gently towards the river and is adorned with very few plants or trees.
15561: The dirt road bends north and west. A few rocks are scattered across its surface and some larger boulders lie to the sides of the road. On the southern edge a field of brightly flowering plants and shrubs seems to spring up out of a grassy field, whereas the surroundings to the east appear to be just green grass with clover cropping up intermittently.
15562: The stream to the east has soaked up so much water from the lands around it, that it has become a small river when it flows into here. A shadowy finger of the northern forests touches the north bank of the river and provides a bit of shade for that edge of the river.
15563: The stream is slowly beginning to grow and deepen as it leaves the forested areas north of here. Runoff from the plains to the east, and from atop the cliff to the south, adds to the stream. With no massive forest to drink from the stream, or to prevent water from making it to the stream, it has begun to deepen and widen here. To the west it might even grow to be a real river. The stream has dug into the southern slope of crumbling rock, turning it into a near vertical wall of rock that is too unsafe to climb.
15564: A small animal, all covered in spines, snuffles amongst the undergrowth.

This bank, of the stream to the west, is not very firm. Water from the stream has crept its way underground and up to near the surface here. Holes here are quickly filled by water from the surrounding moist soil. Only in a few spots, where stone lies close under the surface, is the soil hard packed. Elsewhere the ground becomes more like the dragging mud that can be found in a swamp. The vegetation here is a mixture of grasses and plants that like to grow in bogs. Farther north the ground is moister and even less firm. Drier land lies to the south and east where slopes rise up from here.
15565: Low green grass covers this plain with only a few shrubs to break its stark simplicity. At the western edge of the plain is the beginning of a slope that descends slightly and is covered in more varied vegetation than this plain. The plain stretches out into the distance at the other compass points.
15566: A plain of rich, golden stalks of wheat is before you in any direction you turn except to the south, where a narrow ravine cuts into the plain and begins to slope gently downwards. No trees, shrubs, rocks, or other features break the line of the horizon in the other directions.
15567: Golden grass covers this field, intermixed with weeds and a wild mixture of other small plants. Lines of plants show that the field was once cultivated, but neglect and time has all but destroyed the work of the cultivators. Small thorny shrubs block the route to the north, but nothing blocks travel to the plains in the other directions.
15568: The garden snake slithers harmlessly here.

This plain lies covered in small plants, perhaps placed, perhaps from seeds blown by the wind; only hints of a pattern exist. A light smattering of small trees covers this area, and helps to protect the soil from being blown away by any winds that cross this flat area. Patches of grass and taller varieties of plants grow near the western edge of this plain. A jagged outcropping of rock, and a number of large boulders, prevent travel to the east and north.
15569: A meadow of tall, green grass stretches out around you in all directions except the west. The grass is very resistant to movement, springing back up soon after all but the heaviest tread lifts off it. To the west a line of boulders, and a jagged outcropping of rock, prevents travel or sight in that direction.
15570:
A shallow pond is here, tinted green with algae.
The wild ox seems ready to charge you.

Tall brown and yellow grass contests with the equally tall green grass to dominate this meadow. A few small bushes grow around a pond that lies just slightly south of the centre of this large meadow. The meadow stretches to the south and west, while plains begin to the east.
15571: This grassy plain is a mixing area for several varieties of grass. Tall yellow and brown grass, short bright green grass, and a more densely packed dark green grass have grown inwards from the western, southern and eastern edges of this plain. A deep depression lies to the north, but there is no access from this point because of the sharp drop. The land slopes upwards gradually to the south, and far to the south the land rises to an area that overlooks this plain.
15572: An Ohurk-uai warg-rider, wielding a lance, is here, riding a hungry warg.

Sloping plains gradually rise westward towards grass-covered plains which connect to a much higher plateau overlooking the great river Bruinen southeast of here. The land still remembers the old road but there are few signs of it now. A rocky wall to the south prevents passage in that direction.
15573: A large brown wolf stands here, its teeth partly bared.

This low plateau lies to the south of some lowlands. The plains stretch for miles to the west, sloping gently upwards and becoming less inhabited in that direction. To the south the plains end abruptly as they encounter the near vertical wall of a much higher plateau. The short grass underfoot is thick and does not let even a single flower or tall weed penetrate its green body.
15574:
An orkish warg-rider, wielding a lance, is here, riding a hungry warg.
A hungry warg is standing here, ridden by an orkish warg-rider.

The plateau continues on flat and fertile to the west. To the east and south the grassy ground drops steeply into the river, winding its way through the surrounding landscape like a jagged knife wound. Beyond the river one can make out a lower landscape and the beginnings of some marshlands.
15575: The prominent fin of a silver-yellow fish breaks the surface of the water.

The river cuts its way through the western plateaus, meandering through the landscape. It flows gently towards the south here, through a river valley that was formed many years ago. Towards the west, solid ground is too high up to climb to without any footholds on the sheer face. The water is muddy in that section, where it has continued to eat away at the base of the cliffs.
15576: The river flows steadily from the north, and curves gently towards the west. The surface is calm, with small whirlpools continuously forming and breaking apart at the southern edge. The bank there is not very steep, and it would be quite easy to leave the water there. Along the bank are a lot of covering river-growing weeds. The road lies just beyond, following the course of the river.
15577: The road runs east and south here, at the foot of a large ridge that extends towards the north. The roar of the Bruinen River is loud, as it makes its way southward just to the west of here. A small slope leads downward towards the river valley, making it possible to enter the water from here. The road curves west following the course of the river.
15578: The trail widens into a large road, composed of dark brown dirt. On either side of the roadway short grass grows tightly cropped to the ground. The river can be heard roaring in the distance to the west. The road leads in that direction, as well as to the north as a narrowing trail. A large field of grass grows abundantly to the east.
15579: A buck runs swiftly from place to place, looking about warily as it grazes.

An odd mixture of grasses grows here. Emerald stalks are intermingled with short, dark green mosses and blades of medium height. The shades of green range from being so dark that they are almost black to a pale colour that is little more than white. To the south lies an immense floodplain that one could easily mistake for a pond after a heavy downpour. An overgrown trail leads east and west.
15580: At first sight, the seemingly endless plains look monotonous. Upon close examination, however, it becomes evident that they are made up of a variety of different grasses. Some stand motionless with their panicles thrust into the air while others wave feather-like in the wind as if celebrating life. An overgrown trail leads east and west.
15581: The ground slopes gradually downward into the beginnings of a small valley. A blanket of grass covers the ground, with patches of moss and a few trees. The footing is fairly even, making it quite easy to travel on a mount. Towards the south shrubs dominate the view, growing in small clumps in the rocky soil. An overgrown trail leads west.
15582: The hard dirt surface leads north and west through grassy fields. The road is lined with a few small shrubs and some brightly coloured flowers. The occasional rabbit or other small animal scurries for cover at the sound of travellers and their mounts. To the south a large pasture is visible, and would seem a likely spot to rest on a long journey.
15583: The road curves east and south here, following the contours of the Bruinen River which flows to the north and west of here. The river seems to have cut its course out of the surrounding terrain, creating a large bluff on the far side of it. The dark brown surface of the road is marked with hoof prints and other signs that show it is still travelled.
15584: The prominent fin of a silver-yellow fish breaks the surface of the water.

These bends in the river were formed long ago when it first cut through the landscape, following some contours or underground rock beds along its path. The river flows from south to west here, leaving two places where one could easily leave the water for solid land. Roads lie to the east and south, and one could easily assume that they meet somewhere in southeast. The water flowing west begins to pick up speed as it heads for another bend.
15585:
A large sturgeon swims slowly along the bottom.
A large sturgeon swims slowly along the bottom.

The river cuts its way through the plateaus, creating a deep trench in its course east and south. High up to the north a grassy plateau is visible but it would require climbing from here to reach it. The dirt face of the rock wall has several roots and crevices that could serve as handholds if one wanted to scale it. To the west however, the sheer vertical climb would be impossible. The river continues on southward, steadily picking up speed.
15586:
A orc patrol-leader of the Ohurk-uai is looking for enemies here.
An orc sentry of the Ohurk-uai is here on patrol.
An orc soldier of the Ohurk-uai is here, patrolling the area.

This is the highest of several plateaus in the surrounding area, defined by the River Bruinen cutting its course through the landscape to the east. As it runs south of here it begins to bend, rushing by the base of the outcropping. Far below to the north a low-lying plain spreads out towards the east, while to the west the ground slopes gently downwards to a grassy plain.
15587: The plain climbs eastward towards a high plateau while in the northeast there is a low plateau. There is a lot of grass on the ground but very few flowers can be seen, making for a somewhat barren blanket of short grass. The sound of running water indicates that a large river flows nearby. The ground to the north drops down sharply to a lower area.
15588: A swallow flies high above the ground.

This nearly flat plain is covered in small bushes, shrubs and a type of short, bright green grass. A subtle slope begins near the centre of this plain and slopes down into the east and north. The slope and its effect on water on the plain have caused the bushes to grow more densely towards the bottom of the slope, where more water is absorbed as it leaves here after a rainfall. The land rises slightly to the south allowing a clear view of this plain.
15589: A garden snake slithers harmlessly here.

Tall green stalks of grass mix with some shrubs and numerous bushes to cover this meadow in greenery. The plants change slowly from the dominant bushes in the south to the more open grassy areas in the north and west. Eastwards the land grows somewhat more barren and flat. A gentle slope leads down from here into the south.
15590: A thick green carpet of grass dominates this large meadow. The grass blades grow closely together and make it hard to see anything smaller than a foot tall except for the ripples in the grass caused when something moves. The same plants and terrain stretch outwards at the north and east sides of this meadow. Tiny hills begin to appear near the western border of the meadow, only visible because of the nearly perfect horizon they rise out of. A sheer cliff drops down to the south, and beyond it in the distance is a tower on a mound that looks down on this cliff top meadow.
15591: Deep grass covers the tiny valleys formed by small hills here, each of about two or three feet in height. The tall grass partly hides the hills but they are still readily apparent against the flat plains around here. The land flattens and remains mainly covered in grass towards the north and south. The eastern and western directions however tend to a larger variety of plants, and the land in the east is not quite as flat as around the other edges of these hills.
15592: A wild bull seems ready to charge you.

Tall green grass, intermixed with weed-choked shrubs, covers this plain. To the west is a narrow ravine, with low cliff walls, which prevents travel that way. The grass stretches off in all directions except the west, but in each of the directions the shrubs make way for other types of plant life or disappear.
15593: This narrow ravine starts in the plains to the north and grows wider as it deepens to the south. The low but almost vertical walls could easily be climbed if the rock was more stable. The floor of the ravine is a gentle slope covered in small boulders and outcroppings of rock.
15594:
A very strong, orkish patrol-leader is looking for enemies here.
An orkish soldier is here, patrolling the area.
An orkish soldier is here, patrolling the area.

This plain of low, green grass contrasts sharply with the higher plants and small trees that grow in the west. The plain becomes somewhat more rocky and less grassy towards the south. East of here is a narrow ravine, its sides are like low cliffs, making travel impossible that way.
15595: This field is covered in foot long grass, small shrubs, and some small but straight trees. Only a few trees exist here, and none seem to exist near the edge of the plain. Dense, lush patches of flora grow at the northern border of this plain, where it slopes down. Numerous small game trails go to and from here into the watery lands in the north, and the surrounding plains.
15596: A flat plain of low grass, lacking trees or bushes, lies here. Dangerous slopes drop from the western and northern edges of the field to the water below. At the bottom of the north slope is a stream that turns there from north to west. The western edge of this plain descends sharply to a small river.
15597: From the north this small river flows through here and into the west. A tall hill with a steep slope of crumbling rock rises to the east, blocking travel, so that travellers can only go to the south and north. Bushes in the field to the south line the banks of the river and hang over it in many places.
15598: The high plateau to the north shelters this place from the cold northern winds during the winter. It would be difficult to climb up there from here, as the plateau above extends over this area, making a sheltered hollow underneath it with a depression in the dirt wall at the back. To the east a deep river flows quickly, while a shallower section lies to the south.
15599: The prominent fin of a silver-yellow fish breaks the surface of the water.

The river bends east and south, creating a dirt wall to the north and a deeply cut river valley to the east. The cliff to the north has enough hand and foot holds that one could climb up to the plateau above. The terrain to the west seems to be an ideal area to climb out of the river, as the ground slopes gently into the river.
15600: A large sturgeon swims slowly along the bottom.
High above the river, to the east and south, is a well-travelled road. The riverbank is steep and slippery to the east, making it hard for anyone to scale it. The river bends abruptly to the west.
15601:
A noticeable crack runs down one of the walls.
An orc of the Ohurk-uai stands here, cursing and grumbling.
A burly orc-guard is here, sniffing at the air.
A burly orc-guard is here, sniffing at the air.
An orc of the Ohurk-uai stands here, cursing and grumbling.

Under the shelter of the jagged rock ceiling this tunnel is shaded from bright sunlight and the elements. The rock walls seem to have been hewn by sheer force, with no thought to architecture or planning. The rock itself is a greyish white, hard and somewhat brittle. The cave seems to lead down and inward while both north and south the walls do not look quite right. Among the piles of rubbish on the floor discarded, and in many cases broken, pieces of armour and weaponry can be seen.
15602:
The corpse of an Ohurk-uai cook is lying here.
The corpse of an Ohurk-uai foot-soldier is lying here.
The corpse of an Ohurk-uai foot-soldier is lying here.
The corpse of an Ohurk-uai foot-soldier is lying here.
A large stone fireplace with a roaring fire warms the room.

The wall is cut in a roughly circular pattern. A niche in the wall seems to have been smashed with a single, mighty stroke of a club, but only rubble lies there now. The walls curve about you, jagged with stones that threaten to scratch skin and tear at clothing. A single, crudely made table stands in the centre of the room, covered with junk. The dust on the floor looks more disturbed than usual, as if something had been covered up.
15603: A noticeable crack runs down one of the walls.

The dark and cold water flows steadily southward through numerous cracks. None of them are wide enough for you to pass through. Upwards is a dry and rough cave. The exit to the east is completely filled with cold and dark water.
15604: The River Bruinen seems to have a parallel underwater stream flowing westwards along the river's bottom. The water is cold and dark, and nothing but weeds seems to inhabit this waterway.
15605: The water of the river is nice and fresh here, but closer to the bottom it grows dark and murky. At the very bottom, a weak underwater current flows westward through an opening in the riverbed. Looking upward, you see the riverbank with a trail passing along it just above the surface of the water.
15606:
A sturdy peg for hanging armour from is on the wall.
A large, dusty alcove sits in a wall, smelling of soot.
A wooden chest stands in the corner.
A strong, tall orc-guard is looking for enemies here.
A strong, tall orc-guard is looking for enemies here.
A strong, tall orc-guard is looking for enemies here.
The Ohurk-uai orc chief is here, leading his tribe.

A chamber obviously designed for resting, this room is filled with mats of animal hide and bunches of cloth wadded together to form primitive pillows. Along one wall bones and scraps of meat have been piled to create a mound of animal waste. At the back of the cavern old weapons and tools have been piled, although most of them appear unusable.
15607: The prominent fin of a silver-yellow fish breaks the surface of the water.

The river splits here, with a section flowing eastward into an underground waterway. Pushing through an opening low down in the eastern wall the icy black water flows turbulently over a collection of sharp rocks and onwards through a submerged tunnel. Westwards it becomes shallow and the already fast flowing water gains some more speed.
15608: This easy swim crossing seems to never freeze, nestled between the even faster waters to the east and the wide waters to the west. North a small sheltered area is visible and south a narrow trail runs east and west near a high cliff.
15609: The river flows through here from east to west, fairly wide and clear, and of medium depth. The jagged rocks on the south bank and the northern cliff, that overlooks the river, prevent travel in those directions, only travel upstream and downstream is possible from here.
15610:
The prominent fin of a silver-yellow fish breaks the surface of the water.
Klaees (thedon), wielding a great warsword, is standing here.
Drazud (freshmeat), wielding a great warsword, is standing here.
Bulg (pukespy), wielding a great warsword, is standing here.

The river seems to be somewhat shallow here, especially on the north side where a shallow slope begins underwater and continues above the water into the distance northwards. The depth of the river is still too deep to attempt to ford here without swimming or a small watercraft such as a raft. A landing can be seen on both the south and the north shores, marking where river traffic might be able to land.
15611: The prominent fin of a silver-yellow fish breaks the surface of the water.

The flow of the river here is quick despite the river being wide and deep. Clear water here lets you see quite deep into it as it moves from the east to the west. A giant mound of stone and earth rises to a shattered tower in the south that overlooks the river here. The rocky riverbank makes travel to and from the field, north of here, awkward but not impossible.
15612: A large river flows from the east to here, with a slightly muddy tributary adding to the river from the south, before they flow west together. The darker water from the tributary can easily be seen as it forces its way deep into the heart of the Bruinen before being swept along west by the powerful current of the river. A tall, sheer cliff blocks travel to the north.
15613:
The prominent fin of a silver-yellow fish breaks the surface of the water.
A brook trout is here, swimming in the current.

The river here is slightly muddy, and is somewhat wider than upriver to the east. There is no shore to the north where a high cliff rises above the river. South of here is a plain that is only a bit higher than the regular flow of the river, according to water marks on the cliff, and could easily be flooded if the water flowing through here was even a foot higher.
15614: The river widens a bit here as it flows into the west. A wide ravine breaks the cliffs that wall the northern side of the river. It is possible to leave the river to both the north and the south. The border of the field to the south is covered in deep grass and shrubs.
15615: The river is flowing fairly swiftly here from the east to the west under a high cliff rising on the north side of the river. The river is narrower at the centre of this stretch because of boulders lying along the south bank that extends into the river. To the both the east and west the river widens somewhat. Beyond the rocky south bank lies a rocky covered field.
15616: The river is deep and wide at this point as it flows down this river valley. The water flows from east to west, passing underneath a cliff that overhangs much of the river on the north side. A field with a pebbled bank lies to the south.
15617: A large eagle soars above you.

The river Bruinen rushes swiftly along its course here, from the east into the south. A soft rushing noise comes to you from the south. A stone bank, with watermarks up its side, prevents the river from flowing westward to the plain there. A tall, sheer cliff borders the river to the north.
15618: This plain of grass and silt piles lies just above the level of the river to the south. The plain is slightly below the river to the east with only a low stone bank preventing this plain from being underwater all the time. Northwards the land slopes up slightly and begins to be covered in small bushes.
15619: This flat, grassy bluff stands above the lands to the east, west, north and looks down on the river to the south. A long sheer drop lies on the eastern and southern sides, but on the western side the drop-off becomes shorter the further to the north you go, ceasing to be a cliff at some distance to the northwest. The view from here commands the area around it.
15620:
A orc patrol-leader of the Ohurk-uai is looking for enemies here.
An Ohurk-uai soldier, wielding a scimitar, is here, fighting Klaees (thedon).
An Ohurk-uai soldier, wielding a scimitar, is here, fighting Klaees (thedon).
Klaees (thedon), wielding a great warsword, is here, fighting an Ohurk-uai soldier.
Drazud (freshmeat), wielding a great warsword, is standing here.
Bulg (pukespy), wielding a great warsword, is here, fighting an Ohurk-uai soldier.

This gentle slope runs from the meadows in the north down to the river. It also slopes down to the west, a bit, so that it is just above the rivers flow there, making the highest point of the slope in the northeast, and the lowest at the southwest. A high cliff rises to the east, preventing travel that way, and also allowing those on top to view this slope. A few large blocks form a line from the west to a landing here on the shore of the river.
15621: An abandoned quarry lies here, with blocks of stone scattered around that have been removed from the sides of the north and west cliffs. A trail of large blocks runs in a scattered pattern from the cliffs towards the east. Smaller, more finely shaped blocks are piled near the cliff. All the blocks are in excellent condition to be used in buildings, but were apparently abandoned here. To the east lies a sloped area, and beyond it lies a cliff top which overlooks this quarry.
15622: The land here has been worn by wind and water, forming small gullies and ridges. Small broad ridges of three to five feet in height run towards the north where they have breaks in them and look like hills. Short grass covers both the ridges and the gullies. The gullies run to the edges of cliffs east and south. To the far east if a place on top of a cliff that can oversee these ridges.
15623: This plain is covered in foot high golden grass with a few large trees scattered through it. Its bounded on the west by a broad ravine with high walls, and by a cliff overlooking the river to the south. This flat land continues into the north, but eastwards the ground begins to ripple like waves on an ocean.
15624: This wide gully has a gentle slope running from the north, down to the Bruinen in the south. Beneath the tall cliffs that form the sides of the gully are small boulders and rocks. A smooth path has been carved into the centre of the floor of the ravine, and it would seem that this was made by water rushing down toward the river below. The path offers an easy route for travelling up or down the canyon.
15625: A brown fox is here, looking for some rabbits to chew up.

Short grass and lichen grow here, between the rocks and on them respectively. A broad ravine cuts sharply into this plain to the east, with almost vertical slopes on the sides. To the south is a cliff that overlooks the river and stretches into the west.
15626: The sparse vegetation and thin soil here barely covers the rock of the plain. The southern edge of this plain hangs over the river so that only part of the river can be seen without leaning over the edge of the cliff. To the east and west the cliff continues, and so does the sparse vegetation.
15627: This cliff overlooks the river to the south and is covered with short grasses, and a few defiant trees bent from the winds that blow down the river valley. A sheer cliff drops to the west, but to the north and east the land bordering this plain continues to be flat.
15628:
A shrub with maple-like leaves is growing here.
On the shrub, there are two handfuls of blackcurrant berries.
A small grasshopper clings to a blade of grass, ready to spring.
A small grasshopper clings to a blade of grass, ready to spring.
A small grasshopper clings to a blade of grass, ready to spring.

Low shrubs and small berry bushes cover the ground here, with small areas of grass between them. The brush of this field grows almost over the edge of the small river to the north. This land is bounded by a cliff to the east that seems to grow higher as this field slopes gently down, towards the south, to a plain.
15629:
A light boat made of reeds has been left here.
A big cavebear is padding around here.

This cave rises at a slight angle and has a small bend at the entrance. Its shape prevents the full light of day reaching deep into the interior. The rough natural lines of the walls have been smoothed in spots, and in other places shelves and benches have been cut from the rock.
15630: A large beautiful rose bush is blooming here.

The rough terrain allows only for meagre plant growth. A few bushes and hearty weeds manage to survive on the moisture they absorb from the rocky soil. The ground is somewhat higher in elevation than the surroundings. Any rains that might fall here quickly flow downward into a valley towards the north, or into a low-lying floodplain to the west.
15631: Unlike the various grasslands surrounding it, this tiny piece of Arda is filled with a variety of shrubs and bushy plants. No trees are in evidence. In fact, nothing higher than a man's waist or lower than a horse's knee grows here. One might expect grass to fill in the places between the shrubs, but that is not the case in this landscape.
15632: After a heavy downpour the water seems to hover above the surface before being absorbed into the soil. The ground seems to be saturated with water without becoming a muddy mess. This may have once been a flood plain for the nearby river when it overflowed. Now, however, the river has instead cut a path through the surrounding landscape.
15633: A porcupine is waddling around here, its tail full of sharp quills.

The grass stands at various heights as if it were intentionally kept short near to the road on the north and western edges. Towards the east it grows more lushly in the damper soil. It gradually increases in height as it moves to the south. When the air is still, one can sometimes hear the quiet roar of the Bruinen River.
15634: Unlike the rolling grasslands to the south of here the raised ground is only covered by a thin layer of grass, growing closely to the surface. Shadowed by some foothills further to the west, and by the higher ground just to the north, very little vegetation grows here. The soil is also rocky, with very little moisture that might allow some mosses to grow.
15635: The ground is barely covered with grass; great brown patches of bare earth seem to dominate the view. For some reason no hearty vegetation ever made its way here. Rocks are visible in the soil, but do not hinder progress. Unlike the verdant surroundings they are not covered with any moss, and the presence of sunlight would prevent any lichens from growing here.
15636: The bright purple stems of heather dominate the view. As this field is open to the elements, the plant does not grow very high, perhaps just a few inches off the ground. The bell-shaped flowers of the plant are visible for most of the year. Towards the east a plain coverage of sparse vegetation is visible, whereas the view to the south is filled by a bright green sea of grass.
15637: The tall grass is very dense, and seems to spring up out of the soft ground. Crabgrass and other weeds grow in clumps through the area, but the dominant foliage is definitely the tall blades of grass that shift gently in the breeze, making them come alive to the onlooker. To the south a similar scene unfolds although without the same vigour of the grass.
15638: Bright green grass grows abundantly out of the soft dirt. The southern edges of it are marked, as if there had been a great fire. The grass there does not grow very high, just a few inches above the ground. This green carpet continues on to the east.
15639: Supplied by rainwater flowing down from some foothills to the east, and higher ground to the north, hearty grass thrives here, covering the ground almost completely. An occasional large rock stands alone against the verdant backdrop, perhaps the remains of a great boulder that once rolled down from the mountains of the Misty Mountains far to the east.
15640: Unlike the sparse ground cover to the north of here, the tall sea of grass seems to go on for miles in all directions, except to the south-west where the land takes on a marshy appearance. Here, small burrowing animals or an occasional snake can be seen darting about among the thick blades of grass.
15641: This is the northwestern corner of what seems to be a great grassland area that continues onwards east and southeast for miles. Although there are a few hills the entire area seems to be on raised ground, or perhaps it is just that to the south the marshy ground has sunken deeper. Bright, violet heather seems to grow along the northern edge of this wading grass.
15642: The grass grows to a medium height with an occasional shrub or small flower hidden among the tussocks. The earth seems to roll gently eastward, creating small valleys. To the south the ground is much lower than on this tiny ridge, and seems to absorb much of the runoff water from the surroundings. To the west the earth looks barren and the vegetation blackened by fire.
15643: Although there are no signs that the earth was recently burned, signs of a fire long ago are everywhere. What were once trees are now blackened husks. A few are still standing, but most are fallen logs. A bit of grass and a few weeds manage to grow among these charred remains. Whether it was a great battle or some force of nature is not known.
15644: This large field of brightly coloured flowers lies near a large bend in the road to the northwest. In the warm season, a variety of poppies and forget-me- nots seem to thrive among other flowers and bunches of large shrubs with bright orange blooms. The grass underfoot is a bright green colour. To the east, however, the field looks blackened as if it were once burned.
15645: A bright, green grass covers the entire landscape. Even in the colder months of the year the blades manage to maintain their appearance, encased in frost or ice as the weather dictates. In the warm seasons a quiet wind can be seen rippling across the surface, like waves across a great, gentle ocean; but there is no ocean nearby, only the River Bruinen flowing far to the west.
15646: This was perhaps a section of foothills of the Misty Mountains farther to the east. The plain is by no means flat as the name might imply. It rolls forward to the south, as if the passage of years had eroded the hills and shaped the landscape to become a series of peaks and valleys that are neither very tall nor very deep. To the west, behind thich bushes, the sides of these undulating plains dip downwards into a wet lowland. Thorny bushes prevents you going west.
15647: Perhaps these plains were once part of the floodplains of the mighty Bruinen in times past, or of some unknown river that flowed from the Misty Mountains, but now has run dry. One could imagine that the waving plains were a series of natural levees and that the water would flow over one and into the next, receding over decades to leave behind this odd plain, the land fertile for plant life. Thorny bushes prevents you going west.
15648: A porcupine is waddling around here, its tail full of sharp quills.

The ground underfoot is quite rich in nutrients. This is clear from the dark soil that lies here, almost free of rocks. Large puddles are formed on the surface after rainstorms, an inviting sight for various birds. Small bushes to the east seem to be a nesting ground for quail and other game birds, which can sometimes be seen here.
15649: Because a fen such as this would normally lie close to a river, one could guess that there is an underground river or other large water source flowing deep under the ground that surfaces here. The fen seems to continue on for some distance to the west, making it impossible to ride. Towards the south, one would have to wade some distance to reach solid ground.
15651: This small hill stands at the edge of a large swamp, almost as if placed there as a sentinel. It is covered by grass and small plants, and the crown of the hill is littered by small yellow flowers. Not much can be heard except the buzzing from the swamps to the west, but the view is excellent. The landscape all around here is like a large thick blanket of green, billowing in the wind. On the horizon, far to the southwest, an old tower can be spotted in the haze.
15652: Standing just north of the stream, this small hill provides it with water in the early spring as snow melts and the water starts to flow down along the sides of the hill. The hill itself is rather low and flat, but its location near the stream makes it thrive, the grass and flowers covering it completely in a colourful pattern when spring sets in.
15653: A green frog is here, hopping around.

Here the small stream starts its westward passage. Already growing in strength and speed, it still has a long way to go before it becomes the wild and rapid river that joins up with Bruinen far to the west of here. Flowing sedately westwards, it makes its way through the small hills.
15654:
A clear spring babbles as cool water trickles out of the ground.
A bass swims here.
A bass swims here.

Small trickling streams of water, slowly making their way here from the nearby hills, gather to form the beginning of one of the tributaries to the mighty and powerful river Bruinen. As the water gathers and begins its arduous journey west, it is the birth of a small, albeit steady, stream of life.
15655: The stream runs swiftly here, between hills to the north and the grassy plains to the south. Not yet a river, it rushes west as fast as it can, eager to join Bruinen. West of here it seems to slow down, broadening as it reaches the marshlands where it joins with other small streams to form a river.
15656:
A frog is standing here.
A frog is standing here.

The small stream to the east becomes a river here, broader and deeper but not any swifter. Much of the river merges with the surrounding marshland, becoming stagnant in the swamps to the north. Another small stream flows in from the swampland, forming a delta. Together they form one of the many tributaries of the Bruinen.
