15657: A Shallow and Marshy Part of the River

You can see that here used to be a trail fording the river, since the stones marking the passage still stand on the riverside. The trail itself is rather overgrown and broken to the south, and disappears entirely to the north, where it has long been submerged. The surrounding ground is rather marshy, turning into noisome swamp to the northeast.
15658:
A brook trout is here, swimming in the current.
A brook trout is here, swimming in the current.
A brook trout is here, swimming in the current.

Here the river is deep and broad, flowing rapidly downstream to the west. North lie some hills, while to the south are some old and overgrown fields that have long been abandoned. A few birds hover over the water here trying to catch today's meal as the river is rather rich in wildlife.
15659: A River below an Ancient Stone Wall

The river runs swiftly below an old stone wall here. The old lord of the castle above seems to have used both the wall and the river for his defence, making entering the keep from this direction near impossible. Parts of the ancient wall have been undermined by the water and have collapsed, forcing the river to flow along a slightly different path.
15660: A brook trout is here, swimming in the current.

Swift and powerful the river runs west, dragging debris and some dead trees with it. It is hard to spot anything on the banks here at the speed the river flows at, but one thing is noticeable - a tower above you on the cliff top. Standing like a sentinel on the southern bank, it overlooks the surrounding land.
15661: The river speeds up as it enters a small canyon here, making a sharp turn around the cliffs to the west. Strange sounds echo between the walls that surround you, as the river roars through the gorge. There seems to be no easy way to leave the river here, as the walls are slippery and steep.
15662: Running swiftly and noisily westward, the river is deep and cold. It is almost as if the river is eager to join with the Bruinen far downriver. The banks are rather steep, and it would take some effort to climb up them. Not much of the surrounding landscape beyond the river is distinctive, but one thing makes itself known. A tower, dark and lofty, rises high enough for you to notice it on the southern horizon.
15663: Roaring westwards, deafening in its might, the river hurls itself forward in its long search for a companion. The walls of the canyon it runs through are steep, and impossible to climb to the south. Atop the northern bank little can be seen except the sky, and some dense vegetation poking over the edges. The slope is high and probably hard to climb, so leaving the river here could prove both taxing and dangerous.
15664: Making a sharp turn the water plunges northwards on its journey towards the mighty River Bruinen. Strange sounds echo between the cliff walls and white foam flies into the air as the water smashes into the sheer rock of the walls.
15665: Rushing swiftly westwards the white foaming water makes a deafening sound as it echoes among the high cliff walls. A white mist hangs in the air and everything is both wet and slippery.
15666: White mist hangs in the air as the water hurls itself over the cliff's edge. A deafening roar drowns all other sounds and the air is damp. The steep cliff walls surrounding this area, and everything around, is wet and slippery, thus becoming impossible to climb. Drawing towards the edge, the water eagerly rushes forth towards the mighty Bruinen.
15667: Basin at the Base of the Waterfall

A bass swims here.
A swallow flies high above the ground.

A large waterfall, easily eighty feet tall, drops from the south to the basin here. The water from the waterfall drops into this deep basin and then flows westwards out of the basin as a swift river. The flow is constant and the rock faces on the east and south cliffs are always slippery. A low, jagged wall running from the eastern cliff blocks travel to the north.
15669: A brook trout is here, swimming in the current.

Swirling swiftly around the bend to the south the river bubbles and foams its way to the north, slowing slightly as it widens and runs towards the tower showing in the distance. To the east a narrow field sits perched precariously between the cliff and the river, while to the west a few decayed wooden posts appear to mark the boundary of an old pasture.
15670: This river flows swiftly from the south to here and then north in a long line. Large ditches run from the western edge of the river deeper into the western field. Loose earth and silt has blocked the ditches so that no water flows in them. The eastern bank is quite rocky, but travel onto it is still possible. A tower upon a mound lies far to the north and overlooks this part of the river.
15671: A wide river flows through here, swiftly passing northwards over a shallow part of the riverbed. Small ditches run from the edges of the west side of the river into a bleak looking field. The eastern bank shows a great deal more life along the rivers edge. Far to the north a tower on a great mound looks down on this part of the river.
15672: A brook trout is here, swimming in the current.

This section of the river is still quite fast as it rounds this gentle curve, bringing the water from the south along the curve and into the west. The water is slightly dark with silt, but still fairly clear. A stone and earth mound to the north rises sharply from the river until it reaches the ruined tower that overlooks this river. A barren field stretches along the waters edge to the east.
15673: This small, fast river flows from the east, through here, into the north. A few large rocks can be seen above the waterline, with more below causing a few ripples and eddies at the waters surface. Despite the rocks there is ample room for people to safely travel along the river.
15674:
A brook trout is here, swimming in the current.
A brook trout is here, swimming in the current.

A slightly muddy river runs from the south of here, widening and slowing as it flows into the north. A plain lies to the west, only slightly higher than the normal waterline which is marked on shattered stone blocks. East is a high artificial hill of grey stone blocks and earth upon which a shattered tower overlooks this river.
15675:
The corpse of a hungry warg is lying here.
A hungry warg (Rood) is standing here, ridden by you.

Near the water the greenery springs into life, growing well above your head and limiting sight to only a few yards. The sounds of small insects and of a swiftly running river can be heard, somewhere beyond the green curtain that blocks sight of the water.
15676:
A large beautiful rose bush is blooming here.
Deep inside the bush, there is a red rose with leaves and thorny stem.
A sturdy pack horse is standing here.
A tall stag is here, grazing peacefully.
Von (twitter), wielding a cruelly-spiked mace, is standing here.
Ducaht (tooprettytodie), wielding a great warsword, is standing here.

This plain runs alongside the ancient road to the east. It extends towards the north, covered by a variety of bushy plants. To the west, the ground slopes upwards towards the top of a cliff or promontory. The grass underfoot is thin and is shadowed by bushes, creating bare patches on the ground. To the east, the road runs by north and south.
15677: A flat, rock covered plain lies here covered in a green grass of average height with a thin blade. A number of bushes have pushed their roots into the thin soil and the cracks in the rock beneath. West and south are drops from cliffs, but the one to the west is quite a longer drop, perhaps ninety feet, while the one to the south is only ten feet or so to the river there.
15678: Bush Covered Plain above a Cliff

A few large bushes spot this rock-covered plain with short green grass growing around the bushes and between the rocks. Several trees grow near the western edge where there is a sheer drop down the cliff. The plain continues into the east. To the north and south lie other plains above the same cliff that lies west of here.
15679: This field is slightly narrow with the river pressing from the west and the cliff from the east. Green grass and lichen cover this field on the soil and the rocks respectively. A wall of jagged, tumbling rock prevents travel to the south.
15680: This plain is covered in grass with little rock showing through except along the edge of the cliff to the west. Along the west side of the plain at the cliffs edge are many small cracks and, in places, missing pieces of rock. Several small sections are unsupported and could slide down the face of the cliff with little notice. The cracks become fewer towards the north.
15681: A rocky field lies here, somewhat jagged because of the large areas where rock has been thrust from the ground. Several types of grass cover this field, the yellow and green grasses growing well in the deep soil between the stone areas, and very poorly in the cracks of the stone outcroppings. Patches of lichen cover much of the stone. Southwards rises a cliff, and to the east a large stone outcrop makes travel impossible that way.
15682: The corpse of a black snake is lying here.

Large and small rocks cover this field, with a few scattered patches of soil for grass to grow in. In some places the rocks sit on top of each other forming large piles that rise several feet above ground, and extend into the ground. The uneven size of the rocks allow small tunnels to be formed in the piles, possibly leading down into the soil beneath. A cliff with a clear view of this field can be seen to the far north.
15683: A small trail runs through this flat, grassy field. Newer growths of bushes and other marks, such as ruts on the edges of the trail, show that the trail was at one time more widely used. The trail has not been cut back in quite some time and the vegetation has grown inwards leaving it only a few feet across. The plant life is so low to the ground though that travel through it in any direction is fairly easy except to the north where a small drop over jagged rocks leads to a river. To the west a tower overlooks this area, as does a cliff beyond the river to the north.
15684: This field is covered in rocks of the same type as the cliff that rises to the east. Most of the rocks lie at the foot of the cliff that runs north and south here. The cliff and the river along the western edge move toward each other to the north and to the south.
15685:
A large eagle soars above you.
A small rabbit glares angrily at you.

Grass covers large amounts of this field, but not everywhere. The grass seems to die off farther towards the northern border of the field. Bare earth shows where the grass has died. A quickly moving, wide river flows along the western edge of this field, and the land becomes more rocky but still covered with some grass towards the east and south.
15686: A finch flies low above the ground.

Little of green can be seen in this barren field, except some small patches of grass and a few small bushes. The shallow soil that covers this area is not providing much of what the plants need to grow, so what little plant life that exists here is small. A river runs to the west of here though the soil seems not to have absorbed any moisture from it. Fields extend off to the east, south and north and appear to be in a similar better condition to this field.
15687: Small Trail in a Field of Bones

This large field has no trees in it and shows sign of having been burned several times. A fairly large, but now somewhat overgrown, trail leads east to another field, and west upwards to the ruined tower that overlooks this field. Bones and small pieces of rusted metal can be seen on the ground all over the field, but they are very dense within a bow shot of the tower. The river flows along the northern edge of this field past a small spit sticking out into it.
15688: The water in the river to the north has a light blue colour, indicating that it is probably not as fast flowing as the river section northeast. It might be one of the spots where it is easy to swim to the other side. A high cliff looms above to the south, making travel in that direction impossible. However, a skilled climber would be able to climb up to the summit by making use of various outcroppings as handholds. This trail continues on, both to the east and west here.
15689: The small trail carefully snakes its way through the plains. This section seems to have once been part of the flood plain of the River Bruinen, lying below the fields to the south, and sloping gently upwards to the east and west. Entry into the river to the north would be fairly easy at this location.
15690:
A beer barrel has been left here.
A noticeable crack runs down one of the walls.
A tall brown-skinned orc, with wide arms, examines you harshly.
A tall brown-skinned orc, with wide arms, examines you harshly.
A demon wolf lurks here, its dark form twisting and hiding its shape.

Hidden in a crevice, this camp is carefully concealed within the side of the slopes of the hill. Bushes and rocks ensure that the entrance to the small cavern is not found from the outside. In the back of the crevice what seems to be small hand and footholds have been carved out in the rock to allow passage up to a small rocky ledge some meters above. A small metal plaque is attached to the wall below the ledge.
15691: Summertime flowers make a yellow and orange carpet bordering the large road to the east. As the field moves away from the road, the vegetation becomes sparse and lacks the greenery that one would expect to find in the vicinity of large bodies of water. To the south the ground is bright green and covered with clover.
15692:
A small cluster of clover grows here.
A tall stag is here, grazing peacefully.

This is the corner of a great field that continues northwest. Southeast is a large and well-travelled road. Once in a while creatures and other living things use this field as a shortcut while travelling north to south or vice versa. A large green field is visible to the west, offering an area where one might take a break from an arduous journey.
15693: This field extends on eastwards as a bright green blanket of healthy grass mixed with clover during most of the year, only yielding in the heart of winter. In contrast, the field to the north is almost completely bereft of greenery. The ground slopes upwards towards the west, leading to a much higher outcropping. To the south bushes seem to dominate the view and the road is barely visible in the distance.
15694: A large beautiful rose bush is blooming here.

Situated just west of the road, this section of plains is covered with a variety of bushes and bushy plants. Signs of small burrowing animals and snakes can be seen here and there on the ground, either tiny holes or collections of twigs and leaves. The ground continues in this way towards the south and slopes upwards towards the west.
15695: During the summer months the sun turns this field light green and yellow, breathing a small amount of life into it. When the nights start to become shorter this area wakes up to begin its difficult existence. The short grass starts to grow again and the few evident flowers struggle to bloom. To the east, the same sort of barren terrain continues. Towards the north, a stone outcrop or cliff rises quickly up out of the ground.
15696:
A cute young hawk is standing here.
A cute young hawk is standing here.
A large mother hawk is here looking for prey to feed her young.

The ground angles sharply here, jutting up from the desolate fields that lie to the east and south. There is not much vegetation here; the ground is almost completely covered with stones and large rocks. However, a very few species of grass are struggling to survive here and there. To the north one can see a trail running below the ridge, and the River Bruinen coursing in the distance.
15697: A finch flies low above the ground.

A small section of floor remains here, no more than a few yards square. The tower walls which once must have continued higher now range from floor level to several feet high along the outside edge of this platform. The tower walls farther around the circle do not even rise to this height. The height of the tower gives this floor a commanding view of the rivers to the north, south and west, and the trail to the east that is the only land route to this tower.
15698: Ground Floor of a Ruined Tower

This tower is heavily damaged, almost destroyed. The circular tower wall of grey stone is now more of a half circle with almost no eastern or southern sections. Only a small piece of the floor of the level above remains and is now more of a platform than a tower level. That small platform overlooks this level from above and to the side, leaving this floor open to sunlight and weather. Some stairs along the curved wall lead up to the remainder of the floor above, though not many supports remain for the stairs or the upper floor. Some stairs also lead underneath this level.
15699:
An old, strong cave troll is standing here.
A finch flies low above the ground.

This large circular cellar is almost entirely made of stone. Only a doorway sized area to the west is not made of stone, being filled instead with earth and large stone blocks which have spilled out into this chamber. The support pillars seem to be in good condition, but the rafters that help to support the levels above have been heavily damaged by fire. A small stone staircase leads upwards along the curve of the wall.
15700: A brook trout is here, swimming in the current.

The river flows fast here, with the water rushing loudly from the east into the west. The water has many ripples and bits of foam in it. The soil in the plain north of here is quite silty, due to runoff water from the river. A field borders the river in the south.
15701: Water roars through this bend in the river. The water swiftly flows from the north and is compressed by the southern cliff wall and the rocks that make up the rapids. The churning water is then spit out to the west at a dangerous rate. The water smashing against the cliff wall and the rocks make it easy for travellers to hit one or the other.
15702: The trail seems to have been a path leading to some location eastwards, but all that is visible in that direction is rolling fields of flowers, bordered farther by some sort of scorched or blackened grassland. What remains of this trail leads north and west towards the road. On the southern edge of the road thick grass replaces the brightly coloured flowers that lie east.
15703: The thick, green grass grows tall along the hard-packed surface of the road to the west. The northern edge seems bushier, and a trail leading in that direction has been overgrown for what appears to be many years. The dense grass grows even more abundantly towards the south, mixed with small white flowers that seem to grow year-round. To the east the grass hosts quite a few bright flowers.
15704: The soft grass waves in the wind all year round except when the snow makes it sleep under its white sheet. During the summer the grass is dense, the leaves are light green, and the buds are yellow before it sets its seed. During the winter it all turns a pale white colour, waiting for the spring. Towards the east yellow and white are replaced by blue.
15705: The dense blanket of green grass is interrupted only by the dark brown surface of the road to the west. The blanket of green seems to shift from dark to light when wind blows across its surface. Towards the east, small yellow flowers dot the landscape, and clumps of clover seem to huddle in between dense patches of thick green grass.
15706: The grass grows shorter near the road to the west, undoubtedly trampled down by travellers or perhaps grazed by the various mounts that travel the road. Signs of cows and a few other herbivores are visible here and there, as well as small holes that might be signs of snake activity. Towards the east, yellow flowers are visible.
15707: Dense green grass dominates the view for miles around. The surface of the ground is fairly even, making it easy to see for quite a distance in every direction. Towards the east yellow flowers grow in abundance, leading on to some marshy ground visible farther away. A road runs along the edge of a large bushy plain in the west. This place would seem a good location to take a break from travelling in relative safety.
15708: The enchanting will-of-the-wisp beckons you with a blurred light.

Not much can be seen around here, except the endlessly flowing grass that covers the plains totally. As a gust of wind ripples through the plants, it resembles an ocean, with waves endlessly rolling across the vast expanse.
15709: As the river makes a few turns, a small section of plains has been almost completely surrounded by water. The area does somewhat resemble an island, completely covered by grass and a few small trees. Just on the other side of the river, a dark and ominous tower rises from a wall of dense thorns.
15710: Closing in on the trail, the grass and plants try to reach out and cover the remnants of civilisation. Not many marks of man can be seen here, but a careful eye might notice small fragments that still recall the power of ages past.
15711: Bordered on the west and north by a large road, the plains seem an ideal location for taking a break on one's journey. This may have once been part of a larger farmland, as there are raised bits of ground that could be where a farmer would have placed posts for a fence or some other enclosure. In fact, on closer inspection, one might notice that the raised bumps are square in shape. This grassy area continues on towards a more open plain to the east.
15712: Grassy flatlands stretch to the north and west while, to the south, the vegetation thickens near the water. Splashing noises can be heard from the river as it flows rapidly by and birds can be heard, hidden in the undergrowth. Just east of you, a small hill rises above the plateau.
15713: This hill separates two markedly different areas. To the west the grasslands stretch for many miles, while to the east lie the swamps, an area of noisome brown and blackened water. A river running south of here has eroded some of the southern flank, making the slope down that direction rather steep. The view is excellent, giving a good outlook over the surrounding areas. Far to the southwest the remains of an old castle can be seen, with one tower still standing.
15714: Below the water surface, a strip of hard and firm ground runs in a straight line from the north to the south. Here used to pass an old trail, but it has now sunken below, as the swamps reclaimed their land. Still, it will be of use to you, as it provides sure footing in this marshy, water-covered place. Even so, the support might prove short and treacherous as there is no way to tell if the trail ends.
15716: A swarm of midges is here, humming around you.

Covered by nondescript grass, this small hill is notably different from the marshlands north and west. It has no special features or marks, nor does it seem to be of any interest to the buzzing clouds of stinging insects that inhabit the swamps.
15717: A small leech is here, floating in the water.

Everything is mud - below you and all around you. You even breathe mud. The air is filled with bloodsucking insects, making your passage almost a living hell, filling your mouth as you gasp for breath and stinging you even if you try to cover your face and hands.
15719: A green frog is here, hopping around.

The fen is host to very few plants or animals above the surface. The occasional swarm of midges or mosquito frequent the area, but very few animals that are not of an aquatic nature would be tempted to stay long and even those would likely prefer the marshes or swamps further south. To the west a large tree is visible in the distance.
15720:
A porcupine is waddling around here, its tail full of sharp quills.
A quail stands motionless.

This landscape seems to be both in the midst of transformation and halted in time. The firm ground of the plains is slowly losing ground to the wet and marshy ground that borders it on the north and west, and to the wetter fens that lie to the south. This seems to be one of the few patches of truly firm ground for a few miles in each direction.
15721: A duck is here, quacking happily.

The soft earth is covered by a bright green moss, and at times with sparse grass or other low-lying vegetation. To the north the marshy ground continues. East is blocked by dense bushes and south of here the plains seem to rise slightly, causing the ground to be more solid and able to sustain heartier plant life. Thorny bushes prevent you going east.
15722:
A heron is stalking the area, looking for fish.
A heron is stalking the area, looking for fish.
A green frog is here, hopping around.
A duck is here, quacking happily.

The ground here slopes upward toward the north, rising gently up out of the surrounding marshy ground. At this angle it cannot retain the same amount of groundwater as the marshes around it, making it somewhat firmer. The ground mists that are sometimes visible on the lower ground do not occur here, and the ground itself is covered with short grass. Thorny bushes prevent you going east.
15723:
A porcupine is waddling around here, its tail full of sharp quills.
A porcupine is waddling around here, its tail full of sharp quills.

When a breeze blows across the surface of the dark green grass it seems to sway and move in time with some unknown rhythm, showing the pale underside of the blades. The grass continues on north and east, but to the west lies something quite different. The ground there is sunken as if some great weight had been pushing down over time, creating a low-lying marshy area.
15724:
A frog is standing here.
A swarm of mosquitoes is here, humming around you.
A swarm of midges is here, humming around you.

The soft footing can be perilous if one were to tread without caution. The area almost seems to be in a transition from becoming a plain of solid ground and grass to a loamy surface of moss. To the north and east the ground is higher; it would be difficult to climb up there from here. There are only a few roots and twigs on the slopes, and nothing that could secure the ascent.
15725:
A duck is here, quacking happily.
A swarm of midges is here, humming around you.
A swarm of midges is here, humming around you.

The ground underfoot is a mixture of both a soft, moist soil to the north and firm earth to the east, where a slope ascends gradually out of the marshes. A low mist often hangs above the ground at about the height of a man's knee. Some holes in the ground in various locations are signs that snakes live nearby.
15726:
A frog is standing here.
A frog is standing here.

Perhaps long ago this was once part of the course of the Bruinen, before it carved its path out of the landscape far to the northwest, or maybe some mighty underground river flows nearby. Whatever the reason the ground is quite wet and very soft underfoot. To the west, the surface is sunken deep and appears quite waterlogged.
15727: The soft ground underfoot is sometimes slippery. A few rocks are visible on the ground, covered with a bright green moss. A heavy, damp feeling pervades the air and there are frequent ground mists, making travel difficult at times. There is also peat, but no evidence that anyone has been using it. Towards the south, a large tree is clearly visible.
15728: An immense oak tree stands at the centre of the marshy ground, buoyed by its large root structure. A few small leaves cling to the branches, but the tree is half-drowned as the lowlands sink even lower into the depths of Arda. To the west solid ground is visible. On all sides tough marshes and fens seem to be the only visible landscape. Far off to the east the caps of the Misty Mountains are barely discernible in the distance.
15731: An Old Path through the Hills

A small brown snake is slithering around here.
A small brown snake is slithering around here.

A small line of hills rises out of the marshland. Between the hills flow several small streams. Over the hills runs a trail, stretching out from north to south. Almost completely overgrown, it still provides sure footing for you and has kept many a weary traveller from wandering out into the swamps and the mud.
15732: The ground here is muddy with quite a bit of groundwater. The marsh must be formed by a combination of the run-off water from the grounds to the north and the underground water source that seems to seep into the soil from deep under the ground. Towards the south a small line of hills is visible, with a path leading around them.
15733: The land here does not have the same fate as the small pasture lying to the west, where the bright green grass grows abundantly. Here, on lower ground, the grass grows only on the slopes leading west and south. Year after year, a bit more solid ground is eroded away by the torrents of rain water flowing from the west, and the ever-rising waters of the marshy plains to the south.
15734: This low-lying area serves almost as a pit for the surrounding plains. Runoff water and vegetation that is swept by it flow into this secluded area. Surface rock deep at the bottom of this quagmire prevents the water from being absorbed into the ground. The situation in the south does not help, as the small slope running from that direction encourages more water to flow into the quagmire.
15736: Running just to the east of a ridge this wet ground is covered with a soft moss instead of the typical grass that one might find in these surroundings. East of here grass grows abundantly, although the ground is still quite soft. To the south the situation becomes even more severe; the field there seems to have collapsed or sunken into the ground across a one mile radius.
15737: A swarm of mosquitoes is here, humming around you.

Lying at the bottom of a ridge line, and on lower ground than the surrounding area, this gully is quite muddy. Any rain or snowmelt that occurs within a few miles is either absorbed by the ground where it falls, or runs down here, which keeps the ground muddy. It would be impossible to ride here, and it is a bit difficult for even a mountain goat to keep its footing.
15738: Clumps of green and yellow grass grow sparsely throughout the blackened remains of what was once a fertile field. Swathes of blackened trees and grass mark what must have been a wildfire sweeping across the plains. Towards the south the source of the blaze seems evident. The ground is dry and cracked, and does not support any life.
15739: During spring and early summer an abundance of colourful flowers bloom into life to adorn the normally solid green landscape with bright yellow, orange and blue splashes of colour. Towards the east the ground has more of a scorched appearance, and even the grass struggles to grow along the edges. Towards the west a trail is visible, but is densely overgrown by thorny shrubs.
15740:
A plain leather belt is lying here.
A long lance has been stuck into the ground.
An orkish shield, bearing the effigy of a red skull, has been left here.
A fine pair of rigid leather boots are on the ground.
On the ground is a foul orkish-looking metal helmet.
An old-looking ring, covered with runes, lies here (glows blue).

Despite the poor soil that is evident in the surroundings closely cropped grass and a few flowers manage to grow. Towards the west the grass grows much more lushly for some distance as it approaches the brown earth of the road. Off in the distance southeast some sort of ruins are visible, just south of a large blackened section of ground.
15741: The burnt and blackened skeletal remains of a human are here.

The ground is dry and cracked like a pond when it dries up during the hot summer. However, no amount of rain seems to improve it. This tiny plateau sits on higher ground, so any water that might fall here immediately flows into the surrounding lower ground. To the east, one could probably climb down to the wet ground below.
15742: An orkish warg-rider, wielding a lance, is here, riding a hungry warg.

A few low stones in a roughly square shape are all that remain of what was once some sort of dwelling. Perhaps a hermit or someone once lived here, but the hovel was long ago abandoned. A few small broken tools lie on the ground here and there, and what looks like the remains of a trapdoor are in the centre of the dwelling, covered by a large rock. The paths to east and south are both blocked by large hedges.
15743: The corpse of an orkish warg-rider is lying here.

No matter what time of year one might travel through this area, the entire landscape looks as if it is on the verge of blooming to life. In the warm seasons of the year small blooms can be seen throughout the grassy terrain. To the east a copse of bushes grows on the edge of some wasteland and there is some sort of ruins visible beyond them.
15744: The soil underfoot is quite dry, seemingly inhospitable, yet bright green grass and a variety of yellow flowers grow in patches. Towards the south the same yellow flowers dominate the landscape. The ground leads down gently to the east, where a large meadow is visible. A flat area in the west is alive with various tall grasses and stands of wild wheat growing up out of the earth.
15745: Situated just to the south of the ruins of some sort of dwelling, this bright green meadow sits atop a raised section of ground. The elevation allows it to be well watered by natural sources yet leaves it safe from the flooding that appears to have turned the land to the east and far south into dense quagmires of mud and rotting vegetation.
15746: One of many small grassy areas that are scattered about the region, this small pasture is covered with a bright, green grass. It seems to be supplied by the same underground source that makes the plains south of here into marshy ground. Luckily for the grass, the entire area is raised on higher ground than the surroundings.
15747: The corpse of an orkish warg-rider is lying here.

The land here appears to have once been cultivated as a garden, evidenced by the regular rows of bright flowers that grow in geometric patterns. The ground is raised as if a mole had burrowed perfectly straight, parallel lines running north and south. To the east the ground slopes gently upwards towards a flat area which is carpeted with bright green clover.
15748:
Elerin the Elf, wielding a double edged eket, is here, riding a pack horse.
A pack horse is standing here, ridden by Elerin.

The mixture of goldenrod and honeysuckle that seems to grow abundantly just north of here is sparse because the ground is rather unstable. Great upheavals of dirt seem to have torn up any roots that were taking hold in the rocky soil. Towards the east there is a noticeable transition towards very damp ground, and an almost marshy surface.
15749:
A swarm of mosquitoes is here, humming around you.
The enchanting will-of-the-wisp beckons you with a blurred light.
The enchanting will-of-the-wisp beckons you with a blurred light.

Large quantities of groundwater and deep mud make travel through this section quite difficult. The mud seems to draw everything deeper into its depths. The river which flows underground farther to the north must be the reason for the water rising to the surface once again. Perhaps a natural spring once flowed here, but there is no evidence of it now.
15750: The ground grows softer and softer, but it does support your weight. Underfoot it squelches, trying to drag you below. The tracks behind you fill quickly with water. Rising all around are dense clumps of reeds, separated from each other by small passageways of marshland.
15751: The plant life grows lusher as it nears the water. Still no sound of a river can be heard, although the air is moist. The incessant chirping of some small birds can be heard in the distance and, nearer by, some small animal scurries into the safety of the thick grass.
15752:
A tree-snake lies wrapped around one of the tree branches.
A tree-snake lies wrapped around one of the tree branches.

The air is damp. A wall of branches and leaves block out the sky. But still there is a certain amount of freedom since you can leave in almost any direction, climbing out on long branches, let yourself safely drop down to the ground or just simply climb back the way you came.
15753:
A small campfire burns here, its low flames giving off only a little light.
A swallow flies high above the ground.

You find yourself just south of a small stream, on the edge of a vast ocean of grass. Here, the undergrowth is thick and healthy, being so close to the water. To the south the landscape changes colour, becoming bleaker as you look towards the horizon.
15754: The ground is soft here, every footstep sinking down a few inches into the earth. Just north of here you can hear the soft trickling of a stream running by, and the sounds of a few small birds above it. As you gaze around you see that the plains continue in all directions, but that they seem to be more hilly and perhaps more marshy on the other side of the stream.
15755: An Ancient Trail in the Plains
A pack horse is standing here, ridden by you.

This ancient trail is one of the few reminders of the civilisation that once ruled these lands. Some small marker stones at the edges of the path can still be seen, although many have been overgrown and lost amongst the grass. Not much else can be seen except an ominous black tower rising above the horizon to the west.
15756: Once a field used by the inhabitants of the keep to grow crops of different kinds, it has long since been overrun by weeds. Far west of it lie the remnants of the ancient castle wall, which has fallen into disrepair. A small trail skirts around the southern edge of the old field, heading west to the old castle and east into the plains.
15757: Plains by an Ancient Stone Wall

Once the ground was cleared here to prevent enemies from sneaking close to the castle but now the high grasses and bushes have started to work their way back towards the castle wall. Just west of you the old stone wall rises high above the ground, still mighty and strong but aging and deserted. Its surface is covered by vines and plants, giving it a peaceful and solemn look.
15758: The thorns in the northwest have started to reclaim this old field where once the keep's soldiers had their practice ground. What looks like old archery targets lie broken and crumbled on the bare soil that still, after all these years, bears marks of heavily burdened horses charging after imaginary foes. In the east the old castle lies silent, still keeping watch on the old land.
15759: In front of you are the old castle gates, towering high above. Once they always stood open, letting the farmers pass in and out with a mere guard to keep watch, but now the gates are firmly shut and no sign of life can be seen. The walls are covered by smaller plants and vines climbing towards the sky. The bushes have crept up on the wall almost as if they wanted to sneak in and ambush the keep.
15760: Here the wall crumbled and fell. Great cracks yawn in the stonework and several large stone blocks have fallen down, crushing the ground. Wild weeds and vines have destroyed some of the larger stones, creating a landscape littered by boulders of various sizes. Just skirting the havoc, the old trail passes on the outside of the ruins of the wall, almost hidden from view, through the grass striving towards the old castle.
15761: This old trail once ran into the fields that surrounded the keep, but now it has fallen into oblivion. The plains have reclaimed the very ground that it used to run on, and now the trail is cracked and overgrown, making it very hard to follow.
15762: The faint remnants of an old trail run through the plains here. Once well-trodden, it is now nothing but a faint memory of an older era, when men tamed these plains and grew crops on them. The crop fields were long ago reclaimed by the plains, but the trail survives, the small marker stones lining the way not yet completely overgrown.
15763: Here the ground is covered totally by grass in every direction you look. High and thick, it makes travel slightly taxing, as movement is little more than wading through. Just to your west you see something that looks like a dark streak through the plains. Far to the southeast, the plains give way to hills.
15764: A swallow flies high above the ground.

A rather large boulder, over one yard across, lies here, almost completely overgrown. A few bird droppings on the top of the boulder show it to be a popular place to watch for prey. Looking around, you can see a hill a bit to the south of here and, far to the north, the blue ribbon of a river stretching through the plains.
15765: A soft trickling can be heard from the north, the faraway sound of water flowing. Even though the noise is steady and firm, it is soft and low. A bird calling out high up in the sky and the light breathing of the wind create a peaceful, yet strong and living, feeling in this place. Everything is green as far as the eye can see, and the only things changing are the waves flowing towards you as the grasses bend to the winds.
15766: A large rabbit looks peacefully at you, ready to dart away.

You find yourself at the foot of a rather high hill, rising just southwest of here. Covered in grass, the hillside would not be discernible from the plains if not for its height, and the hill seems out of place here, rising so high from the flat grassy ground. Periodically, gusts of wind come rushing from the other side of the hill, making the grass flow like waves over the sea.
15767: The vast, flat plains are broken off here by a rather high hill, rising in the midst of the grass just south of you. The plains stretch out around you, enveloping you and the hill in a living blanket. You spot a small rabbit hole in the ground and you hear, clearly, a small bird singing somewhere in the distance.
15768: The plains here are dominated by the high hill rising just southeast of you, and not much else can be seen in this ocean of grass. Faint sounds can be heard from the vicinity, possibly a bird calling for its mate, but other than that, the surroundings are rather quiet.
15769: A small rabbit glares angrily at you.

The ground here is rather soft, and gives way a little as your weight is placed on it. As you travel through the high grass, you manage to scare something that rushes swiftly and noisily through the grass. Looking around, you see a high hill far to your east, but elsewhere the landscape is just plains, stretching towards the horizon.
15770: The old fields here are now nothing but a memory as the ground is once again covered in wild grasses and weeds. In a few places remnants of some old fences can be spotted, but it takes quite a lot of imagination to see the old fields in front of you.
15771: A swallow flies high above the ground.

Remains of a small farmhouse can be discerned on the ground. Not much is left of the walls, but some of the stonework of the hearth is still in place. Wooden splinters lie scattered all around in the grass. A short distance north you see the old castle rising above you, watching and guarding its old and undiscovered secrets.
15772: Passing through the centre of the ruined farm village the trail makes a turn here, heading north towards the castle and west towards the horizon. Ruins of a small farm lie just east of you and several overgrown fields lie scattered in the area surrounding you.
15773: The small path runs between old unused and overgrown fields from the old broken road in the far west towards what once was a small farmer village. Small ruins of houses can be seen around you as well as broken and rotted fences. A small distance to your northeast lies the ancient castle that was the focal point of the area in times of old.
15774: This small path runs alongside the thick thorns for quite a while, leading you onward. South of the trail the grassy plains begin, stretching south and east for what seems to be forever. The path leads east towards the old ruined keep, and has obviously lain unused for many a year.
15775:
A hungry warg stands here, sniffing around for flesh.
A very strong orkish patrol-leader is looking for enemies here.
An orkish warg-rider is here, riding a hungry warg .
An orkish warg-rider is here, riding a hungry warg .
A very strong orkish patrol-leader is looking for enemies here.
An orkish warg-rider is here, riding a hungry warg .
An orkish warg-rider is here, riding a hungry warg .

Movement at any speed here is a hardship, as the dense thorns tear and grab at you. The rumbling of fast flowing water can be hear to the north, where the land falls away in a huge drop down to the river. To the west the thorns are impossible to pass, becoming so thick and dense that you cannot see through them. East the thorns become sparser, and travel is easier there.
15776:
The remains of a mass of vines lie here in a heap of rotting compost.
The remains of a thick tangle of vines lie here in a heap of rotting compost.

Thick dense thorns surround you, filtering out the sun, so that only a few lonely rays of light manage to get down to the ground. In the everlasting dusk a few small birds live and thrive, but the thorns are not a very friendly place for larger animals. To the west and south there is a hedge of thorns that makes those directions virtually impassable. East of here a path has been hacked through the thorns, while northward the bushes become even thicker.
15777: The ground here is hard, well packed and far from perfectly covered by the grasses and weeds. Brown spots of dirt show through the green and yellow sturdy tufts of grass. The ground slowly slopes upwards as a rising cliff ascends to the west, blocking sight farther westwards. North of here stands a small thicket of thorns.
15778: As if fallen down from the cliff to the north, the vegetation here consists of high thorny bushes making it so difficult to ride or even walk here one would wonder if they grew here on purpose. Small animals seem to thrive in the safe haven the thorns provide, and noises from small birds can be heard from all directions.
15779: The thorny bushes covering the land have all but exterminated any other kind of flora. Coming from the west the thorns have climbed these cliffs to get more sunlight. The steep drop to the south has not been an obstacle for the thorns either, and thick tangles protrude creating the illusion of a sturdy overhang.
15799:
A clear spring babbles as cool water trickles out of the ground.
A river otter splashes playfully here.

This isolated field is covered in shrubs with a few trees scattered across it. A small spring trickles into a tiny ribbon of water that flows to the river bordering on the north. The high cliff south of here curves and blocks travel to the east but is climbable in the south. Many layers of rock, each one of a different colour, can be seen stretching in bands across the cliff wall.
15800: Tall grass covers this field in most places, though several circles have been cleared and rocks moved so that simple makeshift fire pits could be created. Scattered stumps show the origin of the rotting logs that were set as seats around these fire pits. A cliff drops sharply at the north but the rock face seems to be climbable.
15801: A large rabbit looks peacefully at you, ready to dart away.

Around you stretches a field of rocks, covered in places with simple plants like lichen and grass. The cliff to the north overlooking the river below also blocks travel to the west. A soft rushing sound can be heard over the edge of the northern cliff. The rocks here seem to settle deeper into the ground towards the east and south, making it easier for plants to grow.
15802: This field of grass, small trees and light brush stretches from the cliff in the north into the south. The trees and brush grow thinner towards the edges of the field. Small spots of rock thrust out of the ground, and grow more common to the west.
15803: Surrounded by water to the north and west, with a cliff to the south and a narrow field to the east, this field is somewhat isolated from the lands around it. Small plants of various types struggle to live in the poor soil of this field and are interspersed with pebbles.
15804: This narrow field is nearly lifeless except for some patches of grass. It stands below a cliff to the south and the river to the north. Rocks and boulders have fallen off the cliff and lie here, making it hard for the plant life to find a place with good soil. Some of the boulders have rolled into the river and make the shoreline a big jagged. Plants begin to grow more common towards the wider lands of the east, and the more narrow field to the west.
15805: This field is well watered by the river and well served by the silt the floods bring. Grass, shrubs and a few trees crowd this land, with no dirt to be seen anywhere, not even at the rivers edge. The southern cliff is well away from the river, though it comes near the water in the western part of the field. Past the eastern border of this field the ground becomes covered in deep patches of silt that prevent any plants from growing except grass. In the far east a tower rises on a mound overlooking this field.
15806: Piles of silt litter this plain of grass. A rabbit could hop from pile to pile and never trod on the grass lying between them. The rivers to the north and east have natural levels, marked by a narrow shoreline lying just below the level of this plain. Remnants of what might be ancient stone levees lie shattered near the banks of the rivers. beyond the shattered stone and the river sits a mound topped by a tower which can be easily seen from here.
15807: A lush field lies here, well watered by the runoff from the tall cliff that rises along the western edge, and the water table resulting from the river to the east. Tall grasses cover the field with a few large trees growing near the rivers edge. To the south begin rows of stumps or posts, and northwards the ground cover begins to die and small patches of silt lie scattered.
15808: Cracks and small gullies make this field very hard to travel through. Many of the cracks originate from the northern and eastern cliffs and the large western crevice. The crevice running from the northwest to the southwest stretches too far across for anything to jump, but the cracks in this field are generally less than a foot wide and a few feet deep. A few large trees and some patches of grass are all that grow in this field.
15809:
A large rabbit looks peacefully at you, ready to dart away.
A brown fox is here, looking for some rabbits to chew up.

This field is covered in light brush with large areas of grass. The lack of large vegetation, such as trees, makes travel through here simple. The cliff that drops to the north overlooks the river valley and appears cracked and unstable. A crevice several paces wide runs from the cliff in the northeast along the eastern of this field blocking all but birds.
15810: A large rabbit looks peacefully at you, ready to dart away.

A large field full of small bramble patches makes travel through here a bit difficult since paths through it must be used. These patches are offshoots of the giant bramble patch to the south that have become isolated. A round section of the southern wall of bramble is slightly discoloured.
15811: A field of tall grass is here, almost two feet high in some places. Small trees and high shrubs make it hard to see any great distance here. Anything on the ground is impossible to see from more than a few feet anyway because of the terrain and plant life.
15812: A Field of Small Game Trails
A large rabbit looks peacefully at you, ready to dart away.

This field of grass and small shrubs has several game trails going through it, though most of them are sized for a rabbit or other small animals. These trails go south, west and north through here. To the east of here is a large crevice running along a north-south axis that is quite wide and impossible to cross.
15813:
A black snake hurries towards you with sly intentions.
A black snake hurries towards you with sly intentions.

A large circle of thirteen stumps and the fallen ancient oaks that spray outwards from them dominate this field. An altar of granite sits in the centre of the clearing, equal distance from each of the tree stumps. Small vines grow up the side of the altar. A crevice runs along the west side of this field. To the east begin posts or stumps set in rows.
15814: Lines of stumps stand here, the remains of an orchard which has been hacked down by axes and burned. The stumps are a few feet high and many have had their hearts burned out. There is evidence of a deliberate burning of the core and then a dousing when the surrounding part of the trunk started to burn. The repeated burning of the cores has created hollow stumps of the former fruit trees. The land grows more barren towards the east, with the other directions showing more signs of life.
15815: A chunk of salt is here.

This former farmland is barren and dead, the earth has been sown heavily with salt. No plants are growing here despite the irrigation from the old ditches that lead to the river in the east and north. The old farm stretches to the south and west. Beginning towards the west are what might be short posts standing in rows.
15816: A chunk of salt is here.

Barren earth upon which nothing can grow makes this field very lifeless. A large depression seems to have once been a pond. Ditches used to connect the depression to the river in the east but they have been filled up with too much loose blown earth to let water flow through them. Rotting wood and broken stone in the ground show what might once been a farmhouse or a barn.
15817: This meadow is mainly covered in tall grass though large patches of dead ground exist where no life grows. The dead areas are mainly along the eastern and northern edges of this meadow and the farther in those directions the larger the patches become. Posts or stumps rise from a field to the north.
15818: This meadow is covered in stalks of golden coloured wheat. There is no sign that people have ever tried to cultivate this meadow, though the soil is rich and fertile. The meadow is flat and stretches towards the horizon in each direction except the north where a field with several stumps lies.
15819: Tall stalks of grass and wheat grow scattered in patches across this meadow. Each patch is separated by small sections of bramble that keep the two grasses separate and roughly equal in area. A large patch of brambles blocks travel to the west. Tiny game trails at the northern edge run to and from this meadow.
15820:
A carrot is lying here.
A carrot is lying here.
A roe deer is standing here, watching the terrain while chewing the vegetation.

This field has a number of small vegetable plots that have grown wild and no longer grow in neat and orderly rows. Marks on the ground show where those rows once were. A gigantic patch of thorny bramble stretches off into the distance in the east.
15821: A roe deer is standing here, watching the terrain while chewing the vegetation.

A field of small tangled plants and grass lies here. The plants seem to be trying to grow on top of each other in their struggle for light and good soil. A few larger shrubs stand out among the other plants, but they themselves are little more than two feet high, and only noticeable because of the shortness of the other plants.
15822: Several varieties of green grass cover this field, each a different shade and height. A tall, light green variety covers about half the field, but the other types intermix with this variety. Fields continue to the north and east, while flat grasslands stretch out in the south.
15823: A variety of garden plants, small trees and bushes grow in this field. Only a little free room is left for travellers to move through except where grass is growing by itself. There are enough grassy areas though that this field can be walked, but not ridden, through.
15824: A tall, thin, yellow grass reaches high towards the sky here. In many areas the grass reaches over four feet in height. The density of the growth prevents a quick look from seeing if any other plants are growing here hidden by the grass or by a small depression in the ground.
15825: A porcupine is waddling around here, its tail full of sharp quills.

This broad, grassy field has a number of mature trees in it but they are well spread out across the field. Each tree is surrounded by a circle of brambles about ten feet wide like a wall around a tower. The brambles are not spreading since between the circles only tall grass exists.
15826: A beautiful and docile horse is standing here.

Clover covers this meadow in a deep, soft blanket. Only a few patches of tall, green grass exist here scattered among the clover leaves. Two types of clover compete here, a green clover and a much more prevalent white variety. The white clover continues northwards but in the other directions grass dominates the flora.
15827: A small cluster of clover grows here.

White and yellow dominate the colours of this meadow. The yellow comes from the grass that encroaches from the east and north. White clover dominates most of the meadow between the grassy areas and the brambles to the west. A few patches of bramble lie scattered here, perhaps offshoots of the patch in the west.
15828: A light green grass covers the ground with its tall, wide-bladed stems. The tall grass almost entirely prevents other species of grass and larger plants such as bushes and trees from growing here. A few bushes have managed to push their tops above the grass to receive sunlight, but they are deeply entangled in grass.
15829: This meadow of tall yellow grass has been overrun by low green shrubs. The very vivid contrast between the colours makes it somewhat easier to find things here since few animals are equipped to fade into both backgrounds. Grasslands and meadows lie at the edges of this meadow, with a large campsite to the east.
15830: A beautiful and docile horse is standing here.

Large areas have been cleared of all grass and brush in circles around one hundred earthen fire pits. Little loose wood or other good material for a fire is left here, only grass and some small shrubs cover the ground between where the old campfires were. There is enough cleared area and fire pits prepared for an army or many groups of travellers to camp here.
15831: Some cracked and splintered pieces of wood float here.

This bank lies beside the river to the east and has a long gentle slope at the edge making access to the river easy. The slope also makes it easy for the river to come far inland when it floods. Small pieces of driftwood lie on the bank, or float in small coves that protect them from being washed along by the rivers flow. Anything floating in a cove can be reached quite easily from the riverbank and the sides of the coves.
15832:
A chunk of salt is here.
The starving cow stands here looking for a patch of grass.
A large eagle soars above you.

A few remaining posts still mark the boundaries of this dead pasture. Almost no green or colour can be seen, except the brown of the soil. Small hills of dust show where the wind has blown dried-up soil. Tiny chunks of salt exist in a few places protected by posts from the weather. A river lies to the east but no irrigation ditches or ponds are here to provide water to plants that attempt to grow. Northwards is an equally barren land but more life shows towards the west and south.
15833:
A well-fed cow stands here chewing her cud listlessly.
A finch flies low above the ground.

This field of tall grass has been left to grow, as it will for quite a while. A few scattered small bushes and several small trees have managed to take root here. The land grows barren towards the east and north. A meadow lies to the west while a campsite is to the south.
15834: Yellow grass grows here, fighting the elements to stand straight and tall at all times of the year and gain as much sunlight as possible. The grass can be easily bent or broken since its stalks are not very strong unlike other types. In all directions but the east stretch meadows. To the east the land is lush and fertile.
15835: Sunken deep into the barren surroundings, a ravine opens up to the east. The brown grass doesn't completely cover the dead soil on the steep slope down into the ravine, and travelling there might be somewhat slippery. Small, thick and hairy plants spot the landscape here, as well as scattered stone blocks.
15836: A swallow flies high above the ground.

Two miles wide, this broad ravine cuts through the barren lands. The walls of it are impossible to climb, and the few plants and trees that grow on them are remarkably durable. The ravine bends and turns in various directions, making it difficult to tell in what direction it leads. Birds can be seen flying in and out from the ravine walls, where they probably have their small underground nests. Once in a while a large bird of prey can be seen high up in the sky.
15837:
A rock lizard is here, motionless as it observes you.
A sand viper is slithering here on the ground.
A swallow flies high above the ground.

Twisting and turning, the deep ravine keeps everyone without wings trapped on the bottom of it. The ground is bare and only in a few places can brown grass be seen. In the middle of the ravine there are clear signs of where an old brook must have been, dried out now for many years. Old and dead plants are scattered along the dried out brook.
15838: Grasses grow tall and dense, covering the fertile soil completely. The white and green clover growing some distance to the north has lost its grip on this part of the plains. Stretching out towards the horizon in every direction but west is the hazy green of grass-covered plains. A deep ravine opens up west of here, cutting through the lands creating an impassable obstacle.
15839: Seemingly endless the high grasses dominate the surrounding area. The land seems deserted except for some small animal tracks leading north towards a meadow. To the south the grass seems more reluctant to grow and the land is more open.
15840:
A small grasshopper clings to a blade of grass, ready to spring.
A restless rabbit bounces around.

Seemingly endless, high grasses dominate the surrounding view. The land is all but deserted here, with the exception of some small animal tracks leading north to what appears to be the remains of a large campsite. To the south even the grass seems reluctant to grow, leaving that area even more open than here.
15841: Reaching high above the land the cliff to the south is clearly unable to be scaled. To the north the River Bruinen makes another natural border and thus all travellers are for the most part restricted to journeying east or west. However, judging from the lack of disturbance in the well-grown grass this area sees few strangers.
15843: The cliff comes to an abrupt end here as a tributary of the River Bruinen has carved its way through the rock, blocking further passage. The fast flowing waters swirl below the edge, sending echoes reverberating through the small canyon. South of here a few low thorn bushes can be seen and westwards the plateau looks to reach towards the horizon.
15844:
An orkish warg-rider, wielding a short spear, is here, riding a hungry warg.
A hungry warg is standing here, ridden by an orkish warg-rider.

Several sturdy tufts of short and broad grasses grow upon this high plateau, trying in vain to cover wind-ridden rock. In places where the soil has been swept away by the fierce winds the dark rock shines through. To the west the plateau expands, reaching toward a sharp edge and southwards it slopes gently downwards. From the east one can hear the faint sound of a flowing river.
15845:
An orkish warg-rider, wielding a short spear, is here, riding a hungry warg.
A hungry warg is standing here, ridden by an orkish warg-rider.

This rocky plateau is sparsely covered with small tufts of sturdy grasses that stand defiantly as the fierce winds howl by, ripping and tearing the very soil upon which they grow. Southwards the plateau is completely covered by green grasses while eastwards the rocks show through in a few of the barer spots.
15846: A lone hawk soars high above you.

The plains of the west and the grasslands of the north come to an abrupt ending here, as a vertical wall in the form of a cliff rises from the ground. The cliff is clearly impossible to climb, lacking any recognisable hand or footholds. As climbing is not an option travellers are forced to seek out reversible routes further north or south.
15847: A large, loyal falcon is circling above.

This grassland, devoid of any interesting landmarks, has suddenly, as if correcting itself, sprung a tall cliff to the east. The shadow cast by this earthen wall must cover miles each dawn. To the south the land rises some to meet the wall, but it only serves to emphasise the contrast between the cliff and the surrounding flat land.
15848: A large rabbit looks peacefully at you, ready to dart away.

Desolate and solemn, these grounds lie silent below the open sky. A large ravine lies to the west and south, creating an insurmountable obstacle. The only sound to be heard is the faint whisper of the wind as it gently causes large ripples in the grass. Few animals can be seen in the dangerous open ground, as stealth is the key to survival for many of the smaller animals inhabiting this dense grassy area.
15849: A swallow flies high above the ground.

The eastern side of the valley floor slowly ascends until it finally meets the wall of the ravine, where it makes a full stop. The slope has been travelled recently, as several large tracks clearly show. A lonely tree grows on the western slope, long since dead, and some of its old branches have already fallen to the ground.
15850: The resilient green grass slowly grows more and more dense. Perhaps, sometime long ago, other species of flora were represented here, but they have long ago drowned in the sea of grass. The area grows denser to the north, maybe a sign of more fertile grounds. A deep ravine opens up to the north and east, making travelling in that direction impossible.
15851: Resembling a large open sea the green grass of the plain here waves gently in the passing winds, faint ripples rolling across the vast expanses of tall straws. Reaching about a foot above the ground the sturdy grass covers everything in sight, as well as reaching out towards the horizon.
15852: The grass-covered lands clear up a bit here and you can barely discern faint brown spots where the soil shines through. Even a few bushes and taller plants have managed to get a hold here, although they are fighting a losing battle against the sturdy grasses that stretch out in all directions as far as the eye can see.
15853: The vast desolate plains stretch out endlessly towards the horizon in all directions, lying flat and unbroken as far as the eye can see. To the east a deep ravine breaks the monotony, cutting deep through the barren landscape. The grass covered ground almost resembles a large expanse of water, rolling as the wind gently caresses the sea green surface, causing rippling waves throughout the vast ocean of greenery.
15854: The ravine continues its way, cutting deep into the barren lands of this part of Arda. Stone blocks and dead plants cover the uneven bottom of the ravine, as well as clear signs of an old dried out brook. The ground is muddy at intervals, showing signs of the brook being filled with water at times.
15855: The steep walls of this deep ravine make any sound reverberate between them and echo for a few seconds before finally coming to an end. This part of the ravine is devoid of life, and the only proof that life once existed here is the collection of small dead plants that have failed their struggle for survival in the stony soil.
15856: The ground here seems to surge up from the surrounding plains, ending at a steep wall to the east. Otherwise the uninterrupted view spans several miles in all other direction. The deep ravine to the west makes a grand view. Even still, spotting movement would be difficult due to the patches of different tinged grass and their constant motions caused by the passing winds.
15857: A swallow flies high above the ground.

Lying in shadow for most of each day, the grasses here grow rather sparse and low. Bleak fragile weeds cling to the ground in a vain attempt to suck what little nourishment they can out of the barren earth. Some of the passing winds howl across the cliff's edge high above while others whistle as they blow down the side of the cliff.
15858: The plains are cut in two as the high cliff wall rises ominously into the air, creating an eighty foot drop just to the west. This plateau is covered in short and sturdy grasses which thrive despite the fierce winds howling by, ripping and tearing at the soil. To the north the cliff is rather bare, the stone showing through the grasses, while eastwards the grass grows stronger as the plains slightly slant downwards.
15859: A very strong, orkish patrol-leader is looking for enemies here.

Hindered by natural barriers of various kinds, it is unlikely this plateau would be accessible by many animals. The serene environment is reminiscent of a farmed meadow. The only kind of life here is that which could and would traverse the various obstacles to get here.
15860: The grasslands abruptly come to an end to the east as the soil of the cliffs lacks the nourishment for the grasses to thrive. More resilient vegetation, such as thorn bushes, cling to every crevice and crack in the cliffs. While these cliffs are scaleable, it would surely be a taxing and unpleasant experience.
15861:
A restless rabbit bounces around.
A large rabbit looks peacefully at you, ready to dart away.

Stretching endlessly towards the hazy line where green meets blue the tall broad grasses grow carelessly here, completely enveloping the fertile soil in a dense green carpet. Moving slowly back and forth as the wind gently rolls in from the distant misty mountains the grass whispers gently in the breeze.
15862:
A small grasshopper clings to a blade of grass, ready to spring.
A lone hawk soars high above you.

The structure of the plains changes gradually as the grasslands span these lands from north to south. To the south the plains lie rich and green, filled with the sounds and smells of life. Northward the plains become more desolate and void of animals. Even the colour of the plains slowly loses its depth as the grasses turn bleak to the north. Just east of here there stands a small cluster of young trees and westward the plains seem to reach on infinitely.
15863: A large rabbit looks peacefully at you, ready to dart away.

Breaking the monotony of the surrounding flat terrain the trees form a rough circle, clustering together as if they were looking for protection in numbers. To the north and east the trees grow all the way to the edge of a deep ravine. Many small animals seem to have taken refuge here from the dangerously open lands around and judging from the faint noises the fauna is thriving.
15864: Some places seem to mysteriously attract moisture, but this place is just the opposite; every little breeze makes the dust swirl up, creating mini tornadoes that travel across the bottom of the ravine. Lacking vegetation that binds the dust to the ground, the sometimes steep slopes of this ravine are slippery to tread. The ravine comes to an end just south of here, climbing up towards the level of the surrounding barren lands.
15865: In these far-reaching plains the dominant feature is the never ending grass growing unhindered in all directions, north to south and east to west. Small insects and tiny birds fill the air, but the ground is less lively since the grass provides no hiding place for even small animals. No large predators would be able to make a life feeding solely around here. To the west a large ravine opens up, making travelling in that direction impossible.
15866: The rolling plains stretch out without doubt or hesitation, reaching for the distant horizon in all directions. The only inconsistency in these grass-covered lands is the cliff wall rising high a few miles northeast of you. Whispering softly in the wind the grass speaks of ages of old and of a history it can sense through its roots.
15867:
A big cavebear is padding around here.
A big cavebear is padding around here.
A swallow flies high above the ground.

This dry cave digs deep into the sandy, and sometimes stony, soil. The exit, that lies in the western wall, leads out into a ravine. The floor is uneven, and in some places stones rise up from the floor, creating obstacles for anyone traversing this cave. The cave is obviously inhabited, as several bones from dead animals are scattered all around.
15868: A large rabbit looks peacefully at you, ready to dart away.

The curved rock wall lies in shadow most of the day, making it look smooth and dark. The ground below is only partly covered in grass and the brown dry soil can be seen shining through the bleak green grass. The grass grows more fertile and lush the further away it is from the towering cliff wall.
15869: Somewhat flatter than the surrounding areas, this place resembles a farmed meadow with strictly defined borders formed by thorn bushes and cliffs. This place could probably support several families of large animals, but its inaccessibility probably deters them from settling here. Crowning the plateau sits a small copse of trees.
15870: Climbing slowly as it travels north, the rising cliff is not very steep and can carry the grass-covered soil well on its surface. Farther north the ground levels out into an open plateau covered in a hazy greenery. Towards the south the vast open plains roll out as far as the eye can see.
15871: Here in the almost ever-present shadow of the cliff wall the grasses are not as dominant as in the surrounding areas. The few tufts of grass that try to live here are short and weak. The cliff wall climbs higher as it travel northwest from here and descends to the level of the plains further south.
15872: What appeared to be plains land with no end comes here to an abrupt stop. To the north a dark, ominous wall of granite effectively ends the plains. The shadow cast by the wall is the favourite resting place for all kinds of animals judging by the well trampled ground.
15873: The sturdy green grass continues seamlessly from horizon to horizon with the lone exception of far to the northeast, where some kind of high hill or small mountain can be seen. The land looks to be devoid of life, but with such an unobstructed view of the surrounding area any creatures living here would have had ample time to hide from your approach. For now, though, even the blue sky seems deserted.
15874: A lone hawk soars high above you.

Flat, monotonous plains stretch from horizon to horizon. The short grass covering everything does nothing to break the uniform looks of this place and as the only source of food for animals, there is not exactly an abundance of life milling around. Small insects and an occasional rabbit might find sustenance here.
15875: Swiftly changing from dry dust covered grass in the north to richer fed grass in the damp south, these plains sprawl unhindered in all directions. Most of the animals dwelling here are of the smaller sort, at least those that dare enter the open ground. This is a place where the wind rules along with the dust it carries.
15876:
A large, loyal falcon is circling above.
A restless rabbit bounces around.

The short resilient grass covers most of the area and with the sole exception of a small cluster of trees to the north this type of vegetation continues in all directions. To the south the grass grows denser, and the ground seems moister.
15877: The grass covered plains stretch out towards the horizon in all directions. The thick and high grass covers and hides the soil from the sky and provides shelter for several small animals which can be heard scurrying about in the dense vegetation. High above small black shapes can be seen, riding the wind currents and searching for prey.
15878: The grass-covered plains stretch endlessly towards the hazy horizon, as if slowly reaching out for the thin line where sky and land meet. The knee-high grasses sway slowly in the passing breezes that make the area roll and billow like a wide ocean, its waves slow and unstoppable, travelling without rest or sleep across the surface.
15879:
A orc patrol-leader of the Ohurk-uai is looking for enemies here.
An orc soldier of the Ohurk-uai is here, patrolling the area.
An orc soldier of the Ohurk-uai is here, patrolling the area.

Weather and wind over time have taken their toll, eroding the land. Nowadays these gently rolling hills are bordered by roads to the east and south, and to the west some small trees or high bushes cover the land.
15880: Small and thin trees fight for sun and space as they break through the hold of the grass here. Creating a small sparse thicket they have won a short respite as they now manage to shadow a small part of the plains. Within the branches of the low trees the sounds of small animals moving about can be heard as they hide carefully among the shadows.
15881: As if they continue on to the sea, these monotonous plains stretch forth in all directions. Their journey appears almost ceaseless with only a minor interruption by a few scattered bushes that grow a ways to the east, struggling valiantly to compete with the vigorous grasses.
15882: Open space surrounds this area and the only moving thing visible is the grass, swaying in the passing winds. The place is hospitable enough for some large animals, but if some exist the grass effectively covers all tracks of them.
15883:
A large rabbit looks peacefully at you, ready to dart away.
A finch flies low above the ground.

Soft and spongy the ground is clearly getting its share of water. The lush grasses grow high and strong, reinforcing the fact that there is ample, but still not an over abundance of, moisture contained within the soil. A small distance to the south you can hear a small spring babbling. This sound blends in with the soft noises of the passing winds blowing across the vast surrounding plains.
15884: A brook trout is here, swimming in the current.

This old field has gradually given way to the water, slowly becoming drenched and marshy. Large tufts stand high above the soft ground and the grasses are dark green in colour. The ground below sucks and drags upon the weight of travellers, causing bubbles to reach the surface of the soggy soil. Each step sends the stench of rotting vegetation pouring into the air.
15885: A colourful butterfly is fluttering around here.

This ancient field often lies drenched in water, drowning the green grasses as the stream just south of here floods its banks. Small pools of dark and murky water stand still in various depressions in the field, emitting the stench of rotting vegetation. Further north the grasses lie on higher ground, out of the waters reach, and thus grow healthier. Further east fields lie drowned by the stream for years, creating a small swamp in the midst of the lush grasslands. To the west there lies a ruined old farm.
