15886: In the middle of these old fields stands the cracked and blackened remains of an old farmhouse. This decaying framework is what is left of this once large and well-built structure. The wood is cracked and splintered, as well as almost completely overgrown by sturdy weeds that try to lay claim to the area. The grassy plains reach north and west, stretching endlessly towards the distant horizon. Just south of here there sparkles a small river.
15887: The plains slope downwards here as a small river runs wildly westward just south of you. The babblings of the rushing water mix with the chirping of hidden birds as well as the scratching and scraping of small mammals running through the dense undergrowth. The plains stretch out towards the horizon without end in all directions, lying flat and almost completely unbroken for miles and miles, but just east of here you can spot some small structure rising above the grass.
15888: The deep river rushes swiftly westwards, frothing and cascading as it travels towards some distant goal far away in the west. The passage south is blocked by a rocky wall, carved out by the river throughout the ages and the northern bank slopes steeply upwards, making the journey in that direction arduous, but still accessible.
15889: Running between ruined farms and old, overgrown pasturelands this water courses on rapidly westwards, picking up pace as the river grows deeper and narrower. The slopes of the riverbanks not so steep as to prove an obstacle for the seasoned traveller, although the incline of the grassy riverbanks could prove taxing for the weary or the weak.
15890: The once small stream starts picking up its pace as the water rushes westward, running between old fields and pastures. The banks of the stream are not very steep, nor very high, thus leaving one's view almost completely unobstructed in all directions. To the south an old landing can be seen, lying abandoned and broken on the bank. Northwards lie wet fields.
15891: A brook trout is here, swimming in the current.

The small stream runs westwards, slowly picking up pace as it is continually fed water from the surrounding wetlands. It travels carefully between the old overgrown pastures and old drenched fields, babbling and sparkling as it seeks the adventure of a long and rough journey.
15892:
A clear spring babbles as cool water trickles out of the ground.
A swallow flies high above the ground.

Bubbling out of the ground amid the grassy plains, this small spring is the centre of daily life for many small animals. Supplying the surrounding grasslands with water the small spring is also the source of a minor stream journeying westwards, dividing some long unused farmer's fields and once tamed pastureland.
15893: A fallow deer is grazing peacefully here.

Tough green grasses totally engulf this place making even the various hardy weeds compete for their survival. This place could easily feed even large herbivores, but strangely there seems to be a lack of them here. The stench of what remains of some large carnivorous creatures kill rises from spots where the grass has turned yellow-brownish under the scant animal remains.
15894: Open plains stretch out for what seems to be forever with only some small differences in hue to the west and a faint sign of trails or maybe even a road to the southeast. The monotony of the place would surely drive more intelligent creatures insane if forced to dwell here but the small amount of wildlife seems content.
15895: A pack horse is standing here, ridden by you.

Underfoot the ground is hard and cracked, the remnants of an old trail still a part of the landscape. While still visible, the path is slowly being reclaimed by the sturdy grasses and plants that grow on the plains that open up towards the western horizon. To the south the path runs towards the rising cliff wall and eastwards the trail reaches out for an abandoned road that appears only as a thin line in the greenery.
15897: Slanting sharply the cliff wall rises towards the sky, gaining height as it travels southward. Further south a large plateau opens up atop the sheer rock wall. Below runs a small trail that curves and continues just to the north; beyond the trail everything is green as the vast plains stretch towards the horizon.
15898: A pack horse is standing here, ridden by you.

This small cracked trail is losing the battle against the malignant grasses that grow all over the surrounding plains. Following the rising cliff wall that reaches towards the sky both to the east and south, the trail runs north and west from this point onwards. The high wall of rock seems to rise sharply as it travels southward although at this point it would still be possible to climb.
15899:
A restless rabbit bounces around.
A large rabbit looks peacefully at you, ready to dart away.
A pack horse is standing here, ridden by you.

The small path curves here, following the towering cliff wall that rises high in the sky to your east. The ground is cracked and hard and the once well-used path is being reclaimed by the sturdy grasses of the eternally expanding plains that surround it.
15900: A finch flies low above the ground.

Small paths that lie to the east and south border these grassy plains. Though growing wildly the grass here is clearly trampled regularly by some heavy beasts; the tracks look as if they were made by a creature with large paws. Half buried bones from some old carcasses give a hint that there might be large predators around.
15901: Bordered to the south by a small path these plains offer no hiding place for even small animals. The denser vegetation to the east gives the animal life some cover, so the area is not totally devoid of fauna. The small spring to the north provides ample water for the animals and plant life.
15902: A hungry warg stands here, sniffing around for flesh.

The grass grows thick and high as the fallow and lush ground is once again reclaimed from cultivation and covered by the sturdy plants. The rustle of swaying blades of grass blend with the babbling of a small stream just north of here, creating a sharp thin line in the landscape, stretching out in all directions.
15903: A boar cub is playing here, and exploring the wide world.

Just south of the swiftly flowing stream lies this abandoned landing. A small ruined wooden pier runs a few yards out into the water. Further out single wooden poles can be seen as the sole remains of a once well-constructed structure. All around there are high sturdy grasses, diligently working to reclaim what wild lands were once theirs as they cover the land in a dense and green blanket.
15904: The banks of the rapidly flowing river, just to the north, used to be fallow and rich pasture lands, crowded with domesticated beasts that spent their days grazing in the grass. The babbling of the water mixes with the rustling of the high grass, moving slowly in the wind, to create a soft background noise for this setting. To the east lies an old landing, murky and abandoned for ages, and a neglected, now overgrown, field lies dormant to the south.
15905:
A boar cub is playing here, and exploring the wide world.
A swallow flies high above the ground.

A swift flowing river runs along a deep cutting several feet below. The ground drops steeply in an uneven wall of rock dampened by the mists that hang over the water. Brambles and briars fill any tiny gap among the stones covered in thick, green moss. Below, the waters flow swiftly, singing loudly as they pass by the rock faces.
15906: This large plateau opens up and slowly climbs higher to the south and west and slants down to the east, where it soon reaches a once great road that now lies crumbled and ruined. The ground is still covered in grass but the turf grows sparser here, as the soil is not as fertile atop the plateau.
15907: This entire plateau slopes towards the east, as if reaching out for the old road running at its feet. Still covered by sparse grasses, the ground is rather hard and the rock shines through in several spots. The plants that grow here seem to live their lives in constant battle against the strong winds that occasionally threaten their existence.
15908:
A big, nasty vulture is sitting here, protecting its nest.
A big, nasty vulture is sitting here, protecting its nest.
A pack horse (polde) is standing here, ridden by you.

In a small depression on this cliff a few vultures have built their nest, allowing a clear and undisturbed vantage point for the chicks when they hatch. The nest is made of several large branches and huge piles of twigs thrust into a large circular design, carefully sheltering the inhabitants from the worst of the howling winds.
15909: The plateau levels out here as it reaches the cliff wall's edge. The rock lies bare as the soil has been swept away over the decades by the fierce winds that howl by. A few small tufts of grass have managed to get a grip in a small crack but they are dry and ragged, fighting a losing battle against the rough elements of nature.
15910: A pack horse is standing here, ridden by you.

This small path was once well used but now it is cracked and abandoned. The wild grasses are closing in and slowly devouring it as the years go by. The remains of the path run west and north from this point, curving to avoid hitting the cliff wall rising to the east.
15911: Looking high up into the sky, one notices this place is below a sheer cliff wall. The grass does not grow well here, as the ground lies in shadow most of the day. The rock wall rising above has been polished by the rain and wind making any ascent impossible. Just north of here is a faint old path trudging along through the vast plains. To the west there are some abandoned fields.
15914: A skeleton of some humanoid lies in the dust.

Below the branches and twigs in the nest there are several cracks in the stone. Small piles of crushed leaves have fallen down here, as well as a large number of tiny bones from various small animals. Piles of rubbish and dirt cover almost everything and a few small loose stones lie scattered in the dust.
15917: A mole is looking out of a mole-hill here.

Standing just beside a faint and overgrown path lie these remnants of what seems to have been a large wooden structure. The building is ruined and cracked, the roof has fallen in and the walls are on the verge of collapse. Parts of the building have been blackened by fire and large portions of the walls have rotted away. All around the old house lie the grassy plains, stretching out towards the distant horizon.
15918:
A finch flies low above the ground.
A pack horse is standing here, ridden by you.

The path curves here, gradually changing direction to lead both north and east. A tiny branch of the path continues westward, almost buried below the thick and sturdy grasses. Lying all around are the endless expanses of grass-covered fields that have been reclaimed by nature as the years passed by.
15919: An old and almost completely covered path leads travellers through the high grasses here, towards the remnants of an old farming village just to the west. The path turns here, continuing on north and east, through the old and abandoned fields that surround it.
15920:
A fierce boar is here, making grunting noises.
A boar cub is playing here, and exploring the wide world.
A boar cub is playing here, and exploring the wide world.

What was once a house of some sort is now merely a pile of rotting and decaying wood topped with a slanting roof. The doorpost still stands and the broken door hangs loosely on rusted hinges, seemingly ready to collapse at the slightest disturbance. All the walls have caved in and the entire house seems unstable and ready to crash down at any moment.
15921: Once an old corral for bred horses, the fences are now rotting and murky. A large heap of bones and skulls lies in the far southwest corner and a foul stench of death and decay surrounds you. The once so lush and green grass is withered and dead and there are faint imprints made by large paws in the soft soil.
15922:
Some thick writhing vines whip all around you.
A swallow flies high above the ground.
A finch flies low above the ground.

Overgrown by dark reeds and vines the old fields are now hostile and dark. Any trace of the old farmers have since long been destroyed and now only vile nature leaves its trademark on the forgotten field. Imprinted in the soft soil are the faint marks of great paws.
15923:
A finch flies low above the ground.
A swallow flies high above the ground.

This old field, once used by farmers inhabiting the surrounding area, is now overgrown and covered in tall and sturdy weeds that have reclaimed the land. The soft soil below shows markings of recent passage, as parts of the grass are trampled and bent. Surrounding the field are several ancient ruined buildings, some of which are merely wooden skeletons, blackened and cracked. North of here lies abandoned pasture land. The overgrown fields reach out further to the west.
15924:
A swallow flies high above the ground.
A pack horse is standing here, ridden by you.

A small path leads through the grass, passing a crumbled ruin as it turns, to the southwest. The path is almost completely lost to the fierce grasses that fight to reclaim the land where the trail was marked. The ruined wooden structure is an old farm, burned and cracked, leaving only a wooden skeleton as a reminder of the once proud village. North lies an old and abandoned landing just visible from this place, while to the southwest are some old abandoned fields.
15925:
A large rabbit looks peacefully at you, ready to dart away.
A swallow flies high above the ground.
A pack horse is standing here, ridden by you.

This faint path stretches out as a thin, vague line through the grass covered old fields reaching from east to west. All around lie overgrown and abandoned pastures and fields that are now being reclaimed and restored to their pre-cultivation status by the fiercely growing grasses. Further west the remnants of a small farming settlement can be seen.
15926: A fallow deer is grazing peacefully here.

Running east to west this old path lies abandoned and broken. What was once a broad and well-travelled trail has now become narrow and partly covered in grass as the hardy grasses slowly, but inevitably, reclaim this once populated land. Stretching out northward lies a vast expanse of plains, resembling a large green ocean. South of here there lies an old rotting building. The path continues both to the east and west, valiantly fighting a losing battle against the encroaching grass.
15927:
A lone hawk soars high above you.
A large rabbit looks peacefully at you, ready to dart away.
A swallow flies high above the ground.
A pack horse is standing here, ridden by you.

Coming from the west and leading off to the east, this path has clearly not been in regular use for ages. The plains to the north and the old fields to the south slowly creep towards the path with the clear intent of overwhelming it. On the portions of the small path that remain faint tracks of large paws can be seen.
15928: A worm is here slithering around.

Once someone lived and farmed this land, but now the fields lie long forgotten and long grass has been given free reign. To the west you can distinguish some kind of old structure where whomever farmed the land might have lived. East and south vast, lifeless plains stretch out and to the north you can spot a small path zig-zaging across the fields.
15929:
A bloodthirsty bat is sleeping here, hanging from the ceiling.
A bloodthirsty bat is sleeping here, hanging from the ceiling.
A bloodthirsty bat is sleeping here, hanging from the ceiling.
A bloodthirsty bat is sleeping here, hanging from the ceiling.
A bloodthirsty bat is sleeping here, hanging from the ceiling.

This old structure was once a barn, that much is obvious from the remnants of the building. It seems to have been partly attacked by flames at some time as part of the wall and ceiling to your west is blackened and cracked. The northern part of the house has caved in, allowing the wind and rain to freely ravage the old barn. Several of the walls are rotting and the overall impression is one of decay and age.
15930: This small cave in the ground is littered by debris; a few scraps of wood, a small boulder and several carcasses of unfortunate animals. The walls of the cave are roughly cut and entirely undecorated.
15931:
A large earth troll is digging here, looking for some tasty morsels.
A small, mean earth troll is standing here, thinking of something hideous.

The small passage twists downwards in an endless slope, smoothly cut through the rock and dirt. Strange echoes and voices are carried by the walls and small spots of light flicker in and out of existence.
15932:
There are two half-rotten corpses here.
An ancient black altar stands in the centre of the room.
Brolg, shaman of the Ohurk-uai, is here, chanting some evil incantations.

At the bottom of the sloping corridor a small chamber opens up. The walls are smoothly cut out of the rock and the floor is packed dirt. On the walls there are several inscriptions and carvings that surround replicas of a red eye. On the ground in the centre of the room stands a small black altar.
15933:
A very strong, orkish patrol-leader is looking for enemies here.
An orkish soldier is here, patrolling the area.
An orkish soldier is here, patrolling the area.

Close to the edge of the cliff the grass still grows thick and dense, not caring about the eighty-foot drop to the plains below. The plateau reaches further north along the edge of the cliff as well as sloping gently downwards as it travels towards the east.
15934: The hill slopes upward to your west, slowly climbing as if it was waking up after a long night's sleep. This hill is the only break in an otherwise plain and flat landscape, rising majestically and overlooking the vast expanse of the flowing plains.
15935: The plain slopes slightly as it approaches the hill just north of you. Strange patterns appear and disappear in the grasses as winds blow in gusts around the hill. The vegetation is not very high or dense here, but further away you can see that it grows thicker and higher. The hill blocks your view north, but in all other directions you see the endless plains stretching out towards the horizon.
15936:
A small rabbit glares angrily at you.
A small rabbit glares angrily at you.

Here the grasses are waist high, thick and dense, being the perfect environment for smaller animals to hide and thrive. The height of the grass makes it behave like waves rolling on the sea, shifting even at the slightest gust of wind. High up in the sky you can see a few small, dark dots, swirling and twisting about in strange patterns.
15937: The green flowing grass here resembles an ocean, waves rolling over its surface as the wind blows. The way it stretches out endlessly towards the horizon makes the similarity even more striking. Not much can be seen that breaks the surface of the plains, and nothing disturbs the peace except for an occasional bird or animal that scurries about in the undergrowth.
15938: A swallow flies high above the ground.

Waving in the wind, the grasses stand proud and tall here, covering the ground completely. As you look at the scenery, you notice that the appearances of the various grasses change to your west, as the grasses become shorter, thinner and bleaker. A bit to your north you notice a hill rising in the plains.
15939: The ground of these plains is cracked and dry. Nothing grows here and the few turfs of grass that remain are yellow and completely dead. Dust rises as a gust of wind blows by, slowly falling back, covering almost everything with a thin layer of brown. The brown colours seem to prevail no matter where you look, but suddenly you catch a glimpse of some greenery far to the east.
15940: The grass here is withered and yellow, almost as if life was sucked out from it. You notice that there is a clear difference as you look at the grass from north to the south, changing from yellow to a bleak green. At the horizon to your north you see some kind of stones lined up, almost as an army, marching to war.
15941: The plains here are dead. Nothing grows or lives here. No sound can be heard and no animal can be seen. The plains are as green as ever south and west of you, but north and east they seem withered and dying. Northeast of you there seem to be some black shapes at the horizon.
15942: An Ohurk-uai warg-rider, wielding a lance, is here, riding a hungry warg.

The ground is irregular here, broken by a few small cracks and a few low hills. A small rabbit hole can be seen in one of the small hills, and sounds of movement can be heard in the grass near it. A few yards from the rabbit hole lies a large flat rock on which snakes seem to sunbathe, as indicated by the remains of a scaly reptile skin on the rock's surface.
15943: In the high surrounding grass, you can see small cracks in the ground. As you look closer, you see that they get wider as they continue north, opening up into a wide, deep canyon. The passage north thus being effectively blocked, the only route available seems to be along the grass-covered plains to your east and west. Not much else can be seen in the flowing greenery, but small animals create a veil of background noise, embedding you in the everyday sounds of nature.
15944: In the plains here a few small bushes grow in the short, thick grass. The bushes are not very high or thick, but they seem to compete with the grasses for the space to live. So far, the bushes seem to be on the loosing side of the war.
15945: The wind makes a soft rustle in the high grass, making it flow back and forth, gently rocking in the breeze. The ground you pass on is soft and gives a little as you travel along. First, it almost seems as if you are on an endless plain that stretches out eternally, but finally you spot a small black dot on the northern horizon. Judging by the distance, the dot must be very large to be seen from here.
15946: A swallow flies high above the ground.

Close to the old broken road, the plains are still covered in thick and high grass, rising as a mighty wave that is rolling in towards the road, to crush it and sweep away the last traces of humanity. Still the road runs in a straight line in the green of the plains, a clearly visible landmark.
15947: The grassy plain here is bustling with activity, small animals rustling about in the undergrowth chasing insects, and birds singing high in the sky. Not even your presence or the proximity of the old abandoned road seem to dampen the sounds of living nature.
15948: Here the plains have exploded into life. The nearby water has made it possible for the grasses to grow tall and thick, making the passage difficult. As the plants thrive, so do the animals. Everywhere you look you see movement and hear the sounds of animals running about in the grass. All around you the plains stretch out, with a few exceptions. Just southeast of here you spot a small thicket of trees and due west you see the faint outlines of a road running as a silver line in the plains.
15949: The grass grows rather short here, being so close to the old road that runs through the plains as if someone cut the ground with a knife. Not much disturbs the peace here, an occasional bird or some small animal rustling through the thicker undergrowth. The sharp line indicating the road lies a bit to your west and north, while the thick green expanses of grass cover the soil all around you.
15950: Enveloped by the high grass, you are surrounded by the eternal struggle for survival. Small birds fly in mystical patterns in the sky, chasing creatures invisible to you. Sounds from crawling animals can be heard from all directions as the smaller inhabitants make their way through the grass. Around you the plains stretch out like a huge green blanket, covering everything that you can see.
15951: Here used to lie an old field, but the farmers that used to live here are hardly remembered by the soil these days. The once so rich fields are now grass-covered and several kinds of weeds grow wild here. Rotting poles of wood can be spotted in a few places, indicating where the old fences used to be. This old reclaimed field now bears every likeness to the vast, surrounding ocean of grass.
15952: A swallow flies high above the ground.

The field extends all the way up to the old castle wall. Once burned to keep it clear so the keep's inhabitants would be alerted of approaching enemies, it is now, once again, covered in grass and weeds. The wall blocks all passage to the north, but nothing prevents you from going elsewhere. Some kind of ruin lies dead east, and on all other sides the plains flow endlessly.
15953: Not much is left of this old farm. The walls and the roof caved in, leaving nothing but a few rotting logs intact. Everything else is now covered by the grass of the plains growing in on every side, as nature strives to reclaim what was once in its possession.
15954: This old vineyard has now grown wild. Weeds, grasses, and vines compete for the soil, and the match is even so far. Remains of a fence litter the ground, and just west of here you spot some old ruins. The flowing plains surround you on all the other sides.
15955: A swallow flies high above the ground.

You travel on a part of the plains that connects the old overgrown fields of the nearby abandoned keep with the dried grass south and the lush green grounds to the north and east. You can spot a high hill due east, it being one of the most prominent landmarks here. Far to the northwest you spot a tower.
15956: You find yourself below a high hill in the flowing plains. Rising high above, it is an obstacle that you can't pass, thus preventing any passage east. You might be able to climb to the top if you circle it, passing through the green plains to your north or through the withered, yellow grass you can spot just south of the hill. Not much can be heard or seen here, except an occasional bird flying by.
15957: Here, on top of the hill, your view is excellent. You can see far as there are no other obstacles close by. Far west you see the outlines of a tower and several miles north you can see the blue band of a river. All around you the plains stretch out, covering the land like an immense blanket, with ripples running across it as it is flowing in the wind.
15958: The plains rise sharply just to your north, rising to become a high and steep hill. In the otherwise featureless land, this hill is an excellent landmark, being visible from afar. Around you in all other directions the plains flow on as lush as ever. Something is strange about the colour to your west though, as it seems to be more bleak and yellow than green.
15959: The grass lies flat on the ground here, as if something has weighed it down for some time and was just recently removed. The remains of an old campfire can be spotted as well, the blackened pieces of wood scattered about on the ground. The surrounding high grass has hidden the old campsite from view rather well, as it is thick and almost man-high.
15960: Now and again, a small gust of wind lifts the dust from the ground, forming a small hazy veil that for a second prevents you from seeing what lies ahead of you. After it slowly falls to the ground, you can see that most of the grass here has withered to dust and not many things live in the area. The ground starts to become green due east, but as you look farther west, you cannot see anything living, not even grass.
15961: Absolutely nothing grows here. The ground lies bare, the soil long since blown away since nothing could bind it here. Somehow the death and decay of the area seem to emanate from the centre of the large stones that stand on top of a small burial mound. The stones are black and about two yards high. There are four of them, standing in a circle, with a smaller, flat stone block lying in the middle. Not even the wind seems to blow there, and everything seems to slow down, waiting for something to happen.
15962: The area seems silent, almost dead, but you can feel the small animals move around you and small insects fly by. Still nothing can be heard. The farther east you look, the lower and bleaker the grasses appear. To the west the land is as green as ever, but north and south it does not seem any better.
15963:
Some small rocks have been piled into a mound here.
A swallow flies high above the ground.

West of you the ground opens up into a deep and dark chasm. The ground must have been cracked and broken by something powerful to split up in such a way. The canyon stretches out further south, trailing off in the distant southwest. Even though the ground is cracked and broken, the grasses still thrive here. They even grow a bit down the canyon walls, as if trying to claim the cleft for themselves.
15964: As you continue your travel along the grassy plains, you notice that the smooth ground has been broken here. As the ground split open, a winding chasm has formed here, preventing any passage farther east or south. The chasm is not so wide, but still broad enough to make it impossible to pass. The plants and grasses that live here do not seem bothered though, but grow all the way out to the edge, and even a bit down on the chasm's walls.
15965: Just west of you is a small thicket of trees, which is the only noticeable landmark for some distance. The ground here is soft, covered in low but sturdy grasses that keep the soil in place. Far to your north you can barely discern a vague outline of a small and thin needle-like construct and through a haze you can just make out the far reaches of the Misty Mountains in the east.
15967: In the ground there is a small depression, that over the years has collected water and thus has almost become a small lake. The vegetation is dense; several types of grasses and small trees grow here. Just south of the depression some trees have managed to grow taller, creating some shadowy places on these large sunbathed plains.
15968:
A snake slithers towards you.
A swallow flies high above the ground.

Just north of you lie what seems to be remnants of an old field, and you can spot something that might have been an old pond just west. All around you the grass still spreads out, covering the ground completely. Farther to your north you can spot what seems to be a tower, rising among a dark thicket of some kind of bushes.
15969: Plains Close to the Old Tower

Surrounded by green, you find yourself in the middle of the flowing plains. Once this might have been a field, where farmers worked for the old lord of the keep that you see towering up over you to the north. The vast expanse of green stretches out in all directions, only disturbed by a few small ruins in the east. As you travel through the grass, you feel that the weeds are bubbling with life as the small inhabitants of the earth run around, hidden from view, but still creating a soft but perceivable wall of sound.
15970: It is hard to discern anything in the rubble of rock and rotting wood here, but the mere size of the pile suggests that it should once have been a barn. The proximity to the ruined farmhouse just to the north only strengthens the impression. Now, the once cleared area is overgrown and wild, once again.
15971: Here the plains seem absent-minded, as if they were waiting for something, or someone. Nothing grows here, no animals pass here and the soil lies bare beneath the sky. The surrounding plains do not look much better in the southeast, but as you look north and west, they seem to be alive and thriving. A few small, dark shapes can be spotted just at the south-eastern horizon.
15972: A swallow flies high above the ground.

Even though the air is moist and the surrounding plains are lush and green, this particular area seems dry and void of any animal life. The grasses growing here are yellow and short, as if they are fighting for their very existence every second of the day. As you scan the surroundings, you notice that no matter in which direction you look, it only seems to get better to the north, and much worse as you look south.
15973: The plains here seem drained, tired and lifeless. Void of anything that walks or crawls, the only things living here are a few sturdy grasses and some small weird-looking plants. Although the land seems alive and vibrant just north and east of here, the area south and west seems to suffer from some sort of plague that keeps the land in eternal pain and misery.
15976: Yellow flowers, with grey-green foliage, grow in clusters here.

This area of the grassland stands sheltered by a higher plateau to the east. Without the constant assault of the chill prevailing winds a rich little meadow has sprung up here. The grass is particularly long and thick, and more bushes grow here than anywhere for miles around. Even a lone elm tree stands proudly here, ancient and tall.
15977: North and west the land seems blighted and this part of the landscape has not escaped the effect entirely. The grass underfoot is limp and rather dry. Yellow-green in colour, none of the vegetation looks healthy, but a few coarse weeds hold their heads up defiantly. To the east the picture brightens, where a sea of lush growth can be seen.
15978: Where once there must have been lush, dark green grass now there remains only limp blades. A dull grey-green cast dominates the area and in places this is being replaced by a yellow pall which increases in proportion the further to the north you look. But if the grass is bad, the other vegetation is worse; the few small bushes dotted across the area appear to be completely lifeless and even the toughest weeds are hanging limp.
15979: Further to the north it appears that the once verdant plains have been visited by some sort of blight, for no vegetation now remains. The lush grass here, however, did not succumb, growing as wild and untrammelled as ever. Amongst the bright blades of grass a number of wildflowers and tough weeds also flourish, but on such an exposed plain no larger plants seem able to survive particularly well.
15980: Long blades of grass dance upon the breeze, rippling and rolling like the water of a lake lapping upon its shores. East and south the vegetation seems not nearly so lush, but north and west of here the emerald ocean stretches far into the distance.
15981: Deep fissures scar the ground, running north to south across the landscape. To the north they open out markedly, whilst to the south they disappear into a field of massive boulders. A few stubborn weeds and thick tufts of yellow grass grow between the cracks and boulders, and this vegetation becomes more lush even as the clefts grow wider.
15982: On a Bleak and Windswept Plain
Prickly, white-stemmed plants, with blue flower heads grow in abundance.

Thin, rocky topsoil makes for only the poorest of vegetation in this area. Further north the ground apparently improves and lush grasses dominate the landscape, but here only the coarsest of weeds, a thin covering of sickly, yellow grass and a small number of stunted bushes cling to life. East and south the terrain worsens.
15983: On a Bleak and Windswept Plain
Prickly, white-stemmed plants, with blue flower heads grow in abundance.

Whilst to the north the plains boast lush vegetation the ground here is rather rockier and its thin soil supports only tough clumps of yellow grass, coarse weeds, and a few small and scattered bushes. With no protection from the elements this is a bleak and uninviting area, perpetually buffeted by strong winds.
15984: The vegetation here is spread rather thinly. Only a few stunted bushes, some tough weeds, and some scattered tussocks of coarse, yellow grass have fought their way through the rocky ground. A small circle of stones has been set on the ground, not far from the eaves of the woods to the south, and a few small bones lie on the ground beside it. To the east of here the landscape remains much the same, but in all other directions the plant life grows more dominant.
15985: A few stubborn bushes mark the outermost reaches of a forest which rises above the landscape to the west of here. The predominant groundcover is loose stone and small boulders, but a few tough hummocks of grass and some coarse weeds sprout up amongst the rocks.
15986: Deep fissures and small gullies criss-cross the landscape. Between these the ground is covered by rocks, boulders and loose stone. Grass grows in thick clumps wherever it can find purchase, but the soil seems to be thin and little other vegetation can be seen in the area. To the west and north the landscape seems more lush, but south and east ever more boulders and rather fewer plants are to be seen.
15987: A finch flies low above the ground.

The land is split and scarred by dozens of narrow, parallel cracks which run from north to south. Between them the ground is peppered by loose rocks and stones, and no small number of massive boulders. To the north the fissures grow wider; to the south it is the boulders which dominate the landscape.
15988: A finch flies low above the ground.

To the north the land is blanketed by a lush covering of grass, but here the vegetation must do battle against the many rocks and stones that litter the ground. The soil too is thin and coarse. Clumps of yellowing grass stand amid the scattered rubble, but no larger plants can be seen in this area.
15989: Yellow flowers, with grey-green foliage, grow in clusters here.

Plant life proliferates here. Thick, dark green grass grows tall and strong, bent but not broken by the constant winds which assail the plains. Amid the lush grass grow wildflowers which pepper the meadow with bright colour, and here and there a small bush adds height to the otherwise flat landscape.
15990: East, west and south of you the land is blanketed by rich vegetation. Here the story is different; the grass is thin and yellowing, its limp blades bent and broken by the wind. The small bushes which are scattered about the area appear weak and diseased. To the north the picture steadily grows worse.
15991: Whatever has blighted the lands to the west and north of here, this part of the plains seems to have escaped its touch. Perhaps the sheltering influence of the high plateau to the east has played a role. The grass here grows tall and dark, and numerous small shrubs have sprouted up amid the green blades.
15993: Many heavy feet have trod the ground here and what little vegetation there was has been reduced to a muddy pulp. A stiff wind howls across this high plateau, made icy in the distant heights of the Misty Mountains. Not far to the west and north the highlands come to an abrupt end. To the south the high ground gives way more gradually, where a more gentle slope offers access to the low-lying plains beyond.
15994: East and north the ground climbs toward a vast plateau which stretches toward the foothills of the Misty Mountains in the east. South and west it falls off gently toward a lower-lying plain, lush with deep green grass. Despite the slope a good deal of vegetation can be seen here, from thick tufts of grass to coarse weeds and even a few rather small shrubs.
15995: Sloping gently down to the west, this land marks the eastern boundary of a vast area of rolling plains. Thick, green grass fights for supremacy over the coarse tufts of yellow grasses, which are dominant on the higher lands to the east. A few stunted bushes have also made their home here, clinging to life despite the gradient. Someone or something has recently uprooted many of them, although the reason for this destruction is not apparent.
15996: The land slopes very gradually upward to the east, climbing toward a higher, more exposed portion of the plains. In the shelter of this plateau the land here is relatively protected from the prevailing winds, and the grass grows tall and strong. Thick bushes are dotted across the landscape and the ground is peppered by wildflowers.
15997: A dense carpet of vegetation covers the ground. Tall grass and thick heather battle for domination over the land. A number of small bushes and shrubs are scattered amid the resulting patchwork of green and purple foliage, which stretches far to the south. East and north the grass wins out, but westward the plant life must contend with a harsher, more rocky landscape.
15998: A finch flies low above the ground.

Coarse tufts of grass and thick little weeds sprout up through the rocky ground. A few small, hardy bushes have laid claim to the open areas between the larger boulders which litter the landscape here. Westward the massive stones grow more numerous and finding a clear route among them appears to be rather a difficult task.
15999: A mottled snake is sneaking here, ready to sink its fangs into flesh (hidden).

All around you the land is covered by enormous boulders, as if an entire hillside had been blasted apart. Some bear thin veins of metal or ore. Some are rough, others almost perfectly smooth. Their size and variety, their uncountable numbers, and their very presence here are a mute testimony to the grandeur and to the dangers of Arda.
16000:
The corpse of a mottled snake is lying here.
A mountain mule (polde) is standing here, ridden by you.

An unforgiving wall of granite stands before you to the south, blocking the way completely. Nor is there a clear route from this place to any other side, for the entire area is crowded with gigantic boulders. Between them the ground is covered by smaller rocks and stones, and of plant life you can see none.
16001: Gargantuan boulders clutter the landscape. Between them lie scattered rocks and stones, and vegetation is almost completely absent. North and west there lie so many of the massive stones that it is impossible to see any clear route. East and south the way seems at least a little more open.
16002: By the Border of a Twisted Forest

A few rough bushes and shrubs have taken hold amongst the rocks and boulders as the encroaching forest to the west slowly takes hold of this area. The uneven ground makes treacherous footing, and the scattering of rocky debris becomes more concentrated as you move to the east or south.
16003: By the Border of a Twisted Forest
A robin is here, carrying small pieces of wood to its nest.

To the north and west of you a large, but strangely twisted, forest rises above the landscape. A little of its tangled undergrowth seems to be spreading this way, but it is hard for anything to grow in the thin soil of this area. Tumbled piles of rocks and boulders are scattered about the place, and these grow more numerous to the east. To the south the terrain begins a gentle climb into a narrow ridge of hills.
16004: Not far from the edge of the forest, and nestled against the flank of a range of hills to the south, the land undergoes quite a dramatic change. Grass, brush and trees are replaced by rocks, stones and a few huge boulders. The topsoil is thin, almost completely absent in places, and even the most stubborn weeds seem to have difficulty finding purchase in the rocky ground. To the east the terrain actually worsens, with ever more boulders to be seen.
16005: A large pile of boulders is sitting here, probably debris from a rockslide.

To the south a solid wall of granite rears high above you. Massive boulders are scattered across the land, as if an entire hillside somehow lay shattered here. East and west the rocks become less numerous but to the north their numbers increase, and it is hard to see any clear route between them.
16006: An unforgiving wall of granite stands before you to the south, blocking the way completely. Nor is there a clear route from this place to any other side, for the entire area is crowded with gigantic boulders. Between them the ground is covered by smaller rocks and stones, and of plant life you can see none.
16007: The ground is entirely blanketed by rocks and stones. No appreciable amount of vegetation can be seen here, with only a few weak stems of yellow grass peeping up between the smallest pebbles. The landscape is dominated by vast numbers of colossal boulders, interspersed by many monumental heaps of rather smaller stones.
16008: A pack horse (Rood) is standing here, ridden by you.

The coarse grass and heather of the open moors is largely replaced here by a jumble of rocks and stones. With the cold, hard pebbles and larger boulders littering the landscape vegetation must fight for even a small foothold on the area, and of larger plants there are almost none. Westward the rocks are even more dominant and massive piles of stones, in addition to many massive boulders, stand in your way.
16009:
Prickly, white-stemmed plants, with blue flower heads grow in abundance.
A sparrow is flapping around on the ground.

A flat landscape stretches out before you in all directions. One could be forgiven for thinking it featureless, but closer inspection shows that the terrain is beautiful, albeit in a bleak and windswept fashion. Low tufts of purple heather grow in profusion, offering bright patches of colour amid the tough, yellow-green grass. In the far distance the Misty Mountains stand tall on the horizon. Closer to here stand two lower ranges of hills, and not too far to the south the land slopes away into a river valley.
16010: Prickly, white-stemmed plants, with blue flower heads grow in abundance.

Not far to the northeast the land begins a gentle ascent towards a higher plateau. In all other directions the ground is quite flat, stretching out far into the distance. All that strives to grow here must do so despite the constant buffeting by the winds which howl across the open moors. Low tufts of coarse, yellow-green grass form a chaotic patchwork with thick clumps of purple heather, but no taller plants are to be seen here.
16011: This is a transitional area. Westward a vast, gently rolling plain opens out before you covered by a thick blanket of dark green grasses. Here the ground rises gently, climbing toward a higher plateau, where the only plant life is the coarse, yellow grass characteristic of peaty moorland. Both types of vegetation vie for control of this area and despite the slope it seems that the more verdant, lowland species are going to win out.
16012:
A rusted key lies here.
A orc patrol-leader of the Ohurk-uai is looking for enemies here.

To the south the land slopes gently toward a small stream. East it climbs to a high and bleak plateau which stands in stark contrast to the lush plains you can see below you to the west. A variety of plant life makes its home on these slopes, but the dominant feature is coarse, rather yellow grass which grows in thick clumps all about you.
16013: A Rocky Path to the Hills

Climbing to the east, the land rises above the forest and plains into a narrow ridge of hills. Though you are not upon a trail as such, few shrubs or large plants obstruct your way and it seems comparatively easy to pick a route among the rocks and boulders which lie scattered all about you.
16014: The land falls off precipitously to the north, making travel in that direction quite impossible. To the west and south, however, it slopes gently toward the plains below. The ground underfoot is a mass of rough stones and scree, making your footing more than a little unsteady, and only a few small tufts of coarse, yellow grass manage to grow in the thin topsoil.
16015: Though the slope down from the ridge to the south is rather steep it is as nothing compared to the northern flank of this narrow ridgeline. It appears as if at some past time the entire northern face of the hillside had been blasted away, and the valley floor below is littered with gargantuan piles of rocks and boulders.
16016: This ridge of hills stands high above the plains, completely exposed to the elements. Westward a rough trail, made more by an absence of vegetation than by any other agency, leads gently down; in all other directions the way is too steep and littered by loose scree, making any attempt at descent impossible.
16017: The corpse of a mottled snake is lying here.

A tall cliff rears above you to the west. Its cold, rocky face is broken by a rough aperture which gapes wide, like the maw of some mighty beast. All around you the ground is littered by massive boulders. No plant life has taken root among them, the land instead being covered by smaller rocks and stones.
16018: Thick, purple heather and coarse tufts of yellow-green grass make a patchwork of the land, but this colourful quilt is marred by the innumerable rocks and stones which are littered across the entire area. Westward these grow larger and more numerous, completely blocking the way. South the land slopes gently off toward a river valley. Eastward stands a windswept expanse of open moors, and north the stony meadow stretches out before you.
16019: Prickly, white-stemmed plants, with blue flower heads grow in abundance.

Only to the south does the land vary at all. In all other directions you see a vast expanse of open moorland. Bleak in aspect, the terrain is dominated by coarse tufts of low-growing grass, interspersed by bright patches of purple heather. No larger plants seem able to thrive on this windswept ground. To the south the land slopes gently downward, approaching a river valley.
16020: Barely climbing above the wetlands to the east, and marking the crest of a longer rise to the south, the land here slopes only a little. The earth is blanketed by a patchwork of coarse, yellow-green grasses and dark purple heather. Here and there the vegetation is interrupted by splotches of open ground where water pools.
16021: Clusters of slender stems and tall leaves thrive in the mud and shallows.

A small stream flows by, its muddy waters sometimes washing over its banks to create what is almost a marshland. The lush, green grasses of the plains below give way to wetland species here, with tall reeds and cattails proliferating. This wet shoulder of land stretches south, following the course of the brook, born and nurtured by its ever-present waters.
16022: Twisting and turning, this shallow stream makes its haphazard way across the high plains. Cutting its channel readily through the peaty ground it picks up a lot of the red-brown dirt as it travels sluggishly along, turning here from a westerly to a southerly course.
16023: Shallow and sluggish, this stream makes only slow progress as it wanders across the high plains. It gathers a little more speed as it flows onward to the south where the land gradually begins to fall away, losing altitude with each mile it travels towards the valley floor southeast of here.
16024: The stream gathers speed here as it traces the descending landscape. Resuming a westerly course it chases down a gentle grade, frequently undercutting its own banks and picking up more of the red-brown earth which has already given its waters a rusty hue.
16025: Turning here from a westerly to a southerly course, the stream has begun to undercut its own low banks. Already tainted by red-brown earth, the waters now become even more turbid as they flow onward, picking up more of the soft dirt as they go.
16026: Two lively streams meet here forming a single larger waterway. Where the waters mingle you can see a swirling pattern, for the slower stream from the north bears heavy traces of red-brown earth whilst the more lively southern waterway runs quite clear. Flowing together the water cascades westward, tumbling over rocks and boulders as it makes its way along the valley floor.
16027: At the Bottom of a Waterfall
A brook trout is here, swimming in the current.

Chilly water cascades down from above, pouring into this basin from the east. Following the contours of the land it then traces a channel to the north from here, then onward down the length of the valley, racing westward toward an eventual confluence with the Bruinen. A number of large boulders break through the surface of the pool and the waters roil and play about them casting a thin veil of mist high into the air.
16028: A brook trout is here, swimming in the current.

Through the years this lively stream has cut a deep but fairly narrow channel into the living rock. Following the slope of the land it races west from here, cleaving a path around a massive granite prominence before dancing over the lip of rock to tumble to the valley floor below. Swirling on a few boulders which stand proud of the chilly surface the water splashes merrily and a fine mist cools and dampens the air.
16029: Ambling across this relatively flat countryside the waters of two streams have combined to form a small river. Its bed is wide here, held in to the north by a soft, low, peaty bank, whose earth is readily washed away by the gentle current. South the terrain is rockier and slopes more steeply upward.
16030: The low northern shore of the river is comprised of soft, peaty earth and appears to be somewhat marshy, judging by the vegetation. Though the current is rather languid the waters nevertheless sweep along more dirt as they pass by. Thus the river widens a little more to the north every day. To the south, however, the bank is rocky and stands firm.
16031:
The prominent fin of a silver-yellow fish breaks the surface of the water.
A robin is here, carrying small pieces of wood to its nest.

A firm, rocky bank holds the river to the south. The north shore is lower and formed from soft, peaty soil. As the water swirls past, it picks up ever more of the brown earth, carrying it west. The perpetual undercutting has made the river rather wide and its waters flow lazily along. Further downstream, where the land grows more rocky, the river is funnelled into a tighter course.
16032:
A sparrow is flapping around on the ground.
A robin is here, carrying small pieces of wood to its nest.

The river remains fairly wide here, and rather shallow. A number of small rocks break its surface, making the waters dance and swirl about, sending a thin mist into the air. Both shores are fairly low but rocky and strong, guiding the waterway firmly along its westerly course.
16033: As the river progresses westwards its course becomes ever more narrow and ever more rocky, causing it to splash and frolic, casting a fine mist into the air. The banks here stand only a little higher than the water level, but they are stony and firm. It will be many long years before these lively waters manage to undercut the shore.
16048: A brown fox is here, looking for some rabbits to chew up.

A small river traces its course through this sloping valley. Following the waterway back towards its source, to the east, the slope is very gradual. To the north, as you approach a ridge of hills, the valley floor makes a steeper ascent. A thin mist pervades the air, offspring of the lively waters which splash along a rocky channel.
16049: A thin mist fills the air all around you, leaving dewy drops on everything it touches. It is plain to see that this is the result of the lively little river which bubbles through the valley. The vale itself runs from east to west, losing altitude as it travels away from the foothills of the Misty Mountains.
16050: A small river rushes through the valley, tumbling over rocks and sending up a fine mist which hangs in the air all about you. The land rises sharply to the north, where it climbs toward a tall ridge of hills. To the south, beyond the river, a second ridge, foothills to the Misty Mountains, marks the southern boundary of the vale.
16051: Westward the valley loses altitude and becomes narrower as it is forced between two long, hilly ridges. To the east it opens out as it travels through a wide area of open plains, hemmed in only to the far south by the foothills of the Misty Mountains. A bright brook rushes through the vale, its chilly waters sending up a light mist all around.
16052: The ground here is fairly rocky, but rich enough to support a thin blanket of grass. To the south a small river flows by, its silty waters splashing against a rocky bank. Sloping gently along the length of the valley, and down towards the river, the land climbs more steeply to the north where it draws near to a ridge of hills.
16053: A sparrow is flapping around on the ground.

The valley runs from east to west, making a steady descent. Here the river bank is rather rocky, but does not stand at any great height above the flowing waters. This has apparently resulted in repeated flooding of the area, leaving behind a rich, silty soil which supports a lush growth of dark green grass, weeds, wildflowers and numerous small shrubs and bushes.
16054: Clusters of slender stems and tall leaves thrive in the mud and shallows.

A wide but shallow river flows by to the south, its lazy waters swirling idly by. It is hard to tell where the river really ends and the land actually begins. A broad ribbon of shallows and mud flats stretches along the shore, a result of the perpetual flooding and erosion of the soft, earthy bank by the unforgiving water.
16055: Clusters of slender stems and tall leaves thrive in the mud and shallows.

Wetland species dominate the landscape. A small stream flows by to the east, merging with another waterway then flowing sedately past immediately to the south of here. The low banks have often been breached by the waters, leaving this area more like a marsh or mud flat than a shoreline.
16056: The ground slopes here, descending both to the south and to the east. Climbing to the north it rises above the river valley to an area of open moorland. To the east the descent is much more gradual, so that this sloping ground barely stands above the muddy wetlands there. Lush green grass carpets the earth, and a few small shrubs are dotted across the landscape.
16057: Clusters of slender stems and tall leaves thrive in the mud and shallows.

Though the stream which flows by to the east is small and quite sluggish its waters have nevertheless breached its banks here often enough to leave this an area of marshes and mud flats. To the west the landscape is dominated by flowing grassy plains which give way, in the distance, to a rockier valley but here it is the plants of the shallows that proliferate.
16058: Though some distance from the river this place has been chosen as the site of a camp. Further south the land becomes quite marshy, but here the ground makes a gradual ascent, climbing toward an area of bleak, open moorland. This slope affords at least some measure of shelter from the stiff winds which howl across the flatlands. A small ring of stones has been set out, and next to these a single, far larger boulder rests.
16059: A fat rabbit sits here, chewing on some grass.

The ground changes slightly here, as it makes a very gentle descent toward the river valley below. Whilst to the north there is a patchwork of coarse grass and tufts of heather, here some hardy little bushes have sprouted; the grass is softer and the heather is present only in isolated clumps.
16060: Grass, rocks and heather fight for possession of this sloping ground. To the northwest, where it draws toward a ridge of hills, the terrain becomes ever more rocky. To the east, along the valley, it is the grass that wins out, fed by the waters of the river below. To the northeast a vast area of open moorland stretches before you, blanketed by coarse grass and heather.
16061: In the Shadow of a Ridge of Hills

A tall ridge of hills rears above you to the north, its sheer sides quite unclimbable at this point. The land here is peppered by loose rock and stone, which probably tumbled down from the rocky slopes above. Many lie hidden under a thick covering of dark green grass which grows tall and strong in the shelter of the hillside. A few small, stout bushes fill out the landscape.
16062: On the Slopes of a Ridge of Hills
A finch flies low above the ground.

The valley floor slopes steeply to the north, where it nestles against the flank of a tall ridge of hills. Eastward the land also rises, though more gently, as it climbs steadily toward the distant Misty Mountains. The ground itself is a mixture of lush grass and rockier patches as the two terrains mingle here.
16063: Thick grass covers the lands immediately to your south, but looking north the land becomes sloped and rather less lush. Scattered rocks lie all about you, fallen from the rocky ridge which looms over the landscape to the north. East and west the valley cuts across the land, with a small river tracing its way along the valley floor.
16071:
A tree-snake lies wrapped around one of the tree branches.
A tree-snake lies wrapped around one of the tree branches.

More grey than green, a tortuous tangle of twisted trees rises out of the dank haze. Moss blankets almost everything here and only a few stubborn, stunted shrubs and scattered patches of tough, yellow grass have taken hold amongst the moss and rocks. Some strange animal cries can be heard from somewhere deep amid the vegetation, but it is not possible to identify the source.
16073:
A tree-snake lies wrapped around one of the tree branches.
A tree-snake lies wrapped around one of the tree branches.
A tree-snake lies wrapped around one of the tree branches.

A knotty tangle of tall, twisted trees grows up out of the seemingly perpetual grey haze which blankets the area. A damp, musty smell permeates the air and the undergrowth of this strangely warped woodland consists of nothing but a few sickly clumps of weeds. To the east and north the trees thin out, giving way to a ribbon of rough brushwood, but south and west the vegetation becomes thicker.
16075: A small river travels the length of this valley. To the east the glen opens out, but here it is funnelled between two ranges of hills. As the waters descend toward the plains below they rush through the narrow gully, splashing over the rocks and stones which lie in the channel, kicking up a fine mist which hangs all around you.
16076: Eastward the valley widens but here it is quite narrow and tall hills loom above it, both north and south. With their rocky flanks standing tall above the valley floor the thin mist which rises from the rushing river below has no way to escape and the cool water hangs in the air all about you.
16077: At the Mouth of a Narrowing Gorge

Two narrow ridges of hills rise to the west, looming high above the floor of the valley. Its sides rise steeply here, especially on this side of the river, where they climb toward a lofty cliff. The ground is rocky and, despite being fed by the rich waters of the stream below, support only a thin covering of grass.
16078: The land slopes steeply from the river up toward the cliffs to the south. Thin clumps of tough grass compete with rocks and loose scree for dominion on this side of the waterway. No larger plants seem able to gain a foothold despite the nutrient-rich waters which flow by just below.
16079: East to west the valley gently descends, carrying a small river towards a narrowing gorge. To the far side of the waterway the landscape opens out into a vast expanse of rolling plains, but here the ground climbs steeply, rising toward massive cliffs. The footing is rocky, with little vegetation aside from a thin covering of tough grass and weeds.
16080: Along the Floor of the Valley
A sparrow is flapping around on the ground.

Further west, where the valley walls rise at a more gentle gradient, travel south would necessitate a strenuous uphill walk. Here the walls are steeper, so that progress to the south would require at least some skill in climbing. The ground underfoot is quite rocky, but is also level enough to retain a decent covering of topsoil. Thus, nestled below the small cliff face, this ribbon of land supports a rich variety of plant life, springing up between rocks and stones, everywhere you look.
16081: On a Narrow Ribbon of Land
Clusters of slender stems and tall leaves thrive in the mud and shallows.

Extending westward from the base of a small waterfall, a narrow ribbon of land stretches along this side of the river. A thin veil of mist hangs in the air, feeding the moss which blankets the cliff face to the south. Though the soil is rich, fed by the stream-water, it is also rather marshy, and under the shade of two looming cliffs the plant life here is rather poorer than might have been expected.
16085: East and north the hillside falls off in a sheer, unclimbable cliff. To the south the hills rear high above this smaller summit, ascending sharply into the Misty Mountains. Westward lies the only route off this small summit, where it is possible to scramble down a steady slope, seeking a path among the massive rocks and boulders that are scattered across the ground.
16149:
A small and well-kept fire lights and warms the room.
A saddle lies here on the ground (glows blue).
A large sack is on the ground.
A water barrel has been left here.
An elven scout stands here, blending in with the background.
An elven scout stands here, blending in with the background.
A sturdy trained horse is standing here.

Well hidden, this small earth chamber is the hideout of a few of Elrond's elven hunters. The small room is aligned along the western hillside as to let the inhabitants have a clear view west, towards the tower. The room is very dark and only the flames of a small campfire keep the shadows at a distance. A few rays of light sparkle along the eastern wall, barely managing to pass in via the minimal watching aperture on the western wall.
16154:
A cloak mottled in green and brown, and stinking to high heaven lies here.
A scimitar has been left here.
A soft leather helmet lies here.
A pair of rigid leather boots are on the ground.
You see six disgusting elf-stews on the ground.
There are three chain mail hauberks here.
You see three pairs of chain mail sleeves on the ground.
A half-decayed corpse of a goblin lies rotting on the ground.
A large metal shield is on the ground.
A large sack is on the ground.
A small and tough weed grows here.
A skeleton of some humanoid lies in the dust.
A pool of darkish water has formed in a depression of the stone.

The canyon floor forms a natural depression here as it slopes upwards both northwards and westwards. Rocks and boulders lie strewn all over the rocky and uneven ground, making passage here both tiresome and dangerous. Rain water has collected here in the natural basin. Surrounding the small icy pool of water, small patches of green grow, trying to conquer the harsh, rocky surroundings.
16155:
A scimitar has been left here.
A crude key made out of metal is discarded here.
The remainders of a disgusting elf-stew cover the ground.
The remainders of a disgusting elf-stew cover the ground.
A large sack is on the ground.
A leather helmet lies here.
A large sack is on the ground.
The remainders of a disgusting elf-stew cover the ground.
A plain leather belt is lying here.
The remainders of a disgusting elf-stew cover the ground.
There is a water skin lying on the ground.
A chain mail hauberk is on the ground.
A pair of hard leather pants are lying here.

Steep walls lead up from the canyon floor, ending in a hazy blur far far above. The floor is littered with boulders and debris from minor rockslides and slopes gently southwards where the canyon continues. The walls are covered with cracks and crevices from which can be heard the soft sounds of scales moving on rock.
16156:
The corpse of Mrak the orkish shaman is lying here.
A bent old shaman stands here, chanting and cursing.

A small and cold chamber in the wall of the canyon, this rough cave is a work of haste and need. The walls are rough, the floor is covered by stones and dust and there is nothing in the room except a roughly made bed.
16157:
The corpse of an orc-guard is lying here.
The corpse of an orc-guard is lying here.
A strong, tall orc-guard is looking for enemies here.
A strong, tall orc-guard is looking for enemies here.

This small cavern is cut out of the rock of the canyon wall. The walls are roughly cut, obviously in haste. The room is void of decorations and furniture. In the eastern wall there is a small opening, leading into a seemingly small chamber.
16158: Some small rocks have been piled into a mound here.

Like a scar in the rock, the canyon cuts deep into the mountain base here. The floor is covered with an abundance of rocks in all sizes and shapes. Rising high above you, the steep walls of the canyon contain numerous crevices and dark and foreboding cracks. High above, the sky can be seen, almost vanishing as the rocky walls seem to close in on you.
16159: A big, nasty vulture is sitting here, protecting its nest.

This lone mound of granite is an extension of the high plains and hilly ranges to the east and south of here, although it actually stands rather higher than any of the nearby ground. This lofty eminence affords a good view of the immediate area. A long valley stretches off to the east. South your view is blocked by a high cliff, a part of the rapidly rising foothills and westernmost ranges of the Misty Mountains. To the north a vast, rolling plain dominates the scenery.
16160: Just north of here a small river cleaves a narrow channel through the rock. South a massive cliff rears above you, just a small part of the rising foothills of the mighty Misty Mountains. Under its sheltering shadow this small plateau is afforded a measure of protection from the prevailing winds. This, together with the ample supply of fresh water, has allowed a surprising variety and quantity of vegetation to flourish here, from small shrubs and dense weeds to a single small fir tree which stands not far from the water's edge, with its lowest branches trailing close to the ground.
16161: A fine mist rises from the south, climbing up past the top of the cliff towards you. A gentle roar of water greets your ears. Though the ground here is quite rocky, it bears a surprisingly rich amount of vegetation, perhaps due to the sheltering influence of the cliffs which rear above you to the south. East of here the greenery grows even thicker.
16162: A narrow plateau stands above the valley floor, sheltered to the south by steep cliffs. Westward the land slopes gently downward but to the north the drop-off is so sheer as to prevent travel in that direction. The vegetation here is surprisingly rich, but seems oddly flattened in places, as if it had regularly been trodden down by heavy feet.
16163: To the south the foothills of the Misty Mountains rise sharply above you, too sheer to scale. East and west the land slopes gently, following the countours of the valley floor below. Progress north would entail scrambling and climbing down a steep slope covered in scree. The land here is rocky and the topsoil thin, but under the shelter of the cliffs a number of small shrubs and weeds manage to thrive even so.
16164: The ground falls off steadily to the north and west and its slope makes for only the thinnest of topsoil here, yet a number of small bushes and coarse weeds have managed to grow and even thrive, perhaps because a sheer cliff to the south affords the area a good degree of protection from prevailing winds.
16165:
An albino fish is swimming here, looking for some food.
An albino fish is swimming here, looking for some food.
An albino fish is swimming here, looking for some food.

Though the lake is pitch black, because it is shallow the small stones and sand which cover the bottom can be seen. Along the bottom of the lake there are also a few larger rocks and even a small boulder or two scattered among the small stones. The walls are lined with a thin layer of algae and a few small, aquatic plants grow in the dark, rich sand. To the south the bottom of the lake slopes upwards, forming a shoreline at the back of the cave.
16166: This cave was most likely formed by water draining through the small cracks in the roof and flowing downwards. To the north, where the floor stands lower, it has formed a pool which fills that part of the cave entirely. Though it is possible to move in that direction it would be necessary to swim in order to reach the mouth of the cave.
16167: A narrow, turning tunnel links two larger caves. Its walls are rough and come quite close together in places but the ceiling remains high, opening up even more both west and north of here. The steady sound of dripping water can be heard echoing about you, and the air feels quite chilly.
16168:
An ancient she-troll awaits her next meal.
A large earth troll is digging here, looking for some tasty morsels.

The chamber is littered with bones of small animals. While it is a mystery as to how these creatures found their way into the cave it appears that they did not meet their doom naturally, for almost all are broken into many pieces. Though the chamber is fairly cramped movement is possible in three distinct directions.
16169: A skeleton of some humanoid lies in the dust.

The rough floor of this cave slopes downward to the east and the roof also rises in that direction. Thus, as you near the western extremity of the chamber, the roof and floor draw ever closer together until they almost meet. It is here that a large, deep crack can be seen in the rocky roof.
16171: Standing at some height above the plains to the north the valley wall climbs steadily eastwards. Sheer cliffs loom to the south, blocking all travel, but the protection they offer from high winds has meant that a few thin bushes and coarse weeds have managed to take hold even in the thin soil of this sloping ground.
16172: Sheer cliffs rise above you to the west and to the south. To the east the land slopes gently upwards, climbing toward the far distant Misty Mountains. North lies a rocky slope which leads down toward the floor of a narrow valley, where a bright little river cuts its way across the countryside.
16173: A big cavebear is padding around here.

Though relatively large in area the cavern has a low roof, which is fortunate for the only apparent exit from this place is through the rough, round opening above your head. The walls and floor are uneven and a number of bones lie scattered all around. The most notable feature of this chamber, however, is the smell of damp fur, mingled with that of rotting meat.
16174:
A powerful young troll stares at you.
A grey-skinned mountain troll stands here.
A powerful young troll stares at you.
A grey-skinned mountain troll stands here.
A grey-skinned mountain troll stands here.
A powerful young troll stares at you.
A powerful young troll stares at you.
A grey-skinned mountain troll stands here.
A mottled snake is sneaking here, ready to sink its fangs into flesh.
A finch flies low above the ground.

Though this cave appears to be a natural one with rough, untooled walls and a number of small stalactites hanging from the roof it is apparent that now it is occupied by someone or something. Animal bones lie scattered on the floor and the southern wall bears what can only be described as a door, crafted from a single massive block of stone. A similar attempt to block the wide mouth of the cave to the east was less successful, and three massive, shattered, rocky slabs lie at the entrance.
16176: An old, strong cave troll is standing here.

Here must be where the trolls come to rest during the hours of daylight. Furs and skins of various creatures, big and small, are scattered in rough piles all around. None have been tanned and all are in varying states of decay, a partial explanation for the odour of decay which fills the air.
16177:
A skeleton of some humanoid lies in the dust.
A large stone chest is here.
A moaning ghost advances towards you, shimmering with a pale light.

Cold stone walls close in around you on all sides and the only apparent exit from this chamber is through a square opening in the northern wall. Should this somehow become blocked the only escape would be death. Apparently this is a storage chamber for those treasures which the trolls steal from their hapless victims. Much that is here seems to be worthless garbage, testimony to the intelligence of the trolls, and of those who would risk their lives attempting to purloin their hoard.
16178:
In the corpse (here):
a forest green cloak (used)

There is a water skin lying on the ground.
You see two half-rotten corpses on the ground.
A large sack is on the ground.
A large rabbit looks peacefully at you, ready to dart away.

The floor of this rough cave slopes downward to the east, deeper into the cold rock of the hills. The air is chilly and dry, but tainted by an odour of decay. A few bones lie scattered about the floor among the rotting remains of any number of perishable items that are now too decomposed to be identified. Wood, leather and cloth are all present among the garbage, but there is no indication that anything of value remains.
16243: Eastwards, the white lace of a series of waterfalls can be seen tumbling down into a rich dale. A deep, shadowy forest runs the length of the valley, skirting the eastern banks of an oval mere. To the west lies a shallow cave, whose rear is barely concealed in shadows.
16244: A light boat made of reeds has been left here.

Large, jagged boulders lay scattered on the cavern floor. The thick scent of mildew and fungus is overwhelming. Light trickling of water reveals an icy pool of water in the back of the cave. Eastwards, an arched entrance allows access onto a stone shelf.
16245: Narrow stone walls prohibit much lateral movement in this icy pool. Various pieces of jagged rock protrude on the sides of the chamber making it necessary for all movement to be deliberate and cautious. Upwards, a faint shimmering of light can be seen in contrast to the utter blackness in the pool.
16246: A shade is here, shrouded in an inky blackness.

The blackened stone walls and faint trickling of the underwater chamber to the east emphasises the isolation of this small cavern. Eastwards, it is possible to travel through a U-shaped tunnel into a deep pool, but it is a narrow passage and requires time to maneuver. A big boned, decaying skeleton lies on the floor in disarray.
16247: The fine, gravelly scree provides no traction whatsoever. Almost immediately, the rocks give way, allowing no safe footing. Southwards the slope is less severe and the grade of rock is larger. Additonally, it is possible to travel upwards by means of a stone ladder onto a broad shelf.
16248: A colourful butterfly is fluttering around here.

An unsteady pile of moraine rests here threatening any who might try to scale its side. Deep grooves in the scree slope to the west demonstrate the path that these rocks must have taken. To the east can be seen a talus slope, descending fast into the dale.
16249: A long and wide slope of talus connects this ridge to the dale below. The terrain here is rocky with an occasional hint of the black soil that is particular to the lowlands of this area. To the northeast a large slab of rock extends from the ridge creating a stone shelf above you, but due west of you the land falls off dangerously toward a severe rockfall.
16250: Directly across the dale the steep slopes of Celebdil rear up above you, their craggy faces hemming in the valley below. From here, a precarious talus slope stretches eastward, leading toward the distant mere. The ridge continues its ascent to the north, but diminishes as it runs south and west.
16251: A large marmot is here, scurrying in between the rocks.

Broken dolomite and scree compose the ground of this narrow ridge. Small spindly heather attempts to grow in the shattered rock but its brown hues betray its failure. Far to the southwest can be seen a dark, oval mere, which lies amidst a rich dale, stretching from southeast to northwest.
