The narrow, rocky ridge above looks more stable but no less treacherous than this spot, situated about two rods above a deep cleft surrounding a narrow trail. The slope continues in all directions.
16486: This is the northern tip of the vast mountain face that spreads out like a huge blanket covering the southern side of the mountain. To the north the face slopes up into a very steep and narrow ridgeline.
16487: A steep rockface extends from the mountain peak towards the stream which runs on slightly lower ground. The ground is dead and barren, life is unapparent on this mountain. Rocks of all sizes and colours are strewn all over the face of the mountain. To the north high above you a prominent peak enshrouded in clouds is distinguishable. To the south you can see a mountain pass far below.
16488: A small stream trickles out of a crack in the rockface. It is not very deep and is easily fordable. The water is frigid to your touch, which is not a very pleasant sensation. The stream flows downward from the west to the east, following the Redhorn Pass. There are many bends and curves as the stream is obviously a new one and has not settled into the mountain yet.
16489: A thin rivulet of water flows smoothly alongside the Redhorn Pass. The small current picks up and carries along the sand from the riverbed. Dark brown pebbles line the floor, looking much like a thin layer of dirt. Damp dark moss surrounds the rocks which are situated alongside the stream.
16490: A cold glacial stream flows eastward here through a deep, steep-walled valley. The stream's rocky bed is full of stones of all sizes and colors which have fallen from the rocky mountain faces and were washed down here in the spring melt. There are a few evergreen bushes clinging to the valley's walls but little other vegetation.
16491: This is a part of the long mountain ridge which travels adjacent to a small stream in the south. The ridge stretches east and west, rising toward a higher ridge in the west and getting lower to the east, where it crosses a bleak grassland.
16492: This mountain ridge stands on the side of a small waterway and seems like a barrier protecting, guarding whatever secrets the stream holds. You can follow the ridge eastwards or go down the slope to the stream.
16493: The trail takes advantage of a rocky valley notched into the side of the mountain as it descends to the east. A small stream fed by glacial run-off also utilises the valley, running parallel to the trail a short distance to the north.
16494: A lone hawk soars high above you.

Large dolomite formations protrude from the ridge, making the area appear jagged. Westwards one of Celebdil's mighty rock formations rears above you, and to the east the ridge continues around the side of the bluff. Southwards a long scree slope connects the ridge with the valley floor below.
16495: Shattered rock and lichen-covered stones litter the floor of this rugged ridge. To the north and west the ridge curves about the flank of Celebdil, reaching then for the south. Broad talus slopes make a precarious descent to the floor of the Dimrill Dale below you.
16496: This rocky slope forms the southern side of a jagged ridge that bends from the north to the west, descending into the hills lying far southwards. A lush woodland stretches out to the east, terminating on the banks of a dark, oval mere.
16497: Wide slabs of talus lie here, rocking unsteadily, apparently the product of a recent slide. Small flat fragments of stone slip and clatter downhill under your feet. To the west the ground slopes up, and the slope reaches the base of Celebdil; to the east you can see a lush, grassy field.
16498: Giant slabs of weatherworn rocks lay unsteadily here. Rotten tree trunks and dead pine needles under the lichen covered stones reveal that this was once a grove of pines trees. A deep gully running down the eastern flank of Celebdil demonstrates the path the rocks had taken. Directly above, a ornate dome structure emerges from the rock face.
16499: The ridge here is descending rapidly toward the Dimrill Dale, and far in the distance, cradled by the rising mountains to either side of it is a dark, oval mere, whose reflective waters offer a panorama of the mountains of Moria. East and west, the ridge stretches before you, but to the south you might clamber down the rocky slopes toward the valley floor.
16500: A traveller heading east now would begin his descent in earnest, while the westward bound traveller just now begins the true ascent leading to the snowfields on the high shoulder of Caradhras. The trail runs along a small stream flowing just to the north, sharing its narrow valley before taking to the steep slopes.
16501: The trail descends sharply to the east, following the floor of a shallow and rocky valley. To the north, a shallow glacial stream dances among the rocks. To the east, the valley seems to end, though perhaps it simply turns abruptly.
16502: A panoramic view of the valley floor opens out before you, as the mountain ridge tapers off at an angle in the Redhorn Pass. To the southeast you can see the clear waters of the Mirrormere, which reflect the peaks of Fanuidhol and Celebdil. Westward this gutted ridge of small pebbles and dirt continues.
16503: This is a broad basin full of deep, packed snow. To the south rises a winding mountain ridge, and to the east great rocky tiers rise to an impressive peak. Travelling on the snow is difficult, but there are no obvious signs of fissures or crevices.
16504: A huge stone giant is here, glaring at you.

You are standing in the middle of an ancient rockslide, one which has obviously hit the mountain with a terrible toll. It appears that the entire mountainside has been completely destroyed and devastated. The only exit lies to the south.
16505: A big cavebear is padding around here.

This is a completely blocked off and devastated area, many rockslides and harsh weather over the years have ruined the ledge. All exits are blocked off except the one from which you entered. This part of the mountain has many sharp and jagged edges, from where chunks of rock have been displaced. Above you the weathered outcroppings look like the teeth of some evil creature just lurking in the shadows waiting to devour you.
16506: The ledge continues here leading upwards, off to its side a great fall to an unpleasant death beckons you. It may be wise to walk on the inner cutting of the ledge. You are able to follow either upwards to a damaged area or you can head to the south where the ledge began. One thing is for sure: you had better not linger at this point contemplating the direction in which to continue your journey.
16507: A renegade uruk is here, dirty and ragged.

A damp and murky tunnel has been dug under the mountain. The walls and floor are covered with mould and slime due to the dampness in the air. The ceiling is very low and there is not much room for movement. The air is stuffy and unclean. The tunnel continues to the south.
16508: A damp and murky tunnel has been dug under the mountain. The walls and floor are covered with mould and slime due to the dampness in the air. The ceiling is very low and there is not much room for movement. The air is stuffy and unclean. The tunnel continues to the south.
16509: Here the tunnel makes an abrupt bend. Gnawing sounds come from the darkness and echo from the walls. No daylight penetrates into this tunnel system, and all connections with the upper world seem severed. The tunnel continues to the west and to the north.
16510: The wide tunnel ends here, and all that remains of it is a small and narrow crawlway that leads north into the darkness. The floor under your feet is slippery, and the walls drip with moisture. A stench of decaying flesh and rotting cadavers attacks your nose.
16511:
An old, strong cave troll is standing here.
A bulky cave troll is here, fighting Calarion.
Calarion the Elf, wielding a broadsword, is here, fighting a bulky cave troll.
A large warhorse is standing here, clad in mail.

This is a gargantuan cavern, the surrounding walls are so far apart that from one side the other side seems non-existent. Skulls and bones from all kinds of creatures are strewn on the floor, traces of dried and matted blood are also evident on the ground. Rotted wooden and rusted metal equipment are heaped in small piles all over the place. The entire cavern carries the stink of death.
16512: At the Top of a Sloping Tunnel

The shaft is almost vertical here. Were it not for what appears to be a stair- case, it would be impossible to climb this passage, and even now the task will not be easy, as the rock is worn quite smooth and is coated by damp moss and algae. Twisting and turning, the tunnel descends into the stony depths of the mountain beneath you. Not far above you the passageway ends at a wide hole, which appears to exit only to the skies themselves.
16513: Soaring high into the sky, as if attempting to reach for the clouds, this lofty eminence stands proudly above the surrounding countryside. Whilst it is far from being the highest of the Misty Mountains, much shorter in stature than the Redhorn, Silvertine or Cloudyhead, it is nevertheless the quite the highest peak for many leagues.
16514: Climbing down from the mountain's lofty peak, this ridgeline must once have offered a route to the foothills below. Now, however, that avenue is closed, for the ridgeline which once travelled south from here has been shattered, leaving behind it a mighty crater. The walls of this deep hollow are highly unstable, and even as you view the area, another landslide sends rocks and stones cascading into the depths, testifying to the danger of this region.
16515: In a Cave behind the Waterfall

A small campfire burns here, its low flames giving off only a little light.
A mother eagle is sleeping here.
A sturdy trained horse is standing here.
A mother eagle is sleeping here.
A lion is sleeping here.
Aramarth the Elf (AA), wielding a sharp thorn, is resting here.

This tiny cave is little more than a small rocky niche, and its walls and ceiling are cracked all over. Tiny rivulets of ice-cold water trickle through many of the deeper fissures, gathering in a small pool on the floor, which overflows at one end, to run out of the cavern through a larger crack.
16516:
Alexia the Half-Elf, wielding a double edged eket, is standing here.
A mother eagle is sleeping here.

From this vantage it is clear that this is no mere mountain. There is no doubt that these caverns and corridors were formed by a great eruption of molten lava. The hot liquid burned through the mountainous rock on its journey to escape through the crack in the mountain's summit. In some places, such as this one, the lava's path was halted and the pressure formed a cavernous hole.
16517:
The corpse of a vicious rat is lying here.
A large bat is here, hanging in the darkness (hidden).

This place resembles a great staircase as it is home to a cascade of uneven steps. Some are only a few feet wide, others much larger. What began as a fast flowing stream of lava, here slowed and formed these steps with each hesitation. The surface of each step is rough and charred, with small holes where the hot liquid seeped farther into the ground.
16518: Even holding a torch, a non-nocturnal creature, venturing into the dark cave, could not see more than a few feet in front of themselves. The walls, burned black by the violent fires of this volcano, reflect firelight no more. They have the texture of rock scalded smooth. The ground is covered with a layer of ash.
16519: The corpse of a vicious rat is lying here.

This place is even more lacking in light than the cavern above. The walls, floor and ceiling are a deep black ash colour. It is difficult to discern for certain but one can estimate being about half a mile down from the crack in the summit. Just as in the chamber above, no plant life can be found.
16520: A sturdy rope is hanging from above.

The air is a bit stale in the vast cavernous hole. The walls are as black as night. This inner sanctum appears to stretch for miles across and the entrance crack above is too high to let in any illumination. The ground is covered in a black charred material that crumbles easily. Under that layer is a black substance hard as rock. Nothing grows here, not even moss or mildew.
16521: Pools of lava unable to burst free formed these large black chambers. Where the floor meets the walls, the ground curls upward unlike structures made by mortals that have sharp corners. The cavern resembles the inside of a bubble of blown glass, fittingly so since both are created by intense heat.
16522: The corpse of a vicious rat is lying here.

The walls of this cavern are as smooth as glass. Molten lava from the volcanic eruption pooled here and waited for a fissure to open allowing it to continue its upward journey. The intense heat cauterized and blackened the walls of this chamber. There seem to be some cracks in the floor toward the west.
16523:
An ashen aberration almost blends into the cavern walls.
Alexia the Half-Elf, wielding a double edged eket, is standing here trying to concentrate.
A mother eagle flies high above looking for prey.

Pulverized bone covers the floor of this chamber like chalk dust. Only a few stray bones stacked up against an inner wall are left intact. Amongst the dust lie the remnants of what must have been the armour of the owners of these bones. Small shredded pieces of metal and wood beg the question if anything belonging to those vanquished here could be left in its' entirety hidden among the remains. On one wall, there is a strange indentation that merits closer investigation. Another wall seems to bulge outward in a similar shape.
16524:
An ashen aberration is here, fighting Alexia.
Alexia the Half-Elf, wielding a double edged eket, is here, fighting an ashen aberration.
A mother eagle is here, fighting an ashen aberration.

The gashes in the passage walls look to have been made by claws and the sharp slashing of evil weapons. The depth of the cuts gives evidence that whatever made such marks did so quickly with strong and eager sense of purpose. It is also evident, by the haphazard nature of the construction, they were carved with little regard for giving the tunnels any structural integrity.
16525: The crumbling bits of this passage's ceiling show those building it gave no consideration to the weight of the mountain above. It appears that it was not long after dirt and rock that once filled this place was removed, that the strain on the ceiling became too much. The blockage of the passage northward appears to have occurred about the same time as construction judging by the amount of ash covering the rock. Air escapes through the cracks. Peering into those same cracks one can see the passage once continued farther northward.
16526: This rocky precipice gives travellers a unique vantage point from which to witness the etched trail below to the north and gaze over the fertile plains down toward the east. Looking straight down in either directions rocks fallen from this point can be seen littering the ground.
16527: The ground to the western edge of this plateau seems to be crumbling away with the wear of the wind. Below the weathered edge rocks fall and litter the narrow trail below. It seems possible to traverse the cliff and reach the trail below. Returning to this point the same way, however, would be impossible.
16528:
A wild sheep with a short, greyish coat grazes here.
A wild sheep with a short, greyish coat grazes here.
A wild sheep with a short, greyish coat grazes here.
A powerful ram stands here, poised and alert.
A powerful ram stands here, poised and alert.

Aglow in the sunlight or moonlight, these tall grasses carry a deep orange pigment. Their sturdy stalks grow strong, thriving in these rolling lands. Oftentimes they grow so thick it cannot be seen where the hills slope down and then rise up again. Animals can easily conceal their form in this thick, grassy cover.
16529: The smell of clover fills the air. The thick carpet of these leafy plants stretches for at least a mile. The leisurely traveller might be tempted to rest and look for one clover with four leaves. The plant's horizontal growth patterns cause it to spread far in every direction rather than skyward like the fields of flaxen wheat grasses to the east.
16530: A colourful butterfly is fluttering around here.

Greener than surrounding meadowlands, this area is a haven for birds that nibble and pick at the soil in search of a worm or grub. Some young trees are just strong enough to support the feathered creatures' weight should they desire a high perch on which to plan their search. On the higher branches is the start of a nest that one such bird is building in hope that the fertile land will provide plenty of food for a coming family.
16531: Blades of intertwined green and gold grasses grow so closely together they hide the dark soil beneath them. Small hills separated by only a few feet between each other create the look of flaxen waves rolling toward a far off shore. Gusts of wind have spread these grasses' seed far to the north and west.
16532:
The bee flies around here, collecting nectar from the flowers.
The bee flies around here, collecting nectar from the flowers.

Grasses the colour of sunshine stretch out in every direction. A few scattered trees grow here, their thick dark trunks providing some shade when the sun shines from the east. From one tree hangs a small beehive which sends the lingering scent of honey drifting on the wind.
16533: A colourful butterfly is fluttering around here.

Honey coloured grasses mixing with verdant shrubs create a patchwork of green and gold. In the spring, the shrubs are covered in ruby coloured berries that are quickly devoured by small herbivores. In the fall what was vibrant plant life dries up becoming thick clumps of hay, enough to make many bales should a farmer need.
16534: Light coloured wheat grasses grow beside the carved trail to the west. However, those blades of grass closest to the trail have been so often trampled upon by careless travellers they have lost some of their hardiness. To the east the grasses grow thicker, stronger and in some places even waist-high.
16535: The trampled grasses are apparently the result of travellers straying off the trail to the northwest. The natural design of this golden meadow has been marred with hoof marks, abandoned campsites and the remains of butchered game. Long blades of what would be tall grasses, have been bent in half and hang sadly beyond repair.
16536: A few travellers, straying from the trail to the north, have damaged the golden grasses that cover this land. The tall stalks have been bent as they were pushed aside or trampled to make passage easier. The few rocks that at one time dotted this area are often found gathered together where someone has made camp.
16537:
A large, loyal falcon is circling above.
A large, loyal falcon is circling above.

Wheat grasses the colour of cornsilk rise into the air knee-high. The scampering of a small animal creates a domino effect of bending stalks that make this meadow glisten in the afternoon sun. At night cool winds blow the winsome blades back and forth, each blade rebounding back into place.
16538:
A colourful butterfly is fluttering around here.
A large wild horse is here, protecting his herd.
A young colt is frolicking playfully.
A young colt is frolicking playfully.
A young colt is frolicking playfully.
A wild mare is watching you warily.
A wild mare is watching you warily.

The soil here must be rich in nutrients as there are very few spots of ground where the wild grasses do not grow. The dirt is a deep brown and would prove resistant to winds that might carry away more arid soil. The prints of some animals are visible in the dirt but then are obscured where the grasses grow. To the north and west, the meadowland ends abruptly along the edges of a trail.
16539: The dark bark of this group of old trees is covered in moss. Its moist, green colour reflects both the sun's and the moon's light making the trees look like carved jade statues. The trees' leaves, almost the same colour as the moss, add to the statuesque illusion. The wet feel of the moss however shatters the image and reveals this forest to be very much alive.
16540: Amber stalks of wild wheat grasses fill these hills giving off a sweet wholesome smell. The tall blades of grass grow skyward two to three feet above the soil. Unlike the wheat planted by careful farmers, no harvester has cut down or controlled these grains since they took seed. The only danger to their continued growth comes in the form of strong gusts of wind.
16541: A powerful ram stands here, poised and alert.

A spot of exposed dirt provides a sharp contrast to the rest of these rolling hills. On this one low hill, the topsoil has been blown away and all that remains is a reddish dirt, so thick it could be mistaken for clay. A middle-aged tree grows here on an angle. Its roots have been exposed to the elements as they protrude from the ground. All around, the hills are covered in grains the colour of the sun on a blistering hot day.
16542: A soft amber glow emanates from the winsome grains that grow here. These sun kissed hills rise and fall like tides. The small hills and shallow gullies covered with tall wild grasses provide excellent cover for small animals as they scurry to collect seeds or hunt animals even smaller than themselves.
16543:
A brown furry gopher is here, ready to dive back underground.
A brown furry gopher is here, ready to dive back underground.

This uneven land rises and falls every few feet yet the tips of the tall golden grasses remain even. Occasionally a gust of strong wind blows the grasses flat and the inconsistencies of the terrain are more visible. In places the shifting height of the dirt exposes the roots of the few trees that have grown to maturity. Holes, a few inches wide, have been dug into the ground.
16544:
A large wild horse is here, protecting his herd.
A young colt is frolicking playfully.
A young colt is frolicking playfully.
A young colt is frolicking playfully.
A wild mare is watching you warily.
A wild mare is watching you warily.

The golden grasses grow thick in this area, cushioning the footsteps of travellers to this land. Tiny insects, almost too small to see, feed on the grains. A few scattered trees dot the landscape but they provide meagre to no shade during the day. To the east the land continues on flat and fairly featureless.
16545: A large, loyal falcon is circling above.

The sunlight, that reflects off this land during the daylight hours, has nurtured these golden grasses. They thrive and form a thick carpet over the soil. The lay of the land is flat and there are few trees to block the sun's rays. When the wind blows the blades of wheat grasses shimmer like gold. The soil is arid yet rich with minerals.
16547: A rabbit is here eyeing your presence warily.

The trees here are tall and thick, the lower parts of their trunks covered with moss and fungi. Smells of moisture and rot are in the air. Among the animal tracks on the ground one can see more regular tracks which look as if they had been left by humanoid creatures.
16548: The tall trees of this forest loom high over the shorter ones which look as if they gave up trying to grow high enough to reach the sunlight. Smells of moss and fungi linger in the damp air. Small insects feed upon the moss. Some animal tracks can be seen on the ground.
16549: The trees here stand somewhat apart and the sky is visible in the gaps between their branches. Many shrubs and bushes grow on the ground beneath the trees. Grass and a few bright forest flowers adorn the area and to the north the trees grow taller as the forest becomes more dense.
16550:
A brown fox is here, looking for some rabbits to chew up.
A large elk is standing here, chewing grass and leaves.
A rabbit is here eyeing your presence warily.

Green grass grows plentifully on the hillsides along with many varieties of flowers. Many bushes, some that produce fruit and some that don't, grow all around together with an occasional stunted tree. A little to the north one can see the beginnings of a forest. A path of trampled grass crosses the terrain from the north to the south; it seems that many feet have walked this way.
16551:
A low, many-branched shrub covers the ground here.
A large thorny branched shrub is growing here.
On the shrub, there are two piles of blackberries.
A large eagle soars above you.

In all directions the rolling hills continue. Covering the ground is a mixture of different grasses, some of them brown, others green and gold. Large bushes with black fruit on them grow together in thick knots. Some of these bushes also have sharp thorns on them that could easily penetrate the bare skin of a careless traveller. A path of trampled grass runs north-south across the terrain; the path is little more than a few tracks running side by side.
16552: The light golden grass that covers the slopes of the hills is gently caressed by the wind that carries itself through the landscape. Trees, bushes and occasional flowers enliven the even hillsides and the hilltops. All the trees have one distinct feature: they are stunted, as if for some reason they were unable to reach their full height. Jutting out of a grassy hillside, a large boulder attracts the eye; the few tracks that lead through the terrain seem to converge at the boulder.
16553: A bear is here, covered with coarse black fur.

The landscape here is ever-changing, as with every gust of wind the movement of the waves of grass makes small hills and deep ravines appear seemingly out of nowhere. Huge clumps of dry grass are carried across the plains by the wind. A few small, wiry-looking bushes that grow here and there appear to be the only static part of the picture.
16554: This area is slightly different from the plains all around. More trees grow here, and they are somewhat larger than those in the surrounding plains, and some of them even bear fruit. Occasional clumps of bushes also dot the even landscape.
16555: A rabbit is here eyeing your presence warily.

These plains continue to the east and north. The gentle weave of the grass in the wind ripples like waves in the sea. Gently rolling hills carry onwards over the entire plain. Many varieties of bushes, flowers and trees can be seen everywhere.
16565: The river flows swiftly south, gaining speed as it reaches a hilly section of the forest. The banks are too steep to allow climbing up the shore and there is no choice but to swim along. As the waters rush onward, the river appears to bend east, gently turning at the outskirts of a golden forest.
16566: At the Bank of the River Celebrant

Several blooms of snow-white and palest green cover the ground.
A sturdy pack horse is standing here.
A stocky mountain mule is here, waiting to serve.

From the edge of this peaceful forest one can look and marvel at the harmonic view of the River Celebrant. A steep bank runs down toward the river. The clear glittering waters coming from the northwest make a turn and rush due east, passing a natural arch formed by two trees on either shore.
16567: On a small hill to the south stands a majestic tree arching over the swift river, where it meets the crown of another tree growing on the opposite shore of the Celebrant. The two trees form a natural bridge over the water; however, crossing the strong branches doesn't seem that easy, as opposed to descending into the peaceful forest to the east.
16568: The forest around is quite sparse. To the southwest a majestic tree has bent across the river and entwined with another such natural pillar on the other shore. It might not be the best bridge over the rushing waters to the south, yet there appears to be no evil that would dare plant here trickery, throwing you into the swift Celebrant. It just might be that in the end it is the skill of the climber that will count.
16569: Delicate golden blooms adorn the ground like a cascade of stars.

The trees and grass of this area seem to have been woven from ancient lore, no longer being born in this world. The trunks of the mellyrn are coloured a gleaming silvery grey and their roots are covered with last spring's golden leaves. Together with the sparkling river to the south, the forest forms a picture of nearly perfect harmony. The waters of the river might seem tempting, but it would be folly to challenge destiny and plunge down from the high rising bank.
16570: Several blooms of snow-white and palest green cover the ground.

The mallorn-trees here are of varying shades of gold and silver, their bark rough to the eye yet smooth to the touch, their colour somewhat reserved yet glorious, their wisdom unseen, yet striking anyone with awe. Water flickers through the tangled branches to the south, while in all the other directions, the golden forest continues.
16571: Trees shift their branches and rustle their leaves, whispering stories as old as the great seas rumoured to lie many journeys west of here. What words of wisdom they exchange, what mysteries they unveil, one cannot tell. To the south the Celebrant flows unhindered eastwards. The river bank is very steep, and the tree roots climbing out of the bank do not seem to be strong enough to support the weight of anyone climbing down into the water.
16572: This opening in the forest might appear to be a good place to climb down into the refreshing waters to the south. The shore, however, has not fashioned itself according to the desires of a weary traveller. The tree-roots could be used to reach the Celebrant, yet one cannot be sure of safe return to this bank of the river. In all other directions the golden forest continues.
16573: Delicate golden blooms adorn the ground like a cascade of stars.

The golden forest is quite dense here, at the northern shore of the River Celebrant. Branches seem to make way for a good-spirited traveller east and west but block the way to the south. Perhaps it is nature itself protecting the unwary by making it impossible to step down from the steep bank of the Celebrant? The river can be heard flowing in the south, in all other directions the mallorn forest continues.
16576: The trees that line this section of the river bend inwards, forming a series of bridges across the running water. In some spots the trees completely block the daytime sunlight, laying deep shadows across the river. In other places the trees are less frequent and the sky can be seen above the Celebrant that flows slowly eastward.
16577: Flowing lazily between two lines of trees the river Celebrant slowly changes its direction from east to north. Some leaves and broken tree-branches can be seen floating on the surface of the water. Other branches that failed to navigate the sharp curve have been washed up onto the eastern riverbank and collected there, forming a rather large pile.
16578: A pack horse (ulo) is standing here, ridden by you.

The gentle slope of the land is broken by a sharp dip which becomes nearly vertical just before the land joins the river to the west and north. While little effort is required to fall into the river, obtaining a foothold on dry land from the water will be difficult. Some of the trees grow on the edge of the bank where the land drops into the river, while others, which once grew where the river now flows, have fallen and begun to rot.
16579: A woodpecker is here, tapping on a tree.

The forest, containing mostly beeches and mellyrn, is quite dense. Several varieties of low-lying vegetation have grown into what little open space once lay between the ancient trees. Despite the dense growth of bushes, a river can be seen to the west, flowing lazily between the trees. A huge rock lies on the ground among the tree roots. The rock is weathered and covered with grey lichen.
16580: A colony of red ants is here. The ants seem to ignore you.

A few elm trees can be seen growing here. Their number rapidly increases to the north where the forest obscures your vision. Even though you cannot see beyond the trees, the faint sounds of a distant river can be heard from that direction. A faint trail leads to the east, towards the borders of the shimmering Golden Wood. If you were to study the trail closely, it would seem to be fading even as you look at it. A wide but shallow mound of soft dirt forms the nest for a colony of ants against the side of one of the smaller trees.
16581:
A horse of the Rohirrim (ulo) is standing here.
A great warg (KOLM) is standing here (red aura).
A great warg (KAKS) is standing here (red aura).
A great warg (YKS) is standing here (red aura).

The silvery trees rise high into the skies, murmuring softly as the wind moves through their branches. The surrounding ground is uneven, sloping up and down. One of the mallorn-trees is much larger than the others and has a much thicker foliage. The foliage of this tree is more than capable of concealing the dwellings of Elves, who are known for building their homes in the trees in order to escape the dangers of the forest.
16582: Delicate golden blooms adorn the ground like a cascade of stars.

The dense forest continues in all directions, filled with a variety of bushes and trees. On this spot, however, many of the plants appear to have been smashed by an inhuman strength. It is possible the damage was done by a storm, though the pattern of destruction is unlike that of a common storm. Regardless of the cause of the destruction, many trees lie dead upon the grass like corpses after a battle. The ground, sloping up and down, remains covered by a soft green grass which escaped the destruction that did not spare the larger plants.
16583: This is the middle of an ancient forest full of very tall and thick trees. Judging by their height and girth, many of the trees appear older than the oldest living creatures on Arda. Their gentle whispering fills the forest and sounds much like a song. The soft grassy ground is filled with flowers, many with blooms that appear brighter than the stars during the dark nights.
16584: Delicate golden blooms adorn the ground like a cascade of stars.

Most of the trees in this area are covered with a greyish silvery bark. A few willows and orphaned oaks can also be seen here and there, looking small and lonely like children without parents. The endless rows of trees continue in all directions, inhibiting vision of the surrounding landscape, though farther to the east the forest does seem to thin out. A faint sound of running water can be heard north of here; the source of it is likely to be a small river.
16585:
A shrub with maple-like leaves is growing here.
On the shrub, there are three handfuls of blackcurrant berries.

The tall trees here almost obscure the sky, however glimpses can be seen beyond the massive branches. Small shrubs decorate the area, and many types of sweet-smelling berries can be found growing here in a variety of colours. Here and there footprints can be seen leading in various directions through the forest. To the north the mighty Celebrant can be seen.
16586: The tall trunks of mellyrn rise all around. Their leaves, blowing gently in the wind, glimmer slightly as they waft from side to side, dazzling the senses of any passers-by. A large tree has fallen here, blocking any passage to the east. The forest continues to the west, and to the south a clearing in the forest can be seen upon a small hill. The river Celebrant lies to the north.
16587:
Several blooms of snow-white and palest green cover the ground.
Delicate golden blooms adorn the ground like a cascade of stars.
A squirrel scampers around here, looking for nuts from the trees.
A cute rabbit is here.

A large mallorn has fallen down to the west here, blocking all passage in that direction. Except for the fallen tree which has lost its shine, the rest of the area glows with a slight golden tinge, illuminating the surroundings with wonder. The forest path runs east and south, where it continues on through the woodlands. The Celebrant can be heard flowing in the north.
16588: Large mellyrn grow all around the path, reaching for the sky with their slender branches. Bathing the forest in a pale golden light, they seem to span the woodlands as far as the eye can see. A sense of peace permeates the air. The forest path continues to the south and east, while to the west a large fallen tree can be seen. A wide river runs just north of here.
16589: Mellyrn surround the path, rising high above the tops of other, smaller trees. Numerous footprints in the soft ground indicate that the forest is inhabited by many different creatures. The ground by the bases of the trees is fertile and the growth wild, aiding these forest dwellers with nourishment. The path runs east-west.
16590: A small forest path begins here and heads west, deeper into the forest. Three small white stones mark its outset. It winds among the mellyrn, offering a breathtaking view of the surrounding forest. Off the path, a small, clean stream can be seen, winding its way southwest through the trees. The river Celebrant can be seen to the north. The forest stretches out in all directions.
16591:
An elf, clad in the garments of a woodsman, moves stealthily among the trees.
An elf, clad in the garments of a woodsman, moves stealthily among the trees.

A pale golden light shines from the leaves and branches of the trees, bathing the area with a radiant sense of tranquility. The atmosphere here is very calming, and even the animals and birds seem to be affected by it. All sounds of wildlife appear to be slightly muted, as if the woodland creatures did not wish to disturb the peace of the forest. The forest continues to the west, south and east. To the north you can see a large river.
16592: A large rabbit looks peacefully at you, ready to dart away.

A pale golden light emanates from the crowns of the great mellyrn. The other trees and the growth on the forest floor bathe in the soft warm radiance. Tracks of small woodland animals can be seen by the base of the trees. The forest continues in all directions save north, where the Celebrant can be heard flowing swiftly.
16593: Several blooms of snow-white and palest green cover the ground.

If any travellers ever passed through this forest, their passage does not seem to have disturbed its tranquil peace. The local wildlife and the trees seem to co-exist perfectly, neither one disturbing the presence of the other. The golden forest continues in all directions but north, the glow of the mellyrn fading slightly to the south.
16594: The forest continues in all directions. Its great trees stretch the branches towards the sky. The mellyrn appear to shine lightly here, but the soft glow fades and ultimately disappears to the south, where the forest thins out slightly. To the east and west, the forest continues unchanged. The Celebrant can be seen to the north.
16595: Delicate golden blooms adorn the ground like a cascade of stars.

The air in this light forest is fresh and pleasant. On this side of the Celebrant, the silvery mellyrn grow shorter and more sparsely than farther into the forest. Here and there you catch a glimpse of gold behind the silver-grey tree trunks. Low, soft grass and undergrowth flourishes on the ground.
16596: The forest opens up to a small, secluded clearing where trees give way to low bushes. Daylight reaches the level ground here, lighting the clearing in daytime and playing on the silvery and golden trees of the mallorn forest. A winding path starts from here and runs eastwards, picking its way through the spacious woods. The sound of rushing water can be heard from the north, where the swift Celebrant lies.
16597: Delicate golden blooms adorn the ground like a cascade of stars.

Among the silver-grey trunks of the ancient trees a winding path runs through this forest. The mellyrn are covered in a lush foliage which flickers in golden shades as an occasional gust of wind rustles the leaves. The path leads eastwards following the edge of the wood.
16598: Several blooms of snow-white and palest green cover the ground.

This path runs east and west, circling onward around the old, silver-grey trees. Here it follows tightly the channel of the rapid Celebrant which runs north from here. The path seems somewhat used; debris and dry leaves cover it, but it is broad and not overgrown. Southwards the vegetation thins out, and the mellyrn give way to other trees.
16600:
Delicate golden blooms adorn the ground like a cascade of stars.
An elven archer dressed in green is here, watching the forest.

At this place the path becomes faint and seems to end quite abruptly. The ground sinks, forming a small basin. The trees cling together; their thick trunks tower around and their many branches arch high above you. The forest floor seems to be lit by the elusive glow of the mallorn-trees.
16603: Some trees seem to have fallen on the edge of the forest here, perhaps having been struck by a storm or some other force. Because of the increased amount of light, undergrowth has quickly taken over this area, and even some flowers can be seen growing between the tree-trunks that lie on the ground. Short, thick stumps lie about, already growing light moss. One stump appears devoid of any undergrowth at all, as though the forest itself were recoiling from its presence here.
16608: The heavy forest to the west gives way to lighter woodland here. The trees seem to filter the light, giving the forest a soft glow. Single mallorn-trees stand here and there in islands of light; they appear to be more prevalent to the north and east. By sunlight or moonlight they magnify the light, making the woods as bright as if you were on an open plain. The grasses between the trees are grazed short to form natural lawns.
16609: Delicate golden blooms adorn the ground like a cascade of stars.

The woodland here is enchanting. The mallorn-trees seem to capture spring, summer and autumn all at once, with many in blossom and a gentle rain of leaves and petals in the almost undetectable breeze. Each tree stands separate from the others, forming a matrix of natural avenues. Not all the trees are mellyrn, but those that are not seem to be enchanted with the same spell, following the discipline of the mallorn-trees. The light here is soft, with the golden leaves glistening in the higher branches. You hear the murmur of the river a short distance to the east.
16610: Water flows slowly along a wide bend as the river changes its course from the north to the east. While the flow is strong and the river is wide, the water makes little sound. The northern bank is steep and high and it is impossible to see what lies beyond it; only from the odd tree root protruding from the ground one can gather some clues about the vegetation. The woodlands to the west glitter with bright greens, golds and other light colours, giving the land a look of springtime. You occasionally catch the sound of what seems to be laughter carried on the breeze or perhaps just the chattering of birds.
16611: The river turns from the west to the south. The flow is strong and the river is wide yet silent. The eastern bank is high and nearly vertical; a narrow ledge near its bottom might serve as a safe, if none too dry, landing for a small boat. Bright pine trees cover the top of the eastern bank, while the northern bank is higher and allows no glimpse of what lies on its top. The forest to the southwest is bright with fresh colours of green, white and gold. You catch the odd glimpse of golden and white trees; the latter must be in blossom.
16612: A swift and agile forest cat moves silently through the vegetation.

Just to the west the land drops abruptly to where a large river flows many feet below. From the edge of the steep bank the ground rises steadily to the northwest. Bright green pine trees cling precariously to the slope, perhaps only just winning the constant battle with gravity. The ground has obviously slipped recently, leaving a great scar of mud in the slopes that elsewhere are covered with pine needles. Near the riverbank you can see several dead trees.
16613: Tall pine trees stand on the top of this high bank. They are widely spaced and the ground between them is crossed with the lattice of their roots in the shallow soil. Fallen trees can be seen here and there; large flower-shaped fungi grow in the rotting wood. Far below to the south you can hear the roar of the great river scouring its way through its rocky passage. The trees continue in all other directions.
16624: A small and tough weed grows here.

Under the shadow of the forest to the east, this patch of grassland is less exposed than the land to the west. Grass and other plants hold the soft earth together. To the east the ground is water and mud, making progress in that direction impossible. A small trail or animal track leads north-south helping to pick out firmer footholds. Three small circles of stones show that someone camped here but it is not clear how long ago this happened.
16625: A natural basin filled with clear water lies here amidst the rolling green meadows. The lush grasses of the meadows are interspersed with marsh marigolds and other colourful flowers. In the lowest spots small dark pools of water stand surrounded by sphagnum moss. Strong smells of herbs penetrate the air.
16626: The gently rolling plains are covered by a varied tapestry of rich greens, golds and browns. Here and there you spot the bright pink of a tall thistle or the yellow of a marsh marigold. The grasslands continue in a similar vein in all directions with a general incline to the south where the ground appears to be retaining water and softening. In the softer spots water fills footprints as soon as they appear.
16627: The rolling landscape is formed by many low hills that are slightly elevated above the plains to the north and east and continue to rise to the west and south. Between the hills are a few narrow, well-defined valleys with gurgling streams tumbling east. Here and there one can see a spring emerging from a hillside. Some of the taller hills are capped with crags which look as though they may harbour caves.
16628: A low hill or natural mound with a flat top rises here. The ground around it is little more than bare rock. Wind and rain have created small cracks in the rock where enough soil has gathered to allow a few short tufts of grass to take root. The ground to the west drops quickly, forming a small plain, and then rises again to form a small group of hillocks. A low mound stands at some distance to the north, and a small rocky outcropping rises to the northwest. To the east the ground slopes away to the rolling grasslands below.
16629: A coloured game bird is visible in the vegetation, watching you warily.

Low hills surround this small plain covered by long dry grasses. The rocky ground to the north rises more gently than the hills to the east. The plain continues into the horizon to the south; on a bright day around noon it would be an almost blinding suntrap. The grasses rustle in the wind and when disturbed by small birds and animals.
16630: Here the trail, which is no larger than a rough animal track, picks its way through the hills. The gradients become steeper to the south and far to the southwest you can see the greys and blues of the mountains. To the south, as the ground continues to rise, the vegetation prevalent in the grasslands gives way to heather-covered moors interspersed with sparsely covered heathland. The trail passes through a few high points where one can catch glimpses of the track as it continues north and south. Here and there you see outcrops of large rocks which would allow you some protection from the elements if you were to camp.
16631: A brown toad is here, hunting flies.

The purple, brown and green carpet of heather ripples in the wind on this exposed heath. A crag the height of three men stands above you. Some cracks in the rock might allow you to climb up. You see the remains of a small campfire at its base on the flat rock. Some water has collected in the small bowls eroded in the granite by aeons of harsh winds.
16632: From the top of a hillock in these scantly covered grasslands you are able to see a faint north-south trail picking its way through the rolling hills to your east. Far beyond the trail the grey shadow of a narrow band of woodland picks out the course of a great river. The only features breaking up the monotony to the west are a few rocky outcrops; a clump of trees huddled together is to your north.
16633: Large rocky formations rise here and there, making passage difficult. Heaps of loose debris cover the ground and some bigger boulders lie about; these rocks have a rough, scratched surface, and they stand a bit slanted, as if leaning against the wind. Nothing grows here except some stunted grass which tries to survive amidst the rocky debris.
16634: A small and tough weed grows here.

A carpet of sparse, stunted grass and weeds covers this rolling plateau. Occasionally patches of green, healthier-looking grass mix in with their more common cousins. Plains continue in all directions, and a dried-up streambed can be seen to the west.
16635: A shallow channel of an old stream furrows the flat plains here. The source of this river had obviously run dry long ago and although the grass on the partly crumbled banks of the streambed still grows quite densely, the ground around it is barren and covered by the carpet of dry grass.
16636: A field vole has frozen to the spot, sensitive to your presence.

The arid lands stretch out, growing little here but low yellow-brown grasses and occasional clumps of taller, green grass. Nothing rises from the level landscape, nothing casts a single shadow, and travelling here can be quite unpleasant in the summer. An old streambed can be seen crossing through the plains in the east.
16637: The sandy, dry ground has a yellow-brown hue here and vegetation is very sparse. The desolation continues as far west as the eye can see. In the east the ground slopes slightly and some big rocks can be seen on the horizon. No kind of wildlife can be seen here, and an oppressive silence prevails.
16638:
A small and tough weed grows here.
A large rabbit looks peacefully at you, ready to dart away.

Here and there small cracks cut through the yellow soil. The plateau is open and flat, but westwards the ground rises and some hills can be made out in the distance. The air is still and quiet. Tufts of tough yellow grass grow sparsely in the dry earth.
16639: An oppressive silence prevails in this grim part of the desolation. Living things do not seem to come here very often and the air feels heavy and seems to hush all sounds, as though the land itself did not wish to be disturbed. The dry ground seems to deaden even the sounds of footsteps.
16640: The lands here are barren, as though the life in this area were in hibernation. A few sparse shrubs can be seen scattered about the landscape, providing barely any shelter or sustenance for any creature. Plains can be seen to the west and east, while a low hill can be seen to the north.
16641: A small hilltop graces the otherwise unimpressive landscape here. The vegetation is poor, consisting mostly of stunted grass and the occasional withered shrub. Downhill to the west the terrain becomes rocky, while the plains continue in all other directions.
16642: The terrain becomes more rocky here, and some large boulders lie about providing some shelter from the winds. In the middle of this immense desolation one might wonder whether this ground has even seen a living creature before. Only the wind is always present here, passing through the lands, licking the rocks and wiping the occasional loose stones away.
16643: The plains here are dry and barren. The grass looks dull and grey. The few trees and bushes are half-dead and the wildlife seems to be non-existent. A few small hills mark the landscape. The hills continue to the north, while the land to the west appears to be flat. To the east the terrain looks more rocky.
16644: These flat plains are filled with tall, lush grass, yellow and white flowers, some shrubbery and a few trees. Actually it is quite easy to hide in the grass, but on the other hand, your worst enemy could be hidden there as well. The plains stretches before you in all directions.
16645: The even landscape is covered with lush grass. There are no hills, a few trees and some scattered shrubbery. Judging by the noise, the wildlife here is rich and consists mostly of birds, frogs and locusts. Plains fill the view in all directions, but one thing is more dominant in the north: a great tree.
16646: The land is completely flat here. The ground is soft, but numerous small paths make it easy to travel through the terrain. Thick green grass covers the ground like a lush carpet, its pattern changing with every gust of the wind. A few trees and bushes can be seen rising out of the tall grass. To the west and north the plains seem to grow more muddy.
16647: These plains are covered in thick grass and low shrubs interspersed by occasional bushes and trees. The ground is soft and muddy, making it hard to travel across the terrain on foot. To the west a fogbank can be spotted on the horizon. Grasslands dominate the view to the north, east and south.
16648: Most of the ground is covered by water. Thick vegetation covers the spots where the ground rises above the water level. It would be hard to travel in one consistent direction through this terrain, and the fog that covers the land would not make it easier. The fog seems to grow in density to the west, while the area to the east appears more friendly.
16649: Baghor the Dwarf (BG), wielding a mighty dwarven axe, is standing here.

In the middle of the marshes, where the water seems to take control, a large plateau rises suddenly out of the swamp. The ground is solid and covered by grass. The fog seems to clear a bit, but the surroundings are still the same: dirty brown water, knolls and smaller plateaus of earth and grass with plenty of swarming insects.
16650: The fog is dense here, so dense that you can barely see your feet. The ground is covered with water, mostly about one foot deep, but in some places apparently deeper and maybe even bottomless. The fog seems to drop in density to the west while it looks impervious in the other directions. There is no wildlife to be seen here, but the swamp makes its own sounds.
16651: Dark and dirty water dominates here, but small plateaus and knolls of earth and grass make it possible to move between the narrow paths. The marshes seem to continue to the north and east, judging by the fog that covers the ground in these directions. To the west you can leave the marshes.
16652: A brown fox is here, looking for some rabbits to chew up.

The fields are covered by grass and water. The ground is soft and muddy from the water of a small brook that flows out of the side of a tiny hill. Surrounded by small bushes and shrubs, the brook runs north. To the east the land is covered in fog; in all other directions, the grasslands continue.
16653: Much like the surrounding areas, this part of the plains is covered by a soft layer of grass interspersed by small plants. On the horizon, in the distant north, the shape of a large tree is visible. Also, in that direction the soil becomes drier and the grassy cover thins. To the east, in a stark contrast to the dry areas directly north of here, lies a patch of damp swampy ground.
16654: A small centipede is here scurrying about.

These fields are dry but still manage to support a wide variety of grasses and plants. Many tiny insects can be seen feeding on the lush grasses. West of here the ground begins to slope upwards where it eventually forms a small mound. Except for that mound, no landmarks are visible in this otherwise featureless terrain.
16655: The ground here is slightly higher than the surroundings. A soft layer of grass dotted by many weeds and flowers covers this elevated area. To the north and east nothing of significance can be seen. To the west the silhouette of a small wooden shack is visible.
16656:
A grey wolf is here, snarling aggressively.
A brown fox is here, looking for some rabbits to chew up.

It appears that much of this land has been cleared, as only a few fresh blades of grass can be seen sprouting from the fertile ground. A small wooden shack is standing here; it appears to be some sort of sentry post. To the east a small mound rises from the plains, and to the northwest, where the grass is quite thin, a huge boulder is visible. In all other directions the vast grass-covered plains continue with no interruptions or landmarks.
16657: The ground is dry, dusty and is composed almost exclusively of compacted rock. While a few clumps of soil can be seen between the rocky plates, they are too small and too shallow to support plant growth. To the north a very large boulder can be seen. Except for the boulder and a small wooden structure towards the east, no landmarks break the monotony of these desolate plains.
16658: The ground here is solid rock, covered with a thin layer of dirt and sand. The shallow soil makes it impossible for any plants to take root and survive. The lack of plant roots allows the slightest wind to create a wall of sand that obscures all vision. To the west are the remains of a number of structures which appear to have once formed a thriving village. In all other directions nothing but empty plains can be seen.
16659: This area appears to be the ruins of a once busy village. While a few buildings are still standing, most have been reduced to nothing more than piles of rubble and dust. While it is impossible to determine exactly when the village fell into ruins, it clearly happened many years ago for moss has overgrown most of the rubble.
16660: A nightingale is here, chirping a sweet melody.

This region is dry and barren. For years plants grew in harmony upon the land, but now they grow here no longer. First the rain stopped, then the soil turned hard and one by one the plants withered and died. When the rains returned, the soil was unable to hold the water. While a few plants took root while the soil was moist, most were unable to live until the next rain. To the west a group of trees rises among the plains, their lush foliage seeming out of character compared to the rest of the visible region. A few ruined buildings and some rocks piled high can be seen towards the east.
16661: A few maples, no more than twenty or thirty, grow here in a clump, making this one of the few productive spots on these otherwise desolated plains. The trees grow very close together and seem rather short for mature trees. On some of the trees in a few spots the bark has worn off, and on other trees the living trunk has splintered.
16662: Almost no plants have managed to grow in this sterile soil - even the common weeds and hardy grasses of the plains soon perish after they sprout. Without plant life, there is nothing to obscure your immediate vision of these dull, infertile plains as they extend in all directions until they meet the horizon. Only a small clump of trees has managed to grow due east of here and provides a break in the monotony.
16663: The small rise in the landscape offers a good view of the surrounding fields. The slope ends to the east, where plains continue as far as the eye can see. Anyone desiring the cool shade of green trees and the fragrance of lush foliage could head north, where far off in the distance a large forest can be seen. One can also continue westward, where the barren slope continues and passes a small but remarkable mound.
16664: At this elevation, the fields are exposed to strong winds that make staying here somewhat uncomfortable. The gusts have blown away most of the thin layer of soil that used to cover the dry sand. Sand dominates these fields now and more demanding plants cannot grow here anymore. The slope rises high above the northern fields where one can spot a small patch of green.
16665: The ground here is a bit elevated, offering you a good view of the surrounding fields. The darker bar of green on the northern horizon must surely be a sign of some forest. The slope, that does not surprise with abundance of lush nature, continues to the east and to the west. This might be a good place for setting up a camp, for certainly no flood will ever cover this rising.
16666: A large eagle soars above you.

From this vantage, one can get a good view of the fields lying north of here, although there does not seem to be much to discover in these barren plains. Far north lies a belt of green that might be some kind of a forest. Looking around, it is easy to see why the few plants that grow on this slope are trampled by horsemen. The barren land is extremely easy to travel through, and an approaching enemy, not so uncommon in these troubled times, can be seen from a great distance.
16667: The slope has reached a small but noticeable mound that rises a bit above the northern fields. A seemingly natural wall of trees blocks the way to the top of the mound. Waters of many springs have carved wide furrows into the earthen side and revealed the hard stone core underneath. The slope, that continues east and west from here, seems to have been trodden by many hoofs, suggesting that this may have been the favourite riding path for some groups of travellers.
16668: Small rocks cover the ground where earth has slid away from the side of the mound that rises to about the same level as this slope. Occasional blades of grass have penetrated the rubble, but on the whole these fields have little to offer for wildlife to graze upon. This slope continues east and west, where you can probably get a better view of the surrounding lands.
16669: A beautiful view opens from this slope, which is not so impressive in height as the mound that stands at some distance to the northeast. Far north you see a forest covering the fields that in other directions seem barren and desolated except for a small coppice of trees to the northwest. Closer to the coppice the ground bears signs of intelligent activity, perhaps failed efforts to make this soil yield crops.
16670: A few lonely birches and pines waver in the wind that carries dust and sand from the lower desert-like fields. There seems to be an island of green to the north and a dark green belt of trees farther in that direction. No animals or birds can be seen here. The lack of wildlife might be the source of the strange and eerie sensation that even this last outpost of verdure is bound to vanish.
16671: The grass-covered slope continues east and west as far as you can see. To the north the greenery extends and forms a small grassy peninsula among the northern barrenness. Even farther to the north you spot a green wall, the edge of the forest of Lothlorien.
16672: Rising out of the barren plains in the west, the grass-covered slope continues east as far as the eye can see. Occasional winds blow up clouds of dust from the northern sandy fields, where no trees can be seen and probably only few animals manage to subsist. Far north there appears to be the start of a thick forest. Looking east, you can see the bar of green extend a bit northward.
16673:
A rabbit is here eyeing your presence warily.
A fallow deer is grazing peacefully here.

The earth is bare here as there is almost no grass. Most of the topsoil has been carried away by the wind, since there is nothing here to keep it rooted. Few signs of animal life can be seen and no vegetation except for a few tough weeds that continue their never-ending fight for survival. To the west and the north the plains continue unchanged, but to the east a gentle slope climbs upward, in its ascent slowly changing colour from ashen-grey to the soft green of grass.
16674: A sharp-eyed hawk is here stalking some prey.

The ground here is grey and unpopulated, except for some thorny bushes and withered brown grass. These seemingly dead fields stretch out in all directions, making it easy to get lost among the similar surroundings. Occasionally, a bird can be seen flying high above the land, perhaps an indication of something other than deserted plains nearby.
16675: As the land slopes down from the west to the east, the grass grows thinner and thinner as the plains become more barren. The grass that does grow here is mostly brownish in colour and looks wilted, more dead than alive. The trees that do grow here are low and stunted.
16676: Light green grass waves back and forth in the gentle, yet persistent, wind. A few stunted trees grow here, their brownish-coloured leaves hanging limply from their thin branches. A few bushes grow by the side of the trees, some of them bearing pink flowers and orange fruit.
16677: The consistency of the look of these plains could be amazing to a traveller used to faster changes in the terrain. As far as the eye can see, green and light golden grass covers the earth, its even expanse only rarely interrupted by a half-grown tree or a clump of bushes.
16678: The rolling landscape seems hardly to change, as the grass, green and light golden, is everywhere, but to the south you can see a small copse of pine-trees standing in a circle. While it is many miles to the nearest forest, some of the pines appear so ancient that they they might well be the survivors from the time when the forest of Lorien extended much farther south. Inside the circle of trees pine-needles cover the grass like a thick carpet.
16679: A brown fox is here, looking for some rabbits to chew up.

The ground is covered in thick grass the blades of which are light golden in colour. The grass sways ever so gently in the slow, caressing wind. Animal tracks are easy to spot as the grass appears to have leaned aside to allow them passage.
16680:
A sharp-eyed hawk is here stalking some prey.
A fallow deer is grazing peacefully here.

The ground here is moist, made fertile by the frequent rain and abundant sunshine. The grass grows high and thick, and its blades are mostly light golden in colour, in some spots tinged with green or brown. Small insects can be seen feeding upon the bountiful grass.
16681: The surrounding area is one teeming with wildlife and vegetation. Thick and bountiful bushes, which during the spring and summer produce many kinds of fruit, grow everywhere. Many trees grow here as well, but most of these are mere saplings. Every free spot on the ground is covered with grass which grows up to two feet in height.
16682: A shallow pond is here, tinted green with algae.

Roots of a tree entwine around a huge rock that lies against the side of the hill that rises to the north. The rock is almost completely covered with roots. A small spring comes down from the top of the hill and runs down the hillside, forming a small pond at the bottom. Many animal tracks can be seen in the mud around the spring, as they come from all over to drink from this water-hole.
16683: In this area of the plains there are almost no trees, but there are many dry tree-roots in the ground, apparently remaining from the time when this land was more forested. Thorny bushes dot the landscape, and some berries can be seen growing on them. The land slopes upwards gently to the west.
16684:
A tall pine tree grows here.
A rabbit is here eyeing your presence warily.
A fallow deer is grazing peacefully here.

This flat area is open to all the winds and seems an unlikely spot to find a lonely tree, yet here one grows, casting its shade upon the ground. As far as eye can see, green plains stretch out in all directions, waves passing through the sea of grass with every gust of wind.
16685: Winds blow constantly through the level landscape, filling the dry air with scents and sounds of the surrounding lands. With every gust of wind the thick green grass bends back and forth, making a gentle rustling sound that seems to fade as soon as it reaches your ears.
16686: A fallow deer is grazing peacefully here.

The thick green grass that covers these plains seems to grow even as you watch, its tall stems concealing every track and every mound or depression in the ground. A few clusters of bushes and an occasional tree can also be seen in the plains, rising like islands from the grassy sea.
16687: A well-beaten path has been made here through the jungle of grass. Without it passage on foot would be much harder if at all possible. All kinds of tracks can be seen on the path: tracks of various wild animals, hoof-prints of many horses and occasionally unmistakably humanoid tracks, prints of boots of a traveller that walked through this area on foot.
16688:
A large thorny branched shrub is growing here.
On the shrub, there are two piles of blackberries.

The land here is barren and dry. The sparse vegetation consists of grass and occasional bushes. The grass is brownish and not too lively, but the bushes appear well adapted to this type of environment, their branches bearing long thorns and their roots digging deep into the ground.
16689: Withered, dying trees can be seen everywhere, wilted by the power of the abundant sunlight and lack of water. Brown, curled leaves, fallen from the surrounding trees, litter the ground. Weathered tufts of brownish grass are spread liberally about the area.
16690: A giant, mean looking earth beetle is standing here.

These plains are made up of mostly dry dunes of bare soil. The vegetation clings lightly to the eroded ground. The occasional gust of wind creates clouds of sand that fill the air, likely to deter even the most weathered traveller for a short time. To the north, the ground appears to become less sandy.
16691: Grassy hillocks, sparsely scattered across the landscape, add little variation to these sandy fields, where the few surviving plants are stunted and seem to be one step from losing the struggle against the intrusion of barrenness. Gazing eastward, one cannot help but wonder if there is a mirage up ahead, mockery for the weary traveller, or in fact a grove of trees, with real grass and, perhaps, even water.
16692: In Front of the Rustic House

A huge, smoking campfire is burning here.
A tall and strong hunter is standing here.

To the north you can see a lop-sided old house, its balks damaged by bark beetles and its door about to fall off the hinges. Pelts have been hung on the racks in front of the cot, suggesting that the owner uses his hunting skills to acquire daily nourishment. That being the case, it is no wonder that poverty echoes from the building. The island of green is too small, and the surrounding fields too barren to provide ample game.
16693:
A woody evergreen plant grows here, with many stems reaching upward.
A starving cow stands here, looking for a patch of grass.

Infrequent stunted birches and tall pines, indifferent to dry and sandy soil, decorate this small island of green in the midst of infertile fields. You spot a small cultivated corner where someone has tried, with little success, to grow some crops. Larger stones have been moved from the cultivated land and arranged so that they could now serve as a rest site for occasional travellers.
16694: Plains along the Side of the Mound

The barren plains stretch out in all directions, producing few plants and showing few features of interest. To get a better look at the surrounding fields one could head east, where a small mound rises to some height above the plains, or south, where a grassy slope would probably offer a spectacular view. Unlike this barren and sandy ground, the coppice to the west offers cool shade of stunted trees.
16695: Gently climbing up the eastward slope, the faint path leads to some greenery and a large boulder. Occasional gusts of wind blow sand and dust up from the ground, making dry air creep into your throat as you breathe. Looking west, you spot another island of green amidst the dry and barren fields.
16696: On the top of the mound a strange boulder inlaid with writing stands encircled by tall and graceful trees. Combining artistry with extensive, perhaps magical knowledge of nature, careful hands have planted the trees close enough for them to entwine and form a sturdy wall of this shrine. This small grove appears to bear great significance to whoever has cleaned the ground of fallen branches and wiped the dust off the rough surface of the boulder.
16697: The surrounding terrain, still maintaining the overall impression of desolation, varies here more in height and features. The ground rises to the south and forms a slope, and climbs even higher to the west where a mound catches the eye. To reach it one would have to travel around a wall of closely growing trees that obstruct the way. Here and there junipers form small groups that get thicker and eventually become an extensive coppice to the east. The sandy ground bears tracks of reptiles.
16698: A large eagle soars above you.

The dry grass sighs like autumn leaves rustling in the wind. The sandy soil makes it difficult for flora to thrive, yet some tougher plants stubbornly fight their way towards the sky. Perhaps they retrieve sustenance from damper northern grounds; but surely not from the south, where the land seems to be even drier.
16699:
A short evergreen plant, with slightly bluish needles, grows here.
On the plant, there are two clusters of hard, round, black berries.
A snake slithers towards you.

A small patch of juniper bushes stands here, even though their stout and hardy souls are not a common sight in these lands. Harsh conditions and an extremely thin layer of soil do not disturb their frugal life. Their branches rustle as wind carries sand up and at the same time blows more and more fertile ground away. The desolate landscape rises to the south to meet a low slope.
16700: The ground steadily climbs upwards and forms a small but noticeable slope to the south. The few plants that used to grow here have dried up from thirst and the sandy winds that blow across these plains. Some bleached bones indicate that a few animals still wander here, although there is practically no grass and certainly no trees to find shade under.
16701: The ground is hard and rocky, preventing plant life from growing on these plains. Unobscured a lonesome large rock, covered with a brittle yellow-green moss, can be seen clearly as it sits upon hard rocky soil. The empty, desolate lands continue in all directions for as far as can be seen.
16702: Several piles of tiny white pebbles are scattered across these otherwise featureless fields. To the north and slightly to the west you can see an old hut that appears decrepit and abandoned. A small but thick grove of trees lies to the south, somewhat enlivening the otherwise desolate landscape.
16703: Most plants find it difficult to grow in the hard dry ground which is more clay than soil. Only a few small clumps of brownish grass still struggle in their quest for life. To the northwest a wooden cabin rises among the plains, while a number of structures, possibly ruined buildings, can be seen to the southeast. Below you a small section of the earth has given way forming a shallow hole.
16704:
A small grasshopper clings to a blade of grass, ready to spring.
A brown fox is here, looking for some rabbits to chew up.

This desolate and featureless terrain continues to the east and west as far as the eye can see. To the south a few old and half-collapsed buildings can be found amongst piles of rubble. To the north a seemingly endless line of trees crosses the plains.
16705: Few plants have managed to grow in this dry and arid place. Those plants, mostly grasses, that have managed to grow on this soil are pale-brown or green and brittle to the touch. While a line of trees can be seen to the north, much of your vision is obscured by clouds of dust. To the south the ground becomes more rocky and solid, while to the east, a great distance from here, a large boulder blends in with the swirling dust.
16706: A small brook flows in from the north and slowly trickles its way towards a huge solitary boulder, under which it vanishes. While a few plants still manage to grow in the rocky soil, the vegetation thins rapidly towards the south where the ground slowly turns from soil to rock. Many rocks and small stones can be seen to the south.
16707: A dense carpet of tall grasses covers these lush fields. The grasses are a mixture of many varieties and grow rapidly with some blades over four feet high. A huge boulder can be seen to the west where the grasslands are more sparse. To the east and north tall grasses continue making travel in those directions difficult, while to the south there is a small wooden hut.
16708: A small grasshopper clings to a blade of grass, ready to spring.

The grass here is over two feet tall and wavers gently in the soft breeze. Clumps of wild flowers dot the landscape and fill the air with their fragrance. South of here a small mound, little more than a bump upon the plains, can be found, while towards the southwest the shape of a small hut is visible. In all other directions the terrain, mostly grasslands, remains unchanged.
16709: Except for the small mound to the southwest, these grassy fields are flat for as far as one can see. While the ground is firm and dry, the plants and grasses find enough moisture to remain alive and healthy looking. To the north the ground becomes more moist, perhaps from an underground stream, while to the east conditions for plant life become less favourable. To the west the grasslands continue seemingly unchanged.
16710: A brownish grass with a short stem and prickly tip dominates this area. Except for the struggling grass few other plants have been able to grow in the dry, hard soil. To the north, where the soil contains more moisture and the grass is greener and thicker, a large tree can be seen standing lonely on the plains.
16711: A brown fox is here, looking for some rabbits to chew up.

The fields are covered by an uneven carpet of grass. Below the grass, the ground is soft and muddy. Shallow puddles of water can be spotted here and there. A small brook is coming from the south and continuing north. A few low bushes and trees stand near the brook. To the north, west and south, the grassy plains continue. To the east, the land is covered in fog.
16712: Brownish water is all over, with grass and small knolls of earth rising above its surface. The air is filled with fog which makes it hard to see far, but small paths make it possible to move around. The marshes spread out to the north, east and south. To the west you can move out from the fog, while it gets more dense to the east.
16713: The water is about one foot deep here. This appears to be the centre of the swamp, although it is hard to tell because of the heavy fog that covers the area in all directions. The fog seems to be less dense to the east. Some strange noises penetrate the fog; their source is apparently the swamp itself, since no wildlife can be seen anywhere.
16714: The ground is very muddy. Most of it is covered by dark and dirty water which often makes it hard to even see if there is any solid bottom below. The fogbank is dense but still growing in density to the west. To the east and north the terrain seem less severe. The air is filled with the buzzing of insects.
16715: Grass dominates the ground which is very soft from various puddles and streams of water. Small bushes grow in clusters with smaller growth surrounding them. To the west the water is more dominating, a heavy fog seems to cover the land in that direction, while to the east the plains continue to the very horizon.
