According to the humming and buzzing noises, this area is inhabited by a multitude of insects. A light fog covers the ground. To the south and west the fog gets much thicker as the grassland turns into a swamp.
16934: The soft, muddy ground is mostly bare in this part of the plains. Puddles of water of different sizes can be seen everywhere. The only growth is some thorny shrubbery. The southwestern horizon is filled with a heavy grey fog which might indicate the presence of a marsh. In all other directions, plains and fields spread out.
16935: In the middle of the monotonous plains lies a small field with vigorous grass growing beautifully along with many yellow and purple flowers. Around the field, the plains can be seen stretching out in all directions. On the southwestern horizon a large fogbank can be spotted and to the east a grey dust cloud covers the area.
16936: The ground is rough and black and the grass is scorched. Nothing lives here and nothing grows here. The air is heavy and hard to breathe from the dust filling it. The silence fills every good soul with sorrow and every evil soul with hope. The sombre atmosphere absorbs any noise. It is hard to determine whether this is an old burial site or whether the strange aura of this place is due to something else.
16937: This area is grey and black, and the air is heavy to breathe because of all the dust in it. The ground is rough and black; the grass is scorched. Nothing lives here and nothing grows here. Some might want to scream, but it is impossible to even say a word. The sombre atmosphere absorbs all sound. This could be an old burial place, or maybe it is just the way of nature, or maybe something else caused this.
16938: The tall, lush grass is dominant here, but a large path has been trampled through it by the passage of many animals. The path leads from the north to the south. Some tracks lead away from the path to the east, but none lead west where the horizon is covered with a heavy, grey dust cloud.
16939: Tall, vigorous grass is dominant here. The land is flat, but a few small hills can be seen on the southern horizon. The wildlife is rich, according to the sounds and the occasional matted patches of grass. A few groups of trees mark the otherwise featureless landscape. The plains continue in all directions, but to the south the terrain becomes drier.
16940: Almost no signs of wildlife present themselves here, save the occasional bird circling in the sky, probably on its way to a more lively environment. The carpet of grass continues, following the gently varying contours of the landscape which continues in every direction.
16941: A field vole has frozen to the spot, sensitive to your presence.

As one progresses southwards, the grass becomes more sparse and the soil more barren, indicating a drier climate. It seems that rainfall is not common in this part of the plains. Some species seem to have adapted to this environment, however; these plains are not entirely lifeless.
16942: A thin, hairy plant, with small, oval leaves, grows here.

Rising southwards the ground slopes steeply forming a low hill. A narrow path runs through the grassy slope, winding around clumps of shrubbery, avoiding the occasional holes in the ground and leading towards the hilltop in the south.
16943: Prickly, white-stemmed plants, with blue flower heads grow in abundance.

The ground rises southwest towards a flat, grassy hilltop which seems to be the highest point in the surrounding areas. From here the visibility is already good to the north and east, over the bland rolling plateau which extends for miles.
16944: A small and tough weed grows here.

A shallow, winding ditch cuts through the ground here like a scar, its banks partly crumbled in. The ground is barren, but the ditch seems to provide shelter for some patches of low, tough grass. Dirt and withered grass cover the bottom of the ditch.
16945: A small valley cuts the plateau to the east where an old, ruined building can be seen next to a dried streambed. To the south the ground descends more gently. Much time has passed since these fields were last inhabited. Now, the area is dry and abandoned; rarely does a traveller pass through this place.
16946: Though the stream in the east has not brought water to the valley for ages the stony walls of an old watermill still stand here, surrounded by the rolling fields. The building has survived the years well, and though the roof has partly collapsed the walls and the channel which once led water to the wheel have not crumbled yet. A stony doorway leads in to the upper floor of the mill, but from here it is not possible to see what lies inside.
16947: The stream has been quite narrow here, as this channel is only about five yards wide. It is deeper, though, but not difficult to cross, as the sandy banks have mostly crumbled and are easy to climb. Small tufts of grass can be found growing on the ruined banks.
16948: Grasslands extend in all directions here, open and flat except to the west where the land slopes gently towards a shallow valley floor. A dry streambed can be seen in that direction; a river must once have run through this area. Some ruined buildings can also be seen to the north and west.
16949: This bleak, fairly lifeless desolation continues in all directions. Farther to the south the terrain becomes rougher and some dark, rocky shapes can be seen rising in the distance. Here nothing but some loose stones lie around the dull-coloured dusty ground.
16950: The lands here are bare and lifeless with only the odd tuft of grass or thistle waving in the wind. The terrain gently rises to the south, where the grasslands become more undulating. The breeze carries a light smell of salt which seems to account for the lack of vegetation. At low points in the landscape the horizon is limited to the surrounding grasses; on the high points one could see little to break the unchanging plains other than the hazy shadow of a large forest far to the northwest.
16951: These plains are covered by tall dry grasses that rustle in the wind. The land to the west seems bare and lifeless. The hills to the south exhibit a variety of plant cover judging by the shades of blues and greys visible in the distance. Just to the north a fine trail bends east and then curves southwards.
16952: Here the ill-defined trail through the wild grasses turns east and north. The fields to the west seem to indicate some previous habitation of the area, whereas the grasslands to the southeast are the product of poor soils and weathering. A forest dominates your view to the east. The trees nearest to you are leafless and silent.
16953: You can see from the remains of several rows of fencing and dry stone walls that these fields were once used for agricultural purposes. A square of stones marks the place where a farmhouse once stood. To your east you spot the thin line of a trail through barren lands. To the south the ground begins to rise and roll a little.
16954: Once a fertile area, this land is now completely barren with nothing but short grass populating the widespread fields. The open plains are spacious, but empty; rarely does a traveller disturb the peace of these lands, and few animals can be seen.
16955: The terrain here might have once been a part of a local farm, as it is open and very level. Now, however, the soil is barren and unfertile, allowing hardly anything to grow. These fields appear to have been ruined long ago.
16956: The riverbed bends here, going west and south and passing some ruined foundations of farm buildings which lie in the north. The banks are higher and steeper here, but it would not be very difficult to cross this channel. While the grass reigns on the banks, not much grows on the shadowy bottom.
16957: The streambed runs east and north here, descending from the hills in the north toward the desolate valley. The banks are crumbled and overgrown, but not much grows in the shadows of the dry, sandy bottom. The stream obviously dried up a long time ago. Some bleached bones can be seen resting against the eastern bank of the riverbed.
16958: Yellow flowers, with grey-green foliage, grow in clusters here.

The bluff has partly crumbled here, creating small potholes in the ground. To the north an old path descends gently toward a shallow valley. The path seems to cross the valley floor and continue to the other side in the distance. Some large boulders lie to the west, making the passage uphill difficult.
16959: Hard, rough boulders lie about, blocking passage over this slope in some places. The rocky edges seem very sharp, making passage difficult, and loose debris dots the ground along the surface of the slope. Farther downhill the terrain becomes harder to navigate; passage back uphill would be tiring.
16960: Not much moves between this dry, cracked ground and the high, open sky. Only an occasional bird can be seen circling high above you. The silence is surprising, almost oppressive. The land is very flat, providing little cover to any passers-by from wind, rain or the watchful eyes of those who would see.
16961: Ever on, the grasslands continue. An occasional gust of wind caresses your skin and goes away as suddenly as it came. But for the wind the landscape is lone and quiet; wildlife has not spread to such conditions as these. Here the ground begins to rise slowly, climbing towards the hilltop in the south.
16962: The silence that prevails here is almost oppressive. No sounds of wildlife or birds can be heard, only an occasional rustle as the wind creates waves in the sea of grass. The grasslands continue in all directions; very little activity can be discerned among them from here.
16963: The silent plains stretch out here. In the ground, one can see same tracks indicating that there is some wildlife here. The plateau reaches on in all directions. Several shapes appear to be moving in the distance; but in a blink, the land seems completely still again.
16964: Tall, lush grass covers the ground completely. Only a few trees rise above the grassy cover. Judging by the noises, the wildlife appears to be rich; the grass is tall enough to conceal any small animals. Plains seem to continue in all directions.
16965: A path runs through the tall, lush grass from the north to the south. The path widens as it runs south and is joined by many small paths coming from the east and west. The plains continue in all directions. Groups of trees and patches of shrubbery are the only landmarks in this level terrain.
16966: A brown fox is here, looking for some rabbits to chew up.

The plains are covered with grass, yellow, white and red flowers, bushes and occasional trees. The land is flat; not a single hilltop can be seen. The soil is soft, as if it has rained recently. The wildlife is rich, according to the sounds; birds are singing, and frogs and locusts can be heard as well. The plains continue in all directions, but a grey dust covers the land to the south.
16967: The tall grass is dominant here, but it looks as if a pack of animals or a big party passed here recently because the grass is trampled in many places. The tracks continue in the western direction, but it is hard to see where they are going or coming from. The plains continue in all directions, but the land to the south is covered with grey dust.
16968: Tall, lush grass covers the ground here. A large patch of the grass lies flat on the ground as if many animals have trampled it down. The trampled grass seems to run east-west. The grassy plains extend in all directions, but the southeast is covered by a grey dust cloud, and to the north, the outline of a ruined building can be spotted.
16969: Lush fields covered with vigorous grasses dominate the view. Bushes and smaller shrubs serve as landmarks in this terrain where few trees can be spotted. Judging by frequent animal sounds, the wildlife prospers in this area. Many animals have trampled a path through the grass; the path continues north and east. A large fogbank can be seen to the southwest.
16970: Thick wet grass dominates these plains, with a few bushes and some smaller plants sporadically making their appearance. Here and there lonely trees can be seen standing tall and proud. Judging by the tracks in the grass, the wildlife consists of birds, small animals and maybe a few deer. To the south a large fogbank can be seen covering the land, while in the other directions plains and fields stretch out to the very horizon.
16971: Lush grass, small bushes and even smaller shrubs cover these plains. Lonely trees can be seen reaching for the sky here and there. Unseen birds fill the air with their melodious singing. These surroundings continue to the horizon in all directions except to the south, where a dense bank of fog covers the land making it impossible to see far.
16972: Covered with water and grass, the ground is soft and muddy. Small bushes and trees grow all around. To the north, east and west the plains continue, but to the south and southeast the marshes begin, covered in fog. To the west you can see a few hills in the horizon.
16973: Tall grass interspersed with small bushes covers the ground. The stems move slightly, indicating that living beings lurk underneath, but there is no way to tell what creatures those might be. A few small hills can be seen on the northern horizon; in all other directions the plains continue. The plains to the southeast are covered in fog.
16974: A pack horse is standing here, ridden by you.

A number of bushes grow in groups of three and four on the slightly undulating ground that is covered by thick layers of grasses. Some of the taller grasses sway whenever there is a light breeze, which is common to this section of the vast plains of Lorien. To the northwest there is a hill that might offer a clear view of this region, while to the south a tall tree stands alone.
16975: This gentle slope slants from the summit of a small hill in the north to the grassy valley in the south. The ground is moist and covered by dense patches of tall grass. Where the hillside begins to ascend in earnest, some cracks are visible in an otherwise solid rock plate. To the west the land dips into a shallow bowl.
16976: The butchering of the land here indicates that this was once an old quarry. The rocky ground seems almost out of place as the surrounding areas consist of rolling plains. The floor of the quarry was once white rock, but it turned a dull green as it was covered by moss. Several muddy pools of water have collected, but they do not look clean enough for drinking.
16977: The endless plains are covered by a vast quantity of grass and small bushes. An occasional tree, little more than a small shrub, can be seen between the bushes; none of these trees manage to reach even four feet in height. In all directions the terrain is the same with the exception of a few small mounds that rise and fall without any visible pattern.
16978:
A small brown snake is slithering around here.
A small brown snake is slithering around here.
A brown fox is here, looking for some rabbits to chew up.

A small brook runs from north to south, winding gently across the plains. Along the brook a well-worn track has been shaped over many years of passage by animals and people alike. To the west a large stone circle is visible on the horizon; in all other directions the featureless plains continue.
16979: These desolate plains are interrupted by a number of large stones that are arranged in a circle. The formation is too symmetrical to have formed naturally, yet there are no indications of why or when the formation was constructed. While an occasional sound, whether it be bird, land animal or wind, can be heard across the plains, it appears that sound is unable to penetrate the circle.
16980: These fields are teeming with plants and trees. Grasses of various shades of green form a rich carpet covering the soft, moist ground. To the east several tall, oddly shaped stones rise in some kind of formation. In the north the vast forest of Lorien covers the land.
16981: The earth gently rises here, forming a low mound. While the mound might be the remains of a burial mound, this could just as easily be the natural contour of the earth. Regardless of how the mound was formed, several trees sprouted on and around it many years ago, for now they are mature with a few of them showing signs of decay. To the north the trees become more dense as the vast Lorien forest begins in earnest.
16982: This is a fruitful area, teeming with trees and other plants. The trees, mostly maples and other soft woods, grow more dense to the north, where the forest of Lorien begins. To the southwest, some distance from here, a fairly large wooden hut has been built.
16983: While the boundary of the great forest of Lothlorien lies to the north, a number of hearty trees have managed to grow here, where the soil remains fertile. Farther to the south, the density of the trees rapidly decreases as the plains begin to form on significantly less fertile soil. To the east the woody plains continue unchanged, but westwards the soil becomes sandy and the area barren.
16984: Only a few grassy tussocks can be seen in these sandy fields, where probably only reptiles feel comfortable. A little to the north one can spot a green belt of trees where the forest of Lothlorien must lie. Even the thought of such powerful nature seems inappropriate, for here and for many miles to the south not a single tree can be seen; however, the plains appear to grow more fertile to the east.
16985: A clear spring babbles as cool water trickles out of the ground.

Quite unexpectedly a slit opens in the ground here, revealing a small sparkling underground rivulet that quietly seeps from between mossy rocks and vanishes as it continues its secretive journey. Small bushes have gained some strength from its soft murmuring, but the effects of the water do not extend very far. The northern coppice is probably the source of the spring and most likely the water is being absorbed by the southern dry and sandy fields.
16986: A few mossy willows and birches rise toward the heavens here, marking the beginning of the forest of Lothlorien. Some younger trees contribute to the undergrowth amidst which small plants and occasional bushes spread their branches and leaves. The ground is fairly dry, resembling the barren lands surrounding this small coppice, except for the thickening forest north, where a couple of muddy pools can be seen.
16987: Sparse bushes and dry grass form the outskirts of the small coppice to the east, which in turn becomes a larger forest. The forest undoubtedly houses a larger variety of plants and animals than these relatively barren fields. Large stones encircle a small burnt patch where someone made a camp-fire, probably considering this a safer place for rest than the lifeless fields to the south.
16988: If not for the small white rocks gathered from the nearby fields, the footpath would be barely discernible in the bleak plains, where only occasional patches of wild grass grow. The hemmed path is the sole evidence of any activity. From here it continues west and south, where the ground begins to rise.
16989: Compared to the barren lands to the south, nature on both sides of the faint path seems much more lively and colourful. Even the ground here seems softer. The footpath is lined with small white rocks gathered from the nearby fields. Except for the stones and the chirping of birds of the northern forest, no other sign of life or activity can be seen.
16990: At the Border of the Forest

Occasional faraway howls come from the northern forest, mixing with the chirping of birds and the other sounds of nature. The wall of pine and birch trees seems impenetrable at first glance, but surely there must be a simpler way to enter the forest of Lothlorien than hacking through this thicket. Looking south, one can spot a small mound at some distance, and judging by some tracks leading in that direction, the tenants of the forest may have found some easy way to travel to the mound and back.
16991: At the Border of the Forest

The northern forest echoes with the sounds of nature, yet there seems to be no way to enter it. It would take days to hack through the thick undergrowth. Yet, it might be wiser to camp in the shade of trees rather than here in the bleak and barren plains, where beasts and reptiles of an unknown nature might be only waiting for weary eyelids to close.
16992: A cluster of dark green, feathery fronds flourishes in the shade.

The ground is somewhat wet and muddy here, getting drier to the south but getting even marshier as it begins to descend northwards. Drawing their strength from the fertile soil, bushes and plants of different kinds seem to thrive on both sides of the ditch. The merry chirping of birds and occasional howls can be heard from the north.
16993: Some mossy willows and birches rise toward the sky here, marking the beginning of the forest of Lothlorien. An unnatural and rather deep ditch opens up in the north. Climbing down there could probably cause a couple of bruises. The ground is fairly dry, resembling the barren lands south and east of the small coppice, except for the thickening forest west, where a couple of muddy pools can be seen.
16994:
A large eagle soars above you.
A sand viper is slithering here on the ground.

These fields end abruptly at a wall of trees and tangled bushes. Looking north and south one could get the feeling of being in two places at the same time. The southern fields seem to have no end in sight and no hill or grove hinders your view of the horizon. Turning north, one can witness a seemingly impenetrable forest that might perhaps be accessed through the western coppice.
16995: A small grasshopper clings to a blade of grass, ready to spring.

The ground here is firm and dry. Though the forest is sparse, to the north it thickens. The ground between the trees is littered with grass and several saplings struggling in the shade. The vast plains of Lorien can be seen to the south where they extend as far as the eye can see.
16996: This is the edge of the great forest of Lorien. The trees stand slightly apart, allowing easy passage between them. In all directions, except south where the plains dominate, the trees thicken as the massive forest takes shape.
16997: The trees that sparsely populate this section of the forest stand tall and proud, towering high above. Noises from the forest wildlife can be heard emanating from the rich undergrowth below and tree-tops above. While the forest continues in all directions, it rapidly thins to the south and east where the land has transformed into wide rolling plains.
16998: A small grasshopper clings to a blade of grass, ready to spring.

Unlike the region to the north and west, this land is dry and infertile. While a few trees have sprouted here over the years, those that have not withered in the inhospitable soil are little larger than small shrubs despite many years of growth. Between the few trees that continue to struggle, a tough hardy grass has taken root. To the south the plains become more fruitful while to the north and west a rich forest extends.
16999: This area is the bottom of a large bowl, for in all directions the ground slopes gently upwards. The rich soil allows the few shrubs that choose to grow here to become lush and verdant. Far to the north is a very large dense forest, while in all other directions nothing but plains can be seen from here to the horizon.
17000: A small grasshopper clings to a blade of grass, ready to spring.

A small brook runs north to south, making little noise as it flows over the small pebbles and rocks that obstruct its path. The footprints of many small creatures and of a few large ones can be seen along the path of the brook. Looking across the brook, nothing but the spanning plains can be seen.
17001: Fresh, invigorating air flows across these plains as they extend in all directions, slowly merging with the horizon. Long grasses grow all around interspersed by a few small but hearty bushes. To the far east a small hill is clearly visible against the skyline. While this hill is little more than a small mound, on the otherwise flat plains it appears to be the only major landmark in the neighbouring area.
17002: The only feature which distinguishes this area from the surrounding regions is the slope to the east that leads to the top of a mound. From the top of the mound there is a wide, panoramic view of the undulating plains which extend south of Lorien.
17003: This hilltop allows clear vision in all directions, even though there is not much except for the undulating fields to be seen for as far as one can see. The ground around you is covered with small sharp stones that make passage difficult for a barefoot traveller. Some larger boulders rise from the ground here and there, half-hidden by the tall grass.
17004: This is a region of rich, fruitful grassland that supports a large variety of plants and shrubs. To the west the terrain slopes gently up towards the top of a small hill. In all the other directions the vast grasslands disappear into the distance.
17005: Grass dominates these plains, its even cover sometimes broken by a lonely shrub or a cluster of bushes. A small hill rises above the plains to the north, contrasting sharply with the seemingly endless flatlands that continue in all other directions.
17006: Grasslands continue in all directions except to the northwest, where a small hill can be made out in the distance. To the east the grass appears to be thinner and somewhat trampled. The sweet fragrance of flowers and leaves wafts in hazily from the north where the forest of Lothlorien lies.
17007: The grass is worn and trampled here, as this spot is obviously a part of a migration route for the local wildlife. The animal route continues to the south and east, while more grasslands can be seen to the north and west. The land is very flat here, providing little cover from the predators, and yet wildlife seems to prosper in this area.
17008: A brown fox is here, looking for some rabbits to chew up.

Several small bushes and other low lying vegetation can be seen among the wild and lush grasses of these plains. Many animals or travellers seem to have passed here, causing many trampled and worn spots in the grass. The path of trampled grass continues to the east and west.
17009: A sheer rock wall, fashioned over thousands of years by the climate, blocks passage to the north here, providing shelter for many insects and possibly also small animals in its nooks and crannies. A small ruin can be seen to the east. A path meanders its way through the grasslands to the south and west.
17010:
A cluster of white star-shaped forget-me-nots flourish here in reminiscence.
A snake slithers towards you.

An ancient ruin of a stone building stands here. The remainders of the walls and the floor are overgrown with grass and trailing plants, but in the centre of the ruin nothing grows. To the north, the great forest of Lothlorien can be seen in the distance. The grasslands extend in all directions.
17011: A small stand of trees grows here. The trees look almost as if they were envious of the breathtaking forest of Lothlorien to the north. In the centre of the stand of trees a grassy clearing houses a small pond, the watering place for local wildlife and a source of drinking water for a traveller through these lush grasslands.
17012:
Elemmire the Elf (el), wielding a double edged eket, is here, riding a pony driven by you.
A pony is standing here, ridden by you and Elemmire (el).

The air is full of all kinds of sounds, as small animals and birds go about their ways, uninhibited by travellers through these lands. A small stand of trees can be seen to the west, dwarfed by the large forest to the north. Plains dominate the view in all directions, but to the east the grass appears to grow less vigorously.
17013: A pack horse is standing here, ridden by you.

A small, animal-made path runs north and south here. There are many tracks leading in other directions as well, as the area's residents passed here searching for food, water and shelter. Grasslands continue in all directions. In the north, the great forest of Lothlorien looms in the distance.
17014:
Elemmire the Elf (el), wielding a double edged eket, is here, riding a pony driven by you.
A pony is standing here, ridden by you and Elemmire (el).

This vast grassy plain is apparently home to many different types of creatures. Animal tracks and holes in the ground are everywhere. Small areas of foliage and trees can be seen here and there, providing sustenance and homes for small and large animals alike, as well as rest for the weary traveller. Many animal tracks lead west of here.
17015:
A large rabbit looks peacefully at you, ready to dart away.
A large rabbit looks peacefully at you, ready to dart away.
Elemmire the Elf (el), wielding a double edged eket, is here, riding a pony driven by you.
A pony is standing here, ridden by you and Elemmire (el).

At this spot it is very quiet, and even the sound the withering grass creates underfoot sounds very noisy. There is something oppressive in the air, as if no sound is welcome here. Nothing seems to be moving in the lands surrounding you, and a complete stillness prevails.
17016:
Elemmire the Elf (el), wielding a double edged eket, is here, riding a pony driven by you.
A pony is standing here, ridden by you and Elemmire (el).

The ground drops here, forming a low depression where the vegetation seems a little healthier than in the surrounding plains. Various bushes grow densely at the bottom of the hollow, but in the shadow below them the vegetation is not as rich, and the roots of the bushes dominate the ground area. The depression appears to provide home for a few small animals as well.
17017:
Elemmire the Elf (el), wielding a double edged eket, is here, riding a pony driven by you.
A pony is standing here, ridden by you and Elemmire (el).

Gently rolling the landscape goes on, the carpet of grass following the contours of the soil. Gusts of wind come and go, keeping the grass slowly moving all the time. Luckily the winds are not very strong here as the low shrubbery would not provide much of a shelter.
17018:
A cluster of dark green, feathery fronds flourishes in the shade.
Elemmire the Elf (el), wielding a double edged eket, is here, riding a pony driven by you.
A pony is standing here, ridden by you and Elemmire (el).

These grasslands seem less inviting than those to the west, the ground becoming cracked and parched. The winds gust around the small, dwarfed bushes and shrubs, biting at the land as well as any who might be travelling upon it. The barren lands continue in all directions except west.
17019: This seemingly lifeless slope falls slowly to the east, while climbing wearily to the west. The sides of the sloping ground have been blasted by the wind for so long that they are all but bare, yet small patches of life do exist here and there.
17020: A field vole has frozen to the spot, sensitive to your presence.

The ground slopes steadily downwards to the east, providing a good view of the lands in that direction. The soil here is generally worn and crumbled, however patches of somewhat fertile soil can still be seen. A dusty path runs through the landscape north from here, descending to a small valley in the northeast.
17021: A field vole has frozen to the spot, sensitive to your presence.

The dry channel wanders north-south here through this small valley. The ground rises gently to the north and west. The bottom of the streambed is sandy and dry and the banks mostly crumbled. Northwards the channel becomes even more shallow, and there seems to be an old trail crossing it.
17033: An old, dusty path cuts east-west through this barren landscape. The path is faint and worn, but still easily followed. To the east it dives into a shallow valley; there seems to be a dry channel of a stream running through the valley floor. Some old buildings can be seen to the east as well, but the valley seems completely deserted.
17034: Yellow flowers, with grey-green foliage, grow in clusters here.

Some isolated greenery attempts to eke out a meagre existence on this shallow slope but most of the area is brown and solemn, wind-beaten over many years. A small path can be seen at the base of the slope to the east, while barren grasslands can be found in all other directions.
17035: The bare, lifeless plain stretches out, the yellow-brown colour of the soil blending with the green, grassy spots. Only the wind is not afraid of this harsh environment; it is a frequent visitor. Plains continue in all directions.
17036:
Prickly, white-stemmed plants, with blue flower heads grow in abundance.
A grey wolf is here, thin from starvation.
A grey wolf is here, thin from starvation.

Not much breaks the peace of these monotonous, quiet grasslands. An occasional bird can be seen circling in the sky but there are no other signs of wildlife. In the north a broad, dark green belt of shrubbery can be seen cutting through the bland grasslands.
17037: A swallow flies high above the ground.

Some faint paths can be seen criss-crossing the grass here, made by the small animals which live in this wilderness, and every now and then something can be seen scurrying through the foot-long grass. The grasslands stretch out in all directions. To the south, the ground appears to drop to form a hollow.
17038: A swallow flies high above the ground.

The land rolls gently upwards from the low basins, where the ground is a little softer and the vegetation richer, to the bare hilltops, which provide a monotonous view: immense grasslands continue in all directions. A variety of grasses and plants grow here, but no wildlife is to be seen.
17039: The grass is very lush here due to the plentiful rainfall and healthy soil in the region. Most of the wildlife seems to focus their attention on the area of trampled soil and grass north and west of here. To the east, south and west, plains extend to the very horizon, while the forest of Lothlorien can be seen far to the north.
17040: The soft soil and lush green grass is trampled from the passage of many animals, possibly on their way to feeding or water. Many animal tracks can be seen heading south into the plains and north towards the forest. To the east and west the land is less trampled and the plains continue as a seemingly endless flow of green grass.
17041: The fertile ground of these plains is covered with lush grass and large bushes. A few trees can be seen standing proudly alone, stretching their branches to the sky. The forest of Lothlorien gleams in the north, its glory but a distant memory. Yet while the forest scents are light in the air here, the presence of the Golden Wood can still be felt drawing the wanderer towards its eaves. More plains can be seen in all directions. The land to the east looks well travelled.
17042: Rich grasslands cover the land here, stretching out in every direction. Only occasional bushes and a few scattered trees try to break the domination of the grass. The forest of Lothlorien can be seen to the north, towering to the sky. A gentle golden glow seems to emanate from the treetops. At a distance to the south a small group of trees can be seen.
17043: The forest reaches high into the sky, inspiring awe even in the travellers looking at it from aside. The sounds of creatures scurrying through the tall grasses indicate that there is an abundance of life here. Small bushes dot the grassland, providing sustenance to many of the local inhabitants.
17044: A brown fox is here, looking for some rabbits to chew up.

Majestic in its appearance, the light forest on the outskirts of Lothlorien rises in the north, obscuring most of the sky with its array of foliage. Vast plains stretch out to the east and west, covered with a rich carpet of green. To the south the land drops abruptly. The only way in that direction would be down a nearly vertical cliff wall which appears impossible to scale if you cannot fly.
17045: The plains are dotted by low trees, mere saplings compared to their brothers and sisters in the majestic forest to the north. Although the forest of Lothlorien is miles away, the air is sweet with the fragrance of its trees. The grassland continues in every direction but to the north, where a huge fire burned away everything up to the forest border.
17046: The plains continue in all directions. The soft ground is lined by lush, rich grasses. Scattered among the plains, occasional tall trees proudly reach for the sky. Small ponds and pools dot the area. To the south, the grass appears to be slightly trampled.
17047: A brown fox is here, looking for some rabbits to chew up.

The flatlands seem to continue endlessly to the east and south. To the west, however, a small hill rises above the landscape, its sight unusual amidst these level lowlands where even the smallest elevation acts as a landmark. Far to the north a forest can be seen, its tall trees stretching up towards the sky.
17048: A small hill rises from the surrounding plains here. Short tussocks of grass grow upon its top, making it look almost comical. From here one can see across vast miles of plains in any direction. The ground on the top of the hill seems somewhat downtrodden, and large footprints can be made out in the soil near the top.
17049: Many plants and grasses thrive upon the moist soil of this fertile land. Numerous small flowers, as well as a few larger ones, often sprout here during the spring, filling the land with an abundance of colour. In all directions one could watch the vast plains roll on endlessly. A small hill to the east breaks the monotony of this otherwise dull landscape.
17050: Here the ground is moist and fertile. To the south a small hill rises above the surrounding land, however the slope directly south is far too steep to ascend to the top. Perhaps the top can be reached from the west or east where the slopes are less steep.
17051: A few small trees dot the landscape in this otherwise featureless terrain. For many miles around in all directions nothing can be seen across a stretch of barren plains. The sheer vastness of this area could make one feel small and insignificant. To the north and west, at the tip of the horizon, the brown shade of a forest can be seen.
17052: A clear spring babbles as cool water trickles out of the ground.

A thick carpet of grass spreads across the soil of these fertile plains. A number of small shrubs and bushes dot the landscape, none of them tall enough to be visible from a substantial distance where they appear to merge into the grassy landscape. The air smells pure and unpolluted as does the water of a spring that emerges from the firm ground. A small brook is formed as the spring drains westwards.
17053: Plains at the Edge of a Forest

The ground here is dampened by the water of a small creek that runs from the east to south. The creek's waters are crystal clear and flow almost silently over the small pebbles in its path. The Lorien plains extend in all directions from here except to the north where the beginnings of a mighty forest can be seen.
17054: Plains at the Edge of a Forest

Many different grasses and shrubs thrive upon these plains. A couple of trees have also managed to sprout in the rich soil. The boundary of the forest of Lorien can be seen to the north and west. To the south the ground dips forming a shallow bowl.
17055: Here the forest is fairly thin and the spaces between the trees allow clear vision in all directions. To the north and west more woodlands are visible, while to the south and east the rolling plains of Lorien extend seemingly forever.
17056: The terrain around you is lightly wooded. Most of the trees in the immediate area are elms, though a few maples and an occasional oak can also be found here. The ground is littered with small saplings struggling in the shadow of the older trees. While the forest continues in all directions, it thins out towards the south.
17057: A partridge attempts to hide in the undergrowth.

Many trees and smaller plants thrive in the rich, fertile forest soil that is found here. Sounds of small insects can be heard, as they move about unaware of the sheer size of the huge forest they occupy. The trees become less dense towards the east and south.
17058: The large number of trees growing in this area provide a rich food source and shelter for many of the small woodland animals. Any travellers who happen to venture this deep into the forest would find it difficult to make their way through the thick roots that swell out of the ground. In all directions the vast forest continues, obscuring your vision.
17059:
A brown bear is sleeping here.
A green frog is here, hopping around.
A black wolf pads restlessly, looking for its next prey.
A black wolf pads restlessly, looking for its next prey.
A wolf cub happily plays here.

Thick moss covers all the rocks and infrequent fallen trees as well as willows and birches stretching their branches up toward daily sunlight. The undergrowth is quite thick and makes progressing in any direction tiresome. This is probably the way it has been for countless years already, and if allowed it will stay this way for countless years to come. A few fallen trees to the south make it impossible to continue in that direction.
17060:
A low shrub with bright green, oblong leaves is growing here.
A black wolf pads restlessly, looking for its next prey.

Recent land shifts or the work of some powerful minions have caused the ground to be torn apart here, revealing a deep ditch. Like a wound that turned into a scar, the soil is now covered with lush grass and bushes, some of them perhaps yielding edible berries.
17061:
A black wolf pads restlessly, looking for its next prey.
A huge, black wolf is here, ready to devour.

To the north and west the forest gets thicker, while to the east the ground slopes downward, marking the beginning of a deep ditch. Respectively, the undergrowth seems to become more rank and the soil damper in that direction. Animal noises coming from the east suggest that some of the dwellers of this wooded realm might not be friendly at all.
17062: A black wolf pads restlessly, looking for its next prey.

The forest grows extremely dense, making it impossible to continue north or south. One must be cautious to avoid getting tangled in thick undergrowth or waving branches overhead. The obstruction north bears marks of an axe or some other sharp blade, but in other ways it completely resembles piled trunks and entwined branches placed there by elven-folk or nature itself - some might wonder if there is a difference.
17063: A rabbit is here eyeing your presence warily.

A faint path leads you amidst tall trees, bushes and plants of different varieties. This area is quite a contrast to the southern barren lands, as if the forest was drawing upon some magical power of the land. Looking east and west, one can see no other entrance to the forest. The path bears signs of both light feet and hoofs, trodden equally by elves and animals.
17064: A brown fox is here, looking for some rabbits to chew up.

Although one might decide from the scanty nature of this part of the forest that this is its southern edge, a thick wall of entwined bushes obstructs your way to the south. The ground is covered with small twigs and half-rotten leaves from sparsely growing birches and with thorns and cones from pine trees. To the west there seems to be a clearing, in all the other directions the forest continues.
17065:
A small animal, all covered in spines, snuffles amongst the undergrowth.
A fallow deer is grazing peacefully here.
A fallow deer is grazing peacefully here.
A nightingale is here, chirping a sweet melody.

Birches and golden mallorn-trees stretch their boughs towards the sky. The soft wet ground is covered by an assortment of undergrowth. Lush ferns make it hard for a traveller to mind his step, because one can see the ground only by pushing the tall plants apart. You can spot the plants moving here and there, indicating busy wildlife underneath.
17066: A brown fox is here, looking for some rabbits to chew up.

The ground here is quite marshy, being fertile and containing excellent soil for the ferns that keep most of the local wildlife under a secretive green carpet, penetrated only by a few bushes. The white, black-dashed bark of tall birches and the silver bark of the mellyrn is enlivened by their green and golden crowns. A sound of flowing water comes from the north.
17067: As the terrain varies, so does the vegetation. Here begins a sea of ferns that extends westward where everything is covered by these thick green plants. The southern forest mostly consists of conifers and smaller bushes, due to its greater distance from the river, which one can hear flowing north of here. A faint footpath seems to lead east, where an enormous mallorn-tree aspires towards the sky.
17068:
An elven archer dressed in green is here, watching the forest.
A long-tailed bird watches you from the vegetation.

Busy feet have trampled the lush grass into a soft lawn under this mighty tree which could support the weight of numerous animals and even of houses that local elves are rumoured to construct in the crowns of sturdy mellyrn. This very tree may have witnessed generations of elves and their few but honoured guests smile and grieve, laugh and mourn to the joys and sorrows of Lothlorien.
17069:
A saddlecloth lies here on the ground.
A beautiful and docile horse is standing here.

Much like rumours describe the elven tree-houses, this barn is built using what nature provides, yet simpler and more robust, considering the needs of its occupants. The soil is trampled by hoofs, and fresh hay and oats have been laid where animals eat. Bridles, stirrups and other riding equipment on the walls suggest that nearby dwellers are used to taking longer trips out of the forest.
17070: Looking north and south, one can see the difference in the surrounding forest. The more north, the less nature is afflicted by the intrusion of barrenness. Whereas the trees to the south are of more common varieties seen in other parts of Arda, the northern forest glows golden. To the west, the path is obstructed by a wall of a building, while a similar but natural wall prevents one from going east; yet no building exists in that direction.
17071: The mother wolf stands here, protecting her young cubs.

This is a somewhat concealed lair, surrounded by natural piles of fallen trees and entwined bushes. It must be the favourite breeding place for the wolves of this forest. Branches and twigs have been carefully laid on the ground and covered with leaves; these crude beds are surrounded by teeth-marked bones.
17072: A huge, black wolf is here, ready to devour.

Mighty trees aspire skyward, while smaller bushes and undergrowth balance the sight of the beautiful forest. Several trees differ from the more ordinary ones by their silvery grey trunks and golden crowns. The howling of wolves might scare off the faint-hearted, but the forest seems to absorb some of the threatening calls of these beasts. From the north, the soft murmur of flowing water can be heard.
17073: Mighty trees aspire skyward, while smaller bushes and undergrowth balance the sight of the beautiful forest. Looking north and south, one can see the difference in the surroundings. While the southern trees are of a more common kind that can be seen in other parts of Arda, the northern forest glows golden. From the south, occasional howls of wolves can be heard.
17074: A long-tailed bird watches you from the vegetation.

The trees that populate this area are mostly mellyrn, though other types of trees, most of them shorter, grow here as well. Far to the north the sounds of a river can be heard. In all directions the dense forest extends, inhibiting the vision of even those with the keenest eyesight.
17075: Here, deep in the forest, the trees are very tall. The long branches spread out from the trees, forming a canopy over the forest floor. The ground, soft and fertile, is covered by a carpet of green moss. Sounds of small animals and insects can be heard both near and far.
17076: A woodpecker is here, tapping on a tree.

In this part of the forest the trees are of many different shapes and sizes. They range from the small fruit-bearing varieties, some of which are little more than a large bush, to the mighty elms which have towering trunks and spidery branches. While the forest continues in all directions, it thins towards the south.
17077: The trees that surround you are tall and majestic. A few trees have been set off from the others by a series of gaps. These trees form a circle around a central tree that towers high above all others. To the south and east the forest becomes less dense. At a distance to the south the vast plains of Lorien are faintly visible.
17078: A small animal, all covered in spines, snuffles amongst the undergrowth.

Large gaps between the trees in this part of the forest allow for good vision. Noises of many small forest animals can be heard from all directions. To the north the forest becomes much more dense while to the south it thins until it eventually fades into an open plain.
17079: A long-tailed bird watches you from the vegetation.

Here the forest is sparsely populated yet long ago, before a number of trees in this area withered and died, it was quite thick. The shade from those trees that did survive has made it difficult for new trees to sprout and grow. To the south and east the land opens out into the vast plains of Lorien, while to the west and north the forest thickens.
17080: Plains at the Edge of a Forest

The forest to the north is enormous and encompasses the land for many miles to the east and west as well as to the north. While the few trees that grow here are relatively small both in height and girth compared to the mellyrn that can be found deep inside the wooded area, they are still quite impressive compared to the trees of the other forests. Looking towards the south the plains which border this area continue until they join the horizon.
17081: Plains at the Edge of a Forest

A few sickly blades of grass can be found growing between the stones that litter the ground. A large pile of rocks has been placed under the largest of the trees that grow here at the edge of the forest. To the north the woods become denser as the forest begins in earnest, while to the south and east the fields seem to roll forever. The trees to the west also become denser as they merge with the large forest.
17082: The ground is quite moist and covered by a dense layer of tall grass. A lonely tall tree with thick bark towers overhead and is singular on these vast, deserted plains. In the distance, far to the north, an immense forested area spreads across the land.
17083: Clumps of brittle green grass provide a stark contrast to the otherwise dry, dusty soil that dominates this section of the plains of Lorien. A forest is visible far to the north, while in all other directions the plains seem to roll on endlessly. Farther to the south the land becomes less dusty as well as less sparsely populated by the grasses.
17084: The plains continue in every direction but to the north, where a forest can be seen in the distance. The ground appears to be less firm in that direction, perhaps due to the small streams or other sources of water that nourish the trees and the lush forest undergrowth.
17085: A few scattered tall trees and smaller bushes, interspersed with other types of flora, complement the lush grass bed. Grasslands stretch out in all directions, except to the north, where the outskirts of the magnificent forest of Lothlorien can be seen in the distance.
17086: Lush grass grows vigorously here. It is teeming with life, moving like a living carpet in the wilderness. Here and there beautiful flowers grow in small clusters or all alone. The majestic forest of Lothlorien lies to the north, its heady scents lingering in the fresh air.
17087: Some time ago a large fire burned away everything living here. Yet when it reached the border of Lothlorien, its life appears to have been sucked away, judging by the distinct boundary between the scorched plains and the grassland. Dense underbrush makes passage north into the forest impossible, although entry to the east is possible. Plains can be found to the south and west.
17088: The trees here are smaller and more sparsely placed than their cousins to the north. The ground is slightly damp due to the wetlands to the west and south; a damp woody smell hangs in the air. In the distant north a faint glimmer of mellyrn can be seen, a reminder of the beauty found not so far from here.
17089: A large rabbit looks peacefully at you, ready to dart away.

The large trees grow sparse here as the forest comes to an end, giving way to plains to the south and east. Although less impressive than their kind to the north, these trees are still awe-inspiring, and much larger than the trees of the other forests. The ground is slightly damp here.
17090: Leaving the cover of the forest, the plains stretch out into the open lands south of Lothlorien. The ground is somewhat wet, allowing one to see the footprints of occasional animals distinctly. The vast plains continue to the east and south. The forest lies to the north and west.
17091: Vigorously growing grass covers the plains. Many rocks are scattered across the grass bed; some of the rocks are quite big and it is not clear how they got here. Plains stretch out in all directions, reaching the edge of the forest to the north. The scent of mellyrn drifts hazily in from the north, drawing the senses closer to the beauty and awe of Lothlorien.
17092: The grass here is trampled down and matted into a natural pathway. Winding through the plains, the path leads east and south. The majestic forest of Lothlorien can be seen to the north. Plains continue in all directions.
17093: A brown fox is here, looking for some rabbits to chew up.

Scattered trees and bushes can be seen here and there, growing larger and closer to each other in the north and almost disappearing to the south. The grass is matted down as if many large animals regularly pass this way. One can only surmise that food or water is plentiful in this region.
17094: The soft brushwood blends into the low grass, and southwards the vegetation thins out. Except for the shadowy forest in the north, not much breaks the horizon here. The vast plains seem lifeless, yet you can make out faint tracks in the dusty ground, indicating that some small wildlife actually thrives here.
17095: A green carpet of grass prevails here, only challenged by an occasional tree. The trees are of a low, persistent type with dry, twisting branches and small dark leaves, adapted to survive in harsh conditions. To the north the edge of the forest towers, dominating the horizon.
17096: The belt of shrubbery grows sparsely here, and it is not necessary to push through the bushes. Occasionally small animals can be heard prowling among the undergrowth through the bush roots, probably looking for food. Northwards the shrubbery becomes more dense.
17097: Something has burned down a large area of shrubbery here, revealing the bare, sandy soil. Pitch black, partly burned branches lie everywhere and pieces of wood litter the ground. What has caused the destruction is not apparent; possibly the shrubbery has been set on fire by lightning.
17098: This secluded hollow is well protected from the wind and grows many kinds of plants. Near the bottom of the hollow lie some square-shaped stony formations which seem man-made, though very old. They are completely overgrown and covered in moss, but seem too regular to be natural. Possibly they are remains of a house which has once stood here, for they look like foundations of a building.
17099:
A low shrub with bright green, oblong leaves is growing here.
Scattered in and on the shrub, there are three piles of blueberries.

A row of bushes grows here lining the old path which cuts through the hillside, dropping towards the bottom of a shallow valley to the south. Here the valley walls are not high, and have probably once been used for cultivation. Now only grass prevails on them, and the whole settlement of the valley is but a half-forgotten memory.
17104: A large thorny branched shrub is growing here.

You are in the middle of a patch of thorny brambles that grab at your arms and legs as you move. Some black berries grow among the thorns. Small animals could take refuge here with little change of being seen, let alone caught. You cannot see far and have lost all sense of direction. The smell of animal droppings does little to help you in this respect.
17109: A swallow flies high above the ground.

Clumps of short bushes dominate the landscape here. Far to the east and west this wide belt of brushland extends. The bushes are of the kind which thrives in these dry conditions; the long, tangled branches are protected by sharp thorns. Only stunted grass and brambles grow amidst the thorny bushes.
17112:
A small evergreen plant grows here, its woody stems reaching two feet.
A field vole has frozen to the spot, sensitive to your presence.

Between the forest in the north and the line of bushes in the south this wide, open field grows mostly grass and low shrubbery. The ground is even and easy to travel over. A small path winds its way to the north, picking its way through the vegetation.
17113: Prickly, white-stemmed plants, with blue flower heads grow in abundance.

Lush, green grasses flow smoothly across the land, providing a carpet of habitation for the creatures of the area. The heady scent of the forest to the north floats occasionally through the air, drawing one's spirit towards the trees' leafy canopy.
17114: A clean fragrance drifts up from a thick clump of leaves.

A sparse belt of shrubbery runs here, following the border of the mighty Golden Wood which lies to the north. The air here is fresh and the wind carries a sweet, inviting scent from the depths of the forest. The ground is uneven, as the wide roots of the bushes spread all around.
17115: A swallow flies high above the ground.

The trees lie sparsely here while other vegetation prevails. A dense layer of green, narrow-leaved bushes grows here. Trodding through the carpet of shrubbery would leave clear tracks but the brush seems to mould and reform quickly, leaving little evidence of passage through it.
17116: Though the trees grow more sparsely here than to the north the underbrush is thick and soft, almost sinking under your weight. The visibility to the south is good and although the grasslands are level here, the shapes of hills and valleys are evident in the distance.
17117: A grey wolf is here, snarling aggressively.

Among the low, soft carpet of brushwood an occasional tree rises from the green sea of grass. The trees here on the eaves of the forest seem less healthy than those in the north; round clumps of fungi grow on them and they are lower and more twisted. Southwards the trees disappear completely, giving way to the rolling plains which begin here at the edge of Lorien and continue for miles to the south.
17118: A few trees grow here, their branches dancing merrily in the wind. The trees appear to bend slightly north, as if they could sense the fresh scent of Lothlorien and wished to get closer to the eaves of the great wood. Plains can be seen to the south and west. The sparsely growing trees continue to the east.
17119: The spacious plains open up, leaving a great forest to the north. Small bushes and lesser trees mark the border of the forest. The flat terrain seems to stretch endlessly into the southern horizon. The sweet scent of the forest is still in the air, a gentle reminder of the beauty of the mellyrn of Lothlorien.
17120: The ground here is somewhat wet, the moisture apparently due to the forest that rises to the north and west. The array of rocks and trees to the north seems impassable. Quite a few footprints can be seen in the soft ground by the rocks, leading west into the forest. The footprints appear to have been made by an orc war party. The plains continue to the east and south.
17121: The mellyrn here are not as numerous as to the north, yet their presence is quite visible for they are the source of a faint golden radiance that permeates the air. The forest ends to the south, giving way to vast plains that appear very fertile. The soft ground shows many footprints left by what might have been a war party of some sort. The tracks lead north into the forest and disappear there.
17122: A dense blanket of leaves blocks most of the sky here. Nonetheless, the forest is very light. The soft ground below the magnificent mellyrn reveals many footprints of forest dwellers that passed here. The forest continues in all directions, growing in density to the north. The presence of something watching this forest is quite obvious, but nothing can be seen; it is more like a feeling.
17123:
An erect shrub with green pinnate leaves is growing here.
A brown fox is here, looking for some rabbits to chew up.

The majestic, tall trees seem to keep a close, silent watch on this forest. A peaceful feeling is in the air, as though no evil could abide in this place for long. Small bushes can be seen growing beside the trees. The branches of the bushes are covered with an assortment of wild berries.
17124: A squirrel scampers around here, looking for nuts from the trees.

Covering the sky above with leafy branches, the trees seem to sway back and forth with the wind, slowly singing a song without words. A small forest path can be seen to the north; the trees gently embrace it as it winds through the forest. More woodlands lie to the east and west. Dense underbrush makes southern passage impossible.
17125: A small path starts here and runs north through the forest. Branches of pines and firs overhang the path. The air below them is scented with resin dripping down from their tips. Alongside the path, below two closely standing trees, remains of what appears to have been a tree-house lie shattered on the ground. At first glance the rubble seems to be just a pile of broken wooden planks.
17126: A fallow deer is grazing peacefully here.

Less magnificent than their counterparts to the north, the trees here are nonetheless almost breathtaking. The sweet scent of firs and pines fills the air. To the north, a small clearing in the forest can be seen, beyond which rises a stand of mellyrn. Plains lie to the south and west, while the forest continues to the north and east.
17127: A light grass dusts the ground of the plains here, slightly damp from the increased moisture in the area where the plains gradually turn into forest. To the east and north large trees can be seen rising above the landscape, majestically spanning the sky. The plains continue to the south, where the ground starts to become firmer.
17128: Wavy grass covers much of the ground, interspersed by a few small shrubs. At some distance to the west and to the north the beginnings of a large forest can be seen. A few scrappy trees struggle in the poor soil along the southern border of the forest. Rolling softly, the plains gently rise and fall to the south and southeast for as far as one can see.
17129: This entire area is covered by a thicket of some tall grassy plants that thrive in the moist soft soil. The ground is level and there are no landmarks except a pile of old-looking mossy stones that sits beside a particularly thick clump of grass. From the condition of the stones, it appears that they have probably been undisturbed for many years. To the north lies the edge of a very large forested area teeming with all kinds of plant life.
17130: A number of large trees surround you, many towering high over your head. A few smaller trees, little more than saplings, can be seen as well, as they strive to grow in the moist soil. The forest continues to the north and west, but to the south the vast rolling plains start and continue until they merge with the horizon.
17131: A nightingale is here, chirping a sweet melody.

The trees here are tall and majestic although the forest here is less dense than in the surrounding areas, allowing for a good view of the immediate surroundings. The wooded area continues to the north, east and west, while to the south lie the vast and empty plains of Lorien which extend as far as one can see. While the plains are fertile only occasional mounds, which appear to be little more than drifts in the otherwise flat soil, provide useful landmarks in the level terrain.
17132: Crumbled Boulder in a Dense Forest
A woodpecker is here, tapping on a tree.

An ancient crumbled boulder stands here. Set in this place by the powers of the world, it may have originated during the First Age when the first Elves were awoken by the will of Eru. A slender young tree has recently penetrated the stone and sprung forth with a natural beauty.
17133: A small animal, all covered in spines, snuffles amongst the undergrowth.

Under these tall fir trees, where sun seldom shines, a fluffy green moss flourishes. The firs' trunks are moss-covered and grey from age and harsh weather. Tiny trails, made by various animals, can be seen criss-crossing among the trees. A small clearing can be found north of here, where the trees become shorter and more sparse.
17134:
A clear spring babbles as cool water trickles out of the ground.
A colony of red ants is here. The ants seem to ignore you.

On this grassy slope fir trees grow among the tall grey-barked trees producing a stunning contrast of bright and dull greens. On the ground a few small mounds form the homes for the many tiny ants which are busy building their underground tunnels. A small spring babbles nearby emitting refreshing water from the soft earth. To the west a small bushy mound, which appears to be a mountain when compared to the ants' mounds, rises from the ground. The forest continues endlessly in all directions.
17135: A group of silvery-barked trees grows upon a small moss-covered mound. Their tall trunks cast long shadows across the ground that is covered with grass, bushes and tiny flowers. While to the north the mallorn forest continues uninterrupted, to the east and south it thins out as the mellyrn mix with other trees.
17136: Fed by the waters of the river Celebrant, the mellyrn have grown tall here and given seed to many saplings. Occasionally birds sing among the tree-brances. Beyond the silvery boles a bend in the river can be seen where the rapid current changes direction as it hurries away from its source in the east towards the north. From here several tiny animal trails can be seen leading southwards and westwards into the forest.
17137: A squirrel scampers around here, looking for nuts from the trees.

The forest extends in all directions except north, where the greenish water of the river Celebrant flows eastward. Slender trees arch towards the river, their dewy leaves showing a soft glimmer. While few strands of green grass have managed to grow in the rich soil, many new saplings of the mallorn-trees vigorously reach toward the sky.
17138: At the Shore of the Celebrant

A huge, black wolf is here, ready to devour.
A black wolf pads restlessly, looking for its next prey.

The foliage of mellyrn is reflected in endless shades of gold in the pearly waters north of here. Every drop of Celebrant rushes the journey east once, yet united they can tell tales of joys and sorrows from the source of the first mountain stream to the never-ending seas. To the west, the riverbank seems to get marshier and to the south the forest deepens.
17139: A tall silvery plant grows here, surrounded by mist.

Much like the steep shore on the other side of the waters that flow north of here, this riverbank is covered with golden mellyrn. A small underground stream seems to emerge here and contribute to the glimmering waters of the beautiful Celebrant. Soft tussocks reveal tracks of some large and relatively heavy animals that must have come here to quench their thirst. Judging by occasional howls coming from the southern forest, the beasts might not be far.
17140: Clusters of slender stems and tall leaves thrive in the mud and shallows.

The muddy riverbank is covered with reeds. To keep from getting wet, one would have to jump from tussock to tussock. Trying to ride here would be folly and might result in a mount with broken bones. A natural ladder formed by tangled roots can be spotted hanging above the river to the north. In all other directions the golden forest echoes chirping of birds. To the south, fallen trunks have piled into a natural obstruction.
17141: Clusters of slender stems and tall leaves thrive in the mud and shallows.

The riverbank is muddy and covered with reeds, which skilled hands might make into light boats suitable for travelling on shallow rivers that require covering some rapids by foot. Such troublesome waters can be seen to the north. In all the other directions the golden forest echoes chirping of birds.
17142: Golden trees give way to what appears to be a beautiful meadow, where local folk used to gather around fires to pass news and stories of great heroes and their deeds. In less troublesome times the surrounding mallorn-trees would echo merry songs and joyful laughter, though there is no doubt that some elves would prefer to gaze silently into flickering fire and think of the great and safe western realms of their kinsfolk.
17143:
A light boat made of reeds has been left here.
A fishing net has been left here.

Formed by a mossy fallen tree, this pier extends into the River Celebrant. It may be here that elven fishermen sometimes cast their lines, providing nourishment for their families. The tree branches have dug deep into the river-bottom, preventing the trunk from rolling over. To the north, below the pier, one can see the waters flowing eastwards. In all the other directions the golden forest continues. A faint trail leads south from the pier.
17144: East of the Gracefully Arching Tree

Wisps of fog escape from the soft turf when tussocks yield, disturbed by travellers' passage. The River Celebrant that flows to the north dampens the soil here, giving the flora an exceptional lushness. Tall mallorn-trees with silvery trunks and golden foliage sparkle with unending brightness. To the west you see a graceful tree arching above the river.
17146: Delicate golden blooms adorn the ground like a cascade of stars.

Tall and proud, the trees here are ancient even by elven reckoning. Stepping into this forest amidst the wise silver trunks and softly swaying undergrowth it seems that you have entered a land free from the grasp of time. The majestic, golden-crowned mellyrn do not merely recall the Elder Days, but rather dwell in them still. To the north the woods grow impossibly dense, dazzling and confusing in their novel shape and colour. The occasional snowy-barked tree provides a stunning contrast to the vast sea of mellyrn.
17149:
A copper penny lies on the ground.
A sturdy pack horse is standing here.

The trees here are tall and tightly packed, limiting visibility in all directions. Oak, beech and other deciduous hardwoods intermix with several varieties of evergreen trees, which have liberally layered the hard dirt floor with a prickly carpet of dark green needles. Most notably the occasional gold and silver mallorn-tree sprouts from a small clearing in the forest, towering high above the less ancient and majestic plant-life. One of these mallorn-trees is exceptionally tall; its great crown rises high above the surrounding forest. The faint sound of running water is barely detectable from the northeast.
17150: Several blooms of snow-white and palest green cover the ground.

A glade of silver-barked mallorn-trees rises high upon the banks of the crystal clear Anduin, which flows away to the east. Each mallorn has a single, smooth trunk which gives way to a golden crown supported by broad, upswept limbs not unlike those of the beech. At ground level small snowdrop flowers lie scattered across the soft turf as if a brief flurry of florae had passed through. A single, white-barked tree grows in this woodland, beneath which lies a natural garden of pale, bell-shaped and tall, star-silver flowers.
17151: Delicate golden blooms adorn the ground like a cascade of stars.

This forest is inhabited exclusively by the ancient mellyrn native to Lothlorien. In contrast to the woodlands lying south and west, the wide-trunked trees here are well spaced, leaving room for flowers of myriad colours to flourish in the golden shade. To the north and east a wide, white-capped river flows swiftly away to the south; farther in this direction a heavily wooded ridge rises from water level and follows the Anduin's progress. Fair sounds of laughter and sweet song seem to drift by occasionally, but perhaps they are only illusions produced by the river's steady hum.
17152: A large thorny branched shrub is growing here.

This wooded rise protrudes into the wide, swift waters of the Anduin, which wrap around from north to east. The forest continues to the west, following an upward slope which culminates in lofty glades of a golden hue. Across the river in the northeast a wooded ridge runs for several miles on a north-south axis.
17153: The river flows deeply and swiftly between tree-topped riverbanks, emitting a smooth, low pitched murmur as it bends from north to east. Healthy green woodlands rise on the eastern and western shores; however their splendour is dwarfed by the magnificent golden forest visible to the south and far away to the west.
17154: These waters are wide and extremely clear, yet it would be difficult for even the most acute eyes to detect the rocky riverbed which lies far below the smooth surface. Massive grey boulders, rounded smooth by the flow through countless centuries, lie scattered and submerged near the western bank, as if mindlessly dropped there by some earth-hewing immortal of old. The crisp water flows over these boulders silently, creating dynamic arcs of blue and white.
17155: A narrow, dark grotto opens into the rocky depths of the stone face. Water filters in through countless crevices in the western wall in a slow but steady ebb and flow as on a tiny beach, but one with a shore of bare rock. The very waters of the Anduin seem to have carved the cavern whimsically throughout the years, forming angular walls that look like scarred faces. The ceiling is dotted with stalactites like outstretched fingers trying to touch the waters that flood the cave. The atmosphere is cool and very wet, and yet more pleasant than one would expect.
17156: Narrow and uneven, a natural passageway opens its way through the rock. It is somehow connected to the Great River and totally flooded with its cold waters. These do not remain utterly still; one can notice slight currents running in both directions. The tunnel takes a sharp bend here. Muffled echoes and a dim glimpse of light reach faintly from above. Northward the passage continues, shrouded in the deepest blackness.
17157: A large pale fish with bulbous eyes is swimming here.

Even in its broadest spots the tunnel is no more than a couple yards wide. At some places the walls of bare rock seem to stretch inward in sharp-edged projections, as if trying to hinder your passage, although never actually blocking it completely. The passage is plunged into utter darkness, but one can grope ones way along the enclosing walls. The narrow tunnel continues southward at the same level, but to the north it apparently turns upward.
17158:
An albino fish is swimming here, looking for some food.
An albino fish is swimming here, looking for some food.

You find yourself in a recondite grotto in the depths of the rocky ground. No sort of natural light can ever reach this secluded cave that lies shrouded in the thickest shadows. A small lake takes up most of the room in the cavern. Its waters, black like a moonless night, hardly show any sign of motion, as if frozen, or as though time had stopped long ago in this forsaken cave. At the far end of the cave, to the west, you can catch a glimpse of a dry corner rising slightly above the waters.
17159: At the Back of the Cavern
A crooked, long-armed creature glares around.

In the darkest corner of this forgotten grotto, where the deep shadows have never been disturbed by the sunlight, lies a small, roughly level area, like a rocky beach descending gently into the silent lakeshore. Its stony ground is uneven and dangerously slippery. Here and there heaps of fishbones lie carelessly piled, mixed with other filth of dubious origin. Both muck and moisture contribute to the piercing stench that fills the air. But even in this lost spot, as in the wilderness outside, the atmosphere remains mild no matter the season, perhaps under the influence of the same strange power.
17160: Rurthag the Dwarf (r), wielding a battle axe, is standing here.

A narrow ledge juts out of the high, sheer cliff wall that forms the riverbank. Unable to break the resistance of the cliff, the river makes a turn along its side, its waters washing over the ledge that lies just above the water level. Crests of foam spring up on the waves that break against the protruding edges in the rock. The ledge is slightly over four feet wide and could serve as a landing spot for a small craft.
17161: A wooded hillock rises above the banks of the wide Anduin, which wraps around these lands from west to south. The trees here have slender trunks but are lofty in height and seem to become closer together in the north. Beyond the western banks the river flows powerfully yet quietly over several large, rounded boulders scattered throughout the waterway.
17162: Slender birch trees weave their limbs overhead, providing an airy ceiling to these woodlands. In sharp contrast to the deciduous trees which can be seen in all other directions, the forest in the south is dominated by long-needled pine trees. The faint sounds of a river seem to drift in fleetingly from the west, but they are too vague to be definitively distinguished.
17163:
A mailbox stands here stuffed full of messages.
An elven archer dressed in green is here, watching the forest.
An elven archer dressed in green is here, watching the forest.

The wide, smooth and silver-barked trunk of this mallorn-tree rises over four yards above ground level before several sturdy yet flexible boughs branch off it at an upswept angle. Upon the great branches, which sway smoothly in the passing wind, a small, unobtrusive platform of slender grey planks has been constructed. A hole has been cut in the middle of the floor, next to which has been secured a finely crafted rope ladder. The platform has no walls or ceiling, but rather is enclosed in all directions by glittering golden masses of the broad mallorn leaves, supported by streaks of silver boughs. It is doubtful that even the most keen-eyed passer-by would be able to detect this structure, which blends seamlessly into its woody surroundings.
17164:
A small oaken table has been set here.
On the table, there are two lembas wafers, three large yellow apples, and two flagons.
A circlet of golden flowers has been left here.
An elven lady is walking around here.
An elven caretaker is standing here, offering his guests a rest.

This flet is actually constructed of several irregularly shaped wooden platforms, interconnected by the broad silver boughs of the great mallorn-tree.
