The individual platforms have been designed to exist in harmony with this golden-crowned wonder; each structure is shaped so that it fits perfectly within the natural nooks and corners created by the smooth branches and the wide trunk. Furthermore, the platforms are not nailed into place but rather supported by the skilful lashing with bright green cord of the grey planks around the boughs which support them. This flet appears sturdy but happily weathered; it is notable, then, that the cords wrapped around the branches have not dug into them with the passing years. The elves which inhabit these lofty homes must unwrap the cord frequently and re-lash the platforms so as to avoid harming the great tree.
17165:
A skeleton of some humanoid lies in the dust.
An ancient fungus smothers the boulders.

Perhaps an extension of this underground area at one time, this chamber has collapsed, leaving a dead end of dirt and stone in all directions except to the west. The air is slightly less damp here than the rest of the tunnel, perhaps owing to the raised elevation of this room.
17166: Massive roots shift uneasily all around you.

A foul stench rises up from the water which is about ankle-deep. Various algae and moulds float upon the surface of the murky water, covering any view one might have of the ground itself. Parasitic bugs almost too small for the eye to see line the cavern walls and straddle the mark of the water level against the dirt walls.
17167: A giant slug is here, oozing around.

The ground slopes downwards a little from north to west and the moisture visibly increases. The floor sinks down with even the least amount of weight applied to it. A thin layer of water coats the ground at all times, making this place a haven for water-loving creatures.
17168: The soil leading into this corner passage is less damp than the rest of the room. It seems that the water is being siphoned elsewhere; the dripping of water in another part of the passage confirms this. The air is dank and musty. The ceiling shows several straggling roots, hardly able to grab hold of the earth.
17169:
An ancient fungus smothers the boulders.
A huge black fungus is here, exuding a foul stench.

Walls made of a tangle of tree-roots and the dirt spanning the small gaps between them form this underground room not far below the surface. Enough air reaches this place to allow the moulds and fungi to thrive here. The earthen floor is damp and shifts slightly underfoot; any impressions in the floor quickly fill with muddy water.
17170: This underground cavern seems to be made from a complex root system of the trees above. The roots are so dense that they hold back the dirt, creating a system of spaces almost like a tunnel. This would-be passageway extends into the darkness to the south, while one can reach the surface above through a makeshift doorway below a tree stump.
17171: Very little light filters through the trees here, allowing only parts of the forest around this flet to show themselves depending on the angle of the sun. The forest floor is not visible from here, making it seem miles away. The mallorn-trees seem to glow faintly, emitting a sweet fragrance. The forest to the south is thin enough that this tree offers a good view of lands in that direction, and this flet could be used as an outpost.
17172: A big, nasty vulture is sitting here, protecting its nest.

As you need to cling to the rocks to stop yourself from falling, you are not able to see much of the surrounding land without considerable effort. Fortunately the cracks by your feet are large enough to allow you to catch your breath. The additional height that you have gained with this precarious climb does not seem worth the effort.
17173:
The corpse of a small termite is lying here.
The corpse of a small termite is lying here.
A cup has been set here.
A woodman's axe lies here.

On the outside the wood of this tree is still green, indicating that it has fallen recently. However, the inside of the tree is brown and dry, as if it has been hollow for some time; this fact might have contributed to its fall in high winds. The space inside forms a low tunnel, in which a man would just be able to crouch. A number of objects are visible in the gloom, the most obvious ones being a makeshift bed, small stool and table made from tree stumps. A few small shelves are cut into the walls. These contain a few small cups and some carved ornaments in the shape of woodland animals.
17174: The corpse of a mottled snake is lying here.

This small cavern is sheltered by a number of large rocks that protect it from the elements. A rotten stench and the sound of dripping water permeate the air. On the ground there is a pool of water, some old bones and many humanoid footprints. A few bundles are arranged in an orderly row on a natural shelf in the back of this small cave; the bundles are wrapped in mouldy canvas.
17175: The branches of the two great trees merge into one crown. Dry and partly charred, these branches still appear to be quite strong; stronger perhaps than they were when the trees were alive and green, as if in death they had obtained some new strength previously unfamiliar to them. The trunks of the trees are as hard as if they were petrified, but the branches haven't hardened completely and still bend slightly under their own weight.
17176:
A brown bear is sleeping here.
A brown bear is sleeping here.

Branches reach out towards the walls of the broken-down mill, providing a sheltered area which apparently serves as an animal den. The humidity of this place most likely made it very habitable, once the mill had fallen into disarray and those taking care of it had left.
17177:
A small campfire burns here, its low flames giving off only a little light.
Little parts of a broken weapon are lying on the ground.
A patch of moss grows here on a wet, flat stone.

The basement of the old water mill is damp and musty, even though no water has been pumped here for a very long time. The equipment and inner workings of the mill are rusted and corroded; most of it has begun to fall off and decay. Without water it is likely that no need was found to repair it. A large pile of branches is resting against the northern wall.
17178: A swallow flies high above the ground.

The entrance to this old water mill is very dusty, as though nary a person has been here in many years. Without water flowing to the mill it seems to have been abandoned by even the local wildlife, as there is no longer anything here for them. Stairs lead up and down. Some debris can be seen in a corner, possibly the result of a battle once fought here.
17179: From the top of the old water mill the surrounding land can be seen in all directions. The now-dry streambed to the east, that used to provide the valley with water, can be seen winding its way past the mill. A flight of stairs heads back down into the mill.
17180: This old cellar looks as if it had been used for food storage a long time ago. The walls, the floor and the ceiling still appear to be in good shape, even though the air is moist and drops of water condense on every smooth surface. Judging by the trash and the remains of a small fire on the stone floor, this place was used by travellers that stayed here for a night or more. A large arched door is in the southern wall. Slightly incongruous in these somewhat plain surroundings, the door is very carefully crafted and appears untouched by time.
17181: This is a small room with broken shelves along one wall and a large ruined closet on the other wall. The room is softly lit by small glowing crystal prisms hanging from a thin silver chain on the ceiling. In the northern wall is a magnificent arched door decorated with fine carvings. As the room does not appear to be inhabited, the lack of dust on the floor is intriguing.
17182: This is a rather large room with a large table and some ruined chairs in one corner and the remains of a couch and a smaller table in the other. The walls are decorated with paintings, a few portraits and one landscape. A dark curtain covers the western wall. The lack of dust is intriguing, but even more so are the small glowing crystal prisms that hang from a thin silver chain in the middle of the room, bathing the place in a soft cozy light.
17183:
A short, broad stabbing blade lies here.
A softly glowing green cup has been left here.
Several silver coins lie scattered about here.
A delicate indigo crystal lies here.

This appears to be an old study room. The walls are lined with shelves. Several broken chests lie on the floor and a large desk stands by one wall. The interior of the room has not survived the aging well, but the structure itself looks as if it could last for many decades to come. The eastern wall is covered by a large dark curtain which oddly enough looks untouched by time.
17184: This small cave is dug out of the soft, fertile soil; the digging appears to have been done by a large animal. The floor and the walls are of caked mud, and a muddy hole leads back up to the surface. To the east, a dark recess can be seen. A sharp, musty smell pervades the air.
17185:
A huge grizzly bear is here, roaming the wild.
A huge grizzly bear is here, roaming the wild.
A grizzly cub is here, snarling loudly.
A grizzly cub is here, snarling loudly.

This room, like the entrance, shows signs of having been dug by a large animal with sharp claws. The room is damp, perhaps absorbing moisture from an underground water source. The floor consists of soil and mud and has been packed down hard by the constant trampling of whatever creature lives here.
17186:
A mottled snake is sneaking here, ready to sink its fangs into flesh.
A subterranean lizard is here trying to blend with the surroundings.
A mottled snake is sneaking here, ready to sink its fangs into flesh.
A subterranean lizard is here trying to blend with the surroundings.

This dark and damp alcove is filled with musty, foul-smelling rubbish. The earth walls are almost covered by the running water. The floor is covered by one foot of cold and dirty water. The only exit is an opening to the north which seems to lead to a larger cave of some kind.
17187: This cave is large enough to hold a small army and appears to be the centre of this underground complex. Three smaller caves are connected to it. The uneven walls are of earth and clay. Water runs down the walls, and about one foot of water covers the floor. A strong, stifling smell of mould comes from the north and south.
17188: This alcove seems to be a sleeping chamber of some kind. A large rock nest can be seen in the back. Water runs down the walls, and the floor is covered by one foot of cold and dirty water. The air is almost unbreathable, filled with the heavy odour of mould that seems to come from the nest and the walls of the cave. The only exit is to the south, to what appears to be a larger cave.
17189: The corpse of a subterranean lizard is lying here.

The cave is dark and moist. The walls are hard-packed earth. Water runs down the walls, and the earth floor is covered by one foot of cold, dirty water. The air is heavy, damp and musty. The musty odour seems to come from an opening to the east which appears to be the only exit from this dark cave. This should encourage you to head that way, but there is something scary about this place.
17190:
A tree-snake lies wrapped around one of the tree branches.
A tree-snake lies wrapped around one of the tree branches.

Although the foliage of the tree is dense and thick the gaps between the branches provide a good view of the surrounding area. A vast forest can be seen far away to the north; a couple of small hillocks dot the level terrain to the east, west and south. The branches appear to fully support your weight and it is unlikely any of them will break.
17191:
A grizzly cub is here, snarling loudly.
A grizzly cub is here, snarling loudly.
A huge grizzly bear is here, roaming the wild.
A huge grizzly bear is here, roaming the wild.

This is a fairly small cave with a very low ceiling. The walls and the floor are of a cold, hard stone on which there is a thin coating of white moss. There are signs of animal life, such as the skeletal remains of many small creatures piled up in the corners. The only way out appears to be upward.
17192:
A black spider crawls here, a shiny red spot visible on its belly.
A huge, venomous spider is here.

The tunnel comes to a sudden halt as it sharply narrows. Whereas the northern wall contains a few specks of brownish dirt, the eastern and southern walls are formed from a sickly grey substance. Although the cavern is quite humid, even algae finds it difficult to grow on the clay surface. Only in a few spots where once no vegetation could grow, now a few strands struggle.
17193: You are in the eastern portion of a long east-west tunnel. The walls of the tunnel are largely composed of thick, stale grey clay with embedded pieces of rotted wood. With the reduced flow of fresh air, some of the wood has petrified. The stale air is motionless and ripe with the smell of decay. The floor is littered with a few small bones and even a skeleton or two from the small critters that once burrowed into the soil.
17194:
A skeleton of some humanoid lies in the dust.
A small pool of red-stained water lies here.
A huge, poisonous tarantula extends her legs to you (red aura).
A huge, poisonous tarantula extends her legs to you (red aura).

This pit is little more then a shallow indentation in the tunnel. A pool of dirty water has collected in the southern part of the pit. The walls of the pit are composed of a thick, stale grey clay-like substance of a rubbery texture that consists largely of ancient pieces of rotted wood. The air here is stale but not as foul as to the north. The floor is composed of soft greyish clay with a few brown specks. There is an intangible feeling that evil had once touched this place and it may be many more years before this region is fully healed.
17195:
A tiny spider is here, eating a tiny bug.
A tiny spider is here, eating a tiny bug.

This is a section of a long and relatively straight east-west tunnel. The air is stale and dry. Apparently the soil here turned foul and the trees above died, for dead roots hang from the ceiling. As the soil turned foul, the air here filled with ammonia causing the small critters in the soil to die as well. To the north these signs of decay recede, while to the east they grow more frequent.
17196:
A giant slug is here, oozing around.
A giant slug is here, oozing around.

The tunnel comes to a sudden end here. From the south to the north the space narrows as the dirt walls transform from a sickly grey to a deep rich brown. A few tender plant roots can be seen poking through the soft dirt at the northern end of the cavern.
17197: This is a long and narrow tunnel with one end leading towards an opening above and the other digging deeper underground. An old stench of decaying flesh comes from the east where the tunnel slants downwards. The soil which forms a shell around the tunnel is a sickly grey and would probably be poisonous to most plants, though a few patches of algae, with the texture of mould, can be found here.
17198: Once, long ago, the soil here was a rich and deep brown. Tall hearty trees covered this land, as they still do to the north, and grew with great vigour as their roots traversed the soil unhampered. Now that the soil has gone from deep brown to a sickly grey, the roots lie rotting in the ill earth, with the trunks they once nourished long dead and mostly decayed. The soil, now acidic, sags in places, indicating the presence of an unstable base. In a few spots large holes can be seen, and in other places it is doubtful that the weight of a small dog could be supported for more than a few minutes.
17199:
A simple wooden chest is here.
A large stone fireplace with a roaring fire warms the room.

The floor and walls of this hut are made of a plain wood stained dark. The hut is composed of a single room which is mostly bare of furniture. The ceiling seems solid and shows no signs of leakage. The stone fireplace against the back wall appears to be frequently used for cooking food in the adjacent pot. A supply of wood is stacked next to the fireplace.
17200: Either by the recent spasms of Arda or by the work of some fiery weapon of the minions of the Dark Lord, the ground has been torn apart here, revealing a deep ditch riddled with dark pools of smelly water. The two earthen scars coming from east and west meet here and continue south, where the ground seems to rise to support the sparse forest. A pile of wood covered with rank grass and plants bars passage to the north.
17201:
A wooden chest stands in the corner.
An elf of the Galadhrim is walking around here.
An elven lady is walking around here.

A platform has been built on the silvery-grey branches in the crown of this mallorn-tree. The leaf-walls of the natural house are soft, yet unyielding, fashioned in the true spirit of the elven-folk. Twined plants and clay-coloured wooden carvings bear signs of devoted decorating, weaving their beauty and lustre from a few magical whispers.
17202:
A small oaken table has been set here.
On the table, there are two pieces of smoked, cured meat, a handful of blueberries, and a cup.

Four walls and a roof seem to be all that is needed for the tenant of this rustic building. Furs and trophy-heads of various animals decorate the walls, and the furniture of the cot consists of a bed, a table and a shaky stool. The bed is covered with fresh branches and leaves, and some food and drink have been left on the table.
17203:
An elven lady is walking around here.
Taurion the Elf is standing here.

High up in the trees the elves of Lorien can live feeling safe from the many dangers that plague the forest below. On the strong branches of this stout mallorn-tree a stable wooden platform has been built to serve as a dwelling. The platform extends to the north where a mass of leaves and branches conceals it completely, sheltering those that dwell here.
17204:
A neat straw pallet is lying here.
A wooden chest stands in the corner.
An elf of the Galadhrim is walking around here.
An elf sits here delving into some old tomes of elven lore.

A dense canopy of leaves and branches surrounds this part of the large platform. Well hidden from view, this simple flet offers shelter and protection for its proud residents. Some of the branches which form this dwelling are furnished with a variety of elven decorations, from wreaths of leaves and flowers to carefully crafted wooden ornaments depicting scenes from the legends as far back as the First Age.
17205:
A black bear is sleeping here.
A black bear is sleeping here.

Dug out of the inside of the hill, this bear den seems cozy enough. A small pool of dirty water can be seen on the ground near the back of the den. The water is apparently from an underground source and appears clean enough to drink. The earthen floor is quite smooth and clean, which might indicate present or recent habitation of the den.
17206: The view from here is breathtaking. You can gaze upon the mighty Misty Mountains in the west and upon the magnificent forest of Lorien that rises to the north and to the east. To the south you can see a wide plain stretch out to the very horizon. You can look in all directions as nothing hinders your vision.
17207: Tall trees rise all around the barn. A few ladders and ropes can be seen in the tree-crowns, leading from branch to branch mostly, as it seems, into nowhere, as the dense foliage masks most destinations making it impossible to see anything except leaves and branches. Nestled in the tree-branches slightly above the level of the barn one can see two platforms to the east and to the west that appear to be reachable from the roof. A thin board forms a slim bridge that leads to the eastern platform while the platform to the west can be reached by climbing the tree-branches. A small shack can be seen on the roof to the north.
17208: A simple wooden chest is here.

A small wooden chest sits in the corner of this platform, its back against the trunk of the tree. Looking over the edge of the platform, you can tell that you are high above the ground. Slightly below the eastern edge of the platform you can see the top of a wooden building but everything below the level of its roof is concealed by branches and leaves. The slightest breeze that passes through the trees seems magnified here as it makes all leaves rustle loudly.
17209: A small wooden platform without any railing sits in the branches of an enormous tree, one branch successfully supporting the entire weight of the platform. Except for a sea of branches and leaves there is nothing you can see above, around or below, except to the west where a wooden building rises among the trees. A slender bridge made just of one board leads from the platform to the roof of the building slightly below.
17210:
A water barrel has been left here.
A simple wooden chest is here.

The walls and the roof of this small shack are of a dark wood. There are no windows as this is apparently not a dwelling but a storage place. A low desk sits in a corner. In another corner there is a hole in a floor. Attached to an iron ring in the wall, a rope descends into the hole, apparently intended as a quick exit down to the forest floor.
17212:
There are two disgusting elf-stews here.
A wide pair of snowshoes lies on the ground here.
A water barrel has been left here.

This small cavern has been dug so carelessly that it is a marvel that it has not collapsed at all. It has apparently been used by orcs as a storage place, and the slovenly nature of orcs can be seen both in its construction and in its contents. Bones are strewn all over the uneven floor together with many bits and pieces of broken armour and remainders of food and drink.
17213:
An orc-guard of the Morgundul is on patrol here.
An orc-guard of the Morgundul is on patrol here.
A hungry warg stands here, sniffing around for flesh.
An uruk of the Morgundul tribe is here commanding his soldiers.

This cavern is little more than a hole in the ground and one can tell that it had probably been dug not so long ago. The earthen walls are uneven as they appear to have been quickly dug out without any care for the appearance. In the northern wall of the cavern there is a dark opening.
17216: Only low, defeated-looking shrubs and coarse grass grow in this rocky terrain. A large rock lies here, partly buried in the ground. To the east, an unclimable outcropping rises abruptly; to the south, a wild river runs from east to west.
17217: Grass grows thick and the ground is very broken. In the summer wild flowers cover these uneven fields and provide multitudes of small insects a never-ending feast. In such times flocks of swallows demonstrate their aerial skills. The tireless hunters eat their fill from the inexhaustible supply of swarming creatures. There is a long chain of hills to the north which extends from the west to east. A large bush grows at the foot of the steep hillside.
17218: Between the grassy hills this long vale stretches from the east to west. Golden grass grows thick all around. Some large stones, half buried in the ground, stand up from the grass. Steep hillsides form tall walls of the vale to the north and south. To the west the valley opens out to some bushy grasslands. In the east is a trail through the hills, crossing the vale.
17219:
There is an old street-lamp on the border of the street.
A large fountain, made from grey stone, pours water from its centre.
A sturdy pack horse is standing here.

This is a section of the main road, with a small fountain built directly in the middle of the street! The water looks clean and refreshing, and it seems that the children in the city think so too. Many elven children play in the water, and splash others as they hurry up and down the street. To the north is a narrower street and the main road continues east and south.
17220: Here the road runs east-west. You see that wagon wheels have dug deep ruts into the road that are filled with water from recent heavy rains. There are many potholes, and the road is bordered by high plains to the south, and a light forest to the north.
17221: A humble man stands here, ready to help you with your things.

You are inside a simple home built on a large tree, the only furniture being a pair of chairs and a small table. Large windows in the east and west walls give a view of the surrounding willows and poplars. There are exits to the north and south, and a trapdoor gives access to the world below.
17222: A hobbit is here walking around.
After walking around this area for a while, you realise there's not much point in heading further east. You'd only get lost.
17223: Looking around, you realise you must be inside the Great Smials, home of the Took family. Many passageways lead to other rooms. This place is large.
17224:
A hobbit farmer is here, thinking about seeds and vegetables.
A hobbit is here walking around.

This room is large, tall enough that noone needs to stoop to walk. You are in an antechamber, with rooms north and south of you. Stairs go up. Several members of the Took family have seen you, and stand up. These hobbits don't look so easily cowed, though they offer you their hospitality.
17225: A fine marble chessboard with ivory and ebony pieces is set here.
This appears to be a game room of sorts. Various playthings and boards are scattered about, only a few of which you recognize.
17226:
A small pouch, made from leather, lies on the dust.
A light leather sling lies in the dust.
A Shirriff stands here, keeping a watchful eye on things.
A Shirriff stands here, keeping a watchful eye on things.
The Thain, wielding a longsword, is standing here.
A rabbit is here eyeing your presence warily.

You have entered the office of the Thain, master of the Shire-moot, and captain of the Shire-muster and the Hobbitry-in-arms. The office means less nowadays, but it still holds significance. There are signs that someone here has been drinking.
17227: There is a room to the south, and a long hallway leads north. Judging from the clothes that one messy hobbit has left lying around, the living quarters are to the north.
17228:
A busy hobbit female is here worrying about the home labours.
A busy hobbit female is here worrying about the home labours.
There are many bedrooms along the hallway. Other than the hobbits, there's not much of interest here.
17229:
A beer bottle has been left here.
A beer bottle has been left here.
A beer bottle has been left here.
A smiling hobbit child is playing around here.
You are in a large dining hall. A long table runs the length of the room, though it is small for anyone but a hobbit or dwarf.
17230:
An infusion of herbs gives out a nice scent.
A busy hobbit female is here worrying about the home labours.

You are in a large kitchen. There are several large fireplaces, for cooking food. From the size of things, you think, this place could probably feed a small army. Then you remember the famous appetites of hobbits.
17231:
A beer barrel has been left here.
There are two oak barrels here.
A tiny spider is here, eating a tiny bug.
You have entered a musty wine cellar. Beer barrels line the north wall. Wine bottles lie upon racks about the room. You'd better not get caught here!
17232:
There are three mince-pies here.
There are three loaves of bread here.

This is the Tooks' pantry, and, as such, it is often full of good things to eat, that family being large, energetic, and affluent. On the other hand, as they are equally hungry, perhaps the shelves will be empty, while the cooks are busy preparing the next meal or course.
17233: A Hobbit shopkeeper stands here, eager to sell you his wares.

The shop is small, but the range of wares offered astonishes you. From pots to spoons to lanterns, every conceivable item an average hobbit household may need seems to be stocked. Perhaps the relative isolation of Dwaling accounts for this self-sufficiency. A sign has been placed on the counter at the front of the shop.
17234:
A well-crafted white fountain is here, water pouring forth from it.
A Shirriff stands here, keeping a watchful eye on things.
A Shirriff stands here, keeping a watchful eye on things.

The village square appears peaceful in comparison with the bustling fish market, though you are surrounded by shops selling various necessities of life - notably food and cooking condiments. A big sign under a wide arch on your east proclaims the entrance to the only and therefore popular inn for miles around.
17235: You stand in the small courtyard of the Waterside Inn, reputed for miles around as the favourite meeting spot of the queer fisherhobbits and other equally queer hobbits who fool with boats on the River. On your east, some low steps lead up to a wide open doorway from which the mingled smell of beer and pipeweed emerges. The stables lie north.
17236:
A large stone fireplace with a roaring fire warms the room.
A small hobbit bartender is here, bragging about the beer.

You have entered the smoky common room of the Inn. Hobbits sit in groups at the large round tables drinking, smoking and telling tales. Now and then a voice rises above the din, calling out for one more round of beer. At the north end of the room, a small but well-stocked bar is recessed against the wall, beside a dim corridor which leads into the back wing of the Inn. A sign is on the bar counter.
17237: A well-fed hobbit has set up an inn here, renting out rooms.

You are in the back wing of the Inn, where the guest rooms are located. The Inn seems to have been built just for hobbits, for two rows of round doors stretch off as far as you can see. A small counter has been set partway across the corridor such as to partially block it, and a sign is displayed prominently on the counter.
17238: You see a row of hay-lined stalls, some with ponies in them. The stalls look clean, tidy and comfortable, the ponies content and well-looked after. This will be a good place to leave your mounts and pets. You see a painted sign nailed to one of the stalls. A cheerful stablehand greets you as you enter.
17239: The Baker looks at you calmly, wiping flour from his face with one hand.

A delicious smell of baking greets you as you enter. Your attention is immediately drawn to the glass display case from within which a tantalizing array of fresh pastries, cakes and breads tempt you. A big sign rests on top of the display case.
17240: There are two fishing rods here.

You seem to have entered some sort of storage shed. Empty barrels stand piled in one corner, fishing nets and rods lie in another, and other boxes of odd shapes and sizes line the entire length of one wall. Surprisingly, there is no sensation of floating. The damp floorboards are the only indication that you are not on firm ground.
17241:
A placid pond is here, inviting you to take a refreshing drink.
A fat carp swims here.
A fat carp swims here.
A bass swims here.
A bass swims here.
A trout swims here.
A trout swims here.
A salmon swims here.
A salmon swims here.

The inside of this room surprises you. The floor - or what there is of it - consists of long planks laid criss-cross over the water surface at wide intervals, such that square islands of water are formed between them. Fine-meshed nets extend down from under the planks to form underwater barricades. You see various types of fish in the clear water.
17242: A hobbit fishtrader loudly advertises his fresh fish here.

You stand in the Fish Market of Dwaling, famed in all the Shire for its constant supply of fresh fish. Barrels and crates arranged in distinct groups mark the territories of the fish sellers - or fishtraders as the Dwaling folk call them. On your north, rows of neat hobbit houses line the path to the village square.
17243: The corpse of a hobbit is lying here.

You are on a wooden landing which extends a little way onto the River. A few small boats are moored on one side of it. Some fisherhobbits are gathered beside these boats, loudly discussing their latest catches. On your north, a wooden structure very much like a small shed has been built on the River itself.
17244: You are on the River Brandywine which forms the east border of the Shire. To your west, a wooden landing which straddles a part of the water links the River with the bustling village you can see. Except for the occasional splashes and waves caused by hobbit activity on the numerous boats moored to the landing, the water is extremely calm. Indeed the stillness of the water leads you to believe you are in a sheltered bay.
17245:
A fishing rod has been left here.
A busy hobbit female is here worrying about the home labours.
A pretty hobbit maiden is walking around here.

You have entered the living quarters of the shopkeeper. The furnishing is simple and comfortable, but not what you would expect in a hobbit home. An old fishing net is draped over some mathoms displayed on the mantelpiece, and the hat stand in the corner looks suspiciously like old fishing rods bound together. A round window in the northern wall looks out on the calm water of the River Brandywine.
17246: A Hobbit shopkeeper stands here, eager to sell you his wares.

Shelves upon shelves of fishing rods, bits, tackles and other fishing equipment take up most of the space here. A low counter stands at the front of the store, with a sign on it. In the far wall at the back, a round door catches your attention. You wonder what it opens to.
17259: A diamond-back rattlesnake is coiled here, ready to strike.

This is a dark and shady place, there is almost no vegetation and everything looks cold and grey. Dry mud is cowering the ground and only a little grass manages to grow. There is no wind and the air is thick and old.
17260: You are standing in a magnificent hall, the walls are filled with all sorts of things collected from near and far. To the east there is a sturdy oakdoor which leads out from this home, south of here there is another chamber.
17261:
A wooden chest stands in the corner.
A fine marble chessboard with ivory and ebony pieces is set here.
A large stone fireplace with a roaring fire warms the room.
Vubur the innkeeper is here, offering a room at his inn.
A domesticated pony, beast of burden to many, stands here.
A domesticated pony, beast of burden to many, stands here.
A stocky mountain mule is here, waiting to serve.

Tall ornamented pillars rise towards the smooth curved ceiling where small round holes provide the inn with fresh air and light during the days. Around the walls, small booths have been excavated, containing tables with surrounding chairs for the guests. A large fireplace is placed in the centre of the room, and a big counter can be seen at the far end of it. Behind the counter a narrow corridor leads to the inn-rooms.
17262:
A large fountain, made from grey stone, pours water from its centre.
A doorwarden stands here ready to obey his master's wishes.

A large archway, made entirely of marble, leads into this home. An example of the finest Dwarven craftsmanship, the stone is unblemished, save for an inscription at the top and each base of the arch, stating in both Khuzdul and Westron that this is the home of Durin's Army. Near the bottom of the archway, smaller inscriptions can be seen.
17263: This place offers the most amazing view, with the possibility to enjoy the sight of different terrain in every direction. South-east from here another hill like this one can be seen. Down below, a small path running along the cliffs. The road and river to the north-east, the flat lands to the north and plains to the west. Far to the east lies the Misty mountains with their peaks piercing the clouds.
17264: A canoe has been left here.

After twisting about a bit, the cave comes to an abrupt end in a small sized chamber. A stone shelf has been cut into one side of the cave, which looks as if it hasn't been used in years. Water seeps through the walls of this room and it runs towards a large hole in the centre of the floor. The water makes the floor of the cave very slippery.
17265: Widening to the west, this cavern twists to the south. Many rocks protrude from the walls of the passage and in places it is difficult to squeeze between them. It looks like there may be a large chamber at the western end of the passage, but it is difficult to tell.
17266:
A simple wooden chest is here.
A huge, smoking campfire is burning here.
A neat straw pallet is lying here.
A wooden longbow is lying here.
A hermit, wielding a short spear, is sitting here on a straw pallet.

The rather odd set of stalagmites in the centre of the cavern are dwarfed by the sheer size of this immense cavern. The stalagmites seem to be leaning towards the northern edge of the cavern,while the ceiling above has a similarly strange set of stalagtites hanging from various rocky protrusions. This room is guarded from the spirits that roam the rest of the complex by a cleverly crafted secret door hidden in one of the stalagmites.
17267: Shadows dance around the rough walls of this passage which must have been cut by a huge volume of water at some time in the past. However, the rocky sides appear to have been chipped away in places to allow something easier passage. The chippings now cover the rough floor of the cave, making it virtually flat.
17268: Stalactites hang from the ceiling of this cavern, which in times gone by was carved from the rock by a large flow of water. The ground is very smooth and slippery, and faint traces of algae and moss indicate that it is usually damp. The walls are not so smooth, but natural passages branch out to the north and west.
17269: A shadowy haunt floats here, oblivious to your presence.

The ceiling of this huge natural cavern is covered with stalactites high above. The air feels cool and damp, but no breeze can be detected. Faint traces of moss and lichen grow on the rocks about you. The frequent passing of some kind of creature seems to have worn a smooth path in the rocky cavern floor.
17270: A dark intangible shadow turns to face you.

Rocky protrusions hinder your movement along this twisting natural passage, which appears to have been carved by a great flow of water at one time. Presumably the water has found another path now. The channel twists from east to north here.
17271:
There are two potatoes here.
A grey wolf fur is here lying on the ground.
An old man is sleeping here.

This miserable hut, which is separated from the main settlement that lies west of here, was constructed with branches driven deep into the ground. The grey-blue cavern ceiling arches high above you, supported by tremendous limestone pillars dripping with moisture. A dank, smoky odour pervades the air, mixed with pungent food smells. The walls shimmer and sparkle in light; strange fluted columns rise from the cave floor far up towards the ceiling, coloured translucent peach, strawberry, and lavender. Water drips slowly from the ceiling, enhancing and multiplying the crystalline brilliance of the rock surfaces by coating the forms with an aqueous luster. Small passages open up on either side of the cavern, and small rivulets of water coalesce and run sparkling down to a wide opening to the east. A delicate pathway, whether chiseled by water or humanoid hands, spirals up into the darkness.

Today, you can't hear the hobbits' merry laughter in the valley any longer, the tavern itself is hardly more than a heap of debris, and the path has fallen into disuse, partially covered by weeds. This is the most spacious hovel in the village, and the most profusely and ostentatiously decorated as well. Shields of varnish wood with shiny metal reinforcements hang from the walls, together with impeccably polished weapons. A thin, elaborately worked wool carpet, tinted in ochre, covers all the ground. At the back, a wide fireplace keeps the room warm in the cold winter nights, fed by a stack of carefully cut oaken logs lying by its side. A great oval-shaped table, with smoothly carved edges, stands out in the middle of this meeting hall. Several dark wooden chairs, upholstered in fine white wool, are disposed around it, a large, higher armchair towering at the head.

17480: The passage leads north and south. The walls and ceiling consists of large square pieces of black stone. Upon them images of winged warriors and dragons has been painted. There is no movement in the chilly dry air. Lampholders are fitted in the walls approximately four yards apart.
17481: A twenty by twenty yards large hall has been duged out in the hill. The walls and ceilings are made of large square pieces of black stone. A well with the radius of about one yard leads downwards in the middle of the room. A whining sound can be heard from the well, but it might be a chilly draft. To the north a passage leads into the darkness.
17482: The stonewell continues up and down from this ledge. There is no way to get back up, and down there is only darkness. On the southern side of the well there is one black stone missing, leaving a hole large enough to crawl through, southwards.
17484: A dirty hobwill is standing here.

A very narrow tunnel has been carved out of the rock in a rough manner very unlike the craftmanship of the dwarves. The air is damp, moist and a slight draft can be felt from the north where there is only darkness. A flickering light can be seen to the south where the tunnel extends into a cave.
17485: A dirty hobwill is standing here.

A small cave opens up on both sides of the tunnel. It is being lit by torches fasten on the walls evenly spaced out to supply a soft gentle glow. The cave is ten yards wide and a tall dwarf would scratch his head against the ceiling if he was standing on his toes. There are a few small benches by the walls and small tables in front of them. Old residues of rotten food lies on the tables.
17486: Tunnels lead north, south, east and west. They have been carved out in a rough fashion. The damp air is filled with a scent of garbage, seemingly coming from the eastern tunnel. The southern exit is smoother and adorned with fresh leaves and flowers.
17487: The Hall of the Hobwill Chief

This is a hall, about twenty yards wide and thirty yards deep. The ceiling is higher here than in the surrounding tunnels and rooms, some six feet up. The floor is filled with fresh leaves, and a large wooden bed dominates the southern part of the room. A mirror is placed besides the bed. The only visible exit is north.
17488: The room is filled with garbage, and the smell leaves evidence of decay in the air. The garbage must have been left here for years. Low squeeks can be heard from inside the garbagepiles, perhaps the sound of rats. West of here a tunnelcrossing can be seen.
17489: The corpse of a hobwill is lying here.

This is a fairly large room, with ten small beds scattered along the walls. The mattresses are composed of off-white linings filled with dried grass. At the footend of each bed stands a small wooden stool with three legs. There are empty doorframes east, south and west.
17490: The soft earthen walls are about ten feet apart and the ceiling is low. Pale lichen growns upon the walls, soaking up any condensed water. The room seems to have no apparent use as it is very empty, a mere hallway almost. Every sound is carried away long distances into the tunnelsystem.
17491: A dirty hobwill is standing here.

Heavy is the burden these earthen walls carry. A whole mountain is laid upon them, and the pressure has formed small cracks in them. Ten small beds stand along the walls in disorder. Dry grass has been put in old cloth creating soft mattresses to lie upon.
17492: A dirty hobwill is standing here.

Here tunnels connect from all directions. The small room is unfurnished save for a tiny chair in one corner. The air is damp and chill, and from the south comes the smell of cooked food. There is a tiny draft coming from the eastern exit drawing out old poluted air.
17493: This is a small room, with the main exit west. There is a ventilation shaft in the ceiling, with a ladder going up to enter it, and a narrow tunnel going north. A heavy barrel of water is placed in the middle of the room, and water is trickling down from the ceiling into it.
17494: A dirty hobwill is standing here.

The air is damp and cold in this dark tunnel. The walls are covered with condensed water, gathering up into small rivulets running down on the floor. Small puddles of water can be found inbetween the stones on the ground. The tunnel bends north towards a larger room, and eastwards to something that resembles a kitchen.
17495: A dirty hobwill is standing here.

This is a room set up for preparing food in various forms. There is a basin of soggy water in the southeast corner and a table filled with different herbs. Shelves has been carved out in the soggy earthwalls and they are stocked with cooking utensils. The air is filled with a scent of newly cooked food.

A cramped pathway leads up into the hill northwards. It is dark and the walls are narrowing in further north. There is a strong draft, the wind is moist and cold penetrating all and any cloth, skin or fur. The floor is overgrown with mosses nurturing on the moist and minerals.
17500: A long tiny shaft has been duged out here, apparently used for the ventilation of the tunnelsystem beneath. The walls are glistening with water condensing when it gets in contact with the colder air from the outside. Up ahead there is a faint light, a promise that the shaft has an ending.
17501: The End of the Ventilation Shaft
The ventilation shaft ends in a cave, facing north. The caveentrance is located approximately seven yards up a sheer cliff face. A few low bushes would probably break a fall from this position.
17502: The walls of this hole are fairly roughcut, similar to those of the hobwill tunnels. A ladder, going up and down, has been attached to one of the walls. It is made out of a red coloured wood, and the damp air has made it quite slippery and dangerous to climb. There is no movement in the cold air.
17503: This is an old, looted crypt. The coffin, where presumably some noble was laid to rest, is now empty and broken. A rough hole in the ceiling seems to have been constructed in a differing fashion from the elegant design of the crypt, which is about ten yards by ten yards in size. There is a doorframe set in the south wall made in stone with huge hinges, indicating that the now crumbled door was immense.

A huge doorframe adorns the north wall. A wide corridor runs from east to west, disappearing into the darkness in both directions. The walls are covered with elaborate runes of a long forgotten language. In the south wall a small hole leads off into the darkness beyond. There is an almost palpable sense of evil all about, and the air is very cold.
17518: A war-weary wight-warrior is standing here.

This is a four-way corridor intersection. All the corridors in this complex are turning left and right, with stairs going up and down, with three and four-way intersections everywhere. It is easy to lose any sense of direction. The walls are supported by large wooden pillars, and the roof is held up by wooden beams secured to the pillars.

A bold rune has been painted upon the floor in brilliant white, and strangely this chamber does not share the same air of evil prevalent in the rest of the underground complex. There is a huge portal north and another exit east, framed by elaborate sculptures of vicious snakes. The doorway seems to be veiled in shadows and it is impossible to tell what lies beyond it.

You feel the fresh air here blowing gently in your face from the north. The only exit here is back into the forest to the west.

17531: A large stone fireplace with a roaring fire warms the room.

A few wooden rocking chairs and a comfortable leather couch surround the fireplace that blazes during the cold winter months. It looks like many long nights are spent here, visiting with friends or just pondering until the late hours. Along the wall is a weapons rack and a place to store armour. An arched door leads to the bedroom to the east.
17532: A humble man stands here, ready to help you with your things.

In this room is a large feather bed with posts at each corner, each post carved obviously by an artisan of great skill. The floor is a mosaic of an intricately pieced, many coloured wood. Murals are painted on two of the walls, and there are windows on the others. As you look up there is a window on the ceiling, that lights up this room during the day, and lets moonlight in during the night.
17533: This is a small corral, obviously a place the master of this home exercises and trains his horses. Near the entryway are some flowerbeds full of colourful, well-tended flowers. Wild rose vines and ivy grow up the wall that surrounds the corral and the stone cottage. A bench is placed near the backdoor so in the evening the master and his friends can enjoy the cool night breeze, the scent of the garden, or even watch the pure bred horses graze.
17534: A huge, black wolf is here, ready to devour.

You have entered a dense, gloomy, entangled forest. The trees grow in all directions, and the thick undergrowth forces you to turn frequently, totally ruining your sense of direction. From time to time, a couple of red eyes blink in the dark, and you hear deep growls and high pitched howls. The entwined branches of the trees above you are so thick that almost no light filters to the ground.

A rather heavy clay jar stands here.
