Here the walls are covered with wooden shelves. The cool air smells slightly moldy. Piles and piles of berry jars are placed on the shelves. This cellar, deep under the hill, is supported by a couple of large oak beams supporting the heavy earthen roof. The floor is covered with flat stones, acting as floortiles. Following them, they lead to an outside door and into another room cut deep into the hill. A simple wooden door separates the two rooms.
17541:
Some curdled goats milk sits inside a cheese mould.
Some curdled goats milk sits inside a cheese mould.
Some curdled goats milk sits inside a cheese mould.

Air is very cool here. Sound of dripping water echoes somewhere in the shadows. Room is quite small. In the back wall three wide shelves are constructed from wood. Upon the shelves are some cheese moulds and some aging cheese. There is a distinct aroma of goat milk here. The floor is built from long wooden rods. Some old skins lie in one corner filled with milk.
17645: After Thrain and Thorin settled in the Blue Mountains after the battle at Nanduhirion, the exploration of the mountain lead the Dwarves farther and farther into the underground. As the excavations continued, this tunnel was created to host a large rock-grinder; here the largest of ore fragments are brought to be mauled to a more manageable size. The tunnel leaves the grinder to the south where, in the distance, a large opening leads into a mine shaft.
17646: In the days of Thrain, the gift of Aule and the will among the Dwarves forged together an entrance into the very heart of the Blue Mountains. A vast system of mine tunnels takes its beginning at a steep shaft located south of this tunnel-branch where neither crack nor scratch can take root in the meticulously carved stone. In an opening in the western wall is set a plain oaken door.
17647: As the shaft continues its vertical journey through the underground, a tunnel suddenly opens to the north. A ledge has been cut into the wall allowing easy access to the tunnel. From the ledge wooden ladders leave both up through the shaft and further down into the mines. Thick ropes, emerging from the darkness above, continue down towards the bottom of the shaft.
17648:
A small oaken table has been set here.
A dwarven craftsman dressed in leather is here.

A large rectangular cavern, excavated with utmost skill and precision, extends fifty by sixty feet in the underground beneath the Blue Mountains. Straight walls of hard trusty rock form the solid base for a high wooden ceiling fifteen feet above. Arranged along the walls are many tables, cabinets and boards for tools, and in the centre of the room is a large anvil. Metal buckets, some filled with scrap metal and some with iron-ore, stand by a door in the eastern wall ready to be emptied into the hot fire.
17652:
A woodpecker is here, tapping on a tree.
A large marmot is here, scurrying in between the rocks.

A gravel path winds around the top of a small promontory jutting out of the side of the mountain. The park itself is unimpressive; several sullen trees stand atop a mangy patch of grass. The surroundings, however, are magnificent. The Blue Mountains tower up just to the west. From your vantage several hundred feet above the ground you can see quite a ways to the east, where the Nan Duin winds through the plains on its way to the Nabrethril Forest.
17653:
A doorwarden stands here ready to obey his master's wishes.
A tall and strong guard is here.
A tall and strong guard is here.

This large hallway is carved right into the side of the mountain. Hung on the sides of this hallway are large colourful murals, interspaced between torches which serve to light it. A large stone door is set in the north wall, which opens up into a small park. To the south, two wooden doubledoors are set in place to partition it off from this area.
17654: The large stone hallway to the north leads into this room. Carved out of solid rock, this dome shaped room has many mystical signs and symbols carved onto its walls. Large benches surround a stone altar which has two large fire pits on either side. A large circle of green tiles has been set onto the floor which surrounds the altar and benches. Another tile pattern on the altar is the shape of a fist.
17656: This hallway was cut straight from solid rock. The ceiling and walls are coarse and lack refinement. Along the walls are mounted brackets containing lit torches that cast dancing shadows down the length of the hallway. There is a large opening to the south from which a great deal of heat and the sound of hammer crashing against an anvil emerge. To the west another opening can be seen covered by a woolen curtain.
17658: The narrow fissure twisting through the underground is bordered by a finely chiselled wall to the west. Set in the wall is a heavy stone door with great iron hinges. Despite the obvious skill and persistence with which the western wall was carved, the passage is unadorned. A faint draught refreshing the musty smell in the passage comes from the east.
17667: The dark water surrounds you with a chilling touch, reaching to your very bones and quickly exhausting your strength. A layer of sediment and rubble covers the bottom, making the ground look fairly level. No algae or other plants grow in the dark water or on the surface which seems to be only a few feet above.
17668: Beneath the lake is a floor of sharp rocks making diving a hazardous adventure. With every swim stroke care has to be taken not to collide with the rocks that are well-hidden in the dark water. The floor slopes gently downwards to the east and the south, and there is a faint stir in the water as if something was moving in its depths.
17669: Beneath the surface of the dark underground lake the water is chillingly cold. A springy bed of mud obscures the primordial rock that forms the bottom of the lake. To the south is an opening into a dark water-filled cavern. The surface of the water is only a few feet above.
17670: A fierce-looking eel lurks in the darkness.

At the bottom of the lake the dark water is freezing cold. A bed of mud and rubble covers the bottom which is fairly level except for a few rocks peering up through the mud. Occasional stirrings in the water indicate that something is moving in the lake. The surface is only a few feet above.
17671: Barely visible through the dark water, the cavern walls bend to form a curving ceiling of hard rock. A hole in the flat floor near the southern wall leads into a dark pit, only accessible to the most skilled swimmer. To the north is an opening that leads into a flat bed of mud.
17672: The dark chute is less than ten feet wide and filled with cold water with nothing to hold on to. There is an opening in the stone ceiling about fifteen feet from the surface of the water, but the vertical walls are smooth and climbing up seems impossible.
17673: A little stone lies on the ground.

The cold and opaque water chills you to the bones in this sloping chute. The bottom is covered by a thick layer of mud that is swirled up by the water at your every movement. To the west is a rock leaning against the wall.
17674: Cold water fills the dark depression in the underground. The bottom is covered by a soft layer of mud that is whirled up by the water with every swim stroke you make. The depression opens into a dome-shaped cavern above. Swimming up into the cavern seems to be your only option for reaching air soon.
17676: A large bulletin board, entitled "Warriors' Guild Board", is mounted here.

Standing on the second level of Barazinbar, you behold the war library of the Dwarves. Shelves and shelves surround you containing countless scrolls and books detailing Dwarven battle plans and tactics. Many a Dwarven student of war has spent long hours studying the battles of the Dwarves of old, paying reverence to those who died to protect their families.
17677: The walls of this chamber are very smooth and if it wasnt already known there would almost not be any way of telling this is a chamber dug out of the stone. The floor is made of marble and is very carefully polished almost making it possible to see reflections in it. To the west a velved passage leads into a small back-chamber which probably is the bed chamber of the owner of this beautyful home. North of here is an entrance hall.
17678: A stout Dwarven steward stands here, ready to defend the home.

This bed chamber is has a very relaxing atmosphere, along one wall there is a magnificient bed made out of sturdy oak-wood and over it is lays a bedspread made out of the finest furs. Several very interesting metalpieces and other trophies are hanging from the walls and standing in the corners, the owner of this home must be out of the ordinary, even for being a dwarf.
17679: At the Bottom of a Lake

Here, far below the surface, the water is cold. In the vague light from above the green and brown vegetation can be seen on the muddy bottom, gently waving as the water slowly moves back and forth. It is extremely difficult to see anything further than fifteen feet away.
17680: A dwarven miner is here, digging the hard rock with his pick.

The cave has been cleanly carved into the stone of the mountain. A wood bed occupies the eastern wall, great furs heaped on it. A fire burns in a carved fireplace, the smoke slowly curling up through a crevice above. The floor is covered with a giant fur, from some animal that does not live close by. Great carvings cover an ancient hardwood desk.
17681: The tunnel bends slowly on its way through the black stone, deep inside this dark mountain. The smooth walls and expert cant of the floor show signs of true Dwarven craftsmanship. The tunnel continues to the west, and a large cavern opens up to the south, smelling of dust and coal.
17682:
A large sack is on the ground.
A pair of soft leather sleeves is here.
A soft leather helmet lies here.
A rusty pickaxe with a broken handle lies discarded here.
There are two torches here.
A brass lantern has been set on the ground.

This room used to store large piles of raw material for the Dwarven smiths who toiled over burning forges, crafting their many weapons and armour. Heaps and stashes of coal and metal lie here still, yet over the years they have been tainted by moisture and rust. Among these piles one can find an assortment of discarded tools and lanterns which may still be salvageable. The eastern wall is cut almost vertically, and all the supplies have been moved away from it.
17683: Dusty piles of coal, empty barrels, wooden wheelbarrows and unused anvils occupy this big tunnel. The rock floor is smooth and cold and the roof hovers above you, black, heavy and monumental. The faint sound of dripping water can be heard in the silence. Openings to adjacent caves lie to the east and south, and a door can be seen in the western wall.
17684: This armoury is set up in a low-roofed cavern and is even more secretive and hidden than the one you previously visited. A few fireplaces, benches and tool racks are spaced out across the floor. The tools and ovens seem larger and more detailed, allowing for more complex and delicate manufacturing.
17686:
A silver wedding ring lies here.
A large stone chest is here.
A huge, poisonous tarantula extends her legs to you (red aura).
A newborn spider is here, hungrily crawling about.
A newborn spider is here, hungrily crawling about.

This room has been built as a small auditorium with shelves instead of seating. The shelves once displayed the finely crafted weapons and armour of the hidden armoury nearby. All the shelves are covered with a thick layer of dust; some even house the dwellings of various creatures that roam these cavernous passageways.
17691: The tunnel is completely filled with dark, cold water that flows swiftly to the east. The constant rush of water keeps the rocks completely bare on its path through the mountain.
17692:
A wooden chest stands in the corner.
*Murkling the Orc*, wielding an ornate, steel-shafted warhammer, is standing here (red aura).
A slavering warg stands here, sniffing around for fresh meat (red aura).
*an Orc*, wielding an ornate, steel-shafted warhammer, is standing here (red aura).
A hungry warg stands here, sniffing around for flesh (red aura).
The shadow of an olog-hai troll is floating here.
The shadow of an olog-hai troll is floating here.

This attic probably looks as it always did. Light shines in through narrow slits in the ceiling, and the water damaged floor seems unstable. You make your way around the cobwebs and realise that not much is up here.
17693: This tunnel is the natural result of water flowing through here for many years and digging its way into the earth. The tunnel is surprisingly deep and though it flows at a high rate here, below in the darkness the water looks calmer. North the tunnel ends and slopes up gradually to meet open water. The current keeps pushing you out of the tunnel southwards into what must be the continuation of a river.
17694: Directly above you some logs have been tied together forming a crude bridge. The water flows quickly here and increases even more towards the south. Tall trees rise up to the east beyond the rivers edge. A narrow tunnel, totally engulfed in water is visible northwards. The slopes to the east and west are soft and with the ends of the bridge placed upon them, climbing up either side is impossible.
17695:
A dirty shovel is lying on the ground here.
A sack of flour has been placed here.
A sack of flour has been placed here.
A pitchfork has been carelessly left lying here.

Just as you expected, this is a very clean barn unlike some others you may have seen before. There are cows and pigs in different parts of the barn, and a whole section has been fenced in for the fowl. Different farming implements can be seen lying around.
17697:
A tall and strong guard is here.
A tall and strong guard is here.

Although this gigantic tree is still alive, the centre was hollowed long ago. The elegance of this place makes it clear that someone, or something, lives here. A natural, spiral staircase ascends to a dimly-lit second floor.
17698:
A small oaken table has been set here.
A smiling hobbit child is playing around here.
A busy hobbit female is here worrying about the home labours.
This comfortable hole protects the hobbits from the cold winds that blow over the prairie during a Westfarthing winter. A long tunnel links the kitchen with the bedrooms, larder, and dining room.
17699:
A tall and strong guard is here.
A tall and strong guard is here.

This is a typical dwarven home cut into one of the hills. The floor is expensive marble polished to a mirror-like finish. The walls have paintings and tapestries depicting dwarven heroes. There is a tunnel continuing to the south from which emanates a soft light.
17700:
A large bulletin board, entitled "Tales", is mounted here.
A Bounder is here, patrolling the Shire and watching for evil.
A Bounder is here, patrolling the Shire and watching for evil.

In the dim lighting of this large room a huge collection of objects can be seen, amongst the shadows. On the southern and western walls there are several shelves upon which the smaller mathoms are placed. The larger mathoms rest on a sturdy oak stand against the eastern wall. A stack of dusty, cobweb-covered paintings lean against the wall in one corner. There are also many books, some of which lie open, as if someone read them not so long ago. To the south a few steps lead up to a door.
17701: Hmm... Perhaps that last step was a poor choice. You seem to have fallen into a tangle of small traps and snares perfect for catching small game such as foxes and rabbits. But since you are none of the above, perhaps some kind soul will help you free, hopefully.
17703: This is a small path going in north-south direction across the plain. Cultivated land surrounds the path in every direction with a board at the entrance to the east field. At some distance to the south, the ground slopes gently upwards until it reaches some woody hills.
17704: The ground begins to slope upwards and the first trees of a dense forest, which covers the small mountain to the south, can be seen here. To the north there are some fields and to the west the remains of the path disappears.
17705:
There are two piles of pipe-weed here.
The garden snake slithers harmlessly here.
The garden snake slithers harmlessly here.
The garden snake slithers harmlessly here.

This is a very well maintained field. Usually hobbits fields are well-kept but this one is really carefully maintained. It is covered with parallel lines of plush green plants with large leaves. A tobacco smell fills the place.
17707: A smiling hobbit child is playing around here.
The fields end here. To the south is a hedge bending north to the east and south to the west. Behind it you see a dark forest. There are large fields north of you.
17708: A small hobbit bartender is here, bragging about the beer.

This is the famous Golden Perch Inn, where all hobbits long to go. They serve the best beer in the East Farthing, maybe you should have a taste? This seems to be a favoured meeting place, and you hear all sorts of stories being told by the merry hobbits. A sign is attached to the wall here.
17709: A hobbit is here walking around.

You are in the southern part of Stock. To the west you see a small house, and a little shop is to the east. You hear the sounds of hobbits doing various activities all around you, and you can't avoid hearing about the Golden Perch, the famous inn.
17710:
A Hobbit shopkeeper stands here, eager to sell you his wares.
A Bounder is here, patrolling the Shire and watching for evil.

You are standing in a nice and homey shop that supplies the people of Stock and those of the surrounding countryside with the basic necessities of life. You see a small cheerful halfling shopkeeper standing behind a small oaken counter. He smiles at you and you feel at ease to browse through his wares. A sign rests on the counter.
17711: An old, and slightly overweight Shirriff sits in a chair.

You are standing in a small building which apparently is some kind of office for the Shirriffs. Judging by the looks of this, the Shirriffs in the Shire are more adept at tea-drinking than fighting, and you guess that most of the Shiriffs would rather hang out in the inn.
17712: Garden in front of the Church of Stock
A large sign stands in front of the doubledoors.

The gardens in front of this small church are lush and well maintained. The weather here seems to have no effect on the many flowers and plants that blossom in this garden. The gate to the north leads back to the harsh world you came from, while the doubledoors to the south lead you to the serenity of the cozy church.
17713: A Bounder is here, patrolling the Shire and watching for evil.

This small cozy church offers a quiet place for the local hobbits to reflect and pray. An altar at the front of the church stands only one foot in height. The pews are occupied by a couple of the local hobbits who are kneeling in quiet prayer. To the north lies the garden and to the south a small oakdoor can be seen.
17714: The Priest's Sleeping Chamber and Study
A hobbit is here looking over various parchments and tomes.

This small room is comprised of bookshelves, a writing desk, and a small bed. The bookshelves line all the walls except where the oakdoor lies. A small stained glass skylight lets in a bit of sunlight during the day. Cluttering the desk are a few old books. Going north will return you to the sanctuary.
17715:
A pig is here, covered in mud.
A pig is here, covered in mud.
A pig is here, covered in mud.
A pig is here, covered in mud.
A pig is here, covered in mud.

YUCK!!!!!! Your foot sinks down into the slime and mud of the neglected pig pen. You begin to sink lower, and soon you're almost knee deep in this mess. The pigs are not happy with your invasion of their happy home, and begin to move towards you.
17716: You gasp for air as the dust from this broken down old barn fills your lungs. From the light rays filtering in from the cracks of the rotten boards barely holding this barn together, you are able to watch huge dust particles flow around the room. Through the haze, you see that the floor seems to be littered with objects. Also, in the far northwestern corner of the barn, you can barely make out the ladder obscured by this polluted air.
17717:
A mouse is here nosing around, looking for a safe place to hide.
A mouse is here nosing around, looking for a safe place to hide.
A mouse is here nosing around, looking for a safe place to hide.
A wise barn-owl is sitting in his nest, watching for signs of mice.

The floor of this loft creaks and groans under your weight. Some of the floor boards seem barely able to support your steps. In the roof you see one small hole that leaks when it rains. There is a musty smell of some wet hay, but for the most part the hay is dry. Some of the bundles of hay are intact, and the outer straws are yellowed with age. You notice in one corner of the rafters above you, there seems to be a large nest. You can hear the faint sound of barn mice scurrying within the hay.
17718:
A doorkeep stands here ready to obey his master's wishes.
A tall and strong guard is here.
A tall and strong guard is here.
A tall and strong guard is here.
A tall and strong guard is here.
You enter a large, neat foyer. There is a hook on the wall for you to hang your coat on. The room is a bit dirty from all the weary hobbits who forgot to wipe the dust from outside off of their feet.
17719: You walk on a narrow trail which seems to have lain undiscovered for ages. Rows of tall trees line both sides of the trail, leaving just enough room for two to walk abreast. Overhead the tree branches form a canopy which sways in the wind, causing the sunlight filtering through to constantly shift and move shadows around. To your east, the trail leads into and under the hills.
17720: You wander upon a large grove of pine trees, their scent filling your nostrils. This grove is a very large and majestic grove of very green and unbelievably tall trees. This seems almost uncharacteristic for this part of Northfarthing, as there is hardly any other forest to speak of near here. The pine trees become unusually thick in the centre of the grove, and very dark. It is from here that you notice some tiny tracks, probably some hobbit's, leading out of the forest and continuing east.
17721: A heavy desk, made of solid oak, stands here.

Sturdy bookshelves dominate the walls of this room. Many ancient tomes which rest on these shelves appear quite dusty, probably from not being opened in a while. A wide window surrounded by curtains lets you view the garden and a good part of the nearby road. A fireplace warms up the room in wintertime.
17722:
A hobbit stable-lad is standing here, checking on the horses.
A drunk hobbit is sprawled on the the ground before you.

The sharp smell of the excrements of the ponies fills this place. The stables of the Ivy Bush Inn are busy and it seems that there is a lot of people staying at the inn. The room is divided in stalls separated by wooden walls. Troughs are well-filled and the animals seem to be happy. There are no windows in the walls and the only opening is a door leading to the north, to the road before the inn's entrance.
17723:
south lies a small path, a white picket fence blocks your way into the garden to the east.
A sparrow is flapping around on the ground.
The bank here is ideal for launching boats into the water north. To the south lies a small path, a white picket fence blocks your way into the garden to the east.
17724: You are completely surrounded by flowers. Every possible flower you can think of is here. Red and White roses, Lilacs, Mayflowers, Violets, Carnations, Mistletoe, Apple Blossoms, and many more. Although, there seems to be an abundance of Lilies of the Valley closer to the middle of the garden. Almost in the centre of the garden, is a quaint little gazebo, painted white, with ancient vines stretching up into its rafters. There are benches in all four corners of the garden, and lanterns lit at intervals around the garden. To the north, you can see the Water as it makes its way towards the Brandywine River.
17731: A large stone chest is here.

Placed beneath the earths surface its air is cold and fresh. This is where most of the castle supplies and spare equipment is stored. Rows upon rows of shelves store every conceivable thing the inhabitants and their servers might need. The room is made out of the same stone as found in the Quarters. The black stone seems to absorb most of the light brought in here, making it impossible to distinguish shadows of any kind.
17732: Well hidden beyond the Storage Room this is one of the last resorts to get away from the castle should it be attacked. Made partly of rock partly of wood the small corridor leads southwards. Near the end of the corridor barly noticable a small crack leads upward. Its made in such a way that once left there is no way to get back in.
17749:
A wolf cub happily plays here.
A wolf cub happily plays here.
A wolf cub happily plays here.
The mother wolf stands here, protecting her young cubs.

Though the entrance to this hole was rather small, the cave opens up somewhat, further inside. The roof hangs low above your head, forcing anyone of great stature to stoop uncomfortably. A crunching sound underfoot gives pause for thought; the entire floor of this chamber is covered by splinters of bone, most of which seems to have been from small animals.
17750: This cleverly concealed trail has been marked with pieces of dark cloth tied among the bushes at regular intervals. It weaves its way among the fens, heading generally east and west. The path would be almost impossible to spot if one did not know exactly where to look.
17751: Winding amongst the fens, this tortuous trail skilfully takes advantage of the exposed land to lead generally east and west. Small pieces of dark cloth tied at regular intervals to bushes mark its course, but it would be almost impossible to find if one did not know exactly where to look.
17752:
An intact skeleton of a man is walking around here.
An intact skeleton of a man is walking around here.
An intact skeleton of a man is walking around here.

Here lay more bones of gallant warriors, the grounds around them seem burned as well, a few large scales lay across the land. Elven daggers lie amongst orkish armour. The skulls of obviously northern Orcs lay in large holes along the ground. The battle seems to have continued on for quite some time. Another plate is inscribed with an insignia.
17753:
An intact skeleton of a man is walking around here.
An intact skeleton of a man is walking around here.

Fewer bones lay along this trail, it appears you may be reaching the horror that these poor souls could not avoid. Daggers seem to mark the road as if they had been searching for a way out of this terrible passage. Spears lay along the ground embedded in some scales, the ground is hot and dry, no grass grows here still. Battle cries can be heard as the wind picks up from where the battle once raged. A dagger with battle scars lies in the middle of the trail. Along the blade is a small warning.
17754: A large final battle has seemed to have taken place, all around you you see hundreds of decaying bones and scarred armour. This is truly the end of the trail, the predator here has shown its cunning and intelligence. Many of your own brethren have died to pay you forbidance. You can hear stirring from the north. The trail seems to just blacken as you look forward into nothingness. A skeleton stands here in full warrior armour with one hand reaching up at you. Again one final message is left on his breastplate.
17755: All around you spreads a blackened and burnt field. No smoke rises from the ground, as the damage was done long ago. Still, you see the charred bones and armour scattered on the ground, and no trees or vegetation grow here.
17756: The pass forms a deep, narrow valley between the steep sides of two of the Weather Hills. It slopes gently up eastwards towards the top of the pass, which is blocked by a ruined fortress.
17757: At the Top of the Pass

Long ago someone built a fortress here, and you can see that that would be an excellent place to block east-west travel if you were a King and so minded. But now ivy grows on the fortress' walls, and low bushes bloom before its walls, their yellow flowers splashed blood-red as if the land itself remembers the soldiers who fought and died here. Where its gate once stood there is now only a gaping hole. The pass itself slopes gently down towards the plains in the west. The ridge that forms the backbone of the hills slopes gently up the northern hill, and steeply up the southern one, and a wall has been built atop it where the slope of the land alone is not enough to block travel.
17758: A long time ago a fortress was built here, where it would block passage through the Weather Hills. Although much damage has been done to the fortress since it was last inhabited, from the great breach in the eastern wall and the ruin of the west gate to the slow work of wind, rain and vine on the stones of the walls, the craftsmanship is still plainly recognizable as that of the Dunedain, the humans who dwelt here long ago in friendship with the Elves of Rivendell and the Grey Havens. But now it is at peace, and the only sound is the whisper of the wind.
17759: The hazy grey shadow of a long-dead man floats in the air.

Once, men must have been able to see far and wide from the battlements of this tower, but the wooden stairs and roof have long rotted away, leaving only the stone walls to grow ivy and the stone floor open to the Sun. Nevertheless, the tower is in better condition than the other fortifications among these hills. It appears that it was abandoned, not captured.
17760: You are just south of the top of the rocky crag which forms the summit of this hill. A league beyond it you can see another hill. To the west you look over the wide grassy shoulder of the hill to see the plains stretching into the blue distance. The rock of the crag continues eastwards, forming a steep-sided ridge which leads down to the pass below you. Beyond it you see plains far below you, and in the far distance there is perhaps a glint of white. You can see the top of a slightly smaller hill a league south of you, but the only way to it is by the ridge, for there is a steep cliff immediately to the south. At the top of the crag there is an old, abandoned tower. The former location of the door is marked by a hole in the wall.
17761: The hill's flat shoulder forms a grassy plateau. In the east, a rocky crag forms the hill's summit. A tower has been built upon it. The plateau stretches some distance north, where an old stone wall still stands, and west. To the south the hill ends sharply. There are other hills to the southeast and the northwest.
17762: The flat shoulder of the hill forms a grassy plateau, which stretches some distance to the east before ending abruptly in a rocky crag. An old tower stands atop the peak of the crag, looking down on you imperiously. The plateau slopes gently to the north, but falls off abruptly to the south and west, offering a spectacular view of the plains stretching into the distance below you.
17763: A small grasshopper clings to a blade of grass, ready to spring.

Not even thin grass grows on this ridge of solid rock. It runs northwest- southeast, and the sides fall off steeply. To the southeast it slopes gently down to the pass; to the northwest it rises to a rocky crag, on which someone long ago built and abandoned a small tower. The view to east and west is spectacular, but the unobstructed wind blows fiercely.
17764: Here the pass was once blocked by a stone wall. The workmanship is similar to that of Fornost. But long ago it was breached by some assault, and since then only the wind and the rain and the grass have worked on it. It would be easy to climb through the ruins at the old breach. The hillside north of you is steep, but climbable. A ridge of black rock runs up it, ending in a crag far above you. The side of the southern hill goes upward more gently, and westward the pass slopes down towards the plain.
17765: The pass runs east-west under the shoulders of two great hills. It is much narrower than the slopes about it are tall. Thin grasses cover some of the stony ground. The northern hill is unclimbable here, for its steep lower slope ends at a rocky cliff reaching up to the peak. The southern slope is less forbidding, but still a long, steep climb. The pass continues upwards to the east, where a stone wall blocks your view. To the west, it slopes gently down to the plains which stretch off into the horizon.
17766: This limestone cave, certainly inhabited at some juncture, now lies disused, abandoned to the elements. In one corner lies a bed-frame of strong oak branches beside some crumbling stools and chests. Near the door is a hearth with a red plaster mantle marked with the fingerprints of its maker. A light ringing noise draws you to the back of the cave--under a mossy chink in the rock is a little pool brimming with clear water, fed by a spring that erupts from a furrow in the wall.
17767:
The corpse of an orc-soldier is lying here.
The corpse of an orc-soldier is lying here.
Almost rotten wooden steps make their way up to something that looks like a bigger room. The stonewalls are also covered with moss. A rather awful stench of rotten meat is coming from downstairs.
17768:
A wooden shield is on the ground.
A small oaken table has been set here.
On the table, there is a stiletto.
A large stone fireplace with a roaring fire warms the room.

The round room houses one small table with some dirty equipment on it, as well as one bed, some chairs and something moving in the shadows. A floortrap in the floor has disappeared so there is just a square hole now. Another hole can be seen in the ceiling, probably a place for a ladder. Several little windows line the walls.
17769: This is just a small hole in the ceiling of a round room. A ladder has been set in it to access the top of the tower.
17770: The tower of stone comes to an end in an area with very low walls, only about half a foot high and no ceiling. Wind and rain have left their marks on the once firm floor, made of thick wooden planks. Above, the open sky looks to goes on forever. Looking outward the surrounding landscape can be seen for a very far distance. Undulating hills and a circling trail can be seen to the south.
17771: From here you have a better view to what appears to be a tall tower on the edge of the forest. It rises just east of here and goes up maybe ten yeards before reaching the top. In the west and north the canopy continues, but seems to be less accessible than here, unless you are a bird.
17772: Ducaht (tooprettytodie), wielding a great warsword, is standing here.

You are in the deep gloom of a crypt housing the slain heroes of Rhudaur of ages long past. The air stirs as if annoyed by your disturbance of its silence. The carvings of battle on the walls stare at you malevolently, sending a shiver straight down to your bones. You cannot encompass the dimensions of the vault as even the brightest light is muted here.
17773:
A broadsword lies here.
Klaees (thedon), wielding a heavy morningstar, is standing here.
Bulg (pukespy), wielding a great warsword, is standing here.

The carvings of battle on the walls stare at you malevolently, sending a shiver straight down to your bones. You cannot encompass the dimensions of the vault as even the brightest light is muted here.
17774: There is some snow on the ground.

You see no shelter from the icy wind on this barren plateau. The ground is rocky and broken and frozen, the earth hard against the soles of your boots. Quickly the landmarks you steered by before become lost, hidden by Eru knows what. There seems to be no easy way out of this ainur-forsaken land. Uncomfortable thoughts of the ancient evils of Angmar are brought to mind by the sight of the path which leads to the ruins of Angmar...not far off enough, you think.

17781: There is some snow on the ground.

The top of this range of cliffs has a slight depression in the centre, perhaps this mountain was once an active volcano. In the very centre of this cold and barren plateau, where you stand now, there are frozen and dead stumps and trunks of trees. By the sheer volume of broken trunks, this must have once been a fertile vale, but now, twisted by some foul sorcery, it is a dead, oppressive forest. Once you have entered it, every direction seems the same, as the lifeless stumps crowd about you, confusing your mind.
17782: There is some snow on the ground.

17783:
The corpse of a large bat is lying here.
The corpse of a large bat is lying here.
The corpse of a large bat is lying here.
The corpse of a large bat is lying here.
A small vicious black rat squeaks at you for disturbing it.
A small vicious black rat squeaks at you for disturbing it.
A small vicious black rat squeaks at you for disturbing it.

As you enter the hidden cavern you shiver, it is cold and damp in here. You hear a faint sound of water running down the rocks at the other side of the cavern. Some small bugs rapidly run across the rocks and disappears again. The only visible exit out of this cave is through a hole in the rocks to the west.
17784: The hidden cleft under the huge rock is quite narrow and moving around down here is not that easy. Some other clefts and openings can be found leading out of here in all directions, but none of them seem to lead anywhere interesting though, some of them are quite dark and you can never be certain. On the ground you see some bones from an animal which probably has fallen down into the cleft and died.
17785: Overgrown Track at a Valley Edge

You are on a path at the edge of the moors, overlooking a wide and deep valley. From here you can choose either one of the myriad of small footpaths to the north and west, or the trail into the valley to the east. The path across the slope leads down to a pine forest a long way below, and is rather steep in places. It would be well-advised to pick one's footing carefully down there.
17786: At the Top of a Valley
A domesticated pony, beast of burden to many, stands here.

One of the many paths from the moors nears the cliff edge, and descends several hundred feet across the slope. The valley itself is an oasis of green in this bleak landscape, shielded far below from the harsh winds that whistle across the moors. It is obviously inhabited, as a large house and some fields can be seen below.
17787:
The corpse of a hunter is lying here.
A small oaken table has been set here.
A tall and strong hunter is standing here.

Some chairs sit here placed neatly around a table in the centre of the room. On the walls you see an assortment of furs and animal heads, obviously trophies belonging to the occupants of this hut. The animals represented are quite an impressive collection, the prowess of this hunter must be almost legendary. You can see a kitchen to the north, and south there is what looks like some sleeping quarters.
17788: A mailbox stands here stuffed full of messages.

The walls are made of closely fitted split logs, the floor laid in wooden planks. The workmanship is good, so whoever built this place obviously knew how to work with wood. The hut extends to the west, where you can see a room with a few chairs and a table, obviously where the occupants spend most of the time they are here.
17789: A black metal stove is the centrepiece of this kitchen, with a chimney climbing the wall to speed the smoke on its way. On the wall a few shelves hold a large variety of spices and seasonings. A large cupboard adorns the eastern wall, and through the slightly open door you can see some choice cuts of meat hanging up to cure.
17790:
A neat straw pallet is lying here.
A neat straw pallet is lying here.
A neat straw pallet is lying here.

Three straw pallets lie on the floor, and although they don't look extremely comfortable, you guess that they must be much better than sleeping on the bare floorboards. A chair sits in the corner, and a small lamp is resting on a little wooden box in the middle of the southern wall. A large chest sits at the other end of the room, and this must contain the possessions of the hunters who own this abode.
17792:
A nest is here.
A big, nasty vulture is sitting here, protecting its nest.
A big, nasty vulture is sitting here, protecting its nest.

You find yourself at the top of the outcrop. The view from this spot extends for many miles around. On the west, the river Anduin can barely be discerned. Far to the east, running from north to south, the dark line of Mirkwood marks the boundaries of the grasslands. Closer at hand, a strange circle of small stones and dead branches has been built in a crack of the rock.
17794: A barn-owl is here, looking for easy prey.

Only about eight feet above the floor of the stables, this fairly narrow loft has bales of hay stacked two and three deep from one end to the other. Peering over the hay down into the stables, one can see a row of wooden troughs and a seemingly endless row of stalls. From this vantage point, one can also clearly see all three entrances to the stables. Also, three narrow slits on the south, east, and western walls provide a good view of the land for several miles.
17795:
There are three large barrels here.
A rather dirty young boy is here, ready to tend to the stable.

Spacious, yet draughty and quite smelly, this large wooden building has stalls for about two dozen steeds. Hay conceals the earthen floor of the stables plus the base of a large wooden trough in the centre of the room. A few barrels are piled against the northern wall next to a wide, covered pathway leading toward the tavern. Almost curiously, vines from the trellises of the passage climb up the walls and twist their way along the beams and rafters of the high ceiling, past the loft on the southern wall and outside through the three open windows.
17796: Meticulously crafted from thin, delicate-looking wooden slats, the latticework overhead is covered with thick, winding vines. From the tavern on the northern side to the stables in the south, the lush, green espalier gently flows across the trellises, sometimes spilling onto the nearby buildings, but often pouring down the walls to meet the grass on the edges of the path. A break in the wall to the west reveals a small shop beyond a narrow wooden door. Right above the door rests a white sign painted with green letters to match the flora.
17797: A teenager is here, looking after the shop.

Wide, squatty windows placed right under the ceiling make the room seem airy. The wooden walls are decorated with intricately carved panels with different motifs, some obviously of foreign origin. Tall racks packed to their limits with various clothing stand along the south wall. Behind the counter in the northwest corner, there is a closed wooden cabinet, and several shelves with various miscellaneous objects are situated in the west part of the shop.
17798:
A small oaken table has been set here.
A sturdy man wearing weather-beaten clothes is here carrying a lute.
A barman watches you calmly, while skilfully mixing a drink.

The tavern itself is lit dimly by four sets of candles suspended from the high, sloped wooden ceiling. A larger fifth set of candles located in the centre of the room appears to have given its last flame. As a result, the corners of the tavern are much brighter than the middle where most of the customers sit, talking loudly and enjoying their meals. Just west of the bar serving food and drinks in the northeastern corner is a short corridor leading to what appears to be an inn. Opposite the corridor a long covered passageway heads south through an empty doorframe. Small torches reflect on the smooth, polished wooden floor and frame the sturdy metal doors on the east and western walls.
17799: Jasper the Tavern Keeper is keeping an eye on his customers.

Not more than ten feet in each direction, this room serves as a reception area for the inn. A long counter about three feet in elevation sits near the western wall with a small note nailed to the side facing the centre of the room. Simple carvings adorn the edges of the countertop, and its surface is smooth except in the places it has been scratched. A tall, narrow red curtain runs from floor to ceiling in the middle of the northern wall, concealing whatever lies beyond it.
17804: You have climbed out onto a branch of the tree. From here you have a fine view of the river below and to the north, a small stream to the east, and the grasslands surrounding the tree.
17805: You are within a small alcove of the tree house, which appears to be a simple sleeping area. A pile of soft furs is on the floor, and a few hooks adorn the southern wall. You can return to the living area through the opening in the north wall.
17806:
A Dwarven battering ram stands here.
The corpse of a doorwarden is lying here.
A doorwarden is here, fighting Vat.
Guano the Cave Troll is here, fighting a doorwarden.
Kong the Hill Troll is here, fighting a doorwarden.
Goliath (GG), wielding a great warsword, is here, fighting a doorwarden.

Scorpion the Tarkhnarb Orc, wielding a black metal staff, is standing here.
A hungry warg stands here, sniffing around for flesh.
Prasil, wielding a mighty dwarven axe, is here, fighting a doorwarden.
Vat is here, fighting a doorwarden.
Fart the Cave Troll is standing here.
Nugs, wielding an ornate, steel-shafted warhammer, is standing here.
Gigant the Cave Troll is here, fighting a doorwarden.

Ismashu is standing here.
Earthquake, wielding a great warsword, is standing here.

Tollo the Cave Troll is here, fighting a doorwarden.
Spears is standing here.

Vesor the Black Numenorean, wielding an engraved broadsword, is standing here.
A beautiful and docile horse is standing here.
Manandoun the Hill Troll (MM) is standing here.
Himzelf is standing here.
Monster the Cave Troll is standing here.
Teh, wielding a war mattock, is standing here.
Xirt, wielding an ornate, steel-shafted warhammer, is standing here.
Vurgh the Cave Troll is standing here.

The walls of this stone entryway were carved long ago by the hands of superior Dwarven engineers. The walls and floor have a sturdy look, and the stone comprising the ceiling contains intricate carvings of battle scenes.
17807: This lengthy stone hallway shows the remarkable skill of its builders. In addition to the intricately-carved and gem-laden floor, walls and ceilings, numerous statues are positioned throughout the lengthy hall. A closer examination of the statues reveals that they celebrate the heroic deeds of legendary dwarves.
17808: A massive arched ceiling traverses the entire length of this long, stone hallway. Doric columns run the distance of the passage and help support the heavy ceiling. Underneath foot, carved tiles possess elaborate designs. A gigantic marble statue standing in the centre of the hall depicts a dwarf holding a gigantic weapon. To the south lies a similar stone chamber while to the north a huge table is barely visible.
17809: Torches in the wall provide nominal light throughout this lofty, vaulted room. A great, ring-shaped table made of carved stone dominates the centre of the room. Deftly crafted chairs surround the table. The seats number at least a dozen, indicative that someone utilizes this room for extremely large meetings. A door to the east leads into a small stone alcove while the path to the south opens into a large arched passageway.
17810: A stout Dwarven steward stands here, ready to defend the home.

Carved from the dense limestone prevalent in this area, this modest stone dwelling possesses smooth walls and a well-worn floor. A disheveled desk made from wood stands in the corner. Papers covered with various numbers crowd the desk. A small door to the west leads into a dimly lit space dominated by a large table.
17811: This splendid stone vestibule features polished marble floors and beautiful jade ornamentation. The complex carvings picture mostly battle and hunting scenes. A large, exceptional statue is displayed prominently in the centre of the room. To the east there is a small wooden door while a sturdy iron door blocks the way to the west.
17812: This magnificent stone hall extends from above and below. Although the walls are solid granite, they were carved and polished brilliantly by master craftsmen. While the room has many small figurines, one larger statue honouring the god Thoiram is the focal point of this area.
17813: Lit by tin lanterns fixed on the stone walls, this area is cluttered with a variety of shields, breastplates and other assorted ring mail and chain mail armour pieces. Tools and pieces of armour being repaired lie on a large, oaken work table in one corner of the room. In another corner, iron bars are stacked neatly in preparation for future use.
17814: A stout Dwarven steward stands here, ready to defend the home.

Carved from dense igneous bedrock, this crude chamber lacks the fancy statues and masonry that are prevalent in this area. A diminutive fireplace in one corner of the room reveals unadorned, rough walls while wrought stones and boulders form an assortment of furniture.
17815: A stout Dwarven steward stands here, ready to defend the home.

In contrast to the otherwise clean rooms in this home, this place is a mess. Weapons and armour hang randomly on the walls, without thought for order or property. Axes and hammers dominate the ranks of weapons, as they seem to be the inhabitant's weapon of choice. On the right wall, you see old breastplates and other pieces of beaten-up armour hanging. They were probably used in battles long ago.
17816: A small rat runs about, oblivious to your presence.

You have entered a dark and simple hole which was probably once used as a storage place. The rotten remains of something can still be found here and there. Empty crates and barrels are piled up against southern wall.
17817: A hobbit is here walking around.

The single room building is a small but functional home for one of the many hobbits living in the village. There is a small kitchen area in one corner and a bedroom area in another corner. However, thin curtain partitions make the two areas into small rooms in themselves. Right in front of you are a pair of armchairs and a table and some chairs.
17818: It is quite clear that the owner of this house did not save money in arranging this room. The massive mahogany desk and chairs are nicely crafted and painted, on the walls you can see paintings and even the fireplace is well decorated. The floor is covered by a compact carpet which makes walking comfortable even without boots. The large window in the western wall gives a nice view over a well maintained garden.
17819: You have entered a rather large living room. Most of the space in this room is occupied by a large square wooden desk placed in the middle. The desk is skillfully decorated everywhere where it does not hurt its functionality. In the western wall the huge stone fireplace is placed, which seems to be able to warm up all the room.
17820: This room has that strange aroma which you can find in all better equipped kitchens. Along the eastern wall there is a huge and nicely decorated cook-range with space for a lot of pots. A fine looking cupboard is occupying the western wall. The cupboard contains a lot of pots, plates and glasses. The other equipment is having the best position to be able to make cooking fast and enjoyable as much as possible.
17821: This is the entrance to a big house built of stone. The accessway from the gate to the door is made by stone bricks with a small red carpet in front of the house door. Besides the small accessway someone put a lot of effort to maintain a garden with many different kinds of flowers. The garden is demarcated to the north and the south by a small stone wall.
17822: A fallow deer is grazing peacefully here.

You look about in wonder. This plain appears to be well-tended. There are various signs of cultivation. You realise that it is allowed to run wild, but in a controlled state. The plain is teeming with life. You are standing in the southwest corner of the plain. It stretches to the north and to the east.
17823: The newly built stables of Rushey stand freshly painted just west of the old River Inn. The structure is made out of logs with a thatched roof to keep the worst rains out and several large boxes has been created to allow a number of mounts to be housed while their owner visits the tavern. A small plaque can be seen next to the exit.
17826: Halfway up the massive trunk of the tree there is a large crow nest made of branches put together hastily. Some of the branches crack when stepped upon. In fact most of the branches seem to be dead, but there are still quite a few thick branches stretching out from the trunk.
17827:
A brown bear is sleeping here.
A brown bear is sleeping here.
A brown bear is sleeping here.

This peculiar-looking cave could be better described as a prolonged crack in the face of the hill. The crack looks as if it may have been caused by a tremor that rippled through the earth long ago, because it is very narrow with a high ceiling. The crack ends in a smooth, rounded hemisphere, forming a cosy home for a warg or, perhaps, a bear.
17830:
The corpse of a bent, drooling troll is lying here.
The corpse of a demon wolf is lying here.
The shadow of a bent, drooling troll is floating here.

This smelly lair has been coarsely dug in the earthy ground. Long, twisted roots hang from the wet ceiling. The remnants of the rotten undergrowth lie everywhere. The stench of dead vegetation is piercingly strong, only to be accentuated by the suffocating smell of several putrid corpses and other filth of undetermined origin. Here and there a dim glint of metal attracts the eye to some rusty tools half-buried among the decayed rubbish.
17831: You find yourself at the top of a huge tree standing several feet out of the impenetrable, tangled foliage. Here at the treetop, however, the leaves bear a much more wholesome appearance, as if the fresh air and the warm sunlight had breathed renewed energy into them, revitalizing them. The forest ceiling spreads all about below, like a sinister, waving sea. And the thick trunk rises up above the dark-green waters, like a lofty, natural lighthouse.
17832: A big cavebear is padding around here (red aura).

A spacious cavern opens inside the ancient hill. It is shrouded in darkness and silence reigns, yet the atmosphere is warm and sultry. The walls are of bare rock, with sharpened edges and angular shapes, and the ground seems uneven and unsafe. A closer inspection reveals deep scratches and shreds of thick hair lying on the ground, unequivocal sign that some large beast inhabits this big grotto.
17835:
A spirit floats towards you and howls with an evil laughter.
A spirit floats towards you and howls with an evil laughter.

It was a bad idea to come down here. The smell here is twenty times worse than it was up above. The coffin you are standing in the middle of has long rotted away, and only its general shape remains. The bones of whomever was buried here are still intact. You have an odd feeling that you and the corpse are not the only ones here.
17836: A humble man stands here, ready to help you with your things.

The view from this room may indeed be unsurpassed on arda. Thick crystal walls surround the chamber, leaving your eyes to wander across the vast ocean to the west and back to the towers and other buildings of Grey Havens to the east. Several padded benches are here, providing a comfortable spot to rest regardless of which view you wish to enjoy. The floor is polished white marble. Several marble columns carved into great trees seem to grow from the very stone of the floor.
17838: A sparrow is flapping around on the ground.

In the north you can barely see the road to the Grey Havens. You are standing in an endless-looking ocean of grass. The colour of the grass changes between bright green and the brown-yellow of dried out grass. Further in the south the vegetation becomes more dense. In the east, the fields appear a bit rough.
17840: Drazud (freshmeat), wielding a black metal staff, is standing here.

The room is twenty by twenty yards with the ceiling about five yards up. The walls, initially painted with light and colourful scenery of the nature, has now been painted with vertical stripes of black conceiling most of the initial painting. There are identical exits north, south, east and west. The exits are framed with golden glowing sculptures of snakes. A veil of shadows conceils what is hidden behind the exits.
17841: The room is twenty by twenty yards with the ceiling about five yards up. The walls, initially painted with light and colourful scenery of the nature, has now been painted with vertical stripes of black conceiling most of the initial painting. There are identical exits north, south, east and west. The exits are framed with golden glowing sculptures of snakes. A veil of shadows conceils what is hidden behind the exits.
17842: You stand in a room sized 20 by 20 metres, and 5 metres to the ceiling. The walls, initially painted with light and colourful scenery of the nature, have now been painted with vertical stripes of black, concealing most of the initial painting. There are identical exits north, south, east and west. The exits are framed with golden, glowing sculptures of snakes. There is a veil of shadows, conceiling what is hidden behind the portals.
17843: You stand in a room sized 20 by 20 metres, and 5 metres to the ceiling. The walls, initially painted with light and colourful scenery of the nature, have now been painted with vertical stripes of black, conceiling most of the initial painting. There are identical exits north, south, east and west. The exits are framed with golden, glowing sculptures of snakes. There is a veil of shadows, conceiling what is hidden behind the portals.
17846:
A mighty wight-noble is watching you.
A mighty wight-noble is watching you.
The lord of wights floats here, its red eyes filled with hatred.
A mighty wight-noble is watching you.
A mighty wight-noble is watching you.

This is the large hall of an old Angmar lord. It is fifty by eighty yards, and lit by dim shining stones set into grasping skeleton hands protruding from the walls. Towards the northern wall, raised approximately six inches above the floorlevel, stands an ivory throne. It has no markings. Along the walls there are broken statues. An exit framed with golden snakes leads south into a system of corridors, and a large portal leads west.
17847: A large chest of stone sits solidly here.

A small cavern has been hollowed out in the rock. The walls are rough as well as the floor and roof. Littered about the room are several broken wooden creates and a few weapon racks and armour pegs. The air is dry and still and not a single sound can be heard. Against the back wall stands a huge intact stone chest.
17850:
A war-weary wight-warrior is standing here.
A war-weary wight-warrior is standing here.

Walls of stone surround you completely, except for the staircase going up. There are no ornaments, no altars, no colours and no coffins, just bare, grey stonewalls. The room is about five yards by five, and ten feet high.
17855: The staircase ends here as it reaches its top at a small landing. There is a doorway on the western wall, and a ladder which leads up to the top of the tower.
17856: An experienced Dunadan officer is standing here, keeping things under control.

You are standing on the top of this old, crumbling tower. Like everything else in Fornost, it has been heavily patched, so you proceed with caution as you lean on the battlement and adore the splendid view of Fornost and its outskirts. This would make a great spot to watch anyone moving on the road that leads south from Fornost. A high cliff with a castle on its top blocks your view westwards.
17857:
A Dunadan gateguard is standing here.
An experienced Dunadan officer is standing here, keeping things under control.

You stand in a room which contains lots of strange machinery, some winches and a fireplace with a big pile of dry wood beside it. By the size of this fireplace you can tell it is not made to keep the soldiers warm and dry, but rather to warm up a large pot containing a thick fluid, probably oil of some kind. The pot is mounted on an axis which allows it to be tilted, so its contents can be poured down through holes in the floor. You look through these holes and see the passageway between the gate and the portcullis. An old, worn book has been thrown away in a corner.
17858: Various pieces of machinery, fallen into disrepair from lack of care, lie in one part of the room, next to spare pots of oil for the defence of the Fornost gates. An empty rack at one time may have held spare weapons for the soldiers, or a last-ditch defence should the evil of Angmar strike the city again. This place has been recently maintained however, and a heavy black curtain stretches across the top of the stairs leading up. A few open barrels store reserves of drinking water for the city.
17859: A humble man stands here, ready to help you with your things.

This tower room is wide with curving walls, which vault upwards into a larger ceiling, from which hangs suspended a sparkling crystal chandelier, decked with scented candles, which gives the room a rather relaxed and peaceful atmosphere. Dim light is supplied from the overhead candles and the fireplace, which still has a few logs that remain in it, ready to warm the interior against a harsh winter. The floor is covered with rich plush carpeting, and the walls are hung with tapestries. A large bookcase stands here, filled with ancient tomes. A luxurious bed stands in the corner, covered with furs and silks.
17860: You are standing on the top of this old, crumbling tower. Like everything else in Fornost, it has been heavily patched, so you proceed with caution as you lean on the battlement and adore the splendid view of Fornost and its outskirts. Thick green forests lie to the west, as well as the ruined parts of the city, that have fallen into decay. A brightly-coloured banner hangs from the ramparts, flapping in the wind.
17870: A humble man stands here, ready to help you with your things.

You have entered a vast chamber with rough and irregular stone walls which rise almost fifty feet above you. The floor has been carved smooth, and against the northern end an area has been furnished with carpets, a large desk, several shelves and a huge canopied bed. The area is poorly lit by several sconces built into the walls, barely revealing the corners of the room. The air is cool and moist, and you can hear the trinkle of water echoing faintly.
17871: A war-weary wight-warrior is standing here.

Walls of stone surround you completely, except for the staircase going up. There are no ornaments, no altars, no colours and no coffins, just bare, grey stonewalls. The room is about five yards by five, and ten feet high.
17872: One can tell from the thick vegetation and the loud hum of insects on the sides of the path that a bog is nearby. The path leads eastwards while to the north a trail breaks in between the sedges.
17873: A clear spring babbles as cool water trickles out of the ground.

The maker of this home took advantage of a crystal formation in the hill. During the day sunlight filters down and creates a myriad of rainbows which shimmer in the mist from a spring. The spring pours into a small basin in the floor before it flows out again through a hole in the wall.
17874:
A black snake hurries towards you with sly intentions.
A black snake hurries towards you with sly intentions.
A black snake hurries towards you with sly intentions.

You are standing in the bottom of a deep well. The sides are slick with moisture, making its walls unclimbable. It is quite large in circumference, but quite empty, the water it once held long gone. The ground squishes underneath your boot and the air is quite chill, a draft blowing from some unknown source. Your breath materialises in front of you, like a spirit rising from the netherworld.
17875: A wooden chest stands in the corner.

At the top of the stairs there is another well decorated room. There is a large four poster bed against one wall, with some heavy red velvet drapes at at the windows. A large wardrobe leans against another wall.
17876:
A large bulletin board, entitled "Mages' Guild", is mounted here.
An elven woman is here merrily walking along.

This room is reserved for private discussions among sorcerers. Here they can share with each their knowledge of both old and new spells. Information about how a spell works and when it probably should not be used can often be heard in this chamber. The lighting is dim and it is furnished with several couches.
17877: A large bulletin board, entitled "Clerics' Guild", is mounted here.

This softly lit room, illuminated with a pale blue radiance, serves as a sanctuary for those that worship Osse or Uinen. Little in the way of sculpture or artwork adorns these walls. Simple depictions of ocean scenes serve as pious decorations. Contrasting images of the peace of a calm sea and the might of a raging maelstrom come to mind as you rest here.
17880: A hairy black spider wraps up a silken package with her hind legs.

A layer of opaque material covers this entire enclosure. Occasionally stems of waterweeds are visible that have been weaved into the cocoon. Rocky walls can be seen through a small section of thinner material, the rest of the outside world is hidden by the silky webbing. The air here is thick and smells strangely. There is a single exit through a small opening downwards and west, out of the chamber. A number of bones wrapped in a silky package hang on the sides of the waterproof enclosure.
17881: You are standing at the bottom of a deep pit. The walls are very smooth and hard. There is a hole in the roof, but it is beyond your reach. Examining the walls more carefully, you discover the presence of a tiny stair, carved in the rock that may allow you to reach higher to a point where there has to be an exit at the end of the steps. Even though the climbing is rough and quite dangerous, there is simply no alternative.
17882: You find yourself upon a very wide branch, the middle of which has been hollowed out. The remaining depression is used as a natural basin in which water pools occasionally, providing an inviting area for birds to bathe in. Several other branches stretch out to form a kind of platform which is very stable to walk on. To the west, the branch grows thicker as one makes the way back to the tree house.
17888: Small, exquisitely carved, ebony lamps hang every few feet around the smooth, stone walls. Around two large oaken tables stand eight robust chairs, embellished with delicate inlays of ivory and small glistening gems. On the floor, a couple large, soft carpets efficiently reduce the echoes in the large living room. The spiral staircase continues up and down.
17889: A humble man stands here, ready to help you with your things.

A large fireplace is situated in the middle of the room just a few feet to the left of where the spiral staircase ends. In front of the fireplace, two large chairs stand beside a low table. The light from the fireplace is reflected by small gems inlaid in the snow-white, arched roof. By the northern wall, beside a large closet, stands a large bed made of finest oak.
17890:
A large bookshelf sits against the wall.
On the bookshelf, there are a map of Bree and a map of Fornost.
A Dunadan soldier is here busily performing his duties.
An experienced Dunadan officer is standing here, keeping things under control.
An insolent scholar is here, pondering.

You have entered a large hall on the upper floor of the library, which contain the collection. The room has the obvious furniture: Shelves, shelves and more shelves, packed with books and scrolls. The hall extends further west.
17891: The Librarian of Fornost sits here perusing a tome.

The bookcases here are not quite as packed as the ones in the eastern end of the hall, allowing space for the collection to grow. You can see a couple of comfortable chairs arranged in a circle around a table. There are also some ladders, which are needed to get books off the higher shelves.
17892: This stairwell is made from a very fine oakwood. The grain shows both strength and elegance. Both beautiful and fine carvings were added to the wooden walls that line the stairwell long ago. The floor of the stairwell consists of solid marble plates. The stairs connect the Modest Temple above, with the small but well built home below.
17893: Along the walls of this chamber many elegantly decorated chests have been placed. A dazzling display of light seem to originate from the chests, making their details difficult to distinguish. To the east a curved wooden stairway leads up while to the west an bright light shines.
17894: An Elven steward stands here, watching over the household.

As you enter this room the heat from the fireplace provides warmth that is otherwise absent from this cold dreary home. A huge glowing table shaped as a circle stands in the middle of the room. Two big chairs that like look miniature thrones have been placed next to the table on opposite sides of each other. In the eastern portion of this room a bed can be seen.
17895:
A giant, strange looking green fungus is here, ready to devour you in seconds.
A giant, strange looking green fungus is here, ready to devour you in seconds.

The walls and ceiling here are very wet, and moisture falls all around, pooling in any small crack or indentation on the floor. A putrescent smell pervades the whole chamber, and rotting flesh lies scattered all about, among the dust and rubble.
17896: Walls of smooth, grey stone surround you completely, except for the staircase leading up. There are no ornaments, altars, colours or coffins. Only the bare, grey stone walls can be seen in this empty room which measures about ten feet high and sixteen feet on each side.
17898: A Natural Bridge over a Fissure
A pack horse (Rood) is standing here, ridden by you.

The bumpy worn trail continues onto a bizarre natural bridge over the fissure, a slice of rock twenty foot wide. Below, the fissure drops away into depths too dark to perceive. Billowing grass with many small colourful flowers cover the rock here, a natural garden suspended on high.
17899: A rotten corpse is hanging here.

It appears that this is some foul beast's lair. All around are the remains of victims that have fallen to this chamber's owner. It looks as if many who have entered did not ever leave and some who have fled left limbs behind.
17900: The narrow valley turns here, allowing you to proceed to the west or to the south. A few tufts of grass grow along the path that is covered with footprints of orcs.
17901: This small overlook to the west of the trail affords a magnificent view of a deep forested valley to the south. West and north are nothing but the cold grey peaks of the Misty Mountains -- the tallest stretching thousands of metres above this vantage point.
17902: Gently sloping hills cover the landscape, all seeming to point to the south, where a dense, ominous forest broods. A couple thin, tortured trees cavort here painfully, their black limbs thrown about in strange positions. To the north lies a strip of barren marches.
17903: Four stone pillars support the domed ceiling of Moria's eastern gate. A great arch frames the impending darkness to the west. The two large bronze gates are nicked and marred in ancient battle. To the east can be seen a lush dale, the fragrance of pine and wildflowers fall in stark contrast to the dank humidity of the caves. The north and south yield sheer drops onto a talus covered field. Below, a wide marble staircase leads to the broken road of Durin's way.
17908:
A raft has been left here.
A large bat is here, hanging in the darkness.
A large bat is here, hanging in the darkness.
An ancient fungus smothers the boulders.
A cockroach is scuttling across the floor carrying some debris.

This cave is rather dark and wet. It was dug by the Sirannon many years ago, when the level of the river was higher than now. The walls are made of smooth rock, polished by the stream during the centuries, but now covered by moss. An acid smell and the white guano on the ground prove that birds or bats choose to live in this damp cave.
17916: Though it is almost vertical in places, there seems to be no difficulty in climbing up or down this narrow, sloping tunnel, as there are many large rocky outcroppings, which almost seem like a stair. The ceiling above is beaded with small droplets of water, which drip all around, creating a quiet splash as they hit the stony floor.
17917:
A water moccasin slithers out of sight just below the surface of the water.
A water moccasin slithers out of sight just below the surface of the water.
A water moccasin slithers out of sight just below the surface of the water.

The cavern creaks with the pressure of the river above, and the ceiling bulges downward, as if barely able to support its own weight. Water pours in from above, running down the walls to add to the flow in this tunnel, and the rock all around has been worn quite smooth by its unending flow.
17919: An albino fish is swimming here, looking for some food.

Cold water seeps in on all sides, adding to the eastward flow, which continues its way through a small opening in the rock wall. To the north lies a stony landing, whilst to the west, the stream stretches onward into the darkness.
17920: An albino salamander is here, perched on some rocks.

Water floods into the cavern from the river above, but the sloping floor causes rapid drainage, into the beginning of an underground stream, to the west. Large stalactites hang down from the ceiling, reaching to the floor in places, like massive columns, seeming to support the cave. The walls to each side are pitted with innumerable tiny holes, which might be the home to small creatures of the darkness, and animal bones lie scattered about the floor.
17921: A little stone lies on the ground.

No sound is to be heard, except for the insistent flow of the river above. The very presence of this sound is unsettling, and the many cracks and fissures in the roof of this small chamber, through which water trickles and drips, can only add to the impression that one day the river will break through, and flood this area.
17922: This hallway is the centre of the upper floor of this farmhouse. There are two doorways, one is at the north end of the hall and the other is to the east. The ceiling is made up of a series of boards placed next to each other. Some of the boards seem to be older than the others.
17923:
A rather heavy clay jar stands here.
A rather heavy clay jar stands here.
A beer barrel has been left here.
A sack of flour has been placed here.
A small vicious black rat squeaks at you for disturbing it.
A giant rat patters against you, squeaking maliciously.
A giant rat patters against you, squeaking maliciously.
A small vicious black rat squeaks at you for disturbing it.
A giant rat patters against you, squeaking maliciously.

This small room is cold but quite dry. The floor is made of hard-packed earth, which has a slight, but not overpowering, musty odour. Judging by the neat row of shelves along each wall, this place was obviously constructed with storage in mind.
17924:
A wooden top is lying on its side.
A cute little girl is here.

This rustic bedroom is small, but well furnished. The small bed in one corner seems to indicate that a young child sleeps in here. The large toy-chest, which stands at the foot of the bed, also suggests that this is a child's room.
17925: A woman is here, looking for someone to chat with.

This comparitively spacious chamber must be the bedroom of the owner of the farm. Though simple in style, the furnishings are all well-made, hewn from the finest oak. A large bed stands against one wall, beneath a curtained window, and a copious wardrobe stands beside the door.
17926:
A small pile of copper pennies lies here.
A simple wooden chest is here.
A black spider crawls here, a shiny red spot visible on its belly.
A black spider crawls here, a shiny red spot visible on its belly.

A strong smell of musty and stagnant air pierces your nostrils. The roof is rather low, and anyone taller than a human child would need to stoop in this place, to avoid a nasty knock on the head. Every part of the room is covered in a thick and choking layer of dust.
17927: Inside a hole stained with blood, you find a large cave. It shows signs of habitation, with strewn bones and mouldy pieces of something even an orc will not eat. Some chairs are put around a large table, which is covered with bones and other dead parts of animals or human beings. However, this cave does not seem like others you have seen in this area. Shields marked with strange pictures and walls with strange colours mark this cave as an alien one. What once must have been an opening in the northern wall is now completely covered with debris. The only way out is to the west.
17928:
A greenish slime mould is here, smelling badly.
A filthy straw pallet is lying here.
A small pool of water has collected on the ground.
A greenish slime mould is here, smelling badly.

You are in a dark and spartan cave which you recognise as the birthplace of the Troll race. This recognition is one of racial rather than personal memory, on the wall is a mural of an imposing dark clothed person standing above a collection of hideous monsters some of which resemble yourself. Your pitiful mind struggles to draw meaning from the picture but it fails.
17929:
A large bulletin board, entitled "Numenorean Chronicles", is mounted here.
A large bonfire is burning here.

After the fall of Numenor only some of the shores that were once colonized remained property of the 'pure blooded' as the fierce Black Numenoreans called themselves. You are standing in one of those places and the landscape reminds you of Eru's wrath and the days of the Fall. Where once stood the glorious purple temples for the Black Lord's worship, dark ruins fester like wounds upon the land. But, who knows, some power might still hide through the shadows of the past...
17930:
There are nine loaves of bread here.
There are two large sacks here.
A mailbox stands here stuffed full of messages.
Water drips slowly into a grey, still pool.
A large, engraved sarcophagus lies on the floor.
On the sarcophagus, there are eight torches, a pair of ashen grey pants, and an ashen grey shirt.

You find yourself in the ancient crypt of a Numenorean prince. Glyphs are etched into the walls, still clear after so many years. The carvings depict the struggle of the proud Numenoreans against the deathless Elves and Valar. The defeat of Ar-Pharazon's fleet and the diminution of Sauron's power is also portrayed, with the aims of the surviving people set on complete revenge over all of Arda. On the floor itself there are broken pieces of weapons and armour strewn about. Perhaps with some luck, a clever adventurer might find something still of use. Above, dark waters leak through into the crypt.
17931: The burnt and blackened skeletal remains of a human are here.
