18744: The fertile grassland underfoot continues unabated in every direction. Several small conifer trees grow on the prairie and provide minimal shelter from the elements. The only discernible breaks to the abundant grasslands are a few small foothills in the north and a small trail running across the southern and eastern horizons.
18745: Prickly, white-stemmed plants, with blue flower heads grow in abundance.

Thick snarls of thistles cover the grasslands everywhere. Standing nearly two feet high, the thistles are marked by sharp barbs and small, purple flowers. Far to the north lie several small foothills, while to the southwest runs a small road. Vast, undulating plains dominate the remaining landscape.
18746: Dense, yellow-green grass covers most of the plains with the exception of a trail perceptible to both the west and south. The edges of stones thrust from among the grass and make travel tiresome. Sprouts of clover rise amidst the grass and create a thick tangle, which serves to further hinder travel.
18747: The stone-strewn land to the north slowly gives way to a lush, grassy plain spotted by several copses of hickory trees as well as plentiful clusters of cowslip. Similarly sculpted grasslands extend to the east and south. Far to the west, the fast-moving waters of the River Isen are barely discernible.
18748: A finch flies low above the ground.

Small boulders and tiny stones lie strewn atop the grass from a recent rockslide down the hills to the north. Tufts of grass poke out from among the stones. The rocks slowly give way to tough, green grass that stretches far to the south and east. A small trail is barely discernible to the southwest.
18749: Tiny mounds gradually give way to foothills in the north. Numerous boulders and smaller stones mar the thinning grass. Small patches of vegetation also gash the withered grass in places, leaving large clumps of soil uncovered. To the northwest lies the peak of the small foothills while to the south and west lie smooth, flourishing grasslands.
18750:
Yellow flowers, with grey-green foliage, grow in clusters here.
A cute rabbit is here.
A cute rabbit is here.

Buttercups and foxglove grow abundantly here, a stark contrast to the coarse and stony grassland to the north. Vibrant flowers can be seen in all around. Lesser foothills to the northwest and the craggy plains to the north represent the only break to the predominant sea of grass throughout the area.
18751: Yellow flowers, with grey-green foliage, grow in clusters here.

Abundant flowers grow unrestrained. Flowers with yellow centres and sun-kissed petals represent the most copious variety. To the west, additional clusters of untamed plant life sits atop the green prairies. In the east the beautiful flowers end abruptly and give way to dry earth possessing little vegetation; a vivid contrast to the rolling plains prevalent in the south.
18752: Rough weed grass represents the only form of vegetation in this dry, forsaken plain. Small cracks in the earth reveal a dire lack of water and the cause of the lack of plant life. The area to the north and west provide a stark contrast to the arid conditions here as flora and even a few trees can be seen. To the south and east, the desiccated landscape continues.
18753: Marked by thinning grass and large blotches of bare earth, the ground appears dry and plagued by cracks. Although little vegetation grows here, few stones mar the landscape. A close look at the scorched earth divulges the tracks of the small animals that inhabit the plains. In all directions, grass grows more profusely but remains disfigured by stones and other markings.
18754: Leading away to both the east and south, a small trail splits the grassy meadows in two. A large number of rocks and stones lie strewn atop the roadway, most likely ripped from the roadway by some traveller. Thick, plush grass covers the land on both sides of the road. The grassland to the north appears particularly vibrant.
18755: From the west, the trail winds slowly across the rolling meads. Large, deep ruts mar the road's ragged surface in places, adding to the danger created by other holes. The trail narrows considerably to the northeast as it cuts between a river to the east and a forest to the northeast. To the south, a large number of cattails stands beside a peaty bog. In the north, lush grassland covers the floor of the vale.
18756: A shrub with maple-like leaves is growing here.

Short and trampled straws lay between the patches of green grass. Some sleek and tender bushes stretch their branches a few feet above the ground. The light brown soil is damp and fertile with puddles of water forming here and there. A trail can be seen nearby in the west.
18757: A brown fox is here, looking for some rabbits to chew up.

A few streaks of grass and small bushes mark the edges of the sodden ground. The soil is brown and muddy forming an intricate pattern of dark brown and green where the grass starts to grow again. A small stream can be seen making its way southwards in the east. The faint sound of a waterfall can be heard at some distance in the north. The plains stretch away far to the southern and western horizons.
18758: The stream slowly grows wider and easier to navigate along its southward course. A couple of bushes grow on the grassy banks of the waterway. The faint sound of rushing water can be heard coming from the north where the current seems to get somewhat stronger. The water here is too muddy and deep to make out the bottom of the stream.
18759:
A restless rabbit bounces around.
A field lark stands here, focused on finding food.

Coarse yellow-green grasses, about two feet high, cover the plains. A grove of young trees lies to the north, where the faint sound of a waterfall can be heard coming from. A stream running southwards can be seen cutting across the plains in the west where it bends this way, passing nearby in the south.
18760: The yard has long since overgrown with tall, wild grasses and weeds. In the east stands a decaying hay barn, its wooden walls are about to fall apart and the roof has partially collapsed. To the north lies the remains of the farmhouse, now just a pile of blackened stones and rotting boards with only two of its crumbling walls still standing. A dusty path overgrown with weeds leads west to the fields.
18761: Pieces of rotting boards lie scattered amidst a decomposing pile of hay where the roof has partially collapsed. The wooden walls are barely standing, one of the walls tilts outwards at an awkward angle and the rotting floorboards creak menacingly underfoot, as if it could give in at any moment. To the west lies the farmyard, overgrown with weeds.
18762:
A brown snake watches you.
A brown snake watches you.
A large brown snake with black patches is coiled here.

Some twisted roots stick out from the dirt and could possibly be used to climb out of the dark, seven feet deep hole. The floor of the hole is covered in rocks and debris from the cave in. The pungent smell of decomposing hay wafts in from the barn above.
18763:
The corpse of a vicious rat is lying here.
The corpse of a vicious rat is lying here.
The burnt and blackened skeletal remains of a human are here.

A pile of blackened stones, rotting boards and two crumbling stone walls are what remains of the farmhouse. By the looks of it, the house has been pillaged and burned down; nothing of value lies amidst the rubble. To the south lies the farmyard, overgrown with tall grasses and weeds, a decaying wooden barn barely standing on the east side of the yard.
18765: A wooden chest stands in the corner.

Coarse timbers form the frame of this small structure. Between the timbers lies mud, designed to provide further protection from inclement weather. Rough-hewn wooden boards comprise the floor of the structure. In several places, hay lies atop the rough boards. Farming implements line a rustic rack on the southern wall.
18766: Storage Shed beside the Neglected Courtyard
A tall Dunlending man stands here, sad and solemn.

At one time, this diminutive shed housed many of the implements needed to run a self-sufficient farmstead. Deep nicks and scratches mar the surface of a long bench along the southern wall. A hefty, circular block of wood stands along the eastern wall while a small doorway to the north leads to a courtyard occupied by weeds and other scrub brush.
18767:
A burly blacksmith is here, working at his anvil.
A Rohir boy is here, running around.

This dwelling must have been built with two purposes in mind because no sane craftsman would have left the eastern wall half open. The eastern wall simply stops half way between the north and south walls, leaving a wide opening. A massive animal hide hangs from a nail near the opening, apparently a makeshift door. A very large stove has been built into the eastern wall as well, allowing someone to use it both within the house and without. A proliferation of metal working tools hangs upon the walls inside this house and just beyond the door a black anvil rests. Along the western wall, two soot covered beds and a small table can just be discerned under the pile of filthy clothes.
18768:
A well used clothes line is strung between two walls.
A circular stone well has been built here.
A young milkmaid is here, taking a break between chores.
A little Rohir girl peers about shyly.

Inside this small circle of homes, one is witness to a rare site in these hotly contested plains, a Rohir homestead. A few small homes have been built in a circle surrounding a communal well, a few young trees and some strategically placed benches. All the houses are made from large flat stones and split logs, apparently to conserve the hard-to-come-by wood. The thatched roof of every house appears well cared for. However the real connection between all these houses is not their appearance but their clotheslines. Strung up between every house are clotheslines, connecting one neighbour to the next. Then each house has put up a second line between their house and the nearest tree. The whole of the village takes on the look of a massive spider web.
18769: A sturdy Rohir farmer is here planning his chores.

Entering this small dwelling, a multitude of smells reels your senses. A large variety of wild flowers and herbs grow from hanging planters, hooked into the ceiling by sturdy ropes. Long shelves are covered in dried or drying spices, stored for winter use. A stout wooden table sits in the centre of this one room home, surrounded by four simple chairs. A large but tattered cloth hangs across the western side of the house, forming a partition for the sleeping area.
18770: The interior of Dol Baran seems to have been hollowed out some time ago. One can only speculate as to the original purpose, perhaps to lie in wait for enemies. The walls are rough, as if carved by some blunt instruments. Wooden beams were built against the walls and ceiling as supports. A layer of dust covers the ground, making it almost impossible to discern how long it has been since anyone has been through here. To the west, a passage leads off into darkness.
18771: The support beams that lie to the east comes to an end in this section of the tunnel. The walls become gradually smoother from the east to the west. The ceiling is sloped along the contours of the hill above. There is no indication as to who may have built this place. A few bits of metal lies scattered about the ground, along with the occasional rock. The tunnel is very quiet, although sound would travel very easily through it.
18772: The surface of the passage walls is smooth and cool. Some sort of wall hanging, with faded dyes, has been suspended on the southern wall. It seems as if this was once inhabited. A small table lies along the western wall, but broken in many pieces. Faded papers are strewn all around the floor, but they are completely illegible, the ink must have faded long ago.
18773:
A black merlin waves its wings menacingly.
A black merlin waves its wings menacingly.
A black merlin waves its wings menacingly.
A black merlin waves its wings menacingly.

The ceiling in the cave is tall and rocks that lie scattered around are blocking the passage. Piles of bones and rotting corpses are on the ground, perhaps the remains of previous inhabitants. No farther travel is possible, because several large boulders, stones and other fallen debris line up on all sides.
18774: A handful of feathers are strewn upon the floor of this section of cavern, which is wider than the area to the south. The walls here lack the scars of claw marks visible to the south, as if whatever creature or creatures pass through here either took more care or had more room to manoeuvre. Towards the north, what might be a wooden support beam can be seen stretching high above.
18775: A large spool of thick, braided cord stands prominent against the western wall. Behind the spool, there seems to be a few yards of sturdy leather, which is marked to be cut and sewn. There are clearly wooden rafters, crossing the width of this place, only a few feet overhead. Some small feathers that might have covered the floor sit in a pile, nearby an old straw broom.
18776: A small vicious black rat squeaks at you for disturbing it.

The walls of this section of the tunnel are quite smooth unlike the adjacent caves. To the east, the ground slopes upwards towards a curve in the cave. The air is still and cool, seemingly undisturbed for some time. It appears as though any sounds would travel easily in here. Strange drawings mark the tough rocky wall to the south.
18777: The roughly-shaped walls run smoother to the west. It seems as though the bridge between the entrance, from the plains to the south, was added much later than the walls that run west. They are both cool and dry, unlike the slick, rough rock to the south. The ceiling overhead is low, but does not hamper progress. The ground slopes downwards to the west.
18778:
A small oaken table has been set here.
A sturdy bed made from solid oak lies here, covered in warm blankets.
An old man is here, a wild look on his face.

This small, side cavern is clearly man-made. The walls are rough, yet regular in the way it has been carved out of the side of the tunnel. Not much more than a place to put a small bed and desk, as this seems to be the resting place for whoever inhabits these tunnels.
18779: Something cold and scaly slithers past your leg.

The darkness swarms in around you as you descend into the channel. The walls of the channel are smooth from centuries of rushing water. Faint shapes can be discerned in the inky blackness, a pair of eyes bulging here and a flick of a tail there. The channel continues east into the abyss.
18780: Something cold and scaly slithers past your leg.

The water becomes colder, as beneath you the floor of the tunnel drops away into the inky blackness. The silvery flickers of small fish darting in, out, and between small nooks and crannies provide the only source of illumination. The walls of the tunnel are smooth from the erosion of centuries with only small pockets to provide anything to hold on to.
18781: A long slender eel glides along the water, its body coiled to strike.

The walls of the tunnel are covered in small holes and pockets, from some of which eyes, glinting in the blackness can be seen. The floor of the tunnel is covered with a fine dark sand absorbing any light that might manage to penetrate the gloom. The water is cold and sharp, biting your exposed flesh. The ceiling opens up leading towards what must be the surface and to the east the tunnel continues on into the dark depths.
18782: A long slender eel glides along the water, its body coiled to strike.

The submerged tunnel comes to a dead end, rocks closing in and creating passages too narrow for you to pass. Cracks and crevices line the walls, dark and glum in the icy cold water. Above, a piece of dark wood is jammed into the ceiling.
18783:
Some small rocks have been piled into a mound here.
A deranged man pierces you with fierce eyes.

This small chamber shows evidence of once being water-filled. The smooth and rounded walls together with piles of small, round stones on the floor are plain to see. However, traces of men are also evident, as sections of the wall have been chiselled to enlarge the cavern. In places, the workers have been slightly careless, and piles of rocks show where parts of the ceiling has caved in.
18784: This massive chamber was carved out of rock as dark as wet earth. The cavern was created by quickly flowing water, evidenced by the smooth, round edges on most surfaces. On the northern wall, a ruined tapestry has been nailed into the rock and is surrounded by deep etchings. A small lantern hangs from a tiny outcropping near the tattered wall covering. Broken pots, half-eaten food and battered clothing are just a few of the items that can be spotted in the trash that litters the floor near the light.
18785:
The corpse of a demented Dunlending is lying here.
The corpse of a demented Dunlending is lying here.

Rock walls, worn smooth by eons of water erosion, rise into the darkness. The ground quickly slopes down to the west and small rivulets of water form an unusual path into the darkness. On the southern wall, an extrusion in the wall mars its near pristine surface.
18786: The corpse of an eel is lying here.

A solid wall of rock blocks passage to the north. The cold water is beginning to sap your strength and your vision blurs in the icy blackness. Eyes glint in the darkness as the inhabitants of this tunnel move around. The tunnel continues to the south and the walls to either side are covered with shelves about a foot apart. This tunnel has been purposely made and then flooded some time later.
18787: The catacombs twist north and east. Many of the shelves adorning the walls of the tunnel have remains of old soldiers. Within some of the skeletons, eyes can be seen twinkling in the darkness. The floor of the catacomb has been worn smooth by the passage of time and water. Swimming in the icy water is rapidly depleting your strength, above you the ceiling is cracked in places.
18788: A long slender eel glides along the water, its body coiled to strike.

The catacomb bends to the south and west here. The remains of countless warriors lie in the shelves adorning the walls. The water here is cold and dark, piercing your clothes and sending a chill to your bones, sapping your strength every second you remain.
18789: Something cold and scaly slithers past your leg.

The darkness seems to engulf you in the icy waters of the catacombs. The walls are lined with shelves from floor to ceiling, within each shelf a solitary skeleton rests. The skeletons of past warriors seem to watch you pass with an eerie solace, as if they know you may get out of here alive but they will surely not. The catacombs lead off north and east into the dark water.
18790: Something cold and scaly slithers past your leg.

This section of the catacombs, now flooded, was hidden away for a purpose. The skeletons lying in the shelves that adorn the walls have the armour of officers and leaders. This section of the catacombs was for the higher ranking Numenoreans and was hidden away to prevent looting. The catacombs continue to the west and a ladder leading to the surface is visible on the eastern wall.
18791: An icy pool of water forms the floor of the tunnel. Treading the cold water is beginning to sap your strength. Looking down it is apparent that your feet can't touch the bottom. There is a ladder on the western wall leading up with the base of it immersed somewhere below. All around you are shelves containing the remains of many Numenoreans, these catacombs were built some time before they were flooded.
18792:
An animated skeleton is here, fighting Calarion.
Calarion the Elf, wielding a broadsword, is here, fighting an animated skeleton.
A large warhorse is standing here, clad in mail.

A large, domed tomb opens up before you. Occupying the centre is a large altar, its sides and top etched with runes in a language lost eons ago. The altar is black and seems to warp the space around it. The walls are lined with shelves, each containing the remains of a once great warrior. The remains replete with weapons and armour now rusted beyond repair. A tunnel opens up to the south and seems to be the only exit from this eerie place.
18793:
A skeleton of some humanoid lies in the dust.
A skeleton of some humanoid lies in the dust.

An eerie chill catches your breath. All the walls of this tomb are covered with shelves from floor to ceiling. Looking closer you can see each shelf contains the remains of a once great warrior replete with armour and weapons. The tomb was used to bury the fallen from the battlefield above. Silence rules this tomb and only the very brave dare utter a sound. The shelved walls continue on to a chamber to the north.
18794:
A wooden chest stands in the corner.
A foot-soldier of Rohan is here.

This large tent is the sleeping area for the Rohir soldiers of the camp. Sleeping mats lie in bundles along the sides, ready to be used. Small chests filled with personal belongings stand in a corner. The tent is rather dark, and only lit by a small fireplace in one of the corners.
18795:
A wooden chest stands in the corner.
A foot-soldier of Rohan is here.

This tent contains the sleeping area for the soldiers of the camp. The area can house a large number of men at the same time, but currently, all the sleeping mats are rolled up and stacked along one of the walls. The thick fabric of the tent does not allow much light to enter.
18796:
A wooden chest stands in the corner.
A swarthy Dunlending warrior is here, guarding his village against intruders.
A swarthy Dunlending warrior is here, guarding his village against intruders.
Mab the Dunlending Chieftain, wielding a sabre, is standing here.

The interior of this dwelling, though seemingly crude and squalid from without, is well furnished and decorated. The walls are of stone and timber, with the existing furniture being of carved wood and bronze. Some hand painted friezes of a clan history decorate the walls and the floor is covered in warm animal furs.
18797:
A simple wooden chest is here.
An old man is standing here.

This room consists of a little more than a cool and dry, solidly built hut, containing storage bins, barrels and shelves of useful stores for the hard winter months. The walls here are plain and undecorated, and the floor is of clean looking straw.
18798:
A circular stone well has been built here.
A swarthy Dunlending warrior is here, guarding his village against intruders.
A swarthy Dunlending warrior is here, guarding his village against intruders.

The ground underfoot is hard, packed earth, trampled by generations of clansmen. The dwellings inside the palisade are all squat, windowless, round huts with roofs made of hides and stone, with timber walls. Northward, there is a durable and well cared for hut, looking as though it belongs to someone of importance. To the south, the sturdy, low roofed, but somewhat run down, barracks seem to have seen better days.
18799:
A sickly hen is here, thinned from malnutrition.
A sickly hen is here, thinned from malnutrition.

The dwellings here, within the timber, palisade walls, seem to be of the typical Dunlending style. The houses are round and lack windows, with hide roofs with an opening in the centre which allows smoke from cooking fires to escape. There is a building to the north that has no such opening and has huge stacks of firewood piled up against the walls, while the smoky hut to the south looks large enough to be lived in by several families.
18800:
A small and well-kept fire lights and warms the room.
A small child is here playing happily.
A Dunlending woman is here tending to her children.

This vast and round, timber-walled hut contains thirty to forty woven sleeping mats. The focal point of the room is a smoking fireplace inside a shallow pit, which is surrounded by blackened stones. Some of the smoke from the fire escapes by a hole in the thatched roof high above, but almost as much seems to try to escape through the rest of the roof, the walls and the woven door.
18801: A swarthy Dunlending warrior is here, guarding his village against intruders.

The lack of natural light inside these barracks lends a certain degree of dinginess to the interior. Woven, sleeping mats are scattered around the floor and several, crude obscenities carved into the wooden walls give ample evidence that this is a building inhabited by men, as if the smell alone were not enough.
18802:
A small termite is running around making strange sounds.
A small termite is running around making strange sounds.
A small termite is running around making strange sounds.
A giant termite is here, crushing skulls and bones.

Just below the wagon, a large cavity has been dug out, creating a very large, termite's nest. They feed on the remnants of the rotting and decaying wagon together. The cavity itself is irregular and crude, clearly made by animals and littered with droppings, along with small carcasses and bones.
18803:
A huge, poisonous spider is here.
A huge, poisonous spider is here.

The deeper part of the basement lies in an eternal darkness. Most of the cellar has avoided destruction, but the decay is still a prominent feature of the room. Rotting shelves, barrels and containers litter the floor, and if there was anything of value left when the inhabitants left, it has vanished long ago.
18804:
A large bat is here, hanging in the darkness.
A fierce bat is here, lusting for your blood.
A huge bat is here, emitting piercing squeaks.

The old cellar is in a state of decay, its walls crumbling from old age and from sturdy roots pushing into the small cracks. Large blocks of stone have fallen from above, crushing much of what was once here. Cracks and openings in the ceiling allow a few rays of light to pierce the darkness at day, but fail to illuminate much of the basement.
18805: A spirit floats towards you and howls with an evil laughter.

The walls of the crypt are covered with large, flat stones. Along them, three small recesses have been cut out to hold the remains of fallen warriors. In the middle of the room, a slender stone pillar emerges from the earthy soil. The pillar has obviously been here for ages because it is cracked, with some fragments that have fallen off. The entire chamber appears to have been built around the pillar.
18806:
A Rohir marksman surveys the landscape, targeting would-be adversaries.
A sturdy warrior is here, guarding the tower.

More than ten feet above the battlements, this watchtower provides a perfect, unobstructed view of the land for many miles. The tower is large enough to allow for a lookout and for a well-armoured man to comfortably draw a bow. Thick leather strips are tied about the tower's posts to protect anyone from falling. A small lantern hangs from a rope attached to the tower's slanted roof.
18807: A foot-soldier of Rohan is here.

Roughly ten feet above the ground, a narrow walkway has been constructed near the top of the fort walls. This thin platform is supported with wooden spikes that continue another ten feet into the air, forming the parapets of the battlements. Sturdy ladders lead down from the battlements and up to a small watchtower. A vibrant green flag with the image of a white stallion flies atop the tower.
18808:
A neat straw pallet is lying here.
A small oaken table has been set here.
A commanding Rohir officer presides here, watching for unwanted intruders.
A foot-soldier of Rohan is here.
A Rohir marksman surveys the landscape, targeting would-be adversaries.
An archer of the Mark is here.
A stout Rohir lieutenant is here.

A large campaign tent has been erected adjacent to the mess hall. A flimsy wooden table stands near the southern wall of the tent, covered in maps and small position markers. Upon the earth, several flat planks of wood have been woven together with iron straps, forming an extremely sturdy floor. In the back corner of the tent, a wide piece of fabric has been attached to the tent-top, forming a wall of sorts. The wall has been partially pushed to one side, and behind it sits a small cot.
18809: A neat straw pallet is lying here.

This room reeks of mould, decay and human sweat. The source of the pungent odour is not apparent although, as the room appears to be fairly clean. Racks hanging from the four wooden walls are resting places for weapons and shields. Small cots, lined up along the front and rear walls, are neatly covered with grey blankets that look clean enough. At the foot of each bed, a wooden chest sits closed with a small lock on most. Other than the inadequate lighting for human eyes, provided by tiny lanterns dangling from the ceiling, the entire barrack appears in order. The source of the mysterious odour is nowhere to be seen.
18810:
A sturdy warrior is here, guarding the tower.
A Rohir door-warden is here.

A small courtyard has been formed by earthen walls surrounding this area. The piled up dirt is supported at the corners by wooden beams but otherwise all that protects this encampment is well-packed soil. Inside the battlements to the north, a small hut has been crafted out of an assortment of spare wood, as has a shack directly east. These structures have a haphazard appearance, being made up of whatever was lying around at the time. The only sturdy wood in this camp rests against the earthen walls, in the shape of well-constructed ladders.
18811:
A wooden chest stands in the corner.
A water barrel has been left here.
A weapons rack stands against the wall.

The architects of this fort must have had a limited supply of wood with which to construct it. A storage room would have been the last priority in a project such as this. Nevertheless, here stands a storage area made entirely out of earth. Small walls have been crafted from heavily packed dirt to form the supports for the roof. The roof itself is nothing more than heavily oiled hides, stretched across the walls and held in place by some sort of weight atop the edges. Nothing sits upon the floor for fear of water damage. All the weapons, armour and foodstuffs sit upon makeshift shelving crafted from piles of dirt and long wooden planks.
18812:
A foot-soldier of Rohan is here.
A Rohir marksman surveys the landscape, targeting would-be adversaries.
An archer of the Mark is here.
A stout Rohir lieutenant is here.
A sturdy warrior is here, guarding the tower.
A Rohir door-warden is here.

Four earthen walls surround a sienna dirt courtyard large enough to accommodate dozens of horses and as many men. At the intersections of the walls, sturdy wooden ladders lead to and from a small ledge that runs the entire length of the dirt battlements, some fifteen feet above the ground. Deep ruts in the ground lead from the north gate to a large stable in the east, the result of numerous horses passing into and out of this fort. Directly opposite of the north gate, a ramshackle barracks has been constructed from wood, leather, straw and earth. Scattered around the entrances to the barracks and the stables are various weapons and shields, all in desperate need of repair.
18813: The battlements stand as high as four feet and run along all the walls. Men can move along the wall two to three abreast along wooden platforms that have been inserted into the earth walls. In the south corner a wooden tower rises above the walls to give the soldiers a good view of the land. A ladder leads from the walkway up to the tower.
18814:
A small oaken table has been set here.
On the table, there are a carrot, a large piece of smoked, cured meat and a potato.

This hastily built mess hall seems the worse for wear. Irregular shaped gaps in every wall allow the light from outside to shine in, and shoddy patching of holes in the roof threaten to drench diners with every storm. But in stark contrast, the stove in the northwest corner of the hut is in pristine condition, clean and well built. It is not new, but cared for very well. This speaks volumes about the priorities of this fort's inhabitants. In the middle of the room, long but very narrow tables have been set with small stools placed underneath.
18815:
A Rohir cavalier, wielding a longspear, is here, riding a trained horse.
A foot-soldier of Rohan is here.
A foot-soldier of Rohan is here.
An elite Rohir knight appears alert.
An elite Rohir knight appears alert.
Haldin the Marshal, wielding a bastard sword, is here, riding a horse of the Rohirrim.
A horse of the Rohirrim is standing here, ridden by Haldin the Marshal.
A trained horse is standing here, ridden by a Rohir cavalier.

A wide, well-kept road runs between two fortified encampments. On the north and south sides of the road, the two earth forts face each other like near mirror images. Two heavily reinforced wooden doors lead into their respective forts. Massive earthen walls that would tower above even the tallest troll run most of the length of the eyot and are topped with wooden spikes. On the eastern and western sides of the island, smooth, white pebbles form wide fords, leading to either riverbank. The sound of rushing waters from the Isen, slamming into the northern banks of the eyot, can be heard day and night.
18816:
A trout swims here.
A brook trout is here, swimming in the current.
A brook trout is here, swimming in the current.

The Great South Road runs directly into the waters of Sir Angren, forming one of two large fords. White, smooth cobblestones have been stacked onto the riverbed, allowing easy passage for large numbers of people or animals attempting to cross the swift waters. The ford doesn't completely cross the river, but leads to a small eyot, centred in the Isen. The river runs around the eyot on either side, forming large streams. Upon the eyot, two massive earthen forts stand guard over a wide road that leads between them.
18817:
A Rohir marksman surveys the landscape, targeting would-be adversaries.
A sturdy warrior is here, guarding the tower.

Standing nearly ten feet above the tallest battlements, this lookout tower offers an unimpeded view of the land for miles in every direction. A small ladder, no wider than a large man, leads up to a wooden platform, which is covered with a slanted roof. There are also rails built around the tower to keep anyone from falling over the side. A small lantern hangs from a thin rope attached to the makeshift roof.
18818:
A worn leather saddlebag has been left on the ground.
A sturdy pack horse is standing here.
A Rohir stable-hand stands here, ready to help with the horses.
An archer of the Mark is here.

Impeccably clean stalls run the length of this carefully maintained stable. Each animal has its own stall, complete with a wooden roof, three sidewalls and a half-open gate. Each stall has its own food trough and water bucket. The ground is covered with a thick pallet of clean straw. Perfectly aligned racks and hooks hang next to each gate where saddles, bridles and blankets are stored.
18819:
A neat straw pallet is lying here.
A weapons rack stands against the wall.
A large stone fireplace with a roaring fire warms the room.
A foot-soldier of Rohan is here.

A rectangular structure, constructed from a variety of building materials serves as barracks for the Rohir soldiers manning this fort. Overhead, thin wooden planks are covered by hay, bound and braided together with leather straps, to create an effective roof. Old and worn cots line the southern and northern walls. A large fireplace, no more than mud bricks stacked up at a hole in the western wall, warms and illuminates the long room. Armour, weapons and other small items are scattered about the room.
18820:
A well-used clothes line is strung between two walls.
A mailbox stands here stuffed full of messages.
A wooden chest stands in the corner.
A large stone fireplace with a roaring fire warms the room.
A smiling innkeeper is here, ready to offer you a room.

This section of the barracks is shielded by a large screen of wicker. Small sleeping mats and chests for personal belongings stand along the walls. Even though the structure is a barrack, this part does not seem as orderly as the rest of it. Evidence of non-military guests are present in the form of various clothes hung to dry in a corner.
18821: Lush grasslands to the north and east give way gradually to the coarse grass underfoot. The choppy grass and small rocks conceal the rich soil of the vale. In addition to the grass and rocks, several masses of decaying leaves rest against the larger stones, pushed together by intermittent winds. The remains of a decaying village to the west appear worn over time by the harsh sun and pounding rain that characterise the Rohan plains. A very faint, barely discernable footpath leads from the village towards the underbrush to the east.
18822: Empty stalls line the northern wall. In days gone past, the stalls assuredly housed the animals that allowed this small hamlet to flourish. Now the stalls lie empty and badly maintained. Several planks hang loosely from old nails. Extremely aged hay and silage clutter the floor of the barn and stalls. To the south, an empty doorway opens to a weed-filled courtyard.
18823:
A black crow flies low to the ground here, looking for carrion to eat.
A black crow flies low to the ground here, looking for carrion to eat.
A black crow flies low to the ground here, looking for carrion to eat.
A black crow flies low to the ground here, looking for carrion to eat.
A black crow flies low to the ground here, looking for carrion to eat.

The view from the top of this high, dead tree is marvellous. The valley floor stretches out in all directions. The view is only limited by the dust clouds that lie over the dry, dusty plains. The branches of the tree are sturdy and have formed almost a platform up in the crown. Several birds are perched up on the high branches, spying for prey.
18824: Small and twisted black bushes are scattered all over the rocky landscape here, providing some protection for what little topsoil is left on arid and brittle earth. The plains continue to the west and south and the land rises higher in the mountainous terrain northwards. A small valley lies due north, wedged between rocks.
18825:
A noticeable crack runs down one of the walls.
A shallow pond is here, tinted green with algae.

A high crack in the northern mountain wall has opened up a small confined space, providing ample protection against the elements. The rock walls protect from weather and wind, blocking out the sun and rain. A small body of water has collected on the rock floor, filtering up from below. The water is clear and cold. The ground is covered with sharp pebbles and rocks.
18826: The mountainside is rough and rocky; a hasty traveller could get badly injured. There is a fair amount of ground cover here, with small patches of twisted, black bushes surviving in the parched land. Mountains rise in majestic formations all around the large valley, and the ground slopes upwards, towards the high peaks in the north. Against the backdrop of mountains, a high black spike stands out, the tower of Isengard - Orthanc, behind the stone walls in the east. A small guardhouse, made of stone, stands against the wall to the south.
18827: The mountains rise tall with high peaks to the north and east, with terrain cluttered with huge boulders and loose scree, making travel difficult. The passage east and southwards are steep, but north and west looks impossible to climb. Below, to the south the mountains break first into rocky, barren hills and then onwards to a large mountain valley. To the southeast the mighty tower Orthanc splits the horizon, and plain to see is the ring of Isengard surrounding it with all its strength. A small trail of hoof-tracks leads upwards.
18828: The dry, cracked plains extend in all directions as far as the eye can see. The plains are divided in two by a huge dike, spanning from the northeast to the west, across the valley. The dike is deep and wide, forcing any traveller to go a roundabout way to get across. Sporadic clusters of low, twisted shrubs and hulking formations of long since cooled slag or weathered sandstone dot the plains. The dry wind howls across the arid plain and is throwing up sand and dust into small clouds.
18841: This is one of the most ruined and desolate places you have seen in Fornost. It looks as if it has once been a large house of entertainment, but the roof has fallen in at many places, and the stairs are steep, rugged and broken. There is a huge fireplace in the room and the chimney is blackened with smoke; but no warm blaze lights it up now. The white feathery dust of burnt wood is still strewn over the hearth, but the stove is cold, and all is dark and gloomy.
18849: A tall and strong guard is here.

A warmth fills your heart as you enter a spacious room dimly lit by torches in the four corners of the room. Quickly catching your attention in the centre is a large marble statue glowing faintly. The statue is Sylan's noble father, a soldier of the Arthedain. His face appears firm and solemn, ready to engrave himself in battle at any cost to protect the city of Arthedain. Among the walls are many tapestries filled with beautiful art and paintings showing the renovation of the new city of Fornost. The crest of the Arthedain is mounted on the wall across from you with battle insignias and jewels surrounding it. To the east is another lit room.
18850: This vast area appears to be Sylan's hall of honor. His nobleness and dedication to the Knights of Arthedain is evidently reflected throughout this room. Along the floor are long carpets of battle insignias foreign to you. Written in Westron is a scripture mounted under another crest of Arthedain. Looking at it closely you see the following: "For I have taken the Arthedain solemn promise to protect the cities of Fornost and Bree from evil at any cost to my life. I will uphold and protect the walls of Norbury my family has worked in vain to build. --- Sylan, Noble Knight of Arthedain. At the top of the hall is a window which almost pours out the vastness of the sky, allowing the sun to give warmth to your bones and the moon to shine it's glimmering rays among the many trophies of battles and challenges Sylan has won. Thick metal and chain mail armour hangs on the northern wall along with an empty sheath in the middle. The size and vastness of the sheath makes it evident that the sword of the kingdom of Arthedain is not one to reckon with. To the west is the foyer and the east Sylan's quarters.
18851: A humble man stands here, ready to help you with your things.

This room stands in stark comparison to the rest of this elegant home. The walls are spartan and free of decoration -- save a few candles along the walls and a large oak desk along the northern wall. A pile of furs lay in a corner near a small lantern, clearly, where Sylan prefers to sleep.
18852: A humble man stands here, ready to help you with your things.

As you walk past the guard's post and into the dimly lit room, you quickly notice an unusual odour. A rather grandiose fireplace occupies the centre of the west wall while the assortment of chairs around the fireplace would seem to accomodate virtually any guest. On the south wall, a large portrait is proudly displayed between two fine tapestries.
18853: As you enter the room, your suspicions of the source of the unusual odour are confirmed as your olefactory senses are overwhelmed. The small room is obviously where Ticar practices and perfects his magical mastery. Books line the north and east walls with an occasional scroll folded between the books. On the south wall, several shelves hold some small pouches and an occasional potion. In the southwest corner, a large sack hangs from the ceiling by a rope. Nestled in the northeast corner is a small table with a stool shoved under it. An unusual spherical crystal is perched upon the table. A cauldron precariously occupies the southeast corner.
18854: After squeezing by the small iron gate, the tranquility of the very private courtyard immediately puts you at ease. The courtyard is surrounded by an enourmous stone wall that separates the bustling capital city from Ticar's own private garden. The wall is consumed by an ivy that completely covers it. To the west, two benches large enough for two people each sit facing each other near the wall and under a large oak tree. To the southeast, a large flat stone sits on top of a dirt mound. In the centre of the courtyard, a statue of a petite elven child is surrounded on three sides by small rose bushes. As you walk closer, you notice that the child is the centrepiece of a fountain and a small stream of water flows from the child's mouth. The scent of honeysuckle tantilizes your senses as you stand in awe of this beautiful setting. Nestled under the eve of the house in the northeast corner of the courtyard you notice a small hut and next to the entrance to the hut stands a proud suit of armour.
18858: Massive oak timbers frame the interior of this private home. Large glass lamps hang from the high vaulted ceiling on long iron chains. The far side of the lodge is dominated by a massive fireplace with an immense mantle hewn from oak and stained pitch black from the soot of countless fires. All along the granite walls are large storage shelves and hanging pegs that hold a wide variety of hunting gear, stable tack, and implements of war. A spiral stone staircase leads to the rooms above.
18859: Sacks of flour, crates of dried cured beef, and baskets of vegetables and potatoes are stacked along the left wall of this room. To the right stands a small but well-used food preparation table, a sink, and a wood stove. Clearly, this is where the master of the house prepares his rations for his long hunts, as well as his home cooked dinners. Hanging on hooks from the ceiling are various herbs and plants being dried for use in herbal remedies.
18860:
A humble man stands here, ready to help you with your things.
A stocky mountain mule is here, waiting to serve.

An immense four post bed with a huge feather-stuffed comforter dominates this room. Its large posts have been cut from oak and appear to be small trees themselves. A huge oak dresser stands next to a granite wall, and a huge white pelt of a cavebear serves as a rug on the stone floor. Torch sconces are placed into the walls, and the stone above them is blackened by their soot. A window, draped in red velvet, looks out onto the street. Above the bed, a portrait hangs on the wall.
18861:
A large bulletin board, entitled "Legendhomes", is mounted here.
A sign reading, Building Permit Information, is here.
A Dunadan soldier is here busily performing his duties.

In this small office is a rather large round table surround by eight wooden chairs. The table, like the walls, is covered in an assortment of maps and land surveys. Markers on one of the larger table maps show which parcels of land are in use and what is available for future construction.
18862: A sign, reading Building Permit Information, is here A large bulletin board, entitled "Legendhomes", is mounted here.

Large maps, showing the city divided by many dotted lines, cover the walls. Within each of the divisions are scrawled names of the current occupants or owners. A large ornate table, almost filling this small office completely, stands in the centre of the room surrounded by half a dozen equally ornate wood-carved chairs. Most of the table's top is obscured by papers.
18863: A small barrel stands on the ground.

What must have at one time been a stable filled with fresh hay or straw has become a stable filled with flies and some sort of bird droppings. A wooden bowl lies knocked over in the middle of the small chamber, its contents of seeds spilled onto the ground. In the north eastern corner stands a barrel filled with murky water.
18880:
A sign reading, Building Permit Information, is here.
A large bulletin board, entitled "Legendhomes", is mounted here.
A stout Dwarven steward stands here, ready to defend the office.

This large room is wide enough for an enormous wooden table and a dozen or so chairs. The table itself is piled with papers, which appear to be mainly maps and city plans for new excavations and mining. A small shelf stands beside the table with rolls of paper neatly tucked away. Most likely the plans, plats and copies of deeds of finished homes currently in use.
18912: There are two beer bottles here.

Although this room is lit rather poorly, the jovial atmosphere in the room reveals that the darkness is not indicative of danger. This tavern seems to be an ideal place for dwarves to meet and socialise, while resting up from long journeys with a refreshing brew.
18913: A stout Dwarven steward stands here, ready to defend the home.

In this echoing dome lit by the light of crystal lamps, bright gemstones and veins of precious ores can be seen. The marble walls are jet black and polished like glass. Intricately carved forms within the walls depict a scene of battle from days long ago. A sturdy weapons rack laden with axes of various shapes and sizes stands in the corner surrounded on all sides by bright banners, fine armour and jewelled weapons which adorn the walls.
18963: This place is very narrow, lying beneath a foxes trap. A shallow pool of water fills the bottom of the depression. The water, also a bit muddy, seems to be safe.
19003: A Break in the Great Hedge
A large flat rock lies here, its surface etched with markings.

A sudden opening in the great hedge allows one to pass through the dense vegetation. Some humanoid tracks, among others, leading north and south are easy to spot in the grass in between the high bushes. A few miles to the south a castle rises above the landscape.
19023:
A giant rat patters against you, squeaking maliciously.
A giant rat patters against you, squeaking maliciously.
A giant rat patters against you, squeaking maliciously.
A bear is here, covered with coarse black fur.

Upon descending the rotting steps to the cellar, clouds of putrid air fill your nostrils. Smells of both decay and mustiness are here, all making your fight against vomiting difficult to say the least. As you entered, many of the new inhabitants of the Fallen Inn were stirred from their normal business. High pitched squeaks and the shuffling of small feet fill the room, adding to your disgust.
19024:
Several silver coins lie scattered about here.
Several silver coins lie scattered about here.
Several silver coins lie scattered about here.
Several silver coins lie scattered about here.
An experienced smuggler is here, conspiring with his cohorts.
An experienced smuggler is here, conspiring with his cohorts.
An experienced smuggler is here, conspiring with his cohorts.
A smuggler is here, angry at having been seen.

Spiders and dust shroud just about everything in this dimly lit room. In the centre is a small round wooden table, with hard chairs arranged around it. Various footprints in the thick dust suggest that this may be a meeting room.
19029: A water moccasin slithers out of sight just below the surface of the water.

It is rather dark and damp inside this cave. You can see some stirring in the back of the cave. You can feel the presence of something else inside the cave along with you, but with all the signs of snake presence around, most likely it is no more than another snake. There are some rocks towards the side that appear to move slightly as if something live was hiding between them.
19452: This smial doesn't look very sturdy. The walls need painting, the floor needs a deep cleaning, and the roof is in disrepair. It appears that the room will not offer much protection if a storm comes. The dust and cobwebs lead you to believe the place has been abandoned.
19479: A swarm of mosquitoes is here, humming around you.

Due to excessive moisture from the nearby bog, only a few larger bushes have been able to hold their root in the wet soil long enough to gain size. The taller they grow, the higher becomes the risk of a strong autumn wind simply pulling them up from the loose ground.
19486:
A large stone fireplace with a roaring fire warms the room.
A large cabinet capable of storing goods is here.
A smiling hobbit child is playing around here.
A smiling hobbit child is playing around here.
A busy hobbit female is here worrying about the home labours.

It is obvious that this smial was built with children and their play in mind. Plenty of open space has been left in the centre of the round main hall and everything that might be dangerous to little ones has probably been put safely away in the closets and cabinets that line the walls. A few steps of stairs lead outside.
19798:
A waist-high evergreen shrub grows here, with thick, reaching branches.
On the shrub, there are two piles of grey-green leaves.
A rabbit is here eyeing your presence warily.

You have come to the southern end of the Hills of Scary. Here, the terrain seems rockier, and there is a noticeable thinning of the grass which covers the ground. In some places there are only occasional spots of grass between larger patches of bare soil. Looking down the steep western slope, you see what appears to be a quarry, but there is no way down. On your east and south are sheer drops down to a flat stretch of grass.
19814: This hallway is dimly lit by a few torches mounted along the walls. Below your feet an ornamental carpet rests atop a floor of thick, hardened rock. A strange bubbling sound seems to come from below. To the west lies a passage of polished marble leading to a well-lit gallery, while to your east a hallway leads towards the sleeping quarters.
19815:
A sturdy bed made from solid oak lies here, covered in warm blankets.
A humble man stands here, ready to help you with your things.

These quarters have been built to provide a relaxing environment for the warrior Ganon to rest. There is a large bed in the centre of the room, draped with soft blankets and pillows of various sizes and colours. An ivory bookcase lined with many old novels sits alongside the bed. A few torches have been installed over the entryway to provide soft lighting at night. By day, a large glass skylight lets the sun into the room.
19816: A large bookshelf sits against the wall.

Large torches mounted in metal holders and a roaring fireplace in the centre light the chamber brightly. Paintings line the north and south walls, flanking a great mural along the west side of the room. Skilled artists have drawn these paintings, each of which portrays an epic battle. From time to time, stories of these battles are told here. Around the room various chairs and tables are arranged, some of them containing an old book or a table game of some kind.
19817: A doorkeep stands here ready to obey his master's wishes.

In this room, the tree's bark runs from bottom to top. Small baskets of flowers and plants hang from the branches which spread through the ceiling of this large natural hallway. Seats made of wood, with pillows made of leaves are placed at each corner of the room, serving as resting spots for the folk that pass by here.
19818: A rack of weapons stands tall on the Eastern side of this room. From time to time, swords, axes, spears, daggers, and myriad other types of weapons are stored here. On the Western side of the room, leather, metal, and various assortments of personal protection are hung against the wall. Use of this equipment is reserved for the frequent practice and training battles which occur here.
19819:
A sturdy bed made from solid oak lies here, covered in warm blankets.
The Housekeeper looks fed up with her job. She scowls at you unhappily.

Cracked walls, shaded windows and an old and noisy door compose this room. This seems to be the bedroom of a great dwarven warrior, weapons hanging on the walls, shields and pieces of armour over the chair. On the walls there are some pictures of the fallen people of Arda. In the most comfortable corner there is a sturdy bed where great dreams about glory and victory are made every night. By its side, there is a little table full of beard-combs, mauve petals and wooden pipes.
19820: This is apparenly the underside of a great hill. The room is lit up a bit by some light that has filtered through the sides of the hatch above. The surrounding walls are made of damp brown dirt and the quarters are quite cramped with not much room for movement. Looking down its possible to see the dark depths of the hill.
19821: This is a long, dark, narrow tunnel leading even further down into the hill. The walls are made of the same dirt as was seen underneath the hatch now far above. Other than a few parts of the wall still lit up by the light coming from above, the surroundings are difficult to see. However, further down there is a sense of life coming from the chamber below, though from this vantage point it is still shrouded in darkness.
19822: A humble man stands here, ready to help you with your things.

After travelling down from the damp tight tunnel above, there is finally enough room for a full-grown person to stretch out their limbs. Looking back up through the black tunnel, all that can be seen now is what looks like a tiny hatch far above with light creeping through the sides. This is apparently very core of the bottom of a great hill. The room is lit by a set of dim magical lights floating around the room. From afar, the lights look like small faeries, but they seem to avoid closer examination by floating away if anything draws near. The walls are made of a silver metal accented with engravings of great armour and weapons carved into the sides. This chamber clearly is the home of a great dwarf, who might not appreciate the intrusion.
19823: A humble man stands here, ready to help you with your things.
This bedchamber is most inviting after a long adventure. There is a big bed, which looks quite comfortable. There are pegs and shelves about the room to store weapons and equipment.
19847: Ah, The lovely Brandywine! As you step out of the door you are standing on the top of a hill. The end of the hill drops sharply into the banks of the river. Standing here you feel relaxed. Watching the babbling Brandywine flow smoothly down the track, several fisherhobbits are making their way up and down the river hoping to catch some fish. Looking around the place, you realise that this must be Torque's place of relaxation. There are a few scattered tables and chairs, but for the most part, it is a tidy place. Along the edge of the hill, you see a couple of fishing rods, perhaps put there by Torque after catching his dinner. By the doorway, you see a small counter with an attendant lazily standing behind it. Above the doorway behind you, there is a huge fish, mounted to the wood behind it.
20169: A brown bear is sleeping here.

This is a dark natural cave, carved by wind and water acting on the softer rock beneath the harder layer that forms the surface of the hill. A pungent smell tells you that animals of some kind have made use of this shelter.
20230:
A worm is here slithering around.
A large elk is standing here, chewing grass and leaves.
The large elk gazes coldly at you, chewing on a small branch.

The outer edge of the fire graced this area with its presence. The yellow-green grass has begun to grow once again. It has reached a height of about six inches in some areas. More flowers have also sprouted here due to the lack of competition from the grass. Some of the ground towards the north is still charred black from the fires. The areas to the south and west were unaffected by the fire.
20231: The yellow-green grass completely dominates the area. Not a single flower, rock, or weed can be seen anywhere in this sea of grass. The grass is a uniform two feet tall, and every strand stands on end. To the north and east the ground looks black in places, suggesting a fire might have raged and scorched the earth there.
20232: The grasses have formed a circular clearing in the middle of the plains. At the centre of the clearing stands a solitary tree. The tree has big leafy branches and looks like it would be a good climb. The clearing is dotted with red flowers and a few animal tracks can be seen leading away from the tree. The grass continues in all directions.
20233: The yellow-green grass completely dominates this area. There is no sign of any other flora having ever been here. The grass is very thick, making walking difficult, but not impossible. Some animal tracks are seen heading into the clearing to the east. The scent of grass overpowers all other smells.
20234: The plains are covered in yellow-green grasses, with the tallest reaching about two feet in height. Every once in a while there is a small flower or weed, about to be choked out by the grass. Some animal tracks wind in between the blades of grass. The plains are all that can be seen.
20235: The grass in this area has taken on a peculiar brownish tint. It is just as tall and straight as it is everywhere else. Small clumps of flowers are pushing their way through the thick grass, attempting to reach any available sunlight. Small animal tracks are running all over this area. The grass continues in all directions.
20236: A multitude of flowers dot this area of the plains. The colour of the flowers is almost drowned out by the grasses filling the plains. They stand straight, even during the hardest wind. Around the flowers, there are some tracks from small animals leading off into the grass.
20237: A large rabbit looks peacefully at you, ready to dart away.

The plains are full of a yellow-green grass. The grass is standing tall, like it is guarding something important. Small flowers are dotting the landscape, adding to the overall colour of the area. A stream can be seen running to the west, with what appears to be a small footbridge allowing passage across it. The grasses continue on into the eastern horizon.
20238: A rushing stream continues down from the forest to the west. A dilapidated wooden foot bridge spans a shallow place along the stream's course. Just past the bridge, the stream curves sharply south, becoming the main tributary to a small lake. A trail leads north into the plains from the foot of the bridge.
20239: The scent of rotting trees hangs in the air. Many of the trees seem to have been torn out of the ground and their trunks litter the area. The scattered remaining trees would provide little shelter from the sunlight. There are small amounts of grass and what look like weeds poking out from underneath a layer of tree bark that covers the ground. A small stream flows down to the east.
20240: The layer of bark seems to dwindle in this area. More of the grass is visible and it is able to stand up to its full height. The number of trees is getting smaller and smaller until the forest finally gives way into a field of two-foot tall grasses.
20241:
A buck runs swiftly from place to place, looking about warily as it grazes.
A buck runs swiftly from place to place, looking about warily as it grazes.
A finch flies low above the ground.

Grass has completely dominated the plant life in this area. Not a single flower or weed seems to have survived the squelching effect of the grasses. The grass stands up straight like the hair on a cold person's arm. To the west, the southern edge of the Misty Mountains rises into the sky. Off to the south lies a ragged little forest. The back of a camp blocks travel east.
20242: A Trail on the Edge of a Forest

The trail continues from the east on its way south. A few shaggy looking trees surround the edges of the path, offering some shade from the sun during the day. The trail is covered with grass and weeds, suggesting not many people have travelled here recently.
20243: The trail continues from the north, heading west towards a small forested area. The trail is barely visible here, being almost completely covered by weeds and grasses. Endless fields of grass extend to the east and south, but there is a glimpse of some water off to the south.
20244: A large rabbit looks peacefully at you, ready to dart away.

The yellow-green grasses here are about two feet tall. A few small weeds have taken hold around what looks like a foxes burrow. The grasses, not being obstructed by anything, are standing tall. Looking east, a field of blue flowers can be seen. To the north and west lies a small, rarely travelled trail.
20245:
Yellow flowers, with grey-green foliage, grow in clusters here.
A colourful butterfly is fluttering around here.

A small, bluish flower has taken hold in this area. There are so many of them, that the grass is actually being choked out by the flowers. The grass is still populating a small area, but it is slowly being covered up by the flowers. The flowers stretch to the north, but don't seem to have spread elsewhere.
20246: Small red flowers dot this area, poking up through the grasses. A few blue flowers are scattered on the western edge of the area, attempting to rejoin their companions. The grasses stand tall, running off of the hillock to the north. A small patch of weeds is growing under a rock. More grasses await to the east and south.
20247:
A snake slithers towards you.
A brown fox is here, looking for some rabbits to chew up.

There are some rather large patches of red flowers surrounded by the grass. A few orange flowers have taken up residence in the centre of the red flowers. Mosses and weeds grow in the shadow of a large rock that was deposited here some time ago. The grasses stretch out in all directions.
20248:
A worm is here slithering around.
A brown fox is here, looking for some rabbits to chew up.

The yellow-green grasses stand up to two feet tall. They are stiff, even in the strongest wind. There are red flowers dotting the landscape, along with some weeds that are growing under the shade of some rocks. A clearing lies to the south, with a tree in the centre. The grasses extend in all other directions.
20249: The outer edge of a fire burned away some of the eastern area of the grass. Many red flowers can be seen sprouting out of the charred black ground. Some grass has also started to grow back in the burnt soil. The ground slopes down to the north, leading into a dip in the plains. The grass continues to the south and the west.
20250: This whole area is devoid of vegetation. The ground is covered with black soot from when the area was ravaged by flames. The rocks that survived the fire have been coloured jet black. The fires burned to the south and west, but the area to the north was unaffected.
20251: The grass stands tall at two feet high. Small red flowers grow here, adding some diversity to the local flora and a little colour. The border of Fangorn Forest stands to the north while the land dips down to the west. The land to the south has been charred by fire.
20252: The land slopes down into a bowl filled with yellow flowers. The grasses grow down the sides, stopping once they reach the bottom of the bowl. The border of Fangorn Forest lies up the slope to the north. Tall, yellow-green grasses grow to the east and west, but the ground looks blackened to the south.
20253: The grass stands tall at two feet high. Small red flowers break up the yellow-green monotony. Weeds are growing wherever they can survive. The ground slopes to the east resulting in a dip in the plains. The border of Fangorn Forest stands to the north while grasses extend to the west and south.
20254:
A restless rabbit bounces around.
A brown fox is here, looking for some rabbits to chew up.

The grasses stand tall, as if they had been marching towards the border of the forest to the north but then been abruptly called to a halt. Some weeds grow among a few scattered rocks. A small hillock rises out of the plains to the west. The grasses extend to the east and to the south.
20255: Yellow-green grasses spread all over this small hillock. A few red flowers and a small tree are fighting for space within the dense grass. At the base of the hillock lies the entrance to a large den. From the top most peak of the land the surrounding areas become visible.
20256: The trail disappears into a massive bed of blue flowers. The flowers seem to stop just past the north side of the trail, west of where it turns sharply north. The grass is almost at war with the flowers for control of the trail. The edge of the Fangorn Forest looms to the north.
20257: The trail, the part not covered by the grass, is running from east to west. The rest has been completely enveloped by the wild grasses. The forest of Fangorn can be seen to the north and the endless plains of grass reach out to the south and east.
20258:
A cute rabbit is here.
A fallow deer is grazing peacefully here.

The trail continues from the east, cutting off a small section of plains to the north. The trail is covered in weeds, unobstructed by the passage of people. Time has not been good for this trail, as most of it is being slowly covered by the wild grasses. The trail continues on southward.
20260: Under the Eaves of the Entwood

Massive rowan trees stand here, seemingly untouched by the passage of time. The trees are covered with dead and decayed leaves and the forest floor is very rocky. Though not very far into the forest, the amount of light during the day has already vastly decreased. The air seems thicker in here, making it harder to breath.
20261: The ground slopes upward as the plains approach the Misty Mountains. The grasses begin to dwindle and are being replaced by rocks and other debris. Fangorn Forest lies off to the east. To the south, you can see fields of wild grasses with a small green dot far away. To the north, the peaks of the Misty Mountains stand tall.
20262: The rocky terrain slopes slightly upwards towards the north. The forest has the smell of stale leaves. In a few places, yellow rays of daytime sun pierce through the forest canopy. The forest is very dim with pine and fir trees all around. There are no signs of animals ever living here as there are no plants for them to eat.
20263: A mountain goat is here, jumping from cliff to cliff.

A vertical wall of stone rises to the north, dotted with deep-green plants. Large amounts of debris litter the ground around the base of the wall. One area of the rock face seems have a larger concentration of plants then the rest of the area. The wall extends to the west and slopes down slightly to the east.
20264: The base of the mountain is covered with rocks of all shapes and sizes. Small, green shrubs cling to the rock. The slope of the mountain to the north is not very steep, allowing even the most inexperienced to scale it easily. The mountain rises to the north, allowing for a good view of the surrounding areas. The grass stretches out to the south, dotted with some colour from the flowers.
20265: A vertical wall of stone rises to the north, dotted with deep-green plants. Large amounts of debris litter the ground around the base of the wall. Small green shrubs grow in patches on the ground. The wall extends to the east and up the mountain.
20266: A Field near the Border of Fangorn

With Fangorn Forest so close to the north, it is no wonder why this field has not had much traffic. The grasses have grown to about four feet high in this area, and with nothing to hold them back, they could grow even taller. The grasses continue on into the east, and a trail can be seen to the south.
20267: A Field under the Eaves of Fangorn

This field has not seen much traffic in a long while. The grasses have reached a height of four feet and stand straight on end. The air seems to be a bit thicker here than in the surrounding areas. A disused trail can be seen to the south while more of the tall grasses grow to the west.
20268: A Trail out of the Forest

The trail runs up to the edge of Fangorn and disappears into the trees. The grasses running along the trail break off and begin to taper as the trail enters Fangorn. A few solitary flowers have taken hold along the edge of the trail. The trail continues on to the south, were it is swallowed up in a field of blue. The air seems a bit thicker in this area.
20269: These high-reaching trees stand unwavering, marking what is the entrance to the forest for some and a step closer to the fresh air plains just outside the forest boundary to the south. Regardless of the direction being travelled, it is difficult to ignore the stark contrast of the airy plains against the dank confinement of the forest which is thicker to the north.
20270: The trees are covered in lichen and dead leaves, showing their ages and through the number of seasons they have witnessed. The air is thick and dank from being trapped between the moist ground and the canopy of limbs above. East and west the border of the forest continues displaying a very clear natural boundary between the two areas.
20271: The yellow-green grasses that approach the outer borders of Fangorn Come to an abrupt stop at the forest's boundary. The lack of light, because of the thick canopy of tree limbs and the musty smell of trapped air and moisture is a stark contrast to the plains just a short walk to the south.
20272: The air is thick here, trapped between the moist moss and grass covered soil and the large canopy of limbs that cover much of the forest. The air has an almost stale quality about it, unlike the fresh airs that fill the grasslands to the south. Toward the north the air and the trees both grow thicker.
20273: The forest to the north stands in stark contrast to lands to the south. The air in the plains south of here is fresh and carries the smell of a variety of grasses and flowering plants. Here within the forest, the air is dank and stale. The humongous trees blocking out all but the smallest drafts of air from above the canopy of limbs and forbidding the odour of the moist soil and moss to dissipate outward.
20274: As the grasses approach the edge of Fangorn, they seem to shrink smaller. The grass ends about a foot before the forest border. The dark pine trees stand tall, like they are guarding the forest border. The air is stale and thick here, making it difficult to breathe.
20275: A tall birch is here, watching over the landscape.

The grass is overwhelmed by the massive trees of Fangorn. The trees seem as if they have little trouble asserting their dominion over all other plantlife. Even the air within the forest is under the tree's command, trapped between their tangled roots in the moist ground and the thick canopy of limbs above. Very little fresh air seems to reach this place through the holes in the forest canopy let in an equally scant amount of the light.
20276: The grasses shrivel as they approach the forest. The birch trees appear to be guarding the edge of the forest from intruders. A short, green grass is growing in patches around the bases of the trees. In a few places, what looks like the remains of a trail can be seen. The trail appears to lead south, out of the forest. The bulk of Fangorn lies to the north.
20277: A tall birch is here, watching over the landscape.

A warm, green grass covers the entire area. Some sweet smelling ferns grow between the roots of some of the larger birch trees. The trees are clad in the leaves of a generation past, while one of the trees is covered only in lichen. What looks like plains can be seen through the trees to the south.
20278: The ground slopes down from the north and then flattens out. Many rowan trees are growing here, covered with dead leaves. Grass grows out from between the tree roots and a few ferns have taken hold at the feet of the larger trees. The plains can barely be seen through the trees to the south.
20279: A tall birch is here, watching over the landscape.

The ground levels out as it comes down from the cliff to the north. A few birch trees are growing here, covered with dead leaves. The roots of the trees wander around below ground before emerging on the surface, only to dive back underground. Warm, green grass grows all over the area. The plains can barely be seen through the trees to the south.
20280: A finch flies low above the ground.

A lot of rowan trees are growing here, their roots dominating the forest floor. The trees are covered with old, dead leaves. Grass grows anywhere it can find the space to grow. None of the ferns seen elsewhere in the forest has been able to grow here. The plains can be faintly seen through the trees to the south. The forest extends in all directions.
20281: A finch flies low above the ground.

The tree-growth is very dense in this area. It is difficult to tell the birch trees apart, since they are growing so close together. Their roots are staying mainly under the ground, allowing for green grass and ferns to grow around the packed groups of trees. The forest continues in all directions.
20282: A tall birch is here, watching over the landscape.

The trees are packed together very tightly in this area. There is no grass growing in what little space is left. The roots of the trees have been forced to grow above ground due to the immense number of them. They have formed an impassable wall to the north. The ground rises up to the west.
20283: The rowan trees continue to grow as the forest floor increases sharply in altitude. The ground is almost completely free of tree roots, allowing the green grasses and ferns to flourish. The branches of the trees create a barrier so thick, not even the daytime sunlight can penetrate to the forest below.
20284: A finch flies low above the ground.

The ground suddenly falls away to the north. The birch trees here are giving the edge of the cliff a wide berth. A few tree roots reach out and over the edge of the cliff, helplessly dangling in the air. Grass grows up to the edge of the cliff, providing some much needed traction. The ground slopes down from the cliff to the south.
20285: A finch flies low above the ground.

A group of birch trees is growing at the top of a long cliff. The trees are growing right up to the edge of the cliff and some look like they might fall off. The cliff is covered in roots and grasses, providing some traction. A portion of the cliff extends out about thirty feet from the base. The ground slopes away from the cliff to the south.
20286: A tall birch is here, watching over the landscape.

This area is very dim. The forest canopy has almost completely sealed off the outside light. Short grass grows in the darkness provided by the trees branches. Dead leaves cover the trees, while a few have what looks like a beard of lichen. The top of a cliff lies to the east, while the ground slopes downwards gradually to the south.
20287: A tall shrub with strong-smelling foliage is growing here.

A very large birch tree stands here, surrounded by smaller birches. The smaller birches are standing around the larger tree, appearing to guard it from the elements. A few flowers and ferns grow around the base of the large birch. There are a few breaks in the canopy, allowing light to stream in. Trees await in all directions.
20288: The birch trees here are very spread out. The ground is covered in a short, green grass. Some ferns have popped up in patches around the few stones that rest here. All passage to the west is blocked by a pile of boulders. A wall of stone rises out of the ground, continuing to rise as it heads to the west. The forest completely encompasses this area.
20289: A vertical wall of stone rises to the north. The base is littered with large rocks. In fact, a pile of boulders have stacked up against the wall, blocking travel to the east.
