The face of the stone wall is very rough, but the masses of moss clinging to it make the rock face impossible to climb. The wall slopes quickly down to the east, appearing to end just beyond the pile of boulders.
20290: The birch trees are loosely dispersed throughout the area. They are covered with dead leaves and a few have beards of lichen. Green grass is growing around the masses of tree roots, with a few ferns scattered around. The ground slopes up sharply to the south.
20291: On a Plateau in the Forest

Grasses grow this small plateau and there is a distinctive lack of trees. The only other flora is a variety of ferns. The land is quite higher, being south of a steep incline that leads to a dell just north. Southward the land makes a sharp drop as a sheer rock face dotted with some mosses makes travel that direction completely undesireable.
20292: Below a Cliff in the Forest

A tall birch is here, watching over the landscape.
A large rabbit looks peacefully at you, ready to dart away.
A large rabbit looks peacefully at you, ready to dart away.

The birch trees here appear to be a bit taller than their neighbours. They, like most of the other trees, are still clad in the leaves of yesteryear. Short, green grasses grow around the base of the trees, and ferns grow up around the exposed roots of the trees. There is a steep rock cliff to the south and the ground slopes upwards to the east.
20293: A scattering of rowan trees grow between the tufts of short, green grass that covers much of the ground. Some small ferns have sprouted around their roots, just beginning their lives in contrast to the large trees that are covered in dead leaves from seasons past. The ground rises gradually to the south. What looks like the bottom of a cliff can be seen to the east.
20294: A mass of low-spreading shrub quivers on the ground.

This area rises about fifty feet above the rest of the forest floor. Small ferns dot the patches of grass that cover the top and sides of the hill. The rowan trees here aren't any shorter than the trees in the rest of the forest. The stale air has also become thinner with the increase in altitude. All directions lead back down to the forest floor.
20295: A few rocks are scattered around the landscape. This area is very dim, as there are no breaks in the branches of the massive pine trees to let any light through. Short grass grows all over the area and it seems to flourish in the darkness provided by the trees. Dead leaves cover all of the pines, while a few have what look like beards of lichen.
20296: A sharp ridge ascends to the west from the forest floor. The pine trees here are covered in a massive amount of dead leaves. The air is stale and the visibility has decreased under the forest canopy. The ground is covered in rocks and smaller stones. A sheer drop awaits to the south while the forest unfolds to the east.
20297: The steep slope ends abruptly in a sheer drop to the south. The surface of the ridge has been beaten smooth by time. There is no plant life attached to the slippery rock. The ridge disappears into the east, but flattens out to the west, allowing a myriad of bushes to take over the bare rock.
20298: The mountain ridge is almost completely covered with green bushes. Although the ridge is very high, all you can see of the ground below is trees. The ridge continues on up to the west until it meets a peak of the Misty Mountains. The mountain slopes down slowly to the north. A sheer drop waits to the south. The ridge runs down into the east until it disappears into Fangorn.
20299: The area is completely devoid of plant life. Only large, grey rocks dot the landscape. The rocks are large enough that they would provide a decent amount of shade from the daytime sun. The slope is slight and it continues up to a ridge farther to the south. A very steep climb can be had to the east.
20300: A sturdy pack horse is standing here.

The mountain rises to a level area before starting to ascended very quickly. The slope is so steep, it would take a master climber to be able to scale this rock face. The rock face is bare and almost devoid of foot or hand holds. To the west, the slope looks easier to climb. The ridge runs east into Fangorn.
20301: The terrain rises gradually to the west. The ground is littered with stones and a few clumps of ferns dot the surroundings. A large rock is here, and a few holes in it would allow a skilled climber to climb to the top. The tall pine trees have grown in a circle around the boulder.
20302: The forest floor is free of rocks and other debris. A warm, green grass covers almost the entire area. Some sweet smelling ferns grow in patches under a few of the pine trees. The trees are carrying the leaves of a generation, but one of the pines seems to have more than the rest. To the west, a rather large rock lies amongst the trees. The forest spreads out in all directions.
20303:
A solid, but stunted, rowan tree has established itself here.
On the rowan, there are a cluster of rowan berries.

Something must have happened here. One of the great rowan trees has been ripped from the ground and its trunk completely blocks off passage to the east. Dead leaves and lichen litter the grass about the dead tree. The other trees seem to have formed a circle around their fallen comrade, almost as if mourning. The forest continues on in the other directions.
20304:
A tall shrub with strong-smelling foliage is growing here.
On the shrub, there are two clusters of elderberries.

Roots and low-laying branches touch each other allowing travel only so far toward the east and none at all to the north and south. What are little more than tiny crawl spaces between the gnarled vegetation would make excellent homes for small animals seeking a protected place to sleep however, curiously not a single sign of inhabitants can be seen.
20305: Willow trees grow all around this area. They stand tall, almost regally, untouched by the passage of time. The ground is covered with their roots, making walking difficult. Some ferns and grasses grow in patches that have yet to be disturbed by the tree roots. The ground slopes down to the west, but the roots of the trees, along with the steepness of the incline, make it too difficult to navigate.
20306: Green grass and some sweet-smelling ferns grow in the shade that the forest provides. The trees growing here seem to encircle a much thicker tree, whose massive roots have completely blocked off travel to the east. What looks like a depression in the forest can be seen to the west.
20307: The ground is covered with masses of tree roots, only penetrated by the trunks of the massive willow trees. The trees grow straight up into the sky, creating a dense, almost impenetrable canopy with their branches. The roots have grown into a wall, blocking travel to the east.
20308: The oak trees here are covered in dead leaves. The roots of the trees twist in and out of the ground, mingling with each other above ground before returning underground. Green grass grows in between the masses of tree roots, with a few ferns sticking up. The ground dips slightly to the south, into what looks like a small valley. The forest extends in all other directions.
20309: A large rabbit looks peacefully at you, ready to dart away.

The oak trees here are very broad across their trunks. These trees are some of the thickest in the whole forest. They have beards of lichen and wear their dead leaves like heavy winter coats. Green grass covers the floor of the forest. A single break in the canopy above yields a bit of light. The forest extends in all directions.
20310: A tall, slender hornbeam Ent walks around here, keeping watch over his trees.

The oak trees grow here in what appears to be a circular pattern. One large oak tree grows in the centre. The ground is covered with short, green grass and some sweet-smelling ferns are growing between the tangles of the tree roots. Through the trees, what appears to be a small hill can be seen to the west.
20311: The forest opens into a knoll of wild grasses and ferns. There is one massive oak tree at the top of the knoll, seemingly surveying the rest of the forest. At the base of the knoll, a small burrow entrance has been dug. The forest encompasses this area.
20312: Some stones have been deposited here by an ancient rockslide. Grass grows around the rocks, with some sweet smelling ferns poking out. The pine trees in this area are remarkably free of dead leaves and lichen. The air is a bit stuffy, making it slightly difficult to breathe at first. The forest stretches out in all directions.
20313: A spiky broomrape plant pokes its blooms out of the soil.

The rocky terrain is flat and level. The trees seem to be more concentrated here than in the other areas of the forest. The pines are wearing beards of lichen and the dead leaves are reminiscent of the fur coat on a mammal. Small ferns dot the landscape. The base of a mountain rises out of the forest to the north. Trees stand in all other directions.
20314: The terrain slopes upwards to the south. The pine trees have grown around a rather large boulder that has rolled down off of the mountain. The trees stifle the air here, making it hard to breath. To the west, the mountain rises up into the clouds while more of Fangorn waits to the east.
20315: The side of the mountain is covered in thick green brush. Many rocks are scattered about, ranging in size from that of a petite hobbit to a massive troll. The mountain continues to rise steadily to the south. The mountain ends in a wide ridge farther south. The edge of a dark forest lies to the east.
20316: A waist-high evergreen shrub grows here, with thick, reaching branches.

The base of the mountain is covered by green shrubs. The mountain slopes up to the south at a very leisurely pace, an easy climb for anyone. Another mountain rises to the north. To the east, a group of tall dark trees have filled the valley created by the feet of one of the peaks of the Misty Mountains.
20317:
A mountain ibex is jumping from rock to rock.
A mountain ibex is jumping from rock to rock.
A mountain ibex is jumping from rock to rock.

Multiple yellow sandstone boulders ply their way out of the mountainside here. Smooth, but shaped at odd angles, these rocks reach out from the dark brown earth and flow past the yellow-green grass blades that line the mountain. Among the soft foliage of the mountain lie a few other boulders that still are implanted in the rock.
20318: In the distance the mountains still climb, but at a more drastic and chaotic rate than before. Grey chunks of rock litter the ground in forms of oddly shaped pebbles and boulders, between the debris grow a few thin yellow-gray coloured grasses in stark contrast to the landscape in the east where a grey forest can be spotted.
20319: The ridge here ends at the base of the mountains. The wind screams down from the cold white peaks bearing a biting cold chill. To the south, the ridge continues its way downwards as a brown streak of broken rock and yellow grass. To the far east the ground is silhouetted by an ancient forest, grey and ominous.
20320: The ground slopes slowly upward and erodes away into a jagged structure of solid rock. Following the lines of the ridge, the mountains ascend once again at a renewed pace. At lower elevations the vegetation thrives and then booms into a grey forest. At the top of the rocky slope lies a cluster of stones that denote the entrance to a dim moist cave descending deep into the earth.
20321: A thin spine of grey rock pierces its way out of the crude ground. Pebbles and sharp rocks layer the landscape. In the distance towards the mountains, the spine continues, while to the east and west the land curves upwards. Towards the far east a grey forest can be spotted, covered in mist.
20322: The terrain slopes downward from the north with deep scrapes in the ground due to wind and rain. Grey rocks poke out at all angles giving a bit of shelter to the occasional patches of yellow grass. Very little plant life has managed to find enough soil to take root within the crags of this forsaken ridge.
20323: Grey rocks cover the ground, allowing very little grass to grow. Short thin blades of yellow grass grow in small patches among the rocks and boulders. A large amount of rubble crawls out from the ground in the rugged northern ridge and then roughly proceedes towards the rockslide that sits in the south.
20324: A colourful butterfly is fluttering around here.

Brown pebbles litter the ground. Their curved surfaces are nearly smooth from weathering. Between them spawn many small grasses, yellow in colour and small among the pebbles and moss. A few larger rocks accumulate to the west. Farther to the south and east the ground becomes more malleable until it reaches a wall of trees and roots.
20325:
A low and wide-spread tree grows here.
On the tree's branches, there are four juicy plums.

Trees can be seen digging their way into the earth in every direction except to the north. Their gnarled roots crawl across the earth, splicing groves in which grasses grow and pebbles are planted. Looking farther up, the roots become a giant wall of trunks and branches, stretching upwards and topped with a canopy of immense size.
20326:
There is some snow on the ground.
An imposing beech tree sways gently in the wind.

Thick knotted grey roots sprawl across the ground. Around them small ferns grow and upon them, mosses in return. The stale air is very misty, stringy lichen hang from branches and trunks. Everywhere, spring trunks from a pile of roots and they stretch into the sky with branches sticking out in all directions. A thick canopy of branches and leaves makes it difficult to tell how high the trees reach by glancing upward.
20327: There is some snow on the ground.

A jungle of weeping willows grows here, each having its branches reach high and then bedeck the area with its curtains of tear like leaves. As the mist wisps in a ghostlike apparition through the wood, one cannot help but notice the wet ground, littered with pebbles and vegetation of small ferns and light grasses.
20328: Oak trees grow loosely around the area, creating plenty of room for the growth of ferns and grasses. The roots of the trees poke up out of the ground in places, creating many good resting spots. The trees begin to fan out to the south, creating what looks like the entrance to a secluded dell. The trees continue on in all other directions.
20329: A tall shrub with strong-smelling foliage is growing here.

Very large oak trees grow here. They are covered in dead leaves that have never fallen. The ground is covered in a short green grass. Sweet-smelling ferns grow beneath some of the trees, creating a distinct fragrance. The canopy of the forest is pierced by only the slightest amount of outside light, making this area very dim.
20330: Many large oak trees stand here in silence, unwavering in the dank stagnant air that has been trapped by their massive branches. They are covered with dead leaves and lichen. The rocks that have fallen on the land just west of here from the mountains in that same direction have left this area untouched seemingly just out of their reach. The forest extends in all directions.
20331: There are fewer rocks here than along the border of the forest. Some green ferns have sprouted on and around the roots of some of the larger pine trees that dominate this area. The ferns and roots look like hairs covering pairs of large flat feet while the trees look of old men, with beards of lichen and dead leaves. All around, more of the vast forest awaits.
20332: The ground is covered in rocks and stones from rockslides coming down the high slopes of the Misty Mountains. Tall pine trees have grown about the slope, not minding the rocks. Some soft grass has sprouted up around the bottoms of the rocks enjoying the shade. An endless amount of trees extends to the east and south.
20333: The ground slopes upward to the north where it joins the rest of the mountain. The area is covered with green shrubs and many large rocks rest in the lower areas. A valley of pine trees lies to the west. Fangorn awaits to the south, while the mountain beckons from the north.
20334: A Valley between the Feet of a Mountain
A mass of low-spreading shrub quivers on the ground.

The rocky terrain coming off the base of mountains has formed a small valley. Pine trees have grown in the natural shield created by the mountain. The trees are covered in the needles of years long past. The air inside the valley is very stuffy and hard to breathe. The forest opens up to the south.
20335:
A mountain ibex is jumping from rock to rock.
A mountain ibex is jumping from rock to rock.
A mountain ibex is jumping from rock to rock.

Many fragments of what once were great rocks together with mounds of disturbed earth lie in a catastrophic disarray. Within the now shattered grey bedrock lie deep gouges, and within them streaks of rust and silver veins of iron. To the southeast of this collapsed mountainside lies a seemingly very thick and grey forest. The ridge rises gently further to the north.
20336: The earth here consists of a rich, dark red flavour, possibly due to iron in the bedrock. Green grasses grow with great vigour upon this red ridge, and they sway calmly with the wind in waves of great beauty. Among them are also many clusters of rocks leaving the impression of an ore field. Yet among the grey mountains, the green that towers in the southeast is easily spotted, for a giant forest springs from within that area.
20337: Flowing downwards, the grim brown mountains follow the same smooth circular contour that can be seen for miles. Many short yellow grasses thrive in patches among the grey rocks that spot the earth, while larger grey sandstone boulders lie buried in the ground. To the southeast lies a misty forest of great size from which a warm current of air rises upwards.
20338: A thin, crippled deer looks around timidly.

Sloping into the ground, the valley is drastically different than the nearby environment. Grasses grow much taller, reaching nearly twice the height of the higher altitude strains. Large stones reveal themselves among the grasses, in rather unexpected places. A thick, grey forest of trees lies to the far east.
20339: A giant slab of grey rock sits implanted into the earth. Its multilayered form is coloured in many intricate variations of grey and then slowly turns to a green as more dirt and moss cling to its base. Around it, there grow multiple types of grasses, some long and some short, but none as tall as the immense grey wall of ancient tree trunks that blockades the south.
20340: Small brown pebbles litter the ground in random patterns. Locked around them grow yellow-green grasses and ferns. As the forest approaches from the south the rocks start to accumulate in grey piles, from which the forest mist glides over onto the ground. A wall of predominantly oak and other species of trees grow here and to the south, blocking the view.
20341: A tall birch is here, watching over the landscape.

A grey canopy lies above, interwoven with branches and twigs, blocking out most of the light that tries to pierce its way through. The slope of the ground rises noticeably to the north, where a giant limestone boulder lies covered in roots and fallen leaves. The air is stuffy and covered in a grey mist.
20342: Only a few mossy green plants find their way through the root systems of the large willow trees that dominate much of this part of the forest. The roots rise up so high that the trees' long weeping limbs brush across and sometimes tangle themselves within the mass of roots.
20343:
A brown striated fungus hangs here, clinging to a tree trunk.
A finch flies low above the ground.

Short green grasses and a few ferns are growing around the roots of the trees growing here. The trees in this area are covered with a lot more lichen and leaves than most of the other trees in the forest. Their massive roots have created a wall nearly twenty feet tall, blocking movement both south and north.
20344:
A spiky broomrape plant pokes its blooms out of the soil.
A spiky broomrape plant pokes its blooms out of the soil.

The forest flows into this small dell. The floor of the dell is covered with green grass and ferns. The oak trees here have fewer leaves, but more lichen on their trunks than in other areas of the forest. The roots of the trees, combining with the steepness of the inclines, make travelling any way other than north impossible.
20345: The oak trees growing here are surrounded by their massive roots. A very small amount of grasses and a few ferns are able to grow in this choked atmosphere. The ground slopes down to the east, into what looks like a dell. Unfortunately, the ground is too steep and the roots do not provide enough footholds to be able to climb down.
20346: The tall rowan trees are growing around an old, dead log. Dead leaves and lichen litter the ground around the log, suggesting it has not been lying there too long. Green grasses grow all around the area and some ferns are sprouting around the exposed roots of the trees. The log completely blocks off travel to the west.
20347:
A clear spring babbles as cool water trickles out of the ground.
A mountain ibex is jumping from rock to rock.

A smooth overhang projects itself across the cliff, providing shelter to a small spring. The water trickles down from the side of the cliff into a crystal clear collecting pond. Green mosses grow nearby in the comfort of the scattered grey pebbles that make up the floor. The top of a ridge is seen in the east, and the ground slopes down in the south to what appears to be a mountain pass.
20348: Here a huge barren rock sits a foot higher than the rest of the ridge and lies implanted in the ground. Around it protrude other rocks from the ground, coloured in grey and brown similar to those found at lower heights. The ground slowly climbs towards the grey mountains, making very slow progress. In the distance, at the bottom of the mountains in the east, a grey and shrouded forest can barely be seen.
20349: Rocks of multicoloured grey, brown, and red stand out in jagged formations in the land. The barren wasteland of stone is not very stable and rocks constantly tip if too much pressure is applied by anyone that treads upon them. A rocky cliff stands to the north, leading from east to west. From where the cliff heads to the distant mountains, the ground slopes eastward into a grassy plateau and a sombre wood.
20350: A colourful butterfly is fluttering around here.

In lines of green, yellow, and blue, the field upon the plateau waves as the mountain air blows down across grass blades in a coquettish dance. Jutting through the soil are sharp grey rocks that lead toward the north and west where they are met by a giant cliff. Leading down from the heights, the land drops into a rock covered terrain that abruptly halts at the eve of a forest.
20351:
A giant boulder sits here among the swaying grasses.
A colourful butterfly is fluttering around here.

Grasses of vibrant greens and yellows grow around the plateau. Everything sways in the wind with the exception of a giant boulder that sits permanently in the soil. The dark cliff that has been trailing in the north now ends abruptly and turns towards the west. Similarly, the shrouded forest in the southwest follows the same contour.
20352: Grasses in a multitude of greens and yellows billow in waves across the land, moving according to the wind that blows down from the mountains. All around these wild grasses grow, hardy from winter months and frigid air. A cliff blocks the way westward and stretches from the white mountains all the way down to the warmer lowlands. To the east, a dim forest stands, covered in mist.
20353: A crumbling spine of scattered brown rocks crawls up the ridge. Some grasses grow in tufts and alter in colour as the land rises. To the west the rocks stretch off towards the seemingly unreachable snowy mountains beyond the cliff. A grey forest topped in dark green grows to the north.
20354: Different sized slabs of dark rocks pile at the bottom of the cliff. Vertical grooves and overhangs are scratched into the sheer sides that stretch from west to east. The top of the cliff is barely visible as an abrupt halt of broken rocks. The base sprawls across the landscape and is met by a misty forest in the northeast.
20355: Fallen debris lies scattered all about the ground, creating a maze of rock coming out of the cliff wall. The gouged rock on the cliff glistens with water, only enough to make the cliff damp. A misty forest lines the cliff to the north and east, nearly reaching the same height as the wall of stone. A chilly breeze blows down from the cliff heights.
20356: A dark cliff rises to the south, littering the ground with slabs of dark rock. It is gouged with vertical and horizontal grooves, places from where the slabs might have fallen. Away from the cliff, in the distance, a forest can be seen shrouded by mist, reaching an immense height.
20357: An old man, swathed in a great light-coloured cloak, is standing here.

Certain portions of the ground are solid sandstone, whereas other parts are composed of loose dirt topped by yellow grass blades, struggling to survive. Northwest, in the distance, a huge cliff can be seen. Stretching out towards the east a proud forest of trees grows blanketed by a misty air.
20360: In the distant west, a dark cliff grows ominously, but here, only a few pebbles dot the moist ground. For the most part, the ground harbours a few green grasses and a modest bit of moss. Yellow stones look as if they had been tossed about the area randomly. To the north, there rises a wall of trees not higher than three men, forming a dark canopy of grey and green.
20362: The ground here slopes down towards the northeast. The rich earth that covers the ground has been swept away, indicating that perhaps this area was once a riverbed in ages past. The tree roots crawl like fingers into the abandoned riverbed and then burrow into the dry earth. From the north and east the sound of rushing water can faintly be heard.
20363:
There is some snow on the ground.
A bright red mushroom is growing here.
A solid, but stunted, rowan tree has established itself here.
On the rowan, there are a cluster of rowan berries.

A patch of rowans has started to grow here upon the hill. Through the trees and ashen mist one can make out the branches that spring out of the low lying trunks of these proud rowans. Most miraculous of all however, is how these slender branches weave up into the canopy, delicate yet strong. Covering the ground between the gnarled roots grows a variety of moss and mushrooms, taking advantage of the uncomfortable humidity.
20364:
There is some snow on the ground.
A cluster of dark green, feathery fronds flourishes in the shade.

A creeping mist flows over the roots that cover the ground. It swirls about the trees and stifles everything in the moist air. From out of the ground rise giant boles with trunks that stretch up until their branches become entangled and form parts of a canopy that chokes out the light from above. Moss and ferns grow along the ground, speckled with dew.
20365: There is some snow on the ground.

The ground drops significantly to the south. Giant trees with interlocked roots grow at an angle to the ground with their majestic trunks reaching towards the sky. Small plants litter the ground, trying to prevent erosion. Roots line the slope southwards as well, making the passage up or down a bit easier. The sound of water can be heard from the northeast.
20366:
There is some snow on the ground.
An ash tree with mottled bark stands here apparently guarding its surroundings.
A tall birch is here, watching over the landscape.

Grey roots crisscross on the ground, shattering the earth with their strength. They grow around each other and smother almost everything, leaving barely enough space for smaller plant life, such as ferns and mosses that grow in cracks. The trees themselves reach an enormous height and create a thick canopy that allows no light to pierce it.
20367:
There is some snow on the ground.
A large boulder is here, it must be heavy.

A worn limestone stream bed can be seen through the fallen leaves and twigs. Once a mighty riverbed for the Entwash, this route has now gone silent. A few trees have begun to reclaim the land with their weeping branches and roots but all is solemn. A giant boulder lays here, forgotten by the ancient river that had once brought it over from the mountains and now abandoned it in the forest.
20368:
There is some snow on the ground.
On the ground, there are two bright red mushrooms.

Grey trees tower around this area, while little grasses pop out of the ground. Dull coloured ferns thrive here and their small leaves cover the forest floor. The trees tower above the rest of the plant life, their branches and leaves entangled, blocking out the light. The moist ground dips and rises, leaving holes underneath roots where a few mud-stained mushrooms slowly grow.
20370:
A colourful butterfly is fluttering around here.
A colourful butterfly is fluttering around here.
A colourful butterfly is fluttering around here.

The ground is almost absent of plant life, a few scraggly grasses manage to take root and many sun-tanned sandstone rocks are displayed in low lying curved packets. With the exception of the west and north, there lies a forest of great trees, their branches reaching enormous heights and their gnarled trunks forming a wall. As the slope continues westward, the grasses grow in great quantities.
20371: A fallow deer is grazing peacefully here.

Sun bleached rocks are scattered throughout the dirt here. The earth is hard, being mostly clay, and the signs of erosion are very visible. Ruts are scrawled into the earth with the exception of a few spots of solid sandstone that endure the onslaught. To the north a grey forest is seen, and in the distance the mountain seems to reach its highest peak.
20372: A colourful butterfly is fluttering around here.

The earth begins to slope to the south and to climb to the north, all in harmony with the dull dirt-covered mountains to the west. Here, the forest is a bit more colourful. Huge boles and strong roots start at the base and climb upward into the canopy of green leaves. Further within the forest, a mist can be seen floating about.
20373: To the northeast, there lies the Forest of Fangorn. A wall of grey brown tree trunks stops all further sight deeper into the forest. Their branches tower above at a terrible height, creating a huge curtain of twigs and leaves that blocks out any light from above. To the southwest lie the roots of the snow-capped mountains.
20374:
There is some snow on the ground.
A tall birch is here, watching over the landscape.

Paper bark litters the ground where some magnificent birch trees have shed their skins. Brittle orange leaves grow on their branches, and upon the ground a grey and orange blanket has been lain over time. High above in the canopy, the birch joins the storm of leaves and branches that helps the forest keep the light from above at bay, and the forest grey and dim.
20375:
There is some snow on the ground.
A tangly shrub seems to rustle as if alert to its surroundings.
An ash tree with mottled bark stands here apparently guarding its surroundings.
A tall birch is here, watching over the landscape.

The moist ground that harbours so many ferns and grasses suddenly takes a giant dip due to the remnants of an old rocky sinkhole. It has long since been filled with organic debris, but the sharp rocks that jut out in all directions give it a unique shape compared to the rest of the forest. Roots have progressively filled the depression with their gnarled forms.
20376:
There is some snow on the ground.
A white centipede is here.

One giant oak tree, which is larger than all the others, silently grows here. Its crooked bark is filled with dirt and moss while young ferns grow between its ancient, mushroom covered, roots. Around the giant oak grows its offspring, far younger, but still old. From their branches the oaks block out most of the light, and with their roots they crush their way into the earth.
20377: Some thick writhing vines whip all around you.

The ground is covered by giant grey vines and roots, making it more difficult travelling through all the vegetation. Looking farther, the grey trunks blend with the mist that covers the forest and ascends up into the air. Tree limbs shooting out in all directions form a mesh that finally disappears into the grey canopy in a blanket of leaves and branches.
20378:
A spiky broomrape plant pokes its blooms out of the soil.
A colourful butterfly is fluttering around here.

A great wall of trunks, roots, and branches lie directly to the east. It is an ominous visage as the trees reach up and blanket the sky. The ground is moist, harbouring many small green grasses and reddish stones that seem to have crawled down from the mountains. A grey mist seems to flow in from the east, the most likely source of the moisture found on the ground.
20379:
There is some snow on the ground.
An imposing beech tree sways gently in the wind.

Grey coloured trees grow out of the dirt among the moist grasses. The trees tower above all other plant life with their branches and leaves entangling the light and absorbing it. The moist ground dips and rises, leaving small depressions underneath the roots, where a few mud-stained mushrooms and dull coloured ferns are able to grow.
20380:
There is some snow on the ground.
A spiky broomrape plant pokes its blooms out of the soil.
A spiky broomrape plant pokes its blooms out of the soil.

A ghostly mist creeps in from the west and flows over the damp moss that seems to flourish in the moist ground. The grey and brown bark that covers the trees is tinged slightly green from the grasses and moss that grow on them. However, they still grow up into the canopy that covers the sky in all directions. Willows are seen growing closely together in the far west.
20381: The forest seems as old here as the world itself. It is as if this place is close to the heart of Fangorn and the primordial power of its creation remains. The trees are grey, gnarled beyond recognition and covered in shaggy thick coats of moss and tendrils of ancient dusty lichen. Yet, everything is still very much alive.
20382: The forest here is ancient beyond measure. Near the heart of Fangorn, a living power seems to suffuse the area. The most prominent feature is a tall and dense impenetrable wall of dark evergreen trees, bearing many olive-coloured flowers. A narrow entranceway leads through it to what appears to be a large grassy clearing south of here.
20383: This part of the forest has the feeling of being close to the heart of Fangorn. There is a feeling of ancient power and life here that permeates all things. It must be due to that power that the trees survive into such old age. Certainly, the great willow tree standing here is quite hollow, and one would expect it to be dead and rotten. Yet the topmost leaves are clearly a fresh green and are swaying contentedly in the air high above.
20384: The area is dominated by a grove of weeping willows, leaning over the clear waters of the Entwash as they feel the fresh air and drink of the cool clear liquid. This is an area of great tranquillity. The atmosphere suggests that these trees are as gracious and humble as any in the forest, despite their great age. The same cannot be said east of here, where blackness seems to hang over the area.
20385: There is a great feeling of animosity and hatred here, emanating strongly from the bank of elm trees lining the river to the east. However, the trees are somewhat preoccupied with reaching across the river. It would be wise to stay well out of their way. North of here the river surges through some rapids, but the steep bank leading abruptly into the water would be none too easy to climb back up.
20386: There seems to be a permanent transition between light and dark in this region. Not so much between daylight and night time, which still pass in the regular way, but of brightness and goodness west of here in comparison to a gloom and sense of evil to the north. The Entwash glides past sombrely just a short distance east of here.
20387:
A tiny spider is here, eating a tiny bug.
A tiny spider is here, eating a tiny bug.
A tall and haughty elm stands here.
A black alder looms threateningly over its surroundings.

The trees here are spaced slightly further apart than is usually seen in Fangorn, allowing a fresh breeze down to the forest floor. Also the trees in this area are unlike any others around these parts. They are not as large as most of the Fangorn trees, and have elegantly sweeping branches that bear heart-shaped leaves and soft yellow flowers. The air is heavy with their fragrant scent.
20388: A tall and haughty elm stands here.

In stark contrast to the ancient and greying trees in this part of the forest, a large impenetrable hedge rises up on the west side. It seems composed of broadleaved evergreen trees, like a thornless holly, and towers many feet high in a totally impenetrable barrier. Yet there is one narrow opening in it, leading through into what appears to be a large and deep clearing.
20389: Deep, wide and almost as round as a bowl, Derndingle is smooth, grass-clad and treeless except for three very tall and beautiful silver birches at its base. Three well-worn paths lead down from narrow openings in the encircling hedge on the west, north and east sides, and there is a small well in the north slope.
20390:
A tall shrub with strong-smelling foliage is growing here.
A colony of red ants is here. The ants seem to ignore you.

Amid one of the most ancient parts of Fangorn Forest, age-old tree roots lie under a thick covering of old leaves, lichens, mosses and other debris formed from long-since-fallen foliage. On the east side a fresh tall hedge of dark evergreens stand in stark contrast to the other trees in the area. A narrow opening in the hedge leads into what appears to be a large grassy clearing.
20391: The river a little north of here certainly seems to lend a great deal of vigour to this area of Fangorn's vegetation. Even the ground cover seems greener, healthier and stronger than in other parts of the forest. The shrubs and trees soar to the skies with abundant energy.
20392: The ancient trees have stood here so long they are almost hidden under thick tousled layers of moss and lichen. Long-fallen leaves litter the floor in a deep carpet, unmoved for countless years by the lack of any circulating air at the ground level. Although the Entwash can be heard north of here, southwards things seem very still and quiet.
20393: A small patch of dark-green moss grows in the deepest shade.

An ancient stand of weeping willow trees cluster around the bank of the Entwash. Their low drooping limbs almost trail the ground as their twisted roots reach into the flowing water. Elsewhere, the forest is made up of mainly broadleaved oaks and chestnuts, offering a little more light and air down to the forest floor than in most other areas of Fangorn.
20394: A great rarity for Fangorn forest indeed, some small hawthorn shrubs have proven more successful in this area than the otherwise ubiquitous ancient trees that the rest of the forest seems composed of. The result is that fresh air easily permeates down to ground level, creating a pleasant freshness normally only experienced in open clearings.
20395:
A comfortable-looking mossy stone lies here.
A tall, slender hornbeam Ent walks around here, keeping watch over his trees.

The forest opens up to greet the Entwash here, where a large, smooth and water-rounded mossy stone sits on the bank. This would be an ideal place to drink of the refreshing waters before resting awhile on the perfectly placed rock at the water's edge. To the west the forest continues with a lack of taller trees, while eastward and southward the trunks rise up again, closer and thicker.
20396: A colourful butterfly is fluttering around here.

A comfortable and calming atmosphere pervades this area, with the Entwash flowing by to the north and east. A beautiful stand of silver birches arch over the water, intermingled by graceful rowans, in the spring their red berries bright in the calm air. To the west there seems to be a clearing of some sort, while south of here, a grove of what appears to be apple trees grows in an almost organised fashion.
20418: The distinctively shaped maple leaves cover the ground in a red, gold and green carpet as if this place lies under perpetual Autumn. Many maple trees arch above, their foliage every imaginable shade of fiery red to soft green and yellow. Occasionally, little winged seeds spiral down from above, adding to the carpet of leaves below.
20420: The forest opens up suddenly into a smooth grass-covered glade. Why the trees have not taken root here like elsewhere is hard to comprehend, yet the effect is stunning. A dense carpet of bluebells sways perpetually in the breeze, sending a heady fragrance into the air.
20422: A green hill runs east to west, growing steeper and more banked the further west it goes. Travel southwards from here is impossible as the ground falls away into a tangled undergrowth. In all other directions plenty of air and light is able to penetrate through this whole region.
20424: Under a smooth green bank lies a great mossy stone set upon grassy turf. A circle of graceful rowan trees surrounds the peaceful spot, perhaps for decoration and companionship or perhaps for defence also. As with all Ent-houses there is water from a clear spring bubbling quietly from the bank. The area is filled with wholesome, peaceful and fragrant scents of grass, rowan berries and water fresh as spring rain mingling in the cool air. A ring of graceful rowan trees grows here.
20438:
A short evergreen plant, with slightly bluish needles, grows here.
On the plant, there are two clusters of hard, round, black berries.
A colourful butterfly is fluttering around here.

At this, one of the most dense areas of evergreen trees in the forest, junipers crowd the lower levels of the canopy while tall and ageing firs spread wide above them. Together, they block almost all light from reaching the ground level. This dim area gets more illumination sideways than from above. Pinecones and needles from seasons long past litter the floor in a prickly but spongy mat.
20463: Upon the uneven ground a great tangle of thorns has taken hold, limiting the ability to travel any farther south. Tall trees, all of great age and stature rise above the undergrowth. Their broad leaves do not block out all of the light, but create a dappled effect at ground level, where shadows dance and flit as the forest roof responds to the wind high above.
20464: A colourful butterfly is fluttering around here.

In stark contrast to the wildness of the rest of the forest, a few neat rows of apple and cherry trees stand in this spot. They look to be of great age and bear nothing more than a few small wizened fruits now, yet their spacing suggests that once they were much more lush and productive. But now this orchard has long since fallen into old age and obscurity, just as the rest of Fangorn Forest has.
20465: Amid the other trees stands a massive horse chestnut. Its trunk would take five fully grown men with arms outstretched to encircle and its massive branches spread out over an area so large that it becomes an umbrella for many of the trees around it. Conkers abound on the ground in such numbers as to be hazardous to walk upon lest they roll aside causing one to lose their footing.
20466:
The remains of a mass of choking bindweed lie here in a heap of rotting compost.
The remains of a mass of choking bindweed lie here in a heap of rotting compost.
The remains of a mass of choking bindweed lie here in a heap of rotting compost.

Maybe the Ents and Huorns have let down their guard, or perhaps the smothering moss, lichen, creepers and bindweeds have been encouraged to dominate this particular area of the forest. Certainly, nothing seems to last long here without being dragged down and throttled by bindweed and then covered utterly by a thick mat of undergrowth.
20467: Sloping up from the Entwash north of here, a wooden wall of countless trees rises out of the ground, blocking progress in all directions save west or onto the river itself. Trees grow right up to the stone, but even they cannot gain sufficient hold on the nearly vertical slopes to grow further up it. Mosses and lichens do a better job however, slowly etching and eroding the surface as the seasons pass.
20468: A giant and ancient yew stands here quite eerily.

A giant tree stands here, dominant over the others. This mature yew grows, proud and aloof, with needles so dense about it as to form an immeasurably thick spongy carpet. Its massive bole dwarfs all the trees around it. A small outcrop in the ground nearby yields a spring of fresh water, a feature that perhaps helped this tree to outgrow it's neighbours to such an extent.
20469: A colourful butterfly is fluttering around here.

Whether it was formed on a well-weathered outcrop of rock or a trunk of a long-fallen tree it is now impossible to tell, but there is a notable clearing here, in the middle of which is a mountainous shape covered in thick moss. It must have laid undisturbed for countless years, because the moss itself is grey and dusty, totally obscuring that which it lies on.
20470: This seems to be part of the oldest areas of Fangorn Forest. It is packed with densely grey trees, covered with thick coats of lichen and moss. The most noticeable feature is a tall dark barrier of closely packed evergreen trees, totally impenetrable from this position.
20471: Tall Grey Trees and Tangled Roots

It is as if this place has been lost in time. The air is totally still and rarely, if ever, is a sound heard. Tall smooth grey trunks stretch up to a broad canopy high overhead. Twisted roots lie motionless and still, covering the ground. Yet there is an atmosphere, not of emptiness and lifelessness, but alertness; as if this area is being watched.
20472: There is a water skin lying on the ground.

Washed rocks and pebbles cover the ground as a small tributary of the Entwash rushes down the hill into the grey and misty forest beyond. The ground rises to an open, grass-covered hill to the west. It is covered with rich yellow and green blades of grass, but there also grow two proud and dark polished pines. It slopes southward into a significantly less dense forest composed of deciduous trees.
20473:
There is some snow on the ground.
A majestic scots pine grows tall and straight here.

Two great trees stand here, one on each side of the hill, like living gate-posts. The two proud evergreens are polished dark, and gleam in the light that makes its way from the sky. From beneath their boughs and roots, the river Entwash splashes at a slow pace from a hidden location.
20474: There is some snow on the ground.

Beyond the dark pines to the east, there lies a wide level space, as though the floor of a great hall had been cut in the side of the hill. Two walls follow the level space on either side, growing in height. On each side of the path, there sits an aisle of trees that grow in size as they progress towards the back of the hall. Running from the west, a small tributary of the Entwash river gurgles its way down the slope towards the east.
20475: There is some snow on the ground.

Trees of various species grow here at medium height and gradually get taller as they progress westwards towards the rock-face. The forest floor consists of a multitude of green ferns, grasses, and mosses that patch the brown damp earth. The slow rustle of water can be heard from the north.
20476: There is some snow on the ground.

A rock face that reaches about fifty feet stands here, its sheer face made up of solid yellow granite. The trees have grown to an enormous height and their canopy nearly blocks out all light from above. To the east, the forest starts to shrink in height and a slight rustle of water can be heard towards the large level area in the north.
20477: There is some snow on the ground.

The end of the path has now stopped at the rock wall that stretches upwards for fifty feet or more. At the bottom, it has been hollowed back into a shallow bay with an arched roof of stone. Far above, a spring pours silver drops of water down upon the face of the rock wall and spills like a fine curtain in front of the arched bay. The water gathers in a stone basin in the floor and then flows out beside the open path, down towards the east.
20478:
A worn clay bowl is lying on the ground.
A great stone table has been set here.
An old, wise tree with penetrating green eyes stands here.
A stocky mountain mule is here, waiting to serve.
A domesticated pony, beast of burden to many, stands here.
A domesticated pony, beast of burden to many, stands here.
A domesticated pony, beast of burden to many, stands here.
A domesticated pony, beast of burden to many, stands here.
A domesticated pony, beast of burden to many, stands here.
A domesticated pony, beast of burden to many, stands here.
A domesticated pony, beast of burden to many, stands here.

A large, hollowed out bay has been dug out of the rock-wall. Its arched roof makes a perfect turn about the cave for fifteen or more feet into the air. The inside of the bay is considerably dimmer than the outside, but a silver curtain of water that rushes down the outside of the bay gives a feeling of warmth to the room with its cleared basin and large stone structures.
20479:
There is some snow on the ground.
A tall and haughty elm stands here.

A sheer rock face now tells the end of the forest that grows within this hewn hall of granite. Reaching fifty feet into the air it surpassed all the trees of many forms that grow here within the hall. The damp earth that harbours plants, mosses, and ferns has been locked within a matrix of roots that then springs upwards into the tallest of the trees of this forest aisle.
20480:
There is some snow on the ground.
A domesticated pony, beast of burden to many, stands here.
A domesticated pony, beast of burden to many, stands here.
A domesticated pony, beast of burden to many, stands here.
A domesticated pony, beast of burden to many, stands here.
A domesticated pony, beast of burden to many, stands here.

The forest here grows well. Its roots stretch across the damp earth that harbours a myriad of fungi, mosses, and grasses alongside the giant trees that grow upwards in many slants and forms. As the forest progresses further towards the east, the sheer rock wall follows on the north, growing in size directly proportional to the surrounding forest. From the south, a slight whisper of water can be heard trickling away.
20481:
There is some snow on the ground.
A tall pine tree grows here.
A tangly shrub seems to rustle as if alert to its surroundings.
A tangly shrub seems to rustle as if alert to its surroundings.

Giant roots criss-cross along the ground, shattering their way into the earth and causing the forest floor to be littered with pebbles and debris. The canopy nearly shuts out all light in the massive tangle of grey branches found above. Still, the absence of light is joined by the sound of water towards the south, where the limestone bedrock is exposed to the air. The northern direction seems to be blocked by many closely growing pine trees.
20482:
There is some snow on the ground.
A tangly shrub seems to rustle as if alert to its surroundings.

A misty grey forest, composed of gnarled trees with an interlocking canopy of boughs and leaves, grows in near silence. A giant rock structure lies to the south, gouged with scrapes and nooks. Grey roots stream across the ground and anchor themselves into the mossy, twig covered forest floor of green and grey tones. The northern direction is blocked by several ancient trees that seem to have grown closely together for ages, in a west-east leading row.
20483:
There is some snow on the ground.
A rooting heap of stems is here, smothering the smaller plants.

The soil here has been scraped away, exposing rough limestone along the moist, twig covered ground. Though the limestone is hard, tree roots easily pierce their way through the stone rather than grow around. Through time the limestone has become more solid woven between age-old roots. The sound of water can be heard trickling away faintly.
20484:
There is some snow on the ground.
A mass of low-spreading shrub quivers on the ground.
A tangly shrub seems to rustle as if alert to its surroundings.
A rooting heap of stems is here, smothering the smaller plants.

Broken bits of limestone cover the ground as roots dig their way into the earth along the forest floor. The roots grind through all sorts of forest debris, littering the ground and heading in a vaguely southward direction. However, without apparent reason, everything seems to drift to this direction. The sound of water can barely be heard from the south, perhaps giving some reason to the southerly descent.
20485:
There is some snow on the ground.
A bright orange bracket fungus grows on some decaying wood.

Perception is entirely limited to three yards in any direction. Moist mossy and brown boles grow from the ground, stretching upward with immense power. A giant root slowly rises in a large arch before grinding into the limestone bedrock. Within the arch grows rows upon rows of orange mushrooms among a variety of moist mosses and green ferns.
20486:
There is some snow on the ground.
A mass of low-spreading shrub quivers on the ground.

The monotony of the forest is broken by an extremely dense grove of pines. Their knotted trunks are mottled in brown, and their thin scraggly branches plum out with greyish green needles. The air smells strongly of sap and there is a red bed of needles lying on the forest floor, mixing in with the moist rich earth where many light green ferns grow in the dim light.
20556: The Dwarven miners who carved these tunnels would despair at the state of disrepair which they have fallen into. A heavy coating of dust lies over the carefully piled stones they long ago removed from this corridor's walls. The walls, however, show signs of recent attention. Deep pick marks have been gouged into the rock, exposing ore and some other minerals.
20562: The top of this hill has been crowned with a large and perfectly round stone, apparently not shaped by nature. It is of a white-grey colour and probably dragged here from somewhere else. The other rocks in the vicinity are grey and some have been piled to protect the corpses of long dead men.
20645: The path continues east and west. To the east, you see a T-crossing. From here, a small path twists it's way up on a plateau, and on a bridge over the river Bruinen, while a trail continues into the Misty Mountains. South of here you see a barn. However, you cannot enter it from this point. The old farm-yard is south-west of here.
20658:
A huge black fungus is here, exuding a foul stench.
A huge black fungus is here, exuding a foul stench.
A giant, strange looking green fungus is here, ready to devour you in seconds.

This part of the burrow has been taken over by something a little less than benevolent. Where the other part was at least clean, whatever lives here just throws the remains of its meals into the corner. Joining the smell of wet fur is the cloying smell of the decaying remains in the corner. The burrow ends here, and the only way out is back to the west.
20659: You reach the peak of this small group of hills. Visions of glory and fortune enter your head as you look around you to the majestic plains, the wild forests, and the mysterious mountains. The hill slopes down to the west and to the east.
20660: Small Rapids in the River Bruinen

The river enters some rapids here, making swimming much harder. Flecks of foam and spray spit into the air, obscuring your vision, and the current begins to tug you westward with increasing speed. Looking downstream, where the valley narrows to a gorge, you can see the river being churned between towering walls of stone. To the east the river is calmer, and is crossed in a single span by a slender bridge.
20680:
An albino salamander is here, perched on some rocks.
An albino salamander is here, perched on some rocks.
An albino salamander is here, perched on some rocks.
An albino fish is swimming here, looking for some food.

It is a very strange cave. Magical powers surround you. Perhaps this cave was a meeting place where magic users in old days created new spells. Some years ago the cave was flooded by the nearby river, and new inhabitants moved in here.
20697: Sun-tanned stones of a light brown shade clutter the ground, locked in piles. Around them, the moist rich soil harbours moss and green grasses. The ridge rises toward the snow-capped mountains, turning slightly with the land contours. To the east the ground slowly seems to drop, and a forest is seen shrouded in a grey mist.
20698: An ancient oak is here towering above you.

A towering forest lies to the east with its branches reaching an enormous height. Grey bark and gnarled roots make up most of what can be seen in that direction. Far above, the branches consist of an entangled mess of differently nuanced leaves. A brown ridge with some spots of green foliage grows toward the white mountains to the east.
20699: There is some snow on the ground.

A giant cliff of rock towers in the east, with boulders and giant slabs lying around at different angles at its base. To the south lies a cliff of black rock with a slab propped up against it. Grasses grow interweaving between the rubble that litters the ground. The ridge seems to rise yet more to the west and onwards to the north.
20700: There is some snow on the ground.

The ridge slows its ascent and becomes nearly straight. Yellow and brown rocks make up clumped formations around this area. As the ridge trails onward, the rocks become larger and jut out of the ground to form an unclimbable maze. Boulders cover the ground, blocking passage to the south and west. To the north and east there is a rising ridge.
20701: An ancient fungus smothers the boulders.

Jagged rocks cover the dirt floor. The ceiling is composed of the same grey rock that makes up the giant slab for the entrance. The roof rises in an uneven arch until reaching the back wall of the cave. The slow drip of water can be heard from somewhere, carried along by a cold draft.
20702: Flowing from the west, the Entwash swiftly glides over rocks and pebbles. Rippling and ever in motion, it flows on towards the east into the mist. Above, a grey canopy covers the sky as branches struggle to gain access to any, even the most scant, rays of light. Rising sharply, the river bank of cracked limestone grows a few feet into the air, where tree roots dig their way down into the river.
20703: Cold water rushes down from the west to the east. Farther along the river, the water quietly trickles around rocks making many perfect ripples across its surface. At the top of the limestone bank lays a wall of brown and grey tree boles. They reach upward, each tree covered in moss forming a thick canopy of boughs and leaves that shuts out any light from above.
20704: Crystal clear water gurgles smoothly down the streambed, gliding in from the west and flowing south. It moves gracefully over the stones until it reaches one of the many rocks that it cannot completely rise over, and thus splashes into the air. Grey limestone, worn and old, makes up the bank, upon which a snarl of roots hints at the immense and thick forest that towers above.
20705: The water flows from the north and then on towards the east. It glides over river-worn pebbles and scrapes against the limestone that makes up the looming bank of the river. Trees, that grow into the sky, smother nearly all light from above with their branches forming an intricate web of leaves and twigs. From their boles reach roots of enormous size that grow down into the river.
20706: Sending ripples and gurgles along the water surface, the river Entwash flows from the west and down into the south. It swiftly moves across and around pebbles and stones until it meets a giant boulder that sits in the middle of the river, where it splits to pass on either side. The limestone bank consists of roots that slither among the giant boles and rocks in the misty light.
20707: The river flows from the north to the east. It flows over pebbles and stones, and along the banks, sending ripples across the water's surface. A bank composed of worn limestone rises a few feet into the air, where row upon row of strong roots dangle. At the top of the forest lies a tight blanket of woven branches and leaves that connect into a wall of grey trees in the mist.
20708: A Graceful Bend in the Entwash

The Entwash river gracefully meanders south. Its progress is smoother and less lively than where it descended from the spring at the foot of the Misty Mountains. Its water is crystal clear and looks refreshing and wholesome. The rich vegetation to either side of the river seems testament to the water's qualities, at least for plant-kind.
20709: The Entwash curves from south to east, carving a path through the lush green vegetation to either side. The open freshness of the area is invigorating indeed, compared to the dim stuffiness of much of the forest. Dense plant-life on both banks seem to thrive on the water's richness.
20710: As the river glides smoothly from west to east it passes by an ancient coppice of beech trees on the northern bank. Their roots twist thirstily into the water's edge as their boughs spread out overhead to catch all the light and air they can. One tree in particular has managed to grow a great branch almost entirely across the river, so the Entwash slips under a natural arch as it passes the trees.
20711: A Straight Stretch of the River

The river is straight and calm along this stretch, with both banks sloping so gently that it's impossible to tell where the reeds and bulrushes end and the solid banks start. To the east the river continues, though there seems to be something of a constriction of the waterway some distance downstream where the land gets more rocky and uneven.
20712: The river narrows and speeds up considerably as its way eastwards is blocked by a cliff. It is forced to bend around to the south. The cliff wall itself is made of a hard rock, though it is deeply cracked and worn, bearing deep underhangs and niches formed by the slow eroding flow of the Entwash.
20713: A Winding Curve on the Entwash

The Entwash river winds its way through hilly terrain, while changing its general direction of flow from southerly to more easterly for a few miles. The north-eastern bank is largely comprised of a rugged cliff which, although heavily forested on top, means little vegetation reaches the water's edge on that side. By contrast, to the west and south, large graceful stands of willow trees stand, swaying in the air and reaching into the currents to quench their ancient thirsts.
20714: The river straightens for a couple of miles, narrowed between a steep earthen bank to the south and a rocky pitted cliff face to the north. With the rough riverbed littered with worn boulders, the water leaps and surges as it careens along, white water jostling and throwing around any river-travellers in an alarming fashion.
20715: A change in the terrain of this area is echoed by a similar transition in the Entwash river. To the west, where the land is hillier and rockier, the river is fast and rough. However, despite a cliff making up the northern bank, the land begins to flatten out as it goes south and east. The river, though still rock-strewn and turbulent here, slows down considerably as it makes a southward turn. The vegetation on either side is rich and dense, fed by the clear waters of the Entwash.
20716: A Dark Stretch on the River

As the Entwash flows slowly along it deepens until the bottom is dark and scarcely visible. The river narrows and less light reaches the surface as a line of old mossy larches leans in threateningly from the eastern bank and a rank of ancient and hoary elms looms menacingly from the west. Tentacle-like roots snake into the water from both sides, writhing and snatching at anything that passes close by. The banks are definitely out of bounds to travellers.
20717: A Gentle Curve in the River

The river widens and brightens as it curves gently eastwards, the southern bank sloping softly into a pleasant grassy sward with a single large boulder resting at the water's edge. Meanwhile the river continues to flow lazily along, becoming increasingly shallow as it does so.
20718: A Straight Course on the River

The river seems to carve a divide between darkness and light. Ancient larches, twisted and bent with writhing grasping roots and tendrils reach into the water from the northern bank. One cannot leave the river on that side. Meanwhile a proud cluster of silver birches and the occasional rowan tree stand tall on the southern side, lifting each and every leaf to the fresh air above the Entwash.
20719: As the river turns slowly from east to south once more, a large sandy bar stretches into the water from the north bank, making it possible to wade almost half-way across the river. The pebble-strewn riverbed can be seen through the relatively clear water as if looking through a glass. In great contrast to this peaceful spot, to the east a great darkness appears to descend on the forest as if some great evil lives there.
20720: Though deeper here than to the north, the waters remain shallow. Yet the bottom, previously sandy, has more silt to it now, muddying the clarity of the river. Thick stands of reeds and bulrushes cluster on the south bank, making eerie hollow scratching noises when the air passes through them, rattling their woody stems against each other.
20721: The northern bank is dominated by a black brake of larches and pines. There seems to be a sense of looming hatred and malice, so much that the very waters of the Entwash seem to shrink back from the earth on that side. The river continues smoothly straight to the east where things seem somewhat brighter.
20722: The forest of Fangorn stretches mile upon mile before it opens up into the Plains of Rohan toward the southeast. The river Entwash passes the leagues in its own slow and meandering fashion, seeming in no hurry to either leave the forest or cross the broad plains before it meets and joins with the great River Anduin in a wide delta, before finally turning to the distant sea.
20723: A Dark Bank on the River
A swarm of mosquitoes is here, humming around you.

Although the Entwash flows serenely along just south of here, this area is extremely dark and foreboding. Light seems to actively avoid this grove of dark pines and larches. The river may be entered to the south, though a return up the steep muddy bank appears to be impossible. However, southwards looks to be a less dangerous direction than into the black forest north or west of here. A great evil can be felt close by, and this area is not far from the heart of it.
20724:
A black alder looms threateningly over its surroundings.
A swarm of mosquitoes is here, humming around you.

Upon entering this part of the forest, a rustling noise emanating from the edge of vision can be heard. The low groaning sound seems to contain great anger for whatever has disturbed this area. The trees jostle with grasping branches, and seem to move in closer surrounding intruders. No escape may be had north or west of here, and a deep ravine scores the land on the east, barring the way in that direction also. The only path away from here lies to the south.
20725: A giant and ancient yew stands here quite eerily.

The trees crowd and jostle one another and now and then a snide whispering can be heard amongst the leaves and twigs. The floor is thickly matted with ancient pine needles which muffle the air into a heavy and inert mass. To describe this place as dangerous would not even be close to accurate.
20726: The very air here throbs with malice. Even light and water, sacred to all plant-life, shun the area. The source of the dread is not clear, but it is probably ancient indeed. Yet it is clear that plants, as with other life, are swayed by evil as well as good. Surely, this is one of the most hateful of Fangorn's many dark groves.
20727:
A giant and ancient yew stands here quite eerily.
A tall and haughty elm stands here.

A dark brake of larches and pines has grown up in this part of the forest, extending south and east into even darker areas. The air is thick and laden with animosity and hatred as the evergreens rattle and creak ominously all around. Many might find this reason enough to beat a hasty path west or north to lighter areas of Fangorn.
20728: From west to east the ground becomes rocky and hilly, a steep slope pushing its way eastwards. In all directions travel looks like it could be tough, especially uphill, where the trees seem to have no regard for the rough terrain and just grow tighter and tighter together. A bare outcrop of rock here yields a very small spring.
20729: The forest is dominated by evergreen trees, primarily firs and spruces, yet they do not grow so thickly as to make the air unpleasantly stale. In fact, this region of the forest feels decidedly fresher and more open in comparison to the area east and south where the vegetation grows denser and darker.
20730: An Airless Part of the Forest
A colourful butterfly is fluttering around here.

The forest looms threateningly around any outsiders that dare travel here, creating a dark pocket, often unnerving all but the bravest or most foolhardy. The closely packed firs and spruces make travelling difficult as roots and twigs seem to grasp and trip at limbs with uncanny purpose. Things seem brighter to the west and north however. Perhaps progress would be easier in those directions.
20731: Deep inside this part of the forest, firs and spruces abound, clustered so densely together that little light reaches the forest floor. Yet the trees do not seem to be particularly malicious here, even though the air is rather stuffy from their considerable density. To the north the forest seems more open. Eastward there seems to be an opening of some kind.
20732: Where the ground is too rocky to allow growth as thick as in most other areas, the trees seem to have been forced to grow further apart. Indeed the air currents above the canopy can reach down to rustle the leaves of the lower branches and inject an uncommon freshness to this place. With the oppressive airlessness gone, this forest seems almost inviting and friendly, albeit still somewhat watchful.
20733: The ground rises sharply from west to east, and is not easily negotiated. As well as the uneven rocks, roots and low scrubby plants between the trees make going particularly tough. Whether climbing up or down the slope, or attempting to traverse it north or southwards, travellers face almost equal challenges. The forest seems to open into a small glade west of here.
20734: At the Top of a Steep Slope

To the west a treacherous and rocky slope falls sharply away. The trees, densely packed seemingly everywhere, do not thin out even on so steep a gradient. In all directions, shabby old oaks and horse chestnuts dominate, covered in blankets of lichen and moss. A deep littering of dried leaves and twigs covers everything as if they have not been disturbed for hundreds of years.
20735: Unexpectedly, the ground drops gradually away into a round depression about two-score yards from side to side. The dense line of trees around the edge stops quite suddenly on the lip of the dingle and green grass takes over. The bowl itself is devoid of all larger growth and there are no paths or tracks of any sort, though the grass is long and rampant. If this place was used for some purpose in the past it looks to have been abandoned many years ago.
20736: A clear pool of water has formed amongst some nearby tree roots.

The ground slopes gently from north and west to south and east. It is not particularly steep, but among the thickly grouped trunks of oak and beech is a small rocky outcrop, from which cool clear spring water tinkles. It splashes between some worn and moss-covered rocks before sinking slowly between root and stone out of sight.
20737: Despite being so crowded, the elderly beech trees that cram together on each side seem to fit so neatly together that they hardly jostle each other at all. Indeed, the trees look comfortable together in a way that only the aged-old strangely sentient trees of Fangorn Forest can.
20738: The forest here seems to be almost entirely made of broad-leaved trees. They are packed in so tightly that movement to the east and south seems impossible. Yet there is still enough light coming down from the thick canopy above to provide for dense brambly undergrowth as well. Spongy masses of moss and lichen cling to every ancient surface.
20739: It is scarcely possible to move among the trees, with every step involving a forced struggle past twisting grasping tendrils and branches. Every twig seems to pull, scrape and scratch, hindering movement as effectively as a giant spider's web. Indeed, further progress east and north is entirely impractical from here.
20740: Within the Depths of the Forest
A tall and haughty elm stands here.

Why the trees crowd so thickly in this area is a mystery. Perhaps the soil is particularly good here, or water is plentiful, or perhaps the reason is something beyond mortal comprehension. Yet it is clearly impossible to forge a path further east at this point. The forest seems no less dense north or south either, though to the west the trees thin out considerably.
20741:
A black alder looms threateningly over its surroundings.
A swarm of mosquitoes is here, humming around you.

The forest grows so thickly here that there is scarcely enough room for one trunk to widen and grow between its neighbours. One can only imagine the tangled battle going on with all the roots beneath the ground. The way eastwards and southwards is entirely impassable, with scarcely an easier path north, though mercifully the trees thin out a good deal to the west.
20742: At the Edge of a Deep Cleft

Northwards the pines and firs are pressed so tightly together that no progress can be made, while east of here a deep cleft runs north to south as if a dragon of an earlier age raked the ground asunder. There is no way down, and certainly no way back up. Southwards, though the forest seems darker and more foreboding passage is possible.
20743: There seems to be much more open land to the northwest while travel looks progressively harder southeast of here. The ground becomes rocky and is crossed by deep ridges, hard to climb down into and even tougher still to emerge from. The trees seem to pack ever closer together on any land flat enough to support them.
20744: Along an Open Stretch of Forest

Stretching from west to north, this seems to be a surprisingly open and airy swathe through Fangorn Forest. The trees, mainly fir and pine, are spread wide as if this is an avenue sometimes travelled upon. There is no actual path discernible however, so care must still be taken to not stumble on twisted roots or half-buried stones.
20745: A tall shrub with strong-smelling foliage is growing here.

The pine trees thin out rather suddenly, surrounding an almost perfectly round area of soft grass. They seem to be keeping their distance almost reverentially as if in respect and awe of the home of a great elder. An easily passable area cuts south from this clearing, seeming almost like an intentional path.
20746: It is a reflection of the unpredictable and dynamic nature of the land of Fangorn that even the very earth seems somewhat aware. There appears to be a struggle between the oaks and beeches and the coniferous trees, yet a sandy break in the earth has caused the two forces to remain separate. The strip of land is so dry not even the deepest roots of the most ancient broadleaves are able to penetrate it and encroach on the evergreens on the southern side.
20747: A change is taking place here. The broad-leaved oaks and beeches to the north are giving way to the pines and firs of the west and south. If it is a battle between the deciduous trees and the conifers it is much too slow a conflict for the hasty folk to see. Nevertheless, there is a feeling of animosity and tension here, but one that seems to be entirely between the trees themselves.
20748: There is some snow on the ground.

The ground is covered with a deep carpet of moss, quite soft to the touch. The trees that are standing here are dim coloured and their branches are strung with enormous grey-green leaves and stringy mosses upon their boles. There is a faint trickling sound in the westward direction, hinting towards a source of water.
20749: A solid, but stunted, rowan tree has established itself here.

The forest seems thickly and oppressively crowded here, giving the air a half choked and stifling feel. The effect seems to worsen as one travels eastward. An elderly rowan tree stands from the rest slightly, its limbs pointing southwards as if to gesture away from the darkest groves.
20750: At a Dark Knot of Pine Trees

Grey looming pine trees press densely here, keeping out not only all light but all other vegetation as well. They seem to lean inwards maliciously to block and hinder anyone who dares travel here so much so that movement in any direction other than back westward is impossible.
20751: Across what little passage there is through the forest lies a massive and ancient fallen tree. Curiously, the remaining trees seem gathered around it, leaning over as if lamenting the loss of a dear old friend. It is remarkable that none of them were crushed when the old tree fell, if indeed they were in their current positions when it did so.
20752: A swarm of mosquitoes is here, humming around you.

The land slopes gently upwards to form a low hill here, and a reasonable view of the surroundings may be gained from the top of it. Scores upon scores of trees lie on every side, though there does seem to be a clear glade a little to the north. Westwards, the forest appears much darker and more impenetrable.
20753: The ground is rough and uneven here, with a tangle of rocks and roots that hamper the growth of many plants. The earth rises to the west and also to the north where the east-west slope steepens. No terrain seems too tough, however, for the mix of old and shabby oaks and ashes that dominate this part of Fangorn Forest.
20754: The land slopes away in all directions from this point. Although there is no clear view out of the forest from this rise, the air is a little fresher here than in the thick depths of the forest. The vegetation gives way at the very top of the hill to a mossy and lichen-covered outcrop, giving the hilltop a rather bald look.
20755: The forest crowds densely around, preventing fresh air from reaching anything living at ground level. Even with the lack of wind there is often a low howling sound coming through the trees. A tall, old and entirely hollow pine stands here and perhaps the wind is entering the top of its trunk, causing an eerie reverberation down its length, like a huge living pipe organ.
20756: A majestic scots pine grows tall and straight here.

Coniferous trees abound in this area, clustering close together.
