They give the impression of protecting each other as if safety in numbers is a priority, rather than merely growing together because of space constraints. Whatever it is that can cow an entire grove of evergreen trees must be dangerous indeed.
20757: A black alder looms threateningly over its surroundings.

The pines that grow in this part of Fangorn are particularly tall, shaggy and bear the signs of age. Their grey bark, when not obscured by moss and lichen, is gnarled and peeling. Yet the place has a clean and fresh aura to it, enhanced greatly by the cliff face to the west. Its smooth rock face serves to reflect fresh air down into the trees at its base.
20758: A spiky broomrape plant pokes its blooms out of the soil.

The air is noticeably still and oppressive, with oaks and ashes looming close, creating a confining atmosphere. The huge trees block out virtually all sound, light and breeze. The way west is blocked by a huge tangle of thorns. Southwards things darken even further, leading into an ominously black grove.
20759:
A large thorny branched shrub is growing here.
A spiky broomrape plant pokes its blooms out of the soil.

The area is dominated by a dense tangle of hawthorns and blackberry brambles. One specimen in particular is so large, ancient and twisted that it is hard to identify anything other than impenetrable sharp twigs and spines. The way south is completely blocked and it would be a struggle clearing a path eastwards.
20760: The densely packed pines, though tight here, give way considerably to the north where the small hill climbs upwards to rise a little above the rest of the land. To the west and south the ground seems flatter, though with the trees as closely spaced as they are, walking would not be easy in either direction.
20761: Despite the shallowness of the soil and the barrenness of the frequent rocky outcrops, pines and hemlocks manage to grip the earth and flourish as thickly as anywhere else. Walking is tedious though, with both stones and roots aplenty to turn a misplaced ankle.
20762: This area of the forest is one of great contrast. To the west and south the land opens up and widely spaced oaks and beeches dominate the earth. To the north and east, however, lie denser packed pines and firs blocking light and hindering the growth of any shorter vegetation.
20763: A swarm of mosquitoes is here, humming around you.

Majestic oak trees soar over this area. Despite being large and well-spread, their fronds let plenty of light through, allowing for an undergrowth rich in tall grasses. The ground is slightly moist and boggy which no doubt aids the grasses' growth. Insects flit from leaf to frond, filling the air with a quiet humming.
20764: At a Coppice of Beech Trees

A docile air permeates this region of Fangorn Forest, where elegant beech trees rustle and sway on the bank of the river Entwash, as if greeting those who pass. The beech trees all arch high and gracefully over the river, one sending out a great bough that almost reaches the opposite bank.
20765: The larger trees give way to ferns and reeds as the ground slopes gently down towards the Entwash river south of here. The air is light and airy, a welcome relief from the oppressive stuffiness between the trees. Those observant of their surrounds might often feel that they are being watched from all directions.
20766: A tall shrub with strong-smelling foliage is growing here.

The vegetation is dense at all levels, as each plant struggles for supremacy over its neighbour. Pines and beeches combat within the high canopy while bushes of rosehip and brambles smother each other and the ground-covering grasses and ferns below. However, the earth of Fangorn is a match for them all, somehow providing sustenance to each and every one.
20767: At the Edge of a Black Grove

This is not a pleasant part of Fangorn Forest. It is altogether silent and ominous. North of here a vicious tangle of thorns and briars bars the way as thoroughly as any artificial wall, though south and east of here, passage may be made through the dense and tangled undergrowth to lighter parts of the forest. To the east lies a frighteningly dark grove.
20768: A black alder looms threateningly over its surroundings.

The trees mysteriously shuffle to block the way out for any intruders entering this most evil and perilous place, leaving a narrow escape northwards only. No outside light penetrates this grove at all, and an intense feeling of malice and hatred to all the outside world permeates everything.
20769: At a Dense Wall of Greenery
A swarm of mosquitoes is here, humming around you.

The evergreen-rich forest continues in all directions apart from west where a large dense tangle of branches bars the way completely. It is impossible to see beyond the massive living wall, let alone pass through it. The trees must either be protecting something or blocking something, but whatever the reason, that barrier is most effective.
20770: A Lighter Passage through the Trees
A colourful butterfly is fluttering around here.

North and west of this area, dense vegetation makes travel very cumbersome. Yet the passage south of here, through this swathe of forest and on eastwards is a great deal easier. There is no set path to follow but the way is much clearer than normal for this part of Fangorn, as it someone or something passes through from time to time.
20771: The trees suddenly give way to the west and south, where steep cliff faces plummet thirty feet or more into the turbulent waters below. One could certainly leap from here into the Entwash, although avoiding smashing onto rocks within the fast-flowing river could prove difficult. The trees gather thickly to the north and east as the land slopes away from the cliffs.
20772: A tall and haughty elm stands here.

Passage through the forest suddenly constricts to form a narrow corridor, where the land slopes sharply downwards west to east, bordered by the Entwash to the south and an impenetrable wall of branches to the north. What lies beyond that wall is impossible to see from here. The boughs are so tightly interwoven together that the traveller is forced either uphill to the west or downhill to the east, unless a dangerous jump into the river is more appealing.
20773: A colourful butterfly is fluttering around here.

The trees seem to part slightly in this region, creating a clearer stretch of land running from south to east of here. This not only allows for much easier travelling in those directions, but the stuffiness and claustrophobia under which so much of the forest lies, is almost totally absent.
20774: The trees grow unevenly, thick to the south and east, yet widely spaced and invitingly clear north and west. But in this area they are particularly thinly spread, creating an elongated glade inhabited by grasses and ferns only. The air is clear and fresh right to ground level, unusual indeed for Fangorn.
20775: Lush Undergrowth under a Mixed Canopy
A tiny spider is here, eating a tiny bug.

The plant life in Fangorn Forest is astounding in its richness and variety. Despite the omnipresent stuffiness and age, with tendrils of moss and beards of lichen hanging from every aged tree limb, there is a tangible vigour to the place. Indeed, the undergrowth is thick and active, every plant striving for more light than its neighbour. Even the trees have their own slow battle, broadleaved oaks, ashes and beeches pushing against the needles of the firs, pines and spruces.
20776: The air is fresh and clear, despite the dense forest all around. The ground slopes gently downhill from north to south, towards the Entwash. Indeed, a slight sound of gurgling water can be heard. To the east things look decidedly darker and more foreboding.
20777: With the Entwash curving around so close by, the earth here is spongy and soft. Yet the banks are still able to support a wild grove of larches, twisting threateningly across the river, and blocking any passage to the water from this area. Northwards there is some open space, a pleasant relief from this malignant atmosphere.
20778: Although no permanent path through Fangorn Forest can be found, there seems to be a remarkably clear way through the trees in this area. It leads from the bank of the Entwash on a heading north-eastwards into the forest. Certainly the way north of here would be much easier going than any other direction. It is as if the forest itself wants to guide travel that way.
20779: A brown fox is here, looking for some rabbits to chew up.

This is a very small, cramped burrow. The inside of the walls are covered with blood and small bones litter the ground around the entrance. A mat of grass and fur lies in a corner. A shallow indentation has been dug into the back wall.
20780:
A wolf cub happily plays here.
A wolf cub happily plays here.
The mother wolf stands here, protecting her young cubs.
A finch flies low above the ground.

This rather large cave has been carved into the soft dirt. Fur and feathers cover a section of the ground, providing a nice place for the cave's inhabitants to rest. Bones and bits of flesh are strewn around the ground. Towards the back of the den small tunnels run deeper into the ground.
20781: On Top of a Large Boulder

The top of the boulder is largely flat. It is covered in moss and ferns that have begun to grow in the small cracks and crevices scattered atop the boulder. All that can be seen past the edge of the boulder is the trunks of the massive pine trees that grow in this area.
20783:
A large bonfire is burning here.
A short Urughash is here, watching the area.
A short Urughash is here, watching the area.
A short Urughash is here, watching the area.
A tall, dirty Urughash commands your attention.
Elemmire the Elf, wielding a double edged eket, is standing here trying to concentrate.

In the centre of the watchtower's thick support beams lies a large, smoking fire. An ornate chair sits close to the fire, surrounded in a pool of blood. The bones of many creatures lie on the floor, covered in piles of soot and other debris. Directly in front of the foremost tower support is the entrance to what looks like a cave. A rickety ladder runs up to the top of the tower.
20784: An orkish soldier of the Urughash is here.

The top of the tower is a cramped lookout. The structure is enclosed with loosely nailed slabs of wood. A railing surrounds the edge, preventing anyone from falling off. The only furnishing is a chair sitting in the northwestern corner. A creaky wooden ladder leads back down into the camp.
20785:
A rusty pickaxe with a broken handle lies discarded here.
A weapons rack stands against the wall.
In the rack are two picks.
A noticeable crack runs down one of the walls.

This shallow cave was delved using only the hands of the miners. Long, deep scratches run the length of each wall, a testament to the methods of the orcs. Shelves have been attached to the walls to hold any necessary tools. Broken tools litter the floor, along with the bones of uncooperative miners. An old, wooden door is seated to the north, marking the entrance to the mines.
20786:
A short Urughash is here, watching the area.
A short Urughash is here, watching the area.

The black stones that line the cave have claw marks riddling their sides. The cave reaches upwards in a ragged arc and then sweeps downward to the north in a more constricted area. A deep layer of muck lies on the ground and is pebbled with broken bones and tools. A line of metal mine cart rails has been lain here and they move towards the north and south where a wooden door has been installed to keep things in, not out. Crude wooden torches line the walls.
20787:
A soot-covered orc, wielding a pick, is here, fighting Elemmire.
Elemmire the Elf, wielding a double edged eket, is here, fighting a soot-covered orc.

The tunnel has dimmed considerably, a very little amount of light from the torches arrives from the northern and southern parts of the mines, but is enough to cast a few shadows across the matted floor. Claw marks riddle the darkened rock that plates the walls in jagged formations. A cold draft of air flows in from the south and moves northwards along the iron rails and broken tools.
20788:
A soot-covered orc, wielding a pick, is here, fighting Elemmire.
A soot-covered Urughash is here, mining away at the rock.
Elemmire the Elf, wielding a double edged eket, is here, fighting a soot-covered orc.

Once again the torches have been driven into the sides of the tunnel, their light sending dancing shadows across the tunnel. Among the debris that covers the ground one can make out several small fragments of iron ore. A pair of rusted metal rails move from the south to the north, following the cold draft of air that is in the orkish mine of the Urughash.
20789: A soot-covered Urughash is here, mining away at the rock.

The tunnel walls of black rock gleam in the light that flickers from the bonfire in the north. From the north lead a pair of rusted rails that move along southward in the trampled ground. Strange shadows jeer about as the lights from torches in the south reach this section of the tunnel. Among the debris of broken tools and bones a cold draft of air can be felt.
20790:
A large bonfire is burning here.
An old, sturdy mine cart stands here on the end of a pair of iron rails.
A soot-covered orc, wielding a pick, is here, fighting Elemmire.
A soot-covered Urughash is here, mining away at the rock.
Elemmire the Elf, wielding a double edged eket, is here, fighting a soot-covered orc.

The tunnel here has been enlarged greatly, the cave walls heavily marked with scratches and many stone slabs serving as seats in the centre where a campfire blazes. The cavern floor has been pressed down from all the tramping of many feet and it is heavily littered with disarrayed piles of broken cups and other rubbish. The area appears to have been mined out leaving nothing left. A collection of tree trunks and branches provide ample fuel for the fire.
20791:
A soot-covered orc, wielding a pick, is here, fighting Elemmire.
Elemmire the Elf, wielding a double edged eket, is here, fighting a soot-covered orc.

The light glows brightly to the south where tongues of a bonfire can be seen, sending shadows down the tunnels in sombre waves. Dark rock has been picked, chiselled, and broken from the solid rock walls, making progress deeper into the mines for the orcs. A metal line of rusted rails make their way from the north to the south among the many broken tools and rocks that litter the ground.
20792:
A soot-covered orc, wielding a pick, is here, fighting Elemmire.
A soot-covered Urughash is here, mining away at the rock.
Elemmire the Elf, wielding a double edged eket, is here, fighting a soot-covered orc.

At this section of the mine a multitude of torches have been set up, their glow casting eerie shadows upon the rocks that scatter upon the wet roughened walls. A deep hole has been cut into the western side of the mine where the work has doubled. The gleam of iron ore explains the extra mining that has taken place. An old set of rusted rails has been laid here, running from the north to the south, among the patted down earth and rubble.
20793:
A soot-covered Urughash is here, mining away at the rock.
A malicious Urughash is here, keeping the miners in line.
A short Urughash is here, watching the area.
A short Urughash is here, watching the area.

Following the rusted set of mine cart rails, the sides of the roughened tunnel slowly start to narrow at the middle. Shadows appear an interesting game as the flickering torchlight reaches this section of the tunnel from afar. Dark veins of ore spread along the sides of the wall towards the north following the cold draft that can be felt in the dusty air of the orkish tunnels.
20794:
A half-decayed corpse of a goblin lies rotting on the ground.
Elemmire the Elf, wielding a double edged eket, is standing here.

The orkish tunnel has entirely collapsed here. Large cracks run down the sides of the tunnel where it still holds, hinting towards further danger if a lot of movement were to occur. A large pile of rubble and dirt lies at the far east side of the tunnel, their shadows flickering in the dim torchlight. The intact portion of the tunnel leads onwards to the west, where more torchlight can be seen.
20795: The cave expands until it reaches a small underground lake. On its shores lie small black pebbles and a thick layer of muck. Most of the cave floor consists of this dirt, but not nearly as wet. To the west the cave seems to have collapsed and the only other passage is to the north, where all the air within the cave seems to be drifting towards. The constant dripping of water into the lake can be heard.
20796: Within the cavern lie dark slabs of solid black rock. The ceiling is mostly open until the cave jaggedly progresses deeper into the earth among the slabs that have already fallen from above. On the east side, near the exit, lies a natural ladder of steps formed from the black rock that leads up into the mountains. A draft of cold air rushes from the inside of the cave.
20800: Ancient white and black spruces grow here at the foot of the mountain, hidden below a large cliff. Their tops flat and spreading, their foliage blue, and nipt with cold, as if centuries ago they had ceased growing upward against the bleak sky. Their smooth bark is peeling off in small patches and countless lichen hang in festoons from their lower branches, as testimonies of their great age. While south the forest seems quite airless, east and west of here, spruce trees are to be found.
20801: The forest seems thinner, when compared to the forest east of here, showing that it is coming to an end. Long tree-clad slopes rise from the lip of the dingle. Beyond them, above the fir trees of the furthest ridge rises the peak of a high mountain, sharp and white. On its sides, numerous crags prevent passage. Only firs and mountain goats can be seen there. However, a path of yellow green mountain grass seems to be outlined, up north among the firs, while east of here, ancient white and black spruce trees can be found.
20802: As the earthy soil becomes more sparse, trees get scattered and firs replace the less sturdy spruces. High up, sheer crags of rough limestone rocks form the only passage along a tortuous curve. In many spots, the path only leads to a dead end. A particular bluff leads to a place where a lonely cloud-flower grows. Its strong star-like cluster of woolly silvery-gray leaves holds out firmly against the mountain wind. Travelling eastwards from here, leads to a dusty trail bordered north by wind carved stone pillars, while the way north leads up to a fir plateau. Below to the south, the forest is quite thin, while clinging on to the slopes of the mountain.
20803: A narrow and shadowy breach between two wind-carved stone pillars seems to be the only passage upwards. In front of it, a dusty pass runs straight, from east to west, following the edge of a sheer rocky brink south, and surrounded north by the cliff walls. From this overhang the higher-altitude evergreen forest seems welcoming and hearty as the trees are more sparse than in the deeper woods. Looking more carefully, one might remark on the absence of any visible wildlife among the trees.
20804: A succession of tall stone slab steps makes a wretched path, probably used only by nimble mountain goats or long legged giants. As the path reaches a plateau, the ground lowers into a grassy theatre bordered by tiers of bulky rock seats. In the middle of the place grows what should be the tallest fir of this land. Its dark green fans, full of purple cones, extend almost to the border of the grass, as if it were trying to protect the tiny young fir-trees below. While the way southwards leads down a silverstar path, the way east takes one to a gusty plateau, covered with limestone boulders.
20805: A large marmot is here, scurrying in between the rocks.

The walk to the ridge is fairly steep in places and it may be quite a difficult hike among the pebbles dislodged from the mountain slope. However, above the last ledge of rocks, the ground flattens a bit, and the footing changes to green meadows carpeted with a dazzling variety of wild-flowers. Alpine poppy, sea pink, and saxifrages add their bright red and purple colours to the shades of green and grey of the forested mountains. Heading south leads to an elevated plateau of firs, while going eastwards brings one to a cliff brink.
20806:
A mountain ibex is jumping from rock to rock.
A mountain ibex is jumping from rock to rock.

The foot of the western summit ends here abruptly. North and east a sheer brink leads to an upsetting precipice of black shining rock, some hundred feet above the world of sharp boulder heaps beneath. This is a great lookout point to a vista of rolling, wooded mountains and valleys. Some of the higher elevations appear to be permanently covered in snow, almost elsewhere, treetops march down the slopes towards the plains, as far as the eye can see.
20807: A huge white limestone cliff beetles over the valley, forbidding any passage to the south and west. Along the base of the cliff, overhanging a scree leading down and north, a bulge provides shelter from the frequent rock slides and the cold howling and shrieking wind. Under the bulge, a small dusty trail runs leading to a wide grassy ledge jutting from the cliff face east of here.
20808: This dangerous scree seems to be the only passage between this side of the glacial valley and the mountains above. The difficulty of the walk across the sharp edged and wobbly stones is increased by the frequent avalanches of stones from the nearby summits. Loose stones roll down, as if thrown by raging giants, in a deafening din. Their frantic fall lasts until they clash against a bigger rock or disappear into the valley below.
20809: This lateral moraine ridge marks the edge of a past glacier. Rock materials from the valley walls were broken up by frost shattering and carried here by the glacier as it followed its curve east along the valley. The resulting heap of unconsolidated granite and limestone rocks makes travel difficult. From time to time, loose rocks from the scree above roll crashing down.
20810: The glacier that once stretched along this trough is still visible on the slope of the nearby summit. North of here, where the ice tongue starts, the last seracs block the way further up along the valley. However, it appears possible to climb a bit further northwards, walking cautiously on the ice, or south, on a pile of moraine dragged there by the glacier. East, the glacial valley follows its way down towards the Fangorn Forest.
20811: The glacier ends here, enclosed between two abrupt mountain walls. The ice tongue that covers the ground is not very thick, but quite slippery. The danger however, comes from the impressive pinnacles of bluish ice hanging from above. These seracs formed at the end of the icefall, where the glacier's surface suddenly drops down, torn by many sets of crevices, block any passage further north.
20812: The snow from the mountain dome to the north, extends down to here, covering patches of dried mountain grass. A few yellow tufts emerge here and there on the slope, shaken by ascending winds. In the opposite direction, a glacial valley can be seen down below. It is as if it is a field of bitter battle, between the retreating ice tongue of the glacier and the climbing pines of Fangorn, slowed down only by the harshness of the rocky soil.
20813:
A small leech is here, floating in the water.
A small leech is here, floating in the water.

Only a few stunted spiky green pine trees grow here on the earthy lines. Everywhere else, the valley is cluttered with grey and brown rock fragments. From the moraine barrier to the north, a trickle of water slips gently into a small basin, where a few leeches wave harmlessly. The water then disappears back under the rocks. While north of here, the glacial valley, following the eastern lateral moraine ridge, heads towards the heart of the mountain, to the south, some thin pinewoods extends on the less rocky soil.
20814: South of here, the pines seem to have been stopped by the impassable barrier of the last recessional moraine, which crosses right through the valley. This mound of material, however, is only an obstacle for the trees as the walk is made easier by the large flattened granite slabs. From the top of the mound, most of the valley is visible, from the pine hollow to the slopes of the sharp horn to where the glacier has retreated. Heading south leads to a cluttered part of the valley, while west brings one through a large trough. East, and upwards, a goat track runs up across grass covered slopes and passes.
20815: A succession of grassy hollows, full of young pines, descends into larger woods to the east towards the heart of Fangorn. North, as the valley rises, enclosed between the mountains faces, pines disappear quickly. And the moss- covered rocks are replaced by cracked granite slabs and huge marble boulders, leftovers from a now withdrawn glacier. West and south, cliffs of grey rocks, rising from the depths of the earth, block any passage.
20816: Starting from the base of the western cliff is a ledge, a few feet wide, extending towards the east, bordered north by a sheer precipice and abutting south in a steep scree. The easternmost part of the ledge rises against the green waves of the forest, like the prow of a majestic vessel. From there, the view is outstanding and colourful. Different shades of green, lighter in the mountain pastures, darker and at times deep in the woods, mix with the grey of the rocks that become white where the snow remains. Heading down towards the south takes one to the base of a small scree, on a pile of rocks threatening to fall further down, whereas to the west, the ledge leads to the base of a huge cliff from the nearby summits.
20817: A mountain goat is here, jumping from cliff to cliff.

Large and smaller rocks have slid from the cliffs above into this breach and below into the forest. Only the most skilled climber would be able to climb down from here, and the sharp edges of the fallen rocks lying below at the base of the cliff make it an unpleasant place to fall. The travel eastward could be accomplished by jumping and clinging to one of the tree branches, as some of them are hanging only a few feet away from the cliff wall. The passage south and west is blocked by the rising cliff walls, yet it seems possible to walk up in a steep scree, and reach a few feet wide ledge north of here.
20818: The scenery of green sods and gray rocks suddenly stops as it reaches the brink of a very steep escarpment dominating the valley. From there an immense country of uninterrupted forest stretches away up the Anduin Vale toward the east and north. The trees spread over the least dell, leaving only a few bare bare rock places. Even on the cliff walls, stubborn stunted firs manage to grow on the slightest shelf of earth, firmly thrusting their roots into narrow cracks. Somewhat to the south of here, a gusty plateau stretches out, while to the west it seems possible to follow the cliff brink further.
20819: A large marmot is here, scurrying in between the rocks.

Sloping just slightly, this elevated plateau is covered with piled up round limestone boulders, lying over the edges of treacherous swallow holes. The ground is worn away by the flowing spring water, yet on the thin earth layer, a bright green bed of grass flourishes, sprinkled with deep blue gentian patches. And under the shadow of the rocks, sheltered from the gusty wind, rosettes of leathery plants with fragrant yellow flowers grow. East of here, a lonely tree clings on to the edge of a cliff, which brink seems to run north of here. Heading west leads to an elevated fir plateau, whereas below, a breach passage spreads towards the south.
20820: Following the northern slope, an occasional warm ascending wind gently blows through the fine thorns of the trees. The larch laces flutter softly, caressing the spruces, motionless like concerned elders. These lush ornaments and the quiet atmosphere greatly differs from the soberness of the forest's old colonnades of deciduous trees rising east from here, and leading deep into the heart of Fangorn. In every other direction, various kinds of evergreens fill the landscape, larches in the harsh northern terrain, spruces in the west and firs in the dark south.
20821: Upright in their strength, with their dainty boughs standing black on the white sky, the beeches of this forest seem to hold firm against the oak colonnades, with shaggy foliage coming from the depths of the forest. Motionless, the trees seem to take part in a solemn and endless palaver. The damp, leaf-covered ground muffles even the lowest sound, as if the trees did not want to be disturbed during their private conversation. Except for the warm grove of spruces and larches to the west, the surroundings are mainly populated with deciduous trees, beeches lie to the north, oaks stand east, and south horse chestnuts border a small glade.
20822: A mass of low-spreading shrub quivers on the ground.

The oaks here are large, stately trees with thick trunks and wide irregular canopies with glossy dark leaves. Their brownish-grey bark is highly striated and devoid of any lichen, moss or parasites. Despite their odd awry aspect, the trees do not have an unfriendly look, however, they seem to possess an ageless wisdom, weird and awry, but ageless. From here, to the north, a mix of beeches and oaks can be spotted, and the forest remains a mix of various deciduous tree species in the other directions, as well.
20823: This part of the forest is a mix of deciduous species from the surroundings. Beeches, birches, hornbeams and ashes grow scattered among chestnuts and oaks of diverse kinds. Even between the same species, it seems impossible to find two identical fellow trees or two identical leaves on the same tree. Even the unlikely regular visitor of this place, after eons spent here, would still find a new unexpected or unknown tree species. This strangely mixed forest extends a bit more east from here, while in the other directions oaks seems to be the most common kind of tree.
20824: When lit, this area of the forest reveals all sorts of trees from the surroundings. Ashes, beeches, hornbeams and many more, are all easily found in this place. The mixed forest in this area continues from a bit west of here. To the east, ash trees dominate the forest, while to the north, the forest somehow appears sadder than in other places. As a consequence of the variety of trees growing here, all kinds of different leaves and branches of different feel and make lie scattered, covering the ground here. The ground appears to suddenly drop a little, into some kind of round depression south of here, forming a small dingle.
20825: Medium-sized ash trees dominate this part of the forest, their bark firm and brown-coloured with interlacing ridges, and their wood hard and strong. Even though several sorts of ash trees can be found here, green ash trees appear to be the dominant sort. Northwards from here, a rocky headland forms, with hornbeams and taller ash trees than can be found here, while to the west, the forest is a mixture of many different kinds of trees. To the east, ash trees continue to be the prevailing sort of tree.
20826: The ash trees in this area mostly consist of the green and black sorts. The green seeming to come in from the west, and the black from the east, gradually fading into each other. When compared to the west, the bark of the trees appears softer than before, easily reduced to some sort of powder if rubbed hard. But even though the wood of these trees appears soft, it is quite durable and sturdy. Both to the east and west of here, ash trees dominate the forest. Northwards, however, a low-growing kind of plant with glossy leaves form a kind of carpet on top of some rocky outcrop, while some crowded beeches lie to the south of here.
20827: A rooting heap of stems is here, smothering over the smaller plants.

The ash trees dominate the forest, both here, and to the north and west. The footing is soft, padded with leaves and all other sorts of plant and tree debris that have fallen over time. Passage is free in all directions but to the east. In this direction, an extremely dense thicket renders any passage impossible. It is also a bit more moist in this area than in other parts of the forest, conditions the black type of ash trees prefers.
20828:
A colony of red ants is here. The ants seem to ignore you.
A small termite is running around making strange sounds.

Despite the small size of the thicket, it is dense enough to block out almost all natural light. What little light makes it through is scattered by the leaves above. No plant life survives these conditions. A few ants scurrying about are all that can be recognised from normal forest wildlife. Heavy masses of vines grow between the trees, preventing any travel south, but beyond them the forest stretches on, deeper and more dense than here.
20829: A murmuring sound fills the air. No actual words can be discerned from the soft muttering, but the quality of the noise resembles that of a strange language. What little of the forest is visible through the twisted and disfigured limbs of the trees growing here indicates that the surrounding area is just as dark. The ground slopes away to the north seemingly leading into a small valley. To the east and west the forest continues unbroken.
20830: The quiet enshrouding of the forest is broken by a high-pitched chattering, seemingly emanating from the canopy above. While no birds can be seen, the source of the sound remains somewhat of a mystery. To the north the trees grow extremely close together, and a small gap between two of the more prominent trees appears to lead into a dark tunnel. Further south the trees are just as dense, an unbroken barrier to further travel.
20831: There is a distinct feeling that something is not right here, as if a great evil reshaped this part of the forest and it is still suffering from it. It is very dim and stuffy. Patches of darkness appear to twist and distort themselves when looked at and the creaking sound of ancient trees blowing in the wind only adds to the sense of unease.
20832: Any hope of venturing further south has to be abandoned in the face of the foreboding wall of towering fir trees. Underneath the overhanging canopy everything is damp and the unmistakable smell of rotting plant-matter lingers. Some light enters the forest from the north, it would appear that the trees are less dense there.
20833: Approaching a Wall of Fir Trees

The green carpet of grass advancing into this area from the north is halted by a line of fir trees. The grey hue of the trunks stands in stark contrast to the deep green foliage spreading out from each tree, blocking out the sky. The occasional fallen tree shows up deathly white against the background of brown pine needles and cones. At the southernmost edge of the firs, an unnaturally large number of dead trees lie in various stages of decay. Some great evil must have changed this area of the forest long ago.
20834: The trees here appear to shift slightly, perhaps it is just a trick of the light. A closer look reveals that the trees are covered with a heavy blanket of lichen giving them an almost hairy appearance. The only light to enter this place comes from the north where a small clearing barely can be discerned between the boughs. The southern boundary has become overpopulated, it would be difficult to make much headway through the dense branches. The other directions will surely prove to be easier routes.
20835: The ground here slopes away to the west. To the east a steep climb leads to the top of a hill, however there is no respite from the thick forest surrounding as the canopy continues unbroken. Gnarled and twisted trees are clustered together on the south face of the slope creating an impenetrable barrier.
20836: Thick branches hanging low make movement arduous and painful. The long vines and gnarled limbs protruding from the trees become hurtful obstacles on the way through the forest. In every direction, there is more of the same gloomy forest. To the south, piles of rocks between the trees make travel that way impossible.
20837: Even at high noon on a cloudless day, it is doubtful whether the sun's warmth could be felt here. On the ground, piles of leaves undergo the slow process of decomposing back into the soil from which they grew. The only sound here comes from the few insects that have made the damp leaves their home. To the east the unbroken canopy continues.
20838: The trees continue on immeasurably in all directions. The events of the outside world seem completely forgotten beneath the awning of branches and sheets of foliage, that plunge the enclosed land into darkness. The trees are nonchalant and uncaring and the only sounds are a faint rustling of leaves in the canopy above, and the skittering of some forest insects taking refuge amongst piles of debris and leaf litter.
20839: Some roots lie here waiting to ensnare weary travellers.

A maze-work of large buttress roots shoot out from the base of the massive trees. It is nigh on impossible to avoid these roots in the gloomy darkness that resides beneath the dense canopy. The branches and tree trunks are clothed with countless years of lichen that thrives in the moist musty air. Silence dominates the forest. Even a strong gale would bring nothing more then a muffled rustle of leaves. Away to the north the ground slopes gradually downwards and the forest grows thick and impenetrable. In all other directions the trees continue, seemingly without end.
20840: Pervasive darkness dwells like a ruler beneath the enclosed canopy. Large buttress roots growing through the littered forest floor make travel very slow and cumbersome. All seems quiet and still, and even the strongest breeze moves between the leaves in apparent silence. The air holds a musty odour and is cool and clammy to the skin. The forest continues to the south, west and east. To the north the ground slopes gently downwards, but travel that direction is suddenly cut off by a mass of fallen and tangled trees.
20841: Some roots lie here waiting to ensnare weary travellers.

It is oppressive and stuffy beneath the dense, overhanging canopy and the air is cool and moist to the skin. The absence of natural light has left the forest floor devoid of undergrowth, granting more space for the impeding buttress roots. Patches of dark tree trunk show through between the covering of grey-green lichen. Sounds are muffled and quiet. The ground slopes slightly downwards to the north.
20842: The oppressive dimness and fusty, dank air create a dismal atmosphere. Dark trees reach out their limbs in an umbrella of foliage, completely shutting out any sight of the sky. Their gnarled bodies are home to a patchwork of frilly lichens and furry mosses. Numerous insects scurry beneath piles of leaves and debris which are scattered across the forest floor. The forest continues in seemingly endless waves of trees as far as the eye can see.
20843: A mass of low-spreading shrub quivers on the ground.

Thick musty air and compact foliage make the forest here dense and smothering. Many branches grow low to the ground, their outermost twigs drawing patterns in the soft earth. These low branches and the many protruding roots make travel a journey of careful and selective climbing, ducking and weaving.
20844: A junebug buzzes slowly through the air.

Moss-covered roots spread out from the base of the trees like creeping green tendrils rummaging through the brown leaf litter. The textured grey bark is cracked and in many places peeling away, revealing a lighter colour beneath. The trunks have developed deep wrinkles as the branches have grown larger and heavier, and the interlaced canopy allows only sufficient light through to nourish the moss and lichens.
20845: Dark-grey trunks support a proliferation of branches that reach up like fingers grasping for the skies. Clinging to these fingers is a plethora of dark-green leaves that would have appeared glossy in the younger days of the forest, but are now dull and almost lifeless. The forest floor is scattered with dead leaves and numerous moss-covered roots creep amongst the litter.
20846: Woody broad-flanged buttresses support the base of the thick crooked trunks. In turn, the trunks support masses of contorted branches that carry large, lifeless leaves. These leaves were once powerful factories, catching the light in the sun-dappled lower parts of the forest and converting it into vital energy and nutrients. Now, the once-reaching branches stretch no more and the leaves do nothing more than block the light and trap musty air.
20847: Eerie creaks and groans echo between the trees as the interlocking branches move with the slightest breeze. A number of poplar trees grow interspersed and the rustling of their fine branches adds to the cacophony. Surrounding the poplar trees are aged and misshapen trees of many kinds that managed to take root during the vast history of the wood. The dense soil has been leached of its nutrition throughout the long years, leaving nothing to promote new growth or to sufficiently feed the trees.
20848:
A large extending poplar tree with dark branches grows here.
A nightingale is here, chirping a sweet melody.

Poplar trees have gathered here in a vast but tight clump, preventing other trees from developing. Their compact growth and network of arching branches makes it hard to traverse through the centre of the clump. Each tree guards the cluster by sending out its strong roots far into the surrounding forest. The bases of the old trunks are deeply furrowed into firm dark ridges and each lobular leaf clings to its limb so firmly that it remains attached even through the dormancy of winter.
20849: Long-established trees grow here, embedded into the littered earth. Their branches are slender and weak, bowing under the weight of the voluminous foliage grown over their countless years. The trunks also are relatively thin and many of the frail forms have crumpled beneath the weight. During winter, the fine branches on most of the deciduous trees seem to transform into the strands of a tangled spider's web. Mist condenses on these delicate limbs and glistens in the light of day.
20850: Delicate branches droop low to the ground, no longer able to support their vast twisted length and cumbersome weight. The trunks also are bent beneath the burden of their upper frames, and the wrinkled coating of bark has begun to peel, leaving the rich brown soil littered with the discarded skin. The air beneath the bowing limbs is musty and pungent with a woody odour. From time to time, a gentle rustling can be heard through the canopy as the wind blows and an occasional creak or snap fractures the stillness.
20851:
Some thick writhing vines whip all around you.
A mass of wriggling vines drops on you from the trees.

Gnarled trunks and twisting branches are enmeshed in a complexity of tangles. Winding throughout these tangled masses are thick spiralling vines, their tendrils reaching out into the cavities searching for the next limb to cling to. Olive-green lichens tumble down in flowing web-like cascades from many of the overhead branches. The cluttered foliage makes the forest dim and the air stuffy.
20852: An imposing beech tree sways gently in the wind.

The trees here produce a living picture of health and vibrance. Many young red-tipped shoots sprout from the ends of the sturdy branches, jostling upwards to find their place in the sunlit canopy. The straight solid tree trunks are coated with crinkly brown-grey bark that has developed deep cracks as the trunks expanded over time. A strong woody aroma leeches out from the foliage and permeates the air.
20853: A lofty elevated canopy of spreading foliage breaks forth in an expansive jade and emerald mantle. Beneath this canopy, a sanctuary is formed by enormous pillared trunks of burnished brown and grey. The forest floor is coated with a carpet of golden leaves that look so flawless and vivid that not one appears to have begun decaying. The crystal clear air is fresh and wholesome, and borne upon the slightest breeze is a light fragrance of hemlock and beech.
20854:
A clear pool of water has formed amongst some nearby tree roots.
A tall figure, like that of a fine-looking beech tree, is slumped sadly here.

Untouched by shadow or decay, this virgin forest displays a tranquillity and beauty rarely experienced in the lands of Middle-earth. Tall trees of many varieties reflect the purity of the air that they breathe and the waters that they drink. Each emerald leaf is perfectly formed, and the arrangement of branches is as intricately woven as a fine tapestry. The forest floor is layered with a carpet of golden leaves.
20855: A polluting shadow slowly creeps from north to south across this region of the forest. One by one, the trees gradually succumb to this threat. In the north they droop sadly and defeated, their colour and vibrance lost. However, the trees to the south have so far withstood the menace. Their robust trunks stand bold and proud and the branches defiantly display their glorious foliage.
20856: A spreading illness is destroying these once robust and noble trees. No young growth is visible amongst the ailing forms and the thick, old bark has been severely tarnished. Many naked branches droop towards the ground, their vibrant foliage now piled like mounds of drab refuse. Once laden with a fresh woody aroma, the air is now stuffy and tainted with decay.
20857: A tall and haughty elm stands here.

Storeyed elms and ancient oak trees have begun to be affected by a spreading malignancy. Their branches sag slightly and the vibrance is gradually fading from the foliage. The occasional sapling that manages to grow withers and dies without ever glimpsing the sun. This steady, unending demise shows no favour as everything is slowly polluted by its spread.
20858: The thick robust trunks of various trees show that this is an old, yet healthy part of the wood. Numerous small plants try to squeeze a place for themselves amongst the developed trees. Their vigorous growth and bright foliage are in distinct contrast to the brownish-grey leaf litter on the forest floor.
20859: Having been expelled from the gathering of birch trees to the north, the oak and fir trees take refuge here in a scattered assembly. Their stately forms display a forgotten glory and the branches that they once held up high and dignified have now begun to droop low. Cracked, woody wrinkles have taken the place of their smooth, leathery bark and on the ground drifts of leaves prevent new growth. The air holds such a sweet, almost alpine aroma, that even the stagnancy here cannot subdue it.
20860: Dank misty air swirls with fresh air drawn from the pure forests to the south and west. Fine finger-like branches wave eerily in the eddying air and lichens growing from the branches sway as though dancing to a mournful lay. Mist, that condenses on the trees, drips down with little splashes to form numerous murky puddles that dot the ground. To the east, the forest becomes lighter and the presence of oak and fir trees increases.
20861: An Ailing Grove in the Forest

A worm is here slithering around.
A worm is here slithering around.

Long ago this ancient grove must have had exquisite leaves and strong, powerful limbs. Now, those leaves have become discoloured and fragile. Once sturdy branches are now buckled and broken under the pressure of their own weight, caused by a strong sapping sickness. Slowly the varied colours of the forest have faded into a pale and dreary grey. Everywhere the touch of decay is present.
20862: The trees growing here are diminishing rapidly, rotting from the inside and then falling in upon themselves. They are slowly losing a noble battle against the rampant sickness that has spread through the forest. Dreary stumps poke up out of swirling mists, like the unmarked graves of forgotten soldiers. Twisted roots, coupled with rotting stumps and fallen trees, make it hard to find a good footing upon which to walk.
20863: The oak, ash, and fir that live in this part of the forest are very near death. The bark of some of the trees seems to be hanging off in long shreds, whilst their leaves and needles have lost their colour altogether. A thick mist blankets the ground here, and makes it difficult to pick a path among the twisted roots that snake along the forest floor. A sickly smell wafts through the air, making it hard to breathe.
20864: The knotted roots of the oak trees here resemble great piles of blackened bones, strewn around the forest floor. The trees appear to be suffering and poisoned by some dreadful unknown blight. Limbs hang limp from the occasional sickened fir, all of which have lost the majority of their needles. In all directions, the sickness of the forest extends without pity, with no sign of what could be responsible for such devastation.
20865:
The corpse of a huge millipede is lying here.
A huge millipede is writhing around here.
A tall and haughty elm stands here.

The forest floor seems bare and lifeless, its musty soil broken only infrequently by lonely twisted questing roots or the occasional dell of decaying leaf litter. The cloying scent of musty decay is particularly pungent here. Ancient ash and oak stand tall and still here, their limbs blackened and leafless, bereft of any signs of continued life.
20866: A tall and haughty elm stands here.

The thick, black muddy soil is sodden and barren. Every footfall accompanied by sucking squelches that raise a pungent rotten stench. This odour combines with the forest's already musty environment to make breathing decidedly unpleasant and difficult. Decayed, rotting tree stumps and twisted black-hearted, blight-ridden giants surround. For ages unknown they have been hidden from the sun by a darkness that seems to never lift from this dip in the greater forest.
20867: There is a heavy darkness here in this dell, deep within the forest's clutches, that has been hidden from the light of the sun for ages unknown. Twisted branches and tree trunks are densely intertwined and overhead a dense canopy obscures all light. Underfoot, snarling roots and fallen debris lie as snares to trip the unwary.
20868: Hawthorn bushes may be found beneath the shaded canopy of this area of oak. Elder also grow beneath the mighty oaks, rising to nearly ten yards at their best, wherever some slight gap in the canopy allows light to reach the forest floor. In particular, the elder and hawthorn have flourished where the forest is cut through by a river, running its way through the western and northern fringes of this land.
20869: The water sparkles as light from above pierces the forest canopy. Perfectly rounded pebbles can be seen distinctly through the deep, clear water. A complex variety of woodland loving flowers have made their homes alongside the grassy riverbanks to either side, whilst overhead you can see the branches of trees that extend out over the river.
20870: A small termite is running around making strange sounds.

Beautiful full-grown trees overlook a sparkling river to the south. A great variety of trees have made this land their home, whilst lush verdant grass tries to make its presence known on the forest floor. Mosses and lichen cover the trunks of the trees and several trees have branches extending over the river.
20871: A black alder looms threateningly over its surroundings.

A chill wind drifts through the forest here and runs straight to the bones. A very thick and heavy mist covers the ground, making it nearly impossible not to trip over whatever may lie there. Very little light makes it through the thick mass of branches and leaves that hang overhead.
20872: With the golden prairies still visible to the north and west, this part of the forest is very inviting. Light still filters in from the north leaving this part of the forest edge well lit. To the south, the forest darkens as the light has to filter through the thick canopy of the forest.
20873:
A fierce boar is here, making grunting noises.
A lone hawk soars high above you.

The lush deep green of the trees to the south showers the golden grass in colourful arrays, giving the area a surreal appearance. The depth of the forest eerily call to the traveller to enter and explore the heart of the forest. However, the stillness of the air and the soundless surroundings would make any adventurer wary to travel in that forest.
20874: The marsh here is covered in all sizes and sorts of reeds as the water pushes its way over the side of the river and into the shallow lowlands. The swift current can be heard to the north as the water makes its trek to the great river in the east. The odd sound of some insects is the only thing that breaks the monotony of the sound of water.
20875: A number of small pools have formed here off from the main flow of the river. This seems like a perfect breeding place for fish and the perfect hunting place for predators. However, the only wildlife that seems to be living here are a few fish that can be seen in the pools. The river flows out of the north and continues to the east. Small marshes seem to have formed in the other directions.
20876: The river here flows from the west to the south, and the current picks up slightly as it hits some very small and tame rapids. The north bank is raised too much to allow anyone to climb up out of the river. To the west, the Misty Mountains glare down from afar.
20877:
A large beautiful rose bush is blooming here.
A grey bird with a bright orange-red belly sits here, singing a melodic tune.
A field lark stands here, focused on finding food.
A restless rabbit bounces around.

This tiny meadow seems completely cut off from the rest of the world. At one time, this meadow appears to have been a sprawling garden. Remnants of flowers that were once well-tended are all around. To the south and west, you can hear a river as it continues on its everlasting journey, although a stand of bushes and trees blocks your way in those directions. The only way out seems to be into the foothills to the north.
20878: The foothills here are barren of everything. Not even grass seems to grow here. It is as though the earth here was scarred long ago and has never fully recovered. A small meadow lies to the south, and beyond that, a river flows south. To the north, a small statue is visible on top of one of the hills, and more hills spring up everywhere else. From the tops of the hills, the Misty Mountains seem to cover the entire western horizon.
20879: A Large Stone on a Hill
A black crow flies low to the ground here, looking for carrion to eat.

On the top of one of the hills, there is a large stone, standing straight up as if guarding something. The foothills continue in all directions, and the sound of running water comes faintly from the south and possibly from the distant east as well. In the distance, the Misty Mountains are vague shapes on the western horizon.
20880: The lands all around seem so inviting, but there is something about these hills that must emanate a less than comfortable aura as none have dared set up a homestead or even travelled very often through this land. Far off to the west the peaks of the Misty Mountains are barely visible.
20881: A few small rocks and stones intersperse the soil here. Some larger boulders are also strewn across the fields, pressing down even the last bit of healthy grass. The surface of dirt is hard-packed and riddled with cracks from the lack of moisture, giving this area a barren and abandoned look. The dusty and rocky plains continue towards all directions, and sometimes, animal life can hardly be noticed.
20882: A colourful butterfly is fluttering around here.

This dirt-trodden area is bare and barren beside a few stunted and sick-looking trees which have managed to take root here. The grass is of yellowish colour with thin blades and only grows in small scattered patches. A few shrubs and spiny plants have also managed to survive despite the poor conditions.
20883: Bare earth and tufts of sick grass share the open space here, giving these fields a burnt look. The ground is grey, dusty, and devoid of plants or foliage, apart from a small amount of crabgrass or a single spiny shrub here or there. A fallen tree lies on the ground, rotten and hollow inside. Its stump has already begun to decay.
20884: The stench of sun-baked dirt spreads over the surrounding plains. Dust covers everything with a thin layer of light brown. Some large bushes grow in the rock-pebbled dirt, their branches supporting only a few leaves. The rest have fallen down, lying under the bushes in a state of decay. A few weeds have taken root, and a few tufts of fresh grass grow on the ground, fighting for survival.
20885:
A brown snake watches you.
A fat rabbit sits here, chewing on some grass.
A small black cricket is here, chirping loudly.
A small black cricket is here, chirping loudly.

A thin layer of dust covers everything here. The grass has a slight brown tinge because of the dirt and dust that covers it. The few bushes that inhabit these fields are thin and spiny, apparently having lost their leaves due to the lack of nutritious soil. A few brownish plants grow in between the grass. To the south, the grass seems to be fading out of the plains, leaving only bare earth underfoot.
20886: The trail that comes from the north narrows at this point. Small bushes and foliage line the walkway, forcing travellers to pass this area in single file. The surrounding fields are full of healthy and verdant grass, swaying in the passing breezes. A few large trees grow at the edge of this path, occasionally offering shadow.
20887: As the ground to the south begins to drop, the trees transform into dark eerie figures. Branches become more tangled, and the canopy closes in. Lichens grow dominant, hanging like beards from the twisted trees. A stale, smothering odour of decay drifts up from the darkness to the south, and the dank air moistens everything, from the clumps of soil to the leaf tips.
20888: A spiky broomrape plant pokes its blooms out of the soil (red aura).

The air has become thinner, but breathing is still laborious. The random growth of branches is knotted and tree trunks lean at strange angles. Finding a path through this seemingly forsaken wood is awkward and difficult. Natural light is scarce and the few rays which may pierce the canopy only serve to highlight the murky gloom.
20889: The trees here are immersed in what seems to be an endless mourning. In silence, they appear to grieve for the fair days of yore, their tears of sap frozen to their gnarled and peeling trunks. Dead leaves cling to the branches, unwilling to be forgotten like those that have piled on the forest floor and are now slowly decaying.
20890: As shafts of light stream through breaks in the canopy, the rays form columns of illumination through the dusty air. The change in ambience is accompanied by a waft of fresh air which brings a vibrant, woody aroma. The trees here are spread out and have less lichen and moss to spoil the rich, brown colouring of their massive trunks.
20891: Twigs stretch out their long, leafy fingers, grappling for warmth and energy from any sunshine that falls through the canopy. The limbs grow tangled, reaching towards the sky in spiralling masses. Other branches have broken off and lay discarded on the ground like antlers torn from a majestic stag. This scene continues far in all directions until the forest fades into a gloomy grey twilight, broken only by a sporadic shard of light.
20892: A very large tree branch has been ripped from a tree.

The trees have been subjected to severe deforestation, in some places entire sections have been torn down. To the north of the area a large log pile sits. The pile itself looks to be abandoned judging by the thick layer of moss covering the wood. Whoever cut the trees has not even bothered to use the timber they produced. From all around, the sound of a faint wailing can be heard, almost as if the trees were mourning.
20893:
A tall birch is here, watching over the landscape.
A huge millipede is writhing around here.

A solid wall of wood surrounds this grove on its northern and western boundaries. Massive oak roots have grown there, knotting and twisting themselves together to form a panel preventing further travel in those directions. A few small gaps in the western wall allow a glimpse of what lies beyond, however, they are small, and it is difficult to make out much detail.
20894: An immense tree rises from amongst its smaller brethren dominating the thicket. Its upper branches reaching through the living awning of leaves that sentence the plants on the ground below to endure a perpetual gloom. To the east thin shafts of light can be seen, the forest is less dense in that direction.
20895:
Massive roots shift uneasily all around you.
Some roots lie here waiting to ensnare weary travellers.
Some roots lie here waiting to ensnare weary travellers.

The sombre, oppressive nature of the forest seems to be concentrated here. The trees growing here are stunted, unable to reach their full height. Around the base of each tree several thick roots have curled themselves, squeezing the boughs as if trying to strangle the life from the oaks. The roots have become so overgrown that they block movement in every direction, only the path to the west remains passable. Despite their difficulties, the oaks have still managed to develop a large system of branches shielding the forest floor from natural light, and almost completely preventing fresh air from reaching this unpleasant place, making the air stuffy and stale.
20896: Everything here seems to be peaceful, even the ants that can be seen scurrying around the base of a nearby oak, moving leaves to their home, seem to do so silently. To the west the forest canopy becomes more open, allowing a small amount of sunlight to reach the ground. A number of species of mushroom have taken advantage of this and now grow over the stump of a long-dead tree. Heading north would take travellers deeper into the woods but a mass of hanging vines and branches make travel there impossible.
20897: The cool grass covering the ground here reaches around the boughs and stumps of the oak trees which grow nearby. A cold, sharp draft can be felt and, listening carefully, a dull murmuring can just about be made out above the noise of the rustling leaves.
20898: The trees here have grown particularly close together causing their branches to become entangled. In certain areas, the forest appears to be completely impenetrable, a wall of solid wood preventing progress. In order to make any headway, travellers would be wise to choose their path with care.
20899: Some ugly blow-flies are buzzing around here.

Under the concealing canopy of the trees towering above, the moisture in the air has been trapped resulting in a damp, boggy area forming between the trees. Ferns have taken advantage of these conditions and seem to flourish. The swampy terrain makes movement difficult.
20900: An imposing beech tree sways gently in the wind.

Lying among the trees, the fallen remains of a long dead rowan dominates the surrounding area. Even after all this time, a large depression is still evident where the tree's roots were pulled free as it fell. On the eastern side of the trunk some stones and twigs have been collected and placed against the boughs lying there.
20901: Tall rowan trees have taken hold here. The ground is littered with decaying leaves and a musty smell of decay hangs in the air. Above, the sky is almost totally obscured by the intricate network of branches stretching between the neighbouring trees.
20902:
An ancient oak is here towering above you.
An ancient oak is here towering above you.

In the midst of this obscure and foggy forest, the trees are of a slate grey, looking like inert stone pillars. Only a few grey leaves remain on their limbs, and the ground, of an ash-like sand, is devoid of any debris. This forest seems petrified, yet still alive and unwelcoming against any legged visitor, and it will not allow any passage further north where nothing grow except dark grey trees. Even the surrounding dark area of the forest seems to be a more preferable place to visit.
20903: Here, the escarpment rim is dominated by hemlock but dotted by groves of maple, birch, white ash, and red oak. Trees grow as far as the cliff edge to the east, where the earthy ground ends abruptly in a mix of hanging moss and roots. Nothing seems to point the brink of the cliff, and it would not be wise to run aimlessly around, even less so close to the precipice. The forest extends south of here following the abrupt end of the mountain, and rises in tiers on its western slopes.
20904: A spiky broomrape plant pokes its blooms out of the soil.

The trees here are old and decrepit, their brown leaves turning to a ghostly grey as they fall. Large boughs can be seen lying on the ground, rotten and formless. The great silence of this deep forest girds the least unusual noise, and only the wind dares to pass with its complaint, like a cry of hunger and lassitude. Last vestige of greenness, ivy clings on the cliff wall to reach the sunlight or maybe to escape from this dreary place. Beside, a large cleft running up along the cliff towards the south, seems to be the surest mean of leaving this place, as everywhere else the forest seems unfriendly, even forbidding any passage north.
20905:
A low shrub with bright green, oblong leaves is growing here.
Scattered in and on the shrub, there are two piles of blueberries.

The ground here is all covered with patches of low shrubs with wiry, angular branches and leathery oval leaves. They rarely exceed a foot in height, but they can hold as many berries as a full-sized bush. It seems impossible not to tread on them, squeezing out of them their dark purple juice. Here and there a few pines spring up, protecting the shrubs from the direct sunlight. But east, as the ground falls rapidly, deciduous trees grow among the leaf-covered rocks. South, the ground lowers, albeit gently, remaining grassy, while east, a bare rock scenery extends from the foot of the mountain peaks.
20906: Dominating this wonderful and unusual world of cracks, a huge boulder forms a natural gate that opens westwards to another valley. Here, the rock is of a bright white hue and the scenery is open on most sides. To the west, beyond the massive porch of greyish rock, the valley is dark and always charged with electricity, as clouds bump and stick to the nearby summits. The mountain renders passage north from here impossible, its side being much too steep and treacherous to climb.
20907: This valley is nestled between high cliffs on all sides, forming a magnificent mountain cirque. The altitude of the mountains around adds a rather dark and unfriendly atmosphere to this place. The only ingress or egress is through a large natural gate, a few dozen feet wide and surmounted with a mighty unreachable boulder. This huge rock, wedged between the cliff walls and covered with a few wispy saplings, will probably fall down eventually, but not for some time.
20908: Judging from the numerous tracks, this pass is used very often by mountain goats, living in the rocky part of the mountain and grazing below where the grass abounds. Northwest of here, an imposing snowy dome seems to serenely dominate the area, while eastward, a seemingly endless view of sharp rocky peaks surrounded by black clouds threaten the valley.
20909:
A mother eagle flies high above looking for prey.
A small, helpless eaglet screams for more food.
A small, helpless eaglet screams for more food.

Rising a few hundred feet above the grassy pass to the west, this place is only made of sharp rocks and small boulders torn off from the mountain walls. The rough gneiss rock offers a sure hold. Walking along the edges between the peaks should be easy, if one does not suffer from vertigo. On both sides, the view is breathtaking, to the east the sheer precipice overhangs a mountain cirque while to the southwest, vast grassy slopes lead quickly down to a glacial valley. The safest passage down seems to be west through a green mountain pass, while the passage south along a sharp ridgeline, might be less wise.
20910: A goat track runs gently across grass covered slopes and passes. Dandelions, hare's foot clover and trefoil seem to be the favoured meals of these goats, as the track winds around many patches. The rather aerial passage below to the west, leading to the glacial valley also seems to be frequently travelled, judging by the amount of goat droppings. There is no doubt that there should be a water source near there. South, the ground flattens and a grassy plateau can be seen extending some in that direction, while north, a grassy slope leads to a green pass.
20911: A mountain goat is here, jumping from cliff to cliff.

This flat extension, richly adorned by herbs, suddenly declines south towards the valley in large steps of levelling granite slabs. The soil is wet and often marshy, and trickles of water slip along the flagstones, making the way down quite hazardous for the hasty. Below, on the firm ground, the forest of Fangorn claims the land and no animal seems to dare venture there. North from here, the green scenery continues with mountain pastures, while east a large cornice makes the only passage through a more rocky landscape.
20912:
Some pine nuts lie scattered upon the ground.
A tall pine tree grows here.

At this altitude and on this rather rocky soil, only mountain pines grow. In the winter these solemn pines bend down with snow and bristle with icicles. While during summer their branches point towards the sun light, revealing their blood-red trunks amidst the bright yellow green of mountain grass and lichen covered rocks. In the valley hollow, where once a clear mountain stream raged south, is now a bed of rocks with loose moss concealing the gaps between them. East of here, some rowan trees blend in among the pines, while the pinewoods continue both south and east. Heading up and north, is a grassy plateau.
20913:
Some pine nuts lie scattered upon the ground.
A low shrub with bright green, oblong leaves is growing here.
Scattered in and on the shrub, there are a handful of blueberries.

Following the bottom of the valley from north to east, a very wet and rocky gutter, hardly a path, leads through a succession of clear scotch and stone pine groves, standing like opencast temples, rippling with light. Lower, the gutter disappears as it reaches flatter grounds, and a dense undergrowth of heather, bilberry, crowberry and higher shrubs, starts to develop under the pines. The passage west is blocked by a huge rising cliff but a wobbly alley runs south, from here along its base.
20914: At the base of the cliff, where trees are scanty, runs a great tumbled slope, down towards the fringe of the forest. There stand the great trees, unwilling to ascend the steep slope, their broad foliage extending as far as the rock face. The result is a large wobbly alley running north-south along the foot of the cliff. North and south, the forest stretches out, while to the west, and almost reachable from here, a rockslide has happened on the cliff wall.
20915: A rooting heap of stems is here, smothering over the smaller plants.

West and south, a high cliff keeps this place cool and moist, hiding the sunlight most of the day. Droplets of water can be seen dripping on thick velvety green patches of moss hanging from the cliff wall. Beech groves, scattered with white birches in the highest places, are gradually replaced by great thick trees from the deep forest further east. This damp area of the forest seems to continue to the east, while north, following the cliff wall, the forest clears a bit as fallen rocks cover the ground.
20916:
A mountain ibex is jumping from rock to rock.
A mountain ibex is jumping from rock to rock.

A lonely tree has grown on the edge of a cliff overhanging most of the forest. Below, from the foot of the cliff, the forest of Fangorn stretches as far as the eye can see. The rustling of the leaves reach up here like a soft whisper and the subtle scents of the various tree species mix with the smell of the humus. The roughness of the foliage spreads over the whole shade of green, making the forest shimmer like a living ocean. The serenity of the forest below strongly contrasts with this austere place. The only way to avoid the dangerous cliffs is west through a gusty limestone plateau.
20917: As the forest climbs along steeper mountain slopes, spruce groves are replaced by larch woods and isolated fir trees in the rockiest places. The steepness of the terrain yields a view of southern Fangorn through the trees. The forest stretches as far as the eye can see, only limited to the north and west by the last range of the Misty Mountains, which ends far away in the distance with the snow-capped peak of the Methedras. The forest of larches and other evergreen trees stretches south from here, while east, beech trees gradually replace them.
20918:
A tangly shrub seems to rustle as if alert to its surroundings.
An imposing beech tree sways gently in the wind.
An imposing beech tree sways gently in the wind.

Although obviously from the same kind, the trees vary from the colour of their leaves, from the usual green to a bright copper or a dark purple. Through the fan vaulting of this foliage, the diffused light from the sky can hardly reach the dark underwood, and only some evergreen tree-like bushes, with little dark green leaves, grow there, among the beech grove. This place seems to be at the crossing of four different kind of woods.
20919: A mass of low-spreading shrub quivers on the ground.

Down into the lower lands, the beech trees are replaced by a mix of hornbeams and ashes, and as the ground becomes flat, durmast oaks form the greater part of the forest. Although hidden in a dark stony soil, a copse of chestnut trees stands out, young and lively, like a jarring note in the middle of the old immutable forest. While north of here, the forest becomes increasingly tangled, a part of it appears to weep, east from here. To the south, the oaks seem to grow quite large, standing tall between the other trees in the forest, while a beech grove is to be found west of here.
20920: Some thick writhing vines whip all around you.

The old feeling of this wood is reinforced by the weeping trailings, beards and whiskers of lichen, and most of the trees seem to be half covered with ragged dry leaves that have never fallen. All here is dim, and frightfully treeish, and no sound can be heard but the slight flutter of the leaves from the top of the robust oaks. North of here, the forest is very dense and great trees obstruct the passage. Yet inside a hollow tree an odd looking stair made of rocks and roots seems to lead in a network of gullies extending north, below the forest floor.
20921:
A brown striated fungus hangs here, clinging to a tree trunk.
A brown striated fungus hangs here, clinging to a tree trunk.
A mass of wriggling vines drops on you from the trees.

An intense feeling of sorrow comes from the trees of this wood. The forest seems resigned to its forthcoming defeat against its parasites. Small brown striated fungi have started to grow along the ancient oak trunks. The more resistant younger trees are not yet infected, but north of here, the fungi grow bigger and bigger and no single tree is able to withstand the invasion for long. In every other direction the trees look healthier, though the old oaks west of here all covered in lichens and moss have an odd and sad look.
20922: An ash tree with mottled bark stands here apparently guarding its surroundings.

Hornbeams and tall ashes grow widely here, on what seems to be the last foot of a distant mountain. Here and there, the bare limestone rock of the mountain can be seen, in small unexpected clearings. The largest of these rocks, still warm from the sun light, overhang the southern section of the forest and offers a nice view of the surrounding landscape. North, however, a living wall made up of huge, bulky trees both blocks out line of sight and denies any further passage in that direction.
20923:
An ash tree with mottled bark stands here apparently guarding its surroundings.
An ash tree with mottled bark stands here apparently guarding its surroundings.

Dark, evergreen low growing plants with glossy leaves spread here, forming a delicate carpet on the top of a rocky outcrop. The place is quiet and rather sunny, under the light shade of the short hornbeams and the tall but slender ashes. The seasonal brilliant blue of the periwinkle flowers even offers a refreshing alternative to the usual shades of green of the Forest. This scenery extends a bit to the west following the outcrop of rocks, and the forest remains of ashes and hornbeams all around here. Although, as the ground lowers, large rocks and thick vegetation render the way down a bit difficult in the east and even impossible in the north.
20924: With hornbeams to the north, this part of the forest is composed mostly of ash trees. They populate this area of the forest with their leaves broad and flat, their bark firm and grey, with diamond shaped furrows. The ground is littered with leaves and all sorts of debris from trees and plants, making the footing soft and muted. West of here, some outcropping rocks appear to surround a grassy area.
20925: Southern Border of the Hornbeam Wood

The hornbeam wood spreads out from here for quite a distance, mostly to the north, but also a bit westwards. To the south, ash trees are dominant. The bark of these trees is blue-greyish and smooth, while the trunk is deeply rippled, almost like sinewy muscles. The soil here is quite moist, conditions favouring this type of tree. The ground here is littered with wet leaves and similar plant and tree debris that has fallen from the nearby trees, few other types of vegetation growing here.
20926: A mass of wriggling vines drops on you from the trees.

For quite a distance to the north, the hornbeam wood stretches out, the only landmark being a big, moss-covered rock north of here. Even a bit to the east, the hornbeams continue as well. Southwards, a thick natural wall of both hornbeam and ash trees render any attempted passage seemingly impossible. This is the case to the west as well, where a living wall of bulky trees block any passage or line of sight in that direction. The hornbeams in this area are noticeably larger than the others of their species to the east, probably as a result of better soil conditions in this area.
20927: A strange, sad-looking tree is here.

To the north, east and west, a living wall of bulky trees blocks the way and line of sight from the surroundings. From the top of the gibbous hill, rays of light straggle into the aisles of the wood as into some noble hall. The surrounding trees are bulky, and their leaves made of a healthy green. They seem arranged like an ancient and altogether admirable and shining family.
20928:
A brown striated fungus hangs here, clinging to a tree trunk.
A brown striated fungus hangs here, clinging to a tree trunk.
A brown striated fungus hangs here, clinging to a tree trunk.
