The western part of this place is filled with great majestic trees, alas the scenery eastward is much less healthy. Trees are warped as if numerous wounds have forced them to grow, following these devious ways, and with the usual cosy scent of humus mixes an odd pungent smell of animal putrefaction. However, this foul smell clearly comes from the many-sized round fungi growing on the tree trunks, their roots drawing the bark aside in deep, cranky scars. North of here, some elevated ash trees lie, while south the trees appear sore, as here, only to a less greater extent. East lies an open and sparsely forested butte, appearing to be some sort of cul-de-sac.
20929:
Some roots lie here waiting to ensnare weary travellers.
Some roots lie here waiting to ensnare weary travellers.

Large rocks, fallen from the nearby mountains, make the ground around here uneven. Trees are forced to cling on to huge rocks, in useless attempts to hold back the earth between their roots. Meanwhile the forest is very dense, as if the trees are not willing to allow any passage. The only obvious way through is a maze of earthy gullies, overgrown with hanging roots and dusty screens of rootlets from the trees above. The exit south to this maze is a passage beneath a hollow tree where a stair of rocks and roots leads up back to the forest level. While following the ditches as they widen and merge together leads north in a large gully covered with the roots of the trees above.
20930: A spiky broomrape plant pokes its blooms out of the soil.

The slopes going down from the Misty Mountains end here in a fertile hollow dale. The great trees of Fangorn grow there in close lines, and the slightest remaining parcel is filled with intertwined holm oaks, holly bushes and the occasional juniper. North and east the underwood is extremely dense, rendering the forest impenetrable. The only way through would be up in the trees, but no low branch can be reached to climb on the high trees from here.
20931: Some long roots thrust out by the nearby mountains, run down from west to east. This ridge is bristled with large deciduous trees of a dark grey bark, clad with broad flat hairy leaves. Their foliage is so dense it leaves no sunlight for the lower shrubs, apart for some box bushes on the southern flank of the ridge. The beech forest extends south and north from here on both sides of the ridges, while east the forest becomes quite tangled and large great trees grow there. West, where the ridge takes root, a rock-wall hampers access to the mountains, making for a very difficult climb.
20932: The thick branches of the great trees of Fangorn intertwine to form a network of footbridges above the bole of the trees. Their bark, grey and gnarled like the stones of a road, offer a sure footing while avoiding the dangerous travel into the dim and stuffy dark grove above. To the west, the forest becomes brighter and thinner, while east the branches lead deeper into the heart of Fangorn.
20933: A rooting heap of stems is here, smothering over the smaller plants.

A strong scent of humus coming from the bed of beech leaves littering the ground adds to the already damp atmosphere of this place. Patches of moss cover all the rocks down to the tiniest, and even dare to cling on the oldest trees. The beech forest extending west and south from here, is quite sparse due to the sloping ground, yet downwards, an impenetrable wall of tall thick trees prevents anyone from going further into the heart of the forest.
20934: The ground suddenly falls away into dark, muffled pinewoods, with a low but dense undergrowth and a soil carpeted with fallen pine nuts. The only way out from this sombre place seems to be back along the north-west slope. In every other direction the trees grow very dense, like menacing grey walls they seem to forbid any passage into the deep forest, where unspeakable things may lurk and await.
20935: Here, the foliage only consists of grass and lichen in the sunniest parts. Elsewhere, under the pines, as it is often the case under coniferous trees, the ground is littered with pine nuts, and almost no plant nor tree grows there. Only some rowan trees grow sporadically on this acid soil, especially along the eastern part of the cliff wall. West of here, some pinewoods cling on to the side of the mountain, gradually ascending, while south the pinewoods darken somewhat.
20936:
A large eagle soars above you.
A mountain goat is here, jumping from cliff to cliff.

A large cornice made of bright white limestone follows the grey brown walls of extruding granite and gneiss of the northern peaks. The soil is covered with dust coming from the wear of the daily water and ice cycle, right at the two rocks boundary. However, it looks as if the two rock layers, rubbing against each other, are trying to wear out mutually. The rocky landscape continues on to the east along a dusty path, while travelling east leads to a grassy and mountainous area.
20937: Following the mountain crest that runs north to east, does not require great climbing skill, although walking with a precipice on both sides can be quite breathtaking. North of here, the ridgeline leads to mighty sharp peaks, almost continually draped in clouds, while east, in the lowest part of the ridge, a crumbling rock wall, spread in large steady blocks, leads down to a cornice dominating the forest tree tops.
20938: This rocky edge is the easternmost part of the sharp ridgeline starting west from here, and although a bit lower, it is certainly the best point of view of the surroundings. The view provided is impressive, it overhangs a dark mountain cirque to the north, a white limestone desert to the east and the evergreen pinewoods of Fangorn to the south. In the last direction the forest extends in shades of green, dark for the evergreens, lighter for the beeches and ashes beneath, and then darker again for the oaks of the lower dales. South of here, a stacking of large angular granite rocks leads down to a dusty path.
20939: A stacking of large angular granite rocks, worked out by the alternation of the water freezing and thawing, falls down from the very top of the ridge to the north unto the limestone layer beneath. At the bottom of the fall, the flat and released aspect of the ground, could lead to thinking that this is a well used path. However, this false impression is quickly revealed as each step raises a small amount of dust that slowly rise above the ground before slipping along the cliff overhanging the forest. The dusty trail leads west to a large cornice at the feet of the ridge and east to a flat area where a few scattered pines grow.
20940: A solid, but stunted, rowan tree has established itself here.

Along the cliff to the north, some rowan trees seem to have been sown, forming a hedge around a large white flat rock. There, under the shadow of the sorbs, the slightly filtered light makes the falling mountain's dust sparkle and dance slowly. All this creates an odd feeling of quietness and sorrow, as if the trees were meditating in memory of one of their kind, lost or dead. West and east from here the rowan trees slowly fade into the pine woods, while south great trees seem to block any passage towards the heart of the forest.
20941: Everything below this elevated path is kept in utter darkness, as if the trees wished to deny any light to that which lies at their feet in some sort of protest. A more pleasant atmosphere can be found south of here, where the foliage is looser. In this direction, a succession of large horizontal branches offer an easy path, leading to the forks of exceptionally large trees.
20942: On the Branches of the Great Trees

Trees are larger, taller, and thicker here than in any part of the surrounding forest. They have grown so close that it is possible to travel from limb to limb effortlessly. Meanwhile, the ground below is scattered with intertwined roots, fallen twigs and huge rocks blocking the way. Above, the sky is often visible through the sparse foliage, and the sense of stifling often felt in the depths of the forest, is totally absent here. South of here, a tree has leant on its neighbours affording a way down to the ground.
20943: The trunk is several feet in diameter, and judging by the amount of lichen covering its bark, the tree might have been very old. Scattered along the whole length of the bole, numerous twigs and boughs might help for an easy climb up to the forest-roof or down to the ground. Up, to the north, on the branches of the great trees of Fangorn, it should be possible to move about, with more ease than on the overgrown ground.
20944:
Some roots lie here waiting to ensnare weary travellers.
Massive roots shift uneasily all around you.

Trees here seem to float above the ground, held there by the skein of their roots. The ground level used to be higher but the flowing water drained the earth lower into the forest. West of here, one of the trees, insufficiently rooted and dragged down by its own weight, has leaned against its neighbours, in the middle of a wide gully. Its trunk, slightly bowed, affords an easy way up in the highest trees. The gully shows no obvious slope, but it might run down to the north, as it appears to split south in a maze of smaller tributary ditches littered with muddy rocks and forest debris.
20945: Ash Trees Rising above the Hornbeam Forest
An ash tree with mottled bark stands here apparently guarding its surroundings.

Below, to the east of here, through a succession of rock walls with fissures and fallen leaves, one approaches a part of the forest dominated by hornbeam trees. The medium sized ash trees in this area, perhaps white ash, have littered the ground with all kinds of tree debris. Leaves, twigs and branches cover the ground completely. This makes the ground very padded and since the soil is quite moist, hooves and feet sink slightly into the ground for every step taken. Still, movement is virtually muted. North of here, the ash forest goes on for a while, while south, some great, majestic trees fill the landscape.
20946: A wall of large bulky trees form an impassable barrier to the south of here, blocking any line of sight or passage in that direction. West of here, and slightly elevated, large groves of ash trees are accessible, spreading out towards both north and south. North of here, for some distance, the blue grey of the hornbeams can be seen spreading far to the north. On the ground, the wood of the branches and twigs that have fallen to the ground recently, are already decaying noticeably. Along with the branches on the ground lies quite a few leaves, padding the footing to the best of their ability.
20947: In between a few large and healthy looking hornbeams, a fairly large rock, all covered up in moss, rises from the ground. The spacing between the trees is wider than in most areas of this hornbeam forest, but still, the trees form a kind of roof above the ground, hampering the rays of the sun. Despite this, the area is likely hit by enough sunlight to feed the undergrowth. From beneath the stone, a clear, cool spring bubbles up from the ground, most likely a safe source of drinking water. Near the rock, there are some fairly large footprints on the ground still visible.
20948: In all directions, but east, the hornbeam forest spreads out from here. To the east, the forest appears to gradually become denser and denser. The spacing between the trees is quite narrow here, and the atmosphere is noticeably denser than what is the case both to the north, south and to the west. Spread around on the soft footing padded with branches and leaves from the trees, some quite small rocks are to be seen, all of them covered with a reasonably thick layer of moss.
20949: Whilst surrounded on all sides with similar types of trees, this part of the forest is noticeably lighter than its neighbouring areas. For the most part, this is caused by the density of the trees decreasing to a certain extent. However, the trees here also tend to have fewer leaves, something probably caused by the fact that the ground is not as moist in this area, as compared to the other parts of this hornbeam forest.
20950:
A tall, slender hornbeam Ent walks around here, keeping watch over his trees.
A tall, slender hornbeam Ent walks around here, keeping watch over his trees.

The density of the hornbeam trees in this area of the forest has greatly increased, as opposed to that of the surrounding areas, greatly limiting the line-of-sight in every direction. It nearly appears as though the trees have artificially drawn towards each other here, standing close to each other while conversing, or whatever else it is that they may be up to. As this is approximately in the middle of the hornbeam forest of this area, there are hardly any other species of tree to be found at all. Because of the density of the trees, the daylight here is greatly dimmed.
20951: To the west, elevated above this area of the forest, some ash trees grow, while to the east and south, the hornbeam forest continues. Northwards, passage is impossible, because of the cliff rising vertically from the ground in that direction. On the ground, the branches that have fallen from the trees are already decaying, even those that have just recently fallen. Along with it, on the ground, lie quite a few leaves and similar debris from the trees nearby.
20952: An ash tree with mottled bark stands here apparently guarding its surroundings.

Ash trees, with their firm grey bark, occupy this part of the forest. Their broad, flat leaves with short stems litter the ground here, making travelling here very quiet. Beneath all the debris, the ground appears a bit moist. Below to the east, accessible through a succession of fissured rock walls, cluttered with fallen leaves, hornbeams seem to take over the scenery and spread eastwards throughout the forest, while north and south, more ash trees are to be found. To the west, some gigantic old and bulky trees rise from the ground, making the ash trees in this area seem quite pale in comparison.
20953: Trees here are old and bulky, almost regularly spaced out and the size of columns in a gigantic cathedral. The ground is very rocky and the roots of the great trees plunge deep into the earth, splitting even the largest rocks into flat slabs of marble. No young sprout of this kind of tree can be seen and only some midget larches and firs try to survive, growing in the earth filled fissures in the rocks. North and east the forest looks normal, as birches or ashes grow there, but elsewhere the great trees grow in close rows. Although south of here, the trees hardly seem to touch the ground at all and it might be possible to travel beneath.
20954: A tall birch is here, watching over the landscape.

The forest here mainly consists of yellow birch and rowan-trees. The bright green grass, the neat white of the rocks and the sparse foliage of the birches give this place the brightness lacking from the surrounding parts of the forest. To the north dark climbing pinewoods rise and west and south the ground falls into shadowy hollow dales with a thickset undergrowth sometimes impassable. The ash trees east of here, somehow appear to be whispering amongst themselves, or is it the wind blowing in the leaves?
20955: A tall pine tree grows here.

The soil here is smooth and earthy, but on top of all, dark. Even the pines are murky when seen from below. Only some rays of sunlight manage to break through the dense foliage and reflect off the small quartz crystals of the white rocks below. However, when the sun sets, the forest becomes even more mysterious, the pines change to giants under the moon light, and a host of silent inanimate eyes start to glow beneath the gloomy undergrowth. The vicinity of the mountains can clearly be seen as pines or beeches grow along the slopes east and west from here. Northwards, the forest thins out while reaching a limestone plateau, whereas it gets denser and denser to the south.
20956:
A mountain goat is here, jumping from cliff to cliff.
A young goat playfully charges and hops away.

On this uneven limestone plateau, extending here and towards the north, grass patches and tufts of gilded and yellow lichen cling to the polished surfaces of the gray rock, adding a key of colour to the scene. South, as the ground declines, pines start to appear, covered with the same rust-like yellow lichen and dripping with resin. There, near the forest border lies a large flat stone slab, on top of two smaller round rocks, like a rough dolmen on which moss abounds. Underneath, the rock is always damp, undoubtedly the exit of a small underground brook, maybe part of a large subterranean network.
20957: A mountain goat is here, jumping from cliff to cliff.

This incredible untamed rocky landscape is made of an inextricable chaos of vast structural flagstones engraved with fissures and faults. The tender limestone surface was levelled by the slow erosion of the now gone glacier, and then washed up year after year by the snow melt water, resulting in an almost lunar surface, a succession of stone slab fields intersected with grassy strips. Strangely enough, this place now looks like a great frozen stone glacier. This landscape of stones and rocks is blocked west by a rising mountain ridge, while it extends in every other direction, only a bit more grassy east and south.
20958: A short plant, with lance-shaped leaves, waves its purple petals in the breeze.

This area is covered with sturdy grass tufts and blue gentians sheltered under lichen-covered rocks. In the west, near the outcropped limestone rocks, bare of almost all vegetation, the grass is dry and yellow. However, it becomes vivid and green as it approaches the rocky escarpment in the east. There, along the cliff brink, daffodils flutter under the gentle wind, but it seems more natural to go for a safer passage around the cliff, either to the north or to the south, than to try a short but hazardous climb.
20959: A rooting heap of stems is here, smothering over the smaller plants.

A few scattered beech trees grow here, outside the border of the nearby forest. They are the last copses of trees before the mountains, replacing the usual conifers. Their bark is fresh and moist and redolent of dewy odours, and they stand in the sort of vigor and perennialness that only the largest deciduous trees suggest. South and east, the ground plunges deep into the beech forest, while west, as the land gets rockier, only grass and lichens grow.
20960: While north of here, great white mountains dominate the scenery, forest is to be found in all other directions. To the west, some dark climbing pinewoods cling on to the side of the mountain, while south ash trees stand. To the east, more beech trees, just like the ones standing here, can be found. The footing here isn't very densely populated with bushes and undergrowth, but much more stable and safer than in the areas south of here. North, however, the beech trees become much more scattered, while east the forest becomes more moist.
20961: To the far north, it is possible, albeit barely, to see parts of a mountain, extending up towards the north. Ash trees surround this area both to the east and south, while northwards, beeches are dominant. West of here, are some birch and rowan thickets. Strangely enough, there is no sign of animal life in the forest, and because of this it feels awfully quiet here. When one listens, though, one might feel as if the trees are whispering among themselves, or as if some of the trees move, or arch towards some target.
20962: An imposing beech tree sways gently in the wind.

The density of the trees and bushes increases greatly in this area, and due to the fact that the only exits south and east are off a cliff, vertically, quite a few feet downwards, passage in those directions is impossible. Northwards, the ash trees of this area are bordered by a beech forest, whereas to the west more ash trees, similar to the ones here, can be found. As the density of the trees increases, so does the chance of tripping in some roots from the trees, or in some bushes or undergrowth on the ground here. One had best watch one's step, if one wishes to stay on one's feet in this area.
20963: A brown striated fungus hangs here, clinging to a tree trunk.

The dark-grey beech forest continues in all directions from here, except to the south, where it gradually fades into a majority of ash trees. While the ground here is not particularly wet, it is noticeably moist, making for suitable conditions for the beech trees growing here. Still, there are a lot of branches, leaves and other kinds of debris from the surrounding trees and plant life covering the ground.
20964: Bordered by mountains to the west and trees clinging on to the lower parts of the mountain northwards, this area of beech forest is surrounded by elevation on all sides but to the south and east. In these directions, more beech forest is to be found. Normally, beeches would provide shelter for many kinds of animals within its hollows, however, there is not much to be found of this sort here, hardly any at all, which is easily noticed, due to the absence of any kind of noise revealing animal activity here.
20965: A mix of maples, ashes and red oaks grow here, their roots dangling over the edge of the precipice. The undergrowth is full of low growing green shrubs and flowers, like the splendid large harebells that nod over the edge and in the clefts of the cliff, their dainty pastel lavender blossoms supported by delicate stems. Almost hidden behind them is a small passage leading down and following a fissure full of fallen leaves, straight towards the north. North and up from here, following the escarpment edge, the forest remains the same, while south as the land flattens the forest is composed mostly of beeches.
20966: A spiky broomrape plant pokes its blooms out of the soil.

Twilight shadows creep in through the odd trees of this wood. The height of the cliff on one hand, and the density of the foliage, conspire to produce a gloominess, if not an absolute dreary-like, effect. The old and dreary shapes of the trees is caused by common moss, lichen and algae, covering their limbs like a thick veil of green and grey. More unusually, along the cliff wall, even ferns and stray flowers have managed to take root in the debris-filled joints of the tree branches. North and east from here, the forest seems even more dreary, inviting any legged visitor to travel south into the more quiet beech forest.
20967: North of here, the forest becomes more entangled and much darker than it is here. To the west the number of beech trees gradually fades, although it still remains the dominant sort of tree for quite a distance. To the northwest, a more mountainous region can barely be spotted through the thick cover of the trees. As with most other parts of this forest, the footing here mainly consists of leaves and other debris from the nearby plants or trees, with some twigs and similar added to the mix as well. This makes for a, most of the time, muted footing, albeit with some exceptions.
20968: A mass of low-spreading shrub quivers on the ground.

In all directions but southwards from here, the beech forest continues, stretching out quite a distance. Although the ground here is still a bit moist, the degree of moist appears to gradually decrease both to the north and south. Southwards, the percentage of beeches in the forest decreases gradually, until all that is left is hornbeams. The ground is littered with broad and flat leaves with coarse teeth, that have fallen from the beeches. There is a lot of other debris on the ground as well, in some places effectively muting any sounds made when one walks upon it.
20969: A spiky broomrape plant pokes its blooms out of the soil.

Elevated above this area, to the north, a beech forest is located. Both to the south and east, however, the hornbeam woods continue for a while. The ground is filled with many fine, double-teethed leaves that have fallen from the blue-grey trees, in addition to a lot of twigs and branches as well. The branches and twigs that have fallen off the trees are already beginning to decay because of the moist soil here. As a side-effect of the moisture, feet and hooves sink slightly into the soil when someone passes here.
20970: Numerous beech trees, elevated above this area, rise north of here, while in all other directions, the hornbeam woods continue. On the ground there are many medium-sized rocks, most of them all covered up in moss, making them quite slippery to step on. The hornbeam trees appear to flourish here, because of the moist soil, and even though the rays of the sun do not always reach down through the thick roof of leaves and branches, the trees seem to pull through pretty well.
20971: The beech forest spreads from the north and west, bordered by blue-grey hornbeams and continues southward. The moisture in the ground is still noticeable, albeit decreasing in comparison with what is the case west of here. The smooth grey trees stand proud here, making no apparent noise, but sometimes it appears as though they are almost alive, communicating with each other, and swaying close to any traveller who might have made his way down to this part of the forest. Littered with twigs, leaves and other debris, the ground is padded to a large extent, making for very soft footing. Bordering the forest, to the east is a rocky area.
20972: While to the north the forest becomes tangled and quite dark compared to here, it continues to be filled with mostly beeches. They continue both to the south and west for quite some distance, before other sorts of trees become more dominant. The density in the eastern part of this area of trees nearly block all passage eastwards, but not quite. Still, the ground is padded with leaves and other sorts of plant debris, as is the case with most parts of this forest. The ground is also quite moist and both foot and hoof often sink into the ground when traversing upon it.
20973: The trees stand silently, rank upon rank, fading away north into the grey twilight. Travelling around is difficult, no undergrowth can be seen and almost no debris, but many roots emerge everywhere and sometimes out of place, as if on purpose. North and west from here, the forest is still odd and dark and it might not be a pleasant place to travel. The passages south and east, where the forest is greener and at least more normal, if not welcoming, are the easiest.
20974: As the ground rises here, the trees thin slightly. Through a small gap in the trees to the west, the dim outline of a mountain range can be made out on the horizon, many days of travelling away. Short grass carpets the ground, covering the tree roots that have erupted above ground. To the south the trees stretch along a steep rise.
20975: An enormous tree, overgrown with moss, is here.

If it were not for the unbroken canopy blocking the view of the valley below, the top of this hill would make an excellent vantage point from which one could observe movement in the forest. To the east the hill slopes steeply away.
20976: The slope to the eastern side is littered with rocks of various shapes and sizes. Worn by years of exposure to wind and rain the rocks have become smooth and even, their unprotected backs polished by weather and time. To the east the ground slopes away while the hills continue to the north and south.
20977: The ridge runs north-south and the forest follows it unbroken. Roots from the old trees stretch far from the trunks, occasionally breaking clear above the ground, presenting a great hazard for the careless or unwary traveller.
20978: The Southern Edge of a Ridge

Climbing steadily upwards, the forest rises away from the valley to the south- east. The long slope is clad with grass beneath the tall evergreens that creak softly as the wind plays through their branches. From the vantage point here, high mountains can be seen towering to the west. It would take many days of travel to reach their base.
20979: While the valley opens out to the northeast, further south and west the forest becomes increasing dense. The ground here is cold, unnaturally cold. Nothing grows near the base of the trees save some of the hardier varieties of moss. The leaves on the branches above make a soft rustling sound as they sway in the gentle breeze.
20980: Entering this part of the forest is no simple matter. Thick tree roots snake their way across the forest floor and strong vines hug the trees as if trying to strangle the life out of them. It is noticeably darker here than in the area to the north. Besides that, the cool air and silence creates an eerie, almost oppressive atmosphere.
20981: A small pool of red-stained water lies here.

Great dark trees grow in a line on either side of a small stream. Gnarled boughs betray the age of the ancient trees. The stream itself is almost the same colour as the bark on the trees. The soft earth surrounding the water being slowly eroded over time. A wise traveller would do well to avoid drinking from such a polluted source. Looking further downstream, little can be seen save a shallow gully to the east.
20982: A spiky broomrape plant pokes its blooms out of the soil.

A thin trickle of water runs across the ground making the area very boggy and the air damp and humid. A musty smell prevails and since the canopy of leaves still arches above, evidently sheltered from the wind, there is little chance of fresh air here. Further north, the sound of rustling leaves can be heard. To the south the ground slopes gently away, leading to the bottom of the valley. A small hill flanks the valley to the west, clearly the source of the water that drains into this area.
20983: To the south the willow trees at the tunnel mouth frame the woodland beyond in the shape of an arch. The tunnel walls are constructed of small twigs woven into solid panels that confine movement. To the north and east the tunnel seems to lead away, deeper into the forest. The only obvious exit is the southern path stretching into the forest.
20984: An ash tree with mottled bark stands here apparently guarding its surroundings.

The tunnel comes to an abrupt end, the body of a giant willow tree forms the eastern wall. Supple ash trees growing in straight rows have been bent together and fixed in place to form a natural canopy overhead. The branches high up have woven together over time, casting the area into darkness save for a few narrow shafts of light that pierce the gloom only when the sun is directly overhead.
20985: The forest seems to stir as if to direct wanderers to a weeping willow. Standing forty feet high it is a magnificent specimen. The parasol of leaves and branches reaching the ground some twenty paces from the trunk, creating a haven of relaxation underneath. The bark of the tree is covered with patches of white lichen giving it a slightly unnatural, mottled effect. The remnants of an ancient track can just be made out winding through the trees. The path goes no further west than the willow.
20986: In stark contrast to the rest of the forest, the trees growing here appear to be quite young. Their thin trunks are covered with a rich dark-brown bark, their branches waving in the breeze, the movement of the leaves creating waves of noise. Around the base of each willow a carpet of grass has sprung up. Only the thin, brown line of a small path leading to the west spoils the uniformity.
20987: The southern end of the wide path between the birch trees opens out to reveal a thicket of imposing greenery further to the south. The path turns and heads to the west but only continues a few yards before becoming nothing more than an overgrown track. On the eastern edge of the opening, amid the surviving trees, several tree stumps lie covered with ferns.
20988: A bright orange bracket fungus grows on some decaying wood.

These pale birch trees appear to glow in the dim light. The silver bark has few blemishes and stands in stark contrast to the remainder of the drab forest. Insects crawl back and forth, busily attending to their tasks, among the moss and fungi growing between the roots.
20989: The forest becomes increasingly tangled as the numerous branches grow closer and closer together. They almost seem to have a mind of their own as they appear to actively inhibit movement progress. To the west a break in the dense forest appears, at least the woodland seems lighter in that direction. Further to the south the ground levels off as the top of the hill is reached.
20990: A rooting heap of stems is here, smothering the smaller plants.

Oak and beech trees grow mingled together, lichen clinging to their trunks. Although silent and still they seem to have an aura of menace about them, almost as if they do not appreciate travellers passing through. Beneath the piles of leaves that litter the ground, numerous thick roots lie hidden, ready to trip the unwary. The thick forest continues, seemingly endlessly, in all directions.
20991: The watchfulness of the forest lingers here. The trees stir as their branches follow any movement below. Lichen clings to the enormous trunks like the beards of old men. Piles of leaves and debris cover the ground and one must tread carefully to avoid the obtrusive roots that often block the way. The air is thick and musty, and carries a stale fragrance of oak and birch. Looking to the east a line of trees have grown into an entangled web, forbidding travel that way. In all other directions the forest goes on as far as the eye can see.
20992:
A tall and haughty elm stands here (red aura).
A tall and haughty elm stands here (red aura).

This hollow seems to have never been touched by sunshine nor starlight, yet the trees grow thick and strong. Their branches have developed into tangled webs that hinder or block passage in every direction. With the slightest disturbance, the sound of rustling leaves ripples through the canopy and an occasional hissing whisper is discernable amidst the muffled sounds. The ground underfoot is soft and muddy with small pools of murky water dotting the forest floor. An acrid stench rises from the puddles and mixes with the stuffy air, making every breath a chore.
20993: Dark menacing trees dominate this oppressive vale. Their gnarled unmoving shapes are watchful, yet silent. The air is heavy, and filled with the stifling odour of age and decay. Nothing stirs here and there is no sound from bird or beast. The ground squelches underfoot as water from a small filthy pond leeches into the soil and seeps away westward into a foreboding hollow. The forest floor rises gently to the north and to the south.
20995: The air is chokingly thick and carries a pungent scent of age and decay. Trees cluster together according to their type. To the north, a wall of eerie, white birch trees stands in stark contrast to the gloomy surroundings, and to the west grows a clump of strange, dark trees which form a tangled mass of branches and trunks. The soggy leaf-littered ground slopes downwards towards these tangled trees. Up above, the canopy is completely closed, preventing any light from penetrating.
20996: A tall birch is here, watching over the landscape.

The dense occlusive canopy in this part of the forest traps thick stuffy air that smothers the environment. Breathing is made even more difficult by the pungent odour of soggy, decaying earth. To the north-east an intimidating array of tall, birch trees slowly encroaches on the gnarled old trees that grow here.
20997: Deciduous trees grow intermingled with numerous aging trees that appear to have never shed their foliage nor borne more shoots. This mixture of trees allows the forest to breathe during the winter months. The deciduous trees, which stand like skeletal remains, create pockets where natural light can pour in around the bare branches. During summer, the regrown canopy causes the air to stagnate and harbour a strong, woody fragrance.
20998: The majority of trees that have dwelt here through the ages are deciduous. In the autumn, they display their conspicuous, scarlet garb like balls of fire amongst the dull and ageing evergreen trees. Amber and brown leaves, which crunch loudly underfoot, layer the ground as a reminder of the previous year's winter slumber.
20999:
You see two mushrooms on the ground.
A bright orange bracket fungus grows on some decaying wood.

This long-established evergreen wood is dotted with deciduous trees. Their cyclical change of foliage is the only thing that breaks the monotony of the dim drab forest. Large lawns of moss and hanging beards of lichen proliferate in the dappled light beneath the patchwork canopy. Fungi grows rampant and fallen leaves survive for only a short time before they decay into the dark humus of the forest floor.
21000: Ever-changing colours adorn these mighty trees. The bare tree skeletons of winter begin to flourish with vivid greens as the days lengthen through spring. Then summer arrives with greater vibrance and the foliage around and above traps the warm air and fills the canopy with the deepest green. Though the scene is magnificent the trees save their most glorious display for autumn when they blaze with gold and crimson leaves and the forest seems to rain with fire. Each leaf floats down like a flicker of flame and melds into the scarlet sea of leaves that moves and fades with the seasons.
21001: A mass of low-spreading shrub quivers on the ground.

The trees in this part of the forest grow dense and thick. The trunks in some places are no more than a few feet apart and their branches grow intertwined, making it difficult to determine which tree they have grown from without carefully tracing each limb back to its trunk. The compact growth makes it dim and stuffy and the lack of any breeze has left dead leaves hanging from the branches for many years before they fall and carpet the ground.
21002:
A spiky broomrape plant pokes its blooms out of the soil.
A mass of wriggling vines drops on you from the trees.

Tangled complexes of gnarled trunks and twisting branches are enmeshed in an endless struggle for light and position. Winding throughout these tangled masses, thick vines spiral around, sending out their tendrils in search of the next limb to cling to. Grey-green lichens tumble down from overhead branches like cascades of ruffled tulle, and the cluttered foliage makes the forest dim and the air stuffy.
21003:
A small centipede is here scurrying about.
A junebug buzzes slowly through the air.
A junebug buzzes slowly through the air.

Massive trees grow here. Their every fibre holds onto life, defying age with bold determination. Not a single branch is without a lush array of leaves, nor has any trunk become hollow or disfigured. These evergreens form an expansive canopy of rich, emerald-coloured foliage which begins just ten feet from the gently sloping forest floor. Every once in a while, a dead leaf falls from above, twisting and weaving towards the bare, moist ground and is quickly devoured by scouring insects which emerge from the soil when it lands.
21004: Amidst the shadows of decay that pervade Fangorn, there is light here that continues to endure. An undisturbed forest of phenomenal grandeur opens out in a panorama of striking colour and form. The majestic trees carry the burdens of time with dignified boldness, their crowns reach skyward and their branches stretch outward as though holding the skies. A rich woody fragrance flavours the air and the warbling of birds is the only natural sound that breaks the tranquillity.
21005: In firm denial of the spreading decay in other parts of the forest, these trees stand as a vestigial reminder of the magnificence that this forest once had. The hemlock and beech trees are resplendent in their robes of rich vibrant foliage and their mighty trunks seem to be a manifestation of the strength of Orome and the beauty of Yavanna.
21006: The mighty trees here have resisted the corruption that threatens them from the north. The leaves are unstained and the glossy surfaces glimmer with the snippets of light that break through the canopy. Frequent rain or mists often leave the branches wet and glistening, like a multitude of stars shining beneath the parasol of foliage.
21007: Sleep-enchanted trees grow here, perhaps dreaming about the once pure and magnificent days of the forest. The lush foliage adorning their noble bodies creates a variegated array of textures and shades which crown the sturdy trunks with splendour. A scattering of leaf litter and large, protruding buttress roots provide a few scuttling insects with safe cover beneath the dense canopy. The air is crisp and clear with a faint scent of pine.
21008: These trees of regal nobility have survived as a mere remnant of this once great and incomparable wood. Their stunning form nears on perfection. Every leaf and branch grows with youthful vivacity even though the trees are so aged they appear to have become one with the earth. The radiance and health of the trees gives the impression that it is perpetually spring here, however, a scattering of old autumn leaves on the ground betrays this notion.
21009:
A tall plant with a perfectly smooth stem gracefully marks the landscape.
A clear pool of water has formed amongst some nearby tree roots.
A junebug buzzes slowly through the air.

An undisturbed forest of magnificent splendour pans out here like a panacea against the shadows and gloom that dominate Fangorn. The long ages measured by the wheeling of the stars have not brought any blemish to these stately trees. The lush, dark-green foliage of hemlock and vibrant ever-changing colours of beech show that the glorious days once celebrated in the forest have not yet been forgotten. The crisp, clear air is accompanied by the gentle bubbling of a nearby spring.
21010: Emerald-coloured foliage is swathed about the reaching branches and trunks of these stoic evergreen trees. In their midst grows a few lush conifers that bring a haphazard dark-green contrast. The fallen conifer needles form isles of rusty-brown that seem to float on top of the deep-brown earth. A soft woody fragrance fills the air and an occasional breeze from the north-west brings a fresh pine aroma.
21011: Some roots lie here waiting to ensnare weary travellers.

A labyrinth of gnarled old trees, entwining vines and protruding roots spreads out far into the dim musty surrounds. Hedge-like trees with twisting, deformed branches and dense foliage grow in a confused pattern, diverting any travellers from a straight path. Amidst this mazework stand drab and drear trees of many varieties, each one so faded that it is barely distinguishable from the next.
21012: The trees in this part of the forest grow dense and thick. The trunks in some places are no more then a few feet apart and their branches grow intertwined. Compact growth makes it dim and stuffy, and the lack of any breeze has left dead leaves hanging from the branches for many years before they finally fall and carpet the ground. To the south, the forest becomes dominated by deciduous trees that give the woodland a dynamic, ever-changing hue.
21013: The deciduous trees that dominate the forest form an ever-changing panorama. The trees stand as bare skeletons throughout winter, and when spring comes they begin to flourish with vivid greens. Then summer arrives bringing with it an even greater vibrance. The foliage around and above traps warm air and fills the canopy with a deep jade colour. Rather suddenly, the trees begin to withdraw during autumn. The resultant display is glorious. The trees blaze with gold and crimson leaves and the forest seems to rain with fire. Each leaf floats down from its branch like a flicker of flame and melds into the scarlet sea of leaves, which remains until winter strips everything bare again.
21014: Deciduous trees remain dominant here, but they look thinner and more delicate than in other parts of the forest. Their weakly frames bend under the weight of summer foliage and the glorious ablaze landscape expected here in autumn is nothing more then a browning of the leaves that tumble down into drifts of discarded foliage on the forest floor.
21015:
A tall, slender hornbeam Ent walks around here, keeping watch over his trees.
A junebug buzzes slowly through the air.

The trees here continue rank after rank, fading away into a greyish twilight. The diversity in the textures and tones are subdued by the thick musty air and dense looming canopy which consumes any light from above. Layers of peeling bark, shed leaves and fallen branches litter the ground and crunch noisily when trampled upon.
21016: Trees of many kinds stand rank after rank as far as can be seen. Each of their shapes and shades seem to reflect an individual nature. A dark stout thick- limbed founder grows beside his slender daughter adorned in lime-green foliage. Behind them stands one who wanted to be different from others and so divided his strength into numerous branches before he had grown three feet tall. Some trees have taken the appearance of wise grandfathers, leaning on their exposed roots like an elderly man leans on a cane. Beside them stands one resembling a delicate dancer with twisting vines draped about her. Each tree is unique, and the variety is endless.
21017: A tall, slender hornbeam Ent walks around here, keeping watch over his trees.

Firs, pines and conifers have taken control of this part of the forest. The dense needle-like foliage and low branches block the piercing rays of the sun and trap a heavy pine scent in the air. The rough-barked trunks emerge like pillars from the sea of discarded needles and cones. Underfoot, the layers of fallen needles slide against each other creating a slithery surface.
21018: Pines, firs and other coniferous trees grow plentifully, but one tree in particular stands out with its enormous size and majestic stature. Its cracked grey trunk would take the outstretched arms of ten large men to circumscribe. The low branches reach far amongst the surrounding forest, its outstretched fingers tickling trees up to thirty feet away. These lower limbs provide perfect steps that can be used to climb the tree.
21019: A tall pine tree grows here.

Dominating the forest here are large and healthy fir trees, which perfume the air with a strong pine fragrance. The rough, greyish-brown trunks stand almost naked from their roots up, until about twenty feet above the ground where a lush green canopy breaks forth. The forest floor is bare of undergrowth, even though streams of light pour through the canopy when the sun shines. In place of the expected ferns or shrubbery only needles, cones and fallen branches are found.
21020: The oak and fir trees are strong in this part of the wood, yet an unusual pall hangs over them. Branches cling close to the trunks as though fearful to extend far from the security of their stout bodies. A grave stillness dominates the wood and as the evening rays cast their last light the silence deepens and the forest becomes mantled in silver-grey.
21021: Stagnancy and shadow has grown within this part of the forest. The once beautiful and noble trees are becoming twisted and tired. Grey-green lichens trail from their branches in long, web-like beards and the air has lost the fresh sweet fragrance of a healthy wood. The ground is scarred with channels where water from heavy rains has coursed downhill to the west.
21022: A dominance of pines and firs perfume the air with a sharp alpine scent. The thick canopy is proof that the majority of trees are healthy, however, there is an occasional naked lifeless trunk that bares testimony that not all is well within the wood. The multitude of pine needles and cones that lie on the ground must be kicked aside in order to make passage easier.
21023:
A tall pine tree grows here.
The embodied shape of a linden tree stands shiftlessly here.
A junebug buzzes slowly through the air.

Silver fir, spruce and pine have overtaken other varieties of trees. They grow like massive, green wizards hats stretching sixty feet or more into the air. Many branches grow low to the ground and the clusters of sharp, dark-green needles spike the skin if care is not taken. Other needles that have fallen from the trees layer the ground in a slippery brown carpet and occasionally a pine-cone falls from above to join the myriad that already lay on the forest floor. A fresh pine fragrance lingers in the air.
21024:
A clear pool of water has formed amongst some nearby tree roots.
The embodied shape of a linden tree stands shiftlessly here.

Numerous old willow trees encircle a small glade in a leafy wreath. Within the glade bubbles a small spring that is crowned with gleaming light. The spring is clear and blue by day but by night, when all is still, it becomes a mirror for the stars. On a gentle rise to the north, fir trees take the place of willows and a fresh scent of pine is wafted in by slow airs. Outside the willowed glade poplars with raining foliage mingle with frowning yews creating a subdued splendour in the aged forest.
21025:
A junebug buzzes slowly through the air.
A junebug buzzes slowly through the air.

Walking amongst the glossy dark-green leaves, olive lichens and jade-coloured needles is like stepping through an abstract collage. It seems that the various trees have been pasted into this dim and dreary picture. Dead leaves are scattered on top of the rich dark soil, providing homes for the occasional insect.
21026: A tall birch is here, watching over the landscape.

A mingled selection of trees grows here. Variegated foliage and irregular trunks are the common sight, however there is one type that stands out. To the south-west, the occasional ghostly-white trunk of a birch tree stands stark against the dim gloomy surrounds. The other trees are leaning, almost as though cowering, away from their intimidating presence. The air is muggy and is filled with tense watchfulness, or maybe even fear.
21027: Withering leaves fall like raindrops from the ailing trees. The branches are twisted and have begun to shrivel and die. The vibrant colours of the leaves have faded and are replaced by a monotonous grey-green, which matches the lichens that now grow in the place of most of the foliage. Papery leaf litter rustles underfoot and the shards of light which pierce the canopy serve no further purpose than to spotlight the dust-laden air.
21029: Before a Threatening Line of Trees

The trees here are closer and more ominous than in neighbouring regions. Other species have been overrun, and the unearthly white trunks of birch trees have become the dominant sight. The ground is covered in drifts of papery leaf litter, and the scent of musty decay is pungent.
21030:
An ash tree with mottled bark stands here apparently guarding its surroundings.
A tall, slender hornbeam Ent walks around here, keeping watch over his trees.
A junebug buzzes slowly through the air.

Silver-grey ash mingle with other varieties of trees as the forest becomes thick and stuffy. A few white birch trees can be seen stretching out like fingers from a ghostly wall that runs far to the south-west. Other trees stand in stately form, fashioned with mottled-green lichen and coated in leaves of various textures and shades. The forest floor seems bare and lifeless, except for an occassional insect scurrying away to its home.
21031: In this part of the forest, various kinds of trees blend together in a rather monotonous scene. The canopy only allows sufficient light through in order to feed the moss and lichen that smothers the tree trunks in a pallid-green blanket. Many trees here are evergreens. Their glossy, green leaves provide the only contrast to the otherwise dim surrounds. A few shrivelled leaves are scattered on the ground and every so often an insect scuttles beneath one of them.
21032:
A black alder looms threateningly over its surroundings.
An ash tree with mottled bark stands here apparently guarding its surroundings.

Oak, linden, rowan, ash, fir and various other unrecognizable species grow here in a disorderly fashion. The diversity in foliage creates a mottled canopy, like a patchwork blanket stretched across the sky. Similarly, the unique perfume from each of the trees blends together perfectly to form a rich aroma that stimulates the senses with its vibrancy, but also stifles them with its intensity. Through the canopy, shards of light pierce the innate gloom and cast speckled patterns on the forest floor.
21033:
A giant and ancient yew stands here quite eerily.
A giant and ancient yew stands here quite eerily.
A nightingale is here, chirping a sweet melody.

These once burgeoning trees have become a mass of decrepit trunks over time. Their twisted shapes make passage difficult and cumbersome and their foliage is so dense that light cannot penetrate. The ground drops to the north into an ominous area of darkness and a faint, rancid stench wafts in with the slightest breeze from that direction.
21034:
A brown pond between old branches and roots is here.
A huge black fungus is here, exuding a foul stench.
An ancient fungus smothers the boulders.
An ancient fungus smothers the boulders.

Nightshade lies deep here. An eerie silence prevails and it seems that the shadows that reigned before the coming of the sun and moon have never been vanquished from this ancient hollow. Though this area is devoid of trees, an enveloping watchfulness still survives. Fungi grow out of the soggy earth and a rancid stench permeates the air.
21035: The thick stuffy air is engulfing as the trees close about in a tangled web of branches and foliage. Their massive trunks slump under the weight of their limbs, which are laden with foliage and lichen. The entwining branches are so dense that a great deal of scrambling over one branch and under another is required to clamber through the forest.
21036: Passage among the forest here is near to impossible. Trees crowd together like a multitude jostling to escape from the dejected wood. They grow so densely that light barely penetrates the forest, and only the rarest shaft has the privilege of bursting through the dim, stuffy air onto the littered forest floor in a flash of contrasting brilliance.
21037: Dull, grey-green shades from the underside of oak leaves mingle with the glossy, vibrant hues of beech trees. Looking up at this mosaic of colours is like gazing through a stained-glass window. Sadly, however, this spectacular artistry is lost in the dim, unvarying scene which pans out at eye level. Lichens smother the tree trunks with a pallid grey, drawing away the intense silvers and browns which naturally paint their bodies. The dead leaves strewn across the ground take on this same grey pallor.
21038: Grey shabby trunks of various trees stretch far into the distance. Their once noble bodies are draped with olive-coloured lichens and their branches stretch forth into a canopy of intricate lacework. The air is dim and stuffy and filled with an odour of mild decay. On the forest floor, insects scuttle beneath the leaves which are strewn about haphazardly.
21039:
A tall birch is here, watching over the landscape.
A cluster of dark green, feathery fronds flourishes in the shade.

The shabby, silver-grey trunks of ash trees are evenly distributed here. Their pinnate foliage provides a contrasting rich, green tone. The air is fresh and the streams of natural light allow ferns to grow thickly on the forest floor. To the east, the forest becomes much thicker and darker, and a solid wall of eerie white birch trees appears to encroach from the south.
21042: A tall and haughty elm stands here.

Though many varieties of trees grow here, they all have the same watchful, menacing appearance. Oak, birch, ash, fir, and chestnut tower above the littered forest floor. Over the ages, the canopy has grown into an unbroken umbrella of foliage, blocking any natural light and making the air dense and oppressive. The forest is motionless, yet the sounds of faint rustlings and whispers can be heard through the leaves. Away to the south, the ground slopes gently down toward a small ditch, and to the northwest a white wall appears through the tree trunks.
21044: A small black cricket is here, chirping loudly.

The endless monotony of the forest is forgotten as the trees give way to the vivid green ferns that populate this clearing. The sudden clear openness and crisp, fresh, sweet-scented air is startling. The feathery ferns, which wave with the slightest breeze, would provide a warm niche to rest in. In the north-west section, numerous fronds have been trampled on and many stems appear to have been broken off. On the borders of the clearing, small branches and twigs stretch out, hustling for any sunlight which streams into the clearing.
21045: A clear pool of water has formed amongst some nearby tree roots.

The canopy has become more open as the trees thin out. The streams of natural light that tumble through provide energy for the thick undergrowth and ferns to thrive. The trees are gnarled and weeping with age, and only the bark which grows beneath the tree's own shade is blemished with pockets of lichen. Fresh air rolls from the clearing to the south and mingles with the stuffy air from the forest. A gentle bubbling sound emanates from a small spring trickling up from the ground.
21046: Overcome by the burden of age, many ancient trees have fallen, and their trunks are now nothing more than rotting ridges across the ground. Their demise brought a chance for rejuvenation and many generations ago new trees took root. These younger trees have now aged and their appearance is shabby and drear. Their branches droop forlornly and a coating of lichen and moss has formed on the trunks and larger limbs. On the ground, knee-high drifts of leaves have accumulated between the decaying ridges.
21047: In ages past, when the forest was young, this was a dynamic and thriving area. Time has now past and the trees have declined into old, sad-looking figures. The lower limbs have broken off, leaving their bare trunks standing like ranks of sombre statues protecting the gloom. No undergrowth has found root among the leaf litter, though insects feast on the nutritious compost and decaying branches.
21048: The forest has become drab and almost lifeless. Trees stand in forlorn silence, as if they are mourning the years when all was brighter and the Entwives brought joy to the forest. Their branches droop heavily, and many have broken off with the burden of countless ages. From these scars sap has oozed out and trickled down the trunks leaving a trail like blood from a wound. The air is dust-laden and stuffy, and movement amongst the leaves is barely noticeable even when a strong breeze blows above the canopy.
21049: Heavy musty air lingers in the overcrowded forest. Low branches hang sadly to the ground making travelling in a straight line impossible. The old trunks are lined with peeling bark and in places sap has seeped from the core of the trees and trickled like tears down their bodies. On the forest floor, a scattering of leaves creates a mottled carpet that crunches when tread upon. The forest extends indefinitely into the monotonous grey gloom of countless trees.
21050: Younger trees flourish amongst the remains of some ancient trees that have taken their eternal rest on the forest floor. What caused the demise of such mighty trees has been buried with the passing of time. The trees that have taken root here show by their dreary, worn appearance that they are still old beyond the years of other forests, and their branches droop forlornly in sad remembrance of their forefathers which lay here.
21051: Long trailing beards of lichen hang profusely from gnarled and leaning trunks. The massive stature of the trees and their wrinkled bark provides only a glimpse of their history and a shadow of their age. Dead leaves stick to the old branches and litter the forest floor. No sign can be seen of any animals living here, though a few insects scurry away at the slightest sound. Breathing is difficult in the musty environment and the hanging lichens and dim surroundings hinder travel.
21052: Saggy old trees prop one against another like a troop of old men needing each other's support. Long, trailing lichens hang from their bodies like scruffy beards and ragged unfallen leaves cling to their branches like unwanted hair. The air is stuffy and heavy with a stale, though not oppressive, woody aroma. The ground is cluttered with dry leaves and numerous broken branches.
21053:
A small centipede is here scurrying about.
An ancient oak is here towering above you.

Majestic oak trees govern this patch of land. Their massive trunks and far-reaching branches give only a glimpse of their former glory. The forest floor, littered with insect-ridden acorns, is pierced irregularly by shafts of light penetrating the laced canopy. The air is crisp here, and the smell of oak is reminiscent of the days when mighty forests stretched far across the lands of Middle-earth. To the east, the forest is lighter and less dense as the undergrowth becomes prominent.
21054: A tall birch is here, watching over the landscape.

The trees here grows closer and more ominous than in neighbouring regions. The warm, brown atmosphere painted by the oaks is overrun by a dominance of chilling, white birch trees. On the ground, a layer of papery leaf-litter has replaced the covering of acorns and the rich scent of oak has deteriorated into a stench of musty decay.
21055: Dense overpopulated thickets of ancient birch trees form a solid, seemingly unbroken, wall to the west and north. The trees stand vigilant and watchful for any intruder. Their bark gleams an unearthly white against the gloomy surroundings and their papery leaves grow so close together that any breeze sends waves of hissing through the dense canopy. About the floor, the forest roots form a maze of obstacles and away to the south a tangle of hoary, old trees can be seen. There seems to be no relief from the dense, stuffy air.
21056: An eerie watchfulness is present here and the menacing trees bend their limbs to follow any movement. The branches hang heavy with thick lichen, dressing the trees in a shabby grey-green mantle. A distinct absence of undergrowth is evidence that only the rarest thread of natural light can pierce the dense canopy. This enveloping cover of foliage traps musty stagnant air, making it difficult to breathe. The forest appears to run endlessly in every direction except to the east where a palisade of eerie white trees barricades the way.
21057: A worm is here slithering around.

Oak trees dominate the forest here. Their smooth reaching branches are dotted with grey-green lichen. On the ground is strewn a multitude of acorns, which crunch loudly underfoot. Each acorn is infested with insects and grubs gnawing away at its contents. Speckles of light come streaming in through a lacy parasol of foliage thirty feet above the forest floor and the air remains stuffy with a heavy earthy scent of oak.
21058: An ancient oak is here towering above you.

Oak trees dominate much of the forest here. Their thick smooth branches are marred by a covering of lichen. A myriad of acorns crack harshly as the hollow, insect ridden nuts crumble underfoot. The spreading canopy forms a lacy parasol thirty feet above the forest floor and speckles of light come streaming through. The air remains stuffy and thick with dust and the heavy, earthy scent of oak. The forest continues in every direction, though the dominance of oaks wanes in the east as the trees become darker.
21059: Ancient trees tower overhead. Long grey lichen-beards trailing from their massive gnarled bodies give them a regal appearance. Although the soil is moist and rich, there is a lack of young growth and saplings due to inadequate light reaching through the dense canopy. The thick, heavy air seems as ancient as the trees themselves.
21060: A cluster of dark green, feathery fronds flourishes in the shade.

Towering old trees lean at various, lopsided angles. Their shabby beards of lichen hang long from their bodies and limbs, giving them a grandfatherly appearance. Dense foliage shows that the aged forest is still healthy and growing, despite the lack of young trees that would thrive if only sufficient light were able to break though the canopy. The stuffy air is almost oppressive and a faint smell of decay rises from the piles of scattered leaves littered on the ground.
21061: An ancient oak is here towering above you.

Though in many places the forest takes on a different character, the trees here are frustratingly monotonous. One more branch to push out of the way, one more root to step over, one more pile of dead leaves to kick away and one more hanging lichen tickling the scalp of any who pass. The unchanging forest provides nothing for nourishment and little of noteworthy interest.
21062:
A bright red mushroom is growing here.
A bright orange bracket fungus grows on some decaying wood.

The trees growing here are in pitiful condition. Their forlorn bodies droop discouragingly and their old withered branches languish sadly. Small twigs stretch out, desperately seeking for the sunlight that seems to have forsaken them. Nothing palatable grows here. The occasional mushroom displays a warning against its consumption and the trees bear no fruit. Many large roots jut out from the base of the trees. They are covered in tacky moss and would be slippery to step on or lean against. The odour of decomposing leaves fills the air and the monotony of the daylight gloom is outweighed only by the pitch black night.
21063: There is no undergrowth to hinder passing, not even a fern. This can be partly explained by the lack of sunlight, it would appear that nothing could penetrate the thick canopy far above. The smells of the different tree species interweave, producing a pleasant, relaxing fragrance. Peering through the dimness, more trees can be seen spreading out in all directions.
21064: A mass of choking bindweed grows here.

On all sides, there are dense trees interspersed with vines and rock piles. The trees are small, almost stunted, as they try to force their roots deep into the wet ground looking for nutrients. The damp earth feels extremely soft underfoot and a stench of decay fills the air. The thickest parts of the forest lie to the east, west, and north. Only the rising ground to the south offers any change in surroundings.
21065: A cluster of dark green, feathery fronds flourishes in the shade.

A sense of stillness and calm fills this area. The trees here are not troubled by any wind so the leaves and branches remain motionless and silent. The ferns growing in the thicket provide a burst of greenery in contrast to the dark matting of dead leaves covering the ground. To the west the forest thins slightly while the closely packed trees stretch as far as the eye can see in other directions.
21066: A group of tree stumps dominate the centre of the path. The stumps vary quite dramatically in girth. The smallest is less than seven inches across while the largest measures two feet. On each of the stumps a number of axe marks can be clearly seen. The cuts do not appear to lie in neat lines, whoever cut these trees either did so in a hurry or lacked the skill to fell them with more care. Around these stumps several deep furrows have been made in the soft earth. The furrows lie along the line of the avenue as if heavy items had once been dragged along here.
21067: This is the fringe of a lighter, less populated part of the forest. To the east a number of trees can be seen clustered together as if in a regimented line. The fragrance of fresh flowers and herbs drifts in from the north.
21068: A tangly shrub seems to rustle as if alert to its surroundings.

The land here is flat and open, gorse bushes and shrubs outnumber the trees that are struggling to grow in the sandy soil. There is little to distract the eye from the monotony of stunted trees. To the north the trees thicken slightly.
21069: The land here is far less fertile than in the forest to the north. The trees are smaller and more widely spaced, allowing much more sunlight to reach the forest floor. Scattered around are several piles of dried brushwood and leaves. With each footstep upon the ground a loud cracking sound can be heard.
21070: The tunnel ceiling is barely six feet high in the centre, taller travellers are forced to stoop in order to gain access to the darker recesses. Very little light reaches this place, making it difficult to see exactly how the chamber was created. What is obvious is that it is made entirely of natural materials, as if the trees had been bent and forced to grow into certain shapes.
21071: A huge millipede is writhing around here.

The trees crowd around the valley sides, blocking any sunlight from reaching the depths of the valley far below. Movement here is difficult as the sheer number of roots and fallen branches impede progress. Climbing out of the valley to the east looks to be impossible, a solid wall of wood blocks any movement that way. To the south the gully continues.
21072: As the valley opens out to the south, the same kind of plain trees that populate this area can be seen far to the south. While the surroundings does not offer any spectacular botanic impressions, the near complete lack of undergrowth makes way for unhindered movement.
21073: An ancient oak is here towering above you.

Tall, straight, silver-bark trees, reminiscent of the ash, grow at the foot of a hill. Off to the west, scattered groups of trees can be seen lining the ridge as it climbs towards the horizon. In the evening these trees block the light as the sun sets, casting this small grove into a premature grey dusk.
21074: A spiky broomrape plant pokes its blooms out of the soil.

As the ground slopes gently upwards, the predominance of rowan trees gives way to hardy evergreens. At the base of the trees, the twigs stretch out as if searching for the warm sunlight. Further up the slope to the west, the ground becomes increasingly stony.
21075: Some ugly blow-flies are buzzing around here.

This area of the forest is populated almost entirely by rowan trees. One tree in particular stands out, at thirty feet high, it stands tall above the smaller ones that surround it. To the west a rocky slope leads up to a ridge while to the east the forest becomes noticeably thicker.
21076: A colony of red ants is here. The ants seem to ignore you.

The trees here tower high above. One of the older ones has branches drooping low to the ground, and the number of ants and beetles emerging from within its trunk indicates that it may be rotten. The forest continues in all directions.
21077:
A tall and haughty elm stands here.
A dense carpet of blue flowers dip their heads in the breeze.

Amid the boggy ground several clumps of trees can be seen. The forest is less dense here and further to the east the trees completely vanish, resulting in a clearing. A large number of flowers grow here, giving the area a peculiar odour.
21078: A Clearing Deep within the Forest

Fangorn is surrounding this clearing that is composed of little more than some grass and brushwood. An excessive amount of water has caused a flooding in the western edge of the clearing. The water emerging from the soggy, saturated ground is brown and has a musty but sharp smell.
21079: Very little light enters here. The branches of neighbouring trees have grown together, creating a natural ceiling and casting the forest floor into darkness. Some ivy is making a vain attempt to grow far enough to reach what little sunlight may penetrate the forest canopy.
21080: A tall birch is here, watching over the landscape.

Ancient oak trees stand here, their trunks penetrating the forest canopy and their roots burrowing deep into the earth. These oaks have clearly grown here for many decades, perhaps even hundreds of years. Around the base of these magnificent trees a kind of dark, glossy shrub, resembling a type of thornless holly, clings to the trunks.
21081: There is a very noticeable change in the forest here. To the east, the trees grow close, their high-reaching branches knotting and twisting together to form a kind of wooden ceiling. In years long past, the forest there would have been glorious, supporting varieties of wildlife now gone from the Fangorn forever. Further to the west, the trees have fared better. Their old boughs supporting many leafy branches, however, there is a sense of unhappiness that cannot be fully explained. It is almost as if the trees are grieving for the loss of the Entwives all those years ago.
21082: A wall of tangled roots blocks the way to the north. It would take a large group of skilled woodsmen many days to clear a path through the twisted wood. An easier path presents itself to the west and south. The forest to the east appears dark. Forcing a path between the dreary, almost lifeless, rowan trees will be tiring work.
21083: A very heavy branch is lying here on the ground.

The lack of natural light reaching through the thick mass of branches growing across the ceiling, prevents the growth of anything save the lichen clinging to the drab and cheerless trees. The forest floor is littered with debris, broken twigs and dry branches. Clearly, nothing has disturbed them for many years.
21084: A tall birch is here, watching over the landscape.

All around, the view is blocked by the darkened trunks of trees. Branches grow thick and heavily laden with foliage forming a natural barrier blocking out the rays of the sun. It is cold here and the silence creates a sombre atmosphere. It is obvious that very little happens here. The trees are bounded on all sides by more dark and uninviting thickets.
21085: Old and twisted trees stand here as a sad reminder that the forest has suffered years of neglect. The nearest oak has sap weeping like tears from its ageing, scarred trunk. Travel in a straight line is impossible, the trees grow too close together. Between the ancient boughs, several large pines stand tall as if on guard, ready to right the wrongs of years past.
21086:
A round tangle with waxy leaves and white berries grows on a branch nearby.
A mass of wriggling vines drops on you from the trees.
Some thick writhing vines whip all around you.
A small termite is running around making strange sounds.

Small gaps in the canopy send shafts of light piercing through the dimness. The light has caused thick creepers and vines to take hold here, a tighter and more fierce hold than anywhere else in the forest. Movement between the trees is very difficult, the undergrowth must be fought every step of the way.
21087: The surrounding forest now seems to be getting lighter. Through the trees, it is possible to see something of what is beyond them, however, the forest is still dark enough not to reveal all its secrets. From deep within the forest, to the south, a rustling sound can be heard, but nothing save more trees is to be seen.
21088: Fir and rowan trees jostle for position. The smaller rowans are concentrated mainly on the western side of the dip leaving the firs to spread their roots on the eastern edge. A feeble trickle of water meanders its way around the boughs feeding little more than few drips a minute into a large puddle in the centre of the depression. The fragrance of the two varieties of tree fights with the smell emanating from the stagnant water.
21089: Standing here, it becomes apparent that the area is cold because the dense canopy of leaves above blocks out nearly all of the sunlight. What little light does manage to pierce the barrier casts long eerie shadows. Wildlife does not seem to favour this place, there is little evidence of any creatures living in the trees here.
21092: A tall birch is here, watching over the landscape.

The forest surrounding this area has grown taller and appears more densely packed than the trees that stand here. At the base of several trees grow a variety of fungi and lichen. They seem to be taking advantage of the increased sunlight this area enjoys during the day.
21093: The forest stops abruptly to the north. The distinctive glint of still water can just be made out in the clearing to the north, but nothing else is remarkable. On the ground, numerous insects are at work slowly cutting, moving and eating the dead leaves that lie about.
21094: A huge millipede is writhing around here.

The trees here surround a natural hollow within which the remains of an old camp can be seen. It seems that whoever rested here did not wait very long as they do not appear to have made a fire. Around the edge of the hollow a number of small flowers carpet the ground. Looking further, the forest stretches as far as the eye can see in all directions.
21095: In the Shade of an Oak
A small cluster of clover grows here.

Under the sprawling branches of this large oak tree the air is cool. The leaves of the tree are sheltering the ground from the sun and create a soft green shadow. The ground is blanketed with thick grass and the occasional flowering shrub giving the area a fresh, airy feeling despite the lack of natural light.
21096: A mass of low-spreading shrub quivers on the ground.

There is a faint scent lingering here. A smell of fresh grass, a reminder of summer. The trees here are younger than most in this forest, the usual dimness of the deep forest does not permeate here. Instead, a soft green glow bathes the area in a cold light during the day and at night the moon makes each tree shine as it plays its silver beams across the bark.
21097: Flanked by a pair of towering willow trees, the path to the south leads into a dark tunnel. The tunnel is made out of living wood, the branches of the willow trees intertwining themselves to provide shelter. Looking deeper into the tunnel, an aisle of trees can barely be discerned amid the gloom. How much further this passage extends cannot be guessed at.
21098: A rooting heap of stems is here, smothering the smaller plants.

Each footstep is muffled by the mat of rotting leaves that covers the dark forest floor. A smell of decay hangs in the air, overpowering the scent of the flowers that are growing in the rich soil. To the south and east the forest gets lighter, and thus allowing for at least a little light to enter.
21099: Some ugly blow-flies are buzzing around here.

Fallen trees restrict movement on all sides. The only gap visible in the dense woodland is to the north. On all sides the towering pine trees give the area an oppressive feeling, standing tall and mighty, they unremittingly watch over the forest and its visitors.
21100: The trees here are so huge, their uppermost branches appear to reach into the clouds. The view around is blocked by the large number of trunks that have grown close together. To the south the forest is but a dark shape, very little can be seen in that direction.
21101:
A huge millipede is writhing around here.
A small termite is running around making strange sounds.

The sky above the forest roof is completely obscured from sight, only the leaves and branches of the surrounding trees can be seen. Glancing over the southern trees, trying to discern what lies in the shadows, the branches shift slightly.
21102: The trees here have a rich, deep black bark closely resembling polished leather. In the centre of this area the trees seem to cluster together as if for warmth or protection.
