Passing between them there is a sense of stifling that leaves as quickly as it came. Even at the outer edge of the trees an uncomfortable feeling of being watched remains.
21103: A rooting heap of stems is here, smothering the smaller plants.

Sturdy oak trees have put their roots deep into the soil and now stand here proud and tall. Around the base of the trees, a few crushed stems indicate that some wildlife may have rested here recently, however, there is no sign of it now. Looking further into the forest, paths lead off to the north, west and south.
21104: The forest here is old, very old. Several trees have fallen down, and their trunks lie here, the size of them testament to the long life that the trees have led. Small termites are at work burrowing into the dead wood. Despite the number of old fallen trees, this part of the forest is certainly not dying. Dotted around are many young saplings, being much smaller than the old trees they are growing to replace, the forest appears more open here than elsewhere. In a few more years this area will have regained much of its former glory.
21105: The trees that grow here are much less mature than the others in the forest. Whereas the older trees jostle for position, the young saplings that grow here enjoy a great deal of space. Further south the forest appears to be stunted while to the east the trees stop completely.
21106:
A small cluster of clover grows here.
A mass of low-spreading shrub quivers on the ground.

The forest gives way to an area of open, fertile ground. Many different types of plants grow here as if it was once a well-tended herb garden. The fragrance of fresh lavender and clover fills the air, a refreshing change from some of the other smells in the forest. Surrounding the clearing on all sides, Fangorn stretches out into the distance.
21107: Dominating the landscape here is a graceful archway, formed by intertwining branches, leading to the north. It is hard to make out what lies in the darkness there. However, the grandeur of the entrance suggests that it was once an important place. In recent times the arch has fallen into disrepair, weeds and dead twigs have piled up to block the entrance. It would take some work to clear a path large enough to squeeze through.
21108: Massive oak trees have taken over this area of the forest. The dry ground is covered with roots, twisting and turning as they seek out fertile soil. Each tree has a light, hairy covering, presumably some form of moss. On the eastern edge of the oak grove a huge pile of dead branches and brushwood has collected. Further south the ground is littered with rocks and boulders.
21109: Standing tall as if on guard duty, old hoary oak trees are clustered together here, their large buttress roots reaching deep into the earth. Underfoot, a blanket of crisp, dry leaves and acorns amplifies the noise of every footstep. The covering appears to be relatively undisturbed indicating that there is little traffic through this part of the forest. There is no sign of any living creature, even the soil appears to be dusty and infertile. Only the fungal growths on some of the older trees seem to thrive in these conditions. To the south, a wall of solid wood prevents any further travel.
21110: A brown striated fungus hangs here, clinging to a tree trunk.

Many rowan trees stand here, reaching only fourteen feet into the air, the lower branches droop low to the ground impeding the passage of all but the smallest. Clinging to the branches are a variety of leaves, some with a healthy rich green colour and others appearing a shade of dull yellow, dead and withered. All around, larger trees encircle this quiet woodland.
21111: Densely packed, towering fir trees grow here, leaving little room for the the younger rowans to grow. The lower branches of the firs are covered with dry, brown needles, and small twigs carpet the ground, muffling the sound of footfalls. A few slugs try to survive, clinging to the dark areas under stones.
21112: The ground here slopes down to what looks like an earthen bowl to the south. While traversable, each step must be carefully planned in order for one not to lose their footing. A thick wall of huge trees and ferns stand on the eastern side of the incline, with a bit of effort however, it is possible force a path that way.
21113: A cluster of dark green, feathery fronds flourishes in the shade.

These trees are spaced just enough to allow a few beams of light to enter, bathing the ground in a pale light and casting long shadows under the boughs. The local flora has taken advantage of the favourable conditions and the grove is awash in a great sea of ferns. The grove continues to the north, the other directions all lead into darker areas.
21114: At the Edge of a Dark Dale

The trees grow close to each other, letting little light enter the undergrowth. Only a few green ferns struggle to grow among the huge trunks, but their future is as dark as the surroundings. Something seems to move in the shadows, although looking deeper into the dale where the movement seemingly occurred reveals only trees, there is nothing there.
21115: At the base of the depression, the ground opens out into a large bowl shape. In the centre a small group of oaks are clustered together, a thin mist swirling around their base. Vines have covered some of the trees, they have become thick enough to make it impossible to see through the gaps between adjacent trees.
21116:
A solid, but stunted, rowan tree has established itself here.
On the rowan, there are a cluster of rowan berries.

All is silent below the canopy, and no single leaf or branch moves. The air is still and smells of decay. The rowans come to an abrupt end at the sloping depression to the east but ancient oaks and pines take over, filling the space and continuing the forest without changing its shape.
21117: Standing at the foot of this tree, one could be overwhelmed by its sheer size. It would take nearly thirty man-sized paces to encircle it at the base. The bark of the tree bears a number of odd marks, which seem unlikely to have been made by nature. While the true cause of the scarring cannot be determined, it is certain that this tree would have its fair share of stories to tell. Around the base of the tree great clumps of grass grow up among the roots.
21118: A spiky broomrape plant pokes its blooms out of the soil.

Two lines of silver-bark birch trees flank a wide avenue in the forest. Filling the space, a bed of soft green grass has grown. Here and there a few tree stumps erupt through the sea of green indicating that trees have once stood where there is now just cold empty space. To the north an impressive oak tree can be seen, framed in the gap between the birches.
21119: A majestic scots pine grows tall and straight here.

Rising from the bogs and mire, these rounded knolls are densely blanketed with a multitude of fragrant evergreens. Despite the poor soil they are growing in, the trees have prospered, their massive boughs supporting a network of branches far above. Under the protective canopy some frail looking green ferns struggle to push through the layer of pine needles.
21120: Small, dried fallen branches and pine needles crackle underneath the feet of travellers throughout this dense forest of huge trees. Above, the branches are so intertwined that nearly no light filters through them. Despite the dim light and entangled trees, the grove carries the fresh smell of pine resin, a change from the usual musty air. To the south, the forest becomes more dense and gloomy.
21121: A tall pine tree grows here.

This grove is a cold but peaceful area of the forest. The trees, mostly pines, cast deep, dark shadows all around, not allowing much natural light to seep in. Although the forest seems peaceful and empty, a sense of something present can be discerned, a sense of life among the trees.
21122: A tangly shrub seems to rustle as if alert to its surroundings.

The gaps between the trees grow smaller, the trees tower high above and the air is musty and stale. There is a claustrophobic feel to the forest here, it is not a pleasant place to linger in for too long. There is a loud rustling sound accompanying every footstep as the blanket of leaves covering the ground is disturbed. To the west lies a dark and foreboding area of the forest.
21123: The carpet of leaves that covers the ground conceals damp, black soil. No smaller vegetation, other than mosses and lichens, has managed to exist here. The forest is silent save for the occasional rustling of leaves as the wind catches them. Despite the silent, peaceful appearance, the presence of something else can be distinguished, of something moving in the shadows.
21124:
A tall pine tree grows here.
A low shrub with bright green, oblong leaves is growing here.
Scattered in and on the shrub, there are two piles of blueberries.

As the forest climbs the slope, the pine trees seem to grow in stature too. Thick brown bark covers the trunks, the age of the trees given away by the number of long, sticky trails of sap clinging to the massive trunks. The smell of pine is overpowering, a refreshing change to the usual damp, musty air in the rest of the forest. Dark shapes are moving slowly among the trees off to the east.
21125: The gap in the trees runs north-south from here. Bordering the area are birch trees, standing in neat rows as if part of some army guarding over Fangorn. The bark of the trees shines in the pale light admitted through the break in the forest canopy. Clumps of ferns surround the base of the nearest trees and yet traces of stale, musty air remain, overpowering the scent of growing plants.
21126: Here the forest is mostly ash and wych elm. The once smooth, thin bark of the elms peels off in thin, grey-green strips that litter the forest floor. Their branches do not droop as much as that of the other trees, as they are thinner and have less weight to bring them down. The key-shaped samaras of the trees flutter, in slow spirals, towards the infertile ground.
21127: An ash tree with mottled bark stands here apparently guarding its surroundings.

A variety of trees have taken root here, their branches growing strongly toward the sun. Many new saplings can even be seen attempting to grow in the already compact forest. The trees here appear to be amongst the tallest in the forest. This is in stark contrast to the dark patch of forest just to the north.
21128:
A spiky broomrape plant pokes its blooms out of the soil.
The embodied shape of a linden tree stands shiftlessly here.

Several birches have clustered together here in a thick group. A few oaks and several firs have attempted to join the cluster but have been entirely rebuffed. The trees here appear all healthy, the branches being strong and the leaves firmly attached. The roots here are all well planted in the fertile soil, endowing the trees with great stability and strength.
21129: A dense foliage of ferns and woodland grasses cover the forest floor beneath the canopy of interlocking branches. Distinctive leaves of the oak cover the limbs of these trees, as well as the great multitude of their fallen brethren lying in different states of decomposition amongst the forest litter.
21130: A bright orange bracket fungus grows on some decaying wood.

Large colourful toadstools form a striking component of the woodland flora. Moss-covered twisted trunks strike crab-like poses, with claw-like branches reaching out to grab at you. The tangled trunks and branches of birch, oak and ash support colonies of young puffballs and sulphur tuft mushrooms.
21131:
The remains of a tangly shrub lie here in a heap of rotting compost.
A tangly shrub seems to rustle as if alert to its surroundings.
The embodied shape of a linden tree stands shiftlessly here.
The embodied shape of a linden tree stands shiftlessly here.

An overly congested canopy of dark ash and twisted oak creates a dusky gloom, unbroken by any intrusion of the sky above. An overbearing stuffiness makes breathing difficult as the trees crowd around, limiting free movement and imposing a claustrophobic environment.
21132: Hart's tongue ferns, with their light shiny green colour and broad, strap-like fronds fill the undergrowth around you. The ground here is moist and the oak and ash canopy is thick overhead, making for a particularly well shaded area of woodland. To the north of here, an opening in the trees is just visible.
21133: At a slight earthen rise in the forest landscape, large cushions of pale green moss and intermingling liverwort form the major components of the forest floor. The moss is damp and springy underfoot, despite the general dryness of the slope. The spread of the trees is more open here, allowing more light reach the ground.
21134: Much of the oak and ash forest in this area is initially difficult to distinguish. An encrusting lungwort, one of the largest species of lichen, conceals the trees distinctive coloration and hides their textures beneath a cloak of bright greens, reddish oranges and brownish growths.
21135: A Slight Gap in the Forest

An ash tree with mottled bark stands here apparently guarding its surroundings.
A colony of red ants is here. The ants seem to ignore you.

As the ground slowly rises to the west, the oak and ash woodland gets steadily thicker until it becomes interspersed with pine in higher grounds. The mist-shrouded outline of a great mountain range can be seen far to the west through a slight gap in the trees.
21136: A great watchful silence hangs over this area as the forest mourns its fallen kin. Great boughs and the trunks of more than one fallen leviathan mark a great tragedy in some distant time. The remaining giants standing here are wide and tall, their bark ghostly grey and their trailing beards of lichen and ivy the only testament of life.
21137: Wood sorrels and anemones intersperse with primroses, tangles of brambles and the occasional hazel, all within a great grassed clearing in the forest. Such a vast empty space surrounded by the all-encompassing canopy of the forest seems most strange.
21138: Ancient oak and the occasional pale-skinned birch mingle here, their twisted branches now sporting a covering of dusty lichens in place of the papery leaf litter that rustles underfoot with every step. A pungent, dusty odour overlays the senses, irritating the nose and throat with every laboured breath of stagnant air.
21139: A very heavy branch is lying here on the ground.

A thick dark gloom of reaching, grasping and knotted branches hangs over the twisted and deformed landscape. A dank dusty scent fills the air, dulling the senses and casting a heavy lethargy. The gnarly trunks and boughs of the trees seem to almost move on their own accord, snarling and grabbing as you pass.
21140: The slender supple trunks of irregularly shaped silver birch grow here beneath an over-canopy of oak woodland. Densely-packed, green-leafed ferns carpet the forest floor together with an occasional deep drift of papery crisp leaves. Here the snow-white branches of the birch show a scattering of fresh dark green leaves, whilst overhead the towering oak branches are mostly bare of new growth. To the east the land slopes down into a darker region of the forest.
21141: An Unhealthy Part of the Forest

Oak, fir, and birch grow thickly here. To the north-east, the health of the trees drastically declines. Their limbs have begun to droop, their leaves blackened and shed from their twisted limbs, which have become frail and brittle. Blackened mouldy roots twist and rise out of the ground, creating a dangerous path for travellers, whilst a foul stench overwhelms the senses.
21142: A Sickly Patch of Ash Trees
A tall birch is here, watching over the landscape.

Once proud ash is now wasted away, victim of whatever sickness plagues the trees in this area. Many of the thickest branches in this grove have at some point become too weak to support their own weight and have snapped. They now hang down by long strips of ash-grey bark, or lie on the ground like the blackened bones of giants.
21143: The rowan trees that still grow here must have been thirty foot tall at the height of their splendour. Now their limbs droop lazily towards the ground, sapped of strength by the spreading sickness in this part of the forest. The leaves of the trees are faded from their once healthy colour to a diseased, mottled brown. A thickening mist covers the ground, making the roots of the trees hard to discern.
21144: A giant and ancient yew stands here quite eerily.

The ground slopes steeply down towards the east. The oaks are not as tall or straight as in the lowlands. They are more gnarled, the boughs dip lower, and more of the sky can be seen. Little or no wildlife can be seen and little can be heard except the occasional sighing of the wind in the branches overhead. The forest seems still and watchful.
21145: The ground, thickly forested in oaks and ashes, slopes noticeably toward the north and east, giving a vague feeling of disorientation, as there is no opportunity to see the horizon. Looking downhill through the ranks of trunks is like staring into a deep pool; no bottom can be seen, only shadow. The soil is firm, dry, and somewhat stony.
21146: Great oaks surround you on all sides. In whichever direction you look, a seemingly endless multitude of trunks and boughs stretches into the dim and shadowed distance. The black, rich earth is covered with a thick layer of oak leaves from autumns past. Little vegetation grows between the great trunks. These monarchs of the forest are greedy and the canopy of their branches consumes too much light for weeds and saplings to thrive.
21147:
Yellow flowers, with grey-green foliage, grow in clusters here.
An imposing beech tree sways gently in the wind.

Wood sedges populated intermittently by various wild orchids grow through the general scrub of the woodland blanket. The deep shade provided by the seemingly ageless oaks, casts a primeval feeling over this quiet glade. Ragged, dry leaves hang from many of the branches, giving an impression that this part of the forest pays no heed to the changing seasons of the world outside.
21148: A selection of tufted and large flowering dark green grasses loosely carpet the open beech wood floor. The trees form a canopy, providing a fair amount of shade beneath their branches. Patches of the sky may be seen peeking through the forest ceiling.
21149: The trunks of the pine trees, predominant in this area, are cast into constant shadow by the thick, green canopy. Layers of thin branches stand out at right angles to the trunks, whilst needle-like leaves cover both the branches and the forest floor beneath you. The surrounding air is perfumed with an ageless scent of pine. A steady rumbling sound can often be heard from the north.
21151: A majestic scots pine grows tall and straight here.

This area of the forest consists of a number of stunted pine trees on the rough craggy slopes of an outlying portion of the mountains, barely visible far to the west. Here some height allows one to look out over the vast expanse of forest, which stretches off into the horizon as far as the eyes can see. A steady rumble of thunder emanates from the south as a waterfall plummets from a fast moving river.
21152: This part of the forest is slightly sunken compared to the rest of the area. However, the decline in altitude has not affected the growth of the trees, and in fact, many tall and ancient oak trees cover the land. The heavy mist lays thick around everything, as can be expected when the entire forest is covered in it. The ways north and west are completely blocked by a sharp incline in the land. The ways east and south have a much more gradual incline.
21153:
A low shrub with bright green, oblong leaves is growing here.
Scattered in and on the shrub, there are two piles of blueberries.
Some roots lie here waiting to ensnare weary travellers.

The forest here mainly consists of large oak and beautiful white birch trees. A thick layer of mist covers the forest floor, and from time to time, a green glow from the light of the sun or moon filters through the canopy of the trees, bringing a dim light to the area. Thick tree roots cover the forest floor, and somehow some small bushes have managed to grow in the area. A wall of these bushes blocks the way west, while in all other directions, the forest continues.
21154: Inside the Border of the Forest

The forest is quite dark here, especially considering the proximity to the open plains to the north. A large black rock is the only marker in the sea of grass in that direction. Covering the forest floor is a tangle of roots from the various types of trees that grow in this part of the forest, and the fog that always lies upon Fangorn Forest is not as pervasive here. The forest continues to the south and east.
21155: The golden grass here rushes to meet the green borders of the forest just to the south. All seems to be relatively quiet in the expanse of prairie here, however, a quiet humming sound can be faintly heard from the south. To the east, an arm of the forest extends out into the prairie, and to the north, a huge black rock sits in the middle of the grass.
21156: Surrounded by tall prairie grass, with a stretch of forest to the east, this large rock seems completely out of place. No moss attempts to cover its ancient black surface. Almost thirty feet in diameter, the rock is impossible to move, and seems to be made of a rare and unusual black stone.
21157: A Small Rise in the Prairie

At this point, the prairies seem to be fighting their way towards the sun, their source of life. The rise onto which they climb seems to be some ancient remnants of yet another arm of the great Misty Mountains that was cast down ages ago. To the south, a large dark shape can be made out, lying flat on the ground.
21158: A Small Rise in the Prairie
An opossum stands here, sniffing around the ground.

The golden grass here has risen onto a small rise in defiance of its counterparts covering the eastern landscape. To the south, the rise continues, while to the north, a small valley houses a grove of trees. The shadow of the Misty Mountains seems to have avoided this place.
21159:
A tall pine tree grows here.
A restless rabbit bounces around.

Just below the foothills, this small grove stands in a shallow valley. Signs of life can barely be seen here, as a small bird skirts from one tree to another. This might be a great place to stop and rest before continuing through the prairies and foothills that rise all around.
21160: A trained horse is standing here, ridden by you.

The foothills seem to be alive with grass. The sounds of grazing animals and birds can be heard from time to time. In the shadow of the great Misty Mountains the lands are devoid of civilization, making this place a haven for wildlife.
21161: A small animal, all covered in spines, snuffles amongst the undergrowth.

All around, the fields seem very inviting and warm to the soul. The fair green grass looks as if it had been spared the trampling of feet and hoofs. To the south, there are foothills continuing to a small grove of trees. The land to the east seems to run on forever as the grass there takes on a golden colour.
21162: Grass-covered fields stretch out as far as the eye can see. Some bushes also grow in small groves around the plains. Flowers of countless colours give the fields a contrast to the bright green grass. To the south, another set of foothills begins to slope upwards leading to the mountains further away in that direction.
21163: A field mouse noses about hungrily, searching for food.

Vibrant grass grows all around on this field in varying shades of green. A few clumped-up bush formations break the monotony of the knee-high grass. Some trees stand in the middle of the bushes, looking like statues of some sort. The greenery seems to continue as a far as the eye can see, like a flowing carpet of grass.
21164: Dark green grass covers these bushy fields. Below, their healthy roots grow in the rich soil. A variety of shrubs and bushes grow in scattered clumps and its own formations, berry plants being the most prominent kind of all. Tiny insects seem to be feeding on the surrounding flora, and their constant buzz often drifts on passing winds.
21165:
A small black cricket is here, chirping loudly.
A small black cricket is here, chirping loudly.

Broad blades of verdant grass cover these fields. Small bushes of sun-dried green and brown hues contrast the brighter colour of the grass. Small groves of younger trees grow here and there on the grassland, offering shelter and a resting place for passing travellers. A few rocky boulders lie scattered over the grass, having been parted from the mountains to the north.
21166:
An angry bee is here, collecting nectar from all the flowers of the garden.
A colourful butterfly is fluttering around here.

Protruding rocks and pebbles dominate this high slope that leads northwards towards the mountain peak above. The hills are bare and covered with dirt and flint, offering a small chance for plants to root. A few stunted trees have managed to push their roots into the rocky surface, feeding on the remaining soil in the cracks of the stone. Crabgrass and some other shrubs grow here and there, shivering in passing winds. To the south, the barren landscape seems to give way to healthy grassland.
21167: This is the highest point of the surrounding mountain range. Pebbles and rock flint cover the heavily sloping cliff, making it hard to traverse. A quick glance southwards over the surrounding lands gives an excellent view over the bush-filled grassland and small coppices, which dot the calm landscape.
21168: A rooting heap of stems is here, smothering the smaller plants.

Decrepit ancient trees weakly reach towards the dim light of the covered sky far overhead, while paper-like brown leaves occasionally show on their brittle twigs and branches. Here the cycle of life has stalled and passed the forest by, the seasons forgotten. A long drawn out twilight remains. To the west the trees stretch alongside the base of a steep rise, preventing easy travel.
21169: A Tangle of Ferns and Nettles
A rooting heap of stems is here, smothering the smaller plants.

The forest cover here is dense but not complete and where light has trickled through the canopy, a wild undergrowth of tangled nettles and towering ferns covers the forest floor. As one passes through the undergrowth, no trails exists to follow, nor are bare patches of relief to be seen.
21170: A majestic scots pine grows tall and straight here.

Gnarled and twisted branches overlap and intertwine here as great oak and large leaved lime make passage difficult and strenuous. The air smells musty, feels thick with age and seems to weigh you down. The closeness of everything in this forest threatens to strangle the breath of any traveller.
21171: A dense canopy overhangs this part of the forest, trapping thick, stuffy air that smothers every breath. Dried, withered, brown leaves hang from the heavy aged branches and gnarled, twisted, finger-like twigs of the ancient oak. The constant rustle of dried leaf litter accompanies your every footfall, breaking the cloister-like silence of the forest.
21172: On the Edge of a Depression

Woodland beeches stand along the top of a steeply sloping depression leading down into the east. At the top of this slope the trees are old and worn, with browned dried-up leaves and wreaths of trailing lichens. Most are still hale and deeply rooted, although in contrast, the trees in the dark depression below are mottled and sickly looking greatly at odds with the remainder of the forest.
21173: A brown striated fungus hangs here, clinging to a tree trunk.

The forest here seems to be suffering from some kind of ailment. A foul scent rides the air, wafted along by a light mist as the ground slopes down from the north and west. Sick as the trees here seem to be, to the east they are even further along in whatever malady is spreading through this part of the forest.
21174: The limbs of these feeble, sagging trees droop sadly towards the ground, as if the forest here has lost the will to live. Bark peels back from the trunks and roots of the trees, exposing sickly looking decaying wood beneath. A low, obscuring mist covers the ground, making it hard to avoid tripping over knotted roots and sudden hollows.
21175: An enormous, brooding, black oak looms overhead upon a great bole on knotted roots. Its gnarled bark appears charred, but on closer inspection is extremely leathery and tough. A huge twisted mass of roots creep and crawl in every direction from the base of the tree, snarling underfoot. The oak's thick, dark limbs reach out to grasp at you like the bony hands of death, as it deeply shadows the glade around its base.
21176: A Poisoned Grove of Oak Trees

Tall, sick oak trees populate this area of the forest. The trees are dying, their leaves coloured with sickly mottled colours and blackened edges. Above all hangs a reek of some indefinable odour. A light mist dips down into the lower parts of the forest, making it hard to walk without tripping over unseen roots.
21177:
A brown striated fungus hangs here, clinging to a tree trunk.
A tall and haughty elm stands here.
A black alder looms threateningly over its surroundings.

The dying leaves of the blackened twisted trees emit an extremely sickly odour. The smell of death wafts through the air, carried by a light mist that cloaks the forest floor. The mist has a soft, green glow to it, very faint yet eerily distracting.
21178: A Small Drop in the Forest

The floor of the forest descends steeply towards the south and the east. The trees here grow straight and strong, even where the slope of the forest floor falls sharply. Looking over the edge of a small cliff, you see trees that look as if they have died. The leaves of the trees have fallen and their limbs appear weak. A malodorous smell reeks in from the south and east.
21179:
A solid, but stunted, rowan tree has established itself here.
On the rowan, there are a cluster of rowan berries.

Oak, rowan, ash and fir together with a plethora of other plant-life grow here. Natural light is filtered down through overlapping layers of tree canopy interspersed with bearded lichens and trailing vines. A musty, heavy scent overwhelms the senses, forcing one to take deep breaths to get past the stuffiness of the air.
21180:
A small termite is running around making strange sounds.
A small termite is running around making strange sounds.
A colony of red ants is here. The ants seem to ignore you.

Laid down to rest among auburn-gold sheets of delicate leaves and musty loam, to bathe in a pool of fungal kisses, arms poised with early-light gestures, a once majestic giant lies now at rest. Its forest brethren stand apart, a respectful distance from their fallen comrade, their mournful tears of respect the steady fall of faded weather-worn leaves.
21181:
A brown striated fungus hangs here, clinging to a tree trunk.
A tall, slender hornbeam Ent walks around here, keeping watch over his trees.

The heavy scent of ancient wood and musty earth labours breathing in this thickly overlapping and mixed woodland. Ancient oak intermingled with ash, elder, hornbeam and birch stand tall and massive, old beyond belief, wreathed in aged leaves and trailing thick ivy. The trees seem to be almost aware of your presence, making them appear watchful and wary.
21182: An abundance of dead wood lies at your feet, moss shrouded and rotting with the passing of the seasons. A steadily thickening stand of oak and beech gives evidence that new woodland has slowly replaced the fallen monoliths that provide such a fine meal to the beetles and termites that feast here.
21183:
A giant and ancient yew stands here quite eerily.
An ash tree with mottled bark stands here apparently guarding its surroundings.

Short grasses carpet the ground, covering the fallen branches of ages past. The ash, oak and beech woodland is quiet and dull, the sky obscured within its densely packed folds. A musty scent of great age overwhelms the senses.
21184: An imposing beech tree sways gently in the wind.

Holly and ivy are to be found in great masses, growing here with wild abandon amongst the oak woodland so prevalent in this part of the forest. Plant-life neither flowers in this ageless wood, nor shows its fruit, perhaps due to the heavily shaded conditions imposed by the dense foliage overhead.
21185: In a dell in the greater forested landscape, a natural spring has been cleverly captured so as to cascade down over a series of moss-covered boulders before playfully splashing over the stones into a small pool formed by huge, carefully placed rocks. The trees overhead, and to three sides, appear to cradle the pool and spring, growing around the pool and almost providing a crude shelter.
21186: On a slight rise in the forest, a group of aged pine stands out from the predominant oak and ash. The great age of the trees here is evident in their girth, thick bark and the long trails of sticky scented sap that have fallen over many years in a long trail down their immense trunks. To the west the pine gives way to a densely packed multitude of species, forming a natural barrier to travel.
21187: Silvery-grey barked trees standing over ninety foot in height stand here, interspersed with more common ash and sycamore. These strongly rooted trees have hard yellow-white heartwood and unlike their more numerous kin, the common elm, that have toothed leaves, distinguishing them as wych elm.
21188: Great trailing beards of lichen hang from massive ancient trees, blowing and swaying in the breeze. Dim light trickles down through the wildly dancing branches overhead. Mosses cover the roots and climb the trunks of the great trees, whilst everywhere one looks, a multi-coloured leaf patchwork of green and brown, yellow and orange rustles at your feet.
21189: All colours have faded from the weatherworn leaves here. Few still tenaciously cling to the tree, although they have mostly shrivelled and dried. Having reached the final stage of life, many relinquish their hold on the ancient trees and succumb to the pressures of age. A gentle breeze catches them one by one, nudging them in spirals as they flutter and float to the ground.
21190: While standing amongst intermingled oak and poplar all in fair health, it is hard to imagine what can be wrong with the great swathe of forest that lies dark and twisted below to the south and east of here. A foul, malodorous, sickly stench rises from the forest, stinging the eyes and gagging the throat.
21191:
A tall and haughty elm stands here.
Some roots lie here waiting to ensnare weary travellers.
Some roots lie here waiting to ensnare weary travellers.

Deeply wrinkled trunks and branches whirl in knotted tangles where fallen branches stretch no more. This once hale woodland has succumbed to an unnatural blight, which hangs heavy over the forest with a dank stench of decay and despair. The few remaining blackened leaves on the twisted dying branches now do little more than block out the light and trap the foul musty air that fills this shadowy, dying dell.
21192: The tall poplar and massive oak trees that frequent this region of the woodland are under siege by a dark decaying blight that is slowly invading from the south. There the land slopes downwards into a dark, sickly smelling hollow. Here the trees still retain much of their strength and vitality, yet the decaying touch of blackened mould is occasionally visible on leaf and root.
21193: A multitude of dimly-lit, wildly-interspersed nettles, out of control woodland shrubs and hanging lichens crowd around, reaching out with snarls and creepers for exposed flesh. The dark oak canopy overhead shields the glade from any direct illumination, leaving the woodland in a perpetual state of dusk, dimly lit by an eerie florescent glow.
21194: A Meander in the River's Course

The break in the green canopy overhead reminds you of the world beyond the forest's embrace. To keep the open sky above you it would be necessary to follow the river north as it flows still generally eastwards in its own time. To the west, a small, natural ford has formed in the river.
21195: A Forest Approaching the River Limlight

Oak, ash, maple, and many other species have made this land their own. Approaching the river, the plant life changes slightly. Not many trees are seen along the riverside. Instead, shrubs, bushes and a variety of flowers can be seen thriving there.
21196: Over time the direction of the river has slowly changed, cutting away at the south bank as the river bends from the south to the east. The trees here grow at a slight distance from the riverbanks and small shrubs and flowers have taken root in the fertile land that lies beside the river. The river here steadily deepen and the water remains clear.
21197: Common oak and sweet chestnut trees are densely interspersed throughout this part of the forest. The ground beneath the trees is rich with tall grasses and various woodland flowers, whilst occasionally a prickly chestnut case from some long fallen seed of the chestnut trees may be kicked up from underfoot.
21198: A grove of maples stands here as a part of, yet apart from, the greater forest landscape. Beneath their supple branches, a verdant meadow of soft grasses and woodland flowers spreads along the riverbanks. The area has a look of a wild yet cared for woodland, once well tended. Nowhere can be found evidence of who would be responsible for such an endeavour.
21199: The river here looks to be fordable, as little as two to three feet in depth at its shallowest and no greater than five to six feet at its worst. The waters are slow moving and clear, with a pebbled and gravelled base visible in the shallowest parts. Signs of pond-weeds and other aquatic vegetation may be seen here and there and the riverbanks are low enough to allow entrance and exit.
21200: A densely packed forest of oak and ash is interspersed with the occasional maple tree, especially along the banks of the quietly flowing river to the north. The banks of the watercourse at this point are low and stable, affording easy access to the water.
21201: A large extending poplar tree with dark branches grows here.

A grove of tall upright poplar stands at attention in the midst of the greater forest. The trunks of these trees all appear to be perfectly straight and healthy, with a dense and vigorous covering of foliage.
21202: Prickly branches layer grey boles, while lichen, like old men's beards, drips down and encircles every tree. Light from high above scatters down, forming pools of darkness and speckles of green on the carpet of needles and leaves. Alone amongst its ancient brethren, being lightning scarred and shattered, stands a wounded oak, its iron boughs bent and battered. Still it stands defiant and majestic.
21203: On the South Bank of a River

Hummocks of wild fescue grasses interspersed with primroses, clovers and the occasional orchid have made a home here on the banks of the stately flowing waters that pass by to the north. Elder and willow grow here in a peaceful harmony, drinking deeply from the heady waters of the Limlight and standing tall and strong, free from disease or damage of any kind. The forest here seems less musty and aged then elsewhere.
21204: At a Widening of the Watercourse

The river, while looking as if it at one time was quite deep, now seems to be shallow and moving slow enough to be fordable. Perhaps because the riverbed is wider here than to the south or east. The banks seem to be stable and are covered in grasses, wild flowers and the more light-loving tree species. Here at least, the generally stuffy, enclosed feeling of the forest is lessened somewhat.
21205: Yellow primroses peek forth from beneath the tangled undergrowth, beneath a canopy of elder, dogwood and ash woodland. This forest glade seems less stuffy and dim than the vast, surrounding woodland. A fast flowing river bends around the southern and western fringes of this area, widening and losing speed as it turns.
21206: A huge mass of woody, yellow-green plants grows high up on the branches of the oak and poplar trees that call this area home. Fleshy white berries identify these huge parasitic clumps as the evergreen plant known as mistletoe, although it is rare indeed to see such a proliferation of this plant.
21207: A giant, strange looking green fungus is here, ready to devour you in seconds.

Filamentous growths of fungi encircle the exposed roots of the trees throughout this area. The woodland primarily consists of birch and aspen, although some hornbeam may also be seen here. The soil appears to be rich in organic matter and despite the obvious fungi, the trees here all appear to healthy.
21208: At a Bend in the River

The fast flowing river cuts a steep bank into the eastern edge of the bend as the river turns from an easterly to a southerly course. The inner curve of the riverbank is gentle, allowing easy access to the river water while the outer curve is populated by wet, mossy and slippery looking rocks and boulders.
21209: The lustrous greens and teals of the willow trees overhang the meandering banks of the river as it turns from the north-west to the east. The crooked and grey-green trunks of the crack willow wildly sprout their offshoots in all directions, whilst the yellow-brown trunk and branches of the weeping willow cascades downwards to drink deeply from the river's edge.
21210: The dominant trees of this overgrown glade have long straight trunks, with thick branches rising from their upper reaches. The crowns of these trees are whorled and they rise in height to over sixty feet. The bark of these trees is leathery to touch, silvery grey or black and is cracked in many places. The branches show a covering of dark wrinkled leaves, yet there is no sign that these trees have ever fruited.
21211: A huge millipede is writhing around here.

Moss-covered roots support thick, crooked trunks of roughly textured grey bark, cracked and peeling in numerous places exposing lighter sapwood beneath. The interlaced canopy overhead allows only limited light through its clutches, barely enough to provide nourishment for the mosses and lichens that live within this forest's grasp.
21212: A mass of low-spreading shrub quivers on the ground.

The verdant grasses, here beneath the shifting forest canopy, are filled with tiny flowers, sparkling like many-coloured stars in a firmament of green. Pale greens and silver boughs shift in the wind. The rustle of the forests innumerable green, brown, red and gold leaves is like a spell of music that entrances the senses and brings to mind what this most ancient of forests must have been like in its youth.
21213: The forest floor beneath this intermingled stand of deciduous woodland is covered by a dancing mist of green and blue. A horde of bluebells have crept forth from beneath the rustling leaf litter. The trees and other plant life here seem to pay no heed to the seasons outside. To the north, the reflective sheen of a watercourse may be seen through the tree line.
21214: A Sweeping Bend in the River

As the river's course shifts from the north back to the east in a grand sweeping curve, it starts to slow, becoming more stately in its progress. The dense, forested river banks to either side drop in height as the river slowly widens.
21215: The fast flowing waters of the River Limlight move through the forested landscape from the mountains far to the west. The river winds its way through Fangorns ageless grasp before passing into the east, joining the Anduin far away. At this point in the rivers life, the waters are fresh and young, cold and hard from their birth in the mountains, rich and ageless from the influence of this most ancient woodland.
21216: Densely clustered colonies of a red, coral-like fungus cover many of the recently fallen twigs, trunks and branches that lie upon the forest floor here, slowly decomposing. A number of saplings and some semi-mature alder are growing here between the occasional mature oak and ash. The woods appear to have been thinned out at some time in the recent past, whether by some great storm or through another agent is impossible to say.
21217:
A mass of wriggling vines drops on you from the trees.
Some thick writhing vines whip all around you.

The trees in this area of the forest have grown in a twisted tangle of jutting roots, briars and branches. Vines and brambles choke new growth, whilst twisted ash compete with broad and needle-leaved incursors. The heaviest congestion is to the north, where the mass of vegetation has grown so great that no travel is easily done in that direction. A fast flowing river can be seen and heard flowing to the south.
21218: A steep and swift moving watercourse, broken up by rapids and mini-waterfalls passes through the ancient forest. Only few plants grow in this fast flowing river, or on its steeply banked edges to either side. Although in several places the roots of young and old trees are exposed where they jut out from the river banks.
21219: A rooting heap of stems is here, smothering the smaller plants.

The forest floor in this area of beech and lime woodland is interspersed with a great number of jutting rocks, some of quite prominent height and girth. Huge swathes of honeysuckle may be seen covering much of the scrub, rocks and the lower branches of trees as it trails and scrambles its way through the forest.
21220:
Some thick writhing vines whip all around you.
A rooting heap of stems is here, smothering the smaller plants.

A claustrophobic tangle of honeysuckle, vines and creepers battle overhead for domination as they weave between the branches of beech and ash. Underfoot, a tangled mat of creeping vines, twisted roots and splintered rocky outcroppings conspire to trip and turn you at every step.
21221: A giant and ancient yew stands here quite eerily.

Huge splintered boulders, moss-shrouded and root-entangled, stand out from the undergrowth of the vine covered ground. Ferns, nettles, brambles and wiry grasses surround these great stones, whilst tall trunks and interwoven branches of beech, oak and ash loom overhead.
21222: Oak, ash, beech and birch are all to be found in this part of the forest, but no tree is more prevalent here than the broad-leafed lime. The trees' straight thick trunks topping forty yards in height, their strong gnarled branches rising up to a broadly dome-shaped thick crown. To the south the trees become more and more packed, gnarly branches interweaving to block southward passage.
21223: Ivy trails across much of the forest floor, criss-crossing this woodland. Together with a soil that seems damp, heavy and continuously clogging underfoot, travel here is hard going. Much of the oak woodland has become interspersed with wildly sprouting young and semi-mature hazel.
21224: A giant and ancient yew stands here quite eerily.

An area of broad-leafed deciduous woodland extends in every direction. The undergrowth beneath the trees cover is primarily composed of fallen leaf litter, decaying extremely slowly in this dry unchanging land. Various brackens and ferns sprout from around the base of the trees, providing some protection for whatever may choose to live here.
21225: A tangly shrub seems to rustle as if alert to its surroundings.

Tangling vines and trailing creepers hang from the reaching branches of the oak, beech and lime that populate this area. The tree canopy overhead is interwoven with ivy and twisted creeping vines existing in fierce competition, with the trees.
21226: A brown striated fungus hangs here, clinging to a tree trunk.

Lichen cover the twigs and branches of many of the oak and ash giants that fill the land. This area has a distinctly ancient feeling about it. The dusty greens and greys of the trailing lichen that adorn many old trees here give them a bearded appearance. A fast flowing river can be heard to the north.
21227: A mass of low-spreading shrub quivers on the ground.

The canopy here reaches heights of thirty to forty yards and consists of trees with crowns high on their trunks. The bark of the trees is orange-brown in colour. Where some have previously been damaged by bad weather, a sticky resin has been exuded. Sounds of a fast flowing river can be heard from the north, and the trees grow right up to the edge of the steep riverbanks.
21229: A Fallen Tree Bridges the River

An ancient oak tree, well over two yards in girth lies here, spanning the two banks of the River Limlight, whilst the river itself flows furiously some three yards below. The fallen tree seems to have lain here for some great length of time and appears to have lost a fair amount of its bulk over the years to rot and the river below.
21230: A colony of red ants is here. The ants seem to ignore you.

Throughout this area a large number of especially ancient trees stand tall amongst lesser younger saplings. Reddish bark and dark leaves help to distinguish these ancient trees as yew, the preferred wood of the master bowyer and fletcher.
21231: A majestic scots pine grows tall and straight here.

This area of the forest comprises of a large number of coniferous trees, the needles and cones of which have accumulated over many years into a deep litter underfoot. Here and there, an occasional yew sapling has invaded from the east, although these invaders are not doing well in the soil conditions here. A narrow river can be seen flowing to the south.
21232:
A tall birch is here, watching over the landscape.
An opossum stands here, sniffing around the ground.

A cold wind blows up from the south through all the trees, and the faint sound of water can be heard to the distant south, presumably the source of the cooling wind. Tall evergreens mix with great white birch trees and a thin mist covers the ground but does not quite obscure it completely. The canopy of the forest is thin here, and much light breaks through the leaves. The prairies to the north are visible and the forest continues in all other directions.
21233: A tall birch is here, watching over the landscape.

As the forest approaches the mountains in the far west, the number of fir trees seems to be constantly growing and all other types of trees seem to dwindle. Still, there are a number of oaks and birch trees with the odd tree being of a completely different variety. The only light that can filter through the treetops here is that of the sun, but even that can barely burrow its way through the thick canopy of the forest.
21234: Tall, thin fir trees make up the majority of this part of the forest, with the thick trunks of some oak trees providing a nice contrast. Some white birch trees are intermingled between the other two species as well. The ever-present dim green light filters through the treetops giving off some light to the area, but barely enough to see by. A very ancient oak tree stands here, rising above the other trees surrounding it. A massive trunk almost ten-feet wide makes this tree especially astounding to see. The forest continues in all directions.
21235: The forest here is extremely dark. Barely a glimmer of light filters through the treetops, and even that does not touch the ground. A heavy mist has set itself upon the ground, obscuring anything that might lie below its thick vapours. The only trees to be found in this area are large oaks. The forest brightens as it progresses northwards and to the east. To the south and west it is nearly as dark as here.
21236: A tall birch is here, watching over the landscape.

The gloom of the forest is overwhelming. An eerie mist surrounds most of the ground, covering any undergrowth that may trip an unwary traveller. Large, regal birch trees control this area of the forest, with a mix of fir and oak trees as well. A very faint green glow penetrates the canopy of the forest, giving off what little light there is. The forest continues in all directions.
21237: A light mist arises from the ground here, completely covering the forest floor. The trees are closer together than in most of the surrounding forest. Dim green light filters through the canopy of the forest making the mist glow green as it shifts below your feet and around the trunks of the trees. Faint outlines of uncovered roots are barely visible through the mist.
21238: A colourful butterfly is fluttering around here.

Darkness completely covers this part of the forest, the canopy is so thick that not even the brightest sunlight can penetrate it. An eerie mist floats along the ground, covering the forest floor. Even the trees themselves are dark, some appearing a solid black in colour, yet the eyes can easily be mistaken in this lighting.
21239: Set on the border of the forest, the trees here seem to have an almost ancient quality. The occasional soft sound, perhaps a whisper on the wind, might cause some to wonder if these trees are more aware than others one might find across the lands. The forest border grows thinner to the north where the ground is covered with vast plains.
21240: A trained horse is standing here, ridden by you.

The forest borders are well lit, and the golden grass to the north and west is visible through the light underbrush and trees. To the south, the forest quickly darkens and only a dim green light echoes through the leaves, creating an eerie glow to the forest. The east remains well lit.
21241: To the south and to the east, the great Fangorn Forest looms in a splendid display of nature at its prime. However, here the prairies still rule the landscape, covering miles to the north in a rich golden colour. Long stalks gently brush together creating a low rustling sound. Just to the west however, the forest that once covered that area is now nothing more than rotting tree stumps.
21242: A small grasshopper clings to a blade of grass, ready to spring.

The landscape here is very dismal, covered in burnt grass and foliage as well as being littered with tree stumps. The entire area smells of ash and decaying wildlife. Many of the tree stumps are covered in thick green moss and were very old judging by the size of them. The damage continues to the east and north.
21243: The way here is dimly lit as very little light filters through the leaves of the trees, giving the area an eerie green luminescence. The trees here seem to form a natural north-south path, which ends abruptly to the north as the forest closes the path. The way to the east is completely blocked off by black scorched trees.
21244: A giant and ancient yew stands here quite eerily.

Darkness engulfs this part of the forest, and the mist that lies over the ground is extremely dense, so as to completely cover the forest floor and whatever may lie there. The trees here are very old, some can even be called ancient amongst trees. Through the darkness, it is nearly impossible to make out exactly what types of trees grow here. To the east, the forest brightens.
21245: The forest thickens here, and becomes very dark. Only a very faint green glow emanates through the treetops. A tall and very ancient evergreen grows here among the birches and oaks, its age alone gives it a regal appearance, with branches as thick as a troll's torso. By far, this must be one of the older trees in the forest. The forest continues in all directions except to the north.
21246: A colourful butterfly is fluttering around here.

The forest here seems to shift around the wary traveller, but in this lighting, the eyes can play tricks on the mind. A light mist covers the ground, obscuring whatever lies beneath it. Coupled with a chill wind from the southeast, this place feels as though it may be haunted. No sounds can be heard except for the leaves rustling against each other. The forest darkens in all directions.
21247: Tall firs and ancient oak trees populate much of this area of the forest. Because of this, light still breaks through the treetops in daytime, and the fog that plagues most of the forest is not as present here as it is elsewhere. Thick roots cover the ground, almost as in an attempt to trap the inattentive traveller. The forest continues in all directions.
21248: Near the Edge of the Forest

Large trees sprout up all around, but in the distant northeast and northwest, the vast prairies spring to life and spread like wildfire to the north. A thin branch of the forest continues northward from here, and the forest darkens to the south. A thin mist filters in from the south, and the air around here is heavy and stagnant.
21249: The forest border is surprisingly dark, especially considering that the prairies are visible to the north. A light mist covers the ground, but the tree roots that may pose a problem are not hidden completely. Large oak trees cover the ground here, and no younger trees seem to be growing anywhere about. The forest continues to the west and south.
21250:
A rotten corpse is hanging here.
A brown fox is here, looking for some rabbits to chew up.
A brown fox is here, looking for some rabbits to chew up.

Standing here on the borders of the forest, with vast plains to the north, is a small niche in the forest which is completely isolated from the rest of the forest, and the only exit being back towards the prairies. Several types of trees are dominant here, including the regal white birch tree and the massive oak tree that seems to hold majority on the northern end of the forest.
21251: A large thorny branched shrub is growing here.

The forest here remains thin as it borders the vast prairies to the north. However, it seems that the ground cover has grown up to cover what the trees did not. Several bushes with edible berries grow nearby. To the south the forest quickly darkens as it progresses closer towards the heart of the forest. Strangely, there are very few sounds of wildlife anywhere around.

The remains of a haughty elm lie here in a heap of rotting compost.

A black alder looms threateningly over its surroundings.
Kut the Mountain Troll is standing here.
Gorthauk the Mountain Troll is standing here.
Cromdreath the Mountain Troll (CC) is standing here.

The forest here seems to close around the unsuspecting traveller. In fact, it has. There seems to be no exit from this section of the forest. The trees are packed tightly together, and any gaps are covered with thick foliage and undergrowth.
21253: The grass here is burnt to a crisp and the soil coloured a deep black from the scorching of the earth. A small ditch has been dug a fair distance to the east of the wall that marks the beginning of the forest, and the grass grows thick and tall beyond that. The burnt earth continues to the south and north.
21254: Golden grass covers the landscape here, giving the area a glowing golden colour that permeates everything nearby. Just to the south, the green borders of the Fangorn Forest stand in defiance to the grass. To the west, a strip of land is burnt black, with a wall of trees visible beyond it.
21255: The borders of the forest lie just to the south. The magnificent colours of the forest seem to draw the traveller towards them. Rich and deep green in colour, they are a perfect contrast to the golden grass that grows on the outskirts here. In all other directions, but to the south, the golden grass rules the landscape. Somewhere, far to the north, the faint sound of running water can be heard.
21256:
A fat rabbit is here, chewing on some grass.
A black crow flies low to the ground here, looking for carrion to eat.

The flat landscape stretches out, covered with waist-high bushes and plants, clinging together in small patches. Long and verdant grass sways in the passing breezes, and a few trees bow over the plants, their branches hanging like knotted fingers of giant hands. Towards the east, bushes seem to grow closer together, almost creating a hedge beside the passing trail.
21257: A colourful butterfly is fluttering around here.

The landscape spreads out in a grand vista of long grass and small bushes. Tiny plants spring up around the thick and tall blades of grass, spiralling upwards and protected in their growth. Despite the healthy plant life, the ground seems pebbled and rocky.
21258: The land here seems rather barren. Only a little bit of grass grows on it. Shrubs and some small bushes fill most of these plains, springing up from between various ploughed patches of earth. Most of the ground lacks plant growth, although the soil has a deep brown colour. The slightly barren landscape continues southwards. To the west, the lush greenery indicates another change in soil and surface.
21259: Numerous flowers grow scattered on these lush plains. The shrubbery that dominates to the north fades within the thriving grass here. The greenery is soft and most likely cushions each step taken on it. Many insects fly around feeding on the nectar of flowers. Tiny bugs scurry around the stems of the undergrowth.
21260: A badger is here, exploring for food.

The land is flat. Healthy shrubbery covers the plain. Frequent patches of flowers provide a rich contrast to the dark green of the bushes. Hills can be seen far to the west, while more plains are located in all other directions. A few large bushes that grow here decorate the plain with a random pattern. A glimpse of village walls can be caught to the south.
21261: The hills are covered with dense and vibrant foliage. Everything from berry-bushes to small lily flowers grows here. Small animal trails criss-cross between grass and plants. Some of the hills barely rise above the plains, while others are higher, forming steep foothills.
21262: A colourful butterfly is fluttering around here.

The land seems to wave up and down here. A tall kind of green grass covers the hills. To the west, the land slopes higher and higher up towards the mountains. Small bushes are at the top of every hill, and tiny flowers dot what looks like a grassy carpet. To the north, the landscape changes, becoming a rocky, grey surface of stone.
21263: The mountain continues its descent eastwards. To the north, the landscape steeply descends downwards to a narrow pass far below. It appears as if this pass might be reached with a great climbing skill. The ground consists of cold, hard stone, covered with rolling pebbles and flint underfoot. To the west, the massive rock rises up all the way to the highest peak.
21264:
A colourful butterfly is fluttering around here.
A colourful butterfly is fluttering around here.
A small boar with big yellow tusks looks eager to fight.

Long blades of bright green grass cover the fields. Its thickness and height make passing these plains quite strenuous. A few trees grow parted from each other, their branches hanging low. Travelling to the north is impossible, as the mountainside is steep and offers no footing even for the most skilled climbers. However, to the west, rocky hills rise, leading upwards on the stony surface.
21265: A small boar with big yellow tusks looks eager to fight.

This field is full of plants, flowers and bushes of many varieties. The grass grows in healthy abundance. A few trees grow skywards, scattered across the field. Their bark has become coarse because of the harsh winds. The plants that peek through the thick grass offer little insects and small animals something to feed upon.
21266: Knee-high grass covers the terrain this area. Small bushes frequently rise up in scattered patches, varying in type and colour. A few trees are interspersed within the grass. To the south-east, there grows a small forest with its treetops reaching high to the sky. The land begins to slope upwards to the north, leading to the grass-covered foothills at the base of the nearby mountains.
21267: The trees grow far from each other, varying in size and age. The ground is covered with a layer of dead leaves, which often cushion the steps of passing travellers and animals. Some patches of thorny brush invade the forest floor between the trees. To the east, the woodlands seem to become thicker.
21268: The trees are closely packed together, leaving barely two feet between them. Some are even closer together, and it appears as if they had grown into each other. Thick brush consisting of thorns and bushes covers the ground to the height of an average man's chest. To the south, the thick woodland continues, while to the east, passage is impossible because village walls prevent everybody from travelling there.
21269: The trees grow close to each other here in the middle of the forest. The ground is covered with a tangle of twisty roots and weeds, mixed with prickly plants that stick to the feet of passing travellers and their mounts, making their progress slow. To the west, the forest floor seems to be less populated with undergrowth, and to the south, the land gives way to thorny plains.
21270: This wooden gate provides access to a small village behind it. A footpath can be seen leading from the gate towards the forest to the south. Walls surround the other sides of the village, closing it off from the forest and plains. The gate was once sturdy but hangs lopsided on its hinges now.
21271: The grass is a thick mat of green blades. The shortest of the blades are about knee-high to an elf. Some small plants peek through the densely growing grass. A group of large trees stands in the middle of the field. They rise up in defiance of everything around them. Looking to the west, a wooden gate leading into a village can be seen.
21272: The grass grows thin and patchy. The dark brown soil is the most prevalent sight. Loose dirt and dust cover the surface and leave little room for plants to thrive. To the west and the south, the surface seems to change, offering more nutrients and allowing a variety of plant life. A single tree looms on the fields to the south.
21273: Thinning rows of grass cover the hard layer of packed dirt beneath. Small plants and shrubs dominate the other vegetation. A few bushes grow between a variety of thin and wiry trees. A few signs of animal life can be easily spotted, but even the buzz of an insect is sometimes heard. To the north, the grasses seem to thrive and prosper.
21274: A black snake, with red markings, is lying here.

The grass is covered with a thin layer of brown dust, making it seem burnt and withered. Some patches of grass have died or faded out, leaving bare areas of earth visible to the eye. A few prickled and spiny bushes grow on these fields, unable to shake off the barren look of these lands.
21275: Rocky pebbles cover the dirt-packed land. A few smaller weeds have managed to take root here despite the harsh conditions imposed on them by the dirt. Boulders are strewn across the grass tufts that are yellowish and withered, as they have no nutrition to feed on. The low and open plains seem to continue in all directions.
21276: A clear spring babbles as cool water trickles out of the ground.

Despite the barren-looking ground that lies to the east, the grassland thrives in full force. The soil is moist and enriched by the growth of numerous plants and flowers. Upon closer examination, a small mound of protruding rocks can be seen coming out of the grass. To the south, a stand of willows sways its branches in the wind.
21277: A fierce boar is here, making grunting noises.

The plains are covered with a thick carpet of healthy green grass. The long and wide plains reach out in all directions. Some small bushes grow between the patches of grass, surrounded by small weeds that feed upon their roots. To the east, the ground looks moister, indicating the existence of a water source close by.
21278: Many bushes and plants cover these flat plains. A large and gnarled old tree stands in the middle of the field. Beside and between its roots, grows various small plants and moss that feed on the fertile soil. The grass is a thick coat of long green blades that cover the fields with what seems to be a soft cushion of green.
21279: A fierce boar is here, making grunting noises.

Large and stately trees grow in this forest. Their branches reach high towards the sky. Countless leaves rustle in the wind. A small, barely visible trail runs along its course from the north. To the west, the forested area continues, leading to foothills and a mountain top that towers afar.
21280: The land is lush and teeming with plant life. The grass is coloured in a bright shade of green and grows long and thick. Large bushes sprout among the grass, and their branches are filled with leaves. Flowers also peek through the thick coat of grass and bring a colourful change to the carpet of greenery.
21281:
A field mouse noses about hungrily, searching for food.
A fierce boar is here, making grunting noises.

Many differently coloured flowers appear on the dense layer of verdant grass. Small plants also thrive here. They are of many different kinds and cluster around the blooming flowers. Some bushes are set intermittently throughout the plains. The lush greenery provides good nutrition for many small animals that are often seen scurrying back and forth, even during night time.
21282: A few patches of flowers stand in great contrast to the verdant grass that covers most of the area. The grass is long and thick, and many of the blades stick straight up into the air. Several bushes grow in small groups scattered over the field. Some of these bushy places give a home to one or two small trees. The seemingly endless green fields continue in all directions. However, to the east, the population of bushes seems to grow denser.
21283: Lush golden grass covers the land as far as can be seen with the exception of the foothills to the west and the great Misty Mountains far beyond. To the distant southeast, the faint sound of a spring can be heard through the silence.
21284:
A colourful butterfly is fluttering around here.
A finch flies low above the ground.

Rolling foothills cover the landscape, and the grass here seems almost alive as it sways back and forth in the breeze. To the east and north, the foothills come to an abrupt end as prairies sprout up and cover the land in golden grass. To the west and south, the foothills continue.
21285: Golden grass covers all the land in sight for miles upon endless miles. To the north, the foothills begin, while to the west, the tall golden grass has risen onto a small rise in a desperate attempt to get closer to the sky.
21286: The foothills here are soft on the feet, as the ground feels almost padded. All around the foothills, prairies stretch out as far as the eye can see. In a small valley to the west, a grove of trees battles for the soil that the grass seems to want to hoard for itself.
21287: Vast lands of endless golden grass stretch out in all directions. With the exception of the Misty Mountains that dominate the western horizon and the dark forest to the south, the grass covers everything within sight. A low rustling sound can be heard throughout these lands, as the wind constantly brushes the tall grasses together.
21288: Like a great arm, this section of forest splits away from the main body that lies to the south. Great trees of all varieties grow all around. However, there seems to be no sign of animal life anywhere around. Not even the chirping of birds can be heard.
21289: Outstretched like an arm, this part of the forest is still well lit by the sun during the day, and faintly by the moon at night. To the south, the forest becomes darker. But to the north, the woods become a little more sparse as the forest gives way to the plains that surround its northern borders. To the east, and to the west, the prairies stretch out. A large black object can be seen to the north west, breaking through the golden waves of the grasses.
21290:
An apple tree with bright green leaves grows here.
On the tree's branches are two apples.
A woodpecker is here, tapping on a tree.

Amidst the prairies and near the forest lies a small grove of trees. Some wildlife can be seen here, which one would have thought unusual this close to the dark forest that lies to the south and west. The tall peaks of the mountains can be seen over the green leaves that block the view to the west.
21291:
A large wild horse is here, protecting his herd.
A wild mare is watching you warily.
A wild mare is watching you warily.
A young filly is just learning to walk.
A finch flies low above the ground.

The golden grass that surrounds the landscape seems to rush towards the green foliage of the forest that lies to the south, almost as if trying to drag any travellers into the dark depth. Not a single sound can be heard. It is as if even the grass refuses to rustle in the ominous presence of the dark forest to the south.
21292: As the forest approaches the prairies, the battle of green against gold commences. The dense green of the forest foliage and canopy makes a startling contrast to the vast golden prairies that lie to the north. The mountains are vaguely visible in the west and they continue their march ever onward through time.
21293:
A grey wolf is here, thin from starvation.
A trained horse is standing here, ridden by you.

The golden grass runs north like an endless sea, as far as the eye can see and beyond. To the south, one can enter the depth of the forest, yet to the east, an impenetrable wall of trees blocks any hope of travel in that direction. The vague shapes of the Misty Mountains can be seen far off to the west.
21294: A large extending poplar tree with dark branches grows here.

The trees here make a narrow alleyway as they approach the forest. Both to the east and to the west, passage is blocked by large rows of trees, and the gaps filled in with dense foliage and bushes. The dark depths of the forest are visible to the south, and the trees seem to be guiding you in that direction.
21295: Barren land is all that is left here. Once either part of Fangorn or the prairies around it, this portion of the land is scorched and unrecognizable. One can only wonder what could have caused such damage to the land. The way west is completely blocked off by blackened trees and slightly burnt foliage.
21296: The lush golden grass of the prairies rages here, but ends abruptly in the west as the land becomes a barren scorched wasteland before the forest. To the south and east, the borders of a forest are visible, while the ever-present grey mass on the western horizon marks the Misty Mountains.
21297: The ground here is slightly damp and the result on the grass is incredible. The golden stalks are taller here than anywhere else, standing almost seven feet in height and blocking the view of everything around. Even with the fertile nature of the place, however, the only sounds seem to come from the north where running water can be heard.
21298: A water moccasin slithers out of sight just below the surface of the water.

The reeds here seem to never be silenced, between the winds forcing the stalks to bend and slide against each other and the water that flows in from the north constantly pressing at the bases of the stalks. The great shape of the Misty Mountains looms on the distant western horizon. To the south, the land is covered in tall golden grass.
21299: A lone hawk soars high above you.

Golden grass encompasses the landscape, yet somehow a glittering pool of water has formed in the midst of the vast prairies and lies just to the north. A faint sound of running water can also be heard in that direction, and the ground to the east seems to be slightly flooded, forming a small marsh.
21300: The vast prairies seem to swallow everything in sight. The only break in the monotony is the ever-present form of the Misty Mountains to the distant west, and a faint green line on the southern horizon, possibly the great Fangorn Forest. The faint sounds of birds can be heard far to the north.
21301:
A wild mare is watching you warily.
A young filly is just learning to walk.
A wild mare is watching you warily.
A wild mare is watching you warily.

Miles of lush golden grass cover the lands in all directions. The wind gently blows at the grass, causing a great rustling sound as the long grass brushes against its neighbour. On the distant horizon to the west, the southern peaks of the Misty Mountains are faintly visible, and to the south, a green line above the fields marks the beginning of a forest in the distance.
21302: A trained horse is standing here, ridden by you.

The green of the forest to the south draws your attention away from the vast prairies that continue in all other directions. Even the shapes of the great mountains to the distant west are not as forbidding as the forest that lies at the southern end of the prairies.
21303: As the wind blows gently upon the tall stalks of golden grass that grows all around, the results are only a faint rustling of the stalks sliding against each other. The vague sound of a cricket breaks the monotony as the sound drifts in from the north. The forest of Fangorn rises above the grass and draws the eye southwards.
21304:
A restless rabbit bounces around.
A field lark stands here, focused on finding food.

Beautiful golden grass sprouts up and spreads like wildfire in all directions. Nothing else seems to grow here. Despite the wildlife, the grass shows little sign of grazing. In the distant west, the southern marches of the Misties dominate the horizon and to the south, a thin green line is visible between the golden grass and the sky.
21305:
A wild bull seems ready to charge you.
A finch flies low above the ground.

Miles of golden grass encompass the land in all directions. In the distant west, the Misty Mountains rise out of the sea of gold and reach far into the sky. A fair distance to the south, the great Fangorn Forest can be seen as a line of green between the grass and the sky.
21306: Tall grass grows all around, stretching as far as the eye can see. The only sounds that can be heard are the rustling of the grass as it sways beneath its own weight and the might of the wind. The massive grey shape of the Misty Mountains can be seen in the distant west.
21307: Long and golden grass flaps in the wind, making a gentle rustling sound. For miles all around, the golden grass is the only feature that this land has to offer to the lonely traveller. To the west, the ground starts to roll as the foothills of the mountains start, while the entire western horizon is covered by the southern marches of the Misty Mountains.
21308: The tall golden stalks seem to be healthier here, a sure sign of nearby water. A small pond is visible just to the east, and the sound of a river is audible beyond that. The air is still as the wind is fended off by tall grass.
21309: A Small Pond in the Prairie

A placid pond is here, inviting you to take a refreshing drink.
A swan swims gracefully on the surface of the water.

A small pool of clean water has formed here from the river to the north and east. To the south and west, a traveller can see the vast plains that this area is famous for as they seem to stretch on forever from this vantage point. To the distant west, on the far off horizon, the Mountains stand against the test of time.
21310:
A crayfish is here, snapping its claws at you.
A brook trout is here, swimming in the current.

The river may be shallow, but there is a fair amount of pull to it as it rushes off to meet the great river Anduin to the distant southeast. Birds can be heard chirping from unknown locations. The river continues to the north and east. To the west, the river seems to have formed a small pond, while to the south, the ground has flooded and mild marshes are visible.
