21311: A brook trout is here, swimming in the current.

The river continues its trek from west to south as nature has devised it. The land to the north climbs up from the river bank into some foothills. To the east, the river bank is far too high to climb, and is edged by bushes and trees that seem to make a wall.
21312:
A crayfish is here, snapping its claws at you.
A crayfish is here, snapping its claws at you.
A grey wolf is here, thin from starvation.

This shallow river seems to house the only significant amount of wildlife in the area. The river flows quickly to the southeast, but is too shallow to pull anything of size along. A small pond builds up to the south from a small stream that branches off from this one, and the mountains loom over the distant horizon to the west.
21313: A black and white skunk is scuttling about here, searching for food.

Golden grass grows all around, yet there is no sign of life anywhere. The faint sound of water comes from somewhere to the north, while to the east a river flows on its eternal course, promising the possibility of some fish.
21314:
A sturdy pack horse is standing here.
A sturdy pack horse is standing here.
A fierce boar is here, making grunting noises.

Stretching as far as the eye can see, tall golden grass covers these lands and gives a rich colour to all around it. In the distant east, the faint sound of a river flows out over the grass while the Misty Mountains cover the horizon to the west.
21315: From east to west, north to south, the prairies stretch out, covering the entire landscape in lush golden grass that stands almost six feet in height at some points. On the distant western horizon, the Misty Mountains loom over the prairies, giving hope that the prairies do end somewhere.
21316: As far as the eye can see, the entire landscape is covered with lush, golden grass. Nothing seems to break the monotony around here, just endless grass stretching from east to west, where the prairies finally reach the distant Misty Mountains.
21317: All that can be seen, as far as any mortal eye can see, is endless golden grass. Yet there is no wildlife anywhere around to be seen. On the distant western horizon, the great Misty Mountains take to the sky.
21318: Lush golden grass radiates in all directions, stretching as far as the eye can see and beyond. To the distant west, past the foothills, the Misty Mountains rise in defiance of the sky.
21319: Everywhere within sight, the prairie continues in an endless wave of golden grass. To the north, a small pond breaks the monotony of the grass, inviting wild animals and weary travellers alike to take a drink. The Misty Mountains loom ominously in the west.
21320: An opossum stands here, sniffing around the ground.

Golden grass blankets the landscape and continues on almost endlessly in all directions, with the exception of the hills to the west. To the east, a pond of glimmering spring water can be spotted. Far into the western horizon, the Misty Mountains continue in their endless battle for control over the sky.
21321: A Small Pond in the Prairie
A shallow pond is here, tinted green with algae.

This small pond seems to be fed from an underwater source, with water as clear as the best cut diamond. Despite this, little wildlife can be seen anywhere around here, with the faint chirping of birds being the only sign of life.
21322: Lush golden grass extends for miles all around. Aside from the occasional small mammal, the only sound that may be heard is the rustling of the tall grasses as the winds unceasingly toss them against each other. A small pond to the southeast breaks the sea of grass and brings a welcome resting spot to any weary and thirsty traveller in these lands.
21323: An opossum stands here, sniffing around the ground.

For what seems like endless miles, the prairies continue in all directions, north, east, south and west, as far as the eye can see. The tall grass to the south blocks the view in that direction, yet the faint sound of a spring can be vaguely distinguished. On the distant western horizon, the great Misty Mountains cover the sky.
21324:
A nest is here.
A field mouse noses about hungrily, searching for food.

Spiny bushes populate this area of thorny brush, leaving little room to grow for the small and seemingly weak grass in this area. The thorny shrubs easily mark the armour and clothes of passing travellers, making travelling here often slow and tiresome. A single, sick and stunted tree grows amidst the thorny fields. Its leaves are dead and fell down a long time ago.
21325: Waist-high bushes and spiny shrubbery fill these fields for miles. The plants grow in small groups, leaving little room for grass or flowers. Not many signs of animal life can be spotted, as these fields have nothing nutritious to offer. The bushes continue towards all directions but to the south, where a grass-filled prairie seems to dominate the landscape.
21326: Thorny plants thrive in these fields. They choke almost everything that attempts to grow here. A few small plants have managed to push themselves through the thorny brush. Also some weeds have barely survived amidst the multitude of the prickly vegetation covering the ground. To the west, the landscape changes, as seemingly better soil offers a good environment for lush grass.
21327: Small bushes are abundant in the landscape around this place. They randomly grow in clumps and patches, while others stand alone. Brush and thorns fill the space between the bushes. Beneath all the foliage, a layer of grass grows green and healthily.
21328:
A low and wide-spread tree grows here.
On the tree's branches, there are two juicy plums.

The forest is very thin, with a fair amount of distance between the trees. The ground is covered with sun-dried shrubbery. Thorny plants are abundant, filling up empty spaces between trees. A layer of dead leaves covers the ground, most of them in a fair state of decay. The woods continue towards the north. In all other directions, shrubbery dominates the landscape.
21329: The plains are covered with a dense layer of grass and small plants. Thorns dominate the flora as they grow up and spread over large parts of the fields, overgrowing the rest of the undergrowth. Bushes prosper cramped together in small clumps. To the west, a slightly forested incline rises upwards.
21330: Shrubs cover the grass all across the landscape. The grass is bright green and surrounds the shrubs with a carpet of long blades. Thorny plants also grow between the various patches of shrubbery. A few trees prosper, scattered among the shrubs.
21331: A colourful butterfly is fluttering around here.

Flowers and plants sprout up from the fertile fields. The grass is strong and provides a bright, green background for the vibrant colours of flowers and other undergrowth. Some bushes grow in large clumps amid the healthy grass. A few smaller trees grow up between the clumps of other vegetation.
21332:
A tree-snake lies wrapped around one of the tree branches.
A colourful butterfly is fluttering around here.

A large and old tree stands alone in the grass. Its bark is beaten and coarse because of the weather, a testimony of passing winds and time. The branches are crooked and hang low. Its leaves are thin and coloured in a pale shade of green. Most of them that fell on the ground in a circle around the tree have begun to decay. In contrast to the aged tree, the grass seems to be thriving, reaching knee-height at most places. To the south, the greenery is a mix of various colours as a flower-dotted field comes into view.
21333: A colourful butterfly is fluttering around here.

A stand of aged willows grows in the middle of this deep green field. The trees bow down towards the grass, and their branches hang low, as if about to embrace the earth. Various flowers bloom and sprout up from the grass, topping the green plains with most of the colours of a rainbow. Small animals scurry around the stems of the plants trying to remain unseen.
21334:
A large pile of boulders is sitting here, probably debris from a rockslide.
A field mouse noses about hungrily, searching for food.

Burnt rings of grass fill these rock-pebbled fields. The ground is cracked and small crevices run on it like spider webs. Thorny bushes grow throughout the land, encroaching on the last remains of the grass. A few boulders lie scattered among the grass, and a bigger pile has formed between a patch of brush. It is covered with a layer of dust and pebbles, small weedy plants and bits of moss growing on it.
21335: Long thin grass grows on the pebbled ground, diminished by the poor soil and unable to reach its full thickness and height. The ground is dry and rocky, with only a thin layer of nutritious earth. Small pebbles roll under the footsteps of travellers. Some green-grey weeds feed on the barren soil. Dust and barren rocks seem to dominate the surrounding lands.
21336: Small rocks fill the soil, making it almost inhabitable for any plant life. Some weeds have managed to plant their roots here, although they appear to be thin and sick. A couple of shrubs grow in the pebble-packed dirt, but their state indicates a lack of good nutrition.
21337: A brown furry gopher is here, ready to dive back underground.

The height of a low hill here, although small compared to many other hills, provides a decent view of the surroundings. At the very top, the miles of golden grass surrounding the hill is breathtaking. Anybody with a mind for farming would be drawn to settle this beautiful landscape and live out the rest of their life tilling the fresh, untained soil. The foothills to the south, and east, would be perfect for livestock, and the endless plains to the west would produce an abundance of crops. The hulking shape of the Misty Mountains can be made out far to the west.
21338: A small grasshopper clings to a blade of grass, ready to spring.

The foothills are almost nonexistent here. The grass here is a mixture of green and gold, but in some spots it does not seem to grow for some reason. The foothills continue to the east and south while the golden grass continues to the north, and the green grass spreads like wildfire to the west. The Misty Mountains spread wide on the horizon to the far west.
21339: A lone hawk soars high above you.

The foothills here run high, and there is a decent view of the river to the south as it flows down towards the great river to the distant southeast. A lake lies close to the west, while foothills rise out in all other directions. These foothills must have at one time been as tall as the mountains that can be barely made out in the distant west.
21340:
A bass swims here.
A bass swims here.
A restless rabbit bounces around.
A small grasshopper clings to a blade of grass, ready to spring.

The lake seems to be rather deep, and fed from some underwater source that cannot be seen. However, the source of the water appears to be located at the western end of the lake. The water picks up speed as you approach the southern end of the lake, just before it forms a small river and heads southeast. Green meadows can be seen to the north and to the west, while on the east bank of the river a short climb will bring you into some foothills.
21341: A colourful butterfly is fluttering around here.

The green grass that springs up all around seems to swallow everything for miles. The ground here seems to be moist, if not even a little wet. To the south, a lake seems to shine in the light. To the east, the land starts to roll as it turns into some minor hills, while to the west and north, the fields turn a golden colour. Beyond the vast fields and to the distant west, the peaks of the great Misty Mountains can be seen.
21342: The smooth and even terrain here, with its rich soil, is perfect for growing crops. Yet there are none in sight, nor even a hint of civilized life anywhere around. To the east, the land continues until it eventually starts to turn into gentle foothills. To the south, the grass becomes greener, an evident sign of a source of fresh water in that direction.
21343: In contrast to the lush fields to the west, this area is only covered with sparse and thin patches of grass. At many places, the ground is bare. At others, thin and wiry stems of grass have sprouted with a yellowish-green shade, which indicates a lack of nutrients in the soil. Dirt and pebbles seem to cover the lands more to the north and the east.
21344: A black crow flies low to the ground here, looking for carrion to eat.

The barren plains that dominate the eastern fields seem to give way to fresh earth here. The soil is richer and healthier, offering grass a new chance to grow. Deep green tufts sprout from the surface. Small weeds and flowers poke their blooms and leaves up towards the sky.
21345: A field mouse noses about hungrily, searching for food.

Numerous blooms dominate this part of the grassland, reaching out in an array of countless colours. Growing together in clumps, they form patches of yellow, white and blue, breaking up the monotony of the green carpet of grass. The soft and moist soil has also welcomed a few larger bushes that thrive here, growing between the flowering plants.
21346: A boar cub is playing here, and exploring the wide world.

The surrounding fields are covered with grass that grows about two feet high, untamed and hardy. Several blooms of white and blue flowers spring up out of the grass, reaching for the sun. Insects buzz around the flowers feeding on the results of the pollen. The lush greenery continues in all directions.
21347: A grey wolf is here, thin from starvation.

All around for miles, the prairies continue almost endlessly. However, far to the east, gentle rolling hills can barely be discerned. The vegetation turns greener further to the south, possibly nurtured by fresh water.
21348: The golden grass that springs up all around seems to continue endlessly to the north and to the west. To the east and south, the gold turns to green as the lands approach the river that can be heard far off to the southeast. Far off to the west, the great Misty Mountains rise above the horizon.
21349:
A large shrub grows here, its branches loosely spreading.
A field lark stands here, focused on finding food.

This beautiful meadow seems to house a variety of small animals and insects. The lake to the east is almost blocked off from this meadow by some bushes and shrubs, while everywhere else golden grass springs up into the horizon.
21350:
A gigantic weasel glares at you.
A brown furry gopher is here, ready to dive back underground.

The grass here is a mixture of golden prairie grass and the green grass of a meadow. To the east, the green grass dominates as it comes closer to a lake in the distant east. Everywhere else around you, the golden grass is dominant and spreads as far as the eye can see.
21351: A small black cricket is here, chirping loudly.

Golden grass covers the countryside for miles and more seemingly endless miles. Tall grass blocks the view of everything around. Yet always present in the distant west, the Misty Mountains are barely visible over the grass.
21352: Endless prairies continue in all directions, covering the ground, and in the odd case, the grass seems to be attempting to reach the sky. To the west, a glimmering pond can be seen, and past that, on the distant horizon, mountains loom ominously.
21353: Golden grass stretches as far as the eye can see in all directions. However, all things must come to an end, and in the distant west, the Misty Mountains stand, putting an end to the seemingly limitless prairies that lie all around.
21354: A beautiful and docile horse is standing here.

Grass, tall, lively and golden, is everywhere. For many miles, this grass is all that there is to be seen. Above the grass, and to the distant west, the shapes of the southern peaks of the Misty Mountains dominate the sky.
21355: The Northern End of the Prairie

Soft tall grass sprouts up all around. Endless in all directions, except to the north where a dense patch of shrubs grow, the prairies seem to continue on forever. In the distant west, the southern marches of the Misty Mountains can be seen.
21356: A black crow flies low to the ground here, looking for carrion to eat.

Thick and spiny bushes densely overgrow these fields, dominating the few trees that manage to push upwards through the thick and thorny undergrowth. In small areas where the bushes have not managed to complete the cover, the grass tufts fight for nutrition and light against the dense shrubbery.
21357:
The bee flies around here, collecting nectar from the flowers.
The bee flies around here, collecting nectar from the flowers.
The bee flies around here, collecting nectar from the flowers.

Foliage and plant life is abundant in these fields. Despite the denser shrubs that seem to take hold to the west, the grass grows knee-high here, allowing flowers to bloom and sprout up between its healthy blades. Small insects buzz around, collecting nectar for their nurture, and the signs of several other animals can be spotted. The fertile grasslands continue to the north and the east.
21358: A large rabbit looks peacefully at you, ready to dart away.

Various clumps of bushes thrive in the fertile soil, accompanied by lush and thick grass, growing to a height of almost two feet. At a few places, the tops of flowers pop up amidst the tall greenery, giving it a speckled look. The fields seem to continue towards all directions. The walls of a small village can be spotted further to the north-west.
21359: A fat rabbit sits here, chewing on some grass.

Thorny shrubs and weeds densely grow beside each other, filling nearly every bit of space amidst the grass. A few smaller trees and bushes grow here along with other plants in the fertile soil. To the south, the vegetation seems to become thicker, as the grass disappears from view. A variety of weeds now dominates what one can see.
21362: Halfway up an Enormous Fir Tree

The branches growing from the rough-barked trunk are still strong and solid halfway up this enormous tree. Their coarse bark and convenient spacing provides ideal climbing and an adequately stable place to rest. The branches continue upwards, but become thinner and more fragile. Gazing beyond the dense, needle-like foliage just above this height, the outlines of trees waving to the gentle currents of the wind can be seen.
21363: Reaching the flimsy branches at the apex of this enormous fir tree brings not only an uninterrupted view of the surrounding lands, but also freedom from the isolation of the forest. The warmth of the sun and the soft light of the moon and stars are a stark contrast to the forest's gloom. A fresh breeze floats by in an unhindered stream as small twittering birds dash in and out of the canopy below. Extending for many miles beyond this place is the panoramic vista of Fangorn. Its complex, green patchwork incorporates every shade and tone of green imaginable. The vast, green plains of Rohan stretch along the farthest horizon to the south and east and the majestic snow-covered peaks of the Misty Mountains arise from the forest about fifty miles to the west.
21364: This once noble willow tree bears many scars. It has been hollowed out by crude tools many years ago. Whoever did this was certainly not a skilled carpenter, sharp slivers still protrude from the wood. Here and there it is almost possible to make out symbols carved in the wall. A whisker of lichen near the floor is the only sign of life that can be found.
21365: A clear spring babbles as cool water trickles out of the ground.

In the centre of the room, a great stone table stands six feet high. There are no chairs to be seen here, presumably the Ents had no need for them. Several tufts of grass are scattered on the floor. Looking around the rest of the home, it seems a few rays of light enter during the day through the eastern wall, drawing attention to the dilapidated state of the place.
21368: A tangly shrub seems to rustle as if alert to its surroundings.

Despite the utter darkness of this part of the forest, the undergrowth is quite developed, although the leaves appear to be in shades of grey and black, rather than the usual greens. This peculiar vegetation even seems to thrive on darkness, as the rare places where a bit of sunlight breaks through at times, are strangely deserted. In every direction, large dark trunks, almost regularly spaced out, stretch out in the far distance, like the bars of a colossal portcullis. But the real hindrance comes from all the sharp-leaved black bushes overgrowing in the undergrowth.
21370: The queen bat is here, emitting piercing squeaks.

Water once used to flow here, between the granite and limestone layers. All that is left now is a succession of large dry pots, sculpted in the tender limestone. Still, if one listens carefully, it is possible to hear the rumbling noise of water flowing somewhere, on a deeper level. North, the cave seems to come to an end, in a star-shaped room where an icy breeze whirls as if it had been misled there and was seeking an exit.
21371:
A large bat is here, hanging in the darkness.
A large bat is here, hanging in the darkness.

This almost flat cave ends here in front of a wall of moss. The brook which used to spring from here is gone, flowing deeper underground. In this part of the cave, draperies of whitish diaphanous stalactites cover the walls, often obstructing or concealing the way. Deeper west, the rock above changes to a dark grey, and going further becomes difficult and hazardous, in the middle of this chaos of crystalline rocks.
21372: The rock-pebbled hills have given way to mountains here. There are cliffs and jagged precipices all around. Sharp, rocky flints lie underfoot. No plant life or foliage can be seen growing, with the exception of some crabgrass which has pushed its roots between the cracks of the stones and cliffs. The mountains form a narrow pass to the east, while a massive stone towers to the south.
21373: A narrow pass runs between the cliffs. High walls of stone rise up to the north and the south, their jagged edges covered with moss. Loose, rolling rocks and pebbles crumble underfoot, forcing travellers to choose their way carefully. A few spiny weeds have pushed their roots through the cracks in the stone. Their slender branches wave in the wind. A thin, long crack runs vertically in a rock wall to the south, forming a small slit.
21374: The hills have coalesced into a mountain here. The dark stone is full of jagged edges and steep cliffs. To the west, the cliffs narrow so that there is only a small way visible between the mountain walls. To the north, the mountain abruptly ends at a steep cliff, discouraging from any travelling to this direction.
21375:
A fierce boar is here, making grunting noises.
A boar cub is playing here, and exploring the wide world.
A field mouse noses about hungrily, searching for food.
A fat rabbit is here, chewing on some grass.

Hills form the base of a mountain here. Bare patches of stone cover some of the hills, while others have a cover of grass or dirt. To the west, the mountain quickly ascends high above the hills and fields around, seeming like a sudden change to this otherwise calm landscape.
21376:
A fat rabbit sits here, chewing on some grass.
A wolf cub happily plays here.

The land starts sloping upwards to the west, still covered with lush grass. Some trees grow on the top of the hill, and their branches are bent by passing winds. Flowers thrive up from the undergrowth, blooming in various colours. To the west, the foothills of a mountain continue, and further to the south, a small village sits in the middle of the grass-filled lands.
21377: Large shrubs dominate the view over these flat plains. Accompanied by a fair layer of grass, they form thick undergrowth. The prickly stems of the shrubs and plants could easily tangle the foot of a traveller, slowing their progress. A few lone trees stand like pillars between the shrubs. To the west, the terrain begins to slope upwards, as the grassy fields lead further to the foothills.
21378: Long and vibrant grass covers these fields with a seemingly never-ending green wave. Small trees have sprung up. Their branches reach towards the sky, but not many of them manage to grow between the large amounts of grass. The northern lands are more densely populated with trees and a faint trail leads off into the forest.
21379: An angry bee is here, collecting nectar from all the flowers of the garden.

The land stretches out as flat fields of grass. Small bushes and trees grow eventually coalescing towards the north, at the edge of a small woodland area. The grass continues as far as the eye can see, waving in the passing winds like a green sea. Blooming flowers sprout up from the grass, tempting little insects to feed on them.
21380: The trail widens as its surface becomes well-trodden and packed with dirt. No plants or tufts of weeds grow on the path, giving it this often-travelled look. A flat landscape surrounds the area, forming seemingly endless seas of grassy plains. Green bushes grow here and there sideways with the trail, carrying various berries. To the west, the pathway enters the grassy fields that surround these areas for miles.
21381: A thin layer of grass grows on the dirt-covered trail. Small plants spring up from the rutted tracks. The grass grows thick and high beside the path. Some trees have taken root alongside the path and hang above, often providing shade and a good resting place for weary travellers. The trail makes a turn here as it enters dull-coloured plains to the south.
21382: A colourful butterfly is fluttering around here.

Small bushes cluster in miniature groves on these plains full of healthy and green grass. The trees are large and strong, indicating their age. Miniscule plants sprout up from the knee-high and thick cover of grass, often tangling the foot of a passing mount or traveller. To the west, the edge of a trail can be spotted, and to the north, the lush sea of grass continues.
21383: The trail is dusty and uneven with plant roots poking out of the thick, dirty surface. Some small bushes slightly block the trail, while grassland closes in from the north and the east. Shrubs sprout up at the edges of the trail, and a few flowers dot the starting grassland. To the south, the pathway continues, meandering through the grassland.
21384: A colourful butterfly is fluttering around here.

The trail widens as the trees and bushes grow less densely, giving room to the grass that pushes in from the south. The packed, dirty surface of the path is covered with dead leaves and old pine needles that have fallen from the trees. A few shrubs and tufts of trampled grass peek out of the dirt, cushioning the travellers' footsteps.
21385: The trail runs through a stand of pine and oak trees which form a green canopy overhead. Some large bushes line the edges of the path, at a few places encroaching on the trail and forcing travellers to take greater care passing by. To the north, the trail becomes more difficult to walk on. Untamed grassland and fields are located to the south and the west.
21386:
A small boar with big yellow tusks looks eager to fight.
A boar cub is playing here, and exploring the wide world.
A fierce boar is here, making grunting noises.

A green carpet of grass sways on these plains like a gigantic sea. Numerous patches of blooming plants and shrubs dot the greenery in a cacophony of colours. A few thin and tall trees grow on the grassy cover, providing a strong contrast to the short shrubbery. To the east, a trail surrounded by pines runs on its course.
21387:
A black crow flies low to the ground here, looking for carrion to eat.
A boar cub is playing here, and exploring the wide world.

The long verdant grass is abundantly interspersed with small plants. Flowers dot the carpet of green, and a few trees grow here and there, their branches hanging low towards the ground. Some bushy patches cover portions of the field, giving it a pockmarked look. To the south, the land slightly begins to rise.
21388: The plains mainly consist of dirt here, with a few tufts of grass sprinkled around. Rocks are the primary feature. Some stones are seemingly placed by an invisible hand. To the south, some rocky hills rise up from the flat plains. They form a strong contrast to the area around here that slopes up and down in small knolls only.
21389: The plains are covered with rocks and boulders, forming a collage of stones and dirt. To the south, the mountain rises almost straight up, blocking any attempt at passage. To the north, the plains are lush with green grass and large bushes. To the east and the west, the ground is flat. Pebbled fields of grass are everything that can be seen in these directions.
21390: The land is flat but has a fair amount of foliage and greenery. The plants seem to be healthy and thriving. Many bushes grow in the area. To the south, a wall of mountains rises up almost vertically, preventing any further travelling in this direction. Westwards, the ground slopes upwards, forming small rocky hills which lead up to the mountains.
21391: A fierce boar is here, making grunting noises.

The ground slopes upwards, forming a rocky hillside. A thin layer of dirt covers the stony surface, only offering the least demanding plants and shrubs enough nutrients to survive. Patches of moss grow on the sides of chunky stones and boulders, which are both piled up or scattered over the area. To the south, the mountainside becomes higher, making the journey more exhausting in this direction.
21392: The grass gives way to dirt and rocky pebbles here. Large boulders lie on the plains. Some are randomly scattered, some seemingly placed according to a strange design. Between the scanted grass tufts, the grey colour of rocks and moss dominates, giving the area a barren look. To the south, the predominance of grey colours continues, as rocky hills rise up towards a mountainside.
21393:
A clear spring babbles as cool water trickles out of the ground.
A black crow flies low to the ground here, looking for carrion to eat.

Lush grass grows in abundance. Blades wave in the passing breezes, almost constantly producing rustling noises. Bushes of green and brown colour and little flowers with their colourful leaves and blue and red blooms dot the undergrowth. The soil seems to be soft and wet, making the ground soggy. Upon closer examination, a small spring of clear water can be seen spurting out of the ground, watering the surrounding fields.
21394:
A small black cricket is here, chirping loudly.
A small black cricket is here, chirping loudly.

The plains stay flat for miles, dominated by various shades of green grass. The waves of the greenery rise up two feet with smaller plants growing amidst the tall blades. Tiny, white flowers dot the waving carpet, while bees and other insects fly around them collecting their nectar. A few animals can often be seen scurrying through the grass. To the south, the land becomes rocky, while the sea of grass flows on in other directions.
21395: The land slopes up and down in small hillocks. The grass covers the fields with a dark shade of green. Here and there, patches of dirt interrupt the grass with brown spots. Some weeds spring up in various places across the field, and a few crabgrass plants can be spotted peeking up from the dirt.
21396: A black snake, with red markings, is lying here.

Green grass provides a bright contrast to the duller shades of green of the forest to the east. Some small shrubberies dots the plain at various places. Trees are scarce but some can be seen to the north and the east. To the west, the land opens up in a broad expanse of plains.
21397: A fat rabbit is here, chewing on some grass.

The dirty trail runs along the small edge of a forest here. The landscape to the west and the south is flat and covered with lush grass. Some trees grow here and there around the trail, becoming denser to the north-west. A few shrubs peek out of the surface of the path, covering it with trampled stems of grass.
21398: An Overgrown Part of the Trail

The trail narrows as it gets closer to the forest. Knotted roots of trees meander in and out of the path, seemingly wanting to ensnare a careless traveller. Thick and spiny shrubs grow along the edges of the trail. A few fallen and rotten trees also help to prevent any fast movement through this landscape. To the north, the trees grow closer to each other, leading deeper into the forest.
21399: The corpse of a black bear is lying here.

Tall pine trees fill the forested area, filling the air with a sweet odour. A brown bed of soft pine needles covers the ground. Green plants sprout up between the cover of needles. A few bushes have planted their roots into this calm environment. A small trail runs further to the west and the south, leading to the edge of a forest.
21400: Long green grass covers the landscape. Its vibrant and healthy stems rise skyward, reaching almost two feet in height. Small plants and shrubs grow between tufts of grass, almost struggling for gaining space in this thick carpet of growth. Looking westwards, pine trees belonging to woodlands dot the horizon.
21401: A fat rabbit sits here, chewing on some grass.

Large bushes are spread out amidst the abundant and thick grass. Small trees rise up here and there, growing together with lush bushes that shoot up between the blades of grass. Prickly nettles and briars mix with the grass and little blue-white flowers that reach up for sunlight. Small insects buzz around, and tiny animals can often be seen scurrying around while searching for food. To the west, the grass appears to be growing higher.
21402: The grass is fertile and thrives, presenting itself in healthy shades of green. To the north, foothills can be seen leading up to the distant and high mountains. Small plants and shrubs grow between the grass, and the bushes paint an epic picture of natural beauty. To the south, the land becomes extremely barren. The ground flattens to the east, as the plains extend in this direction.
21403: The flat lands are overgrown by plants and other foliage. However, the dark green shade of grass seems to be the most dominating life. Scattered groups of little white flowers appear at some places, providing some contrast to the sombre green. Small chunks of rock and pebbles interrupt the sea of grass as well. Each of them is covered with moss.
21404: The ground is soft, and the rich soil welcomes the amber and green grass that grows here in abundance. Small plants and flowers have firmly placed their roots in the ground, giving the impression of small ornaments in the grass. The tracks of a few wild animals can be spotted here and there, criss-crossing the field. To the south, the land becomes bushy, with a few trees standing close to the horizon.
21405:
A wolf cub happily plays here.
A wolf cub happily plays here.
The mother wolf stands here, protecting her young cubs.

The calm landscape, covered with low grass, looks like a swaying sea of dark green colour. Bushes and small clumps of shrubs grow scattered over the area. A few flowers peek out of the grass with blooms of various shades. To the east, a visible trail passes by, surrounded by a few trees and bushes.
21406: A colourful butterfly is fluttering around here.

An earthen pathway meanders along the edge of this land, dotted with several trees. The undergrowth and the trees themselves grow denser to the east, where a small grove has formed over time. The trail leads to the east as it runs closer to the coppice, meandering between trees, bushes and foliage. Around the edges of the path, grows green vibrant grass that spreads on the plains that lies to the west and the south.
21407:
A porcupine is waddling around here, its tail full of sharp quills.
A fallow deer is grazing peacefully here.
A colourful butterfly is fluttering around here.
A boar cub is playing here, and exploring the wide world.
A large rabbit looks peacefully at you, ready to dart away.

This earthen trail runs along the forest trees. It winds back and forth amidst the undergrowth and shrubbery. Several twisty roots of trees stick out of the dirty cover of the pathway. The woodland continues towards the east, while the path leads southwards with a small turn.
21408:
A large mother hawk is here looking for prey to feed her young.
A porcupine is waddling around here, its tail full of sharp quills.

Tall and aged oaks grow here, mixed with broad-leafed trees and a few young pines. The dense undergrowth and spiny shrubbery make travelling here difficult. A layer of twisted roots and dead leaves covers the ground. The trees grow sparser to the east, and a small trail can be spotted leading to the south.
21409: A large mother hawk is here looking for a prey to feed her young.

This woodland area is sparsely populated with young trees, a mix of pine and cedar. Some small bushes and shrubs dot the undergrowth. A few forest flowers have planted their roots in the soil, just provided with enough light and nutrients for their needs. To the east, the forest seems to fade, giving way to the bush-filled grassland.
21410: Small bushes abound here, providing a break to the monotony of the short green turf. Amidst the waves of grass, there grow small foliage plants, shrubs, and red and white flowers. A burnt and ashen tree stands alone in the middle of the plains, hollowed out over time. To the west, tall trees rise up towards the sky.
21411: Small hills rise and fall upon the surrounding land, making the landscape look wavy. Trees top the higher points of the hillocks, growing up from between the healthy grass and plants. Bushes and shrubs flood the small ravines, and grass grows knee-high. To the west, a small group of trees catches the eye.
21414: This pathway is heavily littered with drifts of undisturbed dead leaves. The increasing shadows and the smothering wall of birch has had a disturbing effect on this avenue of beech. These ancient trees were once aisles of glossy evergreen boughs welcoming the Shepherds of the Trees into a homely abode at the southern end of the path. Now the trunks are dark and ominous, and the remains of their smooth silver bark is cracked and peeling. The ground is uneven and is covered with the fractured limbs and fallen leaves of the beech trees which line the avenue. It is apparent that this area has not had any visitors for many long years.
21416: The cave opens up from the narrow entrance. A tunnel-like descent leads down to the depths of the mountain. A small trickle of water drops on the floor from the condensation on the ceiling. The cave appears as if it had been carved on purpose, but neither by nature nor time. The cave walls seem slimy and are cold if touched.
21417:
A dirty uruk stands here, the leader of a small pack of renegades.
A renegade uruk is here, dirty and ragged.
A renegade uruk is here, dirty and ragged.

The filthy cavern is wide, its walls jagged, covered with slimy algae of some sort. The floor is covered with refuse and decaying remains of corpses. Besides the thick and nauseating stench, the air is stale and thin. A few small puddles of water are on the ground, filling small holes in the otherwise plain cave floor.
21418: An old man is walking around, cleaning up.

The odour in this dingy room is a musty mix of stale alcohol and tanning oils. Along the eastern wall, there is a neglected bar with dirty glasses carelessly left on it. The few tables, upon which patrons rarely sit, are decrepit and run-down. There are holes punched through the various chairs that are strewn around the tables. The decline in patronage has led the owner to dabble in other trades. An array of oils and instruments, which were used to fashion animal hides into useful leathers and other similar things, covers a rickety bench on the western wall.
21419: There are stalls in the stable. Most of them are empty and look as if they have been unused for years. The walls of the stable are thin, and there are holes scattered all over the boards. A large and rusty water trough lies in the middle of the stable. The water in it is green with algae.
21421: A horse trainer is resting here.

A wooden fence creates a large oval around the field. A few posts and beams make hurdles of varying heights. A small, open-air shelter stands at one end of the practice yard, attached to the stable. In it, there stands a small workbench with various tools scattered and piled on it. A modest bed with linen blankets sits close to the bench.
21422: A small woman is here, appearing thin and malnourished.

This house is broken down and seems to be on the verge of falling apart. Holes are readily apparent in the ceiling, and the floor seems to consist of nothing but dirt. Various hunting tools are displayed on the walls, worn and well used by the last inhabitant of the house.
21423: The street surface has transformed over many years of neglect into nothing more than a thick layer of gunk and mud. Deep soggy ruts run back and forth through the gooey matter, making it troublesome to cross without slipping or getting dirty. The narrow street barely allows two fully-grown men to stand shoulder to shoulder. A horse would have to be relieved of both coach and carriage to be able to pass. A doorway leads into an abandoned house to the west.
21424: What passes for the centre of this small village is just a part of a street that appears slightly wider here than to the east and the west. Thick mud lurches underfoot, making it difficult to traverse with or without a mount. A few stones poke out of the mud, indicating that once, this road was paved with cobblestone.
21425: A circular stone well has been built here.

A small well is here, giving water to the poor denizens of the village. The footing around the well is muddy and soggy from regular spillage as the villagers draw water from the well. The rest of the surface of the street consists of packed dirt, littered with small cobblestones. Deep ruts, running from the east to the west, scar the ground on the northern side close to a shabby building.
21426: Furs and pelts cover the walls of this dwelling. A large bear fur, complete with head and claws, covers almost an entire wall. The floor is creaky, and cracks have formed in the wood. A few small pieces of wooden furniture are scattered across the room, leaving an undemanding look, apart from the trophies of wild animals.
21427:
A brown bear fur is here lying on the ground.
A grey wolf fur is here lying on the ground.
A tall, well-muscled man fingers an old axe hanging from his belt.
A rugged-looking man is standing here.

The walls of this room are lined with animal skins, and the floor is carpeted with fur and skins. A modest table sits at the southern end of the room with an old wooden chair placed right in front of it. A few pieces of a half-burnt candle are scattered over the table, and dots of old wax-drips decorate the surface. The bed is only big enough for one and is made of simple, rough wood. It has a thick but tatty bearskin serving as a mattress, and two crumpled sheets on it replace the blanket.
21428:
A large sack is on the ground.
A wooden cupboard stands here.
A woman is here, looking for someone to chat with.

The small kitchen is crammed with mostly empty shelves, cupboards, a table and two rickety chairs. The drawers and benches are strewn with dented pots, pans and a few other kitchen utensils. The plates and bowls are chipped and worn, indicating a long period of use. A measly number of basic ingredients can be found, but unfortunately there is no delicious aroma coming from the large oven sitting at the southern wall of the room. Instead, it is filled with black ash and food residue. The wooden floor is creaky and has small holes in it.
21429: A small oaken table has been set here.

A small sitting-room leads into the house. While the owners of the house have tried to furnish their quarters in a rather lavish manner, it still seems frugal. A single, large animal fur fulfils the role of the carpet, and cut tree stumps serve as benches. A small table sits in the corner of the room.
21430: A sturdy bed made from solid oak lies here, covered in warm blankets.

The bedroom area is filled with knickknacks made of parts of various wild beasts, lying around on the small drawer and the bedside table. Necklaces made of bones, noisemakers of teeth and backscratchers made of claws are just some of these items. Furs cover every square inch of the floor making it warm and soft to step on.
21431: On the Branches of the Tree

A tree-snake lies wrapped around one of the tree branches.
A tree-snake lies wrapped around one of the tree branches.
A tree-snake lies wrapped around one of the tree branches.

The bark of the tree is gnarled and coarse, offering fair support to anyone who has decided to climb up here. The lush green leaves rustle in passing breezes, their colour varying from dark to light, depending on the time of the day, and therefore the warm rays of sun or the cold and shallow moonbeams spreading over the surrounding lands.
21432: The riverbank slopes steeply away from the Anduin on either side, culminating in the west in a tall, golden-crowned forest. The trunks of these magnificent trees are smooth and thick; it seems unlikely that any mortal force could sway them. In the east, a dense, green forest follows the path of a northerly ridge. These waters are deep and swift as they flow southwards, away from the great river nexus lying northwards.
21433: The mighty Anduin undergoes a transition as it curves broadly from north to east. In the north, the river is wave-filled and swift as it flows away from a junction of two rivers. Powerful currents work in many directions, all the while maintaining a downstream flow. Above the eastern riverbank, a high wooded ridge follows the river on its north-south course. Conversely, as the Anduin moves east and then south, it widens and becomes less turbulent.
21434: The banks of the Anduin are widely spaced, yet the river flows swiftly and with significant force. Several large grey boulders can be seen in shallower water near the western shore, but they are submerged and create little disturbance in the smooth river surface. The river flows in from the west, where it bends, and away to the south. A high, forested ridge rises to the north, echoing the Anduin's sounds back this way.
21435: These clear waters choose a deep and narrow path as they flow swiftly past riverbanks carpeted in violet, bell-shaped flowers. In the east, the Celebrant bravely encounters the mighty Anduin, whose powerful currents shift the course of both rivers to the south. In the north, a broad golden lawn rises above the river nexus, bordered to the north by a tall, green wall. The same kind of green wall can be seen upon the steep southern riverbank.
21436: Meeting of the Anduin and Silverlode

Chaos ensues as the Anduin and Celebrant crash into each other, their white-capped currents pounding forcefully against the steep, rocky riverbanks. Despite the swift fury of the eastern-flowing Celebrant, the Anduin wins the battle of rivers, incorporating the foreign waters into its southerly course. The wooded ridge visible to the east becomes a steep cliff as it extends northwards along Anduin's path. In the northwest, a shining lawn stretches between the waterways and a thick, green hedge. Beyond this natural wall, the ground rises and mallorn-trees reach their graceful crowns high above the horizon.
21437: Vast, craggy fissures in the rocky base of the Anduin, combined with the river's swift current, have caused the current here to be swift and dangerous. Foamy, white waves smash against the solid stone of the eastern riverbank, which rises into a tall, wooded cliff. In the west, the terrain rises steeply above water level, giving way to a glistening lawn of soft golden grasses. Farther in that direction, golden-crowned mellyrn rise high into the heavens.
21438: The Anduin flows swiftly between steep, rocky banks, crested by the golden crowns of the mallorn-trees. Any attempt to cross from shore to river would be futile, marred by the overgrown riverbanks and unforgiving current. To the southeast, the forested ridge bordering the waterway grows in height, forming a thickly wooded cliff. Beyond the western riverbank lies a break in the lofty tree-tops, as if there was a clearing in that direction.
21439: Greatest of Arda's many rivers, the Anduin thunders as it moves quickly from north to south, bordered on the east by high green banks and ancient woodlands. In the west, the tumbling waters of a small stream smash into the mighty river with no effect on the Anduin's deliberate course. To the south, the current seems to become even more powerful, as the channel deepens and the banks grow steeper and closer together.
21440: The current here is swift and unrelenting, flowing in from the east and away to the south. Tall, golden-topped trees loom high upon the sloped riverbanks that rise to the north and west of the wide river. Far to the east, the woodlands are of a different breed than the majestic mellyrn of Lorien. The eastern forests are tall and healthy in their own right, but somehow lack the timeless and magical air of that elven forest of legend.
21441: The current here is swift and powerful, quickly carrying floating objects away through a wide bend in the river. In contrast to the great mallorn-forest that rises high above the western bank, the woodlands bordering the eastern shore consist of smaller, younger beeches, larches, poplars and birches. Immediately above the eastern riverbank, a small clearing with a carpet of soft grass and wildflowers interrupts the forest continuum.
21442: The course of the mighty river follows a straight path from north to south, rushing rapidly past verdant riverbanks. The river is wide and in most places very deep, although clusters of partially submerged boulders near the eastern shore indicate shallower waters in that direction. To the west, the woodlands are dense and rise high upon upward sloping ground.
21443: The waters of the Anduin enter a smooth bend, flowing swiftly from the east and away to the south. On either side of the river the lush, green banks rise steadily, giving way to tall woodlands. Far to the west, the trees grow even higher and seem to be crowned in gold.
21445: The crystal-clear waters of the Celebrant flow deeply and quickly beneath tall woods of silver and gold. The river bends from the north away to the east; visible on the far side of this bend is a lush lawn of golden shade. To the west and south, the ancient forests of Lothlorien continue upon rolling, grass and flower-covered slopes.
21446:
A swan swims gracefully on the surface of the water.
A swan swims gracefully on the surface of the water.
A nightingale is here, chirping a sweet melody.

The Celebrant bends from west to south as its glittering waters wind through the tall mallorn forests of Lorien. In the north, a faint path rises above the river level and quickly disappears into the gold-topped forests lying in that direction. Directly to the east, a white stone hythe has been constructed at the water's edge; moored to it are several narrow wooden boats, clearly of fine craftsmanship. Beyond the structure, a broad, shimmering lawn stretches north and east before encountering a high wall of lush, green bushes.
21448: Deep and wide, the Celebrant flows steadily eastwards, flanked by the eternally watching mellyrn that line the riverbank, like sentinels standing the honour guard. The cold and clear water fills the air with a happy babbling that echoes into the dense wood on either side, blending with the soft whispers of the slowly moving tree-branches.
21449: Flowing gently eastward, the deep waters of the Celebrant flow strong. Clear and cold, the water has travelled all the way from the heights of the Misty Mountains, restlessly searching for the great rivers of the east. Banking the river are the wooded slopes of the enchanted forest of Lothlorien, standing forever watchful and guarding over the river's passage through the Golden Wood.
21450: Flowing gently, but with hidden strength, the Celebrant glitters and sparkles as small eddies churn and ripple across the surface. The banks of the river are covered by tall mellyrn that stand in lines like an honour guard, showing its respect to a passing king.
21451:
A trout swims here.
A robin is here, carrying small pieces of wood to its nest.
A blue dragonfly is circling around.

Bending sharply eastwards, the river flows steadily onwards on its eternal quest to join the river Anduin far far to the east. The deep and clear water is chilling to the bone, as it has travelled far from the peaks of the Misty Mountains before passing beneath the eaves of the Golden Wood. Lining the banks, the proud and mighty trees of Lothlorien stand tall and solemn, almost as if watching over the river's passage, making sure it flows unhindered towards its goal.
21452: A brook trout is here, swimming in the current.

Running in the deep ravine that it has carved out for itself throughout the ages, the Celebrant lies shadowed by the wooded banks that border it. Swiftly flowing, the cold and clear water makes its way steadily onwards to the east and the great river Anduin.
21453:
A blue dragonfly is circling around.
A salmon swims here.

Rushing swiftly through the widening ravine, the Celebrant turns sharply northwards. Even though forced to change its course, it seems anxious to reach its faraway goal. The deep and cold river passes below the wooded river banks that are lined with towering mellyrn that stand guard, forever watching and guiding the loved river onward.
21454: A nightingale is here, chirping a sweet melody.

Flowing slowly eastwards, the cold waters of the Celebrant continue their long journey begun high up in the Misty Mountains and strive towards the east to meet the great river Anduin. The clear water runs deep and slow here, and the sloping banks are lined by the eternally watching mellyrn.
21455: A brook trout is here, swimming in the current.

The deep, cold and clear Celebrant flows steadily towards its goal far away in the east, the great river Anduin. The steep banks of the river are lined by the towering mellyrn, standing solemn and silent as guardians, forever watching the water flow by.
21456:
A salmon swims here.
A salmon swims here.
A salmon swims here.
A trout swims here.
A brook trout is here, swimming in the current.

Slowly flowing onwards, the deep river gently twists and turns as the wooded river banks move farther apart. Lining the banks are the towering mellyrn, standing like guardians as the cold and clear water runs without hesitation towards the great Anduin far away to the east.
21457:
A nightingale is here, chirping a sweet melody.
A salmon swims here.
A nightingale is here, chirping a sweet melody.
A brook trout is here, swimming in the current.

Hurling itself northwards, the deep and clear water rushes between the rocky river banks, its wild pace gradually slowing as the river widens. The rushing water sends echoes reverberating throughout the forested river banks, almost drowning out the soft whispers of the breeze that gently rocks the surrounding trees.
21458: As the ravine bends, the water smashes into the rocky walls with incredible force and large, jagged stones rise above the surface like pointing fingers, ready to crush anything unwelcome. The roar of the water drowns out all other sounds as the echoes within the ravine are hurled back and forth without respite.
21459: In the narrow ravine, small whirlpools dance across the turbulent surface, eddying and sucking at everything. Water smashes into the rocky walls and hurls itself onto the jagged rocks rising in the middle of the raging river. The roar of the water drowns out all other sounds and echoes sharply out towards the solemn forest that stands above.
21460: The river Celebrant flows here, marking the border of the protected lands of the Naith of Lorien. The river is deep but not too wide, and the water that flows past is cold and clear. It seems that to drink this water would provide lasting refreshment beyond the mere quenching of thirst.
21461: The sparkling river bends from the west to the north. Fallen leaves float along the surface of its crystal-clear water. Pale-green mossy stones line the bottom of the river, almost reaching the surface of the water at shallow points near to the banks.
21462: The River Celebrant bends here from the south to the east. The forest along the western side of the river is thick and the trees overhang the river. Years of erosion on the east side of the bend have moved the river somewhat, leaving a silty buildup on the western bank.
21463: A sparrow is flapping around on the ground.

The Celebrant River continues its course here, making its way ever eastward. The water is cold enough to chill any swimmer after only a few moments spent immersed. The river is very deep here; even the tallest Elf would not be able to stand straight up in the centre of the current.
21464: Flowing in from the west, the river Celebrant makes its course toward the north where it joins with a small tributary. The water moves fast as it approaches the confluence. From here the sounds of the crashing water are clearly audible. The river banks to both south and east have been undercut by the fast-flowing waters, making it impossible to ascend.
21465: Spilling down a low forested slope to the north, a tributary joins the mighty Celebrant River that flows in from the south. At the confluence the joined rivers become a single swirling mass of foamy water before rushing on eastward with the combined force. The churning pool of water is not very safe to traverse.
21466: The flowing water of a tributary stream plunges down a low, but steep waterfall here. The rushing current pours over slippery, mossy stones that make travel to the north quite impossible. At the base of the waterfall, a wide pool has formed, its glistening surface constantly rippled by the stream that plunges into it from above, before streaming onward to mingle with the waters of Celebrant to the south.
21467: To the north this river appears to be little more than a stream, but here it begins to widen as it gathers strength. It continues south, where it plunges down a waterfall on its quest to join with the Celebrant that cuts through this section of the Golden Wood, separating the sacred home of the Elves from the outer forest.
21468:
A brook trout is here, swimming in the current.
A small grasshopper clings to a blade of grass, ready to spring.

The stream is moving at a greater speed here than it is farther upstream. It can not be too far away from the point where it meets the main river. The clear water that passes downstream seems to beckon you to take a drink; it is so clear that stones can be seen, glittering on the bottom of the streambed and bright flashes of fish scales frequently flash by at the periphery of your vision.
21469: A brook trout is here, swimming in the current.

The stream flows steadily as it makes its way towards the Celebrant. Golden mallorn blooms occasionally float down from the great trees above to become as little boats on a journey through Lothlorien. Some gather along the edge of a green, mossy stone, but the current quickly dislodges them and sends them on their way.
21470:
A colourful butterfly is fluttering around here.
A brook trout is here, swimming in the current.

The stream is wide and fairly deep here. It would be possible to dip a shortsword into the water at the midpoint between the two banks and still not touch the streambed below. The clear water is as cold, as if it was all runoff from the ice-melts in the mountains to the west.
21471: The stream begins to widen as it leaves the higher lands and heads farther down toward the main arm of the Celebrant. The banks of the stream are laden with flat mossy stones that give way to lush green grasses that seem steeped in dew. The water of the stream itself is clear and bright, allowing the pebbles on the bottom of the stream to be seen as they reflect the golden light from above.
21473: The stream cascades down a waterfall to the west and gathers into a small pool here. The water falls about five feet over slick mossy rocks, making travel to the west difficult to attempt. Large rocks covered with thick green algae dominate the bottom of the pool. It would be easy to slip and fall head first into the chilly waters.
21474:
A long-necked bird, with a fairly short spear-like bill stands here.
A tall stag is here, grazing peacefully.
A small grasshopper clings to a blade of grass, ready to spring.

A small stream exits from under a low wooden bridge to the north and turns east, where the water cascades over a small waterfall and gathers in a pool below. Many large flat-topped rocks are embedded into the streambed, making it easy to traverse the stream.
21476: The river enters from the west and flows away to the east, cutting a straight channel through the Golden Wood. The banks of the river are smooth and not too steep. It is possible to enter the Golden Wood to the south, but the forest to the north is thick and too difficult to traverse.
21477: The River Celebrant continues on its straight course here, flowing from west to east. Its north bank, crowned by great, thick-trunked, silvery mellyrn, is steep and the land there is not accessible from the water. The trees to the south are much smaller and thinner; they are beeches and elms, the companions to the mellyrn of the Golden Wood.
21478: On this stretch the river continues on its course from the west to the east. It is a swift and cold river. Arising from the its chill source high in the Misty Mountains to the west, it carries no dirt or mud to discolour its clear and bright water. A steep riverbank looms to the north; it appears difficult to climb.
21479: The river bends from the west to the south, its swift clear waters continuing their course ever eastward, toward the fair elven city that lies within the Naith. Only the true of heart may attempt to cross into the Naith, and as one peers into the forest ahead, it is not even possible to fathom how many eyes are watching.
21480: The Celebrant makes a bend from the north to the east. The clear waters make it possible to catch an occasional glimpse of the fish that swim just below the surface of this life-giving river. These fish help feed the elven inhabitants of the Golden Wood, while the waters sustain a myriad of plant life.
21481:
The prominent fin of a silver-yellow fish breaks the surface of the water.
A large sturgeon swims slowly along the bottom.

The river takes a sharp southward turn here, leaving small whirlpools in the recesses of the northern bank. Small golden flowers washed away from the shore are captured in those eddies and dance rapidly in circles upon the shimmering silver carpet of Celebrant before getting caught up in the current and disappearing downstream. The mallorn-trees of gold and silver grow on the banks of Silverlode. A tiny trail is hugging it very closely from the north.
21482: The Silverlode bends east here, guarding the southern border of the Gore from the tumults of the world beyond. Elves call it the Naith of Lorien - the land that lies like a spearhead between the arms of Celebrant and Anduin the Great. It is well protected indeed, for evil is loth to cross the shining cold waters of the stream which has been touched by the mysterious powers of the Lady of the Golden Wood.
21483: Swift and strong runs the river here. Clean and deep are its waters. Many small stones are scattered over its bottom carried down here from the Misty Mountains and then away toward Anduin. A great golden forest rises on its banks, its trees standing above the water like timeless guardians of the First Age protecting the last remnant of the Elder Days left on Middle-earth.
21484:
A trout swims here.
The prominent fin of a silver-yellow fish breaks the surface of the water.
A large beaver is here, gnawing on a piece of wood.

The cold waters of Celebrant dance and ripple with many colours as it makes its way east. Mighty golden trees line the banks, their boughs gently swaying in the wind. The forest is sparse to the south, but it thickens north as if trying to conceal the mysteries that lie within the Naith of Lorien, perhaps the most perilous and beautiful place in the waking world.
21485: The prominent fin of a silver-yellow fish breaks the surface of the water.

Tall trees with golden crowns reflect in the river. Silverlode they call it in the far lands, perhaps for the silvery trunks of the trees that reflect in its water giving it an elusive quality. A small trail runs in and out of the forest along the north bank. Watchfulness permeates the wood on either side of the river, for no evil can cross it undetected and walk the Naith of Lorien unpunished.
21486: Entering a narrow passage in the ravine, the river hurls itself forward at an incredible pace, smashing into the rocky walls and sending out a deafening roar accompanied by a spray of white foam. Like sentinels, the grey-clad mellyrn stand above, silently observing your passage.
21487: As the wooded river banks close in, the languid flow of the Celebrant quickens, hurrying eastward. The voice of the water pouring over the stones is sent splashing and babbling into the sparse stands of mellyrn on either side. On the northern bank a small trail follows the river, darting in and out of sight as it winds amongst the great grey boles of the trees.
21488: Celebrant becomes narrower here, turning fast, deep, and furious. The banks stand high on either side and fall off sharply providing little foothold. Mallorn trees, Lorien's faithful guardians, shield the riverbanks in a thick endless fence, beckoning one to continue east as the stream flows, rather then risk the forest fortress of the magic powers that hold this land.
21489: The river falls down a shallow stair, which is not tall enough to cause a splash. A thin layer of mist gathers above the water downstream compounding the mystique of the forest of tall silvery trees that grow along the banks. The trees grow as far as the eye can see, upriver and downriver, on both banks along the stream that swiftly appears from the west and, just as rapidly, vanishes in the east.
21490:
A trout swims here.
A trout swims here.

Silverlode journeys across the land from the springs of Dimrill Dale. Joined by many smaller streams, it becomes a swift and powerful river. Its surface, playfully uneven, flickers with distorted reflections of the mallorn trees that flank its sides. Its waters are clear, and small fish can be seen darting here and there near the banks.
21491:
A trout swims here.
A trout swims here.
A fat carp swims here.

Transitory, yet magnificent and calming, the waters of Celebrant speed to their ultimate destination. Irrevocably, they rush in a shower of falling stars, never to see this place again, yet still a part of the whole. They are droplets of water that may have heard Ulmo speak at the dawn of the First Age, or have been part of the treacherous currents that swallowed Numenor of the damned when the world was transformed. No one will know, for they will hold their peace forever.
21492: The river is wide and open here. Tall mellyrn that flank its banks raise their arms toward the stars and do not intrude upon the river. The sky of Lorien is reflected in the water, on clear days transforming the middle of the river into an interplay of blues and whites instead of Celebrant's customary silver.
21493:
A salmon swims here.
A large sturgeon swims slowly along the bottom.
The prominent fin of a silver-yellow fish breaks the surface of the water.
The prominent fin of a silver-yellow fish breaks the surface of the water.

The river flows east here. The grey and gold forest on both sides is interrupted north by a small depressed clearing, barely visible from the river but for two square pillars of white stone. An image of a star is carved into the misaligned top of the east most column. The guiding rune seems to shimmer in the shadow of the trees, its light a memory of comfort to the weary, a glimmer of hope for the dispirited.
21494:
A small plant grows here, with long, pointed leaves and flowers at its top.
A fallow deer is grazing peacefully here.
An elf, clad in the garments of a woodsman, moves stealthily among the trees.

The forest opens up to the river Celebrant both to the north and west. Across the river, the Golden Wood seems to glow with a radiance that is less tangible than simple light. The wet, mouldy leaves of elms and birches litter the ground.
21495: The forest is dominated by a row of large broad-leafed elm trees that line the banks of the Celebrant. The river rushes by just north of this place, while the large elms with their thick trunks overhang it, creating a canopy beneath which the water flows. Intermingled with the darker trees are a few stark white birch trees and a few mellyrn.
21496:
An elf, clad in the garments of a woodsman, moves stealthily among the trees.
A fallow deer is grazing peacefully here.

The forest floor is wet and muddy here, most likely a result of river water seeping up through the soil. The roots of the trees are exposed in some spots, tangled in gigantic limb-like snarls that cannot find proper grounding in this muddy area. A large elm has fallen, its root base sticking up into the air like some grotesque spider.
21497: The ground is soft and moist here, giving the plant-life in this area little support for deep roots. Small, lithe birch trees have flourished here where the heavier, thicker mellyrn and elm trees could not. The muddy forest continues to the west. Drier ground can be spied to the east.
21498: In this part of the forest a few great jagged rocks protrude from the earth. As ancient as if left over from the time when this land was shaped by the great, tumultuous battles of old, these spears of rock have been dulled over the ages by both wind and rain. Still their looming presence sparks awe and wonder at the powers of old.
21499: A fallow deer is grazing peacefully here.

Here a huge branch has fallen, due to a recent storm as it appears. It is possible to get around the branch by squeezing close to the great trees that rise all around. The fallen branch has opened up a patch of the forest sky, and already hordes of vines, brush, and saplings have grown up and around the branch.
21500: The river rushes past to the north of here. The sound of rushing water is close and loud, but the thick elms that line the riverbank make travelling to the north quite impossible. All around, the dark-leafed trees spread their broad branches. The forest continues to the west, south and east.
21501: On the Bank of the Celebrant
The large elk gazes coldly at you, chewing on a small branch.

Swift and deep, the Silverlode, Celebrant in the elven tongue, flows by to the north of here. The bank of the river is covered with mosses of various pale yellows and greens. Perpetually slick and wet, the black stones at the edge of the river offset the colours of the mosses. A cluster of birches can be seen to the south. Large beech and elm trees loom to the east where the forest gets thicker.
21502: On the Bank of the Celebrant

Delicate golden blooms adorn the ground like a cascade of stars.
Several blooms of snow-white and palest green cover the ground.

The forest gives way to the river Celebrant, which flows past to the north and west. The mossy bank is damp with moisture from the river. Dense clusters of pale niphredil and yellow elanor sprout up on this rich and fertile river bank. All around the mallorn trees grow tall, their foliage seeming like a reflection of the carpet of golden blooms that blanket the ground at their feet.
21507: The woodland opens up by the bank of the Celebrant. The flowing waters stream by to the south and east of this point of land that juts out into the river bend. Light green mosses and ferns mixed with mallorn saplings dot the landscape, and the steep descent into a narrow, but deep gully precludes travel to the west.
21512:
A roe deer is standing here, watching the terrain while chewing the vegetation.
A squirrel scampers around here, looking for nuts from the trees.

A huge rent in the forest floor opens to the east. The forest floor drops off sharply, making travel that way impossible. It looks as if some massive blade sliced the very earth itself, leaving a deep cut that is slowly being filled up with old leaves and golden blooms.
21513:
A finch flies low above the ground.
A squirrel scampers around here, looking for nuts from the trees.

The golden forest unfolds its beauty for all to see. The tall, silvery grey mellyrn stand in lines in this part of the forest, creating a corridor from north to south. Their blossom-laden or leaf-laden boughs dip and sway, making their leaves or golden flowers dance in the breeze. On the forest floor, flowers of light purple, pale yellow and bright white grow in abundance.
21514:
Delicate golden blooms adorn the ground like a cascade of stars.
Several blooms of snow-white and palest green cover the ground.
A finch flies low above the ground.

All around, the immense mallorn trees heave their silvery trunks toward the heavens. During the day, the golden tree-crowns filter the sunlight from above, casting warm golden hues over everything that dwells in this peaceful wood. The yellow elanor and pale niphredil flowers are abundant here, dotting the lush grasses and growing in clusters at the base of the mighty mellyrn.
21515:
A finely crafted crystal lamp is hanging from a tree branch.
A nightingale is here, chirping a sweet melody.

This narrow trail is lined with majestic mellyrn, their great boughs spread wide overhead, creating a canopy. Occasionally a golden flower floats down from above and glides softly to the moist green turf. The turf is spotted with holes and divots; apparently a family of squirrels or other small animals has been storing food here.
21516: A finely crafted crystal lamp is hanging from a tree branch.

Covered with green grass, the forest trail runs from the west to the east. The sound of running water comes from somewhere nearby. Mallorn trees seem to guide the path; to the north the majestic silvery trunks block passage, but the Golden Wood can be entered to the south.
21517: A finely crafted crystal lamp is hanging from a tree branch.

This small bridge offers a vantage point over the area. The Golden Wood is all about you; mellyrn of various heights raise their stout, silvery trunks high to the canopy above. Laden by foliage and blossoms, the branches sway slowly from side to side as a gentle wind blows through, bringing sweet smells to your nose and lilting notes of the forest to your ears.
21518: A sparrow is flapping around on the ground.

The forest grows dense here. The great silvery arms of the mellyrn intertwine to create a patchwork of green and pale golden hues that mask the view above after only ten feet or so. Soft winds whisper through the trees. Occasionally the melodic tune of the rustling mallorn boughs is punctuated by a bird call. Barely visible among the grey trunks, a silvery stripe hangs from one of the larger mallorn-trees.
21519: The green grass here is reminiscent of freshly fallen snow because it looks as if no living being has ever tread upon it. The canopy of leaves and branches conceals the sky, yet the light from above is still able to make its way down through the mallorn boughs in bright slants.
21520: A finch flies low above the ground.

A deep gash in the ground opens to the west; the drop is sharp and steep. A mighty event must have caused such a huge opening to form in the floor of the Golden Wood itself. A solitary mallorn-tree overlooks this ravine, its great boughs sagging over the depths below.
21521: The forest is of medium thickness here. The mallorn boughs stretch from one tree to the next, blending into a living patchwork that extends all over this part of the forest. The intertwined branches work to split the light from sun or moon like a kaleidoscope, creating patches and slivers of light on the forest floor.
21522: A colourful butterfly is fluttering around here.

This dense forest is populated with mallorn-trees, birches, occasional elms and various low-lying bushes and shrubs. The foliage of the trees has clogged the sky overhead, making this part of the forest a bit darker than the Golden Wood to the north.
21523: The trees of this forest seem to glint and catch any rays of light from all around, bouncing them off their silvery and pale white trunks and tangling them in their golden crowns. The forest thickens to the north and east. To the south, the trees thin out and the forest opens into a clearing.
21524:
Delicate golden blooms adorn the ground like a cascade of stars.
Several blooms of snow-white and palest green cover the ground.

The forest opens up into a clearing at this point. The large mallorn-trees have stepped aside, opening the glade to the full radiance of the sun during the day and giving many flowers and flowering shrubs a chance to flourish. Here the yellow elanor, the pale niphredil and many other forest flowers fill the air with their sweet aroma.
21525: The land slopes down toward the south. Barely audible among the noises of the forest, the sound of running water can be heard from that direction. To the north the forest thickens. Sweet woodland smells waft to your nose, not over- powering but sweetly enticing, might be thought to beckon you deeper inside.
21526: The forest opens up here. The rushing Celebrant can be seen to the south and the vast expanse of the Golden Wood lies to the north. The running water has slowly eroded the water bank, leaving the deep brown silty earth exposed. Massive tree-roots are protruding from the banks; if the river continues to undercut the soil here, some trees may be lost to erosion.
21527: The forest opens up dramatically here, exposing the rapidly flowing Celebrant as it follows a course that began leagues away at its sources in Nanduhirion, known by men as the Dimril Dale. The clear, cold water made a long journey from this icy source above the dwarven halls of Moria, ere it came to this land.
21528: A small grasshopper clings to a blade of grass, ready to spring.

All around the silvery mellyrn stand proud and tall. Occasional signs of activity can be detected in the boughs above. Numerous shrubs and low-hanging branches hinder passage beneath the trees. The thick, green grass that covers the forest floor is deep and lush. It has grown quite tall, especially around the thick trunks of the ancient mellyrn.
21529: The forest opens up here to reveal a rocky outcropping blocking the way east. Various ferns and ivy crowd around its base, and the outcropping itself is covered with greenery. The forest trees have grown around it, and it seems to have become a permanent part of the trunk of one of the trees.
21530: The forest opens up by the bank of a small stream that runs just east of here. Close by its banks little eddies play with clusters of mallorn blooms that float on the surface of the water. Mixed in with these tiny blossoms are tiny posies of elanor. A great mallorn bough leans out over the stream; a long rope tied to it hangs lazily down, a thick knot tied at its end.
