21733: A partridge attempts to hide in the undergrowth.

The long, thin limbs of beech, larch and poplar arch gracefully outwards above the clear waters of the river Anduin. The forest floor is covered by soft, organic soil so brown that it is almost black, from which sprout a thousand varieties of flowering plants that grow right up to the river's edge. The woodlands continue east and south as far as the eye can see.
21734: These woodlands are young and healthy, comprised mainly of small deciduous trees and thick, flowering shrubs. Patches of sky are visible high above a ceiling of long, sloping tree-limbs. Every so often a grassy clearing interrupts the forest continuum, and here and there a large boulder lies sunken into the soft ground, layered with years of moss and lichen.
21735:
A buck runs swiftly from place to place, looking about warily as it grazes.
A fallow deer is grazing peacefully here.

The land here can't be summarised as either a forest or a field, but rather marks a transition between the two. Thick, soft grasses, deep enough to cover a grown man's knees, lap gently at the thin trunks of the prospering trees that sprout happily from the rich soil. To the west the forest thickens; a faint sound of rushing water can be heard from that direction. In the east the trees become more sparse, giving way to vast plains.
21746: Although these woodlands are bordered on all sides by more trees, the area is distinctly transitional. The forest here and to the north is light and airy, inhabited predominantly by slender birch trees. A similar environment exists in the west. Eastwards, a tall, scraggly bunch of trees juts up into the sky and out against a backdrop of flowing plains. Southwards, the personality of the forest undergoes a great change, as needly pines and dark earth replace the deciduous trees and soft turf found here.
21747: These woodlands are composed almost entirely of slender birch, which rise to a height of no more than ten yards. The trees grow in clusters between which may be found stretches of open turf, lending an open, airy feel to the forest. Grassy meadows lie past the northern and eastern tree line, while to the south the woodlands continue, with beech and maple trees intermingling with the familiar birch.
21748: The trees in this light and airy forest seem to belong to one of two groups, groves of which coexist while retaining distinct borders. In some areas clusters of short birch trees rise from a soft, grassy floor, their pale bark providing a stark contrast to the deep colours of the surrounding foliage. In other places, however, the green turf gives way to a brown, earthy, acorn-littered floor from which sprout groves of tall oak. The forest continues in all directions, becoming much more dense in the west.
21749: The corpse of a forest giant is lying here.

The trees here are tall, thick and healthy, growing close together and sending long, arched boughs into every inch of space exposed to the sky. Visibility in any direction is significantly impeded by the woodland growth, but it appears that the forest becomes lighter to the north and east. Drifting in from the southwest are the pounding, splashing, and gurgling sounds of a swiftly flowing river. The elevation rises in that direction.
21750: This forested spur of land is made a peninsula by the swiftly flowing river that wraps around it from west to south. The ground is very soft, indicating that there may be hollows beneath the grassy turf. Straight beech and paper-skinned birch rise from the brown soil and lean out over the water, which is deep and clear. The land rises steeply to the north and slopes away to the east; in both directions the plant growth is thick and verdant. Several large, grey boulders rest submerged in the somewhat shallower waters on the far western shore of the river.
21751:
A large owl with small sharp horns looks cautiously around it.
An elven hunter, fair and mighty, roams here warding against evil.
An elven hunter, fair and mighty, roams here warding against evil.
A tawny-coated bear is snuffling about.

This forested ridge reaches a densely wooded, rocky pinnacle before descending steeply to the swift river lying westward. The high ground continues to the north and south, whereas the terrain to the east becomes lower and the vegetation more conservatively spaced. The river beyond the western bank is noisy and frothing, becoming smooth-surfaced and serene as it bends around to the south.
21752: Moving from east to west, the upward slope of this hillside increases as the vegetation hugging the ground becomes more dense and tangled. Farther to the east, the low-lying bushes that make this terrain difficult clear out, giving way to an airy forest of tall-trunked hardwoods and slender birches. A ridge of thick vegetation continues from the northwest to the south. Distantly but clearly, the sound of a powerful river can be heard over the western ridge.
21753: The massive oak trees are by far the dominant feature here, their thick, knobby trunks a silent testament to the vast age of this forest. Clusters of thin birch trees sprout in the better-lit areas beneath the natural ceiling of broad oak branches, their papery bark and light green leaves frail and delicate in comparison to the ancient giants. The ground slopes upwards to the west, where a forested ridge can be seen in the distance running on a north-south axis.
21754:
A porcupine is waddling around here, its tail full of sharp quills.
A furry, striped raccoon is here, nosing around for some berries or roots.

An ancient and healthy forest begins here and spreads away to the south and west. The oak and birch trees that dominate the woodland setting are tall and well-spaced, so that visibility in those directions is substantial. In the east, a sheltered meadow is like a hidden cove branching off of the massive sea of grass which stretches into the northern horizon.
21755: Bordered on the south and west by a light forest and to the east by a brush-covered slope, this green meadow is well sheltered from wind and view. The grass covering the earth is soft and delicate-bladed, unlike the tall, tough variety growing in the grasslands visible northwards. Here and there oak and birch trees sprout from the living carpet, spreading their boughs in a high ceiling that adds to the hidden feel of this glade.
21756: A small cluster of clover grows here.

Lush, green grasses of several varieties coat rolling slopes like a highly textured layer of paint. The grasslands continue to the north and east, where the terrain becomes flatter and windblown and the vegetation is less verdant. Moving west or south, peaceful meadows give way to the trunks and boughs of a light, healthy forest.
21757: A badger is here, exploring for food.

The plant life inhabiting these plains is more varied here than to the north and east, where the grasslands roll redundantly off into the horizon. Small flowers sit atop green shoots which are thin but surprisingly hearty, providing colourful contrast to the broad-bladed grasses which dominate the landscape. The ground has a slight upward slope to the south and west, as if it were rising to meet the hardwood forest which grows there.
21758: The tall grasslands growing unfettered in the north and east have become docile and unobtrusive as they transition into stately woodlands. In contrast to those rolling plains, the ground here is covered by a soft, green layer of turf no more than two inches in height. Thick-trunked oak trees climb high before spreading their boughs, so that this meadow has a sheltered feel even in broad daylight. More forest lies south and west.
21759: A small plant grows here, with long, pointed leaves and flowers at its top.

Tall hardwoods of myriad varieties cohabitate to form this forest, which stretches away in all directions. The air carries with it the fresh aroma of soil rich in organic content. Spotted with occasional tufts of flowers or grass, the earth is indeed fertile, as indicated by its moist, coarse feel and dark colour.
21760: A sturdy pack horse is standing here.

Woodlands from the north, south, and east come together at this lofty point to witness the marriage of two great waterways beyond the western riverbank. Celebrant, the smaller of the two rivers, splashes energetically as the currents pull its clear waters into the pounding, irresistible force of the mighty Anduin. Many miles to the west, beyond this aquatic nexus, the Celebrant can be seen winding upwards into a tall forest of golden hue.
21761: A woodpecker is here, tapping on a tree.

This wild outcropping lies on a higher elevation than the surrounding lands, affording an excellent panoramic view when weather allows. The immediate area is covered by low, wide trees sprouting from rocky soil between massive, grey boulders. The earth drops off steeply to the west, where a mighty river pounds powerfully against a sheer cliff side. Travel in that direction is clearly impossible. The forested ridge continues to the north and south, while in the east a thickly forested slope gives way to a healthy forest. Farther off in the east, the woodlands falter and give way to a wide expanse of plains. Westwards, across the powerful Anduin, a majestic lawn opens between tall trees of golden hue. Barely visible beyond this ancient forest, the sharp peaks of a vast mountain range provide a snow-capped backdrop.
21762: This forest is dense and overgrown, yet no plant seems to thrive at another's expense. Visibility in any direction is limited by a layer of smaller trees and bushes that grow to a height of several yards. Nevertheless, the woodlands to the east and north seem slightly more airy and open. To the west, the ground rises steeply upwards to a thickly wooded and rocky pinnacle of land, beyond which can be heard the sound of rushing water.
21763: The soil must be rich and fertile in order to support the lush habitat that exists here. Small plants and flowers mingle with taller grasses, which in turn lap at the mighty trunks of great oak and beech trees. Sounds carried down on the breeze indicate that the forest canopy is rich with birds and other warm-blooded wildlife. Plains extend to the east, while in the west the woodlands become too thick for mortal eyes to significantly penetrate.
21764: The ground here is relatively flat and covered liberally with thick, hearty grasses of several varieties. To the south and west, a thin forest can be seen rising from the sprawling green expanse. In the east, the plains flow into the horizon, changing in colour from verdant green to weathered yellow.
21765: A nightingale is here, chirping a sweet melody.

The landscape here is boring and redundant. Plains thickly overgrown with grass spread out in all directions, unhindered by mountain, forest or stream. The soil here is hard and the vegetation leathery and yellowish in colour. On the contrary, the grasslands to the south seem to impart a greener hue on the horizon. Several miles to the southwest, a change in terrain can barely be detected.
21766: The grass covering these plains is thick and sharp-edged. The vegetation rises to an average height of approximately two feet and ranges in spectrum of colour between yellow and green. Several miles to the west, a thin forest can be seen rising from the redundant grasslands. Eastward, the vast plains can be seen as far as visibility allows.
21767: A coloured game bird is visible in the vegetation, watching you warily.

The soil here is firm but soft, providing a forgiving surface for the weary-footed. Verdant grasses grow abundantly from the fertile earth, reaching over a yard in height. Moving westward, the vegetation becomes softer and taller still, so that one might initially mistake the line of trees in that direction for towering plant life of a grassy variety.
21768: A thick forest covers this terrain, which rises steeply to the west before giving way to a sharp, brush-covered drop off. Beyond this natural boundary, a tumultuous river slides past banks of moss-covered stone and black soil. On the western bank, trees of magnificent stature grow high towards the heaven, culminating in graceful crowns of golden hue. The ground slopes downwards to the east, yielding more forest before plains eventually dominate the landscape several miles in the distance. To the south the ground level rises slightly, giving way to a rugged peak which might allow a decent view of the surroundings.
21769: A cluster of birch trees, their bark a clean shade of white, sit upon a small incline bordered to the north and west by the stately waters of the river Anduin. The forest floor is soft and healthy, woven from a dozen species of soft, broad-bladed grass. To the east, several other varieties of small to medium-sized deciduous trees mingle with the thin, peeling birch. Continuing south, the ground slopes steeply upward, and the sound of the river is louder and more violent.
21770: There are two woody, stemmed plants here.

The hardwood trees growing here are thin-trunked and well-spaced, so that large patches of sky are visible beyond their rounded tops. The forest floor is a brilliant shade of green, covered completely by a short, broad-bladed species of grass. Flowers of multiple pastel colours dot the spongy turf, lifted above ground level by slender shoots of green and brown.
21771: The beech and oak trees that form this forest are narrow-trunked and evenly spaced, so that the floor beneath their boughs is well lit and airy. The area between the trees is covered by a spongy, green, moss-like plant, that quickly springs back to its original height after being trodden upon. Several clusters of small flowers grow in the shadows of some of the smaller trees, their violet blossoms resembling five-pointed stars. The ground rises sharply to the west, where the forest becomes dense and wild.
21772: This is a land of dichotomy. A healthy forest extends far to the west, while vast grass-covered plains dominate the eastern landscape. Here, the fingers of each habitat clasp together to form a land of transition, where woodlands and grasslands coexist. Tall, hearty shoots of grass lap at the smooth-barked trunks which rise straight out of the earth, culminating in crowns of curved boughs and symmetrical leaves.
21773: No tree sprouts from these grasslands, but the effect is certainly not one of a wide, never-ending plain. To the north, west, and south, trees and grasses may be seen mingling, giving way eventually to healthy hardwood forests. Only to the east do the plains extend uninterrupted by such taller forms of plant life.
21774: The grassy vegetation becomes taller and more verdant as the broad plains drift closer to the fertile soil of the woodlands which lie some ways to the north and west. Conversely, moving eastwards the height of the grass decreases and the dominant colour of the landscape shifts from green to yellow. Far to the west, the level of the horizon rises slightly, indicating that a thicker forest grows in that direction.
21775: The land rolls gently away in all four directions, covered by thick grasses of several varieties. The hue of the vegetation is much greener to the north and west, however. Here each blade of grass is a sun-bleached shade of yellow, wilting towards the ground so that the overall height of the plant-life is quite low.
21776: A sparse but healthy forest lies to the north and west, framing these treeless lands into a corner of the wide plain which extends to the southeast. Several varieties of grass sprout from the fertile, hilly earth. Most obvious of these is a tall, wide-bladed species, which sprouts in thick bunches and reaches to heights of up to three feet. Partially hidden by this thick vegetation is another notable variety of grass, which is soft and spongy in texture and coats the soil like a sun-loving breed of moss.
21777: This forest of white-barked birch and grey-trunked larch has thinned as it meandered eastwards, and here it finally ends. The woodlands which for many miles have mingled with rolling meadows have been replaced by the grasslands. To the north, a few trees are still visible within the sea of tall grasses, but to the south and east the fields continue uninterrupted.
21778: A roughly circular grove of young larch and birch dominate this woodland setting. As they reach to the sky, their thin, flexible limbs intermingle to form a web-like ceiling of leaves and branches. Some small flowering plants dot the landscape, but for the most part the forest is carpeted with a layer of coarse soil.
21779: A badger is here, exploring for food.

The border between forest and plains is surprisingly pronounced. To the north and west, thin-trunked larch and birch trees sprout from a soft, grassy carpet, their healthy limbs stretching unopposed towards the sky. At a certain point, however, this thin forest simply stops, as if an invisible border were drawn on the ground. Beyond this roughly straight line plains of tall grass coat the hills and meander eastwards as far as the eye can see.
21780: A handful of lively, young hardwoods sprout from a rolling lawn of thick, broad-bladed grass. To the south the trees become even more sparse, marking the beginning of a great plain. Westwards lies a flowery clearing, bordered by thin woodlands similar to these.
21781: These woodlands are airy and spacious, spreading out in every direction as far as the eye can see. The ground is firm and dark brown in colour, spotted green by the occasional thin-leafed shoot. The deep, resonant sound of a mighty river drifts in from the northwest, and in this direction the land has a slight downward slope.
21782: A squirrel scampers around here, looking for nuts from the trees.

The soft earthen floor is painted green by the tall grass that grows abundantly in this clearing. The ground slopes gently down to the west, where the Anduin flows wide and deep. To the north, west, and south, young trees sprout from similar grasslands.
21785: The ancient mallorn trees here stand apart, so that the sky is visible far above their golden crowns. These trees rise from a gently swaying sea of soft grass and star-shaped flowers that seem to glimmer and change colour before your eyes. The sounds of swiftly flowing water and soft, musical voices float through the air. A small trail opens up in the east, quickly disappearing into the thick maze of silvery trunks.
21786: The golden mellyrn lend a golden hue to the landscape, which seems to glitter like an ancient treasure hoard. Tall, slender shoots spring from the ground, culminating in pale green and white bell-shaped flowers. Just to the east, a faint trail winds gracefully amidst the verdant undergrowth, but there is an elusive quality about this land that makes it impossible to gain any definitive sense of its direction.
21787:
Delicate golden blooms adorn the ground like a cascade of stars.
A finely crafted crystal lamp is hanging from a tree branch.

Overhead, mallorn boughs weave amongst each other like slender grey and gold fingers engaged in a gentle grasp. Beneath this natural ceiling a small trail weaves through the forest floor, its path having been chosen to avoid the delicate flowers that sprout from the lush green undergrowth. A rocky brook tumbles alongside the trail, filling the forest with the sound of water lightly dancing upon stone. The stream flows away to the east, where a simple stone bridge rises above the soft, living carpet. The trees are dense in the northern section of this woodland, but to the south the sky opens up above the path.
21788:
Several blooms of snow-white and palest green cover the ground.
Delicate golden blooms adorn the ground like a cascade of stars.

The sky opens above this circular glade, a small island in the sea of ancient trees visible in all directions. The ground rises to the south, where widely spread boughs of the golden-crowned mellyrn seem to reach up like immortal hands and hold the stars in place. To the north and east an unassuming path dances amid the slender shoots and jewel-like flowers.
21790: A finely crafted crystal lamp is hanging from a tree branch.

The forest here is tall and imposing, thick with growth in shades of green and gold. Upon initial inspection, it would seem to take hours to move even a short distance through this verdant woodland. A closer look at the soft carpet of grass and flowers reveals a faint pathway meandering northwards. Whoever built this trail seemed to do so with the intent of harming as little wildlife as possible. The gurgle and splash of a swift stream reaches your ears from beyond the trees to the south. To the east, the forest thins out, and a sweet-smelling breeze drifts in from that direction.
21791:
A finely crafted crystal lamp is hanging from a tree branch.
A small animal, all covered in spines, snuffles amongst the undergrowth.

This verdant forest is composed of thick green undergrowth sheltered by tall, proud mallorn-trees. A narrow trail forms a winding line of dark, organic brown colour that meanders on a general north-south axis. To the north and east the gurgles and splashes of a small stream reach your ears. Although the source of these sounds is hidden behind the wide trunks of the golden-crested mellyrn, their intensity suggests the running water is quite close.
21792: A finely crafted crystal lamp is hanging from a tree branch.

This bridge is but a narrow arc of weather-beaten stones spanning a lively brook, which splashes and gurgles over speckled grey stones. Barely two feet wide, this structure has no posts, railings, or other visible reinforcements. Nevertheless it is solid and unmoving, a model of simplicity but certainly not of amateur construction. The stones are ancient and carved to fit so masterfully that at first glance the bridge appears one giant curve of solid rock. Countless varieties of moss and lichen cover those areas of the bridge not directly walked upon, so that the structure almost appears to be just another living organism sprouting from the soft, fertile soil.
21793: A finely crafted crystal lamp is hanging from a tree branch.

The trail here is narrow and does not intrude far into the surrounding woodlands. The path is smooth, firm, and slightly concave, making for utmost ease of travel. From the south the sound of swiftly flowing water reaches your ears, and a simple stone bridge can be seen rising from the earthen path in that direction. Stately mallorn-trees rise from the lush green forest floor, their tops golden and graceful.
21794:
A long-tailed bird watches you from the vegetation.
An elven lady is walking around here.

The bank of the Celebrant slopes steeply southward, almost as if the forest itself longed to join the clear water as it rushes away eastwards toward the great river Anduin. Yet the trees stand dense upon the bank, giving little heed to the rocky slope that lies beneath them and about their great grey roots.
21795: An elf, clad in the garments of a woodsman, moves stealthily among the trees.

Running steadily southward towards the Celebrant, the small stream crosses a forest trail. Small stones have been placed to ease the passage across the swift waters. The swift stream continues on into the forest, soon disappearing from view, while the trail marches onwards through the forest towards a distant goal.
21796: Several blooms of snow-white and palest green cover the ground.

The forest is sparse here, proudly striving towards the sky, as if to catch the bright stars above. In daytime the light of the heavens dispels all shadows, nurturing a lush and green undergrowth that has spread out like a soft green carpet, covering all of the ground that you can see.
21797:
A clear spring babbles as cool water trickles out of the ground.
A brook trout is here, swimming in the current.
A brook trout is here, swimming in the current.

Sparkling and shining in the light from the stars, the city of Caras Galadhon, and the sun, a babbling stream emerges from the ground here and starts the long journey through the forest towards the great rivers. Running amidst the tall grey trees that are the heart of the Golden Wood, the stream almost seems to tease the forest it leaves behind.
21798: The forest grows more sparse here, the mellyrn standing farther apart, allowing the undergrowth to expand and grow into a lush, flowing carpet that covers and caresses the soil of Lothlorien. From the south, you can hear the soft babbling of a small brook and in the distance, you hear faint voices that are carried through the woods from the green mound of Caras Galadhon.
21799: A dense carpet of blue flowers dip their heads in the breeze.

The ground here slopes up from the east to the west, where on top of the slope a road runs through the forest, bending as it approaches the great hill of Caras Galadhon. A gentle wind blows from the green hilltop, bringing music and sounds of singing and laughter. A line of white birches rises at the bottom of the eastward slope, marking the border of the realm of mellyrn and the start of the ordinary forest. A feeling of remoteness is about the birches, yet they seem to drink the air of Lorien with every branch and twig.
21800: Before the Walls of Caras Galadhon
An elf of the Galadhrim is walking around here.

The road turns from the north to the west, following the brink of a deep fosse. The sides of the fosse are almost vertical and covered in grass, while its bottom is concealed in green dusk. Upon the distant side of the fosse there rises to a great height a green wall encircling a grassy hill thronged with mallorn trees taller than any of the trees in the forest. Their height cannot be guessed, but they stand like living towers, and amid their branches countless lights are gleaming, green and gold and silver.
21801: A robin is here, carrying small pieces of wood to its nest.

Two forest roads end here at the base of a white stone staircase leading up to the paved road that encircles the green walls of the fair Caras Galadhon. The white stairs are sprinkled with red, green, blue and silvery sparks which glitter like the jewelled dust that, according to the legends of the First Age, sparkled on the quays of Alqualonde and the stairs of Tirion upon Tuna.
21802: A Road through the Golden Wood

Two winding lines of round white stones trace the southern and the northern edges of the grass-covered road. White and blue flowers grow between and around the stones in a seemingly random pattern, spots of blue scattered among the spots of white as if the flowers were playing tag. The golden trees that grow on both sides of the road seem to stay at a respectful distance from the lines of stones, as if unwilling to disrupt the work of an unknown gardener or architect.
21803: At a Bend in the Forest Road

Golden trees stand densely to the north and the south of the road that turns from the east to the north, skirting a fern-covered slope to the west. Like stars or tiny flowers, bright sparks of different colours, red, purple, blue and yellow, seem to glimmer here and there among the ferns on the slope, blinking out of existence when one tries to examine them. Whether this is an illusion, or actual glimpses of something hidden beneath the fronds, or minute displays of a magic innate to these great green plants, the elves that dwell in the Golden Wood might know, but a mortal eye cannot tell.
21804:
A swift and agile forest cat moves silently through the vegetation.
A blue dragonfly is circling around.

Running down to the road that crosses the forest to the north and east, this slope is entirely covered with ferns. There are many different types of ferns here, some of their fronds lacy, some splitting into sickle-shaped, round, oval or sword-like leaves. These leaves range in colour from light green, as if bleached by the sun, to the dark green of evergreen trees. No ground can be distinguished below the ferns, and of all the plants only trees rise above them, their leaves high enough to gather the sunlight before it is lost and absorbed by this green sea. If anyone were to drop something on this slope, it might never be found unless the landscape changed completely, and the ferns were driven away.
21805: A Road through the Golden Wood
An elf of the Galadhrim is walking around here.

Northwards the majestic golden forest stretches across the horizon, but to the south a low grassy slope rises from the ground. At its top, a white paved road runs by the foot of the green walls of Caras Galadhon, almost in parallel to the forest road but slightly above. At some distance in the east the two roads converge at a white staircase which seems to glitter from afar; the stone road reaches the top of the stair, and the grassy road reaches its bottom.
21806: Among the great grey trees, several elves of the Galadhrim have built their homes. Living high up in the trees upon wooden platforms, they work in harmony with the surrounding forest. Close to your west, the woods open up into a small clearing, but in all other directions the forest is dense and lies in deep shadows.
21807:
Delicate golden blooms adorn the ground like a cascade of stars.
There is a huge, pyramidal beehive here.
A bee flies around here, collecting nectar from the flowers.
A bee flies around here, collecting nectar from the flowers.
A bee flies around here, collecting nectar from the flowers.

Here in the heart of Lothlorien the proud mellyrn stand tall. The mighty boughs support a few wooden platforms nearly hidden among the branches. A few ladders stand against the grey trunks of the trees, allowing access to the lofty homes of the Galadhrim. A little bit away from the populated trees a large number of beehives stand in a small cluster of buzzing activity.
21808: A brook trout is here, swimming in the current.

Moving swiftly through the forest, the stream creates a faint veil of sound that blends with the soft whispering of the surrounding forest. The tall mellyrn surrounding the stream stretch their branches across the surface of the water, creating a dazzling display of shadow and light as the light of sun or stars falls upon the forest of Lothlorien.
21809: Gathering speed, the small stream runs swiftly and eagerly towards the deep Celebrant in the southeast. Surrounded by the solemn trees that stand tall and proud, the babbling brook sings along with the soft rustling of the wind through the boughs. The scenery, together with the winding forest trail, is splendid, almost without match.
21810: The small winding path carefully twists and turns, navigating through the maze of great boles that crowd here. The canopy above is not very dense but still blots out most of the light, creating a moving display of shadow and green as the stars and the sun move in their eternal dance across the sky. From within the far reaches of the forest, you hear the faint song of birds mixed with the happy babbling of the small forest stream lying just east and north of you.
21811: As the stream continues towards the Celebrant, the ever-accompanying path turns and crosses the flowing water. White stepping-stones have been placed in the current to ease the passage of any traveller. Vanishing into the dense forest, the trail runs on west-east, while the stream runs swiftly southward into a small crack, vanishing underground.
21812: The small path runs east and west, bordering the dense wood just to the north. From the south, you can hear the Celebrant rushing by in its stony bed, and you can barely discern the flowing water through the sparse woods. Eastwards, the forest opens up, allowing the passage of a wide road, and to the west the path crosses a small stream that happily flows southward on its quest to join greater waters.
21813: A sturdy pack horse is standing here.

Beginning just atop the sloping bank of the Celebrant, this broad and paved road runs in a straight line north, towards the fair city of the Galadhrim. Standing dense at the edge of the road, the towering mellyrn whisper softly as the wind flows through their boughs and the faint noise of the Celebrant echoes among them.
21815: Delicate golden blooms adorn the ground like a cascade of stars.

Tall grey mellyrn rise towards the sky all around you, blotting out the light and shrouding the forest in shadow. No matter which direction you turn, all you can see is more trees, standing silent and solemn, as if sharing a great secret. The few breaths of wind that manage to pass here only create faint ripples of whispers before the secrecy of the forest once again makes the Golden Wood go silent.
21816: Bordered by two straight lines of white stones, the great forest road runs directly north and south, leading from the fair Celebrant to the marvellous Caras Galadhon in the north. Standing at a respectful distance, the tall mellyrn parallel the white stones, seemingly out of reverence for the Elves that dwell within these woods.
21817: You are in the very heart of the enchanted golden forest of Lothlorien. The spacious woods stand tall here, reaching towards the heavens, almost as if yearning for something that is not of this world. Golden and grey, the mellyrn sway slowly, whispering softly as the wind gently rocks the tree-tops.
21818: The stream is growing wider and faster as it rushes forth among the great trees of the golden woods. As it runs along, broad enough now to prevent the gold-laden boughs of the ancient mellyrn from shadowing its surface, the light of the stars and the sun sends sparkling displays of light dancing about the surrounding forest.
21819: Close to the white stone road, the forest still stands dense, unaffected by the craftsmanship of the Elves. Tall and proud, the trees rise high towards the sky, preventing almost all light from reaching the ground. Still the forest is light and lush and birds thrive among the lower branches.
21820: Running just outside the great city of Caras Galadhon, this road is paved with white stones. Laid out in fine patterns, the different shades of white make the road appear alive, as the light of the city reflects from its surface. Just outside the circle of the road lie the eaves of the great Golden Wood, the enchanted forest of Lothlorien, while the inner border of the road passes by a deep, dark fosse, protecting the enclosed fair city.
21821: As the forest opens up to let the land bathe in the light of heaven, the great paved forest road meets the white stone road that circles the fair city of the Galadhrim. Just north of the cross lies the graceful bridge that is the entrance to the capitol of Lothlorien, and branching off to the east into the dense woods runs a small forest path.
21822: A long-tailed bird watches you from the vegetation.

Travelling from west to east, this small forest path follows the deep shadowed fosse surrounding the high walls of Caras Galadhon for a short distance before bidding a gentle farewell. Winding carefully among the great mallorn trees, the path soon vanishes on its continued journey eastwards. To the west, you can barely discern how the forest opens up, hinting at the passage of a larger road through the woods that lie so dense south of you. Apart from the whispering of the forest, you hear an occasional peal of laughter coming from the north, from within the fair capitol of Lothlorien that stands high upon a green hilltop, covered in tall trees of unsurpassed greatness and beauty.
21823: Here, at the bottom of the deep shadowed dike that encircles the fair city of Caras Galadhon, you can only faintly make out any details of the terrain. The bottom of the fosse is soft and moist as a small stream, emerging from high above on the slope of the hill, runs along it. The air is moist and filled with the sounds of the city that filter down from above. The soft splashing of the slowly flowing water is the only other sound that disturbs the silence. The stream seems to have an outlet, as the fosse never seems to flood.
21824: Curving softly, the deep fosse lies shrouded in shadow. A soothing splashing sound can be heard from the small stream flowing onward gently at the bottom of the elf-made ravine. High above, you can make out the glittering line that reaches across the fosse, leading from the eaves of the Golden Wood into the fair city of Caras Galadhon. A low murmur of musical voices filters down upon you with an occasional burst of merry laughter.
21825: A colourful butterfly is fluttering around here.

Running in a wide semi-circle, the white stone road that lies just outside the walls of Caras Galadhon is a work of art as well as master craftsmanship. The finely chiselled stones are laid out in such a way that they reflect the light of the city in a myriad different shades of white, creating dazzling displays of beautiful patterns.
21826: The grey trunks of the proud mellyrn rise high towards the sky in this open and spacious forest. The branches grow wide and stretch far across the open areas, covering the forest soil in green and golden shadow. As the wind gently blows, the foliage whispers softly along with the faint song of nightingales.
21827:
The corpse of a fallow deer is lying here.
The corpse of a fallow deer is lying here.
The corpse of a tall stag is lying here.
A patch of orange mushrooms springs from the ground here.

The woods stand quite sparse here, opening up to the skies. The tall grey trees tower high above you, striving forever upwards. With the forest roads so near, the underbrush is lessened here, allowing the soil to be illuminated by the occasional ray of light reaching through the green foilage. Carried from within the forest, you can hear the song of hidden birds mixed with the song and laughter of elves living in the woods.
21828: The white stones that pave the circular road are laid out to create marvellous patterns formed by the shifting of nuances, as the lights of the city reflect and bounce off the stony surface. Bordered by the dense mallorn forest and a deep shadowed fosse, the white road circles the fair city of Caras Galadhon, the capital of Lothlorien.
21829: The bottom of the deep circular fosse that surrounds the capitol of Lothlorien is enveloped in soft green shadow. You can feel the moisture in the air rising from the thin layer of water flowing along the fosse. Just southeast of you, the great hill rises, covered by the great grey trees of unmatched height and beauty.
21830: The shadows about you lie deep as you find yourself on the bottom of a deep fosse. A soft trickle of water runs along the circular base of the great green hill that is the foundation of the city of Caras Galadhon. Soft voices carry across the high green wall and the air is filled with laughter and song as yet another day passes in the enchanted realm of Lothlorien.
21831:
A large elk is standing here, chewing grass and leaves.
An elk cow gazes coldly at you, chewing on a small branch.

Protected by the magic of the Golden Wood, this land has never been touched by winter frost and knows no sharp transitions between seasons. Whatever the time of year might be in the world outside, here, on this tree-covered slope, a feeling of Spring is in the air. The green and the gold of the mallorn trees contrast with the sombre colours of the dark forest visible at a distance in the northeast as the young foliage and blossoms of flowering trees in Spring might contrast with the dark conifers that are still in the grip of Winter. Fresh scents of grass, earth and water rise from the ground and spread, carried by a soft wind.
21832: A blue dragonfly is circling around.

The soft forest floor slopes gently downwards to the east, making its way towards a timeless mallorn tree. The trunk of the great tree is smooth to the touch and silver-grey, showing no signs of old age. The elegant branches stretch towards the ground, spreading over a large flat boulder, as if trying to hide it from strangers. Patches of the sky are rarely visible through the golden-green foliage, and only a faint glow from above reaches through the tree-tops.
21833: Stretching their silvery limbs and shimmering with the golden burden upon them, the mellyrn stand tall on the forested slope, and yet the sky above their tops seems to be very close to the ground. Suspended in every opening among the branches, reflected in every drop of water on a leaf or a blade of grass, the ever-changing sky seems to be looking straight at the exposed forest floor, as if the sun, the moon, and the stars of Elbereth were watching the protected land, guarding it so evil could never enter it under their watchful eye.
21834: A coloured game bird is visible in the vegetation, watching you warily.

Half concealed by grass, low shrubs and flowers, a faint trail runs through the golden forest. To the west it climbs slightly upward, reaching the bank of a forest road. To the east it slopes down and turns north, continuing on its way to the outer reaches of Lorien and to the valley of the Great River Anduin.
21835: Among a Thick Growth of Mellyrn

A large elk is standing here, chewing grass and leaves.
The large elk gazes coldly at you, chewing on a small branch.

The mellyrn here have grown thick and broad, as if the trees were soldiers fortifying an invisible rear flank. A soft ray of light slips through the dense, towering canopy above, before finally coming to rest upon the majestic landscape below, illuminating the mellyrn with a warm, golden glow. Upon the ground is a layer of emerald-green moss, seemingly untouched by hoof or foot; it bears no unnatural scuffs or abrasions, as if a blanket of deep-green colour was draped over the forest floor to keep the roots warm and cosy.
21838:
A small campfire burns here, its low flames giving off only a little light.
An ancient she-troll waits here.

Here, in a small glade by the stream at the northeastern border of Lorien, a fire is burning on top of a small mound of stones which serves as a simple hearth. A few dry pine branches and pine cones lie at the base of the mound, obviously meant to feed the fire, which, however, seems to consume almost no fuel. Elves fear neither darkness nor shadows, but the Third Age has taught them the insecurity which used to be the lot of Men. Elves used to have no need of fire, but in the night, when the outside world approaches the borders of the Golden Wood and creatures of the dark stand, staring, on the very bank of the border stream, the fire might serve as a defence, or just as a spot of light and warmth in the dark.
21839: A green frog is here, hopping around.

A swift stream carries its clear waters through a shallow depression, forming a natural border of the forest of Lorien. The western bank is shrouded with a mist through which one can only faintly distinguish the shapes of the trees of the Golden Wood. The stream bends from the north to the east around a large grey rock which sits deeply in the sandy soil. A few yellow rockroses grow on the rock and by its sides, their colours strangely bright by contrast to the golden forest which is almost completely concealed by the mist.
21840: The Edge of the Golden Wood

The forest ground descends to the north and east in a ragged, brush-choked slope, and the golden forest thins out during the descent. Through the gaps between the trees you can see a swift stream on the border, beyond which the colours of the landscape change to ordinary brown, grey, and dull green. A faint mist hangs in the air above the stream. Although the eastern bank can be seen quite distinctly, the land in that direction seems to fade away dizzyingly fast, as if a gap of many leagues separated it from the borders of the Golden Wood.
21841: A Road through the Golden Wood
A robin is here, carrying small pieces of wood to its nest.

Tall mellyrn surround the road. On its western side the trees grow so thickly, it is as if they had been planted there to prevent passersby from straying into the forest. At some distance to the north the road reaches the border of the Golden Wood. In that direction all colours seem to fade and all shapes seem to blur, as if you were looking through a piece of uneven glass; it is as though the air itself had thickened, forming an invisible barrier.
21842: The light is dim and the air itself seems green in the deep shade of tall trees. Dark green spikes with crowns of lilac-coloured flowers surround the small gully through which a tiny stream makes its way. No golden trees grow here, and only a faint memory of their light reaches into this green place - just a distant tinge of gold, like the receding glow of a sunset when the sun has already set beyond the treetops.
21843: Tall irises stand in ranks on the sides of a small stream that runs through the forest here, emerging from an unseen opening to the west. Their wavy petals are deep blue and amethyst violet, and their dark green stems each bear three wide, flat leaves. The cool fragrance in the air about the flowers seems as refreshing as the water of the stream that trickles down into the small gully eastwards. The irises continue halfway into the gully, where they mix with other plants and finally retreat, as other flowers, lilac-coloured, on taller stems and with smaller crowns, take over the banks of the stream.
21844: A Trail through a Quiet Glade

A large thorny branched shrub is growing here.
On the shrub, there are two piles of blackberries.

Turning from the north to the west, the trail crosses a small glade. The grass in the glade is soft, and the air is almost completely still. The golden forest around is so quiet that it seems to be sleeping, and its colours seem to be dimmed. Silence reigns here, and anyone who walks into this glade finds himself trying to move noiselessly, as if to avoid disturbing the enchanted sleep of the forest. A few flowers and berries grow here, their stems and leaves clinging to the ground, and their heads hiding in the grass, as if the plants were also sleeping.
21845: A Trail through the Quiet Forest

A strange, chilly and serene feeling is in the air around the trail, that turns from the east to the south as it runs through the forest. Wintry winds do not reach into the heart of the land of Lorien, yet this part of the forest looks as if a freezing cold had once touched it, draining it of colour. The crowns of the mellyrn have paled from golden to almost silver, and the greens of the forest all seem a hue darker than normal. The drops of water on the leaves and grass look like tiny crystals of ice, and the silvery cobwebs among the boughs glitter like frost or miniature icicles. Few sounds can be heard except the ever present whisper of the wind and the occasional crack of a branch.
21846: From the west to the east, the colours of the forest change distinctly, passing from gold and bright green to pale gold, darker green and silver. The look of the forest changes together with the colours as if the fabric of the land itself was sewn together here from two different pieces, of which one is much brighter in colour than the other, the latter having weathered too many winters. The boundary seems to pass along a small trail, that runs through the forest just to the east.
21847: A light breeze sways the branches of the trees around you. Each time a stronger gust of wind passes through the forest, a gentle chiming sound comes from the west. The forest echoes the chiming with tones of its own - pale silvery, deep golden and clear like the sound of water falling. Then the wind drops, and for a moment everything is quiet, until, as though aware of the sudden silence, all the forest birds begin to sing together.
21848: Several blooms of snow-white and palest green cover the ground.

A few delicate crystal bells hang from a branch of a great mallorn tree. Low enough to be clearly visible from the ground, yet high enough to be out of reach even for the tallest of elves, the tiny bells sparkle with the colours of the rainbow and sway even in the gentlest breeze. The trees around stand still and quiet, and even the wind itself seems to stop and listen to the gentle chiming.
21849: A fallow deer is grazing peacefully here.

With every breath of the wind, a gentle silvery chiming fills the forest. Coming from the north, it spreads and multiplies like the sound of an unseen orchestra, accompanied by the singing of the woodland birds. The gold-laden tree boughs, their shadows on the ground and the forest flowers seem to sway gently in time with the music. The forest opens up to the south, where the ground slopes upwards, approaching the great mound of Cerin Amroth.
21850: At the Foot of Cerin Amroth

To the south of you rises Cerin Amroth, the tree-covered mound named in memory of Amroth, the King of Lorien, who dwelt here in the ancient days. As you look upon it, memories of the days of old come upon you in waves, as distinct as a sound or a scent and more powerful than your recent memories. It is as though in the Elder Days the world had been painted with brighter and stronger colours which are now shining through the pale fabric of this age.
21851: Several blooms of snow-white and palest green cover the ground.

The white trees and the golden trees rise around you, and the South Wind blows upon Cerin Amroth, sighing among their branches. As you listen, you can hear far off great seas upon beaches that have long since washed away, and seabirds crying whose race has vanished from the earth. A ladder hung along the bole of the tallest mallorn leads to a white flet that gleams amid the foliage.
21852:
Delicate golden blooms adorn the ground like a cascade of stars.
A blue dragonfly is circling around.

A wonder comes upon you, as if you have stepped through a high window looking on a vanished world, on which a light lies for which your language has no name. All you see is shapely, but the shapes seem at once clear cut, as if they had been first conceived and drawn at the uncovering of your eyes, and ancient as if they had endured forever. You see no colour but those you know, gold and white and blue and green, but they are fresh and poignant, as if you have at that moment first perceived them and made for them names new and wonderful. In Winter here, no heart could mourn for Summer or for Spring. No blemish or sickness or deformity can be seen in anything that grows upon the earth. On the land of Lorien there is no stain.
21853:
A blooming water-lily floats on the surface of the water.
A snowy-white egret stands here alertly.
A brook trout is here, swimming in the current.
A blue dragonfly is circling around.

Rushing down an eastward slope, a forest stream is interrupted by a low, but solid rock ledge. Over time, the waters have smoothed a depression in the sandy soil at the ledge's bottom and, overflowing, continued south. The rock ledge and tree roots on the banks let the small pool hold shape, as the stream flows through its centre. Never still, always sparkling and shimmering, the clear waters reflect the trees, the sky and the white statue of an elven maiden that stands on the ledge.
21854: A Stream in the Golden Wood

Mallorn branches hang so low over the stream it is as if the trees had knelt to wash them in the water. The water is lucid, and every shadow or line on the bottom is so clearly visible that the sandy streambed sometimes seems a sunlit hilly landscape with clouds casting shadows on it as they float by.
21855: A Stream in the Golden Wood

The ground slopes to the east, and the stream turns and gains speed, following the slope. Mallorn leaves lie on the bottom of the stream and float on its surface, some of them green and some golden, as if the water had preserved them unchanged the whole year long. The leaves in the water seem completely untouched by decay, but some are semi-transparent as if they were not real leaves, but only reflections that could disappear if somebody stirred the water.
21856:
A shrub with maple-like leaves is growing here.
On the shrub, there are two handfuls of blackcurrant berries.

The mellyrn on this low rise stretch their boughs towards the north, to the sound and the scent of running water. Closer to the stream, the golden trees are perched precariously at the very edge of dry land, dipping their long roots into the current like travellers checking the water to see if it is warm enough to enter. A small trail meanders among the mellyrn, descends to the stream and disappears in the water.
21857: Here a stream drops abruptly from the height of about twenty feet into a wide, bowl-shaped depression and fills it, forming a small lake. Fine white sand covers the shores of the lake, and many smooth stones of pearl-like colours and shapes are scattered in the sand. The stones seem to shine from the inside, and their colours seem to flow and change like the water of the stream. Sometimes the picture shifts, and for a brief instant the waters of the small lake seem the waters of the Great Sea splashing on the sand of pearls in Eldamar, the Elven-home.
21858:
A blooming water-lily floats on the surface of the water.
A river otter splashes playfully here.
A brook trout is here, swimming in the current.

The forest stream bends, passing under the tree branches that almost touch its surface, and comes splashing down a drop of about twenty feet into a small lake to the south. Rainbows hang in the fine spray above the small waterfall, where light breaks on myriad tiny droplets of water. The water is fresh and clear, yet the air seems to smell of sea salt and the spray seems to have a slightly bitter taste, like the taste of salt water.
21859: A finch flies low above the ground.

Turning from the north to the east, the forest road widens, forming a round lawn. In the centre of this smooth grassy circle a cluster of blue and white flowers grows, surrounded by small white stones. A row of larger white stones marks the lawn's border. Mellyrn surround the grassy circle, but southwards the ground drops so abruptly that only the high branches of the golden trees reach the lawn's level.
21860: On the Road through the Flowering Shrubs

Rising on the sides of the road are many brightly coloured shrubs, springing out of the ground like fountains of tiny blossoms. Every shrub is formed by many thin branches that rise directly from the ground, without a single trunk to support them. The branches are leafless, covered with tiny blooms that tint the air around them gold, pink or purple and fill it with a soft fragrance. At a distance to the northwest, the great hill of Cerin Amroth is visible, and to the west you catch a glimpse of water sparkling beyond the trees.
21861: Delicate golden blooms adorn the ground like a cascade of stars.

To the west of you stands a great mound, covered with a sward of grass as green as Spring-time in the Elder Days. Upon it, as a double crown, grow two circles of trees: the outer have bark of snowy white, and are leafless but beautiful in their shapely nakedness; the inner are mallorn trees of great height, arrayed in pale gold. High amid the branches of a towering tree that stands in the centre of all there gleams a white flet.
21862: The great mound that the Elves call Cerin Amroth rises to the west of you. Its grassy slopes climb up to the circle of white trees which crowns its top. Although about you living trees and flowers are stirred by the same cool wind that fans your face, the land around seems a timeless place that does not fade or change or fall into forgetfulness.
21863: A Trail through the Golden Wood

The trail runs through the lush undergrowth of the mallorn forest, sometimes disappearing out of sight beneath the cover of the plants. To the east it continues deeper into the forest, but to the west it follows a tiny stream that trickles down a low slope and together with the stream suddenly comes out into the open. The stream disappears among the mallorn roots, but the trail continues on its way westward, to where a tree covered mound stands tall beneath a deep luminous sky.
21864:
A finch flies low above the ground.
A nightingale is here, chirping a sweet melody.

Rising over the other trees is a great mallorn, its lofty top blackened and split in two by a lightning bolt. With the favour and aid of Yavanna, the tree survived the strike. Its branches still bear clusters of golden flowers in Spring and green and golden leaves throughout the rest of the year. Yet the unearthly power of that lightning strike seems to have affected the ancient tree, imprinting some magic in the wood forever.
21865: A Trail through the Golden Wood

Mallorn branches hang so low over the trail they tug at the hair and clothes of an unwary traveller. The golden trees themselves seem motionless. Yet with every movement of air, a windy whisper passes through the grass, rises on the warm air currents and spreads among the branches, making the leaves tremble slightly as they pass it on. The trail continues to the east and south.
21866: A Trail through the Golden Wood

A large weathered boulder sits deep in the ground here, crowned by the white and yellow flowers of a trailing plant. Stumbling upon the boulder, the trail splits itself in two tracks which run separately for a while, selecting their own paths among the tree roots until the dips and rises of the forest ground finally bring them together again. Except for the whisper of the wind in the golden crowns of the mellyrn, the forest around the trail is as quiet as if it was sleeping as forests sometimes sleep in the hour before dawn, waiting for the rising sun to wake all the birds.
21867: Though the air here is fresh, the colours bright and the shapes clear, for some reason few birds sing in this part of the forest. There is no wind or movement of the air and no sound except the sound of water slowly dripping. The golden trees standing around you seem silent as if they were bound from movement and sleeping under the spell of a deep sleep from which they could not wake.
21868: A nightingale is here, chirping a sweet melody.

A light mist rises from a glen to the south of you, and the golden trees around seem whitened as if touched by an early frost. Rime seems to cover their branches and their leaves, and though it is obviously an illusion, it is hard to shake off the vision and to see the forest again in its bright colours of green and gold.
21869: Though standing tall and proud, the golden trees here seem slightly paled and there is a sense of sadness about them. Like the Elves themselves, this immortal land cannot be touched by decay; but like the Elves themselves, this land can fade. All of the colours here are still clear, but dimmed, as fading is neither a disease nor a distortion. Yet the picture is sorrowful as the passing of such things may be when the power that keeps them unchanged can hold sway upon them no longer. Every now and then a momentary change of light makes the paleness disappear, and the golden branches radiate again in a glory that it would seem could never pass.
21870: A Road through the Golden Wood

Golden mellyrn grow on the western side of the road, and silvery birches grow on its eastern side. As different as the trees are, here they seem to be of almost the same colour; the white boles of the birches seem to be slightly tinged with gold, and the mellyrn seem to have paled, acquiring a silvery hue. Northwards the road approaches the border of Lorien, and although the edge of the Golden Wood is still miles away, one can already feel the presence of the outside world, as an alien sound bringing discord in the harmony of the land.
21871:
Several blooms of snow-white and palest green cover the ground.
A woodpecker is here, tapping on a tree.
A fallow deer is grazing peacefully here.

Slender white birches rise all around you, their branches reaching toward the sky. No mellyrn grow amid the birches, but the air around is permeated by a soft golden light, as if the radiance of the golden trees was lingering here. In the mild golden glow the green leaves of the birches seem as fresh and new, as if they were lit by the Sun of the days when Arda was young. To the west the trees part, and in the gaps between their silvery boles you can see a grassy lane running through the forest.
21872:
A beautiful, ivory coloured rose with a tint of crimson is blossoming here.
A dove rests near one of the flowers.

Narrow paths wind between the tall trees, circling small hills and tussocks crowned by clusters of blue irises, yellow daffodils, white snapdragons and lilies of many colours. The scents of the many flowers mingle in the fresh air together with a light, barely audible sound like the ringing of many tiny bells. No hedge separates this area from the surrounding forest, yet it is apparent that this is a garden, tended by caring hands and warmed by the smile of its fair gardener.
21873: The tall golden mellyrn have stepped aside, as if to give more light to the younger trees that grow here on the slightly elevated forest ground. The young mellyrn are all only about four feet tall, but their glossy leaves are already of the same colour and shape, and their slender limbs already have the same chiselled look as those of the older trees. Behind the trees to the west you can see a road running from the north to the south through the golden forest. A faint path leads north.
21874: Near the Edge of the Golden Wood

Standing at a low elevation, the golden trees watch the road that passes through the forest to the west and south. The warm air beneath the trees is calm like water in a lake - stirred only by light breezes, it allows you to see far away. The edge of the golden forest seems to lie just a few miles to the east. In that direction, ordinary trees are visible through the gold, green and silver of Lothlorien and are tinted by these colours, as if seen through a painted glass window.
21875: The road turns from the west to the south, descending from a low elevation. A faint trail runs away from the road to the east, climbing down a gentle slope. Looking in that direction, one can see an opening in the boundary of the Golden Wood where the faint golden glow in the air ebbs and flows, sometimes giving place to darker, simpler colours of the outer forests. Now and again, the diffused glow recedes, letting the stark shape of a dark pine come into vision, and then envelopes it again, giving it a dreamy enchanted look.
21876: A Road through the Golden Wood
A robin is here, carrying small pieces of wood to its nest.

Here the road dips, passing through a small depression, and then straightens and continues at its previous level. Wisps and swirls of warm mist curl above the grass, indicating that warm underground waters pass here very close to the surface. Small rainbows twinkle amid the grass, stretching from the tip of one blade of grass to the tip of another as if supported by invisible gossamer threads.
21877: A Road through the Golden Wood

The ground here slopes downward from the west to the east, and the road has to bend slightly to stay at one level. The golden trees at the western side of the road are sparse, and the ground below them is covered with a carpet of flowers. Small rose-like flowers, blue and purple, run out onto the road down the western slope and stop a few feet from the road's edge.
21878: A Road through the Golden Wood
A finch flies low above the ground.

The road runs from the north to the south through the golden forest. At a distance to the south you can see the green hill of Caras Galadhon. The elven city is still too far away to see clearly, yet it is impossible not to feel its presence. Every gaze and every movement, the course of every road, trail or stream in the land, every current of air seems to be directed to the distant city, bound by the power and light that flow from it.
21879: The Edge of the Golden Wood
A tall stag is here, grazing peacefully.

The golden trees stand slightly apart here, and in the gaps between their boles to the east and to the south you can see a wide curve of a road passing through the forest. The road makes a turn from the north to the west as it approaches a white staircase that leads up to a green wall. The white stairs glitter from afar as though covered by snow or ice, yet the glitter does not seem to be cold and remote like that of ice on a mountain peak - rather, it might remind one of the whiteness of a snowy hill atop which the lights of a village merrily twinkle.
21880: Here, beneath the eaves of the Golden Wood, a light lies on tree and shrub, on leaf and flower, on the grass and amid the branches. Clear and golden, it seems to spring not from a source in the visible world, but from the depths of time, like the light which seems to shine from the darkened pages of ancient books or from the fair elven faces unmarred by age and untouched by darkness.
21881: The air beneath the eaves of the golden forest is full of a sweet mingled scent that seems to bring forth memories, making them as distinct as scents or sounds. As they blend with the picture, even time itself begins to seem an illusion, an invention by the clock-makers for making the clocks run. Gaps of many centuries seem no greater than an hour, and deeds of a thousand years ago seem as alive as if they had happened today before breakfast. The silvery trunks, the singing of birds, the changing of light and shadows all seem to be part of one eternal picture, as old as the sun and the stars.
21882: At a Bend in the Forest Road

Turning from the west to the south, the road passes by a great chestnut tree. Coloured in earthy brown and deep green hues, the tree is sharply silhouetted against the golden, bright green and silvery grey backdrop of the mellyrn. Whether its stature and girth are due to its own life force or to the soil and the air of the Golden Wood, the tree seems quite determined to outgrow its golden neighbours. Chestnuts are scattered on the ground all around its roots, most of them broken or gnawed by the teeth of squirrels or other omnipresent forest creatures. A few saplings of the same earthy colours grow around it, their leaves smaller replicas of the leaves of the great chestnut.
21883: A Road through the Golden Wood
A finch flies low above the ground.

Changing its direction ever so slightly to avoid the rising ground, the road passes between two slopes. The northern slope is covered with mellyrn that climb high over the golden forest to watch the road from above. The southern slope is covered mostly by dark green ferns. Brightly coloured sparks glimmer here and there among the ferns, vanishing whenever one tries to focus one's eyes on them and instantly reappearing elsewhere on the slope. Ahead to the west, the road skirts a limestone outcropping and turns, disappearing from sight; eastwards it continues straight on its way through the golden forest.
21884: On a Road Passing a Limestone Outcropping

Turning from the east to the north, the forest road skirts a limestone outcropping, leaving it to the southwest. About two yards high, the outcropping is composed of a dozen layers of limestone, interspersed with a few darker stripes. The warm, even weather of the Golden Wood has allowed the greyish slab to preserve its original shape, yet the forest plants have finally begun to take their toll on it. The winds have carried some soil and seeds onto the surface of the slab and into the cracks on it, allowing many grasses and flowers to take root. Blue sage grows supported in the cracks at the base of the outcropping, and a cluster of bright stonecrops crowns its top. From beyond the outcropping, to the southwest, the singing of water is heard at a distance, where a stream seems to drop down a small waterfall.
21885: A Road through the Golden Wood

The road runs from the north to the south here, on its journey from the mound of Cerin Amroth to the elven city of Caras Galadhon. To the south, it approaches a limestone outcropping, and northwards it plunges deeper into the forest. Through some trick of light or an illusion, the grassy surface of the road to the north looks so smooth that it appears to shine, reflecting light. From beyond the trees to the west you can hear the merry babble of a forest stream, which seems to be talking too fast for you to make out any words.
21886: On a Road through the Rowan Trees
A nightingale is here, chirping a sweet melody.

The road turns from the south to the west where it widens, forming a circular lawn. Rowan trees cluster to the north and east of the road, silhouetted sharply against the backdrop of mellyrn. Their branches extend over the road, casting striped shadows across the grassy surface. Clusters of bright red and orange rowan berries hang from the branches, a delicious fare for many birds if Winter were ever to come to this land.
21887:
A patch of orange mushrooms springs from the ground here.
A robin is here, carrying small pieces of wood to its nest.

A few darker and thinner boles stand in contrast amidst the silvery boles of the mellyrn, and tracing their trunks upwards with your eyes you can see that they belong to rowans. Clusters of red berries hang from the branches of the rowans, bright yet barely noticeable amid the splendour of the golden trees.
21888: A Clearing in the Golden Wood

A large beautiful rose bush is blooming here.
Deep inside the bush, there are three red roses with leaves and thorny stems.
A robin is here, carrying small pieces of wood to its nest.

The clearing is completely overgrown with flowers. To the edge of the clearing the flowers grow in shades of white, yellow and pink. Flowers in shades of red dominate in the centre of the clearing, where a small mound is surrounded by red and orange marigolds and crowned by a bush of dark red roses. Like a golden frame encircling a jewelled ornament, golden mellyrn stand around the clearing. Their leaves, when touched by a light wind, seem to ring gently.
21889:
A large shrub grows here, its branches loosely spreading.
On the shrub, there are two piles of cherries.
An apple tree with bright green leaves grows here.
On the tree's branches are three large yellow apples.

Some warm Lorien years ago either a few saplings were planted in this clearing between the tall mellyrn, or a few cherry pits and apple seeds were dropped carelessly on the ground after a picnic. Fed by the fertile soil and the soft rains that fell on the forest day after day, the seeds or saplings have grown into large trees. Their spreading branches bear gentle pink and white blossoms in the Spring, bright green leaves in the Summer, large yellow apples or clusters of red cherries in the Autumn, and then stand leafless through the Winter watching the Sun and the Moon rise and set, and the stars roll by in the Winter sky. Elves and forest creatures come here now and then, to pay their respects to the trees and their sweet fruit.
21890: A Trail through the Golden Wood

Delicate golden blooms adorn the ground like a cascade of stars.
A fallow deer is grazing peacefully here.
A squirrel scampers around here, looking for nuts from the trees.

Winding among the boles of the trees, the trail runs west and north as it passes a large mallorn. The branches of the golden tree bend almost to the ground, and a glistening rope ladder climbs up the bole, blending with the silvery bark. The grass just below the tree is sprinkled with white and yellow flowers, growing in clusters near the base of the tree, as though somebody had spilled them there while climbing the ladder.
21891:
A bright red mushroom is growing here.
There are two mushrooms here.
A patch of star-shaped moss covers the ground.
There are two bunches of chanterelles here.
A squirrel scampers around here, looking for nuts from the trees.
A colony of red ants is here. The ants seem to ignore you.

Lying just off a small trail that passes through the forest to the west, this glade is almost entirely covered in mushrooms. Mushrooms grow in the grass, in the moss by the tree trunks and on the moss-covered stones that sit on the ground. Only the trees that stand around the glade have escaped their attention, as they rise over the host of brightly coloured caps like fairy tale giants watching a crowd of little people. The mushrooms are grey, brown, yellow, orange and red; some clearly edible, others less tempting, but most of them are unfamiliar kinds. Here and there, broken caps and stems lie on the ground where some woodland creatures feasted on their favourite fare.
21892: To the east of you the forest ground slopes down into a small glen, the sides of which are covered by soft green moss and little white flowers. A faint mist rolls slowly out of the glen, and the golden forest beyond its veil looks pale, unreal and a little sad, like a landscape seen in a dream just before you are awakened by the bright sunlight.
21893: A tall plant with a perfectly smooth stem gracefully marks the landscape.

Green moss covers the bottom of the glen, and a faint mist rises above it, white and chilly near the ground but almost invisible in the air. Behind the thin curtain of the mist, the golden trees look drawn as if with age, and pale as if an early winter was upon them.
21894: Twilight lingers in the secret glade, hidden and protected from strangers' eyes by a circle of dark elms and pale hemlock-umbels. A grey rope ladder leads up the bole of a tall elm into the canopy of tree branches. Silvery moths flutter above the soft grass, and a faint enchanting tune hangs in the air, as if an unseen piper was playing a flute, waiting for a dark-haired elf to step into the circle of trees and start a dance.
21895: A Road through the Golden Wood
A blue dragonfly is circling around.

A grass-covered lane leads through the golden forest, looking more like a recently mowed lawn than like a forest road. Golden mellyrn rise to both sides of the lane, making no attempts to step on its grassy surface, as if they had willingly moved aside to let the travellers pass.
21896: A Road through the Golden Wood
A blue dragonfly is circling around.

No wheel-tracks or hoofprints mar the springy carpet of grass which covers the road, softening every footfall. Little flowers lift their heads above the grass, as though they were curious about something and not afraid of being stepped on. Tall mellyrn rise on both sides of the road, their boles and branches slightly tilted, as if the trees were watching the passersby.
21897: A Road through the Golden Wood
A blue dragonfly is circling around.

The road runs steadily from the south to the north on its way from the city of Caras Galadhon to the outer reaches of the forest of Lothlorien. Golden trees rise around the road, and their leaves seem to be whispering and ringing at once, as if trying both to talk and to laugh. Now and then, the sounds stop for a moment and then renew, as if the forest was watching you with curiosity and barely concealed mirth.
21898: A Road through the Golden Wood

The road turns from the north to the east, passing a low hill to the west. Winds blow from the hill onto the road incessantly, making the grassy surface swirl and ripple. When the waves travelling across the road stop for a moment, the grasses straighten their blades and the pink anemones that grow by the western edge of the road rearrange their petals, only to be ruffled and brought into disarray again by the next playful breeze.
21899: A sparkling spring bursts out of the grass here and trickles back into the ground between the mallorn roots. Warmed by the rays of the sun and fed by the waters of the spring, flowers grow here as fair as any flowers on this side of the Sea, bright with the colours of dawn and the sky, their fragrance like a memory of dewy mornings under the unshadowed sun in the Spring of Arda.
21900:
An erect shrub with green pinnate leaves is growing here.
Inside the shrub, there are two piles of crimson raspberries.

Here low bushes and shrubs have claimed most of the ground between the silvery boles of the mellyrn. The undergrowth seems to be confused by the warm weather, as some of the bushes are sprouting new leaves while some are flowering and the branches of the others are bearing fruit. A few flat stones, each of them about one foot long, have been set in the ground at regular intervals, as if marking a path to tread upon. Some of the stones appear to have sunk deep into the soft turf, leaving gaps much wider than an elf could cross in one step. The path turns from the east to the west, where it turns into what appears to be a courtyard running through the forest.
21901: The Heart of the Golden Wood

The golden mellyrn rise proudly around you, their boles like chiselled grey pillars and their crowns like a sea of living gold beside which any gold of the dwarves would seem dull and bland, just a lifeless imitation of the glorious golden trees. Here under the eaves of this forest the air itself seems golden; here no evil can survive in the golden glow.
21902: The Heart of the Golden Wood
A blue dragonfly is circling around.

The colours here are breathtakingly bright and clear, and the air is as fresh and fragrant as if a wind had just brought it here from the gardens and the snow-capped mountains of Valinor. Timeless, young and ancient, the immortal golden forest stands like a palace crafted from live trees on one of the first days of creation, like a memorial to the First Age and to Arda the unmarred.
21903: A dense carpet of blue flowers dip their heads in the breeze.

The mallorn trees stand slightly apart here, reaching for each other with their long branches. The air is fresh and clear, and every sound echoes and spreads as if you were not in a forest but in a great hall with a roof of gold and pillars of silver. Above the roof of the golden crowns there seems to be yet another roof, the faraway sky, which here does not seem so distant and looks as if one could almost reach it from a golden treetop.
21904: On a Forested Hill above the Road

This hill is formed by two slopes that join at an angle, climb steeply to the highest point and then run slowly down into the golden forest. A grassy road skirts the foot of the hill, turning from the north to the east. Young mallorn trees climb up the green slopes to the golden cluster of trees that crowns the crest of the hill; the grass between their boles is starred with white and yellow flowers.
21905: The golden forest is alive with the song of nightingales in the tree branches. When the birds stop for a moment catching their breaths, the distant sound of flowing water can be heard, merging with the whisper of the leaves carried in the wind. It is impossible to determine from which direction it comes, and sometimes it seems to come from more than one source at once, as if many hidden streams were joining here on their way to Celebrant, to follow it on its journey to Anduin and to the distant Sea.
21906:
A small animal, all covered in spines, snuffles amongst the undergrowth.
A finch flies low above the ground.

Barely visible in tall grass, a faint path or trail comes from the east and ends at a low grassy mound crowned with a cluster of flowers, each one the size of a small rose, with purple petals surrounding a white core. More flowers of this kind grow at the base of the mallorn trees, looking even more shapely next to the great silvery boles. The golden radiance that permeates the air of the mallorn wood seems to cling to the purple flowers, outlining every delicate petal.
21907: A Clearing in the Golden Wood
A dove rests near one of the flowers.

This clearing looks like one of the places where Lorien elves plant the flower seeds they bring to Lorien from the other lands.
