This side of the river is the beginning of the Naith, and though the forest does not appear to be any different from that on the far side, there is a calming sense here that is not found anywhere else on Arda.
22422: The crystal clear waters rush eastward to a distant bend. The river widens a bit, allowing to get a better view of the surroundings. To the north and south the golden mallorn forest appears to continue endlessly. After the bend, the Celebrant flows northeast, where forest streams make it even more powerful a river.
22423: Small dew-drops glisten gently upon the lush undergrowth, set here by the foamy fingers of the southward lying river. The mallorn-trees are tall and strong, as daunting as mountains yet somehow as delicate as newly-sprouted blades of grass. The woodlands continue to the north, west, and east.
22424: Golden-crested trees upon high banks rise proudly on either side of this river as it meanders steadily over rounded grey stones speckled with black. The water appears clear and fresh. To the east the river begins to alter its course from east-west to north-south.
22426: On the Fringes of the Forest

A line of low shrubbery and other vegetation borders the forest here, southwards blending to the low, dry grass. In the north the massive, cool and shady forest, yet but a tiny area of the huge Golden Wood, stands majestically. The air seems aglow with a faint golden shine.
22427: The path continues on its east-west course, making its way through the undergrowth around the thick silver-grey trees. The higher mellyrn shadow the forest floor, but in the golden glow under the mallorn branches many plants and flowers flourish. From the northwest you can hear the roaring of the river as it rushes on its course through the forest.
22428: The steep, rocky river bank is littered with debris. Branches and splinters of wood lie scattered all about. The roaring river sprays white foam and bursts of water onto the naked rock, making it slippery and wet. The roaring of the river is deafening and the thunderous noise drowns out all other sounds. Higher up the slope, the great mellyrn stand towering towards the sky, blocking your view.
22429: The steep river bank is full of branches and debris. A few smaller trees have managed to creep down to the riverside, but the taller, wiser mellyrn stand farther from the river, packed densely on the upper reaches of the slope. Blending with the sound of the rushing water, the whispers of the golden forest surround and envelope you.
22430: The steep grade of the river bank has not prevented the trees from growing at will here. The growth is not particularly dense, nor is it of any great height, but the trees still seem to thrive. Farther south the woods grow dense and high as the land once more becomes rather flat.
22431: The riverbank is less steep here and cluttered with small rocks and boulders and the occasional debris floating ashore from the Celebrant. The few mellyrn that stand silently on the bank are not as tall, but still give the impression of peace and solemnity, projecting an aura of strength.
22432: Standing rather thin, the mellyrn here have managed to grow to a stunning height, climbing high up towards the skies. Light shines playfully among the branches and the foliage is lit up by the glow of the stars and the sun. The towering trees are ancient and solemn and they stand silent, forever watching and guarding the realm of Lothlorien.
22433: A mountain mule is standing here, ridden by you.

Towering high and proud, these great trees strive towards the sky, forever reaching and yearning for the light. Standing rather sparsely, they have given each other ample room for growth and strength, thus allowing to reach enormous height. Even though the mallorn trees are very tall, they allow the light of the heavens to fall upon the forest soil, letting many smaller bushes and shrubs flower among the great silvery boles.
22434: Here the forest is comprised mostly of mellyrn. Far in the northeast, behind a thicker row of trees, the sounds of a river rushing through its rocky channel can be heard. Here the forest is open and easy to travel through. The effect of Lothlorien can be felt even here, such is the power it radiates; yet this effect seems to dwindle to the southeast, where the forest thins and appears less densely populated.
22435: A mix of mellyrn and smaller, ordinary trees grows here on the border of the Golden Wood. Although it seems that this area of the forest is not travelled very often, closer inspection of the undergrowth reveals a small path travelling north into the forest.
22436: A squirrel scampers around here, looking for nuts from the trees.

The trees do not grow densely packed here, but leave plenty of room for other plant life and gradually thin out to the south. Shrubbery and moss dominates the landscape, but progress is fairly comfortable. To the west the silvery and golden mellyrn can be seen growing on the border of the Golden Wood.
22437: Prickly, white-stemmed plants, with blue flower heads grow in abundance.

Despite the dry climate various plant species seem to thrive on these open plains. Some signs of wildlife are visible as well, the foot-long grass and shrubs providing ample shelter and nourishment for many animals in the area. A dried streambed can be seen to the south.
22438: A swallow flies high above the ground.

Almost completely crumbled, the channel of an ancient stream is still visible here, although instead of water it is now filled by low shrubbery. Southward the channel crosses an old path, pushing farther through a valley. On the old river banks tufts of green grass line the course of the channel.
22439: A faint trail runs here, diving into the dried channel and crossing the streambed, which is quite shallow here. It seems that this is an ancient ford over the stream. Though the trail here is probably very seldom used it is not overgrown at all; the grass grows very sparsely here for some reason.
22440: It seems that a farm once stood here, as the stony foundations of several buildings can still be seen even though nature seems to be taking over. Grass and low shrubbery covers everything; the walls have crumbled long ago and the interiors of the foundations are filled with dirt. The lands around the farm now seem bare and infertile and not suitable for cultivation at all. The farm was probably abandonded long ago.
22441: The dusty path climbs the steep hillside at this place, ascending from the dried-up ford in the west towards the hills in the east. The path is faint and seems to be rarely trodden nowadays. Perhaps it served traders and travellers better once, when the times were better and the valley green and cultivated.
22442:
A clean fragrance drifts up from a thick clump of leaves.
A grey wolf is here, snarling aggressively.

This grassy area slopes upwards slightly to the east, nearing a hilly area. To the west an old riverbed can be made out; it appears to be dry now. The land here is covered with wildlife and greenery and seems like a very lively place despite the lack of tending.
22443: A cluster of dark green, feathery fronds flourishes in the shade.

Passage through the light shrubbery is not difficult. The bushes have small, narrow leaves and some seem to grow small thorns, perhaps as a way of warding off small animals. The flora here seems to thrive in its environment. The ground is uneven and criss-crossed by plant roots.
22444: A thicket of bushes here, a tangle of branches there, yet mostly this forest is quite light and easily lets a traveller through. Soft clumps of bushes grow around, their leaves showing many vivid hues of green. The forest floor is covered by a layer of fallen leaves and other debris.
22445: A beautiful and docile horse is standing here.

A smooth, grassy field borders the edge of the forest in the north. Many kinds of plants make up a uniform carpet of grass here, dotted only by an occasional patch of shrubbery. No flowers appear to grow here, but the air carries a sweet scent from the direction of the forest.
22446: Not many mellyrn grow here, and other trees take over instead. Though they are ordinary, broad-leaved trees they seem strangely tall and healthy. A feeling of health seems to rest in this forest, and a tired traveller could find peace and refreshment from the mere atmosphere of these woods.
22447: A great dark-grey horse stamps restively.

Here, close to the heart of Lothlorien, you can feel the agelessness of the forest. The tall mellyrn standing all about reach high, striving towards the sky, almost as if trying the reach the stars. Solemn and silent, they only pass on an occasional whisper as the wind carefully rocks the enchanted forest.
22448: A great dark-grey horse stamps restively.

The forest stands rather sparse here, allowing for a light and colourful scene, the light passing down through the golden canopy above to spill across the forest floor. The sparkling play of shadow and light creates dancing shapes of green, gold and grey, moving playfully among the tall grey trunks of the towering mellyrn. From within the forest, you can hear the song of nightingales as well as the whispering of the wind through the trees. Just north and west of here, the ground begins to slope gently down towards the river Celebrant, which can just barely be heard through the woods.
22449: A great dark-grey horse stamps restively.

Sloping downwards towards the beautiful river Celebrant, the bank is still not too steep for the great trees of the enchanted forest. Tall grey mellyrn stand sparsely lined, allowing the sound of the flowing water to travel farther into the woods, where it blends with the soft whisper of the trees and the faint song of hidden nightingales.
22450:
A sturdy pack horse is standing here.
A stocky mountain mule is here, waiting to serve.

A small clearing lies here, open to the sky above and encircled by the densely growing mellyrn of the Golden Wood. The grass of the clearing is lush and of a rich, deep green, though some small patches have been trampled with the hooves of passing animals. In the soft soil, a few old hoofprints can be seen. Just outside the clearing, among the great grey trees, stands a small wooden structure. The small building consists of a roof on wooden pillars and a single wall to shelter the horses from the soft rains that pour down on occasion.
22452: The air is moist here and filled with the sounds of water flowing gently among the great trunks of the mellyrn. The joyous sound of the rushing Celebrant blends with the song of hidden birds to create a serene background of peace and tranquility.
22453: Several blooms of snow-white and palest green cover the ground.

The calm waters of the Celebrant form a smooth bend to the north and east, creating a short, rounded peninsula of tree-topped land. Proud mellyrn of unfathomable age are rooted firmly in the soil, surrounded by myriad species of lush, green grass. Here and there long-stemmed flowers sprout from the soft floor, crowned with diamond-shaped petals of pale green and blue.
22454:
Delicate golden blooms adorn the ground like a cascade of stars.
A nightingale is here, chirping a sweet melody.

The mallorn-trees are packed closely together, so that looking up you only see a golden sky of intertwined tree-limbs punctuated by flashes of brilliant silver. In every direction the forest radiates a thousand hues of green and gold. Shadows abound in the west, but no sense of evil radiates from that direction. The breeze carries with it sad melodies of songs unknown or long forgotten.
22455: The shadows lie deep amongst the grey trunks of the mellyrn as they stand tall and dense here, dispelling all light before it reaches the forest floor. Nevertheless, the shadows are not hostile as they are a natural part of the woods. You can barely discern shapes moving within them, happily accepting the shade for what it is. Despite the lack of direct sunlight, the undergrowth has grown here thick enough to hinder movement.
22456: Several blooms of snow-white and palest green cover the ground.

You are surrounded by trees, the towering great mellyrn eternally reaching towards the sky. Immersed in shadow, the forest stands solemn and silent around you. The thick undergrowth hinders any movement. Only an occasional whisper, as a gentle breeze rocks the trees, disturbs the peace of the enchanted wood. No matter which direction you gaze, the forest lies dense, expanding out toward the horizon.
22457: The grey trees stand tall here, shrouded in shadow as only few rays of light permeate the dense canopy to create swirling displays of green and yellow. Even so, the shadows are not dark and threatening, but rather grey-green, and provide protection for the smaller creatures wishing to avoid the watchful eye. The soft song of nightingales can be heard from within the deeper reaches of the forest, as well as the soft whisper of the branches swaying gently in the wind.
22458: Delicate golden blooms adorn the ground like a cascade of stars.

Standing tall and proud, the grey and golden mellyrn rise high towards the sky, almost as if reaching for the beloved stars of the Galadhrim. The forest is quiet and solemn, disturbed only by the birds singing softly from the cover of the lush green boughs and the soft whispering of the wind as it gently rocks the swaying trees.
22459: The ancient forest of the enchanted realm of Lothlorien, the Golden Wood, is surrounding you, immersing you in soft shadow and the gentle whispers of the mellyrn. Grey and proud they stand, towering towards the sky as a reminder of the power and beauty dwelling within the forest borders.
22460: You find yourself at the very edge of the Golden Wood. North and west, the grey and golden mellyrn of Lothlorien rise towards the sky as a reminder of the mystery and power residing within. To the east, the forest is of another kind, still ancient and alive, but not of the Golden Wood. Southward the terrain opens up into a grassy plain.
22461: Beech, oak, and poplar trees grow tall and straight in this forest, many winters having passed since their conception. Nevertheless, the most ancient tree in this woodland appears a mere sapling when compared with the great mallorn-trees that tower above you in the north. The silence here is thick and pervasive, yet these woods do not feel unwatched.
22462: The tall, straight trunks of the mallorn trees are spaced so that each has precisely enough room to spread its golden crown high in the sky. The limbs of these ancient giants are broad and strong, growing off the main trunks at wide, upswept angles. Soft, delicate sounds, like a combination of song and laughter, drift down from the natural ceiling, but the foliage is too dense to discover their origin. The forest floor is soft and grassy; here and there white and pale green flowers with star-shaped petals poke up through the green carpet. In other places, larger, star-shaped blossoms of silver and gold sit upon slender, green stalks.
22463: The forest is ancient and magical, powerful and fragile at the same time. Smooth, silvery trunks give way to a natural ceiling of gold and grey, suspended upon upswept limbs of considerable girth. In contrast to these sturdy giants, who seem an extension of the very rock of the earth, tiny bell-shaped flowers of myriad pastel colours dance amid a floor of soft, thin-bladed grass. To the north, a lively river splashes noisily between rocky banks, sheltered overhead by the overhanging mallorn limbs.
22464: The vegetation here is thick at all levels of the forest. Near ground level tangled bushes give way to closely packed tree trunks which in turn blossom into a ceiling of intertwined limbs and leaves. Thick woodlands continue to the east and west, while in the south a wide trail begins and winds away into the undergrowth. Most stunning of the surrounding features are the tall, glittery-crowned mallorn-trees which grow in the north, marking the borders of ancient elven Lothlorien. A strange, eerie aura encompasses the golden forest, which seems to shift slightly each time a traveller looks away and then back at it.
22465: This is a definite and much used trail skirting the forest which stands to your east and north. It peters out to the north with many fine trails leading off into the trees in the north and east. Many feet have worn away the grasses a stones throw from the trees. The trail runs south where grass covers the rolling flatlands. The rough lands to the west are sparsely covered and exposed to the elements.
22466: Large stones on the trail make progress a little uncomfortable. Tree-roots seem to have broken up the flagstones that used to pave this way. The trail runs north-south with fields to the west and a forest to the east. Light winds make a murmuring sound in the leaves of the trees. The great forest covers the horizon to the north and east.
22467: Near the corner of the forest, between the stony trail and the trees, there is a clear circle of worn grass, indicative of a large number of travellers and their mounts that once camped here. The circle is ringed with a dozen blackened fire circles. The edge of the forest is nearest to the northeast and runs in a dark line southeast. A well-defined trail runs north-south. Scant grasslands lie to the west.
22468: Although this was once a well-kept trail, weeds and grasses cover most of the broken flagstones showing that it is now seldom used. The trail runs north-south with grasslands to the west and a forest some distance away to the east. The lands to your south are increasingly wilder and more desolate. The dark grey of the horizon to the north and west shows the vast extent of the forest.
22469: The paving stones that once covered this part of the trail have been broken or looted, leaving large potholes. Many of these are now filled with water, making it harder to follow the trail. A few tracks at the side of the trail show that this way still sees some light use. The trail continues north and south. The shadow of a forest rises to the east with bare grasslands to the west. A stagnant smell fills the air.
22470: Clearly marked by a strip of bright green grass, the trail passes through a small depression. The ground is soft and wet. In places you see small animal tracks in the tall grass leading off to either side of the trail. A grey leafless forest stands a short distance to the east. The air is still, humid and smells of damp grass.
22471:
Prickly, white-stemmed plants, with blue flower heads grow in abundance.
A toad is standing here.
A black crow flies low to the ground here, looking for carrion to eat.

This stretch of grass to the west of the large forest is pocked with molehills and rabbit holes. Near the forest edge the activity of these small animals has exposed the roots of the trees. The soil is iron-brown and gradually darkens to the south. A north-south trail is clearly visible just to the west. The odd noise of a small bird or animal can be heard near the tree line.
22472: A large shrub grows here, its branches loosely spreading.

A few broken flagstones have been piled up here to stand a few inches higher than the long grasses which are the dominant vegetation in this terrain. A few rough marks have been scratched into the top stone, but they have been weathered to such an extent that they have no meaning to you. A trail lies about twenty paces to your west and the dark outline of a forest is visible to your east.
22473: The ground here is untrodden. Several different types of long grasses are mixed together, with the odd small flower struggling to survive in the poor soil. The forest stands silently to the east like a shadow on a winter afternoon. To the west you can make out a trail running north-south.
22474: The edge of the forest can be seen to the west and south. Here the trees stand quite closely, yet the woods remain light and airy. Animals and birds can be heard rustling in the underbrush, darting among the branches and calling to each other, perhaps alarmed by your presence. A light, warm breeze moves the branches of the trees.
22475:
A fierce boar is here, making grunting noises.
A fallow deer is grazing peacefully here.

Green mosses and lichens cover the trunks of the living trees in this part of the forest. Springing from under the tree-roots, a small stream tumbles down a tree-lined crag. The small waterfall creates a constant spray, keeping the air damp. The rivulet meanders eastwards where it descends a low slope. Little other sounds can be heard over the noise of the water.
22476: This is the very edge of the woodland. The forest here is green and cool. A light breeze rustles in the leaves above, where small birds sing their springtime songs. To the north and east the trees get thicker. To the west and south the forest ends giving way to grasslands. A variety of small trails and animal tracks disappear into the trees but end as abruptly as they start.
22477: The trees stand shoulder to shoulder like guards; perhaps they will not let anything evil pass. There is a distinct feel of springtime here. New growth and bright green leaves on the trees are testament to that. You feel a light breeze from the grasslands to the west. In the distance you hear what could be laughter or perhaps just the trickling of water.
22478: At the Edge of a Camp

A clear circle of worn grass lies between you and a trail to the west. Next to you a small circle of ashes ringed with stones the size of a man's hand marks the edge of the camp. Although the camp appears long deserted, a few broken pots, camp wear and animal droppings give you some clue of the nature of those who passed. The forest stands proudly to the north and east. The whispering of the leaves is reassuring in this otherwise silent place.
22479: A large rabbit looks peacefully at you, ready to dart away.

The bushes in the plains to the west give way to poorly covered grassland. The soil is sandy, rocky in places, and unable to sustain more than a few hardy grasses. You are very exposed here and would perhaps be safer on the edge of the forest that lies close to the north and continues on to the east and west. The air is dry, relatively warm and carries the smell of the woodlands.
22480: Flat and quite featureless, the grass-carpeted plains continue. There seems to be little evidence of any other inhabitants; the surrounding ground bears no signs of any permanent dwellings of the local wildlife. The edge of the Golden Wood rises to the north, its heady scent already tingling the air here.
22481: The grasslands begin to thin out slightly here, leading into more barren areas to the east. The land is flat in all directions, and mostly featureless save for a few patches of stunted grass and bushes that are more bramble than leaf. The wind carries a hint of the Golden Wood as it wafts lazily from the northwest.
22482:
The corpse of a boar is lying here.
Prickly, white-stemmed plants, with blue flower heads grow in abundance.
A rock lizard is here, motionless as it observes you.

Rocks, stones, poor soil, eroding winds and lack of water have combined to make these lands bare and devoid of vegetation save a few tufts of hardy grass. When the wind strengthens it picks up grit and sand making travel uncomfortable. To the east you can see a well defined trail running along the edge of a large forest. The landscape in other directions is unremarkable with only an odd tree, outcrop of rocks or bush to break up its monotony.
22483: Thorny bushes and thistles cover much of the flat ground here. The brambles snatch at your clothes and skin. These plants provide cover for a variety of small animals and shelter you from any would be pursuers. There are some dark berries on the brambles.
22484: A field vole has frozen to the spot, sensitive to your presence.

These plains consist mostly of low, light shrubbery growing in clumps among the coarse grass. The soil is barren and not very fertile, yet some bushes seem to thrive here. Occasionally something can be seen rustling in the bushes farther away; perhaps a rabbit or another small animal. The scrubland continues eastwards.
22485: The shrubbery in the northeast gives way to the low grass which carpets this level and monotonous landscape. To the south some old ruins rise above the grasslands, and in the distant northwest a dark line can be seen on the horizon; the eaves of the Golden Wood of Lothlorien.
22486: A swallow flies high above the ground.

Bushes dominate this mostly barren landscape. Light shrubbery grows everywhere, but does not make travelling difficult. The bushes are of a low and tangled kind and seem to tolerate the dry climate fairly well. Some tough grasses seem to thrive in more densely populated areas of brush. The scrubland continues to the north and east, and an old path lies to the south.
22487: A path once ran through this area, but it is now very faint and almost unmarkable. Foundations of an old building lie about; big blocks of stone lie scattered around, and grass now covers everything. Among the overgrown ruins lie pieces of metal and other debris. The destruction of this area must have been violent indeed.
22488: The old path, faint but still discernible, runs east-west through the wilderness. Here it is now little more than an animal track, and is probably very seldom trodden, yet it appears that it once served many a traveller. Plains lie in all directions, and to the north, the Golden Wood can be spied in the distance.
22489:
A large rabbit looks peacefully at you, ready to dart away.
A cute rabbit is here.
A black crow flies low to the ground here, looking for carrion to eat.

The bushes and brambles to the north gradually peter out as the soil gets poorer and dryer. Small clumps of yellowing grass cling together, barely surviving the wind due to their long roots. There are many large patches of bare earth and stones where nothing grows. A few burrows show that some small animals manage to live here. To the east you pick out a trail in the plains, and far beyond it lies the shadow of a large forest.
22490: The ground in these bare lands seems to suffer from extremes of weather and bears little or no vegetation. The soil is baked hard with gaping cracks which would be an ideal refuge for small animals or insects. The bleached skeleton of a large animal, perhaps a horse, lies here. The lands to the north and west are unremarkable. The only feature to the east is a green trail cutting through the dryer grasses that cover the surrounding plains. The fields to the south show signs of habitation.
22491: A field vole has frozen to the spot, sensitive to your presence.

Rough, rocky debris is now the only thing present on this bleak valley edge which once used to be fertile, arable land, most likely the property of some farm. This slope has been left without tending for many years, and its bare brown and yellow soil allows little vegetation to grow.
22492: Once perhaps a fertile field or a green pasture this area is now a barren, rocky slope, growing just about nothing. The ground slopes downward slightly to the west, forming a small valley in the distance. Large boulders and stones lie about; some of them look as though they were once part of a man-made structure, perhaps a quarry or corral. A broken shield lies among the rocky debris.
22493:
A sturdy crate made of nailed wooden planks sits on the floor.
An elf of the Galadhrim is walking around here.

Ascent of the thin yet strong rope ladder affords access to one of the many flets, or talans in the elvish tongue, that populate the forest of Lothlorien. This flet seems to be used primarily for storage. It is made of the strongest wood, smoothly polished by countless footsteps. You can see a bridge over the stream to the north, and the stepping stones over the stream to the east.
22494:
A small oaken table has been set here.
On the table, there is a chunk of salt, a flagon, a pan and a water skin.
A finely crafted crystal lamp is hanging from a tree branch.
A large encrusted cedar chest is standing here.
Sarion is sitting here.
A graceful golden-haired elven lady is standing here, rocking on her heels.

This oddly-shaped flet placed within the confines of a particularly sprawling mallorn tree is the home of an elven family. Fresh flowers are strewn on the floor. A stunning tablecloth of intricate elven weave covers a square knee-high table in the corner. A ladder is secured on one side of the flet and a length of elven rope on another, ending in a swing.
22495: A pack horse (Rood) is standing here, ridden by you.

Completing its graceful arc, the paved stone road passes below the high green wall that encircles the bright city of the Galadhrim. Carefully laid, the white polished stones gleam and shine as they reflect every ray of light that drops on them, creating a dazzling pattern of light and movement.
22496: Steadily anchored among the branches of this great mallorn, the large wooden flet has been painted white by its inhabitants. Bordered by a low railing, the platform is large enough for a few families. A large round table stands in the middle. A few sleeping mats lie on the floor and a few benches stand along the edges of this spartanly furnished home of the Galadhrim.
22497: This large wooden platform rests firmly among the branches of a great mallorn. It is bordered by a low wooden railing, painted in gold and green flowing in intricate patterns. The platform is covered by sleeping mats and wooden benches. At the trunk of the tree there is a white ladder running down to the ground level.
22498:
A brass lantern has been set on the ground.
A finely crafted crystal lamp is hanging from a tree branch.
A large encrusted cedar chest is standing here.

This square flet with level floor made of pale polished wood is wedged precariously among the bare silver branches of a mallorn tree. Its surface is open to sun and wind. A bundle of mesh ladder, heaped in its south-western corner, looks like the only way in or out of here. The magnificent view over the rooftop of the Golden Wood is breathtaking, but no detail can be ascertained of anything moving below its thick protective cover.
22511: The tree-trunks in this riverside woodland are thin and well-spaced, so that visibility is significant in every direction. Looking towards the sky reveals a season-dependent tapestry of green, red or brown leaves crossed with greyish white branches, set upon a distant background of blue, grey or black. The swift waters of the Anduin curve around from north to west, gliding past the forest which lies just above water level. Scattered among the trees, and along the river, lie pieces of wood, telling a tale of ancient days.
22512: The river here is wide and deep, although small white caps visible to the west indicate that the current picks up speed in that direction. To the east and south grassy riverbanks give way to a thin forest of birch and poplar that lies only slightly above water level. Far to the west, across the mighty Anduin, the ground rises higher and the forest becomes more dense.
22522:
An arrow rack stands upright in the corner.
Standing in the rack are two ash arrows.

A marvellous view opens from the top of the green and broad wall. Circling the city, the broad and high defensive line can be easily defended against any foe that has managed to reach the capital of Lothlorien. The vast forest, reaching towards the hazy horizon, lies at your feet seemingly within your reach. Even closer by, the encircling stone road runs in a perfect semi-circle just outside the deep fosse that lies at the foot of the wall.
22523: An elven archer dressed in green is here, watching the forest.

Curving slightly, the wall here faces almost due west giving one a nice if not to say a splendid view of the white stone road that encircles the city. Just outside a deep shadowed fosse lies the perfect semi-circle of carefully placed white stones as a border between the city and the forest. The tall trees standing to the side of the road seem content with their place as the road runs undisturbed and unmarked by the forces of nature.
22524: High and broad, this strong wall gives ample room for several archers to hold here a defensive position. Facing almost due west, one could see what moves below on the white stone road that encircles the city or, for that matter, anything that comes out of the vast forest.
22525:
An arrow rack stands upright in the corner.
Standing in the rack are five ash arrows.
An elven archer dressed in green is here, watching the forest.

Positioned on the great defensive walls of the fair city of Caras Galadhon, you find yourself high above the ground, thus having an excellent view. Large crenellations are placed along the wall, crafted in such a way as to blend in with the wall and the surrounding greenery, and allowing a defender safely to fire his arrows at an incoming foe. Below lies the deep fosse in permanent dusk. Farther out, the white stone road encircles the city and beyond it the vast expanse of the golden forest stretches out endlessly.
22526:
A placid pond is here, inviting you to take a refreshing drink.
A finely crafted crystal lamp is hanging from a tree branch.
A sturdy trained horse is standing here.

The small clearing close to the side of the path lies quiet and tranquil just below the great green city wall. Surrounded by tall trees, it cannot be easily found unless one knows the way around. When the light of the skies shines down upon the grass on the western slope of the hill, a dazzling display of shadows dances over the greenery to the tune of singing birds.
22527: By the foot of the western slope, the wall surrounding the city towers high above you, only to be challenged by the tall mellyrn standing nearby. The trees grow densely here, undisturbed by will of elves. A short distance to the north the forest opens up where a small but carefully nurtured orchard thrives in the rich soil.
22528:
A large bulletin board, entitled "Mages' Guild", is mounted here.
A finely crafted crystal lamp is hanging from a tree branch.

A soft bed and walls hung with instruments are what first meets one's eye. Taking a closer look reveals several adornments along the walls and a littered table in a corner. The soft winds blowing through the forest create faint yet audible harmonies as they sweep through the room, touching every instrument. Sparkling softly as they move, the instruments reflect the light of a small silver lamp hanging from a branch. A narrow ladder reaches higher up into the tree, to let the bards watch the sky and the stars.
22529: This proud mallorn stands higher than most of the trees that surround it. As you look out over the golden forest of Lothlorien, your gaze is met by an endless expanse of proud mellyrn, reaching as far as the eye can see.
22531: In the Shadow of a Bridge

In daytime, shadows are cast here and dispelled, never keeping the same shape for more than a few seconds as the bridge sparkles and sends light shimmering across the water surface. Although in a permanent state of dusk, the shadows below the bridge are friendly and joyful, never hostile. The quiet trickle of the stream creates a soothing background as the arch of the bridge enhances and magnifies the sounds of the lively water.
22559: Part Way up the Misty Mountains
A furry, striped raccoon is here, nosing around for some berries or roots.

You are only able to get part way down the side of the mountain. You can go no further because the terrain has become impossible to pass. The Misty Mountains are east of here, but you can see no way to get to them. The only way out of here is back up into the untamed mountains you just came from.
22574: A high tree overlooking the dark landscape southeast and southwest. North it brightens up a little where a small river calmly flows eastwards. Further north large conifers builds up another dark forest from where strange sounds reach this place now and then.
22606: The corpse of a large red deer is lying here.

Concealed behind the impenetrable veil of the thick, grassy wall, a wide, deep cavern goes into the gritty rock of the embankment. Even at the entrance light is extremely dim, as only a few scarce rays manage to get through the grass hedge. But their tenuous light is enough to make a myriad of tiny glimmering points shine on the rock surface, and, on the dark, vaulted ceiling, they resemble the starry sky. Further inside, shadows crowd and darkness becomes total. Hundreds upon hundreds of deer skeletons lie scattered on the ground, for this is the secret place where they come to die, and thus they have done for countless generations.
22607: The atmosphere inside the building is cold and very humid, but at least its four walls and ceiling protect from the sometimes icy wind and the rain. Opposite the entrance, a ramshackle table constitutes the only furniture. Small dark marks here and there reveal the existence of leaks in the roof, that, for the rest, appears to be in a reasonably good condition. In the most sheltered corner, a little circle of tiny stones, together with the soot- covered walls, and, mainly, the ash-coloured floor, make it clear that it would be the perfect spot to light a fire.
22608: An Earthy Cave under the Hill

A brown bear is sleeping here.
A brown bear is sleeping here.
A brown bear is sleeping here.
A mighty brown bear is sleeping here.

A wide, serpentine tunnel makes its way down into the heart of the hill, and opens suddenly into a cavern, whose size is difficult to guess in the shadows. The cave ceiling appears to be irregular, but it seems somewhat higher near the middle, like some sort of a natural vault. The walls are made out of coarse-grained, dark, damp earth, and they show sign of many several-inch-deep scratches. On the other hand, small pools and black stains dot the ground here and there, obviously due to the filtering water. But the atmosphere remains always fresh, sheltered by many feet of rock and earth.
22617: A Wholesome Cave inside the Carrock

The cave appears to have been carved out of the same rock that runs underneath the waters of the mighty Anduin, be it by the hand of man or by the force of nature. The surface of the walls is rough, and blackened with ash, most probably from the torchlight and campfires of previous travellers. In here, one could rest on the pebbled surface of the ground, shielded from the outside, in relative comfort.
22618: Climbing up the large branches of this gigantic tree, a wide view opens up. Thick green leaves rustle in the wind, giving shade from the sun and helping to hide from an enemy. The smell of wood and greenery, mixed with passing breezes, floats everywhere. To the far west, a silvery-grey form is visible, moving like a snake between the surrounding fields - the mighty river of Anduin. To the northwest, a grassy mound lies about, higher than the land surrounding it. To the south, fertile meadows have taken root, blooming with countless little flowers at the summertime.
22622: A giant slug is here, oozing around.

Mouldy odours of dank moist soil fill this darkened grotto. The footing here is slippery black mud with lumpy clots of dirt. Long tree roots drape like thick netting from the cavern's ceiling and re-enter the wet soil below.
22633:
A patch of moss grows here on a wet, flat stone.
A snake slithers towards you.
A snake slithers towards you.
A large brown snake with black patches is coiled here.
A large brown snake with black patches is coiled here.
A snake slithers towards you.
A snake slithers towards you.
A black snake, with red markings, is lying here.

Soft freshly dug soil is loosely piled around this dark animal den. The cavern is rather wide although the squat clod ceiling of roots, loam and sharp stones makes the space seem cramped. Bits of bone and rotten remains are strewn about causing a rank odour to hang heavily in the air.
22635:
A large sack containing pepper lies on the ground.
An old and rickety wooden chest stands in a forgotten corner.

A cramped burrow adds needed storage space for the hut above. Simple beechwood shelves line the compacted dirt walls in this tiny root cellar. The cool dark confines are right for storing cool weather vegetables and other foodstuffs.
22636:
A wolf cub happily plays here.
A wolf cub happily plays here.
A wolf cub happily plays here.
A wolf cub happily plays here.
The mother wolf stands here, protecting her young cubs.
The mother wolf stands here, protecting her young cubs.

This den lies dark and humid, unseen from the eye of the outside world. The cave walls are rough, some rocky niches pointing out of it, damaging the careless traveller and snagging their clothing. As the humidity is high, water drips down from the cracks in the cave ceiling, making the ground underfoot a soggy mass of mud and feces. Additional light seeps in during daytime, through the plant roots that have forced their way in from the deep dirt and stone above.
22647: At the Top of a Tall Larch

Large sturdy branches form the base of this great larch that is perfectly shaped like an enormous evergreen tree. It quite possibly serves as a shelter for those hiding from ferocious animals, or as a temporary lodging in the forest. The hungry sounds of what might be wolves can be heard close by.
22650: On Top of the Huge Rock

A wide vista opens up for a person on this tall rock, making it possible for many to see the river Anduin flowing peacefully in the far east. The sides of the rock are sheer except the western edge where descent seems possible. The surface of the rock is covered with the excrement of birds.
22735:
A tree-snake lies wrapped around one of the tree branches.
A tree-snake lies wrapped around one of the tree branches.

You are standing on a thick branch. The thick mass of leaves blocks the sun out. Far to the north is a small stream, to the east a road and beyond it a very dark forest. The landscape to the south is not versatile, rocks and stones are dominating. To the west there is a very steep mountain. Crunch... you stepped on a little bone. Who uses the branch as a dining table?
34061: To the east, housed in a great arch and flanked by huge doorposts, lie the great eastern gates of Khazad-dum. There are several shafts cut in the east- ern wall above the gates, so this area is flooded with daylight whenever the sun shines. To the north lies what must be a guardroom, though it is impos- sible to tell if the current inhabitants of Moria make use of it. Orcs must come here sometimes, however, for the evidence of their crude attempts to block the shafts with debris lies scattered about.
34062: To the east, the high ceiling plunges abruptly toward the floor, forming a stone wall from which hang some broken stone doors. The wall above the doors is pierced with several great shafts which open onto the mountainside, and fresh air pours from them down into the passage. This area seems to have been shunned by the orcs, probably because of the light that must pour through the shafts whenever the sun rises above Lothlorien and the Anduin to the east. To the west, the darkness beckons with promises of secret treasure hidden in the ancient Dwarven mansions.
34063: The great hall running from east to west is met here by a smaller passage that leads north. East and west, the roof soars high above, supported by lofty arches seemingly too slender to support the mountain above them. The air is almost fresh here, lacking the stale musty quality of underground areas that have been infested with orcs.
34064: The First Hall ends here in a broad stair leading down to the west. To the east it runs in quiet splendour, for the most part unused by the orcs. The ceiling is very high here, and there seems to be a slight breeze from the east gambolling among the lofty arches.
34065: These grand stairs lead upward to the east. They are very wide, and have been cut in such a way that both dwarves and larger races can use them with little discomfort. At the foot of the stairs is a great door, built for defensive purposes by the dwarves in their heyday. At the top of the stairs to the east a wide hall begins, presumably leading to the eastern gate.
34066: Crude lice-infested pallets are scattered about, all currently unoccupied, but obviously frequently used. This area is home to the orcs unfortunate enough to be assigned the duty of guarding the eastern gate, for the shafts in the ceiling frequently fill these halls with bright sunlight. To the south lies the gateroom itself, and the exit to the Dimrill Dale and the lands beyond. Apparently this area is not well guarded, for since the great battle of Azan- ulbizar no one has brought an army strong enough to pose a serious threat to the great evil that lies deep underneath the mountains.
34269: Lined with huge blocks of dark black rock, this passage leaves a major hall to the south and goes into the darkness to the north. There is a thick coating of dust resting on every surface -- obviously this place is not frequently visited.
34270: The passage turns to the east here, becoming slightly narrower. The blocks that form the walls and floor are made of a dark basalt-like substance, and have somehow been welded together almost seamlessly. The passage opens into a chamber a short distance to the east, and this whole area has the appearance of having been long abandoned.
34271: Its purpose lost in antiquity, this room has lain abandoned for many years. The passage to the west is made of large blocks of black stone so cunningly crafted that the joints between contiguous blocks are barely discernible. A similar passage leads north, but it appears to quickly fill with rubble. From the east an unpleasant odour is carried on a slight breeze -- there seems to be another chamber in that direction.
34272: A sturdy pack horse is standing here.

For a short distance it is possible to squeeze between the heavy blocks that have collapsed inward from the walls, but after a little ways all space is taken by the debris. Perhaps this passage once led to more chambers to the north, but for now they must remain lost.
34273:
A big, nasty vulture is sitting here, protecting its nest.
A big, nasty vulture is sitting here, protecting its nest.

A significant portion of the ceiling of this high-domed room has collapsed, revealing an irregularly shaped patch of open sky on the other side of the short passage created by the mishap. The pile of rubble on the floor is too short to allow one to exit through the tunnel without aid of wings, but the quantity of feathers and faeces coating the debris indicate that this room is shelter for several foul birds, content to live in their own filth.
34274: This flat area was part of the Dwarven defensive scheme should their mansions ever be invaded from the eastern gate. The imposing door to the east was built of reinforced iron to resist battering rams, and even if it should ever be compromised, the dwarves would simply retreat to the west, destroying the narrow bridge behind them. Any enemies trapped on this side would then be exposed to merciless crossbow fire from the opposite side.
34275:
A great black orc stands here, eager for combat.
A dark-skinned orc, born of the tunnels, draws his weapon.
A dark-skinned orc, born of the tunnels, draws his weapon.
A dark-skinned orc, born of the tunnels, draws his weapon.
A dark orkish archer is wielding a very vicious-looking bow.
A dark orkish archer is wielding a very vicious-looking bow.
A dark orkish archer is wielding a very vicious-looking bow.

This extremely slender bridge was constructed by the dwarves as a last defence should the Eastern Gate and First Hall of Moria be taken. In a single great spring of fifty feet, the narrow stone bridge arcs over the abyss. No guardrails are present to prevent the careless adventurer misstepping and plummeting to his death in the yawning darkness.
34276: Two parallel lines of large pillars march down the centre of this major road, continuing as far as can be seen to the west. To the east, a wide chasm cuts across the road, bridged by a single slender bridge of stone. The road marches right to the edge of the chasm -- there are no signs of guardrails -- so it is possible to peer over the edge into the blackness.
34277: Running down the centre of this magnificent hallway are two parallel rows of carved pillars, stretching both east and west in perfect rank and file. The floor here is made of a glossy black stone -- as are the pillars -- and any light is dully reflected off of the exposed rock. There is little dust here, so apparently this hall is frequently in use by the current inhabitants of the depths. To the north is a low archway, and beyond is another hall.
34278: This is a large avenue that stretches from the Gate of Durin to the Dimrill Gate. It is a very large, arched tunnel and is constructed of grey granite and white marble. Littered across the floor are broken weapons, armour, and bone fragments. Inhuman corpses lay rotting along the north wall in a pool of blood. It appears that there was a battle here recently.
34279: Directly to the south is a low archway, and through it can be seen a major passage -- surely one of the major arteries of Khazad-dum. The keystone of the arch bears a small inscription -- still legible but faded with time -- that labels the road to the south 'Durin's Way'. To the north, the passage continues, but darkness precludes any details from being ascertained.
34280: Another passageway once intersected this one here, but earthquakes or other tumults have caused it to collapse so it only possible to continue north. The north-south passage is still relatively clear of rubble, but whether that is due to blind chance or superior construction cannot be determined.
34281: This passage is worn, but it does not appear to be used at all by the orcs that inhabit this area of Moria. A coating of dust and small cobwebs covers the floor, and from time to time small spiders dart across the floor and quickly scurry back into cracks in the masonry.
34282: This nondescript passageway turns south to east here. To the east much of the passage has already succumbed to the passage of time, and the accumu- lated rubble would make progress in that direction difficult. To the south the passage is clear of debris. The walls of this passage are covered with flat slate panels -- fairly thin judging by the many panels that have fallen to the east.
34283: According to the knowledge passed on through generations of dwarves since the halls of Moria were abandoned, a great many dwarves made their homes in this area of Khazad-dum. These dwelling places have now been sealed off from the outside world, as the passage east has been totally destroyed -- perhaps in the tumults following the awakening of Durin's Bane, or perhaps deliberately brought down by malicious vandals.
34284: This is a large avenue that stretches all the way from the Gate of Durin to the Dimrill Gate. It is a very large tunnel, arched, and constructed of grey granite and white marble. The lanterns, hanging from rings in the ceiling, are broken and useless.
34285: A huge water-drake is coiled here.

This is a huge octagonal chamber with smooth, slime-covered walls of glittering basalt and black obsidian. The ceiling rises to a shallow peak and sits on two rows of massive lamp-shaped pillars. At the centre of each pillar is an enormous lamp, wrought of gold and silver, which are now broken and burned. There is a very musty odour in this room, and the floor is so damp it is almost slippery. An odd well occupies the centre of the room.
34286: This wide arched hallway branches south from the large hall to the north. Dank and musty the granite hall is covered in filth and garbage. Kicked to the side of the hall, broken weapons and other scrapes of wood lie forgotten, while the middle of the hall is fairly clear of debris.
34287: The granite hallway continues to the north and south while a smaller hallway breaks off to the east. The air is dank and musty. Slime and dirt form a fairly thick casing over the granite walls and more garbage and broken weapons clutter the floor along the eastern wall. The rest of the passage is disgustingly filthy.
34288: This wide, arched tunnel is carved from grey granite. Blood stains the floor and the skeletal remains of some hapless victim lie piled in the corner. The tall and plain grey walls continue to the north and south.
34289:
Some tough lichen grows on the rocks.
A large and somewhat round fungus grows from the floor.
A pale bulbous mushroom grows here.
A dark orc crouches quietly, staring into the distance.
A dark orc crouches quietly, staring into the distance.
A dark orc crouches quietly, staring into the distance.

This circular chamber is lined with pallets for seating - presumably it is some sort of gathering place. The place has a musty smell, and it feels damp. Several species of fungus seem to have taken advantage of the favourable conditions and flourished here.
34290: A dark-skinned orc, born of the tunnels, draws his weapon.

A guardroom lies just to the north, while to the east a larger room of some sort opens up. The passage is dank, and in many places fungi have found purchase in nooks and crannies in the walls. The passageway leading west seems to be but a continuation of this one.
34291: This narrow passageway becomes decidedly damper to the east. In that direction, the walls have been invaded by lichen and fungi that have begun the task of crumbling the quarried stone. To the west, the passage is dry, but nothing more can be made out.
34292: A dark-skinned orc, born of the tunnels, draws his weapon.

To the north is a small chamber, probably used to house orkish guards. To the west, the passage opens into a large room that appears to be filled with round, ivory objects. To the east, the passageway continues, becoming dank and musty with each passing step.
34293: A dark female of the Burzruth glares with yellow eyes at you.

This room is filled with the cleanly polished skulls of dozens of orcs. The bones have been bleached to a pristine white, and runes of brilliant crimson have been carefully inscribed in the centre of the low, sloping foreheads. The skulls seem to have been deliberately placed -- there is none of the usual haphazard scattering associated with orcs -- so perhaps they have some ritualistic function.
34294: Cracked marble slabs line this corridor, which appears to have been damaged by an explosion of great force. To the east is an old Dwarven guardroom, perhaps still used by the orcs, while to the south is a chamber of some type.
34295: The walls here are covered by a thin layer of dark soot that diminishes the beauty with which they once shone. In the few places where the soot has been brushed away, white marble banded with ribbons of polished grey granite are revealed.
34296: A dark-skinned orc, born of the tunnels, draws his weapon.

This is a wide and arched tunnel, constructed of white marble with bands of grey granite. The walls have been blackened by soot -- it appears to be deliberate -- and smeared in the black ash are crude runes of burning red.
34297: A dark-skinned orc, born of the tunnels, draws his weapon.

This is a huge square chamber with smooth, glimmering walls of diamond- patterned basalt and black obsidian. The ceiling rises to a shallow peak and sits on two lines of massive tree-shaped pillars. Crystal lamps, now blackened and broken, hang from the high ceiling. Bones and broken weapons are piled up against the pillars.
34298: This is a wide tunnel carved from milky white marble, stained with blood and ashes. Several rows of skulls are lined up on top of the pipes adorning the walls. The tunnel continues to the north and opens up into a wide hall to the south.
34299: This is a wide tunnel lined with large slabs of white marble. Some of the once bright slabs have fallen into the corridor, shattering on the floor. In the cavities revealed by the fallen marble, a series of ancient pipes can be seen. The tunnel continues to the north and south.
34300: This wide tunnel was once lined with milky-white marble that now has mostly cracked and fallen away. A series of pipes have been revealed behind the marble facade. The tunnel continues to the south, while opening into a larger chamber to the north. There is also a doorway to the east.
34301: This is an enormous room set with a high arching, rib-vaulted ceiling adorned with gold filigree and silver leaf. There are seven wide white marble columns spaced throughout the room. Ten rows of obsidian-lined niches ring the walls at even intervals, each of which house a bronze lamp. This room, now burned and its lamps broken, has an evil feel to it.
34302: The tunnel is wide, arched and constructed from band-patterned grey granite and white marble. The battered walls are cracked and weak from whatever battle took place here. Bits of rock and dirt fall from the ceiling and you don't know if it will cave in or not. A series of pipes lines the cracked walls.
34303: This wide, arched tunnel is constructed of grey granite and white marble woven in a band pattern. Stones and dirt fall from the decaying ceiling and walls into piles on the floor. Occasionally you can hear the sounds of the walls settling, and it seems as if the tunnel will collapse at any minute. A set of pipes runs along the walls.
34304: This wide, arched tunnel is constructed of grey granite and white marble. The walls are battered and cracked from some great battle fought here. The sounds of the walls creaking and settling make you wary of a cave-in. Stones and dust fall from the ceiling and settle into piles on the floor. The tunnel continues to the west or opens into a large hall to the east. There appears to be some kind of guard room to the south.
34305: This is a huge rectangular chamber with smooth, glimmering walls of diamond- patterned basalt and black obsidian. The ceiling rises to shallow peaks and sits on two lines of tree-shaped or lamp-shaped pillars. A set of huge crystal chandeliers hang from the ceiling, but they are broken and burned.
34306: A pair of tiny eyes gleam at you from the shadows.
This is a spiral stairwell connecting this level of the city to those above and below it. The stairs, cut shallow to suit the travel of dwarves, are awkward for most people to travel.
34307: This is a wide tunnel cut from jet-black ebony. The walls seem to absorb what little light you can produce. There is an ominous sense of evil here and you want to leave. The hallway opens into a large chamber to the north and continues to the south. There is a guard chamber to the west. A series of pipes lines the walls.
34308: This is a wide tunnel cut from jet-black rock. Although once they must have been polished to a lustrous sheen, now the walls seem to absorb whatever light is present. The tunnel continues north and south and a smaller passage opens up to the east. West of here a larger chamber can be seen, and from this direction the unmistakable odour of trolls can be detected.
34309: This wide tunnel of cut from black rock leads north from the great passage to the south. To the west is an old Dwarven guardroom -- perhaps used by the orcs for the same purpose. Once these walls would have been kept polished until they gleamed like polished ebony, but now the dull black colour simply seems to absorb all light.
34310:
A dark-skinned orc, born of the tunnels, draws his weapon.
A dark-skinned orc, born of the tunnels, draws his weapon.

This nondescript chamber houses a portion of the Burzruth militia. There are three straw pallets in the back of the room - crawling with ticks by the looks of them. The guardroom has an excellent view of the passageways to the south and west.
34311: This is the famous Durin's Way which passes through the heart of the mountain. There are several solid stone blocks scattered here amid smaller piles of rocks and rubble, perhaps due to a small cave-in which occurred not long ago. Heavy ironwood beams have been used in a slip-shod attempt to shore up some of the walls near here, but they appear to be quite ineffective in preventing further collapse. Durin's Way continues east and west, but your attention is especially drawn to a sturdy stonedoor in the north wall here.
34312: A pair of tiny eyes gleam at you from the shadows.

Durin's Way continues to progress both east and west through the stony heart of Caradhras. The roadway is in good condition here and the air seems fresh. The Dwarves of Moria must have spent years of effort carving the surrounding stone with great precision to create this perfect passageway.
34313:
A dark-skinned orc, born of the tunnels, draws his weapon.
A dark orkish archer is aiming a vicious bow at you.
A dark orkish archer is aiming a vicious bow at you.
A squat and filthy troll lurks in the darkness.
A dark-skinned orc, born of the tunnels, draws his weapon.
A dark-skinned orc, born of the tunnels, draws his weapon.
A dark troll, black as night, rushes forth from the shadows.

Durin's Way is blocked here by a large barricade, complete with a crude door of obvious orkish manufacture. A large wooden table lies against the wall to the north, and several pallets have been placed along the southern wall. This place perhaps serves as a guardpost of some kind.
34314: One of the largest bridges in Moria crossed Durin's Chimney here, but it fell into ruin long ago and now only a small portion of it can be seen on the eastern edge of the chimney. In its place, the orcs have a erected a ramshackle span that appears none too sturdy. To the east, the main thoroughfare has been blocked with a formidable barricade - probably demarcating a boundary between two tribes. To the west, the bridge continues, and beyond the passageway appears clear.
34315: This spindly bridge - obviously not of Dwarven make - spans the wide shaft of Durin's Chimney. To the west, a wide road pushes onward toward the western portion of Khazad-dum, while to the east the narrow bridge comes to an end in front of an imposing barricade.
34316: Here, Durin's Way intersects another large Avenue. The markings indicate that this north-south passage is dedicated to Yavanna, the wife of Aule the Maker. To the east, the rock walls suddenly disappear and Durin's Way meets the Chimney of Durin -- a great open area in the heart of Caradhras. Apparently a great bridge once spanned this abyss, but it has long been destroyed, and in its place a shoddy bridge of orkish manufacturer connects both sides of the Chimney.
34317: A dark orkish archer is wielding a very vicious-looking bow.

This section of Durin's Way is cloaked in utter darkness. Although the stretch of road ahead of you appears silent and barren, you get a strong feeling that something is watching your every move. The Way travels both east and west through the gloom here.
34318: A pair of tiny eyes gleam at you from the shadows.

Durin's Way continues to progress both east and west through the heart of the mountain. Battered walls and defiled statuary lend silent witness to the most recent outrages committed by the current occupants against once-proud Moria.
34319: The once glorious road known as Durin's Way intersects a large, ruined avenue here. Even in the darkness, you can see signs of the grandeur and majesty that Moria once possessed, lessened now by time and ill-fortune. Durin's Way runs east-west through the mountain, while the avenue stretches north into some boulders and south from here.
34320: Both to the east and west, Durin's Way stretches grandly into the darkness. The cold and hard stone floor has been worn down by countless feet, first Naugrim and now Orkish. The walls stare at you, unchanging and featureless.
34321: You walk along the once mighty and glorious road known as Durin's Way. Only a hint of its past grandeur now remains, but the sheer scale of this work is awe-inspiring. The Way continues east and west, but your attention is drawn to a wide stone door just north of here.
34322: You have entered a cavernous complex of rooms. Stretching away on all sides, small rooms are carved into the stone walls. A myriad of walkways, ledges and stairs provide access to these rooms. Roads converge on this place from all directions indicating a major junction. The high domed ceiling rises far above you and sometimes disappears from sight, either rushing up into impenetrable blackness, or vanishing behind huge stone columns. Twisting and turning, the passages and rooms are truly impressive and you marvel at the magnificence of it all.
34323: The huge underground passageway slowly bores deeper and deeper into the depths of the mountain and you marvel at the size of this immense tunnel. What once was the dwarves' major highway is now silent except for the echoing sound your boots make as they strike the stony ground. The road disappears into darkness to the west and to the east you can make out a distinct opening in the otherwise endless tunnel.
34324: Continuing its east-west passage, the wide avenue ploughs on under the great mountain. At times you have to strain your eyes to make out the ceiling high above you, and at some places it even disappears completely in the darkness above. As you peer westwards it seems the hard rock walls open up even more, maybe to make way for another passageway.
34325: Here the two giant roadways Durin's Way and Roin's Scar meet up with another. While the size of Durin's Way alone is impressive, the joining of these two great underground avenues makes a truly magnificent sight. Huge, echoing chasms and towering walls of rock extend north and south while a wide avenue swings out across the chasms on a series of massive stone bridges. The vast tunnel that was once the major highway of the dwarves opens up to the east and west.
34326: A large chamber straddles the grand avenue. Large, defaced columns line the walls and most seem to have been carved with Dwarven warriors caparisoned for war. These illustrations must once have been a beautiful sight, but now the passage of time and the desecration done by the caverns' current inhabitants have made them look worn and abraded. The avenue of Durin exits east and north, and to the west a narrow, seemingly bottomless, chute descends into the deeps.
34327: The road tunnels on through the depths, bending from west to south. The hard ground is strewn with small rocks and boulders on either side of the roadway, as if a minor cave-in has been cleared up recently. Looking closer you realise the rocks must come from a fallen stone column now laying pushed to one side of the cavernous tunnel.
34328: The grand roadway slowly bends from north to east, plunging onward through the dark deeps. The air is slightly chilly and damp, sending a small shiver down your spine. You hear the sound of dripping water, and looking closer at the rock walls you see tiny streams of water trickling down from the ceiling to disappear through near invisible cracks in the floor. Though the mining of these caves has long since ceased, you can see distinct signs of the work that once filled these regions with the din of mine-working.
34329: The huge avenue lumbers onward under the mountain, running north and south. Looking in either direction all you see is utter darkness and you wonder if this road is ever going to end. Broken and long-since useless mining tools lie tossed into a cleft in the east wall of the tunnel and a pile of boulders and large rocks rest against the western part of the cavern wall. Clearly, whoever now inhabits these underground passageways cares nothing for keeping this grand creation of the dwarves in good condition, leaving things in disarray, with never a thought to set things straight.
34330: An orkish warrior of the Durghash is here, with a cruel glint in his eye.

Winding away under the mighty Silvertine, the avenue ponderously bends west to south in this huge chamber. The silent, brooding atmosphere is broken only by the sounds you make yourself and the occasional muffled clattering sound coming from the distant west. You pause to try and discern the source of the sound, but hear nothing except deep silence.
34331: A great chamber, hewn by the forces of nature and by the industrious hands of the dwarves is served by three main roadways. Running east is the widest avenue, north a narrower road disappears into the gloom, and west, Durin's Way runs its course onward toward some distant goal.
34332: Here the wide avenue twists from south to east, slowly winding onward into the heart of the mountain. Your footsteps echo through the cavern, but that is all you can hear in this dark and foreboding place. A faint breeze carries a damp smell through the air, suggesting that it must have been a very long times since fires warmed these underground caverns.
34333: This majestic, huge tunnel, the major thoroughfare of Moria, turns from west to north here. What once must have been a well kept and magnificent roadway now lies disused. The dwarves that once lived here are no longer around to keep things in good condition, and who or whatever now inhabits these dungeons clearly seem to enjoy destroying its surroundings much more than expanding upon them, or even maintaining them.
34334: This area of the huge tunnel is filled with several small tunnels darting off in different directions, narrow clefts bored into the rock and the like. The major roadway of Durin's Way runs through the cavern east-west. Even before entering any of the small passageways that depart from the main roadway here, you notice that fallen rubble has filled all of them, making them all impossible to travel.
34335: Looking around this large natural cavern you notice a small dried out pool lying directly below an opening in the western wall, where the water must have once tumbled down. As you look closer, you see that this small spring was probably once fed by a small underground stream emerging from the rock just above the pool, forming a small but beautiful waterfall. Now only scattered drops of water form at the mouth of the hole and fall down into the shallow spring. The remains of a torn waterskin lie beside the now empty pool, as well as a smashed wooden cup. Winding onward under the peaks, Durin's Way turns gently in its path, from east to south.
34336: Slowly turning from west to north, Durin's Way leads on through the darkness. The roadway is somewhat narrower here, but the ceiling still looms high overhead. As you look at the blackened rock walls, you think that you catch a faint glint of gold. Upon closer inspection, you realise that it was nothing more than your mind playing a trick on you. No veins of gold are visible in this part of the tunnel, and you realise that this part of the caverns was never mined, and was only used as a thoroughfare.
34337: The roadway passes through a large cavern, split by a narrow, black chasm. A couple of stone steps lead up to a wide stone arch, on which the great road spans the huge gap of the yawning abyss below. The road exits the chamber east and south. Two towering stone pillars frame the archway on either side of the chasm. All of these columns show signs of recent attempted destruction. The vandals have hacked away at the pillars with great force, leaving them ragged and hacked, but still intact.
34338: The grand, wide avenue of Durin bores on through the mountain's fastness, running north-south. Once worn by the passage of thousands of dwarves, the ground at the centre of the tunnel shows only faint signs of abrasion. These tunnels have now long since been abandoned by those who built them. Still, you are reminded that they are far from empty by the sound of drums beating in rhythm far in the distance. Continually building and fading like a giant heart, the ominous sound appears to come steadily closer. As the deep beating suddenly disappears completely, the tunnel is left in an eerie silence.
34339: The grand roadway underneath the mountain, Durin's way, drives onward in this low-ceilinged part of the tunnel. It bends in its course, veering from west to north. The ceiling dips low in the middle of the passageway, and framing this natural arch are two statues. Depicting a pair of great Dwarven warriors, these two images of stone have been the victims of brute vandalism. Both have had their hands and arms cut off where these protruded from the main body. The heads of both statues have been violently smashed from atop the torso, and to one side of the corridor, you find one of the heads, badly battered.
34340: The broad once-beautiful avenue bends from south to east, flanked on the outside of the curve by an ornamental marble colonnade. Behind the columns there was once a monumental bas-relief. Someone has taken an exceptional dislike to this work; it has been systematically chiselled away, and marble chips litter the floor of the tunnel.
34341: The underground avenue identified as Durin's Way makes a broad bend to the north, from the point of view of an eastbound traveller. East of the bend is a squarish side chamber parallel to the road, possibly a siding for the unloading of freight. Some large stone bins are here with runners on the bottoms. In the east wall are four stone openings large enough for the bins to fit within.
34343: A broad underground road makes a turn here from westward to northward. The walls have been much battered and pitted, but it seems that some mosaics showing the industry of the dwarves and the victories they had won with their axes still remain visible on the tunnel's walls.
34344: This is the end of an underground road which comes from the south and stops here in a square chamber, broad though low, with a strong-looking metal door in the north wall. The four corners of the chamber bear lamps mounted on struts which lean toward the centre. A plain corridor departs westward.
34345: The level corridor continues straight east and west through the mountain. Above you there is a great hole in the ceiling; not the result of a collapse, but a tunnel of the same dimensions as this one, which seems to ascend straight upwards. The air that blows down from above is cooler, but it bears a mixture of pungent animal smells.
34346: This tunnel is like a narrow corridor which has been delved through the stone in an east-west direction. Its walls, floor, and ceiling are flat and meet at precise right angles, but there is little ornamentation. Perhaps it was awaiting further work when the dwarves were driven from Khazad-dum long ago.
34347: You are in a draughty, high-ceilinged chamber where a passage from the west divides into three eastward-trending ways. To the left, a wide road descends a ramp; to the right, a similar road ascends into blackness. Connecting the upward and downward paths is a curved patch of stone floor which was actually worn down about two inches by the traffic long ago. Between the two, a narrower level passage proceeds straight eastward. On the walls are mounted some lamps in pairs. This was apparently a well- travelled junction once. There is a low archway in the north wall of the chamber.
34348: A deep fissure has opened in the rock here, perpendicular to the direction of the tunnel. In the ceiling it is a noticeable crack; on the walls it is about a foot wide. Where it crosses the path you are on, it makes a four- foot gap. However, at the moment the gap is bridged by a huge flat stone slab which someone has placed across it.
34349: The road continues eastward into the darkness. On the north and south the way is marked by the openings of ore-chutes, by uninviting stairways, and by black doorways whose doors swing vacantly wide. Cracks are beginning to appear in the walls and floor, and every so often a chunk of the roadway is found to have collapsed inward into some vacancy of unknown depth.
34350: A circular chamber about forty feet across with a central stone pier has been excavated at the intersection of four ways. The floors of the circle and of the four tunnels are very flat and coated with dried mud. The tunnels leading outward are about sixteen feet in width; about two feet above the floor narrow walkways have been cut on either side.
34351: The east-west passage continues as before. On the north and south sides are some bays or sidings, some of which contain stone bins or notches for partitions. To the east, the passageway opens out into a large intersection.
34352: The east-west tunnel continues through the stone of the mountain, ascending to the west, descending to the east. Here and there the roof of the tunnel is marked by the black opening of a vent or chute. Stairways, ladders, and doorways are frequently encountered, but in this part of the tunnel they are usually blocked or damaged.
34353: An east-west tunnel is hewn through the solid stone here. Its walls and ceiling are unadorned; its floor is caked with dirt. At irregular intervals, the mouths of smaller tunnels open to either side of the main passage. The air is soundless, warm and oppressive.
34354: A Bend in the Underground Road

You are following an underground road or tunnel which winds through the rock in great sloping bends. North of here the course is generally upward; to the east, downward. Here and there great bays open in the rock, in which large lampposts stand, stone benches, offer rest to the traveller, and doors and windows signal the presence of an inn, an eating-place, a public store. Now all are of course abandoned. In the lightless gloom the bays are silent and watchful, and the absolute blackness of the doors and windows is like that of the eyes of skulls.
34355: You have arrived at a broad plaza whose surface is formed of heavy hexagonal stone slabs - white, black, and pink marble, greenish gabbro, and other types you do not recognise. A white marble stairway, the width of the entire plaza, descends to the west. At the top of the stair are two damaged statues. To the north and east you dimly perceive what seem to be white trees. Above them you see some carvings on the walls which rise out of sight in great vaulting curves, skilfully designed to bear the unimaginable weight of the mountain which rises far above you.
34356:
An eyeless white rat with nasty teeth scurries about.
An eyeless white rat with nasty teeth scurries about.
An eyeless white rat with nasty teeth scurries about.

You are on a monumental stairway, two hundred feet wide, which ascends eastward. The steps are strewn with rubble. You cannot make out a landing either below or above, no matter how hard you peer into the darkness. A great ornamental window can be dimly seen above you to the west. The north and south walls are lined with rune-carved panels, with sconces above them; you also notice some odd holes in the walls.
34357: This is a great, once-magnificent entrance hall, whose farthest reaches are shrouded in impenetrable blackness. Sconces and lamps, unused now for centuries, can be dimly seen on the walls nearest to you. In the west wall are the great portals of the Doors of Durin. Opposite them, across a broad marble floor, a wide stairway rises into the gloom and vanishes. The air is still and stale; the echoes of your footfalls are weak, and all sounds are hushed by the immensities of space and age. Once, long ago, this hall was well-lit, festive, and companionable, a meeting-place for elves and dwarves and the gateway to the glory of Khazad-dum. Today it is dark, bleak, and watchful. Some bones lie scattered against the base of the north wall.
34358: You are where a broad underground road widens into an underground chamber, whose roof is supported by a line of square pillars on either side of the roadway.
