The edges of the chamber are lined with low loading platforms and freight docks. Beyond them, in the darkness the black doorways of vacant looted warehouses can be vaguely seen.
34359:
An eyeless white rat with nasty teeth scurries about.
An eyeless white rat with nasty teeth scurries about.
An eyeless white rat with nasty teeth scurries about.

The ceiling soars upward and the pillars lining the road disappear in the gloom above, as the road passes directly through a huge underground room - obviously a warehouse. The upper levels are wider than the lower ones, and a ramp spirals upward along the west, north, and east wall, reaching the top level just above the east entrance. In the great days of the Dwarves, this warehouse was full of goods received from all the peoples of the world. Now it is empty, still, and black.
34360: This road is surfaced with a very dark stone, black flecked with green. So are the walls up to about the height of a dwarf. The ceiling is covered with small rectangular tiles of a much lighter stone. Other than floor and ceiling, there is not much to see in this tunnel, which slopes downward to the south.
34361: The dark-surfaced road slopes upward to the north and downward to the south. Water drips from around some of the ceiling tiles; some have become detached, revealing wet cracked stone. The drips form a rivulet which runs down the base of the east wall of the tunnel, meandering and depositing a layer of silt. There seem to be some bipedal tracks there, but the silt does not hold the outline well.
34362: The dark road bends here, turning left in its downward course. The floor of the tunnel has become coated with silt and slime and is quite slippery. The stones of the walls are also wet. Clearly this location is partially submerged from time to time.
34363: Here a dark-surfaced underground road comes to an abrupt end at the shore of a subterranean lake - at least that is your first impression. In fact, the pavement continues eastward beneath the surface, dropping rapidly off into unknown depths. A great void has opened up above you. Perhaps the cave-in that created this cavern also blocked the drainage somehow so as to form the lake.
34364: This roadway is surfaced with a smooth dark stone, which also lines the walls to a height of three feet. Above that level the unfinished surface of the hard stone through which the road is bored arches overhead in broken curves.
34365: The hard dark-surfaced road bends here, seemingly to avoid a great mass of white crystalline rock on the northwest side of the passage. From this point it ascends to the east and descends to the south.
34366:
A small white snake slithers along the ground.
A small white snake slithers along the ground.

The road bends here, following the path of a natural crevice in the rock which scars the roof of the tunnel, zigzagging from one side to the other and back. The rock here is a dark grey shot through with bright crystalline veins. Some of the outcroppings of the lighter stone in the walls of the tunnel have been crudely chipped and dug into.
34367: The roof and west wall of the tunnel have disappeared. The road hugs the face of a west-facing precipice; above and westward are only a lightless void. Yet you are still underground. The wall to your east does not look like part of any natural cave. There are no natural sounds; all around is black and still. A curb half a foot high guards the western edge of the roadway.
34368: A tremendous cave-in has happened here. A dark-surfaced road arrives from the south, begins an eastward turn, and at that point disappears completely, running at an angle into a great rock face. A second look shows that the rock is a single great slab of the mountain which has fallen from above, obliterating the road. The precipice to the west is too steep to descend, but there is a footpath which climbs up to the east and north along the junction between the fallen rock and the cliff above where the road used to be. The rock here is veined with blue-white quartz.
34369: This path winds over, around, between, and under massive slabs of fallen stone. Here it leads through a crack between two boulders each the size of a hill. There it burrows under a great stone through a pile of fine rubble. And there again the roof opens out exposing you to the awesome blackness overhead, which might collapse on you at any time, of course.
34370: A great supporting column of the mine lies here, broken like the stem of a goblet. Its base juts up just here; the rest of it lies here, extended northward along a rock face. The column was hewn from the stone by the Dwarves; it is smoothly tapered and bent to carry and distribute the weight of the shoulder of the mountain overhead, as if it were an ornamental column in a king's palace. The base, however, shows signs of a later, less skilful mining operation.
34371: You are on a slender, railless, east-west path surrounded by nothingness in all directions. All around you is a great black vacancy, the central digging of a Dwarven mine. The path runs along the top of a structural buttress, and is not designed for ease of travel. Travelling between two elevated points, it makes a long downward curve, at the low point of which you are.
34372: You are at the base of a mighty supporting column in a Dwarven mine. Because of their peerless science of stone and force, the Khazad were able to delve incredible caverns such as this within the northwest shoulder of the peak called Silvertine. The column and the buttresses that lead away from it are carefully shaped to bear the weight of the rock above and transmit it into the roots of the mountain. Doubtless they left behind no more ore- bearing rock than they had to; if anyone were to become greedy and dig more, it would produce a catastrophe.
34373: A small white snake slithers along the ground.

A road surfaced with smooth dark stone abruptly becomes impassable here, as it and the rock supporting it have collapsed into the depths below. The road may be followed back to the east, and a plain side road follows a spur of the walls southward. Surrounding you is the oppressive and threatening blackness of the interior of the mountain.
34374:
A long rope, with a hook at one end, has been left here.
A rusty pickaxe with a broken handle lies discarded here.

You are at the working face of the Mine of Khulakal. Shallow tunnels are dug into the stone. Some are precisely hewn in Dwarvish fashion for part of their length, then become clumsy and misshapen. The ground drops off sharply to the southwest, heaped with mounds of stone. A narrow road slithers precariously up the face, northward and eastward. A larger road, surfaced in dark stone, begins here and goes west along the north wall of the great excavation.
34375: A small bat is standing here (hidden).

This plain stone room was apparently once used for the housing of guards who watched over the intersection outside. Near the door is a well-mouth surrounded by a stone curb. The heavy stone lid lies nearby. On the western wall is an ancient empty weapons-rack, and in the north wall are niches that served as beds.
34377: A broad dark-surfaced underground road or tunnel runs north and south here. On either side is a narrow walkway about two feet above the pavement. The roof here is the native rock of the mountain.
34378: At the Bottom of a Chute

An orkish warrior of the Durghash is here, with a cruel glint in his eye.
An orkish warrior of the Durghash is here, with a cruel glint in his eye.
A lurg leader, with markings of the Durghash tribe, stands here.
A great wolf with a sable coat glares around with red eyes.

The narrow passage comes to a halt as the only apparent exit, besides east, rises up into darkness. The round chute that soars upwards from this small chamber looks impossible to ascend, even to the most adept climber. As you stand staring up into the deep blackness above, a small drop of water comes falling out of it, landing on your forehead. You turn to search for other plausible exits, but find none.
34379:
A lurg leader, with markings of the Durghash tribe, stands here.
A great wolf with a sable coat glares around with red eyes.

This cramped passage runs due east-west, widening slightly to the east and becoming even more narrow going west. It has a slight decline downwards to the west and as you look in that direction, the grim darkness makes it look as if the tunnel suddenly dropped out of sight. Carefully coming closer, you see that the passage actually continues there, the solid rock at your feet not plunging into any grim abyss, as you had first thought.
34380: This very narrow passage runs due east-west and has the look of a little used mining tunnel. To the east it would appear to emerge into a cavern of sorts. Signs of the work of the Dwarven miners can still be faintly seen, as they once burrowed their way into the mountain.
34381:
A lurg leader, with markings of the Durghash tribe, stands here.
A great wolf with a sable coat glares around with red eyes.

A great wolf with a sable coat glares around with red eyes.
An orkish warrior of the Durghash is here, with a cruel glint in his eye.
An orkish warrior of the Durghash is here, with a cruel glint in his eye.
An orkish warrior of the Durghash is here, with a cruel glint in his eye.

Standing in the southwestern quarter of a large chamber, this place is dominated by the wide road entering from the south. A narrower passage runs away west and to the east and north, the cavern stretches away into darkness. In the corner of this section of the huge cave rests a couple of mid-sized boulders that, upon closer inspection, make an excellent place to sit down and rest your weary bones.
34382: You stand at the southeastern corner of a huge chamber. The ceiling rises up into dizzying heights and is soon lost from sight. Judging by the angle of the natural rock walls, and the eerie echoing in this chamber, you wonder if there is a ceiling at all. To the east a wide roadway enters and to the south a crude, narrowish passage runs away. As you look around to examine your surroundings, you cannot help but notice a faint but nevertheless disgusting smell coming from the south tunnel.
34383: A pair of tiny eyes gleam at you from the shadows.

The road upon which you stand runs climbing from west to east. Well crafted, the road has groove marks in it indicating some importance in past times. While the corridor climbing into darkness in the east seems to look exactly the same as the one in which you are standing now, the exit to the west appears to open into a large cave of some sort; much larger than the simple tunnel you are now standing in.
34384: Bending from west to south, the roadway travels onwards and upwards - or downwards to the west, depending on which way you should decide to go. A faint whiff of some sickly smell drifts past you in the gentle breeze that floats through here. Shifting your gaze from the ground in front of you to the walls at your sides, you notice something you either have not encountered earlier on this road, or simply have not paid attention to: Placed at regular intervals in this cavernous tunnel are the remains of several iron sconces. These appear heavily rusted and most of them are unusable, smashed and broken by trolls or orcs.
34385: The road runs onwards, north-south, and continues at a steady incline as it traverses the dark depths. You hear a muted shuffling sound coming from the north, where the roadway slowly descends into blackness. You peer intently ahead of you, trying to make out anything distinct, but the darkness seem endless and you see nothing.
34386: The road upon which you stand turns sharply here, from north to east. To the east it climbs, and northwards it descends into the Deeps. The rough rock walls of the tunnel rise at a sharp angle, making this part of the corridor almost V-shaped.
34387: To the east of this tunnel the passageway opens up to what you think must be a much wider set of caverns. At the eastern end of this cave, you notice that the echoing your feet make as they strike the ground change; it clearly indicates a sizeable enlargement of the tunnel, and since the continual darkness of this place has made you rely more on your sense of hearing, you are inclined to trust your conclusions. The road you are walking on runs due east-west and has a steady incline up to the east.
34388:
A lurg leader, with markings of the Durghash tribe, stands here.
A great wolf with a sable coat glares around with red eyes.
A great wolf with a sable coat glares around with red eyes.
An orkish warrior of the Durghash is here, with a cruel glint in his eye.
An orkish warrior of the Durghash is here, with a cruel glint in his eye.

An orkish warrior of the Durghash is here, with a cruel glint in his eye.
An orkish warrior of the Durghash is here, with a cruel glint in his eye.

You are at the southern end of a great cavern, its northern extremes lost in the darkness. A wide road stands out amongst the myriad of narrow stairs and bridges, running away to the north. To the south the road immediately turns west and enters a tunnel. A slight breeze is in the air and in the distance you hear something sounding like a coarse scream echoing through the caverns.
34389: You stand in the midst of a vast underground canyon. Below, the ground plunges away into unseen depths. A wide roadway traverses the caverns north-south, running along on a series of arches, hopping from pillar to pillar. Giant stalagmites, many of which support the arched walkways, stand everywhere in the caverns - those at the end of your field of vision looking like ghosts of hulking giants. Staring intently at one of these huge columns, you seem to make out movement at a distance. When you blink your eyes, it disappears, not to be seen again.
34390: At the northern end of a colossal cavern, part of the great fault know as Roin's Scar, the road upon which you travel turns from west to south. The air is cold and damp and almost completely silent. The faint, soft sound of dripping water forms a continuous background to other, periodical sounds like the occasional falling rock or the strange rumbling or clattering from some unknown source.
34391: You are in a great cavern, travelling upon a wide roadway. The broad shelf upon which you stand plunges into unseen depths just to the northeast. The road arching out east over the depths also runs north, hugging the western wall. Carved out of the solid rock, these walkways traverse large parts of the great fault-line known as Roin's Scar.
34392: Far above, the ceiling is lost in the dark; below, the distant sounds of water gurgling and splashing in the great depths of the caverns echo. The road on which you stand runs from north to south along the western edge of the chasm. The walkways are made of smooth rock and you cannot help but marvel at the ingenuity of the dwarves that once built this roadway. Whatever few handrails there once might have been have long since been destroyed. You find evidence of such railings, but seemingly, someone have torn them all apart.
34393: Vast echoing chasms drop away on either side as you stand on a wide platform. The road arches away south on a great span. To the north it continues to run along the ridge. Giant towering stalagmites reach up from the depths below, while equally large stalactites loom from the hard rock ceiling above you.
34396: You are on a wide ledge at the south-westernmost point of this part of the system of caverns and passages. Two huge stalagmites loom high above you, like a pair of giant statues, welded to the southern rockface. The roadway continues its progress north and east. Below you, and to the west, the gaping black depths of the mountain seem like a bottomless abyss.
34399: Vast, eerily echoing darkness dominates all else. The floor simply disappears to the north, making the mountain's heartrock at your back, south and west, seem even more reassuringly solid. The road that emerges from the western rockface runs away east, hugging the southern wall of the chasm. A narrow stair clings to the precipice just north, winding its way down, presumably towards the echoing thunder of some underground torrent. A roaring sound is rising from the depths below, as well as a fine watery mist.
34400: The glum road bends from south to east as it travels under the mighty peaks of the mountain above. You get a definite feeling that the air is colder here than in other parts of the underground complex you have been passing through. An eerie echoing rumble is coming from the east.
34401: You stand on a wide, dark road whose smooth rock surface is pitted only in a few scattered places. The tunnel twists and bends slightly during its north-south course and the otherwise silent air is mingled with a faint rumbling sound, coming from the north.
34402: At the Bottom of a Chute

A strange bat-like creature is flitting around.
A strange bat-like creature is flitting around.
A strange bat-like creature is flitting around.
A strange bat-like creature is flitting around.
A strange bat-like creature is flitting around.
A strange bat-like creature is flitting around.
A strange bat-like creature is flitting around.
A strange bat-like creature is flitting around.
An orkish warrior of the Durghash is here, with a cruel glint in his eye.

You are standing in a small damp cavern, feeling a gentle breeze drift from the chute above and out through the only other exit west of here. Critically appraising the smooth rock walls climbing up into darkness at a steep angle you realise that ascending would be impossible. The slight trickling of water, running down the walls of the circular shaft, make nothing to improve that situation.
34403: This small tunnel makes a sharp bend from the south to the east. You are forced to watch your step to make sure you do not stumble and fall on any of the sharp rocks that are strewn about this passage. The air is stirred by a steady, though barely noticeable breeze coming from the east.
34404: You are at the northeastern corner of a large chamber. A narrow passage runs off to the north, while wide flagstone extend south and west across the chamber floor. The cavern itself looks to be natural but the ground has clearly seen some extensive work, judging by the large flagstone tiles. The rough, rocky walls look otherwise undisturbed by mortal hand. Standing in this huge cavern, you suddenly hear a faint, high pitched scream echo through the tunnels from somewhere in the distance.
34405:
A large bat is here, hanging in the darkness.
A large bat is here, hanging in the darkness.
A large bat is here, hanging in the darkness.
A large bat is here, hanging in the darkness.
A large bat is here, hanging in the darkness.
A large bat is here, hanging in the darkness.
A large bat is here, hanging in the darkness.
A large bat is here, hanging in the darkness.

This fairly narrow tunnel has scarred walls and bits of trash all about. The faint but readily discernible odour of something rotten pervades the air. The nooks and crannies in the rough walls of this tunnel makes you shift your gaze constantly. It would seem they make excellent places of hiding, and you dare not leave any side unguarded, should something creep up on you.
34406: The passage bends west to north, debris still scattered all about the floor. The foul stench is getting stronger with every step towards the west and while it is not yet insufferable, you wonder how any kind of creature could live in this awful environment. You draw a quick breath of relief as a sudden gust of wind blows through the tunnel, temporarily dispersing the foul fumes.
34407: This smallish tunnel continues its course from east to west. Faeces are noticeable among the various bits of cloth and bone that lie scattered about and you start to realise where the putrid smell is coming from. Even though the smell is what occupies most of your thoughts, your mind staggers at the sight of what lies in a corner of the passageway: the rotting corpse of what once must have been a small humanoid creature, maybe a hobbit, lies carelessly tossed at the southern wall. Its head has been removed and in its place a much too large Dwarven head made of stone has been set, obviously taken from a statue somewhere. The image is a cruel mockery to all that is good and you fight for control as a wave of nausea sweeps violently over you at the gruesome sight.
34408: The Southern End of a Large Cavern

A powerful young troll stares at you.
A powerful young troll stares at you.

You are at the southern end of a cavern. Trash of all types and manner is strewn about and the stench is really strong. This is obviously part of a lair whose inhabitants do not care about tidiness... A narrowish passage runs east-west through this part of the cavern and to the north, the chamber opens up into the darkness.
34409: The litter seems somewhat less in evidence here as the passage narrows and runs away west. This tunnel has obviously seen less use than the one east of here, and the moisture of the walls and the ceiling becomes more apparent as they are now only a few feet from your face.
34410: The narrow passage suddenly comes to an abrupt end as solid rock walls block all directions except back east, from where you came. It is probable that this might be an old abandoned mining tunnel.
34411: A large mean-looking troll is here.

A stinking pile of garbage is stacked up against the northern wall and a fading cooking fire is in the centre of this chamber. Foul odours waft about in this large domed cavern and a thin greasy film of brownish liquid covers the floor. Each step makes a small sucking sound and you are disgusted as you imagine what the stuff comes from. Large ugly looking flies of some sort buzz around you, doing nothing to ease the discomfort of your battered senses. The cavern continues to the south, while two tunnels exit to the east and west.
34412:
A rotten corpse is hanging here.
A stone-grey troll advances toward you, with fury in its eyes.
A stone-grey troll advances toward you, with fury in its eyes.

Carcasses of various natures lie about the feet of the walls of this natural cave. Crude instruments of torture dot the floor and the large boulders that are placed throughout the place. Bits of some unfortunate creature still seem to be attached to these tools in some cases and rough pliers seem to dominate the horrid collection. Propped against a rock in the far corner of the cavern you see the badly beaten corpse of a hobbit. Horrible gaping wounds cover its body and you catch a glimpse of severed fingers before you avert your eyes.
34413:
The corpse of a troll infant is lying here.
The corpse of a troll infant is lying here.
The corpse of a troll infant is lying here.
The corpse of a troll bitch is lying here.
The corpse of a large troll is lying here.
A large mean-looking troll is here.
An infant troll, baring its teeth, snarls here.
An infant troll, baring its teeth, snarls here.
An infant troll, baring its teeth, snarls here.
A nasty troll female crouches here, with a feral look in her eyes.

This cave would seem to serve as the sleeping pit for the troll residents. Warg furs and other skins lie strewn across the floor. The smell is terrible and you cover your nose and mouth as you wander about this room. You can make out several crude cots and also find a worn-out pot thrown into a corner. Rotten and roughly jagged wooden planks stand against the natural rock walls and lie scattered on the ground, their use a mystery. A few boulders also fill the cavern and you quickly discard the idea of resting against one them, the awful smell and general mess of this place effectively dissuading you.
34414: The condition of the wide avenue has slightly improved at this point. Only a few small blocks have fallen from the high roof to splinter on the floor below, the walls here show no large cracks and the rest of the roof appears to be quite stable. Still, one can never be too cautious when dealing with tons of stone overhead, so you had better keep quiet and move along quickly. The avenue meets Durin's Way just to the north and also steadily continues into the south.
34415: This section of the ancient avenue is in no better condition than those you have seen before. Huge cracks cover the walls and some overhead stoneblocks seem ready to drop at any moment. This is definitely not the place for shouting or loud talk, unless you enjoy the feeling of being crushed to death. The ruined avenue runs north and south from here.
34416: An interesting pattern formed by the cracks covering one of the walls here attracts attention. The pattern appears to spell out the word D-O-O-M. Perhaps this is mere coincidence or evidence of an overly active imagination, but it does make one wonder. The avenue here was once wide and grand, and it does appear to have met with great destruction a long time ago. You can follow the ruined avenue north or proceed south through a portal into a large hall.
34417: This once magnificent great hall now lies in ruins. Large chunks of grey stone have plummeted from the roof to block most of the hall, and shards of rusted metal lie everywhere underfoot. The air here is both damp and dust-filled, a most unpleasant combination which is difficult to breathe for long periods of time. What used to be a wide avenue bends through the middle of this hall then continues through large sculptured portals centred in the north and east walls.
34418:
A large cave troll sniffs the air, sensing an intruder is near.
A large cave troll sniffs the air, sensing an intruder is near.

The damp air here lends a shiny lustre to the dark walls that border this wide avenue. You wonder how long this place has existed, and exactly what happened here that allowed orcs to destroy what must have been one of the most magnificent places on Arda. There are bone fragments scattered everywhere here that crack under your feet with every step you take. The avenue leads west through an elaborately carved portal and continues east as far as the eye can see.
34419: Blasted ruins of iron sprawl out from both sides of this wide avenue. Once- proud Dwarven homes lie crushed beneath immense iron pillars which have been toppled like tenpins. Twisted and melted iron statuary leers out from behind an overturned fountain which blocks the centre of the avenue ahead. Many of the standing structures are covered with strange marks which make no sense at all to you. By skirting the ruins, it is possible to travel east or west from here.
34420: A fierce battle must have raged here within the past day, judging from the blood and flesh that is strewn about this part of the Avenue. There are no humanoid limbs or bodies here, but you do spot a pile of gigantic old bones and some huge sharp teeth piled near a stone pillar just north of the road. Some large, dark pools of water north of the pillar ripple ominously as you approach, and you quickly decide to return to the relative safety of Iron Avenue. The Avenue leads east and west from here, as it ever has.
34421: The massive strength displayed in the design of this great hall forms the overwhelming impression upon you. The walls here are jet black, polished and smooth as glass, and the vast roof far above is upheld by many mighty pillars of stone. There are three dark black arches which lead out of this place onto wide avenues travelling east, west and north.
34422: This narrow portion of the Avenue is choked by the many toppled black walls and crumbling stone dwellings that once bordered the road. A large, rust-covered iron dome which used to crown a small building nearby rests upside-down directly in front of you. Everything here is covered by a fine layer of dust, and the air is stale-smelling and very still. There has been no activity near this place in many months at the very least. To the west lies a huge, rusted iron archway which opens into a dark hall, while to the east there is much more debris cluttering the Avenue.
34423: The Avenue of Iron has fallen into ruin and utter disrepair here, meaning that your progress through here will be difficult at best. Many huge pits and chasms open up in the roadway in front of you, and much of the surrounding overhead stonework has worked its way loose then crashed down in great chunks. Because of the obvious dangers present here, minions avoid travelling this way if possible, and you should also exercise caution when you decide to continue onward to the east or west.
34424: The Avenue of Iron comes to an abrupt end in a most unexpected manner here. It runs directly east to the base of a massive solid steel wall which completely blocks any passage to or from the east. You search every inch of the wall and find no secret doors or keyholes, but do notice several points where the wall seems to have been dented from the other side! What force did this wall serve to hold back? Some mysteries are perhaps better left unsolved. The Avenue leads back west from here.
34426:
A squat and filthy troll lurks in the darkness.
A misshapen troll stands here, stooped over on his twisted legs.

The environs here are shrouded in complete darkness. The road under your feet still feels firm, but you tread cautiously in hope of avoiding any unseen crack or pitfall. The air here is damp and warm, and carries the slight smell of decaying flesh. Though you cannot see exactly where you are headed, you can make your way along the Avenue generally north or south from this point.
34427: A pair of tiny eyes gleam at you from the shadows.

This section of Yavanna's Avenue is wide and clear of all debris. There are many tracks here in the dust indicating that this way receives a lot of use, but there does not seem to be too much activity here now. The road leads north towards a huge chasm and south into darkness.
34428: The Avenue is very wide here and shows several subtle signs of graceful wear from many years of hard use. Several now-abandoned structures near here appear to be storehouses for goods, mining tools and stone destined for trade or sale. Apparently, a lot of activity has taken place near here over the centuries, and perhaps you are approaching a well-used nexus in the city. The road continues south from here towards a huge chasm or runs north into some dim light.
34429: The Avenue receives some scant light from somewhere above here which illuminates some fine stonework characteristic of the Moria dwarves. Many large faces or masks holding a range of expressions have been sculpted in relief into the walls bordering the road. This strikes you as curious, but serves to lighten your mood. The way continues to the north and south into deeper shadow.
34430: This wide avenue leads directly north to the foot of a gigantic brass portal which opens into a huge hall. The thoroughfare is still in excellent condition to the south, and the seamless stonework here provides a fine example of the supreme mastery the dwarves held in the art of roadbuilding.
34431: The scale and splendour of this titanic bronze greathall inspires wonder and beggars description. Two rows of immense sculpted bronze columns support a great copper-clad vaulted roof, now green with great age. Each thick column holds the shattered remains of a great crystal lamp, whose radiance once bathed gemstone-studded murals and walls with soft, warm light. Much beauty here has been despoiled or ruined by age and decay, but enough remains to validate the reputation of Moria dwarves as the most skilled masters of stonecraft and metalwork ever to walk on Arda. The Bronze Hall stretches into the west, and you can pass through wide bronze portals east and south onto wide avenues.
34432: The wide and stately Bronze Avenue shows no signs of any frequent use nearby recently. The air here is damp, still and carries no scent, and the surroundings are silent and gloomy. You see a huge bronze arch to the west and more roadway vanishing into the darkness east.
34433: It has quickly become very dark here, almost as if something was actively absorbing any light that chanced into this vicinity. You are certain that you are travelling on Bronze Avenue because of the familiar pattern of the interlocking stonework under your feet here, but there is nothing else that provides any clues as to what may lie about you in the darkness. There is a layer of undisturbed dust covering everything that you can see, so it appears that no one has been through here recently. The Avenue leads east and west.
34434: This place is now so dark that you feel smothered, as if trapped in a giant black fist which is slowly crushing all within it. You inch along to the east past some huge blocks of dark stone and come upon an obstacle that you cannot surmount: a colossal pile of rubble hundreds of feet high which completely fills the Avenue. It would take an army of Dwarves a month to clear a path through this mess. There is no other choice but to travel west from here.
34435: The sheer size and regal beauty of this titanic hall are such that all who first visit here are struck dumb with wonder. The great vault of the roof overhead is supported by twin rows of immense bronze columns, each as thick and tall as an ancient mallorn. Many raised platforms support the shattered remnants of golden, many-tiered fountains which once spouted laughing streams of water down spillways into a large central pool. In the bottom of this now cracked and empty pit, a halo of seven silver stars shines back at any who gaze there. Amidst all of this faded splendour, signs of the wrack and ruin brought here by the orcs can be found. Everything of any possible value has been plundered or destroyed, and a faint smell of decay still lingers here. The Bronze Hall stretches into darkness to the east, or you can pass through a gigantic bronze portal to the west.
34436: A large earth tremor must have taken place in this vicinity causing most of the roof here to cave-in. Huge boulders and blocks of dark granite cover a large part of the avenue, but it is still possible to pass east or west through the mass of dark rubble. The possibility of another tremor sobers you.
34437: For a brief moment, the shadows disappear and reveal a long and mighty avenue, and you get a sense of the glory and greatness that this place once possessed. The gloom quickly returns, however, and only a short section of the avenue remains in view. You can proceed east or west along Bronze Avenue.
34438: A pair of tiny eyes gleam at you from the shadows.

This titanic hall sprawls out in grand majesty in every direction about you. Its roof and walls seem to be miles in the distance, making you imagine that you have somehow wandered outside under a still and moonless night sky. The floor here consists of brightly coloured mosaic tiles laid out to show scenes from the founding of Moria. The wide Bronze Avenue bends through the centre of this magnificent place, then exits through gigantic carved portals to the east and south. There is also a rough opening chopped through a mural in the west wall.
34439: A squat and filthy troll lurks in the darkness.

As is the case with most of the other ancient avenues near here, this one is in extremely poor condition. It probably isn't a good idea to speak loudly or stand here for long due to danger from the unstable stonework. The avenue continues north and south, and you cannot help noticing a large black opening torn into a sturdy wall to the east. Even your sharp eyes cannot penetrate the blackness there, and fear vies with curiosity as you try to decide what to do next.
34440: A squat and filthy troll lurks in the darkness.

What was once a stately, wide avenue has now become a cracked and pit- filled obstacle field. Man-sized blocks of grey stone have crashed to the floor from the vaulted ceiling high above, crushing walls and cracking stonework all around you. It would be best to remain silent, walk nimbly, and leave here as soon as possible, following the remnant of the avenue either north or south from this point.
34441: The avenue that you had expected to find here simply does not exist anymore: it has been replaced by a rubble-filled boulder field. Making through progress appears to be almost impossible, as every potential passage looks completely choked by huge piles of stone and dirt. Whatever you decide, this is certainly not the place for loud talk or hasty movements due to the extremely unstable nature of the stone here. It may be possible to win your way north or south with a lot of luck and persistence, and you certainly do not want to remain here for very long.
34442: A large stairway winds down from above, pauses at a landing, and then continues downward. To the north and south, rooms that were surely used to station guards flank the wide hallway. East and west, Durin's Way continues its journey beneath the mountains.
34443: This is a large Avenue that stretches from the Gates of Durin to the Dimrill gate. It is a very large tunnel, arched, and constructed of a band-pattern weave of grey granite and white marble. There are broken lanterns hanging from rings in the ceiling.
34444: This is a large Avenue that stretches from the westernmost part of Khazad-dum to the Dimrill Gates. It is a very large tunnel, arched, and constructed of grey granite and white marble. The lanterns that should light the passage hang broken and useless from the ceiling.
34445: You fall without concept of time, beyond all light and deep into the earth. Eventually, your body is broken on a jagged rock wall, before it is plunged into icy-cold water to rot.
34446: You fall without concept of time, beyond all light and deep into the earth. Eventually, your body is broken on a jagged rock wall, before it is plunged into icy-cold water to rot.
34455: This passageway is about half the size of the Avenues running through Khazad-dum. The walls and ceiling are smooth and flat, bearing no decorations or inscriptions. Broken torch-brackets line the walls.
34456: This armoury lies quiet and empty - abandoned now for hundreds of years. There is hardly a sign left from the days when the dwarves inhabited this place. The weapons and armour that were once stockpiled here were plundered or destroyed long ago.
34457: This is a small guard room used by the guards to watch over the Central Gathering Hall. This lower room is where guards stand ready to run out and crush whatever opponent may be in the Hall. This room is filthy and there is a rotting corpse in the corner. There is a window in the northeast corner of the room looking into the Hall.
34458: This is a small room where guards can stand watch over the Western Gathering Hall, ready to rush out and crush whatever enemy may be there. There is a window in the northwest corner looking into the Hall. Bones lay strewn about the room and there is a rotting corpse in the middle of the room.
34459: This small room is the lower room used by armed guards, who stand watch over the Central Gathering Hall, ready to rush out and crush whatever enemy may enter. The chamber is filthy, and a heap of bones lies in one corner, whilst in the opposite corner a window looks out into the hall.
34460: This small chamber serves as a guard room, home to those who stand watch over the Western Gathering Hall, ready to rush out and mercilessly crush whatever enemy who may be foolish enough to enter. A large window in the southwest corner of the room looks out onto the hall, affording a clear view, and piles of bones lie strewn all about.
34461: A dark-skinned orc, born of the tunnels, draws his weapon.

This is a small room where guards can keep watch over the Ceremonial Hall. There is a small window in the northwest corner of the room and a row of arrow slits where guards can use bows to support their comrades if there is trouble in the Hall. This room is filthy, and there is a pile of bones in the corner that probably belonged to the Dwarves who first owned this city.
34462: This is a small guard room used to keep watch over the Gathering Hall. There is a small window and a number of arrow slits in the northeast corner of the room. This room is filthy and a stench of death seems to hang over this place. There is a pile of bones in the corner.
34463: This passage quickly ends in a wall of rubble to the west. The small portion that has survived looks like it was once very elegant -- somehow pristine white marble and some type of glossy black basalt were made to seamlessly melt into one another, creating a striking contrast on the floors and walls. A small inscribed plaque on the northern wall still bears some runes.
34464: These wide stairs quickly narrow and begin to spiral up through the shaft above. The stairs lack ornamentation of any sort, as does the corridor in which they terminate, suggesting that perhaps this area was not for public use. A small bronze plaque, upon which runes are visible, is prominently displayed on the wall next to the stairs.
36309:
An eyeless white rat with nasty teeth scurries about.
An eyeless white rat with nasty teeth scurries about.
An eyeless white rat with nasty teeth scurries about.
An orkish warrior of the Durghash is here, with a cruel glint in his eye.
An orc, of the Durghash tribe, crouches here.
A lurg leader, with markings of the Durghash tribe, stands here.
An orkish warrior of the Durghash is here, with a cruel glint in his eye.

Tall, gilded pillars support slender arches, which rise gracefully to the high ceiling of this large chamber. A raised dais stands at the northern end of the hall, whilst to the south, an ornate staircase climbs to some unseen room, above. A smaller stair, half-hidden in a narrow alcove in the north- western corner of the hall, descends, almost unnoticed.
36310: The metallic skeleton of what was once an ornate chandelier sits squarely in the middle of the hall, but anything of value has long ago been scavenged from its remains. It is impossible to tell from what great height it might have fallen, for the ceiling is lost in the omnipresent darkness far overhead.
36311: At intervals along this broad passageway, large, smoothly arched alcoves have been carved into the southern wall. Most now hold little more than dust and rubble, but in some stand the half-shattered remains of what must once have been magnificent sculptures.
36312: Alcoves are occasionally cut in the walls of this large road, completely empty except for little piles of alabaster shards -- remnants of shattered statues. Deep darkness hides the top portions of the pillars and arches that reach up toward the ceiling.
36313: A shattered sculpture is housed in the alcove before you. The entire top half of the statue has been destroyed, leaving a rough and jagged surface, covered in dust and splintered fragments of stone. Chunks of polished marble lie about the base of the statue, and also litter the floor of the passageway itself.
36314: A ghostly echo seems to linger here, in homage to the days when this chamber stood at an important intersection in the dwarven kingdom of Moria. To the north, Narvi's Smelting Hall now stands broken and unused, and below a great Ceremonial Hall now lies silent. Dust and debris litter a floor, which must once have seen a ceaseless passage of feet, and ancient torches hang useless in their brackets, their precious oils long-since evaporated.
36315: The road seems to come to an abrupt end as it enters this huge cavern. But, in truth, this hall offers only a brief respite from the monotony of endless travel along Azaghal's Way, which stretches onward, north and east from here. Standing all around, are the forges of Narvi. Cold, and covered with the grease and grime of long disuse, the great black forges somehow seem to retain a memory of the volcanic heat, which once erupted from their hearts. Sooty- faced artisans once scurried hither and thither, from anvil to master, seeking approval for their work, before moving on to yet another task. However, now all is still and silent. No more will the riches of Khazad-dum be processed here, and no hammer will strike anvil in this place again.
36316: Blackened by the soot of Narvi's ancient black forges, the walls here tell the tale of ancient times, when the smelting hall, to the west, swarmed with activity, day and night. But now, all is still, and a chilly silence fills the air.
36317: The realisation that a mountain of stone hangs overhead is perhaps a little disconcerting to any but the children of Aule. However, reassurance can be found, in the strong, straight walls, and the smooth stone floor; this proud roadway is clearly a construction of Durin's folk.
36318: In the happier days, before the dwarves closed their doors against the legions of Sauron, Khazad-dum was frequently visited by the elves of Eregion. And so, although built by the dwarves, this roadway was not one constructed solely for their use, as evidenced by the grand proportions of this tunnel.
36319: Massive flag-stones comprise the floor of this passageway, which was obviously built with heavy use in mind. The ceiling is high above your head, and even the span of two men's arms would not bridge from wall to wall. But it seems that this tunnel has seen little recent use, judging by the fine film of dust which carpets the ground.
36320: In the all-enveloping darkness, it would be easy to walk into the wall as this passage swings from west to north. The deathly silence here seems to add to the darkness, making it almost tangible, and the warm motionless air gives a dismaying sense of claustrophobia to even the stout-hearted.
36321: The floor here is quite level, and paved with huge stone flags, as if to reinforce it for the passage of heavy loads. An abandoned and rather badly damaged mine car rests against the smooth stone wall, its ancient load of ore long ago plundered, leaving only a small pile of worthless rubble beside it.
36322: Like a dark and long scar, this tunnel cuts a bold path through the mountain, leading downward to the west of here, and levelling out to the east. Never deviating from its straight course, the passageway stretches onward as far as you can see.
36323: Although finely crafted, the utilitarian nature of this tunnel is obvious in the unadorned and neatly squared tunnel walls, and the heavily flagged stone floor. But the days in which it saw the energetic activities of a hoard of dwarven miners are long gone, and today a crushing silence fills the air, save only for the repeating echoes of your own footfalls.
36324: The shattered and rotten remains of an old mine car litter the floor here, and its once-treasured cargo lies scattered about it, with all valuables long- since plundered. But this senseless act of destruction has made no impact on the tunnel itself, which retains its imposing strength and clean lines.
37072: The passage is dim and barren of all else except rock. The plain grey granite walls run east and west into darkness. There is a small opening to the north.
37073: The air is stale and still. A layer of dust has settled onto everything in this small room. A small table lies overturned on the ground and a small little stool stands upturned in the corner. The granite walls of the room are solid except for the small opening to the south.
37074: This passage is cut from dull grey granite. The air is stale and still in the darkness. Here the rocky corridor bends so that it runs west and south. Bits of rusted metal and bones here and there litter the sides of the passage. Settled dust and rock debris lie on the passage floor.
37075:
A large arrow lies on the ground.
A large arrow lies on the ground.
A large arrow lies on the ground.

Here three paths converge from the north, east, and west. The ground here is scattered with bits of debris which mostly collect in the corners of the room. To the west a room opens up while hallways continue to the north and east.
37076: This hallway is cut out of solid grey granite as the sides of the alley seem to indicate. The way seems to curve to the west while continuing to the north.
37077: The alley appears to have been carved out of solid grey granite as the sides and ceiling are made of the same rock. The ground, however, is littered with bits and scraps of dusty junk which gathers to the side of this hallway which runs north and south. A strong stench emanates from the north.
37079: A dark orkish archer is aiming a vicious bow at you.

The room is strewn with ragged bits of cloth resembling blankets and numerous charred wooden frames hint of Dwarven beds. However nothing in the room appears to have been left in one piece as orcs have probably pillaged their way here once.
37080: Pieces of tables and cracked little stools sprawled all over are evidence that this may have once been a dining area. Cracked bits of plates and rusted spoons litter the floor. A dark little room is visible to the east while there is a larger opening to the north.
37081: This appears to have once been a food storeroom used by the dwarves. Having been ransacked and looted by marauding orcs, there seems to be nothing left save for bits of shattered barrels and some tattered bits of flour sacks. Mould and yellow rotten flour cover the ground. A small archway to the west appears to be the only exit.
37082: This dank cell is used to hold prisoners that are to be sacrificed to whatever dark god these orcs worship - more than likely Durin's Bane. The accommodations are spartan, there is not even a pile of straw to sleep on. The previous occupants of the cell soiled the back corner with their filth, so the stench is horrible.
37083: A small but powerful shaman is here, chanting some evil incantations.

This dark room has had its walls painted black and inscribed with strange runes of flaming crimson. In one corner are the remains of a fire -- the grey ashes have been tracked around the room. On the walls are several shelves stocked with paraphernalia of unknown uses. A straw pallet lies in the southwest corner.
37084: A short, pitch-black tunnel stretches east and opens into a large noisy room. Shouts and shrill screams echo down this tunnel from the east, and you have little doubt that those voices belong to some large orcs. There is a poorly concealed door in the stone wall to the west, again probably the work of the orcs that are lurking nearby.
37085:
An orkish warrior of the Durghash is here, with a cruel glint in his eye.
An orkish warrior of the Durghash is here, with a cruel glint in his eye.
An orkish warrior of the Durghash is here, with a cruel glint in his eye.
An orkish warrior of the Durghash is here, with a cruel glint in his eye.
An orkish cook is here, looking for anything to spice up his stew.

This rather spacious room is used as a dining hall by a troop of Durghash orcs stationed here. There is a wide variety of meats and breads spread out on an immense slab of stone in the centre of the chamber, and also a collection of carcasses hanging from hooks in the ceiling. You notice two large black cauldrons and several iron spits leaning against the western wall, and a large fireplace built into the southern wall. It is very noisy in here, as orcs make quite a racket when feeding, and you hear other shouts and screams coming from the east as well. There are exits to the north, east and west.
37086:
An orkish warrior of the Durghash is here, with a cruel glint in his eye.
An orkish warrior of the Durghash is here, with a cruel glint in his eye.
An orkish warrior of the Durghash is here, with a cruel glint in his eye.
An orkish warrior of the Durghash is here, with a cruel glint in his eye.

The Durghash guards use this small room for sleeping, gambling, and most of all, arguing. They are currently gathered about a small table in the centre of the room with a set of rolling bones on it. Most look very unhappy to you.
37087:
A great wolf with a sable coat glares around with red eyes.
A great wolf with a sable coat glares around with red eyes.
A great wolf with a sable coat glares around with red eyes.
A great wolf with a sable coat glares around with red eyes.

This filthy chamber serves as a holding pen for the Durghash orcs' wolves. Old bones and shredded leather rags lie about the room, with mats upon which you presume the wolves sleep. The floor bears some obvious claw- marks.
37088: There is a cleverly concealed mud-coloured trapdoor built into the roof of this small empty chamber. The north wall has several deep footholds carved into it to allow easy access to the opening through the roof. A narrow tunnel also leads off to the west.
37089: The tunnel floor here is covered by shallow pools of slime-filled water. Large droplets splash into the pools from the roof above, resulting in the echoing drip-drop sound which occasionally breaks the silence. The wet tunnel bends both north and east from this point.
37090: A huge stone troll looms overhead, ready to crush your body.

A cold draft gusts through this section of the wet tunnel, making you shiver involuntarily. The sound of dripping water echoes all around you, but is especially strong from the west. The tunnel bends here from south to west.
37091: The water-logged tunnel bends east to south here. The tunnel walls and roof are coated with slimy water, and the smooth floor is very slippery here. The repetitive sound of dripping water echoes from the south.
37092: Moisture trickles down slick walls here, and falls in large droplets from the ceiling into large pools underneath your feet. The footing is quite treacherous here, so beware! The wet tunnel continues west and north from this point.
37093:
A lurg leader, wielding a nasty orkish fang, is here, fighting Iarion.
Iarion the Elf, wielding an engraved broadsword, is here, fighting a lurg leader.
Kostilam, wielding a mighty dwarven axe, is here, fighting a lurg leader.

This tunnel is quite narrow, and it leads east and north. You feel a cold draft from the east, and the sound of water dripping onto rock comes from there as well. A large, impregnable door of stone blocks your passage north.
37094:
A great wolf with a sable coat glares around with red eyes.
A great wolf with a sable coat glares around with red eyes.

A truly horrendous stench wafts over you from the north. There really must be tons of filth near in order to cause such a strong odour. You hear screaming, angry voices from the north as well, and you shiver as you recognise the shrill cries of orcs! The tunnel leads north into a large cavern and south towards a sturdy stonedoor.
37095:
A plain pair of pants are on the ground.
A large cave troll sniffs the air, sensing an intruder is near.
A large cave troll sniffs the air, sensing an intruder is near.

This very large cavern is cluttered with skeletons and piles of old, cracked bones that emit an overpowering odour. The large cavetrolls that live here noisily shamble out from behind a boulder to look for something more to eat. A quick check for exits reveals two large openings at the north and south ends of the cavern.
37096:
An orkish warrior of the Durghash is here, with a cruel glint in his eye.
An orkish warrior of the Durghash is here, with a cruel glint in his eye.
An orkish warrior of the Durghash is here, with a cruel glint in his eye.
An orkish warrior of the Durghash is here, with a cruel glint in his eye.

This fortified cave serves as a barracks for the troop of Durgash prison guards that lives here. It is furnished with a large table, several crude seats and a few filthy sleeping mats. The screaming and snarling orcs produce a lot of noise and stench as they torture their hapless victims to death. There are steel celldoors to the east and west, and a large cave to the south.
37097:
A weary slave who has lost all hope sits here staring into space.
A weary slave who has lost all hope sits here staring into space.

This is one of many dark, dreary Durgash prison cells. Judging from the conditions present here, the orcs do not treat their captives well at all. No one could live more than a few years in this squalor, and many probably choose death by torture over a slow rot in here.
37098:
A prisoner is standing here.
A prisoner is standing here.

This is one of many dark, dreary Durgash prison cells. Judging by the conditions here, they do not treat their captives well in any sense. No one could last more than a few years in this squalor, and many probably choose death by torture over this slow rot.
37099:
A large wooden wall shield rests on the ground.
A pair of metal vambraces lies here.
A reinforced leather helmet lies here.
A pair of soft leather boots are on the ground.
A broadsword lies here.
A broadsword lies here.

This must be the place where the orcs store the plunder looted from the corpses of their enemies and any others unlucky enough to be waylaid by them in the Mines. Various sorts of equipment lie scattered on the floor, but there is no gold to be found here. The orcs have taken great pains to hide any true valuables from the greedy grasp of outsiders.
37100:
A long rope, with a hook at one end, has been left here.
A great wolf with a sable coat glares around with red eyes.
A great wolf with a sable coat glares around with red eyes.
An orkish warrior of the Durghash is here, with a cruel glint in his eye.
An orkish warrior of the Durghash is here, with a cruel glint in his eye.
An orkish warrior of the Durghash is here, with a cruel glint in his eye.
A lurg leader, with markings of the Durghash tribe, stands here.

This circular room has unblemished walls chiselled out by the skilled hands of Dwarven stoneworkers. Unfortunately, this place is now littered with filth and the decayed remains from countless orc meals. There is a large hardwood table surrounded by six crudely constructed chairs in the middle of the room and a wide, very strong stonedoor centred in the southern wall. From high on the northern wall the mark of the Red Eye stares down on you, emphasising the fact that this is not an ideal resting place for any save the Durghash.
37101: A great black orc stands here, eager for combat.

This Dwarven guard-room has apparently been appropriated by an orc of some importance for use as both living quarters and command post. The ruined cushions shoved in one corner provide a place to sleep, and the large table in the centre of the room is used for both meals -- judging by the remains upon it -- and as a workspace.
37186: The stairs are in bad shape here and many of the individual steps have been pitted and scarred. Even the shaft through which the staircase spirals pos- sesses cracks and fractures in abundance. Below, the spiralling stairs cease their winding, and become a wide and broad stair leading down and south.
37187: The stairs here are slightly damaged -- each exposed surface is pitted, as if an enormous force had hurled sand and small pebbles at the rock. Above, the stairs appear to end in a corridor of some type, while below the steps disappear quickly into the night.
37188: Some sort of disaster to the west has severely damaged this passage. To the west the walls are riddled with fractures and tiny pits, whose frequency decreases as one moves east. A narrow stairway leads down to the deeper portions of Moria -- it also appears to head slightly south as well.
37189: This small chamber has been victimised by a massive explosion of some sort -- too many years have passed to determine if this was done by fell magic or by some fiery device of the orcs. The stone of both floor and walls is covered with fractures, and the rock of the ceiling looks to have been slightly melted by great heat. A passage leading to the west has been completely sealed by debris, but it is possible to proceed to the east. There is a small inscribed plaque set in the wall, but it too has been damaged.
37190: Plunging into blackness, these ancient stairs have been undisturbed for ages. Each step is coated with a thick layer of dust and cobwebs often stretch completely across the vertical shaft through which the stairs pass.
37191: Both above and below, these narrow stairs continue their journey. The layers of accumulated dust bear no sign of footprints, so these stairs have probably lain unused since the time when dwarves last inhabited these tunnels.
37192: A flight of stairs commences here, heading downward to the lower levels of Khazad-dum. This passageway has suffered extensive damage, with small piles of rubble from collapsed portions of the ceiling and walls cluttering the floor. To the east, the corridor continues briefly, but then becomes totally closed off due to a collapse of the entire roof. The passage also continues to the north.
37193: This passage has suffered heavy damage -- probabably in the tumults that fol- lowed the waking of Durin's Bane. The masonry of the walls and ceiling has been severely fractured, and in several place it has collapsed completely, revealing the dark native rock behind. To the east there is a door that has somehow survived, and the passage continues to the south. Almost unnoticed in the rubble on the floor is a small metallic plaque that probably fell from the wall years ago.
37194: This rough passage ends abruptly in a wall to the west. The masonry of the walls and floor has cracked and fallen in several places, giving this area a rough and shoddy look not usually found in dwarven constructions -- perhaps the tremors that shook the earth after the Balrog was awakened proved too much for the stone to handle.
37195: To the south the passage has been totally destroyed, but to the north it is still possible to weave a path among the rocky debris. There are many spider webs covering the rocks and walls, and they get thicker to the north.
37196: The passage is totally choked with sticky strands of spider web. No longer mere cobwebs, these threads grab and hold anything with which they come in contact, forcing one to briefly fight free. The webs are noticeably thicker to the north, while they abate somewhat to the south.
37197:
A huge, poisonous spider is here.
A huge, poisonous spider is here.
A huge, poisonous spider is here.

The webs are very thick here, and there are the dessicated remains of several bats and rats strung into the threads. A shaft begins directly above -- it seems to be the home of many spiders judging from the amount of webs visible. The shaft must lead to some sort of food source for these arachnids, but it is impossible to negotiate the climb required to discover its destination.
37198: These stairs have lain unused for ages, judging from the quantity of undis- turbed dust that greets each falling footstep. Spiralling down a smooth-cut shaft, the stairs approach a passage of some sort below, while they disappear above into the dark.
37199: This flight of narrow stairs continues its winding journey both above and below. There is a small landing here, and to the south the faint silhouette of a door can be seen. The steps were obviously cut by the dwarves for they are suited to the short stature of that people. There is a small plaque set in the northern wall opposite the doorway, and runes are visible upon it.
37200: A very narrow set of stairs that lead down. A thick door made of stone is set in the wall to the west. Judging by the weight of the door, this staircase was rarely used.
37201:
There are three smaller parts of broken weapons here.
A strange white skull lies on the floor looking at you.
There are two piles of greater parts of a broken weapon here.
A wooden chest stands in the corner.

High on the eastern wall of this room, a wide shaft leads upwards toward the open sky, and the ventilation provided has robbed this room of the musty smell that years of neglect have imparted to other areas of Khazad-dum. By both the large door on the western end, and the much smaller door on the eastern side, many bones are lying, and among them are broken swords and axe-heads, and cloven shields and helms. Many of the swords are crooked orc scimitars with blackened blades. There are many recesses cut in the rock of the wall, and nestled within are the broken remnants of large iron-bound chests of wood. In the centre of the room, there is a large table cut of a single block of stone.
37202: This is a small room where guards can keep watch over the Gathering Hall. There is a small window in the southeast corner of the room and a row of arrow slits allowing archers to fire arrows at enemies in the Hall. In the centre of the room is a spear mounted in the floor. Spitted on that spear about halfway up, is an unfortunate goblin, still twitching in agony.
37203: Azaghal's Way traces a sweeping curve to the south here, to be interrupted by an immense cavern, which the dwarves put to use, long ago, as a smelting hall. Traces of that ancient activity are to be found here, in the smoky film, which coats the walls of the tunnel, a residue of the massive fires, whose heat has since been quenched by the cold march of time.
37204: A gloomy silence descends upon the roadway from the south, where it opens into a large chamber. The impenetrable darkness of Moria somehow seems to be more tangible here, as if it were working together with the strange silence, in an effort to protect Azaghal's Way from the prying eyes of outsiders.
37205: A pressing stillness engulfs this vast chamber, and where there should be echoing footfalls, silence reigns supreme. The cold, granite walls somehow seem able to absorb sound, and no crack nor protrusion mars the featureless surface of the rock; even the stone floor remains unbroken. It is tempting to conclude that such a strange cavern can only be the result of some evil force, at work in the rock itself.
37206: A sombre silence creeps in from the chamber to the east, and is so thick that it seems to smother every echo. To the north and south, dark stone walls impose a silent and guarded vigil upon this mighty roadway, as if the mountain itself were wary of any stranger.
37207: Azaghal's Way climbs ever eastward. With a high ceiling, flat, featureless walls, and a floor so smooth that it almost seems polished, this thoroughfare is obviously one of ancient dwarven design. Yet now, it has an inescapable air of evil, as if long tainted by the presence of Sauron's minions.
37208: Ominous shadows and shapes lurk all around, and the cold, grey walls seem to watch every move. It almost seems that any who dare to venture here lose control of their own fate, and surrender to the will of Moria.
37209: Westward, the roadway widens as it approaches the entrance to a large cavern. Here, the cold, grey granite walls give way to delicate, swirling colours, which intensify closer to the cave, drawing the eye ever to the west.
37210: Natural rock can sometimes play tricks on the eye, and so it is here, where each rockface shows a myriad of colours, which seem to leap out and dance across the chamber. Purples and reds, bright yellows and soft blues, criss- crossing and merging, climb the walls, and spiral around huge stalagmites and stalactites. In places, a single colour cuts a bold, yet slender, line across the back-drop of dull, grey stone, climbing to trace delicate loops and whorls on the ceiling above. Azaghal's Way plunges onward to the east and west, seemingly oblivious to the spectacle, whilst to the south, a small, dark passageway cuts into the mountain. The sweeping colours of the northern rock wall are punctuated only by a small opening, which lets onto a stone staircase.
37211: As the roadway widens, and approaches the vast, natural cavern to the east, so the walls to either side begin to take on a new, and rather warmer appearance. Soft veins and small flecks of colour break through the harsh, grey granite, and yet, are but a pale reflection of the beauty of the chamber beyond.
37212: A pressing darkness enshrouds the roadway, dominating thoughts and feelings. Hollow echoes of every sound, however faint, haunt this place, creating the illusion of small armies, trudging endlessly along Azaghal's Way. It is disconcerting to realise that your own echoing footfalls might obscure the sound of an approaching foe.
37213: To the west, the road crosses through a huge cavern, a place of immense natural beauty, but here, the stark, grey walls are cold and featureless. The darkness of Moria presses in on all sides, and the only sound is the repeating echo of footfalls.
37214: Even the most tired and cynical would be awed by the sight of this cavern. The cold, dark reality of Moria seems to be suspended here, as if this chamber, alone, existed in a different and more tranquil time. The walls, the ceiling, and even the floor, sparkle brightly, in even the faintest trace of light, sweeping the observer into a world of fantastic images. But all too soon, the wondrous luminosity gives way, once more, to dreary, grey, granite walls, as Azaghal's Way stretches east and west, and a smaller road slopes gently away to the south.
37215: A mighty chasm opens up to the east, breaking the monotony of travel along this seemingly endless road. Though the darkness here remains complete, a new sense of orientation is offered by the changing air currents, and the more booming echoes, which assail you from the east.
37216: This vast chasm, thousands of feet deep, was once riddled with dozens of stairways, and crossed by a collection of wide bridging spans, which linked great corbels and abutments, far above and way below. But, time has taken its toll here, and as the earth has shifted over the ages, most of these great stone stairs and walkways have been destroyed. Now all that is possible is to peer upward, and wonder what mysterious crevices and tunnels hide aloft, or to gaze into the depths, and imagine the riches which might be hoarded there. For no stair now travels the chasm from here, and the only paths to choose are along Azaghal's Way, to the west, or eastward across the one narrow stone bridge, which still spans this gulf.
37217: The dwarves of Khazad-dum once climbed freely from level to level in this vast shaft, which stretches north to south, and up and down, far into the darkness. But then, in their greed, they delved too deep, setting loose a foe beyond their match, and all their proud work was laid to waste. Where once slender bridges of stone reached out across the abyss to a mighty granite coloumn, at the centre of the chasm, now only shattered ruins remain. And the spiral stair, which winds round the tower, is now quite impossible to reach.
37218: Booming echoes resound from the gaping rift to the west, and a refreshing draught of cooler air breaks into the stifling stagnancy of the passageway. Azaghal's Way turns to the north here, in a majestic, sweeping curve, and marches off into the darkness.
37219: Azaghal's Way plunges eastward through the mountain, as far as the eye can see. But at this small intersection, it curves to the south, before continuing its inexorable westward march. To the north, a small tunnel finds its own path through the unforgiving rock, but it too boasts the smooth stone walls which typify the work of the dwarves of Moria.
37220: A small campfire burns here, its low flames giving off only a little light.

The walls of this small tunnel are smooth and flawless. Gently curving, they give this small passageway an almost circular cross-section, except where they meet the floor, which is flat and level, with no pits or protrusions.
37221:
A strange bat-like creature is flitting around.
A strange bat-like creature is flitting around.
A strange bat-like creature is flitting around.
A strange bat-like creature is flitting around.
A strange bat-like creature is flitting around.
A strange bat-like creature is flitting around.
A strange bat-like creature is flitting around.

Massive aggregates of small, prismatic, indigo and azure crystals completely cover the walls and ceiling of this pretty cave. Even the floor is blue, although its crystalline surface has been worn quite smooth. All that can be seen interrupting this endless cerulean sea are some scattered bands of green malachite, which nestle amongst the azurite.
37222: Empty and silent, the road stretches east and west. In the inky darkness, it is easy to succumb to all manner of wild and terrifying fantasies. These products of imagination are given greater reality by a sense of evil, which seems to reside in the cold, grey granite of the walls, floor and ceiling.
37223: In the ancient days of the First and Second Ages of the Sun, before the years of Sauron's dominion, this imposing thoroughfare must have echoed day and night to the activity of the busy dwarves, and the innumerable footfalls of the hosts of travellers, who passed this way, to trade with the wealthy overlords of Khazad-dum. But now all is cold and silent.
37224: The road stretches off into the darkness to the east and west. At one point it must have been a major artery of dwarven traffic. Now through eons of disuse a thick layer of dust has accumulated in the corners and gutters.
37225: Two major roads come to an intersection. At one time it must have been bustling with traffic. Now the dark is its travelling companion. The ceiling comes to a slight peak forming a quadripartite vault. To the north and south twinkling lights can sometimes be glimpsed.
37226: The sparkling canopy of blueish rock studded with diamonds simulating a starry night ends in a greyish rock that remarkably resembles a cloud blotting out the night. The road continues south though joining another smaller road.
37227: The road continues in a north south direction followed by the twinkling canopy above. The canopy appears to be a blueish rock with jools and diamonds imbedded in it. There is a large opening to the west where a door used to be. The door has been wrenched from its hinges and lies in several pieces to the right of the doorway.
37228:
A half-rotten corpse is hanging here.
A half-rotten corpse is hanging here.
A grey-skinned mountain troll stands here.
A grey-skinned mountain troll stands here.

A simple one room home like the ruins of the ones that pepper the road outside. This one seems to have escaped the destruction that befell the others. The house still has that lived in look as pieces of detritus and debris litter the area. Much of the east wall has been knocked out and the resulting rubble removed creating a serviceable doorway.
37229: A wide road which joins an intersection to the west. It runs straight for quite a while in both directions. A smaller road branches off to the south.
37230: This wide road is bordered to both sides by large structures, but every entrance has been blocked or totally destroyed. The remnants of these acts of destruction have left a fine film of dust everywhere, and small stones and debris litter the road, which continues to the east and west.
37231: A wide road running east west is cut by a small passage going north. To the south it broadens out into a small plaza. There is a very malodorous stench drifting in from the north.
37232: This rough tunnel seems to have been added on at a much later date than the tunnel to the south. The work looks to have been done by much rougher hands and accomplished with much less skill. The walls are quite rough and the footing can be quite tricky. It continues to the north and dumps onto a much more polished hallway to the south.
37233: This passage looks to be of much newer make than the one to the immediate north. The handiwork and craftsmanship is of a much lesser skill level. The walls are neither smooth nor particularly straight and sweep almost drunkenly to the south.
37234: This rather plain hallway continues to the west but slopes rather sharply upward. The hallway, while plain, brings out the natural grain of the rock. This explains the rather steep slope as a striation of the rock juts up at a steep descent.
37235: This rather plain hallway runs both east and west. The natural beauty of the rock has been brought out in the simple yet skilful craftsmanship of the tunnel, which has not a single corner or angle to be seen. All is elegantly curved, and finely polished.
37236: This small simple hallway spills out onto a large road to the west. There is little decoration or masonry evident. The natural lay of the rock seems to shine forth in the simplicity of the design.
37237: The road gives a very convincing illusion of being outside. The craftwork of the dwarves is never more evident than here. Through clever tricks of masonry, the roof soars, clothed in the blue of eternal night, lit by diamonds and blue gems which do a more than credible job of imitating the twinkling canopy of stars. A small hallway leads off to the east.
37238: The road leads out of the valley with the same name. The road is wide and paved offering easy travel. The road continues off to the south and bends to the east.
37239: A wide avenue opens up to the east and a small ramp slopes down to a lower level. Small shops and what looks like the fronts of houses line the avenue. Most of the entrances have been reduced to rubble or otherwise sealed off. The corridor is lit by a myriad of gems and jewels each catching and refracting whatever available light there is.
37240: The Avenue extends in both directions. The destruction on either side of the Avenue is almost complete. All doors and windows have been sealed or completely destroyed. Hundreds of gems embedded in the stone catch and refract any available light.
37241: The destruction in this part of the Avenue is almost complete. Several large blocks which made up a nearby wall of a house encroach upon the Avenue making travel tight in places.
37242: The destruction here looks different then other parts of the Avenue. The rock seems scored and gouged in countless places. Dark red and black marks litter the floor and walls. High above a mosaic sits in pristine preservation making a marked contrast to the rest of the room.
37243: The large hallway coming from the east ends in a set of stairs leading downwards. There is a large mosaic covering the whole ceiling above your head. It is comprised of hundreds of reflective pieces of glass. It seems to have survived largely intact. Probably due to the height of the ceiling.
37244: The road makes a straight path through to the east and west. Blacker holes to the west indicate some passages breaking off of the main road. The sound of water gurgling somewhere off in the distance breaks the silence.
37245: The road heads off to the west. The rough pavement of the road gives way to smoothly polished marble to the east as the road gives way to a large vaulted hall.
37246: The hall vaults up to a lofty one hundred foot height. There are thick black columns of polished marble which hold up quadripartite vaults. Each vault contains a bas-relief in dwarven history. Clever air holes add natural shadowing to the artwork.
37247: The ceiling swoops up to about one hundred feet and is supported by several massive pillars each about fifteen feet around. Several carvings still survive suspended about 75 feet up and filling the spaces between the pillars. The ceiling of the hall is decorated with frescoes and carvings which cunningly mask several airshafts.
37248: The Hall is quite impressive soaring to a height of about one hundred feet. Huge pillars ring the walls of the hall supporting the ceiling. Several cracks have developed under these pillars however and they form a fine patina of cracks that run from pillar to pillar. There is a small exit going north and a large fountain is directly south.
