37249: The hall comes to a corner here while extending to the south and west. Huge pillars about fifteen feet in diameter soar up a stunning one hundred feet to support the ceiling. Large tapestries have been hung strung between the pillars about seventy five feet up.
37250: The hall vaults up to a lofty one hundred foot height. There are thick black columns of polished marble which hold up quadripartite vaults. Each vault contains cleverly carved scenes of dwarven history. A wide set of stairs opens up to the east.
37251: Columns ring the entire hall. Huge black monoliths raising up and touching the ceiling. Blocks of quarts act like huge mirrors set in the ceiling magnifying the available light.
37252:
A lurg leader of the Uruk-moragog looks at you from a bloody helm (red aura).
An Uruk-moragog warrior glares around him, ready for enemies (red aura).
An Uruk-moragog warrior glares around him, ready for enemies (red aura).
An Uruk-moragog warrior glares around him, ready for enemies (red aura).

Columns of shiny black marble support the ceiling. You can see several airshafts arround the hall that allow the daylight to peek in and light the room. Blocks of quartz are used to reflect the light towards the centre of the hall. There is a large fountain in the middle of the hall, just north of here. A dark tunnel exits south.
37253: You are standing in the south western corner of the Hall of Lore. The ceiling is resting on huge pillars about a hundred feet above your head. Each and every sound is hurled back and forth between the walls and the ceiling, making a rumbling echo that reveals your position to everyone in your vicinity.
37254: A small white fountain is here.

In the middle of the hall there is a small pool providing Durin's Mansion with water from the Mirrormere. The water pours out from a tall statue in the middle of the pool. Both the fountain and the pool are cut right out of the mountain and, like the floor, no cracks can be seen. The water in the pool is filthy and looks rather disgusting, but the water coming from the fountain looks fresh.
37255: The walls of this avenue are covered in scribbling. Most of it has succumbed to the vagaries of time and chance. Some newer writing is evident and legible. A small stairway heads down. The avenue continues to the south while a large door occupies the east wall.
37256: A wide set of shallow steps greeted by a low slung handrail on either side. The handrail consists of small squat columns capped by a wide hand rail worn smooth by thousands of hands. The steps once were covered by a carpet, but all that is left is scraps of fabric and a slight indent in the centre of the stairs presumably where the bulk of traffic went.
37257: The road continues on drearily to the south but opens into a magnificent hall to the north. There is little adornment on the walls or ceiling and the road seems to have been designed for more practical uses.
37258: The road goes ever on to the north and south. It is wide enough for two carts to pass with some difficulty. The flagstones are in decent condition with just a few here and there cracked or missing. There is little adornment, just solid dwarven stonework.
37259: The road makes a turn to the north here. The outer portion of the wall makes a grand sweeping curve allowing easier travel for wide loads. The inner portion of the wall comes to a right angle.
37260: The walls of the road here are covered with a fine green moss. The walls are slightly damp but there is no available water. The moss only reaches down about half of the wall and the floor is completely free of it. The road continues to the east and west.
37261: The faint smell of woodsmoke drifts in from the west. The walls accompanying the road are bereft of any adornment. Looking in either direction the road continues almost unerringly straight.
37262: A small air vent blows a fresh breeze through the area. The air vent is high on the wall and covered with a thick iron grate. The air is much warmer and is tinged with a slight taint of wood smoke. The grate is the only blemish on an otherwise smooth wall. The road continues to the east and west.
37263: The soft drip of falling water can be heard falling somewhere off in the distance. The acoustics are tricky and it is tough to tell whence the sound came. The road continues to the east and west.
37264:
A lurg leader of the Uruk-moragog looks at you from a bloody helm.
An Uruk-moragog warrior glares around him, ready for enemies.
An Uruk-moragog warrior glares around him, ready for enemies.
An Uruk-moragog warrior glares around him, ready for enemies.
An Uruk-moragog warrior glares around him, ready for enemies.
An Uruk-moragog warrior glares around him, ready for enemies.

A large doorway breaks off from the road here. The doors are missing and the hinges are nothing more than twisted metal slowly rusting away. The road continues to the east and west oblivious to the flaw to the north.
37265: The tunnel stops its progress south and makes a sudden turn eastwards. The road was probably planned to go further south, but it looks like the dwarves hit harder rock and changed their minds. They left only a small alcove on the southern wall.
37266: The road widens a bit here as if indicating that this road was to become a major thouroughfare. However, it immediately narrows to the south as if the builders changed their mind.
37267: The road continues to the north and south. The walls are bare and bereft of any adornment. The hard rock has been polished smooth, not on purpose but by the passing of a multitude of hands.
37268: This is a small road that lies in disrepair. The gutters are choked with small stones and other debris which occasionally spill out onto the road proper, making footing treacherous in spots.
37269: A wide path that has been covered in cobblestones. The natural rock can be seen peeking up where the cobblestones have given way to decay or forcibly removed. The walls are smooth and straight, broken only by an alcove recessed straight into the rock every twenty feet or so. Most of the alcoves only hold the shattered remnants of once stood there, but occasionally a leg or a marble piece of a torso is still recognizable. In the centre is a statue of a dwarf, staring back almost disconsolately at the destruction that has occured around him.
37270: The wide cobblestone pavement shows signs of water wear here. The mortar holding the cobblestones together has turned a dark shade of green where the water has been allowed to linger. Alcoves spaced every twenty feet extend down the corridor on either side. Most seem to be empty or hold only the shattered remnants of some ancient sculpture or statue. White, presumably marble, collonades can be glimpsed extending to the south.
37271: Huge white marble pillars parade to the south. They contrast starkly with the dark polished marble of the wall itself. The columns abut the darker marble of the wall but are not a part of it. The columns parade to the south.
37272: The white marble columns end abruptly at an opening to the south. The darker marble, however continues its trek to the south and continues into the much larger room to the south. The white marble columns abut the darker marble of the walls but are set apart from it. The colonnade continues to the north.
37273: A crumbling fountain is in the middle of the place.

Exits appear in almost every direction. The archways all meld into one great pattern, twisting and convoluting uniting two great white arches to the south and west. The majority of the dome is made up of a dark purple marble with white striations forking through it. In spots, the marble still looks highly polished, but centuries of wear and tear have dulled most of its lustre.
37274: Rows of white columns pace this small pathway north to a larger domed area. The columns are of a stone other than marble and posess none of the flaws that marble has. The collonade continues to the south.
37275: The beautifully decorated ceiling is held up by numerous white pillars on each side of the street. It looks like this part of the mountain is a naturally white rock, but the dwarves have used rocks and gems from the mines to make the decorations above.
37276: This is a circle formed room with exits in two other directions. It is rather different from the rest of the area. The gold ore coming from the south meets the white quartz coming from the north. A pillar is standing just in the middle of the room, where the two types of rock meet. The gold ore and the pale white quartz are tangled together in a perfect spiral from the floor up to the ceiling.
37277: The walls still contain a fiery vein of gold mixed with quartz. The thread wends its way spiderlike through the granite. Whether the effect is in intentional or something prevented the dwarves from mining this vein is unclear.
37278: Occasionally, the vein of gold threads its way to the surface of the walls. Seeming to trace in a spidery hand magical runes which entice the beholder. The road continues to the north and east.
37279: The gold vein makes a turn to the south. The light catching the gold creating the image of fire alive in the walls. The tunnel widens a bit here as it makes the turn.
37280: The Road has been tunneled out from a Gold vein. The Dwarves have left some ore in the tunnel. The precious metal is shimmering in the walls, it actually looks like small pieces of light that just refuses to be swallowed by the overwhelming darkness that meets your eye everywhere.
37282: The walls of this small tunnel are covered in a dull black matte finish. The black coating extends to the north but curiously and abruptly ends as the road continues to the south.
37283: The road makes a gradual turn here. The outside wall of the tunnel bends gradually in a fluid motion while the inside wall turns at a right angle. This gives extra room for wide turns. The road continues to the south and east.
37284: The walls take on a dull black matte finish here. There is a slight sheen of dampness on the road as the temperature dips slightly as well. The blackness of the walls continues on to the west.
37285: The road splits into two smaller corridors. A slightly cooler draft wafts in from the west. The road looks decidedly darker to the west.
37286: A noticeable crack runs down one of the walls.
A very narrow passage has been cut to connect two larger roads. The passage is very rough and looks quite unfinished. The rough rock gives way to the smoother more finished rock to the east and west.
37292: A crumbling fountain is in the middle of the place.

This is a small room that ascends into a rotunda about thirty feet in height. The walls are of a dark marble. The rotunda is circular and looks as if it were placed on top of the four walls of the room. Hollowed out ceiling tiles etched into intricate patterns make up the bulk of the dome. A small oculus at the peak of the dome appears darker than the surrounding stone and looks like an air passage of some kind allowing smoke to escape. There is a staircase recessed into the west wall leading up and separate tunnels to the north and south.
37293: Several areas converge here. A wide cobblestone path treks off to the west, while the south opens up area reaching up to a large dome. There is also a steep incline going up. Occasionally shafts of light peek down from on high.
37294: The path continues east and west. Several of the cobblestones are missing making footing somewhat tricky. Alcoves set into the walls at even intervals extend in both directions. Most are empty, but a figure of a dwarf looms in one.
37295: A wide cobblestone path meanders east and west here. The shattered remnants of several statues are strewn about. Bits of stone bodyparts can be recognized, with the largest being a full half torso that seems almost alive as it rises out of the rubble.
37296: The cobblestone marking the path narrows a little here before widening out again to the east and west. There is the faintest trace of foetid water trickling in from the west. The alcoves pacing each side of the path are empty except for the buildup of a dark green mossy substance.
37297: The gallery continues in both directions paced by the alcoves on either side. This section seems to have avoided the water damage but not the smell. The rank smell of standing water wafts in from the west caressing the nostrils with the scent of foetid water.
37298: This simple passage connects two larger paths. The passage itself is completely bereft of adornment, consisting of two smooth walls.
37299: A wide road wrought with wondrous feats of masonry heads south. Intricate patterns of stone adorn the walls. The stonework is a weaving pattern, not unlike a painting. Time and damage has taken its toll however, and the story is tough to decipher. There is a sign carved in a strong dwarven hand. A small passageway heads off to the east.
37300: A half-rotten corpse is hanging here.

The road continues in both directions and intersects with an alley which branches off to the west. There are several indications that a large battle was fought here some time ago. Scratches on the wall, presumably by the victor, might have given some insight, but they have been smudged beyond recognition.
37301: A stone-grey troll advances toward you, with fury in its eyes.

A wide road built at the height of dwarven masonry. Intricate patterns of stone adorn both sides of the road. The stonework is a weaving pattern, not unlike a painting. The elements or something even more base has taken its toll in some parts.
37302: A set of runes carved in Khuzdul on the west wall proclaim this the Road of Narvi. The road is wide enough for four to walk abreast with no problem and continues to the north and south.
37303: The hall is square with a raised platform at the northern end, and the floor is covered with granite tiles. Many of the tiles are cracked after years of neglect, and all are dull and scuffed.
37304: This is the northwest corner of the hall. To the east is a raised platform. The floor is covered with granite tiles, some are cracked and pitted. In the highday of Moria this room was probably used as a gathering place for warriors.
37305: The hall is square with a raised platform in the northern end, the floor is covered with granite tiles, some of them cracked or stained with blood. This place was probably used by the dwarves as a place to gather before they went to war. Somehow the foul creatures that live in Khazad-dum seem to have adopted this habit, except they are not going anywhere.
37306:
A sturdy pack horse is standing here.
A stocky mountain mule is here, waiting to serve.
A sturdy pack horse is standing here.
A sturdy pack horse is standing here.
A sturdy pack horse is standing here.
A sturdy pack horse is standing here.
A sturdy pack horse is standing here.
A mountain troll, wielding a stone club, is sleeping here.
The hall is expanding to the north and the west. The outlines of a gate adorn the eastern wall. There are no signs of a door and it appears the gate is just that - an adornment.
37307:
A stone-grey troll advances toward you, with fury in its eyes.
A lurg leader of the Uruk-moragog looks at you from a bloody helm.
An Uruk-moragog warrior glares around him, ready for enemies.
An Uruk-moragog warrior glares around him, ready for enemies.
An Uruk-moragog warrior glares around him, ready for enemies.
An Uruk-moragog warrior glares around him, ready for enemies.
A great warg pads around, looking to rip something apart.
A large bat is here, hanging in the darkness.

The road ends abruptly here and enter a small circular area to the east. A tall spire of quartz and gold can be seen rising from the floor to the east. The flagstones of the road give way to a polished marble surface.
37308: A large boulder is here, it must be heavy.
The road bends to the east and north. The tunnel makes a slight dip but recovers. There is collected silt and sediment in the dip as water seems wont to collect there.
37309: A large greyish cloud fashioned from the natural grey rock of the ceiling to the north gives forth to a starry sky made up of a deep blue marble sprinkled liberally with twinkling gems which reflect the available light. The road continues to the south.
37310:
A rotten corpse is hanging here.
A huge stone troll looms overhead, ready to crush your body.
A large mean-looking troll is here.

This used to once be an inn, but now it is inhabited by something much larger than a dwarf. The room has been littered with large blocks of granite. The remains of several corpses are stacked in one of the corners. By the look of the twisted features and ugly snouts they seem to be orkish.
37311: A strong orc is sneaking around here, trying to hide.

This is a small room just off the inn's common room to the west. The thick layer of dust covering everything in the room is a good indication that whatever moved the large blocks of granite into the inn to the west doesn't come here.
37312:
A large boulder is here, it must be heavy.
A large boulder is here, it must be heavy.
A crumbling fountain is in the middle of the place.

A small plaza has been cut out of the mountain just south of Azaghal's Way. It was probably used as a place to rest on the long travel through the dark realm. A large tile is standing up against the southern wall.
37313: This a small alley which leads off of a large dome to the west. Fluted pilasters lead right into a ceiling carved with a complex net of interweaving branches. The overall look is stylized trees forming a canopy of leaves over your head.
37314: This small alley leads into a larger road to the east. Fluted pilasters lead upward to join a mesh of stylized interweaving branches which form the ceiling. The overall effect is a canopy of trees sloping to a point at the height of the ceiling. To the south between to pilasters is a large opening.
37315: This room was obviously not made by dwarves, but its rough-hewn walls appear to be fairly old. Dominating the room is a winch-like apparatus, which is ap- parently used to lift a large block of stone that is currently positioned on the western wall. On the eastern side of the room is a large pit, and the floor along the edge is scored with deep grooves. The entire floor near the pit is stained ruddy red, almost as if the impervious stone had somehow ab- sorbed a great quantity of blood. On the southern wall is a heavy door made entirely of black iron, and coated with a dark black substance that flakes to the touch.
37316: A blood-drenched commander of the Uruk-Moragog howls for your blood.

The walls and floor of this enclosed chamber are coated in a thick black substance that flakes in places revealing a lighter red colour beneath it. Several rings of metal absolutely caked in the black or red substance have been driven into the walls at varying heights. There are heavy reinforced doors to the north and east.
37317: A large, echoing tunnel slopes away to the east in an unwavering path, so straight that it can only have been the work of the dwarven master builders. The quality of the workmanship is evident in the smooth, squared sides of the passage, and the firm, even feel of the floor beneath your feet.
37318: Curious echoes reach you here from the long tunnel which disappears from view to the east, but otherwise the air is still and noiseless. As you look about you, it is possible to see that the original tunnel has been widened in more recent times, and small piles of rubble and debris still litter the floor by the western wall.
37319: This large unlit tunnel cuts an unwavering southern path from here, but ends abruptly to the north, as it enters a vast cavern. The heavy stone floor has been cracked and pitted with use, and is covered with fine gravel, but remains level and firm beneath your feet.
37320: Standing at the front of a large cave, you can see a few broken mine cars and heaps of slag, the only remaining signs of the long-abandoned activity which must once have filled this chamber. For this is a silver mine, forgotten since Durin's day. All of the smaller debris has been cleared away by the new occupants of this place, and a rough barricade of large loose stones has been erected in the middle of the cavern, restricting movement to the east to a difficult scramble. However, passages to the west and south of here appear to be easily accessible.
37321: A bulky cave troll is here, looking like a massive pile of stone.

Six massive cots line the walls of this smelly cave. Scattered about them are rinds and old bones, small chunks of rotting flesh, and huge wooden jugs filled with a foul liquid. An occasional notched club and broken shield add to the overall impression of clutter. A gargantuan door of solid iron dominates the south wall of the chamber, whilst the way west is partially blocked by a rough barrier of rocks and stones. It may be difficult to scramble back out in this direction.
37322: A large, dusty and featureless tunnel stretches here from east to west. The gravelly floor is dry and level, the walls cool and smooth. To the east, the tunnel opens out into a large cave.
37323: Though apparently used infrequently, this large tunnel must be visited at times by some large heavy biped, judging by the faint footprints you can see in the gravel and dust on the floor at your feet. The passageway travels from east to west, where it narrows markedly. To the south a rough-hewn entry lets onto a spacious room.
37324: A bulky cave troll is here, looking like a massive pile of stone.

Filth surrounds you in this squalid cave, and the air hangs heavy with the vile smell of putrefaction. Old bones and assorted junk litter the floor, and a pair of enormous cots stand against one wall. Against the opposite wall is an assembly of shelves and cabinets, too fine to be of trollish manufacture. But despite the signs of heavy wear on all of this furniture, now only a few large, ugly, wooden jugs and cups sit here.
37325: The floor beneath your feet is blanketed in a thick coating of pale grey dust, marking the passage of time since this thoroughfare was last used. From the fine workmanship, it is obvious that this tunnel was cut by Durin's folk in the ancient days, and it has probably not been used since they fled Khazad-dum. To the east, the passage opens out into a wider tunnel, whilst the way west is a slightly more confined passage.
37326: The musty air here feels thick with dust, but the passage in which you stand seems sound and well-constructed. The walls, ceiling and floor are smooth and featureless, and the tunnel cuts a bold east west path through the surrounding bedrock.
37327: Thick grey dust coats the floor of this tunnel. This thoroughfare has long been disused, but the old, fine workmanship of the ancient dwarves remains apparent in the smooth walls and squared dimensions. The passage continues east, but dead-ends to the west. However, a small opening in the southern wall leads to a natural rock grotto, beyond which can be seen a larger natural cavern. There seems to be a large, still body of water filling the cavern, and the surface of the water can just be seen from here.
37328: This small granite enclave lies to the north of a dismal lake, which stretches out across a mighty cavern, well beyond the reach of your feeble light. At the back of the enclave a barren tunnel opens to the north, before bending to the east, out of view. On the lake, twists of fog writhe above the surface of the water, while the sombre silence is disturbed only by an occasional faint gurgle, coming from somewhere in the distance.
37329: The gloomy waters of this cheerless lake have an unwholesome look about them. The air here is chilled and moistened by small wisps of fog, which rise from the surface of the stagnant water. The lake opens out in the vast natural cavern to the south and west, but ends abruptly where the cave wall comes down to meet the water to the east. To the north is a wide enclave in the rock, just above the water-line. To the rear of this chamber a rough tunnel opening can barely be glimpsed.
37330: Cool, clammy air surrounds you, making your clothes cling sodden and limp to your body, chilling you. Your light cannot penetrate far into the gloom, but you can see that the lake stretches beyond you to the north and west. The wall to the east of you is cold, smooth and beaded with moisture, and to the south, the lake is bordered by a sandy shoreline.
37331: By the Shore of a Dark Lake

To the north of this small sandy shoreline lies a vast dark underground lake. The air here is cool and moist, and beads of moisture festoon the cave walls to the south and west of you. To the east, a few feet above the shoreline, a large tunnel can be seen, and a small runnel of water trickles from the lip of the opening. All is still, but from the tunnel you can hear the dull echoes of heavy footfalls.
37332: The walls and ceiling of this passage are covered in moisture, which collects in small beads, and drips to the floor below. At your feet, small rivulets of water flow slowly to the west, where they trickle over the lip of an opening in the cave wall. The air here is moist and still, except for a faint warm breeze, which cuts across the tunnel from north to south.
37333: The walls here are mossy and damp, stretching far above your head as the stone stairwell corkscrews up away from you. Though the spiral is quite tight, the steps are broad and shallow, making this a safe and easy path to follow. A gentle breeze wafts past you as you stand here, whispering strange tales of what lies beyond you, to the north.
37334: Water drips from the ceiling all around you, falling into small puddles on the ground. Tiny rivulets of water channel down cracks in the mossy walls, and the air about you smells damp and stale. The passageway runs generally from east to west.
37335: Small puddles of water have collected on the gravelly floor, and are added to by the drip drip drip from the ceiling above your head. To the east this damp passage widens into the entrance to a massive cavern, and a reddish glow reaches you from there, casting strange shadows which seem to dance a macabre jig about you.
37336: There is a gentle, almost imperceptible slope here, with the northern end of this tunnel lying only a little lower than the south. However the stone floor is quite smooth, and has been made slick by moisture from the passageway to the south, so maintaining a footing is not easy.
37337: It is hard to see the ground in front of you, but you can vaguely discern that the tunnel here ascends to the south. Since it is quite smooth, it is at times a little difficult to maintain a steady footing, and the featureless walls to either side of you offer no hand-holds to assist you.
37338: The Great Hall of the Trolls

Far above you, you sense rather than see the ceiling of this massive natural cavern, which is hundreds of feet long and over a hundred feet wide. The far wall lies well beyond the reach of your light, but you get an idea of the huge dimensions, as you spy the torches mounted in brackets every few feet around the room. Though originally used by the dwarves of Durin's day, this hall is obviously now the home to a clan of cave trolls. The air is pervaded by the foetid odour of their food and faeces, both of which lie in heaps near the walls. Both of the long north-south walls of this great hall are punctuated by huge openings into large tunnels. Far away to the north, you can glimpse in the darkness a raised platform, shadowed in an eerie red light.
37339: Compared to the Great Hall, which lies to the west of here, this tunnel might appear cramped, but the ceiling is nonetheless far above your head. The eerie red-orange glow of a large fire barely penetrates this passage, but it is just possible to see that the workmanship here is rather crude, suggesting that the original fine tunnels contructed by the dwarves have since been enlarged by a rougher hand.
37340: A simple, but elegant archway opens onto a smaller tunnel to the east of here, whilst this passage continues to the north and south. The walls are slightly rough, and the floor is quite worn, as if by the trampling of many heavy feet. The ceiling above you is the only part of this passage which seems untouched by the marauding trolls, still retaining the original fine workmanship of the dwarves who crafted it so many years ago.
37341: Perhaps because of its smaller size, this tunnel seems to be one trodden only infrequently by the trolls, and the floor here shows little sign of wear. To the west, a simple but elegant archway opens out into a larger tunnel, and to the east the passageway curves north, out of view.
37342: With a graceful sweep, the passage here turns from west to north. No sharp corners mark this transition, but rather an almost imperceptible arc, whose definition is lost in the blanketing darkness just beyond the reach of your light.
37343: The fine workmanship of the dwarven craftsmen, who contructed this tunnel so many years ago, seems unmarked by the passage of time. The path here is bold and straight, the floor smooth and perfectly level, and above you the ceiling makes no dip or rise, but maintains a perfect parallel to the ground below.
37344: A gleaming throne, wrought from a single huge piece of obsidian, rests here upon a raised rock dais. Unearthly shadows dance around you, cast in the hellish red light of a massive pyre. Brighter than the torches mounted in brackets along the walls of this hall, the firelight reaches far above you, and yet still the roof of this cavern is more imagined than seen.
37345: The Great Hall of the Trolls

Here, at the southern end of the Great Hall, the lofty ceiling describes a massive downward arc, becoming the southern wall. This wall is broken by a single exit, framed to either side by massive stone pillars, carved more for effect than for structural support. Huge torches are mounted beside these pillars, and the light they cast flickers in the breeze from the corridor beyond. Rows of smaller torches are mounted on the walls throughout the hall, but their light falls away too rapidly for you to see much of this cavernous chamber in detail. This end of the hall seems little used, but from further north an unpleasant stench assails you.
37346:
A stone-grey troll advances toward you, with fury in its eyes.
A stone-grey troll advances toward you, with fury in its eyes.

Many feet have passed this way before yours, and the floor of this spacious tunnel has been worn smooth by heavy use. A huge stone slab to the west of you blocks a dark entryway, but to the east and south the tunnel branches into two similar echoing passageways.
37347: In a single sweeping arc, the passageway here switches from a north south direction to a curving eastward path. The floor beneath you is quite smooth and perfectly level, the air cool and still, and all about you the darkness reigns supreme.
37348: Smooth and flawless, the cold rock walls, ceiling and floor here bear no scars from the lengthy occupation of this part of Moria by hoards of barbaric trolls. The deep darkness has a strange air of tranquility, and even your soft foot- falls seem booming and graceless. Peering through the blackness, it is just possible to see that the path you tread stretches away from you to the north, and snakes around smooth curves to the west of here.
37349: Small, but well-proportioned, this dark tunnel shares the compelling quiet of the cavern beyond, to the north. But the smooth, flawless walls seem to speak volumes in their silent, ageless testimony to the immeasureable talent of the dwarven artisans, whose adroit hands long ago carved this thoroughfare from the living rock.
37350: A small pool of red-stained water lies here.

A slight putrescent smell diffuses through the air here. Almost lost in this cavernous tunnel, the stench grows a little stronger toward the south, where a rough aperture opens out into a large cave beyond. To the north, the tunnel follows a straight, and well-worn path.
37351: The air from the wide tunnel to the north seems fresh and wholesome compared to the stomach-churning reek here. Though your eyes are watering a little, it is still possible to make out that the ceiling of this cavern rises more than fifty feet above the ground. A faint bloody trail on the gravelly floor leads through a wide opening to the east, but the dark cleft in the southern rock- face could easily escape attention.
37352:
A half-rotten corpse is hanging here.
A stone-grey troll advances toward you, with fury in its eyes.
A stone-grey troll advances toward you, with fury in its eyes.

This smallish cave is clearly some sort of grisly larder. Bones are scattered across the floor, and the sickly-sweet odor of decaying flesh permeates the air. Your eyes are drawn to the disgusting array of corpses, hanging half- rotten from hooks along the north wall of this revolting room. It is no longer possible to guess the identities of these hapless victims to trollish gluttony, but it is clear that not all of these carcasses are animal in origin.
37353: A faint pungent smell wafts toward you here from the east, but this tunnel is otherwise unremarkable. Though the walls and high ceiling are fairly rough, the floor has been worn into a smooth rut from the frequent passage of heavy feet along a never-changing east west pathway.
37354: Several things about this spot attract your attention, not least of all the hot acrid air, which drifts from the chamber to the east. An aura of corruption seems to assault you as you contemplate the ornate opening in the north wall of this passageway, and crude silvered letters can be seen, sparkling on the twin columns of this entrance.
37355: You are teetering on the very rim of a large pit, where the trolls toss the remains of their dead after burning them. Warm upcurrents of air from the chasm carry small particles of ash, which seem to cling all over you, making your nose run and your eyes sting. But that is not all: a strange sinister presence seems to rise from the depths of the crater, enshrouding the whole chamber in gloom.
37356: It is obvious that this room was originally constructed by the dwarves, as the high walls and curved ceiling are smooth and finished, and the hexagonal floor is covered by an intricate pattern of black and scarlet stone tiles. However crude alcoves have been clumsily chiselled into the otherwise featureless walls, and in each of these can be seen a grotesque stone sculpture, depicting some hideous act performed by the trolls throughout the ages, in the name of their dark master. To the north, an elegant archway leads to the sanctuary and altar.
37357: An ancient black altar stands in the centre of the room.

You stand at the altar to the Dark Lord. A miasma of evil fills this place, making even the stout-hearted feel faint. The altar itself is a huge silver cauldron on a raised stone platform. It is in this that the trolls boil alive their sacrifices, sometimes animal, but sometimes an unfortunate prisoner. In an alcove set into the north wall, the skulls and broken helms of famous western heroes are proudly displayed as a token to previous victories.
37358: Your footsteps echo back at you in this dead-end tunnel, but otherwise a deathly hush seems to fill the air. The floor here is less worn than in the main passageways behind you, but it seems that this is no disused walkway, and to the east a well-crafted, heavy stonedoor seems to invite exploration.
37359: Rectangular in shape, and well-crafted, this is the private chamber of Bulag, High Priest of the Temple to Sauron. The floor and walls here are of highly polished stone, and at the centre of the room stands an imposing stone table. Many tokens of high status amongst the trolls are scattered on the table, and also in heavy wooden chests, which line one wall. At the eastern end of this cave a small curtained alcove houses Bulag's bed.
37360:
A musty loaf of bread has been left here.
A weary slave who has lost all hope sits here staring into space.

Anguish seems to become incarnate in this room, which is filled by the ragged husks of slaves, whose spirits long ago left their miserable bodies. The air reeks of death and decay, the floor is caked with blood, and small insects scurry hither and thither, infesting all who enter this dark and squalid place.
37361:
A few gold coins lie on the ground.
A delicate indigo crystal lies here.
A fire opal catches the light.
A few gold coins lie on the ground.
A wooden chest stands in the corner.
A grey spider is stalking here, preparing to drain you of life.

You have found the secret treasure chamber of the trolls. No petty hoardings clutter this room; instead small heaps of coins, gems and valuables are housed in a number of sturdy wooden chests which line one wall. Here is kept the best of the plunder, which the pillaging trolls have collected over many long years of fighting and raiding.
37362: At the north-western border of this large underground lake the darkness seems quite impenetrable. Your faint light barely illuminates the whispy tendrils of fog, which curl up above the dark, still surface of the water around you. All is silent save for an occasional plop or gurgle, emanating from somewhere far out in the lake beyond you. To the north and west the rock walls of this cavern loom above you, offering no exit. You must instead cross the gloomy waters of the lake to the south or east.
37363: You are on the dark still surface of a large underground lake. Tufts of fog curl about the surface in the beam of your light, while every now and again a faint plop or gurgle can be heard somewhere out in the waters; otherwise all remains quiet. You can continue across the lake to the north and east; to the west is a small pebbly beach, beyond which can be seen a passage of some kind.
37364: Here a long pebbly beach defines the western end of a vast underground lake. Ethereal wisps of moisture curl up from the dark, still surface of the water, which lies undisturbed, save for a few tiny ripples, accompanied by a gurgle or plopping sound, heard far out in the lake; otherwise all is quiet in this huge natural cavern. Behind you a passage ascends rapidly to the west, and from that direction a faint cool breeze is blowing.
37365: A chilling current of air wafts past you from above, where this passage climbs away to the north. The gravelly floor falls away to the east, where the tunnel opens out into a vast natural cavern. In the distance you hear the faint sound of dripping water.
37366: The floor in this small passage descends rapidly southward, and rises sharply to the west of you. Though steep, the ground is fairly rough and dry, making it quite easy to keep your footing. A cold breeze blows down from the passage above.
37367: Descending rapidly from west to east, the floor of this steep passage is fairly rough, but a little moist, making it difficult to avoid slipping and falling. A faint but frigid draught assails you from the passage to the west.
37368: This small room glistens white with ice wherever you look. A profusion of icicles hang from the ceiling, and treacherous sheets of ice carpet the floor. Small icy curtains conceal the walls, resembling petrified waterfalls. A faint, yet freezing, airflow is coming from somewhere in the northern wall, but the only obvious exit is to the east, down a steep passage.
37369: An ancient dwarven skeleton lies upon the floor.

The floor and walls of this narrow corridor are smooth and slick with ice. A frigid wind blows steadily from the west, dancing between the forest of spear- like icicles which cover the ceiling, and seeming to penetrate through your garments. A faint hissing noise can be heard from somewhere in the south wall of this passage, which seems to end abruptly here.
37370: A freezing wind whips into this chamber from the north, and whistles past you eastward into a narrow corridor. This freezing-cold cavern is bare and quite featureless, just a small room neatly chiselled from the surrounding granite. A small patch of sky can barely be seen through the exit to the north, which must lead outside the mountain, and just beyond the opening you can see a narrow ledge, where one might perhaps stand.
37371: This narrow ledge has neither parapet nor rail, typical of dwarven design. A fierce blast of icy wind rolls past you, down the mountainside, as you gaze out at the immense spectacle of the valley of Hollin, which lies several thousand feet below, stretching away into a misty haze. To either side, and above you, are the sheer sides of the Misty Mountains, too steep to be scaled here. The only possible exit from this place is to turn into the forbidding darkness of Moria, to the south.
37372: The stairway stretches beyond you in both directions. To the east it begins a tight downward spiral, whilst to the west it follows a less winding path. Each tread of the stair has been carved with infinite care, and shows little sign of wear. However, here and there a small crack or chip can be seen, as if some noisome beast has attempted to destroy the fine workmanship.
37373: As straight as an arrow, the broad staircase climbs away from you to the north. To the east it descends, tracing a more twisted path, and narrowing markedly. The ascent is not a great one, with each individual step being quite shallow, making this an easy way for dwarf and giant alike.
37374: To north and south, the stairway seems to stretch endlessly, its undeviating path becoming monotonous to follow. Each broad step of the stair seems like the last, crafted to an exacting standard; this could only be the work of Durin's folk.
37375: A long, straight stairway stretches before you to the south. Though there is no handrail, the way looks quite safe. Each broad, shallow step has been carved precisely, so that all are identical, and the smooth surface of the stone is quite dry. No crack or chip can be seen, which might cause an unwary traveller to lose his footing.
37376: Sloping downward from east to west, this tunnel follows a sinuous path, which seems to twist and writhe through the solid rock. Small glistening beads of water draw your eyes to the wall, as they slowly from into tiny streams which run down to the floor and away from you into a small hollow west of here. To the south, an unadorned archway leads to a long stairwell.
37377: In an abrupt turn, the tunnel swings north and east, climbing away from you in both directions. Water has collected in this small hollow, but seems to be seeping slowly through narrow cracks in the floor. Though it looks fairly deep, it appears to be possible to wade through it, to reach the tunnel beyond.
37378:
A small and particularly ugly orc steps out of the shadows.
A stone-grey troll advances toward you, with fury in its eyes.
A stone-grey troll advances toward you, with fury in its eyes.

Treading such a convoluted path is becoming quite dizzying. As the tunnel weaves its way through the cold, dark rock, it also climbs and falls, as if unable to find the right course. Only a sharp eye would notice the quartz intrusion, which traces a delicate vein through the granite walls. Perhaps it was this which the dwarven miners were following, in search of deposits of emeralds, pink morganite, and aquamarine.
37379: The tortuous route of this tunnel now takes you north or west. Small flecks of bright shiny quartz twinkle out from the smooth rock walls, but clearly this passageway offered no promise of a great wealth of minerals or ore, and so the dwarven miners pressed on in their search, so many years ago.
37380: Though the tunnel is still quite flexuous, here the turns are shorter, and frequently switch direction, so that it is possible to see for quite a long distance, both north and south, despite the twists and turns. Here too, the floor begins to undulate gently, rising and falling every fifty or sixty feet along the tunnel.
37381: The tunnel sweeps south and east from here, following a seemingly aimless course in its progress through the mountain. But though its path seems a random one, this passage is nevertheless well-wrought, with neatly squared walls, and a fine, level floor.
37382: A simple squared opening to the north marks the end of a long snaking tunnel, which meanders off to the west of here, and disappears from view. The hand which chiselled this place was a skilled one, for the walls are well-crafted, but this passage was never intended to a part of the living chambers of the dwarves; rather, it seems to be an exploratory tunnel, hewn from the rock in search of new ore.
37383: Carved with inexorable patience and care, this chamber still retains the same inherent strength its builders intended, before their flight from Moria. But its nature has twisted, with a more malevolent and constricting atmosphere, which steals the courage from your soul.
37384:
A huge stone troll looms overhead, ready to crush your body.
A huge stone troll looms overhead, ready to crush your body.

As the floor dips and rises with each step you take, it is rather difficult to proceed here. Trying to steady yourself by reaching out to the wall would be a big mistake though, as its surface is quite rough and unfinished, with large outcroppings of rock, which tear at your clothes as you pass.
37385: Rubble and debris are scattered about the floor, as if this tunnel had only recently been chipped out of the rock. Somehow, the ceiling above you seems less solid than in the other tunnels, and a small dustfall occurs even as you stand here.
37386: A jagged hole in the rockface to the east opens out into a large cavern. To the west, this rugged passageway continues, its floor undulating in a hap- hazard fashion. The roof above your head rises and falls to a rhythm of its own, making this tunnel at times soaring, at times cramped and claustrophobic.
37387: Dried blood and excrement mingle with the dirt and gravel on the floor of this large natural cavern. Massive stone benches have been set around the walls to all sides, and at the north-eastern corner of the cavern stand a few stout pikes, atop each of which rests a severed head. This cave must serve as a meeting place and arena for the trolls, and it can only be imagined how many poor beasts have perished here, or how many weary travellers.
37388: The stench here is appalling. This wide, sloping tunnel has been forced into service as a storeroom for a hoard of rotting corpses and detached body parts. Blood oozes from one still warm body, and seeps through the gravel, tracing a downward path to the north. Another cadaver seems alive with a quivering mass of maggots.
37389: All is quiet and still in this dark passageway. The smooth floor beneath your feet slopes gently away to the north, where the tunnel ends in a simple, yet exquisite archway. To the south, the ground becomes a little less even, and a little more gravelly, but what you notice most is the pungent odour which drifts to you from that direction.
37390: The Top of a Treacherous Stair

The faint, distant thundering of water can be heard here, as you stand at the the top of a long winding staircase. It is impossible to see how far below you the stairs continue, and it is quite tempting to reach for one of the loose stones which are scattered around, and drop it to plumb these depths. It seems impossible to fight off a wave of vertigo when contemplating this drop, especially considering that there is no handrail here, and that each tread of the stair is perilously worn and chipped with use.
37391: The bright array of colours shining into this tunnel from the chamber to the north barely break the gloom. Yet somehow your light seems brighter and stronger when you look to the north, compared to when you turn and gaze up this narrow tunnel to the south.
37392: The tunnel here describes a ninety degree turn, climbing away from you to the west, falling off gently to the north. The walls, ceiling and floor here are quite smooth, but as the slope is so gentle you have little trouble with your footing, despite the engulfing darkness.
37393: The air here is still, almost stagnant, and no sound is to be heard. Peering into the darkness, it is possible to see that the tunnel here is somewhat steeper than it was up to this point, falling away quite markedly to the east of you. This passage seems to continue only a short way in either direction, making unanticipated turns to both the east and the west of where you stand.
37394: Abruptly, the passageway turns here, leading upward to the south, and down from here to the east. The floor is smooth, but quite dry, so the gentle gradient offers no difficulty. However, in the all-engulfing inky darkness of this tunnel it is impossible to see far in either direction.
37395: A wide stone staircase leads down from here, spiralling into the darkness. Each stair is badly chipped and worn, with flaked edges, and uneven hollows toward the centre, and part way down, a huge block of masonry obstructs the way.
37396: A cool breeze wafts out of the still darkness within, carrying a blend of unfamiliar scents and an aura of great age. Somehow, this place feels evil, belonging to a different time, perhaps, and only with a certain degree of trepidation would anyone continue to follow this path between the dark, stone walls.
37397: The slate-surfaced road continues to wind upward to the east, and downward to the west, in long, regular curves. There are no side passages to distract the traveller, and the road has not been marred or cracked by tremors as some other roads have - in this vicinity, at least.
37398: The road winds on through the stone in long curves - a long sweep to the north, a broad curve, a long sweep to the south again. It ascends continuously to the east; to the west each curve is lower than the last. The walls and ceiling are faced with white marble, once inlaid with runes of some more precious stone. The filling is gone and the runes chipped and defaced, but it seems that you can recognise the name of that great Dwarven king of legend, Azaghal.
37399: This road ascends into the heart of ruined Khazad-dum in a series of long, goosenecked curves, first north, then south, but each curve higher and further east than the one before. The slate surface is smooth and easy to travel on. The walls are faced with a brighter and finer grade of stone than in the tunnels below.
37400: Broad and straight, with a high ceiling, and smooth walls of cold, dark stone, this roadway runs away from you, to the west, rising sharply as it does so. To the north, it joins the much grander thoroughfare, known in ancient times as Azaghal's Way.
37401: The roadway ends abruptly here, as if its purpose had somehow been forgotten. The cold, dark, granite walls are beaded with condensation, but otherwise seem quite featureless, and there is no indication as to why this passageway was constructed.
37402: This narrow passage slopes steadily upward, twisting and turning as it does so. A cool breeze drifts down to you from above, chilling the air where you stand, and whispering of the possibilty of an exit from the tunnels and caverns. The wall to the east of you seems a little different to those north and south, and a thin film of moisture beads its cool, smooth surface.
37403:
A sturdy peg for hanging armour from is on the wall.
A weapons rack stands against the wall.
A great, black warg pads around, looking to rip something apart.
A great, black warg pads around, looking to rip something apart.
An orc of the Uruk-moragog stands in the gloom.
An orc of the Uruk-moragog stands in the gloom.
An orc of the Uruk-moragog stands in the gloom.
An Uruk-moragog warrior glares around him, ready for enemies.

Perched high on the side of the mountain is a hidden outpost, once used by the dwarves to keep watch on the surrounding lands in relative secrecy. Far below, the raging waters of the Cirith Caradhras flow in a fierce torrent through the valley. To the north, and far distant, the pathway to the Redhorn Gate can barely be spied, nestled among the same mighty glaciers, which cover the mountainside around you.
37404: The roadway is jagged and pebbled, making it a treacherous path to follow. Deep depressions in the rocky walls enhance the shadowy feeling of this place, and send echoes, which bounce and reverberate around you, as if playfully taunting you. A tiny trickle of water creeps southward across the sloping floor.
37405: There is a silence here, profound and forboding, the crouched hush of a predator at work. The only sound, and the only reminder to travellers that they have not lost their sense of hearing altogether, is a distant, and echoing drip of water, which beats like the heart of some ancient, resting beast. The water slips through the silent, watchful stone, to join deep, dark pools, whose distant location can only be guessed at. Huge, tapering stalactites mark each entrance to the cavern, bearing silent witness to the ageless fall of mineral-rich water in this chamber.
37406: Where once the echo of many footfalls resounded, now only the sound of dripping water disturbs the sullen silence. The sloped floor of this road is criss- crossed by a network of fine cracks, and it is through these that most of the water escapes, to the unseen depths, below. The water which somehow remains, follows the westward descent of the roadway.
37407:
A strange bat-like creature is flitting around.
A strange bat-like creature is flitting around.
A strange bat-like creature is flitting around.
A strange bat-like creature is flitting around.
A strange bat-like creature is flitting around.
A strange bat-like creature is flitting around.
A strange bat-like creature is flitting around.

The high, domed ceiling of this chamber is a wonder to behold. Millions of tiny crystals of quartz are embedded in the grey-black granite of the roof, where they glitter, and twinkle, likes stars in a cloudless sky. Perhaps it was Varda herself, the greatest and most beautiful among the queens of the Valar, who wrought this delightful illusion.
37408: Large, shattered blocks of masonry lie discarded to either side of the road, and smaller pieces of debris clutter the entire area, though the origin of this material is far from obvious. The floor, walls and ceiling of this passage are so smooth and straight, that it is clear they were carved by the dwarves of ancient Khazad-dum, whose pride in their work would never have allowed them to leave such a fine roadway strewn with rubble.
37409:
An orkish warrior of the Durghash is here, with a cruel glint in his eye.
An orc, of the Durghash tribe, crouches here.
An orc, of the Durghash tribe, crouches here.
An orc, of the Durghash tribe, crouches here.

No sound intrudes to break the stillness here, save for the repeating echo of your own footfalls. In the impenetrable gloom of Moria, this cold, dark roadway makes its way onward, descending gently, but perceptibly, to the north.
37410: Four columns, cunningly crafted to resemble large oak trees, support the roof of this magnificent chamber. The walls are decorated with a delicate design, made up of tiny tiles of pale, rose quartz, dark green malachite, and highly polished, black obsidian. Here, the wide, dark roadway, from Azaghal's Way, above, intersects with the more opulent Avenue of Gold.
37411: An eyeless white rat with nasty teeth scurries about.

Smooth, straight walls, a level, flat floor, and an arched roof mark this broad passageway as the work of the dwarves, and not of Moria's current barbaric inhabitants. The granite walls are perfectly featureless, save for a delicate inlay of gold, of such craftsmanship that it defied the plundering hoards of orcs and trolls, remaining intact through the long years of their occupation of these halls and caverns.
37412: Two delicate parallel lines of inlaid gold run the length of each wall of this wide passage, but the grey granite is otherwise featureless, and is perfectly smooth. A small arch in the northern wall, undecorated, as if to avoid any attention, opens into a modest chamber, whilst to the east, a larger hall can be seen.
37413:
An eyeless white rat with nasty teeth scurries about.
An eyeless white rat with nasty teeth scurries about.
An eyeless white rat with nasty teeth scurries about.
An eyeless white rat with nasty teeth scurries about.
An eyeless white rat with nasty teeth scurries about.

The Avenue of Gold comes to an end here, in this gracefully arched chamber, which was perhaps built to offer a resting place for those travellers wearied by their journey along Azaghal's Way, above. The arches and pillars divide the room into a number of smaller cubicles, which would have afforded some degree of silence and solitude.
37414: A weapons rack stands against the wall.

This small chamber perhaps once served as a resting hall for weary dwarven miners. Small niches, cut into the west wall, hold what appear to be the shattered and rotten remains of tables and chairs, whilst at the centre of the room, stands what can only have been a stone well. Now, however, its walls have been torn asunder, large blocks of stone obstruct the wide, round opening, and instead of fresh water, only dust and rubble can be seen below. Where once Durin's folk relaxed after their labours, now a tribe of orcs has set up a guard post.
37415:
An orkish warrior of the Durghash is here, with a cruel glint in his eye.
An orkish warrior of the Durghash is here, with a cruel glint in his eye.

No vast hoard of gems lies here, but the walls still twinkle with tiny flecks of blue aquamarine, and bright green emerald. Too dispersed among the granite to be worth mining, these tiny deposits have instead been polished within their dull, grey setting, to produce a passageway of startling beauty.
37416: The slightest sound comes rumbling back from the caverns to the west, in a cacophony of repeating echoes. The riches of those caves are scarcely hinted at by the delicate sprinkling of beryl in the walls here, yet still they sparkle and glitter, with a promise of what lies beyond.
37417: Networks of stone walkways criss-cross this vast cavern, which rears high above you, and reaches into the darkness below. The walls are uneven and ragged, marked still by the scores and narrow gouged clefts, left there, so long ago, by the dwarven miners.
37418: A rusty pickaxe with a broken handle lies discarded here.

Narrow walkways track from pillar to slender pillar across the cavern, linking the many workings of the mine. In ancient days, this must have been the site of great activity, as the dwarves delved diligently into the rock, but today all is still and silent, lending an air of forboding to the place.
37419: A large pile of boulders is sitting here, probably debris from a rockslide.

Jagged nooks and crannies punctuate the rockface of this massive cavern. Many stretch deep enough into the walls to be small tunnels, but it appears that most dead-end after only a short distance, for these are no passageways, but the ancient diggings of this huge mine complex.
37420:
An orkish warrior of the Durghash is here, with a cruel glint in his eye.
An orkish warrior of the Durghash is here, with a cruel glint in his eye.
An orc, of the Durghash tribe, crouches here.
An orc, of the Durghash tribe, crouches here.
An orc, of the Durghash tribe, crouches here.

Perhaps this was originally just another small tunnel, tracing a precious vein of beryl deep into the rockface, but at some time, it was enlarged into a small chamber. Dwarven runes, carved into the south wall, above a small, arched exit suggest that this place was hewn by Durin's people, but the function of this chamber is not readily apparent.
37421: Rough stairs, and narrow walkways once connected the various levels of workings in this mine, but most of these now lie in disrepair, long since rendered impassable by both the ravages of time, and the wanton destruction of the orcs and trolls, who have made Moria their home. Now only one narrow pathway spans the levels here, twisting and turning, with numerous tight switch-backs, into the darkness below.
37422: This narrow passageway links the small room north of here to a larger chamber, which can be seen beyond a sturdy iron portcullis, to the south. Judging by the smooth, straight walls and the low, level ceiling above, this corridor was crafted by the dwarves. And yet, strangely, small scores can be seen in the hard granite floor. Perhaps they were left there by whoever assailed the grating to the south, whose cunning manufacture has defied any attempts at opening it, and whose strength has obviously withstood massive abuse.
37423: The walls of this passageway sparkle with mystery, hinting at a history long- forgotten by all but the dwarves, who once delved deep in Khazad-dum. Only on true riches did they expend their labour, and so this place still glitters with tiny deposits of emerald, embedded firmly in the dull, grey granite.
37424: The broad passageway sweeps to the south here, in a graceful curve. No jagged edges mar the walls and floor, and the ceiling, above, is smooth and level. Every detail of this thoroughfare lends credence to the tales, so often told, of the vast skill of the dwarves in the working of stone.
37425: An eyeless white rat with nasty teeth scurries about.

Never does the warmth of the sun reach this cold, stone avenue, nor does the pale light of the moon ever soften the darkness. Here, hapless surface- dwellers stumble, disoriented by the endless gloom. And yet, even this place has a certain beauty: embedded throughout the dull, grey granite of the walls are innumerable small deposits of sparkling green beryl.
37426: At the sound of approaching footfalls, dozens of small creatures scuttle away, unseen, retreating into the many clefts and fissures in the walls of this passageway. The floor here is cracked and pitted, with numerous small rocks scattered about, and even the ceiling seems somewhat precarious.
37427: The Emerald Way widens out here, into a broad chamber, with a high, domed ceiling. A massive, natural rift cleaves the roof in the northern part of the chamber, but the wide stone stairway which spirals up toward this fault is obstructed by a huge block of masonry, which impedes progress to the level above.
37428: This tiny passageway is in stark contrast with the grand hallway to the south. Its ceiling, though neatly arched, hangs low, compared to the lofty Emerald Way, and its walls stand only one short pace apart from each-other. Clearly, this route was intended to be one of the dwarves' more private accessways, in the ancient days of Khazad-dum.
37429: An eyeless white rat with nasty teeth scurries about.

No mark of hammer, chisel or pick is left to mar the flawless surfaces of the walls here, and the arched roof curves smoothly above. Even the floor bears no blemish. It would almost seem that this tunnel were the work of Aule himself, so skilfully was it wrought by his people.
37430: A vaulted ceiling hangs low in this small, meandering passageway, and the cold, dark, granite walls stand close together, creating rather a claustrophobic feeling, which is enhanced by the stagnancy of the air, and the impenetrable gloom.
37431: Narrow, but well-wrought, this passage was clearly hewn from the stone of the mountain, by the dwarves, for their own exclusive use. The tunnel is narrow, but its walls are smooth, and the floor level. The ceiling, which is quite low, describes a graceful arch above your head.
37432: The stair climbs high above, and plunges downward into the unseen depths below. The rumble of fast-flowing water can be heard quite clearly, and a faint mist rises, to refresh the stale air which fills this passageway. The cold, dark, stone walls are beaded with moisture, which seeks out every tiny flaw and crevice, and each tread of the spiralling staircase is covered by a sheen of water, with tiny pools collecting in any indentation.
37433: A brooding wickedness hangs in the air here, as tangible as the mist which hugs the cold stone. Water falls harmlessly to the floor, adding to the small, dark pools, cradled within the rough stone, which occasionally spill over, to send tiny streams trickling down the passageway.
37434: Cracks and crevices mark the walls. Bas-reliefs have worn away, the lines of an artist's chisel filled in by the dust of centuries, the fine detail of Dwarven craft replaced by the artwork of spider webs. As the passage twists to the south, one wall falls away, leaving a gaping precipice to one side of the path, and from somewhere far below, the sound of water rumbling through the mountain echoes up toward you.
37435: Though this roadway is flanked by no wall except to the north, the cold, dark air somehow seems to close in on all sides. The sense of a chill and evil presence fills this place, as if this once proud thoroughfare were now plotting to trick the unwary traveller, who, in that instant of distraction, would plunge over the edge of the yawning chasm to the south. From somewhere far below, the distant rumble of water can faintly be heard.
37436: In the deep, impenetrable darkness, it is hard even to sense where the floor will be, with each new step. But it rises steadily from east to west, as the road plunges on, hugging the wall to the north, as if it were afraid of the deep rift to the south.
37437: The roadway continues its journey through the mountain, faithfully following an ascending path to the west. It is hard to imagine how the dwarven builders of old managed to construct this traverse, which almost seems to defy gravity, as it clings to the northern rock wall of this massive cavern.
37438: To the west, the traverse hugs the cavern wall, as if afraid of what lies beyond. To the south and east, however, it strides boldly out into the centre of the cold, dark chamber, fearlessly crossing the void.
37439: The traverse here seems to search keenly for the reassurance of the cavern wall to the north. As if seeking to avoid the dark, deadly chasm south, it turns sharply, but remains broad and strong.
37440: The air is still and silent. Above, and to either side, a deep darkness seems to smother all it touches, and even the stone traverse appears to be enveloped in the gloom, making it difficult to tread with any confidence. But although there is no handrail on this stone bridge, the path is quite broad, and would seem to be safe.
37441: A seemingly bottomless chasm looms to the north and south of this broad stone bridge. The absence of a handrail might seem disconcerting to some, but the roadway was well-crafted, and is easy to follow. It would seem that there is little risk, as long as the traveller remains towards the centre of the road.
37442: A broad stone bridge crosses a vast, seemingly bottomless chasm. There is no rail on either side, but the level floor is easy to cross, with no pits or protrusions to cheat a weary and footsore traveller. To the north, however, a wide passage opens out into a large chamber.
37443: You are standing on the edge of an extremely long and large spiral staircase, which leads to long-forgotten halls above and below you. Here the worn, grey steps, that once saw the daily passage of hundreds of Dwarves, reach a landing; to the west, behind a large arch carved in the hard stone, lies a long corridor.
37444: Perhaps, in their destructive frenzy, Sauron's foul followers ran straight past the statue, which stands in the nearest alcove, for somehow it remains almost completely intact. This large, and finely-wrought work of art is obviously a representation of Aule, himself.
37445:
An orkish warrior of the Durghash is here, with a cruel glint in his eye.
An orc, of the Durghash tribe, crouches here.
An orc, of the Durghash tribe, crouches here.
An orc, of the Durghash tribe, crouches here.
A great wolf with a sable coat glares around with red eyes.

The distant sound of dripping water echoes from the west, but no other sounds intrude upon the stillness of this long passageway, which stretches east, into the darkness. Large alcoves have been cut, every few paces, into the southern wall, but most of these now stand empty, except for a little dust and debris.
37446: A series of massive, arched, stone bridges once supported wide roadways, which spanned this lofty cavern. However, most of these are now little more than crumbling ruins, and the broad path, upon which you stand, comes to an abrupt end, just to the west. The only way to traverse the chasm ahead is by way of a network of smaller, and apparently less secure, cat-walks.
37447: This narrow and chipped stone cat-walk seems precarious indeed. Even the dwarves seem to have needed some reassurance as they trod this path, since a series of wooden posts line the route, and suspended between these, by means of stout metal hoops, is a thick, rusty chain. Far below, the floor of the chamber is filled by an uninviting pool, made red-brown by ancient deposits of iron.
37448: The cat-walk terminates abruptly here, in a crumbling and treacherous mass of stone. Twenty feet away it resumes its course, but between here and there, a gaping chasm blocks the way. The heavy iron chain, which forms the handrail here, is rusted and clearly weakened with age, perhaps to the point of being useless. It would seem that the danger of falling into the stagnant red-brown pool, below, is very real indeed.
37449: A dreary red-brown pool is cradled in the rock of the cavern floor, far below this narrow cat-walk. Chips and flakes of stone lie scattered about, in a silent testimony to the age and fragility of the path, and the old, rusty chain, which forms a handrail, seems to offer little guarantee of safety.
37450: Ornate pillars line the sides of this major road, evenly spaced along both walls. Interspersed between the pillars are small alcoves that probably once housed statues of honoured dwarves, but scattered alabaster fragments are all that remain -- an unfit epitaph for these revered ancestors.
37451: The wide road opens into a magnificent chamber before continuing on the other side. The hemispherical ceiling is ablaze with bright coloured tiles, set in an intricate mosaic pattern depicting a Dwarven rout of orcs in some battle of the distant past. Hanging from the centre of the dome overhead is a large globe of crystal -- still seeming to gleam palely, though whatever light it may have once held has been long ago extinguished.
37452: This great shaft once marked the informal boundary between the Dwarven city to the east and the mines to the west. In the centre of the chimney lies a masterpiece of dwarven craftsmanship -- a slender tower that is reputed to stretch from the roots of the mountain to Durin's Tower at the very peak of Zirakzigil. A great winding stairway once encircled the tower, and a multitude of catwalks and bridges would allow one access to any of the various levels of Khazad-dum. Most of this was destroyed shortly after Durin's Bane awoke, for the earth was troubled and great tremors caused many of the bridges to fall away into the inky depths. The bridge here still stands, and to the east it is possible to proceed past the central tower and on into the city area.
37453: Mahal's Way leaves the Dwarven city to the east and arches in a great stone bridge across Durin's Chimney on its way to the mines and the western area of Moria. Extending from the lowest dungeons delved by the dwarves to the peak of Zirakzigil, the pinnacle of the Silvertine, this chimney sheathes a central tower built by the Khazad to provide access to all the levels of Moria. The tower still stands, although most of the intricate network of catwalks and bridges that connected it to tunnels on either side of the chasm fell prey to the frequent spasms that shook the mountain in the time when Durin's Bane first awoke.
37454: Durin's Chimney lies to the west, spanned by a large bridge. Large carved columns of glossy black rock line the walls of this large road -- occasionally connected by huge arches spanning the passage, from whence hang remnants of the magnificent lanterns that once enlightened this black domain.
37455: The broad expanse of Mahal's Way leads into a major intersection to the east. This area has been the site of recent fighting among the tribes of orcs, as there are several bodies bearing the markings of two distinct tribes scattered through the hall. The fighting seems to have been most intense towards the east. Architecturally, this area is similar to the surrounding locales, as the walls of the road house small alcoves and are lined with pillars.
37456: This major intersection was apparently the site of a recent skirmish among the orcs. Several bodies -- some with faces caked in dried blood, others with a pasty white substance coating arms and face -- are strewn about. All the corpses seem to have been stripped of any usable armour and weapons. To the east and west, one of the major roads of the dwarves of old proceeds into the blackness -- carved runes give it the name 'Mahal's Way'. Perpendicular to this runs a grey hall lacking any overt ornamentation.
37457: High overhead, lofty arches from which exotic chandeliers once hung span the wide road. The walls feature pillars and an occasional alcove, some of which still have fine alabaster sculptures sitting within. Apparently this area has not been violated by the orcs as much as some other locales, for though far from cheerful, this place does not feel unwholesome.
37458: A magnificent carved arch has collapsed here -- from the lack of dust probably not too long ago. Large blocks, with runes and carvings still visible, cover the floor of the passage forcing one to scramble over them to continue.
37459: The pillars lining the road to the west have here giving way to bas-relief carvings. Frozen in the wall are detailed scenes from the lives of dwarves, and even an occasional elf can be spotted among the multitude of figures. To the east, there appears to be a chamber as the road abruptly widens in that direction into a large open space.
37460: This large circular room appears to be consecrated to Aule, the Maker, for his likeness adorns the walls and ceiling. The exquisite relief carvings on the ceiling depict Aule lovingly fashioning the seven fathers of the dwarves from blocks of stone, while the murals adorning the walls depict him weeping as he prepares to destroy them so as not to damage the designs of Eru. The floor consists of a tiled representation of Aule, hammer in hand, standing with his left hand on the shoulder of Durin I, first lord of Khazad-dum. There is a large door made of stone leading to the south, while its apparent counterpart on the northern wall appears to have been sealed permanently by crude orkish masons.
37461: A magnificent staircase, leading to the upper levels of Moria, comes to an end here. A small plaque set into the last step bears the mark of the master Dwarven craftsman Narvi. East and west a large hall extends, its walls lined with tiny alcoves and large pillars. Almost unnoticed beside the grandeur of Narvi's staircase, a small ramp going down originates at a rectangular hole in the southern wall. The first few metres of the slope are cluttered with the remnants of a shattered door.
37462: Mahal's Way widens here to encompass two more rows of fluted columns in addition to the pillars that line the walls. The columns are formed of snow- white marble still unsullied by the passing centuries. The refreshing scent of outside air is unmistakable -- it seems to originate from the east -- and combined with the pristine marble, it gives this place the feel of a vast breezy veranda.
37463: This chamber is walled in magnificent white marble with inset designs made of rose-coloured quartz. The forces of nature have had a minor triumph here, for small hallways that once lead north and south from this place are now totally choked with piles of stone. To the west is a large hall filled with white columns, while low steps lead up to an even larger chamber to the east. A cool breeze issuing from the chamber to the east brings with it the promise of fresh air and open spaces.
37464: A glorious climax to Mahal's Way, this large chamber is lined with fine white marble and rose-coloured quartz. Narrow pillars are spaced throughout the room, soaring upwards and joined together by magnificent arches. High on the eastern wall, many large shafts have been cut through the mountainside, and through them the sky can be seen -- dispelling the gloom and despair of the black depths under the mountain. A fresh breeze from the Dimrill Dale brings with it the scent of pine forests, and perhaps a hint of the mallorn trees of Lothlorien located a bit farther east.
37466: Large amounts of rubbish have accumulated in this room -- everything from bits of armour and weapons to bones with rotting bits of meat still clinging to them. There is a large chamber of some kind to the west, while the passage south rapidly becomes choked with rubble.
37467: A blood-drenched commander of the Uruk-Moragog howls for your blood.

This room contains a single bed that, although still filthy, seems luxurious when compared to the other pallets and cots scattered through the Uruk-Moragog environs. The ceiling here is a high dome, its original ivory colour visible infrequently through a skin of sooty stains. At its apex, the dome has been cracked like an eggshell, with tiny fractures radiating from a blackened area that looks melted.

The heavy door to the north is still in great shape, maintained by this tribe of orcs as a defence against incursions by whatever wanders these halls. It would seem that a small contingent of Burzruth are stationed here, probably as a vanguard for raids made against the orcs of the upper city levels.
37469: This small passage connects three large chambers. It is apparently in constant use because the trash that characteristically clutters the unused halls of this region is here limited to an occasional bone or morsel of meat.

A small oaken table has been set here.
