A dark-skinned orc, born of the tunnels, draws his weapon.
A great black orc stands here, eager for combat.

Furnished with crude tables, this room provides a common area for the black orcs inhabiting this region. Piles of greasy furs are apparently used for lounging about, while the flayed remains of several rats hint at other forms of amusement. The walls are grimy, and a pall of grey smoke hangs about the upper portion of the room. Remnants of past meals are strewn haphazardly about the floor, and painted on the wall in child-like scrawls are repulsive scenes of orkish debauchery.
37471: A cloud of greasy smoke obscures the roof of this passage, and all the exposed surfaces of this area are covered with an oily residue, making them slightly slippery. The smoke originates to the west, and from that direction the scent of charred flesh can also be detected.
37472:
A small campfire burns here, its low flames giving off only a little light.
A piece of raw meat is on the ground.
The remainders of a disgusting elf-stew cover the ground.
The remainders of a disgusting elf-stew cover the ground.

A large fire blazes in the centre of the room, sending clouds of greasy smoke into the air. A large spit straddles the flame, its shaft coated with thick deposits of blackened blood and grease. Thrown in one corner are the remnants of three orcs -- little more than the skeletons remain as all usable parts have been stripped and apparently devoured.
37473: A large arrow lies on the ground.

The floor here is tracked with grease, and wisps of oily smoke from the room to the north curl about just below the ceiling. The masonry of the dwarves is here almost totally obscured by the accumulated filth of centuries of use by orcs.
37474:

The passage to the west has been deliberately blocked with rubble, though a narrow area has been left free to permit one to exit that way. A small wire cage has been constructed in the southeastern corner -- it is currently empty. Thrown on top of the cage are the bodies of several dozen small rodents and bats, all with several dozen puncture wounds. Lying next to the cage is a small box holding a set of twelve wicked-looking darts.
37475: A natural chimney has been widened by orkish masons, leaving enough room for a fully armoured man to make his way slowly up a stair of wicked-looking iron pitons driven into the rock.
37476: This plain road stands in stark contrast to the ornate thoroughfare just to the south. The elaborate carvings and pillars common elsewhere are here replaced by simple blocks of grey stone. A reinforced wooden door lies to the east, still in excellent condition despite centuries of neglect.
37477: From the martial motif of the carvings decorating walls of this shaft, these stairs were probably used by the Dwarven guards stationed in this area to quickly access the levels below. The stairs are worn by heavy use, but the carvings have been little touched by the depredations of orcs or time.
37478: This hallway, although large, is missing much of the exotic decoration found on other grand roads throughout Moria. The walls and floor are made of large blocks of grey rock and the ceiling hangs low. The sconces on the wall are made of simple black iron, purely utilitarian in design.
37479: The grey floor of this wide hall has a weathered look, as if it has seen the passage of uncounted feet over the years. There is a large iron door leading east, adorned with wide crimson swathes of a blood-like substance. To the north the passage terminates at a large chamber of some sort, but there is no sign of a door there.
37480: Little parts of a broken weapon are lying on the ground.

The carved runes over the door suggest that in ages past, this room housed a contingent of Dwarven guards. Small holes and notches cut into the walls are all that remain of the racks and shelves that would hold armour and weapons, as the wood was scavenged for other uses, or simply turned to dust over the years.
37481: This cistern supplied drinking water to the Dwarven guards stationed above. The shallow water still here is probably very stale, but it looks drinkable. The stone walls are very cool to the touch, and rough enough to allow one to scramble out of this place.
37482:
A small oaken table has been set here.

This room has been kept in excellent condition. It contains several crude chairs built from scavenged wood and a few cots. The walls have been adorned in typical Uruk-Moragog fashion, almost entirely covered with a rusty residue of dried blood. The heavy iron door to the west is still in excellent shape, lacking even the bloodstains that are characteristic of places inhabited by this tribe of orcs.
37483: The walls and ceiling of this passage look as if they have been seared -- the smooth stone blocks are covered with sooty stains, and some of them appear to have been cracked by intense heat. The passage continues to the east, and opens into a large chamber to the west.
37484: The passageway turns west to south here. It is fairly clear of trash, though a small pile of rodent bones has accumulated in one corner. To the south, a flimsy ladder occupies the centre of the passage, coming down from somewhere above. Overhead and on the walls, the stone is covered with large black and ash-coloured smudges -- reminders of a large fire long ago.
37485: A large stone block has been removed from the ceiling here, and a narrow tube leading upward has been excavated. A crude ladder leads up into the hole, but it is impossible to determine how far up it extends.
37486: The walls here have a dirty appearance, as if stained by smoke, adding to the already gloomy atmosphere. The passage is obviously well-used, for the bits of trash and garbage so common to orc tunnels have been cleared out of the centre by passing feet and lie only in small piles along the wall.
37487: The ash-coloured passage ends here at a primitive canvas partition hung from a flimsy wooden frame to the east. The canvas has been liberally painted with scenes of carnage, seeming to centre around a depiction of a large orc holding some sort of cup.
37488:
An orc of the Uruk-moragog stands in the gloom.
An orc of the Uruk-moragog stands in the gloom.

Filled with insect-ridden pallets, this room is obviously utilised by the orc guards for sleeping when they are not on duty. All of the exposed stone in this room is covered with sooty smudges, as if some time in the past a great conflagration had burned here, staining the walls with its smoke. Apparently there was once an exit to the south, but that has been permanently closed by the work of orkish masons.
37489: This small remnant of the great central stair quickly comes to an end. The dizzying abyss below is no longer accessible by this route, and the halls of the lower deeps must be reached by another way.
37490: This corridor stands in stark contrast to the ornate roads that tunnel through the surrounding mountain. Gone are the fluted pillars and soaring arches, replaced by simple grey granite and occasional wrought-iron sconces, yet its quiet decor seems somehow appropriate for the mansions of the dwarves.
37491: This road was designed seemingly to echo the Dwarven spirit. Its hard grey walls seem to radiate a stoic strength drawn from the roots of mountains. All superfluous decorations are absent, their presence would seem almost trite in this area.
37492: Large blocks of granite weighing several tons each have been so cunningly fit together that the walls of this place might have been built from a single slab of rock. The hall is silent now, though there is evidence of occasional orc patrols -- footprints left in the thick dust.
37493: This road was apparently designed with a spartan theme, for there are no superfluous decorations to be seen. The heavy grey granite blocks making up the floors and walls of this place sit in silence, seeming to wait in the darkness for the sound of dwarves mustering for battle to echo here again.
37494: Once home to a cadre of elite Dwarven guards, this large room is now almost totally empty. The walls and floor are made of large sturdy blocks of granite and are coated with a light layer of dust. From examining tracks, it is readily apparent that this room sees occasional traffic still, though the cobwebs gathered in the corners speak of a long abandonment.
37495: Judging by tracks in the grime on the floor, this passage must occasionally see east-west traffic. The road leading south, however, appears to have been undisturbed for ages. To the east the passage has deliberately been blocked by a pile of rubble, though a small space wide enough for one to pass sideways has been left against the northern wall.
37496: Covered with dust and guano, this road has lain fallow for many years. Even the orcs seem to have totally ignored it, for there is no sign of their having been here at all. To the north is some sort of intersection, but the darkness to the south precludes any observation of the road ahead.

Rustling can be heard in the darkness above, but nothing can be seen in the inky blackness overhead. To the east a flight of stairs leads up, and the smell of fresh air is carried by a breeze originating in that direction.

This small room is set high on a mountainside and provides an unobstructed view of the lands of Rhovanion to the east. Probably used by the dwarves to keep watch on the eastern approaches to Khazad-dum, this watchroom now provides access to the outside world for the large population of bats in the chamber to the west.
37500: This small space owes its existence to the caprice of chance. Large boulders are wedged tightly into the shaft overhead, but some of the rubble to the west looks like it may be safely moved. Below, a magnificent stairway bearing the markings of Narvi proceeds -- apparently it used to continue through the rubble-choked shaft above, but no longer.
37501: The majestic road of black stone that extends the west abruptly ends to the east in a pile of rubble. The hallway here is for the most part intact, the hard ebony rock unmarred by whatever catastrophe occurred to the east.
37502: The road continues its journey beneath the archways. The walls are intricately carved with scenes from an ancient battlefield, with the victorious dwarves gathered about the bodies of two slain leaders. The detail is so extraordi- nary that the grief on each of the faces has been captured, frozen here for eternity.
37503: This area is an intersection of two large halls, crossing each other at right angles. The grand road leading east and west is constructed of some exotic black glassy material, while north and south, the hallway seems to possess a sanguine glow. The pillars in this area slant inward slightly, creating an illusion of great height.
37504: The avenue continues in a north-south fashion. The beautifully crafted walls seem to shine with a ruddy glow undimmed by the ubiquitous filth layering all exposed surfaces. The presence of many footprints indicate this passage still sees heavy traffic.
37505: A large bat is here, hanging in the darkness.

The red avenue continues south-north here, joining a smaller road passing through a doorway a short way to the east. Grand arches carved of a reddish rock line the avenue, their tops hidden in the darkness above.
37506: The avenue goes straight south-north here. The walls are solid and polished, and where the artwork shows through, speckled bands of silver have been laid out, crossing the low, round ceiling and joining the bands from the other wall.
37507: Here the red avenue bends in its course, going south and east into a smaller chamber. The lower parts of the walls are crafted in a deep red material, while the upper parts contain strings of various ores like silver and gold. A very cold breeze is flowing along the floor coming from the east.
37508: You are standing at the entrance to a tomb. Strange hollow voices seem to emerge from the surrounding walls. They could be produced by a breeze blowing through cavities but there is no way to be sure. To the east, a grand archway littered with speckled bands of gold and silver marks the entrance to the tomb itself. There is a grand sign above the doorway.
37509:
A stone sarcophagus lies on the floor.
A spirit floats around, making strange magical gestures (red aura and glowing).
A spirit floats around, making strange magical gestures (red aura and glowing).
An eerie spectyre hovers over a sarcophagus (red aura).

This small chamber is the resting place of a Dwarven Lord. All over the walls carvings depicting scenes from his life, both grand victories and defeats, can be seen. A huge coffin stand in the middle of the room, but it has been broken open and the bones lie scattered all over the room. Nothing is held sacred by the foul denizens who roam these tunnels now.
37510: Little parts of a broken weapon are lying on the ground.

There is a large hole in the floor here. A sizeable block of stone has been uprooted from the floor of the passage, revealing a rough tube probably excavated by orcs. A crude ladder sits in the hole, allowing one to exit in this direction. The door to the east, though obviously a dwarven creation, is painted with horizontal stripes of bright crimson.
37511: The avenue continues in a north-south fashion. The walls are crafted out of a strange deep red material combined with a shining yellow material used for the low, round ceiling. Silvery linings cascade horizontally along the walls, swirling here and there in intricate circles before continuing.
37512: The red avenue goes north-south here, joining a smaller road passing towards a doorway to the east. Some large arches made of a red glowing material are placed above the avenue here. There is a small crack in the ceiling between the arches, from which some water drips down to form puddles on the ground.
37513: The avenue goes straight north-south here. The walls are solid and polished, with some artwork showing in the upper parts where spiralling bands of silver has been laid out, forming swirling patterns in the low, round ceiling. The material in the upper parts of the walls here has given in to time and cracked open slightly.
37514: Here the red avenue bends in its course, going north and east into a smaller chamber. The lower parts of the walls are crafted in a deep red material, while the upper parts contain strings of various ores like silver and gold. A chilly breeze from the east is wafting along the floor.

You are standing at the entrance to a tomb. Freezing hollow voices seem to emerge from the surrounding walls. To the east, a grand archway littered with speckled bands of gold and silver marks the entrance to the tomb itself. There is a large sign above the doorway.

This small chamber is the resting place of a Dwarven Lord. Paintings depicting scenes from his life, both grand victories and defeats, can be seen on the walls. A huge coffin stands in the middle of the room, but it has been broken open and the bones lie scattered all over the room.
37517: Crafted of a type of hardened obsidian, this grand hallway of lustrous black continues its east-west journey. Pillars and arches add to the high ceiling's aura of vastness, and high up among the tops of the pillars a damp mist has form, lazily caressing the dark stone.
37518:
A clear spring babbles as cool water trickles out of the ground.
A squat orkish female glares and spits curses at you.

This large circular room lies beneath an ebony dome of jet-black rock. Dozens of niches are cut into the circumference of the chamber; judging from the copious amounts of alabaster fragments scattered about the statues that once filled these niches have all been pulled down and demolished. The fountain in the centre of the chamber is still functioning, its crystal water probably coming straight from the melting snow atop Zirakzigil.
37519:
A lurg leader of the Uruk-moragog looks at you from a bloody helm.

This grand hallway continues east-west here. To the east, the high ceiling plunges downward toward the floor in an elegant arc, and the wide road passes through the resulting portal into another chamber. The walls here are made of the same black stone found in the surrounding areas, and the carvings present are still as detailed as when first made.
37520: The slender column in the centre of Durin's Chimney is connected to the east side of the chasm by a makeshift bridge of old wooden planks. A large stone bridge once stood here -- the remains of it are clearly visible -- but it probably collapsed during the troubled years following the awakening of Durin's Bane, for it is said the earth would frequently shake as he made his presence felt.
37521: The truncated remains of a mighty stone bridge precariously cling to the western edge of this chasm. Known as Durin's Chimney, this mighty cleft in the heart of the mountains is reputed to stretch from the deepest delvings of the dwarves to the highest peak of Zirakzigil. Replacing the fallen bridge is a makeshift structure of wooden planks, scarcely wide enough for two men to walk abreast. It stretches from the western edge to the slender central pillar -- a construction of the dwarves that once held a stairway allowing access to all levels of Khazad-dum -- and from there to the eastern side. The column itself has been badly damaged -- it appears that the spiralling stair that once encircled it has been completely destroyed below this level, although it some of it does seem to have survived above.
37522: This grand hallway obviously served an important function at one time -- a small plaque insribed with runes labels it 'Hall of Mourning'. The cool black stone of the floor is relatively free of dust, and the slightest sound sends faint echoes reverberating down the length of the passage and upwards into the darkened recesses of the vaulted ceiling. To the north there seems to be some sort of guard station, while the hall itself runs east-west.
37523: The stair of obsidian seamlessly melts into the glossy black rock of the floor. Passageways extend in three directions -- a major road leads east, while to the north and south smaller corridors lead into the murky darkness. The road leading east was built with great care by the dwarves, for intricate bas-relief carvings are visible along the length of its walls, until they fade from vision in the distance.
37524: The deep-black walls of this alley are inlaid with spiralling filaments of shining silver. The threads seem to shine and twinkle with a light of their own as they dance along the passageway. Scattered along both walls are the remnants of several wicked knives, as if in their greed the denizens of this place had tried to pry the strands from the wall.
37525: A huge jet-black door bars the way south, though it appears to have been warped in such a way that it will no longer close properly. The intricate silver patterns in the wall are more prominent near the door than in areas to the north, and they seem to centre around a carving on the eastern wall.
37526: The walls and floor of this alley appear to be carved from a single block of lustrous black stone -- no joints or seams are visible. Inlaid in the deep ebony of the walls are exquisite patterns traced by strands of spun silver no thicker than hair. They cover the wall like lace, disappearing into the vaulted darkness overhead.
37527: The jet-black alley continues its straight course. The intricate patterns of inlaid silver are more prevalent here than farther south, and they dance and swirl around a carving of Aule crafting the first dwarves in his smithy. To the north are the remains of a shattered door.
37528:
Little parts of a broken weapon are lying on the ground.
A large round whetstone rests on the ground.

From the scattered remnants of tools lying strewn about, it is apparent that this room used to be an armoury. Set in the northern wall is a large forge used by the dwarves to fashion armour and weapons in ages past. There appears to be nothing salvageable from the scattered pieces of weaponry and armour that remain -- everything of value must have been looted long ago.
37529: This room is obviously used as a base for the many orc patrols that wander these halls. Dirty pallets and cots are everywhere, and the smell of sweat and filth makes the air almost too thick to breathe.
37530: This small foyer for the room to the east is apparently used as a garbage pit. Various pieces of broken armour, mostly of orkish manufacture, have been tossed haphazardly about, and the butchered carcasses of several large rats lie decomposing near the entrance -- skinned and stripped of meat.
37531: A small pool of red-stained water lies here.

You are standing in the second Uruk-Urgingurz barracks on the fourth level in Moria. The walls are stained with dried blood, probably relics from a recent feast on less fortunate, skinned, prey. Some black rusty shields hang on the walls too, with a strange emblem on them.
37532: A wide ramp leads upwards at a gentle slope and probably at one time provided a method of transporting heavy loads to the level above. Closer examination reveals bits of mechanical rubble that was at one time a winch of some kind, but there is not enough left to know for sure.
37533: This grey corridor is fairly nondescript, apparently designed with an eye toward function and not decor. Shoved to one side is a metal cart, similar to what one might expect to find in a mine, and a few metres of rusted chain too brittle to be of any use to anyone.
37534: Small corridors lead to the north, east, and west, while to the south is a small duct from which a chilly breeze originates. The floor and walls are all done in mundane grey stone and layered with the dust of ages.
37535: There is very little room to manoeuvre here, as this duct was not meant to be used as a route of travel. A steady breeze from the area to the south brings a noticeable chill to the air and keeps dust from settling on the stone of the walls and floor.
37536: This tiny space hardly merits the name 'room', but it is a good deal more spacious than the narrow ducts leading north and west. A narrow shaft is cut in the low stone roof, and from this shaft a fresh breeze is blowing. Unfortunately, this shaft is far too small to permit anything larger than a rat to proceed.
37537: A fresh breeze wafts down this duct from the east, chilling the hard stone that lines this area. Crawling seems the only feasible way to proceed, and it is possible to do this both east and west.
37538: This small duct is carpeted with a fuzzy layer of mould. To the west, this passage empties into a chamber, and it is possible to continue crawling to the east.
37539:
A huge black fungus is here, exuding a foul stench.
A huge black fungus is here, exuding a foul stench.
A huge black fungus is here, exuding a foul stench.
An ancient fungus smothers the boulders.
An ancient fungus smothers the boulders.
An ancient fungus smothers the boulders.
A dripping yellow fungus hangs here, clinging to the crevices and walls.

This room is a veritable arboretum of underground vegetation -- all manner of lichens and fungi cling to the stone of both wall and floor. Somehow these plants have managed to prosper here in the darkness and have over the passing centuries carpeted the room with life. This has not been without price, for the mortar joining the stones of the walls has been made weak. A portion of the western wall has collapsed into to the room, revealing a narrow crack extending back into the mountain. A duct of some type is set in the eastern wall, and it appears large enough for an armoured man to crawl through.
37540: This passage has a distinct musty odour, like bread that has been left outside for days. The odour unmistakably grows stronger to the south, but there is no hint as to its source.
37541: Once a storehouse for foodstuffs needed to feed a large population of dwarves, this place was long ago pillaged of anything of use. There are pegholes cut into the wall where once a system of shelves was set, and small bits of ancient splintered wood lying about are all that remain of what must have once been large storage bins.
37542: The remnants of several ancient casks and vats provide a clue as to the use of this area in ages past. Scattered about in the thick dust are rusted hoops of iron, once part of large barrels perhaps, and other small bits of metallic paraphernalia too corroded to be accurately identified.
37543: Totally abandoned for centuries, the only sign of life in this hall are the scattered rat droppings and rodent tracks in the layers of dust. To the west, large metal hinges hang loosely from the wall -- there is no sign of the door which they once held. In that direction lies a chamber, while to the east is a small intersection.
37544: A steady brisk breeze from the south brings a chill to the air of this place. There is little dust here, for the wind, though light, is strong enough to prevent it from settling to depths found in some of the other abandoned halls. There is an intersection to the south, and to the north the passage continues.
37545: The floor to both the east and west is sunk about two metres relative to the central section. These shallow pits once housed huge blocks of ice cut from the snowfields of upper reaches of the mountains. Combined with the steady cool breeze blowing from the south, this would produce a temperature cold enough to safely store meat.
37546: This room was perhaps another of the many rooms that once held supplies for the Dwarven city. The roof in the northern end of the room has collapsed -- some time ago judging by the coating of powdery dust overlaying the scene. A faint breeze from the south occasionally forms whorls in the dirt, sending small clouds of the stuff into the air.
37547: An ancient mouldering skeleton lies prostrate on the floor, the upper portion of its cranium completely smashed as if by a huge club. At one time, this skeleton may have belonged to a human -- the teeth indicate it was not an orc-- but whoever it was died hundreds of years ago, judging by the layers of dirt that have covered many of the bones.
37548: This corridor probably saw little use even when the dwarves inhabited Moria, for the whole area is lined with simple bricks -- there is no sign of the splendid decor seen in the more important passages of Khazad-dum. The hall continues to the east, unmarked by superfluous decoration, while to the west the masonry seems to have suffered damage at some time in the past.
37549: This room was once much larger -- the entire area to the west apparently collapsed many years ago. A thick layer of powdery dust coats everything, kicking up in great clouds when disturbed. The ceiling here looks extremely unstable, as great fractures zig-zag across its entire area. Passages to the south and east are still free of rubble, allowing one to move in either of those directions.
37550: This room has been devastated at some time in the past. The walls to the east and west have cracked, revealing the natural rock lying behind the old masonry. Large blocks of granite have fallen from above, and the ceiling is riddled with fractures. The dust lies thickly here, undisturbed except for scattered rat tracks and droppings.
37551:
A nasty troll female crouches here, with a feral look in her eyes.
A nasty troll female crouches here, with a feral look in her eyes.

Great piles of rags and furs are stacked here to form an extremely large pallet stretching the entire length of the western wall. The floor is stained with blood, both clotted and fresh, and there are piles of gnawed bones lying haphazardly about. To the north and south narrow passages stretch -- long abandoned judging by the stone rubble that almost completely blocks them. To the east, an ancient wooden door hangs loosely from iron hinges, tenaciously refusing to surrender and fall to the floor.
37552: This extremely narrow crack in the rock has barely enough room for an armoured man to squeeze through. To the west the natural cleft continues, but there is crumbled masonry and a room to the east. From somewhere in the darkness to the west the faint gurgle of running water can be detected in the otherwise still air of the underground.
37553: Footing in this area is treacherous, as the floor consists entirely of debris that has fallen from above and wedged itself into the narrow crack. Though the cleft widens in the area above, this place is scarcely wide enough for an armoured man to pass sideways. To the south there appears to be some relief from the torturous press of rock, for the fault intersects a chamber of some sort.
37554: The natural rock wall to the north contains a fracture large enough for one to uncomfortably enter. The air here is very moist, and from the west the gurgle of running water can be faintly heard. There is a passage to the west, and a natural series of shelves leading down in that direction functions as a stairway.
37555: The roof of this cavern is low, hardly more than two metres separates it from the floor. This entire cavity is filled with wide natural pillars, forming a natural maze. Though the columns of rock indicate this place was once rich with water, aside from the moist air the rock here is dry. For some reason, perhaps the trauma responsible for the narrow crack granting entrance to this complex of caves, the water has moved -- the sound of it is faintly heard from somewhere to the west.
37556: The walls here are encircled with wide horizontal bands of colour, from plain grey to layers of bright crimson. The ceiling arches high overhead, and the walls are extremely smooth -- worn by centuries of running water. To the west this large chamber continues, while the sound of running water issues from a tunnel to the north.
37557: Resplendent swaths of bright colour girdle this cavern from floor to ceiling. To the east this chamber continues, while the area west has apparently fallen victim to an earthquake, for nothing lies in that direction but a huge pile of rubble. The smooth walls hint at the presence of swift flowing water at some time in the past, but this place is dry now.
37558: This tunnel slopes steadily down from south to north. There is not a lot of room here -- frequently boulders have broken from the already low ceiling and further limit the amount of space. The sound of running water to the north is very noticeable.
37559: From the shape of this tunnel, it is clear that once an underground stream coursed through this cavern. Although this cavern is now dry, the stream seems to have migrated to the north due to the caprice of some geological force -- perhaps an earthquake.
37560: This bubble-shaped chamber is completely lined by angular quartz crystals. Every inch of this place shimmers like iridescent glass, giving the illusion of standing inside of a fabulous diamond.
37561:
An albino salamander is here, perched on some rocks.
An albino salamander is here, perched on some rocks.
An albino fish is swimming here, looking for some food.
An albino fish is swimming here, looking for some food.
An albino fish is swimming here, looking for some food.

Water pours steadily from the ceiling, splashing after a short drop into a shallow pool. The pool is at most one metre in depth, and the rocks of its bottom are completely covered by growths of red algae. To the west, water spills over a small lip and goes sluicing away down a narrow chute.
37562: Water races through a narrow channel, heading down at an extremely steep angle. The slick red algae coating the walls makes every toehold precarious, and it is not clear how far below this channel continues.
37563: A steady stream of water empties into this area from above, splashing into small pool. The floor of this natural cavern consists of several shallow pools of rust-tinged water, each pool seemingly scooped out of the native rock by some unknown force.
37564: The rock making up the floor of this natural chamber has been hollowed out in several places that now harbour small pools of rusty water. The entire surface is wet, but in the drier areas a thin crust of mineral deposits coats the rock, looking almost like a delicate layer of snow.
37565: Narrow stone causeways criss-cross this vast, echoing cavern, offering numerous pathways between the stagnant red-brown pools. An icy mist rises from the calm surface of the water, chilling the air, and the cold, granite walls of the cave glisten with moisture. But no moss or algae flourish here, perhaps due to the heavy deposits of iron, which colour the water of Mahal's Wells.
37566:
A grey snake slides along the water.
A grey snake slides along the water.

Cold, wet stone hangs low above your head, but the roof of this narrow tunnel appears to be sound. An icy pool of russet-coloured water covers the floor, but it seems shallow enough to permit wading. However, the smooth stone is slippery and treacherous underfoot.
37567: A narrow, granite stair once clung to the north wall of this cave, but now all that remains is an uneven pile of broken rock, and a few rough out-croppings of stone, connected to the bridge overhead. The tattered remnants of an old rope are still attached to one of these prominences, swinging gently in the cool breeze, far above.
37568: At this end of Mahal's Wells, the sound of flowing water can clearly be heard, and the narrow stone causeways, which span the chamber are crumbling and broken in places. Though most of the red-brown pools stand motionless, the one at the western extreme of the cavern escapes into a fast-flowing underground stream, which is obviously the sole drainage for this vast complex of pools and small lakes.
37569:
An albino fish is swimming here, looking for some food.
An albino fish is swimming here, looking for some food.
An albino fish is swimming here, looking for some food.

A small underground stream flows west from Mahal's Wells, carrying the rust- stained waters off into narrow tunnels, deep in the mountain. The cold, granite walls and stream bed have been worn quite smooth over the ages, the ceiling above drips with condensation, and the air is filled with an icy mist, which chills you to the bone.
37570:
An albino fish is swimming here, looking for some food.
An albino fish is swimming here, looking for some food.

The stream flows faster here than it did to the east, white foam dashing angrily atop the red-brown surface of the water. The ceiling looms lower overhead, and the dark stone walls are converging, making it unlikely that a boat would be of use to follow this waterway any further to the west.
37571: Though the waterway is completely submerged, it is still possible to sense how fast it flows through this narrow tunnel. Twisting and turning, dipping and climbing, the only constant factor about this channel is the seemingly random nature of its course, as it races onward, seeking out weaknesses in the bedrock.
37572: Gaining momentum as it travels westward, the stream flows angrily on through tunnels so narrow and low that they are completely filled by the rushing, mineral-laden waters. Here the current dashes violently against the western wall, before being sent on a new southerly course, where the ceiling rises and the channel once again widens slightly.
37573:
An albino fish is swimming here, looking for some food.
An albino fish is swimming here, looking for some food.

The water surges angrily from the low passage to the north, then floods westward in a raging torrent, splashing high on the cold, grey, granite walls. A cold mist fills the air, obscuring vision, and the roar of a waterfall echoes all around. A small recess in the southern wall causes the water to eddy around in that area, before racing off west.
37574: No rough-hewn chamber, this cramped little cavern bears the hallmarks of the craftsmen of Durin's folk. The walls, floor and ceiling are perfectly smooth, and the dimensions of the room regular. However, massive cracks have scarred the west wall, and it must have been through these that the icy cold water has poured, flooding the entire room.
37575: Just as it was further to the north, the south end of the chamber is well- wrought, with walls, floor and ceiling all polished to a smooth finish. It would appear that this small passageway was constructed in the days when the Mines of Khulakal, above, were active with hoardes of busy dwarven delvers. Set at the very centre of the roof above you is a simple, yet skilfully crafted stone trapdoor.
37576: An elegant marble chest sits against the wall.

Dust blankets everything within the room, billowing up in choking clouds at every slight movement. The air hangs heavy and still, as if time itself were suspended in this cramped chamber. The walls and floor are smooth, the cold, hard granite polished by the skilled hands of dwarven artisans, so many ages before.
37577: You are standing just inside a black opening torn into the thick stone wall. There is some sort of chamber east of here, but it is so dark and silent that you cannot learn anything more without entering it. A feeling of deep despair settles over you as you realise how small and vulnerable you really are here.
37578: A small oaken table has been set here.

This chamber appears to be some sort of guardpost. It contains a large table and a couple of chairs, but it seems not to have been used for some time. A small dark tunnel leads into the north from here, and a large opening has been smashed through the wall to the west.
37579: This is a simple tunnel with a high roof and rough-carved walls that appear to be recently worked. There is a putrid odour in the air here that calls to mind images of meat left to spoil in the open. The simple tunnel continues north, but opens up into a chamber just to the south.
37580: A fairly large tunnel bends east to south from here. Strange grunting sounds and an evil smell come to you from somewhere to the east, but the south is just dark and silent. Looking toward one small side of the niche one can see what might be the corpse of a small bat.
37581:
A bulky cave troll is here, looking like a massive pile of stone.
A bulky cave troll is here, looking like a massive pile of stone.

This gigantic cavern is occupied by some cavetrolls, and it smells awful! The foul, dank air immediately invades your lungs like an unseen enemy, burning your eyes and throat. The awful stench actually originates from somewhere to the north, but the inhabitants of this cavern certainly add to the problem. This place is richly furnished with filthy strawmats, broken stone slabs and plenty of decaying corpses scattered about the area. Trolls surely find it much to their liking, and they seem eager to welcome you into their home. When you decide to leave, you can flee in any of four directions.
37582: This cave is apparently used as both a dumping ground and source of water for the trolls who inhabit this area. There is a small stream trickling through the back of the cavern, but it is almost clogged with the accumulated filth of the trolls.
37583:
A large cave troll is here, staying close to his mother.
A large cave troll is here, staying close to his mother.
A large cave troll is here, staying close to his mother.
The ugly troll mother is roaming the cave, taking care of her loved ones.

This is a filthy and disgusting troll den! The air is ripe with the stench of trolls, and there are quite a few tall, pale cavetrolls waiting in here. You see many bones and colourful rags lying all over the cave floor. The only obvious exit leads back into the huge cavern to the north.
37584: A large cave troll sniffs the air, sensing an intruder is near.
The tunnel bends from west to south here. There are loud grunting sounds coming from the west, and this should arouse both fear and caution in any who would travel that way.
37585: You are travelling in a broad, well-made tunnel that leads both north and south. The walls and floor of this tunnel are smoother than most others you have seen here, and the tunnel seems to run in a very straight line.
37586:
A large cave troll sniffs the air, sensing an intruder is near.
A squat and filthy troll lurks in the darkness.

This tunnel appears to be freshly excavated and is in good shape with no risk of collapse. The walls and floor are not smooth, but the tunnel itself is very straight. You can go north or south from here.
37587:
A large cave troll sniffs the air, sensing an intruder is near.
A large cave troll sniffs the air, sensing an intruder is near.
A large cave troll sniffs the air, sensing an intruder is near.

This tunnel seems to have been recently excavated, though not with dwarven skill and attention to detail. The walls and floor are not smooth, but they appear to be in good shape and there is little risk of collapse. The tunnel itself is very straight and leads due north and south from this point.
37588: This is an extremely small passage, barely big enough for you to fit into without stooping over. It is dark in here and you cannot make out the finer details of your surroundings. The darkness seems to become almost absolute to the south.
37589: A pair of tiny eyes gleam at you from the shadows.

Here a small, dark passage leading north reaches a deadend at a large square hole in the floor. The hole appears to open into unfathomable darkness, and it could be either twenty feet or twenty thousand to the bottom.
37590: A pair of tiny eyes gleam at you from the shadows.

This room is more than simply large, it is positively gigantic. The ceiling rises at least thirty feet above your head, high enough to accommodate any creature that you have ever encountered. Huge, broken stone steps climb the south wall to a large opening in the ceiling, and you cannot help noticing that each wall is pigmented with a distinct colour. There is a huge bed in here as well, and this serves to harden suspicions as to who or rather what occupies this place.
37591: A very strange tunnel indeed! The walls and ceiling here are in such poor condition that you are now certain that work here was abandoned in haste long ago. Your eyes pick out some dark patches clustered on one of the walls here which, for some reason, brings to mind the gore resulting from a slaughtered beast. The tunnel is completely silent and pitch black, and continues south.
37592: A huge stone troll looms overhead, ready to crush your body.

This unfinished tunnel bends sharply west and north. You find many old mining tools scattered about here, but all are cracked and pitted by the weight of many centuries of disuse. The builders of this tunnel must have been in a great hurry to finish here, or maybe they were suddenly forced to retreat from this place. You see no signs of a battle here, but through some trick of the mind you imagine hearing the deathcries of terrified dwarves dying in great agony.
37593:
Iarion the Elf, wielding a steel-tipped spear, is standing here scouting.
Kostilam, wielding a mighty dwarven axe, is standing here.

This 'cave' is really nothing more than the junction of three large tunnels. The rough stonework exhibited here indicates that work on these tunnels was never properly completed and the fossilised mining equipment scattered about here arouses your curiosity even more. Exactly what occurred here and when? Dark tunnels branch off to the east and west, and another smaller passageway plunges into absolute blackness to the south.
37594:
The corpse of a huge stone troll is lying here.
The corpse of a huge stone troll is lying here.

The walls and roof here are jagged and quite irregular, rather slipshop workmanship for Moria dwarves. Perhaps they were pressed for time when they worked here. An unexpected heaviness in the air conjures thoughts of great evil lurking somewhere nearby, and you suddenly feel as though you should be moving along too. The passage continues north and east.
37595: The corpse of a huge stone troll is lying here.

From this point, this curious tunnel continues back to the south. The passageway here is only rough-hewn from the surrounding rock which is black as pitch and cold to the touch. It seems as though whoever made this tunnel worked in great haste and did not take the care to craft the stonework up to the usual standard.
37596:
Umuk is here, fighting Tordol (t).
A bulky cave troll is here, looking like a massive pile of stone.
Tordol the Dwarf (t), wielding a mighty dwarven axe, is here, fighting Umuk.

Here the tunnel comes to an abrupt deadend in absolute darkness. Work seems to be in progress here, perhaps in hope of progressing farther into the bedrock under the mountain. The obvious exit is back to the north, but your quick eyes catch sight of some strange scratches made in the dirt here.
37597: A rather small deserted passageway unlike all the others you have seen before stretches from this point to the west. Although the air here does not stink of carrion as it does in many nearby places, it is quite stale and dead as if it has been unstirred for centuries. Some sort of lichen grows in abundance on the walls and ceiling here.
37598: This passage is unlike most found in this part of Moria, for the walls are extremely smooth and beautifully decorated. The builders must have put a great deal of time and effort into its planning and construction. The air here, however, is very stale and seems unhealthy so you quickly decide to move on.
37599: The air in this narrow passageway has become distinctly cold, so cold now that you begin to shiver uncontrollably. The floor here is coated with a thick layer of dust which billows up as you tread through it, causing you to cough loudly. The silence, darkness, dust and cold combine to make you feel as though you have entered a tomb, perhaps your own. The passageway continues east and west into the stillness.
37600: The passage bends to the south here. The walls are very smooth and cold, and they also appear to be quite ancient.
37601: At this point, the empty passage bends east to north. A thick layer of dust covers the floor here, and the heavy silence is only broken by the clinking of your armour. Magnificent carvings cover the walls here, but their meaning has been lost in the centuries since they were first chiselled from the mountain.
37602: This long east-west passage becomes very narrow at this point. The floor is covered by a thin layer of dust, and the heavy still air is hard to breathe.
37603: The passageway leads east and west from here. The darkness is absolute in this part of the tunnel and you cannot see well, but you sense a powerful evil presence somewhere to the east. The walls and floors here show evidence of good quality Dwarven workmanship.
37604: A funeral chest carved in bas-relief finally draws one's attention.

The long passageway opens up into this small but magnificent tomb. The walls have been sculpted from the bedrock in such a way as to display all of the different kinds of stone found here. There are sculptures of Dwarven hero-kings and detailed battlescenes carved into every available inch of stone with what must have been almost infinite patience and skill. Wonderful, almost hypnotic patterns of light and shadow dance over the many beautiful things to be found here, and this distracts ones attention from the other features of this room.
37605: This is a tiny passage hewn from the rock as a maintenance passageway. The walls are rough and the passage is not perfectly straight like the other passages in Khazad-dum. The layer of dust on the floor suggests that this place has not seen any visitors for a long time.
37606: This tiny passageway was hewn from the rock for maintenance reasons. The rough-hewn passage is not perfectly straight like the other passages in Khazad-dum. The layer of dust on the floor suggests that this place has not seen any visitors for a long time.
37607: This small passage was cut through the rock as a maintenance passageway. There used to be a vertical shaft in the middle of the room leading up and down, with iron rings hanging from its sides; but the passage below is filled with rubble, and the rings above are so rusty that they would no longer support one's weight.
37617:
The corpse of a grey troll is lying here.
The corpse of a grey troll is lying here.
The corpse of a grey troll is lying here.
The corpse of Karcarak is lying here.
Karcarak, wielding a fell blade, is here, fighting Rhulo.
A stone-grey troll advances toward you, with fury in its eyes.
A stone-grey troll advances toward you, with fury in its eyes.
A grey troll is here, fighting Cunh.
Rhulo the Elf, wielding a double edged eket, is sitting here.
Tordol the Dwarf (t), wielding a black waraxe, is here, fighting Karcarak.
Cunh the Dwarf, wielding a war mattock, is here, fighting a grey troll.

This dreadful cavern is used as a throne room by a great troll chieftain. A great throne is set in the north wall, adorned with the skulls of his victims. Piles of bones are set in the corners of the room, and bloodstains cover the walls and floor.
37756: Soupy gore fills the bottom of this pit, varying in depth from two feet along the northern wall to an unknown depth farther south. Undoubtably the remains of countless sacrifices have gone into creating this area, an environment that could not be tolerated by any but the most loathsome of creatures. From time to time great bubbles slowly rise from the depths, reaching the surface and bursting with a splattering of red, and ripples of undetermined origin also occasionally make their way across the surface of the liquid. An almost palpable malevolence can be felt, as if the presence of any other living crea- ture in this pit represents an affront that cannot be tolerated.
37757:
A metal wall shield rests on the ground.
There are two large metal shields here.
An ancient dwarven skeleton lies upon the floor.
A sturdy peg for hanging armour is on the wall.
On the peg, there are two pairs of sleeves, two pairs of leggings, a pair of metal vambraces, a pair of metal greaves, a metal breastplate, a pair of metal boots, a shining chain mail shirt, a chain mail hauberk, a chain mail coif, a metal helmet, and a pair of metal gauntlets.
There are two sturdy pegs here.
A weapons rack stands against the wall.
In the rack are a battle axe and a war mattock.
A weapons rack stands against the wall.

This room has been cleverly hidden from prying eyes. Pegs adorn the walls for the hanging of armour and several weapon racks for any weapons. Obviously from the layout of this small hall, the equipment here was carefully stored away, ready for a unit of dwarves in need of armament. The peg in the middle must hold the armour of the Lieutenant.
37758: Several shattered chests indicate that this room may have once housed some of the fabled treasures of Moria, but there is nothing of value visible among all of the debris. The room is made from the same black rock that lines the hall- way to the north, and the wall to the south is covered in bas-relief carvings decorated with inlaid silver.
37759: This is a small niche in the wall, most likely used as a guardpost. There is a very uncomfortably looking chair made of stone here, but one can assume by the look of it and its position in the room most of the guards on duty here prefer to stand as they watch the passing creatures. This niche would also make a good ambush spot.
37760:
A half-rotten corpse is hanging here.
An orc of the Uruk-moragog stands in the gloom.
An orc of the Uruk-moragog stands in the gloom.
An orc of the Uruk-moragog stands in the gloom.

The carvings on the wall seem to indicate that this room was at one time used by the dwarves for ceremonial purposes, but now this place has been pirated by the Uruk-Goramog for a dwelling place. Smelly rags and furs are strewn haphazardly about, and a crude wooden table carries the remnant of a recent repast.
37761:
An orc of the Uruk-moragog stands in the gloom.
An orc of the Uruk-moragog stands in the gloom.
An orc of the Uruk-moragog stands in the gloom.
An orc of the Uruk-moragog stands in the gloom.
An orc of the Uruk-moragog stands in the gloom.

This room is utilised as a crude dining hall by the orcs of this area, a con- This room is probably utilised as a crude dining hall by the orcs of this area, a conclusion supported by the presence of a large pile of bones stashed in one corner. The artwork adorning this room -- depicting Aule taking a Dwarven king close to his bosom -- suggests that this room may have had a ceremonial purpose originally.
37762: The magnificent stairway comes to an abrupt halt here. The continuation below has been entirely choked with rubble -- the beautiful craftsmanship of Narvi totally destroyed by orcs. To the west a large passage lined with pompous arches and pillars extends, while to the south is a large door of solid iron.
37763: In this room some Uruk warriors have their quarters. Broken pieces of armour and weapons are scattered over the filthy floor, and contraptions which probably are used as beds stand in a row along the eastern wall. In the corners of the room you see piles of rotten meat, probably relics of a mid-night snack.
37764: A wide road passes in the west-east direction. Obviously one of this level's most used roads, it is brilliantly crafted with pillars lining up along the walls. Small busts of renowned dwarves are placed on cutouts in the walls. The deep-black floor is apparently made of a material of great hardness since it is in very good shape after all these years without maintenance, though there do appear to be a few scratches in the area near the northern wall.
37765: This room is quite large, and is architecturally different from the adjacent areas. Above is a lustrous black dome in which can be seen the seven stars of the Crown of Durin -- silver shining so brightly it seems to illuminate the passage. Cut into the northern wall is a narrow flight of black steps leading upward to some sort of chamber. On the southern wall is a detailed carving of a dwarf wielding an axe, his eyes two coal-black gems.
37766: The wide road traverses the darkness from the west to the east. Somewhere in the roof water drips down and forms some puddles on the floor, adding to the overall humidity in here. There are fragments of stone and rocks lying all over the floor.
37768:
A squat orkish female glares and spits curses at you.
A lurg leader of the Uruk-moragog looks at you from a bloody helm.
An Uruk-moragog warrior glares around him, ready for enemies.
An Uruk-moragog warrior glares around him, ready for enemies.
An Uruk-moragog warrior glares around him, ready for enemies.
An Uruk-moragog warrior glares around him, ready for enemies.
An Uruk-moragog warrior glares around him, ready for enemies.

The majestic columns and mosaic patterns characteristic of this portion of Khazad-dum have here been totally destroyed. The main road continues its east-west course, but to the south a rough-hewn passageway has been brutally carved into the rock. North is a passage apparently of dwarvish origin, but from that direction comes a horrific charnel-house stench. A large portion of the roof has fallen here, and from the aperture left behind a steady flow of water drops, eventually finding its way to a narrow opening in the floor.
37770: The wide road leaps in a majestic arch over the chasm of Durin's Chimney. The large stone bridge is in excellent shape despite the many earthquakes that have shaken this area over the years. The great central column of the chim- ney -- an artificial construct engineered by the dwarves -- intersects the bridge at its midpoint, and it seems that a portion of the long stair that wound about the column at one time has survived here.
37771: A wide stone bridge crosses this chasm in a majestic arch. In the centre of the bridge, the narrow central column built by the dwarves is actually incorp- orated into the design of the bridge - splitting it as a large boulder might divide a stream. Once the entire length of Durin's Chimney was accessible by using a spiral stair that encircled the central pillar, but most of it was probably destroyed years ago. A small section seems to have survived here, however, and it may be possible to utilise the stair to access the lower levels.
37773: The majestic road to the east terminates here in a broad flight of stairs that lead down into darkness. North and south runs a smaller thoroughfare, disap- pearing in both directions into the inky blackness of the depths. The stairs are of note, because they appear to have been carved from a single block of hard black obsidian -- craftmanship not seen on Arda since the Second Age.
37774: The floor here is completely covered by blooms of blood-red algae. The air is very damp, and droplets of water bead and drop from the ceiling. The roof here looks very fragile, as the water is seeping through myriads of tiny fractures. The floor must slope imperceptibly toward the south, for the moisture seems to be draining in that direction.
37775: You are standing in a dark passage, going north-south. Moss and lichen cling to the walls, living on water dripping from the roof. The floor is quite slippery due to the thin film of water, and due to the hard, highly polished material from which the floor is constructed.
37776:
A dripping yellow fungus hangs here, clinging to the crevices and walls.
A large bat is here, hanging in the darkness.
A lurg leader of the Uruk-moragog looks at you from a bloody helm.

A large basalt block has fallen from the ceiling, revealing a dark hole from which issues a small but steady rivulet of water. The floor is covered by a shallow pool of water that seems to be draining toward the southwest through cracks in the floor. The corridor to the north appears to be damp as well, but to the east the darkness is almost palpable, blotting out all traces of light. The floor beneath the murky pool is extremely slick due to some sort of algal growth, while the walls and rubble from the ceiling have been claimed by exotic fungi of various colours.
37777: This hall is extremely dark, its black surfaces seeming to eat all light. The prevailing gloom makes it hard for one to get one's bearings, but the hall seems to continue in an east-west fashion.
37778: The darkness here is almost palpable, swallowing all light and hungering for more. The lack of visual stimuli makes it extremely difficult to become oriented -- in every direction is only the omnipresent darkness.
37779: This extremely dark hall runs east and west. The walls are of deep black stone that seems to devour light -- though the passage is at most ten metres wide, its sides are barely discernible in the gloom.

A small oaken table has been set here.

The stench here is overwhelming, arising from a pile of headless orc corpses decomposing in the southeastern corner. A rickety table in the centre of the room contains the remains of a recent meal, that, judging by the amount of blood on the table and floor, was eaten while the meat was rather fresh. Adding to the horrible atmosphere are an assortment of wicked knives and hooks probably used to torture prisoners.
37783: A battered warg fur has been left here.

This is the place where the Uruks sleep, if they sleep at all. Crudely designed beds are lined up against the eastern wall. Bits of armour, clothes and weaponry are scattered on the floor. In the middle of the room, the fur of some huge and unlucky beast lies in the filth.
37784: Several decomposing corpses, apparently once orcs, are stacked here. All the corpses are missing their heads, and there is no sign of them here. The bodies are riddled with wounds, suggesting the orcs died in combat. On the western wall a crude trellis has been erected, with several dozen scalps tied to the crosspieces in a gruesome display of the Burzruth's skill at arms. Clearly visible behind the trellis is a hole where the masonry has been shattered and removed.
37785: This narrow tunnel is has been little touched by the orcs -- except for a small section connecting with the room to the east, this place is essentially a natural chute. The floor is tilted at a steep angle down to the east, and it appears that it is possible to continue down through a hole by the eastern wall.
37786: This natural tube has been lined with crude pitons of black iron, allowing one to proceed with care both up and down. There is a steady stream of oily smoke issuing from the darkness below -- it is being steadily drawn upward.
37787: The narrow passage continues north-south here. South of here there appears to be an intersection, while to the north the passage becomes even narrower. There are piles of rubble everywhere, and sharp jagged rocks jut out from the rough-hewn walls.
37788: You are creeping along a small passage going north-south. The rocky walls are sharp and clumsily crafted, suggesting that this passage was cut after the dwarves left Khazad-dum. Faint noises can be heard from the south, but they are too soft to identify.
37789: The smell from the north is fast becoming unbearable, overpowering the nose and bringing to mind opened graves. The floor is extremely sticky and is coated with a brownish substance that could be dried blood. Bizarre eyeless insects crawl the walls and floor, seemingly feeding on the loathsome residue on the floor.
37790: The large pile of gutted corpses that almosts blocks the passageway here is probably the source of the foul, cloying odour that dominates this area. The carcasses are in various states of decay, those on top appearing freshly butchered, while those on the bottom are little more than bones surrounded by seething hordes of squirming larvae. The floor and walls seem alive with hosts of blind beetles, crawling through cracks in the floor from some horrid abyss below to feed here.

There are two disgusting elf-stews here.

The long stone tables flanked by wooden benches indicate this room was perhaps used by the dwarves as a dining hall in ages past. Unappetizing piles of smelly meat lying on the tables suggest that maybe the current inhabitants of Moria use this place in a similar manner, even though the smell of corruption coming from the corridor to the south is overwhelming. A breeze originating somewhere to the east brings with it the distinct odour of fresh blood and burning meat.

The remainders of a disgusting elf-stew cover the ground.
A rotten corpse is hanging here.

Obviously a kitchen of dwarven origin, this place is still used as a food preparation area for the orcs inhabiting this portion of Moria. Several recently butchered corpses of undetermined race are stacked against the south wall and a pile of various bodily organs lies next to the bodies, housed in a large metal basin. Some of the ovens are currently in use, for the smell of roasting meat fills the air. A strong breeze originates in a shaft above the row of ovens, clearing the room of excess smoke and carrying the aroma of cooking meat down the hall to the west.
37793: The stairs end here, levelling out into a flat passage to the west. The floor here is dingy and appears worn by frequent use. The room to the west looks to be a kitchen, perhaps accounting for the heavy use of this tunnel.
37794: You are standing on some broad and low stairs. On the right side of the stairs, there is a shallow incline probably used for dragging wagons up and down. The passage seem to be well-trodden although it does not contain any special craftmanship.
37795: Here the avenue makes a surprising bend west, going up some fairly broad and low stairs. There are tracks in the stairs, suggesting that they were used for escalating wagons of some kind. As is the case with most of this avenue, this part is not very fashionably painted or designed, but it was probably not meant to be used by the whole population. The finish on the panels on the northern wall has cracked open, revealing the underlying rock.
37796: The avenue is going north-south here. Part of the roof has fallen apart and there are some boulders spread across the floor, contributing to the overall decayed look of this avenue. It is too bad the present inhabitants apparently do not care enough for aesthetics to do some serious repairs around here.
37797: This is the beginning of a quite wide passage apparently used for service purposes, since it is not very ingeniously crafted. Plain marble panels line the walls, without any particular paintings on them. Some tracks in the floor are hardly noticeable, suggesting that wagons of kinds were rolled here when this place was inhabited by dwarves.
37798: Shallow alcoves cut into both walls of this passageway contain debris that at one time probably made up a collection of shelves and racks for storage. There are a few broken pieces of metal strewn about that suggest maybe armour and weapons were kept here. From the east a breeze is blowing, bringing with it the foetid smell of decay mixed with the hint of roasting meat. To the east a large area containing several large tables can be discerned, while westward the broad tunnel fades into the gloom.
37799: This broad passage continues its east-west course, its roof lost in the inky blackness overhead. The floor here is coated with layers of some sort of sticky substance, and from the cavernous heights above, a faint rustling can be periodically heard. From the east a soft wind brings with it the stench of putrefying meat.
37800: The floor of this place is covered in filth. Scattered about are the bones of innumerable rodents and other small animals and the whole mess is coated in an extremely sticky substance. It is impossible to make out the ceiling here, and from the darkness above a faint rustling can sometimes be heard. There is a light and steady breeze coming from the east bringing a rather strong odour of something rotting.
37801: This wide road is not as ornamental as other passages in Moria, suggesting it was used by dwarves for more mundane purposes. Westward, the road appears to end, while to the east it marches into the night. The ceiling here must be very high for the walls extend up until they are swallowed by darkness. The slightest movement here causes echoes to reverberate down the passage, and sometimes a slight rustling overhead seems to answer. From the east, a slight breeze carries with it the odour of rotting meat.
37802: The dark alley comes to a corner here, continuing both south and east. One of the large basalt blocks that make up the floor seems to be missing. In its stead a small tunnel disappears down into the rock. The unmistakable odour of decomposing flesh is being borne along by a chilly breeze originating somewhere to the east.
37803: This darkened alley continues both north and south. The black basalt of the walls and floor has been gouged and scored in several places, perhaps by vandalous orcs delighting in the destruction of beauty. A slight breeze from the north carries a hint of rotting meat.
37804: This side-passage is very dark, its surfaces made of giant dark blocks of basalt that reflect very little light. It opens into a much larger area to the south, while a faint draft is detectable flowing out of the darkness to the north.
37805: This narrow passage slopes down at a sharp angle from the floor of the hall above. Tiny rivulets of water clinging to the steep floor meander downward into the depths below, bringing nourishment to several large slimy patches of blood-red algae.

The narrow tunnel reaches its nadir here -- proceeding east or west will take you upward again. Water trickling down the passageway from the east has gathered here and formed a puddle overlying several inches of cold soupy mud. Beneath the deposit of mud cracks in the rock can be felt, none wider than a finger, which must allow the water to drain from this area.
37807: This narrow tube plunges downward at a steep angle from the floor of the dark alley above. The rough walls indicate that this passage was probably not carved by dwarves, but you cannot ascertain whether it is natural or created by the current foul inhabitants of Moria.
37808: This natural crack terminates in a hole below -- proceeding in that direction requires a drop of a little more than a metre onto a pile of rubble. A steady stream of water rushes out of the darkness from atop the incline leading west, dropping through the hole below into a pool. The floor and walls here are very slick with red algae.
37809: From here, the narrow passage drops down both east and west. The rocks are very slick in this area, due to the water steadily dropping from a tiny crack in the ceiling. The water drains in both directions, gurgling down into darkness.
37810: This narrow crack in the rock extends upward to the west at a fairly steep angle. Below is as drop of about a metre onto a pile of rubble in what seems to be a large area. The walls of this space are slick with growths of blood- red algae, and the footing here is made more treacherous by water seeping through cracks in the roof and flowing out through the opening below.

Judging by the filthy mats and scattered weaponry lying about, this room is heavily used by the orcs of this part of Moria. A circular chalk outline in the centre of the room brings to mind an arena, an impression augmented by chalk tallies crudely scrawled on the walls, perhaps serving to keep score. The corpse of a small orc, only a little over one metre in height, has been tossed in the corner, blood still seeping from a jagged wound in the abdomen.
37812: This shaft vanishes into the raven-black darkness overhead, its sides too smooth to allow one to continue upward. A brisk breeze of fresh air whistles faintly as it flows past the opening and into the room below, bringing to mind the pristine snowfields of the mountainside somewhere far above.
37813: The narrow stairway continues spiralling about the narrow pillar, desperately clinging to the masonry and refusing to break free and plunge into the dark- ness below. Looking down, there seems to be a landing of some sort, while in the gloom above, the underside of a mighty stone bridge can be discerned.
37814: A huge troll, with skin as black as pitch, glowers at you.

The wide flat stairs pause here at a landing before continuing both up and down. Piles of bones are strewn about, often cracked open and bearing the scars of great teeth-marks. From the west comes a an odour reminiscent of unwashed bodies and rotten meat, mingled together and thickening the air.

This hall has been excavated around the landing of a once-magnificent curving staircase. From the centre of the polished marble floor of the hall's west end, stone stairs rise to the west, then boldly vault upwards and toward the north as if unsupported and disappear behind an ornate screen in the northwest corner of the ceiling. In the centre of the east end of the hall, steps descend in a bold curve, east, then south; at the point where they disappear the sheer drop from the landing to the steps is about thirty yards. Along the walls are carved ornate lampstands. The ceiling, 90 feet above or more, is ornately decorated and inlaid with stones of many colours. But their beauty today is hidden behind layers of dust and cobwebs; and near the ground, the delicate carvings are smashed, the sturdier ones are chipped, and all lies strewn with foul debris. Archways leave this hall to the north and south.
37816: A broad, high-ceilinged underground avenue is met at this point by a short flight of steps, fully twenty yards wide, which leads upward and eastward into a forest of columns. While the avenue apparently once carried the main flow of traffic north and south, the northward way has by now been almost completely choked by rubble and debris.
37817: The corpse of a dark orkish archer is lying here.

Here the underground avenue turns upward and to the east, where it is abruptly blocked by a gigantic grim iron portcullis. A heavy metal post is lying here which has been used as a ram in an attempt to break it down, and someone has also attempted to excavate the stone under the portcullis. The Dwarven iron and the dark lustrous roadbed have resisted these crude efforts.
37818: You are in a hall whose high ceiling is supported by a forest of fluted columns spaced more closely together than usual. Lines of columns march away from you into the darkness in the directions of the cardinal points. To the north and south the ceiling bows down near to the floor and touches the top rank of a low tier of benches. This much is clearly Dwarven work; but the food troughs which have been placed near the centre of the room, the small bone fragments to be found everywhere, and the stench of rotting meat and worse are the work of the later occupants of this underground city.

The stench of death fills this once-handsome chamber. Perfectly proportioned, its walls, floor, and ceiling are marble of the purest white, carved in great slabs and assembled here. At the four corners are pedestals which once held great lampstands; perhaps the lamps were made of a valuable material, since they have been taken away. On a raised stone dais is a small seat, made of the same stone as the rest of the chamber. Surrounding it, corpses are arrayed on the floor. Some have been butchered; some appear to have been butchered alive. Some of the grislier carcasses have been wired to metal frameworks and seem to have been a long time dying, and then a long time dead. Most are orcs, but you believe you can recognise an elf and a dwarf, though not much is left of them.
37820: This small passage is lined by false columns of brilliant white marble and of a light blue stone. The stone is soiled and stained now, and foul writings and drawings have been scrawled on the walls. To the east the passage is terminated abruptly by a rockfall, and the walls around it are cracked and black with soot. The passage opens into a larger hall to the west, and another room opens to the south.

This chamber is about thirty feet across and carved in the shape of a hemisphere. The inner surface of the dome was carved and polished so as to display the colours of a vein of marbled quartz. Around the walls is a continuous low stone bench, and in the centre of the room is a hearth. A cool breeze from an unseen vent airs the room. This may once have been a Dwarvish place of contemplation, but it has been turned to other purposes. The hearth, which has been recently used, stinks of ash and burned fat, and is choked with burned hair, skin, and bones. Vats and pots of thick liquid, pigments of black and red, are arranged around it.
37822: A dark female of the Burzruth glares with yellow eyes at you.

Once this dark passageway was a truly magnificent hallway. The walls on either side are carved in bas-reliefs inlaid in many-coloured stones. Dwarven lords bearing the riches of Khazad-dum marched northward at stately pace in these carvings. The pattern of the gouges and pits which have been made in the stone suggest that their axe-hilts, their bracelets, their glittering eyes were depicted using real gold, gems, and truesilver. Nothing remains of this, of course.

This is an octagonal underground hall about 100 yards across with a false ceiling twenty yards high. The false ceiling is actually made of narrow criss-crossing metal beams ornamented with white marble and supporting a multitude of lamps carved in crystalline forms. Very low benches surround a central fountain. All walls but the west are smoothly polished, but the west wall is unadorned and rough. In its centre a low tunnel leads into the blackness.
37824: A spacious corridor, six feet high and fifteen broad, leads north and south here. The floor is tiled with red, black, and white marble in a hexagonal pattern, which can hardly be made out because of the silt and sand which have been tracked in over the years.
37825: This room, 120 feet long, was once a great reception hall or salon for an important personage. Perhaps it was later used for another purpose; there are the remains of railings and notices which suggest that the public came here in large numbers. It is difficult to divine much in the room's state of devastation. Carvings, designs, and runes have been smashed or defaced; fragments of elegantly and delicately carved stone seats and tables are strewn about.
37826: A broad hallway widens here before a large bronze door to the east, making a space which in ages past was occupied by Dwarven guards; stone weapons racks on the north and south walls attest to this. The space serves the same function today. Pelts and wads of cloth - which may once have been shimmering tapestries - have been thrown down for orkish guards to lounge upon. Obscene black scrawling on the walls suggests that they have frequently been bored and searching for amusement.

This great chamber was once the living and sleeping quarters of a great Dwarven lord. The massive soapstone sleeping-couches on which he and his household took their relaxation are still to be found here. Today they are furnished with sacks of sand; with cloths and parchments looted from elsewhere in the city; with mangy pelts and skins, some from four-footed things, some not. A reek of sweat and excreta makes it clear that this room is frequently used.
37828: This east-west passage seems to be an undistinguished mine tunnel, long abandoned. However, midway along its length, a line of heavy marble blocks about 15 inches in height has been placed along the south wall; here also the north wall has been polished flat, and some lines of runes carved carefully in the rock.
37829: A broad underground avenue extends to the north, and at one time must have continued to the south, descending slightly. However, the southward passage is completely blocked, as the passageway is choked with mud and sand. From a broad transverse crack in the ceiling, a curtain of water smelling of foul rot drips mournfully, making rivulets in the soil which chokes the floor and ultimately disappearing into an undetectable crevice. During past flood times, this leak must have brought down enough sandy debris to choke the descending tunnel. There are many large footprints in the sand, and the tracks seem to lead to a crack in the avenue's east wall.
37830: A once-magnificent staircase leads upward and downward from this partly collapsed chamber. From the centre of the polished marble floor of the hall's west end, stone stairs ascend westward, then curve in mid-air toward the south and disappear through the high ceiling. Huge boulders choke the east end of the hall, but it is possible to follow the stairway downward and northward where it curves under the fallen stone. The floor of the room is littered with shattered ornamental stonework which has fallen from the ceiling. An archway is to be found at the west end of this hall.
