This great ten-sided hall, two hundred forty feet across, contains enough stone benches and long tables to accommodate hundreds of dwarves. The walls are low but the ceiling rises into a vaulted dome about sixty feet high. Ventilation grates can be seen in the centre of the ceiling and in the walls. The rock of the ceiling has been polished to highlight the contrast between the deep blue- grey stone and a vein of mingled white and rose which branches from the south in an intricate pattern. At the east end of the room, a pile of debris indicates that the new lords of Moria have established a guardpost here.
37832: A great cast-iron stove dominates this room, stretching the entire length of the north wall. The ash in its firebox suggests that it would burn either wood or coal; but cobwebs and rats' nests testify that it has burned neither for many long years. Cabinets along the south wall are looted and vacant. A trickle of water dribbles from a pipe that emerges from the west wall, splashes into a basin in the floor, and disappears down a drain.
37833: A broad east-west corridor, whose walls are carved and inlaid in a geometric pattern, and which has been built with the cross-section of a low, broad arch, penetrates the stone here. There are no doors or side passages. A thin layer of dust covers the floor; all is stillness and darkness.
37834: The broad corridor continues eastward and westward from here. The dark stone of the walls has been carved with a pattern of rectangles within rectangles, which subtly changes form and the inlaid stones of which alter their color as the furlongs pass. Otherwise there is little to break the monotony. The air does seem to move gently westward through the corridor.

You are on the stub of a broken bridge that once carried the east-west road across a great abyss which stretches endlessly above and below you. All around you is black and empty. A low moaning suffuses the void as warmer air blows up from below and ascends past you. This must be Durin's Chimney, the great vertical shaft known to lore that ascends from the depths to the heights of Zirakzigil. Perhaps it is possible to cross this chasm elsewhere, but this shattered span leads only to oblivion.
37836: A dark orkish archer is wielding a very vicious-looking bow.

This tunnel, faced in precise but simple style with cream-coloured stone, leads north and south. There are large cracks in the ceiling, walls, and floor, evidence of the great tremors that have taken place in the heart of Zirakzigil.
37839: You are on a curving stairway that ascends northward from here, curving to the east. Below you, to the south, the passage has been completely blocked by a great wall of stone. In some monstrous earthquake of the past, part of the mountain's roots themselves have shifted, cutting off this passage as with a knife's blade. The walls and the steps are themselves riven with cracks.
37840: This room may once have been a bath or ceremonial pool. A trickle of clean water runs from a spout in the shape of a dragon's head and pours into a stone depression which occupies most of the rectangular high-ceilinged chamber. The basin is full, now, of rotten stuff, remnants of carcasses, dead bats, bones, and excreta. The stench is overpowering. Within the basin, you can hear unpleasant slitherings and slurpings, as filth-eating creatures burrow and eat. The drain of the pool has been blocked, and the overflow has flooded the floor in the eastern part of the chamber with a stinking brown liquid.

This broad corridor is literally buried in a mixture of gravel and stinking muck. The gravel has apparently been brought here in sacks and on litters, some of which are lying here on the central pathway. The occupants of the ruined city have apparently given this area over to the growing of some sort of fungus. A trickle of stinking brown water enters the corridor from the west and flows through furrows in the "soil".
37842:
There are four bulbous mushrooms here.
There are two fleshy fungi here.
A dark orkish archer is wielding a very vicious-looking bow.
A dark female of the Burzruth glares with yellow eyes at you.
A dark female of the Burzruth glares with yellow eyes at you.
A dark female of the Burzruth glares with yellow eyes at you.
A dark female of the Burzruth glares with yellow eyes at you.
A dark female of the Burzruth glares with yellow eyes at you.
A dark female of the Burzruth glares with yellow eyes at you.
A dark orc crouches quietly, staring into the distance.
A dark orkish archer is wielding a very vicious-looking bow.

The floor of this east-west corridor is largely buried in a sort of "soil" made of gravel and foul refuse. The air is humid and heavy with the smell of waste. Brown water dribbles down furrows from the west and percolates into the soil. Once-handsome doors line the north and south walls of the passage, but as they are hinged to open outward they cannot be budged due to the obstructing dirt.
37843: The corpse of a Burzruth female is lying here.

This dark room, whose floor is awash in brown muck, contains ten stone worktables, small even by the standards of Dwarvish furniture, each abutted by very small seating-rails. A larger chair, now broken and overturned, stood near the west end of the room. The walls were originally ornamented with murals of Dwarven historical scenes, but the details have been scraped away or buried under vile smearings. A line of runes can be dimly seen near the top of the south wall.
37844: This part of the corridor is mostly unencumbered with gravel and muck, although its smooth floor is slippery with muck which has been tracked in from the west. Prints of boots and of naked, clawed feet are visible in the mud. The passage is less ornate here than to the west, and it proceeds for a long distance without encountering side passages or doors.
37845: This is the northern end of a large storage area. A line of sturdy columns supporting the ceiling runs north and south through its centre. Metal shelves and bins line the walls. The floor is littered with trash - shards of pots, rotten grain, bits of glass, empty flasks. Nothing of value can possibly remain here, a thousand years after the dwarves who filled this room with their goods were driven from their home.
37846: This is the southern end of a large storage area. Everything here has been looted long ago. There are wet, muddy tracks on the floor, and a cooler, fresher air blows from a ventilation grille high up on the southern wall. Overturned shelves, upset bins, and smashed urns and flagons clutter the eastern side of the chamber.
37847:
A strange bat-like creature is flitting around (hidden).
A strange bat-like creature is flitting around.
A strange bat-like creature is flitting around.
A strange bat-like creature is flitting around.
A strange bat-like creature is flitting around (hidden).
A strange bat-like creature is flitting around (hidden).
A strange bat-like creature is flitting around.

You are on a precarious ledge in a vertical shaft about 30 feet across. Downward it extends into total darkness; above you it ascends straight up for about fifty feet and then turns sharply east. There is no way to climb the sheer walls above you, but looking down you see a thin ladder descending the west wall of the shaft. The cool air blows downward from above; from below, shrill squeaking cries can be heard.
37848:
A huge troll is here, fighting Bulg (pukespy).
Bulg (pukespy), wielding a great warsword, is here, fighting a huge troll.
Ducaht (tooprettytodie), wielding a great warsword, is here, fighting a huge troll.
Klaees (thedon), wielding a heavy morningstar, is here, fighting a huge troll.
Drazud (freshmeat), wielding a great warsword, is here, fighting a huge troll.

This was once the southeast corner of a broad open space, the ceiling of which was supported by parallel ranks of sturdy granite columns. Now the roof has slumped, crushing and splintering the supports and littering the room with their broken sections; but it has not completely collapsed as yet. The floor is covered with stinking muck and a brownish fluid, and there is an overpowering stench of waste. Strange high-pitched cries are heard from the darkness in the corners of the room and behind the piles of broken stone.
37849: The roof of this open area has largely collapsed, and the floor is choked with the remains of its supporting columns. It is also covered with brownish muck and with chunks of bone and flesh. Thighs, skulls, jawbones, ribs, and armbones, some picked clean, some still bearing chunks of flesh, are scattered in the filth. The odours of rot and waste give the humid air an indescribable heaviness.
37850: The former lineaments of this area have been eradicated by the collapse of the roof. There is now only a jumble of stone, some of it slabs from the ceiling, much of it the remains of the supporting columns. The floor itself is completely buried. Everywhere there are bones and the remains of carcasses, some headless, some devoid of viscera, some dismembered; but all of which once walked on two legs. There are bloated troll corpses, and some others which look more like orcs, although they have been much changed by rot and by consumption. The air is thick with the stenches of blood, of rot, of waste.
37851: A broad plaza or assembly hall once extended north and east of here; but it has largely collapsed. The floor is hidden by thick stinking brown muck and by mostly stagnant pools of yellowish-brown fluid. Bones and pieces of orc and troll carcasses are scattered everywhere, as well as a multitude of tiny bones and fragments which seem to have come from bats. From the darkness around you are heard peculiar piping wails and snarls.
37852:
Bulg (pukespy), wielding a great warsword, is standing here.
Ducaht (tooprettytodie), wielding a great warsword, is standing here.
Klaees (thedon), wielding a heavy morningstar, is standing here.
Drazud (freshmeat), wielding a great warsword, is standing here.

This is the interior of a narrow and unspeakably filthy waste pipe. Water and stinking sludge pour down upon you from above, soaking your hair and garments, and splash down into the blackness below you. Fortunately there are enough cracks and irregularities in the walls of the pipe that it is not difficult for you to keep your footing and to move up and down.
37853: Here, where the road makes a sharp south-west bend, a stream of foul-smelling water flows from a wide irregular hole in a circular standpipe. The pool that it forms contains unmistakable and unpleasant clots of excrement. Broken chunks of the standpipe's casing lie here and there, and it seems as though the hole was deliberately made. There is little else to see here.
37854: At this dark and silent junction three ways meet. A hard-surfaced road from the west curves northward and is met by a corridor coming from the east. There is little ornamental carving here, though there is a sconce in the southern wall which used to light this intersection. The air is pervaded by an odour of body waste.
37855: This is a corridor in part of the Fifth Deep of ruined Khazad-dum which has somehow survived the convulsions that followed the release of Durin's Bane. The doors along it seem to lead mainly to once-comfortable Dwarven residences. The pavement is polished, though not inlaid with marble. A layer of dust has been disturbed by footprints - maybe a century ago, maybe more recently.
37856: This is a Dwarven residence, simple but not shabby. In essence it is a tunnel delved northward into the stone to a depth of about 60 feet and broken up into three areas by partitions. At the northern end is a broad niche which must have served as a wall-bed. There is ornamental carving in a band along the walls about eye level (for a Dwarf). Everything movable, however, has been looted from here long ago.
37857: A modest north-south corridor has been severed here by a great crack or fault in the mountain's stone foundations. The fissure is too wide to cross, especially as the lip of the passage opposite seems to have mostly collapsed into the abyss. Only darkness can be seen above and below.
37858: A great crack in the stone of the mountain's foundation runs east and west here, rising high above your head and descending deep below your feet into the blackness. A whiff of warm, pungent air arises from below. You support yourself by wedging your body between the north and south walls of the fissure and must take care to avoid either being stuck between them or (where they are farther apart) plummeting down to search for the great crevice's bottom.
37859: Vertical fissures lead east, west, and north from this location. Formed in some great subterranean earthquake, each is barely wide enough to pass through but rises far overhead and has no bottom you can see. You must support yourself by using the tiniest footholds and by wedging yourself between the walls. One must pick one's way carefully between the irregular walls, avoiding places where the crevice becomes too narrow to pass, forcing one to laboriously retrace one's steps.
37860: You are supporting yourself between the vertical walls of a fissure which cuts through the rock of the mountain in a north-south direction. The rock of the walls is a drab grey. There is a dank aroma in the air here.
37861: You are travelling in a vertical fissure which runs east and west here. Above you it disappears in unclimbable blackness; below it sheerly descends farther than you can make out. You must support yourself on handholds and footholds in the fissure's walls, as there is no path or indeed any horizontal surface. The fissure is quite narrow, so even if you were to fall there is little danger of your plummeting to your death. No, the likelihood is that you would be wedged between the fissure's walls, there to die of thirst or suffocation.
37862:
Bulg (pukespy), wielding a great warsword, is standing here.
Ducaht (tooprettytodie), wielding a great warsword, is standing here.
Klaees (thedon), wielding a heavy morningstar, is standing here.
Drazud (freshmeat), wielding a great warsword, is standing here.

You are in a wider part of a crevice which travels upward from here at a steep southward slant. Below and to the west the crevice diminishes to a crack, large enough, perhaps, to house rats. There is little to see, as whichever way you go your face is virtually pressed into the rock wall.
37863: A hard-surfaced road ascending from the east here meets a more ornately decorated ceremonial road from the west. To the north is a broad gateway which is sealed by immense bronze doors. The carving on the doors has been marred and gouged; you gather that it was engraved with scenes of battle, but cannot make out much more.
37864: This is a point where three handsome arched passageways meet, each with its own great bronze door. The stones of the arches are decorated with a rayed pattern, and the floor is paved with exceptionally large polished slabs of pink and white marble.
37865: A broad stairway whose treads are paved in a very lustrous black stone descends into this broad room from above and to the west. The stair is cluttered with stone, however, and a glance reveals that the stairway itself is completely choked with large stones, some of which seem imminently ready to break loose, roll down the stair, and crush anyone beneath. The walls of the room are decorated with false columns, and there are archways to the north and south with great bronze doors.
37866: Here the east-west road widens and flattens, becoming a plain underground chamber. A curtain of chains is raised above the eastern exit; if it were lowered, it would effectively obstruct passage on the road. To the north, a stall can be seen containing the windlass which operated the curtain. There is a metal hatch on the floor of the stall, and there are benches along the sides of the chamber where porters and haulers would wait while their cargoes were being inspected and tallied.
37867: An underground road surfaced in a smooth black stone runs east and west here. The walls of the passage are not ornamented, and the vaulted ceiling is dark and unreflective. There is a light coating of dust on the floor, which billows up in black acrid clouds as you pass; it resembles ash more than ordinary dust.
37868: The sloping tunnel curves here, downward to the east, upward to the north. A rivulet of filthy water flows along the inside of the bend. The air here is hot and acrid; numerous smells mingle, not least the stench of waste associated with the foul stream and its cargo, but also the aromas of smoke, of rot, of burned things. At the outside of the curve, a narrow metal ladder ascends.
37869: The smooth-surfaced tunnel makes a broad curve here, sloping upward into the blackness to the east and downward to the south. A stinking rivulet runs down the tunnel, covering the floor with a foul and slippery muck.
37870: The dark underground roadway slopes sharply downward to the west here, and is rather slick due to the sludge carried by the rivulet which runs down from above. The air currents in the tunnel shift and sway; from time to time a breath of hot, drier air blows up from below, bringing with it an acrid, ashen smell.
37871: Here the passage descending from the west becomes a reeking cesspool. A makeshift dam of stone no more than a foot high has been built to block off the rivulet from above and divert its filthy water into a northward-leading tunnel. Above the dam the water has deposited its load of ill-smelling muck. There are few places for lamps along the passage, and it must never have been really bright; but now it is very black indeed. The walls are stained with soot and seem to defeat the power of vision.
37872: This was once an armoury in the days when dwarves dwelt in peace here. The dirty stream which has been diverted into this room from the south has formed a vile pool here. There is apparently a drain in the floor, and you hear water trickle and splash far below you, but it must be largely clogged by sludge. Some broken and rusted metal pieces lie rotting in the water; any valuable items were taken from here ages ago. There are some shapeless pits in the muck, resembling footprints.
37873: This is the western end of Hwain's Way, the long corridor that leads to the King's chambers, armouries and smithies in the Seventh Deep, below the East Gate of Khazad-dum. Above you Hwain's Way ends in an intersection, while to the east the corridor runs - you might think forever - straight, smooth and gradually descending into the darkness.
37874: A broad tunnel descends steadily from west to east. This seems to have been an important road; the hard stone of its surface has survived the abuse of the centuries. The walls are marked by simple columns carved in relief, which no one has thought worth while to destroy.
37875: A large and seemingly endless corridor continues its long way through the lower levels of Khazad-dum. The floor shows signs of great usage in the past, but since the appearance of Durin's Bane, it would seem that traffic has virtually ceased. The same can be said for maintainance, for the passage of time has opened innumerable small cracks in the walls and floor.
37876: In this intersection the long corridor known as Hwain's Way bends from the west to the southeast, where it continues its slow descent towards the King's chambers. A secondary passage to the north abandons the main road and disappears in the distance.
37877: A lurg leader, with markings of the Durghash tribe, stands here.

This is one of the many intersections of Hwain's Way with some other lesser tunnel. The main corridor continues its long descent from the northwest to the southeast; from the entrance to the side passage, to the east, comes a cold and damp air current that chills your bones and carries a strange smell.
37878: You have reached a bend in the long corridor that connects the western sections of Khazad-dum to the King's Chambers, the deepest levels of the old Dwarven city. Hwain's Way seems to go on endlessly both to the east and to the northwest.
37879: An ornate doorway in the northern wall contrasts sharply with the usually featureless walls of the interminable corridor that extends itself to the west and the east. The smell coming from the north, and the crude symbols scratched in coal on the wall, also contrast with the elegance of the Dwarven portal.
37880: The long corridor known as Hwain's Way stretches its way in a west-east direction. Both to the west and to the east, the otherwise featureless rough walls of the tunnel are interrupted by intersections. You can sometimes hear strange growling sounds coming from the west. Who, or what, is making those noises is not certain: their source, however, is not likely to be friendly towards intruders.
37881: You are standing at a T junction between two important corridors. One, that runs as usual from the west to the east, is Hwain's Way. The other corridor, which begins behind a portal on the northern wall, climbs gently and soon bends to the east. The latter corridor's name was forgotten in the years since the awakening of the Valarauko, but, judging from its size, it must have had some importance.
37882: As you stop to remove a small stone from your boot, you begin to realise how long the way from Hollin to Eastern Moria is. Hwain's Way, with its straight walls full of small cracks, seems to continue forever. You might think that your attempt to reach the Deeps, or to return to Hollin, is doomed to failure, and that you will spend the rest of eternity walking along this endless corridor.
37883: You are standing in the middle of a large corridor below the Misty Mountains. As you look west and east you cannot see the end of the tunnel; you are amazed at the skill of the Dwarven miners of old, who managed to create such a large complex of tunnels and to make it possible to live inside them without suffocating. Yet, the same tunnels that once were used to extract the priceless mithril from the roots of the Misties, are now home to a host of orcs - who might take you by surprise any time!
37884: Your footsteps echo in the vast emptiness of the large corridor known as Hwain's Way. The tunnel continues straight as far as you can see to the west, towards West Door, and to the east, where it descends towards what once were the King's chambers and armoury. A smaller passage in the northern wall leads to an ascending spiral staircase not too far away, and beyond, where it gradually disappears in the darkness.
37885: The worn grey steps of a long and large spiral stair lead up from here. At the base of the stair tunnels leave north and south. The southern passage is rather short, and soon joins a much larger corridor, while the tunnel to the north vanishes behind a bend after a few metres. The ground is cracked, as if a mighty hammer had struck it violently: as you move, you are careful not to stumble and sprain an ankle.
37886: Some tough lichen grows on the rocks.

You are walking along a large tunnel, running from the east to the west, and gently descending. The tunnel walls and floor are smooth, while the ceiling's shape is a little irregular. A smaller, twisting passage leads south; its ceiling is wet with small drops of water, the floor is slippery and the air there is humid, as if the water of some subterranean river permeated the pores of the rock.
37887: A pair of tiny eyes gleam at you from the shadows.

You have reached a junction along Hwain's Way. The large corridor, as usual, continues its slow descent to the east and ascent to the west; a smaller passage leaves north. The air coming from the northern passage is cooler than the air in the main tunnel, and slightly damper. To the east Hwain's Way seems to have been partly blocked off.
37888: Many huge, cracked blocks of grey stone fell to the ground when the ceiling of this section of Hwain's Way collapsed, hundreds of years ago. Now, as the gravel crackles below your weary feet, you watch carefully the irregularly shapen boulders, since they all seem on the verge of toppling down and squishing you to death in the process. Yet, if you want to cross to the other side, the only visible way lies through the menacing rocks.
37889: You are standing in the middle of a seemingly endless large corridor, which stretches itself in a more or less west to east direction. The air here is hot; from time to time, a jet of even hotter air blows on your face from a merely noticeable crack in the wall. Some tens of meters to the west, your way towards Hollin and the light of the Sun has partially collapsed.
37890: You are walking along a corridor which seems to continue forever its straight path in a west-east direction, slowly climbing to the west. A smaller tunnel leads north and soon bifurcates into what looks like a minerary area. From the west, if you stand still and are silent, you can sometimes hear some harsh sounds. Are they voices, heavy steps, or something else? You will have to investigate more directly to know.
37891: You have reached a crossroads. To the west and east, the large corridor known as Hwain's Way stretches his way seemingly forever; to the south, a tunnel leads up inside a mining area. Finally, to the north, behind a slender arch carved in the grey stone surrounding you, lies a small chamber. You can feel some strange smell coming out of the chamber, but you cannot guess what might be its source.
37892: The long corridor that connects the West Door of Moria to the Deeps below East Gate is crossing a minerary area. As usual, Hwain's Way proceeds in a west-east direction, slowly descending as it approaches the eastern part of Moria. On both sides of this huge corridor you can see many small passages leading up. Many of the side tunnels have been closed off, but some still remain open.
37893:
The corpse of a mountain mule is lying here.
A hefty stone club is on the ground.
A hefty stone club is on the ground.

The old tunnel, which was once one of the most used connections between the City of Moria and Moria's West Door, is approaching a wide shaft as it slowly descends towards the Deeps. The air becomes cooler as one walks towards the chimney, and the oppressive smell of Moria's denizens lessens, as if an air current from the outside were carrying the heat and the stench away. Yet, the relative absence of orkish smell is not reassuring, as the noise of clanking boots can still be heard, sometimes faintly, sometimes more strongly.
37894: One of the most amazing architectural feats in Khazad-dum (and therefore in Arda) suddenly reveals itself to all travelers who, having walked for a long time on Hwain's Way, finally reach the Chimney of Durin. An extremely vast chasm, running north, south, up and down as far as the eye can see, sunders the mining part of Moria from the city's levels and deeps. Connecting the western and eastern side of the abyss, a lattice of proud stone bridges almost fills the empty space between the sheer-dropping cliffs. A slim stone tower stands in the middle of the chasm, its foundations at the roots of Arda, its summit among the peaks of the Misty Mountains; a spiral stair winds around it. Unfortunately, the cataclismatic awakening of the Balrog severely damaged this place. Most of the bridges, including all those leading to the central tower, have collapsed; most of the tunnels ending in the Chimney have been blocked. This is not so, however, for Hwain's Way, which continues to the east and west. A ledge also allows to flank the western side of the abyss.
37895: This is the northern end of a ledge on the western side of an incredibly wide and deep chasm. The ancient granite cliffs on both sides of the abyss are dotted with tunnel exits, most of which seem to have been closed off. With a marvelous feat of engineering, the Khazad built many arched stone bridges, connecting one side of the chasm to the other. Currently, alas, most of the bridges have collapsed, leaving only their truncated extremities as a monument to the Dwarves' skill. A rare exception is the stout bridge east of here.
37896: You have reached the eastern side of Durin's Chimney, a wide and deep chasm separating the mines of Khazad-dum from the halls of the old Dwarven city. With an enormous effort, the Dwarven artisans once shaped the granite walls of this place, building bridges to connect the tunnel endings on the two sides. A slender, extremely elegant, cylindrical tower stands in the middle of the Chimney, rising from unknown depths to heights far beyond the reach of your eyesight. Stone steps, meant to give access to all of Moria's levels and deeps, circle around the pillar. Unfortunately, as time passed, most of the bridges crumbled and collapsed: there is no way to reach the tower from here, nor is it possible to climb up and down to other levels. The only functional bridge in the proximity leads west: it is part of Hwain's Way. Other bridges might be found by following a narrow ledge to the north.
37898: You have entered what was once a vast complex of interconnecting minerary tunnels. Now many of the galleries have collapsed, and there is no ore to be seen anywhere. The only exits that have survived the ravages of time lead to a large corridor to the south, and to a chamber to the west.
37899: The first thing you notice when entering this room is a huge, nearly vertical shaft, placed roughly in the middle of the chamber. Some small recesses have been chiselled in the walls of the pit, so that it is possible to climb it down. A large stone block, which perhaps closed off the shaft, now lies broken into pieces in a corner. Exits lead in all directions; the southern one is larger than the others and crosses a corridor not far away, the northern one ascends rapidly.
37900: You are in the middle of a maze of small minerary tunnels. Here the main tunnel bends west and south; to the west the floor ascends steeply, while the southern exit slopes gently downwards to a chamber. As you look at the walls, you realise that the miners almost completed their work here before abandoning this place, since there is nearly no trace of useful ore.
37901: You are walking along a narrow minerary tunnel in the depths of Moria. To the south this passage joins a much larger gallery; to the east it ends in a small chamber. All traces of mineral ore seem to have vanished from here a long time ago.
37902: You are at the edge of a vast complex of small and twisted minerary tunnels. The Dwarves who dug them extracted almost all of the ore in this section of Khazad-dum, before the Bane of Durin forced them to flee. The tunnels go on to the west and the south, while to the north you can leave these narrow mines and enter a large and straight corridor running from the west to the east.
37903: Here a narrow mine tunnel turns north, where it meets a much larger gallery, and west, where it bifurcates into dozens of small passages. You can sometimes hear the faint thumping of footsteps in the distance, and you wonder who, apart from you, might be wandering along the tunnels of Moria.
37904: Small tunnels surround you in all directions, but most of them, as you explore them, turn out to be dead ends - either because the Dwarves reached the end of the ore vein, or because of a cave-in. The main tunnel leads north and west from here, descending to the north and ascending to the west.
37905: You have reached the bottom of a narrow stairway, whose worn steps, roughly cut in the grey stone, lead up and westwards. To the east and north, minerary tunnels lead away in the darkness. The tunnel to the north is larger than the other, and nearly horizontal, while the eastern tunnel slopes downwards.
37906: You are in the middle of a long, nearly straight tunnel, running north to south. As you walk, you can hear the faint echo of your steps coming from both ends of this gallery. Yet this is not the only sound you can perceive: sometimes, even when you stop, something - it might be the noise of heavy boots marching on the stone, but you are not sure - reaches your ears.
37907: You have the distinct feeling that you have walked through these small tunnels for hours and hours now. Many passages look alike, and you have been forced to retrace your steps - due to a blocked passage - dozens of times. At last, you come to a chamber from which four major galleries depart. One leads west, sloping upwards. The second is the largest, and leads almost horizontally to the south. The third tunnel descends steeply to the east. Finally, the northern exit is blocked by a pile of rubble.
37908: Following the main tunnel, you have reached a Y junction. The mines continue to the north and east, while a third branch, to the southwest, ends abruptly with an extremely large and seemingly bottomless chasm. A jet of hot air flows from the depths of the earth, and makes you sweat.
37909: Dozens and dozens of small, twisted passages worm their way through the hard rock of the depths of Moria in all directions. As far as you can see, the Dwarves have followed the ore vein and all of its ramifications until no useful materials remained around. After exploring the tunnels, you realise that many of them have been closed off, or rejoin each other after a few tens of meters. The main ways out lie to the west, to the south and to the east; the exits all look alike to your eyes.
37910: At this point the tunnel you have been following becomes very narrow, so that in certain places you have to squeeze yourself between the rocky wall and a pile of debris. To the south the mine ends in a small room; a bifurcation can be seen near you to the east.
37911: A narrow stairway crosses this small room. The steps descend to the east and climb westwards into the darkness. A passage leads to a mine gallery to the north, while, to the south, another tunnel has been sealed by a cave-in, perhaps centuries ago, when the Dwarves were forced to abandon this place.
37912: You are in the middle of a network of small tunnels, leading in all directions. Many of the tunnels, though, have been sealed by cave-ins or large holes on the floor. The main gallery here leads north to south, but a few meters south of here a large pile of debris blocks the way. The only secondary tunnel in decent shape lies to the west.
37913: This place looks like the edge of a large network of minerary tunnels. To the west a large passage slopes gently upwards; its floor was worn by the passage of many loads of unrefined ore. Three tunnels led once to the south; now, one of them has collapsed, while a very large chasm prevents you from entering the second. As you look at the tunnel walls, you realise that there is very little ore left here.
37914: You have reached the top of a smooth-walled tunnel which slopes down gently to the south. A rougher tunnel, nearly horizontal, leaves east, entering a maze of smaller caves, while a short, straight stair leads up to a tiny room. The gentle sound of flowing water comes from above.
37915: The main passage here bends north and west, while a secondary tunnel plunges down to the south. Cold air blows through this latter tunnel, whistling a strange sound. The western tunnel slopes down gently, while to the north the corridor rises somewhat more steeply.
37916: You are walking along a large tunnel deep below the peaks of Caradhras. The corridor gently descends to the west and climbs to the east. Gusts of hot air blow into your face from some small cracks in the floor and walls.
37917: The main corridor, climbing from the west to the east, meets here another passage which goes north for a little while and then turns left. You can sometimes hear a booming noise, similar to the sound of a large drum, and loud cries in the distance. You recall hearing dreadful tales about the orc tribes populating the halls of Khazad-dum: life under the shadow of Durin's Bane has made these orcs particularly vicious and cruel.
37918: Some tough lichen grows on the rocks.

This is the western end of a large, smooth-walled passage that climbs gently to the east. As you look around, you see that, to the south, the passage meets a larger corridor - probably Hwain's Way, the main road from West Door to the Seventh Deep of Eastern Moria. Water drips slowly from a crack in the ceiling. The crack is larger than many other cracks you have seen, but it would be impossible to force your way through.
37919: A sharp turn in the passage is dominated by a huge statue of a Dwarf, placed in a niche to the northeast. The once elegant marble of the statue has been defiled by orkish scrawlings, and its arms lie in pieces at the bottom of the niche. The soft stone walls of the corridor run west and south.
37920: The cracked soft stone walls of this narrow corridor seem to grow nearer as you proceed in your journey, giving you a feeling of claustrophobia. If you stop for a moment and listen, you can hear a thumping noise in the distance, similar to the marching of many heavy boots. The tunnel is still running in a west-east direction.
37921: The ancient walls of this narrow passage stretch themselves from the west to the east. From time to time you bruise your arms against a protuberance in the soft, cracked grey stone which surrounds you; this prevents you from falling prey to the hypnotic effect of the seemingly endless walls.
37922: You are standing at the western end of a long, but rather narrow, corridor. There are many small cracks on the walls of soft stone. The corridor goes on to the east; to the north it joins a damp passage.
37923: Three tunnels meet here, in the depths of Moria. The southern one is larger than the others and dry, while the passages to the north and west are damp. A very strong smell of decay pervades this place, and seems to get even stronger to the north.
37924:
There are two fleshy fungi here.
Some tough lichen grows on the rocks.

As you proceed inside this tunnel, the air becomes even more damp and unbreathable than before. The stone below your feet is slippery because of a very thin layer of water. As you look around, you realise that the source of the smell of decay you noticed before lies here: the stench comes from a pile of semidecomposed orc corpses. Above the grisly sight there is an inscription. The tunnel continues south and east.
37925: Some tough lichen grows on the rocks.

The tunnel here bends rather sharply west and south. A current of damp air comes from the west, carrying the stench of decay, and plunges into a narrow crack in the floor. Water trickles down from many small stalactites with a loud, reverberating sound.
37926: You are standing in a small secondary tunnel, which climbs slowly to the north. Cold, humid air blows through nearly invisible fissures in the old cave walls, chilling you to the bones. South of here the tunnel becomes slightly larger, and bends westwards.
37927: This is the southern end of a small corridor which climbs slowly to the north. The air coming from the tunnel is stale, humid and carries a strange smell. To the west, the corridor joins a much large passage, which, if what you heard about Khazad-dum is correct and if your sense of direction does not betray you, should be Hwain's Way, a large road which crosses all of Moria from the west to the east.
37928: The narrow space of this cleft in the rock makes movement difficult and slow. The walls of this crevice are very wet due to the rivulets of water which snake down the surfaces of the crack from above. This water collects in the narrow bottom of the crevice and flowing as a small stream descends eastwards. A strong air current blows down the length of the crack.
37929: A body of water fills this cove. The surface of the water lies undisturbed with only a few small waves lapping against the craggy walls. To the north the dark lake disappears into a large cavern. A breach in the west wall of the cove leads to a crevice which recedes into the stone. A trickle of water enters the lake from the floor of the crevice and a soft breeze also enters through this cleft.
37930: Still and dark, the waters of this underground lake look cold and uninviting. Nary a sound can be heard, and the quiet splashes you make echo off the high rocks of this chamber. To the east and north the glassy waters continue while the rough rocks of a wall lie west. To the south the cavern becomes smaller, the high ceiling descending towards the waters of a cove.
37931: In the roots of the mountain, the waters of the lake lie still, cold and dark. Within its surface you can see your reflection but the depths are obscured by suspensions underwater. Occasionally a solitary drip can be heard as water falls from the few, small stalactites and stone promontories above. To the west and north the huge cavern ends, and the rocky walls of the cave are gently lapped. East and south the lake stretches out beyond your perceptions.
37932: A rocky ledge protruding from the northern wall lies just below the surface of the lake, providing respite for those weary of swimming. The otherwise calm surface of the lake is disturbed by the uprising of water from below. Down, deep below, murky plumes of silt carried by the currents upwell and disperse gradually, flowing slowly to the southern parts of the lake. The western reaches of the lake lie dark and silent, few drops ever falling to break the quiet.
37933: This is a corner of the lake-immersed cavern which stretches north and east. Slow currents below the surface deposit their suspensions deep on the lake floor. The flow south suggests that an underwater outflow drains the waters from the lake, though no sign of an exit is visible. The slippery walls of the cavern to the south and east are impossible to scale, rising as they do towards a distant rocky ceiling. Water occasionally drops from above but otherwise no sound is heard.
37938: You stand near the southwestern corner of a large, vaulted hall. The walls and floor are of a polished stone blue-greenish in hue. The hall stretches away north and east, receding into the gloomy murk. The western wall is dominated by a grand avenue's entrance, framed by twin columns sculpted to resemble dwarven lords.
37939: The large vaulted hall you stand in is dominated by a wide avenue entering from the west. Stretching away on all other sides, the hall fades into the gloom. To the east, at the centre of the room, lies the well that gives the name to this ancient chamber.
37940: The northwestern corner of the hall is covered in a thin, dark dust, somewhat unusual down here. Tracks of creatures large and small are faintly visible in it, but give no clue to their makers any longer. Hwain's Well lies to the southeast.
37941: The northern wall of this large hall is broken by a once grandly arched entrance of an avenue. The pillars, now defaced, have lost their glory and stand ragged and battered like rotting teeth. The hall stretches away into the gloom in all other directions.
37942: You find yourself in the northwestern corner of a huge vaulted hall. The walls are of a very strange blue-greenish colour, as is the floor. A steady current of warm air, carrying the stench and the war cries of Morgoth's servants, blows in your face from a dark avenue to the east.
37943: You are standing at the eastern entrance to the large vaulted chamber known as Hwain's Well Hall. The Well, which is the reason for the hall's name, lies to the west, in the middle of the room; the hall extends itself both to the north and to the south, while to the east a corridor goes straight on to the extreme reach of your sight.
37944: Bones, bones, bones everywhere. The pile of skulls, femurs and ribcages in this corner of Hwain's Well Hall is truly enormous. Skeletons of all sizes, of animals, of dwarves, of humans and even of trolls lie here, all massed together. Evidently whoever lives here, after satisfying his huge hunger by eating whatever and whomever was available, tossed here the remains. Hwain's Well Hall goes on to the north and west.
37945: A roughly square vaulted hall, which the Dwarves dug from a lode of a strange blue-greenish rock, lies north of you. In the centre of the chamber there is a huge well, surrounded by a thick parapet. The smell of decay comes from a large pile of bones in the southeastern corner of the room.
37946: A large well, enclosed by a thick wall of greenish-blue stone, attracts your attention. The well lies at the exact centre of the large vaulted hall named after the well itself. Thousands of minute runes and strange symbols have been chiselled on the outer surface of the well; whoever defaced the rest of this hall, somehow left the well alone - but for what reason, nobody knows.
37947:
A black uruk, armoured heavily, stands confidently here.
A black uruk, armoured heavily, stands confidently here.
A black uruk, armoured heavily, stands confidently here.
A black uruk, armoured heavily, stands confidently here.
A black uruk, armoured heavily, stands confidently here.
A black uruk, armoured heavily, stands confidently here.
A stone-grey troll advances toward you, with fury in its eyes.
A stone-grey troll advances toward you, with fury in its eyes.

A wide avenue with light grey walls begins here, in the Seventh Deep of Moria, and solemnly strides to the east. Signs of the frequent passage of whoever dwells here are abundant: the floor looks very worn, especially along the route that connects the wide hall south of here to a chamber north. Other signs are much more worrying: the loud clanking of metal boots, the disgusting smell coming from the north, and the wanton destruction which was perpetrated on the Dwarven artwork that once filled this corridor. One of the few beautiful things still remaining in this place is a large carving on the western wall: it was simply too large to destroy out of spite.
37948: The southeastern corner of an extremely dirty (and smelly) square room ends with a wide archway on the southern side. The intense usage of the passage wore out the hard stone of the floor, so that a small depression can now be found around the portal. Sounds of clanking boots and occasional war cries can be heard all around. The hall continues to the north, where the ground slopes down, and west, where a small fire dissipates the gloom.
37949: A pool of water, about ten paces diameter, has collected into this section of the hall. Greenish-brown in colour, the water smells of well seasoned corpses. A cursory glance is more than enough to justify the awful stench: gnawed bones, some with pieces of rancid meat still attached, emerge from the surface near the edges of the pool. No decent folk would even consider drinking this water; unfortunately, the word "decent" can hardly be applied to the inhabitants of the cave to the southwest.
37950:
An uruk-hai is here, growling to himself.
An uruk-hai is here, growling to himself.

The northwestern corner of the hall, if possible even more messy and filthy than the rest of the place, has been recently used as a sleeping area. A big pile of straw, most probably brought here from the fields of Dimrill Dale, seems to have been left here for ages; it has absorbed the typical disgusting smell of Morgoth's corrupted perversions. Flickering rays of light from a small fire to the south reach your eyes from time to time.
37951:
An uruk-hai growls at the sight of you.
An uruk-hai growls at the sight of you.

Around a small fire, used more to cook and to provide heat rather than to light the room, a harsh yet pleasant scent of burned wood struggles against the prevailing stench of decay tinging the entire hall. Whatever light the fire provides, however, is more than enough to make the surrounding places darker by comparison. The hall continues to the north and east; to the west, a tunnel with a low ceiling begins its obscure path.
37952: Gaping as the open mouth of some great, toothless beast, the eastern end of a low and wide tunnel lies not far to the east. Faint light, coming from a small fire in the hall beyond, creates deep, moving shadows on the walls, giving the impression that, sooner or later, the tunnel will crush and slowly chew any unfortunate person walking along it.
37953: Each step taken along this wide and low gallery produces a very deep echo, which reverberates through the ancient halls of the Seventh Deep. West and east the corridor continues its journey, seemingly unchanged in the grey texture of its smooth walls. Far to the east, a pinpoint of light might mark the end of the road.
37954: The ceiling is definitely low in this tunnel, as if the Dwarves had not bothered to make it comfortable for taller people as well. What the road misses in height, however, it makes up in width. Proceeding from the east to the west, the colour of the surrounding stone seems to become darker, passing slowly from light grey to dark grey and finally to pitch black.
37955: In the middle of the thick darkness, the tunnel gently bends to the east and to the southwest. The jet black, smooth stone all around seems to absorb any ray of light, no matter how thin. Here and there, thin rivulets of dark water slowly trickle down the walls, and collect into small cracks on the floor. The flow is so slow and regular that it is nearly impossible to hear it; the oily smell of the fluid, however, is overpowering.
37956: The dark walls of this tunnel are slowly changing their texture. The cracks, very common to the southwest, are becoming smaller and less numerous to the northeast; in that direction, however, a thick smelly fluid slowly flows out of some cracks and down along the walls, perhaps covering the smaller, barely noticeable imperfections.
37957: You have reached the southwestern end of a long, gloomy tunnel. Its dark grey walls are full of cracks; a slow air current from the southwest raises, from time to time, small puffs of dust from the floor. The usual smell of orcs, which pervades the area all around, seems to have lessened; whether because the foul spawn of Morgoth are actually far, or because of the air current, is not known.
37958: Here the tunnel to the northeast opens into a wide road going southwards, flanking the eastern side of an extremely vast chasm. Beyond a stone parapet, which has collapsed in several places, looms the opposite face of the chasm, a sheer cliff dotted with tunnel entrances. To the north, the south and above you the abyss seems to continue endlessly, while, straining one's sight, one can barely perceive a wide shelf perhaps a hundred feet below. A beautiful cylindrical tower rises from the depths of Durin's Chimney and climbs into the darkness above; a slim stair circles around the pillar. Sturdy bridges once connected this side of the chasm to the tower and to the other side, but the ravages of time made all of the bridges nearby collapse.
37959: You are now on the eastern edge of the huge chasm known as Durin's Chimney. A majestic platform protrudes from the side of the precipice: built by the Dwarves a long time before the coming of their bane, the platform allows any who stand on it to gaze at both sides of the Chimney. Once an important crossroads in Khazad-dum, this place is now usually deserted; the black uruks and the trolls who now live here do not seem to appreciate the terrible beauty of this place.
37960: An iron pick has been dropped here.

You have reached the western and lower end of a narrow stone bridge crossing the Chimney. To the east the bridge climbs up towards the City of Moria, while north and south a stone parapet surrounds the small rocky outcropping which supports the end of the bridge. A strange-looking tunnel descends to the west.
37961: The glassy walls of the tunnel grow thicker and thicker as one follows them to the west, until they finally merge in a smooth, hard, impenetrable transparent wall which closes off the passage. One can only try to guess what happened in these depths where the Dwarves dug for mithril, and what the Dwarf - whose remains can still be seen, imprisoned in the translucent rock - saw before he met a horrible, fiery death.
37962: A long time ago a beautiful avenue used to start here, and to cross the entire Seventh Deep of Khazad-dum from the west to the east. Now the road might still run its ancient course, but it cannot be called beautiful any more. Chunks of rock, the product of the Uruks' destructive hammering, lie at the feet of the once finely chiselled marble pillars. What could have been a fine alabaster statue is now nothing more than a pile of rubble.
37963: Your steps produce a faint, cavernous echo in the dark niches on both sides of this corridor. Halfway between one niche and the next, the Dwarves of Khazad-dum once erected mighty half-columns of white marble. The current inhabitants of these halls evidently did not like the proud ornate pillars, since most of them have been severely damaged - on purpose.
37964: A wide road, flanked by marble half-columns, runs from the west to the east. To the west the avenue opens into a large vaulted chamber, whose walls show an unusual blue-greenish tinge. From time to time, strange noises reach your ears - seemingly from the western hall, though the echoes might be deceiving. To the east Fror's Avenue stretches onward into the deep gloom.
37965: The elegant avenue known as Fror's Avenue stretches itself from the west to the east. Hundreds of evenly spaced and finely engraved marble half-columns have been built by the Dwarves along the walls. Something about the northern wall attracts your attention: it seems that, once, some sort of tapestry hung from a series of hooks near the ceiling.
37966: A three yard tall statue of an ancient Dwarf Lord dominates this section of the corridor. Placed in a large niche on the southern side of Fror's Avenue, the statue seems to be watching the surroundings. The Dwarf Lord is holding a large hammer in his hand, while a set of jewelsmith's tools hang from his wide belt. These signs of Khazad-dum's former wealth contrast deeply with the abandoned halls in which you are walking.
37967: You are standing at the eastern end of one of the main corridors in the Seventh and Last Deep of Khazad-dum. Large marble pillars flank the avenue's dark grey walls as they stretch to the west, towards Hwain's Well. East of here Fror's Avenue opens into a small, ornate chamber which seems to have been left relatively untouched by the destructive fury of the Balrog's servants.
37968: About a dozen of large, lifelike statues of Dwarves meet the weary travellers as they enter this vaulted, ornate chamber. The statues represent members of Durin's People busy in the occupations they valued most: stonecraft, gem cutting, metalworking. The emblems of the House of Durin have been engraved on the eastern wall: the Crown, the Seven Stars, the Hammer and Anvil. To the west lies a wide corridor known as Fror's Avenue; a chill, damp wind comes from a dark road to the north. As you look around, you realise that this room has suffered very little from the cruelty of the orcs of the Black Chasm. The reason, however, lies beyond your grasp.
37969: A wide, dark road bends gently from the northwest to the southeast. A faint current of damp air comes from the north, brushes past you and loses itself in some small crack in the tunnel floor. Every few paces a torch support hangs from the walls; however, the torches have not been replaced in the last few centuries. Now only the rusty supports remind the weary traveller who reaches this forsaken place that, once, this was the heart of a prosperous kingdom.
37970: A large, gloomy road extends itself from the north to the south. Originally a natural cavern, this gallery was only marginally changed by the Khazad, who only removed some stalactites and made the floor somewhat smoother. Due to this choice, one might now be able to fully appreciate the sinister beauty of the tunnel - were it not for the ever-present threat of marauding bands of orcs and trolls.
37971: The gaping tunnel to the south ends here, in a wide chamber almost completely filled with dark, chilly water. Thin wisps of mist, similar to curled ghostly fingers, pervade the air all around you. Strange shapes seem to be shifting in the fog and below the surface of the lake: it takes you a while to realize that it is most probably an illusion caused by the mist. Yet, the chance of some huge and deadly monster stalking you under the cover of the fog is not to be underestimated.
37972:
An albino fish is swimming here, looking for some food.
An albino fish is swimming here, looking for some food.

Dark water lies around you in all directions, covered by a thick coat of shifting mist. The ceiling is getting dangerously near to the surface of the water, except to the east, where the otherwise flat lake is disturbed by a series of ripples, and to the south, where, through the mist, a small rocky shore can be seen. The water is chilly; strange shapes can be seen below, but whether they are mere reflexes of the fog or something else, none can say.
37973: Thick layers of mist, slowly rising from the surface of a nearly black lake, surround you in all directions. The visibility is awful: one has to rely mostly on the position of the low ceiling to see where he is going. To the east and north, the free space above the water level quickly decreases to nothingness. The otherwise calm surface of the lake is troubled, here, by a bubbling column of air coming from the depths of the water.
37974: The dark water of the lake smoothly glides below you, as you cross one of the thickest banks of fog you have ever met. The only way to understand where one is going is to look the low, rough ceiling of this flooded chamber. In your immediate surroundings, many huge stalactites protrude from the rock above you and touch the water.
37975: The damp air current coming from the north whistles with a strange, almost whimpering sound as it reaches this intersection. Droplets of water, which have condensed on every surface around you, make the floor slightly slippery. Dark roads leave to the south and to the north; looking ahead, the smooth walls of the latter soon give way to the rougher stone of a natural cavern. Another tunnel, extremely ornate, leaves west.
37976: At its eastern end, the accessway to the Royal Chambers of Khazad-dum joins a wide, dark road running south and north. As elsewhere in the City of Moria, this corridor was enriched with fine art works; as elsewhere in Khazad-dum, the devastating fury of the orcs has defaced the proud Dwarven masterpieces. On the southern wall, among the foul scratches and coal marks, a relief has survived. It seems to have been carved quite hastily, with little of the usual skill of the Dwarves. Yet, when one stops for a moment and looks at the tragic scenes represented on the wall, the reason for the haste becomes evident.
37977: A vast corridor, entrance to the King's Rooms, runs majestically from the west to the east, with no intersections in sight. The Orcs' long hatred towards the Dwarves can be clearly seen in the crude scratches which utterly ruined the former beauty of this place. A large carving on the northern wall seems to have attracted the "attentions" of the Uruks much more than anything else.
37978: A wide, ornate portal opens in the northern wall of a long corridor, stretching itself west and east. The faint, metallic echo of heavy bootsteps reverberates through the ancient halls of Khazad-dum, carried around by the massive rock. The decorations in this part of the corridor have been left relatively untouched; this allows any who pass to see the magnificent relief on the southern wall.
37979: You stand within a carefully-crafted chamber. The columns and arches are elegant yet sturdy, while on the northern wall a relief depicts a Dwarf king in a victorious pose. The shattered remnants of chairs and stone benches are found at the walls. A large door, made from mahogany, fills a doorway to the west, while empty archways lead east and south.
37980: The ceiling of this passageway rises high above you; arched, it supports the massive weight of the stone above it. As the corridor curves north and west, the inner wall has Dwarven runes carven into it. The floor, even though made from very hard stone, bears marks of wear.
37981: Although still curving gently, the corridor heads mostly north and south. A large and solid door of oak stands in the middle of the eastern wall, and carven into the wall, beside the door, are some runes. On the western wall the runic writing continues its tale.
37982: The air about you is stagnant and dusty, filling the corridor with a stale atmosphere. The high, arched ceiling is cracked in certain places, and the floor has been chipped unevenly. The writing continues on the inner wall, and the passage itself bends to the west and south.
37983:
A wooden chest stands in the corner.
A large stone chest is here.
A solid ironbound chest is here.

Although this room is cluttered with stored weapons, armour, and provisions, behind the chests and shelves you can see the features of an abandoned armoury. On the north wall, a great and cold forge lies dusty and filled with soot; on the east, an anvil provides support for a table. A large, barred door is in the south wall.
37984: The curving corridor ends at a large door to the west. The runes on the wall also end here, their message apparently complete. At the base of the northern wall, the remains of a stone chest are scattered. Bits of twisted metal litter the ground.
37985: Beneath the rubble, it is evident that this was once a stocked armoury. The remainders of weapon racks and shelves and chests litter the floor, but now everything has been taken, looted, or destroyed. The walls have been battered, bearing large fist-marks. To the west, a door has been bashed from its hinges; to the east, a door has survived the abuse with only moderate damage.
37986: A large amount of rubble is on the ground. The eastern archway was hacked and broken, and the door smashed. The walls themselves are chipped and marred, with the writing on the south wall illegible. In the centre of the corridor, a small aisle has been cleared away.
37987: The corridor continues to bend in a circle, and the runes still cover the inner wall. A grand door is set in the outer wall, and to either side of it are stone benches. The ground is well-worn here, scuffed by heavy feet. A cart partially blocks the corridor south.
37988: This armoury has been maintained in a reasonable condition, no doubt for the use of constructing weapons and armour. In fact, the forge is burning, and the air is hot and sulphurous. Along the walls, niches carved into the stone hold tools and material and half-finished items. A battered anvil stands in the northern end of the chamber.
37989:
Muranog, the High Lieutenant of Durin's Bane, stands here.
A huge troll, with skin as black as pitch, glowers at you.
A huge troll, with skin as black as pitch, glowers at you.
A huge troll, with skin as black as pitch, glowers at you.

This grand chamber maintains a horrid magnificence. Its seven walls have been blackened, and the ceiling has been covered in sable and purple tapestries. Great columns rise from the floor and are enveloped into the tapestries. Most striking is the throne in the centre of the room, made from stone and decorated with gems and precious metals. On the dark floor are braziers, clouding the room with a grey and incensed smoke.
37990: Northwards a great chamber stretches beyond you. The walls are black and dark grey, and columns bear the weight of the mountain above you. The air is thick with smoke, and before you is a large dish, filled with flame. It illuminates the chamber with a harsh reddish light. East and west are double-doors, made of a heavy and dark wood.
37991: Decrepit opulence fills this room. Cracked and discoloured tapestries from the door to the east, and shattered busts stand to either side of it. An archway to the south reveals a view of an avenue, which age and neglect have destroyed its splendour. Westward a high-vaulted corridor starts to circle.
37992: This passageway is circular, bending north and east. To the east, the passageway leads into a once splendrous chamber. At the connection to that chamber, a strange runic writing begins on the centre wall. On the ground, heavy footsteps have smoothed the stone.
37993: As it goes north and south, this passageway gently curves eastward. Along the eastern wall, runes trace out an intricate history. The stone floor has been worn, and tracks of cart-wheels frame the scuffing done by boots.
37994:
A black uruk, armoured heavily, stands confidently here.
A black uruk, armoured heavily, stands confidently here.
A black uruk, armoured heavily, stands confidently here.
A black uruk, armoured heavily, stands confidently here.
A black uruk, armoured heavily, stands confidently here.
A huge troll, with skin as black as pitch, glowers at you.
A stone-grey troll advances toward you, with fury in its eyes.

The main access to the Royal Chambers of the House of Durin extends itself in a west to east direction. In both directions wide, elegant portals open in the northern wall not too far away. A weak stench reminding of rotten meat can be felt to the west. To the north, between the portals, another part of the long history of Khazad-dum was carved on the light grey wall.
37995: Advancing from the west to the east along this proud corridor, the disgusting reek of orcs seems to lessen. Yet the signs of their presence nearby are more than evident: only a totally corrupted follower of the Darkness would have reduced the once magnificent halls of the Dwarves to their current pitiful state. To the north, behind a portal, lies a small chamber, while to the south, amid the wanton destruction, some of the original carvings have survived.
37996:
Rohal, wielding a mighty dwarven axe, is standing here.
Kostilam, wielding a mighty dwarven axe, is standing here.
Feera the Half-Elf, wielding an engraved broadsword, is standing here.
Iarion the Elf, wielding an engraved broadsword, is standing here.

This small antechamber connects to a large, heptangular chamber to the east. On both the north and south walls, great frescos have been discoloured with age, yet are still readable. Above you, in the ceiling, there sits a large crack, centred on a thin hole. The smell of dust and decay is strong, and the stench of trolls is conspicuously absent. To the west, a great oak door closes off the doorway.
37997: You stand amidst despoiled luxury. The plush, musty carpet beneath your feet silences any footstep, no matter how harsh, and the vaulted ceiling's arches are graced with crackling and discoloured purple sashes. All about you sit once beautiful chairs, some broken and twisted by evil hands, some simply brittle with age. In the southwest wall of this heptangular room a great table has been set, its sturdy wood gashed deeply by fearsome claws. Still, some sanctity has been preserved, and the taint of evil here is archaic. No forces, good or evil, have reigned here for centuries.
37998: A large and sturdy cabinet stands against the wall.

The bedrooms of the most powerful Dwarven rulers spread out, disused, around you. A thick layer of dust coats the crumbling carpet, and it swirls chokingly into the air as you disturb its rest. Cabinets and dressers and wardrobes line the walls, with shattered mirrors besides them. Entrancing tessaracts have been defaced, and priceless statues crushed. Grand beds, unslept in for centuries, lie in the centres of the rooms.
37999: Hidden: a pair of shining chain sleeves

This adjunct room next to the Lord of Khazad-dum's chambers served as the main meeting room for him and his seven closest advisers. The well-hewn stone forms a half-sphere shape, leaving no shadowed corners. An ancient octagonal table dominates the centre of the room, its cured wood intact but showing slashes made many centuries ago. The splinters of broken chairs lie strewn about the room, covered in dust, evidence of destruction that took place well before. Not a sound stirs in this ancient chamber, untouched for so long.
38000: No comforts adorn this room. The floor, ceiling, and seven walls are perfectly smooth stone, of varying shades of grey. A large statue stands before the eastern wall, looking upon you with cold and distant eyes. This room is pervaded by an awesome and strange feeling; the presence of Aule Mahal, the Builder, resides in each stone. No claw marks or other marks of despoilment can be seen, no walls are defaced, and the statue is not marred in any way. The dust that lines the floor does not blanket the statue, and there is no smell of mould or fungus.
38001: A twin line of cracked marble pillars, leaning on the sides of this wide corridor, continues to the west and to the east. Darkened niches open between one column and the next. Looking inside the large holes in the avenue's walls one can only see huge piles of rubble, but - perhaps - the next niche might hide some nightmarish monster who would be delighted to add some more remains to the rubble.
38002: A wide, elegant avenue stretches itself from the west to the east. Large marble half-columns line the walls of the corridor; large niches open between one column and the next. While the niches were originally crafted to house the most beautiful works of art of Durin's people, now nearly all beauty has disappeared from them.
38003: You have reached a small landing on an ancient, seldom used stair flanking the Chimney of Durin. This is only a short respite for the person climbing the grey, dusty steps, since the extremely steep ascent and descent resume after a few meters. Narrow, jagged cracks can be seen on the walls, signs of the long time elapsed since the construction of this stairway.
38004: Carved from the living rock of Zirakzigil, this small tower has stood since the age when dwarves first delved beneath these peaks. The thousands of years that have passed have done nothing to mar the elegant stonework, and, much like a dwarf, this tower stands mute and resolute - stoically resisting whatever fury the mountains can unleash upon it. A solitary window looks out onto a small field of snow, here at the top of the world above even the clouds.
38005: This small and snow-covered plain lies atop Celebdil, the Silvertine. To the south is Durin's Tower - a simple stone edifice that somehow seems the height of Dwarven elegance as it might be part of the mountain itself. In every other direction, the clouds obscure the lands like a great grey blanket - only the most severe of storms can hurl snow at this height, but once it falls, it cannot melt. Some distance away, the equally impressive peaks of Caradhras and Fanuidhol protrude above the eternal cloud cover, forming the remainder of the majestic triumvirate of peaks over Khazad-dum.
38006: The damp mist enfolds you as you begin to plummet towards the distant earth. You break through the bottom of the clouds and are rewarded with a brief but spectacular view of the surrounding lands, but the onrushing ground quickly squelches your sense of wonder.
38007: The damp mist enfolds you as you begin to plummet towards the distant earth. You break through the bottom of the clouds and are rewarded with a brief but spectacular view of the surrounding lands, but the onrushing ground quickly squelches your sense of wonder.
38008: The damp mist enfolds you as you begin to plummet towards the distant earth. You break through the bottom of the clouds and are rewarded with a brief but spectacular view of the surrounding lands, but the onrushing ground quickly squelches your sense of wonder.
38009: A narrow, winding stone stair begins its twisted and secret path behind an arch on the southern wall of this chamber, leading to some place far, far above. The chamber itself is small, containing nothing but dust and a few empty torch supports; its only exit, apart from the stair, is a plain stone door to the west.
38010: A domesticated pony , beast of burden to many, stands here.

The old steps of a secret stone stair become gradually larger as they approach the bottom; the twisted stairwell straightens as it rushes north to enter a small room in the depths of Khazad-dum. A musty smell pervades the air around you, hinting that this section of the City is usually closed off. Perhaps the secret passages leading here have been forgotten by all; perhaps, on the other hand, the final destination of this stair is a place so dreadful that the orcs of the Black Chasm do not dare approach.
38011: More tortuous than the mind of a madman, the stair winds its way through the hard rock of the Deeps of Moria. Though the horizontal direction keeps changing, so that it would take a highly skilled scout not to lose one's bearings, the slope of the stair remains always the same: the steepest that a Dwarf could ever manage to climb without tools.
38012: Here the stair crosses a major fault line in the roots of the Misty Mountains. During the passage of many centuries, the upper section of the stairwell has slowly shifted down and sideways, partially blocking the way. The only passage remaining is a small hole in a corner, barely large enough to squeeze through. Dust and gravel from the cracked walls lie on the steps, making footing unsure or worse.
38013: A dripping yellow fungus hangs here, clinging to the crevices and walls.

The stair has reached one end of a relatively long straight stretch, which is a pleasant change after hundreds of twisting steps. It might be the eastern end, but there is no quick way to be certain - the many sharp and irregular turnings in the rest of the stairwell make it extremely easy to lose the sense of direction.
38014: The stairwell, which, above, is extremely contorted, abruptly stops bending right in this place. The dazzling convolutions give way to a long straight ramp, which gradually slopes down into the darkness. Almost no noise, apart from that of your own making, can be heard here: massive layers of rock separate this place from the rest of the world.
38015: A dripping yellow fungus hangs here, clinging to the crevices and walls.

Bending alternately clockwise and anticlockwise, with no semblance of order, the stair continues its long journey through the hard rock. The continuous bends have a somewhat hypnotic effect, reinforced by the fact that the walls are so close to each other that one has almost no freedom to move: the only choice lies between going ahead or turning back.
38016: The stairwell, enclosed within massive, cracked stone walls, seems to get narrower and narrower as it descends, until it becomes barely wide enough to let a single person through. A thin layer of dust, which has accumulated with the passage of time, rests on the barely worn steps.
38017: The upper end of an old stone stair lies a few paces east of here, where the narrow stairwell opens into a small secret chamber. In the opposite direction the stair plunges down very steeply, and the rough stone walls surrounding it grow nearer to each other. There seem to be little signs of passage here: in contrast with some larger tunnels, the floor and the steps have not been worn out by thousands and thousands of moving feet.
38018: This small room is enclosed by roughly formed walls. They block any movement south or east, but west a passageway leads between them. The northern wall is smooth and well fit, revealing a moveable slab. The disuse of this room is evident, from not only the stale air and dust, but also from the cobwebs forming a silky screen over much of the walls.
38019: This small passageway probably once led to the actual lodging areas of the Naugrim, but the area to the south is now impassable and totally choked with rubble. Whatever once lay beyond has been buried now for many centuries, and will remain so until the dwarves return.
38020: Once just a storage closet, this has been converted to something akin to a grocery store. Messy shelves lined with stinking, rotting wares line the walls. Piles of mildewed bread waste away on the floor. You shudder to think of how long this stuff has been rotting here.
38021: A squat and filthy troll lurks in the darkness.

The walls in here seem to have been painted jet black recently. This tunnel was not made by dwarves because its jagged walls, irregular dimensions and twisty path would never meet with any dwarf's approval. The passage eventually snakes to the west where it becomes swallowed in total darkness, and there is a painted black door at the south end of the tunnel.
38022: The two words which best describe this tight tunnel are narrow and black. Jagged rock from the tunnel walls reaches out to grab at your clothes as you attempt to make your way through here, and it is so dark that you cannot see the ground that you tread on. The tunnel runs east-west.
38023: An orkish warrior of the Durghash is here, with a cruel glint in his eye.

This tiny room has a very low ceiling, so low that you must crouch down in order to squeeze in here. There is a very small hole at waist-level in the south wall, and you can observe a section of Durin's Way through it. Perhaps this place serves as a secret lookout, used to monitor any movement on the Way. A small stone bench is positioned directly in front of the spyhole, and there are fresh orc tracks in the dirt near the bench.
38024: The old steps of a long spiral stair seem to continue their way along the walls of the stairwell forever. A weak current of warm air ascends from the darkness below, carrying the stench of orcs and of other foul beasts.
38025: You are standing at the eastern end of Copper Road, the ancient Dwarven tunnel that connected the Copper Caverns to Moria's main corridors. The road goes on to the west, and a smaller passage - flanked by a sign - leads north. Your attention is captured by a large arch on the eastern wall, as behind the arch lies a stairway leading both up and down.
38026:
A large bat is here, hanging in the darkness.
A large bat is here, hanging in the darkness.

Here the narrow passage you have been following bends to the west and to the south. The walls are much more irregular than the walls of the other Dwarven tunnels you have seen before, as if this passage had been built in a hurry.
38027: A large bat is here, hanging in the darkness.

You are standing at an intersection along a narrow passageway. The main corridor runs from the west to the east; a very small hole allows you to crawl to a chamber to the south. In the northern wall, after a short tunnel, you can glimpse part of a vast natural chamber. The sound of hundreds of fluttering wings comes from that direction.
38028: Uldor (UU), wielding a great warsword, is standing here.

A long time ago, this section of the tunnel must have collapsed. Since this was one of the most important corridors of this section of Khazad-dum, the Dwarves managed to reopen it and to support the unstable ceiling with a large quantity of timbers. Copper Road runs from the west to the east; a smaller tunnel leads north and vanishes in the darkness. A draft of fresh air comes from the latter tunnel.
38029: An iron pick has been dropped here.

Here the old tunnel that you have been following bends from the east to the northwest, perhaps to avoid a mass of harder rock, perhaps for some other reason that has been forgotten with the passage of time. A pile of old, rusty mining tools has been left here.
38030: You have reached a major intersection along Copper Road. While the main corridor climbs west towards the Copper Caverns and slopes down to the south, two lesser passages run off to the east and north.
