A faint sound of fluttering wings seems to come out of these smaller tunnels. A very old sign has been placed at the entrance of the eastern corridor.
38031: A large and somewhat round fungus grows from the floor.

A narrow, seldom used corridor, which seems to have been dug with less care than the other tunnels you have seen in Khazad-dum, runs from the west to the east. An even smaller passage to the north allows you to enter a vast natural chamber. Many small bats are flying in and out of the northern tunnel.
38032:
A large and somewhat round fungus grows from the floor.
A large and somewhat round fungus grows from the floor.
A large and somewhat round fungus grows from the floor.
A fierce bat is here, lusting for your blood.
A fierce bat is here, lusting for your blood.
A bloodthirsty bat is sleeping here.
A fierce bat is here, lusting for your blood.
A fierce bat is here, lusting for your blood.
The queen bat is here, emitting piercing squeaks.
A bloodthirsty bat is sleeping here.

Hundreds and hundreds of bats of all sizes, shapes and colour fly, sleep and rest in this large natural cavern. Most of these bats are small and are quietly hanging from the ceiling, but some others are much larger than any bat you might have seen before... and might consider you as a nice dessert for their dinner.
38033:
A large and somewhat round fungus grows from the floor.
A large and somewhat round fungus grows from the floor.
A large and somewhat round fungus grows from the floor.

As you enter this large natural cavern, you are caught in a strong and cold air current descending from a hole in the ceiling to a series of small pits in the floor. Hundreds, perhaps thousands of bats are dancing around in the current. Most of these bats are small, and can only hamper you by flying inadvertently in your face, but you are worried mainly of the few larger bats - whose size might be compared with that of a large dog. The cavern continues to the west; smaller passages lead north and south.
38034: Some tough lichen grows on the rocks.

The passage here widens into a small natural chamber. Stalactites and stalagmites sometimes merge into beautiful columns connecting the floor with the ceiling. Water slowly drips from the points of the stalactites, leaving behind more deposits for the growth of this jungle of stone. A gallery opens in the southern side of the chamber; from time to time, a small bat or two enter that tunnel or come out of it. Another passage leaves this room to the west.
38035: A large bat is here, hanging in the darkness.

The ceiling of this tunnel is very low, forcing anyone taller than a Dwarf to bend. As you slowly walk along the passage, you wonder whether it would be better to crawl east, where the tunnel becomes narrower and narrower, or to go south and enter a larger corridor.
38036: The ceiling of the cavern is lost high above. A rank smell pervades the place and piles of guano lie splattered all about. The only exit is to the north, where a narrow tunnel emerges into this larger cavern. Bits and pieces of half-eaten smallish animals litter the floor together with the white bones and skeletons of long dead small creatures.
38037: This narrow tunnel is cramped and tricky to negotiate as it bends about. From where you stand, it runs east and south, where it seems to open out quite markedly. You have to twist and hunch down to avoid scraping against the sharp rocks that protrude from the walls and tunnel floor. Small loose rocks cover the ground and you only barely keep from falling, dodging to avoid the razor-edged stone formations as you stumble to regain your footing.
38038:
A large mean-looking troll is here.
A large mean-looking troll is here.

The road runs through a large natural cavern here, exiting north and east, with a narrower passage running away west. Shadows fill every corner of this roughly circular chamber and any sound you make bounces off the dark walls and the high domed ceiling, creating an eerie feeling of abandonment. A sharp cracking sound, coming from the east, reminds you that these tunnels and passages are far from empty of life.
38039: Bending from west to south, the road travels ever on in the deep underground of the mountain. As you trudge onward through the tunnels, you suddenly hear a low rumbling sound coming seemingly from the very core of the mountain, as if the ceiling of some far-away passage had caved in.
38040: Running arrow-straight, north to south, the dwarf-built road travels onward through the dark Deeps of Moria. The craftsmanship of the tunnelling is flawless and the dwarves even had the time to create beautiful carvings on the walls of this tunnel. Now faded and worn by the passage of time, intricate pictures have been chiselled out of the solid rock, depicting now long forgotten Dwarven heroes, proudly brandishing their magnificent weapons.
38041: An orkish warrior of the Durghash is here, with a cruel glint in his eye.

The road runs through a small chamber full of stalactites and stalagmites, where the sound of slow dripping water echoes throughout the place. The road exits north and east. The inhabitants of these tunnels and caverns are obviously of a violent nature, shown by the fact that a couple of the stalagmites, as well as a few of the low-dipping stalactites, have had their tips broken off.
38042: The small roadway makes a sudden sharp turn, bending from west to south. This tunnel has clearly been carved through the mountain by mortal hands, as opposed to other tunnels and caverns, formed by the forces of nature. Dampness hangs in the air though, and the absence of natural rock formations only make the place look even more bleak and deserted.
38043:
A strange bat-like creature is flitting around.
A strange bat-like creature is flitting around.
A strange bat-like creature is flitting around.
A strange bat-like creature is flitting around.
A strange bat-like creature is flitting around.
A strange bat-like creature is flitting around.

You stand at the foot of a rocky stairwell. Climbing up into the darkness runs a narrow stair spiralling around the ascending circular shaft. A small door is set in the west wall. The steps seem safe and sturdy, carved from the solid rock walls, but you would have to take care not trip or stumble on your way up. The air is relatively fresh, probably due to the slight breeze that wafts through this chamber from the darkness above. You notice that something looking like dried bat guano lies scattered randomly across the floor.
38044: You are on a dark Dwarven road. Not especially wide, it appears to have been one of the lesser roads. The passage makes a small downward dip on its way from north to south and to allow easy passage over this incline, the dwarves that once mined these tunnels have carved out a number of steps in the rocky ground. From the north you can hear the sound of softly gurgling water.
38045: Here a wide, swift flowing stream rushes west-east, barring further northerly passage of the road that enters from the south. A narrow path leads away to the west and a wider one runs east. Almost hidden in the darkness of a crevice in the west wall, you see a narrow staircase rising upward. The distant sound of roaring can be heard from the west, sounding much like a huge waterfall. Huge stalactites adorn the ceiling of this natural cavern and although most of the ground has been smoothed to allow easy passage, a few stalagmites stretch upward in the northeast corner of the cave.
38046: The stream continues to flow west-east away below the level of the road, which also runs west-east. The roadway narrows hard to the east, forming a small ledge, clinging to the south end of the tunnel, and replacing the comfortable walkway you are standing on. Several large stalactites hang from the ceiling of the tunnel, forming an eerie kind of forest of sharp, pointed spears. The cold air makes you shiver slightly and long for a warming fire.
38047: The roadway winds along from west to east, the stream churning along below the narrow ledge you are standing on. In the east, the walkway descends a number of roughly hewn stone steps, dropping down to run at the same level as the river. You look down into the murky black waters of the stream and press yourself against the rock at your back; it would not be a pleasant experience to plunge into those waters. Drops of water fall from the stalactites above, the sound as they strike the surface swallowed by the thundering of the underground river.
38048: The roadway is crowded with stalagmites, some stretching up to join the stalactites above in fantastic columns. A path through them runs from the east to disappear into darkness in the west, sometimes crossing small stone bridges built to allow passage over the stream that rushes onward at your feet. At the east end of the corridor the murmur of rushing, falling water can be heard, and a faint current drifts toward you from there. The roadway climbs up a simple set of stone steps carved out of the southern cavern wall, ascending to a narrow ledge.
38049: Plunging out into the inky darkness of a huge chasm, the stream emerging from the west of this natural cavern disappears into the bowels of the mountain, tumbling against the solid rock on its way down. A broad, winding stair is hewn into the walls of the chasm allowing upward progress, while a narrow walkway leads into the small tunnel of the stream. The thundering sound of the waterfall is deafening and the air is constantly filled with small water particles clinging to your clothes, slowly and surely soaking them.
38050: Thundering down from unseen heights, the waterfall crashes into this cavern, quickly forming a swift-flowing stream exiting in the east. The path runs right up to the flow, the footing somewhat treacherous. To the east, the path runs along a dwarf-built ledge, and to the south, it disappears into a dark tunnel. Looking around the cavern, you see a narrow stair hugging the natural wall near the waterfall, winding up into darkness. The loud roaring of the waterfall is deafening and the air is filled with a watery mist, as well as larger drops falling around you, spraying from the downwards plunging water.
38051: The roaring noise of a waterfall, coming from the north, covers the noise of your steps and forces you to speak louder if you want to be heard. The road continues to the north and to the west.
38052: You have reached yet another bend in this long smooth-walled tunnel carved in dark grey rock. The road winds its way to the north and to the east; to the south a smaller tunnel is blocked by a huge crack in the floor. From the east you can distinctly hear the sound of water falling.
38053: The road here bends gently to the south - or to the west if you originally came from the south. Dull grey stone surrounds you in all of the other directions. The air is fresh, and in the distance you can hear the rumbling sound of a waterfall.
38054: The road, enclosed within dark grey walls, stretches its way from the west to the east. As you tredge onward, small amounts of gravel shift beneath your feet and then roll down to the west for a short distance. Though it is not very loud, the noise of your steps echoes along the tunnel, perhaps revealing your position to a lurking patrol of Moria's denizens.
38055: You have reached an intersection of roads. The main tunnel, with its blackened walls, bends east and south; a smaller corridor leads north. Strange, clanking noises can be heard in the distance, from no particular direction. The noise seems the lamentation of Moria's mines, long ago abandoned by the Dwarves... but you are certain that its source is something evil, perhaps lurking right behind the next corner.
38056:
A lurg leader, with markings of the Durghash tribe, stands here.
A great wolf with a sable coat glares around with red eyes.
An orkish warrior of the Durghash is here, with a cruel glint in his eye.
A large bat is here, hanging in the darkness.
A large bat is here, hanging in the darkness.

A large tunnel, which loses itself in the darkness to the north, ends here in a very large cavern with dark greenish walls. Just below your feet a rusty metal ladder leads down to a narrower passage. As you walk near the ladder, you can feel the flapping of wings nearby. Is it a common bat, or something worse?
38057: You are in the northwestern corner of a large cavern with greenish walls. The Dwarves used to extract copper ore from this mine, and later brought it to their furnaces on carts. You can still see the remains of some carts lying on the floor. To the east a dark road leaves this place.
38058: Ealros, wielding a heavy morningstar, is standing here.

This is the middle section of a large copper mine, which continues to the west and the north. In the southern wall an archway opens in the greenish walls of the cavern. As you look at the large road beyone the archway, you can see the marks left by the carts' iron wheels in the stone floor.
38059: You have reached the western end of the Copper Road, the ancient dwarven tunnel connecting the famed copper caverns to the city on the east side of Khazad-dum. To the north you can see the old copper mines, whilst the road continues to the southest.
38060: The cart tracks in the stone floor of this tunnel seem to continue forever in a northwest to southeast direction. The silence is broken only by the noise of your steps and your breath. Small chunks of copper mineral, fallen from the Dwarves' carts ages ago, are scattered here and there along the tunnel floor.
38061: You have reached a slight bend in the long corridor known as Copper Road. The tunnel, coming from the copper mines to the northwest, now bends in a more eastward direction. As you strain your vision to peer in the darkness in front of you, you realise that there might be an intersection not far to the east.
38062: The large tunnel, which connects the Copper Caverns to the main routes from West Door to East Gate, meets here a side passage - a barely noticeable crack in the northern wall. The tunnel floor, as usual, bears the tracks of the enormous number of mining carts that have passed over it in the long years between the creation of Khazad-dum and the coming of Durin's Bane.
38063: The tunnel winds its way through a mass of dark red stone, often turning, so that you find it difficult to know where you are going. A faint sound of fluttering wings can be heard from the north. You wonder what kind of bats might live in caves as deep as these.
38064: You are standing at a bifurcation in a long winding tunnel, leading to unknown places in the vast maze of Khazad-dum. One branch of the passage leads west and slightly up; the second, whose walls show a strange dark red tinge, goes south. Finally, a nearly vertical shaft leads down to another intersection.
38065: A large and somewhat round fungus grows from the floor.

You are squeezing yourself along a small, dark, twisting passage, whose floor is encrusted with bat droppings. The passage used to continue its way to the north, but someone has blocked it with a pile of heavy stones which have been blocked in their place by the passage of time. Now the only way out is east, or up along a rusty metal ladder.
38066: An iron pick has been dropped here.

You are in the southwestern corner of a very large cave. At the base of the greenish walls lie piles of small stones. A draft of cold air, coming from the east, flows into a hole in the ceiling, at the top of a half-rotten wooden stair.
38067: You are walking along a twisting, narrow minerary tunnel in the west of Khazad-dum. To the west the passage continues its tortuous way in the rock of the Misty Mountains. The tunnel once led to the east as well, but now only fallen rocks and gravel lie that way. Another exit leads down, on the rotten steps of a wooden stair, to a large cavern.
38068: A dirty shovel is lying on the ground here.

You have entered a small minerary tunnel, which enlarges to the north and continues its narrow course to the east. Here and there you can see the abandoned tools of the Dwarven miners, most of them completely ruined by the ravages of time. A faint air current flows in from the north.
38069: You are on a curving rampway which ascends to the west and descends to the south. The walls are rough-cut, and the surface is smooth but has had shallow grooves and undulations worn in it by the boots of generations of Dwarven miners.
38070: You are at the south end of a very long chamber which seems once to have provided bed space to the dwarves who worked in the mine. Niches on either side of a north-south corridor, arranged three high, seem to have provided bed space. These wall-bed spaces are actually neatly carved and may once have provided comfortable accommodations, from a dwarf's perspective at any rate. Every usable scrap of cloth, wood, or metal has been looted long ago.
38071: You are in a network of rooms which were once part of the operations of the Dwarven mine. Some seem to be supply rooms, others the personal quarters of important Dwarves. Most of the doors are either locked or blocked by rubble. However, a tunnel has been hacked through the area, piercing the walls of the rooms by brute force. From here it proceeds west and burrows into the natural stone; northward, it continues toward an unknown destination.
38072:
An eyeless white rat with nasty teeth scurries about.
An eyeless white rat with nasty teeth scurries about.
An eyeless white rat with nasty teeth scurries about.

You are at the north end of a very long room which was once the barracks of the Dwarven miners. At this end are the baths, latrines, and cooking facilities. The beds are carved into the long walls of the chamber which retreat southward into the darkness. There seems to be a large pile of rubble here in the latrine area.
38073: This appears to be a room of importance. Its walls are polished, and the junction between the walls and the ceiling is adorned by an ornamental frieze. There is wooden furniture here, including a long counter with a polished crystal top. Some paintings adorn the east wall. An arch with a design on the keystone leads west; to its left is what looks like a lock with four keyholes, mounted in the wall and with no connection to any obvious door. To the north a heavy grille blocks the way to the north, and a heavy steel door blocks the doorway to the south.
38074: This is a short corridor, whose walls are unadorned except for some vertical cracks or panels that run from floor to ceiling. The skeleton of an orc lies on the floor here; the bones seem to have been crushed flat in some way. There are some other marks, like heavy cart tracks, that seem to run across the corridor, from one wall to the other.
38075:
An eyeless white rat with nasty teeth scurries about.
An eyeless white rat with nasty teeth scurries about.
An eyeless white rat with nasty teeth scurries about.

This small room is lined by drawers which extend into the walls. Many of the drawers have been pulled out and left open. The construction of the drawers is very precise and sturdy indeed, and they still travel freely in their tracks centuries since they were last used. On the west side of the room, however, the drawers have been displaced from where a tunnel has been dug through the solid stone.
38076: A small black vicious rat squeaks at you for disturbing it.

This tunnel is very low, about three feet in height, with irregular walls and ceiling, and still contains much of the rubble that was created during its digging. Still, it seems to get some use. The gravel and stones on its floor are packed down, and there is sort of an animal smell.
38077: This was once the working face of a mine tunnel. It is partially hidden by shoring installed by the dwarves, and it must have been abandoned long before they dug too deep and uncovered the fell creature that chased them from their homes. The tunnel extends back to the west; some of the shoring has been removed, and a smaller tunnel has been dug to the east.
38078:
An orkish warrior of the Durghash is here, with a cruel glint in his eye.
A small black vicious rat squeaks at you for disturbing it.

This east-west mine tunnel has apparently suffered a partial collapse. Slabs have fallen from the ceiling and lie in heaps on both the north and south walls. A crevice stretches upward, inaccessible. The passage continues east and west.
38079: A great wolf with a sable coat glares around with red eyes.

This is a broad, plain mine tunnel with a pronounced downward slope to the west. The tunnel floor has little dust on it, but there are some odd bits of rubbish - bones, teeth, discarded useless armour...
38080:
An orkish warrior of the Durghash is here, with a cruel glint in his eye.
An orkish warrior of the Durghash is here, with a cruel glint in his eye.

The wet stone floor is very slippery at this point. As always in Moria, there are no handrails, so the stairs which begin here could be quite dangerous to walk down, especially in this darkness. The tunnel bends from the east to the north, descending all the time.
38082: The tunnel slopes upward to the west here. The air currents waver and change direction here. Now a cooler breeze will blow down from above, now a warmer, more humid, and more pungent air will waft up from below and eastward.
38083: This long stretch of tunnel has a very steep grade as it slowly curves to the west and south from this point. There is a slight current in the air here, a small draft rising from the southern area into the upper tunnels to the west, which carries the strong scent of death and decay from below. The walls and rock floor here show a few traces of the movement of orc patrols through this area, ranging from a broken speartip wedged into a wall crack to a pile of orc spoor directly underfoot.
38084:
A lurg leader, with markings of the Durghash tribe, stands here.
An orkish warrior of the Durghash is here, with a cruel glint in his eye.
An orkish warrior of the Durghash is here, with a cruel glint in his eye.
An orkish warrior of the Durghash is here, with a cruel glint in his eye.
A great wolf with a sable coat glares around with red eyes.
A great wolf with a sable coat glares around with red eyes.
A great wolf with a sable coat glares around with red eyes.

A steep north-south tunnel intersects with a narrow tunnel running to the east, forming this small junction chamber. The walls and roof here are split with wide cracks and large gaps in the ancient stonework, some of which have been patched in haphazard fashion with black mud and small stones. Orc scrawlings and symbols cover all surfaces here, some old and scratched out and others fresh and full of new malice.
38085:
A canoe has been left here.
A bulky cave troll is here, looking like a massive pile of stone.
A stone-grey troll advances toward you, with fury in its eyes.

This precarious passage plunges downward as it travels due south, and it eventually ends in a mass of rubble which completely blocks any further progress in that direction. The roof has given way here and may do so again at any time, and this prospect forces a retreat into the safer areas of the tunnel to the north.
38086: This narrow passage steadily descends as it travels from the east to the west. The floor is coated with a thick layer of decaying filth which results in very uncertain footing and a strong stench everywhere nearby. All walls are covered with bloody splotches, long scratches and depictions of the lidless Red Eye.
38087: The cramped passageway turns sharply west and north from this point, a small straight section of tunnel running past a massive irondoor set in the south wall. The passage rises and becomes wider to the west, and plunges down after it bends north where it appears to taper off to little more than a wide fissure in the rock. Most of the passage walls and floor are covered by filth, scratches and orc scrawlings, but the east wall has managed to avoid this fate.
38088: The walls of this tunnel close in tightly here, limiting passage to small groups of thin individuals travelling in single-file order. Much of the surrounding rock is quite sharp, and there are small drabs of dried blood on shard edges and spattered in spots on the ground. This tunnel appears to widen towards the south, but narrows even further to the north.
38089: There is not much to see in this very small and tight space. One creature can fit inside this crevice at any given time, and any attempt to squeeze another inside would result in pools of blood and screams. There are tight exits to the east and south, but care is required to move in any direction to avoid slicing flesh off on the hundreds of sharp rock shards here.
38090: The southern terminus of the rough, wide tunnel appears to be here at this small cul-de-sac formed by three highly polished black stone walls. None of the surfaces here has any mark or scratch, nor is there any debris littering the passageway which would indicate any recent use of this place. The tunnel climbs sharply north from this deadend, and it is wide enough to permit a few creatures to pass side-by-side as they travel upwards.
38091: The passage has become very wide here, wide enough for a small group to walk comfortably abreast either north or south. The grade of the passage is very steep for an underground passageway, and there are no signs that anyone has passed this point in a long, long time.
38092: A small black vicious rat squeaks at you for disturbing it.

The rough tunnel continues north and south here, passing through dark black veins of stone. The tunnel walls and roof appear rough-cut, showing little of the skill and care usually given by Dwarves to their stonecraft nor any sign that they were formed by some natural process of erosion. The tunnel slopes sharply downward as it plunges into utter blackness to the south.
38093: The passage comes to a dead-end rather abruptly in a heavily scored rock wall. There are no apparent exits, except the one through which you came. Though clearly being a mined passage, and not one formed by the forces of nature, it is obvious that those who once built this tunnel had no intention of making it a good job, leaving rough rocky walls and ground as they were as soon as the job of tunnelling through the hard rock had been finished. A rank smell fills the air and dampness clings to your clothes.
38094: The Foot of Some Winding Stairs

You are standing at the foot of a narrow, twisting stairway. It winds away up and into the dank fastness of the mountain rock. This small chamber appears unfinished and fairly crudely hewn - almost as if it was halted prematurely. Moisture hangs in the air giving a very damp feel to the place, though no puddles have formed. Seemingly, the dwarves who built these stairs aborted their work before it was finished, perhaps called away for other, more important tasks. This is also evidenced by the rough walls of the cavern; they have not yet been entirely smoothed and worked to a professional finish, like most other Dwarven tunnels.
38095: A small black vicious rat squeaks at you for disturbing it.

You are in a cramped and twisting tunnel which runs generally north and south. Its walls, floor, and ceiling are composed of loose rocks; the ceiling has been haphazardly shored with stone slabs and wooden posts. It is about four feet high at best, and repeatedly zigzags up, left, down and right, and in every combination of those. Here and there it bores through a more solid wall or takes advantage of a pre-existing doorway. A sharp, animal reek is everywhere.
38096:
A small black vicious rat squeaks at you for disturbing it.
A small black vicious rat squeaks at you for disturbing it.

You are in a room which was formerly an old mine tunnel or gallery, whose long dimension runs east and west. Long ago it was apparently abandoned and filled with loose stone. Much of the stone was later removed again, but the floor is still very irregular and composed of large and small rocks packed together. The room is pervaded by the smells of urine, dung, and rotting flesh.
38097:
An orkish warrior of the Durghash is here, with a cruel glint in his eye.
A small black vicious rat squeaks at you for disturbing it.
A small black vicious rat squeaks at you for disturbing it.

You are in part of an old mine tunnel which was later re-filled with loose stone. Some of the stone has been removed here to make a bowl-shaped space, whose floor and sides are made of compacted rocks and whose ceiling is the roof of the Dwarven tunnel. The stones of the floor, however, are buried in layers of bones, dung, and animal hair. The pungent reek of animal urine is overpowering.
38098:
An orkish warrior of the Durghash is here, with a cruel glint in his eye.
A small black vicious rat squeaks at you for disturbing it.
A large bat is here, hanging in the darkness.
An orkish warrior of the Durghash is here, with a cruel glint in his eye.

You are in what may be an old mine tunnel junction, but the area is so piled with clutter that it is hard to get a clear sense of where the walls are. Ore carts and skids, bins, metal beams, stone slabs, and the like have been thrown upon each other in a terrible hodge-podge. A sort of burrow snakes through the pile from east to west.
38099: This is a steep tunnel which spirals counterclockwise and downward. By sliding along the walls it is possible to keep your balance here. The smudges on the outside wall suggest that others have done the same before you.
38100:
An orkish warrior of the Durghash is here, with a cruel glint in his eye.
An orkish warrior of the Durghash is here, with a cruel glint in his eye.

The tunnel's steepness is accentuated by a layer of slick slimy mud which has been deposited by a trickle of foul-smelling water which leaks from the tunnel's wall. To remedy the situation, it seems that someone has hacked crude steps or footholds in the stone of the tunnel floor.
38101:
A small black vicious rat squeaks at you for disturbing it.
A small white snake slithers along the ground.
A small white snake slithers along the ground.
A small white snake slithers along the ground.

This is the eastern end of a mine gallery which here intersects a north-south access tunnel. The stone floor, however, is covered with foul hard soil, and furthermore is heavily littered with bones and trash. Overhead is a black, square, inaccessible hole; in the floor is a similar hole covered with an immovable iron grating. Over this grating a makeshift stone hearth has been constructed. Red embers glow dully, and their light does nothing to brighten the room.
38102: A small black vicious rat squeaks at you for disturbing it.

This is a stretch of tunnel about forty feet long which is blocked by a crude wall of loose stone and wood scraps to the south. At the north end is a stairwell with flights of steps going up and down. A heavy wooden bin, which seems as old as the room itself, contains some scimitars, daggers, and shields.
38103: A small vicious black rat squeaks at you for disturbing it.

Much of the floor of the access tunnel here is piled with large stones which clatter loudly against each other as you tread on them. There is little here of interest. The air is stuffy, damp, and thick with a pervasive foul smell.
38104:
An orkish female is here, spitting and glaring at you.
An orkish female is here, spitting and glaring at you.
An orkish female is here, spitting and glaring at you.
An orkish female is here, spitting and glaring at you.
A small white snake slithers along the ground.
A small white snake slithers along the ground.
A small vicious black rat squeaks at you for disturbing it.
A lurg leader, with markings of the Durghash tribe, stands here.

This chamber, which is really just a featureless dead end in a stone tunnel, is evidently used as a sleeping area. Large, filthy pelts are strewn about, and there are some wads of bloody and matted cloth which may once have been garments. You see no luxuries or even furniture.
38105:
The corpse of a dire wolf is lying here.
A large and somewhat round fungus grows from the floor.
A large and somewhat round fungus grows from the floor.

The smell of offal and excrement is overpowering here. This room may once have been used for storage of tools or for the administration of the mine, but now it is a combination garbage dump and latrine. A hole in the floor, about a foot across, leads down into the depths; this is where the waste is supposed to go, it seems, but not all of it has gone there yet.
38106: A great wolf with a sable coat glares around with red eyes.

You are at a landing on a stairway which descends as a square-cornered helix around a central pillar. The steps going up from here are blocked by a huge chunk of stone which has fallen in from the walls. Other cracks mark the walls of the stairwell here. A low, narrow corridor with an arched cross section goes south from the landing.
38107: A low and narrow passage with an arched roof makes a right-angled turn here. On the west wall of the angle, a niche has been crudely cut where some people could stand unobserved from the passage to the north. In addition, an ore cart has been propped on its end as shelter for the niche. The passage continues to the east.
38108:
An orkish warrior of the Durghash is here, with a cruel glint in his eye.
An orkish warrior of the Durghash is here, with a cruel glint in his eye.
An orc, of the Durghash tribe, crouches here.
An orc, of the Durghash tribe, crouches here.
A small vicious black rat squeaks at you for disturbing it.
A pair of tiny eyes gleam at you from the shadows.
A pair of tiny eyes gleam at you from the shadows.

This room may once have had some something to do with the processing of ore; that would account for the long stone troughs and the water that trickles down from a pipe. Now, however, the most prominent feature is the rotting severed heads, stuck on stakes, which decorate this end of the room. The orkish commander who has taken this for his quarters finds nothing so pleasant as the heads of his enemies of other orc tribes or of his own. A guard post has also been established here in the north end of the room.
38109:
An orkish female is here, spitting and glaring around her.
An orkish female is here, spitting and glaring around her.
An orkish female is here, spitting and glaring around her.
A commanding Durghash is here, cruelly eyeing the surroundings.

The south end of this long room has been taken over by the commander of this Durghash outpost for his personal use. Here are his stew pots, his pelts, and the skins and teeth of his enemies. Here is a cooking fire using real wood from the outside. Here is his private food supply, well stocked when every other orc is hungry.
38110: You are on a stone staircase which ascends by means of short flights, north, east, south, and west, around a cylindrical central pillar. The work is not elegant, but precise. Below you, however, the stairway has been filled with loose boulders up to eighteen inches across. There is no way to descend the stairs. However, by the landing here is a slanting door which may conceal a downward-leading path.
38111:
A gaunt, filthy orc is here, looking around him with insane eyes.
An eyeless white rat with nasty teeth scurries about.
An eyeless white rat with nasty teeth scurries about.
An eyeless white rat with nasty teeth scurries about.

This was once the top of a metal-walled chute, but it was blocked long ago, either by a rockfall or by deliberately jamming it with stone. The upper four feet of the chute are now a cramped, stinking cell. The irregular boulders forming its floor are caked with body waste. In a cavity between two rocks you see a corpse, and some other bones are scattered around.
38112: An orkish warrior of the Durghash is here, with a cruel glint in his eye.

Squeezing your way in to this very narrow passage, the fact is made obvious that it was not made for everyday travel. Lots of dust has accumulated here, and the sharp, rocky walls almost seem to get closer to you each second. The passage seems to continue to the east but you cannot make out if it gets even more narrow or if it widens up. The north wall seems to be a door of some sort.
38113: A huge lever is embedded in the north wall.

This is a small compartment, empty except for some peculiar metal objects partially embedded in the north wall. These include a lever which sticks out of the wall. The craftsmanship is clearly Dwarven, but the mechanism seems to have been recently greased.
38114: This access passage could not have been spacious even for dwarves; for larger beings it is a tight squeeze indeed. There is a wider space in the middle, though, which someone seems to occupy much of the time. At any rate, there is a water pot, some discarded bones, and a distinct smell of urine.
38115:
A commanding Durghash is here, cruelly eyeing the surroundings.
A lurg leader, with markings of the Durghash tribe, stands here.
An orkish warrior of the Durghash is here, with a cruel glint in his eye.
An orkish warrior of the Durghash is here, with a cruel glint in his eye.
An orkish warrior of the Durghash is here, with a cruel glint in his eye.
An orkish warrior of the Durghash is here, with a cruel glint in his eye.
An orkish warrior of the Durghash is here, with a cruel glint in his eye.

This is obviously some sort of guard room, useless trash lying all about the place. The centre of the cavern is dominated by a large stone table, with crude wooden chairs and benches surrounding it. A few benches also line the walls of this room, some tilted over and pushed aside. You quickly dismiss any ideas of resting on any of the chairs or benches as you notice a thick layer of greasy dirt covering all of them, as well as the table. Briefly rummaging through the disarray of litter and odd items, you find absolutely nothing of value. A narrow set of stairs occupies the northeast corner, spiralling tightly upward into a dark chamber.
38116: A narrow spiral staircase emerges into this small cavernous chamber. Intended as some sort of watchpost, several peepholes cover the walls. A pair of largish boulders seem to serve as crude chairs and similar to the chamber below, the place has pieces of junk strewn across the floor. The only slightly useful items in this room are a couple of sturdy planks, something the guards probably had intended to use to fashion a simple table, but now they have obviously been abandoned, along with the project. Edging closer to one of the holes and peering through, you see nothing but darkness.
38117: A pair of tiny eyes gleam at you from the shadows.

This is the northwestern corner of a huge stone chamber. The chamber is natural except for the flagstones covering the floor. Peering around you into the dark corners of this immense cavern you see a road running away into the blackness to the north, a narrower passage sloping downwards to the west and the cavern itself opening to the east and south.
38118:
The corpse of an orkish warrior is lying here.
The corpse of an orkish warrior is lying here.

You are at a bend in a passage which slowly climbs up from the Deeps. From here it runs upwards to the east, and down to the south. The tunnel seems to open up to a larger cave to the east and your footsteps echo hollowly in that direction. Small, sharp, splintered rocks lie scattered in the corner of the slowly turning tunnel.
38119:
A lurg leader, with markings of the Durghash tribe, stands here.
An orkish warrior of the Durghash is here, with a cruel glint in his eye.
An orkish warrior of the Durghash is here, with a cruel glint in his eye.

You stand on a smooth roadway running north-south. About five paces in width, it is not one of Moria's widest and it also seems to be fairly unused. Traces of long since aborted mining are evident here, reminding you of the days when dwarves ruled this ruined, gloomy underground complex.
38120: You find yourself at the bottom of a large rampway with a low ceiling. The tunnel climbs very steeply to the east: you realise that the ascent will be hard, especially if you are carrying a heavy load. To the south a short corridor will bring you to a dark passage.
38121: This wide underground chamber is a landing separating two steep stretches of road. To the south a broad ramp with a median strip climbs rapidly; to the west a similar ramp steeply descends. Rotten remnants of rope are still to be found here, attached to bolts or wound on great wooden spools. Much hauling must have been done here to bring great weights up from the lower levels.
38122: Vertical shafts are seen here and there along the sides of this underground road. They are about five hundred feet apart and square, six feet on a side; there is no telling how far down they go. Each is surrounded by a granite curb; on some such, metal mounts for lifts or hoists are still to be seen. Such appliances have been removed or destroyed, and there is no way to descend. From one shaft comes a faint whiff of rotting flesh.
38123: This smooth-surfaced road ascends to the west, adjusting its course according to the types of rock the builders encountered in excavating the tunnel. Here it makes a southward loop to circumvent a great mass of dead-black stone, with the glass-like fracture of obsidian but without the lustre. Here and there a short mine tunnel leaves the road to the north, but piles of rock on the floor discourage you from entering.
38124: You are on a smooth dark-surfaced road, unadorned except for the white veining in the black stone of the pavement. The road seems to pass over a sort of hump or rise here.
38125: The tunnel bends sharply downward as it curves broadly from the west to the north. Its floor and the lower three feet of its side walls seem to be made of black marble and are polished to a high and slippery gloss. There are a pair of eyebolts screwed in the wall on either side. A side passage from the east joins the main tunnel in its downward plunge. You hear a distinct rumbling sound coming up the tunnel from the north.
38126: Here, where an important road surfaced in black stone originally turned from the south to the west, there has been a massive slippage of the mountain's rock. The westward course of the road seems to stop short at a solid cliff. The whole northwest face of the Silvertine must have settled downward twenty feet to create this thorough a blockage. Perhaps it was undermined by careless excavations. A branch of the dark road turns eastward and downward here. There is some writing on the inside wall of this bend.
38127: You are about a foot away from a fatal plunge into a black and horrifying abyss. The treacherous road plunges sharply down and becomes a sheer drop-off. Below you is a roaring cauldron of water; the spume leaps up and licks hungrily at your face and hands. You are holding yourself in place by using a minuscule toehold in the angle between the floor and the wall of the tunnel. Unless you are as confident a stoneclimber as the original builders of this place, the trembling rock will probably shake you loose quite soon...
38128:
A beautiful and docile horse is standing here.
A lurg leader, with markings of the Durghash tribe, stands here.
A great wolf with a sable coat glares around with red eyes.
A great wolf with a sable coat glares around with red eyes.
A great wolf with a sable coat glares around with red eyes.
An orkish warrior of the Durghash is here, with a cruel glint in his eye.
An orkish warrior of the Durghash is here, with a cruel glint in his eye.
An orkish warrior of the Durghash is here, with a cruel glint in his eye.

The smooth-surfaced road continues north and south from here, sloping downward to the north. Here the road is partially blocked by a group of skids which are piled high with rock. Each skid is about fourteen feet long and eight feet wide, and they have clearly been in their present position for a very long time. On the west side of the tunnel is the open mouth of a chute of some kind which leads down from above.
38129:
A strange bat-like creature is flitting around.
A strange bat-like creature is flitting around.
A strange bat-like creature is flitting around.
A strange bat-like creature is flitting around.

A strange bat-like creature is flitting around.

You stand on a narrow ledge at the top of a stairwell. The well is formed from a smooth-sided shaft, about which a narrow stone stair spirals down into the dark. A small stone door opens to the north, being the only exit besides the steps leading down the circular chute. As you walk about the edges of the chamber you notice that the ground is covered with what looks like bat droppings. The ceiling disappears into the darkness above, and you wonder how far up this shaft ascends. Maybe just a stone throw, but perhaps even all the way to the surface of the mountain? This last idea seems appealing, and is fortified by the cold but refreshing wind that drifts through this cavern. You have no way of knowing for sure though, as the walls are virtually unclimbable, and the darkness above you leaves no clues.
38130: The tunnel rises in a spiral curve to the west, while it straightens out to the east and continues to descend at a slow rate. A rivulet from the west spreads over the floor, then trickles down a shaft. Echoes of the water's splashing fall reverberate from below. There are many tracks in the mud here, some very recent.
38131: The floor in this part of the tunnel is muddy and quite slippery, requiring some caution to avoid a nasty spill. The passageway descends slowly as it runs from west to east, becoming less muddy as it drops. There are many signs of recent passage through this point: groups of several types of tracks leading in both directions, bits of hide and splintered wood trampled into the mud, and large red circles splashed onto the north wall. A closer examination reveals sets of orc, troll and wolf tracks and bits of decaying flesh and shattered bone in several spots nearby.
38132: A large bat is here, hanging in the darkness (hidden).

The slope of the tunnel changes rather dramatically at this point, from a steep descent to the east to a gradual easy climb to the west. It appears that the passage suffered damage from an ancient earth tremor which bent its course and increased the drop-off, ruining its original straight and smooth descent. Piles of rubble and other debris still choke the tunnel in several places but the way is quite wide and high and it is still easy to pass through the more congested areas. Both tunnel walls are webbed with large cracks and covered with strange scrawlings and pigments which have added here very recently.
38133:
A small vicious black rat squeaks at you for disturbing it.
A small vicious black rat squeaks at you for disturbing it.

The structural integrity of the tunnel appears to be very dubious here. Large cracked sections of wall and roof are held in place by rusted iron supports wedged into shallow holes cut into the floor, and these seem ready to give way to the pressure of the surrounding stone at any time. The passage climbs up a very steep and rock-strewn grade as it travels from east to west, but someone has cut some footholds into the rock which speed passage over the steepest sections. Every few minutes, a small stone works its way loose and clatters away down the slope to the east.
38134: This steeply sloping passage ends just to the east at a solid mass of rubble resulting from the complete collapse of the roof. The walls and roof nearby have been shored-up with rusty iron poles and stone slabs in an attempt to forestall further collapse, but a light tremor would surely bring the rest of the tunnel down in an instant. The passage proceeds due west up a very steep rocky incline, and there is a wide, sturdy irondoor set into the north wall of the tunnel a few paces from here.
38135:
An orkish warrior of the Durghash is here, with a cruel glint in his eye.
A great wolf with a sable coat glares around with red eyes.
A great wolf with a sable coat glares around with red eyes.
A lurg leader, with markings of the Durghash tribe, stands here.
A bulky cave troll is here, looking like a massive pile of stone.

The Durghash have enlarged a small cave here, adding a few benches and tables, torch stays on each wall and a crude metal drum for raising an alarm. They have set a heavy fire-forged irondoor upon huge hinges in the centre of the southern wall and painted a large orc's head containing the Red Eye symbol upon the door's surface. The room is lit by smoking torches placed within the wall stays, their dim light revealing the terrible squalor so characteristic of all orc dwellings. A small cave lies to the west of the irondoor, and there is a large passage leading away towards the north.
38136:
A commanding Durghash is here, cruelly appraising you.
A lurg leader, with markings of the Durghash tribe, stands here.

This small cavern serves as a meeting place for the Lurg leaders. They have been provided with a fine stone table of Dwarven make along with a set of carved stone seats, a large pile of animal skins, plenty of choice food and drink, and a cache of choice weapons to use at their whim. The table is still covered by the remains of a recent meal, along with stacks of parchments and hide scrolls which contain conquest plans and maps of surrounding territories. There is one exit from this place, a large opening in the east wall leading into a lighted chamber a few paces away.
38137: This end of the wide tunnel is clogged with debris ranging from giant leg bones to twisted fragments of rusted metal vats. Most of the refuse has been pushed from the centre of the passage toward the sides, allowing careful travel to the west and south from this point. The odour of decay and death is strong here, and the clamour made by a large group of orcs echoes down the passage from somewhere nearby.
38138: A large cave troll sniffs the air, sensing an intruder is near.

A wide and well-travelled tunnel curves from the north into the east here, just outside a giant-sized stone archway which leads west into a lighted cavern. A raucous clamour rises from the cavern to the west and filters down from the northern section of tunnel, meeting here in a confusing cacophony of sounds. All passage surfaces are covered with orc scrawlings and tribal symbols, the sign for the Red Eye being especially prominent among them.
38139:
A small and well-kept fire lights and warms the room.
An orkish female is here, spitting and glaring around her.
An orkish female is here, spitting and glaring around her.
An orc, of the Durghash tribe, crouches here.
An orc, of the Durghash tribe, crouches here.

This large, fire-lit hall is the centre of much of the tribal activity of the Durghash orcs. Several fires burn here, providing low light and some heat which the many orcs here appear to enjoy immensely. There are tunnels in the north, south and west walls of the cavern, and a large stone archway which leads into a large tunnel to the east.
38140:
A huge, smoking campfire is burning here.
An orkish cook is trying to sell old food here.
An orkish female is here, spitting and glaring at you.
An orkish female is here, spitting and glaring at you.
An orc, of the Durghash tribe, crouches here.
