An orc, of the Durghash tribe, crouches here.
A small vicious black rat squeaks at you for disturbing it.
A small vicious black rat squeaks at you for disturbing it.

This large cavern is cluttered with rude benches, tables and troughs. Along the southern wall, spits turn over an array of great firepits which cook the unfortunates killed by the orcs this day. Many screaming Durghash orcs crowd this place, the main eating hall of their vicious tribe.
38141:
An orkish warrior of the Durghash is here, with a cruel glint in his eye.
An orkish warrior of the Durghash is here, with a cruel glint in his eye.
An orkish warrior of the Durghash is here, with a cruel glint in his eye.
An orc, of the Durghash tribe, crouches here.

The orcs have enlarged a wide tunnel bend here, forming an L-shaped room with exits east and south. Some recessed seats have been carved into niches in the walls, and these are used as watch stations. The Durghash here have been instructed to check the identity of all who pass this point, making certain that they are in good standing with their leader.
38142: The walls of this round cavern are honeycombed with small berths which are used as bunks by the Durghash. A few dark-skinned orcs are sleeping fitfully in the berths, looking as though they may wake at any moment. A burly, scar- covered warden resides here permanently by order of Shaghosh, watching over his sleeping patrons and guarding their valuables as if they were his own.
38143:
A rather heavy clay jar stands here.
A circular stone well has been built here.
An orc, of the Durghash tribe, crouches here.
An orc, of the Durghash tribe, crouches here.

A small side cave holds the large cistern which satisfies the Durghash tribe's water requirements. The cistern is ringed by large boulders which have been sealed together with dark mud and topped with spearpoints, this to prevent orcs from leaning in to drink directly from the tribal water supply. A heavy clay pot fastened onto the end of a rusted iron chain lies here, to be used to draw a small amount of slimy water from the cistern under the watchful eyes of the orcs who guard the cistern against poison.
38144: This broad north-south passageway is black and cluttered with filth, two sure signs that it has been heavily travelled by the orcs who live in these caves. Pieces of rotted flesh and bone, smears of dung and broken bits of stone and metal decorate the floor, walls and even roof here, what a sight to behold! A screeching din from a frenzied horde of orcs echoes from the lighted hall at the north end of the tunnel while a more muted racket originates in the south.
38145: The general geometry of this tunnel indicates that it was probably originally a Dwarven delving that has been modified over the course of many years to accommodate the abuse that the Durghash tribe delivers to anything it uses. The floor is now a garbage-filled trough, probably home to disease-ridden vermin and carrion consumers, and the walls have been chipped and damaged to the point that they appear untouched by a chisel. The Durghash have painted the Red Eye and other clan symbols on every available surface in a bid to let all know who controls this place and all in it. The tunnel continues due east and descends slightly as it travels west into a loud din of noise.
38146: This wide and tall tunnel has been worn away by many years of heavy traffic and abuse. A set of deep grooves has been chipped into the floor by the tramp of boots and grind of stone on stone, and the tunnel walls and roof are covered with scrawlings and scratches of all kinds. The tunnel turns south here into a small and smoky chamber, and runs west towards the source of some shouting.
38147:
An orc, of the Durghash tribe, crouches here.
An orc, of the Durghash tribe, crouches here.
An orkish warrior of the Durghash is here, with a cruel glint in his eye.
A lurg leader, with markings of the Durghash tribe, stands here.
A bulky cave troll is here, looking like a massive pile of stone.
A bulky cave troll is here, looking like a massive pile of stone.

A small cave has been hewn square and fitted with benches and a sturdy irondoor set in the west wall to serve as a guarded gateway into the Durghash's caves. There is a small smoking fire in one corner which casts a feeble glow on the surroundings here revealing some tattered wolfskins, a crude metal drum and spoiled food scattered about on the ground. A large passageway begins to the north and just to the east, another small cave beckons.
38148:
A small and well-kept fire lights and warms the room.
An orkish female is here, spitting and glaring at you.
An orc, of the Durghash tribe, crouches here.
An orc, of the Durghash tribe, crouches here.

This small foursquare room was probably originally used by the Moria dwarves as a storage room for mining equipment and ores, but the Durghash have decided to use it for more important purposes. The walls are honeycombed with cleverly constructed racks once used to store tools, but which are now filled with sharp knives, whips, irons and other pain-inflicting tools used by the orcs who have come to love torture. There is a large firepit in the cave's centre which is currently heating branding irons used in ritual scarmaking, slave torture or simple murder, whichever the orcs here desire most. A sturdy metal cagedoor is centred in the north wall, and a stone arch opens into a chamber to the west.
38149: This small tunnel twists downward, continues for a few paces, then ends in a small cul-de-sac. Apparently, there is nowhere to go other than back west.
38150:
An orkish warrior of the Durghash is here, with a cruel glint in his eye.
An orkish warrior of the Durghash is here, with a cruel glint in his eye.

A rocky cavern descends into the south from here. The dark walls are festooned with paintings of blood-red eyes and crude scenes of orc-dominated slaughter, as well as a few dried scalps of orcs, trolls and other creatures. There is a wide circle of stones here with the remains of a large fire within, surrounded by the residue of a large orc-meal and many, many Durghash tracks. Loud screams echo from the cavern to the south, perhaps there are some Durghash there still? A cracked and chipped stone portal leads into a small tunnel to the east.
38151:
An orc, of the Durghash tribe, crouches here.
An orc, of the Durghash tribe, crouches here.
An orc, of the Durghash tribe, crouches here.
An orkish warrior of the Durghash is here, with a cruel glint in his eye.
An orkish warrior of the Durghash is here, with a cruel glint in his eye.
An orkish warrior of the Durghash is here, with a cruel glint in his eye.

This large L-shaped cavern is filled with the cries of orcs gathered about the rim of a deep pit which occupies its southern half. The wall above the pit is stained red, and has a large lidless Eye fashioned from gleaming skulls outlined upon it. The other walls and floor are covered with obscene scrawls, bones, rotted entrails and other items of interest to orcs. There is a narrow set of descending steps and an irongate to the west, while the main cavern continues to the north and east from here.
38152:
An orkish female is here, spitting and glaring around her.
An orc, of the Durghash tribe, crouches here.
An orkish warrior of the Durghash is here, with a cruel glint in his eye.
An orkish warrior of the Durghash is here, with a cruel glint in his eye.
An orkish warrior of the Durghash is here, with a cruel glint in his eye.

A large oval-shaped cavern continues east and west from this point. The walls here are covered with various orkish symbols and scrawls, just as the cave floor is covered with a thick layer of orkish refuse. There are many stone slabs which serve as benches for the Durghash who sit above the rim of the deep pit in the southern half of this cave. The sharp sounds of a pitched battle ring out from the pit, while the spectator orcs scream out curses and spit at the unfortunates trapped below them.
38153:
An orkish warrior of the Durghash is here, with a cruel glint in his eye.
An orkish warrior of the Durghash is here, with a cruel glint in his eye.

Many different veins of various ores and stones are embedded into the stone walls of this cave. It is as if all of the basic elements have collided at this nexus point under the mountain to form an underground rainbow showing all of the beauty possible in stone. Of course, the Durghash have done their best to rob the most valuable pockets of their ores, but so far the sheer bounty of Arda has outstripped their greed. This magnificent junction runs east and west into large open caverns and south into a smaller chamber.
38154:
An orkish warrior of the Durghash is here, with a cruel glint in his eye.
An orkish warrior of the Durghash is here, with a cruel glint in his eye.
An orkish warrior of the Durghash is here, with a cruel glint in his eye.

This huge place is just one part of an immense cavern which continues far into darkness east and south of you. The cavern roof tapers down from some vast height to join into the north wall, forming a large tunnel far to the west. The air here seems to swirl and eddy, alive with silent motion and perhaps deadly intent. There are a few scrapes and scratches on the walls, and maybe a faint trace of old blood on some boulders here and there just within sight.
38155: Two gargantuan rock slabs meet here in the northeast corner of this cavern, which is surely one of the largest in all Moria. The cavewalls stretch from this point far up into the darkness overhead and seem to race towards some black infinity both west and south. The floor is riven by many large fissures which belch flames and sulphurous gases, probably resulting from some kind of volcanic vent running under the rock here. The fires and gases produce a strange rhythmic cacophony, almost a kind of speech from molten powers of Arda which must have found a home here long before the Dwarves came.
38156: A small natural passage slopes downward, continues several paces east then ends abruptly in a cul-de-sac. Apparently, there is nowhere to go other than back towards the cavern to the west.
38157: The southeast section of this grand cavern is filled with many natural stalagmite pillars which appear to burst upwards from the sandy soil of the floor below. These sharp rocky formations are slick with dripping water which feels warm to the touch, precluding thoughts of climbing upward to gain a better view. The sandy soil shows signs of recent passage and some wide grooves as well, and one cannot help but notice several big holes in the loose soil near the southern wall. The cavern continues to the west and north.
38158:
An albino fish is swimming here, looking for some food.
An albino fish is swimming here, looking for some food.

This part of the huge cavern appears to be its lowest section, and is partially filled with slime-covered dark water which trickles in from the east. The black water fills the southern portion of this place, but you cannot judge its depth near the south wall where it seems to be deepest. A muddy shore surrounds the black lake to the north and east, and from there you can see that the water does indeed support some kind of life.
38159:
An orkish warrior of the Durghash is here, with a cruel glint in his eye.
An orkish warrior of the Durghash is here, with a cruel glint in his eye.

This perfectly round chamber has been carefully chiselled from the smooth grey stone by Dwarven hands. Four small tunnel openings were initially made in the walls, but the ones to the east and west have been sealed off with tons of collapsed grey stone. The oblong portal north leads into a dark cave, while the rectangular portal south opens onto a large ascending staircase. Some runes in the Angerthas Moria style have been carved into the smooth stone just below the roof of the chamber.
38160: A steep flight of small stone steps curves downward from west to north. The walls here are covered with some defaced murals which depict laughing dwarves sitting in piles of gems. Many of the Dwarven images have been hacked out of the wall, apparently in spite of their creators.
38161: This underground roadway tunnels onward, deeper and deeper into the bowels of the mountain, steadily descending to the east. The wide, dark road's smooth rock surface is pitted only in a few scattered places. The tunnel twists and bends slightly during its east-west course and a feeling of gloom descends upon you as the stony walls of this rocky passageway appear to press in on you, seemingly regarding you as an intruder in a forbidden territory.
38162: The passage bends from north to east, still gently sloping; upward to the north and downward to the east. Pieces of trash have been carelessly thrown about the tunnel, either by orcs or trolls, the cavern's current inhabitants. A rancid smell fills your nostrils and as you look about you see several pieces of rotting meat lying off to one side. Disgusted, you turn your attention to your business. At the south end of the corridor, some mystical large wooden structure occupies a shallow cavern. Built from thick wooden logs, it seems very much out of place in these otherwise bleak tunnels.
38165:
A gaunt, filthy orc is here, looking around him with insane eyes.
A gaunt, filthy orc is here, looking around him with insane eyes.

From inside this cramped, filthy pen, the outside world seems ten thousand leagues distant. The roof is so low that even a young dwarf could not stand erect in here, and there is no area that is cleared of sharp rock and bones which could serve as a seat. There are many small piles of bones around, most gnawed beyond recognition or smashed into tiny pieces. To the south, a fired metal cagedoor with a sturdy lock bars any escape.
38166:
A small bat flies silently from shadow to shadow (hidden).
An orkish warrior of the Durghash is here, with a cruel glint in his eye.

A cramped and rock-filled tunnel leads a short distance from the main cavern and ends just north at a smooth solid rockwall. Several sharp boulders jut out from the walls and roof overhead, threatening to slash pieces from any creature that would try to run past them. Only the tight passage which threads to the south leads out of this place.
38167: Stone Bridge Spanning the Red Eye

This narrow stone bridge is the greatest successful architectural feat ever attempted by the orcs of Moria. A single slab of thick grey stone was thrust across this gaping chasm of molten rock and flame, known as the Red Eye to the Durghash tribe. Thick sideguards of mud were then built up over years to protect those who cross from the intense heat and fumes here, and a small opening was cut through the bridge at its centre and covered over. The grey stone must rapidly disperse the heat it absorbs from below as it is only warm to the touch, though the surroundings are extremely hot. The centre of the Red Eye is visible through the stonegrille in the centre of this bridge, which runs thirty lengths from the Great Hall in the west to the Temple in the east.
38168: In the Heart of the Red Eye

Flames and molten rock swirl around you, as you plunge toward the centre of chaos. An evil laugh rings in your brain, the last coherent thought you experience before exploding into flame above a lake of fire.
38169: An Ancient Black Altar stands in the centre of the room.

This Temple is known and feared as the centre of worship of the Dark Lord by his forces in Moria. It is rumoured that He caused the Red Eye to open here, giving the great gift of molten fire to the Durghash so that they might overcome all who oppose Him and serve his will more capably. This place has been painted with the blood of thousands of sacrificed captives, so that all the surfaces are now a rusty reddish brown colour. A great black altar located near the centre of the cave is the only item that is not stained red. This large temple is surprisingly clean, indicating that the Durghash dispose of the remains of their victims by casting them into the Red Eye to the west.
38170: A vein of molten rock surfaces from a small chasm in the southern half of this large cavern. The Durghash have managed to create an area for the magma to pool, and this allows them to smelt ore and produce metal for weapons in large stone vats which seem able to withstand very high temperatures. Stations have been created for crushing ore and old iron, then melting and recasting it into a wide variety of shapes. Needless to say, it is extremely hot in this area and poisonous fumes escape from the molten rock and metal. It is possible to pass through here into a wide tunnel to the east or into another set of smaller caves which connects to the west.
38171: An orc, of the Durghash tribe, crouches here.

The tunnel twists and turns, bending erratically from the north to the west where it ends at a large and very hot cavern. There are many tracks in the sandy soil on the tunnel floor, a good indication that this tunnel is often used heavily by the Durghash.
38172:
An orc, of the Durghash tribe, crouches here.
A lurg leader, with markings of the Durghash tribe, stands here.
An orkish warrior of the Durghash is here, with a cruel glint in his eye.
An orkish warrior of the Durghash is here, with a cruel glint in his eye.

This wide tunnel connects to the Forge Door several paces east of here, and bends several times before finally plunging downward and into the south. The passage is littered with rotted food scraps and torn fur, and the walls are covered with crudely scratched pictures and other orkish obscenities.
38173:
A lurg leader, with markings of the Durghash tribe, stands here.
An orkish warrior of the Durghash is here, with a cruel glint in his eye.
An orkish warrior of the Durghash is here, with a cruel glint in his eye.

This place is a medium-sized rough-hewn cell which has been equipped with stone benches, a small stoneblock table and a crude metal drum. The most prominent feature here is the sturdy irondoor centred in the north wall, upon which a large lidless Redeye rising over an anvil has been painted. Dim light is provided by five torches set horizontally in holes cut into the walls at regular intervals. Possible exits are north through the irondoor, west into a wide tunnel or east into another smaller chamber.
38174:
A twisted spear is lying on the ground.
A small bow, made of a dark wood, lies here.
A long, single-edged sword lies on the ground.
A lurg leader, with markings of the Durghash tribe, stands here.
A bulky cave troll is here, looking like a massive pile of stone.

The Lurg leaders of the patrol which mans the Forge Door have made this small cave their barracks. The walls are covered by huge black warg furs, giving the illusion of a vast blackness engulfing everything here. There is a set of three giants' skulls set against the wall in the northwest corner, probably used as secure storage by the greedy Lurgs. Several abandoned weapons lean up against the west wall, within quick reach of anyone here. The only obvious exit is back through the opening to the west.
38175: The wide tunnel makes a few detours to the north and south, but still travels generally east to west. The twists and turns cannot hide the steep descent to the west, but they make it difficult to remain sure of the exact direction of travel. This particular section of passageway is dark and quiet now, however a close inspection of the walls and floor reveals many scrapes on the rocks here which seem to indicate recent use of this tunnel.
38176: The wide, smooth section of tunnel bending toward the north stands in stark contrast to the uneven sloping section which winds its way east from here. It appears that this passage was delved by two separate groups of builders with vastly differing abilities at different points in the history of Moria. The older stonework is surely Dwarven in origin: smooth, true and built to last, while the newer work is functional but very erratic in quality and design. It seems that the older tunnel may have been partially destroyed by a strong earth tremor, then later rebuilt by the new residents in rather haphazard fashion.
38177: A sharp east-south curve has been hacked from the black rock of the mountain's underbelly. A few crude iron support bars have been driven into rock here, barely succeeding in holding large, loose crags in place. There are scattered bone fragments among the debris which clutters the passage here, and a faint stench of decay greets all who round this bend.
38178: The footing and general condition of this tunnel are quite poor. Jagged rock fragments jut out from the tunnel walls and large dips and cracks in the floor make every step an adventure. Fortunately, the tunnel is very wide so you can pick your way through the rougher spots with a little care and can avoid the worst pitfalls. The tunnel climbs to the east and descends to the west from this point.
38179: This crude passage is large enough to allow a party of stone giants to pass through comfortably. The floor here is marked by rough scrapes and gouges, indicating that very heavy stones were dragged through by some brute power recently. The passage rapidly descends into darkness to the west, and passes through a jagged opening into a large hall just east of this spot.
38180: Steep Bend in the Sloping Passage

The rough passage curves north to east, climbing sharply to the north. Many grooves have been worn into the rock here, possibly due to very heavy portage through this bend. The black walls appear to have been smashed back to enlarge this passage from some smaller tunnel, as there is a large amount of black slag cluttering the floor near the base of the side walls.
38181: The spacious passage climbs steadily from east to west at this point. There are many crude scrawlings and drawings on the sidewalls, most depicting huge things smashing other smaller creatures with large boulders, along with large hordes of dark beasts circling a large red eye. Two huge skulls have been arranged under this particular drawing, both with large holes smashed through their crowns. The stench of decay lingers in the air here.
38182: Here the tunnel suddenly and sharply bends east to south, descending steadily as it curves south. There is the strong scent of decaying meat in the air, perhaps due to an old corpse concealed behind a loose stone in the wall. The rock here appears quite scratched and battered, as if by frequent heavy use.
38183: Sharp Bend in the Sloping Passage

The large passage curves to the north and west from this point, so sharply that one cannot see what lies just around the bend. A few shattered slabs of black marble lie scattered about the tunnel here, along with broken bits of ancient statuary probably left by those who looted the great Dwarven Halls. The walls here are covered with illegible scrawl and crude drawings, debased in their design and intent.
38184: This very wide passage turns east and south, exhibiting a slight upgrade as it travels north. It is quite clear of all rubble and other debris, and provides good access in both directions. Faint echoes of grunts and harsh laughter seem to come from the somewhere to the south.
38185: This section of tunnel receives dim light from a chamber just to the south, revealing a rough set of black stone walls and a very high tunnel roof. There are several broken swords, clubs and spearpoints lying among broken bits of stone and bone here, these items arranged into small piles near one side of the wide tunnel. Loud cursing, shrieking and growling blares forth from the southern end of this stretch of tunnel, a torchlit chamber which appears to be the centre of some activity. The tunnel also slopes upwards to the north into the quiet blackness of the underbelly of the Misty Mountains.
38186:
An orkish warrior of the Durghash is here, with a cruel glint in his eye.
An orkish warrior of the Durghash is here, with a cruel glint in his eye.
A bulky cave troll is here, looking like a massive pile of stone.
A bulky cave troll is here, looking like a massive pile of stone.

This roughly square chamber was hewn from the surrounding stone by the Durghash to serve as a guarded checkpoint for any passage into their caves. Smoking torches line the walls above several crude stone tables and benches which are covered by dirty animal skins and filthy parchments. Many creatures lurk nearby, and growls, grunts and screams give loud testimony to their vigorous activities. A sturdy irondoor painted with a large Red Eye blocks passage to the south, while other exits lead north, west and east.
38187:
A bulky cave troll is here, looking like a massive pile of stone.
A bulky cave troll is here, looking like a massive pile of stone.
A bulky cave troll is here, looking like a massive pile of stone.

This wide and long cavern serves as a barracks for the troll allies of the Durghash tribe. There are many long, thick slabs of dark marble which line the floor of this place, each of which acts as a bunk for a troll. Many of these creatures mill about in here, looking for someone to fight, something to eat or perhaps both. A graveyard of old bones lies scattered about on the stony floor here, along with many patches of hide and fur. Some large openings have been smashed through the north, south and west walls of this long cave.
38188:
A bulky cave troll is here, looking like a massive pile of stone.
A huge olog-hai troll is here staring blankly at you.

This large and filthy cave proves to be the residence of the large and filthy troll leader of the Durghash allies. He has collected a large number of broken skulls of his former rivals, each of which adds to his status of its owner. A large slab of red granite directly in the centre of this round cave serves as both a table and a bed for the troll leader, depending only upon his mood.
38189:
An eyeless white rat with nasty teeth scurries about.
A huge black fungus is here, exuding a foul stench.
A giant, strange looking green fungus is here, ready to devour you in seconds.
A huge black fungus is here, exuding a foul stench.
A giant, strange looking green fungus is here, ready to devour you in seconds.

Here is a small and humid cave filled with small niches which contain different species of fungi. It is much hotter and more humid in this cave than in others nearby due to steam escaping from several small fissures in the rocky floor of this place. The fungi appear to thrive in this environment and there are many varieties all of which appear to be growing extremely quickly, filling most of the available space here.
38190:
An orkish warrior of the Durghash is here, with a cruel glint in his eye.
An orkish warrior of the Durghash is here, with a cruel glint in his eye.
An orkish warrior of the Durghash is here, with a cruel glint in his eye.
An orc, of the Durghash tribe, crouches here.

Here is a narrow irregular cavern running north to south currently used as a barracks for fierce Durghash warriors hand-picked by Shaghosh. There are small stoneblocks and large warg furs strewn about the cave, and you see a metal drum placed near a great firepit dug into stone in the centre of the cave. Each of the orcs has claimed space here by fencing off an area with broken bones and weapons, many topped with skulls of orcs or other prey for added effect. There is a loud clamour rising all around you here, as orcs love to scream and shout boasts as they prepare to raid and kill the other tribes of Moria. There is a small iron hatch centred in the caveroof, but there appears to be no way to reach it and investigate further.
38191:
A great wolf with a sable coat glares around with red eyes.
A great wolf with a sable coat glares around with red eyes.
A great wolf with a sable coat glares around with red eyes.
An orc, of the Durghash tribe, crouches here.

This large depression forms the northern part of the Durghash barracks and is home to the wolves that faithfully serve the tribe. There are huge piles of shredded hides, furs and bone splinters which the wolves have made through continual sharpening of fang and claw. Here and there, a bright scrap of cloth provides evidence of more substantial meals that these wolves have devoured. The rest of the guard cave continues to the south.
38192: A small and well-kept fire lights and warms the room.

The northern end of the cavern has been blocked off by a large wall fashioned from the tanned skins of six huge dark wargs. There are many symbols carved into the walls here, some crude depictions of hated enemies, others of unknown intent. Stacks of skulls and weapons line the walls here, and many tattered fur hides of various creatures cover all the floor. There is a firering in the south end of this place, lined with 10 huge cavetroll skulls.
38193: A huge and heavy irondoor has been set into the north wall of the tunnel, allowing the Durghash to restrict passage through their caves. Gouges and scratches in the walls and floor here indicate years of very rough use by the legions of orcs and trolls which live here. The tunnel continues south from this point.
38194: The wide, worn passage bends sharply east and north, skirting a large stony rock outcropping which bulges from the west wall here. Sharp shards of shattered black marble lie scattered about the tunnel floor, the remains of an enormous wallpanel which was smashed to bits. Most of the debris has been swept to the edge of the tunnel by recent traffic passing through this way.
38195: Something has smashed a huge gap into the southern wall of the tunnel here, opening a passage into a large cavern to the south. This damage has also resulted in a severe cave-in to the east, where the tunnel is now completely choked with rubble and stone. The wide tunnel continues west, where things appear to be more stable and safe.
38196: An orkish warrior of the Durghash is here, with a cruel glint in his eye.

The Durghash have set aside this large cavern as a home for any trolls who will assist them in their bid to rule Moria. Many massive stone slabs have been gathered into this featureless place, apparently to serve as tables and bunks for the current inhabitants here. Several huge trolls step forward to look you over, and the largest among them gestures towards a large pile of skulls which lies in the far corner.
38197:
A half-decayed corpse of a goblin lies rotting on the ground.
A rotten corpse is hanging here.
The ugly troll mother is roaming the cave, taking care of her loved ones.
An infant troll, baring its teeth, snarls here.
A young cave troll is here, staying close to his mother.
A young cave troll is here, staying close to his mother.
A young cave troll is here, staying close to his mother.
The ugly troll mother is roaming the cave, taking care of her loved ones.

This large cavern is filled with stone, carcasses and trolls! There are stacks of decomposing corpses, most missing heads and limbs and smashed beyond recognition, piled in the southern corner of the cavern. Many immense slabs of stone have been scattered on the cavern floor, serving as crude benches or tables upon which half-eaten corpses lie. Trolls mill about, bellowing at one another, eating, fighting and just enjoying the chaos surrounding them here.
38198:
A small pile of coins lies here.
A leather pouch lies on the ground.

A small chamber has been smashed into the hard stone by the brute power of stony troll fists. The trolls have made this place as safe storage for the various trinkets that they have collected from their victims' corpses over past few months. Some bright troll has realised that the Durghash have stolen everything not secreted away from their prying hands and eyes.
38199:
A sinister grey snake, its length coiled, gazes at you unswervingly.
A sinister grey snake, its length coiled, gazes at you unswervingly.
A reeking, boil infested troll stares madly at you.

The most noticeable thing about this cavern is pungent odour that surrounds. It smells of all kinds of rotten things, both plant and animal. The sickly smell of decaying flesh fills the room much like a thick sluggish mist. The cavern is roughly circular and the walls are covered with dripping fungi and spongy moss. All the ground is covered with a thick brown-green liquid, knee-deep and resembling mud. Tufts of gooey moss and small weird plants seem to be growing out of the dead-looking pool. The smell rises slowly out of the murky sludge, carried on a pale brownish mist. The only apparent exit is to the east, where a short corridor leads to a slab of rock and out. Perhaps the air is fresher there.
38200:
A large wooden wall shield rests on the ground.
Several silver coins lie scattered about here.
Several silver coins lie scattered about here.
A valuable gold coin lies here.

Shelves are set high about the walls of this treasure chamber. Set atop them, and scattered carelessly in heaps about the floor is all manner of loot, much of which is little better than junk, but some of which might command a price: haphazard piles of brass buttons and old wooden pipes sit among pots full of coins, and piles of weapons, shields and armour, most of which is too small for any troll to use.
38201: Though of quite a fair size, this narrow corridor would probably be considered small and secretive for trolls. It is poorly crafted, obviously not the work of Durin's folk, and ends to the east in a crude rock door. At the west end, the northern wall seems cracked and uneven, and weak beams of light pierce through these chinks from a chamber beyond.
38202: An array of rather grisly trophies hang from the walls of this large chamber, which appears to be lavishly decorated, although in a manner which could only appeal to a troll. Well-crafted, yet rather ugly, furnishings fill this room: a huge oak table, bearing silver utensils, stands at the centre of the room, a massive oak dresser and a number of smaller oak cabinets rest in recesses in the walls, and a colossal stone bed dominates the north-east corner of the room.
38203:
A lovely silver ring has been left here.
There are two piles of coins here.
Little parts of a broken weapon are lying on the ground.
A wooden chest stands in the corner.

A rather small and crudely carved cave, this is the secret treasury of the king of this small band of trolls. Several strong-boxes line a shelf, and below them on the ground are a couple of large wooden chests. Along the far wall are a number of shields, several spears and a huge stone club. Beside these stand three sealed barrels, perhaps containing treasure of some other kind.
38204: This is a strange chamber indeed, with walls lined completely with neatly stacked piles of bones. Long bones have been layered at right-angles to the walls, to form stepped platforms. The bases of these benches are formed from elven, half-elven and human bones, whilst the shorter limbs of dwarves and halflings comprise the upper tiers. Scattered on top of this are countless skulls, laughing out at you from between a forest of ribs. In places, the bones have been arranged in macabre patterns. A few old, dry skins hang on the walls, above the bones, completing this grotesque celebration of past glorious battles.
38205: The shoddy cots and grimy piles of fur scattered about indicate that this chamber is used for sleeping by the vanguard of Burzruth stationed in this level of Moria. This chamber may have had a ceremonial use once because the orcs have not managed to destroy completely what must have once been a multitude of intricately carved runes on the walls, though for the most part they are unreadable now.
38206: An extremely unpleasant odour dominates this section of passage -- the odour becomes distinctly more pronounced to the east. The grey granite blocks of the floor and walls are covered with smudges, and several tracks that appear to be made of some type of horrible smelling mud lead into the chamber to the west.
38207: The horrid smell issuing from the room to the north conjures visions of open sewers choked with filth. The dark smudges of footprints covering the floor indicate that whatever area lies to the north is often visited by the denizens of this place.
38208: A great black orc stands here, eager for combat.

This room has been appropriated by the orcs for use as a sewer. Whatever prior function this area had, it is readily apparent that nothing wholesome can live here now. The stench of urine and faeces is overwhelming, like a thick wall preventing entry into the room.
38209: A grey snake slides along the water.

The icy grasp of this polluted pool is numbing. The cold, granite walls are smooth, and glisten with moisture, offering no hand-holds. The red-brown water remains too deep for wading, even at the periphery of the cavern, and a slight metallic smell assails your nostrils.
38210:
The vast grey bulk of an orm is floating here.
A grey snake slides along the water.
A grey snake slides along the water.
The vast grey bulk of an orm is floating here.

The unfathomable depths of this frigid pool defy imagination. The water itself is red-brown, heavy with deposits of iron, leached from the bedrock over countless centuries. And, like icy fingers, the water seems to grasp at your limbs, its chill touch numbing them almost instantaneously.
38211: A grey snake slides along the water.

A chill mist rises from the surface of the red-brown water, which stretches from one wall of this chamber to the other. All is still, and it is impossible to guess the depths plumbed by this ice-cold pool, which numbs your limbs, and chills you to the bone.
38219: Some tough lichen grows on the rocks.

You are standing at a bend in a small passage below the Misty Mountains. The air is extremely moist, so that some small, white fungi have managed to grow on the plain walls of the tunnel. The stench of decay fills this place. To the south the air seems to become more breathable, as the tunnel enlarges and meets a larger corridor. To the east, after a short but steep ascent, you can see another intersection.
38220: You are walking along a large corridor running from the northwest to the southeast. When Durin's Bane was still sleeping in the depths of the earth, this was one of the most frequented roads in Khazad-dum. Since the Balrog came and slew the King of Moria, most of the travellers along this once glorious corridor are orcs, trolls and other foul servants of the Darkness: nearly all of the few intruders from the outer world have been killed by the orcs, or, perhaps, captured and sent to a fate worse than death.
38235: Slightly bending counterclockwise, the Endless Stair continues its steep ascent from the Deeps of Moria towards the upper levels of the old dwarven dwellings. Climbing up is a strenuous task, since the sheer steepness of the stairway would bring anyone to exhaustion in a short time. Climbing down is not easy either: a false step would cause a ruinous - and probably deadly - fall.
38236: The Foot of the Endless Stair

An ancient stairway, carved in the stone of the mountain called Zirakzigil by the Dwarves, Silvertine by the Humans and Celebdil by the Elves, begins here its seemingly endless ascent. Its old, dusty steps are said to connect the deepest dungeon of Khazad-dum to the Tower of Durin, on the peak of Celebdil. Considered a legend for many and many years, the Endless Stair shows very few signs of usage. Perhaps not even the orcs and trolls which now populate Moria have discovered its existence.
38237: An earth tremor must have collapsed the tunnel here recently, leaving a huge pile of grey stone boulders and tons of loose rubble which block any passage north. It appears that someone has attempted to remove some of the rubble and shore up a few of the weakest points in the remaining tunnel with cast-iron supports. One large dark boulder in the east wall appears to be quite different from the surrounding stones, perhaps it fell from the roof during the quake? The remaining tunnel descends rapidly south towards a large metal door.
38238: This quirky passage makes a wide bend from west to north here, rising steeply as it turns. There is a wide, sturdy irondoor embedded in the southern wall of the tunnel, and some dim light spills out from the cracks surrounding its jamb. The irondoor has a keyslot and peephole worked into it, but there are no clues to indicate what lies on the other side.
38239:
There are two large boulders here.
A huge statue made of stone suddenly turns to life.
A huge statue made of stone suddenly turns to life.

Along the northern wall you can see a few statues of the former kings of Moria. A big tapestry picturing Aule and Durin is also hanging here. The chamber was astounding in its heyday when the dwarves were here, but that was long ago. Pieces of rotten flesh, and humanoid bones were carelessly dumped all over the place. The once so beautiful tapestry is torn and stained with blood, and the statues have carelessly been toppled over and smashed.
38240: A wonderfully smooth stretch of curving tunnel stretches out from the west to the south, one with no grade, crack or discontinuity to mar its perfection. Definitely Dwarven tunnelwork, a remnant of Moria's time of glory which has survived into the present Age.
38241:
A large round whetstone rests on the ground.
A broad orc works here, burnt from the fire over which he stoops.
A broad orc works here, burnt from the fire over which he stoops.
A broad orc works here, burnt from the fire over which he stoops.

The sound of iron on iron rings throughout these caves as the orcs struggle to shape weapons and armour on massive anvils using heavy hammers and muscle power. There are several large stone vats filled with dirty water which are used periodically to quench hot metal nearing its final form. A group of orcs mans large grinding stones in the northern section of the cave, attempting to put a sharp edge or round curve on a near-finished item. Another group uses warg skins to apply polishes and poisons to finalise their product. There is a large fissure torn by an ancient tremor through the south wall which now leads into the Great Hall, and there is a much hotter cave which connects onto the eastern end of this set of caves.
38242:
An orc, of the Durghash tribe, crouches here.
A gaunt, filthy orc is here, looking around him with insane eyes.
An orc, of the Durghash tribe, crouches here.

Confusion and torment reign here in the east end of the Great Hall of the Durghash tribe. The surroundings are very hot and noisy, being filled with a loud roar and heat coming from a chasm to the east, the ringing of hammers on anvils from the north and the screams of the orcs and their captives from all around you. The Hall itself was conceived and built on a grand scale by dwarves long ago, obviously ruined by earthquakes and abandoned until the Durghash occupied it when they were driven here centuries later. It is lit by a series of smoking embrasures, stretching westward toward a raised dais. There is a row of iron chains set in the wall near a wide opening in the south wall, and a group of metal cages near the chasm in the southeast corner.
38243:
A large bonfire is burning here.
An orkish female is here, spitting and glaring around her.
An orc, of the Durghash tribe, crouches here.
An orkish female is here, spitting and glaring around her.
An orc, of the Durghash tribe, crouches here.

This large central Hall is the main assembling area for the great mass of Durghash orcs who are charged with the subjugation of all other tribes in Moria. War trophies and battle spoils adorn the walls here, tributes to the successes the tribe has seen so far. An unfortunate Durghash, impaled upon a rusted metal spike near the southern wall, testifies to the fate of those who fail. There is a large firepit built in the shape of the Red Eye which serves as the focal point for planning future raids and conquests, as well as for torturing captives taken during recent sorties. The Great Hall stretches far out of sight both east and west from the firepit, and there is a small portal leading into a sidehall to the south.
38244:
Thror (t), wielding a great warsword, is standing here.
Shandalar the Elf (s), wielding a double edged eket, is standing here.

A large throne cut from a single piece of red-hued granite resides upon an immense black basalt dais, fronting a large Red Eye carved into the west wall. This is where Shaghosh appears to command the Durghash, exhorting them to make merciless conquest of all the other tribes of Moria. This area is normally forbidden to all but Shaghosh and his elite bodyguards, and all must sue for his permission to approach near the granite throne. The Hall itself was built on a grand scale, and though it is mostly ruined now it retains the ability to impress through its great age and size. A long line of embrasures stretches into the eastern part of the Hall, illuminating a great space that continues as far as the eye can see. There are wide openings in the north and south walls here leading away from this nexus of Durghash power.
38245:
A sturdy peg for hanging armour from is on the wall.
A weapons rack stands against the wall.
A solid ironbound chest is here.
A large stone chest is here.

This good-sized sidehall is used by the Durghash to secure the fire-forged weapons and armours they create from the orcs not normally permitted to use them. Some goods are prominently displayed on weapon racks and wooden pegs, while the more valuable ones are locked inside sturdy chests to guard them against any tampering. These orcs are most proud of their metalwork, and will attempt to kill any who dare to disparage it or try to carry it away without the permission of Shaghosh.
38246: A broad orc works here, burnt from the fire over which he stoops.

A great clamour filters into this wide passageway from the large hall to the north. The tunnel is worn away to the point of collapse in several places, though it has been shored up with rotten timbers and some crude iron bars. It climbs as it travels east away from the noisy hall to the north. There are bone fragments and strips of decayed flesh strewn everywhere here resulting in a strong stench and slippery footing, so take care to watch where you step.
38247:
An orkish warrior of the Durghash is here, with a cruel glint in his eye.
A lurg leader, with markings of the Durghash tribe, stands here.
A bulky cave troll is here, looking like a massive pile of stone.
A bulky cave troll is here, looking like a massive pile of stone.

This large stone sidehall has been furnished with two heavy stone benches and a crude metal drum. The Durghash have installed a heavy irondoor in the north wall, painted with a large lidless Red Eye staring out over a pair of bloody crossed scimitars. The irondoor is flanked by a pair of torchholders which support slow-burning torches that provide dim light to all corners of the hall. The stonework here is quality work, but is cracked and pitted by great age and shifts in the surrounding rock. The eastern wall of the hall is in ruin, punctuated by a yawning black gap cracked through its central marble panel. The southern wall is least damaged, and contains a large portal which leads into another large lighted Hall directly south.
38248:
A large cave troll sniffs the air, sensing an intruder is near.
A commanding Durghash is here, cruelly eyeing the surroundings.

Over the course of many years, the Durghash have attempted to shape a rough rift in the bedrock into a hovel which houses one of the leaders of their raiding forces. The result is a large oblong chamber with a pointed roof, reinforced with wide iron poles and rotted wooden timbers spaced at regular intervals. The orc who lives here has furnished his hovel with a large bed of skins stacked inside a wooden frame, a fine marble table laden with a good selection of orc food, and a large collection of teeth and scalps of enemies slain in single combat. The western section of this room is as yet unfinished, degrading into a large rough rift in the rock which ends in a jagged opening to a lit hall to the west.
38249: The wide tunnel begins a broad curve, sloping upward as it runs from south to east in an even grade. The walls here show signs of wear and abuse: chips and cracks made over the years by all the creatures who still travel through here. A large crack in the west wall may be large enough for a large creature to try to squeeze into, but the sharp rock will probably slice pieces from anything that is forced through the opening.
38250: The steps rise up from the dark a slight way but stop abruptly, almost in mid-air. Moist, clinging air hangs like mist and a thundering noise coming from the east wall dominates all sound. The steps wind away downward into the damp, chilly depths. A swift glance at the stair plunging into blackness is enough to convince you that you had better watch your footing; the steps are covered with glistening damp, making them look very slippery.
38265: The air here feels heavy with moisture, which seems to drift in from the east. The cold, stone floor, the straight, tall walls, and the smooth ceiling, above, all glisten with a thin film of water, which intensifies the slightest sparkle, dancing from the minute flecks of bright green beryl, embedded in the dull, grey granite.
38266: Cold, wet walls rear up on all sides of this mighty cavern, which is spanned by a network of narrow, and apparently, rather fragile catwalks. Though the path here is quite broad and firm, the only way to traverse this chamber is via one of those slender footbridges, which seem to be suspended miraculously above the dank, red-brown pools, known as Mahal's Wells.
38268: A narrow stair begins here its slow descent to the lower levels of Khazad-dum. The grey, worn steps almost remind you of the golden years of Moria, when thousands of Dwarven miners laboured in tunnels like this one to extract the priceless mithril from the roots of the Misty Mountains. Alas, the sound of the pick is heard no more in these halls; the only constant sound, now, is the flowing of water coming from the south.
38269: Some tough lichen grows on the rocks.

In the remote times when this section of the mines still yielded ore for the Dwarven smithies, the miners probably used to come here to rest, from time to time. A clean, tiny water rivulet flows from a crack in the wall into a sort of carved washbasin, then vanishes again through a small hole. Along the walls you can see many cracked stone benches, upon which are the broken remains of some musical instruments. To the north a small tunnel leaves this room, while a ramp of stairs goes down to the mine tunnels.
38270:
A small campfire burns here, its low flames giving off only a little light.
An orkish female is here, spitting and glaring at you.
An orkish female is here, spitting and glaring at you.
An orkish female is here, spitting and glaring at you.

Here is a wide, oblong hall lit by a small fire in a ring of grinning skulls, a place for female and young Durghash to congregate. There are plenty of furs, clay waterjars and bits of green fungal mould scattered about this cluttered room, along with a set of bone-tipped pens and dried skins useful for leaving written notes for other orcs. The walls are plastered with such notes, which are often bits of gossip for all to read rather than private correspondences. Exits are available to the west and south.
38531:
The corpse of an orkish warrior is lying here.
The corpse of an orkish warrior is lying here.
The corpse of an orkish warrior is lying here.
The corpse of an orkish warrior is lying here.
The corpse of a commanding orc is lying here.
Iarion the Elf, wielding an engraved broadsword, is here, fighting Shaghosh.
Shaghosh, wielding a broad scimitar, is sitting here.
Kostilam, wielding a mighty dwarven axe, is here, fighting Shaghosh.

A short, narrow east-west passageway made from tightly-fitted stoneblocks runs to the base of blank, black-hued wall to the west. The north and south walls are filled with war trophies such as painted shields, gigantic weapons and captured tribal banners, creating a martial atmosphere here. The east wall contains a small, heavy stonedoor which appears to fit quite snugly into the wall when shut. There are three niches in the south wall, probably used as stations for guards who serve with great status among the tribe.
38534: This is a steep, somewhat insecure path over rubble which has fallen from the roof of the great mine cavern. Despite the fact that it does not obviously go anywhere important, it has apparently attracted some foot traffic which has worn a sort of shallow trench. Northwards the path ascends until it reaches some boulders; southwards it plunges downward into a small tunnel.
38535: The corridor continues its course deep below the peaks of Caradhras, running down from the east to the west. The floor shows the signs of intensive usage; the ancient smooth walls, which were once clean, have been covered with a thick layer of soot, which seems to absorb any, however tenuous, ray of light.
38536: A huge, worm-like creature moves towards you, covered in slime.

One of the many tunnels whick link together the wide halls of Moria reaches its lower end a few paces to the west. The road is mildly sloping up to the east, suggesting that the eastern end might belong to the Sixth Deep. To the west, after a simple arch, the corridor opens into a large vaulted chamber with greenish-blue walls.
38537: A noticeable crack runs down one of the walls.

The cave ends in a narrow hollow, with tall cracks here and there in the otherwise smooth walls. Strong silk webs span across some of the cracks, while others gape open like wounds in flesh. A thin layer of dirt covers the ground, with footprints running in several directions, distorting the pattern of dried up blood and other organic fluids. Smashed metal helmets lie scattered among broken spears and skeletons around the area. The cavern widens in the west, opening up to a bigger space.
38538: The corpse of a grey spider is lying here.

An immense spider web covers the entire upper body of the cave, leaving but a small hole in its centre. A tiny stream of water pours through the opening, splashing onto the stony ground and disappearing through a crevice in the rock. Several cocoons hang from the ceiling, wrapped tight and swaying a little to and fro. The humidity is daunting, and the remains of old cadavers and cocoons add a putrid smell of decay. The cave is vast and appears to expand to the north and east.
38539:
A copper penny lies on the ground.
The corpse of a worm-like creature is lying here.
The corpse of a worm-like creature is lying here.
The corpse of a worm-like creature is lying here.

The corpse of a worm-like creature is lying here.
Zhirinovsky the Elf (ZZ), wielding the broad Elven blade, is standing here.
Staub the Dwarf (SS), wielding a mighty dwarven axe, is standing here.

You are lost in some very deep caverns, hundreds of meters below the deepest tunnels of the Dwarves. Here old, nameless beings gnaw at the rock, digging long, twisted, cold caves in the foundations of the earth. Icy water trickles down from the irregularly shapen ceiling, chilling you to the bones, then collecting into small pools and flowing away through minute cracks in the floor. Strange noises surround you, coming from all directions. Are they merely the magnified echo of your own footsteps and your breath, mixed with the tiny droplets falling, or is there some foul creature stalking you?
38540: There are two copper pennies here.

You are lost in some very deep caverns, hundreds of meters below the deepest tunnels of the Dwarves. Here old, nameless beings gnaw at the rock, digging long, twisted, cold caves in the foundations of the earth. Icy water trickles down from the irregularly shapen ceiling, chilling you to the bones, then collecting into small pools and flowing away through minute cracks in the floor. Strange noises surround you, coming from all directions. Are they merely the magnified echo of your own footsteps and your breath, mixed with the tiny droplets falling, or is there some foul creature stalking you?
38541: You have climbed a natural shaft from the caves below, and you think that, by now, you should have reached once again the tunnels and the halls made by the people of Durin. Above you the shaft becomes very narrow; the only way out of this place seems to be a crack to the... south? The time you spent below made you lose your sense of direction.
38546:
A spirit floats towards you and howls with an evil laughter.
A spirit floats towards you and howls with an evil laughter.
A spirit floats towards you and howls with an evil laughter.
An eerie spectyre hovers over a sarcophagus.

You are taken aback by the biting cold that fills this cavern, almost expecting to see ice covering the walls and floor. That is not the case though, and a sudden sadness fills you as you realise this is a place probably once used as a grave chamber for numerous people, most likely dwarves. The walls are beautifully adorned with intricate carvings, depicting epic battles and heroic feats of long past. Tombs have been carved out of the solid rock and now lie opened, disturbed by someone having no respect for the dead. The slabs of rock that are supposed to cover the graves have been violently shoved aside, leaving the tombs like gaping holes. The skeletons of long dead warriors fill the graves, and while most have been disturbed in their eternal rest, some lie miraculously untouched. Still, you wonder what the source of this terrible cold is; a feeling of doom fills this solemn place.
38921: This narrow tunnel connects the Avenue to what appears to be a small cavern just ahead. A trickle of water courses silently between your feet. Small, evil-looking green fungi grow on the roof here, and you almost expect them to drop down on your shoulders and insert nasty tentacles directly into your veins. Perhaps you should move now?
38922: This unbroken spiral of steps - assumed to exist only in legend even by the Dwarves - climbs ever onward through the heart of Zirakzigil. The steps are cut for Dwarven legs, making travel for the taller folk an arduous task. Far below, darkness floods the shaft and conceals whatever long-lost secrets that lie below.

38942: A cool breeze drifts lazily down from above, where the stair appears to come finally to an end. The dark, stale atmosphere from below seems to fight to gain supremacy here, at the top of the stair, and dust motes dance and twirl around, before falling in a soft carpet on the cold, smooth stone. The walls and floor here are perfectly polished, and their craftsmanship unmarked by the long passage of time.
38943: You are halfway down a very slimy well. Algae and fungus float on top of the water and stick to your clothes. You tread water to stay afloat and hope that someone is at the top of the well to get you out!
38944: At the Bottom of a Well
The corpse of a water-drake is lying here.

This is the bottom of a well. The water here is over your head and you have to hold your breath. Slime covers the walls, and the floor is scattered with fragments of bones from unfortunate victims. The thick, slimy water sticks to your skin and makes movement very difficult. Your only thought is to get out as soon as possible!
38945: This underwater chamber was once an entryway, but the earthquakes of Khazad-dum have changed it considerably. The passages that left east and south of here are filled with rubble, and the wall to the west was broken and is now blocked by loose rocks. Above you, a trapdoor can be accessed by a now rusted, and un-needed, ladder.
38948: This great crystal chamber was cut with great skill by some master enchanter. The room is cut in a vaguely oval shape, with the crystals shaped to catch the light and diffuse it into colourful rainbows. In the centre of the room, one crystal pillar stands straight up. This pillar seems to radiate all of the light in the room.
38949: Although there is no dust here, no signs of any creature -- human, orc, or other -- can be found. Everything in this chamber has been untouched for centuries or longer. Hidden away for ages, it has housed its treasure since its inception.
41064: There are five green slime moulds here.

This is a small, crude cavern where the local inhabitants have stored some supplies. Various kinds of disgusting mouldy food lie scattered across the dirt floor here. This damp and filthy cave seems an odd place for food storage. A well, fashioned from large black rocks, is situated directly in the centre of the cavern. The water within looks filthy and smells very bad. One could wonder if anyone would drink from it unless they were dying of thirst. The only obvious exit is south, back into the tunnel you used to enter here.
41067: The current suddenly slows and you feel yourself ejected into a large watery expanse. The colour of the water clouds your vision, but you see above you the surface. The currents still grab you but unless you want to swim against them, you must surface here.
41068: It seems ages since you were pulled into this underwater abyss. Your lungs now scream for air and your limbs tire. Even your sight is gone, as the rust colouring of the current means even your hand is unseen. The journey is also rough and you bash into the rocky walls as the torrent takes a sharp bend. Your only options are to let it carry you onwards, or to struggle in the opposite direction.
41069: With the water dissolving the rocks, and picking up sediment, you have no idea where you are going. You can either let the water take you, or else you will have to fight against the flow. The only thing of comfort in this airless world is that there seem to be no bends in the watery-tunnel to bash into.
41070: The waters in this part of the watercourse have eroded their way through rocks which have deposited sediment in the flow. Looking back towards where the torrent divided is only just possible. Ahead along the route of the water, only a rusty colour can be seen.
41071: This juncture of passages underwater is quite complex. From the north, a strong current flows into this chamber, pitched at a steep gradient from south to north. To the south and east is visible a dark tunnel leading down, the waters obviously decending into it. Water from the north tunnel also makes its way west, but due to the size of the exit, the water leaves in a more leisurely fashion. Rocks and boulders of all size litter the bottom of the chamber along the south wall.
41072: This broken chamber looks to have once been part of a larger whole. To the north, a strong current of water pushes its way towards you, through a ramshackle wall of rocks and boulders. The few bubbles carried with the water migrates upwards to provide a breathing space in the upper part of the chamber. Strong eddies exist within the corners of the subterrean room and it is hard work not to get swept downstream to the south.
41073: The tunnel winds north and south and water fills it to the top. No sign can be seen of any small cave or side passage where contact with the world of air above could be made. As the visibility is low, it is hard to avoid the small bits of rock that periodically fly past. It is easy to cruise with the flow south, needing little energy. To swim north against the current is entirely different.
41074: The submerged tunnel rounds out here, forcing you to choose between one of the walls for some guidance in the depths. The torrent flows down from the north here, turning sharply to plunge off east. Much of the rock is pitted and worn as small stones carried from upstream smash into the wall at this bend.
41075: A small campfire burns here, its low flames giving off only a little light.

By some caprice of geology, this dome-shaped chamber remains dry and full of air, while below the underwater torrent churns. The cavern has smooth walls, as if at one time it had been scoured by the stream that now flows beneath it.
41076: Onwards and on, the heady flow of water carries anything east. The way west is now inclined upwards, though it passes under a rocky ledge as well. The water is very cold and you cannot see far in either direction. As you do your utmost to hold on to your possessions, you see no hope of any trapped air to refresh your lungs.
41077: In this jagged rock tunnel, the current of water heading east makes life easy for swimming that way. Otherwise, a real effort to make headway west is required. The water is not very clear, but it is good enough for you to keep your bearings.
41078: Below the turbulent eddying of the watery whirlpool, you can barely make out the confines of the underwater current through the mass of bubbles, drawn down into the depths. The fast current flows east along a rocky shelf, wider than it is high.
41079: Here within a a tall, narrow water-passage you are buffetted by the force of two currents which meet here and flow off further east. To the west is a continuation of the narrow tunnel. From the north wall descends a rocky tube, carrying waters containing a few bubbles to join this aquatic corridor.
41080: The current speeds up as the height of the watery shelf under the whirlpool gets lower in height. Just as it looks as if you will get forced into too narrow a passage, the heavy flow arcs southwards and down a dark tunnel. The trapped bubbles thin out and you can see a few dark blooms of life in the narrow crevice at the back of the shelf to the east.
41081: In the altering of the course of the water, the air carried with it has been forced up into this crevice under the shelf. Although small, it provides a useful supply of air for you and a welcome respite. The area still contains plenty of water though.
41082: The flow of the subterranean torrent eastwards halts here as the rocky passage ends and the water is diverted down a wide fissure in the floor. Though the fissure opens up below, you cannot tell how much deeper the currents lead or whether you will find a precious air-pocket from which to take a breath.
41083: This is the bottom of a wide fissure in the ceiling of a large submerged cavern. As it is quite large, the speed of the currents is considerably slower than in the tunnel above. The fissure narrows westwards, becoming too narrow to swim into. Eastwards, the greater part of the cavern opens out but it is impossible to see more than qualitative features.
41084: Swimming about in this water-filled cavern you can see that this place was once dry. A rough rocky wall and large stalactites indicate that the eroding feature of the slow current has not had time to remove these features. Small cracks here and there leak water out of this subterranean dead-end.
41085:
A great key, carved from bone, rests here.
A beautiful emerald pendant lies on the ground.
A golden nugget is half-embedded in the ground.
On the ground is a foul orkish-looking metal helmet.
A broadsword lies here.
Some cracked and splintered pieces of wood float here.

Beyond the rocky crack, a small niche has been left undisturbed by the flow of water. It looks like this has resulted in strange deposits encrusting the chamber, as debris has found its way into here and then calcified. The only way out is back into the cavern.
41088: You are in a ventilation shaft about 30 feet across which plunges downward (and slightly westward) into the heart of the underground city. A cool air current moves downward through the shaft. The rungs of a ladder have been carved into the native rock of the west wall. Because of the tilt of the shaft, you are actually hanging in space, relying on your firm and deliberate grip on the ladder and the pressure of your feet to keep you from plunging downwards an unknown distance into the shaft.
41089: You are in a circular shaft carved into the rock which extends far above and below you. On the west wall of the shaft, it is possible to ascend or descend using a ladder whose rungs have been carved out of the rock. Here, however, there is a break in the ladder where movement along a horizontal fault has moved the lower reaches of the shaft about five feet to the west. Since that time, someone has bolted a rough metal step about three feet across below the resulting overhang. It is from that step that you now look. Squeaks and high-pitched cries surround you in the darkness.
41090: Here a vertical circular shaft about thirty feet across is intersected by a smaller duct, about five feet in height, which plunges westward into the stone. Although this duct is blocked by an impassable metal grille, at least it provides a place to rest from the arduous task of negotiating the rungs of the ladder which extends above and below this point. The trash littering the floor suggests that others have had the same idea.
41091: You are in an air shaft thirty feet in diameter which ascends straight up into the darkness. Directly below your feet the shaft turns west, but the angle is sealed off by a metal grid which slopes downward and away from you to the east. Just above the point where the grid intersects the west wall of the shaft there is an access door. Originally it was flush with the wall, but the rock around it has been crudely hacked away to provide space for a sort of alcove in which a few can stand. The cool air makes an inhuman moaning sound as it passes through the grid. Mixed with that sound you hear from the other side of the door a number of strange piping cries or howls.
41092: After a long, sickening plunge, you land with a bone-crunching crash on a ledge in the east wall of the shaft. It was formed when slippage along a horizontal fault moved the top of the shaft a few feet to the east with respect to the bottom. The ledge is encrusted with stinking guano and small bones.
41093:
A strange bat-like creature is flitting around.
A strange bat-like creature is flitting around.
A strange bat-like creature is flitting around.
A strange bat-like creature is flitting around.
A strange bat-like creature is flitting around.
A strange bat-like creature is flitting around.
A strange bat-like creature is flitting around.
A strange bat-like creature is flitting around.
A strange bat-like creature is flitting around.

You land with a terrible crash on a surface composed of stones, bones, guano, rags, rusted metal fragments, and other unpleasant substances. This pile of debris seems to hang in mid-air as a projection from the east wall of the near-vertical ventilation shaft. Perhaps, underlying it all, there are some bolts or hooks in that wall which centuries ago caught some debris dumped down the shaft, on which the rest of the pile has collected since. There is no way to climb back up from here unless you are part spider.
41094:
The corpse of a cavern-wing is lying here.
The corpse of a cavern-wing is lying here.
The corpse of a cavern-wing is lying here.
The corpse of a cavern-wing is lying here.
The corpse of a cavern-wing is lying here.
The corpse of a cavern-wing is lying here.
The corpse of a cavern-wing is lying here.
The corpse of a cavern-wing is lying here.
The corpse of a cavern-wing is lying here.
The corpse of a cavern-wing is lying here.
The corpse of a cavern-wing is lying here.

You slide, tumble, and at length come to a crunching and injurious stop. You find yourself lying in a pile of garbage and guano. The refuse fills the angle between the east wall of the ascending shaft and a diagonal grid, rising to the west, which blocks the entire shaft. On the other side of the grid the shaft continues to the west; the cool air blowing down from above makes a moaning sound as it blows through the mesh. Other sounds surround you, too - high-pitched squeaks come from all directions, and from the west, you hear, or imagine you hear, guttural murmurs and strange piping cries.
41095: The floor of this small tunnel is coated with a thick layer of fine dust which appears undisturbed by any tracks. It must have been quite a long time since anyone has ventured into this place. North of here, the tunnel begins to narrow.
41096: Rubble covers the floor of this passage, and where it once continued to the north it is now blocked by a single, huge slab. Exit to the north is impossible, however the slab appears secure in its slanted position, propped against the broken remnant of the ceiling. The passage widens to the south.
41099: The ascending passage to the west ends here, in the southwestern corner of a huge hall. The smooth walls have been darkened with a very thick layer of soot, which has deposited with the passage of time. The stench of orcs is rather strong in this place, and gets stronger to the northeast, where a massive dark figure can barely be perceived standing amid the darkness.
41106: Progress along this imposing roadway seems woefully slow. The great breadth of the passage, and its high ceiling, make it appear foreshortened, contributing further to the feeling that despite striding wearily onward, no distance has been covered.
41107: Azaghal's Way marches steadily onward through the mighty Hithaeglir, ascending steadily as it progresses eastward. Unmarked by the passage of time, this broad thoroughfare retains the clean lines and solid feel, bestowed upon it by its dwarven architects, so many years ago.
41108: The impenetrable darkness of this hallway seems never to diminish, and it would almost seem that despite an endless march through the mountain, no progress has been made. The heavy, rock walls press in on either side, despite the generous dimensions of this passageway, and the only sound to be heard is the soft, repeating echo of your own footfalls.
41109: Soft footsteps seem to approach, but it is hard to tell if they are coming from the east or the west. Gradually, however, it becomes apparent that they are only echoes, making mischief in the unending darkness of this roadway.
41110:
A lurg leader of the Uruk-moragog looks at you from a bloody helm.
A great warg pads around, looking to rip something apart.
A great warg pads around, looking to rip something apart.
An Uruk-moragog warrior glares around him, ready for enemies.
An Uruk-moragog warrior glares around him, ready for enemies.
An Uruk-moragog warrior glares around him, ready for enemies.
An Uruk-moragog warrior glares around him, ready for enemies.

Broad and high, with a smooth floor and straight stone walls, Azaghal's Way strides confidently on through the mountain, rising steadily in its eastward progression. No sound is to be heard, save for that of your own footfalls.
41111: A march of dwarves led by Azaghal to confront the dreaded Glaurung, a dragon of the caves, once echoed the halls. Azaghal, being of brave soul, engaged the foul beast, and died an honourable death on a cold and stony battlefield. The folk of Khazad-dum named this mighty roadway in his memory.
42127: As one ascends along this ancient tunnel, cautiously climbing from the west to the east, the sound of clanking boots and of clashing swords becomes more and more pronounced. While, further to the west, only the strongest sounds can be heard - for instance, the occasional war cries - here even some smaller details are perceivable, a sign that the source of the noise is near.
42128: An obscure passage deep below the lake of Kheled-Zaram and the Silverlode ends in an even darker chamber to the east. Westwards, the tunnel slopes gently down, its ancient cracked walls and the its floor - made totally smooth by age - disappearing quickly into the ever deeper gloom. Nauseating smells and menacing sounds coming from the east overflow this place, strongly suggesting it is at least unwise to spend here more time than needed.
42129: A wide chamber, delved centuries ago in the hard stone of the Misty Mountains, reaches its northwestern corner here. The room's walls, as can be seen by some deep scratches here and there, were once white, but now a thick layer of black soot almost completely covers them, soaking the chamber in darkness. The disgusting smell usually associated with the minions of darkness also fills this place, and seems to get stronger to the southeast, where a huge, hulking shape seems to be waiting for someone to fall inside its clutches' reach.
42130: The western side of this wide chamber seems to have been part of a major route inside ancient Khazad-dum, judging from the worn track leading north and south, towards the gaping mouths of old tunnels. Another passage begins here and heads resolutely west; there is something, about its carved walls, that makes one think they have somewhat changed with the coming of the shadow to Moria. To the east, a huge black statue seems to support the weight of the ceiling.
42131: You have reached the midpoint of the northern wall of a large, dark chamber, filled with a nasty smell and with the echos of tramping boots. The hall continues to the south, soon vanishing into the deep gloom; a massive, dark figure stands, frozen in its place, towards the centre of the room. To the north a tunnel, which seems severely damaged - and is, with no shadow of doubt, extremely smelly - leaves the chamber.
42132: A ghastly line of bleached white skulls has been fixed along the walls of the easternmost part of a long, carved tunnel, by means of a long spike hammered through the brow and into the rock beyond. The Dwarves of Khazad-dum evidently did not think that someone might have so perverted the beauty of their halls. The corridor continues to the west, while to the east the walls of a large dark hall stretch away.
42133: The corridor continues its journey in a west-east direction, its shape never changing, its slope almost null. An almost palpable feeling of dread and sheer evil pervades the place, seemingly having its source to the west. East of here the geometric carvings on the walls seem to have been "adorned" in some way by the Uruks, perhaps as a warning of what lies at the end of this passage.
42134: The monotonous geometric shapes which the Dwarves carved on the walls here abruptly stop, the smooth walls to the east giving place to a larger, rough tunnel to the west. Did the Dwarves stumble upon a pre-existing tunnel in their building of Khazad-dum, or did someone else enlarge the dwarven corridor for some unknown purpose?
42135: A rough tunnel in the darkness of Moria seems to have almost reached its western end. At the first sight, the walls seem to end in nothingness, and it takes a long time to perceive, although barely, the jet black walls of the hall to the west. It might only be an impression, but an unnaturally chilly air current seems to flow in and out of the room, as the malevolent breath of a spawn of Morgoth's.
42136:
The corpse of Hshkhlahk the Dark Claw is lying here.
A small campfire burns here, its low flames giving off only a little light.
Kostilam, wielding a battle axe, is standing here.
Rohal, wielding a blackened dwarven axe, is standing here.
Iarion the Elf, wielding a steel-tipped spear, is standing here.
Feera the Half-Elf, wielding an engraved broadsword, is standing here trying to concentrate.
The shadow of Hshkhlahk the Dark Claw is floating here.

Utter darkness enfolds this black-walled room: only the hard floor beneath your feet dispels the illusion of floating in an endless void. A jagged arch of obsidian on the eastern wall and a corridor leading north are the only exits. The air is chilly and - is it mere imagination? - echoes with shrill, tremulous voices lusting for fresh blood.
42137: A vast, dark chamber extends itself to the north. Due to the gloom and the size of the hall, it is not possible to see the other side of the hall.
