79977: Here three rather different passageways come together. The floor, walls and ceiling are a strange blending of the qualities of all three. Depending upon ones views, this blending is the work of a crude and unfocussed artisan, or a glorious balance of all three elements into a greater whole.
79978: This splendid hallway of silver-veined marble goes north-south. Grand pilasters and ornate statuary adorn the entire length. An elaborate pointed vault, textured by marble roots, resist the mass of earth sleeping above. Under the vault, the floor is a complicated weave of flowing mosaic depicting men on a hill. A few sculptures lie broken but otherwise the area is undamaged.
79979: This hallway looks to have been some kind of gallery long ago. Although the pictures and paintings that might have stood here have long gone, the frames remain, being an integral part of the wall.
79980: To the south of this hallway is a room which was once secured by a pair of thick, riveted doors. They were not sufficient for the task, as some great force has smote the wood, sundering the portals. These doors now lie strewn on the floor. Picture frames of stone in a variety of sizes line the north wall of the hallway, though several directly opposite the doorway have been smashed.
79981: The hallway ends at a great steel door, which is framed by stout black pillars. The door is completely devoid of any markings excepting a great lock on the right edge of the door. A lintel of silvery metal hangs over the portal with small inscriptions on it. The walls and ceiling are covered with a thin layer of soot, this soot on the floor revealing footprints both large and small.
79982: A large pile of boulders is sitting here, probably debris from a rockslide.

This looks like a cellar of old, before the destruction was wrought upon it. Huge blocks of white stone have fallen through the ceiling from above, bringing down much of the roof. An open circular stair can be glimpsed leading upwards into what probably was the Tower of Amon Sul. In the west of the chamber a steel door is held between great black pillars. Stairs lead further down. The last route is southwards through a broken doorway.
79983: A solid ironbound chest is here.

Here behind the wall of the armoury is a secret cache of arms and armour, which have lain untouched in a long time. Although unremarkable in appearance, the sealed nature of the stone room has preserved the contents of the room from the ravages of time, since the seal was last broken.
79984: Fallen torso dummies and large racks suggest that this was once a grand armoury. Now there are few signs of what might have once occupied the shelves, except the length of the racks. A small hearth in the east wall contains coals and a few instruments for shaping metal. The paved floor has several man-sized skeletons, bodies without flesh nor finery.
79985: The chamber, once protected by heavy doors to the north, has been breached and the portals have fallen into this room. Large pieces of furniture have been smashed in the ensuing conflict, many of them also having the black stain of ancient blood. All of this must have taken place a long time ago.
79986: The racks and cases in this room obviously were former weapon-holders but they are gone. Locks on several cabinets have been smashed suggesting that the place was looted. Many man-sized skeletons litter the floor, devoid of any flesh or apparel. An anvil and cold-drop still remain although there seems to be no source of heating to complement the process.
79987: The scene left by this room is all too easy to interpret. Many pieces of furniture are piled near both of these doors as some kind of makeshift barricade. They failed. Valiant or desperate, the men fell defending this place. Skeletons lie scattered between the bunks and debris, some man-size, some more bow-legged and shorter. The only other worthy feature is the lockers and cabinets of the room. These have been pried open and their contents removed.
79988: Few remarkable features have been placed along this bending section of tunnel apart from a couple of crude sconces for shedding illumination. The dirty tunnel is however blocked. Large rocks have either been placed here to shut off the area beyond, or the tunnel has collapsed under the strain of the rock above. It is possible to get through, but the passage will be hard won.
79989: The grandiose hallway of marble goes north and south. Delicate sculptures adorn the edge of the walkway, either side of a stunning mosaic on the floor. Ornate fluted pilasters project from the face of the wall. Above, swirling vines and creepers of marble flow across the high-pointed arches. Apart from some deep scratches in the pattern of the floor, this corridor is very well preserved.
79990: Throughout this hall, marble clads the walls, fine veins of green and grey creating a lush environment from harsh stone. Great rock vaulting stretches up into the heights of the passageway. Upon these upper structures are carved a jungle of foliage. Small niches containing robust earthen vessels line either side of the intricate floor mosaic. Between the niches, empty sconces are attached by curling brackets to the veined-stoned.
79991: At this point the great hallway which runs north-south intersects two passages. Amongst the splendour of the large hall, these are very spartan but functional exits. The one heading east is roughly circular in cross-section, and in contrast to the hallway has no outstanding features. To the west, a steep set of stairs descends sharply, the floor, wall and ceiling of basic stone cladding.
79992: This rough tunnel is in contrast with the hallway with which it intersects to the west. Devoid of anything more than simple features, the tunnel is cut out of the hill in a roughly circular cross-section. On the walls, torchbearers are supported but there is scarcely any wood in them to provide a light.
79993: The great marbled hallway continues north and south. Above the height of statues lining this walkway, an ornate entablature connects the wall with the great arches of the centre of the corridor. Over the architrave, a wonderfully carved frieze shows numerous buildings in relief. Principal amongst them is the Citadel of Fornost and the great tower that once stood above this place. Higher than this scene is the cornice, consisting of intricate stone scrolling.
79994: The great hallway comes to an end before a great entrance. Once this way was guarded by a huge pair of riveted iron valves. Now they lie forlorn on the ground between the hall and the chamber beyond. The upper parts of the valves, which lie in the great room beyond, cannot be made out. A swirling curtain of darkness clouds that room from one's vision.
79995: A skeleton of some humanoid lies in the dust.

This is a huge hall which one can only perceive a small part of. Lying on the ground are the great doors which once stood in the stone entranceway, their lower halves beyond the darkness. Framing this entrance is a vast arch that rises towards the high roof of the chamber. Large slate slabs pave the floor.
79996: This is a huge hall that you can only perceive a small part of. To the north and west are great carved walls that arch up to high stone struts in the far ceiling overhead. To the southeast is a black basalt column of stout girth that supports the vaulting. The floor consists of large slate flagstones.

This is a huge hall which one can only perceive a small part of. West is the great, carved wall that arches up to high stone struts in the ceiling overhead. Towards the centre of the Great Hall are two black basalt columns of stout girth, which support the vaulting. This vaulting would impress even a dwarf.
79998: A whip is on the ground.

This is a huge hall that you can only perceive a small part of. To the south and west are great, carved walls that arch up to high stone struts in the far ceiling overhead. To the northeast is a black basalt column of stout girth that supports the vaulting. The floor consists of large slate flagstones.
79999: A black metal shield has been left here.

Central to the southern end of the Great Hall, a sunken floor ten yards in diameter circles a round depression. From the centre of the Great Hall, a low-gradient ramp leads down towards this central depression, flanked by a pair of sable columns. Around the circumference of the dais, the sunken floor is built to seat an audience facing inwards towards this centre, so obviously something is missing from the current scene.

To the northwest is a black basalt column of stout girth, which supports the vaulting. The floor consists of large slate flagstones.

The huge hall if responsibly lit would be an impressive sight, but in the gloom its grandeur designed for King Celepharn of Arnor is lost. The stone carvings on dark granite depict scenes from the lives of the Dunedain nobility. The floor is more mundane, consisting of large closely fitting flagstones of slate.

To the southwest is a black basalt column of stout girth that supports the vaulting. The floor consists of large slate flagstones.

Here in the centre of the Great Hall, one has to struggle to move amongst the debris. The floor is so covered that the slate cannot be seen below one's feet. Between the four black pillars that support the vaulting, are strewn debris of all kinds: wood, rags, rusted mail, broken blades and skeletons of fallen men.
80004: One passes through a sequence of rooms that once stored supplies for the fortress. Each door in turn has been broken, and a trail of destruction leads north and south as if some vengeful giant has taken his frustration out on the inanimate objects.
80005: The Maze of Glass and Mirrors

A skeleton of some humanoid lies in the dust.
Provost the Dwarf (PP), wielding the fine silvery morningstar, is standing here.

Within this enormous glass structure it is very hard to tell one's exact position. Although the room is lit there is no obvious illumination save the bright lights that leak through the glass walls and reflect off the mirrored surfaces. One has to feel in front of oneself to tell where solid structures are as ones visual perception cannot be trusted to guide.
80006: The length of this gallery has been inlayed with oak panels, dyed a distinctive crimson. Gilding on the wood depicts a long chain of mountains capped with snow at their summits. Bathing the chamber with an orange glow, mock suns hanging from the upper ceiling give the room a volcanic feel. The floor is paved with irregularly shaped stones of varying types: granite, marble, slate, sandstone and many more beside. Standing upon a basalt flagstone at the north end of a gallery, is another of those pillars of marble.
80007: The corpse of a brass hound is lying here.

This hallway depicts the standards and crests of a miscellany of institutions and lesser houses of the Arthadan. How they appear depends mainly on what it is they represent, be it tapestry, shield or crest. Much of the more perishable displays have done so, but that leaves several that can be examined. Between the displays, the western entrance has a caryatid, the statues either side. The upreaching arms of the stone pair support a thick stone rod. Opposite the caryatid, a low marble column is the only other notable feature of the hall.
80008: In the confines of this room are stored many crates and boxes, chests and cases: storage for items from a bygone age. Much of the walls are covered by these, but where not covered, granite blocks can be seen to dress the walls. Notable is the fact that in the north part of the ceiling, a block became dislodged and crashed to the floor, exposing chalk behind. Water seeping in through this breach has ruined many of the containers here, leaving few intact. In a pool of dirty water in the centre of the slate floor another of those marble pillars stands, a metal statue of a large hound atop.
80009:
The corpse of a brass hound is lying here.
The corpse of a brass hound is lying here.
The corpse of a brass hound is lying here.
The corpse of a brass hound is lying here.

This hallway leading east and west is tiled in ceramic of varying hues of blue, across the floor and halfway up the walls. Above this line, the wall and arched ceiling are plastered in a cloudy grey, creating a horizon. Mid-way along the hall, a passage of dark ochre opens up, leading south. Beside this passage stands a marble column, perhaps a plinth for a statue.
80010: The white plaster on the walls and arches of this room give this vault a stark appearance, especially as it is lit by four smokeless light-sources hung from the ceiling. A small pool is sunk into the centre of the floor here, the water quite cloudy with the years with foam spread across the surface. Standing by the corner of the pool is a short marble pillar, some two feet in height.
80011: This hall is designed to connect the rooms to the north and south. The walls are hung with tapestries but most of them have decayed, their detail lost. However, still hanging from the walls are the crests of the noble houses of Arthedain, a kingdom of the northern Dunedain. These crests are displayed upon oversized shields, four on the west wall, three on the east. Between two of the shields on the east wall an entranceway marks another passage, a caryatid supporting the low arch. Beside the caryatid stands a low marble column.
80012: This large chamber is remarkable for its huge hemispherical dome of blue-black stone. Encrusted into this ceiling are innumerable glowing crystals providing the illumination of a twilit evening. These crystals show a pattern of stars in their constellations. The floor, an inky-black sheet of fused glass, seems to reflect the world above, yet seven stars in a ring shine unusually bright when compared to the heavens above. Four cardinal exits lead to hallways.
80013: The corpse of a brass hound is lying here.

This walkway is panelled entirely with oiled elm along its entire length. Carved into the wood are multitudes of nautical scenes, depicting the great ships of Numenor before it was ruined. Above the walls hang yellow lights that cast ominous shadows on some of the sections of the wood. A now familiar marble column has been placed at the north end of the walkway.
80015: This hall connects the shadowy dome to the north to a large hall that runs east-west. Carved torch-brackets and pegs holding long gowns suggest that some significant religious event was prepared for here. The floor is a series of small tiles, illustrating begowned men and women walking south.
80016: Entering this chamber one is faced with three identical exits leaving east, west and south. Within the chamber, a single lanthorn hangs from a long metal chain from the ceiling above. The light from it reflects off an inscribed brass plaque secured to a flagstone at the centre of the room. Of the identical exits, they are shrouded in an inky-blackness, leaving little trace of which each would reveal.
93646:
The corpse of an assassin is lying here.
The corpse of a brown-skinned man is lying here.
The corpse of a brown-skinned man is lying here.

A small black vicious rat squeaks at you for disturbing it.

This small room is dominated by an old spiral staircase, circling upwards. The staircase appears old, covered with rust and webs. Though it might support the weight of one person, several people climbing the stairs at once might find the structure breaking under their combined weight. Apart from the staircase, the room appears to be featureless and reveals little of interest.
93647: An assassin is here looking for fresh blood and shining coins (red aura).

A spiral staircase twists its way down into the utter darkness below. Though rusted and apparently not often used, the stairs seem to be stable enough to support the weight of a single person. However, should a whole group of explorers expose it to their combined weight, they might very well find themselves plunging down to be crushed far below.
93648: The corridor stretches, straight as an arrow, from north to south, its floor perfectly level, and its walls parallel. Empty brackets hang in rows to either side, but further along the passageway a faint, flickering torchlight can be seen. The ceiling is beaded with a few drops of water, especially on the east side of the hallway, but otherwise the tunnel seems sound, and heavy wooden doors, to the right and left, rumour the presence of chambers beyond.
93650:
A huge, venomous tarantula extends her legs to you.
A huge, venomous tarantula extends her legs to you.

The walls of this large, echoing cellar are cracked, damp and moldy in some places, and the once hard-packed earth floor is now a muddy morass. The stagnant air is thick with the stench of rotting organic matter and heavy with moisture. It would seem that the river and the creeping marshes are intent upon undermining the foundations of the small building above.
93651: The interior of this building is a single rectangular room of uninspiring design and proportions. Four narrow, slitted openings can be seen: two to each side of the heavy oak door in the western wall. A model of the most spartan functionality with plain stone walls and a well-worn stone floor, this little building was obviously constructed to serve as little more than a sentry box to look over the approaches to the gates of Tharbad.
93832:
The corpse of a doorwarden is lying here.
The corpse of a doorwarden is lying here.
A weapons rack stands against the wall.
In the rack is a longspear.

This large, low-roofed chamber clearly serves as both bedroom and living quarters for a number of people. Narrow bunks of spartan design line two walls, and a long table runs between them, with sturdy wooden benches to either side. A number of simple cabinets stand against the far wall, and the room is illuminated by the light of some foul-smelling tapers.
93833:
A small sign has been placed on the southern door.
A large, heavyset man stands here.
A large, heavyset man stands here.

The corridor comes to an end in front of an imposing double door of burnished black metal. The walls, floor and ceiling here are made of huge slabs of smooth grey stone which sparkle with tiny flecks of mica; high on each wall, wrought iron brackets hold large torches which cast an eerie, dancing light into the darkness of the corridor beyond.
93834:
The corpse of a scarred man is lying here.
The shadow of a scarred man is floating here.

Beyond the narrow and well-hidden doorway lies a small room, whose walls, covered with mortar, show here and there discoloured patches of mold. In the middle of the room stands an imposing marble table, supporting what seems to be an alchemist's set of tools: heavy stone mortars, glass vials, beakers, all more or less dirty with the remains of a former concoction. Several small jars, none of which are labelled, can be seen on a long shelf fixed to the southern wall. A large tome, seemingly well-used, is fixed to the table with a heavy iron chain.
94997: A narrow ledge, flanking the smooth, almost vertical, eastern wall of a seemingly endless abyss, suddenly enlarges as it reaches its northern end. Though the ledge was undoubtedly carved by the Dwarves to connect Hwain's Way to another eastbound tunnel originating here, its purpose has not been fulfilled for many and many years: either an earthquake or the destructiveness of Moria's Goblins caused the eastern tunnel to collapse after a few meters. The bridge connecting the collapsed tunnel to the other side of Durin's Chimney, on the other hand, still stands in its place.
95002:
A tiny warning sign is here.
An orkish warrior of the Durghash is here, with a cruel glint in his eye.

Hopping from ledge to ledge, the roadway continues to run generally north-south as it passes through more of the great fault. Here the road is built to be quite wide and runs most of the time along the eastern wall of the cavern. The gaping blackness of the chasm below is therefore mostly out of sight.
95015: Stony rubble prevents any progress to the south. From the layers of dust coating everything, this passage appears to have been unused for quite a long time. A few dusty cobwebs hang from the ceiling, gently swaying as if caught in an imperceptible breeze.
95028: The road abruptly becomes submerged here as it descends southward. The water is shallow and calm here, but the pavement drops off quickly. Out of the darkness to your south you hear the sound of splashing water.
95029: The water of the stream rushes swiftly over the rocks.

The current of the stream picks up pace here, as it tumbles eastward into the darkness. However, here there is an opening to the north, where it is possible to leave the waterway, and return, once more, to the security of solid ground.
95030: The water of the stream rushes swiftly over the rocks.

Two waterways clash violently here, whirling and raging all about. The air is filled with an icy cold spray, and the roar of falling water assails you from the south, where this torrent gushes over a sharp rocky cliff, into a deep gully beyond.
95034: The water of the stream rushes swiftly over the rocks.
The water here is swirling eastward. Occasionally, you bump your head against the roof of the cave when the water level rises. The stream seems to be shallower to the east.
95051: The water of the stream rushes swiftly over the rocks.

The stream makes a sharp bend here, causing the path to bend likewise. The water's speed at the bend is so high, that some water splashes against the rocks and you notice some barnacles growing on the ceiling, suggesting that this tunnel sometimes gets filled with water.
95052: The water of the stream rushes swiftly over the rocks.

Twisting and turning, the underground stream continues its centuries-old task of eroding the underlying rocks. The air is heavy with moisture from the spray of the stream as it rushes onwards through the underground tunnel.
95053: The water of the stream rushes swiftly over the rocks.

A small underground stream begins its journey from the cold, dark lake, twisting and bending, and washing rapidly over rocks, slick with moss, and all manner of other things, unseen beneath the water's surface.
95054: You hear the water of the lake lapping all around you.

This is the eastern end of a deep underground lake. The dark mirror-like surface is occasionally broken by some ripples of water of some creature swimming beneath the surface. To the south, a small stream begins its journey into the mountain.
95055:
You hear the water of the lake lapping all around you.
The vast grey bulk of an orm is floating here.
The icy cold waters of this underground lake surround you. They exude a strange, unpleasant aroma, at once musky and fishy. The shore is unclimbable here.
95056: You hear the water of the lake lapping all around you.

An underground lake extends northward from here. Its dark, heavy, oily waters lap at a rock wall to the west. Mounds of rubble stick up from the surface. All is still. Whatever spring fills the lake works quietly, unobtrusively.
95065: You are at the intersection of two underground roads. One is a dark-surfaced road, smooth but without much adornment, that leads north and south from here. The east-west road which crosses it here must have been a major highway in its time. Its walls are faced with marble, and lined with carvings and ornaments which someone has done their best to destroy through the centuries. Lamp-standards rise at the corners of the crossroad.

The fissure broadens into an underground chamber about twenty feet wide. North and south, the chamber narrows to an impassable crevice. Overhead, the fissure rises into a network of broad cracks and openings, none of which are reachable at all from where you are. Nearly every surface is caked with pungent guano; with every step, stinking dust rises up around you and chokes you.
95077: The water of the stream rushes swiftly over the rocks.

Water from the north pitches over a deep descent into this gully, throwing great sprays of droplets onto the rocky walls of the tunnel. The surface of the water is white with foam as the torrent twists east and flows rapidly away.
95078: The water of the stream rushes swiftly over the rocks.

The water rushes onwards, twisting this way and that as it descends along the watercourse. The air is thick with the moisture and the sides of the tunnel are constantly lapped by the turbulent waves on the surface of the current. The loud roar of charged waters can be heard echoing from both directions.
95079: The water of the stream rushes swiftly over the rocks.

As the path of the rock tunnel changes direction, the buffeting of the turbulent currents creates great swells of water which oscillate from one wall to the other as it sloshes along. The depths of the water cannot be seen due to the spume, while the ceiling is all too close for comfort. Onwards races the strong flow, heading east towards the loud sounds of gurgling.
95080: Racing faster and faster, the strong currents of the flow have you in their grip. The waters start to pile up on the southern bank of the tunnel and the choppy waves strike the ceiling of the tunnel with their foamy crests. You can hear a great sucking and churning sound ahead.
95081: Caught now in the grip of the watery maelstrom, you see what is causing the deafening roar. The torrent from the low tunnel to the west is swirling viciously around this oval chamber before spiralling down into the deeps. Dark mosses live on the mist-laden walls, on which you can see openings high above. Rotating faster and faster as you approach the centre of the whirlpool, you feel the great eddying currents dragging you down below the surface of the waters.

Some tough lichen grows on the rocks.
A small black vicious rat squeaks at you for disturbing it.

Your eyes are now getting used to the amazing darkness of this tunnel, and bending down you notice that the slick stone paving is wet and moist. Also, it seems to be covered by some kind of fungus, although it has worn smooth in places - perhaps this tunnel is used still today. The tunnel spirals downward from the south to the east.

You have found a small pit between the rocks. It is a perfect shelter for those who like such environment. The walls of the pit are rocky. On the bottom there is some wet soil between the stones. A damp smell fills the air.

A large bookshelf sits against the wall.
A humble man stands here, ready to help you with your things.

The noises of the outside world are left outside the walls of this sanctum, save for visitors and the occasional speech being made in the library on the other side of the door. Throughout this peaceful place, however, a tangible watchfulness lies heavy in the air. A soft yet distinct scent seems to spread from one of the small boxes found in what seems to be this wizard's idea of ordered chaos. A large window dominates the eastern wall. Below it stands a chair and wooden table upon which lie several documents. A wooden bookshelf has been placed beside the table, where it seems to have been left to gather dust over time, even more dust than is seen on the dark wooden floor. Several paintings hang on the western wall.
95142:
A humble man stands here, ready to help you with your things.
An elven guard is wandering here, keeping the peace.

This modest room has walls made of dark oaken wood and a high ceiling painted a pale white. A long narrow bed has been placed alongside the wall opposite the large oaken door in the western wall. A desk has been set beneath one of the room's large windows. Some paintings of local wildlife, including one of a group of rabbits, adorn the inner walls. From the doorway and the nearby windows one has an excellent view of the enchanted valley of Rivendell.
95144:
A doorkeep stands here ready to obey his master's wishes.
A tall and strong guard is here.

This small cottage is hedged by vines on all sides. Well-tended, they seem to be carefully grown by local inhabitants. The cottage itself is made of wooden beams, horizontally placed one on top of each other. The roof is constructed of grey slates, supported by thick wooden pillars. A small window beside the door allows one see into the southern vineyards. To the east a small gap provides access to a snuggery.
95145: A humble man stands here, ready to help you with your things.

This small, secluded room is covered with furs of different animals, making it look more humble than other elven dwellings. A couple of windows allow one to take in the view of the surrounding lands. This room, completely separated from the rest of the cottage, may only be accessed by a small gap in the western wall.
95149: A humble man stands here, ready to help you with your things.

This modest suite has walls crafted of oak matching the tall oak tree that grows nearby. Giant arched windows have been carefully carved out of the oak wood. In the mornings the sun flows through them illuminating the room. A grouping of shelves are lined with jewels and ancient artefacts. On the ceiling there is a beautiful, embellished carving of an Elven sorceress and her Knight, they seem to stare down on the room with lifelike eyes.
95150: The walls of this passage are made of large stone blocks placed one upon another. The blocks are piled from the floor to the ceiling where they form a dome. Inside the dome, bricks of dark and light marble create a intricate pattern across the ceiling. Along the walls of stone, majestic statues carved in the same marble seen in the ceiling contribute to the feeling of greatness the owner must have intended when building this hall.
95151: A humble man stands here, ready to help you with your things.

As a strong contrast to the majestic hall of statues just south of here. This is a cosy and small livingroom, which seems perfect for a dwarf in need of rest. The ceiling if far lower than the hall and is made of oak instead of stone. The rich wood gives the room a deep luxurious aura. The floor is covered with a colourful rag carpet which looks a bit misplaced here, perhaps it was a gift from a friend. A well-used oil lamp can be seen on a black bedside table and the bed itself stands along a short side of the room.
95164: A doorkeep stands here ready to obey his master's wishes.

After climbing through the secret entrance, you have come across a foyer. This room is rather spartan and is devoid of anything of interest. The white door to the north leads into another room, while you may leave via the grate.

A heavy desk, made of solid oak, stands here.
A huge clock is standing here.

Upon entering this room, subtle scent of mauve petals permeates the air. The beautiful aroma originates from a bowl, which is half-full with mythical mauve petals. The bowl lies on a large table made of cedar and next to it lies a bone pipe. Rest of the table is covered with notes and manuscripts, which seem to be of arcaic nature. Large bookcases line the northern wall and a very comfortable looking armchair is placed, between the bookcases and the table, within easy arm's reach from the petals and the books. There is an oakdoor to the west, leading into the bedroom and passage to the south leads to the entrance of this simple house.
95166: A humble man stands here, ready to help you with your things.
This room is rather spartan, consisting of a mere bed and a chest at the foot of it. It seems that the owner of this house is a man of simplistic pleasure.

The moist walls of this corridor are supported by large wooden pillars, upon which lies wooden beams that holds up the ceiling. The corridor slopes downwards in a straight north to south direction. A slight wiff in the air brings a foul scent from the lower parts of the underground system. There is no natural lightsource here.

A memlant is darting around here.
A memlant is darting around here.

This is a four-way corridor intersection. All the corridors in this complex are turning left and right, with stairs going up and down, with three and four-way intersections everywhere. It is easy to lose any sense of direction. The walls are supported by large wooden pillars, and the roof is held up by wooden beams secured to the pillars.
95600: Hot, humid air predominates inside this dark, gloomy cave. Coarse, rigid granite comprises the cavern walls. Clumps of fur line the floor of the cave along the southern wall, indicating that some creature makes this cavern its home. A small fissure to the north leads out into verdant, green grassland.
95601: The corpse of a cave-lion is lying here.

A shallow depression in the ground, together with a wide crack in the mountain wall, forms a small cave. Once beneath the low overhang, the roof is high enough to stand up straight. All throughout the cave, several piles of bones lie littered. In a few placed dark patches stains the rocky floor.
95602:
A dark intangible shadow turns to face you.
A dark intangible shadow turns to face you.

The tunnel reveals many signs of mining. Although a great amount of work must have been needed to seek the wealth in the mountain, there is no obvious sign of ore here. The walls are smooth and hard, and impenetrable except for the eastern wall, which seems to have been blocked by some iron bars. The cavern comes to an end here. The ground underfoot is smooth and is covered by dirt.
95615:
There are three lembas wafers here.
There are two large barrels here.

Several decks are built below, each open from fore to aft and smelling of spices and fragrant foods. Partitions of embroidered cloth provide privacy to those who want it, but generally the passengers prefer to experience the sea breezes above. Dunnage provides good stowage for cargo during carriage, but otherwise, the only major sights are the piercing timber shafts of the masts above.
95624:
There are three lembas wafers here.
There are two large barrels here.

Several decks are built below, each open from fore to aft and smelling of spices and fragrant foods. Partitions of embroidered cloth provide privacy to those who want it, but generally the passengers prefer to experience the sea breezes above. Dunnage provides good stowage for cargo during carriage, but otherwise, the only major sights are the piercing timber shafts of the masts above.
95626: An elven archer is here, honing his skills.

The floor of this flet is more narrow than wide and there is scarcely more than crouching room left here for elf or man. Racks of arrows are secured to the boles of the two mellyrn whose branches support this platform. Through the dense canopy of the branches one can catch a glimpse of the shimmering waters of the river below and the dusky gloom of the forest on the other side of it.
95627:
An arrow rack stands upright in the corner.
Standing in the rack are three ash arrows.

The lower branches of the tallest and mightiest mallorn tree around support this flet. It is secured at about the third of the way up the trunk. The lower part of the trunk is too bare to climb but bears enough young growth to conceal this flet from the prying eyes below. The branches part slightly to the south, providing a vantage point to observe traffic along Celebrant.
95679: The Alchemist is here, carrying out some dangerous-looking experiments (glowing).

Strangely shaped bottles, flasks and containers fill the large workbench in the centre of the room. Some contain boiling liquids in all different colours, others are broken or empty. The room is filled with a smoke which, apart from making you dizzy, also makes it hard to see anything more than a few feet away.
95683:
A white-painted bench is here.
A finely crafted crystal lamp is hanging from a tree branch.
Anarwen is resting here on a bench.

Two arches crossing in the centre support the delicate latticework of this arbour. Vines with glossy, dark green leaves and large, bell-like flowers cover it, creating a gentle shade underneath. The flowers are blue and pink on the sides of the arbour, but those at its ceiling are bright white, reminiscent of lilies floating on the surface of the cool forest pools. The entrance to the arbour is to the west, flanked by two slender mallorn trees. Their golden crowns mingle at the level of the arches and expand westwards, extending the area of cool green shade.
95684: Leading down into the depths of earth is what appears to be at first a ladder, then a chaotic entanglement of tree roots. The very first steps down the ladder are smooth, grey roots of two mellyrn that become almost horizontal as they stretch away from the base of the trees. Descending deeper and to the east, however, one would have to rely for support on gnarled and twisted roots of other, seemingly ancient trees. Hollows have formed between and around the roots here and there, allowing passage into the deeps. A faint, eerie glow shines from below, suggesting that this descent may lead into a large underground cavern.
95685: A white, oddly shaped cloud of mist lies here.

This hollow under the roots of the trees was apparently washed out by an underground stream that long since dried. Barely lit by phosphorescent fungi that grow on the floor and on the overhanging roots, it has an eerie, timeless look. Like a place where magic has warped the world, this cavern seems to lie entirely outside of time and outside of remembered history, as if the Golden Wood did not lie just above it and the sun and the stars did not light the sky above. Yet no magic can be felt in this place that seems to lie like a dark void below the roots of the enchanted wood.
95686:
The corpse of a tall stag is lying here.
The corpse of a queen bee is lying here.
A sticky honeycomb lies on the ground.
A sticky honeycomb lies on the ground.

Here below the beehives kept by the elves a large colony of bees has created a large hive for themselves where they can exist undisturbed. Not as orderly as the hives above, this earthen dwelling still can contain a large amount of the buzzing creatures and the golden treasure they create - honey!
95722: An iron staircase spirals away, above and below you. The wooden handrail is completely rotten in places, and the superstructure and treads are covered with rust and cobwebs. Though the stair might support the weight of one quite safely, it looks as if it might perhaps give way under a greater load.
95746:
The corpse of a brown-skinned man is lying here.
The corpse of an assassin is lying here.
The corpse of a brown-skinned man is lying here.

This small round chamber is featureless save for two arched openings in the perfectly curved wall. One of these appears to lead to another room, but the other, tiny, and partly blocked with rough planks of wood, seems to let onto little more than a cramped alcove. The flat ceiling of the chamber is about twenty-five feet above the flagstone floor, and as the walls are perfectly smooth there is no way to reach the square hole, which can be seen directly above the larger archway.
95760:
A water moccasin slithers out of sight just below the surface of the water.
A fierce boar is here, making grunting noises.

This is a dark, moist corridor of columns under the old Smiths' Road which curves overhead. Water stands about six inches deep on the deep, soft mud. Your feet sink in deeply, and when you pull them out a bubble of foul-smelling air comes up with them.
95761: A small termite is running around making strange sounds.

This is a precarious heap of debris under the main span of the old dwarven causeway. Tree trunks carried down the Forglanduin from who knows where lie here, tangled with brush and mud; two of the supporting columns have fallen down here also and lie in sections, and some chunks of stone have collapsed from the roadway above. Underneath this not-too-solid pile pours the water of the Forglanduin, making a deep rumbling sound.
95762: Here, in the black shadows under the ancient causeway, the air is moist and carries the scent of rotting vegetation and dead animals. Great stone columns rise around you, fifty feet or more in height. The ground is quite muddy and cluttered with wet brush and branches. Little things can be heard squirming and splashing in the mud.
95764:
The ferry is docked here, ready to be boarded.
A graceful sign can be seen at the beginning of the quay.
There is a lit street-lamp on the border of the street, illuminating the area.

Long ago did the Teleri make a home upon the strands of Eldamar, and chief of their towns was Alqualonde, the Haven of the Swan-ships. Like a bason of quiet waters is Swanhaven, save that towards the eastward and the seas the ring of rocks that encloses it sinks somewhat, and there does the sea pierce through, so that there is a mighty arch of living stone. By reason of the surrounding wall, and that the light of the Two Trees never shone on the haven, the town was ever lit by a ring of lamps of gold, and shines to this day. Moreover, upon the quays, lanterns there are too of many colours tokening the wharves and landings of the different houses. Very beautiful is this harbour to gaze upon, as the waters of the harbour mirror the radiance of the lamps into rippling lights, weaving strange patterns of many twinkling lines. Reflected also in this inner sea are the many ships of the elves, more wondrous than any that have ever sailed mortal lands, though they are a mere echo of those that were seized by the Host of the Noldor in the dread events of the Kinslaying.
95765: There is an old street-lamp on the border of the street.

Under the shadow of the southern arm of the rocky cove, a steep stair carved of the living rock climbs to the higher terraces of the Haven. Lengths of flaxen cord, passing through the eyes of silver balusters, provide a flexible support on the narrow steps. The ring of golden lights on the rocky wall of the cove provide plenty of illumination.
95766: The captain of the ferry sings as he goes about his business on board.

Small but robust is this sailing boat of pale timbers and silver fittings. Golden ropes reach up to the single fore-and-aft sail. The boom of the furled sails is currently secured while the boat is drawn along steep steps that lead up to the quays of Avallone. A small rudder of golden wood moves in to-and-fro motions as the waves lap within the harbour.
95768:
The corpse of a great rat is lying here.
The corpse of a great rat is lying here.
The corpse of a great rat is lying here.
A small barrel made of aged oak and strong iron hoops stands here.
A water barrel has been left here.
A beer barrel has been left here.
On the ground, there are two sealed clay jars.
A coil of rope is lying here.
A large metal shield is on the ground.
A weapons rack stands against the wall.
In the rack are two shortswords and a longspear.

This vast room is cold, damp and musty. Shelves line the walls to either side of you, but the wall opposite the door is so damp that nothing appears to be stored there any longer. A few meat hooks hang from the ceiling not far from the door, but it is clear this chamber has to serve many purposes other than food storage, for an odd collection of objects is scattered on the floor and shelves.
95771: A sturdy pack horse is standing here.

This small hall extends off the River House and serves as passage to some select private quarters. The walls are made of oak and lined with white benches ornately carved from aged birch trees. Large wooden planters filled with fragrant flowers and herbs sit on either side of each bench.
95772: A humble man stands here, ready to help you with your things.

The natural wood architecture of this room conveys the peaceful aura of an elven forest. A set of large carved windows in the southern wall open up to a stunning view of the River Bruinen as it flows through the valley below. Looking upstream, one can see a modest pier and turning one's head just a bit more the patio of the River House is clearly visible.
95773:
A pair of ring mail sleeves are lying here.
The butchered corpse of a monstrous black spider is lying here.
A silky, spidery web is here, spun into a spiralling wheel-shape.
A skeleton of some humanoid lies in the dust.

A large, web-filled cavity has been burrowed out of the ground. Cocoons and skeletal remains of various size are laden within the chamber, the bulk of which appear to hold the remains of small animals. However, the odd one seems to be almost human sized. The only discernable exit is back the way you came.
95812:
The corpse of a brass hound is lying here.
The corpse of a brass hound is lying here.
Tordol the Dwarf (t), wielding a mighty dwarven axe, is standing here.

The long chamber serves as a display room for many pieces of fine crystal and porcelain. Standing against the walls are several glass-fronted cabinets which hold the antiques for a future admirer. Unlike the exit to the north and those to hallways at either end, the southern way is barred by an intricate metal gate, obscuring the chamber beyond. A low marble column stands beside it.
95818: This welter of gigantic stones seems to go on without end. Every irregular junction looks different when seen from a slightly different angle. There is no way to know whether you have been near this spot before, much less what direction you are facing. All walls, all veins, all surfaces, all that could give some some semblance of order to your travel has been broken, jumbled, disordered. The air is warm, dry, and smells faintly foul; as you move, you stir up a stinking dust with an acrid, animalistic scent.
95842: You are in a chaotic jumble of rock masses formed long ago in the almost complete destruction of Khazad-dum's Fourth Deep. In a terrible series of shudderings of the earth, almost the entire ceiling of the deep collapsed in a single instant, smashing flat all the homes, storerooms, and cellars that were therein. Into the cavity where the rock of the ceiling had been, more rock fell. Now all is smashed up together here - natural stone and cut stone alike, in a lifeless and patternless heap. Your sense of direction is useless here. Some crevices may lead on - others will double back on themselves, and others will come to an abrupt end.
95843: The jumble of great cracked stone chunks, masonry blocks, and piles of rubble continues without end. You cannot see beyond the nearest bend in your miserable cramped crawlway. Crevices stop short, passages diminish to crannies too narrow for a rat to squeeze through, slopes become fatal plunges. Your sense of north and south is completely confused; you can barely tell up from down in this jumble. The air is warm and very stale, and you seem to smell death in it.
95850: This is a thin shell of space surrounding a mass of rock to the east. Unless one is very short indeed, one must travel by spread-eagling oneself over the rock and clambering up, down, back, or forth like a spider. The mass of the mountain stretches above you with no support in sight; the blackness of the crevice extends around you to the east, north, and south. The crevice also widens below you, extending a little to the west, but mostly down.
95851: This is a very irregular and awkward space, created accidentally as part of the interior of the mountain shifted southward and down, tearing away from the rock above it and to the north. The cavity remaining is like a thin shell of emptiness that follows the curving outline of the shifted mass. Nowhere it is as thick as a man is tall; at its edges it thins and becomes an impassable crack; and its slopes and dropoffs are unpredictable and dangerous. Here the cavity slopes noticeably downward to the west and north.
95852: This chamber is divided in two parts. The eastern part is little more than a broad and very shallow natural opening between two horizontal sheets of rock. Not even a dwarf could stand there. The space is not vacant, however - some process has filled it with crystals of topaz and amethyst in golden and purple profusion. The western part of the chamber has been expanded in order to allow a Dwarven audience to enter and gaze upon the beauty of the stones. Lampstands with brazen reflectors line the western wall.
95853: This room has been carefully excavated in the form of a truncated ellipsoid. At the southern end are ten long, curving benches of stone, arranged to make a sort of amphitheatre facing northward. Behind the highest and longest bench is a row of simply designed lampstands, and behind that is a walkway where three passages enter the room. A person sitting in the amphitheatre is in a position to gaze into the curved and polished surface of the wall of the north end of the chamber, where, however, there is (at first glance) nothing to see.
95854: This is a nearly unimproved passage, actually part of a natural fault in the rock which has been somewhat widened. The fault actually slopes upward to the south at a pitch of three to one, so that unless one is very short one cannot actually stand upright here but must travel while leaning far over to the southern side. The stone is dark and hard, but small crystalline intrusions glisten in some of the cracks.
95855: A great dark cavern has been excavated here, through the middle of which, from north to south, runs an outcropping of white crystalline stone. In fact, this is a vein, a quartzite intrusion, from which the surrounding rock has been completely removed, exposing its intricate and branching form. The sheets and fingers of the stone are in places streaked with other colours - azure, crimson, lavender. The vein seems to shimmer in the darkness and almost to float in mid-air - some of the native stone, the minimum possible, has been left to hold it in place. The walls of the cavern are smooth and unadorned, as if to focus the undistracted attention of the visitor on the form of the vein.
95856: This rock chamber of roughly spherical form was the work neither of dwarves nor of any other mortals; it has been formed in the heart of the mountain by the forces of nature under the guidance of the Valar, perhaps of Mahal himself. Its walls are white, rose, and golden; they are formed of tufts of crystalline needles, thousands of thousands of them, each more delicate than the finest thread. It seems as if the slightest breath of air would shatter them all the way a gust of wind blows away the ripened seeds of a dandelion. And yet such was the skill of the dwarves that they were able to build a footbridge through this chamber, from north to south, apparently hanging in mid-air, without disturbing the delicate beauty around them. The bridge is about three feet in width and has no railing; at its centre it widens to a circular platform, which is about twenty feet from the walls of the chamber in each direction.
95857: This at first glance the junction of two mine tunnels, the main working gallery being the one that extends south from here. The floor is not tiled, and the walls are evenly hewn but unpolished and unfaced. The native rock here is a hard stone, very dark grey, and the tunnel follows a vein of white quartz. However, some benches and tables have been installed here, which would seem out of place in a working mine.
95858: This tunnel, about ten feet in width and in height, ascends evenly toward the east and descends toward the west. Some runes have been inscribed in the north and south walls of the tunnel; nothing has marred them in the centuries since this part of the city was sealed off by the massive earthquakes. All is black and still; the air is dry and perhaps a little warm.
95859: Here a corridor apparently designed for foot traffic meets a sloping east-west tunnel. The corridor leads southward and upward through an unobstructed doorway. The tunnel, which resembles an ordinary mine tunnel except for its breadth, rises gently to the east and descends noticeably to the west.
95860: Here an unornamented corridor arriving from the north terminates at two stairways leading south. The one on the right climbs upward a few steps and terminates at a metal door which is secured by a wheel-like latch. The one on the left descends into darkness through a small tunnel cut in the stone.
95897: This irregularly-shaped vacancy or crevice was left when some of the boulders and rock slabs in this broken assemblage slipped downward and crashed into the black void below - something which the rocks above you could do in their turn at any moment. Which is the original stone of this area, and which is stone which has fallen in from elsewhere, are impossible to discern.
95936: The twists and bends of the crevices through which you clamber have no hint of pattern or direction to them. Here you seem to be at a lower point; this flat grey stone here may be the floor of the ill-fated Fourth Deep itself. But that may be only an illusion. Buried here among the monumental fragments of stone are scores of corpses, you are sure, maybe hundreds - fierce orc and captive dwarf alike impersonally crushed and interred. Treasure house and hovel, armoury and inn, all has been reduced to unrecognisable rubble. The dark gaps around you seem to mock you; every one seems directionless, pointless, endless.
95993: This chamber has been excavated at the point where four rock masses meet. The northern wall of the chamber is formed of a dark grey stone, and the chamber was apparently formed mostly by removing stone of that type. The irregular floor south of the room's centre is formed of a pink marble lined with greenish striations. A black basaltic intrusion bulges into the room from the southeast, while in the southwest is a greenish stone, a sort of olivine- rich granite marked by intricate belts and folds of a darker rock. The effects of colour and texture where the different types of rock adjoin must have been very interesting to dwarves, because there are several rows of marble benches and stools (about a foot high) where short persons could sit and contemplate the southern wall. A row of lamp-holders lines the northern wall, low down, on either side of the entrance.
95994: This simple tunnel, nearly unornamented, slopes noticeably upward to the east and downward to the west. All around is a warm black stillness; it seems as if no one has come this way before you in hundreds of years. No side passages open onto the sloping tunnel in this stretch.
95995: A tunnel, about ten feet wide and with a simple arched cross-section, slopes downward to the west and disappears into the blackness. Its continuation to the east has been blocked by a heavy stone door which has been dropped into place from above. To lift it is beyond the strength of any mortal creature; there is, or was, probably a mechanism which could do it, but if so it must be on the other side of the door. The air is very stale here, and a light coating of dust on the floor is completely undisturbed.
95996: This room houses several large wheeled bins. One contains a heavy brick-red stone, which yields a reddish dust when scraped. Another contains a light, black, lustrous stone: hard coal. A third contains white dolomite, which was used in smelting the iron ore.
95997: The fragments of the clay chimney of what was once a tall and ingenious smelting apparatus in the southeast corner of this room lie where they fell after the quake hundreds of years ago. The ceiling of this ironworks, excavated from the stone of the mountain, is high and shadowed, and may house a ventilation shaft which once drew off the hot air. Iron tongs are bolted to the west wall.
95998: While not entirely ruined, this workshop has certainly suffered from the great earth tremors; the ceiling is riven by cracks, and boulders that have fallen from it lie everywhere. A long forge lines the east wall, while a huge bellows made of steel strips and ox-hide occupies the southeast corner, covered with a layer of gravel. Shelves that contained pans, chains, and pails have been crushed in the west side of the room.
95999: This was once the vestibule of the residence of a reasonably well-off dwarf. The quakes that have wrecked so much of the Third Deep have not spared this home either. All is destruction and darkness. A sculpture, a crystal lamp, an ornamented runic panel - all the possessions acquired in a lifetime so long ago are strewn here in shards under and among the fallen stone blocks.
96000: You are near the southern wall of what was once an east-west underground avenue. In the heyday of the Dwarrowdelf this was a busy commercial street, brightly lit and lined by shops. Now it is a dark ruin. The ceiling has fallen in, bringing down with it the native stone of the mountain; here a slab leaning against the wall has kept open a sliver of the road, but the stones creak and clatter ominously as you force your way past.
96001: You are somewhere in the middle of a jumble of fallen rock. A great quake has brought thousands of tons of stone down into this underground avenue. In places you can see the pavement, but most of it is hidden by a carpet of stone shards that clatters ominously as you scramble under and between the boulders.
96002: An exquisite golden cup lies here.

Only the look and texture of the pavement, where you can see it, gives you any ready clue that you have left the avenue and arrived at what used to be a comfortable commercial establishment. The floor is now paved by a mosaic of small stones, in part of whose pattern you can vaguely make out golden dinnerware, it seems. Is it possible that anything valuable can still be buried here? Among the rubble you see crystal shards, and the bones of a small foot projecting from under a slab...
96003: Less of this avenue has collapsed than to the east and west, probably because fewer rooms were excavated to the north and south. But the pavement is buckled downward in great cracked dips, and large slabs of the floor and wall lie in the roadway and must be climbed over. The air here is very stale; it seems as if no living thing has come here for centuries.
96004: This broad avenue, once lined by shops and residences carved into the stone, has been almost completely obliterated. Rock pressing down from above has crushed the chambers and corridors, squeezing them flat and filling them with massive stone slabs. However, along the northern edge of the avenue, a small remnant of the roadway remains, virtually a crawlway about four feet high at most whose roof is composed of the slanted slabs of the fallen ceiling.
96013: The ledge is small, and even though it is carefully hidden from the trail below, it is possible to watch any who approach the hidden camp just below you. The ledge itself is covered with small rocks and boulders, and among the small cracks and crevices a few plants have gained a weak foothold.
96123: The Resting place of the Palantir

This room is a truly fitting resting-place for a great treasure. Basalt walls curve up to a high ceiling. At the apex of the ceiling, a star of lapis lazuli sends its fronds out to touch all the corners of the chamber. The porphyry floor is surmounted by a glass dais at its centre, whilst pulsing crystals set around the walls illuminate the vault. An ivory plaque is fixed to the dais.
96124: The corpse of the Sentinel is lying here.

Greys and blacks dominate this rectangular room. The floor is of slate, as are the walls. The ceiling some dozen feet above, is flat and dressed with dark schists. Rather than use wood, the builders have erected great timbers of slate, the stone crossing the ceiling. Curious for this complex, none of the surfaces are decorated. The only features of the room stand next to the exits. A large statue in basalt depicts a lion guarding the eastern exit.
96125: Brass shelves lining the room hold a considerable store of knowledge. The books are on a variety of subjects but all of them deemed valuable enough to preserve underground for future generations. Desks and chairs are provided for perusal of the tomes, each having a bright stone for reading by.
96126:
Ambaal the Dwarf, wielding an ornate, steel-shafted warhammer, is resting here.
Miltar, wielding an engraved broadsword, is resting here.

Here the large corridor ends at the bottom of a set of stairs leading up. Large blocks of stone rest on the stairs and on the floor and round a gaping hole in the floor. Perhaps some earthquake created the crack and blocked the stairs many years ago. Perhaps the upheaval is the result of great and destructive magics, who knows? At any rate, a prospect of an exit looks bleak.
96163:
A demon wolf lurks here, its dark form twisting and hiding its shape (red aura).
A demon wolf lurks here, its dark form twisting and hiding its shape (red aura).

The mist was so deep in this section of the land, that you hardly noticed this cave before entering. The cave is large and high, the walls rough and jagged. In the far left corner a small mat of twigs and dirt can be seen. The floor of the cave, mostly near the entrance, is covered by gnawed bones and decomposing corpses that have been ripped apart by strong lupine jaws.
96164:
The corpse of *a Man* is lying here.
A demon wolf is here, fighting Tordol (t).
A demon wolf is here, fighting Tordol (t).
A demon wolf is here, fighting Tordol (t).
A sturdy pack horse is standing here.
Tordol the Dwarf (t), wielding an ornate, steel-shafted warhammer, is here, fighting a demon wolf.
Khelak the Dwarf, wielding a mighty dwarven axe, is here, fighting a demon wolf.
Ambaal the Dwarf, wielding an ornate, steel-shafted warhammer, is standing here.
Miltar, wielding an engraved broadsword, is standing here.
A stocky mountain mule is here, waiting to serve.
The shadow of *a Man* is floating here.

The back of this dark spacious cavern is bathed in shadow. The rugged stone walls rise nearly ten feet to support the looming ceiling, torn and cracked. The ground is littered with bones, torn fabrics, and rusted gear from many a lost traveller. It seems that its inhabitants do not favour visitors.
96165: A riot of colour greets you as you enter this appealing room. An entire wall contains bookshelves filled with multicoloured volumes on many different topics. A section of the bookcase has been converted to a well-stocked wine cabinet. The opposite wall is comprised of cubby holes for yarns and fabrics of all kinds. The wall adjacent to the door has a large window overlooking the scenic landscape. On the large comfortable couch placed in front of the window is a partially completed coverlet. A small wooden table by the couch holds a black and white crystal chess set.
96166: The tempting aroma of warm chocolate fills the air as a plate of freshly-baked cookies cools on the counter. This cozy room is welcoming with its colourful curtains and bright pot holders. The table and chairs are short and round to fit the hobbit physique and lifestyle, but larger and more substantial chairs are available for guests of different statures. Several unusual mugs are hanging on wall hooks to accommodate company. The dishes in the cupboard are old but clean, and indicate that the inhabitants prefer comfort and hospitality over appearances.
96167:
A sturdy bed made from solid oak lies here, covered in warm blankets.
Darby barely notices you as he happily nibbles on his cookie.

You see several glimmering candles burning warmly as you enter the bedroom. On the right are neatly stacked armaments and a tidy masculine closet. On the left is a small boudoir with several scattered silky garments. A large recessed bed comprises nearly half of the room and is covered with a colorful quilt. The ceiling above the bed extends up to ground level, where a large elegant skylight is fixed in position. The skylight is made from amber glass and finely polished on the exterior to make it difficult to see through from the exterior, but enabling the room's occupants to freely gaze at the heavens. On the left nightstand is a fresh bouquet of daisies.
96168:
An Isengard guard is standing here, alert for trouble-makers.
An Isengard guard is standing here, alert for trouble-makers.

This brick building is of fairly crude design. It is practical and sturdily built though, able to withstand time and use. A large wooden door to the south is the only exit, while stairs provide access to the top of tower. The interior is furnished sparsely for the use of a few soldiers, with two beds in the corner. It was built to watch the entrance to Nan Curunir, not to withstand a siege, but merely to serve as a post.
96169: An Isengard guard is standing here, alert for trouble-makers.

The small tower watches over the entrance to the valley of Isengard. Peering out from the arrow slits, would show why its builders chose this particular spot for the watchtower. The mouth of the valley is a few miles across, and from this viewpoint any intruders could be noticed.
96170: An Isengard guard is standing here, alert for trouble-makers.

This medium-sized room seems to have been added on to the watchtower after the main building was constructed, as the wood is significantly younger. Several of the support beams have been placed throughout the room and along the walls and in-between them, lanterns are hung around the room to light it during the dark hours. A few chairs are thrown about the room carelessly, as if perhaps their occupants had to leave in a hurry.
96171: A simple wooden chest is here.

This small room appears to have been sectioned off from the larger room to the south, forming a small storage area. The wooden boards underfoot are neat and in good condition. A few maps of Rohan and the surroundings have been placed carefully along the eastern wall below a small window. The window itself has been painted over and nailed shut to avoid unwanted visitors.
96172:
There are two piles of silver coins here.
A wooden club is on the ground.
A sturdy pair of rigid leather sleeves lies here.
A dark stone chest sits on the ground.
A large bat is here, hanging in the darkness.
A large bat is here, hanging in the darkness.
A large bat is here, hanging in the darkness.

This small cave appears to serve as the loot stash for the local troll band. Bits of chainmail, shiny baubles and all kinds of torn junk lie scattered all over the floor. You almost have to wade through the troll's so-called treasure and you notice that most of it seem to be either utterly useless trinkets, or long since rusted and worn-out weapons and armour. You could probably spend a long while searching through this stuff, trying to uncover everything.
96179: A rickety ladder lies off in the northwest corner, leading to a trapdoor in the ceiling. A strange writing of some kind, done in white chalk, crawls along the northwest wall. The writing continues off into the dark to the east and south. The floor, the ceiling, and the walls are covered with irregular shapes of limestone that have been carved out naturally, by water, over a long period of time. There is a smell of mustiness about this cavern.
96180:
The corpse of a huge warg is lying here.
An iron cage, rusted yet sturdy, rests here.

Cavernous walls loom over to produce a tall vaulted ceiling. The cavern is large here, but devoid of anything. There is no water here, but the walls are moist to the touch. Along the walls, a flowing script has been written in white chalk, but there is little meaning to it. The cavern continues to the north and south. There is some light to the east.
96181:
An iron cage, rusted yet sturdy, rests here.
A silky, spidery web is here, spun into a spiralling wheel-shape.
A tiny spider is here, eating a tiny bug.

This corner of the cavern is covered by the strange script seen from the north and eastern rooms. Further passage to the west and south are blocked by heavy boulders and natural limestone formations. At one time, there may have been a passageway to the west, and this no longer exists. The cavern widens to the east and north.
96182:
The corpse of a mottled snake is lying here.
An iron cage, rusted yet sturdy, rests here.

This is a smaller part of the cavern. The strange writings cover the wall and continue to the east and west. The are small limestone formations here as well, which are difficult to maneuver around. A dim light can be seen flickering off to the north.
96183: This room is filled with broken pieces of limestone and many smaller boulders. The pillar to the north is somewhat cracked in this section, and small rivulets of water can be seen seeping out. There is no sign of the continuous writing that can be found in other rooms.
96184:
An iron cage, rusted yet sturdy, rests here.
A fierce wolverine is here, snarling at you.
A large elk is standing here, chewing grass and leaves.

This area of the cavern splits in three different directions. Strange odours arise from the eastern area and there are no lights in any other direction. The cavern walls are covered in scrawlings and weird writings.
96185: A patch of moss grows here on a wet, flat stone.

Refuse lies in piles everywhere here. There is a strong smell of offal and dung as well as decaying flesh. Scorch marks can be seen along the walls. Strange coloured liquids collect in puddles here. Some liquids are luminescent while others bubble and hiss as though heated by a flame. There is a corpse tucked off in the northeast corner of this room. It looks as though it has been here a long time, and there is little outward sign of decay.
96186:
The corpse of a twisted beast is lying here.
An iron cage, rusted yet sturdy, rests here.
A large elk is standing here, chewing grass and leaves.

This cavern is a little more than a tunnel. A great pillar rises to the cavern wall off to the west. Along the eastern walls, the flowing script written in chalk continues. The passageway leads to the north and south.
96187: This part of the cavern is a little more than a tunnel with small stalagmites and stalactites forming around a passage. Along the walls the hand, which has written in white chalk, continues to form indecipherable formulations. A little to the east there is a dim light. The dark passageways continue to the south and west.
96188:
A small campfire burns here, its low flames giving off only a little light.
An old and rickety wooden chest stands in a forgotten corner.
A small pool of red-stained water lies here.
A filthy straw pallet is lying here.

This room smells strongly of filth and refuse. It seems to be used as a room to sleep in, judging from the pallet and small fire. There is a small pool of water here to drink from, and it makes this part of the cavern somewhat homely, if not for the rank smell. The walls are smooth and have scrawlings of some sort of white chalk.
96189:
An iron cage, rusted yet sturdy, rests here.
A mouse sniffs around, searching for a morsel of food.

The cavern continues to the east and west from here. There are numerous large formations of limestone in this area. To the south, one large pillar can be seen, which is large enough to form an entire wall to this room. The familiar hand continued to write in foreign script using white chalk along the northern wall.
96190:
An iron cage, rusted yet sturdy, rests here.
A huge, black wolf is here, ready to devour.

A large wall to the north is naturally formed with many stalagmites. The ceiling here is smooth. Along each wall many glyphs and strange writings have been written with some kind of white chalk. Even the limestone formations have this writing on them. There is a light to the south, and darkness continues off to the east and west.
96191: An old and rickety wooden chest stands in a forgotten corner.

Bowls and glassware are stacked everywhere here. Within each container is a different coloured liquid or powder. The cavern walls lack any writing, which is so prevalent in the other parts of these caves. This room is very cramped, and seems at one time to have been a much larger room. There are large piles of rock where a recent cave-in is evident.
96192: A huge, black wolf is here, ready to devour.

This room is similar with respect to its surrounding cavern rooms. The ceiling extends down with stalactites forming pillars around the north, south and western exits, making them look like actual exits. The cavern here is somewhat different though, in that it misses the script along the walls like the other rooms have. The eastern wall is part of a massive pillar that has been formed naturally with the rest of the cavern. Centered in this room is a large stone table. There are several torches embedded in the walls in this cavern, which illuminate this room. The floor and walls have numerous scorch marks and broken glass is littered everywhere.
96193:
The corpse of a demented Dunlending is lying here.
A sturdy crate made of nailed wooden planks sits on the floor.
A demented Dunlending, wielding a short spear, is here, fighting Calarion.
Calarion the Elf, wielding a broadsword, is here, fighting a demented Dunlending.
Nimur the Dwarf, wielding an ornate, steel-shafted warhammer, is here, fighting a demented Dunlending.

A single torch hangs from the northern wall, emitting a soft, flickering light that reflects off the quartz in the rock. This small illumination source brightens the entire tiny room. The rounded cavern floor is caked in a thick, viscous mud. The surface of the mud is marred by a small protuberance. Barrels, rugs, foodstuffs and a variety of obviously stolen items obscure the rest of the floor. The air carries a slightly dank smell, as if fresh air was here at some point but became stale not too long ago.
96195: A rather heavy clay jar stands here.

Earthen walls completely surround this small, enclosed basement. At one time, this room undoubtedly served as a root cellar for the home above. Carved into the dirt walls, small shelves line the western and southern walls. A few broken jars lie atop the rustic shelves.
96198: A foul odour cloys the air of this dark cavern. The dark black walls sweat with cold clammy moisture and even the tiniest sound echoes around the void. The floor of the cave is littered with rubble and shattered white bone fragments of long dead creatures. Dried black gore lies hardened onto the rock of the cave floor, a dark stain on the grey rock. The cavern extends at least forty feet into the heart of the hillside. At the very back of the cave, hidden in shadows, a dark hole gapes in the roof.
96199: Dried blood smears the floor and walls of this stinking lair. Many bones lie scattered around, excreted undigested from the creature which consumed the carcass. The black rock of the walls are cold and damp with moisture leaching through the living rock of the hillside. Much of the floor is covered with a dried droppings and a horrid stench grasps at your throat.
96200: The ledge from which you now gaze lies at least one hundred feet above the forest floor far below. The cliff drops vertically from the ledge offering no handholds on its sheer face. The ledge juts out no more than five feet square, a crumbling blemish on the cliff face. Far and wide below, the forests of the trollshaws stretch out like a ragged green blanket.
96201: The birches and other small-leaved trees gradually give way to a different kind of tree here. Mixed with ordinary trees, impressive, grey trees with straight boles reach towards the sky. Their large limbs stretch out high above, filled with leaves that seem to shimmer in gold and green hue, whereas their clumped roots make all paths difficult to travel. Between the large trees, a strange golden haze lingers, sometimes clearly visible and sometimes barely discernible. The trees seem to radiate an aura of watchfulness, as if they were guardsmen of some higher entity.
96202: Along the riverbank, there grow small birches, mixed with larger, ancient trees. The stream flowing east of here is visible between the boles of the trees; some of them lean over the water, dipping their branches in the stream. The air is filled with a sense of peacefulness, and the ground is covered with lush, green grass that is occasionally interrupted by small patches of white and blue flowers.
96203: The ground is sloping slightly down towards the small river stream that swiftly flows from the north to the east of here. The ground is covered with short but lush grass, occasionally interrupted by small weeds and brightly coloured flowers. The trees, mostly small birch and ash ones, stand sparsely, allowing the sky to be visible between the leaves and the slim white-grey limbs.
96204: An elven lady is walking around here.

Here, the stream to the north has carved a large ledge in the cliff, forming a natural overhang. Erosion by water and wind has cleared off the soil, leaving the bedrock bare at the edge of the cliff. Apart from some low bushes and a few patches of weed, this area is open in contrast to the dense forest that grows to the south and the west of here.
96205: Trail between a Bridge and a Forest
A nightingale is here, chirping a sweet melody.

Here, the landscape is level and covered with a carpet of low green grass that thrives in the soft, rich soil. Apart from a sparse population of mixed soft-leafed trees that are strewn about, the area is open. A trail leads to a slender stone bridge to the east and stretches south alongside the edge of a foreboding, massive forest to the west of here. The trail is easy to follow even though it looks ancient and rarely trodden.
96206: A sturdy pack horse is standing here.

The faint trail makes a turn between north and west here. The lightly forested plains that stretch out here stand in sharp contrast to the ominous large grey trees that dominate the area to the west. Birches, ash and elm trees grow scattered about on the grassy plains. West of here, the trail disappears from sight as it continues into a forest. The distinctive edge of the forest forms a formidable border, like the stony vertical surface of a castle wall which looks as if it could serve well as a defence line against unwanted intruders. The branches of the trees hang very low, as if waiting to knock careless riders off their mounts.
96208: Winding Trail in the Golden Wood

The grassy trail continues north and south between the impressive mallorn trees. The trees stand tall and silent with their grey boles and the green and silvery foliage, but still radiating an aura of watchfulness. No sounds are heard here, but the sense of a larger presence is abundant in the air, as if the trees were able to communicate with each other and to relay warnings about unwelcome intruders to other watchmen.
96209: Trail Branch in the Golden Wood
A finely crafted crystal lamp is hanging from a tree branch.

Here, a faint trail coming from the south meets the almost overgrown trail which runs in a due east and west direction between the giant mallorn trees. The soft ground is covered with lush green grass and small many-coloured flowers. Even in the middle of the trail path, the grass grows surprisingly healthy and high, as if it had never been trampled by cartwheels or heavy feet. Westwards, the trail continues towards the interior of Lorien, and to the east, the forest seems to yield to more open areas.
96210: Outer Reaches of the Mallorn Forest

No hedge or other visible boundary separates the mallorn forest from the surrounding woods, yet the border of the Golden Wood is quite distinct. As the forest crosses this invisible line, mellyrn give way to broadleaved trees of a forest as ordinary and as soothingly familiar as the walls and the roof of one's dwelling might look when one wakes up from dreaming of a beautiful, yet unknown land under an unfamiliar sky.
96216:
Delicate golden blooms adorn the ground like a cascade of stars.
An elf of the Galadhrim is walking around here.

Tall, proud mallorn trees, their crowns ladled with shimmering golden leaves, grow throughout this area.
