Overhead, through the thick branches, patches of sky allow the sun to caress the small, delicate flowers that sprout in the rich soil. Mixed with the large golden trees, young birches thrive, leaning in towards their elders as if enchanted by their presence.
96217: A small campfire burns here, its low flames giving off only a little light.

The grassy trail turns between north and east as it meanders between the massive grey boles of the huge mallorn trees that grow densely together. The crowns of the majestic trees shimmer in green and gold, manifesting a peaceful haven, to which no troubles from the outside world can reach. A healthy green grass blanket, mixed with flowers that sparkle in all colours of the rainbow, covers the ground.
96218: Faint Trail in the Golden Wood
A nightingale is here, chirping a sweet melody.

Between the tall mallorn trees, the small trail continues in a due north and south direction. Half concealed by grass and low flowers, the trail is almost hidden at times. Nevertheless, finding the right way is simple, as if the trees themselves guided the wanderer who strays from the right path. High above, between the magnificent tree crowns, a yellow smoke-like mist lingers. At times, faint harmonies are heard, carried by a soft wind from the west.
96219: Several blooms of snow-white and palest green cover the ground.

The giant trees grow densely here, and it is easy to lose one's sense of direction in this maze-like forest. All paths are very narrow and impossible to follow on horseback. The trees almost seem to be alive, even though their grey boles are firmly rooted in the rich, soft soil. High above, their limbs intertwine, and the leaves form an artificial roof that shimmers in silver, gold and green. Between the trees a golden mist lingers, sometimes barely discernible. At times, strange harmonies can be heard faintly, as if they were carried by a soft wind. The ground is covered with fallen leaves that glitter as if they were made of pure gold.
96220: This appears to be the eastern reach of the Golden Wood. The mallorn forest extends to the west, but eastward a more common forest in shades of green, brown and grey continues on its way down the slope. Everywhere the vegetation is quite lush and tangled, making the terrain difficult to travel. A sense of uncertainty and incompleteness pervades the scene, as if neither of the two forests could entirely take over this land nor give it up, for it is here that the winds of Lorien and of the outer lands meet and mingle. The wind of Lorien is warm and bears scents of flowers and orchards whereas the wind from the east brings the clear and cold air of river valleys and pine forests.
96221:
A hollow tree is growing upright here.
A nightingale is here, chirping a sweet melody.
An elf of the Galadhrim is walking around here.

Here, the east and the west trails through the forest are augmented by another smaller trail which branches off to the south into what appears to be a small glade in the otherwise dense mallorn forest. The large grey trees stand straight and tall here like silent watchmen on duty. Their large crowns spread out high above, creating an artificial roof of leaves that shimmer in gold and green, whereas the lower branches hang just at the right height to stop anyone from riding through this intersection. Between the grey limbs, a yellow and golden mist lingers, sometimes barely discernible.
96222: Small Glade in the Mallorn Forest

A finely crafted crystal lamp is hanging from a tree branch.
Several blooms of snow-white and palest green cover the ground.

This secluded forest glade is surrounded by large, golden-crested mallorn trees. Trails extend in several directions, suggesting that the area is a nexus for those who travel this forest. Even though there are no structures or other obvious signs of activity here, a sense of presence can be felt. Every now and then, faint melodies float through the air, lingering for a moment until they blend with the sounds of nature.
96224:
Delicate golden blooms adorn the ground like a cascade of stars.
An elven lady is walking around here.

The massive grey mallorn trees grow more sparsely here, allowing room for a mix of birches and large ash trees to thrive in the open spaces. In a cascade of green and golden colours, the mallorn trees reflect the light cast upon them. The rich, fertile ground is home to lush green hay which is tall enough to make passage difficult, and countless small flowers that seem to radiate in every colour of the rainbow.
96225: A faint trail runs east and west between the high trees with golden and silvery leaves. The trail is sometimes concealed by grass and flowers, but still easy to follow, perhaps by instinct. Obviously, this trail is very seldom trodden by anyone else than the creatures that inhabit this land. The large trees grow closely together here, and like silent watchmen they stand, emitting an aura of vigilance and alertness.
96226: A nightingale is here, chirping a sweet melody.

At first gently, then more steeply until it levels out again, the forest floor slopes downward to the east. The golden forest follows the slope until its lowest point, where the mellyrn come to a halt at a clump of tall firs. Like guardians at the boundary of another world, the fir trees stand dark and solemn, a faint silvery shimmer around their dark branches.
96227:
A sturdy pack horse is standing here.
A sturdy pack horse is standing here.

Several different species of trees have found their place here as tall grey mallorn trees gradually give way to a more common forest consisting of birch, elm and other smaller trees. At some places, the trees stand further apart, creating small glades that allow sunlight to reach the ground. To the east and the north along the bank of the stream that is seen between the tree trunks, bushes and shrubs thrive.
96228:
A tall silvery plant grows here, surrounded by mist.
An elven lady is walking around here.

A mixture of scattered firs, small pinetrees and patches of weed defines this somewhat boggy area, which is limited to the north and east by the swift stream that cuts through the landscape. The ground here is low, at some places almost the same level as the stream, and it might easily be flooded if the tide is high.
96229: A small but well-defined trail runs due east and west between the trees. The healthy grass that covers the ground shimmers in all shades of green. Smaller birches are mixed with larger trees with a grey, smooth bark and leaves that seem to be made of gold. The large trees, which become more common farther west of here, look foreboding as if they were ready to crush any undesired visitor to these lands.
96230: A Slender Bridge over the Stream

This massive bridge made of grey stone blocks gracefully arches over the swift river in order to provide a safe crossing for travellers in these lands. Unlike the bridges built elsewhere, this stony course seems to have sprung from the earth itself, showing perfect harmony with surrounding nature. The stones are skilfully crafted and fit together to achieve a perfectly flat surface, as the walkway is without any parapets but wide enough for two carts to meet. Moss and lichen growth on the foundations reveal that the bridge has withstood many years without the slightest sign of decay.
96231: The trail travels along the riverside where the landscape allows easy passage to the grass-covered bank. A small river flowing from the north-west joins the path of the mighty Anduin just to the south of here, forming unpredictable currents in the wide river. The trail comes to a stop on the eastern riverbank of the Anduin, where a small pebbled beach stretches out along the shallow waterline.
96232: The plains are mostly level; only to the south-east, there is a small downward slope towards a swiftly flowing river that passes by. The ground is mostly covered with green patches of grass that grow almost waist-high. Evidently, the the close proximity of water around creates a hospitable environment for the vegetation in this area.
96233: Outer Reaches of the Golden Wood
A dense carpet of blue flowers dip their heads in the breeze.

A mixture of tall, proud mallorn trees and smaller deciduous trees such as ash and birch dominate the vegetation here. While not as magnificent as the ancient mellyrn, they seem enchanted by their company and look taller and healthier here than in most other areas. To the east of here, the shoreline of a river forms a natural boundary to the golden forest.
96237: The soft ground is almost boggy at some places due to the ample supply of water. The green, healthily growing grass is high, mixed with various reeds that thrive wherever small puddles have formed in the watery ground. The steep banks of the Great River Anduin are rocky and lined with low brushwood and occasional lesser trees.
96238: The tall patches of grass that grow on these fields resemble a thick green blanket which stretches out in all directions. The most common types of vegetation, apart from the dominating grass, seem to be low shrubs and other hardy species. In the distance to the south, the shimmering surface of a large river cuts through the grassland.
96239: A small grasshopper clings to a blade of grass, ready to spring.

The ground here is green and lush due to the ample supply of water. Long-leaved grass grows all over the fields, mixed with small evergreen trees. The landscape slopes down slightly towards the riverbanks of a wide river to the south and the east of here. Behind the bush-lined riverbanks, the river passes by, carrying an endless flow of water southwards.
96240: The ground here is firm, and it seems to be composed mostly of sand and dry soil. The pale green patches of grass seem to absorb whatever moisture their roots might be able to find. Occasionally, thick shrubs decorate the grass-covered fields that open wide in all directions. To the south of here, the plains slope down towards a large river which can be seen in the distance.
96241: A partridge attempts to hide in the undergrowth.

The landscape here is lush and green, clearly thriving in the ample supply of water from the neighbouring river. Apart from a few small, bushy depressions, the terrain is level with a slight descent down towards the riverbanks. Small stands of man-high birches grow scattered in the area, providing both food and protection for the grazing animals that roam this area.
96242: The ample supply of water from the large river that flows by to the east and to the south of here clearly has an influence on the landscape and the vegetation in this area. At places, the ground is boggy and damp. High stands of reeds grow on the wet places. At the more dry areas lush grey-green grass covers the ground. To the south and the west of here, the plains dip slightly down to the riverbanks, where stands of bushes line the shore.
96243: Small birches grow in scattered clumps here, occasionally interrupting the grey-green field of grass. The climate is obviously mild enough and the soil fertile enough to allow also other plants than grass to root here. A few small bushes have sprung up as well, providing protection for smaller animals. To the north-west of here, a small trail can be seen as it curves around a low hill that forms a distinguishable landmark in these plains.
96244: The small trail makes a gentle turn between north and west as it curves around the hills that rise above the surrounding landscape west of here. The green grass grows a few feet high and looks healthy enough to provide nourishment for a variety of grazing animals. The fields to the south-east of the trail descend in a slight slope down towards the bare riverbanks of a wide river far in the distance.
96245: As the trail continues in a due east and west direction, it passes a small hill that lies like a small ship in a sea of grass. Some vague tracks in the dirt seem to be of the animals living in the grassland which prefer to use the trail instead of trudging through the grass. The tracks and various droppings indicate that these fields are home to several kinds of grazing animals as well as a few predators. Even though the trail seems to be seldom used today, small stones erected along the trailside make it easy to follow it across the open land.
96247:
A cute rabbit is here.
A lone hawk soars high above you.

The faint trail carries on in a due east and west direction, crossing the grass-covered plains that dominate the view in all directions from here. The trail, seldom used, is no more that a small depression in the grass. In past times, however, this was probably a major route which was travelled frequently. Small grey milestones are erected at the side of the trail.
96248: The water that spills in from the stream to the west and the south of here is almost flooding these low plains. The water-drenched ground is soft and gives away easily, and the footing is almost treacherous at some places. Here and there, small puddles have formed between stands of reed and sturdy weeds. To the east of here, the ground is slightly more elevated and more firm.
96250: Thick grass covers these plains like a green blanket. Some scattered patches of high reaching flowers and a few thorny bushes are the only things that break the monotone grey-green impression. To the north, a steep, bush-growing slope climbs up the side of a low hill, and the ridge blocks the further view to that way. In all other directions, the flat green fields continue to the horizon.
96261: A small grasshopper clings to a blade of grass, ready to spring.

These lands mainly consist of open plains, mixed with small scattered brushwood. The black soil seems to provide the support for a variety of different green plants, from long blades of grass to small decidous trees. The ground has a slight tilt down towards the bank of the stream that flows east of here, its water washing the riverbank which is lined with rocks and gravel.
96262:
A fallow deer is grazing peacefully here.
A small grasshopper clings to a blade of grass, ready to spring.

This is obviously a crossing, with trails leading away in several directions. The ground is well-trampled and firm from years of use, although the grass has now reclaimed the areas that were once bare soil. To the north, a small dwindling path leads off into the vast grassland. In the eastward direction, a larger trail stretches out, although overgrown in places and sparsely used. To the west, a small bridge spans the stream that swiftly flows southwards. Just beside the head of the bridge, a large flat stone has been erected.
96263: A buck runs swiftly from place to place, looking about warily as it grazes.

This slender bridge was obviously built by skilled craftsmen, since it has withstood the forces of water and weather for many years. It gracefully arches over the swift stream below to provide a safe passage for travellers. The walkway is constructed with sturdy planks of wood onto the rigid system of the supporting columns. Well-crafted handrails provide good support when walking across the bridge.
96264: The small trail continues in a slight slope down towards the bank of the swift stream that flows just to the west of here. The sound of the rushing water is constantly present as a backdrop in the otherwise quiet landscape. The carpet of lush green grass is only interrupted by a few scattered bushes and small deciduous trees that thrive in the dark soil nourished by the ample supply of water.
96265: The small, dirty trail is nothing more but a strip of bare soil with some scattered pebbles and small rocks, stretching across the seemingly endless yellowish-green fields. The trail continues in a due north-south direction without significant deviation. Across the plains to the east of here, nothing but some scattered bushes and undulating hills break the monotone landscape. A short distance away to the west of here, a swift stream rushes by southwards.
96266: The trail continues to the north and the south and is almost overgrown by grass, making it difficult to find the right path between the bushes and the high green weeds. The slight depression in the ground caused by previous travellers is sometimes the most visible evidence of what once might have been a well-travelled path. To the west, in the distance behind a small stream of water, the silhouette of a massive forest can barely be seen.
96267: The swift stream that rushes by just to the west of here provides plenty of water to allow the green grass that thrives here to grow almost waist-high. The healthy vegetation here should provide ample support for grazing animals. To the south, the constant erosion by the fast-flowing water has created a steep gully with abrupt edges.
96268: The plains are covered with thick, long grass that reaches almost waist-high. The ground here is dry and firm, offering little support for much else than the dominating grass and a few scattered shrubberies. Although there is no sign of animals or other living creatures here, some small holes in the ground and a few scattered tracks suggest that this area is not entirely deserted.
96269: The small, earthen path stretches out in a due north-south direction. At times, it is merely a faint trail between the yellow-green, long grass. The earthy surface has formed a slight depression that follows the east-west route in the middle of the slightly undulating landscape. To the north, the trail continues between bushes and undulating low hills until it is lost in the high grass that dominates the landscape. In all the other directions, there only grow some dry grass and occasionally, a few scattered patches of heather.
96270:
The corpse of a great mottled feline is lying here.
A short evergreen plant, with slightly bluish needles, grows here.
A large eagle soars above you.

The yellowish grass that covers most of the ground here stands a few feet high. Apart from a few scattered juniper bushes and patches of weed, nothing else but grass has managed to root in the poor soil of this area. On the surface, some trails of a long dried stream are still visible, as it has eroded the ground on its turning point from its eastern course to the south. To the west of here, a small meandering trail stretches out over the undulating fields. To the north and the east, nothing but the yellow-green sea of grass can be seen as it extends to the horizon.
96271: The plains stretch out here, forming a yellowish sea of grass that seems to heave with every gust of wind. Signs of wildlife are sparse here, only a few holes and some faint tracks in the dry ground suggest that this area is not entirely devoid of life. Further to the north, the grassy fields turn into higher, gently undulating hills.
96272: The yellowish dry grass that grows almost waist-high, dominates the open field that stretches out in all directions. The dry soil seems to be unable to offer support for anything else than the most robust plants. Nevertheless, a few withered juniper bushes have managed to root here. To the north, the sea of grass continues towards the horizon.
96273: The ground here is even drier than in the surrounding areas. The soil is bare, only interrupted by some patches of weed and some of dry, yellow and brown grass. Some remains of huge roots can still be seen half buried in the dusty surface, revealing the evidence of the past lushness of these fields. Some leafless skeletons of small, thorny bushes can be seen growing from the weak shadow created by any larger rock lying on the ground.
96274: A tall stag is here, grazing peacefully.

The terrain here is flat and without any discernible features. The yellowish, waist-high grass covers the ground, only interrupted by some patches of weeds and a few occasional juniper bushes. The vegetation reveals that the rainfall in this area is sparse, although some tracks on the ground reveal that the area is not entirely deserted. To the north, the yellow-green sea of grass stretches out towards the horizon. In all other directions, the landscape continues as lightly undulating hills.
96280: The weak trail continues meandering in its east and west course. At times, it is merely a small depression in the green grass as nature gradually reclaims the area. At a few places, the size of the trail indicates that many years ago, this was most likely a well-travelled path, but now, the only recent signs of life seem to stem from the wild animals that roam these grasslands.
96281: The yellow and green grass grows almost waist-high in this area. The tall blades create a sea that shifts in wave-like patterns with every gust of wind. Like small islands, lone patches of brush grow in several places. The endless grass continues to the north and the east, while the ground to the west slightly descends into a low valley. The ground is somewhat lower to the south where the fields are interrupted by a small trail that stretches out in an east-west direction.
96282:
A fallow deer is grazing peacefully here.
A tall stag is here, grazing peacefully.

The terrain here is mostly flat and only broken by a few scattered undulating hills with gentle slopes. The area is covered with lush grass that grows waist- high in some places. Scattered animal droppings on the ground also give evidence that smaller grass eating animals inhabit this area. Occasional rustling in the grass reveals that small animals thrive in the protection given by the vegetation.
96283:
A roe deer is standing here, watching the terrain while chewing the vegetation.
A sand viper is slithering here on the ground.

With no nearby rivers to feed the vegetation, the grass tends to look drier here than to the east. No flowers or other green plants have rooted in this area. Only occasional patches of weed and small thorny bushes interrupt the dominating grassland. Looking in the northern and western directions from here, the plains looks even more dry and desolate.
96284:
The corpse of a sand viper is lying here.
Provost the Dwarf (PP), wielding an ornate, steel-shafted warhammer, is standing here.

The ground is sunken here, forming a canyon-like formation in the middle of the sandy fields. In the bottom of the depression, the soil lies bare without any larger vegetation, only some small tussocks of dry grass decorate the surface. Cracks scar the dry soil at the lowest point of the canyon, leaving some small rocks half buried in the surface. The stones are round in shape, telling their story about rushing waters modifying the landscape once in the past.
96285: The poor, yellow grass strives to survive in the dusty soil that covers the ground. Patches of small, dry bushes and weeds are scattered among the grass. A farmer would have a hard time growing anything here if he were foolish enough to try to cultivate these desolate plains. Only those animals well-adapted to this environment have the slightest chance of survival here.
96286: Dry yellowish grass grows here, mixed with patches of sturdy weeds and other hardened species. The ground seems somewhat more fertile here compared to the dry fields to the east, but the soil is still quite dry. The landscape reveals that some water has been flowing here in the past, turning its course from the north to the east at this place. To the west, the landscape is greener and more fertile.
96287: The dry grass grows knee-high here, covering the dusty ground with a pale yellow-green carpet. While the earth is dry, it seems to be more fertile in this area compared to the dry and barren impressions that are given by the vast plains to the east of here. West of here, a small track winds its way to the north and south.
96288: Here, the pale green grass grows almost waist-high at some places. The soil is obviously more fertile in this area than in the distant brown plains that stretch out to the north-east of here. Just south of here, a visible trail crosses the fields in a due east and west direction, while to the west, a small narrow dirt track twists back and forth along the north and the south. The two trails seem to conjugate in a large, plain area to the south-west.
96289: This small ridge extrudes from the hill to the east of here. The ground here slightly rises to the east where the top of the hill can be seen. Short yellow patches of grass that seem to be constantly beaten by weather conditions grow on the hillsides. To the west and north, the ridge levels out and disappears in the undulating grasslands.
96290: A small brown snake is slithering around here.

The plains in this area are covered with light green and yellow grass that grows a few feet high. As the distance to nearby rivers and other sources of water increases, the ground turns less fertile. This is more evident in the bleak plains to the north and the east of here, where the meagre vegetation shifts to yellow-brown colours.
96291: With the past years, rushing waters have eaten their way deep into the hillside to the south, forcing the flow to find an alternative way past the higher ground. The soft, sandy ground has given away under the pressure of the flow, slowly eroding into a steeply sloped valley. Now, the bottom of the valley is dry, giving life only to some small bushes and various small patches of grass.
96292: The valley continues to the west, while the surrounding slopes get lower and lower towards the east. The grass grows quite strong here, indicating the change in the fertility of the soil. The steep slopes are covered with small bushes and various kinds of taller grass which can root in the sandy ground. A small trail follows the path of the valley near to the south, occasionally disappearing in the thick grass.
96294: The gentle slopes meet here, forming a natural top for this highest hillock in the nearby grassland. Dry, yellow grass grows only a few of inches high here, maybe as a result of the dominating weather conditions. The elevated position here provides a good view over the nearby surroundings. The pale gleam of the Great River Anduin can be seen in the far distance to the east and south, cutting its way through the grassy plains. Down on the southern slope, a weak path can be noticed meandering along the hillside. On the summit of the hill, a small stone building has been erected.
96307: A sturdy pack horse is standing here.

The small trail makes a turn to the south and the east here, finding a way around the hill that rises just to the west of here. The trail was once well- trampled, even though most of the tracks look many years old. Like an output of some sort, a small stone building crowns the top of the hill. A small path branches off the trail here and winds westwards along the hillside.
96315: Thick and lush, green grass covers this area and provides food and shelter for the numerous small animals that live here. Small holes are dug in the ground at several places, and the soft soil reveals several tracks of different size. The ground steeply rises to the north, forming a natural ridge, rising against the side of a low hill. To the west, the ground becomes even more lush, as the humidity in the soil increases.
96375: The trail, which heads in a straight east and west direction, is sometimes difficult to follow in the high, grey-green grass. At times, it becomes just a small depression in the green field. Evidently, this path is seldom used these days, although it may once have been a well-trodden track. At some places along the trail, where the wild grass has not yet reclaimed the land, old tracks of both horse shoes and cartwheels are still visible in the bare, packed soil.
96395: The stream becomes more violent and roiled as the water is forced to pass a narrow gully here between the rocky walls to the south-west and the steep earthy slopes on the northern side. The once crystal-clear water is gradually taking on a brown hue as it picks up dirt and loose soil from the steep hillsides. To the south, the flow becomes less turbulent again as the stream encounters more level land.
96396: Here, a solid rock wall to the south forces the stream to change its direction. As the water crashes against the wall, foam-topped waves and unpredictable swirls form in the current. The relentless erosion by water has formed a gully between the solid rocks on the southern side and the soft, earthy ground east of here. Loose rocks and stones that have fallen from the rock wall litter the streambed and block the flow of water.
96397: A brook trout is here, swimming in the current.

The stream widens out as it exits the narrow gully to the north. The flow is less turbulent now, but still, the water is agitated by the numerous rocks and old branches that the stream has brought with it and that now litter the banks of the stream. The water is humus-coloured and dark, making the it difficult to see through it.
96398:
A black catfish is here, lurking in the mud.
A black catfish is here, lurking in the mud.
A brook trout is here, swimming in the current.

The stream passes under a portal of wood here, which forms the lower side of a bridge. All sounds are amplified and echoed by the artificial roof, creating a hollow atmosphere. Supporting stone columns stand on the banks on both sides of the stream. Lichen and moss have attached to the flat grey surfaces, and brown horizontal lines on the columns indicate varying water levels.
96399: The stream flows more calmly, but still swiftly, as it encounters the flat terrain that dominates the landscape in this area. The stream makes a wide turn to the east around the light forest to the south of here. The water of the stream, which originates from sources high up in the Misty Mountains, was once crystal-clear but has now acquired a humus-coloured hue.
96400: The stream turns to the east here as it makes its way between the light forest on the western bank of the stream and the open fields on the eastern side. The stream is wide and flows quickly, although without visible swirls or currents. Occasionally, small logs and tree limbs float by in the dark water. The banks of the stream are lined by small groves of reed and patches of long-stemmed weeds.
96401: The stream makes a turn to the south to resume its main direction, after a small detour around the lightly forested areas to the south-west of here. As the once narrow mountain stream is fed by numerous small creeks from the plains, it gradually grows and forms a wide and deep river. The water is humus-coloured, and the bottom of the stream is hidden from sight.
96402: The border stream marks the boundary between the open lands to the east and the large forest that grows to the west. The stream which once originated as a small creek high up in the Misty Mountains is now wide like a river, as it has been fed by many small creeks on its way to the ocean far away. The low banks are lined with patches of reed and grass.
96403: At the Bend in the Border Stream

The stream makes a turn to the south again as it meanders through the landscape. The plains to the north and the east of here are low and would be flooded if the water level rose significantly. The banks to the east are lined with pebbles and small rocks as the stream current has washed away any loose material. To the south of here, the stream widens and flows more calmly.
96404: The Great River Anduin flows steadily to the south here. While the river itself flows rather calmly, the small river just to the west of here feeds a large amount of water into the Anduin, causing turbulent swirls and unpredictable currents that might be treacherous even to the most stable vessel. The water is dark and murky, and the bottom of the river cannot be seen.
96405: The Great River flows more calmly but still steadily as it bends from its straight western course to the south. While no visible swirls or any turbulent water can be seen, the sheer power of the flowing mass of water is felt. Along the shallow riverbanks on the western side a small pebble beach stretches out, looking like a suitable landing for boats.
96406: The river deviates from its present western course in order to take on a dominating direction to the south from here. On the stony riverbanks only some dark, stunted bushes and weak trees grow, providing a sharp contrast to the otherwise lush, green landscape that surrounds the river in this area. To the south of here, the river widens up considerably as it takes on a more steady course to the west again. Upstream to the east of here, the agitated water is thrown between the rocks and stones as the river winds.
96407: Here, the river widens up as it takes on a more southern course again. The water is still stirred by the many rocks that protrude from the riverbed and branches and roots of small bushes that dip in the water along the shoreline. To the south of here, the river seems to flow more calm than in the violent bends to the east.
96413:
A large thorny branched shrub is growing here.
A grey wolf is here, snarling aggressively.
A large elk is standing here, chewing grass and leaves.
A nightingale is here, chirping a sweet melody.

The sparse forest that grows in this area contains a mixture of taller deciduous trees and smaller brush-like trees which thrive in the light that penetrates the high ceiling of long tree-limbs. In the rich soil, a wide variety of flowering shrubs grows mixed with small bushes, many of which probably carry edible berries in the right season. The forested riverbanks approach the wide river to the north and the west.
96414: This light sparse forest, mainly defined by various smaller deciduous trees mixed with thick lush grass that grows in the open spaces between the trunks, stretches out over the flat land. The soil here is rich and provides ample nourishment for many kinds of flowers and green plants that thrive among the woods. The course of a wide river can be seen close to the north, and grassy plains open to the east, while the forest continues to the west and the south.
96418: A trained horse (Rood) is standing here, ridden by you.

The trail, coming from the east, ends here at the riverbank of the Great River Anduin. The river is wide here, making the current less turbulent. The riverbanks are low and occasionally on the very same level as the river itself. A small natural pool has been formed in the shoal water close to the riverbanks, lined with a beach of pebbles and gravel. This place could serve well as a natural landing for travellers using boats in the Anduin.
96419: The river twists and bends from the north to the west as it cuts its way through the green plains. The riverbanks to the east and the south are less steep than the ones on the inner edge of the bend. The banks are covered with rough gravel and small, round blocks, and some small pine trees decorate the slopes. Beyond the surface of the dark, calm but turbulent waters, nothing can be seen expect for a few larger stone blocks that reach up from the riverbed below.
96420: The Great River is at its widest here, thus the water flow is relatively calm. One might be deceived by the seemingly domestic river; however under the calm surface, the dark water possesses forces that are to be reckoned. Even the most stable vessels might easily be swept away by the unpredictable currents if in the hands of unskilled boatsmen.
96421: The Great River continues its majestic flow as it turns its course from the south to the west. While the river is wide and calm here, the riverbed narrows, and the water picks up speed again as the river enters the woodlands to the west. On the eastern shore, a light mixed forest dominates the sloping ground.
96424: The stream has finally found its way here from the sources high up the Misty Mountains. It ends in a small delta, emptying its water into the Great River Anduin. The turbulent flow creates swirls and powerful, treacherous currents as the water of the two rivers mingles. The swift flow of the Anduin to the east and the south of here grabs everything that floats out from the river and quickly carries it downstream.
96425: The swift stream makes its way below a beautifully arched stone bridge here. Evidence of changes in water level can be seen on the surface of the grey stones supporting the bridge, showing clearly that in the past, the river has been carrying more water than it does today. Light green mosses thrive on the flat surfaces above the waterline.
96426: The swiftly flowing stream carries the clear water over gravel and rocks that have been eroded and polished over countless years. Coming from sources high among the mighty peaks of the mountain range stretching out along the western horizon, the water is cold and fresh. On the southern side of the stream, a forest shrouded in misty clouds covers the entire bank of the stream.
96427: A Bend in the Border Stream

The clear water swiftly flows over the rock-laid streambed as the border stream turns to the south here. Between the rocks, where gravel covers the bottom, some patches of long-stemmed grass have managed to root in the ever-rushing flow. The stream creates a natural border for the forest that occupies the southern side of the stream. The trees stand tightly together, and the trees growing closest to the stream bank lean over the water.
96428: The stream is knee-deep here, and the riverbed is still visible under the rushing water, although the water begins to take on a more brown hue as the stream is fed by numerous small trickling streams from the giant forest to the west of here. The stream continues to the south, separating the forested western bank from the vast, grass-covered plains on the eastern side.
96430:
The remains of a clump of roots lie here in a heap of rotting compost.
A quiver lies on the ground.
A brass lantern has been set on the ground.
A plain leather belt is lying here.
A shortsword is on the ground.
A shortbow has been left here.
A cup has been set here.
A pair of soft leather gloves are lying here.
A pair of soft leather boots are on the ground.
A plain pair of pants are on the ground.
A plain shirt is on the ground.
A small hunting knife lies on the ground.

The narrow round tunnel descends slightly to the east, opening into a larger cavern-like space there. The walls of the tunnel are barely standing, and without the numerous roots, they would surely collapse. Some smaller roots hang from the ceiling, making it hard to notice any details of the earthy forms above.
96431: The corpse of a subterranean lizard is lying here.

A wide, cavern-like chamber opens up here, deep below the plains above. The walls are sandy, bound by various woody plants and roots. The floor of the cavern is hard and consists mostly of large slabs of flat rock. The entire floor slopes slightly to the east, where a large pool of dark water fills the lower parts of the cavern. The stone floor is covered with a thick layer of moss, and the air is humid and musty. Occasional drips of water fall from the roof and form small, trickling streams that flow along the floor into the pool.
96432:
A grey snake slides along the water.
An albino fish is swimming here, looking for some food.

The large pool of water that occupies the eastern part of the cavern is surrounded by massive vertical walls on all sides, except to the west. The walls are humid with moisture, and water drips slowly into the pool. The water is almost impossible to see through, as the pool seems to absorb whatever light that would penetrate the surface. Small waves occasionally ripple the dark water, as if something might be moving about far beneath it.
96433:
A large pale fish with bulbous eyes is swimming here.
A large pale fish with bulbous eyes is swimming here.

The dark and cold water is almost impossible to see through, as it seems to absorb whatever light that manages to penetrate the surface above. The bottom of the pool is covered by a layer of fine sand mixed with gravel. Rock fragments have been brought here by the constant erosion caused by the dripping water from the cavern above. Due to the unfriendly environment and the abscense of light, the sandy bottom lacks vegetation of any kind.
96459: A tawny-coated bear is sleeping here.

A small hole has been dug into the soft ground here. Some roots and various other plants hang from the ceiling and the walls, decorating walls of this small chamber with natural forms. Some small branches and dry grass cover large roots which lie on the floor. The dry grass has been trampled by big feet, indicating that this hole is being used as a dwelling place by a larger animal.
96461: A large, dusty alcove sits in a wall, smelling of soot.

The walls of this small structure are built of grey granite blocks that are perfectly assembled to form a stable construction. Thick moss covers the stones in lower parts. The building has only one large room in here, suggesting that it was once build to offer only temporary shelter for those passing by. In the southern wall, a wide opening provides the only entrance to this building. In the northern and the eastern walls, small holes yield a perfect view to the surrounding grasslands.
96462: Hidden: water skin, shortsword, soft leather boots, war arrows
A mouse sniffs around, searching for a morsel of food.

Dug in the hill underneath the building above, this small burrow seems to have been excavated to provide a place to store supplies and equipment. Now, loose soil, dust and mould have settled on everything in here, and small animals, time and decay have destroyed most of what was once stored in this chamber. With a bit of luck, it might however still be possible to find something useful here. A thick layer of moss covers the ground and walls.
96463:
A large torch lies here among the dust.
A dented pail has been carelessly left here.
A scuffed and worn leather satchel has been left here.
A large torch lies here among the dust.

This small room, not more than a few feet wide, has been formed behind the western wall of the nearby storage chamber. The origin of this chamber is not clear, maybe the storage chamber was just built smaller than the empty space inside the hill was. The room is round in shape; the ceiling and the walls are round and consist of soil. Some low piles of soil lie on the floor, showing where parts of the ceiling have come down.
96465: A squirrel scampers around here, looking for nuts from the trees.

Tall trees and dense thickets of shrubs and bushes create natural obstacles for a traveller passing through the forest. At times the undergrowth become very dense and an alternative route must be found around it. High above is a sea of green treecrowns which blocks out most light and the sound of birdcalls can be heard as your presence is announced throughout the forest.
96466: The ancient forest consists of tall slender trees, many of them branchless far up their straight stems, and a thick foliage of bushes and vines filling the area between the trees. The undergrowth often reaches heights taller than a man and the density of twigs and cuttings tangled together makes passage through the forest far from a simple task. Far above are the tree-crowns, that has grown into a dense entertwined carpet of dark-green leaves that leaves the forest cast in permanent shadows.
96467: A cluster of dark green, feathery fronds flourishes in the shade.

Straight-stemmed trees, slender and knotless, support a green roof of leaves that hover far above casting a cold shadow over the forest floor.. At the feet of the trees grows corydalis and goutweed in tall beds encircling the tree stems. The soft forest floor bounces beneath your feet, last years leaf-fall lies thick still. Beneath the leaves is a fertile mould supporting the rich and varied vegetation in the forest.
96468: Towering trees with branchless stems stand majestic swaying in the wind. Dense shrubbery and tangled bushes grow among the trees, and the brushwood shows no inclination towards obeisance to a weary traveller passing through the forest. Vines and sluggish branches seems to lunge at gear and limbs with their captive thorns. East and south the undergrowth becomes so dense passage is impossible.
96469: In Khazad-dum you have been amazed by a thousand things. Feats of architecture that would make the ancient Noldo jealous have you seen with breath-taking frequency. You have passed through halls more massive than most villages, and have seen natural chasms that could house whole cities. The hall before your eyes renders those sights drab and pale. Its length is beyond your sight, far beyond if your intuition holds true. Its breadth is enormous, and you soon realise that you do not stand on a floor, but a raised dome-like platform. At the base of this platform lies a pool of lava, heating the air to a demonic fierceness. A single, arched walk connects your platform with a wide, twisted platform to the north.
96472: To the west and east of you the platform stretches. Under it gurgles the molten lava, and for a brief istant panic seizes your mind -- the platform might melt! But, reason clears your brain; the platform has surely been here countless years, and it has not fallen yet. Still, it is of little comfort, as there are no rails or border at the edge, only a sheer drop into magma. Sweat soaks your clothes as both the heat and the fear unnerve you.
96473: A thin and eerily graceful arch spans the distance between this platform and the one north of here, curving in mid-arch. You can pay little thought to the beauty of this architecture, however, as each step you take threatens to slip, and send you sliding into the magma below. This platform dips in the centre, forming a pool of lava. Surviving its relentless heat is a single column, gracefully reaching up to the ceiling. A doorway breaks the murals of the eastern wall.
96474: From the west, the ruddy and burning glow of the lava enters the room. It floods far into this chamber, casting a weird light upon the reliefs carven into the floor. The walls stretch north and east of here, and every few man-lengths an iron sconce protrudes from the wall. The torches grasped by these sconces are sputtering and orange-red; they just barely to illuminate this smoke filled chamber.
96475:
A huge troll, with skin as black as pitch, glowers at you.
A huge troll, with skin as black as pitch, glowers at you.
A huge troll, with skin as black as pitch, glowers at you.

In this northwestern corner of the hall, a crude set of bunks and mats has been set up. Piles of filthy, decomposing furs and dirt lie about, and various bones and bits of twisted metal armour are scattered near the beds. The smell of troll is undeniable here, and in the dim light the smoke twists into demonic shapes.
96476: The rancorous smell of troll and decay mixes with the burning and smoky odour of fire. A faint pounding is heard, and although only at the edge of hearing it soon irritates your nerves and fills your head incessantly. Torch-filled sconces line the walls, infrequently pushing back the darkness with their smoldering glow. Beneath your feet and lining the walls are strange murals, but time and trolls have chipped and scarred them dearly. In many places the carvings are indecipherable.
96477: From the archway in the northern wall, the harsh red glare of molten stone scorches you. It illuminates the carvings on the walls and floor grotesquely, making caricatures of the figures depicted therein. Also, it allows the eastern door, made from dark stone, to be seen. This large chamber strectches away to the west and south.
96478: This corridor was created for function, not form. The walls are bare and unornamented, the floor is smooth and worn. Burning embers hang in bowls of bronze from the ceiling, smoke spills from these and fills the corridor. Hence, the air is thick and hot, and you cannot see far ahead.
96479: On the smooth floor you espy the traces of greyish footprints, and the walls have been slightly discoloured by the smoke. This same smoke, coming from the brazen bowls, stings your eyes and warms your skin uncomfortably.
96480: The walls and floor and ceiling have been stained black and dark grey. The fine dust on the ground and in the air reveals that this stain comes from soot. Continuing eastward, the soot grows worse, while it lessens to a grey haze to the west. Smoke curls from the torches upon the wall.
96481:
A pair of tongs lie on the ground.
A hammer lies on the ground.

Around you is a large and soot-choked chamber. The walls, many a long stride apart, are deeply discoloured. Upon them hang hooks to hold strange instruments, and deep set in the north wall is a burning furnace. Anvils, hammers, tongs, and such things litter the floor, some crudely made, some masterfully. A passageway leads west, while to the east and south small doors are set in the wall.
96482: Racks and tables fill this small room. Pegs line the walls, but they bear no weapons. Very few arms or armour can be found; but the tailing that lie on the floor have been disturbed very recently. The walls bear marks and gashes.
96483: A large stone chest is here.

A large metal table fills the south-east corner of this room, leaving little space for the boxes and shelves that fill the rest. Upon these features space for raw ore and ingots of metals is plentiful. The air has a very distinctly metallic smell.
96669: Again your life is supported by a mere platform. At its base lies fire, a fire so hot that even the glassy-Laen is heated to a burning tempurature. Above your head the ceiling looms, smoke and glowing embers distorting and obscuring its detail. The smoke stings your eyes and infests your lungs, making breathing and seeing and even tasting an ordeal. An arching bridge spans the magma to the north-east, and southwards a great doorway stands.
96670: From the south-west and north-west graceful archways span the lava, joining the platforms that rise above the fire. The platform you stand on lies against the east wall of this hall, close against the mural of a wyrm being felled by valourous dwarves. The details cannot be seen due to the smoky and foul air that surrounds you.
96671: The platform you stand on is larger than the one to the south-east, yet you hardly feel safe. The flaming sea licks the base, and the acrid smell of sulfur is almost overpowering. To the north, a pair of heavy bonze doors stand, guarding whatever is beyond them from the heat. Arching bridges lie to the south-east and south-west, connecting the platforms in the room.
96672: The flames rise from the burning sea around you; your feet are scorched by the heat of the platform and the fire that warms them. The walls of this hall have been coated with soot and cinders, but still through the filth the original green and white of the stone is seen. Ancient dwarves fighting vile beasts of Morgoth have lost their clarity and expressions, the soot has covered them, making them almost indistinguishable from their surroundings. Yet it makes the creatures they face all the more horrid, accentuating each terrible feature. Intricate patterns trace over themselves beneath your boots, leading off to the arch to the north-east and the archway to the left.
96683: The rounded platform narrows, and then spreads out again as it reaches the eastern wall. The wall splits the dome-shaped Laen, and the other side can be seen through a gaping archway. To the north and south is the molten lake, the fires on its surface spinning and contorting in an unholy fashion. In their movements you sense a tortured, shattered sentience.
96684: A strong and agile dales-pony is standing here.

Here the platform splits -- while it still goes east and west, a thin section transverses the fire to the north. The flourishing designs on the floor flow to the north, almost throbbing in your sight. A single, massive column grows from the centre of the platform, rising to the ceiling. Around the top of the column is the cobalt-blue glass, and energy dances and plays above its surface.
96685: In the centre of this vast hall a small, yet almost valiant platform stands, thrusting any who stand on it above the lethal fire at its base. Yet safety is far from your mind, as a terrible evil can be felt to the north. Above you, a soft blue light trickles down from the ceiling, but it is soon engulphed and devoured by the harsh glow of the pool of lava. Strange bridges arch to the north-west and the south-east, curving between this platform and the other it reaches.
96686: Although the heat is still unbearable, for some reason the colours and light are less harsh. A tinge of numbing grey cloaks the visages of horror about you, and even the magma below you seems a bit more distant. The platform on which you stand curves gently as it goes east, and from a portal in the west comes an eerie fog.
96687: A copper penny lies on the ground.

Glassy Laen supports you, and the ridge on which you stand forms a gentle semi-circle, curving north as it travels both east and west. The ridge encloses another fiery pool to the north, and over that a single platform can be seen. Another arch goes southward, gracefully supporting itself over the lake of magma.
96688: The Laen isle curves from the east to the north, ending in an archway. Standing on either side of the archway are grotesque columns, and through them only a dark chamber can be seen. Far to the west, over a large fiery lake, alcoves dot the wall. In each one stands something, but it is indiscernible from the heat rising from the lava.
96689:
A huge troll, with skin as black as pitch, glowers at you.
A huge troll, with skin as black as pitch, glowers at you.
A huge troll, with skin as black as pitch, glowers at you.

Once, perhaps, this was a grand antechamber. Perhaps mighty kings and proud Eldar kneeled before Naugrim lords here. Perhaps... but now those that bow are foul and evil creatures that inhabit the depths of Moria; the lord they serve is the fell Valarauko. The walls and ceiling still maintain their ancient majesty, but now an evil blackness covers them and dread grips your heart.
96690: The lava surrounds you, and you burn horribly. A curving semi-circle of Laen lies to your east, and another platform can be reached to the south. The walls to the north and west are filled with alcoves, containing grey figures.
96691: The semi-circle of Laen stops at the northern wall, where an archway opens into a grey darkness. On either side of the archway, a penitent statue of a Dwarven lord kneels. The surface of the Laen bears many Khuzdul runes, which end with the platform. Although the fiery lake to the south-east holds only some mysterious niches as ornamentation, the pool to the north-west supports some isle.
96692: The fiery hall south illuminates this chamber with a red glow. The starkness of this barren room is accentuated by the flickering light. Shadows darken the northern end of the chamber, but what light does reach it reflects off of a great brass door. To either side of the archway to the south, an empty pedastal stands.
96694: A dark shadow, wreathed in flames and exuding malevolence, towers above you.

The walls are carved from the purest marble, illuminating the chamber and the columns that support the high, vaulted ceiling. The arches far above you are crafted from fine jade, and the engravings on them depict Durin's ancestors toiling contentedly, forging gems and metals of the greatest value. The columns that support these arches are obsidian, catching and reflecting the light, casting black and green shades over all the chamber. However, none of these sights can hold your eyes for long, they cannot help but be drawn towards the centre of the room. Like a moth to a flame, you eyes trace out the brilliance, but are forced to dart away lest they are blinded forever. On a dais there sits a mighty throne. Forged and formed from true-silver, mithril, and bejewelled with diamonds and opals and emeralds, it contains, still, the essence of the Dwarf-lords of the past. However, even its beautiful surface has been charred by an unholy flame.
96765: Obscuring your sight, obscuring your mind, obscuring your will, the gloom clings onto you and sucks out your resolve. Weak and pitiful you feel, and a whispering, tinny voice asks unintelligible questions softly, yet sharply. In your nose and lungs and mouth the thick mist waits heavily, and each sound that is made you hear a hundred times.
96766:
A tawny-coated bear is sleeping here.
A tawny-coated bear is sleeping here.

This part of the underground cavern is considerably drier than the area to the east. The floor here is comprised of soft, dry, silty soil. Bunches of dried leaves are scattered on the ground, and large tentacle-like tree roots hang down from the earth ceiling above.
96767: The floor of this cavern is comprised of dark, cold mud that stains all fabric it comes into contact with. The walls are literally seeping water as this underground area lies directly alongside the river. To the north the cavern continues, sloping downwards. There is a small alcove to the west whose floor is elevated slightly.
96768:
A grey snake slides along the water.
A grey snake slides along the water.

The water begins to get deep here, covering the floor in this part of the cavern completely. The muddy bottom is thick and oozy, and anything that stands still for too long begins to sink into the mud at an alarming rate. The cavern rises up and partly out of this slick mess to the south, but continues its descent to the north.
96769:
A long slender eel glides along the water, its body coiled to strike.
A long slender eel glides along the water, its body coiled to strike.

The cavern has become an underwater pool here. The thundering rush of the river can be heard all around you, echoing off the walls. The river must be right over your head now, and somehow this little cavern has remained unscathed. The ceiling is dripping water like rain; looks like it won't be long before this cavern is washed away entirely.
96770:
A huge black fungus is here, exuding a foul stench.
A huge black fungus is here, exuding a foul stench.
A giant slug is here, oozing around.

Under a fallen branch is a deep depression in which the fallen leaves of this area of the forest have been accumulating. Combined with the water seeping in from the nearby river, the fallen leaves of many seasons have decomposed into a knee-deep, slick, smelly, rotting mess.
96822: The ground is suddenly met by a giant wall of roots and trees. Nothing else can be seen past a few feet into the grey wood. Ferns and grasses grow along the forest floor accompanied by moss on the trunks. Looking up, there is only a web of grey branches and green leaves. The only thing in the far distance that can be seen is the line of trees and the dark cliff that rises in the south.
96823: Rough wooden beams still keep this passage intact, but they appear to be quite rotten, and touching them might not be wise as they sag and bend under the weight of the earthen roof and walls. Dust flies about you at even the slightest movement, rising from the floor to swirl around for a while before slowly sinking back to the ground.
96824:
A fierce bat is here, lusting for your blood.
A fierce bat is here, lusting for your blood.
A large bat is here, hanging in the darkness.
A fierce bat is here, lusting for your blood.
A large bat is here, hanging in the darkness.
A fierce bat is here, lusting for your blood.
A malevolent bat hangs from the ceiling.

A long time ago someone must have excavated quite a large chamber within the hill. Parts of the walls have collapsed now but wooden beams keep the whole chamber from collapsing completely. Dust and earth sprinkle from the darkness above, slowly covering you.
96825:
A large black bat flitters near you.
A large black bat flitters near you.
The small fierce-looking bat is hanging from the ceiling, obviously sleeping.

Charred and blackened walls curve slightly forming a dome with the highest spot a dozen feet above your head. The walls seem to have been made of stone and are covered with soot in which someone has carved an intricate pattern. In the middle of the chamber there is a brownish stoneblock with its upper parts blackened with something unidentifiable.
96836: A sturdy target for arrows, made out of thatch, stands here.

A vast lawn of green grass grows all around, providing food for the many horses you see prancing about. Other horses are being ridden or led about by trainers. In one area, there are some dogs being commanded to perform basic actions, and some falcons and eagles are circling overhead, occasionally heading down to the ground. In another area archery targets and length markers have been erected. To the east lies a large wooden stable, and west is a stand where fine trained animals are sold. To the north is the warrior's yard, where the elves train to fight the creatures of Sauron.
96837: This old and disused cellar holds a murky smell. Debris and parts of broken tools, armour and weapons lie scattered on the earthen floor. Brown water trickles down the moist walls.
96845:
A large bulletin board, entitled "Warriors' Guild Board", is mounted here.
A weapons rack stands against the wall.
A graceful and slender tree grows here.
An impressive elven knight stands watch here (glowing).

Young students, both men and elves, are trained here in the style of the elven warrior, which emphasizes swift attacks and avoidance of blows. There are always groups here, sparring or learning new techniques. Just south of here is a large field, where horsemanship and jousting can be mastered.
96846:
A small oaken table has been set here.
A large stone fireplace with a roaring fire warms the room.
The Housekeeper looks fed up with her job. She scowls at you unhappily.
A sturdy pack horse is standing here.

This small wooden building is made up of a single room. A narrow bed stands in the north-west corner of the room, and a large fireplace rests in the opposite corner. A square table stands at the window on the southern wall, surrounded by four wooden chairs.
96849: A sturdy pack horse is standing here.

This abandoned cellar room is filled with broken things; weapons, gardening tools, armour, blacksmith's tools. Many of the items are so wrecked there is no chance of knowing what they once were. The earthen floor is a little wet, as are the walls.
96867: A humble man stands here, ready to help you with your things.

This room is quite crowded with furniture, dozens of shelves filled with books, bandages and herbs and potions covering the walls. Almost hidden among all this is a picture on the eastern wall of Rilmamir's hero, a strange looking man, wielding a brutal cleaver. While the floor itself is spotless, a large number of used bandages and half-drunk potions lay scattered about showing this room is often used by wounded warriors Rilmamir must have treated. A smell of dried, exotic flowers and athelas float in the air, covering the smell of blood.
96871: A doorwarden stands here ready to obey his master's wishes.

Oak panelling lines the walls of this room, while wide slabs of thin marble make up the sturdy floor and lead out to the west where they join up with a large marble balcony. There are several chairs and a sofa around the room, good for large gatherings of friends. An arched doorway covered by a silk curtain leads south to the bedroom. Through a window to the east, a gazebo can be seen in a small grassy clearing.
96872: You find yourself at a beautiful quiet place. This little peaceful Gazebo in the forest is surrounded by great, ancient trees and magic seems to fill the air. There seems to be a strong protective spell here, making this space feel safe and comfortable. The grass and the leaves of the trees are fresh and green, sparkling like living emeralds. The sky above is beautiful and clear - so calm that one wonders if it ever changes, even when there are storms around. The shadows of the trees provide privacy for those who seek it. It is obvious that the mistress of this place and nature cherish each other very much.
96873: You find yourself on a large balcony made of marble. Thick columns extend from the floor in a semicircle, forming a protective railing topped by solid oak to prevent one from falling off into the courtyard below. The balcony affords an impressive view of the Imladris valley, its inhabitants and the many forms of wildlife that roam free in the area. A wide bench sits near the railing, suitable for relaxation.
96874: An Elven steward stands here, watching over the household.

The smell of roses permeates the room, accented by the soft glow of a few candles which sit on top of a large dresser. Pale marble walls display a few paintings, one of which is a prominent oil print of a graceful dove in mid-flight. A simple vanity lies against the back wall next to the entrance to a walk-in closet. On the west side sits a large four-poster bed with embroidered, silken pillows adorning it, the biggest piece of furniture in the room. A screen of royal blue silk hangs down from the posts. Another silk curtain hangs underneath an arched doorway which leads to the north.
96875: You stand inside a large, megalithic, stone structure. These huge stones are arranged in a sequence of rectangular pillars rising in height on each side of the circle to a climax in the east. The stones have none of the characteristics of the local rock and must have been hauled here in ages past from some distant quarry. In the centre is a large stone slab with a huge number of notches and scores - looking closer it seems to be stained red in places.
96879: The walls of this tomb are covered in strange runes and paintings. These are barely legible now after the legions of time that have passed, but some shapes and images can still be made out. Terrifying images of death and destruction, but amidst the chaos a small party of various people can be made out surrounded by what looks like a bright light. There is a dark passage leading off to the east and stone steps leading up to the ceiling.
96894: With each step and each word, the sound reverberates about the chamber, reflecting off walls you cannot see. The echoes start out faint, but are magnified and grow to a deafening magnitude. And, over all that, the mind strains to hear a faint voice, inquiring into your presence. The gloom plays on your skin and in your nose, deadening all sensations except for the sounds and the voices.
96895: Light. Blinding, stabbing, painful light. It fills the chamber, burning in your eyes and dazzling your mind. Refracted, reflected, and coloured by glassy walls and standing crystals, you cannot make sense of this room. Images of you and others with you fill the room, leaping out at you and disappearing with a random pattern. Pathways lead out in every way, but as you attempt to egress, you find yourself against a cold crystal. With each turn and each step, a whirl of images and half-people contort and laugh at your puny attempts...
96896: Light. Blinding, stabbing, painful light. It fills the chamber, burning in your eyes and dazzling your mind. Refracted, reflected, and coloured by glassy walls and standing crystals, you cannot make sense of this room. Images of you and others with you fill the room, leaping out at you and disappearing with a random pattern. With each turn and each step, a whirl of images and half-people contort and laugh at your puny attempts...

Images of you and others with you fill the room, leaping out at you and disappearing with a random pattern. Pathways lead out in every way, but as you attempt to egress, you find yourself against a cold crystal. With each turn and each step, a whirl of images and half-people contort and laugh at your puny attempts...
96908: The grey mist thickly cloaks your surroundings, isolating you from the rest of the world. The stone floors and walls are cold and grey, and the gloom about you destroys any sense of direction you try to maintain. Each sound you make is amplified and multiplied, bombarding you with nonsensical noise; and besides that you hear other sounds, garbled beyond recognition. The thick air makes your head light, and your sense of time is distorted.
96909: A murky gloom settles about every corner of this stone-walled room. It is not utter blackness, rather a nondescript blankness, of a dull grey that obscures everything beyond a hands length from you head. The darkness echoes with long-past questions and whimpering answers, filled with screams that once were filled with horror and fear but now only contain a feeble sobbing. You grasp for a wall, hoping for some substance in this unreality, but stumble upon a skeleton attached to the wall with only a thin cord.
96943: The orange-red glow of the hall is pierced by a brilliant and almost painful white light coming from the west. Entranced, you nearly forget about your perilous position and wander too close to the edge, but seize yourself in time to prevent your ignition. The platform you stand on encircles a pool of lava, and in its centre a black and red column rises up, holding the ceiling high above you.
96970: You stand between two horrid worlds. An engulfing, choking darkness seeps even from the mithril and adamant doors to the north; over the centuries, even the once-brilliant mithril has been stained black with evil. To the south, a pervasive greyness comes. It threatens you, seeking to sap your life and sanity from your mind...
96971: This chamber is situated between two sets of doors; to the north a single forboding iron door is fitted into the wall, and the southern wall is overwhelemed by a pair of bronze doors. Four urns stand along the walls, one near each corner. The room is otherwise barren. The grey walls smell of soot, and the room is noticeably hotter to the south, growing chilled to the north.
96979: You are immersed in lava, and your flesh burns and melts. West and south you could escape, but to the north and east walls, with strange alcoves in them, block your way.
97003: A smiling hobbit child is playing around here.
The road bends softly here. The air here is fresh and clean, and many pretty flowers grow by the wayside. This road is often used, as the many cart wheel tracks and hoof prints would indicate.
97004: Around you are many acres of hay fields, however, they seem to have been harvested some time in the recent past. The rolls of hay are piled relatively neatly in the south-west corner of the fields. A small flower garden lies to the west; to the north you can see a small path running behind a line of trees.
97005: The road here continues through the heartland of the Shire. Small forests and plains dot the horizon. Somewhere to the south-west is the village of Waymeet, and farther past that Michel Delving. Eastwards lies the largest town in the Shire, Hobbiton.
97006: The road makes a bend here in its long way. Rows of trees on the sides make your walk comfortable as you go exploring the land known as the Shire. Forward to the south-west is Waymeet. Beyond it is the sea, somewhere in the distance.
97007: The road continues, leading as always to mysterious places where an adventurer can find a meaning to his life. Around you, the land seems to be very quiet and peaceful. This is the nature of the hobbits. They just like to stay away from troubles.
97008: The hills here have been a ploughed and excavated until the area is almost level. A yoke and plough are lying in the northeast corner of the fields, and there are a few cart and oxen tracks leading to the south. The grass is starting to grow back in some areas and the fields look ready for planting. To the east, you can see a small orchard.
97016: You are in a grassy field that seems to stretch out to the east. North of you someone is growing some kind of plant in straight rows. To the west a trail can be seen going south and westward. Small bushes make homes for several kinds of birds here and holes in the ground give shelter to other animals.
97017: The trail makes an abrupt turn from the south to west here. To the north you see an immense field stretching out, and beyond that you can see the southern peaks of Ered Luin. To the southwest you can see a fast flowing river making its way to the Gulf of Lhun. Down the trail to the south you can make out Mithlond.
97059: A doorwarden stands here ready to obey his master's wishes.

The walls are clad in tapestries, telling stories about Durin's folk and how they conquered Khazad-dum but finally got defeated themselves, about battles of ancient times and about treasures lost forever. The well crafted hallway leads to a council chamber north of here, and ends in a sturdy stone door south of here.
97060:
A sturdy bed made from solid oak lies here, covered in warm blankets.
A large stone fireplace with a roaring fire warms the room.
A young dwarven servant is standing here, smiling pleasantly.
A small, warm chamber without any decorations. At the southern wall a small bed is placed, and the walls are hung with blue and purple tapestries.
97061:
A water barrel has been left here.
A small oaken table has been set here.
A large stone fireplace with a roaring fire warms the room.
A mother eagle is sleeping here.

A circular council chamber, warmed by a large forge-like fireplace. In the centre of the room a majestic, octagonal table is placed, circled by mahogany chairs. Gem-inlaid lamps light the room from far above.
97154:
On the ground, there are two small piles of coins.
A skeleton of some humanoid lies in the dust.
A small termite is running around making strange sounds.
A small termite is running around making strange sounds.
A hateful wraith glares at you and groans in torment.
A small termite is running around making strange sounds.

This once massive tree has been subject to an age of decay. Insects and grubs have hollowed out the trunk sufficiently to allow enough height for a man to stand up straight. The stench of the dank rotting wood is oppressive and the flakes of old mouldy wood crumble from the remains when touched. The hollow extends about six yards along the length of the trunk and is at most three yards wide.
97155:
A tall birch is here, watching over the landscape.
A tall birch is here, watching over the landscape.

The dim forest is silent save for the occasional creaking as the ancient trees are bent in the wind. The forest floor here has lain undisturbed for years, a thick layer of slimy, decaying plant matter covers the ground. Oak trees dominate the forest as far as can be seen in all directions.
97156: Even when the sun reaches its zenith only a few beams of light would enter here. As a result, moss is one of the few species of woodland plant to have taken hold here. Around the base of every tree a thick blanket of damp, green moss can be seen. Occasionally a lone mushroom sprouts from the ground, however, it is difficult to recognise what variety they are and they are probably best left well alone.
97157: You are walking on a long, winding road heading north-south. It is really more of a path than a road, consisting of hard-packed dirt and a few stones here and there.
97210: The walls that enclose you are of a strange rock: either born black, or blackened from the darkness that fills the room. On the walls are strange carvings, perverted from their original intent of the glory and splendour of the Dwarven empire. South is a great obsidian door, and the chamber extends into more inky blackness to the north and west.
97211: The dark air that fills this high-ceiling chamber is tainted by a disturbing, somewhat metallic smell. At the north wall, in gloomy alcoves, strange terror-stricken statues of dwarves stare into the centre of this hall. Also, between two alcoves, a stout iron portal solemnly seals this chamber from whatever lies beyond it.
97212: The walls curve around you to the north and south, and in the middle of the floor a great mound has been raised. Nine studs of a silvery material jut out of the dais at regular intervals. Along the north wall, broken statues of dwarves, charred by some unknown fire, stand in alcoves. A marble door also stands in the north wall, and the west wall has a dark crystal door set in it.
97213:
A box made from dark wood is on the ground.
A wooden box, made from rich wood, rests on the ground.
An elegant marble chest sits against the wall.

Momentarily blinded by a rainbow of scintillating lights, you struggle to focus your eyes on the contents of this alcove. In it are chests and pedestals, of marble and onyx, all covered filled with jewellery and gems beyond your paltry mind's count. A collage of colours leaves you disoriented and bewildered, and finally your eyes wander to the centre of the room. Around a stone podium hangs a crystal phial, beaming light out to all directions to be reflected and coloured by the contents of the room.
97214:
There are three bars of gold here.
There are three small piles of copper pennies here.
A large stone chest is here.
A few gold coins lie on the ground.

Carefully designed by the elders of the Dwarven race, this chamber is small perhaps in dimensions, but every wall and every angle fills you with a vastness... perhaps the vastness of the riches that were once held here. Now, once again, there are riches beyond most mortals' comprehensions, however they are dark and foul things, hoarded by the evil spirit that inhabits these caverns.
97215: Far from ornamented, this chamber is bleak and oppressive. The walls are smooth and unbroken iron, wrought it seems from a single sheet. The smell of iron or blood -- they are so alike -- fills this chamber, and with horror you look down to your feet. A pile of ghastly skulls, covered in some silvery metal, sits importantly in the centre of the chamber.
97216: Although it has receded, the horror is still present, gnawing at your mind and clutching your heart. A strange and unreal silence is here, and instead of inducing calm it plays with your mind, amplifying your fear and terror. Almost peaceful, the corridor stretches to an evil blackness to the west, and a numbing cold eastward.
97217: A somber blackness fills this hall. No evil or maliciousness fills the air, no feeling of horror grips your heart. The black walls that stretch away to the north and east bear dark runes, and the black floor has grey flourishes embedded in it. The rest of the hall is to the north-east.
97218: The darkness grows heavier, and any sound seems harsh and alien. In the northern wall, a black stone door has been set. Along the arch above it writing has been deeply chiselled. Several long arms of the pattern on the floor stretch out and leave the mesh; they travel to the door and spread out before it.
97219:
An ancient shield lies on the ground (glows blue).
A breastplate, seemingly of pure silver, lies here (glows blue).

Any light brought into this room chases little darkness away -- in fact, the walls of the chamber seem to absorb the light, and its only remnants reflect and dance within the obsidian walls of this niche. This chamber is taller than the others, allowing even the tallest humans to stand without hinderance.
97220: Although the room is dark, a soft light reflects off of the doors to the east and north. The air is infused with an ancient presence, and the silence is sovereign. A strange, morbid peace fills your heart. The flowing patterns on the floor divide into two arms, one reaching to each of the doors.
97223: The wall to your east is black and monotonous; only some barely detectable runes interrupt its stone surface. A large iron door breaks the runes on the southern wall. The ceiling cannot be seen, but the chamber feels smothering and close. To the northwest, the hall widens. A sad quiet fills the air.
