97224: A cold and terrible evil draws the heat from your body. The walls of the chamber, black perhaps naturally or from charring, curve around you. Although the floor is unadorned, and the ceiling is lost in the darkness, the walls have bronze and onyx perversions of a once glorious battle. The air grows blacker to the northeast.
97225:
An orkish soldier of the Urughash is here.
An orkish soldier of the Urughash is here.
An orkish soldier of the Urughash is here.

This cavern has been only recently extended and carved, just like the tunnels that lead south and west. The ceiling is black with soot, from the constant cooking fires. Iron bars guard the way north, while to the west and south are badly dug tunnels, barely supported on wooden beams.
97226:
Water drips slowly into a grey, still pool.
A small vicious black rat squeaks at you for disturbing it.
A prisoner is standing here.
A weary woman stands here, looking miserable.

Iron bars have been erected to isolate this part of the cavern. Chains and shackles are riveted to the walls, some of them holding only bones. These are the living areas of the slaves, both captured human prisoners and occasionally orcs of other tribes. Their labour is used to carve new caverns, and to mine the poor lodes of iron. Not a single piece of furniture eases their life here, where they have to watch the rats feeding on the bodies of their dead fellows.
97252:
A nasty troll female crouches here, with a feral look in her eyes.
A nasty troll female crouches here, with a feral look in her eyes.
A nasty troll female crouches here, with a feral look in her eyes.
A large mean-looking troll is here.

Black-rocked and cold, with small, dark niches hewn crudely along each rough stone wall, this cavern has clearly been chosen as a resting place for the trolls. The gravelly floor is strewn with all manner of litter, and through a jagged opening to the north, a strong smell wafts into the room.
97253: A huge pit, reeking with rotting matter of all types, lies just to the north. Deep and dark, smooth-sided and sheer, anything dropped here will probably be gone for good. The air is heavy with with decay and filled with the high- pitched chatter of rodents.
97255:
A big cavebear is padding around here.
A big cavebear is padding around here.

This dim cave with black, deep shadows lies hidden in the bowels of the hill. However, there are evident signs of animal life in it: hair shreds hanging from the rocky projections, some of them at a suspiciously excessive height; unidentifiable remains of food; an abnormally high temperature; and also the unmistakable smell of living beings in an enclosed place. Undoubtedly, this gloomy cavern constitutes the lair of some great beast.
97256: The dense vegetation of dark trees covers hills to the north and east. To the south and southwest there is a large dark forest. To the west are the only flats in this area. Northwest rolling hills makes the landscape smoother.
97257: A ferocious warg is here, snarling angrily.

This flatland borders the verdant forest to the south. Few trees grow here, only a few hardy birches. It does however give you a good view, allowing you to spot potential enemies a mile away, or they you.
97258: The mud sucks at you, trying to drag you down. A short pause to get your breath and bearings back almost made you a permanent resident of the swamps. Vicious, buzzing insects fly all around you, trying to get as close as possible. Small itches start to ache all over your body, even in places you did not think possible.
97259:
A small leech is here, floating in the water (hidden).
A swarm of mosquitoes is here, humming around you.
The enchanting will-of-the-wisp beckons you with a blurred light.
A swarm of mosquitoes is here, humming around you.
A small leech is here, floating in the water.

Close to where the river and swamplands meet, a lot of ground is under several inches of water. The few remaining turfs of grass that still grow above water seem unstable, yielding unsure footing. Underfoot the ground is not at all firm, but rather spongy and clinging. It sucks at your feet, trying to drag you down. Endless clouds of buzzing insects surround you, feasting on your blood.
97260: Perhaps in some time past this was once part of an immense floodplain of the Bruinen before its course altered to take it far west of here. The southern end seems to lead deep into swampland. In fact, this seems like a bridge of land between the swamps and a large fen of stagnant water to the north.
97261: The enchanting will-of-the-wisp beckons you with a blurred light.

The ground underfoot is unstable, making it difficult for one to stand still in one place. A thick mud covers the surface, drawing anything heavier than a feather into it. A variety of mosquitoes and the occasional duck inhabit the area, but even a duck does not stand still very long in this muck. Towards the south the water overtakes the ground and a large swamp dominates the view.
97262: Waters from the surroundings gather here. Silt and gravel are deposited here by rainwater that flows down from the foothills to the east, and the fens farther north. This bog is easily travelled on foot but the going is slow. A set of hills lies further to the south, where the terrain is more easily travelled.
97263: It might be possible to reach the ledge below, but the straight course could well prove to be fatal. There is a magnificent view from this landmark and many paths that may reach firmer ground can be spotted. Some routes may prove to be dead-ends or passages through which there is no return, so a traveller in these lands should be wary and careful before setting out on a journey.
97271:
A young cave troll is here, staying close to his mother.
A young cave troll is here, staying close to his mother.
The ugly troll mother is roaming the cave, taking care of her loved ones.
An old, strong cave troll is standing here.

This is a dry cave apparently beneath the hill. The stench of rotting flesh is is all around. Some here might even feel the urge to vomit. Putting the stench aside one can very quickly notice the cramped quarters.
97309: The hall bends sharply here, curving north and west. All around you are entrances into simple homes, carved into the chamber's walls. Each wooden door fits snugly into its stone frame, with straight sides and a curved top, and the name of the home's owner carved proudly in the centre.
97310: Here the hall bends sharply to the south and west. Along most of the way are Dwarven-homes dug into the walls. To the north, though, there is no wall, only an opening into an enormous cavern.
97311: Various Dwarven homes fill the southern wall of this passage, and around many doorsteps stand small groups of Dwarves, engaged in conversation and greeting passersby. There is no wall to the north, only an opening into a large cavern.
97313: The hall descends slightly as it continues to the west, and the simple homes seem to become a bit more prosperous. Many Dwarves amble along here, as in the rest of this hall, but you see almost no children. The people of Mahal are strong and hardy, but still, as the long years pass, they diminish.
97325:
A dwarven child wanders around.
A dwarven female is here walking around.

This is a large, grand hall with a curved ceiling rising far above your head. All along the walls extend hundreds of Dwarven apartments, built into the living rock, rising into the darkness. All along these living quarters, balconies extend, and Dwarves walk around on them, or from apartment to apartment, or along the floor where you stand. This seems to be a prosperous area, dotted with marble pillars and elegant statuary. The cavern extends to the west and north.
97326: This is a large, grand hall with a curved ceiling rising far above your head. All along the walls extend hundreds of Dwarven apartments, built into the living rock, rising into the darkness. All along these living quarters, balconies extend, and Dwarves walk around on them, or from apartment to apartment, or along the floor where you stand. This seems to be a prosperous area, dotted with marble pillars and elegant statuary. The cavern extends to the east and north.
97327: This is a large, grand hall with a curved ceiling rising far above your head. All along the walls extend hundreds of Dwarven apartments, built into the living rock, rising into the darkness. All along these living quarters, balconies extend, and Dwarves walk around on them, or from apartment to apartment, or along the floor where you stand. This seems to be a prosperous area, dotted with marble pillars and elegant statuary. The cavern extends to the west and south.
97328: This is a large, grand hall with a curved ceiling rising far above your head. All along the walls extend hundreds of Dwarven apartments, built into the living rock, rising into the darkness. All along these living quarters, balconies extend, and Dwarves walk around on them, or from apartment to apartment, or along the floor where you stand. This seems to be a prosperous area, dotted with marble pillars and elegant statuary. The cavern extends east and south.
97368:
A dwarven cityguard is patrolling the streets.
A dwarven cityguard is patrolling the streets.
There is a small stretch of apartments here, in a passage between two large caverns. To the west the rows of Dwarven doorways abruptly ends where a new tunnel is being delved.
97369:
A dwarven miner is here, digging the hard rock with his pick.
A dwarven miner is here, digging the hard rock with his pick.

This rocky tunnel is still being excavated, but already a few hardy Dwarves are claiming it for their homes. There is a small vein of silver running through the mountains here, and the Dwarves mine it carefully. Carts of iron ore are also frequently wheeled away to the blast furnace.
97395: Starting from the mouth of a tunnel to the east, it appears that many dwarves have already chosen this place to make their homes. A marble hall, though its construction is kept very simple, glimmers brightly when answering the reflection of the burning flame from the torches that are hung on the walls.
97396: The marble hall takes a turn northwards, as it leads to the dwarven homes that are built deep inside the mountain. Torches line the way, their light flickering and dancing on the walls. Most times, the faint sounds of mining and falling rocks can be heard echoing off the walls.
97397: The marble walkway takes yet another turn, leading deeper into the stone-laid dwarven tunnels. The polished marble glitters in return to any light source that passes, and echoes hollowly upon every step taken. Most times sounds of further digging echo off the walls. It seems as if the dwarves here seldom rest.
97398: The marble tunnel comes to a stop at an intersection of excavations. To all directions but east lie sites for new dwarven homes, carefully channeled into the stone by the busy dwarven builders of the Blue Mountains. A few piles of flint and rocks litter the floor of the hall, indicating that the construction here is at the final stage.
97399: A grand hall connects the marble corridor which connects a network of dwarven homes. The polished finish of the stone bears witness to the grand craftsmanship of the dwarves, showing off their strength and will when molding the stone to their liking. To the north stands an archway, leading to a dwarven home site.
97400: This enormous underground hall leads to the east and west, connecting several dwarven homes and home sites. The grey and black stone walls are partly tiled with marble, though it seems that some parts of these tunnels are still under construction. A cart with a load of ore has been left to stand in one corner, evidence of further building.
97401: A rocky landing marks an entrance to a Dwarven home. The construction is not finalised, lots of larger rocks and piles of flint circle the site. However, it seems that the basic building has been finished, providing a perfect spot for any eager dwarf to build a cosy and luxurious home here.
97402: The partly tiled hall comes to an end here as it reaches the western part of this housing section. Slates of rock are piled against the western wall, a result of digging the large halls that will be inhabited to north and south. Eastwards the mixed corridors of marble and stone take one closer to the inner heart of the Blue Mountains.
97403: The walls of the tunnel are still coarse from the large excavation tools. Rocky pebbles can be felt rolling underfoot. This opening however, looks perfectly suitable for building a home. Most of the needed alterations have already been made. A few mining carts stand at the northern end of the landing, probably left here to aid the homeowner in further construction.
97404: This rocky landing has a smooth stony floor. It looks as if the dwarven builders have started to work on this vacant lot in order to make it more suitable for a comfortable home. Some spots on the wall have been reinforced with polished stone plates. The rest lies bare, waiting for the touches of its new habitant.
97405: The landing rises up from the marble hall, a set of stone stairs carved in between, probably for easier access. The landing has been cleaned up, apart from a lone mine-cart that stands in the corner, half-filled with rubble and stones. It looks as this arched stone tunnel could be easily arranged to fit to a dwarfs' liking, providing them with a comfortable home.
97406: The large hall is filled with large tables with all sort of miniature mining equipment placed on them. On one of the tables small carts are placed on some sort of railway, while miniatures of dwarves are equipped with small picks, hammers and tongs.
97407: In the rough cut walls small sparkles of silver reflect the light comming from the large hall to the north. A huge wooden desk, with a silver plated top, is placed in the center of the hall. An unfinished picture of mining equipment is placed on the desk. Cabinets and racks with bound sheets of paper are placed along the walls.
97408: A humble man stands here, ready to help you with your things.

This small oval shaped hall has rich decorated walls; gems, each with a label attached are placed on one of the shelves at the left wall, while several maps, with marks of dwarf mining activity are attached to the opposite wall. At the far end of the hall you notice a bed made of solid granite and a couple of chests. One of them has dirty clothes hanging out of it.
97410: The Entrance of the Emissary of Durin's House
A doorwarden stands here ready to obey his master's wishes.

To the west one can see a small wooden structure, where the guards loyal to the Emissary of Durin's House can take turns to rest. The well-worn stone floor leads to a roomy hall to the north. To the south the bulky metal-plated wooden gate protects the entrance.
97411: This hall is one of the greatest achievements of modern masonry, perhaps not comparable to the great works of Khazad-dum, but still magnificent. In the center an old table with 24 chairs around it waits to host the next feast. Shiny metal in the ceiling together with the numerous torches create the illusion of stars in the sky.
97412:
A clear spring babbles as cool water trickles out of the ground.
A humble man stands here, ready to help you with your things.

This looks like a fine place to end the hard day of a military leader and start a well deserved rest. A door is complemented with woolen cloth to make it soundproof. A simple but comfortable bed waits for its master.
97413: A humble man stands here, ready to help you with your things.

Following the small stream that flows from the pond, a traveller would find themselves in the entrance of this large cave. Several torches sit in a metal bracket on the wall, drenched in oil and producing a blazing fire. Dominating the scene is a rack which stands beside the wall with several pegs hanging upon it. This arrangement is home to a great many various type of weapons and armour.
97414: This small room looks more like a tiny cave. There are no distinctive walls or a ceiling. A small, seldom used firepit with a spit over it is cut into the floor in the middle of the room. A small pile of trash has accumulated beside the firepit. There is a small pallet in the corner where one might sleep. The room is lit by a solitary torch that hangs aside the firepit, casting a dim glow throughout the room.
97415: A dwarven smithy stands here surveying his latest works.
This crude room is filled with the ringing of hammer and anvil. Waves of heat spread from the furnace cut into the western face of the room. A small cart filled with bars of iron rests in the corner.
97416: A heavy desk, made of solid oak, stands here.

Here, bookshelves adorn every inch of wall except for the oakdoor leading to the south. Books lie open and lay about everywhere gathering dust. A small windowed hole in the ceiling provides a hint of what lies outside in the mountainous land of the Blue Mountains.
97447: The golden vein ends here. A large hall opens up to the north paved with granite stone and looking very martial. A small set of stairs heads down to a lower level.
97448: These stairs, connecting the magnificent Golden Road with the fifth level of Moria, are made of a combination of gold and naurond. The two materials intertwine each other and spiral around the stairs adding to the majestic atmosphere of the level above you.
97451: At the Base of a Staircase

An exquisite black and gold staircase spirals down from above, terminating in the cool black basalt of the floor. This chamber is fairly large, with a huge domed ceiling rising above to merge with the tube from whence the staircase descends. A pair of huge stone doors is set in the wall to the east, both doors propped open with grisly pyramids of heads torn from the necks of unlucky orcs. Passages to the north and west have been almost sealed off with crude ramparts built of loose stone.
97452: A small and tough weed grows here.

A ridge of hills stretches eastward for miles, like a series of deep folds in the land. The ground is often broken, providing shelter for the grass and small bushes in fissures and hollows, while elsewhere heather prevails. To the south a deep valley opens suddenly at your feet. Many hundreds of feet deep, it is wide and open - no mere gorge. Woods cover its flanks, and water runs at the bottom.
97453: A few scattered trees dot this green meadow, between the brook and the sheer wall of rock to the north. The cliff, noticeably marked with undulating stripes of darker stone, shields the valley against the harsh wind of the north. It is high and impassable here, but to the east it lowers and breaks. No track you can see crosses this uninhabited country.
97460:
A small white fountain is here.
A large bookshelf sits against the wall.
A sturdy bed made from solid oak lies here, covered in warm blankets.
A humble man stands here, ready to help you with your things.
A tall and strong guard is here.
A tall and strong guard is here.

This magnificent and spacious room has the air of a meticulously maintained museum. To the right there are intricate paintings of fair Beleriand that now lies under the sea. To the left are paintings of the realm of Hithlum. Hanging on the remaining walls are the weapons of Telessars' fallen enemies, gathered from battles he has fought for as long as he can remember.
97461: Deciduous trees rise up into the sky from the moist, sandstone covered ground. Their roots creep around the solid boulders and dig into the soil that harbours yellow and green grasses. The view north and west is dominated by solid walls of nearly vertical dark stone. Towards the south, the trees disperse, and the ground starts to rise.
97462: Medium sized trees rise from the ground, barely reaching above the height of three men. The trees are not nearly as dense as others towards the north or east, but the foliage grows significantly better due to the amount of light available. The ground is covered with hard yellow sandstone, limiting growth of the trees and allowing an abundance of foliage that sits in the comfort of the shade.
97463: The remains of a clump of roots lie here in a heap of rotting compost.

The trees make a giant transition here. To the west they begin to disperse, yet here they grow with more vigour. Giant roots strangle the earth with their grip, pulverizing the limestone that shows up in certain locations. Small types of flora grow on the forest ground in many shades of brilliant purples, giving some colour to the blandness of the grey trees and misty air.
97464: Wooded hills roll the landscape, their tops bald silhouettes against the skyline. The hillsides are mainly covered by moss and young pines and spruce. To the west a magnificent, sheer rockface flanks a very tall hill. A cliff to the north obstructs passage in that direction. To the east the range of wooded hills continues and south of here the Old East Road can be seen, like a brown ribbon in the landscape.
97465:
A huge warg is here, moving in for the kill.
A huge warg is here, moving in for the kill.
A huge warg is here, moving in for the kill.

A flat, broad elevated area looms above the hills to the south. The floor of this plateau is covered by sand and twigs, rubble and dust. Sloping downwards a tad, this flat area stretches further on to the east. Climbing the cliff to reach the hills south of here would be impossible. Some hills with flat tops lie to the north and a tall hill rises off the ground west of here; reaching its top from here is unfeasible unless flying.
97466: You find yourself amid a stand of thorny bushes which tear your clothes and skin as you try to wade through it. It is at times so thick and dense that you wonder whether you will become stuck in it. But, fortunately, your constant pain pays off as your limbs move you, albeit slow and painfully, through this sea of thorns. `Where has the road gone?', you ask yourself as you scan the brush for any sign of the road, but unless your eyes decieve you, you find no sign of the road. It is as if the Old East Road never was.
97467: Always hugging the old road that you follow, hoping it will not lead you astray to either the east or the north in which directions it flows. But, the mute pain and stillness of these dark plains are starting to get under skin. You think you see things where nothing is there, and you begin to hear things from places where nothing stirs. You want to leave this place. Suddenly, you spot a dark shadow moving through the brush on the side of the road to the west! You wonder if this is what had been tracking you all through this place or is it merely your imagination again?
97468: A beautiful and docile horse is standing here.

From the Misty Mountains runs a spur of hills for some miles, creating a steep climb up to the top of Dol Baran in the north. Eastwards, the land drops into a sudden brush-covered dale, accessible from its southern side, but not from here. Here, the land is much like that to the south, although it is sloping and with frequent patches of rocky boulders that have fallen from above.
97469:
A young colt is frolicking playfully.
A sturdy pack horse is standing here.

The ground here is soft and rich, allowing many varieties of grass to grow in the plains. Thin and short, green grass slowly gives way to the taller, waving stalks of brown. A small trail of trampled grass leads to the north, where a spur of hills runs off from the southern Misty Mountains.
97471: A rock lizard is here, motionless as it observes you.

The waterfall dominates the entire cave, with its constantly moving water as a thick curtain to the south. The other walls are in contrast with their hard black rock. Everything is covered with water; the humid air deposits drops everywhere. The wall of water to the south whispers a never-ending murmur, blocking out all sounds from the outside, making room for an unreal silence.
97472:
A shrub with maple-like leaves is growing here.
A fat rabbit is here, chewing on some grass.

Multi-coloured wildflowers accent the lush green grass as the meadow flows to the north and east. The rich earth, in which the field flourishes, is soft and yielding to any pressure, and offers a suitable environment in which a few small bushes and shrubs can thrive.
97480:
A large bookshelf sits against the wall.
A wooden chest stands in the corner.
A humble man stands here, ready to help you with your things.

Located off to the side of the Hall of Fire, this residence is simply but comfortably furnished in typical elven fashion. Placed flush with the northern wall is a single bed, next to which is a desk that is nearly buried in various maps of Arda. Along the western wall, multiple bookshelves stand, containing all types of books and writing equipment. Against the southern wall a lone cushioned chair sits, worn down over the years until almost threadbare.
97481: A humble man stands here, ready to help you with your things.

Most noticeable in this small suite are the intricate carvings upon the marble walls. Upon close inspection they seem to tell the history of the Noldor. Tales of the Kinslaying, the Helcaraxe, and the story of the Silmarils each have their own place of honour. Glory, defeat, joy, tears - all are depicted here.
97482:
A heavy desk, made of solid oak, stands here.
A sturdy bed made from solid oak lies here, covered in warm blankets.
A large stone fireplace with a roaring fire warms the room.
A humble man stands here, ready to help you with your things.
A tall and strong guard is here.
A tall and strong guard is here.

The high, arched ceiling of the room is covered with carvings depicting many of the great battles of ages long forgotten. Light entering from several windows illuminate the room with the colours of blood and war. The resident of the room seems to be haunted by sacrifices that his people have made through the ages.
97483:
A large bookshelf sits against the wall.
A doorkeep stands here ready to obey his master's wishes.
A humble man stands here, ready to help you with your things.

You find yourself standing inside a well lit study of some sort, books and assorted tomes of information are neatly placed on oaken bookshelving which adorns the walls. There is a bed in the corner, as well as a solid desk with various writing utensils. Polished wooden framed windows overlook the activity in the courtyard below.
97484: This dwelling is sparse with the functional kind of furniture of a person who does not pay much attention to art or wealth. The ceiling is arched and high and the walls still exhibit the familiar colour of the wood that was used to build the Last Homely Home. A rather large tile stove for heating purposes is placed in the southwest corner of the room, between the small doorways that lead into the bedchamber to the east, and the balcony to the south. A door is between the room and the Mage guild to the north.
97485: With its good location to the south and delicately ornated iron railing, this balcony should be a relaxing place to sit and watch as the calm waters of the river Bruinen passes by. Farmland and patches of green meadow dominates the landscape and the forested sides of the valley confines the view. A light, warm breeze smelling of burning wood comes from a small doorway to the west. A thin but sturdy table stands here, in front of a small and simple wooden chair.
97486:
A large bookshelf sits against the wall.
A sturdy bed made from solid oak lies here, covered in warm blankets.
The Housekeeper looks fed up with her job. She scowls at you unhappily.

A thin curtain separates the bedchamber from the living room. Like in the rest of this modest dwelling, it is high up in the arched ceiling and the walls have no paint. The floor is covered in a light blue colour and there is a colourful rag carpet that looks a bit misplaced here, maybe a gift from a close friend. A well-used oil lamp can be seen on a black bedside table and the bed itself stands along a short side of the room.
97487: This passage is made of bright wood as well as being brightly lit by several bronze lanterns. The walls left and right are made of parallel planks raised one upon the other and made from teak and fir. The planks extend from the floor to the ceiling where they form a dome. Several different shaped bricks form from teak, fir, oak and pine creates an intricate pattern across the dome ceiling. Looking closer you can recognise the shapes as various incarnations of Eru. Southward the passage widens into a large hall. To the north lies the Cleric Guild, where Rivendell's old priest teaches his art.
97488: Candles and lanterns light this huge hall which is built of dark oak. The whole eastern wall has a strip form of bright pine and centred below the strip is an oilpainting of Elestir. Under the painting is a cosy fireplace and a comfortable chair. Besides the fireplace a dark door can be seen. From the midst of the southern wall an able teaken table stretches to the centre of the room, and along the table wooden chairs are found. Swords and shields of different origin are carefully hung on the western wall. To the north a long passage can be seen.
97489: An Elven steward stands here, watching over the household.

This room centers around a very dark wooden altar. The altar seems to be made of one teak block, there being no lines or cracks indicating the use multiple blocks. On the altar several books are scattered around, all which are about ancient magical items. Some notes have also been left here, none of which make any sense. Even though the altar dominates the room, some other items can be seen scattered about. Along the northern wall stands a small bed with a nicely carved bedtable beside it. The bookshelf over the bed is filled with books, some of them old and dusty others new and bound in leather. A dark door can be found in western wall.
97491: A large eagle soars above you.

Little rain has apparently fallen here lately, and the grass grows on the dry soil in stiff brown clumps, nibbled short by grazing animals. A road can be seen to the east, in the distance; and a couple miles to the north can be seen a building of some kind. A muddy slough just north of here makes it hard to go in that direction.
97492: The road makes another bend here,leaving you with the options of following the road north or east. West there are some plains. To the south you can see something that looks like a high tower of some kind.
97493: A small oaken table has been set here.

You find yourself inside a small outpost with a single door in the north wall. There are some shelves and tables here. On the table there are a few plates with some disgusting leftovers. The floor is not dusty so there has to be someone who goes here regularly.
97495: A colourful butterfly is fluttering around here.

Here the small footpath continues through the trees, now more visible and clear with only a few leaves and twigs fallen upon its path. It is strange however, that you can faintly make out numerous footprints leading north, but none return from that direction.
97498: This small, well maintained field is one of many to be found on the plain of the Shire. As all well maintained fields are, this one is covered by cultivated plants. Amidst this peaceful land there are some towns to the north and a nearby woody hill nearby to the south.
97499: A well-fed cow stands here chewing her cud listlessly.

You are surrounded by rolling hills, all covered in lush green grass. This entire area is perfect for grazing livestock, and that is exactly what it is being used for. You can see a few odd brown spots where the livestock has eaten the grass through to the soil. To the north the rolling hills continue; in all the other directions the terrain appears to be more level.
97501: A hobbit is here walking around.

You are standing on the Old East Road, just east of the Brandywine bridge. A dusty road leads to a gate in a tall hedgerow to the south - the High Hay. It was grown to protect Buckland from the old forest many years ago, and is thick and nearly impenetrable.
97503: The great river flows gently through a wide stretch in the riverbed. Grassy banks turn into steep cliffs in the southeast, where the water seems to gain speed again. At the eastern bank, several rocks have fallen off an escarpment making it possible to climb out of the river. Long, green weeds sway in the current near the banks, but disappear to the south where the force of the water seems greater.
97505: The pale blue-green gleam of the Great River of Anduin can be seen just east of here as it passes by the grasslands. The ground slightly descends down towards the river. Being closer to the water, the ground is more fertile than in the high ground to the north and the west of here, and the grass grows almost waist-high, mixed with some small birches and a few patches of hazel that thrive in the moist soil on the riverbanks.
97506: The small, faint trail here is nothing more than a slight depression in the grassland that stretches out over these fields. At a few places, some small stone mounds have been erected alongside the trail which makes it easier to follow the right path. The trail continues its way in an east-west direction. Some parts of the trail look washed away, indicating that water has once streamed across the trail on its way to the south.
97507: A large rabbit looks peacefully at you, ready to dart away.

The landscape here is dominated by lush green grass, which reaches a few feet above the surface below. Only some patches of weed and a few colourful flowers interrupt this otherwise monotone grassland. The soft, brown earth seems to be fertile enough to support a variety of plants and flowers. Just to the south of here, the form of a weak trail is barely visible in the thick grass.
97508: The green grass unfolds in the every direction across the flat plains and the low, undulating hills. The land lacks distinguishing features, apart from some occasional low bushes that interrupt the dominating vegetation. The soil is quite soft, and tracks from several different kinds of animals are easily distinguishable between green tufts of grass. Some freshly dug holes indicate that moles and other small animals seem to live in this area.
97509: The ground in this area is covered with lush green grass that has found enough moisture and fertility in the poor soil to be able to sustain a healthy growth. Scattered all over the surrounding area, there is a multitude of small holes, dug by some smaller animals that thrive in the protection given by the vegetation. Just to the east of here, a low hill is easily discernible against the green fields. Endlessly undulating landscape continues all the way to the north, until it fades in the distance.
97510: A Grassy Hillock in the Plains

Being slightly higher than the surrounding plains, this round hillock is easily noticeable even farther from the fields. Only low, almost indiscernible plants grow inside the soft green grass covering the ground here. Tall flowers rise above the grass on the southern slopes, while on the northern, steeper side of the hillock, several small animal burrows can be seen.
97514: A Bend in the River Anduin

The river changes suddenly and considerably here. While at the northern part it is still rocky and clear, the southern part is muddy and the riversides are full of reeds, which grow even higher and thicker farther to the south. Amidst the roots of the weeds, some fishes have dropped their hard roe; clusters of tiny, translucent spheres can be seen in the water near the banks.
97515: Owing to their good location beside the river, these plains are full of greenery. Only a narrow line of white sand on the riverbank is different from the general view. Being very nutritious, the bright green grass here has been chewed away at many spots, perhaps by wandering herds and cattle.
97516: Smooth green grass and some bushes cover these fields. A few of the bushes seem to have small red berries growing in them, but they do not seem very nutritious. The ground is slightly ascending to the north, where a small hillock is visible. The lush grass, small bushes, and a few grass-covered rocks add some bright colours to the landscape, while occasional trees shade the undergrowth with their hanging branches.
97517: Vast fields of grass and small bushes, continuing far to the northwest, meet the edge of a lush meadow here. Many small holes of animal burrows are visible in the soft ground amidst sparkling dandelions and other colourful flowers. The thick carpet of grass grows even mightier in the north, as the ground ascends, while the valley to the east is considerably lower than the plains here. The sloping landscape is marked by occasional tall trees, and a faint trail can be seen travelling through the lands in the south.
97519: The wide river, constantly flowing, continues to turn more and more to the south as it runs past undulating grasslands. The bottom of the riverbed is flat, covered with sand and seldom rocks. Strange green weeds float here, swaying in the current. In the west, miles of grasslands lay, and northward, the outline of a small trail can be seen at the top of the rugged bank.
97520:
A bee flies around here, collecting nectar from the flowers.
A buck runs swiftly from place to place, looking about warily as it grazes.
A buck runs swiftly from place to place, looking about warily as it grazes.

Being slightly higher than the valley across the river, this one seems to remain dry even at high-water periods. Yet, the ground here is a bit lower than the grassy plains and meadows to the west and north. The valley itself is covered with bright green grass and seldom higher plants, including a few sunflowers flattering bees and other insects. High walls of reeds block any direct view to the river.
97521: Flowing southwards the current slightly weakens, as the Anduin reaches a wider and deeper part of the riverbed. At some spots the water is practically impenetrable, full of dirt, rotten logs and mud. The high walls of reeds continue on both riverbanks and in the shallow water. Small water plants with white flowers grow amidst the reeds.
97522: Like a tunnel through a mountain, the Anduin river flows through high walls of reeds. Since the bottom of the riverbed is muddy, the water here is quite blurred. Near the eastern banks, a hammer-shaped cliff reaches out from the water. A tiny sprout, barely even clinging to the rock, is attempting to grow on the cliff.
97539: A squirrel scampers around here, looking for nuts from the trees.

This part of the forest is populated by tall pine trees. There is little vegetation at ground level, but areas of rocky outcrops prevent easy travel in any direction, often making it necessary for a traveller to retrace his trail to make progress. At high points one can see a barren plain stretch out to the east. The forest continues to the west where it is perched on the cliffs. To your southwest and below you can hear the distant roar of river rapids.
97540: A large elk is standing here, chewing grass and leaves.

Here a wood of mixed trees clings to the eastern bank of the river Anduin. Here and there you can see some structures high in the trees. Judging by the manner of their construction they might well be elven, although there is no sight or sound of those people. The forest continues in all directions except to the west, although to the east the trees seem to thin out.
97541: A swift and agile forest cat moves silently through the vegetation.

The trees in these woods by the river stand close together. Their thick foliage prevents you from seeing far in any direction, but you can hear the river rapids some distance to the southwest. The ground rises steeply to the south and gradually to the east. Some of the trees seem to be in blossom. The ground is covered with fragrant herbs.
97542: A large elk is standing here, chewing grass and leaves.

Rising atop the sheer cliff that forms the east bank of the great river, a line of grey, sparsely clad trees marks the river's edge. The noise of the river tumbling over rapids comes from the west. The sound fades to the south as the river's flow becomes calmer after the turn. To the east the forest stretches out for some distance, thick with undergrowth.
97543: Some roots lie here waiting to ensnare weary travellers.

The tree trunks in the forest are large in girth and towering out of the ground closely together. Along the base of the trees the undergrowth is thick and very tangled. A few large vines have climbed the old trees so far above, that they seem to disappear into the leafy branches. The leaves of the trees are dark green, and the bark protecting each trunk mainly dark grey or deep brown.
97544: A fallow deer is grazing peacefully here.

The trees here are tall and tightly-packed, in sharp contrast to the well-spaced woodlands which extend westwards. Grassy fields lie to the north and east, sculpting from the vast forests a wooded peninsula jutting out into a sea of rolling plains.
97545: A flat, grassy meadow is here, bordered to the south and west by woodlands and to the north by a stretch of brush-filled plains. Small flowers dot the lawn, their triangle-shaped petals discarded seasonally and blown about by the winds. Farther to the west, the ground rises into a densely forested ridge of land which can be seen extending on a northerly plain.
97546:
An erect shrub with green pinnate leaves is growing here.
Inside the shrub, there are two piles of crimson raspberries.

In contrast to the seemingly never-ending grasslands that extend away to the north and west, this sloping terrain is covered by patches of dense brush. Small red berries growing in clusters give a polka-dot appearance to these bushes, which rise to a height of three to five feet. In the west and south, a serene meadow rests under the boughs of tall oak-trees.
97547: A furry, striped raccoon is here, nosing around for some berries or roots.

These plains are generally flat and covered by a thick layer of grass which has been matted down by countless years of sporadic windstorms. The grass blades are tangled and intertwined, creating difficult footing for land-roving creatures. Short brush grows to the south, beyond which a forest can be seen rising from the horizon. To the west, the grass appears less trampled.
97548:
A roe deer is standing here, watching the terrain while chewing the vegetation.
A small black bird with red markings on its beak is here.

Travellers on foot must wade through tall, thick grass in order to traverse these plains. The footing is somewhat tricky, as downward visibility is poor and exposed roots form lumpy knots of dirt and vegetation. The terrain looks similar in all directions, if slightly more hilly to the north.
97549: Grassy plains stretch away for miles in every direction, swaying rhythmically with the movement of air across these open lands. The soil beneath this sea of plant life is coarse and rocky, which probably accounts for the struggling, faded appearance of the vegetation.
97550: You are in a land of transition, between verdant fields and forests to the west and brown, empty plains to the east. The colours of the landscape fade from bright green to a sun-bleached yellow as your eyes follow the landscape along this vector. Farther to the west, a thick forest of golden hue rises up to meet the faint outline of tall, snow-capped mountains.
97551: A small cluster of clover grows here.

Grasses and flowers of all varieties sprout abundantly from the soft soil. The gently rolling slopes of this green land look like swells in a deep, calm ocean. This rich meadow is but a narrow corridor, however, between the rising trees in the west and the harsh, brown expanse spreading into the east. Far to the west, a forest of tall, thick trees rises proudly from the horizon.
97552: A carpet of lush grass spreads before you, rich with wildlife. The vegetation here must thrive on the same soil that supports the majestic mallorn-trees of Lorien, whose golden crowns can be seen rising above the banks of a great river several miles to the west. Looking southeast, the colours fade from green to brown, as a vast, barren plain extends as far as the eye can see.
97553:
A small black bird with red markings on its beak is here.
A roe deer is standing here, watching the terrain while chewing the vegetation.
A nightingale is here, chirping a sweet melody.

You are upon a threshold. To the west, thick, green grasses sway softly in the breeze, mingling with slender trees and colourful flowers. Farther in that direction, the forest becomes dense and verdant. The powerful song of a great river caresses your ears. These lands seem to exude health, providing a sharp contrast to those hard, brown plains that extend lifelessly into the east.
97554: A cover of thick green grass interrupted by occasional bushes and colourful flowers dominates the area. The rich vegetation is clearly influenced by the close proximity of the river Anduin, which can be seen in the distance to the north-west. Just to the west of here, a dark green forest contrasts sharply against the open plains in all other directions.
97555: A trained horse (Rood) is standing here, ridden by you.

Twisting back and forth between small pine trees and some occasional moss- covered blocks of stone, the trail heads to the north and the west of here, following the southern riverbank of the wide river that divides the land. The trail is wide and easy to follow in the sparse woods bordering the river. To the west of here, the trail heads down closer to the riverbank.
97556:
A swarm of mosquitoes is here, humming around you.
A trained horse (Rood) is standing here, ridden by you.

The green landscape mostly consists of grassland, only interrupted by scattered pine trees that thrive on the slopes of the riverbanks to the north and the west of here. Between the trees, the pale blue and green water of the river can be seen from here. The small trail gently follows the changes in the landscape as if it was planned with greatest consideration to nature. At some places, where the earth seems to be softer, some carefully crafted paving stones have been laid out to form a solid walkway.
97558: The river is narrower here, causing the water to be even more turbulent as it is forced to flow between the steep riverbanks. The water is dark and agitated, and the bottom of the river cannot be seen, only some rocks right below the water surface can be felt as the rushing water reveals their existence. Some twisted, low trees and small brushwood grow along the sides of the river, but the majority of the vegetation there is strong, tall grass.
97559: A narrow and rocky trail following the course of the river leads through a copse of birches here. Soon after passing the steep cliffs overlooking the river, it starts twisting as it enters a forested area in the east. Many of the younger birches have had their bark gnawed off near the ground, hinting at some small rodents living amidst the undergrowth.
97560: A circle of sooty stones lies here in a small depression situated on the top of a hillock. Several yards away, a length of wood is tied between two trees over a smelly hole in the ground, indicating that this spot is used for camping regularly. From here, a trail can be seen in the north, while the thick bushes surrounding the campsite keep it hidden from anyone in that direction. Setting a large fire here, however, could be noticed even on the other bank of the Anduin.
97561: A forest spider is here crawling around.

The trail bends northwards as it passes through a group of tall birches. Threads of spider's web glisten among the trees, and more can be seen gathering some dew near the ground. High and yellowed grass covers the ground from here to the heathlands in the south, where some junipers stand on a low hillock.
97562: No paths can be found leading past the puddles of muddy water sprinkled among patches of cotton-grass and hay here. It seems that travellers have avoided this part of the plains and passed through the heathlands in the north instead. The ground gets harder in the east, where one can see bushes and taller plants. Here, only the slender stems ending in a tuft of cotton rise above tussocks of grass.
97563: At this part of the plains, the brown and barren land from the west meets with muddy earth from the north. There are only some wilting plants, while elsewhere rich ferns, bushes and even a few smaller trees grow. A second look around the brown plants reveals hard rock below a fine layer of unfertile earth. The water from rain cannot be stored in that rock, thus making it hard for the vegetation to conquer all of this land.
97564: The most remarkable feature of this plain is the brown belt of hard soil which runs from the north to the south. Dense rocks beneath a thin layer of earth prevent any larger plants from taking root. Even while some tracks of smaller animals and an occasional bear can be seen, this plain seems to be desolate. Small rocks lie scattered in the dust and between clusters of brown grass. To the east, where the sun rises in the morning, the thin grass gets greener and greener, until it finally meets the first smaller bushes. From there, it grows into a high meadow.
97565: This hard soil has seen a big fire not long ago. The formerly dry grass has burned down as well as the few bushes from which only a few blackened and crumbled remains stick out of the soil. To the east, the plain becomes greener and moist, so the fire was forced to stop there. The remains of an old campfire lie in the middle of the ash-covered plain. At the borders of the great burning, nature is just starting to reclaim what was lost, but to the north, the south and the west, the ground does not seem to be fertile enough for fast regeneration.
97566: A brown furry gopher is here, ready to dive back underground.

In the northern part, the plain is scorched and black, and only some grass has just started to grow again. Obviously, the burning stopped when it reached a broad girdle of stone and rock where only a few thistles could take root - not enough for a fire to spread further. Behind that girdle to the south, the plain becomes covered with medium high, yellow and green grass which hides many little holes dug by gophers, rabbits or similar creatures. Little piles of loose rocks, maybe of the size of a halfling's fist, are scattered over on this plain. With all these rocks and holes around, any rider is forced to dismount.
97567: A dense carpet of blue flowers dip their heads in the breeze.

All sorts of grass cover the plain here and form much more than only one meadow. At some spots, the grass is thin, yet high, while elsewhere, it grows low with broad leaves and a thick, healthy green colour. Where two or more of these meadows meet, they mix and form an area which seems nearly colourful, yet it only contains many shades of green. Only very low bushes peek out of the sea of grass, and some of them are nearly overgrown by patches of particularly high grass.
97568:
A large shrub grows here, its branches loosely spreading.
Some cereals that look like wheat are lying here.

Swaying and bowing in the rhythm of occasional breezes, a large, obviously wild wheat field fills the plains, surrounded by a large green meadow, stretching only to the south. A few rowans and cherry trees grow in it, offering shadow during hot summer days. A few tiny furrows running through the ground create waves in the wheat, making it look like a yellow sea.
97569: Northwards, a solid looking wall of briars and pines slowly and smoothly blends into a field of golden wheat that is enclosed by green grass to the west. Dog roses arise amidst the wheat, growing in a few spread clusters, while bluebells and coltsfoot can be seen in abundance among it.
97570: A tall pine tree grows here.

A field of high grass mixed with thorny weeds turns into a tangled wood of briars more and more to the north, building a living wall of thorns. Small, crouched pine trees are visible among the briars, making the thicket even harder to pass. Small scarlet bushes with large clusters of red berries grow in small patches, adding bright dots in the colour of the landscape.
97571:
A cluster of white star-shaped forget-me-nots flourish here in reminiscence.
A roe deer is standing here, watching the terrain while chewing the vegetation.

Manifold flowers grow among high green grass, filling the meadows with different colours during the course of the seasons, apart from winter. A single, high willow tree overlooks the field, its branches reaching out wide and low down to the grass. To the north, the vegetation becomes denser, and thorny shrubs take over the place of the flowers.
97572:
A hollow tree is growing upright here.
The rabid rabbit is here, frothing at the mouth.

Lush green grass inhabits the fields, crowded with wildflowers of manifold sizes and colours. The plains expand far into the forests to the south and the west, creating deep grassy pockets in the woods. Close to the borderline where the forests and the plains meet, bushes and smaller trees have claimed their share of the ground, and ferns are rather common in the eastern parts.
97573: The transition of the forest, from the meadow to the east, takes place here. There are numerous saplings which have sprouted from the earth. Each sapling has a light-coloured brown bark at the base where it meets the ground. Developing branches on the saplings are still quite green though. The trees along the outer edge of the forest are small in comparison to the ones that are deeper within. There are a few pine trees growing within the forest transition, their needles being soft green in colour. Eastward, there is a meadow filled with different lengths of grass. A forest cabin stands to the north.
97574: A large stone fireplace with a roaring fire warms the room.

The walls of the cabin were made from some red stained wood, probably from the trees of the surrounding forest. Decorations of leaves and drying floral arrangements adorn the high timber ceiling and sturdy walls. A polished oaken table stands in the centre of the room, beside an empty bed. The bed has a wooden frame, ornamented with elegant embellishments. A soft rug, made of animal fur, lies on the smooth floorboards in front of the fireplace. The cabin seems uninhabited but frequently visited, perhaps providing shelter during long hunting trips.
97575: A dense carpet of blue flowers dip their heads in the breeze.

The forest is not heavily wooded here at all. The trees reach to a tall height above, the sky being visible still due to the spacing between the trees. Each tree has a slightly different shape to it. Some of the trees are wide, their branches being very full of leaves. Other trees are more slender in appearance, as the branches are very thin and do not bear many leaves. The bark that protects the trunks of these trees displays an assortment of colours. A few of the trees have bark of a light-coloured grey and leaves in the shape of a diamond. The leaves are soft green and appear as though they were made of silk. Other trees in this forest have different tones of brown on their trunks and leaves of dark green.
97576: A forest spider is here crawling around.

This area of the forest becomes closely wooded as it continues to the west, then begins to slope gently downhill. In the east, the trees begin to thin out as they meet the edge of a brushwood. To the south the trees are cluttered together and the undergrowth surrounding them seems almost impassable. There are tiny vines of ivy attempting to scale the trunks of many of the trees here. In the centre of every ivy leaf, there is a soft white stripe. There are a few fallen branches upon the ground, surrounded by a thin bed of grass.
97577: There are two light boats of reeds here.

The dense forest surrounds the riverbank here. Massive trees are looming above, with their uplifted roots making it difficult to travel. Some of these roots are even cluttering the riverbank as they take a dip into the rushing water of the Great River. The only passable way from here would be to attempt to cross the swift waters of the river to the south, or take a chance of surviving the dark journey under the trees of the forest.
97578: The trunks of the trees in the thicket are slender and have a silvery tone to their bark. A majority of the trees are short in height in comparison to the trees looming above to the west. Each leaf on the trees is light green on the top, and underneath they are white. Several blades of grass have grown in the thicket as well, quite refined and a soft colour of green. On the east side of the thicket, a large tree has fallen to the ground and is starting to rot. Looking above the trees of the thicket, a tower of some kind can be seen standing in the distant south.
97579: There are a lot of bushes and shrubs growing in the brushwood. Debris from the forest lies in pieces of various sizes on the ground. Some small trees are growing in the thicket to the south of the brushwood. A few brown shrubs with an abundance of thorns growing from their short branches are spread out among the brush here. Only a few blades of dried-up grass can be noticed, with the rest of the ground being composed of dry and bare soil.
97580: A waist-high evergreen shrub grows here, with thick, reaching branches.

Many sage plants are growing here in the meadow. The plants have a two-toned colour of grey and green, blending in well with the light-coloured grey bark of the forest to the west. Encircling the sage plants in the meadow are blades of grass that appear closely grown together in bundles. Most of these blades are a lighter shade of green.
97581: The meadow expands in all directions other than west, where a forest can be vaguely seen. Grass consumes most of the meadow, along with a few weeds. Most of the weeds are long, slender and brown in colour, some of them have dried flowers at their tips. Several tree saplings have sprung up from within the earth as well. These saplings are extremely young since their bark is still a light shade of green. The grass displays a different shade of green, along with a few patches that are golden brown.
97582: A small cluster of clover grows here.

A river coming from the east leads to a waterfall, tumbling down over a couple of rocky patios resulting in spray and myriads of tiny water drops filling the air. With a thundering noise, most of it finally disappears somewhere behind the spumy curtain, while some of the water flows over the patios and forms a tiny lake below the waterfall. Ferns and moss prosper everywhere near it, while lush green grass, rarely interrupted by a small sapling, dominates the surrounding meadows.
97583: Perched in a weird formation by forces of nature, large red blocks of sandstone solemnly rest atop a small pedestal of rock. It is likely that their order is a result of common winds laden with dust, eroding a tower of sandstone over centuries. The stones are encircled by thick, green grass, and the air smells fresh, sometimes carrying a faint scent of water from the south and resin from the north when appropriate winds carry it along.
97584: Embedded in a wide valley with overhanging walls, long and high ferns thrive below large firs and spruces. Encompassed by the ferns, moss nearly completely disguises rocks, and broad, intertwined briars form a dense, thorny thicket, forcing even the most skilled rider to lead his mount. A dark, hollow pathway, shielded by the treetops against the sun, leads through this wilderness.
97588: Hissing and tumbling, water rushes along a river, filling the air with its sound and smell. Lush grass flourishes on its banks, interrupted by hibiscus bushes and dandelions, and inclined trees hang their branches wide over the stream, casting shady places on it. The surrounding plains are clad in gold and green, their colours coming from the high grass populating them.
97599:
A round tangle with waxy leaves and white berries grows on a branch nearby.
A rabid rabbit is here, frothing at the mouth.

A wide basin with high and overhanging walls lies embedded in the nearby plains, about a mile in radius. High firs inhabit it, and among them, a subspecies with hard, spiky and triangular warts instead of needles makes travelling in this forest painful for a careless wanderer. The air seems somewhat hotter and wetter than one would guess, further aggravating travel conditions, and often loud, sharp noises of animals can be heard. A tree much higher than all others grows close to the northern wall.
97603: A steep rock spike with a flat plateau, seemingly polished by the forces of centuries of wind, looms here over the bed of grass surrounding it. Myriads of dandelions and daisy chains sprout among the high, green grass. Near the base of the rock spike, a spring gurgles forth from a large crack into a small basin of granite.
97606: A few trees have taken root in the plain. High grass grows near their base, thick tendrils have chosen their trunks as place to grow closer to the light by climbing up their brown bark. The sounds of things living here can be heard all around. Unseen insects and vermin create a constant humming and rustling in the background. To the south, a steep cliff arises from the nearly flat plain and casts a huge shadow, which only disappears completely in the darkest and moonless nights. Like a guardian of the northern parts, a huge and ancient row of bushes blocks sight and way in that direction.
97607:
A small animal, all covered in spines, snuffles amongst the undergrowth.
A small animal, all covered in spines, snuffles amongst the undergrowth.
A snake slithers towards you.
A sparrow is flapping around on the ground.

Grass and a few low bushes cover the northern plain while, the vegetation to the east and the south gets much denser. Travelling here is not hindered, but it does not seem to be possible to pass through the high row of bushes which stretches from the northeast to the southwest. All around there, are signs of animal life to be recognised, as nests and droppings of birds or the rustling of rabbits and other beasts, too small to be spotted among the high and bent grass.
97608: Groups of large bushes, high grass and the occasional cluster of ferns cover this plain. There are a lot of rocks and stones here hidden by the leaves and the grass coloured in all of the many shades of green and yellow. It is impossible to cross this place while riding, as any mount could break a leg here among the rocks too easily. To the south, a white pile of rocks rises from the plain, while the ground has less vegetation. The soil there seems to be drier than in the surrounding areas. Many small cracks run through it and vanish down into the soil.
97609: A Pond in the Overgrown Plain

Many trails have been trampled into the rich ferns and the high grass, leading through and around bushes to a small, nearly completely overgrown pond. In the soft mud, many imprints of various animals can be seen. Next to the pond, there lie three big rocks, all half sunk into the soil, as if some giant had placed them here for the weary traveller to rest on.
97610: Dense ferns cover the plains, hiding every part of the soft soil. The light green of the fern is only broken by the round stems of trees, which stretch their branches six to twenty feet above the ground. A few paths created by all kinds of animals appear here and there in the thick green, meander through the underbrush before disappearing out of sight.
97611: Grassy fields and thick ferns cover this end of the plains. In the east, tall trees rise above a tangled shrubbery, marking the outskirts of a forest. The ground slopes gently towards a heath in the north. Some dry stalks of tall plants stand in the grass, spreading their seeds to the wind.
97612:
A short evergreen plant, with slightly bluish needles, grows here.
On the plant, there are two clusters of hard, round, black berries.

Several juniper trees cover a low hillock in the heath, adding greenery to the otherwise barren landscape. Some juniper branches have been cut off with a sharp object; someone passed through here, but the markings are more than a few days old. In the east, the heath turns into a field of weeds, and in the north, a trail is winding through a group of tall trees.
97613: A large beautiful rose bush is blooming here.

Clusters of smaller trees stand scattered to the north, while to the south, a dense row of bushes grows. Between these, there is not much diversion for the eye, since only high grass grows there. The trees themselves are young oaks with dark brown trunks, while the bushes are partly thorny but mostly thick and old so that they even block the path to the south.
97614:
A pile of dry, brown leaves lies here.
A sparrow is flapping around on the ground.

Layers of dried leaves cover the floor of this oak forest with a swathe of dulled red and greyish orange. The trees here have seen numerous autumns and springs, but now their time seems to have come to an end. The trees stand still, tall and unbowed. Yet, their successors can already be seen: Young birches grow scattered all over this part of the forest and wait for their time to come. One day, a forest of birches is likely to grow in this place.
97950: Clustered tightly with the rare exception of a few small, narrow pine trees spotted amidst them, large magnolia bushes fill the plains, drowning them in a sea of blooms during spring. Bright green grass fills the gaps between and under the magnolias, and a few clusters of wildflowers protrude at places where the grass is lower. Many obvious traces of activities of small animals are visible, and occasionally some of their noises can be heard.
97951: Not long ago, this plain has been a wild orchard of apple trees. Since then, most of the trees, some of them being quite old, have been felled. A great fire has burned here, and the gnawed remains of many animals lie around scattered. Many of the trees seem to have been felled for no reason, since they have been left here to decay.
97952:
There is a red, delicious-looking apple here.
An apple tree with bright green leaves grows here.
On the tree's branches are two apples.
A dove is standing here.

Wild apple trees grow here. Each of them has its own area of influence where its wide branches throw their shadows. The trees spread as far as the eye can see on this plain. A huge row of dense bushes grows from the north to the west, and probably this row has caused just the right circumstances for this wild orchard to prosper. Low, yet very thick grass covers the soil and forms a soft carpet.
97953: Spirals of earth, formed by numerous eddies over many years, interconnect and weave upon the plains into a strange, twirled pattern. The vegetation, mostly long, soft, golden grass, has adapted to the shape of the ground below. It shows the same circular constellations as it, shimmering like glowing runes when sunlit.
97954: A tall, stately, dome-topped tree grows here.

A small river in the plains coming from the east passes a few narrows on its way to the south-west. They are created by some boulders in the streambed, making the river rush rapidly past them, foaming and gurgling. Birches and willows seam the flanks of the water, highlighting them and dipping their branches deeply in it, and in spring, their pollen creates yellow cords on the surface of the current. Beyond the trees, high green and golden grass flourishes, spreading over the plains and overflowing the ground.
97955: A small bubbling stream coming from the north slowly changes its course and turns westward in a long curve, as if an invisible barrier forced it to bend. The vegetation of the plains, mostly grass, is rich and lively nearby, growing untamed and high. Animals passing by have left their signs, as here and there a patch of grass is pressed down. A constant sound like muffled thunder is carried along when the wind blows from the west.
97956: A grey wolf is here, salivating profusely.

This area of the meadow is directly north of a wide, grassy plateau. At the base of the plateau, there are long blades of grass, stretching up high towards the sky above. There are small patches of weeds mixed among the green grass. Most of the weeds are prickly, with fine spikes extending from their leaves. The leaves on the weeds are shaped like spearheads and rather small in size. The meadow continues to expand to the east.
97957:
A black crow flies low to the ground here, looking for carrion to eat.
A grey wolf is here, salivating profusely.
A grey wolf is here, thin from starvation.

Atop the plateau, much of the surroundings is visible. A brushwood begins to fade to the south, where a lot of debris can be noticed on the ground. There is a meadow to the north of the plateau, filled with long green grass. The footing here appears to be stable. Being covered by grass, it is easy to notice how the ground is truly flat on the plateau. The grass is of a soft colour and shorter in length than the grass that arises around the slopes of the plateau.
97958: The brushwood diminishes from the larger portion of it to the west. Shrubs that are of different sizes and colours are in growth. Many broken tree branches lie scattered around on the ground. Some of the branches are skinny, others are truly bulky. Stuck in some of the brush are dried-up leaves that must have drifted in from the forest. To the east there is a meadow filled with grass, and a grassy plateau arises just north of the brushwood.
97959:
A grey wolf fur is here lying on the ground.
The butchered corpse of a rabid, grey wolf is lying here.
A small campfire burns here, its low flames giving off only a little light.

The grass of the meadow is lengthy, each blade being slender and green. To the south, where the forest stands, the undergrowth is very noticeable. The plants become tangled right along the eastern edge where the open meadow begins. Many weeds are growing all over, though some of the grass is much higher, causing a large majority of the weeds to be overlooked. Together they seem to conceal much of the slightly rocky ground.
97961: This underground lake measures nearly twelve yards from one wall to the other. It is nearly perfectly round, and a cascade of shimmering water falls from above and splashes into the lake. The water is pretty clear in the upper part of the lake, but around two, three yards below the surface, it gets darker and dirtier, making it impossible to see the bottom. A small, crystal clear stream rushes out of a narrow tunnel to the east and flows on through a lower, but broader one to the west.
97962: The narrow tunnel becomes wider to the west, and the water rushes to that direction. It is just some two feet deep and so clear that it nearly emits its own, light blue light. The ground is smooth and mostly flat, whereas moisture makes the walls shimmer slightly. To the east, the tunnel seems to have caved in years ago, and to the south someone created carvings in the stone.
97963: A Stream in a Low Tunnel

The tunnel is quite low while the walls, ceiling and floor have been polished by the rushing water. From the ceiling, dark green algae hang into the water and soft moss grows in spots at the upper part of the walls. Further west, the tunnel gets even lower and finally, the rock touches the ripples and the fast flowing stream continues underwater.
97964:
A black catfish is here, lurking in the mud.
An albino fish is swimming here, looking for some food.

The rock is smoothly polished by the permanent current. Some low plants, growing on the bottom of this stream, move their tendrils in the flow of the water, and little, yellow dots shimmer on their long, flexible leaves. The tunnel gets narrower but also much higher in the southern part.
97965: A Narrow and Deep Underground Stream

While the walls on the sides could be touched by stretching the arms, the bottom and ceiling of this stream are barely visible in the dark. Yet, it can be made out that the floor seems to be covered with dark soil and an occasional plant with large, nearly perfectly round leaves.
97966:
An albino fish is swimming here, looking for some food.
An albino fish is swimming here, looking for some food.

As the underground stream becomes narrow and very low, the current is very strong in this place. In this current, it is hard to figure out where bottom, ceiling or side are. The walls, however, are slick and napless, and only very few, thin algae are able to grow on the bare rock. In the far end of the sight, the tunnel gets even narrower, and the stream rushes into a black hole to the south.
97983: The surface on the top of this cliff is nearly flat and offers a good stand. A few big rocks and protrusions offer shelter against strong winds, while the view over the mostly flat landscape around is reached only by few places.
98013: A mass of wriggling vines drops on you from the trees.

This section of the forest lies just north of a gigantic pine tree. The pine tree must obscure most of the sunlight and moisture that would land down here, for most of the smaller trees under it look slightly withered and worn. The fields to the east look grassy and should be easy to travel through.
98024:
A cluster of dark green, feathery fronds flourishes in the shade.
A large, loyal falcon is circling above.
A grey wolf is here, salivating profusely.
A grey wolf is here, thin from starvation.

Light-coloured ferns grow all over the ground here. The ferns have spread out from the forest that stands to the west, along with many other types of undergrowth. Most of the ferns are several feet high, their soft green colour standing out from the rest of the plants that are closer to the edge of the forest. The forest itself appears to be very dense, dark, and full of growth. The plains begin to expand towards the east from the bracken field.
98025: Deep Bend in the River Anduin

The river is deep and dark here. Popping bubbles along the surface of the water show that this section of the river is not completely devoid of life. The constantly moving river turns to the south, while in the east there is a tall pine tree, a rarity in the soft soil of this area.
98026: There are two piles of wild strawberries here.

Lush from the moderate rainfall and temperate climate, the plains here look wide and inviting. A relatively barren clearing lies eastwards, its red-brown soil a stark contrast to the bright green here. There are a few small bushes which may bear fruit when the season is right.
98027:
A fierce boar is here, making grunting noises.
A boar cub is playing here, and exploring the wide world.
A boar cub is playing here, and exploring the wide world.
A pack horse (loot) is standing here, ridden by you.

A large, rotting pine trunk lies on the ground here, blocking travel to the west. Judging by the jagged stump nearby, the flexible body of this tall tree must have snapped from powerful winds. Off to the east, there are several other trunks that were certainly cut down from the surrounding forest, as these logs are stripped bare of their branches already. A few stumps still stick out of the earth here, while only a couple living trees remain standing.
98028: A swift and agile forest cat moves silently through the vegetation.

The forest of pines here appears to be thinner than the range of lush and deciduous forest to the west. Brown pine needles litter the ground, and a few weeds have sprouted from the earth. To the east, the large conifers give way to tall grasses and diminutive weeds, signalling the edge of the forest. The trampled ground and some blackened pieces of wood inside a circle of stones indicate that this spot has been used as a campsite.
98029: Tall weeds, grasses of every size and tiny flowers dot this section of the riverbank. The soft mud near the river's edge gives way to much firmer ground farther away. This has allowed small saplings to take root as an extension of the forest. To the west lies the winding Anduin River.
98030: The riverbank here is covered with thick mud composed of dirt and decaying materials that are being washed downstream. There are only short grasses and dirty weeds growing here, but intermittently a fungi-covered tree trunk can be seen decaying in the muck. The river lies to the west, while to the east and northeast there appears to be a large field.
98031: The plants that occupy these plains are gentle and tall. The grasses and weeds look as though they will rustle and sway at the slightest breeze. A thin layer of flat grass covers the dirt, probably felled by pouring rain or harsh winds.
98032:
A placid pond is here, inviting you to take a refreshing drink.
A crayfish is here, snapping its claws at you.
A crayfish is here, snapping its claws at you.
A beautiful and docile horse is standing here.

A small pond is here, in the centre of the meadow, surrounded by long blades of green grass. There are several types of weeds growing among the grass here as well. Some are extremely tall and lean, while others are wide and short. The water of the pond looks very clean and clear, and has several long-stemmed plants growing along the edges. The spear-shaped leaves upon these plants are of a dark green colour.
98033: The ground here is covered by grass, but drops to the north rather suddenly. There is a dale below the shelf to the north, where there probably was once a small stream flowing through. Several weeds are scattered in bundles here, dark green in colour and with small leaves upon their stems. The shelf seems to fade away both to the east and west, but with less grass growing in the eastern direction.
98034: A rock lizard is here, motionless as it observes you.

Grass emerges from the shelf to the west, but is cut off by dried and cracked ground here. Only a few weeds have survived to keep growing, and only from within the cracks along the ground. Most of the water from the rain probably seeks its way into the cracks, giving these weeds enough nutrients to survive. There are stones of various sizes scattered across the ground, with different textures and colours. Some smaller pebbles cover the ground in sections to the east. To the north, there is a steep ledge that leads down to a small dale.
98035:
A rabbit is here eyeing your presence warily.
A beautiful and docile horse is standing here.

A small ledge begins to form in the centre of these dried grounds. It slowly gains height as it climbs to the west, with a few rocks mixed into the soil. The ground is dry and only few blades of grass have survived here, with three small bushes standing on the eastern side of the ledge. The bushes are short, and their leaves are crisp and dying.
98036: Movin the Hobbit, wielding a black runed dagger, is standing here.

It looks as though a streambed had once passed through here, though now it is diminished and only a slight trace of it along the ground can be noticed. Many fine grains of sand cover most of the ground here along with tiny pebbles, a mixture of various colours. The grass along the west and east side of the faded streambed is bright green, as though it really flourished near the water at one time long ago. Near the south end of the old streambed, young blades of grass have grown, but it is not nearly as thick as the surrounding patches.
98037: A colourful butterfly is fluttering around here.

The streambed appears to have once led here from the west, and after a slight curve it headed in a southbound direction.
