There are several plants trying to emerge from the dried and cracked soil of the dried-up bed, but it would appear they are struggling to survive here. Some bright green grass has grown thick to the north, where it looks like the plains expand.
98038: The ground is rough and cracked, with very small pebbles upon it in random piles all over. The remains of a streambed can be noticed by the markings and patterns along the ground, travelling east and west. A slight ledge forms in the south and appears to grow higher as it continues westwards. The ledge to the north is very tall, with some green grass noticeable on the top, continuing both east and west.
98039: The dale is half covered by small pebbles on the west side, and dry patches of bare earth on the east. An occasional weed can be noticed, sprouting up from the earth between the pebbles and looking very dry and unhealthy. To the north and south are large walls of natural earth. This dale, long ago though, was most likely a small and quiet stream, but has since dried up and remained bare.
98040: The ground of the dale is covered by rocks and tiny pebbles. Portions of bare and cracked earth can be noticed, with only a few scrawny weeds trying to grow there. The dale appears to continue to the north and east, while there are large walls of natural earth both to the west and to the south. On the ledge above, a bed of grass is growing. Clumps of dirt fallen from above lie along the base of the walls.
98041: On both the east and west sides of the dale are large walls of solid earth. Some grass can be noticed high above, on top of these walls, but nothing else has grown out the sides of it other than a few stray roots. The ground is covered with small pebbles and rocks, mixed evenly across the soil. A small stream may have flowed through here long ago. The dale is also very damp, probably due to all of the shade caused by the surrounding walls of earth.
98042: The dale stretches across from wall to wall by a good twenty feet, one would guess. The walls on both the west and east side are solid earth, but a few stray roots have emerged from them. Along the top of the ledges, tall grass can be noticed, with each blade dancing back and forth. The dale becomes more narrow to the north, and seems to become wider as it continues south from here. The soil along the ground is damp, probably from all the shade.
98043: The dale is very narrow here, ranging between ten to twelve feet across. It becomes even more narrow to the north, but expands in width to the south. It is very damp here, due to the high walls of earth blocking sunlight on both the western and eastern side. It would appear that this used to be some kind of a channel or a small stream that flowed through here, because the ground is evenly worn. High above the walls, a grassy ledge is noticeable, and it looks as though some tall lengths of grass sway in formation there.
98046: Long blades of green grass consume the meadow here. Some tall weeds are seen scattered across the meadow, surpassing even the tallest blades of grass. There are many stones spread out among the meadow as well, some being more noticeable than others. The meadow appears to expand to the west and to the north, while a small pond is clearly noticeable to the south. Though this part of the meadow is mostly flat, it appears to end abruptly to the east, where there is a drop down to what seems like a small valley or dale below.
98047: A sparrow is flapping around on the ground.

The grasses grow here without trouble it would appear. Some stalks have reached nearly the height of a full-grown man, but numerous brown stalks also litter the ground. Perhaps after certain seasons they wither, and then begin to grow again after.
98048: The fields part here, revealing a clearing covered with dust. The reddish hue of the dirt means that the soil must contain some red clay. The clay might not provide ample nutrients, since there are only a few withered weeds at this clearing. A few cracks can be noticed within the ground also, probably due to lack of water. The fields which surround the clearing appear to be more fertile and green.
98049: A sturdy pier stands in the river.

Oak and elm trees inhabit this part of the forest, and a thick carpet of fallen leaves from autumns past covers the ground. Dense groups of hawthorn bushes grow along the riverside, the river to the south and to the west provides a ample supply of water the plants need to flourish. There is a sturdy pier on the river facing towards the west. A thick rope is running across the water towards the other side of the river.
98050:
Some pine nuts lie scattered upon the ground.
A woodpecker is here, tapping on a tree.
A boar cub is playing here, and exploring the wide world.
A swift and agile forest cat moves silently through the vegetation.
A boar cub is playing here, and exploring the wide world.

A pine tree, nearly five feet in diameter, is blocking the path to the north. The height of this tree appears impossible to estimate, as it seems to nearly touch the sky. Streaks of sap along the trunk of the pine tree show that while it has stood here for a long time, it is still full of life.
98051: On a Bough of a Pine Tree

A squirrel scampers around here, looking for nuts from the trees.
A squirrel scampers around here, looking for nuts from the trees.

The branch of this pine tree is large enough to support the weight of several men, but the ends of the limb look too precarious to dare. A number of skitters and scuttles suggest that some woodland creatures call this lofty place home.
98052: A fallow deer is grazing peacefully here.

The ground is very flat across the plain here, with few plants other than the ubiquitous grass. Even though the plains are completely covered with it, it is quite short since the trees to the west seem to absorb most of the moisture. Small purple wildflowers can also be seen jutting out of some patches of grass.
98053: This area is rife with thick stalks of grass and large weeds. The soil here must contain an abundance of nutrients, while the plains south of here look very flat and barren. The minute slivers of rotting wood that are on the ground here may have something to do with the robust plant life.
98054: In the southern half of the plain stands a large boulder. Surrounding this boulder are many stones of similar texture, but they range differently in their sizes. The boulder has a unique shade of grey, almost metallic under certain lighting. Grass has grown around the odd boulder, being very thick near the soil, but as it reaches upward it begins to slump. The wide plain stretches to the east from the boulder.
98055: The grass is very long and full in the meadow. Most of the grass is a colour of green, but a few dead blades of grass remain a light shade of brown and appear very crisp. A fading brushwood can clearly be seen to the west. Some of the debris from the brushwood has made its way here to the meadow, swept along by the wind.
98056:
A blooming water-lily floats on the surface of the water.
A green frog is here, hopping around.
A red-breasted mallard swims about, periodically upending to look for food.

An oval-shaped pond lies in the middle of the meadow, though along the western side of it is the slope of a plateau. Along the northern half of the pond stand truly long blades of grass, weeds and other vegetation that have grown out from the water. Though most of these plants within the pond are green, the lower portions of their stems are brown where they have idled in the water for too long. Small pebbles sit beneath the water, adding more colour to the pond.
98057: Prickly, white-stemmed plants, with blue flower heads grow in abundance.

From this point in the grassy meadow, an oval shaped pond is in sight to the far south. Grass of varying textures and sizes covers the meadow together with a few weeds. Small thistle bushes sit widely apart from one another, nestled in among the longer blades of grass. The meadow continues to expand to the east and south.
98058: Thorny weeds and wide brambles are vigorously prospering amidst a dense blanket of heather shrubs. The ground is pretty uneven with sudden holes concealed under the heather plants, and large, white rocks rest on a herbal pedestal. The sounds of many tiny animals can be heard nearly all the time, busily scurrying around.
98059: A sprawling green bush of stinging nettle grows here.

Dense and crowded, a sheer endless number of rhododendrons populates the plains. Green, short grass filled with dandelions forms a dense underbrush together with on the first glance inseparable heather, making travelling quite hard with only a few paths in it. Rarely, a short, narrow pine juts out of the wilderness, the lower parts of it concealed by the rhododendrons.
98060:
A sprawling green bush of stinging nettle grows here.
A small rabbit glares angrily at you.

A deep chasm cleaves this plain in two to the east. Like a deep wound, it extends from the far north to the south. The plain grass covered with thin grass abruptly ends and vanishes into the clammy and cold depth. It seems possible but dangerous to climb down with the help of some protrusions, cracks and some thin plants, which have been able to find some firm spots for their roots in the steep and moist walls. The far side of this chasm seems to offer some more foothold for growing things, since it is covered with loose tendrils and maybe even the occasional wild cherry tree or young birch.
98061: The craggy ground, uneven and covered with rocks of all shapes and some twisted bushes, makes this plain impossible to ride on. Even some cracks run through this plain, and many of them are only partly filled with earth. Grass and some trees grow out of these cracks, and some dirty puddles of mud have formed all around. Whether this ragged area has something to do with the deep chasm to the east or not can not be said for sure, yet it is quite likely. It seems as if many decades or even centuries ago a strong earthquake had ripped this plain in two. In the northern parts, more and more trees take root in the soil and grow high above the grassland.
98062: A Protrusion in the Chasms Wall

A rocky protrusion has formed on the walls of the chasm, big enough to stand or rest on with a small group, yet it is very uncomfortable. A few smaller bushes grow on the edges, and some grass grows in the cracks of the wall. Every part of the rock and bushes is damp, and small fungi grow all around. It seems to be quite easy to climb down into the deep and dark chasm, but only a very skilled climber would be able to find a way up without breaking his neck when trying.
98063: The walls rise so high that only a small portion of the sky remains to be seen. While some parts of the walls seem to offer some hold to plants and even smaller trees, other parts are blank and steep, and not even a crack can be spotted. The bottom of this chasm is moist, and large sections have been filled with dirty water which stinks of decay and old mud. Some patches of black grass grow here, and from the tenacious, black mud, a few broken bones of animals and travellers, which have been so unlucky to slide into the chasm, stick out.
98064: The Bottom of a Dark Chasm

A mass of dark green leaves clings to a wall.
A skeleton of some humanoid lies in the dust.
A large and twisted beast lurks in the rotten pool.

Being this deep in the earth, this place seems more like a cave than a chasm. Down here, it is dark and damp, and only a small glimpse of the sky can be seen high above. A pool of dark, rotting water has formed underneath the northern walls. The few plants and bushes that grow down here are blackened and so twisted that it is not possible to tell from what kind their seeds have originated. The only sign of rich vegetation is a mass of tendrils that hangs down the eastern wall. In the dark mud, some marks have been left, running towards the silent surface of the pool.
98065:
A fierce bat is here, lusting for your blood.
A fierce bat is here, lusting for your blood.
A bloodthirsty bat is sleeping here.
A bloodthirsty bat is sleeping here.
A large bat is here, hanging in the darkness.
A bloodthirsty bat is sleeping here.
A large bat is here, hanging in the darkness.

The narrow walls of this cave are covered with white droppings. On the floor, a thick carpet of these droppings combined with countless bones of mice or similar creatures and deceased bats has formed. Everything on the floor seems to be wet from trickling water. Many cracks can be seen in the high ceiling.
98066: An orchid of light violet petals blossoms nearby.

On this large meadow, many clusters of wild flowers can be seen. All around, patches of them grow in all colours and sizes. Deep in the grass and the clusters, rustling of vermin or similar beasts can be heard, and a faint humming hints at all kinds of insects. Some clusters have had their time of prospering in this season, while other plants have not yet matured and are still waiting for their time. To the east, the meadows suddenly end. A deep abyss stretches from the north to the south and it is not possible to see its bottom.
98067: Hazel shrubs are rather common here, spread over the bed of grass and only rarely clustered, yet numerous. They grow more densely in the southern part of these plains where the ground seems to be wetter, and the grass even greener. Numerous obvious tracks of small animals can be noticed especially in the close vicinity of the hazel shrubs.
98068: A cluster of dark green, feathery fronds flourishes in the shade.

Bubbling out of the ground, water flows out of many tiny and a few major springs, joining up to a small stream and watering the surrounding muddy plains. Grass grows high and wildly in the proximity, and hop and cattail sprawls untamedly near the springs. Fungi, moss and a few solitary overhanging weeding willows round up the impression of a very lively vegetation.
98069: A sharp-eyed hawk is here stalking some prey.

A tiny stream meanders through the meadows here, slowly flowing in a more or less curvy way from the north and then bending westwards. A few distant trees are scattered over the plains, looming out of the high-growing golden grass that populates it. A few clusters of poppies add strong red dots to the colour of the plains when blossoming.
98070:
A cluster of dark green, feathery fronds flourishes in the shade.
A squirrel scampers around here, looking for nuts from the trees.
A bear is here, covered with coarse black fur.

Many old birches grown high in the sky, their leaves and branches filter the light of sun, moon and stars. All around, there can be seen the white and thick stems like thousands of vertical lines. The floor is covered with soft grass and thick moss. The lack of noise makes this a very quiet part of the forest.
98080:
A low and wide-spread tree grows here.
On the tree's branches, there are three juicy plums.

While only sparse trees cover this plain, many bushes of all kinds seem to prosper all around. They are not dense enough to hinder any movement or sight and grow here in a wide variety. Some have long and thin leaves, while others seem quite broad and their leaves are from a more blue than yellow shade of green, or their stems seem to be as thick as smaller trees. In between these bushes, low grass covers the ground in which animals have left many paths, leading from or towards the forest to the west and the north.
98081: A round tangle with waxy leaves and white berries grows on a branch nearby.

An ancient oak stands here all alone near a deep chasm. Only soft grass covers the plain, and the next bush or tree can only be seen in quite a distance from the enormous tree in the centre. Its old, broad branches cast a huge shadow and loom over the abyss to the west. Under it, many mounds dug by moles can be seen. Its crown looks as if only the strongest of storms were able to move it and to force it to move out of the position it is used to.
98082: A black crow flies low to the ground here, looking for carrion to eat.

Half a dozen poles have been set firmly into the earth. They are all covered with old and dried blood. The poles now have a brownish, encrusted surface. The grass around this spot is dark and blackened in a wide radius. Not much damage has been caused to the formerly thick grass and the bushes around, it may have been a bit trampled, but not enough to explain this dying area. To the west, a deep chasm blocks the way in this direction. Many decades ago, a very heavy earthquake seems to have torn this plain literally asunder.
98083: A Huge Boulder in the Plains
An orchid of light violet petals blossoms nearby.

What brought this huge boulder here cannot be said. It lies within a low meadow, and all around, herbs and some wild flowers grow. To the west, a deep abyss formed a long time ago, and the plain suddenly vanishes into the darkness. Apart from the boulder, only a few bushes arise above the grass and the flowers.
98084: The corpse of a boar is lying here.

The intense fragrance of herbs growing wildly in the plains fills the air, adding a fresh and spicy note to it. Only rarely, grass manages to grow between the spices, being nearly completely crowded out by them. The ground looks rather rich of humus, being able to save water over a long time, feeding the plants plentifully even in drier times.
98085: A huge, black wolf is here, ready to devour.

On a gold-filled and green meadow, low-hanging and cantilevered weeping willows stand far from each other, giving anything hiding under them rather good cover from eyesight. The ground is smooth and flat with occasional dents and looks as if it stretched for miles. Rather often, noise can be heard in the grass, indicating a lot of busy animals hiding in it.
98086: Embedded and sheltered by seemingly endless golden and yellow grass, manifold flowers prosper among it. During their bloom, the area is coloured with blossoms in all colours of the rainbow, changing its face every day. Rarely, a solitary tree can be seen, its root partially hidden behind the plants. Occasionally, the wind carries the sound of flowing water with it from the west.
98087:
A brown fox is here, looking for some rabbits to chew up.
A cute rabbit is here.

Poppies and cornflowers are widespread among fields of golden and green grass, painting the area in lucent red and bright blue during most times of the year. In some places the flowers grow so dense that it seems impossible to distinguish them from others. The ground which is only barely discernable under the vegetation is reddish-brown, containing clumps of clay.
98088: Short and low grass and hard, sturdy weeds grow here in thick, interwoven clusters. While occasionally a bush grows here and there breaking up the dense vegetation, the stony, dark soil is clearly visible at other places. Grey boulders and smaller stones rest among the grass, partially protected against the common wind.
98089: The long blades of grass from the meadow to the west become quite shorter in length here as the plain stretches eastward. The wide plain grows many weeds, all scattered around in small bundles. The grass is very coarse and it is not covering the ground in some areas. There are several patches of dirt visible around the plain.
98090: The open plain is very bare with little to notice other than the fine growing grass. The grass is very thin, and looks quite refined. The plain continues to the north while to the west some water is visible. Dry patches of soil begin at the edge of the grass to the south, where it appears to be even more desolate.
98091: A beautiful and docile horse is standing here.

The bare plain is covered with small patches of coarse grass and some weeds that are very tall and of a bright green colour. The patches of grass are contrastingly dark in colour, and also add a touch of brown to the vegetation. The ground appears rough where it is bare of grass, giving the plain a very desolate look; there are some dirt plots in the area that the weeds have not conquered yet.
98092: The low country around here is all dry. Small hummocks of dried grass colour the landscape with their variety of hues. Between all those hummocks some sand can be noticed, ready to consume all moisture that any possible rain might give. The grains of sand appear to be very fine and evenly spread out. Some deadwood breaks through the tussocks here.
98093: Rocks are spread out along the plain in various sizes and colours. There are some patches of rough-looking grass that are filled with overgrown weeds as they battle for dominance over the plain. A few tiny pebbles lie among the dirt in places where the grass has not grown for awhile.
98094: A black crow flies low to the ground here, looking for carrion to eat.

Countless boulders are strewn across the plain. Not very many blades of grass are visible, only some rough-looking weeds stand tall. There are several tiny stones mixed into the large areas of bare dirt. The stones are all dark-looking and blend in well with the soil. To the west, a lot more vegetation is distinguishable in various shades of green.
98095: The plains stretch from here, showing an assortment of grasses, wildflowers, and small bushes of many different colours. A large stone stands almost in the centre of the plain, light grey in colour, with a rough texture to it. Several branches, all being very thin and splintered, are scattered around along the ground.
98096: A colourful butterfly is fluttering around here.

The grass has grown quite fine here, bright green in colour and very thick in appearance. The grass ends abruptly to the south, where there is a long drop down to an old streambed below. The stump of an old tree stands firmly in the earth still, with a few flowers growing out from around it. The plains appear to expand to the east, and the ledge continues to the west.
98097: A sparrow is flapping around on the ground.

The rolling country here is covered by a thick grassbed. Some small herbs can be found growing amongst the regular vegetation of these grassy plains. A weak maze of animal trails can be seen in the grass. The ground becomes bare of grass, with only a few weeds noticeable, towards the western side of the plain.
98098: The broken country here is growing weak and dry grass, which is both brown and green in colour. Occasional stumps of deadwood are scattered around, half-rotten and half-buried into the ground. A lonely skeletal form of a long dead bovine is lying here, almost covered by a hummock of exceptionally strong grass.
98099: Various stumps and boles of long dead trees are lying around here. On a few of the stumps some scar-like markings can be seen, probably cut by a crude hatchet or axe. Now some thick and dry brushwood dominates this area, covering everything and choking back the trees' every attempt to regain their former glory.
98100: The ground here is barren and dark, being coloured by shades of black and brown. Most of the ground is dry, so dry it appears like concrete and is filled with small hollows and cracks. Small patches of dry grass and various half-dead plants are scattered among the ground.
98101: At the Edge of a Narrow Dale

A rabbit is here eyeing your presence warily.
A horse is standing here, ridden by you.

Several weeds have sprouted from beneath the ground here, mixed in among long blades of grass. The grass appears to be very crisp and dried. There are some flowers growing along the western edge of the field, where a narrow dale courses through the landscape. It looks like a dried-up streambed. The furrows in the ground suggest that the water once flowed in from the east, perhaps creating a small waterfall at this point.
98102: A brown fox is here, looking for some rabbits to chew up.

The field grows long blades of grass spreading out evenly across the ground. Between them are patches of dried and bare ground. The grassy ledge, which is almost unnoticeable until it is too late, travels along the western side of the field, completely covered by tall lengths of grass and weeds. There are a few stones littered about the field as well.
98103: A small evergreen plant grows here, its woody stems reaching two feet.

The grass is fine here, bright green in colour, with only a few weeds noticeable between the slender blades. Four trees have also grown here, spreading out several feet from one another, all having long and thin branches. The leaves on these trees are small, green, and oval in shape. The bark upon the trees appears to be very smooth and light brown in colour. The grass gets taller as it expands to the east, where there is also a small mound noticeable in the distance.
98104: The grassland here seems to continue to the south, though to the west, a few trees stand barely discernible. The soil is broken up, with crisp blades of grass growing in large clumps all over. Small mounds are rising out of the earth, giving this landscape a distinct appearance.
98105: The grassy meadow continues in several directions here; north, west and south. To the east, there is a drop down to the ground below, to the bottom of a valley or a small dale that exists there. The grass is very soft and bright-coloured green at the edge of the drop, indicating that the soil must be very fertile there. Occasional weeds can be noticed throughout the meadow, but all of them are of the same kind, with spear-shaped leaves and dark green colour.
98106: The meadow here consists of mainly bright green grass that appears very young and healthy. On the western side of the meadow, there are a few weeds, and the grass is much thicker and more dried. The grassy meadow suddenly ends on the eastern side, where there is a long drop to the dale below. Tall grass has grown on the ledge, almost hiding it from view.
98107: The meadow is covered by soft grass that is the colour of bright green. The soil must be very fertile here, as the grass appears to be so healthy. To the east, the meadow suddenly ends, and a grassy ledge can be noticed bordering a narrow dale. Along the ledge, some of the bare earth is revealed, and the grass there grows wild and long compared to the grass of the delicate meadow.
98108: Tall but strong grass dominates this very flat field. This goes to show the extreme lushness of the ground, though it is choking back every other possible plant form which might sprout here. Not even a bush or a small tree breaks the monotony of this grassland.
98109: The ground is covered by a thick bed of grass, with very few noticeable weeds. To the east the grass becomes longer, though the growth is not as thick as it is here. Some small pebbles are also noticeable along the east side of this grassy area. This appears to be a ledge, since to the west and south there is a great distance down to the ground below.
98110: A large eagle soars above you.

Tall yet dry grass dominates the area here. Though suffering from aridity, the grass still shows the fertility of the ground. Some weak trails can be spotted in the thick carpet, revealing the existence of animal life in these fields. The grass meets a dale running through the lands in the south, where the roof of a wooden structure can be noticed below.
98111: The channel is completely dry, filled by tiny grains of sand and small pebbles. It looks as though water had at one time flowed southwest from here, where the sand slowly begins to fade and small spots of grass can be noticed. On one side of the dried-up channel stands a tall tree, coated by a grey-coloured bark. A few flowers have sprouted up from the earth on both sides of the sandy bed together with several stones. A large hill stands to the east, but due to the erosion over the years, it is impossible to reach it from this side.
98112: The barren, sandy landscape here is dominated by a dried, meandering channel, which still bears visible marks of once flowing water. Pebbles along the dry valley are round, as the once gushing water has curved the edges from all stones. Small bushes have surrounded the channel and dried there in the past, leaving only empty skeletal branches behind. The channel continues to both the north and the south.
98114: A few leafless trees are scattered around. Their naked branches hang in the moist air, weighed down by the silence. There is little evidence of wildlife on the ground, but now and again you hear the sounds made by some creatures in the trees. The ground begins to slope down to the east, where you catch the sound of water trickling down the side of the valley.
98115:
A huge, venomous spider is here.
A huge, venomous spider is here.

Here barren trees stand quietly, isolated in pools of mist. The ground is soft, sticky in places, with soil that seems barely able to sustain life. The damp air is still and smells musty and unhealthy. The silence is only broken by the odd crack of a decaying branch. The surface under foot deteriorates preventing any further progress to the south and west.
98116:
Von (twitter), wielding an ornate, steel-shafted warhammer, is standing here.
Drazud (freshmeat), wielding a great warsword, is standing here.

There is a dense forest of birches, elms, and oaks all around. The tops of the trees are not visible due to the thick canopy of leaves and branches above. The canopy is so thick that the rays from the sun cannot reach the undergrowth of this forest.
98117: The leafless trees cling to the sides of the valley that slopes sharply down to the northeast. The air smells of damp or rotting wood. The interconnection of the tree roots makes it impossible to ride here. From the vantage point of a raised rocky outcrop one can make out the glitter of the great river Anduin in the distance.
98118: The ground climbs steeply to the south. The soil is soft and there is much evidence of mudslides. Many trees have failed in their battle to grow on these slopes. The few trees that survived sport moss-covered roots and have beards of vegetation hanging from their branches. The noise of a river is carried from the north on a breeze.
98119: Small Grove of Trees by the Riverbank
Some ugly blow-flies are buzzing around here.

Only medium and small trees grow in this section of the forest. The logs and cracked stumps here must belong to larger trees which eventually failed to maintain a hold of the root-filled earth. The soil seems rich in nutrients brought downstream by the river, and the ground has become very wet.
98120: Dense Forest near a River Bend

A forest spider is here crawling around.
A woodpecker is here, tapping on a tree.

The Anduin river to the east has separated this forest of oaks and pine trees from the wide grasslands that spread out across the other side. The dense and leafy canopy created by the criss-crossing tree branches looks as if it would block out any form of outside light. The river appears to be flowing to the south.
98121:
The ferry is here, tied to a pier.
There are two light boats of reeds here.
A sturdy pier stands in the river.

A few huge oaks and large sycamores are all that reside in this area of the forest. The closer to the river, the more lush the vegetation becomes, until some of it becomes submerged, yet thriving still. The river flows strongly on from the north to the east past the riverbank. A thick rope is running across the water towards the other side of the river.
98122: The cloudy waters continue to move downstream. A variety of small pebbles, dead leaves, and broken twigs are being washed along in the moving current. Their turbulent motion in the water serves as a reminder of the forces of nature. The river seems to be gradually bending eastwards.
98123:
Von (twitter), wielding an ornate, steel-shafted warhammer, is standing here.
Drazud (freshmeat), wielding a great warsword, is standing here.
Lhurank (brenny), wielding a narrow runed awlpike, is standing here.

The river continues to flow here, with some leafy trees on both banks. These trees are bent slightly towards the water, in order to get a better amount of sunlight. It is almost as though they were bowing to any travellers who make their way down the river.
98124: Fast Moving Bend in the Anduin

Small rocks tumble down the fast-flowing river that cuts through the bend here. The jagged edges of the rocks are slowly becoming smooth, as they collide with other rocks in the deep river. Perhaps these rocks are clastic sediment that has broken away from the mountains far to the west. The river bends to the east.
98125:
A bass swims here.
Von (twitter), wielding an ornate, steel-shafted warhammer, is standing here.
Drazud (freshmeat), wielding a great warsword, is standing here.
Klaees (thedon), wielding a great warsword, is standing here.
Lhurank (brenny), wielding a narrow runed awlpike, is standing here.

This section of the Anduin River narrows as it goes from the north to the south. On both sides of the river, ancient forests reside, uncaring of the war that consumes Middle-earth. The current of the river is slow, but it is powerful and constant.
98126:
A trout swims here.
Von (twitter), wielding an ornate, steel-shafted warhammer, is standing here.
Drazud (freshmeat), wielding a great warsword, is standing here.
Lhurank (brenny), wielding a narrow runed awlpike, is standing here.

The current of the Anduin does not stop or falter along its ongoing course to the southeast. A light forest of oaks and elms blocks all view to the north, while to the east there is a muddy riverbank and an expanse of plains. The water continues to rush onwards, carrying an occasional piece of wood or debris along with it as it flows to the south.
98128:
A bass swims here.
A trout swims here.

The current changes its direction to head south from here. Leaves from all kinds of trees can be seen tumbling in the water. There are also the submerged husks of uprooted trees residing on the bottom of the river, waiting to surprise any traveller on the water with an errant branch.
98154: High, tree-like bushes and a few isolated trees dominate the vegetation, and hawthorn stands out against a green background in some places. Forming a dense undergrowth interlocked in the bushes, ling patches cover the brown soil rich in humus, shielding it against erosion from rainfall and wind which both seem to be common here.
98155: Nothing but thick grass covers the windy landscape. The grass is not very high, making hiding rather hard, and since it is sharp, it also makes travelling unpleasant in this area. It looks as if wildlife mostly consisted of birds and rodents, judging from the sounds that can be heard occasionally. Here and there, smooth dunes rise from the ground.
98156: A huge, black wolf is here, ready to devour.

The high grass here is trampled down by many passing animals, perhaps seeking food and water, forming a small, vaguely recognisable path. The common presence of small animals has left its marks, as many remains can be discerned. A tiny bit of fur or a strand of hair hanging on a thorny bush, or piles of dried excrements near the path can be noticed on a second glance.
98157: A trained horse (Rood) is standing here, ridden by you.

A noticeable natural track that has developed from animals wandering the same way for years is winding through lush grass. A few bushes covered with dusty red berries line up the borders of the path, while scattered among the plains, more bushes are visible. In the south-western part of the area, the path widens and leads to a bubbling spring.
98158: The air is filled with soothing scents of herbs and plants that are spread throughout the fields. Wherever no herb grows, golden grass has claimed its share of the ground. Veins of clay can be noticed on the earth, being hardened and cracked and forming a solid layer over the more fertile bed. Although much of the rain drains off over the surface, it still seems to be sufficient to feed the well-adjusted vegetation.
98159: The ground here serves as a home for plants of a great variety in height and shape. The dominating golden grass shifts in colour from its natural royal tone over yellow to grey, and in some smaller areas, it is even spotted with tender purple traces. Other plants are growing allotted among the grass like small colourful dots.
98160: Row upon row of tall and proud golden hay stands in the field. In this field, moisture seems to be available in abundance, allowing the hay to grow at its peaks to the size of a small man. Activity of busy insects is heard through the stems, and from time to time their noise becomes loud and angry.
98161: A brown fox is here, looking for some rabbits to chew up.

Overlapping turfs of golden hay are covering the fat and rich earth, mostly low and wide. A few patches of grass among them reach out for the sky, growing to the height of a man's waist with bulbous heads swaying in occasional breezes. Coming from the east, a fragrance of wood and resin fills the air, although it seems to be quite a distance away.
98162: A huge, black wolf is here, ready to devour.

The wind-beaten land is scarcely covered with grass. The turfs seem to be clustered, and dirt and gravel cover the ground between the coasts of grass. Where the wind has been able to work freely, on small rises and inclines, grey rocks sticking out from beneath the soil have been left naked to the elements.
98163: A beautiful and docile horse is standing here.

Small bunches of dried grass colour this otherwise pebbly and gravelled area of the plain. The dullness of the surroundings forces even the most persistent life forms to seek cover and rest from other places, though by the traces on the ground they appear to at least travel through.
98164: The scenery here is flat, slightly rising towards the east. The ground is barren and only some persistent grass manages to find its living here. Where the grass grows weak, a rocky ground peeks from below. Some bare land can be spotted around as well, eroded by heavy rains in the past. The thin, struggling grass appears to be growing stronger and taller to the south.
98165:
A wolf cub happily plays here.
A wolf cub happily plays here.
A wolf cub happily plays here.
An orkish wolf-rider is here, warily looking at his surroundings.
A large brown wolf stands here, its teeth partly bared.

The cave is large, yet not very high. The floor is covered with dry soil and near the rear end, it is padded with straw. A sharp smell hangs in the air. Trampled grass still grows near its entrance, and bones of animals lie here and there on the ground. Some of them are picked dry, others still have remains of rotting meat on them.
98166: It looks as if lots of animals passed here on usual basis, travelling from the north-east to the south-west, and vice versa. The path is partly hidden among the high grass surrounding it, but once found, its course is clearly visible. Along it, the grass is trampled down, the earth is partially bare where too many animals have wandered, and several little bushes are broken. Many animal tracks can clearly be seen on the ground even by the most unskilled.
98167:
A sharp-eyed hawk is here stalking some prey.
A brown fox is here, looking for some rabbits to chew up.

Tall grass and wild cereals cover the ground, bending and rustling under gusts of wind. Here and there, flowers protrude from the grass, sparkling when lit by the sun. Noises of rodents darting and cheeping around can be heard rather often, and clear imprints on the dark, soft soil indicate that game seems to be common here.
98171: A black crow flies low to the ground here, looking for carrion to eat.

This deep, dry basin seems completely lifeless. The ground is dry and extremely hard-surfaced, coloured with shades of black and brown. The brinks of this bowl do not rise very steeply. Along the northern edge of the old pool huge logs and small boulders can be noticed, perhaps the remains of an ancient pier.
98172: Short, stunted grass covers this area into austere embrace. Even the land is arid and barren, with its grass growing dark green. Some holes of various small rodents can be seen all around the landscape, and almost non-existing trails connect the burrows to each other. There are some old fences piled up along the northeast side of the plain, and some large boulders stand in the southeastern parts.
98173: The slightly rolling country here is filled with stunted hummocks and tussocks. Some brushwood, mainly heather and some various herbs grow here. The ground appears pretty dry, while the growth is strong and stable. A couple of large rocks and circular-shaped stones are scattered around on the ground. To the south, a slight rise in the earth can be noticed.
98174:
A cluster of white star-shaped forget-me-nots flourish here in reminiscence.
A cluster of white star-shaped forget-me-nots flourish here in reminiscence.

In the centre of the plains is a large knoll, emerged slightly from the earth. Grass has fully covered the knoll, along with some white flowers that have grown upon it. There are large stones at the southern end, which were probably some type of a marker long ago, but have since crumbled and toppled over into a large pile of debris. Long-stemmed wildflowers and tall blades of grass cover the largest portion of debris, making it almost unnoticeable.
98190: A grey wolf is here, salivating profusely.

The flat field here consists of extremely dry ground. Some remains of fences built long ago, made of some huge, dry logs, can still be seen around. Now their skeletal forms are the sole guard of this long abandoned area. Some half-buried bones are the only other reference to what this land might have formerly been used for.
98191: A large beautiful rose bush is blooming here.

The slightly rolling country has suffered badly from continuous erosion, caused by aridity, heat and time. The pebbly and sandy ground here grows only some weak grass but incredibly lush bushes, which reveal some of the landscapes former fertility. Some ancient formations of stone can be seen around, half buried into the sand and bush growth.
98192:
A large thorny branched shrub is growing here.
On the shrub, there are two piles of blackberries.

The landscape here is barren, growing weak grass and various thorny bushes. The ground is mostly composed of sand and pebble instead of soil. Some man-sized boulders are lying here, half buried in the sand, and branches of thorny growth are rising out from their sides. To the west, the scenery rises slightly while it becomes more rocky.
98193: A small cliff rises from the ground here, covered by boulders of various sizes. The bald ledge points northwards, offering no base for any growth. Chutes of esker lead in all other directions. In the middle of the cliff there seems to be a boulder-covered crevice.
98194:
A small oaken table has been set here.
On the table, there is a bloody piece of meat.
A sleuthing orc, wielding a dagger, is sleeping here.

This part of the cavern is filled with smoke and other strong aromas floating in the air. The stone floor is covered with a thick and soft carpet, which is dirtied by all possible blemishes. Pieces of crude furniture, some wrecked and some undamaged, share the floor space in disarray. Above a fireplace in the corner, the cavern ceiling seems to disappear out of sight.
98195: This dark cavern opens as wide as high, enclosing all of the surroundings to deep shadows. The basement rock along the ground is flooded with all sorts of rubbish and food leftovers, which could be fresh marks of the inhabitants. Some light can be seen further into the darkness. A small stream of water flows onwards along the ground, only to disappear into a small hole.
98196: The threshold is long, though narrow, and leading toward a building that lies to the north, with an oaken door marking its entrance. Thick, dark wood was used to create the threshold, and a glossy finish was placed on it. The ceiling was created with the same kind of wood, but at the southern end of it, there is a red banner that dangles down. The ground is bare of any debris, materials, or even grass, with only dry earth to walk over. The threshold is large enough so that it appears to block any sunlight or rough weather from entering.
98197: This shelter was obviously reconstructed over time from its original build, as some of the wood used for the walls is new compared to the rest. It has a glossy coating upon it, while the old portions appear to have started to splinter due to age. The western part of the ceiling is solid wood as well, while the rest is covered with a thick tarp along one side of the shelter. Large wooden beams with some engravings support the solid part of the roof, but the other side lacks them. Especially the north-eastern portion of the roof looks extremely aged and buckled. Large sheets of wood cover the floor, with an old rug lying upon them.
98198: This roof covers a very old structure of some kind, even though the boards are quite decayed and splintered in several different places. On the southeastern side of the roof here, a dark-coloured tarp can be noticed, probably tied there to cover a gaping hole. The roof steeply slants up to the west, while the northern part seems easier to reach. Looking down from the roof, a rocky dale runs to the south from this building.
98199: The boards used for the roof here are very old, cracked in several places, and already well into a decaying state. The roof rises up on a high slant to the west, and would be too steep to climb to the other side. The boards along the upper portion of that slant are even more decayed than those right here. The roof offers a view of the surrounding dale but there is no visibility to the fields above. A ladder is set against the northern wall of the dale, leading upwards to a grassy ledge.
98212: A small depression opens here in the middle of the pebbly fields. Southwards, a steep slope has formed a natural shelter against the elements. A small trickle of water can be found flowing in from the east and into the depression, only to disappear below one large boulder that is standing there alone.
98213: A clear spring babbles as cool water trickles out of the ground.

The growth of tall grass dominates the flat ground here. A small spring gushes here, forming a small stream which then flows rapidly to the west, giving some much needed moisture to all vegetation. Some blooming plants colour the land which surrounds the tiny source of the brook. This paradisiacal oasis does not seem to have any larger plants though.
98214: A short but strong grassbed covers the ground here. The surroundings are painted in various shades of green. A constant wind may have forced most of the stalks of grass to bend low in this open area. Some small plants have grown at random spots here and there, wherever they could manage to find shelter against the weather.
98215: Short, strong grass covers the ground here. Some ancient stumps and boles have broken through the grassbed, revealing the remains of some destroyed forest. A single tree is still remaining, raising its naked trunk up to the heights. It may have stood here branchless and leafless for ages, but still offers some shelter to various small animals such as birds and insects.
98216: Thin bushes rise from the rocky soil here, covering almost all of the ground with their growth. More than half of the vegetation is dried and extremely close to death. The rest of the bushes still try to grow some weak leaves, which are dehydrated by aridity and sunshine. A few stones are scattered here along the ground, smashed into the dry earth.
98217: Some stunted and slow-growing bushes rule the landscape here. Weak grass and some especially strong plants grow below the bushes. The undergrowth is formed mostly of different waxy-leafed herbs, which can accept this barren plain as their substrate.
98218: Small bushes have spread their growth all around this area, leaving all of the grass as a weak minority which is forced to fight for its existence. The alteration of different ground types is clearly visible here, when the lush steppes, the arid field and the scrubby plains meet. Only a few weeds appear to stand out, mainly due to their dark colour.
98219: A large thorny branched shrub is growing here.

Various bushes grow here, rising knee-high and covering the dry ground below them. The brush has long and slender branches, extending out from the earth. A few thorns which seem to be rather sharp and very short in length can be noticed upon these branches.
98220: Bushes and shrubs rule the ground, spreading more in width than in height, adapting in shape and colour to the underlying earth. A few turfs of golden grass sway by their stems, and a scarce supply of herbs stands rebellious against the dominating vegetation, struggling not to get crowded out.
98221: A finch flies low above the ground.

In the air here, there flows a gentle fragrance of wood and resin, generated by low, woody shrubs covering the ground. Where bushes and twigs have lost their grasp on the land, dirt and grass cover the earthy ground, here and there adjourned by clusters of dandelions and moss. Chickweed seems to grow everywhere.
98222: A large beautiful rose bush is blooming here.

Short but wide shrubs nestle to each other, forming a dense, green and brown living carpet which burdens movement. Only at a few spots, the carpet opens for some kind of natural pathways paved with nettles, thistles and other small plants. The fragrance of different herbs can be smelled in the air, mingled with a faint, yet sharp stench.
98223: A mouse sniffs around, searching for a morsel of food.

Thick and strong brush covers the area, growing in all shapes and sizes. Nearly hidden by the brushwood, a soft slope eases down into a vague sink in the land, barely noticeable for an inattentive observer. Many tiny rills and small holes in the surrounding ground yet indicate that the water from rainfalls steadily flows into the dip, eroding the vicinity and slowly but steadily filling it.
98224: A colourful butterfly is fluttering around here.

Shimmering stems of grass growing in colonies spread out all over the dark, earthy ground. A few herbs grow among them, and a bush here and a shrub there are the only things disturbing their dominance. The air is filled with the smell of the grass, making it fresh and spicy.
98226: The field is covered with thin, woody grass. A few flowers manage to survive while being at a permanent strife for survival. Rocks lie here and there on the ground, and close to most of them, bushes and higher grass grow. The soil is hard and poor, and dust can be felt in the air.
98227: The landscape here is dominated by wildly sprawling shrubs and brush. On the wind-beaten ground, various rocks are uncovered, protruding through the thin layer of soil. The air is light, enriched by the spicy smell of the bushes which nearly conceals the elusive scent of herbs and dirt carried along by the wind.
98234: The dry lands are filled with golden grass, grasping through the thin layer of soil on the stony ground with their stems, leaving it cracked. At some places the grass grows to the height of a fully grown man's waist, and yet, at in other places it has lost the battle against the hard ground, leaving it barren and only covered with a few patches of moss.
98235: Among fields of grass in tones of gold and yellow, a tiny hill arises, overlooking the vicinity. Although being only small in size, the hill is still noticeable compared to the flat surrounding ground. Green grass and moss cover it, and a few barren spots can be seen on it. Flowers of all colours grow everywhere, making this a good landmark for a traveller.
98236: The rank ground seems to have hardened over time here. Fragile stems of grass in gold and yellow and cabbages in all tones of brown and green cover it. Gravel, rocks and hard chunks of soil form the surface between the strays of grass. Small patches of moss clutch at the earth, slowly easing the ground again.
98237:
A large thorny branched shrub is growing here.
On the shrub, there are three piles of blackberries.

Clusters of grass silently sway as if troubled by their state, fighting for existence on the meagre, yet wet soil. Thorny weeds, thistles and other haulms fill the large gaps between the grass turfs, seemingly growing out of the grass. Gravel accompanies the lowest straws and cabbages on the ground.
98238: Large patches of golden grass is growing here, now and then being interrupted by solitary and small clusters of trees. The shimmering grass predominates the landscape as the soil seems to be somewhat unyielding, but compared to what can be seen to the south, it would do well for any farmer willing to bestow it.
98239: Tall and proud grass grows here in abundance, dominating the ground and rising to the waist of a man, confident in its becoming. Its edges are pointy, tickling a wanderer with every move, while small plants of many different kinds grow among it. A few rocks lie around, being a disruption of the otherwise perfectly level landscape.
98240: A rabid rabbit is here, frothing at the mouth.

A low ledge cuts through the land. Tall and golden grass grows throughout the area, bathing the surrounding ground in gold and green. Its cause is uncertain, but it has left a glaring scar in the fertile landscape, and grass and small plants can only cover the edge. Rocks and gravel have tumbled down and lie in a stony field to the north below the ledge.
98241: A rocky ledge cuts the flat and even landscape like a scar, separating the lower ground to the north from the higher one to the south of it. High grass grows on the higher side of the ledge and hangs over its sharp edge, smoothening its appearance. Among the grass, many different flowers paint the landscape with their natural, colourful ink.
98270: The soil here has a genuine richness that would make any attempt at farming a success. The grass of these fields, uninhibited by poor soil or lacklustre weather, have covered the entire landscape with their golden threads, growing tall and strong. Among them, other weeds can be spotted only very rarely, and wherever they strive for survival, the grass seems to overwhelm it.
98276: The grass here sparkles with an impressive variety of colours. While only a few fully green straws can be seen, there are all shades and sizes of golden, yellow, brown, grey and orange grass. In the setting sun, this field of colours would have one face, while in the rising sun, an entirely different one would be visible. Downfall is obviously plentiful to feed this variety of plants.
98277:
A brown fox is here, looking for some rabbits to chew up.
A sharp-eyed hawk is here stalking some prey.

To the south, the way is blocked by a wide ledge, crossing through the fields. In the shadows beneath, there it lie rocks and gravel as if hurled from the edge above. Traces of animal activity can be seen all along the wall as this location is perfect for protection from the path of the sun in the south. A few dark spots can be seen along the rock of the ledge.
98278: A finch flies low above the ground.

Golden and green grass covers the rich ground, growing only small in height, yet flowing in every breeze of wind, bowing to it in wandering waves. To the south, a ledge runs through the land, looming up over the flat fields. On top of it, more of the golden grass grows in abundance and high in size, flowing over the ledge. In a small stony circle formed by a few well placed rocks right beneath the ledge, a small pool of water has gathered.
98285:
A sharp-eyed hawk is here stalking some prey.
A huge, black wolf is here, ready to devour.

Small dunes and some bumps cross through this area, mostly in the southern part of it. On the higher parts of the ground, it seems to be drier. Only some golden grass grows there that has partially turned grey and brown. In the lower and wetter areas, the grass grows stronger with a more luscious tone, and large shrubs spread their branches wide and high.
98286: A sharp-eyed hawk is here stalking some prey.

A thin layer of top-soil tries to cover the ground here, but in some places, it has been eroded and reveals a thick layer of granite. Grass can only be seen in a few places among large areas of ling, and a tiny path leads northwards sloping between a few hills. Rocks of all shapes and sizes rest upon the path from their brief fall down the nearby elevations.
98287: A colourful butterfly is fluttering around here.

The flat surface of a steep cliff rises high to the north, looming over the lower, grass-covered ground. Many flowers with a short stem and bulbous, triangular blossom bloom here for most of the year, painting the dull landscape in tones of violet, blue, pink and white. Among them, where the flowers grow densest, there rests an old, mostly weathered stone with inscriptions on it.
98288: An intangible sense of rot and decay hangs here, making this barren land similar to a carrion feeding ground. Even though this place is located near a cliff visible to the south-east, the air still feels stale, and only the sound of a few insects gives the impression as if it were filled with anger. The vegetation of the surrounding land very abruptly ends. Close to the middle of this ground, a few tiny rocky mounds arise.
98289:
A little stone lies on the ground.
A colourful butterfly is fluttering around here.
A rabid rabbit is here, frothing at the mouth.

Due to a caprice of nature, a quartz deposit which normally lies deep under the rich and dark earth has come to the surface, mixing with it and being home to a few plants only. Short and thin grass and some erica patches grow here and there, and in a few places where the sand seems to have mixes less with soil, even a few squat bushes manage to grow, while the majority of the ground is lying idle, although there seems to be sufficient moisture.
98290: The fields come to an abrupt end here, as the plateau is suddenly cut short by a steep cliff to the south. The edge of the cliff is weather-beaten and cracked from years of erosion, and grey lichen and green moss cover a few parts of the scarp. Giant white rocks dot the flowery landscape below as a result of past landslides. The grassy landscape below stretches out as far as the eye can see, and to the south-west, a long ledge can be noticed.
98294:
A bee flies around here, collecting nectar from the flowers.
A bee flies around here, collecting nectar from the flowers.
A sharp-eyed hawk is here stalking some prey.

Up to the height of a large man, dense grass grows here in abundance. Fed by frequent rainfall and the nutrient, dark brown soil below, the grass is strong and sturdy, yielding great cover for all kinds of animals, making travelling in this area rather tiresome. During all seasons except for winter, insects can be seen and heard diligently buzzing around, and tiny beetles crawl on the thick stems.
98295: Protected by a small circle of stones in the surrounding ground, a marshy dip filled with reeds, flowers and fungi can be noticed. Around the dip, the soil seems to be very fertile for a while, as it is covered with long, golden grass and a few, solitary trees.
98296: Some time in the past, a fierce brushfire must have raged here, burning to ash most of the vegetation. Small and coaled trunks, partly uproot, are sad remains of what once were trees. Only a thin layer of moss and grass covers the ground, rejuvenating the partly cracked, partly grey ground, loosening the soil and preparing the rebirth of the flora.
98297: A fierce boar is here, making grunting noises.

The land is covered with woody, low grass and a few tree-like bushes. A few patches of ling grow here and there, and a strong smell, coming from large clusters of oregano, fills the air. The soil is brown and crumbly, and traces of white sand can be noticed here and there among it.
98298: A green hillock almost seems to leap out of the middle of the fallow plains. Although it only has the size of a full-grown oak tree, the existence of the hillock is still remarkable on this otherwise flat landscape. Grass and simbelmyne cover the slopes of the knoll, and broad bushes grow at its foot, concealing the base of the hill with their branches and leaves.
98299: Made uneven over years of exposure to the power of constant winds and rain, the ground here is uneven. Long, grass-covered ridges and small water-filled gullies form the landscape, and heather and sturdy bushes are the dominating plants. Large boulders brought over time from rivers stand like attached sentinels, overlooking the plains.
98300: Fresh grass covers the soil here like a bright, green and brown blanket. The soil is coarse, sticking together as if bound by an unseen glue, making it form large chunks at many places. The peaks of a few large boulders and rocks, remains from ancient times, protrude through it.
98301:
A cluster of white star-shaped forget-me-nots flourish here in reminiscence.
A fierce boar is here, making grunting noises.

On the grassy, flat area, a huge, several hundred years old oak with a wide crown is towering over the plains below. Obviously, in the past, other trees were growing here as well, but now nothing except for a few rotting stumps has remained of them. Wild rose bushes grow in the proximity of the tree, and many flowers bloom on the ground.
98302: A few small birch trees and a couple of oregano plants are all that break through the sea of grey-brown grass that comprises the whole landscape. Small animals, rain and erosion have dug holes in the ground, which are now covered with grass, making travelling quite unpleasant in this area. Small surface irregularities further worsen travel conditions, making riding impossible and giving the grassy sea the appearance of having waves.
98303: A swallow flies high above the ground.

A blood-red streak of clay, nearly a hundred yards long, cuts through this land like a wound on Arda herself. Sun and wind have dried out parts of it, making these spots hard and cracked. Spindly grey-green plants writhe in the wind around the clay gash, while moss partially grows on the clay vein. The land is flat and uniform in all directions, but it seems as if in some distance, the earth became less barren.
98304: Some roots lie here waiting to ensnare weary travellers.

The cave is quite small. It smells of fresh and slightly moist soil. The skeletons of two big animals can be seen; from their appearance, they could have been bears. The bones are covered with notches, caused by swords or similar weapons. Thousands of thin roots hang from the ceiling, and probably belong to the vegetation growing above.
98305: The ground is soft and damp here, covered with a rainbow of various fungi and some shallow grass. In the middle of this area in a shallow dip, a muddy pond has developed from some sort of underground source of water, flowing only a small distance to the southwest where it disappears into the ground. The earth near the basin is marshy, showing obvious tracks of various animals.
98306: Almost resembling a well-disciplined army, squat, widely cantilevered and woody hawthorn bushes grow in well-ordered rows. The earth seems to be a thick layer over a more rocky, solid base, and the tinge of rich soil in the air and the number of shrubs growing suggests that these plains are more than suitable for plant life. The odour of fresh water adds the impression that moisture is in abundance in the area.
98307: Tall grass and young saplings grow indomitably here, giving the area the imression of the wilderness that it is, interrupted by large patches of heather. A few trees grow scattered in the grassland, with a tendency of becoming stronger in numbers and in size, but also changing in kind in the western parts of the plains.
98308:
A tall pine tree grows here.
A small animal, all covered in spines, snuffles amongst the undergrowth.

A dense forest of conifers, like firs or pines, gives shelter from wind and light rain. The grass grows high and mixes with the lower branches. Only the closest or loudest noises can be heard, everything else gets somewhat damped. Low tunnels have been formed in the grass by smaller animals like rabbits, foxes or the thistly hedgehog.
98309: The top of the high oak provides a natural vantage point for observing the surrounding land. The branches of the ancient tree are sturdy enough to support several men at once, and since they diverge in all directions, they form a natural platform. During the seasons from spring to fall, lush leafage hangs from them, providing shadow and an excellent place to hide.
98313: Thick, round bushes cover the fields of hay at the border of a forest. Young trees rise above the bushes here and there, their chewed bark and branches hinting at an abundance of local game. Several animal paths run amidst the bushes, showing an occasional track or a dropping on the hard-packed soil. The twists and bends in the paths are well concealed by the growth, but most of them seem to be leading from the open plains in the east towards the forest in the west.
98314: A skull is here, spiked to the end of a pole.

This deep pit has been dug straight into the ground, and is surrounded from above by some bushes. The walls of the pit are almost vertical and offer no good handholds, making climbing out of the pit quite hard. Sharpened, sturdy sticks have been placed at the bottom of the pit, where they point upwards waiting for some hapless victim to fall on them. The trap is crude, but its efficiency is without question.
98315: A swarm of mosquitoes is here, humming around you.

Ferns and mosses of all kinds grow in the moist soil. The ground in the depression is not as hard as on the fields surrounding it, hinting at the presence of water. The undergrowth is very dense, proving the earth to be very nutritious in addition to being rather moist. The few rocks here are covered in lichen of sickly green colour.
98316: A Spring in the Stony Plains
A clear spring babbles as cool water trickles out of the ground.

Some clear water wells up from a soft, dark mound on the ground, announcing the presence of a spring. It forms a small pool before flowing to the west and being soaked into the sand. Stones in different sizes cover the ground, making it seemingly difficult to tread on, but no other features to hinder travel can be seen in the open landscape. A rise in the plains towards the east is noticeable, as well as soggy plains to the west and the dry field to the north.
98317: Surrounded by similarly open plains, this field of weeds is nothing remarkable. Some small stones lie on the bottom of the occasional depression here, as if they had rolled in from somewhere. The landscape turns slowly barren towards the south, where the hue of the weeds becomes completely brown. The fields in the north seem more fertile.
98318: A Small Rise in the Barren Fields

At this small rise the view over the expanding plains is remarkable. Even though the rise is but a few yards above the normal ground level, the lack of trees and large bushes allows one to see almost a mile in each direction on a clear day. Below the slope the grass stretches endlessly as far as the eye can see, only broken by some bushes appearing in the north.
98319: The ground descends gently to the north, while the bushes appearing here and there become more dense towards the bottom of the slope and finally form an almost impenetrable thicket. The surrounding landscape is dominated by knee-deep hay, especially in the east where no other noticeable features are in sight. A network of vines crawls along the slope, climbing up a bush or a twig wherever it has the chance to do so. Wide leaves of the vines add noticeable greenery to the otherwise dull colour of this terrain.
98320: Light patches of moisture can be seen on the ground at all times, arising from the spongy soil that forms the surface below. The ground is covered with weeds growing completely wild, yet there are some spots where vegetation has not settled in permanently. There, fungus-infested branches and rotting leaves can be seen on the ground, showing how the old makes way for the new in the eternal cycle of seasons.
98321: For no obvious reasons the ground here is dead. As if it had not rained for months, grass looks burnt and worn out. Fine grey dust rises from the ground, covering the leaves of what little vegetation is left around here. The lands surrounding these fields seem to have had more rainfall recently, since lush grasses dominate the landscape farther away.
98322: This area may have been a farmland many years ago, but it seems more likely that some grains of wheat ended up here by chance and grew into a small field. The wheat has grown wild among the local weeds and could not be harvested easily. Still, it supplies the occasional grazing animal with food that will last long into the winter, even under the snow. The fields extend featurelessly away from this patch.
98323: A Gloomy Corner of the Forest
A great horned owl looks cautiously around it.

A great brushfire seems to have raged in the western part of this forest some time ago. Still, the old trees here have remained unharmed by the scorching flames, even if some of their trunks are slightly soot-covered. The ground is covered with dense vegetation and clumped roots extending from the trees, hinting at the fertility of the soil and making the terrain difficult to travel. Twilight enshrouds the thick foliage and a hollow sigh echoes through the dark trees whenever the wind blows.
98324: A large brown wolf stands here, its teeth partly bared.

Lying just north of a forest, this huge field still shows no sign of the trees or heavy undergrowth that can be found there. Beside a few bushes, all visible vegetation is grass, which covers the rocky ground with a smooth yellowish green layer. Odd shapes, like rusty shards of metal, stick out of the ground here and there hinting at some battle fought here a long time ago.
98325: A Lonely Mound in the Grassy Fields

The corpse of a slithering snake is lying here.
A cluster of white star-shaped forget-me-nots flourish here in reminiscence.
A frog is standing here.

A lonely grave mound, located among some dry bushes, catches the eye in this grassy field. The mound is large enough to contain a few man-sized bodies, or perhaps that of one large beast. No signs of habitation in these lands are visible, only faint depressions in the grass hint at something passing through here often. To the north, the grassy field turns into rolling plains.
98326: The smooth carpet of grass is broken by a wide, sandy pit. A narrow dirt path leads from the north to the edge of the pit, where someone has built simple wooden stairs to make climbing up and down the sand-covered slope easier. At the bottom of the pit, a blackened skewer hangs above a bed of burnt logs and stumps. The old, burned down fire is surrounded by shreds of charred skin and gnawed bones, giving some hints on what the hunters' latest catch might have been. Judging from the amount of leftovers on the ground, it is no small group that enjoys their meals here.
98327: Far away from all inhabited lands, the weeds on these fields have been growing without any limitations. Grass of medium height covers the ground in all directions and grows thicker to the north. Small paths lead through the grass, making movement easier. Neither grass nor rocks can be seen to add colour into the constant brown of their worn surface of dirt.
98328:
The corpse of a green snake is lying here.
The corpse of a green snake is lying here.

Here, a thick and high hedgerow, yet no more than twenty feet wide, separates the vast plains in the east from the grassland in the west. A dirt path winds in the north-south direction inside the hedge, protected by a wall of bushes on both sides. Even though peeking through the dense foliage is possible, finding a way to pass through easily is very hard. To the north the hedges seem to be growing closer towards each other, yet the path continues.
98329: A Patch of Herbs in the Thicket
A low, many-branched shrub covers the ground here.

Hidden amidst a dense thicket of tall bushes, this small field is sheltered from anything that could disturb the growth of its vegetation. The multitude of herbs growing in the field and under the bushes suggests that a wide variety of plants find just what they need here: a perfect combination of shade, nutrients and water. Some of the plants seem uncommon and strange to these lands, almost as if someone had planted them here, yet the amount of wild weeds indicates that no one tends them.
98330: A variety of grasses have grown tall on this field, making movement on anything but the narrow animal paths quite hard. At the sides of the paths, hummocks of tough weeds rise from the ground, and one can spot several places where animals have been digging for roots to eat. One path going west seems wider than the others, suggesting it is used by wandering herds or perhaps even hunters or travellers.
98331: The ground here is notably lower than in the surrounding meadows. For anyone standing on the bottom of the hollow, there is no way of seeing if someone is approaching. Being protected from the wind however, the hollow offers a sheltered place for listening the sounds of the plains. Some dropping-covered turf at the inner side of the hollow suggests this is also the home of some large animal.
98332: A clear spring babbles as cool water trickles out of the ground.

A small spring with fresh and pure water beckons those who pass by to take a refreshing drink. It has formed a small, clear puddle at the bottom of a sandy hollow, where fragile plants draw nourishment through small, grey pebbles. The grass around the spring grows low, yet there are no visible signs of animals coming here to drink. Apart from the quiet shuffling of sand and leaves, there usually seems to be a notable silence about this place, as if it was beckoning the occasional traveller for rest and contemplation.
98333: The slightly sandy and rocky ground seems to have little to offer for the local vegetation, yet some shrubs with crooked branches and dry needles grow here in tightly packed groups. Occasional white and blood red stones add colour to the dull grey soil; their shape is round and smooth, almost as if they had been under running water in some ancient times. However, no signs of streams or rivers can be seen amidst the shubbery dominating this rugged landscape.
98334: A Maple Tree among the Bushes

The branches of a huge maple tree hover above the small, round bushes growing here. The tree seems very old, for many hollows filled with dry leaves and broken twigs can be seen along its trunk. Judging from the signs of nesting in the nooks and crannies, maples like this one seem to be quite popular among the local bird life; the thin shrubs around it cannot offer such protection. The brushwood continues in every direction, and seems to get thicker in the north and west.
98335: Tall bushes rise high above the ground, standing in winding rows and forming twisting corridors where one can pass between them. The lower branches of the bushes are leafless, while those near their tops spread out and create a green ceiling. The ground is bare and soft, even slightly muddy. Many kinds of vines seem to thrive here, as they can be often seen creeping up along the shrubs.
98336: A black crow flies low to the ground here, looking for carrion to eat.

This slight depression in the middle of a field of sand seems to be a frequently used place for camping. A lonely tree on one side of it offers some protection from the elements under its branches, where someone has built a small shelter. The crude structure is made of pruned young trees bound together tightly with some lengths of rope, and seems adequate for spending a night or two. A sooty pit near the shelter, obviously the spot for a campfire, is surrounded by large stones to keep some of the heat.
98337: As if planted by hand to show the beauty of Arda, this meadow contains a variety of flowers. Bushes of eglantine are spreading their lush branches at some spots, while on the ground one can see anemones and asphodels growing in the shade. Some irises grow in the soft mud along a few ditches, where also the footprints of different animals coming here show easily. The ground near the clusters of flowers is rather flat but begins to slope farther away from this field. In the north, the landscape seems much more barren.
98338: A large brown wolf stands here, its teeth partly bared.

This crude outlook built of logs and long planks can be seen from far away on these open fields. It is only about a dozen feet high, but standing on the seemingly highest hillock anywhere within several miles, it could grant an impressive view over the surrounding grasslands. The bushes growing below the wooden stand fail to hide the ladder leading up from view; it seems whoever built the structure had little concern for secrecy here.
98339:
A woody evergreen plant grows here, with many stems reaching upward.
A brown furry gopher is here, ready to dive back underground.
A tall stag is here, grazing peacefully.

Here and there, green tufts of grass peek out of the sand covering these wide fields. The landscape is open with hardly any trees, allowing one to see far in every direction. The season's weather has left its mark on the smooth ground, where wavy patterns decorate the surface. Among them, an occasional animal track, even that of a snake, is visible.
98340: A large rabbit looks peacefully at you, ready to dart away.

A wide mound, several feet high, rises above the fields of sand here. The top of the mound is covered by a carpet of tangled, dry grass, while on its sides nothing seems to hold the dirt in place. Some old stumps stick out of the northern side of the mound; perhaps this area was once part of a great forest. The open field extends to the south, where no signs of vegetation can be seen.
98356: This outlook post has been constructed of old timbers which seem sturdy enough to endure the years of standing on this open hilltop. Wide planks make up the floor of the platform, where some gaps and holes offer a glimpse of the bushy ground below. There is no ceiling, so this place was most likely not meant to work as a shelter. However, it seems to be well suited for serving as a watchtower: the view over the surrounding landscape is remarkable.
98357:
A fierce boar is here, making grunting noises.
A fierce boar is here, making grunting noises.

The ground slopes up and down, but is still plain enough not to hinder any movement. Anyone wanting to travel fast between the vales of Anduin and the southeastern expanse, could take a quick ride over these plains. Other than a distant tree standing in the west, and what seems to be an outlook tower far in the east, no remarkable features can be seen in the landscape.
98358: The ground slopes slightly to the west, down towards the Anduin River, giving a good view of the wide fields spreading out there. The ground is covered with grass and clover, which has grown unusually tall. Some round bumps on the slopes, crowned by this vegetation, make the fields appear sheltered despite the lack of trees and bushes. Here and there, small rabbit holes can be found.
98359: Thorny thickets cover the ground, but the vegetation has not grown high enough to hinder any movement. The shrubs stand almost motionless in this open landscape, since their tough branches could only be swayed by the strongest of winds. The hay growing here is light, and passing through the fields is easy along the numerous animal paths leading to the west.
