A slope to the east leads up to a meadow and a great oak can be seen to the south.
98360: Grassy Plains by a Great Oak

There are some acorns lying here.
A large rabbit looks peacefully at you, ready to dart away.

Rising well above thirty feet and being about twice as broad from branch to branch, a great oak dominates the field. Its thick branches are covered with huge leaves, offering a shelter against most kinds of weather, while the nooks and crannies among its roots and on its burly trunk give the same for small animals. The grassy plains around the oak are flat and to the east they extend towards the distant Mirkwood forest.
98391: A black crow flies low to the ground here, looking for carrion to eat.

A field of fine sand spreads out over the open landscape. Occasional stunted trees seem to be the most visible landmarks around here, while hummocks of weeds with long leaves make up most of the vegetation on the ground. No signs of water are visible in the area, yet a number of holes and burrows in the sand hint at an abundance of animal life.
98392: A swarm of mosquitoes is here, humming around you.

The dry soil here seems to offer little nourishment for the local plantlife, yet some thin bushes with round, leathery leaves manage to thrive on these otherwise open plains. Their branches are quite crooked and their bark grey, making it hard to guess their age, while the rich green hue of their leaves suggests they could survive for many years to come. The bushes mark a noticeable transition between the verdant grasslands to the west and a wide, sandy area to the east.
98393: Most of the fields here are covered with low but thick green grass. Only a small thicket of globular bushes with tiny sharp leaves breaks the monotony of these fields overlooking an ancient trail in the north. These plains are often inhabited by many forms of wildlife, as one can tell from the chewed twigs and blades of grass.
98394: A colourful butterfly is fluttering around here.

Following the course of Anduin as it turns westwards, the worn trail continues to pass through plains and grassland. Only a lonely brushwood growing on the eastern side of the trail differs from the surrounding landscape. White, small pebbles lie on and around the trail's path.
98395: A large rabbit looks peacefully at you, ready to dart away.

Thick bushes with sharp thorns grow wild in this small valley. The layer of fine sand covering the valley floor seems to offer little nourishment for other vegetation, allowing one to move rather freely in places where the bushes have not yet spread into. Some animal paths lead up and down the surrounding slopes, showing where travelling through is easiest. A low hollow lies in the middle of the valley, perhaps marking the spot of a now dry pond.
98396:
A large thorny branched shrub is growing here.
On the shrub, there are two piles of blackberries.

The landscape descends steeply towards the Great River in the north. In some places, where the weather has worn out the carpet of grass, loose soil and pebbles are slowly spreading over the slope. Some blackberry bushes grow at spots where the soil is still rich, sinking their roots into the layer of gravel and holding it in place. Tiny trickles of water run down the bedrock in the few places where it is visible, indicating that some groundwater might break through the surface here.
98397: A Bend in the Worn Trail

Sharply the worn trail turns west, passing an ancient milestone with faint markings on its rough surface. Once, a long time ago, this place used to be a crossroad for two trails. Unused in the recent years, the east going trail quickly disappears under the soft mat of grass. The main trail comes from the north and continues westward, while east and south from this point lie plains of green grass and occasional bushes.
98398: Moving closer to the river the trail reaches a place where many animals, small and big, come to refresh themselves with the flowing water. Because of a thick layer of limestone in the ground, the soil is as hard as rock. It is likely this is why there are almost no plants growing around here.
98399: Being considerably lower than the surrounding fields, meadows and plains, this valley is only slightly above the water level of the Anduin. The riverside edge of the valley is covered with dark yellow reeds and the ground gets rather wet and swampy. It seems this valley is usually flooded at the high-water periods in the springtime.
98400: A Bend in the Trail along the Anduin

A low hillock, shaped like a bowl turned upside down, rises above the fields. A small wood of bushy pines stands on top of the slope, hiding the lands to the east behind them. An ancient trail travels through the terrain along the river Anduin, bending slightly on its course where it meets the pine-covered hillock. The surface of the trail consists of hard-packed dirt with some loose pebbles, making it seem like an easy route to travel to the north and west.
98401:
A huge warg is here, moving in for the kill.
A ferocious warg is here, snarling angrily.
A ferocious warg is here, snarling angrily.
A ferocious warg is here, snarling angrily.

Here, the ancient trail following the Anduin narrows considerably as it is engulfed in a shrubbery of willows and other bushes with slender branches. The ground is furrowed amidst the bushes, showing signs of water having formed ponds and ditches or flown towards the river. The trail winds past dense shrubs and deep hollows as it continues out of the shrubbery and towards more open land.
98402: Passing through fertile grasslands and meadows, the trail reaches an area of less greenery. While some grass is still visible, much of the ground is covered with stones. A thick green mat of moss grows all around, even on the largest rocks. Right next to the trail, some rocks have tangles of vines with small leaves growing on them.
98403:
A small green mound rises from the ground.
A worm is here slithering around.
A large brown wolf stands here, its teeth partly bared.

This is a perfect place to get a good sight over the Anduin river flowing by. An about two feet high bank, falling straight down into the river, is covered with smaller plants only, so the view of the Anduin is remarkable. Farther away from the river the grass is higher and even a few bushes appear. Signs of small animals living around here are visible in the undergrowth.
98404: Rocks of various sizes and shapes dot the smooth grass at this southern bank of the river Anduin. A chain of knolls runs along the river, offering a few good places to see the swirling waters below, while level grassland continues away from the river. The vegetation is sparse here, but some bushes begin to show far in the south. A pyramidal pile of rocks sits on the top of the highest knoll around.
98405: A swift stream of cold, clear water babbles cheerfully as it breaks through the layer of rolling pebbles covering the ground, creating a shallow yet noticeable obstacle. The rivulet seems to enter this low point in the landscape from the east, following the trail for a while, then making a swift turn across it and towards the river Anduin. Slender saplings grow here and there along the stream, which seems to carry along occasional twigs, leaves and seeds, helping the local vegetation to spread.
98406: An ancient trail passes by a bend in the Anduin, offering a view of the banks on this side of the river. Steep, grassy slopes descend towards the water, which seems quite calm below this point, while surges and whirlpools appear farther away where some rocks stand out. The trail continues to follow the river to the west and to the north, while from the east, a narrow rivulet slithers down the slopes to meet it.
98407: A black raven flies in the sky searching for flesh to prey upon.

This edge of the forest is quite open since the trees stand far apart and their thin branches offer little shade. Clusters of colourful flowers and clumps of wriggling roots enliven the ground under the tall birches, whose white trunks reach for the skies like pillars of finest marble. Moss-covered cliffs rise among the trees and thickening vegetation in the east, where the forest seems to get much darker.
98408: A clear stream flows gently through the mixed forest, carrying fallen leaves and broken stems among the quietly swirling waters. Bushes with hanging branches outline its sides; here and there a fallen trunk has pushed them aside, forming a natural bridge over the stream. The looming shapes of various tall trees are reflected from the almost still surface of the water, until it begins to ripple considerably towards the west.
98409: A steep face of rock, about six feet high, separates these sloping fields from the forested area to the east. A gap in the small wood standing above the ridge reveals a clear rivulet, which gains speed as it meets the sudden fall. The sounds of water breaking against stone at the bottom of the waterfall can be heard even from a distance, and small droplets hang on the leaves of the surrounding vegetation. The stream continues down to the northwest where the river Anduin lies in the distance.
98410: The dry, waist-high hay in these fields hides every rock and stump from view. Amidst the hay some old tangled nests of small birds can be noticed. In some places, the hay has been flattened either by rain or by large animals following their paths through the plains. From here, wide grasslands spread out to the east.
98411: A carpet of grass covers the gentle slope leading up from a wide hollow in the west. Bushes are scarce here and the only place for animals to hide in seems to be the high hay in the north. The plains continue as far as the eye can see to the southeast.
98425: A Green Pond in the Forest

Clusters of slender stems and tall leaves thrive in the mud and shallows.
A black raven flies in the sky searching for flesh to prey upon.
A black raven flies in the sky searching for flesh to prey upon.

A still pond lies here in the middle of a dense forest, slowly being engulfed into a growth of moss and reeds. The tiny leaves of some water plant form a tinted green cover on its surface, suggesting that the water is very good for their nourishment. The dark depths of the pond do not reveal anything from a distance, while a shallow stream with a clearly visible bottom runs from the pond towards the woods in the west. Some old snags stand out in the middle of the pond, forming a tangle for birds and fishes to hide in.
98431: Most of the trees in this part of the forest are old beeches with thick trunks and reaching branches. Little light, be it sun or star or moon, can reach the ground from the sky, yet dense undergrowth has spread over the mossy soil below. Large boulders block some of the paths leading past the huge trees, especially to the west where a cliff seems to rise from the deepest part of the forest.
98452: A rock lizard is here, motionless as it observes you.

Rocks about the size of a man's head, covered in black and green lichen, lie about everywhere on this field. The ground must be quite dry since only tiny flowers, sprigs and weeds grow in the otherwise smooth fields of yellowed grass. The hay gets higher in the east, but even there the only source of water seems to be rain. Some tall rowans stand in the middle of the fields, providing berries for local birds even in the winter.
98453: A Narrow Rivulet through the Plains
A clear spring babbles as cool water trickles out of the ground.

A wide hollow in the plains separates a rocky area in the north from grasslands extending to the other directions. Water is seeping from an embankment, forming a puddle at the bottom of the hollow. From there the water flows westwards, turning from a narrow stream into a rivulet near a pair of boulders. The rivulet soon disappears from sight as it runs into some dense vegetation.
98454:
A fallow deer is grazing peacefully here.
A fallow deer is grazing peacefully here.

Thick bushes grow here and there in a field of weeds, flanking the furrow of a rivulet running towards the river. The ground seems somewhat muddy, but not too soft to cross. Some young trees stand among mossy boulders in the north where the ground slopes upwards to meet a low hillock of bare rock. Thick shrubbery continues in the east, but farther south the bushy area seems to turn into an open meadow.
98455: The Trail Passing a Sandy Beach
A trained horse (Rood) is standing here, ridden by you.

Water flows in trickles through the sand where a rivulet joins the great river Anduin. A narrow trail following the river leads over the beach, where crossing the small stream seems easier, then disappears back into the surrounding brushwood. It seems possible to follow the rivulet eastwards; the vegetation gets less dense on higher grounds. Some droppings can be noticed near the stream, suggesting that wild animals come here for water.
98456: On the Trail over a Small Cliff

Patches of moss covering the ground leave the rock bare only where the trail climbs over a low cliff. Young birches growing on all sides of this rocky outcrop make room for the trail as it goes up towards higher cliffs in the west and downhill in the north. Grassy plains extend eastwards, and the ground slopes steeply down to moist fields in the south.
98458: Tussocks of weeds and grass make the ground seem soft to tread on. Some larger rocks lie hidden under flattened hay, but avoiding such obstacles would be easy on these open fields. The ground slopes steeply to the east where one might get a better look over the plains. Small bushes grow here and there, gathering into a hedgerow far in the north.
98459: A single boulder stands on top of a grassy incline, marking the highest point in the plains. If this was anywhere near a populated area, there would probably be a tale about how the boulder got there. But here, it is surrounded only by desolate grasslands stretching as far as the eye can see.
98460: The corpse of an orkish wolf-rider is lying here.

The blackened trunk of a long-dead tree stands tall in the middle of a field of hay. The wood is splintered and hard as rock near the ground; perhaps a lightning struck here a long time ago, setting fire to the tree and burning away the rest of the forest. There seems to be a hole under the roots of the tree, but it is covered by a tangle of dead branches. In the south, a stand of shorter but living trees forms the outskirts of a forest.
98461: A low shrub with bright green, oblong leaves is growing here.

The young birches growing in this part of the forest cannot be older than a decade, but many charred stumps of once mighty trees lie on the ground among rocks and weeds. In the south, the rocky furrow of a dried-up stream separates this part of the forest from dense brushwood. All around, the tiny holes of some rodents can be seen in the nooks under the stumps. The growth of birches becomes much more dense towards the east and south, where the wall of branches hinders visibility greatly.
98463: Field in Front of a Small Cabin

Some delicious wild strawberries grow on the ground.
A coloured game bird is visible in the vegetation, watching you warily.

Short grass, wild strawberries, and small plants with large leaves cover this small field. Three narrow dirt paths meet in the middle of the field and continue to the door of a cabin standing near the outskirts of a forest. In the south, a thick shrubbery engulfs the grass, and also some taller trees begin to show in that direction.
98464: A fishing rod has been left here.

There is enough room inside this lodge for several travellers to sleep on the dirt floor. A niche in the middle of the cabin seems to have held campfires in the past, and there is a slit in the roof made of sticks to lead any smoke out. Walls build of thick logs and sealed with moss keep the wind out, leaving a musty smell to the air inside. Two broken shelves hanging from the back wall are the only pieces of furniture in the lodge.
98465: A squirrel scampers around here, looking for nuts from the trees.

Thick shrubs under the trees make travelling through this end of the forest rather hard. Stinging nettles among the undergrowth make the woods seem unfriendly and seldom visited, yet a dirt path leads north towards what seems to be a small cabin near the edge of the forest. In the south, the path quickly disappears under dense shrubs and tall, looming oaks. Deeper in the forest, the huge trees seem to keep everything under a constant shadow.
98467: Short stalks of grass intermingle with gnarled walnut trees and hoary ashes in this small forest. Although bursting with life, the forest is mostly silent. The grassy ground underfoot is damp and gives forth a fresh vigour. All over this forest, small patches of light blue flowers can be seen.
98486: Low grass suddenly turns into a field of waist-high goldenrods, which make a whooshing noise whenever a gust of wind ploughs its way through them. In the west, a small cabin can be seen near the edge of the forest that spreads around the field. The woods in the east seem less dense, while in the north open grassland stretches over a steep slope.
98494: Through the clean water the bottom of the riverbed is visible. It is covered with sharp-edged stones and some higher formations of rock. Some of that rock even reaches the surface, making this part of the river rather risky to pass for an unwary traveller. With some skill and care however, it seems possible to take even a large boat through here.
98495:
A stocky mountain mule is here, waiting to serve.
Buka the Dwarf, wielding a great warsword, is standing here.

The Anduin widens considerably here, and the riverbed becomes quite shallow. Probably because of that, the vegetation in the water is very dense, consisting of reeds and clusters of blossoming plants with large leaves. Still, the bottom of the river cannot be seen here; the water is quite brown and full of drifting stems and leaves. Even the banks are hidden behind the walls of reeds for the most part.
98496: A steep face of rock rises in the south, causing a slight change of course to the Great River. The flow becomes rapid as the river narrows, and little swirls moving along the surface turn into whirlpools near the cliff. Stunted trees and shrubs cling to the ledges, yet climbing out of the water seems challenging there. However, currents have piled up fine sand at the eastern bank, where it seems possible to even land a boat.
98497: The ancient trail turns south as it approaches the river Anduin from the east, so that only a few feet of grassy bank are left between it and the water. On the other side of the trail, grassy plains, a home for many wild animals, continue to the horizon and probably even further. The high walls of reeds, which seem to be growing very well on the northern bank of the river, slowly become less dense and finally disappear as the river turns south again. The trail itself is slowly being taken over by small bushes and other low vegetation.
98500: Trail with a View over the River
A trained horse (Rood) is standing here, ridden by you.

A narrow trail leads over the cliffs bordering the riverbed, making a sharp turn at the edge of an escarpment overlooking the river. On a clear day, the other bank and the lands far to the north might be visible from there. In the north below the cliff, tall bushes cover the ground just before the river, but they would not stop one from breaking some bones with the fall. The trail continues above the steep rock to the east, and in the south it passes close to a dark hole through the cliff before disappearing into brushwood.
98501: Having flown past a muddy armlet, the waters of the great Anduin slowly clear here. The bottom of the river, covered with rocks and piles of pebbles, is clearly visible through the water. Garbled red weeds growing on a few rocks, at the bottom of the riverbed, give the water a strange pink tone. A worn trail on the eastern bank follows the river as it keeps turning west. In the south, some bushes grow on the riverbank, but behind them a vertical face of rock prevents climbing on the high bank.
98502: At the End of the Grassy Trail

An old trail, overgrown with grass, comes to an end here at the steep cliffs outlining the river Anduin. Only a few bent twigs on the path indicate that it is still being used these days. The trail fades into the grass and finally disappears amidst the dense bushes at the edge of the riverside cliffs. The ground south of the trail becomes slightly rocky and sandy as it slopes down towards a distant bend in the river. North of the trail, neither rocks nor sand can be seen, as green grass dominates the landscape together with a huge beech standing only a few yards away. Heading west through the grasslands, the trail starts its long journey towards Lorien.
98507:
A copper penny lies on the ground.
A small campfire burns here, its low flames giving off only a little light.

In most parts of this forest, the bushes and shrubs have grown that high and thick that the only glimpse that can be caught of trees are their stems and trunks if they come in the range of one's hands. Since not much light from the sun reaches down here, most of the bushes consist of wooden and knobby branches or remains of old, died and withered shrubs. Yet, many of the bushes have developed thin, light brownish leaves for which the fractions of light reaching down here are sufficient.
98508:
A small campfire burns here, its low flames giving off only a little light.
A copper penny lies on the ground.
A copper penny lies on the ground.

A few paths can be seen before they vanish somewhere in the thick underbrush below the thick leaves and branches of the trees. The birds above and squirrels near the ground have no problem with all these shrubs, trunks, bushes and dense vegetation. But anything bigger than them has to find and force its own path. For many years, this forest has grown to become the impenetrable thicket it is today.
98509: Schmidt the Half-Elf, wielding an engraved broadsword, is standing here (shrouded).

The trees have dense crowns which block most of the light of day or night, and the shrubbery is thick and thorny. The ground is uneven, and at many spots, little holes or depressions lurk below the deep grass. At some spots, where the bigger bushes grow less dense, low plants with light yellow leaves and small, green berries try to fight for their place in this heavily overgrown forest.
98524: A woodpecker is here, tapping on a tree.

The bushes in this part of the forest are not very dense, yet moving among the trees without cracking branches or stumbling over roots seems hard for the unskilled. Mixed woods turn into a grove of ashes in the west, while in the north only young birches grow on the other side of a dried-up stream. The forest continues far to the east before it meets the edge of widespread, barren plains.
98536:
A copper penny lies on the ground.
A copper penny lies on the ground.
A copper penny lies on the ground.
A copper penny lies on the ground.
A copper penny lies on the ground.

At this place, some paths coming from the surrounding brushes and trees meet, while only low bushes grow nearby. The looming trees and their thick branches with their many leaves and the thorny bushes prevent this place from being a clearing, but compared to the rest of the forest, it is a place of free movement. Yet this changes fast as one steps away from the meeting of the only barely visible paths and gets closer to the high and dense shrubbery and the thick stems of ancient and young trees.
98544:
A copper penny lies on the ground.
A copper penny lies on the ground.
A copper penny lies on the ground.
A copper penny lies on the ground.

Thick trees grow high towards the sky and block most of it. Below the huge and darkening crowns, there do not grow many bushes, yet a thick entanglement of tendrils and vines is interwoven with them. Only a few paths created by stronger animals like boars lead through this very dense scrub, but they soon disappear from sight between and below bushes or tendrils.
98555: A cluster of dark green, feathery fronds flourishes in the shade.

Ashes with burly trunks and far-reaching branches dominate this part of the forest. Dead wood, rocks, everything on the ground is covered in thick moss and little else; only in spots where sunlight can directly shine through the trees, ivies crawling up along the trunks can be noticed. A single man-sized rock stands erect in the light of a small opening; elsewhere the twilight and the trees conceal similar shapes, making the forest seem more lively than it actually is. The terrain soon gets much harder to travel towards the deeper parts of the forest; coming back out could prove to be extremely difficult.
98595: A strong hermit is quietly observing his surroundings.

An eerie quietness dominates these woods. The near-reverent silence is broken only sparingly by the soft rustle of young leaves. Only a few bushes grow between the high trees. All around, there are slight and subtle signs of habitation to be spotted. In a bush, some furs have been stuck on poles and form a low roof, only big enough for someone to sleep under it. Nearby, a low shed of branches has been built, while again a few steps away, some jars of clay hang in the branches of a lower tree. A sheltered fireplace hides well behind two smaller rocks. It seems as if someone has distributed everything needed for a living within this copse of trees.
98599:
A trout swims here.
A trout swims here.

Although the river is wide, the water here is deep and hurries between the high banks. This is truly a great river. In places the long thirsty roots of the bare trees dip into the river providing you with a chance of scrambling up the bank. The forests on the banks make it impossible to get a view of the lands to either side. The trees to the southeast seem to be thinner. Only the gurgle of the river swirling among the roots breaks the silence.
98600:
A trout swims here.
A trout swims here.
A trout swims here.

The river widens and turns southwards here. Tall thin trees on the steep banks to the north and east block the view of the lands beyond. The air is fresh and clean, reminiscent of the springtime. From time to time bubbles break the surface of the water as fishes come up to gulp some air or snatch an insect.
98601: This narrow trench lies deep in the middle of a mound of head-sized rocks. Some wooden supports have been set against the neatly piled stones forming the walls, which seem stable enough to allow moving here safely. The trench is covered from above by some dry, leafless branches, while a mat of weeds torn off the nearby rocks has been dragged here to seal the entrance. The surrounding fields and the sky above can be seen though the dead vegetation and some loose stones, but there is no doubt this place is hidden well from the outside. Rusty chips of metal and a small piece of fabric on the ground hint at supplies being stored here at times.
98603:
The corpse of a tiny spider is lying here.
The corpse of a tiny spider is lying here.
The corpse of a huge, poisonous spider is lying here.

Dirt covers the stony ground of this old corridor. It seems to have once been furnished but the wood has collapsed into rotten heaps long ago. Decayed remains of old tapestries and shields hang on the walls. Everything down here is covered with layers upon layers of old, dusty cobwebs. Where the corridor bends to the east, a few broken beams of stone hang down. A dark hole is visible high above on the northern wall, constantly dripping moisture and tiny pebbles.
98604:
The corpse of a huge tarantula is lying here.
A tiny spider is here, eating a tiny bug.

Thick, dusty cobwebs cover the walls and ceiling of this small chamber. Only a closer inspection reveals rotten furniture below layers of webs, dust and dirt. The floor is made of large flagstones and many seem broken or at least sunken in and askew.
98606: Once this chamber seems to have been quite big, yet the larger part to the north has collapsed as have most of the walls. The last leftovers of beams of stone hang from the ceiling and most of the large tiles on the walls and floor are broken and cracked. Clear, cold water now fills the entire chamber. Remains of decoration such as shields, tapestries or weapons can be seen floating near all of the walls but everything is too soaked and decayed to be of any use.
98607: The beams supporting this corridor have rotted away long ago and the walls and the ceiling have collapsed, leaving a narrow passage filled with rocks, dirt and soil. A small runlet of water makes the floor wet and has started to polish the fallen stones. It flows down towards the eastern end of the corridor which seems to have completely filled with water. Far above on the western wall, the entrance to a dark tunnel is vaguely visible.
98609: The rocky tunnel leading down from the cliffs above gets wider when it reaches the water level, then expands into a small cavern several feet under the surface. Water stands still in the middle of the tunnel, but some algae near a gap in the rocky wall are swaying in the current. In the far corner of the underwater cavern, a wide tunnel leads away from the river.
98610:
An albino salamander is here, perched on some rocks.
An albino salamander is here, perched on some rocks.

Water trickles through a wide crack in the rough wall of this circular cavern. A gentle breeze passes through the crack, but the air down here is stale and smells like rotten fish. On the muddy cavern floor, tiny insects scurry away from droplets of water falling from the ceiling. At one end of the cavern, a quiet pool turns into a tunnel leading towards the river.
98611: A fierce wolverine is here, snarling at you.

A network of thin roots forms the ceiling of this somewhat cramped earthen burrow. The ground here is very sandy, and all kinds of tracks are visible on the dust-covered floor. It seems like this hole was dug a long time ago by some animals, perhaps a fox couple. The markings on the walls and the debris lying around suggest this sheltered dwelling has had many different inhabitants since. The hole is probably larger nowadays than it originally was, since at a few spots it is large enough for a man to stand up straight.
98612: Murky Waters of the Green Pond
A large pike is lurking in the mud by the bottom.

The dark waters of this somewhat overgrown pond do not allow one to see very far beneath the surface. Quietly swaying water plants grow here amidst some submerged trunks, getting shorter towards the deeper parts of the pond where even less light is available. The muddy bottom of the pond seems soft and treacherous as it is slowly sucking down broken branches and other litter. Near the northern brim, some burly roots of living trees standing above the pond reach into the murky waters. More immersed snags can be seen among these gnarled roots.
98613: A skeleton of some humanoid lies in the dust.

The huge sunken tree above forms a dark ceiling to this small hollow far beneath the surface. Some roots from the tall trees growing on the bank crawl towards the bottom of the pond, and hold this tree firmly in their grasp. Dark green weeds surround the hollow completely, but here, only occasional twigs and leaves cover the dull, grey mud. Only one opening between the weeds and the roots seems to lead towards more open waters.
98614:
A brown bear is sleeping here.
A brown bear is sleeping here.

This is the cave of a big animal. There is no telling who built the cave, but the current inhabitants certainly do not want to share it. The air is musty and pieces of half-eaten meat have drawn the attention of insects and rats. The earthen ground is quite smooth.
98615: A Deep Hole under the Tree

A small termite is running around making strange sounds.
A giant termite is here, crushing skulls and bones.

The tunnel leading through the roots seems narrower near the base of the tree, but down here it looks wide enough for a bear to sleep in. Sand has fallen off the ceiling and walls at many spots, but the roots sticking out of the soil everywhere have kept the tunnel from collapsing. Some of the larger roots have holes running through them, and the whole place is crawling with insects.
98621:
The corpse of a brown snake is lying here.
The corpse of a brown snake is lying here.
The corpse of a mottled snake is lying here.
A small brown snake is slithering around here.
A small brown snake is slithering around here.
A small brown snake is slithering around here.
A small brown snake is slithering around here.

A small natural cave has formed over the past ages. The walls consist of hard rock. The rain of past decades and centuries must have washed out all the soft soil so that this cave has been able to take its form. The walls, ceiling and floor are all covered with dozens of cracks of all sizes, yet there seems to be not much circulation of fresh air and the temperature is stable. The floor is covered with the tracks of snakes and mostly consists of little bones and dirt. Seemingly thousands of small animals like rabbits, mice, rats and maybe even foxes must have found their final demise down here. A part of the eastern wall looks as if it had collapsed some time ago.
98622:
A skeleton of some humanoid lies in the dust.
A nest is here.
A diamondback rattlesnake is coiled here, ready to strike.
A black snake, with red markings, is lying here.
A black snake, with red markings, is lying here.
A mottled snake is sneaking here, ready to sink its fangs into flesh.
A mottled snake is sneaking here, ready to sink its fangs into flesh.
A small brown snake is slithering around here.
A small brown snake is slithering around here.

Cracks run along the walls and the ceiling of this small natural cave. The bottom is not only covered with the remains of many little animals but also with many skins of snakes that outgrew them. Near the lower part of the cave, most of the cracks become broader. The air is dry and smells of earth and something else strongly. Near the walls, many nests of snakes with dozens of eggs can be seen.
98623:
A smoked and salted piece of meat lies on the ground.
A smoked and salted piece of meat lies on the ground.
A water barrel has been left here.
Peapend the Noldo, wielding a black runed dagger, is standing here.

This place seems to be more like a small alcove than any tunnel or actual cavern. The walls are crowded with shelves, which are carrying various junk and garbage. The footing here is filled with piles of some rotting food supplies and fragments of containers which have fallen off from the shelves.
98624: High grass grows all over in this cave, and the rocky walls are also covered with many thick, green tendrils. Where no other plant could take root, soft and shimmering moss covers the grey rock. Near the southern wall, clear water flows from a small spring and vanishes between some cracks in the rock.
98625: A large stone chest is here.

This room, secreted away by a convienent cave-in, has many different items of the surrounding areas. Surprising items from Dunland, Eregion and even a flag from the city of Tharbad can be found here. Most of the items seen here are useless, except for the large chest in the southern part of the room.
98628:
A skeleton of some humanoid lies in the dust.
A black pond of water is here.
A large mean-looking troll is here.
A large mean-looking troll is here.
A huge black fungus is here, exuding a foul stench.

Scattered among the bones and debris are piles of dung and old carcasses. A foul odour of decay and filth pervades this area. It is the stink of trolls. Upheaved stumps play the role of stools and table, being covered in blood and entrails.
98629: A Bear's Cave in the Ridge

A big cavebear is padding around here.
A big cavebear is padding around here.

The dark and dry cave seems to resemble a home that would belong to a family of bears, judging by the massive paw marks indented into the ground. Also on the ground are many broken bones along with shreds of cloth that appear to have been garments of clothing. There is a strong stench of decaying carcasses all around you. The ground is very soft and moist and every step you take seems to create an imprint of your footing.
98631:
A small bag of elven make is lying here.
A large encrusted cedar chest is standing here.

In this small and very high cave, all the cracks in the bottom have been filled with sand, and the walls have been straightened out with clay. High up, there are a few cracks left, which let in a few rays of light when the sun or the moon is up. Hammocks made of fine, silvery cords hang near one wall, and a small table has been built in a corner. Below the table, there is a big pile of firewood. The walls, which are painted with lively colours to resemble a prospering forest, bring life to this cave, making perfectly clear that this underground place was not built by Dwarves or Men, but by Elves.
98646: You know that the ground is almost one hundred and fifty feet below, but you can't see it. Branches block the view down. From here, in the southeastern part of the forest, you have a marvellous overlook on a clear day. The heart of the forest is to the west. East, at some distance, are two of river Bruinen's contributors. They meet and run southwards. The river disappears into a deep valley far to the southwest maybe the valley of Rivendell, or Imladris in elven tongue, signifying deep-dale-cleft. Close to the river there is a trail.
98647: You are in one of the big trees a good climber can reach. Another tree is to the north. The thick branch pointing that direction seem stable enough. Dense leaves block out the sky. This place is left in eternal darkness.
98651: The air is damp. A wall of branches and leaves does not allow any light to enter here. The only exits are down and south to another tree. It looks easy to climb down but it might be hard or impossible to come back here that way.
98652: A Flet in the Great Beech

A dented pail has been carelessly left here.
A warm blanket covers the ground.
A wiry elf is treading quietly here.

A set of planks has been bound together to form the floor of this small flet, supported by the solid branches of the ancient beech. There are no shelves, tables or other furniture here, suggesting that if this dwelling ever was inhabited, those days are now long past. Some dirt is noticeable on the floorboards, however; someone has been here only recently, otherwise the soil would have been wiped away by the last rain. Also, a light curtain woven of sturdy reeds hangs on one branch, perhaps to give some protection against cold winds or bright rays of the sun. Even the ladder leading down, while hard to notice, seems to have been in constant use.
98653: The wide branches of this ancient beech seem to retain their strength even farther away from the trunk, allowing anyone with some climbing skills to move among them with ease. Below these old branches, the cliff at the edge of the river Anduin suddenly ends, followed by a fall of about sixty feet straight down onto the water. Some of the branches even reach far past the rockface, granting an impressive view of the river for anyone daring to climb that far. The foliage looks thick enough to catch any sudden gusts of wind but also stops one from discerning details in the surrounding landscape.
98654: A humble man stands here, ready to help you with your things.

Shelves upon shelves adorn the walls of this library. Delicate oil lamps give the room a bright glow. There are books and scrolls scattered all over the house--on shelves, on tables, on the floor, even on most of the chairs. Some of the books seem to be quivering and vibrating slightly on their own, as though the magic contained within is trying to escape. A silver tea service has been left in the exact centre of a small occasional table, ready for its owner to take a rest from his labours. In one corner of the room, that gets little light, there is a mahogany liquor cabinet securely locked by ensorcellment and a devious mechanical catch. From time to, visitors to this place get a feeling that something is guarding the books here and it would be unwise to one of them without permission.
98657:
A stocky mountain mule is here, waiting to serve.
A domesticated pony, beast of burden to many, stands here.
A large rabbit looks peacefully at you, ready to dart away.

Small stones lie spread across the ground beneath the thin grass. A few bushes and even fewer trees have managed to grow up through the stony soil. Larger rocks can be occasionally seen. The grassy plains continue far to the south and west. A steep loosely covered hillside leads down to the east. It would be too dangerous to traverse.
98658:
A lone hawk soars high above you.
A mountain lioness pads quietly through the terrain.

Huge boulders line the stony paths leading through these hills. Brush grows thickly along the washed-out trails. Grasses grow softly beneath the shadows of the large rocks, perhaps safe from the stones collapse. The rim of a plateau can be seen circling around the hills to the west and south. Water has worn paths deeper into the hills to the east.
98659: A finely crafted crystal lamp is hanging from a tree branch.

This woodland trail is narrow but well-trodden. The earth is a rich, fertile shade of brown, spotted here and there with rounded grey stones. The border between trail and forest is sudden and distinct - rich colours dazzle the eyes as organic browns give way to the lush greens of the grasses and the pale blue of flowers. Whoever made this trail, which continues to the south, clearly intended to disturb the natural environment as little as possible.
98660: A small grasshopper clings to a blade of grass, ready to spring.

Dark grey rocks cover this bank of the great Anduin. Some of them lie in the shallow water, where the droppings of some birds colour their surfaces with lighter tones. The ancient trail follows the riverbed at a distance, bending at a few points to avoid some of the rocky areas. Towards the east, the dirt of the trail slowly becomes covered under a layer of scattered pebbles.
98661: A Pebble-strewn Trail at the Forestside

Tufts of hardy grass grow here and there on this ancient trail, trying to thrive in the hard-packed soil. A layer of white pebbles covers most of the trail making it hard for trees and bushes to take root in it. Some trees can be seen in the surroundings, but the way along the riverside fields here is free of obstacles; it could be the trail is as easy to travel as it ever was. Some animal paths lead from the river towards the forest in the southeast.
98662: Under the Eaves of a Dense Forest

A large elk is standing here, chewing grass and leaves.
An elk cow gazes coldly at you, chewing on a small branch.

A narrow dirt path, separating from the trail to the west, follows the border of a dense forest here. Tall trees rise above the path in the south, screening it with their reaching branches. Only some roots lie on the path, while tangled undergrowth and fallen trunks seem to dominate the parts deeper in the forest. Smooth grassland spreads out to the east past the wooded area.
98663:
A large elk is standing here, chewing grass and leaves.
A large elk gazes coldly at you, chewing on a small branch.

An incessant rumbling and drumming can be heard as turbulent waters crash into the rocks below. From this vantage point, the mighty Anduin River can be seen for miles, rapidly approaching from the north but then forced westwards by this raised terrain, before pushing on southwards once-more. A crisp fluvial scent drifts with the enduring zephyrs which are so common near the river.
98664: The occasional grinding squeak of smooth, water-worn stones can be heard while travelling along this path. The dirt here is hard-packed, indicating that at one stage, this was a frequently used trail. The dimmed roaring sounds of a great river can be heard from the northwest.
98666: Bend in the Great River Anduin

The river shimmers blue and is so clear nearer the riverbank, that the fine pebbles and underwater vegetation are visible beneath the transparent waters. Arcing westward, the river flows away from an impassable cliff to the east.
98667: Near the banks at this bend of the river, there are big gloomy rocks hiding in the rushing water. Where the flow of the water is swiftest, it looks very dangerous for small boats and rafts, while in the middle of the river the water looks dark and quite deep. Small whirls are moving quickly along the surface of the Great River there.
98668: At a Broken Raft in the River Anduin

The Anduin flows in from the east and continues westward. A number of wooden beams float in the river, gathered together in the middle of a whirlpool. The swirling water also plays with some ropes and splinters stuck between the nearby rocks, dragging everything around in an endless dance. All this looks like the remains of a big raft. To the west the river seems somewhat calmer.
98669: Dense Weeds in the River Anduin

Deeper and narrower than most parts of the Anduin, the riverbed bends past a small bluff in the south. Low grass is growing on it, adding to the smoothness of its outline. Dense green weeds float on the water, covering almost half of the river; their tiny pink blossoms sway gently above the surface.
98670: Swiftly the water, pure and clean, flows by. Just a barely noticeable green tone, caused by water plants, hinders the visibility through water. The riverbanks are grassy, with neither rocks nor sand covering them. They meet the surface of the water in a steep angle, making the riverbed seem quite deep nearby.
98671: Slowly ascending westwards, the meadow climbs up towards a grassy hillock. The green grass, with a slightly mossy cover, is full of various sparkling flowers and smaller bushes. The sight here is truly motley. Plains and grasslands continue in all directions.
98672: In Front of a Garden Gate

This plain is covered with an abundance of long thriving grass and some small shrubs and bushes. Here are no trails, but to the west a long wall of grey stones separates the plain from more cultivated land. A small wooden gate is set in the wall.
98673: This stretch of land is abandoned farmland. Dotted around are many traces of the former inhabitants, like old field enclosures and old cart tracks that are deeply cut into the soil and still not overgrown. The most prominent trace of former inhabitation are the dense hedges that prevent travel to the north and west.
98674: The grass grows long in this huge plain. A few shrubs and bushes provide shelter from the sometimes strong winds blowing over the plain land. Animal life seems to be rare, but there are a few tracks from small animals that can be hidden in the high grass.
98675: Between a stretch of ancient farmland to the west and a dense hedge of hazels to the east lies a strip of land that is easily recognisable as an old field. Some patches of the old crop can be found amidst the usual long grass. No bushes or shrubs have made their roots here.
98676: Like all the terrain between the Misty Mountains and the Anduin this area is a plain, flat land covered with grass. There is only grass visible all around. There is absolutely nothing interesting in the landscape that could catch an eye.
98677: Grass covers the land, with small dots of shrubs and bushes interrupting the monotony of the grassland, but there are no trees that could provide shade. Westwards the land begins to rise and form small hills. Southwards the bushes grow denser until a strong hedge makes further travel impossible.
98678: The plain grassland begins to change into soft sloped hills here. Between some of the small hills and north of a hazel bush hedge some traces of former inhabitation can be found. The stone foundation of a longhouse with a central heath and two sheds looks like a long abandoned farm. Grass has grown over the foundations.
98679: The way further south is blocked by a grey wall of fine set stones and to the east and west long rows of dense planted hazel bushes form impassable hedges. Once upon a time a similar hedge to the north made this grassy plain an enclosed corral, but there is a hole in it where once there was a gate.
98680: This brushland is a rather uncommon sight since the ground under the small, light bushes growing here is covered by a bumpy layer of velvety green moss. This layer extends over the fields with hardly any gaps or loose patches, indicating that large animals rarely stray from the few paths crossing this area. The fragile moss could easily be torn off, revealing the sandy soil below. The landscape descends slowly towards the river in the southeast.
98681: In the middle of this big plain of grass grows a huge lonely oak. Its trunk is enormous and its tree-top is thick with branches thicker than other trees trunks. This tree seems to be old enough to see the first elves arrive. South from the tree the mighty Anduin River flows with a strong current, its waves topped with small crowns of white foam.
98682: A large rabbit looks peacefully at you, ready to dart away.

Long grass covers the huge plain. Beautiful flowers including sword lilies, dandelions and marigolds grow among the grass. The earth is soft, dark and wet, it must be fertile. To the west a big tree towers over the plain land. Long weeds grow in the water of the Anduin to the south.
98683: Much of the rich green grass here has been cropped short by grazing animals who have nosed through the verdure, selecting only the most luscious leaves, grasses and other flora. Brush lines the base of a slope at the edge of the meadow and slowly gives way to clumps of sedge and sharp-leaved reeds on wet low ground. This leads down into a marshy inlet choked with tall reeds.
98684: Lush meadows of green-glossed grasses cover the ground. The land rises and falls slightly, like a green silk, caught by a gentle breeze. All around, tiny flowers provide embroidery for this vast, flourishing carpet. The air smells wet, the Anduin River flows not far to the southeast.
98685: A fat rabbit is here, chewing on some grass.

This is a slight depression in the land, which forms a very shallow but still perceptible valley. The verdant and plush grasses form a rich tapestry, which furls and unfurls as the land undulates all around. The small bowl is surrounded by variegated shades of green and yellow, grass, flowers and sky all merging into a prismatic feast for the eyes.
98686: A Tiny Streamlet in the Plains
A clear spring babbles as cool water trickles out of the ground.

The plains are full of plant life here. The grass is very long and is in intense green colour. Even a soft breeze will move it and create waves of rolling grass. A whispering murmur leads to a very small streamlet appearing under some stones. It flows east to join the great river Anduin.
98687: The earth of this plain land is thick, dark and wet. It must be fertile. The grass is very long here and many colourful flowers grow between them. From time to time old abandoned fields can be discovered where once settlers made this land a larder.
98688: A tall stag is here, grazing peacefully.

Like most of the land between the Anduin River to the east and the Misty Mountains to the west this area is flat and fertile. The vegetation consists of a huge variety of grasses and flowers, low shrubs and bushes. To the south there is a big tree. A dense hedge prevents travel to the west.
98689: The soil in this flatland is dark and wet. The ground is deep and very muddy, every move makes a sucking noise. Looking around, there is grassland in all directions. To the east the grass looks longer and greener, while to the far south a huge lonely tree is visible.
98690:
A carrot is lying here.
A carrot is lying here.
Some plump juicy grapes are growing here.

This land was once a well tended and very productive garden. Making full use of the fertile soil the gardeners grew many different plants, but today no one cares for the garden. A solid stone wall with a gate in the eastern wall protected the garden from unwelcome visitors and still gives a good protection against strong winds and grazing animals. In the protection of the wall some garden plants still grow and flourish.
98691: An elven waybread wrapped in a leaf has been left here (glows blue).

This is a small platform of woven branches and twigs, an elven-build talan with only one moveable wall to shelter it from the wind. The flet looks uninhabited, but not abandoned. A few provisions are stored at the foot of the moveable wall. A small ladder hidden in the hollow trunk of the tree allows departure from the flet.
98692:
An apple tree with bright green leaves grows here.
A large eagle soars above you.

A pattern of old hedges and knee-high stone walls covers this area. Old paths between the enclosures, the occasional growth of farm crops and an old fountain mark this land as a former farmland. Now the wild plant life slowly conquers the land back and covers the remains of civilisation with a green cloak.
98693: A Plain South of a Hedge

Along the northern border of this stretch of land grows an immense hedge of hazel bushes. Beside this hedge the land is covered by the typical brown grasses, some low bushes and small groups of tousled trees. Tracks of small animals show that the area is not totally deserted.
98694: Dense and long grass covers this land. The soil seems to be very fertile, but this plain lacks all plant life that needs deep roots. Only measly trees and a few bushes can be discovered. It looks like something in the ground prevents them from taking root.
98695: The land is flat. It is covered only by grass and a few patches of thin shrubs. Taking a closer look on the grass a great variety of grass species and tracks of small animals that probably hide in the high grass can be found.
98696: Some ugly blow-flies are buzzing around here.

The land here is fertile, but no one lives here to farm it. Everywhere grow sword lilies and other flowers dotting the long, rich grass. Further east the mighty Anduin River flows. A little slope leads to a small garden and to the north there is a small cabin built of logs.
98698: This broad landscape is sparsely adorned with thorny trees, many of which have had their succulent, nourishing lower leaves ravished - their bare branches indicate a healthy population of wild deer and similar grazers. Barring these few trees, the ground is wide and open and cloaked with tall, yellow grass. Strangely enough, the dry foliage in this region is evidently enough to support a wealth of wildlife.
98699: Here the tall hardy grasses of the plainsland in the west gradually give way to an increasing proliferation of bushes and shrubs, forming a dense blanket over the ground. Conversely, this region is considerably less colourful than the bright, green, flower-covered grasslands in the east.
98700: A Small Rise in the Plains
A large rabbit looks peacefully at you, ready to dart away.

This large treeless stretch of grassland reaches far in all directions and is enhanced by a spattering of many-coloured flowers. An earthy scent combines with the softness of the blades of grass to create a peaceful atmosphere. The mighty Anduin River flows south and east, making the plains fertile.
98701:
The remains of a thick tangle of vines lie here in a heap of rotting compost.
The remains of a thick tangle of vines lie here in a heap of rotting compost.

The ground is very soft and wet in this place. Tall brown reeds grow in dense patches. The great river must be very near, and it might be possible this area becomes flooded if the river swells in the spring or after strong rainfalls.
98702:
The corpse of a huge tarantula is lying here.
The corpse of a water spider is lying here.
The corpse of a water spider is lying here.
A dark chest covered in mildew and cobwebs lies here.

Staleness clings to the air as much as the thick layers of dirt cling to everything else in this small room. Shiny gossamer nets hang in the room's corners where their arachnid hosts may eagerly await tasty guests. The pungent odour of rotten plants and mud lingers here. The floor is covered with a thick layer of dirt and mud, broken by deep pools of dark water. A chest that looks much newer stands in one corner.
98703: A myriad of stems struggle to grow between the grey rocks, their leaves and flowers reaching desperately for the open air above. This natural, raised embankment affords a panoramic view of the surroundings. To the north, behind a deep gully, is a small rise and on the eastern and southern flanks, the Great River meanders ever onwards. A peaceful meadow flourishes in the west.
98704: Scattered about are the weathered remains of various tools. Probably once used to sift through the gravel and soil for gemstones, they have been long since abandoned. Over time, the mighty Anduin has deposited this alluvium here - fertile soil and a potential for gems that were released from their source rocks by aeons of erosion. The local grassland around this soil bed is of little interest, but to the west is a small rise in the endless plains.
98705:
Yellow flowers, with grey-green foliage, grow in clusters here.
A bee flies around here, collecting nectar from the flowers.

A profusion of colourful flowers seem to explode from the ground and attract a multitude of small insects. These colourful fields are home to countless creatures. Bursting buds offer themselves to the passing insects which visit each flower briefly before moving on.
98706: A tall stag is here, grazing peacefully.

This area began as a side loop of the river that swayed back and forth, as flowing water does when traversing open land. Eventually, the loop closed back on itself and filled, to form a small, shallow lake, which was isolated when the river changed course. Many plants thrive in this now-rich meadow, with water-loving bog plants nearer the river, where some stagnant water remains. The water of the lake gives off a slight swampy odour.
98707: A sturdy pack horse is standing here.

Loosely clustered upon the banks of the Anduin River, these trees are covered in rich, dark olive-green masses of foliage and overhang golden beds of marsh-marigolds, or, later in the year, the foamy banks of meadow-sweet and the magenta spikes of the loose-strife. Like all water-side plants, they retain their leaves longer than the deciduous trees of drier regions.
98708: In every direction, a ubiquity of green stretches to the edges of the horizon. The spongy grass is like a vast cushion, soothing to travel. Traversing these steppes is an interminable process due to the unchanging landscape. However, many creatures probably migrate through this area between seasons.
98709: A thin, hairy plant, with small, oval leaves, grows here.

The grassland lowers to the southeast where the mighty Anduin River flows. The nearby stream has its influence on the vegetation in this area. The ground is fertile. The grass grows very tall and has an intense green colour. Scattered over the plains are some groups of alders. Some miles to the north begins a forest, in all other directions is open land.
98710: The area is an endless expanse of arid terrain. The parched earth yearns to be quenched. Here and there a tenacious shrub clings to life. These rugged plants are few and far between, dotting the landscape.
98711: Scatterings of scraggy, grey trees are all that decorate this bleak, rocky terrain. Their gnarled, torrid branches are naked as if the broiling, merciless sun seared away all life. The whine of blood-drinking insects vibrates in the air, but there is usually enough of a breeze to keep them to a minimum.
98712: A small evergreen plant grows here, its woody stems reaching two feet.

A few square stone settings mark old patches where someone grew herbs, vegetables and flowers a long time ago. Missing the hands of a gardener the beds are overgrown by the grass now. A slope to the south leads to a flowered plain and the backside of a log-cabin. It seems to be in much better shape than the garden.
98713: The land between the Misty Mountains and the Anduin is covered by grasses and small bushes. It is fertile but lonely. Looking around there are traces of former inhabitants like overgrown fields and gardens. To the east a small structure in the endless grassland can be seen.
98715: A brown pond between old branches and roots is here.

This land looks like the surrounding area. It is covered by long grass and dotted with some small bushes. A group of trees that are larger than the average birches catches the eye and leads to a small pond of brown water in a dell. The banks of the pond are muddy and littered with rotten plant material. Some rotting wood is floating in the water too.
98717: Bushes, small groups of tousled birches and an abundance of different grasses cover the land and show its fertility. Despite the very rich soil there are no settlements, only grassland as far as one can see. A hedge blocks the way to the south.
98719: A beehive shaped stone structure crowns the top of a small hill in the grass plains. It looks ancient, but the hard stone is untouched by the ravages of time. The north side of the structure is covered with mosses. A tablet with a withered inscription is set in the stone wall there.
98731:
A large stone chest is here.
A large bat is here, hanging in the darkness.
A large bat is here, hanging in the darkness.
A large bat is here, hanging in the darkness.
A large bat is here, hanging in the darkness.
A bloodthirsty bat is sleeping here.
A bloodthirsty bat is sleeping here.

While the outside of the tomb is withered and dirty from bird droppings the inside is more richly decorated. The walls are panelled with slates of fine brown travertine. Bands of interwoven lines sculptured in the slates frame fine reliefs. A tessellated floor shows a hunting horn, a symbol related to the Vala Orome. Droppings of animals cover most of it.
98732: Long brown grasses cover most of this area. A few soft hills dot the land and provide some shelter from the winds. Hardy bushes and occasional birches grow in the few protected spots. A small stone structure stands on a hill to the south.
98733: Some ugly blow-flies are buzzing around here.

The plain looks borderless. Long thriving brown grass covers the land. When wind comes up, it bends and rolls in waves. There are no landmarks or traces of settlements with the notable exception of a sharp cliff edge that blocks travel northwards.
98734: The plains in this area are marked by numerous small rocks, stones which are scattered between the grass and some thin shrubs and bushes. The rocks and stones are withered by the forces of nature, the vegetation seems sickly. The lands north and south look more fertile. East are some ruins, to the west is plain land.
98735: A stonewall which has now many holes in it was once the border of a holy site. The shrine is a roofless ruin now. Only a corner of the building protecting the remains of the statue of a goddess can be recognised. The other walls were reduced to piles of stones by an unknown force. Grasses and mosses grow in the cracks between the stones. The place is surrounded by plains. An alley of trees leads northwards.
98736: Many flowers grow among the thriving grass that covers this plain. The grass is very long; it looks like the soil in this area is very fertile, although the area lacks larger plants like bushes or trees. The plain land continues in all directions.
98737: A tall stag is here, grazing peacefully.

The terrain changes from verdant green to a grey, dried out brown. The soil seems unable to support plant life. Only the hardiest mosses and weeds find a living in cracks of the ground. The lack of plants is made up by a surplus of bloodsucking insects that make this plain inhospitable.
98738: A sprawling green bush of stinging nettle grows here.

Brown and dry grass covers this land. Very few other plants grow between the reeds, and most of them are stinging nettles. The earth is hard and burnt. Some small knee-high stone walls, dried out trenches and the ruin of a fence show this land was once much more fertile, but an unknown force eroded it. Some ruined building that might be the relics of a farmhouse can be seen to the north.
98739: The corpse of a rattlesnake is lying here.

There is an abundance of plant life in this area, but there are no useful plants to find. Everywhere grow thorny bushes, and between them are patches of thistles and nettles. The place looks unfriendly and inhospitable.
98745: A Small Hut in the Plains

This small hut is built of logs, straw and earth. A small fireplace provides heating and makes this hut a comfortable shelter. A pile of tattered furs, obviously the bed of the inhabitant, is the only furniture here.
98748: The terrain changes from plains to woodland. The ground is flat, falling slightly towards the Anduin that must flow somewhere southeast. The trees are mostly oaks, but between the oaks some fruit-trees can be found. Some rotting poles show that parts of this forest were a fruit garden in the past. A deep, muddy gully blocks the way deeper into the forest northwards. To the east the gully continues, and behind it is a windfall that looks even harder to travel.
98749: Deserted Farm by the Edge of the Wood

A dark forest looms to the east of this old farm. Yet no one seems to be living here. The thatched roof has large holes, and the hinges have lost the grip of the door. On the yard the weeds have filled the flower beds. A tiny roof protects a well hole in the middle of the yard.
98750: This stretch of land is a huge, very flat plain. Covered by the long grass that is typical for the Anduin vale, it lacks all higher vegetation. Some small gullies, hidden in the high grass, could be natural or ruins of some sort of irrigation, as there is a ruined farm located to the east. A hedge of thorny bushes protects the area to the north.
98751: A squirrel scampers around here, looking for nuts from the trees.

This area is covered with rich plant life. It lacks big trees, but there are many shrubs and bushes that grow well in the dark, rich soil. Between the bushes is long, green grass. In the northern part of the area a few remains of fences indicate this green land was once used as pasture. An alley of trees can be seen in the west. A dark line at the horizon to the northeast could be a forest border.
98752: Two rows of poplars mark a stretch of land that was a well-travelled way a long time ago. Today the road is overgrown with grass. Some of the large trees have fallen, and some stumps mark where other trees stood. The path connected the now ruined settlement north with the shrine south. West of the poplar rows was once farmland; east of them are wide plains.
98753: Small walls and rotting wooden fences show this land was used to grow food. Irrigated by small trenches coming from a waterhole east of it, the farmland was very fertile. Without the caring hand of farmers the trenches have filled with mud and the fields were claimed back by nature. The grass that has overgrown the fields and pastures is very long and green.
98754: A duck is here, quacking happily.

The land forms a small dell which is filled by a waterhole. There is no running water that feeds the waterhole, but it looks deep enough to be fed by ground water. The hole is surrounded by steep slopes to the north and west and a crumbling cliff to the south.
98755: The soil of this land is too dry and sandy to support bushes or trees. The plant life is poor. Most of the land is covered by thin, dried out grass whose brown colour gives the area a monotone look. The steppes to the north look more arid, while the land south seems to be more fertile. The way east ends at a cliff edge over a waterhole.
98756: This stretch of land seems not to be fertile. The grass is brown and looks sickly. Patches of dry, brown soil can be found amidst the grass, as well of small islands of bare grey rocks. The land to the north seems to be very dry, while to the south it looks more fertile. To the east is an extremely dense hedgerow of thorny bushes.
98757: The naked rocks and the small patches of dried grass are covered by a reddish brown dust. Thick clouds of the red dust quickly rear up like angry spirits at the slightest gust of wind. Small thorny brush grows in cracks and crevices where the dust gathers providing some shelter for the few lizards and rodents that manage to survive here.
98758: A tall stag is here, grazing peacefully.

The pressure of the frequent howling winds and lack of rain for extended periods of time has left the ground devoid of all life. A few skeletal tree trunks, polished by the wind and the sand are the only signs that life ever existed here. Sharp rocks protruding through the dry soil make passing through the land difficult.
98759: The brown, dried grass barely manages to cover the ground. Stretches of jagged rocks and hard packed dirt where the wind has carried away the fertile soil lie like open sores across the plains. To the east the sores grow larger and more frequent.
98760: A large dangerous looking green snake is coiled up here.

A thick carpet of grass covers the gently rolling terrain. The green grass of the east however slowly turns drier and browner further west. Any wind will cause waves rippling through the tall grass like a stormy sea. A few rocky outcrops seem unnaturally still in the moving grass.
98762: The vegetation in this area shifts from brown grass to green. A few rises are covered with reddish heather. There are few rocks scattered over the grassland and the heathery hills providing shelter for insects and small animals. The plain continues in all directions, with some ruins visible to the south. A deep ditch, maybe an ancient drainage canal, to the east is too muddy to cross.
98763: A small cluster of clover grows here.

The terrain is marked by rows of gently rolling hills covered by tall, dense grass. The land is treeless, but a dark line on the eastern horizon could be a forest. No traces of settlements are in the immediate surroudings; only to the south of this grassland a few ruins can be spotted. The Anduin is in some distance to the southeast.
98764: Only the hardiest of grasses and the occasional stunted shrub manage to eke out an existence on the poor soil. Conditions seem to improve towards the east and south though, where a wider variety of grasses and weeds thrive. The layer of soil appears thicker there as well with fewer rocky crags emerging from the field of grass.
98765: Only the stone foundations of what was once a small, but prosperous village remains. The stone outlines of three large barns and a dozen of smaller buildings can be seen sticking up through the tall grass. The buildings were arrayed in a circle around a central yard, now swallowed by the surrounding grasslands. The most prominent feature of the settlement is the wide well at the centre of the yard.
98766: A few hardy tufts of short grass dot the otherwise hard and dry ground. Low stone fences mark the borders of once arable fields where wheat and rye was grown. A few stalks still stand between the grass. Traces of shallow ditches leading south suggests the fields were once irrigated. A high, strong hedge of thornbushes blocks the way west and gives a little shelter from the wind.
98767: A large rabbit looks peacefully at you, ready to dart away.

Atop a tiny hill sits the charred and blackened ruin of what was once a small manor. Once surrounded by a belt of beautiful orchards and farmland it is now the centre of dry badlands to the northeast, and grass covered plains in all other directions. The manor itself was burnt to a husk a long time ago and the erosion of wind and rain has slowly begun to wash the black off the scorched stone.
98768: This stretch of land was farmland in a long forgotten past. Today the small fields are overgrown by the typical long, brown grass. Stones and small trenches that marked the borders of the fields can still be found everywhere. The most prominent features are the strong hedges of thornbushes that protected the fields to the north and east.
98769:
A small vicious black rat squeaks at you for disturbing it.
A huge, hungry-looking rat is here.

A heavy blanket of dust covers a multitude of broken furniture and discarded household items, which clutter the room. Along the southern wall piles of broken crockery shows where shelves once stood, now long since rotted away. In a corner the remnants of a small campfire and a neat stack of splintered wood suggests travellers have sought shelter here in the past.
98770: A patch of moss grows here on a wet, flat stone.

Inside the well a faint glow can be detected from the fluorescent mosses and algae growing here. The moist, slippery walls are made out of granite bricks, expertly fitted together without mortar. Rusted iron rungs, placed a foot apart, provide a slippery way out of the well. The two feet of water at the bottom is cold and crystal clear.
98782: Boundless fields of unbroken green stretch forth in all directions. Though made up from several different types of grass they are all rather short giving the appearance of a well kept lawn. Only the outlines of a forest to the east and the silhouette of the Misty Mountains to the west break the monotony.
98784: A small rabbit glares angrily at you.

The plains here change to a dry moor. Heather covers the land, colouring it red-brown. Small drainage trenches show that once someone tried to change the moor into fields. A broad and very muddy trench to the west makes it impossible to go there. To the south is a hedge of dense bushes that looks like a field border.
98786: A small cluster of purplish-pink flowers lies here.

West of a dark forest lies a soft sloping moorland. Bushes of heather change with sandy spots and patches of brown grass. The sparse vegetation indicates that the soil is not very fertile. There are only little traces of larger animals, but numerous rabbit holes.
98787: The ground becomes more and more uneven and some big stones lie scattered around as if some giant had played with rocks out of boredom. Somewhere in the west are flattened fields where the stones have been removed with great effort and a small line is visible behind the rocks. The line turns out to be a hedge wall that is too high to jump over. It is grown of thousands of bushes with sharp, protruding thorns planted close to each other. To the south a similar hedge provides some shadow. Its rampant thorns and leaves and bits of small branches sticking out of the green and brown mass make the hedge an impenetrable obstacle.
98789: Huge old oaks with dense foliage are the most common trees in this forest, but some poplars and chestnuts grow between them. The trees branches and leaves form a dense roof that blocks most light, making it difficult for smaller plants to grow on the ground. The underwood is sparse with only a few ferns and some thorny shrubs at the forest borders. A huge windfall blocks all travel south.
98792: West and south from a dark oak forest, these plains are covered with dense grass. Clusters of bushes and small trees are scattered over the grassland. To the south some ruins, probably of a farm, can be seen. A huge windfall creates a barrier that prevents travel northwards.
98798: This is the border of a huge wood. It looks like that the trees that are lacking on the plain land to the west have gathered here to form a dark, hostile looking forest. Most of the trees are oaks with trunks that are more black than brown. The forest has grown wild, and obviously has never seen the caring hand of a forester.
98799: This woodland looks very ancient and dark. Formed by huge oak trees with wide-spread branches, it looks like nobody ventured in it before. The ground is covered by a thick carpet of rotting leaves and fallen branches. The smell of rotting plant material is in the air, adding to the unpleasant atmosphere of the forest.
98800:
There are two mushrooms here.
A bright red mushroom is growing here.
A huge black fungus is here, exuding a foul stench.

Deeper in the forest almost no light reaches the ground. The ancient oak trees loom dark and musty. The ground is soft from layers of fallen leaves rotting away. No brushwood is under the trees, but a few mushrooms grow on the gnarled roots.
98802: Some roots lie here waiting to ensnare weary travellers.

Ancient oak trees dominate in this forest. Fallen trees, stumps and roots make strolling around difficult. A few gaps in the dense ceiling of branches and leaves allow the sun to reach some spots on the ground. Bushes and vines grow in these spots. Windfalls to the south and west block the way.
98803: A dense roof of leaves and branches covers this place. The forest is formed by thick, old-looking oak trees with moss-covered trunks. There are very few smaller plants; it looks like the light that reaches the ground is not sufficient to support more plant life.
98805: This forest is very dark and musty. Most of the trees are ancient oaks with dark bark and thick roots. Dense underwood, fallen trunks and branches, and masses of rotting leaves cover the ground. A deep, dark hole is visible below the gnarled roots of an outstanding large oak. The forest continues in all directions.
98806: The forest stretches in all directions. It is very dark, almost lightless. The thick, ancient oak trees look strong and healthy. Their dense foliage blocks the sunlight, therefore the ground is covered only with ferns and rotting leaves. The air smells musty.
98807: In all directions there are trees. Fungi grow on the roots of the ancient oaks. The forest is very dark, the branches and the leaves form a green ceiling. The smell of rotten wood would be overwhelming, but usually there is enough of a soft breeze to carry fresher air from other parts of the forest.
98808: Dark oak trees form a dense and musty forest. Here, at the forest's border, the oak trees are mixed with other sorts of trees, like alders and elms. Under the trees is a dense underwood of bushes and berry shrubs. South and east of this place are open plains separating the forest from the Anduin River.
98809: Plains between a Forest and the River

Between a dark oak forest to the north and the mighty Anduin river to the south and east stretches a green meadowland. The grass grows tall. Groups of young trees provide some shelter. The riverbank to the south is steep; most animals seem to go east to drink out of the river. This pasture looks like a good hunting ground, and a rich tent to the west could belong to a hunter.
98810:
corpse (here) :
a pair of plain trousers (well-maintained)
a pair of rigid leather boots (well-maintained)
a plain shirt (satisfactory)
a plain silken sash

A long strip of plain silk lies here.
A rotten corpse is hanging here.

Large rugs and bear furs cover the ground inside this pavilion. The tent itself is made out of large canvas pieces sewn together. A large mast stands in the middle of the pavilion and several bracing wires and support poles help to keep the tent erect even in harsh weather conditions. To one side of the tent, below a vent, are the ashes of a campfire. Near it a table and a few chairs have been placed. To the other side of the pavilion stand a few crates and barrels, and there is a line stretched between two poles. In the back lies a warm-looking sleeping fur against one of the poles, and several cushions and blankets lie piled beside it.
