A corpse, rotting away in his clothes, hangs from the line, with a long slit through the throat.
98811: A clear spring babbles as cool water trickles out of the ground.

There is a small clearing located here between the river Anduin and dense, dark forests. The bushes and low trees on the riverbank, as well as the large forested area, offer a shelter from winds. An old place for campfires is still visible here, hinting at the past use of this place. Next to the campsite, there is a small spring bubbling out of the grassy ground.
98812: Dark woods continue to the north and west. Many large tree stumps lie all around here, looking as if they were cut down ages ago. Some of the stumps appear to be slightly loose. An especially large stump has some carved marks on it, slightly worn by age and weather conditions. A small clearing opens to the south, and a small, flat area of grass gently descends to the east, only to meet a distant river there.
98813: Between the Forest and the River

A flat, plain area of grass opens here, dividing a wide, forested area from the river Anduin. Strong, tall grass growth continues towards the water to the east. Only some small, dry, and mostly dead twigs lie between the densely growing and juicy blades of grass. The wide riverbed cuts through the plains to the east, slowly turning its course westwards.
98814: A dark tunnel ends here, to a strange, wooden pillar at the roof of the tunnel. The dark tunnel continues towards the east, hiding its secrets in the lurking darkness. The cavern floor consists of solid rock, on which thin streams of water run down to the east, making the mossy surface slippery. Some lichen grow on the walls of this narrow passage.
98815: The dense tops of trees block out all direct light from above. Huge branches around here could make a good hideout for anything, or anyone. The dense growth of trees and bushes completely blocks the way to the east. The dark, dense forest seems to continue towards all directions from here.
98816:
A small mushroom grows nearby.
A wooden chest stands in the corner.

Some old storage chests lie on the ground on a flat part of gently descending tunnel. The floor is covered with droppings of large animals, making the surface a mess. Strange carvings decorate the northern cavern wall here. The floor and the walls are overgrown by some weak moss, and a few small mushrooms grow in the shadows.
98817:
A skeleton of some humanoid lies in the dust.
An ancient fungus smothers the boulders.
A huge black fungus is here, exuding a foul stench.

A wet and mossy tunnel steeply rises to the west, offering no hold for climbing on its slippery surface. Small streams of clear water run down the slope. The bottom here is covered with fungi, moss and mushrooms, and large, sharp rocks peeking from below them. Some broken bones of a human skeleton lie on the ground, presenting the fate of an unfortunate adventurer.
98818: The plains by the river Anduin continue towards the north and the south. The grassy surface here is broken by small tufts of low bushes. A thick forest rises to the west. Huge trees and dense bushes block the access to it from here. The wide river to the east gently flows southwards.
98819: A sturdy pack horse is standing here.

A gently sloping sea of grass slightly descends to the east, only to end above the strong currents of the rapid river there. Small, stunted trees grow here, gaining in size and strength towards the west. Farther to the west, some old, large trees dominate the area, strangling the growth of all smaller plants.
98820:
The remains of a clump of roots lie here in a heap of rotting compost.
The remains of a massive tangle of roots lie here in a heap of rotting compost.
A very heavy branch is lying here on the ground.

Many great oaks tower high above with their thick trunks standing straight. Large roots slither on the ground, peeking from below a mass of leaves. These trees seem to be quite old and affected by weather. Some various sized branches, which fell down from above, decorate the ground. The dense forest continues to the southwest, while wide, open plains dominate the scenery to the east.
98821:
A big, brown, angry-looking bear is here.
A big, brown, angry-looking bear is here.

Under the dark forest opens an even darker cavern. The walls consist of earth, and only the roots of the large trees prevent this hole from cave-ins. The ground is covered with rotting plant material formed in comfortable sleeping places for the dangerous predators that seem to live here.
98822: Bend in the Great River Anduin

The Anduin is wide here, with its waters swollen. It approaches a marshy inlet to the west, where twelve-foot phragmite reeds reach up out of the murky waters, before winding southwards. Above the quagmire is a green lea.
98823: These tall trees, standing shoulder to shoulder like green sentinels, bent by the prevailing winds, seem to bow down in deference to the awesome might of the river. Their mossy, mottled branches droop down occasionally to caress its waters and they offer a small refuge of shade for the hot, tired traveller.
98824: The slopes of the knoll are sprinkled with flora of all kinds. The lush soil here shows hints of life everywhere. Small animals made their homes into these hillocks, as little holes can be seen which were dug into the ground. These fertile lands continue towards the north. A weak trail circulates around this higher area, approaching from the east and leaving to the south-west.
98825: A Pebble-strewn Trail across the Plains
A rabbit is here eyeing your presence warily.

The trail slithers through the plains and stretches from the west to the east. At this point, the course of this trail circulates around a low knoll, protecting the traveller from the winds of the open plains. At times, the path weakens and almost merges with the landscape. Tiny little pebbles cover the ground together with several boulders, most of them already partially covered with grass.
98826: The trail stretches here from the west to the north, where it suddenly makes a sharp bend, disappearing out of view. Some low bushes grow on the path, forcing the traveller to go around them. Some tall cherry bushes flourish to the east, offering a sheltered place for a rest.
98827: A meandering trail travels through the lush area here. The grass covering the sides of the narrow, muddy path is almost enshrouding the pathway from sight at some places. Slightly sloping plains border the trail to the north and the west, while the trail itself continues towards the east and the south.
98828: Yellow flowers, with grey-green foliage, grow in clusters here.

A great number of low, grass-covered hillocks irregularly rises from the ground like soft waves on the ocean. Some small tufts of various flowers and herbs can be found around here. Lush, green fields continue towards all directions, offering no visible change to the landscape.
98829: Lush grounds surround this area with an undying growth of florets, while fertile grass and a sea of various herbs colour the landscape here. To the west, the great river of Anduin rushes on its travelling course. A small tree sits on the bank of the great Anduin, bathed in the moisture of the river. A fertile plain seems to continue in the distance to the east and the south.
98830:
A large beautiful rose bush is blooming here.
A tall stag is here, grazing peacefully.

Various bushes grow here, being well-nurtured by the moisture of the river. Occasionally, leaves fall into the rippling stream, only to be carried away by the strong current. Some bare rock can be seen wherever the flooding waters have washed away the soil. Further away from the riverbed, strong, tall grass dominates the landscape.
98831:
A clear spring babbles as cool water trickles out of the ground.
A tall stag is here, grazing peacefully.

A translucent spring is welling up in the middle of the field, offering a good place to drink for various wild animals. Low bushes form an arch around it, as if trying to hide it with their evergreen leaves. Wild flowers grow here in abundance, adding colour to the scene. Thick grass covers the plains as far as the eye can see.
98832: A colourful butterfly is fluttering around here.

Dense, purple bushes of lavender cover the plains here, making it hard to travel through them. Small hummocks of dark green grass try to make their way to free air but are choked by the density of the bushes. More low bushes can be seen to the south, colouring the green plain with darker spots. The great river of Anduin runs by to the north and the west, increasing the humidity here.
98833: A colourful butterfly is fluttering around here.

The ground here is uneven from tussocks of thick, dark grass. Some small stones lie around, mostly buried under soil. From among the tussocks, a couple of flowers are striving on their way to open air. A gentle rise in the landscape offers an opportunity to eye the surroundings. A higher spot to the north seems to have a building on it, while endless plains continue towards all other directions.

A low, wooden shelter was built here, now partially collapsed and rotten. Its walls are made from thin, soft twigs which are tied together with small branches cut from the nearby bushes. The partially decayed structure can still offer good protection from what falls from the sky. The stakes of the shelter were made of soft wood which rot and time have partially destroyed already. A wide circle of stones is located in front of the shelter, still having some charred wood on it. Vast plains open to the east and the south, and a steep riverbank descends to the river Anduin to the west.
98835: A thick and tall layer of grass sways here constantly, forming a perfect green sea. The ground is a dry mixture of soil and sand, yet offering a fertile base for the grassy vegetation. No other growth is visible here, but some faint trails of wild animals can be spotted around. Green plains continue onwards in all directions from here.
98836: The dry soil here makes it impossible for anything to thrive. The broken and folded land extends to all directions. Some small tussocks of grey and yellow grass struggle here among a couple of sharp stones, partly buried deep under the hard surface. The ground seems to turn more fertile to all directions.
98837: A shrub with maple-like leaves is growing here.

The ground here is fairly even, moist soiled, darkish red, and quite lush. The grass covering it is short but strong. Some low, rust-hued bushes grow here in quite irregular forms, adding colour to the scenery. Eastwards, the ground becomes more arid, offering no good base for any growth there. Green fields open to all directions on the slightly undulating plains.
98838:
An orkish wolf-rider, wielding a lance, is here, riding a brown wolf.
A brown wolf is standing here, ridden by an orkish wolf-rider.

These arid plains do not have much to offer. The earth is brown and cracked by the dry air. Old footprints have dried into the ground, showing vague signs of life. Yellow and green vegetation stands out in contrast to the dry land. To the south, an odd shape in the scenery distinguishes itself from the surroundings, while the dry landscape continues towards the east.
98840: The dirt which forms the trail is barely visible below the tall grass. The path meanders from the east to the west, narrowing down and almost disappearing at times. Tall grass, shrubs, and various low bushes cover the area to the north, while a low grove of cherry bushes can be found nearby to the south.
98841:
Yellow flowers, with grey-green foliage, grow in clusters here.
A large shrub grows here, its branches loosely spreading.

A small grove has formed to a small depression in the ground here. Cherry shrubs grow all around, forming a nice shelter from wind and rain. Yellow and blue flowers grow on the rich ground. Fertile growth continues towards the east, while the gently sloping surface to the west and the north remains a green sea of grass. To the west, a vague trail slithers through the plains, turning to the north close by.
98842: A large thorny branched shrub is growing here.

The grass here is very weak and short, making some dense bushes stand out. These short bushes add a diverse set of colours to the plains here. Some faint paths of animals can be seen between the hedges. A small nest is built into the edge of one shrub. The slightly bushy area continues for a while towards the north, while the landscape to the east rises slightly, only to form an odd round shape.
98843: An apple tree with bright green leaves grows here.

A few, low hillocks rise from the ground here, forming a low, circular valley. In the middle of the depression, a lonely, small apple tree stands as a gracious opposite to the never-ending plains all around it. Tall grass around the tree strongly stretches upwards, almost hiding a small spring welling up nearby.
98844: Low bushes grow here, partially covering the small pathway. The places with tall grass and the weak growth of trees make it sometimes impossible to tell where the way runs. Above the plants, hilly fields can be seen stretching out to all directions. The path opens up to the east as the bushes become thinner.
98845: The top of this knoll offers a view over the surrounding plains. No other similar formations can be seen nearby. The surface is covered by thick grass, and a few small trees grow here, stretching their branches all around them. To the west, the vegetation thickens in the bushy area, while the weak form of a trail can be seen to the east, curving through the flat plains. A strange, quite rotten half of a large trunk lies on ground here.
98846: Low tunnels were dug into the side of a hillock. The walls are made of dirt, and the floor is covered with ankle-deep mud. The narrow tunnel continues towards the north, fading into darkness there. Some thin roots of vegetation above hang from the roof and the walls of the cavern. A few small bugs run around everywhere, making the walls seem to be alive.

A huge, venomous tarantula extends her legs to you.

A rotten corpse is hanging here.

The room is lit by one small torch on the wall. Dirt, filthy rags and garbage cover the floor here, while a strong stench of rotten food and mould fills the air. A wide crack from the floor to the ceiling is visible in the eastern wall. Some disgusting pieces of waste lie on ground, having strong marks of teeth on them. To the west, the light dims to total darkness.
98849: A large beautiful rose bush is blooming here.

Various types and sizes of bushes colour the flat, sandy ground here. The low, sandy area has enough soil on it for some grass to grow on it. Some slightly higher hummocks have more soil. There, some flowers and thicker grass guard the sandy and rocky ground around them. A few small holes were dug into these knolls. A wide river runs near to the west.
98850: Some small stones lie here, mostly buried under the soft, wet sand bordering a great river running by to the west. The shallow beach still continues far away from the riverbed. A few small pools of muddy water are here, being slowly absorbed by the sandy ground. The growth of some low bushes dominates the flat landscape to the south and east, while the area to the north becomes more dry and rocky.
98851: A dense carpet of blue flowers dip their heads in the breeze.

The rocky plain here is covered with some large boulders, lying among some smaller stones and pebbles. An especially large boulder lies here together with some smaller ones, creating a lone landmark on the plain. The ground under the pebble consists of a layer of rough gravel, offering no hold for any growth. The ground becomes more sandy to the south and rises slightly to the east, having a thin layer of soil with a weak growth of grass above the gravel.
98852: The low, rocky riverbank borders the great Anduin here. Various small plants grow on the ground at places where the stones offer space for them. The pebbles here are round, clearly shaped by rushing waters in the past. Some larger boulders lie on the ground to the south, while the rocky fields to the east continue flat.
98853: A fat rabbit is here, chewing on some grass.

A cruel, rocky field opens around here. The ground is dark brown, only allowing a few dying tussocks of yellow grass to vegetate it. Some sharp stones which lie there mostly buried under the dry ground, add some grey colour to the blasted landscape. The stony flat continues all the way towards the great river to the west, while the areas to the east and the south seem to turn more fertile.
98854: From here, the ground descends slightly in all directions. The flat plains continue as far as one can see. A group of large boulders has been piled on the dark, lifeless plain to the west. A few young trees sprout here, gaining their vitality from the dry and sandy ground. Short, partially yellow and brown grass colours the top of this elevation.
98855:
A clear spring babbles as cool water trickles out of the ground.
A lone hawk soars high above you.
A robin is here, carrying small pieces of wood to its nest.

A few large bushes decorate the banks of a tiny basin here. Thick, tall grass grows nearly everywhere, almost covering a small, gurgling spring. The grass becomes slightly shorter elsewhere on the flat area. The ground seems to be a fertile mixture of sand and damp soil. A slight elevation in the plains can be noticed to the north, while flat, grassy plains continue towards all other directions.
98856: The rabid rabbit is here, frothing at the mouth.

The soil here offers a fertile base for all kinds of plants. Thick, tall grass rises high from the ground. Various saplings of broad-leaved trees grow here, trying to gain height above the tall grass. Some thick bushes block the way to the west. Smooth, slightly undulating plains dominate the scenery around here.
98857: The flourishing lea here is filled with a wide range of different growth. Thick, strong grass covers the ground with its vital, green shade. A large selection of different herbs also grows here, adding colour to the flat ground with their blossoms. Smooth plains continue towards all directions from here.
98858:
Some small rocks have been piled into a mound here.
A fat rabbit is here, chewing on some grass.

Smooth, constantly swirling, tall grass creates the image of a wide area of green water here. The flat area turns into gently sloping plains to the east, while the growth thins out on the field to the west and turns into dry and broken lands. The form of an unusually tall tree decorates the view to the south.
98859: A tall pine tree grows here.

The low plains here are extraordinarily lush. Small tussocks cover the ground, making it hard to travel on it. A few shrubs struggle to gain in height under an unusually tall tree standing here. The top of the tree reaches towards the sky, while it stretches out its ramified branches. A faint trail slithers through the plains to the south.
98860: The brown, dusty path is wide and smooth at some spots, while it can barely be espied at some places below all the overgrowing plants. Tall grass also borders those clean parts of the trail, threatening to bury it completely. The trail turns from the east to the south here, while a lone hillock with bushy slopes rises to the west, blocking easy access there.
98861: Small bushes follow the path on both sides from the west to the north, partially hiding it below their growth. Dry, stony fields stretch all around this rather flat land, only having a few stunted bushes and dying grass growing on it. The trail continues towards the north where it curves eastwards through the plains.
98862: A hungry warg is standing here, ridden by Backdraft.

Small brown pebble covers the flat land here. Some grass growth has made its way through the rough soil, breaking the surface and allowing a few small bushes to root here. The grass grows stronger to the east and the west, where the ground gently rises. The dry area to the north is covered with tall but weak grass and several small bushes.
98863: A hungry warg is standing here, ridden by Backdraft.

The grass here is short and shifts in a range of yellow-brownish colours. The meagre vegetation is the result of the dry and thin soil. No trees grow within sight. The scenery slightly slopes towards a lower region north-west of here. The signs of wildlife are sparse, only some faint tracks on the ground imply that this vast grassland is not completely lifeless.
98864: A small grasshopper clings to a blade of grass, ready to spring.

The terrain slightly descends downwards to the west from here, but otherwise it lacks any outstanding features. The area, devoid of hills and ridges, was once flat land which seems to have been reshaped by the movement of water. The vegetation in this area mainly consists of waist-high grass, which gets its much needed moisture only from the occasional rainfalls.
98865: A tall stag is here, grazing peacefully.

As the trail makes a turn between the north and the west, it traverses the slope between the western lowlands and the higher land to the east. Despite the slope, the trampled earth still provides pretty good footing. A few bushes try to cover and hide the pebbly path here. Just close to the east, a large stone structure stands out against the grass-covered plains.
98866: A cockroach is scuttling across the floor carrying some debris.

The trail bends to the south and the east here, as if it was avoiding the cairn to the south-east. The trail is nothing more than a faint track in the dirt here with yellowish, dry grass growing several feet high on its sides. A lone figure of a large tree can be seen nearby to the west as a sole landmark on these unending fields of grass.
98867: The ground to the west slightly slopes downwards. What once was marshes and lakes has been turned into a flatland by now, vegetated by dry, yellow grass and patches of weed which have found their footing in the poor soil. To the north and the west, a wide plain stretches out, covered with yellow grass. South of here, a small, winding trail is barely visible between grass, weeds and low bushes.
98868: These gently sloping plains are covered with a thick, bold greenish layer of various grasses. No other growth can be found around. A few weak tracks can be seen where the grass has been walked on, giving a hint of rich wildlife around. The landscape continues towards all directions as a similar, slightly sloping plain.
98869: A coloured game bird is visible in the vegetation, watching you warily.

The surface here is slightly damp, obviously because of the pond close to the east. It replenishes the grass, giving it a bold green colour. A few shrubs and bushes in this area are also benefiting from the damp ground, while they serve as homes for a variety of wild birds and animals.
98870:
Yellow flowers, with grey-green foliage, grow in clusters here.
A badger is here, exploring for food.

A few bushes which appear in this area are a bit lower than their cousins around here. The layer of grass is thick and strangling all the other vegetation, as all other growth needs to have an endless fight for their living space. The endless plain seems to continue towards all directions from here.
98871: Much like the surrounding areas, grass and small weeds dominate this area. The scenery remains a flat, slightly undulating grassland. The landscape rises to the east, towards a slight elevation there. The grass is vital here, but it still clearly suffers from the lack of humidity.

98873:
Some thick writhing vines whip all around you.
A colourful butterfly is fluttering around here.

A few dry standing trees here lost their lives and are slowly starting to decay. The ground, like the trees, is very dry, cracked, and coloured by shades of brown. Thin, short grass covers the area thoroughly, making it hard to see the initial surface. Struggling vines hang down from dead branches of trees.
98874: The dying grass and weeds colour this area brown and yellow. However, some large, bare bushes seem to grow healthy here. A few partially rotten tree stumps are still visible, dried by the arid climate as desertification has not yet managed to strike its teeth to the area completely. Some low sand pits can be detected around.
98875: Some small rocks have been piled into a mound here.

The stunted vegetation here is badly rotten, dry and overgrown by some lichen. Shrubs, small trees, bushes - they all seem dead and far in the decomposition process. A small, muddy and smelly stream flows from the south, only to disappear in the damp, smelly soil. Further to the west, lush green fields open as an opposite to this contaminated land.

Some dark vapour rises from the water surface, emitting some heat to the surrounding area. The slippery sides of the pond mean that extra care must be taken here, lest one falls into the nauseating waters.
98877: Some faded remains of a path are still visible here. A few, partially overgrown and flat stones have been buried in the ground, once forming an inviting pathway. Now, a thick layer of grass and moss covers most of the stepping stones. Small piles of rocks can be seen nearby, mostly buried under tall weeds and low bushes. Flat, grassy plains open to the south and the west.
98878: A colourful butterfly is fluttering around here.

The even land continues towards all directions, not showing any distinguishing features to break off against the monotonous terrain. Knee-high grass covers the ground, shifting in different colours. Occasionally, some spots of taller weeds can be found scattered in the surroundings.
98879: The trail stretches to the east and the west through the lush grassland. As the terrain is fairly even and lacks any natural obstacles, the trail can maintain its course fairly straight. At some places, the trail is merely a small, dirty track, mostly trampled by animals and almost overgrown by grass and weed at parts. To the south from here, a large stone structure forms a distinguishable landmark. An almost completely overgrown path branches off from the trail, leading south towards the structure.
98880: A badger is here, exploring for food.

A large rock pile dominates the area. It stands out against the grass in solitude, being visible from several miles away in these flatlands. The cairn rises high from the ground level and looks as if it were climbable. A weak, dirty track meanders from the passing trail just to the north of here, ending in the front of a narrow opening between two large stone blocks. The end of the hollow opening fades into darkness inside the cairn.
98881: A brown fox is sleeping here.

The chamber inside the cairn is large enough to provide room for a few persons. The floor consists of trampled earth, and the solid stone walls are covered with moss and lichen. Earth and stones make up a waterproof ceiling, making this place a good shelter from forces of nature. The ground is littered with old, mostly broken equipment left behind by earlier visitors.
98882: A colourful butterfly is fluttering around here.

The cairn is skilfully built of stones and rocks of different sizes, making it easy to find a footing on the flat top of the structure. The top is a few feet wide and steeply descends to all other directions but the north. The elevated position gives an impressive view over the slightly undulating plain around.
98883: A hungry warg is standing here, ridden by Backdraft.

Dry grass unfolds in all directions along this flat highland section. The grass grows to the height of a foot and covers most of the ground together with some scattered patches of taller weeds. The plains continue slightly descending towards the east and the west.

An enormous pile of various sized rocks blocks the way to the north. A more open and fertile field opens to the east, while the area to the south remains dry.
98885: A hungry warg is standing here, ridden by Backdraft.

The terrain here sinks into a vast, natural bowl, looking very much like a dried-out lake or an old watering hole. In the middle of the depression, there grow tall, thick grass and green-leaved bushes. Unlike the meagre vegetation of the surrounding area, the grass here looks green and healthy. Several weak tracks of wild animals mark the soft ground, only to disappear into the small holes dug in the slopes.

98887: A hungry warg is standing here, ridden by Backdraft.

Vast, grass covered plains continue as far as the eye can see. When judging from the yellow-brownish colours, the land is dry, and rain is seldom in these lands.

To the north, a faint trail is barely discernible between the weeds.
98894: A hungry warg is standing here, ridden by Backdraft.

A small, winding trail meanders across the plains in a straight east-west course. The trail does not seem to be used frequently, as patches of weed have sprung up on the trampled path. At times, the trail is barely discernible as it loses itself in the waist-high yellow grass. The vast grassland which surrounds the trail looks rough and desolate.
98895:
A small and tough weed grows here.
A snake slithers towards you.
A hungry warg is standing here, ridden by Backdraft.

The ground is almost entirely covered with dry grass and tall weeds. The terrain is flat and lacks any distinguishing features. The dry grass reaches no more than a couple of feet from the ground and slightly shifts whenever a gust of wind touches it. Some scattered animal droppings and tracks reveal recent activity of wildlife.
98896: The ground here is mostly even, without any discernible forms of hills or ridges. The surface is dry and sandy and is not able to support more growth than this of weak grass and a few patches of weed which grow in the area. To the south, a weak trail can be seen running from the east to the west. The flat terrain stretches out to all directions, leaving the landscape without any noteworthy features.
98897: The trail continues towards the east and the west, twisting and turning between patches of yellowish grass on its course through the wide grasslands. At its wider sections, the trail is easy to travel on and wide enough for a small wagon, but occasionally, it narrows down to be no more than a small track in the dirt, and it is almost impossible to follow it. The growth bordering the path is trodden down at places, as some animals have been trudging their way through the grass.
98898:
A huge, black wolf is here, ready to devour.
A black wolf pads restlessly, looking for its next prey.

The path here runs meandering to the east and the west through the grass- covered fields. The slight depression in the ground following the path suggests that this trail has been quite well used in the past, although it seems long abandoned now. On both sides of the trail, the grassland stretches out as far as the eye can see. To the west of here, a round stone structure can be seen in a close distance.
98899:
A large thorny branched shrub is growing here.
On the shrub, there are two piles of blackberries.

The yellow, dry grass and weeds which cover the majority of the ground here grow no higher than a couple of feet. The flat terrain was once a moist and waterlogged grassland but has now dried out. The scenery consists of vast meadows now, stretching out to all directions. To the south, a meandering trail traverses through the flatland in a straight east-west course.
98900: On the ground, there lie some scattered chunks of an old headstone, shattered into pieces and mostly buried under soil or overgrown with moss and tall grasses. Some small cairns are piled around it, barely visible through the thick layer of vegetation. One large boulder rests on a few smaller stones. Parts of a collapsed stone fence can still be found around this place.
98901:
A pale figure of a battle-scarred man stands here.
A roe deer is standing here, watching the terrain while chewing the vegetation.

The vegetation in this area has a healthy green colour, revealing a hint at nutrients in the soil. Here and there, rowan trees sprout from old stumps which have already decayed to a large degree. The grass is lush and tall, hiding most details of the earthy surface. Open plains continue towards all directions without any visible landmarks.
98902:
A rabid rabbit is here, frothing at the mouth.
A badger is here, exploring for food.
A hungry warg is standing here, ridden by Backdraft.

As the first thing, a huge termite hill meets the eye. Obviously, these termites live from eating and destroying the decaying log wall to the west. From the termite hill, a thin, black line runs on the ground, as those small creatures pace around to get their meals. The ground around the termite hill is brown and barren, while lush, green grass grows all around it.
98903: An orchid of light violet petals blossoms nearby.

The lush ground blooms with an undying growth of florets, as some fertile herbs and tall grass colour the scenery. The ground under the vegetation is somewhat soft and humid. Widely open plains seem to continue towards the distances towards all directions from here, except to the north, where some unnatural form in the scenery can be seen.
98904:
A stone sarcophagus lies on the floor.
A spirit floats towards you and howls with an evil laughter.
A spirit floats towards you and howls with an evil laughter.

An ancient, well-made chamber used for burial purposes is carved to stone here. Everything is covered with thick dust, and cobwebs hang in every corner. In the middle of the room, there is a wide stone table, on which an ancient sarcophagus lies. It has some barely noticeable, engraved letters on its side. Otherwise, the room is free of furniture.
98905: A few struggling, thorny bushes lie here, fighting for their existence. The barren ground barely allows them to sink their roots into it. Some tussocks of yellow and brown grass is visible around. The landscape around is flat, and lacks all noticeable features.
98906:
A low shrub with bright green, oblong leaves is growing here.
Scattered in and on the shrub, there are two piles of blueberries.
A fat rabbit is here, chewing on some grass.

A pile of old stones and logs lies here as a memorial to past days. Rotting logs are still recognisable as a roof of an old building, now only waiting for time to wear them out. The ground around the debris is bald and solid, formed by a dry, thick layer of hardened soil. Only some brown vines climb up the pile.
98907: A fat rabbit is here, chewing on some grass.

At this spot, some unknown travellers have rested during their journeys, seeking shelter below the old walls rising to the east. A large place for fire was made next to the stone wall to the east, the stones still being blackened by ash of long decayed campfires. A few rotten and mostly decayed furs lie on the ground.
98908:
An apple tree with bright green leaves grows here.
On the tree's branches are three apples.

Some of the plants in this long abandoned garden are spread around, forming a thick bed of flowers on the ground. Some parts of old stone fences can still be seen around, mostly collapsed into piles of variously sized stones. Some rampant growing old apple trees grow here, their roots buried deep under the ancient stepping stones. Lush green fields open to all directions.
98909: A colourful butterfly is fluttering around here.

Tall grass dominates this area, rustling and bending whenever a gust of wind touches them. Some dry standing trees can be seen close to the west, while the area to the east looks somewhat reshaped. Only some small bushes grow here, as well as a few saplings of young rowan. The green field continues towards all directions.
98910:
A fat rabbit is here, chewing on some grass.
A boar cub is playing here, and exploring the wide world.

A narrow path here leads towards an abandoned barn to the east and continues towards the south, partially disappearing under the blooming growth. At some places, only a few low, piled cairns indicate where the path has once run. Some old rowan trees grow here, only accompanied by stunted growth of thorny bushes. The landscape is fertile here, allowing the grass grow to tall and healthy.
98911: A fat rabbit is here, chewing on some grass.

A wide and grass-covered area opens in front of an old building. A large, yet abandoned barn stands there, made of medium-sized logs. The time and weather have caused strong marks of decaying processes to appear on the walls. The door of the barn swings back and forth along gusts of wind. Some weak remains of a trail leave to the west from the door of the old barn.
98912:
Some small rocks have been piled into a mound here.
A fierce boar is here, making grunting noises.
A boar cub is playing here, and exploring the wide world.
A small boar with big yellow tusks looks eager to fight.
A hungry warg is standing here, ridden by Backdraft.

The overgrown path here is approaching a building to the south. Low, partially ruined stone fences rise on both sides of an old trail. Some wild bushes and even a few larger trees have grown up on the path, indicating the eternity it has been since the way was last used frequently. Lush, fertile grass fields open to the east, while further to the south, some old ruins can be seen.
98913: Endless plains open from behind the old building which blocks the way to the north. Some weeds and wild cereals thrive here, stealing all nutrients from the weak, infertile ground. A few low willow bushes and some young rowan trees grow here, yet unable to absorb enough energy from the ground to gain any strength or size.
98914: Some small rocks have been piled into a mound here.

This was once a secure place with heavy stone walls protecting the entrance to a small village. Now, the walls are mostly collapsed, and on the remaining parts, there grow moss and small trees. A few ancient, mostly ruined buildings are located south of here, forming blackened ghosts in this once harmonious place. Weak remains of a pathway leave to the north through a collapsed archway.
98915: A hungry warg is standing here, ridden by Backdraft.

Tall, strong grass dominates this area. A few small herb bushes grow here, adding some variation to the otherwise dull, even surface. Some faint animal paths lead across the grass bed. Far to the west, there loom some old remains of habitation as a lonely landmark on these flat fields. The plain area continues towards the horizon, and even past it.
98916: A small termite is running around making strange sounds.

This once enormous, welcoming building has been badly damaged over time. Lower parts of the walls are made of large boulders, and the higher part, or whatever is left of it, was made of huge logs. Now, the wood has mostly decayed, and stones on walls are blackened from fires blazing here in the past. A few rotten roof rafters lie on ground, overgrown by lichen.
98917: A depressing, chewed up central square is here, connecting a few more or less ruined buildings around it and a massive stone wall to the east. Small trees have broken the paved ground, lifting the cobblestones from their holes. An empty, dry fountain is here in the middle of the depredated area. To the north, the back of a building is badly blackened by fires in the past.
98918: A hungry warg is standing here, ridden by Backdraft.

A few old stepping stones lie on the ground, mostly covered with soil, rotten leaves and dust. The building itself consists of a stony basement and walls made of huge, already decaying logs. A large termite hill can be seen close to the south. Stunted grass grows around the area, allowing some low bushes to root on the barren ground. A wide, open plain opens around the building.
98919: A tiny spider is here, eating a tiny bug.

This barn used to be a shelter for animals. Now, it is a home for the termites, cockroaches and spiders. Nobody has used this place for ages; the inner walls are rotting, covered with lichen. Fusty, humid air stands still here, indicating the decay. A few bones of a large animal lie on ground, mostly stuck in the rotting wooden floor.
98920:
A large, dusty alcove sits in a wall, smelling of soot.
Some small rocks have been piled into a mound here.
Several shards of broken glass lie scattered about the ground.
A small grey mouse is sleeping here.

The remains of a large bed are here in one corner, completely decomposed but yet recognisable from its shape, even though it is hard to tell what is the bed, and what is the floor there. A small window in the stone wall is long broken, resulting in shards of glass lying on the floor. Some large holes in the roof reveal the decaying process going on here.
98921:
A large, dusty alcove sits in a wall, smelling of soot.
A small oaken table has been set here.
On the table, there is a spoon.

This small building, consisting of one large room, shows strange marks of habitation. A few musty duvets lie in a corner, still free of signs of decay. The roof of this building seems to be intact, protecting the room from the changes of weather. The hastily built door to the north is set up with a large bar which can be used to lock the door from inside. A sturdy obstacle to the south blocks the way through the narrow opening in the wall.
98928: The river Anduin flows here on a straight course from the north to the south. The whirling current is strong and tries to drown everything it can catch. The riverbanks are low and grassy, covered with a few small bushes growing on them. Far to the west, the shape of a large forest can be seen shadowing the horizon beyond a wide, grassy plain.
98929: The Wide Spot in the Anduin

The Anduin is wide and shallow here, revealing a bright and clear sand bottom. However, the current is very strong, dragging along everything it can catch. Some branches quietly float southwards with rapid speed. The low, grassy riverbank borders the riverbed to the west, while the riverbank to the east is higher, making landing there impossible.
98930: The river Anduin flows straight from the north to the south here. The riverbank to the east is a low and gently sloping beach of fine sand. The low, sandy area seems to continue further towards the east, still having trails of flowing water there. The western bank is higher, consisting of soil, rocks and small bushes.
98931: The river narrows into rapids, as its course sharply turns from the north to the west. The riverbank to the south is high and steep, covered with large, bald boulders which the force of water has washed clean of all soil. Some large bushes fill the bank to the east, leaving only some openings to show a hint of the vastness of the open plains behind them.
98932: The great Anduin makes a wide turn from the east to the south here, being rather calm but still strong by its current. The low riverbanks are covered with man-sized rushes and a few young trees trying to sprout on the inner bank of the bend. A grassy plain opens to the north and the west.
98933: The great river turns from the north to the west here, while the strong current causes some backwaters to form. The riverbanks to the south and the east are high and steep, making the riverbed run through a low pass between plains. A few young willows and alders grow on the banks, only waiting for the next season of floods to wash them away.
98934: The river Anduin makes a bend here, flowing from the east to the south. Some small rocks and larger boulders cover the riverbanks. Some litter is alternately appearing and disappearing in the backwaters which the current forms at a few spots. Open, grassy plains with only some bushes growing on them open behind the riverbanks to the north and the west. A kind of a large forest darkens the horizon in the north-east.
98935: Leaves and other litter slowly float down the strongly flowing stream, fallen down into the river somewhere in the distance. A single, large boulder stands in the middle of the river, splitting it in two. To the south, a few trees hover above the riverbank, while the area to the east is covered with some low bushes.
98936: Conflicting currents produce odd pockets of calmness and furious churning everywhere else. Enormous boulders here and there within the waters add to this effect. Around them, the water splashes violently up into the air before rejoining the flow. The tumultuous waters of the Anduin surge southwards.
98937: This powerful river continues onwards, inexorably. The waters are muddy brown and thick with soil, loose reeds, driftwood and branches that it has collected from riverbanks on its tremendous journey. The fast current carries the dirt southwards. Around some stones that are too big to be washed away the current forms small foaming waves.
98938: Bend in the Anduin by a Cliff

The Anduin River's course is diverted around a section of land to the south, where a cliff blocks its path and is battered at futilely by the raging, indignant waters. Above stands a grove of trees, their branches drooping low over the face of the small cliff, sometimes touching the waters that spray up. In the right season, they even reach the surface waters, when the river is higher and filled by the rains of pregnant clouds.
98939: The water here is foamy after crashing into the cliffs visible to the east. Meandering steadily southwest, the mighty Anduin deposits much of its load of silt just west of here in an alluvial bed. From there on the waters appear much clearer. When sunlight or moonlight hits the water it sparkles like dark silk covered with diamonds.
98945: Bend in the River Anduin below a Trail

There appears to be a trail above the southern cliff, here, but no details can be made out from this angle. The river flows slowly past the grove to the east, but picks up speed greatly as it rushes down toward the cliff and explodes against it, producing a deafening roar.
98946: The fresh waters of the Anduin begin to calm here, with the rapids left behind in the east. To the west, a rocky embankment ushers the majestic, royal blue river to the south, away from the alluvial beds of the north - and the shame of its previously dirty, silt-saturated state.
98947:
A doorkeep stands here ready to obey his master's wishes.
A tall and strong guard is here.
A tall and strong guard is here.
A sturdy pack horse is standing here.

A sturdy wooden ladder rests here attached to the wall, ready to be moved into position to allow an easy climb down to the old study below. Pictures hang on the wall here, painted recently. A nice little carpet lies on the ground, blazing with bright colours of blue and red.
98948: A large stone fireplace with a roaring fire warms the room.

Plantlife sits here along the sides of this room, lit by the sun during the day. Large plates of glass mix in with the wooden ceiling allowing rays of sun to warm the room throughout the day. There's a small ladder leading down into the bedroom.
98949:
A large bookshelf sits against the wall.
A sturdy bed made from solid oak lies here, covered in warm blankets.
The Housekeeper looks fed up with her job. She scowls at you unhappily.
A sturdy pack horse is standing here.

You find yourself inside a small room surrounded by walls of a blue colour. The air is fresh and clean and the bedroom is brightly lit. Along the wall is a wooden desk with a bookshelf beside it, free of dust.
99000: A humble man stands here, ready to help you with your things.

Along the path to the fields, travellers often find this humble garden awaits them inviting those who pass near to sit down and relax. Often times a gentle breeze passes through causing the flowers and grass sway softly. The sound of birds singing quitely high in the trees and fluttering of butterflies and buzzing of bees are also common sights and sounds as they fly among the Alfirn. The whole place seems to have been designed to create a soothing ambience. This garden is clearly filled with the magic of its elven caretakers.
99001:
A well-crafted white fountain is here, water pouring forth from it.
A doorwarden stands here ready to obey his master's wishes.
Staub the Dwarf, wielding the Axe of Durin, is standing here.
There is a dazzling display of magic in this room. All around the fountain there are balls of fire, ice and lightning flying around or flashing in and out of existence. Nice trick...
99002: Staub the Dwarf, wielding the Axe of Durin, is standing here.

The walls of this room are covered with bookshelves, some of which seem to have been burned recently. Inspecting a bit closer, the only thing that appears unscathed is the huge table, covered with stacks of scrolls and books, in the middle of the room. This has to be the room where the mistress of the house works on her new spells. Maybe not the safest place to be...
99003: Room does damage to players over time ("The unnatural cold bites into your skin.").

A large stone chest is here.
A stone statue of a bear looks very lively.

This room has the shape of a beehive, and its six walls are decorated in a honeycomb pattern. In the centre of the chamber a huge, richly decorated stone chest is set. Everything is covered by a fine film of ice crystals. The air in this crypt is extremely cold.
99004:
A musty loaf of bread has been left here.
A musty loaf of bread has been left here.
A small barrel stands on the ground.
A small vicious black rat squeaks at you for disturbing it.

This tiny chamber was created to an excavation inside the cairn. The cleverly hidden entrance shows that this room was built with the intention to keep it concealed. The ceiling arches low, forming a durable roof for this room. Some old, musty supply items are still lying here, waiting for decay to destroy them.
99008: A mighty wight-noble is watching you.

The hall, about thirty yards by thirty yards, seems to be a collection point for sacrifices. Littered all about the stonefloor are skeletons and pieces of ragged clothes, rusted armours and dented weapons. The eastern exit is adorned with a large portal while the western exit is framed with golden glowing sculptures of snakes. North there is a small underground beach.
99009:
A copper penny lies on the ground.
A stocky mountain mule is here, waiting to serve.

This is a small room, painted all in white, with grey runes on all the walls. A small portal leads eastwards, and the western exit is framed with golden glowing sculptures of snakes. A veil of shadows conceils what is hidden behind the exits.
99010:
A small campfire burns here, its low flames giving off only a little light.
Bulg (pukespy), wielding a great warsword, is standing here.
Drazud (freshmeat), holding a black metal staff, is sleeping here.
Gaakt, wielding a black runed dagger, is standing here.

A swift stream of cold water passes by following its course eastwards. There is no space to stand on either side of the water, except here on the craggy beach. The water flows quickly and moving west upstreams is impossible, although it is shallow enough to allow travel downstreams without a boat or raft. A large hall extends south of here, a part of an old underground system.
99020: The field is big and full of grass. Sometimes it is even hard to walk. All around it is silent and you can feel some animals hiding from you. Like everything in the Shire this place is quite peaceful.
99021: The field is quite large and filled with grass. Sometimes it is even hard to walk. All around it is silent, and you can feel some animals hiding from you as you draw near. Like everything in the Shire, this place is quite peaceful.
99022: The fields here are furrowed and healthy vegetables grow in them. North the natural fields continue, but a fence prevents you from going there. East the cultivated fields continue.
99023: A duck is here, quacking happily.

The field is big and full of grass. Sometimes it is even hard to walk. All around it is silent and you can feel some animals hiding from you. Like everything in the Shire this place is quite peaceful.
99024:
A sturdy pack horse is standing here.
A duck is here, quacking happily.
The field is big and full of grass. Sometime it is even hard to walk. All around it is silent and you can feel some animals hiding from you. Like everything in the Shire this place is quite peaceful.
99025: A Bounder is here, patrolling the Shire and watching for evil.

You are now behind the house. This is a large yard, almost a field, where the grass doesn't grow quite well. On the ground you can see some implements for cultivation. To the south, you see The Water flowing quietly.
99026: A Bounder is here, patrolling the Shire and watching for evil.

Here is where the farmer comes when he is taking a rest along with his workers. On a tiny table you can see some tools and the remainder of a recent meal. Through the small, round windows... you can see the fields.
99027: A Bounder is here, patrolling the Shire and watching for evil.
The fields here are furrowed and healthy vegetables grow in them. A fence prevents anyone from entering from the east, and leads right up to the river, which flows quietly to the south.
99028:
A dark green cabbage is growing here.
There are two turnips here.
A small evergreen plant grows here, its woody stems reaching two feet.
A hobbit farmer is here, thinking about seeds and vegetables.

Here, you can see a little house, in whose yard you are now. Everything seems quite small for any race, except hobbits. Around you, you can see vegetables growing healthily. The house is rather poor, so you think it could be just a room for tools and implements.
99104:
An uruk of the Morgundul tribe is here commanding his soldiers.
An orc-guard of the Morgundul is on patrol here.

Colossal stalagmites stand like guardians while stalactites loom ominously overhead, lending a distinct feeling of being within the jaws of some prodigious, sinister creature. Scintillating crystal formations sparkle when light catches them, bringing the ordinary rocks to life - like flowers do in grassy fields. In the middle of the cave is a rude camp, just some dirty mats around an old fireplace.
99105: Fluorescent moss on the walls emits a faint light, bathing the tunnel with an eerie green glow. This illuminated passage winds and eventually begins to curve sharply northwards, leading into a large cavern. A freshwater spring is here, trickling and collecting where the water has eroded a small basin in the rock. Innumerable bones litter the floor near the cavern's entrance.
99106:
A raft has been left here.
A canoe has been left here.

The cave has numerous small, dark ponds that were probably filled by water finding its way in during times when the river swelled. Some of the walls are a little moist, encouraging growths of moss. Water drips from the ceiling and echoes across the cave. This, combined with the muted cacophony of the river pounding against the cliffs, produces a watery orchestra.
99107: A snaga orc stares at you with interest.

These small intersections are nearly the only signs by which to orientate yourself in these confusingly similar grey tunnels. Smoke from fires has made the ceiling black with soot, indicating that the passage has been in use for many years. Corridors branch in all quarters except west.
99108: The corpse of an orkish nurse is lying here.

Scalps and other mutilated trophies of reckless intruders decorate the walls of the intersection, which divides into a network of tunnels. The floor is covered with neatly placed grey tiles, much too well-laid to have been built by orkish hands. Time and much passage has worn them, but the original pattern is still very evident.
99109: Above a gigantic natural fissure extends, the sky barely visible a long way above. Among all the fallen rock debris some paths north and west have been cleared to ease movement, but elsewhere it is a slow clamber over countless stones. The walls bear signs of merciless tools, parts of the rock having been crudely hacked away without much skill.
99113:
There is a lot of water on the ground.
A rock lizard is here, motionless as it observes you.

Here, far above the plains west of you, a chilly wind blows through the thin air. It is extremely hard to travel here and the rocks and boulders strewn on the steep mountain side forces you to move slowly. The mountain peaks still loom far above you east of here.
99114: Path on the Slope of the Misty Mountains

A Dunlending huntsman is here.
A pack horse (Rood) is standing here, ridden by you.

This tiny path is twisting through the high slopes of the Misty Mountains, across ridges and through valleys. It is surrounded by low birches and bushes, moss growing only a couple of yards up their stems. Rocks and large boulders are strewn everywhere, sometimes causing the path itself to change direction.
99129: There are several directions to chose from at this junction in the river bluff walk. The walk curves a bit to the north, aiming travellers toward a decaying structure. To the east one can ascend an aged causeway over the bluff. The sound of river water beckons to the south and this scenic walk continues upward. A plethora of choices in which one can walk in the long ago forgotten footsteps of this once grand city's residents. There is a sticky substance covering the ground to the north.
99150: A snowy-white egret stands here alertly.

Five rectangular stone pillars coming out of the water look to be part of an ancient pier. A sixth pillar must have existed at some point but it is gone now, either crumbled or washed away. It is easy to imagine planks of wood running between these stones creating an S-shape landing stretching out over the river.
99151:
A blooming water-lily floats on the surface of the water.
A large pike is lurking in the mud by the bottom.
A large pike is lurking in the mud by the bottom.

A long metal chain with links so strong they have withstood the centuries extends from a stone column into the depths of the river. Several other stone columns extend out in a line several feet into the river. The various water stages of the river have left their marks on the columns by eroding and discolouring the granite. One can imagine that in the past the citizens of this ancient city docked their ships in this safe river harbour.
99152:
A snowy-white egret stands here alertly.
A sturdy pack horse is standing here.

A few stone posts and some badly rusted chains are all that is left of this abandoned pier. So old is the chain, one good tug from a small child would surely loosen several links. Much of the bluff has eroded over the centuries leaving some portions totally surrounded by water. Each time the river rises much of the southern section of this area floods leaving everything here knee-deep under water.
99183:
Yellow flowers, with grey-green foliage, grow in clusters here.
Some delicious wild strawberries grow on the ground.
A cute rabbit is here.

Nestling in the lee of a small hillock to the east, this quiet hollow is quite sheltered, and fed by the waters of the nearby river its fertile soil is carpeted by thick grass and wildflowers. A faint trail can barely be discerned among the lush vegetation, but it seems that someone often travels north and south through this area.
99265: This forest must be one of the last remnants of a far greater woodland, which once covered all Minhiriath, before the devastating deforestations by the men of Numenor, who sought wood for their shipwrights, and to build their haven at Lond Daer, far away on the coast. Tall and ancient trees completely surround you, their long branches forming a leafy canopy overhead, but it seems that to the north, the woodland thins out somewhat.
99266:
A cluster of dark green, feathery fronds flourishes in the shade.
A beautiful and docile horse is standing here.
A nightingale is here, chirping a sweet melody.
A nightingale is here, chirping a sweet melody.
A huge, black wolf is here, ready to devour.

This forest must be one of the last remnants of a far greater woodland, which once covered all Minhiriath, before the devastating deforestations by the men of Numenor, who sought wood for their shipwrights, and to build their haven at Lond Daer, far away on the coast. Tall and ancient trees completely surround you, their long branches forming a leafy canopy overhead, and amid the dense, knotted tangle of underbrush, any pathway is rapidly swallowed up, making it a difficult task indeed to find a way through the woods.
99267:
A cluster of dark green, feathery fronds flourishes in the shade.
Some thick writhing vines whip all around you.
A sturdy guardsman is here, his weapon at the ready.

This forest must be one of the last remnants of a far greater woodland, which once covered all Minhiriath, before the devastating deforestations by the men of Numenor, who sought wood for their shipwrights, and to build their haven at Lond Daer, far away on the coast. Tall and ancient trees completely surround you, their long branches forming a leafy canopy overhead, and amid the dense, knotted tangle of underbrush, any pathway is rapidly swallowed up, making it a difficult task indeed to find a way through the woods.
99268: This forest must be one of the last remnants of a far greater woodland, which once covered all Minhiriath, before the devastating deforestations by the men of Numenor, who sought wood for their shipwrights, and to build their haven at Lond Daer, far away on the coast. Tall and ancient trees completely surround you, their long branches forming a leafy canopy overhead, but it seems that to the south, the woodland thins out somewhat.
99269:
A cluster of dark green, feathery fronds flourishes in the shade.
A domesticated pony, beast of burden to many, stands here.
A bear is here, covered with coarse black fur.
An old, yet beautiful woman looks piercingly at you.
A nightingale is here, chirping a sweet melody.

This forest must be one of the last remnants of a far greater woodland, which once covered all Minhiriath, before the devastating deforestations by the men of Numenor, who sought wood for their shipwrights, and to build their haven at Lond Daer, far away on the coast. Tall and ancient trees completely surround you, their long branches forming a leafy canopy overhead, and amid the dense, knotted tangle of underbrush, any pathway is rapidly swallowed up, making it a difficult task indeed to find a way through the woods.
99270:
A cluster of dark green, feathery fronds flourishes in the shade.
A tree-snake lies wrapped around one of the tree branches.
A huge, black wolf is here, ready to devour.

99278:
A cluster of dark green, feathery fronds flourishes in the shade.
There are two piles of pine nuts here.
Furdul (FF) is here, riding a trained horse.

A few scattered trees mark the border of a forest, which stretches north from here, rapidly thickening. Though thinly spread, the trees here are old and gnarled, yet still strong and healthy. Perhaps this is one of the few remnants of the massive forests which once covered the lands, before they were laid bare to provide wood for the mighty Numenorean fleets.
99279:
A large beautiful rose bush is blooming here.
Deep inside the bush, there are two red roses with leaves and thorny stems.

An old stone well stands at the centre of a small glade of trees. In contrast to the ancient woodland north of here, these trees seem to have been planted and cultivated on purpose, though they appear to have been left untended for many years, judging by the thick weeds which have sprung up around them. The well itself is surrounded by a broad pathway of heavy stone paving, but even this is in a poor state of repair, with many of the blocks cracked and weeds poking up between them.
99289: At the Top of a Small Hillock

This small hill rises only a little above the height of the surrounding lands, but it nonetheless offers a commanding view of the countryside, as the terrain is low and flat in all directions. A small river flows by to the east of here, its waters keeping the land lush and fertile, and further in the distance a wide road can be seen.
99290: Sparkling Waters of a Small River

A bass swims here.
A fat carp swims here.

The river is surrounded by leafy bushes and weeds, which plunge some of their stalks and branches low, creating small whirling eddies in the current. The water here is deep, but very clear, so that it is still possible to see the riverbed, but further to the east the river grows wider and shallower, with large rocks and boulders breaking the surface of the water, creating waves and small sections of whitewater.
99313:
Farmer Black is standing here, looking very angry and crazed.
A small, loyal beagle is here, eager to please.

Perhaps this was once a much-used path, but now it is cracked and over- grown with weeds. Loose stones are scattered about, and it is hard to tell for certain where the path ends, and the garden begins. And the garden itself, lying to either side of the trail, is also choked with rough weeds, apparently not tended to in many months. Even the barn to the north, to which the pathway leads, stands in a state of disrepair.
99326: The waters of the Glanduin have made a kind of flooded valley here. The land is not overused by the small animals here and is not very comfortable to walk across.
99327: This area of the valley is much more peaceful than the expanses of lush vegetation filled with excited birds and other wildlife. The river is almost still here. The water seems to be used by animals for refreshment and it is perfectly clear and looks quite safe to drink.
99328: Under the Bridge across the Hoarwell

A bass swims here.
A salmon swims here.
A salmon swims here.
A bass swims here.
A salmon swims here.

The river Hoarwell flows under a worn wooden bridge, that casts a thick shade on the water. The river itself flows from the north to the south at a steady pace and the sounds of two great rivers mixing their waters comes from the east.
99341: A low stone-walled passage leads northward from the river into the levee which carries the old dwarven road. Its floor is awash with mud, slime, and river water; soft, scaleless living things brush past your feet.
99342: A little stone lies on the ground.

This stone passage formerly carried the waters of a stream through the levee supporting the elevated road. Something has blocked the culvert at the north end, however, leaving it dry. Silent, isolated, thirty feet beneath the solid stones of the ancient pavement, and completely black, the empty passage seems untenanted except by small animals who have left their tracks here and there in the dried mud on the floor.
99343: A heron is stalking the area, looking for fish.

Here the Forglanduin is a broad, shallow expanse, with exposed gravel bars running parallel to the east-west current. Clumps of grass have sprung up from some of the higher mounds of sand. To the north, standing on stone columns forty feet tall, an ancient causeway carries the Road of the Smiths.
99350: A green frog is here, hopping around.

Here in the permanent shadow of the ancient causeway is a long dark expanse of apparently lifeless mud and earth. The smell of decaying leaves fills the blackness. On the outside of the columns, nearest the light of the rising and setting sun, the stone is covered with a thin blanket of moss.
99351: A large rabbit looks peacefully at you, ready to dart away.

This ancient stone road follows the outside of a bend in the Glanduin here as it curves from the south to the west. The road is elevated a few feet above the surrounding flat, moist terrain here. In the cracks between the stone, grasses and weeds have begun to sprout. Built five thousand years ago and more, today it is nearly unused.
99352: A fallow deer is grazing peacefully here.

Here the ground is moist and fertile; tall grass and leafy bushes grow thickly, and some great old oak trees stand in clumps. In the daytime songbirds might be heard twittering in their branches. A small stream trickles out of the rocks to the east, winding about and emptying into the fens to the north.
99368:
A holly bush with dark green leaves is growing here.
Partly covered by the bush's green leaves, there are two piles of inkberries.
A diamond-back rattlesnake is coiled here, ready to strike.
A small brown snake is slithering around here.
A black raven flies in the sky searching for flesh to prey upon.

Small bushes eke out a meagre existence on this patch of barren ground. Thorny vines intertwined among the thin brown branches of the bushes make the thought of trampling them an undesirable option. The ground is cracked and parched in some places, a good indication that this area either does not receive much moisture or that it does not retain it well.
99383: A giant rat patters against you, squeaking maliciously.

You find yourself amid a stand of thorny bushes which tear your clothes and skin as you try to wade through it. It is at times so thick and dense that you wonder whether you will become stuck in it. But, fortunately, your constant pain pays off as your limbs move you, albeit slow and painfully, through this sea of thorns.
99384: You find yourself amid a stand of thorny bushes which tear your clothes and skin as you try to wade through it. It is at times so thick and dense that you wonder whether you will become stuck in it. But, fortunately, your constant pain pays off as your limbs move you, albeit slow and painfully, through this sea of thorns.
99388: This is the valley of a small, muddy stream, the banks of which have become so overgrown with a jungle of thorny bushes and vines that the walls of vegetation have met overhead to form a ceiling of interlaced canes and creepers. There is no direct sunlight here at all; when it is noon outside and above, it is twilight here. The streambed is flat and stony; otherwise thornbushes would be growing everywhere, and this vacuity would not exist. The water trickles mournfully from pool to pool.
99390: This is a long, stone-vaulted passage, now sunk hip-deep in sand and peaty mud, leading under the East Road and carrying a trickle of water southward. The roof-stones seem sturdy, but trickles of water leak around them here and there, and pale dribbles of lime have solidified as dirty, fragile stalactites. Strange footprints can be seen in the mud - almost human, yet smaller, and clawed.
99412: Here the battered reminants of the road twist north and west, retreating from a stand of spiney bushes and dark gnarled trees. You hear no sounds of birds besides those of carrion birds circling constantly above and you see no animal but only insects which attack your skin and attempt to blight your food and water. A sense of foreboding washes over you and you wonder if you will ever leave this barren place.
99414: You can now walk with ease on this nice path. At last, you feel a nice wind blowing in your hair. You can smell the fine perfume of the flowering bushes growing next to you; a sensation of freedom fills your body. Isn't life beautiful?
99415: As a trustworthy companion, the trail follows the hedge closely in every small twist and turn. Like an elder brother the hedge guides the trail west and east towards bree and the lands beyond Weathertop. South of here lie bleak sandy plains, the south downs.
99416: South of here is the eastern end of the barren lands called the south downs, a long stretch of sand where few living creatures and plants will be found. The earth around here is more hard soil, brown and cracked. The hedge grows fairly thin a few yards north of here, with large burnt areas for some reason.
99417: A worm is here slithering around.

This is where the downs seem to end. You can see the hedge far north, while the hilly, sandy plains stretch out to the west. The snakes and worms around this place are not exactly the sort of company most people prefer, and the area seems desolate and uninhabited.
99418: Around here the downs are somewhat sandy and hilly, with bleached grass growing in sparse tufts. Small traces on the ground gives evidence of snakes that inhabit the area, dousing on the small flat rocks on hot sunny days.
99419: It is difficult to walk here, as the thick black mud underfoot grabs and holds feet, and the reeds -- some more than an inch in diameter -- press close on every side. To the north, the stand of reeds becomes even more tangled, while in every other direction they gradually peter out into the standard vegetation of the marsh.
99436:
A neekerbreeker is standing here.
A frog is standing here.

The frequent stretches of deep mud and black ponds makes it impossible to travel in a given direction with any certainty. On all sides the marshes reign unchallenged, providing a home to ravenous hordes of biting and stinging insects, who in turn sustain a huge population of frogs and other less familiar predators.

A stocky mountain mule is here, waiting to serve.
The reeds in this area are dense almost beyond belief. Each step requires a huge effort to clear a path, and after passage the resilient reeds spring back as if no one had been there at all.
99460: The reeds press in on all sides, obscuring vision in every direction. The ground is covered with a foot of black water, and below the water, thick mud sucks at each footstep. Occasionally the incessant hum of the insects is broken by the splash of something falling into the water.
99461: A sturdy pack horse is standing here.

The soil in this dense stand of sedges is very moist, but not so much that it sticks to boots. All around the buzzing of hordes of insects fills the air. To the south a thick blanket of mist covers the ground, but in every other direction the marsh continues.
99462: This is a dense stand of sedges mixed with various species of marsh plants. The noise of multitudes of insects is omnipresent -- a constant reminder of why this place was called the Midgewater.
99471: A swarm of mosquitoes is here, humming around you.

In every direction, the marshes continue unchallenged. It is nearly impos- sible to move consistently in a given direction, as every few feet some obstacle or another presents itself. Here the primary obstruction are dense impassable growths of sedges that cluster together on may small islets.
99503: Much of the open water here is covered with green algae that hides the murky depths beneath. The odour of marsh gas and rotten vegetation is prominent, and the smell seems to cling to everything. The black mud has the consistency of thick soup, and care must be taken not to step into the sporadic deep pockets of it.
99507:
A sturdy pack horse is standing here.
A sturdy pack horse is standing here.
A stocky mountain mule is here, waiting to serve.

Deep pockets of mud and frequent stretches of murky water make travel here an arduous ordeal. Each step must be taken with care, for who knows how far one may sink into the muck. The incessant droning of throngs of insects cannot drown out the occasional splash of some larger creature taking to the water.

Travel through this area forces a difficult choice on the wanderer -- whether to slog through the murky water or to fight through the tangled knots of sedges that completely cover every inch of exposed land. The hordes of insects that fill the air gleefully dive at every bit of skin left uncovered, inflicting annoying bites and stings.

There are two woody, stemmed plants here.
A clear spring babbles as cool water trickles out of the ground.
A domesticated pony, beast of burden to many, stands here.
A black snake hurries towards you with sly intentions.

You are standing in front of a small lodge to the south. North is the river Bruinen, hidden behind a grassy slope. Another slope, to the west, leads to a high plateau overlooking the surroundings. To the east, you see a hill.
99912: A wolf cub happily plays here.

A rather steep grassy slope carries you up to some high cliffs extending north, over the river. You can reach the riverside by going down, to the east. From the south, you hear the sound of water running in a small spring in front of a wooden lodge.
99936: There are two handfuls of clover here.

You are standing in the middle of a grassy sea. Vast plains stretches in all directions, and you see nothing exciting anywhere. Only to the east, something disturbs the flat view - the Misty Mountains towering over the world, hiding it's secrets.
99965:
A small cluster of clover grows here.
A small cluster of clover grows here.

Rocks fill these plains, and make it very hard to move. To the east, you see a black hole, extending into a hill. Dare you enter to check what that snoring sound comes from? Turning to the south, you notice a small, nearly overgrown trail leading east and west. West and north is nothing but vast plains.
99972: What is this? You have found a very dark and narrow tunnel leading east. You suddenly notice that you have no possibility what so ever to turn back west - the only way to go seems to be on. Making your weapon ready for any unexpected encounters, you crawl on...
99973: You have found a small hill, not reachable from any direction except the small tunnel to the west. Something gives you a feeling that this place had better be left undisturbed. As you look around, to see what the origin of that particular feeling is, you see a small stone standing on the hill. Thick bushes and rocks stops you from moving north, east and south.
100047: A hobbit is here walking around.

You are on the only path to Dwaling, which stretches straight east-west for some distance. The path is not too wide, but old criss-cross tracks of wheels and hooves suggest it is well-used. On the two sides of the path, the vast grassland and undulating hills create a scenic contrast.

100468: Narrow Path in the Woody End
A black wolf pads restlessly, looking for its next prey.

You stand on a narrow path going through the forest, or around it. You could not figure out which it was. Oaks, beeches and other great trees border the path. Old fallen branches lay on the ground. Now and again you notice something in the corner of your eye, however, when you turn or look you notice nothing.
100523: You have entered a clearing between the woody path and the forest. The grass has had the chance to grow tall here and the place has its own atmosphere. The peacefulness of the place is sometimes bothered by animal bellows from the eastern woods. Otherwise there is nothing else here, but you can see some ruins to the south.
100524: A gnarled and crouching old orc is here, his head hung low.

This chamber is filled with shackles, irons, vices and other equally cruel torture devices. Dried stains of blood give the floor a marbled look. A foul stench can be felt from an opening leading to a cave below.
100525: A hungry warg stands here, sniffing around for flesh.
This is the strangely decorated sleeping chamber of Golfimbul. A huge bed made from bones is placed against the northern wall of this smelly cave.
100526: This cave seems to have been abandoned for years. The air is stale and heavy; dust has settled everywhere. In the corners, where old bones were thrown, mould has grown thickly and then died for lack of nourishment.
100527: A gnarled and crouching old orc is here, his head hung low.

The owner of this cave has been gone for a long time, though his servant has waited timidly for him to return. Other orcs have pillaged the place, however, and there is nothing of value here... just a few scraps of skin lying around, with some writing on them.
100528: This tunnel must have one time been completely filled with water. Though there is still a large amount of water passing through here now, it does not reach the top of the passage, thus allowing for some breathing room.
