The entire passage consists of smooth rock, undoubtedly molded by water. Rushing water leads west towards what seems to be the outside, however there appears to be a steep drop in that direction.
100529: A Side Tunnel in the Cavern

This tunnel emerges from the eastern end of the cavern to the west, and suddenly bends to the south. It is clear that this tunnel is not natural: it looks as if it was axed into the mountain with brute force. The ceiling is much taller and rougher to the south than to the west; gravel and boulders are piled along the tunnel walls.
100530: This circle-shaped cave is old but not natural. Many toolmarks and other imperfections from the making of it can be seen all around. The ceiling is high, and though the cave is likely not of the making of skilled mountain dwarves, it is spacious and should be able to fit the purpose it was meant for. In the eastern part of the cave stand two stone tables of different sizes and behind them a small furnace made of dark stone.
100532: The trail here bends east on its way to the Mountains, skirting the Bruinen moors to the south and riding the eastern end of a rolling expanse of heath to the north.
100537: You are wandering in the heath, a rolling expanse of country covered with earth golden underbrush. The land gently rises and falls, smoothed and rippled by the west wind carrying precious moisture from the Bruinen to all the life that inhabit this heath under the unbounded sky.
100581: A domesticated pony, beast of burden to many, stands here.

A small stream flowing eastward flows under an old wooden bridge here. Although there are a few mossy corners where perpetual shade reigns, the space under the bridge is breezy and well lit when the sun or moon is in the sky. The stream, which is easily waded, flows gently over old grey rounded rocks and makes a musical sound as it trickles toward the sea.
100582: This is the mouth of a small forest stream which joins the great Lhun here. It is shallow enough to wade, but the banks are steep. Westwards one can see the outline of a bridge. The trees grow closer together to the east, casting a dark shadow on the ground below them.
100639: A blue dragonfly is circling around.

The golden forest stretches out in all directions except to the east, where it gives way to a mixed forest of elm trees, oaks, ashes and rowans. In that direction the trees are mostly brown, green and grey, but the glow of the Golden Wood lies about them like the merry firelight from a hearth lit during a feast in an elven hall.
100782: On the Top of a Hill
A copper penny lies on the ground.

You find yourself on the top of a hill. The ground seen barren here. You try to look through the misty air, but all you see is the shapes of the other hills, looking like huge, ancient, grazing creatures.
100806: On the Top of a Hill

You find yourself on the top of a hill. The ground seems barren here. You try to look through the misty air, but all you see is the shapes of the other hills, looking like huge, ancient, grazing creatures.
100807: The grasslands end here, but stretch out to the north and east. The south and west boundaries of the fields here are made by a cracked road as it follows a river to its south. The evidence of some farm animal, possibly sheep, lies all around with criss-crossed tracks and spoor.
100835:
A small termite is running around making strange sounds.
A small termite is running around making strange sounds.
A small termite is running around making strange sounds.
A small termite is running around making strange sounds.

This cavern appears to be home to various small insects. Here and there in the dirt, a dead beetle or a squirming maggot can be noticed. The dirty cavern descends further, but one could only guess what is at its end. There is a tiny animal skull lying on the floor of the cavern, stripped completely bare.
100836: The corpse of a giant termite is lying here.

Silence hangs in this cave like an ever present gloom as all noise seems muffled and absorbed by the earthen walls. No draft of fresh air is felt in this dark place, yet a passage seems to ascend towards the surface through another, smaller cavern. Flecks of stripped bone dot this cave's dirt floor like mosaic tiling.
100838: A large stone door is set into the eastern wall of this blackened cave. Marks of charcoal and dried blood can be seen on the walls and floor. A round opening to the north leads to a downwards sloping tunnel. A sharp, strong smell makes the atmosphere thick in here. A stonedoor is set in the eastern wall, and high above it a large, dark hole leads into the darkness.
100878: The passage, or what remains of it, runs east-west here, ending with an arched door to the east. Once it had been quite wide and high, with ornamented walls and curved ceiling, but now the destruction looks as complete as if the hills themselves finally brought their wrath down on those who dared to disturb their rest. Somebody has cleaned the rubble just enough to make it possible to pass, but there is no telling when the walls or the roof might collapse again.
100901:
A sprawling green bush of stinging nettle grows here.
A bright green holly bush is growing here.
Partly covered by the bush's green leaves, there are three piles of hollyberries.

The ground here is slightly inclined, rising as it travels to the west. Although a layer of grass covers much of the ground, the dominant vegetation is definitely the many types of bushes and shrubs growing everywhere. Holly bushes grow close to patches of nettles, creating an intricate maze which can easily leave a traveller lost and scratched. Portions of the ground under the brush is bare earth, worn down by animals seeking shelter for the night.
100921: Inside a Dark and Damp Cave

The corpse of a huge millipede is lying here.
The corpse of a huge millipede is lying here.
The corpse of a huge millipede is lying here.
The remains of a large puffball lie here in a heap of rotting compost.

The river's surging against the rock outside causes large and continuous waves of sound to echo around this rocky void. As if that were not unsettling enough, the roof is pierced through with tangled roots and the floor and walls are rough with cracks and crevices. Anything could be lying in the dark, waiting to feast on whatever creatures happen to stray in here.
100922: At the Back of the Cave
A large bulbous puffball is pulsating slightly.

This is the back of the cave. The sound of the river is less loud here and the air less moisture-laden. Yet tree roots seem to penetrate every crack from every wall, giving many dark nooks and crannies. It seems that things are constantly moving in peripheral vision. Who knows what is hiding and lurking in this dark hole.
100923: A Deep Alcove in the Cave
A huge millipede is writhing around here.

The cave seems to extend no further than this. The darkness here is total and permanent, outside the direct line of the cave entrance. The moist walls are covered with twisted roots and the floor is damp and rough, giving plenty of opportunities for creatures of the dark to hide.
100980: An albino fish is swimming here, looking for some food.

This large cave has two sections, the western half here is dominated by a large pool of water running from the west wall to a stone dock on the edge of the stone floor in the eastern cave. The roof and walls of the cave are all made of dark blocks of stone with the cracks filled by mortar. The floor of this part of the cave might also be artificial but it lies too far below the surface of the pool to see.
100981:
A skeleton of some humanoid lies in the dust.
A giant trained dog is here.
An outcast hunter is here.

Dark stone blocks that have been fitted together closely make up the floor, roof and walls here. This part of the large cave is full of the remains of shelves, barrels, and other commonly used methods of storing materials. The wood has decayed and rotted in the moist air over time. The edge of a large pool of water lies on the west edge of this section of the cave. In the east wall is an area about the size of a door that has filled with debris from what might be a collapsed tunnel beyond.
100982:
A colourful butterfly is fluttering around here.
A small grasshopper clings to a blade of grass, ready to spring.

The living pressure of the River Bruinen has gnawed away at the countryside and formed this calm basin adjacent to the river. The slower water makes it a popular place for the animals of the land to gather and drink. The water is murky from the settling mud brought down from the water to the north; the murky colour makes it impossible to tell what could be found deep within its depths.
100983: Sharp Bend in the Tributary River

The river bends sharply here as it flows from the east to the north. White foam and bubbles can be seen in the swift water. Branches and other flotsam float along the western edge of the river. All the flotsam is heavily damaged or broken into small pieces.
101062:
An experienced husky smuggler is here, plotting his illicit ventures.
An experienced husky smuggler is here, plotting his illicit ventures.
A sturdy bandit bodyguard stands here, eager to hack you to pieces.
A sturdy bandit bodyguard stands here, eager to hack you to pieces.
The chief of smugglers is here, planning his next move.

A soft, dim light fills this cavern, casting dancing shadows on the dirt and litter, which are spread all over the floor. In the centre of the room, the ashes of a large fire remain, within a ragged circle of stones, and next to this stands a crude but functional table, surrounded by eight wooden chairs. Along the south and west walls, a few niches have been cut out of the hard stone, to offer more secluded sleeping places for the occupants of this cave.
101063: A clear spring babbles as cool water trickles out of the ground.

The faint trail you have been following ends here in a small valley, and you can only travel back to the east. At the end of the valley a small mountain spring wells from between two rocks, and drips slowly into a pool of water, ice cold and crystal clear. To the east of here a large hill rises above the rest, and from there, you could probably get a good view of the surrounding country- side.
101064: A brown fox is here, looking for some rabbits to chew up.

A faint grassy trail leads onward through the upland, rising and falling with the rolling hills. From here, little of the surrounding country can be seen, as the trail has found its way into a small grassy hollow, which nestles deep between the surrounding hilltops. However, at least this coomb offers some shelter from the unrelenting winds.
101065:
A woolly sheep is grazing here.
A woolly sheep is grazing here.

It is hard to imagine anyone living in these high hills, and yet just east of here, a small, ramshackle, wooden building can be seen. A rough trail through the grass leads to the doorway, suggesting that this area still sees regular travel. Far to the north, the silver ribbon of the Nen Kalthar winds gently east and south across the land.
101108:
An elven hunting-spear is on the ground.
A large wooden wall shield rests on the ground.
Several silver coins lie scattered about here.

This is a small chamber, only a few paces across in either direction, but much has been stored here. Some paintings hang upon the walls, and a fine statue stands in the far corner. A massive piece, this statue dominates the room, with its big sword and a shield with the head of a lion in the middle, it is indeed a shame that this is all but part of a sculpture, and not an ornate set of armour, which would lend style to any warrior.
101109:
A small campfire burns here, its low flames giving off only a little light.
Lhurank (brenny), wielding a darkened orkish axe, is standing here.

Dry air fills the cellar and dust rises from the floor as you step on it. Still it looks less decayed than the ruins on the surface, like some invisible hand would have been fixing it up every now and then. Surely the wooden pillars by the western wall have been just recently put there to keep the roof up.
101110: The tunnel has been smoothly carved into the sandy soil and the flat rocks on the sides keep the walls and roof up, along with a few wooden support pillars. North end of the tunnel is blocked with a metal door, painted to look like a stone. In the west the tunnels descend down to some wider space.
101112: A large boulder is here, it must be heavy.

The cave comes to an end here, leaving the only obvious exit out the tunnel in the east wall. It might also be safer to stay there, since the wall here has crumbled down in places, and probably will not take many years until the whole cave comes down.
101142: The mountains here are rocky and irregular, and boulders and ledges protrude at odd angles all over. It is on one of these ledges that you now stand. To the south and east, the mountainside steepens into a sheer, impassable cliff. A small trail winds its way to the west and to the north.
101143: Here the trail hugs the mountainside. Your path is straight, but you can only see half a mile or so in the mists that begin to rise. You sense a subtle change as the trail rises almost imperceptibly.
101144: A weapons rack stands against the wall.

This storage basement has somehow survived the destruction of the fort, although the opened chests and broken weaponry scattered everywhere show that this place was ransacked long ago. Small cells open in the north wall, although their bars and rusted locks now lie on the ground, half covered in thick dust and debris. The last steps of the stairs that once led to the upper rooms peek from under a pile of stones - that passage is now almost completely obstructed. To the east a large tunnel descends into darkness.
101145: A large passage follows the wall westwards and rises steeply, blocking your view of what lies further on. In the past the passage continued to the east also, but now it ends abruptly at a wall of fallen rubble. A thick layer of dust rises in clouds at your passage, showing the time that has passed since this place was held by the Witch-king. A door leads out of the tunnel to the north, probably used in ages past to sally against the flank of the enemy.
101155:
A rock lizard is here, motionless as it observes you.
A hungry warg (Rood) is standing here, ridden by you.

The broken ivy-clad walls and ruined watchtower tells you that here stood a fort. It was erected on this corner of the hills during the long siege by the Witch-king, probably to quarter his troops and watch the moors against a sudden sortie. Nothing blocks your view for many miles over the moors and the path which runs east-west just north of you. It is difficult to walk through the ruins, because of the piles of stones that are scattered everywhere, sticking out of the brush now covering the top of the hill.
101156:
A spirit floats towards you and howls with an evil laughter.
A spirit floats towards you and howls with an evil laughter.
A trained horse (Rood) is standing here.

The walls of the chamber are covered with a black-green moss which seems to suck up all sound and light. The grey stone flagging on the floor is chill under your feet and is covered by bone fragments. The air currents swirl sluggishly around you in strange patterns, it feels as if the crypt has a mind of its own. Set in a niche in the south wall is an ancient coffin with its lid cracked open, it exudes an evil aura.
101262: The path slopes downward quickly into a large pit filled with loose rocks and gravel. Smoke rises from a tunnel in the mountainside, only to be dispersed by the cool mountain air. Broken tools and scraps of cloth litter the area, along with some bones.
101281: Loose rock is all over the corridor, carried from the ore pits and quarries from the east, up a sloping tunnel and into a great slag pit. The cold mountain winds whistle here, howling eerily up and down the mineshafts.
101282: A swift and agile forest cat moves silently through the vegetation.

The land slopes upward from south to north, gradually at first then rising steeply into dim highlands. Trees huddle somewhat close together all along the incline, thinning slowly to the south and west. The earth is rocky and in the main barren; only a few hardy weeds and lichens find a home among the broken stones.
101283:
A pile of firewood is here, ready to be lit.
An orkish soldier is here, patrolling the area.
An orkish soldier is here, patrolling the area.
An orkish soldier is here, patrolling the area.
An orkish soldier is here, patrolling the area.
An orc sentry is here on patrol.

A black tent has been hastily erected on this windy plateau. All vegetation has been trampled and destroyed, and the ground is littered with all manner of animal remains. Together these have formed an unsavoury morass which makes your footing slippery and leaves a foetid odour which even the brisk breeze cannot completely dispel.
101284:
A small campfire burns here, its low flames giving off only a little light.
A scuffed and worn leather satchel has been left here.

The roof of the tent dips low to one side, suggesting that it is either in a poor state of repair or has been erected carelessly. The ground upon which it stands has been trampled and despoiled, but a few badly-tanned furs, which have been tossed into one corner, offer a place to rest. The bones of small game animals are scattered about, stripped of even the smallest shred of meat.
101288:
A toad is standing here.
A brook trout is here, swimming in the current.
A frog is standing here.
A large beaver is here, gnawing on a piece of wood.

Here the bit of water from the Sirannon joins a smaller river on its long bend towards the south. The water seems to rejoice at the thought of more company along the way. The stream coming from the north is probably no more than some snowmelt from the mountains, but even so it dwarfs the amount currently flowing in the riverbed. The river must have been dammed upstream, as there is hardly a trickle in the streambed that should be carrying a decent volume.
101290: A finch flies low above the ground.

The evident lack of nutrients has left the shrubs weak and twisted at this place. On the ground, more rocks than soil can be seen, and the fine layer of dust that lies atop shifts in occasional breezes. A low, lonely tree can be seen on a small incline. Large rocks surround it in a nearly perfect semicircular shape as if specifically placed there, and surprisingly dense bushes grow close by.
101292: A cramped tunnel opens into a small cavity. In its corners, there lie straw and moss, placed as primitive resting quarters. In the centre, there is a rather large hatch, covering a hole or a tunnel leading down. Sounds from the lands outside only pass through the thick brush-walls as dampened whispers. The air could be fresh, but a scent of blood and depreciating flesh lies above the smell of leaves and wood.
101293:
A huge, smoking campfire is burning here.
A hungry warg stands here, sniffing around for flesh.
An orc-guard of the Morgundul is on patrol here.
An orc-guard of the Morgundul is on patrol here.
A very muscular orc with a cruel and dominant gaze in her cold eyes is here.

The smell of rotting meat and blood becomes more intensive further down in the hole. A cave with numerous holes and cavities in the walls has been dug here by removing the scarce supply of soil and dirt, uncovering a natural cave with walls of rock. Bones and rotting corpses have been hung in one of the holes in the rear wall, while the others are filled with straw. Next to the biggest hole, a table and a kind of throne have been built from heavy branches and long bones.
101296: Behind the rocks is this little room. Nothing seems to have been here and you seem to be the first to disturb its resting. You might as well leave here or take a small break, after getting past that snake you deserve a break. This is nothing more than a natural hole in the wall of the cave where nothing seems to go. It is of very little interest.
101297: Back in here there seems to be a cave that goes on further, the light from beyond is dimming and it is hard to know what might be back there, more of the snakes could be laying in there waiting for you to come along. Rustling can be heard in the distance, a cool breeze from inside penetrates you. It is not a lovely place to visit, but traveling in there seems possible.
101298: This part of the cave seems to make it's way to a larger more comfortable cave, beyond it grows narrow. There is no light in here, just the cool feel of the breeze hitting your neck as you move along, and the wet feel of the water dripping on your head from the cave ceiling above. Slime grows along the walls and it is easy to see why in this atmosphere.
101299: A small passageway is here, moving along it is difficult. It is growing narrower and narrower as you move along it. Going down to your hands and knees seems to be the only way to move along it now. Trying to fight in here against the things crawling around here would be impossible. You are better off leaving here and moving along, even trying to concentrate in here is difficult as you feel slimy things crawling along your hands.
101300: Back in here there seems to be a cave that goes on further, the light from beyond is dimming and it is hard to know what might be back there, more of the snakes could be laying in there waiting for you to come along. Rustling can be heard in the distance, a cool breeze from inside penetrates you. It is not a lovely place to visit, but traveling in there seems possible.
101301: A small bat is standing here.

Bodies of poor new adventurers lay with only the bones remaining, snake skins lay all around here, shedded from previous snakes. The cave is filled with the bodies of their prey. A few skulls lay along the walls, bones have been piling up in here for some time now, it is no wonder there are so many snakes in these caves. The poor adventurer whose resting place became final.
101302: The wet feel of the cave cools your feet as you walk along in this cave. The air in here is moist and there is a rustling sound off somewhere. It is not much of a place to stay. The darkness makes it hard to move around and trying to feel you way around is not a good idea from the feel of the walls.
101303: Darkness fills the cave with drops of water falling from the top of the cave. There are many squeaks and rustling sounds echoing from the cave. A pungent odor moves slowly through the cavern, filling it with its strong scent. Loud splashes sound throughout the cave from places distant to here.
101304: The Back of the Snake Cave
A pile of coins is here.

You are in the back of a cave. Huge rocks block what look to be a way out of here. The stench of the mold overpowers your senses and keeps you from being able to think clearly. Little creatures crawl around on the floor, moving around your legs. The darkness is uncomforting and the sound of water can be heard in the distance.
101313: A large boulder seems to block the entrance to some more caves. The rustling sounds can be heard from there and a cool breeze comes from behind the passageway's blocked entrance. Dripping water can be heard nearby, as apparently this is a water cave. The slime is beginning to grow even in this part of the cave.
101314:
A mewlip is here, faintly wailing at you.
A mewlip is here, faintly wailing at you.

You are in a cave, it's walls are slimy and caked with some sort of green living thing. The sounds of footsteps can barely be heard above as water drowns them out from some where. Things seem to be crawling around by your feet maybe you best take a look around. Staying here could be a bad idea. There are some exits around here, this cave may not be all that small.
101315: A rustling sound can be heard moving closer towards you. The cave is so dark, maybe coming in here was not such a good idea. On your feet you can feel some slimy creatures sliding across them. Touching the sides of the cavern, you get a moldy film on your hands. Water can be heard coming from somewhere.
101316: Coming into this room you can barely make out where the walls are. This area is long and narrow and you can barely see in front of you. With all the things crawling around it may be best if you light a torch or something and see where it is you are heading. This may had been a mistake to enter this cave. Water drips from the ceiling falling onto your head sending chills down your back.
101317: In the cave is nothing, there looks to be a few holes that lead no where along here in the walls. There is nothing but what feels like sticks laying in here, stumbling along in here may not be a good idea, dead ends go in all directions and getting lost in here could be easy to do.
101318: The cave at this part of the area is losing its light from the above ground. Going further into this area is going to be a blinding experience. There will be no light from here on out and this coolness of the cave can be felt already on your skin. A faint sound of water can be heard coming from somewhere. A slimy feel along the ground is also there.
101319: Some small rocks have been piled into a mound here.

A smelly, damp cave lies dark here. A large stone door was once set in the northern wall but it lies broken on the floor now. Some old rags and rubble cover the floors, the walls being cracked and broken.
101320: In the middle of this room a large pile of crystal shards glows sickly green. It is surrounded by a chaotic mass of broken items, splinters, parts of furniture. Everything is devastated, ruined, crushed and ripped apart. A large stone door lies cracked in five parts at the entrance to the northern cave.
101321: What once must have been a dwarven home is now just rubble and wreckage. Ripped apart tapestries, a broken desk, fragments of weapons and wooden splinters cover the cracked rock floor. At some places it looks as if a giant has pounded on the walls with his bare fists, leaving huge cracks and marks. Some water is running along the small clefts in the ceiling, making the air in here cold and moist.
101322: A fierce boar is here, making grunting noises.

Here looks to be many large holes in the hill. Probably just an old Hobbit dwelling. Looking around most of them do not lead anywhere but back a few feet then end abruptly. Looking around though is leading to a few that aren't so deadended. A couple of the holes look like they could go down further than just a couple feet.
101323: Walking along here you go over another little hill. This land is just full of hills and nothing else. Some trees grow around here providing shade for that summer heat or protection from rain and snow. There are a couple of holes in the hills most likely just some moles or something. Still, exploring can be a lot of fun in an area of little danger like this.
101329: A wooden sign stands next to the path here.

A small path leads through the pine forest and bends to follow the slope high in the Bruinen valley. It winds past the tall trees, as if those who made it tried to avoid cutting the wood. At a few places the path meets small openings which look recently cleared.
101330: The path travels along the northern slope of the Bruinen valley. South of the path the slope is dominated by vineyards, where Elrond's elves grow grapes for fine wines. There are more vineyards north of the path, but they look abandoned. High above, the slope is topped by the dark and dense pine forest that hides Rivendell from outsiders. Some pine trees have been planted along the path to form an alley when they grow taller.
101331: The path leads past a few ancient pines guarding the northern slope of the Bruinen valley. South of the path, vineyards and the Last Homely Home with its magnificent elven architecture can be seen, and north of the path the vineyards continue. A dark forest above the vineyards marks the border of this hidden valley. A small shelter with six lancet arches supporting a decorated roof has been constructed here to provide cover from the sun or harsh weather.
101332: The path widens and splits in two to enclose a small, round lawn. A circle of tall pine trees surrounds the lawn and some wooden benches have been placed underneath. In the middle of the lawn stands a statue of a great hunter. This small park offers some view over the roofs of the Last Homely Home and the river Bruinen below.
101333: The small gravel path leads through the northern side of the Bruinen valley. It travels along the slope to the east and west, whereas some smaller paths lead up or down into the nearby vineyards. Several thick pine trees protect the path from harsh winds. A small shelter, built in the typical elven style with lancet arches and a vaulted roof, invites the traveller to rest and offers a pleasant view down to the river Bruinen flowing far below.
101334:
A tall pine tree grows here.
A pack horse (Rood) is standing here, ridden by you.

The path ascends towards the east while following the northern slope of the Bruinen valley. Vineyards have been cultivated along the path, as this side of the hidden valley receives the most sunlight. High above the vineyards, the dark outline of a forest marks the border of Rivendell. Some ancient pine trees stand closer by as if guarding the path.
101335: Leading through the vineyards, this small gravel path winds up the northern slope of the Bruinen valley. It climbs the valley side along a carefully built serpentine route. A railing protects those who travel the path from slipping and sliding down the slope. Some small benches have been set at the bends of the path for tired travellers and those who want to enjoy the wide view over the valley and the rushing Bruinen far below.
101336: Healthy grass reminiscent of a well-tended lawn covers this small opening under some tall pines. There are no large rocks or gnarled roots in the ground, making this seem like a great place for building a small house. A narrow footpath leads to the trail at some distance to the east.
101339:
The corpse of a living statue is lying here.
The corpse of a living statue is lying here.

The hall is nearly fifteen feet high and perfectly round. A dozen pillars stand next to each other along the outer wall and each one bears a darkened coal pan near the top. Even if the room looks truly ancient, even if most tiles and pillars have at least cracks or have started to crumble and everything is covered with a thick layer of white dust, the coals still burn with a magical fire and spread a little light and heat. Below the dust, the floor is covered with numerous shattered skeletons and smashed equipment. In the eastern wall there is a completely collapsed and blocked passage, while behind a rusted grate on the northern wall, a narrow shaft winds upwards into the darkness.
101422: You are in a big round room with green walls and high ceiling. Some windows are situated around the room, letting in light during the daytime. Some strange magical symbols are drawn on the walls around the door. The only furniture here is a sturdy coat hanger by the door, and some chairs near the walls. A sturdy spiral staircase leads upwards in the tower.
101423: You are inside the round tower with green stone walls. Four large windows are here, each one facing one of the four cardinal points, making it possible to view the surroundings in every direction. Around the walls there are several pictures on display. In the centre of the room, some comfortable armchairs and a large oaken table stand. It is obvious that every effort has been made to make this room as comfortable and relaxing as possible. A spiral staircase continues both up and downwards in the tower.
101424: A humble man stands here, ready to help you with your things.

You are at the highest point in the tower. It is a large room with a high ceiling and the walls and floor is made out of stone. A lot of windows are situated all around the walls, presenting a beautiful view and letting a lot of light and fresh air into the room. A large oaken bed stands here, facing east, and some chairs are placed in different locations around the room. It seems you can rest here for ages without any disturbances and noise. A spiral staircase wind its way downward in the tower.
101425: This is the entrance of a huge cavern. The entrance doesn't seem to be big enough to allow many people inside. You see another room to the east that instills a sense of great danger about this place. A wise person might think it would be a good idea to leave quickly. On the ground you see footprints, tracked in blood.
101426: This room evokes a feeling of strength. Seems it was made just for the purpose of sitting and thinking about great fights and long travels. On the walls you see pictures of great fights, and they seem to be the exploits of just one person. When you look up you see large words made with fresh blood, 'KAO,' and many scalps of Sauron's minions on the floor.
101427: A humble man stands here, ready to help you with your things.

At the top of the stairs, here is Kao's lair. You see some great pieces of armour on the walls, and many different foods and drinks on the table. However, there is just one glass... It seems the owner doesn't have many visitors, or perhaps they are simply not welcome.
101434: This entire area is cluttered with an assortment of books and tomes. At first glance most of these texts appear to describe spells as they relate to medicinal knowledge. However, a closer look at the bookcases would also reveal a nice collection of poetry by many of Arda's famed authors. A desk constructed from driftwood is located in the right corner of the room, next to an extremely large bookcase. On the desk a candle burns brightly. The spiral staircase leads up and down.
101435: An Elven steward stands here, watching over the household.

This small room is dominated by an extremely large bed which is located in the centre. While the room is sheltered from the rain and cold, several small holes in the sturdy tree allow you to see the forest and valley below.
101436: A humble man stands here, ready to help you with your things.

This large hall is the sanctuary of Doyok, a noble elf who from the look of things spends his time here sitting in the large lazy chair facing the window. Through the window lies a large vineyard. Fine elvish wine bottles lay about, ranging from current vintage to those dating back to Grey Haven's glory days. Next to the chair on a small table is a well-used clay pipe.
101437: This beautiful garden is filled with colourful flowers carefully tended by one of the finest gardeners on Arda. The air carries a rich sweet smell and transports the soft fragrance of the blooms to the adjoining homes. Often times some elves can be found here singing enchanting songs that may add warmth to the hearts of those who listen. To the east of this garden lies the sanctuary of one of Middle-earth's noble elves.
101438:
A white-painted bench is here.
A humble man stands here, ready to help you with your things.

Most of this structure's space is taken up by large wine barrels and racks upon racks of bottles of elven brews ageing to perfection. In the southern corner there is a place for the farmers employed by Sihir the Elf to work on mixing and developing the various vintages. The northern corner seems to be used for the bottling process.
101439: This balcony stands above a beautiful garden on a huge old oak tree. This place is being used by the elves to chant their songs while watching the beautiful garden below or the vineyard to the north. This place is also used by the owner of the winery and his friends while enjoying the best weed of the Longbottoms.
101440:
The Housekeeper looks fed up with her job. She scowls at you unhappily.
A seagull is soaring above you.

A single rusty door leads into this dark small hall covered in dust. The amount of dust, and the disheveled appearance of the few pieces of furniture in the room, might lead one to believe this place was abandoned if not for the trails of footsteps leading toward a stairway at the rear. A small bed, almost hidden by the stairway, seems to be the only other thing that has seen any recent use. A faint shimmering light seems to be coming from the room above.
101441: This dimly lit tower looks well organised, a stark contrast to the state of the room below. Looking around one could see many items that look to be used in the magical arts, as well as a table in the centre of the room upon which several weapons have been set. Some of the weapons have a soft glow about them; while others look like they lay in wait for the same treatment.
101442: The portico of this Elven home looks out onto a vibrant, green lawn speckled with silvery-white flowers. A set of rickety steps on the western side of the portico leads towards some shrubbery; a sturdier set of steps leads southwards to the path through the front lawn. The steps and floor of the portico are made of ash wood that emits a brilliant shine on cloudless nights and a paler, warmer glow during the day. The intricate railings and roof supports are made of a metal sturdier than iron, but they shine silver with the light of many stars. Strands of ivy weave themselves around the railings and the bottom edges of the portico so that the house seems to be growing from the ground itself. To the north is a door leading to the inside of the home.
101443:
A sturdy bed made from solid oak lies here, covered in warm blankets.
A humble man stands here, ready to help you with your things.

This room serves both as a bedroom and a private study for Hawa Jadestone, the mistress of the house. Each wall, except the one containing the door, holds a large, curtained window. These three magnificent curtains stretch from the rafters of the ceiling all the way to the floor and serve as eloquent reminders of far-off Elven cities. The curtains give the room a quiet aura of tranquility infused with sadness about wonders lost. The walls and floor are made of a marble very similar in colour to the wood of the portico and glisten when moonlight makes its way through the curtained windows. Tucked away in one corner of the room is a wooden chest that contains various pieces of jade jewellery as well as other trinkets from times gone by.
101444: This rooftop terrace has been constructed entirely of white and silver materials. The perimeter of the terrace is marked by a short, white railing that serves not only as a precautionary measure, but also as a trellis for radiant honeysuckle to grow on during the warmer months. The floor is covered by a layer of pale, flat stones that seem to catch moonlight and harness its brilliance so that the stones radiate their own light even during the day. In the centre of the terrace stands a white crescent-shaped fountain that seems specially designed to capture moonlight. Light reflected off the water within the fountain plays over the floor in shining waves.
101445: At the Edge of a Plateau

Prickly, white-stemmed plants, with blue flower heads grow in abundance.
An orc sentry of the Ohurk-uai is here on patrol.

Regular gusts of frigid air buffet everything atop this bluff. This is the most western margin of a vast plateau which stretches eastward to the very foothills of the Misty Mountains. Standing at some height above the lower-lying plains to the west this promontory has a bleak aspect, and only the most stubborn, low- growing vegetation clings to life here.
101446: A sturdy pack horse is standing here.

You find yourself inside a fairly narrow tunnel. The walls high above you appear natural, but closer to floor level show signs of working. Rough chisel marks scar the cold, grey rock, speaking to the effort that must have been expended to enlarge a smaller, natural crevice. A crude stair ascends the northern wall giving access to a large stone trapdoor in the roof. The floor slopes downward to the east as the tunnel widens and approaches a larger cavern.
101448: An ancient black altar stands in the centre of the room.

Where the tunnel to the west appears crudely made, the craftsmanship in this chamber is of a higher calibre. The walls describe a near-perfect circle and are quite smooth. Strange runes cover their surface from floor to eye level and high upon the wall, immediately facing the entrance, is painted the image of a huge, lidless, red eye. Above your head a domed ceiling has been carved, and its surface bears a thick coating of oily soot, as if attesting that many fleshy pyres have been lit in this place.
101449: A mountain goat is here, jumping from cliff to cliff.

Looking south, you see the mountain range that separates the upper and lower branches of the High Pass. To the west the trail is climbing up into the mountains, and to the east it becomes wider. North of here is something that looks like a hill.
101450: Deep underneath the hill this tunnel comes to a sudden stop as a solid wall of stone hinders anyone from digging further ahead. No sunlight ever permeates down here, creating an everlasting night. The air is very moisty, condensing upon the cold walls. South of here lies a tunnelcrossing.
101451: Deep under the mountain four tunnels gather at this point. Small rivulets gathers the water in small pools in the shallows on the ground. Tiny patches of moss grows upon the walls, nurturing on the minerals in the water. Any sound echoes off the walls and amplifies as it travels into the tunnels ahead.
101452: The corpse of a striped snake is lying here.

The tunnel gets narrower for a few yards, until it comes to a complete halt. There is no movement in the air, but it is very damp and crisp. Moss grows in small patches on the walls and from the ceiling hangs some lichen suspended. Any noise echoes of the walls and travels ahead in the tunnel.
101453: This is a three-way intersection point, with tunnels going north, east and south. The air is chill and moisty, and the moist condenses on the walls, creating tiny rivulets that gathers in small puddles inbetween the huge stones and rocks that litters the ground.
101454: The tunnel is a few feet wide as it abruptly ends with a chasm. The chasm seems to be bottomless, and its walls are naturally rough. There is no way to descend down into the chasm as there is no place to secure a climbing rope or hook, and the walls are slippery and wet as the damp air condenses when it hits the cold earth.
101455: A black snake, with red markings, is lying here.

Four tunnels meet at this point, deep down under the hill where the sun never permeats, creating an endless night. The walls are rough but soft, and drenched in water that has condensed from the moist moveless air. Small stones litters the ground, impeding travel.
101456: The dark tunnel gets smaller and more narrow until it comes to an end. The roof is low, and the floor is rough. Water condenses upon the cold walls, forming tiny rivulets that runs down to the ground. It gathers in puddles in the small hollows in the floor.
101457: Deep underneath the hill, where the stars never shine, a large hall extends in all direction. It measures some fifty yards from side to side and the ceiling reaches about twenty feet up. It is completely and utterly unfurnished, but there is a distinct smell of something rotten in the chill moveless air.
101458: The walls and ceiling of this tunnel are roughly cut, and fragments of stone covers the floor. It continues east and south into the dark heart of the hill. There is no movement in the chill air, but it still makes its way through cloth, fur and skin. Lichen grows in abundance on the soft walls, nurturing on minerals and the damp air.
101459: A black snake, with red markings, is lying here.

The pitch-black tunnel comes to a sudden stop without any explanatory reason. Water trickles down the cold slippery walls in intricate patterns, hits the floor and continues along the sides westwards. The passageway is narrow and the air stale and moist. To the west, the tunnel enters an underground crossing.
101460: The tunnelwalls are rough and composed of soft earth. There is a hole in the eastern wall. It is without any specific shape and has ragged edges, as if either natural, or hewn by one who had no care for its form. The cavetunnel turns north and west.
101461: This small room seems to be a natural cavity, with a very small crack in the western wall. The floor is litered with dirt and old dried out snakeskins, aswell as faeces in different sizes, all originating from snakes. There is no natural lightsource in this part of the cavesystem.
101467: Fragments of stone covers the floor of the cave. The walls and the ceiling are roughly cut, tunneling into the dark heart of the hill. The air is still, damp and cold, making its way through any cloth, fur or skin. The cavetunnel splits here, and continues north, south and west.
101468: The walls are very rough and composed of earth. The cave is fairly large, with a distance from the floor to the ceiling of about six feet. There is something written on the wall, and a large white rune has been painted on the floor. The cave continues south, and northwards lies the catacombs.
101470: A Small Hill by the Bend

Tall grass, small rocks, and scattered bushes cover this small hill. Standing on its top it is possible to get a good view of the surrounding land. A road runs around this hill to the north and west. Beyond the road to the north is a sea of grass. Down the slope to the east is a wild patch of weeds.
101472: Bend in the Old Forest Road

The Old Forest Road bends around the small hill to the east of here. Westwards fields surround the road along with a group of trees to the northwest. It is possible to travel east to the top of the small hill.
101473: A boar cub is playing here, and exploring the wide world.

A heap of rags, rotten vegetables and pieces of wood lies here in the middle of an open field, just south of a bend in the Old Forest Road. Upon closer examination, even broken tools and containers are noticeable, but it seems unlikely that there is anything of use under all the junk. A small wagon with a broken wheel leans to the pile of garbage; all this looks like leftovers from a merchant or a group of settlers.
101474: Recent cart traffic through these fields has left pairs of deep, narrow tracks into the soft ground. The tracks rise up from a ditch in the south and continue towards the Old Forest Road in the north. A small footpath appears from the bushes in the west, joining the cart tracks at an opening, which is surrounded by short trees. At the edge of the opening, some chopped logs lie on the ground, and the grass is burnt in some places.
101475: A swallow flies high above the ground.

Fallen trees from the clump of trees to the north have almost blocked this road. The logs appear to have been here for quite a while since the sun has made them greyish and hard. Carts would have an extremely hard time trying to negotiate their way past these logs, but a person or their mount would have little problem jumping over them.
101476: A swallow flies high above the ground.

Bushes and high grass line the fringe of the Old Forest Road. Occasionally a bush finds a place in the middle of the road to set its roots. Northeast of here a large clump of trees can be seen and further to the east a small hill stands. To the west, the road bends to follow the Anduin River's bank north towards its source for a short distance.
101477: Bend in the Old Forest Road

As the road bends here it runs north along the riverbank to where it makes another turn and east towards a small hill. Grass has taken root in the old cart tracks that scar the road and bushes of several kinds surround the road.
101478: A Hedgerow South of the Road

A neat row of thorny bushes starts here, and continues for about half a mile to the east. The hedge is impenetrable in most places, but there are a few gaps where passing through would not be difficult even for a rider. In the north, grassy fields separate the hedgerow from the Old Forest Road; a road that lies partially hidden from view behind the bushes of various sizes and shapes that grows in between.
101479: A pair of round, smooth hillocks stand out in this treeless meadow of weeds and flowers. Molehills dot the slopes on all sides; the loose soil coupled with the absence rocks here seems ideal for digging tunnels and hovels. A dirt path leads around the hillocks towards the Old Forest Road in the north, while to the southeast it disappears into a shrubbery.
101480: A babbling brook runs through a hollow in the plains here. The streambed is rocky and much wider than the stream itself; travelling on the bottom of the hollow is somewhat hard compared to the gentle, grass-covered slopes in the north and in the south. Thin-branched bushes stand out among the rocks on both sides of the stream, and occasionally signs of small birds living among them can be noticed.
101481:
There are two handfuls of clover here.
A bee flies around here, collecting nectar from the flowers.
A snake slithers towards you.

A verdant field of clover and small flowers spreads out from here towards the muddy furrow of a stream in the southeast. In the summertime, the local bees must find an endless supply of nectar from the round flowers of the clover; there are also plants that rabbits and deer might dig up to eat during long winters. Some droppings lie on the ground, but whatever animal left them seems to have scurried away; almost no bushes to hide in grow along the paths leading through this field.
101482: The slender stems of flowering plants standing in this verdant field undulate slightly whenever there is a breeze. Many of them are spreading their seeds over the field; their petals have dried up and fallen away, but the time has not wiped out their colour entirely. Large bluish petals lying on the ground are slowly turning brown, and there are also some dry sunflowers that still have seeds left for birds to eat. Clusters of tiny flowers are thriving in the shade under a lonely elm standing in the fields.
101483: The thick grass growing here is wet, especially near the bank in the north, where the waters of Anduin occasionally splash over the embankment. Clear puddles cover the grass in depressions, and smaller ones are slowly forming to fill in any tracks left on the soft ground. The riverbank to the west is covered by small, grey pebbles, which have turned smooth and round over the years they have spent on the bottom of the river.
101484: A green frog is here, hopping around.

A stream flowing into these muddy fields from the east has carved a wide ditch into the soft ground. Steep slopes lead away from the stream in the west and in the north, where some cart tracks can be seen leading down to the stream and continuing over to the cultivated fields in the south. The mud looks somewhat sinking around the tracks, but the ground in the east seems rockier, and there are even places where the water of the stream is clear enough to drink.
101485:
A fierce boar is here, making grunting noises.
A black crow flies low to the ground here, looking for carrion to eat.

High hay and small bushes grow here and there, while a carpet of thick, tangled grass covers most of the ground. Some of the dry plants among the grass have been crushed by something that recently passed through here, spreading their large, flat seeds to the ground. In the west, the grass suddenly disappears and a field of sand continues down to the river.
101489: This is all that remains of an old homestead that was burned to the ground a long time ago. Cauliflowers, turnips, and celery grow in what appears to be an old garden. North of here a road runs across the plains, and to the east the Anduin River flows.
101490: A grey wolf is here, salivating profusely.

Bushes of various shapes and sizes dominate the landscape. An occasional burst of buttercups gives this ragged land a bit of lustre. To the west, the bushes are gradually replaced by trees. To the north the bushes continue.
101491:
A great horned owl looks cautiously around it.
A grey wolf is here, salivating profusely.

The soil is much rockier than in the forest west of here, which seems to inhibit the growth of the dense forest. A few tall and stout trees grow here but bushes dominate this edge of the forest. Several large and sharp rocks lie scattered about.
101492: A large owl with small sharp horns looks cautiously around it.

Tall trees with stout branches form a thick and vivid forest that provides shelter for the animals living here. The undergrowth looks very dense and is formed by a large variety of plants. Different kinds of spoor cover the soft ground providing proof of active life in the region.
101493:
A forest spider is here crawling around.
A squirrel scampers around here, looking for nuts from the trees.

This spacious forest consists of a variety of trees all with large leaves that form a very thick-looking canopy. The lower sections of some trees have been gnawed by animals leaving bits and pieces of bark on the ground. The forest grows denser in the east and the closest edge of this forest is somewhere to the west.
101494: This bushy region forms the border between the forest that spreads eastward and the grassy lands to the west. The mellow soil that nourishes the bushes can easily be imprinted by the tracks of various animals as they pass through this region.
101495: Though short grass and a few small bushes still manage to cover this plain, many of them have been trampled by animals. Most of the moss that once grew here has wilted although a few tussocks of it still remain. The grasslands continue to the west and north while to the east the land begins to be dominated by bushes.
101496: A black crow flies low to the ground here, looking for carrion to eat.

The land here is entirely covered by grass with a few small bushes and richly coloured flowers pushing up between the stalks. A few low mounds are scattered about and blanketed with a moss. The terrain has more bushes to the west but the grass here continues into the east and north.
101497:
*Flux the Orc*, wielding an engraved broadsword, is here, riding a hungry warg.
A hungry warg is standing here, ridden by *Flux the Orc*.

Different kinds of bushes cover this smooth plain, which is south of a mud- covered trail. A few small rocks lie across the exposed surface and some earth- worms are wriggling on the muddy surface. The land continues to be covered by bushes to the west but turns grassy in the east.
101498: The plains here are very soft, covered by numerous large bushes growing close enough to each other to conceal the ground with their giant leaves. A collapsed guard tower with blackened walls rises to the west where it stands next to a burned out village. A muddy trail to the north passes near here and comes to an end in front of the ruined village. This bushy region continues eastward.
101499: The collapse of most of the supporting walls, the broken ladders, and the dilapidated ceiling of this wrecked tower makes reaching the upper floor nearly impossible. The floor is littered with blackened bricks that are highlighted by several white bones that stick out from underneath. A massive, but worn-out stonewall can be seen through the hole in the western wall.
101500: The vegetation here is very patchy, with only small areas of plants which are mostly grass. A few small withered-looking bushes have managed to take root in the surrounding area. To the north-east is the gateway to a burned down village and a collapsed guard tower can be seen to the east.
101501: The corpse of a dreadful snake is lying here.

Many flat rocks cover this plain which appears very barren with almost no vegetation. Only a few tussocks of dry grass can be seen growing from the surface. The ground has fewer stones to the north where a dry-looking plain can be seen. Farther to the north several mountains loom.
101502: Peaks of swaying stems of grass lie like a blanket over the fields. Beneath, a rich earth feeds the vegetation. Smells of herbs and dirt, and a sense of soft moisture fill the air.
101503: When sun or moon shines the reflected light plays in the fields. It jumps from straw to straw, changing their hues as it goes. The sway of the grass helps, making the scenery even more spectacular. Beneath this, insects have their homes among the gravel and dirt, digging tunnels and feeding on whatever they can claim.
101504: A large, loyal falcon is circling above.

The grass rolls out in all directions as a carpet covering the land. An occasional rock or lonesome tree can be spotted, but very little disturbs the rule of the grass. Deep within the green tangles white and yellow flowers struggle to spring up and reach for the beams of the sun.
101505: The green tangles hold a firm grip of the earth, letting few or none of the beams from the sun reach down to their roots. Close to the ground there is little growth, except for the close-packed stems of grass reaching for the sky. Gazing out over the fields flowers of white and yellow dot the green, and in the west a drier landscape reaches out.
101506:
An orchid of light violet petals blossoms nearby.
A brown fox is here, looking for some rabbits to chew up.

Here the ground follows a gentle descent to the south. Streaks of shallow ditches run across the land letting the water flow towards the lower lands in the south. The grass here uses this water to flourish in green, and along the sides of the shallows white flowers grow closely in patches.
101507:
The corpse of a wild ox is lying here.
A small cluster of clover grows here.

These green fields are spotted with moss and lichen, as the rows of hay grow thinner, decaying in the soggy ground. To the south a sharp descent begins the ruling of the Gladden Fields. At this descent a grey type of sturdy grass grows tall and strong, with roots reaching far down in the soft ground.
101508: Inner Borders of the Gladden Fields

Tall yellow flowers cover the moist ground, prospering in the lowland.
A frog is standing here.

Moss and lichen form complicated patterns in varying colours over the undulating ground. Their intricate figures are covered in a thick mist, floating a couple of feet above the ground. In the north and west the borders of the Gladden run sharply across the land. In these parts sturdy grey grass grows high above the mossy earth, serving as the harsh keeper of the marshes.
101509:
A frog is standing here.
A frog is standing here.
*Asha the Half-Elf*, wielding a bejewelled oak staff, is here, riding a horse of the Rohirrim (shrouded).
A horse of the Rohirrim is standing here, ridden by *Asha the Half-Elf*.

Soft moss flows over the landscape into the south and west. The marshes reach out as far as the eye can see, covered in an apparent mist close to the ground. The stench of rotten grass and decay lies distinctly in the air. The ancient shores of the Gladden run in the north and east, spotted with grey grass that bends into the wet ground. A sharp edge of slippery grass and turf makes it impossible to move to the east while the marshes smoothly connect with the fields in the north.
101510: A small cluster of clover grows here.

Crawling in from the north-east branches and tangles are desperately reaching for a hold in the soft ground. All that meets them here though is moist and muddy earth, and the woody stems quickly decay covered in moss and lichen. In the south the marshes of Gladden Fields stretch out. Grey grass grows in narrow rows on the edge, flourishing in the moss.
101511: A colourful butterfly is fluttering around here.

Shallow natural furrows run from north to south across the green fields. Occasional rains fill them with water travelling to the south. There is however a constant supply of water in these trenches as they are fed with dew and mist from the endless fields in the north. Venturing upwards to the east takes the traveller into a maze of tangles towards a sharp slope in the fields.
101512:
A small cluster of clover grows here.
A small grasshopper clings to a blade of grass, ready to spring.

Flourishing green grass stretches out, flowing over the fields. Small bushes and tangles snare the land to the east, but in this area the swaying grass has a firm grip of the land. Natural shallow ditches run across the fields in a disordered pattern. Most of these paths are dried out, with only wet mud to show for the water that once ran there. Even during rains, the ground is thirsty enough to not let any water flow away. To the east the path is blocked by a tangle of brown branches.
101513: Between the stems of the green grass, snakes, rats and other small animals may go about their business. The hay rattles occasionally in the wind or when disturbed by something deep in the thick green. These lands seem satisfied with water and sun, flourishing in their growth.
101514: Here, as in the fields around, the grass grows in hundred different hues of green. All straws of the hay have their unique shades like swaying individuals. But growing together as they do the result is a rainbow of greens covering the land. Brown herbs and yellow and white flowers can be spotted within the deep sea of grass by a keen eye.
101515: A cluster of dark green, feathery fronds flourishes in the shade.

Here the landscape is covered in hues of green, spotted with streaks of white and yellow flowers. To the east and south, the ground becomes rougher and further away tangles of wood and snares spread out. In this area, though, the undulating grass still rules firmly, covering the earth with its ordered rows of green stems. A steep hill covered in tangles blocks further travel southeast.
101516: Herbs and flowers fight for the their existence beneath the swaying sea of green hay. Although they can hardly be spotted they fill the air with all kinds of scents, some earthy, some fresh, some thick, some casual. The herbs have come together in small patches, creating islands of low brown grass.
101517: A small cluster of clover grows here.

A rich cover protects the earth, shielding it from rain and wind. The green grass serves as food source for numerous hungry animals that pass these fields on their way to the refreshing water of the Anduin. The grass rattles whenever light breezes travel over the lands.
101518: A large, loyal falcon is circling above.

Close to the north and east, birches are scattered throughout the fields. These lonesome pillars serve as a wall, hindering the wind from ruling freely. In the cover of this wall the dust and gravel lies firmly on the ground beneath a jungle of green straws that seldom have to bend in the power of moving air.
101519: A black and white skunk is scuttling about here, searching for food.

Short, perky bushes grow here in some places while only a few trees remain of the forest in the north. Together with rocks of various sizes, they provide cover for small animals in the otherwise bare fields of grass. The great river lies somewhere to the southeast, where the ground begins to slope gently towards the riverbed.
101520: A black snake hurries towards you with sly intentions.

The broken remains of a wooden fence surround this old pasture, where shrubs and small trees have taken over. The grass covering the ground is lush and seems perfect for domestic animals to graze on. Still, no signs of cattle can be found here, except for the bleached skull of a cow that sits tucked between two rocks. The field continues all the way down to the bank of the river in the east.
101521: A swarm of mosquitoes is here, humming around you.

Sticks and branches litter the ground in this brushwood near the riverbed. Some open ways lead west and north through the dense shrubs here, making it possible for a rider to follow the course of the river. The paths bend and twist, stopping anyone from seeing very far, as the shrubbery seems to get thicker at every turn.
101522: Soft hay covers the wide fields here, partly hiding any tracks that could have been left in the muddy ground. Slender stems of taller plants sway gently whenever a breeze passes through; no shelter from the wind can be found in any direction. In the southeast, some bushes stand near the river.
101523: A large thorny branched shrub is growing here.

The ocean of green so apparent in the surrounding fields, is here spotted with tangles and shrubs. In the middle of these lakes of brush rocks and stones lie, serving as the little cover the bushes need to get a hold of the land. By every stone and every rock, tangles and branches grow close to the sides, and then spread out into the greens.
101524: A small cluster of clover grows here.

In all directions the green grass keeps a firm grip on the land. Far in the north-west horizon however the peaks of mountains can be spotted by the keen eye gazing down through mists and clouds. In this area though there is little sight of slopes or peaks, and this form stretches far away in the distance.
101525: Looking out over the fields rolling away into the horizon offers a sight only comparable to an ocean. The colours of the ocean have been switched from the marine blue to green and brown, but still undulate and shift like waves on a frantic sea. The earth beneath the grass is soft and even soggy in places, but solid enough to not give way when rain and snow falls.
101526: Moisture and wealth of growth dominates the fields. The level landscape is covered with a thick, swaying coat of straws in a vast range of shapes and colours. This area serves as home, playground and pantry for its inhabitants. The earth is soft and rich, and fills the air with a smell of soft dirt.
101527: A large mother hawk is here looking for a prey to feed her young.

The carpet of grass and plants stretches over the landscape, shifting from the lightest shades of brown, to sharp, almost luminous hues of green. As the old plants decay they are replaced by fresh crops of grass, forming layers of either seasoned or keen stems. The decaying smell fills the air, mixing with the piquant scent of new growing.
101528:
The corpse of a grizzly cub is lying here.
The corpse of a grizzly bear is lying here.

The fields are coloured in green and brown, shifting and flowing through the landscape. Below in the nestled floor of decaying brown grass, ants and other hard working insects rearrange the miniature scenery as they see fit. To the south a sharp ridge quickly climbs and reaches its top. Beyond this high ground sun-burnt grass and brown reeds quickly replace the lush greens. The ridge is covered in rocks and gravel, serving as home for numerous insects and small reptiles. To the east gravel and a large stone has formed a shelter protecting the ground from wind and rain.
101529: Luscious Greens at a Narrow Crest
A cluster of dark green, feathery fronds flourishes in the shade.

The luscious cover of grass fills the air with scents of herbs and dirt. The plain stretches out and touches the horizon in all directions. To the south a steep slope quickly works its way up to an impassable sharp top. On the ascent the plants and grass crave the sun, but their location on the north-faced slope only grants their wish during a few short hours every day. To the west large stones and gravel fallen from the side of the slope effectively block the path.
101530: Old Pastures at a Steep Ridge
A cluster of dark green, feathery fronds flourishes in the shade.

The ever flowing green is abruptly interrupted here by long since overgrown squares of pasture. They are framed with what once could be called ditches in a pattern far too symmetrical to be made by nature itself. The ground is level and the elsewhere so mandatory gravel and small rocks are nowhere to be seen. The shallow ditches are soggy and overgrown; apparently rain still gathers in their lines and a thirsty wanderer will be able to find enough here to dampen his need. In the south a sharp ridge cuts through the land, creating a grey scar of rocks and gravel in the fields.
101531: Small squares of fields, regulated by shallow overgrown ditches, break the flowing dominance of grass and herbs. While the stems of green and brown still cover the landscape, here it has been ordered into tidy shapes. It is obvious that these pastures has long since been abandoned, but they nevertheless still serve as a haven for more craving plants and herbs, with rich earth and gravel free ground. In the grass-filled trenches, water is collected as rain falls.
101532: Swaying grass, layered with brown and green in different heights and appearances, rules the land. To the west a more ordered line of fields can be seen, as if placed there by hand, but here the unordered scheme of nature takes its grasp of the earth again. A gentle slope stretches up in the south, and beyond its face more dried out scenery can be seen.
101533: A small grasshopper clings to a blade of grass, ready to spring.

This field is covered with golden grass reaching to the knees of a full-grown man, and in places even higher. The straws grow closer to each other here than in the surrounding areas, swaying when the wind blows as golden waves in the grass. Every footstep here is followed by a small cloud of dust, disturbed by the movement.
101534:
An orchid of light violet petals blossoms nearby.
A small animal, all covered in spines, snuffles amongst the undergrowth.
A brown fox is here, looking for some rabbits to chew up.

Close to the ground the golden straws of grass create a labyrinth in the dust and gravel. The earth is cracked in places, and serves as home for numerous insects and small reptiles. In the north greener fields resembling pastures cover the land, while in the southwest a stony ledge stubbornly cuts the land.
101536: A mass of wriggling vines drops on you from the trees.

Here the shrubs and tangles grow thick. Rocks and large stones are also a common sight. Their presence shapes the landscape into a dense brush. The flora changes with the diminishing grass, into more brown herbs, instead of the colourful flowers so common in the surrounding fields. The composition of this immensely tangled hill makes travelling westwards impossible while its smooth flow towards the river Anduin almost encourages venturing in that direction.
101537: This field flourishes in its own richness; the land is alive with animals using it as home and hunting ground. An occasional bird might be spotted, casting its shadow on the green grass, along with a quick rabbit running through the stems, or a snake hiding its presence among the gravel. To the north the landscape shades in gold and yellow, and in the south the land is sickened with the excessive supply of water.
101538: In the north a steep ridge cuts through the landscape and continues westwards while it in the east gently levels out with the landscape. It lets this area keep the rain that falls, and the grass can offer itself some shade during early and late hours of the day. While the land further in the south becomes soggy and damp, this area keeps a good balance and the green can flourish. The smell of herbs and flowers fills the air, but for the keen nose a scent of fungi and wetness flows in from the south.
101539: A small animal, all covered in spines, snuffles amongst the undergrowth.

Yellow and golden straws spread like a carpet over the fields. To the south and east their richness increases into a far greener appearance. Water running from the cracked earth in the north makes the land in the south wet and misty. Gazing even further the contours of the Gladden Fields paint their dark shapes on the horizon.
101540: A small cluster of clover grows here.

Dirt and dust flows through the air, reflecting any light from sun or moon as countless fire-flies. In the northeast a sharp, prominent ridge runs over the fields. The northern side is steep and rocky, while the southern side slopes gently downwards, placing the thirsting plants in the cross-line of the sun, parching their presence.
101541: In the north a sharp ridge runs from east to west, filled with hazardous rocks and gravel. Beyond it rich green fields stretch out into the horizon, but here the earth is harder and the surface is covered with dust and gravel between the yellow straws of grass. The busy insects are ever present, but the sound flowing in the air seems damp and lazy.
101542: On a Crest in the Fields

The corpse of a huge, black wolf is lying here.
The corpse of a huge, black wolf is lying here.
The corpse of a wild ox is lying here.
The corpse of a wild ox is lying here.
A small cluster of clover grows here.

Climbing a daring crest to the north, the green grass turns into a mesh of dry straws, sloping down into the south. The slant is sharp and mostly noticeable by the occasional shifting of rocks on the slope. There is nothing here that provides shelter from the sun, and the rain that falls quickly flows away on the hard earth.
101543: A fallow deer is grazing peacefully here.

The earth is dry and dusty, but in the south where the slope levels out into the rest of the land, the intense green colours of fresh grass reclaim their hold of the scene. Small flowers and plants fight for their presence among the ruling grass, offering a change of colour in the otherwise so sectarian hues.
101544:
The corpse of a pack leader is lying here.
Yellow flowers, with grey-green foliage, grow in clusters here.
The wild ox seems ready to charge you.

The slope in the north gently evens out here, allowing the downpour to feed the thirsty plants. Crevices and lines in the moist earth lead muddy water southwards, into a mossy and mist-filled landscape. The swaying hay in these fields seems to enjoy the mixture of wetness and sun, and exhibits it in its green splendour.
101545: While green hay and small yellow flowers still grow in rows, the earth here has become soggy and moist. Moss springs up, covering the ground between the straws, colouring the landscape in a hue of dusky green.
101546: This peninsula shoots out into the marshes, serving as a last stand for the green hays that flow in from the north. It ends abruptly into the Gladden Fields in the south, east and west. On the border of the marshes, a grey kind of grass stands tall in the moss and water, as if watching over the fields.
101547:
Tall yellow flowers cover the moist ground, prospering in the lowland.
On the cluster, there are two tall yellow irises.
A speckled, brown and white bird with a long curved bill stands here.

Stretching in from the north the edge of a large peninsula cuts into the Gladden Fields. Its body is spotted with dots of yellow flowers and patches of green hay, but as it descends into the moss and muddy waters only grey stems of grass still stand.
101548:
The corpse of a wild ox is lying here.
Yellow flowers, with grey-green foliage, grow in clusters here.
The wild ox seems ready to charge you.

The dry slanting ground levels out with the green fields to the south. A large rock covered in dust and gravel, but with little signs of moss and lichen, has seemingly scrambled down on the long slope and come to a rest here, among golden straws and crushed gravel. The hay has embraced the boulder and crawled half-way up its sides.
101549:
A wolf cub happily plays here.
A wolf cub happily plays here.
A wolf cub happily plays here.
The mother wolf stands here, protecting her young cubs.

Descending down a rather narrow opening between the earth and the foot of the rock, a damp space opens up. Its sides are dug out from the invigorating soil, and the dirty rock serves as a hard and stable ceiling. Along the walls small cavities have been dug out and in them decaying carcasses of small animals rot away, instigating a strong odour which makes the air heavy to breathe. On the floor straws of hay and moss have been laid, creating a resting place for the residents.
101550: As the descent from the north evens out into a wide field, the ground can once again claim its need for moist and sun. The surrounding fields are covered in high green hay, so common for this area. Small flowers spread along the ground letting patches of hay sway among them.
101551: A boar cub is playing here, and exploring the wide world.

The green plains of the north are quickly covered with moss and moisture here. The hay still stands tall, swaying silently, but the rows of stems have grown thinner, and the mossy ground beneath is clearly visible. A decaying stench flows in from the south, almost visible to the eye, as it lies as a blanket over the fields.
101552:
The corpse of a watersnake is lying here.
Tall yellow flowers cover the moist ground, prospering in the lowland.
A frog is standing here.

At the western side of this part of the marshes, a thick row of sturdy grey grass grows for miles and miles. They seem to protect the marshes from the piercing peninsula in the west, which cuts in among the moss and lichen. The soggy ground continues fearlessly in the east and the south firmly covering the land with its wetness. To the north a small slopes climbs into the fields above.
101553: A boar cub is playing here, and exploring the wide world.

The thick rows of green grass flowing in from the north spread out in thinner and thinner patches as the field rolls southwards. The ground is spotted with patches of moss and lichen, which grow thicker as the borders of the Gladden Fields approach. A small slope separates these wetlands from the marsh in the south.
101554: The wild ox seems ready to charge you.

Patches of green and brown grass flow over the earth, flowing towards the horizon. From the north a gentle slope descends to these fields. The fragile contours of solitary trees spread over the lands; they are drawn in black and grey on the canvas of the sky. Patches of white flowers spring up here and there, claiming a scrap of land as their own.
101555: Along the Border of Gladden Fields
A small cluster of clover grows here.

Small yellow flowers spot the mossy ground, and among them high swaying stems of green grass stand proudly. The ground has however become soft and moss-filled compared to the lands in the north, and neither flowers nor grass can grow to any significant stature, as their roots rot away in the wet ground. The border of the Gladden Fields quickly ends the chance of further growth in the south. Even further away the dark marshes reach out, covered in mist.
101556: A brown fox is here, looking for some rabbits to chew up.

Grass in hundreds of hues of green and brown embraces the soft earth. The landscape flows gently in all directions, undulating towards the horizon. In the north and west the fields continue in this fashion as far the eye can see. In the opposite directions, a gentle mist is starting to show over the fields, connecting with the Gladden Fields in the south, and the mighty Anduin far in the east.
101557: A small cluster of clover grows here.

As the ground slopes into the south rainfall and moisture from the fields in the north seeps through these fields, leaving them soft and wet. Moss has started to spring up between the ever growing rows of green grass, and gentle yellow flowers have found a place to flourish. The air is filled with a gentle mist, and from the south a distinct smell of wet and rotting fields flows in.
101558: A small cluster of clover grows here.

A sparse growth of orange grass is bravely fighting for this piece of land. The moss-filled ground fights back, rendering the ground soggy and too wet for the fragile roots of the grass. In this battle small yellow flowers have found their way to grow beside the moss, sending their stems down in the moist earth.
