In the southeast the fields fall down into a sink where dark marshes grab a hold in the land.
101559:
Tall yellow flowers cover the moist ground, prospering in the lowland.
A frog is standing here.

Row upon row of thick grey grass covers the border of the Gladden Fields in the north and a sharp edge of turf and grass cuts into the marsh in the east. Behind this wall of grey, a sharp descent reaches down into the moss-filled mire. The marshes consist of patches of undulating moss and lichen, travelling up and down in shallow muddy waters, stretching miles at end.
101560: Outer Shores of the Gladden Fields

Clusters of slender stems and tall leaves thrive in the mud and shallows.
A frog is standing here.
A black crow flies low to the ground here, looking for carrion to eat.

The marshes reach out in the south, covered in a firm mist ascending from the soggy ground. Soft moss flows over the marshes in patches, enclosed by ponds of grey, muddy water. A damp odour of decay fills the air. To the north the sharp slippery shore of the ancient Gladden makes passing impossible.
101561:
Tall yellow flowers cover the moist ground, prospering in the lowland.
A frog is standing here.
A frog is standing here.

Grey moss and lichen crawls over the lands, up and down through sinks of water, ever continuing southwards, stretching out into the horizon. A shallow mist covers this display with its foggy appearance, rising from the wet ground. In the north the mosses come to a stop as the Gladden Fields border to the green fields above.
101562:
Tall yellow flowers cover the moist ground, prospering in the lowland.
A black crow flies low to the ground here, looking for carrion to eat.

The moss-covered sloping sides of the peninsula in the northwest quickly descend into the water-filled marches. This must have been a shallow part of the ancient lake, but a few hundred feet further out it levels out with the rest of the soggy ground. Row upon row of grey grass grows along the border of the cape, spotted with small yellow flowers. Turfs of lower grass and decaying bushes decorate the sides of the mossy patches in the swamp.
101563: Descending from the isle in the east, the moss here sinks low into the ground, so low that the pools of water connect and create a small lake in the marsh. There is no telling how deep it might be; the muddy water renders seeing the bottom impossible, but a daring diver might find it further down than expected. The small lake stretches out into the south. In the north and west the mossy ground quickly levels with the surrounding land, while in the east there is a steep drop trickled with small currents from the marshes.
101564: Tall yellow flowers cover the moist ground, prospering in the lowland.

A shallow isle rises from the soft moss and muddy waters. Compared to the surrounding areas the ground is firmer and even dry at places. The dense mist of the mire does not reach to here, but it encircles the base of the ascent. Sharp slopes descend in the north and west, while the promontory stretches further in the east and south.
101565: Mossy Hill in the Gladden Fields

Tall yellow flowers cover the moist ground, prospering in the lowland.
A large, loyal falcon is circling above.

A trifling of a hill reaches up from the soggy marsh. It is surrounded by lower pools of water and floating moss, but up here grey and, in some places, even green straws of grass sway obliviously. At the borders of the incline, sturdy thick grass with a sharp grey tone carefully watches the deceiving mire around. The hill stretches out in the west and south, but declines back into the marsh in the north and east.
101566: In the east numerous trees are spread out from the forest in the horizon. They have attempted to claim this land, but the soft ground sick with water and mud has rendered it impossible. Rotten stems and moss-covered trunks tell stories of unfortunate attempts of trees settling. Only a few have managed to send their roots through the moss into healthy soil hidden beneath the mire.
101567: Tall yellow flowers cover the moist ground, prospering in the lowland.

By the look of this confusing landscape the grey and green mosses have played in the sinks of water, resting their soft bodies against dead branches and shallow rocks. The result is an obscure pattern of undulating mire making no attempt at an ordered growth.
101568: Tall yellow flowers cover the moist ground, prospering in the lowland.

On the ground rotting leaves and branches are spread out between the peaks of mosses and lichen. A struggling forest is located in the south, and these branches are the results of the attempts of the forest at spreading into the wet marshes. The steep border of the Gladden climbs to the fields above. Along the sides of the border grey grass with sharp stems covers the earth and moss. From beyond this grass the flow of the mighty Anduin can be heard.
101569:
The corpse of a forest spider is lying here.
A forest spider is here crawling around.
A forest spider is here crawling around.
A fallow deer is grazing peacefully here.

This patch of trees has broken in on the soggy grounds of the Gladden Fields. At its borders the earth has become too wet and soft for the sturdy roots to grip the soil. It serves as the borders of this small forest. In the east a moist field stretches out between the trees and the Anduin, and some of the young pines have started to spread in that direction, extending the edge of the wood.
101570:
A relentless uruk of the Morgundul tribe is leading his soldiers here.
An orc-guard of the Morgundul is on patrol here.
An orc-guard of the Morgundul is on patrol here.

When the wind comes from the east these fields are sprayed with a gentle mist from the Anduin. Even as the wind seize, the dew holds firmly to the swaying grass, with never-ending moisture. In the west a mossy wall of trees grows closely together, clinging to each other in the mossy ground as if to avoid sinking into the earth. Some of the trees have immigrated into these fields, but the rest quickly turn away in the north and south.
101571:
The corpse of a vulture is lying here.
The corpse of a vulture is lying here.
A speckled, brown and white bird with a long curved bill stands here.

Following the shores of the Anduin to the south, these fields get cornered in by the border of the Gladden Fields and the steep banks of the Great River. The earth is damp and moist, but the grey moss of the west has not completely filled the plains. The rain that falls gets transported either into the swampy grounds in the west, or the river in the east. This leaves the ground with a healthy moisture giving place for flowers and fragile stems of grass. To the west a sharp slippery decline leads into the marsh.
101572: Cramped in between the Anduin and the Gladden Fields, these fields are covered in a gentle mist. The roaring of the Great River rushes over the plains, and a strong scent of decay flows in from the west. Yellow flowers grow in patches, and in the west sturdy grey grass decorates the border of the marshes. A sharp drop into the marsh makes travelling this way impossible.
101573: The wild ox seems ready to charge you.

Yellow patches of gentle flowers spot the land, spreading out in the grass that still stands tall in the soft ground. The rushing sound of the Anduin flows in over the lands, and its sparkling flow glitters in the south-east. Sturdy grey stems of grass grow in row after row at the border of the Gladden in the west, and a sharp slippery decline leads into the soggy marsh.
101574: The wild ox seems ready to charge you.

Dead rotting branches of the brush reach in from the north. The ground has become soft and soggy, and unusable for the woody stems of bushes and tangles that try to complete their ruling of the lands. Orange grass still sways gently in the plains, but the earth is spotted with moss and lichen.
101575:
The remains of a clump of roots lie here in a heap of rotting compost.
A large thorny branched shrub is growing here.
A mass of wriggling vines drops on you from the trees.

On this peak in the undulating fields a noticeable part of the ground is covered with short brown shrubs and tangles, which make riding through here difficult. Their woody stems are spotted with delicate green leaves, desperately holding on to the bark. At the sharp border of the brush-covered hill and the green swaying hay in the west, intricate patterns of grass and tangles are formed close to the ground. Higher up the grass stands proudly above the bushes, majestically swaying when the wind blows.
101576:
A diamond-back rattlesnake is coiled here, ready to strike.
A mass of wriggling vines drops on you from the trees.

All around small sturdy tangles and shrubs cover the earth. The hollows beneath the branches, close to the ground, make perfect homes for snakes and lizards. They also make the terrain rather dangerous for those travelling on horseback. The brush spreads out over a hill with sharp impassable edges in the north and west, but gently levels in the east and south.
101577: Clusters of slender stems and tall leaves thrive in the mud and shallows.

An itching odour rises from the ground, soaked in rot and decay. Along with it a thick mist spreads a few feet above the moss and pools of water like a blanket cuddling the land. Between the isles of moss, muddy water runs to and fro in an intricate pattern that runs miles at end in all directions. A peninsula in the marsh stretches in from the north and drops sharply into the soaked land. A branch of it divides the waters a bit further in the east.
101578:
Tall yellow flowers cover the moist ground, prospering in the lowland.
Clusters of slender stems and tall leaves thrive in the mud and shallows.
A frog is standing here.
A frog is standing here.

Patches of grey moss and lichen float like isles in the shallow waters. An occasional rotting tree springs up where the ground is firmer, but mostly the landscape is flat and rolling, covered with moss and pools of water. At the sides of the moss, small yellow flowers stick to the ground, avoiding the murky waters below.
101579:
Clusters of slender stems and tall leaves thrive in the mud and shallows.
A frog is standing here.
A frog is standing here.

Dead branches and leaves cover the soft moss on the wet ground. In the north, the origin of these can be spotted in the form of a small forest reaching into the marshes. To the east a sharp ascent up to the higher fields above lies in the way of travelling. It is covered with sturdy straws of grey grass spreading out even into the plains above. To the south a heavy thicket of ensnared branches and rotting grass covers the shores of a gathering of water.
101580: Tall yellow flowers cover the moist ground, prospering in the lowland.

The undulating marshland reaches out, covering the ancient lake floor with moss and lichen that peaks up between the countless pools of dark water. An occasional shrub or tree draws its silhouette against the sky beyond. Roots and undulating water-soaked lichen make the way west impossible to pass.
101581: Green and flourishing, these fields lie snugly in a valley at the turn of the Anduin in the east and south. The Great River's rushing water echoes over the land. The ground is soft and wet, caused by the close relation to the flowing water, but the level earth serves as good growth place for grass and flowers. Close in the north a large gathering of rocks and debris has been gathered next to a few sturdy pines, forming a moderately concealed hovel in the field. Peaking out from the top, a column of rocks and crudely cut boards form a watch tower, not higher then the trees next to it, but protected with a slanting roof and walls in all directions.
101582: A speckled, brown and white bird with a long curved bill stands here.

Not far in the east the gentle murmur of the Anduin current echoes through the land. These fields are once in a while filled with the rising water as the bending river sometimes cannot follow its destined path. Rain and dew also choose these fields as a course towards the flowing water of the Anduin. This results in a soft and muddy field sparsely filled with swaying hay and the shrubs reaching in from the north rotting away in the mist. In the south a rocky mound blocks the path along the river.
101583: A huge, black wolf is here, ready to devour.
The soil is soft and wet, spotted with moss and lichen. The rain that falls occasionally drains to the south and east ending up in the Anduin. Shrubs and tangles reach in from the north and west.
101584: A mass of wriggling vines drops on you from the trees.

Low shrubs reaching to the knees of a full-grown man, cover parts of this landscape. The tall swaying grass is however not ready to ease its firm grip of the fields. In the mixture of brush and orange grass, flowers and herbs take the opportunity to flourish and fill the air with sweet scents.
101585: The tangles and shrubs stretch in from the north crawling over the land as if alive. Between the bushes moss and flowers struggle for a piece of earth. A scent of wood and resin fills the misty air. In the southeast the glittering shores of the Great River sparkle when it curls through the fields.
101589: The tangles of shrubs crawling in from the north meet their sudden end here. The far shores of the Anduin are soft and drenched with moist. Here the roots and life of the brush quickly rot away, loosening their grip in the soil. The stems that have survived here are spotted with moss and lichen. Instead the fields are patterned with fragile straws of green grass, and small yellow flowers.
101590: Almost no trees grow on this bank of the river, whereas a hedgerow clearly outlines the riverbed in the southeast. The ground slopes gently away from the riverbed, turning from an undulating meadow of weeds into a flat field. Large rocks break the hedge in some places, but climbing up on them would not give a much better view over the river.
101591:
Tall yellow flowers cover the moist ground, prospering in the lowland.
On the cluster, there are two tall yellow irises.

Pools of water running across the land make the rather large patches of moss look like islands in a sea. Looking closer, the water is however rather shallow, with more moss and mud beneath. Only the mire knows how deep this moss runs. Far in the south, beyond mile upon mile of marshland, the two rivers Anduin and Gladden River connect in a sparkling display. A sharp drop filled with flowing water cuts the undulating marshes in the west.
101592: Marshes between the Gladden and the Anduin

Clusters of slender stems and tall leaves thrive in the mud and shallows.
Tall yellow flowers cover the moist ground, prospering in the lowland.

This little piece of the marsh neighbours the bends of the two, nearby rivers. The Gladden makes a turn towards the south right to the west, while the Anduin follows its considerably straight route in the south-east. The soil is humid, and its lowest parts are often transformed into puddles.
101593: The River Gladden makes one of its last bends here, before it meets the large Anduin, which then continues southbound. The surrounding landscape is mainly constituted of marshes; however some remote, dark green spots may be forests, which appear to be medium-sized.
101594: Tall yellow flowers cover the moist ground, prospering in the lowland.

The mossy turfs slope away towards the Gladden River in the south. Although the ground is sloping gently the pools of water have a firm stand in the earth, not flowing in any direction. Close to the ground, a thick layer of mist lies as a carpet over the waters and a stench of rot and decay fills the air. A sharp incline in the marsh creates a steep streaming slope in the east.
101595: Along the Shores of the Gladden River

Tall yellow flowers cover the moist ground, prospering in the lowland.
A frog is standing here.
A frog is standing here.

A sharp turn of the Gladden River cuts through the marshes here, dragging away turfs of moss and lichen in its stream. The water roars as it passes and stretches out again towards the south. The moss and mud, already sick with water, are desperately holding a stand against the rushing water at the banks of the current.
101596: A prominent slope of the marsh reaches southwards into the Gladden River. Small streams of flowing water stretch away, trying to reach the current in the south. The heavy patches of moss peaking up from the shallow waters point out in all directions, but in the south they come to an abrupt end in the streaming waters. A firm scent of decay dominates the impression of this mire.
101597:
A blooming water-lily floats on the surface of the water.
A frog is standing here.

Dark muddy waters flow quietly between large patches of moss and lichen. Turfs of grey hay stand wherever the ground is firm enough to support their fragile roots. Between the straws, yellow flowers struggle on the soft ground. The whole area is covered in a strange mist ascending from the ground, and with it a scent of decay and rotten earth rises.
101598: Tall yellow flowers cover the moist ground, prospering in the lowland.

This incline in the marsh stands in sharp contrast to the surrounding mire. Here green grass can grow freely as the soggy ground is turned into more manageable soil. On the surrounding borders of the isle yellow flowers and high thick grass grow in rows. Beyond the isle the dense mist reaches up from the moist ground. It does not reach this hill, but stays around it like clouds around a mountain. A snare of roots and water-soaked lichen makes the path to the east impossible to pass.
101599:
Tall yellow flowers cover the moist ground, prospering in the lowland.
A frog is standing here.

From drenched moss and lichen this incline has ascended into a large island in the marshes, dry in comparison with the surrounding mire. Flowers and green grass hold to its firm soil with rigid determination. While the ground is much drier than the surrounding marsh it is still drenched in water and walking on the springy surface reveals water flowing beneath the mud. In the south branches and grass, gathered by the barely visible streams, create a natural barrier.
101600: The corpse of a horse-fly is lying here.

In contrary with most other parts of these marshes, the water here does not lie calmly in its pockets; it rather moves in a fluent motion into the south. The quiet stream is fed by the countless pools of water in the north, and gains speed as it moves ahead towards the Gladden River further away. The floor of the mire is stirred by the moving water, and mud and dirt fills the current. To the east a steep slope feeds more water from the marshes above.
101601:
The corpse of a watersnake is lying here.
Clusters of slender stems and tall leaves thrive in the mud and shallows.

Large isles of moss and wet soil come together and serve as a resting point for travellers daring to venture into these lands. They also serve as growing ground for the small type of yellow flowers, so common in these marshes. Between the mossy isles dark pools of water cover the ancient lake floor.
101603:
Clusters of slender stems and tall leaves thrive in the mud and shallows.
Tall yellow flowers cover the moist ground, prospering in the lowland.
A long rat with a white-tipped tail seems indifferent to your presence.

The large Anduin unevenly borders this quite flat marsh to the south-east. The humid soil has been covered by some high weeds, but there are a couple of tall bushes that are noticed here and there. Several puddles, all hidden under the vegetation, may sometimes be a cold surprise.
101604:
Tall yellow flowers cover the moist ground, prospering in the lowland.
Clusters of slender stems and tall leaves thrive in the mud and shallows.
A water moccasin slithers out of sight just below the surface of the water.

The water from the gently flowing Anduin trickles in from the east. A soft, almost distant, clucking noise of the river can be heard, as if coming from further away than the actual current. The ground is soggy, filled with water and moisture. The water has seemingly coagulated in the ground and formed a thicker form of liquid, greyish in colour. An itching mist rises from the soft earth, leaving little sight of the ground. To the north a large cluster of rotting branches and grass has gathered near a pool of water. To the sides sharp slopes makes travelling difficult, dropping into the marshes in the west and the rapid water of the Anduin in the east.
101605: A crayfish is here, snapping its claws at you.

Some middle-sized stones, most being covered by mosses and small algae on their sides, brush the surface of the water, creating small eddies in this otherwise calm and slow-flowing river. Some larger ones are visible to the west, probably created in the river bend located there.
101606: End of a Bend in the Gladden

A heron is stalking the area, looking for fish.
A fat carp swims here.
A bass swims here.

This is the site of one of the last bends in the Gladden. Hereafter the river heads straight east where it meets the great Anduin. It flows regularly on its pebble-strewn riverbed, except around a lone huge rock that rises taller than a man out of the water. It seems to have been stuck in the middle of the stream for ages, something that is made evident by its smooth surface at water level.
101607:
Clusters of slender stems and tall leaves thrive in the mud and shallows.
Tall yellow flowers cover the moist ground, prospering in the lowland.
A worm is here slithering around.

Here, the damp ground slopes gently downwards, as it dives under a bend in the Gladden. South of here, the stream flows in from the west towards the east. A few pebbles, hidden among the roots of the low and sparse vegetation, are covered by wet mosses which cause the riverbank to be slippery and the travel somewhat dangerous.
101608: A Slight Bend in the Gladden

A long rat with a white-tipped tail seems indifferent to your presence.
A large pike is lurking in the mud by the bottom.

The Gladden makes a bend here in its path from the mountains, which is visible to the north-west. This appears to be one of the last curves of the riverbed before it meets the Anduin. While the northern riverbank forms into a gentle slope, the southern riverbank has an abrupt wall of earth that stands close to five feet tall in height.
101609: The flow of the Gladden is slow here, steered between a gentle slope towards the northwest and an earthen wall of medium height standing in both the south and the east. Between the rare patches of weeds growing on the vertical surface, some small holes can be distinguished.
101610:
Clusters of slender stems and tall leaves thrive in the mud and shallows.
Tall yellow flowers cover the moist ground, prospering in the lowland.

This flat slope is leading downwards to the Gladden river, which currently flows from the north, then into the west. There is a heap of brick-sized stones, which may have been aligned towards the north-west long ago, but the elapsed time and the occasional water overflows dislocated them.
101611: Marshes by a Bend in the Gladden

Clusters of slender stems and tall leaves thrive in the mud and shallows.
Tall yellow flowers cover the moist ground, prospering in the lowland.
A long-necked bird, with a fairly short spear-like bill stands here.

This part of the marsh appears to look as though there is an outcropping of some earth above the Gladden. It appears to border it with a bend in its flow, coming from the west, then passing to the north. Directing itself to the east, it then takes a last noticeable curve in its bend towards the south.
101612:
A fat carp swims here.
A long rat with a white-tipped tail seems indifferent to your presence.

This is the last, straight part of the River Gladden; after its northern bend it now flows slowly towards a last turn to the south. Its widening, muddy riverbed is bordered on both sides by vast marshes, sometimes covered by some dark grass. In spite of the material it flows on, the water is rather clear.
101613: North of the Meeting of the Rivers

Clusters of slender stems and tall leaves thrive in the mud and shallows.
Tall yellow flowers cover the moist ground, prospering in the lowland.
A speckled, brown and white bird with a long curved bill stands here.

This thin strip of the marshes is stuck between the parallel riverbeds of the Gladden to the west and of the Anduin to the east. Towards the south, part of the vegetation-covered land dives slowly below the water level, allowing both of the rivers to meet each other.
101614: This flat piece of land ends abruptly to the north, where there is a steep drop down to the river. However, though most of the riverbank is flat, there are a few collapsed areas of the soil, covered by some dark grass, which allows an easy access to the river that flows several feet below.
101615: A swarm of mosquitoes is here, humming around you.

While the surrounding landscape is flat, this part of the field here is slightly higher than its surroundings. It would allow a clear view of the nearby marshes if it was not buried in a forest of yellow flowers. To the north, the Gladden's bank can be reached after a gentle, downward slope in which a few stones are embedded.
101616: This part of the marshes forms a slight gentle slope, between the upper marshes to the north and a little terrain depression southwards. Four stones have been placed to form a little circle, where one could easily keep a campfire burning. Some rotten branches have been piled up around these stones, perhaps some kind of precarious night shelters months ago.
101617: This part of the marsh, slightly higher than the surrounding piece of the land, is bordered to the east by the calm flow of the Gladden. There is a slight, but noticeable slope that travels downwards to the south-west, where an oval shape can be distinguished.
101618: The Last Bend in the Gladden

After a straight part to the north, the Gladden bends around a bushy riverbank, located in the northeast, and finally meets the great Anduin river to the east. The bed is now quite large and flat, with a rather thin water layer that covers it, while some islets are emerging here and there.
101619: The soft sound of the two rivers that border this rocky part of the marshes, then meet in the north-east, is to be heard here. The Gladden flows to the north into the small meeting lake, while the resulting waters flow eastward, then south from here.
101620: Marshes between a Pool and Two Rivers

This portion of the marsh is quite elevated here, abruptly cut off to the north-east by the enlarging bed of the Gladden. Another natural border lies to the south-east, where the Anduin river creates a natural border. The western part of the marsh lowers itself slowly through a slope, towards a large pool which is visible in the distance. The soil here is covered by some dense, but mostly very low vegetation.
101621:
A large leech is moving close to you, searching for blood.
A long slender eel glides along the water, its body coiled to strike.
A small leech is here, floating in the water.
A large pool of mud is spreading here.
A stocky mountain mule is here, waiting to serve.

Some event in the history of the marsh has made this place lower than its surroundings. The area is on the same level as the two rivers, the Anduin and the Gladden, which flow several miles to the north and the east. The bottom of this depression is now filled up with water, creating the large, opaque pool that lies here now.
101622: Sticking out of the low vegetation, and marking the landscape, stands an old, dead and twisted tree. It may have been an oak, though it is hard to tell since its bark has been torn away by the passing years. Nearby, one can spot some water-filled holes, deeper and larger than usual, which seem to be the last traces of similar elders.
101623: A large pool of mud is spreading here.

The few, low patches of tangled rushes add a clear tone to the otherwise sombre colour of this flat marshland. Some puddles are scattered behind them, where there are many pebbles of varying sizes. Most of these pebbles have been covered by a thin layer of dark, green moss.
101624: A long-necked bird, with a fairly short spear-like bill stands here.

Some shrubs and low trees are growing here on this slightly damp patch of ground. While some thick-stemmed rushes can be found here, the vegetation is not quite dense enough to hinder travel. It is, however, thicker than the surroundings, except southwards where it transforms into a wooded area.
101625: There is a continuation of all the western vegetation here, leaving the area to be covered by scattered bushes, slightly darker than the low weeds that are in growth between them. This appears to form a basin between the higher marsh that is northwards and the forest that is visible to the southwest.
101626: This gentle slope in the marshes connects the large pool that is visible in the northern depression with the surrounding average marsh level. The surrounding vegetation is mostly lower than the western one that comprises some very widely scattered bushes, adding some height to the area.
101627: Marshes by a Bend in the Anduin

The marsh here is slightly higher than the surrounding area, that ranges from the north to the southwest. A terrain depression appears to be lying in the northwest, while the large Anduin can be noticed flowing slowly around here, from the east to the south.
101628: Creeping tangles of some bulrushes can slow travel in the northern parts of this place. However, they are progressively replaced towards the south by a few, low trees. Some thickets of small birches add a white touch to the otherwise darker tones of this wooded marsh.
101629: This may be the border of what was once a cultivated field of flax plants long ago, since the proportion of this plant among the weeds is higher than normal, especially to the south. The former cultures are bordered by a forest towards the south and the west.
101630: The low, but rather dense, vegetation contains a small part of useful plants. Most of these are located in the neighbourhood of what appears to have been an ancient field towards the southward. There are some vaguely aligned slabs along an north-south axis which might be the remains of a trail.
101631: According to the amount of wild useful plants growing here, this part of the marshes was once a cultivated field. Among others, flax plants seem to be the most present in the west, but some cereals are also noticeable in the rest of the field.
101632: Mixed weeds, medium shrubs and many flax plants have formed the vegetation of this humid field. There is a relatively flat corner which cuts through into the forest that is visible in both directions to the west and south. A small ruin can be noticed through the first, southern trees.
101633: These low woods are the continuation of the relatively small, southern forest. The trees here are fairly small, widely spaced out from one another and mixed with various shrubs. While this woody area somewhat extends itself northwards, the landscape to the east seems to be much clearer.
101634: None of the surrounding trees seem to be of an exceptional size. The trees are mostly beeches and dark oaks, but some birches somewhat lighten the tones that are introduced by the latter. A thin layer of mixed twigs have nearly hid the sight of the soft ground.
101635: The Border of a Forest at a Small Ruin

The forest forms a little clearing, which surrounds a small ruin. The trees seem to disappear northwards, however, leaving place to a flat landscape. Some climbing weeds are growing along the walls of the ruin. The walls appear to be in very poor condition, but they are still holding parts of the ruined roof up.
101636: The very dense trees darken this place greatly. None of these trees seem to be very high, however. Maybe is it because of the unstable and damp ground, which seemingly caused the tallest of the trees to fall, leaving some large cavities in the flat forest soil.
101637: While some wheat plants can be seen here and there, the main vegetation growing in this area is some high grass, which seems to be smothering most of the weeds. Some of them are, however, climbing upon the wall of the small ruin that lies to the west.
101638: There are no pieces of furniture standing on the floor in this room. The soil is made of raw earth, except for a small path of broken slabs between its western and eastern doors. While the roof is still complete, it seems ready to collapse and bears a regular hole in its centre. The remains of a small campfire can be noticed underneath it.
101639: Formerly supported by walls in poor shape, the northern part of the roof has fallen down, ruined by the years and a termite colony. The debris is not the only thing lying on the ground, however, since cubic shapes are standing in each corner of the room, next to what may have been chimneys.
101643: The Border of a Thick Forest

The thick forest, which appears to continue to the north and east, comes to an end suddenly, leaving an area of flat and damp plains. The various trees that have grown here are less dense than the rest of the trees in the forest, just letting enough light pass through their foliage for some small bushes to grow beneath them.
101644:
A small termite is running around making strange sounds.
A small termite is running around making strange sounds.
A small termite is running around making strange sounds.
Massive roots shift uneasily all around you.
A giant termite is here, crushing skulls and bones.

This moist cavity in the ground, which is about five feet deep, is filled by the odour of decaying, large roots that are still stuck into the earth here. Judging by the holes in the walls, some of them were violently pulled out, probably when the large tree that once grew here fell.
101645: A swan swims gracefully on the surface of the water.

Some puddles can be noticed between the roots of the eastern trees, that seem to connect with the river which flows in that direction. Towards the northwest, the relief is a bit higher. The trees have grown very thick there, with their roots containing some small holes between them.
101646: The opaque, waist-high water here is almost totally covered with ferns and some other vegetation, making it impossible to discern what might be found beneath the surface. South of here, the ground appears to be decidedly firmer, whereas the soggy reaches of the swamp continues east of here.
101647:
A heron is stalking the area, looking for fish.
A heron is stalking the area, looking for fish.
A small leech is here, floating in the water.
A small leech is here, floating in the water.

Treacherous to say the least, the ground here is far below the fern-covered surface of the sluggishly moving swamp water. The swamp continues west and south of here, whereas to the east, the pace of the water can be noticed picking up speed as the main current of the river Anduin cuts through the landscape.
101648:
Some roots lie here waiting to ensnare weary travellers.
A woodpecker is here, tapping on a tree.

The forest is very dense from all of the numerous oaks that have grown here. A few, lonely weeds are in a great struggle to grow, due to the ground that lies beneath them being permanently shadowed. The lowest part of these tree trunks do not bear any living branch, probably because there would not be enough light at this level. Low dead branches, however, impede any mounted movement.
101649:
A small chick is in the nest squawking at his mother for food.
A small chick is in the nest squawking at his mother for food.

While taller trees block the view in the other directions, it is quite possible to have a peek at the eastern Anduin. The load-bearing branches of this oak are hopefully still thick enough to safely carry some weight, but going any further would become dangerous.
101650: A Forest Bordered by the Anduin
A sturdy pack horse is standing here.

This part of the forest is made of oaks for the most part, however, it appears less dense than the trees that stand westwards. The ground is slightly higher than the water level of the Anduin, which flows east of the forest here. The ground here is not high enough to prevent the formation of puddles between the roots of some of the trees though.
101651: The firm yet springy soil here is covered with huge clumps of an unusual sort of grass: it is at least four feet high and sports a dark, dark hue of green. It is quite obvious that the lushness of this field is due to the proximity of the Gladden Fields north and east of here. Further east from here, the mighty river Anduin flows steadily through the lands.
101652: A speckled, brown and white bird with a long curved bill stands here.

Cold all year around, these blackish waters at first seem to be standing still. Yet, upon closer inspection, a swift movement in the water can be observed below the water-lily covered surface. The Anduin, whose mighty flow can be seen east from here, obviously barely bothers to stir these weed-infested swamps.
101653: A speckled, brown and white bird with a long curved bill stands here.

The characteristic giant leaves of water-lilies are nearly covering the somewhat stagnant surface of these leech-infested marshlands. East and south, the main current of the mighty Anduin speeds southwards on its way to the sea, whereas the Gladden Fields continue northwards. West of here, the ground looks a lot firmer, supporting a stand of thin-trunked, gnarly birch trees.
101654: Far firmer than the swampy marsh east of here, this field is covered by several species of lush grass and finger-sized ferns. A handful of gnarly birches also grow here, eagerly drinking the plentiful water that saturates these somewhat spongy fields.
101655: Far from flat, this rugged riverside field features a number of jagged boulders. These huge rocks appear to be the nesting spot for some of the local birdlife, at least judging from the plentiful droppings on and around them. Looking east, one can bask in the sight of the mighty Anduin rounding a corner, as it cuts a path through the undulating grasslands and high-grown old forests of this part of Arda.
101656: Gently sloping down towards the Anduin river east of here, this grassy plain is dotted with jagged rocks and some hardy juniper bushes. By the river's edge, a pile of fist-sized rocks comprise something that could almost be described as a natural jetty, poking out fifteen yards from the bank into the river. Downstream from the jetty, the lack of current forms a haven of slower-flowing water.
101657: A speckled, brown and white bird with a long curved bill stands here.

Thick green, almost carpet-like growth covers this springy strip of turf by the river Anduin. East of here, a small copse comprised of a handful of slender saplings partly obscures the view of the river. The outskirts of a thicker forest can be seen south from here.
101658: Being amply provided with water by the neighbouring river Anduin, this mixed forest is comprised of a number of different tree species. However, quite a few of them appear to be afflicted by some kind of parasite that makes their trunks look all scurfy and rough. The forest continues further south, whereas north of here, a broken plain opens up.
101659: A small brown snake is slithering around here.

Dark, yet somehow not that imposing, this riverside forest sports a mix of old firs, oaks and alder trees. Whereas the same type of vegetation appears to continue north from here, the forest to the south seems both lighter and younger. East, the mighty river Anduin can be glimpsed between the trunks of the trees.
101660: The butchered corpse of a female elk is lying here.

This riverside forest is comparatively light, at least when one glances at the older and thicker part north of here. Mostly birch and alder trees grow at this particular spot, interspersed with the occasional fir and pine tree. The undergrowth consists mainly of some light-green, high grass, along with a few other hardier kinds of shrubs and ferns. South from here, the forest thins out and gradually gives way to a grassy plain.
101661: A large thorny branched shrub is growing here.

This would be the ideal setting for a camp, if it were not for the jagged rocks that litter this grassy plain. North and east from here, a dark evergreen forest obscures the view of the river Anduin. There is no denying that the river is there though, since the noise and smell of that major waterway easily carries on over to this spot.
101662: A fallow deer is grazing peacefully here.

Long blades of grass, along with many slender weeds, fill the meadow here. Some of these grass blades are a light shade of green and very long; their ends often curl over. Brown, drier blades of grass stand out in tufts here and there in the meadow.
101663: Many shades of green fill the meadow between the long grasses, weeds, and other kinds of vegetation. There is an occasional plant that is slightly brown in colour among the green grass. Most of these brown plants though, are vaguely noticeable because of the overwhelming amount of green throughout the meadow. There are also a few small saplings growing on the eastern side.
101664: The rich soil that beds the meadow is very soft, with brightly coloured green grass to cover it. There are only a few bushes blended among the grass of the meadow and they are very short in height. The bushes are not very wide either. They are adorned by many bundles of small, oval shaped leaves. The meadow appears to continue to the south, though it begins to fade on the far eastern edge along a riverbank.
101667: The river flows by just east of the bank here. There are several rocks, stones and small pebbles that align the bank at the waters edge. They are all different shades of brown, grey, black, and even a few maroon coloured ones. Some are small, and a few of them are rather large. Each one has its own unique texture and finish to it. The bank continues towards the south, with a meadow on the western edge of the bank.
101668: A brown fox is here, looking for some rabbits to chew up.

Large, circular and oval-shaped stones line the bank at the waters edge. The Anduin runs swiftly in a southward flow, east of the bank. A few reeds have sprouted on the south edge of the bank, right along the water. Grass from the western meadow thins out as it blends into the weeds along the bank.
101669: A fallow deer is grazing peacefully here.

Many different coloured stones lie along the edge of the riverbank. The stones have various shades to them, as well as different types of textures. Some of these are brown with a rough texture, others being a shade of grey that have a flat, smooth texture. The western meadow slowly emerges its growth, leaving a few patches of grass along the bank.
101670: A brown fox is here, looking for some rabbits to chew up.

The rushing water of the Great River Anduin swiftly flows southbound just east of the riverbank. The long grass from the meadow meets the rocky riverbank, with some iris plants of different colours mixed in between. The stones that line the bank have a glossy finish to them, and they vary greatly in colour. The grass from the nearby meadow to the west has grown over onto a small portion of the bank. Several trees are visible towards the north, where a forest grows.
101671:
A small patch of dark-green moss grows in the deepest shade.
A colony of red ants is here. The ants seem to ignore you.

This forest of great, grizzled old firs looms above the swift-flowing surface of the Anduin. The trees are old, and their crowns are thick enough to block out quite a lot of the sky, which probably explains the relative sparseness of undergrowth. North and east of here one can see the surface of the mighty river Anduin.
101672: The bank, as it continues further south, makes a very steep decline from here. There are a lot of small pebbles and stones that lie atop the drier soil of the bank. However as the bank makes its decline the soil becomes very soft, with larger stones of an odd shape that line the bank closer to the waters edge. Towards the south-east corner of the bank, many reeds have clustered together in their growth. It appears the course of the river shifts along this particular bank, as it flows south into a sharp curve leading back towards the west. The curve of the river has caused the bank to have a rounded shape as the river borders both the eastern and southern bank here.
101673: The riverbank is quite wide here, as if the river had at one time overcome much of the bank. Scattered along the bank are a few stones, along with some oddly grown patches of weeds in different locations. The bank forms a very steep incline to both the north and west, where it appears to meet a wild meadow on both those edges.
101674:
A large bonfire is burning here.
An orc-guard of the Morgundul is on patrol here.
An orc-guard of the Morgundul is on patrol here.

Behind a small wooden gate a chamber opens up, larger than one might expect from the outside. Inside the walls are dark and crude, and little attention has been given to details and perfection. As a matter of fact the large rocks and other debris seem to barely hold together, but serve as the needed shelter it was created for. Along one side of the room a roaring fire burns with an intense glow fed by large beams of wood and the many holes in walls, letting air flow through it. At the opposite side of the fire a flimsy ladder leads up through a hole in the rocky ceiling. Straight ahead a small opening of which half is dug in the earth, leads down a short slope further into the hovel.
101675:
A wooden chest stands in the corner.
A large cockroach is crawling up the wall.
A large cockroach is crawling over the floor.

A few blankets, worn and filthy, are spread over the dirty floor. The walls in this room are mostly made of the dirt of the very earth. Only close to the rocky ceiling stones and debris form the protection from the fields above. There is a rigid stench flowing in the air, and the room is cold and damp, reminding more of a cellar than a living quarter. In one of the corners a heavy chest has been placed.
101676:
A beer bottle has been left here.
A large cockroach is crawling over the floor.

A ladder reaches from the chamber below, and after several yards the narrow tunnel arrives at a small crude watch tower. On either sides of the hole created by the tunnel a few feet wide ledge serves as an outpost for watching the lands. The ledge is enclosed by rocky walls reaching up a yard or two, serving as protection from wind and rain. The ceiling consists of a sloping hoard of debris created in such a manner that it protects more from the burning sun than falling rain. Remains of numerous meals lie spread around the opening, telling about the countless hours spent on guard here.
101677: A Sandy Beach at the Riverbank

This beach reaches further into the river than the grassy banks; it looks like most of it would be under the water if the surface was a few feet higher. The river has left bundles of loose branches, leaves and hay on the beach, where they slowly rot under the sun. A dead trunk sticks out of the sand several yards away from the water, leaning towards the ground. The droppings on the trunk indicate that birds must often sit there, watching the river.
101678: Thick layers of mud along with tufts of hardy grasses cover the ground here. A narrow stream flows in from the east and carries fine sand and clay into the Anduin, clouding the water near the bank. The furrow of the stream widens as it turns into a muddy ditch farther inland, where it continues to the east past grassy fields and meadows of flowers.
101679: A Field of Weeds and Flowers

Dry weeds and woody stems snap and crackle whenever anything moves around in these fields. Some dead flowers lie on the ground, and their rotting petals still show hints of crimson and blue. Tall grasses grow in the south, where a slope leads away from the riverside into a rocky area. Short bushes outline the course of an overgrown trail leading east and west.
101680: Old Ruins of a Water Mill
A robin is here, carrying small pieces of wood to its nest.

Some bushes and tall trees grow near the riverbank here, partly obscuring the view of the old structure of a stone building. It might well have once been a working water mill; it is built close to the river, and the stream near the rocky bank seems strong enough to turn a pair of millstones. It looks like there was once a trail leading to the east from the yard of the building, but the ground is now covered in weeds and short bushes.
101681:
A low shrub with bright green, oblong leaves is growing here.
Scattered in and on the shrub, there are two piles of blueberries.
A colony of red ants is here. The ants seem to ignore you.

Clusters of blueberries grow among the rocks and short birches here. The ground is hard and covered by dry leaves, sticks and splinters of wood which form neat lines along the ant trails in the undergrowth. The highest point in these dry fields, an outcrop of bare rock, is surrounded by a carpet of moss and stunted conifer trees.
101682: A black crow flies low to the ground here, looking for carrion to eat.

A carpet of grass and tiny flowers covers the ground here, just above the cliffs that border the riverbed of the Anduin. The ridge starts from the river's edge and continues to the east, where the vegetation seems to get taller. One could have a good look over the river from this open field, but one would also be in danger of being spotted oneself.
101683: A brown fox is here, looking for some rabbits to chew up.

The small dirt path running through the fields and shrubberies here does not look like it was made by animals. After following it for a while, a pair of boot prints, preserved in the hardened mud, can be noticed. Their size is quite small, but the tracks are too old to tell who passed through here. In the northwest, lush fields spread out towards the river, while in the opposite direction tall bushes dominate the landscape.
101684:
A robin is here, carrying small pieces of wood to its nest.
A great male deer with reddish hair and twisted antlers stands here proudly.

Round shrubs with large leaves grow in tightly packed groups here and there, covering this dry field. The ground declines slightly to the southeast, but moving that way seems as hard as going in any other direction; the paths amidst the shrubbery twist and bend as they lead through the narrow openings between bushes. A wider path, covered in grass and loose stones, leads through the field as it follows the direction of the slope.
101685: The bank of the river has turned into a landslide where roots and vegetation failed to hold the sand in place. In many spots the grassy mat suddenly ends at the waters edge, and a steep embankment of loose soil leads down to the river instead. A small path follows the course of the river here, and then disappears into the grass.
101686:
A speckled, brown and white bird with a long curved bill stands here.
A black crow flies low to the ground here, looking for carrion to eat.

Small ponds and puddles of water break the monotony of these wet plains near the banks of the Anduin. Clusters of irises and reeds thrive in the shallow waters, and tall weeds cover the higher grounds. A stretch of rocky fields farther away from the river offers an easier route through the plains, reaching from the riverside in the north to the sloping grounds in the south.
101687: This secluded valley seems to be teeming with life; here and there one can catch glimpses of small animals' tracks and tunnels amidst the thriving undergrowth. Starting from a spring near the ridge in the north, a small stream runs down to the bottom of the valley, where it quickly soaks into the ground; there it serves to nourish the thick clusters of various plants. Rocky fields separate this area of lush vegetation from the riverside wetlands in the west.
101690: Here, a gentle slope rises towards the high hills in the south. Stunted trees and bushes grow in some places, but there is a clear line of sight almost all the way down to the wide plains in the north and east. Moving along the hillside seems rather easy, and many paths lie open to travellers; paths leading past rocky outcroppings and dry fields.
101691: There seems to be no end to these plains. While looking over yet another grassy ridge, all one can see is sloping ground that spreads out towards the horizon. Travelling to the north seems easier than to the other directions, since going that way is mostly downhill. Luckily, there are several animal paths to help a traveller maintain his direction on the way through this featureless landscape.
101694: The grass grows high and thick here, covering most of the land. In the west the sparkle of the Anduin river reflects in the fields, the furious sound of its rushing water echoes even this far away. Bare scraped branches of small bushes and trampled flowers witness a great deal of activity here. Food is plentiful for the animals, and water can be found only a couple of miles to the west in the clear current of the Anduin.
101706: The ground on the bottom of this depression is muddy and it looks like it may be sinking down. Roots and loosely hanging branches of the tall bushes growing here hinder movement in most places, while the plains surrounding the hollow seem to offer easier paths for travellers. A puddle of water in the middle of this depression is full of rotting leaves and moss; the field is slowly turning into a peat bog.
101707: These sparsely wooded ridges offers good viewpoints over the plains for anyone willing to climb up the ridge here. A mounted traveller, however, would have no choice but to ride through the fields below the ridges, where the terrain seems perfect for setting up ambushes or lookouts. Decent paths are nowhere to be found, yet the old remains of a campsite among some rocks suggest that someone passes through here occasionally.
101708: In the surrounding areas, with the Anduin in the west and the Gladden stretching beyond it, are plains upon plains. This patch of hills stands out as a break in the lands. To the east the hills stretch a bit further, but quickly flatten out again. In the south a small forest grows on the feet of the hills. The ground is still covered with thick grass, but on some of the slopes rocks and gravel have been left bare under the sky.
101709: The hills in the north quickly flatten out here making room for trees to gather and form a colony next to the Anduin. The ground is soft and mossy, watered by the Anduin and numerous stains of water, gathered in pools beneath the trees. The trees themselves are covered in moss and lichen, and many have started to decay, rotting away in the wet climate.
101710: With the ground being raised slightly higher than the northern forest, this area is rather safe from the Anduin, which flows to the north-west. The bottoms of the tree trunks are covered by some green moss and some rotten branches can be seen among the fallen leaves.
101711: The ground, bearing patches of fallen leaves, is rather flat here, except in the south where it transforms into low slopes. The forest, mix of beeches and oaks, continues in all the directions, although only the northern part remains somewhat dense.
101712: A large elk is standing here, chewing grass and leaves.

The earth of these tree-covered slopes seems to be mixed with quite some large and irregular pebbles. To the south, the relief increases considerably, where most of the trees have faded and are finally leaving the place to a tall, rather bare hill. However, the hill can barely be noticed, through the thinner parts of the surrounding forest.
101713: The Anduin River borders to the west of this rather thin and mixed forest, which then thickens to the east. There is some relief, slight mounds and depressions here and there, however insignificant compared to the southern small and wooded hills.
101714: Small, thorny thickets are growing here and there, raising the relief of this otherwise rather flat riverbank, save from its south-eastern part maybe. It is bordered to the northwest by the Anduin, where some relatively small trees can also be found, especially near the eastern forest.
101715: Groups of young oaks and rowans stand out on these windswept hilltops. More trees can be seen in the south, where dense bushes border the outskirts of a forest. Bare outcrops of rock and fields of small flowers fill the hollows between the hills, while in the east a steep slope leads down to a patch of thick vegetation and grassy fields.
101716:
A small mushroom grows nearby.
A forest spider is here crawling around.

The slim trunks of the young trees that grow here bend slightly whenever there is a gust of wind. Brown leaves, fallen from the rowans and birches during last autumn, still cling to the twigs that stick out among the mossy rocks and stumps. The ground is damp, and the soil is bare near a spot where a large animal has been digging for roots or mushrooms to eat.
101717: These small hills, some only being low mounds, slightly rise up southwards. As they do, they appear to slowly lose their trees, finally matching the bare and low eminences that are visible in this direction. Westwards, they slowly fade into a rather bare and flat plain.
101718: Grassland in Front of a Hill

While there are wild weeds and grasses in growth upon the front of the southern hill, no thorn can be distinguished among them. The hill itself appears to be part of a larger portion of hills, ranging to the south. The nearest slope is nearly vertical and completely covered by climbing weeds.
101719: Taller hills overlook these lower ones from the west and east. All the nearby slopes are pretty steep, each covered by a slippery moss, making climbing the slopes to be nearly impossible. Besides reaching the forested hills that are to the north, it appears the terrain is safe to move southwards, along the flat parts between the slopes.
101720: The western slope of this tall hill, rather tight and slippery, leads to a sea of steep mounds, that is much darker than their surroundings. Though nearly vertical, the northern incline appears possible to climb down using the large and numerous stones that have been partly embedded in the earth.
101722: Unlike the similar mounds that are visible westwards, to the east stands a tall, green hill, having a top that is seemingly strewn with small bushes. While the slippery vegetable matter covering all of the area nearly prevents anyone from climbing any of the slopes, a safe and flat path can be found towards the south and the north.
101723: This tall hill is easily reachable from the northern one, by following a common, curved crest. While the western slope is rather steep and slippery, leading to a lower and natural eminence, the southern landscape is made of plains. They appear to be reachable by a bush-covered incline.
101724: The earth in this area is very slick and the thin, wet moss that has grown on the surrounding slopes does not make their climb less dangerous. The flat path between the hills quickly stops east after a few of dead-ends, while the southern one is blocked by a long mound.
101725: The hills here are rather small, but their slopes are steep and slippery. It is possible to safely walk and ride between them to the east and south, judging by its appearance. Besides a few dead-ends, there is no safe passage visible that leads northwards towards the higher hills. The tops of the trees of a forest are noticed behind the western hills.
101726: The slopes of these small hills are slippery and very tight, causing them to be very difficult to climb. The bottom of the slopes between the hills, while strewn with sharp protruding rocks, appears to be rather safe. A somewhat usable path can be found towards the north and the south.
101727: The hills here are much smaller than the ones that can be seen northwards in the distance. Their slopes are less steep, especially the one which leads to a lone, large mound to the south. The trees appear to border this range of hills in both directions to the west and east.
101728: Unlike the northern hills, this tall one is reachable using easy slopes. While the eastern slope soon transforms into a slightly wooded area, a similar mound can be seen westwards. However, the western eminence is lacking the several shrubs that are growing atop of this one. Distinguished among these are many boulders, partly buried into the ground.
101729: A couple of small trees is in growth on the top of this hill, separated from the northern forest by a bare and steep slope. While the hill continues east, towards the west and south there are some long and curved slopes that appear to finally lead to what seems to have been a trail long ago.
101730: The beech-covered, wide mounds that slightly hinder the movement in this area are quite flat, compared to the tall hill that stands westwards and is visible through the thinner parts of the surrounding foliage of the trees. Although the bottom of some of the depressions is wet, no moss that can be seen grows on the base of the trunks.
101731: A large thorny branched shrub is growing here.

Among the overgrown grass and the few bushes growing here, there are a couple of scattered slabs which are distinguished, the last remains of an old trail. This old trail appears to be leading to the Anduin, which is flowing only a couple of miles away to the north-west. There, it meets another old trail that lies in the nearby south-east, at the foot of a bare hill.
101732: Clusters of slender stems and tall leaves thrive in the mud and shallows.

This little triangle of wild grass is bordered by the Anduin to the west, after a vertical bank by some trees to the north-east. Also noticed, are the remains of a trail towards the south. Some vaguely rectangular and big stones can be seen lying here and there, partly buried into the earth.
101733: This appears to be the southwestern part of this thin forest. The trees in growth here are mainly beeches, but they mix with oaks towards the north. The remains of an old trail can be seen loosely bordering it, with a couple of lone, smaller trees growing among its dislocated slabs.
101734: A pack horse (Rood) is standing here (shrouded), ridden by you.

This thin, oaken forest is replaced in the west by a rather bare, green hill. To the north stand mildly high bushes, however spaced apart. In all the other directions, the forest continues, even though its tree species vary. There are more oak trees eastwards, but beeches are in growth to the south.
101735: The Centre of a Thin Forest
A half-decayed corpse of a goblin lies rotting on the ground.

The trees here are less sparse than the surrounding pieces of the thin forest. The forest contains mainly oaks, except to the south, where they are slowly replaced by beech trees. The growth of these trees comes to an end quite fast on the unstable, eastern hill slope. There are large holes that were left by the fallen trees, revealing some stone blocks that lie within.
101736: The Border of a Thin Forest

A huge, venomous spider is here.
A forest spider is here crawling around.
A disgusting forest troll is searching for fresh meat here.
A disgusting forest troll is searching for fresh meat here.
A brutish forest troll is hunting here, looking for some tasty flesh.
A disgusting forest troll is searching for fresh meat here.
A disgusting forest troll is searching for fresh meat here.

While the trees are slightly less thick than those which stand northwards, they are quite tall in height. This is probably due to all of the shadows cast down by the steep slopes of the hills, which are located to the east and south. At earth level, this area is very gloomy and rather damp, while the soil is covered by some sparse dark grass.
101737: This piece of the thin forest is constituted of sparse, but rather tall oaks. The size of these trees begins to decrease to the west, leaving the area to be a bush-covered plain. Towards the east, the top of a seemingly very old wall seems to emerge from the slope of the hill, its use probably forgotten a long time ago.
101738: A sturdy pack horse is standing here.

This part of the thin forest, bordered by the Anduin to the west and some bare hills to the north and the east, is growing on some mounds itself. The nearby slopes contain some piled, large rocks, which are mostly buried in the earth and vegetable matter.
101739: Between the Anduin and a Forest
Clusters of slender stems and tall leaves thrive in the mud and shallows.

For some reason, maybe from the unstable ground, the forest that circles around this bushy marsh to the east and the south, never expanded itself here, leaving place for wild weeds and mild bushes to grow on. The Anduin borders the place in the remaining directions.
101740: Remains of a Trail by the Anduin
Clusters of slender stems and tall leaves thrive in the mud and shallows.

Some scattered stones among many, wild weeds may be the remains of an ancient trail. It seems to be coming from the south-east, meeting the Anduin River that borders this little marsh to the west. There are large rocks that appear to form an embankment of some sort.
101741: The Great Anduin River bends around this lonely hill, which is covered by some wild grass. The eastern slope is bushier, as it sinks under the small forest that can be seen to the east. Some stones with a regular shape are noticed near the top of the hill, but their purpose remains unknown.
101742: While it is possible to follow the crests to reach the northern hills, among which a taller one stands out, the eastern and southern surroundings consist of quite smaller hills. The small hills are separated from the rest by very tight and mossy slopes. The western, woody slope leads to a thin forest.
101743: On the Top of a Hill

While the northern landscapes are rather flat, save from a small forest in the north-east, it becomes a sea of hills south from here. The nearby hills to the west and south from are continuous enough, that it is possible to reach them without having to climb much. However, the hills in the east are pretty small and only reachable by a tight, slippery slope.
101744: The height of this hill allows a great view on a small lake that is noticed to the immediate north-west, where the two rivers meet. On the other hand, there is a thin forest that stops at mid-height of the southern slope that does not permit anything to be watched in that direction. Although some bushes can be seen near the last trees, the top of the hill is rather bare, with its grassy monotony only broken by some large stones.
101749: A lone hawk soars high above you.

The ancient trail, now in very poor shape, comes straight from the east, ending in front of the Great Anduin River. The scattered slabs, among which wild weeds grow, appear to continue in the water by huge stone blocks. The blocks may have formed a pier for some small boats long ago, but they are now too dislocated to be of any use.
101750: This old trail, which wild weeds have now settled upon, is following a vague, west-east direction, from the Anduin towards the dark shape of Mirkwood. Then at some point, it makes a minor detour to the north, where it meets a blurred form among the high grasses, which could be the remnants of another trail.
101751: This old trail follows a west-east axis, but makes a gentle curve around the slope of the northern hill. It does not seem to have been used frequently, for large weeds are growing between most of the slabs. However, some of the plants have been recently crushed, possibly by some lost traveller or large animal.
101752: A brown fox is here, looking for some rabbits to chew up.

This old trail can be guessed to meet the Anduin, which is several miles to the west, but it is hard to tell whether it ever reaches the shadows of Mirkwood to the far east. Its slabs have been laid on the lower part of the gentle slope of the northern hill. Some of the slabs have been broken by whatever has travelled upon them.
101753: A lone hawk soars high above you.

This old trail appears to follow a vague west-east direction, however entire parts of it have disappeared. The used slabs have either been looted or maybe simply buried under the vegetable matter over the time. There are some small trees, probably the result of the nearby, northern forest which appears to further dislocate the path.
101754: A pack horse (Rood) is standing here (shrouded), ridden by you.

The nearby mounds and depressions are easily noticeable, even through the forest that is surrounding them. While most of the forest consists of beech trees, a few weeds are strewn over the rough mix of earth and angular pebbles. While the relief is less visible to the north, a whole range of steep hills stands to the west.
101755: A pack horse (Rood) is standing here (shrouded), ridden by you.

The hills here are rather low and would actually be better described as a succession of mounds and depressions. The soil is grassy and mixed with some irregular pebbles. There are also some lonely trees, probably the offspring of the southern forest, which can be seen marking the landscape here and there.
101756:
A brown fox is here, looking for some rabbits to chew up.
A pack horse (Rood) is standing here (shrouded), ridden by you.

The accentuated relief of the plain here nearly hinders travel, however, it is still easy to avoid the steepest slopes. While patches of mild bushes are in growth among the flat parts, none of this vegetation has grown above the size of an average shrub.
101757: A pack horse (Rood) is standing here (shrouded), ridden by you.

While these plains are somewhat uneven, made so by small mounds of earth, their slopes seem no taller than the short bushes that have been strewn over the rest of the land. There are some rare pebbles that are visible through the thinner parts of the grass layer which completely covers the soil.
101758: A hungry warg is standing here, ridden by Backdraft.

The bottoms of all the slight depressions here on this somewhat, uneven plain are too muddy to contain any drinkable water. It is, however, well enough to allow a luxuriant vegetation to grow, parasite weeds covering the grass, a lonely boulder and the trunks of the few trees that grow here.
101759: A Bend in an Ancient Trail

A rabid rabbit is here, frothing at the mouth.
A hungry warg is standing here, ridden by Backdraft.

The old slabs of this part of the ancient trail appear to have remained in a somewhat decent shape, covered only by weeds and vegetable matter. The road, bending to the south, is breaking its relatively straight course coming from the west, but soon it looks to change its direction once again.
101760:
A brown fox is here, looking for some rabbits to chew up.
A pack horse (Rood) is standing here (shrouded), ridden by you.

Mounds and terrain depressions strew this uneven plain, however, they are not tall enough to hinder movement. Some high grasses of some sort are covering everything, their monotony broken here and there by a dark bush or a partly buried boulder. A range of steep hills border the area to the west.
101761: A Small Coppice at the Hillside
A pack horse (Rood) is standing here (shrouded), ridden by you.

Growing near a range of hills in the west, this brushwood comprised of young trees and bushes is slowly turning into a forest. Many of the oaks are already taller than most Men, and slender birches have sprouted out among them during the past few summers. Some older trees can be seen to the southwest, where a forest continues towards the hilltops. Wide, grassy plains spread out away from the hills as far as the eye can see.
101762:
A large elk is standing here, chewing grass and leaves.
A large elk gazes coldly at you, chewing on a small branch.
A pack horse (Rood) is standing here (shrouded), ridden by you.

Small dirt paths, covered in old animal tracks, lead through the plains towards areas of vegetation in the north and in the west. High hay covers the ground here, and the tops of bushes and saplings that grows here and there have been chewed off by deer or other large animals. In some places, tiny tufts of feathers or fur stick to the hardy straws near the ground, hinting at the fact that a multitude of small animals live in these fields.
101763:
A brown fox is here, looking for some rabbits to chew up.
A pack horse (Rood) is standing here (shrouded), ridden by you.

A smooth carpet of grass covers these slopes and fields, creating an unbroken surface that seems to continue very far in every direction. Even rocks and bushes are scarce here, and those that can be found are far too small to provide cover for anyone but the tiniest animals. A single animal path leads to the northeast, however, and the thickening vegetation suggests that water might be found in that direction.
101764:
A small campfire is here, ready to be lit.
A reddish fawn romps harmlessly among the tender grass shoots.

A wooded ridge, shaped like a crescent moon, separates this dry field from the bordering plains. Dense brushwood surrounds the field completely, leaving only one opening at the side of the ridge where passing through is easier. A huge log has been dragged to the middle of the field where it serves as a bench; the circle of sooty stones lying in front of the log seems to have held campfires in the past. At the inner side of the ridge, an entrance to a small cave lies almost hidden by a pair of bushes.
101765: A pack horse (Rood) is standing here (shrouded), ridden by you.

Wind, rain and a lack of vegetation have turned this part of the plains into a bare field of soil and gravel. Hardy weeds and twigs cling to sheltered spots near some larger rocks, but other than that the landscape is completely barren. A dry streambed leads to the west, towards areas where bushes thrive among richer soil.
101766:
A piece of raw venison is on the ground.
The butchered corpse of a swift buck is lying here.
A sparrow is flapping around on the ground.
A pack horse (Rood) is standing here (shrouded), ridden by you.

The gravelly remains of a trail leads westwards, past meadows and small stands of trees, towards a field of shrubs. In the east, the trail becomes too overgrown to follow, and it ends near a lonely elm that stands upon a hillock. A narrow ditch following the trail bends to the north, where it too gets engulfed by dense vegetation under a gentle slope.
101767: A hungry warg stands here, sniffing around for flesh.

Large rocks covered by mosses and lichen stand in this field of dry hay. The ground slopes up towards a stand of young trees in the west and down towards grassy fields in other directions. The high hay conceals some smaller rocks, which might make movement without stumbling over them hard, but would also provide cover for small animals scurrying from one hiding place to another.
101768:
A sprawling green bush of stinging nettle grows here.
A hungry warg stands here, sniffing around for flesh.

Two sooty walls built of logs are all that remains standing of this destroyed farmhouse. There seems to have been a fire; the bark on the trees near the house is somewhat charred and piles of blackened debris lie near the walls. The house also had a fireplace and a chimney, but of those only a pile of rubble remains. Stinging nettles and other tall plants thrive in the rich soil among the ruins.
101769: The gravelly remains of a road can be seen under the vegetation here. An old milestone still stands on a visible spot in front of a shrubbery; it seems that the main road used to turn to the south while a smaller road, wide enough for a cart, branched off to the west. However, no signs of heavy traffic are visible, and the short bushes growing on the lane suggest that there has not been any in years.
101771:
A brown cow is here, contemplating a higher reality whilst chewing slowly.
A well-fed cow stands here chewing her cud listlessly.

A solid, wooden fence surrounds the trampled field of grass here; this is clearly a pasture, since there are also signs of grazing and soft heaps of dung on the ground. The pasture is connected to a paddock in the east, with only a rickety gate standing in between, and the roof of a farmhouse is visible farther away. A compost pile lies behind the fence near the gate; the weeds thriving in the rich soil fail to cover up the strong smell of decay.
101772: No vegetation grows on this field of bare soil; the only signs of grass and bushes are the sooty sticks and blackened leaves scattered on the ground. Heaps of stumps and large rocks stand here and there in the open ground, and it looks like this area is being turned into a cultivated field. The clusters of hay on a small hillock in the south have also been burnt away; recent rains have made the loose soil slide down the slope, exposing the bedrock at the hillside.
101777: Heathlands at the Edge of Fields
A pack horse (Rood) is standing here, ridden by you.

Waist-high rocks, covered in lichen, and young trees growing in thick clusters hinder movement on the bottom of this small valley situated between the slopes in the north and in the south. The grassy plains extending to the west gradually turn into heathlands here, and the hardy weeds are replaced by evergreen sprigs bearing berries of many different colours. In the east, the vale ends in a sparsely wooded heath.
101778:
A small rabbit glares angrily at you.
A pack horse (Rood) is standing here, ridden by you.

Tussocks of yellowed grass and weeds cover the bumps and depressions in these treeless fields. The ground is dry and sandy, but it appears even more so in the east where the fields slowly turn into a sparsely wooded heath. In some places, a bare field of sand with no vegetation other than the occasional tufts of grass spreads out. Any tracks would be clearly visible there, if the wind did not wipe them out regularly.
101779: A pack horse (Rood) is standing here, ridden by you.

An outcrop of rock, shaped like a giant clenched fist, breaks the monotony of the fields spreading out everywhere around it. The ground slopes steeply upwards in the east, where a clear path leads around the ledge to the fields above. Boulders about the size of a pony lie scattered around the outcrop, while smaller ones dot the fields in the west.
101780:
A bear is here, covered with coarse black fur.
A pack horse (Rood) is standing here, ridden by you.

The bedrock is quite close to the surface here, since masses of bare rock stick out of the dry fields of hay in some places. In the west, a rocky ledge breaks the grassy slope leading to the plains below, but there seems to be a path going around it. The few trees growing above the ledge are stunted; a small wood of birches stands much farther away, thriving in the rich soil of the moors that extend to the east.
101781:
A rock lizard is here, motionless as it observes you.
A pack horse (Rood) is standing here, ridden by you.

The high, yellowed hay growing in these windswept fields rustles quietly even when the air stands still. Cracks run through the dry mud in places where the water formed puddles during last rains, and the ground is hard like rock in most places. Small piles of fist-sized stones can be seen among the hay near the rockier grounds in the east; grooves in the sand amidst the stones hint at the presence of small rodents, lizards or even snakes.
101782:
