A black crow flies low to the ground here, looking for carrion to eat.
A cockroach is scuttling across the floor carrying some debris.

A field of high hay, clear of any bushes or small trees that would make reaping difficult, spreads out here. This is the type of hay that farmers grow for feeding the cattle and keeping their floors warm in the winter; there are even some stacks left rotting around the sharp wooden poles standing in the fields. A small path enters the hay in the north, and it seems to be leading towards yet another cultivated field in the west.
101783:
Prickly, white-stemmed plants, with blue flower heads grow in abundance.
A pack horse (Rood) is standing here, ridden by you.

Tall thistles with thorny leaves and stems grow among the grass in these undulating fields. There are no clear paths through the vegetation, and in some places the tangled grass and plants have grown tall enough to stick to boots and legs, making movement hard. Some boulders stand in the fields, half hidden by grass and thistles, and much more than just rocks might lie unseen in the undergrowth. While standing, however, one can be seen from afar, since there are hardly any trees or large bushes growing in these fields.
101784: A cockroach is scuttling across the floor carrying some debris.

Muddy furrows surrounded by wild weeds lead the water away from these fields towards the streambed in the northwest. It seems like someone tried to grow wheat here, but either there was too much rain or the ground was simply too wet, since there are blackened and mouldy ears of wheat bending to the ground. Some cart tracks lead past the field in the northeast, while a small dirt path branches off that trail and leads to the south through the field. Gentle slopes separate this wet field from the higher grounds in the southeast.
101787: A Narrow Stream through the Grasslands

A trickling stream has carved a muddy furrow deep into the grassy ground here. Embankments of loose soil rise steeply above the streambed on both sides, making climbing up to the fields in the north or in the south difficult. The water of the stream is surprisingly clear regardless of the surroundings; tiny insects can be seen swimming in the water and crawling over the brown leaves that cover the bottom.
101788:
A carrot is growing here.
A large potato is growing here.

This is a small field that spreads out in front of a cabin. It seems to be used for growing potatoes, carrots and probably other vegetables as well. The tops ends of the vegetables stick out of the soil in neat rows, with shallow furrows keeping them separate. A pile of ash, burnt leaves and sooty pieces of wood lies behind the patch. No flames are rising from the pile, but the steaming ground indicates that something was burnt here recently. A footpath leads from the fields to the cabin in the south.
101790:
An orchid of light violet petals blossoms nearby.
A sprawling green bush of stinging nettle grows here.

Here, a peaceful meadow of flowers spreads out under a huge willow. A pile of large, round stones stands under the tree; the stones are sandy and brown, as if they were dug out of the ground only recently. There are some cart tracks on the ground, and it looks like the stones were brought here instead of having been gathered in the immediate surroundings. A small path leads to the north, where a thick growth of stinging nettles separates this meadow from what seems to be a small cabin.
101791: Some hollow trunks are all that remains of a small patch of forest that once grew here. There must be at least a dozen of these lying around on this meadow alone, and the high hay in the south might conceal more. The trunks are very dry and scarred, and there are small splinters and pieces of fungus on the ground. It looks like someone has gathered a supply of touchwood here, though it could be that these markings are made by just animals. Some living trees still stand far away to the east.
101792: Thick mud and watery depressions makes moving on the bottom of the ditch difficult. A small stream runs towards the Anduin here, but following it is hard since it occasionally fades into the mud and vegetation. Grassy fields extend north and south, but there does not seem to be an easy way to get over or out of this wide, muddy ditch.
101793:
Clusters of slender stems and tall leaves thrive in the mud and shallows.
A shallow pond is here, tinted green with algae.

The murky waters of a oblong-shaped pond fill the wide ditch that runs through the plains here. The pool of water is surrounded by a field of sinking, deep mud, which makes walking there really hard and riding impossible. Long rushes stick out of the mud, their brown heads brushing against anything trying to make its way past the pond. Farther away from the pond, a steep embankment rises above the mud at the edge of some grassy fields.
101794: A narrow, gravelly path gently curves to the west as it passes through a group of short, thorny bushes. It seems like these are the remains of a road that once led from the settlements in the northeast to the south and towards the river. Vegetation now covers this level strip of land, but the ground is hard and there are some rusty pieces of metal half buried into the gravel, hinting at some traffic in the past. Cracked, dead branches hang off the sides of some bushes; it seems like they used to block the path earlier.
101795: Two dead oaks stand tall in the middle of this field, surrounded by patches of flowers. Only one crooked branch remains on the taller tree; the rest seem to have been cracked off by strong winds and fallen into a dry tangle on the ground. The shorter of the two trees died only recently, and caps from its last acorns still cling to the thin branches. Grassy fields spread out in all directions around the pair of trees.
101796: A Field of Stumps and Branches

Catualda the Man is here searching for something, riding a trained horse.
A trained horse is standing here, ridden by Catualda.
A pack horse (Rood) is standing here, ridden by you.

Ancient stumps of what were once mighty trees stand out among the mossy rocks in this bumpy field of hay. The thick branches that are lying on the ground are grey and without bark on them, and it seems like the trees that grew here were cut down many years ago. Still, there are some recent axe cuts on one stump, and splinters lying on the ground around it; someone has been here looking for firewood.
101797: Clusters of wild wheat grow in this smooth field. Two poles that might once have held the hinges of a gate stand at the edge of the field - an edge where one can also see the end of a trail. The trail leads to the east past similar fields and overgrown pastures. No signs of cattle are visible, but some droppings on the ground hint at game animals coming here to graze.
101798:
A small brown snake is slithering around here.
A pack horse (Rood) is standing here (shrouded), ridden by you.

Smooth grass covers the ancient ruins of a village here. There seems to have been at least two dozen houses built of logs, but most of their woodwork has rotted away or slowly sunk into the ground over the years. The structures that were built of stone stand out better; the foundation of a large hall lies in the middle of an open field, surrounded by the other ruins. While looking into a few spots behind the large grassy mounds that used to be houses, a collapsed underground storage and a large stone well can be noticed among the rubble.
101799: Among the trees growing in these dry fields, someone has piled up rocks about the size of a man's head into mounds several yards wide. Perhaps the ground was being cleared for planting a field; perhaps the mounds were built for burial. In any case, whatever took place here happened many years ago; some of the smaller mounds are now almost entirely covered in grass.
101800: The fields here are dotted by knee-high stones covered in velvety evergreen moss. Tiny ferns clinging to the sides of the stones seem to be the only plants thriving in these dry meadows; the grass is yellowed and all the flowers seem to have withered away before growing to full height. A group of rowans standing on a hillock seems to be the best landmark on the otherwise level landscape.
101801:
A small oaken table has been set here.
On the table, there is a loaf of bread.
A young boy is here, bumping into things.
A very large, hairy man is standing here, examining you carefully.

Thick boards have been laid down to cover up the dirt floor of this small cabin, but there is still bare ground near the door and around the crude stone oven that sits in one of the corners. There is no fire in the oven right now, but the stones are quite warm and are radiating heat into the whole building. A wooden table and a pair of benches, carved out of huge logs, stands near the back wall. A piece of bark attached to a metal holder is burning above the table, giving faint light to the room. There is a rack close to the ceiling, possibly meant to store food or supplies.
101802:
Some cereals that look like wheat are lying here.
A pitchfork has been carelessly left lying here.
A sturdy pack horse is standing here.
A sturdy pack horse is standing here.

This paddock is surrounded by a sturdy wooden fence with a gate leading out to the pastures in the west. The fence connects with the back wall of a farmhouse in the east, where a small door leads inside. A heap of hay has been left on a rack at one corner of the fence for the animals to eat, and there are also some cereals from a better meal remaining on the ground. Some water is dripping to the ground from a trough standing next to the rack.
101803:
A dark woman moves with a determined look upon her face.
A little girl runs around underfoot.

A long table, with benches lying on both sides, stands in the middle of the main hall of this farmhouse. A wall made of huge logs separates the hall from a cramped kitchen, while the chimney leading down through the wall turns into a fireplace on this side and into an oven inside the kitchen. Some beds lie in the far corner of the hall, surrounded by a curtain that can be pulled around them for some privacy. There also seems to be a large bedroom at the end of a short hallway near the main entrance to the house.
101818:
A water moccasin slithers out of sight just below the surface of the water.
A crayfish is here, snapping its claws at you.

The water on the basement floor is less than two feet deep, and a barely noticeable current suggests that it is somehow connected to the river. The piles of debris in the water consist of floorboards, broken cogwheels and other parts of the old woodwork. Most of it is buried in the mud; the wood has not rotted away over the years, but recovering any parts would be hard work. Two wooden beams lean against the wall, making climbing in and out of the basement a bit easier.
101820: A brown pond between old branches and roots is here.

This quiet pond, surrounded by a thick shrubbery, lies here on the bottom of a hollow in the plains. The pond is somewhat overgrown; thick growths of moss, hardly solid enough to walk on, cover its surface near the banks, and dense bushes makes it hard to reach the water in most places. The hollow continues to the south, where one can spot some trees among the shrubs.
101821: A brown furry gopher is here, ready to dive back underground.

The ground here seems to be too dry for most weeds and flowers, but hardy shrubs cover the patches of sand and gravel where even the widespread carpet of grass has died away. It seems like there have been better seasons for growth, since many of the bushes are still quite massive. In many places they have gathered into dense shrubberies, where small animals can seek cover from the birds of prey that can sometimes be seen circling in the sky far above.
101822: A speckled, brown and white bird with a long curved bill stands here.

This pond of water, starts out not more than a foot or two deep here, gradually turning into a deeper pool in the north. Thick bushes and stunted trees grow on tussocks of grass, sinking their clumps of roots into the shallow water. While moving around through the bushes, some empty nests among the roots can be noticed, and branches sway in some places as if small birds were hopping on them.
101823:
An erect shrub with green pinnate leaves is growing here.
A large rabbit looks peacefully at you, ready to dart away.

Tall ferns along with round bushes with thorny branches grow in clusters in this field of bracken. The shrubbery is most dense on the bottom of a moist depression, which separates the sloping grounds in the southeast from the wide plains extending to other directions. An old trunk, buried in evergreen moss, can be seen lying among the thick ferns down there; dead leaves cover the rest of the ground.
101824:
A Dunlending Captain is here, overseeing his men.
A swarthy man is here, keeping a wary eye on things.

This musty cave seems large and dry enough to keep supplies or even a small band of travellers protected from the elements. The cave was clearly not formed naturally; a layer of straws lies spread on the floor, and some of the roots sticking out of the earth seem to have been chopped off with a shovel or some other tool. A single gush of water trickles down the surface of a rock in the back wall, where it harmlessly soaks into the ground.
101826: Passing through dense growths of bushes and bracken, winding paths lead down into this quiet hollow surrounded by brushwood and small hillocks. The slopes that lead away from here are so steep, and the vegetation is so dense, that the rays of the sun do not reach directly into the hollow. Everything is cloaked in twilight; clusters of horsetails grow under the trees, covering the ground with a feathery shroud of green and grey.
101829: A partridge attempts to hide in the undergrowth.

A wide stretch of short grass leads straight to the south, through the plains. Somehow this spot does not seem to have formed naturally; tall plants grow everywhere in the surrounding fields except here, yet there are no signs of cattle or anything that might rid this area of such vegetation. Perhaps the soil is too dry or the bedrock too near for any bushes or trees to take root.
101830: No shelter from the wind can be found on these widespread plains of grass. In some places the hay is lying low, flattened by the last rain, revealing rocks and other small bumps on the ground that might have otherwise remained hidden from sight. Keeping an eye on the features of the open sky seems to be the only way to keep a direction while travelling through these vast plains.
101831: A field of yellowed hay and tall perennial plants spreads out here. Some of the plants have had their dry cores picked clean by local birds; others are still spreading their seeds into the breeze. Sparse bushes grow in the north, while the fields of hay continue to the west as well as towards the sloping grounds in the eastern reaches of these plains.
101832: Sandy depressions break the smooth carpet of grass in many places on these gently sloping fields. Small puddles of water have formed on the bottom of many such hollows, and tiny tracks of birds can be noticed around them. Sparse bushes surround the areas of sand, and there seems to be a thick shrubbery at the bottom of the slope to the north.
101833: Some rust-coloured leaves still cling to the branches of the bushes growing here, but much more can be found drying up on the ground. The bushes rustle quietly in the breeze as their branches scrape against each other, with leaves and sticks making a crackling noise underneath. Still, it seems possible to move among the bushes undetected; even without leaves they are concealing, and it is hard to tell if any noises are caused by anything but the wind.
101834: A colourful butterfly is fluttering around here.

Moving on these sloping fields can be somewhat straining at times, but the wide plains in the north and in the west seem to offer easier ways for travelling. A steep slope, covered in short hay and clusters of heather, leads up to the southeast, where the short bushes growing here are replaced by tall pine trees. Rain water has carved sandy furrows into the ground; they lead down the slope through the vegetation.
101835: The ground begins to slope gently upwards in the east, as the even, bushy plains extending to the northwest come to an end here. The slopes are covered in short, hardy bushes, but climbing up and down seems easy enough even without grabbing the vegetation. A small stream, not more than two feet wide, streams in from the east, babbling cheerfully until it gradually dries up while running towards the bottom of the slope.
101836: The smoothly curving slope suddenly turns into an unnaturally flat terrace. There are no signs of any recent farming in the area, but the shape of the field and the narrow furrows running through it in neat lines suggests that many years ago something was grown here. Currently the ground is covered in tangled vines, thistles and small woody-stemmed shrubs, and the field does not seem readily arable with all the roots and moss smothering the soil.
101838: A smooth carpet of grass covers the hilltops and small valleys between them. Travelling among the hills seems easy, even if keeping one's direction might require climbing on a hillock and taking a look around occasionally. Nothing taller than flowers grows on the round, windswept hilltops, and if there is any shelter from the weather, the thick bushes enshrouding the hillsides keep it hidden well. In the east, even taller bushes dominate the rising landscape.
101839: An even meadow of tiny flowers spreads out here above the slope going down in the north. The field is surrounded by an almost perfect circle of trees, most of them burly elms of indeterminable age. There are also stumps and fallen trunks of dead trees; one of them is so thick that even the tallest of Men would have trouble putting his arms around it. A small pool of water has formed on the bottom of a depression on the western slope at the edge of the wood; there might be a spring nearby.
101840:
A large bat is sleeping here.
The small fierce-looking bat is hanging from the ceiling, obviously sleeping.

A short, curved tunnel, maybe five or six feet high, leads into this circular cavern under the hill. The long roots that are hanging from the ceiling and reaching for the stony floor seem to keep the soil together; a cave-in does not seem likely, even though loose dirt is slowly piling up near the back wall. Some lengths of wood stick out of the soil, implying that perhaps this cave was once used as a storage or even a shelter.
101843:
Some pine nuts lie scattered upon the ground.
A tall pine tree grows here.
A colony of red ants is here. The ants seem to ignore you.

Solitary, tall pines, standing above the field of moss and lichen here, do not offer much shelter against the sun or the rain. The ground is sandy and dry, and the only plants thriving here seem to be the heathers, which grow in thick clusters covering the roots of the pines. Old stumps sticking out of the ground here and there are grey, probably ant-infested, and seem to break apart easily.
101844: Oblong bushes, many of them taller than Men, shade the slopes and hillsides with their foliage. Some of the slopes are so steep that anyone would have difficulties climbing on them, but it is not hard to find a twisting route amidst the shrubbery to lead around the most difficult spots. Bird droppings cover the ground under some of the cliff tops that are hardest to reach; perhaps these are nesting grounds for eagles or hawks.
101850: This slope separates the heathlands in the southeast from the plains below. Climbing along the slope is hard; the paths leading past large boulders and moss-covered outcrops of rock are impassable in many places, while loose peat and moisture make the ground slippery. Slender rowans grow in the few places where trees can easily take root; most of the slope remains barren, even though water is trickling through the cracks in the cliff.
101855: A small boar with big yellow tusks looks eager to fight.

Far more akin to a track than to a road, this old trail takes a corner here, bending to the north and the east. By the side of the track stand a few, long-dead trees that apparently provide a resting spot for the local birdlife. Other than those dead trees, only some tough, grey-green grasses and the occasional juniper bush grow here.
101856: A brown fox is here, looking for some rabbits to chew up.

A few, old logs have been dragged here by someone not too long ago, creating a makeshift camp. A heap of old coals that once were a camp fire is still lying around. East of here, one can discern a trail or track of some sort. South of here, a plain that stretches out for long while. However, the plain looks as if it has been split into two different elevations; a higher eastern part and a lower western part.
101857: This place bears the marks of significant geological upheavals that took place aeons ago. Some unthinkable force has somehow managed to crack the plain open, and an escarpment has risen out along the fault line. Looking south, one can see a reddish rock wall rising out of the plain along the fault. The wall appears to continue for miles and miles.
101858: A wolf cub happily plays here.

A couple of boulders form a strange formation here, as two seemingly separate chunks of rock are piled upon each other. Their combined shapes somehow appear to resemble the head of a bird of prey. Around it, a number of bushes and ferns are growing. A bit further away from the boulders, a tough, grey-green grass begins to grow. Looking further out from the rocks, one can see that this grass is the staple type of vegetation here.
101859: A wolf cub happily plays here.

An abrupt change of terrain vis-a-vis the high and thick forest west of here, these plains are almost bereft of all types of vegetation higher than a few feet. Only a few hardy, juniper bushes contrast to the uniformity of the rolling plains that reach around east and south of here. West of here, a giant boulder rests on the flat plain.
101860:
An orkish expedition leader, wielding a scimitar, is standing here, gazing at the trees.
An orc-guard of the Morgundul is on patrol here.
An orc-guard of the Morgundul is on patrol here.
An orc-guard of the Morgundul is on patrol here.

Comprised mostly of mid-aged pine and alder trees, this mixed forest partition also sports a quite varied underbrush. One might think that this could be an ideal playground for all kinds of wildlife. West and south from here, the forest lightens up a bit. East of here, the forest opens up onto a huge plain.
101861:
A raft has been left here.
A filthy straw pallet is lying here.
A water barrel has been left here.
A simple wooden chest is here.
An orc-guard of the Morgundul is on patrol here.
An orc-guard of the Morgundul is on patrol here.

Here, amidst the normally peaceful, riverside forest, an untidy, semi-permanent camp has been set up. Dirty, rotting pieces of canvas has been tied up between some tree trunks and boulders, providing an effective but smelly wind shelter. On the ground, more of the smelly, old pieces of canvas have been tossed out, and are now being used as mattresses. Branches cut from pine trees serve as stuffing and pillows. Leftover foodstuffs of unknown kinds and descriptions have been thrown about, and whoever set this camp up does not appear to care whether their camp site is tidy or not. The whole, grotty camp is centred around a crudely set up hearth. On the outskirts, further signs of defilement are present, as whoever camps here obviously takes pleasure in breaking every fresh tree-branch and trampling every young sapling.
101862:
A large brown wolf stands here, its teeth partly bared.
A hungry warg is standing here, ridden by Backdraft.

Tough weeds, hardy bushes and withered rocks dominate this rugged plain. One would be safe to assume that this is truly untouched wilderness. If there were any settlers here once, they would soon have been driven away by the obvious lack of water, fertile soil and security. At least the road that runs north from here can provide the traveller with a route to more enjoyable destinations.
101863: Quite a sharp rise, this ridge-line overlooks the vast and forlorn plain west of here. Far to the west, the Misty Mountains can barely be discerned as a haze at the horizon. The vegetation here is quite sparse: only a few, tough grasses and the occasional briar or shrub cling to the reddish earth that comprises this field.
101864: Whereas the rock wall that looms east of here appears quite unclimbable, it looks as though it declines both in height and steepness north of here. Westwards, a rolling, grassy plain stretches out towards a faraway forest. At this spot, however, only a sharp, tough, grey-green grass manages to thrive.
101865: A wolf cub happily plays here.

Although it is slightly lower than its surroundings, this field is still exposed to the winds that blow across the undulating plains. Gazing north, one can discern the silhouette of some kind of rock formation. Southwards, a slight rise in the grass-covered plain provides a higher vantage point.
101866: A field lark stands here, focused on finding food.

Weather-worn and rugged, these fields somehow manage to retain a lush quality, mostly because of the luxuriant grasses that make up the main part of the vegetation here. To the west, a mixed forest lines the horizon, whereas the grassy plains roll out towards a faraway rock wall to the south-east.
101867: A small boar with big yellow tusks looks eager to fight.

Centred around a huge, dying oak tree, this light but solid forest belt grows here surrounded by open areas both west and east of here. For some reason, the trees and bushes appear as though they want to give the old oak all the room it wants or needs, because there is a large, glen-like space that lies between the old behemoth and the next ring of younger trees.
101868: The vegetation is very scant here, probably because the Anduin at some point washed up a huge number of black, hard rocks and pebbles. These rocks litter this riverside plain, and only a few strands of ferns grow between them. North, east and south from here, a mixed forest grows about, whereas the view west overlooks the Anduin and the swampy areas beyond.
101869: Rough and uneven, the ground here on this riverside field is full of black rock shards and jagged boulders. The field is only sparsely graced with a few, tough bushes and patches of green grass. South and east of here stands a forest comprised of what appears to be truly majestic old oak trees. The rugged fields appear to continue north from here.
101870:
A cockroach is scuttling across the floor carrying some debris.
A cockroach is scuttling across the floor carrying some debris.

A family of majestic old oaks make out the core of this otherwise mixed and heterogeneous forest. A cluster of pesky and young birches seem to be the most recent upstarts. At ground level, the forest floor is covered by tough but hardy vegetation. Below the foliage, the ground is made up by various debris and pine-needles.
101871:
A field lark stands here, focused on finding food.
A cockroach is scuttling across the floor carrying some debris.

An old and gnarled, yet unmistakably still alive, iron oak is the only thing higher than a man growing here on this plain. More than likely, the old tree used to belong to the forest further west of here, but sometime long ago, the rest of the trees vanished, leaving this sole old warrior of a tree to enjoy its solitude through the ages.
101872: This diminutive hillock, a part of the plain that reaches around in all directions, rises slightly higher than the lands themselves, thus providing a view of the grasslands that extends in all directions save west, where a tall forest grows a few miles away. Further east, the plains roll on towards something that looks like a rock wall.
101873: A swallow flies high above the ground.

Looking south or west, one sees only a long and reddish cliff wall that rises out of the plain along what must be a geological fault line. Vegetation-wise, this field hosts a few, hardy grasses and bushes. Along the very edge of the cliff wall, pockets of water must have gathered at times, since one still can see old animal tracks among the moist and muddy patches of clay.
101874: Here, the soft, reddish rock face of the escarpment sustains quite a large patch of ivy that covers a sizeable part of the wall. Some juniper bushes crouch at the base of the rock face. In all directions save east, a rolling country unfolds, here and there dotted with clumps of darkish forests.
101875: Here, in the heartland of these ever-rolling grasslands, a few small but tough bushes have found a home in a small crevice-like depression. Far to the east, a high cliff-wall rises from the plain, effectively separating these lower fields from whatever may lie beyond the escarpment.
101876: A domesticated pony, beast of burden to many, stands here.

Sometime not too long ago, this area was scorched by some kind of fire that burned off a large patch of this otherwise lush field. However, signs of new vegetation are already beginning to show here and there. Looking west, a mixed forest looms, whereas the rolling grasslands continue in the other directions.
101877:
The mother wolf stands here, protecting her young cubs.
A partridge attempts to hide in the undergrowth.

A mix of old to middle-aged oaks and several tall and straight firs make up the trees of this untouched forest. The forest floor is almost devoid of any undergrowth. East of here, a vast and undulating plain appears to open up, while the forest continues in all the other cardinal directions.
101878: A large rabbit looks peacefully at you, ready to dart away.

A few, majestic old oaks have in a most persuasive manner claimed this part of the forest as their domain, overshadowing the other trees by any measure. The undergrowth here is comprised by the usual plethora of grasses, mosses and bushes. West from this place, the waters of a great river can be glimpsed in between the tree-trunks.
101879: A large number of boulders, covered by six-inch thick, green mosses and lush patches of evergreen grass comprise the underbrush in this part of the forest. Mostly tall, mature, conifers grow here, but here and there one can spot other types of trees that have found a spot to grow and prosper upon.
101880: Pointing straight to the sky, these silvery-green firs must be supreme material for ship's masts or flag-poles. Among the trees, moss covered rocks and boulders are embedded in the underbrush. East and south, the forest opens up onto what looks like an undulating, grassy plain. The forest continues north and west.
101881: Frugal, however not dismal, rolling grasslands have developed in all of the cardinal directions save west, where a tall and looming forest of fir trees abruptly shoots straight up from the plain. A couple of bushes and boulders provide shelter and distraction for the local wildlife. To the north, some kind of fire seems to have swept away most of the vegetation.
101882: However uninhabited by the more or less intelligent races these plains may be, they are in no way devoid of life: a fact that is prosaically demonstrated by the innumerable piles of bird droppings that sit under this solitary, old oak. Further east, the view is obstructed by an escarpment that runs in a north-south direction.
101883: Rain and wind have made their mark on the rock face which blocks all passage eastwards. In the process it has eroded the soft, reddish rock, causing plenty of jagged shards to fall down onto this lower plain. A few bushes also grow here close to the wall, apparently sheltered from the winds that freely roam these forlorn fields.
101884: Some animal must have had a field day here, trying to dig up something that was far below the ground; there can be no other explanation for the three foot deep pit that has been hastily dug here in the middle of the wilderness. North of here, a looming and tall forest comprised by tall and proud fir trees can be seen, whereas the rolling grasslands so prevalent in this part of Arda reaches out in the other directions.
101885: A small boar with big yellow tusks looks eager to fight.

Assessing this plain, one could easily come to the conclusion that a few trees have decided to escape the dense forest clump that stands north of here. However, upon further inspection, one can discern that quite a few trees that had grown in between have been chopped down. If one was to guess, one would probably be led to believe that it took place quite some time ago, since the chopped-off tree stumps have already turned into a silver-grey hue.
101886: A field lark stands here, focused on finding food.

A heap of crackling twigs and branches is all that remains of the shrubbery that grew here quite a long time ago. Now long dead, the branches serve a new purpose in sheltering and nurturing a new generation of brush, however, still in their infancy. Around this patch, a wild plain reaches around in all directions.
101887: A great slab of rock lies here almost totally embedded into the tough-looking, bushy turf. The rock's colour is in stark contrast to the big, red boulder that rises out of the plain south from here, telling a tale of ancient geological upheavals. The grassy plains stretch in all directions, ultimately reaching a reddish rock escarpment far to the east.
101888: A colourful butterfly is fluttering around here.

Quite a few rocks and boulders have fallen down off of the rock wall east of here, this quite recently as damage to the various bushes and briars at the foot of the escarpment is still fully discernible. What looks like a crevice in the rock might actually be an opening into a cave. Westwards, the rolling plains reach out towards the tree-dotted horizon.
101889: Huge patches of green grass have been torn away in long patches by some kind of torrential rains on this sloping field, and this not too long ago. East of here, a large boulder partly obscures the view of a large and red rock escarpment that reaches for miles and miles in a north-south alignment.
101890: Not far away from the great river Anduin, this field is quite fertile and provides plenty of nourishment for most kinds of herbivores: thick, lush grasses and the occasional birch tree litter the landscape. A few rocks and boulders provide cover for small animals to hide from each other or from whatever threats that might be found on this idyllic little patch.
101891: A few, moss-covered stones and a cluster of lowly juniper bushes are the only features of this plain that offset the monotony of an unbroken horizon. Far to the east, however, one can barely discern some kind of shadow, a dark line above that horizon that could possibly be a cliff wall of some sort. Onwards travel is possible in all the cardinal directions.
101892: Not quite as high as the cliff wall that is just east of here, a great, reddish boulder stands firmly entrenched onto this juniper infested plain. The rock serves as a lean-to for a variety of plants and shrubs. Thick, grey-green mosses cover large parts of its surface. West, north and south from here, a rolling plain reaches around, dotted here and there by patches of trees.
101893:
A lone hawk soars high above you.
A wolf cub happily plays here.

Growing next to an impressive, twenty feet tall rock wall, a few trees have taken to clinging to the red and withered rock itself. On the ground, a few ferns of a hardy kind, along with other plants and bushes, provide potential cover for any number and species of animals. West, north and south of here, a green and luscious plain reaches out, peppered here and there by dark green clusters of trees.
101894: Gently sloping eastwards, these green and undulating fields make quite a decent home for a number of small animals. Various kinds of shrubs and bushes, along with a few young oaken saplings, comprise the flora of this place. South-west of here, the Anduin river can be noticed through all of the shrubbery; the mighty flow appears to be rounding a corner, twisting away on its steady southward journey.
101895: This slight elevation in the rolling grasslands overlooks a sweeping bend in the mighty river Anduin. The river, which carves a route from north to east, is certainly far too broad to be crossed without proper caution and equipment. The view allows a vague glimpse of the forest across the river, as well as of the rolling grasslands east of here. A handful of pebbles have been piled upon each other here, resembling some kind of a marker.
101896: Overlooking the mighty river Anduin, which is making its way through the landscape west of here, this green and grassy field gently slopes down towards the river. To the east of this patch of land, a forlorn wilderness reaches out towards a faraway ridge at the horizon.
101897: Tough, yet lush, these plains east of the mighty river Anduin could very well be ideally suited for farming. However, there are no traces of permanent settlement visible anywhere, just the predominant mix of grasses, shrubbery and bushes. Quite a few telltale signs of wildlife are also present, and one might guess that this place is a favourite trail for local animals to approach the river for a refreshing drink.
101898: This is a strip of land that juts out into a bend of the mighty Anduin. The ground is littered with mossy boulders that are resting on a spongy bed of green, waist-high ferns. To the south-east, a great wild plain opens up, whereas east of here, a dark forest lurks on the horizon.
101899: In contrast to the greenery surrounding this spot, this unusual field is quite barren. Some sort of natural pollution must have taken place here at some point, because the ground is covered with some sort of saline crust, mixed with a fibrous, white fluff. The only things thriving here are a few thick old bushes.
101900:
A short evergreen plant, with slightly bluish needles, grows here.
On the plant, there are a cluster of hard, round, black berries.

Compared to the rest of these wind-exposed plains, this area stands out as a cosy little nook: mostly because this field is considerably lower than the ones around it. The fact that the wind cannot exert its wear and tear on the vegetation here, hints at a probable explanation to why the junipers grow higher here than elsewhere.
101901: The monotony of these surroundings is somewhat lessened by the impressive wall that rises out of the plains east of here. Consisting of some kind of reddish rock, the ridge does a lot to offset the frugality of the predominantly green plains. Far to the northwest, a shadow on the horizon gives away the location of a dark and foreboding forest.
101902: Boulders, rocks and a coarse, reddish kind of dust pepper the ground here, obvious signs that the red-rock escarpment that lies east of here is slowly retreating from the plain - probably due to the slow but relentless forces of erosion: wind, rain and time. While passage east of here is hindered by the rock wall, travel is still possible out onto the shrubby, undulating grasslands that unfolds to the north, west and south from here.
101903: East Bank of the Anduin River

The bank of the river is quite treacherous, mostly due to the fact that the steep bank is swiftly being eroded by the river. There are various kinds of young trees growing here, quite the opposite from the other side of the river, where some quite impressive, old oaks huddle close to the water. They seem to be dipping their roots into the rushing waters.
101904: A slight rise, at least when compared to the surrounding land, provides a neat view of the rolling plains and forest lands of these parts of Arda. Far east of here, a rock wall cuts through the land, obscuring the view of whatever might be behind it. Looking westwards, a few seagulls in the sky give away the location of the great river Anduin.
101905: Three old and squat oaks are camped up here on this slight rise in the plains, offering some, though scant, protection to various kinds of birdlife. A slight depression is situated some distance north from here, offering another sanctuary from the ear-piercing winds that often blow across this open landscape.
101906: From the northern end of the horizon, all the way as far south as the eye can see, a looming shadow rises up from the ground east of here. In all probability, it could only be a ridge or escarpment of some sort. Slightly lower than the immediately surrounding plains, this spot gives shelter to a few lonely oak saplings. Not higher than eight or nine feet, the trees' future shape is already foreshadowed by their current appearance, as the yearly autumn storms would most certainly take away anything taller.
101907: The looming cliff-wall north-east of here seemingly reaches out towards you, poking a jagged pinnacle-crowned fist-like formation in the general direction of the mighty Anduin river. Apart from this impressive geographical feature, the plains that surround the escarpment provide a comparatively lush backdrop to the stern, sterile ruggedness of the escarpment.
101908: A field lark stands here, focused on finding food.

Turning a sharp corner, an escarpment the height of a very large horse blocks the way north and east. There has been considerable erosion of the cliff face; thousands and thousands of reddish rock shards lie scattered on the ground, interspersed with though green-greyish grass and waist-high juniper shrubs.
101909: A curious geological formation, this natural escarpment divides the plain into a lower and a higher part. Northeast of here, a slightly curved, ramp-like path leads up onto the higher section. Northwards, a reddish rock wall can be seen rising out of the plain for miles and miles. Looking in a westerly direction, one sees a fairly lush plain, interspersed with clumps of trees. Far in the distance, a misty haze above the horizon reveals the location of the mighty river Anduin.
101910:
A brown fox is here, looking for some rabbits to chew up.
A lone hawk soars high above you.

The common juniper that grows here has the ability to take on a number of interesting and bizarre shapes. Here, where the wind and the other elements can torture the plants throughout their lives, the shrubs opt to stay low and close to the ground; a fact that makes travel here somewhat difficult, whether mounted or not.
101911:
A short evergreen plant, with slightly bluish needles, grows here.
On the plant, there are a cluster of hard, round, black berries.

These lush and green plains are the domain of various kinds of wildlife - a fact that is made evident through various tell-tale signs: here and there, tracks of mammals of various kinds can be discerned, particularly in the muddy patches that lie interspersed among the spongy tufts of hardy plains-grasses.
101912: A sharp-eyed hawk is here stalking some prey.

Untouched by any kind of civilisation, this plain obviously harbours a varied flora and fauna. The lush, evergreen grasses that grow here are probably the staple food for a number of herbivores, evident since the ground bears the marks of quite intense grazing.
101913: This area would have been ideal for a farmstead, considering the lushness of the plain. The proximity to the great Anduin river grants these fields a gracious amount of water, turning them into prime grazing lands. However, the land is sorely lacking of signs of habitation. If anybody ever did live here, they have left a long time ago.
101914: East Bank of the Anduin River

Here, the muddy bank of the swift river threatens to crumble and fall down into the Anduin. This is probably due to the eroding forces of spring floods which have long passed by, transporting away the supporting hard-packed soil. Some of the young aspen that grow on the banks have indeed fallen over and lodged themselves halfway into the river. The saplings are now making trails in the flowing water, as if waiting to be torn away and transported downstream to the Sea.
101915: Both rugged and desolate, this dusty plain offers little incentive for any vegetation to grow. Only some tough, grey-green grass manages to survive here, thriving in coloured patches - in stark contrast to the reddish soil that makes out the ground on this part of the plains. To the west, a steep slope leads down towards far more fertile plains.
101916:
A shallow pond is here, tinted green with algae.
A thin, crippled deer looks around timidly.
A hungry warg is standing here, ridden by Backdraft.

At least one can be certain that these lonesome plains are not totally devoid of life, as many creatures evidently use this spot as a watering spot. This is quite incontestable, because tracks and droppings of many kinds of animals are abundant. The lure of the location must be a slight depression in the reddish plain, a basin-like pocket that serves as a reservoir of life-giving water, something to be enjoyed by all kinds of local wildlife.
101917:
A small boar with big yellow tusks looks eager to fight.
A hungry warg is standing here, ridden by Backdraft.

Quite monotonously, these forlorn plains continue in all directions, only occasionally livened up by the odd tree or bush. Upon closer inspection, this particular site does actually bear the marks of recent occupation by one traveller or another: the residues of an old campfire have been wedged in between a dog-sized boulder and a tough-looking bush, and tiny splinters of wood lie neatly piled next to it.
101918:
A tall and strong hunter is standing here.
A small boar with big yellow tusks looks eager to fight.
A hungry warg is standing here, ridden by Backdraft.

A brutal-looking, jagged boulder tops this location - this is the very edge of the escarpment that effectively cuts through this landscape, dividing it into a lower and a higher part. The boulder itself is a red, weather-worn giant, and would provide a great look-out if it only could be climbed. Almost hidden by the edge of the boulder, traces of a recent campfire are strewn about.
101920: A hungry warg is standing here, ridden by Backdraft.

These stark and wind-pined plains reach an abrupt end west of here, where a sheer cliff wall sharply dives down onto a lower plain. There are a few scattered juniper bushes growing here, and they appear to keep well away from the rock wall. Only tough, grey-green grass interspersed with a couple of wind-eroded boulders dares to approach the vertical rift.
101921: A hungry warg is standing here, ridden by Backdraft.

One can see quite far to the west from here, since the plain below the escarpment is considerably lower than the wind-pined patch up here. Only the toughest of grasses and mosses can thrive here among all of the reddish boulders and sharp, jagged rock shards that litter the ground. Looking in all directions save west, one's view takes in a tough and desolate plain.
101922: A hungry warg is standing here, ridden by Backdraft.

The scant vegetation that grows here is mostly comprised by tough grey-green grasses and tough-looking waist-high juniper bushes. The austere plains are interrupted by a sheer cliff wall that drops down onto a lower field west of here.
101923: A hungry warg is standing here, ridden by Backdraft.

A drop in the plain west of here makes travel in that direction impossible. However, the sloping ridge here offers easy passage to the rolling grasslands in other directions. The great fields reach out towards what must be the mighty river Anduin far, far to the west.
101924: A hungry warg is standing here, ridden by Backdraft.

A handful of man-sized boulders rise out of this infertile plain, contributing to the eerie appearance of this dusty patch of land. Confusingly enough, the boulders look nothing like the harsh reddish ground: the pinnacles are of a dead grey hue. Upon further inspection, one can discern almost humanoid features among the withered pillars.
101925: A boar cub is playing here, and exploring the wide world.

The reddish earth that comprises these plains appears unable to sustain any vegetation apart from the thick grass and low bushes that surround the site. Thus, it is a feast for the eyes to look up from the dust and gaze westward towards the mighty Anduin. The great river can barely be discerned far to the west, and even further west, a jagged line that can only be the highest peaks of the Misty Mountains rises above the horizon.
101926:
A fierce boar is here, making grunting noises.
A boar cub is playing here, and exploring the wide world.
A boar cub is playing here, and exploring the wide world.
A boar cub is playing here, and exploring the wide world.
A hungry warg is standing here, ridden by Backdraft.

Among these sombre plains, one would be more than surprised to find an abundant flora and fauna. Thus, it is not a surprise that the same tough grass and the same tough bushes that one can find in all other cardinal directions grow here. Looking west one can discern a sudden drop in the plain, followed by more plains. However, a misty haze obscures the horizon: evidence of the great Anduin that brings life to the lower plains.
101927: A hungry warg is standing here, ridden by Backdraft.

Once upon a time, this was the place where this great, old grandfather of an oak grew in perfect solitude. However, at some point lightning struck, splitting the trunk in two and incinerating the whole tree. The new saplings that are trying to replace the old behemoth have their work cut out for them, trying to grow on these barren, unforgiving plains.
101928: These undulating grasslands stretch in every direction. The plain is peppered by trees and bushes of various kinds, giving the traveller the impression of an untouched wilderness. One may wonder if the people that once inhabited these lands abandoned them in order to seek out the company of fellow souls, or if they were persuaded by some other kind of force.
101929: Most decidedly a great vantage point, this massive red sandstone boulder rises some fifty feet from the lower plains. The verdant plains gently roll westwards towards a faraway river. Access to this place is only granted from the air, or through a severely difficult climb down unto the higher plain that lies on top of the escarpment. Six consecutively smaller rocks have been piled upon each other at the highest point as some kind of marker.
101930: A small harmless centipede is here.

This big cavity in the cliff face has a dusty, hard-packed dirt floor strewn with jagged rock shards and other debris. A few giant foot-prints can be found in the dust, allowing the world to know that the cave indeed is inhabited by some kind of creature. From the cave's ceiling hang strands of age-old spider webs, webs that appear to have been disturbed quite recently. Westwards, a twelve feet high crack allows passage to the outside world. It is also possible to venture further east into the inky darkness of the inner parts of the cave.
101931: Blackish stalactites reach down from the slightly domed ceiling of this dark cave. The floor is littered with rocks and boulders, and the rough rock walls lean into the room, defining the shape of the room into a neat 'T'. Towards the south, the ground rises up to meet an equally lowering ceiling, enabling access to what appears to be a continuation of the black grotto. Just north of here, a portal-like formation allows passage into a pitch-black section of the cave.
101932:
The small fierce-looking bat is hanging from the ceiling, obviously sleeping.
The small fierce-looking bat is hanging from the ceiling, obviously sleeping.
The small fierce-looking bat is hanging from the ceiling, obviously sleeping.
The small fierce-looking bat is hanging from the ceiling, obviously sleeping.
A cockroach is scuttling across the floor carrying some debris.
A cockroach is scuttling across the floor carrying some debris.

The stalactite-covered ceiling here is considerably lower than the cave part north of here. The floor is littered with something that cannot be anything but bat excrement, a fact that is effectively confirmed by the more than musty smell in here. North of here, the cave appears to open up a bit, but it is hard to tell in the prevalent darkness.
101933:
An infant troll, baring its teeth, snarls here.
An infant troll, baring its teeth, snarls here.
A large cave troll is here, staying close to his mother.
An infant troll, baring its teeth, snarls here.
A large cave troll is here, staying close to his mother.
An old, strong cave troll is standing here.
An infant troll, baring its teeth, snarls here.
A nasty troll female crouches here, with a feral look in her eyes.
A huge stone troll looms overhead, ready to crush your body.
A cockroach is scuttling across the floor carrying some debris.
A cockroach is scuttling across the floor carrying some debris.
A cockroach is scuttling across the floor carrying some debris.

By any measure, this cave is a complete and utter disaster zone. Gnawed bones, dried up pieces of hide, skulls from animals and other creatures lie thrown about in atrocious-looking piles. One would not have to think too long and hard to find a plausible source for the absolutely rancid smell that permeates this square, blackened cave room. A huge, jagged rock slab has been set up against the eastern wall, blocking further passage in that direction. South of here, the air appears to be easier to breathe.
101934:
A large sack is on the ground.
A rotten corpse is hanging here.
A rotten corpse is hanging here.
A rusty pickaxe with a broken handle lies discarded here.
A rotten corpse is hanging here.
A cockroach is scuttling across the floor carrying some debris.
A cockroach is scuttling across the floor carrying some debris.
A grey-skinned mountain troll stands here.
A cockroach is scuttling across the floor carrying some debris.

The most prominent feature of this narrow alcove is the stench of rotting meat that permeates everything in here. Spoils of war and strife are littered about on the cave floor, mostly bones and skulls that have been crushed by merciless hands not very long ago. The only exit from this unwholesome, dark hole lies to the west, where a big opening leads into a big, nasty-smelling cave room.
101935: Only a few shrubs grow in the field here, the rest is consumed with long blades of green grass. The grass has a variety of texture to it: some of the blades have a refined texture, whereas others are very coarse. There are a few weeds visible in the field as well, though they are not very tall in length, and the grass hides the majority of them. However, along the northern edge of the field the soil is exposed, giving off a red hue.
101936: A few shrubs are growing in the field, spread out wide apart from one another. There are many leaves on each branch of the shrubs, oval in shape, with a dark green colour to each. There are several weeds growing throughout the field, very tall and of different shades of green. The grass is a mixture of green and brown colour, with varying length. There is a slight incline upon the earth as the field continues to the north.
101937: Shorter, fine grass grows among the very long, green blades of the field, making it very thick in appearance. Tufts of brown grass are visible here and there, stunted in their growth. Various types of weeds have mixed themselves into the field among the grass here as well.
101938: Many weeds are scattered in the field here. The most common weed of the field has wide, arrow shaped leaves and stands quite tall. The dark, green leaf of this weed pokes out from everywhere, unlike some other weeds that blend into the green grass. The grass has grown tall, each blade appearing to have a soft green texture.
101939: A tall stag is here, grazing peacefully.

The field consists of lengthy grasses of different textures and colours. Some of the grass has a rough, crisp looking texture to it, with a light tone of brown, whereas some of the longest blades are green with a soft texture. A few weeds attempting to blend in among the grass stand tall with prickly, large leaves. Each leaf on the weeds appears to have a waxy finish to them.
101940: The grassland begins to expand towards the east from here, though along the west it greets a riverbank. Iris plants stand mainly between the western bank and the grass, however, there are a few that have sprouted among the long, fine blades of grass. Several weeds grow on the northern edge of the grassland, with spiny shaped leaves.
101941: A heron is stalking the area, looking for fish.

The riverbank along the Anduin is bare here, other than the long irises that are growing sparsely along the eastern edge of the river where it greets the grassland. The footing upon the bank is soft from all the moisture absorbed off the rushing water from the river. Many weeds have grown along the northern edge of the bank here, with small leaves of dark green colour bundled closely to their stems.
101942: Almost the entire bank along the river is populated by the growth of dark green iris plants. Each stem of the iris is long and slender, with many sword-shaped leaves that have extended from the plant in every direction. The soil along the bank is very soggy close to the river; under the irises it is very damp from moisture, but stable enough to walk on with ease.
101943:
A large elk is standing here, chewing grass and leaves.
A large elk gazes coldly at you, chewing on a small branch.

Tall blades of grass cover the field in assorted green colours. There are a few stems of brown with grains at their tips; they have slumped over slightly due to their own weight. Jagged edged leaves of a dark green colour are arrayed over the stems of weeds here. The grassland appears to expand towards every direction other than the west, for there lies a riverbank in the distance.
101944: Long, slender blades of grass consume the stretching field. Most of the grass is a soft green colour, appearing very refined in texture. However, there are a lot of dried up, dead blades of grass that have nestled along the base of the much younger grass that is still in growth. The decaying blades scattered among the ground are various tones of brown. A few weeds have sprouted themselves from the earth, blending in well with the grass due to their similar green colour.
101945: Wild grains of some sort stand very tall here and are scattered throughout the grass of the field. Though the grain has risen over the blades of grass, the grass still reaches an impressive height. Between the grains and the grass being so thickly grown, it is very difficult to spot even the few weeds that have hidden themselves in the field. The vegetation of different plants growing here gives a blending mix of colours.
101946: A colourful butterfly is fluttering around here.

Wild, brown grains are clearly dominating the grass in the field. The grain stands very tall, though each one is quite slender. Slightly visible through the thick, growing grain are light green blades of grass. The grass is very scant in comparison to the wild grains. The field continues in all directions.
101947: A large elk is standing here, chewing grass and leaves.

Grain flourishes in the field here among the grass. The grain plants are all several feet high, with a slender stem of light brown. When the stem finally reaches its tip, one can see the actual seeds of grain which are hanging, most being cluttered tightly together. The grain seeds are a darker tone of brown than the stem. A few soft green blades of grass have grown between some of the grain.
101948: There is a large variety of grass growing in the field here. Some of the grass is a soft shade of brown, other grass is fully green in colour. A few stems of grain have also grown along the western side of the field, blending in with the long blades of grass. There are also a few shrubs, low in height, which have grown rather wide. Each shrub is thickly covered with leaves of an oval shape upon their branches.
101949: Blended within the long blades of wild grass on the western side of the field are a few stems of brown grain. The rest of the field is covered very thickly by long blades of grass with different textures and colours to the blades. A few weeds grow among the blades of grass, with diamond shaped leaves extending from the stems. The weeds are a dark green, however, the stems of these weeds are a much lighter green. A single shrub of a dark green colour grows within the field as well.
101950: The field is quite thick, filled with grains and grass standing tall above the soil. In all directions the field seems to be very expansive. There is an even mixture of many different plants, all giving off their own natural essence to the field. Along the ground, there are many decaying blades of grass, as well as younger grass that has begun its growth.
101951:
An orchid of light violet petals blossoms nearby.
A furry, striped raccoon is here, nosing around for some berries or roots.

An even mixture of grain and lengthy grasses is covering most of the field. Natural shades of green and brown from the plants in the field blend together so well that only a few of the scrubby looking weeds stand out. The weeds have a slight difference in tone to the grass surrounding them, making them a little more noticeable.
101952: The grass of the field here becomes very coarse and tattered looking. Each blade of wild grass is thick, being deep green in colour, until it reaches to the tip of the blade. Most of the blades have dried out at the very tip. There, the deep green diminishes to a dark, browned edge. Some brown grains have sprouted up in random areas throughout the field of grass.
101953: A large portion of the field is covered by grass. However, there are a few spots that reveal bare soil, edged by weeds and coarse grass. The rest of the blades of grass, within the field, are of various colours, with differing textures. Some of the blades are green, others a light coloured brown. There are a few blades that look as if they are two-toned, green in the centre of the blade, with edges of light brown.
101954: The thick field is composed of long, green blades of grass. Some of them are so light that their ends curl over, dipping back towards the earth. Some dead grass has bundled up along the base of the grass which is still in healthy growth. There is a riverbank to the west, but the grass continues to thrive in every other direction.
101955:
A huge warg is here, moving in for the kill.
A ferocious warg is here, snarling angrily.
A ferocious warg is here, snarling angrily.

Several iris plants grow in massive bundles across the bank along the edge of the water. Along the northern portion of the bank is where the irises seem to really flourish. Towards the southern area on the bank, younger plants of the iris family have emerged from the soil. They are much shorter than those that are fully grown; their long, sword-shaped leaves are very distinctive.
101956:
Tall yellow flowers cover the moist ground, prospering in the lowland.
On the cluster, there is a tall yellow iris.

The footing along the riverbank is softened from the nearby river, but is rather stable to travel upon. Several reeds are growing along the western side of the bank, close to the river. Iris plants of different colours have bloomed in several locations upon the bank, but the larger portions gathered together lie at the east end of the bank. There, lush grass is noticeable, blending in with the irises.
101957: Each long, lush blade of grass here extends to a tall height above the soil. The grass is a light shade of green, with a very refined texture. Though the grass appears to really expand to the east, there are several iris plants growing along the western side of the grass, where the riverbank lies. Even the footing here appears to be very soft, evident from the great amount of dampness beneath the soil.
101958: The grass is extremely tall here, including the blades that cover the slight dip that depresses towards the eastern side of the grassland. The grass blades are very refined, being a soft coloured green. Within the dip that leads east, the grass is rather soggy, as the rain water that has built up must have travelled down the depression in the same frequent pattern.
101959:
A blooming water-lily floats on the surface of the water.
A sly cat prepares to pounce from its grassy hiding place.

The surrounding grassland has long, light coloured green blades of grass which keep the mere more secluded. The mere itself is of an odd shape, neither exactly in the shape of a circle, nor an oval. Instead, it almost appears to be the shape of a crescent, with jagged edges all around the water. On the western side there is a small indent leading into the water of the mere. The indent is noticeable from all of the dead grass in its course. It appears that the water has slowly trickled from the dip in the grassland in the west, forming the small mere from all of the buildup. The water is not very clean, as all of the grass it has drowned can be seen decaying under the water.
101960: There is a slight depression in the grassland here which inclines slowly on the eastern side. The incline is gradual, not very steep even at its highest point. The soil of the grassland is very soft and moist. Long blades of grass that have grown here look very unhealthy, some are even frayed upon their edges. Along the western edge of the grassland, where the ground becomes level, lies a dark hatch that stands out as a landmark among the surroundings.
101961: Many different coloured blades of grass consume the field here. However, there are a few bushes that have grown within the field, with many oval-shaped leaves of dark green upon each branch. An indentation through the centre of the field reveals that something rather large has trampled the grass. It travels in a straight line between the east and the west.
101962: A furry, striped raccoon is here, nosing around for some berries or roots.

There are many blades of grass of several different colours growing wild here. Many weeds grow exceedingly tall on the eastern edge of the field, where the grass becomes very thick. A few dry shrubs are scattered around the field as well. The leaves on the shrubs are small and oval in shape.
101963: A large portion of the field here emits an essence of golden-brown. Almost every blade is slender, tall in length and has a very refined texture to it. However, at the northern end of the field, hints of green appear, blended in among the rest of the golden-brown blades of grass. The difference in length of the green blades is very noticeable, in comparison to those which are brown. The green grass in the northern portion of the field is very short, whereas the golden-brown seems to tower over the rest.
101964: The field is mixed with different coloured blades of grass. Some of the blades are green, but the majority is a golden brown. There are a few places within the field where the wild grass has been flattened, only to leave the once healthy blades to decay, smashed into the soil. Two patches of bare soil are also noticeable within the field.
101965: The majority of the blades of grass here are green in colour, with only a few hints of brown at the southern portion of the grassland. Several shrubs have grown far apart from one another, with branches filled with many dark green coloured leaves. A slight depression can be seen in the grassland, dipping gradually as it continues north.
101966:
A huge warg is here, moving in for the kill.
A ferocious warg is here, snarling angrily.
A ferocious warg is here, snarling angrily.

The grassland is mixed with assortments of grass and a few, short shrubs. The shrubs have leaves that are very tiny, but each branch is filled with many of these oval-shaped leaves of dark green. The grass has many different shades of green, some even brown, with textures that vary. Some of the textures appear very coarse, whereas others are soft and refined.
101967: The blades of grass are of different lengths, along with a variety of lush green to their colour. All of the grass, however, appears very refined in its texture. Some of the blades which are longer begin to curl over at their tips. Along the southern side of the grassland, the grass becomes more blended with blades that are a darker, green colour. Those blades have a texture that appears coarse, if compared to the lush green blades that cover the majority of the grassland.
101968: There is no sight of a single weed in growth here in the grassland. The grass looks exceedingly fine and is not very tall. It is quite green; each blade looks as healthy as it could possibly be. In the east, the grassland appears to expand, more wild in growth than it is here. Along the western side of the grassland, irises and reeds from the nearby bank greet each other, blending themselves into the grass.
101969: Once long, slender reeds grew tall along the bank; now they lie smashed into the soft soil. A few irises bloom along the eastern edge of the bank, where it has begun to blend with the tall blades of lush grass. There are several tiny rocks that have been clustered together along the western side of the bank. The rocks are all dark in colour, but vary in shape.
101970: A beautiful and docile horse is standing here.

The riverbank has many reeds lying loosely upon the soil. Towards the northern portion of the bank, there are several that are still rooted in. These appear to stand very tall and still even in strong winds. On the edge of the bank, closer to the river, the reeds have been trampled into the ground so much that they look as though they were just a part of the muddy bank.
101971: A colourful butterfly is fluttering around here.

There is a large combination of thorny brush and long blades of grass along the south here. Each thorny stem of the brush is long and has a tangled appearance to it. The many brown and thin stems are greeted by coarse blades of grass at soil level. To the north are blades of grass that are a darker green and not as rough looking in their texture.
101972: A beautiful and docile horse is standing here.

There is a vast mixture of vegetation growing along the ground here. Lush, green blades of grass are growing thickly together towards the north. A few weeds have begun to grow along the eastern edge, blended in among the different lengths of the grass. Towards the southern edge of the grassland, the brush becomes visible, though it is very thin. Throughout the grassland, there are various shaded blades of grass, of all different lengths. Their textures seem to vary from being very coarse in appearance, to very refined.
101973: The grassland has long blades of green grass that have grown thick here, all having a fine texture to them. The grass begins to blend towards the east into many different shades of green, some even brown, as it becomes a little more thickly grown. Southwards, some brush is visible and the ground looks very bare, with only a few, small rocks atop the soil.
101974: Along the northern portion of the grassland the grass is the more lush in appearance, and more thickly grown as well. Towards the far southern edge of the grassland, many stones lie upon the bare soil and it appears that the grass is slowly coming to its end. The coarse grass that has grown in the southern area of the grassland is very dry and brown in colour. Several weeds have sprouted in random locations throughout the grassland and there are some large stones embedded in the grass.
101975:
A beautiful and docile horse is standing here.
A huge warg is here, moving in for the kill.
A ferocious warg is here, snarling angrily.
A ferocious warg is here, snarling angrily.

The field has an overall golden-brown hue to it, since every length of grass is of that colour. The blades are all very long and slender, yet refined in texture. The soil has been revealed from under the grass in a few locations, though even that is a light shade of brown, blending into the colour of the grass. Towards the south, a very bare plain can be noticed.
101976: A small brown snake is slithering around here.

Slender, tall blades of grass, all golden-brown in colour, grow in abundance here in the field. On the south edge of the field the grass begins to diminish until only bare soil remains. Even the bare soil is of a golden-brown hue. Some stones are lying upon the earth where the grass has ceased to grow. The stones are not very large and have a rough looking texture. There is a slight depression throughout the centre of the field however, in a straight line, which looks as though something rolled through in a north-south direction.
101977: Scattered around the plain are several large pits in the ground. Near some of these pits are large rocks that appear as though somehow they were lifted out from their deep bed of soil, for dirt and mud remain around the base of each rock. Several of the pits have an odd shape to them, whereas a few of the pits are extremely circular in shape.
101978: Many rocks, stones and tiny pebbles of different shades of brown, grey and black lie on the plain. They all have their own unique shape. Some of the rocks have a rough texture to them and others are quite smooth. There are very few patches of grass growing in this part of the plain, due to all the rocks which lie scattered about, smothering the soil. The few grass patches that do exist, appear to be very coarse; for the grass, there is a great struggle to stay alive here, much less to thrive in growth. Towards the north of the plain, the grassland has started. Its light, golden blades of grass meet the dry soil there. The bare plain continues along to the east of it.
101979: A grey wolf is here, thin from starvation.

There are many large patches of rocky soil in the plain here. As it continues to the north, the soil becomes hidden by lush grass. There are a few larger rocks that the grass has encompassed, but most of the rocks sit in the dirt free from grass. A few weeds also grow in the plain. The weeds have sprouted only where the rocks have hindered the grass from growth; on the northern side of the plain where there is more grass, there is not a single weed in sight. The brush from the west is slowly beginning to expand into the plain here.
101980: A colourful butterfly is fluttering around here.

Scrawny, low growing stems that emerge from the bare soil are struggling to grow here. To the west the brush seems to be much more plentiful than it is in this area. A few pebbles and stones appear on the eastern edge of the thin brush, with soil so bare that one can see even the smallest weed trying to grow. As the brush thickens towards the south, many dark coloured thorns on each stem are far more visible. Northward, in the distance, is an expanding grassland.
101981: Green grass from the northern meadow meets the reclining brush. As the brush continues south, it becomes exceedingly dense in its growth. On the many stems that form the brush, there are tiny thorns attached. There are various kinds of weeds as well, in many different shapes, sizes, and colours that blend together well. Eastward, the brush really begins to thin out as it forms into a bare plain.
101982: The brushwood forms along the edge of a thinly wooded forest to the west. Many bushes and shrubs have spread wide apart from one another throughout the vast brushwood that expands on its way into the east. Tightly bundled stems of brown are reaching out from the soil, creating the majority of the vegetation here. Broken-off branches from the nearby forest lie tangled among the brushwood. A few of the weeds growing here have prickly covered leaves of a dark green hue. To the south it appears that the brush is becoming more thick and tangled.
101983: A large eagle soars above you.

Slender trees stand here with long, reaching branches and large, green leaves. Though the forms of these trees are slender, they still reach to a tall height above. Many immature trees are spread out across the ground of the scant forest. Several vast stumps are still rooted into the earth, remaining of old trees cut down quite some time ago. Some trees that were cut down more recently lie on the ground with their branches still intact.
101984: In the north, the river makes an S-shaped curve before returning to its original course towards the south. The bank is surrounded by the water on its northern and western side, trees of the forest loom above in the south, and a thinly wooded forest spreads towards the east. Several reeds have grown up from the soggy earth along the rushing waters off the bank of the Anduin. There are also several stones, of many different sizes and colours, aligning the bank at the waters edge. Cornered by the trees to the far southeast corner of the bank, lies a fire pit made of large stones. There are several pieces of debris from the nearby forest lying upon the riverbank. A large piece of canvas has been left here, along with the wooden poles that once held it up.
101985: The plain presents a desolate appearance. Rough grass of mixed green and brown colours covers the ground in the middle of the plain. The soil is very dry and light brown in colour. Eastward, across the plain, there are many rocks of various sizes. There is a mixture of colour to the rocks, varying in shades of brown, grey, and black.
101986: A rock lizard is here, motionless as it observes you.

Coarse grass is growing in bundles throughout the plain. There is a large area where the bare soil is revealed with nothing growing in its vicinity. Two large rocks have settled deep into the earth in the midst of the plain. They each have a jagged texture, though they are also matching in a light brown colour. A few weeds have grown up around the massive rocks.
101987: The brush slowly begins to fade here from the thick, brown plants that grow in the west and south. There are several rocks on the ground, where the soil looks very bare and dry. A few weeds growing here are dark green in their colour, with many leaves sprouted from each stem. Fine, tiny hairs grow upon each leaf of the weeds in the brush. The brush itself has several thorns that are spread apart on each long, tangled stem.
101988: An erect shrub with green pinnate leaves is growing here.

Quite a few pebbles, some larger stones, and clumps of soil lie across the dry earth. Some tangled debris also remains scattered around the bare plain. From the looks of the debris, it appears to have come from some kind of brush plants. A few thorns are noticeable upon the tangled stems of the debris. Some brush can be seen to the west, giving a brown hue to that direction.
101989: There is not much to observe in the plain here, as the land appears very sterile and dry. A few weeds have grown out from beneath the rough ground, along with small patches of grass that looks as though each blade has been shredded. The entire area gives off a brown essence, for even the few patches of grass are parched due to the lack of shade.
101990: Much of the soil is exposed on this plain. There are only a few patches of crisp looking grass, scattered far apart from one another. These patches of grass only show green at the base of each blade where it continues downward into the earth. As each blade gets taller though, the green begins to fade into brown. A few rocks, and clumps of loose soil, are noticeable on the eastern side of the plain.
