101991: A large brown wolf stands here, its teeth partly bared.

The soil in the plain is not only bare, but very dry. Only a few slender weeds have grown, although even these are not very tall in height. Large clumps of dry soil lie upon the ground, easy to be mistaken for a large stone from a distance. Along the western side of the plain, a few blades of coarse grass are visible.
101992:
A grey wolf is here, thin from starvation.
A hungry warg is standing here, ridden by Backdraft.

The diminishing brush appears to come to an end here from the larger portion to the north and west. Towards the east, the footing becomes extremely barren, with various stones lying upon it. Several weeds have grown in between the thorny stems of the brush, their hue of green making them very noticeable among all of the brown colours. The weeds have tiny hairs covering their leaves, all of them being very short and fine.
101993: The deeper into the brush one goes, the thicker it becomes. The brown, thorny stems reach to waist height for most. The soil here is very dry, with a few weeds of dark green colour, that have emerged from the earth and grown to a decent height. The stems in the brush have tangled themselves around a few of the trees that have been growing on the western edge. Even further towards the west, is a large amount of trees emerging from the nearby forest.
101994: A large shrub grows here, its branches loosely spreading.

Surrounding the forest to the east, north, and west are scattered brush and some brambles. Though there are several different types of trees in the forest here, it is not dense at all. The lush green grass beds the spaces between the trees at decent lengths. Each tree has a different coloured leaf and bark than the next one does. The barks of the trees are not only arrayed in several different shades of brown, but their textures vary as well.
101995: Thorny bushes and large weeds have grown thickly together to form the brushwood between the trees of the forest. There are quite a few slender, short trees in growth mixed between some of the brush. Most of the brush is leafed in a dark green hue, but the larger, thorny vegetation in the brush is brown. The thorns on the brush appear to be small, but rather sharp at the tip. On both of the eastern and western sides of the brush, the trees of the nearby forest begin to expand further into the brush.
101997: The brush expands in every direction from here, other than where the forest has begun to unfold to the south. The brush is dense from both the thickly grown stems bundled together, and from thorns that have extended from their branches, so that it would be quite difficult to pass through to the north or east. Many large, brown patches of coarse grass grow among the vegetation in the brush. There are weeds that have fine hairs spread about over each leaf, with a few sharp thorns growing off of their stems. The weeds are very tall, even though their girth is not very wide at all. Many of these weeds line themselves along the northern portion of the brush.
101998:
A large thorny branched shrub is growing here.
On the shrub, there are a number of blackberries.

The brush has a tangled appearance to it. Vegetation from the forest to the west has expanded greatly into the dry, thorny brush. Several weeds that are growing here stand out alongside the other plants because of their rather large leaves. Brown, dried up blades of grass stand tall, scattered within the brush in thickly grown patches.
101999: The trees of the forest have grown to a great height here. The leaves are soft and mint coloured, which contrasts with the light brown bark that protects the trunks of these trees. Strands of ivy hang in several of the trees. The ivy has climbed even the highest of branches, disappearing beyond sight. The leaves on each strand of ivy are a dark green, with slight hints of white which extend throughout each leaf from the centre.
102000: Trees of various heights are growing in the forest here, broadly spaced from one another. There are a few different types of trees as well. Some look as though a darker green leaf grows from the branches, others are a lighter shade of green. A few strands of ivy have laced their way up the trunks of a few, select trees. Long, refined grass is edged along the very base of some of the trunks, but as it expands from around the trunk it gets shorter in length. Westwards a riverbank is visible in the distance.
102001:
Tall yellow flowers cover the moist ground, prospering in the lowland.
On the cluster, there is a tall yellow iris.

Many long stems of green and brown reeds are clustered together along the muddy riverbank, whereas the trees of a forest line the bank along its eastern edge. The Great River runs swiftly to the south. Spread out between the reeds are delicate looking plants that belong to the iris family. The ground is very soft, due to the amount of moisture brought to the area from the river.
102002:
A hungry warg stands here, sniffing around for flesh.
A duck is here, quacking happily.

Along the east side of the Great River Anduin a gentle sloped riverbank greets a nearby forest. There are many thick reeds covering the sloped bank. A few iris plants are lining the northeastern edge of the thick forest. The footing is stable, but the ground becomes rather moist and soft as it merges into the waters of the river.
102003: A giant form rustles among the trees.

Ivy scales up the trunks of the trees in delicate, tiny strands. Their leaves are evergreen, with a glossy finish to each. At a closer glance, tiny white veins are revealed, as they scatter out of the centre of each leaf. The undergrowth in the forest is not very dense. Many trees have grown close together however, making travelling through the forest somewhat difficult.
102004:
Tall yellow flowers cover the moist ground, prospering in the lowland.
On the cluster, there is a tall yellow iris.
A duck is here, quacking happily.

Long, slender stems rise several feet above the ground. The reeds are in various shades of green, some even lightly browned. The rushing water of the Great River flows along the riverbank on both its northern and western edge. Nearby to the east stands a forest with large trees. Under the eaves of the trees on the eastern edge of the bank grow plants that appear to be irises. The footing is soft from all of the moisture the river produces. A few rocks are scattered along the northern border of the bank where the river has washed them ashore.
102005:
Tall yellow flowers cover the moist ground, prospering in the lowland.
A bear is here, covered with coarse black fur.

The forest is thinly wooded, with lush, long blades of green grass bedding the soil between the trees. A few healthy bushes grow beneath the trees, each one filled with many oval shaped leaves. On the western edge of the forest, a couple of reeds are visible from the nearby riverbank. On the northern portion of the forest, there are even more reeds gathered together. Some have been mixed within some extremely long blades of grass. A few iris plants seem to flourish in growth here near the banks.
102006:
An erect shrub with green pinnate leaves is growing here.
Inside the shrub, there are two piles of crimson raspberries.

There are several stems growing out of the ground at the base of each shrub here in the brush. Most of the stems are very slender, almost bare of leaves, giving the brush an overall woody appearance. A few coarse, lightly browned patches of grass have sprouted within the brush as well. The brush gets more intense as it unfolds into the east. In the distant south, and north, the brush continues but a vast forest emerges and greets the western front.
102007: Many of the trees in the forest have grown close together here. There are several low branches expanding out from even the most slender of the trees present. Dark green, stout bushes are also adding to the already dense forest. Long blades of grass can be seen growing from the dry and coarse undergrowth.
102008: A huge, black wolf is here, ready to devour.

The brush is very dense and difficult to manoeuvre through. There seems to be a slight indentation noticeable through the brush, as if some form of being had passed through before. Even with the slightly cleared path, the brush consists of many thorny, rugged bushes, causing each movement to be quite complicated. Passage only appears possible towards either the east or west through the brush. To continue north or south is impossible due to the thickness of the bushes and their many sharp thorns.
102009: There is a tiny depression in the middle of the brush that indicates travel has been done before through the thorny plants. The thorns on these bushes are not small, but rather large, making their sharpness all the more perceptible. Attempting to move through the brush in a northward direction, or to the east, is rather impossible due to the thickness of the brush.
102010:
A huge, black wolf is here, ready to devour.
A demon wolf lurks here, its dark form twisting and hiding its shape.
A demon wolf lurks here, its dark form twisting and hiding its shape.

Through the dense northern and eastern brush, a rift has formed. The thorny brush is impenetrable to the south and the west. The soil of the rift itself is very barren, causing a lot of loose particles of dry dirt to flit around in the air once it has been disturbed. Along the edges of the rift, there are many weeds growing under the thorny bushes. Though they are only some simple weeds, their various shades of green add some colour to the surrounding brown, dense brush.
102011: Vast thorns grow on the bushes with fine, sharpened edges to each thorn. The branches are dark brown, the texture of each one alludes to the extreme dryness that affects the area. A slight gap between some of the brush hints that some kind of travel has gone through here before. The gap between the brush is very narrow, only leading east or west. The brush is so dense towards the north and south, that passage in either direction would impossible.
102012:
A wolf cub happily plays here.
A wolf cub happily plays here.
A wolf cub happily plays here.
The mother wolf stands here, protecting her young cubs.

Within this den are earthen walls made of natural clay. The den is not necessarily large but has a rather decent amount of space inside. The clay walls are all different shades of brown, some are even red, and have a clumpy, natural look. The den overall has a circular shape to it, with the base having a very dark colour of brown. Debris is scattered upon the ground of the den, along with long, dried up blades of grass.
102013:
A large, dangerous-looking green snake is coiled up here.
A huge, poisonous spider is here.
A large, dangerous-looking green snake is coiled up here.
A huge, poisonous spider is here.

The walls forming the tunnel are of natural materials. Consisting of a lot of packed mud, roots, and other plant-like materials, they appear to hold quite well. A lot of moisture has built up in the tunnel making it very humid. The space here is very narrow, and becomes even more so near far end, making it difficult to pass through.
102014:
A huge, poisonous tarantula extends her legs to you.
A tiny spider is here, eating a tiny bug.
A tiny spider is here, eating a tiny bug.

The narrow, muggy tunnel opens widely into a rather large, old dwelling place of some sort. The underground dwelling at one time must have been the home to a small being, as much of the remaining debris appears to once have been made for a creature of much smaller stature if compared to Men. Though there is a large portion of stone that was used as a ceiling, it has now been collapsed for what appears to be a long time. Even with this fallen stone, there is still a sufficient amount of space within the enclosed tunnel. Between the fallen stones near the southern corners hang many webs, some weaved in unique patterns.
102015: Near the Meeting of the Rivers

The Anduin, which comes from the north-east in an almost straight line, suddenly enlarges its bed, enough than to become part of the small lake that is noticed to the west, where it accepts the waters of the River Gladden. The surrounding riverbanks are flat, except to the south where a range of hills can be seen.
102016: A speckled, brown and white bird with a long curved bill stands here.

The hill which forms the eastern riverbank delimits the northern, small lake, where the Gladden meets the Anduin, forcing the latter to shrink back to its usual, although wide, size. After that, it appears that the river resumes its roughly straight course towards the south-west.
102017: A Slight Bend in the Anduin River

The great Anduin makes a slight bend here, before continuing with its roughly, straight course towards the south-west. A thin, mixed forest is standing on the eastern riverbank, the tiny waves of the river washing against some of its nearest roots.
102018: A Small Bend in the Anduin

This is another bend in the Anduin, similar to those that can be seen in the south-west and the north-east. However, the riverbank is more varied, with a grass-covered hill to the south. There is a small forest noticeable towards the southeast, while the eastern part is covered by a bushy marsh.
102019: The Anduin by Some Ancient Fields

What might have been some fields, once long ago, can be seen on the western side of the riverbank. However, these few, useful plants are largely intermixed with weeds and some high grass. On the other side of this wide part of the Anduin, a grassy hill can be noticed.
102020: To the east of this relatively slow and wide part of the Anduin, what appears to be the remains of an old trail, can be distinguished under the wild grass that grows here. A small ruin, partly covered by wild weeds, can be distinguished to the west behind a marshy riverbank.
102021: The Anduin still flows quite slowly in its wide bed here, while it tightens and speeds up as it travels into the south. The roots of the trees that grow on the western bank maintain their consolidating grip only on a part of the humid and unstable soil, causing the riverbank to be quite irregular after ages of water erosion.
102022: The Anduin river, that flows from the north, bends around a tree-covered bank that can be noticed southwards, while its width decreases gradually, speeding up its flow. The remains of a small trail, covered by weeds, is noticed on the eastern bank.
102023: A speckled, brown and white bird with a long curved bill stands here.

Taking its time on its route to its ultimate destination, the sea, the flow of the mighty river lends its waters to the tranquil marshlands west of here. On the eastern shore, a rough and jagged plain serves as the receiving buffer for spring-floods long passed. Looking closer, one can see mounds of whitening debris that has piled up there over the years.
102024: Unusually sluggish for being such a swift and mighty river, the Anduin seems to be pausing for breath here, widening and delegating its waters into a great marshy area west of here. To the east, a mixed patch of forest is overlooking the passage of the river. Gazing north, the river appears to be less broad, and the flow of the water seems faster.
102025: The Anduin is slightly picking up pace here, but lots of water is being diverted into the marshes west of here. Eastward, a rough and desolate field is gathering debris from spring floods passed, whereas the river approaches a bend further downstream. Gazing west, the peaks of the snow-capped Misty Mountains rise above the forest-lined horizon.
102026: Approaching a great bend, the mighty Anduin is gaining in pace as it makes its way downstream, all the while creating eddies of all sizes. East of here, a stand of ancient oaks loom above an otherwise mixed forest flora. Upstream, the river looks decidedly slower and quite a lot broader, as its waters appear to be diverted onto some kind of marshlands.
102027: Broad and mighty, the great river Anduin cuts through a lush but uninhabited plain. The main current of the river stays close to the centre, whereas closer to the shores, the pace of the murky waterway is decidedly slower. Debris from previous spring-floods has piled up on both shores. Downstream, the river heads steadily in a southern direction, whereas there appears to be a easterly bend further up north.
102028: Steady on its southern course, the broad and mighty river Anduin makes good headway through these forlorn wilderness plains. On the western shore grows a stand of young alder trees, trees that are partly obscuring the view of what lies beyond. To the east, a rugged plain develops towards the horizon.
102029: Keeping a high and steady pace, the main current of the great river ploughs through the land in a north-south direction, a feature of the land that has effectively divided these lands into two separate partitions. West of here a forest grows close to the river's edge. On the eastern shore, a green and grassy field rolls gently towards the horizon.
102030: Steady and fast, the main current of the river keeps itself to the centre part of the broad waters of the Anduin. At the shores, froth whipped up by eddies and currents has gathered in fluffy piles among the shore-side debris. West of the river grows a tall, mixed forest. To the east, a rolling grassland stretches out, dotted here and there by bushes and lonely trees.
102031: Bend in the Great River Anduin

Creating a great 'S', the wild river Anduin cuts a broad path through the landscape. The current continues southwards, while upstream, the river bends westwards. Trees line the shores on both sides; however, the growth is far too sparse to be described as proper forest.
102032: Coming out of an S-shaped bend, the mighty Anduin flows towards the sea in a straight, southward direction. Along the western shore, a tall forest graces the riverside, while to the east a rolling plain stretches out for miles and miles. Upstream, the river appears to bend around a patch of forest.
102033: A heron is stalking the area, looking for fish.

The river flows in a southbound direction here. Though the water flows very fast, it is still clear enough to see the bottom of the river. There are many pebbles beneath the rushing water, lying along the riverbed. To the west, a nearby meadow can be seen meeting the riverbank. There is grass visible on the eastern bank as well.
102034: The rushing water flows southbound, between a riverbank of irises on the east, and a bank of many stones on the west. The water flows quickly, which makes it harder to view the bottom of the river. Through the ripples, however, several stones are visible. The stones are rather large, though they do not stand over the surface of the water.
102035: As the river flows south, the water looks as though it accelerates. There are several stones lining the bottom of the river, visible through the ripples of the clear water. Some of the stones are large, others quite small in size, but each noticeable from their dark colour. Along the eastern riverbank there are many iris plants growing. To the west, there are many large stones resting on the riverbank.
102036: The water of the Great River is very clear, though it is harder to see the bottom of the river through the ripples from the fast flowage. There are some wide shaped stones that are visible through the water, noticeable from their dark colours causing them to stand out. Irises are growing along the eastern bank of the river, very close to the waters edge.
102037: The western bank of the mighty Anduin, which appears to be particularly steep, leads to a grassy meadow that lies above. The water of the river is rather clear, with a very chilling appearance to it. The bottom of the river is very hard to view clearly, not from dirty waters, but rather from the quick flow of the river as it drives south at a fast speed. Towards the east, along the bank, the ground seems to have been disrupted by some means, as the soil has been piled up in one particular place, close to the rushing waters edge.
102038: The river travels from the north until it plunges into the southern bank, turning towards the west as it continues in the river bend. Along the southern bank, bare soil with a lot of debris can be noticed. The eastern bank has many reeds, but most appear to have been trampled. The soil that lies along the eastern and southern edges of the river has been dug up. The water of the river is very clear, though it is chilly in its temperature.
102039: The river comes from the northern direction, bending towards the west again as the water continues its steady flow. Along the eastern bank, the soil appears quite level with the river. The bank that lies to the east has many visible pieces of debris. On the edge of the southern bank, many reeds are flourishing near the clear and chilly water. The water becomes slightly clouded over here due to the rushing flow that breaks away the soil at the bank.
102043: While the western bank of this wide part of the Anduin is just another flat, marshy plain, the eastern one is wooded and bordered by a thin layer of fallen leaves. It is, however, slightly above the normal water level, and that keeps the base of the trees safe from the river.
102044: Making a slow turn to the west the river heads straight for the Gladden Fields. The landscape around is soggy, filled with pools of water and to the west a mist is forming a few feet above the ground. From the shore long grey straws of grass bend down in the water, touching its surface with their tips. From the muddy bottom of the current other plants peek up in greeting.
102045: The Anduin continues here on its rough path towards the southwest. While the bottom of its wide bed is muddy and sluggish, the surrounding riverbanks are rather flat plains. A small forest can be distinguished, beyond a couple of mild bushes that are in growth on the eastern side.
102046: As the water flows gently to the south, animals can take their daily drinks here without risk of being swept away in the currents. An occasional tree branch, most likely ripped away by the roaring floods in the north, flows slowly down the river. The shores are lower and less steep here, and make for a possible crossing for anyone wanting to travel through the streaming water.
102047: Following the sharp turn west the river just made it now eases back onto the original path south. The roaring madness of the river further north is calming down here. Only occasional white swirls can be seen as the water hits a concealed rock or tree trunk. To the west, the elsewhere so scattered trees form a haven for themselves, growing closer and closer together. Beyond this weald the marshy lands of Gladden Fields can be spotted under the mist.
102048: The Anduin stream takes a rather sharp turn to the west here. Gazing further south the river quickly moves back to its original path though, heading south through the green landscape. Anything entering the water would quickly be dragged into the rushing waves in the centre of the flood, and then swept away.
102049: In the centre of this stream water rages like it wanted to crush the white foam on its own waves. Rocks and stones peek up from the sandy bottom, but never break the surface. Their presence is still enough to upset the river. Small trees grow close to the shore flourishing in the presence of the clear water.
102050: The Anduin Passing a Steep Cliff
A swallow flies high above the ground.

The river runs past a rocky outcrop in the east, slowly eating away the cliff. Farther away in the south it meets a steep, grassy embankment and bends slightly to the west. The bottom of the river is not visible here, but it should not be too deep since some rocks are sticking out of the water near the cliffs. Branches and dead trunks floating in the river have gathered into a tangle among some of the largest ones.
102054: Here, the river meets a low cliff in the south, then turns gently to the west where it continues on its course through the plains. Some of the trees growing on the eastern bank gather the litter floating along the surface into their hanging branches while leaning over the river. Their roots also reach into the water, forming hiding places for fishes and water birds.
102055: Swiftly Flowing Waters of the Anduin

Sharp rocks and surges on the water make the river look quite challenging here. However, going downstream should be easy for an experienced boater or swimmer. The river bends westwards, where the water loses some of its speed as the riverbed gets wider. Near the eastern bank, a muddy stream joining the Anduin makes the water slightly clouded.
102056: The river flows in a straight southward direction for about a mile here. The current seems strong and the landscape is constantly changing. The banks appear to slope downwards in the south, but the difference is hardly noticeable on the water. The river is quite deep in most places, yet some reeds and rocks can be seen above the surface downstream of here.
102057: The river flows gently here, passing wet fields and the occasional shrubbery or stand of trees. To the south, the river bends westwards where it meets a beach; a beach that actually seems to be an exposed part of the river's sandy bottom. The field of sand continues far away from the waters edge, so a part of it should stay above the surface even during floods.
102058: The course of the river suddenly turns to the south, where the water seems to gain more speed. The river also gets quite deep here, and one cannot see the bottom further than a few yards away from the bank. Swift currents make ripples on the surface, and fishes splash in places where they nibble at insects and litter moving along the water.
102059: Small Islets in the River Anduin

Several rocky islets rise a few feet above the water near the northern bank of the river. Some have grass and stunted trees growing on them, some smaller ones are only covered by bird droppings, although it seems like they might also be used for nesting. The river bends southwards as it passes the bushy banks in the west.
102060: A long, grassy island near the western bank splits the river into two separate streams. The upstream part of the island is overgrown with reeds, wild lilies and other plants thriving in the shallow water, whereas only clusters of rushes can be seen growing in the wider of the two branches. In the southeast, some cliffs stand above the river, and the currents seem strong in the murky waters below.
102061: Clear water rushes furiously southwards, dragging with it everything that dares to cross its path. Closer to the shore it calms down, but it still moves with distinct determination. A low slope separates the water from the grassy fields beyond; on these sides animals visit frequently to drink from the water.
102062: Bending back to its original path to the south the river stretches out, cutting through the green landscape. Behind a couple of rocks peeking up from the bottom of the river, shadows of resting fish reflect in the clear but disturbed surface. The water flows quickly southwards carving its way down in the soft earth, leaving the banks numerous feet high.
102063:
A trout swims here.
A trout swims here.

Here on the very border of the Gladden Fields the river makes a turn south again, as if avoiding the marshy landscape. Following its path it becomes obvious however that it cannot avoid it much longer. In this area the land is covered in a gentle mist rising from the ground, and the fields on either side of the current are drenched in moss and water. This was once the shores of a great lake, but now looks more like the shores of a moss-filled sea, stretching as far as the eye can see in the west.
102064: The monotony of the mud that covers the riverbed of the Anduin is broken here and there by large rocks, however, these rocks are not tall enough to bruise the surface of the water. The surrounding riverbanks are quite flat, except to the south-east, where some hills can be seen in the distance.
102065: The smaller, but far more clear, Gladden meets the larger Anduin in a remnant of the former lake that once covered all of the Gladden Fields. The size of it is now more like a large pool, though. There are quite a few eddies near the border of the triangular mouth of the western and lesser river.
102066: A Small Bend in the Anduin

The Anduin heads into the southwest, its bed forming a rough line, broken apart in many places by slight bends among the usually flat marshes. Some floating water plants and algae can be noticed here and there, bordering these widely spaced out and grassy riverbanks.
102067: The Anduin makes a bend here in its bed around a hill, being located towards the south-east. It is bordered to both the north and west by vast marshes. While the river seems to make another bend not far to the east, its course appears to be roughly straight to the south.
102068: The Anduin river, which flows from the north-east, progressively tightens its bed towards the south. Here, it leaves the slow Gladden Fields and returns to its normal, fast flowing stream as it travels. Some old leaves can be seen in some of the small inlets, leftovers of the last autumn.
102069: A speckled, brown and white bird with a long curved bill stands here.

Curving west to south, this section of the river is a part of a larger s-shaped bend in the Anduin. North from here, a wet and broad swamp feeds debris into the river's main current. Passage westwards onto a rugged, boulder-strewn plain is also possible. Downstream, eddies and maelstroms speak of a current that is increasing its pace as it makes its way through these forsaken lands.
102070: Bend in the Great River Anduin

Flowing steadily to the south into what appears to be a bend, the mighty river Anduin broadens slightly; thus allowing rich beds of ferns to grow high along the river banks. Some unevenness or another on the bottom of the river causes quite a lot of eddies and swirls to appear mid-river. A lot of debris, presumably from the forests south and west of here, seems to have been caught in the whirlpools.
102071: The Great River flows from the east, running along the curved edge of the bank on its northwestern side, and continues to flow southbound from here. There are a lot of pebbles and stones which are visible along the bottom of the river. The bank to the north appears to be very steep from this distance, though towards the west it looks flatter.
102072: The river has travelled from the east here, taking a bend towards the south as it continues its course in that direction. Towards the northern bank, it is noticeable how level the soil is, appearing as though at one time long ago the river had even flowed over the bank there. The river itself expands a wide distance from each bank. The water does not flow as fast here, but it is very clear to see the riverbed it flows upon, through the ripples of the water.
102074:
The corpse of a husky bodyguard is lying here.
The corpse of a husky bodyguard is lying here.
You see a bloody, disgusting scalp lying on the ground.
The corpse of Azra-Zaira is lying here.
A large torch lies here among the dust.
The shadow of a husky bodyguard is floating here.

This underground chamber's walls were made of natural stones and pieces of rock. The stones and pieces of rock were firmly placed into the earthen walls with some kind of black material in between the stones to seal them. The stones were placed tightly together, even though each is oddly shaped. The floor of the chamber was laid with several pieces of flat, black slate. Between each piece of slate there are cracks that were left unfilled with sealant; now water has built up in between them from all the moisture in the earth. On the eastern wall, there are two torches braced between stones by small metal brackets. Below the torches is a scarlet coloured canvas concealing the wall. However, on the northern wall a lever of golden colour is visible.
102075: Within this chamber there are four slender pillars, which are providing support for keeping a black sheet of slate, used as the ceiling, in its proper place. The flooring is of the same slate that was used for the ceiling, though there are many carved grooves upon the surface. The four walls were made of many natural stones pressed tightly together into the earth, with a black sealant to fill the tiny spaces between them. In the centre of the chamber, there is a large, black orb.
102076:
A large bookshelf sits against the wall.
On the bookshelf, there is a black journal.

The library has four walls made of black slate. Two of these walls have a few shelves built within them, with a golden-coloured lining at the base of each one. Upon the shelves are several different sculptures and a fleet of model ships, each looking unique in their fashion and design. The south wall contains a bookshelf and a large map, with a golden frame holding it to the wall. The north wall has a dark, cherry-coloured door that has a rounded arch design at the top of it. Above the arched door, a golden banner was placed on display. The floor of the library is lined with carpet, matching the colour of the banner above the arched door. A large candle is set in a brass stand between the bookcase and the framed map upon the wall, giving off a soft glow of light to the library.
102318: Once this earthen tunnel was mined, judging by the rotten wooden supports that prop up its roof. Now it has flooded completely, a dense mixture of mud and water which makes it hard to see any distance. Through the hazy water you can just see a hole in the roof, and the main tunnel leading upwards to the north.
102320: A thinning grove of conifer trees borders the bank of a fast flowing brook. Lined with algae and water lilies, during the summer months the water's edge teems with insect life. To the east and west the stream continues. The trees begin to fade to the south, where rolling plains pick up and dominate the landscape, while a sheer side of the Misty Mountains looms to the north.
102444:
The corpse of a huge, poisonous spider is lying here.
The corpse of a huge, poisonous spider is lying here.
The corpse of a huge, poisonous spider is lying here.
A heavy chest of oak, banded with iron, stands here.

This is less of a room and more of a niche. It is no more than about six feet across in either direction, and the curved ceiling sweeps down toward the floor on all sides, meaning that only at the very centre of the room can anyone of average human stature stand upright. The floor is made from robust wooden boards, with a square trapdoor set just to one side of the centre of the chamber.
102490: A brown fox is here, looking for some rabbits to chew up.

The vast expanse of grass lasts well beyond your eyesight. The most significant deviation in the monotonous scenery comes from patches of rocky soil where the grass has not been able to penetrate. Common sense tells you to stock up on food and water before going much further into these parts.
102491: Ancient Stairs to the River Anduin

Set in a narrow pass between two steep, rugged cliffs, these ancient stone stairs descend towards the Great River flowing by in the east. Each step is at least four feet wide, allowing one to haul goods or lead mounts down to a sheltered bay which seems like an abandoned landing for boats. The roughly hewn stone of the steps is covered in a carpet of fragile grass and lichen, yet at some points, intricate engravings are faintly visible below the growth. The staircase bends slightly, and together with the high walls of rock, it offers shade during the daytime. Some lengths of iron rail, attached to the rock, seem sturdy despite their apparent age, and offer a firm handhold for climbing the stairs.
102492:
A blooming water-lily floats on the surface of the water.
A fat carp swims here.
A fat carp swims here.

Drawn by their own weight, the stone structures of this quay are slowly sinking into the mud of the river. Being abandoned, almost the whole quay has been surrounded by walls of reeds, only the very end reaches out to the more open part of the Anduin. The greater part of the quay has already sunk under a few feet of water and is growing algae. All kinds of shallow-water plants are thriving here despite being shaded by the cliffs above.
102530: A doorwarden stands here ready to obey his master's wishes.
Leaving the loud bustle of the city, you have entered a hallway covered in old paint. It quietly leads to the north where it meets up with a brightly lit kitchen.
102531: From the hallway south, you enter a large room filled with strange utensils and the smell of fresh baked bread. A small fire burns at one end of the room, providing light and warmth to those who visit. On the far end you see a broad oak door providing passage to the north.
102532: A humble man stands here, ready to help you with your things.

This is a large chamber, decorated with artefacts, paintings and art work from times long past. To the side of the room lies a small table with two chairs neatly tucked beside it. A large bed lies in the centre of the room, laced with white silk sheets and satin pillows. The air itself feels warm and relaxing.
102533: A large fountain, made from grey stone, pours water from its centre.

The room is mostly unfurnished, allowing one to easily move around and train. In the centre of it lies a large straw mat where soldiers can practice their fighting arts. A large shield hangs on the wall to the north, encrusted with the symbol of the Rohirrim.
102534: The Housekeeper looks fed up with her job. She scowls at you unhappily.

A small simple bed lies in the corner of the room, along with several chests which bear personal belongings inside. A large window is set on the east wall, allowing you to view the citizens of Fornost as they go about their daily duties.
102535: You enter a small space, filled with the smell of metal and rust. To the side of the room there are many pegs and racks supporting the weight of many fine suits of armour and weapons. Most are shiny and new, although some show the wear of the glory of battle.
102536: You find a warm room with many tables and chairs huddled around a fire at the north side of the room you see a large granite fireplace, it warms the room allowing you to feel at ease.
102537: An Elven steward stands here, watching over the household.
You enter a simple bedroom, with a large oak bed at its centre. The room is circular in nature and is kept very neat. Two bookshelves are set against the walls, filled with books of the arcane arts.
102538: As you enter this room, the noise of Fornost seems to fade into dead silence, you see four straw mats laid along the floor. Obviously this is a place where you can escape the world and be at peace.
102539: A humble man stands here, ready to help you with your things.

A strong aroma of meat, ale, and sweat fill this cosy tavern. With no natural light source, the dark almost stifling atmosphere might be relaxing to adventurers who have experienced a hard days work. Loud snoring and some other muffled noises can be heard from the sleeping area.
102568: The King's Road by the Palisade

The road makes yet another sharp turn, towards a passage through the wooden wall which lies just west now. An old crumbling building lies north of the road, its broken shutters slamming against the walls every now and then, reminding you that all things must eventually come to an end.
102569: Named for the eleventh Chieftain of the Dunedain, this road connects the ancient gardens with the King's Road. The cobblestones are well worn, as much of the city's traffic, warriors, adventurers and merchants, pass it on their way to the southern or western gates of Fornost.
102570: Stepping into these ancient gardens, it might seem as if it is hundreds of miles away from the city. In contrast to the noisy cobblestone streets, this greenery exudes peace and calm. The clumps of flowers are partly overgrown, but their shape is always neat. Flower bushes line the dirt paths that crisscross the garden. To the south and west start cobblestone streets.
102571:
A man passes by, intent on his business.
A rugged-looking man is standing here.

Old ruins of a house stand in this rocky lot. The base still seems to be intact, its condition most likely allowing another rebuild for anyone's need. At one corner of the ruins, wild berry bushes grow in abundance. Looking down, one can see a door made of stone leading down into the rock.
102572: A Dunadan soldier is here busily performing his duties.

The cobblestone road ends here, at the site of an old garden. To the north, a small fence lines an entrance of a house which probably belongs to one of Fornost's many citizens. A large pile of various pieces of furniture draws attention just south of the road.
102573:
A Dunadan soldier is here busily performing his duties.
An experienced Dunadan officer is standing here, keeping things under control.
A citizen-mercenary is here, waiting for a job.

Off the busy Guild Street, the noise of the city seems to decrease. Small flower gardens line the sides of the cobblestone road, looking well-tended and taken care of all year round. The street continues westwards, moving closer to the private houses of the citizens of Fornost.
102574: There is a lit street-lamp on the border of the street, illuminating the area.

Strolling along, you can't help to notice the attitude of people you encounter; Scholars and wealthy merchants in expensive clothing, with clerks and servants in hot pursuit, all seem to regard your presence here as a bit unfortunate. You are something that doesn't quite belong here, but a necessary evil perhaps.
102578:
An insolent scholar is here, pondering.
A man passes by, intent on his business.

You have entered a crowded building, in which some kind of auction is taking place. It is here that merchants, local or from far away places, gather in order to trade, buy or sell their many different wares.
102579: Building materials are piled up all over this place. Shops are to the left and right though they look all unfinished. There are no workers here and everything is covered with a thick layer of dust. It seems that there wasn't anyone working on the shops for a long time. A portal is to the west leading to an overgrown garden. A sign is nailed to the portal.
102587: A large overgrown garden in front of a marble palace to the south. It maybe once was bright and pleasant but now it looks like no one has entered or cared for it for many long years. A small path is leading towards the palace. It is covered with a few washed out footprints.
102588: A humble man stands here, ready to help you with your things.

The inside of this palace also looks unfinished. A stairway is leading up and in the east is the kitchen. The west side isn't finished yet. The main rooms are further south. There is only a thin layer of dust covering the furniture. It looks like someone is taking care of this place from time to time.
102589: A large bulletin board, entitled "Warriors' Guild Board", is mounted here.

Here warriors are among themselves so they can relax, heal their wounds and chat about new weapons and new protective clothing. A bulletin board is mounted here, its purpose is to spread such information. The room looks comfortable, with soft chairs along the walls, and colourful carpets.
102590:
A sturdy bed made from solid oak lies here, covered in warm blankets.
A humble man stands here, ready to help you with your things.
A sturdy pack horse is standing here.

This is a tall rectangular bedchamber. During the day, thin streams of light enter the room through several grilled windows set high up the wall, almost to the ceiling. A large four-poster bed, draped in embroidered material, stands against the western wall. Beside it is a small oak cabinet, which looks to be filled with personal artefacts. Against the eastern wall is a legendary sword set into a magically glowing stone, raised atop a short marble dais. The southern side of the room contains a series of iron weapons, armour and racks of the finest equipment in the known world. An oak and mahogany-crafted doorway leads northward to a warrior's common room.
102591:
A large stone fireplace with a roaring fire warms the room.
The Housekeeper looks fed up with her job. She scowls at you unhappily.

Isolated from the noise and the crowd of the city, this room looks perfectly maintained and well arranged by its owner. There are racks hanging on the walls containing trophies taken from the battles fought by Aquiles, the legend from Eriador, who keeps this home for resting and meditating from his deeds on the battlefield. In the corner a couple plants and flowers decorate the room making it a more comfortable place. The floor is entirely covered with fine carpets. Over the front window hangs a soft curtain which protects the room from any watchful eyes outside.
102592: A humble man stands here, ready to help you with your things.

All around there are weapons and shields adorning the walls. Many paintings depict scenes of epic battles. In the far corner there is what appears to be a small collection of digusting scalps apparently torn from those that have fallen at the master of this dwelling's hand. This home obviously belongs to some great and merciless warrior who might not be pleased to find strangers inside his home.
102593: Large pieces of disused or no longer wanted furniture have been piled up here. Some wooden slates have started to rot so that grass and moss are spreading their roots over them. Despite the first impression being quite ragged, a person with few resources but good handicraft skills could find things to fix a place up easily enough.
102594:
A small white fountain is here.
A rather dirty young boy is here, ready to tend to the stable.
A doorwarden stands here ready to obey his master's wishes.

This is a rather large garden full of flowering plants and shrubs. There are so many different kinds of blooms it is hard to imagine any variety or colour of flower not represented. Zack, the owner of this garden, clearly must have some strange fixation with flowers. Most likely a well kept secret to all but those friends that know him well enough to merit an invitation to his home. To the north, there is the entrance to a large armoury.
102595:
A humble man stands here, ready to help you with your things.
A cockroach is scuttling across the floor carrying some debris.

This large armoury has rows upon rows of weapon racks arranged in such a way that each is displayed so it can be seen clearly, as well as taken down quickly, in time of need. Beyond the weapons, at the rear of the structure, are suits of armour, shields and helmets. What is most notable about this collection is the variety of unique styles, clearly this armoury's owner is serious about his weaponry. At the centre of the room is a large wooden platform.
102596: A doorwarden stands here ready to obey his master's wishes.

This is a very nice garden with lots of flowers all arond. There seems to be almost every kind of flowers you can ever imagine in here. Utgbald who lives here must have some strange fixation about flowers that not many people know about. North of here is Utgbalds living room, and to the south is the magnificent Arnor Square.
102597: All the walls of this room are filled with bookcases, except for the west wall that leads into Utgbalds bedroom. There is a nice set of comfy couches there, with a really neat table in between them.
102598: A humble man stands here, ready to help you with your things.

In one of the corners of the room there is a really huge bed. Maybe Utgbald is looking for a companion that wants to share his bed, since it really is huge. The walls in here are covered with all different kind of pictures.
102599: The Room of the Gate Guards

A falchion lies on the ground.
A falchion lies on the ground.
A small wooden shield is on the ground.
A falchion lies on the ground.

This room probably once contained the gate guard of the castle. A hole in the wall to the south, once filled by a door, takes you back towards the gates. In one corner of the room, a stone stair leads down into the darkness of the basement, and up in a small tower above.
102600: This small tower overlooks the outer gates of the castle, and the drawbridge below it. The battlements once continued both north and south, but to the north they seem to be anything but safe to walk. A small stair leads down to the old guard room.
102606: You have reached the battlements just above the drawbridge. To the west, you see a small, overgrown path winding slowly up the slope towards the citadel on the small hill to the north east. You can continue your stroll on the battlements to the east, although they don't look very inviting.
102615: A black snake hurries towards you with sly intentions.

The battlements are indeed in a poor state of repair here, and the narrow walkway has crumbled almost completely away in some places, so that progress to the east is quite impossible from here. The only choice is to head west, where the walls are in a better condition.
102616:
A large bulletin board, entitled "Free Peoples' Chronicles", is mounted here.
A huge clock is standing here.
An amber-coloured pint of ale sits here in a large frosty mug.
A fine marble chessboard with ivory and ebony pieces is set here.
A large stone fireplace with a roaring fire warms the room.
A barman watches you calmly, while skilfully mixing a drink.
Tundur the Lamplighter is resting here.

This is a loud place! You hear harsh voices, shrill laughter, and the high sound of glasses clinking. An endless stream of beer finds its way into the bellies of the rough men who frequent this room. The swords are removed, however, and it is usually very peaceful here. A sign hangs on one of the walls.
102617: A humble man stands here, ready to help you with your things.

This looks to be the simple home of an old dwarf. There are several weapons hanging on racks upon the walls that looked to have been acquired on the owner's travels. In the far right corner there is a fireplace. When lit the flames provide a light and warm the room. The bed sits to the left of the room and near the door two beer barrels have been set.
102618:
A large fountain, made from grey stone, pours water from its centre.
A doorwarden stands here ready to obey his master's wishes.
A tall and strong guard is here.
A tall and strong guard is here.

A long, spiralling stairwell extends down from the corridor above and leads into these spacious living quarters. The ceilings are very high, yet well lit from top to bottom. Small shafts inserted into the ceilings help to circulate the room, bringing in fresh air from the outside all the time. The floor is smooth, polished by the wise and skillful hands of master Dwarven craftsmen.
102619:
A weapons rack stands against the wall.
A tall and strong guard is here.

This large cave is well lit by various size lamps on all sides. Ornamented shields and shiny armour hang from pegs built into the walls. A sword rack leans up against the south wall, full of blades both sharp and dull. To the east, the cave opens up to a large hall.
102620:
A sturdy bed made from solid oak lies here, covered in warm blankets.
A small oaken table has been set here.
On the table, there is a bottle and a mince-pie.

This room is smaller than the large hall to the north and lined with shelves dug into the walls. The air is filled with the smoke of pipes from recent celebrations and leftover plates from a grand feast are deposited here and there. There is a large table here for visitors to use, as well as a few beds for the weary friends of Khazdul.
102621: Though at the entrance this hallway looks narrow, from within it can be seen expanding to a cavernous size. The smooth, polished floor slopes gently down to the north. The walls are covered in mosaics of semi-precious stones, forming images of Dwarven lords and heroes. With their eyes made of shining rubies, they look down at all those who pass beneath them.
102622:
A small oaken table has been set here.
A large stone chest is here.

A stalactite hangs down from the roof, a bright gem suspended from its tip. A faint light emanates from the gem, flickering and making shadows dance on the walls. In the middle of the room stands a giant stalagmite masterfully carved into a statue depicting the stout Dwarven warrior Khozdul. One could linger here for many an hour, simply sitting and pondering, perhaps smoking pipe-weed and absorbing the past as if to gain from it strength for the future.
102623:
A sturdy bed made from solid oak lies here, covered in warm blankets.
A stout Dwarven steward stands here, ready to defend the home.

The walls and the floor of this large hall are made of black stone streaked with gold. Suits of armour line the walls, glittering in the soft light. A couple of regal carpets cover the floor. Several pillars decorated with sapphires, opals, diamonds, and other precious jewels stretch towards the smooth marble roof. The room is so neat and clean that it could probably accomodate even the fairest of Elves.
102624:
A sturdy bed made from solid oak lies here, covered in warm blankets.
A humble man stands here, ready to help you with your things.

This chamber is inhabited by the dwarf Khazdul. It is a spacious room, yet dimly lit in comparison to the brightness of the main hall to the west. The light from various candles bounces and flickers as the flames cast shadows on the walls from all sides. A large bed sits in one corner, on top of an old, woven rug.
102625: The walls of this passage are made of large stone blocks placed upon one another. The blocks are piled from the floor to the ceiling where they form a dome. Inside the dome, bricks of dark and light marble create a intricate pattern across the ceiling. Small bronze lanterns provide the cavern with a bright but yet warm light.
102626: Candles and lanterns light this huge hall which is cut deep into the rock. Across the western wall hangs a large beautifully carved pine branch. Centered below the branch hangs an oil-painting of Bagger. Below the painting a fireplace is situated. In front of the fireplace stands a comfortable chair. From the midst of the northern wall, an old table made out of teak stretches towards the centre of the room, and along the table some chairs stand. Axes and shields of different origin are on displayed all over the eastern wall.
102627:
A large stone fireplace with a roaring fire warms the room.
A small white fountain is here.
A doorwarden stands here ready to obey his master's wishes.
A tall and strong guard is here.
A tall and strong guard is here.

The solid oaken doors open up into a large, high-ceilinged hall with a strange construction of metal and glass in the centre of the roof. This dome allows the light of day to illuminate the interior of the hall. Two statues of bronze dragons with ruby eyes stand in eternal watch for their master on either side of the door. In the centre of the northern wall, a well-decorated oaken door gives passage to another room. On either side of the door carpets can be seen hanging on the wall. The left carpet portrays a golden dragon on a field of crimson and the right carpet shows a battle scene on which one man is battling a threesome of orcs. In the northeastern and northwestern corners of the hall there are fireplaces, which often give warmth to the place. Near the northwestern fireplace a comfortable sofa has been placed making it an ideal place for reading. A pile of books, neatly stacked atop each other, lie next to it. Beside the northeastern fireplace a large table has been set with eight comfortable, but functional, leather chairs.
102628:
A large stone fireplace with a roaring fire warms the room.
A large bookshelf sits against the wall.
A weapons rack stands against the wall.
A sturdy peg for hanging armour from is on the wall.
A humble man stands here, ready to help you with your things.

In the northern wall there are two large windows which allow the day light to illuminate the whole room. Set between them is a large, very comfortable looking, bed. On the right side of the room a desk has been placed facing the door. All sorts of maps, covering all of Arda, are laid out on it. On the left side of the room stands a peg for armour, covered with a gleaming suit of mithril chain mail. Next to that stands a weapon rack with a master's choice of hammers and swords. Two small fireplaces, one in the southeastern corner and one in the southwestern corner of the room, maintain a comfortable temperature in here.
102650: A rack with large, wooden hooks made for hanging hats and garments stands in the corner of this tidy kitchen. A bench has been placed against the west wall, facing a small, green table with matching chairs. Pots and pans of various sizes and shapes hang from the wall, atop a cast iron oven which has been inset into the room. On the east wall stands two bookshelves which have been neatly organized with many books of recipes and ornamented, metal silverware.
102651: A humble man stands here, ready to help you with your things.

A rather large bed is dominating this pretty small bedroom. A fluffy, checkered quilt is covering the bed that is facing the eastern wall, allowing the morning light to filter in through the window in the eastern wall and waking whoever is sleeping in the bed. A thick wool carpet is covering most of the floor. A door in the west wall is leading to the kitchen.
102652: Oak shelves line all four walls in the food storage. The contests of the shelves varies a lot, to west the shelf is filled with apples and pears lying side by side without touching each other. The shelves south and east are filled with jars containing a big variety of different jams. The last shelf, the one to the north, is containing the most important things. Bottles of whisky and liqueur are standing in lines, the innermost ones covered with dust. A worn staircase in the centre of the room is leading up into the kitchen above.
102653: Lit torches make shadows dance along the walls in this curving hallway, which stretches out to the north and east. The polished walls are completely smooth to the touch. Small veins of ore can be seen, illuminating the corridor with a faint glow.
102654: The large hallway curves slowly to the west and south here, barely lit by the ensconced torches on the walls. Small veins of ore glow slightly in the dim light of the torches. The ceiling is quite high, echoing any sound of movement in the otherwise still air.
102655: A large stone fireplace with a roaring fire warms the room.

The high ceiling of the corridor rises even higher, opening into an enormous hall. A fireplace crackles in the centre of the room, filling the hall with warmth. Comfortable chairs have been placed around the fireplace, allowing the residents of this place to relax after a hard day. Small corridors lead off to the north and south.
102656: A stout Dwarven steward stands here, ready to defend the home.

A small, cramped chamber opens up from the corridor to the north. This room is large enough for only one inhabitant to sleep in comfortably, though more could occupy the area in time of need. A statue in the likeness of Durin the Deathless stands is the corner, a monument to the great Dwarf-lord.
102657:
A large bookshelf sits against the wall.
A stout Dwarven steward stands here, ready to defend the home.

This small chamber is lit by only one torch. Slightly cramped, it is nonetheless a comfortable place for a hardy Dwarf to sleep. The entrance is large enough for even an Elf to enter; however, more than a few people in this room would be uncomfortable at best.
102658: Stairs carved directly into the rockface provide passage from Durin's Hall to the chambers below. An abundance of torches light the otherwise dark room, allowing travellers to carefully avoid mishaps on their way up or down. Much activity can be heard from Durin's Hall, while the corridor heading east at the base of the stairs is strangely quiet.
102659: The walls of this corridor are almost pitch-black, yet strangely reflective, allowing the light from the torches ensconced on the walls to play on the smooth surfaces. Although there is usually much activity in the halls above, almost no noise can be heard here. Small rooms can be seen to the north and south, while the stairwell leads back to Durin's Hall to the west.
102660: The corridor continues, heading deep into the mountains underneath the Trader's Way. A swell of heat can be felt from the room to the north, and the banging of hammer on anvil is heard constantly during the day; the Dwarves must keep busy forging weapons and armour. A small chamber opens up to the south through a stone door. The obsidian walls glisten in the torchlight, confusing the eye.
102661:
A large bookshelf sits against the wall.
A stout Dwarven steward stands here, ready to defend the home.

The walls are lined with Dwarven historical artefacts, setting this place of worship apart from the other temples. On the western wall hangs a portrait of Durin the Deathless himself, standing in all his glory. In keeping with the vow of poverty chosen by the Patriarch, the room lacks many decorations and is poorly-lit, giving the Dwarves that pray here a sense of unity as they pray to their deity.
102662: A stout Dwarven steward stands here, ready to defend the home.

This room has few furnishings of interest. Only a large chest in the far corner of the room displays an impressive collection of elements of war, most of them having seen at least one bloody battle. The inhabitant of this room obviously lives for warfare and takes pleasure only in a battle well-fought.
102663: A humble man stands here, ready to help you with your things.

Inside the sleeping quarters of the Bodyguard of Durin's Army can be found the tools of his trade. Glittering armour both new and old lines the walls, waiting to turn the blade of a fell minion of Sauron's. Swords, axes and bows rest in weapon racks, biding their time until they are called forth to do battle with an evil Orc or Troll.
102664: A blast of warm air sweeps across the entrace to this vast room. The tall chimneys of the smithy of Durin's Army extend high above the ground, disappearing into the darkness above. The bodyguard of Durin's Army is also a skilled craftsman, and aids his fellow Dwarves if there is a need, be it a dent too large or a scratch too deep.
102665:
A small oaken table has been set here.
A mailbox stands here stuffed full of messages.

The large hall stretches out deep into the mountains. A strong but pleasant smell of food wafts into the room from the south, where the sounds of cooking and cleaning can often be heard. Several large tables have been placed around the hall, apparently made for a large number of Dwarves to feast at.
102666: This large kitchen is roomy, allowing many Dwarves to create a large feast for a seemingly even larger number of Dwarves waiting outside. Since Dwarves are generally very fond of food and drink, there are large pantries leading away from the kitchen, where any number of delicacies can always be found.
102678: The walls of this deep pit slope up sharply and are covered with sharp spikes which prevent anything from climbing them. The pit is wide enough to permit three large trolls to fight side by side, and runs for quite a distance to the east and west. There is a very narrow crack to the west which may lead out of here, but a single opponent could block any escape that way.
102679:
An orc of the Uruk-moragog stands in the gloom.
An orc of the Uruk-moragog stands in the gloom.
An orc of the Uruk-moragog stands in the gloom.

This large, deep pit serves as the proving ground for aspiring orc and troll warriors and as a deathpit for slaves and prisoners who have nothing left to offer the Durghash. The walls are steep and covered with razor-sharp spikes which dispel any hope of climbing out of here, so it seems that it is time to fight or die. The only possible escape is west.
102725: Running north-south, the tunnel continues its sloping passage, delving ever deeper into the heart of the mountain. These underground tunnels seem endless and you wonder if you will ever find your way out. The passage seems once to have been very well travelled, the centre of the roadway looking thoroughly worn down. A faint breeze whispers past you, making a welcome change to the otherwise damp and chilly still air.
102726: This corridor slopes smoothly downwards to the south, continuing on its arrow-straight course from north to south. The ceiling is well out of your reach, even though it's lower than previously in this part of the tunnel. You notice the remains of a short wooden stick or plank smashed into the ground, seemingly with terrible force, and wonder who or what would possess such incredible strength.
102727: Running north-south, the tunnel continues its sloping passage through the Dwarven mines. A considerably smaller passage angles off to the west, quickly twisting beyond view in the dark. The passageway itself also disappears into darkness and turning to look back the way you came, it truly looks as if there is no end to it. You draw a deep breath and consider; what if there really is no exit?
102737: The small twisting tunnel comes to an abrupt end, leaving you no choice but to turn back. The walls are rough, this short passage maybe once intended as the beginning of a new passageway. That idea has been abandoned though, and now only black rock stares back at you where the tunnel might have continued. To the east, the passage twists out of this dead-end. The bones of some small creature lie in the corner, reminding you of the harshness of this underground, at times prisonlike, dungeon.
102738:
An orkish warrior of the Durghash is here, with a cruel glint in his eye.
An orkish warrior of the Durghash is here, with a cruel glint in his eye.

What must have once been a natural cavern now shows signs of extensive work. Hard-angled rocks have been smoothed out and most rock formations have either been worn or chopped away. The ceiling is much lower than usual in this part of the caverns, hardly twice a grown man's height. Placed in several niches and alcoves, and along the walls of this cavern, is a number of huge round boulders. You also notice some sturdy wooden beams lying in a few places, as well as a couple of heavy iron bars.
102778:
A pair of metal boots are standing here.
A plain leather belt is lying here.
A fine chain mail coif lies here.
A plain pair of pants are on the ground.
A plain shirt is on the ground.

The wooden walls of this dilapidated building have an indeterminate colour of a rotting barrel. The crumbling ceiling beams support the earthen roof, with roots of weeds hanging from it in foul congregations. The mud floor is layered with trampled dirty hay. Rudimentary shelves line the walls, empty but for a few clay mugs. A small window facing west lets in a modicum of light; opposite it is the hut's only man-made entrance. The southern wall is gone, collapsed by the heat of a raging forest fire.

A narrow path littered with darkened stones leads away from a small mud hut and up a gentle incline. The gargantuan trees in the surrounding forest hang over the path ominously. Their black crowns drown out the sky. They hover above the hut, their branches like giant tentacles ready to pounce at any moment. The stones marking the path are dark with soot, though whence it came one cannot tell.

Drowning among the decaying tall black trees of indeterminate origin is a small path, twisting and turning among their humongous roots. The branches of the trees, tantalizingly ugly, hang over the path precariously. They almost touch the ash-covered ground in a few places. The twisted shadows of the surrounding forest come alive in its darkness.

Large black boulders, massive like the stones of Angband, are scattered about the ground here. They impede the offensive of the dark wood that is pressing on the rock-strewn path that twists from west to north. The high ground gives way in the east with a sharp drop. The sound of water can be heard from below it.

Black water, deep and menacing, runs slowly southwards. Outlined by tall unclimbable banks, the stream turns into tarred barely moving sludge along the edges. Rotting pieces of wood and partial bones, of which few are of animal origin, dot the shallow parts of the river. To the south it merges into a black lake, and a wooden bridge is visible further north.
102783: Half-rotten rickety planks hammered haphazardly together are standing on the tall black beams, rising high over the foetid water. The scaffolding that supports the bridge has seen better times; one of its sections bends westwards precariously. A noxious fog is rising above the black water, which from the bridge looks bottomless and poisonous. A greenish frothy residue sticking around the support beams grows half-way up to their tops.
102784: There is some snow on the ground.

This pool of pitch-black water, perfectly round like the eye of Ungoliant, glares menacingly at the surrounding forest. Not one tree bole or branch is suspended over the lake. Silence hangs over it like a shield, and there is an almost physical feeling of danger permeating the air. How deep this ghastly pool is one cannot guess, for the evil waters conceal everything and reveal nothing.
102785: There is a lot of snow on the ground.

This forest is a nightmare of twisted trees, roots, and shadows. Indeed its shadows move with a life of their own and suck the colour from wherever they fall. Delicate tapestries of webs, shining black with slime, congregate among the lower branches and trunks of the crooked black trees. A low noise, humming, hammering, hollering, and haranguing, emanates from all around here, giving the place a certain feeling of genuine helpless insanity.

Giant footprints, each a dozen handspans long, are crowding in front of the gate.

This trail, twisting and turning among disfigured black trees, is covered with charred pebbles. Thin columns of smoke rise from among the larger stones. They reek of peat bog, rotten wood, and burning flesh. To the west, the path crosses a dark stream. To the east, walls of a mighty citadel rise starkly against the sky. Hardy black flowers on short greying stalks glare evilly from the ground.
102789: There is a lot of snow on the ground.

Incredibly tall and twisted dark trees, like the heart of Morgoth, grow here. They stand file by file, rank by rank: a mighty army of darkness, a harbinger of ruin, a scrounger of light. The reality warps itself among their trunks and their shadows, and distance loses its meaning to a mortal eye. No movement, no small forest animals, no life can subsist here.
102790: There is a lot of snow on the ground.

Tall trees, black, like the darkest moonless night, are standing here upright, their branches shooting straight into the skies. Their breed, common to this forest, seems to have been released of their twisted souls in death. The pungent air hangs heavily over the puddles of water collecting at their feet.
102791: There is a lot of snow on the ground.

Dark and menacing, the trees in this part of the forest are twisted into strange primeval forms. They are the spirits of the forest, the guardians of this forsaken land, the invaders of dreams, the destroyers of hope. In their shadows, no thing retains its true form. Under their boughs, all living things become small and insignificant. Dread hangs over the forest here like a thick winter cloak.
102792: There is a lot of snow on the ground.

The crooked black trees, tall, mighty, and as ugly as the fires of Udun, have planted their roots here. The roots themselves, their bulges and tentacles, crooked fingers and twisted arms, cover the forest floor so thoroughly that no hint of earth is seen anywhere. The darkness of the forest is permeated by a rancid smell. It is windless here, but among the trees, their shadows move, while their twins stand still, as if suspended in some dream of calamity and horror.
102793: There is a lot of water on the ground.

The narrow winding path is twisting and turning among the ash-covered boulders and contorted trees, whose limbs keep trying to reach the parched earth upon which the trail is running. Darkness and the feeling of foreboding hang heavily in the air. Remnants of isolated fires dot the ground, as if some great army broke camp here on the way out. Some persistent weeds, twisted by their very nature, much like their larger cousins, grow on both sides of the path.
102794: There is a lot of snow on the ground.

The muddy ground here is covered with holes and burrows - ghastly sores on the skin of the land. The monstrous trees growing in this forest are twisted into demonic shapes. The stooped trunks of some of them bend so much that they reach the ground with their deformed tops. An acrid smell rises from the hollows in the ground; it is almost tangible in the heavy-hanging atmosphere of this forsaken forest.

Roaring into the eternal twilights of the Angmarian sky, the massive iron gates span the opening between the black walls of the outer citadel. The sheets of iron are hammered together by square blackened nails whose caps bear rudimentary engravings of an iris, malevolent even in its basic incarnation. Thirty feet tall, the gates can move outwards on large metal wheels deviously concealed within their structure. Sharp spikes run along their top edge, and the front part of the gates is covered with them also, much like the skin of a porcupine. This is the entrance to one of the mightiest dark strongholds, its main tower silhouetted ghost-like against the eastern sky.

Black cobblestones, worn with age and flattened by feet and paws of many Angmarian armies, line the square in front of the mighty iron gates. Bits of ash swirl around the square like first winter snowflakes. A chill wind blows back and forth, a captive within the tall black walls. A black menacing guard tower rises to the east, and behind it the main citadel blots out the sky. A dark road runs from here toward the keep's centre and along the perimeter walls.
102797: Darkened cobblestones, flat from all the feet that have marched along here over the ages, run along the western outer wall of the castle. A couple of dilapidated hovels hug the walls. The road turns from the north to the east here, dodging the burned remains of army barracks. Inescapable, the smell of droppings and human remains lingers in the air.

Propped against a black stone wall, this wooden contraption leans heavily on the structure of its front wall. Its ceiling is surprisingly tall, its details receding into animated darkness. Horizontal bars supporting the roof bear leftovers of many rotting ropes. Crunching underneath, the dirty mud floor is covered with thick piles of human remains. Soft screams, echoes of things past, pierce the air with their parting pleas, forever captured by the dreadful magic of this place. Ghastly and intimidating, this house is a graveyard of the ages.
102799: The inner road leaves the square in front of the gates and departs north. Wide and spacious, it still seems insignificantly small compared to the walls encircling the castle. The wall of the guard keep runs along its eastern side, a stomach-turning smell of burning flesh coming strong from that direction. Battlements are outlined high up along the castle walls.
102800: The road turns along the northwestern corner of the walls of the Angmarian castle. Several levels of heavily fortified battlements are visible all the way to the top of the wall. Some tall metal ladders are heaped in the corner. They would allow for quick access to the lowest floor of defence installations in case of emergency. Link-chain ladders connect the rest of the levels among themselves.
102801: Countless couriers, prisoners, and armies trotted down this road before its dark stones turned flat as they are now. The huge monoliths comprising the walls have a bearing of terrifying prowess. They and the cobblestones seem to have come from the same mine, dark, lifeless, but with a soul-weakening magic of its own. The north walls of the citadel and the guard keep protect the road from the elements both within and outside the Angmarian castle.
102802: Bleak and dismal, the cheerless stone road is squeezed between two ominous black walls, and thus is forever destined to be in their murky shadows. Nothing grows or lives here, for the joyless stones of Angmar can provide no nourishment. In fact, they are repositories of the darkest and foulest magic which holds this land of nightmares together. The only break in the monotony is a small arched passage to the south, leading in towards the keep.
102803: The road passes from east to west here, running between the walls of the keep, narrowing as it goes into the corner to the east. Rotten wooden scaffolding of defensive nature rises several levels, leaning precariously along the northern wall. The blackened cobblestones with puddles of dark foetid water look particularly malignant.
102804: An overhanging corner of the guard keep depresses this corner of the keep, where the road narrows as it goes into a bend, and re-emerges, widening on its way to the gate of the citadel proper. Piles of bones in the bend conceal the foetid puddles that make this place reek far and high.
102805: Vaulting impossibly high, while bending inwards ever so slightly, the inner wall of the castle of Angmar rises to the east. The uneven surface of the citadel defensive circle belies its true nature: the carved cliff surface on the western side of a mighty mountain, a sister-rock of Gundabad. The road runs south here, toward a set of gates that lead into the fortress.
102806: Looming high above the courtyard, the inky-black wall of the keep looks down on a small crossing. The murky road opens south into a dimly lit square while allowing escape from the keep through an arched passage to the north. East, a narrow but heavy door is set in the monolithic wall like an afterthought. Across from it a darkened archway looms. Bloody stains cover the walls all around from its foot to about the height of an ordinary human. Many a prisoner has been used here for target practice by the keep's garrison.
102807: Five tall birch stakes smoulder in the middle of the plaza. Lying in heaps around them are copious amounts of burning firewood and bones. Skeletons chained to the poles are not entirely fleshless yet, and the stench rising from them is overwhelming. The silhouette of the guard keep is sketched in the smoky twilights along the edges of the square. A blood-red picture of a crown appears above the archway leading south, and north seems to be the sole way out of the keep.
102808: The wooden walls of this house have rotten through in places revealing that the whole structure is propped precariously between several rather impressive stone walls. The western wall is missing entirely, the view opening out into a square of burning stakes. The flat ceiling still holds its own. Several heavy-duty metal hooks are screwed into it at regular intervals. The dirt floor has been so heavily trampled down over the years, that nothing leaves tracks anymore on it. One has to be careful to not tumble into the large round hole dominating the centre of the floor.
