In the corner near the stove hams are hanging on iron hooks, which in turn hang from the straw-thatched roof. The floor is covered with baked red tiles, except for the cellar door. Some furniture, obviously old, is placed in the house.
104628:
A rather heavy clay jar stands here.
A rather heavy clay jar stands here.
Some curdled goats milk sits inside a cheese mould.
A wooden chest stands in the corner.

Built underneath one of the buildings from the farm, this basement seems to serve as some kind of storage facility. Wooden planks, filled with jars, have been attached to the stone walls. Some of the jars have yellowish labels on them describing their contents. The floor is mostly unoccupied except for a large wooden chest in the far corner. A hatch with a ladder leads to the house above.
104629:
A long water trough made of wood stands here.
A pitchfork has been carelessly left lying here.
A gardening tool that looks like a sickle lies here.
A white-painted bench is here.
On the bench, there are a hammer and a metal file.
A young farm-hand is here hard at work.

This large wooden barn is sectioned into several compartments by low wooden walls. The back compartments are filled with piles of rye. Those more to the front contain baskets with vegetables like carrots and cabbage, while the front one, left of the entrance is equipped with a crib and a trough filled with water. Right of the entrance a wooden bench with various tools, like sickle and pitchfork, hanging next to it, marks the workroom of the local farmer.
104630:
A large thorny branched shrub is growing here.
On the shrub, there are a number of blackberries.

The soft ground is covered by green plants and tall grasses. A row of huge logs covered with mosses separates the fields from the path in the south. Dark bushes, covered with small black berries grow at the eastern edge of the fields, while some of the plants in the middle of the field seem to hide some sort of vegetable under it. To the east the fields come to an abrupt ending at a very deep and quite wide crevice.
104631:
A green frog is here, hopping around.
A green frog is here, hopping around.

The surrounding area seems to be quite flat, allowing a broad view. A beaten path ending at a steep slope leading down is surrounded by small plants and grey stones. There are a few bushes to the north and south,impeding travel somewhat in these directions. To the west three ropes forming a very simple bridge span a deep crevice.
104632: A worm is here slithering around.

These grasslands south of an overgrown trail are rich with flowers and insects. Small holes, not larger in diameter than the size of worm, with tiny piles of black earth beside them, suggest recent underground activity in the fertile soil. To the south, the bare soil appears even darker than usual, while to the west the ground simply vanishes.
104633: The earth rises here with a few barely noticeable hills. At a secluded part the soil is suspiciously black and rich with compost. Its lack of crop or any other sort of plant indicate something must have been harvested here in the recent past. Jutting from the earth at the centre of the grasslands stands a boulder reaching about three feet tall. In the lee of the stone to the south, a makeshift shelter has been constructed. Some black corn cobs lie spread around a recently burned-out camp fire.
104634: The ground here seems lower than the surrounding areas. Assorted grasses create little patches of green here and there. Small clusters of purple and white wild flowers dot the ground and provide a sweet scent to the air. To the east, a dark patch of bare soil scars the grasslands, while to the north a deep crevice blocks the way.
104635: Soft, rolling fields of tall grass dominate most of this area. Very little can be heard except the cooing of a few doves in the distance. The fragile grass provides the wind a blank canvas, painting its every movement across the golden fields. To the north a deep crevice blocks the way.
104636:
A low shrub with bright green, oblong leaves is growing here.
Scattered in and on the shrub, there are a handful of blueberries.
A huge, black wolf is here, ready to devour.
A black wolf pads restlessly, looking for its next prey.
A black wolf pads restlessly, looking for its next prey.

Dominating the surroundings are what looks like the charred remains of a dense, brush-filled flatland. An apparent brush fire must have swept through the area recently, undoubtedly killing the plants and small animals alike. A number of blackened stumps rise a few feet into the air with no hope of ever bearing new growth again. Gusts of wind have blown ash through the air and most lies towards a narrow crevice in the north.
104637:
A huge, black wolf is here, ready to devour.
A black wolf pads restlessly, looking for its next prey.

The uneven grassland is filled with small cracks and crevices, as if something violent tried to reshape the landscape. In some of the moist cracks, wild orchids can be seen within the green surroundings. To the east the grassland ends at a rock slide, leading down into a crevice that is dozens of yards wide and quite many feet deep.
104638: A small ruin constructed of rough grey stones stands between the fig and vines. The walls are overgrown with ivy and other plants, suggesting that it has been in disrepair for a long long time already. Some old rotten planks fill an opening which once used to be the entrance. Behind these boards, dense bushes fill the the whole interior. Around the shack, rough fields continue in all directions.
104639: A tiny spider is here, eating a tiny bug.

The meadow here has been completely enveloped in a rich, green blanket of low-lying fig. The vines seem healthy and vast, stretching for miles to the north and south. Moisture seems to stay trapped under the dense leaves, keeping the ground below soft and cool; an ideal environment for bugs and spiders. An old set of wooden fence posts have almost succumbed to the vines, with just their tips appearing above the thick foliage.
104640: The ground here seems especially soft, but it is unclear if that is due to the thick foliage or soft ground below the fallen leaves. The slightly rolling hills are almost completely consumed by a low-lying creeping fig. A slight stench rises from the ground, indicating the recent death of something small hidden beneath the leaves. Close to the west stands a petrified tree, grasping at the sky with its claw-like branches.
104641: The surrounding plots of lands appear to have been lush and green in the past, but now only bald stems and trunks, filled with small holes from termites, are left from that era. The former spring is covered with a hard crust of mud in which here and there a skeleton of a fish or small animal has been trapped. The mud spreads a malodorous smell over the surrounding plains.
104642: Plains at the Edge of a Ravine

The earth here is covered with various knee-deep grasses and an occasional broom bush with slender green stems and very small leaves. From the dead leaves beneath these bushes the noise of small animals, like hedgehogs or mice, nosing around for worms can be heard. To the northwest the plains raise slightly before coming to an abrupt end at a deep ravine, while to the south the plains dip slightly.
104643: A hungry warg (ulo) is standing here.

The path, leading to an old hut in the west, is marked with granite stones, which are mostly hidden under huge piles of leaves. The raised northern and southern edges of the path shelter it from strong winds. To the east it ends at the edge of a crevice. However, a flimsy bridge constructed out of three ropes spans the crevice, enabling travel to the other side.
104644: Broken-up farmland stretches in all directions. The dark and nutrient-rich soil shows itself through the occasional break in the rye patches. Riding uniformly along the western edge of the fields stand dozens of old fence posts. They may once have prevented unwanted wildlife to this area, but now decomposition has robbed them of their rails. To the east a deep crevice blocks passage to the plains beyond it.
104645: Stretching all around are abandoned fields with here and there a small patch of rye. Though it looks as if it could have been productive land, all that remains are a few rusty, corroded tools and an old steel plough half buried in the ground. To the east, on the other side of the crevice, some cultivated fields are visible.
104646:
A goat is here, grazing in the hills.
*Enzetee the Black Numenorean*, wielding an ashen blade, is here, riding a trained horse.
A shadowy and lithe orc stands here, half-hidden in the darkness.
A shadowy and lithe orc stands here, half-hidden in the darkness.

The ground slants slightly to the northeast before ending at a deep ravine. The once groomed fiels are now overgrown by wild weeds and other brush. A large part of this vegetation has dried, which indicates the water that can be heard dripping inside the ravine is not available for plants on the surface. At some miles distance in the west a small open spot in the landscape can be spotted.
104647: The bottom of the crevice consists of sharp loose rocks, making walking difficult. An occasional tussock of grass grows in the dust between these rocks. Almost vertical walls of solid rock rise north and south from the bottom of this crevice. To the west the floor rises steadily towards the ground level of the surrounding fields, to the east however, the floor lies many feet lower.
104648: A rock lizard is here, motionless as it observes you.

Ferns, perfectly adapted to the shade, grow in small hollows in the claystone. Between the sharp rocks small lizards crawl around looking for food. The overhanging walls reflect the sounds of birds protecting their nests, which are constructed on isolated ledges in the eastern wall.
104649:
A cluster of dark green, feathery fronds flourishes in the shade.
A small brown snake is slithering around here.

The crevice floor is covered with dark soil washed down from the steep slopes. Various plants grow in the shade; bugleweed with green leaves with purple highlights and purple flowers dot the middle part, while small ferns with light green leaves cover the regions close to the overhanging walls.
104650: The crevice which splits the surrounding lands into two stretches from the northwest to the southeast. The floor is covered with sharp pieces of quartzite and other rocks. The northern wall has weathered unevenly, forming many small ledges on which birds have built their nests.
104651: The bottom of the crevice is littered with small pieces of slate which are covered with imprints of fern leaves. Streams of water drip from the eastern rock face forming a small stream which disappears to the south beneath the loose rocks.
104652:
A cluster of dark green, feathery fronds flourishes in the shade.
A swallow flies high above the ground.

The floor of the crevice is covered with loose rocks originating from the eastern side. This eastern rock face has partly collapsed forming a huge rock slide of sharp edged rocks which enables travelling in and out of the crevice by a skilled climber. The occasional fern grows near the eastern wall which consists of layers of slate on top of solid granite. The crevice stretches for miles in the northward and southward directions.
104653:
A large pile of boulders is sitting here, probably debris from a rockslide.
A cluster of dark green, feathery fronds flourishes in the shade.
A large brown snake with black patches is coiled here (red aura).

The crevice is bordered by overhanging rock walls to the west and east. The bottom is covered with some huge boulders between which ferns and other shade loving plants have found a habitat. A dried out hide of a snake is stuck on one of the sharp edges of the boulders. To the south the crevice looks greener as if water has found its way there.
104654:
A cluster of dark green, feathery fronds flourishes in the shade.
A pool of darkish water has formed in a depression of the stone.
Clusters of slender stems and tall leaves thrive in the mud and shallows.
An albino salamander is here, perched on some rocks.
An albino salamander is here, perched on some rocks.
A swarm of midges is here, humming around you.

The bottom of the crevice is partly hidden beneath a pool of murky water with reeds and ferns growing on its banks. Some beetles and salamanders and some bubbles which emit a faint sulphurous smell disturb the surface. High above the pool three ropes, forming a bridge, span the crevice from east to west.
104655: A rock lizard is here, motionless as it observes you.

The bottom of the crevice is shaded by the overhanging walls. The bedrock is covered with a thin layer of sand coming from the sediment layers in the rock faces, and loose rocks with sharp edges broken from the lower granite layers. The yellow sand consists of thousands and thousands of tiny fossil skeletons of primitive creatures. Northwards the crevice grows deeper.
104656: Various bones of large animals lie scattered between the numerous sharp rocks that cover the solid bedrock.. The hollows between those rocks have been filled with dirt originating from the grasslands around. Pioneer species like greater plantain and common horsetail add some green to the otherwise grey landscape. To the west a rock slide filling the crevice makes it possible scramble up to the grasslands.
104661: A great male deer with reddish hair and twisted antlers stands here proudly.

A weather-beaten trail running north to south can still be clearly seen, nevertheless time-worn and faded tracks are evidence of little, if any, recent traffic. To the north, in the distance, a small farm can be distinguished. To the west some field, the uses of which cannot be determined from this distance, fill the horizon.
104662: A great male deer with reddish hair and twisted antlers stands here proudly.

As the curvy trail continues from north to west, one can see a little path, probably made by animals leading southwards. The trail, originally covered with some small pieced gravel, is now mostly overgrown by low grasses and weeds. Beside the trail an old log, providing a view of the marshy grasslands to the east, is placed like a bench.
104663:
A green frog is here, hopping around.
A swarm of mosquitoes is here, humming around you.

Luxuriant grasses cover the extent of this tilted grassland. Scattered among the grass small woody shrubs with crimson and yellow flowers grow, filling the air with their scents. In the low southwestern part of this grassland tall cattails, with staminate flowers rising above the leaves, grow between the grass hinting at a soggy underground.
104664:
A small campfire burns here, its low flames giving off only a little light.
Clusters of slender stems and tall leaves thrive in the mud and shallows.
A heron is stalking the area, looking for fish.
A green frog is here, hopping around.

Man made ditches, filled with a few feet of water, cut through the wetlands, dividing it into long stretches of floating mats of vegetation. On one of these mats a small shelter, with a view across a small lake, has been constructed out of rough wooden poles and braided twigs. Near the trail to the northwest some small piles of dark brown peat have been placed, ready for transportation.
104665:
A sprawling, twisted tree grows here.
On the tree, there are a few hawthorn berries.
Prickly, white-stemmed plants, with blue flower heads grow in abundance.
A dove is standing here.
A dove is standing here.

Some bushes and small trees grow here. Among these a few patches of thistles and some scattered ground-level thrive. Around the flourishing bushes a number of small birds fly around, picking up the occasional insect hiding between the leaves. The ground gradually slopes down toward a small pond to the south. Some winding animal tracks head in that direction.
104666:
A placid pond is here, inviting you to take a refreshing drink.
A fat carp swims here.
A fat carp swims here.

Over time a small depression has developed in these grasslands. Rainwater from the surrounding fields drains to there forming a large, tranquil pond. This pond has a distinctive green colour from algae that exists among the water- lilies growing along the shoreline. Despite being surrounded by reeds a small small path leading to the waterfront, can be distinguished.
104667: The fields here are overgrown with thistles, shrubs and bushes. Standing in the middle of the fields, the weather-beaten remains of an old building can be seen. An old, fading trail leads from the village remains to the east, across the fields and down the gentle westward slope to a small pond.
104668: An open plain stretches from east to west, bordered in the north by some lone birch trees in a soggy loam. The plain provides little in the form of shelter from the elements or predators. Nevertheless, faint trails of animal tracks, most likely deer, criss-cross through the open landscape.
104669: A pack horse (Rood) is standing here, ridden by you.

Soot covered walls are all that remains of this small village. Once a place for farmers from the surrounding areas to gather, it seems to have been abandoned for many years now. Weeds and bracken have spread past the gardens surrounding the derelict buildings, adding to the sombreness of the location. A few small animals scurry among the debris, seeking cover from some unseen threat.
104670: Thick bushes grow among the grasses in this stretch of the plains. Some twisted animal paths can be clearly distinguished, interweaving among the tightly packed bushes. The ground slopes downwards slightly to the north leading to a soggy area. Scattered among the bushes a few slender plants with bluish petals grow. Small animals scurry about, alert to the slightest sign of a predator. Some buildings have been erected in the distance to the south.
104671: Lush, green grass now covers the abandoned fields that lie next to the village in the west. The earth rises slightly to the south, elevating as it turns into vast grasslands. To the northeast, hills rise above the plains providing the most salient landmark in the terrain, as well as a vantage point over these extensive plains.
104672: A boar cub is playing here, and exploring the wide world.

The battered fencing that surrounds these fields is the clearest evidence that whoever claimed ownership of them has long ago given up. Thistles, scattered shrubs and bushes grow sparsely in the area covering up any other evidence of farming activity. To the east a tall hill rises above the plains while to the southwest the remains of a small village dot the horizon.
104673: This lush valley has a rich vegetation dotted with many different coloured flowers. This provides an environment that is favoured not only by large grazing mammals but also by small rodents and insects. A few scattered bones suggest that predators also find an occasional meal in this location.
104674: A small boar with big yellow tusks looks eager to fight.

Navigating these hills requires not much climbing. Sparsely distributed along the hillside oak, ash and birch trees grow and among these several shrubs and bushes. To the east the ground rises, while the northern and southern slopes lead to small valleys in the plains. Among the bushes a worn trail indicates significant transit of some large animals into a small creek among the hills.
104675:
A small boar with big yellow tusks looks eager to fight.
A magpie is flying around looking for some food.

These fertile plains show a increased number of birch and oak trees as the terrain slowly rises towards the south into the hills. In addition to the trees a few small bushes and shrubs provide food and shelter to a variety of small birds and mammals. To the east the terrain slowly rises to the sky before ending abruptly at a steeply declining rock face, preventing travel in that direction.
104676: The grasses, richly coloured with flowers, grow abundantly in these fields, providing a perfect habitat for insects and herbivores like deer and wild sheep. Some stones, covered with moss, stick out between the grasses covering this field. Just above this moss, small capsules carrying spores weave in the wind. To the west the grassland drops significantly showing some small pools.
104677:
A small boar with big yellow tusks looks eager to fight.
A boar cub is playing here, and exploring the wide world.
A fierce boar is here, making grunting noises.

Lush grasses cover these fertile fields which stretch north, east and south. These grasses are filled with insect life that provides ample sustenance to the birds that fly overhead. Several trees and shrubs grow, scattered across the landscape, providing roosts for these birds and hiding places for other small animals. To the southeast a hill rises, towering over the plains.
104678:
A large, loyal falcon is circling above.
A boar cub is playing here, and exploring the wide world.

Lush grasses cover these fertile fields and those that stretch west and north. While the thriving insect life provides ample sustenance to small birds and mammals, the sparse bushes and shrubs provide little protection from predators and inclement weather. Southwards a lightly wooded plain leads to some rising hills.
104679:
Clusters of slender stems and tall leaves thrive in the mud and shallows.
A water moccasin slithers out of sight just below the surface of the water.

The grassland in the east is replaced by wetlands with small pools whose banks are covered by spike-rush, with tiny flowers at the top, and long reeds. The wetland itself consists mostly of thick floating mats of slender sedge characterized by bare stems with very long, very thin leaves. On the thicker parts of this floating surface some orchids dye the landscape purple.
104680:
A low shrub with bright green, oblong leaves is growing here.
Scattered in and on the shrub, there are two piles of blueberries.

The soggy nature of these wetlands makes it hard to keep balance. The surface, consisting of mosses, has a healthy light green look, apart from the places where the water level has risen above the vegetation. At the places where the ground is more solid thick patches of grass and some solitary birch and willow trees grow. To the west, at higher grounds, a trail can be spotted.
104681: The Old Forest Road runs through a vast, grassy plain. The broad and well-built road must have been actively used in the past, but is nowadays partly overgrown with the wilderness, making the road look somewhat decayed and almost abandoned. At the outer edge of the road, a steady row of low bushes follow it with an occasional tree growing here and there among the bushes.
104682: The surface of the low grassland is mainly coloured in different shades of light brown, but green and yellow are also well represented. Half buried in the dry grass, an animal skeleton is visible. A row of old fence poles sticks in a straight row between the road and the plain. Farther away at the plain, there are a few isolated clumps of yew trees with lowgreen bushes growing around them.
104683: A thin, hairy plant, with small, oval leaves, grows here.

The grass grows in abundance in this field. The vast plain is filled with grasses and various kinds of flowers. Around them, bees and other insects hover in search of nectar. The rich vegetation makes these fields a pleasant habitat for herbivores as well; fresh deer and rabbit tracks wander aimlessly throughout the area. South of this sea of life, an old road can be spotted.
104684: The wide grassland is covered with high grasses and lush, dense bushes. The ground looks quite tangled and messy due to all the wild vegetation. At some areas, several acres are covered by dark green bushes, while elsewhere it is fully covered by plants with hollow stems and parallel-veined leaves. Throughout the plains a few small tree saplings grow.
104685: A long time ago, large trees, most notably oaks and beeches, dwelt here. Now only large stumps spanning more than five feet high remain. Ferns and mosses grow between the roots of the trunks, among the occasional holes made by small animals, that can be spotted on the ground. The gaps between the stumps are inhabited by young willow trees and bramble bushes.
104686: The Old Forest Road bends around a small rise to the north-east. A few old cart tracks imprinted in the dry mud form the surface of the road. At the southern boundary of the road, rocks and stones of all sizes have carefully been aligned with each other to prevent the erosion of the road in the case of heavy rains. Thin grass tufts grow from the cracks of the stones.
104687: This clear stretch of the Old Forest Road runs directly from the east to the west. The sparse vegetation close to the road, in combination with the thick bushes further away show that the road has been wider in the past. To the north flat plains can be seen, whilst to the south a thick thorny hedge planted on top of a low dike blocks all passage.
104688: The Old Forest Road runs from the east to the west. In most places, the surface of the road is hard and dusty. In the middle of the road, faint traces of cartwheels can be spotted among the other bumps and holes of the road, while at the edges, grasses and clovers are in the process of retaking the road. On the south side of the road, a low dike covered with bushes blocks the view.
104689: The sandy, light brown road makes a long, steady curve, as it winds from the west to the south. The road is several yards in width, allowing even two wagons to easily pass each other. There are low, grassy trenches on either side of the road. Behind those, the ground elevates quickly a few yards, giving the impression of travelling in a dry riverbed. Thick trees grow on the eastern side of the road, making both the travel and visibility very limited.
104690: These fields have clearly been used for farming in the past, but since then they have become quite feral. The ground, partly covered with young bushes and high grass, is uneven. Several long rows of bumpy furrows are still visible within the undergrowth. To the north, the fields are bordering the Old Forest Road. Apart from that, the flat fields continue on in all directions.
104691:
A brown cow is here, contemplating a higher reality whilst chewing slowly.
A cow stands here, chewing her cud.
A brown cow is here, contemplating a higher reality whilst chewing slowly.
A restless rabbit bounces around.

The field is covered with different types of vegetation. A short yellowish grass, with several shades of brown and green, fills the ground. Low bushes and occasional flower clumps grow here and there. Few beech trees stand above the other foliage, giving some protection from the sun. Open plains seem to continue in every direction, although to the south the ground begins to slope.
104692: A thin layer of soil covers the barren, rocky ground. While some spots are totally bare, other places are covered by grass and dark green bushes. Here and there are nasty, rough rocks sticking up from the ground, making travelling quite slow and unpleasant with their sharp edges. Underneath the sparse bushes, tracks of small animals criss-cross the soil before disappearing into the small holes between the rocks.
104693: A magpie is flying around looking for some food.

Half of the plain is completely covered by bushes and dense vegetation, whereas the other part has been charcoaled by a devastating fire. Shrubs and bushes to the east have been eradicated entirely, and only a few large rocks and stones stick up from the burnt ground. An extremely steep slope leads to a bare valley to the south. There are no visible paths around, which makes the movement difficult. Behind the valley, magnificent hills can be seen.
104694: Short, yellow-green grass grows on the bottom of the valley with several rocks and spiny bushes covering the ground. Steep valley walls rise abruptly, and cliffs on the northern wall are especially filled with loose rocks and boulders which make it too dangerous to proceed in that direction. A narrow but flat valley floor slithers among the rocks and continues in every direction but north. A majestic hill stands proudly in the south.
104695: This small, steep valley lies between the high hills and vast plains. The ground is rocky and quite barren, offering easy access in all directions but the north, where the valley wall is too dangerous to travel in. A fire recently spread through the northern plains, carried by a wind and dumping ash, covering parts of the valley with death-like greyness.
104696:
A nest is here.
A large hawk-like bird is here overlooking its territory.

The top plateau of the Great Hill is small, rocky, and contains a very limited amount of low bushes and stunted grass. The wind has no obstacles here, and it occasionally blows hard, making the sparse vegetation of plateau to bend. The plateau offers a truly magnificent view of the surrounding areas. Looking around, slopes and valleys encircle the hills from all sides. Looking beyond those, vast plains continue in all directions as far as one can see.
104697: This deep valley lies peacefully beneath an enormous hillside, beckoning the travellers to settle down upon it. The towering hill completely blocks the view northwards. The inclined, rocky wall makes a perfect home for a great number of birds, and some of them can be seen circling the sky. A tiny path runs through the elevating plains to the east and west, peacefully winding in the shadows cast by the high hills.
104698:
A large, loyal falcon is circling above.
A large hawk-like bird is here overlooking its territory.

The sloping ground inclines gradually throughout the whole area. The surface of the ground is rather grim: dark, grey stones are scattered around the slope, and the short, stunted grass does not offer much comfort to passing travellers. No trees are visible on the slope, as a narrow path can be seen descending from the northern hills towards the more fertile lands to the west. To the east, the ground is too steep and rocky for travelling.
104699: A large hawk-like bird is here overlooking its territory.

High on the hills, an old path slithers through the rough terrain, descending dangerously towards a slope in the north. There are rocks, stones, and boulders on both sides of the path, which limit the view from here. There are some old tracks on the path and the blackened remains of a few abandoned campfires.
104700: The slope is growing with thick, but relatively short, green grass. The incline starts from a broad valley a few miles to the north, and then elevates steadily throughout the whole region, towards the steep slope of an enormous hill in the south. To the west, the ground descends abruptly into a rocky valley, allowing no access. A small path winds down from the hill, turning around some grey boulders, and leading to a junction which is visible from the east.
104701: A large, loyal falcon is circling above.

A rocky valley is resting at the foot of a majestic hill. The steep edges of the valley rise upwards towards the sky as the end of the valley gets closer. The valley ends at a round clearing, which is surrounded by a sheer rock face from all directions. Brown rocks form an impassable hillside, covered with small pits and black narrow hollows. Far above, few bushy trees have managed to grow on the vertical surface.
104702:
An apple tree with bright green leaves grows here.
On the tree's branches are three apples.
Some small rocks have been piled into a mound here.

Grey rocks and withered bushes are scattered over this rather flat plain. The western side of the plain has a slightly higher elevation, where the terrain is slowly rising towards some high hills that are visible to the southwest. Several paths meet each other here, forming a small junction. A huge rock rests solidly in the middle of it, with three arrows carved upon it. There are no signs of life anywhere, except for a few old fireplaces along the path left by travellers.
104703: This flat plain is covered entirely with tall, dense grasses, which sway back and forth as a cold breeze passes by. There is a small path slithering through the thick, rolling fields. The landscape is dominated by high hills, which can be spotted not far to the west. The open plain continues in all directions, with the exception of the west, where a steep incline, filled with boulders, prevents any further travel.
104704: The barren, flat plain is covered with tangled, yellowish grass tussocks. Large areas are entirely dry, where grass is coloured almost orange. Only a few trees are visible on the whole plain, and every single one of them looks grey, dry, and dead. A huge hill is visible to the northwest, but a steep ridge blocks the direct route there, forcing travellers to use a detour.
104705: The feral plain opens up in all directions. The ground winds up and down, forming small mounds. The surface of the plain is covered by messy, bright green bushes, and light grey, nearly white, stones, which are strangely grouped together into small piles. Some high hills can be spotted to the west, whereas the plain seems to end further to the east where it gets progressively rocky.
104706:
A man's-waist high evergreen shrub grows here, with bright green branches.
On the shrub, there are several splayed leaves.

A foot long, brown-green grass covers the plain, forming a slowly winding sea around the clumps of thick bushes that grow in great numbers around the area. The eastern part of the plain holds vegetation so dense, that it is impossible to go any further in that direction. A large number of small stones forms the remains of a rarely used path through the field, which cuts the sea of grass into separate areas.
104707: A grey bird with a bright orange-red belly sits here, singing a melodic tune.

Dense foliage and a thick growth of low shrubs covers the plain, forming a wild mixture of both deciduous and evergreen plants. The vegetation opens up just enough for a wagon-wide path to clear through the field. The western parts of the plain are more rocky, and a steep valley prevents those who pull themselves through the bushes to pass by any further.
104708: A fire has burned down most of the vegetation, only grey ash and charred, black branches remain. A path leads through the fields, it is not very wide, and at some regions it is hard to find under the windswept shrubs and ash. The land to the north has been untouched by the fire, and has the look of cultivated farmland. The eastern terrain is filled with sharp rocks and charred bushes, making it impossible to travel there.
104709: The plain has been completely consumed by a raging fire. As the flames died out, they left behind a few charred bushes, sooty stones, and a large amount of dark grey ash. The landscape is otherwise flat, except for to the south where the charcoaled plain transforms into a steep, dangerous-looking slope which descends abruptly into the rocky valley below.
104710: The grass grows sumptuously on the field, which contains the old remains of beets, carrots, and potatoes. The field is divided by an ancient, weathered fence made up of old, grey poles and rotten planks. The majority of the planks have come lose from the poles, and now lie rotting under the grass. A few old reinforced mangers, made of thick oaken beams, are still standing on the fields.
104711:
A carrot is lying here.
A carrot is lying here.
Farmer Ocher stands here, seemingly worried.

Several square-shaped open areas have been cleared on the otherwise bushy plains. Squares look cultivated, and are growing vegetables and other plants. Regularly used grassy paths surround the fields. At the lower places a faint smell of excrement, possibly manure, comes from the ground. At the end of the fields are piles of leaves and rotten vegetables. A long, trimmed hedge surrounds a small farm area located to the east.
104712: This field is covered with beets. They have green leaves with red veins, and in many cases the top part of the red root has been transformed to a slight green by the light of the sun. At the northern end of the field, a broad dike covered with dense bushes protects the fields from cold winds and from the unwanted trespassers travelling the Old Forest Road.
104713:
There is a huge, pyramidal beehive here.
A bee flies around here, collecting nectar from the flowers.
A bee flies around here, collecting nectar from the flowers.

A small, dusty path, covered with old footprints, courses between the fields. The western field has been retaken by high grasses, bushes, and other plantlife. Here and there, a pole from a former fence is visible in the middle of this feral wilderness. A small ditch separates the eastern wheat fields from the path. A wide track of fallen wheat is visible on the field, it looks as if some big animal has wandered through the crop.
104714: A circular stone well has been built here.

A narrow trail separates from the dusty path, leading into the front yard of a farmhouse made of thick, wooden planks. The outside of this house was once painted in bright red and orange, but due to the sun's bleaching, the colours have faded into a shade of light brown, with the exception of right below the roof where the original splendour is still visible. A long, thick hedge circulates the fields behind the house.
104715:
A large potato is growing here.
A large potato is growing here.

A major part of this farmed soil has been planted with potatoes, which are growing well with green leaves and white flowers. Everywhere else, rotten potatoes can be seen breaking out of the soil, ravaged by critters. A tall dike, topped by several thick bushes, blocks the passage to the north and east. A small natural passage has formed through the wall to the north, due to erosion.
104716: The Old Forest Road is covered with dirt and short grass. It curves around a small hill located north-east of the road. The hill is mainly covered with low bushes and a few solitary tree that rise into the sky. On the west side of the road, the passage is blocked by a long dike covered with bramble bushes. In the south, a dirt path lined with trees leads to some buildings.
104717: The brown plain is covered with bushes. A small path runs through the terrain, almost completely hidden by all the thorns, leaves, and branches. At the southern end of the plain, a path travels through a minor dip. Dense bushes are blocking the way to the east and south, and the bushy plains continue onwards to the northwest.
104718: Thick thorn bushes surround a small, windy path that is partially visible from all the dead branches that cover it. Something seems to be rustling among the surrounding thorns, making the vegetation move. The northern and western parts of the field are completely covered with sharp thorns, allowing travellers to only move to the east and south.
104719: The scrubland is a tangled mess of feral bushes and small trees, which have grown together with long, dry weeds. Parts of the shrubbery have formed thickets so dense that the slithering old path heading south has become half-buried under the vegetation. Thorny shrubs seem to continue on all directions, making navigation through these plains restricted.
104720: A cockroach is scuttling across the floor carrying some debris.

With no other way out of the deep vegetation than to the north, the path ends at a stony clearing within the shrubbery. The dense thicket encircling the path makes it impossible to penetrate through, or view beyond, towards the surrounding area. This seems like a good place for travellers to settle down for the night, as it provides shelter against the strong wind that often crosses these plains. Several deep tracks can be seen in the grass, maybe left by mounts and wagons of other travellers.
104721: Shrivelled grasses, bushes, and small plants are located all over this flat plain. The terrain has been under drought, keeping the plants stunted. A few noises that can be heard are coming from the small insects that fly by. The rocky ground to the north and west hinders travel there, while the plain stretches out elsewhere seemingly endless.
104722: This infertile and desolate plain extends a great distance eastwards, allowing the wind to blow harshly through the area. Stones of various sizes and types lie on the ground, especially to the north, where the plain seems impenetrable due to the sharp rocks and stones. The plains are riddled with cracks among the short grass, where the mud has hardened and split due exposure from the elements.
104723:
The corpse of a huge warg is lying here.
The corpse of a ferocious warg is lying here.
Hentario, wielding a yew longbow, is standing here.
A sturdy trained horse is standing here.

Dry, yellow-brown grass covers the central parts of this wide plain. The sea of short straws is bent and cracked from the occasional gusts of wind that has blown across this shrivelled landscape. Brush and thick bushes border the windswept plain to the south and west, blocking the passage effectively, while the plains extend in all other directions.
104724: The grassland peters out in this gaunt, windswept landscape. Everything is very dry, and there are a few large blackened areas, where all the grass and other undergrowth have totally been burnt away. A few bare trees are still standing on the field, their trunks twisted and blackened, and their leaves having shrivelled and fallen off. This bleak barrenness continues to the north and west.
104725: This bleak plain is barren, containing only some modest vegetation, as even the most adaptable flora has difficult time trying to gain a foothold in this dry terrain. Some sandy brown and light green coloured, dried bushes still exist, growing among the stunted grass tufts. The soil is withered as far as the eye can see, and cracked in several locations.
104726: A small cluster of clover grows here.

This extensive tract of uncultivated open land is covered with herbage and low shrubs, like raspberries, brambles and spiky bushes, which form occasional bright green spots in the otherwise somewhat insipid undergrowth. The terrain looks modest, and harmless. Several foot-high fertile grasses surround this peaceful plain. To the east, the grasses grows gradually longer, and have a browner hue.
104728: A fierce wolverine is here, snarling at you (hidden).

This is a large, rocky area composed of narrow passes between steep rock faces; coarse cliffs filled with dense briar thickets; and rounded boulders exposed by erosion. Some of the rocks are half-buried in the ocher clay; some of them are laying upon each other in dangerous looking, unbalanced manner. There are deep burrows among the rocks, making it perilous to proceed further between the boulders. The only easy way out is the green plain that is visible to the east.
104729: A giant slug is here, oozing around.

This rugged cavern has been formed by nature ages ago. The pathway makes a confusing and narrow route between the dull edged stalagmites which protrude from the rocky and uneven floor. The sheer rock walls of this crude cavern are slimy and moist, and some pearls of water are visible on the stalagmites as well. The cold, damp air hangs still.
104730:
A woolly sheep is grazing here.
A colourful butterfly is fluttering around here.
A swallow flies high above the ground.

Vegetation in the area is primarily low bush and scrub. The land is mostly without trees; instead a lot of tall, yellow grass grow here. Amongst it, occasional patches of foot-high green grass make the landscape look vivid and colourful. No clear path exists in any direction; on the other hand, the terrain is so easy that pasturing animals can just wander wherever they want.
104731: Various vigorous, shrubby plants dominate this area, blooming in rich shades of yellow, orange, red, and crimson. Around them, large blue and deep purple flowers make vivid colour patches that stand out from the mottled undergrowth, which is painted in uncountable slight variations of green, brown, and even grey.
104732: A mass of dark green leaves clings to a wall.

The terrain is a verdant grasslands, with a few scattered clumps of trees and bushes growing here and there. Rising from the lush grass, a long, rocky escarpment dominates the area to the east, creating an impassable stony wall in the otherwise featureless terrain. A few boulders are planted at the foot of the rock wall, which looks so worn that the new boulders may fall down at any moment.
104733: A grassy, green path runs through the winding fields, connecting the Old Forest Road from the north to a small farm located in the west. A neat line of beech and ash trees has been planted on both sides of the path at regular intervals. The slender and delicate trees are about four or five feet tall.
104734: The road is covered with loose sand, with an occasional small tussock here and there. It is hard to distinguish the boundary between the road and the surrounding plains, because the grass gradually increases in height and in density. The northern edge of the road is interrupted by a small path running north towards a hut. To the east, the border of the forest consisting of huge trees can be seen.
104735: Small Path by the Forest Border

An erect shrub with green pinnate leaves is growing here.
Inside the shrub, there are two piles of crimson raspberries.

A low roofed hut stands at the forest border. There is a modest yard around the house, surrounded by a rough, bright yellow plank fence. Huge piles of wood have been placed between the nearest trunks of the forest. A thicket of dense branched trees and messy underbrush starts behind the fence. A small path starts from the garden gate and forks, where the path to the south joins the Old Forest Road opposite the eastern path leads into a dark forest.
104736: The walls and the floor of this small hut have been constructed of thick wooden beams, while the roof is roughly built of planks and bricks. There is a small window next to the entrance, giving a view to the garden outside. Axes, saws and wedges hang from nails on the wall, along with some worn working clothes. Close to the back wall, a cupboard divides the hut in such a way that a confined space containing a bed has been created to the far end of the room.
104737:
A patch of orange mushrooms springs from the ground here.
A patch of orange mushrooms springs from the ground here.

A worn out path leads through the dim forest, winding slowly between the trees and bushes. Someone has been chopping a lot of trees down recently, as stumps, cut branches, and other trash from the fallen trees litter the forest; even a few small clearings have been formed next to the path. Outside the cleared parts the tall, shady trees are covered with hanging vines and other entangled vegetation. The forest looks dark and dangerous.
104738:
The corpse of a black widow is lying here.
A black snake hurries towards you with sly intentions.

The shady forest is dark and extremely threatening. It is unknown how high the ancient trees reach, as the unbroken net of vines, leaves, and branches form the ceiling a few yards above the ground. Nothing seems to be moving anywhere, even the air is totally still. This place has a strong malignant aura; it is as if the gloomy forest was alive and an ancient evilness was creeping behind every bush and tree.
104739:
A white and brown cow, with a yellow tuft of hair, is mooing here anxiously.
A huge, poisonous spider is here.

Huge, bumpy trees grow here, forming impenetrable clumps in the dense forest. The colour of the trunks varies between green, brown, and black among the occasional fungi that grows upon some trunks. There is quite a lot of miscellaneous ground-level foliage, but not so much that it would block the passage. The uppermost branches tangle together forming an almost impenetrable canopy.
104740: A dense carpet of blue flowers dip their heads in the breeze.

The eastern edge of the forest is filled with young, vital trees, thriving clusters of thorn bushes, and small, open areas within the forest, where the mushrooms and ferns grow. Looking deeper into the woods, the trees are significantly taller and thicker, and the vegetation gets quickly denser. Here and there are closely set copses, where brambles grow around the thick tree formations.
104741: There is a wide, flat clearing occupying the area. It grows hay, low bushes and other undergrowth allowing clear visibility into all directions. The surrounding trees slowly continue their attempts to reclaim the earth, having began their journey many years ago. Someday the looming forest walls on both sides will meet here again, as they did in the ancient times when Mirkwood was still known as Greenwood the Great and the shadow had not fallen on the peaceful forest.
104742:
A sack of flour has been placed here.
A simple wooden chest is here.
A sturdy crate made of nailed wooden planks sits on the floor.
A water barrel has been left here.

The spacious barn looks very clean, as if someone has been taking excellent care of it. All of the supplies and items are in good condition and well- organised. The walls of the barn are made of broad planks and slightly spaced apart to let the fresh air circulate freely from the outside. At one end of the barn there are large doors leading out; and at the other, a small door leading to the living quarters. A huge haystack towers in the corner of the barn, and a small, blue cart stands next to it. The other side of the barn is filled with animal stalls.
104743:
A dirty shovel is lying on the ground here.
A stove stands against one wall here.

The farmhouse has been split into two parts. One part is filled with crates full of carrots, potatoes and other vegetables. Next to them, a neat collection of various gardening tools has been arranged on the back wall. The other part of the house, separated partly by a wall and partly by curtains, contains a stove, with a kettle on it, and other furniture usually found in small homes.
104747: A mottled snake is sneaking here, ready to sink its fangs into flesh.

An overgrown ruin, half buried in the high grass, stands within a bushy thicket. A long time ago, there was a partly wooden barn standing on a firm foundation of stones. Now, the building has collapsed inward into a pile of rotten planks covered with ivy. The lone southern wall still stands upright, being the last sign of the construction. Around the ruins, the landscape has been retaken by bushes too dense to travel through.
104748: A coloured game bird is visible in the vegetation, watching you warily.

Dense vegetation covers the soil, among the faint remains of the low irrigation ditches that mark the presence of former agricultural developments. Near one of these ditches, a small, ruined shelter, the kind that usually was built for livestock, has been built between the bushes. The shelter consists of a few rocks, planks, and poles, and has now been overgrown with nettles and brambles.
104749: The Old Forest Road runs along the tree line, following the curves of the gloomy forest, located on the north side of the road. The surface of the road is rough; sometimes there are medium sized stones; sometimes there are deep ruts in the road. On the border of the forest, large trees and the messy undergrowth have grown so tightly next to each other that it is nearly impossible to enter the forest. On the south side of the road lie vast, feral plains.
104750: The outskirts of the northern forest frame the road. In general, the road is in proper condition, although occasional grass tufts and even small bushes grow here and there on it. Based on the condition of the road, it is evident that only few, if any, travellers frequent the road nowadays. The surrounding terrain is not particularly harsh, and one could travel easily in any direction from here.
104751: A dense carpet of blue flowers dip their heads in the breeze.

The tall trees suddenly part into a forest clearing, where weeds and some small bushes grow. Winding between the trees, a small forest trail meets another path in the clearing where an odd looking stone, covered with green and grey moss, stands at the crossing. The forest opens up to the south, while in other directions it gets denser.
104752: A boar cub is playing here, and exploring the wide world.

The grassy plain is almost like a canyon between the two forest walls, which are standing at the both ends of the open area. Although the dark forest to the west is big and truly majestic, it is still nothing compared to the endless Mirkwood, which extends into unknown distances in the eastern horizon. The Old Forest Road runs to the south.
104753: The forest has suffered a bitter loss here, as if someone has been cutting trees down throughout the area. In the middle of a small opening, an especially enormous tree has fallen and only a gigantic stump remains where it once stood. The stump has a strong, thick bark which is covered with fungi. However, the upper part of the stump is clear, showing hundreds and hundreds of growth rings.
104754: A small cluster of clover grows here.

Low undergrowth fills the plains, allowing excellent visibility in all directions. The only exceptions to this pattern are the lonely bushes and occasional larger rocks that rise upwards from the ground. Here and there, animal tracks run back and forth on the ground. To the north, the Old Forest Road is located between the plains and the forest. In other directions, the lonesome expanse of plains can be seen.
104755:
A hollow tree is growing upright here.
A small grasshopper clings to a blade of grass, ready to spring.

The sloping landscape is covered with brambles and other shrubs. The surrounding area can be seen easily from this high perch in the terrain. To the northeast, a road can be spotted. Further to the east, the border of the dark forest of Mirkwood fills the whole eastern horizon. A tangled mess of stinging bushes spreads out to the west and south. Behind the bushes to the far south, a few high hills are visible in the distance.
104756: The wild scrubland descends slightly, but continuously, from the west to the east. The soil is filled with green shrubbery, although the vegetation does not rise very high, save a few lone trees. Travel through the plain would be easy, and one can continue in any direction.
104757: A placid pond is here, inviting you to take a refreshing drink.

Between the winding slopes lies a small, flat plain with a circular pond in the centre of it. Green, long grass rustle gently around the pool, some of it trampled down by the animals wandering in this area. The ground level of the adjacent areas is slightly higher, forming a natural dell. The bushy scrubland continues in all directions but to the east, where the vegetation changes into thick, wild-looking bushes.
104758: The northern edge of the wide scrubland is covered with a myriad of plants, such as tall grasses and scraggely bushes. The ground is sloping slightly and there is no sign of any kind of organised agriculture. The open scrubland stretches onwards to the south and west, with the exception to the east, where the terrain transfers into a long, abruptly-rising slope filled with thickets.
104759:
A small boar with big yellow tusks looks eager to fight.
A small boar with big yellow tusks looks eager to fight.

The land is uncultivated and covered with sparse stunted undergrowth; the only exceptions are the small clumps of bushy trees that are growing throughout the expanse. Between these scattered copses, the vast, wild scrubland extend in all directions, but to the south, where a huge amount of crude boulders, and dense, almost-tangled foliage blocks further travel.
104760: A boar cub is playing here, and exploring the wide world.

The wide scrubland is very flat and seems to extend many miles in all directions. The ground appears dry, but still quite fertile. Thick, yellow grass surrounds the holly trees, thistles, and other bushes occupying the area. Wild weeds grow in abundance across the terrain mixed with a few small trees. Behind the fields, at the eastern horizon, looms the dark wood of Mirkwood.
104761: Man-high, healthy looking bushes have occupied vast areas of the plain. Each shrub stands alone, having a few yards distance from the other bushes, thus making the travelling on the flat plain easy, but very unpredictable. The soil seems fertile: the grass here is taller than in most surrounding areas, and even some tiny, white flowers grow in small patches among it. The landscape is open in all directions.
104762: The terrain transforms to a peculiar dead end in form of a stony valley filled with several jagged boulders. It encloses the area, preventing access everywhere but to the east. The ground is rocky and shattered; many dips and hollows pierce the earth around the area. In the middle of the valley, a huge, rectangular boulder with sharp edges rests on top of few others, forming a room-like space under it.
104763: The road runs through a desolated landscape. The terrain is rather forested, trees and bushes of various types grow all around the road, especially large black beeches grow here in abundance. North of the road, the wilderness looks impenetrable, whereas the southern region is mainly covered by bushes and is easy to travel. To the east, the mighty Mirkwood is quite close.
104765: A broad zone of bushes spreads between the plains and the great forest of Mirkwood. The bushes are so high and so filled with branches that they do not permit a clear line of sight; resulting in a confusing warren of vegetation where it is easy to get lost. To the west, there is a bush filled slope with so steep an inclination that it is impossible to go there at all.
104766: The corpse of a dreadful snake is lying here.

Diverse green shrubbery has occupied this area, forming a wide section of dense, continuous thicket where bushes are rather tall and wide, rich with branches. The soil is covered with leaves, weeds and other undergrowth. So thick is the vegetation that it is possible to weave one's way through the copse only where the brushwood allows it.
104767: Numerous spike bushes grow on the scrubland, along with a foot high dark green weed. The thick, impenetrable-looking brushwood continues to the north, while to the east the landscape is dominated by outskirts of the Mirkwood. To the south, vegetation turns into grassy plains which seem to extend far into the horizon.
104768: A colourful butterfly is fluttering around here.

Broad, nearly level stretches of land seem to continue in every direction from here. Tufted grasses fill the landscape, colouring it with a rich variety of slightly alternating shades of brown, yellow and green. A few woody plants have taken root among the spiky bushes that get taller to the eastward. Neither trees nor boulders stick out from the general blandness.
104769:
A small cluster of clover grows here.
A sparrow is flapping around on the ground.

These plains are a part of a flat, almost treeless, grassy country. Small bushes and other woody, rough plants, like briars and thistles, grow here. Green is the predominant tone of the foliage of these vast grasslands, which extend in all directions except west, where a steep escarpment, abruptly sinking more than ten yards down, breaks the mostly even landscape.
104770:
A woolly sheep is grazing here.
A woolly sheep is grazing here.

Rigid, dense grass spreads across the landscape here, cloaking everything in deep green. The terrain is mostly level, with a few grassy mounds scattered throughout. The soil looks sunburnt but fertile; among the grass a number of herbaceous plants are showing new bright green leaves. To the east, a long hedge of thick bramble bushes separates two grassy plains from each other.
104771: This flowery and fertile land consists of scattered trees within a continuous vast, flat grassland. The grass has an auburn-tinted hue to it, and on several spots it appears to have been trampled on. A couple of worn stone boulders are standing in the sea of grass. Numerous white flowers grow around the rocks, adorning the area. Lightly rolling mats of grass and forbs stretch onward in every direction.
104772: The starving cow stands here looking for a patch of grass.

Lush grasses and small plants have occupied this area. The ground elevates slightly, creating small mounds covered in green grass with only a few small bushes with narrow leaves growing on the ground. The general lack of bigger trees suggests that this is a land of little moisture. The plain continues in gentle slopes to all directions, granting clear and unobstructed visibility.
104773:
A reddish-brown shrub with purplish-pink flowers grows here.
Inside the shrub, there are two clusters of purplish-pink flowers.
A sparrow is flapping around on the ground.

A beautiful sea of modest heathers dominates the undergrowth, occupying most of the land surface around the widely spaced, scattered trees. It is coloured with a rich mixture of deep green leaves, brown stems, and fragile violet blossom. In addition, blueberries and other woody plant species grow here in abundance, complementing the scale with blue and more shades of green. Far to the north, a dark green forest breaks into the horizon and the vegetation gets more bushy.
104774:
A sprawling green bush of stinging nettle grows here.
A colourful butterfly is fluttering around here.
A red-furred doe wanders peacefully among the grass.

A dense thorn barrier separates the scrubland from the dark, sinister Mirkwood. The ground looks really messy with spiky shrubs mixed with some coarse grass which grow all over the area. Everything is covered with broken twigs and fallen leaves which are littering the ground. No signs of wildlife exist, making the atmosphere silent and oppressing. The thorn barrier continues to the west.
104775: A thick, impenetrable thorn barrier follows the border line of the ancient forest of the Mirkwood which lies just behind the thorns. The foreboding presence of the forest hangs in the air and makes even the vegetation look tainted and grim. Numerous decaying leaves cover the earth, colouring it with dull shades of brown.
104776: The soil is porous and fertile; a well developed grass stratum and a few trees of low height grow on it. A wide zone of thick bramble bushes has formed a broad and tall natural hedge that cuts the passage to the west. The tranquil open plains continue in other directions, allowing easy and clear travelling. The ground is filled with small fragrant flowers and plants.
104777: A red-furred doe wanders peacefully among the grass.

A huge, solitary tree stands alone on a small mound; the only break in the vast expanse of open plains extending to the horizon. Once a truly royal representative of its species, the tree looks now just old and dried; its uneven bark has cracked from several spots, and the branches are thin and spindly. A large brown patch of dead earth surrounds the tree. There, a tiny plant struggles to survive.
104778: The Mirkwood is dark, silent and dense. Huge, black trees loom next to each other; their tangled branches, murky leaves and hanging vines forming a solid canopy above that is preventing all the light and quickly suffocating all the sounds. The ground is full of fallen, black leaves, totally hiding the soil underneath them. A high thorn barrier runs throughout the area, encircling the dark, silent trees. An uncountable amount of huge spikes is protruding outwards from the barrier, as a warning of impending death for anyone who dares to attempt to venture deeper into the forest.
104779: Perched within the folds of the lonely, parched tree, the thin branches spread out in all directions. There is scarcely any foliage on the tree, only a few dry, narrow leaves cling to the tips of the fragile branches. The tree is a good and obvious vantage point. It offers a clear view of the surrounding lands. The vast grassland continues in every direction as far as the eye can see except to the north where the murky Mirkwood looms.
104780: Yellow flowers, with grey-green foliage, grow in clusters here.

The eastern end of the wide plain transforms into a rocky area filled with stones and boulders of all sizes. A long, bushy cliff stretches through the area, twisting and branching, forming a confusing sprawl of sheer rock faces, irregularly shaped boulders, and tangled, dark bushes. In most places, both visibility and travel is blocked by the eastern boulders.
104781: The nearer the Mirkwood gets, the denser the brush is. Spine bushes, brambles and thistles grow in abundance forming a kind of natural passageway which arches gently towards the west and south. To the north, there is a copse of bushes which sticks out of its surroundings as the bushes have dried and died where they stand. To the east and south, one can sense the presence of the dark, huge forest.
104782: The terrain is very challenging inside the dense thicket. Neither clear path nor any kind of wider open area exists, which would make the smooth travelling in this green shrubbery possible. Behind every bush there seems to be just another copse waiting. It is difficult to keep track of directions here.
104784: Concealed from the eyes of the common wanderers, a hidden path runs inside the bushy vegetation. The way is narrow, but provides enough room to allow one to rest for a while, or even to make a temporary camp here. The southern exit has been camouflaged with loose bushes. It must have happened some time ago, as the bushes have withered and died.
104816: The bridge, which is constructed out of three ropes, spans the crevice from west to east allowing a somewhat safe route from one side of the crevice to the other side. The thickest rope hangs several feet lower than the other two thinner ones. Far below the ropes a murky pool covers the base of the crevice.
104817: This small lodge had been erected by stacking thick wooden beams on top of each other. A heavy wooden door marks its entrance, while a small window with shutters gives a great view over the long crevice in the south. The interior of this home consists of some simple furniture with a few paintings of farm animals attached to the walls.
104819:
An ancient fungus smothers the boulders.
An ancient fungus smothers the boulders.
An ancient fungus smothers the boulders.
A giant, strange looking green fungus is here, ready to devour you in seconds.

There is a small and moist hole underneath the ground. The walls are near each other and made of stones intertwined with roots and dried mud. Soft, white mushrooms are growing on the walls in vast mats and are spreading their mycelia everywhere. The floor consists of coarse gravel which is covered by leaves and twigs. The air is very dense, almost overwhelmingly so, due to the spores of fungi which fill the air.
104824:
A colourful butterfly is fluttering around here.
An angry bee is here, collecting nectar from all the flowers of the garden.

Lush, green grass covers these plains for as far as the eye can see. The plains continue south and eastward, seemingly without end. Many miles to the west, even the most inexperienced traveller could spot the smoke and, if the wind was favourable, smell the telltale signs of a village.
104825:
A garden snake slithers harmlessly here.
A garden snake slithers harmlessly here.
A fat rabbit is here, chewing on some grass.

The massive plains, so characteristic of the lands surrounding the Anduin River far to the west, end abruptly here at a small grove of trees. As large and unyielding as these plains appear to be, they are not so mighty as to withstand the domination of man. Just to the west, a small man-made grove of elms stand as cover for a large village just beyond.
104826: Though not as impressive as the walls surrounding some towns, the walls of this village appear impossible to penetrate. On close inspection, it becomes clear that these walls are not solid but live vines and brush intertwining live elm trees. The brush has been woven so tightly that no light from inside the village escapes.
104827:
A giant, strange looking green fungus is here, ready to devour you in seconds.
An ancient fungus smothers the boulders.
A beautiful and docile horse is standing here.

This cave has been formed deep within the bedrock. The walls are covered in chip-marks, as if this cave has been widened by simple stone-working tools. Dripping from the ceiling, bat-guano accumulates on the floor, its stench making breathing unpleasant. Some moss and fungi grow on the fertile compost provided by the mixture of decomposing organic matter.
104828:
Some roots lie here waiting to ensnare weary travellers.
A small bat is standing here.

The encompassing soil is held together by thousands of thick, gnarled roots. Their sporadic growth patterns make any type of movement tedious. The dirt is packed tight with the exception of the ceiling, which seems especially soft and moist. A few sharp rocks also make this place somewhat hazardous for the unwary.
104829:
Herb: honeycomb x 2
Food: honeycomb x 2

A bee flies around here, collecting nectar from the flowers.
A bee flies around here, collecting nectar from the flowers.

The entire panoramic view of this enclosed area is packed full of ornamental shrubs and flowers. Though not everything is in full bloom, it seems there is a wide enough variety for something to be providing colour throughout all four seasons. Around the edges of the enclosure stand tall, vine-covered walls. The garden floor is covered with a short, thick green turf, insulating the ground below. In the centre bubbles a fresh spring, providing life to all the surrounding foliage.
104836: The cavern is filled with large, grey rocks which lie scattered around. At some places the floor is plain, smooth rock, elsewhere it is filled with sand and gravel. There is an obscure pathway which flits its way around the boulders, rocks and winding walls, creating a confusing, but fairly passable route throughout the barren area. At one end, the cave ascends and finally leads up to a wide ledge and a massive boulder.
104837:
A powerful young troll stares at you.
A powerful young troll stares at you.

A round, rocky cave rises up into great heights. It is filled with boulders and rocks, intact stonewalls and crude gravel. There are plenty of shady ledges, overhangs and other obstacles formed of stone that creates numerous hideouts and places to lurk in the shadowy darkness.
104838:
A skeleton of some humanoid lies in the dust.
A small, mean earth troll is standing here, thinking of something hideous.
A small, mean earth troll is standing here, thinking of something hideous.
A nasty troll female crouches here, with a feral look in her eyes.

A wide cavern opens up in the underground. The place is full of filth and mess, and emits a foul stench. Roughly constructed, giant sized furniture have been made of rocks and tree logs. There are a few sitting places and a stone ledge working as a table. Old bones, broken wine jars, and other junk lay scattered around the cavern. A few dark alcoves in the stonewall seem to be serving as sleeping areas. One exit leads down via a dark hole in the floor, while a massive, old padlock is used to secure an obstruction made of rock and stone to the east.
104839:
An infant troll, baring its teeth, snarls here.
A mouse sniffs around, searching for a morsel of food.

A windy, dark tunnel shrivels inside the ground. At some places the solid stone walls are near, sometimes they are far from each other. The floor is made of cold rock as well. While the ceiling and most sections of the walls are rather uneven, the floor seems smooth in most places and bears the signs of having been worn out and smoothened by countless heavy feet over a long time.
104840: Behind the heavy boulder, a twisted tunnel runs towards the darkness. The air appears to be rather damp. Although it is very dark, there is visible evidence of odd tracks on the cold earth floor. The walls are leaning towards each other, and the space between them gets narrower and narrower when one proceeds forward. The tunnel ends at a wider cavern where several shattered rocks and some old bones lay scattered on the dirt floor around a dark hole leading down.
104851: A giant termite is here, crushing skulls and bones.

There is an airy and surprisingly spacious pit under the giant stump. The entrance is nicely camouflaged either by a strange coincidence of nature or by cunning skill. The ceiling of this room is covered by numerous roots of all sizes, while the walls and the floor are a mixture of hard sand, some trunks and smooth-edged rocks. It remains unclear whether this space is used as a home, and who or what would live here, under the roots.
104893:
A huge orc bodyguard looks at you suspiciously.
The Guardian is standing here, watching the treasures.
A huge orc bodyguard looks at you suspiciously.
A huge orc bodyguard looks at you suspiciously.
A huge orc bodyguard looks at you suspiciously.

Painted images line the walls, though many are blurred with age and even more have been defaced by the orcs. This is a massive corridor which runs north and south, but the mining operations above have caused a cave-in to the north. To the south is an arch, leading into a hall.
104899: A dark orkish archer is wielding a very vicious-looking bow.

At this point a hard-surfaced road bending from the south to the east joined a smaller corridor leading north. However, both arms of the road seem to have been completely blocked by a tremendous rockfall. The ceiling has fallen in to the south and east creating a jumble of mixed boulders and smaller stones which prevents any further travel.
104900: A dark orkish archer is wielding a very vicious-looking bow.

At one time this was apparently a warehouse containing tools, utensils, bolts of fabric, hides, and other useful materials. Fragments of some of these can be seen buried amid the general devastation. Not only have cabinets and bins clearly been broken into, but a great stone block has fallen down into and through the cavity, crushing and burying the southern half and strewing the rubble of floors and walls over the other half. It may be that something useful is still buried here in the blackness.
105039: A cave-in has brought much dirt into the corridor and it has become necessary to bend and crawl to pass through. The earthy environment is a combination of clay and loose rubble through which many roots have found their way. With time the damp air becomes pressing and longer periods of confinement in the cramped space takes its toll on your endurance. A rubble-slide has sealed the corridor off to the south, working your way through would appear to be hard work.
105067: The road ends here. You can see that the intention was to make the road go further south, but the only exit apart from the road back north is a passage to the west.
105068: The road is in very bad repair. Cracks and fissures have occured on the road surface making travel very difficult. The surface has become almost like steps as the unstableness has caused one end to lift higher than the other. The walls have been reinforced haphazardly with wooden beams and stone columns. The columns look to have been pulled from other parts of Moria as they are a mismatched set of differing colors and styles.
105069: The road extends for some distance in both directions. The stonework here is in good shape - in many places there is clear evidence of repairs having been done sometime in the relatively recent past.
105070: This section of the road is in very good repair. None of the flagstones which comprise the bed of the road are missing or even cracked. The road extends to the north and south.
105071: This is an intersection of sorts, with exits in all directions but east. The way continues to the south but opens up into a larger room to the north. West is a small passage.
105081: A small white fountain is here.

This circular place is maybe ten yards in diameter. It is surrounded by three rings. The outer ring is a row of seemingly wild bushes that grow leaves of all shapes and shades of green. The second ring consists of roughly a dozen elven statues made from white marble, which show only barely visible signs of age. All of them were created in great detail and seem to carry expressions of immortal dignity. The inner ring consists of flower beds in which colourful blossoms of all kinds are to be seen, and all are very pretty to behold. A small wall to the south puts a stop to anyone falling down the steep slope and into the valley below, while a path winds itself a few yards up in the north.
105082:
A sturdy pack horse is standing here.
A humble man stands here, ready to help you with your things.

This is definitely the most beautiful place of Rivendell. The Hallway, approaching the room also known as the Hall of the Lost Footsteps, was used to receive visiting ambassadors, or to host royal wedding celebrations. The Mainroom illustrates the owner's wish to dazzle and mark his power. The 17 arcades decorated with mirrors that majestically alternate with 17 windows over 240 feet, represent a real technical feat. All is splendor, beauty and sophistication: the chandeliers, the marble, the bronze, the gilding, and the large paintings recalling victories.
105083:
A sturdy pack horse is standing here.
A sturdy pack horse is standing here.
A humble man stands here, ready to help you with your things.

This house has been decorated warm and cosy. A bright light illuminates the entire room, growing brighter further inside. Placed in the centre is a round wooden table, accompanied by three chairs. A lit and thus warm fireplace occupies one of the corners. The southern wall is covered with cabinets made of glass, filled with numerous old and new trophies of war. Various helmets, shields, and tribe artefacts are displayed along the walls and on pedestals.
105091: Standing on broken bits of gravel and concrete, this was once a very sturdy road, expected to carry no doubt, the heavy loads of ore and metals gutted from mining Turngurth. All around you, a sombre mist lies, the strength of Angmar is heavy here.
105092: A hungry warg (Rood) is standing here, ridden by you.

The grey dullness of the river, picked up from the mountains to the east, has mostly settled or been strained from the water. However, the cold water still tastes bitter and foul. This scar of its tortures will be with it for a long time, and perhaps only the healing lands of Elrond can ameliorate it. The river flows straight to west.
105142: A humble man stands here, ready to help you with your things.

The room is sparse and cloaked in darkness. A slited window lets in a single ray of light that falls upon the hard, grey-stone floor. The walls are covered with black curtains that stand still, undisturbed by any draft or breeze. In a corner of the room is a single bed, hard and uncomfortable. A desk stands here with a half-melted wax candle, illuminating a feather-pen and ink vial, the desk's only other contents.
105143:
A heavy desk, made of solid oak, stands here.
A large bookshelf sits against the wall.
A sturdy bed made from solid oak lies here, covered in warm blankets.
An Elven steward stands here, watching over the household.
A tall and strong guard is here.
A tall and strong guard is here.

You enter a brightly lit room, with candles all over. The walls are covered with bookshelves, filled with ancient, dusty books about priests' knowledge.
