Along the southern wall you see a thick oaken desk covered with notes, featherpens and books. Along the western shelf a small, yet cosy bed stands, ready for recovery.
105144: Gail's Hideout among the Swaying Branches
A humble man stands here, ready to help you with your things.

A hollow space in the tree-trunk leads upward into the swaying branches overhead. A system of ropes has been strung between the larger limbs, creating a soft floor which sways with the branches in the breeze. On the western side, a modest bed is covered with a sky-blue blanket, with a large oilcloth nearby in case of inclement weather. A small bureau anchored to the trunk holds writing and drawing utensils. The hollow base of the trunk has just enough room to stable a horse temporarily. From up here there is a lovely view of the sky and surrounding mountains, and a gentle breeze stirs branches and leaves in a peaceful natural symphony.
105145: A small, seldom used trail leads north, towards the Blue Mountains, and south, where it ends on the bank of a river. The trail follows the edge of a light forest, where you can hear birds tweeting. It should be safe to relax and rest your weary feet in the shade of the trees, it looks like a very peaceful place. Beyond the river, a tower dominates the landscape.
105153: A large beautiful rose bush is blooming here.

You are in the famous forest of Woody End. There are many trees around you which block and limit your view to within a few paces. Most of the trees are oaks and beeches, heavy vegetation is apparent on the floor and the density of the humidity is such that you sense you could almost touch it.
105209: Misshapen trees give way to a rocky gully to the north. The wind can be heard sweeping across the trees and through the gully, making a howling noise, a perpetual scream quite suitable to the atmosphere of the rest of the forest.
105212: High above the ground, a graceful archway leads to the northern part of the Last Homely Home. The sides of the archway are decorated with white, fine carvings of flowers and leaves that intermingle with real leaves and climbing plants. The arch makes a slow curve towards the east and south. On the eastern side is the Fountain square to be seen while the view opens to the west and north over a blooming, prospering valley.
105219: A fine marble chessboard with ivory and ebony pieces is set here.

The white, wooden platform measures at least seven or eight yards in diameter and its borders are decorated and marked with wide flowerboxes. Many colourful and well-grown plants thrive in the boxes and climb on filigrane supports made of light brown wood. Above is a roof made of darker wood. It is also overgrown and under it hang flowerpots from which plants seem to flow like water. A wind chime hangs from the southern border of the roof, so that each small gust of wind produces silent chimes.
105220: The fine carvings on this roofed archway's banister are barely visible, as the entire archway is heavily overgrown with healthy, green and blooming plants. The plants grow up from below, from hanging flowerpots as well as from well-tended flowerboxes made of light clay standing on the ground. Towards the north, the archway becomes wide enough to support a couple of Rivendell's small, filigrane housings; all of them are also heavily decorated and sometimes overgrown with dense, healthy vegetation of all kinds.
105221: The archway becomes much wider as it runs through a long, oval shaped garden. Between white statues showing elves and scenes from the ancient times stand other finely crafted shapes that represent growing plants and trees. All the statues and climb aids are overgrown by countless different flowers or other plants; between those plants stand white benches. Northwards, there are a few small housings to be seen which have been elegantly fitted within the thriving vegetation of this high garden. To the east, the archway transforms into narrow stairs which lead steeply upwards. The ground below, as a look over the flowered banister reveals, is at least twenty yards below.
105222: This part of the Last Homely Home consists of a small number of strewn, separate housings that are connected by raised walkways. Every so often, one of the walkways connects to another one, thus creating some sort of seemingly weightless net, as the slender supports are well-hidden in the vegetation growing from below.
105223:
A well-crafted white fountain is here, water pouring forth from it.
An elf is here walking around.

The building becomes very wide as it opens up to a large open area where several gardens, separated by massive hedges, have been created. Strewn all over the garden are small pavilions, gazebos, statues, benches, and occasional ponds in which shimmering fishes of all kinds and sizes swim. There even seem to be a few smaller housings that have inspiciously been crafted - or grown? - within these prospering gardens. Right in the centre of this area splashes a large fountain.
105224: The building has been skilfully built into the landscape, making it hard to tell where the vegetation starts and the building ends. It winds itself over and around the terrain and seems to have grown right out of the bushes, vines and trees that surround it. Once in a while pavilions, statues, benches, or small niches invite for a rest or to take a look at the numerous flourishing plants and the ever-blooming flowers around. A steep stair rises towards the south and actually leads more upwards than southwards towards a curving bridge.
105225: Northern Entrance of the Last Homely Home

The Last Homely Home here is made from stone, but the brown material could very well be hard wood. The building's decorations mimic growing vines or even thicker trees that intermingle with actual ever-green vegetation. The stairs here lead down towards a path and spiral upwards around a wide yet still graceful tower. Every so often, the stair widens into a larger balcony.
105226:
There is a huge, pyramidal beehive here.
A white-painted bench is here.
A bee flies around here, collecting nectar from the flowers.
A bee flies around here, collecting nectar from the flowers.

This large and mostly untended garden features countless wild flowers, long grasses, and occasional bushes. Whenever a plant seems to reach the end of flouriscence other flowers take over, so the garden is always filled with an ocean of colourful dots of petals. Many narrow paths snake through the high grasses and around the thickest patches of flowers, and several bee hives can be seen all over the landscape. Countless bees are constantly buzzing around, flying from flower to flower and come and go from the hive. Here and there, one can spot gracefully built and with higher vegetation entwined houses of Rivendell.
105227: Path towards the Northern Part of Elrond's Home

A narrow path curves itself around larger bushes, groups of trees and statues made of white marble showing ancient warriors. It raises a bit towards the north and finally leads to one of the entrances of the sprawled Last Homely Home. The northern part seems to consist of small pavillons, archways, and small housings decorated with countless small features. Many of the walls have been climbed by blooming plants such as clematis, roses, and white-blooming ivy.
105228:
A large and finely decorated harp of white marble has been built here.
An Elf is here walking around.
An Elf is here walking around.

This high bridge is very narrow and seems fragile although neither your feet nor the winds seem to be able to shake it in the slightest way. The banisters have been carefully carved over years - or even decades - to show times and events of old. On the banisters stand narrow flowerboxes of clay in which countless well-smelling herbs of healing or appeal grow.
105229: The banisters have been replaced in this part of the bridge with dense, green hedges which grow on both sides of the pathway. The bridge curves several times to the left and to the right, making it much longer than it would have been if it ran straight. The bridge descends a bit while curving towards the north until it finally ends at a small, flowered platform where a relatively steep stair leads downwards.
105252: A humble man stands here, ready to help you with your things.

A benevolent magical aura embraces all who enter this shadowy demense. It looks like the light dances and sparkles softly around the room, especially upon a desk standing in the middle of the room, covered with potions and runic scrolls. The shadows grow deeper in the corner where a neatly kept pallet is located for sleeping. Attached to the far wall is an exercise apparatus to increase agility and speed.
105253: A humble man stands here, ready to help you with your things.

A calm, green light is suffusing from above, enlightening a network of wide, solid branches which form the floor of this simple but comfortable house located high above the ground. Looking up one can see leaves, leaves and more leaves, leaving just enough room in between them to see sun shining or stars glinting. The dense layer of leaves continues on small branches on every side of the room, and some of the leaves seem to be covered with strange runes. One of the underbranches has a natural waterhole, suitable to collect water that has rained down.
105261:
A skeleton of some humanoid lies in the dust.
A rock lizard is here, motionless as it observes you.
A fallow deer is grazing peacefully here.

A sheer cliff wall stands here, blocking passage to the north. Many jagged rocks lie on the ground here, as if they are acting as teeth for the bottom of the cliff. High above, some patches of grass can be seen on the top of the hill. To the east and the west it appears that the hill can be passed by walking around.
105262: A fallow deer is grazing peacefully here.

This field is covered with dry weeds and tall grasses. The ground consists of pebbles and does not appear very welcoming for any vegetation which might attempt to grow here. The field is quite flat, with some rocks jutting out of the ground in the northeast.
105263: A few plants of grain sprinkled in with thick growth of grass approach this field from the north, but the ground is unforgiving to vegetation here. The soil is too dense with stones and pebbles to allow grass to grow here, although some persistent patches still live here and there. To the west there is an impressive wall of brambles, intertwined in such a dense thicket that it will not allow any travellers through at this point.
105264: Wild grain flourishes here in this fallow field, intermingled with grass. The grain plants grow to several feet high, surpassing the tall blades of grass in height. The seeds at the tops of the grain weigh some of plants down causing them to bend and stoop.
105265: Brown grass covers the majority of this field. There are patches of green grass growing in places but the overall hue of the field is of a golden-brown colour. In the middle of the field some natural grain grows, rising above the brown grass. The grain plants expand towards the east, dominating the horizon. There is an impressive wall of bramble bushes to the west and south and there are also some broken branches of bramble on the ground next to the bushes.
105266:
An erect shrub with green pinnate leaves is growing here.
Inside the shrub, there are three piles of crimson raspberries.

Thick brambles tangled together make up the huge vegetation wall to the north and the east. The bramble bushes grow too thickly to the northeast for any animals to pass through. The bushes begin to thin gradually from the east to the west. In the west, some plains with low bramble bushes continue.
105267: The riverside is steep and rocky, while the plains are covered with long grasses and small bramble twigs, which become longer and thicker towards the east. The sound of the rushing water of the Anduin comes from the west, as it continues its southward flow.
105268:
A black crow flies low to the ground here, looking for carrion to eat.
A small grasshopper clings to a blade of grass, ready to spring.
A sly mongoose keeps an eye out for danger.

The bramble bushes grow wide apart from the south and begin to grow thicker towards the north. Some patches of brush twigs are cut on the eastern side of the bramble wall here. Overall the brush wall growing north to south looms large here.
105269:
A canoe has been left here.
A small grasshopper clings to a blade of grass, ready to spring.

Small pebbles cover the bank of the river, while grass covers the area further from the river. On a smooth, sandy part of the bank, some thick wooden poles have been erected; ropes, firmly attached around them, are visible. The placement of the poles indicates a landing place for boats. The opposite shore, covered with fallen trees, rises high above the river.
105270: There are two slender-stemmed plants, with brown heads here.

Most of this riverbank is covered by a field of reeds, while the plains to the east are covered with grass. An occasional bramble twig can be spotted between the blades of grass, but further towards the east the brambles become more dense, so dense that it is impossible to spot anything behind them.
105271: A grey wolf is here, snarling aggressively.

There are flat plains grown over with grass covering this area. Some small rounded rocks are scattered around thick, bushy sections of grass. Brambles, bushes, and small thornbushes grow among the patches of grass surrounding the rocks. Far to the southeast the contours of bushes are visible.
105272: These plains are covered with long grass. Here and there, dry brambles grow from the ground, becoming very thick toward the south. The horizon to the south is completely concealed by the wall of bramble, so thick that it cannot be seen through, let alone travelled through.
105273: These plains are flat in the northern part of this field but to the south the ground gets higher and the vegetation becomes more dense; huge bramble bushes on a hill can even be seen in the distance to the southwest. Apart from the occasional animal tracks and droppings, the ground here does not have anything more than grass.
105274: Long grass covers the flat plains. At a few places some high bushes grow in between the grass and there is even one dead tree. Small holes can be seen under some of the bushes; typical for the entrance of rodent holes.
105275: A small evergreen plant grows here, its woody stems reaching two feet.

The grass covered plains seem to go on forever to the east. Some small bushes grow in between the grass. A barely visible animal track bends from the east to the south. Far off, at the horizon to the south, dense and high bushes are visible.
105276:
Clusters of slender stems and tall leaves thrive in the mud and shallows.
A swamp iris grows here.
A large rabbit looks peacefully at you, ready to dart away.

Typical swamp plants, such as reeds and irises grow at this submerged riverbank, while the soft ground further away from the river is covered with long grass. In some areas the grass seems to be trimmed down to a height just above the soil. Some small excrement is visible around the trimmed areas, as if small animals had grazed on the grass here.
105277:
*Penrose the Black Numenorean* , wielding a dark broadsword, is here, riding a pack horse (shrouded).
A pack horse is standing here, ridden by *Penrose the Black Numenorean* .
A great dark-grey horse stamps restively.
A great, wild boar with large tusks is here, ready to charge.

The flat plains submerge into the calm river here. Various animal prints are visible in the soft mud at the shore; this must be a frequently used drinking place for the local wildlife. From the water front, an animal track leads inland to the east.
105278: The river can be seen flowing southward to the west of this riverbank. The ground is rather high above the river in the north and gently slopes down as it continues to the south. There are brown weeds that cover the ground and expand to the east in a sea of dry plains.
105279: A brown fox is here, looking for some rabbits to chew up.

This riverbank is surrounded by flowing water on two sides. The great river Anduin flows westward then makes a turn south along the northwest edge of the bank. The riverbank is fairly steep when approaching the surface of the river. Short grass grows here continuing to the east and south.
105280: Dark green grass covers the majority of this field, save a lone, dense tree which stands proudly in the middle of the grass. The blades of grass are quite short starting from the eastern side of the field and grow taller toward the east. At some places the grass has been stamped down, a clear trail being visible on the ground.
105281:
A tiny spider is here, eating a tiny bug.
A buck runs swiftly from place to place, looking about warily as it grazes.

Green grass covers this field which lies next to the great river Anduin to the west. Where the meadow meets the river there is a short drop off into the river, which does not cause any obstruction for a traveller wishing to swim. The meadow continues in all other directions.
105282: Waist high grasses cover the ground in this meadow, which meets the Anduin river to the north and the west. Reeds grow along the riverbank before meeting the grasses of the meadow on this side of the river. The meadow continues to the east and south.
105283: This meadow grows waist high grasses and a few weeds interspersed throughout. The ground is a little soggy, causing fertile soil for a lush, green look to the grass growing in the field here. The ground gradually slopes upward to the south.
105284: Clusters of slender stems and tall leaves thrive in the mud and shallows.

Short grass and irises cover this low-lying riverbank. The ground is soggy but solid enough to walk on without slowing one down. Reeds border the river to the west. The ground begins to gradually slope upward to the east and south.
105285: The field slopes down from the east, covered with a spattering of flowers and grasses. The grass is quite healthy here in this low green field. On the western horizon the ground continues to lose elevation. To the south the green fields and assorted flora continue.
105286:
Yellow flowers, with grey-green foliage, grow in clusters here.
A small grasshopper clings to a blade of grass, ready to spring.

The ground seems to slope downwards toward the west here, creating a natural protection against the wind in this otherwise flat landscape. The local flora has seized control of this protected field; flowers and other plants are growing in abundance. The plains south of here seem rather barren with the exception of some short bushes.
105287: A large, yellow crab is crawling around here.

While the riverbank towards the northeast is steep and grassy, the shore of this area sits a bit lower. The rich assortment of rocks on this riverbank add a colourful grey texture compared to the rich blue of the Anduin river. They have been smoothed and polished from years of the river rushing over them as it makes its way southwest.
105288: Bushes and small trees grow here, but the most notable landmark would be an old cottage. Vines cover it from top to bottom, as it has been left by caring hands here for quite some time, and nature has taken it over. Just west of it lies a huge millstone.
105289: A circular stone well has been built here.

Four columns mark there was once a house here, though the remnants have been burned and blackened. Much of the debris is covered with a green moss, while others are slowly sinking into the soil. Absolutely nothing stands to give shelter to anyone travelling through here.
105290: Tufts of grass and small rocks dot this extending wasteland, giving it a desolate look. The caked soil is unforgiving to the grass that has sprouted up, relentlessly forcing it to struggle for its life among the rocks.
105291: The riverbank is covered in brush, while the fields around it are green with grasses. The brush and soil have been trampled on several places, indicating that animals have made the riverbank and its surrounding fields their home.
105292: A hungry warg is standing here, ridden by Backdraft.

Many small trees grow on the plains here, among a few stumps that dwindle in number as they span deeper into the landscape. While the top of the trees makes a somewhat healthy impression that cannot be said about the lower parts, especially near the roots. The soil is somewhat soft and smells slightly of mud, the grass and bushes look bleak and dying while patches of fungi thrieve everywhere. In many places the fungi have started to grow between the trees' roots and have started to climb even higher.
105293: Field of Stumps next to the Anduin

A colourful butterfly is fluttering around here.
A hungry warg is standing here, ridden by Backdraft.

The landscape of this area has been harshly ravaged by some woodworkers. The mottled landscape is littered with stumps of varying heights; who ever chopped this field bare did so very hastily, and without any care to its surroundings. The Great River flows directly to the west, with a huge mess of logs stuck in the brush on the riverbank.
105294: A raft has been left here.

A huge wooden dock, built from heavy logs, covers the terrain like a massive floor. The first pilings of the dock have crumbled so that the dock floor is tilted and slowly descends into the river, creating an unstable stair into the water. However, the dock can still be used as a landing area for small boats. What seems to be a trail begins here, and continues on to the east.
105295: The well worn trail bends here, leading to the west and south. Old wagon tracks are occasionally visible on the edges of the trail. It appears to not have been in active use in recent years, with patches of tall grass covering the trail in many areas.
105296: A line of trees grows along the northern border of a trail coming from the river and heading southeast. The trail cuts the plain deeply. Descending from here to the road is impossible due to the steepness of the escarpment, while travelling to the east along a gentle slope will lead to the trail.
105297: The ground raises towards a small hill to the south. The slope is covered by grass and small plants, and some occasional gullies make the ground uneven and somewhat hard to travel. The top of the hill is covered by a patch of trees. Further to the south, a sort of road comes from the west and, turning around a steep rise, vanishes to the southeast. The plain continues to the north and east.
105298: The ground is completely covered by high grass. Some stems are two feet high with little panicles to the top, some other are even higher with a flower-head made of densely packed spikelets. To the west some trees dot the plain. To the north the vegetation becomes thick and hard to travel.
105299:
A large thorny branched shrub is growing here.
On the shrub, there are a number of blackberries.
The garden snake slithers harmlessly here.

Many blackberry bushes cover the ground making it difficult to travel. To the west the terrain descends to the river, while to the east and south vast plains can be seen. Small tracks can be seen all around on the ground, revealing intense activity of insects and small animals.
105300: This vast grassy plain extends in all directions. No sign of any kind of humanoid activity can be seen. To the west, towards the river, the vegetation becomes thicker and hard to cross. To the east the steep banks of a hill block the way.
105301:
The wild ox seems ready to charge you.
The wild ox seems ready to charge you.

The ground is dry and bare, and occasional cracks and fissures make travelling through this area quite dangerous. No vegetation but grass and heather grows here. The terrain becomes harder to travel to the west, approaching the river. To the east and south lies a grassy plain, while to the north the ground is dotted with rocks mixed with grass.
105302: The grassy plains extend towards the north, east and south from these mixed plains. To the west the terrain is quite rocky and becomes difficult to travel across while riding a mount. Some trees can be seen growing in this part of the plains. A little track made by animals leads west to the river.
105303: Plains between the River and Forest

The ground is grassy and level. Some trees, surrounded by a number of rocks and boulders, grow among the grass giving shelter to birds and little animals. To the north and east some woody slopes can be seen, while to the south the plains seem to continue for miles.
105304: A fallow deer is grazing peacefully here.

The grass is lush and thick in this area, probably due to the influence of the Great River Anduin that flows nearby to the west. To the east and north, lines of trees mark the beginning of a forest. A vast plain continues to the south. A little animal track comes from the forest to the east.
105323:
An orc-guard of the Morgundul is on patrol here.
An orc-guard of the Morgundul is on patrol here.

Rocks jut out from all directions along the walls here. This cave seems to have been hollowed out ages ago from some water source. Now it can be used as a hiding place for any travellers needing shelter. The cave entrance is quite wide but begins to narrow gradually as it burrows its way to the west.
105324:
An orc-guard of the Morgundul is on patrol here.
An orc-guard of the Morgundul is on patrol here.

This hollowed out cave comes to its end here as it becomes too narrow and finally disappears into a stone wall on the west. There are some ancient crates lying about in disarray here; perhaps some supplies for some ancient travellers, using the cave as a shelter.
105325: A small grasshopper clings to a blade of grass, ready to spring.

Some patches of dry, thirsty grass grow here and there in this sloping field. The ground begins to slope upward to the east, as it approaches a hill. Many pebbles cover the ground here causing a crunching sound underfoot.
105326: The sloping ground gives way to a stony peak here. There are some large boulders on this hill, and the ground is covered with small stones. Patches of grass grow among the boulders, and a few small bushes grow here and there as well. The rocky hill is smooth in its descent on all sides, except to the south, which gives way to a sheer cliff. The cliff bottom below to the south can be easily viewed from here but tall bushes and boulders block the view to any other direction.
105327: The field is filled with long, green blades of grass. Some of them being so light, that their ends curl over, dipping back towards the earth. The ground begins to slope upward from the east to the west. A hill can be seen climbing in the horizon to the west. Some large boulders stick out of the ground here and there.
105328: A grey wolf is here, snarling aggressively.

This field has healthy, green grass growing at waist level, but the most striking feature of the field is the amount of wildflowers growing here. There are irises growing in the north, but as the field unfolds toward the south, wildflowers of all types emerge in the field, peaking their petals over the top of the grass.
105329: This is a vast plain of waist high grass and wild flowers, dominated by plants with forked leaves and white composite flowers. To the north the ground starts descending and the bushes of bramble, which are rare here, start growing denser. Nests in the branches of larger and older bushes and frequent cries of birds indicate active wild life.
105330: A tall plant with a perfectly smooth stem gracefully marks the landscape.

Dark-green hemlock plants with finely divided leaves and strong, spotted stems prosper and dominate the vegetation. Their large umbels consisting of numerous small, white flowers attract hordes of insects and butterflies, which fill the air with the sounds of buzzing. Fields clothed in white continue in the west, whereas in the north, where the grass gets darker, some small hills dot the landscape.
105331:
The corpse of a drone bee is lying here.
A bee flies around here, collecting nectar from the flowers.
A bee flies around here, collecting nectar from the flowers.
A swarm of hornets is coming out of its nest.
A swarm of hornets is coming out of its nest.
A fallow deer is grazing peacefully here.
An elven hunter, fair and mighty, roams here warding against evil.
An elven hunter, fair and mighty, roams here warding against evil.

An enormous tree towers above the fields here, having withstood many years of raging storm, but now finally faltering due to old age. Its lower branches are dry and dead, and the trunk is hollow. Yet the leaves on upper branches are fresh and green, showing that the tree has not entirely given up. Bees fly continuously in and out of the huge, hollow trunk, and loud buzzing fills the air, apparently coming from a little opening in the trunk. A muddy-looking, bubbling swamp opens up to the east, blocking the travelling to that direction.
105332:
A sticky honeycomb lies on the ground.
A sticky honeycomb lies on the ground.
A drone bee flies around here, angrily buzzing.
A drone bee flies around here, angrily buzzing.
An angry bee is working on a honeycomb here.
An angry bee is working on a honeycomb here.
An angry bee is working on a honeycomb here.
A huge, bulky queen bee is here.

The humming and buzzing sound becomes deafening inside the trunk, as the bees do not like intruders. No wood is actually visible, because all sides of the trunk are covered with waxy honeycombs and are swarming with drones. Despite the immense size of the tree, there is not much room in this chamber, making it hard to fight the drones guarding their nest. A small opening in the trunk leads to the plains outside of the tree.
105333:
Yellow flowers, with grey-green foliage, grow in clusters here.
A bee flies around here, collecting nectar from the flowers.

Many colourful wild flowers flourish in this dense, almost impassable thicket. During summer time, when all the flowers bloom and fill the dense brush with sweet fragrance of pollen, numerous bees are attracted here. Faint buzzing and humming sounds fill the air when the bees work hard to collect nectar, and when they fly home, they are packed heavy with their load.
105334:
Some thick writhing vines whip all around you.
A mass of wriggling vines drops on you from the trees.

The northern portion of this field is comprised of knee-high grass. There are a few weeds here and there in the northern half. The southern part of this field consists of a mass of thorny bushes, tangled together in a never ending wrestling match. Brambles grow on the eastern side of the brush, mixing in with the thornbushes. The ground towards the west begins to become less populated with vegetation and some rocks are revealed on the bare ground.
105335:
A large thorny branched shrub is growing here.
On the shrub, there are a number of blackberries.
A mass of wriggling vines drops on you from the trees.

Thick brambles intertwined with razor sharp thornbushes and thick raspberry bushes comprises this almost impenetrable field of brush. Berries can be seen within the tangle of brush but for the most part all that is visible are dried stems with sharp thorns attached.
105336:
An erect shrub with green pinnate leaves is growing here.
Inside the shrub, there are three piles of crimson raspberries.

The level ground is covered with a thicket of wild raspberry reaching higher than a man's waist. Tangled thorny canes which are frequently impenetrable force travellers to search for easier routes. Barbed plants scratch the body and a layer of dried stems below the feet makes crunching sounds with each step. Some of the still standing stems are dry and dead, whereas others carry leaves and have remains of little berry clusters.
105337:
A sprawling green bush of stinging nettle grows here.
An erect shrub with green pinnate leaves is growing here.
Inside the shrub, there are some crimson raspberries.

Patches of wild raspberries with four feet high canes are interspersed with stinging nettles, forming a thicket which stings and tears the exposed skin of any travellers. Old stems, thorny vines and branches form a mass which is hard to penetrate. The earth beneath the plants is hard and dry, waiting for long- needed water.
105338:
A colourful butterfly is fluttering around here.
A swallow flies high above the ground.

Various wild flowers and flowering weeds liven up this grassy slope with colourful tints and hues. During summer time the air is filled with humming and buzzing sounds of bees and other small insects, whereas in winter time the tracks of small animals indicate active wildlife.
105339: The meadow is covered by lush grass dotted by red and white flowers stretching towards the sun above the grass. A small calm stream with dark cold water moistens the vegetation, also attracting numerous small insects buzzing above the water. Animal tracks all around the muddy banks and in shallow water indicate that wild animals use this spot for drinking.
105340: The land is covered with tall grasses interspersed with flowering plants, which are growing in thick bushes around the slowly bubbling brook. Huge splotches of bracken and bramble coloured in different tones of green give the plain a mottled look. The ground gets harder in the south and east, where the wetland plants are replaced with more common grass.
105341: A brown fox is here, looking for some rabbits to chew up.

The ground dips here, causing water to collect and saturate the soil. Swamp plants thrive in this area. There are flourishing swamp irises growing all about here. Healthy grass surrounds the depression here in all directions except the east.
105342: Long blades of grass, along with some weeds, fill this field. Some of the grass blades have a glossy, shiny appearance. The weeds that grow here bend over at the top. To the west the ground begins to slope upward. There are some large stones lying around.
105343: The ground begins to gain elevation here, starting from the north. The slope in the landscape gives way to a hill in the south. The hill itself is quite bare of vegetation. There are some large stones sticking out of the ground and some patches of grass here and there. In the west some light brush can be seen. Tall grass can be seen to the east.
105344: Thick bushes grow in the middle of this field, laced together with a scraggly thornbush. The leaves of the bushes grow outward, as if trying to escape the grasp of the thornbush, reaching for sunlight. To the southeast the ground begins to gain elevation and the soil is less fertile, with a sprinkling of pebbles. A decrepit farmhouse can be seen to the west.
105345: A small oaken table has been set here.

Lying in the middle of the field is the remains of an ancient farmhouse. Dust covers everything in this small farm house, which appears to have been abandoned long ago. A broken chair sits on its side next to an old table. There is debris lying about within the ruined frames of the farmhouse but nothing of value. The farmhouse seems to have given shelter to one or two occupants who once tilled the fields to the north, but no one has lived here for many years.
105346: Brown coloured weeds and numerous jagged boulders cover the slopes of this small hill; creating small ravines, grooves and deceptive deadends all around the rough ground. Along the eastern slope, the remnants of an ancient fence are running from north to south, but so decrepit is the fence that it hardly poses any obstacle to travelling. Beyond the fence a neglected farmhouse can be seen. Numerous bramble bushes are growing along the western edge of the hill, making it impossible to pass through. The vegetation begins to turn greener further to the north.
105347:
An oaken wine rack stands here.
Lying in the wine rack are three fine bottles.
A moaning ghost advances towards you, shimmering with a pale light.

The former habitants of this long ago abandoned farm must have used this cellar as a place for storage, as there are left over boxes and crates lying about, collecting dust. There are a few broken barrels and some dusty, broken glass, leftover from a broken bottle of wine lying on the ground. Dust covers everything in this ancient cellar, which has not been used for ages.
105348:
A large potato is growing here.
A large potato is growing here.
A grey wolf is here, snarling aggressively.

The ground here looks as if it was cultivated in ages before. There is some debris lying about in the field, nothing discernible. The land appears to have once held a healthy crop, but has long since been abandoned. To the north some bushes conceal the horizon, on the eastern and western sides of the farm the ground is wet and fertile.
105349: Soggy ground to the east gives way to a drier, more solid soil in this field. Lush, tall grass blades grow unhindered here by weeds or other vegetation, thriving in the sunlight. A short, ancient fence stands here, running in a north to south direction. The fence is ancient and decrepit, and hardly gives an obstacle.
105350: These plains are overgrown with dark green reeds and tall cattails. There is also a short layer of lush, healthy green coloured grass growing on the ground. The grass on the ground seems very delicate though, as if even a footstep would disturb the ground and uproot the grass. A small brook, originating from the north flows southbound, then makes a turn towards the east here.
105351: A brown fox is here, looking for some rabbits to chew up.

The brook flows gently to the east as it tumbles over rocks. There are reeds growing on either side of the brook and further outward from the brook grows healthy grass. There are clear tracks here, showing that this is a common drinking spot for many of the small animals that live in the surrounding plains.
105352: A dark, shallow brook flows calmly from the west to the south through this entangled, mould-smelling area. The numerous roots, bushes and high grass thrive around the brook, accompanied by tall patches of reeds and cattails growing both in the water and in depressions near the brook. The dense shrubbery have eventually taken over almost the whole area, only to the east the terrain is clearer, as it rises below the bushes towards a rugged ridge.
105353: A Lone Tree on the Ridge

The ground sinks abruptly to the north, providing a clear and unblocked view to the vast plains that extend everywhere to the north. The top of this ridge is stony and bare, save a huge, lone fir tree which has rooted itself firmly to the ground, bearing the sun, wind and rains without any signs of weakening: Its branches spread widely and trunk is covered in grey lichens.
105354: The garden snake slithers harmlessly here.

The plains expand in every direction here. The brown weeds that populate the western area of the plains intermingle with lush, green, blades of grass. The occurrence of green in the plains increases gradually to the east.
105355:
A worm is here slithering around.
A large rabbit looks peacefully at you, ready to dart away.

Nothing more than grass covers the ground. Small holes are visible in the soil. Tracks of a fox are visible around one of the excavated holes, along with the remaining earth work of a worm. Most of the grassy soil is trampled by animals. A small animal track running east-west is visible in the grass.
105356: Tall, healthy grasses populate this area. There are a few brown-tipped blades of grass on the western side, but the grass seems to thrive on fertile soil to the east. Some areas on the eastern side become very soft, even swampy. Thick, dark-green bushes grows to the north.
105357: A natural shelter has formed between and under giant boulders leaning against each other. Being surrounded by rocks and the densest bramble thicket, this weed covered area is well-hidden from anyone passing through these wild borderlands. There is a small path between the bushes leading to a hill, and a murky tunnel which leads deeper into the ground.
105358: Inside the hill, the twisting tunnel opens up into a circular cavern. The ground is formed of a mixture of bedrock and loose gravel, and is littered by red stains, and some old and some apparently not so old bones. There are visible tracks on the floor, like something heavy has moved back and forth inside this underground tunnel complex. The steep walls are of pure rock, and contain small cracks and tiny ledges. Far above, the cavern walls seem to get closer to each other, before their faint shapes disappear into a total darkness.
105359:
A small grasshopper clings to a blade of grass, ready to spring.
A black crow flies low to the ground here, looking for carrion to eat.

The dense bushes are almost impenetrable here; they grow all about in this area. The sound of birds, safe from enemies, can be heard from the surrounding bramble bushes. The bramble bushes create an impassable wall of intertwined branches to the north and towards the east.
105360: A black wolf pads restlessly, looking for its next prey.

Small, yellow flowers cover this fertile field in large clusters. The hardy plants seem to have no trouble growing where other flowers would have a hard time surviving. To the north and east, the open field ends abruptly to a tall wall of bushes, and the landscape seems to rise a bit there. Wide grasslands, with flowers dispersing gradually, stretch to the west.
105361: A fallow deer is grazing peacefully here.

The lush grassland is covered by flowers and small bushes. Small animals seem to forage around here, as several piles of animal droppings and half-eaten berries are lying on the ground. There is also an entrance to what appears to be a rather large foxhole. To the north, the amount of bushes increases, and the terrain transforms into a thick, continuous mass of brush.
105362:
A large brown snake with black patches is coiled here.
A large brown snake with black patches is coiled here.

A large pack of foxes appears to have lived in this hole at some point in time but now it is empty. There are some rotting bones in the corner, perhaps left over from the foxes and whatever must have eaten them. There are slithering tracks covering the ground in here, appearing to be from a snake.
105363: The ground does not have the level of vegetation that can be seen in all other directions here. The lack of grass allows all of the pebbles and stones to be exposed on the ground. The grass is lush and green from the north, until it hits the sparse ground here. To the east brown weeds and green grasses continue despite the barren ground here.
105364: The plains here are quite high. The grasses seem moderately thick here, but begin to thin out toward the east. Towards the south some small animal holes are visible. To the west in the distance a river is visible. Dark green vegetation can be seen in the north.
105365:
A coloured game bird is visible in the vegetation, watching you warily.
A small grasshopper clings to a blade of grass, ready to spring.

Waist high, green grass blades growing with a lush glossy texture gradually thin out until they meet dry ground in the southern half of this field. Patches of grass and weeds continue on the sparse soil but rocks and stones cover the majority of the ground. To the east, an old gate stands in a narrow opening between dense bushes.
105366:
A giant termite is here, crushing skulls and bones.
A small termite is running around making strange sounds.
A small termite is running around making strange sounds.
A small termite is running around making strange sounds.
A small termite is running around making strange sounds.
A small termite is running around making strange sounds.
A beautiful and docile horse is standing here.

An old, abandoned-looking gate stands between two impassable thickets of vegetation. Lush growth embraces the gate from the both sides, long hay grows all around it, and the surface of its sturdy, wooden bars has been occupied by light-green moss. Nevertheless, the gate looks stout and strong.
105367:
Some roots lie here waiting to ensnare weary travellers.
A beautiful and docile horse is standing here.

A rugged clearing opens up inside the thicket. In the middle of this brushy area lies the remains of a huge, old tree, broken and fallen to the ground. Branches are withering away from age and lie scattered about, soon to be reclaimed by the nature. The stump of the tree, as well as thick roots, still stand firmly planted in the ground. Around the glade, a continuous, dense thicket extends to all directions.
105368: This fertile grove is covered with grass and some flowers, along with weeds of many types. There are long, slender grass-type weeds and squat, sprawling weeds low to the ground. Some of the weeds have needle sharp stickers, warning any travellers from trampling them. Countless willow trees are surrounding the grove, seemingly enjoying the moist soil and thriving in growth.
105369:
A shallow pond is here, tinted green with algae.
A black snake, with red markings, is lying here.

This bushy area is dominated by a large pool of cold water. Originating from a small tunnel beneath a big boulder, the water trickles forth creating a natural waterhole. In the outskirts of the water, reed-like grass grows first in clusters as high as a man, creating excellent cover for smaller animals to nest in, and then transforms into a dense, unfathomable shrubbery.
105370:
A half-decayed corpse of a goblin lies rotting on the ground.
A moderately sized copperhead snake is here.

Water drips from all around in this wet, humid pit. There are streams of water running along the ceiling of the cavern all around. There is a light underground stream running along the bottom of the pit, draining the water that collects from all around.
105371: Roots intertwine with the hard earthen walls inside this hollowed out trunk. The smell of rotting wood and vegetation intermingled with the musty smell of earth fills the humid, hollow cavern. Evidence of wood-eating insects shows on the surface areas of the trunk.
105372: In the Shade of a Brushwood
A beautiful and docile horse is standing here.

Wide bushes, roots, and dense undergrowth have intertwined together, forming an impassable thicket that surrounds this small sanctuary. The ground is dominated by unorganized patches of dark green bushes, although they are less dense to the south where grass takes over. The soil looks rather fertile; small patches of yellow flowers spring here and there between the bushes.
105373: A large rabbit looks peacefully at you, ready to dart away.

These barren fields hold little support for anything except low grass. The soil here seems to be sandy and dry. To the northeast, the view is partially obscured by high stands of what looks to be reeds. Green plains stretch out to the east and west, while to the south, giant bushes block the way forward.
105374: Light green grass covers this field. There are a few wild flowers growing in the northern part of this field but for the most part it is only grass. Being that the light green grass is the dominant feature here, the field has an overall single colour of green to it.
105375:
A small and tough weed grows here.
A fallow deer is grazing peacefully here.

Grass is growing in the northern and the western portions of this field, while a dense wall of dark-green vegetation dominates the area to the south and east. Weeds of many types are growing here, thriving in the fertile soil and plentiful sunlight.
105376: This field is covered with meadow plants of many types. There are wheat grasses mixed with regular grass, with waist high weeds. Tall dandelions are also growing in the field. This ground is somewhat higher than the fields in all other directions.
105377: Standing on a large field of green grass, there are no topical marks whatsoever. The ground is dotted with occasional clusters of taller grass. To the south and west the field stretches out seemingly forever. To the north the view is obstructed by taller, reed-like grasses. The sound of open water can be heard from the east.
105378: Several small rocks protrude out of the ground in this bleak, barren field where little else but grass and low bushes grow, bending and hugging the land under the pressure of the cold, harsh wind. High grass and untamed, continuous thicket of willows and other small trees border this area to the west and south. The ground appears more fertile to the north and east.
105379: Stretching all across the land like a blanket, a sea of grass covers the area here. The grass continues to the east where it is met by brush which gradually takes over the horizon. A deep and rather sweet smell rises from the ground. A few bumblebees hover over some wildflowers nearby.
105380: High, reed-like clusters of dark green grass cover the land, giving protection to various rodents that inhabit this area from the frequent winds. Moist and soft ground exhibits evidence of some rat prints, it seems larger animals also visit these fields. Grasslands dominate the landscape in every direction but west, where a solid wall of brushwood blocks the way.
105381: The soil lying under these grasslands is very moist and fertile. Water trickles in a small brook from the west, having somehow found its way through the impassable-looking thicket that stands there. Animal tracks can be seen on the ground and this place looks well-travelled. The brook continues its way to the south, bending around several large stones, before disappearing into a reed- filled swamp. The sound of running water fills the air.
105382: A garden snake slithers harmlessly here.

Occasional bushes that cover this otherwise grass-dominated landscape slowly wave in the wind. The sweet and gentle smell of flowers fills the air. Majestic plains continue to the west, yet dark green brush begins to take over the grasslands to the east. A sinister-looking bog opens up to the south, blocking all travelling there.
105383: A furious, wild dog is here, snarling and growling.

Small evergreen bushes spot the landscape and slowly flow into a dense thicket to the north. Strangely, hardly any grass covers the sandy yellow coloured earth and hoof prints mark the ground. Grasslands go on to the west farther than eyes can see. To the south, the terrain transforms into a deceptive swamp.
105384: The grass around here is low and burnt yellow by the sun, lacking the necessary moisture. At places where the dry soil is exposed, small cracks of contraction are visible. A sun-bleached skeleton of some large animal lies on the ground, with most of its bones intact. Grass has already started to grow through the rib-bones, soon hiding the skeleton from view.
105385: An Ant Hill under the Pine Trees
A colony of red ants is here. The ants seem to ignore you.

Among the surrounding grassland rises a small clump of tall pines consisting of no more than ten trees. The ground underneath is layered with old needles, pieces of dry branches, and thin slices of brown bark, which together form a natural carpet. In the centre of the clump, stacked against a tall pine, resides a huge ant-hill. The hill is over five feet high, consisting mostly of dry brown needles, earth, and some sand.
105386: The huge expanse of endless green grass continues in every direction except north, where it is broken by the silhouettes of small jagged hills. Long grass growing all around is laying near the ground, probably the result of strong winds blowing across the plain. Winds also bring sweet scents of flowering plants mixed with the smell of fresh grass and moist earth.
105387:
A young filly is just learning to walk.
A young colt is frolicking playfully.
A wild mare is watching you warily.
A wild mare is watching you warily.
A wild mare is watching you warily.

Many bright, fragrant wildflowers push up from the meadow covered in two-feet high grass, livening it up. Even though the grass is dark green and looks strong and healthy, indicating fertile soil, no trees nor any plants higher than a man grow here. Long honeysuckle branches hanging over the grass give the meadow a distinct sweet smell, which also attracts numerous bees during summer months.
105388: Even though no flowing water is visible, the soil here is moist and squishy. Saturated with water throughout most of the year, the meadow has a large variety of different grasses and herbs which prosper in these conditions. The meadow is the home and breeding ground for numerous different birds, who have easy access to food and good nesting places.
105389: This huge meadow of lush green grass would make good farmland, as the soil is fertile and moist. Some large animals must have grazed here, judging by the grass which at places lies chewed down and trampled. To the north and east the meadows continue, whereas to the south the ground rises abruptly to the top of a rugged hillock.
105390: A placid pond is here, inviting you to take a refreshing drink.

Eventhough the tall grass growing here is bent down by frequent winds rushing along the steep ridge to the south, the grass is still particulary thick and healthy. A small pond has formed to the plains, collecting water from the areas above, and providing enough watersupply to all fauna and flora around here. Bubbling sounds of water are mixed with quiet splashes, which are probably made by small fish rocketing out of the pond.
105391: The ground is covered with lush flowering grass and lowers slightly to the west and south, where the vegetation is dominated by wetland plants, and terrain transforms gradually to a dangerous-looking bog, too deceptive to be entered safely. Some stunted rowan trees growing on higher places are the only tall objects here, forming harder islets in the muddy and soft ground. Evergreen ivy plants climb on the trees, almost hiding their barks under thick layer of leaves and stems.
105392: The rolling moorland with yellow, sparse grass slightly slopes downwards to the east, dotted with numerous bushes and shrubs, but no trees grow in this barren soil. Interspersed with the coarse grass are tufts of purple heather, which colour the otherwise bleak land. Stronger winds pick up gritty dust and throw it in the air, making travelling unpleasant.
105393: Rolling Moors next to a Steep Hillside

The rolling moors of lush, green grass have traces of ancient habitation; some irregular mounds with simple stone monuments are visible amidts the vegetation. A straight line of old and majestic ash trees crosses the moors. Elsewhere, the landscape is dotted with ancient oak trees marking old vantage points. Towards the north a steep side of knoll blocks the path. There seem to be some deep cracks a bit higher up in the rockface, large enough for a man to hide in. The moor below that steep rockface is very dark, rotten, and exudes a foul stench.
105394: A sandy slope leads into a dry valley in the east which seems to have been formed by flowing water. Various colours of limestone are revealed on the rough walls at either side of the riverbed, which are high and impossible to climb. The dry bottom is covered with pebbles of different sizes interspersed with low grass. Small, crippled trees cling to the crumbling limestone, struggling to survive on the almost vertical walls of stone.
105395: The old, dry riverbed cutting through the ground in an east-west direction splits the surrounding plains into two. Thorny bushes growing on the southern side are replaced with smooth grassland in the north. Water that eroded through the layers of limestone is now gone, leaving the gully dry. Even though no green plants have rooted on the steep sides, a layer of low grass is growing on the bottom.
105396: The ancient, dry riverbed makes a turn here, going from west to south. Rocky walls rise high on either side, giving no handholds for climbing up. The bottom, which was once filled with clear water, is now just a sandy trail, marked with rounded pebbles and occasional small shrubs. Faint trails of snakes in the sand and cries of birds high up are the only indications of wildlife in this lone place.
105397: Dead End of an Old Riverbed

An emaciated warg, half-mad with hunger, is here.
An emaciated warg, half-mad with hunger, is here.
An emaciated warg, half-mad with hunger, is here.

The ancient riverbed cutting through the soft rock in the north suddenly ends here, leaving only looming walls of rock on every side. The water, which once poured from an underwater cave, is long gone, and huge boulders from the rocky walls have blocked the way down completely. The rocks and small pebbles are round and smooth, worn by the water rushing by in the distant past.
105398: The landscape here consists mostly of rolling grasslands which curve upwards and finally level in the south. Some stunted firs peep out from amid the thick green foliage growing on the slope, struggling to survive. The alternating vegetation consists mainly of tough weeds and grasses which are replaced with thorny bushes in the east.
105399: Rolling grasslands suddenly end with a thorny thicket in the east. The dense brush growing in a straight line is twice as tall as a grown man, making passage in this direction hard. Thorns and sharp, dry branches hinder movement, scratching travellers. Foliage has moved high up towards the sun, leaving lower branches without leaves. A slightly musty smell surrounds the damp darkness in the heart of the brush.
105400: The bushes that flourish to the south have grown to the very edge of this valley and some of the smaller plants even cling to the face of the cliff in an attempt to gather light. The plants look as if they may have been planted in times past to act as a wind barrier, but have now grown high and dense, making passage impossible to the east and south, whereas the passage to the north is blocked by the vertical walls of the valley.
105401: The damp, marshy ground carries many marks of animal feet both upon the short grass and amid the clusters of tough weeds covering the ground. Occasionally small rivulets wind through the grass, feeding little green-scummed pools. To the west the land drops slightly and grasses give way to sedges and reeds.
105402: The plains are split by a small valley, which runs from north to south. Even though the valley is not deep and only a small stream runs along its bottom, it looks like a scar in the earth, separating the vegetation. The western side of the valley is bordered by reeds and ferns growing on wet and muddy ground, while grasses and brush cover the drier ground in the east.
105403: The valley runs in a straight line from north to south, like being cut with an enormous knife into the earth. It continues towards the horizon in the north, but ends in the south where the small stream on the bottom suddenly dissappears under rocks. Tones of brown dominate in the west where the plains are wet and muddy, while green-grey coloured grasses grow east of the crevice where the ground is more sandy and drier.
105404: The fields are clothed thickly with heather, with their tiny flowers giving purple tint to the plains even during the wintertime. Little patches of low grass struggle their last match, but the heather has won. It is virtually everywhere, even pushing up from the barren soil beneath the rocks in the north, where the plains suddenly stop. In the west, however, the heather is gradually replaced with wetland plants.
105405: The ground here is quite wet, but the vegetation looks dull and small. Besides the clusters of low heather and moss only a few crippled alders are scattered around. Barks of the trees are shaded in brown and black tones, and only a few of their branches have leaves. Most of the plants are growing atop of their dead relatives, forming soft springy layers on the ground. Farther to the west, the plain ends abruptly to a continuous wall of brush.
105406: A placid pond is here, inviting you to take a refreshing drink.

A small pond hides in a thicket of willow trees. Its cold water is clear and fresh, yet no plants grow along its sandy bottom. The shores are flanked with heather, which covers the surrounding plains with uniform carpet. The quietness of the pond is occasionally disturbed by the noises of small animals quickly flitting away and hiding among the heather.
105407: The plains stretch out for miles in every direction, with only a very few changes in the landscape. A carpet of heather interspersed with low-growing shrubs covers the ground, concealing shallow fox holes and pitfalls. Occasional granite boulders, polished by the rain and wind, are half-hidden among taller shrubs, which also give shelter to small animals.
105408: The hard ground is overgrown with thorny bushes and tough weeds, all coloured in grey-green to brown tones. A few patches of brown grass struggle in the shadows of smaller bushes, but the thorny weeds are taking up all the nourishment from the soil, leaving nothing for smaller plants. To the east the hedges grow denser and denser until they finally block the way, but it might be possible to clear a path through the tangle in the west.
105409:
A giant, strange looking green fungus is here, ready to devour you in seconds.
A huge black fungus is here, exuding a foul stench.
A huge black fungus is here, exuding a foul stench.

The small passage in between the thick thorns is easy to follow, but thriving bushes in the east and west threaten to close the way soon. Bigger bushes have reached the size of trees, and in east and west their branches are interwoven with each other, making passage impossible. The damp air is filled with the smell of rotting wood and the only sound is the rustling of the wind in the thorns.
105410:
A bear cub is here, looking around for something to play with.
A bear cub is here, looking around for something to play with.
A big, brown, angry-looking bear is here.
A big, brown, angry-looking bear is here.

A narrow tunnel leads steeply down into a small, earthy cave. Tiny bones lie scattered on the ground, and the penetrating smell of animal excrement emenating from the darkest corner is mixed with the smell of moist earth. Fresh clawprints are clearly visible on the sandy ground, leading in both directions.
105411:
An ancient fungus smothers the boulders.
An ancient fungus smothers the boulders.

Thorny bushes dominate the vegetation, spreading over the fields. Most other plants have given up the fight for space and only a few patches of low brown grass struggle to survive. Concealed beneath the thick vegetation, a few weathered boulders are half-hidden under a soft layer of moss. To the west the density of bushes increases and their branches are interwoven with each other, making any movement through the brush difficult, whereas it might be possible to open a way through the hedge in the east.
105412:
Some cereals that look like wheat are lying here.
A large eagle soars above you.

The crops of a long-gone farmer are still growing, but the once well-tended fields are now partially overgrown with wild weeds and grasses. In the west the thorny hedge that once protected the fields from winds sweeping across the plains has grown high, making passage in this direction seemingly impossible. Low stone walls surrounding the fields in other sides have decayed with age and are covered with a layer of moss.
105413:
The corpse of a sleuthing orc is lying here.
The corpse of a sleuthing orc is lying here.

A small village that once stood here has long been abandoned. Nature has started claiming back the land: low walls are all that remain of formerly taller buildings, barely standing out amid the brush that flourishes everywhere. Streets connecting the ruins are covered with creeping grass interspersed with occasional loose stones peeking out from under the overgrowth.
105414:
A well-fed cow stands here chewing her cud listlessly.
A well-fed cow stands here chewing her cud listlessly.

Most of the orchard has been cut down by axes, with only straight lines of stumps remaining. In the southern part some of the old and gnarled apple trees are still standing, but their trunks are cracked from bearing too much fruit. Crippled pines and other conifers have started to replace the fruit trees at the eastern side, and towards the dark line of brush looming to the west the trees also fade, giving way to woody, dark bushes.
105415:
The corpse of an old bull is lying here.
A large thorny branched shrub is growing here.
On the shrub, there are three piles of blackberries.

The small valley is occupied and surrounded by thick, impenetrable bushes. Shrubs of blackberries grow around the thickets, holding the soil and small pebbles in place with their roots, but elsewhere in the valley the lower vegetation has been suffocated by the tall, twelve feet high thickets. During the day time, the light passing through the high plants makes shadows dance on the ground as the leaves move in the wind.
105416: A dense carpet of blue flowers dip their heads in the breeze.

Amid the plains of green grass is a clump of sparse beech trees, looking old and ageless. The ground around the trees is covered with a thick carpet of bluebells, so dense that they leave almost no room for any other plants. In the spring, when the flowers bloom, bees will come here to collect their first nectar. Meandering paths around the trees and small droppings on the ground indicate that the area is populated with little animals.
105417: The plains to the west and south are slowly turning into a forest. Sparse trees shade the plains, and a dark line of a forest is visible to the north-east. The grass under the trees is green and healthy, protected from harsh sunlight which dries the vegetation in open plains.
105418: A large eagle soars above you.

The grass on the fields around the village is lush and green, concealing rich soil underneath. Even though the crops are mostly replaced with wild weeds, they sometimes still push up through the lower grass. Around the long-abandoned ruins in the west runs a low stone wall that harsh sun and pouring rain have worn even lower. A very faint footpath leads from the ruins to the south, towards a larger trail.
105420: A trampled path surrounded by high grass and a few bushes follows the course of a small brook. The muddy brown water flows slowly, covered by a layer of green and yellow algae prospering in it. In the east the path turns away from the brook and heads towards the line of forest visible near the horizon.
105421: A narrow, barely visible trail winds across the plains, twisting and turning to find a path among thornbushes and high grass. The trail is rarely used, but it still offers a less tiring route than wading through the surrounding vegetation. On rare occasions small items like a broken arrowhead can be found among the strip of grass fringing the trail.
105422: A squirrel scampers around here, looking for nuts from the trees.

A giant fir tree towers above the forest, its magnificent crown soaring high above in the sky. Its trunk is thick and knobby, indicating the tree's age, yet the upper branches look young and fresh. Strong branches at regular intervals form a natural spiral staircase around the trunk, and looking up, a wooden platform is visible resting on upper branches.
105423: The woodland area is sparsely populated with young firs and tall pines, which have filled the forest floor with a soft carpet of thorns. The forest gets denser to the east but opens up into plains to the west, where the trees suddenly end. To the north and south the light forest continues, however in the north the conifers are replaced with alders and other hardwood.
105424: A few scattered alders with dark grey barks and white beeches with black markings grow on a slope gently rising eastwards. The trees are sparse, with wild grasses and ferns growing around them. In the north, where the ground gets rockier, the trees disappear completely, giving way to low yellowish grass. To the west, however, the slope suddenly ends with a cliff too deep to descend.
105425: The rocky plateau in the north and east suddenly falls off at a cliff in the west. The sheer face of rock drops vertically from the ledge, offering almost no support for climbing down. Forty feet below a grassy slope spreads out to the horizon, broken by the silhouettes of a few pines. Heading northwards a small trail seeks path among the massive boulders lying on the ground.
105426: The rocky field is covered by innumerable small rocks and few larger boulders. The stones are fringed with dense profusions of heather and gorse, which are the only plants in the area besides some stunted mountain pines. To the west, the ground slopes slightly downwards, where heather is replaced with clumps of brownish grass growing amid the scattered rubble. To the north a dark line of a trail running across the plateau is visible.
105427:
Clusters of slender stems and tall leaves thrive in the mud and shallows.
A mewlip is here, faintly wailing at you.
A mewlip is here, faintly wailing at you.
A green frog is here, hopping around.
A green frog is here, hopping around.
A swarm of mosquitoes is here, humming around you.

Huge cattails have replaced all other plants in this swampy area, reaching out of low-looking water and thick, black mud. At the end of cattails' strong stems are brown cigar-shaped catkins, which are grouped with tall sword-like leaves. The swamp continues to the north and west, while the other directions seem to lead to drier places. The air is filled with the sounds of small insects and chorus of frogs.
105428: A meadow full of thick, rusting grass has turned into a wet, foul bog a while ago. Water has collected in lower parts of the meadow, and swampholes seem to be somewhat of a danger below the stinking, decaying surface of old vegetation. One of these patches seems particularly large, yet also even more foul than the others.
105429:
A large leech is moving close to you, searching for blood.
A large leech is moving close to you, searching for blood.

The ground is covered with a thick layer of moss and lichen forming a deceivingly stable-looking green and brown carpet. Underneath the layer, however, is concealed soft mud, ready to suck in the legs of uncautious travellers. Here and there grow clusters of small plants, looking sick and barely alive. The air is filled with the noises of myriads of different small insects, and from time to time bubbling sounds can be heard from the ground.
105430: It is hard to tell if the surroundings consist of murky water or dense mud and bog; it is probably something in between. In some places the water is so liquid that you are forced to swim. The deeper you dive down, the more liquid the mud seems to become.
105431: Down here, it is a bit easier to swim than higher above, but the surroundings still consist of a very tenacious foul liquid. Soil, old roots, rotten grasses, and other undefined parts of mud and bog make up this swamphole, in which you can more feel than see your surroundings.
105432: The water and mud around are too dense to see anything at all. You are lost and cannot find your way back, even knowing what is up and what is down is a very hard task in this dense, foul bog. The only chance seems swimming towards what might be upwards - and hope.
105433: The remains of a clump of roots lie here in a heap of rotting compost.

The water does not seem that deep here but the ground consists of very soft mud and bog, so actually standing or walking on it is quite hard. The ceiling becomes somewhat higher and is covered completely in hanging, black roots. Everything around, even the soil itself, seems to exude a strong smell of decay.
105434: Some roots lie here waiting to ensnare weary travellers.

Very dark, muddy water has collected here and fills the tunnel to a larger part. From all around thin nets of roots hang into the water, while the soil in the walls feels very soft. So soft that a collapse of entire portions of them does not seem that unlikely.
105435: Dark Water in a Dripping Tunnel

The dark, putrid water seems to lie under the cover of dark whisps of cold mist. The same mist seems to hang everywhere: below the ceiling covered by roots, as well as around the soft, wet walls of the dark and stinking soil. Drops of dirty water constantly drop from the tips of roots and splash into the surface of the still, stinking water, like drops of corrupted rain.
105436: A Stinking Tunnel Overgrown with Fungi

A deeply black, oddly shaped cloud of mist has gathered here.
A cold shroud of dark grey mist covers the ground.

The area is much drier here than to the west, yet the soil is still quite wet. Countless fungi have started to grow in the dark down here and cover the walls as well as the floor. Most of these fungi are white but others are also pitch black. Here and there, a few dead roots hang into the tunnel and provide a ground for the patches of small, white fungi with a unusually pointed hat.
105437: Some roots lie here waiting to ensnare weary travellers.

The air is still filled with foulness and around are still patches of fungi, rotting roots, and corrupted soil, but there is also a hint of fresher air. The area here ascends quite steeply from the dark water in the west and becomes a very easy climb at the narrow cavern's end towards the east.
105439: A Foul, Shallow Pond of Mud

The corpse of a tentacled beast is lying here.
A deeply black, oddly shaped cloud of mist has gathered here.
A deeply black, oddly shaped cloud of mist has gathered here.

What first seems to be a pond turns out to be mostly shallow, a few deeper holes that left aside. The entire pond smells of rot and decay and once in a while a bubble of gas breaks open on the black surface. Decaying things of all kinds are rotting in the corrupted water and fill the air of this cave with their choking stench.
105440:
The remains of a clump of roots lie here in a heap of rotting compost.
A skeleton of some humanoid lies in the dust.

The water here is very foul and rotten. It stinks and is more mud than water and you have a feeling as if the mud or unseen hands would try to pull you down. The rather liquid mud seems to become even fouler and much more treacherous to the east.
105441: The mud has a deadly drag downwards and it even feels as if some invisible hands were grabbing your feet, pulling you downwards. The extremely foul air makes you choke and shortly after your mouth fills with the stinking mud, your lungs follow, and you suffocate.
105442: The air is cold in this tunnel, but all the shimmering ice that has formed along the walls seems not to belong here. The dirty crystals of frozen moisture, growing only on the wall near the tunnel's western end, should have melted, as the tunnel towards the east is still too warm for ice to form. Something towards the west must make them persist.
105443: A small cluster of clover grows here.

The low, green grass that covers the ground is lush and soft, with occasional patches of red and white clover giving it a mottled look. The soil underneath is black and fertile, as visible from molehills, which frequently rise above underground burrows. In the west the ground gradually slopes up, with some small hillocks looking over the surroundings, whereas in all other directions the plains continue.
105444:
An erect shrub with green pinnate leaves is growing here.
A low shrub with bright green, oblong leaves is growing here.
Scattered in and on the shrub, there are two piles of blueberries.

Many small, stony hillocks are grouped together in the plains, looking remarkably similar. Among the moss-covered rocks on the sides of some hillocks grow small blueberry shrubs, whereas the others are covered with dried stems of wild raspberry. Dried droppings on the ground testify that some small animals must have passed through here.
105445: Thorny bushes that spread over the grassland are easy to bypass at daylight, growing five to ten feet apart. Nevertheless, should a careless traveller run into one of the bushes, the thorns stick to clothing and tear skin, making it much harder to advance in low light. The brushland continues to the west, where the bushes are starting to grow back after suffering in a recent fire.
105446: Coaled and blackened stumps of trees that once grew here are the only signs of the fire. Brush has started to grow back and has hidden the wounds caused to nature. Frequent cries rising from scattered bushes indicate that even birds have started to claim back their old nesting spots. The effects of the fire are more evident in the north, whereas the brush gets thicker and more healthy in the west.
105447: The land here is completely overgrown with twisted, dark-green bushes, some serving as a safe nesting place to various small birds. To the north, the brush becomes thicker and taller, covering the horizon. Never-ending grasslands stretch all the way west.
105448: A carpet of green grass covers the land here, prevailing over other vegetation. A lonely twisted tree bends to the ground, making a whistling and howling sound as wind passes through its leaves and branches. A few blue wild flowers dot the ground around the tree, thriving in its shadows.
105449:
A squirrel scampers around here, looking for nuts from the trees.
A squirrel scampers around here, looking for nuts from the trees.
A small grasshopper clings to a blade of grass, ready to spring.

The area here is covered by waist-high bushes, stretching their vines over the grass in an eternal fight for sunlight. This is truly a place where nature thrives. The brush gets too dense to pass through, to the east.
105450: A fire must have raged here long ago, yet nature has started to regenerate. Fresh grass is growing on the now cracked and burnt ground and around blackened tree trunks young saplings have sprouted. Once thick brush is now lying near the ground, coaled and scorched by the fire, making passage through the burnt land harder.
105451: Several huge boulders are sprinkled across the grass-covered plain and are now half sunk into the soil. Even though winds and pounding rain have eroded the stones, it is evident that they were once hewn into rectangular blocks. The grasslands stretch for miles in every direction besides north, where a stone quarry opens up.
105452: There is little vegetation in the sand. Most of the cutting weed that once grew here has given up the fight in barren soil and has turned reddish brown. On the ground lie dry, grey straws, still holding on to the soil with their dead roots. Everything is dry and desolate, and scattered pieces of sandy wood and small, smooth stones give it even more lifeless look.
105453: The vegetation here continues its never-ending struggle for life, the only survivors being low bushes and tufts of dark grey grass hiding in the shadows of stunted pines. The plants are crawling near the ground, reaching out for every little drop of water. The barren sandy soil is covered by a number of footprints of little creatures, their tracks crossing each other and running in zigzag, suddenly ending in small burrows.
105454: The rolling ground is covered by low, yet thick grass, dotted with occasional wild flowers. Some small knolls rise above the surroundings, providing natural vantage points. From atop those knolls, an outline of a building is visible in the north-west, whereas on other sides the plains continue without much changes.
105455: A Small Stream in the High Grass

A small, clear stream swiftly makes its way from north to south through the grasslands, almost knee-deep at its deepest point but narrow enough to jump over.
