Green weeds growing at the bottom of the stream are clearly visible through the water. Soft and sticky mud on either side of the stream is covered with footprints of numerous animals, their tracks leading around the riverside trees to lush grasslands stretching to the horizon on all sides.
105456: A pack horse (Rood) is standing here, ridden by you.

A massive oak tree overlooks the flat landscape of the lush meadow from high above. Its almost eight-feet wide trunk is covered by a thick dark-brown bark, hardened with ages. The unreachable lower branches start high above, providing almost no support for climbing up. The nesting spots that the hollow trunk and huge branches provide are well hidden from view. Sloping ground around the tree is covered with a layer of rusty-coloured dead leaves and strewn with greyish- brown acorns.
105457:
An apple tree with bright green leaves grows here.
On the tree's branches are two apples.

A faint footpath wanders through the fields in a north-south direction, turning and twisting to avoid larger clumps of brush. The path is overgrown with low, brown-stained grass and its sides are covered with various shrubs of different sizes. At the south end of the path stands an old and gnarled apple tree, stretching its huge moss-covered branches towards the sky. The thick dark-brown bark around the trunk is cracked and some smaller plants have rooted there.
105458: In contrast to the rich grasslands to the west, the hardy weeds here are sparse and grow in tufts, exposing poor soil and small stones. To the east the grass grows thinner and the ground gets more rocky and barren as it slowly rises. Occasional stronger winds pick up dirt and grit, making breathing harder.
105460: A Trail in the Field of Flowers

An emaciated warg, half-mad with hunger, is here.
An emaciated warg, half-mad with hunger, is here.
An emaciated warg, half-mad with hunger, is here.

The trail runs through a colourful field, stretching out from west to east. Glimpses of green and yellow grass can be rarely seen in the variety of wild flowers growing in different colours and sizes. Most noticeable are the cornflowers, with their intense blue heads, and foxgloves, which are in both white and purple colour. Occasional yellow coneflowers reach out for the sun, standing tall above all other plants.
105461: An Abandoned Campsite along a Trail

A small circle of blackened stones have been placed in front of a decaying hut north of the trail. Tall grass around the fireplace almost completely hides a few larger logs sitting firmly on the ground. Once a favoured place to rest during the night, this camp seems to get little use now. The trail continues to the west and east, and a small footpath leads into the vast fields of grass southwards.
105462: A fat rabbit is here, chewing on some grass.

The trail bends to the north and east here, twisting to stay on higher ground. It is easy to follow and provides sure footing, though the overgrowth slows progress. The trail is flanked with blackberry vines and other thorny shrubs, and covered by thick grass. A small hut to the east contrasts sharply to the wide plains stretching to all other sides as far as the eye can see.
105463: A short evergreen plant, with slightly bluish needles, grows here.

Over the green grasslands rises a steep, grey hill, strewn with stunted juniper bushes which have been twisted and bent by raging winds. On the south side near the highest point of the hill the bushes thicken, forming a dense tangle. Around the foot of the hill and for many miles around there are no junipers to be seen, as if they all moved together to the hill.
105464: The worn path makes a long bend here, staying close to the high walls of the stronghold in the north-west. To the west the trail heads towards the gate in the wall, but to the north it soon disappears among the plains. Some rough boulders stand next to the path, but whoever placed them there must have lost interest, as they are half-sunken into the soil and fringed with low shrubs.
105465: In Front of a Wooden Gate

Atop of a height in the north stands an old, relatively massive structure encircled with a wall. It seems like a fortified farmhouse or a small outpost. The passing time has left its traces, and a plaque that had been fixed to the wall has fallen down long ago. The only visible entrance to the simple stronghold is an old gate made of thick hardwood planks, fastened together by wrought iron studs. In the wall's western part, a small tower rises above the fort, giving good overview of the gate and surrounding plains. The upper part of the tower was once made of wood and has toppled long ago, now covered by vegetation.
105466: The gently rolling plains here are lonely and dun-coloured, stretching as far as the eye can see in most directions, with only occasional trees breaking up the monotony of the land. In the west, however, an overgrown trail runs down a debris-strewn slope to an old stone quarry.
105467: Some small rocks have been piled into a mound here.

In the east side of a hill is an old stone quarry. Large chunks of granite have been taken out of the hill and transported away, leaving only sheer walls with drilling holes and other quarrying marks behind. The steep hill-faces with ferns and brambles growing in their niches encompass the quarry to the north, west, and south. In the east, a long inclined ramp with a grade gentle enough to haul the stones leads out of the quarry.
105468:
A half-decayed corpse of a goblin lies rotting on the ground.
A moderately sized copperhead snake is here.

The room here is built into a natural cave, probably by the miners to keep their tools and supplies. Some broken pieces of old mining equipment and rotten ropes are still scattered on the floor, but most of it has been rendered useless by time. The air is damp, and the heavy scent of mould and rotten wood is mixed with the smell of moist earth. An old door in the south leads out of the room.
105469:
A large pile of boulders is sitting here, probably debris from a rockslide.
A sprawling green bush of stinging nettle grows here.

Rolling grasslands give way to a barren slope rising steadily until it meets a sheer cliff towering above in the east. The vertical wall rises almost forty feet, providing no support for climbing up. Fallen rocks and boulders lie scattered at the base of the cliff and the sound of a falling stone can be occasionally heard. High nettles seem to be the only plant thriving among the debris.
105470: A big, nasty vulture is sitting here, protecting its nest.

The lush meadows in the north and west suddenly end with a steep valley in the south and a sheer cliff in the east. Rising almost forty feet above ground, the vertical wall looks impossible to scale. The ground is filled with sharp rocks and small pebbles, dislogded from the cliff towering above.
105471: Overlooking a deep valley in the south, the grassy meadow spreads to the very edge of the almost vertical rock face. Rocky walls of the old riverbed are still smooth, offering no handholds for climbing down. In the north, however, the plains continue in all directions, covered with lush grass and dotted with occasional lone trees.
105472:
An emaciated warg, half-mad with hunger, is here.
An emaciated warg, half-mad with hunger, is here.
An emaciated warg, half-mad with hunger, is here.

Besides the tall grass, reaching up to man's waist, nothing can be seen in a northerly direction. In the south, on the contrary, the meadow is suddenly cut off with a deep valley running in an east-west direction. A tiny fir tree stands just above the steep face of rock, watching over the ground below like a shadowy guardian.
105473: A Knoll in the Thick Grass

A sprawling green bush of stinging nettle grows here.
A pack horse (Rood) is standing here, ridden by you.

A little cluster of thorn trees marks the top of a low knoll. All of its sides are covered with huge granite boulders blocking the way up, only on the southern side the boulders have been parted just enough to make room for a small trail going up to the top. Man-high nettles grow among the rocks, interspersed with patches of wild raspberry.
105474: The shores of a small stream going through the meadow are filled with stumps of fallen trees sticking out of the mud. Trunks reaching across the water are covered with tooth marks of the creatures that cut down the trees. Near a bend where tree trunks, several large branches and some mud are piled up in a crude dam blocking the flow of water, saplings and green plants have sprouted. The dam is wide and strong enough to provide support for crossing the stream, though water forced out of its bed has turned surrounding areas into a bog.
105475: A shallow pond is here, tinted green with algae.

Tall willow trees separate a clear water pond from surrounding meadows and almost completely hide it from view. A small stream supplying the pond with fresh water gently slides through the plain from north-west. The slight slopes leading to the pond are covered with animal tracks, and seem to be quite slippery due to a mud and a wide blanket of old, fallen leaves. Bottom of the pond is covered with green and brown weeds growing on underwater flat stones, providing good hiding spots for smaller fish.
105476: A Huge Boulder in the Grass

A massive angular boulder of the size of a small house is resting in the high grass. Soft and moist green-coloured moss covers the boulder at the northern side while at the south side the plain time-worn rock is exposed. Natural steps formed on the eroded surface lead up to the top like a stairway. The ground near the boulder is overgrown with bramble and honeysuckle, giving way to green, rolling grasslands.
105477:
A small cluster of clover grows here.
A small cluster of clover grows here.

The fields are thickly covered with clover, which flourishes in the rich, fertile soil. Only occasional patches of lush, green grass and few higher bushes are mixed in, whereas white and red clover dominate everywhere else. In the summertime when the clover blooms, bees and other insects are attracted by the sweet-smelling nectar dripping from small flower-heads, but when the flowers wither, the insects also disappear.
105478: The soil here is moist and fertile, giving life to long, lush grass and occasional tall trees towering above the plains. The way east opens up to a deep quarry, with sheer unclimbable walls dropping down below, making it too difficult to traverse. To the south are bushes which are small and infrequent but begin to get denser, making passage in this direction harder. Intermingled with the bushes are scorched grasses and burnt twigs; evidence of a fire that must have raged south of here.
105479: The moist yet sandy soil here is surprisingly fertile, as it gives life to the lush vegetation. A wild mixture of foot high grass, flowers and rare bushes covers the land, taking advantage of some underground source of water. To the south, thick bushes overtake the terrain, blocking the view.
105480: The sea-like grasslands sway to and fro in the breeze. Sparsely growing clusters of bushes stand here and there, barely rising over the long, hair-like blades of grass. To the north, the ground slowly elevates towards a small hill.
105481: A clear spring babbles as cool water trickles out of the ground.

Thriving vegetation grows here due to the proximity of the small spring that bubbles out clear, cold water, excellent for drinking. Tracks of wild animals cover the wet, grass-covered soil around the water. Wide grassy plains extend to the horizon in the east.
105482:
A large thorny branched shrub is growing here.
On the shrub, there are a number of blackberries.

A tangle of thorny bushes interlaced by dry yellow grass makes this area barely passable, yet gives plenty of cover to the local fauna. Small patches, clear of brush, are blooming with flowers. To the south, thick brush continues, although not as dense. The brush is too thick to the west to pass through.
105483: A wild dog bares his yellow fangs at you.

A worn path cuts through the grasslands from the west to the east. As it approaches the stone wall of an ruined, fortified farm, the path turns to the south and runs alongside the wall for a while. Sitting atop a high cliff, the building's stone walls appear higher than they are. To the east, north, and south the grasslands continue, dotted with numerous trees and small hills.
105484: The faint grassy trail bends around a dried pine tree, heading north and east. The sides of the trail are covered with small tangled shrubs, not high enough to hinder the view. In the near distance the trail disappears from sight, almost indistinguishable from the wide plains stretching to all sides. The grasslands, dotted with numerous trees, slightly slope downward toward the west.
105485: A Faint Trail over a Hill

A faint, grassy trail runs over a small hill and continues to the west and south. The gently rising slopes are thickly clothed with green bushes, the only visible passage being the narrow trail. The western slope is covered with soft, thick grass and filled with pitfalls, making it hard to travel with any wheeled vehicle. Thorny shrubs guarding the trail are reaching out, trying to grab weary travellers.
105486: The rich vegetation west and north of here is gradually replaced with brown-stained low grass. Interspersed among the grass are patches of small, dry bushes and weeds. Most plants have given up the fight to survive in the barren soil consisting mainly of dry sand, with the remaining cutting weeds fighting for every little drop of water. The barren ground continues to the east.
105489:
A large thorny branched shrub is growing here.
On the shrub, there are three piles of blackberries.

Tall grasses grow densely together with large bushes. Sharp thorns, briars and brambles all strive for space and entwine together forming a thick mesh of foliage. The grass seems to be fighting a losing battle against the large bushes that dominate the immediate surroundings.
105490: Long, fertile grass grows everywhere. The tall stems grow in some places higher than a large man. A long-dead tree stands here, and in its rotten trunk a bird seems to have made a nest.
105491: The grass of the plains grows tall and strong. Green, gold and brown seem to have been the primary colours on Yavanna's palette. As far as the eye can see rolling plains stretch in all directions. From time to time, the top layer of the grass ripples gently on the open plains.
105492: The lush, verdant grass of the plain surrounds everything here. Hues of green, brown and gold dominate the view in all directions. Occasional rabbit holes and mole hills are the only signs of life in this secluded area, the only sound is the rustling of grass.
105493:
A stocky mountain mule is here, waiting to serve.
A boar cub is playing here, and exploring the wide world.

The trail winds its way west towards the Anduin and south through rolling plains. Weeds and grass threaten to take the trail back into natures grasp as the weeds creep across its edges. The vast plains flow like a sea of green and gold on each side, the tops of the grass undulating slowly like soft waves.
105494: Only the occasional stones lying along the borders of the trail reveal that this was once a well-travelled road. Now the trail looks abandoned and has been invaded by grass that covers the surrounding fields.
105495: Small valleys and hillocks slope up and down, lining the plain in an intricate drawing. In the valleys small downs covered by lush grass extend all around. A grassy trail lies to the north of the hillocks, and turns to the south east of here. The plain continues to the west, but to the south a silhouette of a larger structure resting on top of a low hill is outlined against the green grasslands.
105496: Some cereals that look like wheat are lying here.

The grass has grown wildly over the area. Several parts of the field are filled with wild cereal, their high ears making the travel a bit difficult, while in other areas of the pasture lush grass makes it easy and pleasant for a traveller to walk through. To the north a faint trail cuts the plain from east to west. The grassland continues in all other directions.
105497: The grass is high and thick providing the ideal food for the animals of the prairie. To the north a trail crosses the plain. To the west the ground rises gently, while to the east the pasture continues unaltered.
105498: The corpse of a wild ox is lying here.

A gentle slope covered with grass leads to an escarpment rising up to the north. The grass on this slope is unusually lush and, beneath it, small channels can be seen to furrow the ground, dug by rain running down the slope over time. Small holes are barely visible through the thick vegetation underfoot. A green pasture can be seen to the east, bordered by a small trail. South and west the plain continues uninterrupted.
105499: A low, many-branched shrub covers the ground here.

The barren land here is unnaturally flat, with only a few mottled trees towards the north, bordering the hill in that direction. The soil must have lost its fertility, as absolutely nothing grows within its bounds and the few trees that stand have no life flowing through their bark.
105500: The ground is unnaturally flat here, one can assume that someone took the time to level the terrain. The soil is loose and moist, perhaps because of the northern hill that partly shades these grounds. Although nothing is growing from the ground now, a razed house to the west gives way to the notion that this and the surrounding areas were once a small farming settlement.
105501:
A buck runs swiftly from place to place, looking about warily as it grazes.
A snake slithers towards you.

Wide patches of tall, reed-like grasses rise above the yellow coloured sandy ground, obscuring much of the view. The same kind of high grass can be seen to the south but the grass seems to open up both to the east and west. Here and there tiny trees and bushes struggle to survive.
105502: Long grasses are growing all over the plains here, drooping over from their own weight. A number of small evergreen bushes dot the gentle slope to the east, where a small hill rises over the horizon.
105503:
A small grasshopper clings to a blade of grass, ready to spring.
A small grasshopper clings to a blade of grass, ready to spring.

A flat hill barely rises amid the expanse of plains that stretch in every direction. Gold and green coloured bushes grow bountifully on the western slope, leaving few free spots for grass. To the east, a few miniature trees can be seen: a rare sight in this area.
105504: Several midget-sized trees barely rise over the grass covered landscape. To the west the ground rises slowly, coming to a peak at the top of the small knoll. Reaching the horizon to the south and east, the terrain looks monotonous, giving nothing to focus on.
105505: A sea of tall, lush grass which waves slighty with wind covers the ground completely. Small white flowers that reach out above the grass to catch every last sunray add colour and variety to the plains. Judging by the noises and small holes in the soil, the place is rich with small animals to which the lush grass is the perfect hideout.
105506: A placid pond is here, inviting you to take a refreshing drink.

A small pond is hidden in a thick grove of birches. The sandy bottom of the pond is clearly visible through the clear water and only a narrow strip of firm wet sand separates it from the trees. In contrast to the crippled trees in surrounding grasslands, the birches here look strong and healthy, and a lot of different wildflowers fringe the forest floor around their trunks.
105507: Rolling Plains by the Stone Wall

The walls of the farm in the east tower above the rolling plains, which blend with the horizon far away in a blue haze. Just next to the wall lies an old, dry pond that was once filled with deep water and probabaly fishes, but now only high grasses and thorny brambles flourish in the shade provided by the walled farm. Small weeds have even started to grow between the stones high up at the wall, as if trying to climb over to the other side.
105508:
A circular stone well has been built here.
An apple tree with bright green leaves grows here.
On the tree's branches are three apples.
An elven Marchwarden is here, vigilantly guarding Lothlorien's borders.
An elven Marchwarden is here, vigilantly guarding Lothlorien's borders.
An elven Marchwarden is here, vigilantly guarding Lothlorien's borders.
An elven Marchwarden is here, vigilantly guarding Lothlorien's borders.

A long desolation has taken its toll on what looks like the abandoned courtyard of once a strong farm. Mixed shrubs and trees have grown around the old well, concealing in the shade the chaos of the overturned tiles. A ruined arch stands to the south, possible remnant of a taller construction around a more imposing entrance. Its pillars are still sturdy enough to support the current crude gate.
105509:
A large skin is lying here.
A butcher knife is lying here.
A huge, poisonous spider is here.

Most of the masonry of this old building has crumbled away after centuries of wilderness assaults and is now scattered on the ground under a significant layer of organic decay. The northern wall and a pillar to the southeast still stand, while the rest has been more recently replaced by rough planks or bound dead branches.
105510: A wooden chest stands in the corner.

With the northern wall crumbled away and the eastern one collapsed over a larger pile of rubble outside, this part of the farm does not offer much shelter. Furthermore, the remaining sections are covered by a thick layer of black soot, turned into a dark crust by the passing of time. However, fallen trees have been laid on the northern foundations and lean on the top of the southern wall, their dead foliage forming a makeshift roof. Debris of masonry, decayed wood and soil partly cover the old floor tiles.
105511: A Ruin under a Wide Tree
A mass of dark green leaves clings to a wall.

Not nearly as ruined as the rest of the building, this room actually has a roof albeit in the form of the wide foliage of a tree. This oak has been spreading its roots under the floor, slowly reclaiming the place to nature. The rest of the structure is still upright, with a small niche in the southern wall and two stone blocks carved as benches and embedded in the foundations near the western window.
105512:
An elven scout stands here, blending in with the background.
Amdirion the Marchwarden, wielding a longsword, is standing here watching the surroundings.

The construction that once stood here is no more. The base of the walls may still exist, but as everything else has collapsed on top of them they are unlikely to be seen ever again from here. The resulting high heap of broken masonry is treacherous to walk over but provides a great view to the landscape around.
105513: A wooden chest stands in the corner.

Rays of sunlight pass through cracks in the walls during daytime, and a puddle of water formed on the earthen floor at the far end corner suggests that the roof is leaking water. Some rusty tools are hanging on a wall over a small bed, and another, larger bed is placed next to a tiny window. Blackened bits of wood lie scattered under a rusty iron pot suspended by a tripod. A trail passing through the plains can be seen from the window.
105514: A sparrow is flapping around on the ground.

From the top of this small hill, a tiny trail can be seen snaking from the north into the southern forest. The hill gradually descends to the west, until it meets the majestic Anduin. The healthy grass that covers this knoll rolls outwards to the east, creating a green carpet that fades out of view.
105515: The plain comes to an abrupt end here. After climbing in a gentle slope from the south, the grassland sinks to the north in a bush-covered escarpment. The bushes lining the top of the escarpment are too dense to move through; they rise to no great height, but their branches are interwoven to form a continuous, compact tangle. Low below to the north and to the east a trail can be seen, coming from the west.
105516: A hungry warg is standing here, ridden by Backdraft.

Sloping down in all directions, this grassy but rocky hill gives a panoramic view over the areas nearby. The Anduin can be seen far to the west, flowing from the north to the south through vast grasslands. The thick grass continues upwards to the east, blocking the view in that direction.
105517: In its travel across the plains, the trail turns here once more to go round a steep escarpment that raises to the west. Green pastures grow south while the trail continues to the east bordered by a deep ditch.
105518: This trail is faint and almost completely covered by grass. A deep muddy ditch borders the road to the north. The trail continues to the east and to the west. To the south the sea of grass continues endlessly.
105519: A boar cub is playing here, and exploring the wide world.

The trail comes from the banks of the river to the west and continues east towards Mirkwood. Possibly once used by traders, now the road is completely covered by grass and can hardly be discerned among the plain. The presence of a ditch to the north is the only evidence that people once worked in making this track.
105520: The trail is faint and hardly recognisable among the grass. The trail leads from the west and turns to the south here. It is bordered by a sparse line of trees to the north. To the east the ground is plain and grassy.
105521: A colourful butterfly is fluttering around here.

Man-high grass stretches in all directions in a sea of gold, green and brown. The slightly hypnotic nature of the undulating fronds and the calming hiss of the stems lightly brushing against each other, distracts from the fact this place is empty and isolated.
105522: A brown fox is here, looking for some rabbits to chew up.

The grass is thinner here and well-trodden. A trampled path leads northwards towards the ruins of an old building. The building looks quite derelict and the upper levels look to have fallen long ago, most of the wooden frames around the doors and windows look rotten. It appears that there are current inhabitants as there is a faint wisp of smoke coming from the inside. There is a wooden gate to the east that looks to be some kind of animal pen.
105523: A giant rat patters against you, squeaking maliciously.

Inside the building, broken objects scatter the floor; old furniture, broken jars and something that looks like the remains of a large animal. There is a faint, acrid smell in the air and some smoke can be seen slowly drifting from the cracks in the floor. Whole floor is covered by dust and litter, except a rectangular area near the door.
105524:
An uruk of the Morgundul tribe is here commanding his soldiers.
An orc-guard of the Morgundul is on patrol here.
An orc-guard of the Morgundul is on patrol here.
An orc-guard of the Morgundul is on patrol here.

Down here the air is cold and damp, and green mould and lichen are growing on the moist stone walls of the cellar. Parts of the walls are stained with a rusty red tinge, which looks like blood. One pair of shackles is hanging on the wall, the debris strewn on the floor around them indicate that they have been used recently.
105525:
A dented pail has been carelessly left here.
A wooden chest stands in the corner.

Several crude pallets line the walls here, with rough stained blankets strewn on top. A pail in the corner with a large wet stain around it suggests that it is being used as a makeshift waste bucket. This room is also quite damp, with small rivulets of water trickling down the walls.
105526:
The starving cow stands here looking for a patch of grass.
The starving cow stands here looking for a patch of grass.

The ground in this enclose is worn and only has small tufts of grass growing on the otherwise bare earth. There is a small trough half-filled with stagnant water. A pile of hay has been heaped in the corner, whether its use is as a bedding place for animals or as a compost is not obvious, for the ground here is covered in animal droppings. The only exit from this area is the gate to the west.
105527:
A placid pond is here, inviting you to take a refreshing drink.
A red-breasted mallard swims about, periodically upending to look for food.

Aquatic plants grow in abundance both in the water and around the edge of this small pond. The water looks cool and clean. Animal tracks lead from it in every direction. A hill to the north is visible above the swaying grass.
105528: Small flowers grow amidst lush, soft grasses here. Blue, pink and yellow spots break up the otherwise green pasture. Considering its short, almost well-tended appearance, it seems that this pasture is a popular grazing area for the local wildlife. The large meadow is surrounded by the tall grasses of the plain.
105529: The grass grows very tall and thick here, surrounding everything in an almost claustrophobic way. The landscape is filled by green-shaded grass moving in a slow fashion. To the west stands a hill, its peak poking through the grasses, and to the north the grass transforms into dense shrubbery; bushes, vines and branches tangling together forming a dense wall of mixed vegetation.
105530: A boar cub is playing here, and exploring the wide world.

From the top of this small hill the surrounding landscape can be seen spreading for miles all around. Mostly, the area is dominated by vast plains which extend to all directions like a huge, lush, verdant sea. To the north, a dense thicket stands in the middle of the otherwise open area.
105531: Tall grasses grow densely together here, creating an almost impenetrable wall of green- and brown-coloured vegetation. Newer grasses entwine themselves around the older ones, creating a maze-like effect and making it easy to lose sense of direction in this entangled labyrinth. Although giving an appearance of a soft and rolling blanket, the stems are tough and sharp, blocking all travelling to the south.
105532: The lush, green plains dominate the area continuing as gently flowing grass far to the west, and as bushy, tangled landscape to the east. To the north the ground is more rocky, and the plains descends down between boulders and small rocks, transforming into a narrow canyon.
105533:
A bee flies around here, collecting nectar from the flowers.
A robin is here, carrying small pieces of wood to its nest.

The plains flow in all directions here, lush green grass grows amongst the dry browns of last season. Thorny weeds grow amongst dainty flowers, concealing the dangerous thorns. An old nest lies here amongst the stems presumably from some small rodent long since deceased.
105534: A line of sparse trees borders the northern side of the trail. A steep rise leads to the plains north. To the west the ground sinks into a muddy ditch, while to the east lies the vast plain.
105535: A stocky mountain mule is here, waiting to serve.

A tall, verdant sea of grass sways gently on the plains coloured in all shades of green and gold. It is difficult to see in any direction as the grass stands so tall, but to the west the plain is cut by a steep and narrow canyon, and to the east the tall grass is changing into an impenetrable shrubbery.
105536: The trail comes from the west and turns here to the south. Turfs and debris cover the ground making the trail hardly visible, but it can be still travelled over easily. To the north, a thick group of trees is preventing a clear view to the plains behind. To the east a deep ditch runs along the road.
105537: Sharp Bend in a Deeply Cut Trail

The giant, mean looking earth beetle is sleeping here.
The wild ox seems ready to charge you.

The trail makes a sharp bend here to go around a high escarpment that prevents travel to the south and west. Bushes cover the steep slope of the escarpment and nearly block the trail itself. High earth walls surround the path to the north, blocking the view after a short distance. The uneven ground shows that the road is not often used. To the east the plain lowers and the trail seems to disappear, covered by the vegetation.
105538: Turn of a Deeply Cut Trail

The trail cuts the plain like a deep wound. The track is easy to follow, even in places that show disuse. The path comes from west and here it turns southwards. To the north the slope is too steep to climb, while to the east it seems possible to reach the plain above.
105539: Although it appears to have not been used in ages, this overgrown trail is easy to follow as its texture is quite different than the plains that it cuts through. It was probably once a very basic supply route, leading from the river Anduin, however it has not seen such use in quite some time. The brush on the south side of the trail is very dense, thwarting travel in that direction.
105540:
A large, loyal falcon is circling above.
A sparrow is flapping around on the ground.
The garden snake slithers harmlessly here.

Thin, green brush covers the heightened landscape here, almost completely shielding the ground from view. The brush becomes denser as the field slopes down towards the east and north, rendering travel in those directions impossible.
105541: A fallow deer is grazing peacefully here.

A group of trees grows along a trail giving some shelter from unwanted observers. The trail is covered by sand and gravel, and occasional tufts of grass and weed grow on it, indicating that this path is rarely used. The field around the road is covered by green, lush grass.
105586: A rabbit is here eyeing your presence warily.

The plain slopes toward the south, ending in a ditch which borders what once could have been a road. To the north a dense patch of shrubs can be seen. To the west the plain is dotted by a group of trees and to the east a thorny hedge crosses the plain.
105587: The terrain elevates steadily from a mossy ditch located to the south, through the peaceful and grassy plain, towards a wall of thorny brush to the north. The plains continue to the west. The thick, long wall of brush seems to prevent the travelling to the north. To the east, a steep and unstable slope can be seen.
105589:
A fallow deer is grazing peacefully here.
A stocky mountain mule is here, waiting to serve.

Short, dense bushes and rolling, dry grass cover the plains. The only signs of living creatures are tracks on the ground and some holes among the grass. Far to the west the bank of the Anduin is bordered by some trees. To the north a steep hill blocks the way, while plains continue to all the other directions.
105590: A wolf cub happily plays here.

The ground here is hard and the grass is dry. The benign influence of the Anduin does not reach this part of the plain. The signs of animals are rare and hard to find. To the west and north the vegetation is lusher. To the east and south the plain becomes barren.
105591: There is very little that would be of interest here. The grass is shorter, but it still looks basically the same as the rest of the vegetation in the plains. There are a few dull, dark grey rocks laying around.
105592: Tall stalks of grass wave in the wind, slightly browned by the sun that usually beats down upon the plains. To the north lies an ancient section of wall built by whatever peoples inhabited this land long ago. To the east and west the plains continue.
105593: A fallow deer is grazing peacefully here.
In sharp contrast to the surrounding grass, this bit of earth is completely bare. Some kind of trampling or some foul event has removed all the vegetation leaving the soil hard and smooth.
105594: The faint path coming from the west, turns here to the north and sinks in a bowl of grass that lies below the plain. To the south another gorge opens in the plain, showing that this part of the land is rich of springs and water.
105595:
The corpse of a boar is lying here.
A tiny spider is here, eating a tiny bug.

The plain here is crossed by a faint line that once could have been a path. It comes from the west and leads east towards Mirkwood. No signs of recent usage are visible, and it seems that the creatures that tracked this path are not using it anymore.
105596: A large hawk-like bird is here overlooking its territory.

The grass on these verdant plains grows thinner here, allowing various types of plants and flowers to populate this area. There is a large gorge to the west, while to the south the smoothly flowing plains transform into an entangled mess of bushes, grass, and other vegetation.
105597: Giant Kettle in a Wide Gorge
A worm is here slithering around.

The sides of this deep gorge, although rising high at a gentle rate, are almost circular in shape, giving the appearance of a bowl. The tall grass of the plains can be seen swaying all around the tops of the gully save to the south where an impenetrable-looking thicket grows. Rocks and stones litter the floor. Clearly visible near the centre of the ground is a strange dark hole; a faint echo of water dripping can be heard emanating from its dark depths.
105598: Rocks and boulders have fallen down from the steep faces of a gully, making the visibility to be very limited in this narrow passage; little is visible ahead as the huge boulders block the sight. What is still visible is the grass from the plains, as it sways gently far above, on the edges of the gully. The sides of the gorge look too steep to climb though, so it seems to be a choice of either pressing on or turning back.
105601:
The corpse of a yellow-grey prairie dog is lying here.
A sparrow is flapping around on the ground.

This patch of ground dips below the surrounding plains. The borders of the depression resemble the shape of a bowl. On the eastern slope some shelves of sand and rock border a small crack, just large enough to fit through.
105602: A wide, round area opens up inside the rock. The floor is smooth, level and covered by dust. In the eastern wall a niche has been carved out in the rock, and in the middle of this cavern some flat stones have been gathered into a circle, offering a comfortable-looking place to sit down and rest around a camp fire. In the northern wall two pillars have been carved around the steps of a staircase leading up. The air is still and warm.
105603: Niuldor the botanist is here looking around with grey eyes.

Cracks and fissures on the rocky wall form natural, dust-covered steps making it possible to climb between the cavern below and a narrow opening in the ceiling. Based on the wisps of fresh air that seem to come from the passageway above, there is probably an exit out somewhere nearby.
105604: This narrow ledge opens a bit above the plain, dominating a hollow in the grasslands below. A little opening in the hillside leads to a mossy stairway leading downwards. This shelf is wide enough to be used as a place to rest under the vastness of the sky.
105605: To the larger creatures of Arda the height of the grass might be a mere hindrance. However, to a hobbit, dwarf and to other smaller creatures the height of the grass holds a real danger of getting lost as the tall stalks go on forever as an entangled maze. One can only pick a direction and hope that it leads out of the sea of grass.
105606: To the north and west the ruins of a stone wall can be seen, but this particular area is virtually devoid of anything but grass. If it were not for the occasional landmarks of small trees and stones, it would be quite possible to get lost in this endless sea of vegetation.
105607: This wall section has survived over the countless years. It is a rather unremarkable wall, having nothing to show that it was used for any type of military fortification in the past. In fact, it seems likely that it was used in an attempt to keep livestock from wandering too far. This section blocks the movement to the west and the north from here as it makes its turn to the north, further east.
105608: A few young trees have grown up in the shade of a decaying stone wall, sheltered from the elements. The grass is a little bit shorter having been deprived of sunlight, giving other plants a chance to flourish. At the base of the ratty and old stone wall, some of the stones from which it was constructed, sit scattered around.
105609:
A rabbit is here eyeing your presence warily.
A colourful butterfly is fluttering around here.

The ground is grassy and covered by small plants growing in thick groups. The terrain is slightly sloping and pleasant to travel. The plain extends to all directions without an interruption but to the west, where a steep hillock rises above the plains.
105610: A sparrow is flapping around on the ground.

Lush grass grows all around. Many holes of prairie dogs are visible among the vegetation. Far to the north, the horizon line is shaped by the edge of a forest. The way south is blocked by a cliff, while the plain continues in all other directions.
105611: A rabbit is here eyeing your presence warily.

Travel across these plains is easy and pleasant. Some excrements mark the presence of cattle and other large animals. To the north-east a forest breaks the monotony of the landscape that continues unaltered in all other directions.
105612:
A rabbit is here eyeing your presence warily.
A fat yellow rodent scurries away, barking wildly.

A lean-to shelter has been built against the side of a fallen tree. Whoever made this shelter must have been in a hurry, as the result is a somewhat rickety construction, which could have been a decent shelter had more time been spent with it. Before the shed, some stones have been arranged in a rough circle around the campfire's location, and old cooking pots and other trash can be seen around, half-buried by dirt showing that this place has been abandoned for a long time. Barely noticeable against the trunk of the fallen tree are some rather large spots of old, dried blood.
105613:
An apple tree with bright green leaves grows here.
On the tree's branches are three apples.
A fat yellow rodent scurries away, barking wildly.

Saplings of several different types grow here in the grass. Larger trees grow up just beyond the plains on the western side, giving way to a true forest. Perhaps someday soon this small piece of land will cease to be a plain anymore. Some ivy has grown along a stone wall to the south.
105614: A rock lizard is here, motionless as it observes you.

A section of an ancient wall has not withstood the test of time. Fallen stones lay all about, partially sunken into the earth at the foot of the structure. Moss has begun to grow on part of the wall that still stands. A path is worn between the standing sections showing use by different creatures to come and go as they please.
105615: The grass here grows far thicker than almost any other nearby region. Some cattails have also grown up towards the northern part, adding variety to the mostly bare scenery.
105616:
A clear spring babbles as cool water trickles out of the ground.
A fallow deer is grazing peacefully here.
A robin is here, carrying small pieces of wood to its nest.
A pack horse (Rood) is standing here, ridden by you.

In contrast to the rest of the plains, this area has some plant-life other than grasses. A few hardy shrubs sprout from the ground here, providing a slight change of scenery from the seemingly endless plains about them. Nestled among the shrubs is a pool of water with a rather muddy bank. Pawprints in the mud suggest that this is a frequent spot for the denizens of these lands to stop and take a drink.
105617: Standing alone, tall and forlorn, is a single dead tree. Its branches have been stripped away by harsh weather. Over time part of the trunk has split off to rest beside its standing portion. To the west, past the plains, the remains of a stone wall can be seen.
105618: The tree above has rotten from inside. Its roots must have been affected for a much longer time, as the remains that are still visible all around are deeply black and covered with dry, now also dead fungi. It also seems as if the roots and all the soil around had been saturated with some sort of black slime that also has dried by now. The area feels cold and thick mist fills the air that smells foul of rot and decay.
105619: A large hawk-like bird is here overlooking its territory.

The native grasses have made themselves quite at home around an ancient stone wall. The wall itself, however, seems to have seen better days. Stones are missing along the top and side, leaving small niches for dirt and water to collect. A few plants have taken advantage of this, growing out of the ancient structure itself.
105620: A woodpecker is here, tapping on a tree.

The light forest gives way to larger trees here. Vines and moss can also be seen, adding life to the branches on the forest floor. Deeper inside forest, the songs of birds can be heard along with the occasional scurrying of a small animal. The crumbling remains of a stone wall block any passage to the east.
105621: A bee flies around here, collecting nectar from the flowers.
Wild flowers have grown tall between the trees here, shedding their colour into this fairly dry land. The flowers and other foliage here seem to be the perfect habitat for insects and small animals.
105622: Scattered trees mark the border of the forest that extends north and east of here. To the west and to the south lies a vast grassy plain. Signs of animal life are visible everywhere.
105623: A wild bull seems ready to charge you.

The vast field covered by lush grass and wild flowers extends to all directions, although further to the east, the horizon is outlined by the shape of a forest. Towards the river to the west the terrain becomes rocky and more inhospitable.
105624:
A huge warg is here, moving in for the kill.
A huge warg is here, moving in for the kill.
The mother wolf stands here, protecting her young cubs.
The mother wolf stands here, protecting her young cubs.

The ground here is bare and with no sign of living creatures. The vegetation grows thriving in all other directions. A tall hedge can be seen to the west. To the south a slope of sliding terrain ends at some trees.
105625: Every direction, as far as the eye can see, is coloured with different shades of green and gold. The main colour is green, but occasional bushes of flowers are visible trough the grass, struggling to survive among the weeds and grasses.
105626:
A large thorny branched shrub is growing here.
On the shrub, there are three piles of blackberries.
The monotony of the sea of grass is interrupted by a tall hedge of thorny bushes that block the way to the south. Travel can be continued to the east, north or west.
105627: A squirrel scampers around here, looking for nuts from the trees.

The ground looks very unsteady, sand and dirt being ready to shift upon any pressure laid upon the ground. Parts of the land have already caved in, giving way to dangerous sinkholes. Especially to the west the ground looks so difficult that it prevents travelling into that direction.
105628: Flat land stretches out in all directions, studded with occasional skinny trees. The land is very green, tall grass covers most of the plains rippling with every breeze that passes. The dark shadow of Mirkwood can be seen far to the east.
105629: A sparrow is flapping around on the ground.

Old, dry bones litter the ground and have killed some of the grass around them, leaving small, bare spots in the plains. Around the mound of gnawed bones some pawprints, new and old, can be seen leading off to different directions.
105630: A hungry warg is standing here, ridden by Backdraft.

Debris from the forest just to the west is prevalent here, adding some variety to the characteristics of a typical grass field: large branches emerge above the grassline, twisting among the briars and weeds. To the south, a crumbling stone wall cuts across the plains.
105631:
An erect shrub with green pinnate leaves is growing here.
Inside the shrub, there are three piles of crimson raspberries.

Thornbushes have grown tall and wild among the trees here, bearing long and dangerous thorns. On some of the bushes grow different types of berries, but reaching for them might greet the unwary scavenger with a hand full of puncture wounds. The bushes are not too dense towards the east, south or west but to the north they form an impenetrable brush wall, not allowing anyone or anything to move through.
105634: A sparrow is flapping around on the ground.

Oak, chestnut and elder trees grow and flourish all around. Some small rodent holes can be distinguished among the roots, and next to the trees there is one bigger hole as well, with several fresh footprints around it. The forest extends to the north and east from here. Some grassy plains with scattered trees can be seen south and west.
105635:
A colony of red ants is here. The ants seem to ignore you.
A colony of red ants is here. The ants seem to ignore you.

The tree that was once likely the king of these woods appears to have swayed for its last time and crashed to the ground. It is now overgrown with ivy while ants make their nests under its bark and squirrels store their nuts in holes under its decaying trunk. In its place, younger saplings have begun to grow in the freed up sunlight.
105637:
The remains of a thick tangle of vines lie here in a heap of rotting compost.
The remains of a thick tangle of vines lie here in a heap of rotting compost.

There is a surprisingly wide, open area inside this tree. Long vines grow along the edges of the trunk, and several narrow cracks are visible among them, allowing daylight to shine upon the vegetation. The air smells of rotten wood and mould. Mushrooms and toadstools can be seen growing out of the dead tree, while a few skeletons of small animals lie around, accented by a deer's skull.
105640:
A bear cub is here, looking around for something to play with.
A brown bear is sleeping here.

This cavern has been dug from the ground by some kind of animal. The floor is covered by dry leaves and the walls are of bare earth with roots hanging out. Many recent footprints show that the den is still in use.
105666: A colourful butterfly is fluttering around here.

The great river Anduin flows close to the west. The shore is low and sandy. Small channels in the ground lead from the eastern plain into the river; they are bordered by lush, green grass within the plains, and laid bare while cutting across the sandy shore to the river. Some rocks and boulders lie along the shoreline; to the east they are replaced by grass and small plants. To the south the terrain becomes rocky and harder to travel.
105668: Travelling this terrain is arduous and riding is quite impossible. Many jagged rocks cover the ground and some huge boulders make difficult to keep a straight direction. Some cracks line the ground, descending towards the river. To the north and south the landscape is all the same. To the east the rocks are replaced by grassy plains dotted with trees.
105669: Approaching the river the ground becomes rocky and hard to travel, making it impossible to ride here. To the east the terrain becomes low and grassy, while to the south some thick vegetation can be seen. To the north the rocks and boulders continue without a break.
105670: This rocky spur dominates the river flowing below to the west. The cliff is made of grey stone eroded by the power of the river. Some large, flat boulders with jagged edges make moving along the riverbank a dangerous task. To the east the cliff lowers towards a plain. The bank continues to the south. Heading west will result in a dive into the river and climbing back onto the riverside will not be possible.
105671: The great power of the Anduin has carved the ground, revealing its bones. The riverbank is made of bare rocks and only a little vegetation grows among them. The rocks continue to the north and east, while to the south the bank becomes a cliff.
105672: A large, yellow crab is crawling around here.

The riverside here is low and sandy. Many smooth pebbles lie on the beach; some are white or grey and some are of bright colours. Part of the bank is covered by a reed thicket. To the west flows the great river Anduin. To the north the bank becomes high and rocky. East and south the ground is covered by thick vegetation and trees.
105673: A huge black fungus is here, exuding a foul stench.

Once this must have been the bed of an underground tributary of Anduin. The walls are smooth and the ground is covered by some rocks and debris. From the ceiling, stalactites point menacingly at the floor. Some piled boulders lead towards a possible exit from the vault of the cavern. To the east the tunnel narrows in the darkness.
105674:
A giant, strange looking green fungus is here, ready to devour you in seconds.
A giant slug is here, oozing around.

The cavern here is damp and the ceiling is low. The floor is covered by debris and it is quite clear that a stream once flowed across it. To the east, a pile of fallen rocks make it impossible to go further. To the west, the cavern broadens.
105675: Some willow trees grow here, along the bank of Anduin the Great that flows near to the west, giving moderate shelter among these vast grassy plains. The trees stretch their roots toward the water and little leaves dance in the air as they fall, carried by the breeze, to the ground or water. The ground is soft, rich and covered by leaves. To the north and east the plains continue as far as the eye can see. Southwest is a trail coming from the south and heading west to the river.
105676: A few groups of trees, namely willows and pines, are spotted in this field that overlooks the majestic Anduin River. The steep cliffs to the west and north prevent one from entering and exiting the Great River, as it clashes with the rock and speeds its way southwards. A huge boulder stands here, the only rock that can be seen for miles. The ground around appears to have been trodden recently, allowing the notion that it may be a marker of some sort.
105677:
The corpse of a large bat is lying here.
The corpse of a young cavetroll is lying here.

Harsh, horizontal lines deface the black rock walls of this crudely cut tunnel, making them jagged and unpredictable. Many small pebbles are strewn about the floor, slowly dissipating as the tunnel continues to the north.
105678: Celirion the Elf, wielding a black runed dagger, is standing here.

The tunnel looks like it would have ended here, if it was not for a crudely cut passage leading to the south. The predominately smooth floor is a sharp contrast to the jagged walls and ceiling, which add many hazards to those who may traverse through.
105679:
The ugly troll mother is roaming the cave, taking care of her loved ones.
An old, strong cave troll is standing here.
An old, strong cave troll is standing here.
An old, strong cave troll is standing here.
An old, strong cave troll is standing here.

The rock that makes up the jagged walls of this tunnel is dark, causing the walls to absorb any light that may be cast upon them. The floor of the tunnel is quite rough and very dirty. Many small stalagmites are protruding every few feet, while most of them have been shattered and broken. The signs, and the smells, indicate trolls have made their lair here. The tunnel continues to the east and ends at a massive pile of rubble in the west.
105680: Grassy Mound above the Great River

This elevated, steep-sloped hill provides an excellent view of the Anduin River as it flows from the north and through the grassy plains to the west. Far in the distance, the Misty Mountains stand tall in the sky with their sharp peaks resembling huge, pointed teeth growing out of the ground.
105681:
Clusters of slender stems and tall leaves thrive in the mud and shallows.
A shallow pond is here, tinted green with algae.

A wide, round swamp lies here, surrounded by reeds. The water supplying this swamp appears to flow somewhere from the north, bubbling through some large rocks. The reeds growing in the swamp thrive on the marshy ground. The water- soaked ground gives the lush grasslands to the west their supply of water. The overflow of water in this area creates makes the swamp continue to the east.
105682: The soggy ground here gives an almost swampy feeling in some parts. Water floods in from the north. There are a few reeds growing here but mostly lush, green grass blades. The ground begins to become dry further to the south.
105683: Dark-green grass, brown reeds and low bushes grow here, supplied by the fertile, wet ground. Narrow, muddy path borders the swamp, winding and wheeling around the deep water puddles that occupy the ground in several places. The ground is impassable to the north, gets more wet to the east, while to the south it seems to slope upwards.
105684:
A swamp iris grows here.
Clusters of slender stems and tall leaves thrive in the mud and shallows.
A large green shrub grows in the middle of a large pool of mud.
A swarm of mosquitoes is here, humming around you.

These wetlands are populated with reeds of many types. The ground is covered with large, deceptive-looking pools, which produce occasional bubbles to the sticky surface of water. Around the pools, the land is saturated with mud and moisture. There is a patch of irises growing toward the west. Far beyond the bog, at the edge of the wetlands to the north and east, thick brush meets the reeds.
105685: Granite Boulders on a Rocky Hillock
A sparrow is flapping around on the ground.

A hillock rises amid the plains which stretch for miles in every direction. The elevated area provides a good view of the surroundings, but the huge granite boulders lying everywhere allow one to remain hidden at the same time. The grass on this hillock looks dried and yellow in some places, but in the shade of the boulders it is lush and healthy, interspersed with some colourful wildflowers.
105686: The tall, thick grass makes rustling sounds and sways gently back and forth when the winds blow through here. Ranging three or four feet at places, it is long enough to hide any smaller animals from predators. Plains continue in all sides except in the east, where a low, grassy hill breaks up the monotony of the landscape.
105687: A small wooden platform rests in the upper branches of a huge fir tree, with a hole in the middle to ease descent down. Remains of a handrail still surround the platform, but all of the ropes are gone and some of the posts decayed, giving little or almost no support to prevent falling down. High crowns of trees in the east block any view to the forest, but in the west a dry riverbed is clearly visible during daytime.
105693: A large brown snake with black patches is coiled here.

The plains abruptly cut off as they approach from the north-west here. Very little grows in this deep gorge. It seems to be either an old dried up river bed or perhaps an underground stream that flowed underneath the soil that has collapsed. Rocks litter the ground, making passage rough and awkward even for the most sure-footed travellers.
105694: The canyon is steep and narrow. The walls are rocky and wet. Some debris and little boulders cover the ground making it unstable to walk across. The canyon widens to the north into a deep gully, while to the south the ground climbs to a flat area. The east and west walls are too steep to climb.
105696:
A large thorny branched shrub is growing here.
On the shrub, there are a number of blackberries.
A large brown snake with black patches is coiled here.
A black snake hurries towards you with sly intentions.
A black snake, with red markings, is lying here.
A mottled snake is sneaking here, ready to sink its fangs into flesh.

Everywhere around this area the tall grass, spiky bushes and rocks of various sizes seem to knot into a messy network of snarled passages and dead-ends, each one more perplexing than the previous. So narrow are the paths amidst the vegetation, that riding is not possible here; it almost seems that the tangle of swaying bushes twists into a web of confusion just to thwart the traveller's passage. To the east the ground sinks abruptly in an unclimbable canyon.
105697: The top layer of soil is sliding southwards making this area hard to travel through and impossible to ride. To the east and west the plain is covered by grass. North of here there is no sign of vegetation. Some trees grow to the south.
105699: A small brown snake is slithering around here.

A deep ditch lies on the border of the plain and a faint trail which runs through the area in west-east direction. The ground is muddy and covered by crawling plants. To the north a gentle slope rises towards a more solid soil covered by grass and bushes.
105700:
A worm is here slithering around.
A colourful butterfly is fluttering around here.

The mud here is deep and travelling is hard. Both sides of the ditch are steep and slippery. The ditch continues to the west, while to the east it disappears into a line of trees. Climbing the north side of the ditch will lead to a hedge that crosses the grassy plain, while the southern side of the ditch, too steep and muddy for one to climb up, borders a faint trail.
105703:
An erect shrub with green pinnate leaves is growing here.
Inside the shrub, there are three piles of crimson raspberries.

The grass here is overgrown by dense shrubs and bushes. Mounts which travellers may have brought through must be led by hand in this tangle of branches and thorns. The plain extends in all directions from here.
105704: A sloped hillock breaks up the landscape here. No tree can be seen for miles. Only green lush grass covers the ground. The steep banks of this hillock prevent the travelling in all directions but down.
105736:
Klaees (thedon), wielding a wightblade, is standing here.
Drazud (freshmeat), wielding a great warsword, is standing here.

The rough stone walls and floor of this tunnel are lined with moisture which must come from the mighty Anduin River which flows above here. The ceiling is very low in some areas, which could cause difficulty for those traversing through this tunnel. Here the floor of the tunnel slopes steadily downwards, from east to the west. The tunnel's walls have collapsed at its eastern end, yet it seems someone could move the rubble with a lot of effort.
105737: The walls spread apart as the ceiling gets lower in this small underground nexus. The dark rock which this small tunnel cuts through seems to have been worn away from years and years of water flowing through, eroding the rock from the floor up. The floor slopes up in all directions except for south, where it continues its slight downward decline.
105738:
A pool of darkish water has formed in a depression of the stone.
A subterranean lizard is here trying to blend with the surroundings (hidden).

The air is stagnant and still here in this small cavern. The only exit is to the north, up a small slope. Due to the lower elevation of this cavern, a dark pool of water has formed at the southern end from all the water which trickles down into here.
105739: The walls of the tunnel are getting closer and closer to each other, making the passageway only a few yards wide at the narrowest point. The uneven floor combined with the rough ceiling cause the height of this tunnel to vary, causing it to be very cramped.
105740: This passage is very narrow, and seems to be natural, rather than cut into the stone. While the tunnel continues toward the east, one can exit by climbing out without much difficulty, as the jagged edges make for great footholds for bipeds to use. Many small bones are scattered on the floor, in solemn tribute to smaller animals which have fallen in and been unable to exit.
105741: From atop this hill, one can look down and see the Anduin flowing directly to the east, and follow it around the hill towards the south where it continues into the horizon. The river is unreachable from here, as the banks are very steep. A small opening which leads down into the rock can be seen on the ground, marked by a obviously placed white stone.
105742:
A moderately-sized copperhead snake is here.
A moderately-sized copperhead snake is here.

This small valley is lower than all of the plains that surround it. It is quite rocky, with no plant life trying to grow among the small rocks which have been chipped off of the walls of the valley. Due to the steepness of the northern and western walls, travelling in those directions is impossible.
105743: Dense brush flourishes on the riverbank here, growing well due to the Anduin flowing directly east of it. The land here slopes downwards suddenly to the north, leading to what looks like a small valley. The loud sound of rushing water is heard to the east, as the Anduin flows along its journey.
105744: The plains here are thriving with grass, creating a seemingly endless carpet of green that turns to blue towards the north where the plain meets the tributary. The plain gently rises towards the east and south, leading to the higher ground that borders the Great River.
105745:
A fallow deer is grazing peacefully here.
A beautiful and docile horse is standing here.

Scattered trees and brush dot the plains here, giving the impression that the loose soil here is very fertile. Short grasses also spread across the plains, connecting the various trees and shrubs together and giving a unified look to the landscape.
105746: A small cluster of clover grows here.

If one turns in a complete circle here, the landscape differs in each direction. Towards the east, the river Anduin slides through the fields and plains. A tiny wooded area can be seen toward the south, and the plain slants upwards to the north towards what seems to be a small hill.
105747: A boar cub is playing here, and exploring the wide world.

All around, this plain is dominated by a thick, tall grass that stands about a yard high. While the field seems to be flat, the thick stalks and pointed tips of the grass hide the ground from view, suggesting that it could rise and fall slightly.
105748: A boar cub is playing here, and exploring the wide world.

This plain looks like many others, save for a huge blackened oak tree which looms over the field with an ominous presence. It was probably struck by a lightning long ago, so charred and burned are its once lively branches and trunk.
105749: A boar cub is playing here, and exploring the wide world.

Hard ground and dead grasses make up this barren field, giving it a solitary look compared to the fertile plains one might expect to find here. It stands a little bit higher than the surrounding fields. Perhaps the elevation is a factor to this field's demise, letting water drain off into the lower meadows.
105750: This hill is blanketed in short, dense grass. From atop this hill, one can see water to the north, east, and south, as the tributary meets the Anduin, which continues to flow southward through a small gorge. The riverbank to the east is quite steep, making it impossible to enter the Anduin from this hill. South of the hill, the small gorge compresses the Anduin causing it to crash through the formation.
105751: This muddy riverside offers stark contrast to the green plains behind it. The great River flows on the eastern and southern end of the plain, yielding a muddy riverbank that is dotted with what seems to be the footprints of small animals that have traversed here to drink from the river.
105752: Log Jam in the Anduin River

Hundreds and again hundreds of old, sturdy logs have gathered and and become stuck together, creating a massive log jam which seems to span across the whole Anduin. The logs are intertwined into each other in several layers, forming a dangerous, rickety, but possibly passable, passageway across. Some of the logs are more than eight yards long, and as thick as a medium-sized stone troll.
105754: Log Jam in the Anduin River

Partly underwater, partly afloat, an enormous log jam stretches across the river Anduin. The logs lie side by side and they overlap each other, with individual logs protruding in all possible directions; forming a mostly solid but definitely rough and tricky path over the river. The whole construction is in a state of slight, continuous movement, being rocked as it is by the currents and waves of the Anduin.
105758:
A waist-high evergreen shrub grows here, with thick, reaching branches.
On the shrub, there are three piles of grey-green leaves.

Light-green grass covers this mostly flat plain. In some areas the grass is quite tall, suggesting that the soil that lies underneath it is very rich. The plains slope downwards to the south and east, where the great river can be seen winding its way through the vast landscape.
105759: Rising Plains near the River Anduin

The field here rises upwards ever so slightly, offering a full view of the bushy riverbank along the southern side, that borders the mighty Anduin. The southern bank leads steeply into the river, forcing those who might wish to embark into it to search elsewhere.
105760: Rolling over the plains and meadows, the carpet of lush grass here adds a soft perspective to this field. The ground is hardly flat, but it is not harsh or ragged, providing a very gentle grassland that is reminiscent of a feeding pasture found on farms for livestock. What appears to be an old streambed lies to the west, one could jump down the bank, but probably not climb back into this pasture from it.
105761: With the Anduin River bordering the plains on two sides, this grassy field seems quite fertile. The two banks bordering the river offer a contrast to each other. The southern bank is predominately rocky, and seemingly very hazardous, while the eastern bank has thick, waist-high brush blocking entry to the Great River.
105762:
A blooming water-lily floats on the surface of the water.
A black pond of water is here.

A small pond of calm, dark water has placed its bed in the ground here. Its shape is reminiscent of an eye, not exactly rounded, but more of an oval, pinching at the east and west sides. Because of its small size, the edges of the pond rise higher than the grassy ground surrounding it.
105763: Many rocks are strewn about the riverbank here, most of them small in size and of light colours. The Anduin splashes noisily over them, causing them to be quite slippery and making traversing to the river possible, but unsafe. The ground beyond the riverbank is grassy, with full shrubs protruding from the fertile soil.
105764: Rocky Plain near the Great River
A tall stag is here, grazing peacefully.

Many rocks and stones litter the plain here, perhaps cast here after being slowly moved through the Great River that flows immediately to the south. Many of the rocks and stones are tiny, however, a few of them are quite large and have been smoothed by the river flowing over them for many years.
105765:
An orkish wolf-rider, wielding a lance, is here, riding a brown wolf.
A brown wolf is standing here, ridden by an orkish wolf-rider.

Thin brush grows all over this field, with its green foliage rising and dipping throughout the area giving the landscape a very textured look. The pointed leaves adoring the branches serve as a defence from grazing wildlife, however, many smaller animals could seek refuge from predators under the brush.
105766:
The corpse of a grey wolf is lying here.
The corpse of a rabid, grey wolf is lying here.
Radikas the Dwarf (RR), wielding an ornate, steel-shafted warhammer, is standing here.
Huntwind the Elf (HH), wielding an engraved broadsword, is standing here.
Elerin the Elf, wielding an engraved broadsword, is standing here.

With the River Anduin directly to the east and south, this low bank is never devoid of water and has allowed vast amounts of brush to grow all about the riverbank. While most of the brush is quite harmless, there are some varieties that stand almost a yard high that make navigation among this riverside slightly difficult.
105767: The plains here rise from the east and south, yielding a view of the majestic Anduin as it snakes it way through the plains to the south. Thin, soft grasses cover the fertile plains, giving the notion that the environment here is not very harsh during any of the seasons.
105770: The grassy field here is almost unnaturally flat, with most of the terrain near it rising away from here. Passage to the north is blocked by an old stone wall that is crumbling from years of decay and what appears to be hasty, cheap work. To the south and east the grassy plains rise slightly upwards, keeping the far view of what may lay beyond them. In the middle of the field on the western side, an old dilapidated hut barely stands.
105771: This small hut would fall in upon itself, were there not a few sturdy log columns, which seem to be placed here after the original construction work, to keep the roof standing. This hut was probably constructed long time ago by travellers following the Anduin, to seek shelter from the rain. Judging from the lack of any furnishing, it was meant to be a transient dwelling. The dust on the floor is marked with fresh footprints that seem to stop in the middle of the room.
105772:
An uruk of the Morgundul tribe is here commanding his soldiers.
An orc-guard of the Morgundul is on patrol here.
An orc-guard of the Morgundul is on patrol here.
An orc-guard of the Morgundul is on patrol here.
A slender orc scans the area, his bow ready for a sudden strike.

Built with defence in mind, the cavern is like a small bottleneck, with a low floor and close walls, giving an obvious disadvantage to anyone who happens to find themselves here. A steep slope on the south wall marks the only exit to the outside world from this underground network.
105773:
An uruk of the Morgundul tribe is here commanding his soldiers.
A hungry warg stands here, sniffing around for flesh.
A hungry warg stands here, sniffing around for flesh.

Many crudely built iron cages with tied gates line the far wall of this tiny, filthy cavern. Tufts of fur and piles of droppings litter the floor, giving very little clean walking space and adding to the musty odour of animals that emanates from here.
105774:
An arrow lies on the ground.
An arrow lies on the ground.
An arrow lies on the ground.
A wooden chest stands in the corner.
A water barrel has been left here.
A Morgundul uruk, wielding a backsword, is sleeping here.
A Morgundul orc guard, wielding a longspear, is sleeping here.

The parallel walls of this cavern are lined with crude bunks, with no apparent care for organization or neatness. Against the far wall, stand many weapon and armour racks, in close reach of the inhabitants of this filthy barracks. The floor is covered in dust and dirt, and in a far corner many bloody blades lay in disarray.
105775:
The corpse of a slender orkish archer is lying here.
A circular stone well has been built here.
A large bonfire is burning here.

A huge bonfire marks the centre of this room, surrounded by rickety chairs and tables. Bones litter the western floor, perhaps from tortuous sacrifices and forced fighting among the slaves for amusement and ceremonies. On the eastern wall, raised upon a pedestal, a crude stone chair that is probably reserved for the warchief sits next to a small well. Along the western wall there are many torches flanking a huge, heavy gate. It appears to use some sort of a chain mechanism to open it.
105776:
A weapons rack stands against the wall.
In the rack are a bastard sword and a battle axe.
A simple wooden chest is here.
A sturdy peg for hanging armour from is on the wall.
On the peg, there are a fine pair of chain mail leggings and a fine pair of soft leather gloves.
A red-eyed shaman of the Morgundul tribe is here, chanting in evil tongues.
A Morgundul orc snarls about here, looking for a fight.
A Morgundul orc snarls about here, looking for a fight.
A slender orc scans the area, his bow ready for a sudden strike.
A tall Uruk paces about, issuing commands to his troops.

This chamber connects to the vast hall to the south and entry is blocked only by a curtain that stands to give a little privacy to the owner. The chamber contains three messy beds that are placed next to a weapons rack along the northern wall.
105777:
An enslaved troll is here, eager to unleash its rage upon you.
A grouchy uruk is here, lashing his whip.
An enslaved troll is here, eager to unleash its rage upon you.

Carved into the stone, this chamber is completely barren and desolate. No torches light it, and no furnishings can be found on the dusty floor. The only way out is through the heavy gate to the east which appears to use some sort of a chain mechanism to open it. The chamber is probably used to house slaves and prisoners of the inhabitants.
105778: Lots and lots of brush dominate the plains in every direction, having pushed the grass away by sucking the nutrients from the soil and blocking the sun from enriching the grass with its large, pointed leaves. The ground here is slightly lower than the surrounding plains, but one can not tell that just by looking around, as the brush stands taller than the surroundings.
105779: A colourful butterfly is fluttering around here.

Thin brush and lush grasses cover the plains here, adding a myriad of colours and textures to the landscape. The rich, soft grass flows endlessly here, contrasted by the rough, prickly brush that dots the plains. The plain tilts upwards to the west, where a small hill lies.
105780: Rising from the plains, this low hill has very little plant life on its crown. There are tufts of grasses littered about the bases of the hill, but gradually they become less common towards the crest of the hill. While the hill stands above its surroundings, it is not quite tall enough to command a pronounced view of the area. The way south is blocked by a crumbling stone wall.
105781: A grassy slope gently rises from here, leading to the south. The grass on the slope is quite lush, fed by the rain water that drips down the hill before being absorbed into the topsoil. The bottom of the slope is dotted with various shrubs and brush that has found solace in the fertile soil.
105782: Suddenly rising from the grasslands, a large, jagged rock stands about three yards high here. Its sides are grey and rough, with the bottom half mostly covered by a thick, brown moss. The grass covers the field completely, with the giant rock being the only object blocking its flow.
105783: The plain gently rises here, yielding a view east and north over the remains of a dried stream. The grass on the plain here is very lush, contrasting the brown that can be seen in the riverbed. Travel to the east is made more difficult by a ledge that lowers into the streambed.
105784:
The corpse of an orkish wolf-rider is lying here.
The corpse of a boar is lying here.
The corpse of a boar is lying here.
A large brown wolf stands here, its teeth partly bared.

A thin strip of hardened mud streaks through the green grass here, arriving from the northern end of the plain and continuing south to what appears to be a pond. The streambed, while not very large, is lower than its surrounding ground offering two very distinct terrain types to the plains. A high bank halts anything that wishes to proceed east.
105785: The plains extends in all directions, void of any hills and dips, completely flat. Thin, short grass covers the ground, flowing smoothly over the plains. The grass reaches out in every direction, connecting the vast fields together.
