105786: Scattered shrubs dot the field, and dissipate towards this field, which is mostly covered in grass, with a few barren plots of a hard, brown soil interrupting the ground. To the north, a steep hill rises from the ground blocking passage in that direction.
105787:
An orkish wolf-rider, wielding a lance, is here, riding a brown wolf.
A brown wolf is standing here, ridden by an orkish wolf-rider.

Slanting downwards from the west, and continuing to the east, this plain is made up of caked, brown soil. Hard and desolate, nothing is able to grow in the immediate area. Grass lightly creeps in from the north, starting from the ledge which prevents travel in that direction.
105788: The remains of what once used to be a small stream cuts through this field, its low path and hardened soil brings a solemn mood to the area that goes against the playful scene of lush, green meadows that surround it. Steep ledges on the north and east banks prevent travel, and outline the path the stream once followed.
105789: A mountain mule (ulo) is standing here, ridden by you.

Various grasses extend to the far corners of this field. They range from a short and dark grass, to a taller, lighter variety. The field does not appear to be flat, but the terrain can not be guessed for certain, as the taller grass could be hiding many small dips and rises. A brush-covered hill towers above the field on the east side.
105790: The field here is covered in the vast grassy carpet which flows in from all directions and continues onward through the fields and plains giving the impression of a seemingly endless landscape. The grassy cover slopes upwards to the south, meeting the horizon.
105791: This plain is all but flat, with small hills and depressions making up the field. Short wide-bladed grass covers the whole plain, and rolls over the hills and through each dip, never breaking to show the plain ground that hides under the undulating grass.
105792: Healthy bushes make up most of this plain, standing about half a yard in height, and flanked by short grasses on all sides. The bushes themselves have wide, dense leaves that shroud most of their thorny stems from eyesight. There are also a few shorter bushes with long, pale leaves that grow sparingly around the plain.
105793: A brown fox is here, looking for some rabbits to chew up.

Desolate and barren, this field is populated very sparsely only by patches of grass and tiny shrubs which are struggling to maintain themselves. The brown earth has dried with large cracks on it, likely from the lack of plants to shield it from the strong rays of sunlight.
105794:
A snake slithers towards you.
A brown fox is here, looking for some rabbits to chew up.

Wide plains come into view here, in a vast field with rolling grasses and a few bushes making up the scenery. The field slants down towards the east, opening up a panorama of the various landscapes that creep toward the Anduin river in that direction.
105795: The fields here are covered in small shrubs and brush, differing in height from about half a yard to over three yards tall, colouring the landscape with hues of green and brown. Towards the east, a small forest rises out of the plains, perhaps a sign of that an abundant water source is near.
105796: A lone hawk soars high above you.

The plains here meet a small, sparse forest which stretches lightly to the west. The forest seems to be made of mostly pine trees. Their bark and needles bring new textures and colours, which contrast the grassy landscape that surrounds the trees.
105797: The blots of sand and grass change repeatedly over the terrain, making the landscape more interesting with various colours. To the north the foliage becomes more dense, and behind the small bushes the shape of a small sparse forest can be made out. Far in the west, the peaks of Misty Mountains rise as a wall between these wide plains and the western land.
105798: The grasslands flatten out here, opening up a wide view of the surrounding fields. Most of the grasses on this plain are quite dense, providing many small nooks and thickets for the various indigenous rodents to claim a haven. A steep bank prevents travel to the dried old streambed which lies to the west.
105799: A fallow deer is grazing peacefully here.

A light sand covers most of the terrain here, along with patches of rich soil and lush green grass. Giving a more interesting appearance to this field, small sinkholes are formed within the sand, making the terrain taxing to traverse.
105800: A brown fox is here, looking for some rabbits to chew up.

The land here intertwines with its surroundings very well, making it hard to tell just how far, or how long one has travelled in this meadow. A few different types of grasses cover the meadow, the most abundant being a thin bladed, brown grass. A good-sized cliff borders the southern part of the meadow, leading to what appears to be a dried up stream.
105801: Dipping downwards from the west, the land here becomes increasingly wet, suggesting that this slight dip holds rainwater for a bit longer than its more elevated neighbouring plains. The ground is covered with scattered shrubbery and grass is seen growing in the wet soil that makes up this miniature swamp.
105802: A beautiful and docile horse is standing here.

Standing alone above the plains, this small hill rises from the ground, offering a unique view of the encircling lands not possible from the lower fields and meadows. Rising smoothly from the north and east, travel is cut off to the south by the steep slope in that direction. While the western side is steep, the brush would make great footholds for climbing down.
105804:
A boar cub is playing here, and exploring the wide world.
A rabbit is here eyeing your presence warily.

Sloping in from every direction, this tiny valley appears to be very fertile, with a carpet of thick-bladed grass and many small shrubs dotting the fields. The soil appears to be a little loose, probably from the rainwater that drains into the field from the surrounding plains.
105805: Short, thick grass covers the land here, stretching out in all directions but the north, where a swift tributary flows through the plains. The proximity of the tributary has helped the grass flourish here, keeping the soil very fertile during dry weather.
105806: A small boar with big yellow tusks looks eager to fight.

Green grasslands stretch out in all directions, sloping upward to the north, and down towards the south and east. The whole field is covered in thick grass which crawls about the landscape, giving it a soft, fertile appearance.
105807: This small hill stands proudly over the tributary that runs from the cold Misty Mountains. It commands a view in all directions. To the north, the tributary from the Misty Mountains flows down to meet the Great River. The Anduin itself, is in the far east, a winding ribbon heading south. Plains roll on south from the hill, interrupted by a small, sparse forest before continuing on.
105809: Grasses, thin brush, and small rocks are scattered about here, bringing a sight that is different than the surrounding plains. Many different colours make up this field, from the brown soil with green grasses to the grey and white rocks that have been seemingly tossed about.
105810: The plain slopes downward towards the east, opening up the view of the lands that lead in the direction of the River Anduin. Scattered among these fields, a few small groups of pine trees offer contrast to the grasses with their rough bark.
105811: A rabbit is here eyeing your presence warily.

Vegetation flourishes here, with multiple small bushes and shrubs springing from the ground, along with a short, dense grass that grows all over the plain, seemingly endless as it connects the plants and hides the dirt from view.
105812: Small Group of Trees amid the Soft Plains
A rabbit is here eyeing your presence warily.

The wide open plains bring their lush carpet of grasses here, adding to the colours set by the small group of willow trees towards the west side of this field. The towering willow trees appear to be well nourished, with thick foliage hanging down from high branches, creating a canopy that shrouds their huge roots.
105813: The ground here is quite soft, with thick grasses and scattered brush thriving due to the pond sitting in the north west corner of this meadow. The grass is broken and trampled upon in many places, leading to and from the pond, a sign that small animals converge here to replenish themselves with the water.
105816:
A rabbit is here eyeing your presence warily.
A rabbit is here eyeing your presence warily.

Rich grass seems to crawl over this wide plain, hiding the ground beneath it from eyesight. It is quite flat, with a slight upward slope towards the east. The plain must be very fertile, as the grasses cover the landscape, save for a few small bushes that have also found the fertile soil of this plain to be homely.
105817: Lush green grasses cover this plain, along with the occasional tiny shrub. The soil feels very soft, but is hidden from view by the thick-bladed grass that drapes over the terrain like a blanket, rising and falling with the rhythm of the landscape.
105825: The river begins to spread out and become slightly more shallow as it bends from the west and heads south. There are many pebbles covering the river bed here, visible under the calmer parts of the river.
105826: The river seems deeper here as it is squeezed by its banks on either side. The steep bank to the west drops off so sharply that passage upward is impossible. To the east a riverbank can be seen with some poles standing out of the water. The current of the river flows quickly here, causing small rapids to show on the surface of the river.
105827: As the great river makes the turn here, from the west towards the south, the river seems to narrow some, causing the depth to increase. The eastern bank is covered with reeds and a few irises, thriving on the low lying riverbank environment. The western bank towers above the river toward the southwest.
105828: A large beaver is here, gnawing on a piece of wood.

A large tree, fallen from the forested riverbank to the west, lies across the river here, branches dragging against the water. The river runs at a fast pace here, bending to the east as it continues its way south.
105829: The Anduin river flows faster in this part than elsewhere. The water is so fast that it forms many white-water eddies. To the east, reeds and irises grow in the shallow part of the river. The increased flow drags them down, making them sway like darting vipers with the current of the river's flow.
105830: The river flows rapidly downstream towards the south. There is a steep riverbank to the west. On the eastern side of the river there is a shallow, calm pool. The riverbank to the east seems to slope down and come close to the elevation of the water's surface here. The river seems to increase in speed as it flows south, and rapids can be seen cutting the surface of the water at certain places.
105831:
A trout swims here.
A bass swims here.

The water flows at a decent pace here, but the rapids are not so fast that one could not see the bottom of the river. There are well polished rocks covering the riverbed. To the west the riverbank looms above the river. To the east the bank is steeper coming from the north and angles to a lower elevation before continuing south.
105832: Water flows briskly downriver towards the south. Both riverbanks are fairly steep on either side, but the western side is steeper than the eastern one. To the north the river appears to make a turn from the east. A large, black boulder sits deep in the water along the western shore.
105833: The great Anduin river flows in from the north and bends to the west as it flows through this section of the river. Reeds and irises line the southern riverbank. There is a short drop off to the east where the river meets the meadow.
105834: The river flows calmly to the south after finishing its southwesterly curve. The water is quite serene here; rocks at the bottom of the river are visible through the water. To the east, a riverbank lined with reeds reveals a green meadow. To the west the bank is steep but still climbable.
105835: Flowing in from the north, the river makes a gradual curve toward the southwest. The low banks on the northwestern and southeastern sides of the river allow shallow river plants to grow healthily. Reeds and irises conceal the ground close to the sides of the river. The water moves at a swift pace but has a calm look to its surface.
105837: Great Curve in the Anduin River

Almost as quickly as the water speeds in from the north, the Great River quickly turns its way to the west, finding its way between large stones that sit in the riverbed. White foam and small bubbles develop from the water as it pushes over the stones hiding just beneath the surface.
105838: The wide river is flowing from the north to the west here, rushing to carve its way through the undulating plains. A small hill blocks the view to the east, and the shore to the south offers a rocky landing spot before the great river turns towards that direction.
105839: A small hill blocks the flow of water to the south, so the Great River takes a turn to the west. A mess of water-rotten wooden logs and smaller branches are stuck in the overhanging brush that reaches out from the eastern bank.
105840: Clumps of wooden logs clutter the banks of the Anduin here, stuck along the southern shore, or in the brush on the eastern bank. The river starts to shrink again as it flows west, speeding up slightly and changing the calm that is experienced towards the north, where the river was much wider.
105841: Log Jam in the Anduin River

Hundreds and again hundreds of old, sturdy logs have gathered and and become stuck together, creating a massive log jam which seems to span across the whole Anduin. The logs are intertwined into each other in several layers, forming a dangerous, rickety, but possibly passable, passageway across. Some of the logs are more than eight yards long, and as thick as a medium-sized stone troll.
105842: The water is spread between the low riverbanks, giving it a calm demeanour. The northern riverbank is covered with rocks, behind them the grassy plains drift away, calmly dropping out of sight. To the west, the Anduin is slightly altering its course southwards.
105848: The Great River is making its turn from the east to the south. The curve is quite placid, with the water surface not showing any signs of disturbances at the turn. Weeds and small bushes can be seen on the banks to the north and west. Many stones on the northern bank are textured with white tags, clarifying the visit of many birds.
105849: The great river Anduin flows in a southwestern direction as it cuts through the meadows on either side. The banks of the river on the north and south sides are quite gradual. Reeds grow at the edge of the river with grass further away from the river. When the river finishes its curve, it directs itself southbound.
105861:
A salmon swims here.
A bass swims here.

Here, the river Anduin flows in from the east, continuing its flow to the south. There is a small, shallow pool collecting at the northwest corner of the bend in the river, where bits of debris can be seen, trapped among small eddies and currents. The riverbank on the southeast is lined with reeds.
105867: The flow of the Anduin is gathering speed here, rushing in from the east and continuing to the south. Lush plains flow west of here, as far as the eye can see. The banks on the northern side are inaccessible, with rocks and thick vegetation making it too dangerous to reach the shore.
105868: The majestic Anduin turns and speeds its way southwards here again, after crashing into the high banks to the west. The water seems quite deep around this point, as no rocks are sticking out of the blue surface. The northern and western riverbanks are not safely accessible as the water rushes over the rocks.
105871: After coming through a narrow gorge to the east, the mighty Anduin widens here, allowing the water to calm down while it spreads to wider area. Taking advantage of the still part of the river, an old log dock is located not much further downstream the river.
105873:
A brook trout is here, swimming in the current.
A brook trout is here, swimming in the current.
A salmon swims here.

Here the tributary changes its course, heading towards the east again. It picks up speed as it nears its destination, the Anduin. The riverbank immediately south of here raises slightly, shielding the distant view in that direction.
105874: The tributary is now at its fastest pace since the beginning of its journey from the Misty Mountains. The path is blocked by a hill towards the south, so it continues eastward, where it crashes into the rushing Anduin, causing water to be sprayed in all directions.
105876: As the tributary continues along its path to meet the Great River, it makes a sharp turn southwards. The eastern bank is quite grassy, and appears to be easily accessible. The clear water is quite noisy as it rushes over and around various large boulders that have come to rest in the path of the tributary.
105877: The Great River continues its seemingly endless journey southwards. It is beginning to pick up pace, and it would take great strength to swim across here. The banks on the western side are low, and covered in lush green grass. The water seems to get louder towards the south.
105878: Sharp Turn in the Great River

The fury of the Anduin is evident in the chaotic maelstrom, which throws water all over the sands that make up the eastern bank and the walls of the cliff to the south. The glittering pebbles lying on the eastern beach seem quite complacent as the water crashes over them and ebbs back into the river before continuing to the west.
105879: The fast flowing waters are now completely mixed into one body and are compressed into this gorge. Jagged walls rise directly on both sides. The water flows extremely fast through this pass, violently continuing to the south.
105880: A large sturgeon swims slowly along the bottom.

The Anduin flows majestically towards the south. The current is moderate and some small eddies are gurgling near the banks. To the east the riverside is rocky and covered with vegetation. To the west the width of the river makes it difficult to distinguish the shape of the terrain. Some leaves and branches are floating on the water and the sparkling shape of a fish is now and then visible under the water's surface.
105881: Meeting of a Tributary and the Anduin

Here the fast flowing tributary from the west meets the Anduin in a whirlwind of confusion and chaos. The waters from the tributary crash upon those of the Anduin, making swimming or boating extremely dangerous. The rocky bank towards the east is the only way to exit the river here, if it can be reached amid the white caps and swirling waters of this intersection.
105885: A Ruined Log Dock in the River Anduin

A huge, blackened wooden dock rises from the eastern bank. Like a clumsy stair, the logs lie next to one another, ragged and rotten. Still, it can be used as a comfortable landing place for rafts and boats. Thick brush covers the eastern bank all around the dock; it is clear that it has not had regular use in many years. The river is very wide here, allowing it to drift lazily southwards, perhaps this is why the dock was built at this location.
105886:
The rib-bone of an animated skeleton lies here.
The rib-bone of an animated skeleton lies here.
A half-decayed corpse of a goblin lies rotting on the ground.
Covering a section of ground is a pool of a thick red liquid.
A sturdy trained horse is standing here.

The underground tunnel ends in a small, stinking cave. Among the dark rocks, numerous bones and some half-eaten corpses lies an open area which is clearly a residency of some large beast. A small, worn-looking tunnel leads to the north on the ground level, and judging by the occasional bats that flit above, there is another passageway above, twisting upwards through the darkness.
105887: A smooth, narrow ledge runs along the rock wall near the cavern's ceiling, forming a dangerous path over the dark emptiness where one wrong step can cost a lot. On the southern end, the passageway transforms into a steep tunnel which leads sharply downwards into the rock, while on the northern side of the cavern the rocky path ends up into a small cave. Beyond the edge of this three feet wide ledge only a sheer and probably deadly decline awaits.
105888:
A large bat is here, hanging in the darkness.
The queen bat is here, emitting piercing squeaks.
A large black bat flitters near you.
A large black bat flitters near you.
A large black bat flitters near you.

Surrounded by stalagmites, irregular rock formations and deep shadows of this sinister cavern, this hidden vantage provides a view through a wide crack which splits its rocky floor to the rocky cavern floor located below. A narrow ledge leads southwards, crossing the cavern far above its stony bottom. The way down from this cave is almost vertical, but possibly passable for a skilled climber.
105893: A cold shroud of dark grey mist covers the ground.

This tunnel cuts through the wet soil below the plains. The entire area stinks of the mud above, and everything is dripping wet. The walls and floor are wet and decaying, and countless roots of plants from the plain hang from above and keep touching you. A somewhat strange feeling also fills this place, yet it is hard to exactly say what it is, but it surely feels a bit colder than it should here.
105894: The ever-present stink of decay and corruption here is much stronger than in any other area around and even seems to become corporal and actually feelable. The roots and mud around are much fouler than they naturally could be and small clouds of mist hang over the floor and seem to creep into the roots all around.
105895: Fast Bend in the Anduin River

The Anduin picks up speed as it races through this gorge, flowing faster and more violently than it had been towards the east. It is impossible to exit the river here, as the banks are steep and unforgiving. Sharply turning towards the south, the river carries on.
105896: Sudden Bend in the Great River

Continuing through this gorge, the Anduin rushes in from the north, violently splashing against the walls that make up the banks to the east and south. Flowing out and to the west, the Anduin River opens up and grows calmer.
105914: A spirit floats around, making strange magical gestures (glowing).

The underground river that once rushed through the caves is long gone, leaving only smooth rock behind. The cave has a high ceiling which is lowering in the south, towards the gaping mouth of a tunnel, where a passageway is leading deeper into the caves. The rock walls have been worked in places making sure that the path is thoroughly wide enough. Stone steps leading up at the northern wall end with a rocky door hiding the passage from outside.
105915:
An arrow lies on the ground.
An arrow lies on the ground.

A wide chamber has been skilfully carved to the stone; the work has respected the earth's form and veins while anyway making room for a large square. A decorated, bear-shaped fountain stands in the middle of the cave, strangely not bearing any signs of decay and violence that has obviously raged through this hall. The walls are decorated with carvings, some of them are still visible under the dirt, red stains and dust that overwhelms the place now.
105916:
The rib-bone of a no-longer animated skeleton lies here.
Little parts of a broken weapon are lying on the ground.
A large, dusty alcove sits in a wall, smelling of soot.
A dark intangible shadow turns to face you (red aura).
A dark intangible shadow turns to face you (red aura).
A spirit floats towards you and howls with an evil laughter (red aura).

This place has been the living and sleeping area for the inhabitants of this cave. Now the sleeping alcoves are empty, and the furniture has been razed or rotten away. Signs of a fierce battle are still visible around the room, as one can recognise the crude marks left by slashing swords and hitting axes in the stone. The stone floor is littered with broken dishes, old bones and some tattered furs.
105917:
A small hunting knife lies on the ground.
A pan is here, ready for use.

The small side chamber is littered with barrels, chests and crates which take up most of the room here. In the far end corner, crammed in a small free space between two storage boxes, lies a large pile of old animal furs. It appears that this cave has not only been used for storage, but as a sleeping chamber as well. The chamber is separated from the larger open area in the east with an old, rotten door.
105918:
A patch of moss grows here on a wet, flat stone.
Tollin the Dwarf, wielding a mighty dwarven axe, is standing here (glowing).

A narrow, slippery-looking staircase descends along the cavern walls from high above, directly to a wide underground pool which has occupied this abandoned cave. The ice cold water is black and calm, disturbed only by an occasional quiet plop of dripping water which sends tiny ripples across the surface. The room and the corridor that once existed here are sunken into deep water, but the passageway continues again in the east where the ground rises from the water.
105919:
A huge statue made of stone suddenly turns to life.
A huge statue made of stone suddenly turns to life.

Unlike the upper level of this underground stronghold, this skilfully decorated room shows no signs of destruction done by the time, and no mischief caused by the enemy. The walls contain small shelves and a few large carvings in the stone. A massive, arched doorway leads to the east; its broad frames are uninviting, discouraging to go forward. A row of statues sculpted into forms of mighty Beornings stand on the both sides of the doorway.
105920:
A stone sarcophagus lies on the floor.
A large flat rock lies here, its surface etched with markings.
A noticeable crack runs down one of the walls.
A huge statue made of stone suddenly turns to life.
A huge statue made of stone suddenly turns to life.

An ancient, underground riverbed has been transformed into a simple but beautiful sanctum, which seems to be abandoned a long time ago. The room is dominated by a large, smooth rock altar which has probably been carved out from the bedrock itself. Above the altar, three symbols are visible in the rocky wall: a huge bear, the river and the moon. Some kind of disaster has hit this sanctum in the past, as the eastern side has caved in, and a wide crack runs across the back wall.
105922:
A soft leather jerkin is on the ground.
You see two piles of silver coins on the ground.
A pair of soft leather pants are lying here.
There are two sealed clay jars here.
A small box has been left here.
A large cockroach is crawling on the floor.
A large cockroach is crawling up the wall.

This cellar had originally been constructed using large granite blocks, but now the partly collapsed walls have been temporarily repaired by rough wooden planks. To allow storage of clothing and other items large iron nails have been hammered into the planks. On the top shelves in the back corner some small boxes and jars, containing various foods, have been placed, while the lower shelves are filled with various tools.
105924:
Traces of pale red and white tones form the aura of this place.
A cloud of black, icy shards is here, fighting YOU .
Tasen the Hobbit, wielding a sharp thorn, is here, fighting a cloud of black, icy shards.
All around is only darkness and the temperature is freezing cold. The air and floor do not feel like substance at all, yet what you actually breathe and stand on is impossible to tell.
105925:
The remains of a black fungus lie here in a heap of rotting compost.
A worm is here slithering around.

It is unclear if the roots of the surrounding trees and bushes have grown into a natural cavern, if this here are the remains of a once mighty tree that has completely decayed by now, or if the tight space here has formed due to other means. All around are rotting roots that are mixed with dark, wet and somewhat muddy soil. A very strong stench of foulness and decay fill the air and nearly makes it unbreathable.
105926: A huge black fungus is here, exuding a foul stench.

A narrow crack in the soft and stinking soil leads further south and descends a bit. It cannot be said for sure if the walls and floor are just soft or are covered with a spongy, foul mass of... something. A deeply grey mist covers the ground at the southern end of this crack. From every direction grow dark, very unhealty roots into this space.
105927: A cold shroud of dark grey mist covers the ground (red aura).

It appears that corruption and rot have grown so strong here, that the soil itself became victim to decay and fell apart, creating this space. Rotting roots stick from every direction, and a thick mist hinders vision. The air feels freezing cold, and the strong stench bites your nose.
105928: The corpse of a sleuthing orc is lying here.

Bones of small animals and tufts of brown fur litter the ground of this cavern. This must have once been the resting place of a big mammal or two - perhaps a bear. The air has a musty odour and all noises seem to absorb into the brown dirt that makes up the walls of the cavern, lending to its quiet, eerie aura.
105929: Massive trees and dark, dense vegetation border the age-old, sandy road running through the forest. The road was originally several yards wide, but since then the forest has overwhelmed it in several places, and only a narrow trail remains. A tangled mess of leaves, ferns and branches grows around and above the road forming a thick cover of vegetation and absorbing most of the light and sounds to itself which creates an echoless and oppressive atmosphere.
105930: This is the place where the Old Forest Road meets the border of Mirkwood. The huge, gloomy forest wall seems to continue endlessly, as ancient and malevolent looking trees fulfil the view by towering into great heights. The edge of Mirkwood is intact, save for a place where an arching tunnel mouth looms between two massive, leaning tree trunks. An old, worn sign stands by the road, and behind it the road disappears into the dark, silent foliage. Only a short way into the forest an old tree has fallen recently and blocks the path with its entangled crown.
105931: A trail of densely packed soil covered with gravel makes its way through high grass and bushes. Roots break the carefully laid-out path from time to time. The forest looms over the trail, with beech and oak growing very dense both in the north and south. Darkness engulfs Mirkwood in all directions save to the east and west, where the fictive safety of the trail continues.
105932: Some parts of the forest have been cleared of their once majestic trees. An old trail makes its way through Mirkwood. Old stumps alongside the road are covered in old, grey moss, and others infested with malicious fungi and pests. The forest itself lies dense, but traversable, to the north. In the south it once again grows tall, and the trees stand close, denying any possible way for further exploring. The trail continues its slithering route through the heavy undergrowth in the east and west.
105933: A huge warg is here, moving in for the kill.

Stumps and roots interrupt the weather-beaten old trail, which was made by pebbles and gravel being laid over densely packed black soil. The trail has no defining borders, simply merging into the young trees of the forest on either side. The woods grow unfriendly and twisted to the south, leaving only a small passage available for further travel. To the north the trees grow in dense lines, looming in a threatening manner over the pathway. The trail itself continues its way through Mirkwood to the east and west.
105934: The trail rises a few feet here, having been built on a mound of dirt, as it makes its way through the stout, tall trees. The terrain is relatively undamaged. The few huge branches and tree trunks which have fallen lie covered in vines, moss and various other plants. The menacing oak and beech lean over the trail, shutting out the natural light efficiently with their crowns. The old forest trail extends its arms to the east and west.
105935: Fallen branches and twigs lie scattered across the trail. Small pebbles and decomposing vegetation lie in small mounds, serving as homes for various insects. Tree stumps, covered by fungi and moss, lie dead alongside the pathway. Low, forested hills rise tall in the south, engulfed in a dark, menacing gloom. The trail itself continues its path to the east and west.
105936: Zigzagging its way through the grass which stands several feet tall, the trail cannot avoid the disrupting power of ancient roots. Decayed shrubs and fallen trees line the trail. The threat of the forest is ever present, with its oak, beech and fir uneasily following every move of possible intruders. The trail marches on to the east and west.
105937: Mirkwood grows dense in the north, completely engulfed in darkness. The forest is murky and its vegetation leaves little space for exploration. Weathered and old, this road slithers through stumps and tall grass to the east and west. At the feet of a great oak a bear's den has been pillaged and destroyed.
105938: The trees grow dense to the south, growing tall on a forested ridge. To the north the slope leads downwards into a pitch black forest, while to the east and west the dwarven-made road continues its uneasy path. Alongside the forest road lie burned-out shrubs and trees, with young plants growing up out of the fallen and withered remains. The wood appears to sway slowly back and forth, hovering over the trail, closely watching all of its immediate surroundings, awaiting new travellers.
105939: The road shows signs of neglect, as if rarely travelled and never maintained. Dark green bushes, vines and shrubs lie spread across the forest floor. In some places roots have extended their arms from the ground, disrupting the once-level surface of the road. The forest with its gnarled, twisting trees grows very dense both in the north and south, while the ravaged road continues to the east and west.
105940: Beech and oak closely line the road, warily guarding the secrets of the forest. Felled trees and their gnarled branches lie broken next to the pathway, most of them heavily clad with fungi and mosses. The road itself leads south and west. Vile darkness is spread across the forest, aided by the heavy forest canopy which blocks out the natural light. The air is still, but somehow full of the uncanny silence of Mirkwood.
105941: A blackened, dense soil forms the foundation for what once could have been a major road through the forest. For centuries the wilderness has fought its way onto the pathway, covering it in mosses and shrubs, sometimes disrupting it with the roots of the great trees lining it on either side. The road cuts its way through the heavy forest to north and east.
105942: A very large, hairy man is standing here, examining you carefully.

What looks like an ancient, mostly overgrown thoroughfare spans from east to west. Plain grass covers most of the ground, while dark, twisted and rotten trees tower on both the south and north side of the road. A muddy path can be discerned closer to the southern half of the road, and small footprints are obvious in a few wet muddy spots.
105943: A sprawling green bush of stinging nettle grows here.

An overgrown road stretches through this forest from east to west. Waist-high shrubs grow here and there along the road. Great trees stand beside the road like enormous, blackened guardians; shielding against the daylight from the sky above and cloaking what lies beyond them with their massive, tangled bulk. The road must see some use these days, as a path of trampled grass can be seen at the southern edge of the road.
105944: A slightly rusted casserole lies here.

Thick dark trees line this partly overgrown forest road. The massive oaks and beeches that grow here reach over and across the path, blocking out the sky above. A small niche on the northern side of the road looks like it has been used as a resting place for travellers recently: a circle of stones mark the spot that has been used as a fireplace.
105945: As the road approaches a turn, the forest grows thicker and branches entangle themselves across and above the road, creating an impregnable roof. Strings of spider webs hang from a few branches, and trees on both sides of the road are covered in silky webs. High grass covers most of the roadway, but what looks like a trampled path through the grass meanders along the southern edge.
105946: Bend in the Old Forest Road

The road here bends from south to west, striking boldly through a dark, musty and rotten alley of giant oak trees. Above, an impenetrable ceiling of boughs and old cobwebs obscures the sky. The leaves of the canopy are withered and infested with silky webs and small spiders. The ground is covered in clumps of clay and patches of pale, yellow grass like thin fur on a giant beast.
105947: A fallen tree lies on the ground, its clump of roots pointing upwards.

The road bends in from the north and deflects towards the east as it makes its way through the dense, dark forest. Withered dead grass covers the roadway and a few dried-up shrubs grow close to the southern tree line. A small muddy patch stretches from the north to the east, parallel to the roadway: it looks as if the road is being used sometimes, after all. An old log lies across the road, preventing anyone from passing by on a carriage or a cart. Branches and boughs reach in from all sides above, creating a roof-like structure interwoven with old, decaying cobwebs.
105948: This overgrown roadway stretches out from east to west. It is covered in thick, waist-high grass, peppered with dense, thorny shrubs and the occasional oak or beech sapling. North of the road stands a massive wall of mighty oaks, whose thick boughs reach over and across the road. South of the road, there is a seemingly younger forest where beech and oak grow in varied and somewhat eerie shapes. At a casual glance it looks like the beeches have yellow, black-eyed faces and the oaks have snarling, fanged mouths - upon closer inspection it can be discerned that it is just the way they have grown.
105949: Branches and boughs from trees on both sides of this overgrown road reach over it, creating an impregnable roof of dark leaves and foul, worm-scarred branches. The road itself is mostly covered in pale grasses and clumps of withered, dead shrubs. A small, well-trampled path follows the roadway along its southern edge, maybe a trace of whoever has been using this forsaken road recently.
105950: Long ago, someone cleared a large patch of forest in this area, and created a camp alongside the Old Forest Road. Looking around, one can find a number of traces of whoever used this place: an old well was dug here, some rocks are arranged like a fire place, rotting planks and rusted nails litter the ground, and a broken old wooden bucket tied to a decrepit rope lies next to the well. Whoever it was who once used this place as a base seems to be long gone.
105951: Enormous, sinister-looking oaks line both sides of this dark, forsaken road. On the southern side, a thick gaggle of black roots and vines snakes up onto the roadway; it is as though they were actively seeking to suffocate the road and cover it entirely. A thin trail can be discerned on the northern half of the roadway, where heavy feet have plodded a path through the yellow, waist-high grass.
105952: Oak and beech are the two dominant tree species in this dark and shadowy forest. The canopy above blocks out all chance of ever seeing the sky. A small pool of water can be seen along the northern side of the overgrown roadway, its surface covered with rotting leaves and absolutely quivering with the activities of mosquito larvae. A short, squat tree grows in the middle of the roadway, surrounded by wild thorny bushes and dense grass.
105953: At this part of the Old Forest Road, canopy does not hang over the road, allowing a clear view to the open sky. The road continues its journey east and west through Taur-e-Ndaedelos, the Sindarin name for Mirkwood, meaning Forest of Great Fear. On both sides of the road, heavy foliage and dark bushes warn travellers to stay on the beaten path.
105954: In an almost surprising fashion, the road dog-legs into a tight turn here. Dense vegetation gives no easy entrance to Mirkwood proper as the sides of the road are fully covered with thorns and brambles. Lurching oak and birch lean out over the road from above, heavy grey-green mosses dangling from them.
105955:
The corpse of a rabid, grey wolf is lying here.
The corpse of a starved grey wolf is lying here.
A pile of dry, brown leaves lies here.
A black wolf pads restlessly, looking for its next prey.

The Old Forest Road bends north-east underneath a canopy of thick limbs that almost completely block out any external light. Strange sounds emanate from the woods on all sides of the road and the feeling that something or someone is watching is somewhat disquieting. Old leaves and dried moss crackle underfoot, snapping and cracking loudly in the tense silence.
105956: The road is clear and easy to follow here, despite the thorn-bushes and thistles that are slowly regaining the area. Debris fallen from the trees litters the road, making the going slow and difficult. On both sides of the road, black trees are stretching towards it, as if to drive away the travellers who do not belong here.
105957: Greedy branches interlace overhead to form a dark canopy above the road. Leaves crunch on the ground loudly underfoot, and the tension of Mirkwood fills the air. Long, putrid mosses sway gently just overhead as creatures rustle and scurry through the nearby woods.
105958: A large, black butterfly is fluttering about erratically.

Here the dark trees bordering the road have managed to reach across to intertwine high overhead, forming a living ceiling of sorts that completely blocks the sunlight. Long, hairy mosses in hues of grey, green, and white dangle down like ancient beards left unshaven. The feeling of being watched is heightened by the canopy above.
105959: The road looks just as unattended here as everywhere else. Grass and ferns cover most of it, however the seemingly once so majestic way can still be discerned where the vegetation is sparse. The trees seem to have been closing in on the road over the years, making it a lot narrower than in its glory days.
105960: Bend in the Old Forest Road

The road has a gravel surface here, with green grass and wild bushes growing in profusion over it. It makes a long bend from south to the west, following the edges of a high cliff that can be observed in the east, high above the road. Dark-green bushes, with long, sharp thorns grow on the north side of the road.
105961: Bend in the Old Forest Road

The Old Forest Road turns significantly here and continues to the east and north. The road has not seen any maintenance for centuries, and at places it is just a wide trail between the bushes, not a road anymore. Tall trees loom above, their dense foliage casting deep shadows upon the road.
105962: A stocky mountain mule is here, waiting to serve.

What once was a well-kept, well-travelled passage through the forest of Mirkwood, has decayed over the centuries into a faint memory of its former self, being now an overgrown, grassy path that runs through the menacing forest. Bordered by a steep cliff and dense, black willows, the road continues to the west and east.
105963: A lush carpet of grass gives barely any hint that the Old Forest Road here was once a majestic, busy passageway through Mirkwood Forest. Occasional old tracks are barely visible through the grass and forest debris of littered leaves, fallen branches, and loose rocks.
105964: An old path, at times only two or three yards wide, is all that remains of the Old Forest Road as it runs through dense shrubbery of black wild bushes. From above the road is shadowed by thick, leaf-covered branches and hanging vines which totally block the sky from view. Tough, sharp-looking weeds grow on the ground and beyond the brush stand the towering, huge trees of Mirkwood.
105965: A Bend in the Old Forest Road

The Old Forest Road makes a long, sweeping bend here, following the upwards slope of a grass-covered ridge towards the north. To the west it leads down the ridge and into the dark shadows of Mirkwood forest. The road itself is mostly overgrown with grass and weed, although a trampled path in the middle of the ancient road is proof that it is still used occasionally.
105966: Although the wilderness has taken back most of the Old Forest Road, with grass and shrubs now growing on the hard-packed earth, it would take many years still for the last traces of the road to vanish. Large, brown bushes dot the ridge, sprawling thorny things often several yards across.
105967: The ancient road moves along the highest point of the ridge, where the grass-covered ground is flat and solid. There are few obstacles to force the road to bend or detour up here and it follows a straight route from east to west. The grass grows high and wild, swaying gently whenever a breeze stirs the air.
105968: The dense grass grows several feet tall, long stalks swaying gently whenever a breeze stirs the air. Many different types of bushes and shrubs also thrive on the gently rolling ridge, most of them tangled masses full of prickly thorns. The Old Forest Road follows the highest point of the ridge from east to west.
105969: A brown snail is crawling across the ground here leaving a slimy trail behind.

This wide hollow is filled with a dense growth of large, tangled bushes which form a complex mess of vegetation all around the area. Towards the east and west, the ground seems to rise softly in the form of two long, grass-covered slopes. Little can be seen of the Old Forest Road, the thoroughfare being mainly discernible by a lessened density in undergrowth.
105970: The grass-covered slope rises in a soft curve from west to east and the Old Forest Road follows the slope faithfully towards the top of the ridge. The grass grows high and wild and is interrupted only by clusters of large, thorny bushes. Dark trees of Mirkwood lean over the road on both sides, their branches almost meeting above.
105974: A fallen tree lies on the ground, its clump of roots pointing upwards.

Giant, oppressive trees stand tall and silent, their canopy enveloping the forest below. On the ground level dense thickets and numerous spider webs make it hard to traverse this area. Mosses and ferns have spread throughout the undergrowth. Some fallen trees lie here, slowly decomposing and acting as a valuable source of nutrients for the green and white mould that resides on them.
105975: These hills bear very little life, only a sprinkling of grass and some fairly gnarled bushes. Eastward, the ominous border of Mirkwood can be observed, dark and thick. Erupting from the ground here and there are rocks of various sizes and shapes.
105976: The hills here begin to support more life as evidenced by the thickening stands of oak and birch. A light ground-covering of sparse grass provides a soft layer of yellow-green while small, dark green bushes sprout up here and there. Among the rocks a rare sight is visible: a trickle of clear water emerging from the hillside, running among the rocks, and disappearing again to the ground. Birds not brave enough to enter Mirkwood directly, make their homes here in relative safety.
105977: Hills in the Forest of Mirkwood

The bald steep hills stretch in every direction. The ground is barren, desolate and bare of any living vegetation. Loose rocks and smaller sharp chips of rock cover the ground, making walking on foot difficult and unpleasant. There is an abrupt downhill to the west, and almost vertical wall of rock to the east. So steep are the hills that one cannot see a single tree, despite being actually surrounded by the giant forest.
106008: A great wolf with coal-black eyes stares intently at you, drooling saliva.

Prickly shrubs and thorny bushes pack what little spaces there are between the majestically tall trees. Dark, flying shapes flit from branch to branch overhead and the ever-present insect buzzing seems a bit louder in this place. Unseen creatures rustle within the deep thickets as their home is disturbed.
106009:
The corpse of a giant earth beetle is lying here.
A desecrated mound rises from the ground, its contents scattered.

The area is surrounded on all sides by dark foliage which makes travelling difficult and limits visibility to minimum. The trees stand tall, reaching so high that their tops are not visible in the deep darkness. There is a straight row of mounds on the ground, next to something that was once a man-made structure: now only the overgrown foundation gives hint to its former existence.
106010: An unusual haze has settled upon this part of Mirkwood. Though not quite at the level of fog, this mist is thick enough to reduce visibility in all directions. The filtering effect gives the forest shapes a grotesque quality and suggests movement just outside of reach.
106011:
A great wolf with coal-black eyes stares intently at you, drooling saliva.
A giant, mean looking earth beetle is standing here.

The normal forest sounds lessen in this deep and dark portion of Mirkwood. Spider webs have been woven between the black trunks, protruding branches and hanging vines. So dense is the vegetation that only the quiet crunch of steps on dried leaves comes through. The air feels close and tight, making it more difficult to breathe.
106017: Great, serpentine vines cling to the trunks of various trees, climbing upwards until they disappear between the boughs above. The forest has no distinguishing features by which to orientate, it is all ancient, twisted trees casting black shadows in the perpetual gloom. Tangles of thorny brush grow throughout the forest, with occasional cobwebs being spun between the trees.
106018: Dying and rotting trees litter the landscape as Mirkwood turns a sickly grey pallor. It seems as if a sickness or power has been spreading from the south for ages now, causing decay and destruction. Even the fungi and lichens cannot seem to survive here in this sickly woods.
106019: The overhanging tree branches and hanging cobwebs create a sad, dismal feel to Mirkwood. It seems that after being angry for so long, the trees have fallen over, leaning against each other in gloomy resignation. Even the thorny bushes and lesser vegetation here are thin and puny. Everything seems bowed under the weight of ages and permanent darkness.
106020: This part of Mirkwood has a sullen feel to it. The trees seem to be angry at the disturbance yet too depressed to care much. Thick bushes and thin saplings fill in the spaces between the large trunks while decaying leaves mix with needles all over the ground.
106027: Foul webs span across Mirkwood, engulfing the exit south with their complex patterns.

The forest closes in from all directions; watching, listening, disdaining. The powerful trees seem to block efforts to leave and strive to trip, catch, and snag all who try to travel through. Overhead, wind-tossed branches flex down from the black, continuous canopy with each gust.
106028: The tall trees are thick and robust here in Mirkwood Forest. They emanate a sinister power that disdains all non-vegetative life. Creaking and cracking, limbs and boughs seem to vibrate and rustle at the slightest disturbance, giving rise to the feeling that perhaps some form of intelligence persists within the Forest.
106029:
A tremendous black oak looms here.
A tremendous black oak looms here.

Dark, malignant trees loom over this small forest glade, as if trying to reach and hurt any travellers who might venture here. A thick layer of bushes, thorny plants, and undergrowth have mingled together, blocking the way in all directions save to the east. Above, branches and black, scarred trunks are so covered in cobwebs, vines and other tangled vegetation, as to prevent the sunlight from ever touching this place.
106030: A dense network of old trees blocks out the sky with their great crowns. The majority of the darkened trees are covered by a damp, grey moss, which seems to make the air even more humid. Many trees have fallen and lie rotting on the ground to the south, creating a passageway to an old trail. The forest grows close to the north and east.
106032: A fallen tree lies on the ground, its clump of roots pointing upwards.

The trees stand tall and dense, their majestic crowns block out any possible natural light. Fungi and a variety of mosses cover the fallen as well as standing flora, leaving many of the trunks and branches in a brittle state. The forest is growing thicker in all directions, leaving only a narrow passage to the south.
106043: Great oaks reach towards the sky, leaning their great crowns against one another, supporting each other's heavy weight. Together they create a natural blanket blocking most outside light. The undergrowth is extremely dense in the south, forming an impenetrable wall of vegetation. To the north Mirkwood opens up slightly, sloping down towards a trail. It seems possible to travel through the murky vegetation lying to the east.
106045: The skeleton of Mirkwood is slowly starting to wane. Old, rotten trees have fallen to the ground, piling up in the east to form an impermeable wall. This pile of decomposing vegetable matter has turned into a haven for cockroaches, termites and various deteriorating fungi. Dense, heavy forest grows in the north and west, while in the south a trail runs on its way through the woods.
106047: A huge warg is here, moving in for the kill.

Poison ivy reaches out from the trees, entangling fallen trees and decomposed bushes. The stifling humidity makes the already foul air even harder to bear. Some thick vines and roots have been cleared away to the east, leaving a small trail which appears to lead between the bases of the trees. Darkened trunks block any vision to the north and south, leaving weary travellers with just two options for further exploration: down the slope eastwards, or deeper into the dark forest in the west.
106048: The sloping forest falls in from the west, with its trees poised over a myriad of bushes, branches and other fallen vegetation. The ground is covered in a dense mishmash of vines and shrubs. Roots and ivy create a natural roof, keeping out most of the natural light. The shadowed forest continues to rise above you in the south, while in the east it settles slightly. The view to the north is completely blocked by the heavy vegetation.
106049:
An ancient fungus smothers the boulders.
An ancient fungus smothers the boulders.
Massive roots shift uneasily all around you.

Great vines and roots have taken over here, leaving the trees in despair. Leaning towards each other they form a close-to-regular, knitted pattern, shielding the lower forest from any outside light. An old animal's den has been completely ruined by the abundant vegetation. The boulders and rocks by the entrance seem to have frozen in time, forever stuck among the twisted roots. The forest ivy climbs several feet up into the air towards the west, creating a brittle roof.
106050:
A black, thorny bush grows here, enshrouded in a murky gloom.
Some roots lie here waiting to ensnare weary travellers.
Massive roots shift uneasily all around you.

Poison ivy descends the trunks of the surrounding trees, together with roots and decomposed trees creating a very cumbersome environment to explore. Similar growth can be seen in the north. In the west the tangles reach for each other, ensnaring each others' stems in midair, forming an impenetrable quilt. Like a fortress wall, Mirkwood rises tall and strong to the south.
106051:
Some thick writhing vines whip all around you.
Some roots lie here waiting to ensnare weary travellers.

Enormous roots of black oak trees rise high above the ground creating an intimidating, tight meshwork, rendering the area extremely difficult to traverse. A change in the structure of vegetation can be noticed to the east and north, where vines and ivy seem to seek the forest floor. A steep, overgrown slope blocks any further travel to the west while the imposing vegetation to the south doesn't leave any obvious route to move forward.
106052:
Foul webs span across Mirkwood, engulfing the exit west with their complex patterns.
A black crow flies low to the ground here, looking for carrion to eat.

The great oaks and beech stand tall and proud, their leaves, branches and twigs mingling together in a single mass like a patchwork quilt far up in the air. Roots and vines entangle each other on the ground, as though refusing to reveal any easy way to walk here. Great bushes move uneasily in the north, blocking out any further view in that direction. The whole forest is engulfed in a sombre darkness.
106053:
Some roots lie here waiting to ensnare weary travellers.
A black crow flies low to the ground here, looking for carrion to eat.

Rustling ivy and periwinkle evoke a sense of uneasiness in these forested hills. The vines have engulfed several skeletons of great animals. A smell of decay and death lies heavily on the air. Ruptured tree trunks open up a steep passage further up onto the hills in the east. In the north the darkness leads into a murky place.
106054: Beech, fir and great oaks grow very densely here. Their trunks rise high, aiming their crowns toward the sky. Most natural light is efficiently blocked out by the great Mirkwood canopy. A quick fall to the west leads any travellers through ravaged trunks and vines deeper into the darkness. Downhill in the north and east the aggressive vegetation leaves just enough space for weary travellers to continue their exploration.
106055: The ground makes a steep descent to the south, leaving the peak of the hills behind and leading into a dense growth of oak, fir and beech. Here the surroundings are somewhat less overgrown, yet the forest canopy maintains its density, blocking out all natural light. Just below a great oak tree, a large bird's nest has fallen and been looted, and is now slowly decaying, a pile of debris. A slope full of malicious vegetation leads up westwards, deeper into the gloom.
106056: A fallen tree lies on the ground, its clump of roots pointing upwards.

The hills are low, with darkened trees leaning over one another. Fir, beech and oak alternate in regular patterns, together building almost solid walls of trees -- as though on purpose... The heavy, thick roots of fallen trunks intertwine with hanging vines to make the going treacherous, with almost no clear way through for the average traveller. A steep slope to the north climbs into yet more forested hills, while to the west the forest seems slighly lower.
106059: An almost fortified forest rises up to the south and east, standing tall and proud. Decomposing vegetation lies scattered over the forest floor, making further travel quite demanding, and the malicious vines hanging down from the branches of the trees leave little room to move. To the north the heavy forest covers more treacherous hills.
106061: A huge black fungus is here, exuding a foul stench.

Colossal, twisted trees hover over one another, composing a dreadful pattern with their interwoven branches and foliage. Gnarled, fungi-clad branches and roots encompass the surrounding, spreading a smell of death and decay. The vile forest stretches its darkness across the landscape, allowing for few easily accessible spaces. With some effort the area may be further explored in the east. In the south Mirkwood opens up onto a minor trail.
106062:
A few hawthorn berries lie on the ground, slowly rotting.
A few hawthorn berries lie on the ground, slowly rotting.
A sprawling, twisted tree grows here.
A huge warg is here, moving in for the kill.

The corrupted forest displays a scene of twisted trees, bending over one another in agony. Mossy roots, gnarled and withered, create a treacherous environment, demanding careful navigation through holes and pits. Periwinkle and ground ivy grow into a frantic meshwork in the east, blocking any possibility of further exploration, while in the north small trails and narrow alleys between the trees allow for investigation.
106063: The trees ensnare each other with their vast branches and roots, purposefully creating an almost-impenetrable mesh of vegetation. Many great trees have fallen heavily to the ground, and are now festering with termites and centipedes. A faint mist spreads across the forest floor. Traces of strife mark the trunks of the ancient trees and thorny bushes; but despite being scorched by fire and wounded by axes and arrows, the forest still stands strong. Dark and dreary Mirkwood lies open to further exploration to the east and south, while in the north it turns into an eerie mixture of undergrowth and decay.
106064: Great roots arch a few feet above the ground, partly covered with poison ivy and an assortment of mosses. Thorny bushes grow from the damp ground, surrounded by decomposing foliage. A faint breeze blows through the twisted trees, spreading a thin mist across the floor. The woods appear to be in deep agony, their distorted shapes and wounded trunks witness to a recent onslaught. The trees plunge into a tall thicket in the west, while in the east vines and tangles smother much of the tall tree trunks. In the south, withered forest passes into less dense terrain.
106065:
A huge warg is here, moving in for the kill.
A mountain mule (ulo) is standing here, ridden by you.

Many trees gape open with vicious wounds, a clear reminder of the evil that resides within Mirkwood. Fallen vegetation lies decomposed, scattered among the younger flora, partly covered in ivy, fungi and mosses. Beech and ash create a dark, grey surrounding. The trees appear to hover over you, closely watching every move. The forest expands further into the north and south, closely guarded by the tall shadows of the attentive trees.
106074:
A small and tough weed grows here.
A mountain mule (ulo) is standing here, ridden by you.

Cobweb-covered dark oaks are the dominant species in this area, where a long, hollowed-out tree-trunk is lying on the ground. The canopies above appear infested with silky, lead-grey webs. To the west, the forest opens up onto what looks like a disused, grass-covered roadway.
106075: The grey-coloured forest seems to lack vitality and strength here. Several once-robust trees, now withered, twist as though in misery. Above and around the trees blasted bushes and shrub remnants scrabble for survival in this devastated landscape, completely covered in huge, sticky spider webs. Tree branches and a few cocoons hang down from the intact canopy, seeming to grab anything that moves under them.
106076: The wicked undergrowth rustles malevolently, shifting and widening.

Penetration deeper into Mirkwood has become extremely difficult as every bush and vine sprouts long and sharp thorns that pierce flesh and snag clothing. The protruding roots of gnarled trees add to the challenge of making it through unscathed.
106077:
A small green mound rises from the ground.
A thick tangle of dark vines is here, fighting Klaees (donny).
Ducaht (tooprettytodie), wielding a great warsword, is here, fighting a thick tangle of dark vines.
Klaees (donny), wielding a heavy morningstar, is here, fighting a thick tangle of dark vines.
Bulg, wielding a great warsword, is here, fighting a thick tangle of dark vines.
Drazud, wielding a two-handed axe, is here, fighting a thick tangle of dark vines.

Like guardians at the entrance to a royal tomb, the heavy oaks and thick birches grow in a dense circle as if preventing one from wandering any further. Their criss-crossed branches angle down to overlay each other like crossed spears and gnarled roots have joined with bristly bushes to block the way.
106078: A shimmering glow is here, emitting pale, green, light.

Time seems to slow in this part of Mirkwood. Majestic firs stand like mighty kings, attended by maples and hazels. Coating the ground like a royal carpet, feather mosses intersperse with acid needle droppings to create a rich, organic fragrance. Twisted vines and fallen branches frame the view in all directions.
106079: The blasted landscape hints at the tale of a massive occurrence that left this area of forest completely barren and lifeless. Ancient, blackened stumps litter the ground, crumbling at the slightest touch. The very air seems to sap energy out of the living. Nothing moves here, nothing lives.
106080:
A small termite is running around making strange sounds.
A small termite is running around making strange sounds.
A small termite is running around making strange sounds.

Musty and dank smells rise off the forest floor from rotting tree trunks and glowing fungi that cover almost everything. Dark insects scuttle through the underbrush on their secret missions. Decaying branches rupture in pungent putrefaction with each step.
106081:
The corpse of a small termite is lying here.
A small termite is running around making strange sounds.

The gloom of Mirkwood covers this area like a wet blanket as huge malicious- looking trees tower above, limiting the visibility and preventing any light from the sky entering here. It is hard to throw off the feeling of being watched and the desire to look behind is very strong. Somewhat surprisingly, an old fence runs through the forest here, blocking the way to the west.
106083:
The corpse of a small termite is lying here.
The corpse of *a Man* is lying here.
The remains of a mass of vines lie here in a heap of rotting compost.
A mass of wriggling vines drops on you from the trees.
A mass of wriggling vines drops on you from the trees.

Dark, giant trees stand tall their stretched branches tangling into the intact canopy above. The ground is covered by roots and thorny bushes with sharp- looking spikes. The underlying depression of the living forest has intensified to a point of morose melancholy. It is as if the trees remember a happier age, long ago, when sunlight permeated the woods and frivolous creatures ran to and fro. Now, the thoughts of ages past are a distant memory reflected in the twisted woods.
106084:
A skeleton of some humanoid lies in the dust.
A swift and agile forest cat moves silently through the vegetation.

Like a badly painted picture, the forest is so tangled with trunks, bushes, vines and other vegetation that it is very difficult to see more than a few feet in any direction. Looking skyward is no better than looking at the ground. The oppression of Mirkwood has become the only point of awareness now.
106085: A cockroach is scuttling across the floor carrying some debris.

A plethora of plants, from common ivy and periwinkle to calluna and crimson clover, grow here. The soggy soil appears to be an ideal place for the heavy vegetation to grow. However, some of the trees have gaping, open wounds on their trunks, and some of them have had their trunks cleaved down the middle. There is a myriad of small bugs and animals nesting in the various bushes and protective spaces created by the warped roots. The surroundings are extremely dense, and together with the never ending darkness of Mirkwood, it makes it difficult to scout anything but the immediate surroundings.
106086: A cluster of dark green, feathery fronds flourishes in the shade.

The air is damp and heavy in this part of Mirkwood. The forest floor consists of mushy soil which is saturated with moisture. Snails, worms and other smaller animals live off the decomposed, fallen vegetation. Spiders have spun their webs between the twisting roots. The roots and vines compose a thick tangle, perfect for setting traps or nesting. The intertwining tree crowns keep the forest in perpetual darkness, making it difficult to discern much else but the immediate surroundings.
106087: Deep in the Tangle of Mirkwood

Some roots lie here waiting to ensnare weary travellers.
Massive roots shift uneasily all around you.

The ground consists of a mixture of nasty-looking mud and decomposing vegetation. The vegetation is heavy, and appears to be thriving in this humid environment. The roots of the beech and oak trees break out from beneath the mud, reaching far across the forest floor. The trees are gnarled and twisted, and their canopies intertwine, supporting each other's heavy crowns. Stumps of old trees stand here and there, completely covered by old, grey moss. Movement through here is very difficult due to the dense undergrowth.
106088: Deep in the Tangle of Mirkwood
The corpse of a pack horse is lying here.

Gradually, the forest terrain is slowly giving way to a marsh here. The puddles of water are quite large in size, while the putrid soil is very porous and water-logged. The gnarled forest is mostly composed of old, grey, withering trees. The air lies heavy and humid in the darkness, and the smell is quite decidedly rancid - almost certainly emanating from some kind of fungi. There are several species of bugs and millipedes crawling around among the brambles and roots on the forest floor.
106089: Deep in the Tangle of Mirkwood
A monstrous grey, putrid fungus is growing on a large oak here.

Here, cracked and broken trees make up a haunting scene. The withered old oaks barely stand up on their own and are being propped up by nasty, corpse-yellow vines. The soil has been washed away from underneath them by flooding, leaving their root systems exposed to the stinking, putrid air. The roots form an extensive meshwork from which strands of dead material hang. Large clusters of bracket fungus are slowly decomposing the fallen trees. A rancid stench pervades this swamp-like forest, and the looming thorn-bushes, together with the dense undergrowth, together create a natural maze.
106090: The corpse of a striped snake is lying here.

This watery, forest-covered bog stretches far in all directions. The earth has been washed away from underneath the withered old trees, leaving their skeletal roots exposed to the air. The roots create natural shelters for small animals and insects. Rancid-smelling fungi and mosses cover many of the malnourished, dying trees. Bushes grow sparsely on patches of semi-dry ground. Great, silken funnel webs cover some of the warped birch and maple trees, and other cobwebs span from trunk to trunk, like bizarre gangways.
106091: Birch and maple trees grow close together in this swampy marsh. Their large roots rise a few feet above the ground due to the abundant water. Here and there, piles of dark soil form small islands that emit a foul, rotting stench. A large carcass lies half-submerged in the dirty water, infested with worms, flies and grotesque, yellow centipedes. The air is extremely damp, and the terrain is arduous to move through. The common ivy which grows between many of the trees gives a good foothold for the silken cobwebs that hang down from the trees. The webs also decorate many of the trunks, where they have trapped a great number of insects.
106092: The trees here are a mix of dead, withered trees that barely stand up, and great oaks that stand on little islands of dark soil in the swamp. Where not completely covered by mosquito-infested pools of water, the porous forest is severely water-logged. A myriad of small animals and bugs buzz around in the air. Fallen trees occupy a great deal of the area, all infested by smelly bracket funguses and spongy mosses. Residues of what once were great cobwebs hang down from the gnarled boughs of the oaks. A pervasive stench of death and decay fills the air of the forest here, unlikely to dissipate any time soon.
106093:
The corpse of *an Elf* is lying here.
*a fearsome Troll* , wielding a blackened spear, is standing here searching for something.
*a grim Man* is sleeping here.

Massive, silken cobwebs intertwined with the skeletal canopies of several trees form this platform sixteen feet up in the air. The space is fairly confined, perhaps six feet by six. A webbed tunnel leads north from here, and passage is also possible down to the forest floor.
106094: Vines and ivy ensnare the gnarled boughs and trunks of the forest. A few trees have fallen heavily to the ground. Completely rotten and on the verge of disintegration, they have succumbed to the heavy undergrowth. Tall thorn-bushes grow dense here, their roots digging deep into the moist soil. The aggressively expanding vegetation makes it very difficult to move on smoothly.
106095: A colony of red ants is here. The ants seem to ignore you.

Here, a mass of vegetation has grown up into the forest canopy, and, supported by the massive branches, now forms a narrow pathway which leads upwards and eastwards. Vile-looking, old trees loom above the lower vegetation, casting the forest into a pitch-dark blackness. Massive amounts of small vermin are crawling around here, feasting on weakened trees and shrubberies. The pale-yellow, warped roots and vines create a very unwelcoming surrounding, and the options for going forward are limited to going south, or venturing up along the packed, dense vegetation.
106096:
A huge black fungus is here, exuding a foul stench.
A black squirrel peers down from the branches of the trees.

Tangled branches, thick vines and thorny shrubs form a tangled slope here, creating a tilted path downwards to the west, and upwards to the east. Underneath and above, decomposing, water-logged, brown foliage serves to hold the unsteady formation in place. Fungi and mosses thrive down below at ground level, and thorny bushes makes passage in other directions impossible.
106097: Massive, black, oozing vines reach out from the choked canopy.

The withered forest has grown particularly dense here. Vines and common ivy ensnare whole trees, wrapping themselves around the trunks in a suffocating embrace. The leafy branches have grown so closely intertwined as to form a kind of platform in the forest canopy, high above the forest floor. The damp air renders the boughs and branches slippery, making footing here far from sure. In fact, the whole structure seems decidedly unstable.
106098: Branches, shrubs, vines and roots all intertwine with each other, creating a tangled platform above the forest floor. Around the platform, the tall trunks of gruesome-looking trees rise upwards, disappearing into the dark, intact canopy which keeps the forest in eternal shade. The air here is extremely damp and saturated with an unwholesome, foetid quality.
106099: A beautiful and docile horse is standing here.

Shrubs and other forms of undergrowth grow far and wide, getting their nourishment from the water-soaked soil. The forest floor is quite soft and spongy, and water collects in small pools at certain places. The trees intertwine with one another, their trunks twisted and gnarled. The roots and vines, together with the overabundance of bushes, form an extremely difficult environment to travel in.
106100: Strands of perpetual fog pass across this dreadful, opaque mire. The water stands two, at times three feet deep. The trees look sombre and malnourished, and their crowns barely hang on to their trunks - yet still they keep the forest in a state of permanent shade. An odour of decay lies in the air. Great roots and vines intertwine with the trees, and massive thorn-bushes have made this place their home.
106101: Here, the withered tree crowns above manage to keep the natural light from piercing through forest canopy. Warped roots and branches intertwine with the layers of heavy undergrowth beneath, creating a maze of alleys and passageways. Navigating through the vivid tangled forest is extremely arduous. To the south, a thick tangle of thorn-bushes grows taller than a man, forming a funnel-like opening that by the looks of it could be hard to pass through.
106107: A light mist spreads over the dark mire. The withered forest is half-way to death; many great trees have fallen, semi-covered by the putrid water. Great thorn-bushes, covered by moss and fungi, rise tall between many of the trees. Where such vegetation still manages to grow, the plants have become tangled together, which severely limits the choice of routes for further scouting.
106110: Thorny and twisted, the roots and vines rise high and dense here. The trees stand closely together, nearly smothered by the heavy underbrush. Periwinkle and common ivy climb up every trunk, whether it is lying down or standing up. The soil is saturated with water, and it emits a foul stench. The sordid remains of a huge animal skeleton has sunk deep into the bog, where its once so white bones now have taken on the brown, dark hue of the swampy ground.
106113: A large bonfire is burning here.

Massive, vine-ensnared trees surround this forest glade on all sides but to the south. The site itself appears to be the home of someone or something that does not care about tidiness or organisation. Dirty cots have been haphazardly hung from branches and vines, and shards of broken pottery litter the ground. In the centre of the glade, a number of thick, smoking logs are burning on a huge fire, making the air soot-ridden and difficult to breathe. Various items used for cooking and drinking have been thrown around the fire as if whoever tossed them there did not care for them anymore, and did not mind if they were destroyed. At the south-eastern corner of the space, an eight foot, carved pole has been erected.
106126:
A mass of dark green leaves clings to a wall.
A diamondback rattlesnake is coiled here, ready to strike.

Two and a half walls and a narrow, unoccupied floor space between the invading bushes, vines and a massive, fallen tree trunk is all that is left of this cottage. The furniture has rotted away and the mighty forest has taken over. Dark, sharp thorns seem to reach out towards the open area, foul-smelling vines are hanging down from the dark canopy, and black, mostly rotten leaves and other vegetation fill the ground.
106127: The ground is hard and lacks any real nourishment. The darkened soil cracks open in places where great roots pop out. Despite the sad state of the soil, there are great bushes and thorns growing, oak and beech standing tall, all of which engulf the forest in darkness. The beech and oak line up, creating massive walls in the west and east. To the south, among an incredible mass of vines, brush and decomposed vegetation lie the remains of a completely dilapidated dwelling.
106128: Withered by the passage of time, the forest looms in its perpetual state of darkness. The tree crowns subtly shift, uneasily following the inexorable winds. In places, great branches have fallen down and become submerged, rotting under mosses and thorny bushes. Some trees have fallen completely, creating large craters where their roots once sought nourishment from the ground. Vines and roots make up a lot of the flora, hanging down from boughs, dipping into bushes and old stumps. The forest seems to stretch far in all directions, but it is hard to see through the dense forest.
106129: This stand of ancient beech and oak once thrived on the nutritious soil of the great Greenwood, but in this age the once proud and healthy trees are struggling mightily against each other.
