With trees grappling with each other and everything around them with great, massive roots and vines, it seems like a war more than a forest. Their vast crowns blot out most of the sky, leaving the forest floor in perpetual shadows. Vines and ivy grow on a few fallen specimens, as well as hanging in rotting heaps from boughs and trunks. The forest seems to continue endlessly in all directions.
106130: A bear is here, covered with coarse black fur.

A range of different trees make up this densely packed forest: the crowns of beech, birch, ash and the odd oak combine to create a densely packed canopy above. The trees all look old and withered, some with apparent scars from axes. The forest floor is heavily layered with a myriad of shrubbery, thorns and periwinkles.
106131:
A sprawling, twisted tree grows here.
A huge grizzly bear is here, roaming the wild.
A bear cub is here, looking around for something to play with.
A bear cub is here, looking around for something to play with.
A bear cub is here, looking around for something to play with.

The forest slopes down and inwards, creating a large pit full of thorny briars, bushes, vines and undergrowth. Gnarled and twisted trees lean in towards each other, interweaving their huge boughs into a dense canopy above. Poison ivy encircles some of the trees and branches, drooping down close to the forest floor like a lifeless strand of web.
106132: Dense and discoloured old trees stand here like corrupted, menacing sentinels. Their boughs are reaching towards each other almost as if they are trying to cooperate in keeping the daylight above away from the ground. Pale, yellow grasses and blackish, dark-green mosses grow on the spongy ground, making this marshy forest hard to travel through.
106133: The fir and oak trees here grow tall and majestic, leaning their far-spanning crowns onto one another. Roots expand out from the bases of the trunks at certain places, some of which are covered in silky, immaculate spider webs. Fungi and moss cover most parts of the fallen, decomposing vegetation. Mirkwood lies dark and reasonably open all around.
106134: A tall pine tree grows here.

There is an odd mixture of fir, oak and pine growing here. The trees grow densely together, stretching their trunks and crowns toward the sky. Massive boughs intertwine to create an immaculate quilt, denying any natural light from seeping through. Tangled vines and assorted species of ivy have spread across the forest floor, covering fallen old trees and branches. Mirkwood lies open for further exploration to the east and west.
106135: Great roots span across the forest floor, intertwining with dense, thorny bushes and ensnaring tangles of vines, choking everything in sight. Warped, pale boughs stretch through the air. Vines are wrapped around many of the great tree trunks, offering good hideouts for nesting or trapping animals. The forest seems to shift restlessly, almost as if it were alive. The ashen gloom of the surrounding area expands to the west, while in the east and north Mirkwood stands in complete darkness.
106136: Thick vines hang down from the gnarled forest ceiling, half-covered by old, withered moss. A scent of decay is noticeable throughout the forest. A large cocoon lies at the foot of a great oak, decomposing and seemingly infested with larvae and tiny gnats. In the east, the forest rises up like a vast wall, making it completely impossible to travel there, while the other directions offer more accessible environments.
106137: A dense patch of dark ferns grows in the shade.

The humidity here is higher than elsewhere in the forest, and the trees appear even more twisted and sinister-looking. Withered old silky spider webs consume the canopies of leaves and branches, blotting out the sky above. The ground slopes gently southwards, where the ground gradually becomes more soggy. A thick tangle of thorny shrubs blocks all passage north and west of here, while further travel into Mirkwood is possible to the south and east.
106138: Far above, the vast canopy of leaves and branches encloses the surrounding area with its dense, suffocating presence. The trees stand intertwined with one another, their trunks partly covered by dark green moss. Infestations of fungi grow on old, rotting stumps. Clusters of dead roots lie partly covered beneath the damp soil. There is a powerful odour of decay in the air. Mirkwood grows even denser to the west, while to the east and north the forest opens up for further exploration.
106139: Perversely twisted, dark trees are growing increasingly thickly here. The ground slopes abruptly to the south, creating a horse-shoe shaped bowl lined with thorny, impassable shrubs and man-high bushes. The only way out of here seems to be to the south, further into the darkness of Mirkwood.
106140: Great dark trees reach far up into the air, their immense canopies intertwining into a dense quilt that blocks out all sunlight. The dark trees are shifting into a shade of grey, with silvery spider webs covering large chunks of the tree trunks. Large bushes and thorns grow here in dense clusters, making the terrain difficult to travel through. The forest opens up onto narrow natural pathways to the south and east.
106141: Life has been completely sucked out of the flora here. Great branches and fallen shrubbery lie decomposed across the forest floor. The scent of death spreads around the forest. Great webs span across the tree crowns, some of which create immaculate patterns, others half-broken and abandoned. The withered forest creates narrow, north-south bound alleys, while to the east Mirkwood refuses anyone further exploration.
106144: A Path along the Forest Wall

A hollow tree is growing upright here.
A sturdy pack horse is standing here.

Beech and oak rise tall in the north, creating a virtually impenetrable wall. The path is slowly making its way through the darkened vegetation, leaving few open routes to travel. A great tree can be seen in the distance to the west, while in the south and east a veil of darkness spreads across the woods. Looming over the trail, Mirkwood stands tall and dark in the south, leaving no passage to reach the meadows beyond the forest borders.
106145: A Trail through a Great Tree

Two enormous beeches have grown into each other, living in symbiosis. Divided only at the base, they create a large underground cavern, protected from rain and wind. Their bark is darkened and withered from old age, with patches of light grey moss covering it. Malicious fungi infest parts of the old, brittle roots, adding to the intense, foul smell which spreads across the air. The never-ending darkness of Mirkwood appears less stifling here. The trail running through this natural cave continues its path to the east and west.
106146: Atop the Crowns of the Trees
A black squirrel peers down from the branches of the trees.

The tree on whose crown you now perch rises far towards the sky, overlooking its neighbours of oak and beech. Stretching towards the horizon to the south the landscape is one of vast plains and brush, while to the north, west and east the dense forest of Mirkwood forms a great quilt of leaves. Great, gnarled branches offer good support here.
106153:
The remains of a coil of oozing vines lie here in a heap of rotting compost.
Some black, oozing vines reach out from the choked canopy towards you.
A large brown snake with black patches is coiled here.

Vines and roots create a forest floor shaped like a pit filled with serpents. Shadows of branches, trunks and roots form a complex pattern on the ground. Ivy is hanging down from the tops of the fir and oak, making this area fairly demanding to explore. A slight uphill slope in the east leads from this entangled area into a gloomy forest. Heavily forested hills rise in the south. The vicious underbrush broadens its space to the north, creating a natural tunnel, deep underneath the trees.
106157: Massive tangles of evergreen, coniferous shrub grow beneath the dark canopy of the Mirkwood. The large, thorny bushes are interlaced with climbing vines and strands of grey lichen. The gloomy forest consist chiefly of oak and beech, although there are rowan, maple and yew present.
106158:
A wild dog bares his yellow fangs at you.
A wild dog bares his yellow fangs at you.

Stands of fir and beech are interspersed with the gnarled, ancient trunks of oak. The ground is littered by dead leaves, fir needles and cones. Large, evergreen juniper bushes and smaller, bristly shrubs also flourish here. Towards the north there is a grassy slope rising from the forest's shadow but the way to the top of it is blocked by the dense undergrowth. Instead, the dark mouth of a tunnel looms ahead.
106159: The shadows are deep and many here in the depths of Mirkwood where the ground has not been touched by the bright rays of the sun for countless years. The soft soil is covered with brown leaves and fir needles, and various types of mushrooms and fungi grow in glum shadows. Towards the east and south, large bushes covered in sharp thorns block the way.
106160: Foul webs span across Mirkwood, engulfing the exit west with their complex patterns.

Soft, rustling sounds can be heard from above, where the wind constantly shakes and stirs the crowns of the trees. Here beneath the dense cover of branches and leaves, the shadows are deep and many, and the light of the sun may not have touched the ground for hundreds of years. Most of the trees are gnarled and hoary, overgrown with fungi and vines. The undergrowth is sparse, but there are dense tangles of large, thorny shrubs towards the north and south.
106161: A small centipede is here scurrying about.

This narrow, cramped tunnel is filled with a musky, earthy smell. The soil is soft and moist and smells of rotting leaves and worms. Small clumps of earth fall from the tunnel's roof occasionally and should it collapse the entire tunnel and everything in it would be buried.
106162:
A tiny spider is here, eating a tiny bug.
A tiny spider is here, eating a tiny bug.

This damp earthen tunnel leads out into Mirkwood towards the north, where the forest lies as dark as the inside of this passageway, and continues onwards toward the south. It is beyond a doubt created by someone or something and not a natural thing, for it runs straight as an arrow through the soft soil.
106163: The ground is littered with a multitude of dead leaves mixed with fir cones and needles. Thorny thickets grow across the area, encroaching on the dark, gnarled boles and open spaces in between trees alike. Above, the heavy boughs and intertwining branches of the tree tops form a roof that separates the forest floor from the outside world.
106164:
Foul webs span across Mirkwood, engulfing the exit north with their complex patterns.
A black moth flutters around.
A black moth flutters around.
A black moth flutters around.
A fierce boar is here, making grunting noises.

Deep shadows and impenetrable darkness stalk between the gnarled trunks of ancient oaks. Little light ever finds its way through the crowns of the trees down to the forest floor. Yet even in the eternal gloom there is life in the form of large thickets of sprawling, thorny bushes that creak and rustle softly as the dense, intertwined branches brush against one another.
106165: The forest here has no distinguishing features. The dark shadows and dense woods conceal any useful landmarks. There is nothing to be seen in any direction but never ending rows of dark, gnarled trunks rising up to meet a dense canopy above. One thick bole looks much like the next, hoary and gnarled, overgrown with lichen and clumps of fungi. The ground is soft and damp and covered by dead leaves that rustle softly whenever stepped on.
106166:
A black, thorny bush grows here, enshrouded in a murky gloom.
A small, red-spotted spider lurks here.
A small, red-spotted spider lurks here.
A small, red-spotted spider lurks here.
A small, red-spotted spider lurks here.
A small, red-spotted spider lurks here.
A small, red-spotted spider lurks here.

The dense forest lies shrouded in shadows and gloom. The tree tops above are so thick with intertwining branches and foliage that the sky beyond can barely be glimpsed. The ground around the boles is covered with knotted roots, clumps of small, brown mushrooms and dead leaves.
106167: An iron-grey wolf stands here, grizzled from countless hunts.

Large, thorny bushes grow between the dark trunks of oak and beech, at places completely filling the space between the tree-trunks with masses of tangled, intertwined vegetation. The southern part of the area has the highest density of undergrowth and looks all but impassable. To the north passage is blocked by jagged rocks rising from the forest floor to form a formidable obstacle, the highest tips disappearing into the thick canopy above.
106168: In an Overgrown Corner of Mirkwood Forest

A large variety of bushes grow here, tangled in large masses of impassable vegetation, many of them with sharp thorns ready to snag and prick the unwary. There is a constant rustling from the deeper parts of the undergrowth, seemingly from beneath piles of decaying leaves that fill the air with a faint smell of rot, yet the small forest creatures causing the noises can but rarely be glimpsed.
106169:
A fallen tree lies on the ground, its clump of roots pointing upwards.
On the tree, there is a nest.
A black moth flutters around.

A massive oak has been uprooted here and now lies on the ground rotting away. A large, uneven hole in the ground shows where the large roots now reaching up into the air were previously buried. Several smaller trees lie crushed beneath the fallen behemoth. The decaying trunk has become the nesting ground to swarms of small, black insects that fill the area with a faint droning buzz. A corpse-grey lichen can be seen on many of the trees, growing in strange patterns on the dark trunks.
106170: Forest at the Foot of a Slope

A colony of white aspen grows amidst the beech and oak of the surrounding forest, their thinner, pale trunks a stark contrast to the otherwise dark and gnarled trees. The canopy above is no less dense and impregnable than elsewhere in the forest and there is not the slightest hint of a sky above. The ground rises towards the south but passage in that direction is blocked by a tangled mass of large, thorn-covered brush.
106179: The Old Forest Road follows an unswerving path along the top of the ridge on its course from east to west. Only at one point is the ancient pathway forced to a small detour by a rocky outcropping. Nature is working hard at reclaiming the old road, grass and weed sprouting up from the hard, solid earth that has seen centuries of use by wagon wheels and tramping feet.
106187: Most of the ancient road that leads along the top of this ridge from east to west is now overgrown by grass, dense brush and low trees. Yet there is a well trampled pathway in the middle of the old road that seems to be in use still. The dark canopy of Mirkwood rises to meet the descending slope to the south and north, with large, tangled bushes in the shadow of the trees forming an all but impassable wall of thorns and intertwining branches.
106188: Old Forest Road by a Ruin

The old road follows the flat, high ground at the top of a grass-covered ridge on its way through Mirkwood forest. Next to the road there are several low walls of stone visible in the high grass. The ruins, perhaps once a way station or inn along the road, are long since overgrown with moss and lichen. There are signs of recent battle among the ruins. Broken pieces of armour and weapons lie scattered among the grass, and there are several dark splotches that could be blood.
106189: The Old Forest Road, although largely overgrown with grass and weed, is still visible against the denser vegetation to the sides where it follows the high point of the ridge towards the east and west. Large bushes sprawl across the downwards slopes to the north and south.
106190: The grass-covered ridge begins a slow, gentle descent towards the east. The Old Forest Road cuts a straight, unswerving path through undergrowth and high grass. A few boulders, overgrown with moss and lichen, dot the landscape like dark, hulking shapes half hidden by the brush.
106191: Bend in the Old Forest Road
A brawny wisent is slowly striding through the vegetation.

The Old Forest Road runs on top of a small ridge. The road makes a lazy curve following the natural shapes of the terrain, ascending to the west and descending slowly to the south, avoiding the forested slopes to the east and north. The gentle slopes give no trouble for travellers, although the surrounding forest constantly presses in around the road, as though threatening to swallow the road completely along with any unwary traveller.
106192: Bend in the Old Forest Road

A large hawk-like bird is here overlooking its territory.
A large hawk-like bird is here overlooking its territory.

Tall, dark trees surrounding the road make it impossible to see the sky above. To the north the road starts to climb along a gentle slope of a ridge and the forest opens up slightly in that direction. Eastwards the road continues on its east-west course through the thick and inhospitable forest.
106193:
An emaciated warg, half-mad with hunger, is here.
An emaciated warg, half-mad with hunger, is here.
A huge warg is here, moving in for the kill.
A huge warg is here, moving in for the kill.

The old road cuts straight through the forest on its way from the west to the east. While the road is in a state of neglect, it is still possible to travel through Mirkwood via the road, something that does not hold true for the surrounding forest; dark and twisted trees lean on each other, their branches intertwining together, blocking the passageways between most of the trees.
106195: The old road cuts straight through the forest on its way from the west to the east. While the road is in a state of neglect, it is still possible to travel through Mirkwood via the road, something that does not hold true for the surrounding forest; dark and twisted trees lean on each other, their branches intertwining together, blocking the passageways between most of the trees.
106196: The old road cuts straight through the forest on its way from the west to the east. While the road is in a state of neglect, it is still possible to travel through Mirkwood via the road, something that does not hold true for the surrounding forest; dark and twisted trees lean on each other, their branches intertwining together, blocking the passageways between most of the trees.
106200: The old road cuts straight through the forest on its way from the west to the east. While the road is in a state of neglect, it is still possible to travel through Mirkwood via the road, something that does not hold true for the surrounding forest; dark and twisted trees lean on each other, their branches intertwining together, blocking the passageways between most of the trees.
106201: The old road cuts straight through the forest on its way from the west to the east. While the road is in a state of neglect, it is still possible to travel through Mirkwood via the road, something that does not hold true for the surrounding forest; dark and twisted trees lean on each other, their branches intertwining together, blocking the passageways between most of the trees.
106205: Gravel and dark-green weeds cover the old, decayed road. Dense bushes line it on both sides, trying to conquer all the open space available. The trees along the road grow like giant pillars, their gnarled trunks rising to great heights, disappearing from sight into the darkness of the shadowy canopy. To the north, the forest is more open, and a clearing can be seen through the trees.
106207: Some old tracks are visible on the sand of the bumpy road that runs here through a lush grove of huge beech trees. Some of the trees are really massive, so big that the road could run directly through the trunk and still it would be just a hole in the bark. The enormous roots are like veins on the surface of the ground, some of them crossing the road.
106211: Huge, gloomy oak trees reach over the narrow road that snakes through the forest. Shrubs and tangled berry bushes border the road, limiting visibility to a minimum. The surface of the road itself is dusty and sandy, and covered by dry weeds and occasional litter that has fallen down from the engulfing forest.
106215: Tall trees reach high into the sky and bend their trunks and branches towards the centre of the road. The road appears to be very old, but, very strangely, quite well maintained. To the east and west the road continues on through the dark and dreary forest. Along the south edge of the road a tree wall can be seen. Fallen trees would prevent any move to the north.
106218: The Old Forest Road runs through a dark grove where large, twisted trees line the immediate border of the road. One of the gigantic oaks has fallen onto the road and is now slowly rotting away on the path. Spider webs cover the trees, and dead branches and other forest litter lie on the ground. To the northeast, an opening is faintly visible in the distance.
106221: Old Forest Road along a Meadow
A bear is here, covered with coarse black fur.

To the north and southeast the forest has faded into the distance. Tufts of green grass poke their way through the black and grey brush. Directly to the south the forest remains dense and dreary. The flowing meadows here are much easier to traverse, not least due to the absence of such dark thick trees. Further east the forest seems to lighten as the meadow expands further south.
106224: Road at the Edge of a Meadow

Meadows stretch along this section of the road, giving one a good view of the surrounding terrain. The road here is composed of gravel and appears to be very old. Although in some places large boulders rest on the road, overall it is quite smooth and easy to travel on. It leads straight through the meadow from east to west, where it again enters the forest, which can already be seen down the path.
106227: A small cluster of clover grows here.

The forest road continues to the east and west. To the south, a large flowing meadow can be seen where tall grasses sway back and forth in rhythmic motion, giving this area a sense of calm. The otherwise lifeless meadow emits a foul stench. To the north the mighty forest recedes.
106230: A bear is here, covered with coarse black fur.

The road changes a bit here. An evil power has made the trees partly destroy the road to the east, but it seems in a better state to the west. A giant spider web hangs on some branches, sign of the closeness of a spider lair. To the north and east the trees look dead, but they get gradually healthier the further to the west one looks. However, there is not enough foliage to stop the sunshine from reaching the ground.
106233: The grey road sometimes almost disappears admist the trees, as though the forest wanted to absorb it. The forest is dense, here and there a trunk has fallen across the way, but they can easily be jumped by anyone. Lots of broken branches lie around. To the north and south stand the sinister trees of Mirkwood, the road continues to the east and west.
106236: A large brown wolf stands here, its teeth partly bared.

The Old Forest Road is being ruined here by the roots which are slowly working towards taking over the land. Many cobbles are missing, and many small plants grow between the remaining ones. To the south, the forest seems dead, the only living plants being small ferns. The road continues both west and east, but the trees along it to the east seem to have more leaves.
106239: A bear is here, covered with coarse black fur.

A clearing opens up around the road. Some missing cobbles make potholes in the ruts that road traffic formed, but if one can judge by the plants growing between the cobblestones, no waggon has used this road for years. The Old Forest Road goes on to both west and east. In the west, the trees seem dead. To the north a small hill rises above the forest.
106242: The road is irregular here, as some roots have grown under it, making bulges in its surface. Some old trails lead between the trees, shortcuts across the curve which the road makes here. The road continues to the west and to the south. To the north, a trail snakes between tall pines. An insurmountable hedge of bushes blocks the way to the east.
106245: This regularly-paved road continues to the north and to the east. Two small paths lead to the south and to the west, through Mirkwood. Trees were obviously cut down when the road was built, hence the stumps lining the road; but the forest came back and now trees from both sides make an arch above the road.
106248: A wolf spider is here, among the trees.

The small trail snakes through the forest between big beeches and old oaks. It leads to the Old Forest Road to the north, deeper in the forest to the south. An even smaller path leads to the west and disappears in the thick forest. Lots of trunks are covered by moss, and toadstools are growing everywhere in this humid forest.
106251:
The corpse of a seasoned Durbuk-hai scout is lying here.
A hollow tree is growing upright here.

One dead tree towers up through the canopy and opens a big hole through which light can flood down to the forest floor. The bark has at some places peeled away from the trunk, forming handholds and allowing one to climb up the tree. Except for this tree, all the rest here are alive and fully grown, with big lush leaves. Lots of threads of spider-silk join some trees. The trail leads around the dead tree to both north and west while the brambles and vines get denser in other directions.
106254: The upper part of the tree is littered with the remains of an ancient spider web. This tree-top hideout is covered with white, silky spider webs displaying an elaborate design which is both beautiful and deadly. At this altitude the mountains of Mirkwood can be seen to the northeast.
106264:
Foul webs span across Mirkwood, engulfing the exit south with their complex patterns.
A colossal tree, its trunk as wide as a small cottage, stands here.

The trees in this area have thinned out enough that sunlight is able to penetrate to the forest floor. Due to the increase in light the ground here is covered with a vast array of mosses and ferns. As well as a multitude of small vegetation, a myriad of larger plant life is also present. In short, the forest floor in this area is covered in a moist carpet of green plant life.
106265: The forest has now become dense with dark old larches. The ground is littered with small dead branches and leaves which lie lifeless on the dark rich soil of the forest floor. Brambles have overwhelmed this area, making it hard to traverse. About twelve yards above the forest floor, leaves and branches are intertwined into a dark, thick layer of foliage which almost completely blocks sunlight from reaching the forest floor.
106266: This colossal trunk was probably uprooted by a storm, and crushed down all the nearby trees on its way to the ground. The soil its fall threw up made a steep ramp that rains have compacted. Further up the trunk, the sky is visible through a gap in the foliage. To the south, the forest gets too dense to allow you to leave in this direction. Neither to the west nor to the east is there any way to climb off the trunk, but it might be possible to clamber over the branches to the west, down towards the base of the tree. Between the trunk and the foliage a large number of spider webs spread out wide. A few of them still have partly decaying victims in them.
106267:
Foul webs span across Mirkwood, engulfing the exit north with their complex patterns.
Some roots lie here waiting to ensnare weary travellers.
An elaborate red flower sits within a dark mass of briars.

The forest here is so thick and dense that all sunlight is blocked by the towering canopy high above. The ground is full of thistles and thorns, making movement tough and tiresome. One distinct anomaly is present: there is a massive uprooted tree lying to the west, its bulky, cumbersome roots hanging in the air and blocking the passage to a dark hole which opens up inside the hollow tree. The tree and the roots are covered in spider eggs of all sizes varying in size from a fist to a pumpkin.
106268: A tangled creeper writhes its shoots between the forest's roots upwards.

There is a small open space in the shade of a giant trunk of an ancient, fallen oak tree. The only way out of here would be to the west, if one were to head there, it looks very unlikely that one could come back, since the sharp branches are angled and point west, making it far easier to go than to return. Partly covering the ground are the skeletons of snakes in various sizes; notable are the long, thick chain-like spines.
106269:
The corpse of a huge, hideous spider is lying here.
The corpse of a huge, hideous spider is lying here.

The forest has become incredibly dense. The forest floor is made of roots, stumps and a lot of big rocks covered by moss. A natural trail weaves its way between trees and rocks. To the south the forest is too dense to allow anyone to pass through. To the east, jumbled heaps of branches nevertheless leave some room to move. To the north the forest seems even darker, if that were be possible, and definitely menacing.
106270: The majority of the trees in this area have one unique quality: they are branchless. As well as lacking branches, these trees are extremely tall. Their canopies reach so high into the sky that the tree-tops appear to spin due to the high winds at such an altitude. To the east the forest appears to grow darker and more dense as bushes and other forest floor vegetation reemerge. To the north trees become less numerous but the vegetation in this area becomes vast and dense, creating a thicket which presents a major problem to the unexperienced traveller.
106271: Beech trees abound in this corner of the forest, amidst dry ground covered with small green bushes. A narrow largely overgrown trail leads toward the north. The other part of the trail has been reclaimed by the forest and no hints of it can be seen. Some trunks of the large beech trees here have a purple sheen to the bark. To the west of the faint path, there is a large anthill and some rocks.
106272: This thicket is dark and dense, with masses of shrubs and bushes which reach five feet into the air. A small part of the forest floor is visible, with small tufts of grass hiding between the bushes and shrubs. Some beech trees fight for ground with the thicket. The ground is soft and damp; branches from bushes reach out and scrape the traveller. To the south, the forest changes: the trees there lack any branches, giving an impression of openness.
106273: A small campfire burns here, its embers barely giving off any light.

The ground here is wet from the moisture which lingers in the air. The soil is black as night, a sign that this is rich healthy soil for growing things, and indeed an array of plants thrives on the forest floor, ranging from beautiful, colourful flowers to simple green and black molds. To the south the forest gains strength as it becomes denser and more treacherous. Traces of what may have been a forest trail can be seen on the ground, though it is now almost completely overgrown by an abundance of undergrowth.
106274: A fallen tree lies on the ground, its clump of roots pointing upwards.

There are so many fallen trees here that the ground is scarcely visible. Huge branches, half-rotten and agglomerated with old leaves and soil, form crude gangways over and around the fallen trunks. Young trees have sprouted under the remains of the older ones and are already growing a new layer of foilage to conceal this green and grey landscape. To the east, it is possible to crawl under the dead branches and enter a weird cave. The cave has dusty old spider webs hanging like drapery in the entrance, partly concealing it. To the south and to the north, the forest is too dense to allow anyone through. In the west, there are less branches and trunks, and a trail is visible under the dead leaves.
106275: There is a wide open space inside this dead, fallen tree. The interior walls have been emptied of its pith by insects which left only the very hard bark. To the east the trunk ends at a network of tangled roots, and there is a small crater under the stump. Inside the crater lies a spider's victim, mummified in webbing. To the west, just before leaving the bark, the wood seems burnt, maybe due to a lightning strike. The border between the trunk and the branches to the west is not easy to see.
106276: Huge trees form a thick tangle of branches overhead, letting in little light. The thick bark of the trees gives them a wrinkled and old appearance. Faint traces of mist drift out of the layers of leaves on the forest floor. At places there are hints of an old, mostly overgrown trail that seem to disappear beneath the tangled growths of thorny bushes to the west.
106277: Not very long ago, perhaps less than a year, a ferocious fire burned off the oaks here, leaving behind tall, skeletal remains that jut up against the sky above like blackened spears. The burned area continues to the north, while in all other directions tall, black oak and beech trees obscure the view.
106278: A steep and rocky hillside rises up to the south and east, blocking further exploration. Approaching from the north, the beech and oak grow dense, engulfing the entire area in darkness. A sombre mist spreads across the forest floor, making it even more difficult to discern any details. To the west great beeches stand united to form a strong barrier, some of which has been marked by fire. Wounded and withered, Mirkwood still holds together. The ground is littered with fallen branches. Stripped of leaves and bark they have been left to the infestation of small malicious bugs. The ensnaring vegetation make travelling yet more arduous.
106279:
A fallen tree lies on the ground, its clump of roots pointing upwards.
A brown, long-legged spider swiftly charges at you.

Great oaks rise toward the sky, intermingling their crowns with the beech and birch. The fine quilt made up from the leaves far above efficiently blocks out most natural light. Trunks have fallen to the ground, as if forced away by their younger offspring. Rotten and decomposed, they now serve as homes for a myriad of parasites. In the east, south and west Mirkwood spreads its darkness, while in the north the woods grow even more dense, indeed impenetrable.
106280: The forest floor is cast in shadow by the roots and vines rising from the ground and encircling the trees. Oak and beech dominate the forest here, their mighty crowns casting shade over everything. In the east the vegetation appears distorted and seems to have been viciously ravaged, while in the west the darkness engulfs the forest completely. An entrance into a pitch-black grove opens up to the south, just in between two great trees.
106281: A brown, long-legged spider swiftly charges at you.

The vicious-looking trees lean in to one another, guarding each other's backs from intruders. Mirkwood stands twisted and tall, engulfing the vegetation in an immaculate veil of darkness. The beech and oak leave a passage open to the east and south, ensnaring the heavy underbrush with their roots and vines.
106282: Gnarled branches have fallen to the ground, left dehydrated and brittle by an old fire. A few majestic trees still stand strong, with their crowns reaching for the sky, and their trunks forever marked with burns and deep cuts. Vine-entangled roots rise from the murky soil, offering new foundations for ivy and periwinkle. In the north Mirkwood lies engulfed in shadow while in the west it bears the marks of long-forgotten fires. Far below, down an uneven slope, an old forest trail can be discerned to the south.
106283: Great branches from the ancient trees lie spread across the forest floor, broken under the twisted, scorched tree trunks. Stout young birch and fir have already grown dense since the fire, and are already well on the way to restoring the darkness of Mirkwood. The forest with its young trees expands into the east and north. A steep hillside leads further west into a more heavily-wooded part of Mirkwood.
106284: Trees, scorched to their core, have fallen heavily to the ground. However, the still standing giants of the forest, despite their gaping wounds and obvious marks of fire, still manage to embrace the area in darkness. Light vegetation has slowly started to take over from the incinerated trees. The disfigured forest expands far into the south, while in the east a tall mound of rocks and boulders appears to have protected the remaining forest from the fire.
106290:
A tiny spider is here, eating a tiny bug.
A tiny spider is here, eating a tiny bug.
A tiny spider is here, eating a tiny bug.

Oak and beech dominate the forest here, their mighty crowns casting shade over everything. A small space free of trees opens up centrally in the area, engulfed in darkness. Roots and vines, all covered in a shimmering web of spider's silk, are everywhere. Abandoned cocoons lie scattered across the floor. To the north darkness lies solid, while to the south there is a hint of rocks and stones.
106293: Huge, gnarled trees grow tall and wide, yet seem as though in despair, with heavily wounded trunks and branches. Many oak and beech have been ripped out of the ground, leaving their roots to rot and decay as they lie. The undergrowth rises strong in the east, while in the south the befouled forest lies suffering.
106294:
Foul webs span across Mirkwood, engulfing the exit west with their complex patterns.
A black moth flutters around.

The ground slopes continuously upwards to the east. The towering trees grow very close together, creating a dark canopy which obscures the sky with a continuous blanket of interwoven branches and vines. Only a few open paths are available through the surroundings, as thick-threaded and sticky-looking spider webs have been spun everywhere: from branch to branch, from one trunk to another, and from the ground to the upper canopy.
106295: Several trees have broken in half to the west, the broken-off trunks piling up into a tall, stout barrier. The many fallen beech and oak here have been overgrown with thorny bushes and vines. Zigzagging between the roots of those trees still standing are long columns of various insects, making their way to and from the decomposing debris. The vegetation hinders further exploration to the south and west, while in the north the despair which is Mirkwood continues.
106296: Here, gloomy walls of trees form a narrow passage which runs approximately north to south inside Mirkwood. On this path, two leafless, skeletal trees stand alone; their shapes resemble a strange mixture of tree and man. Around and above the open area, dense vegetation and thick tree trunks block travel in any other direction.
106297: Large and gloomy oak trees dominate the flora here, growing close together and creating a sombre canopy above. A few white stones have been piled up here, almost acting as some kind of landmark. Maybe it was set there to help weary travellers to find the direction of the road, which can be seen between the trees. North of here, the trees grow even thicker, and the darkness makes it hard to see very far.
106298: Great ashen-grey boughs hang down above this relatively clear patch of forest. Further north, the trees grow tighter together, intermingling their branches with each other. Between the thick trees to the south, some kind of flat, treeless area can be spied.
106299: The dark forest spreads out in all directions. All kinds of shrouded, indistinct oak trees have grown into different shapes and forms; some of them are badly twisted, as if something eldrich influenced their growth. Patches of bare soil can be seen through the leaf-litter and moss that cover the ground. A few large webs are stretched between the oaks to the east and south.
106300: The trees that cover these darkened, rolling hills are badly twisted, as if some unfathomable source of evil has caused them great pain. The bark on the looming trunks is black and infested with green and grey fungi. The dense canopy above is also darker than one might expect of a forest; the leaves are a dark shade of green and seem unusually thick.
106301: A lot of the trees here are covered by large spider webs. A dried-out cocoon made out of silky web is lying next to a tree, covered with a mass of maze-like webs. It is impossible to discern the sky through the canopy overhead, because the trees here are growing far too densely for the outside world to be seen.
106302: These lands are populated by numerous dark, twisted trees. The ground mostly consists of decaying leaves and rotting stumps of old trees. The forest of Mirkwood continues in all directions, and to the west the forest floor rises into low hills. Massive strands of what look like old, decaying cobwebs are hanging from the leafy canopy above.
106303: The trees of the forest are growing very close to each other here, their trunks look swarthy and dark as though infected with a contagion. An unusual number of dead and rotting ant hills litter the ground, discarded decrepit husks of colonies long since extinct. The only obvious route of travel through Mirkwood here is towards the west, where the density of brooding trees and tangled undergrowth is the least obstructive.
106304: A small, mean earth troll is standing here, thinking of something hideous.

Among these defiled lands, great maze-like spider webs cover almost everything in sight. The mesh-like, silky webs reach from the corrupted grass bed to the degenerate treetops, creating pathways of silk that hang between the warped trees. These thick cobwebs combined with the dark, smothering trees prevent any light from penetrating all the way to the ground, making it difficult to scout ahead in any direction.
106305: Murky, hollowed-out oak trees stand here closely together like a legion of great black grotesque statues. At ground level, they are blackened and rotting, but further up into the canopy small green leaves can be seen straining upwards towards the unseen sky above. Great fly-infested cobwebs hang between the trunks, they appear to be as big as fishing nets.
106306: Trees at the Edge of the Road
A forest spider is here crawling around.

Occasional faint sounds originate from somewhere in the tree tops above, scraping and rustling noises unlike those that branches do when the wind move them against each other. Silky webs connect the trees above at canopy level, creating what looks like pathways between them. The bark on the trees looks dead and rotting, as if the silky webs have sucked all normal life from it.
106307: A forest spider is here crawling around.

The webs are everywhere. Walking over branches and leaves should be easy but the sticky webs hinder progress. Here and there strands of web hang down from the ceiling, traps of an unseen predator. To the south the webs continue much the same, while upwards a darker, stickier tunnel continues to unknown destinations.
106308: A dark-green spider is here, poison dripping from its fangs (hidden).

This small area of the treetops is neatly boxed-in on all sides except the north where the ever-present webs continue. There is a range of small cocoons of spider-silk here, made of small animals left here long ago. The remainder of the cramped dead-end is lined with long webs, both old and new. The ground below is hardly visible through gaps in web, leaf and bough.
106309: The webs here are becoming more dense. Grey to white, they cover the sides of what is now effectively a tunnel stretching up to untold heights. With no ground visible below, it is impossible to tell where the rest of the forest lies. The tunnel is rough and imperfect, and its route seems to be the result of the lay of branches and ease of passage between them rather than design.
106310: This section of the passage is very uneven, branches strike up from below and force a hard turn in the way ahead. More webs cover everything in sight in a thick, sticky grey mass. A few skeletons and remains of small animals are lying around, evidence of an unseen terror. The webbed expanse continues to sprawl into several directions, all routes looking the same, making it hard to tell which way leads where.
106311: Light does not behave normally here in this, the highest tier of tunnels. Deep green mottles the grey and white shades of the thick clinging webs like an infection. There is a smoother supporting floor here and the webs are finer but more dense. It seems like a beautifully intricate tube stretching out at bizarre angles, a junction within a web of tunnels.
106312:
Foul webs span across Mirkwood, engulfing the exit south with their complex patterns.
A black moth flutters around.
A small, mean earth troll is standing here, thinking of something hideous.

A noticeably-large oak tree elevates itself from the surrounding, smaller trees. While its majestic size is breathtaking, the tree itself appears to be befouled by a ghastly sickness. Its once royal branches and imposing trunk are clad in silken webs, and the last leaves are slowly dying. Falling for the last time, the final act is to nourish the encircling vegetation.
106313:
A very large, hairy man is standing here, examining you carefully (hidden).
A very large, hairy man is standing here, examining you carefully.

Unnaturally dark oaks grow in bizarre, twisted shapes here. The leaves of their crowns appear dead and withered, yet they still manage to block out any view of the sky above. At ground level black soil, mud, stones and patches of corpse-yellow grass are all covered indiscriminately by a fine mesh of old, rotting cobwebs studded with the corpses of uncountable dead moths.
106314: Sombre grasses cover the many fallen branches that blanket the ground. Dreary-looking trees grow towards a dark canopy of leaves and patches of spider web. A few baby spiders can be spied moving tirelessly along the tree-trunks south of here. Eastwards the ground starts a gentle ascent, while the southern lands seems to descend further and further into the great dark of Mirkwood.
106315: Thick oaks grow sparsely here on a slightly ascending bed of leaves and overgrown grass. To the south, the oaks appear to be darker and more corrupted-looking; and their gnarled, bone-white aerial roots are growing towards the more healthy-looking brethren. A few of the fairer oaks have had their trunks embraced by roots from the southern trees, and it certainly appears like the forest is trying to spread whatever plague that torments it. The canopy above shifts from lush green colours up here, to dark, rusty, dead tones further south.
106316: Smaller oaks grow here among dense bushes and thorny shrubs, a combination that serves to completely obscure the ground. A large stone, shaped by decades of wind and rain creates a shelter-like structure towards the south, where the broken and rotting shaft of some kind of weapon has been left next to what looks like an old, forgotten campsite. Scant patches of moss decorate the stone in shades of grey and green.
106317:
skeleton (here) :
a strange white skull
an orkish shortbow
some greater parts of a broken weapon
A skeleton of some humanoid lies in the dust.

Cobwebs are spreading like a plague in this area, consuming trees, stones and bushes. Skulls and bones from small animals and man-like creatures litter the ground, and broken shields and shafts of weapons lie scattered among them. A few silken cocoons are swaying from the low-hanging boughs that stretch out from the tree-crowns. To the west a large tree can be distinguished, while further to the east, a few trees looks like they have been burned by fire.
106318: Large, dark oaks grow tightly together here, their great crowns completely blocking out the sky above. Examining the trunks reveals that a forest fire once scorched these trees. Black soot stains reach along the trunks, almost looking like black shadows creeping up towards the sky along the dark brown bark.
106319: Great sturdy dark-leaved oaks grow tightly together, creating a terrain that is very hard to travel through. Dense shrubberies with sad-looking, withered leaves grow tightly beneath them, sucking nutrients out of the rotting, muddy soil. A few large boulders can be spied between the trunks to the south.
106320: Here, the terrain consists of overgrown bushes and dense oaks, great old trees whose roots have grown bizarrely large, growing outwards from the trunk twenty feet in every direction. Some of the aerial roots are growing upwards, ensnaring the trees around them in a suffocating embrace.
106321: Twisted, dense oaks grow here, their great branches grasping for space and suffocating all other growth around them. The boughs above are so densely interwoven that no sign of the sky can be discerned through them. North of here, the ground looks water-logged, while what could be a road lies to the south.
106322: The fire has completely devastated this part of the forest. A blackened glade with a few charred tree trunks is all that remains of the forest that is looming around the opening, as dark and oppressive as ever. New undergrowth has started to grow from the ashes: short grass and a few short plants grow on the ground.
106323: A half-decayed corpse of a goblin lies rotting on the ground.

Here, the tree-crowns above are covered by silken cobwebs with long, elegant threads hanging down from the branches. The ground is littered by skeletons of small animals and dead, decomposing spiders. Great sticky walls of web stretch between the trunks of the forest, creating impassable obstructions.
106324:
A demon wolf lurks here, its dark form twisting and hiding its shape.
A black raven flies in the sky searching for flesh to prey upon.

A few tall hills dominate the scenery here, rising over the nearby forest floor like a row of darkened, rotting teeth. The hills are fully covered by the blackened, ancient trees of Mirkwood; the trees make passage on the slopes tiring, and severely limit visibility. The ground is strewn with mossy boulders, black weeds and a few dry, dead bushes.
106326: A black raven flies in the sky searching for flesh to prey upon.

A dark, thick forest covers a range of jagged, blackened hills that rise above the forest floor. Sinister oaks grow in abundance in this area; some of them are dried-out and leafless, while others are huge, thick and lush. Boulders litter the ground, set between patches of cracked, dried-up mud and small, thorny bushes.
106327: This large, swamp-like bog makes the ground in this area treacherous and hard to navigate. However, it is possible to get around by staying close to the trees that grow here on the spongy, grass-covered islets that jut out of the sodden, reeking ground. Walking is difficult here, riding is impossible.
106328:
A small, sickly green mushroom grows here.
Clusters of slender stems and tall leaves thrive in the mud and shallows.

The thick black trunks of long-dead beech trees still stand here in this murky, water-logged bog. Here and there, strange mushrooms and unusual-looking plants grow in disproportionate patterns. A small path, marked by yellowish rocks, snakes through the area; however it is unclear what the purpose of the trail could be.
106329: A lot of large, thick oaks grow here. Their root systems are partially above ground, making passage difficult and strenuous. At the base of some of the trees, great chafing marks are visible, and it looks as if some large animal has used the trees to sharpen its tusks or horns.
106331: Great Jumble of Rocks under the Black Trees
A small and tough weed grows here.

The terrain slopes up and down, following the shape of heavily forested hills. The travelling is hard as rock formations punch upwards between the huge tree trunks like granite fists, and numerous moss-covered roots twist on the ground as if trying to trip, grab and trap anyone coming too close to them. Far above, the branches and vines have entangled into each other forming a dense canopy.
106332: Forested Pass between the Craggy Hills
A sparrow is flapping around on the ground.

Tall, craggy hills rise all around, leaving a long but narrow valley between them. The hillsides to the north and south are covered by thick trees, entangled shrubbery and occasional sharp-edged boulders. Uncountable branches meet each other in layer upon layer, almost completely covering and shadowing the tunnel-like pathway on the ground level.
106333: A large, loyal falcon is circling above.

An intact canopy of Mirkwood covers a tall hill which rises above the surrounding ground. Black trees stand like towers and in the darkness below them continuous shrubbery, rock boulders and small stony ridges fill the landscape. The slopes of the hill are descending relatively calmly making travelling possible although potentially treacherous.
106334: The ground level of the forest slopes up and down in a random fashion, making movement possible only with great care. The area is filled with black pine trees and grey, crumbly rock. The canopy continues in all directions, filtering and blocking out most of the light. There are especially steep and rocky hillsides to the east and south.
106335: Dark trees and lush, black bushes cover the terrain which starts to angle sharply upwards to the north, and to sink abruptly to the south. Down the slope, the trees get even thicker and crowd together, blocking the view further on. Up the slope, a turf war is being fought between vegetation and rock with neither side winning.
106336: Breaking away from the northern slopes is a series of heavily forested hills. Steeply sloping ground, gigantic trees and occasional boulders and moss-covered loose rocks make the terrain hard to travel. Taken over by thick brush and dark trees, all directions save north are quite impassable.
106337:
Foul webs span across Mirkwood, engulfing the exit east with their complex patterns.
A black spider crawls here, a shiny red spot visible on its belly.
A brown, long-legged spider swiftly charges at you.
A brown, long-legged spider swiftly charges at you.

The scent of musty trees and rank vegetation is overpowering in this dark and thick grove. The whole area has been wrapped into a thick layer of silvery, sticky-looking spider webs. A dozen grotesque cocoons dangle from the branches, like hanged men on the gallows. Some of the cocoons seem to be moving occasionally.
106338:
A man's-waist high evergreen shrub grows here, with bright green branches.
On the shrub, there are several splayed leaves.

Large stands of birch and pine seem to whisper to each other, each and every tree being woven into a huge network of spider webs which covers the whole area. Above, gangways made of spider silk reach from one tree top to another, creating a network of passageways within the canopy. On ground level, shrubs of all sizes hug the trunks.
106339: Serving as a transition between the rising hills and the deep forest, this swell in the landscape is dotted with pine and birch trees. Small boulders are planted here and there in the loamy soil. Between the rocks, pine needles and decaying leaves litter the ground.
106340: The corpse of a brown, long-legged spider is lying here.

Pale spider webs have been woven between the old gnarled trees whose dark branches hang over the ground as if poised to grab unsuspecting travellers below. The ground is littered with broken branches and ancient, rotting trunks mixed with heavy mosses. Above, the continuous dense canopy continues to all directions totally blocking the view to the sky.
106341: The uneasy presence that permeates Mirkwood is very strong here. Towering pines and birch jostle with ancient oak, all covered with an intact, endless-looking wrapping of old cobwebs. With any passing breeze, the forest seems to come alive with a chorus of whispers as if a great, quiet discussion was going on. Gnarled roots mixed with heavy shrubs and bushes make the way tough.
106342: The sloping hillside here is festooned with trim fir and birch trees. Nestled between the trunks of the trees are rock protrusions, popping out of the ground in random places. Long beards of moss hang off slender branches to drape the ground in a luxuriously soft carpet. Evidence of birds and other small animals can be seen near the forest's edge.
106343:
Foul webs span across Mirkwood, engulfing the exit south with their complex patterns.
A quail stands motionless.

A dense, shady forest dips and rises in a somewhat undulating manner. Fallen trees from long ago lean against standing trunks like old men tired of living. Dappled leaves and verdant mosses cloak almost every surface while the fungi try to take over from below.
106344: Tension fills the air in this dark, heavily-wooded area. The towering trees seem to be whispering to each other every time a leaf rustles or a branch creaks noisily. Thick, sticky spider webs have been woven to the branches and between the trunks, creating traps for careless travellers. Animal noises are few and far between although the way here is crowded with dense shrubs and thick bushes that scrape and catch.
106345:
A huge black fungus is here, exuding a foul stench.
A huge black fungus is here, exuding a foul stench.

Here, the ground slopes downwards to the south, where some kind of overgrown roadway can be glimpsed in between the dark-barked oak trunks. Between two enormous, moss-covered trunks lie the remains of what once must have been a hut of some kind; all that remains of it now are a few rotting planks that used to form its walls. A musty smell permeates the area, hinting that particularly pungent mushrooms grow nearby.
106346:
A large boulder is here, it must be heavy.
A brown snail is crawling across the ground here leaving a slimy trail behind.

A black morass, with high reeds and shallow, opaque water forms north of here, where large oaks and beeches grow out of small, grassy islands. The ground here is covered by mud and a few strangely pale plants. A large stone stands next to one of the oak trees here, overgrown with black and red lichen and moss.
106347: A long and very sharp thorn is lying here.

Tree-trunks stand shoulder to shoulder in aggressive poses as the way becomes tight and close. A menacing feeling of intelligent awareness is present among the woods and intensifies deeper inside. Angry boughs shake thorny branches at whoever passes underneath and the wildlife seems almost scared to scurry around.
106348: A long and very sharp thorn is lying here.

Aside from the heavy foliage, few living things dare to penetrate this deep into Mirkwood. The menacing presence of the forest is almost overpowering and every root, twig, and branch tries to catch and snag anything that moves of its own accord. The forest is disturbingly quiet here.
106349:
The corpse of a brown, long-legged spider is lying here.
A quail stands motionless.

Putrescent fungi and grey spider webs stick like a thick spackle on the sides of dark trees that have been twisted and gnarled to resemble angry old men, hunched over and yelling. Glistening knots give faces to the menacing trees while lurid dangling mosses drape thick outstretched branches like a fur stole.
106358: The perpetual gloom here, caused by the green canopy above, ends towards the north where a steep slope littered with large rocks leads upwards into the hills. Large, sprawling bushes overgrown with black and grey lichen can be seen in all directions and they seem to flourish here in the dark, protected from the glare of the sun.
106359: Great, web-covered trunks rise up from the ground, their upper parts hidden from view by a dense growth of branches and leaves. Silky spider webs extend from trunk to trunk and from bush to bush, blocking passageways and steering travellers deeper into Mirkwood. The brooding silence and eternal gloom of the forest is interrupted to the south where a slope can be glimpsed beyond an impassable tangle of thorny bushes.
106360: Neither paths nor trails exist in this tangled part of the forest, and passage is limited to travelling upon patches of black moss between the towering tree trunks and large, sprawling bushes. A continuous, foreboding web has been spun above, entangling branches, vines and black leaves. Several dead trees lie rotting on the ground, the decomposing trunks covered by lichen and large clusters of brown fungi.
106363: The ground slopes slightly downwards from the east and south towards this dark, wet corner of the Mirkwood. Motley patches of moss and lichen are intermingled with shallow pools filled with rotting vegetation and dead leaves. Animal life seems to thrive amidst the decomposition and there is a constant humming, buzzing and droning from the multitudes of insects that make up the menu for various frogs and lizards.
106365:
Foul webs span across Mirkwood, engulfing the exit south with their complex patterns.
A wolf spider is here, among the trees.
A black spider crawls here, a shiny red spot visible on its belly.
A wolf spider is here, among the trees.

Strands of grey, foul-smelling lichen cover the bushes and shrubs growing here, giving the impression of large, tangled spiders' webs haphazardly strewn across the forest. The darkness beneath the intertwining branches above is complete and there is not a hint of sky to be glimpsed. Passage towards the east is blocked by jagged rocky outcroppings.
106367: The corpse of a brown, long-legged spider is lying here.

Small bushes with tiny dark leaves and many needle-sharp thorns grow in clusters around the dark trunks of ancient beech trees. Where old trees have fallen and now lie rotting on the ground, the bushes grow over and on top of the fallen trunks, sprouting from the rotten bark like parasitic fungi. There is a faint smell of corruption and rot in the air.
106369: Large, thorn-covered bushes grow along the edge of a rocky outcropping to the south. The rocks protrude from the earth like sets of uneven, jagged teeth, five or six yards high. The dark canopy above stretches out above the rocks, long branches extending across the gap to meet other branches, likewise reaching out from the other side.
106371:
There are two mushrooms here.
A small, red-spotted spider lurks here.
A small, red-spotted spider lurks here.

Most of the forest in this part of Mirkwood consists of tall, stout oaks, all of them ancient, hoary and overgrown with fungi. Tangles of thick, twisted vines snake up along the gnarled trunks, twisting around boles and branches as if trying to choke the life out of them.
106379:
A huge, venomous tarantula extends her legs to you.
A red-spotted spider is lying here, incapacitated.
A small, red-spotted spider lurks here.

Dense thickets grow in the shadows of the ancient trees of Mirkwood. Towards the south, part of a grassy slope is visible beyond a wall of thorny bushes. The ground is covered with dead, decaying leaves that fill the air with the smell of decomposing plants.
106380:
A small campfire burns here, its low flames giving off only a little light.
The corpse of *a Half-Elf* is lying here.
The shadow of *a Half-Elf* is floating here.

The gnarled boles of ancient trees loom like troubled shades in the gloom. Vast spider webs stretch between branches and trunks, far too large to be meant to catch butterflies or moths. The ground is mostly bare of undergrowth, covered only in dead leaves, fir needles and patches of dark, moist moss.
106388:
A huge, poisonous spider is here.
A huge, poisonous tarantula extends her legs to you.
A huge, poisonous tarantula extends her legs to you.
A forest spider is here crawling around.

The ancient trees loom in the dark gloom like gnarled, twisted shades, deeper black shapes in the encroaching shadows. There is a constant soft, rustling sound from the tree crowns above, where perhaps winds sweep across the roof of the forest. The ground is covered by dead leaves in various stages of decay.
106389: Old gnarled trunks of oak rise up from the forest floor to disappear in the canopy above. The trunks are covered in patches of lichen and fungi, and entangled in spider webs. At places on the great trunks, there are deep marks and scratches as if by claws. From these wounds dark, yellow sap has poured forth and dried on the bark.
106390: Dark Woods at the Foot of a Slope

The deep shadows of Mirkwood extend to the very base of a grass-covered slope to the south, where a dense tangle of thorn-covered bushes takes over where the trees end. Various shrubs and bushes seem to thrive here in the dark even though they are never touched by the bright rays of the sun that are usually essential for plant life.
106392: A wolf spider is here, among the trees.

Oak and beech stand close together, interconnected by periwinkle and ground ivy. The forest has completely dehydrated the very soil it stands on, leaving the forest floor dry, brittle and dusty. The imposing darkness may be further explored in the south and east, while the north is completely blocked by the dense trees, making it impossible to venture in that direction.
106393: Fir and beech spread their majestic crowns through the air, efficiently preventing most natural light from seeping through. Ravaged ground-ivy and wisteria lie lifeless on the ground. Further up in the trees fungi and mosses have almost overwhelmed the very trees they get their nourishment from. A slope descends down to the north, leading deeper into the murky forest of Mirkwood.
106394: A large, venomous-looking green snake is coiled up here.

Great birch and beech gather in a great collaborative effort, interweaving their branches and roots to form an impassable wall in the south and west. A grand canopy, reinforced by periwinkle and poison ivy, effectively closes out any form of natural light. The hills appear to come to an end in the east, while in the north a steep slope leads deeper into the malicious forest of Mirkwood.
106395: To the east a small entrance seems to have been purposefully opened between the great roots of the trees. To the west the forest appears more open and more readily accessible. An uneasy rustling stemming from the heavy vegetation, together with the twisted poison ivy and darkened roots, gives the forest an eerie aura. In the south the forest opens up into ancient, wide plains.
106397:
A gorcrow is standing here.
A big, nasty vulture is sitting here, protecting its nest.

The light brown earth here is home to patches of grass growing no more than two feet tall. A burned old farm cart lies in line with an old skeleton of what must have been an ass or a horse. Far in the east a small trail appears to lead up to a house; the deserted meadows expand to the south and west. The forest of Mirkwood stands proud in the north.
106399: The salty, dehydrated ground is littered with pebbles and boulders. Nothing can be seen growing for several leagues in all directions, except for the great forest of Mirkwood to the north. The forest springs out of the ground like a compact castle wall, and no obvious way in can be seen from here. The famished land stretches further into vast plains to the south, west and east.
106400: The grass stands almost two feet high, bending to any wind that may blow on it. The greenery spreads its influence strongly to the south, while the northern parts of the field appear less fruitful. A scorched fence encircles a burned out farm in the east, and in the west an esker marks the horizon.
106401: A dusty path almost wholly covered in tussocks of grass lies stretched across the field. Westward it can barely be made out among the meadows and quickly disappears in the earthy ground. To the south its contours become more apparent as the grass grows less abundant. To the north and east the mighty trees of Mirkwood have created an impassable wall of twisted trunks and vines.
106402:
A low and wide-spread tree grows here.
On the tree's branches, there are two juicy plums.
A rooster is here, strutting about.

A small, dusty path makes it way to a burned-out farm. The scent of decaying carcasses befouls the air. There are remainders of what could have been a stable lying all across the pathway. To the south stands the sooty skeleton of what appears to have been an old farmhouse. An old fence encircles the farm, and behind it the plains open up to the west. A heavy brush area grows every so close to the east, slowly approaching the farm.
106403: The lifeless plains stretch as far as the eye can see, except for the north where the mighty forest of Mirkwood rises up much like a great wall. The trees stand aligned, with enormous bushes and shrubs growing between the trunks, leaving no gaps through which to pass. The ground is covered with rocks of various sizes, and the dirt on which they lie is slightly white, resembling salt. Nothing in remote need of nutrients would be able to grow here.
106404: The meadows are covered with grass, closing in to the ridge stretching from the north and southwards. Long lines of perfectly rounded pebbles and stones line the stone ridge. In the north the feet high grass slowly disappears, replaced by barren fields, and in the south the meadows turn into a vast steppe, while in the east the undergrowth grows thicker.
106405: A layer of salt covers the entire ground, preventing anything from growing here. The plains are mostly covered with stones, varying from small pebbles to a handful of major boulders. Far away in the east the earthy ground appears to be overwhelmed by rocks, while in the north and south the malnourished plains expand ruthlessly.
106408: An ridge disrupts the flat steppe, rising high and steep from the ground. Rounded pebbles and rocks lie scattered along the stone ridge. Grass has slowly turned the dried-out surroundings green. The steppe gradually turns into a more vivid prairie to the east, a flowing meadow to the north, and back to its own pale self to the west.
106409: A flat, lonely landscape spreads far away towards meadows in the north, and more plains in the west. The horizon in the east is marked by a heightened esker in the steppe. The grass here grows to almost one foot in height, and adds a slight nuance of colour to the otherwise-barren area.
106410: A dull, ashen landscape stretches far in all directions. The pale colour of the earth is due to the layer of salt which covers it, preventing anything from growing here. Pebbles and rocks lying scattered across the cracked ground are the only things giving this land shape. A vast steppe opens up to the east.
106412: The grass stands a few feet tall, growing quite dense. Small bushes and a sole tree grow here, nourished by the rich soil. The prairie continues in the east, while in the west the landscape becomes grey, turning into a vast steppe. A farmhouse has been heavily ravaged, barely standing behind its picket fence in the north.
106413:
A Beorning herder is standing here, watching around.
A young boy is here, bumping into things.

Scrawny trees and bushes of different sizes are slowly taking over more and more land, disrupting the prevalence of flowing grass. A small snake pit lies poorly hidden under some rocks, with obvious traces of snakes slithering to and fro the pit. The vegetation grows thicker in the east and north, while in the west it appears to be more or less the same as here.
106414:
A large thorny branched shrub is growing here.
On the shrub, there are a number of blackberries.
A beautiful and docile horse is standing here.

Great thorn-bushes rise tall to the east, making it close to impossible to move much further in that direction. To the north the heavy undergrowth gradually turns into thorny bushes and malicious ground ivy. The brush land slowly turns into a gentler, greener landscape in the west.
106415: A steady amount of thorns and bushes grows here, reaching towards Mirkwood in the north and the abundant brush land in the south. A small trail navigates its way to the west, into vegetation similar to the current surroundings. Small holes burrow into the ground, leaving entrances and exitways for common field animals. Rose thorns grow quite tall in the east, making it difficult to move much further in that direction.
106416:
A sturdy pack horse is standing here.
A sturdy pack horse is standing here.
A sturdy pack horse is standing here.

Undergrowth and foliage are very abundant here, spanning from the south into the east. Poison ivy uses the burned-out fence in the west as its foundation. In the north the great forest of Mirkwood leans over the thorny brushland, creating an impermeable wall of vegetation. An abandoned fox den lies wide open beneath a clump of shrubs. It appears to have been ravaged by another animal. Remnants of small animals, doubtless those who fell prey to foxes, lie scattered on the ground.
106417: A skeleton of some humanoid lies in the dust.

The roof has partly collapsed due to damage from a fire. The southern wall still stands, and an old skeleton reclines against it. The door is damaged, and is just barely hanging from its hinges. The walls to the east and north carry what is left of the ceiling. The vast meadows can be seen through the western window. Vegetation has slowly started to creep into this area, with vines climbing through the cracked windows and walls.
106418: Great bushes and other foliage are competing for space with the tall grass, leeching all they can from the poor, dry soil. Small cracks in the field provide good hunting grounds for spiders and snakes. The majestic Mirkwood forest stands tall in the east, creating an impenetrable wall, while in the south and west the brushwood area continues.
106419: Mirkwood is accessible to the east, through a narrow passage lined by roots, trunks and vines. Dense thorn-bushes unfold in the west and north, reaching quite far towards the sky. The north, although it offers only thorns and spines, appears slightly less intimidating than the east, where the withered beech, oak and ash of the vast forest rise tall and dark. A light mist is wafting slowly out of Mirkwood, cloaking everything around, bringing with it a smell of decay. Hovering over the nearby brush land, the darkness of Mirkwood seems to attentively watch its surroundings. The darkness appears more treacherous than anything else.
106420: A narrow passage formed by twisting vines, interwoven with the oak and beech opens up into thorn-clad brush in the west. The crowns of the trees, far up in the air, are so thickly grown together as to be almost solid, efficiently blocking out the sky. The heavy undergrowth and dense foliage make the terrain very demanding to pass through. Gnarled trees stand twisted in agony all around.
106421: Beech and oak stand tall, stretching their crowns far through the air. Grey mosses and fungi leech off the ancient forest trunks. Here and there trees have fallen, rotten, to the ground, and now serve as homes for termites, beetles and other insects. The ground is very rough and cumbersome to traverse. The forest continues in the north and west.
106422: Poison ivy reaches out from the trees, as if grasping for someone or something. The crowns of the trees form an impressive network of branches and foliage, like a roof over Mirkwood, efficiently preventing any natural light from getting through. The dull darkness sets an eerie tone to the forest, as though it were carefully choosing what to hide, what to reveal. The going grows more cumbersome to the east, while in the west the terrain appears to be more or less the same as here.
106423: A small green mound rises from the ground.

A treacherous darkness covers the woods here, making the seeing very poor. A faint breeze from deeper within the forest gives life to the hanging vines and ivy. Withered roots and gnarled old branches blanket the forest floor, making it difficult to travel. Oak and beech stand high and strong in the west, leaving no passage for further exploration. A small trail opens up in the north, while in the east the forest appears similar to here.
106424: A brown snail is crawling across the ground here leaving a slimy trail behind.

Heavy greenery covers the vines and roots which expand long distances across the forest floor. Dark mosses and fungi almost completely cover many of the oak and beech trees. A scent of decomposing, rotten vegetation spreads through the air. Branches high above cast long, weary shadows upon the ground. The forest is readily accessible to the north and west, while in the south heavy, menacing undergrowth threatens to ensnare all who pass that way.
106431:
A tiny spider is here, eating a tiny bug.
A small harmless centipede is here.
A huge warg is here, moving in for the kill.

Vile trees reach out with their branches, grasping at the crowns of their neighbouring trees to create a vast canopy of leaves. The ground ivy thoroughly engulfs the roots rising up from the earth. The carcass of a bear lies rotting below a great oak, completely covered with flies, worms and other pests. The forest expands to the north, while the terrain seems cumbersome in the east and south.
106432: A large green shrub grows in the middle of a large pool of mud.

Rotting vines, leaves and fallen tree trunks lie spread across muddy ground, filling the air with a scent of decay. The poison ivy reaches out from the vile-looking trees which stand hunched over one another with their twisted, gnarled trunks and branches. The forest is pitch-black, and it is difficult to discern what lies beyond the immediate surroundings.
106433: The dark forest guards itself closely from intruders with its densely-growing vines, dark ferns and thorny thickets. Some of the great trees have fallen heavily to the ground and now house a myriad of pests. The gnarled trees spread their territory far into the north and east, leaving no vegetation untouched by its corrupting darkness.
106434: A skeleton of some humanoid lies in the dust.

Corrupted trees, ensnared by darkened vines, have fallen heavily to the ground. There are obvious traces of strife here, with scattered bones, rusted shields and axes still jammed into stumps across the forest floor. The vile surroundings stretch further into the west and south.
106435: A shadowy haunt floats here, oblivious to your presence.

Vines and poison ivy are aggressively approaching the ground, hanging down from the trees which support them. Roots are crossing each other's paths, creating small pits for thorny bushes, as well as small animal hideouts. A great earth mound rises to the north, leaving a small passage that passes just east of it. To the extreme east gnarled Mirkwood spreads its canopy crowns high and far. Great shadows encompass the forest, blotting out any specific details of the land to the south.
106446: The trees of Mirkwood grow as dense as ever at the bottom of this depression, with forested slopes stretching upwards to the east and west. A sad moaning can be heard from within the trees, whose crowns sway restlessly back and forth, yet keep their interwoven forest roof intact. Shrubs grow densely between the vines, which entangle each other in a complex web-like formation. Darkness engulfs the surroundings, demanding attentiveness from the average traveller.
106470: Rotten debris lies scattered across the forest, partially covered by ageing, grey moss.
