Various pests and maggots are in the process of devouring an animal carcass, which lies propped up against an especially dense clump of roots. Traces of cobwebs hang down from great branches of the forest above. The tree crowns form a fine mesh with twisted, gnarled branches, efficiently screening the lower forest from the natural light sources above.
106472: A very heavy branch is lying here on the ground.

Rustling vines and ivy are spread across the forest floor. Twisted, gnarled branches lie scattered amongst the vegetation, spreading a rotten scent through the air. Deep cuts have left gaping wounds in some of the trees; but they stand tall still, leaning their majestic crowns on those in neighbouring parts of the forest. Although pitch-black, more of Mirkwood lies traversable to the north, but the way to the east, west and south is completely blocked by serried ranks of beech and oak.
106505:
A huge grizzly bear is here, roaming the wild.
A bear cub is here, looking around for something to play with.
A bear cub is here, looking around for something to play with.
A bear cub is here, looking around for something to play with.

Gnarled and twisted, these malicious-looking trees intertwine their branches with each other. Their crowns above blot out the sky, preventing any natural light from seeping through. Roots and vines span far across the forest floor, creating a chaotic environment that is extremely hard to move around in. The dense vegetation continues to the west and south, completely blocking any attempts at further exploration, while in the east the darkened Mirkwood forest almost seems to open up, creating a natural alley of sorts.
106506: The darkness here engulfs the whole forest. Great trees appear to line up, forming a natural alley, to the east; while the forest appears to become darker and wilder in the west. The bare roots and yellow, thick vines on the forest floor create a difficult terrain to walk through. Here and there, mighty trees have fallen, and their trunks now play host to a myriad of different mosses, lichen and fungi.
106507: The trees appear to shift uneasily, their massive crowns and branches hovering over the forest floor. The trunks stand lined up next to each other, creating a major alley that leads east and west, deeper into Mirkwood. Irregular, more chaotic flora overwhelms the forest to the west. The forest floor is covered by various kinds of ivy, vines and roots, leaving plenty of space for small creatures to nest and hunt for bugs.
106508: Putrid fungi and a plethora of beetles, centipedes and insects completely cover what looks like an old bear carcass that sits propped up against a fallen trunk. Great beeches and birches form a pitch-dark alley through the forest. The tree crowns above encroach on each other's spaces, stopping any natural light from penetrating through to the ground. The dark soil is densely packed, and it is partly covered in thorny, vine-infested vegetation, partly disrupted by sprouting yellow roots. The natural alley cuts a path through the forest, creating a north and west-bound route.
106509:
A half-decayed corpse of a goblin lies rotting on the ground.
A colossal tree, its trunk as wide as a small cottage, stands here.

The murky forest smells strongly of death and decay. An enormous cocoon of some sort lies cracked open underneath a heavily damaged tree. Centipedes and larvae seem to crawl all over what could only be a carcass, held by the yellowing, silken cocoon. Above, spanning from bough to bough are great cobwebs, some of which have withered, dangling down, reaching towards the forest floor.
106510: This web-covered platform has the appearance of having been put together for the purpose of having a guarded entrance into a dark and dreadfully cramped crawlspace. Rough steps have been cut into the trunk of the giant oak tree, and hanging vines and cobweb-covered branches makes moving around in here possible, if not exactly easy. A black, webby funnel leads eastwards, and this site also provides a very good view of whatever might be going on down on the forest floor beneath it.
106511: A tiny spider is here, eating a tiny bug.

Great, sticky nets of cobweb have been stuck together with twigs and branches in order to fashion the walls of this dark and narrow pocket of air. Passage is possible only to the west and north of here, since great boughs and branches would block any attempt to venture into other regions of the canopy.
106512: Blackish, decaying cobwebs are stuck to every surface here, blocking out any possibility for outside light to shine in here. The webs that comprise the walls and floor of this place are of an unusual, not very sticky kind - something that cannot be said for the strands of fresh, sticky webs that hang down from the branches above, clinging to anything that moves in here. Passage is possible up from here, along what looks like rough steps that have been cut into a tree trunk.
106513: This narrow space is nothing more than a cylindrical passage that closely hugs the trunk of a massive, blackened oak tree. The floor is made up of a number of roughly-hewn trellises, kept together by sticky, thick cobwebs and vines. The trellises form a few rough steps that lead either upwards into what appears to be fresher air, or down, further into the bowels of this grotesque treetop.
106514:
Foul webs span across Mirkwood, engulfing the exit east with their complex patterns.
A mass of wriggling vines drops on you from the trees.
A black spider crawls here, a shiny red spot visible on its belly.
A huge, poisonous tarantula extends her legs to you.
A wolf spider is here, among the trees.

Thick, slippery oak boughs make a sort of trellis that serves as a floor on this rickety platform. East of here, a dark, funnel-like hole opens up into the canopy of a gigantic, black oak. The only other option is to go down through a dark hole, further into the bowels of these grotesquely webbed, stinking trees.
106515: This platform is a gangway between two huge tree-trunks, and the air here seems fresh compared to the stinking holes east and south of here. The platform itself seems to have been constructed out of thick oak boughs, bundled together and held in place by thick, sticky cobwebs. Travel is possible east, into a smelly, pitch-black hole in the leaf-works of a gigantic oak, or west, into lighter but still dark and dense foliage. There is also an option to head south, into a tight, black cocoon-like structure.
106516: A greenish slime mould is here, smelling badly.

The horrific spiders that use this place as a lair surely must not care much for cleanliness or tidiness. Large piles of unidentifiable rotting organic material lean against the trunks and boughs of the surrounding trees. Blackening, decaying cobwebs hang down from the branches, intermingled with fresher, transparent webbing; it appears that while the inhabitants do not care for the appearance of this sordid place, they do seem to know how to keep it from falling apart.
106517:
A newborn spider is here.
A newborn spider is here.
A newborn spider is here.

The stench in here is strong enough to take on a physical quality of its own - a thick, dark miasma that has ben absorbed into everything in here, coating the six walls and all it contains with an oily, dark-brown substance. The floor of the cocoon is covered by huge stacks of brittle, blackish material in varying states of decay - it is more or less impossible to tell whether they once were bones or branches. The only exit out of here is to the north, out into what appears to be far fresher air.
106518: A wolf spider is here, among the trees.

Compared to the pitch-dark, stinking hole down from here, this little webbed platform among the trees appears to be closer to the outside, judging from the much fresher air in here. Still, the place is tiny and dark. Layers upon layers of thick, dark cobwebs have been plastered on every available surface. Apart from the smelly, black hole leading down, further exploration is possible west from here.
106519: A huge, poisonous spider is here.

Shredded, rotting filaments of spider webs hang down above a dark hole south of this swaying, creaking platform high up among the tree tops. The platform itself appears to be made out of cobwebs woven together with branches and vines, making it a reasonably solid place to stand on.
106520: On top of the Highest Tree

A large, black butterfly is fluttering about erratically.
A large, black butterfly is fluttering about erratically.
A large, black butterfly is fluttering about erratically.

Upon the highest and slenderest branches of the enormous tree, an unblocked view opens up in all directions. An endless sea of dark green and black tree tops can be seen all around, ruffled here and there by the breeze. Above is nothing but the sky, and a number of butterflies can be seen flying around.
106521:
A tiny spider is here, eating a tiny bug.
A tiny spider is here, eating a tiny bug.

This tiny, claustrophobic space is completely covered in blackened, sticky cobwebs that hang from every last tree-branch, creating a midnight-black passage that stretches west and upwards. The space measures just three feet by eight, with no standing room for anything taller than a Dwarf or Orc. A foreboding, rustling sound can be heard in here, but it is impossible to tell whether the sound is emanating from this room or from one adjacent to it.
106522: A brown wolf is standing here, ridden by you.

The dark soil here is packed densely, creating a very solid surface to walk on. The even ground is disrupted by roots that spring out of the ground, only to dive back into the dirt a few feet away. Darkness enshrouds the forest, its trees creating a huge alley. Their boughs and crowns entangle each other, forming a dense, leafy ceiling above. The natural alley continues its path to the south. Northwards the forest appears to be unusually tangled and dark.
106523: The forest starts to gather itself slightly. Its darkened trees and heavy vegetation grow more and more dense. Great roots extend from the dark soil, spanning far across the forest floor, only to dig into the ground again. Darkness enshrouds Mirkwood, making it difficult to discern anything other than the immediate surroundings. Old, fallen vegetation gives nourishment to every growing thing, expanding and weaving underneath and around the warped roots and trees on the forest floor.
106524:
A quail stands motionless.
A cockroach is scuttling across the floor carrying some debris.

Misshapen and twisted trees with great branches and roots form a difficult area to travel through. Although relatively spread out, the thick clusters of plants that span the forest floor require caution as to where to put ones feet. Some of the trees here suffer from cleaved trunk and broken boughs, as if someone had taken an axe to them in the recent past. The dark and malicious forest opens up for further exploration in the east and west, while it looks perfectly impassable to the north and south.
106525: The dense forest is full of gnarled and twisted trees that are engulfing the surroundings in the pitch-black darkness. The soil beneath has become quite soft allowing new shrubs and roots to take hold more easily. Some of the great oaks and beeches have fallen down; slowly decomposing they are now bringing a perpetual smell of rot and decay to the air.
106526:
A huge grizzly bear is here, roaming the wild.
A bear cub is here, looking around for something to play with.
A bear cub is here, looking around for something to play with.
A bear cub is here, looking around for something to play with.

The trees of this forest rise tall, stretching up towards the sky. The great tree crowns unite up there, forming a tightly interwoven quilt that keeps the forest in eternal darkness. The majority of the trees look agonized, their trunks warped and their branches twisted. Some have been cleaved in the middle with axes, while others appear to have been struck by lightning at some point. Vines and ivy smother most of the many fallen trees that litter the forest floor. The route to the south appears impossible to take, as a wall of tangled, thorny shrubs and gnarled trees rise up to form a formidable wall. The east and west offer more room for further travelling.
106527: This corrupted forest appears to stretch far away in all directions. The tree crowns above intertwine, creating a dense and impenentrable quilt. At ground level, the blackened soil is grainy, greasy and somewhat soft to the touch. Fallen trees have left great craters behind, from where their roots used to dig deep into the forest floor. Vines and ivy cover most of the fallen trunks, and small centipedes, beetles and various other insects crawl around on the ground, feasting on dead and decomposing plant materials as well as on each other.
106528: Great, warped roots spring out from the ground, criss-crossing the forest floor and digging into the dirt with gusto. The gnarled trunks twist and turn in a most unnatural manner. Heavily-intertwined branches and boughs create a natural patchwork that leaves the forest in a pitch-black darkness. The dark soil is quite soft and saturated with water, giving off an unmistakable smell of rot and decay. An immense tangle of vegetations rise in the south, leaving the area impossible to travel through. The warped forest looks slightly more open to the west.
106529:
A very large tree branch has been ripped from a tree.
Massive, black, oozing vines reach out from the choked canopy.

Warped trees lean onto each other for support here. Their heavy crowns grow so densely together that no sunlight from above can penetrate down to the ground. The tree-trunks carry open, gaping wounds, while others have been smitten with some kind of black, lumpy parasitical growth. South of here, an immense tangle of roots rupture out of the ground. Vines and shrubs grow everywhere in between the great, malicious-looking trees. The air is quite moist, and the dark soil is spongy and almost saturated by blackish, foul-smelling water.
106554: Shimmering Webs in the Sombre Woods

The trees are bent under the weight of aeons of unfettered growth, while bushes and shrubs grow unchecked. Many trees appear twisted and bent as if frozen in a state of mourning. Laced with oddly shimmering spider webs, weeds and long branches, the forest is very difficult for all but the smallest creatures to move easily in.
106555: A fine haze swirls through the air in this part of Mirkwood forest. It has a peculiar scent that is difficult to place. Moisture clings to clothing but none of it seems to pool on the ground in drinkable quantities. The very trees seem to be sucking every drop up before it can puddle.
106556:
A cluster of dark green, feathery fronds flourishes in the shade.
A huge black fungus is here, exuding a foul stench.
A huge black fungus is here, exuding a foul stench.
A small termite is running around making strange sounds.
A mass of wriggling vines drops on you from the trees.

Black, huge oaks stand side by side, their great branches reaching upwards, entangling themselves into the intact canopy that does not allow any sunlight to reach the forest floor. The haze drifting in from the north thickens here to become actual fog, that now makes any kind of travel hazardous. Dim and dark tree-like shapes seem to move with menacing gestures, cloaked by the mist.
106557:
Some thick writhing vines whip all around you.
Some thick writhing vines whip all around you.
A mass of wriggling vines drops on you from the trees.

The trees gather together in a tight circle, forming a deep and dark grove. Thick gnarled trunks and black branches stick together creating an intact wall which prevents travelling anywhere but to the west. Nothing but a sinister canopy can be seen above, blocking any light to reach the grove. Occasional noises of small animals creep through the underbrush.
106558: Darkness pervades the sad trees in this part of Mirkwood. Heavy foliage and thick branches crowd out any hint of the sky above. The weight of the overhanging vegetation causes the trees to droop, contributing to the feeling of dreariness so evident throughout the woods.
106559: The oaks, birches, and firs here seem to be congregating to decide how best to deal with interlopers. The feeling of being unwelcome is quite strong and progress here is impeded with each step as thorny bushes, hanging branches, and virulent weeds catch and snag flesh and skin.
106560: A swift and agile forest cat moves silently through the vegetation.

Silence drapes this forested area like a thick, black executioner's cloak. Branches overhead move in the wind without making a single sound. It is like walking in an underwater landscape as the air feels so oppressively thick. Dark and gloomy, the trees appear to be pondering your presence.
106561:
The corpse of a black squirrel is lying here.
The corpse of a slithering snake is lying here.
The corpse of a striped snake is lying here.
A shrub with maple-like leaves is growing here.
On the shrub, there are two handfuls of blackcurrant berries.

The dark soil is soft and moist here, and the air is heavy and damp. The trunks and roots of the warped trees are almost completely covered by ivy and vines. Small bugs, centipedes and other insects are abundant; no doubt they have found a perfect place to spawn here. Bushes of various sizes grow between the large oaks and beeches, making it difficult to discern anything but the immediate surroundings. The undergrowth appears to shift slightly, constantly rustling. The darkness lies dense over Mirkwood, a darkness that is well protected by the heavy, depressing canopy of tree crowns above.
106585:
A large brown snake with black patches is coiled here.
A tree-snake lies wrapped around one of the tree branches.
A tree-snake lies wrapped around one of the tree branches.
A tree-snake lies wrapped around one of the tree branches.
A large, dangerous-looking green snake is coiled up here.
A large brown snake with black patches is coiled here.

This forsaken dead end in the forest of Mirkwood is hemmed in on all sides by the looming, immense trunks of oak and beech trees that rise up between thorny, tangled bushes. The resulting dark, pit-like glade seems to be home to great number of snakes that seem to be everywhere at once, slithering around amongst the smothering undergrowth and fallen twigs and branches. The only way out of this miserable place is south, where it appears to be at least a little bit possible to travel through the dark forest.
106586: Heavy, sticky cobwebs tightly woven together with debris and boughs form this almost bridge-like gangway between two tree crowns. The sky is completely blocked out by the canopy above, a leafy, webbed entity that rustles ceaselessly as if animated from within by something fairly large. The passageway spirals lazily upwards upon a sticky platform, following the natural shapes of the dark forest.
106587: Movement in this narrow space is severely hampered by the sharp, thorny branches that seem to grasp at every movement. The branches themselves are covered in sticky, slimy cobwebs in varying stages of decay. The smell in here is unbelievable and can only be described as utterly alien yet frightfully familiar: akin to something sickly-sweet that has been burned by some unthinkable otherworldly flame. Passage is possible down, north and west, further into similar webbed, confined areas.
106588: Great filaments of silken webs form a thick, sticky coccoon-like room here, high up in the forest canopy. Judging from the sticky quality of the webs, one can deduce that they were spun fairly recently by something unnaturally large. The webs are thick enough to block out all outside light, forming a suffocating, cramped dead end.
106589:
corpse (here) :
a double edged eket (used)
a silver wedding ring
a gold ring

A rotten corpse is hanging here.
A half-decayed corpse of a goblin lies rotting on the ground.

It is obvious that this dark and unwholesome place serves as a storage area for the spiders that inhabit these dark, webbed tunnels. Judging by the bones and rotting flesh that fester in piles here, the spiders are decidedly carnivorious. The only exit from this horrid-smelling place is to the east, into a pitch-black, cramped tunnel.
106590: The corpse of a forest spider is lying here.

It is hard to get a general idea of the layout of this webbed space, where strands upon strands of silky filaments hang from bough to bough, creating a dark, confined space where twisting passages lead further into this acrid-smelling maze. To the north the cobwebs appear to have been torn apart by something forceful and sharp.
106591: This tunnel bends around a trunk, or perhaps it is an exceptionally thick bough. No longer a neat circle in shape, the tunnel is squashed by the bend. Intricate and beautiful, the webs here are pristine, pure white silk entwining slivers of silver. In the south it appears major damage has been done to the tunnel; something has sliced through web and leaf alike.
106593: A greenish slime mould is here, smelling badly.

Along the upward slope, spoiled and decaying cocoons line the floor and walls. A narrow gap leads upwards into further tunnels, apparently the source of the refuse lying scattered here. Death is heavy in the air, a presence of evil and malevolence lingers here among the corpses and decay. The webs here are decayed and discoloured as though the corpses have stained the tunnel. While unblemished silver-white lines the ceiling, brown decay scars the floor and walls.
106594: Branches continue to spiral around, bent and growing wildly out of shape. Within the structure, webs spun of chaos line everything in their beautiful silver-white patterns. From the ceiling, low-hanging webs entangle anything and everything that brushes against them. Strong and sticky, they cling to insect and beast alike.
106595: The structure of the tunnel is subtly different here - from the look of it, it is part of a more ancient section. Branches have been bent around, twisted in amongst the webs so they continue to grow in a bizarre spiral shape, supporting and holding up the structure - the tunnel is now quite cylindrical and solid. Webs still maintain their dense and sticky presence, but now filling in spaces between thick and bent boughs.
106596: The webbing here is ancient and, though still thick and sturdy, especially worn. Much traffic must pass this intersection. The ceiling sags slightly and tiny amounts of water seep through it. The pronounced sag continues further in the east. All tunnels leading off this intersection seem to be narrow, poorly lit and difficult to pass unhindered due to the chaotic mass of webbing. Small hapless creatures have been caught in the sticky webs and left for dead, covered with new layers and forgotten.
106597: Cocoons litter the floor, interspersed with clusters of eggs, nestled carefully into the surrounding webs. Red, black and white clusters are visible in the lining of the tunnel web: glinting slightly, they appear like rich jewels embedded upon a thick luxurious fur. The webs here are very extensive, providing protection for the gleaming eggs and looking rather more like a thick fur than a web.
106598: The base of the tunnel is very solid here, though the ceiling seems to sag with age. A small hole above, running next to a sturdy trunk allows passage upwards, though it is a very tight fit. A stench hangs heavy in the air here, rank like a fog of death. Remains of corpses litter the ground, and lead into the east. There is some water on the ground here, weeping through the ceiling webs above as though in protest of the surrounding death and decay.
106599: A piece of bloody meat lies here.

Without any direct source of illumination, this chamber is nevertheless lit by a faint, inexplicable glow. However, far from providing a touch of beauty, the light merely emphasises the mess which covers the floor and some of the sticky walls. Heavily-webbed cocoons litter the floor, stick to the walls and hang from the ceiling. Remains scattered all over highlight the number of deaths that must take place here every day. Tucked behind two corpses lies a small cluster of eggs, glistening like eyes of a giant spider.
106600: Silky, lead-grey spider webs cover absolutely everything here. A group of darkened old beeches have been completely overtaken by arachnid activities. The ground is soggy and muddy, and patches of moss provide the driest patches to stand on. Two dead trees have fallen against each other here, and their branches reinforced by the webbing serve to create a solid opening upwards into the forest canopy.
106623: The trees of Mirkwood stand aligned with one another, reaching for the sky. Their crowns unfold far up in the air, covering every inch of the sky, leaving the natural light outside. Across the forest floor decaying vines, twigs and bushes spread an odour of death. The dark forest opens up to more readily-accessible woods to the north and south.
106624: Oak and beech stand tall and proud, their crowns cooperatively forming a vast canopy, stretching far up into the air. Darkened vines and ivy encircle their trunks, while heavy vegetation of bushes and roots cover their bases. The ground is covered in decomposing leaves and twigs. The aggressive vegetation allows for little exploration, leaving only the north accessible.
106625:
Some roots lie here waiting to ensnare weary travellers.
Massive roots shift uneasily all around you.

The threatening, malevolent forest is dark. The sky above cannot be seen through the net of thick branches, thus eternal darkness encompasses the seemingly endless, massive trees that tower eerily into the great heights. Tangled, half-rotten vines hang gloomily down from the twisted tree limbs, here and there intertwining with the feral, unhealthy looking black bushes. A stench of death hangs heavily in the air.
106628: The uneven ground, covered in damp moss and the occasional patch of grass, undulates around the oak and fir. The trees cast faint shadows in the already dim light. To the east a trail of broken branches and disturbed moss leads into the heavy undergrowth.
106645: A Dead End in the Forest

Beech and oak stretch their branches far towards the sky, meeting in a great collaboration of crowns far up in the air which creates a veritable quilt of leaves, preventing almost all natural light from seeping through. Mirkwood grows into a great barrier to the south, west and east, creating an impenetrable wall. The soil is dark and nourishing, giving life to an immense amount of greenery and insect life. The old forest trail opens up in the north.
106680: Dark Woods south of a Ridge

A grassy slope can be glimpsed to the north, through and beyond an impassable wall of brambles and dense, thorny vegetation. Patches of black moss grow on the ground in between thick, knotted roots and several clusters of grey mushrooms sprout up in dense clumps among the moss. A faint smell of decay seems to emanate from the moss or the mushrooms, or possibly both.
106681:
A huge, poisonous tarantula extends her legs to you.
A black moth flutters around.
A black moth flutters around.

Several of the massive, ancient oaks growing here seem affected by some kind of disease. The bark has fallen off from large areas of the gnarled trunks. The whole area around the trees is covered by a thick, foul-smelling cobweb. Passage to the north and south is blocked by a tangled mass of large, thorny bushes.
106682: Lush, evergreen foliage encroaches upon any open space here on the forest floor beneath the dense boughs of Mirkwood. The boughs above are thick and the canopy dense, and even during the brightest of days, only slivers of light would reach the ground. Beyond the impassable tangles of thorny brush to the north, there is a grassy slope leading upwards to a ridge.
106683: The earth is covered by layers of dark green fir needles. The forest is shrouded in deep shadows and little light ever finds the way through the thick foliage above down to the forest floor. The woods have an air of ages immemorial about them and many of these trees have probably stood here for centuries.
106684: A pile of dry, brown leaves lies here.

This entire area of Mirkwood is cast in eternal gloom, with a dense canopy above shutting out the outside world. The twisted shapes of ancient trees loom like obscure, menacing shadows in the encroaching darkness. The forest floor is covered by layers of decaying leaves and green fir needles.
106685: Some roots lie here waiting to ensnare weary travellers.

Dark, malignant forest spreads in all directions. The numerous roots and dense, black bushes that grow all around the area make travelling difficult. A group of twisted trees looks strangely different than the other surrounding trees; with their hunchback trunks, dried branch arms and lichen beards they closely resemble a band of old, withered men, eternally frozen to the positions where they stand.
106686: A small clearing opens up under the black, web-infested canopy of Mirkwood. The opening is surrounded by thorn-bushes and a tangled network of vines that hang from the boughs above. Grey spider webs of different sizes have been woven throughout the area; one especially vast web is located to the south, completely blocking the route towards that direction. A road is barely visible behind the trees to the north.
106687: Mirkwood gets very dense here, as if being reluctant to allow one to travel any further, and trying to hinder and resist every single step forward. Giant, dark bushes block the openings between the trees and gnarly roots reach forward, tripping and trapping the travellers. A malignant, grim aura lies above the forest - the forest is listening, watching and waiting.
106688: Foul webs span across Mirkwood, engulfing the exit east with their complex patterns.

The surrounding forest is composed primarily of large black firs. The trees look strange: they have no needles, and their dark barks have been disfigured. Some trunks have fallen down, while others have strange roots which intertwine with each other and dig deep into the forest floor, making travelling very difficult. Numerous spider webs litter the canopy. The forest opens slightly to the east and south where the trees are mainly oaks and beeches.
106689: A long and very sharp thorn is lying here.

A huge, flourishing tree stands tall among dead but still menacing-looking black trees. Its branches, decorated by the remains of spider webs, are very impressive and seem to move slightly independently of wind's blowing. There is some open space to the west while to the other directions the vegetation looks too dense to allow anyone to pass easily through.
106698: The forest is very dense and the ground sometimes seems marshy. It is quite impossible to leave the narrow trail which snakes between the trunks. To the west, some old, dead roots are entangled with huge bushes. To the north and east, the Old Forest Road extends its grey shape, barely visible between the trees.
106699: The open meadow provides an uninterrupted view to the sky, a rare sight in Mirkwood. To the north the Old Forest Road can be seen winding to the east and west. The ground slopes to the southeast here, and gets increasingly more moist as one moves to the west. The dark forest stands at the southern edge of the meadow, although there seems to be a narrow gap between the trees.
106700: This corner of the meadow slopes slightly downhill, leading towards the trees in the south. The ground gets marshier on the southern side of the meadows, and deep animal tracks can be seen in the soft black earth. Thick black tangles of roots and vines make their way up the slope toward the southern edge of the flowing meadow. A young sapling sprouts in the southeast edge of the meadow, an indication of invasion by Mirkwood from the south.
106701: A grove of trees is spaced out here, along the edge of a meadow which continues to the east. Each of the five trees has a slightly different appearance: one has a deep, thick bark with red edges; another, a thinner shinier bark with white accents. They stand in a rough ring shape, and their creaking in the wind makes it seem as though they are talking to one another. To the north a road can be seen continuing to the east and west.
106702:
A large bat is here, hanging in the darkness.
A large bat is here, hanging in the darkness.
A large bat is here, hanging in the darkness.
The queen bat is here, emitting piercing squeaks.
A small, red-spotted spider lurks here.

The air here feels as evil as the decrepit corpses look. Death and decay are everywhere, and rotting cocoons further mar the yellowing webs. Eggs can be seen carefully inlaid within the webbed structure. Where to the east the webs have a kind of beauty, it is not so here. Whatever spun this nest created a chaotic mess, apparently designed to ensnare anyone who enters while deftly reflecting its own utter madness in the construction.
106703: The great branches upon which this section is wound creak slightly in protest at their jobs. From below and in the west, the pungent aura of death emanates into this tree-top web. Rotting corpses left under layers of silk scar the otherwise hauntingly beautiful webbed tunnel. The intricate and delicate webs continue into the east, away from the death of the surrounding tunnels. Branches arch overhead, but no longer wrap their lengths around the tunnel in a silent embrace.
106715: An odd fog engulfs the forest floor. Thick blankets of warm fog push out and wrap around the passerby as they seem to glide over this forest floor anomaly. To the touch, the fog is oddly warm and moist. Underneath the white covering, the forest floor is damp and covered with molds and fungi which leach off the moisture in the air. To the west the fog appears to rise from the forest floor up into the forest, reaching high into the canopy. In the south the fog dissipates and a faint opening can be seen.
106716:
A cluster of dark green, feathery fronds flourishes in the shade.
A brown, long-legged spider swiftly charges at you.
A brown, long-legged spider swiftly charges at you.
A brown, long-legged spider swiftly charges at you.
A brown, long-legged spider swiftly charges at you.
A grey spider is stalking here, preparing to drain you of life.
A huge, poisonous spider is here.
A huge, poisonous spider is here.
A black spider crawls here, a shiny red spot visible on its belly.

The terrain is cumbersome here. Ferns spread across the forest floor underneath tall fir and beech, and cobwebs stretch through the air between the old, gnarled branches of this ancient forest. The tall undergrowth impedes freedom of movement, while offering a perfect hunting ground for such carnivores as are suited to this enviornment. Rotten cocoons hang from a few trees, cracked open and emptied. Nearby lie half-eaten carcasses, infested by larvae. A stench of death spreads across the area.
106717: Thorny vines hang down from the gnarled branches of the trees growing densely together here. From a decaying corpse, already almost covered with vines and fallen leaves, spreads a stench of death. The forest has been heavily ravaged in the east, leaving an open way through the foliage. An eerie gloom imposes itself from the west; in the north, the forest continues.
106718: The earth cave is quite narrow, yet deep and tall. The walls of black soil are covered partly by fungi and mosses, partly by insects and stains of blood. Small roots and twigs stick out from the roof and sides, some of which carry rugged tufts of black hair. A gnawed-on carcass of a bear cub lies among a neatly-gathered pile of leaves and twigs. Remains of cracked bones lie scattered across the cave. The ground has been heavily packed, as if walked upon for many a year.
106779: A gloom settles deeper upon the forest the further in one travels. The ominous presence of an evil force permeates the vegetation all around. The trees seem to darken and lean in while the soft growth underfoot seems to grab at feet. At all turns, vines and mosses hang down as if looking for a catch.
106780: The thick foliage of the trees above prevents the sun ridding the forest floor of its perpetual dusk. These woods seem almost too thorny to allow travelling in any direction, though one might try to squeeze through the dense thickets growing in the east and south. Going northwards seems impossible, while westwards it appears to be clearer.
106781: The deeper in the heart of Mirkwood, the darker things become. An uneasy tension intensifies as a rustling whisper scuttles around and through the leaves of the overhanging trees. Each step must be carefully placed as broken branches and scraggly roots seem to cover the ground. The air has a chill in it that has nothing to do with temperature.
106782: The canopy of treetops overhead block out direct light, adding to the feeling of tension that underlies all of Mirkwood. Red and verdant mosses tangle with thick, tawny vines to create a densely packed forest. Moist, decaying leaves exude a sour smell when disturbed. Beetles and ants seem to crawl everywhere.
106783:
Foul webs span across Mirkwood, engulfing the exit east with their complex patterns.
A great wolf with coal-black eyes stares intently at you, drooling saliva.

Dark, tall trees stand silently in the forest, spreading their branches in all directions and intermingling with each other to create an intact canopy which blocks all the light to reach the ground. The air is thick and heavy with a distinct odour of moist and rotting plants rising from the dank undergrowth. Undisturbed fungi and lichens choke the surrounding tree trunks.
106784: Thick and humid air weaves in and around the stout trunks and hanging vines. The moisture in the air encourages the lichens to bloom on almost every stationary surface. Slimy moss and vines dangle from overhead branches to form what feels like wet hair that has to be pushed through in order to pass.
106786: Thick boughs and a dense canopy of leaves form a roof above that blots out the sky completely, not allowing even a sliver of light through. Yet even in the perpetual gloom here on the forest floor, dense tangles of undergrowth seem to thrive. A scent of corruption drifts through the forest, seemingly emanating from grey, pallid mushrooms that grow in clusters on some of the ancient tree-trunks.
106787: This gloomy part of Mirkwood is overgrown with large tangles of intertwining brush and bramble. Old, twisted trees rise up from among the brambles, the heavily-leaved treetops forming a dense canopy above. The only viable directions of travel are to the south, deeper into the tangles, or up a short slope towards the east.
106791: A dark iridescent dragonfly flies by.

Large, tangled shrubs of evergreen flourish in this part of Mirkwood forest. The dense branches above blot out most of the sky, yet at places, openings in the canopy allow a glimpse of the heavens above. The light that might slip through is not enough to lift the deep shadows that shroud the forest.
106792:
Foul webs span across Mirkwood, engulfing the exit south with their complex patterns.
A dense patch of dark ferns grows in the shade.
A quail stands motionless.

Great thickets of thorny, entangled shrubs cover the forest floor, their tangled, twisted branches intertwining so much that it is all but impossible to tell where one large bush ends and the one next to it begins. Yet even amongst this abundant undergrowth, there seems to be just enough open spaces to squeeze through to other areas of the forest, if one do not mind being pricked and stung by the many thorns.
106793: Thick, slithering vines crawl up the suffering trunks of ancient oaks. The vines ensnare the ancient, gnarled trunks as if to choke the life out of them. Large patches of bark have come off the trees and the wood underneath is covered by a thick, slimy layer of grey mould. The many large, tangled bushes growing here collude to make these woods a hazardous maze to travel, with sharp thorns ready to sting and snag, and twisted branches and knotted roots to trip and hinder, the careless traveller.
106794: This part of the forest is almost cave-like in appearance. The vegetation is thick and impassable on all sides except a small opening between two ancient, gnarled oaks to the north. The centre of this small hollow is surprisingly free of undergrowth, creating a small open area maybe twenty feet across. Yet even there long branches reach out above, blotting out the sky and shrouding the small glade in darkness.
106795: A variety of bushes and shrubs thrive here, despite the shade and gloom. Little light manages to find its way down through the dense crowns of the trees. Large mushroom patches grow on the ground, but many of them seem to be attacked by a parasite or suffer from some kind of disease for they are covered with specks of grey mould and surrounded by a thick stench of rot.
106796: The ground is wet and soggy, almost marsh-like. Ancient stands of beech and maple intermingle with tangled growths of thorn-covered bushes. The air is thick with the smell of decay and the ground is covered with a moist mess of decomposing plants and leaves.
106798:
A bright red mushroom is growing here.
Pitch-black water with a strange smell has collected here.
A huge black fungus is here, exuding a foul stench.
A giant, strange looking green fungus is here, ready to devour you in seconds.
A huge black fungus is here, exuding a foul stench.
A monstrous grey, putrid fungus is growing on a large oak here.
An ancient fungus smothers the boulders.

Small, filthy pools of shallow water filled with rotting vegetation have formed between the trees. The murky gloom and tangled undergrowth make it all but impossible to separate solid ground from rotten plants with water underneath, yet with care it might be possible to move from one dry spot to another.
106800: A hollow tree is growing upright here.

Great, old trees with their gnarled trunks, hanging boughs and intact crowns grow in abundance in this area, preventing sunlight from reaching the ever-dark ground of Mirkwood. Between the trunks enormous, tangled bushes have conquered whatever space is left. The ground itself is covered with black leaves and other litter.
106801: A tight, endless canopy darkens the forest. Below it, the ground slopes slightly upwards to the east where a continuous mesh of sharp-leafed, black bushes are growing next to each other, completely filling the ground and blocking travel in that direction. The bushes have encircled the gigantic tree trunks, and intermingled with the vines hanging from the dark, thick boughs.
106802: Some black, oozing vines reach out from the choked canopy towards you.

Some sturdy branches of dark oaks are growing near to the ground, allowing travel in the lower canopy of Mirkwood. Down below, the ground is completely choked by the dense, intermingled undergrowth. Giant roots are stretching outwards, thorny bushes grow all around, and sticky vines complete the chaos by binding shrubs and boughs together.
106803:
A dark green, foul-smelling shrub grows to about a foot in height.
On the shrub, there are two piles of white, egg-shaped berries.

The oppressive, dark forest continues in all directions. Gloomy black alders tower upwards and their wide, black crowns integrate into each other high above, creating an intact canopy which blocks out all the light from the sky. The ground slopes steeply towards the east. The numerous roots and darkling shrubs that cover it, seem to shift around in the darkness, as if blocking the way on purpose.
106804:
A cluster of dark green, feathery fronds flourishes in the shade.
A brown snail is crawling across the ground here leaving a slimy trail behind.
A dense patch of dark ferns grows in the shade.

A narrow, forested ravine runs between two slopes, which tower upwards to the west and east like darkened, tree-covered walls. At the bottom of the hollow the air is moist, making the black, dense undergrowth wet and partly rotten. Strong roots twist on the ground, black leaves create a sticky layer of forest litter, and ferns grow here in abundance.
106805:
A cluster of dark green, feathery fronds flourishes in the shade.
A cluster of dark green, feathery fronds flourishes in the shade.

The air is humid in this part of Mirkwood. Giant, poisonous-looking ferns cover the forest floor and among them occasional, moss-covered rocks litter the ground. The black oaks and other trees are infested by a sickness, as some of the branches are leafless and dead, and on the trunks of the giant trees are grow sickly-green fungi.
106813:
A huge, poisonous tarantula extends her legs to you.
A quail stands motionless.

A multitude of dead leaves in hues of brown and green are ensnared among the dense shrubbery here. The ground is covered in yet more dead leaves that lie piled up against trunks of trees and beneath the shrubs and bushes. The area is dark and visibility very limited due to the deep, dark shadows and heavy foliage.
106834: Pitch-black water with a strange smell has collected here.

The ground here is soft and wet. Small, shallow pools of dark, vile water have gathered in the lower parts of hollows. Dense undergrowth grows across drier land and foul water alike, leaving few paths open for travel. Amidst the undergrowth, gnarled and twisted trunks of oak and beech rise up, their heavy boughs above casting the forest into gloomy shadows.
106882: Vast expanses of densely growing shrubs and brush fill every hollow and nook, making passage difficult as sharp thorns snag, prickle and sting even the most heedful traveller. The dark shadows and perpetual gloom further heighten the need for caution when attempting to traverse these woods.
106920: This piece of tunnel seems to serve no purpose except for joining the depths below to the broadening tunnel in the west. Powerful boughs break through the upper section of tunnel, squashing it down until there is nothing but crawling room. It is almost impossible to move about here at all, down or west are the only possibilities.
106921: There is a slight but clear downwards slope from the north to the east. The webs below sag with weight, stretching the whole structure from top to bottom. Around the vast trunk of a tree, the tunnel bends from north to east with grace and beauty, scarred only by the sorry state of this bend. The tree has been scuffed and scratched by an unknown source, not deeply, but through much of the thick, brown bark.
106922: Tree branches create bulges in the floor and ceiling, leaving only a narrow gap through which one may pass. Along the northern side of the vast boughs the tunnel branches out westerly. In the south the tunnel floor seems to slope downwards slightly and there is clear evidence of heavy use. The webbed lining of the tunnel is identical to most sections of the tunnel: grey and sticky.
106923:
A newborn spider is here.
A newborn spider is here.
A newborn spider is here.

Abruptly the tunnel ends at a very solid, dark trunk. The bark appears to have been worn off the trunk and the bare wood beneath exposed by some kind of crude, etched markings. The innermost webs here seem oddly different than elsewhere. Instead of sublimely intricate, they appear haphazard; as though whatever created these webs had very little control or knowledge of what the final beautiful sculpture should look like. Haphazardness gives way to the more organised and carefully woven webs once again as a larger junction opens up to the east.
106924: The interior of this tree is partly hollow and partly solid black wood. Small tunnels zig-zag at hollow parts, creating a network of connections, dead-ends and small passages. The floor of the tunnel is smooth as if having been travelled several and yet again several times back and forth. Few old cobwebs hang from black wood walls.
106925: The splintered and partly decayed interior of this gigantic tree has empty, hollow spots inside the trunk, creating narrow tunnels which crawl up and down and left and right in the dark. At some places the wooden walls look rotten and are covered with a thick layer of mould, while at other spots the wood is as hard as stone. The air feels musty and damp.
106928: The remains of a black fungus lie here in a heap of rotting compost.

A round horizontal passageway leads through the interior of this huge ancient oak. At times the tunnel divides into two or more branches, allowing an entrance to narrow cracks and into wider hollow spaces, at times the entrances are blocked by thick, oozing spider webs. The black walls are growing fungi.
107037: Tunnel around a Huge, Gnarled Trunk

Snaking around a huge tree the tunnel stretches up and descends below like a narrow endless cave. A small platform to the south is the only blemish in its snake-like quality. Dense and strong, the webs of this area appear to be essentail to the structure. Bugs, leaves and twigs help form the cocoon-like structure, sticky and slightly glistening like an eye holding a deadly secret.
107038: Foul webs span across Mirkwood, engulfing the exit east with their complex patterns.

Intermingled with the webs are thick strands of vines, woven firmly between webs like a tapestry of the forest and its history. A vast trunk is plainly visible to the north east, partially blocking the view north and providing one side of a slide downwards into the dark. The addition of the vines as part of the structure of the tunnel lends this place an ethereal green glow which continues into the north around the trunk.
107039: The long passage from almost vertically above comes to a sudden halt and instead worms in amongst the westerly tree limbs. The platform appears very solid and somehow gives the impression of being close to the ground level of the forest. Debris from the network of tunnels above has collected here in random assorted piles of mess and muck. Nothing moves here, no outside signs of life, no small caterpillar or moth desperately searching for escape, all is silent and breathless.
107040: A very large tree branch has been ripped from a tree.

Stillness reigns here, an eerie harmony of forest and web. There is no movement, even the air itself seems pale and withdrawn, unwilling to bring any disruption to the strange beauty of this harmony. The webs here seem more damp and sticky - perhaps this is a rarely-used section of tunnels. Clutter and debris is scattered here, brought in from the eastern tunnel.
107041: Due to the trunk in the south east, there is very little space here. There are very few signs of wear on the base of the tunnel, and the webs seem infinitely complex and chaotic above. For some reason, the sticky webs here are clean of bugs and leaves.
107057:
A copper penny lies on the ground.
A copper penny lies on the ground.
A copper penny lies on the ground.
A copper penny lies on the ground.

At the bottom of the ridge, the dark forest grows quickly dense and entangled, a mass of dark oaks with tightly-entwined branches forming a solid roof above the ground, shutting out all light. Loose gravel fills the side of the ridge facing this way, making it impossible to ascend to the west from here. To the south a mass of dense, high bushes grow making it impossible to pass that way.
107058: A Tall Oak in the Dark Woods

A huge and tall oak dominates the area, reaching high above the other trees, though how high is impossible to tell due to the thick and entwined crowns of the other trees. The forest seems open enough to the north and west, while to the east and south the trees grow far too close to each other to allow passage through, or even seeing through.
107059: The branches of this old oak are strong and broad, forming a natural landing in the tree. Using the boughs, one can proceed further into the canopy without touching the ground of the forest at all. There are old cobwebs and freshly-woven, oozing spider webs on the boughs, indicating that spiders are living in these trees.
107060:
A forest spider is here crawling around.
A forest spider is here crawling around.
A small, red-spotted spider lurks here.
A small, red-spotted spider lurks here.

A delicate, shimmering spider web is hanging in the air next to the blackened trunk of an ancient, giant elm tree. Being finely-woven, the strands of the web seem strong and robust even when the silky threads themselves are quite thin. The strong branches of the elm form bridges to nearby trees, while the swaying spider web can be used as a ladder to proceed upwards, into the canopy.
107061:
A small, red-spotted spider lurks here.
A small, red-spotted spider lurks here.

A spiralling, dark tunnel rises steadily in the trees. It has taken its course from the natural shapes of the forest, following supporting boughs and circling around the trunks which, together with grey, sticky spider webs, form the walls of this tunnel. The visibility in this long, twisting passageway is very limited, reaching to the next turn of the tunnel, but never further.
107062: A black squirrel peers down from the branches of the trees.

There is a myriad of webbed tunnels in this area, forming a maze-like network as they twist to and fro, with passages leading in practically every direction. Sometimes the tunnels cross each other, sometimes they stop abruptly at dead ends where sticky spider webs block further travel.
107065: This sticky, webbed platform offers a view under the dark canopy. Ancient trees stand like giants in the darkness, their crowns joining together somewhere above, beyond the range of visibility. Platforms of some kind have been constructed on the nearby trees, here and there connected to each other by rope bridges made of thick spider webs. An exceptionally large net-like web hangs close to this platform, descending downwards like a giant curtain.
107089: A greenish slime mould is here, smelling badly.

Giant, oozing cocoons and a number of slimy, pulsating egg sacks are sitting in a gross mixture of slime, spider silk and rotten vegetation. This sheltered, stinking nest has been completely covered with a wall of entangled spider webs from all sides save to the south, where a dark tunnel leads out of this place. Above, the dark canopy of Mirkwood with its numerous spider webs overlooks the area.
107094: A cylindrical tunnel snakes along inside the canopy. Its sturdy, solid walls consist of an entangled mess of branches, twigs and black vines, everything having been glued together with spider silk and some kind of sticky, grey paste. The tunnel splits, passageways leading towards the north, east and up.
107107: A greenish slime mould is here, smelling badly.

The tunnel inside the canopy makes a long curve towards the west and south. Travel is hindered by large amounts of trash and stinking filth which cover the floor. Along the way, there are several remains of dead animals, some of them wrapped in rotten cocoons, accompanied by unidentifiable organic tissue splashed on the silky, grey walls.
107120: Some thick writhing vines whip all around you.

High above the ground and an unknown distance below the tree tops, this small platform is located in the ever-dark canopy of Mirkwood. It is based on a few sturdy branches, with vines, leaves and spider silk as construction material. A tremoring spider web has been woven between the trees, providing an unstable- looking bridge to the south, crossing the area in the air.
107121: A small platform has formed on the lower tree branches, offering an unblocked view to the ground. The canopy continues without a break in all directions, forming a black, sheltering roof above the forest floor. Below, a great oak tree has fallen to one side, its crown still stretching up to the canopy, its trunk leaning diagonally against the nearby trees. The trunk itself is broad and gnarled, providing a passageway between the ground and the canopy.
107122: This is a small open area in the forest, almost like a valley. It is surrounded by steep, tree-covered slopes climbing in all directions but the west, where a winding passageway runs deeper into the forest between the tree trunks and hanging vines. One of the gigantic trees has fallen down: its crown still strives towards the canopy, its trunk is leaning at an angle, pointing up, and its clump of roots protrudes from the ground like an accusing arm.
107123: Masses of dark lichens are hanging from the gnarled and bent branches protruding from the wide, dark-grey and black, hulking boles of the twisted trees. They form gloomy curtains in the forest that have to be passed through to travel forward. The visibility is poor, but what one can see indicates that the vine-covered trees are growing too densely in the west and south to allow passage.
107124: Underneath the thick, continuous canopy that covers the forest and envelops it in perpetual darkness, narrow passageways twist between the hulking, dark boles of the trees. To the west the low-hanging branches are covered with some sort of dark vines, and a large mass of thin but heavily-entwined thorny shrub grows densely in the east.
107125:
A huge, horrific spider is prowling here (hidden).
A huge, poisonous tarantula extends her legs to you.
A huge, poisonous spider is here.
A huge, poisonous spider is here.
A black spider crawls here, a shiny red spot visible on its belly.
A black spider crawls here, a shiny red spot visible on its belly.

Old trees have grown close to each other, their low-hanging, entwined branches reaching downwards, as if trying to grab careless travellers. The trunks are surrounded by black bushes and a mass of heavily-entwined, thorny shrubs that rise from the gloomy ground. Silky spider webs have been woven all around, blocking ways between the trees and creating sticky traps. So dense and wide is the network of spider webs and shrubbery of vegetation that it hinders passage in all directions save to the east.
107126:
A huge, poisonous tarantula extends her legs to you.
A huge, poisonous spider is here.
A huge, poisonous spider is here.
A black spider crawls here, a shiny red spot visible on its belly.
A black spider crawls here, a shiny red spot visible on its belly.

Some huge boulders overgrown with vines and mosses block the way to the north. To the east the boulders are replaced by trees covered in thick grey spider webs but the end result is the same: the way is blocked. A small passageway leads to the south and west from here, guarded by moss and lichen-covered trees which seem to reach inwards over the path.
107127: In the perpetual dusk under the cover of the thick canopy the trees stand firmly in the ground, low shrubs growing all around them and vines hanging from their branches. To the east stands an abandoned-looking cottage. Its weather- beaten grey walls are growing moss and mould and vines hanging from canopy have already entwined themselves with the roof and chimney. To the south and west the forest grows denser and no paths can be found while to the north it continues in the same dusk that shrouds this part of the forest.
107132: A large, black butterfly is fluttering about erratically.

Dark the surrounding trees rise, preventing the sun, the moon and the stars from lighting up the paths. Wide the trees twist and stretch, forcing travellers to pass only where the forest allows it. To the north the ground rises and with it each tree seems to grasp at the opportunity to rise above its brethren, to deny them as much space as it can. The trees on the slope are denser and more twisted around each other than elsewhere.
107161: The dark trees keep up their everlasting struggle with each other for what space still remains between them. To the south this battle has temporarily ceased: an unusually wide and gnarled oak rules the area, with no more space left for anything else. The forest allows travel to the west and east, and to the north where it climbs slowly upwards, although remaining as dark and twisted as everywhere else.
107162: A large, black butterfly is fluttering about erratically.

Dark, lichen-covered trees stand tall and silent, their boughs and crowns integrated into the seemingly endless canopy that covers Mirkwood. Great spider webs have been woven all around, making riding impossible and forcing travellers to move with caution to avoid getting stuck in the sticky traps. Narrow and forever-twisting routes lead to the west and south in this inhospitable forest, while dense vegetation blocks all other directions.
107163: The ground slopes upwards to form a large, tree-covered rise in the forest. The ever-present canopy and entwined branches of the dark and gnarled trees keep the area shadowy, providing no more visibility than elsewhere in the forest. The slopes to the west and north are too steep and entangled to be travelled, but one can continue on to the east or the south.
107167: The ground is covered in roots and strange black weeds. Old, angry-looking trees twist around each other in their eternal struggle to reach higher and higher. There are only narrow passageways between the pointed boughs and sharp vines available for anyone or anything to pass deeper into the confusing forest, or to search for an exit to less tangled parts of Mirkwood.
107170:
A shimmering glow is here, emitting pale, green, light.
A large, black butterfly is fluttering about erratically.

Surrounding this hidden glade is a large circle of huge, twisted and bent oaks, which leave only a small opening to the east. The oaks seem to be reaching inwards, towards the centre of the circle, as if to claim something they want but can not reach. The centre of the circle bears an aura of calmness and serenity that is not present in the surrounding woods.
107189: A skeleton of some humanoid lies in the dust.

The black and dark-grey boles of the ever-bending and twisting woods close in, shadowing the shrub-covered ground and limiting visibility. A skeleton is lying against a huge trunk, its pale bones contrasting with the deep, dark colours of the surrounding forest. To the south the forest opens up into a glade, while to the north one could continue travelling deeper into the forest.
107209: Beech trees grow in abundance in this area, their long branches reaching upwards and blending in to the canopy. Dense undergrowth, composed of thick ivy, shrubs and thorn bushes, covers the ground. However, to the north the dense vegetation clears slightly, giving a view of a road that snakes through the oppressive forest. To the east and west the forest seems as dark and dreary as ever.
107210: Huge oaks with thick overarching branches grow in this area of the forest. The soil is dark and gnarled roots twist on the ground. The vegetation is dense, especially to the north and west making it impossible to continue travel in those directions. The faint rustling of leaves can be heard occasionally, like small creatures moving amidst the dense vegetation.
107211: Tightly-growing, shadowy trees result in an intact canopy that does not expose the ground to the sky above. Low branches and shrubs are covered in dark lichens and bracket fungi. The trees are covered in spider webs and spider nests, their small inhabitants patiently waiting for prey to become ensnared. There is a faint trail running to the east and south that shows evidence of regular use.
107212: A faint smell of decomposition pervades the area. A gloomy, oppressive silence hangs here underneath the forest canopy. Spider webs can be seen covering the high and low branches of the trees, mingled with the dark lichens that are abundant in this part of the forest. Trampled vegetation to the north suggests the passing of creatures on a regular basis.
107213: A skull is here, spiked to the end of a pole.

Some ancient trees were cut down around the area, forming a round clearing in the forest. A small shelter stands here, two entrances to the building being visible. Leftovers and carcasses littering the ground attest to the lack of cleanlinesss on part of the inhabitants. Dense vegetation prevents passage to the south. To the west a faint trail, a result of the somewhat frequent passing of creatures in that direction, is barely discernible.
107214:
A small piece of raw meat is on the ground.
A small oaken table has been set here.
On the table, there are a casserole and two small pieces of raw meat.
A large, dusty alcove sits in a wall, smelling of soot.

This unclean, filthy, and stinking room serves as a place to prepare meals: there is a blood-stained table, a blackened fire pit, and a rather large, and very dirty, pot to cook meat in. The floor is covered with half-rotten bones and other litter, the origin of which is not clear. The crude albeit sturdy walls are made of logs and clay. The only properly-made thing in this pigsty is the door: made of heavy material and equipped with an iron lock, it seems capable of keeping unwanted visitors out.
107215: A rudimentary-looking tunnel runs under the ground. The floor is well-trampled, its clay surface being smoothed and packed down over time so that it is now hard as rock, and there is neither litter nor loose gravel on it. At the western end of the tunnel steep stairs, made of logs and a few bigger rocks, lead to the upper floor, and to the east the passageway continues deeper into the earth. The ceiling is relatively high, and shows signs of erosion.
107216:
The corpse of a slender orkish archer is lying here.
The corpse of a robust orc is lying here.
The corpse of a robust orc is lying here.
The corpse of a battle-hardened orc is lying here.
A sturdy peg for hanging armour from is on the wall.

The walls of this room are made mostly of branches, dirt and rocks. The flimsy ceiling, providing some protection from the elements, seems to be designed mostly with the intent of providing shade rather than keeping out any kind of precipitation. Some blankets, filthy and covered with twigs and leaves, can be seen scattered across the room. An acrid smell permeates the room, betraying the lack of cleanliness of its inhabitants.
107217: The corpse of a slender orkish archer is lying here.

Inside, the shelter is dark and crude, with little care taken to keep the place clean. The walls, made mostly of thick trunks, branches and rocks seem to be barely held together by an occasional application of thick, dark mud. The remains of a small fire can be seen in the centre of the room. Scattered on the floor are the remains of past meals, being finished off by small scavenging insects and rodents.
107218: The tunnel has been constructed with rough efficiency. The marks left by picks, hammers and shovels are still visible on the clay walls, and only occasionally have the builders had time and motivation to erect poles supporting the ceiling. The tunnel splits up to the west, east and south.
107219:
A beer barrel has been left here.
A rotten corpse is hanging here.
A wooden cupboard stands here.

Carelessly-assembled, crude shelves line the walls of this small, damp room. There are some containers, lumps of meat and miscellaneous small items on shelves. The ceiling is upheld by several rough pillars of wood, into which pegs have been hammered so that items can be hung from them. The stench of mould and rotten meat hangs in the air.
107220:
The corpse of a great rat is lying here.
The corpse of a large bat is lying here.
A large bat is here, hanging in the darkness (hidden).

This roughly-built passage runs in a north to south direction inside the earth. The walls and the ceiling have been reinforced with occasional logs, otherwise the the walls consist only of hard, dark clay. The floor is smooth, as though there were regular travel back and forth. To the north, the tunnel leads to a junction. There is some kind of separate room to the west. To the south, the tunnel ends at a sturdy wooden door.
107221:
A sturdy crate made of nailed wooden planks sits on the floor.
Several shards of broken glass lie scattered about the ground.
Little parts of a broken weapon are lying on the ground.

This is a small room with arched ceiling and walls constructed of crude bricks. It is being used as a storage room, and is filled with miscellaneous items such as crates and barrels. Alas, the moisture and rot have taken their toll, and old, decayed junk is mostly all that remains. A thick layer of dust covers the floor and all other surfaces.
107222:
The corpse of a bald orc is lying here.
A weapons rack stands against the wall.
In the rack are a dark broadsword, a large wooden wall shield, a sturdy chain mail hauberk and a sturdy pair of chain mail leggings.
A small oaken table has been set here.
On the table, there is a map of Ingrove.

This room is a strange mixture of pompous decoration and filthiness. It seems to be some sort of command post. In the middle of the room stands a desk, with some maps and other small equipment on it. There is an empty space around the table, and the other furniture - a weapon rack, bed and cabinet - stands against the walls around the room. The walls are covered with colourful tapestries whose colours are very different from each other, and many of them are dirty and stained. A huge, rotten spider's head has been nailed to one wall.
107223: A skilfully camouflaged tunnel has been dug under the surface of Mirkwood. The exit leading upwards is hidden under a fallen trunk and giant, black ferns, and the other end of this small passageway ends at an underground door to the north. Next to the door is a small peephole in the wall. The other walls and the floor of the tunnel are made of the soil itself.
107224:
The remains of a swarm of hornets lie here.
The remains of a swarm of hornets lie here.
The remains of a swarm of hornets lie here.
The remains of a shady patch of ferns lie here in a heap of rotting compost.
A fallen tree lies on the ground, its clump of roots pointing upwards.

The branches of dark and gloomy trees hang overhead under a shadowy canopy. Gigantic, gnarled tree trunks and dense undergrowth prevent passage in any direction save to the east. Large fungi grow here among decomposing branches and logs, surrounded by a dense, continuous mat of black ferns.
107225: This part of the dark forest contains a large number of oaks and beeches. Mushrooms grow in clusters between the beeches, taking full advantage of the humid environment that hastens the decomposition of the abundant leaf litter in the area. To the south the foreboding shadows of Mirkwood grow darker with dense, thorn-covered underbrush making passage all but impossible.
107226: Gigantic branches, devoid of leaves, reach down from the canopy. Huge trunks, covered in lichens and black shelf fungi, grow cluttered to the west, leaving no space for passage. The forest floor is uneven at best with many roots having grown through the tree litter that covers the ground. Among the decomposing trees, button fungi of different kinds thrive.
107227: The forest here is as black as night. Trees are densely packed within this area. The forest floor is completely void of all plant life; small animal tracks can be seen on the soft, moist ground. The trees in this area are twisted together in a manner that makes a disorienting view. The black trees look the same all around, making it even more difficult to find a way through. In all directions an entangled mass of branches and roots is visible, and seemingly prevents going anywhere save to the east.
107228: An ancient fungus smothers the boulders.

The forest remains dark, and the ground lacks any form of life outside of the annelids and insects which swarm over most of the forest floor. The stench of wet dirt and decaying leaves is heavily present in the air. Above the forest floor giant trees block out the sun, while large vines and roots protrude from it, making passage through this dark terrain very dangerous.
107229: An ancient fungus smothers the boulders.

Several big, thick trees stand close to each other. Their rough, hardened grey bark seems old and makes the trees look almost invulnerable. Leaves and twigs lie scattered on the ground. The trees have thick branches just a few feet above the forest floor making the travelling hard. A large nest can be seen far up in one of the trees and the branches around it is so dense the sky cannot be seen.
107230: The branches overhead make this area very dark. Strands of moss hang from above, nearly touching the ground. To the south, two especially large trees stand next to each other, their branches crossing each other regularly and forming a natural ladder. The ground is covered in a thick black mud, which smells of herbs.
107231: Red-barked trees dominate the forest in all directions except west. A purple lichen grows on the south-facing trunks. The air has a acrid, salty smell to it. The ground is quite dry here, with dry brown underbrush and loose leaves that stir in the wind. An occasional faint humming noise comes from the southeast corner.
107232:
A three-foot-long queen bee is here, buzzing agitatedly.
A drone bee flies around here, angrily buzzing.
A drone bee flies around here, angrily buzzing.
A drone bee flies around here, angrily buzzing.

This is a small chamber, covered with a waxy substance on the walls in a hexagonal pattern. A large buzzing noise seems to come from everywhere at once. The floor is sticky and slopes towards the north. Something sticky drips from the ceiling. Sunlight reaching the room makes it glow a dull amber colour.
107233:
A black raven flies in the sky searching for flesh to prey upon.
A black raven flies in the sky searching for flesh to prey upon.
A black raven flies in the sky searching for flesh to prey upon.

Up here in towards the top edge of the canopy, some new leaves grow upon the black twisted branches. Three large branches come together here, forming a natural platform that seems fairly safe to stand on. On the the black and brown bark you can see insects crawling. A rare sight opens up above, at places one can see the sky between the uppermost branches. The air up here is fresh.
107235: A rock lizard is here, motionless as it observes you.

A dark misty woodland continues uninterupted in all directions. Tall slender trees of various kinds stand side by side, their trunks forming a continuous wall of dark wood, their crowns creating an intact canopy above. Black oaks with twisted, old branches seem to grasp at anything passing through here while dead, dried-out birch trees stand still with their old branches looking like pointing fingers. Leaves of different sizes and colours cover the ground and make a crunching sound when walked upon.
107236:
The remains of a black fungus lie here in a heap of rotting compost.
A huge black fungus is here, exuding a foul stench.

Inside the hollow, rotten trunk of this giant, fallen tree the wood has become spongy and wet. The trunk forms an unusual passageway where a multitude of mosses and fungi grows on the bottom, and worms and centipedes squirm in the decaying wood. The trunk has partially collapsed in places, leaving small cracks and holes in the ceiling and sides.
107237: The corpse of a dark wisent is lying here.

Small animal trails wind their way through the forest. The trails are narrow and light, and disappear here and there. Prints in the shape of boots are visible as well, hinting that these trails are used by more than the occasional forest animal. The footprints continue deeper into the forest to the north. While the forest to the south is too dense for travel, a small hole can be seen in this direction. It appears to be the exit from a massive fallen tree which is barely noticeable due to the dark forest landscape. To the west the passage is wide enough to be able to squeeze through.
107238: The small hill is covered with grass in various colours such as green, red brown and almost grey. Thick branches and underbrush obscure the way to the north, and a dank smell and dampness seem to flow out of the forest from that direction. To the east, at the very edge of the forest stands an especially large tree, rotten pieces of bark sitting at its trunk.
107251: A large, black butterfly is fluttering about erratically.

The only traversable routes through this dense part of Mirkwood are to the south and west. The ground is slightly spongy, and a humid and chilly air flows in from the north. Many of the thick vines hanging from the oak trees, that would normally obstruct movement, have been cut off.
107252: The corpse of a dark wisent is lying here.

The feet of many small woodland animals have left their prints on this piece of land. The trail weaves in and out of the dark trees, but appears to head north. To the east, Mirkwood shows its true structure. Masses of thick vegetation block any chance of travel there.
107253: It is hard to be sure, not only because of the thickness of the forest, but also because of the rapid growth of all the small plants and fungi on the forest floor; yet it would appear that some kind of a trail leads east, toward the more dense regions of Mirkwood.
107254:
A brawny wisent is slowly striding through the vegetation.
A young wisent is here, staying close to rest of the herd.

Single footprints are visible here and there, converging onto a small path, and continuing deeper into the dark woods to the north. Occasional sounds can be heard from the forest gloom beyond the trees. Dense bushes make travel to the south and west impossible. Pieces of bark and old dried twigs covers most of the forest floor.
107255: A squirrel scampers around here, looking for nuts from the trees.

An old overgrown path runs through the area, coming from the south. It ends at a large rock, where twigs and moss cover it, making it impossible to keep following. The rock which was most likely placed here as a small navigational landmark has a roughly triangular shape, and the sharpest corner points to the west. In that direction the forest appears to open up a little bit.
107256:
A crude-looking bag, smelling of rotting stuff, has been left here.
A sturdy chain mail hauberk is on the ground.
A seasoned orkish scout is keeping an eye out for any intruders.

This is the site of a small fortified outpost. Logs, branches and vines were used to build obstructions and simple fortified walls among the trees. The crude construction style suggests that this camp was built and inhabited by orcs. Some scattered equipment lying on the ground look like they were dropped in a hurry. Several strange marks cover the camp ground. Partly between the vines and one of the walls is a big strong spider web, recently built; a couple of big raven feathers are stuck in the web.
107257: The trees of the forest are now far more dominant. Massive firs and oaks grow in abundance here, their crowns allowing no sunlight through to the ground. The lack of sun has made the vegetation of the forest floor minimal, which makes identifying and following the narrow path easy. To the north a wall of trees prevents any travel in this direction.
107258: The forest has given way to a vast bog. The ground is completely saturated with water, making travelling very tiresome and extremely dangerous. The air is full of sounds, as though to compensate for the void left by the sudden absence of living trees: Only dead, tall trees tower up like pillars from the otherwise quite clear marsh. The sounds join into a deceptively soothing melody, so powerful that only the most focused traveller can resist its power and avoid being luring into the marshy depths.
