A strange white skull lies on the floor looking at you.

The dark earth tunnel opens up into a natural, underground stone cave. Bones bearing teeth marks, and even whole skeletons, lie higgledy-piggedly in a huge pile just below a narrow hole in one wall of the cave. The hole gives onto another, smaller cave which floor is higher than that of the main cave, so that it forms a sort of raised platform which has been covered with brittle twigs and leaves. The hard stone floor is stained with large patches of dried-up blood, combined with traces of tails, legs and decaying skulls.
108245: Deep inside the tunnels, the air is noticeably cooler and the smell of offal has grown stronger. As one goes deeper, the roof becomes higher and the floor slopes very deeply down into the depths beyond. Faint grunting noises echo all around as well as sounds of crunching and snarling, that seem to mainly come from the east.
108246: The tunnel continues for maybe thirty yards, roughly in a north-south direction. There is some kind of junction to the north and to the south the way ends abruptly in a solid wall of stone. The walls, floor and ceiling are dark, cold stone.
108247: Out of the other caves' darkness springs forth an unusual sight: a large cavern full of crystalline formations and projections. A dim green-tinted glow can be detected deep inside the floor and walls giving this space faint illumination. Crystal stalactites and stalagmites jut from the ceiling and floor while quartz shards litter the ground.
108248: A powerful young troll stares at you.

The tunnel circles around a large crystal boulder which is more than two yards wide and at least three feet tall. Its surface is perfectly smooth as if melted by dragon's fire or some other immense heat. The boulder is glowing faintly, lighting the room with reflections of red, purple and green. A few giant stalactites are hanging from the ceiling, while sharp stones which look like gems stick out from the floor.
108249: An elder mountain troll, wearing a coil of rope on his belt, is here.

Jet-black gravel and occasional bones cover the floor of this dark tunnel. To the west there is a hole in the ceiling revealing a steep tube from above, and next to it is another passage which slopes gently upwards and northwards where the tunnel seems to expand into a more open cavern. A confusing network of smaller passages lead towards the north-east and east. There is a black hole in the tunnel floor, leading downwards into the darkness.
108250: At the Foot of the Scarp

Standing at the foot of the escarpment face your passage north is blocked by a really thick stand of trees and heavy undergrowth. The way west looks like it is barred by the chalk face, leaving only east and south as routes away from here. At least there is a modicum of shelter here...
108251: Standing on the edge of the scarp face you can see the downs rolling east towards the White Hills and further on to the Shire. The gentle dip and climb speckled by odd pools dotted here and there occasionally reflecting the light. The view west is of a gentle downslope unfolding into plains as bleak as the Far Downs and thence to the Emyn Beraid a few leagues further. Unless you can fly it looks like any easterly travel will be out of the question due to the sheer drop.
108258:
The corpse of a tiny spider is lying here.
An ancient fungus smothers the boulders.

A small opening is there in the roof which may keep the room lit during the day. A tunnel leads north under the grassy plains. Out of the tunnel, a small stream of water is coming. The stream leads up a little before vanishing in the ground. The tunnel's ground level appears to be about the same depth as the water level in this area.
108259:
The corpse of a tall stag is lying here.
A brown pond between old branches and roots is here.

It is in this spot that animals from all over the plains congregate, seeking to quench their thirst. The water-hole is a large brown pond, fed by an under- water supply. No fish swim here and the land surrounding the hole is sandy and covered with tracks.
108289: Yellow flowers, with grey-green foliage, grow in clusters here.

A small path continues westwards, passing by wooden structures that lie both to the north and south. The path consists of small rocks and has been virtually cleared of grass. A border of yellow flowers has been planted along the path, giving it a well groomed appearance. Further east the path seems to merge with a more frequented road.
108290: A Path between an Orchard and a Wet Meadow
A bee flies around here, collecting nectar from the flowers.

Beyond a wild orchard and a wild garden a fairly large building stands to the west and south of here, no windows facing towards this side. Beds of flowers and herbs lie close to the building, their blooms attracting a variety of insects. A tiny path continues south along the mostly untamed vegetation and fades towards the north.
108293:
A blooming water-lily floats on the surface of the water.
A green frog is here, hopping around.

This meadow is swampy: water-liking vegetation of all kinds has been growing nearly without restriction. The ground is more murky and muddy than actual water: old, decaying vegetation can be seen and smelled everywhere.
108297: A small rat runs about, oblivious to your presence.

This resembles more a beach than a field, but occasional hardy plants have grown strong enough roots to withstand the beating winds from the west. The rear of a wooden building stands directly east, but there are no entrances visible from here. The soft sand is covered with tracks from a variety of small creatures that have dragged themselves across the sand.
108298: The sand here nearly reaches the gulf but there still remains a small stretch of beach to the west before the waves engulf the land. A fairly large wooden structure borders the region to the east with a curtain covered window facing towards the open waters. Solid land continues both towards the north and south.
108299: A trained horse (ulo) is standing here, ridden by you.

Fine white sand without the presence of rocks covers the ground. The sand has been blown up into piles to the north and east where solid wooden buildings block off the area. This location may have served a purpose some time ago, but right now it appears to be only a place where mounds of sand collects. A larger sandy area opens up to the west.
108300:
There is a huge, pyramidal beehive here.
An apple tree with bright green leaves grows here.
On the tree's branches are three apples.
A bee flies around here, collecting nectar from the flowers.
A bee flies around here, collecting nectar from the flowers.
A bee flies around here, collecting nectar from the flowers.

This orchard is either not attended to on purpose or has grown wild due to neglect. The trees are mostly old, the grass on the ground grows high and is only broken by occasional spots of larger bushes. Some of the trees are so old and gnarly that they are barely recogniseable as trees and could very well be old bushes.
108301: A Garden of Herbs and Flowers
A sprawling green bush of stinging nettle grows here.

This is a wild garden in which aromatic herbs of all kinds as well as flowers grow in patches. Small paths snake through the grass, which also has been cut back near the patches were the planted vegetation grows. To the south, the garden ends at a houses's wall.
108320:
A stove stands against one wall here.
A rather heavy clay jar stands here.

A window is set on the eastern wall providing view of the courtyard outside. Below the window a rock has been hewed creating a flat work surface. A number of barrels and jars stand by the southern wall apparently containing a variety of preservatives. Small wood chunks are piled by the northern wall next to a black stove.
108323: An Apple-Tree within an Old Ruin

An apple tree with bright green leaves grows here.
On the tree's branches are three apples.

This was once a great elven building, but it has fallen in disuse years ago. Time, rain, and the winds have taken their toll as the roof is collapsed, the decorations on the walls are fading and the walls shelter all kinds of thriving bushes, plants, and flowers from harsh weather.
108324: A raft has been left here.

This small building is quite rickety and the roof contains numerous holes and cracks. Many wooden planks of all sizes and shapes lie scattered on the floor, which itself is covered in splinters and sawdust. In the centre of the room, the beginnings of a small boat seem to be taking form, yet it is not even close to completion.
108325: This has been, decades or even centuries past, a quarry where stones got broken. Even though the soil is sandy, thin bushes have taken over where once people toiled and their roots found grip in even the tiniest crack in a stone. Towards the east the area becomes more moist and the vegetation denser until the view is blocked by a building, which roof is overgrown with vines.
108326:
A seagull is soaring above you.
A seagull is soaring above you.

The bushes' leaves are very dense on the outside, but the inside of these old plants resembles more woody branches than green vegetation. The result is that looking through these bushes is not much obstructed, yet passage through the by years hardened and thickened wood is such much harder.
108327: A humble man stands here, ready to help you with your things.

This modestly furnished cottage is filled with a cosy, tranquil atmosphere. A soothing, dim light cast by a few candles enlightens the room, revealing many obscure and ancient artefacts that the landlord has brought along from his long journeys. In the corner of the room, a fireplace and a comfy armchair are located next to each other, allowing one to sit by the fire and perhaps to read a book about gardening. Deciding by the choice of available books, it looks like Shaodan really knows a thing or two about the legumes.
108329:
A tall, stately, dome-topped tree grows here.
There is an old street-lamp on the border of the street.

You are now in a small square where many nearby residents gather to relax. Directly in the centre of the square is a large Elven statue. There is a small, golden plaque mounted on the base of the statue. A small village lies to the north.
108330: A humble man stands here, ready to help you with your things.

This simple circular room has been built of white stone. Although the stone work looks ancient everything is in good shape. There is a wide firepit in the centre of the room, offering warmth and cooking facilities. The other furniture consists of a small bed, a wooden table, some chairs and cabinets. Two big round windows offer a view to a small square to the north. A tranquil atmosphere prevails in the room.
108331: A humble man stands here, ready to help you with your things.

This white marble house's small and simple appearance belies its surprising elegance, warmth and comfort. The front door is adorned with an exquisite carving of a Mallorn tree, and behind it a large table and several chairs sit in the centre of the main room. Above the fireplace's mantel hangs an ancient sword of Elven make; its blade probably still sharp. Other features include several furs and carpets lining the floor, and a few green tapestries on the walls. Through the windows, a small garden can be seen. Smaller rooms include a modest kitchen and a few guest rooms with soft beds for welcoming friends and visitors.
108332: The Housekeeper looks fed up with her job. She scowls at you unhappily.

A small but comfortable-looking hideout has been skilfully constructed on the top of a tall tree. The walls, roof and door are all made of living branches making the room to blend perfectly into its surroundings. A splendid view opens up from the tree, one can see the roofs and walls of the elven city of Harlond, its famous lighthouse and the Gulf of Lhun itself. The hideout has serene athmosphere, only seagulls and wind are making occasional, faint noises that echo in the air.
108333: The corpse of a rattlesnake is lying here.

A dry and warm cavern, its earthen walls and floor scattered with plenty of nooks and smaller holes. Higher up on the walls, patches of muddy granite shows through the hardened earth. Some roots and twigs cover the eastern flank of this place.
108347: An elven vintner is standing here looking for someone to talk to about wine.

This is the home of the farmers that tend to the fields outside. Many diff- erent tools adorn the toolracks here. Looking around you, you notice that the hut is actually quite large inside, there is room for a winegrape mill and tapping equipment. The farmers who work here must live somewhere else and only come here to work the fields and turn the winebottles. If there is any- one in you might be able to buy a bottle or two at a reasonable price.
108348:
A tiny spider is here, eating a tiny bug.
A tiny spider is here, eating a tiny bug.
A tiny spider is here, eating a tiny bug.
A tiny spider is here, eating a tiny bug.
A tiny spider is here, eating a tiny bug.

You enter the cellar of the hut. This cellar is primarily used to store wine- bottles before they are ready to be sold and to let the wine age and set properly. It is a large room filled with the sweet scent of wine and the stronger scent of alcohol. Racks adorn the wall and bottles lie resting in them. This is the last stage for the wine, before this the wine must mature in large barrels and those are located just underneath the wooden stairs. A large and soft spiderweb covers many of the bottles.
108349:
The corpse of a huge, poisonous spider is lying here.
The corpse of a crazed dwarf is lying here.
The corpse of a huge, poisonous spider is lying here.
A dirty shovel is lying on the ground here.
The shadow of a crazed dwarf is floating here.

Many picks, shovels, and other abandoned mining tools litter the ground. This cave was obviously a mine used by the dwarves in a quest for iron or other precious metals. Unfortunately, the walls of this cave do not appear any more than a reddish hardened clay. The smell coming from the east smells like rotten flesh and would only appeal to an evil soul.
108350:
A grizzly cub is here, snarling loudly.
A grizzly cub is here, snarling loudly.
A huge grizzly bear is here, roaming the wild.
A huge grizzly bear is here, roaming the wild.
A sturdy pack horse is standing here.

The smell of half eaten flesh fills your lungs and makes you choke. The floor is littered with decaying corpses that seem to be deer, elk and the like. You shiver at the thought that whatever lives here may decide to make you its next meal. You do not want to end up as a pile of unrecognizable remains, perhaps you had better leave.
108352: You have reached the southern end of the narrow ridge, flanked by sheer drops on all three sides. The clear water of the River Brandywine is now directly below you on the east. On your west and south, a grassy field meets the foot of the hills.
108356: Thick grass and pretty wild flowers make these meadows an attractive pasture. Above you to the north is one of the steep bluffs that mark the edges of the Hills of Scary. Eastward is a green hill, and beyond it must be the Brandywine.
108367: As you step into this hobbit hole, you are immediately taken back by the warmth and splendour of it. You are particularly impressed by this room because it is immaculate. There is not a cobweb or a speck of dust to be found. This is not at all like the other hobbit holes in the Bridgefields! You have entered the house of Torque the Hobbit. While his neighbours may have abandoned their cosy hobbit holes, Torque continues to live well in this one. A fine red carpet covers the floor and an adequate amount of leather furniture fills the room. A roaring fire catches your eye and fills your body with warmth. The mantle above the fireplace looks like it has several interesting things on it. At a quick glance, you can see jars of tobacco, a few well-used books, and a wooden box. This seems to be a delightful little home for a hobbit.
108368:
A low shrub with bright green, oblong leaves is growing here.
Scattered in and on the shrub, there are three piles of blueberries.
A fallow deer is grazing peacefully here.
A fallow deer is grazing peacefully here.

This place is well within the security of the light forest. There are many paths to follow from here, though some less travelled than others. The main path heading to the east looks like the easiest to traverse.
108500: A humble man stands here, ready to help you with your things.

Battle-scarred shields and war-worn furs hang along the walls in this round chamber. A pair of crossed axes is secured above the doorway, whereas a low, sombre lantern is hanging from the slanted wall. The lantern slightly brightens the room and throws long shadows along the room. There is a thick, worn rug on the floor. The rug shows a barely discernible figure of a brave, scarred warrior in combat, only his slightly crazed look clearly discernible.
108501: The lane bends in a wide curve and thus forms a right angle around a ruin that looks like it was once a magnificant building. The coat-of-arms of the Hyarrs family can be seen here, inlaid into the white pavement. The coloured stones have faded over time. A few massive carts loaded with heavy blocks of stone have been left along the road, they seem to be used to deliver material to build new housing where ruins have been removed.
108502: There is an old street-lamp on the border of the street.

The Arnor Lane passes a small park that houses the ruins of an once palace-like building. All other ruins in this short section of the road were removed and have been replaced with new houses. In one place, the coat-of-arms of the Emeries family, one of the seven major noble houses of the fallen Kingdom of Arthedain, has been inlaid into the roadway. The colourful stones are covered with dirt and are only partly visible. A wild park can be seen towards the south.
108503: Here, Arnor Lane bends in a wide curve forming a right angle around the ruin of an odeon or theatre. Bushes and even a few small trees have taken root in and around that fallen building, while a few smaller new houses have been built near it. The now-shattered coat-of-arms of the Foros family is inlaid in the pavement in the road, right in front of the broken theatre.
108504: A humble man stands here, ready to help you with your things.

A square rug made of soft, brown fur covers a majority of the floor here in the home of Logazor the Dwarf. The room consists of a wooden-framed bed, a small table, and a dresser all carved alike by the same maker it would appear. Along the walls there are several animal trophies displayed from the hunting skills of the home's owner. A shelf near the back of the room has several different hunters knives and other trinkets upon it for show.
108505: A humble man stands here, ready to help you with your things.

Unlike the ruins of once so proud city of Fornost, this surprisingly large and light house is in perfect condition. It has been built from smooth, large stones and gives out a safe and cosy impression. A large fire pit used for cooking and warming dominates the western part of the room. The other furniture consists of a huge, oaken desk, a group of chairs around a table, and a soft-looking sofa. There is a bed under the windows, and some paintings have been hung between them. The most curious thing in this room is a bronze figure of a valiant man, wielding a shining sword and fighting a horrible beast.
108506: A humble man stands here, ready to help you with your things.

This comfortable-looking villa gives a serene and cosy impression. There are a few bedrooms, a living room and a kitchen. All the rooms have large windows, allowing sunlight to enlighten the house round the day. The furniture has been made of light-coloured wood. Flowers and herbs are growing all around the house, adding a sweet, fresh scent to the air. In front of the house there is a well-kept, large patio that opens up towards the Arnor Lane.
108507: A humble man stands here, ready to help you with your things.

This small house has been built entirely from wood. The construction work is of high quality, and the room gives a light and cosy impression. An eloquent picture has been hung on the wall, portraying a young Dunadan woman. The other furniture of the house consist of some cupboards, a table with a set of chairs around it, and of a soft-looking bed in the corner. The floor is covered with a wide, forest-green carpet. There are numerous flower pots on the window sills, and outside one can see a ruined theatre.
108508:
A well-crafted white fountain is here, water pouring forth from it.
A doorwarden stands here ready to obey his master's wishes.

A proud garden spreads out here between the buildings. It is defying the surroundings with its tamed, disciplined flora and serves as an invitation to the low white round tower to the north. A richly adorned white marble fountain makes out the heart and centre of the garden. Broad waves of flowers roll out in growing circles from it, the perfect shape interrupted only by narrow walkways leading to a small adjacent stone building and the entrance to the tower in the north.
108509: A Simple Building at the Garden's Edge

The stone floor has recently been thoroughly broomed and is, despite the bare earth showing in the gaps, clean and tidy. The building, consisting of one big room, has only three walls to allow horses to easily enter from the west. In the middle of the house, a four foot high wooden plank divides the space in two. On the walls of the southern part hang bridles and saddles together with horse shoes and grooming brushes. Next to the plank stands a large water trough that spans almost the whole breadth of the room. Securely fastened to the north wall is a massive workbench, filled with various tools and gardening utensils.
108511: A humble man stands here, ready to help you with your things.

Deeply stained wood panels line the floor, walls, and ceiling of this large hall. There are finely crafted tapestries depicting ancient battles lining the walls. A tinted glass lined cabinet stands against the outer wall. Figurines of unique and exotic creatures, made of various precious metals, line the cabinets' shelves. The figurines stand as a visual testament to foes slain.
108514: There is an old street-lamp on the border of the street.

You are standing on the Market Square, right outside the recently opened post office. In the same building, but west some, you can see the city's council. The 'Crown of Arnor' Inn is south of the square, and between it and you there is a well. In the east you can spot a section of the high city wall.
108515: An elderly herbalist is here, surrounded by a cloud of spice.
Surrounding you are herbs of such variety and diversity that you are in awe. Spices and leaves, teas and beans, they fill each nook and cranny. Behind the counter hangs a sign.
108519: A trim Bounder is here, patrolling the Shire and watching for evil.

The long path to Dwaling makes a final turn to the east, before ending at two low signposts which are apparently meant to mark some sort of entrance to the village. The strong smell of fish is unmistakable even from here, so it is not hard to guess the main trade of Dwaling. A small, well-used path leads north from here.
108540:
A little dog is here.
A hobbit farmer is here, thinking about seeds and vegetables.

From the outside this may look like a place where someone lives, but once inside it is pretty clear this wooden structure is nothing but a temporary shelter for workmen and the like. Tools, most of them related to the breeding and keeping of horses lie neatly ordered on a large nearby bench. To the east a large doorway leads out towards a corral. South of here another exit opens up towards the village of Dwaling.
108542: Here begins the path to Dwaling, coming out of a crossroads to the south. Ruts and tracks crisscross the hard packed dirt, obviously well travelled and seemingly mostly by carts from the renowned fisherhobbits of Dwaling.
108543: Running straight north and south by the hills of Scary, this well worn path is somewhat muddy. The countryside around here is more hilly in the north than in the south where there seems to be a wide flat cultivated plain.
108544: Bearer of many carts laden by the fish of Dwaling, this packed dirt road turns here to the east from the south, following the lay of the land as it traces the contour of the hills of Scary in the east.
108545: This road made of hard earth is the well-travelled path to Dwaling, skirting among the foothills of Scary which rise gently to the east. The road curves north-east from the crossroads, carving through the lovely countryside that lies on either side.
108546: Here the road turns from the south and runs straight eastwards as far as the eye can see, skirting the hills of Scary and heading directly for Dwaling. The ruts and tracks on the road attest to its oft usage, and the hard packed dirt feels comfortable underneath the step.
108547: The path continues its north-south way between the hedges here. The hedge prevents any movement to the east, as well as blocking the view in that direction. The White Downs rise in the west. It does not seem to be any accessible climb up to them anywhere.
108548: A faint path, lined by very high and thorny hedges, goes in a north-south direction. It is not possible to see anything above the high hedges, and they prevent moving in any direction but the path itself. Although a few prints can be made out on the path, it does not seem to have been used much lately. To the north and east of here lie several hobbit dwellings with carefully tended gardens.
108549: A humble man stands here, ready to help you with your things.

This cozy smial has few rooms, comfortable-looking furniture and most importantly; a well-equipped kitchen that comes with a proper pantry. Several small windows enlighten the dwelling and allow a view outside where a lightly- chequered pathway runs through a well-tended garden full of blooming forget- me-nots and other flowers. To the west stands a perfectly round door painted in green.
108550: An open, meadow-like landscape grows mainly brown heather, which have gathered among the rocks covered by pale green moss, and around the roots of the few existing trees. Most of the vegetation that covers the ground is dried grass, although some small plants with glossy, green leaves rise from it. To the west, a boulder-strewn area can be seen, while in other directions the vegetation looks more fertile and is flourishing.
108551:
A black moth flutters around.
A black raven flies in the sky searching for flesh to prey upon.
A black raven flies in the sky searching for flesh to prey upon.
A black raven flies in the sky searching for flesh to prey upon.

Black, gnarled trees grow side by side, populating these forlorn hills and shading the sloping ground with their dense canopy. Silvery spider webs have been spun between the dark branches of the trees, and the uppermost threads disappear into the dark leaves above. A broken crow's nest is lying beneath one of the trees, and a few cracked and rotten eggs lie next to it. Southwards the ground turns to mud.
108552: This dark and murky forest is comprised of blackened oak trees growing on a craggy, underbrush-covered slope that descends westwards into a swampy, foul- smelling bog. Movement is very difficult as the ground is covered with stumps, vines, bushes and other tangled vegetation. A heap of branches, twigs and leaves has been piled against one of the oak trees; it looks like someone prepared a huge bonfire but never lit it.
108555:
An orc slavemaster is here, looking for someone to abuse.
An elven slave is standing here.
An elven slave is standing here.
An elven slave is standing here.

The orcs have created an ingenious machine for crushing rock. A pulley and gear system hooked up to some huge metal teeth crushes rock as it is fed into the machine by slaves. More weary slaves work at turning a turnstile to grind the rock into dust. Judging from some bloody pulp you see mixed in with the dust, the overseers enjoyed testing out their machine.
108560: A narrow tunnel cuts through the cold soil. The walls are partly blackstone mixed with gravel, clay and dirt. Huge roots snake in and out, helping to hold the soil in place. Old bones and shattered rocks line the floor. To the south, the earth has collapsed in a rather abrupt manner, denying any further passage.
108561: A confusing network of tunnels runs through the stone. They twist to and fro, making it hard to see very far ahead. The walls reach in towards each other as they rise, so that the ceilings of these tunnels form natural arches, spoiled only by an occasional ledge high above the ground. Some foot prints are visible on the floor: someone or something has been wandering here not so long ago.
108562: A wide tunnel runs through the stone, making a long bend from the west to the south and then meeting a sturdy door which blocks the passageway. Small rocks and dust litter the floor, giving an impression that this tunnel is not in frequent use, although large footprints that lead through the area indicate that someone, or something, has been here not so long ago. Occasional ledges and small cracks create deep shadows on the rocky walls.
108613: A hefty stone club is on the ground.

Littered with bones, broken armour, scraps of fabric, and other castoffs, this area is obviously used by trolls. In one corner, a pile of pine needles has been thrown in an attempt to make a bed. The remains of former meals are strewn across the dirty, hard-packed floor. A sturdy, crude door is located the the east.
108614: A large bat is here, hanging in the darkness.

The passageway transforms into a long, twisting slope rising towards the west and descending to the east. There is a number of high, crude stepping stones on the path, every single one of them being more than two feet tall, and several yards long. At the top of the slope there is a crude but sturdy-looking door to the north. The visibility is rather limited due to angular steps and numerous bends on the path. The ceiling of the tunnel looms somewhere above, mostly hidden in the dark.
108615:
A large bat is here, hanging in the darkness.
A fierce bat is here, lusting for your blood.
A fierce bat is here, lusting for your blood.

Large, jagged boulders and smaller rocks border this snaking passageway which runs in an west-east direction through the rock. The way is rather wide and rises upward to the west. On both sides of the passage, the walls rise steeply upward, like in a steep ravine. The rocky ceiling is far above, with some grey stalactites hanging from it.
108616:
A large cave troll is here, staying close to his mother.
A large cave troll is here, staying close to his mother.
The ugly troll mother is roaming the cave, taking care of her loved ones.
A fierce bat is here, lusting for your blood.

This round, rocky cavern is located inside the stone. Its floor is approximately ten feet wide, the walls are formed of grey stone, while the ceiling looms somewhere above in the dark. Some smooth rocks have been placed in a circle giving the impression that they have been used as benches. There is an exit out to the east, with a large boulder used as the door. A crude bar mechanism has been bolted to the boulder making it possible to operate it. At the opposite end of the cavern a passageway leads deeper inside the hill.
108617:
A half-rotten corpse is hanging here.
A wood elf, fair and noble, stands here.
A large cave troll is here, staying close to his mother.

The prison cell is a damp and dark room. It has been dug into the dark rock, offering no exit out save to west where is a sturdy-looking stone door. There are rusty shackles on the walls, some of them still containing remains of unlucky prisoners. The floor is littered with bones, some of them apparently gnawed with large, strong jaws.
108656:
The corpse of a forest spider is lying here.
The corpse of a huge, poisonous spider is lying here.
A red-spotted spider is here, fighting YOU .

The thick, evergreen undergrowth forms darker, tangled shapes in the deep gloom. Trees rise like twisted, oddly formed pillars from among the dense undergrowth. The shadows cast by the gnarled trunks, a deeper black in a world of shadows, seem to quiver and shake with barely restrained malice. Shadows of thick branches reach out across the ground, shadows that do not always correspond to any real branches above. Across it all layers of sticky, grey spider webs have been spun. In some webs the small dark shapes of Mirkwood moths and butterflies can be seen.
108657: A great, dark wolf stands here, sniffing the air.

This part of the forest is big and green and luscious, its air deep and misty and filled with noises. The mist so thick it leaves a wet surface to anything or anyone that would move through here. The unmistakable smell of composting leaves fills the air. To the south a rock covered in moss blocks the way. An old, almost fully overgrown path comes from the west and leads north, towards an old trunk.
108658: A menacing looking tree is here, just waiting for a lost wanderer.

The roughly circular clearning is surrounded by twisted, ancient trees among which deep shadows seem to loom and move. Many of the trees are cracked and broken, stains that look like dried blood can be seen on their old trunks and sharp branches.. The floor is littered with debris and sharp wood, there also are remnants of small animals but also those of humanoid origin. Perhaps it was an orc or an elf; now nothing more remains of them than their bones littering the floor.
108677: Foul webs span across Mirkwood, engulfing the exit south with their complex patterns.

The dense and continuous canopy of the forest, the result of hanging vines, thick branches and giant-sized black leaves, spreads in all directions engulfing the area in darkness. The undergrowth is dense with patches of ivy and shrubs growing all over. Some rocks and stones lie scattered on the ground, mostly covered in dark moss and lichens. An oppressing silence pervades this place.
108678: A porcupine is waddling around here, its tail full of sharp quills.

Grand oaks and beech create a shadowy forest, rising from a brittle, dry ground. The great roots and vines have sucked the life out of the earthy forest floor. A great bird's nest has fallen to the ground, broken up by pests and putrid fungi. The dense vegetation, combined with the presence of death, bury Mirkwood in a sombre darkness. The dark forest lies explorable to the south, west and east.
108679: The surrounding forest stands tall. The fir, beech and oak grow close together, and their heavy branches and wide crowns engulf Mirkwood in darkness. An old bear's den has been dug out below the giant roots of an oak, exposing several cub skeletons. A heavy stench of decay encompasses the area, reinforced by the moist air. The forest floor slowly rises upwards to the south, leading into heavily forested hills, while in the north and west the tree trunks and undergrowth are completely engulfed in darkness.
108733:
corpse (here) :
a gold coin
a pair of rigid leather boots (flawless)
A half-decayed corpse of a goblin lies rotting on the ground.

Under and between the black roots, a narrow tunnel snakes its way in the darkness. The surrounding roots are thick and gnarled, seemingly penetrating deeper and deeper to the ground to suck any life force there still may be. The black soil around the roots is humid and rather cold. The tunnel ends to a dead end to the west, and leads forward to the east.
108738: A clear spring babbles as cool water trickles out of the ground.

Underneath the leaves, in the thickest shrubbery, runs a narrow but straight and otherwise decent thoroughfare. In the heart of the thicket, the path widens and forms a small clearing growing soft, bright green grass. This place is well covered from the external world and could be used as a place to take a rest, or as a secret hideout. The path continues to south, whereas the entrance here has been hidden among the bushes.
108814: A porcupine is waddling around here, its tail full of sharp quills.

Close to the edge of the forest, a couple of small hills rise towards the sky. Healthy green in colour, the grass of these hills thrives as the gloomy shadow of the forest does not reach here. Some low bushes and small patches of ferns stand out in the vegetation.
108815: The high, dense trees prevent effectively with their thick bole and concealing crowns any sunlight to reach the ground, making any form of undergrowth life impossible. Moist soil covers the ground, fallen branches and twigs are lying here, slowly disintegrating.
108816:
A grey wolf is here, salivating profusely.
A grey wolf is here, thin from starvation.

Completely surrounded by high beeches and oaks, one might lose all perspective and orientation here. The rough ground with its thorny bushes makes it difficult to traverse the area. A lot of tree roots stick up from the ground, further hindering advancement into the forest.
108817:
The corpse of a brutish forest troll is lying here.
The shadow of a brutish forest troll is floating here.

With white and green lichens growing on the towering, ancient trees and green, fluffy moss covering the ground, this forest seems to have been left undisturbed and preserved for a very long time. Vines are climbing the trees, not minding the years rolling by as they reach for the treetops.
108824: Bordering the great forest, these hills bear surprisingly little vegetation in the form of trees. The ground is covered with small patches of grass and a few bushes. Other than that, the land is rocky, covered with dust and the occasional monolithic boulder.
108827: The trees here grow extremely close and impressively high, blocking even a single sunbeam from reaching the ground with their crowns and thick trunks. A few rotten tree trunks lie scattered around here, slowly decomposing and emitting a foul stench.
108828: Tall, thick oak and birch stretch ever skyward, outdoing each other to gobble any available light to ensure their growth. At ground level, a deep gloom settles like a thick blanket, making vision difficult at best. Small rodents and forest creatures scurry into hiding with each noise.
108829: A large, black butterfly is fluttering about erratically.

Under the intact canopy of the ancient, malicious trees, the ground is covered with spiny bushes and thorny shrubs, making sure any traveller will have a tough time passing through. Ominous roots, covered with dead leaves, penetrate the soil, further complicating advancement. Northwards, a rise in height can be noticed.
108830:
The shadow of a brutish forest troll is floating here.
A large, black butterfly is fluttering about erratically.
A large, black butterfly is fluttering about erratically.

Sloping down from the tall hills to the north, this gentle incline is covered in vegetation. Thick beech and birch jostle with each other for the light while massive oak and maple ponder the passage of time. The ground level is relatively free from forest litter, only some vines are hanging from the canopy.
108831:
An ancient fungus smothers the boulders.
An ancient fungus smothers the boulders.

Dense groves and tightly-packed stands of oak of Mirkwood are blocking out the light and hindering the passage. Debris from the trees litter the ground, decomposing in putrefaction. Several trees have collapsed, fungus covering their broken, rotting, corpse-like trunks.
108832: Mirkwood forest has spread up these hills, and the trees shade the ground heavily, making it difficult for the undergrowth to flourish. The soil is moist, but drinkable water can not be found. Moss can be found growing on several trees, as well as on some boulders.
108833: Here, the ridges and hills rise high making the terrain hard to travel. A continuous mass of small bushes with needle-sharp leaves grows on the slopes, surrounding the massive tree trunks and occasional boulders and rock walls. The sloping ground continues to all directions but to the south where the ground seems to be steadily descending down.
108834: Massive, black, oozing vines reach out from the choked canopy.

The continuous canopy of Mirkwood covers the ground, leaving everything into the dark shadows. Underneath the canopy bushes, vines, and trees fight for space in the densely packed sinister forest. Broken limbs and rotting stumps add to the sense of decay and gloom that is ever present in this dank grove.
108835: Overhanging dark branches push down from above like the huge, muscled arms of the powerful trees which seem to be glare at any intruder through huge knots and gnarled bark. The grim trees seem to nod to each other whenever a light breeze cycles through this oppressive grove. Except for the leaves rustling, all is strangely quiet.
108836: A large, black butterfly is fluttering about erratically.

A dark grove of mighty oak trees stand in a tight circle leaving a small open area between their trunks, roots and branches. The trees outside the grove appear to be shorter and not as thick as the black oaks, but still the forest seems very dark and tangled. The dense growth of trees subsides only towards the south where the grove of trees borders the Old Forest Road.
108856: The dark beeches and blasted oaks twist together in a visually confusing mesh, deceiving the senses. Layered with tangles of vines and weeds, the forest seems to be menacing any living creature that is not some form of plant. Thick tree crowns overhead block direct light, making navigation near impossible.
108857: Cliff Overlooking the Old Forest Road

This cliff rises high over the Old Forest Road, thereby providing one with an exceptionally good view. Except for the good view, the cliff has nothing to offer, being bare and devoid of any vegetation. The cliff ends abruptly to the south: there is a steep fall down to the road below.
108858: These hills are totally abandoned by all kinds of plant life. The terrain is very uneven making the travelling hard; steep hillsides are filled with sharp rocks and the edges of occasional gorges look unstable, as if collapsing at any moment. All around, dust and detritus cover the surface of the ground.
108859: A dense patch of dark ferns grows in the shade.

Trees grow tall in this uneven landscape, preventing one from taking advantage of the high ground in order to scout the surrounding area. Lichens have formed on several of the trees, bringing some variation to the landscape. The ground is covered with ferns and low, thorny bushes.
108860: The great forest has spread to the top of this hill, despite the high altitude. The trees here, however, seem to have some trouble to flourish and grow more sparsely than in the adjacent parts of the forest. A steep hillside to the east and unfriendly vegetation to the north and south leaves only one way to get away from the hilltop.
108861: Huge, onyx-black trees stand at the border of the forest, leaving just enough room between the trunks to allow passage to and from the forest. A row of gloomy hills, sloping steeply up at the edge of the forest, are seen all around save in the west.
108895: A small tunnel has been dug out through the dark soil, just below the great roots of Mirkwood. Spider webs span across the spaces between the entangling vines and twigs, trapping small bugs and insects. The tunnel continues quite far to the west, as well as east. The walls have been reinforced by logs and rope, and even rock at some places. Dense roots and ivy grow by the entrance and exit of the dark earth tunnel.
108901: There are obvious traces of a great battle here, with many trees and bushes showing damage. Something which could be a burial mound rises just at the foot of a great oak tree. A perfectly-rounded boulder, overgrown with vines and moss, blocks the way to the north, just below the forest trail. A dreadful stench is slowly pervading this area, creeping in from the south.
108907: The ground is very uneven here and old, decomposed trees are incorporated into the heavy undergrowth. The ancient trees rise tall and dark. It appears difficult to travel further east, up over a small rise, due to the heavily entangled roots and boughs. Parts of the forest here have been heavily ravaged, their trunks gaping with open wounds. Animal trails lead into the heavy undergrowth to the south, while to the west a faint gloom spreads across the forested hills.
108991: An ancient forest road can be vaguely observed to the south, made almost completely invisible by the thick forest. The undergrowth seems somewhat trampled and some trees bear marks from knives, indicating that humanoids have left the road at this place.
109013: The ground slopes heavily here, getting higher to the east. Trees grow sparsely here, though still not sparse enough to provide the undergrowth with sufficient sunlight. Several tree species grow here, beeches and oaks being the most commonly occuring.
109014: Malicious-looking periwinkle reaches downwards from withered oak and ash, intertwining with the foliage and stretching far across the smothering terrain. A dense canopy hangs far up in the air, efficiently preventing most natural light from penetrating. Mouldy vines and roots spread over the forest floor. Fallen beeches serve well as homes for various parasites. The darkness which is Mirkwood may be further explored to the east and south.
109015: The forest rises into a ridge, overlooking the surrounding area. An old forest trail lies far below, to the north. The oak and beech lean their gnarled branches against one another, while supporting each other and forming a solid canopy of leaves, keeping the surroundings dark and dreary. The carcass of a great horse lies, rotten and pest-infested, close to the northern ridge. Mirkwood is rather easily accessible to the west, while travelling north looks both cumbersome and dangerous.
109056: Some small rocks have been piled into a mound here.

The walls and ceiling are made out of pitch black soil, tightly packed between the roots of the great trees outside. Puddles lie scattered over the muddy floor, nourishing the malicious poison ivy. Loose rocks and forest debris occupy the south of the cavern, while to the north a passageway opens up behind falling roots and vines.
109081: In this slight hollow of the ground, the grass seems to have gathered even more densely than in the plains nearby. The stems sprout high and strong, up to several feet, and their edges, straight and sharp, cut like knives. Be it due to the abundant rain, the damp, or the water in the soil, the grass is always wet, almost soaked. But nothing attracts your attention as much as its green colour, deep and pure, and especially under the sunlight, when it shines so intensely that it overwhelms your eyes, remaining so even after you close them.
109082: The steep ravine's walls are full of needle-sharp rocks. There are also big boulders, small stones, medium-sized rocks and the common feature for them is that they are all rock-hard and sharp. Some dry grass tufts and occasional bleached bones have stuck to the wall. When your body lands on the hard ravine wall still high above the ground, you barely have time to think that this was it...
109099:
A skull is here, spiked to the end of a pole.
A bear is here, covered with coarse black fur.

The trees in this area are different than any other trees in the nearby surroundings. They are a mixture of oaks and firs, reaching far into the sky. The bark of these trees is an ashen grey, with lichens populating the outer surface of the trunk. The trees have twisted together in a manner which has created a massive forest wall, which is practically impenetrable. The branches of the trees twist overhead, making impossible the climbing of this wall. The ground here is warm and moist, as the evil forest protects its roots from the sun. A small glimpse of light can seen penetrating the southern wall of forest.
109100: Here the dark woods have been forced to loosen their grip on the environment, causing an almost serene glade to open in the midst of the more malevolent forest surrounding it. The high grass and the absence of gnarled roots to trip unwary travellers makes this area far easier to pass through than the forest around it. The glade continues to the west while the forest takes over to the north and south, though in the south the forest isn't quite as dense.
109115: A deep, bottomless-looking crevice opens up in the ground. It almost surrounds this brush-filled ledge, leaving level ground only to the south. On the opposite side of the crevice the trees are growing tall, dark and extremely twisted; it looks almost as if they are trying to strangle each other. To the east, the land on the other side of the crevice descends lower and a huge stock reaches out across the chasm. The trunk is hollow, and it looks possible that one could walk inside it, across the abyss to the other side, although the trunk does not seem to be very firmly attached to where it lies now.
109118: Inside the dark, fallen trunk the air is moist, and the surface of the hollowed-out tree seems wet to the touch. There are numerous track-like markings all over the walls, clear and visible paths of different bugs who once thrived here. The floor has been worn down from thousands of steps over the years and is very smooth to walk upon. A torn-down bird's nest and pieces of eggshells lie on the ground.
109119: The hollow oaken trunk is rather tight here, but seems to expand towards the west. The round walls bear countless scratch marks, as though rough metal armour and various weapons have time and again rubbed against the wood. As well as those, there are the distinctive marks of digging bugs. The bumpy inside of the tree makes a good solid roof, and the closed, narrow space makes every little sound echo several times. A small pool of mud is collecting in a cavity on the floor.
109165: Forest at the Edge of a Meadow

A bright red mushroom is growing here.
Some small rocks have been piled into a mound here.
A forest spider is here crawling around.

Here, on the western side of a great meadow, bright green tufts of grass stand out against the brown brush and dead undergrowth surrounding the trees to the north and west. To the south, a road makes its way through the forest. At some places, barely noticeable, very old trails start and end without any obvious purpose, but they all seem to lead from the northwest to the east.
109166: The forest has overcome all surrounding terrain. The sun is unable to penetrate this deep dark world. Evil lurks in these areas in many forms, and the darkness seems to draw its strength from a foreign power. A very old path, invaded by barely younger trees, wanders between the trunks, leading to a less dense forest to the west, and into the deeps of Mirkwood to the east; brambles and fallen trees prevent move to the south and north.
109173: This part of the forest smells strongly of rotting vegetation. Branches have fallen all about here, their twisted branchlets snapping underfoot as you walk. Bones and various debris lie scattered on the forest floor. The bones have obvious traces of charcoal, indicating that someone has tried to burn them. The trees grow together very tightly in all directions but west.
109181: At the Top of a Muddy Slope
Some dark, thick writhing vines whip all around you.

Thousands of thick boughs covered in a multitude of black leaves stretch out above, shrouding the forest in an unbroken gloom. Under this oppressive, intact canopy the ground itself is soft, moist and covered with surprisingly abundant plant life. The earth falls away towards the south and there is a steep, muddy slope there.
109182: Massive, black, oozing vines reach out from the choked canopy.

Much of the undergrowth in this area grows in perpetual gloom, yet even so dark silhouettes of thorny bushes can be seen in every direction. The boles of the old, gnarled trees standing here are overgrown with large, ensnaring vines and clusters of dark fungi. The ground is descending heavily downwards to the south, and transforms into a wet and marsh-like, shallow valley.
109190: A mass of dark green leaves clings to a wall.

Rough, sharp gravel covers the ground in this round opening between and below the cliffs, making it difficult to stand or walk on. The gravel varies in colour, from light red to deep grey, creating an odd contrast to the black, looming cliffs. The visibility from down here is poor and all that can be seen are steep rock walls towering up on all sides, save to the west, where lush vegetation covers the rock wall.
109191:
A sprawling, twisted tree grows here.
Some dark, thick writhing vines whip all around you.

The valley is shallow, barely more than a depression in the forest floor. Huge, tangled bushes fill the entire floor of the valley, limiting visibility and the possibility for travel greatly. The ground is wet and soft and covered by wet, black moss wherever there is a reprieve from the dense undergrowth. At the very bottom of the hollow lies a murky, dirty-looking pond.
109192: At the Fringe of a Corrupted Forest

A tremendous black oak looms here.
Black roots shift uneasily all around you.
A tremendous black oak looms here.

Dark gloom shrouds the forest in this dismal corner of Mirkwood. Strange, dark trees possessing forms and shapes no tree should rightfully have loom in the shadows like malevolent beings with evil intent. Strange, dark choking vines snake and twist their way up the queer trunks and thick, knotted roots, oddly pale and flesh-like, poke up through the ground.
109194:
A tremendous black oak looms here.
A tremendous black oak looms here.
Black roots shift uneasily all around you.
Black roots shift uneasily all around you.

The canopy of the dark, malignant forest hangs low. Its black leaves, uncountable twigs and occasional vines create an intact roof over the forest's floor, completely preventing sunlight from reaching this place. Behind every single gnarled trunk there are more trunks to be seen, and more bushes to get scratched from, and more roots to get entangled in.
109195: Some dark, thick writhing vines whip all around you.

Mossy boulders stand so tightly side by side that the way through this area is just a narrow, leaf-covered path between the rocks. Dark oaks stand silently, their crowns disappearing into the darkness above and their roots entangling the rocks. Grey- and blue-coloured spider webs have been woven between the trees.
109196: The remains of a thick tangle of dark vines lie here in a heap of rotting compost.

Various trees grow here: there are oaks, birches and yews, all standing side by side forming a densely-grown forest where movement is rather difficult. Characteristically for Mirkwood the thick, gnarled trunks are dark, much darker than these trees usually are elsewhere on Arda. Vines and branches hang from the canopy. The ground is rather flat except to the east where it rises steeply upwards.
109197:
Black roots shift uneasily all around you.
Black roots shift uneasily all around you.
A tremendous black oak looms here.
A tremendous black oak looms here.

A narrow, passable route snakes through the forest, curving round obstacles, in general running from the north to the east. Trunks and dense, impenetrable brush border the way, blocking any attempts at trespass. Above, the black branches hang low, filled with cobwebs and rotten vines.
109206: Some roots lie here waiting to ensnare weary travellers.

A group of black firs bare of needles stand next to each other, forming a half circle around this small, oppressive glade. The branches stick out like spears; they are strong and sharp, and seem to reach out as if trying to stab careless travellers. Beyond and above the firs, the vegetation intermingles together, blocking both any view of the sky and any movement save to the west.
109236:
The rib-bone of an animated skeleton lies here.
A small, red-spotted spider lurks here.

Bones and corpses wrapped tightly in cocoons of web lie scattered carelessly like rubbish or toys. The webs are thicker here than in the tunnel north, lining utterly everything in a beautifully horrific manner. The surroundings of this rancid dead end are so dense that no sunlight can possibly penetrate through.
109263:
A black moth flutters around.
A black moth flutters around.
A black moth flutters around.

Long, twisted and heavy branches seem to grasp all around for anything to hold, to crush, to suffocate, to kill; to take from the others what the trees do not have but yearn for, to ease their endless torment. In some places bones can be seen half-sunken into the trees: some small, some large, all victims of the trees' malice and hatred against all other living things. Deep, long grooves cover the ground as if something huge and heavy has been moving around here.
109264: The surrounding woods seem wilder and even more twisted than other parts of the forest, giving an impression that something is infusing them with power and purpose, so that the trees are now trying to escape their age-long imprisonment to the earth. Gnarled roots have found their way above the ground, trunks are leaning to the north, and huge, thick boughs are twisting to each other, as if trying to grab support for movement. A distinct and clear smell of rotting plants comes from somewhere close.
109265: The huge, dark, and heavy trees that grow in this oppressive corner of Mirkwood rise higher than most of the other trees, as if being nurtured by something the other trees are denied. The sheer size of the trees opens some space, but to the north and east the forest quickly thickens again and thus prevents passage. The trees look almost as if they were trying to lift up their roots from the ground and walk. A distinct smell of decay wafts in the air.
109266:
A black moth flutters around.
A black moth flutters around.

This part of the forest is warmer and more humid than the rest, leading to much quicker and more noticeable rotting of dead plants, leaves, and branches. The stench of decay hangs heavy in the air. While the decay is clearly visible on the ground, the rest of the forest seems strong and full of life, though dark, and twisted. To the south and east thick walls of densely packed trees allow passage only to insects and other small animals.
109267:
Traces of fierce white tones form the aura of this place.
A small campfire burns here, its low flames giving off only a little light.
Frychra is here, fighting YOU .

Thick, large, white web covers the ceiling where three different mummified bodies have been spun up within the web. Like the underside of a hammock, the large webs hang from the roof, camouflaging the exact shape and size of the chamber. The extensive floor is of clean, flat rock. The northern part is roughly a foot higher than the south and as such forms some sort of plateau.
109268:
The corpse of *a Dwarf* is lying here.
A bulky cocoon hangs from the ceiling.
A strange white skull lies on the floor looking at you.

This stinking chamber is filled with multiple hazy walls of sticky spider webs, limiting the visibility and making it difficult to move without getting stuck. Some cocoons are hanging from silky threads, occasionally swinging a little bit among and above the webs. Parts of dismembered corpses, empty husks of deceased, and clusters of huge spider eggs have sunk into the grey slime that covers all the surfaces.
109269:
The corpse of *a Hobbit* is lying here.
The rib-bone of an animated skeleton lies here.

An abundance of silky webs fill this underground chamber from the floor to the ceiling. Few grotesque cocoons of different sizes hang in the air; some look grey and dry while others look stickier and their colours contain splashes of green and brown as well. Zig-zagging among and between sticky webs, it is hard to tell which way leads where.
109271:
The remains of a thick tangle of vines lie here in a heap of rotting compost.
A clear spring babbles as cool water trickles out of the ground.
This secluded clearing contains knee-high dry grass. In all directions forest can be seen. To the north the trees grow most densely, making travel impossible in that direction.
109273:
A huge, poisonous tarantula extends her legs to you.
A huge, poisonous tarantula extends her legs to you.

Fuzzy green moss grows up the northern facing tree trunks, favouring only that side of the trees. The deep forest gloom seems to grow darker and more dismal in every direction. South the trees grow substantially denser preventing any movement in that direction. Small shafts of light dapple down through the treetops, imprinting faint patterns in the blackness of the forest floor.
109275: As you walk underneath the mountain, nagging worries prey upon your mind, and you wonder if perhaps you should reconsider your exploration. A disgusting crunching sound emanates from the end of the corridor, and your blood runs cold as you realise it is the sound of bones being chewed.
109276: As you walk underneath the mountain, you begin to wonder whether or not this is such a good idea. The east wall is covered with a sheet of bones, and your fear is doubled when you hear a loud growling from the end of the tunnel, which grates your ears and gives you shivers.
109279: A huge stone giant is here, glaring at you (red aura).

You have stumbled onto some sort of secret cave lair. Bits of stone, bones, and destroyed equipment litter the floor. A foul stench burns your nose and begin to think this was not a good idea. The occupants seem to think the same thing, and you prepare to defend yourself.
109283: As you have grown accustomed to, in these dull mountains, everything seems bland. Everything, that is, except for the high peak just north of you. Although you cannot seem to go either east nor west, you can follow the mountains both north and south. In addition, you can climb a slope up to a mountain top.
109284: The entrance to the tunnel is cramped and damp. The walls and ceiling are of hard-packed soil and rocks. Wooden poles maintain the structure of the tunnel. Traces of cobweb and nesting spiders can be seen among rocks and other debris. The tunnel twists and turns northwards.
109285:
skeleton (here) :
a leather backpack
a plain scarf (flawless)
a large skin

A rusty pickaxe with a broken handle lies discarded here.
A skeleton of some humanoid lies in the dust.

The tunnel is in a deteriorated state. Wooden poles lie scattered across the floor. Some of the beams in the ceiling have started to split open. The turning tunnel leads to the west and south, the dark, packed soil to the south giving way to stone in the west. The air in the cavern is humid and lukewarm, and there is a a smell of death and decay. Small humanoid bones lie spread out among fallen rocks and boulders.
109287:
Needs weight to open exit d
Fall damage
A large boulder is here, it must be heavy.

The tunnel is in complete disorder here. It slopes downwards to the east, big rocks and wooden bars covering most of the floor and leaving quite a difficult route to travel. The tunnel comes to an end at a collapsed shaft. A vast cobweb spans the ceiling, filled with moths and other small bugs. Among the debris one can discern skulls, ribs and other bones, many gnawed upon.
109288:
The corpse of a giant slug is lying here.
The remains of a giant green fungus lie here in a heap of rotting compost.
A large boulder is here, it must be heavy.
The corpse of a pack horse is lying here.
A half-decayed corpse of a goblin lies rotting on the ground.
Some small rocks have been piled into a mound here.

There are three obvious exits at this nexus of tunnels: one leading to the west, another descending down towards the north, and a dangerous-looking old shaft leading upwards. Great spider webs span across the ceiling, along parts of the walls, from stalagmite to stalagmite and from stalactite to stalactite. Decomposing cocoons hang from the webs. Seemingly fresh traces of blood and a drained, yet not rotten, body are clear evidence of recent activity. A sour smell engulfs the entire area, irritating skin and eyes. The humid, lukewarm air makes a good habitat for the fungi which have started to take over the cave.
109290: A seemingly small underground spring creates a pitch-black pool at the furthest side of the cave. A rancid smell stems from the water. There are remnants of smaller animals floating about in the pool. Great stalactites hang from the ceiling. Webs and cocoons span across the cavern in the south, the cave system continuing beyond them.
109291: The remains of a giant green fungus lie here in a heap of rotting compost.

Stalagmites and stalacites encompass the whole cavern. A narrow crack in the ground between tall stalagmites emits a stinging stench. Fungi and moss cover parts of the walls and crevices. Webs span between the pointy stalacites in the ceiling, some in better shape than others. The tunnel continues to the east; the only other exit is down through the crack into the putrid water below.
109292:
A grey snake slides along the water.
A grey snake slides along the water.
Something cold and scaly slithers past your leg.

The water is very cold and vision is limited. Something in the water stings the skin and eyes. The cavern walls are marked by many small pit-holes, suitable perhaps for hiding captured prey -- or concealing predators? The walls are bare, with not a trace even of weeds or moss. There is a small crack in the south side of the ceiling, leaving a possible passage of escape.
109310:
A mass of wriggling vines drops on you from the trees.
A mass of wriggling vines drops on you from the trees.

The twisted, gnarled tree trunks standing here are overgrown with clusters of pallid, corpse-grey fungi and thick layers of mould. A heavy stench of decay and death enshrouds the trees and undergrowth like a fog. Tangles of thorny bushes and sticky-looking spider webs make the area hard to pass through and great care is required to not get snagged or caught on needle-sharp spines.
109311: In a Dark Corner of Mirkwood

Impassable walls of entangled bramble and brush surround this area to the west, east and north. Towards the south passage seems possible, yet even in that direction one might get snagged and prickled by thorny bushes, or get stuck in the thick, smelly spider webs that have been stretched between the trunks. Oak, beech and fir grow among the tangle, the treetops forming a dark, green ceiling above that casts the forest into deep shadow.
109313: A short, steep slope leads downwards to the south, deeper into the tangled undergrowth. Here at the top of the slope, the undergrowth is not quite as dense and tangled but thick enough to block passage towards the east and west. Thick, dense branches above block out the sky from sight and the forest is shrouded in shadows and gloom.
109346: Wide expanses of thick, impassable brush encompass the gnarled old trees in this part of Mirkwood forest. The dark, sprawling shapes of vast thickets reach almost high enough to merge with the wide, heavily-leaved treetops that blot out the sky above. The only obvious route out of these tangles lies towards the west, where narrow gaps between thorny bushes might allow those who do not mind being scratched and pricked to squeeze through.
109362: Snaking through the forest a small pathway passes a peculiar-looking group of jet black trees. A thick layer of black lichens covers the whole area, giving the trees and rocks their, even for this forest, unusually dark colour. Densely growing trees are spreading their twisting branches and tangled vines are hanging from the canopy as if trying to prevent any movement away from this oppressive place.
109363: A riotous mass of dense shrubs surrounds the dark trees to the north, seemingly blocking one's way in that direction. To the east a sharp ridge rises, its side covered with the same type of shrubs that grow to the north, making it impossible to get to the top of the ridge from here. A small pathway leads to the south and west through the dusky forest, the part going south looking a lot more used.
109364: Large trees covered in dark mosses, lichens and fungi crowd the area. The vegetation that surrounds the trees grows denser and denser to the south, effectively blocking passage in that direction. There are broken branches and twigs in the shrubs to the north, as well as lightly trampled vegetation, providing evidence that living creatures do travel in that direction on a regular basis.
109365: Well hidden by the thick, downwards-reaching branches and evergreen shrubs, this small rise in the forest serves as an excellent watch post for anyone who wants to watch the road passing by just to the north. The broken twigs, the flattened undergrowth, and the remnants of someone's meals suggest that this place is in regular use. In all directions save to the south the ground slopes downwards, making it highly uncertain if one can get back here after descending.
109415: The old road cuts straight through the forest on its way from the west to the east. While the road is in a state of neglect, it is still possible to travel through Mirkwood via the road, something that does not hold true for the surrounding forest; dark and twisted trees lean on each other, their branches intertwining together, blocking the passageways between most of the trees.
109437:
An orc-guard of the Morgundul is on patrol here.
An orc-guard of the Morgundul is on patrol here.

A narrow path leads into a tunnel of dense, thorny bushes. The opening in the twigs is bordered by thick thorns and branches. Forcing a path through the brush in either direction would quickly prove impossible. Many smaller, broken twigs can be seen on the ground and on the bushes left and right, indicating someone or something walks along this path quite regularly.
109439: A large and old Beorning is standing here, slowly stroking his beard.

You find yourself in a furnished room with only the most necessary facilities. A bed stands close to one of the corners. Next to it is an old bedside table. A table and chair are placed close to the bed beneath a small round window. The house is built of a dark wood that looks very solid. A stone fireplace stands in another corner and beside it lies a heap of bright firewood. A small square on the floor in front of the bed is made of a slightly brighter wood.
109443: This crude but functional flight of stairs has been crafted in the simplest of ways: a series of stone slabs of various shapes and sizes has been arranged to secure footholds along a steeply-angled shaft. The top of the stairs leads to a large opening, while the lower part veers off in an eastwardly direction. In contrast to the turning and sloping nature of the stone steps, an almost horizontal shaft cuts a path southwards through the rock and soil.
109444:
The corpse of a large earth troll is lying here.
The corpse of a large earth troll is lying here.

With nothing supporting this tunnel except the occasional latticework of roots, there is little to suggest that this is the handiwork of skilled craftsmen. The walls are part dirt, part bare rock; the rock seems to have been tunneled through with little care, and bears deep scars from the crude excavation process. A deep and earthy smell hangs heavily in the air, partially masking a faint undertone of something far more acrid.
109445: The corpse of a small bat is lying here.

A crude shaft, the walls bearing scars from a hasty excavation process, allows passage either further into the depths below, or up the slope to the west. The bare stone floor is etched with deep grooves, presumably the result of large and heavy objects being dragged or pushed from one place to another.
109446:
The corpse of an earth troll is lying here.
The corpse of a large earth troll is lying here.

The earthy tunnel walls give way to bare rock to the north and east. No attempts appear to have been made to tunnel through the rock; the tunnel instead bends here, following a path of least resistance through the softer soil. A crevice in the rock to the north extends from the ceiling of the tunnel all the way to the floor, widening and deepening as it descends; at the level of the floor it is large enough to allow access as it continues straight down into the cave system.
109447:
The corpse of a large earth troll is lying here.
The corpse of an earth troll is lying here.

A tunnel of varied width snakes its way further through the soil and bedrock as it continues from south to north. The crude craftsmanship suggested both by the irregular sizing of the tunnel, and the chunks of broken rock and hacked-up roots left in piles along the walls, indicates a hasty excavation. The southern part of the tunnel narrows considerably as it reaches a natural grotto.
109448: A small, natural grotto lies nestled deep within the bedrock and loose soil. The smooth, aged surface of the rock suggests that it is indeed a naturally occurring cavern, and not the result of digging. This impression is underscored by a contrasting, roughly-cut tunnel that has left a gaping hole through the rock and soil to the north. Debris piles have been left at the junction of tunnel and grotto, almost as if someone or something broke through the wall with sheer force.
109449: A slightly-slanted tunnel offers passage through the dark, smooth bedrock. Though the smooth walls of the tunnel suggest a natural origin, someone has made makeshift steps by hacking away at the floor to provide better footholds. There is a large opening leading downwards, wide enough to cater to even the largest of beasts.
109450:
A half-rotten corpse is hanging here.
An infant troll, baring its teeth, snarls here.
An infant troll, baring its teeth, snarls here.
An infant troll, baring its teeth, snarls here.
A nasty troll female crouches here, with a feral look in her eyes.

Debris from a cave-in covers the ground in this partially-obscured passageway. The tunnel tapers off into a seemingly impassable crawlspace to the east while the western direction offers a far more conveniently-sized opening. Partially-eaten remnants of humanoid corpses have been left near the rockfall.
109451:
The corpse of Clunker the clumsy troll is lying here.
The corpse of a cave troll is lying here.
The corpse of a cave troll is lying here.
The corpse of a large earth troll is lying here.

The walls of the tunnel here are jagged: the surrounding bedrock is broken and cracked, leaving deep crevices and protruding edges. The passageway itself is relatively level; the rock underfoot forms a somewhat concave surface as it slopes up to form the surrounding walls. Droplets of water have beaded on the smoother of the surrounding surfaces, and the air is damp and cool.
109452: The western end of this tunnel has caved in, leaving a pile of dirt and broken rocks. The rockfall appears to have originated in a cavern above and broken through into this passageway; two particularly large slabs of stone have wedged, leaning against each other, to form an impromptu archway while keeping the access-way into the cave above clear from debris. As the tunnel continues to the east, away from the rockfall, the surrounding stone becomes smooth, suggesting that this tunnel was formed naturally by water running through the bedrock long ago.
109481: The small fierce-looking bat is hanging from the ceiling, obviously sleeping.

Deep furrows mar floor and walls alike throughout the shaft. Rocks of varying shape and size are scattered along the passageway; some were clearly broken from the deep gouges in the walls, while the comparatively lighter colours of others suggest that they did not originate in this part of the tunnel. A faint, putrid odour hangs in the air.
109482:
Some ugly blow-flies are buzzing around here.
Some ugly blow-flies are buzzing around here.

Strong odours fill this large cavern. The walls, roughly-cut from the surrounding stone, suggest that this cave is not a natural feature. Large piles of refuse, consisting of a mix of debris, faeces, bones and half-rotted pieces of flesh, have been deposited throughout. A smaller cave has been dug in the bedrock to the north, while passageways to the south and east grant access to a nearby network of tunnels.
109483:
A half-rotten corpse is hanging here.
A stone troll is standing here, scowling about.
A small vicious black rat squeaks at you for disturbing it.
Some ugly blow-flies are buzzing around here.

Excavation tools, both broken and functional, have been piled on the floor of this cave. The curious presence of shackles and lengths of chain may indicate that the cave is used as storage for living creatures as well as inanimate objects; nothing, however, is currently chained here. A putrid smell hangs heavy in the air towards the southern end of the cave.
109484: Walls of rock to the east and west press in close here, creating a vertical shaft that drops straight down into the depths of the cave system. The walls appear to be made from great shelves of stone, stacked unevenly upon each other to form tall but shallow steps and recesses; the resulting ledges are too far apart to be used ladder-like when ascending or descending, and are mostly too shallow to be stood upon. One ledge, wider than the rest, is wide enough to allow purchase; it is precarious, however, slick from condensation and the piles of bat guano that cover every horizontal surface.
109485: Some ugly blow-flies are buzzing around here.

Piles of refuse partially obstruct this passage. Those nearest to the centre of the tunnel have been trampled down by passing feet; bones, skins, and faecal matter have been spread from wall to wall, creating a slightly slippery layer that covers the bedrock beneath. Closer to the walls the piles are less disturbed; some are heaped nearly to the ceiling, their contents buried beneath a moving layer of large, iridescent flies. The air here is thick with the odours of putrefaction and faeces.
109486:
The corpse of a large earth troll is lying here.
A huge olog-hai troll is here staring blankly at you.
A large earth troll is digging here, looking for some tasty morsels.

A wide but low space opens up here at the juncture of several tunnels. The rock overhead is pitted, hinting at many aborted attempts to enlarge this cavern; the rubble obstructing the passageways suggests that not all attempts were in vain. Several distinct paths have been cleared through the piles of dirt and broken rock, although several large boulders have not been moved from the centre of the junction, the point at which all paths meet.
109488: Broken rock fills this passage, creating unstable footing and making the ceiling appear low. The cracks in the ceiling, paired with several badly-broken sheets of stone on top of the rubble, suggest that there was a minor collapse here at some point in the past. The original floor of the tunnel has been buried under fallen rock, but enough space remains to allow passage from north to east.
109489: Huge chunks of broken rock fill this part of the tunnel, resulting in a low ceiling and difficult passage. The rubble is stable; most of the rocks are large or tightly-packed enough not to shift underfoot, although in spots narrow crevices extend a significant distance downwards.
