The rubble is piled highest along the walls, reaching almost all the way to the ceiling; it appears that the rubble in the centre of the tunnel has been pushed aside, creating a slightly more level, and spacious, path.
109490:
An old, strong cave troll is standing here.
An old, strong cave troll is standing here.

Broken rocks are piled in the western part of this passageway, reaching nearly to the ceiling and creating difficult obstacles over which to pass. A path has been partially cleared through the centre of the rubble, the rocks pushed to either side; the path extends into the tunnel to the west, which is similarly obstructed. In the eastern part of this passage, however, the rubble has been completely cleared away, revealing a spacious tunnel that slopes downwards.
109491: A large earth troll is digging here, looking for some tasty morsels.

A wide burrow of hard-packed dirt runs from north to south. The walls to the east and west widen considerably before the dirt gives way to solid rock; deep gouges in the rock suggest that attempts were made to expand this tunnel in both directions before being abandoned in favour of easier passage through the soil. The air is cool and damp in this part of the tunnel; it has a strong earthy scent that carries a hint of mould and decay.
109492: A tunnel winds through the hard-packed dirt here, curving from west to north. The walls and the ceiling of the tunnel are furrowed, creating ridges that appear to spiral down the passage. Some of the deeper furrows have exposed an underlying layer of rock; in places this rock has scratches and gouges, presumably left over from the excavation process.
109493: Walls of rock to the east and west press in close, creating a natural fissure that starts here and extends upwards. The bottom of the fissure is covered with gravel and larger rocks that have broken from the walls; some of the gravel is a lighter colour than the surrounding rock, suggesting that it has fallen from much higher up. The western wall is smooth and almost completely vertical, while the eastern wall is staggered, the stone alternately angled inwards to form recesses and outwards to form shallow ledges. One of these recesses gives way to an earthy tunnel that cuts under the rock ledge above; it is wide and tall, and does not appear to have been formed naturally.
109494: The small fierce-looking bat is hanging from the ceiling, obviously sleeping.

The slope in this part of the shaft becomes steep as its descent continues to the south. The rock that forms the floor of the shaft has been dug out crudely, creating a tunnel floor that is neither level nor smooth; passage through the shaft here is made easier by this irregular footing, as the raised chunks of rock and deep gouges serve as footholds on the steep slope. The air is cool and slightly damp, with moisture beading on the furrowed rock walls.
109496:
A huge olog-hai troll is here staring blankly at you.
A huge olog-hai troll is here staring blankly at you.

The solid, coarse-grained granite has been excavated to create a sort of crossroads deep underground. The excavation must have required great effort; the very core of the hard, unforgiving bedrock has given way in the face of brute strength and hard-headed will. White marks are faintly visible on the dark stone surfaces, left over from the scraping of metal against stone. Tunnels diverge in five directions, and the rugged walls quickly fade from sight around corners and down slopes.
109497: A large earth troll is digging here, looking for some tasty morsels.

This tunnel runs horizontally as it cuts through the rock from north to south. The stone underfoot is rough but level, and a layer of dirt has accumulated on the ground near the tunnel walls. A series of small cracks in the walls seems to be the source of the dirt; it is being squeezed through the cracks slowly by the pressure from above, and is piling up along the edges of the tunnel. The resulting smooth transition from walls to ground gives this narrow passage a slightly rounded appearance.
109498: A stone troll is standing here, scowling about.

A tunnel leads here from the west, through the solid grey granite bedrock. The tunnel tapers to nothing; perhaps the effort required to dig through the hard rock became too great, and the attempt was abandoned. The walls are laced with cracks and the gouges from pick axes and other instruments used in the digging; clearly, not even trolls could dig through this rock without tools.
109499:
The corpse of a large earth troll is lying here.
A large earth troll is digging here, looking for some tasty morsels.

Here, the digging activities of the trolls have run into a large, natural cavern. Tunnel openings in the northeast corner of the cave show where the trolls burst through the wall as they were burrowing; large, broken stones are piled near the openings, having been pushed aside but not removed. The ceiling is high, and the cavern floor is littered with huge, craggy boulders of various sizes.
109500: The corpse of a large earth troll is lying here.

The tunnel slopes sharply here, coming from the north and leading upwards; it forms a wide, steep ramp. The surface underfoot is littered with small, sharp chunks of rock that roll and slide underfoot, hindering passage up the slope. Near the top of the ramp these rocks become more numerous and much larger, forming a layer of rubble that shifts when walked upon. The ceiling overhead slopes at less of an angle than the floor, creating a more restricted tunnel near the top of the ramp, and a more spacious one at the bottom.
109501: This oddly-coloured dirt tunnel leads further north, while a spacious cavern opens to the south. The dirt that composes the surrounding walls and ceiling is a deep reddish-brown colour; small trickles of water running down the walls seem to pick up the reddish tones, creating rivulets with the appearance of blood. The air here is cool and still, and a faint metallic smell can be detected beneath the heavy earthy odour that fills the tunnel.
109502: A rock wall curves around here from east to south, forming the northwestern corner of this huge cavern. The ceiling above is cracked, pitted, and uneven; it is possible that some of the many sharp-angled boulders strewn across the floor here have fallen from above. The presence of truncated columns in various places support this possibility; they appear to have been at one time growing stalagmites, but are now broken, smashed by the same huge rocks that now demand circuitous pathways when traversing the cavern.
109503: A large earth troll is digging here, looking for some tasty morsels.

The southern wall in this part of the cavern appears to have caved in at some point in the past; a large rockfall has spread outwards towards the middle of the cave, creating an uneven slope that extends from the ceiling down to the floor. A significant amount of dirt is mixed in with the rubble, and has been spread across the cave floor; many large footprints can be seen in the dirt, forming criss-crossing paths that extend in every direction.
109504: A tiny spider is here, eating a tiny bug.

An enormous cavern opens up here and extends to the north and east. Giant boulders and cracked slabs of stone litter the cave floor; some of these are smooth, but most are badly pitted and eroded. Small spider webs fill the pockmarks in some of the stones, and larger webs are stretched between the crevices created where several rocks have been stacked together. Some of these stacks of stones are irregular and suggestive of rockfall rather than purposeful construction.
109505:
An infant troll, baring its teeth, snarls here.
An infant troll, baring its teeth, snarls here.
An infant troll, baring its teeth, snarls here.
A nasty troll female crouches here, with a feral look in her eyes.

The walls and ceiling of this vault are made up of a of rough white stone, and upon further inspection it appears to be naturally occurring marble. Scattered bones and heaps of filth litter the ground, and the white of the stone walls is in places marred by dark streaks that appear to be smeared faeces. The walls are even and the vault is nearly square in shape, constructed with a regularity that seems at odds with its natural origins. A low opening through the eastern wall is similarly ambiguous; it is unusually regular in shape, yet bears no marks characteristic to purposeful excavation. A wide crack in the northwestern corner of the ceiling appears to lead into some sort of tunnel, but it is too far above to reach.
109506: A powerful young troll stares at you.

Rough white stone forms the south and east walls of this tunnel. Looking closer one can see that it appears to be naturally-occurring marble. The tunnel curves away from these rock faces, turning from west to north as it burrows through softer stone and soil. To the west the marble rock face cuts across the tunnel, and a low, evenly-shaped opening in the stone enters what appears to be a marble cavern.
109507:
A powerful young troll stares at you.
A powerful young troll stares at you.
A powerful young troll stares at you.
A powerful young troll stares at you.

This wide, natural cavern seems to be a dumping spot for rubble and rock. Rock fragments and gravel of various sizes have been piled in the middle of the cavern, while larger boulders have been pushed against the walls. Some of the rock debris appears to have been tamped down to form indistinct pathways. Footing is easier along these paths, as the stones underfoot are less likely to shift and slide. To the south the granite walls give way to a whiter stone.
109509:
An infant troll, baring its teeth, snarls here.
An infant troll, baring its teeth, snarls here.
An infant troll, baring its teeth, snarls here.
A nasty troll female crouches here, with a feral look in her eyes.
A powerful young troll stares at you.

Tall piles of rubble rise from the cave floor. These piles primarily consist of chunks of granite, likely broken loose during the excavation of the nearby tunnels. Between the piles, refuse and bones litter the ground, and the odour of putrefaction hangs heavily in the air. There is a wide, jagged crack in the ceiling above; another cavern is barely discernible above, yet despite the height of the rubble piles, the opening is beyond the reach of even the tallest troll. The wide, rubble-strewn cavern continues to the south and west.
109510:
A powerful young troll stares at you.
A powerful young troll stares at you.

Large piles of broken rocks are heaped against the western and northern walls in this cavern. The rest of the floor of the cavern, while not free from rubble or debris, is at least relatively level. The layer of broken rock underfoot has been packed down, and the rocks shift only slightly when trod upon. A small tunnel cuts through the western cavern wall, between the heaps of rubble. A number of broken bones and patches of stringy, matted hair or fur have been left next to the opening.
109511: A burrow has been dug here through the brown, sandy soil. Underfoot the soil is compacted and dense; it has been worn down to partially expose a dense gravel layer underneath. To the south the soil on the floor of the tunnel gives way entirely to gravel, then larger chunks of rock. Most of the larger rocks have been piled against the walls, narrowing the tunnel and creating a bottleneck.
109512: The dark surface of an underground lake can be seen in the northwestern corner of this cave. When still, the surface of the lake reflects the cavern ceiling above; this image creates the illusion of a basin of great depth, filled with crystal-clear water. A tunnel, excavated through the hard rock, leaves this cavern to the east. Westwards it climbs up a steep, jagged slope. Several large, cracked blocks of rock rest at the foot of the slope; this accumulation of rubble, paired with the relative scarcity of loose rocks on the slope, suggests that the slope has been cleared in a purposeful manner.
109513: The trolls have expended great effort in creating this tunnel; sandy, grey-brown dirt and large blocks of granite have been cut straight through as the tunnel continues its path deep underground. Holes in the walls and floor show where boulders were removed during the digging process; the resulting cavities have been left unfilled, lending an uneven look to the walls and creating hazardous pits in the ground. The crudely-dug tunnel branches here, leading off in three separate directions.
109514: An albino fish is swimming here, looking for some food.

The basin is narrow here, barely twelve feet from wall to wall in the widest part. If it did not continue to the north, this would be little more than a water-filled hole. The walls look black beneath the water, but on closer examination appear to be made from a grey, rough-grained granite. The bottom is uneven, and several loose rocks rest upon it; perhaps they have fallen from above.
109515: An albino fish is swimming here, looking for some food.

The water in this subterranean basin is cloudy with dirt and unidentifiable particles of organic matter. A layer of sediment is visible on the bottom of the basin; when the water is disturbed, the sediment rises to cloud the water and reduce visibility. The rock overhead is grey and dark; it forms a smooth expanse, unbroken by crevices or pockets that could trap air. The basin widens slightly towards the north, and narrows to the south.
109516: An uneven, rugged tunnel has been cut through the hard, grey, granite bedrock. Large chunks of rock protrude from the ground, pebbles litter the slope, and loose rocks lie where their downhill roll was stopped by the aforementioned obstacles. Further down the tunnel, the bottom of the passageway is visible.
109517: This tunnel has been dug through the coarse-grained granite bedrock, and tremendous effort and determination must have been required to tunnel through such dense, hard stone. The cavern continues to the west and east. To the east it slopes down steeply. The rock surface of the slope is covered with furrows and gouges; it looks as if the rocks broken loose during the digging were simply dumped into the tunnel and down the slope.
109518:
The remains of a giant fungus lie here in a heap of rotting compost.
The remains of a black fungus lie here in a heap of rotting compost.

Water has gathered in a natural basin in the southern part of this cavern. The dark waters reveal nothing of the depth of the subterranean lake. The surrounding walls are wet with condensation; growths of fungi and moss thrive here. The cavern may have been isolated once, but the eastern wall has been dug through and a low passage leads into a tunnel.
109519: This deep, narrow passage has filled with water. A sediment layer is visible on the bottom of the basin, and is stirred up when the water is disturbed. The walls and bottom are of solid rock, and the sharp edges of protruding stones clearly show that this is a body of still water, because flowing water would have smoothed the edges over time. The pool is not deep here, and the reflections from the surface above are clearly visible.
109527: An old, strong cave troll is standing here.

A solid path has been created on the soft earthen floor of the tunnel by the continuous trampling of heavy troll feet. The tunnel walls consist mostly of dry, crumbling dirt and small stones; a few large, gaping holes show where larger boulders have been forcefully excavated and carried away. The rich smell of soil has been muted by the odours of decay and faecal matter; rot and faeces have been tracked into this part of the tunnel by the trolls and trampled into the dirt underfoot.
109528: A crude tunnel has been dug through the soil here. The walls are uneven and appear unsteady; no bracing has been put in place to support them. A huge black boulder to the west seems to have blocked the digging in that direction, and the tunnel instead burrows down underneath it.
109529: A wide tunnel with a rough, uneven wall has been dug out of the loose, earthy soil. Rocks and rubble have been left along the walls, as if the work to create this tunnel was hastily abandoned. Several large boulders have been left by the southern wall, serving as a crude set of stairs as the tunnel ascends steeply.
109530:
A large cave troll is here, staying close to his mother.
A large cave troll is here, staying close to his mother.
A large cave troll is here, staying close to his mother.
The ugly troll mother is roaming the cave, taking care of her loved ones.

A wide, low grotto has been dug out of the bedrock. The walls are a mix of brown earth and grey stone, and large holes open where boulders have been removed. The floor of the cave has been stomped flat and smooth; no rocks are visible in the dirt underfoot. Crude sleeping piles of straw and fur line one wall, while several bones and other unidentifiable mounds of waste lie in the opposite corner.
109532: The passageway here, a tunnel through bedrock of coarse grey granite, has collapsed with devastating results. The floor disappears into a jagged hole with the bottom barely visible below. On the far side of the hole the continuing tunnel is forever sealed by enormous masses of fallen rubble. The tunnel continues to the east: following it in that direction may be safer than attempting to climb down into the hole.
109534:
A large earth troll is digging here, looking for some tasty morsels.
A small, mean earth troll is standing here, thinking of something hideous.

This tunnel has been dug out of the surrounding rich, reddish-brown soil. The soil is loose, and crumbles away from the walls and ceiling easily; various furrows and pits in the surrounding surfaces are evidence of either natural erosion or purposeful digging. The air here is cool and damp, with the occasional draft coming from the east.
109535: This soft-walled tunnel, comprised of a curious reddish-brown soil, comes to a dead end here. The soil underfoot at the end of the tunnel is very densely packed; above, a large, irregularly-shaped hole can be seen. The air stirs at irregular intervals as drafts blow down from the hole. However, as the hole is too high to reach, the only passable exit is to the west.
109550: An elite orc-guard is on sentry here.

The tunnel has been roughly worked here. Rocky outcroppings are both a bane and a boon, alternating between tripping and providing support. Support beams on either side indicate this might not be the strongest part of the tunnel.
109551:
A beer bottle has been left here.
A rather heavy clay jar stands here.
An orc-guard is on patrol here.
An orc-guard is on patrol here.
An elite orc-guard is on sentry here.

The entrance is a small space and littered with rubble. Along the grey rock walls stand benches and a few tables. The roof is jagged, with sharp edges protruding in different directions. The cave is damp, and moss has spread across the ceiling. Brown bottles and clay jars lie cracked open on the ground. A small desk with a stool stands next to the entrance. A narrow tunnel burrows deeper beneath the Misty Mountains to the east.
109552: A black pond is here, filled with putrid water.

A vast cave opens up inside the mountain, rising more than thirty feet tall. Water trickles down the eastern wall into a small pond located centrally in the cavern. Stalagmites and stalactites cover much of the cavern floor and ceiling. Scattered about the cave lie crumbling bones and rotting pelts. A stone stair has been carved out from the mountain, with a steep incline from the tunnel in the west, to a tunnel entrance in the north. Small torches sit lit in iron claws attached to the wall along the staircase.
109553: A long tunnel, more or less rounded, has been dug through the rock here. Sharp edges of the cold, grey stone interrupt what could be a proper passageway. Along the walls lie cracked pickaxes and abandoned broken ore carts. A thick layer of dust covers the ground. Beams of dried, cracking wood support the tunnel, keeping it from collapsing. A faint flickering light can be discerned at the end of a passage that leads deeper down under the mountain.
109554: The ground is rough and uneven. Footprints of various sizes and other unidentified tracks run deep in the heavy layer of dust which covers the area. Rocks lie heaped in big piles along the rounded tunnels. The ceiling and walls are supported by thick, dark logs. A pile of boulders and rubble blocks the passage to the east, while the darkness to the north hints at another cave or tunnel in that direction. A tunnel slopes slightly downwards to the west.
109555: The mines twist back and forth, with tunnels leading off in four directions. Damp and dark, the excavation expands further to the east, south and west. A hole in the northern wall leads into a steep, inclining tunnel. Cracked timber shores the ceiling, keeping the tunnels from collapsing. Broken tools lie abandoned in deep layers of dust along the tunnel's walls. A lantern hanging from one of the beams in the ceiling emits a faint light.
109556:
A long water trough made of wood stands here.
A weapons rack stands against the wall.
A rusty pickaxe with a broken handle lies discarded here.
A weary woman stands here, looking miserable.
An orc slavemaster is here, looking for someone to abuse.

A wooden trough stands centrally placed in the damp cavern. An abundance of pickaxes and heavy hammers are lined up in a rack on the northern wall. Wooden beams steady the arched ceiling, keeping it from collapsing. Shackles connected to heavy balls and chains lie grouped in different piles, just next to the mining areas. The mine opens up to the west while a narrowing tunnel leads deeper into the mountain to the south.
109557: An old mining tunnel comes to an end here, partially collapsed and completely in ruins. From pebbles to boulders, broken planks to cracked wooden beams, everything lie scattered about on the floor of the mine. The ceiling appears to have caved in completely to the west. Humanoid bones poke out from the rubble, crushed from the weight of the collapsed mine. The air is damp, and dust lies heavily on the ground. A small passageway to north seems to be the only route from this tunnel.
109558: A dwindling mineshaft descends deep into the mountain. Narrow, with rough walls and ceiling, it twists its way downwards. The cavern itself is not very large, and appears to have been dug out carelessly. Sharp edges protrude from the walls; rocks and rubble lie scattered on the caverns floor, covered in a layer of dust. The air is damp and heavy. There is a myriad of footprints, leading to and fro between the mineshaft and the eastern wall.
109559:
An iron pick has been dropped here.
A beer barrel has been left here.
A sturdy crate made of nailed wooden planks sits on the floor.
A beer barrel has been left here.
An elite orc-guard is on sentry here.
An orkish patrol-leader is here, keeping an eye on the mine.
Bofut the Dwarf, wielding a mighty dwarven axe, is standing here.
A stocky mountain mule is here, waiting to serve.

Crates, chests and barrels crowd this small room. A table stands along the southern wall with shards of clay and broken bottles scattered on it. An iron shackle, nailed to the ceiling, holds a skeleton covered in ragged clothing. The floor, walls and ceiling are smooth and heavy beams supports the ceiling, tightly bound together by thick, black rope, creating a supporting arch. The room exits through a door-opening in the east.
109560:
The burnt and blackened skeletal remains of a human are here.
A dark intangible shadow turns to face you.

Several large boulders, surrounded by smaller rocks and shattered wooden beams, create an upwards slope to the north. A charred skeleton has been crushed underneath scorched timber. The cave was extensively mined in the past, but by the looks of it has been abandoned for a long time. Carts have fallen over, broken into many pieces. Some of their load has a small shine to it, beneath the covering dust.
109561: The trail bends north and east here, around a large pillar of black rock standing at the side of the road. In the east the trail continues further into the range of mountains, and to the north the trail seems to make another sharp bend. From this distance the pillar of rock appears to have been crudely carved in the shape of a humanoid, wearing some sort of crown, but the ravages of the weather make further detail impossible to see. To the south there is a rocky path leading to a wooden hut.
109563:
A small termite is running around making strange sounds.
A small termite is running around making strange sounds.
A small termite is running around making strange sounds.

A small circular chamber occupies the centre of the treetrunk, but leaves enough living wood to keep the massive tree healthy and strong. The ground is soft and mossy, and the air has a surprisingly wholesome feeling to it. High above you the walls of this living chamber grow closer together, and eventually meet, forming a domed roof of heartwood.
109565:
A tiny spider is here, eating a tiny bug.
A huge, poisonous spider is here.
A tiny spider is here, eating a tiny bug.
A tiny spider is here, eating a tiny bug.
A huge, poisonous spider is here.

Thick brown roots poke through the walls of this small cavern, twisting and turning, and forming a dense tangle, which supports the earthy walls and roof. A sticky web bisects the chamber, and tiny beads of moisture hang from its silvery threads, like miniature diamonds.
109566: A simple wooden chest is here.

This is a simply constructed cabin, yet it looks solid enough to withstand weather and wind. There is one window each on the northern and southern walls. A door to the west seems to be the cabin's only exit aside from a trapdoor of solid-looking wood in the floor. An old rug lies on the floor in the centre of the room, covered in dust and dirt. An old burnt-out lantern is standing on a small table next to a bed. The bed itself is tipped over, and its mattress and cover lie discarded in a corner, gathering dust and mould.
109567:
The corpse of a great rat is lying here.
A greenish slime mould is here, smelling badly.

There is a small cabinet in one of the corners. A small wooden table has been placed between two shelves. Some cutlery and old, dirty plates lie covered in dust on the floor. Mouldy groceries have been left to rot on the shelves. The tight space opens into a main room to the south.
109568:
A wooden chest stands in the corner.
A simple wooden chest is here.

The cellar is in complete disarray. Bookshelves cover the walls on all sides. The books, pamphlets, scrolls and parchments that once stood on said shelves lie scattered on the floor. An old lantern lies in pieces on the ground. Another lantern, unlit and its glass cracked, hangs from the ceiling. Several simple chests stand along the walls, their locks broken or lids smashed, and their contents apparently looted. A small, unsteady staircase leads up to another room above.
109569: Some thick writhing vines whip all around you (red aura).

Whilst eastward there is a narrow, winding path between the huge, gnarled trees, the trail dead-ends to the west, where the undergrowth becomes extremely dense. The sickly brush and scrub here are choked by moss and fungus, as if the wood were trying to consume itself in its sickness. The lower branches of the trees are bare of leaves, and their bark is peeling, as if afflicted by disease.
109570: At the Heart of the Woods

A dark green, foul-smelling shrub grows to about a foot in height.
On the shrub, there are some white, egg-shaped berries.
A mass of wriggling vines drops on you from the trees.

The trees crowd in on one-another here, with dense tangles of withered branches, and sickly shrubs making the area almost impassable to the east and to the north. The ground is spongy and damp, made slippery with foul- smelling mosses and fungus. However, to the south, the trees open up into a surprisingly wholesome clearing.
109571:
A large thorny branched shrub is growing here.
On the shrub, there are two piles of blackberries.
A small animal, all covered in spines, snuffles amongst the undergrowth.

Short, thorny bushes add to the otherwise awfully barren scenery. Beneath these dark green shrubs, scattered clumps of light green, long bladed grass seem to thrive above the shorter, darker grass that lives without this kind of competition south of here. While the bushes are sparse enough east and west, the thicket north of here looks impenetrable.
109572: The corpse of a bloodthirsty bat is lying here.

Natural rock forms a dark tunnel here, with jagged and sharp edges protruding from the ceiling. The wide tunnel continues to the west, where it appears to narrow and descend slightly. There are indentations in the rock along the eastern tunnel wall above a pile of scattered debris, suggesting excavation that was started but not finished.
109573:
The corpse of a bloodthirsty bat is lying here.
The corpse of a bloodthirsty bat is lying here.
The corpse of a giant slug is lying here.
A stocky mountain mule is here, waiting to serve.

The jagged walls and uneven floor of this roughly-hewn tunnel suggest that it was once a natural cavern. An effort to expand the cave to make passage easier is evident, but the work is crude and incomplete. Water drips through cracks in the ceiling above and gathers in a small, dirty puddle along the northern wall.
109574: A sturdy crate made of nailed wooden planks sits on the floor.

This fort consists of a single, circular room formed by massive walls of natural rock. The walls are rough and uneven, extending from the floor to the ceiling only a short distance above; this lack of height contrasts with the breadth of the cavern, creating an area that is at once spacious and cramped. Stairs carved from the natural rock lead up to an opening in the ceiling.
109581:
The corpse of a dirty uruk is lying here.
The corpse of a renegade uruk is lying here.
The corpse of a bloodthirsty bat is lying here.
A renegade uruk is here, dirty and ragged.
A renegade uruk is here, dirty and ragged.
A renegade uruk is here, dirty and ragged.
A fierce bat is here, lusting for your blood.

The walls here form a large, circular chamber. Narrow stairs extend out from the walls, carved from the same stone, and allow passage up or down. The floor has been smoothed, creating an even surface; the ceiling, which is jagged and uneven, seems to have received less attention. Several racks holding crude weapons line the walls. These racks, together with a row of mouldy blankets, suggest that this chamber serves as the fort's barracks.
109583: The crown of the fort is a crude, small chamber. Narrow slits look out over the hills below, and provide a perfect view of a crevice to the east. The slits are hidden beneath an overhang on the outside and are unlikely to be visible from the ground below. A set of stairs leads down into the fort. There is a door-sized hole in the wall to the south which leads outside onto a ledge.
109584: This narrow ledge is only a couple of feet wide and less than five yards long. It clings to a near-vertical rock face and does not look particularly stable. At one end the ledge narrows until it disappears, while the other end leads to a dark opening in the rock. A rocky crevice is visible beneath the ledge.
109641: A ravine opens up towards the south. The hollow in the northern wall of the ravine provides a stony roof above, offering some protection from the elements. This grotto could possibly mark the beginning of a deeper cave, as a huge bear fur hung against the inner wall seems to cover an entrance deeper into the underground.
109642: While this was in all likelihood a natural cavern in the past, it has been expanded with crude tools to form a wide, high-ceilinged corridor. On the roof above, broken remnants of stalactites cling to the rock. Anything reaching down below ten feet has been hewn off, leaving jagged, shattered remains. On the lightly grey limestone floor, any stalagmites rising up to meet the opposing stalactites have been removed with brute force. The now widened corridor leads deeper into a cavern to the west, while a huge bear fur has been hung on the southern wall to cover what looks like a narrowing tunnel.
109643: These caves may well be natural in origin but have been converted into a rustic living area by whomever that now occupy them. Rocks or boulders one would expect in a cave have been cleared out, and the ground is worn smooth by the regular passage of its inhabitants. Towards the west, the cave leads through a narrow opening from which scents of meat and blood come drifting on the slowly circulating air.
109644: Four tunnels lead off in different directions from this subterranean juncture. The cavern is lofty, the ceiling no less than ten feet high at its lowest point. A vague scent of wood smoke fills the air, hinting at a recent fire in one of the nearby caves.
109645: A clear spring babbles as cool water trickles out of the ground.

This wide tunnel takes a rough, uneven path through the surrounding rock, moving through this area in a south-to-west bend. A small spring seeps up from the cavern floor at the eastern wall, gathering in a small pool to provide fresh water. The dust on the ground is mostly cleared away in a path from the pool and towards the south; although more because of regular traffic than any obvious intent to keep the area neat and clean. The tunnel to the west seem a lot less disturbed.
109646:
A small oaken table has been set here.
On the table, there are two large pieces of smoked meat and two smoked pieces of meat.

This narrow cave has been converted into a crude larder. The walls are speckled with spots of dried blood, and on the dusty floor dark, drying stains attract flies and other insects. Simple iron hooks have been set into the walls, ready for whatever meats may be hung from them.
109647: A young ill-tempered stone giant is here, muttering incoherently.

A low, narrow opening to the west seem to be the only entrance to this dwelling. The interior is stark, the walls harsh bare stone and the floor rough and uneven. Three tall piles of grass, leaves and animal furs could be passed off as sleeping places, and the scorched stones in the centre of the chamber suggest that at times a fire is built here.
109648: A very large set of stairs has been hewn out of the hard rock, leading further down into deep caverns. The cavern floor has been cleared of irregularities and any sharp or protruding stone has been removed from the walls. With a little decoration and lighting, this cave could almost pass as a hallway.
109649: The tunnel enters this wide, spacious grotto from the east. To the south and west, hard solid walls of rock block any passage, but towards the north the cave opens up and the far wall is barely discernible. Travel northwards is interrupted by a jagged crevice, and the only obvious way onwards in that direction is to climb down into the crevice and find a way from there.
109650: This crevice is narrow, with steep and jagged walls and sharp rocks everywhere. At the very southwestern end of the crevice, a rock shelf is visible. This looks to be the only reasonable place to climb out of here. If one were inclined to stay in the crevice, it appears to continue eastwards.
109651: Huge steps have been hewn out of the solid rock to the west, where a slight slope ascends and provides easier passage to the levels above. Each step is so high that a hobbit would need to use his hands to climb to the next, and so wide that said hobbit could place his bed on it. The cavern floor looks well trodden, free of loose rocks and remarkably smooth.
109652:
A mass of tattered fabric lies here in a heap.
A young ill-tempered stone giant is here, muttering incoherently.

The cavern system comes to a dead end here, and this small cave has been converted to a crude abode. Judging from the size of the long, wooden bunks against the back wall, the inhabitants are of impressive dimensions. The walls are rough but seem to have been smoothened to some extent, the worst of the sharp edges chopped away.
109653: This deep cleft is barely passable. The broken, jagged rocks of the crevice's walls makes travel to the east and west very difficult. Climbing out of the deep fissure is completely out of the question, the sides being much too steep, the rock cracked and broken; and most likely prone to falling apart if any weight is put upon it. The ground is littered with rubble fallen from the walls.
109654: Eastern End of an Underground Crevice

Here at the eastern end of this crevice, deep beneath the surface, little hope is given to a weary adventurer. The bottom of this crevice is a bleak place, the ground littered with broken rocks and fallen rubble. The sides of the deep fissure appear impossible to climb and the only viable direction of travel is to follow the course of the crevice towards the west.
109655: Here, the vast cavern that extends west of here ends in a small retreat. Lots of rubble lies strewn across the cavern floor, fallen from the unstable roof above. Most of the cavern walls and gravel consists of hard, grey stone prone to breaking apart into smaller shards with sharp, jagged edges.
109656: The size of this wide, vast cavern would put the throne room in many a castle to shame. The walls stand far enough apart to be shrouded in inky gloom. A great aggregation of rocky formations on the floor level makes the area hard to navigate. The floor itself is full of cracks, some of which are wide enough to step into if one were careless.
109657: A cave-in has created an enormous mass of crushed boulders along a wall in this colossal cavern. Any pathway in that direction has been lost forever. The remainder of the cave can still be described as pasture-sized. The rock is of a dark grey variety, and the rugged formations of the walls, floor and ceiling leaves no doubt that this cave is a work of nature.
109658: Faint sounds of dripping water can be heard echoing from some dark corner of this gigantic grotto. A wide variety of rocks make up the walls and floor, much of it granite but also volcanic rock types. Pillars of basalt stand tall in the stale air, remnants of chutes of volcanic magma that solidified in ages long gone. There is also thin veins of pitch black obsidian embedded in the rock bed, the slivers of glass-like rock glitter alluringly.
109659: A vast, natural cavern has formed here, deep down underground. The ground is very uneven, with cliff-like formations several yards high that rise from the floor throughout the cave. Much of the rock seem rich in ore, and there are veins of a dark, rusty red colour and some of brighter yellow shades.
109660: A sturdy rope has been tied here and descends below.

This smaller tunnel connects two huge, open caverns to the east and west, while to the north and south the walls of rough rock stand much closer together. The ground falls away in a steep treacherous fall to the east. A heedless traveller could walk right off the edge and crash down into the dark depths of this subterranean world.
109661: The ground here is covered in thick layers of knee-high bat guano. The cave-dwelling bats roost in the airy lofts high above, where they must have found access to the outside world. The air is filled with a stinging, acrid scent. The deep aggregation of guano continues uninterrupted towards the east, while the cave southwards may be a route to cleaner places.
109662: Vast deposits of bat guano have accrued on the floor of this grotto. The white, acidic droppings lie in layers thick enough to reach a hobbit's waist, filling the air with acrid, unpleasant smells. The cavern continues to the east and west, and so too does the guano, although there seems to be slightly less of it towards the east.
109663: A small bat is standing here.

The fluttering sounds of batwings higher up in the lofty spaces of this cavern is ever present. A shaft can be glimpsed high above, likely a route the cavern-dwelling bats take to the surface. Down here at the cavern floor, a great deal of spider webs have been spun between boulders and ledges. The webs reach as far up as halfway to the shaft above. Higher up, where the walls are closer together, the great webs stretch from wall to wall, obviously intended to entangle any bat that swoops down too low.
109664: A sturdy rope is hanging from above.

This cave is shaped like a terrace with wide, stair-like ledges to the east and west. Towards the west a cliff wall looms, so smooth it looks almost polished. Eastwards, the cavern floor falls away again in another steep decline. A narrow ledge leads out above the eastern chasm, following the southern cave wall in a sharp bend, only to quickly disappear from sight.
109665: Some ugly blow-flies are buzzing around here.

This narrow, unsteady ledge clings to the rock face, painstakingly winding its way southwards. To the west the ledge enters a cave, and footing is likely to be more stable. The ledge itself is is littered with earth and pebbles. In places there are gaps that must be stepped over, which further speak of the dangers of loitering here.
109666: Some ugly blow-flies are buzzing around here.

In places, this uneven ledge slopes downwards out from the rock face, and small rocks and pebbles crunch underfoot: further heightening the risk of a fall. A step in any direction seems hazardous and potentially fatal. At places the ledge widens enough for easy passage, yet in other it is narrow enough that brushing against the cave wall is inevitable.
109667:
A skeleton of some humanoid lies in the dust.
Some ugly blow-flies are buzzing around here.
Some ugly blow-flies are buzzing around here.
Some ugly blow-flies are buzzing around here.
Some ugly blow-flies are buzzing around here.

With a sharp twist, this tunnel bends toward the south and the east. The walls are smooth and rounded, made of earth rather than hard rock. It is hard to say if this is part of natural cave system or if this tunnel has been dug out. Towards the east the tunnel open up into a wide space while it continues in a slight downward slope to the south. The air is foul here, a stench of rot and decay ever present as if something died and was left unburied.
109668: Earth Tunnel at the Top of a Slope

Droves of loose earth has fallen to the floor of this tunnel, making the footing soft but taxing. The tunnel slopes down steeply toward the east to disappear deeper into the ground. The tunnel seem much too rounded to be a creation of nature, although there are no obvious sign of it being intentionally designed.
109669: A small vicious black rat squeaks at you for disturbing it.

This serpentine, sloping earth tunnel winds its way down through layers of densely packed earth. The tunnel seem to level out not far below this point, although if that means that it is any closer to anything of relevance is indeterminable. A long, wide groove runs along the centre of the tunnel, as if something heavy was dragged along the floor recently.
109670: A deep furrow, almost a yard wide and half as deep, has been ploughed along this tunnel. Something very heavy may have been either dragged or rolled through here, going up the slope or coming down it. The walls hard-packed earth walls are interspersed with small grey rocks of varying shapes.
109671: This long, narrow tunnel winds through hard, densely packed earth strewn with rocks of varying sizes. Neither the tunnel's origin nor eventual destination is obvious from this part of the passageway. To see beyond the next curved bend, one would have to set out in either direction.
109672: The walls of this tunnel consists of hard, densely packed earth. The southern wall has been punched through from the other side, and loose earth lies sprinkled on the floor around the opening. A tunnel in that direction leads into another cavern. A large, crude slab has been put in place at the tunnel opening to serve as an obstacle. The tunnel of packed earth continues to the west, and to the east the tunnel leads into a ravine with jagged, steep rock walls.
109673: A long, narrow ravine lined by steep rocky slopes begins here and leads off into the distance to the north. Loose rocks has fallen to the ground and lie in scattered fragments everywhere. Towards the west, there is a tunnel opening and a huge boulder that has been moved to this area to serve as a barricade between this ravine and the western tunnel.
109674: dig if way n is blocked by boulders

The ravine is deep and almost impassable here. The sides rise high to disappear from view above, lost in darkness and gloom. Boulders come bouncing down the slopes of the ravine every now and then, shattering and splintering into tinier rocks. The slightest sound bounces back and forth between the walls, echoing up and down the ravine.
109675: This deep fissure runs through the bedrock like a terrible wound made with a saw-edged blade. The sides are jagged and unstable, rocks and pebbles constantly sliding down the sides to come to a rest once they reach the ravine's bottom. Here and there large rocks lie scattered into dozens of fragments where they've landed after a long fall from an unseen ceiling above.
109676: The cavern floor is littered with rocks and crushed boulders that have fallen from a roof so far above that it is lost in gloom. The walls of the narrow, steep-sided tunnel are most accurately described as a ravine. The slightest sound travels up and down the ravine, bouncing back and forth as the echoes multiply. A concentration of fallen rubble at the western wall speaks of past rockfalls and the dangers of these deep caves.
109677: A small vicious black rat squeaks at you for disturbing it.

Sheer walls rise on both sides with no signs of places where climbing could even be considered. The only way out of this place is to continue onwards, or head back the way from which one came. The sounds of falling rocks echo in the ravine intermittently, the sound travelling up and down the length of the great fissure.
109678: A small vicious black rat squeaks at you for disturbing it.

Three branches of a winding, narrow underground ravine meet here. A steep, harsh slope blocks any conceivable travel towards the north. The three ravines lead off to the south, west, and east, neither direction showing any sign of an end of ravines or a way up.
109679: A small vicious black rat squeaks at you for disturbing it.

A deep, narrow fissure follows the length of the ravine here, reminiscent of a long, irregular wound of unknowable depth. Luckily, the fissure is too narrow to fall down into, or the unwary could vanish forever in a moment of carelessness. The ravine itself continues to the east and west.
109680: A small vicious black rat squeaks at you for disturbing it.

Landslides consisting of large boulders and jagged rocks have crashed to the floor of the ravine here some time in the not too distant past. The ravine runs like a great fissure through the subterranean landscape. It is slowly being filled by the falling rocks, and one wonders if perhaps one day it will become completely impassable.
109681: A large boulder blocks most of the underground ravine here, firmly embedded in the mix of hard earth and gravel underfoot. Passage through the area requires squeezing oneself between the boulder and the rugged walls of the ravine. Many smaller rocks lie scattered across the ground, hinting at a roof above that is far from stable.
109682: The great ravine through the deep subterranean bedrock comes to its end here, the sides simply coming together to meet at a solid wall of rock. Where the ravine is a bit wider, there is an area where the northern wall is considerably less steep than elsewhere. A tunnel opening lies there, the opening a black hole against the surrounding stone.
109683: A narrow cavern to the north leads out onto this open area. The tunnel ends at the very brink of an underground ravine at least twenty feet across. The slope down to the ravine's floor is steep, but rugged and uneven and should be easy enough to traverse. A cold draft can be felt from below, slightly rustling some old, dead cobwebs that cling to the limestone walls.
109684: Rugged, steep slopes enclose this cavern, forming a deep and almost impassable ravine. Large rocks lie scattered across the floor of the ravine, and scree-like formations almost completely block it in other places. Every now and then a large rock comes tumbling down the side of the ravine, setting off a landslide of gravel that join the accruing piles at the bottom.
109685: This steep and narrow ravine leads off into the distance to the south. Here, the two walls meet, and the ravine comes to an end. There is a breach in the western wall of the ravine, where something punched through from the other side. A rough, uneven hole near the corner where the ravine ends leads deeper into whatever may be found below.
109686: A patch of moss grows here on a wet, flat stone.

The sides of this steep but cragged hole are lit by a faint sickly green glow from patches of phosphorescent moss growing on the cave walls. A tunnel opens up to the west, the opening partly covered by strands of sticky spider webs. Above, the edge of the hole is easily reachable even for those of humble stature.
109687: Faint skittering sounds can be heard from the north and west. Noise travels far in these deep tunnels and the sounds are faint enough to perhaps be imagined. A snarl of webbings line the cave, covering boulders and deep dark holes in the uneven walls.
109688: The ceiling hangs down low enough in this grotto to give even the least claustrophobic of travellers pause. The cavern is made of a mineral-rich rock mostly a light grey in colour. Only the lack of seeping water keeps this cave traversible, for if the stunted stalactites hanging down from the ceiling were of the lengths such formations can grow into, they would meet the floor and close this tunnel completely. Passageways leads off to the east, west, and north.
109691: The forest floor begins to rise slightly to the south. The smell of pine sap permeates the forest. The trunks of the pines deposit sticky sweet smelling sap on anyone or anything which brushes against them. High overhead the branches of pine needles sway in the wind.
109692: This dark tunnel, far beneath the fresh air and open spaces of the outside world, show plenty of signs of a habitual presence of spiders. Webs have been spun, stretching between rocks and boulders, crags and stalactites. Any careless movement could cause severe entanglement in the sticky traps.
109693: A tiny spider is here, eating a tiny bug.

A great number of stalagmites have formed across the expanse of this cavern, rising up from the floor as thick, peaked pillars. Above hang the corresponding stalactites, which are much slimmer in shape. Many spider webs have been spun here: most of them are empty, although some of them hold the dried husks of bats or lizards.
109694:
The corpse of a huge, poisonous spider is lying here.
A tiny spider is here, eating a tiny bug.
A tiny spider is here, eating a tiny bug.

Here, deep down near the roots of the world, the rocks enclosing this narrow twisting passageway are as black as the darkest night: shot through with veins of faintly glittering minerals. A fair amount of spider webs cover the walls, some of it new and sticky and some merely tangles of old, dry cobwebs.
109695:
A tiny spider is here, eating a tiny bug.
A tiny spider is here, eating a tiny bug.

The presence of spiders is evident no matter in which direction one turns. Thick, sticky webs cover the walls, floor and ceiling and the dry, empty husks of past prey litters the ground. A smaller chamber lies to the north, the entrance so covered in webs it could easily be overlooked. Towards the south there seem to be less webs, and more of the dark rock beneath visible. A way out would surely lie in that direction.
109696:
A tiny spider is here, eating a tiny bug.
A tiny spider is here, eating a tiny bug.

This entire grotto functions as a hatchery for the spiders of the area. Grey, bulging eggsacks hang from sticky spider webs and tiny, hatched eggs litter the floor. Most of the cave is covered in thick webs, the strands far too thick to having been spun by a common house spider.
109697: A tiny spider is here, eating a tiny bug.

Great webs spun by what must be truly intimidating spiders cover holes and cavities in the walls, possibly providing nests and hiding places. A patch of bare rock on the southern wall is surprisingly free of webs, and the stone is a much lighter grey than the surrounding stone. The tunnel leads towards the east, where faint reflections of water can be glimpsed.
109698:
The corpse of a huge tarantula is lying here.
The corpse of a huge, poisonous spider is lying here.
The corpse of a huge, poisonous spider is lying here.
A huge, poisonous tarantula extends her legs to you.

Tremendous patience and effort has gone into entangling the walls, floor and ceiling of this lair in a mesh of webs. Here and there, dry old husks of bats and lizards can be seen among the cobwebs, leftovers from creatures the spiders in these deep caves have feasted upon.
109699: A pool of darkish water has formed in a depression of the stone.

A dark pool has formed in a hollow in the eastern part of this cave. Thin, pointed stalactites hang above the pool, some so long that their tips touch the surface of the water. Drops of mineral-enriched water fall from the smaller stalactites, as if they were a part of a slow, steady rain.
109700: This low, wide cavern lies nestled in the very foundations of Arda, deep beneath the world of men and elves. Erosion has hollowed out an uneven cavity with grey limestone walls. Numerous stalagmites rise from the ground where slowly, dripping mineral-enriched water has built up small, stunted formations over the eons.
109701: A hollow cavity has formed here in the limestone bedrock. Layers in shades of white and grey are easily distinguished on the walls. A narrow shaft, a natural tunnel hollowed out through the ages, leads upwards here. To the west, a limestone cave continues into the darkness.
109702: Here, a long, slim shaft has formed in the limestone bedrock. The walls are of a stratiform of lightly grey and white layers of limestone. The various layers have eroded in varying degrees, providing a multitude of small ledges to place hands and feet on, making the shaft accessible to even the most inexperienced climber.
109703: The walls of this grotto shift in streaks of white and grey limestone. The low ceiling above could cause concern for the claustrophobic, and small stalactites hanging down are a potential danger for the tall, unwary adventurer. A chute near the southern wall leads down, deeper into the underworld.
109704: Towering stalagmites, ancient things built up through the ages by the slow dripping of water filled with minerals, rise from the cavern floor towards a ceiling lost in the darkness above. The cave is the size of a large cathedral, with the walls to either side lost in gloom. Towards the eastern end the ceiling is considerably lower than elsewhere in this massive cavern. A great crack runs along the cavern floor near the centre of the area, and in places it is wide enough for a horse to fall through.
109706: This hole is located in the floor of an underground ravine. The stony ground of the ravine above is gradually replaced by dirt towards the bottom, the shift in the geology easily evident on the hole's walls. A tunnel through the soft earth leads off towards the south, sloping slightly downwards further toward the roots of the world.
109707: A small vicious black rat squeaks at you for disturbing it.

Here, a long tunnel, ten feet wide and equally tall, burrows through soft, moist earth. The tunnel continues onwards to the south but seem to come to its end towards the north. It requires arduous effort to travel here: the soft, moist earth cling to ones feet and legs, not unlike walking through a mire.
109708: It is unclear whether this rounded tunnel deep in the underground is a work of nature or a burrow created by something. It may seem much too rounded and conveniently straight to be the work of nature, but it is also inconceivable that something would go through the trouble to dig a tunnel in this soft dirt, a material so soft that it is likely to collapse at any time.
109709: The air here is very humid, and the surrounding earthen walls are dripping wet with moisture. Small clumps of wet earth frequently fall to the ground, joining the ankle-deep soft mush that makes travelling here a strenuous affair. The stench of mould and mildew is very strong, no doubt it comes from the sickly-white filaments that cling to walls in big, putrid patches.
109710: A pool of darkish water has formed in a depression of the stone.

The air in this spacious cavern is hot and humid. Thin wisps of steam rise from a dark pool, only to slowly dissipate and form condensation of the walls and ceiling. Water drips from the ceiling at a steady pace and runs down the walls in tiny rivulets. A narrow chute leads upward at the side of the cavern opposite of the pool. Tunnels lead to the west and south.
109711: Small pools of muddy water have formed in places on the tunnel floor because the earth is too saturated to absorb it. The tunnel itself is round and low, barely ten feet from floor to ceiling. Clumps of wet earth fall to the ground constantly, and the entire tunnel seems to be nothing more than a hole through wet, soft clay just waiting to collapse.
109712: The walls of this tunnel consists of wet and pliable dirt. Here and there, big puddles of water have formed, where stale water gives off a rancid, unhealthy smell. The tunnel continue in a straight line towards the north, while to the south it slopes upwards.
109713: The tunnel continues here through soft, moist earth. Further up the tunnel, the wet earth gradually gives way to rocks and gravel. In some places, large rocks have come to rest after a tumbling fall down the slope. In the opposite direction, the tunnel leads deeper into the earth.
109714: The walls on both sides of this passage have partly crumbled and fallen inwards. A passage has been cleared through the middle of the rubble: a wide swath of pathway leading towards the south, and down a slanting passage to the north. Among the rubble on the eastern side there are scraps of rotting cloth poking through, as if something was hastily buried beneath the stones.
109715: A huge circular grotto of black stone has been created here: a magnificent example of nature's architecture. The ceiling is shaped like an enormous, pitch-black dome. Large heaps of rubble have been piled against the walls to keep passageways clear. Tunnels lead off in all directions, and judging by the occasional crashing sounds of falling rocks, this chamber is an island of stability in an otherwise dangerous cavern.
109716: Big, sharp rocks poke up through the hard earth floor in this passageway, stuck where they fell from the roof above. In places, holes in the floor show where rocks has been cleared away to keep the path accessible. The walls are full of cracks and cavities where loose rocks have tumbled down to the cavern floor.
109717: A narrow, winding passage leads through the deep underground. Fissures and cracks run up and down the walls, some even cross the whole arc of the cavern's roof to meet other fissures on the opposite walls. Obviously, these walls are under great stress, and the danger of lingering here needlessly is very clear. Broken rocks lie scattered across the floor. Against one wall far along the southern end of the tunnel, a huge boulder has fallen down, blocking off half of the passageway.
109718: The walls of this passage slope inwards, and the roof is considerably narrower than the floor. Sheets of rock and dirt have fallen to the ground where they now rest as piles of rubble. The centre of the corridor is surprisingly clear of debris and easily passable. The passage leads on towards the north and south. Occasionally, falling rocks nearby are announced by the rumble and hard cracks of stone smashing against stone.
109719: A small black vicious rat squeaks at you for disturbing it.

Dank, slimy rocks provide useful hand and footholds in this narrow chute. Several wide, faintly glimmering veins of copper and quartz run through the rock. A hint of warmer air can be felt in the weak updraft coming from below. A steady drizzle of water is coming from above.
109733: A small vicious black rat squeaks at you for disturbing it.

Climbing this narrow, steadily ascending shaft is easier than it may seem, mostly because the walls are filled with niches, ledges, and jutting boulders. Water slowly trickles down the walls, only to disappear down into the depths below. Faintly glittering veins of minerals streak through the stone, displaying a mixed palette of greens and yellows.
109734: There is a slight hint of warm air rising from below. Faint wisps of mist or steam dissipate in the air. Brown and green slime slowly oozes and trickles down the walls, tainting the air with an odour of rot and putrefaction. A small recess in the wall of the steeply sloping tunnel offers cover in case something comes tumbling down the chute. A series of crude indentations in the walls make for a makeshift ladder.
109735: A constant drip-drop of falling, dribbling, and trickling water is ever present, the source lying somewhere further up the chute. Thin rivulets of sickly green slime ooze down at a more leisurely pace, mixing with the water and covering parts of the wall in a wet, glistening layer of goo. The chute snakes up and down through the bedrock. Travel here is hard but not impossible, largely thanks to numerous small ledges, jutting rocks, and other hand and footholds.
109736: The walls are covered by a wet sheen of water and slime, originating from a hole in the ceiling clogged with rotting vegetation. The slime oozes slowly along the wall, dripping from rock to rock and gathering in miniscule pools. Downwards, a chute leads off into the darkness. Its sides are uneven and have plenty of hand and footholds, thereby make climbing it a fairly easy thing to do.
109737: Above, this hole opens into a wide opening several dozen yards across. The sides of the hole slope inwards, forming a funnel. At the bottom, the hole is circular and only a few yards wide. Various vegetational detritus has fallen into the hole, some sticking to the wet sides, but most gathering in a rotting heap at the bottom. The decomposing plants, a mix of fungi, vines, moulds, and leaves, is kept wet by water slowly dribbling down the hole's sides.
109738: A statue of a troll is posed in a moment of flight yet forever frozen in stone.

These caves are a veritable marshland. The air is humid and filled with the smells of a varied flora. Fungi, moss, and various plants seem to have found ideal conditions in which to thrive. A large number of fractures run across the cavern's ceiling, and through these water constantly seeps in, adding to the marshlike and spongy cavern floor. The fractures open up to the outside world, and although rarely more than a hand's breadth wide, they provide ample sunlight for the plants in here to flourish.
109739:
A small harmless centipede is here.
A tiny mould slowly oozes across the surface of the mire.
A tiny mould slowly oozes across the surface of the mire.

A wide expanse of wet, spongy bog covers most of the ground is this watery cave. From cracks in the ceiling, tiny rivulets of water come seeping down into the cave, making splattering noises in the pools and mud in a neverending downpour. Various plants find the constant moisture ideal to live in, and the sparse sunlight that finds its way down through the fissures gives them enough light in which to thrive.
109740:
A large toadstool grows nearby.
A mottled snake is sneaking here, ready to sink its fangs into flesh.
A mottled snake is sneaking here, ready to sink its fangs into flesh.
A large brown snake with black patches is coiled here.

This narrow niche has been converted from a stony burrow to a wet and unpleasant morass. The muddy water is deep enough to be knee-high for a troll, and any hole or pit beneath would be impossible to see before stepping in it. A couple of large boulders rise from the mud, overgrown with grass and small plants. The roof is fissured, allowing water and sunlight to find their way down here.
109741:
A huge black fungus is here, exuding a foul stench.
A huge black fungus is here, exuding a foul stench.
A huge black fungus is here, exuding a foul stench.
Some thick writhing vines whip all around you.
A giant, strange looking green fungus is here, ready to devour you in seconds.
Some thick writhing vines whip all around you.
A giant, strange looking green fungus is here, ready to devour you in seconds.
An ancient fungus smothers the boulders.
An ancient fungus smothers the boulders.
A giant creature, covered with mould and slime, oozes across the ground.
A slimy spotted mould is lying here, incapacitated.
A tiny mould slowly oozes across the surface of the mire.
A giant creature, covered with mould and slime, oozes across the ground.

The ground is moist and covered with a layer of mud, yet in places boulders rise above most of the sodden pools. Fungi seem to find this area ideal and are positively thriving here in a state of general abundance. The soft sounds of dripping of water are ever present, as water falls from the cavern's ceiling, eventually finding its way down through cracks and fractures.
109742:
A huge black fungus is here, exuding a foul stench.
A giant, strange looking green fungus is here, ready to devour you in seconds.
An ancient fungus smothers the boulders.
A tiny mould slowly oozes across the surface of the mire.

In these caves, a wide variety of fungi and vines grow in abundance. The air is full with the sounds of buzzing insects and dripping water. Dead vegetation rot away in an ever deepening marsh-like mire, at places deep enough for a hobbit to drown in. Many of the fungi that flourish here seem sensitive to being disturbed, if the faint quivering, spurts of released spores and odd pulsating movements are indications to be relied on.
109743:
Some thick writhing vines whip all around you.
A spotted mould covered in slime is here, partly submerged in the wet muck.
A tiny mould slowly oozes across the surface of the mire.

Dead vines and rotting vegetation float in shallow, mud-brown pools of water, and an unpleasant odour of decay fills the air. There is a constant inflow of water from above, where fissures in the ceiling opens up to the world outside. The water trickles down, already filthy from whatever marsh lies above, and it oozes down along the walls, slowly adding to the mire-like cavern floor.
109744:
The corpse of a large bat is lying here.
A large pile of boulders is sitting here, probably debris from a rockslide.

Piles of broken rock clutter the room, mainly at the wide cavern's western end where an opening high up on the wall is clogged with stones of all sizes. Choking, silvery-grey dust hangs suspended in the still air, hinting at a recent rockslide. The cave seems to be a natural formation, and it opens up into a wider hall to the east.
109745: The walls and ceiling of this small niche consist of hard but brittle grey rock. In places, there are large clear surfaces on the walls where sheets of rocks recently have fallen to the floor. The ground however is surprisingly devoid of rubble, as if someone cleared it regularly. The niche opens into a much larger chamber to the west.
109746: Cracked rocks lie scattered across the floor of this wide passage. Jagged fissures run up and down the walls on either side of the tunnel, and dust sifts down from cracks in the ceiling at irregular intervals. A path clear from obstructive rubble and rocks follows the centre of the tunnel from north to south: it is too straight to be natural.
109747: A wide section of the eastern wall has collapsed and now partially blocks this passage. Rubble covers most of the tunnel floor, yet a surprisingly rubble-free path runs down the centre of the tunnel. Where the rubble has been cleared, a hard-packed dirt surface, worn down to a deeper gravel layer, is visible. Deep, wide cracks line the walls of the tunnel, and there is no place where the rock seems completely solid or stable.
109748: A tunnel through unstable, crumbling bedrock comes to an end here. A massive cave-in has blocked the southern part of the passageway, and a hole as wide as the tunnel itself opens up just before the massive piles of rocks and boulders. Rocks are scattered across the tunnel floor, and the occasional creak of boulders scraping against one another deep in the rubble lends little faith to the idea that this area has completely stabilized after the collapse.
109749: An unfinished tunnel leading in from the north comes to its conclusion here. The excavation seems to have caused a cave-in as the southern part of the tunnel comes to an abrupt end in a jagged hole that leads down into a deeper, natural-looking cavern. Piles of rock are heaped against the walls, the effort to remove them apparently abandoned.
109750: A crude, unfinished tunnel has been dug through the dark bedrock here. The walls are uneven and edges of large boulders of harder rock jut out into the tunnel. The effort of removing them was obviously not worth the bother. Rubble is strewn about the tunnel and the floor is covered by a deep layer of dust and grime.
109751: A burrow has been created through the hard bedrock. Great brutal force must have been used in the effort to create this tunnel. The walls and floor show no sign of chiseling and minecraft. Rather, the stone has been forced to give way before raw power with great furrows and raw wounds giving witness to the impressive effort applied to creating this tunnel.
109752: This crudely dug-out burrow, twelve or thirteen feet in diameter, lies abandoned and dust-covered in the depths of the mountain. Quickly-rigged wooden poles and planks secured by old, thick ropes prevents the whole area from caving in. The soil is dark and wet, and the air is thick and heavy. To the north, there is a massive, black troll-door resting on five massive, rusted iron hinges. The burrow itself continues to the south.
109753: This rounded, carved grotto is roughly twelve feet high and just about as wide. Poles of wood brace the walls, keeping them from caving in. There is no doubt that this excavation project is unfinished and abandoned: mouldy ropes and wet, broken tools lie scattered about the area, arranged in a way that leaves the impression that the excavators left in a hurry. The burrow makes its way through the moist, hard-packed earth to the north. To the south, a huge slab of black stone blocks further passage.
109754: The earthy ground shifts in colours of dark brown and black, some parts softer than others. The tunnel seems to have been hastily dug out, and cracked, half-rotten wooden beams have been put up to support the irregular ceiling and walls. A hole in the western wall leads into a shaft, while the tunnel itself continues to the north and south.
109755: A half-decayed corpse of a goblin lies rotting on the ground.

An irregularly-shaped hole in the ceiling, neither round nor square, opens into a dark cave above. Small ledges remain from a recent excavation, creating easy access to that higher tunnel. The eastern exit is lined with broken planks, tilted boulders, and loose rocks, suggesting that a barrier was smashed to pieces.
109756: A giant, strange looking green fungus is here, ready to devour you in seconds.

This tunnel is but a dozen feet high and wide, and tapers off to the north. It looks much like the tunnel of an exploring badger: round, with rough edges and no apparent purpose. Beams of dark, rotted wood support the densely-packed, wet soil walls and ceiling, keeping them from collapsing. The tunnel continues to the south, where it widens slightly.
109757: There is a hole in the centre of this cavern floor, opening up into a steep shaft. The shaft is lined with ledges every three to four feet, creating a crude yet usable semi-natural staircase. The chute is deep, and its bottom must lie too far down to be seen from this height. Broken planks, rusting pickaxes and other tools lie spread about the cavern, seemingly abandoned. The cave ascends to the north.
109758: This rock-choked tunnel continues to the north and south. Huge rocks and boulders turn the steep slope into a maze, creating a terrain that is both difficult and painful to navigate. The deep black walls and ceilings have been crudely dug out with little skill and in obvious haste. A faint draft can be felt from the north, bringing cold, dry air into the tunnel. Small spiders scurry along the dirt-packed ground, disappearing into cracks and beneath rocks when disturbed.
109759: The black rocks that make up the floor, ceiling and walls of this tunnel feels dry and cold to the touch. The dark tunnel slopes steeply downwards to the south, steeply enough that passage that way looks perilious. At the top of the passageway, located to the north, a bigger cave can be discerned.

Five tunnels converge here at this spacious intersection. To the south one tunnel makes a steep descent, while the east and north offers wearying ascents. A crude tunnel burrows deeper into the mountain to the west. Between the southern and western tunnels a crack in the wall leads down towards a crude-looking, descending staircase. The area is covered by a thick layer of dust and dirt, imprinted with wide tracks leading off in all possible directions. The ceiling is high and the cave is truly vast.
109761: The corridor ascends slightly from south to north. The ceiling arches overhead, smooth and dome-shaped. Protruding edges and rocks stick out from the cavern walls in a few places. The stone walls are black as night, and the air is cold and damp. The dirty, dust-covered floor is marked by a number of footprints that cross back and forth from south to north.
109763: A young troll is here, gnawing on a bone.

An arched corridor extends from east to west. Green and grey moulds grow over vast areas of the walls, covering large swaths of the wet, black bedrock. Boulders and bigger rocks have been left in seemingly random places, most likely remnants of the excavation process. Small, crumbling, dried-out husks from insects litter the cavern floor along the walls, and spider webs stretch between rocks and boulders.
109764: The dark stone walls and ceiling creates a dome that covers the entire length of this corridor. Furhter passage is possible to the east and west. The walls are, where not smooth, at least fairly even-textured. Traces of bat droppings line the sides of the tunnel, and a decaying bat corpse lies covered with dust and maggots next to a small boulder. A light, constant breeze of humid air blows through the area.
109765: This dome-shaped, arched corridor is pitch-black in colour, and has been excavated using crude methods. Sharp edges protrude at various points from the walls, and some boulders and smaller rocks lie scattered throughout the hallway. Footprints have been left all over the area, deeply imprinted into the thick layer of dirt and dust on the ground. A light breeze blows through the corridor, spreading a strong, rancid odour. The tunnel rises to the south, while to the west it descends slightly.
109766: A dome-shaped tunnel comes to an end here in a rather narrow cavern. A lukewarm breeze blows through the area, coming from the north and continuing through a wide crack in the cavern's western wall. A narrow ledge just beneath the crack gives easy access to it. A putrid odour envelops the cave, carried here by the draft. A narrow, ascending stone tunnel works its way upwards through the large crack in the western wall. The bedrock here is very dark and the walls are lined with sharp, protruding edges. A carcass lies crushed under some boulders beneath the narrow ledge.
109767: The tunnel narrows here, creating a short bottleneck. It widens again to the east and west. On the western side a massive, round stone door lies cracked on the ground, its hinges still hanging from the circular doorway. A massive hall opens up beyond the broken entranceway. To the east the tunnel widens to a cave, tall and spacious. Remainders of well-gnawed bones, rusted goblets and other trinkets lie scattered on the ground here.
109768: The caves open up here, going from tighter tunnels to spacious halls. Tall, black pillars, crudely carved from the surrounding rocks support the vast ceilings. In some areas, the pillars have been replaced by enormous, old, withered logs. A long, centrally-located table rises from the floor, hewn directly from the black stone that forms these caves. It is covered by the remains of once-living creatures: long-dried entrails, cracked skulls, and pulverized bones. The vast halls extend to the north and west. To the east a cracked entranceway leads into a tapering tunnel.
109769: A large bat is here, hanging in the darkness.

The ceilings extend far above, creating halls dozens of feet tall. Pillars of black stone, bordering on a deep purple, have been carved directly from the surrounding rock. In some areas, the walls have been reinforced with massive planks and boulders to prevent a cave-in. The entire area is scattered with decomposing remains; the smell permeates the humid air. The halls continue to the east and south.

A bonfire flickers with a fading light at the centre of the cave. The halls continue to the south.

Smashed chests, rusted iron tools and moulding foodstuffs lie scattered in the dirt. Rats, roaches and centipedes scurry along fissures in the ground. To the south a wooden door is slowly rotting and falling apart; it is the only visible exit out of here.
109772: The stone stairs turn quickly, leading upwards to another level of the underground caves. A rotting, skewed wooden frame outlines the tunnel to the north. 109773: Small openings to the north and west both appear to lead to large, dark halls. To the east a smaller cavern can be seen, flickering with a faint light.
