Broken tools lie spread in the hallway, along with smaller rocks, broken planks, live cockroaches, and the bones from some sort of animal.
109774: Tall, rough black pillars extend down the centre of this hall, forming parallel rows. The hall is wide and tall, its walls lined with sharp stone edges. Little care was used when excavating the area: some of the pillars are crooked and appear to be buckling under the weight of the mountain, and now and then ominous creaking sounds can be heard. Small rocks and pebbles lie in the dirt around some of the pillars. A big stone table rises from the ground: it has been carved directly from the surrounding stone. A strong, putrid smell is ever-present in the thick, humid air. The halls widen to the north, while to the south they narrow into a smaller hallway.
109775: A half-decayed corpse of a goblin lies rotting on the ground.

This hall is in complete disarray: the innermost part has collapsed, leaving a heap of rocks, planks, and other debris. A thick layer of stone dust covers the whole area. Huge blocks of black stone lie cracked along the walls. The dried-out husks of dead bugs and pulverized bones large enough to be from a troll have been crushed by the rockfall. A small hallway leads eastwards.
109776: The stairs lead down, deeper into the dark mountain. The cave is crude, with rough edges protruding from the walls. The unevenly-cut stairs are covered with dust, rocks and random debris. Little bugs, roaches and spiders climb the walls along the stairs. The dark, murky tunnel to the east appears passable.

109780: A roughly-hewn staircase has been dug out of the deep, dark mountain. Its ascent is steep, and it turns sharply to the northwest. The steps are quite high, uneven, and worn-down. A similar ledge as this one can be seen on the other side of the chasm, well out of reach to the north. The burrow makes its way upwards, both to the east and west.

Small webs stretch between sharp edges protruding from the rough wall to the north, and some of the webs appear to have entangled some of the small bugs that are ever-present in these caves.

The study of Oropher the elven Wizard is full of light, and its air is thick and warm. The room has been furnished both for the studies and relaxation: a large, wooden desk is littered with documents, scrolls and maps of old, while a comfortable-looking armchair stands next to a large, decorated window. The scent of pipeweed hangs in the air, originating from a small, wooden box on the windowsill, hinting where the wizard likes to sit and ponder the mysteries of the world. The window faces to the west, offering a magnificent view to the valley of Imladris. Among the trees and plants outside many birds and smaller animals can be heard; the tranquility of Rivendell is very profound.

A large vanity is set against the top, boxes spilling over jewelry, an incense burner on the side. See-through silk leggings are draped over the chair in front, a huge chest filled with boots of all sizes lies in the corner, and suggestive artwork covers the walls.

This wooden, light-coloured room contains a big bed and a large window which allows the sun to shine in during the day time and offers a view towards the forest on the northern slopes of the Rivendell Valley. There are pictures and paintings on the walls and one of them illustrating a large red dove stands out from the rest. The floor is covered with a thick red mat. Other furniture consists of a table, a few chairs and a cupboard.
110001:
A large stone fireplace with a roaring fire warms the room.
A tall, fair-haired elf stands here quietly.

This cottage is small and simple in design, consisting of but a single room. The colours are muted, consisting of various shades of brown: the brown stones of the walls, the dark-stained wooden planks of the floor, and the light, unstained undersurface of the peaked wooden roof above. A loft is nestled beneath the roof, covering perhaps half the area of the floor, with a wooden ladder providing access. A single table with two chairs sits in the middle of the room, and aside from the fireplace that dominates the northern wall, is the only furniture. Large windows are set in the eastern and western walls, with dark-stained wooden shutters that have been thrown wide.
110002:
A wooden chest stands in the corner.
A humble man stands here, ready to help you with your things.

This cosy, small structure has been skillfully built as an extention from the vegetation clinging to the overgrown archways. The simple room is large enough to fit some essential personal belongings of a traveller, in addition to a table and some cabinets there is just enough space for a single bed on the finely-woven vine structure of the floor. There are no windows, but nevertheless sunlight penetrates through the canvice of vegetation that makes up most of the walls and ceiling.
110004: A humble man stands here, ready to help you with your things.

This chamber is made out of wood from the black pine tree. The dark colours of the room are contrasted by a marble altar standing in the middle of the room. There is a bed in one of the corners, a desk with a chair next to the window, and a large bookshelf standing against one of the walls. The window shows a beautiful scenery of Rivendell.
110005: The Housekeeper looks fed up with her job. She scowls at you unhappily.

Entering the domicile, the foyer gives way to a cluttered, messy room. The walls have been overtaken by an assortment of plants and vines. From the ceiling the dense vegetation hangs low, and is apparently very healthy. In the center of the room rests a giant boulder covered in strange markings. A diverse collection of pipes lies on the table in the corner next to an antique clock, while bits of trash and pipe-weed litter the floor. The inhabitants of this dwelling clearly lack any form of personal hygiene.
110009: You are walking on seemingly endless fields that lead far north. To the south you can see a light forest, and still further the Old East road winds its way west to the Shire, and east to Bree.
110015:
A smiling hobbit child is playing around here.
A brown fox is here, looking for some rabbits to chew up.
You are walking on seemingly endless fields that lead far north. To the south you can see a light forest, and still further the Old East road winds its way west to the Shire, and east to Bree.
110016: A brown fox is here, looking for some rabbits to chew up.
You are walking on seemingly endless fields that lead far north. To the south you can see a light forest, and still further the Old East road winds its way west to the Shire, and east to Bree.
110034:
A cute young hawk is standing here.
A cute young hawk is standing here.

Much of the inside of the oak has been hollowed out at this level, without killing the tree or disrupting its growth. A number of feathers along with bits of grass and leaves line the bottom of the small chamber. There appears to be a tiny opening further up inside the oak that leads outwards, but it is very narrow.
110035: The corpse of an eel is lying here.

Here the forest floor above forms a natural roof as a small stream flows in from the south beneath the vines and flows north, deeper underground. The dirt is packed with roots affording strength yet effectively blocking out most natural light. To the south, tangled vines drape an opening like a fabric veil. There is just enough solid ground next to the stream to walk safely without slipping.
110036: From the south, a thin stream flows in to create a small underground lake. On the edge of the lake, a well-crafted landing has been carved out of dark wood with hand-worked walls and ceiling. The landing has been designed to dock a handful of smaller boats. In the east wall, an iron-reinforced door looks daunting as it blocks a tunnel opening.
110037:
A sturdy crate made of nailed wooden planks sits on the floor.
An experienced smuggler is here, conspiring with his cohorts.
A smuggler is here, angry at having been seen.
A thug is here waiting for his prey.

Dense, packed dirt provides solid footing on a floor littered with crushed bottles, crates, and other junk. A lit brass lantern is mounted securely on thick beams of dark wood embedded into the walls. A narrow pipe runs upwards through the natural roof, providing fresh air into the tunnel. The burrow expands further to the north and east, whereas a solid-looking door blocks a doorway to the west. Rows of boxes and shelves line the southern wall.
110038:
A small barrel made of aged oak and strong iron hoops stands here.
A water barrel has been left here.

This space is irregularly-shaped like most naturally-formed caverns. However, the smooth walls and floor betray the work of skilled hands. Hairy roots poke through the ceiling from above indicating trees or other vegetation overhead. Several wooden crates and barrels line the eastern and southern walls.
110039:
A small barrel stands on the ground.
A sturdy crate made of nailed wooden planks sits on the floor.
A sturdy crate made of nailed wooden planks sits on the floor.

Mouldy planks form rows of simple shelves along the walls of this confined depository. Sturdy wooden beams, installed to keep the ceiling from collapsing, anchor the planks upright. There is a small air shaft covered in cobwebs between the beams. A fairly flat, well-made stone floor is covered with a thick layer of dust. Some shelves have rotted and fallen down, spilling their contents carelessly.
110040: On the ground, there are three round stones.

Narrow paths run between rows of barrels, chests, and crates that seem to be ducking under a very low ceiling that is criss-crossed by beams of wood installed to prevent the earth above from collapsing. Above, a one foot wide round shaft rises through the soil providing natural light and fresh air to the burrow. Large, flat stones tile the floor up to a sturdy door in the north wall. Through a small opening to the west, a tiny earth cave is visible. A large storage chamber can be seen through the eastern wall.
110041: A wooden club is on the ground.

Dark, moist earth forms the walls, floor and ceiling of this passageway. It travels east where it seems to open up into a larger cave. Plenty of footprints can be spotted in the wet earth, tracking between the tunnel opening in the east and up to a small pile of boulders high along the northern wall.
110042:
A large bookshelf sits against the wall.
On the bookshelf, there is a bag of cinnamon.
A beer mug is here.
A ruffian is sneaking around here, looking for some mischief to do.
A ruffian is sneaking around here, looking for some mischief to do.
The chief of smugglers is here, planning his next move.
A thief is here looking for some stranger to rob.
A thief is here looking for some stranger to rob.

This small room might be an office; however, it is in disarray. A table of dark wood and several crude chairs are toppled, broken and scattered about in the room. A lantern, mounted high on a peg in the eastern wall, flickers with faint light.
110049:
A fat rabbit is here, chewing on some grass.
A restless rabbit bounces around.

The sides of the hills here are the only possible routes one can travel. Rocks and trees soon make climbing to the top impossible. A rocky outcropping blocks the passage to the south and west here, blocking the stream that flows below.
110050: Some small rocks have been piled into a mound here.

Small rocks dominate the ground of the hill here and overgrown weeds climb around small boulders alongside the stream to the south. The bank of the water here is too steep to climb in either direction. The hills continue to the east and west, and quickly the forest at the base of the hills becomes too dense to see through.
110054:
A wooden chest stands in the corner.
A tiny spider is here, eating a tiny bug.
A tiny spider is here, eating a tiny bug.
A tiny spider is here, eating a tiny bug.

This tight space is a tiny chamber cut out from hard, rocky soil. Small niches dug into the northern, eastern, and southern walls look as if they were intended to hold items of value though most are empty now. The western wall is made of heavy wooden planks covered in putrid fungi and mould.
110062: The walls are just a few feet apart only allowing movement in a single file. The air is damp and condenses upon the cold earthen walls, forming tiny riulets that flows down on the floor. There they gather in the shallows creating small puddles. The passageway gets more narrow further north, where it ends with a metal hatch.
110063: The stonewell continues up and down from this point. The top is reachable, and about ten feet down there is a ledge that might be able to support a person. There is a slight draft coming from the bottom of the well, with a scent of decay, and any sound echoes back much stronger.
110064: The corpse of a hobwill is lying here.

The dark tunnel twists and turns as it makes its way through the hill. There is a strong draft in the damp and crisp air. Small patches of moss grows on the walls, and lichen is suspended from the ceiling. Any noise echoes of the walls and travels ahead in the tunnel.
110065: A doorwarden stands here ready to obey his master's wishes.

This medium-sized room looks like a mixture between a library, a laboratory and a geographer's workshop. A number of shelves cover the walls, each and every shelf filled with heavy tomes and ancient-looking books, some of them stored in glass boxes apparently to preserve them from exposure. Piles of yellow scrolls and parchments are lying on top of the books. A wooden desk stands in front of the windows. A great part of the desk is covered with a spread-out map of the Misty Mountains east of Rivendell. Some quill pens and vials of ink rest on the map, to force it to stay open, and to be always nearby, available when needed. Other maps hang from the walls, showing places both near and far.
110066: A humble man stands here, ready to help you with your things.

The pleasant warmth of a bright fireplace welcomes all friendly visitors to the house of an Elven wizard, explorer and part-time orc hunter Sarion. A large wooden table, surrounded by chairs, stands in the middle of the room, upon a brightly coloured carpet. In the southwest corner of the room a sofa and a couple of armchairs offer a more comfortable way to rest. A mantelpiece, definitely unusual in its nature, stands beside the inner door. Wide windows on the northern wall offer a staggering view to the Misty Mountains.
110067:
A black, runed sceptre, the token of a King, lies abandoned here.
A humble man stands here, ready to help you with your things.

In a quiet section of Rivendell stands this humble home. While modest in size, the grand views of the valley impress beyond imagination. Flowerbeds surround the windows filling the air with a sweet fragrance. A small bed sits under the south window which frames the cascading waterfall above. On the west wall a simple kitchen lined with cupboards catches the eye. The cupboards are filled with delicate plates and glasses of the highest quality.
110068: A humble man stands here, ready to help you with your things.

This narrow but tall room has been built simultaneously both in ascetic and in luxurious way. There are only few very simple furniture but the decorations around the walls and on above dome are marvelous, hinting about the great skill and lots of time required to create them. Engraved silver plates cover the walls, and between the plates occasional bright dots of mithril shine like stars on the night sky. The corners of the room rise up like pillars which bend towards each other to form a round dome above. A small alcove exists at the backside of the room, with a simple bed for sleeping.
110069: A humble man stands here, ready to help you with your things.

Walls of ivory enclose the serene chamber here, slightly glistening in the dim light. There are four candle holders fastened into every corner of the room; each holding a long, slender candle which emits a delicate light. A bed stands along the northern wall, its hand-crafted woodwork matching the small dresser besides it. The threshold to the balcony stands along the eastern wall, draped with an immense amount of laced ivy.
110070: Hundreds of ivy strands are weaved together along the balcony, draped along all three sides from above. Between the twined strands at a closer glance, one can notice the glossy, ivory rails that form the patio itself, connecting at its base to a matching ivory floor. The ivy is thick in most places and it creates a very secluded and private area to relax within.
110086: The forest forms a surprisingly straight and clear passageway that cuts through the wilderness in north-south direction. Some weeds, smaller bushes and occasional roots cover the ground, while dense shrubs of black willows grow everywhere around, entangled together, reluctant to allow passage forward. Beyond the willows, huge trees of Mirkwood stand in unison, covering everything under the dark canopy.
110087: A huge, venomous tarantula extends her legs to you.

A twisting and narrow pathway exists between an exceptionally dense and bushy cluster of black willow trees. The shadowy and slender bushes have grown around the area, limiting the visibility to minimum, forcing the path to zig-zag back and forth, and making it very hard to tell which way leads to which direction. Grey spider webs have been woven to the branches.
110112: You walk warily on, following the twists and turns of the tiny tunnel. With every step, the smooth mud walls seem to edge ever closer, threatening to close in on you.
110115: At one end you see the circle of light which marks the exit out of these tunnels, and you find yourself heaving a sigh of relief. All your fears and fancies in the depths of these tunnels seem so laughable now. You are still in the Shire, in the old Brockenbores, and the exit is just a few steps away.
110116:
A pair of rigid leather sleeves lies here.
A pair of soft leather boots are on the ground.
A water barrel has been left here.
A Stoor child is playing peacefully here.

This small dwelling is obviously used as the gate-guards' resting place. There are racks on the walls holding small shields and swords. A few pieces of leather armour hang on nearby hooks. Some small shelves hold daily food supplies and a small book or two.
110117:
A large bulletin board, entitled "Clerics' Guild", is mounted here.
A simple wooden chest is here.
Filatior the elven acolyte is here performing sacred ceremonies.

This small but beautiful temple is often visited by the elven residents of this part of Harlond. They come here to relax and to be reminded of the wondrous Valar who await them in Valinor. It is also used by many young elves who wish to enter the healing profession since some minor skills are taught by the priest here.
110118:
A large bookshelf sits against the wall.
A sturdy bed made from solid oak lies here, covered in warm blankets.
A sturdy pack horse is standing here.
A sturdy trained horse is standing here.
A humble man stands here, ready to help you with your things.

In a silent corner of the winding building is a surprisingly spacious abode, perfect for a small bed. The room is decorated sparsely with a handful of maps, many of which are faded and hardly recognisable due to heavy usage. A bookshelf, worn at the edges as if itself had once been read from cover to cover, is the other singular piece of furniture. A tidy and clean atmosphere sets the surroundings. A selection of aged, yet clean rugs, slightly mismatched in colour have been placed carefully across the floor, small areas of pine appearing among the gaps, creating the impression of wooden slats between the fading colours. Cutting across the ceiling is a single bolt of lightning, carved into the granite roof, appearing to lack the deliberate care of the rest of the room.
110119: The stair that winds upwards on the outside ends on a large terrace in the north. The view opens over the vineyards in that direction and finally meets the end of the valley. The floor of the tower is made of soft wood and all around are large flowerpots from which countless plants and vines grow that merge with the building's graceful decorations. The round tower is wide enough to feature two livings, one to the east and one to the west. A small, white stair winds itself upwards towards a third home.
110120: A humble man stands here, ready to help you with your things.

The old wooden floor is strewn by various chemical journals and dusty scrolls. The meagre and rather tasteless furniture coupled with the thousands of pages of chemical journals, stacked on top of an old oak desk alongside numerous laboratory flasks, leads you to believe that the owner is likely not an aspiring architect but rather an acknowledged wizard. A dusty golden harp hangs on the wall, possibly once used to play soothing tunes and provide occasional refuge for an otherwise chemically obsessed mind.
110124: A humble man stands here, ready to help you with your things.

This old dwelling is located inside a dense thicket of entangled vines. It has been decorated with a few simple furnitures, and a magnificient pelt of an elk has been set on the eastern wall. It is hard to tell whether this room is still in regular use; an ancient smell of wood coming from the old furnitures and from the walls suggests no, yet the room is surprisingly tidy and clean, and its air is filled with strange, small sparklings radiating bright light.
110125: A humble man stands here, ready to help you with your things.

A white marble house has been built on a narrow terrace below the Last Homely Home. Undecipherable runes have been carved and painted on all possible surfaces - on walls, on the table, even to the floor. What they all mean remains unknown, even the language is unclear. There is a painting on each wall, each one illustrating the same character. The man in the pictures is in his thirties, dressed in a bright red tunic and has a white frill collar in his neck. He has two white curlies above his ears, otherwise his hair is short and thin. All in all this place creates quite an absurd impression.
110126: Sleeping Alcove above the Soothing River

A large cabinet capable of storing goods is here.
A sturdy bed made from solid oak lies here, covered in warm blankets.

This room is a small and serene sleeping alcove. There is a soft bed, a table, and some cabinets. A peaceful aura of tranquility embeds the whole room, welcoming one to sleep safely or to have a refreshing moment of meditation. Two windows offer a magnificent view towards south and west; one can see statues, cozy houses, and of course the deep valley where the River Bruinen flows.
110127:
A small white fountain is here.
A humble man stands here, ready to help you with your things.
A tall and strong guard is here.

The dimly lit hall, built from solid rock, has a cavernous resemblance. It is elaborately decorated with several coat of arms and precious gems. Torches adorning the walls provide a flickering light, and give the home a warm welcoming quality. Between the torches hang various paintings which alude to the Numenorean ancestry of Arvegil. The largest of the Numenorean paintings hangs over the banquet table, very majestic and immaculate. The Lord of the Hall presides from the throne in the centre of the hall, which is cut from the same rare stone surrounding you.
110128: A humble man stands here, ready to help you with your things.

A large window opens up in the ceiling, allowing sunlight to reflect from the mirrors set up on the walls, efficiently lighting up the den on sunny days. A weapon rack filled with a collection of weapons and memorabilia, likely gathered during the adventures of the houseowner, is set up on one of the walls. On the other side of the room stands a sturdy bed, next to a table cluttered with maps covering every nook of Arda. A grand chair filled with inscribed notes of vile creatures slain by Razputin, sits in the middle of the room. It faces a wall with portrays of the entire bloodline of this mighty dwarf.
110129:
A fallow deer is grazing peacefully here.
A nightingale is here, chirping a sweet melody.

This place in the forest stands out for its ordinarity. Surrounded by a mass of trees which all looks exactly the same, you have completely lost all directional sense. You decide you can either use the sun and the moon as beacons, or just wander randomly on.
110131: You can hear water running through below the plank. Some light from the torches attached to the wall here sneaks into the darkness below to uncover a deserted cavern. Further east you can see how another huge cave stretches out. To the west you can see a mineshaft.
110132:
A dwarven miner is here, digging the hard rock with his pick.
A dwarven miner is here, digging the hard rock with his pick.
You have entered a dwarven mine. This mine is in working order and you can spot metal tracks ending up here. The cave is well-lit by torches attached to the walls. The only exit is back west.
110143:
A sign reading, Building Permit Information, is here.
A large bulletin board, entitled "Legendhomes", is mounted here.
A Hobbit valet stands here faithfully, keeping the office in order.

Upon the white walls of this small office are a variety of maps. Some look to be topographical; others seem to show land ownership and easements. A large table with over a dozen chairs sits at the centre of the room. The table and chairs fill up so much of the room that there is barely a foot between the chair backs and the map-covered walls.
110144: A wealthy hobbit merchant stands behind the counter, greeting you.

This room is cluttered beyond belief. On every wall a thousand things are hung, and on every shelf and desk another hundred lie. Hanging from the ceiling is a curious device, boasting three red balls. Behind the counter, some of the more valuable goods are kept.
110145:
A small white fountain is here.
A doorwarden stands here ready to obey his master's wishes.
A tall and strong guard is here.
A tall and strong guard is here.

The old and ragged walls of this room are composed of packed dirt, some of which falls to the ground from time to time only to be trampled by the countless members of a hairfooted society. In one corner of the room is a mound of rubbish that appears to have been collected for quite a period of time. While much of the rubbish is inorganic, an odor is still emitted from the pile that would make any elf gag. To the west and north rooms with better lighting and more appealing content can be found.
110146:
A large stone fireplace with a roaring fire warms the room.
A Hobbit valet stands here faithfully, keeping the home in order.
A tall and strong guard is here.

This room is the cleanest and most tranquil in the house. In the east corner of the room there is a dresser that contains an assortment of boxes and trinkets. In the centre of the back wall one of Tolman's dagger has been mounted. This particular dagger is from his better days of battle and adventure. In the westernmost part of the room, a man size bed has been placed, awaiting all those who are willing to risk the comfort of this rich hobbit.
110147:
A beer barrel has been left here.
A small oaken table has been set here.
On the table, there are two loaves of bread.
A tall and strong guard is here.

This room is scented with the wonderful makings from a hobbit's feast and the after dinner smoke of mauve petals. Roast mutton and biscuits, libation and mauve, the warmth of the glowing lights, all contribute to an atmosphere of delight and perpetual relaxation. Glorious feast must be held here! Candles and lanterns, when lit, set this room afire with the glow of a thousand fireflys. Were it not for the window to the west, which allows some of the light to escape, one might be blinded by the intensity of the lights. In the middle of this room is a grand table made from the stumps of several large oak trees. Around this table there are six wooden chairs, crafted by Tolman himself.
110148: A humble man stands here, ready to help you with your things.

This room is made of grey stones and beautiful, dark-brown wood. It has a peaceful, yet mysterious athmosphere, created by a magical aura that is faintly shimmering on all surfaces. There is a painting of a great wizard on one of the walls - Sylvari himself performing some strange incantations. Bookshelves have been stacked from the floor to the ceiling with scrolls and old books. Their strange, arcane look suggests that many of them are enchanted, or even cursed, making it very unwise to touch anything.
110149: In front of you, you notice a pile of old tree trunks. There seems to be no more woods in this part of the region; green bushes spread overall.
110151: A doorwarden stands here ready to obey his master's wishes.

This room has obviously just been dug directly out of the ground. The walls and ceiling have been rubbed incredibly smooth. This room was built for someone of short stature, as the ceiling is only 4 feet high. Earthen tunnels continue to the East and West.
110152: A large bookshelf sits against the wall.

This room is made for visiting. The walls, once again, are dug out of the earth and rubbed incredibly smooth. Several sitting areas are scattered around, where visitors can sit and share stories of their journeys.
110153: A humble man stands here, ready to help you with your things.

This room is hardly more than a depression in the dirt. Plush pillows are laid out for sleeping. A soft glow eminates from a tiny banked fire in the corner. The walls of smooth dirt reflect earthy colours in the light and sooth the senses.
110154: A humble man stands here, ready to help you with your things.

This room is small and simply furnished, in the fashion of the wood elves. There is a variety of house plants arranged under the tall windows, most of which do not grow in the hidden vale. Crowding the windows, the plants give the abode a wild appearance. The back of the room has a massive tree as a part of the foundation. The trunk of the tree is lined with deep recesses in its bark, which are being used as shelves, now filled with books on a variety of magical and mundane topics. Instead of a bed, a soft silk hammock hangs in one corner, with a large pillow undearneath it, acting like a bed for a dog.
110155: A desk, propped up at one end by a couple of elf skulls, marks the centre of the room. A beaten old chair made of genuine warghide is the room's only other furniture. A handful of rocks, a severed humanoid hand, and a heavy club serve as paperweights. The foreman is obviously an orc who spends most of his time out of the office. A huge box labeled 'IN' contains a handful of elf ears. The office looks to have been abandoned for a while.
110156: The Bottom Floor of the Tower
A tall and strong guard is here.

There are no walls separating the different sections of this floor. Instead it all molds into a pleasant blend of comfort and function. An iron stove stands against the wall in the northwest corner of the tower, not far from the simple yet elegant dining table, large enough for several guests. On the opposing side stands a row of bookshelves, skillfully crafted to fit the curve of the wall. Between the stove and the two armchairs resting on a red carpet below the shelves, an open fireplace provides some light to the windowless room. A large spiral staircase leads up to the second floor of the tower.
110157: A pack horse (ulo) is standing here, ridden by you.

The road is wide and hard-packed from many travellers over the centuries. Sets of wheel tracks have carved deep ruts on both sides of the path, the legacy of countless wagons and coaches that have traversed it. Brown dust covers the rocks and pebbles found along the edge of the roadway. A wooded area can be seen to the east.
110158: This quiet forest area stands at the base of an escarpment. One particularly large tree dominates the landscape, a ruined old ladder clinging to its mossy bark. Hundreds of smaller trees cluster around it, as if paying homage to their lord. The Greenway can be seen to the west, stretching its course to Bree and Tharbad.
110159: A pack horse (ulo) is standing here, ridden by you.

The downs stretch away far to the south, extending in long lines of stony ridges divided from one another by sloping valleys. Thin grass and wildflowers cover most of the bedrock here, but several patches of bare stone push their way through the thin layer of soil. At the bottom of the slope to the west, a narrow brown line traces its way through a sea of green.
110160:
A grey wolf is here, thin from starvation.
A pack horse (ulo) is standing here, ridden by you.

This large road has a surface of choking dust. The hard-packed soil of the road bears the tracks of many hooves and feet. Deep ruts have been dug into this road by the passage of coaches and wagons over many years. The land rises to the east, leading towards a grassy hill. The road continues its nearly straight path to the north and south.
110161:
A huge, black wolf is here, ready to devour.
A pack horse (ulo) is standing here, ridden by you.

The wide rutted road runs straight north and south here. The soil is hard and bare after the passage of thousands of coaches and wagons. Two sets of wheel tracks run each way on the road, obviously formed after ages of traffic. The road is bordered by a ridge of grassy hills to the east.
110162: The Greenway extends both north, leading to the somewhat civilised community of Bree, and south, leading into lands far wilder. The road is wider than many, but still barely enough for two wagons to pass one another. Short, thick grass lines either side of the road, though that nearest it is painted in brown dust. A line of cultivated shrubs has been planted west of the road.
110163: The wide, dusty road bends east and north here. The soil is hard and bare after the passage of thousands of travellers. Deep wheel ruts bend in an impressive curve through the grassy plains. A line of cultivated shrubs has been planted along the western side of the road, but to the south they appear to have grown wild.
110165:
A small cluster of clover grows here.
A pack horse (ulo) is standing here, ridden by you.

The forest here is primarily composed of younger trees, with only a few older giants towering above their lesser kin. The narrow trunks stand close to one another, making movement difficult, but the canopy created by their branches is not dense enough to block out the sky. The trees give way to a solid thicket of bushes to the north and east, blocking any travel in those directions.
110166: A pack horse (ulo) is standing here, ridden by you.

A gentle slope leads eastward into a valley containing rocky fields. The rich vegetation of shrubs, bushes and grass lead upwards to a ridge of hills to the west. An abundance of flowers can be seen growing toward the eastern end of the downs: pale blue bellflowers, yellow pimpernels, pink knotweed, and countless others.
110167: A pack horse (ulo) is standing here, ridden by you.

This ridge is not the tallest in the South Downs, but nevertheless it towers over the narrow roadway visible to the west. A steep bank descends toward the road, its surface littered with loose and broken rocks. Only a few stunted trees manage to cling to the slope. Eastward, the hill drops at a much gentler incline that is liberally coated in grass and wildflowers.
110168: A pack horse (ulo) is standing here, ridden by you.

Burgeoning vegetation spreads across the plains within this valley. Flowers are in bloom all across the terrain, thriving in a wide array of both colour and size. A long slope begins to rise out of the valley toward the grassy downs to the west. Rolling fields continue in every direction.
110169: A pack horse (ulo) is standing here, ridden by you.

Thousands of small bushes dot this area, most no more than two to three feet in height. They resemble an enormous herd of green sheep grazing on the short, fertile grass that grows between them. The bushes become denser to the north and west, bunching closer together until they form an impenetrable barrier.
110170: A pack horse (ulo) is standing here, ridden by you.

Signs of erosion can be seen here as rocks lead up a steep slope to a ridgeline to the east. This rocky outcropping is covered in grass and a few small bushes grow amongst the stones. Massive boulders lie at the base of the slope, circled by smaller chunks and fragments of rock. The land gradually rises to the west, leading to an overgrown grassy field. A small house sits just to the north.
110172: A pack horse (ulo) is standing here, ridden by you.

The ground here is firm and level. The valley floor itself consists of layers of sedimentary rock that have been exposed over many years of erosion. Grass and small bushes can be seen growing amidst the rocky terrain. Some trees can be seen to the south, while the plains to the west grow wild with flowers.

A narrow valley cuts into a high scarp that overlooks it from the east. The valley floor is itself very flat, but it is flanked by high cliffs which exhibit layers of white and brown chalk. A dense growth of shrubs, bushes and other plants grow at the eastern end of the valley.

A dense, tangled forest begins here and stretches out toward the east, becoming denser as it goes. Oaks, maples, and beeches dominate the area, creating a thick but incomplete canopy overhead. A number of saplings have sprung up in the areas where sunlight manages to reach the ground, pushing their way toward the sky. A thick layer of dead leaves coats the land, muffling sounds.

Saplings can be seen sprouting up in the green grass that cover this field, but none has yet managed to grow above a few feet in height. Small, thick shrubs and perennial flowers grow in abundance throughout this valley. Just to the east, the dark wall of a small forest can be seen, while rolling fields extend in other directions.

Green sloping downs lead eastward into a rich green valley of blooming flowers and shrubs. Thick, wide-bladed grass fills the gaps between the other plants, gradually becoming dominant near the base of the slope. Beyond the fields, some saplings can be seen sprouting up in a sparse coppice. The slope rises to the southwest until it meets a long ridge.

This area seems to be particularly fertile, as it is covered in a wide variety of vegetation. Several species of bushes and shrubs can be see, along with a great deal of grass and wildflowers. Even a few plum trees have managed to take root here. The land slopes upward toward a line of hills to the west.

The grass in this valley grows in thick, dense layers, the living green shoots barely able to push their way through the tangle of dead blades. The grass hides holes and dips in the land, adding hazard to travelling through the area. A few thorny bushes are scattered around the valley, becoming denser and taller as they near a forest to the east.
110179: A pack horse (ulo) is standing here, ridden by you.

The cycle of life is well-illustrated in the generations of trees that populate this forest. Tall, stately oak and beeches oversee dense thickets of younger trees. Vibrant green saplings cluster around an uprooted elderly tree, whose death leaves room for the younger generation.
110180: A precipitous escarpment offers a striking view of undulating, wavelike downs that face the western horizon. This ridge, like those of the downs that flank it, runs northeast-to-southwest, rising and falling along its way. Though the western slope is steep and littered with rock, the top is smooth and covered in short, soft grass.
110182: A pack horse (ulo) is standing here, ridden by you.

This ridge descends eastward into a valley of grass with a small bosk. To the west the hill angles sharply, sloping downward to a grassy field. The hills lead off to the northwest and the southeast, a rocky divide between valleys. Years of weather and erosion have smoothed the walls of the escarpment, leaving them impossible to descend.
110183: A pack horse (ulo) is standing here, ridden by you.

These hills dip east to a backslope that leads into a grassy ravine. To the west, a steep escarpment descends toward a wide and dusty road. The hills lead off to the northwest and the southeast, a green and rocky divide between two long valleys. Little grass manages to grow here, but there is an abundance of weeds.

Great stretches of grassland fill the level bottom of a valley between ridges of downs. Tall, flaxen grass stalks grow out of a soft, reddish-brown soil, stretching their flowering heads upward to the sky. Scattered oaks and pines provide patches of shade; to the north, these trees grow more densely in a forest where the blanket of tall grass fades to tufts, which there mingle with leafy ferns.
110186: High, yellow-brown grass grows around old stumps that litter a field just south of a forest's edge. Lichen and moss blanket the sides of the stumps, whose cores are now hollow from decay. A jagged, grey line of rock several miles to the east indicates a high ridge of the downs.
110187: The ground dips in a narrow trough where a gentle slope descending from the west meets a rocky incline belonging to a high ridge that looms to the east. This shallow trench is filled with rock and gravel which has gathered there after falling from the eastern slope. The grass that grows here is short and pale, in stark contrast to the taller variety that grows in the fields that stretch away westward.
110188: Atop a Cliff Overlooking a Forest

A sheer slope layered in sandstone, shale, and chalk falls away westward from the apex of a high ridge. The exposed chalk is a brilliant white, a stark contrast to gentler slopes both north and south where vegetation obscures the underlying rock. The top of the ridge is covered in waves of tall grass. The abrupt drop off to the west leads to a forest filled with aged trees.
110189: A pack horse (ulo) is standing here, ridden by you.

Tall brown grass thrives on a gentle slope that stretches eastward from one of this region's high escarpments. The long stalks bear yellow flowers and clumps of hard, black seeds. The wispy tips of the stalks bend before the slightest breeze; gusts can be traced through the rippling waves sent sweeping across the grassland.

Yard-high fields of grass seem to stretch in every direction without end. The ground slopes slightly upward to the north, eventually falling off as an abrupt cliff, hidden by the tall dense grass which perpetuates the illusion that the field extends in that direction. The cliff forms one wall of a narrow valley whose bed lies several dozen yards below.
110191: Clustered shrubs occupy a low valley between two ridgelines to the east and west. Tall grass fills the spaces between shrubs, and scattered wildflowers add touches of purple and red to the green expanse. Directly to the east, a narrow valley cuts downward, splitting a tall escarpment.

A steep escarpment cuts across a forest, separating a grove of young oaks at the top of this slope from their more elderly kin who reign at the bottom. The tallest trees are scarcely more than three yards in height, and their slender trunks are only a few inches thick. Green, leafy ferns thrive in the open spaces between the youthful oaks.
110193: A pack horse (ulo) is standing here, ridden by you.

Dozens of oaks line the edge of a steep escarpment, gazing westward over a broad valley. These oaks are tall and broad; they appear to have aged in peace for many years. A dark-green murk to the southwest belies a forest that fills the valley there, while a broad meadow stretches to the east.

Swathes of yellow, red, and purple intermingle across a fertile valley. Bees and birds hover over the bountiful blooms, harvesting their stored nectar. These vibrant, busy fields come to an abrupt end where a steep cliff of red and orange sandstone topped with ghostly chalk rears up to the east.
110202:
A worm is here slithering around.

Dense shrubs and squat trees line the gentle slopes of a fertile valley that carves its way between two cliffs. The centre is covered in gravel and small stones, remnants of a long-dry stream. Tufts of grass poke upward through this rocky soil, obscuring it with splotches of green.
110225:

A small mushroom grows nearby.

This forest is filled with aged trees stooped from centuries of growth. Soft, fuzzy moss covers the gnarled trunks, as if it were a blanket sheltering them from the cold. Part of a large branch has broken off from one of the trees; still attached, it leans against the tree like a cane supporting it in its old age. Colourful mushrooms spring up between the crooked roots of the trees.
110226: A small, dense tangle of roots covers the ground.

Tall, aged oaks rise out of a thick carpet of grass, fallen leaves, and ferns. Thick webs of roots stretch across the ground, supporting the stately stature of the oaks. Nests and burrows hide in earth-packed hollows beneath these roots, which protect them from weather and the rummaging of large predators. High above the floor, the mighty boughs of the oaks intertwine to cast the forest in shadow.
110227: The wide and dusty road takes yet another bend here, going west and south through the grassy plains. Coarse, grey-green grass lines either side of the roadway. It has been cropped short in many spots, perhaps by horses taking a rest here before being driven or ridden onward. A long, low escarpment lies to the northeast, one of many found in the South Downs.
110228: A pack horse (ulo) is standing here, ridden by you.

A steep stony face leads up toward an eroding ridge that flanks this area on the northeast. Grass covers much of the land here, replaced in spots by a few shrubs and flowers growing between the rocks. The terrain begins to level out toward the southwest, leading to the curving swath of a wide and dusty road.
110229: Despite the hard, packed surface on this road, a few weeds have managed to take hold in the stony terrain giving the road an unusual, mottled effect. Open pastures border the eastern edge of the road while to the west thorny bushes with wickedly sharp barbs grow along the edge of a shallow ravine.

Acres of lush, fertile grassland lie all around. Small hillocks rise up from the otherwise flat ground with the occasional shrub the only other break in the grassy monotony. In places some of the grass has become trampled indicating recent animal activity.
110231: An abrupt slope leads north-east toward the ridge of hills in this area. The grassy surroundings feature a few shrubs and flowers growing between the rocks. 110232: Thick, tangled thorn bushes and woody-stemmed shrubs flourish in the rich, dark soil that lines this shallow ravine. A few scrawny berries adorn the larger shrubs but getting to them to pick the fruit would be tricky. The briars seem to have overwhelmed the neat hedgerow that once lined the road to the east, turning the decorative vegetation into an imposing obstacle. It should be possible to find a route through the brambles to the south.
110233: A variety of thorny bushes have engulfed this valley having seemingly grown unrestrained for many years. Growing so closely together, the bushes have become entwined, forming an unbroken mesh that prevents any passage to the east or west. The very bottom of the north-south valley is lined with patches of wild grasses.
110234: A bear is here, covered with coarse black fur.

Steep banks, lined with devilishly sharp thorn bushes, surround this narrow, secluded valley. It would take many hours and specialised tools to clear the brambles that run rampant here. The only easy route runs from north to south along the base of the depression where shallow puddles have collected and cannot drain away.
110235: At the lowest point this narrow valley opens out into a marshy depression where the heavy vegetation of the surrounding areas gives way to islands of massive thornbushes surrounded by watery mud. Atop the steep bank to the east, masses of briars twist and contort until they form an impenetrable barrier.
110236: Some roots lie here waiting to ensnare weary travellers.

Upon the uneven ground a great tangle of thorns has taken hold, strangling the life out of any smaller shrub that tries to grow. Their thick, twisted limbs do not block out all of the light, but create a dappled effect at ground level. Small animals seem to thrive in the safe haven the thorns provide, protecting the vulnerable creatures from circling birds. To the north the ground slopes away into a steep-sided hollow while to the east the vegetation opens out onto the Greenway.
110243: A swarm of hornets is coming out of its nest.

The majority of the field is covered with a rich blanket of grass interspersed with small shrubs that have been chewed by passing wildlife. Tracks of various animals have been left in the soft soil and several of these tracks disappear though a narrow gap in the hedge to the west.
110244: The Greenway lives up to its name here as it runs straight and true between two thick, green hedges. To the west a dense tangle of bushes run along the edge of a steeply sloping ditch while the smaller shrubs bordering the road to the east separate the highway from the flat, grassy fields beyond.
110245: To the east, a narrow trail climbs up the side of the ridge, snaking back and forth as it seeks out the easiest route to the top. Underfoot, small stones stick out among the thin grass, providing a habitat for all manner of buzzing insects. To the west grass reigns, spreading like a carpet over the earth.
110246: In the shadow of hills that loom high above in the north and east, a solitary tree grows tall and proud. Its presence here is an anomaly, but presumably the result of a single seed having been deposited by a bird and surviving against the odds. Surrounding the tree a sea of tall grass carpets the land, fading away to barren rock as the ground rises up to the escarpment to the east.
110247: This stretch of the Greenway runs directly from the north to the south. The road surface is wide, but dense, thorny bushes growing on the western edge have encroached over the road, forcing passing wagons to slow as they negotiate the obstacle. A carefully built dyke lines the eastern edge dividing the busy road from the farmland beyond.
110248: The road here is pitted with holes, ruts, and cracks in the hard ground, most likely damage caused by wagon wheels. A narrow opening in the thorn bushes to the west seems to lead to a narrow valley while the face of a hillside rises almost vertically to the east. Despite the sheer, rocky surface, the hill is covered in greenery.

The hard, bare soil of the road bears the marks of many passing wheels. Deep ruts along the middle of the road are parallelled by more ruts, perhaps where wagon drivers have tried to avoid the worst parts of the road. Weeds and small shrubs grow alongside the road, but are kept at bay from the road's surface.
110258: A gentle slope descends from a high ridge to the west. The vegetation that blankets this slope is lush and fertile. Clumps of cowslips peek above thick grasses, dotting the slope with brilliant patches of yellow. The soil is soft, and its colour is a rich and fertile black.
110261: A field mouse noses about hungrily, searching for food.

The lowest point of a valley stretches north to south in the shadow of a steep escarpment to the east. The terrain swells gently to another ridge several miles to the west. Clusters of wildflowers thrive here: sunny cowslips, violet rampion, and red-and-white orchids.
110263: Steep slopes flank a narrow valley that descends from west to east. Swathes of reddish brown trace clay and sandstone layers exposed by long ages of erosion. The valley floor is covered in brambles and thistles growing on thin, ochre soil that is mixed with stones and pebbles. A few scattered pine trees grow in this infertile ground, their squat and spindly stature a testimony to their struggle.
110264: Great, rolling plains lie before you, the ground rising and falling as it passes between the two prominent hills to the northeast and southwest. In the east, the grassland fades away to become rough, stony plains. Tulips and other bulbous flowers grow here between rabbit holes, and faint tracks, perhaps made by foxes, circle the holes.
110265: Yellow flowers, with grey-green foliage, grow in clusters here.

Vegetation flourishes here. Yellow buttercups cluster together at the base of the dyke that runs along the western edge of the field, as if huddling out of the wind, while daisies spread themselves out on the thick carpet of lush grass. The southern edge of the field slopes steeply, rising to form one of the many hills in the South Downs.
110266:
An apple tree with bright green leaves grows here.

A vast field covered by grass and wildflowers reaches away in all directions, although to the west the horizon is dominated by a rocky ridge. Quite a few pebbles and some larger stones litter the field and among them grow prickly shrubs and small thorn bushes. A few wisps of fur caught on the thorns give proof of wild animals passing through here from time to time.

From the top of the downs you can see the land rolling out to the north and east over rich, fertile grassland until it reaches a rocky ridgeline on the horizon. To the south the downs rise and fall in austere splendour, devoid of flora, bleak and forbidding. To the west the Greenway cuts through the land, leaving a wide, straight scar on the landscape.
110268: Rising high above the surrounding plains, this hill offers fresh, clean air and a commanding view of the surrounding landscape. Underfoot the ground is stony with little vegetation clinging to the peak. To the east the hills flatten totally and turn into a wide expanse of grass, while the Greenway and its passing traffic flanks the hill to the west.

A number of worn etchings can be seen; it appears that someone carved initials into the wood some years ago. Scraps of cloth and pieces of wood lie abandoned on the platform, and a piece of metal glitters where it has gotten stuck beneath two planks. Thick branches surround the platform, preventing you from seeing much of the landscape beyond.

Instead of the familiar green colours that are found elsewhere in this region, this field is unusual because it has been graced with patches of colourful blossoms. At some point in the past a fire must have burned here, clearing away large areas of grass and allowing wildflower seeds to prosper.

Cracks and fissures riddle the ridgeline, some so small that they are barely visible, others of sufficient size to swallow an unwary hobbit, or even a man.

Patchworks of colours and textures fill this area. Some of the grass has grown long and some has been cropped short where grazing animals have had their fill. To the south the ridge continues but is badly eroded and care must be taken to avoid slipping on the loose scree. There are some scattered weeds fighting for a meagre existence amid the rubble, but very little other fauna survives in this rocky terrain.

The land falls away in a sweeping slope toward the northeast, while a ridge rises to the southeast. The slope becomes less pronounced to the east.

Scattered bushes nestle in low-lying areas and appear to be hunched down to the ground, perhaps to avoid the strong winds that often stream down the slope.

Tall grass flourishes amongst the rocks, interspersed by a wide variety of colourful wildflowers. Cultivated land and a couple of large buildings are visible to the south.

This farm is quite sizeable, covering well over a hundred acres, and must be tended by several people. The land is planted in wheat and oats, which seem to thrive in the rich soil. The fields are bordered on the east by a barn and to the south by a large house. A small area is fenced off next to the barn, no doubt intended to hold animals of some sort, but it is currently empty.

The ground is uneven, pierced in many places by upthrusts of bare stone in a wide range of brown, orange, and dusky yellow hues. The eastern side of the hill is also quite steep at first, but becomes much shallower after a quarter mile or so. A few stunted bushes cling to the hilltop, fighting to maintain their grip against the winds that sometimes scour this landscape.

The South Downs stretch out in every direction in long ridges and wide valleys. This ridge continues both to the northwest and southeast for many miles. A few short pine trees have driven their roots into cracks in the rock and stand as silent sentinels over the land.

Lush, green grass thrives in gently sloping fields which descend from west to east. Elder shrubs, bearing brilliant white flowers, grow in dense clumps dotting the slopes.

The hillside here slopes gently downward from southwest to northeast. Thick, dark-green grass covers most of the land, but is broken in many places by exposed rocks of deep grey and pale brown. The rocks become less apparent toward the bottom of the slope as the layer of soil thickens.

A low ridgeline runs to the northwest and southeast. This appears to be its lowest point for miles around, as the ridge rises in both directions. The western face of the ridge is very steep and bare of any vegetation, while the eastern slope is much shallower and coated with thick grass. A flowery field can be seen at the base of the ridge.

This ridge in the downs gradually rises as it extends to the south. A steep, nearly vertical scarp drops away to the west, revealing a green valley below but offering no way to reach it. The eastern face also drops quickly, but levels out to a more moderate slope after only a few hundred yards. The ridge is bare of most growth, with only a few thin weeds sprouting from cracks in the rock.

This ridgeline is bare of all vegetation, revealing faded brown stone. It turns gradually eastward as it progresses to the south. The western face of the ridge is steep and fragmenting, allowing no safe passage in that direction. A layer of soil has formed on the shallower eastern face, allowing short grass and tall wildflowers of white and orange to take root.
110322: A pack horse (ulo) is standing here, ridden by you.

The land is nearly flat here, rising only gradually to the west. A tall scarp rises to the northeast, sheltering this area from some of the worst weather. Thick grass coats the ground, interspersed with dandelions and daisies in tiny pools of yellow on a vast green carpet.
110324: A pack horse (ulo) is standing here, ridden by you.

The land levels out into a broad, nearly flat field. Low, thick grass covers most of the area, but it is highlighted by dozens of varieties of flowers in an array of different colours. A tall, bare scarp rises to the north and east. The valley stretches further to the south, while west of here cultivated fields surround a large farmstead.

A rabid rabbit is here, frothing at the mouth.
A badger is here, exploring for food.

A tall, barren hillside rises to the east until it reaches a stony ridgeline. Only a few stunted shrubs cling to cracks in the hillside, which is otherwise clear of any vegetation. Patches of loose rock threaten to come tumbling down at any minute, and a thick layer of scree at the base attests to this happening many times before.
110332: A pack horse (ulo) is standing here, ridden by you.

As the plains extend eastward, they drop further into a deep valley. Here the land rolls in a series of dips and hillocks like rolling waves upon the sea. Emerald grass covers much of the land, broken in spots by stretches of exposed rock. Dozens of isolated trees stand like islands among the grass, mostly oaks and maples. A large farmstead is just north of here.
110343: The ridge runs directly north from here, but bends somewhat to the east as it extends to the south. The ridge is not level, but instead rises and falls in uneven crests and dips, making travel along it more difficult. Only a small amount of grass and weeds are able to find purchase on the otherwise bare stone.

A faint line, no wider than a goat trail, marks an easy route leading down from the hills onto the grassy plateau below. Little vegetation grows on the rocky surface of the ridge other than a few tufts of yellowing grass.
110347: This crest in the downs stretches from northwest to southeast, bending until it points almost due south here. The western face is steep and barren of nearly all vegetation. Several copper and iron cauldrons of various sizes are lined up along the south wall. Above them is another shelf that bears a number of tightly sealed ceramic jugs.
110456:
A dirty shovel is lying on the ground here.
A mouse is here nosing around, looking for a safe place to hide.

This dimly lit barn is filled with the scent of livestock. The livestock is kept in rows of stalls, each of which is large enough for a single animal. Each stall contains a pile of straw for sleeping, a trough for drinking, and a bin for the hay these creatures consume during the winter months. In a corner, manure has been collected for use as fertilizer.
110460: A trained horse (ulo) is standing here, ridden by you.

The land is rockier here than in the grass-covered fields to the north. Small mounds of rocks and gravel rise a few feet above the surrounding plain. Isolated clumps of bushes have found soil to take root in, while the rest of the area is sparsely vegetated. A wall built from stones piled atop each other separates this land from whatever lies to the south.
110461:
A wild bull seems ready to charge you.
A wild bull seems ready to charge you.
A beautiful and docile horse is standing here.
A trained horse (ulo) is standing here, ridden by you.

Dense grass, much of it over five feet tall, covers this field. The ground is uneven and marked with long grooves. Standalone boulders lie here and there. A few bushes grow around these large boulders, making for ideal dens and nests for small animals. A dry stone wall stands to the south, separating these wild fields from the pastures it encloses.
110462: A trained horse (ulo) is standing here, ridden by you.

Suddenly ending at a sheer escarpment dropping away to the west and north, these exposed grasslands offer little shelter. The grasses themselves are low and stunted, grimly clinging to life in the hard soil. A pile of animal bones lies near the edge of the low cliff, and many skulls can be seen.
110463:
A cute rabbit is here.
A trained horse (ulo) is standing here, ridden by you.

The plains here are nestled against a long, low ridge to the east and south. The grass is long and thick, dotted here and there by low shrubs that appear to provide shelter for birds and other small creatures. At the apex of the ridge, a narrow stone tower rises above the plains and hills.
110464:
A fierce boar is here, making grunting noises.
A trained horse (ulo) is standing here, ridden by you.

The land is wild here, with thick grasses and patches of scrub growing to the height of a man's waist. The ground beneath is rocky and uneven, with scattered larger stones. There is no sign of that anyone has tried to civilise this land in many years, if ever. A single pine tree rises above the land, its trunk bent toward the east.
110465: A trained horse (ulo) is standing here, ridden by you.

A carefully-tended field of wheat grows here, its long brown stalks weaving an intricate dance in even the slightest breeze. The ground below is dark brown, nearly black, rich with loam and excellent for nourishing these crops. The field stretches to the north, but seems to be untended there. A small farmhouse sits just to the west.
110466:
A large beautiful rose bush is blooming here.
Deep inside the bush, there is a red rose with leaves and thorny stem.
A trained horse (ulo) is standing here, ridden by you.

The ground slopes quickly down from east to west. Hundreds of widely-scattered bushes dot the landscape, including wild rose bushes, sage, and honeysuckle, filling the air with their scent. A narrow ravine blocks the way to the south, its depths filled with dense, thorny brush, while just to the west a cultivated field is visible.
110467:
A clear spring babbles as cool water trickles out of the ground.
A trained horse (ulo) is standing here, ridden by you.

A low shale rockface rises to the east, ascending nearly fifty feet at its highest, but dropping off to the south. Trickles of water squeeze out from the layers of rock, merging to form a tiny rivulet that gathers into a small pool before disappearing into the grass. Moss clings to the rocks, feasting on the moisture and its abundant load of minerals.
110468: The land slopes down into a shallow bowl here, framed on the east by a towering cliff that rises nearly one hundred feet above the ground. The cliffside is composed of shale, its dark-grey stone laid down in layers aeons ago. The rock is angled, rising to the north. The top of the cliff sticks out several feet, threatening to fall at any time. Several deep crevices cut into the rockface, splitting the already fragile stone.
110469: A trained horse (ulo) is standing here, ridden by you.

A small cliff rises to the east, no more than fifty feet at its highest point here. The ground slopes upward to the north, until it meets the upper lip of the cliff. The exposed rockface is mainly shale deposited in flat layers, but some ancient upthrust has broken it, forming a chevron pointing toward the sky. Despite the steep angle and the loose shale, it may be possible to ascend the cliff.
110470: A sparrow is flapping around on the ground.

High, dense grass covers these undulating plains. Clumps of of bushes grow in small dells and break the monotony of the green ocean. Bypassing these dells makes travelling slow and difficult. Just to the north bushes form a long belt going from the east to the west. Foothills rise to the south-east, as the Tower Hills lie in that direction. There is a well-maintained wooden fence to the west, protecting cornfields beyond it. A small wicket in the fence allows access to the fields beyond the fence.
110471:
A grey wolf is here, salivating profusely.
A grey wolf is here, snarling aggressively.
A black wolf pads restlessly, looking for its next prey.
A black wolf pads restlessly, looking for its next prey.

Dense isolated islands of wide, thorny bushes grow in the high grass that covers these hills. Towards the west they form a wall that looks impenetrable. The land rises further to the south-east, where the foothills become the Tower Hills proper. Tracks of wildlife can be seen in several places and grass and bushes alike show sign of being set upon by herbivores.
110472: A few hills form a narrow ridge slowly rising from north to south. The slopes of these hills are steep and covered with small shrubs. A descent looks to be a feat beyond mere mortals. A narrow, barely visible trail climbs the ridge towards higher peaks to the south. There is a small valley at the foot of the slopes to the west.
110473:
A clear spring babbles as cool water trickles out of the ground.
A stocky mountain mule is here, waiting to serve.

Steep slopes to the east and south create a small valley here. The valley's bottom is covered with grass nurtured by a small creek originating from a spring at the foot of the eastern slope. There is a wooden hut with a bench close to this spring. It is a quiet place where one can rest, if needed. It seems that it is possible to climb the southern slopes up to a low ridge.
110474:
A grey wolf is here, salivating profusely.
A grey wolf is here, snarling aggressively.

Gently rolling plains extend in all directions. High grass covers the ground, suitable as forage for livestock. Someone recently scythed a large area to the west, and a few haystacks stand there. The plains turn into hillocks to the south, and a small valley leads into the foothills of the Tower Hills to the east. A steep, long scarp borders the plains to the north, blocking any way in this direction.
110475: A tall stag is here, grazing peacefully.

Vibrant green grass thrives in these fertile plains. Scattered bundles of hay have been left to dry in the centre of swaths of cleared grass. Shallow wagon ruts lead west, and tracks of livestock lead south into a fenced pasture. A wall of low bushes runs along the northern end of this grassland.
110476: Verdant, level pasture extends for miles in all directions. Immediately to the south there is a small hill. Beyond it to the south and east, the plains begin to undulate as they approach the Tower Hills. The vegetation here is tall, and seems to see little grazing. However, clear swathes cut across the land where grass has been gathered for use as hay.
110477: Green pastures stretch in all directions. The grass is tall and luscious, delicious grazing for wandering livestock. To the west a giant rock slab towers over the grasslands. Alhough it is possible to climb up this side of the rock, it would probably be better to ascend the southern slope, where the side of the rock is not so steep. There is little else to catch the eye in this endless sea of grass.
110478:
A grey wolf is here, salivating profusely.
A grey wolf is here, snarling aggressively.

Endless flat plains extend to the west at the foot of these hillocks, and the horizon to the south-east is dominated by the Tower Hills. The hills are covered with grass, with a few bushes dotting the slopes. A large but lonely pasture to the west, enclosed by a sturdy wooden fence, is the only sign of habitation.
110479: Low hummocks begin to rise out of grassy plains, increasing in height to the south and east. A few bushes grow in shallow vales between the mounds, but grass still covers most of the ground. The grass flourishes, and will no doubt provide excellent grazing for livestock. A steep slope towers to the west, where a ridge ascends to a bluff.
110480:
A brown cow is here, contemplating a higher reality whilst chewing slowly.
A bull stands here, calmly looking around.

A small hill rises from the surrounding plains, providing a clear view of distant features lying beyond the miles of grassland. A fenced pasture lies immediately to the east, with the summits of the Tower Hills forming a distant backdrop. Trampled swaths of grass reveal the paths trod by cattle roving between this hilltop and pastures to the north.
110481: Luscious, green grass carpets the ground, stretching away south and east as far as the eye can see. The rich and fertile soil supports diverse plant life; small clusters of daisies and buttercups grow among the grass. Low mounds covered in brush rise to the west.
110482: A bushy plant grows here, with tall clusters of yellow flowers.

Rolling hills blanketed in brush run from the north to the south where the ground suddenly dips into a small depression. The mounds are high enough so that a clear view of the landscape is only visible from their summits. Paw prints and wolf-droppings suggest that a pack of wolves has moved into this area, feasting on the rodents dwelling in the underbrush as well as livestock in the surrounding pastures.
110483: Meadows at the Foot of a Rocky Ridge

A trail that crosses these meadows ends at the foot of a rising ridge to the north. The ridge is barren and stony; if the travellers who made the trail also regularly ascend the ridge, there is no sign of it. The grass is green and seems to thrive in the wet lowland soil. Flowers aplenty dot the meadow, and the humm and buzz of insects is ever present.
110485:
A wild sheep with a short, greyish coat grazes here.
A colourful butterfly is fluttering around here.
A wild bull seems ready to charge you.

These fields lie in the shadows of hills rising to the southeast. The grassland provides grazing for livestock when adverse weather forces them down from the hills. A fence runs along the northern side of the pasture, perhaps built to protect the grazers of this pasture from the threat of predators. A few patches of white wool are caught in the fence.
110486:
A wild sheep with a short, greyish coat grazes here.
A wild sheep with a short, greyish coat grazes here.
A tall stag is here, grazing peacefully.

The grass grows tall on this gentle slope. The land continues to climb into the hills to the east, and to the west the foot of the slope meets a seemingly endless plain. An animal track is discernible among the grass, leading south along the slope.
110487:
A wild sheep with a short, greyish coat grazes here.
A wild sheep with a short, greyish coat grazes here.
A wild sheep with a short, greyish coat grazes here.
A powerful ram stands here, poised and alert.

Gently rolling pastures stretch in all directions. The grass is kept short by sheep raised in this pasture; they leave telltale piles of dung hidden among the grass. The pasture is enclosed with a sturdy wooden fence. In the northwest corner of this enclosure, there is a small shelter for the herdsmen who tend these sheep.
110488: A simple wooden shelter stands here as a resting place for animals bred in the surrounding pastures. It was built from rough wooden logs and planks, and one of its walls is open to a pasture to the south. An old, hollowed trunk used as a watering trough stands in one of the corners, and a hay rack in another.
110489: Five small, closely spaced hills form a ridge going up to the east. The peaks are round, covered by grass and clumps of bushes. It is possible to ascend the ridge but the slopes to the north and south are steep and covered in gravel. The southern slopes are rocky, unstable and falling down would seem unavoidable if a climb was to be attempted. There is an eroded peak not far to the east towering above the foothills.
110490: A pleasant grassy slope descends from a pass in the hills to the east, towards lower lands in the south-west. To the north the hills are topped by rocky outcroppings, and piles of scree lie broken along their base. A low wall of stone can be seen encircling a paddock to the south.
110491: This narrow pass twists through rugged hills. The northern and eastern walls are covered in loose rocks, making them too treacherous to climb. Judging from the numerous tracks winding between the sides of the gorge, this pass is often used by livestock who live higher up the slopes and graze in the valley when there is an abundance of grass.
110492:
A wild sheep with a short, greyish coat grazes here.
A wild sheep with a short, greyish coat grazes here.

A large wooden shack stands to the south. Its position takes advantage of natural shelter provided by a crag that towers behind it. There are steep, impassable slopes to the east and south, and a fence along the western edge of this field. Open pastures stretch away to the north.
110493: A tall stag is here, grazing peacefully.

This tiny path does not seem to get much use. Southward it leads into a valley wedged into the Tower Hills, while to the north it fades away to be almost indistinguishable from the surrounding terrain. Several animal bones are scattered around here with a sheep's skull lying to the side of the path. Low bushes cover the surrounding slopes and grass prevails as the path goes up into the hills.
110494: The trail widens slightly here as it winds its way along the bottom of a valley. The valley is deep and its slopes too steep to be ascended. Small bushes grow on both sides of the path and they show clear sign of being set upon by grazing animals.
110495: Craggy slopes to the south and west force this narrow valley to bend sharply. A prior landslide has deposited a large number of small stones onto the path making travel difficult. A small bush is wedged between large rocks to the south, barely surviving the rockslide. Next to it, there is a patch of fresh dirt visible beneath one of the piles of rubble. The valley rises to the east, where it terminates at a dead end surrounded with hills.
110496: Much of the headwall to the east has crumbled away and sent huge piles of scree down to the valley below. It is not possible to get a clear view of the bottom without risking a fall. Fortunately, the path to the west seems to offer an easier route. A gully to the north prevents travellers from reaching the peak that lies directly beyond it.
110497: A large rectangular wall has been built here. The walls are made from loose stones that have been carefully arranged to fit together without any gaps. Clearly, this was the work of a skilled hand as the structure has stood the test of time. Moss grows over the stonework yet it is as secure as the day it was completed. A sturdy door protects the contents from wild animals.
110498: Wide-bladed grass carpets the ground underfoot, leaving no trace of the rocks found elsewhere in the Tower Hills. Occasional patches of berry bushes and bunches of flowers provide bursts of colour. In some areas, the bushes are missing leaves and the grass is much shorter, a telltale sign of grazing fauna.
110499:
A grey wolf is here, snarling aggressively.
A large elk gazes coldly at you, chewing on a small branch.

A small tarn surrounded by green grass and small bushes lies at the bottom of a depression in the valley floor. The water is cold, dark and churns into foam in numerous places where streams flow in from surrounding the slopes. Many tracks are imprinted on the banks, showing that a diverse range of wildlife lives here. A rocky hill towers to the west; its eastern slope invites a climb up.
110500: Dislodged boulders and mounds of rubble at the bottom of this valley are clear evidence of a massive landslide. A headwall to the west has collapsed, spreading layers of gravel and scree down the slope. The loose surface provides no traction whatsoever, and climbing that way is impossible. The valley that runs from north to south is far more forgiving for the average traveller.
110501: Densely packed clumps of large bushes break up the grass that dominates this sloping valley. The bushes flourish in the fertile soil and have grown so thick that they block the way in many places. An eroded ridge rises up from the valley to the west and the valley narrows into a pass to the south.
110502: Bushy Grove at the Base of a Rocky Slope

A mottled snake is sneaking here, ready to sink its fangs into flesh.
A grey wolf is here, snarling aggressively.
A grey wolf is here, snarling aggressively.
A large elk is standing here, chewing grass and leaves.
A grey wolf is here, snarling aggressively.
A black wolf pads restlessly, looking for its next prey.
A large eagle soars above you.

Clumps of bushes blanket a small, narrow valley. The valley descends to the west, and is closed in by rocky slopes to the east. Luscious grass and numerous flowers grow among the bushes. The ground is very moist, and sags slightly under any weight. Numerous large rocks broken off from the surrounding slopes have now partially sunk into the damp ground of the valley floor.
110503:
A small oaken table has been set here.
On the table, there are three apple tarts, two large biscuits, two pieces of cheese, a plain leather belt and a torch.

This small hut consists of one main room with a storage space in its rear. The main room is furnished with a wooden table, two chairs, and a simple bed with a pillow and a blanket. A pile of chopped wood sits next to a small fireplace in one corner of the room. The storage space has a large wooden shelf along with a number of hooks.
110505:
The mother wolf stands here, protecting her young cubs.
A huge, black wolf is here, ready to devour.
A wolf cub happily plays here.
A wolf cub happily plays here.
