This den is simply a dark, narrow tunnel hidden under the cover of a cluster of bushes. The walls are solid and dry, and are covered with large claw marks. The tunnel provides shelter against adverse weather conditions, making a secure hideaway for its inhabitants.
110506: Two ridges meet here, coming together to form a rocky, eroded peak. From atop this peak, the entire western countryside, all the way to the gulf of Lhun, is visible. This would be an ideal place to observe the coming and going of others in the fields and hills below.
110507: Rocky dirt, combined with a lack of moisture, makes life very difficult here. The land is almost completely devoid of animals and the only plant life is dry, struggling shrubs with a few insects buzzing around them. The bluff ends in a vertical drop to the north, casting a deep shadow over the orchard at its foot. The slopes to the west and east are steep, but it is possible to climb them with some effort. A long, finger-like ridge descends southward from the bluff to the fields below.
110513: The ground is strewn with rocks and gravel; the only vegetation is tough bushes and a few clumps of struggling trees. The safest way off the ridge would be to follow it until its end; either northward, where it levels out at the top of a bluff, or southward where it descends to merge with the grasslands. However, it is possible to climb down the eastern slope with some effort.
110516: Runoff from nearby hills collects here in small mossy depressions. A coppice of willows has established itself here to take advantage of the abundance of water. There are willows at all stages of development, from venerable old trees with densely intertwined canopies to newly cut stumps with fresh new shoots. Brambles and woodland flowers surround the stumps, soaking up the abundant light. There is a mound of willow logs set up for charcoal burning in a clearing atop an elevated patch of ground.
110517: A black wolf pads restlessly, looking for its next prey.

A small trail winds through meadows covered with grass and clusters of flowers in bloom. Wide rows of tall shrubbery runs across the meadows, following shallow creeks across the fields. Birds are ever present, flitting from bush to bush, and the air is filled with twittering. There is a stone wall to the west around a garden and a small cottage. The Tower Hills rise in low, rugged rows far to the southeast.
110518: White and yellow flowers surround a patch of bushes in the middle of luxuriant grassland. To the south, the ground slopes upward, forming the foothills of the Tower Hills. Fences have been erected to the east, preventing travel in that direction. There is a small, wet depression to the west.
110519: A narrow, grassy valley cuts between two rows of hills that rise steadily to the south. A tall peak rises above the ridge to the west, crowned by a grey stone tower. The fertile land nestled between these heights is remarkably fertile, sustaining abundant wildlife.
110520: A large elk gazes coldly at you, chewing on a small branch.

This hilltop offers a clear, unbroken view of a verdant valley that opens into plains to the northwest, which themselves lead eventually to the faint, shimmering blue of the Gulf of Lhun. A small wooden shelter is tucked under the base of a crag to the north. A faint, narrow path follows a ridge to the south, climbing eventually to reach the top of a towering peak. A gentler ascent to the west descends into a long valley.
110521: A grey stone tower soars atop the summit of this hill, the first significant peak when the range is approached from the west. The tower sits upon a cap of a grey rock overlooking a cliff to the north. The only way down is a steep path to the east or a narrow path following a ridge to the south. To the east and south, the Tower Hills undulate wildly like waves in a storm. Not far to the west, farmland and a small river stretch out below the hills like a carpet. Far to the west the land recedes beneath the blue-grey expanse of the sea.
110522: A prominent mound on the western slope is the only noteworthy feature of this otherwise unremarkable hill. Rocky patches among the heather have been worn smooth by wind and rain. Small bones and scraps of fur on one such bare patch show that birds of prey have been active in the area.
110523: Steep slopes flank a narrow pass, a stark contrast to rolling hills that fall away to the north. A sharp ridgeline climbs to the east, continuing deeper into the Tower Hills. A broad, stable slope descends westward. There is little in the way of vegetation; there are only a few pine trees and patches of yellow grass on the rocky, barren slopes.
110524: Trail through Pine Tree Clad Hills
A large elk is standing here, chewing grass and leaves.

A trail climbs through a pine forest covering the slopes of a hill. The way west is easy as the trail cuts gently across the slope. At the summit of a high hill, the trail turns northward and climbs up a narrow ridge leading up to a peak to the north. There is no viable passage to the south as there is a deep, abrupt crevice in front of a broad, flat-topped hill.
110525: The sides of this rounded hill are steep and rocky. Climbing straight to the top would be very difficult. However, a trail from the farmlands to the north winds gently up the hill, making for an easier ascent to the top. A small fault on the western slope slices open the hill to reveal a steep cliff.
110526: Trail at the Foot of the Hills

Clusters of colourful flowers dot these green fields, and the grass grows wild and tall. A trail comes from the north and splits here. One branch leads southwards where it ascends into the Tower Hills and the other crosses the fields towards a small forested hill to the west. An old tower stands atop a steep hill to the south.
110527: The sound of rushing water from the rapids below is somewhat muffled by a fringe of trees that leans over the steep slope to the west. The slope is slick with water and covered in lichen, liverwort and drooping ferns. Away from the edge, the ground is mostly covered in thin turf, with slabs of white rock forming islands in the sea of green.
110528:
A small oaken table has been set here.
An elven shepherd of indeterminate age assesses you with an inquisitive look.

Haunches of preserved meat hang from the ceiling of this small shack. The only light is from a small window in the western wall. Some faded, threadbare rugs cover the floor. Clearly, this is not the home of a rich person. Jars for herbs and spices line the shelf over a stove.
110529:
A big, nasty vulture is sitting here, protecting its nest.
A big, nasty vulture is sitting here, protecting its nest.

This rocky peak towers thirty yards above the nearby hills. The climb up is reasonably difficult as there are no paths and little traction on the grass-covered slopes. From the summit, there is a clear view of the foothills and plains to the north but higher peaks restrict the view to the west. A green valley cuts from north to south at the base of the hill to the east.
110531:
A wild sheep with a short, greyish coat grazes here.
A wild sheep with a short, greyish coat grazes here.
A wild sheep with a short, greyish coat grazes here.
A wild sheep with a short, greyish coat grazes here.
A powerful ram stands here, poised and alert.

Four sturdy rock walls and a strong wooden gate protect this place from predators. The ground underfoot is muddy and the last remnants of vegetation have been worn or chewed away years ago. Despite the pen having no roof, the smell is strong enough to indicate that it is still in constant use. Dung and hoofprints cover the ground.
110532:
A mountain lioness pads quietly through the terrain.
A mountain lion eyes you closely and prepares to pounce for his next meal.

Heavy erosion has created a shallow cave in the mountainside. The walls are rough, and crumbled pebbles cover the ground. The cave is only a few yards deep and high. Numerous bleached bones and crushed skulls litter the ground near the entrance to the cave. A narrow ledge leads away from the cave, descending to a rocky ridge.
110533: A path runs along the top of the ridgeline that stretches away to the west of here. Erosion has left a steep drop on either side removing any hope of leaving the ridge safely. The ground slopes away to the east where the ridge descends into a wide valley. Bushes and tall grass grow partway up the slope, as if to greet the ridge.
110534: The hills here are heavily eroded, leaving steep and impassable sides to the north and south. Piles of scree lie at the foot of these slopes as testimony to the dangers of attempting a descent. Only a narrow path along the top of the ridge provides safe passage through the area. A few trees grow near the ridge, their crowns almost level with the top of the ridge. To the east, the Tower Hills dominate the horizon.
110535: The route narrows and climbs to the top of a distinct spiny ridgeline twisting through rugged, rocky outcrops. Sparse trees dot the slope to the west, cutting off abruptly where the rising ground exposes this area to the full, unsheltered effects of the weather. Tufts of yellow grass cower among rocks and in small hollows.
110536: The peak here consists mostly of loose talus with a few wisps of grass vying for survival amid the rocks. The lack of soil here has left the area bald and devoid of substantial vegetation, a stark contrast to the fertile valley floor that can be seen in the distance to the northwest. A steep ridge falls away to the north.
110537: The ground here is damp and soft, sinking slightly when tread upon. To the north, the grass has is flattened where prevailing winds sweep around an old grey cottage. A small path wraps around the base of a hill covered with trees. A dense hedge runs along its northern border; a branch of the path leads up to a gate which blends cleanly into the rest of the hedge.
110538: A colourful butterfly is fluttering around here.

A narrow path stretches around a steep riverbank to the east, slowly turning northward and away from the river. The ground around the bank is solid; it is rocky with only a thin layer of soil. Further from the river, the land becomes more fertile, covered with wildly growing grass. Although the path does not continue westward around the bank, many tracks head in this direction.
110539:
A goose waddles around here.
A goose waddles around here.

A path starts at the backdoor of a farmhouse and leads south over farmland. Dry stone walls divide the land into manageable fields. To the north, a long wall runs from the west to the east, enclosing this farmland against the wilder scrubland around it. The cottage is made from large, pale grey stones inset with a number of small windows. The woodwork is old and cracked but has been recently repainted with a coat of blue. Smoke rises from a chimney in the middle of a dark slate roof.
110540: An elven farmer stands here partially hunched over.

Whitewashed walls and a roaring fire give this farmhouse kitchen a rustic but cosy atmosphere. Small windows in the east wall look out over a quaint cottage garden and the kitchen is thick with the smell of the herbs left drying over the fireplace. The flagstone floor is scrupulously scrubbed clean but for the muddy boots by the backdoor.
110541:
A grouping of soft pink flowers radiates a sweet fragrance.
A field lark stands here, focused on finding food.

Dry stone walls border three sides of this garden, protecting it from livestock in the surrounding fields. A small cottage abuts the western side, completing the enclosure. Well-worn cobbled paths wander between plots of flowers and edible plants. A large compost heap and a water trough are tucked away in a corner of the garden.
110542: Corridor through Dense Trees by a Wooden Gate

An elven guard is standing here at his post.
An elven guard is standing here at his post.
An elven guard is standing here at his post.

A wooden gate, reinforced with solid plates of iron, stands between two massive trees. The gate has two iron rings attached to it that can be pulled when it needs to be opened or closed. A corridor through dense walls of vegetation leads towards the south where it arrives at a square. The ground close to the gate is paved with grey stones. A small shelter, with a long bench and table inside, stands under one of the trees.
110543: Mossy Clearing in a Small Ash Grove

A wide variety of moss covers the ground.
A clear spring babbles as cool water trickles out of the ground.
A beautiful and docile horse is standing here.
A colourful butterfly is fluttering around here.
A cute rabbit is here.
A beautiful and docile horse is standing here.

A small circular clearing is surrounded by a wall of tall, lean ash. Soft, lush, and bright green moss covers every surface in the clearing, hiding several large rocks. This moss comes in many varieties which form large mounds several feet wide. This grove is calm and peaceful in its protected isolation. A few tiny trails cut through the forest surrounding the clearing. The foot of a rocky ridge rises to the east.
110544:
A weapons rack stands against the wall.
In the rack are a chain mail coif and a pair of chain mail sleeves.
A large stone fireplace with a roaring fire warms the room.
An elite elven guard is standing here, guarding the peace.
Hrivesur, ancient among the Sindar, is standing here.

A spiral stair leads down from this tower, and a reinforced wooden door at its foot presumably leads outside. The main room is a living place, providing comfort to anyone who wants to stay here. The room is heated with a fireplace built into one wall. Two beds, a table, four chairs, and a wardrobe stand there. Eight windows are placed around the living room and provide an outstanding view to the surroundings.
110545: The upper part of a broad mesa has been heavily eroded, so that it now forms a labyrinth of rock pillars, crevices, arches, and other spectacular shapes. Most of them are nine to eighteen feet high, creating many sheltered crannies where the wind howls. The mesa ends in abrupt slopes to the north and south, while the slopes to the west and east make for gentler descents.
110546: A very large tree branch has been ripped from a tree.

A pebbled beach rises slowly from a shallow river. The beach is roughly twenty yards wide; across the river lies a grass-covered plain. Branches and other debris lie half-hidden under the grass, as the river frequently overflows its bed here before it flows through jagged plains with steeper beaches to the west. In several places, animal tracks lead to and from the river as the riverbed is shallow and easy to ford.
110547: The river slows down as the riverbed widens. Large gravel shoals rise above the river's surface. Some of these sedge-covered islands are surrounded by reeds and seem to be permanent features of the river; excellent places for birds to build their nests. It is possible to ford the river if care is taken to avoid deeper pools. The river's flow quickens to the west where it enters a narrow valley.
110548: This beach is covered in smooth pebbles deposited here by the river. Larger rocks among the pebbles come in many different colours and sizes. Near the centre of the river, a long shoal covered in sedge rises up to the level of the beach. Further east, the bank becomes steep and high where the river bends.
110549:
A sturdy pack horse is standing here.
A goose waddles around here.
A goose waddles around here.

Dry stone walls enclose this small pasture, separating it from the wilder lands to the north and west. There the ground rises and becomes stony and unproductive. The grass here was once vigorous but is now almost bald from over-grazing. In places the ground has become dusty and riddled with hoof marks. A large pile of hay has been set down near the centre of the pasture; stray strands have been strewn about as horses have pulled at its contents.
110550: The terrain drops away to the west below a long ridge that extends northward. To the south, a small river canyon can be seen, the sheer sides offering no path down. The lands here are jagged and broken as though they underwent some ancient upheaval of catastrophic proportions. As it spreads to the east, the ground levels out into a wide, grassy field.
110551: Many rocky gullies cross the grasslands, running east and west. Bushes running along their edges mark them clearly. The terrain is broken by occasional boulders resting in the grass, and these too are surrounded by low scrub. A wide promontory extends out to the west, protruding from a long ridgeline that runs north and south. A wall of stones separates the plains from an enclosure to the east.
110552: This rocky promontory extends out from the ridge in the east, overlooking the broken plains. A huge stone formation stands here, with ancient, crumbling stairs leading upwards carved into its side. Below, strangely regular lines of stone can be seen amid the grasses, and a tiny goat trail leads down the sheer face towards them.
110553: A few crumbling remains of antediluvian walls can be seen peeking above the soil here. Grasses grow among and atop them, as though seeking to pull them back beneath the surface, returning these lands to the wild. No other signs remain of those who built the walls that once stood here.
110554: Low, tough grass and tall, spiky weeds cover the ground, though in many spots patches of stony soil or bare rock are visible. The exposed stone is mainly orange-brown sandstone or grey shale. The ground rises to the east, but drops off in every other direction. Just to the south, a stream thunders and roars through a narrow canyon.
110555: A brown cow is here, contemplating a higher reality whilst chewing slowly.

This meadow runs between a wooden fence to the north and a stone wall to the south. The grass is moderately tall and very lush, its colour a deep emerald hue. The grass is dotted with thousands of buttercups, daisies, and dandelions, their yellow blooms looking like golden coins scattered across a carpet of green.
110556: Overall fairly flat, this meadow slopes gradually down from the east to the west. The soil is thick and rich in many places, but stones break through the surface in others. Emerald green grass stands a foot or more high, hiding many stones from sight, and making travel somewhat hazardous for the unwary. Several miles to the west, the Gulf of Lhun is visible. A tall stone fence blocks the way to the south.
110558: This land once stood as a broad hill, but is now truncated by the river that flows to the south and west. The water has cut deeply into the hillsides, until the rock beneath has been exposed, leaving tall cliffs. A field stretches out from the cliffs, covered in dry yellow knee-high grass. A sturdy stone bridge has been erected on the western cliff-top, extending across the river.
110559: This bridge is wrought from finely-cut stone, its parts fitted with remarkable exactness. The stone is a uniform light-grey in colour except for the low walls that rise on either side, which are white. The bridge describes a low arc from the top of one cliff-wall to another, providing safe passage over the narrow rushing river below.
110560: A narrow road paved in cobblestones runs straight east and west through a small elven village. Most of the stones are old and show years of wear, but a few new cobbles indicate that they are replaced when necessary. The road comes to a stone bridge just to the east, while to the west it opens out into the centre of the village.
110561:
A well-crafted white fountain is here, water pouring forth from it.
A white-painted bench is here.
An elven woman is here merrily walking along.
A pretty elven girl is strolling around here.

The village road becomes a loop here, running in a circle around a large grassy area. Two gigantic trees grow near the centre of the field, one a laurel, the other a yew. Both look like they have stood here since the beginning of time. The grass around them is neatly trimmed and there is no sign of fallen leaves or branches. The houses and shops of the village are neatly settled along the edges of the road.
110562: An elven citizen is here enjoying the day.

This well-maintained cobblestone road runs due east and west through the elven village, straight as an arrow. It appears to have been swept recently, as it is completely free of stray leaves or clutter. To the north, a river empties out into the Gulf of Lhun, with piers thrusting out into both bodies of water. The strong smell of fish wafts in from the south.
110563:
An elven craftsman is here, performing intricate work.
An elven craftsman is here, performing intricate work.

A blend of coarse and fine sand provides soft, uneven footing, except along the northern edge of the beach where the rolling waters of the Gulf of Lhun smooth out the surface and bind it together. The half-built hull of a ship rests upon a wooden framework, well above the high-water mark. Near it, piles of lumber lie ready to be added. The skeleton of another ship has been laid out nearby, but construction has not yet begun on it. A small village stands to the east.
110564: A brown fox is here, looking for some rabbits to chew up.

Several species of wheat grow unhindered, ranging in colour from dark green to pale yellow and golden brown. Incredibly, there is no clear evidence that this field was deliberately planted, although there are signs that it is harvested on a regular basis. The wheat vanishes to the north, where a beach provides too little nourishment, and to the south, where it is replaced by bushes.
110565:
A large thorny branched shrub is growing here.
On the shrub, there are two piles of blackberries.
An erect shrub with green pinnate leaves is growing here.
Inside the shrub, there are two piles of crimson raspberries.
A restless rabbit bounces around.
A fierce wolverine is here, snarling at you.

Large thick bushes abound throughout the area, most of them covered in fruit at various stages of growth. Blackberries and raspberries seem to dominate. A very faint path winds its way between the patches of growth, bearing primarily north and south. A particularly dense cluster of thorny growth blocks the way to the east.
110566:
A large stone fireplace with a roaring fire warms the room.
The elven bartender is standing here, gossiping behind the bar.
A lovely elven maid is serving beverages here.

This public house serves both villagers who flock here for conversation and travellers who seek a hot meal. Several fine tables fill the room, surrounded by a mixture of chairs, stools and benches. A fireplace centred in the north wall supplies heat on cold winter nights and the cheerful flicker of flames all year round.
110567: An elven farmer is here surveying the land.

Small fields of grain are planted in neat squares. The crops are varied, and include wheat, oats, and rye, each apparently planted at different times, based on the extent of their growth. Some of the crops are damaged along the south edge of the field, evidently grazed upon by wild animals. A tall stone wall has been erected to the north, separating these fields from the lands beyond. A small farmhouse sits in front of the wall.
110568: This field is clearly cultivated, as it contains almost nothing but flax. The plants cover nearly the entire area, tapering off only as they encounter rocky ground to the east. The plants range from six inches to three feet in height, and seem to be planted and harvested in rotation. A large gully, strewn with jagged talus deposits, blocks passage to the east, while a low barn lies to the north, backed by a stone wall that extends all the way to the gully.
110569:
Traces of fierce white tones form the aura of this place.
A small campfire burns here, its low flames giving off only a little light.
A warhorse (ulo) is standing here.

The ground levels out here until it is nearly flat, with only small rises and drops visible. Short grass covers most of the area, though in many places the sandy soil is exposed. Weeds stand tall above the grass, most of them crowned with flowers in various hues of white, yellow and pale purple. The land rises to the east, with a shallow defile splitting its surface in twain.
110570:
A brown snake watches you.
A large mother hawk is here looking for a prey to feed her young.

Small, yet sheer, escarpments rise to the north and south. Though no more than four times the height of a man at any place, they block passage as well as any city wall. The long, narrow plain between them is stony, with small clumps of withered grass clinging wherever they can. Running through the centre of the defile is an unnaturally straight line of lifeless rock.
110571:
The corpse of a raccoon is lying here.
Pilea the Hobbit is resting here.

High grass covers the land, its broad blades bending and rustling in the nearly constant winds that roll in from the west. The land drops off suddenly to the west, where the river below has eaten deep into the earth, leaving only a sheer cliff of dark rock. Faint traces of an old road running through the area are visible, but it has been long abandoned and overgrown.
110572: The soil is rich and well-watered, resulting in an explosive growth of emerald grass. The grass stands two to three feet high in most places, and moving in it requires some effort. In many places the grass has been crushed or bent aside as wild animals have moved through, leaving a bewildering maze of trails that join, split, and cross each other at random.
110573: Several species of grass abound here, covering the landscape in a mixture of hues ranging from pale yellow to deep green. Only a few wildflowers manage to raise their heads above the grass, pink and white blossoms standing out in counterpoint to the green. Broken fragments of shale and small boulders of sandstone litter the ground. A steep, shale-covered slope rises to the east, while the land drops into a wide defile to the north.
110576: This field looks like it was once cultivated, but now lies untended. Wheat and oats grow in profusion, interspersed with their wild cousins. Many patches have been heavily grazed by wild animals glad for the high quality fodder to be found here. The land to the south is still cultivated, and a small farmhouse is visible.
110577: A woody evergreen plant grows here, with many stems reaching upward.

Several large outcroppings of dark-brown sandstone thrust up through the soil. Years of erosion have smoothed them and worn away their surfaces layers to the point where this entire area is lightly coated with coarse sand. Weeds thrive in the poor soil, freed from competition with more aggressive grasses, which are almost absent here.
110578: Tall yellow-green and pale brown grass grows here, but very little of it stands upright anymore. Long years of strong winds and gales coursing across the open vastness of the ocean have pounded relentlessly at the vegetation, bending it almost flat to the ground. Some younger, more resilient deep-green blades poke up between the taller grass, not yet crushed by the scouring winds.
110579: A shallow pond is here, tinted green with algae.

A wide field spreads out here, covered in most areas by green and brown grass. The grass has been cropped low in several spots by grazing animals, and in a few places the sod has been ripped completely clear from the ground. Several small outcroppings of brown sandstone poke up through the soil. A sturdy wooden fence stands to the south, while dense thorny bushes grow in abundance to the north.
110580:
A colony of red ants is here. The ants seem to ignore you.
A fierce wolverine is here, snarling at you.

This broad depression lies lower than the land in any direction. As a result, it has accumulated more than its share of salt carried in from the ocean that pounds relentless on the shore to the west. Patches of weeds, stunted bushes, and coarse brown grass cover the land, but in many places the soil is bare, too salty to nourish life.
110581: Years of ocean spray drifting inland with the wind have left this area covered in a fine layer of salt. Vegetation is patchy, limited mainly to grasses that are able to survive in the tainted soil. The land slopes gently upward from west to east. The distant pounding of waves upon the shore pervades the area.
110582:
A goat is here, grazing peacefully.
An elven farmer is here surveying the land.
A goat is here, grazing peacefully.
A goat is here, grazing peacefully.

A tall, sturdy wooden fence surrounds this place, broken only by a gate in the north and the door of a house to the east. Low grass grows in most spots, but it has been heavily grazed and in many places bare soil shows through. A long, low trough stands beside a small well in the southwest corner, the ground in front of it trampled into a muddy mess by the hooves of goats.
110583: A large cabinet capable of storing goods is here.

This house stands well away from any others, far from the bustle of city life. Great care must have been taken in its construction, as it appears to be quite old but is still in excellent condition. A stone hearth dominates the northern wall. Several finely-carved wooden figures line its mantle. Doors stand in the centres of the west and east walls.
110590: The ground slopes downward from east to west in a gentle gradient as it works its way toward the distant waters of the Gulf of Lhun. Other than the slope of the land, there is little variation in its surface, with only minor undulations to warp the flat surface. Low grass with broad, grey-green blades covers most of the land, interspersed with taller wildflowers. A fenced-in pasture lies to the east.
110591:
A brown cow is here, contemplating a higher reality whilst chewing slowly.
A brown cow is here, contemplating a higher reality whilst chewing slowly.

The soil is a poor mixture of sand, gravel, and clay. Low weeds gather what nourishment they can, but there are many bare patches where nothing has been able to take hold. The distant sounds of waves upon the shore drifts in from the west, and a distinct tang of salt fills the air. The ground becomes much more fertile to the east.
110592: Aeons of wind and waves have eroded the stone to the west of here, carrying the resulting sand to this place and piling it up into countless dunes. The dunes are covered in most places by low, yellow-green grass that has taken seed and now helps these masses maintain their shape. The land gives the impression of rolling waves upon the gulf.
110593: The ground has been scoured nearly bare of soil through years of strong winds ripping their way across the Gulf of Lhun, exposing the bare rock underneath. The land slopes strongly down from the northeast to the southwest. A low cliff lies to the north, its base eroded by the surging waves, but as the shoreline curves around to the south the cliff vanishes until the land merges seamlessly with the waters.
110594: A king crab is crawling around in the sand here.

Large rocks thrust up above the surface of the gulf, the waves swirling around them as they roll in and out. The water is only a few feet deep here most of the time, and almost vanishes at low tide, leaving isolated pools scattered among the sand. Broken fronds of seaweed and bleached driftwood are snared by the rocks and trapped in the pools. The land rises in a stony shore to the east.
110595: A shipwreck lies on its side on the rocky beach.

Large masses of rock rise like small islands all along the shore here. Their surfaces, worn by centuries of wind and water, are in some places smooth, in others pocked by uneven erosion. Pale yellow sand surrounds them, providing a navigable route through the area. Tangles of bleached driftwood and dried seaweed clearly indicate the high water mark.
110596:
A large brown snake with black patches is coiled here.
A swarm of hornets is coming out of its nest.

Like giant stairs beside the ridge to the east, the wilderness here descends from a rocky promontory northwards to a shallow escarpment above the river that lies south. Wild weeds grow up among the stones littering the landscape. Several blocks of stone rest at the base of the ridge. They have been heavily weathered, but were clearly cut and squared at some point long ago.
110597: A large, dangerous-looking green snake is coiled up here.

This huge rock formation stands high above the plains, extending upwards from the ridge below. The area is flat and almost circular, the sides nearly sheer. Worn stairs leading down from the lip indicate that this place was not entirely carved by nature, but the builders have long since disappeared.
110598:
An elven fisher is standing here.
A stocky mountain mule is here, waiting to serve.
A brook trout is here, swimming in the current.

The river bends sharply as it turns away from the Tower Hills to the east and flows westward to the sea. The sound of burbling water can be heard coming from both upstream and downstream, but here the river is deep and silent. A bank rises almost vertically to the north where the river has cut its outer edge deeply into the land. A few huge rocks stick out of the bank, which is otherwise covered with deep, dark and slippery mud. A small beach has formed to the east, making for a gentle approach to the river.
110599: As the river flows towards the west, it drops into a small gorge between rock walls, no more than twenty feet high on either side. The water rushes across layers of worn rock. The grey stone bank to the south appear broken and jagged, while to the north the rocky wall is worn smooth and sheer, offering little purchase.
110600: The ground here is rocky and uneven. Tufts of grass grow between the stones, seeking the soil that has accumulated in the gaps. Three lonely fir trees dot the area, sinking their roots deep among the cracks, widely separated from each other. A narrow river flows past to the north and could be reached by a short scramble down a broken rocky slope.
110601: A sturdy pack horse is standing here.

Pale brown soil, heavy in clay and sand, provides limited sustenance to the myriad weeds and wildflowers that grow here. Thistles seem to dominate, their purple heads appearing dull against the brighter yellow and orange blooms that surround them. A narrow stream, only a few feet across, runs from the south to the north. It crosses a low cliff and plunges to join the river below.
110604: A mass of dark green leaves clings to a wall.

A square greensward is surrounded with wooden houses standing among high trees. The ground is covered with grass, and many flowers grow between paved footpaths. Most of the buildings are two-story houses, which have frontages covered with ivy and glazed windows painted with green leaves. The sound of voices carries from a small house to the east, and a wooden sign hangs over its entrance.
110605: The Southern End of the Village Square
A well-crafted white fountain is here, water pouring forth from it.

The square lies nestled between wooden houses and ancient trees on three sides. The grass-covered square extends to the north with paved paths lined by flowers leading between house and away from the square in several directions. Most of the buildings are two-storey houses, with fronts covered with ivy and glazed windows painted with green leaves. A big house on the south side attracts attention. It has two carved wooden columns on either side of massive double-doors.
110606:
A mass of dark green leaves clings to a wall.
An elven guard is standing here at his post.
A stocky mountain mule is here, waiting to serve.

A street runs between the houses of the village Lhun. Most of the houses are hidden under the boughs of towering trees and covered in ivy, vines, and moss. Thus coloured doors and glass windows are the only features visible from most of the buildings. Small gardens open up in front of the houses, sporting bright flowers, herbs, and other plant life. Gravel footpaths connect the houses to the street. The twittering of small birds can be heard from above. To the east the street leads into a square, and to the west it slowly descends to a wicket in a hedge. Stairs can be seen behind the wicket, leading down around a crag and ultimately to a small beach of the Amber river.
110607: A paved street runs from the west to the east. The street is bordered on both sides by flowerbeds and wooden houses. A dense forest, full of tall elm trees, grows beyond the houses. To the east, the street enters a small glade in the forest. A village square is situated to the west. Cheerful voices and the clinking of glasses can be heard from a house at the eastern end of the street. A large sign hangs over the entrance.
110608:
A weapons rack stands against the wall.
In the rack are four arrows, a quiver and a shortbow.
An elven guard is standing here at his post.
An elven boy is running about here.

This large wooden platform sits on the branches of a massive tree. A palisade surrounds the borders of the platform, presumably both for safety and protection. There is a trapdoor in the middle of the platform, with a rope ladder attached to iron rings next to it. It is possible to see a path approaching this forest to the north, through gaps in the canopy, and a gate just below the platform. A skilled archer could effectively defend the gates in times of trouble.
110609: An elven grocer is standing here, quietly humming to herself.

This place is filled with racks on both sides of the room. The variety of goods is extensive with vegetables such as garlic, potatoes, and onions standing out among them. There is a large window on the front side of the store, just next to the front door. The backside of the room is lit by a row of crystal balls that are hanging just under the ceiling. A wooden counter stands at the back wall. A door leading to the inner parts of the house is right by the counter.
110610:
A small oaken table has been set here.
On the table, there is a plate of baked trout.
A wooden cupboard stands here.
An elven boy is running about here.

A short corridor leads from the front doors to a set of narrow wooden stairs leading up to a garret. There are two other doors in the corridor. A small storeroom lies to the right and a bedroom is to the left. The storeroom is full of fishing nets, rods, and other necessary tools. There is an oven close to the doors in the living room, heating the whole house. A wooden table with four chairs stands near the oven under the front windows. There is a small garden behind the house, visible through a small window at the back of this room.
110624:
A huge clock is standing here.
A large encrusted cedar chest is standing here.
An elven guard is standing here at his post.
An elven guard is standing here at his post.
Lairesur, ancient among the Sindar, stands here guiding his kin (glowing).

The entrance hall is a square room about ten yards wide and is lit by a chandelier shaped as four swans with each of them holding a light-radiating crystal ball. There are two high windows on both sides of the massive doubledoors on the front side of the house. A staircase stands on the opposite side of the room, leading to the upper floors. A sofa, armchairs, and a table stand on one side of the stairs with a chair and a desk on the other.
110625:
A large stone fireplace with a roaring fire warms the room.
An Elven innkeeper stands ready to sign up his guests.

The main room of the inn is lit by crystal balls hanging from the ceiling. A long, solid oak bar runs along the western wall of this room. The aroma of cooking wafts in through doors behind the bar that likely lead to a kitchen. Stairs at the back of the room lead upward to the next floor, and there is a large roaring fireplace across from the bar. The rest of the place is full of tables and chairs. Paintings of remarkably tall trees hang on the walls.
110626:
A clear spring babbles as cool water trickles out of the ground.
A sturdy pack horse is standing here.
An elven youth is busy attending to the animals.
An elven woman is here merrily walking along.

Lush, green grass covers a small round glade surrounded by tall, healthy elms. Their dense, interwoven canopy acts as a natural roof protecting this place from the vagaries of the weather. There is a path among the trees on the western side of the glade that leads towards a village street. Hoofprints cover the ground, especially dense near a natural spring beneath one of the trees.
110627: An elven farmer stands here partially hunched over.

This farmhouse consists of a several rooms along a single corridor. From the perspective of the front door, there is a main room on the left and a storeroom with well-stocked shelves to the right. A trap door at the end of the corridor leads down to a large cellar. The centerpiece of the main room is a large oven which could be used for either cooking food or heating the farmhouse. A wooden table and several chairs sit near the stove. At the back of the room are three beds, a cupboard, and two wardrobes. All rooms other than the cellar are well lit by windows.
110628:
A bulb of garlic with green stems is here.
There are three carrots here.
There are two turnips here.
There are two sacks of flour here.
There are two cabbages here.
There is a water skin lying on the ground.

Simple in its construction, this crude cellar was dug to store the farm's root vegetables. The walls and ceiling are supported by sturdy planks and stanchions. The floor is made of large, flat stones. A set of stairs allows access to a trapdoor which leads up into a farmhouse.
110630:
A wooden chest stands in the corner.
An elf is here walking around.

This house seems to be typical of those built by elves. It has been carefully crafted to withstand the wear of decades, if not centuries, before requiring repairs. The interior is a display of graceful, curving lines and patterns of light and dark woods. The house is very clean and clearly well-tended. A single door offers access to the street outside.
110631: The land rises a short distance above its surroundings. It is not enough to form a true hill, but it does contain the river to the east, forcing it to turn towards the north. Trees dot the landscape, standing by themselves or in small groups, primarily poplars and sweet-gums. A small path runs to the north, where a clusters of houses can be seen.
110632: Some low, dark-green grass grows here, but for the most part it is entirely displaced by wildflowers. Dozens of species flourish here, varying in height, creating a multi-tiered display of vibrant colours. From white and pale yellow to deep purple and red, the blossoms cover the entire spectrum. The heads of the flowers shift and dance in the slightest breeze.
110637:
An elven woman is here merrily walking along.
A pretty elven girl is strolling around here.
An elven boy is running about here.

Built of thick, sturdy wooden planks, this pier stretches out into the junction of a wide river and Gulf of Lhun. The blend of waters swirls around the base of the pier, circling the hardened posts on which it rests. The pier drops down at its northern end until it is only a foot above the water, allowing easy access in and out of the river mouth.
110638: An elven grocer is standing here, quietly humming to herself.

The overpowering smell of fish immediately announces the purpose of this shop. All of the fish here are fresh, however, without even a hint of any gone bad. A narrow counter runs across part of the room, while bins holding bait and other fishing supplies line the walls. A variety of fishing rods and nets hang above the bins.
110639: The ground is completely water-logged. Clumps of grass, reeds, and other low plants provide some footing, but care must be taken not to become mired down in thick mud. Hundreds of small pools dot the landscape, their water tinted brown and green by mud and algae, and completely undrinkable. The land becomes firmer to the west, but to the south the marsh becomes even wetter.
110640: The river makes a wide, sluggish turn to the north as it nears its destination. A rocky cliff frames the northeast edge of the river, while lowlands extend to the southwest. The river flows very slowly here, at times seeming to entirely stop. Tall rushes extend along the south bank, and beyond them a shallow marsh can be seen.
110641:
A water moccasin slithers out of sight just below the surface of the water.
A small leech is here, floating in the water.

Only isolated islands of green and narrow strips of weeds separate broad pools of water. Tall, dense grass provides some stability in places, but the safe paths wind in a maze-like confusion with many dead-ends. Cypress trees rise above the otherwise flat landscape. The water here is dark, nearly black in places, a thick organic soup teeming with insects, and undrinkable. Hidden below its surface is deep, oozing mud.
110642:
A bee flies around here, collecting nectar from the flowers.
A bee flies around here, collecting nectar from the flowers.
An elven beekeeper is standing here, peacefully watching his bees.

The land is mostly flat, with minor hillocks rising and falling just enough to create the impression of rolling waves. Many trees grow here, widely separated from each other for the most part, with only a few small clusters. Dogwoods, poplars, tulips, and hawthorns seem to dominate. A diverse blend of wildflowers grow in profusion. To the south, the trees draw closer together to form a small wooded area.
110643:
A squirrel scampers around here, looking for nuts from the trees.
A porcupine is waddling around here, its tail full of sharp quills.

This grove is more than just a cluster of trees, it is almost a small forest which extends nearly a mile in any direction. The trees growing on the outskirts of the woods are young and fairly small, containing a mixture of birch, larch, and maple trees. Towards the centre, the trees change to towering elms and oaks, rising high above the ground. A large artificial complex has been constructed among the intertwined branches of the trees, resting nearly thirty feet overhead.
110644: A colourful butterfly is fluttering around here.

The ground rises up into a low hill here, standing above the surrounding lands. Large sheets and boulders of rock thrust up above the soil, their grey, brown, and orange surfaces a striking contrast to the greenery that surrounds them. Many of the stones are dotted with pale green lichen. The ground drops quickly to the north into a wet, boggy depression, while a small forest stands just to the east.
110645:
A fat rabbit is here, chewing on some grass.
A fat rabbit is here, chewing on some grass.

Running down from a low hill to the east, the long slope is covered with lines of cultivated grapevines. Well-constructed wooden frames provide support for the vines, and many of them bear fruit. A narrow dirt path extends east from the field, but vanishes as it ascends the rock-strewn hill. A second hillside, entirely uncultivated, rises to the west.
110646:
A restless rabbit bounces around.
A brown fox is here, looking for some rabbits to chew up.
A brown fox is here, looking for some rabbits to chew up.
A fierce wolverine is here, snarling at you.

The ground is saturated, making for a very soft and muddy surface. Grass and weeds hold the ground together in most places, making travel possible, if not easy. A few scattered cypresses rise above the field, enjoying the moisture and rich nutrients that this area provides. The mud becomes deeper and softer to the east and north, blocking travel.
110647: A furry, striped raccoon is here, nosing around for some berries or roots.

Several small plots of crops have been planted here, including wheat and oats, along with a variety of vegetables. Surrounding these plots, wild grasses grow, but they also appear to be tended, perhaps to prevent them from spreading into the planted areas. The rush of moving water to the north is quite audible. A sturdy wall built of rounded rocks stands to the east.
110648:
A large elk is standing here, chewing grass and leaves.
A restless rabbit bounces around.

This hill, barely tall enough to merit that name, rises only a short distance above the surrounding lands. Its slopes carry little soil, and the rocky core of the hill is exposed. A few stunted fir and spruce trees crown the hilltop, providing at least a little shelter against the winds that often whip across the land from the Gulf of Lhun.
110649:
A restless rabbit bounces around.
A fierce wolverine is here, snarling at you.

The trunks of hundreds of dead trees lie upon the ground, evidently the remains of what was once a small forest. Most of the trees were violently torn from the ground, perhaps by a massive storm, their exposed roots long since washed bare of soil. Now the trees lie at peace, covered in green and brown fungi, slowly returning to the soil from which they grew.
110653:
An elven woman is here merrily walking along.
An elf is here walking around.
An elven cook is standing here, busy cooking meals.

A broad platform has been constructed in a triangular form, using three huge trees as its supports. Several bowers of woven branches linked together by live vines provide areas of protection against the elements. A number of simple but comfortable pallets are scattered below the bowers. A large table surrounded by stools provides a communal dining and meeting area.
110654:
A brown bear is sleeping here.
A brown bear is sleeping here.

The cave entrance opens out into a large chamber. Jagged rocks form the walls and ceiling, while sand, dirt, and leaves cover the floor. There are many signs that this cave is frequently inhabited by some wild animal. Strands and tufts of coarse brown fur are scattered everywhere, and countless tracks of padded feet wander in every direction.
110655:
A hairy black spider wraps up a silken package with her hind legs.
A hairy black spider wraps up a silken package with her hind legs.

The river is quite broad and shallow here as it makes a very wide bend from east to north. The water appears nearly motionless on the surface, but random leaves and sticks floating past betray its current. A flat rocky shore runs along the west bank, centuries of silt and small stones paving an area that is nearly free of vegetation.
110656:
Clusters of slender stems and tall leaves thrive in the mud and shallows.
A bass swims here.

A broad, shallow river slowly winds its way through wide, lazy bends towards the distant Gulf of Lhun. The current is very slow here, and anyone floating down the river might take hours to make any progress. The banks of the river are covered in deep grass and reeds, especially to the west, where the edge of the river merges with a marshy area.
110657: As the river flows northwest toward the gulf, it slices through the edge of a low hill. Centuries of water have washed away the surface soil and have gouged deeply into the rock beyond, creating a small cliff that borders the northeast edge of the river. Thick layers of slate form the surface of the cliff, their dark-grey surfaces covered in many places by moss.
110658:
A salmon swims here.
A fat carp swims here.

The river flows steadily toward the northwest. It runs through broad, flat plains which must often be inundated during rainy seasons as the river expands beyond its low banks. The land has a barely perceptible slope, causing the river to flow quite slowly here, and its bed is thick with silt.
110663: The river is wide and almost silent in this place. Its clear waters reveal a bed of flat stone, flowing lightly over a long series of shelves that drop off only an inch or two at a time. Thick reeds grow along the north bank, but many have been trampled by animals coming here to drink. The south bank of the river is barren of most vegetation, covered instead by broken shale and slate.
110664:
A black catfish is here, lurking in the mud.
A black catfish is here, lurking in the mud.
A trout swims here.

Descending gradually from the wooded foothills of Ered Luin, this wide, calm river flows westward across a broad coastal plain. Reeds grow upon the north bank, providing a place for fish and other creatures to shelter and feed. The south bank is covered in a dense tangle of thorny bush, preventing travel in that direction.
110672:
A trout swims here.
A bass swims here.

The river rushes between high stone walls on either side, their sheer surfaces offering no access to the lands beyond. The water courses down over a series of small cascades and falls, dropping a few feet at a time, swirling around and over large boulders and across flat sheets of rock. The river widens and calms as it flows on to the west.
110673: A sturdy pack horse is standing here.

As it flows westward through a small gorge, the river here winds its way around occasional boulders that thrust up above the surface like giants making their crossing. A large tree, dragged into the river by some storm or flood, forms a hazard along the north bank, where it has become wedged. To the south, a narrow ledge rises from the shallows to the top of the sheer bank.
110674: Many types of bushes grow here, most bearing flowers of some sort, colouring the land with pale yellow and purple and dull white. A few bushes bear fruit, though not all of it is edible. Thorny brambles line the edge of a cliff that drops off to the north, preventing any attempt at reaching the river below. The brush continues to the west, but vanishes to the east.
110675:
Some thick writhing vines whip all around you.
A grey wolf is here, snarling aggressively.
A grey wolf is here, snarling aggressively.

Several species of bushes and brambles grow together, leaving little room to venture between them. Vines and roots hidden beneath low weeds threaten to trip unwary travellers, while thorns snatch at clothes and exposed flesh. The brush is particularly dense to the north, where the land descends to meet a river.
110676:
A huge, black wolf is here, ready to devour.
A beautiful and docile horse is standing here.

The ground is soft, but the soil appears to be only a thin layer over sheets of rock. In many places the dull grey stone is exposed and plant-life is entirely absent. A few dozen trees dot the area, huddling in tiny clusters that are widely separated from each other. Just to the north, a wide river flows slowly past. A wall built from smoothed rocks blocks the way to the west.
110677:
A large pike is lurking in the mud by the bottom.
A brook trout is here, swimming in the current.
A trout swims here.
A large pike is lurking in the mud by the bottom.

Large fish dart about under the surface of this dark river. Foam crashes against the west bank as the river slowly turns to the north. A small beach has formed at the bend; it is covered in a diverse assortment of pebbles. The bed of the river is composed of these same pebbles, but is too deep and unsteady for creatures to ford with ease. To the north, the current deepens at another bend in the river.
110678: The sound of rushing water echoes off the steep banks of a narrow river. The rapids calm where water crashes into a rocky bank to the north that towers five yards above the surface. The river's flow slows as it turns to the west where its channel deepens. The full fury of the rapids churns upstream to the south, where several sharp rocks poke up through the surface of the turbulent waters. White clumps of foam sail down the dark river, occasionally becoming trapped in eddies where they form large, spinning whorls.
110680: Plains sweep in from the east, but vanish as they approach the gulf. The soil thins until it disappears entirely, leaving heavily-eroded rock exposed. The land ends abruptly in a tall cliff that drops away into the surging waters of the Gulf of Lhun. The dull throbbing of waves upon the rocks below continues ceaselessly. To the west, far across the gulf, a dim purple shadow marks the opposite shore.
110681:
A large crystal lamp, standing upon a copper column, faces out to sea.
A grey-cloaked elf is here, looking for the tracks of evil creatures.

The land vanishes in a sheer drop to the west. At the base of the cliff, the waters of the gulf boil and churn around enormous rocks that have broken away from the land. A thin mist of salt covers most of the land, but very little soil, and only a few hardy weeds and stunted bushes cling tenaciously to the cracks in the rocks.
110682: A silvery fish quickly darts through the water.

The bottom of the gulf approaches the surface enough to be visible, but it is still too distant to reach. Enormous beds of seaweed grow in the sandy bottom, their fronds weaving back and forth in the constant motion of invisible currents. To the south the water becomes much shallower, but to the east waves swirl around large rocks before crashing against a tall cliff.
110683: This close to the shore, the waters of the gulf are shallow, no more than a handful of fathoms in most spots. Tidal currents ebb and flow around enormous submerged rock formations, creating a dangerous zone of roiling waters. Below the surface, the faint outline of a once-proud sailing vessel can barely be discerned.
110684: The land is completely submerged by the gulf, but drops off very gradually as it slopes away from the shore. Beginning at only a foot, even at its deepest the water is only thirty feet deep, and the seabed is clearly visible. Clusters of life cling to rocks along the bottom, swirling with colourful plants and fish. The bottom sinks rapidly just to the west.
110685: The river bursts out from between two confining cliffs and expands into a wide, shallow stream as it levels out and approaches the Gulf of Lhun. The current is slow enough that at high tide the waters of the gulf mingle with those of the river, creating a brackish mixture that supports a blend of both freshwater and saltwater flora and fauna.
110689:
A silvery fish quickly darts through the water.
A large sturgeon swims slowly along the bottom.

The water is too deep to make out anything of the floor of the gulf. Low waves rise and fall constantly, pushing gradually closer to the shore that is visible a few miles to the east. Schools of silver fish swirl and dart far below the surface, but they are too deep and too swift to approach.
110690: Strong currents battle with one another, constantly rearranging themselves as one gains dominance over the others. Mixtures of warmer and cooler water rise and settle to the bottom, while the wind brushes across the surface, adding its influence to the confusion. The gulf continues in every direction.
110691: The surface of the gulf appears to be mainly calm, its flat face given texture only by the constant roll of low waves. Below the surface, strong currents run through the deep water and even on top of the water their influence can still be felt. To the east, a distant cliff is visible, and before it the waves crash and churn around pillars of unyielding rock.
110692: A large sturgeon swims slowly along the bottom.

The waters of the gulf pound relentlessly against the rocky shore. Over untold years the waves have worn away the coast, leaving a tall, unscalable cliff. The waves surge around hundreds of partially-submerged rocks, threatening to batter anyone caught in their grip. A dark tunnel mouth is partially visible in the cliff just above the sea level. To the west, the gulf becomes calmer and stretches out into miles of unbroken water.
110693: A short and rough tunnel leads from west to east. The ground is wet and tufts of seaweed are caught behind sharp rock edges. A number of heavy bars are set into the rock at the cave entrance to the west. To the east, the tunnel opens up into a cavern. The walls around the eastern end appear to be smoothed and shaped, and barely visible runes are inscribed on them.
110694: The waters of the gulf churn and foam around partially-submerged rocks and pound against a curving cliff face. The constant roar is deafening, and the swirling waters and grinding rocks may pose a deadly hazard to anyone foolish enough to try swimming here. To the west, the gulf becomes deeper and much calmer.
110697: A Damp Cavern with a Sarcophagus

In the sarcophagus (here):
a fine pair of chain mail gloves (flawless)
a pair of white chain mail sleeves (flawless)
a pair of white chain mail leggings (satisfactory)
a white chain mail coif (satisfactory)
a fine chain mail hauberk (flawless)
a double-headed axe (used)
an ancient metal helmet (flawless); it glows blue
a beautiful diamond
a skeleton
an amethyst
a fine pair of metal boots (flawless)
a metal wall shield (satisfactory)
a silvery wristband (flawless); it glows blue
A large, marble sarcophagus sits on a raised dais in the centre of the cave.

A wide cavern was carved out by water leaking down from the surface above and flowing out through a tunnel to the west. Much of the ceiling is covered by stalactites, but the floor of the cavern was leveled at some point, and only a few short stalagmites have started to form. A stone platform dominates the centre of the cavern and bears a huge stone sarcophagus. A tunnel leads out of the cavern to the west. The floor is wet, and several strands of seaweed have been caught behind the edges of the platform.
110698: A large sturgeon swims slowly along the bottom.

The bottom of the gulf slopes off quickly and the waters become suddenly deep. Waves roll continuously across the surface, unhindered in their eternal motion across the deep. The piercing cries of gulls drift in from the east where, a few miles distant, the shore is faintly visible.
110699: A silvery fish quickly darts through the water.

The waters of the Gulf of Lhun stretch out in every direction. It is only a few miles to the eastern shore from here, but the western shore is entirely beyond sight. Waves undulate constantly across the vast expanse of water, their size dictated by the strength of the wind as it roars or whispers its way across the gulf.
110700: A large sturgeon swims slowly along the bottom.

Deep, blue-green water extends miles in every direction. Far to the north, the sails of a few ships can be discerned. Some are westward bound toward the far shore, invisible beyond the horizon, while others sail eastward towards the Grey Havens. Although the water seems calm, strong currents flow below the surface.
110701: The waters of the gulf are vast and deep, disturbed only by low waves rolling across its surface. Miles away, a low cliff can be seen to the east, rising above the waves. Far, far to the west, a barely visible haze may be the far shore, or simply an illusion. The gulf stretches out in every direction.
110702: The river squeezes between rock walls until it reaches its narrowest point for miles. The walls rise above the river a good thirty feet, and are vertical and drenched by splashing water. Many large boulders have been exposed by years of rushing water and, combined with broken branches and snags they have caught, pose a major hazard to swimmers. Stretching overhead, a well-crafted stone bridge crosses the span from one wall to the other.
110704: The land rises up out of the waters in a very gentle slope, creating a broad, shallow shore. The bottom is almost entirely sand, with only a few rocky areas surviving years of pounding surf. Waves roll in and out, performing their slow, eternal dance. To the south, the land emerges from the waters, creating a beach. To the north and west, the Gulf of Lhun stretches out for miles.
110713: An elf is sitting here, fishing for a catch.

This pier is much narrower than the one to the east, meeting it at right angles and running perpendicular to it. The boards on this pier are much thinner, too, but still provide a solid footing. The pier extends out over the Gulf of Lhun, standing high above its surface. Clearly it is intended for fishing only, not for mooring boats.
110714: From its origin in the Tower Hills and crossing leagues of plains and lowlands, the river finally reaches its destination. The fresh water of the river merges with the salty water of the Gulf of Lhun in a confusion of currents. Seaweed and tiny fish flourish in the blended water, feasting upon nutrients washed in from the land.
110719:
A large shark moves swiftly through the water.
A large shark moves swiftly through the water.
A large shark moves swiftly through the water.

This ship once sailed proudly across the Gulf of Lhun, but now rests forever in its depths. Algae, coral, and other sea life cling to the surfaces of the ship, anchored against the currents and slowly absorbing the wood. The starboard side of the ship has been cracked and broken, and a large hole allows entrance into the ship's hold.
110720:
A delicate and beautiful crystal glass sits on the ground.
A silver wedding ring lies here.
A long slender eel glides along the water, its body coiled to strike.

The ship's hold is a jumbled mess of crates, barrels, and ropes. Cracked beams still support the deck above and may survive for years, but will eventually give way to decay. The hatches to the deck above are swollen shut and forever sealed. Some of the cargo containers are smashed open, and appear to have once contained fine cloth and food that is now worthless.
110721:
A sturdy peg for hanging armour from is on the wall.
On the peg, there is a water skin.

This farmhouse is smaller than many of its ilk, consisting of a single room. A small hearth is built into the north wall, with a stack of seasoned wood set nearby, ready to feed it. A narrow table runs along the west wall, clearly used mainly for cooking, while a smaller, square table sits in the centre of the house, flanked by two well-carved chairs. A single large bed, covered in a brightly-coloured quilt, rests in the northeast corner.
110722:
A low, many-branched shrub covers the ground here.
A thin, hairy plant, with small, oval leaves, grows here.
An elven farmer stands here partially hunched over.

A large herb garden grows in the space between the farmhouse and the barn. It is flanked on the north by a high stone wall. A lower wooden fence to the south protects it from wild animals while still allowing ample sunlight to fill the area. A wide variety of herbs have been planted here, including catnip, hyssop, winter savory, lavender, black and silver mint, parsley, thyme, marjoram, and rue. Together they fill the air with a symphony of aromas.
110723:
A saddlecloth lies here on the ground (glows blue).
A brown cow is here, contemplating a higher reality whilst chewing slowly.
A cow stands here, chewing her cud.
A sturdy pack horse is standing here.

This barn is low but spacious. A number of wooden pens have been built all along the east wall. Tools for planting and harvesting dominate the northern section of the barn, while the southwest corner is devoted to drying and storing flax. A large set of double-doors opens out into the fields to the south, while a much smaller door, painted white, pierces the west wall.
110726:
A skeleton of some humanoid lies in the dust.
A huge black fungus is here, exuding a foul stench.
A giant, strange looking green fungus is here, ready to devour you in seconds.

This small cavern has been carved out of the rock. It is clearly not natural, being almost square, with rough-cut walls of layered shale. Extensive effort must have been used to create this chamber, but there is no sign that it has been used in years. The only sign of furniture is a low shelf that runs along the south wall, perhaps used as a bed or table. The walls are damp, and the floor slick with water that has seeped in.
110728: A humble man stands here, ready to help you with your things.

You enter what appears to have been the home of a great queen bee. The hive has been hollowed out leaving hexagonal designs only around the edges of the structure. Light shining through the top of the hive shows Elven decorations and furnishings about the house. A buzzing noise resonates below.
110730: At the Edge of the Forest

A small plant grows here, with long, pointed leaves and flowers at its top.
A squirrel scampers around here, looking for nuts from the trees.

Standing on slightly higher ground, this patch of brush and light woodland looks down over Nimrodel, where she meets with a southerly tributary before flowing onward to the northeast. The land here is fairly fertile, no longer a part of the mountains proper, but approaching the lowlands wherein lies the vast expanse of Lothlorien, the Golden Wood. And indeed, this very copse marks the furthest western boundary of that forest, although it is too far from the heart of Lorien for any mellyrn to be found here.
110732: As she travels onward to the east, Nimrodel becomes ever more gentle in her progress. The lands through which she journeys are steadily becoming flatter and more fertile, and already she finds herself entering an area of brush and light woodland. The cold, clear waters, said by some to be healing to the weary, remain shallow here, and the stream might easily be forded by any who chose to do so.
110734: The land falls away gently to the east and south, where scrubby brushwood grows, marking the beginnings of a vast forest. And through this part of the woods flows a sparkling stream. Succoured by her waters, the ground here, whilst still quite rocky and sloped, is able to support a fairly thick area of bushes and shrubs, as well as bright wildflowers and dark green grass.
110735:
A robin is here, carrying small pieces of wood to its nest.
A fat rabbit is here, chewing on some grass.
A fat rabbit is here, chewing on some grass.

A prominent ridgeline comes to a faltering end here, where it divides a fertile little valley to the north from some craggier terrain to the south. Rising sharply, the land climbs westward toward a mountain peak. To the east it falls away quite rapidly, as it approaches the outskirts of the Golden Wood, and the far distant waters of the Great River.
110736: The valley floor slopes gently away from you to the north and east. To the west a steady climb up the narrowing coomb lies ahead of you, and southward is a steeper trek, as the land rises toward the encircling arms of a mountain ridge. A small stand of trees grows on the lower reaches of the valley floor, but here only a few wildflowers and small shrubs can make a living.
110738: Cutting across the countryside from east to west is an extensive mountain ridge. Here it reaches a low point, almost petering out completely as the lands immediately to the north and south rise to meet it. To the south lies a narrow valley, whilst northward you can see a steady drop-off toward the southeastern end of the Dimrill Dale, called by the dwarves Azanulbizar.
110739: Veering now from the north to the east, the narrow trail continues its march beside the stream. But as it leaves the mountains behind, so the path changes in nature. Whereas to the north and west it was somewhat rough and very rocky, the further you follow it to the east, the more you find that the ground upon which you travel is overgrown with dark green grass. However, here and there you can mark the signs of use, where the grass is trampled and the earth has been scuffed.
110740: Nimrodel runs slowly, her waters swirling into shallow, wide iridescent pools of aquamarine. The stream is flanked by a copse of proud and verdant oaks, their mighty boughs drooping over the streambed laden with the weight of the lushly growing foliage. To the north, the oaks thin, giving way to a wide expanse of rolling grasses where a trail winds roughly alongside Nimrodel's banks. Some large flat rocks have been placed in a row from north to south.
110741: A large, dangerous-looking green snake is coiled up here.

The air is heavy with the fresh scents of new growth emanating from the unusually lush forest spreading from the south. Nestled here in proximity to the forest are mounded clumps of tall-growing grass thick enough to completely envelop a hobbit or even a dwarf.
110742: In contrast to the tumbled highlands to the west, the land smoothes and slopes in gentle grassy waves east towards Lothlorien. Pale flowers are sprinkled among the verdure, and the air is as fresh and new as an everlasting spring day.
110743:
A black crow flies low to the ground here, looking for carrion to eat.
A black crow flies low to the ground here, looking for carrion to eat.
A black crow flies low to the ground here, looking for carrion to eat.

Rolling in soft curves, the land spreads out from the feet of the Misty Mountains, sloping gently towards the Golden Wood. Small tufts of grass grow wherever they find a promising foothold, interspersed with clumps of hardy, low-lying plants. Towering to the west are the omnipresent spires of the Hithaeglir.
110744: Rising slowly from the low-ground to the east, then sloping more steeply upward to the ridge to the north, this area is, in the main, devoid of vegetation. Nonetheless some hardy strands of grass and tough weeds poke from the grainy soil.
110745:
A reddish-brown shrub with purplish-pink flowers grows here.
Inside the shrub, there are a cluster of purplish-pink flowers.

The trail winds downward, then up again, through a bowl-like depression lined with dark, granular earth. Despite the coarse nature of the soil the undergrowth is lush and abundant with alpine grasses and small ground-hugging plants. The river winds on away to the north and to your south the land smoothes into distant grasslands.
110746: Some small rocks have been piled into a mound here.

The trail twists alongside a sheer drop, a great distance above the river, with no easy access to the sparkling river below. All about, short, sturdy trees and hardy grasses cling tenaciously to the rocky soil, eking out whatever sustenance they can glean from the unforgiving terrain.
110748: The watercourse beside which the trail travels has already become quite a lively little stream. Even so close to the spring from which it arose, the merry voice of the Silverlode can be heard clearly from the path, as the waters tumble along their rocky bed. South then east, the trail parallels the creek, turning away from the Misty Mountains, which tower above you to the west and to the north.
110749: On a Path beside a Spring

Running downwards from the dale, the path now draws close to a deep, natural well of crystal clear water. A small rill tumbles over the stone lip of the spring, sparkling and splashing its way along a narrow, rocky course, soon to be augmented by numerous mountain streams, and become the mighty Silverlode. The trail turns south from here, and traces a route parallel to the stream.
110750: Alive with a melody of musical murmurs and burblings, the stream gathers strength from many tendrils of glistening water as it rushes down a steep, rocky channel. The Silverlode leaps down the trough of the valley, running on and away into the lower lands, slowly dissolving into a golden haze many miles distant.
110751: At the Feet of the Misty Mountains

The land slopes upward to the north, first gradually, then becoming a sheer slope thrusting upwards towards great Fanuidhol, his crown wreathed in everlasting clouds. Rough furrows carved by tiny rivulets of rainfall and snowmelt run to the south into the swift-flowing Silverlode.
110752: Sculpted from the rock by a great finger of ice, this hollow is now shrouded by great bushes of holly - a perfect hiding place for fauna seeking shelter from the ravages of wind and cold, or perhaps hiding from unwanted attention. Fanuidhol, mantled in grey, presides over the environs with a stark, indifferent grandeur, blotting the northern horizon.
110753: An opossum stands here, sniffing around the ground.

Spread across the landscape is a great field of talus deposits; a mass of small, perfectly smooth pebbles of basalt polished to a dark, silvery, sheen by the weather over countless ages. Interspersed here and there are much larger chunks of volcanic debris looming above the rocks and scree. To the south, Silverlode plunges over falls of green-hued stone, the clear water sparkling in the light of the skies.
110754: The Silverlode hurries along, eager and swift. Its waters bubble and shimmer as they wander over the streambed composed of polished stone. As the path of the river winds its way through the landscape the water laps gently against the riverbank.
110755:
The prominent fin of a silver-yellow fish breaks the surface of the water.
A trout swims here.

Roiling and gurgling through a steep gorge, constrained by cliffs of sombre hue, the Silverlode rushes over a bed of glistening pebbles. Silvery fish shimmer amidst playgrounds of aquamarine, holding the promise of tasty fare to the traveller in need of sustenance.
110756: A large marmot is here, scurrying in between the rocks.

Glacial debris lies piled in large mounds, tumbled from the mountains above and fractured. Petite white blooms struggle for life among the rocks, their pale beauty contrasting with the barren stones. Below to the south, a small building lies nested in a wind-sheltered nook.
110757: Rising in a great stone-toothed arch above the landscape, this craggy dark ridge of stone seems to have been ground and polished to a fine sheen by some indomitable force. Little to no vegetation grows on it, finding no good foothold on its shining flanks. A trail does manage to find some tenuous line of safe passage along it, winding slowly down, following the contours of the ridgeline.
110758: A clear spring babbles as cool water trickles out of the ground.

A small flat area opens up on the ridge above the river. It is ringed with fir-trees, short and bent. The slopes drop steeply downwards to the north and east, while to the west the terrain is clothed with harts-tongue and shrubs of whortleberry. There is a small spring here, making this a good place to camp and draw water.
110759: Lush grasses and alpine flowers carpet the loamy soil in clothes of the freshest green, offering homes for small thick-furred creatures burrowed snugly into the earth. A small foot-trail winds northwest, climbing slowly towards the spires of the Misty Mountains.
110760: A partridge attempts to hide in the undergrowth.

Shrubs begin to grow among the tall meadows that fade into the west, framed by the peaks of the Misty Mountains. Mostly broad-leafed, sprawling bushes, they gladly drink their fill from the Silverlode, crowding up against her flanks and jostling for the best position to gather water and feed off the rich silt that is deposited on her banks.
110761: A buck runs swiftly from place to place, looking about warily as it grazes.

The trees here grow tall and majestic, elder scions, though not yet mellyrn. Nearly as grand are the stands of oak and beech, even a few drooping willows close unto Nimrodel, drawing their sustenance from her peerless waters. A trail mirrors her progress, wide enough and free enough of weeds and debris that it seems to still be used, if not often.
110762: A soft tinkling emanates from the waterfall to the south, intimating in some fashion the gentle renewal of dreams both forgotten and omnipresent. Mist and vapour swirls upward from the falls below, dancing dreamily amidst the tree-branches, depositing dewy droplets on the leaves. A good distance below, aquamarine pools reflect whorls of colour, transforming into new patterns over and over, infinitely creating and recreating themselves in the turbulent flow.
110763: A dense carpet of blue flowers dip their heads in the breeze.

The forest begins to grow more closely together, the trees gathering first in small clumps, then becoming more plentiful to the south.
