A mixture of trees grow in this area, tall, broad-leafed and deciduous in the main, but a few conifers are intermingled here and there. Nimrodel runs beside the forest, wending her way along a small declivity. A small footpath leads off to the north, joining here with a larger trail.
110764: A trail shaded by flourishing trees and green bushes faithfully follows the Nimrodel's whirling waters to the south and east. The river flows haphazard and wayward as a butterfly's path. Nonetheless, its purpose is apparent as she winds her way ever onward to the meeting with Silverlode, Anduin, and thence to the sea.
110765: Huddled in secret conclave, the wind whispering between their branches with a gentle murmur, these grand trees seem as if they might at any time pull their roots from the ground and march away like a troop of huorns. Indeed the trees' trunks are twisted into strange caricatures, like the craggy faces of dwarves or trolls, with knots and protrusions for eyes, noses, and mouths. Through and around the trees a small trail winds along the banks of Nimrodel; from east to south and upwards to the Misty Mountains.
110766: Vast and hoary, with huge limbs splayed far and high from its impressive trunk, a grand old oak tree stands above all others. Its lesser brethren nestle close under its eaves, almost as if seeking protection and council from their elder kin. Close to the trees, Nimrodel winds merrily, her waters dappled lightly with the illumination filtering through the trees.
110767:
A sprawling, twisted tree grows here.
A woodpecker is here, tapping on a tree.

Trees clutter the fields in increasingly dense patterns draped across the rolling glens. Mixtures of oak and alder, rowan and pine, co-inhabit the landscape with the tossing grasses and patches of scrub and heather. To the southeast the forest darkens.
110768: A small and tough weed grows here.

Bescattered with scree and detritus tumbled from the craggy heights directly to your north, the ground here is by and large devoid of vegetation. Nevertheless, a few strands of grass and other greenery emerge from the shards of rock that perhaps conceal more hospitable soil beneath. Surely something fair must lie beneath the windswept flats, for close to the south and east lush growths flourish freely.
110769: Grand old oaks and pines grow thickly between the two streams, their branches joining together; leaf and needle mingling together and casting mottled shadows upon the ground. To the west the ground rises sharply to a cliff overlooking Nimrodel. Weaving under the trees is a small trail, at times a mere animal path under the low hanging branches.
110770:
A fallen tree lies on the ground, its clump of roots pointing upwards.
A diamond-back rattlesnake is coiled here, ready to strike.

A small belt of land stretches between two rivers, filled with brush, sand, sharp rocks, and trees. The rivers have eroded this fork of land, and as a consequence the terrain is difficult to travel. An old, overgrown trail runs through the area, easily followed in some places and hidden beneath fallen trees and brush in others.
110771: Silverlode runs lazily here over a wide, shallow rock bed, shallow enough to allow fording, given a little care in one's step. A loud rumbling to the south signals the imminent merging of Silverlode with her sister-waters of Nimrodel.
110772: An Expanse of Soft, Loamy Turf

The trees thin momentarily, giving way to an expanse of tufted river-grasses waving sleepily in the breeze. The land is muted and quiet, except for the excited muttering of water rushing. An old, but distinct trail winds through the trees; it appears to receive some use, albeit infrequently.
110773: A brown fox is here, looking for some rabbits to chew up.

A round-topped mound crowned with mellyrn overlooks rolling forests in all directions. More close at hand, a small trail wanders as well, but in this case meandering from west to north. An expanse of soft, loamy turf can be seen to the west.
110774: The ground begins to rise and fall in gentle waves; tall trees cresting upon hilltops with lesser stands below. Small rivulets of water trickle down from a succession of finger-width springs, and the environs have a crisp, pleasant demeanour all told. What appears to be a small animal path winds to the south, then off to the east, deep into the fastness of inner Lorien.
110775: Nestled between two verdant swales, the ground dips into a shady vale where the trees grow tall and stern, groping heavenward in search of extra sustenance. A mat of large, golden leaves grace the fertile ground, no doubt blown here from the golden forest to the south.
110776: Lofty mellyrn stretch skyward, their elegant boughs interweaved to allow only a trickling of light to pass downwards to the soft, moist turf of the forest floor. To the south and west the Celebrant passes with gently controlled fervour.
110777: Flora and fauna burst with almost supernatural vitality, drawing sustenance from the fertile soils deposited by Silverlode on her insistent path towards the sea. The leaves of the trees seem almost to glow under the light of sun and moon, refining and reflecting their illumination in some magical fashion.
110778:
A rock lizard is here, motionless as it observes you.
A sparrow is flapping around on the ground.

Celebrant rushes by, spraying the rocky shore with moisture, nurturing clinging masses of bright green mosses and lichens. It is difficult to hear anything over the playful rush of the river as it traverses large tumbled and polished boulders.
110779: An elf, clad in the garments of a woodsman, moves stealthily among the trees (hidden).

The trees grow thick here, and one can barely make one's way in between them. It is reminiscent of a labyrinth of mighty tree-trunks, aged and unwithered. The trees have been standing here for eon upon eon, though the tiniest signs of decay hint that they have not been here forever.
110780: The prominent fin of a silver-yellow fish breaks the surface of the water.

The stream begins to fan out, widening significantly as it proceeds over a glistening bed of polished milk quartz. Pebbles and larger rocks have been polished by the flowing water to a lustrous sheen. The tall trees of Lothlorien stand on the both sides of the arching river.
110781: A wide expanse of sand, nurturing only a few blades of fibrous grasses, spreads here, evidently deposited by the Silverlode river. Strange tracks run here and there in the loose sand, betraying the nearby river to be a frequent watering place for nearby animals.
110782:
A small, dense tangle of roots covers the ground.
An elven scout stands here, blending in with the background.

Lush oaks, their branches drooping with the weight of their hearty growth, cluster in thick stands on this small overlook. The ground is covered by roots, bushes, and other vegetation that grow here in abundance. A faint tinkling noise of flowing water can be heard from the north.
110783: A few bird nests can be spotted in the trees. The dense canopy of branches blocks out the sun almost completely, making it hard for the sun-loving plants to survive on the forest floor. An opening in the canopy has formed here, as an ancient tree succumbed to the circle of life, creating an opportunity for small trees to compete for the small amount of sunlight that passes through the opening.
110784: Many different kinds of trees grow here. Pine, oak, maple and other species struggle for life. Thick needles of pine-trees cover the ground, forming a dense carpet. When the wind blows, leaves and branches sway back and forth, making all kinds of sounds one can only hear in forests.
110785: A bear is here, covered with coarse black fur (red aura).

Heavily networked branches cast a thick shadow on the ground. Rarely can the eye of a traveller spot a mallorn-tree around here, but to the north and the east the mellyrn seem to increase. Sounds of wildlife come from the west, but in the eastern direction the forest seems quieter.
110786:
Delicate golden blooms adorn the ground like a cascade of stars.
A large eagle soars above you.

Mellyrn can be seen everywhere, mixing with the other trees. Their great golden crowns extend upwards in a breath-taking view. The thin branches of the graceful trees support a shimmering sea of leaves. In some places tree-roots have come out of the ground, as if in attempt to obstruct passage through the woods by sending unwary travellers tumbling to the forest floor.
110787: The trees here grow hoary and grand, their limbs encrusted with mottled lichens and draped with verdant drooping mosses. The turf is a soft springy carpet of verdant green, nurtured by fair weather, rich soil, and the close proximity of Nimrodel. Here and there are sprinklings of tufted pink flowers, their heads nodding gently in the breeze.
110788: This high bluff is covered with venerable trees, their wide branches drooping over the rushing waters below. The ground is richly covered with lush vegetation. A curiously shaped granite rock offers a spot that looks inviting and comfortable to sit on, should one be so inclined.
110789: The trees rise upward to a dizzying height, their branches interlocking to form a thick canopy that blocks out all illumination to the forest floor. No smaller trees grow here, nor are there many ground-plants, as the lack of illumination has stunted their growth. Eventually one of the mighty trees shall fall, leaving a window of sunshine to foster new growth.
110790: Although this forest grows thick and healthy, it bears only a passing resemblance to the far older, grander forests of Beleriand. Though these ancient giants seem timeless, even they will fade and be forgotten in time.
110791:
Delicate golden blooms adorn the ground like a cascade of stars.
A small grasshopper clings to a blade of grass, ready to spring.

Many mellyrn grow here, mixing with oaks and elms. The golden trees grow together in clumps, as if to protect whatever lies in their centre. The slender trunks and branches of the mellyrn contrast sharply with the thicker trunks of the other trees. Occasional bird calls echo down from the thick canopy of tree-branches. A carpet of fallen leaves blankets the ground.
110792:
Delicate golden blooms adorn the ground like a cascade of stars.
A nightingale is here, chirping a sweet melody.

The silvery boles of the mellyrn rise, tall and slender, into the shimmering canopy of green and gold. The leaves of the trees rustle gently though no wind reaches the ground where the air is still and fragrant with the scents of many flowers and grasses.
110793: A nightingale is here, chirping a sweet melody.

Great mallorn-trees extend upwards for hundreds of feet. Fallen golden leaves cover the soft green grass. Small mallorn saplings stretch their slender branches to the sky. While the forest appears ancient, no fallen trees can be seen and the standing trees bear no traces of aging or decay. A soft mixed scent is in the air, like the scent of new grass and flowers in springtime.
110794:
Some small rocks have been piled into a mound here.
A nightingale is here, chirping a sweet melody.

A few grey rocks lie here, partly covered in thick green moss in which some small insects can be seen jumping and crawling. Though this forest is apparently ancient, the weathered rocks are its only part that shows any signs of aging. The golden mellyrn that grow here are of a great height, yet their bark is smooth and firm as that of saplings and there are no fallen trees or tree-stumps. Many small bushes and shrubs grow by the silvery boles of the mallorn-trees.
110795: Delicate golden blooms adorn the ground like a cascade of stars.

The golden trees seem very vibrant here as a powerful river sweeps by, feeding the forest with fresh water. The wind carries the smell of water as it travels by. The soft sound of the river lapping against the shoreline can be heard from the north and east.
110796: A few scattered mellyrn dip their roots gladly into the pristine waters of Celebrant as she flows swift and true towards Anduin and ever onward to the sea. The forest thickens rapidly as one recedes from the banks on either side.
110797: The tall trees of Lothlorien rise to great heights. Between and behind the silvery trunks a flowing river makes a wide turn, running past to the north and east. The riverside is spotted with mossy rocks and small bushes that grow in dense clusters next to the arching river bend. The forest grows denser away from the sparkling waters of the river.
110798: A sparrow is flapping around on the ground.

A few low-lying conifers and scrub oaks huddle under the shade of some ancient rowans, their high-tiered crowns far above you. This forest looks old, old beyond reckoning, where the trees despite the cycle of life appear as old as the rocks. Rough green beards still adorn the tall mountain oaks, with flowers and berries as their mantles.
110799:
A fallen tree lies on the ground, its clump of roots pointing upwards.
A sparrow is flapping around on the ground.

Tall and stark, hoary oaks reach their remaining branches far above the floor of the forest. Below them, humbler trees vie for the remaining light, while underneath all is a blanket of leaves. All about you the forest spreads in every direction, making one route seem as good as any other.
110800: A variety of oaks, ash, and lindens grow tall like elder statesmen, their rough bark cracked and furrowed with age. Their tall crowns reach for the sky far above, with faint beams of light illuminating a carpet of mosses and clumped plants spread below.
110801: Tall and grand, with curtains of dry moss hanging like beards, the trees here stand a bit taller and appear a bit older than elsewhere in the surrounding forest. Oaks, ash, and a wayward rowan all rise proudly above the mottled undergrowth, their long limbs rocking back and forth in time to some vernal rhythm.
110802: A small brown snake is slithering around here.

Fresh and pristine like the first day of spring regardless the season, this section of forest looks like it has not changed in a thousand years, yet there is no palpable aura of agedness about the place. In a strange, Elven fashion it seems both old and young at once.
110803: Each trunk, bough, and leaf is an exercise in beauty; delicately precise yet disdainful of contrived handicraft. Instead there is a blended quality of exact unyielding precision coupled with organic boundlessness: a true expression of creativity polished to magnificence.
110804: A tall stag is here, grazing peacefully.

Soft light illuminates a golden carpet of leaves, belying the dense, deep shade of woven canopies above. Like a story told and retold, yet always retaining its initial energy, these ancient woods follow the pattern of the seasons.
110805:
A shallow pond is here, tinted green with algae.
A magpie is flying around looking for some food.
A magpie is sitting here protecting her nest.

A dark mere, ringed with a dense ring of trees, occupies a small bowl-shaped depression amidst the forest. The pool's surface is laced with algae and small lily-pads, and reflects beams of radiance back upwards to the trees' outstretched limbs and the sky beyond.
110806: Mellyrn intermingle with bushes and other vegetation, forming dense walls coloured in shades of brown and silver, green and gold. Tall and grand do the trees rise, their crowns a symphony of whispering leaves dancing in the breeze. A narrow pathway weaves between trunks and bushes to the west, and a round, dark maw awaits to the north, leading into a cavern beneath the forest's floor.
110807: A big, brown, angry-looking bear is here.

A small cave opens up under the dark soil of Lothlorien. The cave is about five yards wide and ten deep. A few twisting roots hang from the ceiling. The floor has been stomped smooth, only some rocks litter the ground. The exit out is located between two huge boulders to the south.
110808: The waters widen into a crystal-clear pool before spilling in a sparkling curtain over dark, time-polished boulders of basalt. The splashing echoes off a nearby cliff-face encrusted with lichen and petite lavender blooms. To either side of the stream, the forest grows lush and green, nurtured and nourished by the cool, pure waters of the Nimrodel.
110809: Falling with a gentle sigh into a narrow declivity, Nimrodel rushes onward, her progress constrained by the steep-sided gorge. The sound of her passage resounds and builds with an echoing of burbles and murmurs that linger long after the initial sound has faded.
110810: Fresh and bright as a new day dawning, sparkling in tones of blue, Nimrodel careens north, twisting waywardly over and around rocks and obstructions. Great, grand old trees stand watch along her banks, ever dutiful as the centuries flow by.
110811: Soft, musical tones accompany Nimrodel's journey over polished rocks and gravel, the music sad and wistful, yet compelling and beautiful nonetheless. Her fate, though tragic, does nothing to diminish the memory of her loveliness.
110813: An Old Cottage by the River

An old cottage stands in the middle of a fluttering sea of verdant grasses beside the glittering Silverlode. Tiny blossoms like fairy dust are spread amidst the growing carpet. The idyllic panorama is framed by the towering mountains to the north and west.
110814: Warped floorboards and mouldy discoloured walls frame a small entry into what was was once a cosy riverside cottage. Crude pegs fashioned from sawed-off tree branches protrude from the eastern interior above a short wooden enclosure partially caked with mud. The western wall is extremely rotten, having seen more than its share of moisture due to the sagging roof on that side of the abandoned dwelling.
110815:
A large cabinet capable of storing goods is here.
A large, dusty alcove sits in a wall, smelling of soot.

A cold, dark fireplace sits unused in the centre of a large room that must have been used as a primary living area. Old cobwebs now occupy every corner, though even the inhabitants of the webs seem to have moved on. A thin layer of fine dust has settled on the floor and atop every surface, while the northern wall appears damp and rotten from moisture that has seeped in over time. Several small tufts of fur ranging in colour as well as thickness lay scattered across the floor as if left unnoticed by the previous occupant.
110816:
A canoe has been left here.
A dirty shovel is lying on the ground here.
A sturdy crate made of nailed wooden planks sits on the floor.
A well-used clothes line is strung between two walls.
On the line are a black wolf fur, a brown fur and a fishing net.

Various crates and miscellaneous tools still lean against the walls of an old storeroom left in disarray. Sturdy shelves line the walls near the low ceiling, and a pair of large hooks remain fastened securely to the eastern wall. A thin cord, mouldy and somewhat frayed, still dangles diligently between two sets of shelves on opposite sides of the room.
110817: A mass of tattered fabric lies here in a heap.

A meagre nook containing only a makeshift bed overlooks the river to the south through a crude but carefully constructed window. The alcove protrudes from the back of the cottage as if it were added on after the rest of the dwelling had been initially constructed. It affords more living space in the central room while moving the bed into a separate, cosy area with a good view of the nearby water.
110818: Flat lands of dun and grey are relieved by tufts and patches of ribbon-grass, upon which bloom minute alpine berry-blossoms. To the north are the grand peaks of the Misty Mountains. To the west are more peaks, albeit shrouded in fog and clouds. Beckoning the true of heart, the Golden Wood can be seen stretching out to the east.
110819: Mottled patches of heath and briar are interspersed with tufts of dark green grasses. To the east a great forest arises; tall summits pierce the skies to the north. A small burned patch of grass next to a boulder denotes that this place was recently used as a camp by some passer-by.
110820: A few oak and beech trees stand widely spaced among open fields of scrub and tender grasses. The wind can blow freely between the boughs carrying pollen and tree scents to the insects that dwell here. To the southeast there are fewer flowering plants and, perhaps not coincidentally, the forest also deepens.
110821: Here, a giant mulberry tree stands tall and proud, looking from afar like the canopy of a chariot. It seems to beckon in welcome, its limbs softly stirring even in the lightest of breezes. Floral creepers wind up its trunk, caressing its limbs, and beyond it the grand forest quickly thickens, concealing what lies beyond.
110822: A squirrel scampers around here, looking for nuts from the trees.

The trees grow in small huddles. Each stand like a small congregation, they mutter softly amongst themselves, their limbs stirring in the breeze. The forest grows more dense to the east, impenetrable to the eye. Thorny creepers cling to trees, legs, and clothing in turn.
110823: A roe deer is standing here, watching the terrain while chewing the vegetation.

The tallest peaks of the Misty Mountains loom above you to the north, grey- spired veterans of ages long past. The days of their existence stretch back into memories so distant as to resemble the tremulous mists that now enfold the mountain heights. These memories are now reflected only in one place, the eaves of Lothlorien.
110824: A long-bodied animal with thick brown fur bounds through the trees.

Steely-coloured stone that has rolled and slid from the lofty peaks above give way to softly undulating hills dotted with briar and spotty heath. A variety of small bushes and clumps of scrub support a moderate amount of fauna, which struggle to grow amid the wayward rocks.
110825: The rolling spaces here support a healthy quantity of vegetation, despite the apparent absence of water. Despite the growth, the land nonetheless has a bleak quality, cast in grey, only relieved by the sprinkling of petite white flowers shining amidst the thorns.
110826:
A reddish-brown shrub with purplish-pink flowers grows here.
Inside the shrub, there are a cluster of purplish-pink flowers.
A blue dragonfly is circling around.

The land swells abruptly, revealing a backbone of steely grey stone, above which cling hardy grasses and tumbled patches of gorse and brambles. Forest extends as far as one can see to the southeast, but to the west is a wide saucer-shaped flatland of verdant lawns.
110827: First a lone tree, then scattered clusters of broad-leafed deciduous trees stand side by side with pristine mellyrn, the golden trees as fresh and vibrant as the days before Arda was sullied by the hands of Morgoth. To your east, the forest thickens into an endless sea of mellyrn.
110828: Hundreds and hundreds of young mellyrn rise here, silver-skinned and elegant, like a promenade of beauties at a grand, rustic ball. More mellyrn spread out in all directions, growing fresh and unsullied, almost like they did during the age of the lamps.
110829: Tall mellyrn grow profusely here, their graceful, smooth trunks splaying out into weaving branches that shade the sky. The ground beneath is soft turf, rich soil that supports a variety of grasses and small flowers in addition to the grand old trees.
110830: One great mallorn stands here above all others, its limbs stretching far, far above you. Dense foliage blankets its branches, and the other trees seem to huddle close to the matriarchal tree, their tops nodding slowly in the breeze like sleepy children huddled for a bedtime story.
110831: An opossum stands here, sniffing around the ground.

Tall and proud, ranked in evenly spaced rows, mellyrn raise their limbs to the sky, their branches draped upon each other to form a dense canopy. Light filters down through the spaces, glimmering and dancing upon the waters of Silverlode. The forest continues to the east, deepening and thickening.
110832:
A solid, but stunted, rowan tree has established itself here.
A fierce boar is here, making grunting noises.

Scattered stands of straight-limbed oaks coupled with an occasional rowan grow here, thickening to the east and fading to the west into fields of holly and heather. To the south and east, the forest becomes more closely knitted, and silvery trees are seen in all directions.
110833:
A low and wide-spread tree grows here.
On the tree's branches, there are two juicy plums.

The forest parts here and lays itself open to the arching vault of the sky. A field of green and amber spreads out underneath the firmament, littered with golden-eyed flowers of blue and violet. Birdsongs echo on the breeze, their melodies complimented by the soothing murmurings of the Silverlode.
110834: Rendered craggy and twisted by the wind, these small scrub-oaks nevertheless display a hearty vitality and leafy green verdure. Beneath them the grass grows lush and thick in the fine silt cast aside by the Silverlode in her relentless journey into Lorien.
110835: Rising waist-high to a man, the grass here flows like water in the wind, dancing to the weather's whim. A small sandy bank lies alongside the river, shimmering like mother-of-pearl. Beneath the clear water a bed of rocks lies distorted by the flowing stream.
110836:
A trout swims here.
The prominent fin of a silver-yellow fish breaks the surface of the water.

Resplendent in shades of blue and aquamarine, the Silverlode bustles merrily, splashing, frolicking and shimmering with all the colours of the rainbow. There is an old settlement to the north, and behind it, fields of the purest green rise slowly from her northern banks, fading into purple mountain highlights not so far to the north.
110837: The prominent fin of a silver-yellow fish breaks the surface of the water.

Vibrant and alive with a myriad of glimmering reflections, the icy waters of Silverlode tumble gracefully over a fall of green-hued stone, reforming in a spray of foam amidst a beautiful dell. A sharp ridge looms above you to the south, and to the north the dell is replete with fir-trees and layered underneath with lushly verdant brush and undergrowth.
110838: Here a bubbling stream running from the west joins its waters with the hurrying flow of the Silverlode. Together they rush forth towards a glimmering falls, the water pouring over the drop to a boiling foam at the foot of the cascade.
110839: Dodging between great rounded boulders, the Silverlode divides into swiftly- flowing rivulets before reforming again and hurrying on her merry way onwards to Lorien. A number of fir-trees, short and bent, grow on a steep ridge to the west.
110840: The Silverlode swells her banks, slowing her progress momentarily, her force dissipated into swirling eddies and crosscurrents. To the north is a tall, waving sea of grass, the opposite bank in contrast is a thin finger of sand.
110841: Some small trees and shrubs line Silverlode's banks; all in all this seems a peaceful part of the river, replete with twittering birds and the gentle sighing of the wind. The gentle crackling of clear water over a bed of rocks can be heard as the current makes its way down stream.
110842: A river otter splashes playfully here.

Silverlode winds on, pausing only to deposit a large field of sand on the southern shore. A variety of fish dart through the waters. Grand old oaks and pines shroud the southern bank with their crowns of green; roots dip gingerly into the river's water.
110843:
A trout swims here.
The prominent fin of a silver-yellow fish breaks the surface of the water.

Silverlode froths and shimmers as her path rolls over shining rockbeds, among which silver-mailed fish frolic in the crystalline waters. Southwards, the land rises up sharply, forming a rocky, tree-covered patch of land. To the north, a glade of trees obscure the view.
110844: Tumbling over the falls to the east, the clear water sings and glitters like falling silver. The spray from the falls soaks both banks of the river making the ground here soft underfoot. It is said that the voice of Nimrodel herself can still heard in the singing of the water.
110845: Re-forming again from the mists of the falls, Nimrodel moves with swiftness and surety towards the east. The clear water splashes on the rocks of the river bend, and ambient light scatters from the waves on her surface, forming occasional tiny rainbows.
110846: Nimrodel flows now with haste and determination, drawing nigh to her sister- waters, Silverlode. Her banks widen, and she gladly joins arms to form the mighty Celebrant; her crystal waters swiftly intermingling and rushing ever onward, towards the distant sea.
110847:
A brook trout is here, swimming in the current.
A brook trout is here, swimming in the current.
A sparrow is flapping around on the ground.

Wide and strong flows Celebrant, newly joined by Nimrodel's influx, as she nears a bend to the east, the ambient light scattered in random spray from her rippling surface, creates tiny quivering rainbows under the light of the sun.
110848: The river slows somewhat as it turns eastward, rolling ever onward towards the Anduin. Unstoppable yet gentle in her progress, Celebrant graces the woods with her soft murmurings and life-sustaining waters. White-grey granite boulders line the shoreline on both sides.
110849: Large and well-smoothed boulders rise about the water's surface, crowned around with sprays and plumes of mist as Celebrant rushes past and beside them. The sound is nigh overwhelming, so much so that it is near impossible to hear anything else amid the roaring waters.
110850: The waters of fair Celebrant rush insistently onward, over broken boulders worn smooth by the river. As the life-giving water breaks on the rocks, it sends plumes of water onto the fertile soil that line the shores. A white granite boulder sits in mid-stream, causing the cascading waters to divide and then rejoin, all in but a moment of time.
110851: Flowing wide and strong, the Celebrant slices through heavily forested banks. Tall, silver-barked trees sway gently in the breeze, almost as if dancing to some enchanting melody. The water sparkles and glitters as it flows over a bed of smooth, rounded stones.
110852: Wide and gathering steam, the river sweeps all aside in its insistence to join the great river, Anduin. Lorien hides both flanks of the river as it dwindles into the distance with individual trees layered upon each other endlessly blurring into varying shades of green.
110853: The river bends to the east, and to the south and west, a mighty forest rises on its banks. Some tree-roots hang over the shoreline and cast their thirsty arms into the current. The water rushes noisily against the large rocks that lie in the middle of the river.
110854: A mountain mule is standing here, ridden by you.

Various types of grasses carpet this large field, contributing to make a very textured landscape. The ground is mostly covered by short, light green grass which has thin, wide blades. Among the short grass grow numerous patches of darker grass, with thin stems and a split top.
110856: A mountain mule is standing here, ridden by you.

Most of this plain is covered in a hard, brown topsoil with many small rocks thrown about the area. However inhospitable the soil appears to be, there are a few thin patches of short grass that have sprouted up, and seem to be doing quite well enduring the environment of this plain.
110858: A mountain mule is standing here, ridden by you.

An assortment of rocks and stones litter the ground here. They vary in shape, size, texture, and even colour. One of the larger rocks in this field has a smooth, flattened top that looks like a table. Strewn around it are many rough stones that catch the eye because of their very dark complexion.
110859:
The corpse of a black widow is lying here.
The corpse of a copperhead snake is lying here.

This natural, moist cavern appears to have been formed from years of rain and winds eating away the rock in which it resides. Many different types of rock are jutting out of the walls of this cavern, limestone and chalk being the most prevalent. The odd shapes and small nooks create deep shadows to the walls of the cave.
110860: A mountain mule (ulo) is standing here, ridden by you.

Large and small, almost perfectly round boulders are lying on the rocky ground. The landscape looks rather monotonous, with a countless number of grey rocks, indistinguishable from one another. This place has a striking lack of vegetation, literally nothing grows on this field. A few of the boulders are quite large, and have been cracked in half.
110861:
A rock lizard is here, motionless as it observes you.
A mountain mule (ulo) is standing here, ridden by you.

Only a few speckles of green grass grow on this low, flat field. The majority of the ground here is quite rocky, and is covered with moss of various colours, from dark red to pale grey. The tributary from the Misty Mountains can be seen to the north, meandering through the flatlands.
110862:
A reddish-brown shrub with purplish-pink flowers grows here.
Inside the shrub, there are a cluster of purplish-pink flowers.
Some small rocks have been piled into a mound here.
A mountain mule (ulo) is standing here, ridden by you.

The land seems to have merely a thin layer of topsoil on a rocky surface. The landscape is void of any tree cover, only patches of low-growing grass and heather endure here. Some huge boulders stand on the field. This place has a sombre feel to it, even the grass is lustreless and dull yellow in colour.

Yellow flowers, with grey-green foliage, grow in clusters here.
A mountain mule (ulo) is standing here, ridden by you.

Nurtured by the sun, wind and rain these fields are rich with dandelions, willowherbs, nettles and pasque flowers. Rich with colour and life this sea of flower is a sight for the sore eye. To the east, high grass begins to grow and to the south, grasslands that are more barren can be seen.
110965:
A snake slithers towards you.
A brown fox is here, looking for some rabbits to chew up.
A field lark stands here, focused on finding food.
A mountain mule (ulo) is standing here, ridden by you.

Long, lush grass grows in abundance on the plains that continue for miles to all directions. The ground undulates up and down a bit creating small knolls and grassy mounds in otherwise flat fields. There are swathes of dandelions, daisies, clover and other flowers among the grass, spotting the landscape with bright colourful dots. A small forest is visible far to the south-east.
110966:
A rock lizard is here, motionless as it observes you.
A mountain mule (ulo) is standing here, ridden by you.

Waist-high grass grows here coming to an abrupt end to the east where a thick wall of bushes begin. The grass here grows so densely that it is impossible to see through it to the ground beneath, but it feels solid enough to travel. These grass fields continue to the north and south but the bushes growing to the east would be impossible to penetrate.
110967:
A rock lizard is here, motionless as it observes you.
A colourful butterfly is fluttering around here.
A mountain mule (ulo) is standing here, ridden by you.

Solid rocky ground rises up from the high grass fields to the south. The ground climbs sharply to the east blocking the way there. Stunted grass grows where cracks in the rock allow their roots to reach the soil below. Some debris lies scattered around the terrain and the only signs of animals are birds occasionally flying over the plains. The rocky ground continues to the north.
110968: A mountain mule (ulo) is standing here, ridden by you.

Small hills rise all around and the rocky terrain is covered with broken stone. Where grass grows in this desolate plain, it is burned yellow by a relentless glare from the sun. Nothing more could ever grow here. To the north, these plains descend into grassland covered in very high grass and some trees.
110970:
A field lark stands here, focused on finding food.
A mountain mule (ulo) is standing here, ridden by you.

Small bushes and shrubs grow all around. The terrain rises slightly here and there and some signs of small animals can be seen. To the west, the Misty Mountains lie, surrounded by clouds, rising in the distance. Even without the sun, their sheer presence casts a huge shadow over the plains. The flatlands continue to the south and east.
110973: The small clearing inside the thicket is surrounded from all directions by tall, dark-green bushes, which seem to stretch their branches, leaves and twigs to conquer any remaining open space. No sunlight shines here. Numerous sharp thorns and even the small, narrow leaves on them have razor-like edges with little points on irregular intervals. There are some small openings between the plants to the north and south, which seem to reveal yet more bushes.
110974:
A large, dusty alcove sits in a wall, smelling of soot.
A mass of dark green leaves clings to a wall.

This is an old, two story farmhouse. Almost half of the southern wall is missing indicating that this wooden home has definitely seen its best times. Partially decayed wooden stairs, the bannister completely missing, lead up to the second floor. A fireplace stands on the western wall connected to the chimney, and a big oaken table occupies the centre of the room. The floor of the farmhouse is partly covered in grass. Near the northern wall there is a doorway into the kitchen.
110975:
A restless rabbit bounces around.
*an Orc*, wielding a narrow runed awlpike, is standing here.
Baelish the Dwarf, wielding a black metal staff, is standing here.
A stocky mountain mule is here, waiting to serve.

This is clearly a room for food preparation. Some shelves are attached to the walls and a small kitchen table is placed against the eastern wall of the room. Two small windows open onto a view of the front yard, and below them is a sturdy, full metal stove which has collected some rust. On the ground in front of the stove is a metal handle of sort, indicating possible entrance down below the floorboards.
110976:
A brass lantern has been set on the ground.
*an Orc*, wielding a narrow runed awlpike, is standing here.

Two small beds have been placed parallel with each other on opposite walls, these may once have been a soft and warm place to sleep but are now covered in mildew, the sheets have not been changed for quite some time. Between the beds, a window on the northern wall provides a view to the yard, letting light into the room. The ceiling is in reasonable condition and still provides some shelter from the rain. In places, hay can be seen protruding from the gaps in the wooden beams.
110980: Tall, yellow grass spreads out into wide, round field. So lush is the growth that it makes the travelling quite difficult and limits the visibility to the immediate surroundings. To the east there is a steep rise blocking the way while some trees and bushes are growing densely to the north.
110981:
The remains of a thick tangle of vines lie here in a heap of rotting compost.
The remains of a thick tangle of vines lie here in a heap of rotting compost.
The remains of a mass of vines lie here in a heap of rotting compost.

Dense bushes grow all around, the thick, twisted stems of neighbouring bushes have become entangled creating a dense wall of vegetation. The bushes are high as trees preventing the sunlight from reaching the ground and suffocating the lesser growth around them. The air is still, stifling and so dry as to be almost unbreathable.
110983: High trees grow close together with prominent roots that have erupted from the ground only to have moss grow over them. Very little sunlight penetrates the canopy here forcing the branches to grow towards the sky to seek out what little light is available. To the east, the sounds of water streaming by can be heard, and from the north, the smell of swamp-mud seeps in. The ground to the north is very moist and one would have to think twice before venturing there. The forest to the south seems so dense as to be impenetrable.
110986: A woodchuck is watching for enemies here.

The flat plains loom high above the river Anduin. The water, in all its power has worn out the northern bank, which makes it impossible to descend into the river to the north. The eastern bank is very smooth and steep, which makes it easy to slide down into the river, but most likely impossible to crawl back up.
110987:
A forest spider is here crawling around.
A woodchuck is watching for enemies here.

The trees grow wide apart, leaving space for small bushes to grow in the open areas. In one of the tallest trees, a tall oak, visible high above the ground is a perfect shelter for woodchucks to sleep during the night. To the north the trees vanish from sight, and flat land can be seen. The river Anduin flows below to the east. Its steep bank is covered with broken branches and roots of fallen trees.
110990:
Clusters of slender stems and tall leaves thrive in the mud and shallows.
A small leech is here, floating in the water.
A small leech is here, floating in the water.
A sparrow is flapping around on the ground.

This vast bog is filled with tall swamp plants which rise up from the suckling pools of moss, mud and water. Plants this high would only grow so tall if they had lots of nutrients and time. Many of these plants are as thick as an orc's wrist and tall as small trees, creating deep shadows and blocking the light from entering the swamp.
110996:
A large leech is moving close to you, searching for blood.
A large leech is moving close to you, searching for blood.
A long rat with a white-tipped tail seems indifferent to your presence.

The ground is waterlogged, and the soil beneath has turned into viscous, clinging mud. A horrible stench pollutes the air, and tree-like swamp plants grow high all around, blocking clean air and most of the sunlight from entering here. Vines drop down from these high grown plants as if reaching for the watery ground.
110997: Clusters of slender stems and tall leaves thrive in the mud and shallows.

A deep, muddy ditch runs through the area. Layer upon layer of thick, sticky, grey mud covers every surface making walking extremely difficult as the much sucks everything in. A foul smell rises from the stagnant pools of water that have collected in depressions in the soft mud.
110998:
A bass swims here.
A salmon swims here.

The rapids of the Anduin slam into the bank to the south, carving into the bank, as the river turns to the east in its travel. The riverbank to the south has been carved out so much, in fact, that it has a sheer cliff, impossible to climb.
110999: A Food Storage in the Cellar

A simple wooden chest is here.
A wooden cupboard stands here.

This is a cold earth cellar dug into the ground. The only way in or out of here is through a small hatch in the ceiling. The northern wall is of solid rock, which would, even in summer, cool this cellar quite well regardless of the temperature outside. All the other walls are just soil as is the ground. A wooden cupboard is standing against the southern wall.
111000: A Crude Shelter among the Bushes

A Morgundul orc snarls about here, looking for a fight.
A Morgundul orc snarls about here, looking for a fight.

Tall dark-green bushes grow in abundance in this area. Partly camouflaged by the vegetation, an old-looking shelter built from branches and moss provides partial shelter from the weather. There is a crude bench made from a log inside, and in front of the bench a small circle of rocks for building a fire. All in all this rough campsite can offer some shelter from light rain and wind.
111021:
A sturdy rope has been securely caught on a stump.
Some orange-red blossoms grow amid grey-green foliage.
A very old stump is securely rooted into the ground here.
A colourful butterfly is fluttering around here.

You have to climb the rockface for the last few meters, scuffing the soft rock walls with the soles of your boots as you acend. Atop the cliff you stand on a pale white stone slab from which the entire forestland can be seen. The huge stump is even bigger than it seemed from across the river, its immense size dominating this entire ridge. After closer inspection you notice only minor indications of age and decay and marvel at nature's ability to preserve her own as you know this stump must be generations and generations old.
111023: A small patch of dark-green moss grows in the deepest shade.

A thick cluster of trees grows along the edge of the cliff, kept moist by the constant flow of the river below, their thick canopy casting the ground into deep shadow. Dead foliage and decomposing leaves cover the ground, releasing a pervasive odour of decay. Above, high atop the largest tree in the vicinity, a small sheltered shack has been skilfully constructed.
111024: A wooden chest stands in the corner.

Although very small and somewhat ragged, you feel very comfortable sitting and staring out the windows of this little shack. You are yards above all the rest of the trees in the forest, and have a clear view of the land in all directions.
111026:
An arrow made from a grey wood lies here.
An arrow made from a grey wood lies here.
An arrow made from a grey wood lies here.
An arrow made from a grey wood lies here.
An arrow made from a grey wood lies here.
A finely crafted crystal lamp is hanging from a tree branch.
A golden spider rests on a tree-branch.

The forest suddenly opens up into an enchanting glade, ringed with mellyrn, but open to the vaulted sky. Underneath the forest floor is carpeted with grass and mosses of the softest and lushest nature, in the centre is a startlingly wide stump. The surface of the stump has been smoothed and polished, then coated with some sort of clear resin creating a glassy sheen on its surface. A good dozen people perhaps could be seated about it with no fear of crowding, though the soft matting of grass must suffice for a seat. Glistening spider webs lace the trees with dewdrops hanging from them like diamond adornments.
111027: Aspiring to heights above all others, a tremendously large and aged mallorn springs from the soil here. It is as close as could be to an aged mallorn, as its bark has begun to show the faintest signs of cracking and dullness. Nevertheless, the grand old tree radiates no sense of decay or weakness, to the contrary, it shows strength and prominence beyond that of other trees.
111028:
A black and white hound pads about alertly.
A black and white hound pads about alertly.

Sparkling boughs interweave their limbs above, coalescing into faintly fluted trunks of glistening silver rooted firmly in the rich loam of the forest floor. Essences of fragrances found not in mortal lands stimulate the senses, and vague song-like whisperings echo amid the trees.
111029:
A small mushroom grows nearby.
A small mushroom grows nearby.
A small mushroom grows nearby.

Here, the ever-serene trees grow denser and denser together. Their branches and boughs embrace each other, and in doing so they create an almost perfect circle-shaped enclosure with only one exit: toward the south, where the silver-laden forest continues.
111030: Ithildir the Noldo, wielding a scimitar, is resting here.

Spartan, yet comfortable, this flet undoubtedly stays warm and dry even in the fiercest of storms. Furnishings are limited to a sturdy desk and chair of crafted wood, some wooden cabinets treated with simple, elegant, inlaid carvings and a comfy bed. It stands high indeed, perched as far towards the sky as the ancient tree that holds it affords; one can survey the clear aqua gleam of the rivers to the west, framed by the hazy outlines of the mountains towering above. To the east and south stretch the vast glades of Lorien.
111031:
A squirrel scampers around here, looking for nuts from the trees.
A fallow deer is grazing peacefully here.
A fallow deer is grazing peacefully here.

Here the valley floor reaches its lowest elevation, and judging by the terrain, the spring thaws must bring at least a few small rivulets of water through the area. Thus it is that a small stand of trees manages to cling to life here. A lone oak of extreme age holds its proud head high amid a cluster of far younger pines and firs. Perhaps this ancient tree once stood at the borders of Lorien, but now the Golden Wood and the power within it have both faded and diminished.
111032: Small stones cover the bottom of part of the slow-flowing Gladden River. Most of them are covered by a slippery layer of dark green moss. There is a bend in the bed of the river that is noticed to the west, soon followed by another one which is downstream towards the east.
111033: This majestic road stretches off into the darkness eastward. Huge pillars line the walls, reaching up to dizzying heights before being lost in the darkness above. Along the walls between the pillars are carvings of dwarven heroes, shown in battle wielding huge axes and war-hammers. The floor is tiled in a mosaic of elaborate geometric patterns, still undamaged despite the passage of unnumbered years.
111034: Puddles and rubble cover the floor of the corridor here. To the east it looks as if a portion of the ceiling has fallen for the debris is much more prominent in that direction. A path has been kept clear here, apparently this corridor is still used. The statues lining the wall are completely encased in skins of mould and lichen, hastening the demise of these works of beauty.
111035: The road ends to the east in a large rampart of rocks, loosely piled to block further progress to the east. The roof is much lower here than in the passage to the west -- the ominous black stone hovers just overhead, pressing down toward the floor.
111036: The grand roadway passes west-east here. Huge pillars are lined along the walls and busts of famous dwarves are placed on cutouts in the walls. Between some pillars there are also complete statues of dwarves, depicted in their full armoury and glory.
111037: This cave is the repository for all of the skulls of victims sacrificed to the Dark Lord by the Durghash tribe. The floor is quite uneven and very slick here because the rock has been completely covered over by thick troll and giant skulls worn smooth by time and use. Each of the walls is dedicated to skulls from a particular race, and the 'orc wall' appears particularly full. There is a black wall panel left bare in the west wall which must be the inner side of a concealed door, and an archway made from Dwarven skulls in the north wall.
111038: The residence of the Durghash Shaman reflects the fear and power he wields over the rest of the tribe. He owns a vast collection of evil-looking knives which are hung like trophies on the walls here, as well as a huge pile of scalps and skins which all orcs treasure. Pungent incense burns in a bronze brazier which is located at the foot of a large stone pillar in the centre of this chamber. There is a set of stone chests in the northeast corner of this room and a large bed of bear furs in the opposite corner. The only exit from this place is through a black arch in the south wall.
111042: The corpse of a huge, hideous spider is lying here.

Several tiny tunnels come together here, but thick webs and cave-ins have blocked all the tunnels except the one leading to the south. The floor shows signs of regular and recent usage although no exit to the forest above can be seen. The high density of spider webs and the many roots lying around hinder movement.
111043: A rough, dug-out tunnel stretches north. The tunnel is far from straight and slopes up and down, like a giant animal burrow. The tunnel does not appear to be used as a nest, but rather for concealed transportation. Tree roots stick out of the ceiling and walls, and webs are spun across sections of the tunnel, hindering movement and ensnaring the careless. To the south, a cave-in has occurred, blocking that route. A hole in the ceiling leads to the forest above, but it is too slippery to climb up.
111044: Thick brambles and fallen trees have closed off this secluded area from the surrounding forest. The gloom is deep, and the forest canopy thicker than elsewhere. The ground is covered by numerous animal trails, wider and deeper than normal, as if the animals dragged something along with them. The trails lead to a hole in the ground, large enough to pass through, leading to a very steep tunnel. In the wide canopy occasional webbing can be seen, long thick webs hanging straight down from the tree-tops bearing witnessing to the presence of spiders.
111059: In the Shade of Forested Hills

The remains of a mass of vines lie here in a heap of rotting compost.
A colony of red ants is here. The ants seem to ignore you.

The wounded trees of the forest lean their crowns against one other, collectively supporting the heavy forest roof. The canopy is kept solid by the dense intertwining of the interweaving vines, boughs and branches. A steep slope rises to the east while to the west there is a small opening leading into the darkness.
111060: A dense patch of dark ferns grows in the shade.

Dense thorn bushes and bristling trees crowd in from all sides, making travel in most directions basically impossible. Thick moss dangles just above and vines seem to catch at the feet from below. A dim illumination permeates the area, although the forest reduces visibility and hinders any sense of distance.
111061:
A copper penny lies on the ground.
The corpse of a huge, poisonous spider is lying here.
The corpse of a huge, poisonous spider is lying here.
The corpse of a black widow is lying here.
The corpse of a black widow is lying here.
The corpse of a huge tarantula is lying here.
The corpse of a brown, long-legged spider is lying here.
The corpse of a brown, long-legged spider is lying here.
The corpse of a huge, hideous spider is lying here.

Dead leaves, plants and twigs litter the ground, with some branches jutting up through the mass like the rib bones of a bear. The dark and gnarled branches are blotched with lighter patches of lichen and fungi of different sizes and colours. The surrounding forest grows into a wall of tall oaks to the east, beyond which a glade can be glimpsed, and to the south where one cannot find any path between the twisting trees, vines and bushes where one could pass.
111062:
A copper penny lies on the ground.
A copper penny lies on the ground.
A porcupine is waddling around here, its tail full of sharp quills.

Under the canopy of the tall, high-reaching trees, a rarely-trodden path winds its way in a confusing manner between and around the trees of the dark woods. To the north and south the trees have grown their dark boles and gnarled branches so tightly that no trespassing is possible through the living wall of dark vegetation.
111063:
A copper penny lies on the ground.
A copper penny lies on the ground.
A copper penny lies on the ground.

Ancient oak trees covered with dark mosses, lichen and fungi stand tall, their dense crowns spreading high and wide, effectively blocking out the sky. The passage that is heading in an east-west direction through this area could be called a tunnel, so dark is it, and so densely grow the trees and the undergrowth on either side. To the north the vine-covered ground rises upwards, steeply enough to prevent passage up the slope.
111064:
A copper penny lies on the ground.
A copper penny lies on the ground.
A copper penny lies on the ground.
A copper penny lies on the ground.

Without warning a high cliff rises from the ground to the west and north. Tall, dark-green shrubs cover most of the base of the cliff, giving way to huge trees that stand in silence a few yards away from the cliff. One can proceed from here to the south and east, far below the dark canopy which is blocking out the sky, allowing no light for the creatures and plants below.
111069: A very long, narrow tunnel opens up here. The walls are just raw rock that shifts in colour, all varying from pitch black to bone white. The rock is cold to the touch and the sharp edges looks almost hostile as the walls stand so close together. No light comes in through the exit from the north, the air is very damp and every breath you take thickens in your lungs. The ceiling is high above and large smooth stalagmites hang a few feet down from the roof.
111070: The floor is covered with material coming from rocks, crushed over and over again to make a smooth black sand. The walls are rough and do not have the same finish as the floor, as if the work was abruptly stopped for some reason. Along all the walls are deep cracks running from floor to ceiling, varying in width. On various places iron rods have been hammered into the cracks.
111073: Ground ivy makes the forest floor close to impossible to explore. Moving about requires precise navigation and care. A slope leads slightly upwards in the east, through ravaged trees and vines. A stench of decay lies heavy over the area. The dense Mirkwood forest expands its kingdom to the south, into yet darker, more sombre areas.
111075: Log Jam in the Anduin River

A seemingly endless amount of wet, black logs have formed a huge log jam in the Anduin. There is so much timber here that it actually appears possible to cross the mighty river with dry feet, provided that one can maintain ones balance on top of the slippery and deceptive path; a path that zig-zags from one log to another, sometimes rising, sometimes descending.
111078: The floor in this part of the wide halls slopes down until it turns into a wide pool of silvery water. The pool's surface is still and shining like a polished mirror, yet deep down it is filled with a faint light. The light seems clearer and cleaner than anything you have ever seen. Sometimes it seems the light would come from within of the pool's water itself; these silver reflections are only faint, but still bright and blinding as the highest sun.
111100: This cave offers you respite from the harsh wind and cold of the outdoors. But what is this?.. the walls are covered in strange markings..like the claw marks of some very large animal. Or maybe animals. A strange smell wafts from the east and makes you want to gag. Perhaps you may just want to rest here then move on.
111102: A rotten corpse is hanging here.

Pheeeew! This place really stinks. What sort of creatures could make this much stench, you wonder. Looking at the floor, you can see piles of half-chewed bones, many with shreds of putrefied flesh still attached. The cave extends to the south, and from here you can hear some shuffling and scratching sounds. Maybe it would be wise to leave before the inhabitants decide you will be the next meal?
111103:
An infant troll, baring its teeth, snarls here.
An infant troll, baring its teeth, snarls here.
An infant troll, baring its teeth, snarls here.
A nasty troll female crouches here, with a feral look in her eyes.
An old, strong cave troll is standing here.

The stench in here is even worse than in the front of this cave, and suddenly you see what left those bones out the front. The walls look like they have been hewn out of the rock with the bare hands of the monsters that live in here. peering into the gloom you can see the saliva dripping down the chins of these trolls.."dinner is served" they could be saying.
111115: The place seems to have been unused for many years. Grey tombs rise from the ground, with the names of long dead persons on their surface. Everything is ruined and dark, and beyond the grid that surround the graveyard you can only see decayed trees that seem to escape from it. Just when you were convinced that the place was completely abandoned, you think to hear some noises from an impressive grave in the middle of the yard. Your body shivers when you hear the sounds again...
111116:
A mottled snake is sneaking here, ready to sink its fangs into flesh.
A mottled snake is sneaking here, ready to sink its fangs into flesh.
A black snake hurries towards you with sly intentions.

The air down here has a heavy stench. This place has been closed for a very long time, as you realise when looking at the dusty ground. On the walls you see the niches where the occupants of this crypt found a place for their final rest. Beyond the reach of the light you are holding something is moving. The shadows are too deep. Maybe this place was not good enough to rest forever.
111155: A large growth of old fungus grows thick on the walls and causes this small cave to reek like an old dwarven war boot just after a campaign. The shape of the walls suggests that this cave was not created just by the forces of nature. The ceiling seems to have been made into a dome. East is a broken doorway to another cavern. The western wall is covered by a large patch of mold. The cave continues south.
111156: The broken stone shelves on the floor and scattered on the walls suggest that this was a store room for some ancient dwellers. The floor is muddy making it slippery. Two arches rise from the corners of the room and cross in the middle of the ceiling, shaped into somewhat of a dome. Some airducts are worked into the ceiling but no light filters through them. A doorway leading to the west is partially collapsed and if it ever held a door, no remains of it are left.
111157: A crack runs through the low roof of this slighty damp cave. The smooth floor and walls suggest that this cave was carved by rushing water long ago. It is now large enough to allow an easy passage. There is a faint draft of cool air coming from the vegetation southwards.
111158: The tunnel is dug through the stone. The walls are supported here and there by roughly hewn stones. The ceiling is cut into an arch. There are doorways to the north and east. In the south the tunnel has collapsed providing no passage. Water drips down from the ceiling. A large puddle is formed in the middle of the room.
111159:
A little stone lies on the ground.
A large round whetstone rests on the ground.
A large bat is here, hanging in the darkness.

This room is perfectly round and its roof domed. The chamber is surprisingly well preserved from harm when compared to other rooms in the cave. A stone grate is constructed in the floor allowing the water to drain and in the walls, near the curve of the ceiling, are some ventilation ducts which keep the air here quite dry. However, this has not prevented the decay of the arms which must once have been here, for there are none; only a weapon rack made from polished stone stands against one wall.
111160: An elven archer dressed in green is here, watching the forest.

By climbing out upon this broad, silver-skinned branch, it is possible to reach a point within the mallorn tree-top from which one can see for several miles to the east and south. The bulk of the tree lies north and west of this lofty perch, so that visibility in those directions is completely blocked by the foliage. In the east, the mighty Anduin flows through several wide bends, marking one border of Lorien. Beyond this point, a green, forested ridge rises to a rocky peak and follows the river's north-south course. Away to the south, the mallorn-trees intermingle with smaller, deciduous varieties; a trail may be seen leading away in that direction, out of the elven lands.
111169:
A quiver lies on the ground.
A finely crafted crystal lamp is hanging from a tree branch.
A coil of rope is lying here.
A circlet of golden flowers has been left here.
A small oaken table has been set here.
On the table, there are a lembas wafer, five ash arrows, three flagons, two loaves of white bread, and three large yellow apples.

Built high above the ground, deep within an ancient mallorn treetop, this large flet is surrounded by magnificent colours that bring to mind the treasure hoard of a mighty dragon of legend. Sturdy tree-limbs of smooth, unflawed silver support thick bunches of leaves that glitter and shine as they sway in the breeze. Built of wooden planks lashed firmly together by several lengths of thin cordage, this structure has only two walls, above which is stretched a green, woven tarp. It appears that the walls are portable and may be moved around, depending on the wind direction.
111170:
An elven archer dressed in green is here, watching the forest.
An elven archer dressed in green is here, watching the forest.

A small, irregularly-shaped platform has been built into the crook of two thick mallorn-boughs and the smooth, silver trunk that connects them. The structure seems to be designed as a waypoint from which it is possible to continue climbing up into the mighty tree; to this purpose, a slender rope ladder extends up into the golden tree-crown. The sound of soft, musical voices can barely be heard from that direction. Below, the trunk plunges deeply into the forest's earth floor; many more mellyrn grow nearby, so that visibility is hindered at this level by their dense foliage.
111185: At the Bottom of a Steep Staircase

A path runs along the southern side of a cliff overlooking the valley of the Bruinen. A set of stairs leads upward toward the Last Pavilion. A majestic latticework faces this staircase, preventing any climber from falling down the corbelling of the path. The rock wall to the north is very steep, and the only way up is the set of stairs carved into its surface. The flank of the cliff is made of a white stone flecked with countless black spots. A delicately carved trellis along the path supports numerous climbing plants.
111186: A mass of dark green leaves clings to a wall.

This bridge links two parts of a collapsed cliff on the north side of the river Bruinen. Just below the bridge, the mass of rock that would be the missing connection lies in the water, forming a reef around which water flows in small rapids. The bridge is covered by an arched roof of white tile; to either side of it, there are white marble railings overgrown with wild plants. A slight recess in the cliff wall enables a glimpse of the Last Homely Home which lies at the top of the cliff.
111187: A solemn group of statues stands in eternal contemplation.

A path runs along a natural ledge that was carved by wind and rain. The passage is sheltered by the stone mass of a cliff above it, which provides a natural roof. A low railing, dark in colour to match the walls, has been added for safety. A dozen statues are carved into the wall, each bearing great detail in their solemn gaze over the river below. The smoothness of the carvings and the alcoves that host them match perfectly with the well-maintained path. Below and to the south, the Bruinen laps on the rock, producing a soft melody.
111188: A Narrow Ledge over the Bruinen

A very narrow path runs beneath an overhanging mass of stone. The ceiling is delicately decorated with floral patterns sculpted into the rock. The ground has been carved to yield the smoothest possible surface to walk on. In a number of places along the path, there are shallow alcoves which might make excellent places for an artisan to isolate themselves and work while contemplating the Bruinen valley that stretches out below.
111189:
Yellow flowers, with grey-green foliage, grow in clusters here.
A large, orange pumpkin is here.
A dark green cabbage is here.

A broad path forms a natural terrace overhanging the Bruinen to the south. Passing years have gathered a wide variety of plants to this unique environment which is isolated and exposed to the weather. The result is a natural garden where vegetables grow freely in a simple harmony exalted by the colours of many blossoms. A small depression at the foot of a cliff stores rainwater for all that lives here. The peace of the garden is occasionally disturbed by the clamour of a pier on the Bruinen which lies to the east.
111190: On a Balcony over the Bruinen

A mass of dark green leaves clings to a wall.
A white-painted bench is here.

A wide, flat shelf protrudes from the side of a cliff, forming a natural balcony over the river Bruinen. A paved path snakes along the shelf, bending left and right to fit the curves and recesses of the cliff wall. A wooden roof covers this balcony, and at the edge of the shelf there is a railing made of delicately carved marble which perfectly matches the white pavement. A steep and narrow marble staircase plunges down towards a small house at the water level.
111191: Thick tangles of vegetation have taken overtaken this path, joining vines that cover the wide, steep cliff to the north. Though the plants grow wild and untended, the vegetation forms five arches over the trail, meeting a railing that runs along a ledge overlooking the Bruinen. The path broadens to the west, and the cliff wall begins to descend to meet it.
111192: A Slopy Trail over the Bruinen

A path runs uphill and downhill over a series of gentle slopes. To the west, it skirts a rocky spur too rugged to traverse. On the ground, smooth gravel mixes with short grass that softly dampens any footsteps. To the north, a lovely and colourful plain occupies a slight depression.
111193: This path is made of fine, smooth gravel that barely makes a sound, even under the heaviest of footsteps. A natural barrier made of a variety of low, thorny bushes and flowering plants protects travellers from a fall to the Bruinen river, which runs along the trail and fills the air with its soft chant. To the north, a branch in the path turns onto a steep but negotiable slope.
111194: This terrace sits about five feet above the Bruinen. It is encircled by a wooden balustrade which is finely engraved with floral patterns that evoke the summer varieties of the valley. The sounds of the river are tempered by the wooden boards that form the terrace, making the area a calm and relaxing place for contemplation. A rock wall runs along the northern edge of the terrace; a natural crack in this wall provides shelter for a myriad of small herbs and white flowers. In the southwestern corner, a gap in the railing allows an unobstructed view of the valley.
111195: A Plain near the Last Homely Home

This plain sits in a wide depression between slopes which rise to the west and to the east. Numerous, varied blossoms grow in a natural and pleasant hotchpotch. There are a few cottages on the plain; the residents likely benefit from the cool air in the vicinity of the Bruinen as well as the contemplative remoteness of the vale. A lush grove grows to the north.
111196: A broad plateau overlooks a path along the Bruinen. A steep slope descends abruptly to the west, offering nothing but a long fall to the valley below. On the plateau itself, there are a few cottages and cabins. Many flowering shrubs surround them, making the area a lovely place to live and to stroll in. Wildlife flourishes in the calm isolation of the plateau.
111197: A humble man stands here, ready to help you with your things.

Inside a tight circle of trees, an elven home has been built between the trunks, and on the branches of, living trees. The branches have skilfully been shaped into furniture; there are sturdy branches to sit upon, a wooden plate set as a table surface upon a natural framework, and entwined slender boughs forming a narrow bed above. On the ground, a small spring bubbles clear water.
111198:
A white-painted bench is here.
A sturdy bed made from solid oak lies here, covered in warm blankets.
A humble man stands here, ready to help you with your things.
A tall and strong guard is here.

This torch-lit chamber offers a sense of serenity for the homeowner and her guests. The Noldo glyphed hardwood floor symbolizes the race Asako is known for. A bookshelf constructed of red-oak is placed against the wall facing towards the bed, holding a multitude of scrolls. A comfortable stone bench is located next to the bookshelf where guests may be seated. A four pillar king bed is situated next to the open window where cool air entises the room. At the other end of the room, a statue of Rogon is overlooking the door. Jewels and scalps of enemies are placed on the pedestal as an offering to Rogon to whom Asako fights for.
111212: With its low ceiling and bare rock walls this is not a pleasant place. A heavy-looking oaken prison door blocks the exit into a neighbouring cell to the north, and this cell continues further to the south. A few bundles of rugs lie on the ground, obviously used for sleeping.
111213:
A deep, impenetrable darkness lingers here.
Annariel Tingliwinde is here, fighting Lhurank (brenny).
Lhurank (brenny), wielding a darkened orkish axe, is here, fighting Annariel Tingliwinde.
Klaees (thedon), wielding a two-handed sword, is here, fighting Annariel Tingliwinde.
Dracol (reaper), wielding an ornate, steel-shafted warhammer, is here, fighting Annariel Tingliwinde.
Abyzuz, wielding a barbed fang, is standing here.
Drazud (freshmeat), wielding a great warsword, is here, fighting Annariel Tingliwinde.

The red stone of the chamber walls has been carefully carved to form an almost perfect circle - not for any aesthetic reason but a much more sadistic one - the screams of the victims will reflect off the walls causing their shrieks to echo. Prisoners nearby will be in no doubt as to the fate awaits them in here. It is clear that this room has been in near-constant use for a long time. Filthy, bloodied rags litter the floor, and the hideous devices that litter the room are worn from frequent use. To the north-west a furnace burns, filling the room with sulphurous fumes.
111221: A long, low tunnel extends to the east, where it abruptly ends in a featureless stone wall. Along the southern edge of the passage a long, low table holds examples of the torturer's art; knives, thumbscrews, shears, pokers, and collars of various designs, all worn and more than a few bloodied. The northern wall is dominated by a large wooden device, its various straps and attachments folded and gathering dust. The torturer seems to have moved on from simple physical pain to more mental form of torment for his victims. In the corner, next to the abandoned equipment, a wooden lever sticks out of the wall.
111241:
An albino salamander is here, perched on some rocks.
An albino salamander is here, perched on some rocks.

Like the edge of a treacherous mountainside, the ground is filled with marks and slashes. Tiny little streams course through the little valleys formed by the slashes on the floor. From this small cavern there are but two ways to journey. To the north lies an underground stream, whilst another passage climbs almost vertically from here.
111247: The spacious hallway runs east to west. On the red velvet-covered walls you notice some portraits of ancient elves, whose exploits during the first age of Middle-earth are now legend; Fingolfin, high king of the Noldor elves, Maedhros, the most famous son of Feanor, and Thingol Greycloak, Sinda king of Doriath.
111248: This cave runs from west to north, descending quickly into the depths as it goes. Drops of water fall from dozens of cracks in the ceiling, and trickles run down every wall, gathering into a thin stream at the centre of the cave. The floor is smooth and slick, making it treacherous.
111249:
Something cold and scaly slithers past your leg.
Something cold and scaly slithers past your leg.

This entire area is submerged in a lake of dark water that is heavily laden with minerals leached from the stone overhead. Drops fall in a constant shower from the ceiling, and a narrow trickle enters the lake from a tunnel to the south. Echoes bound and rebound from every wall, filling the cavern with noise and making it difficult to distinguish specific sounds. A broad shelf of stone rises out of the water to the east.
111250:
A skeleton of some humanoid lies in the dust.
A shade is here, shrouded in an inky blackness.

This shelf of rock stands just above the surface of a black lake to the west. It is forty or more feet across from north to south, but only half as deep. Walls of flaking, sandy rock curve upward on every side, merging into a domed ceiling high over the lake. The only visible way to leave here is across the lake.
111251: Massive, tangled roots cascade down the round shaft forming a natural stairway and allowing easy passage to both directions. Essential to the thriving life on the surface, water trickles down a fissure and forms a clear pool between the jagged rocks of the bottom. Half-way up, a small passage opens to the east but is abruptly cut off by heavy rocks.
111252: A tall stag is here, grazing peacefully.

You have no idea what or who that might have created this small cave. Small bugs swiftly scurry across the rocky ground as you enter. At the back of the cave the roof slowly slopes down to meet with the bottom of the cave. During bad weather this place could give some shelter to the tired adventurer. The only way out seems to be the same way as you entered from under the bridge.
111255:
A sturdy bed made from solid oak lies here, covered in warm blankets.
A humble man stands here, ready to help you with your things.

The room is crafted out of a thousand dark grey rectangle stones and styled as if it were a giant keep. Several tapestries are lined up on most walls, save for the northern wall where a map hangs instead. A few torches take up the rest of the empty space. A few end tables bear random trinkets and a few chairs are lined with a variety of elaborate cloaks for mending. It feels like home.
111269:
A skeleton of some humanoid lies in the dust.
A huge, hungry-looking rat is here.
A huge, hungry-looking rat is here.
A huge, hungry-looking rat is here.

This tiny room is obviously some sort of jail cell. It is dusty, and the floor is littered with rubble. In the corner is a dark stain, but it is hard to tell its exact nature. But the most overwhelming thing about this chamber is the foul stench of death and decay.
111270: Small Clearing at the Foot of a Golden Trunk

A majestic, golden mallorn stands at the centre of a small clearing, hidden deep inside a dense shrubbery. Tussocks and tufts of delicate grasses adorn the ground, and white perennial flowers dot the clearing. Vegetation in the hues of green, yellow, and gold conspires to form impenetrable walls around the clearing; and indeed naught can be seen of what lies beyond. The golden boughs of the great mallorn hang low and close to the ground, offering shelter and a place for weary legs to rest.
111271: A slim elven ranger casts her gaze over the forest.

High in the air, a round flet rings the trunk of an exceptionally tall and majestic mallorn. The flet blends seamlessly into the canopy, its construction simple and elegant in its imitation of nature. A sleeping mat, several chests, and a table occupy this abode, shaded by a dense roof of tangled branches.
111275:
An elven scout, wielding a dagger, is standing here, eyeing the river.
An elven scout, wielding a dagger, is standing here, eyeing the river.

Several planks of mallorn wood have been fashioned into a long and wide vessel, slightly curved and with a flat bottom. At the side of the ferry there is a large, robust-looking wheel mechanism connected to a thick rope that stretches all the way across the Anduin. Sturdy borders made of thick planks have been erected at the edges of the ferry. A few boxes of cargo are tethered in the middle, next to a post where mounts could be hitched to as well.
111280: The forest is very dark and cold here, and the trees are like black giants that look as if they extend infinitely toward the sky. The trees seem to whisper to each other through their slow, rhythmic creaking. High up in the branches, small, silk-wrapped cocoons can be seen hanging.
111282:
A tiny spider is here, eating a tiny bug.
