A tiny spider is here, eating a tiny bug.
A tiny spider is here, eating a tiny bug.
A tiny spider is here, eating a tiny bug.

The forest is quite dense and the branches from the immense oaks have formed a seemingly impenetrable canopy overhead. Along the trees and on the ground there is a blanket of spider-infested cobwebs. Numerous knotted roots snake across the forest floor which might make unwary travellers stumble.
111283: The forest here is pretty thick and dense, and the sheer quantity of vines hanging down from the huge oaks makes it even darker. The vines seem to protect the old trees from danger and almost appear to react to movement within the forest. Between two giant oaks to the north, the carcass of some long-dead creature is suspended from snaking vines several feet above ground. In a line running from north to south, the forest floor appears to have been disturbed. The disturbance disappears to the south through a large cobweb that is strung between trees.
111284: The Old Forest Road has not been used for a very long time, but it is still in very good shape here. Small breaks, which allow limited travel off the road, can be seen to the north and south. A faint reddish trail runs between the breaks across the road. Ancient trees tower over the road stopping any hope of direct sunlight breaking through. The road continues to the east and west.
111286: Most of the Old Forest Road is intact here. However, some of the stones have come loose from the surface of the road and now lie scattered along the roadside. Otherwise the road is in very good condition for travelling on foot or on horseback. The crowns of the trees to the north reach out over the road casting it in deep shadow. The forest blocks the way to the south.
111287: Over the years wind and rain has washed away small parts of the road. Fallen branches and leaves lie undisturbed on the road. Despite the flaws in the road's surface, travel along the route remains quick and easy. The branches and crowns of the trees lining the road are blocking out most of the sky.
111288: Bend in the Old Forest Road
A dark iridescent dragonfly flies by.

The road makes a sharp turn to the north and west here. Some fallen trees can be seen and need to be avoided. Here and there on the road, roots of the massive trees lining it breaks the paved surface. The place has been cast into deep shade by the thick canopy overhead and little can be heard save for the forest creaking.
111289: Bend in the Old Forest Road

The road stretches from this bend to the east and south. The road surface has deteriorated leaving a thin layer of gravel over the remains of the paved road. To the north, it is impossible to force a path into the forest because the trees stand too close to each other. To the west, a dense thicket seems to have fallen under heavy darkness, and the shifting branches seem to form grotesque shapes that defy closer examination.
111290: A cluster of dark green, feathery fronds flourishes in the shade.

The road through Mirkwood runs straight to the east and west. On the ground, fallen branches and wilted leaves lie scattered, covering roots that encroach onto the road from the surrounding forest. Several small ravines in the road's surface seem to have been made by erosion. Flanking the road, black yews and beeches rise tall, their branches reaching out above the road to cover the sky. The road is kept in deep shadow and the only sound around here is the distant chattering of small animals.
111291: This section of the Old Forest Road runs in a straight line from east to west. Although it was built with great skill, centuries of use have not been kind, and the road has become rough and unkempt. The woods on either side encroach upon the road, with dark trunks rising just feet from the road itself, looming inwards and all but meeting above almost as if Mirkwood is poised to strike and swallow the road in one rustling gulp.
111292: The road continues east and west, lying upon a bed of solid rock apparently carved out of the short bluff to the north. The trees and branches to the south lean out above the road, which meet with the branches of the trees towards the north. The dense canopy makes it very difficult to see the sky at all. To the south of the road, the ground slopes downwards and is quickly obscured behind large bushes covered in thick, sharp and black thorns.
111293: The stonework of the road is worn and weathered. The paving is cracked and in places grass and small plants sprout up through the road's surface. The forest to the south looks oppressive, and no visible path weaves between trunk, root, or shrub. The tree-tops rise a little higher to the north-west, though it is hardly noticeable through the canopy.
111294: A large, flat stone is visible beneath a layer of lichens and fallen leaves.

The road continues here, east and west, a solitary straight line amidst the dark, foreboding forest. On the edge of the road a stone rises from the forest floor. The stone is covered by fallen leaves and lichen. Branches span the road overhead, but appear to be thinning to the east. To the north an exceptionally thick hedge of thistle and thorn-covered bushes bars the way.
111295: The forest is held back by the Old Forest Road here. Instead of the sprawling crowns of trees, a narrow shred of the open sky is visible above. The road continues straight on to the east and west, carving a path through Mirkwood.
111296: A brown snail is crawling across the ground here leaving a slimy trail behind.

The ancient forest road is largely overgrown by bushes and shrubs; the trees of Mirkwood stands further away from the road, as if held at bay by the thorny brush. In some sections of the road, where large bushes have threatened to block it completely, someone has taken a blade to them. Thus atleast a narrow path to follow is ensured.
111297: The ancient forest road continues on through the depths of Mirkwood to the east and west. The brooding trees stand some distance from the road here, as if hesitant to approach it. Instead, the terrain is dominated by large, sprawling bushes. The road continues through brush to the west, while the forest gathers courage to the east and the road disappears beneath the shrouds of a dense canopy.
111298: Obstruction in the Old Forest Road

A massive obstruction of uprooted trees blocks the road to the south.
A fierce wolverine is here, snarling at you.
A fierce wolverine is here, snarling at you.

The worn roadway makes a wide turn as it continues beneath the dark, stifling wood. Massive boughs reach out from every trunk, grating against and fusing with neighbouring trees to form a natural system of cramped tunnels beneath. The road itself carries on as the largest of these gnarled and worn tunnels.
111299:
A huge gnarled oak tree is here, looming ominously overhead.
A dense patch of dark ferns grows in the shade.

Encroaching gnarled oaks grow close enough together to fuse and form numerous solid walls of creaking wood. A great thickness of foliage in the canopy combines with dense tree growth to make both darkness and stale air prominent within the deeps of the wood. No traces of daylight reach the forest floor, and not one current of air stirs so much as a single leaf on the highest bough.
111300:
The corpse of a seasoned Durbuk-hai scout is lying here.
A fallen tree lies on the ground, its clump of roots pointing upwards.
A bright orange bracket fungus grows on some decaying wood.

A slope, rugged and forest-clad, ascends into the Emyn-nu-Fuin. It begins as an imperceptible rise in the forest floor to the west, and becomes increasingly steep to the east. Rugged, rocky soil covers the twisted feet of colossal oaks as they break and split their way through thick bedrock below. Several species of fungi hang from stone faces and fill even the thinnest cracks as dark mosses grow widespread upon the hard bark of trunk and branch.
111301:
A scrawny Durbuk-hai orc is here, chopping at a thick tree with a small axe.
An elite Durbuk-hai guard is standing here, armed with spear and shield.
A scrawny Durbuk-hai orc is here, chopping at a thick tree with a small axe.

Gargantuan trees tower over a wide boulder-strewn mountainside. Exposed slabs of pure granite create steep escarpments between wide patches of rock-filled soil. Various swaths of the forest floor reveal broken stone blocks partially masked beneath layers of great dark roots.
111302:
A tree-snake lies wrapped around one of the tree branches.
A tree-snake lies wrapped around one of the tree branches.
A tree-snake lies wrapped around one of the tree branches.

The forest in this area mainly consists of dark elms and lichen-covered oaks. The lichens sway slightly in the wind, resembling the long grey beards of dwarven-folk. The ground is covered with twisted roots and sickly green undergrowth. A flat broken slab of stone is barely visible beneath the foliage.
111303: A brown snail is crawling across the ground here leaving a slimy trail behind.

The forest here is quite dense, and there are many fallen trees that make travelling here troublesome. The fallen trees are mostly rotten, and they are covered by fungi and lichen. Even the thicker trunks scattered about the forest floor break apart at the slightest touch.
111304: This part of forest is almost impassable; thickets of vines, intertwined roots and branches make walking here tiresome. To the north, it looks like the forest is completely overgrown, creating a wall of interwined vegetation. For a good climber it would perhaps be easier to move above near the treetops if one could climb up there.
111305: A dark iridescent dragonfly flies by.

A very thick and tall black yew is growing in the area. Its branches thicker than a leg, its bark tough and black as night, seems to control the area with its strong presence. Locked in a never-ending battle with vines, roots, and the forest itself, the black yew manages to hold all other vegetation at bay as it stands here in lone majesty. It looks like one could climb up the tree along its strong branches.
111306: Top of a Sprawling Black Yew

A large, black butterfly is fluttering about erratically.
A large, black butterfly is fluttering about erratically.
A large, black butterfly is fluttering about erratically.

Here, in a crown high above the other tree tops, the foliage is crawling with spiders spinning their small webs. Dozens of dark butterflies flutter about here, looking for nectar. As far as the eye can see, the forest spreads out endlessly in all directions. Only to the south can a small line be seen marking where the road is.
111307: An almost imperceptible path is here, running in a westward direction. It parts the trees on either side of it, and no grass grows on it. A thin layer of dirt lies upon this ancient foot path. Small shrubs grow on either side and occasionally spill over into it. To the south, a seemingly impassable wall of vegetation blocks the way.
111308: Several trees bear the scars of axes and many more have been badly burnt. The trees seem to have sustained these injuries many years ago as part of an epic battle fought through the woods. The forest here is a bit sparser than the surrounding forest, which makes travelling here relatively easy.
111309:
A fallen tree lies on the ground, its clump of roots pointing upwards.
A pile of dry, brown leaves lies here.

This part of the forest died a long time ago and only a few blackened, rotten stumps remain. Fallen boughs of once-mighty beech trees lie rotting upon the ground, mosses and lichens having engulfed them in a blanket of green and yellow. The damp air is thick with the scent of decay, and despite there being fewer trees here, it still feels as foreboding as the darker areas of Mirkwood. The forest descends suddenly to the west.
111313: No sign of the sky can be seen overhead as the trees crowd in close and the foliage forms a dense canopy above. So closely do they grow that it is almost impossible to find a path through them. The ground is full of places where roots have broken through, and care should be taken when putting down a foot or guiding a mount through. Fallen branches lie scattered about on the forest floor, covered in mould and grey moss.
111314: An enormous tree stump lies here emitting a strong, rotten smell from its core. The smell is that of long-dead flesh but the stump looks like ordinary wood that is long dead, sodden, and rotted through. An almost tangible veil of darkness seem to hang from the trees.
111315: The trees in this part of Mirkwood are dark and foreboding. They rise on gnarled, twisted trunks that seem to bend and buckle under the weight of massive, sprawling crowns. The thick foliage above forms an impenetrable ceiling that blots out the sky with more finality than even the darkness of Sauron could muster.
111316: A tall pine tree grows here.

Within this patch of forest, shrubs of all kinds grow. The ground is moist and soft and very fertile, serving as excellent soil for plants and trees to grow in. Tall pine trees, their branches reaching down as if to grab at something, creak under the weight of their crowns. Their needles are very sharp and almost seem to gleam threatingly. The shifting trees give the sense that nothing can move here without being seen by their vigilant gaze.
111317:
A Durbuk-hai warrior is here, ill-equipped but ready to fight for his tribe.
A Durbuk-hai warrior is here, ill-equipped but ready to fight for his tribe.
An elite Durbuk-hai guard is standing here, armed with spear and shield.

What were once great oaks, have now become twisted and warped trunks covered in foliage that runs in shades of black and brown. It seems almost as if the massive quantity of ivy and lichen that grow on them drains their life away. The forest floor here is covered in layers of rotting leaves that fill the air with a faint scent of decay. Dry twigs and branches can be seen poking up through the layer of leaves in places.
111318: The forest floor rises upwards slowly towards the east where a mighty tree is visible. The trees grow thick and tall on the slope to the south; ash and oak stand among dense groves of oddly twisted pines. The forest floor is moist and the air clear despite hanging vines dangling like delicate webs from overhead branches. The only evidence of activity here are small animal tracks in the undergrowth.
111319: While the dense foliage makes it difficult to see, something seems to hang up there, suspended high in the trees. There are no easy places to climb up the looming trees though. The undergrowth shows signs of being trampled, as if this area sees traffic from large creatures with some regularity. Thick, thorny bushes growing between the trees prevent passage to the north and south.
111320: The ground, where it's not overgrown by thorny bushes and thistles, is littered with sharp rocks. High overhead, just beneath the thick canopy, cocoons and webs of silky threads sway gently in the wind. Tall, gnarled linden trees appear to twist and shake in even the slightest breeze sending a rustling sound through the woods.
111325: An unusual variety of trees grow here; ash, oak, fir, elm and alder. Their branches intertwine high in the canopy where they form great twisted arches of branch and leaf. The entwined branches from a giant dome-like structure in hues of green and brown beneath which a tainted crowd of thistles and thorns gather amid the trunks and roots. The foliage is less dense to the south where a road is barely visible through branches and shrubs.
111326:
A huge warg is here, moving in for the kill.
A ferocious warg is here, snarling angrily.
A ferocious warg is here, snarling angrily.

The ground between the trees is dotted with black flowers that spread their petals to catch the feeble rays of light that break through the canopy above. Even the few small flowers that have managed to grow here give the place a vibrancy that is missing in the darker areas of Mirkwood.
111327: A huge gnarled oak tree is here, looming ominously overhead.

The trees in this part of Mirkwood grow so dense that the bark of the gnarled trees rub and scrape against one another. Great, wide branches spread out above, creating a thick canopy that leave only hints of a sky visible beyond.
111328: A brown stag looks around with big, startled eyes.

Great gnarled oaks grow closely together to form mishapen tunnels beneath their many fused branches. Long strands of lichen dangle from the upper boughs, standing still in the stuffy stale air under the ancient trees that serve to block both wind and breeze from reaching the lower reaches of the forest.
111329: The wooded foothills dip down into a bowl-shaped depression, making the already stale air even denser and therefore thicker. Untamed foliage encroaches upon even the lowest tree branches while serving to block out any light that might have reached the foresaken forest floor. Massive clumps of thick, spore-covered fungi permeate all of the earth not occupied by hulking trunks covered in shed spores and rotting moss.
111330:
A pile of dry, brown leaves lies here.
A black moth flutters around.
A large, black butterfly is fluttering about erratically.
A large, black butterfly is fluttering about erratically.

Great hulking trees with warped boughs thrust threateningly from the empty ground here. Dry, cool earth has formed a thin crust above a frenzy of tangled roots laying just below the surface, evidenced by their sources standing tall and menacing. The air is quiet and still, save the occasional creak and infrequent rustling among the leaves.
111331: A brown snail is crawling across the ground here leaving a slimy trail behind.

The trees grow so close to one another that their branches intertwine, forming an impenetrable barrier to the north and west. Ancient trunks with rough, cracking bark creak to and fro as they sway in some unheard and unfelt wind. The sheer volume of undergrowth choking the forest floor belies what little light manages to pierce the upper canopy during the day. Large beds of ancient moss, partially covered by thin layers of rotting fir needles, lie beneath thick tangles of vines that grip both trunk and stone.
111332:
Massive roots shift uneasily all around you.
A small, dense tangle of roots covers the ground.
A black moth flutters around.

Old, gnarled trees twist and turn toward one another as they reach around large boulders laying strewn throughout the woods. A near-vertical cliff juts up out of the soil to the north, covered almost entirely by a thick crust of green lichen. Massive roots dominate the ground not occupied by hulking stone as they continue to ruthlessly split rock and puncture soil on their relentless pursuit of that which is nowhere to be found above ground.
111333: A large, black butterfly is fluttering about erratically.

Massive fir trees growing in great clumps have created a vast but very dark grove inside the forest of Mirkwood. Their towering height, combined with their large number of boughs and branches block nearly all light from reaching the ground. Great gnarled roots plunge into the earth around the bases of the trees, leaving paths between them covered in the shed needles of those malevolent and ancient entities.
111334: A brown stag looks around with big, startled eyes.

Thick, knobby trunks intrude upon one another's space as branches intermingle and boughs grow together within the depths of Mirkwood. Clumps of matted ivy race across the ground to claim all soil not already occupied by the great trees, which stand tall and foreboding in spite of their twisted forms.
111335:
A monstrous grey, putrid fungus is growing on a large oak here.
A huge black fungus is here, exuding a foul stench.
A huge black fungus is here, exuding a foul stench.
A giant, strange looking green fungus is here, ready to devour you in seconds.
A huge black fungus is here, exuding a foul stench.
A huge black fungus is here, exuding a foul stench.
A giant, strange looking green fungus is here, ready to devour you in seconds.
An ancient fungus smothers the boulders.
An ancient fungus smothers the boulders.

The thick, strong boughs in the lower reaches of the trees grow together so tightly and so completely that they form an artificial floor in the canopy, preventing access to the ground altogether. Upon the natural wooden platform rest thick piles of dead and dying leaves, decomposing to form the homes of strange fungi that sprout up in various clusters.
111336:
Massive, black, oozing vines reach out from the choked canopy.
Some black, oozing vines reach out from the choked canopy towards you.
Some black, oozing vines reach out from the choked canopy towards you.
Some black, oozing vines reach out from the choked canopy towards you.
A brown stag looks around with big, startled eyes.
A large, black butterfly is fluttering about erratically.
A black moth flutters around.

Crowded trees, steep earthy walls and countless tangling vines combine to form a stifling ravine. The ground is covered with tough, springy creeper growth in every direction reaching up above the top of the ravine itself. Even the tree roots themselves are overrun by one senseless mass of interwoven runners.
111337: A large, black butterfly is fluttering about erratically.

Columns of great oaks and firs reach to the unseen skies along this curved, steep slope. Titanic stones in the form of sheer rock walls prevent passage north and east. Mighty roots thrust downward from the trees themselves, cracking and splitting stone even as great boulders from above lay resting atop broken and shattered trunks in an age-old battle of tree versus mountain.
111338:
A Durbuk-hai warrior is here, ill-equipped but ready to fight for his tribe.
A Durbuk-hai warrior is here, ill-equipped but ready to fight for his tribe.
A Durbuk-hai warrior is here, ill-equipped but ready to fight for his tribe.
An elite Durbuk-hai guard is standing here, armed with spear and shield.

Two exceptionally large pine trees grow here amidst a dark forest of oak and beech. A faint smell of decay comes from the ground where the lower layers of needles and leaves rot beneath more recent fallen foliage. A gate of wood, reinforced with bands of metal, is standing to the west. A high stockade encloses the parts of the area, making it impossible to see what is inside. Above the gate, the huge, fanged head of a spider is nailed onto a beam.
111339: On the ground there are obvious tracks of life. There are some blood stains leading south beneath a half-built guard house that has been erected between three massive black oak trees. All directions, except south which leads toward a road, seem to have been cleared at some point but are now choked off due to the forest undergrowth having vigorously grown in.
111340: A set of steps have been carved into the rock at the eastern end of this tunnel. The steps lead up to a slab that blocks the exit. The tunnel runs through crumbling and cracked rock and the walls are reinforced with stones of irregular shapes. While the craftmanship seems lacking, the mason was aware of his lack of skill for the ceiling is supported by thick beams of roughly-hewn wood at even intervals.
111348: Deep in the Forest of Mirkwood
A pile of dry, brown leaves lies here.

Ominous, black yew trees grow in this area. As a result of that, many rotting piles of leaves lie undisturbed on the ground. High up in the foliage, there are hundreds of cobwebs and threads hanging and swaying slowly in the wind. The dense foliage allows almost no light through.
111349:
A grey spider is stalking here, preparing to drain you of life.
A small, red-spotted spider lurks here.
A small, red-spotted spider lurks here.
A small, red-spotted spider lurks here.
A small, red-spotted spider lurks here.

The trees here are too dense to let any light through and because of that there is barely any undergrowth at all, except some sort of fungi growing here and there. A white and foul-smelling wall barricades the way to the east. The wall seems to be made out of rotten trees and a lot of cobwebs.
111350:
A small, red-spotted spider lurks here.
A small, red-spotted spider lurks here.
A huge, horrific spider is prowling here.

There are cobwebs woven all over the trees and there are spiders everywhere. It is hardly possible to set down a foot here without crushing a spider. To the east stands a great archway formed from stooped trees and masses of thickly knotted cobwebs. From the archway hang several thick, sticky strands of spider-silk, in contrast to the other cobwebs these seem to have been freshly spun. Some pattering and squeaking noise can be heard originating from beyond the archway.
111351: Foul webs span across Mirkwood, engulfing the exit down with their complex patterns.

The forest is fairly bright here but it is not because of any break in the canopy. All around are strands of silver-white webs covered in beads of dew that glitter and sparkle. Everywhere on the ground thousands of small spiders scurry about or lurk in tiny webs. These small spiders are likely newly hatched and, in time, will grow much larger.
111352: Thick, white cobwebs coat every visible surface and numerous spiders can be seen crawling over them, maintaining their sticky traps. The black oaks that grow here have become twisted and bent and now lean over the smaller plants as if threatening their very existence. An overpowering foul stench emanating from the east engulfs the whole place.
111353:
A huge, poisonous spider is here.
A huge, poisonous spider is here.
A newborn spider is here.
A newborn spider is here.
A newborn spider is here.
A huge, poisonous spider is here.
A huge, horrific spider is prowling here.

Silky webs cover most of the walls in this cavern, leaving only small sections of dark stone visible. In some of the webs, huge and bulky spider sacs are suspended. Every now and then a sac quivers and trembles as if the spiders inside were excited by the presence of prey in their hatchery.
111354:
Foul webs span across Mirkwood, engulfing the exit up with their complex patterns.
A huge, poisonous tarantula extends her legs to you.
A huge, poisonous tarantula extends her legs to you.
A small, red-spotted spider lurks here.
A small, red-spotted spider lurks here.
A huge, horrific spider is prowling here.

Broken, crumbled cocoons of various sizes and shapes litter the floor, while those that look fresh hang suspended from the ceiling or cling to the walls. A dark, sticky liquid is seeping from some of the newer cocoons where they hang from the ceiling by strands of silvery spider-silk. The fluid has begun to pool on the ground in repulsive pools of liquified flesh.
111355:
A partly mummified cadaver is dangling in a web.
On the cadaver, there are a plain pair of sleeves, a plain shirt and a plain leather belt.
A huge, poisonous spider is here.
A huge, poisonous spider is here.
A newborn spider is here.
A newborn spider is here.
A newborn spider is here.
A newborn spider is here.
A newborn spider is here.

A strong smell of death permeates the air throughout this part of Mirkwood. The forest is very dense, and dark trunks tangled with thick undergrowth form a small, enclosed area. This area is used as a den by giant spiders, judging from several corpses that are hanging from branches by thick white cords. The forest floor is littered with bones and sharp, jagged rocks, all completely immersed in a sea of cobwebs.
111356:
An emaciated warg, half-mad with hunger, is here.
An emaciated warg, half-mad with hunger, is here.

A rugged mountain slope rises above the lower forest to the south. It is not steep but the terrain is scraggy and strenuous to travel across. The forest grows thick and strong in spite of the difficult terrain. Round, lichen-encrusted stones litter the bases of trees and form strange piles on beds of dark green moss wherever the trees appear slightly less dense.
111357: Slope at the Base of a Great Cliff

A rugged slope rises above Mirkwood; the foothills of Emyn-nu-Fuin to the north-east. The slope ends abrutly at an almost uniformally high natural stone wall. The vertical cliff suddenly shoots upward from among the rocks and tree trunks without warning, blocking passage to the east. Dark, stringy shrubs have pushed their way through the topsoil, revealing their small but menacing tentacle-like vines that grasp greedily at all other vegetation nearby.
111358: Steep foreboding cliffs cuts through the wide, boulder-strewn ridge on its west side; a wooded slope is visible at their feet. Mighty trees, ancient oaks and towering firs, grow abundantly in thick groves. Encrusted lichen forms sporadic patches on the grey boulders that rests under the dark shadows of the foliage.
111359: Wickedly sharp splintered stones jut from the grey, rocky surface of this wide ridge. Ancient fir and oak trees grow among the rubble, forming a dense canopy overhead. Strands of dangling lichen hang from nearly every branch and boulder. Old moss spreads out cross the ridge, entirely filling the various cracks and fissures produced by the insatiable growth of swelling roots.
111360: A deft, young orc monitors the area, ready to attack any enemy.

Even large trees have somehow managed to grow in the nearly vertical walls of this narrow gorge. The gorge leads upward to the south, snaking this way and that. The steep mountainsides to the east block passage higher into the Emyn-nu-Fuin. Long, tensile vines stretch from branch to rock face and back again as they wind their way up jagged cracks and through tangled rootballs. Devoid of any water, the gorge floor consists solely of smooth but frequently-cracked stone, various large trees bursting through fractured piles of pebbled rubble, and mounds of dead leaves that have yet to decay into a sparse layer of soil.
111361: This wide, rugged ridge, gloomy and perilous, is but a harbinger of the higher mountains to the north-east. Thin slices of sharp shale form frequent outcroppings beneath heavily knotted oaks that seem to meld together as their twisted roots and stumpy branches intertwine. The stones themselves thrust upward from unknown depths, lacerating the surface soil to protrude dangerously between great clumps of tangled shrubbery.
111362: A small centipede is here scurrying about.

Untold numbers of towering firs crowd the uneven top and steep sides of a wide, rugged ridge stretching from north to south. Large boulders lay strewn between many of the ancient trunks as they share one continuous bed of twisting tangled roots. Atop boulder, root and trunk alike grows a constant bed of dark green moss that fills every cranny and crevice.
111363: These bluffs overlook a vast, green blanket of canopy to the west. The steep cliffs rise atleast a hundred feet to get to these plateu-like bluffs, and a broad-faced stone wall rising to the north towers another fifty feet. The faces of the stonewalls are covered in grey-green moss and white lichen. Trees crowd on these rugged mountains, chiefly mammoth oaks and towering firs. Around the base of every trunk grows large clumps of dark green fungi with fine hairs protruding from fat stalks topped with bell-shaped caps.
111364: A rock lizard is here, motionless as it observes you.

Untold numbers of jumbled boulders have come to rest in the remnants of a great rockslide on these rugged mountains. The rockslide seems to have originated from the north, where the mountains climb yet higher still. Tall trees have long since grown over the entire slide, once again filling the forest with darkness and stifling the winds that once wafted down through a rare and brief gap in the trees. A thick layer of light-green lichen covers every surface of each individual stone and drapes lazily from various rocky overhangs in thick curtains.
111365:
Massive, black, oozing vines reach out from the choked canopy.
A mass of wriggling vines drops on you from the trees.
A mass of wriggling vines drops on you from the trees.

No light reaches the depths of this narrow stone-walled canyon, and no air currents stir at its bottom. The canyon continues to the north, squeezed in between the ridges and crags of Emyn-nu-Fuin. It's filled to the brim with tall firs warring for the relatively small amount of space available along the cracked stone floor, all other vegetation has been choked out by the thick straining roots of the towering trees themselves.
111366:
A small, dense tangle of roots covers the ground.
A mass of wriggling vines drops on you from the trees.

This canyon is surrounded on three sides by steep mountainsides that looms threateningly, as if ready to bury this narrow canyon beneath the mountains at any moment. Looming fir trees grow so densely here that they threaten to become one great mass of tangled gnarled wood with only low passages still present about their feet. Large knots appear frequently upon the thick trunks like boils on the necks of trolls while long, abundant boughs interleave such that it is difficult to distinguish one trunk from the next.
111367: A giant earth beetle is standing here.

Mountainous slopes climb towards the heights of Emyn-nu-Fuin. The terrain is intersected by ravines, crags, and jutting outcroppings of dark, moss-clad granite. Yet Mirkwood prevails even here, as trees, bushes, and undervegetation thrive. The trees are mostly gnarled oaks and ancient firs; they spread their great boughs overhead, and create a green roof that shrouds all but the largest outcroppings. Winding masses of loose vines hang ominously from stony crags and narrow ledges, forming black tangles that seem to be in constant movement.
111368: While mountains here on the southern outskirts of Emyn-nu-Fuin are not towering, looming peaks, they still make formidable obstacles for a traveller. These slopes are rugged, covered in broken rock and treacherous crevices. Mirkwood, ancient and brooding, covers these parts of the mountains completely, enveloping them in blankets of brown and green. Broad, gnarled roots thrust downard into the dark soil. Hulking arms of hard, twisting wood have splintered the rock beneath the topsoil to produce an uneven slope littered with jagged granite shards precariously covered by a thin layer of rotting leaves.
111369:
A mountain goat is here, jumping from cliff to cliff.
A young orc grips his weapon impatiently, eager to prove himself.
A young orc grips his weapon impatiently, eager to prove himself.
A Durbuk-hai warrior stands here with a frenzied gleam in his eyes.
A Durbuk-hai warrior is here, ill-equipped but ready to fight for his tribe.
A Durbuk-hai warrior is here, ill-equipped but ready to fight for his tribe.

A bald dome bulges from the surrounding forest. Its sides are rounded, worn smooth from centuries of erosion. Rough, mottled lichen coats the surface in an uneven layer. Aged linden trees crowd at the base of the dome, gnarled branches crawling up the sides as if to drag the mountain down.
111370:
A mountain goat is here, jumping from cliff to cliff.
A mountain goat is here, jumping from cliff to cliff.

A narrow range of the Mirkwood Mountains rises in a double peak of jagged summits separated by a shallow dip. This hollow is covered in a tangle of crooked trees growing around massive boulders. The summits themselves are covered in black, twisted shrubs growing in rocky soil.
111371: The range of mountains dips to form a narrow valley surrounded on three sides by densely forested slopes. Overhanging branches spill over into the hollow, tangling with the crowns of the trees that grow from the depths of the valley. Black, sinuous creepers cling to branch, trunk, and twig. Their sharp thorns catch on passing creatures; movement only serves to cause further entanglement.
111372: A large, black butterfly is fluttering about erratically.

Piles of rocks and boulders mix with tangled and knobby roots, making for rough terrain that is strenuous to traverse. Dense shrubbery thickened by fallen leaves hide perilous, narrow crevices that cut deeply into the slopes. Eerie chittering emanates from these gaps, hinting at creatures that thrive in darkness deeper than that under the shadows of the trees.
111373: Strange rock spires crown a string of knobbed crags. Their tips gaze over the treetops. Their bases are covered in phosphorescent moss making them appear to glow at any time of the day. These luminous pillars contrast starkly with the surrounding murk; enveloping branches cast eerie, skeletal shadows.
111374: A patch of moss grows here on a wet, flat stone.

Great cracks stretch across these hills. The larger cracks broaden into crevices several yards wide. Fallen trunks and thick, gnarled roots form natural bridges across these gaps. Vines trail from the trees and wind around blackened vegetation that creeps in from the murky shadows below.
111375: An unbroken wall of densely packed oaks runs along the north side of an uneven, rocky slope. These thick, broad-branched trees crowd out all other vegetation, and stand in stark contrast to snarled undergrowth that forms a writhing mesh down the slope to the south. These two extremes are held separate by a rocky slope between them, where the trees are more sparse, but the sterile soil prevents the growth of underbrush.
111376: Giant, hulking oaks tower over uneven terrain. Swelling hills stretching for miles are visible between the widely-spaced tree trunks. Misshapen mushrooms with caps several feed wide cover the spaces between trees. These fungi rest in a bed of putridly decaying foliage fallen from the canopy.
111377: The slanted ground beneath long, slender trees in the darkness of the forested hillside is covered entirely in soft green moss. The light-coloured vegetation blankets every stone and engulfs every trunk, even growing between exposed roots and down into cracks in the hard gnarled wood itself.
111378: A very heavy branch is lying here on the ground.

The forest floor rises steeply to the east with many twisted roots weaving over one another amidst large rotten branches that lay scattered about the darkness. Exposed rocks dot the slope, resting firmly in hard packed soil that appears resistant to smaller vegetation beneath the mighty trees that devour all light from above.
111379:
A sprawling green bush of stinging nettle grows here.
A small and tough weed grows here.
A man's-waist high evergreen shrub grows here, with bright green branches.

Trees and shrubs are indistinguishable as they suffocate one another in an engulfing blur of darkness beneath the impenetrable canopy. The forest ground seems to rise toward the north and decline to the west, covered in sharp thickets and thorny bushes with wicked spines protruding from trailing creepers.
111380: An east-west line of mountains dips as a valley cuts into it from the north. Grey, crooked lindens cling to the slopes, converging with gnarled oaks that march in from the valley. Twisted roots covered in slimy moss alternate with lichen-blanketed rock to provide slick footing on the slopes.
111381: A forest-covered ridgeline runs east-to-west, punctuated by needle-like peaks. The hollows between peaks are covered densely in lindens; their low-hanging branches drag at any creature that passes between them. The summits themselves are covered in broken slabs blanketed in grey-green lichen. The heights afford a view of a twisted promontory that rises across a narrow valley to the north.
111382: The walls of this cave are riven with numerous cracks which allow narrow shreds of light to pass into the chamber. Large quartz crystals reflect this light, casting shimmering motes on the walls. Wind whispers through the cracks, muffling any sound in the cave, be it footfalls or predatory paws.
111383: A fierce bat is here, lusting for your blood (hidden).

A narrow, twisting cavern descends from west to east. Thin streams of wind issue from small openings in the walls and ceiling; none of these holes are more than a hand's-breadth wide. The sound of these streams is soft but persistent, a whispering murmur that fills the air.
111384: The corpse of a bloodthirsty bat is lying here.

Broad tunnels, steep rock chimneys, and deep chutes meet at a great cavern junction. The ceiling of the cavern is largely lost in the murk, from which great pillars of rock reach down to touch the floor. The massive size of the cavern, and its rough, irregular walls mean that even the slightest sound makes a distorted echo that thwarts any attempt to discern its origin.
111386: A rock lizard is here, motionless as it observes you.

A broad round cavern splits into a plethora of small tunnels, most of which are less than a foot wide, and all are too narrow to enter. Many of these tunnels carry distant echoes of unidentifiable origin. The rocks are mostly black and unreflective, though a few crystals scattered throught the cavern might reflect fleeting motes of lantern or torch.
111388: A long but narrow ledge snakes high on the cavern wall. Here and there the ledge runs behind towering rock pillars, while in other places there is nothing to stop one from falling off the ledge to smash into the cavern's floor several yards below the ledge. A constant breeze flows through the ledge, filling the air with its soft susurration.
111390: Massive, black, oozing vines reach out from the choked canopy.

A twisted mesh of thistle, shrub, and branch resists any attempt to shove it aside. Disturbed foliage snaps back quickly when released, entrapping creatures that trespass in this domain. Heavy, low-hanging branches bar the narrow gaps between trees. A steep hill to the north looms over the snarled tangle of trees and vines.
111391:
Foul webs span across Mirkwood, engulfing the exit up with their complex patterns.
A black, thorny bush grows here, enshrouded in a murky gloom.
A forest spider is here crawling around.
A forest spider is here crawling around.
A wolf spider is here, among the trees.

Squat, gnarled oaks pack together closely in this rounded dip in the valley. Branches reach out from the trees as if to grasp at any creature foolish enough to pass nearby. Webs dangle from the outstretched twigs: snares ready to catch hapless creatures. Simply put, this place is a trap.
111392: The corpse of a brown, long-legged spider is lying here, crushed under rocks.

This deep cavern exists below the trees of Mirkwood. The opening at the surface admits no light, as tangled foliage and loose-looking rocks hide this rift from any birds-eye view. The walls of the round cave are rough and uneven, while the floor is dotted by medium-sized rocks. Faint intermittent chittering echoes from the walls, distorted by numerous cracks and crannies.
111393:
A brown, long-legged spider swiftly charges at you.
A brown, long-legged spider swiftly charges at you.

Ragged briars spread across the ground, threaded by thorny black vines. Thick, sticky webs stretch between branches; fallen limbs drag strands of silk with them, entangling them with the underbrush. This dense morass causes only the lower boles of the trees are visible. These bear gaping cracks which bleed foul sap that oozes along the creepers, coating them in sticky residue.
111394:
A forest spider is here crawling around.
A forest spider is here crawling around.

Thick roots snake across broken terrain, shadowed by overlapping boughs in the canopy high overhead. Swishing veils of vines drape from the limbs, accumulating in tangled piles at the bases of the trees. Branches and leaves appear to float, stuck in the silken webs that stretch between trunks. This fallen foliage is joined by husks of long dead creatures.
111395: Large black oaks with dark leaves cover the forest floor in an eternal darkness. Thick moss clings to the great tree trunks, while wiry lichen dangles from oversized knotted boughs. The air is thick and heavy beneath the ominous canopy looming above.
111396: Gnarled oaks and towering firs stand strong amidst a sea of twisting roots and knotted vines. Thick, hard roots thrust violently in and out of the soft soil in every direction beneath a tangled web of stiff, raspy vine runners attempting to strangle the life from every living thing in the forest.
111397:
A bright red mushroom is growing here.
A small mushroom grows nearby.
A giant, strange looking green fungus is here, ready to devour you in seconds.
A huge black fungus is here, exuding a foul stench.
A huge black fungus is here, exuding a foul stench.
An ancient fungus smothers the boulders.
An ancient fungus smothers the boulders.

Beneath the overarching trunks and limbs that block out all natural light from above lies a dark, moist soil that serves as a guarded home for all manner of fungus. The sheltered bed of warm moisture harbours large black foul-smelling fungi, putrid green mushrooms, and bright red bells popping up all along the forest floor.
111398: A large patch of multi-coloured lichen growths is here in the centre of the grove.

Inside a great circle of towering firs covered by an impenetrable canopy of thick boughs and intertwined branches lies a dark silent grove decorated by every manner of lichen. Large crusts of yellow lichen cling to the surrounding tree trunks while leafy, light green lichen grows along exposed roots in the soil itself. Thin, shrub-like grey lichen dangles from every branch fading up into the darkness of the canopy.
111399:
A skeleton of some humanoid lies in the dust.
A fallen tree lies on the ground, its clump of roots pointing upwards.
A large rabbit looks peacefully at you, ready to dart away.

The trees grow so thick here that, at the height of the midday sun, even a faint dim green glow is absent beneath the impervious canopy. Thorny vines, tall bushes and entangling roots cover the forest floor. Rotting black logs lay scattered along the ground, brought down by some unknown force long ago under the cover of complete darkness. Bones of various creatures litter the ground, including one obvious humanoid skeleton.
111400:
A sprawling, twisted tree grows here.
On the tree, there are a few hawthorn berries.

The trees grow so closely together here that their branches and boughs intertwine to form a dense lattice of gnarled wood just above the ground. Thick roots twisting in and out of one another make up the forest floor, covering up whatever soil might lie beneath the hard warped feet of each grizzled tree trunk.
111401: A black, thorny bush grows here, enshrouded in a murky gloom.

Immense boughs tower ominously high above the ground from mighty trunks that loom upward in the silent darkness of the forest. The air is still and stuffy as no breeze will penetrate the mighty canopy of Mirkwood. Dry dead leaves lay thick between moss-covered stones that litter the forest floor.
111402: A large, black butterfly is fluttering about erratically.

Treacherous roots snake along the forest floor like long fingers from the bottom of gnarled, blackened trees. Each trunk is covered with crusted yellow lichen that clings to the dark bark, extending up into the lower boughs where darkness masks the rest of the towering growth. The ground to the north and east climbs sharply upward toward the mountains of the Emyn-nu-Fuin.
111403: The irregular knobby branches of tall gnarled trees interweave to create an ominous roof, blotting out the sky above and shrouding the forest floor in unending darkness. Slithering vines have lashed out in all directions, strangling shrubs and choking trunks as they feast off of the life-blood of other vegetation along the ground.
111404: The dark earth beneath a fallen tree has been dug out to form a sizeable den for what must be a very large beast. The floor consists of compacted soil covered with colossal dusty paw prints and a few scattered coarse hairs.
111405: A large boulder is here, it must be heavy.

Jagged rocks protrude from the forest floor, jutting out of the soft soil between large tree trunks. The woods are primarily made up of dark green and black oaks, with a smattering of coniferous trees whose pine needles are hardened by the harsher climate of the rising elevation.
111406: Massive boulders rest at the bottom of a mountain valley, covered in green moss and shrouded by the dark forest canopy above. Great black oaks loom ominously over the tall stones, swaying to and fro in an unseen and unfelt breeze far away from the dark stuffy air that blankets the valley floor.
111407: Hulking oak trees, ancient beyond reckoning, twist and turn between and around each other in their rampant growth along rugged mountainous terrain. Massive boughs grind together in their powerful struggle to force space in the crowded forest, wrenching the already warped wood and squeezing it under immense pressures for years untold. The old, compressed boughs appear almost shiny in their ever-stressed but unrelenting struggle as they crush each other in the darkness.
111408: Black Brook in a Dark Mountainous Grove
A massive hoary fir tree is here, towering over the forest floor.

A dark, murky stream trickles and winds its way around great boulders as it slowly descends the mountain slope into a forever-dark grove of menacing firs. The tall, queer trees seem to feast on the filthy water as their roots extend down into the rotten foul-smelling blackness. The roots themselves remain covered in a thick layer of brown slime that extends to the soil and vegetation surrounding them.
111409: A large pile of boulders is sitting here, probably debris from a rockslide.

Great round stones covered entirely in light-green crusted lichen rest deep in the harsh earth on steep forested slopes. Tall oaks and firs loom over the sunken boulders to create an eternally dark wasteland of hard cold stone and dry cracked soil. Ragged and withered undergrowth barely cling to life amidst parched dust under the choking forest canopy.
111410: A massive forlorn tree grows here, dominating the forest.

A huge, forlorn tree grows amidst the mountains with its enormous branches reaching high above the rest of the uneven canopy along the low peaks. The great trunk plunges seemingly into the very stone of the mountain top, its titanic roots cracking and splitting rock in every direction. The ground surrounding the hulking tree is rugged with many boulders covering what little topsoil remains.
111411: A huge gnarled oak tree is here, looming ominously overhead.

Large flat slabs of rock cover the slope that rises to the north. Gaps between the stone create sudden explosions of tree growth. Great dark firs and oaks appear rampant wherever breeches in the granite permit, their great boughs reaching toward one another to block out the sky above.
111412: A fallen tree lies on the ground, its clump of roots pointing upwards.

The small mountaintop is dominated by burnt oak trees encircling a tiny glade still entirely covered by intertwined, scorched branches. Both bark and bough are charred to a uniform colour blacker than night itself. The forest seems to hiss constantly from every direction, the air thick with malice and hostility.
111413:
A huge, smoking campfire is burning here.
A deft, young orc monitors the area, ready to attack any enemy.
A deft, young orc monitors the area, ready to attack any enemy.
A deft, young orc monitors the area, ready to attack any enemy.

A wide rocky cave has been turned into an orkish camp. Several charred pieces of lumber lie against the northern wall of a cave, right next to a midden which is littered with bones. A few large rocks frame the back of the cave, used as makeshift seats next to a large cooking pot. The pot lies on its side towards the back of the cave, its contents emptied.
111414:
The corpse of a green-cloaked Durbuk-hai archer is lying here.
The corpse of a seasoned Durbuk-hai scout is lying here.

Amidst hoary trees wounded with the hacking of axes lies a large, round stump, a decaying remnant of a bygone era in the history of Mirkwood. Its dead roots sprawl in every direction and all around the ground are scattered dark green leaves. Even with meagre light, the girdle of oaks cast an imposing shadow on the forest beyond. The dark surface of the trees struggle to reflect any light. Webs stretch between the very tops of the trees, hanging ready for the return of their masters.
111415:
A colony of red ants is here. The ants seem to ignore you.
A black wolf pads restlessly, looking for its next prey.

Ancient oak trees with black bark stand here, timeless and still in the gloom of Mirkwood. The thick forest-roof remains motionless as it imposes a suffocating darkness upon that which it covers. Webs crawl up the trunks and weave among the branches of the trees, burdening the canopy and further obscuring the roof of the world. Amid rotten debris and long-fallen branches lies a hollow, ebony log conquered by time and moss.
111416: The steep mountain slope is covered by great moss-covered boulders shrouded by tall, darkened oaks and firs that grow in the spaces between the stones. Massive branches and boughs produce a black blanket of dim leaves that blot out the skies above a smothering ceiling of foliage.
111417: Dark oaks and withered pine trees grow at awkward angles as the forest floor rises dramatically in elevation from the south. Long roots grow shallow under the soil, uprooting loose rocks in a scattered pattern throughout the terrain. Dark and slimy umbrella mushrooms cling to the surfaces of the rocks, exuding a noxious odour.
111418:
A sprawling, twisted tree grows here.
An ancient fungus smothers the boulders.

Beneath the untold thickness of the forest canopy lie warped tree trunks looming in the pitch-black air, thick with dust and malice. Gigantic fungi grow on rotten tree stumps between thorny bushes that cover giant boulders. Moss grows thick on every stone surface, while strands of strange lichen dangle from nearly every bough along the steep and rugged mountains.
111419:
A huge gnarled oak tree is here, looming ominously overhead.
A colossal tree, its trunk as wide as a small cottage, stands here.

Nestled in the steep wooded slopes of Mirkwood low in the mountains of the Emyn-nu-Fuin, a grove of great oaks stand bent by years beyond reckoning. The mighty forms of these withered trees even in their tired state envelope huge boulders with their terribly strong roots of enormous girth. Decrepit, knobbed branches still stretch defiantly outward in every direction, each fully clad in unusually long drapes of dry wiry lichen.
111420: A greenish slime mould is here, smelling badly.

Masses of dark fir trees grow in twisted shapes upon a steep slope in the shadowy forest. The bark of the trees appears to hang from the strangely-shaped boughs like willowy drapes, while dark vines dangle in the stifling air from various branches high in the canopy. Slime mould covers various boulders that dot the mountainous forest floor even as bracken struggles to survive in the unending darkness.
111421: A mountain goat is here, jumping from cliff to cliff.

A narrow, winding pass has formed between steep cliffs and unforgiving mountain slopes. The pass winds its way through unstable scree and along steep gullies plunging into darkness eternal. The pass continues, in some places under looming overhangs of dark grey stone, and in other places it narrows considerably due to the huge trees that grow here.
111422: A mountain ibex is jumping from rock to rock.

Beneath the shade of a few dark trees, a pass winds its way through the mountains, weaving around great crags and atop uneven precipices. Slick round stones dot the precarious slopes amidst long patches of dried stiff thickets harbouring long, hollow thorns ending in needle-like points. Darkness covers all as the unrelenting forest canopy blocks out light and fresh air both.
111423: A mountain goat is here, jumping from cliff to cliff.

A narrow mountain pass weaves between steep heights and wanders seemingly without end. Precarious cliffs rise far above to the north, harboring naught but desolation in their weathered crags and wicked cracks. In spite of the rugged cliffside no light reaches this stoney place, as masses of great trees crowd out the light and air from above as they greedily envelop the skies in a great curtain of darkness all the way up to and against the cliffside.
111425:
A large boulder is here, it must be heavy.
A large pile of boulders is sitting here, probably debris from a rockslide.
A mountain ibex is jumping from rock to rock.
A mountain goat is here, jumping from cliff to cliff.
A mountain ibex is jumping from rock to rock.

A winding pass in the mountains cuts a serpentine scar through the rugged terrain, littered with boulders big and small. A tall crest ascends to the north with no sign of life upon it, jutting from the brutal foliage that devours all light and smothers all else. The heights close in, masking the horizon with their jagged outlines.
111426:
A large pile of boulders is sitting here, probably debris from a rockslide.
A mountain goat is here, jumping from cliff to cliff.

Steep inclines on gravel-covered bedrock mark a seldom-used trail leading through the lower Mountains of Mirkwood. An unfelt wind whistles through the unseen treetops above, even as the air remains still and thick beneath the stifling girth of the canopy looming over the trail itself. Piles of splintered stone surround large, cracked boulders that provide homes for small stiff bushes that have taken root between the sharp edges of the cracks themselves.
111427:
A mountain goat is here, jumping from cliff to cliff.
A mountain ibex is jumping from rock to rock.
A mountain ibex is jumping from rock to rock.

Two moderately high peaks rise up through dark baleful woods beneath the choking canopy of the smothering forest. One peak to the northwest thrusts itself up through a stand of dark, withered oaks while another cracked stone peak rises up to the southeast amidst a grove of bent pines. The slopes of the peaks are lined with sharp crags and deep recesses that slice the bark of those trees that grow close enough to rub against their mighty walls in unseen winds high above.
111428: A mountain ibex is jumping from rock to rock.

Crags of jagged stone rise from the ground like crooked teeth, forming a winding path between the rocks that rises steadily to the north. Dark trees stand tall above the crooked stone still blocking out light as well as wind even on the heights of the low Mountains of Mirkwood.
111430:
The corpse of a huge, poisonous spider is lying here.
The corpse of a black widow is lying here.

The entangled vegetation shrouds the lower forest canopy into unending darkness. Tough, clinging vines and sticky webs conspire to make a tangled snarl, limiting the view in many places to a few yards. The poor vision is further restricted by protruding branches, entangling creepers, and the endless amount of thick silk strands that stretch between the trees.
111431: The corpse of a horrible, dark-green spider is lying here.

A round narrow tunnel woven from spider silk, smaller branches, and sticky elastic mass cuts through the dark vegetation. There are occasional openings in the walls of the tunnel, providing small side paths that soon disappear into murk. The tunnel makes a tight curve leading towards the north and east, elevating slightly up towards the north. The floor is sticky, making the travelling slow.
111432: The corpse of a brown, long-legged spider is lying here.

A circular, sticky tunnel zig-zags within the canopy. It takes it course where the branches are providing support, flanks around the dark tree trunks, and in general arches to the south and east. Rotting vines and shattered branches litter the floor of the tunnel. The tunnel walls themselves have been created from grey spider silk.
111433:
A tattered cocoon dangles from a tree.
On the cocoon, there are a lantern, a woollen traveller's cloak and a plain hood.

Sticky webs form thick nets that drape the canopy of densely tangled trees. The silken strands sway ominously with the motion of the trees, accompanied by harmonic vibrations produced by the creatures who skitter along these webs. The branches and silky densely-woven webs form a slender platform which is snaking between the trees. The surroundings are covered in varying patches of white and black, a mixture of fallen silk and sticky ooze.
111434:
Foul webs span across Mirkwood, engulfing the exit down with their complex patterns.
The corpse of a brown, long-legged spider is lying here.

Tall, broad oak trees rise more than a hundred feet to blot out the sky with their entangled boughs. A few stray beams of sun or moonlight sometimes pierce into the canopy, revealing sticky strands of silk. These strands are only a small part of a vast, unbroken web. This spider domain extends in all directions, the only limit being its height which can reach only to the tops of the trees.
111435: The entangled branches form narrow platforms that serve as perilous pathways within the canopy. Here, the thoroughfare encircles a gap in the lower vegetation allowing a view below to a small, circular forest glade. Above the clearing, strands of webs stretch in the air in numerous layers. The canopy itself towers more than one hundred feet above the forest floor. Cocoons and egg sacks dangle from the webs.
111437:
Some roots lie here waiting to ensnare weary travellers.
Some roots lie here waiting to ensnare weary travellers.

A heavy mat of creepers spreads over this broad, forested valley. These creepers are blackened and rotting, yet still summon the strength to battle the oak trees that grow here. An ominous rustle of vine against root fills the air. The canopy of the oak trees eclipses the sky; not even during a bright summer day could light penetrate this dense obscuring foliage.
111438:
Massive, black, oozing vines reach out from the choked canopy.
A cluster of dark green, feathery fronds flourishes in the shade.
A mass of wriggling vines drops on you from the trees.

Dense foliage limits visibility to little more than a few yards. Paths open suddenly among the shifting trees, only to close moments later. Vines swing freely across these ephemeral passages, drawing attention to their fleeting presence. Though animal life is sparse, a quiet murmur pervades these woods.
111439: Some thick writhing vines whip all around you.

An overwhelming stench of rot permeates the air. The oaks in this dense forest ooze jet-black sap, and many have fallen, leaving behind twisted stumps. The density of the forest prevents the collapsed trees from reaching the forest floor. Ochre fungus covers the decaying trunks, issuing dense clouds of spores.
111440: There are some acorns lying here.

A vast legion of oaks leans into a steep slope, hoary and knobbed trunks bending up the incline. Their branches hang shackled by thick, draping vines that drag them towards the valley floor. Twisted roots grasp desperately at the incline as they strain against these living chains.
111441: A brown snail is crawling across the ground here leaving a slimy trail behind.

Forested highlands form the northern slope of a broad valley which stretches away to the south and west. Undergrowth clusters densely around the trunks of aged oaks, as if seeking to strangle these hoary trees. Many of the gnarled branches lack foliage, and the swell of the southern flank of the valley is visible through these wide gaps.
111442: Some roots lie here waiting to ensnare weary travellers.

A deep ravine cuts through the forested highlands. Here at its eastern end the ravine is blocked by towering cliffs to the east and south, while a slope leads up to a ridge to the north. Rocks and boulders lie scattered at its bottom, interspersed with dense shrubbery. Branches from trees above cast murky shadows over the thick underbrush. An unseen stream murmurs quietly, the only natural sound breaking the silence.
111443: A tall peak looms to the north, its steep face scarred with gaping recesses. The oaks in its shadow are squat and stooped, as if cowering in its presence. They stretch horizontally instead: their tangled clumps of roots smother the forest floor. Sickly tufts of grass peek through the gaps, clinging to life despite the stranglehold of the trees.
111444: A fallen tree lies on the ground, its clump of roots pointing upwards.

Tall cliffs bound the western edge of this small valley. Decrepit, skeletal trees fill a hollow at the end of the valley. Brittle branches blanket the ground, interspersed with brown, dry grass and a layer of leaves and pine needles.
111445: A towering peak rises to the north, looming above Mirkwood. Trees, stunted and twisted, grown among the recesses and boulders of the rugged mountain. A dark cavern lies half-hidden in one of the shadowy ravines that scars the surface of the slope.
111446:
A broken slab of rock rests in the centre of the chamber.
A mangled corpse lies crushed beneath the slab of rock.
On the corpse, there are a large skin, a sturdy pair of soft leather gloves, a forest green cloak, a sturdy, soft leather jerkin and a sturdy pair of soft leather boots.

Mounds of rubble line the floor of a cave in the mountainside. Gaping holes in the ceiling show where giant slabs broke off to tumble and shatter on the floor below. Dust blankets every surface, and clouds of it still linger in the air.
111447: Rugged slopes climb from the south and east, forming the eastern end of a ridgeline that extends to the west. Spindly firs and stooped oaks cling desperately to the incline. Their branches tangle mere feet above the ground, lashing at any passing traveller. Many small rills snake through shallow crevices down to a ravine in the valley to the south.
111448: A narrow valley cuts between towering cliffs. At its western end a fairly accessible slope leads up to a ridge. The bottom of the cleft is clogged with dead branches, leaves, and other detritus that gather behind a mound of rubble. Patches of stumps mar the fir-clad mountainsides.
111449: A massive forlorn tree grows here, dominating the forest.

Tangled shrubs and stooped firs blanket an otherwise barren and rugged ridge. The fir branches are spindly and crooked, and seem to grasp at passing travellers. Patches of scree break the cover of vegetation: the slightest disturbance sends cascades of rocks tumbling down the slope. Clouds of dust peppered with gravel fill the air, originating from a mountain to the west.
111450: Massive slabs protrude from a ridge that extends from a peak to the west. Scree fills the gaps, making for unstable terrain between secure rocky islands. Clouds of dust billow from the slopes of the ridge. The scree and rubble is clear evidence of recent rockfalls.
111451: A steep boulder field forms a comparatively gentle transition between two parallel cliffs which together descend from a mighty peak lying southwest to a murky valley to the northeast. The boulders are covered in a thick mat of grey lichen which makes them very slippery.
111452: A large, black butterfly is fluttering about erratically.

Thick vegetation covers every surface of this rugged slope. Hazardous crevices lurk in the shade beneath tall trees, hidden by an obscuring carpet of vines and brambles. A mighty peak towers to the south, its sheer slopes offering no purchase. The terrain climbs to the east, where a sheer cliff overlooks a valley to the northeast.
111453:
There are some acorns lying here.
A black squirrel peers down from the branches of the trees.

Massive, rolling waves of earth run from east to west. Gnarled and bent oaks cling to the slopes of rising mountains, overshadowing murky hollows between ridges. Twisted trunks intertwine with thick limbs, leaving little open space. Beneath these tangles, knobbed roots snake through decaying mounds of leaves.
111454: A tall stack of lumber sits in the centre of a clearing.

The ground seems to sag as it descends to the east, where jagged hilltops rim a low, murky valley. Oak trees cling to the slopes, dense webs of roots mixing with those of their neighbours. Erosion has swept away much of the top layer of soil, exposing the undersides of the roots where swarms of insects now thrive.
111455: Giant oaks tower over the western end of a broad valley. Barrel-thick roots snake through a thick, decaying mat of leaves and acorns, and massive limbs block out the sky. Tough goutweed proliferates in dense patches between the trees. An oppressive stench of rot and mould fills the air.
111456: A huge gnarled oak tree is here, looming ominously overhead.

Mighty, sprawling oak trees prevail over the southern slope of a wide valley. Their heavy branches hang low to the ground, tangling with those of neighbours so that it is often unclear which boughs are attached to which trees. A net of thick vines drapes from the trees, limiting vision and obscuring the outstretched limbs.
111457: Massive mounds of rock separate two forested valleys. Small shrubs and frail saplings try to grow in the gaps between boulders, but there is little in the way of fertile soil. Lichens fare better, draping every exposed face in orange-brown fuzz.
111458: A sea of oaks swells to the northwest, rising as it meets a steep escarpment. Jagged rock shelves stretch parallel to the cliff, ominous outcrops along their edges glaring over the treetops. There are occasional gaps in the shelves where slabs have broken off, but these breaches are clogged with thick vines and rotten vegetation.
111459: Great mounds of earth rise from the woodlands. Rough boulders stud the slopes, bracing the steep inclines. Densely packed trees grip the hillsides, their twisted trunks bent upward as they strain for the sky. Tangled branches drag at the slopes as if grasping for support.
111460: The elongated shape of a stoat can be seen darting across the terrain.

A broad ridge stretches westward from a mighty peak to the east. Tall oaks line these rounded heights, their efforts devoted to supporting high branches. Thick, tangled vines dangle from the limbs, swaying in rhythm with the winds that shake the canopy. There is a gap in the tree cover where a flat stone slab covers the ground. Even there, determined oak roots tear at the rock, sending cracks along its face.
111461:
A soft pouch, made from leather, has been left here.
A soft pouch, made from leather, has been left here.
A black moth flutters around.

This gully is deep enough that it may actually be called a pit, with huge dark oak trees standing tall inside a bowl-like depression among the forested hills. North of here, the trees thin out a bit against what looks like a fortress-like hillock. Travel is possible to the south, where a steep incline leads up onto a wooded hill. The air here is stuffy, and the undergrowth makes it hard to see very far in any direction. Westwards, a mossy, funnel-like rock formation allows passage further into the dark woods.
111462: The top of this mountain seems to be little more than a great mound of gravel. A few boulders, covered in viridescent lichen, emerge from the pile, adding hints of colour to a drab grey and brown landscape. Precipitous cliffs border the mountain on three sides, but a boulder field on the western slope seems to be a viable, if difficult, route of descent. A jagged line of peaks continues to the northeast, separating a wide valley to the north from a much narrower valley to the south.
111463: A great host of stout beeches stretches across the level foundation of the valley, halted only by a steep escarpment that rears up to the north. This cliff overhangs slightly, a cresting wave ready to crash. The forest is immune to this impression of impending doom; bramble and briar tangle to cast their leaves under rare gaps in the cover of foliage.
111464: Three branches of a valley meet in the shadow of a high escarpment. South and west, the valleys are crowded with beeches and the ends of the valleys beyond sight. To the east, stout oaks pack a deep, narrow valley which runs beneath a high crag and into the shadows of a high plateau.
111465: Broad-trunked beech trees fill a deep, narrow valley. Their dense outstretched branches tangle as they grasp at the sky. A jagged overhang is visible through temporary openings in the obscuring foliage. The oppressive density of the forest conceals the physical support of this massive crag.
111466: A valley stretching away to the west comes to an end at a U-shaped set of steep walls which surround a sudden dead-end. These walls preclude any vision of the heights above. A few crevices and niches provide shelter for ragged nests. The deep shade of the dead-end affords little means for the growth of vegetation larger than stunted shrubs.
111467: A broad, forested ledge runs between sheer walls to either side, rising gently to the north until it comes to a sudden halt at a dropoff more than fifty feet high. Little can be seen of what lies at the top of either of the steep cliffs that line the ledge. However, though the depths beneath the ledge lie in deep gloom, the skeletal remains of rotting trees are visible, reaching branches half-sunk in a muddy swamp.
111468: A black, thorny bush grows here, enshrouded in a murky gloom.

This region of the valley is covered in tall beeches whose high branches mask the sky. Far beneath this dark canopy, a soggy mat of fallen leaves and broken branches blankets the floor. Patches of luminescent mould grow on this fertile carpet, emitting a soft eerie glow. Eastward the valley descends into a dank morass cast in a deep gloom.
111469:
Herb: blackflower
can be dragged north

Green, springy creepers meld with oozing mud to drag at every step through a sodden morass in the centre of this valley. A dank, earthy odour permeates the air, tinged with a hint of rot and decay. The thick sludge of the forest floor appears to have suffocated all plant life except for hulking beeches and the vines that cling to them.
111470: Swarms of dead insects float on pitch-black water pooling in the depressions between thick-girthed roots. Putrid mould blackens entire tree boles, stretching upward from the foul water which seems to be its source. The air is suffocating, thick with a noxious vapour which evaporates from the pools and mingles with an oppressive stench of decay.
111471:
A black, thorny bush grows here, enshrouded in a murky gloom.
A dark wisent struggles to move through the morass.

A thick sludge of rainwater, decaying fungi, and mouldy vegetation spreads over the forest floor. Stunted beeches struggle to grow, their roots engulfed by the viscous filth. Rotting creepers reach upward to latch onto writhing branches, dragging them down to the ravenous morass.
111472: A massive tree has fallen here, its death throes bringing down several of its smaller brethren. Their rotting stumps are covered in patches of black mould and vivid orange fungi. Large, grey beetles bore into the soft, decomposing bark to feed on the wood at the core; they are surrounded by swarms of maggots which devour the fungi at the surface. The ground beneath the trunk is damp and marshy; it sags beneath the great weight of the dead tree.
111473: A stream of water trickles over the edge of an opening high up a cliff to the east. Its presence is obscured by a dense curtain of vines, and camouflaged by a vibrant emerald moss that surrounds it. The water flows down leafy beech branches stretching toward the cliff; it eventually meets the ground where it mixes with decaying vegetation to form a viscid muck.
111474: Viscous mud drips from a looming overhang to the east. The rest of the sky is blocked out by the thickly woven foliage of beeches that sprawl across the valley. The leaves closest to the cliff are spattered with mud, as are various boulders and rocks near the cliff. The ground is marshy and covered in a soft, thick layer of mould.
111475: A plateau hangs over the valley from the east. Emerald moss stretches up the steep face, nourished by water that seeps from cracks in a cliff wall. As this water reaches the forest floor, it mixes with a thick, damp sludge composed of decaying vegetation. Broad trunks of beech trees rise from this morass, their distant crowns casting dark shadows.
111476: Silk strands dangle from the ceiling of a smooth-walled tunnel. Aged, grey husks of butterflies hang from tightly-woven webs. One of these hapless creatures seems to have escaped from one web only to get caught in another, telltale strands trailing back to its penultimate snare on the opposite side of the tunnel. The roof rises abruptly to the east, expanding into a vast and murky cavern.
111477:
A grey spider is stalking here, preparing to drain you of life.
A small, red-spotted spider lurks here.
A small, red-spotted spider lurks here.

An enormous chamber cuts into the rock, its lofty ceiling soaring dozens of yards above the rocky floor. Great spiralling webs interweave in irregular patterns: old, dusty silk yields to new, sticky filaments. The floor is blanketed in fallen strands that absorb the echoes one might otherwise expect in a cavern of this size. A patch of fresh-looking webs stretch across a large hole in the floor.
111478:
A huge, venomous tarantula extends her legs to you.
A huge, venomous tarantula extends her legs to you.

A giant, sprawling web covers the ceiling of the eastern end of a spacious chamber. Some of the strands hang to the floor, where they may clearly be seen to be the thickness of a slender rope. Immense cocoons dangle from the web, telling the harrowing tale of a creature capable of snagging such impressive prey. Where the eastern wall of the chamber meets the ceiling, there is a dark tunnel that leads upward.
111479: A rough tunnel zigs and zags as it slopes away from a vast chamber that lies above it. Sticky spiders' weavings span the tunnel. The walls are rough and gritty, made of grey-and-black speckled granite. The floor is covered in dusty clumps of silk.
111480: Heavy clouds of spores hang in the air around vivid fungi that line broad-girthed beeches. The fruiting bodies exhibit various shades of green, orange and red, visible wherever light peeks through the distant, obscuring canopy. The damp air causes the spores to stick together in clearly visible clumps, making it difficult to breathe.
111481: The valley narrows suddenly as a rugged mountain juts into it from the north. Birches blanketing the slope meet densely packed beeches that dominate the valley floor. The beeches continue to thicken to the east, and headway in that direction is only possible by following the northern slope of the valley.
111482:
A sickly beech tree with drooping branches leans into the slope.
A young wisent is here, staying close to rest of the herd.

The beech and birch trees on the northern slope of the valley are stricken with disease; their bores ooze amber sap. Fragile and rotten vines hang from drooping branches. The sodden decaying vegetation on the incline provides little purchase. The few patches of exposed rock are little better, as they are covered in slippery, grey-green lichen.
111483: The beeches in this valley lack most of their leaves, and large swaths of bark are missing from their trunks. Soft, rotten remains of beech-bark lie on the forest floor atop mounds of leaves, providing sustenance to a rampant ochre fungus. The patchy canopy lets in more light than is typical for the murky forest, revealing the cliffs that border the valley to the north and south.
111484: A large, black butterfly is fluttering about erratically.

Ochre mould blankets trunk, roots, and limbs of sickly beeches. No bark is visible in the rare gaps devoid of fungi. The bare, drooping branches afford a clear view of the steep valley walls to the north and south which extend for several miles.
