111485: These beeches are dead, and have been for a long time. Leafless branches droop from their trunks. The floor is a sodden mass of decomposing vegetation covered in a thick layer of mould and fungus. Scattered squat and sickly shrubs struggle to survive in the septic soil.
111486:
A young orc grips his weapon impatiently, eager to prove himself.
A Durbuk-hai warrior stands here with a frenzied gleam in his eyes.

Countless rows of thick grey trunks extend beyond sight in the darkness beneath the great canopy of Mirkwood. From each trunk sprouts twisted, bulbous roots that intertwine with one another to form a hard, knotted floor that rises as it approaches each tree and then falls again. Rigid boughs grow together from tree to tree to form a confusing maze in the smothering lightless environment that the boughs themselves help to create.
111487:
A sprawling, twisted tree grows here.
On the tree, there are a few hawthorn berries.
A brawny wisent is slowly striding through the vegetation.

The evergreen trees here block out all possibility of sunlight penetrating the forest canopy. Twisted trunks and sickly plants dot the forest floor, serving as living examples of the vanquished vegetation in the eternal war of the plants as they struggle for life in the forest of Mirkwood. Steep rocks and sharp stones rise up to the southwest.
111488: Darkness reigns supreme in a low thickly-forested valley of the foothills of the Emyn-nu-Fuin. Great trunks thrust themselves against one another as they reach for light high above, squeezing hardened wood and rough bark alike under the inhospitable pressures of continued growth filled with malice. Huge exposed roots burst forth from the dry rocky ground in every direction only to plunge back down into the hard unforgiving earth once again nearby, forming a twisted lattice of precarious arms worn smooth by weather and the passage of time.
111490: A treacherous forested slope rises to the west beneath an impenetrable canopy of interwoven fir branches. The slope continues northward toward two towering stone spires, leveling off into a valley toward the east. The ground is rocky with sparse outcroppings of larger boulders wrapped in exposed tree roots.
111491: Disintegrating trees lie strewn across a steep slope which climbs to the south. The slope becomes steeper and steeper until it rises vertically to the south and becomes impassable. The slope is hemmed in by grey rock on either side and the surrounding rock walls offer little opportunity for breeze or wind to disturb the heavy odour of decay. The ground is soft and covered in mould, and there seems to be nothing in the way of healthy vegetation; all has turned to rot.
111493:
There are two mushrooms here.
A bright red mushroom is growing here.

Bulbous toadstools blanket the forest floor, thriving silently in the darkness imposed by a thickly-woven canopy. Broken pieces ground into the earth betray where creatures have traversed this region of the forest. The fungi sit on an ample bed of decaying twigs and leaves mixed with sticky mud.
111494: Dark green and black-speckled algae cover several small murky pools of water, contrasted by a soft and damp forest floor, which is littered by splintered pieces of wood and dead leaves. Beeches, stunted but with thick mouldy-covered foliage grow on the drier spots of land. Wiry and gnarly roots stick out in clumps in various spots, forming both sturdier footholds and barriers.
111495: Long, narrow ridges protrude from a high escarpment to the west. Grey-green lichen blankets these large, exposed rock faces. Stands of beeches thrive in the narrow ravines between these ridges. Their stretching foliage obscures the forest floor, reaching up to the height of the ridges. Gusts of wind send waves through the canopy, making these ridges appear as if they were sandbars breaching the surface of a rolling river.
111500: Tall, dark cliff faces hang over this narrow valley, casting shadows over the shifting trees. The rocky walls are covered with deep, narrow crevices lost in darkness. The only break in the trees is an old streambed that has been nearly swallowed by overhanging vines.
111501: This narrow valley is covered densely in oak trees. Patches of stones mark a dry streambed which forms a natural path east and west. Several large boulders sit beside the streambed; shattered trees and a track of debris show the path of their descent from the southern slope of the valley.
111502: A dry streambed curves around a peak that juts sharply from the northwest. The oaks that populate this stretch of the valley have been considerably thinned. Their broad stumps still leak sap, indicating that they have recently been cut. Some of the living trees exhibit severe gashes inflicted during failed attempts to fell them.
111503: By a Gate in a Narrow Valley

This part of the valley is filled with the stumps of oaks, the only survivors being scattered saplings. Rock formations on the northern mountainside exhibit the remains of a waterfall. The rocky bed of a dry stream leads away from this waterfall, and follows the valley to the west.
111504: Tall cliffs dominate this corner of a murky valley. Debris from ages of erosion gathers in mounds at the foot of the escarpment. Beeches and oaks compete for territory, even breaking through fallen boulders in their relentless quest for expansion. Their branches, too, are locked in combat, tangling and intertwining.
111509: Two towering stone spires, ancient and weathered, stand here.

Two great stone spires tower up through the sparse canopy on the western and eastern sides of a lightly wooded slope, reaching far above the forest floor resting between them. Massive moss-covered trunks have burst through the cold hard stone between the great pillars, their lichen-covered branches growing into one another to form a thick layer of tangled vegetation that covers many parts of the steep and rugged terrain near the ground.
111517: A rugged ridge curves from south to east, looming over a level valley which hugs the steeply slanting slope. The bottom of the valley is filled with stout oaks whose branches seem to rake at the slopes of the ridge. Little grows beneath the cover of the branches which extend several dozen feet up the slope of the ridge. However, a few scraggly shrubs take refuge higher up the slope, out of reach of the trees.
111518: A massive boulder sits at the edge of the overhang.

A rugged slab of rock juts from a mountainside to the north and hangs above a charred valley far below. It slants gently downward as it separates from the mountainside. Debris fallen from above litters the surface of the slab. Some large boulders rest precariously at the edges. Broad, jagged cracks zigzag inward from the sides of the slab. It is unclear how deep these cracks run and how many more impacts this overhang can weather.
111519: A sheer rock wall to the west stretches far above the highest reach of decrepit oaks that appear to claw at its face. The cliff face is riven with cracks, and gaping holes show where pieces of rock have broken off. Numerous rocks and boulders lie in the shadows of the trees.
111520: The corner of a plateau towers over this part of Mirkwood, its steep cliffs running south and west. Rocks and small boulders appear to have tumbled down from the sheer plateau wall, creating jagged points in the rock as they crashed their way to the forest floor below. A broad shelf cuts westward, mediator between the plateau and a valley to the north.
111521: Crumbling cliffs surround a dense copse of beeches. Shattered boulders mingled with splintered branches indicate the slow retreat of the trees. A few shrubs and stunted saplings have taken tentative root along unshaded ledges on the rock walls.
111522: This broad cavern is littered with the bones of small creatures. Spatters of blood stain the floor in dark brown patches. Quartz crystals bulge from the ceiling, and shattered pieces glitter on the floor. The cave climbs gently toward an opening to the east.
111523: A big cavebear is padding around here.

A bed of leafy branches and tufts of grass sits in a dark corner of a cave, hidden beneath a granite overhang. Several hard, crusty tubes of solidified droppings rest a few yards away from the comfortable alcove. Piles of dark black fur lie scattered across the floor.
111524: This underground passage weaves back and forth along natural veins in the rock. It climbs from the clammy mist and rumbling din of a river to the stale, quiet air of a den. The walls and floor are dark and smooth, reflecting no light. The ceiling hides in a distant gloom.
111525: Ducaht (tooprettytodie), holding a great warsword, is resting here.

A subterranean river of black water pours from a breach in the cavern wall to the north. It flows westward, carving out a broad channel. To the east the cavern floor climbs suddenly, and is mirrored by the cavern ceiling which rises with it. Shelves of rock climb the steep face at the eastern end, meeting at switchbacks which form a continuous path.
111526: A steady flow of black water pours from a gaping hole in the roof into a shallow, murky pool. It flows thence into a broad, shallow channel that empties into a subterranean river. The spray from the falling water chills the air as it fills it with a fine mist.
111527: An albino salamander is here, perched on some rocks.

A broad ledge overlooks a river that froths and bubbles as it flows through a jumble of jagged boulders. The gurgling water sends a bitter mist wafting into the air. The riverbanks are steep and composed of black and white marbled granite.
111528: An albino salamander is here, perched on some rocks.

A murky river flows through the gaps in a line of rough boulders and broken slabs. Slimy black moss thrives in this damp environment, blanketing the rocky surfaces and making this crossing treacherous. A ledge climbs from the southern bank of the river, rising as it follows the river eastward.
111529: An albino salamander is here, perched on some rocks.

A murky subterranean river cuts around a protruding granite rock formation. The near bank is relatively flat and covered in small rocks and pebbles deposited by the flowing water. Black moss covers the walls of this tunnel, thriving in the wet environment. The damp air bears an acrid taste of noxious vapour.
111530: A small, red-spotted spider lurks here.

A tunnel leading from the west broadens into a large chamber facing a torrent of pitch-black water that disappears around a sharp bend to the south. To the north, the near bank is relatively flat, this in contrast to the steep wall that runs along the distant bank. Tenuous webs stretch from the tunnel and across the river into gloomy shadows on the other side.
111531:
A small, red-spotted spider lurks here (hidden).
A small, red-spotted spider lurks here.
A small, red-spotted spider lurks here.

Droplets of water drip from the cavern ceiling, shimmering as they trail down thick webs laced across this tunnel. The spiders who wrought these webs seem to have now forsaken this section of their domain, perhaps because of the moisture that renders their silken snares useless. The floor is damp; it readily soaks up the sprinkling water.
111532:
A newborn spider is here.
A newborn spider is here.
A tiny spider is here, eating a tiny bug.

Fluffy white sacs hang suspended from strong webs stretching across a bulge in a long tunnel. Several of the sacs are deflated and sway easily with the vibration of the webs. Gossamer-thin strands of silk extend from these empty vessels, the first weavings of freshly-hatched spiderlings. The walls of the chamber are fluid with the motion of skittering spiders.
111534: A large slab of rock hangs precariously off the shelf.

A broad, level shelf runs along the base of a high plateau to the south. Opposite to the cliff there is a steep dropoff several dozen feet to a forested valley floor. A web of cracks stretches across the southern cliff wall, which is fractured in several places. Large slabs and boulders lie strewn across the shelf. To the west, the ledge tapers to an end; there the plateau descends to the valley in a single unbroken fall.
111535:
Ducaht (tooprettytodie), wielding a great warsword, is standing here.
Klaees (donny), wielding a heavy morningstar, is standing here.
Bulg, wielding a great warsword, is standing here.
Drazud, wielding a two-handed axe, is standing here.

Ripped webs dangle from the ceiling of this tunnel. Large rocks litter the ground. Many of them bear stray strands of silk, some of which lead back to the webs from which they were torn. A large mound of rubble sits against the tapering eastern end of the tunnel; on the other end, the tunnel meets a sudden end where it opens into the top of a large chamber.
111536: This chamber forms a rounded dome with smooth walls, except at its western end where jagged scars show where rocks have been torn from the wall. The product of this destruction is a massive pile that sits in front of the entrance to a tunnel in the middle of the same wall. Several broken chisels and a large, crude hammer are strewn around this entrance. The desiccated corpse of a spider rests in the centre of the room, its head crushed by a massive boulder.
111537: The sound of rushing water reverberates throughout a recess at the eastern end of a round dome. A black torrent gushes down a waterfall which intersects the eastern end of this alcove as it cascades downward on its way to an unseen destination far below. The chamber is spattered with spray from the protruding rocks that interrupt the descending water. The floor is slippery and descends away from the falls.
111538:
A large bat is here, hanging in the darkness.
A large bat is here, hanging in the darkness.

Sheer rock walls flank a narrow crevice bottom covered in a layer of shattered rocks. The gap between the walls broadens considerably as the chasm expands upward and eastward. A round hole in the southern wall leads to a remarkably smooth-walled chamber.
111539: A small bat is standing here.

A great empty void extends upward from a rough cave floor covered in mounds of guano. A swarming mass of black specks obscures the distant ceiling. Broken rocks trail from the end of a slab that leans precariously against a ledge on the northern wall.
111540: A narrow ledge runs along the edge of a deep chasm. Its surface is covered in slimy bat droppings, making it very slippery. The ledge broadens to the west, where it provides access to a narrow breach in the ceiling. To the east, this shelf comes to an abrupt end where the slab that formed it has cracked, falling to rest its distant end against the chasm floor below.
111541: A narrow ledge stands at the edge of a vast chamber which is dozens of yards wide. This ledge continues around the chasm, descending gently as it runs eastward along the northern end of this broad gap. A strong scent of fir drifts in from a crack that leads upward.
111542: Tall fir trees tower over this rugged plateau. Bone-white strands of gossamer lichen drape from their branches and seem to hover in the breezes that whisk along the rows of trunks. Enormous, step-like rock formations climb up to a rugged shelf that skirts the terrain to the northeast. A gaping rent scars the centre of the plateau, leading down to a vast chasm.
111543: This uplift in the land gazes west over a broad and dark valley. Fir trees stretch over the precipice, outspread branches casting shadows far below. Strands of grey hairlike lichen droop from the trees. Farther away from the cliff, this lichen is more closely cropped, a sign of grazing.
111544:
The corpse of an ibex is lying here.
The corpse of an ibex is lying here.
The corpse of an ibex is lying here.
The corpse of an ibex is lying here.

This region of the plateau is surprisingly devoid of trees. Mounds of boulders form a half-ring around a dark, stagnant pool. The water is an opaque green, and black lilies float silently on its surface. The rocks surrounding it are densely carpeted in thick, yellow lichen; there are scattered bare patches where it has been torn from the surface.
111547: Short, steep cliffs rim this region of the plateau. Ranks of young fir trees tufted in grey lichen stand in the lee of the overhanging rocks. Large, mossy boulders gaze above the trees, casting shadows over the saplings. Yellow grass grows between mounds of rock, partially obscured by the dry needles that litter the ground. An impressive pile of recently-felled trees, their needles still green, rests in front of a bulge on the southern cliff wall.
111548: A massive slab juts from a high shelf to the north, creating a protected rock shelter secure from the worst of the elements. Further to the east, the slab leans down to merge with the plateau surface, forming a tunnel. A cavern mouth opens northward and downward into the shelf, stalagmites and stalactites lining an imposing maw.
111549: A wall of solid rock lines a short, broad tunnel with openings to the east and west. The only break in the wall is a yawning crevice that splits the floor in half. The eastern end of the tunnel gazes down over the edge of a plateau, providing a view of a valley stretching many miles to the east. A narrow sill climbs northward along the sheer cliff face.
111550: Huge slabs of rock sit on the cliff edges, appearing as if only a slight push would cause them to tumble down the precipice that stretches to the east and south. The plateau is covered with barren trees and small grasses that somehow cling to life, eeking out a meagre existance from the small deposits of soil that made their way into cracks and fissures in the stone.
111551: The rocky plateau ends in sheer drops to the north and east. The cliff edges have crumbled, probably due to rolling boulders that have disappeared from the plateau. Nests and broken eggs can be found in gaps between the boulders and on the the dry branches of withered stumpy trees.
111552: The shelf narrows here, flanked by steep drop-offs to north and south. Massive slabs of rock protrude dozens of feet from the surface, and many hang precariously over the cliffs to either side. The jagged outcrops are covered in a thick layer of moss that makes them all the more hazardous. Various birds make their homes above these precipices, safe in their isolation from the distant forest floor.
111553:
A mother eagle flies high above, looking for prey.
A small, helpless eaglet screams for more food.
A small, helpless eaglet screams for more food.
A small, helpless eaglet screams for more food.
A small, helpless eaglet screams for more food.
A small, helpless eaglet screams for more food.

This wide shelf of rock is concave, forming a depression towards its centre. A stagnant pool of rainwater has gathered in the depression; it is covered in a jet-black film of algae. Rocky outcrops on the edges of the shelf offer homes to eagles and other wild fowl. Far below, a broad valley stretches to the north and west.
111554: Several rock pillars, each several feet wide, run through the centre of this chamber. Piles of bedding lie on an elevated slab protruding from the eastern wall where they are protected from the scattered puddles in the rest of the cavern. A gash in the southern wall climbs up toward the surface.
111555:
A young ill-tempered stone giant is here, muttering incoherently.
A young ill-tempered stone giant is here, muttering incoherently.

Crude garments and massive clubs are strewn about the floor of this cavern, possessions of a clan of remarkably large humanoids. This cave must be an uncomfortable abode for these unfortunates, as the height of the ceiling never exceeds four yards.
111562: Drazud, wielding a two-handed axe, is standing here.

A slick slab juts into a descending deluge of water. A tunnel north of this slab leads away from the torrent of water. It carries a fresh breeze that attempts to sweep away the cold mist of the cascade. The waterfall roars as it reaches its final destination somewhere in the gloom below.
111563: Ashen remains of a campfire rest in a sheltered hollow.

A broad, rounded ridge extends from a towering peak to the east. Massive oak boles stand like stout pillars, supporting a tangled canopy dozens of yards above their bases. These behemoths have choked out most other life below their distant crowns. Hulking moss-covered boulders with blankets of leaves are all that populate the shadows between the trees.
111564: A broad ridgeline reaches out from a looming peak in the northeast, abutting with a twisting promontory that curves around a hollow valley. These landforms are separated by a jagged spine that divides oak-clad slopes to the north from lindens in the south. Twisted roots attack the rocks, and crumbled remains of boulders to either side show that the forest will ultimately prevail.
111565: A shadowed plateau looms over a gloomy forest. Lindens tower high above the ground, their massive crowns blocking all light. The boles of the trees are twisted and scarred with gnarled knots accumulated through many years of growth. Mossy roots grip the hard, barren ground between trunks. The elevated shelf culminates in a promontory to the east and broadens into undulating hills to the northwest.
111566: A tall bluff rises from a valley that envelops it to the east. Ancient linden trees stretch over the encircling cliffs, knotted boles exposed to the open air. Their gnarled trunks are swathed in dark green moss, and twisted roots protrude through the cliff walls to hang over the shadowy murk of the valley below.
111567:
A fallen tree lies on the ground, its clump of roots pointing upwards.
A brown snail is crawling across the ground here leaving a slimy trail behind.
A brown stag looks around with big, startled eyes.

Tall, black oak trees reach across this naturally occurring aisle, forming an almost opaque surface above. To the north and south, steep walls of talus and snarly vegetation make further passage possible only along the V-shaped east-westerly trench. Some moisture can be found along the bottom of the V, but there is not enough of it to use as a drinking source.
111568: A hard-packed, sandy corridor is the only traversable part of this otherwise wild and vine-infested forest. The corridor is shaped like an 'L', and travel is possible to the east and the south. The easterly direction leads to a deeply wooded area, while to the south there seem to be more hills and boulders.
111569: This deeply forested mountainside is covered in a veritable jungle of vines, thorny bushes and other creepers and plants. To the west, a stand of oaks and vines form an impenetrable wall of vegetation, where passage is made impossible thanks to the plethora of clinging and hanging vines and webs that have formed a thick, spongy mat of interwoven, half-rotten foliage. Passage is possible to the north, along a sandy path-like groove, and to the south, up onto a wooded slope.
111570: Some small rocks have been piled into a mound here.

The ground slopes dramatically, down towards the southwest and up to a precipitous peak to the northwest. The ground is dotted with heavy granite boulders, and a great number of tall conifers grows in their midst. Travel here is hard but not impossible, and the air feels comparatively less stuffy if not almost fresh.
111571: Musty, almost harsh fumes of decay hang in the air like a bad presence. The rugged and uneven ground is covered in unhealthy-looking moss and lichen that flocks around the trunks of the tall, thick old oaks that grow among a handful of black granite boulders. Travelling is arduous here, and the only viable routes are downslope to the south, or further along the ridge-like boulders that can be spied between the tree trunks to the east.
111572:
A black crow flies low to the ground here, looking for carrion to eat.
A brown stag looks around with big, startled eyes.

The trees that grow on this boulder-strewn landscape are immensely tall, and their crowns have grown together to form an impenetrable canopy above. Another, taller plateau can be found north of here. More forested boulders lie to the east, and southwards it is possible to descend into a dark, wooded gully.
111573: Black, sharp-edged granite boulders stand close together here, some of which are completely overgrown with moss and other vegetation. Tall and imposing beeches and oaks grow between the boulders, and their mighty canopies block out every last trace of the sky above. The ground slopes down towards the south and sharply upwards to the north, and the terrain in general is very hard to navigate.
111574: Dark Forest beneath a Cliff Wall

Dark and gnarly old oaks stand close together here, blocking out the sky. The ground is covered by a thick mat of some sort of black, foul-smelling moss. Looking north, one can see a big field of black boulders in between the trees, and the ground slopes distinctly upwards.
111575: A rugged line of mountains bulges from the forest floor, looming over the surrounding hills. Crooked linden trees stretch out from the narrow apex to extend their gnarled branches over sudden plunges to the north and south. Dense foliage and vines hang from these branches, forming an obscuring curtain which blots out the horizon. The rocky soil bears no underbrush to hold it in place, thus providing poor purchase at the precipices.
111583:
Massive, black, oozing vines reach out from the choked canopy.
A tangled creeper writhes its shoots between the forest's roots upwards.
A tangled creeper writhes its shoots between the forest's roots upwards.
Some thick writhing vines whip all around you.
A small, dense tangle of roots covers the ground.

This forsaken spot is almost completely surrounded by thick, black oak trees that grow extremely close together. To the north, passage is further hindered by a tall wall of granite boulders, completely overgrown with spiny bushes and gnarly roots. A big, dramatically sloping hill rises out of the forest to the west, a climbing challenge far too difficult to contemplate even for the most skilled of mountaineers.
111584:
A huge warg is here, moving in for the kill.
A ferocious warg is here, snarling angrily.
A ferocious warg is here, snarling angrily.

The trees growing here are old, sprawling oaks that have watched over these lands since the days forest elves made their homes in the Emyn-nu-Fuin. A steep cliff blocks the way to the west, but it looks like it is possible to climb up with some skill. The forest grows dense in all directions, and visibility is very limited.
111585: The ground rises noticeably to the north while the forest slowly transforms from a wide variety of species at the lower elevations to old, gnarled oaks higher up. It is very dark beneath the canopy and the forest is enveloped in an oppressive aura. To the north, a high cliff is barely visible through the foliage.
111587: Sheltered Nook on a Wooded Mountainside

This winding, almost stair-like path traverses a landscape comprised of wooded granite cliffs and boulders, where tall oaks and rugged pines compete for scant patches of fertile soil. To the north, it is possible to descend onto a lower hill. Westwards one can spy a jagged, path-like route through the rocky terrain.
111588:
A black squirrel peers down from the branches of the trees.
A swift and agile forest cat moves silently through the vegetation.

While this stony ridge is not completely void of trees and bushes, compared to the surroundings it is barren and lifeless. The ground is comprised of talus and big granite boulders. A dark-orange sort of lichen grows in wild and odd patterns on the rocks, and if one only glances at them one can be led to think that the patterns depict twisted people and animals.
111589: A black squirrel peers down from the branches of the trees.

Few trees grow here on this nourishment-deprived, gravelly slope deep inside the Mirkwood. The ones that do are of a shrubby kind, a type of black oak that grows slowly and in strange, knotty patterns. Patches of hardy, spiny weeds grow around the base of the trees, making it hard to approach them without wearing some sort of armour. Passage is possible to the north and to the west.
111590: Dark, ominous-looking oak trees grow tightly together on this steep and rocky hill. Thick, tough vines and shrubs also call this place home, and a smattering of cobwebs among them spin a tale of the possibility of some eight-legged inhabitants too. East of here, the forest opens up to a gravelly hilltop, and to the south it is possible to journey downslope to an area with dead or dying oak trees. The hills and the trees conspire to make it impossible to go in any other direction.
111591: The ground here is exceptionally dry, and cracks can been seen in the surface of the earth. Most of the trees here are thin and wasted, allowing for plant-life, such as scrub growth and stunted shrubs, to grow instead. It seems that they have been cut off from their water supply; probably as a result of the massive landslide that can be seen on the western edge of the trees.
111592: This mountain forms part of the foothills of the great mountains of Mirkwood. Higher mountains dominate the skyline to the north and east. The height and relative scarcity of trees allow for an unobstructed view over a great expanse of the forest. This could have made for an excellent place to keep watch for approaching enemies but the dense, green canopy of Mirkwood makes it impossible to see what is moving at ground level.
111593: The forest comes to an abrupt halt here and gives way to an open mountainside to the north. The western flank of the valley is marked with a huge pile of scree and debris, the result of a landslide that began high in the mountains of Mirkwood. Evergreen fir trees thrive in this shady valley, their fallen needles and discarded pine cones forming a blanket across the rocky ground.
111594: Huge, dark, twisted trees grow inside this shadowy part of Mirkwood. Because the bushes and undergrowth are mostly absent, there is enough space between the trees to make the travelling, and even riding, relatively easy. The forested pathway leads to the north and south.
111595:
A massive hoary fir tree is here, towering over the forest floor.
A cluster of dark green, feathery fronds flourishes in the shade.

The trunks of the trees, gnarly roots, bushes, and the ground itself are all shadowed by the thick canopy above. The darkness shrouds the forest in a gloomy embrace, and it is almost impossible to see whether it is day or night. The forest consists mostly of ancient, thick firs and pines.
111596: Large beech trees stand here draped in a curtain of vines. Creepers and vines hang from every branch with their long tendrils brushing the ground as they sway in the breeze. For a change, the trees seem to be losing their battle with the forest as vines twist and bend around the trunks as if trying to strangle them. There is a palisade and beyond it wooden structures visible to the south.
111597:
A Durbuk-hai warrior stands here with a frenzied gleam in his eyes.
A Durbuk-hai warrior stands here with a frenzied gleam in his eyes.
A Durbuk-hai warrior is here, ill-equipped but ready to fight for his tribe.
An elite Durbuk-hai guard is standing here, armed with spear and shield.

This side of the outpost has a crude gate blocking the passage to the north, keeping the animals of the forest and other creatures and potential enemies out of the outpost. In addition, the orcs have a good control of the passage of this part of forest with the strategic placement of the gate, and the other structures of the outpost, such as a high stockade and crude huts.
111598: A patch of moss grows here on a wet, flat stone.

Trees grow very closely here, all connected by their interweaving branches. Small stones lie scattered across the forest floor, almost completely covered by moss. Mottled unhealthy-looking lichen and sickly, green moss grow on almost everything, and the air has an inky, bitter odour.
111599:
A fallow deer is grazing peacefully here.
A brown stag looks around with big, startled eyes.
A fallow deer is grazing peacefully here.

A number of impressive trunks stand here forming a ring around what appears to be a small pool of water. The trees, although numerous, do not grow closely together but stand with what appears as an almost intentional space between them. A few hints of sky can be glimpsed through the canopy above. These great trees grow right down to the water's edge, with the water almost lapping against their roots.
111600:
Some thick writhing vines whip all around you.
Some thick writhing vines whip all around you.
Some roots lie here waiting to ensnare weary travellers.

Huge oak and beech trees grow all over this rocky area. A steep cliff blocks the way to the east and north, but it might be possible to climb up the cliff to reach a ledge. The faint light that might otherwise penetrate the canopy is completely blocked out by the tall, steep cliffs. To the south, the forest foliage is slightly less dense and can be navigated.
111602: A brown snail is crawling across the ground here leaving a slimy trail behind.

The ledge goes on to the east and west, and it looks like it is possible to reach a higher ledge from here. Namely there is a tunnel in the wall that ascends steeply and seems to turn slightly west. On the ground at this fork, there are some scratch marks and loose moss on the rock. Perhaps some animal lives nearby or has passed by recently.
111603: A wide ledge, littered with loose rocks and fallen scree, stretches to the east and west. There seems to be a higher cliff edge visible above the canopy of the forest. Thin vines and ivy grow up along the cliff, but they do not look strong enough to hold even a hobbit's weight.
111604:
A huge black fungus is here, exuding a foul stench.
A huge black fungus is here, exuding a foul stench.
A giant, strange looking green fungus is here, ready to devour you in seconds.

This cliff edge amongst the forest canopy is covered by decaying leaves and rotten branches. Some of the branches of the trees reach the ledge, hindering passage while also allowing squirrels and other animals to travel freely between the nearby trees and the narrow ledge. There is sickly green, slimy fungi growing on the cliff and moss growing on the decomposed earth. A shred of the sky is visible through the canopy.
111606: Vertical cliffs on two sides form the walls of this shaft. The cliffs prevent direct sunlight from reaching this deep crack, but a thin shred of sky is visible above. The dark, narrow shaft leads out onto a ledge to the west. It is also possible to descend onto a lower ledge via a steep tunnel within the rock face of the southern cliff wall.
111607: A rocky ledge lies just below the forest canopy, which continues to the south and west. There are mountains to the north, but travelling in that direction is not possible. The cliff continues to the east. A few saplings and a lot of vines grow on the partially rocky shelves as well as the smaller ledges below this larger ledge.
111612:
Some small rocks have been piled into a mound here.
A young ill-tempered stone giant is here, muttering incoherently.

The shaft ends abruptly at a vertical lichen-covered wall. There is a small niche at the end of the shaft, which forms a shelter from rain and wind. Decaying leaves and branches lie on a thin layer of earth. Some small pebbles have been piled up near the niche, and in the niche itself there is a shelter built from branches, leaves, and ropes of vine.
111613: The cliff drops steeply to the west, its surface smooth and slippery. The only way off this ledge is to follow it north or south, or to try and squeeze into a narrow crack in the face of the cliff. Green moss grows on the cliff and vines have crawled here from the canopy beneath. Strange fungi, mottled in shades of yellow, have found a home here on the side of the cliff.
111614: A boulder is here, lying on the edge of the ledge.

The cliff that this ledge clings to bends sharply from east to north. To the south-west, the view shows a great expanse of Mirkwood's dark foliage from above. A small trickle of water, barely enough to wet the rocks and certainly not enough for a drink, flows down from the higher cliff and drips down on the forest.
111615: This ledge clings precariously to the side of the mountain and continues along it to the east and west from here. The ledge narrows considerably at some points and shattered fragments of scree cover it. Over its side there is nothing but the green canopy of Mirkwood some distance below, and beneath that the hard forest floor.
111616: This ledge seems dangerously unstable. Wide cracks and fractures have opened up in the mountain side and cut clean across the ledge, splitting it into a series of small, crumbling shelves. None of the fractures have yet become too wide to not comfortably step over, but it is not clear how long it will remain this way. To the south, the great green canopy of Mirkwood spreads out as far as the eye can see.
111617: A huge stone giant is here, glaring at you.

A rocky ledge turns sharply towards the north here, following the contour of the mountain. It is narrow, and the forest floor lies far below. A sprawling green canopy of treetops stretches out endlessly in all directions below, save where the dark mountain thrusts up to obscure the view.
111618: At the end of this very high cliff, there is a clear view of the Mountains of Mirkwood to the east, and smaller peaks to the west and north. The green forest canopy is almost level with this ledge. If great care is taken, moving south along the ledge seems possible while the vertical face of the cliff might provide opportunity for the daring to climb down into the forest below.
111619: The ledge gets wider here, and there are lots of loose boulders and rocks lying on it. Some of the boulders are broken into pieces, as if they fell from great heights. There are several dried, brown stains on one of the boulders and on the ledge around it.
111620: A huge stone giant is here, glaring at you.

This mountain, an outlier of the greater Mountains of Mirkwood to the east, rises over a hundred feet above the canopy. The ledge clinging to its face is forced into a sharp bend here, and at the very corner, a large section of it has collapsed.
111621: A rugged mountainside rises steeply to the south and west. The boulders on this shelf, cracked, shattered and fragmented, lie where they landed when they tumbled down from the heights above. To the west, beneath an overhang, a darker opening against the shadows seem to hint at a cave. The shelf narrows into a ledge to the east and disappears around a sharp curve on the mountain.
111622: This cave has the rugged and uneven walls of a natural cavern, but the floor is surprisingly even, as if some effort has gone into making it more habitable. There is a smouldering pile of charred wood and ashes upon the floor in the centre of the cave, indicative of a recent presence here. There are some bones and pieces of fur dumped in a depression behind a boulder just outside the entrance; this is likely serving as a refuse pit.
111629: A black, thorny bush grows here, enshrouded in a murky gloom.

Towering trees grow in small, dense thickets that look almost identical to one another. In between the groves of trees, thick shrubbery thrives. The bushes are tall and thorny and the paths running between them are narrow and dark. The undergrowth rustles with movement from rodents and other small wildlife.
111639: The still, dank air makes breathing difficult and adds a distinct nuance to the area that sets it apart from an ordinary forest. The source of the odour appears to be stands of decaying trees that are scattered throughout the area. A faint trickling sound is ever present even though there appears to be no creak or stream nearby.
111643: There is a huge, vertical cliff to the north and west. In the shades of the cliff, the trees do not grow as high as in the deeper parts of the forest. Passage to the north and west is blocked by a vertical cliff, and there are many small rocks and scree at the foot of the cliff. The shaded cliff is moist with water, and some fallen leaves have gotten caught by the wetness and now stick to the side of the near-vertical cliff.
111644: There is a strong musk emanating from somewhere deeper in the forest. The cliff to the north of the forest is rising almost vertically up, and there is no way to climb it here. There are strong markings of animal paws and claws on the ground. Next to the cliff, there is a mound of soil and dirt.
111645: The entrance to this underground den is dug below the roots of a huge fir tree. The den itself is dug mostly below a cliff; the space is big enough for a pack of beasts and high enough for a man to stand upright. The floor and walls to either side of the entrance consist of dense soil while the back wall is rock. The air is dusty and the smell is musty inside the den.
111647:
A deft, young orc monitors the area, ready to attack any enemy.
A deft, young orc monitors the area, ready to attack any enemy.
A Durbuk-hai warrior is here, ill-equipped but ready to fight for his tribe.
A Durbuk-hai warrior is here, ill-equipped but ready to fight for his tribe.
A deft, young orc monitors the area, ready to attack any enemy.
An elite Durbuk-hai guard is standing here, armed with spear and shield.

Jagged boulders and mounds of broken rock cover the floor of a cramped valley. The piles of debris are precarious, prone to give way under the lightest footfall. Scraggly firs prevail in scattered tracts of stable mountainside, and the slopes are otherwise covered in twisted shrubs and brambles clinging to patches of scree. A narrow cranny hides torn carcasses, ragged furs, and the blackened ashes of a fire.
111648: Monstrous, broken slabs of rock crown a rugged peak. Their rough faces gaze outward at the towering pine legions that coat the surrounding slopes. Lichen and moss mask great swaths of the mountainsides, visible as vivid splotches of green, orange, and red.
111649: A spiny ridge punctuated by massive protruding rock formations stretches between two jagged peaks. While most of these protrusions are heavy slabs lodged deep in the mountain, several boulders sit precariously atop narrow pillars carved by erosion. Fir trees dominate the steep northern slope, which plunges into a murky valley. The southern slope instead descends gently and is covered in scraggly brambles which down to a tangled mass of gnarled oaks.
111650: Jagged granite pillars crown a rugged summit that looms over its surroundings. The pillars are enveloped by gnarled branches of black, vigorous trees that grow on the peak. Sharp ridges covered in streaming strands of lichen extend to the north and west. A sheer cliff face gazes south over the dim vastness of Mirkwood.
111651:
A bear is here, covered with coarse black fur.
A bear cub is here, looking around for something to play with.
A bear cub is here, looking around for something to play with.

Sheer slopes fall away from a spiny ridge. Sharp boulders protrude at irregular intervals, often walling off the entire crest of the ridge. The rock formations are blanketed in slick grey lichen, adding further danger to the already hazardous terrain.
111652:
There are some acorns lying here.
A tree-snake lies wrapped around one of the tree branches.
A tree-snake lies wrapped around one of the tree branches.

Hulking oaks with reaching branches gather in this hollow; mighty specimens at the edges tangle with pines on the surrounding slopes. The crowns of the trees join in an opaque cover of foliage. Down at the forest floor, undergrowth is oddly absent, though low-hanging branches grasp at the open spaces between trunks. Narrow, mossy runnels cut through the surrounding mountain-sides, merging to form a stream that exits through a cleft to the west.
111653:
A sprawling, twisted tree grows here.
On the tree, there are a few hawthorn berries.
A bear cub is here, looking around for something to play with.

Sheer mountainsides close in on this deep depression. Gnarled boughs of ancient oaks intertwine thickly with each other. The oak roots are broad and mossy, and a muffled droning issues from the dark voids beneath them. Rock pillars rising from the forest floor pierce the canopy, allowing glimpses of the sky. A few twisted hawthorns eke out an existence from the scraps of sunlight given them by the pillars.
111654: A rocky streambed cuts a deep course through a sheer cleft in the mountainside. Its smooth stones are covered in slick, jet black moss. Granite cliff walls pocked with dark recesses rise to either side. Several massive boulders are lodged far overhead, waiting for time and erosion to eventually cast them down.
111656: A sharp ridgeline leading from the south breaks up into a line of rounded hillocks. Numerous caves pock the hillsides, dark recesses partly covered by overhanging slabs. Young oaks grow on the crests of the mounds, but elderly trees below them cast a permanent shadow over the slopes.
111657: A tall mound of rock rises in the centre of the valley. Broken branches bearing withering leaves protrude from the pile. The western side is scorched and blanketed in grey ash, and charred trees stretch down the valley in that direction.
111658: A large, black butterfly is fluttering about erratically.

Enormous dark oaks grow among the hills here with sprawling, exposed roots creating impassable obstructions. Thorny brush grows on top of the treacherous root mounds, scraping and scratching the hard gnarled roots as they plunge in and out of the shrouded earth.
111659: A small campfire burns here, its low flames giving off only a little light.

Blackened trunks lie strewn across the valley. The underbrush is scarred as well, charred remains peeking above the ashes. The devastation reaches halfway up the slopes to either side, halted by rock faces barren of fuel. Tufts of grass have begun to peek through the debris.
111660:
A large, black butterfly is fluttering about erratically.
A large, black butterfly is fluttering about erratically.

Hulking trees stand tall upon a lonely hilltop, overseeing the rest of the forest that rises away to the east. Long, snake-like green moulds spiral down the base of the oaks and seem to become continuous with the giant roots that creep from the base of the trees. To the north-west, a plateau looms far above the forest.
111661: A large pile of boulders is sitting here, probably debris from a rockslide.

The mountainside is covered by blackened, ancient oaks. Many of the trees are dried-out and leafless, while others are thick and lively though shadowy and ominous still. Moss-covered boulders are scattered along the ground, some obscured by small vegetation and all harboring some form of lichen.
111662: Stooped black oaks with overhanging ominous boughs grow in thick clumps overhead. The moist-soil is peppered with pebbles and small rocks, and gaps through the trees reveal that this part of the forest is on top of a low mountain. To the north, the forest enters a few small rolling hills while to the east and south, the treeline appears to slope down the mountain.
111663: Towering black oaks and firs reach toward the sky as their mighty roots plunge down into the dark earth along steep mountain slopes. Hooded mushrooms of red and black colour grow along the roots, sapping nutrients from the very trees that shelter them from the harshest sunlight of mid-day.
111664:
A pile of dry, brown leaves lies here.
A sprawling, twisted tree grows here.
On the tree, there are two piles of hawthorn berries.

Twisted trees grow in a disorderly fashion among steep hills, their warped forms contorting around and along one another as they block out all light from above. Beneath the battle of the trees, an ongoing struggle between different types of small vegetation rages on. Vanquished heaps of dead plants lay rotting on the forest floor, their decaying remains dotting the hillsides.
111665:
A large boulder is here, it must be heavy.
Pitch-black water with a strange smell has collected here.
A great pine tree is here, ancient beyond reckoning.

Huge slabs of stone jut up from the earth like blunted knives, point toward the sky in a strange and ominous fashion. Small ferns and moss grow on and among the great stones which are otherwise overshadowed by overhanging pines and black oaks. A small dark puddle has collected at the foot of one particularly large rock slab. The rolling ground slowly descends to the west.
111666: Some small rocks have been piled into a mound here.

Immense black oaks grow in a uniform pattern with an equidistant amount of space between each tree across rugged mountain terrain. Great boughs spread out from the trees above and interlock with one another, creating a ceiling of branches that blots out the sky. The hard stone-filled soil is dry and packed with pockets of gravel where the steep terrain permits small stones to gather.
111667: Dark trees with hunched backs completely cover the rolling foothills of Mirkwood, their branches crossing one another among tangled leaves and wiry vines. Sharp spiny brush covers the forest floor to create a blanket of darkness above a soft and springy moss-bed that makes up the hillsides themselves.
111668:
A large pile of boulders is sitting here, probably debris from a rockslide.
A huge gnarled oak tree is here, looming ominously overhead.

Great black oaks and scraggly vines dominate the darkened forest. The terrain is uneven with large moss-covered boulders strewn about. To the south and east, the ground climbs dramatically with many loose rocks and tangled roots making passage impossible.
111669:
A large pile of boulders is sitting here, probably debris from a rockslide.
A tangled creeper writhes its shoots between the forest's roots upwards.
Some thick writhing vines whip all around you.

Thick, black trunks rise between moss-covered boulders amid terribly steep and inhospitable mountainous terrain. An impenetrable canopy ensures that the forest floor remains in perpetual gloom. The few small spaces between rough trunks and jagged boulders are covered with overgrown vines and thorny creepers.
111670: Malicious dark trees grow on top of a steep cliff that overlooks the forest to the north and east. Overlapping slabs of grey and black stone cover the forest floor, broken in various places by treacherous and unrelenting roots. Brush and vegetation manage to grow in small cracks along the great stone slabs.
111671:
A massive hoary fir tree is here, towering over the forest floor.
A large, black butterfly is fluttering about erratically.

Great dark fir trees grow here with mighty roots spreading in every direction. The sheer girth and height of the trunks and boughs serves to block out all light from the sky above. Slimy, moss-covered boulders are interspersed along the steeply-sloped forest floor, each entangled by long spindly vines that creep from trunk to trunk.
111672: A huge black fungus is here, exuding a foul stench.

The forest gradually slopes up to the north but is otherwise is encroached by rounded mountains to the west and south. The only sign of life beyond the towering trees comes in the form of black twisted fungi that snake their way up the gnarled trunks. To the east, the forest becomes a dark narrow valley.
111673: Pitch-black water with a strange smell has collected here.

Tangled trees grow along the cliffside facing south, their branches interweaving to block out all light from the sky above. Pools of black water gather at the feet of the dark gnarled trunks, while thorny briars and pale, spotted mushrooms lay strewn along the forest floor.
111674: A small and tough weed grows here.

Several narrow, steep-sided canyons cross the rugged Mountains of Mirkwood. One such canyon becomes shallow enough to enter by stepping down several moss-covered boulders suitably located for such a venture. Few trees grow here, the rock being bare and largely free of soil. Tough shrubs and weeds still manage to find plenty of cracks and fissures from which to sprout and flourish.
111675: Darkened oaks manage to grow on the rough ground dominated primarily by rock slabs along the uneven terrain. Thick underbrush and tangly vines strangle all other vegetation to the south and east, partially obscuring the sudden cliffs that rise up in those directions.
111676: Blackened oaks and firs abruptly end before sheer cliffs that overlook the forest valley to the north. The rare forest edge grants a view of the Mountains of Mirkwood to the far east. To the south, the forest appears to continue into the darkness while to the east, the ground descends steeply.
111677: Gnarled, twisted trees grow wildly with giant crowns that blot out the sky across rolling hills. Scraggly vines wrap themselves around the great trunks as they squeeze and suck the life from the towering woods. The uneven ground is covered with dead leaves as well as small shrubs as the hills continue rising steadily toward the west.
111678:
A large pile of boulders is sitting here, probably debris from a rockslide.
A massive hoary fir tree is here, towering over the forest floor.

A great crown of ghastly ash and fir trees sit atop a large hill in the forest. The trees' roots are strangely thin yet long, snaking along the ground in an irregular fashion. Numerous man-sized boulders lay scattered along the hill, creating deep crevices between root and stone. The uneven ground decreases in elevation to the south.
111679: A forested valley is populated by sinister dark trees that seem to leer in every direction above the ground. The air feels stifled and ominous, as if the forest is silently filled with a brewing wrath. Large green mushrooms as wide as tree trunks grow here and exude a sickly, deathly smell.
111680: Ashen trees with blackened leaves stretch menacingly up out of sight into the darkness of the lower canopy. Treacherous uneven slabs of hard grey stone cover the ground with many interweaving vines growing along the tops of the slabs. Stiff sharp bushes fill every crack in the stone, scratching against trunks and roots as they survive in fissures too small for the mammoth trees themselves to occupy.
111681:
A small mushroom grows nearby.
A small mushroom grows nearby.

An isolated hilltop, surrounded by steep slopes and deep crevices, is crowned by a dense grove of ancient trees. Their twisted, moss-covered trunks disappear into a dark green canopy so impenetrable that no hint of the sky beyond can be seen. The forest floor is covered in a thick layer of fallen leaves that serves as a home for fungi as well as various types of mushrooms that thrive among the decaying vegetation.
111682: A large pile of boulders is sitting here, probably debris from a rockslide.

Twisted oaks and firs grow ravenously in all directions as their outstretched branches seem to grasp for any signs of life. The darkened forest floor has no undergrowth and shows no signs of life other than grey and black spotted mushrooms that only grow in the shadows of great round boulders. The steep rocky terrain harbours hidden valleys and sudden escarpments camoflauged by the dark canopy and long leaf-covered branches.
111683: The forest floor is covered by long flat slabs of hulking grey stone as it rises steadily on the steep mountainside. Blackened pine trees and dark oaks grow in the gaps between stones, their hard gnarled trunks cracking and splitting the rock ever more as time passes in the darkness below. Both branch and bough extend to create an impenetrable forest canopy resulting in stuffy dusty air with only the faintest hint of dark green light penetrating the canopy during the day.
111684: A large boulder is here, it must be heavy.

Gnarled oak trees lean ominously over rocky scrambles that dominate the mountainous landscape amid the forest. Large boulders cover the ground while tangly vines weave their way along the tree trunks and around the great stones. The rocky ground descends to the east even as the elevation increases to the west.
111685: A mountain mule (ulo) is standing here, ridden by you.

Tall oak and fir trees reach to the unseen sky, blocking any possible light from reaching the ground. Only a few small withered vines and scraggly bushes manage to survive in such conditions on the ground itself amidst the choking atmosphere of the massive dominating trees.
111686: A deep chasm with steep, slippery walls cuts this part of the Emyn-nu-Fuin off from the mountains to the south and east. Ancient, gnarled trees grow up to the very edge of the chasm, their trunks twisting this way and that as if attempting to escape the strangling vines that ruthlessly encircle them. The canopy above is dense enough to block out the sky. The light that finds its way along the forest floor from the gap created by the chasm will never be enough to dispel the gloom that lingers here.
111687:
A sprawling, twisted tree grows here.
On the tree, there are two piles of hawthorn berries.

The mountains of the Emyn-nu-Fuin climb toward the north-east as they slowly transform into taller fir-clad peaks. The terrain is very rugged as deep chasms and endless ravines clash with sudden cliff-walls rising up into the darkness of the forest above. Amidst this inhospitable terrain, crooked trees and sprawling bushes flourish amidst the cracks and crevices of the cold stone.
111697: The elongated shape of a stoat can be seen darting across the terrain.

This area of broken rocks and boulders is a short way downslope from a tall ridgeline to the west. Little vegetation has managed to take hold here, leaving the land mostly barren. A thick layer of sand and shattered rock fragments coats the ground, leaving only enough nutrients for the hardiest of weeds. A steep slope leads downward toward the east, but a deep crevice blocks the route to the south.
111698: There were once trees here in this mountainous wood, but they have been completely overgrown by strangling vines, creepers and roots. Together, the vegetation forms a dense, spiny mat that chokes off both light and possible directions of travel. The air is stale and thick with rotting fumes - both from decomposing leaves and something else, more sinister.
111699: The ground, as far as it can be seen amongst the dark, towering pines, is sandy and partially covered with needles and moss. South of here, the forest floor rises up considerably, forming a high mountainous wall of rocks, brambles and squat trees. A few dark shapes are standing in amongst the trees. They look like lurking, hulking shadows, but upon closer inspection it is clear that they are merely boulders covered with tortorous roots and branches.

The corpse of an agile Durbuk-hai spear-guard is lying here.

Charred stumps rise from a valley floor blanketed in powdery grey ash. Scorched giant skulls are impaled on blackened poles lining a cleared path down the centre of the valley. Steep rock walls close in to either side, making this a natural bottleneck.
111711: The corpse of a gaunt, vicious warg is lying here.

A cascade of water falls from the southern slope of a charred valley. The cataract flows into a stream clogged with ashes, blackened trunks, and large, rotting furs. Scattered giant bones and massive crude clubs litter the valley, evidence of a recent slaughter.
111713:
The corpse of a gaunt, vicious warg is lying here.
The corpse of a gaunt, vicious warg is lying here.
The corpse of a grizzled Durbuk-scarazot is lying here.

The charred valley splits into two levels, the southern shelf rising several feet above the northern. A stream of black, ash-laden water runs in from the east and pools in the lower section, restrained by an obstruction further down the valley. This stream has found an alternative outlet, trickling into a cave in the northern mountainside. On the higher ledge, a ring of large rocks surrounds a fire pit at the mouth of a gaping cavern.

Massive boulders, blackened trunks, and other debris fill the centre of this valley, damming off a stream flowing in from the east. The surrounding slopes are covered in charred, disintegrating trees. Large swathes of missing vegetation on the northern and western mountainsides reveal the origin of the rockslide. Crude wheelbarrows rest next to piles of rubble gathered farther down the valley, hinting at recent efforts to clear the obstruction.

Xarfax, wielding an engraved broadsword, is standing here trying to concentrate.

Wind and rain have cut into the mountainside, carving out a cleft that runs north and east up the steep slope. Exposed rocks and boulders provide rough, though relatively stable footing. Downslope of this natural trail, uprooted trees and gaping scars in the mountain show evidence of a rockslide. Upslope, scorched trees stand among the disintegrating ashes of burned vegetation.
111716: An erosion-carved furrow divides contrasting terrain as it meanders up a steep incline. Below, a vast part of the mountain slope has fallen away, leaving exposed rocks and reddish dirt. Above, a great fire has left blackened shrubs and shattered trees. Numerous rills trickle downward through the ashes, the beginnings of a process that will send the mountainside cascading into the valley below.
111717: A narrow gap between two peaks shows signs of wear by the elements. Dry runnels meander down the slopes, and there are broad swaths of missing vegetation now occupied by mounds of unstable scree. The entire mountainside is scorched, and there is no hint of green indicating regrowth of vegetation. Even the moss and lichen have not recovered on these black and barren slopes.
111718: A broad ledge curves around a mountain, leading to an overlook immediately to the west. Large boulders have tumbled onto the ledge here and there, and gaps in the ledge show where some have broken through. An unstable scree slope to the east leads down to an isolated plateau covered in fir trees.

A crudely armed Durbuk-hai warrior, wielding a short spear, is here, fighting Xarfax.
A crudely armed Durbuk-hai warrior gazes down at the forest below.

This overlook affords an excellent view of a broad valley stretching from northeast to southwest. Sharp, broken rock juts from either side of this crag, and mounds of debris far below are evidence of its erosion. The surface is somewhat unstable, and idle footsteps send small stones cascading down below. Eagles' nests dot the slopes of a peak to the immediate south.
111720: Sheer, exposed rock lines the valley walls. A few charred trunks rest against the cliffs, leaving scorch marks on the nearby rocks. A fire raged through here in the past. Most of the soil is rocky and meagre and it does not look like there was much plant life to begin with here that could burn.
