A natural arch spans a gap between sheer cliff walls. Skulls, giant skeletons, and other trophies hang from crude nails embedded in the arch. A heavy gate guards the valley to the east, and a recess in the northern cliff shelters a stash of food and weapons. Grey ashes blanket the valley floor.
111725:
A sturdy peg for hanging armour is on the wall.
On the peg, there are a sturdy pair of rigid leather sleeves and a rigid leather breastplate.
A weapons rack stands against the wall.
In the rack are a handaxe, a short spear, and a wooden club.
A scrawny Durbuk-hai orc sits against a wall, mending a piece of leather.

Racks of weapons sit in the centre of a large chamber near the entrance to a cave. Sets of leather and chain mail armour rest against the western wall, ready to be donned at a moment's notice. The cavern branches as it cuts deeper into the mountain; a passage to the east leads toward piles of crude bedding, while a rotten stench betrays a slaughterhouse that lies around a bend in a tunnel to the south.
111726:
A mass of tattered fabric lies here in a heap.
A crudely armed Durbuk-hai warrior, holding a short spear, is sleeping here.
A crudely armed Durbuk-hai warrior, holding a short spear, is sleeping here.
A young, eager Durbuk-hai warrior, holding a short spear, is sleeping here.

Many burrows branch out from this cave, deeper into the mountain. Their darkest recesses are well-shaded from daylight that might seep in from the entrance of the cave. Furs from various animals are strewn across the floor: crude bedding for the rank and file of the outpost. A burrow that is more spacious than the others leads into the north wall of the chamber. A grate blocks off a niche in the deepest part of the cave to the south; a wolf pen lies beyond it.
111727: The corpse of an agile Durbuk-hai spear-guard is lying here.

This burrow is spacious and relatively uncluttered, contrasting with a crowded, messy barrack visible to the south. There are two large alcoves to either side of the burrow; large mounds of furs and pelts piled in these alcoves make for relatively comfortable bedding. Sharp, polished spears and bucklers made of tanned hide lean against the western wall. A crude, narrow tunnel leads downward from the northern end of this burrow.
111728: A crude, marble-lined tunnel running in from the north comes to an abrupt dead-end at a rough granite wall to the south. Notches in the wall show the locations of unsuccessful attempts to try to break through this hard rock; broken pickaxes on the floor further testify to this failure. An alternate route bypassing the granite wall is given in the form of a jagged, crudely-carved hole in the ceiling which leads upward into a spacious burrow.
111729: A crudely-delved tunnel runs north and south, bulging here where it meets an underground cavity. This cavity opens east and west, its smoothly layered walls a stark contrast to the sloppy, uneven surfaces of the tunnel. A faint, acrid burnt odour lingers in the stale, dry air that fills this underground chamber.
111730:
A bloody meat hook hangs from the ceiling.
On the hook, there is a large piece of raw meat.
A bloody meat hook hangs from the ceiling.
On the hook, there is a large piece of raw meat.
A scrawny Durbuk-hai orc butchers a bloody carcass.

Rows of carcasses hang down from the low ceiling of a broad chamber. Cast-off mounds of reeking entrails sit in a corner. Piles of skins and furs lie on a natural rock shelf in the deepest part of the cavern, next to sharp tools that could be used to fashion them into armour and other garments. The walls of the cave have been spattered a deep reddish-brown that could only come from blood.
111731: A skeleton of some humanoid lies in the dust.

A barred grate separates this cramped cranny from the rest of the cave. The ceiling slants downward until it meets the floor a few yards beyond the grate. Cracked bones lie scattered among piles of stale dung and shed fur sits in piles along the walls.
111732:
A deep alcove covered in ash cuts into the eastern wall.
A lithe, devious-looking Durbuk-hai shaman is standing here.
A veteran of the Durbuk-hai watches the area, alert and poised for combat.
A veteran of the Durbuk-hai watches the area, alert and poised for combat.
A blistered commander of the Durbuk-hai glares about him with intense hatred.

Smooth dolomite makes up the surfaces of a large, circular chamber. The floor is covered in small piles of ashes and charred coals, and black scorch marks mar the white walls of the chamber. A crude alcove in the eastern wall holds wood, torches, and flints - materials for making a fire. A raised platform in the centre of the chamber is piled with mounds of singed bedding.
111734: Huge, dark fir trees stand closely spaced apart here in this shrub-filled and quiet part of the great Mirkwood. Shrubs and boulders make it impossible to travel in any other directions than south and east, but at least it is not hard to journey in those directions. Two trees have been chopped down here at some point in the not too distant past, and they are accompanied by the remnants of a small, abandoned campfire.
111735:
A massive hoary fir tree is here, towering over the forest floor.
A tree-snake lies wrapped around one of the tree branches.

The dominant species of tree here is a huge, dark fir that grows to several hundred feet in height. The trees have great, needle-rich crowns that form a dense, almost impenetrable canopy above. Below the canopy, the trunks of the trees are bare, leaving no place for birds to sit or for moss to grow. The general roughness of terrain conspires to make further travel possible only to the east and west.
111736: Huge fir trees stand close together with black oaks in this dark and foreboding forest. The ground is littered with leaves and pine needles, and a rich flora of moss and lichen grow among piles of small, round rocks and talus. This type of terrain is rough, and further travel is only possible to the west and to the north from here.
111737:
A tall pine tree grows here.
A large, black butterfly is fluttering about erratically.

A cairn comprised of mossy rocks and boulders is barely discernible among the abundant trees. There are no signs that the cairn fills any purpose, because it appears utterly abandoned and never used. The thick, bushy forest continues in all directions save west, where tangled shrubs and boulders make it impossible to find a viable path.
111738: The air here is still and unmoving, probably because of the many, many fallen trees and rotting logs that languish on the uneven, sloping forest floor. The only accessible part of this whole area is a small trench that leads west into a fresher part of the forest, and south up onto some sort of wooded hill.
111739: The only thing that gives away the fact that this is a hill is the curvature of the forest floor, because the many trees and the thick underbrush makes it hard to see much of anything here. The only way to go from here is north - all other directions are either blocked by impassable obstacles, or the ground slopes downward so severely that not even the most skilled climber would risk the descent.
111740:
A cluster of dark green, feathery fronds flourishes in the shade.
A long-tailed bird watches you from the vegetation.
A ghostly-white stag eyes its surroundings cautiously.

The rugged mix of oak shrub and conifers that grow here is challenged by the vines and shrubs that threaten to suffocate them with their tendrils and roots. East of here, the forest floor slopes upward onto some sort of hill. Travel is also possible to the south and west, further into the depths of Mirkwood.
111741:
A ghostly-white stag eyes its surroundings cautiously.
A long-tailed bird watches you from the vegetation.

These trees once grew to mighty heights, but many years ago they were blighted by a disease or poison of some kind. Now, only their trunks and main branches remain, whitened by age. Curiously enough, there is no rot in the trunks, and one may wonder if there was some sort of unnatural cause to their demise.
111742:
A dense patch of dark ferns grows in the shade.
A dense patch of dark ferns grows in the shade.
A dense patch of dark ferns grows in the shade.

The trees close ranks here, making it impossible to go anywhere but north. The tree trunks stand incredibly close together, and all the space in between them are taken up by bushes, vines and other overgrowth. A few rotten strands of spider webs hang suspended from the tree branches. The webs look old and withered, almost flimsy.
111743: The ground slopes dramatically here, up from the dark forest floor below and onto a high plateau-like shelf. There are plenty of trees here, mostly conifers but also a handful of dark, old gnarled beeches. Here and there among the roots of the trees and bushes one can discern both talus and larger granite boulders.
111744:
A rabid raccoon is sleeping here.
A rabid raccoon is sleeping here.
A rabid raccoon is sleeping here.
A rabid raccoon is sleeping here.

Aside from the thick, dark roots that criss-cross this confined space, there are hardly any noteworthy features here. Black, rotting leaves and flaky dirt make up the floor, walls and most of the ceiling. The smell in here is foul, a slow-rotting scent of vegetable decay is coupled with something more sinister, that of a sick, dying animal.
111745: A group of dark, black-trunked oak trees grow close together here. The ground beneath them is covered by a thick layer of rotting undergrowth and smelly old leaves. A handful of the trees died a long time ago, but because they stood so close together they have been unable to fall down properly. Now they are rotting in the places where they once grew and prospered, bearing an eerie resemblance to hollowed-out, cavity-filled teeth standing among a row of comparatively healthy ones.
111746: Thick, spiny brambles and dead foliage cover the bottom of this horse-shoe shaped depression in the forest. Naked granite walls are visible through the cascade of dead and dying roots and vines that hang down from the trees that grow along the edges of the trough. Travel is impossible in every direction except the east, where a grove of tall, dark oak trees eke out a tortured and light-starved existence.
111747: A swift, dark stream carves a rocky channel through this region of Mirkwood. The land rises to the east and south, and becomes mountainous. The stream flows north into an area full of rocky outcroppings and canyons. A swarm of maggots feeds upon the mangled remains of a large mammal that rests by the stream. Black, gnarled oaks crowd the western bank, a looming horde held back only by the gurgling water.
111748:
A brown stag is sleeping here.
A swarm of mosquitoes is here, humming around you.

A dark, rocky brook runs through the forested mountains, opaque water clouding its bed. Livid colonies of mould infest wilting lilies that float on the clouded water. Torpid mosquito swarms fill the air with fitful buzzing as they hover listlessly over the stream. Grey moss-clad cliffs rise throughout the forest, obstructing the stream's path and forcing it to detour around them.
111749: Bend in a Tributary of the Gulduin
A brown stag looks around with big, startled eyes.

A dark, clouded stream cuts a sharp bend around a rocky outcrop, disappearing down a narrow canyon to the west. A profound silence reigns among the oaks flanking the waterway. Great boughs, laden with leaves in shades of green and brown, overshadow the stream and further darken the already murky water.
111750: A murky stream cascades from a waterfall to the east and flows down a rocky slope. Its colour morphs as it runs: black-speckled leaves mingle with withered twigs on their way downstream. The forest near the stream is unnaturally still, as if lulled into a torpor by the murmuring flow.
111751: A dark cliff looms over a line of hills, casting perpetual shadows over their rocky summits. Sharp, protruding boulders hang precariously from these heights, as if poised to pounce on some unseen prey. A sea of trees drowns the valleys between these hills and sways under passing breezes.
111752: Rocky outcrops watch silently over a dark green sea of oaks whose branches reach for these heights as if to drag them down. Distant summits soar above the forest to the east, heralds of formidable mountains whose foundations lie hidden beyond the trees. The face of a promontory looms just to the north; dark recesses in its cliff wall provide natural lairs for unknown creatures.
111753: A large boulder is here, it must be heavy.

A tall crest of rock rises to the south, its narrow ridges reaching as if to grasp at these broken foothills. The forest seems to flee from the heights; stunted saplings and scrawny shrubs are all that persist here. Jet-black moss obscures a field of massive boulders that chokes out any vegetation that might otherwise grow between the trees.
111754: Toxic water bubbles from cracks in the ground.

Tall cliffs stretch over this narrow cleft in the mountains. A stream of slimy, viscous water pours into a deep, dark pool which teems with ochre vegetation whose protruding flowers exude a rank stench. Small insects with long, spindly legs skim across the surface of the pool.
111755: A fist of rock stretches over this shadowed depression. Its broken underside is covered in skittering masses of creatures whose chittering fills the forest. Pungent fungi thrive in the shadows of the crag, spreading over a dank, rotten bed of vegetation that swallows any footsteps that may fall upon it.
111756:
A huge black fungus is here, exuding a foul stench.
A huge black fungus is here, exuding a foul stench.
A giant, strange looking green fungus is here, ready to devour you in seconds.
A swift carnivore bustles around.

The surrounding sea of oaks is displaced by a stand of alders anchored to a craggy mountainside that rises to the north and east. Dark foliage obscures the sky, casting a pall over the mottled trunks of the trees. Fleshy fungi spread over the forest floor, devouring a rotting layer of vegetation. The foetid spores of these fungi form choking clouds that hover in the air.
111757:
A massive tree rots where it stands.
A colony of red ants is here. The ants seem to ignore you.

These hills gaze out over gloomy shadows that inhabit the valleys below. Creeping vines have consumed this highland, swallowing tree and rock alike. Fungi envelop a massive rotten oak that exudes thick, viscous sap. The foreboding peaks of the Emyn-nu-Fuin loom to the northeast.
111758: This low, barren peak rises like an island from the murky shadows of the forest. The forest appears ready to devour it. The rocky boulders at the peak's crown have held off the trees, but dark vines crawl through every gap and crevice. Sharp slopes nearly surround this isolated highland, the only escape lying to the west in the form of a narrow ridgeline that connects this hill to the next.
111759:
A pile of dry, brown leaves lies here.
A huge, frothing bear is sleeping here.

Thick clods of black dirt form the walls and ceiling of this cave, supported by a tangle of thick, gnarled roots. The ground is damp and covered in muddy pools. The only dry spot is a massive slab of rock in the deepest part of the cave. A thick layer of fur, leaves, and bark blankets this slab.
111760: A stand of firs grows on a level plateau lying in the shade of a mighty peak to the north. Sheer escarpments on every other side have isolated this alpine biome. A foul spring issues from a cleft in the mountainside, pouring into a dark pool that absorbs all light. Withered branches droop into the pool from trees near the water. The pool drains via a stream which trickles over mossy boulders before cascading over a drop-off to the west.
111761: This mountaintop crowns a ridge that runs northeast from here. Bounded by steep approaches on all sides, this level summit might at first appear to be an isolated shelter from the dangers of Mirkwood. However, frequent gusts of wind seem insistent in their attempts to cast any hapless climber back down to the shadows below.
111762:
A mountain ibex is jumping from rock to rock.
An ibex is watching you from afar.
An ibex is watching you from afar.
An ibex is watching you from afar.
An ibex is watching you from afar.

An elongated mound of raised terrain connects a high ridgeline to the south with the comparatively lower elevation of a mountain range that lies to the north. Sombre alders occupy the relatively level apex of the mound, choking out any other vegetation that tries to grow there. However, the steep exposed rocks on the slopes of this ridge do afford modest growth in the form of moss, lichen, and scraggly shrubs.
111763: A grey wolf is here, salivating profusely.

A spiny ridgeline looms above the vastness of Mirkwood. Vertebral boulders protrude from its rim, and claw-like crags reach out into the murky, seething forest to either side. A towering mountain rears up to the southwest, its tooth-like peak gnawing at the sky.
111764: This narrow ridge is flanked by steep, yawning cliffs. These sheer faces stretch over the mottled shadows of the valleys below. Creeping vines envelop the rocky crest, their crimson buds issuing a feculent stench. Carrion birds perch on scattered boulders, feasting on putrid flesh.
111765: Unstable scree slopes line this narrow ridge, fending off the press of the forest. Nests of carrion birds are visible in crevices below, the results of their scrounging revealed in scattered mounds of bones. Precarious boulders crown these heights, providing fragile purchase for creatures who wish to travel in any direction but down. A formidable peak rises to the west.
111766: Thick shrubs and stunted trees make up the immediate surroundings. However, while the forest is light, the undergrowth is very dense and the thin branches of the bushes thriving here have very long, sharp and black thorns. Especially to the west, branches, shrubs, and thorns are intertwined together, making it impossible to travel in that direction. The forest seems to grow thicker to the north and south.
111767: A cluster of dark green, feathery fronds flourishes in the shade.

Dark vines cling to low branches in this gloomy forest. In the shade of the trees, bushes and ferns thrive, as though the lack of light does not bother them at all. To the south and west the forest and dense foliage continues without reprieve.
111768: A large brown snake with black patches is coiled here.

A grove of twisted oaks, with an almost malevolent aura about them, rise up amidst thorny thickets and sprawling bushes. To the north, a craggy outcrop of dark rock thrusts up suddenly through the forest floor. It is covered in deep-red flowers that give it the appearance of a broken, uneven row of monstrous blood-soaked teeth.
111769: Stygian Shadows beneath a Dark Canopy
A black snake hurries towards you with sly intentions.

Old and gnarled ash trees grow here, watching over a forest landscape overgrown with thorny bushes. There is enough space between these gloomy sentinels to squeeze through in single file. A faint odour of decay and putrifying plants hangs in the air, refusing to give way for weather or wind.
111770:
A small, dense tangle of roots covers the ground.
A small, dense tangle of roots covers the ground.

A strange band of unidentifiable mottled trees encircle a small patch of grass. Long vines hang down from above and lie in tangled coils on an ancient, petrified stump in the centre of the small clearing. Around and beyond the strange grove of trees, Mirkwood awaits, gloomy and veiled in shadows.
111773: The lower end of vines sway gently in the trees here, like some strange creature waiting for a hapless victim to wander into its trap. It is difficult to see further than half-way up the canopy as the higher parts are hidden in gloom. The trees seem to be leaning slightly to the west, where it looks like the forest grows darker and more ominous.
111774: The ground slopes slightly downwards here forming a valley in the forest. At the bottom of the valley, there is a huge black elm standing in lone majesty. Its branches seem to rustle threateningly as if warning away creatures or indeed the very forest itself from approaching.
111775:
A solitary fir tree stands here surrounded by corrupted trees.
A black snake hurries towards you with sly intentions.

An impressive and solitary fir tree stands here, resolute against the surrounding forest of twisted, corrupted trees. It gives the impression of the last soldier, surrounded by a tainted force. The largest boughs of the fir are spread on an east-west axis like arms, and the powerful roots are drawn up slightly out of the ground as though it has been preparing itself to flee from assailants.
111776:
Massive, black, oozing vines reach out from the choked canopy.
A black snake hurries towards you with sly intentions.

The ancient trees are covered by layers of long, grey lichen which makes the forest appear as if there are hundreds of gnarled, hunched figures with long beards standing in the gloom. The lichen sways slowly in the wind, and vines dangling from the branches above caress the ground. Most of the vines have natural, green shades, but one species stands out for its inflamed red colour. This vine winds itself tightly around some of the trunks. The impression is that of ongoing strangulation, and although the effect might be an illusion, the trees suffering the red vines seem less hale than the rest of the forest.
111779: A black snake hurries towards you with sly intentions.

In this havoc of untamed, shifting vegetation, it is unlikely that any permanent paths or trails can be found. Even as an opening between thorny bushes seems to materialise, it begins to disappear again. There is a constant background noise of faint but distinct hissing sounds.
111781:
A tree-snake lies wrapped around one of the tree branches.
A tree-snake lies wrapped around one of the tree branches.
A diamondback rattlesnake is coiled here, ready to strike.
A tree-snake lies wrapped around one of the tree branches.

This huge linden tree is very easy to climb, because of the thick and rough bark. The linden starts branching at low height with several very thick branches that can easily be reached from the ground, which makes the climb even easier. In one branching point, there is an almost flat area. Apparently some creatures have found the place and made it their home, since there is a nest made of pieces of vine, hay, and other vegetation in there.
111782: A black snake hurries towards you with sly intentions.

The forest and undergrowth have created a mayhem of gnarled trunks, thorn-clad branches, entangled vines, and dense bushes. Paths through the undergrowth seem to appear only to vanish instants later, as the foliage shifts in ways no wind could accomplish. The forest floor is barely visible and these woods are perfect hiding places for any manner of wild animal that slithers or crawls.
111784: Shallow Gully in a Stygian Forest
A large brown snake with black patches is coiled here.

The bed of the gully is wet with mud and decaying leaves, and the air is filled with the stench of putrifying plantlife. Vicious-looking, thorn-covered bushes line the steep ridges of the gully, their thick branches leaning out above as if threatening to leap down into the gully and attack trespassers.
111785: Dark Fissure in a Stygian Forest

Ashes and oaks, gnarled with age, loom overhead, lining the sides of this fissure. Fiercely tangled brambles, thorns gleaming with dew, obstruct the way north. The ground continues to slope gently downwards to the south as the twisting fissure disappears from view. On the ground, a narrow crack between cliff and rocks is visible and there is a passage down into darkness.
111786: Stygian Darkness within a Decaying Forest
A black snake hurries towards you with sly intentions.

The trees seem to form a natural cavern-like room from apparently dead branches, vines, and other vegetation. The decaying vegetation has interwoven into a sort of curtain preventing almost any sunlight from shining through. Thorny shrubs and thickets below the trees complement the curtain of decaying vegetation, perfecting the area.

Oak and ash, interspersed with an occasional dark alder, spread out in all directions. A powerful malignant aura seems to encompass these woods. The trees look unhealthy and are spotted with patches of mould and strange growths. Vines dangle from branches above, trembling with inner life and shifting about as if they were tendrils. The ground is unusually soft and covered in rotting leaves, absorbing the sound of footfalls.
111788:
A sturdy pack horse is standing here.
A sturdy trained horse is standing here.
A sturdy trained horse is standing here.

This channel is formed in the rock deep beneath Mirkwood. There is a bit of moisture on the ground, but the water is not flowing. The surface is smooth and corners are rounded by something probably many years ago. The rounded tunnel continues to the east, while its other end to the south has collapsed, leaving piles of rubble on the floor of the tunnel and dark openings in the ceiling above. The air is cool and humid here, dozens of feet beneath the forest floor of Mirkwood.
111789:
An albino salamander is here, perched on some rocks.
An albino salamander is here, perched on some rocks.
An albino salamander is here, perched on some rocks.

This underground channel, is embedded in the rock dozens of feet beneath Mirkwood. The tunnel leads off in three directions. The walls have been smoothened by something long years ago, perhaps water, and a flora of lichen and fungi grows on the walls of the tunnel.
111790: This is a cavern with smooth walls and there is a very narrow trough in the western wall. The trough is not big enough to enter. There is a crevice in the ceiling to the north. Its surface is smooth and slippery, but the walls are not very steep, so it's easy to traverse there. A thin layer of stagnant water gathers on the bottom of the channel, but it is muddy and there is too little for a drink. Sound echoes strangely here in the rocky channel.
111791:
A sturdy trained horse is standing here.
A stocky mountain mule is here, waiting to serve.

This tunnel has smooth walls, and a large bowl-like depression in the floor suggests that water fell from above. There is an unreachable fissure in the ceiling. A pile of leaves and branches lie in the depression where they've fallen through, and from the sides of the fissure, roots can be seen poking through the walls.
111792: Steep Slope above the Old Forest Road

There is a jagged fissure at the pinnacle of this hill, and at the bottom a cave or tunnel can be seen. This steep, rounded hill is surprisingly smooth, clad in green moss and very slippery. It is possible to slide down the hill's sides but climbing back up might be impossible. The Old Forest Road is visible to the north at the foot of the hill.
111793: Shattered Outcrop in a Stygian Forest

An outcrop of broken rock rises from the forest floor but even at its pinnacle the outcrop does not break through the canopy of Mirkwood. Wide branches from the surrounding forest intertwine above and hide the sky from view. Seregon covers much of the dark rock, its blood-red flowers rising up from the clefts like a wound in the rock itself.
111802: Stygian Shadows beneath a Dark Canopy

Black roots shift uneasily all around you.

A tremendous black oak looms here.

The forest here is filled with dense tangles of thorny bushes and thickets. The ground is a maze of roots snaking around each other, and most of the trees are overgrown with vines. The vines seem to be of a strange sort with rows of needle-like thorns growing along their lengths.
111809: Stygian Shadows of an Ominous Forest

The forest thins out to the east and west where dark groves of alder trees keep the undergrowth to a minimum. To the east, a jagged outcrop rises from the forest floor, making movement in that direction seem difficult. Decaying vines hang limp in the shadow of the outcrop like the tentacles of a thousand long-dead octopi.
111811:
A skeleton of some humanoid lies in the dust.
A desecrated mound rises from the ground, its contents scattered.
A huge gnarled oak tree is here, looming ominously overhead.
A black moth flutters around.

Elderly oak trees bent from many long years in Mirkwood lean with skin gnarled and black, wrinkled from the ages. They creak at the joints, a sign of fatigue from old age, yet the end of their vigil is nowhere in sight. This old forest endures, or rather suffers, the great passage of time marching ever on and on.
111812: An army of trees advance southwards to an incline, where the forest continues up the slope. Arrayed among them are many tall oak and beech trees with gnarled bark, obsidian in colour and as dark as the night. Long shadows creep beneath the trees.
111814: The corpse of a green-cloaked Durbuk-hai archer is lying here.

Among many stony crags Mirkwood endures the rough, elevated terrain, dotting the ground with trees of various heights. Detritus rings the larger boulders, evidence of the elements working against these rocks over time. The mountain sharply rises to the east and falls off in all other directions.
111815: These dark, corrupted trees are draped with the raiment of hoary webs, which reach from branch to branch across the canopy as a reminder of the terror that calls these old woods home. Roots twist about the sloping forest floor, sprawling from the black trunks like long, crooked fingers, seeking sustenance.
111816:
A rusty pickaxe with a broken handle lies discarded here.
An old, sturdy mine cart stands here on the end of a pair of iron rails.
A large bat is here, hanging in the darkness.

It appears nobody has used this place for ages. Dwarven tools for the craft of mining, caked with a thick layer of dust from years of disuse, are scattered across many flat surfaces. From the heights of the cave many stalactites thrust towards the ground like teeth, and in most places stalagmites reach upwards as if to meet them. On an old track sits an empty cart of wood and iron. The track and the passageway, braced along the rough walls with thick, wooden beams, continues east. However, the way is blocked by collapsed rubble.
111817: A cluster of dark green, feathery fronds flourishes in the shade.

Among the fray of trees, the forest grows exceedingly thick, allowing only a narrow passage west to east between old, hoary trunks and hanging limbs. The ground is crowded with twisted roots that wind here and there as the soil underfoot disappears almost entirely. Nevertheless, fern and forest weed manage to find a way, growing within the cavities between the greedy roots.
111818:
A tremendous black oak looms here.
A tremendous black oak looms here.

A makeshift shelter of dead logs that once leaned against an array of wide, gnarled oaks has long since collapsed, abandoned and relinquished to the devices of the forest. Ropy webs spread across the top of the ruined hut and climb the trees up to the dark canopy. One of the trees bears the scratches of a large animal, revealing the forest to be desolate but not uninhabited.
111819:
A cluster of dark green, feathery fronds flourishes in the shade.
A black moth flutters around.
A black moth flutters around.

Among the tall black oaks stand coarse, tall boulders as the ground forms a slope leading up to the south. Between root and rock it is difficult to find a path anywhere to the north or east. In the few places of clear ground, bracken has taken up residence seeking all the light the canopy will allow to reach the forest floor.
111820: Rugged crags and large trees cover this part of the Emyn-nu-Fuin. The ground slopes down to the north, allowing a descent to lower forests. The rough mix of mountains and forest continues to the west and south. Tall firs dominate this section of the mountain, but owing to the rocky turf, the forest is thin enough to allow the sky to poke through the canopy.
111821:
The wicked undergrowth rustles malevolently, shifting and widening.
A small, dense tangle of roots covers the ground.
An elaborate red flower sits within a dark mass of briars.
Some dark, thick writhing vines whip all around you.
Some dark, thick writhing vines whip all around you.
Some dark, thick writhing vines whip all around you.

The terrain curves into a dry ravine travelling down from the north until it comes to an impassable wall of trees. The cusp of the gully is lined with aspen, while on the upward slopes west and east there are many beech and oak trees.
111822:
A rotting tree lies here, covered in sticky web.
A newborn spider is here.
A newborn spider is here.
A newborn spider is here.
A black spider crawls here, a shiny red spot visible on its belly.
A huge, poisonous spider is here.

Some dark, thick writhing vines whip all around you.

Twisted oaks, some tall and some bent grow alongside one another, barely allowing room for passage. Thick, strong webs wrap every possible surface, black bark and green roof barely visible behind the dense network of ashen rope. Matted dark green leaves are dispersed all about the ground.
111823: A black squirrel peers down from the branches of the trees.

This area, sloping down to the south, is crowded with trees all the way up to the southern cliff, over which some black oaks lean precariously, paying no mind to gravity. The old forest intends to grow everywhere possible, as some defiant saplings manage to jut out from the clumpy soil of the vertical face of the cliff, their trunks curved straight out and upwards. The drop makes the way south impassable, though it is not extremely far to the forest below.
111824: Foul webs span across Mirkwood, engulfing the exit south with their complex patterns.

The thickness of the dark forest is unhindered by the rugged terrain, which climbs higher to the south. Maleficent shadows lurk beneath the eaves of these wooded mountains, creeping over root, twig, and stone to cover the land in darkness. Some black oaks grow around a giant, granite boulder that has been sundered into two large pieces, the great work of the elements over time.
111825: Foul webs span across Mirkwood, engulfing the exit north with their complex patterns.

A sea of trees can be seen over the edge of the cliff to the south, which stands moderately high above the forest below, while on this level the woods are just as thick. At the cliff the fresh air moves freely in stark contrast to the stiffness that hangs in the area away from the cliff. This escarpment continues to the east and the ground slopes upward to the north until it gradually levels off.
111826:
A massive forlorn tree grows here, dominating the forest.
A brown stag looks around with big, startled eyes.

The way through the mountains turns west and north as it winds through a small gully. Many dark oaks follow the rough and bumpy passage, while the steep sides are covered with bent, hanging plants and dark, clumpy soil. A few standing dead trees loom overhead, ghosts of forest past. The rugged terrain breaks up the forest, allowing many large holes in the canopy to appear.
111827: Barely more than hills among a forest, the heights of the mountains of Mirkwood remain covered with its trees. At this elevation the forest has dissipated enough for the canopy to allow light from above. The terrain grows harsh to the south and west, while a faint game trail winds off to the east. A blanket of rubble lines the mountainside to the north, completely hindering the growth of vegetation, a rare occurrence in this old forest.
111828: A slope rises from the south and onwards to the northwest, covered with jutting crags and old, leaning oaks that brush up against one another, tangling their branches and obstructing the passage of light into the forest. Stony hillocks march along the incline, promising a rugged traversal for those who wish to travel here. A singular beech stands amidst the hills, its knobby skin hiding fallen needles in various grooves.
111829: An array of trees with black, corrupted bark travels up the slope towards the north. These ancient trunks seem heavy with the strain of their own limbs, holding up the dark canopy which hangs in the stillness as if it were a sky beneath a sky. The shadows are long and menacing here, deep in the dark forest.
111830:
A small round stone lies in the dust.
A small round stone lies in the dust.
A deft Durbuk-hai slinger is here, upset at the presence of intruders.
A deft Durbuk-hai slinger is here, upset at the presence of intruders.
A deft Durbuk-hai slinger is here, upset at the presence of intruders.

Burrowed into the mountain, this cramped hovel serves as a guard post for the forest lands claimed by the Durbuk-hai orcs. An aperture formed by a diagonal crack in the soil to the south allows one to monitor the immediate vicinity. The rough walls curve into an irregular ceiling, all layered with clumps of dirt. The air is thick with moisture, and a steady dripping sound can be heard.
111831:
A small barrel stands on the ground.
A sturdy crate made of nailed wooden planks sits on the floor.
A water barrel has been left here.

Deep underground a plethora of crates and barrels containing provisions crowd this tiny corridor of the cave. The containers are made of a crude wood, their sides and tops bound and rivited with iron. The cavern floor is rough and worn from frequent traffic in and out. All about the room a subterranean humidity hangs densely in the air.
111832: Fallen oaks, husks of trees once old and weary, rest along the way north and south. Even in an old forest nothing is wasted, as dark moss and fern grow among these dead logs. In the distance the spectre of the forest can be seen in the dark silhoutte of far off trees.
111833: A black squirrel peers down from the branches of the trees.

The ground falls and rises again forming a bowl dispersed with ancient beech and oak. These timeworn trees appear to be touched by darkness; a strange sorcery has perverted them and tinted their bark black like the raiment of ravens. Dense foliage covers the ground, a dark green bracken that struggles to survive off what meagre light the greater trees allow to reach them.
111834: A thick stump is all that remains of what must have been a majestic tree.

All around but to the east the trees are impenetrable, as if the old forest is jealous of its secrets and weary of sharing them with outsiders. A melee of black branches with dark green leaves crowd the high areas, creating a thick roof through which no light may pass. Even from the eagles Mirkwood protects its hidden knowledge.
111835: The corpse of a grizzled Durbuk-scarazot is lying here.

The trail extends west and east, its gravel worn from age and perturbed on the edges by growing roots. To the north, the thick wall of trees gives way; however, the imposing limbs of the forest trees still reach over the path, their edifice forming a ceiling that denies any view of the sky.
111836: A black squirrel peers down from the branches of the trees.

Sinister branches crowd the area above and to the side of the trail, forming a narrow corridor along which to travel. Many branches and leaves have fallen and begun to decay, attracting a number of insects. Old, black roots dig into the trail, disrupting the packed soil and layered gravel.
111837: Obstruction in the Old Forest Road

A large boulder is here, it must be heavy.
A massive obstruction of uprooted trees blocks the road to the south.

The trail, made of packed soil and layered with gravel, bends here, extending east and south. The way to the south ends abruptly, blocked by dead logs and branches, rotting beneath the eaves of the forest. This pile of debris, reaching high into the tangled, black branches above, is no accident; its construction appears purposeful and malevolent.
111838:
An elite Durbuk-hai guard is standing here, armed with spear and shield.
An elite Durbuk-hai guard is standing here, armed with spear and shield.
A domesticated pony, beast of burden to many, stands here.

Filthy water trickles across the floor of a cave, pooling into stagnant puddles where there are dips in the rock. Sodden pelts scattered on the floor are starting to rot; they emit a rank stench. Several giant skeletons rest against the walls, surrounded by spatters of long-dried blood. The smooth natural walls of the cavern turn eastward, opening into a grisly scene in the chamber to the east. However, the trickle of the water continues down a narrow, rubble-lined mine-tunnel to the north.
111839:
A scrawny Durbuk-hai orc digs away at a mound of rubble.
A scrawny Durbuk-hai orc digs away at a mound of rubble.
A gaunt, vicious-looking warg pads towards you, jaws slavering hungrily.

An opaque stream of water flows in from a tunnel to the south. It proceeds to seep beneath a mound of rubble that entirely covers what would be a gap in the eastern cave wall. Iron chains extend from rings embedded in the walls, leading to shackles meant to restrain the slaves that excavated this mine. The dusty floor is littered with filthy refuse and rotting scraps of food.
111840: Tall gnarled trees grow thick and close together, preventing all sunlight from piercing the canopy above. Rotting vegetation covers the forest floor on top of massive roots that extend from the feet of the dark trees. Huge rocks burst forth from the ground in increasing numbers toward the south where the dark woods continue up toward the feet of mountains.
111841: The fir trees here are hoary and overgrown with sickly coloured fungi that vary in their grotesque shapes and contours. Tangles of thick vines snake up along the trees, twisting around boles and branches. To the south, the terrain becomes elevated as the trees are forced to grow among boulders and rocks, while to the east the forest floor appears to descend.
111842:
A wolf spider is here, among the trees.
A black moth flutters around.

The great bent trees here appear to be sparse amid a gloomy depression. The majority of the trees are covered by a damp, grey moss that smells strongly of decay. The forest to the north and west appears to climb away off into the horizon, while a single dark and narrow gap opens to the south covered in thick sticky webs.
111843: Massive roots shift uneasily all around you.

Great dark oaks and firs grow close together with boughs and branches intertwining in every direction. Thick twisted roots weave their way along the forest floor in a tangled web of strangling creepers. The shadowy woods extend to the north, south, and east beneath the blackness of the unseen treetops until they collide with steep mountain cliffs.
111846:
A copper penny lies on the ground.
A copper penny lies on the ground.
A black moth flutters around.
A black moth flutters around.

Black trees grow wildly and close together in soft soil covered with damp moss. Small plants struggle to survive even in the fertile ground, deprived of sunlight through the impregnable forest canopy looming high above. Small worn stones covered with moss rest in the dirt beneath the trees, just above the roots that visibly deform the ground.
111847: Burrowing into the earth, this dark passageway is covered in unusually large cobwebs. Sticky threads stretch taught forming layers of webbing around all but the floor, which is covered in moist soil and some light vegetation that extends from the forested depression to the north.
111848:
A brown, long-legged spider swiftly charges at you.
A brown, long-legged spider swiftly charges at you.

Thick, sticky webs cover every surface of the black tunnel. Nothing grows at this depth along the hard tacky floor or on the milky white walls and ceiling. The many tightly-woven strands of exceptionally strong silk are coated with a clear liquid that clings immediately to anything that comes into contact with it.
111849: A tiny spider is here, eating a tiny bug.

The web-covered route through the earth is covered in what appears to be a single, thick pale web that suffocates every surface. Occasionally, a light breeze issues from above causing some of the loose fibers along the walls and ceiling to sway to and fro. The slightest touch of the webs here causes a visible tremor to carry on eastward into the foreboding darkness.
111850: A winding webbed corridor winds its way underground amidst numerous pillars, carved from the elements and time, standing fast as if to hold open the pallid veins of the earth. Stones of various sizes protrude from the walls but are veiled by thick webs that stretch to conquer all visible surfaces.
111852: A forest spider is here crawling around.

A narrow corridor winds its way through the bottom of a large canyon that rises to the south. Large white cracks are visible along the steep dark walls of rock. The canyon floor is barren but for a few weeds. Far above, the edges of the forest canopy can be seen hanging over the top of the recess like the roof of a black tunnel.
111853:
A skeleton of some humanoid lies in the dust.
A brown, long-legged spider swiftly charges at you.
A brown, long-legged spider swiftly charges at you.

Dark black moss grows along the sides of the canyon while rotting debris, fallen from the overhanging forest above, covers the ground. A lone crag juts from the otherwise soft soiled wall to the south. Fern and weed fill the moist floor, unhindered by the surrounding decay.
111854:
An ancient fungus smothers the boulders.
A brown, long-legged spider swiftly charges at you.

Black weeds sprout from the moist floor amidst piles of foul-smelling fungi and rotting plant matter. Thick strands of ominous webbing stretch between the looming stone walls, though the canopy above is still visible between them. Drops of moisture collect along the bottoms of the silken ropes and occasionally drip down on the dark mouldy piles below.
111856:
A large, bulbous eggsac is pulsating here.
Pitch-black water with a strange smell has collected here.
A forest spider is here crawling around.
A huge, venomous tarantula extends her legs to you.

Shallow pools of black water have formed in the soft dark soil to form a hidden bog. Tall weeds grow thick in sloppy mud surrounding each pool amidst the darkness in the still wet air. The trunk of a dead ancient oak leans precariously against the west wall, its narrow top having already sunk down into a particularly large black morass. A foreboding rounded tunnel entrance leads into the eastern wall of the canyon revealing only complete and utter blackness in that direction.
111857: Decayed vegetation covers the wet, muddy floor of the deep crevice. The steep passage narrows into a jagged fissure and an apparent dead-end to the south. Thick webs crawl up the cleavage of the canyon, making passage possible only by those fell creatures that produced the sticky strands. Dark vines hang from the forest over the top of the crack as they strain to reach the rancid water below.
111858:
A grotesque oblong eggsac dangles ominiously from the ceiling.
A large, bulbous eggsac is pulsating here.

A round tunnel has been bored into the stone, its walls and ceiling hidden by thickly-woven webs. The wet stone floor seems to prevent silky strands from sticking to it, in spite of the complex weave of tight cords that adorn the rest of the tunnel. All surfaces save the floor are covered in thick white ropes that glisten with some semi-translucent substance as well as clear moisture droplets in the dark passageway.
111859:
A large, bulbous eggsac is pulsating here.
A newborn spider is here, hungrily crawling about.
A newborn spider is here, hungrily crawling about.

A brown, long-legged spider swiftly charges at you.
A brown, long-legged spider swiftly charges at you.
Bulg, wielding a great warsword, is standing here.

Thick black mud and pools of dark water make up the floor of the tunnel even as immense strands of sticky silk cords stretch tightly from wall to wall. Every surface other than the floor is entirely white, covered with hideously strong webs that jiggle and dance in a wavelike fashion when touched or jostled. Strange claw-like impressions are clearly present in the mud along the floor, and a foul reek seems to emanate from the north.
111860:
Traces of fierce red tones form the aura of this place.
The corpse of a great brood mother is lying here.
The corpse of a newborn spider is lying here.
