This cavern is wide and round, though the ceiling is fairly low throughout. The floor is made up of rough stone and is covered in crude bedding made from tattered furs, skins, and pelts. A foul musk fills the air and the stale odour of sweat mingled with a damp rot emanates from the bedding. The ceiling rises gently to the immediate north where this chamber joins with a much larger cavern.
112079: A gloomy passageway carved from the dark bedrock begins here at the foot of a set of crude stairs to the west. The top of the stairs is shrouded in darkness and of the passageway that leads off towards the east no more than a few dozen feet can be seen before it disappears into inky blackness. Some care was taken when crafting this tunnel, for while the walls and ceiling are uneven and rough, the floor is flat and smooth, making for easy travel.
112080: A crude passageway cuts through black shale as it runs east-to-west. Chambers branch off north and south, their contents hidden in gloomy shadow. A foul medley of odours lingers in this tunnel, including an acrid burnt smell mixed with the dank orkish musk and a faint tinge of rot.
112081:
A mass of tattered fabric lies here in a heap.
A battered warg fur has been left here.
A young orc grips his weapon impatiently, eager to prove himself.
A young orc grips his weapon impatiently, eager to prove himself.
A Durbuk-hai warrior stands here with a frenzied gleam in his eyes.
A deft Durbuk-hai slinger lurks in the shadows.
A deft Durbuk-hai slinger lurks in the shadows.

This oblong chamber is dozens of yards long east-to-west, yet only at most three yards wide north to south. A narrow gap in the northern wall serves as the only exit and the only means for a strong and acrid odour to escape into the tunnels beyond. Cobwebs cover the walls but it is quite clear that the chamber itself sees daily use.
112082:
A defensive wooden structure is here, protecting the eastern edge of the chasm.
A Durbuk-hai warrior stands here with a frenzied gleam in his eyes.
A Durbuk-hai warrior stands here with a frenzied gleam in his eyes.
An elite Durbuk-hai guard is standing here, armed with spear and shield.

A great chasm cleaves its way through a carved passageway running east to west, opening suddenly in the centre of the tunnel. Neither the chasm's ceiling or floor can be seen, hidden by a heavy gloom that shrouds both the height and depth of the great crack itself. The delvers of this passage carved walkways into its sides, effectively creating a ring of narrow shelves. The hewn stone ring creates a strong natural chokepoint at the eastern end where the two paths meet that has been further fortified with a wooden defensive structure.
112083:
A smoking pot is here emitting a foul stench.
A crude blood-stained wooden table covered in entrails is here.
A Durbuk-hai warrior is here, ill-equipped but ready to fight for his tribe.
A Durbuk-hai warrior is here, ill-equipped but ready to fight for his tribe.
A cunning Durbuk-hai shaman is here performing a gruesome ritual with bloody entrails.
A veteran of the Durbuk-hai watches the area, alert and poised for combat.

Paint-flecked bones hang from the walls and ceiling of a low chamber underground that is shrouded in complete blackness. A crude wooden table covered in miscellaneous herbs, animal entrails and strange tools sits at the centre of the cave, while a recess deep in the eastern wall contains a pot suspended over a pile of black coals and ashes. The air is slightly hazy and contains an acrid odour interspersed with the stench of recent death.
112084: Hulking tree trunks support a looming canopy of thick, dark vegetation making it impossible to discern night from day. Tough sinewy vines slither their way among branch and bough as they ruthlessly seek out further sustenance in their overtly parasitic fashion. Great roots jut from the uneven hilly forest floor as they continue their own search for water in the rocky soil below.
112085: The forest is dominated by ancient sprawling oaks armoured by thick, ridged bark that spirals down to each tree's rooted feet. Thorny vines and black-leafed creepers snake upward around the knotted trunks, disappearing into the dense canopy above. Ferns and fungi thrive on the shaded forest floor amidst a thick layer of fallen leaves that covers the ground.
112086: Gaps among the dark trees reveal that the tangly forest rests atop tall hills and continues to climb towards the Emyn-nu-Fuin, the Mountains of Mirkwood. As the forest continues to ascend, the composition of the trees become mainly fir and other evergreens. The air is noticeably cooler and brisker here than below in the stuffy depths of the lower woods.
112087: A tangled forest spreads across the floor of a valley nestled among the low but rugged mountains of the Emyn-nu-Fuin. Short and twisted trees with heavy, lichen-covered branches scrape against the thorny shrubs that grow beneath them. The slopes of the valley are gentle to the east and the south while the northern and western slopes are much steeper and covered in outcroppings.
112088: Moulds grow in a slithering, oozing pattern down twisted tree trunks in this hilly region of Mirkwood. Tangled vines weave their way around thorny bushes, creating choked undergrowth filled with perilous obstacles and razor sharp thorn-filled thickets. A faint, diffused green glow makes up the only light that naturally reaches the forest floor during daylight hours.
112089: Mixed oak and fir trees grow interspersed atop rolling hills while small shrubs with withered leaves waste away on the forest floor. Dark stone slabs protruding through the topsoil combine with the rotting plant matter to blacken the hillsides beneath the looming trees that cover them.
112090: The forest covers rough, mountainous terrain as the slopes of Emyn-nu-Fuin grow steeper. Large blackened boulders dot the climbing landscape amid countless twisted trees, each harbouring its own strange perforations in its bark and lower limbs. The rocky soil supports various small bushes even on its steeper slopes beneath the mighty oaks and firs that race upward into the dense canopy.
112091: These rocky outcrops are shaded by tall, hoary trees. A canopy of tree limbs covered with grey lichen obstructs the view of the sky. Cracked boulders sit between the outcrops, perhaps separated from the crags by the action of wind and rain. Vines and roots now intertwine with these boulders, continuing the process of breaking them down into dirt.
112092: A mountain goat is here, jumping from cliff to cliff.

Massive, black oak trees loom to either side of a rugged ridge, their gnarled and sweeping limbs hanging low to the ground. Bone white vines tangle with the branches, wrapping around the massive trunks, cracked and weeping a dark and foul smelling sap. Dense shrubs surround boulders atop the ridge.
112093: Gnarled and twisted trees grow closely together in a large grove, their branches intertwined and entangled. Black moss grows along the bark of the trees and spreads up to the undersides of their branches. A riot of thorn-covered bushes grows in the shade beneath the canopy, seemingly thriving in the light-starved conditions.
112094: Squat, gnarled oaks press close on all sides, leaving only narrow tracts of passable ground between them. The thick, knotted branches of the trees droop low, covered in a dark, moist lichen. The lichen seems to creep along the bark whenever a stifled breeze manages to find its way through the suffocating canopy.
112095: The woods grow thick among these crags, and cast dark shadows on the boulder- strewn forest floor. The air is thick with smells of decay and rot, and several trees lie uprooted and broken on the ground. Black vines crawl across tree limbs in a tangled mess, intertwining to form the dark canopy overhead.
112096: The surroundings become increasingly craggy toward the apex of this rugged ridgeline to the west. Vegetation in the form of hoary, ancient trees, sprawling thornbushes, and plants of all sorts cover the mountains. A long, forested slope descends into a valley to the north. The valley floor is shrouded by dense foliage and nothing of it can be seen.
112097: Heavily forested, rocky, and craggy ground forms a series of ridges that expand in all directions. The cliffs to the east are steep and cut short any thought of travel in that direction. The undergrowth is made up of moss and ferns, with some larger bushes growing along the edges of narrow ravines where the canopy is less dense.
112098: Ancient oaks cover these hills entirely, their green canopies blotting out the sky. A variety of sickly-looking fungi grows on their trunks, on boulders, roots, and the forest floor. These fungi are black and grey, and a rotten smell rises from a yellow liquid slowly oozing from them to gather in repugnant pools on the ground.
112099: The forest in this rocky area grows dense, with a mix of oak, fir and beech competing for space. Large rocks and boulders covered in blankets of green moss litter the ground in-between trunks. The land is shrouded in gloom and shadows as the canopy fights a winning battle of domination over the forest floor against sun and moon.
112100: Dark trees and rugged cliffs cover this ridgeline as it extends to the south and the east. The trees are mostly hoary, gnarled oaks clad in cloaks of mottled lichen. Green moss grows on the rock faces and on scattered boulders throughout the region.
112101: A mountain goat is here, jumping from cliff to cliff.

Some mould-covered boulders sit askew along the apex on this overgrown, rocky ridge. The mountain range itself is quite low, but steep cliffs and densely growing thorn bushes make it difficult to traverse. Some trees have managed to find a home here as well, though they are twisted, stunted things. Dark, thorn-covered vines hang from branches, swaying gently.
112102: Low, rugged mountains rise above Mirkwood. The terrain is rough with jutting rocks, moss-covered boulders, and small gorges everywhere. Trees with black bark and knotted roots rise among the boulders to spread their crowns above, casting the mountains into gloom.
112103: Struggling, sickly trees blanket the slopes of broad, low hills. Their branches droop to the ground, their wilting leaves spotted with black. The trunks of the trees are covered in yellow-green fungi which cloud the air with choking spores. The putrid odour, the mottled bark, and the sagging crowns of the trees combine to tell a story of rot and decay.
112104: A wide variety of trees and bushes grows here, all crowded along the bottom of a long, narrow pass. The sides of the pass rise almost vertically, with some jagged outcroppings and small ledges here and there. On these some small weeds and moss have found a home.
112105: A series of passes allow for fairly comfortable passage through this part of the Emyn-nu-Fuin. Some trees grow here, competing for domination with black, spindly thorn bushes and all kinds of weeds. Dead vegetation has gathered at the lowest depressions in the passes, creating shallow swamp-like pools overgrown with fungi.
112106: As the vegetation and trees begin to recede, the terrain rises above the surrounding landscape. Spiny thorn bushes grow among rocks and stones, thriving even in the shade of large, moss-covered boulders. Black patch of bramble grows along the floor of this ridge, thorns pointing outward in defence.
112107: A dense forest covers these parts of the Emyn-nu-Fuin. The terrain is broken with plenty of ravines and jagged, moss-covered boulders. A short but almost vertical slope to the south leads down into an even denser forest below, while in other directions, deeper into the mountains, the vegetation thins out.
112108: A crude, charred altar with a thick altarstone stands here.

A dozen large rocks lie in a rough circle around an old campfire. Dark stains mar the surface of some rocks, and old bones are strewn around these. Old, rotten pieces of rope hang from the branches of some of the nearest trees. A layer of decaying leaves hide the ground and a brown-green species of fungi grows in abundance here.
112109: A twisted sprawl of thorny shrubs clings to a narrow, rugged ridge. Several massive grey boulders rise above the thick black mat to loom over the rocky terrain. The slopes to either side fall away rapidly, descending into the deep gloom which inhabits the flanking valleys.
112110: A huge boulder rests here on top of the ridge.

Ancient oaks grow on the slopes and across the top of this ridge. Their wide crowns seem to reach for each other, as if trying to create a canopy over the ridge. A wide array of vegetation including berry bushes and thorny brambles thrives in the gaps between trees, where sun and rain can reach the forest floor unhindered.
112111: The forest floor is covered with rocky outcroppings and leaves fallen from the tremendous black oaks of this mountainous region of Mirkwood. Thick, thorny vines climb trunks, circling round and round as if trying to choke the trees. Branch, leaf, and vine conspire to create a canopy, yet it is not dense enough to hide the sky from view.
112112: Deep ruts have been formed in varying patterns on the ground here as a product of erosion and water flowing down from higher ground. Between these cracks, plant life has taken advantage of the cool shade and grows in abundance. One species of thorn bushes seems to thrive unlike any other plant. Their long, spiny branches scrape and scratch anything that comes too close to their domain.
112113: A thick forest of oak and beech covers large, sprawling hills that extend towards the east. The ground is overgrown with large bushes that surround and embrace the old, gnarly trunks. The bushes grow so dense and tall that little of the terrain can be seen in other directions.
112114: The canting nature of the terrain might be what causes the trees to grow twisted and bent in odd angles. Vines twist around the trees, covering their bark like thorny, tangled snakes. A foul and stinking black moss grows across the rocks and boulders. The slope climbs into a mountain pass to the west, while descending into a hilly area to the east.
112115: The narrow, twisting mountain path follows the shape of the mountains. The steep, rugged walls of natural rock severely limit the options of directions to travel to. Black moss clings to the mountain face, coating sections in its darkness. Some vegetation grows even in this desolate area, chiefly tough weeds and the occasional thorny bush.
112116: A narrow mountain pass forges a path through these forerunners of the Emyn-nu-Fuin. A few thin oaks grow amidst the rubble and bushes that line the pass on either side. The oaks are feeble specimens of their kind, with spindly branches and narrow trunks. Sometimes howling winds chase through the pass, bouncing between steep walls as they fills the air with dust.
112117: A large moss-covered boulder stands squat in the middle of the mountain pass, with overgrown bushes on one side and a twisted oak tree on the other one. The gnarled branches of the tree, draped in clinging black vines, scrape against the boulder. The surrounding terrain is arid and sparsely vegetated, though tough weeds seem to find the area agreeable.
112118: Large, black bushes cover this mountain pass. Their thorny branches are clad in small and round green leaves. A few tall alders stand on the steep slopes, and fungi thrive in their shadows rather than the thorn bushes growing everywhere else. While the slopes to either side are very steep, rocky and treacherous, the floor of the pass is flat and not difficult to travel upon.
112119: To the south the terrain rises towards a narrow mountain pass that runs between steep cliff walls. Large boulders and small rocks form a rough and rocky floor covered with dark roots and thorny brambles. The occasional black oak grows on the sheer mountain face, limbs slowly swaying in a foul breeze.
112120: Short and gnarled trees grow in dense rows here. In one area the trees have been felled, leaving only their stumps. A crossroad is revealed in this clearing, allowing to travel in three directions. A rocky mountain path leads south, hugging a steep escarpment, while a trampled area in the dense undergrowth to the east and the west looks quite walkable.
112121: Dense and nearly impassable undergrowth covers this ridge. Thorny shrubs and twisting vines make up most of the vegetation, while gnarly, ancient trees with enormous trunks, which carry great and sprawling crowns, rise through the brush. Though the trees do not grow dense, their foliage creates a green roof which blots out the sky.
112122: The terrain becomes very steep towards the north where a slope climbs towards higher ground; to the west, another short but steep slope beckons. Great sprawls of thorny bushes cover the gentler parts of the slope, and in-between pebbles and small rocks make footing unsure. A few trees dot the area, sparse enough not to be called a proper forest.
112124: This overgrown ridge is littered with broken rocks and moss-covered boulders. A few oak trees grow oddly twisted, standing in odd angles, with dark, strangely contorted branches moving lazily as if in a constant breeze. Thick, green grass covers the forest floor, growing everywhere except where rocks and boulders block it.
112126: A deft, young orc monitors the area, ready to attack any enemy.

A wide, rugged ridge stretches from the east to the west, while a gentle slope descends to the south. The terrain makes for very difficult travel, with crags and cliffs everywhere. Gnarled, twisted trees rise from in-between rocks and boulders. Although stunted and bent, they hold up massive, sprawling crowns that form a dense canopy overhead. On the ground, little but moss and ferns seem to find the dark, stony environment agreeable.
112127: A thin, hairy plant, with small, oval leaves, grows here.

Moss-covered crags and gnarled, ancient trees dominate this region of the Emyn-nu-Fuin. Layers of dead leaves cover a forest floor shrouded in gloom by dense foliage above. Half-buried rocks and thick, knotted roots hide under the leaves. Dense, thorny patches of briar grow in clusters wherever there is a gap in the canopy.
112128: Jagged boulders and deep, narrow gorges await the unwary traveller in the shadows under the trees in this part of the Emyn-nu-Fuin. Grey lichen drapes branches that droop as if the flimsy fungi were of great weight. The forest floor dips sharply to the west, the rocky terrain disappearing from view beneath dark canopies.
112129:
Some small rocks have been piled into a mound here.
A large mother hawk is here looking for a prey to feed her young.
A mountain goat is here, jumping from cliff to cliff.

The steep rocky terrain rises a hundred feet above the forest. These low, rugged mountains host a plethora of plant life, ranging from moss and small shrubs to tall, ancient trees. Steep cliffs rise to the west, separating this part of the Emyn-nu-Fuin from whatever lies on the other side.
112130: The terrain ascends from all directions to reach this flat plateau. The ground is stony with little topsoil and what vegetation grows here is made up of small shrubs and plants. Several large boulders dot the plateau, moss-covered looming giants that stand guard over their domain.
112131: Sharp and jagged rocks covered in slimy green moss protrude from a broad ridge that runs from the east to the west. Twisted trees flank the apex of the ridge, casting shadows on it with their overhanging branches. Dark brown vines hang from the trees, and roots push their way up through the crumbled rocks atop the ridge.
112132: Tall Hills in a Tangled Forest
A black raven flies in the sky searching for flesh to prey upon.

Dark vine-entangled trees sweep broadly across tall hilly terrain in complete darkness under the impregnable canopy looming above. Cracked stones are strewn throughout the soil amidst massive trunks that dwarf the meagre shrubbery eeking out a living between their great twisting roots.
112133: The dark trees twist and stretch into a warped tangle of gnarled boughs and mossy limbs. No natural light pierces the gloom of the treetops, as evidenced by a complete lack of vegetation beneath the canopy. Ominous roots weave their way through the thin soil, becoming a tangled net of hardened wood and scaly bark.
112134: The forest floor descends steeply here, exposing large roots in the earthen walls of a gully. Through dense foliage and weaving vines, the deep crack transforms into a larger rift below the base of the forest. A small dark rivulet steadily runs from above, forming a culvert along the centre of the path.
112135: A mountain goat is here, jumping from cliff to cliff.

The terrain along the apex of this ridge is bare, jagged stone. There is little growing here, only some grey, sickly lichen, struggling patches of moss, and tough weeds. The ridge continues to the east and to the west, while the sides to the north and to the south drop away in steep cliffs to disappear in the canopy of Mirkwood below.
112136: A small and tough weed grows here.

Jagged rocks line the sides of this twisting ridge. A few short, stunted trees grow in the stony soil with spiny bushes around them, as if seeking for protection. The sides of the ridge fall away steeply in cliffs and rubble-strewn slopes. Passage seems impossible in any direction except following the ridge towards the east.
112138: Elderberry bushes and willows grow amongst the hummocks that rise above the moist muck in this area. Ancient, gnarled alders stand defiant amongst the sedges, branches drooping low. The smell of decomposition rises up from the bog, adding to the stifling atmosphere of these marshlands. Ribbitting and chirping can be heard from various places amongst the vegetation.
112139:
A swift carnivore bustles around.
A black moth flutters around.

Noxious fumes rise from the wet forest floor, gasses emanating from the decomposing vegetation that fills the shallow, black soil. Tall reeds surround thorny shrubs growing among the black trees. A thin, dark mist hovers over the ground, a foreboding sign that continues throughout the area.
112141: Dense groves of sprawling trees populate this soggy valley. Some trees lie upended and rotting in the muddy terrain. Poison ivy grows along the bark of the trees, covering some of them from root to crown. The ground slopes down to a dirty rivulet in the centre of this valley, fed by the rainfall draining down the surrounding mountainsides.
112144: Short and spiny thorn bushes cover these low hills, growing thick and wild. A few elm trees stand defiant along the ridges, their arms swaying slowly seemingly independent of the wind; faint, rustling sounds are ever present. The dense vegetation is covered with a parasitic black moss that emanates a foul odour that carries through the whole area.
112145: Thorny barberry bushes grow thick on the rubble-like hillsides. There is a faint trail worn into the crab grass between the bushes. The trees that grow on the floor between hills seem to be mostly gnarled ancients. Sometimes a faint howling rides on the wind from the north, though if it is caused by air being forced through narrow gaps and openings or something else is indeterminable.
112146: This cavern begins at a round hole at the top of a slope to the south. From there, the cavern quickly expands, widening to dozens of yards between the eastern and the western walls. The cave is ovoid with considerably smooth, rock walls of mostly a dim grey colour, interspersed with ash grey. In a few separate locations, thin, dark roots protrude from the ceiling, clear evidence that trees or bushes with deep roots grow above this cave.

Dark brown streaks resembling a deep brown mud seemingly connect each edge to each other. Some of the more jagged edges have broken off, creating a haphazard line of pebble-sized rocks.

The crack twists and turns in a semi-straight line from top to bottom, as if splitting the cave in half, effectively becoming a focal point of the large cave. A few small strands of discarded light brown moss lie scattered on the worn cavern floor.
112150: Pitch-black water with a strange smell has collected here.

Featuring mostly even rock walls, very small rounded, irregular cones form a distinguishing layer to both the top and the bottom of the cave. The glacous stalactites grow longer and denser, their pointed edges reaching over two feet long towards the middle of the cave. Its companions that litter the cave floor are much more subdued, stalagmites adding an uneven surface in sharp contrast to the grey walls. A thin layer of dirty water forms tiny puddles of black water on the cavern's floor.
112151: A spacious den has been excavated beneath a hill. The walls look stable and solid, and are covered with scratch marks. Piles of leaves mixed with animal hair lie at the back of the den. Some dry, gnawed-on bones litter the floor. There is no meat on them and they do not seem part of a recent meal.
112152: Claw marks cover the walls of this den. Thin roots poke through the roof of the den, indicating that there is only a few feet of soil between the top of the cave and a forest floor. A pile of leaves and twigs lies at the back of the den, mixed with a lot of animal hair.

The cavern's moist air, and widely spread moss covering the stones make the ground feel very slippery. An occasional tiny breeze of fresh air seems to flush in from the north.

There are bends and twists, blind corners and shallow alcoves.

The floor is strew with boulders discoloured in shades of yellow, brown, and green by cave-living lichens.

A trampled animal trail can be espied worn into the crab grass in-between bushes where a series of switchbacks allows passage into the rougher terrain.

Several severed appendages, looking suspiciously like those of the great spiders of Mirkwood, stick up from the cauldron and hang over its edge.
112239:
A sturdy target for arrows, made out of thatch, stands here.
A deft, young orc monitors the area, ready to attack any enemy.
A young orc grips his weapon impatiently, eager to prove himself.

At the centre of the outpost, there is an open area with no huts or other buildings. Several wide trees have been left standing here providing some shade while their lower branches and surrounding undergrowth has been cleared away. A variety of objects, such as broken shields of wood, rotting carcasses of spiders, and other junk have been nailed to the trunks. Most objects have been thoroughly demolished by arrows and slingstones, and it is obvious that this area is used for practicing ranged weaponry.
112240:
A rope ladder hangs down from the trees above.
A Durbuk-hai warrior stands here with a frenzied gleam in his eyes.
A Durbuk-hai warrior stands here with a frenzied gleam in his eyes.
A young orc grips his weapon impatiently, eager to prove himself.

In the midst of the trees, this miserable orkish outpost offers protection from malicious creatures of the forest outside thanks to the high wooden palisade. Some of the trees behind the palisade have been hacked down, but not so much as to let the sun shine through. A rope ladder is hanging from a wooden platform visible up in a pine tree, which is overgrown by black vines.
112241:
A small round stone lies in the dust.
A small campfire burns here, its low flames giving off only a little light.
Bulg, wielding a great warsword, is standing here.
Drazud, wielding a two-handed sword, is standing here.
Ducaht (tooprettytodie), wielding a great warsword, is standing here.
Klaees (donny), wielding an engraved broadsword, is standing here.

Several shoddy huts have been constructed here, with roofs of branches and vines, and walls made of mud and wood. A small pit for a camp fire is located between the huts, with a few roughly-made chairs standing around the fire pit. To the west, there is a strong wooden palisade protecting the outpost. The apparently indifferent inhabitants of the huts have discarded trash and food leftovers on the ground.
112242:
A mass of tattered fabric lies here in a heap.
A mass of tattered fabric lies here in a heap.
A mass of tattered fabric lies here in a heap.
A young, eager Durbuk-hai warrior, wielding a wooden club, is sleeping here.
A young, eager Durbuk-hai warrior, wielding a wooden club, is sleeping here.
A young, eager Durbuk-hai warrior, wielding a wooden club, is sleeping here.
A young, eager Durbuk-hai warrior, wielding a handaxe, is sleeping here.

Several filthy mats and blankets lie scattered on the floor of this miserable hut. There are no windows in the walls and only one door leading out. The roof is made of branches and vines, held up by a few rough but sturdy beams. It is sealed with mud in an attempt to make it weatherproof. The walls are built in a similar manner.
112243:
A sturdy crate made of nailed wooden planks sits on the floor.
A fine pelt lies here, soft and smooth.
A brown bear fur is here lying on the ground.
A veteran of the Durbuk-hai watches the area, alert and poised for combat.
A veteran of the Durbuk-hai watches the area, alert and poised for combat.
A veteran of the Durbuk-hai watches the area, alert and poised for combat.
A bulky orc commander stands here with a sinister look on his face.

The crude worksmanship of this hut leaves little doubt that it is a work of orcs. Even so, more effort has gone into it than would be typical; it is likely the quarters of an important orc. The hut stands on a foundation of stone slabs that, even though they are uneven, is further evidence of the effort gone into its construction. Several furs, skulls, and other trophies hang on the walls, and a thick mat of pelts in the centre of the room might serve as a bed, if somewhat oddly placed.
112244:
A pig is here, covered in mud.
A pig is here, covered in mud.

This end of the outpost has an opening in the palisade, but it is blocked by a huge pile of garbage. The pile is obviously working as the final location for trash, filth, bones, and food leftovers of the inhabitants of the outpost. Very strong, foul odours waft from the huge garbage pile. A palisade is blocking the way to the west and east.
112245: The shrouded, dark forest is veiled in shadows and gloom. Long, thin branches droop from the trees, as if grasping at the forest floor. Moving through the forest is not easy, as the trees grow close to each other, and their branches intertwine. The soil is dark and covered by decaying leaves and needles.
112246: A brown snail is crawling across the ground here leaving a slimy trail behind.

The trees of the forest form a natural passage here, offering an easy way to travel to the east and south. The forest in the other directions consist of impenetrable thickets and tangles. The trees have formed a low arch with their branches, under which a man atop a horse would be a narrow fit. A lot of beard moss and grey-white lichen hang from the trees.
112247:
A Durbuk-hai warrior is here, ill-equipped but ready to fight for his tribe.
A Durbuk-hai warrior is here, ill-equipped but ready to fight for his tribe.
A Durbuk-hai warrior is here, ill-equipped but ready to fight for his tribe.

The dense forest blocks passage in all directions except to the south. Thorny thickets grow amongst towering, gnarled trunks, further hindering travel. A carpet of decaying brown leaves covers the ground. The sky is almost completely hidden by the canopy, naught but a gap here and there reveals the world beyond.
112248: The pine trees in this part of the forest are almost black in colour. The ground is covered by a thick mat of decaying needles. Fungi thrive on the forest floor, sprouting among the needles in dense clumps. The branches and the trunks of the trees are covered by beard moss swaying slowly in the wind. A maze of the branches seem to continue endlessly upwards.
112249: A Durbuk-hai warrior is here, ill-equipped but ready to fight for his tribe.

A very small clearing exists here in a tree thicket. The surrounding trees are a mixture of oak and elm. Acorns and leaves cover the ground and rustle with any movement across them. Moss and lichen have slowly started growing up the trees here, but they are a darker shade of colour than they would typically be. The forest is very thick, but small breaks in the umbrage can be seen to the north.
112250: The gnarled but powerful trees in this section of the forest have begun to wither and die. Light can only reach the ground in thin, weak patches through the leafless, yet dense, canopy of thick branches above. Broken and decaying branches lie scattered on the forest floor, slowly rotting away. There is neither sign nor sound of animals here, as if the wildlife knows better than to pass through this region of Mirkwood.
112251: Wandering in the Forest of Mirkwood

Some of the trees here show signs that they have not been growing for as long as the surrounding forest. A huge variety of trees grow here; from birches, to beeches, to oaks, and even some evergreens. A larger break in the canopy in the south can be seen. Apparently, the forest was partially cleared in the past, but it has since started to regrow.
112252: A large pine tree with dark-brown bark and emerald-green needles is here, towering above the surrounding forest. The vast expanse of its massive branches has cast a wide pool of shade upon the ground beneath it, where nothing save a few short, stunted shrubs have dared to grow. A thick blanket of moss encircles the ground around the base of tree, where it continues to grow several feet up the massive trunk.
112254: The woods here are made up of various types of trees, beneath which is a dense layer of undergrowth. Thick, heavy tree foliage can be seen above and allows no light to break through it. This makes the already dark forest appear even darker than the surrounding forest. It is difficult to navigate through this stretch of forest and one could easily end up getting lost while attempting to do so.
112256:
A Durbuk-hai warrior stands here with a frenzied gleam in his eyes.
A Durbuk-hai warrior stands here with a frenzied gleam in his eyes.
A deft Durbuk-hai slinger lurks in the shadows.
A deft Durbuk-hai slinger lurks in the shadows.
An elite Durbuk-hai guard is standing here, armed with spear and shield.

Around the outpost, there is a wooden palisade built from pikes and sharpened stakes. On a few locations along the palisade there are small platforms made of wood and stone, providing ideal positions for archers. The palisade is uninterrupted to the south, but to the east there is a huge wooden gate reinforced with bands of metal.
112257:
An elite Durbuk-hai guard is standing here, armed with spear and shield.
A deft Durbuk-hai slinger lurks in the shadows.

A well-hidden wooden platform has been built amidst the forest canopy; it probably serves as a lookout for watching the road that runs through the forest to the south. There is a rack for arrows and other weapons on the centre of the platform, and judging from the crude craftsmanship, it is of orkish origin. Rough as the whole place may seem, it fills its purpose perfectly. A rope ladder hangs from the hatch in the floor.
112269: Some black, oozing vines reach out from the choked canopy towards you.

Inside this small and sodden cavern, there are a lot of roots growing through the walls. The exception is the wall to the east, which looks like it might be about to collapse. Water rushes in through a small opening among the roots above and splashes onto the sludgy ground.
112270: Water wells out from a small hole in a wall made by the mountains to the north and gathers here in a small pool. The air here seems slightly less stifling than in the surrounding forest. A steep mountain slope rises up to the west, with the forest closing in from the south and east, with the latter direction being impassable due to a recent landslide. Closer to the mountains, the forest and vegetation begins to thin out and makes it slightly easier to navigate through.
112271: Large quantities of bushes grow here, all closely packed together. The majority of the bushes seem to be of a thornless variety, for not a single thorn is visible throughout the whole grove. Black, half-rotten fungi are growing amongst the bushes.
112272: In this part of the forest, the trees seem to move when unwatched. Mammoth roots break the surface of the earth and seem to search for something to ensnare along with branches that bend down menacingly. As faint traces of wind rustle through the branches, the trees seem to be murmuring between them.
112273: A prominent mountain on the northern flank of the sloping ground is vaguely visible behind the thickets of the forest. Rocky patches between the giant trees have been smoothed through centuries of exposure to wind and rain. Not a single sapling or bush grows on the rocks, only some grey lichen and dark moss.
112274:
The corpse of a youthful wisent is lying here.
The corpse of a powerful wisent is lying here.

Great boughs spread out overhead, entwining themselves together. So thickly have they been tangled that no light can pierce the canopy they form. From out of this darkness, faint rustling noises can be heard. Where these noises are coming from, whether the faint movement of the wind or from twisted creatures who live in this forest, can not easily be determined.
112275: A large pile of boulders is sitting here, probably debris from a rockslide.

The forest ends abruptly to the east and gives a view of the huge, dark mountains of Mirkwood. Many sharp rocks have fallen from the cliff to the east and have found their way down to the forest floor. Layers of scree have built up over many years causing the mossy ground to crunch underfoot. The oppressive forest to the west of here is very dense, and it is not possible to wind one's way through the forest in that direction.
112276: Some small rocks have been piled into a mound here.

The dark mountains of Mirkwood loom ominously beyond the rising, tangled forest to the east, where a slope ascends very steeply. A lot of loose debris and scree have accumulated on the slope, making a climb impossible. Rocks, boulders, and stones of different sizes litter the forest floor and hamper travel.
112277: This small, flat summit is located atop the dark mountains of Mirkwood. Steep cliffs on the western and southern sides drop off to the forest floor below. This whole area is devoid of any plant life, with even the hardier varieties having failed to find a place to grow amongst the cold, dark rock.
112278: Small, dark and twisted trees struggle to grow on this inhospitable mountainside. The strong winds that sweep across these peaks have twisted the trees into grotesque shapes resembling that of malformed humanoids. The trees shift and groan, and some almost seem to be stalking through the dark, dense forest. Rocks and boulders create more shadowy places in the forest. One of the boulders is huge and completely covered by moss and lichen.
112279: This cavern inside the mountains serves as the lair of something large and carnivorous judging by chewed and cracked bones on the ground. The cavern is high and wide enough to let even the largest animal enter; which species has made this place home is less certain. The walls are moist and the air humid, and some species of moss and fungi thrive on them despite the darkness.
112280: The many large and sharp rocks jutting out from the steep mountainside dominate the land here. Between the larger boulders, layers of scree have accumulated into mounds of loose stony debris. Almost any movement causes debris to become dislodged and tumble down the steep, rugged slope to the west. While to the north the cliff is so steep that it prevents any travelling, the terrain looks more easy to the east.
112281: There are signs of habitation here with bones and broken weapons accumulated throughout the area on the ground. The remains of campfires can also be seen in various locations but appear to be somewhat centred around one rocky area. The central area has been fortified, but the years of disuse are starting to show on the condition of the wooden walls and spikes. A huge cliff dominates the skyline to the north and casts a shadow over this whole area.
112282: Steep Slope in the Dark Mountains

The ground slopes sharply up to a dark pinnacle in the mountains. Movement here will require travellers to scramble around on the loose rocks that carpet the area, consuming a great deal of energy in the process. A few hardy fir trees have managed to take root in the hard ground in small thickets as if huddled together for protection. The slope to the south ends abruptly in a near-vertical cliff.
112284: A rotten corpse is hanging here.

A deep bowl-shaped pit occupies much of the floor space in this large cavern. Stained and slippery with dark substances, the pit emits the odour of decay and death. Broken bones, ragged clothing, and shattered armour line the centre of the pit. Dark passages lead in all directions where guttural growls and heavy shuffling sounds seem to be getting closer.
112288:
A mountain mule (ulo) is standing here.
A powerful young troll stares at you.
A powerful young troll stares at you.

The air is thick with the heavy musk of trolls. The rock underfoot has been scraped smooth by the frequent shuffling of immense beings. The walls bear jagged claw-marks while even the tall ceiling shows signs of having been gashed. A darkly-stained path leads to the west.
112289: A powerful young troll stares at you.

Dark and musty, this cave is little more than a turn in a larger passageway. Littered with rock shards and decaying matter, the floor is somewhat tricky to navigate in a rush. Ancient cobwebs shroud the high ceiling corners in dark shadows. The clearest path through here bends to the west and to the south.
112290: The air is thick with the heavy musk of trolls. The rock underfoot has been scraped smooth by the frequent shuffling of immense beings. The walls bear jagged claw-marks while even the tall ceiling shows signs of having been gashed. A darkly-stained path leads to the south.
112291: Dark and musty, this cave is little more than a turn in a larger passageway. Littered with rock shards and decaying matter, the floor is somewhat tricky to navigate in a rush. Ancient cobwebs shroud the high ceiling corners in dark shadows. The clearest path through here bends to the south and to the east.
112292: The air is thick with the heavy musk of trolls. The rock underfoot has been scraped smooth by the frequent shuffling of immense beings. The walls bear jagged claw-marks while even the tall ceiling shows signs of having been gashed. A darkly-stained path leads to the east.
112293:
A powerful young troll stares at you.

Dark and musty, this cave is little more than a turn in a larger passageway. Littered with rock shards and decaying matter, the floor is somewhat tricky to navigate in a rush. Ancient cobwebs shroud the high ceiling corners in dark shadows. The clearest path through here bends to the north and to the east.
112294: A powerful young troll stares at you.

The air is thick with the heavy musk of trolls. The rock underfoot has been scraped smooth by the frequent shuffling of immense beings. The walls bear jagged claw-marks while even the tall ceiling shows signs of having been gashed. A darkly-stained path leads to the north.
112295: The scent of trolls is thick in the air here and this cavern shows signs of frequent passage by immense creatures. Clawed, ripped, and torn, the hard rock surfaces of the walls, floors, and ceiling reveal abuse by furious powers. An almost tube-like opening heads east while to the north and west, an ominous darkness hangs over jagged passageways.
112296:
A large troll stands half-hidden in the shadows.
A large troll stands half-hidden in the shadows.

This east-west passageway is a hastily dug tunnel that appears to receive frequent use, judging by the claw marks in the floor. Roughly carved in a tube, this hollow shaft connects the dank, foetid caves in the west with the black caverns to the east.
112297: The cavern widens out tremendously here in all directions. Far off to the east, west, and north are dark openings that look like passageways. The ground is cracked and jagged as old debris, rock shards, and bits of bone festoon the area. A trail of this garbage seems to lead to the eastward opening.
112298:
A large cave troll is here, staying close to his mother.
A large cave troll is here, staying close to his mother.
A large cave troll is here, staying close to his mother.
The ugly troll mother is roaming the cave, taking care of her loved ones.
A young cavetroll looks at you hungrily.

This area is nothing more than a big hole dug in the hard rock and then filled with layer upon layer of discarded bones, clothing, broken weapons and armour, and any other junk that trolls find no use for. Over time, the layers have become several tens of feet deep and consequently exude the very essence of the aroma of rot and decay.
112299: A subtle but deep red glow suffuses this cavernous space. The air is warmer here as heat rises from deep fissures near the far walls. Shadows cast by crystalline stalagmites play tricks on the eyes as the faint sound of hissing and bubbling can be heard deep below. Overhead, intricate stalactite formations catch and reflect the illumination causing the entire chamber to wash in hues of rubies and fire.
112300: The ceiling soars tremendously high in the cavern, opening up the space like a dark cathedral. Exits lead in all directions and it is clear from the trampled floor that this crossing receives a lot of traffic. In addition to the massive footprints, it is also evident that something or someone has been dragged across the floor, leaving a bloody trail that heads east.
112301: Fairly regular in appearance, this connecting tunnel has been dug to allow swift passage for large beings, if the height of the ceilings are any clue. Old bloodstains mar the walls while high up, ancient cobwebs drape down in dusty, furry loops. The dusty floor has been disturbed very recently in this dank and dark tunnel.
112302:
An old, strong cave troll is standing here.
An old, strong cave troll is standing here.

Rough strength appears to have ripped open the rockfaces to the east and west in the semblance of a fork in a path. To the west, silence and darkness pervade a moist passageway while to the east, the cave seems drier but no less dark. To the south, a long dark tunnel extends into the darkness.
112303:
A large cave troll is here, staying close to his mother.
A large cave troll is here, staying close to his mother.
A large cave troll is here, staying close to his mother.
The ugly troll mother is roaming the cave, taking care of her loved ones.

This small cave feels tight and compressed since the ceiling dips low while the floor rises slightly. The granite walls bulge inward somewhat as the path leading in dwindles and dies on the western side of the chamber. The air feels heavy and warm with the musk of trolls and cave beasts.
112304: This dark offshoot of a subtly glowing cavern in the east has been carved in what looks like the design of a nest or a small den. Rank droppings and bits of slimy flesh mixed with bone layer the floor. The walls are rough, uneven, and might, from the look of them, have been excavated with claws rather than tools.
112306: Part of the cavern's floor is covered by a large smear of dried blood.

The passages from the west and north tighten as the path takes a sharp turn. The hard-edged rock walls do not look friendly and the ceiling seems to be pointing needle-like fingers as dark stalactites festoon its surface. The rank air feels compressed and crowded here.
112307: This stony path is little more than a tight squeeze between rock walls as it twists from south to east. A faint rushing or hissing sound can be heard farther east as the air begins to cool slightly. The dirty floor looks like it's hardly been used though it looks ancient. Cobwebs drape the corners in shrouds of pale lace, gently pulsing in a faint breeze.
112308: This tunnel twists from west to south and a slow draft moves the air. A faint hissing sound comes from somewhere to the south. The rock surfaces are slightly damp and their rough edges glisten. The hardpacked floor is too damp to be dusty; however, signs of use are still evident as the way slopes downward from north to south.
112309: An ancient fungus smothers the boulders.

The passage from the north opens into a large cave with a high ceiling covered in glistening stalactites. Each one is intermittently dripping moisture as a wave of cool, moist air continuously flows in from the south. From that direction comes the sound of rushing water. The rock floor is wet and slippery as it dips down to the south.
112310: A young cavetroll looks at you hungrily.

A cavern here has been cut naturally over the centuries by an underground spring that enters high in the southern wall and falls down into a deep pool of black water. A rocky ledge meanders along the western side of the pool and appears to go through and beyond the waterfall's shimmering curtain.
112311: A skeleton of some humanoid lies in the dust.

A ledge from the north descends into the dark pool created by constantly flowing water. The water flows in from the north and through the ages it has carved a passage deep beneath Mirkwood. The water finds an outlet somewhere beneath the black surface, for the constant inflow does not raise the surface.
112312:
An old, strong cave troll is standing here.
An old, strong cave troll is standing here.

The rough, shard-littered floor of the rest of this dark cavern gives way to a pitch-black beach at the edge of an even blacker lake. Smooth and slick, the shore slopes down to the water's edge where silent ripples gently lap against the dark stone. The far side of the lake is impossible to gauge in any kind of light but the water's movement suggests it is not devoid of some sort of life.
112313: A long slender eel glides along the water, its body coiled to strike.

A lake of black water fills the lower half of a vast cavern. The lake is deep enough that the bottom is out of reach except within a few feet of the steeply sloped beach. Warm currents seem to swish around in eddies giving rise to the possibility that there is more than just darkness in these waters.
112314:
An old, strong cave troll is standing here.
An old, strong cave troll is standing here.
An old, strong cave troll is standing here.

Dim light reaches this cavern from the west, though not enough to clearly illuminate it or dispel the shadows that lurk in the corners. Even when the simple door is closed, the faint glow is visible through the cracks around it. Like an afterthought, this roughly-hewn space is a possible nesting site or resting place with no room for large groups. On the eastern side of the room, a giant crack in the floor is covered in moisture from some source deep below.
112316: This cave passage slopes upward to the east while to the west it descends into gloom and darkness. The walls have been roughly hewn out of the black granite and the floor is dusty from frequent use. The rank odour of trolls and rotten meat fills the air.
112317: In this webbed, winding tunnel, there is just enough room to manoeuvre around a massive, web-covered tree trunk that stands just off-centre in this cramped space. The flooring here has been put together from branches and vines that are held together with the help of strong, sticky cobwebs. A sticky web has been woven across the tunnel to the east.
112318: Pocket of Air within the Webs

A forest spider is here crawling around.
A forest spider is here crawling around.

About four feet separates the web-infested walls of this gently swaying abode. One can discern that one of the walls is also the thick tree trunk that keeps this passage in place. West of here, a small hourglass-shaped platform opens up. It is also possible to move up or down along the tree-trunk, utilising a few rough steps that have been cut into it.
112319:
A greenish slime mould is here, smelling badly.
A huge, poisonous tarantula extends her legs to you.

The blackness of the cobweb-covered walls in here are in stark contrast to the large, corpse-white cocoons that have been stuck to the walls and ceilings. The only exit out of here is to the east, into what appears to be a far darker and even more cramped area. A strong stench of slime, stale air, and rot pervades the air.
112320:
A huge, poisonous spider is here.
A huge, poisonous spider is here.

Strange, thick, almost transparent cobwebs cover everything in here, and it would be hard to know that this place is far high up in a tree top if it were not for the gentle, almost lulling rocking of the gigantic canopy. South of here, some sort of dark and foreboding lair can be seen, while a series of bundled logs and boughs lead north. There is also the possibility of lowering oneself into a dark hole that sits in the middle of this area.
112321: A pile of dry, brown leaves lies here.

Twigs and branches have interwoven with each other, creating a natural nest of sorts. The leaf-work is fairly intact, and by the look of the leaves one can conclude that this gigantic tree is indeed an ancient oak. The footing is solid and surprisingly even, perhaps too much so for being a creation of nature. To the south, shiny silky cobwebs hang around a tunnel-like opening leading away from this place.
112322: This place is an almost cave-like structure, made entirely from countless layers of spider web. The temperature and humidity in here are higher than the surrounding areas, and the air carries a foul, bitter smell. Along the walls, open cocoons of varying sizes - up to four feet in diameter - have been meshed to boughs and branches that stick out from the webs.
112324:
A water moccasin slithers out of sight just below the surface of the water.
A water moccasin slithers out of sight just below the surface of the water.
A water moccasin slithers out of sight just below the surface of the water.
A grey snake slides along the water.

The filthy, brown pool is full of dead, rotting plants floating weightlessly, suspended in the still water. Vague, slithering silhouettes can be seen in the murky darkness, yet whether they are dead, floating vines and branches, or something more sinister, is hard to discern.
112325: The water is murky and full of floating parts of branches, dead plants and leaves. The bottom of this pond is muddy and engulfing, and one has to be careful to not get stuck there. Among the slimy algae, slithering shapes seem to move in the darkness, although it might be dead vines floating in the brown water.
112326: Guard Post in a Sombre Passageway

A water barrel has been left here.
A young orc grips his weapon impatiently, eager to prove himself.
A young, eager Durbuk-hai warrior, wielding a wooden club, is here, fighting Lhurank (brenny).
A young orc grips his weapon impatiently, eager to prove himself.
A deft Durbuk-hai slinger lurks in the shadows.
A deft Durbuk-hai slinger lurks in the shadows.
Lhurank (brenny), wielding a darkened orkish axe, is here, fighting a young, eager Durbuk-hai warrior.

A squat, square chamber sits at the intersection of two passageways. The larger runs east-to-west and is carved straight and smooth. The other passage runs north-to-south, and is crudely delved with uneven walls as well as a rough floor. This chamber appears to be used as a guard post; wooden fortifications line the west end of the cavern.
112327: Sombre Passageway before a Broken Portcullis

A great portcullis made from dark wood is here, damaged heavily by a recent cave-in.
An elite Durbuk-hai guard is standing here, armed with spear and shield.
A veteran of the Durbuk-hai watches the area, alert and poised for combat.

A wide passageway cutting through grey-black shale meets a massive wooden portcullis guarding the way east. Natural rock formations line the walls and ceiling, but the floor has been worn smooth. The passage is increasingly covered in dust and small stones as it approaches the portcullis; beyond it to the east, visible through the thick hardwood lattice, lie large mounds of debris.
112328:
A sturdy crate made of nailed wooden planks sits on the floor.
A sturdy peg for hanging armour from is on the wall.
On the peg, there are a sling, a pair of rigid leather sleeves, a pair of hard leather trousers and a rigid leather breastplate.
A sturdy crate made of nailed wooden planks sits on the floor.
A weapons rack stands against the wall.
In the rack are three short spears and two longspears.
A young orc grips his weapon impatiently, eager to prove himself.
A young orc grips his weapon impatiently, eager to prove himself.
A young orc grips his weapon impatiently, eager to prove himself.
A Durbuk-hai warrior stands here with a frenzied gleam in his eyes.

A spacious chamber far underground appears to serve as a well-stocked armoury for the orkish forces that dwell here. A collection of brutal weapons hang on pegs along the walls and stand in wooden racks that rest along the floor in a ring surrounding the centre of the cavern. Crudely fashioned leather armour hangs from pegs and is visible within various crates that appear to have recently been smashed open and then hastily nailed back together by eager occupants.
112329:
A fine pelt lies here, soft and smooth.
A greyish-black pelt lies here.
A splintered piece of a broken shield is on the ground.
A sturdy crate made of nailed wooden planks sits on the floor.
An empty pair of rusty shackles are here, fastened to the wall.
A small barrel made of aged oak and strong iron hoops stands here.
A ragged leather breastplate is on the ground.
A brown fur is here lying on the ground.
A simple wooden chest is here.

An underground chamber that was rudely cut from solid rock shows few signs that attention was paid to aesthetics. The walls and floor are rough and uneven, and a large pile of fine furs and pelts lies strewn across the western half of the chamber. Dilapidated leather armour, broken wooden shields, and shoddy stone weapons litter the rest of the floor. A barren patch of red-stained stone sits beneath a pair of empty shackles mounted to the eastern wall.
112330:
A great portcullis made from dark wood is here, damaged heavily by a recent cave-in.
A scrawny Durbuk-hai orc is here, clearing away rubble from a cave-in.

There is a constant creaking, rustling sound of branches and bushes shifting and settling in new positions.

A ring is fastened to the cave wall with thick but rusted iron spikes, and a chain is attached to the ring. There are some scribblings and scratches on the rocky walls, but they are too vague to be read. On the floor, there are many old brownish stains.

A strong odour of death and decay fills the air, and at times one of the corpses is jerked about as if something in the pool was tugging at them.

Thick vines are wrapped about trunks and branches, giving an impression of ropes that shackle the trees to keep them from escaping.

Occasional rustling noises are audible, originating from somewhere deep in the forest. Some of the willow branches, along with the thorns of the briars, have brownish stains upon them which resemble dried blood.

The substantial, sticky mass must have been created over many years as it is as solid and impenetrable as any wall. A few scattered bones of an unidentified animal lie in the undergrowth stripped clean of all meat. To the north and west, massive roots have been severed along the edge of the road that runs near here. To the east, the ground begins to slope downward and south-east, away from the road to the north.

A horse of the Rohirrim (ulo) is standing here.
Tollin the Dwarf (T), wielding a mighty dwarven axe, is standing here giggling.
Sungha the Rohir (F), wielding an engraved broadsword, is standing here.

This hall is fifteen yards wide, twenty yards long, and at least thirty six feet high. In the north-western corner there is a large staircase leading up, and the remnants of a balcony clings to the southern wall. It appears that there used to be a staircase up to this balcony, but it is no longer possible to reach it as the walls are smooth, with no support to enable climbing. The floor is tiled with flat stones and a large picture of a battle between dwarves and orcs is carved into it. There is a small portal in the eastern wall, with a flooded staircase leading down from it. Another portal leads into a corridor in the northern wall.
112621: The corpse of a stone statue is lying here.

This narrow corridor is only about a yard and a half wide and is entirely filled with water. The corridor links two staircases, both of which lead up. The western staircase runs straight, whereas the eastern staircase spirals tightly, a design choice that would enable easy defence. There are rough holes in the walls, which are overgrown with algae. The water flooding the corridor is remarkably clear, but makes the steps and floor slippery and difficult to navigate.
112622: Landing on the Western Wall of a Column Hall

Traces of white tones form the aura of this place.
Sungha the Rohir (F), wielding an ornate, steel-shafted warhammer, is resting here nodding.
Tollin the Dwarf (T), wielding a mighty dwarven axe, is resting here.

A five yard wide landing protrudes from the western wall of a large hall. There is a portal in the wall, and the top of a spiral staircase is visible behind it. The hall extends to the north, east, and south. It might once have been a mighty hall where an entire tribe of dwarves could gather. However, at some point in the past much of the hall was destroyed or rebuilt. In many places, there are great gaps in the floor that reveal a deep chasm beneath this hall. Isolated islands of remaining floor stand on majestic pillars that rise from the gloom below. These islands are connected by narrow footbridges. A fall into the darkness would certainly be lethal. It is difficult to estimate how dangerous these bridges and platforms are, but a skilful person might be able to determine their stability. There are faint runes carved into the floor of the landing.
112623: In a distant past, a set of steep wooden stairs were constructed in this nearly vertical shaft. Since then, parts of it have crumbled and what remains looks wobbly. The staircase has likely not been used for ages, but it was once solid and well crafted. Remains of dwarven runes and ornaments are still visible on the walls. There are empty torch holders every few yards along the walls.
112624: By an Old Dwarven Rune Stone
An ancient dwarven rune stone stands at the top of the staircase.

Major parts of this tunnel are partly collapsed. The remaining walls look very unstable as several of the trunk-like wooden pillars that support it have crumbled and those still standing look very decrepit. The tunnel slowly descends to the south where it turns into a shaft with almost vertical stairs. A thick layer of dust, mixed with dirt and rubble, covers the ground. However, close to the stairs, the tunnel becomes more solid as it was dug through solid rock. Some of the steps, visible from the top of the stairs, do not look very solid and seem risky to use.
112626:
Traces of fierce white tones form the aura of this place.
The corpse of a shadow serpent is lying here.
A monstrous beast wreathed in shadows scans the forest with a baleful glare.
A diamond-back rattlesnake is coiled here, ready to strike.
A tree-snake lies wrapped around one of the tree branches.
A tree-snake lies wrapped around one of the tree branches.
A tree-snake lies wrapped around one of the tree branches.
A tree-snake lies wrapped around one of the tree branches.
A tree-snake lies wrapped around one of the tree branches.
A dark, sinuous form lurks in the shadows.
A dark, sinuous form lurks in the shadows.
A dark, sinuous form lurks in the shadows.

Twisted elms stand huddled together in groups around this hollow. Shrouded in shadows with crowns of mottled green, they lean inwards creating an enclosed circle-like area inside the forest. The lair between the elms is at least a hundred feet across and overgrown with tall bushes. Bloated, distended cadavers that have started to putrefy, hang from the lower branches. Strewn amidst the razor-sharp thorns, crumbling husks and the dismembered skeletal remains of long-dead creatures litter the area.
112629: This narrow tunnel slides down into the darkness at a very steep angle, its sides slick and smooth as if constructed with great skill. The sides are lightly grooved, as if a master mason had spent countless hours working in this most unhospitable place.
112637: A tall hill, with a bare rocky crest extends above the surrounding terrain. On the top of the hill, low-growing shrubs have taken root in the rocky ground. The hill is mostly bush covered, with some scattered pines and larches. From the top, the view shows the tower hills spreading out for miles in all directions except towards the southeast, where the hills give way to fields.
112653: The trail bends here to pass along the side of a rocky escarpment. Huddled together in the leeward side of the rocks a few stunted pine trees struggle for an existence in the rocky soil. The trees stand silent and unmoving as travellers pass them by. A small footpath can be seen leading off to the east where a solitary wooden cabin has been built.
112654: Sombre tones of green and purple colour the featureless landscape of the hills. The rough grasslands form mosaics on the thin, sandy soils of the higher, steeper slopes and broken ground. On the lower slopes, a few stunted birches grow amidst shrubs and undergrowth. A small number of smooth sandstone rocks are scattered about the hills.
112655: In a small dell between surrounding grassy hills; rusted and broken tools from past mining activities clutter the area, half-buried in the dirt. Large blocks of grey granite, the remains of a ruined building, lie here in the grass. To the south, a steep rock face, covered in dull-coloured grass and moss, looms above the dell.
112656: A craggy hill of grey rock, blanketed with reddish moss projects well above the background of rolling hills. From the bare hilltop, there is an unbroken view of the surrounding area. The foot of the hill is covered with low-growing and bushy pine trees and a dense growth of prickly bushes. A stack of stones has been erected at summit of the hill.
112657:
A swarm of mosquitoes is here, humming around you.
A fallow deer is grazing peacefully here.

Ranges of flat-topped, rugged hills dominate the landscape here. The craggy hillsides are partly covered with vegetation, mostly patches of short grass and red-coloured shrubs. The lower hills are covered with heath, and a few pine trees grow in the stony soil at the foot of the hills.
112658:
A tall pine tree grows here.
On the tree, there are two piles of pine nuts.
A buck runs swiftly from place to place, looking about warily as it grazes.

Moss covered rocks crown this windswept hillside. To the lea of the hill, small brackish pools have formed in the hollows; clearly drainage is a problem and only the hardier varieties of grass and shrub have found a home here. To the south a small thicket of pine trees breaks the monotony of the stony ground.
112659: A beautiful and docile horse is standing here.

The ground is bearably steep, rising from the valley to the north to meet the ridgeline that extends as far as the eye can see to the south. A few heather plants push themselves up from between the rocks spreading, unchallenged, across the ground.
112660:
A colony of red ants is here. The ants seem to ignore you.
A thin, crippled deer looks around timidly.

A thin, brown thread marks the passage of the trail across the green, undulating terrain. The wide, rutted wagon-trail snakes its way between the hills and valleys, picking its path along the contours of the land. At the side of the trail a broken, mouldy wagon-wheel rots away, providing a home for ants and other insects.
112661: The fertile hills support a variety of flora, most of it varieties of grasses that fight for supremacy among the stunted bushes. The lack of animal grazing here has allowed the grass to grow tall; high enough to cause even the tallest of men some difficulty. To the south, a busy track cuts across the land.
112662: The ground underfoot is covered with an abundance of bushy scrub. None of the plants are particularly tall but the thick, woody stems are a trip hazard to the unwary. The rolling hills to the west and south are mottled with browns and greens and stretch as far as the eye can see.
112663: The various types of scrub competing for areas to grow in have created an unusual pattern in the countryside. Mottled squares of green and brown appear to have been draped across the landscape like a giant patchwork quilt. Several woody stems encircle a lone tree on the western slopes. To the north, the cliff has a narrow opening at the base, save for that, the area is unremarkable.
112664: The ground underfoot is somewhat wet and large areas of moss cling to the rolling grass. Between two of the small hills a valley is crossed with dark, black trenches where peat has been cut. To the side of a trench a peat stack has been left to dry and a pungent, smoky aroma emanates from it.
112665: A thin, crippled deer looks around timidly.

The rise and fall of the surrounding grassland would tire even the strongest of wagon horses. Perhaps that is why the trail passes through a deep cutting in the hills allowing the track to stay almost level. Some of the earth forming the banks of the cutting has crumbled and collected at the base of the bank as the wind and rain have eroded it away over many months, the detritus forming a long, thin pile of muck at the side of the trail.
112666: Rising sharply to dominate the low ground that surrounds it, this lofty peak affords an excellent view of the valley that curves around its base and the sweeping trail that traverses the flat lands below. A small thicket of pine trees grows at an angle as if leaning into the prevailing wind. Little else, save for the occasional shrub, grows in the rocky soil.
112667: A sharp turn in the trail to pass between two giant boulders has forced the track to narrow, barely wide enough for a fully laden cart to pass. Forcing all traffic to pass along the exact same path has badly worn the surface of the track and someone has tried to repair the potholes by filling them with sand and crushed rocks.
112668: Hard-packed earth gives way to loose, dusty soil covering a series of slab-like rocks that have been used in the construction of the trail. The surface is treacherous to walk on and tired travellers need to take extra care not to twist an ankle. Thickets of gorse have taken hold at the side of the path making it difficult to leave the main trail save for a narrow path that has been hacked through the vegetation to the south.
112669:
A large, round boulder is here, worn smooth by the weather.
The remains of an old campfire lie here.

A stream cuts across the trail leaving pools of muddy, brown water to fill the ruts in the trail so that it is no longer possible to see how deep some of these grooves are. Further up the hill to the west the source of the stream can be seen, twisting and turning as it flows down the slope. Circles of blackened ash ringed by stones lie along the trail indicating that someone used this spot as a campsite recently.
112670: Verdant, green grass is spread across the hill with a dense growth of ruddy shrubs sheltering beneath a rocky outcrop on the western side. The ground slopes steeply down to a hollow to the south. On the eastern side it looks as if the hill itself has been worn to the bone, the pale greys and whites of the exposed rock is in stark contrast to the rich colours on display here.
112671: A fallow deer is grazing peacefully here.

This exposed plateau stops abruptly at a vertical drop that forms the northern and eastern edge; even an experienced climber would struggle to make a descent as the desolate summit lacks anything to which a rope might be secured. The edge of the precipice is carpeted with russet moss which contrasts sharply with the dull grey surroundings.
112672:
A small campfire burns here, its low flames giving off only a little light.
An old, sturdy mine cart stands here on the end of a pair of iron rails.

A wide ventilation shaft has been cut into the rock. The steep shaft has had crude steps hacked out of the stone to allow miners to climb the shaft and access the machinery that lines the passageway. All that now remains are tattered fragments of twisted iron and a sturdy hand-rail that has been deeply anchored into the rock. A wide cavern opens up to the south where the bulk of the excavations have taken place.
112673: Here the cavern branches with a side-tunnel running off to the east away from the main north-south passage. Red staining around the ceiling to the east indicates that there was once a rich seam of iron ore in the rock but it has long been exhausted leaving only traces of rust deposits in the puddles that accumulate on the ground.
112674: The tunnel opens out into a vast, circular cavern. The mineral deposits that make up this mine are very distinctive and are showcased in the walls here. Bands of minerals alternate from sparkling quartz to the reddish-brown hue of iron-ore to the black of plain bedrock creating a rainbow-like effect in earthy tones. Some thin bands of the iron-ore that the miners sought still remain in the walls.
112675:
A rusty pickaxe with a broken handle lies discarded here.
The small fierce-looking bat is hanging from the ceiling, obviously sleeping.

The tunnel narrows here, twisting and turning to follow the route of the mineral seam that the miners were following until it eventually stops completely. The miners, having exhausted the minerals, discarded their worn-out tools before abandoning the mine forever. The sheer number of broken picks and discarded crowbars indicate that this was a very active area in the past.
112676:
A large black bat flitters near you.
A sturdy pack horse is standing here.

The rough-cut tunnel extends far into the gloom to the north while to the south fresh air flows through a wide opening. The remains of grooves in the floor indicate where a mining cart one ran on rails but the rails are long gone, seemingly having fallen victim to metal scavengers. The uneven walls are covered with pick marks with niches and crevices where the miners have searched for ore.
112677: Before an Entrance to a Tunnel
A colourful butterfly is fluttering around here.

The entrance to a tunnel lies to the north, rough-cut in the rock face. The remains of a broken mining cart sit near the tunnel entrance. By the look of things, this old mine has been abandoned for a long time. A few large, jagged chunks of rock lie beneath the moss-covered rock face.
112678: An accomplished hunter stands here, listening for any hint of danger.

The cabin is simple yet functional. There are few home comforts here, the owner seems to value practicality above all else. A fireplace on the eastern wall is surrounded with piles of seasoned wood, a stockpile that should last the winter. Metal hooks attached to the wooden rafters are used to hang kills although they are all empty.
112679:
A fallow deer is grazing peacefully here.
A thin, crippled deer looks around timidly.
A thin, crippled deer looks around timidly.

The trail curves gently across the valley between two hilly areas, carving out a wide, russet arch on the face of the landscape. Half-submerged rocks and potholes mark the surface of the trail and the deep grooves formed by the passing wagon wheels turn and twist to miss the obstacles. Flowering shrubs and small rocks dot the surroundings and the remains of a large animal has been picked clean by scavenging birds and left at the edge of the trail.
112680:
A snake slithers towards you.
A goat is here, grazing in the hills.

The rolling hills stretch into the distance and the view is interrupted only by a few thickets of bushy oak trees and thorny shrubs. The various clefts and hollows formed by the ground provide ample cover for the small mammals that make this area home.
112681: The undulating peaks are carpeted with long, tufted grass and groves of untamed shrubs. The hills to the north are crowned with a makeshift wire fence that has been repaired many times and is in dire need of replacement. The lack of trees or cover of any other kind makes this particular area feel very exposed.
112682:
A coloured game bird is visible in the vegetation, watching you warily.
A small rat runs about, oblivious to your presence.

The uniform greenery covering most of the gently rolling hills is broken up with large tracts of scorched and blackened vegetation. The burnt scrub is the result of a wild fire that swept through this area some time ago. Already, tiny white flowers have begun to flourish amid the charred remains showing that nature cannot be held back for long.
112683: Stunted bushes and feeble trees are scattered across the rolling hills with only a thin carpet of grass holding the dark soil together. The land appears to be quite inhospitable except for small mammals that dart back and forth among the undergrowth.
112684:
A dun-coloured grouse is sitting still in the heather.
A fallow deer is grazing peacefully here.

A prominent ridge of hills that encircles this region forms a natural bowl that draws the eye towards a rocky prominence that erupts from the centre of the hollow. The boulders are remarkable as the vast majority of the hills here are formed from fertile peat that supports the diverse range of scrub that covers the ground.
112685:
A low shrub with bright green, oblong leaves is growing here.
Scattered in and on the shrub, there are three piles of blueberries.

The ground here slopes gently to the east into a deep valley. Despite the slope the drainage is poor, probably as a result of the peat in the soil which makes the ground soft underfoot and tiring to walk on. Clumps of matted grass and thorny shrubs are all that grow here.
112686: The flora here offers no surprises, it is a continuation of the same vegetation that stretches for miles around. Tufts of long grasses are interspersed with small, wiry shrubs while a few varieties of flowers have managed to find a place to grow.
112687: A seam of peat has been dug from the soft ground leaving a dark, black scar through the vegetation that stretches across the rolling hills. Several neat peat stacks have been left to dry in the sun and faint wagon wheel marks can be seen leading up to them.
112688: A few trees cling to the exposed hillside, their trunks bent and twisted as they try to grow against the prevailing winds which sweep across the hills. The scrub hills continue far into the north while to the south a narrow trail winds its way across the landscape.
112689: The trail stretches straight and true across the countryside, as far as the eye can see a thin brown line marks the route as it rises and falls across various ridges and valleys on the landscape. Some thin, woody scrub grows in the dirt along the centre of the trail but the hard-packed ruts, compacted under hundreds of passing wagon wheels are barren of any vegetation.
112690: Two deep ruts run in parallel through these hills. The gap is scarcely wider than a man's outstretched arms indicating that only smaller wagons have travelled this route.
