The grasses and scrub bushes that flourish here have been worn away along this trail, both within the ruts and between them; the exposed dirt is hard-packed and smooth. The trail curves slightly as it climbs a low hill, avoiding a sparse tree-line; otherwise, it follows a straight path from east to west, rising and falling with the terrain.
112691: An old signpost stands next to a crossroads in the trail.

Two trails converge at this crossroads, to the north the farming village of Black Hill can be seen atop the crest of the hill while to the east a wagon trail, well-used by merchants, leads off across the hills. The wide path heading south wends its way through Emyn Beraid, a route favoured by those heading to the Grey Havens.
112692: An old path weathered and aged leads to a major junction to the north. Heavy traffic has taken its toll on the surface of the path leaving ruts and potholes in the centre of the road. The path winds its way to the west leaving a black scar on the landscape. The Tower Hills lie to the east and south, lush with greenery, game and all manner of life.
112693: A buck runs swiftly from place to place, looking about warily as it grazes.

The road shifts direction as the current route has run into a hill too steep to climb. The rough path is marked with various wheel ruts from wagons that have attempted to use the route while overloaded. Small animals can be seen scurrying about. The hills provide them with good cover to hide from airborne predators circling high above.
112694: The road cuts through the hills to the north and south, hugging the contour lines to make the journey as easy as possible. This wide path is broad enough to support heavy traffic and judging by the state of the ruts in the road, heavy traffic, passing in all weathers, is exactly what this road got. To the west the hills rise too steeply to be climbed. To the east the fabled Tower Hills extend as far as the eye can see.
112695: The wide, worn trail continues onward with the occasional tumbleweed blowing across the path. Age and use have stamped out any potential foliage from growing in the hard-packed soil. What secrets and wonder this old track must hold under foot. The path continues to the north and west while the Tower Hills rise up to the south and east attempting to swallow this ancient route.
112696: The path turns and twists as it snakes around hills too steep for the road to traverse. The old road consists of well-packed dirt with wagon ruts and scuffed footprints spread across it. Small shrubs, interspersed with moss-covered rocks, frame the path making the dark surface of the path stand out from the pastel shades of the surrounding wilderness.
112697: The ancient road that has withstood the test of time slowly bends to avoid a steep drop. The road is wide; wide enough that two carts could easily pass each other. On the surface of the road, ruts have formed from the years of wagon use, most follow the same route but one set turns sharply south. A runaway wagon appears to have left the road careering, out of control, towards the sheer drop leaving a line of broken shrubs and skid marks in its wake. The tracks lead directly over the cliff edge sealing the wagon's fate.
112698: A wide path, created by countless wagons travelling the same route, follows the valleys through these hills. Only a few weeds grow in the spaces between the ruts perhaps indicating that this path sees regular travel. High, grass-clad hills rise on both sides of the path. The trail continues to the east and west while a narrow canyon blocks the way to the south.
112699: A fallow deer is grazing peacefully here.

A wide trail cuts across the Tower Hills here. Wagons use this path with some regularity, judging from the twin ruts worn into the hard ground. Grass and weeds grow between the ruts and on the sides of the trail. On either side, the hills rise and fall with no sign of significant change of the terrain for miles in any direction.
112700: An old, worn path turns west and north here, making a sharp bend due to a tall, green hill to the southeast. Deep, parallel grooves in the earth mark the passage of numerous wagons that have come this way. Still, much of the path is choked with grass and weeds and areas where wagons could overtake in the past have been reduced to a single track.
112701: Following the bottom of the valleys, this partially weed-strewn path twists and turns in deference to the surrounding landscape heading east and south. The lands to the north and west look wild and untamed, completely unmarked by civilisation while to the south and east the trail stretches into the distance.
112702: A worn trail can be found here, making its way between the hills and running along valleys and the gentler slopes. The trail appears to be rather old and the occasional plant has started to grow on it. It continues to the north and west. To the south and east, a rocky scrabble that leads upward can be seen without any way of navigating it.
112703: Sweeping through the rolling grassland, the trail gently meanders along the contours of the low hills, following the flat bottom of valleys. The trail is marked by deep ruts, especially in the narrower sections where it bends around the slopes of hills.
112704: The trail runs along the base of a steep cliff before turning west across a grassy hillside. It snakes its way across the landscape, leaving a thin brown scar in the middle of the verdant, green grass. Rocks and small shrubs line the trail on both sides.
112705: A colourful butterfly is fluttering around here.

Long and straight, the trail stretches out of sight to the east and west. Rolling hills flank the trail forming a shallow valley that offers some protection from the prevailing winds. Patches of flowers are the only flora, other than the omnipresent grass, that has managed to grow in the infertile soil alongside the track.
112706: Far to the north-west, there is a large dip among the hills. The hills in the immediate vicinity are small with gentle slopes. A trail winds its way from the south to the east. The passage of wagons and travellers has worn away any vegetation on the trail, but plenty of grass and wildflowers grow on either side of this trail. There are a lot of animal paths and tracks around, making it appear that plenty of deer and other game feed on the abundent grasses around this trail.
112707: A wagon trail winds through the hills in a northern and western direction. The hills are taller and rougher to the east and to the south. The hills are mostly covered in grass. Various flowers, shrubs, and other plants also thrive wherever the bedrock is covered by soil.
112708: The hills slope upward to the north and west just off of the trail that passes through here. The grass-covered valley that extends to the east and south forms a natural break from the hills that the trail follows. The grass covering the hills flow down from them and covers the valley floor. Only the narrow wagon trail breaks the green monotony.
112709: Bend in the Rutted Wagon Trail

As the trail brushes against the cliff walls to the east and the south, it bends around them while changing direction from the north to the west. Water run-off from above has caused the trail here to become soft and the ruts of wagon wheels past can be seen. The washout from above has only allowed small grasses and weeds to survive here.
112711: An old, worn trail passes through this region of the Tower Hills, continuing to the north and west. Hills slope upward to the south and east, bordering the trail. The steep hillside to the east is unstable, with scree and rubble resting at its foot. Small ruts in the trail show where wagons have passed before. At the narrowest point in the bend they are especially noticeable.
112712: A trail leads east and west, avoiding the steeper slopes of the surrounding Tower Hills. The trail is just wide enough to allow wagons to move along it. Weeds grow along the middle of the trail, but the majority of it is clear enough to show that it is still used at least occasionally.
112714: The ground here rises and falls with regularity, creating low hills and shallow valleys. Hill and valley alike are covered with low, woody bushes spaced at irregular intervals. Most of these bushes would reach as high as the waist on a man and seem to be thriving in this area; some, however, are little more than piles of bare sticks, splayed outwards as they rise from the ground.
112715: The path here has been paved in stone to support the wagons with farm goods heading from the village to the trade-routes to the south. As the road enters the village to the north it narrows slightly to pass between the shops and houses that crowd the edges of the path.
112716: Single-story dwellings flank each side of the path. Through the windows, plain wooden furniture can be seen. Faded and flaking paint adorns the woodwork around the windows and doors of the homes while baskets of flowers hang from hooks set into the walls. Clearly the owners of these properties are very house-proud, if a little poor.
112717: A small cart with a simple canvas cover has been left at the side of the path. Behind it several barrels have been piled up ready to be loaded. The house to the west has a small gate at the side, behind which a small, private garden can be seen. The path widens to the east as the street opens onto the main village square.
112718: An old man walks around slowly, deep in thought.

The road turns here to pass between the tall homes on either side of the road. High above, a laundry line stretches across the street, the bed sheets pegged to it flapping in the wind. At street level, the faded shutters of the houses creak as they pull against their hooks holding them open.
112719: Some delicious wild strawberries grow on the ground.

Centuries ago this area might have been overgrown with trees. Petrified remains of several former trees are still visible even with the current vegetation attempting to grow over the ancient roots. The Tower Hills can be seen extending their reach to the east. To the west and north an ancient path winds its way through the valleys.
112720: The grass has grown taller on this individual hill and care must be taken when forcing a route through it as the rocks and predators hiding within the brush could be disturbed at any moment. This one hill appears larger than most, affording an undisturbed view of the surrounding landscape and the road passing by to the north. This ridgeline continues to the southeast leading deeper into the Tower Hills.
112721: These hills are almost identical to the grassy hills that can be seen stretching away to the north and east. There is virtually no vegetation here except for short grass and no unique landmark to differentiate this set of hills from any other, just more rocks and grass. The hills themselves seem old, worn smooth over time.
112722: The lush, rolling Tower Hills converge on the mouth of the canyon. What starts as a gentle slope leads to a long descending path to the south. This area is teeming with vegetation and game. The greatness of the Tower Hills is swallowed by the shale canyon formation extending southward.
112723: A rock lizard is here, motionless as it observes you.

Etched deeply into the Tower Hills this canyon must have a history all of its own. The splintered rock formations provide cover for various lizards and mice allowing them to escape from their larger predators. The canyon narrows as it slopes down to the south with steep walls rising up on either side.
112724: A tiny, harmless centipede is here.

A steep incline awaits anyone trying to move forward from this canyon. Pebbles have come to rest awkwardly along the canyon path here. The high rising canyon walls choke off any passage to the east or west while to the north a short scramble over rocks may be a way to leave the canyon. A gentle slope to the south leads to the bottom of the canyon.
112725: The remnants of large boulders, fractured by time and weather make up several high mounds now covered in moss. In the lee of the mounds a thicket of trees has found enough shelter from the prevailing wind to grow strong and tall. As the trees gained height they climbed above the shelter of the mounds and were exposed to the strong winds that can sometimes blow across this peak. One unfortunate tree has succumbed to the force of nature and toppled, its roots erupting from the ground. Where the roots have torn free, clumps of dirt rest loosely on top of the grass. A path can be seen to follow along to the north and west while the hills continue to climb to the east and south.
112726: A ring of high hills encircles this lowland expanse. Several of the taller hilltops have grass thickets growing along their ridgelines. Much of the vegetation seems to have been trampled by large animals although little sign has been left to show what species. A wide, worn path is visible to the west while the Tower Hills extend to the north and south in a fairly straight line.
112727: As the hills continue to rise, the various peaks and valleys appear very similar. The terrain, while not difficult to pass, could confuse a careless traveller with the similarities in the landscape making navigation tricky. Large hills dominate the landscape to the north and west but, in contrast, a sheer drop extending from the east around to the south is impassable; the hills ending abruptly in a steep canyon.
112728: The rolling, overgrown hills that dominate the surrounding areas appear to be levelling out here. The heavily compacted earth means the landscape is barren, devoid of almost all flora save for some fairly short grass and a few woody shrubs. An unusual feature of this hill is the deep cleft that has opened up leading steeply down into a canyon below. The exposed rock walls of the fissure are jagged providing wide ledges that could be used as steps to reach the bottom of the canyon far below.
112729: A rock lizard is here, motionless as it observes you.

A multitude of shades of green covers the surrounding brush and tree-strewn hills. Dense undergrowth flourishes on the gentle slopes making travelling tiresome. A number of large rocks are jutting out from the hillside, looking like giant teeth. Dark green moss and pale grey lichen envelop the stones.
112730: A large marmot is here, scurrying in between the rocks.

Rocks and debris fallen from the brittle walls litter the canyon floor. Barren and destitute, the land here is too dry to support plant life. In its place a thick blanket of dust covers the ground. A sheer wall on the southern edge of the canyon blocks any hope of continuing in that direction. An ascending trail can be seen to the north and the bottom of this particular canyon stretches out to the east and west.
112731: A small brown snake is slithering around here.

Small pebbles lie scattered on the ground here at the lowest point of the canyon. Dust clouds fly up when the wind blows and, in extreme cases, dust devils send the smaller pieces of gravel scattering amongst the rocks. To the north the canyon gives way to what appears to be an expanse of windswept fields, to the west the canyon continues.
112732: The black crow flies low to the ground here, looking for carrion to eat.

Pieces of windblown grass litter the open grassy field. The grass grows high enough to potentially hide predators within. The brush that makes up the fields extends to the north and east but slowly thins and gives way to rocky ground far to the south.
112733:
A wild sheep with a short, greyish coat grazes here.
A wild sheep with a short, greyish coat grazes here.
A wild sheep with a short, greyish coat grazes here.

The wild grass growing here butts up against the steep, craggy base of the Tower Hills that dominate the land to the north and west. The thick, verdant grass has scarcely been disturbed, indicating that there is not a significant quantity of game in the area. To the south the grassy fields continue while to the east the field appears to take on a rougher appearance.
112734: The ground here is consists of rocks intermingled with small tufts of grass and low-growing shrubs. Mottled hues spread over the ground; green where grass and moss thrives and grey where stones, large and small, litter the ground. A moss-covered granite crag rises to north, looking impassable to man or beast.
112735:
A clear spring babbles as cool water trickles out of the ground.
A swan swims gracefully on the surface of the water.
A duck is here, quacking happily.
A large eagle soars above you.

These uncultivated fields are thick with wild, purple lupines and crisscrossed with a few undulating streams. A small spring concealed by long grass and shrubs bubbles up from the ground. Old, moss-covered stone walls are bordering the fields, mostly intact even though they appear to have stood here for a very long time.
112736: A hardened ranger is walking around, looking for tracks.

Clusters of bushes and some trees spread on the predominantly flat ground. Among the bushes, there are few open spaces, those that do exist are carpeted with long grass. The ground here is dotted with huge boulders covered with thick, green moss half embedded in the rich loam. Towards the east, the ground descends down to the green meadows visible below.
112737:
A ruined old door lies on the ground, rotting away.
A barn-owl is here, looking for easy prey.

A thick, dense ivy cloaks a small ruined cottage built from dry stone. Fallen into disuse, the cottage is now slowly rotting away. Only parts of the crumbling walls, an old door, and the fireplace remain of this derelict abode. The growth of ivy is creeping up the ruined walls, covering them in a green blanket.
112738:
A rock lizard is here, motionless as it observes you.
A rock lizard is here, motionless as it observes you.

A steep cliff to the north rises high above the surrounding landscape. Some weathered lichen covered rocks are scattered about the area. Tall, thick grass blankets the rugged terrain while oblong-leaved bushes with yellow flowers thrive on the rocky ground bringing some colour to the surroundings. Wiry and young rowan trees grow here sparsely.
112743: Shades of greys and a few streaks of rusty brown from water trickling through the cracks, colour a high, steep rock face. A semi-circular outcrop of rock, overhanging a cliff wall provides some shelter from the elements. The vegetation is sparse here, only occasional patches of grass and shrubs of low height grow on the otherwise barren, rocky ground.
112744: The ground here is rugged and rocky, and there is little vegetation in the barren soil. A tall rock-face overlooks the landscape, obstructing travel to the north. Grey, angular rocks large and small litter the ground among patches of dry, yellow grass. The terrain slopes gently down towards a boggy glen to the south.
112745:
A swarm of mosquitoes is here, humming around you.
A grey snake slides along the water.
A large leech is moving close to you, searching for blood.

Moss-covered peat blankets the soggy ground here. The wetland has a seemingly simple flora; only patches of purple-coloured grass and long-stemmed bog cotton grow on the wet, spongy ground. The small pools of water with their surrounding tufts of bog grass give way to rockier terrain towards the north, where the land rises.
112746: A large eagle soars above you.

A variety of colourful flowers thrives on a low-lying meadow. The dark green grass grows long and lush in the rich soil with a plentiful supply of water. Sedges and rushes form small stands in the damp depressions. Thick greyish shrubs with small, round leaves grow taller than the surrounding undergrowth.
112747: The grass here is thick and lush, growing in dense tussocks. An old ditch runs along an expanding hedge, almost completely overgrown. The signs of cultivation of the fields are slowly vanishing under the expanses of tall grass and shrub thickets. Beside a withered oak tree, the grey fence poles of a sheep paddock are still standing.
112748: A colourful butterfly is fluttering around here.

In a broad expanse of meadowland, splashes of colourful wildflowers punctuate a sea of tall waving feathery grasses. A few mature individual trees grow on this undulating grassland. In addition to the sparse tree cover, wild and untended hedges block the view across an otherwise open landscape.
112749: Tall grass and a myriad of wild flowers grow on the open meadow. Only a few short and shrub-like pine trees stand in the tall grass. This lively place seems to attract a multitude of species of wildlife, providing food and shelter for birds and small animals. Gently sloping hills to the west rise above the surrounding flatlands.
112750: A colourful butterfly is fluttering around here.

A gentle rise ends abruptly at a steep escarpment. Boulders and scree lie around the base of the slope having fallen from the cliff above. A few pine trees and evergreen plants grow on the rocky ground. Some lichens grow hanging from tree branches, resembling the grey hairs of an old man's beard. The jagged terrain to the west looks difficult to reach.
112751: A colourful butterfly is fluttering around here.

Like gnarled fingers of a subterranean giant, a formation of large craggy rocks protrudes from the grass. Standing alone on a featureless expanse with no other stones or mountains in sight, these rock figures are unequivocally massive, dwarfing even the tallest of men at their base. A mound of ash is here, encircled by stones.
112752: An old, rotten stump is here, surrounded by grass.

The ground is covered by tall grasses and small bushes. Scattered stones and rotting wood mark the remains of the fences that bordered what was once a cultivated land. Steep hills rise in the west, continuing their ascent northward where an escarpment can be seen in the distance. In the other directions, the fields stretch for several miles.
112753: A fallow deer is grazing peacefully here.

The ground rises and falls in rolling, grass-covered hills. The hills are low enough to be considered fields. The hilltops, if they could be called thus, allows a slightly better view of the surrounding landscape. The grassy fields extend for miles in all directions. Far to the west, and even further to the north, a range of higher, rocky hills rises above the grasslands.
112754: Man-high thistles tower over coach grass on this overgrown field. Remains of an old stone wall can still be seen beside fields taken over by shrubs and weeds. Some chiselled stones lie in the grass, perhaps marking a place where a barn or a shelter once stood. A thick and prickly hedgerow creates an impenetrable barrier to the north.
112755:
A giant boulder sits here among the swaying grasses.
A large, loyal falcon is circling above.

Tall, thick grass and weeds grow in abundance on this abandoned farmland. A huge boulder, composed of weathered granite stands here. A clump of slender trees surround the granite boulder, forming a small island on the field. Small depressions remain where a ditch used run, long ago overgrown. Patches of wildflowers border a faint trail leading to the north.
112756:
A large thorny branched shrub is growing here.
On the shrub, there are two piles of blackberries.

Several large hawthorn bushes grow in a cluster amidst a sea of swaying, green grass. The tallest bush rises more than fifteen feet above the grass. Small birds fly to and from their well-protected nests, which have been built deep within the shrubbery. The grass-covered fields continue for miles in all directions. Far to the west, a range of rocky hills can be seen.
112757:
A woody evergreen plant grows here, with many stems reaching upward.
A blooming water-lily floats on the surface of the water.

A small brook flows into the fields from the hills in the north. The water gathers into a small pool at the foot of the cliff before gently flowing away across the lush grasslands in the south. A wide variety of plants and tall green grasses flourish along the banks of the brook.
112758: Along a Brook in the Grasslands
A snowy-white egret stands here alertly.

A clear brook runs from the north to the south, its water slowly trickling through the grasslands. The fields are overgrown with tall grass of a healthy green colour, nourished by the fresh water of the stream. The streambed is clearly visible through the water and the brook could easily be forded.
112759: A small number of trees and some low bushes are the most easily distinguishable features of the landscape's otherwise plain appearance. The ground in these fields is mostly covered in tall and green grasses, gently swaying even in the slightest breeze. Here and there amidst the soft soil, animal holes can be seen.
112760: The rolling landscape of these vast fields is formed by many slightly sloping low hills. Despite the sporadic clumps of tall grass, venturing here should offer no more effort than the surrounding plains. The grass grows tall and green on the southern sides of the hills, while the lower grass shares the northern slopes with a large blanket of wet, green coloured moss.
112761:
A large thorny branched shrub is growing here.
On the shrub, there are two piles of blackberries.

The fields slope slightly up and down, yet still flat enough not to slow down any venturer. The ground is covered in unusually tall, green grass and low bushes. Sprawling north and south, the grasslands spread out in a vast blanket of green, rolling and tumbling against the folds and furrows of the land. To the west and east, lies an impenetrable conglomerate of thorny bushes and twisting vines.
112762: Both flowers and bushes alike prosper here. The soil is damp, yet hard to lay eyes upon, as the vegetation grows remarkably dense. The grasslands continue in all directions but east, where a rockier environment presents itself. A few isolated trees grow in the meadow, offering a small shift in the backdrop.
112763: A small brown snake is slithering around here.

A dense forest in the southeast is the only distinctively different landmark around, and without it the fields would seem to be endless in all directions. Healthy grass grows thick on these gently sloping plains, providing fine pastures for the indigenous animals to graze.
112764:
There is a huge, pyramidal beehive here.
A large bee buzzes loudly as it travels from flower to flower.
A large bee buzzes loudly as it travels from flower to flower.
A large bee buzzes loudly as it travels from flower to flower.

Mixed grasses of different heights grow between small patches of yellow and red star-shaped flowers. To the west, the sparkling surface of a stream can be seen between the breaks in the emerald-green flora that thrives along the bank. The ground is situated somewhat higher than the surrounding fields, allowing easy survey of the grasslands that sprawl out for several miles in all directions.
112765: A hardened ranger is walking around, looking for tracks.

Making its way through the countryside, the brook flows southwards. Low bushes grow on the banks of the brook, nourished by the clear, fresh water. Patches of densely growing trees overshadow sections of the brook, offering protection for both animal and traveller alike.
112766: A blooming water-lily floats on the surface of the water.

Meandering in from the west, a lazy stream joins together with a small brook that cuts through the grassland. Where the two converge, the water swirls and bubbles, causing small funnels on the surface of the water. Tall reeds grow along the banks, gently swaying back and forth.
112767:
A large boulder is here, it must be heavy.
A mass of dark green leaves clings to a wall.

Tall grass dominates the landscape, gently bending at the slightest gust of wind. The ground slopes sharply upwards towards the north, rising up to form an overhanging cliff in the hills. Several boulders and small piles of rocks cover the ground, probably having fallen from the northern inclination.
112768: Field at the Edge of a Forest

The grasslands here are sparsely wooded with young trees and saplings. To the west, the trees grow denser and taller as the fields transform into a proper forest. Apart from the trees, the ground is mostly covered with low undergrowth; small bushes and tall, green grass sprawl across the ground.
112769: A small stream emerges from the depths of a dense forest to the west. Although littered with fallen leaves, twigs, and other forest debris, the water in the creek largely appears to be clear and healthy. The vegetation is very sparse outside the forest, consisting mainly of grass and saplings of the spreading forest.
112770:
A shrub with maple-like leaves is growing here.
On the shrub, there are three handfuls of blackcurrant berries.

Large fir and pine trees grow increasingly sparse towards the east here, where the forest slowly transitions into rolling grasslands. However less dense than to the north and west, the canopy above is still thick enough to block any light from reaching the forest floor. The ground is composed entirely of fallen pine needles, twigs, and branches.
112771: Stream at the Edge of a Forest
Some ugly blow-flies are buzzing around here.

Water flows in a small stream, running from east to west. The water meanders around the trees and gathers in shallow pools where the ground is lower. The water is shallow, and can easily be forded by foot or astride a mount. The trees are a mix of mainly fir, pine, and birch, with a few hazel-trees scattered amongst the forest. Most of the growth looks young, as the trees are little more than saplings.
112772:
A brown toad is here, hunting flies.
A restless rabbit bounces around.

The forest grows thick and dense, making it hard to venture any other way than south. The forest seems to be young, no more than a few decades at most. Saplings and small trees grow in impregnable thickets and the forest floor is covered with bushes and plants. The ground, where visible, seems damp and the earthy odour of wet soil fills the air.
112773: A thin fog-like haze hangs suspended above the forest floor. The air is damp and the ground wet. This forest is young, overgrown with saplings and bushes, with no towering ancients in sight. Steep cliffs rise to the north and west, casting parts of the forest in murky shadows.
112774: A brown toad is here, hunting flies.

Seeping from the forest floor here, a forest spring submerges most of the low-laying ground in a few inches of water. Constantly meandering left and right, a murky stream slowly runs towards the east. This spring is unmistakably the source of the surrounding forest's sogginess.
112775:
A large elk is standing here, chewing grass and leaves.
A large elk gazes coldly at you, chewing on a small branch.

Deep puddles of water form still, leaf-covered pools between groves of saplings and sprawling bushes. The northern part of this forest has a particularly moist forest floor. The lower trunks of the trees and the drier parts of the ground are covered in different types of mosses, all thriving in the soggy forest.
112776: A large elk is standing here, chewing grass and leaves.

Sapling pines and firs make up most of the young forest here. The trees grow dense and the needle-covered branches intersect above to create a green canopy. The ground is covered with grass, moss and ferns. The sound of running water can be heard in the distance, and to the south, a large tower is visible through the canopy.
112777: A small rabbit glares angrily at you.

A tall white tower rises gracefully from atop the Tower Hills in the southwest. Every sunset the tower is bound to cast its shadow for miles across these fields. Where it stands on a steep hill, the tower can not be directly approached from here. The grass covered fields extend to the north, east, and south while they give way to a dense forest to the west.
112778:
The butchered corpse of a fallow deer is lying here.
A hardened ranger is walking around, looking for tracks.

Low bushes thrive in the fertile, wet soil here. Flowing lazily through the grassland towards the south, the water of a stream bubbles and clucks as it flows over barely submerged rocks. The streambed is clearly visible, consisting mainly of sand and rocks, worn smooth after years in the water.
112779: An enormous oak tree lies fallen upon the ground.

Lush grasslands stretch out far, save for a forest miles to the southeast. This particular field is completely devoid of any plants higher than a man's waist. A tall, splintered stump stands upon a small grassy mound, next to which lies a massive oak tree. Even in death, the branches spread magnificently, save for many that are charred and blackened, evident of a mighty lightning strike years ago.
112780: The plains here are covered in a dense layer of healthy green grass, with the occasional small mound of flowers and broad-leaved ferns. Gazing south, a fenced pasture can be seen in the distance, with a small farm house standing close by.
112781: The landscape descends into a deep valley. Bordering a low, dense forest in the south, some patches of trees have rooted in the valley. The ground is rich with grass, evergreen bushes, and plenty of saplings. To the east, the trees grow more plentiful as the field transitions to forest.
112782:
A blooming water-lily floats on the surface of the water.
A brown toad is here, hunting flies.
A brown toad is here, hunting flies.

Soggy, waterlogged ground surrounds the tall beech trees that grow in the boggy peat. The fertile land has meant that the forest, which appears to have escaped the lumberjack's axe for many years, has grown lush and dense. Layers of moss cover the thick roots that snake between the trees, seeking out nutrients in the damp ground. To the north and west, the soggy ground becomes an impassable mire, beyond which the ground becomes drier as it climbs in elevation.
112783: The soil is soft and moist here supporting vegetation that is predominantly made up by moss, low bushes, and ferns. Firs and pines grow straight and tall here, the lower part of their trunks completely devoid of the needle-like leaves that coniferous trees usually carry. The trees are spaced well apart from each other, allowing the ground vegetation to thrive.
112784: A brown toad is here, hunting flies.

Large numbers of fir and pine saplings grow here, their thin trunks reaching towards the sky. A tall white tower can be sighted through the forest's canopy. Looming over the forest, the tower stands on a steep hill to the east. At the base of the hill, a small cave entrance is just barely visible behind branches, trunks, and the needlelike leaves of the trees.
112785:
A tiny spider is here, eating a tiny bug.
A tiny spider is here, eating a tiny bug.
A fierce bat is here, lusting for your blood.
A small bat flies silently from shadow to shadow.

The walls of this cave are uneven and rough. The floor at the southern end of the cavern is covered in a layer of grass and leaves. A low and narrow opening in the western wall leads to a forest outside the cave. Along the inner wall to the east, there is a section that looks noticably smoother than the surrounding rock, around which small strands of spider silk gently sway as if pushed by an unseen breeze.
112786:
A large elk is standing here, chewing grass and leaves.
A large elk gazes coldly at you, chewing on a small branch.
A large elk is standing here, chewing grass and leaves.
A brown toad is here, hunting flies.

Firs and pine trees, amongst other types of conifers grow dense here. The canopy is thick, allowing only just enough light for the moss that grows on the lower parts of the tree trunks to thrive. Steep hills rise in all directions but north, where the forest continues its motionless march onward.
112787: A skeleton of some humanoid lies in the dust.

Rising towards the sky, the tower on the western hill overlooks this entire region. Some of the windows of the tower are facing this direction. Without doubt, a fall from there would be absolutely fatal. The landscape east of the hills is flourishing with grass and various meadow flowers, such as daisies and red poppy.
112788: The fields are covered with grass, weeds, and low bushes. To the west, steep hillsides block travel as the land rises and becomes more arid. To the north, east, and south, the grassy expanse continues, only interupted by a small creek to the east.
112789: Seemingly impenetrable hills rise in the west, graced by an impressive tower on the peak in the far north. Soft and moist, the soil here is kept fertile by a nearby creek that flows towards the east. Various kinds of flowers cover the grasslands, among them oxeye daisy and cornflower.
112790: A fallow deer is grazing peacefully here.

The grass that covers the land here is both thick and healthy, due to the nearby creek that flows freely towards the east. The grasslands slope slightly upwards to the west, while eastwards it descends into the small creek. Gazing to the southeast, a faint trail can be spotted amongst patches of tall, green grass.
112791:
A mass of dark green leaves clings to a wall.
An apple tree with bright green leaves grows here.
On the tree's branches are two apples.

A sparkling brook flows in from the elevated northern grasslands. The stream's water is crystal clear, maybe suggesting that it is safe to drink. Small pebbles, rounded by countless years in the flowing water, occupy the streambed Various kinds of grasses and flowers are thriving here in the damp soil. To the east, a wide, wooden plank spans across the water, where it meets a faint path that meanders through the grass towards a small farmhouse.
112792: A large rabbit looks peacefully at you, ready to dart away.

A massive carpet of grass and low bushes covers the landscape. Nourished by the brook that flows through here, the grass looks vigorous and in perpetual growth. The stream looks very fresh, and would satisfy the needs of traveller, animal, and plant alike. A dense forest is distinguishable far to the south-east.
112793: A fresh brook flows through the fertile grasslands. The water's flow is slow and lazy, and the streambed is clearly visible beneath the stream's surface. The plains are lush with healthy, green grasses. An assortment of orange, yellow, and red flowers sprout up in patches amongst the grass, dotting the landscape in colourful patterns.
112794: The grasslands descend steeply from both sides into a shallow brook. Aided both by fertilisation brought by the animals that come to the creek to drink and the clear water of the stream itself, the grass grows very lush and strong here.
112795: The forest floor is wet and muddy in the west, however towards the east, the ground becomes drier. Trees of many kinds, such as birch, elm, and hazel are thriving here, nourished by the fertile and humid soil. The trees are fairly dense, and although not at all impossible, care should be had when moving through the forest.
112796: The forest here is densely populated by young trees, their thin trunks bending at the slightest gust of wind. The ground is damp and covered with brown leaves shed from the surrounding birch, beech, and hazels from autumns past. The trees seem to grow both higher and thicker in the east, indicating that this part of the forest is older.
112797: A very short plant with bright white flowers is growing here.

The trees here are covered in a thick, dark lichen. Birch, hazel, and beech stand tall and proud, suggesting this is an older part of the otherwise young-in-appearance forest. The ground is covered in a thick blanket of rotting foliage. A few gnarled roots protrude from the leaves and snake across the ground, before returning back into the earth in search of nutrients.
112798:
A small cluster of clover grows here.
A long-tailed bird watches you from the vegetation.

Hazel and beech are all the trees that seem to reside in this part of the dense forest. All the trunks are slender, swaying gently in the slightest gust of wind. The forest opens up into grass-covered fields to the north. In the south the trees grow taller and wider. Some trees here seem to have scratch marks on the bottom of their trunks.
112800: A finch flies low above the ground.

This woodland area is densely populated with hazel, birch, and beech. All of them several years from their utmost height and their ultimate width. The forest floor is soft, delicately packed with fallen leaves of the last autumn. To the west, a long, impassable wall of fallen and uprooted trees stretches into the distance.
112801: A buck runs swiftly from place to place, looking about warily as it grazes.

Bordering a dense forest to the east, the grasslands here are to some extent covered with trees. Birch and hazel are among the trees trying to recapture the grassy plains and to turn it into forest again. The ground is soft and muddy, permeated by the creek that flows freely to the west. A small farmhouse is visible in the north.
112802:
A simple wooden chest is here.
A sturdy bed made from solid oak lies here, covered in warm blankets.
A sturdy peg for hanging armour from is on the wall.
On the peg, there is a leather saddle.
A skilled pony breeder is here, wearing a thoughtful expression.

Even for a house in the peaceful countryside, this would be considered a very humble residence. The walls are made from cut lengths of cedar, which lends a sweet smelling aroma to the room. There is no ceiling to this single-room structure, only thick, wooden rafters stand between the floor and the pinnacle of the roof. Upon the southern wall, there is a large mahogany mural of a pony. Several thin ropes and a leather saddle hang from a peg near the corner. From the window to the east, a fenced pasture can be seen sprawling across the land.
112803:
A bale of wheat is lying here.
A domesticated pony, beast of burden to many, stands here.
A domesticated pony, beast of burden to many, stands here.
A domesticated pony, beast of burden to many, stands here.
A domesticated pony, beast of burden to many, stands here.

Enclosed by fences, these grasslands have been turned into a pasture for livestock. The grass is kept permanently short by the ponies that are bred here. Alongside the southern edge of the field, a dense forest grows, its lowest branches growing over the fence to the pasture.
112804: Somewhat elevated, the landscape overlooks a distant trail that can be seen through the trees to the south and east. The woodlands here are composed mainly of birch and beech, their trunks pale and smooth against the dark backdrop of the surrounding forest. A thick blanket of leaves lie in perpetual decay upon the uneven ground.
112805: Some ugly blow-flies are buzzing around here.

The forest shifts as the trail bends to the south and the east. While the forest grows sparse in the south, the trees on the northern side of the trail grow not only high, but also dense enough to prevent any detectable access to those parts of the forest.
112806:
A waist-high evergreen shrub grows here, with thick, reaching branches.
On the shrub, there are two piles of grey-green leaves.
A forest spider is here crawling around.
A forest spider is here crawling around.

This woodland area is densely populated with young trees; a mixture of beech, hazel, and birch compete skyward for the most sun. The undergrowth is littered with old leaves, but occasionally a small tree or a bush finds a spot with enough light to thrive. The west-facing sides of the trunks are covered in a thick coat of lichen.
112807: A hill rises in the northwest, its steepness denying further venture of the forest in that direction. Several of the trees here carry scratch marks on the bases of their trunks. To the north, barely discernible behind some sprawling shrubbery, is a gaping hole at the bottom of a natural embankment. Small tufts of grey and white fur hang from the branches of the shrubs near the opening.
112808: A long-tailed bird watches you from the vegetation.

The forest here is low and very dense. The local fauna consists of hazels, birches, beeches, and elms, none even close to their full height or width. A hill rises in the northwest, covered in dense forest. The forest floor mainly exhibits low bushes and a soft bed of old, rotting leaves.
112809: The trees here grow close to each other and straight upwards, competing for the obtainable sunlight. Covering the forest floor are many thick, moss-covered roots, which seem to dive in and out of the rich soil below. Upon the forest floor lies a thick layer of dead leaves, twigs, and branches.
112810: The trail leads through a dense forest. None at full height, thin hazels and beeches compete for an unrivalled chance of sunlight. A thick layer of fallen leaves are decaying on the ground, providing nourishment for the herbivores that forage here.
112811:
Some ugly blow-flies are buzzing around here.
A brown fox is here, looking for some rabbits to chew up.

A thin forest surrounds the trail on the north and south sides. The trail is partly overgrown with tree sprouts and mosses, suggesting that visitors are a rare sight in these forests. The trees to the north are noticeably higher than those that grow nearby.
112812: The trail cuts through the young yet dense forest. Hazel, beech, and elm grow tall in the west. Towards the east and south, the vegetation is lower and denser and the trees are surrounded by low bushes. The trail is barely visible beneath the fallen leaves. Many years of neglect have slowly erased the boundary between forest and trail.
112813:
A small cluster of clover grows here.
Some ugly blow-flies are buzzing around here.

Dominated by beech, elm, and birch, the forest here extends in all directions. Overhead, thick tree branches grow rather dense, competing with each other for available sunlight. The trail here is barely discernible beneath the fallen leaves, twigs, and branches.
112814: Judging by their appearance, these barren fields have been abandoned for a long time. The fertile top layers of soil have blown away, leaving nothing but dust and stone. Many of the larger rocks are blackened at their highest points, as if they were burned when a fire swept across this land long ago.
112815: This path is dusty and windswept. It follows the edge of a large field to the west. Dry, withered weeds lie upon the edges of the path, continuing further out into the surrounding fields. Several lengths of cracked and blackened poles stand between the field and the path, resembling what was once a proud, sturdy fence. The path continues to the north, into what looks like the ruins of a small village.
112816: A path from the south ends at a small open area here. The open area seems likely to be the village square. Old, partially-collapsed buildings surround the square. The walls that still stand look blackened, as if a fire burned the village down sometime long ago. The ground is dry, dusty, and mostly barren.
112817: These fields are split into large squares with paths between them. The soil is a burnt-clay red, stony, and mostly barren. Nothing but a few struggling weeds grow here, barely clinging to life. The lifeless fields continue to the north and east. The edge of a forest is visible far to the south, beyond a valley.
112818: These fields have a blackened, unhealthy look. A fire may be the cause of the devastation, but if so it happened long ago. Some weeds fight an uneven battle for survival on the otherwise lifeless field. For weeds, they look remarkably miserable. The barren fields continue to the east and south, while the partially collapsed wall of a house blocks passage north. To the west, the ground is covered with thick, thorny shrubbery that clings to the rapidly ascending hillside, making travel in that direction hard.
112829: Some ugly blow-flies are buzzing around here.

Here, the grasslands start to mix with a dense forest to the east. Towards the west, the land slopes considerably, before meeting the clear waters of a small creek. To the south, a partially overgrown trail is barely visible between tall tufts of grass, which predominantly covers the landscape.
112830: From atop these hills, the emerald-green planes of rolling grasslands stretch on for miles. Towards the north, the top of a tower white stands out against the skyline. The hills are dotted with small, star-shaped flowers that lend a vibrant contrast to the surrounding sea of green that sprawls out to the east. In all other directions, the land becomes rocky and arid, as towering rock formations thrust upwards towards the sky.
112831: A trail bends sharply to the south and east here. Overgrown with grass and bushes, it is not obvious how far it continues straight in any direction. In the east, the land appears to be cut by a valley running north and south. Far north, the top of a tower presents itself.
112832: A clear brook intersects an overgrown trail here, where the disintegrating remains of what appears to have been an old wooden bridge lies half sunken in the muddy streambed. Beneath the surface of the water, the beams once used to support the bridge can be seen, upon which several lengths of green beard lichen drift lazily in the mild current.
112833: Flanked by the lush grasses of the plains, the trail is easily discernible in the distance to the east, where a treeline begins to form. To the west, the trail meanders through the vegetation at a gradual descent, until finally intersecting a burbling creek. Upon the ground here, small bushes and twigs intermingle with the grasses.
112834: Faded Trail at the Edge of a Forest

In the north and in the east, a light forest grows next to the trail. The trees at the outskirts of the forest grow in sparse formations of low height, indicating that the forest is both young and expanding. To the west, the trail cuts straight through the lush grasslands seemingly for several miles.
112835: A thin forest surrounds the trail on the east and south sides. The trail is partly overgrown with tree sprouts and mosses, suggesting that visitors are a rare sight in these forests. The trees in the north are noticeably higher than those in the other directions, while still not reaching their full height.
112836: Towards the north and west, a faint trail can be seen weaving between the lichen-covered trunks of towering trees. The low hanging branches are completely devoid of foliage, either from lack of sunlight or the voracious appetites of the local fauna. The ground is covered with clumps of stunted grass and bushes.
112837: A small animal, all covered in spines, snuffles amongst the undergrowth.

Tall grass grows in abundance across these sprawling fields. Moderately uniform in height, various types of weeds, thistles, and bushes thrive here, offering magnificent cover for hiding animals. A low forest flourishes in the northwest, stretching for several miles. Several animal paths cross the grasslands, emerging from the forest's edge.
112838: The forest here bears several markings of animal activity. Most of the trees have noticeable claw marks on their trunks. A hole in the ground is visible in a hill in the south, where many tracks can be seen leading to and from the opening. Towards the east, the trees taper off into a bushy grassland.
112839: A brown fox is here, looking for some rabbits to chew up.

Dug out from the soft soil, this oval cave is undoubtedly the work of some animal. Roots of various lengths and sizes dangle from the ceiling, searching in vain for nutrients. Along the walls of the den, deep claw marks have been scraped into the dirt. Small tufts of silvery hair lie upon the ground next to a gnawed piece of wood.
112840: A few trees grow on this plain, widely separated by green and brown grass. There are few signs of animal activity here, and there are no man-made structures in sight in any direction. There is, however, an old trail to the north, the only thing that stands out on these featureless plains.
112841: A low and wet grassland expands for miles here, the water-lodged ground hosting a wide variety of plants and grasses. A slow stream flows in from the north, and disappears to the southeast. To the east, a forest-like shape gives a hint of somewhat higher ground compared to the immediate surroundings.
112842: A fading trail comes in from the west and leads northwards. The trail crosses an area of wide plains here. The plains slope gently downward to the east, and as the ground gets lower the ground looks water-logged. The vegetation change from grass and shrubs to an expansive growth of long reedmace, their heads looking like cat tails sticking out of the mud.
112843: An old signpost stands next to a crossroads in the trail.

The faded trail crosses grass-covered fields, leading east and west. Another path, carefully laid with cobblestones, but overgrown with lichen and seemingly disused, leads north. Lush grasslands expands for miles to the south; there is no end to them in sight.
112844: The path leading from the south makes a sudden turn westward here, effectively avoiding a vertical drop into the northern and eastern plains. Boulders of various sizes have been placed at even intervals between the edge of the path and the precipitous sheer; to serve a warning, or simply provide a place to sit and view the landscape, the purpose of the rocks is unknown. Thick layers of lichen cling to the cobblestone, lending a greenish-brown stain to the surface of the path.
112845: An old, dust-covered trail leads off to the east and north. To the south, at the foot of a steep cliff, another trail follows the fields at the foot of the hills. The two trails seem to converge to the south-east. Towards the north a tower can barely be sighted. The road is set with stones with vegetation springing up between the cracks where they meet.
112846: A beautiful and docile horse is standing here.

Atop these nearly-barren hills, an old, dusty path leads to a tall white tower that rises to the north. Small patches of grass and a few low bushes constitute the only flora here. Dry twigs and natural debris lie scattered on the ground, caught in various states of decay. To the east, two perky grass-covered hills can be seen rising in the distance, each crowned with a circular bed of vibrant flowers. To the north and south, the path continues onward.
112847: A dusty path follows the ridge of the hill as it bends to the east and south here. At the bottom of the steep northern hillside a dense forest covers the plains for several miles. To the north-east the path seems to lead to a grandiose white tower. Small bushes and wild grass line the path.
112848: An old cobblestone path makes its way through the Tower Hills, making a sharp turn from the west to the north to avoid some rugged landscape. The stones that were once set with great precision and care, now reflect the passing of time and the elements. Lichen has stained the path a ruddy orange, and several weeds have grown up between the stones.
112849: A large tower rises towards the sky to the north. It is made out of large white and grey stones, giving it an almost glittering quality when the light refracts off the smooth surfaces. A large, sturdy door of oak is set within the southern wall of the tower. An old cobblestone path, thick with vegetation sprouting between the gaps in the stones, leads from the tower through the hills to the south.
112850: Overgrown vegetation reaching several feet high grows here. The plants are of dark green colour and are remarkably untouched by grazing wild life. A bit to the west, the grasslands transform into a flowery bed. A faint trail that might carry travellers makes it way through the green lands to the north.
112851: Judging from the vegetation and lower ground continuing to the north, a stream might have flowed through the plains a long time ago. A few long plants that belong to a body of water give hints about seasonal changes that might resurrect the stream. To the west, elevated plains bear comparatively lusher vegetation.
112852:
A reddish-brown shrub with purplish-pink flowers grows here.
Inside the shrub, there are a cluster of purplish-pink flowers.
A large beautiful rose bush is blooming here.
Deep inside the bush, there is a red rose with leaves and thorny stem.

The air is full of sweet scents and vivid colours fill this flowery meadow. The surrounding grasslands look drab and colourless in comparison to this area. A faint trail can be seen crossing the grasslands to the north, running from west to east.
112853: These plains are several feet higher than the surrounding landscape. A tree grows on the edge of this elevated grassland. Beneath the tree, there are signs of a well-frequented campsite. The nearby grass has been sat on and trampled by animals. Colourful spots in the plains to the north hint that many flowers grow there.
112854: These otherwise flat and uniform plains are punctuated by a few scattered bushes. Many green plants that reach several feet high grow on the land. The flora isn't very colourful, being mostly green with a few yellow flowers peeking through.
112855: Green vegetation continues in every direction as far as the eye can see. The otherwise homogenous landscape is broken up by patches of red and blue. To the south, the plains drop a few feet to softer terrain. Fields to the west give a scene of another descent in the nearby grasslands.
112856: The land rises to the north and falls to the south. This landscape marks the last vestiges of the sloping plains which lie to the west. One cannot see much over the slope to the north, but the sight to south-east verifies that the surrounding plains are rich in plant life and could be a sanctuary to all sorts of animals.
112857: A field with mostly blue, red and yellow wildflowers grows in soil that would hinder any passing traveller. The vegetation seems to love the fertility, stretching close to two feet in height. To the north and west, equally vibrant fields give a sense that this is the typical landscape for miles and miles.
112858: A very flat and lush land, covered with wildflowers and grasses, extends for miles. The thickness and height of vegetation give reason to believe that the soil in which it grows is very fertile. The same fertility seems to continue in the plains to the east and a valley to the west. A land of dense bushes opens up southwards, stretching for many miles.
112859: A wide vista opens up from here. Flowery grasslands lie in the east, lush grasslands stretch to the south and trail runs through the plains to the north and west. A few dense bushes stretch their branches over the grass and could provide shade on a sunny day. Near an especially dense and tall bush, there are footprints made by sandals or shoes, and a heap of charcoal from a campfire.
112860: A faint trail runs east and west through these grasslands. A well-travelled path can be spotted to the north atop a steep cliff. Scattered bushes are visible in the grassy plains which lie to the south. The bushes have missing foliage, suggesting either that they are suffering from some sort of illness or that some beast has been eating their leaves.
112861: The corner of a faint trail continues through the grass to the east and south. The trail sometimes disappears and is indistinguishable from the rest of the plains, making it hard to follow and difficult to work out how frequently it is used. A steep hillside lies to the north, blocking any traveller from climbing.
112862: A route through the grasslands seems to continue to the north-east and south-west directions. The sounds of chirping birds fill the immediate vicinity. A few of the birds fly in and out of the many small bushes, then back to the sky. On the trail, there seems to have been recent activity as indicated by footprints and animal tracks. A magnificent sight of colourful vegetation and bushes opens up to the south.
112863: A narrow dirt track runs through a sea of low grass. It looks like the trail was once wider and more used, but the vegetation is encroaching on both sides of the path, threatening to overgrow it entirely. Despite its proximity to the hills west of here, the land itself is largely flat, rising and dipping only a few feet at a time.
112864: This trail runs through a broad meadow. Different types of grass vie with one another for dominance, some low and coarse, others reaching two feet or more in height. A small sprinkling of white and pale pink flowers add colour to the landscape. The trail is hard-beaten earth in most places, thought in a few it is barely visible beneath the encroaching grass.
112865: A faint dirt track twists back and forth through a series of very low hillocks, extending generally from southwest to northeast. The ground is studded with small rocks and the soil is sandy and poor. Some short, thin grass grows in scattered clumps, but the majority of the plantlife here is thistles and other weeds.
112866:
A small and tough weed grows here.
A sharp-eyed hawk is here stalking some prey.
A small rabbit glares angrily at you.
A black snake, with red markings, is lying here.

This narrow dirt path appears to be old and little used, but it is still quite serviceable for the time being. Grass and weeds are slowly pushing their way across the path, held at bay only by the hard-packed surface. A handful of stunted trees grow to the north, while south of here the ground drops away very suddenly into a green valley.
112867:
A small brown snake is slithering around here.
A small brown snake is slithering around here.

The trail makes a sharp turn here, extending to the east and south. A number of bushes run beside the northwestern side of the trail, becoming denser farther from the trail. On the other side, sickly grass competes with sturdy weeds in the poor soil. The path is not difficult to follow, but it looks like it is not as heavily travelled now as it might once have been.
112868: A small black bird with red markings on its beak is here.

The trail runs close to the edge of a cliff to the east, beyond which a wide green valley extends for miles. The track is poorly defined at some points as tall, thick grass fights to reclaim it, but for now at least it is easy enough to follow. At a few points, the trail vanishes entirely for several feet as it crosses bare grey stone.
112869: Running almost straight from east to west, the trail rises and falls as it crosses folds in the terrain. At times it runs through grass, but just as often it passes across bare rock and becomes very difficult to see until it reenters the vegetation. Scattered bushes stand beside the north side of the trail, as does a clump of a half-dozen maples.
112870: Hills rise to both the north and south, leaving only a narrow stretch of lower terrain between them. The ground is strewn with countless rocks of every size and description, deposited here by ages of erosion. A very faint trail picks its way through the debris, nearly vanishing in spots as it crosses flat stone. Just to the east, the hills are lower and far greener.
112871: A faint path winds around large boulders and dodges gullies and hillsides, maintaining as level a course as it can through the hills. At times the trail is difficult to see, but generally reappears within five or ten yards. There is little to see here in the way of vegetation, but to the north the hills become much greener.
112872: This trail appears to get rather little use, although that can be difficult to judge in areas where it crosses bare rock. Small tufts of grass and scattered weeds nestle between the stones and boulders that lie to either side of the path. A plateau rises to the south and east. The slope to the east is far too steep and bare to scale. The hillside to the south is much gentler, but will still require some skill and effort to ascend.
112873: While generally running due east and west, the trail here has to snake its way back and forth around enormous outcroppings of rock. The stone is banded in layers of orange, brown, and grey, along with a few very thin bands of black. Pale green and white lichen clings to many of the exposed surfaces, while dark moss hides in the shadows.
112880: Although not tall, this hill has steep, uneven slopes that can make travel difficult. None is steeper than the eastern slope, which is a nearly vertical cliff, dropping away into a lower, flatter area. Grass covers most of the hill, except where patches of the underlying stone push their way up above the soil. A few scattered oaks and maples dot the hillsides.
112881:
A small evergreen plant grows here, its woody stems reaching two feet.
A grey wolf is here, snarling aggressively.

The hills are very low here, vanishing entirely after a short cliff just to the east. Short, thick grass covers the hillsides, interspersed with wildflowers in an array of pale blues, pinks, and violets. Several isolated elms, oaks, and alders rise high above the land, casting small islands of shades. The hills continue in every direction but to the east.
112882: Numerous pebbles along with missing leaves from nearby bushes suggest that a local animal track must be close by. Landscapes to the north and west betray a hidden path slithering through the plains. Putting the two together, this path might be a way for hunters to detect and catch wild game that rests on these lands.
112883: These wet grasslands are densely covered in bushes, hindering the passage of travellers. A variety of plants grow in scattered pools of water that lie between bushes. Some of the leaves of bushes and plants are missing, indicating some sort of animal presence. To the south, the density of bushes increases, while to the west a land with only grass fills the view.
112884: A field of bushes, through which travelling might be a troublesome act, continue the pattern of lowlands. The land is wet and even covered with shallow puddles, hinting at frequent rainfall and bushes with lots of foliage providing shade from the sun. There is a strange mixture of plants at the pools of water. To the west, a pond can be spotted in the middle of a valley. To the north, the lowlands continue but the density of bushes seems to decrease.
112885:
A fishing rod has been left here.
A blooming water-lily floats on the surface of the water.
A fat carp swims here.
A bass swims here.
A fat carp swims here.
A fat carp swims here.
A large bee buzzes loudly as it travels from flower to flower.

A very large pond is nestled in the valley, hundreds of yards across in every direction. The water is mostly clear and its bottom sandy, where not covered in thick green weeds. Tiny minnows flash and dart in every direction, while larger fish can sometimes be spotted nosing their way through the vegetation. A few tall willow and elm trees stand scattered around the bank, offering both shade and prime fishing spots.
112886: The land slopes downward as it progresses toward the south, where it opens up into a large green valley. Millions of small stones and tiny chips of rock are embedded in the soil here, creating alternating patches of bare earth and thick weeds. Some small bushes are scattered around the area, but nothing manages to grow taller than a few feet.
112887: The land dips down from the north into a large, fertile valley that extends for miles. The quality of the soil here is clearly demonstrated by the thick growth that covers the landscape. Dark-green grass dominates the area, but thousands of wildflowers thrust up above the grass in clusters of colour that span the full range of the spectrum from white to deep purple.
112888: Low but dense grass fills this portion of the valley, rising only a few inches above the soil but creating a thick, cushioned carpet. In the few places where the soil can be seen, it is nearly black. Some of the grass has been cropped off close to the ground, indicating some grazing animals must pass through here from time to time. The greenery extends in every direction, but is broken up to the south by a large pond.
112889:
A tortoise creeps slowly through the mud.
A duck is here, quacking happily.

The lush grass that surrounds this place grows even taller and thicker here, hiding the muddy soil that lies beneath. The dense vegetation provides ample footing and there is no threat of sinking into the muck. The water appears to be rising out of the ground itself, as there is no sign of a stream. Further to the south, the grass is replaced by reeds.
112890: A large bee buzzes loudly as it travels from flower to flower.

Short, thick grass covers most of the land, though there are many small stony patches and large rocks punctuating the greenery. The land rises and dips in small waves, gradually dropping as it flows toward the east. Hundreds of yellow flowers dot the grass and add variety to the scenery. A low wall of natural rock rises to the west, while the smell of rotting vegetation drifts in from the south.
112891: Thick greenery extends on every side. In many places, it is broad-bladed grass of medium height, rising a foot or two above the ground. However, there are also several small cultivated fields here planted with wheat, oats, barley, and various other crops. A narrow line of trampled grass leads west, not broad enough to be a true trail but clearly often used, while a large pond can be seen to the east.
112892: This valley extends for miles in every direction but west, where it ends quite suddenly at a tall cliff. Thick green grass rises two to three feet here in many spots, but in several places wide meadows have been flattened by swirling winds, creating intricate patterns of grass crushed low to the ground. Half a dozen short maples rise above the fields, standing as isolated islands in a sea of green.
112893:
A duck is here, quacking happily.
A large ram guards his flock of sheep.
A woolly sheep is grazing here.

Thick emerald grass fills the floor of the valley here, growing as much as three feet high in some spots. The blades dip and sway in even the slightest wind, as if dancing to some unheard musicians. Only a few tall wildflowers manage to rise above the grass, their white and yellow blossoms showing up in sharp contrast to the green. Sheer cliffs border the valley to the north and west.
112894: A heron is stalking the area, looking for fish.

A mixture of tall sedge grass and broad reeds dominate this area. The land is submerged in most spots by an inch or two of standing water, and the soil below is thick mud. Mats of crushed and dead vegetation allow adequate footing with no fear of sinking. At most times, there is no sound but the whispering breeze and the dull hum of invisible insects.
112895: A swarm of mosquitoes is here, humming around you.

Short, thick-bladed grass struggles to survive in this drenched area, vying for space with tall reeds and cattails. Every depression in the ground is filled with brown, silt-laden water. A few stunted trees cling to life, but many more have fallen and their rotting trunks sport a colourful array of fungi. A short cliff rises over the area to the west.
112896:
A long-stemmed plant that branches into many bright yellow flowers grows here.
A water moccasin slithers out of sight just below the surface of the water.
A swarm of mosquitoes is here, humming around you.
A grey snake slides along the water.

Many trees once grew here, but most have succombed to the ravages of flooding. While some twisted willow and cypress trees still rise above the land, many others lie rotting, sporting dozens of species of puffballs, bracket fungi, and mushrooms. The ground is entirely saturated, and only a few winding paths of thick grass and reeds allows any passage here. A short cliff rises to the west.
112897: A grey snake slides along the water (hidden).

Large stretches of shallow, stinking water dominate the area, interspersed with paths and islands of thick, clinging mud. Only those plants able to survive the perpetual flooding of this land grow here, but they are thriving in the dense, nutrient-rich soil. Hundreds of wildflowers dot the otherwise drab landscape. The swamp grows deeper and impassable to the south and east.
112898: This valley is bordered on the west and south by high cliffs of dark grey stone. The valley extends to the north, growing narrower as it goes. Next to the cliffs there are low mounds of boulders and scree, with very little growing there other than a little moss. Further out, grass dominates the floor of the valley. A faint path leads north to a small village.
112899: A well-crafted white fountain is here, water pouring forth from it.

Too narrow and faint to be a true road, this trail leads its way through the valley floor and runs north into a very small village. The trail is bordered on both sides by white stones, and a multicoloured row of flowers has been planted along the western edge as well. A small but carefully constructed wooden house stands a few yards off the trail to the east.
112900: A narrow trail runs in from the south and forms into a broad loop here in the centre of a very small village. There are only a few houses in the entire village, along with a single barn that stands to the north. The largest of the houses stands to the west. A single tall elm dominates the centre of the area, with a couple of narrow benches set up in its shade.
112901:
A dirty shovel is lying on the ground here.
A dented pail has been carelessly left here.
A sturdy pack horse is standing here.
A brown cow is here, contemplating a higher reality whilst chewing slowly.
A well-fed cow stands here chewing her cud listlessly.

This large barn is entirely open on its southern side, with a large doorway but no doors. Stalls line the eastern wall of the building, while a pile of hay that rises more than ten feet high lines most of the western wall, leaving only enough space for one rack of farming tools and another with tack for horses. This barn seems to serve the needs of the whole community.
112902: A roe deer is standing here, watching the terrain while chewing the vegetation.

This level expanse is covered almost entirely in grass. Most of the growth is only six to eight inches high, but a different species of taller blades grows scattered among the rest, reaching two feet or more in height. In a few spots patches of grey stone thrust their way up through the growth. To the east and south, the plateau drops off into a deep green valley.
112903:
A snake slithers towards you.
A restless rabbit bounces around.

This ridgeline flattens out as it extends to the north, while narrowing to the south. Thick grass covers a large portion of the ridge, although in many places brown and orange rock is visible where there is no soil. A scattering of pale blue and purple flowers add a splash of variety to the greenery. A tall plateau rises to the west in a sheer cliff of dark grey stone.
112920:
A small, dense tangle of roots covers the ground.
A rabid raccoon stands here, frothing at the mouth.

These hills rise and fall without pattern, creating a maze of valleys between them. Weeds and shrubs have taken root in the lower reaches of the hillsides, but most of the hilltops are bare rock, sporting only small tufts of grass and a few stunted trees with tangled roots clingig to the stone. The trees grow taller and become more common to both the west and north.
112921: Firs, aspens, and a few yews dot the hilltop, rising high above the short, dark grass that covers most of the area. In their shade there is less growth, but abundant piles of dead branches, leaves, and needles that might provide shelter for many small animals. To the south and east, the hill drops away sharply in a hundred narrow channels eroded into the rock, giving it the appearance of a pleated green dress.
112922: The elongated shape of a stoat can be seen darting across the terrain.

Enormous cracks riddle the hills, exposing layers of folded rock in a myriad of colours. The rock in the cracks is much less weathered than the rest of the hills. While many of the crevices are deep, most are narrow and do not extend very far in any direction, so it is not difficult to avoid them. Little grows on the hills, leaving them dull grey and brown.
112923:
A field mouse noses about hungrily, searching for food.
A field mouse noses about hungrily, searching for food.

The ground has been buckled by earthquakes or some other incredible force, creating sharp folds. Shattered remains of enormous boulders litter the ground, their edges dulled by ages of rain and wind. While rocks dominate the broken landscape, a large number of durable weeds have taken hold in the scant soil, producing patches of green amid the brown and grey stone.
112926:
A snake slithers towards you.
A small rat runs about, oblivious to your presence.

Steep slopes descend on every side from this low hilltop except to the east, where the hillside rises at a very sharp angle, forming an impassable cliff. There is more soil here than on many of the hills, allowing a profusion of wildflowers to bloom: purplish-pink catchfly, orange hawkweed, blue milkwort, and dozens of other species in a myriad of colours.
112928: A wild bull seems ready to charge you.

Rocky slopes rise on every side of this valley, nestled deep into the Tower Hills. Loose stones litter the hillsides and leave little room for grass and weeds, but a great deal of moss grows in the shadows of larger boulders. There are several dry gullies leading into the valley, but except during the wettest seasons there is no sign of water.
112929: Steep slopes rise and fall on every side, created by folds in the underlying stone. Thin soil clings to the slopes, providing just enough nourishment for thin, yellowish grass and a few stunted bushes. Pale grey and orange boulders thrust through the soil. Just to the south, the hills descend into a deep valley.
112930: The Tower Hills, called Emyn Beraid in the tongue of the elves, rise and fall in every direction. The hills are rocky and steep-sided, with extensive areas of exposed rock and little clinging vegetation. A few scrapes on the rocks and abandoned nests left in nooks and cracks attest to the periodic presence of wildlife here.
112931: This nook is located below high ridgelines and cliffs in all directions except the south. Being such a protected area from the wind and elements has allowed heavy brush, grasses, and even the occasional tree to flurish here. Along with the growth here, signs of animals can be seen in the passages through the brush and grass.
112939: A small rat runs about, oblivious to your presence.

This hilltop rises higher than most, even among the Tower Hills. While it is possible to see a great distance in any direction from here, the folded and broken nature of the surrounding hills make it impossible to use this spot as an effective vantage point. The hill drops slightly and flattens out to the south, where an area dominated by grass rather than rocks is visible.
112940: This hilltop is almost entirely flat, curving downward only slightly to the west and east until it suddenly falls away in sharp cliffs. A deep layer of soil has managed to accumulate here, and now supports a dense carpet of low, coarse grass. A few pale-yellow oxlips and white orchids rise above the grass. A faint path vanishes to the north, but becomes more distinct to the south.
112942: The hills here are nestled against a tall ridgeline that borders them to both the north and east. Steep, barren slopes rise to meet the ridge, but while they are not vertical, they are too smooth to allow an ascent. The bases of the slopes are heaped with scree and boulders that have broken loose from the ridge and come to rest here.
