112943: Deep folds in the ground create sharp ridgelines of bare rock and shadowy valleys filled with twisted shrubs and sparse but rugged grass. Ages of fallen leaves and dead grass decay on the ground, producing more fertile soil than is commonly found in this area. A taller hill dominates the view to the south.
112944: A barren cliff rises to the east until it becomes a tall ridgeline, standing sentinel over the Tower Hills. The cliff blocks any sunlight from ever reaching this place before noon, and the sparse vegetation that does survive here tends to grow on the western-facing hillsides. In the shadows, pale green and white lichen clings to the rocks.
112945: A tall ridge rises to the east and north, its sides too steep to ascend. Loose scree covers the base of the ridge, broken fragments of stone fallen over the ages from above. A few wildflowers spring up from cracks in the rocky ground, fighting for nourishment and adding a splash of colour to an otherwise mostly grey landscape.
112946: A mountain goat is here, jumping from cliff to cliff.

A narrow ridgeline begins here, rising as it proceeds further to the north. The slopes on either side are not too steep at the base, but they become far more vertical as the ridge rises. The eastern slope of the ridge is much gentler and a layer of soil has managed to accumulate there, providing a foothold for thin, pale grass. The steeper western slope is bare of soil, leaving the grey stone of the hills exposed.
112947: The hills are flatter here than those nearby, and have developed a thicker layer of soil. Grass and wildflowers grow in abundance and thrive on the rich nutrients. Hundreds of isolated trees dot the hillsides, from a few short and twisted junipers to tall oaks and yews. A low ridge stands just to the west, descending as it extends southward.
112948: Blackthorns, birches, maples, and a number of other types of trees grow in large numbers on these hills, yet they tend to be separated from one another and form only occasional groves, never a forest. Between the trees, grass has taken hold in most places, giving way only in those areas where bare stone pushes up through the surface.
112949: The hills come to an abrupt end here, dropping away in tall, vertical cliffs to the south and east. Saxifrage and mountain avens cling to the rocky sides, but nothing else has managed to take hold. The hilltop itself is nearly flat and forms a small plateau coated in moss, grass, and a few small wildflowers. The northern and western slopes are much gentler and lead into rolling hills.
112950: Short, thin-bladed grass covers most of the hillside, interspersed in many places by large stones and boulders. A scattering of purple and red wildflowers dot the hillside among the grass. Dozens of trees have managed to find root here as well, most of them elm or hawthorn, along with a few rowans. A tall, steep rock wall rises to the west, leading up to a ridgeline far above.
112951:
A giant, mean looking earth beetle is sleeping here.
A porcupine is waddling around here, its tail full of sharp quills.

This hill is by no means small, but it is dwarfed by the high stony ridge that runs just to the west. Much of the hillside is covered with boulders and loose rocks of every size, but in many places grass, shrubs, and even a few trees have managed to take root. Most of the boulders are rounded with age and coated with moss, but a few have sharp, broken edges, indicating that rockfalls are still a possibility here.
112952: Low Hill in the Shadow of a Ridge

A rabbit is here eyeing your presence warily.
A badger is here, exploring for food.

This hill is overshadowed and in the lee of the high hills to the west and the north. This protected environment has allowed many shrubs, grass, and trees to thrive. Near the rising slopes, boulders and broken rocks lie where they came to rest as they rolled or fell from higher ground in ages past.
112953: The hills here can barely be called hills, and the narrow breaks between them are hardly valleys. This mostly flat landscape is covered in various forms of vegetation from the grasses and weeds on the hilltops to the bushes and occasional trees that dot the areas between them.
112954:
A small cluster of clover grows here.
A badger is here, exploring for food.

The large, rolling hills in the distance to the north-west have gradually shrunk into small rolling mounds here that are easy to walk up and down. A multitude of grasses, shrubs, and weeds have found a place to thrive in the mostly dirt covered ground. The occasional break where bedrock pokes through the surface here is evidence of years and years of wind and erosion. To the west, a sheer rocky bluff rises to the heights far above while to the east a sheer drop off overlooks a dry gulch that splits the hills.
112955: A large marmot is here, scurrying in between the rocks.

A shattered hilltop lies strewn about the area. It is not clear what caused the hill here to be broken into the large boulders and rocky scree that cover the ground for quite some distance, but the large cliffs to the south-west show signs of large chunks having been dislodged over the years. The impact of such large stones would have caused some damage, as would the wind that appears to be funnelled this way from the towering hillside and any up-drafts that come from the rocky gulch to the east.
112956: Crumbling Hillock at the Edge of a Gulch
A large marmot is here, scurrying in between the rocks.

The small mounds that extend from the west and south come to an abrupt halt at the edge of a gulch that lies below. While the rocky hills that cover the area have shown that they are more than capable of withstanding the eons of weather that have played against them, here is proof that they are not impervious and can eventually be broken down. At the edge of the gulch, the hillock shows signs of slow deteriation that will eventually claim more of the exposed rocky hilltop that can be seen here. The exposed and crumbling rocky area here is interspersed with tufts of grass, standing in stark contrast to the abundent vegetation that can be seen to the south.
112957: A tall stag is here, grazing peacefully.

The hills here have no vegetation or soil. They are formed from solid bedrock, and have been polished smooth by the elements. Only in the small valleys between the hills where dirt and soil cover the rock can signs of vegetation be found, struggling to survive the harsh environment.
112958:
A clear spring babbles as cool water trickles out of the ground.
A stocky mountain mule is here, waiting to serve.
A sturdy pack horse is standing here.
A restless rabbit bounces around.

Rough, rocky hills continue to the west, the north, and the south. A sheltered campsite has been established here; a small spring bubbles up from between the rocks, and the surrounding grey boulders provide protection from wind and rain. The campsite is also well hidden from view. To the east there is a sudden break in the terrain where a gulch has formed. Closer to the edge of the cliff, the terrain becomes increasingly broken and rocky.
112959: The terrain on these high hills is rough and rocky. Some grass and bushes still find enough soil to take root. There is a steep drop to the north with grass-covered hills at its foot. To the west, the hills become increasingly covered with vegetation, while the rocky terrain continues to the east and the south.
112960: Natural Vantage Point on a Hill Overlooking the Trail
A slightly rusted casserole lies here.

This rocky hilltop stands taller than the surrounding lands. Its northern and westerns slopes descend abruptly, allowing an unhindered view for anyone wanting to watch and observe the landscape. Below the steep hillsides, a trail can be seen as it winds its way through the hilly terrain. Towards the south and east, the terrain slopes gently down. Colourful flowers dot the thick grass that covers the nearby hills and valleys.
112961: These hills are bare and barren. The bedrock is exposed and worn smooth by weather and wind. The little vegetation that grows here is mostly made up of spindly bushes clustered around rare cracks in the rock, where soil and water get trapped.
112962: The otherwise rolling hills are flatter here, especially to the north, where a trail cuts through them running east and west. The hills that roll onward in all other directions are still negotiable with limited effort, with the exception of several large, thorny bushes that may require a slight detour to the left or right. The land ascends to the south, eventually entering rockier and more difficult terrain.
112963: A series of low, brush-covered hills makes up this part of the Tower Hills. To the north a winding trail crosses the hills. Even though the hills vary in height, they are easily traversable by any reasonably healthy traveller. To the south, a higher hill rises above the landscape.
112964: The terrain here is hilly, and there is a gradual upward slope to the south. Far to the south-east, a high ridge dominates the sky-line. A few grasses and shrubs have managed to take root in the rocky soil, whilst in other areas the soil has been swept away by weather and wind, and the bedrock lies bare.
112965: A tree-snake lies wrapped around one of the tree branches.

These hills are not tall, rising and falling only a little as they roll on in every direction, yet they still have steep slopes in many spots. There is not much grass here, but in its place grow wide swaths of brownish-yellow flowers and a few low shrubs. A number of oaks, willows, and maples grow on the hills as well, but are not thick enough at any point to be a true forest.
112966:
A large shrub grows here, its branches loosely spreading.
On the shrub, there are two piles of cherries.

Dozens of small ridges descend from each of the low hilltops here, creating an array of very narrow valleys between them. Nearly the entire landscape is covered in various types of grasses and weeds, along with a number of short bushes. There are some bare patches of stone-laden dirt that stand out in stark brown contrast to the green hillsides.
112967: Hundreds of trees once stood on this hilltop, but nearly all of them are now gone. It appears that a tremendous storm lashed its way through here five or ten years ago, knocking down all but a few of the trees. Their trunks now lie rotting on the ground. Many saplings push their way up through the grass, but it will take years before they reclaim the area.
112968: A grey wolf is here, snarling aggressively.

Most of this hillside is covered with green weeds and grass, but in several places small patches of pinkish-purple heather have become dominant. There are also a number of low privet and witchhazel shrubs growing in scattered masses. The hillside slopes downward toward the south, becoming almost vertical at its base.
112969:
A sturdy bed made from solid oak lies here, covered in warm blankets.
An elven boy is running about here.
An elven woman is here merrily walking along.

This house is not very large, but it is by no means cramped. The residents have kept their furniture to a minimum, leaving as much free room as possible. The walls are made from a light golden-brown wood that bears a glassy finish which helps brighten the room. A small stove sits against the east wall, while a large rug fills the centre of the room.
112970: This house is significantly larger than the others in the small village, and is the only one with more than a single room. The main room contains a couple of narrow beds along with a small table and several chairs. Shelves line the walls and bear a large number of carved wooden figurines. A wide doorway stands in the north wall, leading further into the house.
112971:
A sack of flour has been placed here.
A pan is here, ready for use.
A stove stands against one wall here.
An elven cook is standing here, busy cooking meals.

This kitchen is both spacious and well-apportioned. A dazzling display of pots and pans hang from hooks along the walls. In addition to a large fireplace, there is also a stove. A sink and hand-pump stand beneath a broad window that allows light and fresh air to enter. There is a single long counter extending for over eight feet against the north wall.
112972:
Some curdled goats milk sits inside a cheese mould.
Some curdled goats milk sits inside a cheese mould.

This room has been carefully excavated beneath the kitchen. The floor is bare dirt covered with a thick layer of sand, while the walls are constructed of small blocks of stone. Wooden racks line most of the walls, some designed for holding bottles of wine, others for supporting general foodstuffs. There are also several bins for holding grain and vegetables.
112973: A black snake hurries towards you with sly intentions.

This enormous flat hilltop extends in every direction except to the north, where a steep slope descends to a lower set of hills. The land here is almost bare of vegetation, leaving the native stone of the hill exposed. Ages of wind and rain have smoothed the rock, erasing every sharp edge. Other than a few weeds growing in cracks in the plateau, nothing grows here.
112974: A black snake hurries towards you with sly intentions.

This flat hilltop extends to the south and east, but drops off sharply in the other directions. Short, coarse grass is interspersed with patches of bare grey stone. A few stunted cedars have managed to take hold here, their trunks bent away from the prevaling western wind that frequently pushes its way across this plateau.
112975: A grey bird with a bright orange-red belly sits here, singing a melodic tune.

Very little is able to grow on this exposed hilltop. Despite the flat surface, no soil has accumulated here, apparently being scoured away by rain and wind before any plants have time to take root. In most places the bare stone of the hill is visible, but in some places it is coated with a thin layer of pale blue lichen. A few small patches of bright green moss adorn the stone as well.
112976: A large brown snake with black patches is coiled here.

The plateau is not entirely flat here, sloping downward as it extends an arm north into the eastern edge of the Tower Hills. However, the edges of the plateau fall away in steep cliffs long before the slope can reach the ground below. It would be impossible to safely descend any of the cliffs, leaving the south as the only direction to leave this place.
112977: The plateau ends here in a rounded corner. Vertical cliffs fall away to the east, where a lower plateau covered in thick grass can be seen, and to the south, where a road runs through a very low set of hills. The ground has been smoothed by ages of wind and rain, yet it is still very uneven in many places.
112978: This plateau extends for a couple of miles in every direction but to the south. There, it drops off in a sheer cliff of more than four hundred feet. From the edge it is possible to make out a road running east and west near the cliff's base, but a line of trees beside the road make it difficult to observe. Beyond the road is a shorter set of hills.
112979: Concealed Observation Post upon a Plateau

A scuffed and worn leather satchel has been left here.
A young ruffian is here, keeping a careful watch over the road.
A young ruffian is here, keeping a careful watch over the road.

The plateau ends abruptly in a rounded corner here, with steep cliffs dropping off to both the south and west. The ground is level and carpeted with a dense layer of short, dark-green grass. This spot provides an excellent view of the road that runs near the base of the plateau, and from trampled patches in the grass and a small lean-to built back from the edge, out of sight of the road, it may often be used for exactly that purpose.
112980: This ridge in the Tower Hills rises as it extends to the north, while dropping off to the south. Very little vegetation manages to cling to the bare rocks, with only a few tufts of grass and weeds springing up from cracks in the stone. The sides of the ridge are very steep and smooth, their grey stone providing no footholds to allow a safe descent.
112981: The flat portion of the ridgeline is very wide here, easily spanning a hundred feet or more. While it does tilt slightly downward toward the east, the ridge is level enough to allow travel without unusual difficulty. Very little grows on the rocky surface of the ridge beyond a few tufts of grass, yet somehow several small pine trees have managed to take root and thrive here.
112982: A narrow ridgeline ends abruptly here as it butts up against a higher ridge to the north and west. The ridge forms a wide, nearly flat shelf, rising only gradually to the south. The ground is littered with stones that have split off from the higher rock walls, ranging in size from pebbles to enormous boulders. Sparse grass and a few low shrubs are the only vegetation.
112983: A mountain goat is here, jumping from cliff to cliff.

The ridge here is wide and mostly flat on top, though it does fall away quickly to either side. The ridgeline is bare of any soil or vegetation, exposing the medium grey stone that forms the hill. The ridge narrows as it continues to the north, while as it moves south it bends to the east and begins to descend.
112984: A small brown snake is slithering around here.

This thin ridgeline runs almost directly north and south, remaining level for most of the way. There is little room to manoeuvre from side to side, but no difficulty in moving along the ridge. Steep, barren hillsides of grey stone fall away to either side, both of them being too sheer and smooth to allow any chance of travel in those directions.
112985: As ridges from the east, west, and south come together, they form a small plateau. The ground here is mostly flat, with nothing but the occasional boulder or clumps of tough weeds braving the exposed terrain. Far to the east, the hills gradually disappears to give way to green fields and forests.
112986:
A small oaken table has been set here.
On the table, there is a bowl of gruel.
A solitary hermit is sitting here, meditating with a serene expression.

This cave extends back only twenty feet or so from its mouth, yet that appears to be more than sufficient for its inhabitant. There are very few furnishings to be seen. A low wooden table sits against one wall, while a woven straw mat lies on the floor by the other. A small scorched area at the opening of the cave attests to frequent fires built there. Clean, dry sand coats the floor.
112987: A gently sloping ridge descends from rugged highlands to the east, linking them with a flat hilltop to the north. The ridge is covered with grass and small bushes; some large boulders on the western slope are overgrown with moss.
112988: A ridgeline descends from the west and bends sharply to the north where it meets a wide hilltop. While this area is traversable, the ridge is narrow and the terrain rough. The sides of the ridge fall away in steep descents covered in loose rocks and scree.
112989: A massive hilltop sits here with ridgelines extending, like spokes on a wheel, to the west and south. To the north, east, and west the hills and ridges continue on a mostly flat trajectory. To the south, a climbing ridgeline ascends higher into the Tower Hills. A few small bushes and tufts of grass have found cracks to take root in, otherwise the hill is mostly bare rock.
112990: Bluffs to the north, the east, and the south marks the end of a wide hilltop. The land below is dotted with small rolling hills. To the southwest a peak towers over the surrounding landscape, and it appears to be the highest point in this region of the Tower Hills.
112991:
A large marmot is here, scurrying in between the rocks.
A restless rabbit bounces around.

A narrow shelf connects the areas to the east and west of here as it runs along the north side of a high cliff face. The rock wall to the south is a near vertical drop with no signs of anything to hold on to. No vegetation grows on the shelf aside from a couple of struggling, miserable weeds.
112992: This large plateau appears to have once been a large hill, but time has eroded away the top. It also serves as a crossroad of sorts for the lines of hills that run in all directions. The ground slopes gradually down to lowlands to the north and west, while lines of hills rise to the south and east.
112993: A small brown snake is slithering around here.

A rocky ledge has formed here as hills from the north rise up and then flatten out as they run to the east. A sharp ledge sits to the south and an enclosed area can be seen down below. Eastward, the hills and ridgelines continue to climb toward a high peak.
112994: The hills that form this area rises to the south-east. To the north, the hills run together to form a small ridgeline that descends from the higher ground. As the hills continue to climb to the south-east they approach the crown of the large hill. Some grass covers the ground and the occasional lonely bush can be seen as well.
112995: The hills narrow to form a ridgeline that connects the lower hills to the north, to the high area to the south. The terrain to the south-east of here continues to rise to a high peak that can be seen in the distance. The ridgeline is covered by rocks and boulders, making it difficult, but still possible to navigate. While it is not very wide, it is safe as long as one continues to follow it. There is no way to descend from here to the east or west.
112996: A narrow ridge rises to form a promontory overlooking the rolling hills below. The hillside is uneven and shows signs of cracking near the edge, and fallen rocks litter the ground below. Vegetation is sparse, but some grass and brush help hold the soil together and thus slow the deterioration at the edge of the cliffs.
112998: The hills that continue onward to the north and east come to a halt against the towering cliffs that lie to the west and south. The cliffs provide shelter from most of the elements, allowing brush, grasses, and the occasional stunted tree to flourish here. Boulders and rocky debris cover the vegetation in some areas where it has fallen from the heights above. There is a looming tunnel entrance to the south.
112999: Tall hills rise against the southern skyline, while the smaller, rolling hills to the north and east are lower. While the hills are possible to traverse, caution may be required as loose rocks and scree cover some slopes. The occasional patch of grass, shrub, and even a few lonely trees dot the surrounding landscape.
113000: Hill in the Shadow of a Peak

A small brown snake is slithering around here.
A tall stag is here, grazing peacefully.

The smaller hills in this region of the Tower Hills lie in the shadow of a large peak to the south. The steep southern cliffs are rugged and cracked, and the ground beneath them is covered in fallen rocks. Elsewhere the hills are covered with grass, brush, and weeds.
113001: The vertical walls surrounding this deadend to the east, south and west leave no means to move in those directions. An expanse of rolling hills stretch outwards to the north, with no end in sight. The ground here is littered with scree and boulders, possibly from landslides though there are moss and weeds growing on them.
113002:
A clear spring babbles as cool water trickles out of the ground.
A tall stag is here, grazing peacefully.

The rocky hills to the north form a barrier from the harsh northern winds that would otherwise sweep across this area. Grass and bushes seem to find the shelter agreeable, and a wide flora of plants grow here. To the west and south, the hills suddenly terminate as they run up against steep, towering cliffs. The hills continue to the east, undulating gently. there are some animal paths leading in and out of this area, and a small spring bubbles up in the middle of this protected part of the Tower Hills, making it an ideal resting spot.
113003: Hundreds of trees stand on these hills, making it difficult to see too far in any single direction. None of them are particularly tall, with only a single tall oak rising above thirty feet. The trees are mostly isolated from one another, with only a couple of denser clumps. Low grass surrounds them, except where creases of bare stone break their way through the soil.
113004: A rabid rabbit is here, frothing at the mouth.

These gently rolling hills are covered in a thin layer of grass, interspersed with chickweed, sowthistles, stinging nettles, and other varieties of weeds. A few low bushes and trees also dot the landscape, most growing in isolation from one another. The greenery is broken by sheer walls of rock in many places, none of them very wide or rising more than a dozen feet or so.
113005:
A rabbit is here eyeing your presence warily.
A rabbit is here eyeing your presence warily.

Scattered trees dot almost every small hill that can be seen from here. The trees appear to get thicker to the south where they form occasional copses. Some areas show scattered weeds and scrub brush, while others show the dirt having been completely blown away down to the bedrock underneath.
113006: Several of the hills in this region of the Tower Hills bear scars in the form of cracks and fissures. While mostly shallow, care must still be taken when travelling across the broken landscape. Weeds, grass and small bushes seem to find the conditions here agreeable.
113007: A colourful butterfly is fluttering around here.

Centuries of erosion have reduced this region to what would more adequately be called an elevated field. Wide, grass-covered mounds are all that remains of what were once towering hills, at least if the surrounding landscape is an indication of what this area once looked like. The hills become increasingly bare towards the west. The exposed bedrock in that direction shows signs of cracks and fissures.
113008: A small cluster of clover grows here.

Rows of low, rugged hills make up this area of the Tower Hills. Most of them are covered in sparse vegetation, green and yellow wildgrass and some small bushes. In contrast, the meadow to the south at the foot of the hills, is vividly green with a multitude of colourful flowers.
113009: The hills overlook a small rocky footpath to the east and a wider, but badly overgrown trail in the south. The ground is covered with rocks of varying shapes and sizes. Small green and brown creeping vines climb up the larger boulders, as if a natural net had been cast upon the surface of the stone.
113010: A tree-snake lies wrapped around one of the tree branches.

Thick branches spread out in every direction from the trunk, many wide enough to walk on without danger. Thousands of thinner branches and twigs create a thick lacework of wood and leaves, blocking out any view of the land beyond. A few tattered fragments of snakeskin hang from some of the branches.
113012: These hills, low with gentle slopes, are covered in scrub brush and grass. The hills expand to the east and south while a deep gulch scars the land to the west. Towards the south the land become increasingly rocky, and features fissures, cracks, and steep cliffs. A rising ridge to the north follows the eastern side of the gulch.
113013: A narrow strip of land runs along a sheer drop to the north and west. Down below, a dry gulch can be seen running to the north and south with a small side passage directly to the north. As the ridge continues to the east from here, it climbs upward gently. A thin layer of top soil covers the ground allowing grass and small bushes to grow.
113014: This meandering ridgeline is covered with loose rocks and small bushes. It makes a wide north-to-west bend around a deep gulch. The bottom of the gulch is a distant grey-yellow smear of stones and boulders atleast a hundred feet below the ridge.
113015: In the absence of trees, these hills are dominated by dense, green bushes. From atop the tallest hill the view stretches for miles across hills to the south and east. An impenetrable wall of dense bushes, dozens of yards across, separates the hills from a steep ridge to the north.
113016: Hills rise and fall, some small and others large. Some have steep sides covered in scree and rocks, while others are overgrown with grass and bushes. A tower stands on a hill to the north-east, a white pillar rising a hundred feet or more above the Tower Hills.
113017: The ground here is mostly devoid of greenery, though a few valiant shrubs and bushes endure the almost desolate landscape. To the north, a prominent hill with very steep sides rises up blocking travel in that direction. The ground slopes somewhat to the east, leading down to a small dirt path.
113018: This rolling meadow rises and falls in low, uneven folds. Two species of grass grow here. One is shorter, with broad, dark blades. The other is taller, thinner, and paler. Flowers in every imaginable colour are scattered across the meadow, in many places crowding out the grass entirely. Tall hills rise to both the north and west, while south of here the ground remains level but grows rockier.
113019:
A large, sturdy table made from oak is sitting here.
On the table, there are a quill pen and a piece of paper.

The floor and walls are made of polished stone in various shades of white and grey. A frayed, red carpet covers the centre of the room from the entrance towards a large, spiral staircase at the opposite end. On the eastern edge of the room stands a large and sturdy wooden table. A black, dusty, iron-wrought candelabra hangs high above, affixed firmly to the apex of the ceiling.
113020: Halfway up the wide staircase, a minstrel's gallery has been built overlooking the main hall. If grand feasts were held below, the musicians might have gathered here to play for the guests. The ominous creaking and groaning that now comes from the wooden platform suggests that it hasn't aged all that well. Wide stone steps lead up through a hatch to the bastion of the tower, or back down to the main hall.
113021: A stove stands against one wall here.

Once filled with the scents and sounds of a busy kitchen, this wide room now stands cold and silent. All items of value that weren't too heavy to move have been stripped out, leaving only the cold flagstones and an old, rusty stove. Above the stove hangs a line of pegs that kept the tools of the trade within easy reach of the cooks. A wide stone staircase leads upwards from the centre of the room, next to which sits two massive iron cauldrons. Towards the back of the kitchen, a long, dark corridor stretches out into the distance.
113022: A patch of moss grows here on a wet, flat stone.

This rather narrow passage is comprised of smooth, grey stone walls. A thick layer of green, slimey lichen clings to the walls where moisture has seeped through the cracks. Upon the floor lies broken pieces of pottery, stained different colours from the various seasonings they once likely held. To the east, the remnants of an old, disused kitchen can be seen, while to the west the dank corridor continues until it is swallowed up in darkness.
113023: This corridor is constructed of large square blocks of grey stone. The corridor leads into a room to the north and continues to the east, where the end is hidden in darkness. Dust lies in a thick layer on the floor. There are footprints in the dust which have clearly been disturbed several times recently. There are iron torch holders set in the wall at even intervals, now covered in flaking red-brown rust.
113024: A narrow, stone corridor is lined with empty torch holders that once lit this passage. Trickles of water run down the walls where cracks in the limestone have not been repaired. A steady stream of cool air flows through cracks in the western wall, the outline of which slightly resembles the frame of a door.
113025: A small rat runs about, oblivious to your presence.

Here the corridor turns and opens out from the narrow corridor to the north to a large room to the east. Polished stones with deep grooves worn into the floor underneath the dust show that, in the past, heavy items have been dragged through here. The walls are composed of large square blocks of smooth grey stone.
113026:
A little stone lies on the ground.
A sturdy peg for hanging armour from is on the wall.
On the peg, there is a black pair of padded boots.
A weapons rack stands against the wall.
In the rack is a handaxe.

This room was apparently an armoury at one time. Racks, hooks, and pegs that line the wall seem to have been made to hold various types of arms and armour but now stand empty, save for thick layers of dust collected during years of neglect. In the southern corner, a pile of storage chests have collapsed, their contents lost beneath a layer of rubble.
113027:
A hammer lies on the ground.
A pair of tongs lie on the ground.
An ancient, black anvil covered in a thick layer of dust sits in the centre of the room.

This room appears to have been used as a smithy once, with a furnace located deep within the basement to spread heat up through the tower. Blackened markings on the walls and crumbled stone indicate the intense heat the furnace produced. Amongst the recognisable remains in the room are an anvil and a selection of hammers and tongs.
113029:
A large cabinet capable of storing goods is here.
A large cabinet capable of storing goods is here.
In the cabinet, there are a cup and a woollen traveller's cloak.

This room is well constructed. The walls are of square, grey stones and fixed in place with mortar. The floor is very even and made of large, flat slabs of the same grey stone as the walls. The ceiling is arched and there is not a crack to be seen even though the room does not seem to have been in use for a long time. Numerous dusty shelves of sturdy wood line the walls and two large cabinets gape empty.
113030: High above the surrounding lands, this turret provides a bird's eye view of the neighbouring countryside. A tall parapet made of hard, grey rock provides the watchers with protection from any missiles that might be fired at them. To the south, an old cobblestone path leads to and from the tower along a rocky escarpment. To the east, a shimmering creek weaves its way through the grasslands like a silvery thread upon a lush green blanket.
113031: A falchion lies on the ground.

This room is plain, verging on the austere; the occupant obviously valued function over comfort and had no time for ornamentation of any sort. Facing the door is a battered but serviceable oak desk, the drawers stuffed with crumbling parchment. The few remaining legible scraps indicate that the scrolls were military maps of the area. A long rack set into the northern wall held pegs from which various weapons were hung, ready to be issued should the tower come under attack.
113032: An old, one-eyed black wolf is here, foraging for prey.

Bigger than any cave that an animal could have dug out, this den must be natural. Hard, dark earth composes the walls, floor, and ceiling of this dwelling. Numerous roots hang down from the roof near the back of the cave, some so long in length they reach the floor several feet below. Tufts of white, silvery fur lie scattered upon the ground.
113034: Fractured pieces of stone have come to a rest on the barren ground. Small lizards and other tiny creatures scurry about the broken rocks. To sustain the little life that is found here a water source must be nearby. The canyon walls continue to rise up to the north and south leaving only the east-west path along the floor of the canyon.
113035: A tiny, harmless centipede is here.

Several loose rocks have worked free from a large cleft in the wall of the canyon and now lie scattered about the foot of the fissure. No vegetation can grow in the desolate bedrock that makes up the canyon floor. Shale rocks lining the edge of the crack provide handholds that would allow a climber to reach the wider ledges further up and, eventually, provide a way out of the canyon.
113036:
A pile of broken timber and scrap iron lies here, the remains of a destroyed wagon.
A shallow pond is here, tinted green with algae.

The expansive shale canyon comes to an end. Multiple varieties of weeds spring up around a small pool. Small animals scatter under the rocks away from the water when the slightest of disturbances occur in the surroundings. The only way out is to the east with the canyon walls extending to the north, west and south.
113041:
A small oaken table has been set here.
On the table, there is a piece of cheese.
A circular stone well has been built here.

Wooden tables have been set on the grass in this garden allowing those staying at the inn to eat and drink outdoors when the weather permits. A simple stone wall running around the edge of the grass keeps this area private. Faint sounds of horses neighing and whinnying can be heard from mounts tethered in the stables to the south.
113042: Common Room of The Foaming Mug

A large stone fireplace with a roaring fire warms the room.
A bartender watches you calmly, while wiping ale mugs with a grimy cloth.

This large room is filled with long, wooden tables and simple benches running along each side. The locals appear to be making great use of this inn with most tables taken and the room filled with sounds of chattering and clinking of mugs. Set into the wall is a large, open fire which burns the local peat providing plenty of heat and a distinctive, smoky aroma.
113043:
A stove stands against one wall here.
A cook is standing here, toiling over a pot.

This kitchen is crowded and disorganized, but quite clean. Shelves line the walls, stacked with pots, pans, flat dishes, and all manner of kitchen utensils. More dishes sit on the large table that fills the centre of this kitchen; many contain dishes in various stages of preparation. A large stone oven dominates the northern wall, with a chimney that rises up through the ceiling; when lit, it provides enough heat to make this small room stiflingly hot. A rickety and steep set of wooden stairs in the northwest corner of the kitchen descends below.
113044:
A beer barrel has been left here.
A tall stone jar with a heavy lid is positioned here.
A small oaken table has been set here.
On the table, there are two pieces of cheese and a cooking book.

This underground cellar is cramped and musty. Low, table-like shelves run the length of every wall, broken only by the doorway to the staircase that ascends back up to the kitchens. The shelves are stacked high with casks, covered baskets, jugs, and all manner of bags and boxes; most of these clearly contain foodstuffs or drink, but some are sealed, unmarked, and opaque. The floor underfoot is dirt, hard-packed by the passage of feet over time.
113046: An Innkeeper is here, smiling at potential customers.

Rows of simple wooden doors leading to the guest rooms are accessed from a long corridor behind a small counter. A small brass bell rests on the counter to summon the innkeeper if he is away from his post. Covering the floor is a threadbare rug which, although worn, deadens the noise coming from the busy common room below.
113047: A huge clock is standing here.

A long corridor leads to the guest rooms of the inn. Each door has been individually styled but only the door to the west has been adorned with a notice hanging from a long iron nail. Large, varnished wooden columns flank the central hallway providing support for the roof. Relief carvings have been crudely cut into each of the columns in an attempt to provide some decoration in this otherwise plain room.
113048:
A sturdy peg for hanging armour from is on the wall.
On the peg, there are a pointy hat and a leather satchel.
A sturdy bed made from solid oak lies here, covered in warm blankets.
An old man in a heavy robe stands here, muttering something under his beard.

This T-shaped bedroom has space for a comfortable bed and an oak desk but is otherwise quite cramped. In order to make it fit, the desk has been tightly jammed into the space between the side of the bed and the door. The window is propped open to allow fresh air into the room and the curtains flutter gently in the breeze. Hard, polished wooden floorboards and bare walls, completely unadorned save for a single faded painting and a set of hooks, result in noises echoing around the room.
113049:
A sturdy bed made from solid oak lies here, covered in warm blankets.
A large bookshelf sits against the wall.

As comfortable as any other room in the inn, the bedroom provides all the essentials but little else. While a long way from being cramped, the room is small and appears not to have been used recently. The northern wall is mostly occupied by a bookshelf although it would appear that it is here because it is being stored by the inn's owners rather than as part of the room's usual fixtures and fittings.
113050:
A large cabinet capable of storing goods is here.
A sturdy bed made from solid oak lies here, covered in warm blankets.

This guest room is barely seven feet across, by the time the bed has taken its place in the corner the room begins to look small rather than cosy. A small patch of damp can be seen at the top of the wall, and the roof of the inn is seemingly in need of some attention. Close to the doorway stands a cabinet where the guests can leave their belongings.
113052: A rugged-looking man is standing here.

Sloping steeply down as it leads to the farmland to the north, the road passes through a residential area where many of the inhabitants of Black Hill have chosen to live. The homes bordering the road differ from those elsewhere in the village. Their ground floor walls are made of stone with only the upper floors constructed of wood.
113053: A short fence bordering a home here allows a glimpse of a small but well-tended garden behind the property. Neatly dug flower beds border a square lawn indicating that someone takes great pride of their garden. Across the road the shutters are firmly closed and barred on one house, the occupant presumably away on business.
113054: A signpost decorated with flowers and plants stands here, pointing to the east.

The cobbles that make up the paved surface of the road abruptly stop and give way to a small dirt path leading north into the fields. A few homes have been built here to give easy access to the farmland, the majority of buildings that make up the village of Black Hill lie to the south. A sign standing next to a door to the east indicates that a herbal shop has been set up in one of the homes.
113055: A beautiful and docile horse is standing here.

A narrow path runs from south to north through the grasslands here, nothing more than bare dirt where the grass has been worn away by passing feet. As the path heads northwards it separates two rows of farmed fields with straight lines of crops that rise tall on either side. The crops appear to be well-tended, they are uniform in size and appear healthy. To the south a small village can be seen, the buildings rising tall above the relatively flat ground and gently-rolling hills that stretch away toward the horizon.
113056: A brown fox is here, looking for some rabbits to chew up.

A small field of crops has been sown here among the short grasses of the surrounding plains. No wall or fence surrounds the field, but a border row of bare dirt outlines the crops and keeps the encroaching prairie grasses at bay. Along this border, and in the dirt between the planted crops, few weeds can be spotted; this field appears to be actively tended.
113059:
A tall, muscular man stands here, heating metal in the furnace.
A woman is here, looking for someone to chat with.

Huge bellows feed air to the furnace that dominates this room, the oppressive heat radiating from it takes some time to adjust to. A large, iron anvil sits, unused, beside a thick, wooden water-trough. Various farm tools have been plunged into the cooling water causing wisps of steam to rise up from the surface. Samples of the smith's finished work, everything from horseshoes to crosscut saws, line the walls.
113060: Several small fields of crops are set here amongst the short grasses of the surrounding plain. All have been planted in neat rows with a narrow strip of bare dirt separating the different varieties. The more mature crops have grown tall enough to hide the ground completely. A single, ruined section of a stone wall runs alongside several adjoining fields. The rocks that have been dislodged by the wind and rain have been carefully gathered and stacked against the base of the wall to the west.
113061: A peaceful farmer is here, whistling merrily.

Several large fields border each other here, separated by low stone walls. The walls, stacked without mortar of any type, rise only high enough to be visible above the rows of plants that stretch the length of the fields. Few weeds can be spotted among the plants, or in the bare dirt between the rows; it is clear that these fields are being actively farmed. A small wooden farmhouse can be seen a short distance to the north, conspicuous among the fields as the only object of significant height.
113062:
A carrot is lying here.
A carrot is lying here.
Some cereals that look like wheat are lying here.

Perfect rows of planted vegetables line the entire field. The neatly-packed dirt is divided into symmetrical rectangles with narrow trails separating the crops. There are a number of root crops growing here. In the southernmost end of the field cereal is growing tall and dense while carrots are flourishing in the eastern part of the field.
113063:
An apple tree with bright green leaves grows here.
On the tree's branches are three apples.

A wide path leads across this yard, connecting the crop fields to the east with the farmhouse to the west. A well-kept lawn with trimmed grass and a few trees flanks the gravel path while a high wooden fence outlines the entire yard, starting from both sides of the house to form a large square with only one opening for the path to the east.
113064:
Some cereals that look like wheat are lying here.
A hen is trying to pick some grains here.
A worm is here slithering around.
A beautiful and docile horse is standing here.
A brown fox is here, looking for some rabbits to chew up.

Several rows of crops run in parallel lines here, separated by rows of bare dirt. This alternating pattern of greens and browns stands out from the surrounding grassland, which is more uniform in colour. The crops appear to be well-tended, the plants looking healthy and vibrant. A low stone wall runs along all borders of this field, outside the prairie grasses grow tall and wild, forming clumps that nearly hide the simple stone-work from view.
113065: Tall, golden cereal rises from the brown, fertile soil. The stalks grow closely together, forming a large shimmering field that appears to stretch endlessly towards the north, east, and west. The southern end of the field ends abruptly at a rugged, rocky hill which rises too steeply to climb. A small trail runs through the middle of the field, allowing access to the crop without trampling the plants.
113066:
Some cereals that look like wheat are lying here.
Some cereals that look like wheat are lying here.

Large, flat fields made up of dark-brown, loamy earth stretch in all directions. A narrow dike which may contain water during rainy weather runs between the different sections of the fields. Tall grass, wheat and a variety of cereal are growing in organised patterns. A small trail crossing the fields from the east leads on toward large barns to the west and south.
113067:
A brown cow is here, contemplating a higher reality whilst chewing slowly.
A brown cow is here, contemplating a higher reality whilst chewing slowly.

Two large, flat fields stretch out here, separated by a low stone wall running north-south along a narrow dirt path. The fields have been planted with straight rows of crops alternating with rows of bare dirt; the crops appear to be well-tended, suggesting that these fields are being actively farmed. In the field to the east of the stone wall, a deep drainage ditch cuts across the regular lines; it is overgrown along its edges and the bushy weeds growing tall in the wet ground look out of place next to the carefully planted rows that continue around them.
113070:
A long water trough made of wood stands here.
A pig is here, covered in mud.
A pig is here, covered in mud.

Rows and rows of ten-by-ten feet boxes line this big, wooden building, each and every one with their own water trough. There is room for at least thirty pigs here but most of the boxes are empty and do not seem to have been occupied recently. The air here is humid and thick with the odours of mud, dirt and animal excrement.
113072: A crippled ranger is here, deep in thought.

This cabin is small and the ceiling is low. Built from stone, the blocks have been packed tightly with some sort of mortar. In places the mortar has crumbled leaving small gaps that encourage drafts. The cabin is split into two areas separated by a thin, wooden partition. The larger of the two contains a fireplace and table, and the smaller, nothing more than a simple bed. Both areas have been kept fastidiously clean.
113074: Some cereals that look like wheat are lying here.

Several small fields of crops border a solitary rut through the surrounding grasslands. The rut appears to be a simple foot-worn path through the grass, a slightly-winding trail that has been passed over frequently enough to wear down to bare dirt. The fields this path runs alongside are fenced in by low stone walls, straight-running piles of rocks that barely rise above the grasses they border. The walls must be used as boundary markings only, as they are too low to hinder entrance to the fields.
113076: A hen is trying to pick some grains here.

Several neglected farm fields rise from the surrounding grassland, visible as rows of overgrown plants now gone to seed. The rows, once straight, are now broken up by bushy clumps of tall weeds that have been allowed to run amok. The remains of a low stone wall outlines one such field; the rocks have been spread both into the overgrown crops and out among the bordering grasses with a randomness suggestive of time, weather, and passing animals. An old windmill stands to the north.
113077: The starving cow stands here looking for a patch of grass.

What used to be several small farm fields dot this section of the prairie. They have been long neglected and are now gone to seed; they are identifiable only by the relatively straight rows the overgrown crops still form. In places even these rows are interrupted, sometimes by mounds of dirt left behind by burrowing animals, and sometimes by larger shrubs, fast-growing weeds that have flourished in the fertile soil that was once being actively farmed.
113078: The gently-rolling grassland is broken by several wildly-overgrown farm fields. The fields, some of which are surrounded by low rock walls, rise well above their surroundings, owing to a combination of fast-growing weeds and fertile soil. The overgrown crops still follow straight lines down each field, although they are hard to make out in their current condition. To the east a clump of trees rises from the grasslands, conspicuous for its height in an otherwise flat area.
113080: An elderly herbalist is here, surrounded by a cloud of spice.

The stifling aromas of rare and valuable herbs mingle together to form a smell that overpowers the senses. An old map desk with many wide drawers in it has been repurposed to become a counter in the centre of the room while sealed pots and oil-filled jars are stacked around the edges of the shop.
113081: The ground here slopes down slightly in all directions, and rises again at a distance; this rise and fall repeats as the land extends toward each horizon. The effect is one of very gentle, rolling hills when viewed from far away and only moderately uneven ground when viewed close-up. The occasional tree rises from these gradual hillsides, conspicuously tall in an area that is otherwise mostly flat.
113082: Long grasses cover these hills, appearing uniform at a distance but showing bare patches close up. The soil in these bare patches is gravelly and weeds flourish in some spots where the grass is sparse, the hardy weeds managing to find nutrients in soil too barren for other plants to thrive. A few trees rise above the gentle hills that stretch toward each horizon; of these, most rise from the shallow valleys and folds that separate the hills.
113083: The grassy hills here are low and smooth, easily accessible from all directions. Several small game trails zigzag their way through the tall grass, showing signs of animal life. One hill sports an overhang, completely enshrouding the barren earth beneath in shadow. Dead vines and ancient moss cling to an old, weathered gravestone that had been placed with care long ago at the head of the mound.
113084: Small clusters of bushes float like little islands on the sea of grass flowing over these hills while slim trees stand like majestic banners at the bottom of shallow valleys. The rolling landscape gently levels off to flat grasslands in the northwest. However, the grasslands lie considerably lower than these hills and the descent is much too steep and long to climb. The rolling hills continue uninterrupted to the east and south while in the north a farmhouse can be seen amidst well-tended fields.
113085: Low hills roll gently out in all directions creating shallow valleys that become hidden from view behind grass-flecked ridgelines. Sparse tree lines flank the steeper slopes and follow several of the valleys; they blend together toward the horizon, dark against the lighter-coloured hills they frame. Long grass grows underfoot, thinning slightly atop many of the hills, varying in colour from tan to yellow to green creating a pale, pastel blend of colours that stretches to the horizon.
113086: The ground here is uneven, rising and falling to form low hills and shallow valleys. Long grass covers the hills and fills the valleys with a uniform greenery except for areas in several of the lower valleys where the ground becomes rocky. These rocks are small; some are nothing more than gravel, spread out in patches that have forced the grasses to grow more sparsely than usual.
113087: The humps and knolls of these hills are low and gentle. The rolling landscape continues to the east and south while to the west and north, the hills give way to rugged, almost vertical drop-offs to fields below. A farmhouse can be seen far to the west on the fields below, surrounded by a tall fence. At the bottom of a small valley, a shallow pond nurtures the nearby trees and shrubbery.
113088: Overgrown with vegetation, the hills continue to the north, west and south as far as the eye can see. A solitary tree occupies the hilltop, most likely home to the birds of the area. Occasionally, the cry of a bird of prey can be heard as it attempts to hunt its quarry. Pieces of broken shale can be found amongst the rocky outcrop near the tree.
113089: While the hills may initially appear grassy, the hard sediment under the surface is formed from pieces of broken shale that shift underfoot. Progress amongst the hills is slow as extra care must be taken not to slip on the shifting surface. While no direct route exists to reach it, a heavily travelled path can be seen to the south and east.
113090: The hills here are low and gentle and travelling is as effortless as can be expected without road or trail to follow. To the south, the gentle hills are interupted by a line of high, rocky ridges and no opportunity for travel in that direction can be seen. To the north, east and west the rolling landscape with its green knolls lie open.
113091: To the south, a steep ridge of jagged rock rises sharply cutting off passage in that direction. Rolling hills flow to the east, west, and north like ripples on a verdant, green pond. In a small valley between two hills, the remains of what appears to be an old campsite can be seen.
113092: A brown donkey watches the surroundings, perhaps looking for a chance to graze.

Here, tall, thick grass blankets the slopes, hilltops and shallow valleys alike. Signs of grazing animals appear here and there. The gentle hills roll on to the north and east while passage to the south is blocked by a steep ridge. To the west, near the foothills, the land evens out to wide, flat plains.
113093: Tall, green grass covers this vast, rolling expanse. To the east and south, the hills rise just high enough to block the view of what lies beyond. Other vegetation is scarce, save for a few scattered but thriving groups of thorny shrub. Westward and north, the gentle rolling hills suddenly give way to steep, rocky slopes. At the bottom of these slopes, great flat fields stretch outwards for miles. The fields to the west appear wild and untended while to the north there appears to be some cultivation.
113094: The height differences between the valley floors and hill tops are rarely more than a few dozen feet in these hills. The slopes up and down are gentle and covered with tall grass. Vibrant patches of flowers in many colours seem to explode across the hillsides, bringing contrast to an otherwise dull landscape.
113095: From the top of one of the taller hills in this region, the view is quite spectacular. The Tower Hills cover a vast area and the rolling, grass-covered landscape continues uninterrupted for miles in all directions. The ground is dotted with small holes with rodents warily peeking out once in a while to see if it is safe to come out and search for food.
113096: A sand viper is slithering here on the ground.

A narrow cavern stretches far into the cliff. Underfoot the ground is stony but a layer of sand covers most of the floor and deep, curving grooves adorn the surface. At the base of the cavern wall lie the skeletal remains of a few small, unfortunate mammals.
113097: A fallow deer is grazing peacefully here.

A grey, moss-covered rockface rises high above the surrounding hills. Large rocks and boulders lie scattered across the slope at its foot, half-buried in the ground as if fallen from a great height. Tall grass, green and wild, flourishes on the slopes of nearby hills and in the valleys while the hilltops themselves are mostly bare and barren of vegetation.
113098: A colourful butterfly is fluttering around here.

The hills rise to their rocky, barren tops then dip sharply to dry valleys where naught but hardy shrubs and wild tufts of coarse grass grow. Large rocks and boulders lie scattered across the hills to the north, where a wide, steep ridge blocks further travel. A trail can be seen further to the south and east, making its way across the Tower Hills.
113099: A tall ridge rises in the north above the Tower Hills. It is steep and covered with loose rock and dirt; unsuitable for climbing. At the ridge's base, boulders of all sizes lie scattered, broken and half-buried in the hard ground. The surrounding hills are sparse with vegetation as only hardy bushes and wild-looking grass cling to the stony ground.
113100:
A small brown snake is slithering around here.
A colourful butterfly is fluttering around here.

There are many signs of game trails among the low grass and sparse shrubbery growing here. In between the patches of vegetation where the earth is exposed, hoof-marks are visible, likely from deer or goat. From atop a tall hill, the view reveals an unremarkable expanse of more hills in all directions. However, a thin, brown scar marking the route of a wagon-trail can be seen to be curving from the east to the south.
113101:
A cluster of white star-shaped forget-me-nots flourish here in reminiscence.
Some delicious wild strawberries grow on the ground.

Stretching for miles toward the east and south, the tall but gentle hills seem to ramble on without end. The land in this part of the Tower Hills is lush with thick grass, moving gracefully with the slightest breeze. Here and there, slim trees stand tall. In the distance to the southeast, a trail can be seen snaking through the rolling hills. To the north and west, the hills end abruptly, revealing wide plains below.
113102:
A waist-high evergreen shrub grows here, with thick, reaching branches.
On the shrub, there are two piles of grey-green leaves.

Undulating in long gentle waves, the hills stretch out in all directions. Carpeted with thick, green grass down to the valley floors, the land sports thriving bushes and the occasional slim tree. The landscape is wild although there are bare spots where grass has been grazed and trampled, probably by deer or sheep. To the south and east, a trail meanders lazily through valley floors among the hills.
113103: Grassy hills rise and fall in gentle green waves, making for easy walking even though there are no trails to follow. The vegetation, mostly lush grass interspersed with various bushes and shrubs, stands several feet tall in the valleys, while it thins out considerably on the nearby slopes and hilltops.
113104: A fallow deer is grazing peacefully here.

These grass-covered hills should be ideal for herbivores and indeed there are many signs of deer; tracks are plentiful and obvious and droppings litter the ground. The land rises and falls through brush-filled valleys punctuated by sparsely vegetated hillocks. Towards the southwest a green valley lies embedded in the hills.
113105: The hills here overlook a valley to the west. The hills continue to rise and fall to the north, the east, and the south. Throughout the vegetation that covers them, mainly various grasses and bushes, trails from various animals hints at a rich wildlife.
113106: Wild, rolling hills expand in all directions. A man-made trail follows the valley floors in-between hills as it makes its way through the Tower Hills to the south-east. The hills are covered with thick grasses, and animal trails are in clear evidence throughout the area. Thicker vegetation flourish between the hills where the wind can not affect them as much.
113107:
A tiny spider is here, eating a tiny bug.
A tiny spider is here, eating a tiny bug.

The walls of this cave have formed naturally in a jagged, sharp and uneven fashion. However, the floor is surprisingly level. Fresh air seems to enter the cave through a thin crack in the southern wall while the cave itself continues on to the east.
113108: The uneven cavern walls are damp with moisture. Every now and then a drop falls to the floor from the cavern's roof as water trickles in from above, albeit very slowly. The floor of the cavern is considerably more even than its walls as if some past effort has been made to level it. The cave ascends slightly as it continues west while a steep slope leads deeper underground to the north.
113109: Walls of dark, brown stone press in from all sides, creating a narrow tunnel-like cavern. Flat slices of shale lie shattered on the floor where it's fallen from the roof and walls and more looks set to fall at any moment. Water drips from the ceiling, wetting the dust-covered ground. Tiny, brittle bones lie on the cavern's floor, covered by the dust. Most probably from bats or birds, and likely very old.
113110:
A large cockroach is crawling on the floor.
A large cockroach is crawling on the floor.
A small bat is standing here.
A small bat is standing here.

A long, narrow cave with walls of grey and brown shale has naturally formed here. Faint sparkles of light hint at quartz and other minerals embedded in the rock. The floor of the cave is smooth and even, making travel through the tunnel easy to the north or west.
113111: A bloodthirsty bat is sleeping here.

Several narrow cracks and fissures high up on the northern cave wall hint at the outside world. However, they are too small as well as too deep to contemplate passage except by smaller creatures like bats or lizards. On the cavern's floor lie many irregular piles of guano attesting bat infestation. Some of the piles look disturbed or uneven, perhaps just by the rocks beneath, although in places it looks like there's a sheen of metal beneath the guano. The rest of the floor is surprisingly even and the walls seem to have crude shelves carved into them. This cave may have served as a hideout or camp in the past.
113112: A giant, mean looking earth beetle is sleeping here.

At one point this hill was covered in heather and other hardy shrubs. Years of exposure to the biting wind and a lack of rain have taken its toll leaving only the dead, woody remains behind. There is little sign of animal life here, even the insects shun these barren hills.
113113: This prominent peak towers above the surrounding countryside, providing a commanding view of the wagon trail that sweeps gracefully around the base of the hill to the north and west. There is little shelter on this exposed spot, and the soil has been washed away into the valleys below, leaving little chance for any vegetation to grow here.
113114: Standing in the shadow of the higher peak to the north, this bare and infertile hill supports little in the way of bushes or trees. A few exposed patches of rocks, worn smooth with the action of rain and frost over hundreds of years, are all that mark the summit.
113115: A landscape of gently sloping, grass-covered hills expands to the east and north. In the shallow valleys between hills, brush and even the occasional tree makes an appearance. Steep cliffs rise to the south and the west. The bluffs at the top of the cliffs no doubt offer a spectacular view of the Tower Hills.
113116: A deep gulch to the east and south forms an impassable gap between these hills and other, similar hills beyond. The vegetation is limited to spots of grass that are scattered across the shattered rocks that line the hilltops. Once, long ago, water may have run through here to help form the gulch. However, there are no signs of water anywhere in the area now.
113117: The terrain here forms a depression between hills to the east and to the west. There is a slope down into a small valley to the north, and the land appears to be somewhat flat to the south. It is quite easy to navigate north and south through this dip, and it is also possible to travel up the slopes to the east and the west.
113118: A rare break in the hills can be found here. The valley runs downward to the west and appears from the south. At one point, a river may have run through here and cut its way through the hills to cause this valley. However, no water can be seen here any more. The river may have expended itself in cutting through these age old cliffs.
113119: A fallow deer is grazing peacefully here.

The valley that cut its way from the east ends here with only a hole in the hillside to the south to be seen. The hole is large enough to allow entrance but it isn't clear what would await inside. The hillsides to the west and north are not ascendable. The valley floor is covered with grass and bushes.
113120: This hill is sparsely vegetated by grass and shrubs. A valley can be seen to the north, but there does not appear to be a way down to it from here. A small hill can be seen to the west that could be easily ascended. To the south and east, sloping hills can be seen continuing toward the horizon.
113121: A giant rat patters against you, squeaking maliciously.

A tunnel begins here. It leads out to an area lush with vegetation to the north, and deeper underground to the south. The tunnel looks to have been carved through the bedrock by a river in the past. Wind-blown leaves litter the floor of the tunnel and fungi clings to the grey stone walls.
113122: A tunnel, low and narrow, leads through a bedrock of grey rock. The tunnel slopes gently downwards to the south. While it's not clear from the featureless tunnel what awaits at either end, the slope of the tunnel seems to indicate that going south would lead deeper underground and north would lead towards the outside world.
113123: A huge, hungry-looking rat is here.

An underground crossroads has formed, with tunnels leading in all directions. To the north, the tunnel slopes upward while in all other directions, they slope downward. The air to the west seems to be more humid than in the other directions, while the walls down the eastern tunnel are covered in fungi.
113124:
A small, clear pool is here, fed by steadily dripping water.
A hairy black spider wraps up a silken package with her hind legs.

The floor of this cave is littered with several small bones, as if something frequents this cave often. A small stream runs down from the ceiling into a small pool at the southern edge of this cavern, and the pool slowly seaps through a crack under the southern wall. The opening into this wide underground space lies to the north, where it appears that several tunnels intersect.
113125: The tunnel bends sharply to the east from the south here. The path to the south slopes down sharply, and faint sounds of trickling water can be heard in that direction. To the east, an upward sloping path can be followed. The air here smells dank and damp, and the beginnings of moss and lichen can be seen clinging to the rocky walls.
113126: This lake exists deep under the hills. The temperature of the water is low enough that it feels chilly, but located as it is deep beneath the surface, it is unlikely to freeze at winter. The lake is not large, a spear could be thrown across it. Water trickles down from the ceiling at a slow but steady pace. There are several large stalactites in a cluster near the centre of the lake.
113127: This tunnel is a long series of bends and turns, winding its way through the bedrock. There are several small boulders scattered about on the ground, as if a small collapse happened here long ago. Stalactites hang from the ceiling, but the water that once formed them is no longer present. The tunnel slopes up to the west, and winds out of sight to the south. The grey stone of the walls is barely visible beneath layers of green and yellow fungi.
113128:
A large black bat flitters near you.
A large black bat flitters near you.
A large black bat flitters near you.
A large black bat flitters near you.
A giant rat patters against you, squeaking maliciously.
A giant rat patters against you, squeaking maliciously.
A huge, hungry-looking rat is here.

The walls, floor and ceiling in this small cavern are covered in mould and fungi, and a damp ripe stench fills the air. There are several moss covered boulders here, and the droppings on the floor indicate that this is the home for a colony of bats. A narrow tunnel to the north leads out of this cavern.
113129:
A skeleton of some humanoid lies in the dust.
A fierce bat is here, lusting for your blood.
A bloodthirsty bat is sleeping here.
A bloodthirsty bat is sleeping here.

This air in this cavern is damp, and lichens grow on the rocks strewn on the ground throughout it. The cave widens to the north where the dark, rippling surface of an underground lake can be seen. There appears to be no way out from here but daring the black waters.
113130: An ancient fungus smothers the boulders.

This appears to be a place previously used to meet in secret. Lots of bottles and broken glass lies strewn about. There are scorch marks on the walls where torches have hung and a blackened circle of stones in the middle of the floor where countless fires appear to have been lit. Rotten wooden boxes lie in one corner, any once valuable content most likely taken away or crumbled to dust.
113131: A badger is here, exploring for food.

This hill is slightly higher than the surrounding hills, and a small area can be surveyed from here. To the west and south, smaller hills continue for miles. Some broken large rocks lie here with moss and ferns growing in their shadows.
113132: A badger is here, exploring for food.

To the east, the hillside ends at the edge of an abrupt cliff face. A valley can be seen below, but there are no handholds to allow one to climb down here. In other directions, the sloping hillsides can easily be traversed with the highest area being to the south.
113133: Long, shallow ravines cross the hills, giving them a broken appearance. Grass and flowers cover the hillsides and show that, although the area is rocky, vegetation can manage to find places to grow. A trail winds its way through the hills to the south and east.
113134: Gently rolling hills extend in all directions. Several types of grass grow in the less rocky areas between hills. There are scattered signs of small game throughout the area such as droppings and foraged vegetation. The slopes of the hills are not steep enough to pose a problem for anyone travelling through here.
113135: Rolling hills dominate the landscape for miles in all directions. The only minor break in their continuity is to the south and east where a trail follows the flatter terrain. Signs of small animals can be seen amongst rocks and tufts of vegetation.
113137: This area has hills all around. There is no obvious path to travel here, but the surroundings do not appear to be difficult to navigate. A slightly taller hill can be seen to the east above the rest of the hills that dot the horizon.
113138: The area here slopes gently upward toward a hill to the east that appears to be slightly taller than the surrounding ones. Broken rocks can be seen scattered across the hillside but there is enough room in-between them to ascend it without too much trouble.
113139: These hills show all the signs of being beaten down year after year by the unforgiving wind. The undulating hills continue in all directions, and it appears that they would be relatively easy to travel around or traverse.
113140: This crevice between the hills is hidden from sight until it is about ten feet away. It seems to have been formed by a long dry underground spring, and it is very shady here. The crevice slants down further underground to the east, where the faint rustling sounds and odour of guano can be detected.
113142: Bracken and rough grass cover patches of the otherwise bleak and barren hillside. Small strands of greyish wool hang from the bracken where sheep have tried to graze and snagged their coats. The ground slopes gently away in every direction save for the south where a deep ravine splits this hill away from the ridgeline beyond.
113143: A rabbit is here eyeing your presence warily.

From the top of a hill, a trail is visible to the west and north. The hill ends abruptly and no way of climbing down from here can be seen. To the east, the hill's eastern slope descends gently. The rocky, scraggly brush-covered hills continue to roll onward to the south and can be seen to the west across the trail as well.
113144: A ravine can be seen cutting through the land below to the east and north. The hills come together and form a minor upward slope to the west. Southward, the hills continue for miles and miles. Grasses dominate the landscape with the occasional shrub making an appearance along with a few solitary trees.
113145: The sloping hills that continue to the south and west appear to come to an end somewhere to the north. They come to a halt immediately to the east where a cliff overlooks a ravine. A few smaller bushes and wildflowers disturb the sea of grass that covers the land.
113146: These hills harbour a variety of weeds, mosses, fungi and other small plants. Yet for all the plantlife that can be found here, the landscape looks almost barren; it is dusty and clad in shades of grey and brown. A ravine cuts through the hills to the north, at the bottom of a steep slope.
113147: The hills slope downward to the north, and a ravine cuts through the hills in that direction. The ground is rocky with some small plants and shrubs lending some colour to the otherwise grey-brown hillsides. To the west, a sheer rock face makes travel in that direction impossible. A small rise can be seen to the east; it appears to lead out of the cut ravine channel.
113148:
A colourful butterfly is fluttering around here.
A rabbit is here eyeing your presence warily.

The bottom of this ravine is dry and level. The ground is covered with loose gravel and struggling weeds. A slope ascends into the hills that abut the ravine to the south. In other directions, the ravine floor continues but it is not clear where it goes, or what is to be found in those branches.
113149:
A rock lizard is here, motionless as it observes you.
A rock lizard is here, motionless as it observes you.

The ravine is deep and narrow with imposing cliff-walls and a gravel bed underfoot. Clearly the area was once host to a river that carved its way through the rock but has long since dried up. To the east, the fragile cliff-walls have crumbled sending piles of shattered rock into the ravine, blocking any chance of further travel.
113150: A colourful butterfly is fluttering around here.

A ravine ends here with the only possible exits being to the east and north. To the east, the floor of the ravine continues while to the north, a rocky scrabble can be seen that looks navigable. However, coming back that way may be difficult due to the loose scree and crushed gravel.
113151: A rock lizard is here, motionless as it observes you.

A gorge cuts through steep-sided cliffs, gradually narrowing until it reaches a dead end to the east. Rising high above, the steep canyon walls enclose a flat, oval area, littered with fragments of rocks that have fallen from the cliffs above. Upon the ground, small tracks in the sand disappear under some rocks.
113152: A majestic hill dominates the landscape, rising above the surrounding, lower hills. To the north, a channel runs downward from the hill into a ravine. A small ridge slopes slightly downward to the west and south. Scattered moss and lichen cover the broken scree that litters the ground.
113153: A colourful butterfly is fluttering around here.

To the south, a copse of trees can be seen at the bottom of a steep, smooth cliff that shows no signs of being traversable. A similar cliff forms a natural border to the east where the land becomes more flat and fertile, and a forest borders the hills. The cliff edge that forms this perch continues westward from here, whereas the terrain to the north consists of sparsely vegetated, rolling hills.
113154: Rocky, scree-covered slopes descend from this rocky peak in all directions but to the east. A ridge-like series of cliffs extends towards the east. They are narrow and broken but look stable enough for the moment. Of the three slopes, only the northern one is traversable, being slightly less steep and rocky than the southern and the western ones.
113155: This hilly area is covered in broken stone and large boulders. A slightly taller hill can be seen to the east, while a ridge runs to the west. The rolling terrain continues to the north and south. Tufts of grass and limited vegetation struggle to scour the ground for nourishment.
113156: A ridgeline follows a deep gulch that can be seen to the west of here. The ridgeline continue to the south, and then bends sharply to the east where it meets up with rolling hills. Is is narrow and rocky, but travel along it is doable as long as one does not venture too far to the east or west.
113157: A narrow, meandering ridgeline runs to the north and south. There is loose scree to the west, where a deep gully can be seen at the foot of the scree-covered slope. No vegetation grows here as the surroundings are covered in broken rock, and with the winds constantly buffeting the area germination is almost impossible.
