113158: A sloping narrow ridgeline runs to the north and east here. No path exists down the steep south-western hillside that descends into a gulch. Broken scree that makes up every colour of grey and black litters the ridgeline, a sign of ages of weather buffeting the hills.
113159: A narrow, easily traversible ridgeline runs from the west to the south here, descending as it goes. A deep gorge borders the ridge to the south-west, while hilly terrain extends for miles to the north and north-east. To the east, another sheer drop ends at a small circular clearing surrounded by hills.
113160: A meandering ridgeline extending to the north and south intersects with a second ridgeline which is narrower, but straight and comfortably traversable. A hill lies to the east, a mile or two along the narrow ridgeline. A long drop on the western side of the meandering ridgeline ends at the bottom of a gulch.
113161:
A goat is here, grazing in the hills.
A young goat playfully charges and hops away.

A timeworn path winds its way through the hills, ever climbing, until it reaches the top of the ridgeline far to the east. The path is surrounded by many patches of weeds and grass. The view here is exceptional; an uninterrupted panorama of a dense forest to the southeast, extending several miles until a magnificent, white tower dominates the skyline.
113162: A mountain goat is here, jumping from cliff to cliff.

The ground slopes sharply upwards as the natural trail reaches the top of the hill. Bushes grow on both sides of the trail, their lower leaves gnawed upon by small folivores. Beyond the bushes on the southern part of the trail, a dense forest can be seen and, beyond that, an imposing white tower.
113163: Walls of steep rock surround this narrow, shallow ravine. The majority of the rocky walls have been smoothed out from exposure to water and wind through the ages, although in places small landslides have thrown fresh, jagged scree onto the floor of the ravine. To the west, the ravine opens up and climbs out onto an open hillside while, to the north, the canyon narrows considerably.
113164: A narrow ravine tapers off to a dead end here. The sides are steep and smooth while the bottom of the ravine is covered with loose rocks and the footing is treacherous. The ravine widens slightly to the south, which seems to be the only way to move from here. Several thorny bushes grow among the rocks and boulders along the ravine's floor; they provide excellent hiding places for reptiles, snakes and other small animals, should any make this ravine their hunting ground.
113165: A mountain goat is here, jumping from cliff to cliff.

A trodden trail takes a sharp turn to the east and south here. The vegetation surrounding the trail is sparse and mainly consists of small patches of weeds and grass, joined by the odd tree. Even though the trail seem to provide the only way to the top of the hill, it seems to be almost completely unused.
113166: On these hilltops, grass and bushes grow rampantly. A narrow trail winds its way through the hills, rarely taking the easier path and often straying very close to the edge of the steep cliffs to the north. The floor of a canyon is visible at the foot of the cliffs. To the south, a flat, verdant forest can be seen flanked by rising hills to the east and west.
113168:
A goat is here, grazing in the hills.
A young goat playfully charges and hops away.
A mountain goat is here, jumping from cliff to cliff.

A goat trail follows a ridge of hills towards the north and east. A steep decline to the south ends at a vast expanse of plains. Hoof marks on the ground leads north and east along the trail. On the northern side of the trail a small circular structure that looks like a well is built out of rocks. Patches of moss grow on the stones, and small weeds sprout from the crevices in-between the rocks. The water in the well is dried out, and there are no other ruins in sight to explain why a well was built here.
113169: The landscape here is composed mostly of short, stunted patches of grass and the occasional bush. Hoof marks mar the path that runs north and west heavily, churning the ground into a tumultuous mix of rocks, sand, and trodden grass. To the south, the ground becomes treacherously steep and rocky, before flattening out into an expansive grassland that stretches far into the distance.
113170:
A lonely goatherd stands here.
A goatherd's dog is here.
A goat is here, grazing in the hills.
A young goat playfully charges and hops away.

The ground here is narrow and uneven. Grass, bushes, and various stones cover the hilly terrain. Towards the north, a serrated escarpment tumbles downward into a wide canyon, preventing immediate travel in that direction. To the south, the path descends at uneven intervals, twisting its way around large rocks. Upon the ground are small tracks, barely discernible against the hard hearth, leading to and from a small hole in the side of a small mound.
113171:
Clear water bubbles up from a cool underground water reservoir.
A lonely goatherd stands here.
A goatherd's dog is here.

An artesian spring bubbles to the surface between two large sheets of hard, grey rock. The ground is significantly softer than the surrounding area, having been permeated by water for quite some time. A thick, vibrant bed of grass flanks the trail on all sides. In several places the flora has been chewed down to the ground, where hoof prints can be seen deeply embedded in the soft, pliable soil.
113172: The rocky hollow is barren apart from some evergreen shrubs growing in the rock crevices. The terrain here is rough and littered with angled rocks and boulders making it quite difficult to traverse. Meandering among the rocky hills, a beaten path winds its way southward under the shade of the cliffs.
113173:
An ancient fungus smothers the boulders.
An ancient fungus smothers the boulders.

This is a roomy cave. The floor is covered in wet sand, and there is a steady but slow drip of water down the walls. Fungus and moss grows all over the walls, and the air smells like damp earth, with a slight hint of decay. A small amount of light comes in from the hole in the northern rocky surface.
113174: The long, gentle slopes of this lone hilltop continue for miles in all directions. The hill is covered with grass and low vegetation. A few large boulders and rock formations, covered with moss and lichen, dot the slopes. The slope to the north descends into a wooded hollow that looks like a dead-end.
113175:
An apple tree with bright green leaves grows here.
On the tree's branches are three apples.
A tree-snake lies wrapped around one of the tree branches.

A small, wooded hollow is nestled among the Tower Hills here. The only feasible way in or out of the hollow is a slope to the south. In every other direction, the steep, rocky hillsides conspire to create this wooded dead-end. The area is lush with vegetation as many trees cover the valley floor.
113176: The ground slopes heavily downwards from the west, continuing its rapid descent eastward until the landscape abruptly gives way to a vertical escarpment below. Gazing further east, the tops of a dense, coniferous forest can be seen tucked between rising hills on all sides except to the north, where the green forest grows ever-onward.
113177: The hills here form many unique rock formations. Northward, the hills give way to a long slope leading to a lone, majestic hilltop. Some faint signs of some ancient structures can be seen, but their meaning and shape have been lost for eons. Small bushes and shrubs cover the low lands in-between slopes, while grasses cover the slopes and peaks of the hills.
113178: Standing Stones upon a Tower Hill

The prominent crown of this hill flattens out into a wide grassy plateau, upon which a circle of stone pillars has been raised. Their purpose is unknown, lost in the mists of time. It is possible that this spot was chosen because of the commanding view of the surrounding countryside. Low bushes and shrubs cover the ground, varying in size and colour.
113179: The garden snake slithers harmlessly here.

Barren hills to the north and west meet here and their slopes form a descent to the south, into a shadowy gulch. There is little vegetation as the ground is covered by a lot of rocky scree. The few bushes and shrubs that do find these conditions agreeable are thorny, tough-looking plants.
113180: A gulch begins at the foot of a rugged, scree-covered slope to the north. The dry gulch is nestled between a ridgeline to the east and hills to the west. It runs north and south, with sheer rocky walls that prohibit climbing out to the east and west. Vegetation is sparse with naught but small, thorny shrubs and weeds that struggly to survive on the dry, shaded canyon floor.
113181: A small off-shoot of the otherwise straight north-south running gulch lies to the west. While it appears as though water once ran through here to assist in the creation of this gulch, none is in evidence anymore. Small boulders and rocky scrabble litters the ground everywhere which could provide places for animals to hide. Most of the bottom of the gulch is cast in shadows as even the noon sun can never quite reach it.
113182: A north-south running gulch cuts through the hills here. Rocky scrabble covers the ground, providing shade most of the day. There is little vegetation growing here and no water. Small cracks along the west rocky wall might provide excellent handholds for a climber who want to reach the rocky ledge higher on the gulch's steep side.
113183: A narrow gulch in the surrounding hills continues north and south. Very little vegetation grows in it, and the majority of the ground is covered by rocky scree. In this area, the rock walls that block travel to the east and west, show little signs of wear, and attempting to climb them seem futile.
113184: A narrow, dry gulch ends here at the rockface that blocks its southern end. Similar rockwalls to the east and west form a natural dead-end cast in perpetual gloom. The only ways out of this gulch is either to follow it north, or attempt to climb the least steep of the sides, the western one.
113190: A small offshoot of the gulch which runs to the west can be found here, surrounded by cliffs that define the walls of the area. No hand holds can be seen along the walls and escaping this dead-end by climbing is impossible. A few boulders lie on the ground, with a few small shrubs and weeds growing scattered about.
113191:
A skeleton of some humanoid lies in the dust.
A large, dangerous-looking green snake is coiled up here.

This north-facing cavern is shaded from direct sunlight by a stone shelf that overhangs the narrow entrance to the north. The view is highly restricted by cliffs that flank the ravine that lies outside this gloomy hollow. There is naught but rocks to be seen in this desolate grotto.
113193: A large eagle soars above you.

A rocky shelf clings to the rock wall, halfway between the hills above and the gulch floor below. There appears to be a way to descend to the bottom of the gulch by using some small cracks as handholds, but the wall above is sheer and smooth.
113195:
A clear spring babbles as cool water trickles out of the ground.
A wild bull seems ready to charge you.

Layers of folded rock are exposed, clearly showing the effect of the violent upheavals that must have occurred to create these hills. A stream of water gushes forth from one break in the rocks, creating a small pool before draining downhill and vanishing again beneath the ground. Deep ruts beside the pool hint that someone often comes here with a wagon. The ruts run to the west, but they vanish on the bare rock and their destination is impossible to determine.
113196: A large number of people seem to come and go frequently here, as the grass has been heavily trampled. There appear to be three main paths. One leads north to a large, crudely-crafted tent. A second path leads south to a wooden hut that has certainly seen better days. The final path extends to the east, where a larger grassy area opens up. A bare stone hillside drops away to the west.
113197: This is the southern end of the hilltop, beyond which the hillside drops away in an almost vertical cliff. The heavy grass present north of here nearly vanishes, to be replaced by piles of boulders and smaller stones. The base rock of the hill is visible, and is pierced in many places by narrow fissures. A very old hut stands just to the west, though it looks like it may not stand for much longer.
113198: Short, thick-stemmed grass dominates this mostly flat area, with a sprinkling of purple and lavender flowers. A single tall oak stands in the centre of the grass, providing a large patch of shade on sunny days. There are a couple of crude wooden benches set up at the base of the tree, and many tracks through the grass lead both to the tree, to the west, and to a large tent that stands at the north edge of the field.
113199:
A brigand, looking at your nice purse, is sneaking here.
A brigand, looking at your nice purse, is sneaking here.
A thief is here looking for some stranger to rob.

This one-room hut looks like it has stood here for decades. It may once have been strongly constructed, but time has taken its toll. The log walls are rotting and in many places coating with emerald moss, while the breeze flows freely through a number of cracks. The roof appears to be intact, though the support beams are sagging and could collapse at almost any time. Large holes gape open in both the north and east walls, the doors that once filled them long since vanished.
113200:
A mass of tattered fabric lies here in a heap.
A brigand, looking at your nice purse, is sneaking here.
A brigand, looking at your nice purse, is sneaking here.

This tent is large but crudely fashioned, patched together from a number of different pieces of fabric. The stitching is poorly done, and it seems almost certain that the tent leaks in even the lightest rain. A haphazard collection of wooden poles supports the ungainly structure. Several bedrolls, all of them quite filthy, line the walls of the tent.
113201:
A solid ironbound chest is here.
A thug is here, plotting his band's next raid (hidden).

This tent is quite extensive for a temporary shelter, and is clearly not meant to be moved frequently. Oak poles and posts support a thick canvas roof and sides, spreading the fabric out and leaving ample headroom for even the tallest man. There is no floor to the tent, and the grass underfoot is long since dead from lack of sunlight. Despite its ability to house many men, the tent contains only a single cot, along with a chest, a small folding table, and a pair of low stools.
113202:
An albino fish is swimming here, looking for some food.
An albino fish is swimming here, looking for some food.
A huge, hungry-looking rat is here.

A broad cavern has been eroded into the stone of the ridge, sloping quickly downward as it extends to the north. Trickles of water run down the walls of the cave, leaving the uneven rocky floor slick and treacherous. About thirty feet from the entrance, the floor of the cavern vanishes below the surface of a dark pool of water.
113205: A small bat flies silently from shadow to shadow (hidden).

No more than ten feet across at most points, this cave runs roughly east and west. The eastern end is partially plugged with thick brambles, though it is likely possible to push through them without too much trouble. The rock walls are rough and the floor uneven, and although the ceiling is nearly flat it is clearly that way naturally. The cave widens out suddenly to the west.
113206: A large black bat flitters near you.

The cave is quite wide here and forms a T-shaped intersection with passages to the north, south, and east. The eastern branch is the narrowest, while to the south the cave appears to enter a large chamber. Layers of rock have fallen from the ceiling, and the floor is littered with giant slabs intermixed with smaller shards of stone.
113207: This cave is not very wide and snakes its way back and forth as it progresses. It is straighter and wider to the south, while towards the north end it takes a sudden turn eastward. Sharp projections abound on both walls, making it more difficult to move without injury. The floor is roughly even, but it slopes a little to the west, while the ceiling overhead is curved in a gentle arch.
113208:
Several silver coins lie scattered about here.
An ancient fungus smothers the boulders.
A huge black fungus is here, exuding a foul stench.
A small bat flies silently from shadow to shadow (hidden).

The cave widens out into a large chamber. The room is roughly egg-shaped, with its narrow point near the entrance. Large slabs and chunks of stone have fallen from the ceiling and cover the floor in broken piles. Water drips from a dozen cracks in the ceiling, coating every surface of the cavern with moisture and leaving the floor slick and dangerous. The sharp smell of mildew fills the air.
113209: A large bat is sleeping here.

The cave comes to an abrupt end here, widening only slightly before doing so. It appears that the tunnel once extended further east, but the way is now entirely blocked by massive slabs and boulders. It would take a major mining effort to clear the way. The walls are studded with countless flecks of mica and quartz that twinkle when lit.
113211: Several small pools of water have collected upon the ground.

The walls of this natural cavern are made of cold, hard soil. Tiny roots sprout from the walls, covering the damp surface in a natural webbing. Drops of water drip constantly from the ceiling, falling softly upon the floor to form small, dark puddles. Towards the east, the dirt walls begin to bear the markings of shovels and picks; long, deep swaths have been cut into the earth, slowly fading into the darkening gloom as the tunnel advances. As the tunnel burrows deeper, the earth and hard soil is gradually replaced by bedrock.
113212:
An iron pick has been dropped here.
A note lies here.
A sturdy crate made of nailed wooden planks sits on the floor.

The ceiling of this damp tunnel slopes sharply towards the west. Grooves have been scored at various depths into the walls and ceiling, evident that this small underground cave was made by unnatural means. Upon the ground, broken rocks and large clumps of hard soil lie strewn about, all bearing the marks left by vigorous application of pick and shovel upon earth.
113214:
A small termite is running around making strange sounds.
A small termite is running around making strange sounds.
A small termite is running around making strange sounds.
A giant termite is here, crushing skulls and bones.

This small earthen cave is little more than a hollow in the ground, yet it is more than large enough for several people. There are signs that the cave has been deliberately expanded, though not by human hands. Only a few roots poke through the ceiling; all of the others have been cut off level with the soil. Tiny tunnels snake off into the walls, too small for even a hobbit to follow.
113220: A wooden chest stands in the corner.

The residents of this house keep it spotless. Every piece of furniture matches with the rest and sits in a carefully arranged location. There is no dust or dirt to be seen on the floor, or on any other surface. Colourful drapes adorn the windows, drawn back by ties of the same material to allow fresh air to flow through the house.
113223:
A large bulletin board, entitled "Shapers", is mounted here.
The Hitchhiker's Guide to Construction on MUME is floating in the air here.
A book titled "Handbook for New Gods" is here.

This is a quiet place where those who watch the world below can share their thoughts on life, death, the landscape and wonders of Arda's mighty warriors and mysterious wonders of good and evil. Those spending their time here maintain a respectful tone of voice for others even when disagreeing with the strongest of adverse opinions. To those who have earned the right to join this collection of minds, all your thoughts on the future of this land are welcome.
113224: A large bulletin board, entitled "Tolkien", is mounted here.

A huge hall stretches away into the distance. Great arched doorways break the flow of the marbled walls. This is the Nexus: the great hall connecting all of the areas of Arda together. Above each archway is inscribed the name of the area to which it gives access.
113225: A large bulletin board, entitled "WesternZones", is mounted here.
113226: A large bulletin board, entitled "Isengard", is mounted here.

This is a very small, rectangular room. The walls are empty and made of dim black stones. In the middle of the room a small model has been placed on an oak table. The model shows a landscape, coloured and with very very small details, like trees and even tiny rabbits. In the middle of the model an impenetrable tower rises above the hills, surrounded by the Misty Mountains. A river runs wildly south from the tower, and not far south of it a ford can be seen, guarded by men on horses. Somehow the model still leaves something for your imagination, it doesn't tell the full tale, something urges you to stay here and look at it to find out what is amiss.
113227: A large bulletin board, entitled "Idea", is mounted here.
For a room which is supposed to represent the cream of great ideas, the contents of the room seem curiously devoid of any meaningful structure.
113228:
A large WARNING SIGN is here.
A large bulletin board, entitled "Bug", is mounted here.

This is a most unpleasant room. Millions of ugly little bugs, all different, are constantly crawling on the floor, pouring endlessly out of holes and cracks in the walls, and eventually up your legs, except those who hang from the ceiling and drop down into your hair instead. Fortunately, a huge battery of anti-bug equipment is hanging on the walls: Very strong insecticides, sticky paper tape, big aerosol cans of DDT, and several tame venus flytraps. Next to the equipment is a bug-proof sign: "All bugs are reported to this board. Please remove them as soon as they have been rectified. All builders are required to correct the bugs in their zones."
113229: The Entrance to the Ainur's Garden

A large bulletin board, entitled "Builder's", is mounted here.
The Hitchhiker's Guide to Construction on MUME is floating in the air here.

To the south of this paved square stands a massive iron gate, with delicate gilding and simple yet beautiful carvings. The small paving stones continue to the north, where the path enters an enclosure, and at the centre of this square a stairway leads down to the Builders' Library.
113230:
A sign with some instructions has been placed here.
A large bulletin board, entitled "Test Zones", is mounted here.

Here it is that the builders and supervisors of test zones communicate. They are often to be seen writing wordy yet wise posts on the board, and yet magically only they, and no others save the Valar can see these words of wisdom... Those wishing to build a testzone should read the sign in this room. Most of the other information (that can be found here and on board 6) is outdated. On a shelf, there are two important books (look books) concerned with testzone building.
113231: A large bulletin board, entitled "MiscZones", is mounted here.

This untidy room is cluttered with all manner of maps plans and documents. Long ago it served as the discussion room for miscellaneous zones, but these days it has fallen into disarray, being used as a rather untidy archive for information on superzones long completed. The Management apologises for any inconvenience, but we'd hate for you to be buried alive under all the archived information. For your own safety, we have restricted access to the hoardes of really useless documents stored here.
113232: A large bulletin board, entitled "Rohan", is mounted here.

You find yourself plunged into darkness. All light has suddenly been extinguished and you find your innards turn. Then after what seems an age, but is probably no more than an instant, a bright light appears about you, blinding in its white intensity. A small pool of illumination is created by the beam from above. You can see nothing else...everything is featureless. You stand alone, your body blanched by the brightness, naked under its scrutiny. Then it starts....a sound, faint at first....then little by little it gets louder. As it grows you start to make out its origin. The sound of metal scraping on stone, as if someone is deliberately dragging a blade across the hard floor. The scraping continues...louder and louder it gets, and all the while your mind becomes more and more focused on the origin. Who is making that sound? Why are they doing it? Are they drawing nearer? You long for the answers, you will endure anything just to have this come to an end...for resolution. Then, without notice the sound stops. Peace for an instant. Then a face appears at the edge of the light staring into your eyes....the Inquisitor has arrived!

113340: This dark corridor runs from north to south, descending from a large hall to the south, halting abruptly above a vertical shaft at its northern end. The shaft is long, and has smooth, rounded walls. A few scattered steps are visible sticking out of the sides of the shaft. The walls of the corridor are very smooth, lacking any sign of chisel or pickax.
113341: Slanting Corridor at the Bottom of a Shaft

This dark corridor climbs steeply from a huge cavern to the east, halting abruptly beneath a vertical shaft at its western end. The shaft is long and has smooth, rounded walls. A few scattered steps are visible sticking out of the sides of the shaft. The corridor walls are very smooth, lacking any sign of chisel or pickax.
113342: This hall is gigantic, spreading dozens of yards in all directions. Massive pillars tower over the floor, rising into murky darkness. Many pillars are broken, their bases surrounded by piles of shattered stone. Ornamented tiles cover the floor between piles of rubble; many are cracked or broken. There is a small portal in the western wall that leads to a dark corridor.
113368: Landing on the Eastern Wall of a Column Hall

A five yard wide landing protrudes from the eastern wall of a large hall. The hall extends to the north, south, and west. All that remains of the floor are scattered stand-alone platforms supported by columns and joined by narrow footbridges. Massive metal doors in the middle of the eastern wall face onto this landing. The doors seem to radiate magic, and appear to be both too heavy to move and too sturdy to break through.
113369: This square room is situated between two portals with massive metal doors. These doors seem to radiate magic. Runes are engraved on them, some glowing faintly; the doors look impossible to break through and too heavy to be moved. There are no handles or keyholes on the doors. However, there is a big metal lever situated in the middle of the room. It protrudes from the floor in a narrow groove.
113370: A twenty yard corridor with a square cross section connects massive metal doors on its western end to a deep pit on its eastern end. The corridor is paved with large marble tiles which vary in shade from white to dark grey. The pit occupies the entire width of the corridor on the eastern end; its walls are extremely smooth, making it folly to attempt to climb them.
113371: A tall statue of a dwarven warrior stands in a niche in the wall.

Four broad corridors meet at this underground junction. The western corridor ends after a few yards beneath a steep shaft with unclimbable walls. The other corridors lead into murky darkness to the north, south, and east. Deep, unnatural scratches mar the stone walls of the corridors.
113372: A tall statue of a dwarven warrior stands in a niche in the wall.

This tomb is small and cramped, with little room for anything other than the sarcophagi resting against the walls. The sarcophagi are covered with heavy lids. All of them are made from marble, with nearly illegible runes carved into their surfaces. There are several shallow niches in the walls in the gaps between sarcophagi. Two corridors exit the tomb; one leads north and the other east.
113373:
A tall statue of a dwarven warrior stands in a niche in the wall.
A stone sarcophagus lies on the floor.

A long, wide hall with a high ceiling extends to the east. The floor is paved with beautiful marble tiles and the walls are so smooth that they look polished. Sarcophagi stand along the walls and the scene of a large battle is carved into the rock behind them. There is a tunnel leading out of the hall to the south and to either side of it there is a wide niche.
113374: A tall statue of a dwarven warrior stands in a niche in the wall.

This cavern is natural in origin, with a few stalactites hanging from its ceiling. The floor is mostly level, though two large niches appear to have been carved into the rock. The niches are perfectly square and smoothly polished, and seem oddly vacant. There is a slightly smaller, more narrow niche on the opposite end of the room. This niche is not as well crafted as the twin niches opposite it. The walls of this chamber are made of various types of rock; the bottom layer is mostly granite, with a layer of quartz above that, finally ending at a limestone ceiling. Two tunnels exit this cavern, leading east and west.
113375: A tall statue of a dwarven warrior stands in a niche in the wall.

Three corridors meet at this crossroad. Though the walls of the corridors are rough and uneven, their uniform width and height suggest that they were not naturally made. The floor is covered with large black and green granite tiles, one of which is cracked. There are two deep niches in the eastern wall.
113376:
A tall statue of a dwarven warrior stands in a niche in the wall.
A stone sarcophagus lies on the floor.
A huge statue made of stone suddenly turns to life.
A huge statue made of stone suddenly turns to life.

A long, wide hall with a high ceiling extends to the west. The floor is paved with beautiful marble tiles and the walls are smooth and polished. Sarcophagi stand along the walls and a scene depicting a big battle is carved into the rock behind them. There are some runes on the eastern wall. A tunnel leads out of the hall to the south.
113377: A tall statue of a dwarven warrior stands in a niche in the wall.

This cavern is roughly circular, and has a diameter of roughly twenty yards. The walls and floor are solid and smooth, even though the composition of the rock varies significantly throughout the chamber. The rock is predominantly granite, with various hues ranging from dark green to grey. There is a pair of identical niches in the south-eastern part of the wall. Both are empty, and might seem to serve no purpose.
113378:
A tile protrudes from the southern wall.
A tall statue of a dwarven warrior stands in a niche in the wall.
A huge obsidian statue of a dwarven leader moves towards you.
A tall granite statue of a dwarven warrior moves towards you.

This corridor is dominated by a large portal in the southern wall that has massive metal doors. The doors have neither handle nor keyhole, and radiate a palpable magical aura. A small tile protrudes from the wall next to the doors, and there are two niches to either side of the portal. The corridor to the west appears to be well crafted, with a paved floor and tiled walls. To the east, however, the corridor is rough and unfinished.
113379:
A tall statue of a dwarven warrior stands in a niche in the wall.
A stone sarcophagus lies on the floor.

A long, wide hall with a high ceiling extends to the east and to the west. The floor is paved with beautiful marble tiles. There are two large sarcophagi along the northern wall, resting atop pedestals. There is a beautiful and detailed carving on the wall behind them. The slightest sound made in this tomb resonates through the halls, bouncing back and forth between the walls.
113380: A long hall leads from the north to the south; it is well built with walls of smooth tiles. Massive doors of metal stand as a portal in the northern wall of the hall. A roughly dug tunnel with crude steps carved from the bedrock leads steeply down at the southern end; the state of the tunnel down in comparison with this fine-looking corridor gives the impression of work in progress that was interrupted before it could be completed. The steps look wet and slippery, and a few show cracks. All things considered, it does not look too safe or stable.
113381: This crudely excavated tunnel runs mostly up and down. There are a number of rough steps in the tunnel walls, but these are slippery due to water dripping down on them from above. Some of the steps wobble dangerously when trod upon, and others are simply missing. The top of the tunnel ends in a small hall, and the bottom end expands into a damp cavern.
113382: Elongated Cavern with a Small Pool

There are many natural structures on the floor and ceiling here as water has penetrated into the cavern from above. Between the stalagmites, oddly-shaped columns and even a pool, the cavern's floor is a veritable obstacle course. None of the stalactites on the ceiling hang low enough be a danger; should one fall however, it might prove fatal for anyone below it.
113383: A long cavern extends here from the east. The ground is level in this part of the cave, but to the east it grows rugged where dripping water has created many stalagmites. There is a large hole, roughly ten yards in diameter, in the ceiling. The hole is both too high and too far from any nearby walls for it to be possible to climb up into it. A tunnel opens in the western wall of the cave.
113384: Tunnel at the Foot of Spiral Stairs

This tunnel cuts straight through solid rock. The walls are smooth and unadorned. There are small recesses in the walls every few yards, possibly used for placement of light sources. To the east, the tunnel slowly widens as it enters a cavern. To the west, it ends under a spiral set of stairs.
113385: At the Top of Spiral Stairs
A tile protrudes from the northern wall.

A short corridor runs from north to south. To the south, the corridor ends at a staircase leading down, but to the north it meets a dead-end at a stone wall. The walls and floor are tiled with flat stones that fit closely together. One tile protrudes above the rest near the northern end of the corridor.
113398: This cavern is black as night and shaped like a funnel that opens up to the north and closes off towards a pile of rubble to the south. There are a few footprints on the ground, but because no flow of air reaches this forsaken place, there is no way of telling how old the tracks are.
113399: The absence of sounds and smells gives this quiet, damp cavern an air of desolation and abandonment. A fine dust has settled on the floor, where a line of tracks tell a tale that the place is used at least intermittently. The roof above is smooth, with just a handful of stalactites. A row of holes have been hacked out of the wall in some far distant past, but it is impossible to tell for what purpose.
113400: Here, a steady drip of water from above has turned the tunnel floor into a muddy mush. Whereas the ground seems drier in the southern portion of the space, tiny streams of water are flowing quietly towards the north. The cave walls are black, with a greenish tinge along the bottom - quite possibly some sort of lichen or mould.
113401: The tunnel floor tilts from south to north and from west to east. If it were not for the gritty, mud-like gravel on the tunnel floor, passage here would be slippery and perilous. Most of the water coming down from the cracks and stalactites above gathers along the eastern wall, forming a slowly trickling miniature stream that runs in a northerly direction.
113402: This tunnel slopes gently from north to south. A small stream of water is trickling along the eastern wall, gathering up the water that drips down from the dark, stalactite-ridden celiling above. A chopped-off torch mount has been fastened to the western wall, but it is now too old and decrepit to use.
113403: The most notable feature of this otherwise non-remarkable cavern are the two streams that meet here, one coming from the west and one from the south. The streams, each just a small but steady trickle, meet here and disappear into a black hole in lower northeastern corner of the cavern. There is a slight smell of mould in the air, coupled with something faint but far more unsavory.
113404: A rapid but quite small stream gushes out from a hole in the western wall. It rushes across the gravelly tunnel floor, heading in an eastwardly direction. Looking around the gravel reveals a number of dry patterns formed by the water, indicating that the water flow varies with time. Higher and somewhat drier ground can be reached by heading north. An odd, fungal smell hangs in the air.
113405:
A greenish slime mould is here, smelling badly.
A huge black fungus is here, exuding a foul stench.
A huge black fungus is here, exuding a foul stench.
A giant, strange looking green fungus is here, ready to devour you in seconds.

The cavern floor here forms a natural platform of sorts, with a couple of crude stairs leading down towards the south. A rich, fungal smell hangs in the air, no doubt emanating from the many layers of fungus and mould that blanket the lower parts of the walls. There is a hole in the middle of the platform, about four by four foot in size. A black, sooty patch can be seen in the north-eastern corner of the platform, where ages ago someone lit a camp fire.
113407: A half-rotten corpse is hanging here.

The tunnel ends abruptly in a huge web, with several cocoons visible from where you are. Large amounts of bones are scattered about on the floor, and the smell of rotting flesh is almost overwhelming.
113408:
An old, strong cave troll is standing here.
An old, strong cave troll is standing here.

This tunnel is filled with rubble and broken rocks, making the ceiling appear low. Most of the rocks are large enough not to shift underfoot, although some are unstable; passage over and through the rubble is made more difficult by the latter, as sudden shifts can reveal surprisingly deep crevices in the otherwise tightly-packed debris. The rubble has been cleared from the very southern part of this tunnel, revealing a large and relatively level passageway; for whatever reason, the rest of the tunnel has not been cleared in a similar fashion.
113409: A Wooden Cottage under the Three Trees
A humble man stands here, ready to help you with your things.

A square cottage built from wooden logs stands under three tall trees. Its walls are covered with ivy a small sand path leads between flowers beds to a front wooden door surrounded with a pair of glazed windows. There is a living room with a small kitchen and a big fireplace, a bedroom with a bed and a wardrobe, a storeroom with a lot of shelves and an underground cellar in the cottage. All the place is tidy and cosy.
113410: A humble man stands here, ready to help you with your things.

Fresh pine needles are strewn about the wooden floor, adding both a pleasant aroma and a natural filter for bugs. A few open windows add fresh air and extra light to the room, often disturbing the needles and creating patches of bare floor. An oak cabinet against the northern wall is half-open, its contents visible to all. A small ornamental chair and matching table offer small comfort to the room's inhabitants.
113411: A humble man stands here, ready to help you with your things.

This is a simple wooden structure located between two large wooden branches. The treehouse is modest and uncluttered with windows on every wall, enabling natural light to enter. A rather unusual feature is the roof overhead that appears almost transparent. A simple carpet covers the wooden floor, often used for meditations.
113413: The road narrows considerably as it passes over an undersized bridge. Designed to cross a small gully where water collects during rainstorms, the bridge remains in place and barely useable. Rotten in places, the wooden roadway bends and creaks when crossed. From opposite ends of the bridge, the road continues to the west and east.
113414:
A grizzly cub is here, snarling loudly.
A grizzly cub is here, snarling loudly.
A huge grizzly bear is here, roaming the wild.

Tall strands of undergrowth choke the surroundings, blocking passage in all directions except to the south. The shade from the slope to the east, combined with the dense growth, creates an environment where wildlife can flourish. In the few spots of earth that is not covered by growth or fallen bramble, the footprints of some large, heavy beast can be seen.
113416:
A doorwarden stands here ready to obey his master's wishes.
A tall and strong guard is here.
A tall and strong guard is here.

A small entrance is made of several oak planks with dirt pressed between the cracks. Round windows on each side of the hole add some natural light to the entrance. Large planks of carved oak wood can be spotted in the corners and in the ceiling of this circular room. A small chandelier hangs down in the centre, illuminating the entrance when natural light is insufficient. A makeshift stable has been erected in the eastern corner, although there is not enough room to ride for sure.
113417:
A small oaken table has been set here.
A tall and strong guard is here.
A tall and strong guard is here.

This lounge is richly decorated. Beautiful wooden figures hanging on the walls are quite the sight for visitors in this lounge. A table is placed in the centre of this room, small lavishly decorated chairs are lined up around the table. In the western corner the is a small staircase with wooden carved banisters.
113418:
The corpse of a village guard is lying here.
The corpse of a village guard is lying here.
The corpse of a Beorning captain of the guard is lying here.
The corpse of a village guard is lying here.
The corpse of a large black warg is lying here.
The corpse of a village guard is lying here.
A circular stone well has been built here.

A shattered well stands in the centre of the square of this village. The posts of the well have been broken in half, the roof burnt, and the bricks pulled out of place. Beneath the watchtower that used to protect this village lies the trapdoor that sat at the top of the watchtower's ladder. Both the trapdoor and the ladder have been damaged, but the ladder is only charred while all that remains of the trapdoor are the metal straps that used to hold in place. On the north of the square lies a razed forge while to the west there once stood a house.
113419:
A plate of roast duck and seasoned vegetables is here.
The corpse of a little girl is lying here.
The corpse of a young boy is lying here.
The corpse of a pig is lying here.
The corpse of a brown donkey is lying here.
The corpse of a pig is lying here.

A pig's head is impaled on the northern post that made the frame of the broken western gate. On the ground there are two broken troughs, the water and fodder has mixed with pigs blood turning it into a red porridge. The wooden palisade is still solid enough to block all travel to the south and east. The barn north of here has been razed, and to the west the village is in just as bad a condition.
113420:
The corpse of a mountain mule is lying here.
The corpse of a pack horse is lying here.
The corpse of a pack horse is lying here.
The corpse of a stable-hand is lying here.
The corpse of a mountain mule is lying here.

The ashes are still smouldering in what was once a barn. The fire must have blazed fiercely when it passed through here. Covered in ashes on the ground are burnt animal corpses. Their meat has been burned off and they are now inedible. A charred palisade runs beside the barn to the north and east and it still blocks any exit. West of here there is a razed forge and to the south are the remains of a wooded pasture.
113421:
The corpse of a soot-covered craftsman is lying here.
A pair of tongs lie on the ground.
A dented pail has been carelessly left here.

Not much remains of what once was a forge. The only thing still standing intact here is a blackened and battered old anvil. Scattered among the other pieces of debris are partly melted tools. The fire here must have fed on the forge's fuel to reach a temperature hot enough to damage even the lowest quality tools. North of here the burnt but partly intact palisade still prevents people from leaving or entering the village that way.
113422: A fire has raged without mercy here. The only things that are not totally burnt to the ground are the logs that make up the wooden palisade, and they have taken quite a bit of fire damage. This small village has been badly hurt by fire, and little of this house remains. East of here there is a razed forge and to the south there is more burnt debris.
113423:
A plate of roast duck and seasoned vegetables is here.
The corpse of a Beorning woman is lying here.
A stove stands against one wall here.

Burnt and blackened logs are scattered about among the ashes on the ground. An ash-covered chimney made of stone is the only thing still standing erect. To the north there is only debris and ashes while to the west and south lie the burnt remains of the palisade. East of here is the regular entrance to this destroyed village.
113424: A humble man stands here, ready to help you with your things.

Tall obsidian pillars rise from the dark floor of this ominous hall and stretch to the curved ceiling above. Glowing runes woven with silver and gold adorn the pillars, narrating Iror's many adventures and triumphs. Rising from the center of the hall is an obsidian throne, so dark it appears to absorb the light which fills the hall from two roaring fireplaces. Flanking the throne are many niches delved between the pillars consisting of Iror's personal library, bed chambers, and other rooms. A lectern stands in front of the throne, with a hastily scribbled scroll tossed upon it...
113425: A humble man stands here, ready to help you with your things.

The room has been carved from granite, now smooth like glass. A fireplace in the southern part heats the room. A bed sits against the western wall, and to the east a small desk and a chair. A sconce above the desk holds a lit torch, giving light to the workspace. A small sign has been nailed to one of the walls. A small ventilation shaft can be seen high up in the north-eastern corner of the ceiling, leading in air which streams out through the roaring fireplace, giving the room good ventilation. The granite floor is slightly heated from the grand fireplace.
113426: Exquisite chandeliers of glimmering metals embedded with shining gemstones have been mounted on the walls, bathing the large hall in a warm light and showing the great craftmanship that has perfected the hard rock of Ered Luin into smooth walls. Centered in the room is a long table made from dark mahogany, large enough to host a full party of adventurers. The seats are mostly fit for dwarves, but a few are there for occasional guests of other races. At the head of the table is an ebony chair, almost looking like a throne, where the host can salute his guests with glasses full of fine beverages. Parts of the walls are covered with heavy draperies of crimson, hemlined with gilded thread. A somewhat greasy hearth along the northern wall is used to keep the awaiting dishes hot during long meals.
113427:
A swarthy Dunlending warrior is here, guarding his village against intruders.
A swarthy Dunlending warrior is here, guarding his village against intruders.
A Dunlending warrior stands here, guarding the gates.
A swarthy Dunlending warrior is here, guarding his village against intruders.

The ground underfoot has been well-trod into nought but dust and mud. Little grows here other than isolated tufts of grass. There is a simple rickety-looking fence to the west, extending north and south to separate a tent camp on this side of the fence from the surrounding fields. A gap in the fence, barely wide enough to allow a wagon, allows access to the outside.
113428: The ground here is well-trampled and the grass has been churned to dirt and mud. A rickety-looking fence to the west separates the inside of this camp from grassy fields on the other side. There is a large tent to the north, and numerous other tents to the east and south.
113429:
A Dunlending Captain is here, overseeing his men.
A large dog curls his lips back and snarls.
A large dog curls his lips back and snarls.
A swarthy Dunlending warrior is here, guarding his village against intruders.
A half wolf is here, loyally protecting his master.

The grass has been beaten down and flattened by what looks to be numerous feet, hooves, and cart wheels. A little pothole, probably created by removing a stone that was damaging wagon wheels, lies in wait to trip up inobservant travellers. Every few yards, paths branch off leading in the direction of tent entrances.
113430:
A sturdy trained horse is standing here.
A sturdy trained horse is standing here.

This tent serves as a temporary shelter and stable for horses. Mounds of straw sit against the western tent-wall. Cloth flaps separate the stalls of individual horses. Saddles and other riding supplies hang from racks flanking the entrance to the tent. The air is stale and filled with the odour of horses and horse-dung.
113431:
A weapons rack stands against the wall.
In the rack are two longswords and two longspears.
A swarthy Dunlending warrior is here, guarding his village against intruders.
A leather-clad man moves nearby, keeping to the shadows (hidden).

This floor is lined with haphazardly laid bedrolls overlapping in heaps. Clearly, many sleepers occupy this tent, though there would be little room for them to do anything else. Various pieces of cast-off equipment scattered around the entrance suggest a martial purpose to this shelter.
113432:
A water barrel has been left here.
A small oaken table has been set here.
On the table, there are six pieces of smoked, cured meat.
A swarthy Dunlending warrior is here, guarding his village against intruders.

There are several long, low tables with benches in the centre of this very large tent. Along the north wall there are stone ovens and an open firepit. Several sturdy spits are suspened over the fires, and several hanging carcasses roast in the flames. Rows of wooden poles, fifteen feet tall, hold up the tent's ceiling.
113433:
A Dunlending warrior stands here, guarding the gates.
A Dunlending warrior stands here, guarding the gates.
A Dunlending Captain is here, overseeing his men.
A large dog curls his lips back and snarls.
A large dog curls his lips back and snarls.
A swarthy Dunlending warrior is here, guarding his village against intruders.
A swarthy Dunlending warrior is here, guarding his village against intruders.

The grass here has been flattened by many boots and hoof prints. To the north, a rickety-looking fence extends to the east and west, marking the borders of this tent-camp. A narrow gap in the fence is the only exit from the camp here. Just inside the gap, a heavy wooden stake with a T-shaped cross section has been placed in the ground, perfect for securing animals.
113434:
A mass of tattered fabric lies here in a heap.
A mass of tattered fabric lies here in a heap.
A small child is here playing happily.
A small child is here playing happily.
A Dunlending woman is here tending to her children.
A Dunlending woman is here tending to her children.

This tent appears to serve many occupants as a home. Tattered bedding sits on the floor in many sorry piles. The structure of the tent is in ill repair; mismatched patches cover the many tears in the fabric. There is a gaping hole in the roof and a simple fireplace in the form of a ring of stones on the ground beneath it.
113435:
A Dunlending Captain is here, overseeing his men.
A large dog curls his lips back and snarls.
A large dog curls his lips back and snarls.
A swarthy Dunlending warrior is here, guarding his village against intruders.
A half wolf is here, loyally protecting his master.

This is an intersection on the pathway going through the camp. A large tent is visible to the south-east. The tent is made of high quality canvas that stands out amongst the more crude tents surrounding it. It can probably protect the inhabitants from harshest of storms.
113436: Surrounded by mud and torn up grass on all sides, a small clump of blooming flowers has been left untouched. There are tents in every direction, but the one to the east stands out amongst the rest. It is very large and while some of the other tents look worn and threadbare, this one is very fine.
113437: A large flat stone lies on the ground outside a tent.

Several tents line the inside of a simple fence to the south and east. The green grass is thoroughly trampled near the tent entrances and several paths lead between the tents and towards the north. A long flattish stone lies on the ground outside a tent to the east, its surface scratched and scarred and blotched by patches of dark crimson.
113440: A heavy white stone sits in the corner.

A hastily constructed furnace surrounded by a haze of smoke looms in the back of the tent. A neatly stacked hoard of recently forged weapons is cooling in the dirt, while next to it lies a pile of damaged pots and pans which have yet to be mended.
113441:
A sturdy crate made of nailed wooden planks sits on the floor.
A weapons rack stands against the wall.
In the rack are a longsword and a longspear.

A makeshift wooden building has been set up on a patch of trampled grass. Armour, weapons, and arrows lie in scattered heaps on the floor. There seems to be little organization to the layout. The building has a roof and four walls, but where there should be doors, there are just wide openings, leaving the interior exposed to the elements.
113445: This abode appears to have seen better days. The tent walls are threadbare and tears in the fabric have been stitched and patched in numerous places. The contents look simple but functional, with bedpiles of animal furs and crude cooking utensils gathered around a small fireplace in the centre of the tent.
113446:
There is a water skin lying on the ground.
A large sack is on the ground.
A saddlecloth lies here on the ground. (blue aura).

This tent looks to be the home of at least ten people, judging by the bedrolls of fur that lie along its walls. There is a stone-ringed fireplace in the middle, beneath a small hole in the tent's ceiling. Next to each bedroll lie belongings to the occupant. Old worn saddles, sacks and backpacks, and all the various items a life in a camp brings with it.
113449: The awning of this fortress of cloth sags voluptuously overhead. At the centre of the abode, an intricately carved pole has been planted in the ground. It towers above, supporting the heavy swaths of canvas that billow out forming the sides of the pavilion. Through the folds, three yawning openings can be seen.
113450: A layer of fine skins and furs covers the tent floor, making it soft despite the hard ground beneath it. Many partitions along the wall to the south indicate small quarters for those of lesser status. An ornate flap of fine, oiled skins spanning the centre of the northern wall indicates a chamber belonging to someone of high standing.
113451: A brightly lit, spacious chamber stretches to the limits of the canvas walls. Straw and sawdust cover the floor. A long table, simple in design, yet well polished and sturdily built takes up most of the space in the centre of the room with long benches stretching along its sides. A chair much grander than the other graces the head of the table with its presence.
113452:
A swarthy Dunlending warrior is here, guarding his village against intruders.
A Dunlending gateguard stands at guard here.

So encased in fabric are the walls that not a sound can be heard through them. The air in here hangs desperately motionless, hot and heavy. Heaps of fine linens and rugs swallow all but the most forceful of footsteps. The chamber is lit by a single lamp, casting a warm glow about the room.
113453:
A swarthy Dunlending warrior is here, guarding his village against intruders.
A swarthy Dunlending warrior is here, guarding his village against intruders.
A swarthy Dunlending warrior is here, guarding his village against intruders.
A towering Dunlending warlord looks about in contemptuous dismissal.

Ostentatious wealth is writ in the decor of this chamber. Weapons both vicious and ornamental line one wall, well-crafted armour and shields another. Novelties of all sorts hang prominently from the ceiling: trophies, teeth, jewellery. A mound of fine furs and hides sits in the centre of the chamber, and several cushions face it in a circle.
113456: Foot of a Massive Oak Tree

The trunk of a massive oak tree captivates the eye. Its bark has had several large wooden planks attached to it in several places, creating a makeshift path upwards into the tree, wide enough to even accommodate four-legged creatures. It leads towards an immense branch that has many offshoots. Time has also created a trail that leads from the north to the east.
113457: Thick hedges accompany a meandering path that follows the Bruinen river, which continues in a general east-west fashion. The path curves quite often, making way for random boulders, budding trees and thick bushes. Some of the bushes are quite thorny, but have been trimmed in order to limit exposure.
113458:
An erect shrub with green pinnate leaves is growing here.
Inside the shrub, there are some crimson raspberries.
A sprawling green bush of stinging nettle grows here.

A soft path runs alongside the Bruinen river. Lush grass grows all around, interspersed with a few cottages of various sizes that have a perfect view of the river; some with small gardens attached and some with a small orchard instead. An oak tree stands tall between two of the cottages; once the seedling of the massive oak noticed to the far west perhaps, with another small cottage being held aloft by large branches. Several bushes accompany the path and all are neatly trimmed, providing a source of food for the local wildlife.
113466: Foot of a Massive Beech Tree

The trunks of a great beech tree stands with many of its kin, the biggest one save for one oak tree directly to the north by which it pales in comparison. A rope ladder hangs next to this massive beech tree, allowing one access to the upper branches. The forest floor is soft and even, with small trails leading to every tree. A tributary of the river Bruinen lies close by, a pier upon it can be found to the south.
113467: A small wooden pier offers a sturdy surface over the river tributary. Most of the wood is quite weathered, warped and faded by the elements, although several spots at the end of the pier hint of them being repaired recently, as the wood there is almost pristine. An abandoned bucket rests at the end of the pier, upturned and cracked.
113474: A humble man stands here, ready to help you with your things.

Dimly lit, this particular room looks like a study, with a small desk and matching chair standing in one corner, covered with hundreds of pieces of paper with varying degrees of unintelligable scribbles. The faint odour of something burning lingers, although no flame or smoke are visible. The frame of a bed stands on the opposite side of the desk, relatively clear of debris, with a small feather mattress and blanket.
113475:
A sturdy bed made from solid oak lies here, covered in warm blankets.
A humble man stands here, ready to help you with your things.

In a quiet section of Rivendell stands this humble home. While modest in size, the grand views of the valley impress beyond imagination. Flowerbeds surround the windows filling the air with a sweet fragrance. A small bed sits under the south window which frames the cascading waterfall above. On the west wall a simple kitchen lined with cupboards catches the eye. The cupboards are filled with delicate plates and glasses of the highest quality.
113476: A humble man stands here, ready to help you with your things.

In a silent corner of the winding building is a surprisingly spacious abode, perfect for a small bed. The room is decorated sparsely with a handful of maps, many of which are faded and hardly recognisable due to heavy usage. A bookshelf, worn at the edges as if itself had once been read from cover to cover, is the other singular piece of furniture. A tidy and clean atmosphere sets the surroundings. A selection of aged, yet clean rugs, slightly mismatched in colour have been placed carefully across the floor, small areas of pine appearing among the gaps, creating the impression of wooden slats between the fading colours. Cutting across the ceiling is a single bolt of lightning, carved into the granite roof, appearing to lack the deliberate care of the rest of the room.
113477:
A sturdy bed made from solid oak lies here, covered in warm blankets.
A humble man stands here, ready to help you with your things.

This room is the bedchamber of half-elven Taramikir. The room itself has precise quadrate dimensions, its walls are high and made out of mahogany from the forest of Fangorn. Burgundy-coloured bookshelves fill the western side of the room, facing two enormous portraits adjacent to the door. The enchanted glass floor emits a bright, glowing light, creating a warm and cosy atmosphere.
113478:
A sturdy pack horse is standing here.
A humble man stands here, ready to help you with your things.

Situated at the edge of the plateau, you find yourself in a tidy but cluttered room with shelving lining almost every wall. Most of the shelves contain books and scrolls, but there are also a variety of keepsakes from the many adventures of Faeona. On the west wall, there is a large window overlooking the steep western slope and the expansive valley below. The windowsill is lined with colourful rocks, various bones from what appear to be very small creatures, and slender containers filled with fragrant herbs. On the floor, carpets and cushions of assorted sizes are piled in configurations suitable for sitting and sleeping. You feel quite relaxed and welcome in this space.
113479: Several thick branches form a steady platform to walk upon. A great many of these branches have offshoots, and although they are not as substantial as the branch they come from, they still appear to be able to support a great deal of weight upon them. Most of the bark that one would stand on has been smoothed down by constant use.
113480: Thick Branch with a Rope Bridge

The branch extends far out from the tree, and at one point it is connected to a rope bridge that leads to the south. The bridge appears to be very sturdy, made from quality rope and several pieces of beech wood. It should be able to hold the weight of many. At a considerable distance from the ground, it provides a great way to travel from tree to tree.
113481: Several thick oak branches grow tightly together, their sturdiness forming a steadfast platform to walk upon. Several structures have been erected upon some of them, offering a place to rest up high if one should wish. The branches appear to be maintained regularly, shown by trimmed offshoots and smoothed down bark, as to not trip or hinder.
113482: Several branches at this level have grown very closely together, almost intertwining. The wood used for building the houses and the platform are of the same colours and patterns as the tree's bark, making it appear as if they are growths of the great oak. The massive tree that houses all of this appears to be tower over all the others, which might give a great view on top.
113483: A great oaken tree features several thick yet flat branches upon which a makeshift platform has been created. The platform is close by the trunk of the tree, which has been smoothed in several locations. Several small markings have been carved into the smoothed bark. A few stubs of what were branches have been fashioned into small seats, for one to rest upon if required.
113484: A Thick Branch with a Rope Bridge

A very thick and heavy branch leads out from the massive beech tree. The branch ends by going upwards, its tips being used as an anchor for a rope bridge that leads to another tree to the north. The bridge is made out of quality rope from the finest elven craftsmen with several pieces of beech wood creating a path for both animal and humanoids to walk upon.
113485: High up in a Massive Beech Tree

Several planks have been roped onto thick branches, forming a makeshift platform. many of the planks bear a great deal of scratches and bite-marks, clearly made by otters, when the tree these planks came from stood by a river's bank. A very thick rope ladder has been attached to the thickest branch leading downwards.
113486:
A colourful tapestry strikes a sharp contrast with its surroundings.
A small oaken table has been set here.
On the table, there are two apples and a juicy plum.

A great hollowed branch has been turned into a shrine for Yavanna. The branch ends in a knot to the east, where a large tapestry depicts her as a tall female in a green robe, crowned with the Sun. She stands in front of a large tree, and from all its branches a golden dew falls upon the barren earth, which appears to blossom afterwards. Several small tables are spread across the shrine, each with small tokens to be offered to the goddess. Two crystal lamps light up the hollow branch, a reminder of her greatest works.
113488: High up in a Massive Beech Tree

A couple of thick and flat branches have grown closely together. Thick and sturdy rope ties them together, forming a makeshift platform. A few structures have been erected on the branches, creating residences high up in the tree. The massive beech tree that houses all of this is surrounded by similarly huge trees, which mostly block the view. A smaller branch leads to the south, over the water.
113489: High up in a Massive Beech Tree

A grotesquely large branch of a beech tree has many offshoots that each appear to lead to a separate treehouse. Some of them are much more lavish than others, with many embellishments adorned into the wood, while others appear to be in a state of disrepair. A few signs hang against the massive beech tree, describing a rope bridge to the north leading to another tree.
113497: High up in a Massive Oak Tree

Thick webs made out of sturdy rope have been hung between several branches. The oak branches have been reinforced upwards as well with matching wood, giving the appearance of wooden structures growing out of the tree. A few cloth tarps have been securely draped over some of the branches, creating resting spots for weary travellers or visiting citizens.
113498: Top of a Massive Oak Tree

At the top of a massive oak tree, one particular spot has been cleared of twigs and branches with several planks forming a platform, offering a resting spot with a magnificent view of the valley. Close by is a grove of matching oak and some beech trees, although none have reached to the size of this tree, which towers over all the others.
113499: High up in a Massive Oak Tree

Five great oak boughs that grow close together have been bound together by a giant net of rope. This provides a makeshift hallway leading to various treehouses constructed out of different kinds of wood, although they are predominantly oak just like the tree they are built upon. A roof of slender branches provides at the very least a semblance of cover from the elements.
113500: High up in a Massive Oak Tree

Thick oaken planks have been tied to great branches, creating a steady path to walk upon. A few ropes have been securely attached overhead, leading to a small treehouse. A few benches have been installed against the trunk of the tree, although there is little view to be had, as the branches and the crafted treehouses that have been built upon it, block most of the view.
113501: High up in a Massive Oak Tree

An enormous branch has entwined itself with another, forming a small boulevard for one to walk upon. The oak branches are mostly flat, and have been smoothed in other areas in order to prevent a nasty fall down. The branches have several limbs, each forming a narrow walkway to a treehouse. Each has its own different flair, hinting of a broad range of tastes from its inhabitants.
113502: A thick beech branch overlooks a deep part of a tributary of the Bruinen. The branch is moderately steady, sturdy yet slightly swaying. Although the branch is not very wide, it could support a fair bit of weight. The massive tree that has spawned this branch can be found just north, where many of its branches have been usurped into becoming beams for treehouses.
113503: This is a tributary of the Bruinen, so deep that even the tallest elf could plunge in it and not reach the bottom. The water is clear and mostly still, and the bottom shows only a bare minimum of rocks. Some large fish can be seen moving far below, undisturbed by the various ongoings on the water's surface.
113504:
An apple tree with bright green leaves grows here.
On the tree's branches are three apples.

All around are the remains of old ruins. Many plants, from grass to bushes and even trees, have been able to take root in between the broken buildings. The result is a wild park right in the city of fornost. Long vines and other creeping plants cover many of the old stones. It appears that some citizens have built small houses in places at the borders of the wild park.
113505: A cockroach is scuttling across the floor carrying some debris.

Rustic stones reach high around a marble door, with opulent tapestries lining each wall of the entranceway. In stark contrast is the ceiling overhead, depicting several identical white trees. The entrance also serves as an impromptu cloakroom, with several coat racks standing near the door. A solid purple carpet with gold-coloured fringes provides a soft surface to walk upon.
113506:
A marble slate engraved with a plaque hangs on the wall.
A cockroach is scuttling across the floor carrying some debris.

Two sets of carpeted stairs occupy much of the nexus, leading up and down in a clock-wise direction. A wavy oaken bannister follows the stairs, offering a handhold for unsteady feet. Two rectangular metal hatches are installed on either side of the stairs. The left hatch is marked as a chute, while the right hatch is accompanied by securely fastened ropes, branding it a dumbwaiter. A small plaque has been fastened on one of the walls.
113507: A cockroach is scuttling across the floor carrying some debris.

A carpeted hallway passes by many doors of various makes and sizes, abodes of the locals of Fornost. Small lanterns emit a muted light and a musty smell permeates the air, both due to a lack of windows. A few tapestries decorate the walls, although many of them have a small coat of dust upon them. Well-cut stones lie behind and beside the tapestries, a sign of a robust and durable building.
113508: Several small lanterns have been fastened against the walls of the hallway, adding a touch of light to illuminate the way, but not enough to notice the dust that has accumulated. A carpet that is mostly violet with yellow-coloured fringes lines the hallway in a north-south fashion, passing by a multitude of different doors, each a different size and make. A few small paintings have been hung on the walls, yet care has been taken that they are far away from the lanterns.
113509: A luxurious purple carpet with frayed fringes covers most of the hallway floor, passing by several small apartments. The doors that lead into these dwellings vary in size and make, some locked and others bolted shut. The overhead ceiling is only eight feet high, tall enough for most Dunedain. A few lanterns are ensconced along the wall, providing light where the Sun cannot reach.
113510: A small layer of dust is visible by the light of small lanterns that have been attached to the walls in between some of the doors that line the hallway. A slightly frayed purple carpet with yellow fringes covers most of the floor, following the hallway to both the east and the south. No tapestries or paintings can be found in this section, although the wall on the eastern side features a large mural.
113511:
A small oaken table has been set here.
A cockroach is scuttling across the floor carrying some debris.

Small lanterns set in the walls illuminate the carpeted hallway, providing a small amount of heat and light to lead visitors of the tower to their destination. The rest of the walls are unusually bare, although some of the stones have been etched with seemingly random symbols. The ceiling overhead is equally bare, but a warm violet carpet with gold fringes covers much of the floor. The northeast corner is anything but bare, and seems to be a haven for clutter.
113512:
A mailbox stands here stuffed full of messages.
A large bookshelf sits against the wall.
On the bookshelf, there are a cooking book and a copy of The Mortal's Guide to Building.
A heavy desk, made of solid oak, stands here.
A cockroach is scuttling across the floor carrying some debris.

A few bookshelves line the eastern wall, mostly devoid of books and somewhat dusty. The books that are present are arranged chaotically and bear signs of misuse. A few writing desks with matching chairs form somewhat of a circle in the middle of the room. The northern corner bears a small window with a cage hanging next to it. Small feathers and down are sprinkled in and below the cage, as well as a specks of parchment and a single broken small tube.
113513: A marble slate engraved with a plaque hangs on the wall.

A staircase occupies most of the area, with the stairs going both up and down in a clockwise fashion. A blockage of several wooden planks nailed together has been erected to the south, preventing any from exploring this floor. At the moment, the only way out would be to go up or down the stairs. A wavy bannister made of oak serves as a handrail.
113514: A marble slate engraved with a plaque hangs on the wall.

The stairs and wavy oak bannister end at the top of the tower. A balcony can be spotted just to the south. Three small rooms are marked in the other directions, their doors elaborate with lush tapestries hanging next to them. Two large lanterns have been affixed to the walls, lighting up the entire staircase and small hallway.
113515: A marble slate engraved with a plaque hangs on the wall.

A wavy oaken bannister ends in a swirl as the stairs it accompanies reaches the bottom. The end of a chute can be seen on the western wall, its shaft poking out of the wall as no hatch contains it. On the floor below the chute, several small fragments of bark remain, insinuating a recent use for moving firewood. A rectangular hatch can be found on the eastern side, labelled as a dumb waiter.
113516: A stone floor leads out to the outside, offering a good view over the city of Fornost. A balcony has been created out of several oak planks. An oaken balustrade serves as a railing, its spindles shaped like long Dunedain blades. A few planters stand on either side of the balcony, although they are devoid of any sort of vegetation. The balcony is barely sheltered, thus anyone upon it must suffer the rigours of the weather.
113517: Roughly dug dirt walls are reinforced by wooden support beams, creating a five foot high tunnel. The beams are quite sturdy and well maintained. A few lanterns have been securely attached with metal rods, their light showing a set of doors of varying sizes lining the walls. The packed dirt floor is mostly devoid of debris, although some dirt has moved around a bit due to trampling boots, collecting on a thick mat that ends at a stone entrance to the north. The tunnel continues to both the east and the west.
113518: A five foot high tunnel, dug out of thoroughly serves as a hallway for underground dwellings. Several small rough apartments have been created out of coarse dirt walls and wooden support beams, each exterior built with their own distinct flair. A lantern accompanies every door, so visitors and inhabitants alike can find their destination with ease. Some small rugs cover the packed dirt floor, where travellers can stomp the dirt off their boots. The tunnel continues to the west, where more homes can be found.
113519: A small stack of firewood, securely bound, stands neatly piled up against the western wall. A few empty boxes, odd pieces of furniture and a small broom closet make up the rest for the storage room. Near the closet is a small pile of dust, small wood chips and dust web: the sweepings from the basement area. One lamp attached on one of the walls, almost at the ceiling, lights up most of the storage room.
113520:
A small barrel made of aged oak and strong iron hoops stands here.
An oaken wine rack stands here.

Several wine racks line the northern wall, yet they are devoid of any actual wine, hinting of either a rambunctious night or a poor supply. The fruity smell of wine does linger, coming from several empty wine bottles that lie in a small pile beside a rack. The wine cellar is quite humid and no light sources adorn its walls, in order to protect the vintage. Round streaks mar the ground, an indication that several barrels were once stored here.
113521:
A sturdy bed made from solid oak lies here, covered in warm blankets.
A humble man stands here, ready to help you with your things.

The floor of this large room is elegantly set in a circular pattern, resembling the garden outside. Rings of marble in different nuances decorate the floor like ripples on a calm pool, spreading out from the spiralling iron staircase that runs through the centre of the whole tower like a giant metal spine. Large lancet windows distributed symmetrically around the walls allow the sunlight to shine in freely, bathing the entire room in bright light. Between the windows hang large silver chandeliers together with tapestries, showing images of proud warriors in battle. Two gilded beds stand on either side of the chamber.
113524:
A large cockroach is crawling on the floor.
A large cockroach is crawling up the wall.

Dark, damp and extremely cramped, this small tunnel seems to have been created by water flowing through a wide crack in the rocks on its way to the catacombs below. Stalactites hang from the low ceiling, formed from centuries of dripping water. These rock formations meet along the wall with stalagmites forming this tunnel. The faint sound of flowing water can be heard from the south.
113525:
A white-painted bench is here.
A sturdy bed made from solid oak lies here, covered in warm blankets.
A heavy desk, made of solid oak, stands here.
A humble man stands here, ready to help you with your things.

Oaken branches twist and turn, and with the aid of a few extra pieces of wood, a rudimentary treehouse has been created. Small spaces between the branches offer both a view of the valley on top of fresh air and light. A small carpet covers a small segment between the bed and the desk, footprints going back and forth deeply embedded within. One small painting of mallorn trees hangs next to the door, glowing with a golden hue that is faded in some places.
113527: An old white bear is crouching here, protecting his masters lair.

For those of Beorning descent, this cave feels right at home, bringing some of the wild in a more civilised settlement.
