The walls of the cave feature mixed shades of brown and grey; and are relatively clean. Very little litter can be found, signs that this dwelling is well-maintained. A fresh pile of leaves can be found in the back of the cave, marking it as the resting place of the cave's inhabitant. Sticky remains of honeycomb are spread on the cavern wall along with large claw marks. A neat pile of bones, most are broken in half and were abused by sharp teeth.
113535:
Some dirty oak barrels are piled up againt the wall.
A large, sturdy table made from oak is sitting here.
A humble man stands here, ready to help you with your things.

This sparsely furnitured room, albeit extremely messy to the point where it almost seems to be abandoned, somehow manages to give a homey impression. Various items such as magic scrolls, poorly written in Khuzdul and beer mugs have been carelessly left on the rocky floor. Dim light is shining in through a dirty lantern that is hanging from the ceiling. In the middle of the room there is a giant oak table with a small brewery that wouldn't even meet the standards of Olly's Tavern. A faint odour of yeast seems to be permanent in here.
113536: A humble man stands here, ready to help you with your things.

As you enter this home, the smell of sweat and leather fill your nose. Lying around the western corner are various types of dwarven training equipment which are all well used. You notice an office in the northern corner, whereupon a picture of Khurmin and his dwarven family is placed. In the eastern corner lies a makeshift bed, comfortable for most dwarves. Looking upwards you notice frescoes depicting the many wars of Arda.
113537: A clear spring babbles as cool water trickles out of the ground.

Small rocks are scattered around a well-tended trail that leads uphill to the east, and descends into a valley to the south. The path takes a detour around a very large boulder that is completely covered with moss and seems quite impossible to climb on top of. A small stream that seems to pop out of the ground is running in a northerly direction. On top of the hill to the east stands a high, white tower.
113539: Trail through a Valley in the Tower Hills

This valley cuts very deep through the Tower Hills, so deep that the sun rarely reaches its bottom. Because of that there is almost no vegetation here, only a few small tussocks of grass. A well-tended path runs through the valley in north-south direction while to the east and west the hillsides are so steep that they seem impossible to climb, even for an experienced climber.
113540: Trail through a Valley in the Tower Hills

Here the hills completely surround the wide, paved path that runs through the valley, bending gently along the valley floor towards the south, and breaking through a small opening to the north. The vegetation is very sparse, probably because the sun almost never reaches the bottom of this deep valley. The sides of the valley are so steep that it seems impossible to climb them at all.
113541: A shallow-looking ford has formed here where a well-tended path crosses a rocky brook. The brook flows between the cliffs, its water flowing in lazily from the east, crossing the shallow ford, then gathering speed as the brook narrows towards the west. An occasional fish can be seen, leaping high above the water surface. A stone-paved path runs from the ford, disappearing between the cliffs to the north, and connecting to a larger road to the south.
113542: Built into the white granite walls, beautifully arched sleeping alcoves cover most of the area of the room. Heavy curtains, made out of the finest cotton with delicate inlays of silver thread, which effectively reduce noise and light hang in front of every alcove. Placed in-between the alcoves, stands sturdy weapon racks filled with all kinds of weaponry. In the middle of the room, a large fireplace is placed, providing the room with light and heat.
113543: Deep fissures scar the hills, exposing twisted layers of rock in a remarkable display of orange, black, brown, and red layers. Flecks of mica and quartz reflect even the faintest of lights, twinkling like a million stars buried deep inside the hills. Only a small amount of vegetation has been able to find sufficient soil to take root here.
113544: This hill is a smaller cousin of the Tower Hills that rise to the north. Its slopes are gentle and easy to navigate. Thin grass reaches a foot or so in height, while white- and yellow-petaled eyebright and pearlwort rise above the grass on slender stems, adding variety to the terrain. The hills grow taller and rockier to the west.
113545: Dozens of low rocky peaks thrust skyward, none of them of particularly large or tall. Jumbled boulders and stones lie strewn about everywhere, requiring some caution while moving. Many of the rocks are dotted with pale lichen, while others are coated with thick layers of bright green moss. Beyond and below the boulders and rocks to the north, a road winds its way through the valleys in-between the hills.
113546:
A stocky mountain mule is here, waiting to serve.
A roe deer is standing here, watching the terrain while chewing the vegetation.
A cute rabbit is here.

These rocky humps are barely tall enough to be called hills, though they are still rugged enough to slow travel. The hills are covered in equal parts of short, sturdy grass and bare brown rock. A narrow but deep crevice runs between the hills, severing the area from another set of hills just beyond and creating an isolated dead-end within the rocky terrain.
113551: Tall hills rise to the east and southwest of the road, which winds its way through the levelest path it can find. The road is worn and well-travelled, but still provides the easiest means of moving through this hilly area. The road runs nearly straight to the west, while it passes through several bends and twists before finally extending to the south.
113552: The Tower Hills rise on every side of this valley except to the south, where the valley continues. Enormous boulders of grey, brown, and pale orange lie scattered across the valley floor, accompanied by millions of smaller stones. There is little room left for vegetation, but grass and weeds have taken root in every available crack and crevice.
113553: A boar cub is playing here, and exploring the wide world.

The boulders that cover these hills are very large and worn down by the tides of time. Among the boulders, small green bushes grow. Elsewhere the ground is covered by soft, green grass that almost reaches a man's waist. A road crosses the hills to the south and a small path leaves it, leading north at the foot of the western slope.
113554: Many large rocks are scattered across the hillsides. Some of these rocks are so large that whole houses could be built on top of them. Far to the west you can distinguish a small mountain path winding its way through the hills, but to the north and south the hills continue uninterruptedly. The hills grow steeper towards the east, as the Tower Hills rises ever higher.
113555: A steep hillside completely blocks the way to the north here. Soft, green, grass covers the ground like a thick carpet. Half-concealed by the grass, many large round stones are scattered all across the hillsides. To the south, east, and west the mighty Tower Hills continue.
113582: A goat is here, grazing in the hills.

Small green bushes grow here and there between the patches of grass, which have been chewed almost down to their roots. This is the highest point on the hill; all around you see similar formations, like waves in the ocean. The north side of the hill is broken and steep. To the south the ground slopes down, just to rise up again into another hill. A large rock stands on the hill summit; on top of it a small birch has taken root. Beneath the rocks are some remains of an animal, decaying among the shrubs.
113587: The hillside slopes down toward a tall, rocky ridge, which looms high into the sky, blocking the way to the south. However, the hill itself slopes quite gently, and is covered by thick, deep green grass, and a scattering of small shrubs and bushes.
113588: The top of the hill lays to the south and it slopes northward. A small grassy patch lies between the shoulders of the hill. In the west the hill slopes down to some flatter ground. Rock and grass is all that's here.
113590:
A black crow flies low to the ground here, looking for carrion to eat.
A fallow deer is grazing peacefully here.
All around the hills grow taller. Here however the wind that blows hard upon the hills is blocked by them. Small gooseberry bushes grow here sheltered from the wind.
113591: Shrubs and stones cover the hills all around. This one is no different from the others. Traversing these hills and the dust from the dry grass is making you dizzy. To the south and west, the hill slopes downward.
113592: Small thorny bushes grow wild on the ground. In the west the hill slopes down to a valley. In all other directions the hills grow taller.
113593: A fallow deer is grazing peacefully here.

A tall ridge extending from the west to east prevents passage to the south. In the west the hillside drops suddenly down to the valley below. In the north seems to be a way down. In the east the hills continue. Ground is covered by grasses and shrubs. Some animals seem to be moving above the ridge, but unfortunately the grasses and bushes that grow upon it hide them from sight.
113595: Some gentle hills rise above a pleasant glen between the hills to the south. Grass has been eaten very short. The small bushes here and there have also lost some of their cover. Little plants with yellow flowers dot the ground, obviously shunned by the animals that graze here. To the north the hills come to an abrupt end and fall down many feet before reaching the level ground. To the west is a small forest. To the east the hills continue.
113597:
A swallow flies high above the ground.
A goat is here, grazing in the hills.
A swallow flies high above the ground.

Small green bushes grow here and there among the grass that covers the hills. A narrow wagon trail weaves a path between hills, keeping to the low ground to avoid steep slopes and other obstacles. A steep cliff to the west prevents access in that direction, and at the bottom of the cliff, nestled amidst vegetation and rocks, a small shingled roof peeks out.
113598:
A rabbit is here eyeing your presence warily.
A swallow flies high above the ground.

A dust-covered wagon trail weaves a path through shrub-covered hills and between boulders. A few large, thorny bushes grow on the west-facing slopes, but the area is devoid of trees. The hills grow steeper and taller towards the east, showing what inspired the name Tower Hills. Yet even so, the trail finds a route that avoids the worst of slopes and other obstacles.
113599: A wagon trail runs through the area here heading west and east. The trail shows signs of being fairly old, but is still usable. The rocky ground that is under the trail shows signs of breaking through at some points and is working on holding back the weeds that are attempting to gain a foothold. Hills slope upwards from the trail to the north and south.
113601: A woody evergreen plant grows here, with many stems reaching upward.

Called Emyn Beraid by the elves, the Tower Hills are ancient. Despite their age, time and erosion have not been able to completely blunt their edges, and sharp, narrow ridges thrust up between steep slopes. A thin layer of soil clings to the lower slopes, supporting coarse grass and weeds, along with a few stunted shrubs that bear pale yellow blossoms.
113612: The corpse of a slithering snake is lying here.

The road makes a smooth, graceful curve around a tall hill. From here, it extends to both the north and east. The road's surface is heavily worn, although there are signs that it has recently been repaired. Thin weeds wearily push their way through the scant soil beside the road.
113613: Very little vegetation clings to these barren, rocky slopes. Naked stone in hues of brown and pale grey dominate the landscape, rising and descending in a series of miniature ridges. The shallow valleys are filled with stones broken free from the hillsides, from tiny sharp flecks to massive boulders and every size in between.
113614:
A sprawling green bush of stinging nettle grows here.
A snake slithers towards you.

This hillside dips to the north and east, where a road winds its way through a valley. It is low and not very steep, allowing a fair accumulation of soil and plantlife. Coarse grass, low and broad-bladed, dominates the area, fighting for dominance with thistles and other weeds. Dandelions grow rampant among the other plants, dotting the hillside with specks of yellow.
113615: The road ascends a low, grassy hilltop, avoiding the more rocky and broken land to either side. The grass is thick and healthy, and has started to encroach on the road, threatening to overgrow it if not cut back. Taller hills rise to both the north and south, with the road running in a nearly straight line between them.
113616: Some great upheaval in the distant past has twisted and folded the landscape, creating swells and dips reminiscent of the sea yet frozen forever in stone. The ground is cracked in many places and littered with thousands of fragments of rock, some dulled with age, others much fresher and still sharp-edged. Most of the stone is medium grey, but there are patches of orange, brown, and even black.
113619: This hill does not rise as high as most of the Tower Hills, and is dwarfed in comparison to a much higher hilltop just to the north. Little soil has managed to accumulate on the hill's surface, leaving most of it as exposed rock and preventing much of any vegetation from growing here. Other than a few short flowers, only two small, twisted pines have managed to take root.
113621: A sharp-eyed hawk is here stalking some prey.

The trail bends and twists so much that it is difficult to maintain a straight course for more than a dozen yards at a time. The path dodges around boulders and upthrusts of bare stone, yet manages to remain nearly level despite the hills through which it passes. Pale yellow and pink blossoms decorate the tops of tall green stems, while purple glasswort hugs the rocky ground.
113623: The road runs both east and north, bending its way around a tall plateau. The road shows evidence of having been washed out several times, but it has been repaired recently and is in good condition. Thin weeds and stunted shrubs grow on either side, struggling to survive in the sandy soil. Low hills border the road to the south and west.
113624: A tall plateau rises to the north, an ominous sentinel standing guard over the land. The road runs almost due east and west near the base of the plateau. Many piles of broken rocks line the north edge of the road, and in some places they extended across and beyond the road, though the surface has now been cleared of stones.
113625: A tall plateau stands over the road to the north, while a much smaller hillside rises to the south. A small line of evergreens grow near the base of the cliff. They are mostly healthy, although several of them have been damaged or even completely smashed by falling rocks. A narrow dirt path splits off from the road and runs south into the hills.
113626: The road wraps around the base of a low hill to the southwest, maintaining as level a course as possible. As it extends further to the west, it runs along the base of a tall cliff. Thick grass runs along the eastern edge of the road and covers a series of low rolling hills in that direction, while the western hills seem to have rockier and less fertile soil.
113631: The earthy path is wide and well-travelled here; a lot of wagon tracks and footprints mark it. To the west, thick bushes surround the path, which gets increasingly narrow. Following the path to the east, it leads to the road to the Grey Havens.
113632: A dirty path runs along the base of the the large hill and widens westwards. Tiny round stones litter the hillside, giving no place for vegetation to grow. Five-foot high bushes frame the path, protecting it from direct sunlight.
113633: The tall and dense shrubbery conceals everything behind it, giving a home to various small animals. Only a few trees managed to get through the thick carpet of bushes to get to the sunlight. The path bends around the mossy rocks and large bushes. It continues to the east and west into the distance, but to the north it seems to connect to a larger road.
113634: A mean looking robber is here, demanding money from you.

A narrow trail of hard-packed earth runs from the north, where it connects to a larger road, to the south, where it winds its way into a series of hills. The path seems to be regularly travelled, as the grass that springs up on either side has not been able to reclaim it. A thinner, less used path extends from here to the east, creating a second connection to the road.
113635: Actually a very low hilltop, this field peaks near its centre, dropping off slightly in every direction. Short, thick grass covers the ground, though in some places where the soil is sandy the grass is replaced by thistles and other weeds. A few stunted shrubs dot the area, sporting blossoms of pale yellow and pink. Farther away to the south, an area of densely growing bushes borders the road.
113636:
On the ground, there are two handfuls of clover.
A black snake, with red markings, is lying here.

Were it not for scattered boulders and upthrusts of stone, this meadow could be mistaken for a broad, flat plain. The grass grows tall and lush. Narrow animal trails weave a dizzying network through the vegetation, and there are a number of signs of grazing. The meadow ends at a low cliff to the east. A flooded area with sick and dying vegetation lies at its base.
113637: A black snake, with red markings, is lying here.

Thousands of stones of every shape and size litter this meadow, from minute pebbles barely larger than sand to enormous boulders and upthrusts of brown and orange rock. Several species of grass have gained purchase between the stones, from short and thin but sturdy blades to tall, broad blades of emerald green. The meadow ends abruptly at a cliff that runs along its east and north edges.
113638: Several species of grasses vie with one another for primacy over this area. Tor-grass and whorl-grass seem to dominate, interspersed with taller oat-grass and to a lesser extent with thick-stemmed horsetails and white-tipped cottongrass. The field extends in every direction except to the west, where a tall plateau rises overhead and casts the field into deep shadows every afternoon.
113639:
A brown snake watches you.
A restless rabbit bounces around.

This narrow ridgeline rises over a deep, lush valley to the east. The centre of the ridge is grey stone, bare and lifeless, but on both sides soil and grass cling to the slopes, giving it almost the appearance of a roadway cut through a meadow. A deep crack splits the ground to the west between the descending side of the ridge and a tall plateau that rises just beyond.
113640: The trail looks like it has not received much use recently and is beginning to fade. It runs roughly north and south but winds somewhat in order to remain fairly flat. A tall plateau dominates the landscape to the east, preventing any sunlight from reaching the trail before noon. As a result, there is not much in the way of vegetation here, only a few stray weeds scattered among the rocks.
113641:
A hardened ranger is walking around, looking for tracks (hidden).
A hardened ranger is walking around, looking for tracks.
A cute rabbit is here.

The road extends in a straight line to the west where it ascends a small hill. To the east, a tall plateau rises over the road, shading it through much of the morning and forcing it to turn south. A pile of broken rocks lies at the base of the cliff, broken from its surface by ages of weathering. Some of the stones lie on the road itself, warning of the ever-present danger of landslides.
113648: Large boulders are scattered across the landscape. Between the boulders, small trees and lush green bushes try to survive in the infertile soil. To the west the hills fall steeply down to a small trail, to the south and the east the rocky landscape continues. A steep cliff wall bars passage to the north.
113649: This portion of the hilltop is largely flat, with only a few rises and dips. The area is covered with short but dense grass that has been heavily trampled. A few tents and crude buildings stand here and there around the hilltop. There are a dozen paths crossing one another seemingly at random, though most of them seem to lead in the cardinal directions. The level area extends both east and west, while becoming more rocky and broken to the north and south.
113650: A sturdy crate made of nailed wooden planks sits on the floor.

This looks like it is primarily a natural cave, though there are signs that it has been expanded slightly and the floor has been leveled. A rickety ladder rises against one wall, making it easy to return to the surface. Several old crates line the walls; many are clearly empty, but a few may contain something of value.
113651: An underground stream pushes out from a crack on the dark rock wall. The water splashes down to a small dark pool, then continues streaming southwards across a twisting rocky cavern. Green algae covers the moist walls here. At one time the current must have been stronger, for the cavern has been hollowed out enough to allow for the passage of creatures.
113652: A stream that flows from somewhere to the north of here spills into a large dark lake, which stretches off both south and east. The surface of the lake is disturbed by small ripples. A number of boulders have broken loose from the ceiling and impede the path of the stream in places. There is a small path next to the stream leading to the north.
113653: The dark water of the lake stretches off to the north, south and east, the surface disturbed only by the occasional ripple which can be seen rebounding from the rocky walls of the cavern. In the south-east a faint glimpse of land can be seen.
113654: A grey snake slides along the water.

Water flows into this underground lake from a small stream to the west. The surface of the lake is for the most part dark and still, but the occasional ripple disturbs its surface, as though some underwater creature is moving about stealthily. The lake stretches far to the south.
113655: The surface of the lake lies still and dark, disturbed only occasionally by small ripples. To the east the lake laps up against a shallow rock shelf which seems to be the beginning of a cavern. To the north the lake continues into darkness.
113656: To the north and west a rocky shelf slopes gently into the dark waters of an underground lake, while above and all around the rock walls form a natural tunnel of stone, cut from the rock by the passage of water. Green slime and algae grow on the walls in this damp atmosphere. The tunnel stretches out to the east.
113657:
The corpse of a thief is lying here.
The corpse of a mean brigand is lying here.
A small ironbound barrel made of fine oak rests here.
A large stone chest is here.
A small oaken table has been set here.
On the table, there are three smoked pieces of meat.

This room seems to be a naturally formed cavern, with the light from a torch hanging in an ordinary iron bracket reflecting brightly from the wet, glistening stonewalls. To the east the roof lowers, and there seems to be a smaller cavern in that direction. To the east the room opens out.
113658:
The corpse of a mean brigand is lying here.
The corpse of a mean brigand is lying here.
You see three musty loaves of bread on the ground.

This room looks like a small storage chamber. The walls drip with water, no doubt due to the dampness of the air down here, and this seems to have affected the food and other items stored here. Flour sacks and mouldy bread lie scattered about the floor, making the rock underfoot slippery with a foetid slime.
113659: The waters of the lake lap against a shallow horseshoe shaped rock shelf to the south, from where the lake radiates out north and west. This shelf seems to form a sort of beach, and looks like it is the entrance to a larger cavern behind. To the north and west the lake continues into darkness.
113660: Hidden into the dark shadows of the cavern's upper parts, a small passageway runs stealthily along the cavern walls. In many parts the pathway follows the natural shapes of the soil, whereas in some places it looks that the way through has been built on purpose. At the lower end, the passageway ends at a trapdoor. At the upper end, the tunnel elevates onwards to the darkness. Along the way, there is a skull lying in a niche in the passageway.
113683:
A long water trough made of wood stands here.
A rather dirty young boy is here, ready to tend to the stable.

Narrow wooden stalls filled with fresh-cut hay provide basic but comfortable accommodation for horses and mules of all kinds. Primitive but functional tack for use on the horses has been stored on a wooden trestle against the outer wall. A ladder leading to the loft space allows the stable-hands access to the bales of straw stored there.
113684:
There are two carrots here.
A freckled young girl with braided ponytails fidgets with her hands.

A cobble stone path connects the back of the stables into an open field lined with hedges on each side. The open field has been evenly divided into eight garden plots, each lined with stones, and richly planted with a variety of vegetables. A large pile of manure lies behind the stable and fills the air with an earthy smell.
113693: A young man is here, seemingly lost in a daydream.

This simple but tidy home has only the most basic of furnitures. A large fire place serves as a place to cook food and as a way to keep the house warm. By one wall stands a sturdy wooden cupboard, and a small table with a pair of simple chairs. There is only one window, and to either side of it there's a narrow bed, suggesting that two people live in this house.
113696: Three large farm-fields lie side by side just south of a small farmhouse. The fields look like they are tended to regularly, and the plants grow in ordered lines with no weeds in-between. A small pond borders the fields to the east while more crops grow to the south on other fields.
113697:
A fishing rod has been left here.
A placid pond is here, inviting you to take a refreshing drink.
A fisherman is sitting here, casting his rod.

The ground slopes down from the north before levelling off into a flat and well-tended farm field. Rows of crops have been sown in neat, north-south rows; only a few small weeds have escaped the farmer's eye, growing low and close to the ground. A simple stone wall forms a border to the field with a gap along the southern edge that might have once housed a gate; here and there, stones have fallen from the wall to sit in scattered piles at its base.
113698:
A small oaken table has been set here.
A large stone fireplace with a roaring fire warms the room.
The farmer's wife is bustling busily around.

This farm house is simple in design, consisting of only one large room. The walls, ceiling and floor are constructed from tight-fitting but unfinished wooden planks, their surfaces rough and somewhat uneven. The roof is peaked, rising up in the centre, with wide beams crossing the empty space. Thick cobwebs are visible among these rafters, offering a stark contrast to the rest of the room, which is tidy and well-kept. A small table sits in the centre of the room surrounded by three wooden chairs that are clearly hand-made.
113700:
An apple tree with bright green leaves grows here.
On the tree's branches are two apples.
A clear spring babbles as cool water trickles out of the ground.
A stocky mountain mule is here, waiting to serve.
A domesticated pony, beast of burden to many, stands here.

A large, grass-covered meadow extends over the slightly sloping field. The grass is emerald green, about two feet tall, and occasionally sway slightly with the wind. In the middle of the meadow, a copse of trees provides shade from the sun. A simple wooden fence encircles the area.
113701: A bale of wheat is lying here.

A wide wheat fields slopes lazily up and down as it extends over the area. The wheat itself is yellow-brown, almost golden in its colour, and grows about two feet tall. Next to the field, a small path runs to the north, towards a cottage that stands there amongst a group of trees.
113702:
A small, loyal beagle is here, eager to please.
A peaceful farmer is here, whistling merrily.

This small wooden farmhouse consists of but a single room crammed with furniture. A large fireplace dominates the northern wall, its hearth occupying a significant portion of the dwelling's floor space; a bed, table, chairs and several small cabinets occupy the remainder. The effect is claustrophobic; the chairs must be pushed under the table to move past, and care must be taken to avoid knocking into furniture when moving from one part of the room to another.
113703: This round windmill has one light and spacious room. In the centre of the room stands a big wooden trough for the milled flour, with a wooden pipe coming from upstairs above it. Next to the door stands a group of furniture; a table, some chairs and a cabinet. A narrow staircase leads to the upper floor, while the mill's outer door is on the southern wall.
113704: The upper floor of the windmill is dominated by two round millstones that lie on top of each other. The millstones are truly huge, approximately two yards wide, and around one feet thick apiece. Around the millstones, various axles and cogwheels fill the most of the space of this room. Narrow stairs, and a wooden pipe for flour, lead downstairs, while the thickest axle leads through the roof to a room above.
113705:
A small box has been left here.
A black raven flies around inside the mill.
A black raven flies around inside the mill.

This small round room exists at the top floor of the mill. A narrow level platform makes a full circle around the room, encircling the mill's engine. The engine is a complex-looking aggregation of cogwheels and axels, that get their power from the wings of the mill, and move it forward to make the millstones move. There is a small hole in the wall, from where one can see the four wooden wings of the mill.
113706:
A brass lantern has been set on the ground.
A sack of flour has been placed here.
A small barrel stands on the ground.

The huge doorway to the east has a high threshold that keeps seed and grains from blowing out as well as dirt or leaves from blowing in. A smooth, wooden floor spans the entire width of the barn. The ceiling is high and triangular in shape. Long beams of timber create a sturdy foundation and wooden planks complete the construction. A more regularly-sized door to the north separates the barn from the living area of this small farm.
113707:
A wooden chest stands in the corner.
A small oaken table has been set here.
On the table, there are a sack of pepper and a chunk of salt.

In this cosy house a gambrel roof rests on thick, sturdy beams of wood, obviously built to last. It has one big room, with an open fireplace in the centre that emits enough heat to keep the whole house warm. Next to the mantle is a wooden table and four stout chairs. Some cutlery, plates and a candelabra rest on it. A small loft sits about six feet up, along the western wall. It has four straw mattresses lying next to each other. Small glass windows offer views of the lush fields outside. The southern door leads into another structure; a barn or granary.
113708: Rickety stairs lead from a dirty cellar floor to a wooden hatch overhead. Small cobwebs have formed elaborate tapestries on the walls and rat droppings are scattered about alongside some straw. Small cracks adorn the walls, some partially hidden by a few torn cotton sacks that have been discarded. A lantern was installed at some point, but now it lies broken on the floor.
113709: A small barrel stands on the ground.

Mildewy walls and a dirty floor form a poor base for a root cellar. Several bags once-filled with grain feature bite-sized holes with several small pieces of chaff littering the ground next to them. Numerous narrow cracks can be found in the walls, some of them boarded up with various small wooden planks nailed together. A few barrels have been piled up against the eastern wall. One barrel lies on its side resting in a small pool of water, with a small crack visible.
113710:
A pitchfork has been carelessly left lying here.
A sturdy crate made of nailed wooden planks sits on the floor.

Crates of all sizes have been piled up neatly, although a few of them have broken. Those who have, have been tossed haphazardly against the northern wall. A few hooks have been installed, a place where tools of the trade are hung. The floor may have been clean at one point in time, but now suffers from a rodent infestation, as rat droppings are scattered in a route that leads from rathole to rathole. The remains of a lantern has been left on a large crate.
113711: A coil of rope is lying here.

A large hole overhead is one of the most defining features of this tunnel. A couple of broken wooden planks have been tossed into a few empty crates. Several other planks of wood have been nailed to the wall, close to the floor. All of the wood features many splinters and bite-marks, with an unpleasant odour accompanying a few brown and yellow piles of goo that stick to the wood.
113712: A giant rat patters against you, squeaking maliciously.

Gnawed bones, chewed strips of leather and a greal of straw make a giant nest that covers most of a small tunnel. A few decomposing rat corpses are resting on top of the nest, their unpleasant odour mixing with the stale air. A large beam half sticks out of the dirt, with some of the wood gnawed showing a pile of splinters growing on one side of the nest. A myriad of different sized holes are found in the tunnel walls, passageways for small rodents only.
113713: A giant rat patters against you, squeaking maliciously.

A small tunnel is a veritable mishmash of straw, randoms strips of cloth, dirt mounds and scraps of wood, forming a large rat's nest. By chance, the tunnel is large enough for a humanoid to enter, although only few would do so with ease. A mostly-rotten beam forms the centre of the tunnel, a remnant of an earlier structure that was abandoned long ago. Several wooden boards, some cracked and rotten, cover the southern wall.
113714:
A giant rat patters against you, squeaking maliciously.
A tiny spider is here, eating a tiny bug.

Crates made of rotted wood and mouldy bags of cotton are tossed onto a pile. Cobwebs both big and small form veritable banners that line the tunnel, the insects that have fallen prey to them are nothing more but dried husks. One larger web features the dried corpse of a small rat. The ground below is littered with droppings and tiny gnawed bones in several small piles.
113715: A rusty pickaxe with a broken handle lies discarded here.

The tunnel is only five feet high, forcing bent heads and knees for many adventurers. A few wooden support beams, covered in grey and white webs, hold the tunnel in place. Sharp cuts mar the beams, and several lines and circles have been drawn upon them. A few broken tools, their wood rotten and rusted beyond repair, have been ditched against the southern wall.
113716: A small pool of stale water has formed.

The earthen floor and walls are mouldy and damp. In one spot, a small pool has formed from water coming from the ceiling. The walls are crumbling and thick roots poke out through the ceiling from above. Some of the walls have small holes, with pathways of rat droppings between them. A few small bones, belonging to a small animal, sit in one corner. The tunnel is quite uneven, creating a bumpy path that ascends from the east to the south.
113717: The precariousness of this location could hardly be overstated, as the walls and ceiling are barely holding up. Large, spongy chunks of turf and peat are hanging down from above, impeding one's vision and ability to move. The smell in here is that of musty, recently uncovered soil, not unlike the first shovel-full taken from an overgrown mound of compost. Several earth-packed mounds have formed in this tunnel, the aftermath of a collapse that blocked the tunnel entrance. One dirt mound is inundated with bones, straw, leather and small bones, forming a small nest.
113719: Wagon Trail by a Way Station

Bending from the south to the east, a trail follows the flow of the hills, avoiding steep slopes and hilltops. This trail is obviously man-made and shows signs of being used to haul wagons through the area. However, signs of the wild reclaiming the land appear occasionally, as though the path has been used less in recent times. An old way station butts up against the steep hillside to the northwest.
113720:
A long water trough made of wood stands here.
A sturdy pack horse is standing here.
A brown donkey watches the surroundings, perhaps looking for a chance to graze.

This stable has a broad corridor between stalls on either side. Each stall has a hefty amount of hay, and a trough containing fresh water. The walls of the stable are old, but clean and in good condition. They are made of broad wooden planks, while the floor has been paved with large flat stones. There are sturdy double doors leading out of the stable to the east, and another exit to the north, leading further inside the way station.
113721:
A sack of flour has been placed here.
A large cabinet capable of storing goods is here.
In the cabinet, there are three eggs and a sturdy rope.
A beer barrel has been left here.

This a small storage room. There are shelves, crates, cabinets, and barrels all over the room, and seemingly all surfaces have been filled with boxes, sacks and various other miscellaneous items. There are two exits, towards the south and east, and a tiny window giving a view to the north.
113722:
A large stone fireplace with a roaring fire warms the room.
A black and white cat is playing here.

This is the spacious main room of a Way Station in the Tower Hills. A broad counter stands in the centre of the cabin; this is where the travellers take care of their business with the station personel. Next to it stands a roaring fireplace, and in the area infront of the fireplace there are some tables and chairs. A row of bunk beds stands against the back wall, capable of hosting a dozen tired travellers.
113725: This chimney looks as if it goes straight up on all sides for at least a couple of dozen feet. A small opening can be seen near the top of the chimney, on the west side. The small rocks jutting out from the walls look as if they would serve as pretty good hand holds.
113726: This ledge is located at the very top of a natural rock chimney. The ledge follows the steep, rocky hillside to the west. The chimney-like tunnel disappears into the dark below. It looks like a good place to sit, but the view is largely blocked by the hills. The ledge is covered with bird droppings, and even more so towards the west along the ledge.
113727:
A large mother hawk is here looking for a prey to feed her young.
A cute young hawk is standing here.
A cute young hawk is standing here.

The rock wall to the north, the very wall this ledge sits on, is home to a number of birds, judging from the bird nests and droppings. Most of them seem to be empty, but not all of them are. To the west is an extremely steep slope, covered in loose shale and gravel-sized rock, making the descent difficult but possible, however coming back up would not be smart to attempt. The ledge continues to the east, though not for long as it ends at a small opening in the hillside.
113730: This long but low tunnel stretches through dark gravel and grey rock in a north-south direction. The tunnel is gradually getting darker and narrower as it crawls deeper under the hills. The ground looks surprisingly smooth for what looks like a natural cavern.
113731:
A long, single-edged sword lies on the ground.
A small metal target shield is on the ground.
A huge, poisonous spider is here.

White, sticky spider webs have been woven throughout this round cavern. The thread is the most dense at the south side of the cavern, from where the individual strings reach out along the walls and through the open space, to block and trap anything entering the lair. Where the cavern's walls are visible behind the web, they are of solid grey rock. The only exit is a tunnel leading to the north.
113733:
A large bat is here, hanging in the darkness.
The small fierce-looking bat is hanging from the ceiling, obviously sleeping.
The small fierce-looking bat is hanging from the ceiling, obviously sleeping.
The small fierce-looking bat is hanging from the ceiling, obviously sleeping.
The small fierce-looking bat is hanging from the ceiling, obviously sleeping.

The ceiling in this cavern looms but ten feet above, but what the cavern lacks in height, it makes up for in width as it extends atleast thirty feet in all directions. There are several outcroppings hanging down from the ceiling, which contributes to casting the cavern in deep shadows. The floor is covered in a thick layer of fine sand, and centuries of accumulated bat droppings. A crevice slopes up to the west toward the only visible exit from the cave.
113735:
A leather helmet lies here.
A pair of rigid leather gloves are lying here.
A sturdy, soft leather jerkin is on the ground.
A sand viper is slithering here on the ground.

The bare bedrock lies no more than a few feet away to either side in this small, narrow cleft. It's not even ten feet deep at the far end and at the other end, it could easily be walked out of without even needing to climb. Dense shrubs grow above the cleft, closing over it almost like a lid.
113738: A small fat hedgehog is sleeping here.

A wild and overgrown hedge surrounds this ruined farmstead. Moss-covered foundations of buildings remain amidst primroses and willows. The inhabitants must have abandoned this place a long time ago, since all the wooden structures have rotted away. A fading gravel path leads to the south through a hedge.
113739:
There are three dark coloured flasks here.
A small vicious black rat squeaks at you for disturbing it.
A giant rat patters against you, squeaking maliciously.

A gloomy room, with mould and mildew colonizing the walls lies beneath the remains of a farmhouse. The floor has a thick carpeting of dust with pieces of rotten wood and broken pieces of pottery littering the ground. There are cobwebs on the ceiling shifting slightly in the disturbed air.
113740:
A large cabinet capable of storing goods is here.
In the cabinet, there are a water skin, a plain leather belt, a sturdy pair of soft leather trousers and a sturdy pair of soft leather gloves.
A small vicious black rat squeaks at you for disturbing it.

This cramped chamber has a low arched ceiling and a dirty appearance; the dingy walls are covered with greenish mould. Rusted hoops and pieces of wooden staves clutter a damp floor of large, roughly cut granite slabs. Some grisly looking metal hooks hang from the ceiling.
113741: These fields may once have yielded great harvests of wheat, potatoes, or whatever else those working the fields planted. Those days are gone and the fields are now abandoned, and nothing grow here but weed and wildflowers. The fields continue to the north and west, while a ruined village lies to the south. There is a ruin of a small house just adjacent to the fields to the east.
113742: A tiny spider is here, eating a tiny bug.

The floor in this ruin is made of compacted earth. Only the walls remain of the ruin to the north and south, and the ceiling collapsed long ago. Wreckage from the collapsed roof, consisting mostly of broken pieces of wooden planks, litter the ground. The walls to the east and west remain largely intact, though they are scorched from an old fire. The walls are painted red, and wherever the fire did not blacken them, the paint is flaking badly.
113743: The grass on this field is tall and green. It sways gently whenever a breeze picks up. The land is mostly flat but a few low hills rise in gentle waves to the west. The field looks as if it has never been cultivated. The grass grows wild and several large, sprawling bushes dot the landscape.
113745: These fields were once farmed, likely by the people that inhabited the ruined village to the east. Now even the fences around the fields are mostly gone, and in the fields themselves, nothing grow but weed and wildflowers. Although most of the village lies to the east, there is a ruin of one old farmhouse much closer, just to the north.
113746: This farmhouse was ravaged by a fire in the past. Most of the roof is gone, and what were once walls now lie in haphazard piles of blackened wood upon the ground. Near the north-western corner, a gaping hole leads down into an old cellar. The remains of an old hatch has long since rotted away and collapsed into the darkness below. The only way to safely leave this ruin is through the empty, skeletal door frame to the south.
113747:
Several shards of broken glass lie scattered about the ground.
A small rat runs about, oblivious to your presence.
A small rat runs about, oblivious to your presence.

This cellar is small and cramped. It's square in shape and no more than ten feet across. It's further restricted by rows of wooden shelves on the walls. Everything here is coated in a thick layer of dust and soot. Broken glass lies on the floor beneath a cracked, broken shelf.
113748:
A weapons rack stands against the wall.
In the rack are a warhammer and a short spear.
A tiny spider is here, eating a tiny bug.
A giant rat patters against you, squeaking maliciously.
A small rat runs about, oblivious to your presence.
A small rat runs about, oblivious to your presence.

This narrow dead end is draped in old cobwebs. The air is dry and dusty and the floor is covered in a thick layer of grime. The walls are close together and there are no shelves to either side, except for an old, empty wooden rack that stands against the back wall. To the east there is a slightly larger cellar with a set of stairs that leads up through a hatch in the ceiling.
113749:
There are two wooden crates here.
A wooden chest stands in the corner.
A giant rat patters against you, squeaking maliciously.

This small cellar room has a floor and walls of stone. The stones are fixed in place with clay and great care was taken to make the floor even and the walls smooth. Several simple chests and crates line the eastern wall. The only exit from this room is a narrow opening in the northern wall.
113751:
A forest spider is here crawling around.
A forest spider is here crawling around.
A finch flies low above the ground.

The surrounding branches grow from the trunk of this large tree in unusual fashion; where normally the branches are thin and dispersed numerous feet apart, these grow thick and close together, forming a natural platform of sorts. The thick branches below follow suit in a semi-circular pattern from just feet off the ground, slowly circling upwards around the trunk of the tree. With the exception of a brief, sparse tangle of intertwined branches just below, even the most unskilled climber would have little trouble navigating the boughs.
113755:
A black snake hurries towards you with sly intentions.
A snake slithers towards you.
The garden snake slithers harmlessly here.
A black snake hurries towards you with sly intentions.

The walls, floor, and ceiling of this musty cavern all consist of dark brown earth. The cave can not be far underground, because roots poke through the ceiling. Upon the ground are several small, broken eggs that sit amongst several ghost-white snake skins.
113760: A heavy desk, made of solid oak, stands here.

What was once a stately and dignified study for the tower's master now lies in a state of disarray. Paint has begun to chip away from the fine wood panels, and strips of ripped fabric are all that remains of the once-rich tapestries that hung upon the walls. A tall window in the southern wall gives a broad view of the path leading to and from the tower gate.
113761:
There are two handfuls of clover here.
There is a huge, pyramidal beehive here.
A three-foot-long queen bee is here, buzzing agitatedly.
An angry bee is here, collecting nectar from all the flowers of the garden.
A bee flies around here, collecting nectar from the flowers.
A bee flies around here, collecting nectar from the flowers.
A bee flies around here, collecting nectar from the flowers.

There is a small clearing here in this small clump of bushes. The ground is carpeted by flowers, and bees flit from one to the next, gathering the golden treasure within. There is a large beehive in the middle of the clearing, from which comes a very distinct buzzing.
113770: The garden snake slithers harmlessly here.

The steep walls on three sides casts this part of the dry gulch into murky shadows. The floor of the gulch is mostly made up of sand and small rocks, with a layer of solid bedrock underneath. Few plants could grow in this unfriendly environment. To the west lies a small niche, even darker than this area.
113771: It looks like something has managed to crack the wall to the east and carve out a small rocky hollow here. As time has passed, the area has become a sheltered refuge for any animals that want shade from the sun. The small cracks lining the walls are not large enough to be used as foot or hand holds to climb upward, but could be used by small animals that may want to find some shelter.
113772: A black snake hurries towards you with sly intentions.

This cave is small and dark. The floor is sandy, and shows tracks of snakes coming in and out. There are a few skeletons of small animals littering the floor, and some dry snakeskins. There is a small amount of light filtering in from the opening to the south.
113774: A narrow, weather-beaten rope bridge has been constructed over a shallow but steep chasm. It provides a path between the flat, rocky area to the east and the taller ridgeline to the west. Around the bridge, the hilltops of Emyn Beraid extend in all directions. The bridge is rickety and poorly constructed and would probably not hold much weight, it looks like something a group of people would want to cross one at a time.
113776: Steep hillsides rise abruptly around this narrow ravine, forming a dead-end where the only way out is to the north. The ground is covered with small rocks and gravel, and there is no vegetation in this bare place. Above, a rickety looking rope-bridge has been constructed as a pathway across the ravine.
113777: A long slope from a hilltop to the south comes to an end here atop these bluffs. The bluffs overlook the surrounding area and hills cover the land to the north, west, and east. The side of the cliff to the north is very steep and does not look like it would provide reliable footing. On top of the bluff stands an old, grey cottage made of stone.
113778:
A large, dusty alcove sits in a wall, smelling of soot.
A large cabinet capable of storing goods is here.

This cottage has been made out of stone. The walls are thick, although the construction work doesn't look especially smooth and some rough edges of the stones used protrude inwards. There are some basic furniture, looking old and long abandoned, and a fireplace in the room. The door is on the southern wall while four small windows offer a magnificent view down to the surrounding valley.
113779:
On the ground, there are two musty loaves of bread.
A simple wooden chest is here.
An ancient fungus smothers the boulders.

The walls and the low-hanging roof of this small cellar are made of stone, supported by a number of wooden beams. The room is few yards wide in either direction, leaving only a small amount of space to move around. There is a wooden shelf with some boxes and other minor items on it. A cramped alcove lies to the north and small ladders lead up to a trapdoor in the ceiling.
113780: Cramped Alcove in a Dusty Cellar

A small lever of metal is attached to the eastern wall.
A pile of broken shelves lie at the foot of the eastern wall.

A small narrow alcove stretches from the south, continues a few yards, and then stops at a grey rock wall. Apparently there have been shelves on the walls, but aside of a few surviving fixtures only the barely-recognisable remains lie scattered on the floor, littering the alcove. The floor is made out of smooth rocks.
113781:
A large metal shield is on the ground.
A large cabinet capable of storing goods is here.
A lever of dull metal sticks out of the wall to the west.
A weapons rack stands against the wall.
In the rack are a spiked war club, a short spear and a longbow.

This round underground chamber is about five yards across. The walls, roof, and ceiling are carved from the bedrock of the surrounding stone, but has been skilfully reinforced where needed with square stone bricks. There are some weapon racks and cabinets in the room indicating this place is an old armoury.
113790:
A mace is on the ground.
A skeleton lies on the bottom of the underwater cave, half-buried in mud.

Dark, still water fills this small cave. The water seems stale as if it does not circulate much. The bottom of the cave is covered by a thin layer of mud, and there are several pieces of some kind of cloth or leather half-buried in the mud, rotting away.
113791: Along the rock walls some barrels and chests are situated, making this cellar look like some sort of storage. The air is stuffy and murky as the hatch in the ceiling is so well sealed that no fresh air slips by it. A fragile ladder is the only connection to the outside world.
113796:
A small evergreen plant grows here, its woody stems reaching two feet.
A fallow deer is grazing peacefully here.

This is a vast plain covered with grass. Some gentle slopes make the landscape a beautiful sight and a pleasant place to travel. No signs of agriculture or other humanoid activity can be seen. The plain continues in all directions.
113834: A Wide Trail on Rocky Ground

A large wild horse is here, protecting his herd.
A young filly is just learning to walk.
A young colt is frolicking playfully.
A wild mare is watching you warily.
A wild mare is watching you warily.
A wild mare is watching you warily.

The trail leads east and west, getting wider on the rocky plateau to the east. The ground here slopes gradually down, as it approaches the grasslands to the west. Rocks and boulders of different sizes are scattered around the area, hindering movement off the trail. Sparse yellowish grass and low bushes cover the ground, providing hiding spots for lizards and smaller animals. A few feet south of the trail stands an old, blackened tree, struck by a lightning.
113835: A small hill suddenly rises from the surrounding plains which go on for miles in every direction. From atop of the hill the dark line of a trail running across a plateau is visible to the south. In contrast to the tough grasses around, the hill is overgrown with juicy, high grass, interspersed with clusters of wild flowers, which roughly outline the foot of the hill.
113836: The land here is barren with only small shrubs and low yellowish grass growing in small tufts. With little to hold the soil together, the erosion from wind has blown most of it away, leaving only a stony surface. In the east the ground slopes up to a small hill, whereas in all other directions the endless plains disappear into the distance.
113838: A field of coarse yellow weeds extends towards the northern horizon of this dry plain. The grass-covered earth is made up of a grainy mixture of sand and soil which holds tufts of long grasses in large patches along with the smaller varieties. The ground becomes rockier to the south and a pebbled trail can be seen heading towards the east into some long rolling valleys.
113839: Thin shards of limestone layer the ground at the foot of this falling ridge. A large number of grey slabs litter the ground as they slowly erode into the grassy plains that sprawl to the north and south. A deep valley can be seen to the south that extends to a forest. The stone-lined trail leads to the east and west wandering through the rocky plains alongside a valley-dip to the south.
113840: A gritty, sandy plain sprawls across this lonesome expanse. Some withered tufts of long grass grow among the smaller heather in the rocky ground. To the south, a trail can be seen on a rising ridge of yellow and green grass. The ridge heads eastwards and then twists around towards the north, where it falls.
113841:
A black wolf pads restlessly, looking for its next prey.
An emaciated warg, half-mad with hunger, is here.
An emaciated warg, half-mad with hunger, is here.

Soft, grey pebbles litter the ground among the gritty sand particles that make up the dark earth. Long green and yellow grasses extend across the plains in soft rolling heaps around deposits of heather and rock. A rising ridge can be seen extending and falling towards the east from its southern start.
113842: This sandy trail turns at the feet of two ridges. The smaller ridge to the west is dotted with rocks, while the larger grass-covered ridge sprawls eastwards. To the south extends a grassy plain of heather leading up to a dark forest in the far distance. Several woody bushes grow on the embankment, forming a mound.
113843: A small grasshopper clings to a blade of grass, ready to spring.

This sandy field extends along the base of a long, rising ridge that continues eastwards. Small plants and grasses grow in the gritty, dark earth in yellow and green tufts around the grey rocks that litter the area. Some woody shrubs can be seen in the east where the ridge starts to fall again towards the north.
113844: Hidden away below the highest point of the ridge and its two falling slopes lies this field of brambles and berries. The shrubs' thick roots dig into the sandy earth among the exposed limestone bedrock at the bottom of the ridge. Animal droppings cover the ground amidst the heather and grass where the brambles have been picked clean of their berries by the local wildlife.
113845: The easterly limestone ridge falls into the expanse of the yellow plains. The grey rocks crumble at the edge of the ridge, where woody shrubs of berry-laden brambles grow thick in the sandy earth. Long grasses poke out from around the slabs of the element-worn rocks. A quilt of multicoloured lichen smothers a misshapen boulder that silently stands watch among the brambles.
113846: A lonely plain of withered grasses and slabs of stone sits on the leveled ridge. The ridge continues sloping downwards to the west, but rises in the east where it then curves southwards. Small piles of rabbit droppings can be seen in between the thickets of grasses and short, woody shrubs that grow here.
113847:
A fat rabbit is here, chewing on some grass.
A black wolf pads restlessly, looking for its next prey.

The ridge continues its downward climb towards the north, until it reaches a great chasm. The brown grasses that wither on the ground become sparse as they reach the cracked edge. A lonely, splintered tree grows on the northern side of the desolate ridge, hanging precariously over a cliff's edge, where its roots desperately cling to the dirt in between slabs of coarse, sandy stone.
113848: The ridge branches into two falling valleys to the east and north from its westerly shrub-covered height. The northern, rocky slope is covered in a brown layer of withered grass, while a dried creek bed follows the eastern slope down into a wide and lush valley of tiny, woody shrubs and green grasses.
113849: This falling ridge-top is surrounded by woody shrubs and small grasses. In the centre of the ridge is an old campfire ring encircled by a couple comfortable stones. The area looks fairly disused, judging from the encompassing view from which valleys extend in every direction. Below the ridge to the south, an old trail can be seen along with a dark forest even farther in the distance.
113850:
A wild dog bares his yellow fangs at you.
A wild dog bares his yellow fangs at you.
A wild dog bares his yellow fangs at you.

A dried creek bed filled with smooth stones continues down the side of the western ridge over the limestone bedrock into a wide valley of shrubs and vivid green grasses. The creek bed then turns its way southward as it cuts through the wildflower-covered steppe as the surrounding ridges continue falling to the north. The valley is filled with lush, rolling grasses and woody shrubs.
113851: A field vole has frozen to the spot, sensitive to your presence.

The grassy ridge bends to the north into a sward as the trail follows the slopes downwards to the east and west. Along the trail embankment, a green thicket sits among exposed, limestone bedrock. To the south, and beyond the ridge's edge, extend rolling valleys that stretch on far into the distance, where a dark forest can be spotted, along with a larger one far to the east.
113852: The overgrown, rocky trail leads over the easterly rising ridge, among the grey slabs of limestone that jut out of the ground, from its western source. Several large shrubs grow around the slabs in patches, providing some cover for animals which have left their droppings in small piles. A grassy valley spreads out to the south before reaching a dark wood, topped with pines, in the far distance.
113853: The rising ridge fans out to the south into a wide steppe of coarse yellow grass. Tufts of long grasses cover the plains in patches among the shorter heather and the occasional rock that pokes out from the expanse. Even farther to the south sits a dark forest. The trail leads up the ridge to the east from its western source. A small patch of woody shrubs grows along the trail.
113854: The trail sits at the bottom of two ridges where a small grassy valley sprawls to the north and south. The trail bends here, from the north and then to the east, up the rising ridge of yellow grass and heather. The land to the south looks much greener than that to the sandy north. Even further to the south, a dark forest topped with great pines can be seen past the rolling valleys.
113855: A sharp-eyed hawk is here stalking some prey.

The flat steppe extends across the east until it reaches a rocky crag that plunges down into a wide valley of yellow and green grasses. Some woody shrubs grow on the plains in dense patches among the rocks, along with some delicate wild flowers. A distant trail can be seen to the north leading westward.
113856: A steppe of coarse grass extends here towards the south, where it slowly slopes downwards into a small valley before a darkened wood. Several wild flowers of white and blue grow in the rich soil that covers the plains. Small thickets dot the steppe in dense patches. A trail can be seen to the north leading away.
113857: A field mouse noses about hungrily, searching for food.

The long ridge ends here from its northeastern source in a field of yellow and green heather. To the east, the ridge falls into another wide, craggy valley of rolling plains. Among the rocks to the south, some small ferns grow around a couple of lone pine trees. Several miles to the south, rises a dark forest.
113858:
A field mouse noses about hungrily, searching for food.
A field lark stands here, focused on finding food.

A lonesome expanse of rocky plains extends to the northwest and dominates the horizon. The grey, limestone bedrock that exposes itself among the shrubs that blanket the field is weather-worn and seems to continue onward to the north. The ground slowly buckles downwards into a sinkhole to the south. Further to the southeast is a dark forest peaked with birch and oak.
113859:
A fierce boar is here, making grunting noises.
A boar cub is playing here, and exploring the wide world.
A boar cub is playing here, and exploring the wide world.
A small boar with big yellow tusks looks eager to fight.

Large boulders are strewn across the yellow plains, half-buried in the thick grass and heather that carpets the area with its coarse blades. The rocky terrain continues on westwards, filling the horizon along with the grassy ridges in the north and east, as a dark forest stands to the south.
113860: A brown furry gopher is here, ready to dive back underground.

Thick slabs of limestone lie in a pile of rubble to the north where the ridge has heavily eroded. Throughout the rocky mess grow a large number of bushy shrubs with roots that dearly hold on to the sparse soil. The number of bushes decreases as the land becomes more rocky towards the south.
113861: A field of stumps sits against the backdrop of a dark wood, while a dry plain stretches on towards the valley-filled horizon to the north. The fir stumps ooze a pungent yellow sap down their boles in coagulated clusters. The coarse heather has been trampled into mud riddled with lines from all the timber which has been dragged through the track into a large pile of wood to the east.
113862: Brown and orange leaves fill the crevices in the limestone where the ground has buckled into a sinkhole, taking the forest down with it. Dirty white strips of birch bark litter the ground around the trees where their boles reach up into the sky to be topped with delicate leaves. Small ferns and grasses cover the ground in a display of colour around a few jutting slabs of limestone.
113863: A cluster of white star-shaped forget-me-nots flourish here in reminiscence.

This forest of alder thickens considerably in the southeast as firs and oaks replace the birches. Underneath the sparse canopy, a field of small grasses and moss grow in between the niches where the limestone bedrock reaches the soil. The land slowly dips down into a sinkhole to the north, revealing some plains.
113864: Some pine nuts lie scattered upon the ground.

The densely-packed fir trees extend high up into the sky and fill the air with a tangy smell of pine. Their straight trunks extend out to brown branches covered with prickly, green needles. In the moist earth below, a bed of fir needles blanket the dark brown roots amid the soft grasses and ferns.
113865: The trail follows along the foot of a dark forest that stretches towards the east and northwest. From the forest canopy extend a number of dark firs, which fill the air with the scent of resin. To the south extends a prairie that dips into a shallow valley in the distance, where a patch of shrubs dot the slope.
113866:
A large eagle soars above you.
A sleuthing orc is tracking here, sniffing along the ground.

A small trail, mostly overgrown with grass, meanders through the plains. Vegetation surrounding the trail is dense with green patches of rushes and blackberry. Even though the trail is the only easy passage through the plains, it shows little signs of use except a few, rare traces of animal life. The trail makes a smooth turn from the south to the east, continuing in both directions. To the west the plains seem to continue for miles whilst sparse trees to the north-east indicate a change in the vegetation.
113869: A lowland valley spreads across the ground in a shallow dip as the land falls from the northern forest and then rises again towards the south. A small, woody patch of dark bushes grows on the southern slope among several limestone slabs. Amidst the grasses that carpet the plains, a number of mole mounds can be seen.
113870: Except for on the far east, where the vegetation becomes clearly lighter, the grass grows high in all directions. Traces of animals passing by now and then lead through the grass straws. The absence of thick undergrowth makes movement here quite easy.
113871:
A shallow pond is here, tinted green with algae.
A tree-snake lies wrapped around one of the tree branches.
A tree-snake lies wrapped around one of the tree branches.

Among the high grass, a couple of firs reach tall with needles healthily pointing up towards the sky. The fresh water from the small pond has let them grow high, creating a landmark that stands out in the flat landscape.
113872: A small animal, all covered in spines, snuffles amongst the undergrowth.

Shaded by bushes and a couple of smaller trees, this grassy plain is a place where many animals come to rest. Droppings and a jumble of animal prints tell the story of a active wildlife. To the southeast the grass quickly becomes lower.
113873: A fierce boar is here, making grunting noises.

The animals populating these fields keep the grass short. Compared to the tall grass to the west, the vegetation here is significantly lower and gradually becomes even lower to the east. The visibility over the flat landscape is good in all directions.
113874: A roe deer is standing here, watching the terrain while chewing the vegetation.
Bushes of various sizes and kinds are spread out in the field, some with leaves and others with needles. They offer room where small animals can hide from predators that might pass by.
113875: A roe deer is standing here, watching the terrain while chewing the vegetation.

A wide field stretches far in all directions, presenting a great number of grasses. Complemented with a stand of firs to hide from the sun under and a pond to drink from to the north, this area would be the perfect place for cows and other animals to go grazing.
113876: Yellow flowers, with grey-green foliage, grow in clusters here.

The field is covered with a huge amount of flowers of different kinds. The shifting colours almost make a full spectrum, looking like a rainbow. To the south, the ground slopes downwards into a dip in the plains.
113877: A tall stag is here, grazing peacefully.

Rows of trees and bushes have split the low growing grass into four smaller oblong fields. Each of the fields has a slightly different kind of grass, with the rightmost field's grass growing really low and the grass of the other fields growing gradually higher.
113878: A beautiful and docile horse is standing here.

The ground and grass of the field is damp and shifts a bit when walked upon. The ridge here continues from the east side curving around to the south side while the plains stretch northwards and slope downwards in the west.
113879: A tall stag is here, grazing peacefully.

At the verge of the southern plateau, a magnificent view of the grassy lowlands lying many miles to south can be seen. To the west, something that looks an awful lot like a border promptly marks the beginning of a field with low grass, while the plain to the east has no vegetation at all.
113880: The wide-stretched grassy fields end with a vertical, unclimbable cliff wall to the north. Many yards above, the plateau continues northwards with even more plains. To the east the terrain becomes rockier and two enormous boulders can be seen among the grasses and bushes.
113881: A giant boulder sits here among the swaying grasses.

Some boulders, so big they must have been torn off of the Misty Mountains in the far west and thrown here by giants, are spread on the ground. Dark mosses and lichens cover the southeastern sides of all the boulders. The thick vegetation does not seem to live; however it is not yet dead.
113882: Some delicious wild strawberries grow on the ground.

The areas with dark grasses slouch moodily, it is obvious that something else is weighing it down. A heavily sloping plain to the west prevents the eye from being able to divulge what is on it in that direction as opposed to the fairly unobstructed northern and eastern plains.
113883: It is hard to tell whether it was the cattle of the farm to the north that once cleared this field of grass or if it was the deed of some evil force. Either way, nowadays nothing grows here and the shapes of the ruin to the north is the only thing that stands out on the horizon.
113884: At the Ruin of a Farm

On the ground, there are two erect shrubs with green pinnate leaves.
The burnt and blackened skeletal remains of a human are here.
A furious, old bull is stamping with his hoof.
A starving cow stands here, looking for a patch of grass.
A sickly hen is here, thinned from malnutrition.

This ruin of a house is all that is left of a once thriving farm. The great fence posts that made up the encircling structure of the large cow pasture are still standing, but have broken apart and are not connected to one another anymore. There is evidence of a fire in the way of some blackened, splintered pieces of the fence that are still spread on the hard ground.
113885: A roe deer is standing here, watching the terrain while chewing the vegetation.

Low brush covers the ground and constitutes a change in the otherwise grassy fields. Southwards, the brush grows higher and thicker, preventing movement in that direction. The bushes to the west are not very thick, allowing some travel without too many difficulties. A ruin of a farm can be seen far to the east.
113886: As the grass was probably grazed away by cattle the soil has been blown away by erosion making the sandy, hard ground not hospitable enough for more foliage to grow back. Instead, thorny brush now grows here in a twisted manner.
113887: A diamond-back rattlesnake is coiled here, ready to strike.

This place has a certain air of death because of all the carcasses and skeletons of various farmland animals lying around in various degrees of decay. None of the skeletons have any flesh left on the bones, but are spread around on the ground among some dark stains.
113888: Except for a few dark grasses, reaching only inches from the ground, nothing grows here. These dark, grey sandy plains stretch in all directions, looking an awful lot much like a plain of charcoal and ash. The sandy plains end on the brink of a deep fault.
113889: Crags break through the grassy surface all over the plains, forcing any traveller to be careful not to stumble. The ruin of an old farm can be seen to the south. Cattle from that farm may have once grazed on this field.
113890: Whatever once grew here is long gone. The hard soil lies uncovered, save for some usual stones of various sizes spread around. The ground is so dry that there are cracks on the ground, and occasionally a gust of wind spreads dust in the air. There are no signs of any animal life and the barren landscape seems to continue to the southeast.
113891: A fierce boar is here, making grunting noises.

The moorlands stretch far to the north and east, while some trees and bushes present some variety in the landscape to the west. The green grass gradually turns darker to the south, ending in an impassable wall of what seems to be thorny, dead brush.
113892: A large brown snake with black patches is coiled here.

The wide-stretched moorlands end before halting at a deep fault to the east. The grass has been trampled near the fault where a steep, rough and wide slide leads downwards to it. Some traces of the animals that have been hunted down, off the end of the brink of the fault, can be seen below. The plains continue to the north and west but travelling south is hindered by a ridge.
113893: The falling ridge makes a sudden, sheer drop as it meanders onward to the southeast among the limestone slabs that stick out of its surface. A fine cover of lichen and moss smothers the bedrock that has been exposed. The trail continues onward to the west and south, within its visible embankment.
113894: Small, yellow grasses poke out from among the rocks and pebbles that cover this ridge as it falls from the north towards a valley in the east. Further to the south, a steep slope prevents anyone from straying from the path. A large valley can be seen to the southwest that slowly reaches a dark forest in the distance. The bedrock exposes itself across the ridge, dividing the vegetation.
113895: A Morgundul wolf-rider, wielding a lance, is here, riding a brown wolf.

A green valley filled with rolling grasses lies enclosed between two yellow ridges, forming a wide plain. Small bushes grow in thickets on the slopes, in between slabs of limestone. The larger ridge can be seen climbing upwards to the southeast while the heather-covered valley continues towards the north parted by a pebble-covered trail that climbs up the slopes of both ridges.
113896: A green field of lush heather grows across the wide valley that sits in between two large ridges that fall towards the north. A dried creek bed continues through the middle of the ridge from the north, where it then sinks into the wide expanse of prairie and disappears. Several limestone boulders line the western side of the valley, covered in lichen and surrounded by woody shrubs.
113897: The shrub-covered ridge falls towards the west as it strikes an enormous limestone precipice to the north. Beyond the rubble that lies at its base, and the grasses that weave in between the stones, a trail courses towards the south and east as it follows the ridge. A grassy valley can be seen to the west.
113898: The grassy trail forks directly below the crest of the ridge, where each path then follows a falling steppe to the north, south, and east. The old, pebbled trails, lined by heather and surrounded by shrubs, weave against the backdrop of an enormous, dark forest to the east and a smaller wood to the south. Before each forest, craggy ridges and valleys extend across the rolling landscape.
113899: The trail dips down slightly as the ridge falls between two crests in the west and east, revealing a glimpse of a dark and rocky coombe to the south. A thick and overgrown embankment of woody shrubs grows along the crag to the north, opposite a grassy valley that stretches out to the south. Similarly, a wall of shrubs grows to the west among the patches of heather, forming a dense sward.
113900: The ridge crests here before falling slightly towards the west. Beyond the grassy trail embankment to the north, a filthy mire covered with mist sits in the far distance to the northwest, while an enormous, dark forest grows in the east, taking up the entire horizon. The trail weaves through a patch of dense woody shrubs as it forks between the western, southern, and eastern slopes.
113901: A Morgundul wolf-rider, wielding a lance, is here, riding a brown wolf.

Beyond the grassy trail embankment, two dark forest can be spotted in the distance. One sits in the west and another in the far east. The eastern wood, despite being further away, looks far darker and more menacing, as if a shadow keeps a grasp upon it. Several limestone boulders line the trail as the ridge extends further to the north, and then starts falling towards the west.
113902: The grassy ridge starts rising above the land, turning into a wide steppe as it travels towards the north. The trail weaves northward and southward along the ridge, where it dips into a switchback towards the valley below. The limestone bedrock is exposed to the air, where lichen and moss grow upon its surface.
113903: The shrub-covered ridge rises towards the north from its southwestern foot as an overgrown trail leads through it. From beyond the trail embankment, a yellow and green steppe of heather stretches over the ridge as it extends itself until reaching the rocky crags, where it falls into the valleys along its sides.
113904: The grassy ridge leads eastwards and westwards alongside a steep, grass-lined crag, which nestles a valley in between another ridge that can be seen several miles to the north.
