Beyond the pebbled trail's southern embankment, the land extends into an abrupt steppe that falls down a natural, stone stair into the dense canopy of a dark forest topped with alders and oaks.
113905: The trail wanders along a raised steppe that stretches northwards until reaching a sheer slope covered with woody shrubs. To the southwest, the dark forest can be seen continuing alongside the trail. The western plains are filled with craggy valleys of grass and stone that roll into the distant horizon. To the west, a white formation of rocks stands near the forest.
113906: A small, bubbling creek flows peacefully here.

The heather that has grown over the trail becomes significantly denser as it reaches a small bubbling creek. The tiny creek, easily hopped across, trickles out of the southern ridge and curves alongside the trail on its northern course until it parts ways and disappears into the dark forest. The overgrown trail heads westwards along a falling forest-covered ridge into some white rocks.
113907: The sun-bleached remains of a couple of walls stand here among the grasses and weeds that have retaken an ancient building. A worn trail navigates around the building, leading east and west. The rubble of the ruins continues into the dark forest to the south, only to be disrupted by a cavern leading downwards. To the north, a craggy steppe extends into a valley.
113908: Ancient Ruins in a Dark Forest

A tangled creeper writhes its shoots between the forest's roots upwards.
An elaborate red flower sits within a dark mass of briars.

The white remains of an ancient, fallen tower rest in its coffin of wet roots and mosses of this dark wood. The trunks of the twisted trees reach high up into the impenetrable canopy, locking in everything. The scarred remains of the tower lie in shattered disarray to the east and south, blocking all passage.
113909: A fat rabbit is here, chewing on some grass.

The vast prairie expands across a rolling steppe in a show of yellow and green among the valleys extending northwards. A dark forest stands in the distance to the south, peaked with firs and oaks. A large, overgrown trail can be seen twisting towards the northeast before it disappears behind a grass-covered slope of woody shrubs, where the bedrock breaks through the surface.
113910: The old trail meanders from east to west along the dark border of an ancient forest of fir and birch. A number of deep scars have been carved through the trail from the north towards the east, leaving fresh timber debris littering the ground, where ferns and grasses have taken up root. Beyond the track a wide, rolling prairie extends in a cascade of green and yellow colour.
113911: The trail wanders into the southern forest and continues eastwards along the forest border. An unending view of the northern valleys meets the eye beyond the trail embankment that drops steeply to the north. Weeds and ferns litter the trail due to disuse, growing wildly among a thick tangle of roots that crawls out of the shade from looming forest's dark canopy.
113912: Under the cover of the thick forest canopy, the trail twists between the roots and fallen branches that litter the area. The path is completely overgrown with green grasses and prickly shrubs that grow where the canopy breaks and the sky breaches through. The fallen remains of a knotted oak lies along the trail in the shade of the forest, now completely covered with grasses and fungi.
113913: The old trail divides two huge glades of trees as it stretches eastwards through the forest. The ground to the west is covered with an orange blanket of fir needles, while the north and east are mostly covered with a rotting patchwork of multicoloured oak leaves. The sky barely breaks through the forest canopy.
113914: The twisting trail leads into the northern dark wood, surrounded by gnarled oaks and straight firs towering high up into the sky. The overgrown trail continues westerly along the forest, surrounded by a raised embankment covered in ferns, moss, and yellow grasses. A rolling plain can be seen to the south, dipping into valleys, which are covered with small bushes and shrubs.
113915: A hollow tree is growing upright here.

An enormous, charred oak provides shade among the smaller trees. A grievous scar splits the tree where lightning struck it. Charcoal and soot cover the forest floor where burned trunks make their way up to a rich canopy of leaves. The underbrush below the resilient, green trees have since grown anew.
113917: The valley floor is covered in a lush meadow of green and yellow heather. The rich soil is topped with a fine carpet of velvet moss proliferating in between the blades of grass. Some small, woody bushes grow on a southern rising slope, where some young saplings have taken root among some large, stone slabs.
113918: A grassy prairie expands to the south, overshadowed by the dark forest topped with high oaks in the north. A dense wall of underbrush grows among the roots to the north, preventing entrance into the forest. The ground is covered in a carpet of yellow heather and fern fronds as the plains continue southward.
113919: A dun-coloured grouse is sitting still in the heather.

Sitting at the roots of an ominous forest of dark pine, the moors expand into a wide grassland reaching into the southern valleys on the horizon. The soil that makes up the moors is covered by heather and a carpet of moss, packed with small, grey pebbles that dot the ground. The dark forest to the east is enveloped by a dense tangle of snaking vines that form an impassable wall.
113921:
A tiny spider is here, eating a tiny bug.
A large, black butterfly is fluttering about erratically.

A glade of brown oaks grows in the northern wood filled with spade-like orange and green leaves. The forest floor teams with ferns and delicate grasses which flourish among the pebbles and moss. A darker stand of firs grows in the eastern forest, softly carpeting the ground in an orange blanket of needles.
113922: A large brown wolf stands here, its teeth partly bared.

Among the gnarled roots, rotting leaves, and patches of grass that cover the ground, sit several smooth shards of white rock. Their unnatural shape hint of their man-made origin, but if a structure once stood here, these rocks are all that remain. Up above, twisted branches interlock under the gaze of a towering, dark oak in the middle of the woods, preventing nearly all light from entering.
113923: This is probably the highest spot of the sides that surround the fault below. It is obvious why the hunters didn't choose the precipice directly to the north for hunting animals down into the fault; there would not be anything left of any animal, or man for that matter, to eat if it has taken the fall to the north. The view of the area below is unlimited and straight across the fault to the north, lies a forest.
113924: A long-tailed bird watches you from the vegetation.

The muddy track turns southwards here from over the declining, grassy slope to the west. Beyond the slope, a dark forest sits in the distance, while to the north a green plain of heather and stone rolls across the horizon. The northern embankment thins slightly where an animal trail breaks through the underbrush.
113925: A giant slug is here, oozing around.

A muddy track from the west leads eastward in a grassy field. Small broken twigs and wooden shards litter the thick mud in long scar-like grooves. Some pungent, axe-hewn fir branches have been laid on the track in a haphazard pile, preventing any further progress westward. The ground sharply rises up to the south, where the tips of a distant, dark forest peak out from beyond the slope.
113926: The rolling valley dips slightly as it continues northwards, spreading into a vivid prairie of green and yellow heather. Several crags scour the land as the limestone bedrock exposes itself to the thick swards of grasses. A distant ridge-wall can be seen climbing in the north, opposite the forest to the south.
113927: A wide prairie extends towards the east from a craggy ridge-wall in a display of green and yellow colour among the many grey, limestone slabs that have fallen from the cliff. The land to the south slopes up slightly to a darkened forest of which only the tops of fir trees can be seen.
113928: A shrub-covered crag ends its northern course and heads eastwards along the valley floor, as the grassy prairie extends in all other directions. A show of yellow and green sweeps across the land from all the thick grasses that grow among the grey slabs of bedrock. To the north, a ridge can be seen that carries itself from the east to a high crest where it then falls to the west.
113929: A long-tailed bird watches you from the vegetation.

Yellow and green grasses grow in between two shrub-dotted crags as this valley sprawls to the east and west. The rocky crags that line the valley scale upwards to an unclimbable ridge, where the grassy southern ridge climbs and the rocky northern ridge falls toward the east. A sole fir tree stands to the south, surrounded by a dense thicket of woody shrubs among fallen needles.
113930: An expansive stretch of small bushes grows in between the two ridge-walls that enclose this valley. Long grasses of green and yellow grow in the field, among intricate wild flowers and ferns. Along the rocky edge of the valley sit a number of lichen-speckled boulders that sink into the vivid grasses, which spread into the wide, western prairie that continues on towards the horizon.
113931: Weeds and shrubs line the craggy face of the ridge that leads upwards at a sheer angle. The limestone bedrock has exposed itself, revealing delicate, stacked layers of grey and brown. Grasses and mosses pockmark the stones as they slowly erode into a fine dust that will sink into the southern plains.
113932:
A furious, wild dog is here, snarling and growling.
A furious, wild dog is here, snarling and growling.
A furious, wild dog is here, snarling and growling.
A furious, wild dog is here, snarling and growling.
A furious, wild dog is here, snarling and growling.
A furious, wild dog is here, snarling and growling.

This yellow meadow sits at the bottom of a steep ridge. Rubble from the ridge's craggy face has fallen and formed a half-buried pile. Since collapsing, the rubble from the ridge has been reclaimed by a grassland as it slowly extends itself towards the south. Clusters of large, prickly weeds grow among the grey, lichen-covered rocks where soil has collected.
113933:
A small mushroom grows nearby.
A huge black fungus is here, exuding a foul stench.

Grey fungal spores float through the dry air of the alder and birch wood, which is hidden deep within a rocky crag. A foul, decaying blanket of leaves covers the ground where mould and mushrooms poke out from in between the white strips of birch bark and rotting branches. With each rotten branch that falls from the canopy above, a furious explosion of sickening spores become airborne.
113934: The canopy breaks in several places, revealing the sky through the branches and leaves. A large number of mushrooms grow near the northern birch and fir trees, in patches where the fern fronds and grasses have thinned. A light mist creeps in from the west, followed by the smell of fir. A stand of gnarled, dark oaks rustle in the southwest, their twisted branches rising upwards like claws.
113935: The remains of a mass of vines lie here in a heap of rotting compost.

The limestone bedrock breaks the surface of the roots, fallen leaves, and soft moss where two ridges steeply meet. Small trickles of water dribble down the rocky slopes among the roots and grasses into the ground. A small, unreachable cave can be seen above a large, mossy slab in the steep wall, while mist clings to the ground underneath the dark canopy that rises up to meet the ridge above.
113936: Some black, oozing vines reach out from the choked canopy towards you.

Twisted vines smother the gnarled oaks in this pitch black wood. The oaks tower upwards into the canopy, completely choked by growths of vines which tighten around their trunks. A thick, yellow substance drips from the oaks, releasing a strange smell and fine mist that hovers above the forest floor, which is covered with oddly-warped plants that seem to grasp towards any movement.
113937: A tangled creeper writhes its shoots between the forest's roots upwards.

The pair of ancient alders grow intricately upwards, their boles and branches scoured by time. Vastly larger than the surrounding trees, they reach up together and touch, forming a dark canopy through which only a small amount of light breaks through. A deep layer of brown leaves covers the ground, where grasses and ferns grow. A fine mist flows in from the west.
113938: The forest stands tall, with stout oaks that rise with knotted branches up to the thick canopy above. Hung from their twisted arms, snake a large number of wicked vines that bite deep into the oaks, leeching sap from their dark boles. The falling ridge from the northwest halts its course, revealing a tiny, dark hole in the limestone wall beneath a tangle of roots covered with wet moss.
113939: Some black, oozing vines reach out from the choked canopy towards you.

Boles of oak and alder rise up to a dark canopy completely choked by strong vines. A thick liquid drips from the trees as the twisted vines leech the sap from the tree trunks, leaving a sour smell hanging in the air. The forest floor is covered with small grasses, a fine layer of moss, and leaves that sit among the gnarled roots that crawl into the limestone bedrock and soil.
113940:
A blooming water-lily floats on the surface of the water.
A black pond is here, filled with putrid water.
A tangled creeper writhes its shoots between the forest's roots upwards.

The wet, mossy slope descends into a dark, limestone sinkhole, lined by several twisted oaks. A small foul-smelling pond of standing water rests among the green reeds and warped boles. A large, limestone slab juts out into the pond beyond the black mud, near some gently-floating lily pads and watercress.
113941:
A half-decayed corpse of a goblin lies rotting on the ground.
Massive roots shift uneasily all around you.
A huge black bear, saliva frothing from its jaws, bellows a challenge.

Thick roots dangle from the limestone ceiling above as they continue downwards into the floor of this dark cave. The floor is covered with the countless, gnawed bones of creatures in varying states of decay. As the cave progresses towards the back of the hollow, it rises upwards into a tangled mess of roots, where a dark hole can be spotted leading further up into the darkness.
113942: The grassy, leaf-covered bedrock dips into a wide sinkhole. The entrance of a root-covered cavern gapes to the west, the result of the underlying cavern buckling and sending the overlying slabs of limestone crashing downwards. Above the rubble, an entwining forest canopy looms, lifted by huge oaken boles from the dark wood that line the rigid, unclimbable walls of the sinkhole.
113943: A long escarpment of weathered limestone rises to the south as it extends from the west towards the east, where it bends northwards. At the base of the scarp, a number of shrubs grow among the heaps of rubble and grass that stretch across the land. The ground dips into a sinkhole towards the west, where a dark forest can be seen towering far above the land on a raised crag that heads northwards.
113944: A small evergreen plant grows here, its woody stems reaching two feet.

Rocky crags poke out of the raised ridge in the west, which is topped by a dark forest with an entangled canopy full of wicked vines. The moors are covered with green bracken as they extend between a falling ridge towards the east and a rising escarpment in the south, which shows a colourful range of limestone layers.
113945: Grasses and pebbles cover the craggy slope to the west, under the canopy of the dark forest that grows on the raised ridge bank in the west. Yellow and green heather covers the ground of the moors, that stretch onward to the east among the many woody shrubs and limestone slabs that cover the landscape.
113946: A brown snail is crawling across the ground here leaving a slimy trail behind.

The field is covered in soft ferns, grasses, and a delicate layer of moss. It sits under the canopy of a dark forest that grows on the top of the craggy ridge in the west. The limestone bedrock is exposed in several locations among dirty roots as the earth climbs up a steep, overgrown ridge to the north.
113949: An ancient hall has been carved out of the limestone cavern that leads to a barricade to the east. Large rocks and sparse grasses litter the mouth of this timeworn entrance, leaving the stone stairs riddled with cracks and debris. The crude, wooden barricade in the east smells strongly of fir, as a dank draft rushes past its axe-hewn wooden spikes to the white ruins above.
113950: A calm valley of green heather grows in the protective hold of a ridge as the land bends around the valley to the east and north. Small ferns and stones cover the ground among the grasses that make up the thickets that grow around here. The steppes expand outwards to the south, in a range of verdant colour. Tiny, woody shrubs dot the landscape as it slowly extends across the horizon.
113951: A small cluster of clover grows here.

Several patches of clover grow in this field, which stretches across the wide steppe in between several ridges. Heather, ferns, and woody shrubs grow across the landscape regardless of where the limestone bedrock exposes itself. A shrouded, dark forest can be seen on a raised ridge to the west, and an even larger and darker wood can be seen in the distant east, shrouded in shadow.
113952: A rock lizard is here, motionless as it observes you.

The foot of a ridge ends here as it drops harshly from its unclimbable heights towards a bracken field. Several large boulders sit in disarray at the bottom of the slope, among the lichen that smother it. Verdant shrubs, ferns, and grasses grow on the ground that leads up to the shrub-covered northeastern ridge, upon which a trail can be seen climbing up into the distance.
113953: A weedy embankment of heather lines the grass- and pebble-strewn trail, as it weaves its way across the flat steppes towards a ridge in the north. Several bushes grow some distance away from the trail, but all sights are dwarfed by an enormous, black forest in the far east that towers over the surroundings.
113954: The trail courses along the grassy steppe, lined with woody shrubs and yellow and green grasses, until it reaches the foot of a grey, limestone ridge, where it rises up on a switchback. Spreading around the trail is a wide steppe, carpeted in heather and rugged patches of shrubs among the boulders and stones.
113956: A diamond-back rattlesnake is coiled here, ready to strike.

The vegetation becomes increasingly sparse as it moves deeper into the shadows of the towering crags that line the ridge. Only patches of grass grow among the thorns and rubble that litter the ground of a rough, descending slope from the walls. Several large, knife-like boulders sit in the middle of valley, where they fell from above and then pierced the dark valley floor.
113957:
A wild dog bares his yellow fangs at you.
A wild dog bares his yellow fangs at you.
A wild dog bares his yellow fangs at you.

The grassy trail bends towards the north and west, as it reaches an eroding, limestone escarpment to the south. The weathered cliffs are highly unstable, as shown by an unsteady pile of debris that has fallen next to the pebbled trail embankment, crushing all the vegetation that grew below it. Further to the north, the heather grows undisturbed and the land widens into a plain.
113958: A furious, wild dog is here, snarling and growling.

The trail bends through a deep crevice as it heads towards the east and south, through the many exposed layers of limestone that make up a precarious, towering escarpment. Among the grey rubble and jagged stones that litter the ground, is a sparse carpet of yellow and green grasses that grow under the cliffs on either side of the steep, unclimbable banks.
113959: Before the trail enters the valley stretching far to the south, it is split by a tall fault that reaches many miles into the plateau to the west. The trail shows signs of being travelled, although not very often, and it is wide enough to let a rider travel comfortably. On the other hand, it offers little cover for someone who wishes to pass by unseen.
113960: The trail is part of the route for travelling between the Misty Mountains far away to the northwest and through the Mirkwood to the southeast. It seems little used although the earth is packed hard by heavy boots occasionally trampling it; the trail gives a slightly rough impression and a few bones, some gnawed upon, can be found here and there along the way.
113961: Instead of just following the trail southwards or eastwards, one has the possibility of going west from here, climbing the up side of the valley, to later perhaps follow the valley on its western side. Going north is made impossible by the nature of a ridge that was created by the fault.
113962:
A moderately-sized copperhead snake is here.
A moderately-sized copperhead snake is here.

This part of the valley is particularly narrow, with less than thirty yards between the very steep sides. The walls consist of hard packed earth without handholds, making any climbing attempts impossible. The sides of the walls are covered with holes about the size of the rocks that seem to cling to the cliff face high above. Some scattered bones rest on the ground among boulders.
113963: The valley makes a long, gentle bend, curving from east to north, and the trail follows the curve of the valley, staying on the valley's floor. Rain and wind have eroded the ground, washing soil away from between small rocks on the stony ground.
113964: A black crow flies low to the ground here, looking for carrion to eat.

Leaving the trail to the east, a quickly narrowing fault leads far into the west between walls of earth. The earth on the sides is too loose to let anyone climb them successfully. The undergrowth here is not very spread out and could have been trampled down by hunters passing by, wanting easier access to the prey hunted down into the fault.
113965: Reaching further into the western craggy landscape of the fault, this part of the land is too rough to give any idea of what might lie ahead or behind. Far above, on the northern side, a forest grows, making a significant contrast to the grassy ground of the fault. One wishing to visit the forest, would however, have to find a way around, because of the huge height difference.
113966: The fault digs westward into the surrounding plateaus, making an east-west passage. Little grass grows on the ground, where as the walls to the north and south are of hard packed earth, without any handholds. Their vertical angle forces the traveller to choose another route.
113967:
A half-decayed corpse of a goblin lies rotting on the ground.
A vulture is here, pecking at a corpse.
A vulture is here, pecking at a corpse.

The natural fault in the ground comes to an abrupt end as it widens and hits a cliff wall to the west. Some stones of different sizes have tumbled down the slide and lie in untidy piles. Some remnants of the animals are slowly decaying into dust at the cliff wall. Far above, some branches stretching south from the forest to the north can be sighted. The steep walls are impossible to climb and the only possible route follows the fault eastwards.
113968: The damp soil makes this a perfect growing area for many kinds of mosses. All stones, big and small, are completely covered with lichen on their northern sides. To the west lies a north-south going trail, while the plains continue towards the south. Movement northwards is made impossible by a limestone cliff.
113969: The field extends southwards to a higher plateau with a steep side covered with the same short grass that grows on the ground around here. The soil here, however, becomes damper as it approaches the vivid field in the north. To the west a trail can be seen going down into a valley in the far distance.
113970: Bend in a Trail through a Valley

From here the trail leads shortly east before it seems to turn north again, continuing in its major north-south direction. The valley becomes unusually wide here with a field lying just beside the road. The brush-covered end of the valley is visible further to the west. Some thick, impassable brush grows to the north. Some gravel is lying on the ancient, mostly-unused trail.
113971: The trail keeps zig-zagging southwest, following the valley between its steep, unclimbable sides. From this deep down, however, little can be known about the fields beyond the sides of the valley. Some eerie shadows from the large forest to the southeast pass by now and then, as if the forest were alive.
113972: At this place the sides of the valley are particularly close to each other creating a close passage that would unavoidably turn into a bottleneck if many were to pass it at the same time. The narrowness of the area concentrates the wind, clearing the area of high-growing vegetation. To the south, the trail straightens, while its northern continuation winds to the northeast.
113973: Following the valley, the trail winds between the two plateaus. Beneath the western side, a pile of debris tells the story of people unsuccessfully trying to climb the wall or perhaps the result of some erosion. To the east, the grassy plains ascend in a less steep manner.
113974: The trail curves here along the plateu to the west. The trail itself grows some turf of grass here and there, but likely the trail is not totally without use. The forest of Mirkwood looms farther to the east, and the air seems to be denser and darker there than here.
113975:
A boulder lies here on the trail.
An ancient fungus smothers the boulders.
An uruk of the Morgundul tribe is here commanding his soldiers.
An uruk of the Morgundul tribe is here commanding his soldiers.
An orc-guard of the Morgundul is on patrol here.
An orc-guard of the Morgundul is on patrol here.

Just next to the escarpment to the west, a trail runs and bends from the east to the south. A boulder, formerly embedded in the side of the escarpment, has fallen down on the trail leaving a big hole where it formerly sat. However, the hole is too high and still makes it impossible to climb up the steep wall.
113976: A giant brown turtle is peeking from under its shell.

This mudddy field is somewhat mushy underfoot but neither humanoids, nor animals risk sinking down. Movement is not more difficult than in any other field, except there is some risk for boots to become dirty. A large amount of vegetative cover in the form of grasses and bushes grows here due to a hidden water source. Some large, plodding animal's tracks can be seen in the mud.
113978: A colony of red ants is here. The ants seem to ignore you.

The grass of the field seems to have been burnt by the sun causing it to grow very short, in a faded yellowish colour. To the west, the grass does not reach over the ground, as it has been trampled by feet and hooves of some animal. To the southeast the vegetation is healthier and several bushes can be seen.
113979: The trees thin out to the east and end before reaching here. Some black undergrowth thrives here, making the terrain very bushy, that at times can be tiresome to pass through. To the north, the ground cover is replaced by mostly dark grasses.
113980:
You see two woody, stemmed plants on the ground.
An elaborate red flower sits within a dark mass of briars.

Standing next to the plains, the trees that constitute this light forest do not appear that gloomy. Further inside, however, there seems to be an impenetrable darkness. To get to it though, another way must be found as there is a steep slope blocking the path to the east, and an even steeper cliff wall to the south.
113981:
An orkish wolf-rider is here, riding a brown wolf.
A sand viper is slithering here on the ground.
An orkish wolf-rider is here, riding a brown wolf.

While there are some blackened tree trunks and bushes strewn about the area, this field is mostly devoid of large vegation as it is so close to the forest of Mirkwood. Some dark lichen can be seen creeping out of the forest, covering the ground among the dark, gnarled roots. The grass disappears as a steep slope leading to the west reveals another field.
113982: An enormous, gnarled tree lies here across the landscape.

An enormous, hollow tree has fallen from the forest above, creating a strange hovel-like structure where its bottom has been cracked open. The bones of several animals can be seen strewn about in various states of decay. Very little grass grows here in the sparse light due to the shadows cast by the forest on the cliff above. The walls of the eastern cliffs are steep.
113983: A tawny-coated bear is snuffling about.

This enormous tree is gnarled, hideous, and reeks of decaying flesh and wood. Black bark is coming off of it in sloughs and the trunk is completely covered with yellow and orange fungi. The huge hollow of this rotting tree seems to have been fashioned into a den by some giant, predatory creature. Large rotting bones of various animals and humanoids are everywhere.
113986: A sharp-eyed hawk is here stalking some prey.

The bushes to the south are so dense that nothing can be seen through them. An ancient trail can be seen leading along the northern and western sides of the plains in the distance. A dark forest spans across the eastern horizon, looking awfully sinister.
113987: The old, gravelly trail passes to the south and north here. On the trail there are signs of a recent skirmish between unknown sides. Some blood markings on the grass and marks on the ground are left as evidence. To the east lies a field that sits opposite a trail running to the north and south.
113988: An old construction has resided next to the trail, maybe an old resting place or trading post for travellers. Now the construction is only a pile of rubble consisting of dark grey stones. There is an old campfire behind the rubble, long since gone cold. The ancient, gravelly trail leads to the north, and turns here towards the east and west, splitting when it meets a rising slope.
113989: A trail leads through this brushland which offers very little nourishment to attract many grasses. To the north, the brush seems to grow too high to allow anyone to pass; but to the south brush turns into grasslands where the trail continues in a latitudinal fashion.
113990: A large mother hawk is here looking for a prey to feed her young.

Following the lower end of the slope to the east, the trail offers no passage to the dark trees that cover the slope to the east. The trail leads on to the west and south. Entering the forest of Mirkwood would require ascending up the large cliff. However, the vertical cliff is not climbable.
113991: A large mother hawk is here looking for a prey to feed her young.

The trail continues along the rock face, atop which a few dark branches from the Mirkwood Forest can be sighted reaching over the edge. The rock face doesn't offer any footholds for someone wanting to try their luck ascending it. Travellers who are going to the adjacent plain in the west will have an easy trip.
113992: A small path twists its way nearby the forest. The path goes through a depression in the plains. There is an open way through the depression in north-south fashion. The depression is mostly of gravel and dirt, a few bigger boulders lay on the side of the path too. To the east and west there are steep bluffs, making a travel in those directions not viable.
113993:
A demon wolf lurks here, its dark form twisting and hiding its shape.
A demon wolf lurks here, its dark form twisting and hiding its shape.
A huge warg is here, moving in for the kill.
A huge warg is here, moving in for the kill.

A small path has formed at the border of the forest, forcing its way around bushes and the many contorted roots that protrude from the undergrowth. A few saplings grow here and there, proof of the continuous growth of the forest. Black thorns grow from a few more mature sprouts.
113994: These plains are unusually flat, as if they had been trampled by giants for millennia, allowing a traveller to go across them without much troubley. To the south, a fir tree can be seen standing solemly in a field, while a north-south trail passes by to the east.
113995:
A lonely fir tree stands here in lone majesty.
On the tree's branches are two small eggs.
A woodpecker is here, tapping on a tree.
Some thick writhing vines whip all around you.

A lone fir tree marks the landscape. Several vines have attached themselves to the tree, ensnaring it slowly but surely. A few small trees have taken root here as well, denoting the continuous forest growth. A large brush grows to the east, its thorny branches spreading far.
113996: The plains rise sharply to the north, ending in a cliff from which more plains can be spotted, as well as two trails that lead through them. Dark grass occupies most of the field, with a few plants growing here and there. A lone tree lies to the east, the tallest that can be found for miles.
113997:
A sprawling, twisted tree grows here.
On the tree, there are two piles of hawthorn berries.

Small bushes bearing few leaves form a small brush patch that grows larger to the east. Many small ditches are to be found, some of them hidden by tall dark green grass that grows together in many round patches. In some places no vegetation can be found, showing only the earthen soil. Small pawprints are found in the earth, although most are quite old.
113998:
An uruk of the Morgundul tribe is here commanding his soldiers.
An uruk of the Morgundul tribe is here commanding his soldiers.
An orc-guard of the Morgundul is on patrol here.
An orc-guard of the Morgundul is on patrol here.
A sharp-eyed hawk is here stalking some prey.

Next to the crossing to the east, there is a building, where whoever stayed, could have guarded the passage or could seek cover from weather and attacking foes. Now it is only a ruin without a roof with walls that are little more than piles of stones. Past it to the south, the unkept road continues through a valley pass.
113999: Several spiny bushes cover the bleak earth, most over three feet tall and over six feet wide. They bear no berries, only sharp black thorns that bear crimson dots. A small skeleton of a bird lies on top of one of the bushes, perforated by a few of the thorns.
114000:
A long-bodied animal with thick brown fur bounds through the trees.
A demon wolf lurks here, its dark form twisting and hiding its shape.
A demon wolf lurks here, its dark form twisting and hiding its shape.
A huge warg is here, moving in for the kill.
A huge warg is here, moving in for the kill.

Several thorny branches of nearby bushes form an intricate maze, preventing travellers from smoothly pass through it. Gnarled roots, an extension of the forest to the east, form a natural barrier to the south and east. The roots are grey in colour. The ends that stick out of the undergrowth are sometimes sharp, sometimes almost completely shrivelled.
114001: Close by the forest, a myriad of different shrubs and bushes have taken root, taking the nutrients from the soil that were denied them in the forest itself. Many brambles and little fruit is found on the shrubs, their thorns coloured a deep shade of red, resembling blood. Many of the thorns litter the undergrowth, urging travellers with light feet protection to proceed with caution.
114002: An overgrown path curves next to a forest border, leading travellers south and west. The dark forest seems to be alive, seen most clearly by small, pitch-black roots twisting on the path. Encircling the path are small bubbling puddles of grey mud. A few roots that have ventured in the mud have shrivelled even more than usual, and lie there forever still.
114003:
An orc-guard of the Morgundul is on patrol here.
An orc-guard of the Morgundul is on patrol here.
A tall Uruk paces about, issuing commands to his troops.
A tall Uruk paces about, issuing commands to his troops.
A Morgundul orc snarls about here, looking for a fight.
A Morgundul orc snarls about here, looking for a fight.
A relentless uruk of the Morgundul tribe is leading his soldiers here.
A demon wolf lurks here, its dark form twisting and hiding its shape.
A demon wolf lurks here, its dark form twisting and hiding its shape.

The path twists and turns through the encroaching undergrowth that seems destined to swallow it. A few bones, possibly humanoid, lie in a small pile, half-hidden under the roots of an upturned tree. The tree bark is heavily damaged, marked by several axes and swords. An axe blade has been left behind in the tree, covered in rust.
114004: Little more than gravel is left of the road that once ran through the plains. Half a mile to the south of the old road a cliff dominates the view. To the east an extremely steep slope leads upwards to a plateau in the plains.
114005: Twisting and turning, the old road makes its last visible sharp bend on its way through the plains. From here on, the road seems to run straight into the distance to the south. To the north and west the plains rise too sharply to allow climbing, but the road to the east continues on level ground.
114006: A huge grizzly bear is here, roaming the wild.

Grey stones have been put together in ages past to create this large road. The road is in an abominable state, heavily overgrown, and it bears many chipped and broken stones. The earth declines to the south, while it slowly increases to the west. A large bush stands next to the road, leafless and without fruit.
114007: Many small tufts of grass form a great patch, increasing in size to the east. The earth slants upwards as well, ending in a small cliff to the north. The south and the east are blocked by steep slopes, which leaves the west, where small white stones form a road.
114008: Withered brown and yellow grass can be found everywhere, with small patches of lush grass growing in between them. A small patch of weeds with purple flowers grows near a small knoll. Many small pebbles litter the limestone soil, leading to the east where they meet a road. The west becomes quite steep, the ridges too far apart to be crossed without climbing skills.
114009: A large road, unkempt and little-travelled, leads travellers south and upwards towards the north. Weeds growing under the bricks have broken them in two or more pieces. Due to its state of decay, the road is now coloured partly green or dark grey, with limited amounts of the original white still showing slightly. Beside the weeds, some tall grasses grow here, adding more green colour to the landscape.
114010: A large black bull stamps his hooves, whilst examining the surroundings.

A medium-sized road, half-hidden by vegetation that has had decades to fester. The large stones that form the road are mostly intact, as the way is not well travelled. Patches of low grass grow beside the road, intertwined with few clover, daffodils, and buttercups, each adding a coloured twist to the otherwise green field.
114011:
An apple tree with bright green leaves grows here.
On the tree's branches are two apples.

Passing a drinking pond to the west, the road continues to the north and the south, although it slopes heavily there. Many different rocks litter the ground, some of them covered with green moss. A few birch and apple trees grow here, providing shelter and shade from the forces of nature.
114012:
A low and wide-spread tree grows here.
On the tree's branches, there are two juicy plums.

The field slopes heavily upwards to the west, although the way there is not very steep. This is not the case to the north, where it is impossible to advance further due to the strong elevation. The soil here is covered with green and brown grasses, with small trees steadily growing upwards. A road lies to the east, although it is heavily overgrown.
114013: The earth gently slopes upwards to the north, whilst a more rugged slope leads downwards to the east. The field is quite treacherous, having hundreds of small pits, most of which are partially overgrown by the local flora and thick moss.
114014: Grass grows all around, in different lengths and colours. On the western side, the blades are a verdant green with an exceptionally sharp edge, growing quite closely together in a large patch of grass. On the opposite side, the grass is at least three inches wide with a much paler complexion. One small white stone lies abandoned to the east.
114015: A clear-watered, turquoise pond is here in between of small hills.

The ground is quite uneven, creating a landscape of many small hills. A pond has formed here, where the local fauna comes to drink, as can be seen by the many animal tracks near the edge of the water and bite marks on twigs and leaves. Many thick bushes thrive here, along with a myriad of different plants and flowers.
114016: Thousands of small cracks with holes over one inch wide can be found in the black, earthen soil. Where there are cracks, there is little or no vegetation, and what little vegetation is here, is mostly stunted or charred. A few small pools have formed here, although most of them are little more than thick mud. Thick bubbles pop up on the pool surface, emitting a foul odour.
114017: A small cluster of clover grows here.

A lone arrow sticks out in the centre of the field, firmly planted into the soil. No vegetation surrounds it, making it an excellent marker. A few lone beech trees add some variation to the otherwise plain landscape, mostly filled with long grasses and thick brush. The earth is mostly flat, yet laden with many small cracks.
114018: Many small white stones have been put together to form a road that runs through these plains. Small roots, belonging to a large oak tree, stick out of a few stones. Many flowers grow on both sides of the road, a rainbow of colours. The earth slopes upwards to the north.
114019: A large rabbit looks peacefully at you, ready to dart away.

Large, white stones close together formed a road once in the past. What remains today are grey and green coloured stones that lie scattered around, broken by nature and time. The road itself is still partly intact, yet unable to suffer large and heavy weights, such as caravans or merchant carts.
114020: Large square stones that have turned grey and dark green with age and wear form a road leading down to the south and northwards. Many small weeds grow in and around it, showing that the road is not well-maintained. Large fields can be found on either side of the road, sloping heavily.
114021: Many small mounds form quite uneven ground on which this road has been built. The plants and grass that grow on these mounds are somehow more lush than those growing elsewhere. A few thornbushes grow west of the road in a strange pattern, one that resembles a skull. The road continues to the north and the south, whilst a cliff can be seen to the east.
114022: A brown fox is here, looking for some rabbits to chew up.

The road that runs west and north here lies in total decay. Many stones have upturned and several of them are broken in half due to growing weeds below. The weeds and dark green moss cover the stones, marking the road as one not well maintained or travelled.
114023: Small grey bricks, chipped and broken, together form a little-maintained road. Grey moss and weeds grow between the stones, almost covering them completely. On the western edge of the road, an abandoned horseshoe catches the eye. The road ascends sharply to the west, leading travellers upwards, whilst to the east the uneven ground mostly remains on the same level.
114024: Leading north and south, a heavily worn road can be found here. Most of the once white and now grey stones are covered almost entirely with grass, moss, and weeds. A few mushrooms grow beside it as well, differing in colour. The ground slopes heavily downwards to the north.
114025: A large beech tree stands upon a small hill, the only point of recognition for miles, as the surrounding landscape is filled with the same small bushes and random vegetation. Thick, grey roots have surfaced over five feet away from the tree, covered with many small fungi.
114026: A grassy field lies south, whilst in other parts the land is quite barren, save for a few bushes and weeds. The ground slants up and down irregularly, creating an unsteady footing. The grass reaches no more than a foot in height, growing in patches a few feet wide. A few small animal-dug holes are found in the earth, hinting of wildlife close by. A road can be seen to the west.
114027: Innumerable bushes of varying sizes grow here, almost turning this area into a jungle. Small twigs litter the ground surrounding them, many of them broken. The brushwood is dense in some places, with roots appearing out of eroded earth. The earth twists downwards to the south.
114028: Many small ridges that are quite close together forming small steps that lead travellers randomly up and down. The ridges also create two stairways, leading to the valley floor below and upwards to a cliff. A few small trees grow in between the grass, although they bear no leaves. The field continues to the west.
114030:
A nest is here.
A big, nasty vulture is sitting here, protecting its nest.

The surface of the cliff is minimal, only allowing room for a few creatures to stand upon it. Crab grass grows all over, yet it is the only vegetation to be found. Looking below, small ridges form a steep path below, although it would be an arduous climb. On the western edge, a sharp rock stands, shaped like an S.
114031: The earth seems to have almost split in two, creating two small hills with a twisting line in the middle. Apart from a lone tree and a few thick bushes, grass is the dominant growth. It varies greatly in height and colour, from being grazed and lush green not so long ago to only a few dark brown inches.
114032: A large rabbit looks peacefully at you, ready to dart away.

Aside from a lone birch tree, this field is laden with weeds, varying greatly in size and form, some little more than woody thorns, while others near the size of young bushes. The leafage is mottled with uneven black spots with hints of brown and red in them. A few small twigs lie scattered on the ground, bleak and leafless.
114033: Short, brown grass grows on a small slope in this barren steppe, the only large patch of vegetation to be found, besides lone patches of weeds. Small rocks litter the cracked earth, which rises up in sharp contrast, creating a heavily uneven ground. A few animal leavings lie to the north, where the soil is much more thick and lush.
114034: A carcass, devoid of meat, lies half-hidden amongst tall, mottled grass. Over two feet high, the grass is uneaten by the local fauna, perhaps due to the odd black specks that mark the grass. It does rustle continuously, hinting of lower lifeforms that populate the ground. In a few places, the grass has been trampled, hinting of higher lifeforms as well.
114035: A brown fox is here, looking for some rabbits to chew up.

In the centre of this area are a couple of blackberry bushes, surrounded by medium-sized grass. Across the field, a few patches have been grazed clean, leaving nothing for the eye but a bare patch of earth. A few animal droppings litter the ground, although they appear to be quite old.
114036: The grass is exceptionally verdant here, something that has not escaped the local fauna, as most of it has been trimmed by bites, leaving only few slightly more brown patches that have grown tall. The green parts only reach a few inches high, where infant bushes and plants have leave to steal their sunlight and forever leave them stunted.
114037: Several lush grasses grow here, some having grown over three feet tall, as yet untouched by the wildlife. The grass is mostly green in colour, although near the western end, some have become mottled and brown. A small, muddy black puddle has formed there, the grass that stands in it black and withered.
114038: Some small rocks have been piled into a mound here.

Jagged rocks litter this grassy field, scattered like disarrayed pawns on a chessboard. A few rocks bear lichen and moss, while a particular rock in the middle has had its edges honed. Thick animal hairs can be found scattered on the ground beside it, proving that it is often visited by the local wildlife. A few boulders stand close together to the south, blocking a direct path southwards.
114039:
A tall pine tree grows here.
On the tree, there are two piles of pine nuts.
A tree-snake lies wrapped around one of the tree branches.

A few pine trees loom here, surrounded by thick brushwood. Many of the pine needles litter the ground, their sharp ends adding to the thorns present on the branches of the bushes. Further away from the trees, the bushes grow more apart, allowing one to spy more details. Their thorns are razor-sharp and oddly, barbed as well.
114040: Small hills of sandy ground populate this area, each small hill bearing one or two small bushes. Grass over one foot high grows in a small patch near the southern edge, leaving the rest bare, in total contrast to the surroundings. While the south becomes more grassy, the vegetation thickens everywhere else, only allowing passage northwards.
114041:
A blooming water-lily floats on the surface of the water.
A water moccasin slithers out of sight just below the surface of the water.

Medium-sized bushes grow abundantly, centring around a small puddle of clear water. A few roots stick out of the earth and dive directly into the middle of it. Succulent, verdant blades of grass grow between the bushes, some of the tufts already trampled or devoured by the passing wildlife. The vegetation increases and becomes more dense in almost every direction, forcing travellers to head westwards to escape this area.
114042: A tortoise creeps slowly through the mud.

Mottled brown and green grass from the west meets thick brushwood here, a mix of high and thorny bushes. In the centre is a muddy hole of over four feet in diameter, with multiple animal footprints leading out of it. Many bubbles can be seen in the mud, one having popped at this exact second.
114043:
A buck runs swiftly from place to place, looking about warily as it grazes.
A buck runs swiftly from place to place, looking about warily as it grazes.

Three-foot high, thick bushes prevail over the lower-lying vegetation, which has largely diminished to due the stolen sunlight and soil nourishment. The bushes concentrate heavily to the south and the west, blocking any direct passageway. One small bush lies alone to the east, blacker and more withered than its comrades.
114044: A large beautiful rose bush is blooming here.

The thick brushwood is cut in half as the earth slopes up and down continuously. A couple of the bushes that are directly on top of the slope, have their roots protrude from out of the earth. Due to the uneven ground, the area is quite difficult to traverse. The brush continues on for miles in every direction.
114045: Thick, thorny stems grow all around, colouring the area green and brown. A few bushes are different than the others. Instead of having grown tall and lush, they are crooked, with withered leaves that emit a foul odour. They are centred around the northwest, yet slowly spread to the rest of the brush.
114046:
A skeleton of some humanoid lies in the dust.
A large brown snake with black patches is coiled here.
A large brown snake with black patches is coiled here.

This small area is infested with thick brush and thorny plants, impeding swift movement. The vegetation is the thickest westward, where it is impossible to move through. A few young trees grow northwards, where they meet the forest. To the east, the vegetation becomes paler and less thick, bushes clearing the way for grass.
114047: An ancient fungus smothers the boulders.

Great, crooked birch and pine trees cover the entire area, their branches flaying in every direction regardless of the wind as they block the sunlight coming from above. The foliage below is pale and stunted, struggling to survive. Thick, blackish moss grows on the trees, along with a few fungi.
114048:
A shrub with maple-like leaves is growing here.
On the shrub, there are two handfuls of blackcurrant berries.
A thin, crippled deer looks around timidly.
A fallow deer is grazing peacefully here.

Tall stands of pale yellow grass grows in dense clusters before slowly fading towards a thick, gloomy forest towards the north and east. Below the grass, smaller plants struggle in vain for sunlight, and have become pale in colour and spindly in height in their attempts to grow upwards. A few bushes have managed to struggle through the high grass and flourish in the moist soil.
114049: The forest begins to get very dark as an air of despair sets in. The trees have a blackened appearance among their trunks and the vegetation of the forest floor has a dark hue to it. It seems as though no sunlight is allowed to travel through the forest ceiling and the ground foliage thrives on malevolence rather than sunlight.
114050:
There are two mushrooms here.
An ancient fungus smothers the boulders.
A huge black fungus is here, exuding a foul stench.
A huge black fungus is here, exuding a foul stench.

Fungi of all sorts populate this part of the forest. There are mushrooms of all colours and huge shelf fungi grow on the trunks of the dark oak and beech trees. The fungus grows so thick here that it has created a flora all its own on the forest floor with chunks of fungal crust covering the ground. The spores are so thick here that they cloud the very air like a noxious fog.
114051:
On the ground, there are two mushrooms.
A tall and proud elf is standing here.
A tall and proud elf is standing here.
A tall and proud elf is standing here.

Gloom fills the air in these woods. There are looming trees in every direction, which have borne the weight of this despair for many years. The trunks here are a dark shade of grey, as is the ground surrounding them. There are grey mushrooms on the ground all about.
114052:
A small mushroom grows nearby.
An elf, clad in the garments of a woodsman, moves stealthily among the trees.
An elf, clad in the garments of a woodsman, moves stealthily among the trees.
Dolion, Marchwarden of Taur-nu-Fuin, blends in with the shadows of the forest.
A large, black butterfly is fluttering about erratically.

The trees, which loom in every direction, open up into a small glade here. There is an air of serenity and calm here, as if the malice and gloom that permeate Mirkwood are held at bay. Some mushrooms grow in the area, clustering more densely toward the south.
114053:
A large, black butterfly is fluttering about erratically.
A large, black butterfly is fluttering about erratically.

The gloomy forest makes a natural corridor as the trees loom in on every side. Twisted patterns seem to form angry faces in the bark. There are thick, heavy cobwebs hanging from the limbs just overhead. The way west and south is blocked by the huge trunks of the twisted trees that grow there.
114054:
A long water trough made of wood stands here.
A domesticated pony, beast of burden to many, stands here.
A domesticated pony, beast of burden to many, stands here.
A sturdy trained horse is standing here.

The overbearing forest thins just enough here to make it passable, but these traveller's gains are not without penance. Jagged rocks stab forth from the cloak of thorny brush and decaying matter that make up the forest floor, slicing toward the veiled sky. The land slopes slightly downward to the south, where the trees look sickly and pale.
114055:
A greenish slime mould is here, smelling badly.
Some black, oozing vines reach out from the choked canopy towards you.
A huge black fungus is here, exuding a foul stench.

The pale, sickly trees here are coated with a thin, dark slime, from which issues the putrid smell of decay and corruption. Their branches reach plaintively toward a sky that is unremittingly just out of reach. The ground underfoot has turned to thick, black mud that sucks at the feet of anything attempting to traverse it, making movement difficult. Grasping, choking vines encrusted with razor-sharp barbed thorns adorn every branch still harbouring enough life to support them.
114056:
A cluster of dark green, feathery fronds flourishes in the shade.
An elven scout stands here, blending in with the background.

A thick matting of fallen leaves covers the ground under the stooping canopy of trees above. A watch post has been created here under the dense foliage. Soft piles of grass lie strategically placed to allow comfort during a long pass of keeping watch. The foliage to the east, north, and west might appear impenetrable at first glance but cleverly arranged branches and leaves allow a view of the trail beyond, albeit somewhat restricted.
114057:
A large toadstool grows nearby.
A gorcrow is standing here.

Sickly pine trees grow here, their boughs hanging low as if in defeated dismay. The tall, dismal pines creak and groan as their rotting trunks shift unendingly. Above, their ragged canopies have grown together, forming a thick cover that blot out the sky.
114058: Tall pine trees with their boughs sagging from some unseen weight grow here in a look of eternal sadness. The ground to the northeast begins to become soggy and a putrid smell wafts in from that direction. The miserable pine trees continue their mourning to the east and west.
114059: Sorrowful pine trees grow here, populating the west part of this section of the forest. Dense bushes make up the undergrowth to the southeast, making the forest completely impassable. The northern area is soggy and wet, as a swamp lies in that direction.
114060: There are two sturdy flowering plants here.

Thick, healthy beech trees grow here, many with significantly brighter shades of colour on their bark. The beech trees grow so thick to the west because of the abundant sunlight that is available there that they create a vegetation wall that is impassable.
114061:
A hollow tree is growing upright here.
A great horned owl looks cautiously around it.
A gorcrow is standing here.

Large, expansive beech trees meet sad, sagging pines which invade with their forlorn, stationary procession from the north. Sticky brambles and huge, demented thorn bushes expand from the east causing a meeting of the different types of vegetation in the middle of this beech tree forest.
114062:
An elaborate red flower sits within a dark mass of briars.
A tangled creeper writhes its shoots between the forest's roots upwards.

Large thorn bushes and tangled brambles grow in a flourish here. Their leaves secrete a sticky black sap which sticks fast to everything it comes into contact with. The thornbushes have huge thorns the size of small eagle talons which threaten to jab at the slightest breath of air.
114063:
A black, thorny bush grows here, enshrouded in a murky gloom.
A half-decayed corpse of a goblin lies rotting on the ground.
A black crow flies low to the ground here, looking for carrion to eat.
A black crow flies low to the ground here, looking for carrion to eat.

Towering trees, hundreds of feet tall, spread heavy branches that let pass no hint of the sky above. These giants so dominate their surroundings that no vegetation grows beneath them other than a rugged and tangled mass of roots, each as thick as a man is tall. Between ground and canopy there is nothing but an expanse of heavy, oppressive darkness.
114064: Massive roots shift uneasily all around you.

The ground here is very bumpy and difficult to grasp a foothold on. There are roots of every size and thickness growing all about as if there is not enough soil to share between them. There are many roots which normally would be growing underground, but are exposed to the forest air.
114065: A shimmering glow is here, emitting pale, green, light.

There is a low point of elevation in the forest here that collects the mist that seems to float all about this area. There are wisps of some transparent forms which float to and fro. Among the trees that grow surrounding this depression can be heard some strange whispering sounds of unseen beings.
114066: A black crow flies low to the ground here, looking for carrion to eat.

Dead trees still rooted in the ground dominate this section of the forest, giving it an eerie appearance. Rotting branches on the ground encourages insect infestations and give off a rotten smell. Barely enough branches with blackened leaves remain on the dead trees to shield the ground from direct sunlight.
114067:
Massive, black, oozing vines reach out from the choked canopy.
A black crow flies low to the ground here, looking for carrion to eat.

A slight rise from the west gives way to leaning, twisted oak trees among which the whispers of shifting branches can faintly be heard. The ground is covered in a thick layer of blackened leaves. Faint whispers of fog swirl around the oak tree's boles, only to dissipate as soon as they begin to take shape.
114068:
The corpse of a grim wolverine is lying here.
A colossal tree, its trunk as wide as a small cottage, stands here.

Huge trunks with blackened bark, these ancient oak trees grow with strange, malevolent vibrancy. The tops of the trees are quite high here, blotting out any sunlight that may attempt to reach the rotting flora below. The air is oppressively humid from the moisture which slowly collects from the swamps to the west.
114069: The forest floor is quite lumpy here as the swamp to the north dissipates itself into this part of the forest. There are dry patches on which great black oak trees grow as small tributaries from the swamp lie in natural moats around them, with stagnant, stinking water.
114070: A hollow tree is growing upright here.

The thick trunks of darkened trees stand in silent watch over the soft, leaf-covered ground. A faint sound fills the air, as if hundreds of voices were constantly whispering from very far away, but no words or meaning can be discerned.
114071: A cluster of dark green, feathery fronds flourishes in the shade.

Dark and gloomy oak trees hang overhead within a shadowed canopy. Not much can be seen here besides the huge tree trunks which obstruct the view in any direction beyond a few strides. Large fungi grow here out of the duff layer, which is mainly composed of tree roots and fallen branches. A constant moaning sound can be heard off to the west.
114073:
A large cockroach is crawling on the ground.
A large cockroach is crawling on the ground.
A small centipede is here scurrying about.
A small centipede is here scurrying about.

Matted moss hangs from the limbs of the oak trees here, choking this part of the forest in its thick infestation. There are disgusting insects crawling all throughout the moss and other vegetation. Huge chunks of moss, which have fallen from the branches of the trees, lie on the ground decomposing and making a terrible stink.
114074:
The wicked undergrowth rustles malevolently, shifting and widening.
A small termite is running around making strange sounds.
A small termite is running around making strange sounds.

Ancient, twisted oak trees grow here with a tortured appearance. Huge, malignant looking burls grow on the sides of the trunks, looking like some tortured goblin-faces. There is a terrible stink in the air as if there is disease lurking about here.
114075:
A gorcrow is standing here.
A black crow flies low to the ground here, looking for carrion to eat.

A soft moaning can faintly be heard, seeming to originate from within the dark oaks that stand here. A faint smell fills the air, a smell of rot and decay and wet vegetation. The leaves on many of the oaks are unnaturally black, making them even more effective at creating an impenetrable canopy.
114076:
A cluster of dark green, feathery fronds flourishes in the shade.
A huge black fungus is here, exuding a foul stench.
A huge black fungus is here, exuding a foul stench.
A huge black fungus is here, exuding a foul stench.
A monstrous grey, putrid fungus is growing on a large oak here.

Decrepit vegetation and decaying flowers indicate the remnants of an ancient garden. If a garden was ever tended in this place, it has now become a breeding ground for atrocious plants that thrive in the oppressive evil of this part of the forest. The ground gets soft to the west.
114077: On the ground, there are two mushrooms.

The trees rooted here in the muck are characterized more by decay than life. Their black, limp leaves hang from drooping branches and the smell of death and rotting vegetation hangs in the air. There are quite possibly the remains of dead animals or humanoids sunken under the mud and dead plants.
114078:
A long slender eel glides along the water, its body coiled to strike.
Something cold and scaly slithers past your leg.
A knotty tree grows here, entangled in a rotten mess of wet shrubbery.

Still swamp water sits here with floating, rotting vegetation on its surface. A few trees grow feebly in the waist deep water, dropping their dark-coloured leaves to add to the rotting muck floating about them. To the west the mire is not as deep and is replaced by a surface of stinking muck.
114079:
A knotty tree grows here, entangled in a rotten mess of wet shrubbery.
A swarm of mosquitoes is here, humming around you.

The mud here is so thick that it is exhausting to travel through. A nasty smell hangs in the air as of death and overgrowth of a swamp. The filth here seems to suck in and devour all that it comes into contact with, making it very difficult to navigate a safe path through the treacherous mire.
114080:
A knotty tree grows here, entangled in a rotten mess of wet shrubbery.
Some black, oozing vines reach out from the choked canopy towards you.
A small leech is here, floating in the water.

The forest gives way to dark, muddy water that continues south and west. No light penetrates the thick, chaotic web of thorn-encrusted vines that bind the forest canopy together. Wretched, pale trees reach plaintively toward an invisible sky. The water appears to be filled with shoals of eyeless fish, spiny forms that dart back and forth just under the surface.
114081:
A knotty tree grows here, entangled in a rotten mess of wet shrubbery.
A large leech is moving close to you, searching for blood.
A swarm of mosquitoes is here, humming around you.
A small leech is here, floating in the water.
A swarm of mosquitoes is here, humming around you.
A swarm of mosquitoes is here, humming around you.

Trees here reach for the sky in a futile attempt to escape the poisonous swamp water, yet some of the plant life here seems to thrive on the life-stealing properties of the swamp. The forlorn trees look to give way to a mixed muck and few or no trees to the south. The muck to the south could be dangerous as it appears that it could suck an unwary traveller under.
114082:
Massive roots shift uneasily all around you.
Massive roots shift uneasily all around you.

Enormous gnarled roots grow all about here as if to protect the cavern which they have carved out below. The roots have grown in a pattern in which to cause a natural wall in all directions except for the curtain-like growth of vegetation made of dead roots to the east. The smell of death lingers in the thick air as faint sounds of movement can be heard from below.
114083:
A large bat is here, hanging in the darkness.
A large bat is here, hanging in the darkness.

Roots are growing all over in every direction here but there is space enough to fit through. The roots are strong and can withstand a large amount of weight. The experienced climber could use the roots growing all about in this vertical tunnel almost as a ladder.
114084:
The corpse of a small bat is lying here.
The corpse of a large bat is lying here.
A patch of moss grows here on a wet, flat stone.
A black, leather-scaled reptile glances around with gleaming eyes.
A black, leather-scaled reptile glances around with gleaming eyes.
A large bat is here, hanging in the darkness.

Padded and moist clumps of moss group thick in this cavern, some giving off an iridescent glow. A hollow wind can be heard coming from above, from a vertical tunnel. There are a few roots hanging down from the tunnel, providing a means for climbing up. The moss seems to move about slowly in some of the darker, tighter corners of the cavern. The cave opens up to a round tunnel to the east.
114085:
A black, leather-scaled reptile glances around with gleaming eyes.
A black, leather-scaled reptile glances around with gleaming eyes.
A large bat is here, hanging in the darkness.

The thick moss continues to grow all about in this round tunnel. Burly chunks of moss, which could no longer be held fast to the tunnel roof, have begun to break free and hang down. The hanging moss sways back and forth as the wind blows through the tunnel.
114086: The moss grows somewhat thinner here but is still quite prevalent. The cave has an unusually symmetrical shape to it. It is obvious that a malevolent force has carved this cavern out of the earth. There is a thick covering of dark green moss on sections of the cavern floor.
114087: A moss-covered beast advances, its movement twitchy and erratic.

A soggy bed of moss lines the bottom of this dark, cavernous pit. The moss seems to thrive in the moisture which sits stagnant in here. There are places here and there within the cavern where the water is deep and then shallow, though the mossy bed obscures much of the floor. In several places in the eastern part of the cavern's ceiling, there are long, narrow cracks where the sunlight that allows the moss to thrive comes in.
114088: Spikes of varying sizes almost completely cover the earthen floor. What space lies between them is occupied by bones of different creatures, although the majority of them are humanoid. Most of the spikes found here are very sharp, although over time, the edges have become more dull. This has been countered by rust however, and the wooden spikes that have broken still bear somewhat of a rough side that would invoke pain on those that land upon them.
114089: The plains resemble ripples, sloping up and down irregularly, gradually increasing in level to the east until it ends in a cliff. From the top, thick brushwood can be spotted on the other side, blocking the view. The cliff itself is quite laden with lush grass, with small black flowers in between. A small hole has been dug in the earth, pawprints clearly visible in the small mound of dirt beside it.
114090:
A small piece of raw meat is on the ground.
A wolf cub happily plays here.
A wolf cub happily plays here.
A huge, black wolf is here, ready to devour.
A huge, black wolf is here, ready to devour.
The mother wolf stands here, protecting her young cubs.

Many small twigs, dried brown leaves, and a large number of long, brown hairs form a mediocre soft footing in this earthen cavern. Gnawed bones, not entirely devoid of meat, lie scattered on the leaves, to be devoured when hunger strikes the creatures inhabiting the cave. The meat has started to rot however, emitting a foul smell. The cave slopes upwards to the west, marking the exit.
114091: A rock lizard is here, motionless as it observes you.

A few maple trees grow in a small grove on a ridge to the east, some of their roots protruding from the earth due to the erosion. Some of the bark has been cut from the trees, providing a sharp contrast between the dark and light brown colours. Lemongrass is abundant here, growing between the normal grass. Some of the plants have been uprooted, and lie discarded on the northern side of the plain.
114092: A large boulder rests in the centre of this area, surrounded by sickly, thin grass, as sunlight nearly never falls directly on it. The surrounding vegetation is a bit more lush, and more varied also. A few small and medium-sized bushes are scattered about, and an oddly formed tree, resembling a willow, provides shadow in the south.
114093: A cave entrance lies directly to the east, its walls an eerie dark. Dark coloured grass, more black than green, grows in front of it. Old pawprints can be seen on some trampled grass blades, at least a few inches in diameter. A large birch tree adds shadow to the field, although its bark has been heavily damaged by what could be claws. A road can be seen far to the west.
114094: A pungent smell emanates from this cavern. Two branches lie against the northern wall, they have been chewed upon and are encircled by twigs, moss and rotten leaves, which cover the entire cavern floor. The walls bear many large claw marks, going as deep through the hard-packed earth as through the thick rock.
114095: The earth suddenly slopes up and down, creating a rippling effect. A field of tall, green grass like any other can be found here, except for one detail. A large carcass devoid of sinew, meat, and fur stands in a barren spot. No grass grows around it and the earth by it is dry and cracked, which makes it very noticeable.
114096: A small valley is created as the earth slopes down towards the middle of the field. A few medium-sized trees grow here, although they are quite far apart from each other. Some trees have taken root on a rather steep section, their roots protruding from the earth on one side. The southern part of this area bears little to no resemblance to the rest of the field. The grass that is supposed to thrive is dried-out and a matted brown, the earth a slippery black.
114097:
A large thorny branched shrub is growing here.
On the shrub, there are two piles of blackberries.

Sloping sharply up and down, mounds resembling small hills are found everywhere. To the east, the ground becomes steeper with every step, slowly leading downwards. A miniscule stream drips from a small ridge into a small puddle. Thick bushes and dark green weeds thrive here, those below nourished by the wet ground and those above by the light of the sun.
114098: Many small ridges create a heavily uneven ground. It declines sharply to the east, forcing one to climb down to proceed. A few large boulders lie to the south, each having a large bush between them. Many different grasses and plants occupy this field, allowing one to spend hours identifying them all.
114100: A stump of a giant tree marks the centre of this area, heavily overgrown by weeds and surrounded by thick bushes. Chipped bark and small twigs cover the tracks of the tree, which appears to have been felled and dragged away afterwards. One thick, rotten branch lies in the northern part, covered by a swarm of insects.
114101: A mix of refuse, rotten food, and large and small bones lies all together with various other garbage on a majestic pile. A ghastly odour emanates from the pile, which would affect even the strongest. The garbage pile covers the entire field, almost tipping over the edge of the palisade to the north. A humanoid skull lies at the bottom of the pile, a crack in the middle of the forehead.
114102:
A little stone lies on the ground.
A grouchy uruk is here, lashing his whip.

The ground is littered with chipped wood and small bones, having come from the tree logs and animal carcasses that are tended to in this yard. The carcasses lie to the north, where they are to be skinned and boned. The logs lie to the west, an axe resting in one of them. A foul odour comes from the east, where a massive pile of garbage awaits.
114103:
A sturdy crate made of nailed wooden planks sits on the floor.
A large cabinet capable of storing goods is here.

Crates, shelves, and cupboards are placed strategically around the storehouse, leaving a very narrow path between them. A great deal of chopped wood has been stacked against the northern wall. A few crates have been broken open, yet appear to be empty.
114104:
A large stone fireplace with a roaring fire warms the room.
A small oaken table has been set here.
On the table, there are two pots of mashed elf.
A mountain mule (ulo) is standing here.
A hungry warg stands here, sniffing around for flesh.
A tall Uruk paces about, issuing commands to his troops.
A Morgundul orc snarls about here, looking for a fight.
A Morgundul orc snarls about here, looking for a fight.
A Morgundul orc snarls about here, looking for a fight.

Piles of dirty pots and kettles are stacked dangerously high on the corner counter of the kitchen. A tub with dirty water filled with more dirty pots sits alongside another pile of poorly cleaned plates. A large hearth stands to the south with a stew-filled kettle boiling underneath the fire. Various cooking instruments and foodstuffs are placed strategically on the kitchen tables. Hanging off a nail on one of the tables is a pail, half-full with trash.
114105: Three rickety tables and matching benches fill the mess hall. The tables are quite different in colour, as much from food stains of the past as from strongly decayed pieces of food that stick between the wooden boards. Empty pots of stew lie cluttered on the ground, a few of them accompanied with some stale content. The aroma of strong liquor dominates the hall and absorbs all other scents.
114106: Short blades of grass that grow in the training yard are covered with dried out blood, giving the grass a reddish brown colour. Most of the grass has been trampled, the footprints of armoured feet clearly visible. Wooden bunkers have been erected on the eastern and western side, whilst the smell of warm food comes from the north. The training yard continues to the south.
114107:
A wooden chest stands in the corner.
A sturdy target for arrows, made out of thatch, stands here.

A great deal of broken weapons lie abandoned against the wall of the warg pens, that lie to the west. The smell of sweat pervades the training yard. Many different contraptions are scattered in the yard, such as straw puppets, some which are beheaded and no longer resemble a humanoid form at all. The training yard continues to the north.
114108: Many beds have been stacked on top of each other, and together with some wooden ladders form a few dozen bunkbeds. The beds are made of straw, a woolen blanket can be found on a few beds. Some of the blankets are badly torn, and have some blood on them. A few chamber pots stand next to the beds, most of them empty. To the south, more bunkbeds can be seen.
114109: Many beds have been stacked on top of each other, forming bunkbeds. Wooden ladders have been put against them, to allow easy climbing onto them. The beds themselves are made of a light coloured wood, with brown straw upon it. One bunkbed in particular catches the eye, as one of its beds is broken, having been cracked in half in the middle. The south bears many more bunkbeds.
114110:
The corpse of a slender orkish archer is lying here.
The corpse of a slender orkish archer is lying here.
A cruel orkish captain is sleeping here.
A harsh orkish veteran is sleeping here.
A harsh orkish veteran is sleeping here.

A few crates have been positioned in the centre of the sleeping quarters, surrounded by many bunkbeds. The crates are mostly nailed down, save for some. The walls of the hut are made of dark wood, filthied somehow, as the wood is deeply discoloured in various places. More bunkbeds lie to the north.
114111:
A sturdy peg for hanging armour from is on the wall.
On the peg, there is a saddlecloth.
