A hungry warg stands here, sniffing around for flesh.
A hungry warg stands here, sniffing around for flesh.

A pile of bones of varying sizes rests against the southern wall. Pieces of bone also litter the area, from mere chips to being chewed in half. Manure has been assembled near the gate of the pen to the east, the odour of it permeating the air. Fresh excrements lie scattered around, large enough to be easily avoided.
114112: A great deal of straw-filled bunkbeds are strategically placed in the hut, most less than three feet apart. One bed against the eastern wall is covered in blood, although it has mostly dried up already. A small window has been placed in the western wall of this hut, thick bars visible on the other side. The sleeping quarters continue to the north.
114113:
An orc-guard of the Morgundul is on patrol here.
A tall Uruk paces about, issuing commands to his troops.
A Morgundul orc snarls about here, looking for a fight.

Thick logs, sharp and formed like cylinders at the edges, are tied together with thick brown vines and form a palisade to the south. A latched wooden gate is visible, laden with knife- and axe-sized cuts. The ground is hard brown dirt, with a strong odour rising from a few darker spots. A bucket stands in the northeastern corner, filled with a pile of animal bones, stripped entirely of their meat. A rickety wooden ladder stands against the northern wall, leading upwards through a small trapdoor.
114114:
A Morgundul orc snarls about here, looking for a fight.
A Morgundul orc snarls about here, looking for a fight.
A bald orc is standing here, silent and focused.
A muscular Morgundul outpost commander stands here.

This small hut bears more comfort than the rest of the camp, as it is furnished with a large rug on the floor, a few chairs, and a large desk. A few meatless bones and an empty pot of stew are on a tray on the desk. A great tapestry adorns the eastern wall, depicting a battlefield. A latched door is visible to the north.
114115:
A slender orc scans the area, his bow ready for a sudden strike.
A slender orc scans the area, his bow ready for a sudden strike.

Small cracks litter the boards that form this makeshift watchtower. The view outside is partly blocked by a thick bush, although also hiding the tower from view. A few vines penetrate the wooden structure, coiling on the floor. Through a small trapdoor in the northern corner, a ladder protrudes through, the only logical exit down.
114116: A small path leads from the western wall to a wooden door to the south. There is very little room to manoeuvre, as the huts that lie to the west were built quite closely against the eastern palisade. A few small bones lie below, a layer of dust and earth upon them. An abandoned pot, smelling faintly of stew, lies against the wooden wall of the western hut.
114118: A few oak trees scattered around the field, present the only protection against the weather elements. A small number of them are diseased however, their leaves and branches withering slowly. The soil around the trees is cracked and dry, which has only allowed the most persistent weeds to grow.
114119: Long tufts of grass cover the soil, hiding the many sharp rocks that lie scattered around. In a few places, the earth is dry, cracked and nearly devoid of vegetation. Small plants with razor-sharp thorns grow out of many of the cracks, yet most of them have already withered completely, having become nothing more than brown husks.
114120: Many small holes can be found in these plains, most half hidden by tall green grasses. The holes are countered by mounds of dirt, a few thorny bushes growing on them. A round patch of grass lies to the south, no longer green but a greyish black. Beyond the grassy patch, a tree stump can be spotted.
114122: A few pine trees grow in the middle of this field, clouding the undergrowth in an array of green needles. Thick scratch marks are clearly noticeable on some of the trees, belonging to a creature with big claws. Eastwards, the earth slowly slopes upwards in a twisting manner, making it too difficult to ascend. To the west, the descent is rather brusque.
114123: A colony of red ants is here. The ants seem to ignore you.

This large grassy field is quite elevated from the lands to the north and the west, giving travellers a splendid view. The flora present greatly varies from tall, rustling grasses to a myriad of different plants and flowers. A large anthill lies near the earthen wall to the east, bustling with activity.
114124:
A brown snake watches you.
A brown snake watches you.

Many rocks, both large and small but equally sharp, lie to the west, the result of a rockslide. Close by, a dried up pond can be seen here, only having undrinkable dregs of muddy water remaining. At the bottom of the valley, the only way out is upwards, moving along the rocks and ridges. It looks like someone has been here, there are traces that the mud in the bottom has been moved.
114125: Upon this ledge, located almost at the top of the valley, it is possible to have an amazing view of the valley below. Many small rocks stick out of the western ledge, enclosed by the ridge as it continues upwards to the west in a smooth unclimbable overhang. Small tufts of grass grow everywhere, some of them grazed by animal, hinting of recent life visiting this ledge.
114126:
A large bat is sleeping here.
A large bat is sleeping here.
A large bat is sleeping here.
A bloodthirsty bat is sleeping here.
A fierce bat is here, lusting for your blood (hidden).
A fierce bat is here, lusting for your blood.

This cave is about forty feet high at the entrance to the east, while the ceiling is lower to the north and west. A colony of bats cling to the cave's roof, while on the floor thick piles of guano teem with cockroaches and worms. The air is quite humid inside the cave, and there is a strong smell of guano and other things.
114127:
A fierce bat is here, lusting for your blood.
A fierce bat is here, lusting for your blood.
A fierce bat is here, lusting for your blood.
A fierce bat is here, lusting for your blood.

A multitude of moon-pale stalagmites stand in this cave. In between the stalagmites there are animal furs and piles of straw and leaves humped together on the floor. There is enough space for very big creatures to stand here easily and to lie down on the soft piles of furs and vegetation.
114128:
A fierce bat is here, lusting for your blood.
A fierce bat is here, lusting for your blood.
A huge stone giant is here, glaring at you.
A fierce bat is here, lusting for your blood.
A fierce bat is here, lusting for your blood.
A fierce bat is here, lusting for your blood.
A fierce bat is here, lusting for your blood.
A huge stone giant is here, glaring at you.

The cave is about thirty feet high here, and there are a lot of rocks and boulders in between moon-pale stalagmites on the floor. The smell is very strong here. There are carcasses of animals and of unrecognisable creatures on the floor. On the back of the cave, there are a lot of bones piled up in a huge mound.
114130: The ground is highly uneven, resembling many small paths that twist and turn with every footstep. Small tufts of grass and low shrubs of heather populate the field, although thick bushes can be seen growing in a few places. Upon a small mound, a cluster of blue flowers thrives. The earth in the centre of the field bears a few cracks, most over a feet wide. A thick, twisted root protrudes from one of the cracks, although there is no tree to whom it could belong to in sight.
114131: A sprawling green bush of stinging nettle grows here.

The area is heavily divided. The southern part is covered with black earth, from which many small saplings grow. The total opposite can be found to the north, where the vegetation is quite thick, with a bed of flowers and weeds, surrounding a small patch of bushes and fir trees. A small mound devoid of vegetation bears a small hole, the home of a small animal.
114132: A once robust tree grove has turned into a bleak field, due to a fire long past. No leaves remain on the trees, which vary in colours; some are white as ash, others charred black, and many are in between. The scorched earth is mostly barren, although a few tufts of grass remain, they bear no green lushness. The earth slopes steeply upwards to the south and the east, barring the way.
114133: Patches of scorched grass are followed by layers of grey and white ash, rendering the area quite desolate. A few bushes that grew lush in the past, now have become grey-coloured, leafless branches. A giant fir tree that stood in the centre of the field upon a small hill, has burnt down almost completely, leaving only half a trunk, its sharp edges pointing upwards.
114134: A few scorched birch trees stand their ground, surrounded by solid black, charred grass. The entire field is coloured bleak; black, grey, and earth-brown predominate. Thick weeds, resistant to fire, grow closely together on a small slope to the north. On the western side, upon a small rise, a few green buds have begun to sprout amidst the burnt ground, indicating that the fire that swept through this area is not all that recent.
114135: A small pile of half-eaten bones bare of flesh lies against the southern wall of this burrow. In the pile, faeces and pieces of fur can be found. Dark and light green moss lies all over the floor, serving as a soft mattress for the inhabitants of the cave. Small bits of wet earth are found near the exit of the burrow to the east, in which the pawprints of a bear-like creature lie.
114136:
A nest is here.
A cute young hawk is sitting here waiting for his mother to feed him.
A cute young hawk is sitting here waiting for his mother to feed him.

The rise in the grassy plains is still rather moderate compared to the flat field to the east, but many yards below the trail that passes by the west and east. The heather that grows here is very sparse and rough. A single tree grows here, and there is a bird's nest on a branch.
114137: Compared to the open plains to the west, that stretch all the way to the great Anduin river in the far distance, the surroundings quickly get gloomier in the forest. Because of the compact darkness, it is impossible to tell how far the forest continues to the southeast. A dense patch of briars can be seen growing in the north that forms a nearly impenetrable wall.
114138: Dark undergrowth of a brush-like kind covers the ground, actually making the underlying soil impossible to see. Towards the south, the undergrowth gradually reaches taller, to the point where it is no longer best described as undergrowth. The dark forest seems impassable to other direction except to the south.
114139: A tangled creeper writhes its shoots between the forest's roots upwards.

The trees have become dense and dark enough that the surroundings feel eerily dangerous. This marks the beginning of the great forest that reaches further to the east than the eye can see. The forest to the northwest is sparser and it might be a good direction to head out of here. The ground still holds some signs of a field but gradually becomes more covered with roots.
114140:
Massive roots shift uneasily all around you.
A green-skinned hill troll is pacing around with a nervous zeal.

Massive roots rupture through the ground, offering many opportunities for a traveller to fall and break their legs. They twist their way around each other entangling and turning into the undergrowth-covered earth. Black trees grow about the area, heavily covered with mosses, lichen, fungi, and fallen leaves.
114141:
A green-skinned hill troll is pacing around with a nervous zeal.
A green-skinned hill troll is pacing around with a nervous zeal.

The vegetation in the area is extremely thick and dark. There is no obvious way out of the dark forest clearing stretching out to the southeast. The forest here is much deeper than that of its surroundings, almost as if it were a pit, and is almost enclosed in a wall-like structure of sheer boulders, gnarled roots, and prickly bushes. The ground is moist and gives off a rotting smell from the putrid undergrowth that is covered with various species of fungus.
114142:
A black raven flies in the sky searching for flesh to prey upon.
A green-skinned hill troll is pacing around with a nervous zeal.

Cuts from different kinds of weapons on some of the gnarled tree trunks tell the story of a skirmish that took place under the canopy here. Some splintered arrows can be found on the ground in the dim lighting. Travelling west is made impossible by a row of massive boulders, but with some time it should be possible to get out through some prickly thorn bushes to the south.
114143:
A green-skinned hill troll is pacing around with a nervous zeal.
A massive hill troll is here, sniffing the air for the scent of enemies.
A black raven flies in the sky searching for flesh to prey upon.
A green-skinned hill troll is pacing around with a nervous zeal.
A green-skinned hill troll is pacing around with a nervous zeal.

The murky, vegetation takes many shapes as it rises upwards from the moss- covered, wet forest ground. The undergrowth rises a yard above the moss, consisting nearly entirely of black ferns whose stems containing only the slightest hint of visible green chlorophyll. Above everything else, the enormous trees of Mirkwood Forest rise with their twisted trunks reaching upwards and never letting any sunshine through.
114144:
A large toadstool grows nearby.
A small mushroom grows nearby.
A giant, strange looking green fungus is here, ready to devour you in seconds.
A huge black fungus is here, exuding a foul stench.

Several decaying animal corpses are here providing nutrition to the blackened lichen and dark mushrooms that cover the forest floor. It doesn't seem possible to travel through the trees to the southeast but going north seems feasible. Grasses grow among the gnarled roots that cover the forest floor.
114145: The trees here seem to feed off of the darkness because they grow impossibly higher with very little light. The vegetation is so dense that even someone accustomed to seeing in the dark would have difficulties judging the distance between trees. Filling in the space between the tree trunks to the north are some high bushes. The northern dark brush seems possible to push aside, but coming back may be more difficult.
114146: This part of the forest holds trees higher than the surrounding areas, as if they refused to bow down to the great darkness being exuded far away to the southeast. Combined with the denseness of the trees to the north, their height gives the impression of a wall reaching all the way up to the sky.
114147:
A green-skinned hill troll is pacing around with a nervous zeal.
A massive hill troll is here, sniffing the air for the scent of enemies.

Mirkwood Forest grows very dense here, creating darkness as its canopy blocks all light, even though it is the edge of the forest. Just a few yards from the western cliff wall, where the forest ends, the trees get so numerous that going any further to the east seems impossible. To the north and south the forest continues. The ground starts sloping downwards to the west, just after the last row of trees, down a steep cliff.
114148: Monstrous fir trees loom here, their prickly branches swaying softly against one another. This in turn causes many black needles to fall down, forming a pitch-black undergrowth. Some of the branches have lost most of their needles already, showing only withered, rotten branches. The forest recedes somehow to the south and to the west, where a small path can be seen.
114149: The ground slopes heavily to the west where a steep, tree-covered slope leads down to a trail. The dark forest here is very dense and its gnarled trees rise up high, blocking nearly all light with a canopy of interwoven branches. The forest ground is covered with dark lichen, ferns, and roots that grow among the many boulders that cover the ground.
114150: A green-skinned hill troll is pacing around with a nervous zeal.

Black wood can be spotted all around, as many dark fir trees have taken root here. Thick roots cover most of the undergrowth, seeking to drain as much nutrition as possible. Thick, withered branches block whatever light might shine from above, which adds to the already gloomy atmosphere.
114151: Thick, dark fir trees grow densely together, their many branches intent on stealing most sunlight from the scarce vegetation below them. Many gnarled roots protrude from the trees, blocking an easy path through the trees. A multitude of fir needles lie scattered on the damp ground, colouring the undergrowth mostly pitch-black.
114152: Balancing oneself on a few thick, sturdy branches, it is possible to stand upright on the crown of the tree. Its branches are marked with odd cracks, that seem unrelated to weight issues, yet as if something was attacking the tree from inside. A couple of branches grow almost horizontally, yet only southwards do they meet another tree branch.
114153: Upon several thick branches, that have entangled themselves into a platform, it is possible to see quite far. However, large crowns of the surrounding trees block most of the sight, limiting the view. A few branches slowly spiral upwards, higher up in the tree. Crimson-coloured specks dot most of the branches, the same colour as the leaves growing on the tree.
114154: On Top of a Huge Crown
A slender orc scans the area, his bow ready for a sudden strike.

From the highest point of the tree, a magnificent sight can be beheld as you can spot the forest around, thousands of tree tops covering the view below. Several branches here have been cut, a blood-like substance appears to have dried up, having dripped to a branch below. Close by, some actual dried up blood is seen, a large blot covering the grey wood.
114155: Massive Tree near the Edge of Mirkwood
A massive tree grows here stretching through the foliage.

There is a massive tree growing here at the edge of Mirkwood. Movement is hampered here due to the massive roots encircling the trunk. However, there are lots of strong branches, giving relatively easy passage up into the tree. There is no way to continue straight to the east or to the north from here.
114157: Bubbling grey pools of mud encircle a few thick, black trees. Thick vines surround the trees, coiling around them and ever growing upwards. Only a small amount of vegetation grows near the muddy pool, most of it being shrivelled. The corpse of a small creature lies in one of the pools, reeking heavily.
114158: The sky above is mostly blocked by dark fir trees, their withered branches adorned with sharp, black needles. A small, nearly dried out pond can be found here, partly hidden by the vegetation that is determined to survive. A few gnarled roots have planted themselves in the pond.
114159: A green-skinned hill troll is pacing around with a nervous zeal.

The surrounding forest gives way to a small copse of red-brown fir trees. The once smooth bark is now covered with deep lacerations and rotting holes that have caused most of the needles to abandon the decaying limbs and fall to the matted forest floor below.
114160: A thick, all-consuming mist moves between the bases of the trees, obscuring the ground in an ominous haze. Occasionally the mist rises and falls, as if it is breathing on its own accord. Rotten stumps protrude upwards from the milky mist, their bark tattered and torn. Thick strands of spider silk prevent the dead bark from falling to the ground, enveloping the stump in a crown of bark and small, half-eaten animal corpses.
114161: A green-skinned hill troll is pacing around with a nervous zeal.

Large dark oak trees have interwoven with various beeches in their decrepit growth. The trees hold the same dark complexion as the surrounding forest. The limbs thrust upwards into a darkened sky and intermingle into a thick, choking blanket that suffocates all light attempting to break through.
114162: A silky, spidery web is here, spun into a spiralling wheel-shape.

Vast trees grow together in tight clusters here. Their trunks are covered with a putrid-smelling ooze that the trees themselves seem to be excreting. Spindly spider silk hangs from the nearby branches and slowly moves towards any warmth that comes near it. A great wall of toppled trees, interwoven with thick, thorny vines prevents travel towards the north.
114163: Enormous beech trees thrust upward from the matted forest floor. A thick layer of webbing has wound its way around the pasty-coloured trunks, restricting the growth of the limbs and forcing them into gnarled, twisted masses through which fingers of thin, rope-like ivy grow. Toward the east lies the source of the ensnaring ivy, which has coiled and roped itself into an all-consuming mass, making travel in that direction impossible.
114164: Large, dark trees close in about a fallen corner of this gloomy forest. Towards the north and west, a large wall of toppled trees lies in a great pile; a thick tangle of branches and limbs intertwined with dense, ghostly-white cobwebs creates an impassable barricade in those directions. A heavy layer of rotten humus crunches loudly underfoot, and moves slightly when trodden upon.
114165: Once massive dark trees of mixed variety grew here in great masses, blotting out the skies above with their twisted canopies and enormous limbs. Now all that remains are the rotting boughs and stumps that scatter the landscape, making travel cumbersome in the least. Snaking arms of ivy, armoured with large, razor-sharp tines grow across the forest floor in a knotted blanket, inviting death to whomever might linger here long enough to become ensnared.
114166:
A green-skinned hill troll is pacing around with a nervous zeal.
A massive hill troll is here, sniffing the air for the scent of enemies.
Some black, oozing vines reach out from the choked canopy towards you.
A black raven flies in the sky searching for flesh to prey upon.
A black raven flies in the sky searching for flesh to prey upon.

The trees are of mixed kinds and have dropped many darkened branches on the ground, that make a silent passing very difficult. The ground holds some moss-covered rocks and there seems to be no end to the forest around here.
114169: A deep chasm entrance, nearly covered by several huge boulders, splits the northwest ridge that lines the valley as it bends towards the east. The valley pass is surrounded by two crags that have eroded, revealing their sedimentary layers to the open air. On the ground of the pass grows a deep thicket of grass and shrubs among the limestone rocks that increase in density near the cliffs.
114170: The dark, twisting chasm widens into a shallow hole littered with dry branches and shattered bones. The stench of rotting meat clings to the air as it becomes increasingly apparent that some animal has made this space its den. Rubble and layers of crumbling stone litter the ground that make the chasm difficult to navigate as it continues to the west among many fallen boulders.
114171:
A rotten corpse is hanging here.
A huge black bear, saliva frothing from its jaws, bellows a challenge.

Shadows drape from the dark, overhanging precipices into a deep chasm that twists and turns its way through the entombing rock on either side. A tangled heap of rotten rope lies to the northwest within the rubble of a landslide that closed off the passage. The sky barely breaks through the jagged crags up above where another rope can be seen stretching across the chasm to the other side.
114172: An old rope spans the divide of a great chasm, allowing passage to a strangely shaped rock formation that towers in the north. The taut rope sways gently as weight is placed upon its long length that dips into the dark chasm below. The twisting chasm seems to curve around the rock formation from the southeast, making the weathered, yet sturdy, rope the only possible way there and back.
114174: A small green mound rises from the ground.

A strangely-shaped tower of hardened sandstone climbs upwards into three steep peaks. The tower of rock is surrounded by a deep chasm and the only way off of it is to the south. A boulder in the south has been coiled with loops of rope whose ends then extend across the chasm. Hidden in between the sandstone spires grows a small sanctuary of grasses, blossoms, and bushes in the shade.
114175: A large marmot is here, scurrying in between the rocks.

Balancing on the verge of a plateau, this field offers a great view of the lands below. The northern slope is too steep to take a mount down, and the climb does indead seem safe only for a skilled climber. The ground is covered with short grass of a darker kind that continues into the plains to the south.
114176: This grassy plain is the last field before entering the huge and dark forest of Mirkwood that stands to the southeast. From here, it is impossible to tell how far the forest stretches, or if it even has an end at all. The ground slopes slightly to the north where a few flowers grow together. To the west and north, the landscape consists of grassy fields that cover the plateau.
114177:
There is a huge, pyramidal beehive here.
A three-foot-long queen bee is here, buzzing agitatedly.
A drone bee flies around here, angrily buzzing.
A bee flies around here, collecting nectar from the flowers.
A bee flies around here, collecting nectar from the flowers.
A bee flies around here, collecting nectar from the flowers.

A valley with a curving trail runs to the west far below the cliff. To the east, the forest of Mirkwood rises high and mighty. On this field, however, there are only a couple of smaller trees that grow without a direct connection to the forest. The stands of lonesome trees grow among the flowers and bushes that mark the landscape. A loud humming noise comes from the stand of trees.
114178: High above the valley, this field has had little protection from the erosion of wind and rain. In the north-western corner, little but loose earth is left, while further from the edge of the plateau some grass has managed to grow a few inches above the ground. The weeds dig their roots into the sparse soil, clinging dearly to whatever nutrients still remain in the wind-blown area.
114179:
A sturdy billy goat stands here, proudly protecting his goats.
A goat is here, grazing in the hills.
A young goat playfully charges and hops away.

The most obvious thing of this flat plateau, is the difference in height compared to the thick forest less than a mile to the northwest. Between the two different areas, however, lies a deep fault with sides so vertical that climbing down it simply is not an option. A path leads across the valley to the south opposite a distance trail to the east that might lead past this fault.
114180: Most notable on the grassy field, are the signs of big boulders that rest in the west on a spot with no grass. The soil there seems to be packed very hard, as if the soil was of poorer quality. From the edge of the ridge, a clear view over the trail is accessible.
114181: There are some smaller fields following the stretching valley to the east. The plains to the west, however, cannot be reached because of some very thick brush. Directly to below, another field can be seen lying next to the trail. A better view of that area can probably be seen from the next field over.
114185:
An easterling veteran dressed in light garments stands sentinel here.
An easterling veteran dressed in light garments stands sentinel here.
An easterling veteran dressed in light garments stands sentinel here.

A large, wooden barricade, which reaches the height of a man, has been constructed on the western side of the cavern. Below it, in a thick layer of dark mud, rocks and garbage litter a spur of water leading to the eastern hall. The worn look of the western hall has given way to smooth walls and a high ceiling. The exception is the southern wall, which has been reinforced.
114186: The dark mud from the west has thinned slightly as the water spurs lead into a small, rune-covered culvert in the eastern wall. Several crumbling pillars rise up, touching the ceiling, as they support the hall from collapsing. The aged limestone has held up very well to time, but even such excellent craftsmanship has its limits, and cracks are beginning to form from the stress of the ages. The original wall to the south has crumbled, but it has been rebuilt more recently.
114187: This section of the ancient, limestone hall has held up exceptionally well through time, except for the partly crumbled wall to the north. Faint remains of elven runes line the pillars and walls with intricate detail, but have been viciously scrawled out. A large statue stands to the west, its missing head has been replaced by a giant, rusty, iron eye.
114188:
A jet-black raven caws from its perch with inquisitive eyes.
A jet-black raven caws from its perch with inquisitive eyes.

The enormous pillars in this room hint at the former grandeur of the main hall before everything was plundered and fell into decay. Shadows drape from the ragged scars where banners hung and ornate awnings laid. A dim light shines among the filth and rubble from behind a large, matted curtain to the south.
114189: Filth and matted straw covers the ground of this dimly lit room in an effort to contain the foul, pasty-white substance that clings to everything. Small chirps echo across the giant hall, while the walls slowly rise up to a smaller natural cavern above. A slight breeze rushes down along the moist fir and oak platform that rises up to the small mossy cavern to the upper east.
114190: A jet-black raven caws from its perch with inquisitive eyes.

Several huge murals tell the tale of this broken armoury, which has been hideously devastated. Only a couple of frames remain; these show the forging of a crystal vial that pierces the darkness. Several coffers lie here which have been cracked open and emptied, leaving only shadows among the cobwebs and rust.
114191:
A rosewood chest with runic markings stands in a corner.
There is a lever next to the southern door.
A small oaken table has been set here.
On the table, there are a bulb of garlic and a candle.
A jet-black raven caws from its perch with inquisitive eyes.
A jet-black raven caws from its perch with inquisitive eyes.
A man clad in red robes mutters in a foreign tongue ( glowing ).

The hewn walls of limestone bedrock bear the rough scars of pickaxe blows, which increase in prominence towards the southern end of the room. A matted drapery encloses the smoke-filled area where a table etched with runes has been placed in the centre. The pungent scent of herbs and incense fills the air. A lit candle creates an eerie mood to the room.
114193: Planks surround the walls of this dark cave. A crude, wooden staircase made of fir and rope rises up to a hatch that is connected to the eastern wall. Nailed into the muddy, wooden floor in the middle of the room is a dark, iron cover, from which rushing water can be heard. The western wall is blocked by a sturdy door, while the northern passage leads onward into the darkness.
114194: An immense cave rises up into the pitch-black darkness above, where menacing stalactites hang from the ceiling. The western cave wall arches up to a steep, unclimbable ledge where a rusty iron grate has been fitted into the stone. The floor is covered with pickaxe-hewn rubble that seems to have been expelled from the grate above. The eastern floor of the cavern is covered with stalagmites.
114199:
Some delicious wild strawberries grow on the ground.
A beautiful and docile horse is standing here.

Sloping downwards into a deep dip in the plains, the ground is probably the bottom of an old lake. However it is not soggier than an ordinary meadow and thus travelling across it could be done without sinking. Some bear droppings can be made out along the western edge of the dip.
114200:
A bear cub is here, looking around for something to play with.
A tawny-coated bear is snuffling about.

The den looks fairly comfortable as it has been lined with leaves and grasses. Outside the den grows a large amount of dense vegetation that hides the entrance while still allowing some sunlight to enter. The walls of the den are made of dirt, stone, and roots. A large boulder can be seen to the south.
114201: Field with a Stand of Ash Trees

A blanket of dark greyish undergrowth covers the ground. Some more of the same undergrowth grows beneath the ash trees slightly taller and straighter, like in many other places in the northern lands. The gloomy vegetation continues in the same fashion to the west, while the plains become rockier in the north.
114202: Field Ending in a Long Stone Row

The grassy plains, stretching miles wide to the southwest, end as a corner to the northeast. The brush has also grown too thick to pass through to the north. Travelling to the east has been made impossible by a long and high stone row; however, looking through it, a deep valley running north-south can be seen.
114203:
A huge grizzly bear is here, roaming the wild.
A grizzly cub is here, snarling loudly.
A grizzly cub is here, snarling loudly.

While overlooking the north-south trail that is to the east, an adventurer would not be visible from down below. This field is part of the expansive plains that continue for many miles to the north, south and west. A few dark bushes are growing close to the brink of the escarpment to the east.
114205: The sides of a hill are sloping so heavily that riding is impossible and while there is some grass on the ground, it offers little opportunities for a good footing. Going south seems impossible, as the slope becomes nearly vertical.
114207: Field Drained by a Dark Ditch
A moderately-sized copperhead snake is here.

Black water flows down a narrow but deep ditch a couple of yards below, leaving patches of dark mud on its sides. Some bushes to the east happily drink from the murky water without any problems. Next to the stream the ground is slightly damp, but closer to the plateau to the west, the ground is completely dry.
114208: After a heavy slope, the field ends in a kind of hill among the plains. The lack of protective trees has left the ground vulnerable to the wind and small but predominantly hardy grasses have grown here because of it. To the south the high plain is on level ground, but to the east the ground slopes heavily.
114209: The ground has dried out and is showing cracks in many places while it slopes down to the east. Because of the dryness of the earth few plants survive here, leaving the landscape with a very barren impression. To the north, a little more grass is growing and in the distant east significantly more. The dark brush and vegetation can be distinguished easily, standing out in the plains.
114210: A tiny spider is here, eating a tiny bug.

Webs cover this small tunnel as it disappears into the darkness to the west. Hundreds of tiny insects have been entombed into the sides of the tunnel within small cocoons. The passage's top seems to stop at a thick, webbed cover that must have been made by some enormous spider due to its immense size.
114211: A newborn spider is here, hungrily crawling about.

Sticky silk webs hang from the ceiling creating a sticky, milk-white curtain in the tunnel. The passage bends towards the north from the east where the tunnel rises slightly. Webs cover the sides of the muddy tunnel which are filled with the cocoons and corpses of small mammals.
114212:
A newborn spider is here.
A black spider crawls here, a shiny red spot visible on its belly.
A black spider crawls here, a shiny red spot visible on its belly.

Thick, white webs cover the edges of the cavern and hang from the ceiling like curtains of intricately-threaded gossamer strands. The bottom of the cave is covered with mud, webbing, and a few discarded corpses which are completely drained of fluid. A few chittering noises can be heard from the western wall.
114213:
A skeleton of some humanoid lies in the dust.
A silky, spidery web is here, spun into a spiralling wheel-shape.
A huge, poisonous tarantula extends her legs to you.
A newborn spider is here.
A newborn spider is here.
A newborn spider is here.
A newborn spider is here.
A newborn spider is here.
A newborn spider is here.
A newborn spider is here.

Hung in the corner of the cavern by thin, gossamer strands of silk is a thick, white spider's nest. Countless bones and sucked-dry corpses litter the ground in various states of decay. Several smaller passages, too small to enter, lead in all directions where the movements of tiny arachnids' feet can be heard.
114215: A slobbering giant greedily lumbers towards you.

For this part of Middle-earth, the bushes and plants of the meadow almost give the impression of a garden. Further to the south, however, the nicely ordered grasses and bushes become sparser and the grass gradually turns into a greyish colour as it starts to shrink in size.
114216:
A grey wolf is here, snarling aggressively.
A large brown wolf stands here, its teeth partly bared.

Thin grass, not growing higher than an inch, of a pale grey colour makes the sloping ground look almost like a worn road paved with cobblestone. The slope in these craggy plains is very mild, but some abandoned fields can be seen above to the west with little difficulty.
114217: The grassy field appears empty and devoid of all creatures, leaving vegetation to grow freely and unabated. Perhaps it was some predator roaming the area, scaring away less ferocious animals and finally, without any prey left, moving on to hunt at other venues, such as the surrounding plains.
114218:
A waist-high evergreen shrub grows here, with thick, reaching branches.
On the shrub, there are two piles of grey-green leaves.

Thick brush makes movement considerably harder and the vegetation grows so high to the north and east that it is not even possible to continue in those directions. Instead, a field with notable bushes to the west and the extension of the brushland to the south are the only options for a traveller.
114219: Dark brush carpets the ground with shrubs and bushes, leaving little ground for unhindered movement. Tracks of some of the animals in the area have become obvious since the high vegetation has been trampled. In the north the brush becomes larger, while in the west there are some ash trees visible in the distance.
114220: The field slopes down heavily towards a brink on the far eastern end of the plain where a trail can be seen many fathoms below. The ground is steadily covered with grasses and low-growing vegetation. Luckily, there is no real risk of falling over and rolling off the edge of the cliff.
114223: As if constantly being fried by the sun, the vegetation on the field is faded and the ground is very dry. Distinct cracks on the ground show where any rain water quickly would drain away. To the south, the ground slopes upwards until some miles in the distance a small hill top can be sighted.
114224:
A placid pond is here, inviting you to take a refreshing drink.
A catfish is standing here.
A snowy-white egret stands here alertly.
A heron is stalking the area, looking for fish.

Lemon grass and other kinds of grasses that flourish in the very damp soil, encircle the small pond in the plains. Plentiful bird droppings on the ground leave a greeting from the many birds that come here and the surrounding plains continue in all directons.
114225: Low brush covers most of the area, giving protection for a variety of insects and smaller animals. In the middle, however, the ground has lower vegetation in a circular area, as if a long lost building once stood there. Plains stretch out in all directions, with the southern ones sloping up in a steep fashion.
114231: A thin, hairy plant, with small, oval leaves, grows here.

From the highest point among the fields, nothing but more grassy plains can be seen stretching in the horizon to the northeast. A little trail runs from the north to the south, far below to the east, but from here it is impossible to tell whether someone is travelling along it. Since there are no trees in the area, laying down here in the grass would be perfect for studying the sky.
114232: The grass-covered ground slopes upwards to the west, leading to the highest point in the area. To the south, however, easy travelling is made impossible when the field ends above an escarpment. Following the field past its northern end leads downward to a wide sea of high grasses.
114240:
A mottled snake is sneaking here, ready to sink its fangs into flesh.
A mottled snake is sneaking here, ready to sink its fangs into flesh.
A diamond-back rattlesnake is coiled here, ready to strike.
An ancient fungus smothers the boulders.
An ancient fungus smothers the boulders.
A huge black fungus is here, exuding a foul stench.
A huge black fungus is here, exuding a foul stench.
A giant, strange looking green fungus is here, ready to devour you in seconds.

Sturdily built and spacious, this cellar was built by someone who knew what they were doing, and wanted ample storage space. The ceiling and floor are of thick wooden boards, while the walls are of hard-packed dirt. In some places, a testimony to its age and state of decay, piles of dirt and small rocks litter the cellar's floor. The ruins of shelves and a table also lie on the floor.
114244:
An elaborate red flower sits within a dark mass of briars.
A tangled creeper writhes its shoots between the forest's roots upwards.

The surroundings are dark and the trees numerous here although it is close to the edge of the forest. To the north, the forest is changing into the plains and fields. The grass has turned from green to some sick-looking black colour and the rocks on the ground are completely infested with dark lichen. While the distant valley holding a trail can barely be seen to the west, it is impossible to tell how far the mighty forest stretches to the south and east.
114262:
The wicked undergrowth rustles malevolently, shifting and widening.
A stocky mountain mule is here, waiting to serve.
A mountain mule (ulo) is standing here.

In the dense forest it is impossible to see very far in any direction. The darkness of the trees casts eerie shadows across the root-covered and fern- covered forest floor. It is possible to walk between the trees and follow the mossy undergrowth in all directions but the south, where a significantly larger effort would be needed to push south through some dark, dense bushes.
114273:
Pitch-black water with a strange smell has collected here.
Massive roots shift uneasily all around you.

A monstrous tree has been uprooted, its trunk forming a roof overhead. Beneath the trunk, a myriad of twisting roots twirl about, seeking to snare the life force out of whatever they encounter. Under the tree, the undergrowth is thick with many needled leaves and every here and there a few oak leaves and small, twisted twigs.
114274:
A half-decayed corpse of a goblin lies rotting on the ground.
A shield, blackened by fire, lies on the ground.
A scimitar has been left here.

Great blackened trees with coarse grey bark tower high into the sky above. The thick bark covering the trees has been contorted into odd patterns; some resembling demonic faces, others depicting a horror-filled snapshot of some unsuspecting victim's last living moments. Whatever evil has permeated these woodlands seems bent on making its malice known. A massive uprooting lies to the west where a great tree has fallen, creating an insurmountable thicket of roots and mulch.
114275: The forest has parted a little here, allowing for slightly easier passage through some brush. Scattered among the undergrowth are several skeletons; some have elongated spines attached to large skulls, and others bear the features of humanoids. A half-decomposed arm, with a bony hand still attached, clutches at a rusty pike that lies half-buried in the decaying matter that decomposes on the forest floor.
114276: The forest here grows stunted and black. The limbs have grown out only a short way from the trunks, and have formed into a tangle of twisted branches and twigs. The bark of the surrounding trees is of a deep black-green colour and is covered with dreadful cracks which ooze a strange, smelly liquid. Several gnarled pine trees, intermixed with dark firs, grow densely towards the west, where several of their massive trunks intertwine with the branches of the pines and create an impassable forest wall.
114277: Large, towering oak trees thrust upward from a rotten blanket of fallen foliage. Blood and carnage almost completely cover the lower base of the trees, while small pieces and gobs of flesh are scattered about. The canopy above grows tightly together, casting a deep gloom over the forest floor below whilst trying to strangle any stray ray of light before it reaches the ground. Toward the west a dense, impenetrable mass of writhing roots coalesces around a thick growth of dark fir trees, completely obstructing passage in that direction.
114278: Enormous black oak trees tower high above, before fading into an ominous haze that engulfs the canopy and swallows all form of twig and branch alike. These black sentinels keep silent watch over all who travel below. Thick, dark bark resembles their armour, enormous branches their arms and weapons.
114279: A green-skinned hill troll is pacing around with a nervous zeal.

The trees here grow in thick clusters, reaching upwards together towards the sky above. At various points, the branches have grown together with their neighbours before protruding out into any available space. A dark layer of green moss grows within the nooks and crannies formed by the struggling tree limbs, which now lie motionless as if frozen in time before the victor could be decided.
114280: Some black, oozing vines reach out from the choked canopy towards you.

Great, twisted tree trunks have grown together into a tangled, writhing mass. Large cracks have splintered down the thin, sickly bark, revealing deep oozing wounds. Thin branches sprout out from the base of the trees and have grown into the shape of gnarled claw-like talons, at the ends of which drip a putrid, yellow substance that emits an abhorrent stench.
114281:
Some black, oozing vines reach out from the choked canopy towards you.
The wicked undergrowth rustles malevolently, shifting and widening.

A thick growth of sickly beech trees stands here in silent disarray. A dark evil continues to warp these trees into a twisted mass of pale-barked, spindly-limbed abominations. Through deep cracks in the bark, a thick, oozing sap is secreted, coating the blackened foliage with a sickly film.
114282: A massive hill troll is here, sniffing the air for the scent of enemies.

Here a large number of dank fir trees have grown amongst the vast number of dark oaks. Their limbs are thin and spindly, and are covered with a brownish-red, bubbling fungus that produces a rancid smell. Small, blood-red berries cling to the ends of the branches in small clusters, the surface of each fruit is disfigured by open slits from which slimy spore sacks are excreted.
114283: The trees here are covered in a pale, sickly bark on which grows a thin layer of green mould. From the pallid trunks extend emaciated boughs of crooked, contorted branches from which malformed foliage sprouts. It is as if some evil lives under the rotten ground, and has allowed the roots of the trees to drink in its sickness. Towards the north and south the trees lie in a twisted mass, restricting any movement in those directions. Upon the ground, there is a patch of rotten leaves, amongst which a few small, pale green tufts of grass have grown.
114284: Dead and broken trees lie toppled and rotting, scattered upon the forest floor. The ground is covered with a thick layer of variegated humus. A closer inspection reveals not only decomposing leaves, twigs and branches, but small decaying animal bones and patches of tattered, bloody fur. A malodorous smell rises up from the rot and decay of the forest floor and seems to thicken the surrounding air.
114285:
A very heavy branch is lying here on the ground.
Some roots lie here waiting to ensnare weary travellers.

Towards the east and west grow massive walls of dark beech which loom tall, obscuring the sky in a gloomy haze of dangling spider webs and clustered foliage. The dense forest walls meet towards the south, where a thick hedge of tangled roots and fallen boughs intertwine into an impassable growth of twisted forest. The only chance of escaping this suffocating wood lies to the north, where a carpet of ground-dwelling ivy spreads across the ground in a writhing mass.
114286: Standing tall and wide, this forest is shrouded in malice. A gathering gloom pervades the space between the leaves, branches and even the filth and decay on the forest floor. The trees are covered in a thick armour of black, furrowed bark. To the west, the gloomy forest continues its span into darkness.
114287:
On the ground, there are two rotten corpses.
A tiny spider is here, eating a tiny bug.
A tiny spider is here, eating a tiny bug.
A huge, poisonous tarantula extends her legs to you.
A huge, poisonous tarantula extends her legs to you.

Far above, a thick canopy of tangled leaves and branches intertwines into a mass of leaves and spindly spider silk. Small, decaying corpses that once may have resembled birds or squirrels have been caught in the sticky webbing; some are partially cocooned, while others have simply been left to rot. A thick tangle of thorny brambles grows to the south and west, cutting off any attempt at travel in those directions.
114288: Blackened oak trees loom over the forest floor here, their bark seemingly darkened by the gloom that hangs about. The limbs of the oak trees themselves appear to be twisted in torment as they interweave with each other.
114289: The trees here are dark and menacing as they grow on the uneven ground. There are rises and falls in the ground and the damp foliage on the forest floor grows thicker as the debris collects on the lower elevations.
114290: The ground here starts a steep incline from the west to the east. The dark forest has an eerie gloom to it as it thins toward the east on its approach to a steep cliff. The foliage above is dense enough to block any attempt to discern the sky beyond this forest.
114291:
A brown stag looks around with big, startled eyes.
A brutish forest troll is hunting here, looking for some tasty flesh.
A brutish forest troll is hunting here, looking for some tasty flesh.
A disgusting forest troll is searching for fresh meat here.

Warped thorns and brambles are scattered about here on the forest floor. Dark, broken twigs lie all about the base of the black, twisted trees which grow here. To the west, through the trees can be seen a drop off as the forest gives way to a cliff.
114292: Large roots twist upon the soil before descending deep into the ground.

A deep, forested ravine cuts sharply into the earth and continues to slope downwards towards the east. Various trees grow out from the steep walls of the valley, struggling for purchase as massive roots rear up, before thrusting back deep into the earth. Thin strands of sticky spider webbing hang down from thick branches, waiting to ensnare anything that might get too close. A gathering gloom spreads from the depths, casting ominous shadows everywhere.
114293: A pile of dry, brown leaves lies here.

In all directions the gloomy woods of Mirkwood spread abroad, save to the south where a thick growth of shrubs and ivy interweave into an impassable wall of tangled limbs and thorns. A dreary mist encircles the trees, rising and falling as it creeps across the forest floor. It engulfs every nook and cranny, leaving a thin film of foetid moisture over everything it touches. A reddish-brown layer of moss covers the north face of each tree.
114294:
A sprawling, twisted tree grows here.
On the tree, there are two piles of hawthorn berries.

Under a thick and gloomy canopy of gnarled boughs and branches grow the wide, dark-coloured trunks that support the dreadful ceiling above. Knotting tightly together, there is little room for anything else to take root and grow between these massive boles. Upon the ground lies a thick layer of rotting foliage, where a few small, jagged rocks can be seen thrusting up into the suffocating gloom that lingers heavily between the trees.
114295: To the north and south, the steep walls of this valley loom high above, stopping even the most skilled of climbers from navigating them. The ground is littered with rocks, fallen boughs and boulders. It seems they have lost the battle with gravity and the elements and tumbled down the sides of the valley and now lie broken and scattered. The bones of those that were unable to move fast enough lie strewn about the ground.
114296: Growing large and in close proximity of one another, the surrounding forest makes it hard to navigate. The air between the rough boughs and branches is musty, and settles heavily on anything it lingers upon. Tall and dark, and in massive quantities lie a growth of gnarled beech towards the north. South and eastward however yields a thick wall of fallen trees, their great blackened trunks lying in various piles and directions, and their enormous root systems exposed in hideous, twisted masses making travel between them quite difficult for even the most adapted of woodland travellers.
114297: A brown stag looks around with big, startled eyes.

Here the dark, penetrating gloom of this forest spreads out in all directions. The forest floor is covered in a thick blanket of broken twigs, leaves, and the occasional bone fragment. Massive roots thrust up from the earth in various places, and have slowly intertwined with each other to form a motionless, brooding monument of root and stem.
114298: Dark mushrooms litter the ground here giving a slight iridescent glow as their poisonous spores are expelled into the air. Thick shrubs and ivy interweave to the north, causing a mass of branches which do not allow passage. The tangle of vegetation continues to the west, with the trunks of beech trees joining in the natural wall.
114299: Two enormous trees that once may have resembled the lavish mellyrn of Lothlorien now lie twisted and corrupt. What once were proud, sprawling tree branches, with golden-yellow leaves and bright blooming flowers now hold no such splendour; drooping branches, covered with coarse, knotted bark hang in dead disarray. The once brightly coloured flowers have shrivelled into oozing clusters of small, black efflorescent spore sacks.
114300: Great dark trees thrust upward from the thick layer of rotting humus that blankets the ground. Swaying spider webs hang from the lofty branches above in great veils of ghostly white silk. An oppressive gloom hangs heavy under the twisted tangle of limbs that forms the canopy above.
114301: The trees begin to slouch to the south as the elevation rises. There are thin spider webs crossing the small trees which grow on this slope. Small animal holes litter the ground on this rise, threatening to trip travellers at their every step and sending them onto the sharp limbs and rocks strewn across the forest floor.
114302: The trees grow thinly at the top of this rocky rise, and instead the ground is covered by dense, tangled bushes. The rise overlooks the forest, yet nothing can be seen of the ground below as the foliage blocks all attempts to discern what Mirkwood hides beneath its leafy ceiling. There is a faint, eerie fog swirling across the ground, forming vague shapes then dissipating again, as if made up of dispersed, fading spirits.
114303: The forest here emanates gloom and despair. There is a noxious stink that hangs in the air. To the south can be seen a glimpse of a trail that travels west to east, but it cannot be reached here. To the west, there is a steep rise up to a hilltop that cannot be seen due to the mist and thick trees which grow in this area.
114304: The trees coalesce into a corridor with a narrow opening to the north. The corridor of darkened trees blocks the way to the south. A smelly mist drifts in from the west. The trees begin to thin out, yet hunch over somewhat to the east.
114306: The forest floor is covered in a gloomy mist here which makes it hard to see very far. The ground slopes slightly to the southwest. The trees make a natural wall to the north which makes travel in this direction impossible.
114307: The gloomy forest becomes thin here and in the middle lies a huge blackened stump. Strange looking insects move all about it, giving it an appearance of infestation. A crack is visible at the top of the stump. The forest thickens to the west and east. The trees begin to form a narrow pass going south.
114309: A dank, musty, hollowed out stump is here surrounded by moss and rotting wood. The wood and roots of the stump give way to earthen walls in some places. Fungus covers some of the root-lined walls of this empty stump. To the east, a tunnel can be seen, dug through the hard packed earth and bits of root growing there.
114310:
A small, dense tangle of roots covers the ground.
A deeply black, oddly shaped cloud of mist has gathered here.

Fungi grows everywhere in this festering cave. Sorts and varieties of black and sickly-looking mould and fungi grow in patches across the walls. There are patches of dirt that are covered by slime which seems to have been secreted from the fungi. A lingering, malign aura pollutes the air in the cave as if terrible crimes were committed here and the evil still lingers.
114311: Fire-cracked rock lying in a ruined pattern that resembles what once must have been a hearth, sits collecting moss here. Small trees, interspersed among the trunks of the larger ones, grow in an almost diabolic fashion as they criss-cross to cause a natural fence to the west blocking any passage.
114312: Some roots lie here waiting to ensnare weary travellers.

Roots of all shapes and sizes are sprawled everywhere here. The mass of roots grows so thick that the individual tendrils become hard to focus on and it seems as if they are moving. The roots grow in a manner here so as to make passage impossible in any direction except for west.
114313: Two great trees form a natural arch right before the ground begins to slope sharply downwards to the north, where a misty haze shrouds the depths of the valley in an ominous gloom. Above, where the dank foliage of the surrounding trees looms high overhead, great strands of silky white spider webbing hangs down nearly to the forest floor. Various insects and small animals can be seen wrapped tightly amongst the webs, indicating the eight-legged architects have not yet abandoned these feeding grounds.
114315: The constricting walls of the valley begin to open up as the gully weaves its way north. The light is dull as the gloomy canopy of the great, blackened forest above grows in closer together, shedding a dreary gloom over the valley floor far below. Toward the south, the ground begins to ascend a hazardous slope covered with fallen debris and strewn boulders.
114316: An enormous pile of fallen debris has settled into the narrow gully at the floor of the valley, evidence of past landslides. Small pebbles, followed by larger stones begin to plummet down the steep sides of the valley as the ground begins to shake.
114317: A steep slope in the forest brings the elevation down toward the east. Twisted limbs reach out at head level threatening to scrape the face. The trees here grow in leaning positions so as to compensate for the slope but it causes a bent over, decrepit look to them.
114318:
A large boulder is here, it must be heavy.
Some roots lie here waiting to ensnare weary travellers.

A thick matting of leaves and forest debris lines the ground here allowing many different types of fungi to grow. The black-barked trees loom high overhead giving an ambience of despair. Of the sky above, there is not even a sliver visible from beneath the dark canopy.
114319:
A brutish forest troll is hunting here, looking for some tasty flesh.
A brutish forest troll is hunting here, looking for some tasty flesh.
A disgusting forest troll is searching for fresh meat here.

Twisted thorn bushes and brambles grow all about here. The mass of thorns reaches high, concealing what little light might have been coming from the sky. The roots and vines at the base of the vegetation somehow thrive in this dark, dreary gloom.
114320: Thorny Tangle of Rock and Bramble

Large rocks and rubble are strewn about here. The rubble is thicker to the west and begins to thin out gradually toward the east. Some of the rocks which make up the rubble appear to be new; others are ancient, with moss and roots of all varieties growing about them. Many thorns and brambles are growing here as well, making it impossible to move to the south.
114321: A huge stone troll looms overhead, ready to crush your body.

A tunnel proceeds into the dark to the west, descending rapidly from a crudely-dug hole. The rough ground here was crudely scraped into a serviceable floor and is littered with torn and rotting vegetation. Several sets of large footprints suggest this tunnel is still home to some trolls. A hint of fresh air drifts from the forest above, contrasting with the foul smell of the tunnel's residents.
114322:
An old, strong cave troll is standing here.
An old, strong cave troll is standing here.

A tunnel extends from west to east, nearly eight feet high and widest in the middle where it almost forms a small cavern. Its dark, earthy walls are uneven and look to have been brutishly carved out by giant hands. Broken roots protrude from the ceiling, walls, and even the floor in some places, crudely cleared from the tunnel's path. The ground at the southern edge of the passage is particularly disturbed, where there seems to be another opening.
114323:
An infant troll, baring its teeth, snarls here.
An infant troll, baring its teeth, snarls here.
An infant troll, baring its teeth, snarls here.
The ugly troll mother is roaming the cave, taking care of her loved ones.
A huge stone troll looms overhead, ready to crush your body.

A crude cavern has been carved out of hard, black soil. The cave is at least twenty feet in height and easily three times that in width. The chamber seems to be located under a forest as many roots break through the soil that make up the ceiling. There are signs of inhabitation on the floor, mainly piles of leaves and other vegetation that might serve as simple bedding.
114324: One end of a tunnel abruptly stops here, narrowing and sloping sharply upwards. Rough earthen ledges of packed dirt provide purchase to anyone moving from the tunnel towards the forest floor above. The other end of the passage extends underground to the east, where the humid scent of damp soil almost overwhelms the ever-present trollish odour.
114326: The rough trail underfoot turns southward, skirting a jagged, rocky slope toward the east and continuing deeper into the suffocating darkness between gnarled, corrupted trees. The forest mixes with dense shrubs to the north.
114327: A thin, silky layer of cobwebs lines the inner layer of the canopy as it stoops above the trail which travels in an east and west direction. The trees blot out the sky here forcing a gloom which hangs in the air.
114328: A looming canopy of trees covers the trail on the northern and southern sides here as the murky path continues in a dark, tunnel-like fashion. There is an eerie fog which hangs in the air here, making all noises in this area unsettlingly muffled.
114329: The looming black trees thin just enough to allow a rough trail to wind its way into the gloom in the east and the west. Their contorted trunks and crooked limbs are adorned with thick, black vines bristling with barbed thorns. To the north, these trees press in close, blocking passage in that direction completely. Passage between the trees to the south looks possible, but difficult. The air is malevolently silent and suffocatingly still.
114330: Bend in the Trail of Shadows
Black, thorny vines grow here, smothering the ancient trees.

The trail continues to weave its way east between the twisted, disfigured trees, whose thick, web-encrusted canopy above chokes out even the smallest sliver of sky. Black, wickedly-thorned vines have wound themselves around some of the branches as if in an attempt to smother what perverted life still exists in them.
114331: An oppressive gloom pervades the space between the surrounding walls of the thickening forest that line this trail on all sides, save to the south where the track continues its way through dark, twisting trees. Overhead, the grasping branches come together to form a ceiling of gnarled, twisted limbs. Ghostly-white blankets of silky spider webs hang down from above, nearly touching the ground in some places.
114332: Trees of mixed varieties grow densely here; some thin, spindly fir trees grow amongst other much wider and hardier oak and beech, and the occasional ash tree. The ground is covered in a mottled blanket of orange fir needles and brown oak and beech leaves, all of which are partially coated in unusual spots of black slime that slowly devours anything it touches.
114333:
A harsh orkish veteran is here, heavily scarred but ready to fight.
A harsh orkish veteran is here, heavily scarred but ready to fight.
A harsh orkish veteran is here, heavily scarred but ready to fight.
An orkish captain is here, gleefully whipping his troops into obedience.

Several skeletons, most of them partly decayed, litter the path that twists through the brush. Most of the skeletons are of animals, big and small, that wandered through the area, yet every here and there the remains of a humanoid can be seen, a rusted axe or sword piercing them.
114334: A heavily overgrown path twists and curves around in the brush, with rotten tree stumps and thick undergrowth, thorny brambles, and gnarled, upturned roots creating a maze. A few trees still remain with their dark leafy crowns, but not enough to blocking light from sun and moon. Thick, thorny vines ensnare a few dark trees southwards, creating cracks in the bark.
114335: Several small mounds of dirt lie alongside the path, which is mostly covered with long, black, and mottled sickle-shaped leaves. Therefore, the path itself is difficult to follow, luring those that travel upon it northwards into the forest. A fallen oak tree, its bark rotten and crawling with a multitude of insects, lies eastwards.
114336:
A slender orc scans the area, his bow ready for a sudden strike.
A slender orc scans the area, his bow ready for a sudden strike.
A harsh orkish veteran is here, heavily scarred but ready to fight.
A harsh orkish veteran is here, heavily scarred but ready to fight.
A harsh orkish veteran is here, heavily scarred but ready to fight.
An orkish captain is here, gleefully whipping his troops into obedience.
A slender orc scans the area, his bow ready for a sudden strike.
A long-bodied animal with thick brown fur bounds through the trees.

The path goes here meandering through a dense brushes, making the path more difficult to follow. It's still possible to ride here. The route to the west and south is impassable due to some dense brushes. The path continues to the north, but someone has built a barricade made mostly of wood and some metal parts on the path. Lots of boulders and wood pillars have been installed on the sides of the barricade up to the impassable dense brushes, making it impossible to go around the barricade.
114338:
A huge, poisonous spider is here.
A huge, poisonous spider is here.

Between the thick, pitch-black trees that thrive here, hang thick cobwebs, their silvery shine in sharp contrast with the flora. In a few places, the webs have been cut, the strands hanging down from the branches. In them, insects nearly a foot tall can be spotted, trapped until hunger strikes the owner of the web.
114339: Artificially enlarged, this burrow now provides enough room to allow several humanoids to occupy it. Several cracks inhibit the earth above, although somewhat hidden by the wooden support beams. A small pile of trash litters the southern wall of the burrow, the only distinguishable items being bones of various sizes. A hole has been half-dug beside the pile, only a foot deep so far.
114340: Sharp spikes of varying lengths have been strategically placed on the earthen floor, leaving almost no room for one to walk safely. The spikes are not the only objects to be found here, as a few carcasses in different decaying states and rusted armour and weapons cover them. This tunnel is quite deep underground, as the entrance from above is too high for even the largest humanoid to reach. The walls are slippery, a slimy and watery substance dripping from every side.
114341: Dark, thorny vines slowly choke the vegetation found here, encircling tree and bushes alike. The vines also cover the ground, its sharp, black thorns menacing unprotected limbs. The few plants that once thrived in these surroundings, have all shrivelled up and turned a menacing black. A few corpses of small fauna, decayed into little more than skeletons, remain trapped in the vines.
114342: Many small trees grow here, not yet tall or thick enough to truly be part of the forest. They are heavily surrounded by thick brush, and a few trees have fallen victim to dark green, thorny smothering vines. A clearing can be found in the southern quarter, where twigs and leaves of tree, bush, and plant alike have been eaten by wildlife.
114343: Looming from high above, thick, gnarled tree trunks blot out most of the sunlight above, their thick leaves and pine needles littering the undergrowth. Where the sunlight managed to shine through, the brushwood has grown large and lush. Scattered through the undergrowth, lie hundreds of black insect corpses, emitting a foul odour.
114344: Tall and dark trees, most of them resembling oak and beech, have firmly planted their roots in the soil here. A great deal of these trees present bare holes of over seven inches wide, grey slime dripping from them. The same slime has created a trail over the undergrowth, bark, and nearby vegetation.
114345: Besides the tall, gnarled trees that loom here, no other vegetation can be found. The trees which, usually are blacker than pitch, now bear grey to light grey marks upon them. No more leaves adorn the trees, allowing light from above to illuminate this area. Ashes and a few humanoid skeletons cover the ground, hinting of a fire not so long ago.
114346: Towering dark trees, which might one day have been beech, oak, or fir trees, bear gnarled branches with sometimes black needles or mottled palmate leaves. The branches and needles are speckled with crimson coloured dots. Some trees suffer from cracked bark, a greyish ooze dripping slowly from the cracks.
114347: Thick, pitch-black trees grow closely together here, their upturned roots and branches intertwining with each other, blocking off obvious paths to the north and west. Between the trees, hot, bubbling piles of mud have formed, reeking heavily. To the south, the forest becomes less dense, as many trees that would normally have blocked the sight have been reduced to stumps.
114348: Only a small number of trees, most of them nothing more than growing stems, still grow here, as their brethren have been felled. Thick dark tree stumps cover the entire area, some of them already overgrown with new vegetation. Every here and there, a rusted axe remains rooted in a stump.
114349: A cluster of dark green, feathery fronds flourishes in the shade.

Hundreds of ferns grow tall here, their many leaves blocking the view everywhere, except above. The ferns are oddly coloured, mostly black and grey, every here and there also hinting of magenta. There are a few small openings, where most ferns have shrivelled completely, covered by dark green, thorny plants.
114350: Small, sharp rocks cover the ground, several of them crushing some of the vegetation. Large bramble bushes bearing sharp, thorny branches dominate the view, although other bushes are not too uncommon. Lots of berries adorn the undergrowth, some of them colouring the rocks almost completely dark purple. A few gnarled roots can be seen in the northern part of this area, part of the dark forest close by.
114351: A myriad of different thick bushes have taken root here. Not one of them resembles the other in terms of length, width, fruit or leaves, yet nearly all of them bear the same large and sharp thorns, over two inches wide, grey to black in colour and bearing red dots. Several thorns litter the ground, their prickly ends a menace to body parts unprotected by good armour.
114352: a horde of black insects crawl on the undergrowth, infesting plants and bushes alike. A few bushes have been entirely destroyed by them, leaving only a few bare branches. A lone gnarled tree, covered in crimson dots and bearing several cracks in its bark, remains unperturbed.
114353: Growing closely together, great pitch-black trees loom here, their thick, leafy branches swaying softly, barring any light coming from above. Black, thorny vines, have coiled themselves around a few trees, cracking the bark. Below lies only vegetation, pale in colour, stunted and gnarled, most being nothing more than weeds.
114354: The forest grows quite dense, tree trunks being no further apart than three feet, their roots and branches curving around each other. The thick, black weeds twist between the trees ensnaring and consuming any other flora that try to take root. Some yellow mushrooms hang from the trees, leeching away the sap and exuding a foul odour.
114355: The trail runs north and east. The ground gradually becomes moist and more treacherous along the southeastern edge. The trees have thinned enough to allow one to peer through them to the south, yet not allowing one to travel through them.
114356: The trail travels from the west where it is marshy and soft and turns compact and hard toward the east as the trail narrows. The way north is partly blocked by thick trunks of trees and vegetation but a narrow passageway can probably be found. To the south, a small path leads away from the trail and into the trees.
114357: Inside the cave, rows of sharpened poles form a partial barricade against those who wish to force their entry into this orkish outpost. Behind the crude fortifications, the camp is in disarray. A couple of crude benches stand in the centre of the room, around which scattered tools, bones, and detritus from expanding the cave make for treacherous footing, particularly as the dirt floor gives way to uneven rock. Several filthy banners hang from metal pegs in the greyish cave wall, proclaiming the glory of the Morgundul.
114358:
The corpse of a slender orkish archer is lying here.
A sturdy crate made of nailed wooden planks sits on the floor.
A water barrel has been left here.
A mass of tattered fabric lies here in a heap.
A Morgundul orc guard is sleeping here.
A Morgundul orc guard is sleeping here.
A Morgundul orc guard is sleeping here.

This small, rough-walled chamber is separated with uncharacteristic privacy from the room to the west by a hanging wolfskin, and houses several rows of uncomfortable-looking bedding. The smell of orc is inescapable in this cramped living space, and despite the organised layout of the room the rough stone floor is a mess of rotten food, discarded clothes, and malodourous stains.
114359:
A small oaken table has been set here.
A weapons rack stands against the wall.
In the rack are two short spears.
A Morgundul orc snarls about here, looking for a fight.
An orc-guard of the Morgundul is on patrol here.
An orc-guard of the Morgundul is on patrol here.
An orkish captain is here, gleefully whipping his troops into obedience.

Twenty feet across, this orkish armory is roughly square, with an open passage towards the cave entrance to the south and an iron grate on the eastern wall. The walls are surprisingly smooth, suggesting that this room was carved out with some care. Racks of vicious-looking weapons lie against the western wall of the room, and a shoddy stack of supply crates fills one corner. In the centre of the room is a broad wooden table, askew with equipment in varying states of repair and carved with a crude sketch of the surrounding area.
114360: A small, dingy room has been carved here, more of a recess in the cave wall than a proper chamber. The ground is a mat of rotten, stinking straw, a thin mockery of comfort. There are no windows, and the rough-hewn walls show no decoration save the hopeless scratching of one desperate former resident. The room is sealed off from the rest of the outpost by an iron grate, which hangs heavy but ill-fitting on its rusted hinges.
114361: Dark, looming trees tower overhead on either side of the trail, giving the impression of a tunnel. The way north and south is completely blocked by the huge trunks of the black-barked trees. The trail itself is little more than a narrow path of trampled soil, mostly free of undergrowth.
114362: The dark trees loom over the trail, keeping it in eternal shadow. The trees are mostly old, gnarly oaks with sprawling branches and dark leaves. To the north, the trees grow so densely that they form an impassable wall. The shadowy trail continues to the east and west.
114364: Massive roots shift uneasily all around you.

The trees here seem almost angry as their limbs twist and grow about each other. As the trees rock back and forth in their hatred, there is a deep groaning sound and an occasional screech of the limbs scratching each other.
114365: Thick, short oak trees grow here in a twisted mass. The tops of the trees just overhead grow together, mutating into one mass of branches. The thick oak trees have been blackened at their trunks by the gloom that hangs over this forest.
114367: Wooden and metal spikes are set in the ground, although the dried blood that covers them makes the distinction hard. They are razor-sharp and with most of the metal ones having varying degrees of rust, provide a painful, if not lethal, experience for those that might land upon them. A skeleton or two are pinned on the spikes already, some still bearing rotting flesh.
114371:
A hideous, feathered beast shrieks as it attacks with frightening speed.
A hideous, feathered beast shrieks as it attacks with frightening speed.

This cavern is dug in the limestone with rough pickaxe blows. The floor of the cavern is covered by a thin layer of jet-black feathers. The walls have many markings like someone or something had scratched it with claws, and there are also claw markings on the floor. The only exit is via the raised metal grill to the north.
114372: A graceful and slender tree grows here.

You feel a sense of comfort and well-being as you stroll along the paved courtyard. You notice the upper floors are built on top of this plaza, except in the centre where the sunlight warms this place by day, and the stars shine in by night. The courtyard as a whole is a popular meeting place for the residents of Rivendell, and you can see elves everywhere talking merrily or singing together. You see a magnificent fountain to the south and some shops along the perimeter of the yard.
114373:
A graceful and slender tree grows here.
Arwen Undomiel stands here in radiant beauty ( glowing ).
An elf is here walking around.

You feel a sense of comfort and well-being as you stroll along the paved courtyard.
