You notice the upper floors are built on top of this plaza, except in the centre where the sunlight warms this place by day, and the stars shine in by night. The courtyard as a whole is a popular meeting place for the residents of Rivendell, and you can see elves everywhere talking merrily or singing together. You see a magnificent fountain to the south- east and some shops along the perimeter of the yard.
114374: A doorwarden stands here ready to obey his master's wishes.

Crushed pebbles form a path in the garden leading from the east, then curving to the south where it leads to a small hut. Flowers grow along the path in vibrant colours and various sizes. A few bushes grow on the northern side of the garden, behind a small rock garden. The rocks and stones all have a shiny finish and glisten.
114375: A humble man stands here, ready to help you with your things.

This particular room looks like a study, with a small desk and matching chair standing in one corner, covered with hundreds of pieces of paper with varying degrees of unintelligable scribbles. The faint odour of something burning lingers, although no flame or smoke are visible. The frame of a bed stands on the opposite side of the desk, relatively clear of debris, with a small feather mattress and blanket.
114376: A humble man stands here, ready to help you with your things.

There is a small pond, surrounded by flowering shrubs with white, purple and blue colours. The wall is made of natural river stone, while the ceiling is wood with a skylight just above the pond. A window right next to the door brings in extra light. A hammock hangs in the northeastern corner, weaved from long and supple black roots that bend easily and stretch slightly for the most comfort.
114377: Sudo's Homestead among Roots and Vines
A humble man stands here, ready to help you with your things.

Natural growth of thick roots form three of the walls of this home besides the one to the west. The western wall is made of fresh timbers that were lightly stained, including a simple wooden door. Strands of ivy hang from the ceiling, bright green and leafy, that have grown and weaved their way up among the roots that form the walls. The floor is covered with an older wood, natural, and slightly curved as it nears the roots. A hammock is tied in one corner from the roots for resting.
114381:
A brown fox is here, looking for some rabbits to chew up.
A large rabbit looks peacefully at you, ready to dart away.

The grass in this area has been stomped to the ground. A camp lies to the west, about one mile outside the forest border. It appears to be covered by a large canopy. A trail of dried blood and tree bark leads into the camp. The camp is situated so that the inhabitants have easy access to the trail to the south.
114382:
A warrior of the Urughash is here, guarding the gates.
A warrior of the Urughash is here, guarding the gates.

Dried blood covers the ground around the entrance to the camp. A pair of skulls spiked to the end of poles flank the hole leading out onto the trail. A heavily stitched canopy hangs overhead, blocking out any natural light. The air is heavy with soot and smells of unspeakable things. The camp opens to the west, where it surrounds the base of a tower.
114395:
An elven guard is standing here at his post.
An elven guard is standing here at his post.
A secretary is sitting at the desk.
Glorfindel the chief of the Guardians of Rivendell is standing here ( glowing ).
An elf is here walking around.

Many guards and citizens traffic through this office. It is here that the cityguards' agenda is planned and executed to keep the peace in Rivendell. On the wall you see some pictures of known criminals you should keep an eye out for, and report them to the guards. A notice hangs on the wall behind the secretary's desk.
114396:
A sign reading, Building Permit Information, is here.
A large bulletin board, entitled "Legendhomes", is mounted here.
An Elven steward stands here, watching over the office.

A flat-file shelving unit carved out of white wood and bearing Elven markings labelling each shelf stands here against the south wall serving as a home for countless rolled parchments. In the middle of the room is a large table that fills up most of this small office. Several high-back chairs with deep green cloth cushions surround the table, which is covered with maps.
114402: A humble man stands here, ready to help you with your things.

The room is small and cosy. The walls are covered with bookshelves packed with ancient books and scrolls. The room is poorly lit with only a small, round window that is high up on the wall, opposite to the door. The curved ceiling makes the room appear very old. The aura of this room is calm and relaxing, creating a focused environment.
114450: You wander into a patch of shrubs dominated by dark gnarled trees whos warped and twisted branches stretch all around, forming a canopy which blocks out all external light. As you move, you step on old blackened leaves which crunch loudly as you tread upon them and dark crows scatter from their shelter as you approach.

To the north, dense and thick green vegetation grows, while the areas south of the road seem to be much drier.

114489: The Road to the Grey Havens

114490: The Road to the Grey Havens

Maybe the underground can't hold the water and it vanishes in unknown depths? South is an endless looking savanna.
114492: The Road to the Grey Havens

You are walking on the road to the Grey Havens. The countryside is not very interesting here. The savannas have faded away and the road is surrounded by plains that stretch far to the horizon. Several books can be found on shelves located around the room.

To the south is a stone fireplace that gives off a quiet warmth.

You notice that you can barely travel along this path. You look down and you see that there maybe a path leading down to the river. You could head back toward the trail, or you could head on along the river. There are a lot of bushes and small trees that wandering too far around could give you some unwanted troubles. The river looks like it could be a nice place to take a swim. You can go south back to the trail or lead on north along the bank. Maybe you can even go down the slope down to the river.
115023: An Overgrown Trail around the Hills
A boar cub is playing here, and exploring the wide world.

This trail seems to have been deserted a long time ago. It is more just a path with little grass growing on it around the hill. Along the hill is a lot of lush grass growing, a good place to rest any horses and allow them to feed. The wind blows cold around the hill and all around you you can only see more hills. There seems to be no civilization out there.
115024: A fierce boar is here, making grunting noises.

This forest is lovely, with lots of fresh air to breathe and beautiful things to behold. The trees are huge and spaced apart in a maze like way. Squirrels and other little animals populate the trees. Best be careful though, other animals live in these kind of areas and they aren't as cute as squirrels. The ground is soft and moist as if a river is nearby feeding the woodland grounds.
115025: A dark forest of firs and pines looms all about you, the forms of trees shadowy and indistinct only a short distance away. Small bushy plants grow amid the trees and purplish vines snake up the tree trunks, with vampiric suckers locked into the bark. Trees can be seen in every direction, but seem to thin somewhat to the east.
115026:
A beer mug is here.
A loaf of bread has been left here.
A large piece of cheese has been placed here.
A round tangle with waxy leaves and white berries grows on a branch nearby.
A wine glass has been left here.

Sitting in the shelter of a beautiful old willow, a stone table was created here with the passage of time by natural erosion. Roughly carved benches have been volunteered long ago perhaps by travellers passing through. Throughout the year the pleasant fragrance of wild grasses intensifies and lingers.
115027: A Belt of Tall and Very Ancient Oaks
A woodpecker is here, tapping on a tree.

An old oak-wood spreads all over this area. The tree branches are long and twisted under the weight of their leafy tops, and the trunks look strong and thick, with their wrinkled barks hardened through the years. Further east, beyond them, stands a high, prickly, dark green hedge, so dense that you can not discern anything on the other side, and the oaks follow its perimeter forming a large belt. A broad and heavy wooden gate, beyond which you can see elegant-looking gardens, opens through the hedge, and a grassy path starts there and leads westwards, in the shade of some trees planted alongside in a row.
115029: A thumb-long bee buzzes loudly as it flutters among the flowers.

A small and simple stall with a neat look stands to the west. The smell of fresh hay, and some occasional loud yet mild neighs reach you from behind its coarse gate, where, half-hidden in shadows, you glimpse heaps of golden yellow straw. A little path, that comes running through wide gardens from the southern end of the house, approaches near here before bending eastwards, to the encounter of the main one that leads into the courtyard.
115031:
A well-fed cow stands here chewing her cud listlessly.
A hobbit farmer is here, thinking about seeds and vegetables.
A well-fed cow stands here chewing her cud listlessly.

You have entered a yard that is fenced in. Obviously you have found someone's farm. Who they are though is another question. There are some horses here. along with a few other animals. The yard has a lot of grass for the animals and it looks to be well kept as well.
115047: Whether started by you or someone else, this fire is out of control. You cannot see farther than in front of your face. Your eyes sting from the billowing smoke and it is so hot it burns!
115051: Whether started by you or someone else, this fire is out of control. You cannot see farther than in front of your face. Your eyes sting from the billowing smoke and it is so hot it burns!
115066: Whether started by you or someone else, this fire is out of control. You cannot see farther than in front of your face. Your eyes sting from the billowing smoke and it is so hot it burns!
115081: A pickaxe-hewn tunnel stretches down towards the west, away from the sturdy, timber door that has been built into the wall to the east. Small piles of rocks lie strewn about, along with some extra timber boards from the construction of the door. The tunnel sides are hewn, and are about the width of a large troll.
115082:
The corpse of an enslaved troll is lying here.
The corpse of an enslaved troll is lying here.
A rusty pickaxe with a broken handle lies discarded here.

The dry tunnel curves from the east to the south into a natural depression in the tunnel wall. Small squeaks can be heard, and the guano deposits get heavier as the tunnel leads southwards. The walls of the tunnel are marked with scars from where the pickaxes struck, and rubble lies on the floor, along with some straw. A subtle draft carries the foul smell of decay from the south.
115083:
A large bat is here, hanging in the darkness.
A large bat is here, hanging in the darkness.
A large bat is here, hanging in the darkness.

The ground lowers into a still-growing and decades-old pile of bat guano. The curved cavern walls are streaked with white lines that go all the way down to the floor. The cavern rises to an unclimbable height up above, where more bat squeaks can be heard. Some bones of unfortunate critters litter the ground.
115088: The limestone tunnel opens up into a larger cavern cut off by a rusted, iron grate. Pickaxe blows mar the tunnel walls as they slowly lead downwards into a dark hatch made of timber. The western wall is heavily hewn, but oddly smooth, as a small, rectangular outline runs across its surface. A small, disarrayed pile of limestone rubble and decaying wooden struts, sits in the northwest.
115089:
A large bulletin board, entitled "Trawl Bored", is mounted here.
A demon wolf lurks here, its dark form twisting and hiding its shape.

This tunnel is really a natural cave that has been expanded by the brute power of stony troll fists. The stink of troll sweat fills your head, proving that many trolls spend a lot of time here. This must be the trolls' home, the place where they conduct whatever crude business they occupy themselves with when not crushing prey.
115090: There is not a single tree on these hills, so the undergrowth is very thick and makes moving rather difficult. All the time one has to change his way to avoid running into thorny bushes. Down on the west side of the hills there is a light forest.
115092: The rough and jagged cuts in the tunnel walls give proof of the massive labour behind the hasty shaping of this underground passageway. The walls display an intricate cross-section of the subterranean vegetation: rubble, packed hard in the soil, together with chopped-off roots and dead twigs and branches. Larger rocks occasionally protrude from the sides of the tunnel, marked with deep gashes from their encounter with the pickaxe.
115095: This well-trodden trail follows the southern border of a forest. Thick matted undergrowth and brambles grow under the shadow of ancient firs there, and at times invade the track. To the south, high grass spreads over the undulating ground up to the foot of a ridge of hills.
115098: A thick mat of orange needles blankets the ground among the fern fronds that grow amid the fir boles. Wrinkled roots curl among the limestone rocks as each tree thrusts itself upright into the impenetrable canopy. The prickly branches are densely woven together, making travel through the dark wood difficult.
115102: Several pine trees have taken root here, interspersed with dark fir trees. The crowns of the trees looming above bear thick, crooked branches that effectively block out all light coming from above. Many branches lie scattered on the undergrowth, preventing easy movement through the forest.
115103: A slender orc scans the area, his bow ready for a sudden strike (hidden).

Thick, silvery cobwebs have been spun between the monstrous, black trees that thrive here. Thick, gnarled branches that bear speckled needles have thrust themselves through some of the webs, leaving only a few strands hanging on the branch itself. A few cocoons, about a feet wide, adorn the webs.
115109: Tall, slender trees extend their trunks and leafy branches into the sky above. The bark, protecting each trunk of these trees, is a soft shade of brown, appearing flawless through years of growth. It is not until several feet above the base of the trees that their branches extend out around the trunks. Each leaf, shaped like a small spear, is a mint-coloured green. An aged wagon remains tilted upon its side in the centre of the forest. Thin, delicate strands of ivy have grown over the top of the wagon remains. There is fine, green grass in growth, stretching from around the wagon to the base of the tall trees that are surrounding it. As this fine grass reaches the trees, it then diminishes among the undergrowth of the forest.
115112:
A large brown snake with black patches is coiled here.
A large brown snake with black patches is coiled here.

The wagon would allow a comfortable amount of space from within, providing that it was in an upright position. However, left in its current position, tilted over upon its side, the height of it while standing is very short. Judging from the appearance of the wagon, one would think that it has lain here for many years. The planks that form the walls look like they were made of some kind of mahogany. There are several racks that have been attached to the left side of the wagon wall, placed along each side of the door to the wagon.
115114:
A cluster of dark green, feathery fronds flourishes in the shade.
Some thick writhing vines whip all around you.
Some black, oozing vines reach out from the choked canopy towards you.

A vague haze hangs over the forest here, giving it a dreary, white glow. The dark shapes of trees are easy to make out, and are thick with moss and vines. Some fallen trees can be seen through the murk, moss hanging off of their trunks like a filthy mane. The trees grow close, further obscuring any view of the nearby area, though the forest floor slopes perilously downward to the north.
115120:
A colossal tree, its trunk as wide as a small cottage, stands here.
Some roots lie here waiting to ensnare weary travellers.
A tangled creeper writhes its shoots between the forest's roots upwards.

Black trunks and light-blocking treetops make this a particularly dark part of the forest. Twisted, serpent-like roots reach out here and there on the ground. The forest floor is covered by decaying black leaves and the smell of rotting vegetation hangs heavy in the air.
115121: A black pond is here, filled with putrid water.

The forest here is thick and hazy, and the floor laden with ivy and sharp, loathsome thornbushes. The land gradually slopes upwards to the north, and more treacherously to the south. A thick mist hangs above a small, shallow pool, and dark trees grow right up to the edge. Indeed, a few twisted willow trees grow within the pool, their leaves covered in small droplets of water. A large number of animal tracks are clustered at the banks, even though the water is dark and distasteful, with scum covering its stagnant surface.
115122:
A piece of disgusting, gristly meat lies here.
A small piece of raw meat is on the ground.

The evil, twisted trees of Mirkwood grow exceptionally densely around here, closing in from all sides save the east where a dark opening among them forms a dismal hollow. The ground is ripe with the bones and other remains of countless animals. Rancid meat lies rotting on the root-covered ground, choking the misty air with a vile, foetid odour.
115123: A half-decayed corpse of a goblin lies rotting on the ground.

A scene of carnage fills this part of the dark, malevolent forest. Amid the bones and blood of many unknown humanoids, the wretched trees seem to thrive in the blood-soaked landscape. Numerous bodies cover the soil among the twisting ivy and the horrid, thorned bushes.
115124: The twisting branches are so tangled here that they form a solid barrier on both sides. The canopy above is dense and oppressive, and the roots are so intertwined that even footing is impossible to find. Dark and hazy, the tunnel runs east and west. A repugnant odour lingers about the hollow, seemingly originating from the west.
115125: The forest grows thick and harsh, obscuring anything in the distance. Looming black trees bear down on all sides; their gnarled branches seeking relentlessly to instil fear into the hearts of travellers. A few holes have been dug here. Most are shallow, but one is much larger, deeper, and shows signs of recent use.
115126: Dark tree roots cover the forest floor as it climbs toward a wide hill. Even at the top, the woods are dense, and little of the surrounding forest can be seen. A thick haze hangs over the lower trees, shrouding them in a dim white fog. The hill drops to the north, leading deep into the misty tortured forest below. The dark woods thicken even more to the west, and to the south the twisted trees grow so close that travel is impossible for all but the smallest of animals.
115127: A very heavy branch is lying here on the ground.

The forest here is dark and extremely dense, with numerous entangled beech trees choking each other for space to grow. Branches crowd in from all sides, including above, where the thick, ubiquitous canopy blots out the sky. The forest floor is covered in spiky, malnourished shrubs, and the ground slopes downwards to the west. The twisted beeches grow so dense to the south that travel in that direction will not be possible.
115128:
An elaborate red flower sits within a dark mass of briars.
A tangled creeper writhes its shoots between the forest's roots upwards.
A swift carnivore bustles around.

A thick, clammy haze hangs in the air, obstructing the view of the enclosing woods. The malformed vegetation that grows here is dank from the haze, and many of the dark trees are covered in a mass of dark green moss. The ground cover is thick and thorny, hampering every movement. The terrain rises sharply to the east, though the foliage is no less suffocating.
115129: Covered in thick, tangled trees, this hill provides a mediocre view of the murky trail which can be seen below in the fog-shrouded lands as a narrow gap in the trees to the north and east. Thorny bushes cover the floor of the dim forest, clawing at the legs of any who have the misfortune to wander here. The ground falls away quickly to the east, and more gradually to the north. To the west, the hill continues to climb, mostly escaping the unnatural, ever-present haze which conceals the rest of the dark woods.
115130:
A patch of moss grows here on a wet, flat stone.
A small termite is running around making strange sounds.

From a small burrow below the trees the tunnel opens up into a wide cavern. The ground is a mix of earth and black rock that shifts underfoot. Vile roots hang from the ceiling, giving a disturbing caress to the heads of those with more stature. To the east, the passage narrows into the darkness.
115131: The earth and rock walls close to just a few feet in diameter. The dark, wet mud looks like it could collapse further at the slightest disturbance. Small insects crawl around, making it clear that not every creature is bothered by the dank atmosphere.
115132: Thick roots jut out from every angle, but they have been crudely severed to form a somewhat passable tunnel. Several of the cuts are fresh, while others were clearly made some time ago. It is evident that there is a constant struggle to keep the forest from reclaiming the earth below as its own.
115133: A steep, wide slope leads down from the forest into a dark, damp passageway. The ground is smooth, indicating frequent use by travellers wishing to avoid the wood above. The smooth trail leads west into a twisting knot of massive tree roots.
115134: A small termite is running around making strange sounds.

The ceiling here is low, no more than six feet tall. Roots from the forest above grow along the ceiling and walls, thinning out as the tunnel descends downward into darkness. The floor of the tunnel slopes steeply downward. A thick layer of mud and dense roots covers the northern wall.
115135: The cavern is vast and expansive, with a smooth, level floor and a stony grey wall. Large slabs of stone jut out randomly along the walls and the ceiling of the cave is covered in a blanket of densely tangled roots from the forest above. Off to the side, there is a steeply ascending tunnel that is lined with thick tangles of roots that are inhabited by small insects.
115136:
A giant termite is here, crushing skulls and bones.
A small termite is running around making strange sounds.
A small termite is running around making strange sounds.
A small termite is running around making strange sounds.

The cavern opens up into a huge space, with large rocks and boulders lining the eastern and western walls. The tops of these rocks and boulders are covered in thick blankets of green and black mosses. The air here is humid and heavy, and some of the rocks to the west are wet with condensation. The ceiling of the cavern rises up high and is covered in densely tangled roots. There is a large crack in the floor that leads down into a deep, dark pit.
115137: Large rocks and boulders line the walls of this vast, open cavern. The rocks have thick blankets of black and green mosses that have settled and spread among the tops of them. To the east, a large stack of flat stones lies neatly piled to form steps that leads up to a narrow tunnel. The ceiling of the cavern is covered in densely tangled roots from the forest above.
115138:
A small termite is running around making strange sounds.
A small termite is running around making strange sounds.
A giant termite is here, crushing skulls and bones.

Several feet of thick, black mud fill this pit in its entirety. Stones jut out from the walls, forming a sort of natural staircase in which to ascend to the cavern above. Insects crawl along the stone walls, disappearing into small cracks here and there.
115139: A small termite is running around making strange sounds.

Narrow and muddy, the floor of the tunnel drops off in the west, where a natural stone staircase leads down into a vast cavern. The walls and ceiling are lined with roots, and small insects crawl amongst them. The tunnel continues to the east, where passage becomes more difficult.
115140: The air in this cavern is oppressively humid, and every surface is dangerously slick. Every rock is covered in moss, although a few bare patches reveal that the walls are made of granite. Roots protrude down through the cavern ceiling, bursting through the rocks and climbing down the walls.
115141:
An albino salamander is here, perched on some rocks.
A small termite is running around making strange sounds.

Thick tangles of roots make passage in this narrow, underground tunnel tedious and difficult. The floor of the tunnel is covered in thick, pungent mud with roots mixed in. Thick roots cover the southern portion of the tunnel, where the wall does not seem to be entirely solid.
115143: Some black, oozing vines reach out from the choked canopy towards you.

The midnight-black vines intertwine with the massive black oaks, creating a dense mass of foliage. Each vine is covered in extremely sharp thornes, making the canopy above a terrifying shroud. Fresh blood still drips from their cruel spines, indicating that something has been entangled here recently. Their seemingly intentional web looks as though any struggle after being caught would only cause more damage and entangle the victim further.
115145: Jutting up from the blackened earth are hundreds of large, oblong boulders, each with a unique horrific etching. Some portray massive scenes of carnage and slaughter, while others show a single terror-struck face, most likely victims of Dol Guldur's overwhelming evil. Black mist lingers in and about the stones; its moisture adds definition and clarity to the etchings.
115146: The forest has not touched these hills, save a few carcasses laid bare by some low-lying predators, baking on the hot black stone. To the west, the base of a sheer incline can be seen, making any passage in that direction impossible. The hills continue to the south, before descending into the black depths of Mirkwood.
115147: The blackened earth rises and falls erratically over the expansive hills, though it is hard to see much in the distance. The sharp rocks and loose stones make travel extremely treacherous. To the north, a steep drop into a ravine is clouded with shadows and is quite impossible to scale.
115148: A few leafless, malformed trees dot the rocky ground, twisting and turning at the whim of the ever-present evil. Concealed in shadow, a few relatively small crevices are lodged into the hillside, undoubtedly a good retreat for the disfigured beasts that roam this land. Far to the west, a black shadow lingers over the hills, even thicker and darker than usual for Mirkwood.
115149: The broken hills of Dol Guldur continue here. A craggy cliff face rises up to the north, while below to the south there is a large camp surrounded by a wooden palisade. To the north and east the hills are slightly less steep, making passage possible, if difficult.
115150: Some small rocks have been piled into a mound here.

The treacherous earth is compounded by the numerous rock formations jutting into the sky. Many of the outcroppings extend far above the low-hanging black haze, making it impossible to judge their true height. Surrounding the protruding rocks are a few short, leafless trees that have somehow managed to survive amidst the harsh terrain. To the north, the rock creates a tall barricade, preventing any passage in that direction.
115151: These hills are dark and dreary. The black basalt is not protected by soil, so wind and water have eroded the rocks for ages. The erosion has formed strange pillars, clefts, edges, cliffs, and crevices that make the steep slope dangerous to travel. The whole area is inhospitable and unfriendly to life.
115152: A massive pile of rubble covers the ground.

Formations of black, ragged rock surround this terrace on Dol Guldur. The terrace lies high above the forest to the west and south and the way down impossibly steep. Opposite these deadly dropoffs the hills rise to the east and north. Only the north hill seems traversible, making this terrace a dead-end.
115153:
A cluster of dark green, feathery fronds flourishes in the shade.
The wicked undergrowth rustles malevolently, shifting and widening.

The area is completely void of any sort of trail, and the blackened foliage pushes in on all directions. Commanding more attention than even the tree branches or thick brush is the presence of an unnamed evil; it lingers in the thickness. The black ground itself can very rarely be seen due to the dense undergrowth, and visibility in all directions is limited at best.
115154: A ledge has formed on the side of the bare hill. It is in the middle of a steep slope that descends towards the south and rises to the north. The only reasonable way off the ledge is toward the west into the hills. To the east, it tapers off into nothing. Erosion has caused the edge of the ledge to crumble. It looks dangerously unstable.
115156: Many boulders jut out from the ground in all directions. There are also what appear to be loose boulders which have ended up here. The rocks and boulders are covered in hanging, stinking moss and cause a block to the east. To the north, the way is blocked by many intertwining trees and roots.
115157: The trees thin out somewhat compared to the north and west, though they have a hunched over appearance as if the air itself has weighed their limbs down. Many spiders have taken advantage and have built their webbed nests in the low hanging branches of the dismal trees.
115158:
A small mushroom grows nearby.
A large, black butterfly is fluttering about erratically.
A large, black butterfly is fluttering about erratically.

As if an enormous dragon had scored a furrow into the living earth, a deep fissure descends like a gaping wound into the ground here. The only way up to the rest of the forest is westwards, while to the north, the ground drops rapidly into oppressive darkness.
115159:
A hungry warg stands here, sniffing around for flesh.
A large, black butterfly is fluttering about erratically.

With looming cliffs towering on each side, a deep, dark fissure is formed. Its floor slopes steeply, uphill to the south and rapidly deeper and darker to the north. There is a strong evidence that something large inhabits the lower darkness as the twisted trees have several branches snapped and the vegetation has been squashed flat in many places.
115160: This narrow cavern is so deep that the towering cliffs on either side appear almost to meet overhead. Though the black trees grow as thick as ever here, there is a definite clear path forced between them, across which the grasping branches do not pass. The ground underfoot is thoroughly tamped down, such that Mirkwood's usual tangle of roots and brush has given way to mud.
115161: A skull is here, spiked to the end of a pole.

No natural light reaches the floor of this black chasm, as the walls to either side close in ever tighter until they join up completely, creating an underground passage to the east. The ground is churned into mud and even the ever-present trees of Mirkwood have been beaten back to form a sizeable clearing. A rough stake has been forced into the ground by the cave entrance, and a strong smell of animal decay emanates from within the lair.
115162:
A bloody and crudely severed pair of pointed ears lie here.
A huge stone giant is here, glaring at you.

This black lair exudes an almost overpowering stench of decaying flesh. Upon the rocks of the floor are semi-dried gobs of raw meat and entrails, along with a number of crushed skulls and other shattered bones. On one wall, fanciful lines and swirls are crudely drawn, and the dye of choice seems to be fresh blood. Another wall seems to have been plastered together using blood, hair, fur, bone and other grisly materials.
115163:
A skull is here, spiked to the end of a pole.
Some roots lie here waiting to ensnare weary travellers.

This deep fissure turns dramatically here. To the south, a stiff scramble uphill leads to less dark but more heavily forested terrain, whereas to the west, the cliffs close in completely overhead, forming a black cavern. The ground has been churned up here and the trees have been beaten back somewhat to create an open area at the mouth of the cave. From within the darkness, a strong stench of animal decay billows.
115164: A cluster of dark green, feathery fronds flourishes in the shade.

The shadowed land drops suddenly here, sinking rapidly into a dark, narrow fissure, with sharp cliffs rising up on each side. Branches have been broken from the tortured trees, and the ground underfoot is compressed in places, suggesting that something of considerable size has passed this way. Westwards, the grim forest opens up, reveaaling sickly trees that are larger and more widely spaced.
115165: A massive black tree, covered in rotting, blistered bark, stands alone here.

Unlike much of Mirkwood, a tree stands alone here. But it is a behemoth of a tree, unlike any other. Half rotten, yet large and strong, it appears to have choked out every plant near it, leaving bare forest surrounding its gigantic, gnarled roots. A thick black mist around the tree emits an awful odour.
115166: A moderately-sized copperhead snake is here.

With the ground dropping away into darkness on both the east and west sides, this area has the feeling of a bridge across a forbidding, black chasm below. The trees are clearly not affected by vertigo as they pack as tightly as always to every scrap of ground. The roots here are particularly treacherous, seeming to curl out unexpectedly, attempting to pitch any passers-by over a precipice and to their doom in the darkness far below.
115167: To the north and west, the trees suddenly stop as the ground drops vertically away into a deep, black chasm. Faint sounds of movement and a hideous stench of decaying plants and animals drift up from below. To the south, passage is also blocked, this time by a tangled thicket of vines, laden with an evil sickness that renders them putrid and slimy, even while they still grow. The only easy way out of this stinking dead end is to the east where the foliage seems to open up considerably.
115168: A sprawling green bush of stinging nettle grows here.

Although the trees in this part of Mirkwood are not as tangled or closely set as in many other areas, the ground vegetation has taken complete control of the terrain instead. Deformed black nettles have overrun every surface, their strangely twisted stems and leaves bristling with stiff hairs, ready to apply a nasty sting at the slightest contact. Though movement through here is possible, it is highly unlikely that any creatures of the forest would relish such an experience.
115169:
The corpse of a Morgundul orc guard is lying here.
The corpse of a Morgundul orc guard is lying here.
The corpse of a Morgundul orc guard is lying here.

The trees in this wet and muddy area of the forest are smothered and mutilated by thick, strangling vines. Forming a dense web, especially to the north where passage is wholly blocked, these constricting growths appear laden with a rotting sickness that infects all that they cover. This renders the entire area putrid, the slimy vegetable matter decomposing even while it lives.
115170: The rocky path narrows here as coiled roots intrude from the south. Many of the roots have been chopped off, and some still ooze a dark, distasteful fluid. A rancid smell lurks about the area, and a thick, moist haze envelops the trail, making breathing somewhat difficult. A crude, low arch is barely visible through the mist to the east, while the trail to the west vanishes into the obscurity of Mirkwood.
115171: Crushed rock has been laid upon the dark, foul-smelling soil of the trail to Dol Guldur, which runs east-west through the morose haze. Still, the ground is treacherous; the trail slopes up to the east, and sharp rocks and pieces of splintered bone await the chance to snag the unwary. Wicked, twisted trees close in from all sides like a pack of deranged wolves, thirsty for warm blood.
115172: The trail widens a bit here as it continues to travel under the limbs of the overhanging trees. The trees are beginning to look more and more twisted by an evil force the further east, this trail goes. To the east the trail begins to turn into a hard packed road.
115175: Thick, coiled roots strive against each other as they attempt to mine the dark soil. The forest floor is so littered with them that only a couple of withering shrubs grow here. All the other plants seem to have been choked away one by one. To the south and east, fallen trees lie rotting after being uprooted by the ruinous, malignant roots.
115176: Covered in grisly carvings, a forbidding archway hangs low over the trail, which continues to the west and east. The arch is vulgar and misshapen, and clearly the work of some crude humanoid. Tree branches crowd close, obscuring some of the detail, but one thing is clear: east through the gates and up into the gloomy crags lies the malevolent citadel of Dol Guldur, overseen by a foul, twisted tower.
115177:
The remains of a grey, putrid fungus lie here in a heap of rotting compost.
The remains of a giant green fungus lie here in a heap of rotting compost.
The remains of a giant green fungus lie here in a heap of rotting compost.
The remains of a black fungus lie here in a heap of rotting compost.
The remains of a black fungus lie here in a heap of rotting compost.

An extraordinarily terrible infestation has taken over the surrounding oaks, strangling them into a disfigured state. Entire trees crawl with millions of voracious insects. A vicious fungal infection also spreads across each massive root. The fungi quiver and convulse as they suck the life out of the massive hardwoods.
115178: A black pond is here, filled with putrid water.

The diseased forest floor is broken up only by the occasional putrid green bubbling pool. Steam rises quickly from the simmering muck, and an overwhelmingly rancid stench floods the thick air with each pop of a new bubble surfacing. Though many pools are easily spotted, several others are barely visible, camouflaged amidst the dense and invasive surroundings.
115179: Covered in rocks and pebbles, the misty road dips here as it runs east and west. Visibility is limited, but a distant red glow can be seen high in the sky to the east. A wide arch, barely visible in the dense gloom, crosses the trail to the west. Sick, sinister trees push onto the trail from the south, threatening to overtake the narrow road. There is a small cliff on the north side of the road, with ill-tempered trees looming overhead.
115180: This area of Mirkwood rises above its surroundings. The height does nothing to dispel the darkness that claims the forest floor and nothing of the sky is visible above. The forest thins to the south making it barely possible to see some sort of trail or road.
115181: The road rises and falls at the whim of the forest, though the invasive foliage is ever present. Twisted and malformed trees reach down from above with their clawing branches, seemingly waiting to pounce on the unsuspecting. Dominating the sky to the east, Dol Guldur sits encased in shadow, malevolent and brooding. A smaller trail leaves the road, disappearing under the shadows of the trees to the west.
115182: The road continues to the north and south, lined with fallen trees and thick brush, while a massive wall of dark foliage barricades the way to the west. Pinned to the occasional tree is a gruesome, rotting, dead body, fully adorned with a barely recognisable frozen face of horror and a few black carrion birds pecking away at the rotting flesh.
115183: The road narrows here, invaded by the surrounding trees and cluttered by thick undergrowth. Various types of mould and lichen cover the forest floor, discouraging anyone from straying from the path. A few of the trees look as though they have been battered and beaten; their wounds seeping with a thick black sap.
115184: Void of leaves, the mix of black oaks and birches has been corrupted by the evil that saturates the air. Two extremely large, black trees stand on both sides of the road as ominous sentinels. Deep groans and the sound of slow, deliberate movements seem to indicate that the forest itself is more alive than it would appear.
115185: To the west, the road dips into the foul oppressive gloom of the dark forest. To the north, it winds up the hills of Dol Guldur. While the air of hills is less foul than the woods to the west, it almost seems more foreboding. The hills to east and south climb steeply. Sharp, jagged rocks cover the terrain that way, making any passage impossible.
115186:
The corpse of a Morgundul orc-guard is lying here.
A Morgundul orc-guard, wielding a longspear, is here, fighting a dark oak.
A Morgundul orc-guard, wielding a longspear, is here, fighting a dark oak.
A dark oak is here, fighting Klaees (thedon).
A dark oak is here, fighting Klaees (thedon).
A tremendous black oak looms here.
A dark oak is here, fighting a Morgundul orc-guard.
Klaees (thedon), wielding a great warsword, is here, fighting a dark oak.

The thick forested surroundings are as abrasive and menacing as ever. Opaque shadows dance between the trees, discernible at one moment and gone the next. The black treacherous ground seems to constantly find a way to make the journey through this area as troublesome as possible.
115187: A pile of dry, brown leaves lies here.

Though the malice-filled forest is as sinister as ever to the north and west, southwards a cliff drops down to a dark road. The ground here is very soft in comparison to the surroundings, seemingly made up of rotten wood, branches, moss, and pieces of decaying forest. Each step squishes into the decay with a moist, bubbly gurgle.
115188:
The remains of a mass of briars lie here in a heap of rotting compost.
The remains of a thick tangle of vines lie here in a heap of rotting compost.
The remains of a coil of oozing vines lie here in a heap of rotting compost.
A greenish slime mould is here, smelling badly.

Vines and growths dangle from the low canopy of trees and emit a chokingly thick smell of rot. The vines themselves drip with a thick black substance, seeping and festering with the poison of Mirkwood. The rocky ground is covered in the black substance, making the ground slippery and treacherous.
115189: The remains of a coil of oozing vines lie here in a heap of rotting compost.

This part of the forest is filled with sounds of constant scraping and hissing from the branches above, mixed with an occasional more substantial cracking. Leaves and twigs spiral down, with a constant threat of something much weightier crashing to the ground without warning. It is hard to tell whether the sound is from some sort of vile animal, or from the trees themselves, but the malice is unmistakable.
115190:
A sprawling, twisted tree grows here.
On the tree, there are a few hawthorn berries.

The ground rises up here to a small peak, but one so thickly forested with a stand of dense trees and shrubs that it is impossible to see far in most directions. Across the valley, a few miles to the southeast, the tall silhouette of Dol Guldur rises up, craggy and menacing. A massive dark fortress sits atop it, towering into the black mists that swirl around the naked hill's summit.
115191:
A large boulder is here, it must be heavy.
A half-decayed corpse of a goblin lies rotting on the ground.

The ground is unusually open here, with trunks of the surrounding trees spaced wide apart almost as if purposefully planted in a circle many ages ago. On the ground are strewn several rounded boulders, most of which are splattered with a great deal of blood, dried into a gruesome black crust. Some intense violence has happened here repeatedly. To the north and west, the open ground has been overrun by intense thorn-laden undergrowth, and passage to the east is hindered by a large pile of burnt rubble.
115192: A fallen tree lies on the ground, its clump of roots pointing upwards.

Enormous, wide-trunked yews grow here, taller and more ancient than in many other areas of Mirkwood. Indeed, it appears that these corrupt yews may have purposefully been planted in a large circle in ages gone by, based on the round clearing that extends west of here. The malice of the forest is as palpable as ever with the sinister, dark trees looming threateningly overhead.
115193:
The corpse of a troll scavenger is lying here.
The corpse of a warty troll is lying here.
The corpse of a troll scavenger is lying here.
A pile of dry, brown leaves lies here.
A battered warg fur has been left here.
A half-decayed corpse of a goblin lies rotting on the ground.

The forest floor is covered with rotting, ancient detritus, save a stamped circular area inside a thicket of dark oaks. Bleached bones and half-eaten corpses lie scattered around, some of them almost buried under the foetid leaves.
115194: Little parts of a broken weapon are lying on the ground.

A few gaps in the canopy provide a rare glimpse into the sky above. To the north, a sheer cliff drops away into a black gorge, where the tops of the twisted trees can be seen some distance below. On the opposite side, a similar cliff rises up, beyond which stretches the seemingly endless, unyielding forest of Mirkwood. Scattered along the ground is a large, wet pile, the stinking contents of which are not immediately recognisable.
115195: The corpse of a scaly hill troll is lying here.

There is a stale, breathless silence here, broken only by constant dripping from the moisture-laden mosses and lichens that cover every surface, down to the forest floor. The very trees appear to be keeping still, as if the entire area is holding its breath. The thick mat of decaying mosses underfoot and the sticky webs of silk overhead muffle sound so thoroughly that this would be an ideal place for the predators of Mirkwood to hunt, which the countless bones of unfortunate animals give testament to.
115196:
A skeleton of some humanoid lies in the dust.
A diamondback rattlesnake is coiled here, ready to strike.

Despite the relatively open ground here, a deep and forbidding mist permeates the dark terrain. Occasional threads of silk hang from the canopy above, and the ground is littered with half-rotten sticks, loose stones, and the occasional bone, making quiet travel a challenge for all but the smallest and most nimble of creatures.
115197:
The remains of a grey, putrid fungus lie here in a heap of rotting compost.
A greenish slime mould is here, smelling badly.

The air is thick here, full of nasty spores and dust. Great tendrils of dark moss and lichen hang low from the branches of each tree. Some of the tendrils are rotting but most are long-dead and surprisingly bone dry. They constantly add to the vile motes floating in the air as they move even in the slight, haze-shrouded breeze. The resulting atmosphere is painful to inhale, cloying one's tongue and throat with the foul taste of ancient death.
115198: A thick, dark haze hangs about the menacing trees and extends in all directions. The darkness is as oppressive as ever, bearing down its evil weight on all who venture here. A minuscule amount of breathable air seems to sneak through the tangles of the amazingly dense and twisted undergrowth. Eastwards, the ground drops away into a small brush-filled gully, making travel around it far easier than through it.
115199: A humble man stands here, ready to help you with your things.

Once large and strong, the oak is now past its better years. The hollow of the tree has been used as a secure hive by bees for ages. Here and there are the remains of honeycombs filling the cracks. Even though bees have abandoned it for some reason, the scent of old oak is mixed with one of honey. A leather armchair stands in the room.
115200: A humble man stands here, ready to help you with your things.

An incredibly large bed takes centre-stage in this room. Fit for a family of giants it is covered with silk sashes and pillows of all sizes, furs made for covers are lining the bottom and a huge purple drape comes from the ceiling ready to hide the bed completely. A large vanity is set against the top of it where jewellery boxes are spilling over and an incense burner stands along the side. See-through silk leggings are draped over the chair in front, a huge chest filled with boots of all sizes lies in the corner, and suggestive artwork covers the walls.
115203: The trees here begin to grow very tightly together, causing a natural dead end. The trunks of the trees are so thick here that the there is no way to get through. There is a dark gloom that hovers over this area as the trees block all light and capture a musty mist which hangs over the forest.
115204: Twisted and mutilated branches criss-cross between the trees so thickly that there is scarcely any room to wriggle between them. The cruel boughs, often sporting rancid fungal growths or wicked thorns, seem almost consciously aware as they manage to always be positioned right where they can gash unprotected skin. A dark void opens up in the forest floor to the south, with cliffs dropping down into blackness.
115205:
A hollow tree is growing upright here.
A skeleton of some humanoid lies in the dust.
A brown stag looks around with big, startled eyes.

There is nowhere to turn here, save west. To the north and east, brambles of such ferocity bar the way, evil thorns protruding threateningly in every direction, that to cut through would take days. To the south, a dizzying void opens up, with slick cliffs dropping into utter darkness. Even overhead, the mass of groping branches forms a roof as impenetrable as any formed by hand. Sticks and roots protrude from the ground, along with some old bones. A couple of discoloured skulls stare vacantly from underneath the brambles.
115206: The evil, black forest pushes relentlessly in on all sides, but especially from under foot. The ground is a massive tangle of twisted, tortured roots that seem almost sentient in their ability to catch and hold anyone travelling through them. The rotting stench of decay that rises up cannot be wholly explained by plant matter alone. The vegetation is thickest to the north, making movement in that direction impractical.
115207:
The corpse of a troll scavenger is lying here.
A sprawling, twisted tree grows here.
On the tree, there are two piles of hawthorn berries.
A black pond is here, filled with putrid water.
A shimmering glow is here, emitting pale, green, light.

Thickets bristling with cruel scimitar-shaped thorns abound in this area, perhaps fed by a putrid, black pool that they cluster densely around. Even the trees are surrounded and covered by these cruel growths, such that a path can scarcely be forged through them in any direction without the risk of some injury. Indeed, many of the sharp spikes are stained black where they have punctured creatures that have previously passed this way.
115208: An elaborate red flower sits within a dark mass of briars.

The ground is rough and uneven here, sloping downwards to the north into an area of increasing gloom and palpable evil. With the thick undergrowth and ever-present darkness, it is hard to see far in any direction, but noises from the nearby gloom indicate the presence of denizens. Some of the rustling is extremely close. Dense thickets of cruel thorns deny movement to the south from here.
115209: Some black, oozing vines reach out from the choked canopy towards you.

The undergrowth in this part of the black forest is almost as thick as the ever-present mesh of branches above. Spiny brambles with long, cruel thorns catch and grasp at all but the most deft of creatures. Navigation through these tangled briars is impossible to the north and scarcely less so to the south, though the forest appears to open up a little elsewhere, especially eastwards where the ground drops away to a steep, rocky slope.
115210: A knotty tree grows here, entangled in a rotten mess of wet shrubbery.

This is one of the more precarious hillsides in Mirkwood. The black mass of trees in every direction make it hard to make out the surrounding land. But it is clear that there are sharp upward gradients in all directions save east, where the ground descends into a deep, black chasm.
115211: Though it slopes slightly downhill to the east, the lie of the land is fairly flat in this area of Mirkwood, but the foetid, evil gloom is as deep and dark as ever. The aged, unyielding trees weave such a dense tangle of branches and leaves up above that it is quite impossible to discern which limb belongs to which tree. Passages to the north, south, and west are blocked equally by impenetrable growth, leaving east the only way out of this oppressive forest.
115212: The black, twisted trees of Mirkwood cluster together in all directions, save north where a steep cliff descends into the deeper darkness of a festering chasm. The ground is sparsely covered with thin, spiky brush and the occasional clump of sickly ivy, with its tattered and discoloured leaves.
115213: The unscalable cliff to the north drops off into a deep, murky chasm, and the air is as thick and foetid as ever. Dark trees are thick with moss, their branches twisted and black. Whispers from an unknown evil fade in and out with the wind, giving a bleak, haunted undertone to the sounds of the forest.
115214:
A copper penny lies on the ground.
On the ground, there are three mushrooms.
A bright red mushroom is growing here.
A knotty tree grows here, entangled in a rotten mess of wet shrubbery.
A gnarly tangle of vines writhes across the ground.
A dreadful hill troll with a skin full of warts is standing here.

The ground slopes sharply downwards to the north, the darkness increasing dramatically in that direction too. Travel is not made any easier by the frequent, jagged boulders in the area, many covered in a stinking, slimy fungus that attracts clouds of huge, black flies. The undergrowth rustles and sways from time to time as something scurries through the dense, rotting plant cover, just out of sight.
115226:
A black pond of water is here.
A large and twisted beast lurks in the rotten pool.
A large, black butterfly is fluttering about erratically.

Even at the bottom of this deep ravine, the dense trees hardly yield. Water drips down from the cliffs above, forming a foul, murky pool among the rocks and trees. A cruel haze hangs above the ground, obscuring the pond, as well as the rest of the low-lying chasm. To the north and south are impassable, sheer cliffs, but the wall to the west is a steep, slimy slope. The land is flattest to the east, but the air gets rapidly heavier with darkness and decay in that direction.
115227:
A cluster of dark green, feathery fronds flourishes in the shade.
A large, black butterfly is fluttering about erratically.

Not only does the rotting and grasping growth of Mirkwood cluster as thick as ever at the bottom of this ravine, but the cliff walls to the north and south are lined with stunted, clawing trees. Their torturous roots bite deeply at the living rock in a constant struggle to support their tenuous positions, an action that slowly breaks the very rock apart.
115228:
A cold shroud of dark grey mist covers the ground.
A large, black butterfly is fluttering about erratically.

This foul, black chasm is at its deepest and darkest point at this location. Finally, even the twisted trees have left the sheer cliff faces alone here, which yields to nothing save some patches of black, rotting moss. A large fault scores diagonally across the southern cliff, and the dark layers of rock to one side are clearly offset against the same strata on the other. A rotten stench emanates from the fault as if the very bowels of the earth are adding their evil effluence to Mirkwood.
115232: The ground is particularly uneven here, even by the treacherous standards of Mirkwood. Though the deep-rooted trees hold on with no trouble, the surface is a constant tangle of loose rocks, ensnaring undergrowth, and hidden potholes. The ground sinks rapidly into stagnant darkness to the west while slimy, laborious slopes climb upward to the east and south. A massive, crumbling black cliff blocks all passage to the north.
115233:
A tangled creeper writhes its shoots between the forest's roots upwards.
A small, dense tangle of roots covers the ground.
A tangled creeper writhes its shoots between the forest's roots upwards.
Massive roots shift uneasily all around you.

Progress through this part of Mirkwood involves scrambling over large slime-covered boulders and pushing through thick, rotting roots. The undergrowth appears to intentionally hamper the traveller, with any headway north or south entirely impossible. The aged trees, primarily dark-leaved oaks and twisted beeches, grow large here, though they are covered in festering sap-warts.
115235: Crossroads at the Foot of Dol Guldur

The Road to Dol Guldur turns here, climbing up the dark, barren hills of black basalt to the east, while winding toward the forest to the south. To the north, a small, craggy trail leads off into the edge of the forest. Passage to the west is impossible, as the slopes descend abruptly into the festering blackness of Mirkwood.
115237: The road seems heavily travelled, worn with the beat of countless hooves and the turns of heavy wagon wheels. The foreboding shadow of Dol Guldur rises to the east, while the road approaches a vast forest to the west. To the south, the land is a mix of hills and trenches. It seems passable, if not for a large pile of broken rock blocking the land between the hills.
115238: A black crow flies low to the ground here, looking for carrion to eat.

The rock-covered trail skirts alongside a deep and long east-west ravine. Twisted trees, as solidly rooted in dark, corrupted soil as ever, crowd thickly down the treacherous slope into the pitch black fissure below. The twisting trail, though narrow here and to the north, appears to widen considerably towards the west. The putrid stench of death and decay closes in on all sides, especially from the fissure below.
115239: Twisting through the trees, this rock-strewn trail appears almost as tortured and maimed as the very plants it seeks to pass by. The ground drops sharply on the western side, descending into a small yet impenetrable gully of thorny brush. Yet elsewhere, despite the ever-looming oppression of Mirkwood's evil, travel is possible without immediate hindrance.
115240: Passing along the dividing line between malice-filled forest and looming rocky hill, a palpable chill haunts this stretch of the trail. It picks a cautious path between the doom-laden boughs of Mirkwood to the west, yet swings sharply to the north to avoid the black, boulder-strewn treachery of the bare Dol Guldur hills immediately east of here. A sickening stench of recent death wafts in from the north.
115241: A black crow flies low to the ground here, looking for carrion to eat.

The foothills of the eerie bluffs of Dol Guldur rise up from the oppressive evil of Mirkwood. The ground hits an almost sheer rock face to the east, yet tumbles precariously downward on the south side into a deep and noxious ravine. The smell of decay and death drifts up from below, while foggy, haunting mists cascade down from the craggy mountainside above, like ancient whispers of tormented souls just on the edge of hearing.
115242: The Road to Dol Guldur continues through the hills here, climbing towards the summit. Black rocks line the road to the north and south, forming inhospitable hills of dark basalt. To the east, the omnious shadow of Dol Guldur looms over the horizon, filling the sky with malevolent energy.
115243: The road through the forest turns here, heading deeper into the depths of the wood. Sharp branches and spines line the edge of the road, ready to punish any who stray from the path. Black roots have completely commandeered some areas, while some sharp, broken rocks make any slip potentially deadly.
115244: The road through the dark forest turns here, twisting around some massive, gnarled trees and a brush-covered hill. The ground around the road is broken, black earth, covered with oozing vines and slick, oily fauna.
115245: The roots of the invasive black trees have erupted here, making the road a bit bumpy. Large thorn bushes line the lane, equipped with nasty looking spines that drip with some dark substance. The road continues to the east and west, just as dark and gloomy as it is here.
115246: The malformed trees, moist and black, encroach on the road from all sides. Mould and disease dominate the foliage, constantly filling the air with a harsh, thick atmosphere. The road appears to continue to the east and west, but the thick trees make it hard to see.
115247: A long, winding road passes through Mirkwood, its path meandering between the enormous trunks of the ancient trees. The road is made of packed dirt with two wide wagon ruts cut into the earth. An oppressive gloom besets the road, the far-reaching branches of the trees form a ceiling above, shielding even the road from the sky above. A large camp is visible to the north, protected by a tall wooden gate, and a spiked palisade.
115248: The trail winds through dense forest, the trees on either side so thick as to make any passage impossible. To the north, a crude timber wall, running east to west, rises up from the ground like an ugly scar on the landscape. The tip of each timber has been sharpened into a vicious point, while the base of the wall has been reinforced with deadly stakes.
115249: A worn-down trail winds its way in between two small hills. The knoll to the west burns with an eerie light, bellowing a thick column of black smoke, and the ash raining down has turned the trail and surrounding ground pitch-black. A huge banner tops the small bluff to the east, showing a hideous black dragon as a warning to invaders. To the south, the trail connects to a dark road winding through the forest, while northwards it meets an ominous gate leading into a filthy camp.
115250:
A large bonfire is burning here.
A sturdy pack horse is standing here.

Surrounded on the west and south by dense forest flatland, this knoll looks out of place. Closer inspection of the soggy ground reveals that it is in fact not made of earth, but of a mixture of ash, bones, gravel, and plain junk. There is a large pile of rotting flesh, trash and refuse that is apparently fuel for a permanently burning bonfire. The fire is massive, spewing forth suffocating smoke and ash like a small volcano.
115251:
A skull is here, spiked to the end of a pole.
A rotten corpse is hanging here.
A half-rotten corpse is hanging here.
An orkish wolf-rider is here, riding a brown wolf.
An orkish wolf-rider is here, riding a brown wolf.

Suffocating black clouds of smoke weave around a broad, grim gate, consisting of two spiked metal wings. The two halves are black metal, held up by two enormous twisted stone pillars on either side. A crude but ghastly image of a dragon has been painted in blood on the front of the gate.
115252: A black banner, painted with a red dragon, hangs from a massive wooden pole.

A small knoll rises up in the forested hills here. In the centre of the knoll, a large cut timber has been fixed into the ground. A black banner with a red painted dragon flies from the timber. The hills rise up in most directions, making passage impossible any way but to the west.
115254: This forest might have once been green and healthy, but terrific storms have uprooted many trees and thrown them around like small twigs. Between the slowly rotting trunks and stumps, new trees have grown until new storms uprooted them too. Hundreds of years and hundreds of storms later this area is a chaotic labyrinth of undergrowth, trees and dead wood.
115256: This forest is ancient, dark, and brooding. The thick crowns of the old trees hold the light at bay. Under the canopy, the forest floor is home to a large variety of shrubs and vines that thrive in the shadows. The branches of the trees are clad in drapes of poisonous-looking fungi and tendril-like vines.
115257: A very narrow ledge among the darkly forested hills allows access to a wooded area to the west. The rolling slopes throw their shadows like massive cloaks over the surrounding woodland. Far to the north-east, a giant spire of black rock juts out of the ground like the blade of a black knife.
115258: Lower Part of the Black Hills

These hills begin to mark the outskirts of Dol Guldur, they are made of the same black basalt as the surrounding hills. The hills to the north and west are higher and appear even more black and shrouded in shadows. These hills are treeless but not barren, full of cracks and crevices, but still they support some hardy shrubs. A dark forest grows at the foot of the hills to the south.
115259: Lower Part of the Black Hills

Black hills rise up in the north, but a larger, cone-shaped hill to the south stretches even higher. There seems to be a path winding up the hill. Along the path, a little hollow gives some shelter. The remains of an old campsite show that others have taken refuge here.
115260: A wide canyon to the west separates this part of the land from a high cliff overlooking the lower and forested hills to the south. This area appears less cracked and eroded than the hills to the north and east, but it is still a treacherous maze of rock formations and steep-walled, debris littered canyons.
115261:
A Morgundul wolf-rider, wielding a lance, is here, riding a brown wolf.
A Morgundul wolf-rider, wielding a lance, is here, riding a brown wolf.

The hills around are dark, bare, and very steep, the slopes to the north and east all but impassable. Far to the north-east a tall rockspire rises above the surrounding hills. A small cleft leads down into a narrow valley covered with loose gravel and larger rocks.
115263:
An orkish wolf-rider is here, riding a brown wolf.
An orkish wolf-rider is here, riding a brown wolf.

Like all of the hills around Dol Guldur, these are also bare. A few thin weeds struggling to find nourishment, but nothing else covers the land. To the north, a huge spire of rock towers above, dominating the landscape. The craggy walls of the spire are rough, but appear impossible to climb.
115264: The hills are made of bare and uneven ground. Steep slopes full of cracks and fissures make the travelling unsafe. No sign of wildlife can be seen around. All is covered by dust and even the poorest weed will not grow here. Far to the north a strange rocky structure raises from the hills.
115265: Lower Part of the Black Hills

These hills are the foot of the black hills which raise sharply to the north and east. The hills are steep and sharp-edged, their shape formed by erosion which leads to many cracks and a ground littered with rocks and stone. The whole area lacks plantlife, as there is no soil left for plants to grow.
115266: These rough, jagged hills are desolate and devoid of vegetation. The stones form bizarre formations of black and grey spear-like spires, rising in groups of tens or dozens. Some are just a few feet high, while others eclipse the tallest trees. They stand in groups, circles, and other patterns that look almost unnatural.
115267: These wooded hills butt up against a taller plateau to the north and east. A thick layer of fertile soil covers what seems to be basalt underneath. In some places bizarre pillars and formations of black rock jut up through the soil and undergrowth. Thick roots snake across the ground, poking up through the forest floor, even so the trees seem to flourish, their dense crowns forming a green ceiling overhead.
115268: These low, wooded hills mark the southern border between Mirkwood and Dol Guldur. Little can be seen through the dense forest of the rising hills to the north, yet the upward slope is undeniable. The slope continues downhill to the west, into a shadowy dell. Most of the trees here are firs, with some birches and hoary old oaks in small pockets.
115269: Nestled between inhospitable black hills is a large dell with steep hillsides to the north and south. Its bottom is densely wooded and the muddy ground is shrouded in everlasting shadow and darkness. There are many rocks and boulders at the foot of the slope, washed down by erosion and landslides.
115270:
A black, thorny bush grows here, enshrouded in a murky gloom.
A knotty tree grows here, entangled in a rotten mess of wet shrubbery.

It seems the evil in hills of Dol Guldur has influenced the trees that grow here at their feet. The trees are grown like old willows with long branches hanging down to the ground, but at a closer look their leaves have more similarity to oaks and their fruit look like fir-cones. The trees seem to move in the darkness and stalk any trespassers.
115271: Hills cover this landscape , and their size grow towards the west. Every rise, valley, and hilltop is covered with dark, brooding trees, most of them fir or birch. The hills here are dwarfed by a plateau, a higher part of Dol Guldur, which towers to the north and northwest.
115272: Forest covers these slopes, conspiring with the plateau to the north to keep these woods in permanent shadows. The slopes ascend gently towards the west, slowly climbing towards higher heights. The trees are gnarled and ancient, some of them true behemoths that must have been standing here since the the time of the last alliance.
115273: Dark and Dreary Corner of Mirkwood

A black, thorny bush grows here, enshrouded in a murky gloom.
The wicked undergrowth rustles malevolently, shifting and widening.

The trees of this forest are towering, ancient giants. Many of them are gnarled and twisted. Large roots protrude through the thick layer of rotting leaves on the ground. Aside from the trees, little grows here except and the fungi and mushrooms that draw their nourishment from the tree's trunks, as little light finds its way through the canopy.
115274: These shrub-covered fields lie in the shadow of a high plateau to the west, and that shade probably kept the trees of Mirkwood to the east from creeping all the way up to the foot of the plateau. The vegetation consists of thorn-covered bushes and sturdy-looking shrubs.
115275: This thicket-covered stretch of land lies between denser undergrowth to the north, the dark depths of Mirkwood to the east, and a plateau to the west. The ground is overgrown with thorny thickets cut with wide paths. Most of the bushes have long, nasty thorns pointing every which way.
115276: The uneven terrain here at the foot of the high plateau to the west is entirely covered by immense thickets. Thousands of shrubs grow in such proximity that to each other that the whole thicket appears like one single plant. A few paths exist where a mount or traveller can make their way through.
115277: The slopes of this hill are covered by a dark forest. The trees are black oaks with gnarled roots and twisted trunks, and tall, dark alders. The undergrowth of strangling vines and long-thorned bushes has been haphazardly crushed and torn up, root and all, as if something very large and impatient smashed through.
115278:
A knotty tree grows here, entangled in a rotten mess of wet shrubbery.
A knotty tree grows here, entangled in a rotten mess of wet shrubbery.

Raised over the surrounding dark forest, this hill might once have been lit by the warm sun. But now the black oaks have stolen most of the light with their dense cover of dark leaves. The hill's summit and slopes are covered by a layer of dead leaves and several large, round boulders.
115279: Brush in the Shadow of a Plateau

This brush-covered area is squeezed between dark woods to the north and a steep plateau to the south. The ground is very stony, but the poor soil seems adequate for a variety of plantlife consisting of brown, tough shrubs, wild grass, as well as some larger thornbushes.
115280: Brush between Mirkwood and a Plateau

This patch of brushland is squeezed between the forest to the north and a plateau to the south. The plantlife consists mainly of low, brown shrubs and long, thorny vines that creep across the ground for lack of trees to climb. The plateau to the south overshadows these lower lands, casting them into gloom for much of the day.
115281: This area has been clear-cut in the past. Old, rotten stumps can be seen dotting the landscape. No one cleared the underbrush, which, liberated from the suffocating ceiling of leaves, has grown to an immense height and density. The brush is bordered by dense, shadowy forest to the north and south.
115282: Some black, oozing vines reach out from the choked canopy towards you.

The ground of this dark forest is wet and muddy, resembling more the surface of a swamp than a forest floor. The smell of rot is everywhere and the air trapped under the cover of the dark crowns is barely breathable. A steep cliff to the south is slowly eroding away, the ground beneath littered with small crumbling rocks.
115283: The forest canopy closes in here, leaving the dark shadow of a moonless night or a tunnel deep under the mountains. The trees are bend and crooked, and their roots seem to grown together. There is no undergrowth except of a few rings of fungi, which look poisonous upon closer look. The almost vertical cliffs of dark hills form the southern border of the forest which continues east.
115284: The hills narrow here between a high wall of black rock to the north and a flat plateau to the southeast. The northern wall forms the buttress of a strange spire of rock which stretches straight up out of the ground. To the east, the hills give way to dark, twisted forest.
115285:
A big, nasty vulture is sitting here, protecting its nest.
A big, nasty vulture is sitting here, protecting its nest.

This is without a doubt the highest peak southeast of Dol Guldur. Shaped like a perfect cone, it towers over the Forest of Mirkwood, with slopes that are steep and brittle. The black mountain consists of a very soft, grainy stone and some harder, glassy stones which are strewn over the flanks. An excellent view is afforded over the whole surrounding area.
115286: Blood and gore is spattered everywhere, both on the trail itself and across the surrounding plant-growth. A terrible fight has occurred here recently, though the nature of the loser cannot be determined. Globs of flesh, covered in flies, semi-dried pools of blood, and some fragments of bone litter the rocky path, yet there is no sign of a carcass.
115287:
A large pile of boulders is sitting here, probably debris from a rockslide.
A Morgundul orc guard stands here, looking about nervously.
A Morgundul orc guard stands here, looking about nervously.
A Morgundul orc guard stands here, looking about nervously.

Ascending above the treetops of Mirkwood, the usual twisted tangle of dark vegetation gives way reluctantly to more open lands, though the fractured black rock and cinder that is strewn across the landscape lends itself no more to travelling than the dim forest of Mirkwood. Sharp, ruthless inclines to the east and south block further progress upwards, and torturous scree-descents to the north and west are the only ways down.
115288: A black crow flies low to the ground here, looking for carrion to eat.

There is blood on this trail. Dark streaks are smeared all across the ground, and the undergrowth has been pushed down roughly. Whatever caused the gore was clearly not hindered by the thick, thorny brambles in the least. The faint path heads northwards into the gloom, and, along with the smears, to the west. A rough scree slope climbs sharply upwards a little to the south, leading into the grim, haze-shrouded hills of Dol Guldur.
115289: A sprawling green bush of stinging nettle grows here.

The land is slowly rising in the south, where the grey hills of Dol Guldur are. The soil of this slope does not support larger trees, but gives enough nourishment for the many nettle plants that grow between the sharp-edged boulders and rocks.
115290: Crude looking hills with many small cliffs, cracks, crevices and stone covered slopes mark this land. The whole area looks like it was carved by a crazed giant. The trees are sparse and provide no shadows, but the hills are not entirely lacking in vegetation. In some soil filled cracks thorny bushes and stinging nettles have stubbornly taken root.
115291: A large marmot is here, scurrying in between the rocks.

This plateau in the hills is covered by piles and piles of slag and debris, likely the remnants of an old mine. A long time seems to have passed since it was last used. Between the rocks, signs of life are bursting forth in the form of saplings and small shrubs. But the mining waste gives almost no nourishment so the plants are thin and sickly, though still thorny.
115292:
A large thorny branched shrub is growing here.
On the shrub, there are three piles of blackberries.

Dense vegetation covers the hills of this area, but the plants are brown and look sickly. Most of them are rooted in small cracks on the stony ground. There are tiny tunnels through the thick scrub and small pieces of fur collected on occasional longer thorns. To the south the hills become more stony, more cracked and even more inhospitable.
115294:
A mountain ibex is jumping from rock to rock.
A mountain ibex is jumping from rock to rock.
A mountain ibex is jumping from rock to rock.

Obviously someone mined for something here a long time ago. There are several old holes in the ground, although most of them crumbled a long time ago. Of the heavy wooden frames that stand guard over them, only rotten, ivy-covered remnants can be seen. One dark opening, a black maw in the hillside, has survived the ravages of time better than most.
115295:
A large thorny branched shrub is growing here.
On the shrub, there are three piles of blackberries.

The grey, almost black, hills of basalt are covered with ash. Small veins are visible in the rock, showing up in the red colour of rust that indicates a high degree of iron. Between the hills to the west there are ruined clusters of ancient buildings which look like two old and long abandoned mines.
115296: In the Shadow of the Fortress

A mountain ibex is jumping from rock to rock.
A mountain ibex is jumping from rock to rock.
A mountain ibex is jumping from rock to rock.

The vast shadow of Dol Guldur's mighty fortress looms ever present over these hills. The stronghold stands ever resolute, ignoring the ravages of time. Its malevolent presence emits an aura of brutal enmity, buffeted by the dark, twisted power of nearby Mirkwood. A stone wall, black as coal, rises up from the hills to the west to form the massive foundation of the baleful citadel.
115297: The mine to the north has produced massive quantities of waste. These hills are largely a result of heavy mining for many years. Climbing the hills is difficult because they are made of the loose slag from the mine.
