A thick wooden door in the eastern wall leads to the camp, while a rough arched opening to the south gives access to a wide yard.
115538:
A small oaken table has been set here.
A Morgundul orc guard is here, relaxing off-duty.
A Morgundul orc guard is sleeping here.
A Morgundul orc guard is here, relaxing off-duty.
A Morgundul orc guard is sleeping here.

Rows of crude slabs covered in furs line the walls of this massive hall. Near the back, small closable compartments are available for more demanding orcs, while lowly snagas can just rest on the bare, filthy floor. There are no windows, but the chaotic noise of the camp still penetrates the thin walls.
115539:
An ancient black altar stands in the centre of the room.
On the altar, there is a candlestick.
A dreadful warg, covered in matted fur, sniffs the ground for prey.
A bald orc is standing here, silent and focused.
A dreadful warg, covered in matted fur, sniffs the ground for prey.
A bald orc is standing here, silent and focused.
An Uruk-rogtar of the Morgundul is on patrol here.
An Uruk-rogtar of the Morgundul is on patrol here.
A harsh orkish veteran is here, heavily scarred but ready to fight.

Despite the noisy activity outside, this circular, windowless hut is very quiet. A round table is placed around the central supporting pole, covered with jars and pots containing unknown body parts. Strange-looking necklaces and medallions hang from a small altar of worship at the northern end, and every surface is dotted with smoky candles, their fumes escaping through a hole in the tip of the cone-shaped ceiling.
115540: The remains of some stairs lie here in a useless pile.

This appears to be one end of a collapsing passage. The tunnel continues to the south. The roof appears to be on the verge of collapsing further. Some water drips slowly down from the decaying roof, forming small puddles that dot the ground like freckles.
115541: A tiny spider is here, eating a tiny bug.

Time and shoddy construction have brought this passage to the brink of collapse. Several ceiling planks have already broken under the strain of the earth above. Clots of fresh mud litter the floor in small piles. The poles holding back the wall have started to lean inwards as the walls close in. The tunnel seems sturdier to the south.
115542: A narrow passage winds its way through the earth here. While to the north several cave-ins indicate instability in the tunnel, this section looks solid and well-maintained. Thick, wooden support pillars look as if they have been installed recently.
115543: This cellar might have been in use at some point, but it is now abandoned. The floor is a mess of upended tables with a thick coating of dust on every surface. A wooden stair has been built against the stone wall, leading up to a hole in the ceiling. A narrow passage leads north.
115544:
An Uruk-rogtar of the Morgundul is on patrol here.
A harsh orkish veteran is here, heavily scarred but ready to fight.

Several benches set around this room allow the prison guards respite while they wait to thwart any escape or rescue attempts. A thick metal door with an iron-barred window is set into the southern wall. The tunnel continues to the west and east.
115545: This narrow passage was dug in a hurry, judging by the shoddy workmanship. The low ceiling consists of wooden planks, bulging under the weight of the earth above, while mouldy and rotten wall panels barely keep the tunnel from caving in.
115546:
A grouchy uruk is here, lashing his whip.
An enslaved troll is here, eager to unleash its rage upon you.
An enslaved troll is here, eager to unleash its rage upon you.

Rusted chains are still attached to the walls, but this underground prison cannot be used to lock up anyone. The metal-barred door that would normally block the doorway to the north has been ripped off its hinges. It now lies useless on the floor amidst the rubble and loose earth. Large roots stick out of the ceiling and walls, some dangling menacingly in the dusty air.
115556: A humanoid skull is hanging on the wall.

This end of the guardhouse is dominated by a dark hole in the middle of the floor. Some old looking stairs lead down into the hole, though they seem barely able to hold together. A musty smell emanates from below, evidently there is not much ventilation down there.
115557:
A small oaken table has been set here.
On the table, there are three tiny pieces of raw meat.
Some ugly blow-flies are buzzing around here.

This room seems to be well-used judging from the filth and garbage laying about. In the centre of the room, a rough table made of a couple of wooden planks surrounded by some stumps of wood serves as the only furniture. On the centre of the table, the remains of a pig are left forgotten. It seems to attract a lot of flies.
115558:
A wooden chest stands in the corner.
A weapons rack stands against the wall.
In the rack are two black waraxes, a wooden club, and a longspear.

This is a typical, if a bit dirty, guardhouse. Against the southern wall a couple of weapon racks provide easy access to arms should the need arise. The building has more rooms to the west but the wooden walls and lack of windows make them difficult to see.
115560:
A sturdy peg for hanging armour from is on the wall.
On the peg, there are a large wooden shield, a chain mail coif, and a pair of chain mail gloves.
A weapons rack stands against the wall.
In the rack are a mace, a cudgel, and a cutlass.

Crude wooden beams hold up the walls of this underground storage room. The walls are lined with dozens of weapon racks and armour stands. Many of the racks are locked with chains. The equipment appears of good quality, but judging by the dust that has settled on the floor, this room is not visited often.
115563: The trail here is rough, the poisoned foliage cleared just enough to resemble a path. To the south, the trail leads into a well-worn road. The trail continues to the east, but above the treetops beyond the trail the massive hill of Dol Guldur stretches up into sky, crowned by the monstrous fortress of the same dreaded name.
115567: A troll mother roams the cave, malformed and muttering about her sons.

Refuse covers the filthy floor of this gloomy cave has been dug out of the black rock. A huge slab of stone has been roughly placed on the dirty floor of the cave that slows a draft. The trunk of a large pine tree has been placed on the western half of the cave to give some privacy to its inhabitants.
115582: Towards the south, there seems to be a little more space between branch and bough, and less constricting are the twisted vines that tie the corrupted wood together in this darkened tapestry. Still, there is no natural light, and an oppressive blanket of darkness hangs heavily upon all it touches. To the north, the darkness seems to thicken, smothering all it touches. The faint recesses of old cobblestones laid together is barely visible underfoot.
115583: The ground here is covered in a thick blanket of rot and decay. Spindly, thin roots weave together clumps of rotten leaves and moss, binding them together in a matted layer. Towards the west, the ground begins to become much soggier, with sickly dew dripping from leaf and stem. Eastward, the twisted flora almost appears to form a tunnel, as if this was once a path of sorts. To the north, a similar sight is seen; unwelcoming, twisted and dank lies the surroundings.
115589: A noxious film of dank-green ooze pocks the standing, stagnant water that encompasses everything here. Putrid gas bubbles rise towards the surface, releasing an acrid and malodorous stench as they pop, droplets slowly burning anything they touch. Gnarled, blackened roots, thick with a dark, putrid ooze, break through the blanket of rot and decay upon the ground, reaching towards the virulent bog of poison as if to drink from the corruption that permeates this place.
115590: To the west, the bent and mangled flora seems to be slightly less constricting, with jagged, broken cobblestones barely visible under the matted rot and decay. Twisted vines, blackened by corruption, hang down as if to ensnare unwary travellers. To the north, elongated branches wrapped in darkened vines grasp towards the south.
115591:
A black, thorny bush grows here, enshrouded in a murky gloom.
Pitch-black water with a strange smell has collected here.

To the north, an impenetrable wall of vines, branches, and trunks form a dense wall of contorted plant life. Towards the west, an almost identical sight awaits. To the south, the oppressive growth of twisting, interwoven branches and vines seems to lessen, almost parting as if it was once an established path, many long, forgotten years ago.
115592: Thick, massive trunks grow tightly together here in all directions, most notably to the east, where a sickly moss begins to hang heavily the further north and east one ventures. Blackened lichen and moss drape from branch to branch, as if the trees are trying to claim any space that could be used for anything other than their own dark intent.
115593: Towards the west, a few small openings in the matted layer of decay that lays heavily upon the ground reveal the once-polished stones of a long-forgotten pathway. What were once healthy trees, evenly spaced and uniform in plantation, suggests this was once a meticulously tended grove, likely of Elven origin. Whatever beauty once lived here, now only death and decay flourishes. What were once elegant, sprawling branches, are now a twisted visage of gnarled mortification.
115594:
A pile of coins is here.
A shrouded figure stands here, hidden in the grove's dark shadows ( glowing ).

Countless gnarled vines and decomposing earthen sinew form a thick blanket upon the ground here. From within this matted layer of rot and decay, menacing vines, heavy with barb and thorn, reach from within to wrap themselves around the dark trunks of these once-proud trees. The thorns, thick with many smaller protrusions, stab at the bark of these towering and sickly trees, causing thick lesions from which a black, tarry substance oozes.
115595:
A black, thorny bush grows here, enshrouded in a murky gloom.
On the bush, there is a black, corrupted flower.

It appears as if evil incarnate itself willed the surrounding area into being. What were once tall, proud mallorn trees, are now blackened, corrupt pillars climbing upwards a great distance. Extending from these trunks are gnarled, ooze-covered boughs and branches, reaching down towards the blackened and twisted forest floor. From these hang blankets of sickly brown lichen and corrupted earthen sinew, as if the trees themselves were ominous puppeteers ready to drape their dark curtains closed upon trespassers.
115596: The evenly-spaced trunks of what once resembled trees now appear to be nothing more than dark, corrupted monoliths of black-rot and malice. Much like rest of this gnarled place, a thick, matted blanket of thorny vines and decomposing plant matter covers the ground in a thick layer. Massive, low-hanging boughs droop towards the ground despite their size; heavy is the corruption that permeates the sheets of putrid decay hanging from them. Blackened vines with elongated thorns, secreting a putrid, noxious ooze, thrust upwards to wrap themselves around the rot-laden branches, slowly pulling them downwards as if arms being bound by an unforgiving rope.
115597: Towards the north, the gnarled mass of vines and darkened boughs, heavy with a rank layer of rot, seem to part ever slightly as if a path once existed in that direction. The ground appears as if it was caught in a roiling, violent upheaval, as the ground is comprised of deep, muck-laden holes, next to which a prominent mound thrusts upwards.
115598: Towards the west, the decay-stricken ground begins to gradually become uneven, seemingly the cause of numerous sinkholes. Several of these low-lying holes are filled with a dark, stagnant water. To the north and west, the trees grow tightly together, with thorny vines weaving between them preventing travel in those directions. The familiar draping blankets of blackened rot hang in abundance from the limbs and branches of the once-mighty, now-corrupted trees here. Several thick branches are snapped and twisted from the sheer volume of death and decay that has fallen down from the higher branches.
115599: The ground here slopes considerably downward from all sides, which are coated in a slick and sickly layer of dark coloured lichen, forming a deep depression in the earth. The bottom of this hole contains a thick layer of interwoven vines, roots, and other decomposing plant matter, held aloft by several inches of stagnant, murky water. From the sides of the hole spring horn-like thorns, tripping with a dark, smelly substance that oozes downwards.
115605: A wooden chest stands in the corner.

This is a small room, more like a closet. The walls are bare wood, and the floor is made of sturdy planks. There are some spider webs hanging in the roof and some dust and dirt has accumulated on the floor. The air is a bit musty. A few wrinkled papers and some pieces of broken pens lie about.
115606: A large stone chest is here.

Many crates and pegs fill up this small room. Many of them are filled with various weapons, although some appear to be broken and beyond use. No windows are to be found, the only visible exit lies to the north, where an oaken door can be seen. The room is quite musty, hinting it may not be visited often.
115614:
A small oaken table has been set here.
On the table, there is a cracked leather journal.

The rock has been hollowed here to form a small bedroom. A wooden desk is set near the eastern wall. It is covered with illegible notes and crude anatomical sketches of what appear to be trolls. The bed is human-sized, with coarse woolen coverings.
115615:
A sturdy trained horse is standing here.
A tall man, clad in black robes, pierces the room with his malevolent gaze (glowing).

This sanctum has a staircase running through it, leading both up and down. Dark worship and dreadful experiments take place here, judging from the table covered with scribbled notes in the dark tongue of Mordor, and old books bound in strange leathers. There are phials and bottles full of foul fluids and others full of strange, swirling mists. Another desk has chains at the ends and a deep channel to collect blood. An object much like an altar stands along one wall, surrounded by a veil of darkness that never seems to dissipate or disperse.
115616: The corpse of the magus is lying here.

A wide stairwell rises through a cone of black rock. The wide steps are simply crafted but functional. Every dozen or so steps, there is a platform where the stairs turn and leads further up and down. Dark shadows play on the walls, as if cast by strange shapes that are not really here.
115617: Wide stone steps rise in a spiral on the inside of a cone of black rock. A solid hatch has been placed at an opening at the very top of the stairs, blocking access to whatever is hidden above. The walls are pitted and rough. They appear natural as opposed to the steps which were clearly carved to fashion a staircase.
115618: A statue of a troll stands here, its fists grasping a thick chain.

A platform has been crafted atop the rockspire. Brute force has been used to clear away the worst outcroppings, creating a fairly flat, rocky surface. The only entrance, for any creature lacking wings, seems to be the hatch near the centre of the platform. Several very large iron rings have been embedded into the platform.
115620:
A skeleton of some humanoid lies in the dust.
A weary woman stands here, looking miserable.
A prisoner is sitting here, looking at you with sad eyes.

A rotting stench hangs in this cramped prison cell. Chains are attached to the walls and some are still locked to long deceased prisoners. Some have started to decay, becoming food for a variety of crawly creatures. Others are bare bone, having already served as nourishment. The skeletons show signs of torture. Many have broken bones or missing fingers, one is even missing the lower half of its jaw. A sturdy barred door is set into the northern wall.
115621:
A large bulletin board, entitled "Thieves' Guild", is mounted here.
A weapons rack stands against the wall.
In the rack are a shortbow, a quiver, and three arrows.
An elven hunter is here, ready to teach.
A sturdy pack horse is standing here.

The masters at this school teach the arts of stealth to those who would oppose the forces of darkness. In better times, such skills were used to hunt game for the many elven celebrations. The revelry is now a thing of the past, and the hunters' quarry changed. More often than not, the hunters become the prey. The guilds skills are much in demand even by the most righteous of warriors. A path in the north opens between two large bushes.
115631:
A large bulletin board, entitled "Free Peoples' Chronicles", is mounted here.
A huge clock is standing here.
A white-painted bench is here.
An elven bartender watches the sea while cleaning a glass.

A lit room, lined with round windows, opens up from its entrance on the wharf as the building expands onto a pier reaching into the harbour. White benches and tables sit throughout the building, allowing customers to see ships coming and going as they relax. A marble stair connects to the inn's reception above.
115632:
A white-painted counter sits near an open window overlooking the sea.
On the counter, there are two loaves of white bread and a flagon.
An elven innkeeper stands behind the counter, ready to attend his guests.

Large windows line the walls of the inn, rewarding guests with a breathtaking view of the harbour. The inn was built on a pier and expands from the wharf into the sea where waves pass underneath it. A few open windows let in a salty, relaxing breeze which flows down the hall into a corridor of cosy rooms.
115658:
A well-crafted white fountain is here, water pouring forth from it.
A white-painted bench is here.
An Elven steward stands here, watching over the household.

Eight broad pillars of pale marble form a private octagon-shaped sanctuary offering relaxation from the hasty world outside. Twinned, silvery linings are attached around the top of the pillars, connecting them with each other. Twisting above the polished floor of stone, grey-green vines ensnare the strings, and like a roof they dazzle with their flowery shrubs as a few lit candles illuminate the surroundings. The sparkling noise of the fountain in the centre of the room seems to diminish as a disappearing shadow uncovers a painting of a black, grandeur ship that sails under the flag of Numenor. The royal bloodline, daubed in gold, spans vertically beneath the shimmering blue surface of water.
115659: A humble man stands here, ready to help you with your things.

Darkness fills the room, only broken by the sputtering light of dying torches. The room is circular, with many oaken shelves nailed haphazardly throughout. On the shelves, there are various magical instruments as well as some unidentified iron-shod weights. In the dead centre of the room, there is an old and abused couch, surrounded by books, drawings, and mysteriously humming objects.
115664: A narrow crevice cuts a path through black and dark grey rocks. The walls press in on the narrow passageway on both sides as the crevice tunnels through the rock towards the north. Jagged rocks provide plenty of steps leading up towards an opening in the rock.
115665: The cave cuts through jagged black and dark grey rocks. The walls press in on the narrow passageway leaving very little room to manoeuvre. The floor tilts at an unsettling angle, the evidence of the mountain's distant past, eons ago when the earth shifted and tore open this gash in the rock.
115666: Broken chunks of dark, almost black rock line the walls in this area. On the edges of the jagged chunks, a lighter grey rock can be seen. A faint draught of air can be felt coming from the north and the east, indicating that there might be more to this cavern behind the fallen rocks. A deep breach in the rock below is where most of the fallen rocks have ended up.
115667: This area of the cave is comprised of vertical blocks of dark stone of various heights. At first glance it looks like someone must have carved them, but upon closer inspection it seems natural. Some of the columns along the wall reach from floor to ceiling, but in the middle of the cave the broken columns hang from above.
115668: Naturally formed vertical columns of coal-black stone have broken off the wall in such a way that it looks like it would be possible to climb up them to a higher part of the cavern. The floor of the cave is littered with the fallen chunks of the stone columns that have broken and crumbled. Stacks of crumbled rocks are also resting against the walls.
115669: The naturally formed pillars of dark rock seem to form steps leading down into the darkness below. It looks like it would be possible to climb down in that direction. The sound of dripping water can be heard echoing off the walls of the cavern from down below. The jagged tunnel continues off to the east from here as well.
115670: The roof of the cave slants off to the north, and the floor slants off to the south here making it rather difficult to walk through this area. The walls of the cave crumble when touched, and rocks and dust have accumulated on the ground. The faint sound of dripping can be heard from the west, and the cave continues off into the darkness to the east.
115671: Large chunks of dark grey basalt stone are spaced in such a way that it looks like it might be possible to climb down into the darkness below. The cavern continues off to the west at a tilted angle. On the northern wall of the cave, there is a long crack in the stone that is about twenty feet long. Probably the remnants of a shift in the stone from thousands of years ago.
115672:
Dripping water has settled into a pool of crystal clear water.
A huge, hungry-looking rat is here.

Stalactites hang from the ceiling like thousands of stone spikes, and the constant dripping has formed crystal clear pools of water on the ground. The floor is also covered with stalagmites reaching upwards towards the roof of the cave causing the footing to be quite treacherous. Some of the stone has managed to connect from floor to ceiling, creating glistening columns.
115673: It isn't possible to see very far ahead in the cavern due to the twists and turns within the passage. The massive mountain above presses down heavily on this winding gap, threatening to crush anyone or anything foolish enough to enter the narrow space. It looks like the cave opens up a little more to the north.
115674: This area of the cave opens up a bit and branches off in three directions. To the south a narrow passageway can be seen winding off into the darkness, and that same fissure in the rock continues off to the east. It also looks like it might be possible to clamber up the stones here to a higher level of the cave above as well.
115676: Eastern End of a Winding Passage
A noticeable crack runs down one of the walls.

The narrow fissure in the rock has apparently come to a dead end here. The gap narrows down so small to the east that only the smallest creature could continue. Whatever earth-shattering force created this rift in the stone so many millennia ago didn't have the strength to tear any further in that direction.
115677: This area is strewn with broken rocks of various sizes that have fallen from above. Some of the rubble here isn't much larger than coarse sand, while other chunks are as big as a boulder. It might be possible to dig through some of the stones laying about, but it doesn't seem like there is much to find other than more rocks.
115678:
A small blotchy mushroom grows here.
On the ground, there are three mushrooms.

This is a much smaller cave that has been naturally carved adjacent to a larger network of caves and caverns. The walls of the cave are slick with moisture and it seems hopeless to try to climb them. Green and black fungi grow all along the floors at the bases of the walls. In some spots, huge mushrooms grow in flourishing clusters.
115679:
A pool of water has formed here, slowly flowing into the cracks.
You see two green slime moulds on the ground.
A huge, hungry-looking rat is here.
A huge, hungry-looking rat is here.

A barely perceptible flow of crystal clear water streams slowly from pool to pool in a southerly direction. The water appears to flush down into the cracks in the rock where it is no longer possible to follow. The walls, ceiling, and floor all glisten and sparkle with moisture. The stalactites and stalagmites occur in a variety of colours from dark grey to brown, and some are even a nearly white colour.
115680: The tunnel runs east to west, and passage is quite easy in either direction. The walls are tall, and made of a smooth grey basalt rock. The floor is dusty, but smooth and level. Strange noises can be heard echoing throughout the tunnel and the direction of the sounds is indiscernible.
115681: The tunnel continues to the east or to the west, into the vast darkness in either direction. Passage here is easy, with the floor being smooth, level, and wide. The grey basalt walls rise high before curving into a smooth grey ceiling above. Echoes of strange sounds can be heard coming from both directions.
115682: The long tunnel continues to the east and to the west here. The walls are made of smooth, grey basalt rock that climb into the darkness above. The occasional drop of water can be heard dripping from the smooth, curved ceiling above. The air is stale and odourless, and strange sounds can be heard echoing all about.
115683:
A giant rat patters against you, squeaking maliciously.
A large black bat flitters near you.

Three tunnels meet here, but the darkness makes it difficult to see where each leads. A very slight breeze seems to be coming from the north, moving toward a large opening to the west, and a dank, stagnant, musty smell emanates from below.
115684: A hideous mottled spider advances with startling speed.

Warm air from the north meets cooler air from the south, creating a surprisingly strong wind through this narrow tunnel. As the wind passes around corners and over irregularities in the wall, it whistles and howls in various pitches, and from several locations, creating a confusing cacophony of sounds.
115685: A large black bat flitters near you.

A large opening from above narrows to a tiny entrance to the north. A foul smell permeates the air, musty, and rank with decay. The slope upward is slick, the smooth stone wet with condensation. Faint scratching sounds can be heard echoing from the long, narrow tunnel to the north.
115686: Stripes and swirls of multicoloured, iridescent obsidian cover every surface of this huge cavern. Condensation from the humid air glistens on the surface of the walls, which further magnifies the dazzling effect of the polychromatic stone.
115687: A menacing mottled spider is here, lurking in the shadows (hidden).

Shards of razor-sharp, jet-black obsidian litter the ground. Large knife-like outcroppings from the walls and ceiling create a treacherous environment. Manoeuvring through this cave will require some skill, and it is unlikely that one could make it through completely unharmed. A small opening has been cut into the wall to the south.
115688:
An old, broken crafting table has been abandoned here.
On the table, there is a large sack.
A large black bat flitters near you.
A large black bat flitters near you.

A small, broken table sits in the corner of this small cave. Bone, antler, and wooden hammers of various sizes and shapes litter the floor, covered in dust. Mounds of sharp obsidian scraps are piled around the table, and rough, unfinished arrowheads, spearheads, and knives are scattered around.
115689: The floor of this cave opens into a large crater that seems to have been formed when the surface collapsed above a large void below. The edges of the pit curve steeply downward, creating a treacherous situation for the unwary. Faint, nearly imperceptible, sounds echo from below, indicating that someone, or something, is moving around in the depths.
115690: This strange little nook has been cut neatly from the surrounding obsidian. The walls, floor, and ceiling are perfectly square and plumb, forming a neat little cubicle. It took master craftsmanship and substantial effort to create this tiny space, but to what end the artist was working is utterly unclear.
115691: A spiralling tunnel of black basalt was formed centuries ago by molten rock flowing from a now extinct volcanic vent. Close examination reveals that this chute was formed when the top, sides, and bottom of the flow cooled and solidified, after which the insides of the lava river continued to flow, emptying out the present cave. The surfaces of the surrounding rock are rippled, giving the impression that the rock is still flowing freely.
115692: A large black bat flitters near you.

Ripples of black basalt seem to flow out of the western wall of this cave, the frozen remnants of a spring of molten rock. Heat emanates from the rock, indicating that a new spring could form at any moment. There is a strong smell of sulphur in the air.
115693:
A hideous mottled spider advances with startling speed.
A spiderling skitters about, looking for small prey to devour.

Dust and fragments of silk float heavily in the musty air. A tangle of cobwebs extends to the east, continuing out of sight in that direction, in sharp contrast to the smooth basalt formations in the rest of this cave. An opening in the hard stone leads upward into total darkness.
115694:
A menacing mottled spider is here, lurking in the shadows (hidden).
A hideous mottled spider advances with startling speed.
A spiderling skitters about, looking for small prey to devour.

A small hole leads down, barely large enough to allow passage to whatever lies below. Sticky cobwebs hang from the ceiling and walls, choking off passageways to the north and west. A thick, musty smell fills the air, making it difficult to breathe.
115695: Something has hollowed out the surrounding stone into a small, spherical chamber. The ground is littered with human and animal bones, empty egg sacs, and moulted spider skins. This appears to be a lair where young spiders are reared until they grow to adulthood. Based on the size of several of the moulted skins, the adult spiders that leave here are quite large.
115696:
An empty exoskeleton of a large spider is lying here.
A spiderling skitters about, looking for small prey to devour.

A long corridor extends to the west from this shallow recess. The only other exit is a small opening in the ceiling. Long, thin strands of sticky web float listlessly in the still air. The air has a dank, earthy smell, faintly resembling rotting compost.
115697: A small centipede is here scurrying about.

Several passages converge at a small chamber. The low ceiling makes it difficult to manoeuvre, and there is some sticky substance on the floors and walls. There are sounds coming from all directions, but they are muted by the thick, velvety material covering the walls. The air is still, with a thick, musty odour.
115698: A large hole opens below, from which odious fumes emanate. Rustling sounds from that direction echo and amplify off of the walls and ceiling. Venturing downward seems imprudent. With some caution, it is possible to travel along the edges of the hole without falling in.
115699: A menacing mottled spider is here, lurking in the shadows (hidden).

Rocks and debris have fallen, apparently from a massive cave-in long ago. The way is blocked in all directions except a small opening to the west. The thick dust on the floor seems to indicate that this small space is seldom visited, perhaps with good reason.
115700: The ceiling extends dozens of feet above, as this tunnel opens into a large grotto. Cobwebs stretch across every corner, spanning numerous stalactites above. The rubble on the ground bears evidence to the instability of the stalactites, making it a questionable choice to linger here below them.
115701: A small centipede is here scurrying about.

Black walls with tiny specks of glistening crystals form a curving corridor. Fine filaments float in the air, making it difficult to see, and the air is stale and musty. Scratch marks on the floor suggest that creatures frequently use this passage.
115702: Tunnels from several directions converge here. The grey stone is strangely free of the sticky threads that are prevalent in adjacent areas. The air is slightly stale, but is free from any real odour. This place looks like it could be a gathering or meeting place of some sort, which might explain the lack of any encumbrances.
115704: A natural tunnel extends north-south, creating an easily travelled passageway. A small hole leads down into the darkness, and muffled sounds can be heard from that direction. In spite of the small size of the opening, the worn edges and scratch marks indicate frequent travel to and from below.
115705:
A desiccated corpse hangs in a tangled web, its lifeblood completely drained.
A spiderling skitters about, looking for small prey to devour.
A spiderling skitters about, looking for small prey to devour.
A mottled spider crouches in the shadows, watching over her young.
A tiny spider is here, eating a tiny bug.
A tiny spider is here, eating a tiny bug.
A menacing mottled spider is here, lurking in the shadows.

Empty cocoons, torn clothing, broken and rusted weapons, piles of bones, and other inedible trash lie in piles all over the floor of this room. A thick reddish-brown substance, likely coagulating blood, covers the floor. Lingering would likely result in becoming a meal for whatever seems to regularly dine here.
115706:
A spiderling skitters about, looking for small prey to devour.
A spiderling skitters about, looking for small prey to devour.
A mottled spider crouches in the shadows, watching over her young.

Broken crates and barrels, torn and dented armour, broken weapons, and other rubbish lie in haphazard heaps on the floor of this cave. There is enough equipment and supplies here to outfit a small army if any of it were fit for use, a testament to the many souls who have braved these labyrinths, never to return.
115709:
A desiccated corpse hangs in a tangled web, its lifeblood completely drained.
A spiderling skitters about, looking for small prey to devour.
A spiderling skitters about, looking for small prey to devour.
A spiderling skitters about, looking for small prey to devour.
A spiderling skitters about, looking for small prey to devour.
A spiderling skitters about, looking for small prey to devour.
A spiderling skitters about, looking for small prey to devour.
A mottled spider crouches in the shadows, watching over her young.
A mottled spider crouches in the shadows, watching over her young.

A deep depression has been burrowed in the ground, clearly home to some creature, or possibly a whole family of them. Countless bones and skulls litter the floor. Whatever lives here clearly has a voracious appetite. The floor and walls are covered with a foul-smelling, mud-like substance, possibly excrement or other body fluid from the creatures that dwell here.
115710:
A hideous mottled spider advances with startling speed.
A spiderling skitters about, looking for small prey to devour.

A long, narrow corridor runs east-west here. The air is cool and damp, with a light, foul-smelling breeze coming from the west. There are several large cavities along the floor, some possibly large enough to enter, and most covered with intricate webs of sticky silk.
115711: A spiderling skitters about, looking for small prey to devour.

Warm, damp air is flowing steadily from the west with a peculiar odour, a combination of brimstone, decaying flesh, and rotting plants. The walls are wet, and condensation drips constantly from above. Short, fine, filaments float in the air, making it difficult to breathe.
115712:
An empty exoskeleton of a large spider is lying here.
A small centipede is here scurrying about.
A hideous mottled spider advances with startling speed.

A long corridor coming from the east ends abruptly here. Warm, wet steam drifts up from an opening below, carrying with it a strong sulfurous odour. Cobwebs swirl around, mixing with the wet air and creating sticky clumps that fall and cover the floor.
115713:
A hideous mottled spider advances with startling speed.
A mottled spider crouches in the shadows, watching over her young.

There is little room to move in this narrow pit. Sticky strands of silk cling to everything, and the floor slopes steeply toward the centre, making it difficult to get out, as if this hole were intentionally constructed as some sort of trap.
115714: A portion of the floor of the corridor above has collapsed, creating a deep sinkhole. Jagged rocks protrude from the floor and walls, making movement treacherous. Water drips constantly from above, collecting in the cracks and crevices in the floor.
115715: A small centipede is here scurrying about.

A passage from the east ends abruptly here. A large hole below is spanned by several webs, waiting to catch anything that falls down from here. Long strands of thin silk hang from above, in varying shades of grey and white, reaching out to cling to anything passing through. Every nook and cranny in this cave is choked with cobwebs.
115716: A hideous mottled spider advances with startling speed.

Layers upon layers of delicate, spiralling webs completely cover every opening. It is questionable whether travel in any direction is prudent, though staying here seems like a bad idea as well. Cocoons, some of them with seemingly live occupants, hang from several of the webs, confirming that this is not a place to linger.
115717: An empty exoskeleton of a large spider is lying here.

An east-west tunnel narrows here, creating a natural bottleneck. Several spider webs cross the passageway, ready to snare anything that ventures into this passageway. Several webs have been broken, and contain large cocoons of silk. Frantic movement can be seen inside several of the cocoons, indicating that whatever, or whoever, got caught in the web was cocooned alive.
115718: Thick, sticky cobwebs cover every surface, making movement difficult. Strands of web float through the air. Openings to the east, west, and south can barely be seen through the tangle of webs covering them. The webs vibrate and shift every now and again.
115719: This tunnel is completely covered in sticky webs. Strands of grey and white thread have been woven into intricate, spiralling patterns spanning the entire width of the cave in several places. The passage to the east is completely blocked with an impregnable mass of overlapping woven webs, hardened with time to form a solid wall that rivals the surrounding stone in durability. It appears that there may be an exit to the west, though making it past several intervening webs without getting trapped might prove to be challenging.
115720: A tunnel branches into several directions here. The passageway to the north seems to open into a larger area, though it is so covered with cobwebs, it is difficult to be sure what lies beyond. A dark tunnel leads to the west, and the air from that direction is rank. There is also an opening above leading to a small cave.
115721:
A sturdy crate made of nailed wooden planks sits on the floor.
A large black bat flitters near you.
A large black bat flitters near you.

Broken crates, chests, and boxes are scattered around here, along with shelves filled with broken jars and other abandoned supplies. Several barrels are lined up against the wall. Thick dust covers every surface, indicating that this place has not been used for decades.
115722: Black basalt forms a tunnel running east-west. The tunnel is nearly perfectly cylindrical, though whether formed naturally or by some intelligent workforce is impossible to discern. Scratching sounds echo throughout this space, seemingly coming from every direction.
115723: A steep chute leads down to a refuse pit to the south, from which a strong, foetid smell emanates. An opening above appears to be a vent shaft, though the stench would indicate that vent is ineffective. Thick clumps of cobwebs float through the air and cling to the walls, and sounds of movement can be heard echoing from the east.
115724: Trash, bones, broken tools, carcasses in various states of decay, and other detritus are piled in rotting mounds all around this chamber. A thick fluid, sticky and foul smelling, oozes out from under several of the mounds, slowly seeping along a slight declivity towards a pit to the west. A steep chute slopes steeply upwards to the north, and there appears to be a small opening to the south.
115725: A large black bat flitters near you.

This narrow shaft appears to have been formed as a vent from the area below. However, it appears that a rockslide, possibly caused by an earthquake, has blocked the opening above with huge boulders. Based on the thick grime covering the rocks, this vent has been blocked for quite some time.
115726: A small indentation in the rock has created this alcove. The foul smells from the garbage pile to the north mix with stale, stagnant air here, creating an entirely unwelcoming environment. Every surface of this cave is teaming with insects or other small creatures.
115727:
A hideous mottled spider advances with startling speed.
A hideous mottled spider advances with startling speed.

The floor is littered with bones and other debris. A thick, brown, sticky substance covers every surface and gives off a strong, foetid smell. There is a large hole leading upwards into the darkness. Wisps of thin strands float in in the air, clinging to everything they touch.
115728: The narrow tunnel from the south ends abruptly here at a large hole leading to darkness below. Sticky strands of fibre float in the air and cover every surface. Fine, hairlike filaments crisscross the opening, glistening with fine droplets of condensation from the humid air.
115729:
A small centipede is here scurrying about.
A small centipede is here scurrying about.

Water drips from the low ceiling, pooling on the floor in shallow puddles. A faint rustling can be heard from the north, echoing through this narrow space. To the south, there appears to be an opening into a larger space, while the passage to the north continues to narrow.
115738: An eyeless white rat with nasty teeth scurries about.

Solid stone has been split somehow, creating a deep cleft. The air here is thick with the smell of sulphur and rot. The walls are rough, black rock, and the floor is jagged and treacherous. There seems to be a passage to the east. From the west, there is the sound of trickling water and the feel of hot, humid air.
115739:
A small blotchy mushroom grows here.
A huge black fungus is here, exuding a foul stench.
A huge black fungus is here, exuding a foul stench.
A huge black fungus is here, exuding a foul stench.
A huge black fungus is here, exuding a foul stench.
A huge black fungus is here, exuding a foul stench.
A giant, strange looking green fungus is here, ready to devour you in seconds.
A giant, strange looking green fungus is here, ready to devour you in seconds.

There are rocks and rubble littering the ground, clearly the result of a massive cave-in long ago. The air here is stagnant, wet, and putrid. Rocks and debris block the way in nearly every direction, but there is a way out to the west.

The stones form a sort of rugged staircase, making the passage up and down this tunnel possible, though still hazardous.

All about the tunnel here are grey and black rocks and boulders of various sizes. A black liquid also runs down the walls and coats the fungi in places. The blanket of fungi comes to an end on the walls toward the south, where they become grey again and open up into a vast cavern.

Large stalagmites climb toward the ceiling from the floor, and dry, dead vegetation covers areas of the floor, packed tightly to form large beds. The ambient temperature here is noticeably high, and the vast quantity of beds indicate that a large population of some primitive species populates this lair.
115850:
A horned bat-like creature is sleeping here, hanging from the ceiling.
A savage bat-like creature is sleeping here, hanging from the ceiling.
A savage bat-like creature is sleeping here, hanging from the ceiling.
A savage bat-like creature is sleeping here, hanging from the ceiling.
A savage bat-like creature is sleeping here, hanging from the ceiling.
Some ugly blow-flies are buzzing around here.

A collection of stalagmites, formed tightly together, sits neatly near the corner of the cavern. All about, piles of dried and dead vegetation lie meticulously formed into large, comfortable beds. Paths have been carefully formed between all of the bedding, with the red dirt pushed away to expose the bare stone floor beneath it.
115851:
A skeleton of some humanoid lies in the dust.
A savage bat-like creature is sleeping here, hanging from the ceiling.
A savage bat-like creature is sleeping here, hanging from the ceiling.
A savage bat-like creature is sleeping here, hanging from the ceiling.
A horned bat-like creature is sleeping here, hanging from the ceiling.

Deep within the vast cavern, more piles of bedding lie all about. Wide, flat rocks jut out all along the walls, forming shelves upon which more beds lie. On the floor below, well-worn pathways weave throughout the lair between the beds, which seems to suggest that they are very well travelled.
115852:
A savage bat-like creature is sleeping here, hanging from the ceiling.
A savage bat-like creature is sleeping here, hanging from the ceiling.
A savage bat-like creature is sleeping here, hanging from the ceiling.

Well-worn pathways snake throughout the cavern, between large and small piles of bedding where the creatures sleep. Rock shelves protrude from the walls, upon which more beds are formed. The air is hot and humid, and the ground is covered with a thick layer of dry, blood-red dirt in which the pathways are formed.
115858: The floor is flat and slopes down toward the south, while it twists upward to the east. The air is warm, humid, and smells foul. The floor is well-worn in the centre, and the walls are crude and jagged. Scratch marks can be discerned along the walls upon close inspection.
115860: You see three green slime moulds on the ground.

A steep ramp leads up this large, flat ledge, high above the cavern below. The large stalactites are close, and it is evident that the clear water dripping from them is feeding the pond below. Geckos crawl on the walls here, but scurry off at the sound of footsteps.
115861: Boulders and large rocks partially fill the tunnel, while smaller piles of rubble and pebbles line the floor along the walls. The passage to the north is slightly obstructed by two large boulders, but manoeuvring around them is quite possible. The floor of the tunnel to the south descends suddenly and is very steep.
115862: As it descends downward into the vast darkness, the tunnel becomes more narrow. Ascending upward, the tunnel opens up and becomes filled with more loose rocks and pebbles. The steep walls and floor are made of a gritty, grey basalt rock. On the eastern wall, a large crack has formed and contains a thick, black liquid.
115863: The tunnel is narrow and cramped, and slopes steeply downward into complete darkness. The ground is covered with a layer of fine dust and the air here is heavy to breathe. There is a large, wide crack in the grey stone of the eastern wall that seems to run off into the darkness.
115864: The tunnel is steep and descends into the darkness below. The grey walls and ceiling narrow downward as they go. A large crack on the eastern wall is covered in a foul, black liquid that glistens when light touches it. The air seems to become more difficult to breathe further down the tunnel, while going up would have the opposite effect.
115865: The floor of the tunnel here is level. There is a tight, narrow opening that leads up into a dark, steep tunnel. The tunnel bends sharply to the south, and the faint sound of splashing water can be heard. The air is damp, heavy, and humid. The walls are covered with drops of water that occasionally run down in streams.
115866: Tunnels open into this huge cavern from the north and the west. The walls are almost entirely vertical and naturally carved out of grey, columnar stone. They disappear into the impenetrable darkness above. The sound of splashing water comes from the east, where the cavern continues into the darkness. To the south, a natural ramp made of grey gravel slopes upward.
115867: The tunnel slopes down toward the west. The ground and walls here are damp and the ground is covered in grey gravel. To the west, the faint sound of splashing can occasionally be heard. There is a foul odour carried by air flowing from that direction. On the ceiling, small dry stalactites protrude downward.
115868: Narrow Ledge above a Dark Lake

The path leads in from the north and continues onto a small ledge, just wide enough for two people to pass side by side. Rocks jut out of the cave wall from the west and occasionally impede passage, making it difficult to continue along the path as it leads southward. To the east, a large black lake sits about fifteen feet below the ledge.
115869: Two large boulders stand side by side to the north.

This is a large cavern with grey, columnar stone walls that ascend up into the endless darkness above. A small opening is visible in the eastern wall, with a ramp made of gravel leading up to it. Occasional drips can be heard coming from the west, and the air here is heavy and humid. Two large boulders stand side by side to the north, with just enough room to seemingly squeeze between.
115870: The walls of the cavern are grey and made of columnar stone, with a foul black liquid dripping down the northern and western walls. There are some small, short stalactites hanging from the ceiling above. In the corner of the cavern is a collection of dust, gravel, and some tiny animal bones.
115872: The cavern wall makes a sudden turn to the west, where it disappears into the damp darkness. Some inky black liquid runs onto the floor of the cavern from the west. The air is damp, heavy, and musty. Black and green mosses line the grey stone walls. Every now and then, a critter scurries across the ground and plunges into the black pool of water.
115873: The ceiling of the cave is low, with stalactites protruding down and the surface of a black, foul pool of water is only three feet below. This is the centre of the pool that is flooding the cavern, and it is deep enough that the blackness of the water within conceals the bottom.
115874: Narrow Ledge above a Dark Lake

The ledge makes a turn toward the east, where it continues into the darkness. The ceiling here slopes low toward the wall to the west and south. The ledge rises up further from the surface of the lake below, and the path is dry and dusty. Grey stones jut out of the walls, making it difficult to walk upright in some spots.
115875: Narrow Ledge above a Dark Lake
A small vicious black rat squeaks at you for disturbing it.

The ledge is wide and passage is easier here than it is in other areas along it. To the west, the ceiling begins to slope downward as the ledge narrows. To the east, the ledge widens even more and the ceiling opens up. The walls here are smooth and made of columnar stone. There is a crack on the southern wall, where some black liquid has run down, dried, and left a stain.
115876: Narrow Ledge above a Dark Lake

The ledge here is nice and wide, making passage comfortable and easy. The ceiling is high and large stalactites hang in the vast darkness above. Splashing can be heard from the lake to the north, far below the ledge. A large gaping crack can be seen in the wall to the south, stained black from some dried liquid that once ran down the crack's surface. Natural grey stone steps lead upward to the east, as the path continues along the ledge.
115877: Wide Ledge around a Dark Lake

The ledge opens up and becomes large, flat, and wide in the corner of the vast cavern here above the large underground lake. It continues to wind to the west, where some natural stone steps lead downward into the darkness. To the north, the ledge slopes downward, making this the highest point of the entire path. The dark surface of the lake sits about thirty feet below. The large stalactites that hang above the lake are now eye level.
115878: Narrow Ledge above a Dark Lake

A large boulder sits against the wall to the east, partially obstructing the ledge and making passage more difficult. To the south, the ledge slopes upward toward the corner of the cavern. Beyond the boulder to the north, the ledge narrows significantly, making travel in that direction slightly more difficult. The smooth, grey, columnar walls are dry and cold to the touch.
115879: Narrow Ledge above a Dark Lake
A small vicious black rat squeaks at you for disturbing it.

The ledge slopes down from the south, where it starts to become even with the rest of the cavern floor. The ledge is narrow, and the surface of the lake becomes closer as the ledge makes its descent northward. The huge stalactites that hang from the ceiling above appear small at first, but become larger as the ceiling slopes down toward the north and becomes lower. Air seems to be flowing in from that direction, and carries a foul, putrid odour with it.
115880: The ceiling here becomes low, with large stalactites protruding down, making passage to the north seemingly difficult. To the south, the floor slopes upward into the darkness and forms a ledge over a large, underground lake. Faint splashing can be heard in the distance.
115881: The cavern narrows significantly into a tight, cramped tunnel that curves to the south and east. There are both stalactites that hang from the ceiling as well as stalagmites that jut up from the ground that densely fill the cavern. While travel in either direction is still possible, the obstacles make it much more difficult.
115882: Wet Corner of a Dark Cavern

A giant boulder is here, slightly recessed into the northern wall.
A cold shroud of dark grey mist covers the ground.

The ceiling of the caverns slant down from the south and east and come to a corner here. There are small stalactites lining the ceiling, hanging down like spikes in the darkness. The floor of the cavern is wet and muddy, and small bones are scattered about. Green and black fungi grows on a giant boulder to the north and the western wall.
115883:
A large pale fish with bulbous eyes is swimming here.
A large pale fish with bulbous eyes is swimming here.

Huge stalactites, as large around as full-grown mountain trolls, hang here in the vast darkness of the cavern. A foul, black liquid covers them and occasionally drips off into the lake below. The surface of the lake is smooth and calm, with the exception of the occasional drip from the stalactites above.
115884: A pair of huge stalactites hang in the darkness over the lake.

A pair of large, symmetrical stalactites hang from the ceiling above. They are almost identical, as if created here intentionally. They resemble the fangs of some large beast, dripping with a black liquid that looks like some foul venom. To the east and south, steep grey columnar stone walls rise from the water.
115885: A large pale fish with bulbous eyes is swimming here.

Giant stalactites protrude from the ceiling above, covered in black liquid that drips into a smooth, calm lake below. The steep grey walls rise up from the edges of the lake, and plateau off at the top at what appears to be a ledge.
115886: A large pale fish with bulbous eyes is swimming here.

Large stalactites hang like chandeliers from the darkness above. They glisten with moisture when the faintest hint of light touches them, and black liquid drips steadily from them into a large, black lake below. The surface of the water is smooth as glass, save the occasional drip from the ceiling or splash of some fish from within.
115887: The roof of the cavern is high and covered with stalactites that hang down like spikes in the vast darkness. They are covered by a thick, black liquid that occasionally drips down the ground below. The air here is thick, heavy, wet, and musty. A foul odour emanates from the east, while the roof slopes down to the west and the stalactites become thick and dense.
115888: This is a large, open cavern with huge stalactites hanging from the ceiling. All about are large, grey boulders. Green and black mosses grow on the wall to the south and line the tops of the boulders as well. The air here is damp and musty.
115889: An albino centipede is here, crawling over the mosses.

The ceiling of the cavern slopes down to this corner from the north and west. There are large boulders all about, with green and black mosses lining the tops of them. The walls to the east and south are also lined with moss. The cavern seems to open up to the west and north, while faint dripping sounds can be heard echoing off the cavern walls.
115890: The cavern here is huge and wide open, with boulders strewn about here and there. Thin strands of green and black moss line the tops of the boulders, while thin grey strands of some sort of cave fungi hang from the ceiling. On the ground, tiny bones and fish skulls can be found scattered about the cavern floor.
115891: A subterranean lizard is here trying to blend with the surroundings.

Slimy, multi-coloured fungi line the northern wall and roof of the cavern. Musty, damp air can be detected coming in from the east. It carries with it the stench of death and decay. The floor is damp and slightly muddy, and there is a large, gaping crack in the stone floor below.
115892:
A long slender eel glides along the water, its body coiled to strike.
An albino fish is swimming here, looking for some food.
A large pale fish with bulbous eyes is swimming here.

The ceiling is densely covered with short, sharp stalactites hanging down over the dark lake below, and dripping with a thick, black liquid. The occasional drop falls onto the surface of the lake. The bases of the stalactites at the ceiling are surrounded by clusters of multi-coloured fungi.
115893:
A long slender eel glides along the water, its body coiled to strike.
An albino fish is swimming here, looking for some food.

The ceiling is high above the lake below and covered in fungi, decaying and dripping with black liquid. A foul odour fills the air. From the lake, large grey basalt columns rise high and connect with the ceiling. The black liquid dripping down covers them, and they glisten when light touches them.
115894:
Something cold and scaly slithers past your leg.
Something cold and scaly slithers past your leg.
A large pale fish with bulbous eyes is swimming here.

The ceiling here is covered with thick clusters of fungi, dripping with a thick, black liquid, and rising high above the lake below. Slimy, multi- coloured fungi cover the wall to the north. The wall to the west is smooth, grey basalt, but the thick, black liquid from the ceiling runs down it toward the lake below. Higher up on the western wall, there appears to be a crawlspace that can be reached by climbing up to it.
115895: A blanket of slimy fungi covers the northern wall.

There is a wide rock ledge that juts out over the dark lake below it. The ledge is slimy and slippery and a foul odour emanates up to it from the lake below. Slimy fungi cover the wall to the north, dripping and oozing with a thick black liquid that runs down and seemingly feeds the lake.
115896:
An ancient fungus smothers the boulders.
A huge black fungus is here, exuding a foul stench.

The crawlspace is small and cramped, but provides a safe area from the dark lake below. Clusters of slimy, multi-coloured fungi line the walls and ceiling here. Some of these fungi ooze with the black liquid that drips from the ceiling. The small space makes the disgusting odour that fills this area more concentrated, which makes breathing difficult.
115897: The ceiling of the cavern slopes drastically to the east and north here. Stalactites hang down low, some almost touching the floor. Thin strands of some type of strange grey cave fungus hang freely from the ceiling, and also run down the stalactites and walls.
115898: The cavern walls to the south and east converge here into a corner. Green and black mosses and fungi grow on the walls and on boulders that are strewn about. The air is damp and musty, and air flow can be felt coming from the north. Small stalactites hang from the ceiling here.
115899: There is a large, gaping crack in the northern cave wall, and a slight breeze can be felt coming through. A dank odour fills the cave, while dead and decaying roots line every wall. The ceiling is low and makes the space cramped, but it suddenly ascends to the north before it stops suddenly when it meets the steep, grey stone wall.
115900:
A small reptile with large eyes scurries along the walls.
Massive roots shift uneasily all around you.
Massive roots shift uneasily all around you.
An albino salamander is here, perched on some rocks.
An albino salamander is here, perched on some rocks.

Hidden behind a huge boulder, the corner of this cave is surprisingly large. A disgusting smell fills the cave here, and the walls are lined with dead and decaying roots and vegetation. Salamanders and geckos scurry all about, trying to hide in the vegetation and stay out of sight.
115901:
A small reptile with large eyes scurries along the walls.
A cockroach is scuttling across the floor carrying some debris.

The walls of this natural indentation in the rock glisten with condensation. A thick, dank draught comes from above, and the air is cold and wet. Every now and then, faint splashing sounds can be heard from above. As there is no evidence that anyone or anything has travelled through here, it seems that this area is avoided by visitors, perhaps with good reason.
115902: Thick, wet mud covers the floor of this shallow depression, at times nearly knee-deep. The walls and ceiling are covered with green-blue slime that gives of a stale, musty odour. While it is difficult to be sure, there appears to be something moving beneath the surface.
115903: Dry stone gives way to hard-packed, damp earth as this cramped channel extends from east to west. The walls form a wedge as they taper inward and nearly come together at the floor, leaving only a thin strip on which to walk. Passage to the west becomes more difficult, while there appears to be an easier egress to the east.
115904: Solid stone has been carved away to form a small chamber. The walls and ceiling are only roughly formed, and mining tools litter the ground. It looks as if work in this mine shaft was abruptly interrupted for some reason, and all work abandoned.
115905:
A deep, jagged crack runs vertically down the east wall.
Something shiny is embedded in the stone above.

A crude shaft has been dug here, apparently the early phase of a mining operation. Heavy, square timbers support the walls and ceiling at regular intervals, giving off a heavy smell of pine tar. The splintered, sagging wooden supports have decayed with time, never meant to be more than temporary.
115906: Sections of the tunnel walls have been chipped away by crude tools. There are short, dead-end tunnels in several directions, as if someone was exploring the surrounding earth for possible valuable ore. A mineshaft extends to the south, while natural openings lead to the north and west.
115907: Veins of glittering ore run through the stone, streaking across the tunnel in a stark contrast with the surrounding dull black walls. The ore glistens with bright silver, gold, and white glints, even in the darkness, and the floor is covered with sparkling dust.
115908:
A tiny spider is here, eating a tiny bug.
A menacing mottled spider is here, lurking in the shadows.

Strange whispers and clicking noises echo in the deep. The tunnel walls are infested with strange insects that crawl over the walls on many legs, appearing and quickly disappearing in the tiny burrows in the black stone. The floor is covered in fecal matter and black, empty carapaces.
115909: A giant rat patters against you, squeaking maliciously.

The tunnel passage winds into the distance. Sharp, black glass-like crystals protrude from the walls and ceiling like daggers. Ragged articles of clothing, stained with dried blood, hang from a few of the crystals, apparently torn from previous travellers as they passed through this treacherous place.
115910: Coarse, black basalt in the northern part of this tunnel changes abruptly to glistening crystal formations to the east. The crystals are sharp, and passage to the east could become perilous. The tunnel seems to expand into a much larger cave to the north.
115911: A giant rat patters against you, squeaking maliciously.

Large basalt columns extend up from the floor at random intervals, disappearing into the darkness above. Crudely drawn pictographs depicting what appear to be scenes of war are scrawled onto the stone walls with some sort of indelible white paint.
115912: A large cavern opens into the darkness, the walls extend upward out of sight. Every noise echoes repeatedly off the smooth stone, mixing with other sounds to create dissonant chords that ebb and flow as new sounds enter the mix while others fade out.
115913: The walls and ceiling of this tunnel are crumbling, littering the floor with rubble. There is evidence that portions of this tunnel have clearly been worked, but the surrounding earth was apparently too unstable to allow mining to continue safely.
115914: Jagged marks on the walls and ceiling show that the original tunnel has been widened in several places. Debris and broken mining equipment lie discarded in neat piles near the areas that have been expanded. Clearly this was an active mining operation at some point, but it appears to have been prematurely halted.
115915: With several abrupt changes in direction, this twisting tunnel is quite disorienting, and the rough and uneven floor, covered with loose rubble, makes it difficult not to stumble while navigating through the tortuous path this tunnel becomes.
115916: A vaulting tunnel ceiling opens up to reveal giant holes scattered across the surface, as if worms had eaten away at the stone. The many passageways continue into darkness as if unending. The floor is covered in filth and debris, and sticky grime is plastered onto the tunnel walls.
115917: The walls of the tunnel are covered with shallow pin-sized holes scattered all over the surface. Cobwebs drape the tunnel ceiling, appearing as large as curtains in certain sections, hanging down to the floor. The layers of web curtains obscure and distort the view in every direction, creating a surreal atmosphere.
115918: This alcove seems to be some sort of antechamber. There are elaborate patterns of intertwined trees carved in the walls and ceiling. The patterns are inset with a lustrous metal giving the impression of being in a moonlit forest. To the east, the glistening images of two large oaks with intertwined branches form an archway.
115919: Two tunnels come together in a perfect corner, neat and square, clearly the work of highly skilled craftsmen. The walls show remnants of intricate patterns and writing that appears to be Elven, but time and erosion has faded both into obscurity.
115920: Faded tool marks, edges worn smooth with time imply that this tunnel was made ages ago. The air is completely motionless, but somehow neither stale nor fresh. This place gives an aura of unrest as if some arcane energy is somehow trapped and struggling to escape.
115921: There is a sense that this tunnel continues for an eternity in both the north and south directions. The utter darkness is sobering, creating a feeling of unease in even the most hardy. No exits can be seen, but there is a sense of expansiveness to the south and an unsettling aura to the north.
115922: Inky darkness permeates the surrounding area, making it difficult to discern space, distance, and even time. While the blackness creates a sombre, unwelcoming atmosphere, there is a sense that the areas to the north and south may be even more disquieting.
115923: The emptiness of this pitch black tunnel is palpable and unwelcoming. Travel would be perilous were it not for the smooth, even floor. It appears that this tunnel was created to provide a passageway for travel, though why anyone would willingly travel here is much less apparent.
115924: It is profoundly dark and silent here, as if the very walls are swallowing every ounce of energy. The utter emptiness is reminiscent of a tomb, and could make someone entering here question whether they are still among the living. The lack of any sensory input makes it difficult to distinguish which direction this tunnel leads.
115925: A tiny, harmless centipede is here.

Cold, hard walls form a tunnel cut from solid stone long ago, sloping upward from north to south. It is cool and dry here, and the air is eerily still. The centre of the floor is smooth, as if worn by many years of foot traffic. The tunnel disappears into utter darkness to the north.
115926: The air in this tunnel is still, and strangely free of any odour. The passageway has been carved from solid rock. While tool marks can be observed here and there, the walls are mostly smooth, apparently worn with age. The floor is even, but clearly slopes upward to the south.
115927: A carved tunnel leading north ends abruptly at a small opening to the south. It is profoundly dark, quiet, and strangely unsettling here. It cannot be determined how far this tunnel extends to the north, or what is beyond the opening to the south.
115928: A cockroach is scuttling across the floor carrying some debris.

A stone stair coming from above ends at this rough landing. There are broken bones and other debris scattered all over the ground, clearly the result of various mishaps on the stairs above. To the north, a long passagway leads into the still darkness.
115929: Other than the steep steps in the stone, this narrow vertical channel is remarkably featureless. From here, it seems that these stairs continue upward indefinitely, but there is a sense that the bottom is not far below. The silence of this place is profound, combining with the darkness and an unnatural chill in the air to create an environment that causes even the most hardy and fearless to take pause.
115930: Steep stairs extend up and down from here, seemingly forever in both directions. The stairs are steep, with exceedingly narrow treads. The slightest misstep would result in finding the bottom rather more quickly than would be safe.
115945: Grey stone stairs, seemingly natural, lead up to a large opening and down into the vast darkness below. The natural stairs are made of gritty grey basalt, creating enough grip for a firm footing and making the passage up and down easy to navigate.
115950:
A crude barricade is being hastily assembled to the south.
A dread guardsman of Dol Guldur is here, compelling the slaves to work harder.
A dread guardsman of Dol Guldur is here, compelling the slaves to work harder.
A pitiful slave toils wearily, assembling a crude barricade.
A pitiful slave toils wearily, assembling a crude barricade.
A pitiful slave toils wearily, assembling a crude barricade.

A tunnel from the south meets an east-west tunnel at this junction. The floor is worn from heavy and frequent foot traffic east and west, but the south passage is covered with dust and shows no evidence of use. Whatever lies to the south, it does not seem to interest those who travel here.
115951:
A pool of thick, red liquid covers a section of the ground.
A spiderling skitters about, looking for small prey to devour.
Some ugly blow-flies are buzzing around here.
A mottled snake is sneaking here, ready to sink its fangs into flesh.

The floor is covered with sticky, viscous slime, which seems to originate from somewhere to the south. The putrid smell indicates that it is some kind of animal waste. Faint scratching sounds can be heard all around, as if hundreds of tiny creatures are scurrying about searching for something.
115952:
A skeleton of some humanoid lies in the dust.
A desiccated corpse hangs in a tangled web, its lifeblood completely drained.
A spiderling skitters about, looking for small prey to devour.
A spiderling skitters about, looking for small prey to devour.
A spiderling skitters about, looking for small prey to devour.
A spiderling skitters about, looking for small prey to devour.
A spiderling skitters about, looking for small prey to devour.
A spiderling skitters about, looking for small prey to devour.
A mottled spider crouches in the shadows, watching over her young.
A mottled spider crouches in the shadows, watching over her young.

Bones of all shapes and sizes litter the ground and hang in the sticky web that covers this whole pit. Egg sacs are everywhere. The different sizes, shapes, and colours of the sacs indicate that this is the lair of several different mother spiders.
115957: Thick strands of sticky silk span this cave at random intervals and angles from walls, floor, and ceiling, creating a haphazard tangle of intersecting threads. The web is so thick that it nearly chokes off the entire passageway. Bones, empty clothing, and other remnants of living things hang tangled here and there in the sticky web.
115958: Long strands of sticky webs hang from the walls and ceiling, seemingly covering every stone, and so thick in places that they could be mistaken for fog. Some strands are as hard as iron while others are soft and flexible, the combination creating the opportunity for an effective, and likely lethal, trap.
115959: A hideous mottled spider advances with startling speed.

Cramped and dark, this small hollow opens into a wide tunnel to the south. The sloping floor and low ceiling make this an inviting space in which to linger. The air is musty and thick with dust and fine, silky filaments. The opening to the south is obscured by thick tangles of cobwebs.
115960: A thin, silky spider web spans the tunnel in a criss-cross pattern.

A thick web, made up of silk strands of various sizes, from thin and sticky to thick and iron-strong, nearly blocks this entire vertical passage. Careful manoeuvring will be required to pass through these webs without becoming entangled.
115961: A cockroach is scuttling across the floor carrying some debris.

A shift in the earth centuries ago has formed a narrow ledge that slopes steeply upward from the cave below and continues to the east. The hard stone ends in a precipitous edge leading into an abyss of darkness below. Travel along this ledge is possible for the sure of foot.
115962:
A cockroach is scuttling across the floor carrying some debris.
A large black bat flitters near you.
A large black bat flitters near you.

This narrow ledge extends east-west, high above the cave floor below. While the width here is barely wide enough to allow a tenuous purchase, the ledge narrows sharply to the east, making travel in that direction impossible. Sand and rubble scattered across the surface prevent sure footing, making a slip and potentially deadly fall a distinct possibility.
115963:
A desiccated corpse hangs in a tangled web, its lifeblood completely drained.
A spiderling skitters about, looking for small prey to devour.
A mottled spider crouches in the shadows, watching over her young.

Cocoons of every shape and size hang from the ceiling on thick strands of thread. Movement inside many of the cocoons indicates that the occupants must still be alive. The floor is littered with empty and broken cocoons, bones from every sort of creature, and lifeless, empty corpses, shrivelled and dried as if every ounce of liquid, and life, had been sucked from them.
115964: A thin, silky spider web spans the tunnel in a criss-cross pattern.

Nearly vertical, this narrow chute is choked with thick tangles of cobwebs. Strong, heavy silk strands, the size of sturdy rope, criss-cross the opening at irregular intervals creating hand- and footholds that make it possible to move through this otherwise impassable tunnel.
115979: This narrow tube in the stone extends sharply up and down. Sticky, silky strands span across the opening, making it difficult to move. Several bones and a few full skeletons are trapped in the web, their original owners apparently having fallen from above to become trapped here and be picked clean by the local inhabitants.
115981:
A tiny, harmless centipede is here.
A tiny, harmless centipede is here.

A steep tunnel coming down from the east transitions to a gentle slope leading to the west. A slight draught comes from the east, bringing with it a stale, musty odour. Every now and again, the sound of small rocks falling can be heard echoing from the west.
115982: A crude tunnel continues into the darkness. The walls are rough and marked with haphazardly arranged jagged cuts that continue down the entire length of the wall. Small veins of black glittering minerals run along the edges. The floor is covered with layers of dust, concealing shards of crushed, translucent black glass.
115983: The floor of this tunnel slopes very steeply downward from east to west, nearly as steep as a stairway, but without the benefit of steps to help with footing. A tiny stream of water splashes swiftly down a narrow gutter, disappearing into some sort of drain to the west.
115984: Two narrow tunnels, one from the west and one from the north meet at a perfect right angle here. The featureless walls rise to meet an equally featureless ceiling above. A trickle of water, formed by condensation of the wet, humid air on the cold stone walls, runs from the north and down to the west, flowing in a small channel that appears to have been intentionally carved to collect moisture and prevent it from accumulating on the smooth floor.
115985: A small vicious black rat squeaks at you for disturbing it.

Perfectly square and evenly-spaced stairs have been carved in the stone, leading down to the south and extending upwards to the north. The smooth black walls glisten with condensation, and small droplets fall from time to time from the ceiling above.
115986:
A tiny, harmless centipede is here.
A tiny, harmless centipede is here.

The tunnel makes a sharp turn here, rising up to the east and sloping down to the south. The walls and floor have been skilfully crafted from the stone, smooth and even, but not slick, despite the dampness from the humid air. A draught can be felt rising from the south.
115987: A giant rat patters against you, squeaking maliciously.

A passageway leads downwards to the west from a smoothly-carved landing that extends to the east. The clean, square lines show that this tunnel was created by master craftsmen, though there are no decorative or other distinguishing marks of any kind. To the west, the downward slope is smooth and gentle, making movement through this tunnel is easy.
115988: This tunnel is wet, filled with mud, slime and pooled water. The air feels more drinkable than breathable, and every step splashes water. A dark hatch carved from black stone can be seen set into the muddy ceiling. To the west the tunnel continues into the darkness.
