115989: A moderate sized tunnel made primarily of dark earth ends abruptly here. It must have been well used at some point, as the ground in the middle has been packed down into a solid earthen path. However, a landslide of thick, brown earth and small rocks has made any passage farther entirely impossible. A hatch, carved from black stone, lies in the centre of the passage.
115990:
A water barrel has been left here.
A big open crate takes up a quarter of the room.
A large cabinet capable of storing goods is here.
In the cabinet, there are two smoked pieces of meat and two pieces of smoked, cured meat.
A sturdy crate made of nailed wooden planks sits on the floor.

This square room looks like a natural cavern expanded on to make room for the numerous crates, shelves, and cabinets that occupy it. The room, being underground, is chill even during summer. An odour of rancid meat fills the air. A narrow stair leads up from this larder, it is much too narrow for the cabinets here; the tunnel disappearing into darkness to the west seems a more likely origin.
115991:
A large pale fish with bulbous eyes is swimming here.
A large pale fish with bulbous eyes is swimming here.

The cave here is flooded with a deep pool of black water. Stalactites hang from the ceiling and drip with a steady flow of black foul water that continually fills the pool below. The water is stagnant and foul-smelling, causing the air here to be heavy and musty. Small fish occasionally break the surface of the water with a splash.
115992: A large and twisted beast lurks in the rotten pool.

A thick, brown mud mixes with the black water that floods the tunnels to create a disgusting substance in this small corner cave. Knee-deep and with the stench or rot and decay, the mud makes manoeuvring very difficult. The walls of the cave are brown with caked-on mud, and a black water ring seems to permanently stain them.
115993: The pool of water to the north and east suddenly comes to a stop here, where the ground is still damp but not flooded. All about, salamanders scurry and chase after small insects. Tiny carcasses of small fish lie scattered about, with flies buzzing about and maggots crawling around. There are black footprints that lead from the direction of the water and into the depths of the caves beyond.
115994:
A small blotchy mushroom grows here.
On the ground, there are two toadstools.
An albino salamander is here, perched on some rocks.

The walls to the south and east have large, gaping cracks in which cool, fresh air can be felt flowing through. The air is dry and makes breathing much easier. Salamanders crawl all about the floor and walls, chasing after small, unseen insects. The ground here is dry and covered with a fine dust.
115995:
A black, leather-scaled reptile glances around with gleaming eyes.
A black, leather-scaled reptile glances around with gleaming eyes.
A black, leather-scaled reptile glances around with gleaming eyes.

Salamanders cover the walls of this nook in the cavern. They scatter at the slightest disturbance. Rotten vegetation covers the top halves of the walls and roots cover the ceiling, dripping with a black liquid. The putrid air here is heavy and difficult to breathe, and flies buzz all about. There are large cracks in the stone floor underfoot.
115996: The dark liquid is captured in the corner of the cavern here, forming a deep, black pool. The liquid is solid black and shows no signs of transparency whatsoever. The ceiling slopes down to the east and south, and the water almost touches it. There are occasional splashes in the water, indicating lots of activity from the fish below the surface.
115998:
The corpse of a white wolf is lying here.
The corpse of a white wolf is lying here.

This is the central square of the village. Wagon tracks lead to the east, and to the north stands a large wooden building. Numerous footprints lead in all directions, and wooden planks have been laid upon the ground, presumably to afford easier passage in an area obviously plagued often by mud.
115999: A hillman warrior is here, ready to fight.

Climbing up a ladder you enter the top of the watch-tower. You have an excellent view over the surrounding landscape. The village is surrounded by barren plains and to the north you can see a cliff. The tower has a wooden roof and no furniture at all.
116009:
A sturdy pack horse is standing here.
A sturdy pack horse is standing here.
A domesticated pony, beast of burden to many, stands here.
The stables have separate boxes for the horses but aren't used much. You see harness piled up in one corner. Primitive looking saddles are here and a horse and cart is standing near the east wall.
116011:
A small blotchy mushroom grows here.
A deeply black, oddly shaped cloud of mist has gathered here.
A cold shroud of dark grey mist covers the ground.

The warm, humid air from the lake wafts in from the south through the cracks and voids around the giant boulder concealing the entrance to this hidden cavern. The floor is damp and muddy, and the bottoms of the grey stone wall are wet as well. The wetness of the walls gradually disappears as it climbs up, and the top portions of the wall are lighter grey. A thick blanket of green and black fungi grows on the floor around the base of the walls, climbing and spreading up the wetness. A thick, black liquid slowly drips down from some cracks in the western wall, and forms a small puddle.
116013: The ground in this forested, rough area forms a V-shaped gully that runs from east to west. It is impossible to travel south, where conifers and oak shrubs grow among talus, boulders and treacherous cliffs. Passage eastwards seems fairly straightforward, but the gully narrows a great deal to the west, leaving only a small, dark opening, partly covered by rotting foliage and knee-high ferns.
116014: There is some snow on the ground.

The trail goes through a narrow cleft. You look at some rocks positioned pretty close to the edges above you. You walk swiftly, but with great stealth through the cleft, and no rocks fall down on your head. To the east, the trail is blocked by a huge rock slide. You can't spot any obvious ways to get across it.
116018: An arcane spirit floats around, making strange magical gestures (glowing).

This mining tunnel was built by dwarves long time ago. The tunnels to north and south are caved in and the only options are to go back or continue eastwards. The wall to the north is beginning to crumble, and clear, cold water gushes forth from cracks in the stone.
116019:
There are three piles of wheat cereals here.
An elven farmer is here surveying the land.

Five-foot stalks of golden wheat ripple in gentle sea breezes. The ears are heavy and full of grain, promising a good harvest. The field is protected by the steep slope of a bluff to the east and a long fence that encloses it in all other directions. Deep ruts in the ground lead to a gate in the western fence.
116020: The trail runs under the overhanging rocky shoulder of a hill, and turns northwards going round a steep, brush filled dike. The soil is barren and rocky, encumbered with broken limestone boulders, but the track is well-trodden and easy to follow.
116021:
Traces of pale white tones form the aura of this place.
A small blotchy mushroom grows here.
There are two green slime moulds here.
A warhorse (ulo) is standing here.
A mother eagle (VEL) is sleeping here.
A mother eagle (MAR) is sleeping here.
A great, wild boar (SIGA) is sleeping here.
Uge the Dwarf is standing here.
A stocky mountain mule is here, waiting to serve.

This cave has a very high ceiling, with large stalagmites protruding from the ground. The walls in every direction are lined with large piles of grey, damp gravel. Green and black moss grows prevalently here, thoroughly covering the stones and beginning their ascent up the walls. There is an opening in the cave wall high above, which seems too steep to climb to.
116022: A large boulder is here, it must be heavy.

A few rolling black hills cover the landscape, void of much life and saturated with the presence of evil. The ground is remarkably hard, almost as if the entire hillside is made of black stone. Shooting up from the earth to the north is a steep wall of solid black slate, offset only by the occasional craggy ledge adorned with sharp, serrated rocks. To the south, the dangerous forest of Mirkwood looms, as terrifying as ever.
116024:
A quarrel has been set down on the ground.
A Hillman tracker is here, watching with weary eyes.

Inside, a single burnt out torch on the far wall and a pile of leaves and straw are all that give indications to its occupancy. A campfire has painted the mountain walls black with ashes and soot. It is humid and the sound of dripping water can be heard in a distance. There is a paper in one dusty corner.
116026: An orange dome opens up above, which has a painted crown of stalactites that drip over a massive stalagmite in the centre of the cave. The wicked-looking rock formations range in colour from red to black, and leave watery streaks of white leading down to the cave below. The pillar below looks like a yellow pile of hardened baubles, around which a pool of water has collected.
116027: An albino salamander is here, perched on some rocks.

A natural drapery of rock flows over the ceiling of this cave, as a gentle stream of water trickles along its edge towards the southern grotto. The many slender blades of the drapery course along with one another in a harmonious span of colour, ranging from spotted yellows to dark reds. The cave is rather cramped compared to the other caves, due to the size of the formations above.
116028: A patch of moss grows here on a wet, flat stone.

The entire cave is bathed in a gentle, green light that emanates from the soft moss, which covers the limestone walls. A sandy shore in the south, peppered with moss-covered rocks, extends down to a silent and calm lake. The moss dims on the rock wall in several places, revealing depressions that create a natural stair that climbs up to the dripping cavern above.
116029: Cold water slowly flows through a breach in the cavern wall, into a wave-less lake that fills the huge, domed cave. A slow trickle of water can be heard as the water pours in, and then trickles out through a tiny crevice in the eastern wall. A dim, yellow glow can be seen coming from the mossy shore to the north.
116030: A deep, underwater crack spews extremely cold water forth from some unknown source. The water rushes noisily southwards through the dark, rocky stream channel opposite a slight beveled, ledge in the north, with some natural handholds that lead upwards. The northern cavern above has been boarded off with some dark timber and a dark, heavily rusted, iron cover.
116031: The cold water plunges around several chaotic bends, as it curves through the darkness along the underground caves. The blackened, limestone walls have been worn smooth by the running water, but scrape painfully upon contact. The force of the water slowly quells as it reaches a larger, solemn cave in the east.
116032:
A rosewood chest with runic markings stands in a corner.
A heavy desk, made of solid oak, stands here.
A sturdy crate made of nailed wooden planks sits on the floor.

This dark cave bares the marks of pickaxe blows from when it was enlarged to hold the many crates and chests that reside within it. Placed deep within the caves, the air chills and protects their contents from the outside world. At the far end of the cavern, within an alcove, sits a lone desk made of dark oak. The smell of herbs, paper, and dust hangs heavy in the stale air.
116033:
A black, leather-scaled reptile glances around with gleaming eyes.
A fierce bat is here, lusting for your blood.

The dusty cave is covered with brown dirt and rubble that lies in several huge and disorganized piles. There is so much rubble in the way that the location of a possible tunnel leading elsewhere is nearly hidden. A slight draft that carries moisture can be barely detected leading towards the south.
116034: These cramped tunnels twist and turn into several subpassages. The bottom of the tunnels are covered with a fine layer of soft, dark mud. Several small pools of water can be found at various locations in the dips and bends. A large crack, leading down a muddy passage, can be found in the middle of the biggest passage. The sound of water can be heard running below the muddy crack.
116035: An albino fish is swimming here, looking for some food.

The blackened cavern walls have been worn smooth by the constant passage of water over the millennia. Cold water races through the underground stream, gurgling noisily as it bends around the passages. The bottom of the stream can not be reached easily, but a muddy bottom can be barely seen through the cold, clear depths of the rushing water.
116036: A hairy black spider wraps up a silken package with her hind legs.

The underground stream suddenly takes a turn to the north where a huge pile of rotting logs has accumulated as the passage narrows. A putrid layer of slimey, yellow foam and debris sits on top of the water like a blanket, unable to drift away because of the blockage. The dark cave is smooth due to all the fine mud that is caked with decaying vegetation. The noise of water can be heard from beyond the slimey logs.
116037:
A little stone lies on the ground.
An albino salamander is here, perched on some rocks.
An albino salamander is here, perched on some rocks.

A tiny, cramped chamber sits here where two muddy tunnels meet. The noise of running water can be heard roaring from the northern tunnel, making hearing anything else nearly impossible. The fine, soft dirt that covers the floor of this cavern sinks underfoot. It looks like the mud at the bottom of either tunnel is wet and will stick to anyone who tries to climb up or down them.
116038: A subterranean lizard is here trying to blend with the surroundings.

A formation of yellow and orange limestone bubbles flows over the ledge that overlooks overhead before sliding down several yards to a tunnel that leads northwards. A sound of flowing water can be heard from above. Stalagmites and stalagtites surround the cave among the puddles that shimmer with each dripping droplet of water.
116039:
Some roots lie here waiting to ensnare weary travellers.
Massive roots shift uneasily all around you.
A subterranean lizard is here trying to blend with the surroundings.

Huge, gnarled roots have cracked the limestone ceiling, allowing water to run down their lengths, and staining the ceiling with various colours of black, red, and orange. Each root looks like a curtain made of cloth, as it slowly forks and splits getting smaller and finer. The roots sway back and forth in the drafts that waft through these caves. The noise of running water can be heard from the north and south.
116040:
Something cold and scaly slithers past your leg.
Something cold and scaly slithers past your leg.
A grey snake slides along the water.

Water is flowing slowly here it seems as though there are underground routes where water keeps on running. Most of the routes are very narrow, and they are not possible to enter, and the pull isn't strong enough to give any problems for a swimmer. The underground pool continues to the west of here. A small ledge can be barely spotted towards the east, a little higher on the wall.
116041: The cold, clear water here flows quickly to the north, and the current has a strong pull to the north, which may give problems for a mediocre swimmer. The tunnel is narrow here, and the walls of the tunnel have been smoothed by the flow of water. The tunnel seems to widen to the north, and the noise of the steady flow of water fills the tunnels.
116042: Far Edge of an Underground Pool
A grey snake slides along the water.

The walls of the cavern are slick and black here, and there is so much water that it is not possible to walk here. The water is very cold, and the bottom of the pool is barely visible. A small rocky formation protrudes out of the pool in the middle area. It looks like there are bones and remnants of dead animals surrounding the rock.
116043: A cold shroud of dark grey mist covers the ground.

This narrow, cramped tunnel looks of entirely natural origin. The rock walls are uneven and the tunnel shift in size from a narrow crawlspace to being high and wide enough to drive a wagon through. Common for the entire tunnel is that it's wet and slimy.
116044:
A deeply black, oddly shaped cloud of mist has gathered here.
A large and twisted beast lurks in the rotten pool.

Rough cavern walls of natural bedrock surrounds a murky pool that has formed in a depression here. A small cavern opening to the east is the only way to access this cave. There are some stalactites in the ceiling above where water slowly seeps in to keep the pool full.
116048: Something cold and scaly slithers past your leg.

A few stalactites hang on the cavern ceiling, each over a few feet long. Drops of water fall down from them, resulting in an ever present dripping sound and ripples forming in the dark lake. A few inches of stalagmite break the surface of the lake. Dark grey and green algae cover the lake, hiding its contents even more. The lake occupies the entire cavern, leaving little space for dry feet.
116049: Several fir planks have been nailed into the crown of this sturdy oak providing a place of rest. The position of this platform has been carefully thought out and hidden due to the heavy foliage. A clever hatch in the floor provides access back down the tree but a sloping branch to the east seems to serve a similar purpose.
116050: Colourful wildflowers cover the slopes among the green grasses that fill the valley; the enclosing ridges widen slightly in the east. The black soil is rich and sinks slightly as it gives away underfoot. A couple of young birch trees grow on the western slope, near the entrance to a narrow valley pass.
116051: The grassland dips in between the feet of two ridges, where it widens into a broad plain of green heather. The grass runs southwards across the valley, where a dark marsh can be seen shrouded in faint mist. A large animal has been grazing on the steppe here, leaving deep hoof impressions in the wet soil and sheered grass. A patch of bare bedrock rises out of the valley floor to the east.
116052: A large black bull stamps his hooves, whilst examining the surroundings.

The ridge crests at the top of a grassy hill, where the bedrock disappears under the thick heather and soil. A view of an enormous, black forest in the far east fills the horizon, as a dark marsh in the southwest lurks in a cloak of grey mist. The vivid grasslands of heather stretch onward through the wetlands and stones to some dark crags on the southern ridge.
116053:
A wild bull seems ready to charge you.
A large black bull stamps his hooves, whilst examining the surroundings.

The wet grasslands sink underfoot as water saturates the sod from some unknown source. The flat area is covered in a vivid, multicoloured array of grasses that ranges from near violet to dark green. Several bunches of strong smelling weeds grow here, displaying white blooms among the wild flowers.
116054: The grasslands extend out towards the north and west, right before a rocky ridge that climbs to the south. The earth is wet and sinks underfoot when any weight is placed upon it. A variety of plants grows in the soil, displaying a large number of shapes among the thickets of long grasses. A couple round droppings, shaped like pies and filled with grass, litter the ground.
116055:
A large marmot is here, scurrying in between the rocks.
A wild bull seems ready to charge you.

The rising ridge reaches an overhanging precipice, where a large pile of rubble have accumulated at its face. Dense thickets of grasses and shrubs cover the slope of the ridge. Further to the east, a distant, dark forest can be seen, while to the north, an expanse of wet lands and marshes shrouded in mist covers the wide valley, before disappearing into another pair of ridges.
116056: The ridge rises up to a dark limestone precipice in the south and west, where two separate ridges can be seen: one falling towards the north and the other bending towards the east. Several green shrubs cover the ground, forming vivid thickets amidst the grasses that grow in the rich soil. A dark marsh can be seen in the mist to the northwest, while wetlands extend further to the east.
116057: A marsh extends to the north, through a deep mire filled with black muck. Lush grasses grows in small clumps around the wet meadow, where the land dips around the small pools of water. A muddy wallowing-pool of filthy water, encircled by crushed grass and strewn grime, lies here with hoof tracks leading to and from it. The land rises as the southern, grass-covered ridge falls into the marsh.
116058:
A giant brown turtle is peeking from under its shell.
A brown toad is here, hunting flies.

Sedges and reeds grow in a small row to the north, as the land opens up into a foul-smelling bog. Several pools of mud run through the land, split by large islands of multicoloured grass and weeds. The stench of decaying plant matter fills the air as a fine, grey mist floats gently on the surface of the water.
116059:
Clusters of slender stems and tall leaves thrive in the mud and shallows.
A shimmering glow is here, emitting pale, green, light.

A stinking bog of grime spreads out across the land, filling it with layers of mulch and pools of muddy water. Lush grasses grow in huge mounds where the land rises up above the muck; there is some evidence of a large animal grazing. The area is filled with a fine mist that reeks with the stench of decaying plant matter. The foul marsh continues towards the southwest, shrouded in grey mist.
116060:
There are two tall, grey-green plants here.
A moderately-sized copperhead snake is here.
A large green shrub grows in the middle of a large pool of mud.

A misty marshland, surrounded by rows of dark reeds and sedges, courses around the murky channels that snake through the bog. A fine, wispy layer of grey mist moves above the muck, where thick patches of long grasses rise above the foul, bracken water. A deep and black pond stirs to the northwest, where it sits under the face of a rocky precipice, enclosed by the surrounding ridge-walls.
116061: A giant form rustles among the trees.

The forest to the southeast does not entirely reach to the edge of this plateau above the valley. Instead a brushland, with the same kind of thick undergrowth as within the forest, spreads towards the edge. Parts of the valley and the trail following it below can be watched from here, but going down is impossible because of the steep slope.
116076: Deep within the infinity of this enormous sea of grass, like a tiny vessel drifting in the roaring ocean, you are at the mercy of the great surges of grass raised by the wind. When it blows, the whole mass of grass bends to and fro, and huge green waves run all through the grassland, the high blades swinging regularly, and the noise of their incessant rubbing, along with the shriek of the wind, contributing to the stormy atmosphere.
116109: The path is leading through dense vegetation northwards towards an unknown destination. West of the path is the road to the Grey Havens. To the south a barrier of trees is making progress in that direction impossible. To the east the path is bordered with undergrowth. The path looks like it is not used very often or the ones using it leave no tracks.
116110: A broken muddy trail runs alongside a fast flowing river, just west of here. Delicate, slender trees grace the rivers edge and their long, slim branches extend over the river below. It should be possible to scramble your way down the steep banking into the river from here. Two buildings can be seen to the northeast while a road runs by south of here.
116112: At first glance, this small bridge appears quite sturdy, but its pine boards creak and wobble as soon as anyone sets foot upon them, threatening to tip the unwary into the small stream, which flows lazily from east to west, below. To the north and south, the bridge is met by an old trail, much worn by the passage of many feet, over the years.
116113: Water flows from the west, turning south in this underground river. The mass of water fills the tunnel completely and the constant flowing makes swimming difficult. The rock walls are mostly black, but there are a few lighter patches here and there. The stream seems to resurface slightly eastwards.
116114: Rising a few inches above the water, a rock allows weary explorers some ground to rest on. Water washes the rock constantly, making it slippery and wet. The massive walls are dark and damp, with patches of fungal growth. Darkness lies above, concealing the roof somewhere up in the shaft.
116116: Rough, rocky stone formations form the walls, roof and floor of this cavern. They show no signs of being used by the dwarves, except as an airshaft for the smoke from the armoury. Several piles of bat droppings and skeletons of tiny animals lay scattered on the ground. Fresh air fills the cave, flowing from the airshaft leading upwards.
116117:
A bloodthirsty bat is sleeping here.
A bloodthirsty bat is sleeping here.

Further up in the crack, the walls begin to close in on each other. The way up gets tighter and tighter, eventually becoming too narrow for anything except small birds or bats to pass through. The chimney widens again downwards as it opens up into a small cave.
116121:
The remains of a clump of roots lie here in a heap of rotting compost.
The remains of a clump of roots lie here in a heap of rotting compost.

A small tunnel coming from the east ends in a pool of water here. This tunnel seems to have been unused for a long period of time, as roots have grown in the wet tunnel and are blocking much of the water. The water is dark but clear, showing few signs of the bottom below.
116124: A swallow flies high above the ground.

Grass and shrubs grow wild all around. The ground is broken, making travel difficult. Here and there among the grass a large stone sticks out like a giant head. Some thickets of thorny bushes create an impenetrable wall to the west. A trail circles this place to the east and to the north.
116125: A small rustic bed is the only piece of furniture in this tiny hut. A few simple tools hang from pegs, which have been driven into the wall in a neat row, and above them a plain wooden shelf bears some wooden plates and small boxes. Wind blows through tiny chinks in the walls, and a square opening, serving as a window, is unglazed. Clearly this must be the home of one who has little care for treasures or comfort.
116126: A small, dense tangle of roots covers the ground.

Large rocks and boulders have broken free from the hillsides to the north and west, coming to rest at the edge of a broad plain. Many species of wild bushes have made their home here, squeezing in between the rocks and clinging to every patch of soil they can find. While the bushes grow clustered in tangled messes, there is ample room to move between the thickets with ease.
116128: A narrow tunnel has been dug here, burrowing through the hill. It's dug at an angle, creating a sloping passage that is difficult to navigate. At times the tunnel makes a tight curve to bypass an obstacle. In a few places, small ladders have been installed on the pathway to enable getting past vertical rock walls. In some places the ground is smooth rock and in some places, rough gravel.
116130: You have a superb view over the whole valley from here. You can see a few houses in the valley, small fields and farms. The castle wall itself is a simple stone wall with embrasures. Archers shooting arrows from here can reach every point in the valley. It seems to be impossible to take this stronghold.
116131: The higher the Tower Hills rise in the sky, the thinner the vegetation tends to become. First the higher bushes vanish and then the lower ones until at the top only grass is growing along with moss and lichen which cover the rocks. Looking east, it seems possible to climb to a small plateau. The Tower Hills continue to rise in the south-west direction.
116134: Once off the road the terrain becomes quite rough: long grasses blow in the wind, the gradual rise and fall of the downs broken by the occasional gully eroded by the action of the weather on the chalk. There is little sign of any form of habitation in the area - the road running to the south and a fairly well-trodden path are the only indications that anybody passes through this way at all. A small pile of stones has been built here.
116135: Pebbles, rocks, and other natural debris cover the narrow valley floor here, with the hillside looming to great heights in every direction other than the south. A slight decline can be noticed along the valley floor leading there, where several patches of yellow and scrawny weeds are struggling to grow.
116136: The valley leads to the north and south from here, with a steep hillside that stands along the west and east. There are rocks and debris scattered along the valley floor everywhere from the hills decaying over time, with small patches of weeds growing randomly along the ground.
116137: A dark hillside stands to both the south and east, where it climbs to a greater height as it travels north. Patches of rock, pebbles, and other debris that has decayed from the hills lay scattered along the valley floor leading toward the west and north. The northern area of the valley seems to have a slight incline. Patches of yellow grasses and weeds are trying to grow the best they can in the valley.
116138: The ground is overgrown with patches of weeds and tall grasses. There are many areas covered with pebbles and small rocks, and the vegetation appears to diminish towards the west side of the hill. The pebbles and rocks are dark coloured and appear to have come from the surrounding hills itself over time. The steep hillside blocks any travel from the north or the south, and continues to the east from here.
116139: A squirrel scampers around here, looking for nuts from the trees.

You are well up on the tree. You see squirrels go whizzing by, playing an intricate game of tag through the treetops. Looking out through the branches, you marvel at the view. To the south-west you notice a small orchard. North-east of here, you see a simple hobbit farm. To the south-east, you see a grassy plain.
116140:
You see three piles of acorns on the ground.
A squirrel scampers around here, looking for nuts from the trees.

Hanging on for dear life, you get buzzed by a couple of squirrels. You begin to wonder what drove you to wander out on such a precarious perch. The view is great but there are some prices too great to pay for just a view and your life is certainly one of them.
116141: You stand in a forest; the many trees around you restrict your view to a few paces. Most of the trees are oaks and beeches, and heavy vegetation covers the ground. The humidity is so intense you can almost touch it.
116142: You are making your way through high vegetation when you suddenly realise there is a passage to the forest from here. The wall of trees to the east blocks the passage and view. Not much light could ever pass through those leaves. You can enter the woody end forest to the east or keep following the road.
116143: You are making your way through high and dense vegetation when you suddenly realise there is a passage to the forest from here. The wall of trees to the west prevents the passage and blocks out the view. Not much light filters through the leaves. You can enter the wooded end of the forest to the east or continue to follow the road.
116145: The various paths around and through the woods are all coming to a junction right here, the east-westward paths are very clearly on sight but the ones going south are quickly swallowed by the trees. You can barely see the Stock Road to the north. There is some structure above the trees there too.
116146: The ground here is so muddy that grass has problems growing in it. The loud noise of the river briskly flowing just north of here drown all other sounds such as bird songs that could be heard elsewhere. To the south, the dark straight line of a road can be seen.
116156: An enormous hall stretches to the south and the east. This was once the great banquet hall of the kings of Arthedain, told to have been one of the finest places ever built by men in Eriador. There is not much to remind you of its greatness left. The hall lies shrouded in darkness, and the thick air makes it heavy to breathe. West of here, you see a small, winding staircase making its way up into some kind of tower.
116158: A pale ghost advances forward, shimmering with a pale light.

You are now in a small room very near the top of the tower. You shiver as a howling sound breaks the silence, and you desperately try to convince yourself that it was nothing but the wind trying to tear down the old castle. It doesn't look as if there was a battle fought in this room, since it, as opposed to the rest of the castle, doesn't have bones and rusted weapons lying all over the floor.
116164: A humble man stands here, ready to help you with your things.

Shelves dominate three of the walls here, with a bed standing in the corner of the fourth wall. A wooden table and chairs stand in the middle of the room, across from the door. The door appears to be plated with a darkened steel, which provides more protection to the shelter. The stone walls look carefully constructed and look sturdy enough to withstand anything. In each corner of the ceiling there are small lanterns attached to steel hooks, bolted firmly into the wall at the top; the soft light emitting from the silver lanterns create a calm ambience to the bunker, yet provide enough light to see.
116166: A black raven flies in the sky searching for flesh to prey upon.

This enormous felled tree now spans the Nen Kalthar where the old rock crossing that linked the path from the forest to the Road to Tharbad used to be. Since a flood washed out the western half of the crossing, this slippery tree serves as the only bridge across the river for miles. Below, you can hear the waters gurgling past the rocks of the old crossing.
116167: Looking around here, a well-trodden track can be seen to the west, seemingly left by wagons. The wheel-ruts run all the way into the yard, where the wagons load with grain destined for a nearby Dunlending camp. There is an incredible stench drifting in from the south, where an animal pen lies. East is a rose garden, while north is the main farmhouse.
116170:
A circular stone well has been built here.
A large beautiful rose bush is blooming here.
Deep inside the bush, there is a red rose with leaves and thorny stem.
A large beautiful rose bush is blooming here.
Deep inside the bush, there is a red rose with leaves and thorny stem.
A bee flies around here, collecting nectar from the flowers.
A bee flies around here, collecting nectar from the flowers.
A bee flies around here, collecting nectar from the flowers.
A bee flies around here, collecting nectar from the flowers.
A dove rests near one of the flowers.

A cherished garden has been planted here. There is a gazebo in the far eastern corner. There are rows of rose bushes, mostly grouped by colour. Between the rows, there is soft lush green grass, soft enough to lay down on. There is a bird bath located in the centre of the rows, and a small clearing and a few benches to rest on. This garden is surrounded on three sides by a huge stone wall, too tall to climb.
116172:
A black crow flies low to the ground here, looking for carrion to eat.
A black crow flies low to the ground here, looking for carrion to eat.

The wastelands sprawl out around you in all directions, covered with gritty sand and broken boulders as far as the eye can see. A fine web of dark cracks can be seen along its flat surface, made by the drought. Nearby, to the north stands a giant, black silhouette of a tree, strangely alone in the flatness.
116173: The ground above has collapsed, forming this dusty, rocky cave. Sharp rocks and debris, partially hidden in the soft earth, are strewn all about. A pile of larger rocks form a makeshift wall to the north. Small strands of dirt sift down from cracks in the ceiling continuously, giving the illusion that something tiny is digging in the sand, creating a miniscule but constant movement.
116174: The dike is deep and does not seem to have eroded naturally. With even, smooth walls the dike effectively prevents armies trying to cross, both from north and south. The ground is uneven, with many sharp rocks and debris scattered. The dike continues in both the east and west directions.
116175:
A holly bush with dark green leaves is growing here.
Partly covered by the bush's green leaves, there are a few inkberries.
A tall stag is here, grazing peacefully.

Every once in a while, a distant wolf howl breaks the idyllic scene set by this grassy hill. The howls seem to come from the thick forest to your east. In every other direction are fertile hills, covered by a sparse forest. Further west, the small hills give way to much larger hills, ones appearing very rocky and jagged.
116177: Tangled brambles in all directions rising as high as an ordinary housetop - if there were houses or any sign of civilisation here - obscure the vision and reduce travel to an utter crawl. There is no path in this muddy earth, though some odd small footprints can be seen in the mud. Briars tear at the legs, and thorny canes spring back at the eyes as you struggle through.
116178: A stone troll is standing here, scowling about.

At the very centre of the dark and dreaded forest, the evil force pulses through the trees themselves. Twisted, yet titanic, they stretch far above you, holding you with their choking embrace. Everything here is black, forcing you to jump at shadows to explore this small clearing. The hideous stench of filthy and disgusting beings mingles with the decaying leaves, forcing you to gag even as you try to rekindle the spark of courage.
116180: A sparrow is flapping around on the ground.

This bridge is located at a spot were the Nen Kalthar is rather narrow. It is a high bridge - not too high to jump into the water, but certainly too high to permit a traveller to climb upon it from the flowing waters below. Made from blue-grey stones, this construction arches smoothly across the river, with a wide, low parapet to either side, perfect for sitting and resting upon.
116181:
A Dunadan soldier is here busily performing his duties.
A man passes by, intent on his business.

You are standing in the large entrance hall to the soldier quarters. This is the place where the daily briefings are held. The room has something cold and businesslike about it, and the floor has been waxed not long ago. A corridor leads east to the commandants office and the prison cell.
116183: A humble man stands here, ready to help you with your things.

This glade is surrounded by large gnarled trees blocking out most of the natural light. In the larger patches of light grow many red roses that sing with an unfamiliar beauty. Near the middle of the glade, there is a small courtyard paved with black marble stones. The centre of the courtyard is dominated by a fountain made from a strange black stone that seems to absorb the light around it lending an erie quality to the scene. Surounding this courtyard are several obsidian statues that have been carved into figures of the fallen kings of Gondor. On one side, a bronze plinth sits empty, awaiting the final statue. Some letters are carved in the plinth. To the east there is a massive marble staircase leading up to black steel-banded ghostwood door set into the western face of an enormous tower. To the west lies an archway with a twisted iron gate leading out into the bustling city beyond.
116184: The base of the tower here has a small landing with a narrow set of grey stone stairs that lead upward in a spiral around the inside of the tower. Despite the many years of service, the stones do not show any wear from use. To the west is a steel banded door.
116186:
A small reptile with large eyes scurries along the walls.
An albino salamander is here, perched on some rocks.
An albino salamander is here, perched on some rocks.

Cold, wet, and muddy, this dark hole has been created under the cavern floor above. Whether it was created intentionally or naturally is unknown. Various insects inhabit this place, a great source of food for the plethora of salamanders that are found down in this area of the caves.
116187:
A water barrel has been left here.
A huge, smoking campfire is burning here.
A stone troll is standing here, scowling about.
An ancient she-troll waits here.
A small, mean earth troll is standing here, thinking of something hideous.
A stone troll is standing here, scowling about.
A powerful young troll stares at you.
A small, mean earth troll is standing here, thinking of something hideous.
A hungry warg stands here, sniffing around for flesh.

Filthy can hardly describe this room. Just by looking about you, you surmise that some group of horrid creatures has been living here for years, without ever bothering to clean anything or show any civility. The centre of the room holds a sizzling fire, and the smoke exits via the hole in the roof. Several large rocks and tree trunks have been arranged to serve as furniture, and an unmistakable odour forces you to wrinkle your nose -- Trolls!
116188:
An infant troll, baring its teeth, snarls here.
An infant troll, baring its teeth, snarls here.
An infant troll, baring its teeth, snarls here.
A nasty troll female crouches here, with a feral look in her eyes.
An infant troll, baring its teeth, snarls here.
An infant troll, baring its teeth, snarls here.
A small, mean earth troll is standing here, thinking of something hideous.
A powerful young troll stares at you.
A powerful young troll stares at you.
A small, mean earth troll is standing here, thinking of something hideous.

Here refuse and garbage and waste is piled up, often waist high. Bones from some previous victims stick out at vicious angles from the heaps, and rotting flesh and dung fill the air with a thick, disgusting smell. Something squirms within the disgusting mess, revolting you even further.
116189: The ancient walls are wreathed in painted flames, strewn by an enormous wyrm.

This was once a well-crafted passage. The walls are made of smooth slabs of grey stone, but time has not been kind to them. Many are cracked and a few lie shattered on the ground, showing the black basalt rock behind.
116190:
An ancient Elven mural decorates the walls, depicting a victory over the wyrm.
A large black bat flitters near you.

This passageway continues to both the east and west. The walls are well-made and clad in slabs of grey stone. The walls encroach on the passageway on both sides, and the hall is three times as high as it is wide.
116191: Ages old building material stands stacked against the walls in this chamber. Everything is caked in dust and it is clear nothing here has been used for a very long time. Most of the material is slabs of grey stone, seemingly the same material used for the walls here.
116192:
The illustrated walls recount the sealing of the great wyrm and its foul lair.
A large black bat flitters near you.
Dark and narrow, this underground passageway connects to a larger chamber to the east. Dust has gathered on the floor and many of the slabs the walls are made of are cracked.
116193:
A stone statue with Elven features stands watch here, spear in hand.
A stone statue with Elven features stands watch here, spear in hand.
A stone statue with Elven features stands watch here, spear in hand.
A stone statue with Elven features stands watch here, spear in hand.
Klaees (thedon), wielding a black metal staff, is standing here.

A layer of dust cakes everything in this large, open chamber. The chamber is mostly empty, except for several statues that stand ready, clad in stone armour with their swords drawn. Some of the statues have crumbled completely and lie on the floor in piles of rubble, others are missing limbs.
116194:
A huge black fungus is here, exuding a foul stench.
A knotty tree grows here, entangled in a rotten mess of wet shrubbery.

The unyielding blanket of darkness and evil that covers the whole forest does not seem any less thick here. All the plants here, including a dense wall of stinging nettles to the north, seem to twist in pain in the breeze. All are tortured and malformed, disease and decay masking their natural shapes.
116195: Moving through this dense forest is tough, and is made no easier by the clawing branches that grasp down from above. One must constantly stoop and duck to toil onward through the dark, twisting trees. Many strange rustlings and hissings emanate down from the branches overhead, though it is not clear whether it is from the trees moving in the wind or from some vile creatures within them. What looks like impassable debris blocks access north and west. To the south, the brambles are thick, but passage seems possible.
116196: The ledge is clear of any rubble or debris, with a few skeletons decaying along edges of a cavern entrance. The ledge leads to the east, where the entrance almost appears to be yawning widely. The ledge leading down is steep and it is hard to judge the distance below.
116197: Large slabs of rock and granite have fallen from above and formed gaping cracks and crevices in the cave floor. A small, murky pool of water has formed beneath where some of the slabs have punched through. A green film forms a slight sheen on the surface of the water, and a green slime has accumulated around its edges. Occasional ripples can be seen on the surface.
116198: The cloudy, murky water makes visibility extremely limited. The jagged rock walls and floor are covered in a slippery, green slime. Visual navigation is next to impossible due to the dense murk. As the water and anything that is settled in it is disturbed, visibility becomes even more cumbersome.
116199: Visibility is extremely limited due to the murk of the water. Through the murk, barely discernible walls can be made out, covered in some green slime. The walls and floor seem to run off to the west, but the cloudiness of the water makes anything uncertain.
116200:
A pool has formed in a hollow in the rock, its water dark and clouded.
A long slender eel glides along the water, its body coiled to strike.
A long slender eel glides along the water, its body coiled to strike.

The cave to the north leads to this small niche near the murky pool. The water is dark and clouded deeper within the pool. Near the edges the stone of the cavern is more visible. Moss grows heavily along the stone walls here; bright green near edge of the water and darker green toward the western side of the pool. The ground is damp and humidity fills the air.
116201: A subterranean lizard is here trying to blend with the surroundings.

The cave is expansive to the north and east, with moss growing in patches along the wall. Cobwebs hang in several places, most appearing to be abandoned long ago. Almost the entire southern wall of the cave is covered by webs both old and new, with natural debris being trapped within. The cave opens up along the western side where a ledge appears to be; the ground slightly inclined and less damp as it leads to the ledge.
116202: The cavern walls are black basalt to the south and east, connecting to a low ceiling that is both rough and uneven. The ground is rough and dark like the walls, with dying moss scattered along the ground in patches. Humidity and dampness can be felt towards the northern area of the cave here and the air appears less thick toward the west.
116203: A subterranean lizard is here trying to blend with the surroundings (hidden).

The dark cave expands in every direction other than the east, where there must have been a large cave-in recently, judging from the dust still settling and the worn path that disappears under the rock and debris. The black basalt rubble from the cave-in looks to be impossible to clear.
116204: The air is damp within the cave here and it becomes quite thick towards the eastern side. Although it is dark and murky, there are small patches of moss growing throughout the cave; the moss is a deep green and appears to be thriving on the humidity and darkness here. The walls of the cave expand to the west and south, and a slow drip of water can be heard echoing off the cavern walls to the east.
116205: A subterranean lizard is here trying to blend with the surroundings.

The dark ground is damp from humidity throughout the murky cave, which continues to both the south and east. The cavern wall rises beyond sight to the north and west, with moss growing from the tiny cracks and crevices along the base of the walls. The moss is a deep green in patches along the edges of the cave, making it appear as if a worn path was formed along the ground from the southern and eastern areas of the cave.
116206:
A subterranean lizard is here trying to blend with the surroundings.
A fell drake roams the caves, bristling at the slightest sound.

The murky and dark cave is wide here, continuing in all directions other than the west, where the cavern wall rises beyond sight into a deeper darkness. Moss grows along the western wall, rooting into the rocks and crevices where it can.
116207: The cave to the south widens here at a long and steep ledge. The damp and murky air from the southern cave lingers here, and a slight draft can be felt leading downward beyond the ledge and out of sight. Moss grows along the mouth of the cave to the south, but the ledge itself is bare and the ground is dark. Some of the ledge appears to be worn, as if often used to reach whatever is below.
116208:
A newborn spider is here, hungrily crawling about.
A newborn spider is here, hungrily crawling about.
A newborn spider is here, hungrily crawling about.
A newborn spider is here, hungrily crawling about.
A grey spider is stalking here, preparing to drain you of life.

This lair has only one way out and that is to the west, where the black basalt walls are covered by fresh and old webs. Several cocoons are suspended within the webbing, with dry corpses decaying inside them. Although it is too high to reach, there are many holes in the ceiling above that appear to be tunnels that twist beyond sight. Moss growing along the base of the cavern walls that lead to the mass of cobwebs to the west is drying out and slowly dying. Cracked shells and other debris are scattered throughout the lair.
116210: An enormous dragon skull blocks passage to the north.

A chamber with walls of slabs of grey rock, well crafted but old. A passage to the west exits the chamber, and there is another opening to the north. A huge skull has been forged into the walls around the northern opening, from the look of it a monstrous wyrm.
116211: A vast cavern of epic proportions expands endlessly to the east and north. The walls, if they even exist, are shrouded in veils of darkness and gloom. The floor of the cavern is smooth but littered with old, crumbled items. Here and there, something shiny glitters amongst the garbage.
116212: The walls are covered with the scratches of giant claws. The ceiling so high it's lost in darkness and can't be seen. In one place, there are some narrow but very deep cracks in the cavern's floor where the rock has split apart. A faint sulphurous stench wafts up from the unknown depths.
116213: Dark Corner in a Dragon's Hoard

Lhurank (brenny), wielding a darkened orkish axe, is standing here.
Von (twitter), wielding an ornate, steel-shafted warhammer, is standing here searching for something.

Once, these vast caves extended to the north and west. In a past age, the cave must have collapsed, for a large cave-in blocks the way. The floor is mostly smooth, aside from where rents of long deep grooves mar it. Scattered across the ground are piles of what might have been treasure once upon a time, though it has long since mostly rotted, rusted, and crumbled.
116214: Far Corner in a Dragon's Hoard

A large cavern expands to the west and south from this dark corner. Black rock make up the walls and ceiling, and most likely the ground as well although it is covered by millennia of dust and dirt. There is also an enormous amount of old, decayed junk gathered in piles.
116215: A slight depression in the floor here, the ground is slightly lower than the surrounding caves. As a result, extra much dust and rubbage have gathered here. The eastern wall is scored by deep gouge marks, it looks almost like an enormous creature had a hissy fit here.
116216: Treasure-filled part of a Dragon's Hoard

An elegant marble chest sits against the wall.
A solid ironbound chest is here.
A large stone chest is here.

Ancient items litter this cavern. Chests, ancient relics, glittering things resting amongst piles of rotted cloth, these halls seems to hide an unimaginable wealth. All of it appearingly unguarded, for a layer of dust coates everything.
116217: Entrance to an Angmar Burial Mound

A dark intangible shadow turns to face you.
A dark intangible shadow turns to face you.

A narrow tunnel leads into the centre of the hill. The main room is a perfect circle, and on the walls there are Angmarian runes. In the centre of the circle is a round stone-trapdoor. It glows a deep blue, and is much too heavy to be lifted. You spot a hole in the northern wall.
116218:
An old, but powerful uruk of the Zaugurz tribe stands here.
Grobb the Zaugurz ranger is here on the lookout for enemies.

During the march of time this shallow cavern has been smoothened by decades of wind and rain. The ceiling slants sharply towards the sky, leaving minor protection against the brute force of nature. The polished floor has been ruptured close to the inner cavewall to establish a place for the trapdoor leading down into the mountain. At the centre of the cave, rather close to the trapdoor, a large bell has been mounted.
116219: The memorial statue of Ugurz rises in the chilly cavern, covered in ice.

Frost and ice line the sides and floor of this cavern, having been blown in by the wind from the smoothed cave entrance to the south. The constant wear of the elements has caused a cascade of cracks to form in the domed ceiling where an enormous ring of icicles now hang; crowning the centre of the cavern.
116220: After walking past the road through a rather flat area, you find yourself on the top of a small cliff. You look down from the top into the riverbed of the Sirannon. The river is dry now, but the former stream has dug a cliff in the soft ground, not more fifteen feet high. The sheer cliff rises to the west of the riverbed.
116221: There is a lot of snow on the ground.

The ground falls away abruptly south of the pass. Here and there lies a scrawny scrub-brush grasping the stony ground as the trail continues to the north and east. Looking up the mountain eastward, snow gathers in the shadows and depressions of the ground.
116223: The path travels north and west from here, where boulders of varying size dot the area. They appear to have fallen from higher up the mountain, though just how remains unclear. Where not covered by snow they have a distinct red hue. When the weather permits, the air is crystal clear here on the side of this greatest of the Misty Mountains.
116235: Directly to the east, a dam of large boulders and tree trunks has been constructing - completely choking the flow of the Sirannon. Only a few rivulets force their way through the barrier, and they quickly merge and flow over the Stair Falls, which have been reduced to barely a trickle. The shallow valley beyond the dam is now home to a dark, still lake of stagnant water, which seemingly extends all the way to the Walls of Moria at the head of the valley. To the north, the ground is too rough to traverse, but the old Hollin Road can be made out as it wends its way up to this height.
116236: A fierce wolverine is here, snarling at you.

A broad fissure cuts several feet into the rock, its upper edge filled with a dense tangle of weeds and brambles. Below the surface, the fissure gradually narrows until it vanishes entirely. A layer of soil has accumulated in the base of the crack. Countless scratches mar is surface, and in one spot the ground has been hollowed out into a shallow bowl.
116238: A haggard man dressed in tattered robes is here, willing to teach his art.

The stone floor of this tower is very old and in poor repair, and provides unstable footing. Plains are visible to the north, bisected by a well-travelled road. The city lies to the south-west with all its small and dark houses, split into two parts by the Greyflood.
116239: The path runs east and west from here, surrounded by tall grass and small bushes while the path itself is covered by short grass and some dirt. North of the path a slope slowly rises up towards some cliffs further north. The slope is gentle and easy to access with its soft grass. Southwards from the path the area is covered with endless grassy plains.
116240:
The corpse of a white rat is lying here.
The corpse of a white rat is lying here.
The corpse of a white rat is lying here.
The corpse of a subterranean lizard is lying here.
A subterranean lizard is here trying to blend with the surroundings (hidden).
Skynd the Hill Troll is standing here.
Cromdreath (CC) is standing here.
Gravy the Black Numenorean is standing here.

A tunnel from the west ends abruptly here. A pile of boulders, rocks of all sizes, and other debris blocks the passage in all other directions. What remains of the low, uneven ceiling appears unstable and likely to collapse at any moment.
116241:
The corpse of a subterranean lizard is lying here.
A white centipede is here.

The tunnel passes through soft, unstable rock, with passages leading to the north and east. The limestone walls and ceiling are crumbling, and large sections have sloughed off, leaving large scars and jagged-edged craters. The floor is littered with scree, making it difficult to walk.
116242: Twisting and turning, this tunnel generally runs north-south, but it is easy to lose track of time and distance while following its zig-zag path. Fissures in the soft stone create intricate patterns, with hair-like cracks criss-crossing larger cracks of varying sizes.
116243: A long, narrow shaft seems to extend nearly infinitely north and south. Piles of fine rubble and shale line the floor, revealing the instability of the surrounding stone. The air here is strangely still, but not stale, with no odour at all.
116244:
A large bat is here, hanging in the darkness.
A large bat is here, hanging in the darkness.
A bloodthirsty bat is sleeping here, hanging from the ceiling.
A huge bat is here, emitting piercing squeaks.

A tunnel from the south opens into a large limestone grotto. Stalagmites of all sizes grow from the floor, reaching upwards towards the roof far above, while stalactites hang from above. Standing beneath these geologic structures is imprudent, as evidenced by several piles of rubble on the cavern floor.
116245: Traces of rich red tones form the aura of this place.

This room is cut from hardened mud and limestone. Water dripping from the walls and the ceiling indicates that a water source is nearby. The walls seem fragile enough to break at any moment. There is a musty smell emanating from the chamber above. There are coloured doors to the east and the west. To the north, an exceedingly powerful field of magic blocks anything beyond it.
116246:
Traces of rich red tones form the aura of this place.
A pile of black, shattered crystal lies in the centre of the room.

This chamber is cut from a strange resonating crystal. Shaped like a huge bell, every tiny sound echoes throughout the chamber, vibrating the strange crystal formations. The vibrating crystals emit a lovely high-pitched musical sound. In the very centre of the room, a crystal pillar stands up from the floor. This pillar seems to be the source of the sound.
116248: This is a small chamber which has remained hidden through the generations. There is a rather large table and a few chairs stacked around it. All the furniture is still serviceable. The table is piled high with a great many things, covered with dust and draped with spiderwebs. Some bookshelves line the west wall.
116249:
The corpse of a ferocious warg is lying here.
A disgusting forest troll is searching for fresh meat here.

There is no path through this dark forest, but a lack of ground vegetation makes travel fairly easy. Dense pines block out nearly all natural light from this area. Now and then sounds echo between the trunks, but they are not from birds.
116250:
A large cabinet capable of storing goods is here.
A humble man stands here, ready to help you with your things.

A proper hobbit hole it is, cosy, well lit, and of course tidy as ever. Porthole sized windows are dotted about the walls and well polished wood makes up the floor. Plush, decorated rugs lie underfoot while up above a tiny chandelier dangles from the ceiling. It looks like an good place to rest one's tired feet!
116251: A large brown snake with black patches is coiled here.

The boulders to the south and the brush to the north make life miserable here. In some places bushes grow so close to the boulders that the passage must be won by climbing the boulders themselves. In others, the boulders have rolled across the path and then an exhausting attempt at penetrating the brush must be made. Both the brush and the boulders look unappealing. No sound of birds can be heard, and even insects are still.
116253: A bright red mushroom is growing here.

While the sections of wrought iron fence are mangled almost beyond recognition the posts of the fencing still stand. Through the years saplings that most assuredly would have been cut down to preserve the lawn have grown into trees that now tower several stories high. The fencing is nothing more than a busy tangle at the foot of their trunks. In the shadow of one of the larger trees is a gap in the mess of sharp splinters of iron. A gate hangs closed by its last remaining fasteners. It seems to be frozen in time vulnerable to fall at the mercy of a strong wind. Perhaps it has survived only because of the trees that shelter it from the winds and hard rains.
116255: As you start walking up the mountainside, you notice the path that you left north of you is getting smaller and smaller. And as you get higher up on the slope, the view over the surroundings grows vaster. Stones and small bushes are making it hard for you to walk here, but there is still a long way to climb if you want to reach the top.
116256: A mountain goat is here, jumping from cliff to cliff.

At this height the wind seems to never stop blowing, chilly and freezing. There is nowhere to hide from it. A little bit above you, you can see the snow covering the peak, but it will not be easy to get there and definitaly not safe. Walking back down is the other alternative, but stones are slippy and you might fall.
116257: You have finally reached the top! It took a lot of effort, but now you are here. The view over the Misty Mountains is fantastic, it is possible to see miles away. Far west of you the land is flat and green but northeast the mountains is growing higher and higher. You are standing on a glacier, which probably doesn't even melt in the summer. There might be a small risk that huge parts of it falls down the mountainside, and brings you with it. Anyway, the other side seems even steeper, you better try to climb down the way you came.
116258: A bear is here, covered with coarse black fur.

The tall and big trees growing here are almost all covered by toadstools. In the darkness one should watch their step, because the roots of the trees are lying everywhere. The dark forest continues to the south and east, while to the west and northwest the forest gets less dark.
116261:
A small mushroom grows nearby.
A black snake hurries towards you with sly intentions.
A bear is here, covered with coarse black fur.
A black snake, with red markings, is lying here.

Thick trees grow together here, blocking out all skylight. Nothing else grows here except strange looking fungi. Some of the trees are covered with a thick slimy substance. There is a large fallen tree that can be seen in the darkness. Moss has grown over most of this log, and the smell of decaying wood is prevalent, especially around this log.
116262: The dark forest meets a river and you can hear the sound of running water from the east. On the opposite side of the river there is an old, seldom trodden trail which seems to lead into the Mountains. Maybe it may lead travellers to a pass.
116263:
A hefty stone club is on the ground.
Yzhnag (YY) is sleeping here.
Ragash is standing here.

There are chests in every corner of the room. You see piles of armour and weapons. Other treasure is placed carelessly on the floor. The weapons and the armour don't seem like they are oiled and polished very often.
116264: You have a beautiful overview of the lands around when there is no fog. To the east there are the mountains of Hithaeglir, the Misty Mountains. Southwards the mountains go on past the horizon and east of them is the old kingdom of Rhudaur. Between the mountains there are flat and rocky areas, hills covered by trees and dark forests.
116265:
The corpse of a grizzly cub is lying here.
The corpse of a grizzly cub is lying here.

Here is a small, cosy hole that some animal made deep within the forest. The hole is warm, dry, and clean of any twigs or needles. There is a distinct smell of some kind of animal, but you don't know which. You worry about being in the hole when the residents are here.
116266: The ground consists of solid blue ice. Every few steps you loose your balance and fall down. Large boulders of ice lie around and you find other, even stranger, structures formed from ice. The country is not made for humans or other living beings but has its own odd beauty.
116267: Deep in the Forest of Mirkwood

No ray of light can pierce the dense canopy here. Many giant cobwebs hang in the foliage above. As a result of the permanent darkness here, the vegetation on the forest floor has died. Nothing is left on the forest floor but dead vegetation on otherwise barren soil between the knotted and twisted roots of the dark, looming trees.
116269: Wretched boughs blackened by forces unknown twist and warp around each other and their neighbouring tree trunks amidst a great glade that ever remains as dark as a moonless night. A sense of great hate and vengeance lingers in the stuffy still air beneath the baleful branches, which regularly emit foreboding groaning noises and occasionally produce a loud cracking sound with no visible rhyme or reason.
116282: A sabre is on the ground.

The door the west is dwarfed by the enormity of this room. Shelves have been carved into the rock itself, several of which lie in splinters on the floor. Water trickles down from somewhere above and the iron hinges on the door show signs of rust.
116285: You are in the middle of a large river which slowly strives from the north to the south with a steady flow of water. The surface is somewhat stirred up by strong currents. Through the clear water you can see small fishes swim beneath you.
116286: You are in the middle of a large river which slowly makes its way from the northeast to the southwest with a steady flow. A trail reveals itself on the river bank to the north and a small island can be made out to the south. Far to the west, a small bridge leaps over a tributary of the river.
116310: The shores narrows somewhat here, making the current strong and powerful. You have no other choice but to follow the tributary west, or struggle your way upstreams to the east.
116311: The shores narrows somewhat here, making the current strong and powerful. You have no other choice but to follow the tributary west, or struggle your way upstreams to the east.
116312: There is some snow on the ice.

The river seems really green and dark. You can barely see what looks like the bottom. The mud on the bottom of the river seems to stir every time you paddle why could that be? You can see what looks like a forest up above the bank of the river. You should keep on moving and keep alert. This does not look like a good place to be caught sleeping.
116313:
The corpse of Tom the stone-troll is lying here.
The corpse of Bert the stone-troll is lying here.
The corpse of Bill the stone-troll is lying here.
A pool of thick, red liquid covers a section of the ground.
A butcher knife is lying here.
The shadow of Tom the stone-troll is floating here.

To the west a quite large rock blocks passage into the cave beyond, and an even larger boulder is used as barricade to the south. Here the rock walls and ceiling are dark red-brown, smooth and sooted. The earthen floor is too hard for anything to leave tracks. To the east the cave continues.
116314: The trail descends at a sharp angle from the west to the east, leading down towards a shallow valley cut into the rock. Further ahead, a small stream begins to run parallel to the trail. An almost vertical mountainside rises to the north of you.
116319: The flow of water that is coming from the north brings dark, silt clouded water into this portion of the Anduin River. Along the sides of the river plants seem to struggle to survive despite the amount of water beside them. Brownish, dead foliage of suffocated plants that were sucked into the river floats languidly along on the surface.
116320: A Great Bend in the River Anduin

Flowing more calmly than the waters to the north, the mighty flow of the Anduin follows the curve of the land, gracefully arching in a wide bend from north to east. The steel-grey surface of the river reflects the towering, snow-clad peaks of the Misty Mountains, their forested slopes and foothills marching swiftly away to the west. Eastwards, beyond the next bend in the river, the grassy plains of the Carrock Vale stretch out to the distant horizon, dotted with small stands of trees and the occasional trickling meadow stream.
116321: A Mighty Sweep in the River Anduin

A trout swims here.
A salmon swims here.

The powerful flow of the Anduin, originating from the distant glacier-capped peaks of the Ered Mithrin and fed by numerous streams and rivers from the eastern flanks of the Misty Mountains, completes a wide sweep from west to south here. A cool and refreshing breeze glides across the rippled surface of the steel-grey water as the river's soulful song plays in your ear. In wave after green wave, the grasslands to the east roll out under the open vault of the sky.
116322:
The corpse of a huge stone giant is lying here.
The corpse of a huge stone giant is lying here.
A stocky mountain mule is here, waiting to serve.
A mother eagle is sleeping here.

Though it is now occupied by untidy giants, it seems they have not always been here. Indeed this was once a complex piece of architecture, if what remains is anything to go by. The high arched vaulting still remains intact though large chunks have been smashed out. A dim glow emanates from these upper structures, providing a low illumination. Subtle murals in dark blues and greens have been filthied by the giants, while clots of blood stain the east wall where a humanoid in robes has been driven into the wall. The giants have made themselves quite comfortable, bringing crude chairs and bedding to this place, oblivious to its wondrous nature. The smell is certainly strong.
116323:
A meticulously carved fountain, made from the finest of marble stands here.
Ebrum the Dwarf is standing here.

This room has more of a natural feel to it than the vaulted chamber to the south. Here the stone has been carved and manipulated, creating the impression of being under the eaves of a rock forest. The summer sunlight glittering through the trees, is here replaced by lichens which give off a green phosphorescence on the ceiling. The rocky walls, carved like bark, have rivelets of water snaking down their length, collecting in pools before leaching away into cracks in the floor. The air in here is laden with moisture, cool and still, yet spoiled by the invasive smell of giants.
116324: A giant brown turtle is peeking from under its shell.

In days immemorial the Sea must have covered this land, many layers of sediment settling on the bottom, allowing limestone to form where later the landscape changed and changed until it was finally overgrown by a forest. Many hundreds of miles away from the nearest sea shore, in a now landlocked terrain, fossils and shells of sea-creatures decorate this cavern, most of them broken and crumbled, but some preserved in the limestone almost intact. Still, as the sound of running water reaches here and bounces among the walls, one can almost imagine that it is the sound of the Sea beating at the walls of a harbour.
116325:
A finely crafted crystal lamp is here.
A brook trout is here, swimming in the current.
A brook trout is here, swimming in the current.
A colourful butterfly is fluttering around here.

A few large stones lie in the water, making it possible to cross the stream without getting the feet wet. Even though the trail is well travelled, the light steps of the Elves of this wood have not worn away the mossy coating on the stones. A few mallorn branches were caught among the stones and lie in the current, glistening silvery as the sparkling stream rolls across them.
116326: A clear spring babbles as cool water trickles out of the ground.

A tiny iridescent stream of pure water bubbles out of the ground and over a few haphazardly laid stones. The grass-covered ground rises on either side of it - enough to make sure no one would get their feet wet while collecting water. The spring is concealed within the shadow of a few very tall mellyrn, whose reflection gives the spring water its opalescent glow. The golden forest hinders the view in all directions.
116327: Running above the raging Celebrant, this small forest trail lies in the shadow of the tall mellyrn towering at its border. The forest stand dense and dark, a solemn wall of grey pillars supporting the overshadowing canopy of gold and green. Soft and soothing, the song of the Celebrant blends with the soft whispers of the woods creating a veil of background noise.
116328: A fallow deer is grazing peacefully here.

Running high upon the cliff that rises above the roaring water, this small trail lies in between the river and forest, acting as a border. Bounded by the great grey trunks of the mellyrn and the deep drop down to the raging Celebrant, this is a place of great beauty as well as a place of danger.
116329: This passage is near the surface, judging by the few tree roots that are visible. Somewhere above lie the dark Trollshaws. The walls are made of packed earth, hardened by the passage of time. However, any pleasant earthy smell is overwhelmed by the foetid odour of trolls.
116332:
The corpse of the tipsy thief is lying here.
You see three oak barrels on the ground.
A noticeable crack runs down one of the walls.
A small oaken table has been set here.
On the table, there is a spoon.
A tipsy thief is here, mad at you, because you disturbed his wine-tasting.

On the shelves are bottles of various green and brown colours covered with dust. On quite a few of them the surface is somewhat cleaner where some hand has revealed the name of the container. On the floor is a lot of trash and some footprints which do not look very old.
116333: The wet ground looks as if someone took a giant fist and pushed down the surface to create a large sunken depression, or perhaps it was mined out from underneath by someone. To the west a slope leads upward to some sort of ruins. Southward the mud and water mix to form a viscous quagmire. It looks quite unstable, but one could easily enter it from here.
116334: The water rises now, reaching almost to your knees. Fighting a swift current, the icy water numbs your legs, just when you need them the most to secure your footing. Scanning ahead, it is clear that the water level isn't receding, this is a dead end.
116335:
Traces of fierce red and fierce white tones form the aura of this place.
A funeral chest, carved in bas-relief, finally draws one's attention.
A huge statue made of stone suddenly turns to life.
A huge statue made of stone suddenly turns to life.
A guardian stone beast is here, protecting the grave.
An arcane spirit is here, fighting Staub (SS) (glowing).
A dark wraith is here, fighting Staub (SS).
A dark wraith is here, fighting Staub (SS).
Staub the Dwarf (SS), wielding an engraved broadsword, is here, fighting a dark wraith (glowing).
Maaskantje the Half-Elf (MK), wielding a sharp thorn, is standing here (shrouded).

This small grave chamber is square and dug out in the rocky ground. To make the walls stronger, the builders put stone blocks as pillars and clad the ceiling with thin slabs of rock. A small raised dais in the centre of the room is the evidence that someone powerful and rich was buried here and the violent scenes on the wall that have been carved and painted into the rock clearly indicate this to have been a great warrior.
116336: In this small alcove, just north of the main grave, a small altar stands on the floor. Once sparkling in the light of torches, it is now soiled with blood and dirt. Crude symbols have been painted onto it and what inscriptions that used to be seen have been scratched into oblivion.
116341: The eastern end of a large cave opens up here. The floor consists of flat rocks on the sand, and a heavy layer of dust starts to dance on them as you step from one stone to another. The walls are completely made up of stones, indicating that the hall might have served some greater purpose than a hideout sometime.
116344: The road is rough and ragged, the wheel marks of many wagons still remaining in the brown, well-trodden land. A lush meadow rises above to the north, and the road bends slightly to the south and west. A tree-infested hill rises sharply to the east.
116345: The hills here seem to grow out of one another making the climb all the more treacherous. The ground is soft and numerous times safe footing has to be sought out after slipping in the mud. A tall stand of trees looms over the hill to the west and a group of lower hills lie to the land in the east.
116347: Water bubbles out from an unreachable ledge to the west. The water meanders down a limestone wall to collect in a small pool on the far side of the cave. The ground is covered with muddy sediment and rocks but gets progressively drier as it leads up a small natural stair to the outside world.
116348:
The corpse of a mindless slime is lying here.
The corpse of a mindless slime is lying here.
A little stone lies on the ground.

This thin scar underground has become the passage for water which flows down the western face from above. Water also pours from a thin crack to the west where it has found a route through the limestone. These collected waters of the hill disappear down a narrow tunnel east. Sediment and rocks have formed at the lowest level, and it is quite slippery, the waters threatening to pitch one down this slide.
116351: The ledge ends abruptly on the southern wall of the Deep, the shelf of rock disappearing to the east. Unlike the rest of the ledge one has encountered, the rock here is not slick with water.
