Only condensation prevents the limestone from drying out. The splash of water can be heard clearly from below.
116355: The river's water flows in slow, fitful eddies here; small fish dart about. The bottom is rocky, with mud and debris settled in the irregularities. Old bits of rusted metal, arrowheads, bolts, buckles and the like stick up from the mud. Little or nothing seems to have retained any value.
116356: The large flat rocks that cover the bottom here grow into irregular boulders further west. The current tugs you in that direction, dangerously fast.
116357: The water is still.. The current in the river doesn't seem to affect it down here at this side, making the soil washed here by the river form a soft, swamp-like bottom. The dirt that is floating around here keeps the light from the surface out so it looks dead and calm down here.
116358: The flow of the river is slow here, causing dirt and debris to sink to the bottom. A vague structure can be outlined in the mud, but whether it is manmade or just a heap of debris is hard to tell.
116362: Smooth, hard mud covers the bottom here. Very little vegetation has managed to get a foothold in the swift current. The featurelessness of the bottom leaves little to hold on to, as you drift westward.
116369: The water is still.. The current in the river doesn't seem to affect it down here at this side, making the soil washed here by the river form a soft, swamp-like bottom. The dirt that is floating around here keeps the light from the surface out so it looks dead and calm down here.
116370: The bottom slants slowly upwards to the north, as this is close to the north bank of the river. The water is calm and the bottom is very muddy, with old waterlogged trees and debris having come to rest here.
116376: Bright sand covers most of the bottom around here. The water flows slowly and is relatively clear. The south bank is entangled by roots, and the river gets more shallow.
116386: The river keeps its fast pace with a swift southwestward current. Hard mud covers the bottom, occasionally permeated by brown seaweed. A wrecked boat hosts a few shy fish seeking cover in its hull.
116400: OUCH! The current here is swift and turbulent, smashing you against large boulders. It is almost impossible to keep any sense of direction in the fierce river, since the water is full of bubbles and dirt.
116413:
You see two copper pennies on the ground.
A fat carp swims here.
The current is swift here, pulling you westward. The bottom consists mainly of mixed hard mud, sand, and rounded pebbles. Little catches your eye, as the river carries any debris past this place.
116422: The river bottom is of smooth, hard mud here. As the current is swift it has scoured it clean of any vegetation. A few bits of rusty iron have sunk here, but you cannot tell what they are.
116449: The bottom is rocky and devoid of loose soil here, as the swift current sweeps it away south. You have trouble holding on to the featureless rock. To the south, there is a booming reverberation through the water.
116450: This is a rather deep section of the river. The water is dirty and blocks most of the light from the surface off. The seaweed covered bottom slopes downward to the south. The north bank rises abruptly in a rotten bluff of crumbling limestone.
116451:
The corpse of a nathrach is lying here.
The corpse of a nathrach is lying here.

The sound of flowing water drenches almost every other sound. This offers a sense of security, since no one will be able to hear your doings from here unless you make a very loud noise. But then again, hearing approaching enemies would be extremely difficult too.
116452: The water travels quickly down a sharp slope in the cavern here, travelling in a narrow ditch near the north of the cave. The cavern is smooth, hewn out by centuries of the water's passage. To the east, some faint light can be seen.
116454:
A dark intangible shadow turns to face you.
A dark intangible shadow turns to face you.

Once a beautiful hall, decorated with large paintings and shining swords, it is now a mere ruin of its former glory. Debris and stone rubble lie haphazardly all over the floor, making the passage arduous. In the western wall a once proud arch leads way into a smaller sanctuary of the keep and northward the hall opens up into a large assembly room.
116455: This was once the great hall of the keep. A roaring fire, large set tables and a thick fog of smoke hovering all around were an everyday sight. Now the fire has burned out, the tables are smashed into splinters and the walls are crumbled and drafty. What is left of a small stone stair runs along the western wall up to the second level of the keep.
116456:
A moaning ghost advances forward, softly floating above the ground.
A moaning ghost advances forward, softly floating above the ground.
A skeletal warrior is staring angrily at the surroundings.
An intact skeleton of a man is walking around here.
An intact skeleton of a man is walking around here.

What is now a great ruined hall was once several smaller rooms like kitchen and small sleeping chambers for the servants and guards. As the inner walls fell, the roof caved in, letting sun and rain play wildly with the interior, bringing havoc and chaos upon the dwindling keep. Not much here bears the resemblance of the once so strong keep.
116457:
A fierce bat is here, lusting for your blood.
A fierce bat is here, lusting for your blood.
A fierce bat is here, lusting for your blood.
A small bat is standing here.
A small bat is standing here.
A small bat is standing here.
A small bat is standing here.
A small bat is standing here.
A large bat is here, hanging in the darkness.
A large bat is here, hanging in the darkness.
A huge bat is here, emitting piercing squeaks.
A large bat is here, hanging in the darkness.

This once so proud tower is now cracked and jagged with several holes in the wall. Parts of the roof have fallen in. Water and wind are now free to play among the remnants of furniture and a large colony of bats that have taken residence here.
116463: A skeleton of some humanoid lies in the dust.

This small chamber was once the lord's bedchamber. As such it had a splendid view over the courtyard and the surrounding fields. Several large pieces of wood lie scattered across the floor - likely remnants of a few large wooden chests and a large bed. In the western wall is a cracked and broken wooden door that blocks the passage west.
116464: A shade is here, shrouded in an inky blackness.
This small chamber was obviously once a chamber for clothes as you can tell by the numerous piles of rotting textile. Splinters of wood lie scattered among the piles completing the chaos.
116465: A humble man stands here, ready to help you with your things.

This little home is made of very thin walls; brown, plain and quite boring! The branch that cradles this comfortable home is probably weak and thin, as one can feel it swaying periodically. The weather and elements have not been able to damage or cause it to fall. An ink stamp is above the door on the west side and a poem or quote was written in a bold ink on the eastern wall, above a window that has a prime view of Rivendell below.
116467: A humble man stands here, ready to help you with your things.

Lightly stained timber forms the walls of this room, with several windows along the eastern and southern walls. The eastern wall contains a simple writing desk inside a large bay window overlooking the tranquil Rivendell valley. The northern wall is lined with bookcases filled with books, scrolls, and loose parchment in all manner of size, shape, and condition. A small bed sits beneath the windows on the southern wall. The door to the west has a silver trim and is made from a heavier wood.
116468: An ancient black altar is here, standing before a pool of dark water.

It is hard to breathe in here, as the air is moist and holds a stench of animal droppings. Winding twisting passages leave this cave in all directions, as if the air itself was trying to escape. The only way that is not a dead end is south. In the centre of the room is a wide pool of clear dark water. The surface is pulsating slowly, as if something was moving down there - rising and sinking.
116470:
A brook trout is here, swimming in the current.
A bass swims here.
This clear stream is beautiful. The water moves gently downstream. Despite its coolness, the water still seems inviting. The Nen Kalthar bends and flows south from here.
116471: The corpse of a brook trout is lying here.

The bank here rises steeply on both sides, topped by a thin forest on the west. You fancy that you can hear birdsong above the gentle sounds of the waters bouncing its way down to the south, where it will ultimately gain its freedom in the Great Sea. For the moment you can only follow the path of the fast- flowing stream, with no possibility to ascend its steep and muddy banks.
116472: A Tributary to the Nen Kalthar

South of here there is a well-built ford which looks like it is in good repair. The fact that almost all of the stones remain intact is a tribute to the skill and workmanship of the men who built it, for many years have passed since such stonework has been carried out by the hands of men. The river here flows south, joining another branch beyond the ford and then flowing onward, to the east.
116473:
A brook trout is here, swimming in the current.
A nightingale is here, chirping a sweet melody.
A bass swims here.

Flowing from north to south here, the river continues its journey through these almost flat lands, its course a leisurely and meandering one. The low banks to both east and west appear easily scaled should one wish to leave the water, but further downstream the land does rise just a little above the level of the channel. To the east, the bank is topped by a massive, flat, moss-covered stone, which lies at an angle, so that its edge barely clears the waterline.
116474:
Klaees (thedon), wielding a heavy morningstar, is standing here.
Drazud (freshmeat), wielding a great warsword, is standing here.
Sza (smurfette), wielding a great warsword, is standing here.
Ducaht (tooprettytodie), wielding a great warsword, is standing here.
Bulg (pukespy), wielding a great warsword, is standing here.
It's very dark in here, there are stairs going down to what seems to be a cellar. The bar is south of here.
116475: You see three large barrels on the ground.

You are standing in the cellar of the Inn. A lot of big barrels and kegs are piled up against the wall to your left. To your right you can see bottles of, what are probably wine and spirits. Most of them are covered with a thick layer of dust, but at one end you notice a rack of clean and maybe new bottles The only visible exit is back up from whence you came.
116484: A ghastly stench fills the room as solid waste litters the northern end of the room. Scraps and large chunks of rotting wood and other junk has also been dumped here. Small holes in the ground serve as crude outhouses for elimination.
116485: The valley floor lies here at some distance beneath the foot of the cliffs. What might once have been a narrow, stony trail tracks along the edge of the sheer rock face. The ground is littered by rubble which has perhaps fallen from the wall, and indeed the latter is pock-marked by many pits.
116487: A humble man stands here, ready to help you with your things.

A glass room built high and nestled onto several branches of a large oak tree where Chezkla and his friends hang out and study arcane mysteries while enjoying the view. With amazing attention to detail the weather never affects the comfort inside, only the view changes. One day it is the dancing Bruinen, the next, it is the flowing beauty of the clouds. In one corner is a homely bed for refreshing sleep.
116488: A humble man stands here, ready to help you with your things.

This spacious lounge has been carved out of rock with a number of windows providing ambient light through the branches and leaves of the trees outside. Several lamps of various colours are lit to bring life into the otherwise shady walls, adorned with paintings and carvings of the celebrated bards of both Elves and Men. A few musical instruments like harps, lutes and flutes lie scattered on the thick blankets covering the floor.
116489: A humble man stands here, ready to help you with your things.

Dark walls of polished brown oak give this room a woodland feel. On one side of the smooth marble door there are small pegs suitable for hanging a cloak, bow, and quiver. There is little other adornment, save a small wooden bed in one corner and a squat wardrobe. The lack of comforts indicates that the home is used only for a brief respite from a life wandering the wild.
116490: A humble man stands here, ready to help you with your things.

Each wall of this study is covered in bookcases full of dusty, aged tomes. The martial symbols on the spines of most of the books indicate this is the collection of a student of the soldierly arts. More books fill piles in the corners, as well as on the modest table and chairs that are the only furniture save an old sleeping mat.
116491: A humble man stands here, ready to help you with your things.

This a small room filled with plain, but well-made furniture. A bed lines one wall while a table with a couple of chairs sits in one corner. A stone fireplace, obviously well-used, sits in the opposite corner. The western wall is dominated by a large painting of Earendil sailing to Valinor. The gleaming gemstone on is forehead seems to burst with light.
116492: A long water trough made of wood stands here.

Some clean, fresh straw covers the floor of this stable. A few stalls line one end, each crafted from solid oak. The smell of feed mixed with a faint whiff of manure fills the area. On the northern end, a solid cellar door with an iron lock has been set into the ground.
116520: You notice that the road seems to continue to the north. As you look to the south you notice a small depression. There seems to be no trees around; only green flourishing bushes grow peacefully there; you are enveloped by a undefinable scent: so beautiful, but so strong that you barely can stand it. What a shame...
116536: You are standing on the most popular road of Middle-earth. There seems to be no real difficulty to walk on this well prepared road. You feel quite safe on this road, but you shiver as you look around you. You wish you'd never have to quit this road...the outside world is so frightening !
116550: You notice that the road seems to continue to the north. As you look to the south you notice a small depression. There seems to be no trees around; only green flourishing bushes grow peacefully there; you are enveloped by a undefinable scent: so beautiful, but so strong that you barely can stand it. What a shame...
116551: Gently undulating plains run from here down to the rivers edge to the north-east. The occasional bush of holly breaks the rolling grasses. To the south-west the holly bushes get thicker and possibly impassable in places.
116552: You are inside an old ship wreck, preserved by the peat bog surrounding it. Most parts of it have, during the many years it must have been here, collapsed or got overgrown by different underwater plants. To the south, however, seems to be a sturdy section, made of reinforced oak. There's a door leading south there, that is also made of reinforced oak.
116553: This must have been the captain's room, judging by the once luxurious furniture in here. Not much has survived staying in the water for a such long time as it must have been. You see remainders of a table and what must have been a bed. In a corner lies a pile of bones from a human.
116554: In the Hold of an Ancient Wreck

A fierce-looking eel lurks in the darkness.
A fat carp swims here.
A fat carp swims here.

As you enter the hold of this ship, you are almost blinded by the filthy, dark, and still water. All wood and timber has rotted, as have the barrels that once might have held food, water, or sail-cloth. A greenish, sediment- covered obstruction traverses the hull from south to north.
116555:
A fierce-looking eel lurks in the darkness.
A fierce-looking eel lurks in the darkness.

This is a cramped and formless crevice or vacuity between two rotting hulls, wrecked long ago and buried by debris. The water in this space is so filthy with rotten wood and slime that it is like swimming in thin mud. Little shapes dart about... they might be fish, or they might not.
116556: This is a water-filled vertical shaft whose earthen walls seem about ready to fall in at any moment. The water is muddy and foul-tasting; and it is about the darkest place you have ever seen.
116557: This is a stifling, damp underground shaft, about three feet across. Its walls are made of crumbling earth; above, it is capped with a stony substance. Worms and little bugs crawl out of the earth. Below is a surface of black, filthy water.
116565:
Greater parts of a broken weapon are lying on the ground.
A fierce-looking eel lurks in the darkness.

This almost shapeless vacuity, bounded by rotten wood, mud, peat, and roots, is barely recognisable as the lower deck and hold of a small cargo vessel. The blackened planks crumble softly at your touch; the crumbs of wood drift slowly in the black and stagnant water. Shapeless debris is everywhere. Dim shapes seem to slither at the limits of your vision.
116566: This square is a busy crossing point in the village. The eastern road leads off towards the main square, while the northern route passes through a residential area before reaching the agricultural fields. Here, the normal village noises are replaced by the ringing of metal on metal coming from the blacksmith's shop to the south.
116569: A little stone lies on the ground.

The air in this cavern is thick and musty, and strangly warm. The ground is covered in a thick blanket of green and brown moss; so thick and supple is the mossy carpet that even the sound of footsteps become muted, lending to the crypt-like silence that pervades the cavern. Small roots protrude from the earthen walls, intertwining together to make ominous, twisted shapes.
116570: A giant crack opens up here, far inside the mountain. The height of the fissure indicates the true depth of these caves, and gazing upwards one can see massive black stalactites hanging down from the high ceiling. Coarse stone, black as night, forms the surfaces of the walls. The floor is covered by a layer of black grit, criss-crossed with large footprints. Broken, twisted skeletons, completely stripped of all soft tissues, lie tossed aside into the corners. The place is massive, and stretches further east and south. To the north a cave-in has occurred, leaving no discernible exits.
116571: An old stone table sits cracked in the centre of the cave. Wiped clean of any foodstuffs, only mould and fungi cover it now. A skeleton the size of a man-child lies broken in several pieces in a corner of the cave. It has been completely picked clean of any soft tissue. Trickles of dirt and pebbles have landed in piles across the expanse of the cave - clear evidence of recent, ongoing seismic activities. An enormous cave opens up to the north, and the cavern also expands further to the east.
116572: A half-decayed corpse of a goblin lies rotting on the ground.

This is a dank, dirt-covered cave, nestled deep among the very roots of the mountain. Thick air, polluted by black dust and a ghastly smell permeates the black cavern. Fragments of bone lie scattered across the room, mixed together with various bits of wooden and metal debris. The entire area appears to be sealed off with no obvious exits out to any sort of tunnel or escape route. Small stalactites hang from the ceiling, and tiny drops of water are slowly rippling down their sides.
116573: The cavern is tall and wide, and the walls, ceiling and ground are dark as night. A layer of dust covers most of the area. Smashed barrels and chests lie scattered all over. Small rocks and pebbles tumble down the walls at irregular intervals, and piles of rubble are slowly growing beneath the most active of these rockfalls. The cave turns in a south-to-west direction, creating a centrally-located natural pillar around which the immediate caves have been dug. There are no apparent exits away from this litter-strewn, forsaken area.
116574: High in the crown of a tall elm rests this light wooden platform, gently held by the great tree on the tips of its branches. A faint silvery glimmer covers the flet and the branches above it like a transparent dome woven of spider webs. An elaborately carved railing runs around the flet, and a grey ladder leads down through an opening by the tree trunk.
116575: Winding repeatedly, Nimrodel swirls to the east, her waters a mesmerizing blur of blue and white; a wild, churning melody surrounds her advance. A promenade of trees line her progress, their long branches drooping in reverence, bowed yet alert, reminiscent of ears heeding a song only faintly heard, yet all the more insistent for its subtly. Close to the east, a soft roar fills the air.
116576: This part of the plain is as barren as the rest. Only thin grasses grow here, and there are even more rocks than further south. On the second glance, you notice a trail. It runs close under the rocky hillside, and is protected from sight from the plains by strategic dips and rocks. The hill-side is too steep for anyone on the hilltop to easily see people on the trail at its foot. The trail follows the hillside north-south.
116577: A humble man stands here, ready to help you with your things.

This walls of this room are crafted from solid stone. On the northern edge of the room a small fireplace sits opposite a fluffy bed. A wooden desk sits against the eastern wall, flanked by a tall bookshelf filled with books. The floor is covered with soft, cosy-looking mats. A window in the southern wall looks out onto the forest below.
116579:
A domesticated pony, beast of burden to many, stands here.
A stocky mountain mule is here, waiting to serve.
A hobbit stable-lad is waiting to look after your horse.

Inside these large stables there are many empty stalls for horses and ponies lining either wall. Each stall has plenty of hay on the floor and a water trough, as if the innkeeper was expecting lots of travellers to arrive at any second. At the back of the stables is a large wooden door. There are lots of muddy horse tracks leading through that door. There is a large note pinned to a wooden pillar which supports the roof of the stables.
116581: You are in a vast, desolate plain. The short grass and small stones could cover nothing larger than a bug. In the northeast there is a dark line of trees. A line of great hills looms in the distance in a great arc from the north to the southeast. To south and west there are only the plains.
116582: You are in a vast, desolate plain. The short grass and small stones could cover nothing larger than a bug. Far off to the northeast there is a dark line of trees. A line of great hills looms in the distance in a great arc from the north to the southeast. To the south and west there are only the plains.
116583: You are on a vast, deserted plain. Small stones stick out among the thin grass. Perhaps a league to the northwest stands a walled town, but no smoke rises from it to tell of hearth fires, nor are there any signs of people or cultivation on the plain near it. The only other feature to break the flat plains is a line of great hills looming on the horizon. They form a great arc from the north to the southeast.
116587: Foolishly you left the safety of the platform and waded into the burning magma. You feel your skin and flesh char and ignite, and your eyes melt; your throat is too destroyed to scream in agony...
116597: Wading foolishly through the burning magma, you burn to char. A platform rings this pool but in the centre, to the north, a small island of laen rises up from the lava. From there, you sense a numbing, potent force.
116600: Foolishly you left the safety of the platform and waded into the burning magma. You feel your skin and flesh char and ignite, and your eyes melt; your throat is too destroyed to scream in agony...
116601: Foolishly you left the safety of the platform and waded into the burning magma. You feel your skin and flesh char and ignite, and your eyes melt; your throat is too destroyed to scream in agony...
116602: Foolishly you left the safety of the platform and waded into the burning magma. You feel your skin and flesh char and ignite, and your eyes melt; your throat is too destroyed to scream in agony...
116613: Foolishly you left the safety of the platform and waded into the burning magma. You feel your skin and flesh char and ignite, and your eyes melt; your throat is too destroyed to scream in agony...
116615:
A weapons rack stands against the wall.
In the rack is a shortbow.
A slender orkish archer, holding an orkish shortbow, is sleeping here.

A large bastion has been built into the palisade wall to guard the western side of the camp against attack, and this broad guard tower stands on top. Thin holes in the walls allow one to watch the strip of cleared land outside the palisade while staying hidden from view. Racks for bows and arrows stand along the eastern wall, near a stair leading down. Past attacks on the tower have left a section of the western wall heavily scarred and dented.
116616:
A green-skinned hill troll is pacing around with a nervous zeal.
A green-skinned hill troll is pacing around with a nervous zeal.
A green-skinned hill troll is pacing around with a nervous zeal.
A strong hill troll is standing here, his hide covered in large scales.
A strong hill troll is standing here, his hide covered in large scales.
A massive hill troll is here, sniffing the air for the scent of enemies.

This cave is a troll lair if there ever was one. It reeks with the stench of unwashed flesh and rotting meat. The floor is littered with gnawed, cracked bones and other refuse. In one dark back corner lie some items of metal, most bent, broken, and unrecognisable.
116618: A massive pile of rubble lies at the end of this passage. Boulders, stones, and pea-sized rocks all lay together. Evidently this is where the miners left stone unsuited for anything else. A dank smell emanates from the pile, apparently there is something wet beyond.
116627: These stairs are made out of stone and can withstand your weight. A thick coat of dust covers each step suggesting that this place is not known to many people or that no one has a need for using it. On the walls, you can see a few holders for lanterns or torches. Some pieces of decayed wood are lying here and there. A few rusted metal pieces are buried in the dust on the floor.
116630:
A tawny-coated bear is snuffling about.
A tawny-coated bear is snuffling about.

An earthy cave, supported by a vault of strongly intertwined roots of silvery grey seems to show signs of recent habitation. Tufts of golden fur line the packed dirt floor, and some gnawed bones and fruit pits are scattered in a particular corner. Opposite this corner is a bed of grass, apparently gathered by a host who desires his comforts.
116640: The road here is flat, and free from holes and cracks. The land surrounding it is trimmed and pruned, and the tall gates of Fornost dominate the land to the north. A trail into a dark forest breaks off from the road and turns east, towards the wooded hills in the distance.
116641: A small hill to the north guides the Road east, and far to the west, a simple wooden house sits among a sea of well-manicured grass. The road here is well maintained, and the cracks between each stone are free of weeds and grass. The road continues far to the south.
116642: This solitary hill rises high above the farmlands to the southwest, and the Road to Fornost to the east. A single mature pine tree provides a wide swath of shade on the rocky ground, and a home for squirrels and birds. The ground beneath the tree is littered with pine cones and needs.
116643: Clump of Trees in Heavy Brush
The butchered corpse of a boar is lying here.

A handful of tall oaks stand on the uneven ground here. Aged, broken branches lie amidst a heavy covering of bushes and vines. The rocky ground gradually starts rising to the east, leading to the first foothills of the Northern Downs.
116644: Fork in the Road to Fornost

The stony road here is swept free of detritus, and continues far to the north and south. A small, less trodden path splits away from the road to the west, past a small farm house, and then towards open plains. A dense forest creeps up to the Road to the east, and little can be seen of its dark interior.
116645: Eastern End of a Dirt Path

An uneven dirt path meanders east-west here amongst a grassy field. Pebbles and larger rocks have collected in its numerous depressions. Stout grass and short weeds grow in large ruts that run on each side of the path. The path widens to the east, as it connects to a larger road.
116646: The dirt path here is mostly even and free from dips and ruts. Low, neatly stacked stone walls line the path on each side. A faint walkway meanders through skinny gaps in the northern and southern walls, allowing access to the farmland beyond.
116647: A dirt path runs east-west here amongst the vast farmland. The path has a few bumps and dips, but is free from large rocks and flora. A thick collection of wheat grows right off the path to the north. The wheat on the southern side is sparse and seemingly randomly placed.
116648: Eastern End of a Dirt Path

A well-managed dirt path is bordered on the west by a rocky cliff. A large pile of haphazardly strewn boulders and gnarled branches lies directly under it. A vast grassy field opens to the south. The path extends eastward through the manicured farmland.
116649:
A cluster of white star-shaped forget-me-nots flourish here in reminiscence.
A shaggy-haired cow looks around curiously whilst grazing.
A shaggy-haired cow looks around curiously whilst grazing.
A shaggy-haired bull stands here, calmly looking around.

A white gazebo sits in a manicured grassy field. Tapered white spires support a peaked roof, and within it a white marble table is surrounded by decorated chairs of pine. A cluster of mature oak trees surrounds it, and aged, decomposing leaves adorn its roof. A white wooden fence borders the field to the south.
116650: Tiny clumps of grass struggle to grow in this dusty, arid field. The ground is dimpled with divets, and roots poke in and out of the earth from a small cluster of oak trees. The mostly featureless landscape continues in all directions but east, where a rock-filled ditch prevents further passage.
116651:
A sturdy pack horse is standing here.
A stocky mountain mule is here, waiting to serve.
A mouse is here nosing around, looking for a safe place to hide.
A shaggy-haired cow looks around curiously whilst grazing.
A rather dirty young boy is here, ready to tend to the stable.

The smell of dirt, hay, and manure permeates these long, squat, animal stables. Twin rows of large pens provide homes to horses, mules, and cows. Wet hay surrounds water buckets placed in each stall. Black mouse droppings create meandering paths amongst the straw.
116652:
There are two carrots here.
You see two potatoes on the ground.
A tall scarecrow shaped vaguely like an orc stands tilted in the field.
A field mouse noses about hungrily, searching for food.
A black crow flies low to the ground here, looking for carrion to eat.
A mountain mule (ulo) is standing here, ridden by you.

Potatoes, onions, and carrots grow here in straight rows. Chickens and mice peck at the vegetables as they scurry amongst the field. Flies and maggots feast on fallen carrots. A long wooden fence to the south indicates the end of the farm. Three scarecrows, in the shape of orc warriors, stand guard amidst the vegetation.
116653:
On the ground, there are two onions.
A handful of beans are lying here.
A large scarecrow shaped like a troll stands watch over the field.
A large, orange pumpkin is here.
A black crow flies low to the ground here, looking for carrion to eat.
A field mouse noses about hungrily, searching for food.

Pumpkins, beans, and onions grow here in neatly managed rows. Depressions between the rows run east-west through the field. A low stone fence surrounds this field to the west and north. A black cloud of flies surrounds a large heap of compost that decomposes next to a wooden fence to the south. Two scarecrows in the shape of mountain trolls keep watchful eyes on the field.
116654: On the ground, there are two piles of barley.

Yellow stalks of mature barley cover this vast, flat field. No path is discernible through the field, but the root-free ground provides easy access through the stalks. To the east, the faint outline of a red house can be seen, and tall cliffs border the field to the west and north.
116655:
A large cabinet capable of storing goods is here.
In the cabinet, there are a dark coloured flask, a piece of smoked, cured meat, and a pan.
A heavy desk, made of solid oak, stands here.
A large stone fireplace with a roaring fire warms the room.
The farmer's wife is bustling busily around.
A hardworking farmer is here, busy with his chores.

A circular brick fireplace serves as the centrepiece to this richly adorned farmhouse. A thick grizzly bear pelt surrounds it, and above it, a long, brick chimney rises high to the ceiling. A sturdy bed made from oak beams, and adorned with black bear pelts and cotton sheets, sits near the fireplace. Large windows in each wall overlook the surrounding wheat fields and forests.
116656: Decaying Waystation near the Gates of Fornost

A crumbling stone bench leans into the earth here.
A colourful butterfly is fluttering around here.

An old bench, grass and weeds form the entirety of the interior of this decaying wooden structure. The walls are made of old oak beams, and the simple gable roof is patchy, providing minimal protection from the elements. Vines have wrapped their leafy arms around the wood, and insects crawl among the plant. The ramparts of Fornost can be seen from the eastern entrance.
116657:
A tall pine tree grows here.
A brown fox is here, looking for some rabbits to chew up.
A brown fox is here, looking for some rabbits to chew up.
An elk cow gazes coldly at you, chewing on a small branch.

The grassy ground here is marked by large quartz rocks and small oak trees. The barest outline of a path runs westward and meanders around tiny gulleys and the occasional mature pine. The Fornost walls can be seen to the distant northeast, and the plains continue far to the east and west.
116659: An elk cow gazes coldly at you, chewing on a small branch.

The flat ground here is covered with a carpet of short grass, and dotted with large quartz rocks, and juvenile oak trees. Far to the east, the land rises to form a small hill. To the northeast, the stony ramparts of Fornost stand watchful guard.
116665: Lumber Mill in a Rocky Field
A brown fox is here, looking for some rabbits to chew up.

Long, bare trunks of oak and pine are stacked in a large pile here. Insects scurry about the dark and protected recesses of its interior. The bottom half of a long tube forms the mouth of a small lumber mill. Surrounding it, wood shavings and dust have created a brown frosting on the ground. Rows of finely cut wood planks are neatly stacked to the side of the mill.
116666:
The water of a tiny stream flows softly over the rocks here.
A dense carpet of blue flowers dip their heads in the breeze.
A tiny spider is here, eating a tiny bug.
A squirrel scampers around here, looking for nuts from the trees.
A squirrel scampers around here, looking for nuts from the trees.

The ground here is soft, with a light coating of pointed leaves and short grass. A vast clustering of mature oak trees provides shade to weary travellers, and nesting spots for birds and insects. Small holes dot the landscape, their dark interiors hidden from all but the smallest animals. A tiny stream meanders through a snaking depression in the forest floor.
116667: The water of a small stream flows softly over the rocks here.

Young oak trees compete for sunlight across the uneven ground. The canopy is thin here, providing little protection from the wind and rain. The trees are coloured various shades of grey; from off-white to near black. Large, tumbled boulders lie in a giant heap at the western end of this young forest. A small stream flows from the east here, and disappears into the crevices of the boulders to the west.
116668:
A colourful butterfly is fluttering around here.
A fierce wolverine is here, snarling at you.

Tall wheat shoots cover the flat landscape here. The thick canopy of wheat obscures any path that may run through it. The field is contained by towering cliffs to the north and east, and a large pile of boulders to the south. The rock pile is topped by twisted sticks and decomposing leaves.
116669:
A shaggy-haired cow looks around curiously whilst grazing.
A shaggy-haired cow looks around curiously whilst grazing.
A shaggy-haired bull stands here, calmly looking around.
An elk cow gazes coldly at you, chewing on a small branch.

Rippled columns of green wheat cover the flat landscape, completely hiding the root-covered ground beneath it. The thick collection of grain sways to the whims of the wind. A small rocky cliff rises far to the north, obscuring the land beyond it.
116670: A fierce boar is here, making grunting noises.

Thick bushes and tall grass indicate light usage of the trail here. To the north and south, the brush is thick and foreboding, but a glimpse of the Road to Fornost indicates that the edge of the undergrowth isn't very far to the west.
116671: The water of a small stream flows softly over the rocks here.

The rocky, pockmarked, and mossy walls of Fornost dominate the western horizon. Ramparts, filled with tall slits, top the fortified walls. Tall vegetation is very sparse here, and few places exist that do not have a direct line of sight to the watching eyes of the ramparts. A small stream runs east-west here, disappearing under the fortified walls of Fornost.
116672: The water of a small stream flows softly over the rocks here.

In the centre of the field, a single, lonely oak tree stands testament to the slow passage of growth and decay that surrounds it. Bulbous and pointy leaves, in various stages of decomposition, feed the ground under it. The land rises sharply to the north, into a tall mountain range. A stream of clear water runs through a small valley, near the southern edge of the plains. A clump of dark thorns grows to the east.
116673: A detached red rose is lying here.

A narrow footpath leads from the western plains into a thicket of thornbushes to the east. Layer upon layer of thorny branches line both sides of the almost invisible path. Shifting gaps in the thorny tangle to the north reveal snippets of a small, black tower.
116674: A small tower is carved into the granite cliff here, its black stonework covered with thick moss and twisting vines. Dry ground and patches of dead grass lead towards the entrance, a wide arch of chiselled stone. Several crude fetishes are hung from the arch, and some strange symbols have been scratched into it. A dark doorway leads into the tower.
116680: A long slender eel glides along the water, its body coiled to strike.

A deep lake of clear water is framed on the east and west by tall, granite crags. Very little direct sunlight reaches the ground here, and the water is very cold, year round. Large, oblong, granite slabs form giant mounds on the eastern and western edges of the lake. A large hole in the southern cliff can be seen, high above the water line.
116681: Old Camp in a Rocky Gorge

A low and wide-spread tree grows here.
On the tree's branches, there is a juicy plum.

A simple, caved-in wooden shack sits amongst overturned wooden buckets, and skeletonised animal carcasses. Dark water has pooled inside the shack, and the surrounding ground is undisturbed. A long, ratty string is strung between two tall pines, and next to it, leaves collect at the base of a large hole.
116682: The remains of a small tangle of roots lie here in a heap of rotting compost.

The land here holds more vegetation than what seems possible, with bushes, and even some smaller, scrawny trees growing on what limited soil they can find. This gorge starts from a steep slope to the north and runs southward, through twin pillars of granite cliffs.
116683: Cragged Hilltop in the Northern Downs
A fallow deer is grazing peacefully here.

Grey and white boulders, of all shapes and sizes, cover the rocky hilltop here, providing small shelter from the winds. To the east, the land slopes downward into a lightly wooded gorge. Further east, sharp, grey hills tower over the land like rows of giant teeth.
116684: The top of this hill is mostly flat and lacks prominent features aside from a few boulders and a single green shrub. This hill ends abruptly with a precipitous cliff to the west, revealing a deep, narrow, and brush-filled crevice and a wooded valley beyond it. The earth slopes downward under the roots of the shrub.
116686: The seeping granite walls are carved flat here, and the ground is covered in leveled, slick rock. The northern wall slants upward at a steep angle, preventing travel up it. There is no ceiling here, only an open, dark expanse. Dark driblets of water seep down the wall, forming a tiny pool at the floor.
116687:
The water of a small stream flows softly over the rocks here.
An orchid of light violet petals blossoms nearby.

The southeast edge of this hilltop is quite steep, and offers a nice view of the flooded gorge to the east. The gorge is contained by rock walls on all sides but its north. The hills to the north meet several tall rock faces, set apart like a row of stairs meant for giant feet. A small staircase is carved into the southwest edge of this hill, offering a safe passage to the plains below. A small stream runs south of this hill, fed by a wide crack in the cliff-face to the east.
116694: The eastern cliffs allow only midday lighting of this wooded and beaten path. The brush is thin here, but even so, the path disappears quickly as it leads further into the darkness to the west and south. A large oak tree takes its final rest next the path here, as its wood slowly becomes part of the earth.
116695: Grey Hills above a Winding Trail

Grass grows in small patches between large rocks on this grey hill. A winding trail in the valley below dips in and out of sight, through the thin canopy of treetops and underbrush. Far to the north, the bulbous mounds of the Northern Downs seem stacked on top of one another, an undulating mass of rock and dirt.
116696: Barren Hills above a Lush Basin

The hilltop here is mostly flat, and a light path amidst the dirt runs eastward, but is quickly obscured amongst the rocky landscape. Tiny plants struggle to grow in the inhospitable ground here. Twin crags far to the north stand high over flat plains of mixed green, grey, and brown.
116697: A small forest of yellow-green ash trees provides a bright backdrop against a featureless, grey cliff-face to the east. A thin covering of hilbert and filbert grows beneath the trees. A black wall of writhing thorns turns, and vibrates against the grey stone. The ground here is soft and spongy, as the decaying leaves provide a brown lattice on the hilly ground.
116698: Large slabs of angled, sheer rock create mini valleys and hilltops on top of this grey hill. To the south and west, the hill drops into a precipitous slide to the basin floor, far below. A long stretch of verdant brush extends far to the west. The rippled walls of Fornost can be seen very far to the northwest.
116699: A large gash runs the length of the rocky hill here. Small shrubs grow on each side of it, obscuring the dark trap from unwatchful travellers. The rolling hills continue to the northwest, and south. Far to the southwest, a lush, multicoloured brush lines a vast basin.
116700: A fallow deer is grazing peacefully here.

Well-manicured grass stretches for miles across the green-grey plains. Far to the south, lush hills rise from the flat ground, dotting the horizon. The flat, green plains continue for miles to the east, and a tall cliff of granite rises to the north.
116701:
A thin, crippled deer looks around timidly.
A large rabbit looks peacefully at you, ready to dart away.

Grass and small bushes grow among the dirt and rock in small clumps, and the ground here is mostly smooth, with occasional bumps of large rock. To the north, a long ridge reaches outward from a granite crag, casting a small part of the ground below it in unending shadow. Twin cracks have formed under it, snaking their way to the grassy ground.
116702: The rocky, barren hill here gives way to a collage of green, brown, and yellow, as a dense basin of brush opens below to the west. A small family of rolling hills is clustered to the north and northwest. A small, black cave opening dots the grey cliff to the east.
116703: A shallow pond is here, tinted green with algae.

Swaths of tree stumps across the hilly plains provide a feeding ground for insects and white fungi. A myriad of small birds are perched on the stumps, pecking at the insects. Tall weeds, thorny vines, and seeding grass all compete for sunlight between the stumps. A small pool of clear water sits in the middle of the field. Two arms of flowing water sprout from it; one feeding, and the other draining.
116704: A tiny spider is here, eating a tiny bug.

Aged pines grow sporadically here, forming a sparse forest. The thin canopy of treetops does little to dampen rainfall, or light from the sun or stars. The uneven terrain here is marked by thick root networks and large boulders. The rocky land rises to the north, as the forest continues.
116705: Tall pine trees have created a carpet of soft needles, amongst the rocks and roots in this thin forest. Clumps of white and blue fungi sprout from fallen trunks, and their cracked skin provides home to colonies of termites and ants. The land slopes downward to the south, into a large basin.
116706: Small groups of juvenile pines and oak grow on this narrow hilltop. Colonies of ants run up and down their trunks, bringing food to their homes in the rocky ground. The rolling hills continue to the north and south, and a sheer cliff-face lies far to the west. The top of a sparse forest lies to the east, and the ramparts of Fornost rise above it.
116707: Tall grass grows in clumps here, amid dirt patches that dot the rocky basin. A few large boulders, intermixed with decomposing tree trunks, lie close to the western cliff-face. The vast basin continues far to the north and south, and the cliff-face extends far to the north and south.
116708: Short shrubs, rock, and aged roots dot the landscape here. Large boulders, some embedded deep into the ground, decorate the field. A sheer rock face rises high to the west. Far to the east the barren land almost disappears completely, as it forms deep valleys between the tall hills.
116709: A black and white skunk is scuttling about here, searching for food.

A sea of tall grass is framed to the south and west by tall, rocky cliffs. A cluster of mature beech and oak trees form a dense canopy near the western cliff. Steps on the western face provide nesting spots for birds, and perching spots for short and gnarled trees. High upon the southern rock face, an overhang forms a small ledge. Under it, a shadowy crack snakes its way to the ground.
116710: Wide Peak above an Oak Forest

A large, loyal falcon is circling above.
A fierce wolverine is here, snarling at you.

The ground on this hilltop is mostly flat, and laden with an assortment of weeds, faded oak leaves, and budding trees. Steep drop-offs to the east and south provide wide vistas of the surrounding land. To the south, a jumbled mix of oak trees form a patchwork of white, grey, and black. The grey ramparts of Fornost stand guard to the east. Below the southern end of the cliff, a ripple of water flows from the east, and into the forest to the south.
116711: A sticky substance covers the walls and floor of this small tunnel, making travel difficult. Large webs hang from the ceiling, and a thick syrup of a white slime drips from it. Very little outside light reaches this rocky hole, and farther east, the light becomes rarer still. A crack runs the length of wall to the north.
116712: A strange web-like substance is clinging to all surfaces of the tunnel here, giving the atmosphere a heavy, muffled feeling. Strange sounds come from a large, web-filled hole in the cave floor. A small breeze from the west ruffles the webs.
116716:
A stocky mountain mule is here, waiting to serve.
A badger is here, exploring for food.

Short pine trees are scattered haphazardly across this rocky clifftop. A sharp drop-off to the east gives way to a vast colouring of green, as a pine forest fills the valley below. The tall ramparts of Fornost peek above the treetops, far to the southeast.
116717:
An apple tree with bright green leaves grows here.
On the tree's branches are four apples.
A large eagle soars above you.
A rabbit is here eyeing your presence warily.

The long shadows created by the surrounding hills have allowed only the most hardy plants to thrive. Toppled oak trees, lined with white fungal crowns, lie amidst a field of seedy grass. High on the western cliff, a single gnarled tree provides a resting stop for migratory birds.
116718: A large, loyal falcon is circling above.

The ground here is mostly flat and rocky, and slopes downward to the south. A few fallen oak trees provide a home for colonies of carpenter ants, and a food source for a multicoloured fungus. High on the western cliff, a long, rocky overhang casts the ground below it in perpetual shadow.
116719: This rocky basin is scattered with small shrubs, and patches of tall grass. A sheer cliff-face towers over the basin to the west. On it, two mangled trees live, intertwined high on a small ledge. Their branches reach eastward, toward sunlight.
116720:
An elk cow gazes coldly at you, chewing on a small branch.
A rabbit is here eyeing your presence warily.

The ground here is slippery with a covering of small pebbles, and among them lies the broken remnants of a wooden watchtower. Green fungi and red moss feed on the aged wood. Rolling hills continue far to the north and south. To the east, the hilltop drops precipitously, and farther east still, a small line of hilltops sits among a deep basin.
116721: Thick blades of crabgrass form a spiky carpet on this hilltop. Cracks in the stony ground create small crevices, and short shrubs reach for sunlight within them. A vast grassy basin lies to the east, and a sheer cliff-face towers over a shallow basin to the west.
116722: A roe deer is standing here, watching the terrain while chewing the vegetation.

A decay-laden husk of an abandoned house stands here, sunken deep into the grassy basin. A dead oak tree is resting across the heavily-bent bow of the house. Three leafy vines run the length of the tree, providing a feeding ground for butterflies and birds.

You see two handfuls of clover on the ground.

A vast sea of green ends abruptly at granite cliffs to the west and south. The uneven land is decorated by clusters of tall oak and pine trees. Tall granite cliffs edge the grassy plain to the south and west, their featureless faces standing testament to the growth and decay of the basin.
116724: A clump of pine trees creates a mini forest at the peak of this grassy hill. Pinecones litter the ground around it, and the shadowy recesses of massive boulders create a resting ground for large animals. A vast basin of green and grey lies to the north.
116725: Precipitous drops frame this hilltop in all directions but north. To the south and southwest, a vast forest of green, speckled with notes of brown, colours the valley below. To the southeast, the ramparts of Fornost hover above the horizon.

A buck runs swiftly from place to place, looking about warily as it grazes.

The grassy, reedy field extends far to the north, before it is abruptly interrupted by a towering cliff of grey stone. The ground slants downhill here, as the valley narrows a bit to the south. Large granite slabs dot the landscape, and few tall trees grow from the rocky ground. The valley continues in all directions.

The soft and spongy ground here is pockmarked with small, foot- and hoof-sized depressions. A large boulder is here, adorned with red moss, and a tuft of grass grows on its top. Blue irises, arrowheads, and brooklime grow abundantly across the wet terrain.
116731:
A tree-snake lies wrapped around one of the tree branches.
A black and white skunk is scuttling about here, searching for food.
A swift and agile forest cat moves silently through the vegetation.

The valley narrows here, as the tall crags push inwards from the east and west. The forest floor is littered with oblong slabs of rock, and the carcasses of long-dead trees. The vegetation thickens a bit to the south, as the widening valley allows a greater cover of sunlight.
116732: The tips of pine trees form soft spikes upon the horizon to the east. The forest sways in unison as gusts of wind arrive, driven by the mountains to the east. The tall crag to the west blocks all sunlight but the morning rays, causing the vegetation here to be short, and sparse. The uneven terrain drops sharply to the east, and the field extends far to the north.
116733: An elk cow gazes coldly at you, chewing on a small branch.

The land slopes gently to the west, but ends abruptly to the east and south, as it plunges rapidly to the grassy valley below. A seemingly random assortment of partially built wood structures dots the green-grey basin to the west.

Far under a sudden drop-off to the east, a tiny dot of water ripples.
116735: Aged Ruins in a Lush Basin

Two mature oak trees provide support to the leaning walls of a broken house. A decayed hole in the centre of the rotting floorboards provides nourishment to a young oak tree. Disintegrating wood planks poke through the leafy ground, creating a jagged, shattered memory of a home.
116736: Heaps of rotting wood is hidden in the depths of tall grass and weeds in this overgrown field. A stout post stands watch in the field, and the four small holes in it provide a home for insects, and a feeding spot for small birds. A rocky cliff rises deep within a hill to the west.
116737: Rocky Hilltop above a Grassy Basin

This peak sits high above a range of rolling hilltops that lead far south. A vast grassy basin continues far to the east, where it meets a small crag range. Far to the west, a massive, grey rock face towers over a basin of stone and grass.
116738: A badger is here, exploring for food.

The crags of the Northern Downs stretch northward, eventually meeting the first hills of the Rammas Formen. The western cliff has heavily eroded, and opens into a narrow valley that snakes southward. To the east, the land drops quickly, ending in a small field. To the south, the mountains slowly slope downward, revealing the gentler plains beyond.
116739:
A grey wolf is here, snarling aggressively.

The curved cliff-face protects this area from the harsh winds, rain, and snow that occur in the Northern Downs. An abandoned fire pit, covered in twigs and brown leaves, sits in a small depression near the northern cliff. A thick, ratty rope is suspended from two mature oak trees. Strips of grey and brown hemp hang from it, still from the lack of breeze.
116740: A long stretch of grassy plateau ends with a cleaved drop-off to the south. A lonely maple sapling grows at the apex of this hill, peeking above the top of the tall grass. The land slowly slopes upward to the east and north, as the rolling hills continue.
116741: A fallow deer is grazing peacefully here.

A steep ridge among the mountains connects the two adjacent plateaus, and offers a safer way to travel than climbing the precipitous and jagged crags. A mossy wall of rock towers ominously over the slope to the north, like a giant wave in a sea of grey stone.
116742: Craggy Hill above a Light Forest
A fallow deer is grazing peacefully here.

The rocky hill ends with a steep slope to the south, providing a wide vista of a light forest. The unbroken land below continues far to the south, climbing slowly downward, towards the flat plains of Fornost. Far to the east, a giant mound of loose rock, and detritus, is set against a tall, grey face of stone.
116743: The flat field, unmarked by boulders or trees, ends abruptly with a steep crevice to the south, which is filled with mounds of rubble. To the west and south, the only visible landmarks are the long ridges of the Northern Downs, leading lost travellers southward towards the city of Fornost.
116745: Thin Clifftop in the Northern Downs

This sharp corner of a rocky plateau sits high above the area surrounding the city of Fornost, providing a wide view over the hills. A single gnarled tree grows here, its height stunted, and body twisted by the rocky ground. A dark forest covers the landscape far to the south, and little can be seen of its interior from this distance.
116746: Rugged Plateau in the Northern Downs

Aside from some boulders and a few bushes, there is only a flat plateau here. The rocky plateau is bounded by a steep cliff to the west, and a narrow crevice to the north. There is a brush-filled valley beyond the western cliff, hinting that these stair-like crags of the Northern Downs are coming to an end.
116747: The northwestern corner of the crag has completely collapsed, leaving a huge rockslide to the north, and a shallower slope to the west. To the south, the ridge still holds fast against the constant barrage of winds. A few shrubs and tufts of grass are still somehow clinging to the rocky ground.
116748: The sharp ridgeline here angles upward, until it resembles a rocky blade. Atop the ridge, a flat outcrop has a small, nest-like niche worn into it by the weather. To the south, the Northern Downs continue until meeting the flat plains of Fornost. A small stone structure can be seen, nestled inside a thicket to the southeast.
116749: The granite cliffs squeeze on all sides here, funnelling travellers to a sudden stop at the eastern rock wall. A large mound of sharp, grey rocks, tree limbs, and detritus is heaped onto the wall. Large patches of furry green moss cling to sky-facing sides of the rock pile, and saplings sprout from clumps of dirt in its depths. Tiny animals scurry within the safety of its dark interior.
116750: The western edge of this rocky hill slopes sharply downward, and a vast expanse of green-grey hills opens below it. Two large boulders sit side-by-side to the north, and a third, smaller rock, sits wedged between them. Two large mossy patches, coloured green and red, adorn the southern faces of the boulders.
116751: A large, loyal falcon is circling above.

The grey and white landscape offers little place to shelter from the wind, as only a few elongated niches in the rock provide substantial cover. Vegetation is scarce, consisting of patches of grass, woody bushes, and short vines. Grey and white pebbles lay scattered across the stony hilltop here, creating a slippery mat for unsuspecting travellers.
116752: Thick brushwood fills the western entrance to this narrow crevice. Steep and jagged cliffs surround the crevice from all sides, making this place a natural dead end. To the east, the crevice gets even narrower and slopes downward into the rock.
116753:
A tree-snake lies wrapped around one of the tree branches.
A swift and agile forest cat moves silently through the vegetation.

Shifting slices of sky reveal themselves through the thick canopy in this old forest. The root-covered land slopes downward to the south; and farther south still, the top of Fornost's stone walls hovers above the treetops. A small stream meanders through a deep depression in the soil.
116754: A badger is here, exploring for food.

Layered slabs of sheer granite form giant, rolling steps, across this rocky hill. Vegetation here is very sparse, and only a few patches of moss provide a hairy texture to the sheer rock. The vast, grey expanse of Fornost lies below to the south. Tall crags and rolling hills dot the landscape, east to west, across the northern expanse.
116756: The water of a small stream flows softly over the rocks here.

Tall granite cliffs to the west and south dominate the skyline of the flat land below. A scattering of short shrubs decorates the short, maintained grass, and a lightly-defined path runs north through it. On the eastern end of the field, a small pool of clear water bubbles out of the ground. The stream it forms flows west, amidst the grass, rocks, and shrubs.
116768: The well-maintained road here continues far to the north and south. The expertly-maintained road travels with no wind or deviation, and a thick brush to the east grows close to the road's edge. The brush grows so closely together that it conceals its interior well from sun and starlight. In contrast, a deep, rock-filled ditch to the west prevents passage to vast and airy land.
116769: Sheer rock faces of smooth granite rise high to the north and east. The tree cover is very thin in this field, and only a smattering of pine and oak trees dot the landscape. The grass is manicured and scythed short here, and the grey walls of Fornost loom large to the southeast. A nondescript path leads through the field, to the west and south.
116770: A closed depression drains underground here, forming a cylindrical tubelike cavern. Only several yards in dimension, there is little room to move about. Large tree roots protrude from the karst walls, giving off the appearance of fingers reaching out at those who dare enter. A smooth limestone chute descends downwards, while a break in the ceiling provides an exit up.
116772:
A short, squat stalagmite grows from the cavern floor here.
A large brown snake with black patches is coiled here.

A mammoth spherical hollow has been etched out by aeons of water erosion. The ashen-grey limestone walls glisten with abundant moisture that seeps through endlessly. The central space of this large cavern room is clean from any fallout or debris, yet huge stalagmites and stalactites form in staggering numbers as the cavern's floor and ceiling meet.
116773: This portion of the cave is of moderate dimensions but richly decorated by numerous cave formations. However, it is hard to focus on anything else other than the foetid odour that saturates the air and assaults the nose from the massive piles of guano that have accumulated over countless years. The grotto opens into a large dome to the south, and a large tree-like column formation can be seen to the north.
116774:
A large boulder is here, it must be heavy.
Some small rocks have been piled into a mound here.
A huge bat is here, emitting piercing squeaks.

It appears at one time the cave system continued onwards in multiple directions but is now blocked by a massive pile of rubble. Boulders of innumerable size and shape form a makeshift wall to the north and west. A stalagmite and stalactite have fused together to form a single massive column. The column gives off the appearance of a branchless tree trunk, gnarled and cracked by countless years passed. The cavern passage continues to slope down from the east and descends further south.
116775: A pool of darkish water has formed in a depression of the stone.

A rotted cesspool has formed here in a cavern sump, the drainage focal point for the cave system. Murky swirls of red intermingle with masses of algae and other indistinguishable detritus. A heavy inescapable odour lingers in the stale air. The occasional drip can be heard, as condensation and run-off collects and falls from the cavern ceiling.
116776: A small brown snake is slithering around here.

A massive outcrop of gypsum flowers has formed along the walls of the cave, reminiscent of a bed of spring ephemerals. Delicate and precarious, the bone-white petals of the crystal blossoms spiral out in innumerable shapes and sizes. Sizeable amounts of cave fallout lie scattered on the cave floor, making any quick movement increasingly difficult.
116777: No trace of daylight ever reaches this part of the cave. Sloping downwards from the bear den to the north, several enormous flowstones and other cave formations begin to appear in growing numbers. Despite the lack of light, a small breeze can still be felt blowing in from the north. A natural stair of limestone descends deeper into the cave system while another passage breaks off to the south.
116778: A large brown snake with black patches is coiled here.

A huge flowstone formation sits in the centre of this cavern room, and takes on the form of what appears to be a bear in a deep, tranquil sleep. Adjacent to formation is a small cavern pool that sits perfectly still, mirroring the formation and cavern ceiling. To the north a natural passage can be seen snaking both upwards and to the west.
116779: A huge bat is here, emitting piercing squeaks.

Above large amounts of ceiling straws and drapery loom overhead, while several fallen pieces lie shattered on the cave floor. Moving north and west are the only options as the cave dead ends.

The air is dry and fettered, and the strong stench of decay wafts in from the north and east. Nary any cave formations are found here given the absence of waterflow.

A few piles of crushed, dried leaves can be seen nestled next to the eastern cave wall. The cave entrance can still be seen to the north, while to the south a darkening abyss grows.

A fierce boar is here, making grunting noises.

116790: Pine and ash trees form a light canopy over the uneven, rocky terrain, allowing ample sunlight to reach the lush undergrowth below it. Eastwards, a vast area of plains stretches away into the distance.

The road surface is pitted and worn through use in places, though there are signs of recent repairs, presumably the work of the Dunedain of Fornost. Not far to the south lies a steep ravine from which the sound of running water can be heard, while to the east lies a wooded riverbank.
116797: A brown fox is here, looking for some rabbits to chew up.

The road bends around from south to east here, in order to avoid a large rocky outcrop to the north atop which can be seen the crumbling walls of an ancient castle. To the west down a steep bank can be seen a swift-running river. The road itself is poorly-maintained this far from any settlement, showing deep signs of wear.
116798: This old and worn stone bridge spans a narrow yet deep ravine. The sound of running water can be heard from the swift river far down below. Though old, the stonework seems to be sound and sturdy owing to being visible reinforcement in several key places, well able to support the traffic that passes across it.
116799: The wide road runs north-south for a great distance in both directions. The western side of the road is bordered by a thick hedge of bushes and shrubs, while to the east is an area of broad, grassy plains. Not far to the north, a stone bridge crosses a gully of some sort.
116800: The road between Bree and Fornost stretches seemingly endlessly to the north and south, a long trek that few but the most prepared undertake. Open plains and distant hills stretch out in the east. The west, however, is blocked by dense hedges, with a grim ruin looming to the northwest.
116801: The long road to Fornost continues its journey north and south. To the east an area of grassy plains stretches away for many miles while to the west the ground is covered with clumps of bushes and the occasional oak tree. Not far from the road to the west is a small, rickety-looking wooden bridge along a dirt trail.
116802: The Road to Fornost is very wide and is leading to the south and to the north. A steep slope makes further travel toward the west impossible while to the east the top of a dark tower can be seen far away. The road shows signs of frequent travel.
116803: The road is very wide here continuing to the north and to the south. A small path leads west ascending a gentle slope toward several buildings while some bushy fields extend to the east. Tracks of carts and horses can be seen in the packed earth.
116804: The road continues its straight path to the north and south through plains. Several large gouges in the road suggest that one or more horse carts were tipped here. To the west a steep rocky slope makes further travel impossible.
116805: The road makes a long bend between some badlands to the southeast and a steep slope on the northwest side. The badlands are scraggy but accessible for further travel, however the road looks more welcoming. To the north the road continues in a straight line for miles toward the horizon.
116806: The ground beneath seems strong and well-used. The wide road makes a long bend between hills and slopes. There are some wild forest weeds to the west that could be hard to cross while to the north is a steep slope which makes further travel in that direction impossible.
116807: The route keeps on across Arda's meagre trees and plains. While badlands extend to the east, it is impossible to travel further due to extensive undergrowth on a steep slope to the west. The road reveals evidence of frequent use, such as wagon ruts.

116809: There are few to no turnoffs along the way, and the road stretches to the north and south as far as the eye can see. The topography is marked by several sizable hills to the northeast and a steep incline to the west, while a sharp drop to the east prevents further travel.
116810: There are traces of frequent transit over a relatively wide route that runs both north and south. A hill covered in trees can be found to the west, although getting there is impossible due to the vegetation. There is no way to move east due to an extremely steep slope.
116811: Here the road widens a bit to allow a more heavy flow of traffic. While the road toward the north is leading through a sparse forest this part of the road is completely out in the open. Bushy plains stretch out far to the east while a steep slope to the west prevents further journey.
116812: The Road continues its long journey north to Fornost and stretches both, north and south, as far as the eye can see. To the east of the road bushy plains continue for miles, while to the west a narrow trail ascends toward a sparsely forested area.
116813: A large mother hawk is here looking for prey to feed her young.

Tall trees sparsely cover the sides of this narrow trail, as it leaves the road in the east and ascends toward the north. Briars and bracken cover the floor. To the west is a clearing which can be seen through a gap between two old oaks, while to the south the forest becomes denser.
116814: The road to Fornost passes between a dense forest to the west and an open field to the east. The road's surface is slightly raised above the surrounding ground to aid the runoff, and two shallow ditches run parallel to the road. Weeds and other vegetation have wholly overgrown the ditches, and even grow between the rock slabs that make up the road. A small track leads across the field to the east, winding around a small building to the southeast.
116815: A wild bull seems ready to charge you.

The track extends east and west here amongst a grassy field that extends far to the north and south. The ground here is mostly flat and free of rocks and roots. Its surface is easy to walk on. Far to the south, a small wooden building sits amongst tall grass.
116817: The road runs north-south from Fornost to Bree. Its monotonous journey is broken briefly to the south, where a steep dip in the ground has been bridged by a wooden structure. A wagon-trail leaves the road heading east, across the fields, its hard-packed dirt a stark contrast to the carefully laid slabs of stone that make up the road's surface.
116818: A wagon's trail winds its way between crop fields. A narrow strip of grass grows between two thin tracks of beaten earth. The fields on either side of the track look well tended, and a wide variety of crops are grown here. Far to the west, a well-tended road runs between Bree and Fornost.
116820: A stone sign stands next to the bridge.

A steep dip, only a dozen feet or so deep, cuts through the fields. A wooden bridge spans the dip, and is wide enough to cross with wagons. The bridge has a foundation of stone on either side of the dip, but the bridge itself is constructed of sturdy wood.
116821: The road runs north-south from Fornost down to Bree. To the north, the road crosses a dip in the lands by way of a wooden bridge, while to the south, the road winds through green fields. The road's worn stone-slab surface is slightly elevated above the surrounding fields; and two ditches, overgrown with rushes and other vegetation, accompany the road on either side.
116822: The road passes through a landscape of sweeping fields and small hillocks crowned with clumps of trees and bushes. A high fence separates the road from fields of crop to the west. Worn, flat slabs of stone form the surface of the road. Some weeds have managed to take root in places between the slabs, oblivious of the constant threat of being trampled by foot or hoof, or crushed beneath a wagon's wheels.
116823: The Road to Fornost was built with great care and skill. The stone slabs that form the road's flat, easily travelled surface are fitted with precision and have stood the test of time excellently. The road takes a detour as it bends around an area to the southwest with uneven ground and several large rocky outcrops.
116824: The road seems narrow here because it's squeezed between large, thorny bushes that grow right up to the edge of the road on both sides. It appears that there were ditches along the road at some point, possibly to aid with runoff, but these are now barely discernible beneath branch and leaf, wild grass and weeds.
116825: The Road to Fornost runs north and south, straight as an arrow, completely unhindered by the terrain. Rushes grow in parallel ditches alongside the slightly elevated road, whose time-worn surface is made from carefully arranged flat stone slabs. Tangled bushes are visible far to the west, beyond a flat field of tall grasses.
116826: The road bends west around a very large boulder, obviously it was easier to just build a bit of extra road over trying to break it apart. Some farmsteads can be seen in the distance to the north on both sides of the road. A gap in the road where one of the slabs that makes up the road's surface have somehow been removed, has been filled in by packed earth.
116827: The road makes a sharp bend here to avoid an area of dense vegetation and rocky outcroppings to the north. A small paved track leaves the road heading west towards a farmstead in the distance. The road itself is well-paved and can easily handle two wagons going in opposite directions without neither of them having to skirt the ditches that border the road on either side.
116828: The state of the Road to Fornost is surprisingly good, a testimony to the skill of those who built the roads of Arnor hundreds of years ago. The road is wide and paved with flat stones expertly fit together, leaving only tiny earth-filled gaps between them. The road is bordered on one side by dense bushes and on the other by more accessible fields.
116829: A wide, paved road runs from south to north through the surrounding fields. The road is slightly raised, and slopes down on either side into shallow but wide ditches that are lush with grasses, suggesting that the soil there stays damp long after a rain. Between the road and the ditches, the downwards slope pauses briefly for a narrow footpath that follows the course of the road; it does not appear to be heavily used, with scrub bushes and tall weed stalks growing up through its gravel surface. The road itself is mostly level, paved with flat stone blocks that still have remnants of a type of cement filling gaps between.
116830: The Lane Meets a Farm Track

A sign stands here, next to a vegetable stand.
A wooden vegetable stand is set near the juncture of the farm road and the lane.
On the stand, there are three turnips, three cabbages, five carrots, six potatoes, four beets, and six apples.
A small box is attached to the post of a vegetable stand.
A young farmer is here worrying about the weather.

A wide, raised road runs from south to north here. It is paved with flat stones, large and naturally-shaped except for their smooth tops, but the gaps between them create a bumpy surface for carts and carriages. Here and there the remnants of a type of cement fills in these gaps, but everywhere else it appears to have long since been worn away by the weather. A narrow dirt farm track joins this paved lane from both the west and the east, and the stones at the edge of the lane at this intersection have been worn down, their edges crumbling from repeated traffic over the bump down to the dirt track beyond.
116831: A wide, paved road runs from south to north here, between tall hedgerows. It is paved with wide, flat blocks that fit together closely enough to leave only small gaps. Its surface is raised, sloping down on each side to shallow but wide ditches sunk down below the level of the surrounding fields. The ditches are grassy but are becoming overgrown, filled with dead weed stalks and scrub bushes growing densely in its low passage where the soil stays moist for long periods after a rain. Past the ditches on either side of the road tall hedgerows rise up, blocking passage to the fields that can be seen beyond.
116832: A raised road runs through this area, paved with irregularly-shaped stone blocks. The blocks fit together closely, with small gaps between; some sort of concrete fills these gaps in some places, but has completely worn away everywhere else. The road surface is level but no longer smooth, as not all of the paving-stones are flat on top, and the resulting unevenness makes for a bumpy ride for the carts and wagons that follow this road. The edges of the road are gravel, wide enough to have once been used as walking paths, but now these gravel pathways are blocked by scrub bushes and young whips of trees, and the easiest passage is along the road itself. Hedges rise up past the edges of the road, blocking access to the overgrown farm fields that can be seen beyond.
116833: This raised road is paved with large, flat stone blocks. Here and there the stone blocks are starting to crumble in place, leading to low spots where the top layers of stone have disappeared. Some of the stone blocks look as if they have been replaced entirely, the new blocks fitted inexpertly in the gaps left behind. A pile of old, broken paving-stones is lying in one of the ditches that borders this road, the detritus left from these road repairs. Past the ditches tall, tangled hedges rise up, blocking movement far off the road. These hedges look like they were once uniform, but now have tall weed stalks and young trees poking through them.
116834: A raised, paved road turns from west to north here. It is paved with flat, somewhat rounded stones that fit together as closely as their shapes allow; the gaps are filled with rock dust and fine grit, giving no space for weeds to grow. The road surface is mostly level, but some of the paving-stones have sunken over time, creating bumps that can jolt a cart or wagon as it passes.
