Between fields to the southeast and the foot of the Bree-hill to the northwest, the road gently swings east and south. Wooden fences divide the fields into small lots. Each field is growing a different crop, giving the landscape an extremely vibrant colour. Due to regular use, the road's dirt is hard and smooth.
117067: The road gently curves east and south. A sizable dike and a towering hedge that appear to comprise Bree's natural defences run side by side to the west of the road. While a field of vivid barley is neatly delineated by a wooden fence to the southeast, the road is inching closer to the dike as it travels south.
117068: The road's gentle eastward and southward curves become a humpback bridge that spans the dike. Following the bridge, a big hedge has been cut to make room for traffic as the road goes through. To the east is a little field with a fence around it and oats growing there.
117070: Green grass and a few plants dot the ground of the pasture. The hedge that delineates Bree's eastern border begins to grow tremendously thick and tall to the west. A road does progressively curve around the base of Bree-hill to the east and south.
117072: There is a lit street-lamp on the border of the street, illuminating the area.

The road stretches east and west. To the east, the Bree gate can be spotted. Westbound lies the trade district of Bree before arriving at central Bree, and houses line the street to the north and south. The noise and the hustle and bustle of the city seems to be much quieter here.
117073: The street continues to stretch to the east and the west, packed firm underfoot by heavy foot and hoof traffic. North lies several houses tightly cramped together, while to the south the noise of metalworkers can be heard. The Bree gate can be seen off in the distance to the east.
117074:
A direction sign, faded with age, leans at an angle here.
There is a lit street-lamp on the border of the street, illuminating the area.

A wide space opens up before the smith's working area to the south, plenty of space for wagons both to deliver and haul off weapons, arrows and armour for buyers. The white sand packed street is divided with poles and ropes to allow a good flow of visitors to pass the wagons parked.
117075:
A piece of raw venison is on the ground.
On the ground, there are three pieces of raw pork.
A large piece of fresh, raw venison lies here.

The street of white sand and gravel widens towards the south, coming to a large bend. Houses align the street both to the east and west, with about six yards between them. A dark and narrow alley winds its way west between some of the shops, contrasting the bright blue and pretty shop to the east.
117076: An elite Bree guard stands here stoutly.

Slightly narrowing to the north and wider towards the south, the road passes between houses on either side. White sand with stones of marbled white and black make the road surface nicely packed over years of use. From the west a constant smell of baked goods fills the street.
117077:
There is a lit street-lamp on the border of the street, illuminating the area.
An old man is walking around, cleaning up.

The Old East Road travels north and south here, and is about three yards wide. This nicely maintained road goes into the trade district in Bree. Several houses on either side flank the road, their colours contrasting the white gravel and sand used to make an entirely flat road.
117078: Sign of the Prancing Pony Inn

There is a lit street-lamp on the border of the street, illuminating the area.
A brightly-painted signboard hangs from the street-lamp.
A large fountain, made from grey stone, pours water from its centre.

This wide space has become the natural travelling hub of Bree. From the north music flows, and the pleasant smell of fresh food beckons. The Old East Road comes from the west and continues south through the village. The Prancing Pony Inn lies to the north.
117079:
A huge clock is standing here.
A white-painted bench is here.

A large front room opens up, where the inn divides further. North lies the foyer, where rooms can be rented, and west lies the bar, common room, and game room. The walls and floor are all solid timber frames, clad with wide planks painted in a pale blue shade on the walls. A few benches for seating stand along the eastern wall, where the view through a few small windows show the Bree stables.
117080:
A key is lying here.
A canoe has been left here.
Barliman Butterbur, the innkeeper, offers you a room in his inn.
A domesticated pony, beast of burden to many, stands here.
A stocky mountain mule is here, waiting to serve.
Romi the Rohir, holding a mighty dwarven axe, is resting here (shrouded).
A sturdy pack horse is standing here.
A mercenary is here, following his employer.
A stocky mountain mule is here, waiting to serve.
Nob the Hobbit wanders around here, looking for work to do.
Clint the Dwarf is standing here.

A risen plateau in the northern part of the Prancing Pony Inn, accessed through a rounded opening from the south, is where the deals for rented lodging are made. From here a few rooms can be seen down a corridor, and several stairs lead into other corridors upstairs.
117081: The Cobble Street narrows going west to east, almost twice as wide towards the large plaza to the west than continuing east. A large portion of the narrowing is the entrance to a tall stable north, built onto the large stone slabs the street is built from.
117082: As the street made from large stone slabs packed with dirt between them sharply bends, it intersects with a smaller road heading north. Towards the south the Cobble Street continues with a small incline towards a tall tower to the south east.
117083: A stocky mountain mule is here, waiting to serve.

The ground is made from packed dirt over years of travelling, with a cover of sawdust and ground rind from pine trees. The width of the road varies, wider to the south but narrows slightly as it winds north up a gentle hill. Buildings accompany the road on both sides, and east lies a large open archery range.
117084: As the road traverses slightly up towards the north it widens, the layer of sawdust and ground rind on the road is thick and bounces slightly when travelled upon. It passed between houses on the east side and a man height fence to the west. Between the posts on the fence one can see a large animal market. Down a slight descent to the south, the road leads between the stables of Bree and an archer range.
117085: The road is narrowing both south and west from here, the bend in the Mill Road is over thirty yards wide. All along the northern part of the road stacks of untreated logs occupy most of the space, with just enough passing space to pass by the loggers' cabins and get to the Bree sawmill. A house with several furs hanging outside is seen to the east.
117086: Sharp Bend in the Cobble Street

Passing between stone walls both west and south and wooden houses northeast, the Cobble Street sharply bends. The stone walls along the southern border stretch several stories up into the air. Nearby east, a park can be seen. Down a decline northbound, a stone road, a dirt road and a large stable can be spotted in the distance.
117087: This park provides a quiet respite from the noise of the city. The grass is well-manicured, with some low rolling highs sprawling in every direction. A short path connects the street to a clearing in the grass here. A multitude of insects teem the grass, feeding on scraps left by city residents. Linked with the wall to the east, a tower rises to the south.
117088: There is an old street-lamp on the border of the street.

Paved with large stones, the Old East Road passes between the walls of the Prancing Pony inn and tall houses. A pleasant smell of food accompanied by the noise of people come from the northeast. Straight to the east the road spreads out to a wide space with a large fountain.
117089: There is a lit street-lamp on the border of the street, illuminating the area.

Narrowing slightly, the Old East Road runs both east and west, still a wide enough road for two wagons to pass each other. North of the road the Bree-hill rises up, winding through the landscape. Several doors painted in rich colours are spread out in the hills. South, an open yard spreads out towards a wooden house.
117090: There is a lit street-lamp on the border of the street, illuminating the area.

Winding both east and south, the Old East Road has been paved with large stones, giving echoes from nearby buildings when horses and wagons pass by. Heading north, a white gravelled road winds its way upwards into the Bree hills. To the east several buildings and most prominently the Prancing Pony Inn can be seen.
117091:
A wooden direction sign is here.
There is a lit street-lamp on the border of the street, illuminating the area.

The wide paved Old East Road continues both west and north from here, and a narrower Road intersects from the south. To the east a tall fence rises far overhead, even while mounted. Several buildings can be seen down the south street, and northwest a stone tower can be seen in the distance.
117092: There is a lit street-lamp on the border of the street, illuminating the area.

A narrower stretch of the paved Old East Road, passing between a steeply rising hill to the north and houses to the south. Any noise here is echoed back from both directions creating a cacophony of sounds. Westwards the road continues towards the west gate of Bree.
117093:
There is a lit street-lamp on the border of the street, illuminating the area.
Eccairandur the Elf (ecc), wielding a black runed dagger, is standing here (glowing).
A sturdy pack horse is standing here.

Stretching both west and east, the wide paved Old East Road passes through the city of Bree. A small patch of grass ends south of the road in a sloping drop into a small lake. North a door opens into a small timber house. The west gate of Bree is nearby, while the city of Bree grows eastwards.
117094:
A wooden painted map of Bree is here, nailed to a post.
There is a lit street-lamp on the border of the street, illuminating the area.
A Guard of Bree is here, watching the gate.
A Guard of Bree is here, watching the gate.
Harry the Bree Gatekeeper stands here.

From the solid black building to the north a solid timber wall rises tall up in the air, featuring a wide wooden gate fixed using metal hinges. The gate has a latch fixed with a chain, to stop just anyone opening the gate from the inside. The sound of water can be heard from the south just down a slippery grass slope, and north a black door leads into the gatekeeper's house. A wooden sign is fixed to the gate.
117095: Outside the West Gate of Bree

The passage between the hedge to the west and the tall gate to the east creates a fourteen yard wide shaded place. The gates are set shallow in a tall timber wall, both to the south and north the wall bends out and goes into the hedge, not allowing any passage. Deep tracks in the ground where the gate has been opened are clearly visible, showing the gate's frequent use.
117096: Growing massively thick and tall, the hedge marking the western border of Bree has been cut to allow travellers through. The opening is over ten yards wide, just like the road travelling straight west and east. The road widens on either side of the almost ten yard wide hedge, travelling west towards the Shire and east to Bree.
117097: Made of packed soil and dirt, the road is both wide and frequently travelled by wagons, horses and feet. Over twelve feet wide, the road travels straight both east and west, bordered by grass and small bushes. To the west the road intersects with the Greenway and towards the east a large hedge spreads afar bordering Bree city.
117098:
A massive boulder with faded letters rests in the corner of the crossing.
A hardened ranger is walking around, looking for tracks.

This is the crossing of the ancient Old East Road and the Greenway, the equally old road that runs north and south. A few trees and thick bushes stand next to the crossing. In the northeast corner of the crossing, an ancient, massive boulder can be seen. The Greenway runs in a straight line southward, and cuts the grass-covered lands to its sides in two. The Old East Road bends in the west and quickly vanishes from sight.
117106: Light grass covers a wide expanse of rolling hills here. To the north is an area of open, grassy flatlands, while to the east the hills continue. Beyond the hills is a green sprawl of brushland. Not far to the west can be seen the a large road which runs north-south.
117107: Smooth, gently sloping hills stretch away to the north and west, covered in a thin layer of grass. To the east is a thick brush, its branches wild and thorned and its tall bushes blocking the view of what lies past the border. Wide plains open to the south as far as the eye can see.
117108: The thick brushland borders a sudden, sloping incline to the south and west. Bounded by the hills, the brushes expand in all other directions, wild and grasping with branches and thorns. Dense growth creates unsteady ground underfoot, and winding vines wrap around each other, making for a treacherous tripping hazard.
117109: The bushes stretch out in all directions at the base of a slick, mossy slope that descends from the north. The slope is too steep to climb, lacking in stable handholds. Visibility is low, and nothing can be discerned about the brush elsewhere.
117110: Broad, old trunks stand amidst the wild bushes like ancient stone pillars, casting the surrounding brush into shadow. A large pile of decaying leaves has amassed at the base of a steep slope to the north. There is only more brushland all around, though the way to the east is a dense tangle of branches that would be hard to pass and harder to return through.
117111: Narrowly bounded by a thick barrier of woody undergrowth and a steep cliff, this north-west passage links the open plains to the south to the heart of the wild brushland to the north. Even at the edge of the bushes, visibility is low, and old trunks and broken branches make for uneven footing.
117112: The butchered corpse of a large elk is lying here.

Deep in the brush the bushes grow denser, having grown isolated in this place for a very long time. Long thorns and snarled vines are everpresent, and the ground is uneven where titanic roots crawl through the earth. Here and there, trees pierce through the top of the gigantic thornbushes.
117113: Massive trees of all kinds loom sporadically above thick, thorny bushes, crowding the view for what must be miles. The heart of the brushland is old and wild, thick with plant life and filled with the faint chirps and deep growling of wildlife.
117114: The thick bushes come abruptly to an end here at the top of a steep muddy bank. At the bottom of the drop lies a swift-running river, and from the roar of the water and the spray a large waterfall must lie further to the north. To the west, a large mound rises up from under some brambles, while to the south the brush thickens.
117115:
There are three large pieces of raw venison here.
The corpse of a boar is lying here.
The butchered corpse of a tall stag is lying here.
The corpse of a starved grey wolf is lying here.
The corpse of a wolf cub is lying here.

The depths of the brushland is a natural maze of branches, vines, and ancient trees. While the thorny, grasping bushes continue all around, the way south is unusually thick with flora. Undergrowth has grown tall over a fallen trunk, making the way impassable.
117116: A brown pond between old branches and roots is here.

A small pond of clean water is here, scattered leaves drifting on its surface. The occasional root reaches out towards the water, but otherwise the area around the pond is clear of branches, a rare opening in the otherwise thick chaos of the brushes. The clearing halts at an eroded, mossy slope to the south.
117117:
The corpse of a wolf cub is lying here.
The corpse of a huge, black wolf is lying here.
The corpse of a black wolf is lying here.
The corpse of a black wolf is lying here.
The corpse of a menacing pack leader is lying here.
On the ground, there are two large pieces of raw venison.
The butchered corpse of a tall stag is lying here.
A low shrub with bright green, oblong leaves is growing here.
Scattered in and on the shrub, there are two piles of blueberries.
A small rabbit glares angrily at you.
A black wolf pads restlessly, looking for its next prey.

The soil is soft and damp near the river to the north, wild and uneven with rough, winding roots. The full height of the brushes is hidden by the thick growth of their branches, blocking out sight of the top of the brush. The brush continues in all directions, though to the west the vines and branches are too dense to navigate.
117118: The corpse of an elk cow is lying here.

The depths of the brushland are a natural maze of branches, vines, and ancient trees. With only wild bushes in every direction, there are no landmarks to guide an explorer's progress. A single point of interest is a broad mound of earth to the north, shrouded beneath the dense undergrowth.
117119:
A pile of gnawed bones is heaped here.
A huge, black wolf is here, ready to devour.
The mother wolf stands here, protecting her young cubs.

This large, warm cavern is thick with the smell of decomposed bodies and damp leaves. Several carcasses litter the floor, some crudely pulled apart, and all showing extensive signs of gnawing. The only exit is a dark, narrow tunnel out towards the bushes beyond.
117120: Dry Streambed on a Boggy Land
A brown pond between reeds connects to a waterway to the south.

There is a streambed that generally flows from west to south. The streambed still carries some water toward the south despite being dry to the west. Only swampy ground remains on the borders of the streambed's dried-up sections. The grass is short and the terrain is flat. A path through the area is indicated by a few rocks laying on the damp grass.
117121: There are scattered trees and wild shrubs across this brushland. There is no sign of water on the sluggish surface of a little dried-up streambed that goes eastward. In the streambed's moist soil, mosquitoes can deposit their eggs safely.
117122:
The remains of a massive tangle of roots lie here in a heap of rotting compost.
A swamp iris grows here.
A swarm of midges is here, humming around you.

High grass grows in this large clearing which is surrounded by thick forest and brush. The ground feels soggy making this the perfect habitat for wildlife. To the south the bushes get very dense making further passage through the underwood impossible.
117123: This is the highest spot of the dry badlands giving a good view of the surrounding lands. To the north the badlands decline toward brushlands covered with wild vegetation while to the east the lands look soggier. A large tower made of black stone is to the south surrounded by an old, hay-covered stonewall.
117124: A brown fox is here, looking for some rabbits to chew up.

In this eastern part of the downs the hills are expanding into wide open areas. Westwards the rolling plains stretch all the way to the horizon. The grass that covers the ground sways in the gentle breeze, almost looking like the waves on the ocean. In the distance to the southeast a tower of black stone rises.
117125:
A large shrub grows here, its branches loosely spreading.
On the shrub, there are some cherries.

Gentle rolling plains stretch far to the east and south while toward the north the downs get more undulating. To the west a frequently used road is leading from north to south. Small groups of trees and bushes are scattered among the plains as the perfect habitat for wildlife.
117126:
A small waterway coming from the west forks toward the north and south.
A swamp iris grows here.

The ground seems fertile and the grass is high with some big rocks scattered over the land. Most of the rocks are covered with moss, which is a sign that travellers do not pass too often. From here it is possible to see the surroundings quite well. While the ground is just marshy to the west and north, the south opens up to wide rocky plateaus.
117127: Several smaller ponds connected through waterways are here.

While the flora becomes denser in the north, the south opens up to wide rocky plateaus. There aren't many trees here, but those that do flourish stretch their limbs skyward. In these otherwise marshy regions, a number of waterways connect smaller ponds.
117128:
A swamp iris grows here.
A waterway is winding its way through reeds.
A magpie is flying around looking for some food.

With the exception of a few reeds near a waterway, this open region is entirely covered with grass and is devoid of any nearby plants or trees. The grass is short, making movement easy. On the western badlands, a huge tower made of black stones may be observed. There is no direct access to the west due to an old stonewall.
117129:
The corpse of a giant turtle is lying here.
A small brown pond connects to a waterway leading north.

The rocky plateaus are covered with ash. A creek connects a brown pond to the north, where it appears that the grounds are more fertile and attractive. Further travel is impossible to the west due to muddy ponds that appear to be dangerous and emit a strong sulphurous scent. There are extensive, arid plains to the south.
117130: The burned ground is uneven and rocky in spots with long dry tufts of grass covering the remainder. The surroundings are black, looking as if burned down by fire. With the exception of the north, where wide rocky plateaus appear, the plains extend in all directions.
117131: The rocky surface of this burned plains looks sharp and dangerous. There is a trail leading toward a sketchy-looking small hut to the west at the edge of a cliff. To the north and south wide barren plains of burned land continue far toward the horizon.
117132: This area shows fewer signs of life and more of draught and malnourishment. The burned plains are covered with ash and dust continuing toward the north. Toward the west a sandy slope descends to a great open space while toward the south the plains slowly descend to fertile lowlands.
117133: The plains continue to slightly descend into the lowlands toward the south. While these lands look healthy and offer enough food for animals the land gets more desolate with every step taken toward the northern direction where the green grass turns into brown and unhealthy-looking lands.
117134: A wild bull seems ready to charge you.

The fertile lowlands are covered with deep green grass and occasional bushes. This is the perfect spot for grazing animals. Far toward the northwest the lands ascends gradually from a healthy green-looking landscape toward a desolate brown.
117135: Deep green grass grows on the fertile lowlands in every direction making this the perfect environment for grazing animals. More trees and bushes seem to grow toward the southern direction while to the west the grass gets a little bit higher making it harder to travel.
117136:
The butchered corpse of a boar is lying here.
A magnificent old tree grows here between the bushes.

Lush green grass grows beside the brook, looking very inviting for a place to rest. The sand on the bottom of the brook is dark, making it hard to see what might hide beneath the surface. Thorny bushes make travel east and south impossible.
117137: Dry cracked plains covered with occasional tufts of dry grass are the only plants visible. A cliff's edge to the west and south prevents further movement in those directions. Excellent landscapes may be seen all the way to the horizon in the direction of the south. A wide rocky plateau can be seen to the north.
117138:
A muddy brown pond connects to a waterway toward the north.
A swamp iris grows here.

There are sporadic trees and parched grass on this rocky plateau. Muddy pools to the east block further travel. At the surface of the murky pools, dangerous-looking bubbles burst, leaving a sulphurous odour in the air. The plains in the north and west appear to be rather marshy while to the south they appear to be burned.
117139:
A brown pond between reeds connects to a waterway to the north.
A swamp iris grows here.
A magpie is flying around looking for some food.

In the east and north, the plains become more humid, whereas in the west, the land dries out. To the northwest, a huge black tower is encircled by an ancient stonewall covered in hay. A treacherous rocky ledge to the south prevents further movement. However, the view is stunning and plains can be seen all the way to the horizon.
117140: An old, hay-covered stonewall surrounds the badlands to the north. Vines and other vegetation are growing on the wall. A little section of the wall is cut off by a large fissure in the eroding plains. The sole visible route to the north is a dilapidated wooden arch bridge that was constructed at this fissure. A tower composed of black stone is the badlands' most distinctive feature. Except for an extremely steep slope of rubble that leads to the western badlands, the rest of the terrain is dry and level.
117141: Black Tower on an Isolated Badland

The tall black tower to the north is slightly tilted to one side and its battlements are twisted in shape and design. Vines have taken root along the shaded areas of the tower and spiral-shaped thornbushes surround its base. At the top of a flight of stairs is a large stone door leading into the tower. The only way out of these isolated badlands, which are encircled by an old, hay-covered stonewall, is to the south, where a wooden arched bridge spans a deep fissure.
117142: A small path paves its way northward toward a tall black tower which can be seen far on the horizon. The plains slightly ascend toward the south leading toward a slightly higher hill while far to the west the plains change toward badlands.
117143: A woody evergreen plant grows here, with many stems reaching upward.

The depositioned plains are flanked by a steep cliff wall to the north and east. The wall is composed of different looking layers of rock that make it impossible to climb. The otherwise rocky plains continue to the west and south.
117144: The rocky plains run through a very wide valley which is flanked by a steep rock wall in a general northeast direction and a rubble covered slope to the southwest. Small rocks and boulders make for hard travel through the otherwise grass-covered plains.
117145: A woody evergreen plant grows here, with many stems reaching upward.

These depositioned plains are flanked by a steep rock wall to the east and north. At the top of the eastern cliff a small shabby wooden hut can be seen. The otherwise rocky plains continue far toward the southern and western horizon.
117146: The extremely dry conditions and the resulting poor vegetation has taken its toll on the land. A wide valley slightly ascends toward the northwest while to the south more fertile lowlands continue far toward the horizon. A sandy, dry slope leads toward higher lands to the east.
117147: The corpse of a wild bull is lying here.

Grassy plains continue in every direction while the lands slowly descend toward the southeast into the rich green lowlands and to the north the colour changes gradually from a healthy green to a more desolate brown. Apart from the grass there is no special vegetation in the vicinity.
117148: The lowlands around here are covered with a deep green grass and lots of bushes and trees except of a small clearing of about sixty feet in diameter which is free of any vegetation at all. In the centre of the clearing there is a large thorny bush.
117149: A buck runs swiftly from place to place, looking about warily as it grazes.

The lowlands in this area are green and fertile however the ground is very uneven and many small rocks cover the ground, hidden between high grass making it hard to travel. Toward the west and south the undervegetation and bushes get very dense, making further travel in that direction impossible.
117150:
The corpse of an elk cow is lying here.
The corpse of a large elk is lying here.

Although dry the plains around here are covered with grass and widely spread bushes. In a general northwest direction there is a steep slope covered with loose rubble leading up toward a long stone wall. The plains ascending toward the north look even more desolate while the other directions lead toward more fertile lands.
117151: Fine particles of dust and sand cover the desolate plains which gradually ascend toward the north, while the southeast is descending into lowlands. A steep slope to the west makes further travel in that direction impossible. The plains toward the south are getting more fertile and the vegetation gets greener.
117152:
The corpse of a wild bull is lying here.
A brown cow is here, contemplating a higher reality whilst chewing slowly.
A beautiful and docile horse is standing here.

The rocky plains gradually ascend toward the north while to the west is a very steep slope. The slope is covered with rubble, making it impossible to climb and on the top is a long stone wall. Toward the southeast there is a large clearing leading into the lowlands.
117153: The ground is cracked and disjointed with numerous jagged edges and stone outcroppings making travel difficult. A small path continues to the west along a steep slope leading toward a long stone wall. To the east and north the rocky plains continue.
117154: This huge field of grass stretches all the way to the horizon. A small trampled path is leading through short grass toward a stone house to the south. The grass beside the path has grown much higher and tall rocks make the passage exhausting. In the northwest some hills are rising over the grass and show their crests by rising high above the plains.
117155: A narrow strip of land covered by white sand is flanked by badlands to the west and north. East of the narrow strip a barely green turf has managed to grow while toward the south a small path paves its way between sandstone boulders toward a cliff.
117156: The plains stretch out towards the horizon in all directions here. The green grass turning brown in the western parts where badlands dominate the view, barren and dry. Only a few tracks can be found of the sparse wildlife, most of them old and hard to make out.
117157: The vast badlands give a good view of the surrounding lands. A wide and well-frequented road which runs in a general north to south direction can be seen to the west. To the north large rolling plains continue while to the east and south the badlands decline steeply toward an eroded landscape. Large boulders to the east seem to make further travel impossible.
117158: Trees are scattered all over the low rolling plains. The ground here is not as fertile as to the north which makes it hard for the vegetation to grow. The road just west of here is leading in a general north to south direction. To the east and south the rolling plains turn into badlands covered with sand.
117159: The badlands are covered with dry grass and sand. To the west and north rolling plains continue while to the east and south a sudden steep and sandy elevation change makes further passage impossible. A big black stone tower to the northeast is encircled by an old hay-covered stonewall where vines and other plants are growing.
117160: The vast, grassy flatland is dotted with a few trees and stretches out in all directions as the surrounding scenery sings a lullaby in warm, nostalgic tones. A broad road that appears to be well-travelled and heading about north to south passes by to the west.
117161:
A restless rabbit bounces around.
A brown fox is here, looking for some rabbits to chew up.

Rolling plains which are free from most kinds of vegetation continue far to the north and west. To the south sand covered badlands rise over the horizon, casting long shadows over the flat landscape. A large tower made of black stone rises to the east. Between the plains and the tower an old, hay-covered stonewall makes further passage impossible.
117162:
The corpse of a werewolf is lying here.
A half-rotten corpse is hanging here.

This small wooden hut which seems to be abandoned by its former owner has fallen into shabbiness and disrepair. Cracks in the walls and roof are a sign that this building has seen better days. The boards in the walls are loose and badly battered. The entrance to the east is covered by a crooked door barely hanging in its hinges. Scattered about the room are fragments of bones, bits of fur, and a partly decomposed human corpse. It is obvious that the cabin remains in use even though the original owner has departed.
117163:
The corpse of a dreadful snake is lying here.
The corpse of a dreadful snake is lying here.

In this dark cave the damp walls are rough in texture and have many tiny flecks and minerals embedded in them. The smell of stagnant water makes it hard to breathe. A small path winds its way up between rocks and boulders until it meets dense bushes.
117164:
A fierce-looking eel lurks in the darkness.
A fierce-looking eel lurks in the darkness.

A large cavern is filled with stagnant murky water. Several parts of the ceiling hang low over the surface and leave only a small space to navigate on the lakes surface. A small rocky underground beach to the west seems to be the only part of this cavern that isn't flooded with water.
117165:
The corpse of an eel is lying here.
The corpse of an eel is lying here.

The grey rocks below the lake's surface have depth, and the water gives them a strong tint. The boulder in the brine waits patiently for all eternity because there is nothing but chilly water around it. There is absolutely no current in the cold water, and there are no obvious ways to keep diving rather than ascending to the surface.
117166: A tall stag is here, grazing peacefully.

A narrow tunnel dug into the earth descends slightly to the south leading deeper under the ground. The tunnel runs in a general north to south direction and seems to be artificially designed. Toward the north the tunnel ascends until it ends abruptly at a ladder leading straight up into a hole overgrown with vines and branches.
117167: A trickle of water flows into a dark pool.

Groundwater drips down the dirt walls that are supported by rotting timber, trickling quietly into a small pool, before flowing out by some hidden passage. The air is damp with the smell of decaying wood, and the tunnel floor is covered with a mix of rock and mud.
117168: This narrow, mouldy tunnel has been dug haphazardly through the earth, with crude support beams providing a modicum of protection against collapse. A trickle of water dribbles northward, creating a small depression through the muddy floor. Twisted roots hang in the air below the ceiling, their journey through the earth ending in this tunnel.
117169: Strong roots binding the dirt walls and roof overhead assist half-rotten timber supports, preventing this tunnel from collapsing. The air within this tunnel, to the north, smells mouldy and damp, and a quiet trickle of water permeates the darkness.
117170: A brook babbles here cascading off the rocks.

A small brook is here, winding through the fields. The water is so clear that it is possible to see the bottom which is covered with round stones. The brook seems to originate somewhere to the south but dense bushes make it impossible to find its source. Fields can be seen west of here, and some bushes are to the east.
117171: The grass on these fields are short and juicy making it perfect for cattle to graze in. Bushes are scattered across the fields and an occasional tree can be spotted. To the north the fields are spreading out and to the east a small brook winds its way through the fields.
117172: A black wolf pads restlessly, looking for its next prey.

Fields covered with lush green grass are spreading out to the north and east. Some bushes are scattered around the fields and some trees that can provide shade on a hot summer day can be spotted. To the south and west large bushes and some trees can be seen.
117173: Here a large clearing opens up, making travelling comfortable. Short green grass covers the ground. To the north dense bushes can be seen, to the west a small trail winds its way through a sea of grass and to the east lush green fields can be spotted. A trail towards a rugged animal track is leading south.
117174: Here the fields are covered with high grasses that swirl in the wind. To the west and south the grass seems to be shorter, thus making it easier to walk through. Thick bushes to the north and east make travel in those directions impossible.
117175: A fallow deer is grazing peacefully here.

These fields are covered with lush green grass, that will sparkle in the morning when the fog is chased away by the warm sun. A small trail is leading to the north beside a dried-out brook toward wastelands while to the east the grass continues. To the west and south the vegetation gets denser.
117176:
A sprawling green bush of stinging nettle grows here.
An erect shrub with green pinnate leaves is growing here.
Inside the shrub, there are two piles of crimson raspberries.
A black wolf pads restlessly, looking for its next prey.

Thick bushes grow here, making travel somewhat difficult. Some bird-chirping can be heard from inside the thick bushes. The bushes seem to be passable to all directions, but seem to be less dense to the north and east where grassy fields can be seen through the thicket.
117177: These infertile plains are covered with dry grass and some bushes which seem to be the only plants that have been able to get a foothold in the dry soil. To the east the wasteland spreads out, but to the west and south some lush verdure is seen. To the north a very steep hillside with a long stone wall on its top makes further journey in that direction impossible.
117178:
A brown snake watches you.
A brown snake watches you.
A fallow deer is grazing peacefully here.
A tall stag is here, grazing peacefully.

Dry vegetation covers the fields, some dead trees are scattered across the land. From east to south a dried-out brook winds its way, breaking the monotony of this infertile landscape. A small trail is heading south, where some greenery can be seen. To the west the wasteland continues while to the north a steep hillside with a long stonewall at its top makes further journey in that direction impossible.
117179: A path descends through grass and bushes toward the west while to the south the bushes are too dense for travel and to the north a steep drop makes further passage impossible. Down to the north a valley trough can be discerned while to the east the dry plains continue.
117180: A small cluster of clover grows here.

A small animal path weaves its way through the grass. A small brook murmurs through the undergrowth of grass and some small bushes. The bushes seems to get denser to the south, and to the east the plains continue to ascend out of the valley.
117181:
A fallow deer is grazing peacefully here.
A small boar with big yellow tusks looks eager to fight.

Dry plains with brown, tall grass cover the ground of the valley. Moving to the east, a forest can be discerned. Tracks and trails of animals can be seen where the grass is pushed and flattened. The valley slightly ascends toward the north and descends to the south.
117182: A small boar with big yellow tusks looks eager to fight.

The dry grassland stretches far into a valley in the south direction, covered with dry grass. To the west and east the valley is flanked by steep and rocky terrain making further passage impossible. To the north the dry grassland ascends into sandy badlands.
117183: A small animal, all covered in spines, snuffles amongst the undergrowth.

Small bushes and dry grass cover the grounds of the badlands and no shelter can be seen in the near vicinity. A large road which runs in a general north to south direction makes a long bend around these hills. To the south the plains continue while to the east the badlands decline steep toward an eroded landscape.
117184:
A skeleton of some humanoid lies in the dust.
The mother wolf stands here, protecting her young cubs.
A wolf cub happily plays here.
A wolf cub happily plays here.

A small opening in the granite wall gradually opens into a wide room of slick, dark stone. Little direct sunlight reaches the interior of this cave, and bulbous mushrooms sprout along its curved walls. The sloped floor here is covered in a thin layer of clear slime, and in the corner, a doline drops into the deep recesses of the mountain. A clump of dark fur lies in a heap next to the doline, and a crumbled mass of bones and sinew peeks out from it.
117185: The steep banks of the river descend rapidly here, being replaced by dense undergrowth and shrubs as the river passes into a rapidly thickening brushland. The flora is especially dense to the southeast, from where strange noises and animal cries can be heard. To the north, the brush thins out somewhat, giving way to more open land beyond.
117186: The river flows swiftly westward here, hemmed in on both sides by steep banks. Many small stones litter the riverbed and shores, and in places larger ones jut out above the surface, making this stretch more than a little hazardous for watercraft.
117187: The river slows its pace somewhat here, as it widens and continues on its journey westward. Tall bushes encroach on both the north and south banks. To the south, the brushland becomes much thicker, and it is impossible to see more than a short distance. To the north, the thorny bushes gradually give way to a large area of plains beyond.
117188: The river runs more slowly here, and bends gently to the west from the north as it meets the tall, bushy riverbank. To the south, the brush and undergrowth remain as thick as ever, while to the north an area of rocky hills can be seen in the distance.
117189:
A salmon swims here.
A brook trout is here, swimming in the current.

The river bends from east to south here and increases its pace somewhat as it is fed by water from a small inlet to the north. To the east it becomes narrower as it passes underneath a rocky overhang. The western riverbank is sandy and shallow, providing a convenient point to enter or leave the river.
117190: The river speeds up suddenly here as it passes between the eroded riverbank to the north and a steep bank to the south. A short distance above, a rock shelf juts out over the water, while to the east the sound of falling water can be heard above the noise of the river itself.
117192: Tall bushes seem to grow taller as they follow the gentle rise of a mound. Just past its peak, the crest falls away into the rapids below. While the drop is not all that high, it is still too far to safely jump, and the eroded soil makes climbing impossible. To the south, a sea of waving branches and dense bushes spreads out for miles.
117193:
A bloodthirsty bat is sleeping here, hanging from the ceiling.
A bloodthirsty bat is sleeping here, hanging from the ceiling.

Water drips from the ceiling of this large cavern and falls on the floor forming large puddles in several places. To the south a loud roaring sound can be heard while to the west, a tunnel entrance is dimly visible in the cavern wall.
117194: This is a narrow stone tunnel that appears to be part natural, part man-made. Perhaps this was once an underground waterway that was at some time enlarged to make a traversable tunnel. The tunnel winds around from the east to the north.
117195: Here the narrow, stone tunnel splits in two directions, one going north and one going west. The only sound is the incessant dripping of water as it falls from the ceiling to land in numerous small puddles on the floor. The faint sound of water is heard to the south.
117196:
The corpse of a merchant lies here.
A huge black fungus is here, exuding a foul stench.
A bloodthirsty bat is sleeping here, hanging from the ceiling.

The tunnel ends abruptly at a dead end at this point, with further progress blocked by a sheer rock wall. At the base of the wall is a large dark pool from which a strange smell emanates. The exit east leads towards the darkness of a long tunnel.
117197: The rough, stone walls of this narrow tunnel runs approximately north-south. The dripping of water is a faint, constant sound as it falls from the ceiling to land in numerous small, dark puddles on the floor. The damp ground bears the sign of old footprints.
117198:
A large bat is here, hanging in the darkness.
A large bat is here, hanging in the darkness.

The tunnel opens out into a small cave at this point, one that bears the sign of active habitation. There are bits of junk and refuse that have been piled up in one corner, with the barest semblance of order. In the north wall of the cave is a small opening.
117199: This is a small cave, crowded with tables and chairs. There are various pieces of junk and useless items stacked around the walls. The ceiling is low, and lanterns dangle from it, providing light. A couple of low beds are standing against the walls. To the south there is a small cave, and to the west there is a lit passageway.
117200: The narrow stone passageway bends between the east and north. Lanterns are attached to the walls with crude fixtures, and the absence of dust makes it obvious that this passage is used fairly often. In the dim, flickering light, openings into small rooms to the north and east are visible.
117201:
A crude shelf has been made from a wooden plank bolted to the stone wall.
A small barrel made of aged oak and strong iron hoops stands here.

This is a large cave with a straw-covered floor and a low ceiling. The cave is lit by several torches along the walls, casting shadows across piles of refuse and junk in the corners of the room. Amidst these signs of habitation is a narrow hatchway, leading down.
117202:
A heavy, reinforced chest sits in the corner of the room.
A sturdy crate made of nailed wooden planks sits on the floor.

Judging by the boxes and barrels that have been strewn all over the floor, this small cave is being used as a storage room. Despite the disorder, the lack of dust over the room's contents suggests this room has not been left idle. The way out is a sturdy ladder leading upwards, towards a lit open cavern.
117203: The river passes through a narrow ravine at this point, with steep walls of rock to the north and south. The sound of the rushing water echoes from the rocks making it impossible to hear anything else. Above, the river is spanned by an old yet sturdy stone bridge.
117221: A furious, old bull is stamping with his hoof.

The trail is ascending toward the west while to the east it joins into a very wide road. The northern and southern slopes ascend steeper and a stone wall makes further passage there impossible. To the west several buildings made out of stone can be seen.
117222:
A circular stone well has been built here.
A starving cow stands here, looking for a patch of grass.

Stone ruins of an abandoned farm can be seen at the end of the trail. Toward the north is an uncultivated ranch while to the south farmlands can be seen. Everything seems to be abandoned and where once surely was a thriving farm now only ruins remain.
117223: Although abandoned, this ranch is still very impressive because of its sheer size. Still intact stone walls and steep slopes beyond them border the land. A big gate to the south leads toward the ruins of a farm and the ranch extends far toward the east.
117224:
An abandoned swing creaks her melody in the wind.
A gorcrow is standing here.
A black crow flies low to the ground here, looking for carrion to eat.

Old stone walls prevent further movement in the opposing directions as the abandoned property extends for miles to the west. A swing makes a musical creaking as if it has become both entertainer and audience over the years. Large, rocky badlands may be seen in the very distant east, and a river in the very far north.
117225: The abandoned farmland must have once served as a source for local produce but now the barren soil can only grow occasional weeds and scrubs. Stone walls border the infield and to the north a large gate leads toward the ruins of a farm.
117226:
An old weathered scarecrow is planted firmly in the ground here.
A black raven flies in the sky searching for flesh to prey upon.
A black raven flies in the sky searching for flesh to prey upon.

Barren farmland stretches for miles toward the west while in all other directions a stone wall makes further travel impossible. A long road leading toward the south can be spotted from up here while to the east vast badlands continue toward the horizon.
117227:
An erect shrub with green pinnate leaves is growing here.
Inside the shrub, there are two piles of crimson raspberries.

These ghastly plains are covered in an extremely thick layer of purple weeds that resemble tentacles. The weeds wrap themselves around occasional rocks as a lover holds the hand of her beloved. In the spirit of adventure that the growing season provides, they yearn to climb and bloom, to decorate and love, and to seize the day. The plains continue to the west and south, and possibly to the east, a road's faint shape can be made out.
117239: A large mother hawk is here looking for prey to feed her young.

Different kinds of vines and weeds cover these grisly plains. It is hard to find a path through this thicket of vines with sharp edges and thorns. Toward the east and west the thicket gets denser and further travel seems impossible.
117240: A large mother hawk is here looking for prey to feed her young.

This valley is barren, save for a high slope to the east that is covered in vines and weeds with jagged edges. There is no way to go any further in that direction due to the slope's severe incline. North the terrain slightly ascends toward plains with denser vegetation while to the south higher hills promise a better view.
117241:
A large hawk-like bird is here overlooking its territory.
A large hawk-like bird is here overlooking its territory.

The Road to Fornost, which is located far below at the bottom of a precipitous descent, is clearly visible to the east from this modest overlook on top of a forested hill. To the west, a simple wooden forest shelter with a cloth-covered door rests in between some trees. Small gaps in the thicket allow for further travel to the north and south, but the path westward beyond the shelter is impossible.
117242: Tall trees encircle and hang over this small, protected glade in the forest. Although no small animals are visible, there are quiet rustling noises coming from the underbrush that indicate their existence. Only minor openings to the west and north allow for further movement, while the east and south are heavily overgrown, steeply descending, and hence impassable.
117243:
A nest is here.
Yellow flowers, with grey-green foliage, grow in clusters here.
A large mother hawk is here looking for prey to feed her young.

The trough valley ends at the valley step where steep slopes make further travel impossible. The valley is barren with only rocks and larger boulders covering the floor. The occasional bush on the steep slopes is the only vegetation visible.
117244: Beneath the trees the floor is covered with bracken and brambles. To the east there is a narrow path ascending up a hill which is covered by trees. A narrow trail continues to the south but ends somewhere in the undergrowth to the west.
117245: Here the trail dips into a small hollow as it bends from east to north. The trees grow more sparsely here and meadows with the occasional bush dominate the fauna. The ground is somewhat damp and mossy, while the air is cool and has a musty smell.
117246: The narrow trail continues to descend to the west and south while to the north and east the undergrowth becomes too dense to penetrate. Through a small gap toward the east a small part of the Road to Fornost and the bushy plains beyond can be seen. An ancient stump stands beside the path, from which small fungi are growing.
117247: A large, venomous-looking green snake is coiled up here.

Heathlands with a low-growing woody vegetation stretch toward the east where the tangle becomes dense and impassable ascending on a hill while to the north suddenly a deep drop into a valley makes further passage impossible. The only passable footpath is toward a sparsely forested area south.
117248:
A small oaken table has been set here.
On the table, there are two strips of dried meat.
A filthy straw pallet is lying here.
A brigand, looking at your nice purse, is sneaking here.

The small wooden shelter provides cover from natural influences. Bushels of straw lie by the northern wall and are partially covered by a blanket. A small table and chair in the centre of the room and a cupboard on the backside are the only visible pieces of furniture. The shelter is lit by a candle that has been placed on the cupboard.
117249: A beautiful bookshelf with intricate carvings stands in the corner of the room.

The interior of this room looks dusty and unused. Ancient furnishings reminiscent of Arda's Second Age are handsomely placed about the room. Several paintings and tapestries depict cruel battle scenes while one painting shows a red-robed man with a mocking smile. A huge bookshelf, which looks as if it was torn from the wall is laying in a cluttered heap on the floor. The space is lit softly by torches that are mounted on the stone walls.
117250:
You see two belt pouches on the ground.
A small pouch, made from leather, lies in the dust.
The corpse of a bodyguard is lying here.
The corpse of Manthor the merchant is lying here.
A sturdy bed made from solid oak lies here, covered in warm blankets.

This room is surprisingly wide and spacious. A thin window in the south wall allows for sunlight during the day however the large room leaves enough shadow to stay out of the sun. The space is lit by candles set on the stone walls. Lavish decor dominates the setting while long dark green velvet drapes line the windows. The large bed pushed against the far wall is made from finely crafted stone. A huge mirror with silver wrought around its edges in delicate designs is secured to the east wall. A small staircase allows access to the ground floor and the battlements to the top.
117251: A large eagle soars above you.

The top of the tower measures about thirty feet from one end to the other. Its edges are secured by battlements twisted in shape and design. The only way to exit the top of the tower is a fairly large trapdoor in one corner through which it is possible to access a staircase.
117252: Small sandstone boulders give the land some shape and shelter the few plants that have managed to grow here. This seems to be a narrow strip of land leading to a cliff covered by white sand to the south. At the edge of the cliff there is a steep drop to the valley below.
117253:
A wooden cupboard stands here.
A sturdy bed made from solid oak lies here, covered in warm blankets.

The house made out of white stone blocks consists of one large room. A simple stone fireplace is built into the western wall connected to a chimney. Right in front of the fireplace is a small wooden table and toward the east side of the room a cosy bed is set up against the wall. There are two visible exits out of the house, one to the north and one leading south onto the large veranda. The room gets plenty of natural light during the day thanks to small windows on the house's northern and southern sides. In order to light the space at night, candles are placed next to the fireplace.
117254: The garden snake slithers harmlessly here.

The barren pasture's ground is covered with dry grass and occasional bushes. To the west, the pasture is limited by a long stone wall which is set up to protect animals from whatever danger might be on the other side of the wall. To the north, the backside of a house made out of white stone is built right into the stone wall with a large veranda facing the pasture.
117255:
A rooster is here, strutting about.
The garden snake slithers harmlessly here.

The pasture slightly ascends and bends to the east. A long stone wall is set up to protect animals from the steep drops in the terrain to the south and west side. The ground is covered with large natural rocks and boulders, rare patches of grass and bushes between them.
117256: The pasture is very exposed to winds on this side of the elevation. Wind-torn grass and small strangely bent shrubs and bushes cover the ground. The small path through the pasture bends from the west and ascends slightly toward the north. A long stone wall protects animals from steep drops to the east and south.
117257: The corpse of a green snake is lying here.

At the top of this slight rise, the narrow route that led up the grassland comes to an end. Most of the bushes around the crest look either dead or sick. Although the land is grim, there is no abundance of small animal life. West of the crest the vegetation seems to be a bit denser just before a long stone wall is set up to protect animals in all directions but south.
117258: This wooden platform is several dozen feet above the ground of what seems to be a natural cavern. Below the platform a wooden construction is set up against the eastern wall which can be used to climb down to the ground of the cavern. The ceiling above the platform is stable rock and a small ladder leads further up toward a hatch.
117259:
A neat straw pallet is lying here.
A water barrel has been left here.

This natural cavern seems to be well maintained. The walls are lined with torch-holders and to the west the floor and walls are clad with wooden planks. Several straw mats indicate that this place is used as a sleeping place. The cavern has a very high ceiling and an improvised wooden construction has been setup at the eastern wall to reach a platform dozens of feet above the ground.
117260:
A weapons rack stands against the wall.
In the rack is a sabre.

Wooden planks cover the floor and parts of the walls of this artificially crafted tunnel which seems to be used as a hideout. Along the walls there are cabinets and shelves which seem to be used to store goods. In the centre of the room a wooden stair leads up to a trapdoor while to the north and east there are passages to other rooms. To provide adequate light to move through the tunnel, torches are set on the walls.
117261:
A small barrel made of aged oak and strong iron hoops stands here.
A large, sturdy table made from oak is sitting here.
On the table, there are three pieces of smoked, cured meat and a long, wicked knife.

This underground room seems to be the main common room. A large table and several chairs around it serve as a place of relaxation. Mounted on the walls are several pegs and shelves which are used to store stuff. At the far side of the room a large map of the nearby vicinity covers the wall. The only visible exit is a passage to the south. A number of candles that have been placed on the large table light the space.
117262:
A small oaken table has been set here.
On the table, there are two smoked pieces of meat.
A tall and strong hunter is standing here.

The wooden hut is built out of wooden logs and consists of one big main room. In the centre of the room is a large table while toward the southern wall there is a bed and a cabinet used as storage. At the far end of the room is a small stove.
117263: Thick Brush at a Valley Trough

An apple tree with bright green leaves grows here.
On the tree's branches are three apples.
A great horned owl looks cautiously around it.

A thick brush covers the trough of the valley. The surrounding flanks are steep and covered with rock and boulders making further passage out of the valley impossible. At the end of the trough is a small hut made of wooden logs.
117265: Quiet Meadow on a Low Ridge

The grass and small bushes that make up this quiet meadow is bordered by tangled, impassable shrubs to the east, and a steep drop to the west. The open meadow continues along a low ridge to the south. In the north, the brush and trees grow thicker.
117266: This long ridge is covered with green grass and sparse but thriving glossy-leaved trees. It descends gently towards the south where it meets a winding, narrow track that crosses the fields from west to south-east. A dense wall of bushes follows the ridge closely to the east.
117267: The track bends this way and that, moving around and in-between obstacles to take the easiest route through these fields. The path winds deftly around several large boulders, and stands of hazel. The brown path is beaten, trampled earth, and too narrow for wagons.
117268: Thorny bushes grow in dense clusters, with barely enough space between them to move across these fields. Towards the west, a low ridge barely rises above the top of a row of tall, thorny bushes. Thick roots snake across the ground, making footing unsure.
117269: Knobby roots, thorny thistles, and heavy brush cover the terrain here. To the north and east the undergrowth is so thick that any passage seems impossible. While to the west and south the bush is slightly less rampant, making the land somewhat more navigable.
117270: A small leathery fluid-sack is on the ground.

This area is overgrown with various bushes, many of which grows taller than a man on horseback. There is little to be seen in any direction except bushes of all sorts and sizes, and they grow so dense that they completely block travel in all directions except to the south where they grow a little thinner.
117271: In all directions the way forward is obstructed by tangled bushes, their branches bound by winding, climbing vines. The earth is loose and scattered about, filling the air with its scent, leaving clear evidence that wild boars were here rooting among the bushes. The bushes grow more sparse to the south.
117272: The dense shrubbery and overgrown thornbushes fill the air with their heavy and earthy scent. To the south and west, the mass of flora is impassable for even the smallest of hobbits. Flowers can be seen poking through to the north and east, where the bushes are more sparsely-distributed.
117273: This meadow is filled with large snarled bushes, growing densely all tangled together. The ground is barely visible beneath all the vegetation and where it is, it is instead covered by gnarled roots. Towards the south the bushes thin out and are instead replaced by flowering rose bushes.
117274: Several large stands of hazel dot a landscape otherwise covered by thriving bushes. Large and small bushes spread out wide branches in all directions, hiding the ground completely. Anything might be hidden from view beneath the dense greenery, and the occasional rustling suggests that there's plenty of animal life.
117275: A black wolf pads restlessly, looking for its next prey.

Great snarls of roots cover the ground, twice or thrice as thick as the stems of the bushes they originate from, whose snagging, bristly thorns further inhibit travel. There is a constant carpet of background sound: chirping, hissing, and rustling that suggests a rich fauna.
117276: The corpse of a huge, black wolf is lying here.

A great many bushes and shrubs grow on these fields, often so close that they form veritable walls of vegetation. The ground is hidden beneath a treacherous layer of leaves, thick, snaking roots, and dead branches. Several stands of hazel rise above the lower bushes.
117278:
A large beautiful rose bush is blooming here.
Deep inside the bush, there is a red rose with leaves and thorny stem.
A small, dense tangle of roots covers the ground.

Sprawling wild rose bushes dominate the scenery here, growing so fiercly that nary a route is available in-between them. Long, nasty-looking thorns protect the pink and red flowers, and the air is full of insects. Towards the north the rose bushes thin out, only to be replaced by other species of sprawling bushes.
117279: Between the few bushes that grow here, the ground is covered by grasses, forbs, and dead leaves. The land descends here from the gnarly bush-tangled wilderness in the north and cradles a small south-flowing stream into a wide valley between the steep, boulder-strewn hills in the east and west. An occasional tree graces the mostly-open landscape.
117280:
A small boar with big yellow tusks looks eager to fight.
A green frog is here, hopping around.
A small boar with big yellow tusks looks eager to fight.

Rushes grow here near the creek that splashes over stones and flows swiftly down the hill from north to south. The ground rises again to the east across the creek, where large, jagged boulders pierce the smooth grassy slope and intrude into the sky. Songbirds occasionally fill the air with their music.
117281:
A green frog is here, hopping around.
A green frog is here, hopping around.

Large, jagged boulders tear through the ground and mark the end of a gnarly bush-tangled wilderness that dominates the north. The land slowly descends to the west into a gentle hillside while the boulders continue their march southward. Visibility is limited by the bushes that grow among the boulders.
117282: A field lark stands here, focused on finding food.

The creek flows swiftly among a cluster of very large rocks that sit at the bottom of a boulder-covered hillside, itself dotted with bushes and long-bladed grasses. Immediately surrounding the creek are rushes and reeds that limit visibility. Only the tops of a few trees can be seen to the south.
117283:
The corpse of a large pike is lying here.
A crystal-clear lake is here at the base of the valley.
A crayfish is lying here, incapacitated.
A green frog is here, hopping around.

A swift creek drains into a fertile lake surrounded by rushes and reeds at the lowest point of this valley. Grasses and wildflowers grow further up the slightly inclined banks of the lake where the valley continues to the south. The northern horizon is dotted with boulders as the land rises. Travelling to the north means following the meandering creek across the path it has cut.
117284: Tall grasses and short woody-stemmed plants inhabit the spaces between the large boulders that mar the steep hillsides sweeping upward, away from this gentle valley. Birds and small animals can be observed among the brush and in hollows under the rocks. The valley continues to the north and south.
117285: A black wolf pads restlessly, looking for its next prey.

The land is flat and open here, a wide expanse of tall, leaf-adorned stalks and stems of growing things. A few trees grow here and there, and an occasional thicket sometimes interrupts the grassy meadow. This wild place is the perfect habitat for animals, birds, and insects.
117286: The remains of a stone building can be seen here where the narrow track bends before entering some hills. Only a few walls left standing and whatever purpose of the building that once had has now been forgotten. The surrounding lands are covered in heath with the occasional island of bushes growing where they can.
117287: A field lark stands here, focused on finding food.

The open hillside here is populated primarily by countless clumps of grass interrupted by a few isolated trees. To the south and west the upward slope becomes too steep for travel, guiding the creek to flow eastward toward a cluster of large rocks barely visible in the distance. Rushes and reeds share the soft banks of the creek with many smooth, flat stones.
117288: The narrow dirt track underfoot is rough and stony as the ground begins to climb toward a tall bush-crowned hill far to the north. To the east, between boulder-encrusted hillsides is the entrance to lush, grass-carpeted valley. Grassy meadows broken by clusters of bushes and trees decorate the soft, rolling terrain in the south and west.
117289:
The corpse of a wild bull is lying here.
A small pile of animal dung is here, attracting insects.

Dense thickets at the edge of a steep slope guide the stony track to the west and south. The sky is open above, and small weeds have found purchase between the rocks underfoot, suggesting that this path is seldom travelled. Evidence of wildlife is observable among the flora beside the trail, which occasionally rustles as something unseen moves through it.
117290: The faint path is overgrown with clumps of grass and forbs here, where it winds around and between many large rocks. Fallen leaves from a few small rowan trees growing among a cluster of boulders lie scattered about in various stages of decay. To the west and south, the relatively flat, bouldered meadow near the trail is swallowed by an impenetrable wild rose briar that covers the steep hillside beyond.
117291: A vague path leads through the boulder-strewn wilderness. In some places it is very hard to discern, since the dense underbrush seems to cover parts of it. Quite a few old willow trees surround this narrow track, leaning in over it with their crooked branches. The rocky ground drops abruptly east of the trail and tumbles down to a green valley in the distance. The way to the west is blocked by an impenetrable wild rose briar.
117292:
A scrawny, injured willow tree grows here between the rocks.
A brown fox is here, looking for some rabbits to chew up.

The path continues north and south from here as it wraps around the side of a hill that slopes down from the northeast to the southwest. Tall deciduous trees grow among the boulders, and the trail is difficult to discern under old dead leaves. An old, scrawny willow stands at a bend in the hillside, and the trail splits in two and flows around it.
117293: A wild bull seems ready to charge you.

A narrow pathway consisting of packed earth and occasional stone markers meanders through fields of grass and hay. To the north there is an inhospitable mass of thornbushes and other shrubbery, creeping ever so slowly towards the man-made path.
117294: The corpse of a wild bull is lying here.

Fields of grasses and forbs surround this narrow track as it meanders through the wild and uninhabited countryside. The hard path of trampled earth is beaten and too narrow for wagons. A few trees can be seen sprouting along the trail as it winds and bends.
117295: A tall willow tree with gnarled branches stands here.

This narrow, stony trail cuts through the wild waves of grasses and short woody-stemmed flowering plants that grow here. Clumps of grass encroach on the hard-packed dirt and small half-buried rocks underfoot. The trail bends north and east around the trunk of an ancient willow tree with wide branches.
117296: Surrounded on all sides by fields of long grass and weeds, a wide, rarely travelled path meanders through the countryside. The ground on the path appears to have had some use in the past, but the long grass is slowly starting to grow through the hard-packed dirt. A handful of trees can be seen in the distance, but they appear to be stunted and very old.
117297: A track here flows across the fields, bending and twisting to avoid any obstacle and terrain that is less ideal for walking or riding. The land is wild and uninhabited, except for some crop fields and farmsteads in the distance to the south-west. Long grasses grow along the sides of the track.
117298:
A small cluster of clover grows here.
Some blackberries grow on a bush nearby.

There is a small hollow here, in which grows an array of wildflowers that almost seem to have been placed there on purpose, long ago. The remains of a campfire can be found in the midst of a sea of colours, perhaps proof of the calming nature of the hollow. The chirps of birds fill the area with an orchestra of competing sounds.
117299: This trail runs across a field wedged between dense brush to the north and a building to the south-west. The trail is little more than a partly overgrown path, not wide enough for wagons. Some dung along the side of the trail may indicate that the path is at least sometimes used by riders.
117300:
A large shrub grows here, its branches loosely spreading.
On the shrub, there are three piles of cherries.

Bushes are making travelling here somewhat tiresome. Toward the north the plains get bushy and thorny while toward the south grassy plains and a narrow track can be seen. Small animals run around in the dense underbrush and birds can be heard chirping.
117301: A fierce boar is here, making grunting noises.

Here, east of the Road to Fornost, bushy and thorny plains stretch out towards the eastern horizon. The soil is dark and nutritious, making the brush dense and full of life. Many tracks can easily be found on the ground, running beneath the carpet of vegetation.
117302:
A black wolf pads restlessly, looking for its next prey.
A fierce boar is here, making grunting noises.

Green and dense bushes are making travelling here somewhat tiresome. Sometimes the noise of small animals can be heard from within the shrubs. These plains continue in all directions except toward the north where dense underwood makes further travel impossible.
117303: A black wolf pads restlessly, looking for its next prey.

These plains covered by sombre brushwood continue in all directions except toward the south where dense bushes make further travel impossible. The soil is dark, making the brush dense and full of life. There are many tracks of animals on the ground.
117304:
The corpse of a brown snake is lying here.
The corpse of a brown snake is lying here.
A hollow tree is growing upright here.
A brown snake watches you.

Burnt down trees are the only remainder of the forest that once covered these lands. The soil is still black from the ash created by the fire that burned the forest to the ground. Vegetation and wildlife have not found their way back to this land.
117305:
A brown toad is here, hunting flies.
A brown toad is here, hunting flies.
A fierce boar is here, making grunting noises.
A boar cub is playing here, and exploring the wide world.

Once cleared by fire to prepare it for farming, this piece of land seems to have been left uncultivated, and is far from suitable for farming in its current state. Charred, decaying tree stumps still spot the ground amid clusters of thick vegetation. A few young trees have survived here, harbingers of the forest bordering this burned land to the south and east.
117306:
A fierce boar is here, making grunting noises.
A boar cub is playing here, and exploring the wide world.
A boar cub is playing here, and exploring the wide world.
A boar cub is playing here, and exploring the wide world.

A smattering of young trees with straight, narrow trunks grow here, where natural succession is reclaiming the burned land for the forest. To the south and east the trees are larger and grow more densely, with broad trunks and gnarly branches. Past fires have painted black bands around the trunks of the few remaining older trees.
117307: The grass on this wide meadow grows above knee-height in some places, and shows signs of grazing in others. Clusters of brush and inedible plants suggest that this field is not currently being maintained as a pasture, but may once have been part of the farmland to the south. Trees and dense vegetation grow across the meadow to the north and east.
117308:
A shaggy-haired cow looks around curiously whilst grazing.
A fierce boar is here, making grunting noises.

Here the grass is low and trampled, and the numerous animal tracks suggest that it is regularly grazed. An old, weathered barn stands to the east, with fresh manure piled up against the side facing this field. The land looks less well-tended to the north and east. The field to the south appears to be used for growing crops.
117309: Yellow flowers, with grey-green foliage, grow in clusters here.

Food crops grow here in long, slightly-raised rows of healthy-looking soil. This field is surrounded by more like it that have been planted with different crops. Tall wooden fences and well-used dirt paths separate each plot from its neighbours. At the northeast edge of the cropland stands an old, weathered barn, beyond which the cultivated farm is overtaken by brush. More buildings can be seen beyond the fields to the south.
117310:
There are two piles of wheat cereals here.
A large thorny branched shrub is growing here.

Kept neatly apart from the potato field to the north, this grain field is dedicated to the cultivation of wheat. The delicate plants have been sown in a meticulous order, as if the farmer were planting a garden. The proud wheat plants grow tall, suggesting that most travellers choose a different route and the occasional visitors are mostly careful not to tramp about.
117311: The land has been heavily grazed, and patches of dry earth can be seen between clumps of low, brown crabgrass and spots of clover. Dust rises with the occasional gust of wind and hovers low to the ground. In the distance to the east, a small house and paddock appear low on the horizon.
117312:
A large ram guards his flock of sheep.
A woolly sheep is grazing here.
A woolly sheep is grazing here.

The forage in this area gives the land a two-toned hue; nearer to the ground, the stalks of the wheatgrass appear darkly green, while the chevron-patterned spikelets at the head of the stalk have a light, golden tinge. Evidence of cattle, sheep, and other grazing ungulates can be seen among the tall grass.
117313: A circular stone well has been built here.

The farmer who planted this field of grain has kept it completely without diversity. This plot is completely dedicated to the cultivation of rye. Line after line, all as straight as arrows, the rye grows with barely a weed to be seen within its depths.
117314: A thin bear is here, hunting for food.

As if the farmer's patience or energy ran out keeping the fields to the south and west in their splendid shape, this one must have been left to itself for years. What may once have been fields of crop is now nothing but weeds and wild grass. A path to the barn to the north is now completely overgrown.
117315: In Front of a Decrepit Barn

This once may have been a yard or at least an open field. It has long since been reclaimed by nature, and brush covers most of it. A decrepit old barn to the west looks equally abandoned and untended. The brush grows denser and taller towards the north, and beyond it a canopy forms an even taller wall of vegetation. The space in front of this barn may once have been cleared, but it has long since been reclaimed by nature, and is overgrown with brush.
117316: Mature hardwoods grow here where their fallen leaves form the soft forest floor. There are trees of all sizes. Large fallen trunks lean askew here and there, some sharing the ground with a few bushes and vines. The view through the forest is mostly clear, and sometimes wildlife can be observed.
117317: Here the forest floor is a jumble of rotted wood and decaying leaves. Vast interwoven roots emerge from the earth like sculptures of wood and mud. The scent of flowers mingles with the rank, humid soil and the rotting vegetation. A heavy silence holds the the forest in its grasp, interupted only occasionally by a bird's chirping or some forest animal causing the undergrowth to rustle.
117318: Thinning Edge of a Dense Forest
A fierce boar is here, making grunting noises.

This seems to be the northern edge of the forest, as it thins considerably along the northern fringes. The ground is covered with needles and fallen leaves and the occasional dry, decaying branch. The forest floor show signs aplenty of wildlife, especially evident are signs of wild boar that have grubbed around looking for roots and such.
117319:
