A decaying shelf bows and creaks with age.
On the shelf, there are a pick and a pitchfork.
A tiny spider is here, eating a tiny bug.

A thick layer of dust coats most of the surfaces inside this old barn, where cobwebs adorn the spaces between heavy wooden beams and rusted farm tools. Along one wall are animal stalls with gates allowing egress into an attached outdoor pen. A workbench stands in a corner against the western wall, opposite the large door. The building seems sturdy enough to provide relief from the weather outside, but seems not to have been well-maintained for some time.
117320:
A stove stands against one wall here.
An old woman is here, stirring a large round pot.

Three chairs stand around a small, scrubbed table that sits in the middle of this small kitchen. An open cupboard is overflowing with cups, pots, and pans. A caped greatcoat and several long scarves hang on the back of the door on the northern wall. Small rugs lie like stepping stones on the scoured tiles. The air reeks of beeswax, kitchen soap, and freshly ironed sheets.
117321: This dining room is sparsely decorated with just a few simple tapestries hanging on the otherwise bare walls. A crudely crafted but functional table stands in the middle of the room, surrounded by a handful of equally basic but functional chairs. Small alcoves along the north wall seem to serve as places to bed down for the night.
117322:
A long water trough made of wood stands here.
A sturdy pack horse is standing here.
A domesticated pony, beast of burden to many, stands here.
A domesticated pony, beast of burden to many, stands here.
A beautiful and docile horse is standing here.

This paddock is enclosed by a shoulder-high wooden corral, its only exits a gate to the west, and a wooden door to the north. The full and rich grass here is trampled deeply in many places, suggesting it normally hosts a number of hoofed animals. Large clumps of animal dung provide a rich feeding ground for beetles and insects.
117323:
An apple tree with bright green leaves grows here.
On the tree's branches are two apples.

Tall weeds lie far to the south, and a fenced paddock to the east might house farm animals. This meadow is very lush, and the grass is thick and rich. A large rope swing hangs from the thickest branch of an old apple tree; yet it appears to be unusable since one of its ropes is torn.
117325:
A shaggy-haired cow looks around curiously whilst grazing.
A shaggy-haired cow looks around curiously whilst grazing.

This pasture has clearly been grazed by cattle and the sounds of soft lowing can be heard from quite a distance on this flat landscape. A shallow gully separates this pasture from a trail to the south. A thicker meadow appears a short distance to the east where the tiny forms of other livestock can be glimpsed, just barely.
117326: The grasses are lush and vibrant in this area. Bright green, tall fescue and sturdy sorghum grow in abundance, providing plenty of forage for the livestock that graze this land. A few willows dip their branches over the edge of the gully to the south. The low trill of crickets vibrates through the air, punctuated occasionally by the piercing chirp of a nearby chipmunk.
117327:
Some cereals that look like wheat are lying here.
A field lark stands here, focused on finding food.

Strips of shorn wheat sporadically dimple the field, and the breeze bears the scent of freshly cut grass. A close look at these lately shorn areas reveals small burrows and every so often, a tiny vole pokes its furry, blunt nose out, whiskers atwitch. A calm quietness pervades the field as the grasses rustle in the wind and the infrequent sound of sheep bleating echoes in the far distance.
117328: A field lark stands here, focused on finding food.

Bright green and golden grasses grow in large patches interspersed between the occasional strip of bare dirt. Scorpion grasses add a splash of pale blue to the ground cover. Overhead, the occasional flock of sparrows take wing, contrasting darkly against the wide sky. To the south, a gully forms an abrupt dip in the level ground.
117329:
A bale of hay is lying here.
A field lark stands here, focused on finding food.

Upturned soil extends to the north in long, uniform rows, and the bare earth in this area becomes charred ground to the south. Rounded bales of hay mark the western edge of this fallow field, and to the east, spots of colour, greens and yellows, relieve the eye of this drab, monotonous scenery.
117330: The field is brindled: lumpy streaks of charcoal spread across the brittle, flax-coloured grasses. In addition to the charred landscape, the ashy aroma lingering in the air is a clear sign that this field was recently burned. A mill looms in the eastern distance, standing in relief against an otherwise flat horizon.
117331:
A newborn spider is here, hungrily crawling about.
A newborn spider is here, hungrily crawling about.
A black spider crawls here, a shiny red spot visible on its belly.
A newborn spider is here, hungrily crawling about.

A seemingly disorganized mesh of white forms the home of spider here. White, fuzzy balls, the wrapped and preserved food for the arachnid, are woven into the fabric of the web. Newly-caught insects struggle against the sticky constraints, their future doom unknown to them.
117332: Dry, yellow grasses stretch toward the east before rising into a dense, tall tangle of prairie. The relatively flat ground rises quickly to the west. The western hillside is rock-strewn, but in between the boulders and bushes are wide swaths of grassland producing pathways more navigable than the unsteady ground farther south.
117333: The meadow is thick here, and the flowers and grasses stretch toward the sky reaching surprising heights. In some places, the goldenrods and switchgrasses stand taller than the farmers and occasional traveller who move through these parts. The dense foliage keeps the soil cool and damp, and the smell of wet earth lingers in the air.
117334:
A bee flies around here, collecting nectar from the flowers.
A field vole has frozen to the spot, sensitive to your presence.
A fierce boar is here, making grunting noises.

South of the trail, the grasses rise quickly. Bright green-yellow clumps of low grass give way to taller, lacy brown stalks and thorny thistles. Black and red burnets and fat, fuzzy bumblebees dart among the flowers. Farther south and west, the meadow thickens and grows even higher.
117335: The rocky path extends east and west, dotted with clusters of blue-green grass and rough stones, some large enough to trip an unobservant traveller. Near the northern edge of the trail, a rough-edged gully gashes the landscape, and the ground abruptly sinks more than a few feet below the level of the path. The depression continues many paces to the north before rising sharply again. On the opposite side, a vivid green pasture stretches toward the horizon.
117336: A mass of dark green leaves clings to a wall.

A tall mill looms nearby and beyond, farther to the west, the fields begin to rise and become low, lightly-forested hillsides. An overgrown trail stretches toward the east, paralleled by a gully on the north and a thick, lumpish hedge to the south. The mill is in a near-dilapidated state: dry rot has begun to eat into the lattice frame of the sails, a few dozen shingles are missing from the roof, and ivy smothers the upper windows.
117337: The trail takes a wide bend to the west, crossing in front of the tree line and bordered on the north by an increasingly shallow gully. The low grasses that line the southern edge of the trail gradually rise into a tall meadow to the southwest, and low hills roll along the otherwise smooth, western horizon.
117338: The trail branches off to the east, running behind a small house before merging into the well-worn Fornost road. A few oak trees bordering the western edge of the road extend their branches overhead, but taper off farther north. Puffs of sheep fescue freckle the trail ahead, and the tallest blades sway softly in the breeze.
117339: Someone, most likely a nearby farmer, while having once completed the strenuous job of laying a path with uncountable stone slabs, has now let weeds grow between them and some slabs are barely visible beneath the dirt. The path trails closely to the fence on the northern side, while splitting into a fork further to the west. Far to the east, the path leads joins the Road to Fornost.
117340: A path runs through a wide open field of swaying grass. The path seems to see regular use, as it's mostly free of rocks and weeds. It is laid with many small slabs of stone, which no doubt help with keeping it in good repair, and keeps weeds at bay. The path leads to a field of brush to the north, and to a larger road to the east. It also continues into the distance to the west.
117341: Having been allowed to grow wild and unchecked, the tangled bushes on these fields grow right up to a wooden fence to the west. Where the bushes don't dominate, knee-high grass flourishes, and not a path or trail crosses these wide fields.
117342: Brushy Field off the Road to Fornost
A black crow flies low to the ground here, looking for carrion to eat.

The ground here is uneven and several rocky outcrops explain why the Road to Fornost takes a detour north and east around this area. Allowed to grow wild, these fields are covered with dense brush and in parts they are almost impassable. To the west, the fields are bordered by a small farmhouse, and a solidly constructed wooden fence blocks the way there.
117343:
A mass of wriggling vines drops on you from the trees.
A mass of wriggling vines drops on you from the trees.

Tall, wooden fence posts frame this brush to the north, and south, and such is the suffocating nature of the vines, that no tall plants rise above the withering mass. No trail can be discerned under the black thorns below, and the vines wriggle and snap as if searching for victims.
117344: A tall pine tree grows here.

The thorny brush is quite light here, with ample sunlight reaching the ground during most of the year. Several tall trees have grown through the low canopy, and their branches provide a resting spot for migratory birds, squirrels, and snakes. Far to the north, a wooden fence pokes its beams above the brush.
117345:
A large sack is on the ground.
A hooded brass lantern has been left here.

The air inside is heavy, the smell of rotten wood having seeped into the stone walls and the damp earth. A thick wooden post extends from the centre of the room upward, and small heaps of grain sacks line the western wall. Four lanterns hang from hooks in the stone, left there by the inhabitants of this tower. Toward the back end of the mill, a surprisingly sturdy wooden staircase ascends to the second level, disappearing into the wooden ceiling.
117346:
Some cereals that look like wheat are lying here.
A large bat is here, hanging in the darkness.
A huge bat is here, emitting piercing squeaks.

The wooden post from the lower level extends upward into a hole in the ceiling, straddled on both sides by two giant millstones. Specks of ground wheat are scattered lightly around the millstones, but otherwise the floor is free of debris. Dim light peeks through slight gaps in the ivy that covers the windows on the outside.
117347: A faded and stained black shirt lies here.

Dark stains of an unknown substance speckle the myriad of junk in this cramped, moist cellar. Old, ratty clothes are mixed with an assortment of spider webs and mouse droppings. The dirt ground underneath the thick layer of debris is slick, and has helped cake the detritus with a thick layer of red and brown.
117348: A goat is here, grazing in the hills.

The ground is rough and uneven. In many places, it is difficult to find secure footing and each step sends smaller stones rolling down the hillside. Despite the rugged landscape, stunning wildflowers bloom between the jagged rocks, freckling the otherwise brown and grey landscape with a palette of yellow, orange, and purple colour.
117349:
A fierce boar is here, making grunting noises.
A goat is here, grazing in the hills.

Despite their unremarkable height, these hills are harsh. Abrupt and surprisingly steep scarps are carved into their sides, and the rocky ground makes slipping an almost inevitable event. The air is dry and dusty; not much grows here except the occasional large sagebrush, adding a welcome seagreen tint to the mostly chalky surroundings.
117350:
A stunted tree struggles to grow on the steep slope.
A goat is here, grazing in the hills.

Ascending this hill takes a lot of effort as it slopes steeply and continuously from its base to its summit. From the peak, a big mill can be seen clearly in the far eastern distance, and it is possible to watch the sails spin in response to the breath of the wind.
117351: A large brown snake with black patches is coiled here.

The hills lay low and fall away smoothly into the surrounding fields. At the foot of the easternmost hill, a line of hay bales mark the edge of the farming lands that extend east to the old, overgrown trail. Stubby grasses cover the ground and a few, short cypresses appear as little more than greenish lumps in the distance.
117352: Standing atop this tall hill offers an unobstructed panorama of the surrounding agricultural lands. Southeast of here lies an orchard and a small farm and beyond that, an old dirt road. To the northeast, the tall sails of a mill can barely be distinguished from the lush pasture stretching behind it. Directly north, the hills dip lower and become more rugged, specked with large rocks and thick, thorny bushes.
117353:
The ruined remains of a wooden house lie here.
A goat is here, grazing in the hills.
A lonely goatherd stands here, watching his herd of goats.

Standing atop this low hill, it is possible to see the tree line along the road far to the east. The hill dips gradually to the west and another, taller hill rises beyond the hollow. To the north and east is a perilous slope, pocked with large boulders and the serrated branches of low, thorny shrubs.
117354: A tall stag is here, grazing peacefully.

Rough and clawing greenery gives way to jutting bedrock as these hills rise to rocky cliffs. Only a few gnarly weeds manage to thrive between the cracks in the rocks on a ridge that drops sharp and rocky. The ground at the bottom of the cliffs is full of yellow rocks strewn between shrubs. As the land extends, it becomes lush and green.
117355: These hills are green mounds of turf, poked through with large boulders. Under many crevices grow crooked juniper trees, clawing at anything that comes near. The ground is firm, and the thick grass grows well. The vantage from this high land gives an outstanding view of the verdant fields south and west.
117356: The field slopes gently upward to the east, cresting into a tall hill in the far distance. Elsewhere, the landscape is grassy, still, and flat. Here and there, a bush or a boulder appears as a dark lump on the otherwise featureless countryside.
117357:
A vernal pool is here, partially hidden among the rushes.
A long-stemmed plant that branches into many bright yellow flowers grows here.
Clusters of slender stems and tall leaves thrive in the mud and shallows.

This broad grassland sinks down, low and almost boggy. Stalwart bulrushes and yellow-flowered brooklime abound among the lush figwort clumps, giving the ground a thick green covering. The air is thick with moisture, and swarms of small gnats fly about as the plants are disturbed. The land is so low that on the east and south sides, small dirt cliffs rise to the surrounding land, brown and crumbling. Tiny puddles are formed in the dirt, providing a drinking source for insects and small animals.
117358: The corpse of a black raven is lying here.

Thick grass is divided by a series of lines of corn cockle on this rolling plain. Curving from east to south, the loose, long, plants billow their purple flowers from ditches in a lazy wave. The grass is kept mostly low, but some patches have managed to evade cutting, growing tall and thick.
117359: A feral billy goat stands here, angrily chewing on some thistle.

This field lay broken as if hammered from above by a giant. The ground is carpeted with sedge and sweet briar on the angles, firm but crooked, giving a tilt to all travel. Some large rocks begin to appear on the southern edge, and to the east the land becomes soggy. To the west the land rises slightly, blocking the view of the top.
117360: A circle of stones is obscured behind tall, majestic trees.

On this vast grassy field is a circle of majestic trees fencing in a round plateau. The ground is flourishing with bunches of sedge, and as it reaches a gentle drop off to the east and south, it becomes thin and rocky allowing a grand view of wild lands, rocky and bushy.
117361: A shelf of hard soil and loose shrubbery juts out from a prominent plateau to the north. The land angles in a grand vista, giving an easy eyeshot east and south where the earth descends to greener fields. The air is filled with an earthy smell as the wind blows the soil down a low rise to the north.
117362: This field sinks deep below the level of the surrounding fields, giving it little sunlight throughout the day. The soil is hard, and exposes the underlying bedrock in many places. Some downy birch trees grow across the land, gnarly and drooping, sharing the land with spindly cock's foot grass.
117363:
An old, grey, many-trunked hornbeam tree stands here, huge and gnarly.
An abandoned hunter's platform rests high up in an old hornbeam tree.

This land appears to have been recently cleared and half ploughed, although no crop has been planted. The resulting fescue grows in straight rows, nature's quick reclamation of the land, as obvious as the creeping greenery that is thick and wild south and west.
117364: A small pile of barley has been left here.

A great field of barley is abandoned, it growing savagely against long and lanky corn cockle that attempts to choke it out. Crookedly splitting the field is a dried creek bed, its banks overhung with buckthorn, the shiny, black branches dropping their small, shrivelled berries at will.
117365: Some small rocks have been piled into a mound here.

Gravel fills a depression in this rocky expanse. Too steep to climb out to the north or west, the ground is full of grey and black sharp stones. Cockle and oxeye grow sparingly among the rocks, giving way to true grasses on the lower points of this field as the ground becomes loamy southeast.
117366: A coloured game bird is visible in the vegetation, watching you warily.

A light breeze wafts through this verdant meadow, blowing the short grasses with a gentle touch. A large moss covered boulder sits at a low spot and provides protection for a short leaved butcher's broom, stiff and fresh. The rest of the land pitches slowly to the boulder, making it the focal point. Elsewhere the meadow is well grazed, the grasses being short and trim.
117367: A black raven flies in the sky searching for flesh to prey upon.

Long, wavy strands of fescue flutter about this vigorous field. Grasses and bushes strangle each other for sunlight, and the mushy gault sucks the plants down. A sparse set of tall oak trees grows thick here, providing a resting spot for small animals.
117368: Strips of straggly, flat grass weave and wind their way through scattered rocks and large, overgrown hunks of earth. The southern part of this field is so filled with the haphazard rocks that there is no clear path through them. The smell of earth is abundant, and the cold stones dampen any sound.
117369: Fog grass and sedge billow at any slight wind on this flourishing upland. The vista gives a grand view of the fields west and south. To the north the land drops off sharply, exposing a sunken field. East, green bushes grow wild and large, hindering any but the smallest of animals from travelling there.
117370: Cocksfoot and foxtail grasses stretch over this shabby field, waving slowly in the breeze. Signs of grazing are evident from the bent and eaten herbage, tufts of fleece, and ordure. To the north, the land rises into an upland. To the east, large, wild thickets impede travel.
117371:
A short evergreen plant, with slightly bluish needles, grows here.
On the plant, there are a cluster of hard, round, black berries.

Green and silver grass bends to the wind on this vast, flat plain. The earth is rich with the smell of life, verdant, and green, and springs up underfoot. The grass itself is wide leaved, and furry, and the heads of spikey flowers droop under their own weight.
117372:
A lonely goatherd stands here, watching his herd of goats.
A goat is here, grazing in the hills.
A young goat playfully charges and hops away.

The land here has been forgotten for a very long time, and wild flora has taken over every square inch. Most of the plants are brambles, sticking small thorns in every direction; so thick that the only way to exit from this vexing land is to the east.
117373: A fallow deer is grazing peacefully here.

Scattered wild privet grows thick on the eastern and southern edges of this wild field. The dull green, lance-shaped leaves and small, white, cloyingly sweet flowers contrast with the clover and thistle that spread through the rest of this land.
117374:
Prickly, white-stemmed plants, with blue flower heads grow in abundance.
A fallow deer is grazing peacefully here.
A grey wolf is here, snarling aggressively.

This rough land is thick with prickly thistle and dandelion, grabbing on to any passing thing. To the west and east, dark green bushes grow shiny and tall, hemming the land in on both sides. To the southeast, large bushes fight with shorter, dull green privet for command of the domain. A sharp, sweet smell riddles the air, luring lazy honeybees to purple and yellow flowers.
117375: Some small rocks have been piled into a mound here.

Below an imposing escarpment, a pitched morass of rocks and shrubbery bound southward, transitioning to lush grasses. The escarpment is dark yellow and stained with watery, rust-coloured rivulets. To the west, the land becomes thick with tall, dark green, shiny bushes, and is impassable.
117376: A brown bear is sleeping here.

North, an overhanging ridge stands dramatically over this rocky land, dark yellow and wrinkled. The base is thick with fallen rock, gradually spreading out and intermingling with small scrub pines and shiny, dark green bushes. Further out, the land becomes flat and is overtaken by hardy grasses.
117377: Dense swards of fine-leaved grasses fight with erect, yellow-flowered ragwort on this field that starts on rocky slopes in the north. Continuing south, the land becomes rich and butcher's broom becomes prevalent: the stringent, leafy bushes reaching waist-high.
117378: This field pitches down east from a rocky hill. The land is covered by short turf on the west, and gradually becomes more lush, growing thick grass, large shrubs and scrub trees. The finality of the plant life crawls up to a stout fence, enveloping the white boards in dark green.
117379: The surrounding field consists of low hills that level off in the east and rise sharply toward the west. The western slope is uninviting. Giant, jagged boulders and thorny bushes cover the hillside, and the ground is littered with smaller, loose rocks that call into doubt the possibility for stable footing.
117380: The grasses are lower here, and wildflowers large and small grow in abundance. Bright corncockle, pastel cornflower and cranesbill, and sunny daffodils paint the landscape in vibrant colour and contrast pleasingly with the green and umber grasses.
117381:
A clear spring babbles as cool water trickles out of the grassy earth.
An orchid of light violet petals blossoms nearby.

Here and there a lone oak rises from the tall grasses, and playful meadowlarks chirp as they glide between the branches. On especially sunny days, a subtle smell of mint and hay lingers on the breeze among the sun-warmed stalks. The meadow stretches farther west and to the south, a dense cluster of trees mark the edge of an orchard.
117382:
A large, venomous-looking green snake is coiled up here.
A large, venomous-looking green snake is coiled up here.

Wide, shallow depressions are carved into the dirt floor of this small cave, their paths meandering from the opening into the dark recesses of the interior. Tree roots form living stalagtites, their tendrils grasping for dirt in the open air of the cave.
117383: The southern dirt road narrows here into a faint and rocky trail and continues north. A sparse tree line borders the western edge of the trail, beyond which a tall meadow stretches into the hilly distance. Unkempt, low bushes encroach from either side of this fading footpath.
117384: Sweet vernal-grass cover this honeyed land. A branch of the old farm track runs north and south through, untended and overgrown. To the east thickets of elder fight with strangling clematis. To the west, a sturdy fence holds back the wild from a well tended field.
117385:
A purple beet is growing here.
A carrot is growing here.

Two dirt tracks cross here. Well worn ruts and short, tough grass give evidence of the constant usage they see. The land around is planted with small fields of onions, garlic, carrots, and beets, all hemmed with short, thorny lattice. To the west, a large farm house stands, steadily guarding the land.
117386: In this sparse, rocky field brome and melic grow shaggily, giving a good glimpse of the soil. A dirt track runs through the land, north and south, the cart ruts shallow on small rocks and gravel. To the east, dark elder thickets grow with abandon, eventually becoming impassable. In the west, a white-painted fence holds back the brush, guarding rows of tended oats.
117387: Cart tracks wind their way through this great meadow of fescue, hard thicket, pimpernel, and honeysuckle. The flowers give the land a deep orange over top of the green of the sedge. On the track, hardy grasses grow short and tough, not letting the wagon wheels crush their life. In the west, a white-painted fence guards rows of tended crops. The track continues north and south.
117388: A wide, grassy field grows thick, thorny creeping bent and soft sweetbriar. Smooth, grey barked whitebeam trees dot the eastern side of the field, which is split in two by an old dirt track. The track's deep ruts left from heavy wagon wheels have crushed the cobble stones that once paved this track into rocks and gravel.
117389: Fork in an Old Dirt Track
A tree-snake lies wrapped around one of the tree branches.

Elder, sweetbriar, and harebell form a rough, blue-black sedge in this field. The land is forked by two tracks of heavy wagon wheels carving through the topsoil, exposing chunks of flattened stones beneath. To the east, the land is home to patches of small whitebeam trees, compact and domed.
117390: Old Dirt Track near a House

Cart tracks wind their way through this dirt track as it passes by the ruin of a stately stone farmhouse that is nearly engulfed in choking thornbushes. An iron structure stands at what might have once been the gate, but has now crumbled into rust. Out from the ruins and the track, the land turns from thick brambles to a large field full of long-stemmed cow parsley and bunched ribwort.
117391: An old dirt track road runs from west to east here. The track surface is uneven in places, with humps and shallow depressions breaking up the otherwise flat passage. Some of the depressions are marred by groups of narrow channels cutting across the road, suggesting that water draining along an almost imperceptible slope has resulted in erosion. Here and there short clumps of grasses have begun to grow in the road itself, eking out a tenuous existence in the hard packed dirt. At the edges of the road similarly short grass quickly gives way to taller blades and clumps as the soil becomes looser in the surrounding fields, which continue to the north and south.
117392: This dirt track is not entirely flat: some areas are slightly raised, forming bumps and low mounds, and other spots are low, holding water when it rains. Here and there rocks stick up from the track, large smooth stones that are too large to easily dig out. Along the edges of the track are piles of rocks that were smaller and easier to remove, dug and tossed aside to create a more uniform surface upon which to travel. Some low-growing weeds have managed to establish in the hard packed dirt in the centre and edges of the track, growing slowly thanks to the poorly-aerated soil. Tall grasses quickly emerge off the track to the north and south, and continue as far as the eye can see, while to the east the dirt track joins a larger road paved with flat stones.
117393:
A white wolf is here, prowling for something to eat.
A white wolf is here, prowling for something to eat.

This area lacks mature trees or even tree stumps, suggesting that it was cleared at some point in the past. Tall grasses and very low heath and bramble bushes grow here instead, struggling to rise above shade cast by the surrounding grasses. Mixed in with the grasses are tall, dead stems from a previous year's annual weeds, some with seed pods still attached to the terminal ends. To the east a long, straight line of bushes rises above the surrounding fields. The bushes grow closely together, forming a dense hedgerow, but do not appear to have been cared for in some time: vines twine through them, shading and thinning out parts of the hedgerow, and young birch trees have begun to poke up through the top of the hedge, reaching for the sky.
117394:
A fierce boar is here, making grunting noises.
A fierce boar is here, making grunting noises.

This area looks like it was cleared at some point in the past, as it lacks any mature trees or even large stumps. Instead it is covered with thick, messy clumps of grasses, the green blades from this year's growth intermingled with drooping brown blades and upright brown flower heads from the growth of previous years. Within the grasses, hard to see but easy to feel, are many young trees, unbranched whips with only a year's growth or less. They stick up no higher than the surrounding grasses, rigid compared to their pliable neighbours, and in some places are numerous enough to form dense stands. To the east a long, straight row of bushes rises above the grassy fields, an overgrown hedgerow that suggests this area was once farmland with defined borders. Beyond the hedge to the east, a road can be made out in the distance.
117395: A grey wolf is here, snarling aggressively.

Tall, spreading grasses have taken over what appear to be old farm fields in this area. There are no trees or stumps visible in these fields, although at irregularly-spaced intervals tall messy shrubs rise from the grasses, forming dense clumps that are hard to move through but easy to move around. The ruins of a farmhouse lie in a clear patch, without the walls or roof left intact. It is little more than a foundation covered with the detritus left from its collapsed frame: rotted boards and stacked stones mixed with some unidentifiable metal debris. The landscape is already starting to reclaim the structure, which is slowly being covered by a sprawling, twining vine. To the west an unbroken line of tall shrubs grows densely enough to block travel.
117396: This area appears to have been cleared of trees at some point in the past, leaving no trace except the rare stump that has rotted into a shallow depression with a few forlorn pieces of wood sticking up on the periphery. A multitude of grass clumps have reclaimed the area, and short scrubby bushes have begun to appear in groups, forming an irregular mosaic across the fields. Some of the bushes are taller than others, and to the west a long line of the tallest form a tangled barrier that prevents movement. To the north a small dirt road can be seen.
117397:
A large, venomous-looking green snake is coiled up here.
A grey wolf is here, snarling aggressively.
A fierce boar is here, making grunting noises.

This area appears to have been cleared of trees at some point in the past, as there are no mature trees or stumps remaining. Tall grasses dominate this area, broken up by scrub bushes and spindly whips of young trees just starting to grow. In one area a broad, low depression in the field is visible. This sunken area has shorter, greener grasses than its surroundings, suggesting that water collects there when it rains and stays close under the surface for long periods after, waterlogging the soil and preventing more aggressive plant growth. To the west the scrub bushes grow taller and more dense, with vines climbing between and through them to weave an impassable barrier.
117398:
A huge, black wolf is here, ready to devour.
A fierce boar is here, making grunting noises.
A fierce boar is here, making grunting noises.

Dense stands of gorse bushes and brambles cover the ground here, creating an obstructive barrier to travel. The brambles are low growing, but thread through the bases of the taller gorse bushes to produce tall stands of brush that are uniformly dense from the ground up. Some clumps of grasses and tall weed stalks poke up through the bushes, both live stems and brown, hollow stems from past years' growth. An occasional small birch tree has managed to push up through some of these grassy, brushy patches, reaching just high enough to no longer be shaded by the plants around it. To the east the brush merges into taller shrubs that appear to be growing closely together in a straight line, suggesting that this area may once have been farmland fenced in by a natural hedgerow.
117399: A grey wolf is here, snarling aggressively.

This area appears to have been cleared in the past, as there are few trees here and none that are mature. Tall, clump-forming grasses are interspersed here with an almost continuous brushcover, large and small shrubs of various types and heights. These shrubs grow closely together, their branches intertwining and forming dense tangles that are difficult to move through. Here and there a narrow deer trail has been worn through the brush, making travel easier, although thorny, whip-like branches reach over the trails at regular intervals, clawing at anything moving past. To the east a road can be made out through the brush, although the tangled mess between here and there prevents passage in that direction.
117400: A white wolf is here, prowling for something to eat.

Dense brush and the occasional young tree dominate this area. Tall gorse bushes are mixed with brambles and lower growing heath, creating a tangled mix of varying heights. Multiple deer trails wind through the brush, the narrow paths marked by trampled weed stalks and the occasional clump of deer droppings. These trails criss-cross as they pass each other, avoiding the young trees and the densest clumps of bushes. To the east and west the brush becomes too tall and tangled to move through, and to the south a wide, paved road can be seen.
117401: Tall, thick grass blankets this area, forming a nearly uniform carpet with clumps of a coarser variety sticking up here and there. Closer to the ground, everything turns into a messy tangle of new blades mixed with old, dead stems and flowerheads. Wide stumps from mature trees dot this landscape; some are cut close to the ground, hidden by the grasses until stumbled upon, while others stick up just enough that the surrounding grasses fail to reach high enough to hide them from view. A narrow deer trail threads its way between these stumps, a ribbon of bare dirt that winds its way through the grassland until it is lost from view. To the south a narrow dirt road can be seen, and to the north and west the remnants of what appears to have been a hedgerow block travel.
117402: A large, venomous-looking green snake is coiled up here.

This field is covered with sparse grasses, growing mostly in clumps. Between the clump-forming grasses a thinner, lower-growing layer of spreading grass mixes with short woody shrubs, creating a mosaic of varying heights, colours, and textures. In clear spots there are old stumps left over from the woodlands that must have been cleared at some point in the past; these stumps are in varying stages of decay, some with only a hole rotted straight down through the top of the stump, and others that have little left besides a ring of crumbling wood rising from the edges of a small depression. To the east a large road can be seen in the distance, raised and paved with stones, while to the south a small dirt road cuts through the surrounding fields.
117403: The forest was partially cleared here sometime in the distant past. Old, mouldy stumps still dot the field, and it does not seem like it was used for farming. Tall trees grow amongst the stumps, and nature has started to reclaim its hold on the land here. A road runs parallel to the fields to the east, leading both north and south.
117404: You see two handfuls of clover on the ground.

These fields look like they were once used for farming. The remnants of shallow ditches can be seen crossing the fields in straight lines, and except for the grass growing tall and unchecked, the fields have not been reclaimed yet by trees or larger bushes. A path runs parallel to the field far to the north.
117406: A tall oak with wide branches is here.

All alone on an otherwise flat and even field of green grass stands an ancient, majestic oak tree. It spreads wide branches in a wide circle around a trunk covered with rough bark. The grass underneath the dense coverage is considerably sparser than on the rest of the fields. There are signs of grazing in some areas, and cowpats lie here and there attracting swarms of flies.
117407: The fields here border a large farm to the west. The farm is surrounded by a high and sturdy fence, meant to keep trespassers out, and its animals in. Occasionally cows' moos and the neighing of horses are heard. To the south and east the fields become wilder.
117408:
A large, loyal falcon is circling above.
A small rabbit glares angrily at you.

A field of low-lying grass covers the land here, with tufts of long grass scattered almost haphazardly throughout it. In the distance, a rooftop can be seen, rising above the horizon. The smell of smoke is faint, and occasionally wafts by, carried through by the wind.
117409: A brown bear is sleeping here.

This field has potential and was clearly intended to be used to grow crops. It is fenced in towards the east and south and paths connect it to cultivated fields to the west. Nothing seems to have been grown here in recent years and large bushes and weeds have begun to take over, making it ever harder to reclaim as a farmland.
117410: These open fields make up a rolling landscape, covered in healthy, green grass and punctuated by the occasional tree or bush. Wildflowers of all types and colours are scattered throughout the countryside, swaying in concert with the wind, and filling it with their various smells.
117411: The relatively flat ground begins to slope upward to the northeast, where an impenetrable rose briar has claimed the boulder-encrusted hillside. Toward the east and south, a wild meadow of tall grasses and wildflower plants is interrupted only by the occasional tree. Birds and insects can be observed in the undergrowth.
117412: An ibex is watching you from afar.

The wild meadow continues to the north and south. The tall grasses and forbs are interrupted by dense clusters of bushes to the west. In the east, the terrain becomes steep and rocky as it ascends a hill. An impenetrable rose-briar grows on most of the hillside and provides shelter to small animals.
117413: Within tall tufts of grass, a long, snaking depression in the land hints at a dried out brook. Its dusty ground hasn't seen much water for a long time, as its soil is cracked, and brittle. Tall ferns grow along its bank, and on the bottom of the former brook are pebbles of all sizes, half-decayed fishbones, and other detritous.
117414: A long depression in the land hints at a dried out brook. The brook's bed looks like it haven't seen water for a long time, as its dirt is cracked and chipped. Ferns and shrubs grow on what was once the brook's banks, and various weeds are busy reclaiming the bed itself. Perhaps a hundred years from now this will look like an overgrown ditch.
117415: These grassy fields look undisturbed and untamed, as if they have never felt the bite of a plough. Tall grasses bend with the wind, forming green waves that sweep across the plain. There is little to take note of here, although the high grass could hold any kind of surprise below it, be it a venomous snake, or a hidden pit.
117416: There are signs of a dried-out spring, and an equally dried out little lake next to it. A small brook seems to have flowed to the west, snaking across the plains. All that remains now is a grass-covered depression as the water probably found another outlet and was directed elsewhere.
117417: These fields are wild and untamed, with the grass growing waist-high on a grown man. The high grasses sway under the slightest breeze, sending green waves across the flat landscape. The field is bordered to the north by a sturdy-looking fence, beyond which crops are grown on more tamed land.
117418: Wagon tracks lead up to the entrance of a farm just to the east, and the trampled grass here indicates that it is in regular use. A long fence continues to north and south, and the sturdy wooden gate is the only visible entrance into the farm.
117419: A skinny young man stands here, a blade of grass in his mouth.

These fields are dedicated to the growing of corn. Several fields, each with a fence around it, consist of perfectly sown lines of corn, and nary a weed has been allowed to take root. Wagon tracks run between the fields and seem to lead towards the north.
117421: Prickly, white-stemmed plants, with blue flower heads grow in abundance.

A simple dirt farm track extends from the paved lane to the west towards a small farm visible in the distance to the east. Two ruts have been worn down the track, attesting to frequent passage of carts or wagons, but otherwise the track is level and smooth. Short clumps of grasses grow in the hard-packed median between the cart ruts, struggling in the poorly-aerated soil. An occasional half-buried stone also sticks up from the median, flat enough to have been left in place despite the traffic this road must see. At the edges of the road short grasses give way to taller clumps as the soil becomes looser.
117422: A young farm-hand is here hard at work.

A narrow dirt track leads eastwards towards a small farmhouse. It is straight but somewhat uneven, dipping slightly in places before rising again, and two well-worn cart tracks are cut into the surface. A split-rail fence runs along the track to the south, blocking movement into the fields beyond, and messy weeds and tall grasses grow along that edge of the track and under the fence. North off the track are rows of crops, orderly and well-tended, while to the west the track passes through a gap in the fence and leaves this farmstead.
117423:
A small, loyal beagle is here, eager to please.
A rooster is here, strutting about.

A narrow dirt farm track ends here in a wide circle before the farmhouse to the east. At the centre of the circle, a well sits surrounded by low-growing grasses and weeds that extend out to the edges of the track before the hard-packed dirt stops them short. The track itself is fairly smooth and level, with two shallow ruts left from carts or wagons. Many small rocks are half-buried in the dirt surface, and more have been pushed to the edges over time, leaving a thin gravel edge that marks the beginning of the adjacent fields. To the south is a split-rail fence, and to the north are well-tended crop fields leading towards a large barn.
117424:
A large, orange pumpkin is here.
A large potato is growing here.
A small pile of barley has been left here.
A carrot is growing here.

Long, straight rows of crops run from north to south in these fields. The crops are sown in raised ridges of rich, dark soil; between the rows are shallow furrows. There are weeds growing in these furrows, short but broad of leaf, and some growing at the bases of the crops as well. In places these weeds have been cut off at their bases and hoed under the soil, leaving only traces of stems and cut leaves behind. A barn is visible to the north, with a broad barn door, and to the east is a small farmhouse with a window.
117425:
A shaggy-haired bull stands here, calmly looking around.
A small black vicious rat squeaks at you for disturbing it.

This large wooden barn is constructed from boards nailed to a framework of sturdy square posts. These support posts run down the centre of the barn, from one side to the other, and rise all the way up to the middle of the peaked roof, with crossbeams supporting them at regular intervals. The interior of this barn is cluttered: hay takes up the west wall in a cascading pile, and junk takes up the northern half of the barn, the detritus left from the wear and tear imposed on the tools necessary to run a farm. Some usable tools hang from the lowest rafters here and there, some of them rusted but otherwise in good condition. The floor underfoot is dirt mixed with stray pieces of hay. To the east and south large barn doors lead out to the fields beyond.
117426:
A stocky mountain mule is here, waiting to serve.
A woolly sheep is grazing here.

These overgrown fields behind the barn are fenced in to the north and east, and blocked to the south by the north wall of the farmhouse. It looks like they were once used as pastureland, but now appear to be unused, abandoned, and overgrown. Tall clumps of grasses mix with small scrub bushes, thigh-high on a man, and an old hay bale in one corner of the field is decaying where it sits, spread out slightly and moulding at its centre. The weeds and stray bushes grow tallest along the fence line, the split-rail fence choked by twining vines and tangled branches that thread through its rails and wrap around its posts.
117427:
A round turnip is growing here.
There are two potatoes here.
A small pile of barley has been left here.

These crop fields are bordered to the west and north by a simple split-rail fence. Beneath the fence tall weeds and messy grasses grow, but a little farther inwards the rows of crops are neat, straight, and well-tended. Bare dirt is exposed between the crop rows, sunk below the slightly raised ridges upon which the crops were sown, and this bare dirt is rich and dark, albeit somewhat rocky. Some weeds stick up in these rows and also between the crops, although they are small: anything larger seems to have been hoed under, leaving only small traces of chopped stems and leaves. To the south a dirt road runs towards a farmhouse visible in the distance to the southeast.
117428:
The corpse of a brown snake is lying here.
An ash tree stands tall among the felled trees.
A quail stands motionless.
A grey wolf is here, snarling aggressively.
A large hawk-like bird is here overlooking its territory.

This area is lightly wooded, with many mature trees that are spaced far enough apart to allow plenty of light to filter through to the ground. This light has encouraged aggressive growth of the understory: clumps of grasses, wide-leafed plants on tall stems, and scraggly gorse bushes grow here in abundance. A large area of this woodland appears to be in the process of being cut down, with recent-looking stumps and felled tree trunks that have already been stripped of a majority of their branches. The brush in this area has also been cut down and left piled by some of the tree trunks, leaving a trampled field with bare dirt showing. To the south a dirt road can be seen in the distance.
117429:
The corpse of a black bear is lying here.
The corpse of a drone bee is lying here.
The corpse of a drone bee is lying here.
The corpse of a drone bee is lying here.
The corpse of a drone bee is lying here.
There is a huge, pyramidal beehive here.

This forest was partially cleared sometime in the past. Mixed in with ancient, looming trees are young ones, and here and there old, rotten stumps form a feeding ground for small insects and fungus. The forest floor has plenty of undergrowth, as the canopy is not very dense.
117430:
The remains of a small tangle of roots lie here in a heap of rotting compost.
A large hawk-like bird is here overlooking its territory.

A mix of birch, pine and rowan trees grow here, spaced far enough apart that light is able to make it to the ground below. More trees, much younger and unable to provide any usable shade, grow in the clear spaces between their mature brethren and alongside a brushy understory. Tall, spreading grasses and herbaceous plants grow along with scraggly shrubs that are open and spreading in the intermittent shade cast by the trees above. Parts of these woods have begun to be cleared: stumps dot this area, and next to them some the felled trunks still lie, already stripped of their branches. Some of the larger scrub bushes here have also been cut down, and left in piles next to the stumps.
117431: While surrounded by forest to the west and south, this open field offers a clear view of the sky with no canopy in the way. The forest surrounding this land is sparse enough that a traveller would have no trouble finding a suitable route through it.
117432: A grey wolf is here, snarling aggressively.

This land was ploughed and left to lie fallow, the furrows still visible underneath the low growth that has sprung up since. Low-growing grasses, sparse enough in some areas that bare dirt is still visible, mix with the occasional heath and weedy plants of varying heights. The ground underfoot is still loose from the plough, not yet packed down by repeated rains, and old weed stalks stick up from the friable soil where they have been cut under. To the west a small farmhouse stands, surrounded by a fence and what appear at this distance to be more fields.
117433:
A brown snake watches you.
A fierce wolverine is here, snarling at you.

These plains are covered with low-growing grasses, mixed with taller clumps of heath and gorse bushes at irregular intervals. The gorse bushes are still small, rising barely above the heath, suggesting that they have not been growing here for long. Some small tree seedlings rise up barely taller than the surrounding grass, puffs of young pine trees and thin birch whips. No mature trees grow here, and no stumps are visible, suggesting that this area was cleared at some point in the past, and maintained as farm fields until recently. The ground underfoot is relatively flat, but to the east it starts to become more hilly.
117434: This grassland is dominated by low growing bentgrass, interspersed with taller clump-forming grasses and short shrubs. Most of the shrubs are heath, but here and there stands of young gorse bushes are beginning to grow, already shading out the grasses around them. No mature trees are visible here, although very young seedlings of pine and birch have begun to sprout, almost hidden in the messy clumps of grasses. Here and there a depression in the grass along with clumps of deer droppings suggest that deer have bedded down in this area recently, and the deer trails that have been worn to dirt hint at where they have gone. To the east and south low hills rise up, impassable due to sheer, crumbling dropoffs.
117435:
A grey wolf is here, snarling aggressively.
A large hawk-like bird is here overlooking its territory.
A grey wolf is here, snarling aggressively.

Low grasses dominate this area, suggesting that these fields were farmed until relatively recently. The grasses are a mix of green blades from the current season's growth and old, brown seed heads and stems from previous years; some of these have bent and broken, giving the area a messy appearance. Some thin, broadleaf tree seedlings rise up through the grass, young whips that have barely begun to branch. No larger trees are present here, and no stumps are visible: the tallest inhabitants of these fields are the tall bushes to the west that make up an old hedgerow. The hedge is a tangled mess, clearly not maintained, and tall weed stalks grow up through its base to stick out the sides and top. Through the hedge a wide, paved road can barely be made out, while to the north a dirt farm road is visible.
117436:
A grey wolf is here, snarling aggressively.
A grey wolf is here, snarling aggressively.
A large hawk-like bird is here overlooking its territory.

This area looks as if it were cleared recently, and not given much time to regrow. No mature trees dot this landscape, and only a few young pine and birch seedlings have started to grow, reaching just above the tall grasses that cover the ground. Some low-growing brambles are tangled in the grasses, with older dead grass stems poking through and wrapped around the thorny branches. Here and there the grasses have been flattened and trampled down, old and new stems bent or lying completely flat, suggesting that an animal has bedded down here recently. To the west a long row of bushes blocks movement, an old hedgerow that has become overgrown. It is irregular in height, the lower portions thinned out and shaded by a twining vine that covers it.
117437:
A huge, black wolf is here, ready to devour.
A grey wolf is here, snarling aggressively.

No mature trees grow here; the area is covered with thick brush instead. Tall gorse bushes grow in tangled clumps, threaded through with lower-growing brambles, creating large patches of thorny, restrictive barriers that are best avoided. Trampled-down deer trails bypass these obstacles, thin ribbons that follow the most open routes through the brush. To the west the tall brush is bordered by a taller hedgerow, unkempt and messy in appearance, with young birch trees poking through its dense branches as they reach for the sky. To the east the ground rises up, turning into low, rolling hills, but the brush growing at their base is too thick to pass through.
117438: The ground here is hilly and uneven, forming low rolling hills. Despite the relatively smooth undulations that mark this terrain, surprisingly steep cuts in the ground are present, masked by the short heath and scrub bushes that grow from the thin soil. These hidden drops and clefts require careful navigation to avoid, and make riding through these hills too dangerous to attempt. Some of these cuts are deeper than others, and a semi-connected line of narrow crevices blocks travel to the east and south, where the hills continue.
117439: Sparse Shrubs in a Grassy Field

Varying types of grasses grow here, both a lower-growing type that has spread evenly through the area and taller clumps that grow at regular intervals throughout. Small, squat shrubs rise above the grasses, some growing in dense clumps and others individually, adding height that is only topped by the stray young pine tree that sticks up above all else. Various broad-leafed plants mix in with the grasses, growing down close to the ground and up on tall hollow stems. The ground underfoot is uneven and rolling, shallow depressions giving way to low hummocks that lack vegetation and reveal bare, crumbling rock.
117440: Here and there a mature tree rises from this field that is otherwise populated only with stumps. Most of the felled trees have been removed, but an occasional trunk still lies here, its branches stripped away and left piled nearby. Short bushes mix with the grasses that currently dominate this area, their relatively restrained growth suggesting that these woods were not cleared too long ago. Young gorse bushes dot the landscape, their small size likely to change quickly with the light available to them absent the trees that used to grow here.
117441: A black snake, with red markings, is lying here.

This is the end of the dried-out brook that snakes through the plains and occasional trees to the north. Beyond the old bank, rough fields lie both north and south, while continued travel to the west is made impossible by too steep a bank. Tree stumps dot the landscape, increasing in number towards the south.
117442: A dried-out depression is the remnant of a stream that used to run through this land. It meanders towards the south, through a natural ditch that runs southwards. The surrounding fields are uneven but rich in plantlife. A stand of old, large rowan trees can be seen growing to the east. Some tree stumps can be seen in the surrounding fields.
117443: Too low and gentle to be called a hill, the land here is still elevated above everything in sight except a range of hills far off in the distance to the north-east. The grass and bushes here grow wild and free, undisturbed by man. A long, gentle slope downwards to the north leads into a hollow, while the elevated plains continue to the east. The Road to Fornost can be seen far to the west, making its way from Bree to Fornost.
117444: The surrounding fields dip into a hollow here, and at the bottom the ground looks wet and soggy. The grass and bushes are mixed with reeds and other plants that prefer more water-logged ground. Albeit all of this, there is no sign of open water here, or a brook.
117445:
A black snake, with red markings, is lying here.
A swarthy, little bandit advances forward.

The surrounding fields are rough and covered with natural ditches that run southward. One of the most noticeable features in the area is a dried-out brook bed that can be spotted coming from the east, and leading south, as it follows one of the breaks in the land.
117446: A tiny skeleton lies here, partially embedded in the dusty ground.

A dried-out brook bed meanders here from the north before heading westward, as it follows a slow decline in the land. Grasses have started to reclaim the brook bed, covering nearly all the small pebbles and sand that the brook was unable to move away, when water still flowed through it.
117447: The flat land sweeps away into the distance, wild and filled with bushes and thick grasses. An enormous impenetrable wild rose-briar grows upon a steep hillside to the northeast. The hillside is further covered by dense thickets as it leads southward. A small stand of pine trees can be seen to the south.
117448: Entrance Hall of a Small Tower
A giant rat patters against you, squeaking maliciously.

The ground floor of this circular tower sports a spiral stone staircase that leads to the floors above and below. The flooring is made of rough stone blocks, and the curved walls are painted black. On the floor lies a circular red carpet, embossed with a green fire breathing dragon.
117449:
The charred corpse of a woman is lying here.
A giant rat patters against you, squeaking maliciously.
A large, venomous-looking green snake is coiled up here.
A large, venomous-looking green snake is coiled up here.
A large bat is here, hanging in the darkness.

This damp cellar is cluttered with old books, soot-covered bottles, musty garments, and rotting bodies. The buckled floorboards are coated in a fine layer of slime, and the fragrant stench of decay permeates the entire room. A circular stone staircase leads upwards into the castle.
117450:
A large cabinet capable of storing goods is here.
In the cabinet, there is a blackened corpse of a man.
A large stone fireplace with a roaring fire warms the room.
A wooden cupboard stands here.
A large copper cauldron stands here on three short, stout legs.

A large black cauldron steams in the middle of this floor, rippling the air above it. Smells of strong spices, and rotting meat, emanate from it. On the southern wall, a few cupboards store bread, vegetables, and spices. A spiral stone staircase provides access to upper and lower floors of the tower.
117451: Living Chamber in a Black Tower

A sturdy bed made from solid oak lies here, covered in warm blankets.
A large, sturdy table made from oak is sitting here.
On the table, there are a piece of paper and a quill pen.
A wicked witch, cowled in black, glares around with mad eyes.
A large bat is here, hanging in the darkness.
A large bat is here, hanging in the darkness.

This room contains a few chairs, a small oak table, and a fine oak bed. Two grizzly bear carpets provide warmth on the cold stone floor. Through a window to the south, a rough landscape of small hills can be seen. A trapdoor leads up to the roof, via a ladder. A spiral staircase leads down.
117452:
A sturdy peg for hanging armour is on the wall.
On the peg, there are a ragged, blackened cloak, a sturdy pair of rigid leather gloves, a dagger, and a pair of rigid leather boots.

An iron fence, topped with red spikes, surrounds the flat roof of this small tower. Below, to the south, rippling masses of black thorns surround a tight path that leads to this castle. Past the thorns, to the northwest, the rolling hills of the Northern Downs cover the landscape.
117453:
A small brown snake is slithering around here.
A small brown snake is slithering around here.

Large, twisting roots poke through the slick muddy walls in a vain attempt to find water. The uneven floor is covered in small puddles, and glossy rocks poke through the ground, making the tunnel a tripping hazard for unwary travellers. The tunnel stretches to the north, and an extensive collection of roots hangs overhead, close enough to reach.
117454:
A large piece of fresh, raw meat lies here.
A grey wolf is here, salivating profusely.
A grey wolf is here, salivating profusely.

The bottom of the crack slopes downward into the rock, widening until it evens out, into a small, round cave. Strewn among the rubble and gravel on the floor are bones, pieces of skin and rotting pieces of flesh, no doubt the leftovers of a predator.
117455:
A newborn spider is here, hungrily crawling about.
A huge, poisonous spider is here.

The tunnel here is surrounded by a vast web, in which small, quivering balls are embedded. The entirely of the web vibrates with the balls, as each step taken sends the mass into roiling waves of white. A small, mossy hole opens in the rock above, and the rocky tube extends eastward into the mountain.
117456:
A black spider crawls here, a shiny red spot visible on its belly.
A newborn spider is here, hungrily crawling about.

The sticky mesh of white webs gets thicker as the tunnel deepens to the south. Light and sound seem to be absorbed by it, as the web vibrates and quivers in frequency to any disturbance in the air. A combination of scratching, and mushy chewing, emanates from all directions.
117457:
The cocooned corpse of a man is lying here.
A huge, poisonous tarantula extends her legs to you.

The web here is thicker, stickier, and hardier than that clinging elsewhere in this muffled tunnel. The webs form large nets, containing bulks of drying corpses, apparently the prepared dishes of unfortunate prey. Decaying corpses lay in heaps on the floor, their identities erased by rot and time.
117458:
A pool of darkish water has formed in a depression of the stone.
A long stalactite hangs from the ceiling here.
A water moccasin slithers out of sight just below the surface of the water.
A water moccasin slithers out of sight just below the surface of the water.
A grey wolf is here, snarling aggressively.

A natural stream of water gurgles up from deep within the limestone rock of the cave system. The sound of trickling water is overwhelming as the rill flows westward. A sizeable chute slopes steeply upwards, polished smooth by the constant procession of water.
117459:
A large, orange pumpkin is here.
A large dog curls his lips back and snarls.

This is an old overgrown track lined with ancient linden trees, their trunks covered in green moss. Past the trees on either side are small gardens of pumpkins and gourds, and beyond these gardens are fields of beans. West, a farmhouse guards this homestead with a steady view.
117460: A round turnip is growing here.

Rows of short green plants stretch over this field. One can only surmise that these plants are turnips from the small pile of rotten turnips that have been piled in a corner. North and east, stout fencing protects the field from larger wildlife. Southwest, a large farmhouse stands proudly over this farm.
117461:
An apple tree with bright green leaves grows here.
On the tree's branches are three apples.

Rows of apple and pear trees sprout their juicy-looking fruit. Some of the fruit hangs low, ready to be picked. The odd grain or vegetable stock grows in the broad gaps between the trees, apparently grown out of a stray seed from the southern fields. West and north, the orchard is protected from deer by high fences, interworked with hard, thorny lattice.
117462: A foetid pile of pickled fish draws flies on top of a pile of compost.

This unkempt field contrasts with the other well tended fields of this farm. Abandoned and broken carts, ploughs, saw horses, and yokes lie about. The rest of the field grows various seeding crops. A large pile of vegetable matter is piled high on the western edge near the fence, and has stained the wood dark brown.
117463: Some cereals that look like wheat are lying here.

Wheat grows here in straight rows, occasionally blowing in the breeze as one billowing mass. To the west, a stout fence marks the edge of the field. The small footpaths between the crops are filled with roots and rocks, a tripping hazard for the unwary traveller.
117464: Oats grow up past a man's belly, bending and weaving in the breeze. The light tan coloured field fills the air with a sweet grassy smell as the long leaves rattle against each other. A stout white fence holds back the thick brush that grows to the east.
117465: A large field of vibrant barley is flanked by smaller fields of rye and oats. In the southeast corner lays an old broken plough. South and east, the fields are demarked by well kempt fences. Looking over the whole, is a grand farmhouse to the northwest. Small paths run between the rows of crops.
117466:
An old weathered scarecrow is planted firmly in the ground here.
A small pile of barley has been left here.

Rows of barley jam this well tended field. Small birds and insects dart in and out of the field, feasting on the plant. A sturdy fence lines the west and south. To the east and north more crops grow in neatly defined rows, footpaths running between them.
117467: A sturdy pair of rigid leather boots are on the ground.

Muddy tracks cover this foyer. A staircase climbs up the south wall. Underneath the staircase, a boot rack holds boots of various sizes. In the north, the foyer transitions into a kitchen while a door leads into the rest of the house to the west.
117468:
A stove stands against one wall here.
A small oaken table has been set here.
On the table, there are a pan, a large wooden cooking spoon, a turnip, and an onion.
Mrs. Appledore is here, looking for her husband.

A sturdy table fills most of this little kitchen. A wood-burning stove rests against the window, and the air is filled with the smell of grains. The walls are hung with old knives, spoons, and pans, and from the ceiling hang loose bags of potatoes, turnips, and onions. The wood floor creaks and is slippery with flour dust.
117469:
Three framed paintings adorn a dark-stained wood wall.
A large stone fireplace with a roaring fire warms the room.
Farmer Appledore stands here, busy with his chores.

A fireplace roars in the northeast corner of this cosy living room. Around the fireplace are a couple rocking chairs and a couch. Next to the fireplace, a door opens into a little bedroom. Smooth wooden planks are covered in the middle by large, pink and white rug.
117470: A small, grassy area is enclosed by a small fence, just high enough to keep children in and animals out. The grass is littered with toys, and numerous tracks of tiny feet are stamped into the dirt. Towards the western side of the yard, an old wooden ladder has been nailed to a small table, forming a crude play structure.
117471:
A wooden chest stands in the corner.
A young girl is smiling at life.

This bedroom is cramped, being mostly filled with a bundled-straw bed covered in woolly blankets. A few toys are scattered across the floor, and along the western wall there are two small, red chests filled with clothes and quilts. The air is stuffy and hot, and the ceiling low.
117472: Slanting walls narrow to a point in the middle of this attic bedroom. A large bed is squeezed next to a brick chimney rising to the wood slats of the roof. Hanging on the northern wall is a large quilt, pink and faded. On the south wall hangs an ancient halberd and shield, nailed over an old grey blanket.
117473: This is a small room filled with boxes of old clothing, unused toys, and linens. In the corner is stuffed a torn painting, a mop, empty bottles, and two old brooms. The ceiling is low, exposed wood slats, brittle, and brown. The floor is made of rough wooden planks, the nails showing their coal black heads.
117474: A swallow flies high above the ground.

A meadow is full of grass, thick and healthy and it is evident why the barn animals love to munch on this stuff. To the east is a gate guarding the crops. South, the meadow continues unimpeded to a lush field, where the signs of cattle trickle.
117475: Green and verdant meadow grass grows in abundance on this cattle field. To the east, a tall fence marks bountiful fields of crops. The grassy field continues far to the north and west, and the faint outline of thick bushes can be seen to the south.
117476: A robin is here, carrying small pieces of wood to its nest.

This field of sedge is trampled in paths by large animals. Obvious piles of dung are scattered between the well munched grasses. The land becomes quite wet to the south where a wide ditch filled with water and rushes would stop travel that direction.
117477: Clusters of slender stems and tall leaves thrive in the mud and shallows.

This lush field is high with clumped bulrush and the brown, poker seedheads of reed mace, giving indication to swampy ground. South, the vegetation grows upwards of eight feet, hiding a wide ditch. North, the field is demarked by a stout, white fence.
117478: A blue dragonfly is circling around.

This field of feral, green and purple grass gives way to unstable muck as it drops down into a flooded ditch in the south. To the north, a well-maintained, white-painted fence guards access to a farm. Over it, a distant barn can be seen behind tops of neat rows of crops.
117479: Clusters of slender stems and tall leaves thrive in the mud and shallows.

This large meadow transitions from a field of sedge in the east to a rough bit of gnarly weeds. It appears that the tough, tall weeds are advancing, taking over the more animal-friendly fodder. To the south, rushes abound from a wide ditch filled with water. North, a tall hedge full of green bushes stops travel.
117480: A squirrel scampers around here, looking for nuts from the trees.

Thick, gnarly weeds cover this field. Their stems are tough and yield only when under the weight of a full grown man. The field gently slopes into a muddy, wet ditch that separates this field from a dirt road in the south. North, thick, dull green hedges impede travel.
117481:
A warped, dead tree trunk stands tall and contorted in the sour muck.
A swarm of midges is here, humming around you.
A swarm of midges is here, humming around you.

This meadow is filled with dead, thin tree trunks, surrounded by short, thick grasses. Smells of sour muck and wet air give the land a deadened sound. Old branches crunch underfoot and the air is filled with a heavy smell of decay.
117482: This lush field gives life to rich grasses. In the low-lying areas, butterbur and moss grow on exposed rocks. Large, round hazel bushes are scattered about, giving shade to withering ferns. To the south can be seen a derelict farm house, while in the north, hedgerows block the way.
117483: Purple headed grass billows soft and erect in this large field. The seed heads look a sour grey when viewed up close and the grass leaves have soft hairs. The field smells of fresh air, grass and dirt. Travel is unimpeded in all directions.
117484:
A shaggy-haired cow looks around curiously whilst grazing.
A swallow flies high above the ground.

A massive grazing field is enclosed by ancient brown hedges, blocking travel to the south or west. Birds can be seen from time-to-time nipping at the hedge berries. The field itself is well grazed, and piles of dung abound. Flies fly lazily about, seeming to ignore the swallows that fly low, scooping them out of the air.
117485: A shaggy-haired cow looks around curiously whilst grazing.

An extensive cow pasture is hemmed in on the north and west by a hedge of well established bushes. The grass is trimmed low, and dung lays in piles drawing numerous flies and the animals that feed on them. To the east and south, the pasture continues.
117486: A child's toy in the form of a wooden bear has been left on the ground.

A small, grassy area is enclosed by a short fence, which curves around from the northern side of the house to the west, then south. The grass is littered with toys, and numerous tracks of tiny feet are stamped into the dust. In the middle of the yard is a tall oak tree with a rope swing hanging from it.
117487: A circular stone well has been built here.

In the corner of this neat yard is an old stone well, the grey rocks covered in smooth, bright green moss. The crank, bucket, and chain are newly built, crude but functional. A low fence blocks access to the rest of the farmyard and a side door leads into the barn to the east.
117488:
An old bull is here, fighting Put.
Put the Mountain Troll is here, fighting an old bull.
Sludge the Mountain Troll is standing here.
Taara the Mountain Troll (TT) is here, fighting an old bull.

This barn is constructed of exposed, roughly hewn wood, hard and old. Underfoot, interlocking, natural limestones form a flat, easy to shovel surface. The air is thick with the smell of barn animals and fresh fodder. A rope ladder leads up to the loft, which extends over the rest of the barn in the south. To the west, a side door, too narrow for a large animal to fit through, leads to the backyard.
117489: A large paddock is hemmed in by a sturdy fence, the ground is exposed on the edges where farm animals pace, and in the middle is green grass and ordure. In the northeast corner is a feed trough and a pile of hay. Near the entrance is a watering trough. A heap of dung and other compost stands in the southwest corner of the paddock and an iron gate blocks passage to the field in the east.
117490:
A long water trough made of wood stands here.
A sturdy pack horse is standing here.
A stocky mountain mule is here, waiting to serve.

This barnyard is well-grazed, being mostly bare dirt with clumps of short, sturdy grass. A heap of dung and food compost stands in the northwest corner of the field and a trough of water sits in the middle, freshly tarred. The smell of animals is strong and flies swarm the air.
117491:
A pig is here, covered in mud.
A young farm-hand is here hard at work.
A pig is here, covered in mud.

The southeast corner of the barnyard is fenced off to form a pig pen. On the near side of the pen is a feeding trough with scraps of rejected food. The bottom of this pen is thick with mud, muck, and small bones, and the air is ripe with offal.
117492:
A large wooden box painted with a chicken sits here.
A brown cow is here, contemplating a higher reality whilst chewing slowly.

Cattle stalls line the western wall of this old, sturdy barn. The floor is lain with smooth interlocking, natural stones, and decades of hard muck fill the cracks. Next to the stalls is an assortment of buckets and milking stools, and the air is rich with ordure and animal feed.
117493:
A nest is here.
A hen is trying to pick some grains here.
A hen is trying to pick some grains here.
A mouse is here nosing around, looking for a safe place to hide.

Built as an extension to the barn, this small chicken coop has rows of nests stacked on top of each other. Hay lines the hard dirt floor, and the walls are hard slats, letting in air and light. Flies and gnats fly about in the air, dodging feathers and hay motes.
117494:
A bale of hay is lying here.
A tiny spider is here, eating a tiny bug.

Bales of hay fill this yawning loft. The smell of their dried grasses fills the air, partially masking the smell of animals from below. The old, dry, dark wooden walls rise high and hold a great many bales of hay. Near the roof peak, unreachable spider webs hang full of ancient dead bugs.
117495: A vast, lush field is overgrown with rangy, hard-stemmed chicory and leafy goat's beard. Spotted on land are small blackthorn trees growing into tangles. East and west, an overgrown, narrow track divides the field. A stone wall lines the southern edge of the field. Tall, thorny bushes grow high above the wall, blocking the view beyond.
117496: A roe deer is standing here, watching the terrain while chewing the vegetation.

This grassy land stretches to the horizon, healthy and wild with succulent sorrel, and hairy ribwort. A narrow track cuts through east and west, littered with patches of black, hard shrubs, preventing straight lines of travel. The northern edge of the land falls away into a waterlogged ditch filled completely with tall grasses.
117497: An overgrown track runs east and west on this lush field of soft sweetbriar, and clumped figwort. South, a crumbled line of stones mark what was once a slender stone wall. A muddy, waterlogged ditch stands at the north of this field, overgrown with bulrushes and soft, dark green agrimony.
117498: On a verdant field, barely seen between a morass of foxtail and cocksfoot, is the likeness of a track giving no signs of humans passing this way for quite some time. Thick hedges grow wildly to the south, almost swallowing that entire side of the track. A watery, muddy ditch, filled with bulrushes and reeds, blocks passage to the north.
117499: Lush Field among a Dirt Path

A morass of foxtail grass grows on this lush field, the bushy-tailed and upright sward grows thick as it blows about in the breeze. Hidden in the grass is a dirt track. Overgrown with grasses, it runs west to east and fades into this field. A wide ditch to the north chokes the land with bushy clumps of meadow sweet, blocking travel. South, rampant buckthorn grows in a thick hedge forming an impassable wall.
117500: Sedge and Field Maple Lined Meadow

A squirrel scampers around here, looking for nuts from the trees.
A black crow flies low to the ground here, looking for carrion to eat.

This meadow is thick with sedge divided by lines of field maple. Going from east to west, each line of maple seems to be growing out of a rut in the otherwise untempered grass. A steep descent flows northwards, while to the south and southwest, lush grasslands roll to the horizon.
117501: Overgrown, busted fences mark fields that have grown back into a wild lea. The few dejected outbuildings that still stand are choked with vines and weeds. Inside the largest building the floor has collapsed in many places, revealing a set of stairs leading down into a dark basement.
117502:
A huge wych elm stands grey-green here.
A great horned owl looks cautiously around it.
