Dense, rippling grasslands stretch in all directions, green and silver, moving with the wind as it wills. The ground is spongy, and gives underfoot, belying a moisture that is evident with the vast number of gnats that whir in small, black swarms.
117503: A pile of boulders lies here, covered in ivy.

This field is lush and wild stretching to the horizon in all directions but west, where a large, stony cliff stands tall, topped with green, tall bushes. The land is thick with waist-high, dark red elder bushes interspersed with clumps of fuzzy, green grasses. The air is abuzz with small gnats and bees, and smells of sweet flowers.
117504: A sprawling green bush of stinging nettle grows here.

The boggy gault has become too much for the grasses native to these meadows, and they succumb to overbearing masses of bright green nettle. A pleasant, bitter, salty fragrance fills the air. Travel is impeded to the east by thick muck turning to a ditch and to the west an imposing escarpment looms.
117505: A grey bird with a bright orange-red belly sits here, singing a melodic tune.

This meadow is overgrown with sedge, nettle and hazel bushes: a jumble of plants fighting for life in the rich, wet soil. Lost in the rampant verdure are five large boulders, weathered to the point of near disintegration. They sit far apart, but seem to be about the same distance from each other. To the north and west, passage is impossible due to the wild, thick plant life.
117506: A faint, spicy smell of hazel wafts along the breeze from hazel bushes looming over the western rise. The land here is flat and lush, covered in grasses grown of good moisture. North, east, and south the verdant view expands as far as the eye can see.
117507:
A small cluster of clover grows here.
A small grasshopper clings to a blade of grass, ready to spring.

A substantial, low, exposed limestone crest gives life to hart's tongue, clover, and spindle near the northern edge of this expanse of pink tinged sedge. The ground rises a bit to the south where encroaching thorn bushes begin to lay siege to the grass.
117508: A goat is here, grazing in the hills.

A field of waist-high grass sways about, green, tan, and purple. To the north, the land increases to a plateau, becoming drier and harsh. This field drops in the south, where it overlooks a watery, boggy land. To the east, the grasses continue to the horizon.
117509: Hazel bushes grow in patches throughout this high land, buffeted about by a hard wind. Grasses and smaller shrubs cover the rest of the plateau, grabbing onto the hard, dry soil. The air is full of dust and the smell of earth is strong.
117510:
Leaves and plant matter form a matted surface on the earth below.
An erect shrub with green pinnate leaves is growing here.
Inside the shrub, there are two piles of crimson raspberries.
A large, venomous-looking green snake is coiled up here.

Tall grasses bob their heavy heads, nodding to large, green bushes along this plateau. The bushes grow in groups, leafy, and rise from six to twenty feet. Small white moths fly about the bushes, and contrast with the dark green leaves. To the east, the plateau gives way to an unexpected cliff.
117511:
An erect shrub with green pinnate leaves is growing here.
Inside the shrub, there are two piles of crimson raspberries.

Tall, dark green bushes sprout over this vast plateau. Standing upwards of eighteen feet, they grow in clumps at low, rocky areas. Their glossy and bumpy branches have grown thick into each other and a sweet fragrance fills the air. Small, white moths flutter about and underfoot, small round nuts crunch easily. In the higher land, brown grass grows short and defiant. To the east, the plateau drops off, providing no footing.
117512: A sprawling, twisted tree grows here.

These small hills are dotted by numerous thorny hawthorn bushes: silver and grey at a distance, green and red up close. The earth is dense and covered in short grasses and dandelions. In the north and east, the thorny bushes become more sparse, opening out to grassy fields. In the south the bushes crowd the hills, making travel more difficult.
117513: Lush, green grass covers the ground of a vast, open meadow. Scattered here and there are small dirt mounds and sunken burrows. A thin, sparse tree line creates a natural border to the south and west, hindering travel in those directions. The vastness of the meadow expands to the north and east.
117514:
A brown pond between old branches and roots is here.
A blooming water-lily floats on the surface of the water.
A green frog is here, hopping around.
A heron is stalking the area, looking for fish.

A small watering hole is nestled in a gradual depression in an expansive, green and purple bog. Lilies reach up from the clear depths to dot the surface of the standing water, reaching the black surface with small green circles and yellow flowers. The ground is boggy, with a slightly rotten odour, and drags down the heavy of foot.
117515: A dense grove of willow trees surrounds the path. Narrow branches hang low overhead with ghost-like moss hanging in small strips. The walkway's surface is unusually well groomed, with clover patches spreading beyond the trail's serpentine path through the surrounding hills.
117516: A small path, slightly covered with leaves and old twigs, continues to the north and east; bordered by tall bushes and trees with thin trunks and branches. To the east the vegetation becomes thinner until it fades away into the low grass of a plain.
117517: A grassy hill emerges from the surroundings, the sides of which are slippery from densely clustered vines with smooth leaves. The ground appears trampled, pounding the vines into a solid surface. To the east and north a trail may be seen avoiding the hill.
117518: This path has been nearly overtaken by an old, thorny bush that has been encroaching upon it for decades. It seems however, that at some point in the past someone used a sturdy rope to bind its branches from completely blocking the way of those travelling along the path.
117524:
A large bulletin board, entitled "Clerics' Guild", is mounted here.
A small oaken table has been set here.
On the table, there are three juicy plums and two dark coloured flasks.

Parts of the walls of this house are living trees which fit perfectly into gaps between the wooden planks. This house is just one large square room. Every available spot seems to be covered with shelves, pots, jars, glasses, and baskets containing potions, herbs, plants, and powders. It looks as if someone has worked here for years, but rarely if ever tidies the place.
117525:
A large cabinet capable of storing goods is here.
An old, wise druid is standing here looking very clever and savant (glowing).
A simple servant quietly walks around, performing his duties.

Stout but simple wooden bookshelves line the walls of this small chamber. Seemingly disorganised stacks of old, dusty books fill the shelves and large parts of the floor. An old, heavy armchair stands beside the only window in this room. The small fireplace is filled with the embers of a dying fire.
117531: Between the low and high bushes this path continues without any discernible pattern. It turns here and there, and back and forth leading travellers sometimes around bushes and other times through them. Short grass grows on the soft earth and dry sticks lie scattered around.
117532:
There are two handfuls of clover here.
The overgrown remains of a boar lie here.

Rich soil must be the reason this plain is covered in such vibrantly healthy grass. Many different varieties of grass grow here. In some spots, the stalks are high and slender, while at other points there are blades of grass with thick stems and broad leaves.
117533:
There are two handfuls of clover here.
A buck runs swiftly from place to place, looking about warily as it grazes.

Short grass covers these plains which stretch out in all directions. The break in the carpet of grass is offered by a few lost bushes that emerge from the flat ground. In some spots, the droppings of rabbits and other small animal tracks indicate the plain is not as lifeless as it may look.
117534:
There are two handfuls of clover here.
A grey wolf is here, thin from starvation.
A grey wolf is here, thin from starvation.

On this plain grows mostly short, unhealthy grass. Even the occasional bush grows very low, their branches being brown and covered in thorns. Yet, at several spots grow rich clusters of plants. It looks as if the plain would make up at these spots for all the other shortcomings. Rich grass, flowers with thick stems and high bushes seem to grow out of the meagre soil for no apparent reason.
117535:
A black wolf pads restlessly, looking for its next prey.
A black wolf pads restlessly, looking for its next prey.

Below the short grass of the plain many flat stones are hidden. The soil itself seems to consist only of hardened earth and stone, while only few animals have left their tracks in the poor vegetation. The plain continues until it meets the horizon.
117536: A small cluster of clover grows here.

The ground is covered in a short carpet of green grass, interspersed with clover and dandelion. The air is filled with sweet smells, and near a low, lush shallow grow a bunch of graceful willows. As far as the eye can see plains extend, with a slight incline eastward giving a lingering view.
117537: A cluster of white star-shaped forget-me-nots flourish here in reminiscence.

A series of rolling crests in the land stretch from north to south. Ascending to the west, thorny shrubs infest a high point in the plains where the grass grows with much less vigour. Flowers, mostly forget-me-nots, line the rolling plains as they spread out to the north and east.
117538: Rodent colonies have claimed the area as their own. The natural landscape has been completely altered with burrows dotting the area with small grassy mounds next to them. The grass has been kept short from their constant foraging.
117539: A huge, solitary tree, spans high into the sky above. Its dense branches and leaves create a huge canopy directly beneath it. Several yards away, a tall, fractured rock stands stricken by lightning. Blackened by fire, this rock must have been scorched a while ago as the grass around it grows tall and healthy. To the south, the grass grows shorter as it rises to an area of thorny shrubs, while in all other directions, the tall grasses wave and bow on rolling plains.
117540: A grey bird with a bright orange-red belly sits here, singing a melodic tune.

A vast expanse of heaving grasses flows in all directions. A few trees and boulders are all that prevent the wind from flowing as it wills, yet even the boulders appear worn smooth by the wind, showing few protrusions on their flat heads. With every step on the lush grassland, the ground seems to spring back up, fresh and light.
117541: A brown fox is here, looking for some rabbits to chew up.

A sea of tall grass descends from the northeast in a series of gentle drops dividing flatter areas as if the wind has carved a broad staircase out of the swelling plain, creating a crescent dip in the grasslands before rising up again in the southwest. The skyline in the north and west bobs up and down as gently as the breeze that flows through this area.
117542: The billowing grasslands rise in a series of gradual steps to a swell. Before the apex of the swell can be reached, a line of crude bedrock stands guard over the ascending land. Stripped of its soil from the relentless wind, the bedrock offers no foothold to ascend, though they stand just a few feet above the head of a tall man. Away from the rocks, to the south and west, the ground dips to a low point in the plains in a crescent-shaped line.
117543: This field sprouts random oats and wheat among the vigorous sedge. The forgotten land has fallen back to nature, and seems the better for it. North, west, and south the land fades to the horizon. To the east, a rampant wall of shiny barked buckthorn blocks the way.
117544:
A large sack is on the ground.
A huge black fungus is here, exuding a foul stench.

The air is extremely musty, making breathing difficult. Moisture drips down the old, stone walls and collects in a puddle in the ground. The dank, stale water overflows into a dark hole in the corner of the cellar, creating a distant dripping sound from down below. A rotten pile of burlap bags lays heaped in one corner, and in another is a mound of broken clay jars.
117545:
A pool of foul, black water fills the bottom of this hole.
An ancient fungus smothers the boulders.
An ancient fungus smothers the boulders.

A tunnel of loose dirt leads down into a pool of foul black water a foot deep. The pool fills the entire hole, getting deeper further away from the entrance. The air smells sour and rotten, and is so thick with dankness that it collects on any dry thing that passes through. At the far south end, an ooze of slime clogs the wall at the water level.
117546: Thick green slime covers the bottom of this small tunnel, the walls oozing a foul coating ever down. In the north, the tunnel descends into some foul water where a clog of slime blocks the way. In the south, the tunnel continues into the darkness. About, the air is thick with moisture and a dank, sour smell.
117547:
A water moccasin slithers out of sight just below the surface of the water.
A hungry-looking giant lizard is slithering towards you.

Sludge walls turn to muck as they give way to the dank, wet slime that covers the floor. The floor is thick and gooey, slurping anything that touches it. Green drips of foetid water fall from above, and the air is wet and stale. The slime below is marked by animal footprints.
117548: This tunnel slants down slightly as it hits a dead end, creating a small cavern. A short ceiling is crowded, round and clammy, oozing with muck that slides down the walls. The thickening slime creeps to a deep and soupy bottom. Drops of rank, green goo drip down, splattering slime with irregular plops.
117549: A squirrel scampers around here, looking for nuts from the trees.

Partway up a huge tree, approximately six yard from the ground, the branches and leaves are so dense that it is almost impossible to discern anything on the ground below. Everything is so thick and dense that climbing is no easy task, and is indeed very taxing, though not impossible.
117550:
A nest is here.
A cute young hawk is standing here.
A cute young hawk is standing here.
A cute young hawk is standing here.
A large mother hawk is here looking for prey to feed her young.

The top of the huge tree does provide somewhat of a vantage point to the low, rolling plains in this area, but not to the immediate surroundings. The branches and leaves below are too thick to discern anything on the ground directly below.
117551: Waist-high grass bobs and sways under the weight of the flowing wind. With every breeze, the grass dips low enough to reveal colourful flowers that add a vibrant hue to the deep green of the grasses. The grassland declines gently northwards where, at an abrupt step, it lifts above the surrounding fields until it is higher than a tall man.
117552: Prickly, white-stemmed plants, with blue flower heads grow in abundance.

The ground here is covered in clover and thistle, spreading green and low, and small stands of field maple attempt to fight for life against the teeming fescue. Grasshoppers and flying ants bounce around, trying to avoid the low flying swallows that swoop about.
117553: Sweeping fields of low grass extend in all directions, growing gradually taller to the north and west. The landscape is almost entirely green, with a few wild flowers lending their vibrant hues to the otherwise uninterrupted flows of verdant flora. The turf is moist, and springs beneath every step. Occasional rustling sounds can be heard from small game scampering through the grass.
117554: A small grasshopper clings to a blade of grass, ready to spring.

Scattered weeds grow among wispy grasses. Occasionally, a bee can be seen bouncing between the few flowering plants of this field. Sloping upwards in the east, the ground crests into a ridge, which lines the eastern and northeastern horizon. In the west, the ground levels out to an expanse of lush fields, while in the south the land rolls forming foothills.
117555: Rolling hills are covered with waving grass bending in the wind, dancing intricately with each passing gust. The grass is so thick that nothing beneath the green waves is visible, only the contour of the land. Lone trees dot the surroundings, their trunks standing out among the grassy waves like rough, brown pillars.
117556:
There are two handfuls of clover here.
A black wolf pads restlessly, looking for its next prey.
A black wolf pads restlessly, looking for its next prey.

Only poor vegetation is growing here. Everything that grows leaves seems to quickly become eaten by animals, as many ripped stems indicate. There are some holes in the crumbled earth, probably having been dug by some small varmint, but there is no sign any animal has lived in them for quite a while.
117557: A buck runs swiftly from place to place, looking about warily as it grazes.

A forest fire has recently blazed through the area, evidence of its heat has scarred the landscape. Burned trunks are all that remain of trees, some hollowed out from the fire. Branches that have burned to a crisp and ash mounds litter the ground.
117558: A lone, burned tree is the only thing that catches the eye on this plain. Apart from the tree, only short, brown grass and low bushes can be seen. The remains of the tree are blackened and split in two, and it looks as if lightning had struck and ignited it. Since there is no other sign of an ignition source and ivy has started to grow on the dead trunk, quite some time must have passed.
117559:
A black wolf pads restlessly, looking for its next prey.
A black wolf pads restlessly, looking for its next prey.

This plain seems to be very fertile, the soil is soft and the grass grows thick. Yet, there is not much to see since most of the vegetation has been eaten by animals and has not yet grown back. The traces which have not been removed by wind or rain, and the echoes of distant bleating, indicate a herd of sheep has spent some time here and moved on, as they finished eating.
117560: A small group of boulders is the only change between the low grass and small, widespread bushes on this plain. The highest of these stones stands three feet above the plain, and it can not be told what brought and piled these stones here. The view continues in any direction until it meets the horizon, only to the south grows more vegetation and the outlines of trees stand out.
117561: High, slightly yellow grass covers the hills and moves in the wind like waves in the ocean. From time to time, paths created by other travellers or animals cross each other. The hills continue to gently roll in most directions, and tree lines block passage to the north and south.
117562: Winding around the hill, a path makes its way up and down the hill. Sparse vegetation covers the path while a few small trees grow on its sides. Sometimes, patches of pebbles lie on the path, making the ground a bit harder to travel on.
117563: A sprawling green bush of stinging nettle grows here.

A few bushes peek out of the grass which lines a small path leading to the hilltop. A few flowers grow on the sides of the path in between the other sparse vegetation. Most parts of the hill itself are covered with medium-high grass.
117564: An unfrequented path winds itself through the rolling hills that cascade the horizon. Tall golden prairie grass skirts the beaten path to expose an accessible foot trail. Only sparse vegetation and trees with light-brown bark can be seen in the surrounding landscape.
117565: Enormous trees loom over a paved road with many smaller bushes and plants as it leads through the surrounding landscape. Groups of young oak trees have recently grown among the fading patches of grass revealing a much smaller, less-travelled path towards the north.
117566: The grassy field is covered with patches of small red flowers. Old flower beds are scattered throughout the field, some of them still contained within their original flower beds. Others have escaped their confinement and now grow wild throughout the grass.
117567: Only a few walls and broken stones remain of what used to be a building. These walls seem to be the ruins of a chapel. Many broken blocks which once have formed the building lie scattered around and make travelling difficult. Most of the stones, as well as the complete floor of the chapel, have been overgrown by grass, bushes, and vines.
117568:
A black pond of water is here.
A water moccasin slithers out of sight just below the surface of the water.
A water moccasin slithers out of sight just below the surface of the water.
A water moccasin slithers out of sight just below the surface of the water.

A small, dark pond with steep, slippery banks lies here, barren from any type of tracks. On the water's surface float lazily a few lost leaves, slowly sinking into the darkness. In the murky water, dark green plants barely grow by the muddy shore, covered in slimy algae. Cattails grow in patches around the pond, in the thick brown mud.
117569: Only a few scattered bushes and tall grasses grow here. A few trees with thin branches have taken root but most of them are pretty low. Only very recently, some travellers must have taken a rest on this plain, since the remains of two small campfires can be spotted.
117570: Various rubble lie strewn about the field, consisting of various sizes of broken cobblestones. Tall weeds grow between the rocks and in the cracks of the stones, seemingly to cause some to splinter asunder. Large piles form a wall against ancient barkless trees to the east.
117571:
An apple tree with bright green leaves grows here.
On the tree's branches are two apples.

An open field lies between hills to the west and a grove of oak trees to the east. Patches of bushy vegetation dot the area and a small ditch flows from the hills and cuts into the ground along the roots of the trees, which seem to swell from the water and grow.
117572:
A sturdy pack horse is standing here.
A colourful butterfly is fluttering around here.
A duck is here, quacking happily.
A colourful butterfly is fluttering around here.

Soft grasses can be seen covering a nearly flat field, stretching until the horizon meets the sky. In some spots, an animal has dug a hole in the ground and ripped up the turf. In these places the brown and fertile soil can be seen.
117573: A sprawling, twisted tree grows here.

At the crest of the small hill grows an extremely old, twisted tree that is surrounded by tall, dead grass. A few younger shrubs can be seen down the hillside. The base of the twisted tree is so wide it must have seen hundreds of winters. A second look reveals a large hole leading down beneath the roots of the elderly tree with a mysterious and damp odour.
117574: A rabid raccoon stands here, frothing at the mouth.

Grassy, lush hills transform into dry and rocky highlands to the north, the greenery turning more brown and silver as the land becomes drier. Thorny weeds and low shrubs provide stable handholds on the steeper drops, and the soil skids out from under foot, loose and brown.
117575: A dense carpet of blue flowers dip their heads in the breeze.

Wildflowers bloom in patches along the grassy hillsides. Low hanging blue, bell shaped flowers bounce lazily in the wind, heavy with nectar. The air is laden with pollen, almost creating a yellow haze which settles into a dense carpet of fine dust on the ground.
117576: Spongy green moss has formed a dense blanket covering the ground. The ground is soft and saturated with water, allowing the lichen to thrive. The moss has covered most of the vegetation in the area, and branches of bushes hang low with the moss strands dangling from them.
117577: A fierce boar is here, making grunting noises.

Patches of grass interspersed with tufts of bare bedrock extend down from the ridge in the west and to the slope in the north. As the land flattens out, rocks gradually become less frequent and waist-high grass takes over. To the east and south, the field drops precipitously, providing a good view of the road to Fornost below.
117578: Dark dirt rankles with ever increasing stones, rocks and boulders as the land rises westward. Sedge, cocksfoot, and foxtail clamp onto any exposed earth. North, the land is blocked by a crumbling stone wall and to the west travel becomes arduous, the land rising to a ridge.
117579: This high, rolling land is dry and rocky, and grasses are short and stiff. Some hardy brushes grow silver and dusty, their leaves long and thin. The descent to either side is precarious, with only a few straggly weeds holding together the rocky soil. Far in the east, the lane can be seen winding its way around hills.
117580:
A shrub with maple-like leaves is growing here.
On the shrub, there are two handfuls of blackcurrant berries.

Luscious currant and gooseberry bushes grow wild on this field, giving evidence to the crops that were once cultivated. Tall grasses often stick their heads up over the short, green bushes, trespassing in abrupt clumps. On the northern edge of the field, a crumbling fence lies, now more a long mound of stones. Far to the east, a rusted gate stands crumbling amidst a mossy stone wall.
117581: Long, wavy strands of grass flutter over the tops of wildly growing crops. The heads of oat and barley stalks are picked at by a multitude of black birds and the air is thick with small swarms of flies, bees, and wasps. A stone wall stretches along the western side of this field. Unlike the north wall that is just crumbled remains, this wall has been plugged with dirt and rocks, creating a patchwork of grey and brown.
117582: Long, wavy strands of grass flutter over the tops of an abandoned field of rye. A barren, rocky ridge rises southwards, casting a long, pointed shadow over this field. A decrepit stone wall appears to have been built over what was once the tail end of the ridge, but has now been reduced to little more than a bump in the field. To the east and north the field continues, while in the west the land becomes loose and rocky.
117583: Patches of wild oats push their stocks above a sea of tall grass. A few other food-bearing crops grow haphazardly throughout the field, as if this were a farm tended only by the animals that graze on it. A crumbling stone wall lines the land south and east.
117584: Tough, purple grasses and short, silver bushes weave and wind their way through scattered rocks. In places, rocks fall into treacherous, deep craters. The southern part of this field is so filled with the hazards that there is no clear path through them.
117585: A large brown snake with black patches is coiled here.

The surrounding field swells up here to a rise of hard soil and loose shrubbery. The view of the fields in the west and south is acute as the land drops at a short, dirt cliff. Passage to the north is blocked by thorny buckthorn trees, tight and thick.
117586: In a great, rolling field, a small grove of trees has been planted with some foresight. On the outside, rowans grow smooth and silver, their red berries abounding. On the inside a great yew stands, defiant. Nary a sound is heard in the middle of the grove, caused by the yew needles underfoot.
117587: This land is wild with large clumps of grasses interspersed in the low ground with shiny barked buckthorn. To the north, west, and south, the buckthorn grows wild and thick, forming prickly, impassable hedges. In the air, birds fly lazily, drugged by the weak poison of the trees' berries.
117588: A fallen tree lies on the ground, its clump of roots pointing upwards.

An ancient, ruined estate of great lawns and paths of gravel sprawl here, dry and fierce, thick with thistle. Thorny cherry trees stick their hard, barbed branches on the edges of the land in deliberate rows. In the east, the ruins of a stately farmhouse are being swallowed by thorns and brambles which climb to the sky like pointy, grasping fingers.
117589: A grand chamber stands unsteady, light seeping in through cracks in the walls and great holes above. The building had a second story at one point, but it has fallen onto this one. Large beams lay smashed on the left and fore, crushing the walls and exposing the room to the elements. Dust covers the ground, and the boards creak loudly. All about, vines reach in, thick and greedy.
117590:
An old iron stove stands against the north wall.
A giant rat patters against you, squeaking maliciously.
A giant rat patters against you, squeaking maliciously.

As opposed to the rest of these ruins, this room is intact. The ceiling is white, spotted with black bits of mould, and in the corners, thick spider webs glom together. The outer wall's window is broken glass, smashed by ropy, thorny vines. On the walls are hung pots, pans, knives, spoons, and shelves of spices.
117591: A purple dresser sits against the wall, ancient and creaky.

This small room sits off the kitchen, dark and cramped. Two beds bunk against the far wall, straw poking through thin, yellow sheets. The walls are painted ochre, and drip with water stains. An ancient, mouldy grey rug covers the wooden floor, and fills the room with a sour odour.
117592: A huge black fungus is here, exuding a foul stench.

Stairs lead down into a large food cellar, the creaking wood still sturdy enough to hold weight. The room is man-high, lined with stones, and has a dirt floor. Thick wooden beams hold up the first floor, and large cracks show in the wood. The room smells thickly of mould and stale flour.
117593: A large road leads through a landscape of grass and green. Thousands of merchants' carriages have turned the soil into a hard road. Many low bushes have grown all around spotting the grassland with dots of different shades of green.
117594: Large, leafy weeds have overrun an old field. Old furrows have begun to fall into disarray, and it is not easy to tell from under the weeds where one ends and others begin. Small patches of rotten pumpkins and squash dot the field in areas where the weeds have not taken complete control.
117595: Vines grow here in many ordered rows. Someone must have once worked very hard since countless stakes have been put into the ground to give the vines the support they need to grow straight upwards. Tall weeds now fill the spaces between the rows of vines.
117596: The centre of this large road is so hard that only vast amounts of rain could turn it muddy. The edges, however, have not been packed as hard and seem to turn into soft mud quite often. The surrounding grasses try to take root on the road wherever it does not get constantly destroyed by hoofs of horses, feet of travellers or iron wheels of carriages.
117597: A colourful butterfly is fluttering around here.

Cutting through the grassland, the Greenway connects the north with the south. The soil is darkened by dirt and firm from many travellers' feet. A few high bushes on the western side of the road offer a change of scenery for the eyes while on the eastern side an old and overgrown camp-site can be spotted.
117598: Many piles of boulders and rocks lie scattered around in the high grass. Most of them are, at least in parts, overgrown by grass or low bushes. The road of firm soil leads through this assembly of rocks and bends around the occasional larger pile or boulder.
117599: The Greenway bends sharply to the east and south here, with the surrounding overgrown grasses encroaching onto the roadway. Columns of smoke, probably from the many chimneys of Bree, can be seen to the north. The hard soil of the roads bear many tracks of carts and feet.
117600:
A black wolf pads restlessly, looking for its next prey.
A black wolf pads restlessly, looking for its next prey.

The surrounding field is cut through by a bending curve in the wide, oft-travelled Greenway. The road curves along the southern base of a nearby down and continues south along a light forest and west through the fields that dot the landscape south of Bree-hill.
117601: A sharp-eyed hawk is here stalking some prey.

This small forest covers only a few square miles of land, lying between the plains in the north, the Greenway to the west and south, and the Downs to the east. Bushes with sharp thorns grow all over the forest, but they seem to be most thickly-clustered near its edges. And yet, to the west, there is a small opening in the mass of bushes that would allow passage out of the forest.
117602:
A decaying corpse lies among the dead vegetation, entangled in the vines.
A duck is here, quacking happily.

Row by row, the vines grow. Every single plant seems to have been planted in a planned spot. The complete vineyard looks to have been in order at one point in time. The soil beneath the plants is full of debris, dead leaves, and various other dead vegetation.
117603: A small, dense tangle of roots covers the ground.

Literally thousands of vines can be seen here, overgrown and snaking all about with no real direction. Small bands have been used to bind each vine to a thin stake to keep its growth upright. As far as the eye can see, each row stands in a nearly perfect order, yet obviously neglected over time.
117604:
A dwarven skeleton lies on the ground, entangled in vines.
A mass of wriggling vines drops on you from the trees.

Vines are growing here, set up in one line after another. Stakes, firmly planted into the ground, hold the vines upright while narrow walls of quarried stones divide the whole area into several parcels. Nature seems to have long ago claimed this place.
117605: A tall stag is here, grazing peacefully.

A vast sea of lush, green grass dominates the landscape, tall and bending in the wind with each gust. Low bushes and small trees grow intermittently throughout the area, providing more than adequate shelter for the variety of small animals who have dug burrows throughout the land.
117606: A grassy hill ascends suddenly from the otherwise flat landscape surrounding it. Mounds of dirt and small holes are scattered about, evidence that small animals are plentiful on the hill. The hill provides an excellent view of the landscape for miles all around.
117607: This low, flat area stretches wide between several areas of rolling hills in every direction. Sparse patches of trees and bushes are scattered throughout the flat landscape and the grass is very tall and overgrown. There are several mounds and holes spread throughout the area, where animals have burrowed.
117608: A large brown snake with black patches is coiled here.

Lush green grass spreads out as far as the eye can see. The meadow is dotted with small, yellow flowers, which grow plentiful all around. A low rock wall, ruined with the passage of time, blocks travel to the north. The wall appears unstable, built from large grey rocks that have large gaps between them.
117609: This is the northern end of a wide area of smooth slopes and hills which traverse up and down. Only low vegetation can be seen, the highest bushes standing no more than three feet tall. Hard grasses grow on the hills to the south, and the Greenway cutting the grasslands from north to south is clearly visible.
117610:
A large stone fireplace with a roaring fire warms the room.
A barman watches you calmly, while skilfully mixing a drink.

The room is dimly lit, the only light coming from the blazing fireplace, and a few lamps hanging from the rafters. The bar is just to the right of the entrance, and a sign has been posted on a pillar beside it. On a good day, this room is filled with all sorts of travellers and residents of Bree, and many races can be picked out of the crowds. At times, it can be hard to see in this room through all the smoke and poor lighting conditions. Behind the bar hangs a large painting of Bree city.
117611:
A large bulletin board, entitled "Board of the Free Peoples", is mounted here.
A large, sturdy table made from oak is sitting here.
On the table, there are a map of Bree and two beer mugs.
The storyteller is sitting here, drinking beer and telling tales.

This is the main room of the Prancing Pony Inn. A big table dominates the decor, sitting in the middle of the room surrounded by many smaller tables and chairs. Often this is the place to witness hobbits, foreigners, and the inhabitants of Bree talk loudly of the events happening in even the farthest regions of Middle-earth. Those that rest here long enough may catch snatches of conversations about faraway places such as Fornost, Rivendell, Tharbad, the Grey Havens, Moria, and even about the unnamed Shadow that grows in the East.
117612: A fine marble chessboard with ivory and ebony pieces is set here.

A small inner room, more silent than the other sitting rooms of the Prancing Pony Inn, offers some peace and solitude. Four comfortable chairs are set up beside two tables made to play each other in games. Through a window set high in the northern wall, Bree-hill can be seen winding north and west. Noise and smell of food comes in from the east.
117613:
A large sign has been nailed above the entrance to the stables.
A long water trough made of wood stands here.
Bob the hobbit stable-lad is standing here, smiling happily.

Equally tall as the neighbouring inn, the stables of Bree are large enough to house animals of all travellers coming through. Both west and east, eight foot tall stalls for animals cover the entire side. Above each stall a roof holding food, equipment and tools for the trade is stored. South through an almost twenty foot tall opening, a wide stone road can be seen. North lies a separate market for trading animals.
117614: A hobbit shopkeeper stands here, eager to sell you his wares.

A dirt-packed plaza spreads out, housing several stalls and small stables housing animals for sale. Tenders and owners occupy their own, all deals here are made through one broker. On the southern end, a tall opening leads into the Bree stables, and a passing road can be seen north. The fence on the eastern side shows a large sign and an advisory on pets.
117615: With a slight descent going west from the wide bend in the east, the road winds its way past an animal market to the south. Packed dirt makes most of the road, with bits covered in sawdust and rind. Towards the west the road progressively turns more stone and gravel. In the western horizon the Bree-hill spreads out, with peaks and valleys en masse.
117616:
A sturdy target for arrows, made out of thatch, stands here.
A short but well-built hunter is here measuring passersby with quick glances.

Enclosed on the southern and eastern side, with thick logs of standing pine to the south and thinner wood with stone behind to the east. Along the eastern wall, six large targets made from packed straw stand out with their painted red circlular stripes. On the ground, immersed white logs mark out three different distances to the targets.
117617: A warning sign stands to the west.

Turning north and east, the rough road of stone and gravel travels through a dip in the terrain. A steep hill towards the west bars any climb into the Bree hills and sliding track attempts to climb can be seen. The road continues northbound towards a suburb of Bree and east towards the sawmill and the rest of Bree.
117618: A tall wooden sign stands on the eastern side of the path.

As the coarse stone road narrows amply, it passes through an opening in a stone wall. The massive stone wall coming from the east decreases in height, being over ten feet on the east end and like a three foot fence when it carries on west into Bree-hill.
117619: A wide pathway covered in sawdust and rind passes south and east outside four equal timber cabins. The cabins hold temporary lodging for all the woodworkers tending the Bree sawmill when they are not out foresting. The doors are all locked, but a steady stream of smoke rises from all cabins showing their occupancy.
117620:
A water barrel has been left here.
A rather ragtag, dubious-looking man is standing here, trying to sell his wares.

The small and dirty path leads around a few corners and ends in front of three houses. Most windows here are protected by wooden folding shutters, whereas many doors were repaired more than once with thin beams. A few barrels with rusty hoops here are obviously used to collect water that drips from rooftops during rain. The alleyway continues westward.
117621: A large bulletin board, entitled "Thieves' Guild", is mounted here.

Tall stone walls form the perimeter of this wide alleyway. The brick walkway here is unkempt and uneven, forming a tripping hazard for unwary travellers. The alley continues to the east, where it constricts as the buildings draw nearer. A road can be seen to the west.
117622: The stone wall to the west echoes all sounds, down to the most silent whisper. The road is made from large stones stacked together, with dirt and sand supporting them. Looking north, Bree-hill stretches out upwards with several buildings in the far distance. South, the road comes up to a bend.
117623:
A white-painted bench is here.
A timetable for a coach service hangs on the wall.

Stretching fairly straight down south from the Old East Road, this road made from large stones packed together with dirt passes between several houses on either side. A coach timetable hangs on a tall eastern wall. A bench provides rest for tired travellers.
117624:
A wooden sign stands beside the road, with a large painted arrow pointing east.
A thief is waiting here to teach his art.

The stone road bends sharply here, neatly cut between the buildings. To the east, a tall and dark building looms on the street corner, the chattering of loud voices heard within. Slightly downhill to the west lies the city cemetery besides a large wooden building.
117625: A broad and shallow stream slowly moves westward, watering the nearby hedge before disappearing under the western walls. The crystalline water flows over jutting rocks, and cream-coloured sand covers the stream's bottom. The Old East Road heads further into Bree to the north.
117626:
Clint the Dwarf is standing here.
A brook trout is here, swimming in the current.
A brook trout is here, swimming in the current.
A guard of Bree stands here.
A guard of Bree stands here.

A clear pond sits among grass and reeds bordering the Old East Road. The water is deep and calm, and the pond's silty floor is ruffled by darting fish, dashing to safety from onlookers. To the north, the road heads east and west within Bree.
117627:
A small oaken table has been set here.
On the table, there is a fishing rod.
A guard of Bree stands here.

A large dock has been built on pilings reaching over the city fishing spot here, allowing easy access with boat or a fishing rod. On the dock a solid shack has been built, with thick walls facing west and east while open both north and south. Inside, tools for the fishing trade are being kept while a fireplace and a few chairs provide heat and comfort. Clear water laps against the sides of the dock.
117628: A guard of Bree stands here.

The stone road comes to a wider stretch here, and is now a mixture of smaller stones among the large stone blocks. A few blocks seems loose on the northern side, where water seems to have washed away some of the dirt. Just off the road to the north a large dock sticks out over the water. To the south a triangular wall dominates the view and not far west the road comes to and end.
117629: Only four large stones stacked together make the width of the road, a narrow five feet between the building to the north and a stone wall to the south. To the east the road turns northbound where a large dark building dominates the corner. Westwards lies the city cemetery and several buildings.
117630:
An elite Bree guard stands here stoutly.
An old man is walking around, cleaning up.

The large stone blocks come to an abrupt end where the road widens into a dirt packed square. Westwards rises a steep hill where a large green hedge stretches towards the skies. A small cemetery can be seen over a stone fence, and can be accessed though a wooden gate.
117631:
A tall stone sign stands here at a slight angle.
A white-painted bench is here.
A tall, stately, dome-topped tree grows here.

The stone road is wide and dusty, and ruts are etched into the stone, cut there over time by wagon wheels and animal hooves. To the north, the road winds toward the heart of the city. To the south, many buildings of different shapes and sizes dot the landscape, where residents of Bree have made their homes.
117632: Long stones have been embedded in the dirt here reminiscent of a cobblestone road, though less sophisticated. A low wooden rail about a foot high flanks the street on either side. The houses here seem to be all made from rough wooden boards discoloured from the winds and rain.
117633: A well-crafted stretch of stone road stretches north and south here. Each stone has been carefully cut, leaving only enough room for a few small weeds to peek through the gaps. A small dirt path follows the road on either side, evidently trod down by those not wishing to be run over by wagons and carriages.
117634: This road is paved with finely cut blocks of grey stone. Shallow trenches. been dug a few inches deep on either side of the thoroughfare to allow the storm water to flow away without damaging the street. Some of the slabs are covered with patches of thick, green moss.
117635: An old man is walking around, cleaning up.

Moss covers most of the rocks lining this section of the street. The stone-paved road is cracked and weathered, with small tufts of grass sprouting up in various spots. To the west, a line of hedges can just be seen between the rows of houses.
117636: A guard of Bree stands here.

The road here is built from packed red clay. Wheel tracks have created two ruts in the dirt making the footing uneven. The walls of the houses bordering the street are mostly covered in a deep red moss, giving the whole area a desert feel.
117637: A high wooden fence surrounds a few of the houses here. The foot of the fence is caked with dirt from the road and little bits of greenery can be seen growing on it. The street consists of packed, reddish-brown clay with sprigs of grass poking up all along it.
117638: Large patches of ivy grow along the sides of the narrow lane. The walls of the houses bordering the street have long strings of ivy crawling up them. Some wooden planks have been placed on the ground here and there acting as a solid place to stand if the road turns to mud.
117639: A large fountain, made from grey stone, pours water from its centre.

Well-maintained grass stretches about the plaza around a wide stone dais raised in the centre. The masonry of the dais seems to be fairly rudimentary with many of the stone blocks being of slightly varying dimensions. Houses surrond the plaza to the north, west, and south.
117640: A small black cricket is here, chirping loudly.

The ground here rises and falls gently. A thick layer of grass and small plants dominates the area with small patches of dirt appearing here and there. A small path of bare dirt winds its way between mounds and divots. A small circle of stones surrounds the charred earth of a camp fire.
117641:
A small oaken table has been set here.
On the table, there are two cups.
A water barrel has been left here.
A guard of Bree stands here.

The wooden floorboards here are slightly warped and grimy, and care must be taken not to slip. The air is slightly damp and smells of mildew. Wooden walls frame this room in all directions but west. The ceiling is low and warped like the floorboards, but provides enough height for the guards to gather needed refreshment.
117642:
A stove stands against one wall here.
A small oaken table has been set here.
On the table, there are a mince-pie and two loaves of bread.
A colourful butterfly is fluttering around here.

The inner part of the guards' mess hall is a large kitchen, where food is being prepared for duty-fulfilling men and women. Several long tables are placed with benches for seating and all the benches are covered with grey and black wolf furs. A braided thick rug covers the room in all directions, and the walls are fully covered with red and golden wool drapes.
117643:
A sturdy peg for hanging armour is on the wall.
On the peg, there is a plain cloak.
A weapons rack stands against the wall.
In the rack is a dirk.
A guard of Bree stands here.

Along the northern and western stone wall, shelves and hooks for storing the guards' equipment are spread equally. The guards' ready room, where they can talk freely, play games, and spend a few minutes on break, is solidly built from stone and wood. A rug of thick braided reeds covers almost the entire room to dampen noise and soak up moisture.
117644: The base of the tower guarding the east gate of Bree is made from large stones, stacked up high into the air and reinforced with metal plates and sacks of dirt against the south and east walls. Along the east wall a stone staircase rises into a level above, and west several rooms can be seen, spreading a pleasant aroma of food cooking.
117645: A guard of Bree stands here.

A wide landing in the middle of the stairs leading up spreads out west, a thick wooden floor holding the office where the Bree guards are administered. The southern wall in small maps of Bree and the surrounding areas. Along the eastern wall the stairs lead down towards the east gate and up to the tower arms storage.
117646:
An arrow rack stands upright in the corner.
Standing in the rack are five arrows.
A weapons rack stands against the wall.
In the rack are a backsword and a shortbow.
A guard of Bree stands here.
A guard of Bree stands here.

A solid wooden landing covered with a thick reed rug spreads out from where the stairs from the administrative office come up. Solid metal lockers are placed in lines throughout, holding armour and weapons for the Bree guards. Any new guard arriving for service is equipped here before heading out for their daily station.
117647: About eleven feet in diameter, a round floor with a stone railing allows for a view of the Bree eastern wilderness. Wild animals, travellers and disturbing elements are under constant watch by vigilant guards, allowing a rapid response to any threat. A light wooden hatch, with a solid metal handle, leads down into the tower. Beside the hatch, a hole allows yelling alerts into the towers main rooms.
117648:
A shallow pond is here, tinted green with algae.
A guard of Bree stands here.

A small path to the north connects to a shallow pond here. The dirt surrounding the pond is muddy and slick, and care must be taken not to fall into the water. A stone wall lines the park to the south and a neatly curated hill creates a natural barrier to the west. The northern path connects this pond to a park to the north.
117649: A beer barrel has been left here.

Grimy and dirty, this house stands out in the Bree eastern area. The dark wood walls, covered in grime and dust, sport no painting or ornament. Tiny ridges cover the warped wooden floor, the result of ill upkeep. The windows are similarly grime-covered, and their frames are rotting, crumbling vestiges of once intricate handiwork.
117650: With exits both from the west and north, the armourer's large working area is divided by a path through it. On the northwestern side the tools, benches and anvils are placed, all worn yet well-kept. A large angular desk is placed to the southeast, where armour, cloaks and shields for sale are placed and a few special items are hung for display on the wall. Between the armour a wooden sign with a notice is hung.
117651: The dirt is mostly packed flat, except in a few places where it has been dug into mounds supporting pieces of metal. The metal, some new and fresh and some remnants of armour and weapons, is being sorted and stacked for use. The fletcher, armourer, and weaponsmith of Bree all use the metals from here for their daily work.
117652:
A note is stapled to the counter.
A weaponsmith stands here.

Several large anvils are the first things that catch the eyes when entering, each longer than the smith is tall. The worn metal is gleaming of oil, and in several places, pieces are missing where a hammer hit wrong. Two stone furnaces blaze the room with heat, fuelled by air blowing over coal. A long counter stands across the length of the room, not far from the door, and the weaponsmith displays his wares safely behind it, perhaps fearing theft.
117653:
A small oaken table has been set here.
On the table, there is a pair of tongs.
A brick-lined forge is here, emitting heat and light.

The walls of this brick room are covered in a thick layer of black soot, and the floor is lined with trails of black ash and silver metal bits. The ceiling is high here, allowing ample airflow for the smelting of iron and steel. A shop can be seen to the east.
117654: A skilled fletcher is standing nearby, deftly repairing an arrow.

The long and narrow interior of this house rises almost two stories tall. Long sticks, the straightest the Bree saw can deliver, stand tall along the southern wall. Boxes of arrowheads come straight from the smith to the south, ready to be made into arrows.
117655: A large room opens up, almost square in shape. The walls are all painted in a bright blue colour, contrasting a red wooden floor. Large hooks on the wall display various ropes, most used for construction and building work and some with hooks for climbing. Tools to create ropes lie neatly placed and organised on workbenches.
117656: An elderly herbalist is here, surrounded by a cloud of spice.

About twelve by twelve yards the park stretches, almost flat with round stones parting walkways and patches for growing plants and herbs. The small fields of dirt are nicely tended and watered, growing what is fit for each season. Two small wooden houses stand on the eastern end, smoke is rising from one of them. Near one of the planted patches a sign is placed.
117657: A large grocer is here, waiting to buy or sell some goods.

Baskets and boxes line up on shelves along the southern wall, some of them have a lingering pungent smell. On the northern wall, larger items like sacks, water skins and ropes are on display. The room is narrow with small alcoves on the eastern side, clearly made for sleeping with pillows and covers ready. A yellow note is hanging on both sides of the entrance.
117658: A hobbit baker looks at you calmly, wiping flour from his face with one hand.

Brightly lit and open, divided by long tables made for baking, the room is both tall and wide. Along the northern wall, several furnaces, warmed by blazing hot coals and wood, are ready for finalizing dough into the finest bread and pastries. Placed against the southern wall, underneath a window, a counter shows baked goods for sale with shelves of fresh bread behind it. A small sign with text is on the counter.
117659:
An ancient flat straw hat is lying here.
A large cabinet capable of storing goods is here.
In the cabinet, there are a blackberry tart and an apple tart.
A sturdy bed made from solid oak lies here, covered in warm blankets.

This space is a comfortable tunnel-like hall. Although built into the ground, this hobbit hole shows no signs of the dirty, oozy, muddy dwelling an uncivilised being might abide in. This room shows that many hours of care and work have been spent in order to make the place as comfortable as possible for the owner and his guests. The wooden wall to the south has a small peephole installed in it.
117660:
A sturdy bed made from solid oak lies here, covered in warm blankets.
A small oaken table has been set here.
On the table, there are two pieces of cheese and a cup.

Tall walls to the north and east and a sloping roof down south and west, create an uneven house. The wooden floor has one long side to the north and three shorter equal sides. Large carpets in rich blue and gold colours hang high, matching the curtains on four wide windows. The inner window edges are painted artistically showing flowers and growths from the Bree area.
117661: Bordered by a tall wooden fence on the western side and houses to the east, a park-like yard spreads out. It is almost entirely flat, rare for the Bree area, and the grass, flowers and water features seem well tended. Pathways made from stone slates over white gravel travel outwards from the centre.
117662:
A heavy desk, made of solid oak, stands here.
Araduin, a retired Dunadan ranger stands here, regarding you with piercing eyes.

An enormous white fur is spread out on the floor, being over nine feet from head to tail, and makes up the focal point. A whole row of chairs is stacked four in height along the eastern wall and a large raised patio with a desk is centred at the western wall, clearly a room used for teaching and meetings.
117663: Rising from the Old East Road in the south this road traverses northbound in the hillsides. Even being over ten feet wide it is by no means straight, but winds its way towards some of the official offices of Bree further north. A small valley opening westwards leads into an isolated garden further down.
117664: A sign on top of a tall pole stands to the west.

Almost twelve feet wide, this road naturally follows the hills of Bree. It is made from an almost white gravel, bordered on the sides with larger blocks of the same stone. Eastwards you can see the roof of the Prancing Pony Inn, and a door set between two windows in a hillside. To the west the Mayor of Bree and other official services can be found.
117665: The white gravelled road bordered with white stone blocks flows naturally though Bree-hill, slightly narrowing where it intersects with an entrance to a large grassy park to the east. Up on a hillside to the west the wooden wall of a large house rising up with several ornamented windows is on display.
117666: A large stone sign sits here.

The white road is only seven feet wide passing through a simple yet sturdy timber passage, going south it widens to twice that width. The stones framing the road southbound stop before the passage, allowing the grass to grow close to the gravel. On either side of the road the Bree-hill rises, creating a shaded area. North of the passage the road narrows down to a trail made from white gravel.
117667: A large wooden archway marks the entrance to the Westhill. The weathered cobblestone streets are well-maintained, but starting to show their age. Houses and cottages can be seen dotting the hillside to the north, while the larger buildings of central Bree cover the landscape to the south.
117668: Both south and north, steep hillsides create a tranquil and secluded garden, with a large flat area stretching in all directions. On the southern end of the flat area a large tent has been erected, and rising up to the west a looming tower dominates a nearby hilltop. A small opening between the hillsides leads to a white road in the east.
117669:
A small campfire burns here, its low flames giving off only a little light.
A citizen-mercenary is here, waiting for a job.

While grass is growing, this place is mostly covered in green. Most of the hill is slanting upwards towards the west, before it tips downwards to the Bree training grounds. When used only muffled sounds make it over the top, making the grassy hill silent and restful. Sitting down here allows a pleasant rest, while viewing the busy life of Bree swarm by to the southeast. A few chosen spots have been used often, where flat areas allow for a campfire and eating a picnic. A large house rises to the north, through a small opening a desk can be seen. Heading down east leads to a road in the hills.
117670: The few patches of grass still visible here are struggling with their survival clearly being stepped on and kicked often. Timber and wooden structures make up several training apparatus for the guards and others using this room for their battle readiness. Some are made to climb, others to go under and they seem to be placed in a circle so one could change the training during an exercise. A few large timber man-like figures have deep wounds from swords, spears and axes being slammed into them. A sign reading 'Quartermaster and Warrior Trainer' is pointing west. North, a stone building housing the guards rises and eastwards the path leading into Bree can be seen.
117671:
A small oaken table has been set here.
On the table, there are a piece of paper and a quill pen.
Jack stands on guard here, collecting money.
The quartermaster of the Bree guard is standing here.

Almost being a part of the training grounds, it still somehow manages to be barred from most sounds. Two solid and tall timber walls with a tarped roof being slanted using timber crossbeams allows some cover from both wind and precipitation. A large number of weapons and armour resembling the ones used by the Bree guards can be seen on display, covering most of the two walls.
117672: A large sign on a short pole is here.

Several old campfires can be seen around the hills, where they rise eastwards towards a park for children. Over some hilltops southwards the roof of the Prancing Pony Inn can be seen, the smoke from its chimneys crawl though the bushes growing nearby. In the north hillside a large door with double windows framed by two windows on each side stick out as a special home.
117673:
A long slide has been built into a steep part of the eastern hillside.
A white-painted bench is here.

With rolling hills rising in the north, east and south a natural flat and shaded area is used as a city playground. Between two trees, a solid trunk of dark wood has ropes with large knots hanging, and a long slide has been built into a steep part of the eastern hillside. A few benches sit alongside a patch of fine sand, where children's toys are scattered.
117674: The cobblestones of Westhill Way wind between the northern knolls of Bree here. A few houses have been built on the flatter portions of landscape, while other homes are built directly into the hillside. To the south, the roof of the Prancing Pony is just visible between the hills.
117675: The road narrows here as it passes between a few of the a few closely packed houses, each slightly different than the last. The cobblestone streets are worn, having seen the tread of many a foot over the years. The southwest side of the street is marked by a giant pothole where some wagons have attempted to cut the corner a few too many times.
117676: This portion of Westhill Way is a little worse for wear, evidenced mostly by a large, muddy pothole that mars one side of the road. A small pool of brown water lies in the bottom of the hole, and the grass beside the road has begun to develop deep ruts from wagons forced to detour around the damage.
117677: Westhill Way turns here, leading into the heart of Westhill to the north and back toward Bree proper to the east. A few houses cover the hillside, most of which have carefully trimmed shrubbery lining the footpaths that lead to each front door.
117678: A guard of Bree stands here.

This corner of Westhill Way marks the end of the main throughfare of the south side of Westhill. A few larger homes have been constructed in the hills here, with tall, multi-paned windows displaying a bit of extravagance amid the otherwise utiliarian achitecture that marks much of Bree.
117679: Junction of Westhill Way and North Ridge Avenue

Here, the wide road of Westhill Way joins with the more narrow North Ridge Avenue. Large houses sit on each corner, with well-manicured, grassy lawns. Each has a well-cut wooden fence marking the edge of each yard.
117680:
A weapons rack stands against the wall.
In the rack are a shortbow and a shortsword.
A large painting of the Mayor hangs on the western wall.

The manicured stone ground is free from imperfections and bumps, and provides a safe ground for practicing by the warrior guild members. Tall stone walls provide cover from wind, and a drain in the yard centre provides a spot for rain water to collect.
117681:
A small oaken table has been set here.
On the table, there is a cup.
A sturdy bed made from solid oak lies here, covered in warm blankets.

Only the four small windows near the top of the eastern and western stone wall allow any natural light inside, while several torches hanging on the walls give it a feeling of evening even during the day. Even the ceiling and the floor are made from the same stone, the ceiling with a dome-shaped arch to support its weight.
117682:
A large bulletin board, entitled "Legendhomes", is mounted here.
A heavy desk, made of solid oak, stands here.
A humble man stands here, ready to help you with your things.

A northern wall in grey stone is contrasting the rest of this large office, where all other walls are made from finely cut wooden planks painted brightly yellow. Windows on three sides make it naturally lit while its day, through the western window a fishing dock can be observed.
117683:
A mercenary-guard is on sentry here.
A mercenary-guard is on sentry here.
A thief is waiting here to teach his art.
An old man is walking around, cleaning up.

In a drastic contrast to the dark exterior of this house, the inside is bright both in colour and lighting. The windows have all been nailed shut from the inside, with only suspended oil lanterns creating the light. A wide wooden ladder leads up to a loft above, and a sign points down towards a gambling room though a wooden cellarhatch.
117684:
A simple wooden chest is here.
A large stone fireplace with a roaring fire warms the room.
A painting of three dwarves hangs on the wall.

This simple room is walled with thick slabs of pine, and the rafters of its sloped roof are exposed, giving the room a rustic feel. The floorboars are similarly composed of pine, and are wide, smooth and without dimples or ridges. The austere abode is heated warmly by a fireplace.
117685:
A small oaken table has been set here.
On the table, there are three loaves of bread, two pieces of cheese, and a cup.
A beggar is here, asking for a few coins.

A damp floor of packed dirt holds several cots and bunk beds, with grass packed mattresses for sleeping. The walls and roof seem solid, made out of different wood, timber and a few stones - clearly built from leftovers. A few torches throw a dim but dancing light, and a fireplace near the entrance warms anyone living here.
117686: A detached white rose is lying here.

Beneath a steep hill both to the west and south, memorial plaques and stones have been placed, shaded by the Bree hedge growing above. Pathways of white gravel marbled with grey and black pass though the well tended grassy area. In several places, flowers and lights have been put down in someone's memory.
117687: An old man, known as Dolbeth the Seer, is standing here.

Both northern and southern walls are triangular, meeting at a high peak almost twenty feet up. All walls have been coloured green to about a man's height and white to the top. Two massive chandeliers are suspended from the ceiling, with large white candles lighting the room and two solid iron candelabrums on each side of a large desk.
117688: A citizen-mercenary is here, waiting for a job.

This oblong loft space has been decorated like a narrow street, being lit by a lamp that looks like any street-lamp found in Bree. Mannequins representing citizens and other travellers have been equipped with purses, handbags and other resembling items that can be stolen.
117689:
A sign of advice is sitting here on the bar.
A huge and awesome dealer in black leather is here (glowing).

A clear sign of dwarven masonry is seen on several of the stone blocks making up the walls in this cellar, being carved with intricate scenes from battles. The air here is thick with excitement and nervousness. It is not always large amounts of money that are at stake; some people pay their gambling addiction with their lives.
117690:
A small oaken table has been set here.
On the table, there are two turnips and a cabbage.

This house is built with a timber front, clad in large slabs of wood painted brightly green on both the inside and outside. Towards the back the house is dug deep into a hillside, with solid clay covered walls and ceiling. A small kitchen and a stone clad fireplace cover most of the eastern wall.
117691: A heavy desk, made of solid oak, stands here.

Built just inside the Bree west gate, this house stands tall and wide. The roof slopes only northwards, making an impressively tall front towards the Old East Road. Tall black planks cover the outside, while the insides are painted in a pale yellow colour.
117692: A sturdy bed made from solid oak lies here, covered in warm blankets.

Halfway formed as a hobbit hole, with one and a half wall built from leftover planks and timber, this burrow is small and narrow. Half of an old barrel make the foot of a table with an old round door on top. Scattered around the room, several empty bottles lie discarded, two bottles with candles in them seem to be the only light source in the room.
117693: A sturdy bed made from solid oak lies here, covered in warm blankets.

Over fourteen feet in diameter this octagonal tent accommodates all features needed for comfortable living. In the middle of the tent a large open fireplace allows for cooking, the smoke rises slowly through an opening in the ceiling nine feet above the ground. Two timber framed stands hold four hammocks for sleeping, and a giant bear fur has been carefully put on a deep chair.
117694:
A large bulletin board, entitled "Mages' Guild", is mounted here.
A sorcerer is waiting here to teach his art.
A sparrow is flapping around on the ground.

Built from a foundation of solid stone five feet high and continuing into a timber frame this tower stands high. Through a tall arched opening eastwards a large garden can be seen downhill, and on the eastern wall a solid winding staircase rises twenty feet up towards a platform.
117695: A sparrow is flapping around on the ground.

A platform is formed from the inside of the tower, stretching close to the Bree hedge to the west. The balcony is solidly framed with a railing, walls and a roof stretching overhead. A few hanging potted plants frame the view west, where the intersection between the Old East Road and the Greenway can be seen.
117696: A sturdy bed made from solid oak lies here, covered in warm blankets.

This large one-room, once a smial, has been cleverly rebuilt into a nice home set in the lush Bree-hill. The western wall has two beds built into it, with heavy woollen covers to draw. The roof is high and shaped like a dome, covered with a bright red coloured clay. The entire northeastern corner is displaying tools from a smith, framing a large furnace still able to give off pleasant heat.
117697:
A sturdy bed made from solid oak lies here, covered in warm blankets.
A large stone fireplace with a roaring fire warms the room.
A small oaken table has been set here.
On the table, there are two apple tarts and a straw hat.
Mr. Mugwort, a busy but friendly hobbit stands here.

Two rooms with an open hallway between them form this cosy hobbit home in Bree-hill. All the walls have been covered with a dimmed pink colour, framed by green-painted timber. The same green colour is on the round door and the window frames. A large painting is hanging over a deeply inset fireplace. Smoke from the fire is flowing out through a wide chimney.
117698:
A large bulletin board, entitled "Warriors' Guild", is mounted here.
A weapons rack stands against the wall.
In the rack is a dagger.
A small loyal dog is here.
Gathrain, a retired Bree guard, lives here, looking for pupils to train.

Only one extra wall is built to house the teaching grounds of Bree. Being set in a corner with the Bree barracks and jail both east and north, large stone walls enclose this yard on three sides. The western wall is not nearly as tall as the other two, only being about six feet. Beyond the western wall the taller green hedge of Bree can be easily seen, quite a few branches even climb into this yard.
117699:
A water basin made of fine oak is here.
A Guard of Bree stands here, waiting in the headquarters.
A Guard of Bree stands here, waiting in the headquarters.
A Guard of Bree stands here, waiting in the headquarters.

Built from stacked stones and isolated with large sacks of packed dirt, this room dampens the noise from the busy training grounds outside. A large number of chairs surround two large tables, allowing the Bree city guards a retreat from the daily rotation. A kitchen with utensils and cups is placed along the eastern wall, with a large basin of water for cleaning easily available for cleaning. Through an opening in the stone wall north, an office can be spotted and southwards through an oblique opening the training grounds can be reached.
117700:
A heavy desk, made of solid oak, stands here.
The Chief Guard is looking very upset.
A cityguard stands here, looking very upset.
A cityguard stands here, looking very upset.
A cityguard stands here, looking very upset.
A cityguard stands here, looking very upset.

The centrepiece of this office is a large desk, made from an elaborate timber structure. It spans over twelve feet and could easily fit several but only one man sits at the desk. All visitors are pointed to the bench along the eastern wall, under a large shelf holding several leather bound books. Several weapons confiscated from criminals are stacked in a corner, under constant watch from the guards. The office opens southwards through a stone opening into the guards' barracks, and a heavy iron gate bars the way into the prison west.
117701:
A bulletin board with a poster titled "Citizenship Information" is hanging here.
A mailbox stands here stuffed full of messages.
A secretary is sitting at the desk.
The lamp-lighter is resting here.

This is a long and narrow, yet tall room, built with standing flat planks on the walls, floor and ceiling. The floor and walls are painted in a bright ochre colour, with dark green patterns forming trees and a hedge around the room. A large sign labelled 'Bounty' is hung between the windows on the eastern wall, alongside a big poster reading 'Citizenship Information'. Outside the office's south entrance, a large park spreads out, and north another office can be seen.
117702:
A heavy desk, made of solid oak, stands here.
A metal plaque with a note is placed on a wooden desk.
The Mayor is sitting in his huge chair, snoring loudly.
An elite Bree guard stands here stoutly.

Three of the walls here are plain dark ochre-coloured, with the northern wall featuring a red-painted pattern. A large stack of books in one corner supports a ladder. The room's centrepiece is a gigantic four-armed cross hanging from the ceiling, holding torches that light the room.
117703:
A wooden rocking horse is here.
A mercenary-guard is on sentry here.
A mercenary-guard is on sentry here.
A ranger stands quietly here, willing to teach his knowledge of woodcraft.
An old man is walking around, cleaning up.

Over twenty feet wide a wooden roof covered in stone shingles covers the entire training yard. A wooden horse meant to teach children riding, large plaques of animals tracks and a wooden wall with attached metal spikes for climbing are spread out, all made to teach wilderness skills. Some solid tents for living are standing along the eastern wall.
117704: A master tanner is here, shaping a piece of leather.

A large open room with smaller compartments along the southern and northern walls spreads out, with tools for the fur handling trade on benches and tables. The compartments along the northern wall seem to be used for tanning and shaping furs, while the southern ones are for coarser work like preservation, salting, and unhairing. Suspended from the ceiling hangs a large skin, with red letters on it like a sign.
117705:
A simple wooden chair sits here.
A sturdy bed made from solid oak lies here, covered in warm blankets.

Beautifully erected with white timber covered with dark brown planks on the outside, this house is completely square in any direction. The white timber creates a double cross on each wall, and a more intricate pattern of triangles in the ceiling. A large open fireplace with a chimney is placed on the northern wall, the chimney holds four large lanterns which light the room.
117706: Over forty yards long, the roof over the saw is supported by logs every two yards, each wide and solid and over four yards tall. Built as a larger copy of the Old Mill in Hobbiton, yet here the water is used to power a saw. Studs and planks for the Bree builders are being produced by sawyers daily.
117707: Statues carved from wood stand tall in the shapes of wild horses dotting the street. The flat, grassy road is bordered on either side by wooden planks laid down neatly lengthwise. Wheel tracks can be seen having crushed the grass flat going north and south.
117708: The road here is composed of grayish white gravel with bits of red dirt leaking out here and there. On either side of the road, rough wooden houses tower above, their thatched roofs glistening with a hint of gold. A few fruit trees grow in front of some of those houses.
117709: A colourful butterfly is fluttering around here.

A thick carpet of grass has broken free from its horizontal prison and begun a desperate escape up the slightly sloped walls of the houses here. Gravel has been kicked up here and there on the road and wooden planks have been placed over a deep gash in the centre of the street.
117710: A guard of Bree stands here.

Sludge-like mud has been splashed on some dark grey stones bordering the sides of the lane. A trail of low bushes streaks along the centre of the street, unscathed by the crushing, grinding wheels that have left indents in the mud.
117711: A humongous oak tree stands proudly in the middle of the intersection.

Two large trees stand in the centre of the dirt road, their trunks acting as a divide for passersby. The road itself is made up of a red, almost claylike dirt. Looking closely there is a statue of a man standing between the two trees. He is short and grey, and seems to be resting on a walking stick.
117712: The houses on this street all have decorative symbols burnt into their wooden doors. Each is done with care, evidently the work of some local artisan. The cobblestone street worn smooth, with and the East Road can just be glimpsed between the buildings to the east.
117713: A woman is here, looking for someone to chat with.

The tall oaks that give this street its name line the road on either side. A few of these have faint figures carved into the bark, some with a few jagged initials under the figures. The road itself is made from gravel packed with earth and mud.
117714:
A small loyal dog is here.
A guard of Bree stands here.
A colourful butterfly is fluttering around here.

The houses bordering the street seem to be rather low, featuring round doors and windows. The doors are painted bright colours presenting a cosy appearance. Most of these houses sport small patches of dirt in front of them, most likely used for gardening.
117716: A humble man stands here, ready to help you with your things.

This private beauty salon is an establishment that offers a variety of cosmetic treatments and cosmetic services for male or female of small stature such as dwarves and hobbits.
