A cook is standing here, busy with her pots and pans.

Wooden tables and benches line the perimeter of this mess hall. In the centre sits a simple serving table. Dried crimson forms a patchwork of stains across the tables, and the meatless bones of mutton and sheep lie scattered about the floor. On the serving table sits a neat stack of wooden plates, forks, and spoons. Two hanging oil lamps provide shaky light to the room. A dirt path starts to the west.
117933:
A small oaken table has been set here.
On the table, there are a beer mug, a dented pail, and a large barrel.
A stained wooden bench sits here in the mud.
A dirty ruffian draped in rags advances towards you.
A furtive footpad is here waiting for his prey.

Faded tan leather forms the walls of this room, and light from the sun and stars stream through ripped patches of ceiling in this simple watering hole. Small discarded bones are embedded in the dirt floor. A deep well opens in the corner, the mud deep around it.
117934: Vegetation here is sparse with heavy use of the trail. An open-air tent used as crude barracks sits among tumbled ruins to the west. The trail becomes more obscured to the south, as shrubs and tall grass compete for sunlight, and continues north and south.
117935: The landscape rises to the north and south, creating a natural path in this small valley. Short and angled grass in the path here indicates moderate use. Thick roots run parallel to the ground, and small shoots struggle to survive the onslaught of constant foot traffic.
117938: The branching path here is faint amidst the thick vegetation. To the north and east, the path continues amongst the hills. To the south, a hitching post is fastened to a large boulder. The branches of an ancient oak reach overhead from the east, providing a small amount of respite from the sun, rain, and wind. The ground here is covered with the fall leavings from the tree.
117942:
A long water trough made of wood stands here.
A sturdy pack horse is standing here.

A place of equine respite and watering is fastened by leather straps and a metal anchor to a large rock on the western hillside here. Muddy ground surrounds a wooden water trowel under the hitching post. Hoof prints and animal hair are embedded within the watery ground. Large stone formations and a large black tent prohibit further travel east, and the path becomes less descript to the south.
117943:
A large boulder sits in the middle of the path.
A mass of dark green leaves clings to a wall.

The dense foliage here partially obscures a dirt path that leads north and east. To the south a decaying tower sits atop a small hill, its cracked columns decorated with centuries of ivy and moss growth. The top of the tower has partially collapsed, leaving a ragged gash in the stonework.
117944: A fortified tent sits amidst crumbling rocky ruins to the north. Large boulders surround the tent's black leather walls, forming a primitive sort of protection from the elements and adversaries. The east-west path here is partially obscured by dense undergrowth. Thick branches of a tall oak sway in the breeze overhead.
117945: An obscured trail continues here east and west. Thick roots peek up from the ground, only to quickly disappear again into the underbrush. A tall tent, covered in a carpet of thorns as a primitive warning to outsiders, sits to the north. A rocky hill rises from the valley to the south.
117946: A small cluster of purplish-pink flowers lies here.

The hills surrounding this small valley guide an overgrown path west and northward. Thick shrubs and tall grass obscure the winding path below. Patches of aeglos, heather, and iris grow on the hillside to the south. The path continues to the north and west.
117947: A dirty ruffian draped in rags advances towards you.

Simple wooden cots, lined with thick leather and animal hides, line the perimeter of these open-air barracks. The tan leather walls on three sides offer limited protection from the outside elements. A table sits in the centre of the tent, and discarded mugs of ale, rotten pilfered purses, and animal bones litter the dirt floor. Two poles wrapped in black leather provide structural support for the entrance.
117948:
A solid ironbound chest is here.
A small oaken table has been set here.
On the table, there are a map of Fornost and a map of Bree.
A wooden dartboard hangs on the wall.
The chief of smugglers is here, planning his next move.
An experienced husky smuggler is here, conspiring with his cohorts.
An experienced husky smuggler is here, conspiring with his cohorts.
An experienced husky smuggler is here, conspiring with his cohorts.
A wiry smuggler is here, attempting to avoid being seen.

The leather tent's oiled walls glisten in the dim light provided by a large oil lamp. Two leather hammocks on the eastern wall provide a respite from the damp dirt floor below. Directly opposite them is a heavy oak table, adorned with paper maps of the surrounding areas, writings, and drawings.
117949:
A tiny pool of black water lies in a ditch here.
A large torch glows brightly and is firmly attached to the wall.
A skeleton of some humanoid lies in the dust.

Smells of earth and decay permeate this cellar. The mud here is deep and marked by tiny trails, no doubt left by insects and small rodents. The walls look to have been hastily dug, as their angles are not straight. Tiny rivulets of water run from a small hole in the eastern wall, feeding the deep mud.
117950: Large boulders, leaves and broken branches lie scattered on the muddy ground here. Stone spires and a cracked staircase form the decayed skeleton of an ancient tower. The circular staircase winds its way along the tower's perimeter as it heads upward. The aged spires and open roof above offer little protection from the outside elements.
117951: The circular staircase ends here at a small stone landing. The stone roof has been decimated by time, and large portions of it can be seen strewn about the floor below. Ancient vines wind their way lazily up the spires. The walls here rise high above the landing, offering protection from the wind, but blocking the view in all directions. On the landing is a jumbled mix of large boulders, perhaps a ruined staircase to the top of the ramparts.
117952: Low rolling foothills stretch as far as the eye can see, grass blowing golden on the highland. A large bowled brake of cedar trees is the discerning view, it writhes and swirls as the north wind blows over sending aromatic scents about.
117953: Shallow rolling hills spread across the land, covered in tufts of golden grass. Dotting the ground are large granite boulders, grey and imposing, strewn about as if dropped from the sky. The boulders seem formidable, but upon further perusal the northern faces are smooth, worn down by velocious winds.
117954: A big, brown, angry-looking bear is here.

The walls of this cavern, several yards apart, are smoothly cut into the earth, likely the result of rainfall and erosion. Several short tree roots have tunneled their way through the rock, and into the open air of the cave. The floor is composed mostly of packed dirt, and black rock.
117955:
A large, venomous-looking green snake is coiled up here.
A large, venomous-looking green snake is coiled up here.

The dirt walls that form this cramped pit lie only a couple yards from each other, making this hole an unlikely home for large animals. The walls are covered with the ragged, bent stubs of tree roots, and the air is thick with the smell of damp earth. Boulders poke their way from the earth, and several small pubbles lay scattered about the uneven ground.
117956:
A brown bear is sleeping here.
A brown bear is sleeping here.
A brown bear is sleeping here.

A low boulder hangs over a large entrance that leads into a rough cave. Inside, the stone walls and ceiling are cragged and dry to the touch. A level floor is covered with a mix of dirt, bark, and leaves, providing a cushioning that gives the den quiet warmth. A slightly musty smell floats about, a display of the beasts that live here.
117957:
A stove stands against one wall here.
A young farmer is here worrying about the weather.

This small farmhouse is simply constructed, with log walls and wood plank floors and a peaked roof with crossbeams. This part of the farmhouse serves as both a kitchen and a living or dining area, with a table and low benches in the centre and a cast iron wood-burning stove set against the southern wall that leads up to a chimney. A large wash basin by the stove sits next to a table and some shelves, which contain jars of flour and sugar and preserved vegetables. To the north an open doorway leads into what appears to be a bedroom, while doors to the east and west lead out of the house.
117958: A sturdy bed made from solid oak lies here, covered in warm blankets.

This small bedroom in the farmhouse has wood slat floors and log walls that lead up to a peaked roof with exposed crossbeams. A single window is set in the western wall, looking out over the crop fields maintained by the farm, but otherwise the walls of this room are unadorned. A single narrow bed with a straw mattress sits against the northern wall, next to a washbasin on a small table. To the south an open doorway leads back to the main room of the house.
117960: Well-cultivated fields replete with evidence of skilful farming surround this intersection in the dirt road, which is wide enough for a cart to pass safely. Beyond the fields, an old moss-covered and crumbling stone wall marks the boundary between the cultivated land and the surrounding wilderness. In places where the wall has fallen, a wooden fence has been erected to patch the holes and keep out wildlife. The track continues to the east and south.
117961: To the west, verdant fields overflowing with cultivated crops eventually give way to the wilderness beyond the old stone wall, interrupted only by the well-maintained dirt road that cuts between them. A house has been contructed into the hillside in the north. The house's front door lies to the east. A tidy stone path travails the short distance north from the road to a heavy cellar door. Along the broken stone wall at the farm's eastern boundary, a rough path determinedly trudges south toward a distant pond.
117962: The road ends here near the top of a grassy knoll. Various herbs grow in raised beds on either side of a flagstone path leading to a sturdy wooden door set into a farmhouse to the north. The dirt road, wide enough for a cart, continues back down the slope to the west. To the south and east the terrain drops steeply to the flat fields below.
117963:
A large beautiful rose bush is blooming here.
Deep inside the bush, there is an ivory coloured rose with a tint of crimson.
An apple tree with bright green leaves grows here.
On the tree's branches is a beehive.
A large bee buzzes loudly as it travels from flower to flower.
A large bee buzzes loudly as it travels from flower to flower.
A large bee buzzes loudly as it travels from flower to flower.
A large bee buzzes loudly as it travels from flower to flower.
A large bee buzzes loudly as it travels from flower to flower.

Fruit trees in tidy rows grow here, bordered on the southern and western sides by the quiet ruins of an old stone wall. The dirt road that ends here, wide enough for a cart, runs north through fertile fields toward the entrance to the farm. To the east, the orchard ends and the grasses grow taller. Insects and small animals interrupt the stillness.
117964:
A verdant pond is here, teeming with life.
A goose waddles around here.
A goose waddles around here.
A large bullfrog croaks loudly.

Cultivated fields to the north and west give way first to tall grasses and forbs, and then finally to rushes and reeds along the edge of an old pond. The clear water provides a habitat for insects, amphibians, and water-fowl that can be observed among the algae and the tops of plants growing from the mud. Near the pond, the ground underfoot is soft with water.
117965: Main Room of a Farm House
An old farmer is here, muttering about young folk.

This farm house is framed by great wooden beams and whitewashed walls that are set with wattle and daub. It is very warm and inviting, modestly furnished, and kept tidy by the owners. A small window peeks out into a herb garden and a narrow wooden staircase in the corner leads down to the cellar.
117966:
A wooden shelf has been mounted to the wall.
On the shelf, there is a lantern.

The walls and floor of this rectangular room are made from stone blocks, and great horizontal wooden beams hold up a wooden ceiling. Wooden shelves are mounted on the walls and many items have been stored on them. A narrow wooden staircase leads up to a hatch in the ceiling.
117968: The entrance to this vast cavern is dark and damp. A musty earth smell fills the humid air, making it a little harder to breathe. The walls are moist, and the ground very muddy. In the ceiling, a large hole can be seen with exposed tree roots protruding from the wall.
117969: This tunnel is relatively narrow and small in size, making it feel a little cramped. Sand and earth have settled, sealing what used to be cracks covering the wall. Dark grey stone makes up most of the tunnel, but here and there veins of brighter granite shimmer in the darkness.
117970: Moisture has gathered here, causing droplets of water on the walls and the ceiling of this small tunnel to drip to the floor. Little puddles of dark water have gathered to form in shallow depressions on the floor. A cramped, narrow tunnel leads off into the darkness in the north.
117971: The walls of this small cavern are formed of dense, hard rock. The humid air makes it hard to breathe and causes the rocky walls to shimmer when even the slightest beam of light touches it. Soft sounds of water are carried by a gentle breeze from the west, hinting that there might be a source of water in that direction.
117972:
A brown bear is sleeping here.
A brown bear is sleeping here.

All around the cavern, a soft golden glow is emitted, comparable to that of sunlight in the early hours of daybreak. Hard, crystalline formations grow upwards as if trying to reach the ones that cling from the ceiling. Sounds of water droplets can be heard echoing off the formations. The floor is covered with soft yellow sand that shimmers in the same faint glow as the walls.
117973: You see two canoes on the ground.

Fine sands and small pebbles form a beach. An underground river flows between the eastern and western cave walls to the south. The roar of a waterfall can be heard, along with the sound of rushing water in that direction as well. The water flowing from the south gently pushes against the beach, forming small waves and pushing sediment onto the sand.
117974:
A giant, strange looking green fungus is here, ready to devour you in seconds.
A giant, strange looking green fungus is here, ready to devour you in seconds.

A narrow tunnel leads to an alcove a dozen feet above a mist-covered underground lake. The surface of the lake seems to be quite calm, yet in the distance of this huge cave the sound of violently flowing water can be heard. The condensation on the ceiling above the lake drips down, soaking the cavern ground.
117975:
A roaring waterfall splashes noisily onto the surface of the water.
A fierce-looking eel lurks in the darkness.

A large waterfall gushes down along the western cave wall. It creates a strong southerly current, as well as a slight northerly current. The arched ceiling lowers even more and several protrusions of stone nearly break the water creating small white rapids. Over the years, some rocks have been polished by the current and they split up the stream to create multiple river paths leading south.
117976: A fierce-looking eel lurks in the darkness.

Below the arched ceiling, the underground streams start to flow swiftly to the south. Several parts of the ceiling hang very low and leave little space between them and the water's surface. Many rock formations jut out of the water creating faster, rolling rapids.
117977: The rushing river ends abruptly as it flows out into this large, underground lake. A thin layer of mist covers the surface and water is dripping from the high ceiling. The water seems to be very still and unmoved, but very slight whirls show a current to the south. Near the southern part of the cave, whirls and ripples become clearly visible and indicate a very strong current.
117978: The fast flowing stream moves wildly about. The current becomes very strong in areas and pulls with great force on everything within the water. Sand and stones, caught in the current, rush by and crack loudly as they constantly erode the walls into a smooth texture.
117979: The strong current grabs hold of anything caught in it. Without effort, rocks are carried away by the rushing water. Proceeding against the fast flowing stream seems hard, since the smooth, wet walls offer nearly no handholds at all.
117980: A large boulder blocks the violent current and creates a bay of relatively calm water. The water is not very deep while the ground is quite slippery from algae growing underwater. Nearby there is some sort of small, stony beach. Even the faintest light, created by algae or moss, bounces off the moist surfaces and creates shimmering effects all around.
117981: Strong whirls, caused by the current, have formed here in this narrow underground stream. Both the ceiling and walls are covered in algae which grows wildly in the ever present moisture. The ground has been polished smooth by the force of the water and offer nearly no traction.
117982: The underground stream rushes through a narrow, low tunnel. The current is very strong, and carries away anything that gets caught within it. The walls are covered with some light-shimmering green moss, making for a smooth, slippery surface. The low ceiling is smooth as well, offering no handhold for relief from the turbulent current.
117983: The narrow tunnel has caved in to the west. Boulders and rocks have fallen to block the passage from going any further. The current is still strong as the water flows through vacancies in between these rocks. There seems to be no way to remove the fallen stones and follow the path of the water downstream.
117984:
A huge bat is here, emitting piercing squeaks.
A bloodthirsty bat is sleeping here, hanging from the ceiling.
A bloodthirsty bat is sleeping here, hanging from the ceiling.
A bloodthirsty bat is sleeping here, hanging from the ceiling.

The bank of the river is grey and sandy. A few sharp rocks scattered throughout the bank can be seen sticking from the sand. The cavern measures maybe fifteen feet in length, but is just about four feet deep. A jagged hole can be spotted in the cavern's roof. However, no handholds can be spotted in the rocky walls that would lead upward.
117985:
On the ground, there are five rafts.
A giant, strange looking green fungus is here, ready to devour you in seconds.
A huge black fungus is here, exuding a foul stench.

Numerous stones and boulders of varying sizes and shapes cover the river's bank of hard rock. The walls are covered in a brownish, very wet slime while long patches of algae or green fungi hang from the ceiling. The ceiling is formed from jagged rock, dripping with condensation that has collected on its surface.
117986: This field occupies the land between the town of Bree and a well-travelled trail to the south. Bree-hill dominates the northern horizon, surrounded by an enormous hedge behind a deeply-dug dike. To the east, the outskirts of the Chetwood forest appear on the southern edge of Old East Road, though the path in that direction is blocked by a tangle of thorny bushes and large boulders.
117987: A faint trail meanders through tall grasses, parts of it overgrown with tufted weeds whose slender stems move with the breath of the wind. The surrounding plain is not cultivated though faint, uniform ruts in the ground indicate that it might once have been.
117988: An old cobbled path twists and turns through old fields, with broken stone walls lining either side. The sides of the walls are collapsed, with large stones strewn about, causing the cobbled path to become treacherous. Causes of the destruction could be from the numerous fallen trees that lie over the path.
117989: The trees of the Chetwood forest seem younger compared to north of here where they grow thick and tall. Beyond the faded trail underfoot, the terrain changes into rolling plains of grassland to the south, interrupted only by a few shrubs. An occasional call of a hunting wolf or the chirps of birds breaks the silence of this field and the lands nearby.
117990:
A grey wolf is here, salivating profusely.
A grey wolf is here, thin from starvation.

There is little to be seen here other than the plains and grasslands that stretch into the distance. An ill-defined trail extends from east to west, though it's not always easy to make out its path. To the north, the trees of the Chetwood stand together in silent ranks, reaching to the sky. Downs to the south prevent travel that way.
117991: A large pile of boulders is sitting here, probably debris from a rockslide.

The trail coming from the west ends abruptly here. To the east, massive piles of rock and hard earth slope inward from the cliffs on either side. On the northern end, loops and knots made of woven plant fiber peek out from the debris and splintered slats of wood lay scattered across the rubble.
117992:
A coloured game bird is visible in the vegetation, watching you warily.
A grey wolf is here, salivating profusely.
A grey wolf is here, thin from starvation.

Grass and small bushes grow in abundance here close to the village of Bree. The tall trees of the Chetwood forest can be seen far to the north, beyond the rundown path that stretches east and west. A much smaller forest lies to the south, with many kinds of trees mixed together and large, thorny bushes inhibiting any travel into it from this direction.
117993: This grassy area is the top of a large down, and a steep escarpment makes travel to the south impossible. The northern side of the down slopes toward a well-travelled trail, beyond which a wide field spreads along the base of Bree-hill. A bend in the Greenway can be seen curving away from the southern base of this down, bordered on one side by light forest.
117994: A circular stone well has been built here.

The remains of an old barn lie strewn about. The walls have long fallen down, and heavy timber frames now lie on the ground covered in moss. An old well lies broken in the centre with the stone walls having caved in. Patches of flowers are all that remain to give life to the abandoned farm.
117995:
A grey wolf is here, salivating profusely.
A grey wolf is here, thin from starvation.

The landscape is dotted with flowery grasses and small, prickly plants that continue north toward Chetwood Forest. On a clear day, the wood can be seen on the far horizon. The ground is covered with mounds and holes made by small, burrowing animals who have taken the land as their home. The path to the east is blocked by a precipitous and eroding rock.
117996: The grasses and shrubbery that inhabit these fields stretch out to the east until they are abruptly stopped by a cliff in the distance. Rocks jut out here and there, dotting the landscape with their massive forms. A small impenetrable forest lies to the south.
117997: Several towering ash trees are lightly distributed across the landscape. To the east, the ground rises quickly, becoming a sea of rolling hills lapping at the sky in the far distance. To the west, dense clusters of shrubs and bushes crowd the edges of a small but thick wood.
117998:
A grey wolf is here, salivating profusely.
A grey wolf is here, thin from starvation.

Grassy downs roll up and down in all directions, some creating steep cliffs, others flattening out smoothly into valleys and plains. Grass and small shrubs grow in abundance amid the rocks that dot the landscape. A small, rock-strewn path winds its way precariously upwards toward a higher plateau on the downs, possibly offering a better vantage point of the surroundings.
117999: A large eagle soars above you.

The terrain here is rocky with some smaller patches of grass mixed in. Passage west is stopped by a sheer cliff that drops down toward a field, its edge crumbling like the corners of a stale biscuit. A valley is formed by a downward slope to the east where a small glint of flowing water can be seen.
118000:
A clear spring babbles as cool water trickles out of the ground.
A small cluster of clover grows here.
Yellow flowers, with grey-green foliage, grow in clusters here.
A fat carp swims here.
A heron is stalking the area, looking for fish.

A narrow valley tucked among the rockier topography of the neighbouring downs to the west and east is filled with a variety of plant life. The field is littered with debris, mostly broken cobblestones of various sizes. A little spring supplies fresh water to thirsty animals and travellers.
118001: A small brown snake is slithering around here.

Rolling hills rise above the Chetwood forest to the north, and a steep but not tall slope leads to that forest. To the west, a small and poorly maintained trail ends in an abrupt fall over a cliffside to the fields below, prohibiting travel in that direction.
118002: The trail continues through the forest to the north. Eventually, it gives way to rocks standing amidst the grass and shrubs of the Downs as the land rises toward here. Beyond the path, a road can be seen making its way through the forest, most likely the Old East Road, leading to Bree in the west and toward Weathertop far to the east.
118003:
A sturdy pack horse is standing here.
A domesticated pony, beast of burden to many, stands here.
A squirrel scampers around here, looking for nuts from the trees.
A rabid rabbit is here, frothing at the mouth.

The southern end of the Chetwood forest continues west and east with the Old East Road cutting through it to the north. The forest gives way to grass-covered downs to the south. A small, modest home lies to the north.
118004:
A grey wolf is here, salivating profusely.
A squirrel scampers around here, looking for nuts from the trees.
A squirrel scampers around here, looking for nuts from the trees.

The trees grow thick and tight together, their branches intertwining overhead. The Old East Road can be seen to the north, and a careful navigation through the tree trunks could grant access to the thoroughfare. To the south, a field can be seen below some rolling hills to the southeast.
118005:
A brown pond between old branches and roots is here.
A buck runs swiftly from place to place, looking about warily as it grazes.
A green frog is here, hopping around.
A large elk is standing here, chewing grass and leaves.

The surrounding forest is fairly dense, but some light permeates the canopy from the north where the Old East Road cuts through Chetwood. To the south, the trees disappear and give way to plains and then the Downs farther in the distance.
118006: A light forest borders the Old East Road which lies just beyond a dense hedgerow in the north. Maples and alders grow somewhat spaced apart here on the outskirts of the forest but crowd more closely together in the east and south.
118007:
On the ground, there are two stout barrels.
A curved horn lies on the ground.

This is a sturdy wooden house, obviously built for and by a master lumberjack. It is small, modestly decorated, and impeccably tidy. A fireplace and shelves line the northern wall, and a small, neatly made bed rests under a picture window to the west.
118008: A buck runs swiftly from place to place, looking about warily as it grazes.

Tall trees grow fairly dense here in this part of the Chetwood forest. Fallen trunks block most off-path travel, and dense branches obscure the way to the Old East Road to the north. The only path extends east and west, deeper into the wood or out into an open field.
118009: A small black cricket is here, chirping loudly.

The trail winds through the grass and little bushes that thrive here. The air is filled with the delicious aroma of life, as insects buzz around, emboldened by their vast numbers. Tall trees obscure the view to the west, where the trail appears to vanish. To the north, the Old East Road is hidden behind an impenetrable hedge.
118010: Fields along the Old East Road

A fallow deer is grazing peacefully here.
A colourful butterfly is fluttering around here.
A roe deer is standing here, watching the terrain while chewing the vegetation.
A restless rabbit bounces around.

From here, the trail runs through a grassy field to the west and east. A thick hedge blocks the trail to the north, allowing only the small critters that can scamper beneath it to pass. The fields become more rough and sloping to the south.
118011: Fields along the Old East Road
A roe deer is standing here, watching the terrain while chewing the vegetation.

The trail running through this field has seen more interesting days when it was travelled often. The fields stretch out a few miles to the south, west, and east, mostly inhabited by grasses and small bushes. North of here, a long hedge disappears off into the west and east as it runs beside the trail.
118012: A brown fox is here, looking for some rabbits to chew up.

Directly to the north, an impenetrable hedge blocks all progress. On this side of the hedge, a small trail winds its way among the low rolling hills, running parallel to the line of bushes and presumably mirroring the Old East Road beyond.
118013: Scrub and high-growing grass dominate this field. To the west and east, the land has been eroded by the elements and passage of time, turning it into a series of downs, with the field occupying the valley between the two. To the northwest, several large boulders tower above the fields.
118014: A small grove of birch trees grows here in the fields, possibly leftover from the Chetwood before it retreated to the north and left this area to the shrubs and bushes. The trees are spread out enough that they do not form a real forest or block the sun much. Grass-covered rolling downs stretch out to the west.
118015:
A large, venomous-looking green snake is coiled up here.
A large, venomous-looking green snake is coiled up here.

The ground is covered with low shrubs and bushes. The monotony is broken only by towering boulders which block the way to the west. Far to the north, a thin line of what might be a road makes its way between a hedge and the Chetwood forest farther on. A small trail lies on this side of the hedge.
118016:
A reddish-brown shrub with purplish-pink flowers grows here.
Inside the shrub, there are two clusters of purplish-pink flowers.
A diamond-back rattlesnake is coiled here, ready to strike.

The hillside falls away steeply from this small down in most directions, making travel impossible except back to the east. The ground is covered with rocks and tough shrubs that have found a place to take root in the soft soil.
118017:
Some small rocks have been piled into a mound here.
A restless rabbit bounces around.
A fallow deer is grazing peacefully here.

The fields start to slope slightly upwards as they come closer to the Downs in the west. The terrain there is rockier and the grasses and shrubs grow more sparsely. An occasional winged insect buzzes by on its way to fulfil some unknown mission.
118018:
A waist-high evergreen shrub grows here, with thick, reaching branches.
A large pile of boulders is sitting here, probably debris from a rockslide.

The grasslands are flat and dotted with small and medium-sized boulders of various forms. The grass is lush and green, with bits of bush sprinkled about. The path is blocked by a short but steep plunge into the plains below. The top of the Down reaches north and south.
118019:
A reddish-brown shrub with purplish-pink flowers grows here.
Inside the shrub, there are two clusters of purplish-pink flowers.
A large, venomous-looking green snake is coiled up here.
A large, venomous-looking green snake is coiled up here.
A small black cricket is here, chirping loudly.
A colourful butterfly is fluttering around here.

This wide area is beneath the cliff to the east and lies above several Downs lower to the west. However, the sharp rocks along the edges, which are such a contrast to this mainly grass-covered spot, prevent further travel to the lands below. There seems to be no way to move but back up to the hilltop above. Small rocks lie here ready to be kicked over the side.
118020:
A reddish-brown shrub with purplish-pink flowers grows here.
Inside the shrub, there are two clusters of purplish-pink flowers.
A black bear is sleeping here.

This is the highest point of the nearby Downs and the land to the west spreads out below. The western edge is crumbling somewhat except along a small section which allows travel downwards to another level of the downs. To the north lies a crumbling, rocky slope that prevents travel toward the forest. A large patch of thorny shrubs prevents travel eastwards.
118021: A roe deer is standing here, watching the terrain while chewing the vegetation.

The fields narrow down to a pathway no more than a dozen feet wide with towering boulders blocking the view to the east and thorny shrubs blocking any travel to the west. To the north, small bushes dot the landscape of grassy plains.
118022:
A restless rabbit bounces around.
A colourful butterfly is fluttering around here.

Rich vegetation composed of myriad bushes, shrubs, and grasses grows here, ending abruptly to the east. There, the chalk hillside rises steeply and makes passage impossible. To the west, the Downs rise slowly as the uphill terrain gets more rugged. Southwards the land eases out into wide fields.
118023:
A shrub with maple-like leaves is growing here.
On the shrub, there are a handful of blackcurrant berries.
A colony of red ants is here. The ants seem to ignore you.

Towering hillsides, rocky and treacherous, block travel to the east and north. Taller downs peek above their harsh slopes, rising toward the heavens above. To the west, the ground flows downhill on a slope, opening up into a valley below.
118024:
A large eagle soars above you.
A large eagle soars above you.

The earth drops away to the east into a grassy valley among the Downs, while a precipitous drop to the west makes passage nearly impossible. There is an infrequently used track that leads down and cuts back a few times to make the descent easier.
118026: A Terrace on the Side of the Down
A rock lizard is here, motionless as it observes you.

The wide area is beneath the cliff to the east and lies above several downs lower to the west. However, the sharp rocks along the edges, which are such a contrast to this mainly grass-covered spot, prevent further travel to the lands below. There seems to be no way to move but back up to the hilltop above. There is also a small opening in the cliff-wall to the east.
118027: Deep, Damp Cave in a Hillside

A giant, strange looking green fungus is here, ready to devour you in seconds.
A giant, strange looking green fungus is here, ready to devour you in seconds.

This small, cramped cave has been naturally cut into the side of the hill outside over the slow passage of time. The ceiling and walls are damp and slimy. There are large rocks scattered about, covered in fungus and lichen. The atmosphere is humid and musty.
118028:
A large sack is on the ground.
A small oaken table has been set here.
A sturdy crate made of nailed wooden planks sits on the floor.
A swarthy, little bandit advances forward.

A long, narrow room has been built into the chalk of the cliff. It is not more than eight feet at the widest, but stretches back more than thirty. The walls are smooth and unblemished. There is a messy mixture of boxes, sacks, cupboards and other furniture around the room. A sturdy door is located on the western wall.
118029: An large mighty oak tree grows surrounded by thick brushwood. It's trunk is light green with various mosses growing up its length. The ground surrounding it is muddy, with dense brushwood seemingly falling down into the depths of the ground, slowly being eaten up by the earth.
118030: Dense young trees grow tightly together, their narrow trunks shooting straight up into the sky, each vying to get as much sunlight as possible. The ground is littered with debris, branches lying on top of each other several inches thick, interspersed with dead and dying vegetation.
118031: Ancient trees dot the landscape, their massive branches dripping with emerald foliage. Underneath each tree are bushes with short thorny branches that appear to defend the tree from anything substantial approaching without being scratched.
118032: Bushes grow densely throughout the area, making it difficult to move; their branches sharp and prickly. Weeds grow wherever they are able, taking advantage to the slightest opening throughout the bushes. The scent of pollen is heavy in the air.
118033: The high grass continues in all directions. Occasionally, patches of rocks and stones can be seen. In some places, the soil is so devoid of nutrients that only the sparsest of grasses and only a few low and brown plants are able to take root. Dry, prickly weeds seem to be the only plants that flourish on the rocky outcrops.
118034:
An apple tree with bright green leaves grows here.
On the tree's branches are three apples.

Tall grass grows all around, rustling with the slight breezes that blow across the plain from time to time. Nothing blocks the view to the horizon in any direction. Sometimes, small formations break the monotony of the plains and add some contrast to the vast grassy sea.
118035: The Old East Road looks as if it has been in use for many ages past. The hard stones are very worn, yet they long strong enough to withstand many ages to come. In some places, a stone is cracked right through the middle. However, most of the stones are well intact.
118036: The passage of thousands of travellers has polished the inner tracks of this ancient road. The borders however have started to break down into the surrounding turf. In the very centre of the path only a few cracks are present testifying to the craftsmanship.
118037: The old road becomes a bit narrower as it leads around a small depression then widens again behind it. The surface of the road is made of dark stones cut into squares. Between the sharp edges of the stones, thin bits of grass grow in the cracks.
118038: A colourful butterfly is fluttering around here.

The Old East Road leads through the mostly flat landscape. At the road's edges, nature starts to take back what was taken a long time ago. Bushes, tall grass and trees stand along the endless line of paved stones which form the road and which lie here for more years than are to count.
118039: Running almost perfectly straight for miles, the Old East Road seems to be more a drawn line than something that has been built. The ancient trees lining the road make it appear to be more an avenue of kings rather than a travellers road through the wilderness.
118041: Small tufts of yellow grass grows close to the ground, never reaching but a few inches off of the ground. Spiky bushes dot the landscape, their branches sparsely covered in dried leaves. The ground is dry and dusty between the meagre plants.
118042: All around, high bushes in shades of light red hinder the view. The stems of the plants are slender and the leaves quite evenly spread. In some areas patches of green, thorny bushes struggle to take root in between the other plants.
118043: The ground is incredibly compacted, from the markings of hooved animals. Their grazing creating vast meandering trails throughout the grasslands. The bushes have lost all of their leaves; only the trees with their high branches still have any leaves available.
118044: The plain is covered with low bushes. Many of these plants have slender branches with green and yellow leaves, which look similar to a three-fingered hand. Only the occasional trees rise above those bushes. From time to time, a bush with leaves red as the setting sun adds a few bright spots of colour.
118045: Sparse woody vines cover parts of the nearby lush green fields. The vines grow most densely around what was once a building but is now fully decayed beneath the vines, providing an ideal nesting spot for the local fauna. Smaller parts of the vines appear to be constantly moving about, looking for a new location to grow.
118046: Rocky hills rise from the otherwise fertile surroundings. The eastern slope of the largest hill seems to have collapsed in a landslide, creating a rocky and impassable wall at the base of it. Small patches of green grass sprout up where it can find space between rocks.
118047: Boulders of all sorts and sizes dot the landscape. Some lie together in large piles, piling on top of each other, others seem thrown randomly around the area without any discernible order. Yellowish grass grows smoothly between the rocks, the colour changing to a dull brown around each rock.
118048:
A large, venomous-looking green snake is coiled up here.
A large, venomous-looking green snake is coiled up here.

Seemingly without end, the grasses and low bushes covering the plain stretch out in all directions. Many mounds and holes dot the landscape, dug by small, burrowing animals who have claimed the land as their homes. A dense patch of brush sits on the western horizon.
118049: A colourful butterfly is fluttering around here.

Low shrubs and brush are sparse but plentiful. Dead and dying vegetation lie low to the ground beneath it. Low hills can be seen on the horizon in most directions. To the south, a large patch of rocks and boulders seem to outline the entrance to a cave in the hillside.
118051:
A reddish-brown shrub with purplish-pink flowers grows here.
Inside the shrub, there are two clusters of purplish-pink flowers.
A boar cub is playing here, and exploring the wide world.
A huge, black wolf is here, ready to devour.

The grassy downs rise gradually from the dense brush in the north and continue to roll out of view to the south and west. The grass is green and lush, with scattered patches of small trees and thick brush in some low-lying areas. Animal paths have been blazed into the ground where passage is the least cumbersome.
118052: A small evergreen plant grows here, its woody stems reaching two feet.

Low hills rise above dense brush in the north and west. The hills are carpeted with a dense, lush, green grass. Earthen paths are blazed into the ground where animals and other passengers have travelled. Small, scattered patches of rocks lie here and there throughout the hills.
118053: A huge, black wolf is here, ready to devour.

Thick briars and brambles form an impassable wall of brush to the north. The ground here is deplete of anything alive, covered only in dead vegetation or bare earth. Large trees grow here sporadically about, some close enough to each other that their branches wrap around each other.
118054: The even soil is covered with many fallen and half rotten trees; over them the brushwood grows dense and repairs the damage the falling trees caused to the lower vegetation. It nearly seems a small forest has withered and died to make space for some other kind of vegetation. Many of the bushes, vines, and thorny scrubs prospering here seem to have grown just within the last few years.
118055: The brush is thin and mostly bare here, but it grows thicker to the north. The land stretches between the dense brush and gradually rises to the west into rolling, grassy downs. Animal tracks can be spotted intermittently among the bare, earthen patches in the ground.
118056: Countless animals have beaten a path through the brushwood. In places it becomes so narrow and low that the branches of the bushes on both sides have met and ensnared each other. Many of the vegetation's lower leaves have been nibbled off by grazing animals.
118057: A large brown snake with black patches is coiled here.

Thick brushwood and a few groups of trees grow on this plain, hiding the soil from view in most places. Many trace signs of animals can be seen here as marks of digging, nibbled leaves, stems and trunks, piles of droppings, and the occasional animal-path through the brushwood.
118058: A lush green carpet of dense grass covers the hills. Low hills roll in all directions, mostly grassy but with a few rocky patches scattered about. A small patch of dense brush and small trees grow in a low area, offering a suitable shelter for whatever wildlife might inhabit the area.
118059:
A grey wolf is here, salivating profusely.
A grey wolf is here, thin from starvation.

The surrounding plains rise gradually into some rolling downs. The lush green grass carpets the hills in a thick, soft blanket. The hills provide a vantage point of the surrounding plains and brush thickets. Wherever it is easiest to travel, animal pathways have been driven into the ground.
118060:
A wolf cub happily plays here.
A wolf cub happily plays here.
A wolf cub happily plays here.
The mother wolf stands here, protecting her young cubs.

This small hill rises slightly lower than the surrounding hills, which obscures the view to the south and west. The hill is smaller in nature and the sides are smooth and neat. Small grey pebbles lie strewn across the knee-high grass, some of which slowly roll down the hill.
118061: Bare earthen animal paths wind between and over the hills, blazed into the lush green grass that blankets the hills. The hills are taller here, providing a great vantage of the surrounding area. In the east, the large Bree-hill dominates the horizon.
118062: The ground of the low hills is mostly comprised of small, broken rocks and gravel. Patches of bright green grass pop up throughout the field of rock. To the north, the ground suddenly drops over a steep, rocky descent. Rolling, grassy downs can be spotted on the western horizon.
118063: Old, broken furniture has been discarded in the cellar, piled in corners with cobwebs floating everywhere. The uneven ground is slippery, with puddles pooling in the deep sections. Pale, white mushrooms grow in the corners, their spores wafting in the air. A large, faded, and torn tapestry covers the eastern wall, obviously covering a large hole in the wall.
118064:
An arrow rack is hanging on the tunnel's wall.
On the rack, there are ten war arrows.

A cramped tunnel, approximately eight feet in height and three feet wide, winds its way underground. It branches off to the north and to the south. The walls and floors have been worn smooth, evidence that the tunnel has been heavily travelled at some point in time.
118065:
A sturdy crate made of nailed wooden planks sits on the floor.
A large bookshelf sits against the wall.
On the bookshelf, there are a map of Fornost and a map of Bree.
A large, sturdy table made from oak is sitting here.
On the table, there are two smoked pieces of meat.
A swarthy, little bandit advances forward.
A swarthy, little bandit advances forward.
A swarthy, little bandit advances forward.

This is a large underground area with plenty of room in which to manoeuvre. Several chairs lie haphazardly around the centre of the cavern, with several low tables lining the walls. The tables are covered in parchments and books. A large bookshelf stands against the northern wall, and maps line the walls all around.
118066: A noticeable crack runs down one of the walls.

The tunnel ends abruptly here, for no discernible reason. The walls, ceiling, and floor are all formed from smooth, grey stone. Cool, fresh air wafts in from a large crack in the ceiling above, and there are large cracks in the southern and eastern cavern walls.
118067:
A large mother hawk is here looking for prey to feed her young.
A cute young hawk is sitting here waiting for his mother to feed him.
A cute young hawk is sitting here waiting for his mother to feed him.

The branches of the old tree offer safe footing, and the rough, dark brown bark provide good handholds for climbers. In between the leaves, the surrounding landscape can be seen, mostly thick brushwood. In one of the higher tree perches, the remains of a disrupted nest of birds can be spotted.
118068:
A sturdy rope bridge stretches eastward to another tree.
A dirty ruffian draped in rags advances towards you.

High in the top of this old tree, the view over the surrounding brushwood is excellent. Brushwood, grass, and other trees of all colours and shapes stretch out in all directions. Whether the occasional movement seen below in a bush is from the local wildlife, some traveller, or just the wind, however, cannot be judged. A man-made, sturdy rope bridge has been constructed here, stretching to connect a tree to the east.
118069:
A sturdy rope bridge stretches to another tree to the west.
A dirty ruffian draped in rags advances towards you.

Rising not only above the landscape but also above all of the other trees, this place gives an excellent view. The branches of the tree's crown are not very thick or strong, but there are many of them, which makes finding a safe position for feet and hands an easy task. A sturdy rope bridge stretches across to another tree in the distance to the west.
118070: A squirrel scampers around here, looking for nuts from the trees.

The branches here are not very thick or heavy, but they are plentiful. Finding safe footing should be no issue. The tree top provides a vantage point of the surrounding landscape, with the Old East Road to the north and the bustling town of Bree to the east.
118071: Some ugly blow-flies are buzzing around here.

The trail beneath your feet is cluttered with splintered logs, sawdust, and pine needles. It curves to the west before resuming its northerly path. To the east, a recently cut coppice lies off the road, while to the south, the trail connects with the Old East Road.
118072: To the south and west, this trail is surrounded by dense foliage. Many animal traces can be spotted here, such as digging marks, nibbled leaves, stems, and trunks. On the outskirts of Combe, the trees are smaller and younger. The air is thick with the scent of damp wood, pine needles, and sawdust.
118073: On the trail leading into Combe, several cow patties have been dried up, as well as some new ones scattered about the ground. This trail is not used very much, as evidenced by the lack of wear and tear. There's a smell of fresh crops coming from somewhere to the east. A rickety door quietly clacks to the west, and the sound of several cows can be heard faintly, a short distance away.
118074: The logging trail extends in an east-west direction while another branch forks to the south. This crossroad marks the busiest part of the village of Combe. Each branch of the fork is well maintained at this section of the trail, despite evidence of heavy use. Small ruts from carriages can be seen in the dirt, as well as footprints of varying sizes.
118075: Bordering Combe on the west side, this trail is lightly worn down as it is not travelled nearly as much as the rest of the village's paths. Bits of tree bark and fragments litter the ground all about the route from the sporadic logging carts venturing this way. Further down the path to the east, the trail appears more worn out. A faint smell of manure fills the air.
118077:
A malicious thug is here, threatening you.
A malicious thug is here, threatening you.

Unlike the rest of the wood, which is densely forested with wild buckthorn, dogwood, aspen, and spruce, this little grove is devoid of variation. Hazelnut trees, which are unusual elsewhere in Chetwood, are plentiful and spaced among the oaks. The forest floor is loamy, with small, dark black boulders scattered about.
118082: The stables of Combe can be seen a short distance to the west. A path has been worn in towards the stables by the endless passing of animals, workers, and farmhands. Various farming tools have been left scattered about the ground. The grass is yellowed and patchy from the grazing of animals. The smell of manure and fertilizer is quite strong in this area.
118083: The trail is even more worn out here than to the west. Ruts from carts and carriages are several inches deep. No longer well maintained, this section of trail is completely saturated with footprints, human and animal. Several fresh and rotting crops are strewn along the ground here and trail off south towards the crop storage building.
118084: A massive iron gate to the north guards the entrance to the log preparation site. A large storage building to the north stands a short distance behind the gate. The ruts are quite deep on the trail from the frequent and continuous travel by huge carts that can hold a considerable amount of heavy logs.
118085: Given its location in one of Chetwood's most remote areas, one could reasonably presume that this acreage is densely forested. Despite this, there are only a few young oaks to be seen. An indication of a former arboreal life can be seen in the large number of short, decaying stumps that are scattered throughout the low grasses and profusion of wildflowers.
118086:
A patch of orange mushrooms springs from the ground here.
A black wolf pads restlessly, looking for its next prey.

Many of the trees in this part of the forest are young, evidenced by their narrow trunks under the low, lacy canopy. Occasional stumps appear among the undergrowth, many of them covered in assemblages of white mushrooms, appearing like pale, fleshy scales interspersed among the decaying bark.
118087: A black snake hurries towards you with sly intentions.

The forest dips and rolls as low hills stretch in all directions. At the bottom of a few of the hills, shallow trenches appear at the base of some of the younger hazels and oaks, and the underbrush appears crushed, as if tread on by a pack of heavy-footed creatures.
118088:
An apple tree with bright green leaves grows here.
On the tree's branches are two apples.
A giant termite is here, crushing skulls and bones.
A small termite is running around making strange sounds.
A small termite is running around making strange sounds.

The surrounding forest is light and slopes gently toward a field in the south. Beyond that, Bree-hill can be seen rising above the landscape and bisected by the Old East Road. The forest extends to the east where a number of felled trees lie waiting to be transported.
118089: A long water trough made of wood stands here.

The path bends around the logging trail past the log preparation site. Farm equipment lays about the ground. A cart and plough are here waiting to be used in the ploughing of the fields. Several pigs play in their pen and are wrought with mud. There is a trough filled with water for the animals to drink from. Standing beside the trough is an iron water pump that can be used by weary travellers and workers.
118090: The worn path creates a cross shape as it is regularly used to move farming and logging equipment to their respective points. The smells are a mishmash of dust, dirt, and mud, along with various types of wood and bark. The wash of previous rains has created some crevices in the earth. Small pieces of tree and log litter are scattered about the ground.
118091: A large sack is on the ground.

Countless woven sacks are stacked along the walls up to twelve feet high, including in the room's centre. The sacks are stuffed to the brim with crops that were harvested from the farmer's fields. Several small tools are hung on the southern wall. Wheelbarrows are laid about strategically for moving the sacks around the storage area.
118092: Despite looking dilapidated on the outside, the shed is in surprisingly good shape on the inside. Some stairs leading to the second level look fairly worn. There are a few wooden log stores here, packed with cut firewood and stumps. A huge logging axe is stuck in the centre of a massive stump in the middle of the shed. The windows are cracked and broken, with dust thick enough that one may never see through them again. An old plough is rusting away in the corner.
118093:
Delicate, finely-woven webbing stretches from the corners of the ceiling.
A tiny spider is here, eating a tiny bug.

The flooring of the attic is almost completely covered with dried-up, caked-on mud. There are soggy wooden planks all about the floor and several small window frames are left open to allow for a slight draft. The roof rises nearly five feet above the planking. Near the attic's west end, the ceiling lifts back upward, angled into the next room. Spider webs line the area in nearly every crevice, and many rat droppings are spread all over the area.
118094: A messy bed with a stained blanket stands in the corner.

The room looks well lived in. Decomposed leaf litter and small twigs are piled up towards the window, which looks to have been broken long ago and has a sharp shard of glass jutting out from the side. There are three bedframes which are rusted, and all of the mattresses look stained and dirty. Red paint has long since chipped and fallen from the walls. Standing in the centre of the room is a single chair, without a seat, and a trash can.
118095:
A pile of plain-sawed lumber boards is stacked against a wall.
A hobbit is here, looking for work to do.
A man is walking around here, trying to look busy.

Several huge carts, loaded with considerably large, heavy hardwood logs arrive and depart from this location daily. Logs that arrive here are completely clean and free from branches and debris. The sliding wall of this building is usually closed, protecting the wood and workers from the possibility of harsh weather. The smell of freshly cut wood permeates the air.
118096: A man is walking around here, trying to look busy.

Within this large open-air building, several weighty hardwood logs have been placed here, roughly, in piles. Other stacks of smaller logs are scattered throughout the area. There is tree bark littered all over the ground, creating a soft yet splintery floor to walk on. The logs have had their branches removed and are placed in smaller, separate piles. The greens of the forest create a harsh contrast with the various browns of logs in the area.
118097: A neat pile of lumber is here, waiting to be transported.

A large path through the forest has been created to allow workers to transport logs to the gathering site, which is housed in a large open-air building to the south. This is the most intensively used area of the region's woodlands, and the surrounding wood is littered with stumps and sapling trees.
118098: A fallen tree lies on the ground, its clump of roots pointing upwards.

The path forks north and east, and beyond its edges, a large patch of forest is cut down to stumps. There are many fallen trees on the ground, some of which have had their branches removed and have been prepared for transport toward the log collection site.
118100: This area has been recently deforested; only the remaining stumps show that there once was a forest here. The forest floor is overgrown by brushwood and thistle, and where the bare ground appears, tracks of long-gone lumberjacks and their horses can still be easily identified.
118101:
A big, nasty vulture is sitting here, protecting its nest.
A big, nasty vulture is sitting here, protecting its nest.

From the highest branches of the mighty yew, a breathtaking vista extends in every direction. The great Chetwood forest sprawls for many miles to the north and west. The well-travelled Old East Road appears far off in the southern distance. And an enormous, murky marsh stretches toward the eastern horizon as far as the eye can see.
118102: This part of the forest seems rarely travelled as passage to the west, leading deeper into the forest, and to the east, leading out of it, is blocked by large felled trees. Massive, lacy webs stretch between the trunks of oaks and young yew trees, collecting dewdrops and small insects.
118103: The wood finally begins to spread out, as the landscape yields toward the open meadow in the east. Despite its visibility, a pile of downed trunks and gathered brushwood looks to impede any access to the north and east, whereas travelling through the forest to the west and south appears to be straightforward.
118104: Here in the heart of Chetwood, the branches of great, ancient oaks are so complexly entwined that it is impossible to tell one tree from another. The canopy seems a wooly green blanket overhead that blocks the light and warmth of the sun and creates an unexpected chill in the air.
118105: Trail through the Depths of Chetwood

A cute, fluffy owlet is waiting here for its mother to return with food.
A cute, fluffy owlet is waiting here for its mother to return with food.
A great horned owl looks cautiously around it.

The forest trail is thronged on both sides by tall trees with trunks both wide and thin, and the thick undergrowth at the base of the trees makes any off-trail travel extremely precarious. Silence hangs palpably in the air: heavy and oppressive. Each rare, innocuous sound that erupts from this silence, a bird chirping or a rodent burrowing in the undergrowth, is transformed into an eerie, muffled echo as it reverberates around the woods.
118106: Trail at the Edge of Chetwood Forest

The landscape transitions quickly from thick forest to open field. To the west, a narrow trail weaves its way through the trees, quickly disappearing into the dark depths of Chetwood. Low dogwood trees dot the forest edges, taking advantage of the thinning canopy. The trail continues east toward a grassy meadow, punctuated by a few ancient oaks.
118107: These woods are filled with mature oak and birch trees, with a multitude of smaller, thin-trunked trees below. There are some pine trees mixed in, but they seem to be struggling in the shade cast by the larger deciduous trees: the pines are still green near their tops, but below that they are skeletal and bare, with broken stumps of branches sticking out from their trunks at regular intervals. Here and there a giant clump of dirt rises over a wide depression, the root mass of a fallen tree that was torn up when the tree fell. The forest floor is mostly bare, covered with fallen leaves from past seasons, and too shaded for smaller plants to grow.
118108: This forest is populated by mature trees, mostly oak with some birch mixed in. Small clumps of pines are interspersed, struggling to compete with their deciduous neighbours: their trunks are bare up to the very top, where tufts of green needles reach for the available light. The canopy above is almost unbroken, creating a deep twilight even during the day. The occasional sunfleck makes it to the ground when the sun is up, lighting the small leafy plants that grow among the leaf litter and fallen branches. Other than these small plants the forest floor is open, lacking obstructive undergrowth.
118109:
A copper penny lies on the ground.
An ancient fungus smothers the boulders.

These woods are populated by many mature oak trees, the trunks broad and broadly-spaced. Despite the room between the trees, their canopies meet overhead, forming a solid unbroken ceiling of branches and leaves that blocks the sun from reaching the ground. A number of fallen trees, most mid-sized or smaller, lie strewn across the forest floor, skeletal remnants of those that failed to reach up through the canopy above to compete for the available light. Very few plants grow among the fallen trunks and leaf litter that covers the ground, owing to this lack of light.
118110: Trail through the Heart of Chetwood Forest

The wood surrounding the forest trail is wild and secluded. Trees and brushwood have grown so densely at its edges that not a single sunbeam finds its way down to the ground, and it is hardly possible to tell whether it is day or night. The surrounding oaks are covered in moss, growing like a green pelt across their wide trunks. A smell of damp and rotting wood fills the air.
118112:
A coil of rope is lying here.
There are two bales of hay here.
A drunk hobbit is standing here.

This barn must be at least five yards long by ten yards wide. Bales of hay dominate the space, with a slew of well-maintained farming tools mounted on the western wall. It is hard not to sneeze as each crunching step on the hay propels copious amounts of dust and debris into the air. Several tattered ropes hang from the rafters and a wooden ladder leads to the barn's loft overhead.
118115: This dense, mature forest is composed mostly of deciduous trees, oak and birch and the occasional rowan. Some pine trees grow here too, but seem to be struggling in the shade cast by their taller broadleaved neighbours: they are bare up to their tops, where a small cone of green needles remains. Here and there one of these pines seems to have died completely, leaving a tall skeletal form whose trunk is ghostly white where the bark has started to peel off. The ground underfoot is uneven, with raised hummocks and shallow depressions, and at the base of one such hummock there is a small hole between exposed tree roots. To the north and west the trees begin to thin out, but the increased light reaching the ground has allowed dense brush to grow, creating a tangled barrier that prevents movement in those directions.
118116:
The corpse of a bloodthirsty bat is lying here.
The corpse of a large bat is lying here.
The corpse of a scarred tusky boar is lying here.

A large pine grove emerges in the middle of this forest. The pines have grown densely enough here that the surrounding deciduous trees weren't able to establish among them, although the edges of the grove are being slowly encroached upon by the surrounding oak and rowan. The pines are bare most of the way up, with a dense canopy of green needles only at the tops where they are exposed to the sun. The ground below them takes on a reddish tint from the years of accumulated needles that they have shed, and is soft and spongy to walk upon. Not much grows beneath these trees, owing to the lack of light that makes it all the way down to the forest floor.
118117: An ancient fungus smothers the boulders.

This mature deciduous forest is composed primarily of oak, the trees growing closely enough together that the canopy overhead is unbroken. Some tall pine trees are mixed in, but they are doing poorly in the shade cast by the oaks: their tops are green and full of needles, but the trunks below are bare and skeletal, with broken branches and peeling bark. The undergrowth here is relatively sparse due to the lack of light reaching the forest floor, with only the occasional thin, scraggly bush or clump of low-growing herbaceous plants visible among the leaf litter from the trees above.
118118:
You see two copper pennies on the ground.
The corpse of a large bat is lying here.
The remains of a black fungus lie here in a heap of rotting compost.

This dense, mature forest is primarily oak, but some pine trees are mixed in beneath the canopy. These pines appear to be struggling to compete for light: they are mostly bare, with tufts of green needles at their tops. The branches below are thin, sticking out from each trunk in regular intervals like spokes on a wheel; many are broken and have lost their bark, appearing white where the wood underneath shows through. Some of the oak trees here are bare and dying as well: bark is sloughing off their trunks, revealing spidery white webs of fungus underneath. Some have fallen, and the trunks are overrun with honey-coloured fruiting bodies of the fungus that is consuming them.
118119:
A huge bat is here, emitting piercing squeaks.
A large bat is here, hanging in the darkness.
A large bat is here, hanging in the darkness.

These dense, mature woods are a mix of oak and pine. The pine trees grow in clumps, and are green near the top but bare and dead looking below, where the soft needle-like foliage has been shaded until it dropped. Most of the side branches on these pines have long since broken off, leaving short stumps sticking out from otherwise bare trunks, and making passage between them easy. Here and there one of the pines has died completely, shaded into oblivion by the oaks towering above, and the bark has peeled off to leave a ghostly white trunk. There are a number of fallen trees in this part of the forest, and a particularly large trunk appears to have rotted into hollow sections.
118121: A black wolf pads restlessly, looking for its next prey.

The surrounding forest opens upon a wide meadow, its edges lined by the tall, thin trunks of golden aspens. Sloping slightly downward into the lea, the trail rises again in the distance. The air smells of wild mint and damp soil, and the buzzing sounds of tiny insects flitting along in the low grasses fill the lea with a low, continuous hum.
118122: This is a simple, yet cosy room. While there is not much in the way of furniture, a small cot along the northern wall provides a welcome spot to sleep after a long day's work. Several loaves of bread are cached within a small cupboard in the corner. A modest study with a fireplace built of river-rock is to the east. Through a small window, a green barn overgrown with ivy can be seen to the south.
118123:
A large stone fireplace with a roaring fire warms the room.
Rose the midwife is standing here. She seems quite busy.

Here within a modest study sits a fireplace that is built of polished river-rock and lit with a fire that burns with immense warmth and brightness. Several wolf furs of obsidian and silver colour lay on the wooden floor, making for a snug and secure spot to relax. Large bundles of firewood, predominately planks of cherry and oak, sit piled in the study's corner ready to stoke the fire at a moment's notice.
118124:
A hobbit is here walking around.
A smiling hobbit child is playing around here.

A cosy smial has been built into a hill just south of the wishing well and dirt path. Clearly meant for hobbit residents, this smial is stocked full of amenities and comforts of every kind. Quaint wooden furniture populates the room, and small porthole windows peak outwards, providing panoramic views of Archet. A carved spiral staircase descends downwards in the back corner of the smial.
118125:
An oaken wine rack stands here.
A fine marble chessboard with ivory and ebony pieces is set here.

Dozens of hooped oaken casks full of cherry wine sit here, sweetening with age. The floor of the cellar is of natural stone, hewn directly into the hill itself. Two small wooden stools sit here with an ornately carved chessboard placed between them. A questionably large amount of empty wine glasses lay adjacent to the board, along with a large scarlet wool blanket.
118126: A barman stands behind the bar, dusting the wine bottles.

This small tavern provides libations and recreation for the locals, where men and hobbits both enjoy each other's company. Countless rows of cherry wine bottles line the barback, along with every sort of liquor imaginable. A single massive slab of cherrywood acts as the bar, with tall oak stools for seating. The entire tavern has been decorated from top-to-bottom in a coordinating purple hue, while a broken chandelier of amethyst and adamant swings precariously overhead.
118127: A mass of wriggling vines drops on you from the trees.

The forest encroaches from all directions except the east. Thick trunked maples are dwarfed by giant spruce. Large pinecones blanket the ground below, making it hard to find stable footing. The air smells of pine needles and the rot of leaf litter.
118128:
A huge black fungus is here, exuding a foul stench.
A huge black fungus is here, exuding a foul stench.

The trees are quite dense in this area and many of them grow very closely to one another. A number of maidenhair ferns spread lushly underfoot, and some of the areas between the trees are carpeted with brushwood. The thick vegetation makes it very hard to move deeper into the forest.
118133:
A large rabbit looks peacefully at you, ready to dart away.
A long-tailed bird watches you from the vegetation.

The southern forest path ends at the door of the famous Blue Trout Inn. To the east, trees have been planted in equally spaced rows to make harvesting easier. The faint creaking of branches can be heard all around the area, and the rustling of leaves adds a hush to the air. There is a sign here, marking the entryway into the Blue Trout Inn.
118134: On the path to the Combe Farmhouse, the trail is well-worn but has never been made permanent. The grass folds over itself on the path's sides as it has long since worn out in the centre. Pebbles and stones line the way towards the house, and when walked upon, the sound of crunching can be heard underfoot.
118135:
A large potato is growing here.
A young farm-hand is here hard at work.

Medium-sized crops grow among the cultivated rows of soil. The field appears to be actively farmed, as there are no weeds to be seen. The footpaths are worn to such an extent that they are nearly a foot deeper than the surrounding ground.
118136:
There are two potatoes here.
A round turnip is growing here.
A young farm-hand is here hard at work.

Many varieties of root crops have been sown here, their long green stems reaching upwards toward the sky. The farmer has tended the fields well, and piles of picked weeds can be seen composting along the northern fence. Some patches of crops have been left bare by birds and rabbits feasting in the area. The wall running along the eastern side of the fields has been freshly painted and borders on the path to the farmer's house.
118137: The soil in the area has not been ploughed well, it appears mostly desolate and bare. Rows of crops line the area but have died out and remain stunted. Black and brown spots can be seen on the leaves, which are also wilting. Mites and aphids feast upon what little crops remain. Tiny stones, small twigs, and debris are scattered about the field, and weeds are growing all over. There is a mild smell of manure coming from the stable to the south.
118138:
An overstuffed scarecrow looms above the tops of the tallest crops.
A hobbit farmer is here, thinking about seeds and vegetables.

Several large fields of crops are planted here, each row uniform, growing tall and towering over one another. Viewing them from a distance, it cannot be determined where they start nor end. There is a strong smell of upturned soil in the air, and some dust moves around in the occasional breeze.
118139:
A small sign is attached to the wall.
A stocky mountain mule is here, waiting to serve.
A domesticated pony, beast of burden to many, stands here.
A skilled pony breeder is here, wearing a thoughtful expression.

Inside the stable, there is a powerful smell of hay and manure. The ropes used to hitch the farm animals to their posts hang on the side of the enclosure. Many tools are suspended neatly along the eastern wall, under which is a small wagon whose handle is resting on a bale of hay. Straw covers the ground all about the stable. Bags of grain and feed can be seen resting on a wooden ledge.
118140:
A black wolf pads restlessly, looking for its next prey.
A black snake hurries towards you with sly intentions.

The trees appear older in this part of the wood, their trunks and branches thicker than the trees along the trail to the west. Strange shadows move in the branches and within the undergrowth; it is difficult to tell whether they are the silhouettes of forest creatures or a trick of the light.
118141:
A low and wide-spread tree grows here.
On the tree's branches, there are two juicy plums.
A black wolf pads restlessly, looking for its next prey.

The trees crowd so tightly together in the heart of Chetwood that it appears as if they are conspiring against unsuspecting travellers. Their mossy trunks provide an ambient dampness and lingering odour of rot. Even during the day, the canopy overhead is practically unbroken, producing a deep twilight.
118142: Mature pine, oak, and beech trees grow in the vicinity while tender saplings struggle to rise from the leafy humus below. Travel westward is obstructed by a massive escarpment whose rocky base transforms into a forested hillside overhead.
118143: In the centre of a small glade surrounded by a dense stand of trees, a curious structure appears. On the ground, dozens of slim, downed trunks are organised in a wide circle with their tops leaning against each other and forming a primitive shelter.
118144: A black wolf pads restlessly, looking for its next prey.

A low hill, densely forested with towering oaks and pines, rolls away from the high, steep ridge to the west. Birds can occasionally be observed scouting for food in the branches. The wood stops abruptly to the south at a harsh, unnatural border, beyond which a field of wildflowers spreads to the horizon.
118148:
A small campfire burns here, its low flames giving off only a little light.
A solitary hermit is sitting here, meditating with a serene expression.

From the outside, this makeshift shelter appears to be on the verge of collapse. But inside, the structure is obviously much sturdier. Recently felled logs line the inner walls, and a mat of slender, woven roots and lichen is laid upon the floor. A little patch of ground behind the shelter has been fostered into a small, private herbal garden, where several unusual and exotic plants flourish, infusing the air with a peculiar tranquil odour.
118154:
A bale of hay is lying here.
A well-fed cow stands here chewing her cud listlessly.
A young farm-hand is here hard at work.
A cow stands here, chewing her cud.

Up to a dozen cows can be stored under the shed's roof, each with their own wooden stall. Broken down bales of hay are placed at ground level for them to graze on. The stalls are separated by sturdy wooden boards, iron bars, and the occasional bale of hay stacked up to form a non-permanent wall. Wooden railings line the length of the shed and serve as tie points for the cows when needed. Openings in the shed walls allow for aeration and light when it is available.
118155:
A tool rack with several hooks is nailed to the wall.
On the rack, there are a hammer, a sickle, a small spade, and a shovel.
A hobbit female is standing here inspecting a bent tine on a pitchfork.

Inside the shed, it is surprisingly roomy. Farming gear (spades and sickles, hammers and hoes, pitchforks and ploughs) is neatly hanging from hooks on the walls or tucked away in corners. The floor is bare except for a thin layer of hay scattered unevenly across the ground.
118156:
A large stone fireplace with a roaring fire warms the room.
A peaceful farmer is here, whistling merrily.

Candlelight from above fills the room with bright golden light. The hallways are immaculately clean despite the dirty nature of the work being performed outside. A painting of cattle is hung on the wall above the fireplace which is filling the home with warmth. The smell of burning lumber and smoke saturates the residence. Wooden pillars, which appear to be load-bearing in nature, look gritty and aged. The wood floor seems to creak and crack under the pressure of those who would walk by.
118157: Ham the hobbit is standing here, serving drinks and watching for trouble.

The Blue Trout Inn is a trendy meeting and resting place for travellers who come to the village of Combe. The building is made entirely out of wood and logs sourced from the local forest. There is a strong smell of sap inside, and the windows appear to be a little more than aged.
