The inn consists of seven sparsely furnished guest rooms with beds of sufficient quality, and linens that look to be clean and well taken care of. A wooden sign is hung behind the bar.
118158: A long-tailed bird watches you from the vegetation.

The hardwood trees in this part of the forest have been planted much closer together than the others, resulting in a thicker canopy above the forest floor. The area has yet to be touched by the loggers as they rotate through the forest sections each year, allowing the others to be regrown. Several animals and birds have taken advantage of this and have found refuge and solace here, in the meantime.
118159: The pipe-weed plants are much smaller in this field compared to those to the north and south. They seem more recently planted, and some of the smaller stalks are attached to short sticks to help them in their upright growth. To the west lies a large barn with an overhang extending from the roof, under which many weathered barrels line the exterior wall.
118160:
There is some pipe-weed here.
The garden snake slithers harmlessly here.

The pipe-weed field extends from the west and south, its expansive rows ending in the east at a track before an enormous barn. Extending from the outer walls of the barn are low covered tables. Small jars lie strewn across their tops, and on a few of the tables, tiny seeds, barely larger than grains of sand, litter the surface.
118161:
There is some pipe-weed here.
A hobbit farmer is here, daydreaming about his pipe-weed plants.
The garden snake slithers harmlessly here.

The air is thick with the smell of manure. Piles of dung lay steaming and stinking at the ends of the rows of pipe-weed, waiting to be distributed to other areas of the farm. A wooden gate lies directly to the north, and its adjoining fence extends far to the east.
118162: Just to the south, the trail bends and travels alongside a long wooden split rail fence. A large gate appears on its western edge, with doors sagging slightly inward. A subtle herbal aroma lingers on the wind. A hedge borders the trail to the west.
118163: The trail follows along a wooden fence, its segments composed of three, sturdy logs extended horizontally between each post. In some places, the logs have collapsed due to age and weathering. Small beetles flit between the short grasses at the edge of the road. A humble cabin stands directly to the north.
118164: An old hobbit, wrinkled with age and a bit pudgy, leans on a walking-stick.

Entering the cabin, a large, brick-lined hearth dominates the back wall. Warmth emanates from the fixture and slowly seeps into the skin. A cast iron pot hangs from an iron bar near the throat of the chimney and the smell of cooked onion hangs heavy in the air. A small table abuts the western wall, and a single, neatly made cot is positioned against the opposite wall. A heap of small animal furs is piled in the southeast corner.
118165: There are two piles of pipe-weed here.

The pipe-weed bushes grow especially tall in this area, their fuzzy green flowers extending well over the heads of the hobbits who farm the land. To the south, a well-groomed hedge borders the field, keeping the precious crop hidden from prying eyes outside the village.
118166:
There is some pipe-weed here.
A hobbit farmer is here, thinking about seeds and herbs.

Through the centre of this field of tall pipe-weed plants runs a wide, tamped-down pathway that leads toward the barn to the north. Small offshoot paths wind through the fields, allowing farmers to harvest pipe-weed and carry their yields to the barn for drying and distribution.
118167: The rows of densely planted pipe-weed end at a tall hedge in the south. While it is possible to find a way through the rows, the long leaves fan out into the makeshift walkways, catching at skin and fabric and leaving behind an unmistakable herbaceous scent.
118168: A field mouse noses about hungrily, searching for food.

Perfectly straight rows of tall, shaggy, and vibrantly green pipe-weed bushes extend far into the southern distance. To the north, a dingy wooden shed leans ever so slightly on its side; a small glass window placed in the centre of the shed's wall reveals only darkness beyond.
118169: A small but well-worn trail arcs in a wide curve and continues on to the west and south. Wildflowers grow in thick bunches at the trail's edge. Beyond that, short grasses extend into the distance, flattened in many places and pocked with patches of bare dirt in others.
118170: A coloured game bird is visible in the vegetation, watching you warily.

Covered by broad swaths of short grass and the occasional shrub, this field transitions to forest in the north while a small trail that runs through the village of Staddle appears in the far eastern distance. To the south, the landscape slopes upward toward Bree-hill and dozens of hobbit holes appear as dark specks on the eastern side of the hill.
118172: A black wolf pads restlessly, looking for its next prey.

Here, the forest protrudes from the progression of low hills that spread across Chetwood, forming a narrow ridgeline high above a valley to the south. On its western, eastern, and southern sides, the ridge features steep, rocky slopes, graced by only the most resilient of trees that lean at precarious angles but remain firmly rooted in the rockface.
118173:
The remains of a black fungus lie here in a heap of rotting compost.
The corpse of a giant slug is lying here.
A black pond of water is here.

A small fissure of the earth, eroded over time, has created this crevice. A thick carpet of moss conceals it from light and wind, making the air feel cool, but also damp and sticky. The base of the crevice collects rainwater that seeps in from the edges of the fissure, and it has become a breeding ground for small, biting insects.
118181:
A sturdy bandit bodyguard stands here, eager to hack you to pieces.
A sturdy bandit bodyguard stands here, eager to hack you to pieces.

A fairly low cliff overlooks the plain here, and the land gently climbs to the east, drawing ever closer to the height of the plateau above. Although the rock face is not tall, it is quite smooth, and the ground undercuts it just a little at its base, offering an environment in which a thick tangle of prickly briers can flourish, sheltered from the cold northern winds, but not completely from the life-sustaining rains. A soft blanket of heather covers the slope.
118182: A brutish forest troll is hunting here, looking for some tasty flesh.

A faint putrid smell pervades the air that seems almost to stagnate among the mossy boles standing all about. The trees appear to be quite old, judging by their height and girth, but they have taken on a sickly hue in this dank air. Whatever pervades this woodland also besets the undergrowth, which is comprised of scattered patches of yellowing grass and weeds, interspersed with only a few spindly bushes.
118183: The wide valley floor climbs northward, approaching a lonely ridge of hills. The ground is fertile, fed by the lively stream below you, and thick, lush grass covers the sloping terrain. The closer you come to hills, the more rocky the land becomes.
118184: A fat rabbit is here, chewing on some grass.

The large, flat shards of shattered paving stones and countless smaller rocky fragments lie scattered amid the grass and shrubs. A small glade of pines begins here, where it circles along the northern border here and curves in the distant south-west, protecting the end of the valley here. The valley expands to the east from here. Medium and large boulders are scattered throughout the northern area where the pines begin.
118185: Foot of a Ridge of Hills
The corpse of a brown bear is lying here.

Looming out of the plains, a rocky ridge of hills rears up to the east, making the ground slope above quite precipitous. By contrast, the ground slopes down gently to the south as a narrow valley opens out into the plains. A number of scrubby bushes have sprouted from the rather rocky terrain, growing greater in number, yet somehow more sickly as they approach the forest to the north.
118186: A few stunted bushes and some scattered patches of sickly, yellow grass begin to overtake the slippery moss that carpets the ground further north. But the trees here are still assaulted by the creeping moss. More grey than green, they grow upward in strange, knotty tangles, as if seeking refuge in the heights from the encroaching moss.
118187: Forest of Twisted and Gloomy Trees

A shrub with maple-like leaves is growing here.
On the shrub, there are two handfuls of blackcurrant berries.
A black pond of water is here.
A brutish forest troll is hunting here, looking for some tasty flesh.

Green-black moss creeps up the trunk of every tree, almost smothering them. The branches strive to escape this blanketing presence, twisting and writhing into seemingly unnatural shapes. Instead of the usual undergrowth associated with woodlands, the ground here is carpeted by the same dank moss that assails the trees, making for a slippery footing indeed.
118188: Massive roots shift uneasily all around you.

The walls here are covered in a dark, slimey layer of what appears to be a putrid amalgamation of rotting insects, small animal corpses, and decaying plant matter. Pinpricks of light can be seen through the thick tangle of roots and plant matter above, suggesting that egress is possible but not without pointed effort. Downward, root and decay weave together in a sickly blanket, with nothing but darkness discernible beyond.
118189: Sickly, stunted shrubs have sprouted from the somewhat rocky ground. To the north they grow greater in density, and yet begin to assume an ever more sickly pallor. The fallen leaves that drift this way from the tall trees should have helped create a rich, fertile and loamy soil, but instead they have carried with them the creeping moss that befouls the woodland to the north.
118190:
Some roots lie here waiting to ensnare weary travellers.
A tree-snake lies wrapped around one of the tree branches.
A tree-snake lies wrapped around one of the tree branches.

From somewhere deeper in the woodland, a strange animal cry can be heard, but it is not possible to pinpoint its source. The air here seems strangely still, and a foetid aroma pervades everything. A fuzzy coating of green-black moss covers almost everything here, choking out all but the most persistent under- growth.
118191: A large rabbit looks peacefully at you, ready to dart away.

Whereas further north a field of charred stumps attests to the fact that once a forest thrived in this area, the land here is devoid of even that clue to the past. The ground shows scars not only of fire, but also of the action of mortal hands. Gaping holes in the scorched earth are all that remains to mark the places where once large trees must have grown. No shrub, weed, nor vegetation of any kind has yet sprung up in the blackened ground, as if somehow the earth itself has been poisoned. A small building stands immediately to the south.
118192: At some time in the past, a forest covered this land. Now, however, all that remains of the trees are blackened stumps. Yet it is apparent that this was no accidental fire. Nor was it fire that razed the forest, for the shape of the stumps speaks to the work of an axe in the felling of the once mighty trees. It would seem that someone purposefully destroyed the trees, and feeling that was not enough, set it alight, destroying it even to the smallest shrub or sapling.
118193: Thick tussocks of coarse grass compete with dense clumps of dark purple heather to create a colourful patchwork that blankets the ground. A sombre dark brown border of scorched vegetation bounds this area to the east, where a sizeable expanse of land has been scarred by fire. A few miles to the southeast, a small stone structure stands close to the foot of an escarpment, but there is no other hint at habitation in the surrounding countryside.
118194: Small, red-brown rocks and a few larger boulders lie tumbled amid the coarse, yellow grasses and occasional patches of thick, purple heather that clothe this bleak and windswept plain. Not far to the south, a tall plateau looms above the lowland, but in all other directions the land for many miles around stretches out flat, and is seemingly featureless.
118195: An old wagon, ravaged by time and the elements, lies here abandoned.

Scattered rocks freckle the landscape, though most lie almost hidden beneath a tufted beard of purple heather, and yellow-green grass. The land marches for several furlongs in every direction with scarcely a feature that stands above the flat, but rugged surface, save for an occasional dogged patch of briars that seems to cling tenaciously to life in this bleak and windswept environment. Yet, in the distance to the south, drawing close to a sombre plateau, both rock and bramble become more numerous.
118196: Far to the east the Misty Mountains form a barrier that can be traversed at only a few passes. Closer at hand, a tall plateau stands to the southeast, but that is yet some miles distant. In the immediate surroundings, there is a gently rolling plain, clad mostly in heather and coarse grass, with only an occasional small patch of brush.
118197: By a strange trick of perspective, the silhouette of the plateau that looms above the plains at some distance to the south looks like the prow of a mighty sailing ship, cutting through the expansive green sea of grasses that spread in all other directions, rippling like water against the wind.
118198: Low tussocks of coarse, yellow-green grass and patches of dark purple heather clothe the landscape. A few isolated briars send spindly limbs snaking out amid the ground cover, their sharp thorns threatening to ensnare the unwary, but no taller vegetation is to be seen for many leagues in any direction.
118199: The land folds slightly here, creating a narrow gully. Though quite shallow at this point, the cleft becomes both deeper and wider as it stretches out to the east. A few small, thorny bushes crowd in the sparse shelter offered by the low walls of the channel, and as those walls grow taller, the briars grow larger and more numerous as well.
118200: Coarse grasses and low purple heather compete for dominance on a broad expanse of lazily undulating plains. This windswept landscape stretches far into the distance in all directions; in the immediate vicinity, nothing taller than a short clump of grass stands above ground level, and even that bends, straining to stand upright against the prevailing winds.
118201:
The mother wolf stands here, protecting her young cubs.
A grey wolf is here, salivating profusely.

Though the land here is rugged and uncultivated, not far to the north is an area that bears the scars of civilisation. East to west, atop a low dike, an old and rotting fence marks the boundary of a small-holding that has apparently long lain abandoned to the ravages of nature, and the predations of whatever beasts roam the countryside hereabouts.
118202: The bleak and windswept plains begin to descend to the north suddenly, where a rocky incline defines the transition that leads to a shallow trench. At the margin of the gully, the thin limbs of a low patch of brambles snake out amid the heather and creep around the tussocks of coarse, yellow-green grass.
118203: A deep trench opens out to the north, a ragged wound that dissects this flat, and otherwise largely featureless tract of land. For miles in every direction this fissure represents the only break in the monotony of a landscape marked by nothing more distinguishing than the few small brambles that grow amid the endless sea of heather and bracken.
118204: The land dips and rolls in a series of heather-clad folds that stretch away north and west, growing both wider and deeper as they draw near to a yawning trench. Low, rugged tussocks of grass peep up along the lines defined by the little gullies, cutting a yellowing scar across the ground, and bending in the blustery winds that seem to perpetually swirl across this bleak expanse.
118205: A field of stumps that stands to the east gradually gives way to an expanse of grass and heather-clad land, with a scattering of low, thorny shrubs. Isolated tussocks of coarse grass, and a number of small, shallow clefts in the rolling landscape conspire in their attempt to trip the unwary traveller.
118206: This land was once a part of a thick forest, the last vestige of which looms at some distance to the east. But every tree here was felled long ago, leaving only a field of hefty stumps. The demise of the trees has made way for the growth of a profusion of small, sturdy brambles and a confused carpet of tangled weeds that blankets the ground.
118207: Looking east, across the road, a dank and musty forest rises out of the land. Here, however, where once the woodland continued, there now remains only fields of dark and scorched stumps. The mighty trees met with the bite of cold iron, felled by axe; many of the massive stumps that remained have been licked by fire. Further to the south, drawing close to a small stone structure, the destruction becomes more marked, as if protecting that building from the denizens of the forest were the motivation behind the assault.
118208: Patches of dark bracken compete with heather, grass and moss to blanket the gently undulating land. A few rangy brambles stretch their thorny limbs across the ground, grasping out at passing feet with their sharp barbs. To both west and north the otherwise gently rolling landscape plunges rather more abruptly, opening out into quite a deep and decidedly steep-walled gully.
118209: Small, scattered patches of briars stand amid the coarse grass and heather that dominate the landscape. This thin shroud of vegetation is not enough to mask the small fissures and rolling undulations in the ground. Running from east to west, these folds grow much larger to the north. In the distance, one of them opens up to form a much deeper chasm.
118210: While much of the surrounding land supports no plant life except thick tussocks of coarse grasses, here a mass of thorny bushes has sprung up, extending from the denser tangle of furze that thrives in the shallow gully to the north. The briars reach off into the distance to the east and south, where they fight for dominance with coarse weeds that flourish in a field of stumps. A ridge running along the western side prevents passage in that direction.
118211:
The corpse of a striped snake is lying here.
The corpse of a dreadful snake is lying here.

Opening out to the west, the gully spans little over a yard here at its eastern end. The northern boundary of the gully gains height as it continues to rise to the west, blocking any passage to the north from here. To the south is a gentle grade which leads out of the shallow trench. Even though the channel is very shallow, it has nevertheless served to accumulate a thicker and richer covering of soil and to collect the waters running off the lands to either side. As a result a thick tangle of brush has sprouted up in this area. The trench curves along the eastern side, lined along the top with thick shrubs and bushes, also impassable from this area of the trench.
118212: Ruined Remains of a Thick Forest

The corpse of a burly orc is lying here.
The corpse of a burly orc is lying here.

Massive stumps stand all around, the last tokens of what was once an area of thick woodland. Where once the trees were dominant, now a bristling field of thorny briars has taken control of the landscape. Coarse weeds weave a snarled mess about the stems of the brambles, many climbing and curling over the ruined tree stumps. A tall ridge stands behind the vegetation here.
118213: A tall plateau looms above the plains just east of here. Its sheer wall offers few visible hand or footholds, and appears quite impossible to climb. Although the plateau affords the land here some degree of protection from the prevailing winds, it casts a deep shadow for much of the day, depriving the vegetation of light. All that survives here grows weak and tall, as if striving to find its way to the sun.
118214: The land rolls down from the north in mighty waves. But here they seem to halt abruptly, due to a large ridge that forms along the north-west that curves along the southern area of land here, and then it travels to the north rising higher as it goes. Rocks and boulders take up a lot of the space between the coarse grasses, shrubs and briars scattered over the land.
118215:
The mother wolf stands here, protecting her young cubs.
A great black and silver wolf is standing here, at the head of the pack.

Whilst the terrain hereabouts is characterised by coarse grasses, growing in scattered clumps, here the landscape has a softer countenance. Purple heather fights for dominance with a blanket of lush, dark green grass. Such a contrast between this area and much of the surrounding lands suggests that at one time this land was farmed. Yet there is no trace of recent use, hinting that the acreage has long since been abandoned.
118216: A wolf cub happily plays here.

A deep, steep-sided gully dominates the land to the south, like a massive scar that stretches east and west across the plains. East and west a vast expanse of thick, dark green grass and purple heather lies, offering no promise of shelter from the prevailing winds that sweep across the countryside. In the distant north, the last vestiges of some ancient habitation stand amongst the ruins.
118217: A wolf cub happily plays here.

Bordered to the north by a low earth bank and to the south by a wide and rather deep gully, the land here is an ocean of dark purple heather, mingled with dark green grass. These lands are so much lusher than the surrounding countryside that they must once have been pastures for the abandoned farming community that lies to the northwest. Further west the vegetation becomes considerably more coarse, as if there the local flora had more quickly regained complete domination.
118218: Stretching east and west, a low bank rises above the current elevation. In the distance beyond, a few crumbled ruins can be seen. It is apparent that this land was once part of a farm or smallholding as the ruins of an old, stone wall stand at the brink of a deep gully that lies to the south. It is equally clear that it has been many long years since anyone tended this acreage, as the lush grasses that must once have blanketed the entire areas are now fighting for dominance with the dark purple heather that is so common hereabouts.
118219: Just a short march to the north, a low, earthen embankment stretches from east to west across the land. Though the bank is not especially high, a sturdy pile of timber and stone has been heaped along its length, creating a crude, but nevertheless quite impenetrable barrier. Yet this would seem to have been an odd act, for the lands nearby were apparently once part of the now ruined smallholding that lies to the north.
118220:
The corpse of a striped snake is lying here.
The corpse of a mottled snake is lying here.
The corpse of a striped snake is lying here.
The corpse of a mottled snake is lying here.
A swallow flies high above the ground.

Amid a nearly impenetrable labyrinth of briars, it is difficult to see the walls of the trench. From an occasional thin spot in the prickly vegetation it is possible to see that the gully makes a noticeable turn here, travelling to the south and to the east. Its walls are quite tall, and only by climbing can the plains beyond be reached.
118221:
A small plant grows here, with long, pointed leaves and flowers at its top.
A large brown snake with black patches is coiled here.

So steep and tall are the walls of the trench that the entire area is enveloped in shadow for much of the day. Yet despite this a thick snarl of briars thrives in the gully, their sharp and grasping barbs making travel along the fissure difficult at best. Loose rocks and scree characterise the walls both north and south, making escape from the entangling shrubs by that route impossible.
118222: Although the trench is quite wide here, its walls are very steep, and comprised primarily of loose rocks and sharp scree, rendering ascent impossible. Deep shadows engulf this area for much of the day, but a dense tangle of prickly shrubs has come to dominate the area nevertheless; their thorny branches impede progress to the west, where the vegetation grows more prolific. To the east the gully becomes noticeably shallower, and the plant life slightly less dense.
118223:
The corpse of a mottled snake is lying here.
The corpse of a dreadful snake is lying here.
The corpse of a dreadful snake is lying here.

Turning from its north-south route to travel westward, the trench becomes noticeably shallower. Here, at its turning point, the gully remains deep, and its sides so sheer that only by climbing these walls could the plain above be reached. Journeying along the fissure is little easier, as a dense tangle of thorny bushes fills the ground from wall to wall, their sharp spines tearing at any creature that brushes by.
118224: The ground slopes upward to both the north and south. The slopes define the walls of a fairly shallow gully that rises higher to the east and west across the plains. Sloping at a gentler grade, the land climbs out of the cleft to the west, but to the east the fissure grows deeper with sharp brambles that almost fills the cleft, becoming ever more tightly packed and making progress that way rather difficult.
118225: The land rolls gently down toward a fairly shallow gully that runs west and north-east across the countryside. Heather and coarse grass covers the ground all about, but the long, spindly arms of a dense tangle of briers grope from the margins of the trench, their sharp thorns seeming to strive for any flesh that they might be able to tear into.
118226:
A filthy straw pallet is lying here.
A noticeable crack runs down one of the walls.
A water barrel has been left here.

The floor of this little grotto is covered in a thin coating of soft, red-brown dust and its walls are quite dry. Apparently someone has made their home here, for a heavy animal skin has been set across the mouth of the cave to shelter it from the winds outside. A thick bed of dried grass lies by the rear wall, while a small ring of stones sits close to the entrance. A number of small fissures fairly high in the front wall expose the interior to any natural light outside.
118227: Dark, dry, and an extension from the cavern to the west this small cave looks as if it was meant to be larger. The walls all appear to be half dug out along the base to the middle section of the cavern and then continue toward the top but in a very narrow manner. An echo from the continuous scuffling from above can be heard from this portion of the cave.
118228:
The corpse of an orkish scout is lying here.
The remains of a black fungus lie here in a heap of rotting compost.
A sprawling green bush of stinging nettle grows here.
An ancient fungus smothers the boulders.
An ancient fungus smothers the boulders.

Set on a gently rising plain, this must once have been a well-tended garden. It has now fallen into decay, its terraced beds overgrown with brush, weeds and tough grasses. A wooden fence stands around the plot, its planks loose and rotting, and a dead tree stands toward the middle of the garden. Thorny shrubs with vines and ivy that twist between branches now grow along the southern portion of the garden, restricting movement any further in that direction. To the east stands an averaged size shed, worn from the weather and time, attached to a much larger building behind it.
118229: The flat plains start to give way here to a rising bluff that climbs toward a rocky plateau. The slope climbs steadily southward, the ground covered by a shaggy stubble of grassy tussocks. To the east an old wooden fence marks the boundary between the wild lands and a small oasis of what might once have been termed civilisation.
118230: A low cliff rises out of the plain, a red-brown wall of sandstone pocked with numerous cracks and fissures. As it sweeps northeast the rock face loses height and begins to merge into an area characterised by a gentler grade. Thorny shrubs grow along the foot of the cliff, and a proliferation of grasses and weeds form a patchwork carpet underfoot.
118231: Rising quite precipitously out of the plains, an immense plateau presents an imposing, and rather tall, red-brown wall of sandstone. Climbing even higher to the west, the cliff bears countless small cracks and fissures; many of these could offer good hand and footholds to a climber, others might even hint at the presence of some hidden fissure or cavern. Tough gorse bushes march along the foot of the scarp.
118232: Low, thorny shrubs are scattered amid a field of broken rock slabs and clumps of coarse, straw-coloured grass. Some of the largest and flattest of the rocks are concentrated so as to trace a barely discernible line, west and northeast across the land, hinting that perhaps, at some time long ago, there might have been a rough trail here.
118233: Brush and boulder compete with heather and grass to dominate the landscape, but ultimately it is the yellow-green tussocks that hold sway, the coarse tufts sprouting out and clinging to life all around. Rough accumulations of red-brown rock pockmark the terrain, and a dense collection of them has created an arc across the land, from south-west to east.
118234: The land for miles around is blanketed by a patchwork quilt of purple heather and tufts of yellow-green grass. Here and there a low patch of brambles stands proud above the ground cover, stubbornly clinging to life in this bleak and windswept landscape. The vista is hardly inviting, with no sign of any nearby shelter, or even clean running water. The only possible refuge from the weather would be by seeking shelter in the lea of a plateau to the south, but a bare rock face would surely provide scant comfort.
118235: A lofty plateau towers high above, and its sheer cliff face forms a wall that sweeps to the northeast, and stretches away to the west. The sandstone bears innumerable cracks and fissures, and in several places mighty slabs of the rock appear close to breaking away entirely. A number of massive plates of the same red-brown sandstone lie amid the bushes that surround the foot of the cliff, as if to support to the idea that this is not a rock face that should be climbed.
118236: The corpse of a hungry warg is lying here.

Mighty slabs of reddish-brown rock lie scattered amongst the grass and bushes here. To the west, the grass and bushes become more dense, with large boulders sitting between the patches of tangled brush. More earth and rock can be noticed to the south, where slabs have been piled up slightly, forming a narrow pass to an area that is more open. The land appears to incline slightly towards the east.
118237: As a line of cliffs turns away to the south, the band of prickly furze that stands along its foot stretches westward. As brush and rock wall diverge, the vegetation becomes more scattered, giving way to more of the coarse grasses that characterise these lands. Drawing south, the ground also becomes markedly rockier, with boulders of ever increasing size scattered amongst the bushes.
118238: This land is not the meadow that might have been expected standing leeward of the plateau. Perhaps that it lies in shadow so much of the time can account for the insipid colour of the grass and of the bushes that line the base of the cliffs. But the soil should be richer and deeper in a spot so sheltered from the prevailing winds, more suited to lush vegetation. Instead, a few thin patches of grass grow between rugged mounds of rock, and everywhere else lies nothing but a bed of smaller stones and gravel. A structure was constructed to the south, behind the natural rock and earthen-walls that form here, secured by a sturdy gate.
118239: A vast table of rock is here, with piles of slabs in the northern corners, which appears to form a narrow pass to the northern plains. The plateau curves to the southwest of here, and not too far into the distance it comes to an end in a high, rocky promontory that must afford a commanding view of all of the surrounding lands. The red-brown stone underfoot bares only the hardiest of plant life, and nearing the edge of the mesa the ground underfoot becomes quite unstable.
118240:
The corpse of a demon wolf is lying here.
The corpse of a demon wolf is lying here.

Sloping almost imperceptibly upward to the west, the plateau here stands high above the surrounding plains. The red-brown sandstone is covered by only the barest trace of topsoil, buffeted as it is by the harsh prevailing winds. And so only the hardiest of vegetation can cling to life here, with tough roots that force their way down into minute cracks in the rock. The rim of the mesa is particularly cracked, and appears to be quite unstable.
118241:
The corpse of a young mountain lion is lying here.
The corpse of a mountain lioness is lying here.

The flat table top that defines the plateau slopes gently and leads upward to the west, so that by this point it rises to a significant height above the surrounding lands both north and south. A river flows along the southern foot of the plateau. The waters look quite deep at this point, so that it should be fairly safe to make the jump down, but the sheer, moss-covered rock-face would probably prevent any ascent back to this area.
118242: The land surrounding this plateau presents a bleak and windswept aspect. Little vegetation can thrive on this stark and rocky plateau. High above the surrounding plains, the land here is buffeted by the very harshest of the wind, rain and snow. As a result, the topsoil is thin and only a few small, hardy, pine-looking plants cling to life among the rocks.
118243: The plateau stretches out far to the east and south. To the west and north it comes to an abrupt end at the top of a cliff. The rocky precipice looks quite unstable, but some places appear less fragile than others. Red-brown rocks and small boulders lie littered across the ground, and little plant life clings to life in this bleak and windswept location.
118244:
The corpse of an orc sentry is lying here.
The corpse of an orkish patrol-leader is lying here.
The corpse of an orkish scout is lying here.
A large rabbit looks peacefully at you, ready to dart away.

Red-brown rocks and a few small boulders lie scattered across the ground with virtually no vegetation to be seen. The land here atop the plateau is punished by all that the weather can throw at it, and only bare rock remains, making it impossible for all but the hardiest of pine-like plants to cling to life.
118245: A bleak, windswept countenance characterises the land here atop the plateau. Loose rocks and small boulders lie scattered all about, but there is little plant life to be seen. Instead of lush green grass, or even the coarse yellow tussocks that can be seen on the plain below, the ground here is the same red- brown colour of the rocks.
118246: The land rises gently to the west and south, climbing toward the top of a flat and windswept table of ground. Thick tussocks of coarse, yellow grass cling to life like a stubbly beard on the stony slope from here to the plains below. A few tiny patches of low weeds sprout up amid this growth, but no taller plant life is to be seen.
118247: Climbing gently to the west and falling away to the east, this tongue of land marks the end of a long, flat plateau that stretches into the distance to the west. Red-brown rocks lie scattered amid the coarse grass and thin weeds that cover the ground. But no bush or shrub can cling to life on this bleak and windswept slope.
118248: Medium-sized pine trees line a rim of this corner near the road along the north and east side of the glade. An old structure can be noticed between the pines to the north, and large boulders stand between them to the east. Just west of here, an ancient and long-since-abandoned road begins its gradual ascent toward a flat table of higher ground, the pathway having nearly vanished from view. The land falls away toward a river, snaking through the country to the south, as it climbs slightly toward the mouth of a long vale to the east.
118249:
A large mother hawk is here looking for prey to feed her young.
A large rabbit looks peacefully at you, ready to dart away.

The land slopes gently here, rising in the north to well above the height of the river. Dipping down almost to the level of the water to the south, much of the ground is quite muddy. A thick carpet of long grass grows all about, but toward the water's edge it is forced to compete with the sedges that flourish in the wetter ground.
118250:
A brook trout is here, swimming in the current.
A brook trout is here, swimming in the current.

The river flows from east to south, gathering momentum as it travels onward through its narrow, rocky channel. The bank to the north looms steep and tall above the water, the cold stone slick with moss. However, though the western bank is equally hard and rocky, withstanding the efforts of the roiling waters to push their way relentlessly forward, it nevertheless stands at a lesser height above the surface of the river.
118251: The prominent fin of a silver-yellow fish breaks the surface of the water.

The waters of a small river are funnelled through a fairly narrow valley here. The vale is hemmed in both north and south by tall, hilly ridges, and at the valley floor only a rather thin, rocky channel remains for the waterway, causing it to dash and splash as it makes its way westward on towards the distant Bruinen.
118252: The prominent fin of a silver-yellow fish breaks the surface of the water.

Tumbling along a narrow, rocky channel the small river rushes on through the narrowing valley. Dashing against rocks and boulders, both on the streambed and along its shores, the waters roil about, casting a fine, cool mist into the air throughout the vale.
118253: This small but lively river runs from east to west through the valley, making its way inexorably down toward its eventual meeting with the mighty Bruinen. To the west its channel steepens and its course becomes narrower, forcing the waters to rush ever faster on their way, dashing against rocks, and creating a fine mist which hangs like a haze over the whole valley.
118254: A large rabbit looks peacefully at you, ready to dart away.

East and north, the ground climbs gently toward a flat table of land that looms above the plains. To the south a small, but lively river cuts its channel along the foot of the plateau where the ground suddenly drops. Between the deep fall and large boulders at the edge of the plateau here to the river below, passage to the south would be impossible from here. Thick patches of vibrant purple heather compete with tussocks of coarse, yellow grass, and this blanket of vegetation hides the red-brown rock beneath it almost completely.
118255: Sloping steeply upward to the north and west, the ground climbs towards the top of a large table of land that looms above the plains. To the south the slope falls away, approaching a merry little river that cuts along the foot of the plateau. Between the drop and cliff wall, it is impossible to reach the river below safely from here. Grey rocks and stones tumble amid the coarse tussocks of yellow grass. Scattered patches of purple heather soften the rocky ground.
118256:
The corpse of a young mountain lion is lying here.
The corpse of a mountain lioness is lying here.

A flat table of land stretches out far to the north, east, and west. To the south, a small river travels along the foot of the plateau. Sloping gently downward to the east, the plateau here stands high above the river. The ground above is peppered with loose rocks, and there is virtually no vegetation of any type to be seen.
118257: A small river snakes along the foot of the plateau below. The ground slopes gently upward to the west, as the flat table of land rises above the plain, and even here it stands quite tall above the surrounding lands. A few thin tussocks of coarse, yellow grass nestle amid the tumbled rocks and stones, but no other vegetation is to be seen. The cliff edge is ragged and uneven, and it seems that standing too close might cause some of the stone to break away.
118258: A vast, flat table of land stands high above the plains and stretches off to the east. Reaching its highest point here, it also comes to an abrupt end. Loose, crumbling, red-brown rock defines the margin of the plateau, and little vegetation clings to life on this windswept land. At the westernmost edge of the mesa a massive boulder rests on the ground. The sounds of rippling water can be heard below where a brimming waterfall is noticed.
118259:
Clusters of slender stems and tall leaves thrive in the mud and shallows.
A large mother hawk is here looking for prey to feed her young.

Rising quite steeply to the west, the land gains the top of a plateau. The fragmented remains of an ancient road sweep past this expanse of land, defining a border to both west and north. A third boundary is marked by the waters of a lively little river whose waters have apparently breached the bank on many occasions, to leave the margins of this land almost swampy. There it is coarse sedge that flourishes. But in the rest of this area thick grass predominates.
118260:
A large thorny branched shrub is growing here.
On the shrub, there are two piles of blackberries.
A swarm of mosquitoes is here, humming around you.

Some thorny bushes are scattered here and there in these grasslands, but not much else grows here. The grass itself is patchy and not very dense. There is little to obstruct the passage of the wind as it blows through the land.
118261: A long stretch of sharp-bladed grass cuts its way through the plains here flanked by patches of dirt. The ground is quite uneven with small mounds rising and dipping into tiny ditches all around. Some rocky hills can be seen to the north but the horizon is dominated by the Misty Mountains to the east.
118262: The hills here are quite dense with no even footing to be had. Boulders, rocks, and pebbles cover the slopes with the occasional patch of grass or lonely bush. The land to the east and west is steep and covered in loose scree but easy passage can be seen traversing to the north or south.
118263:
A sharp-eyed hawk is here stalking some prey.
A mountain goat is here, jumping from cliff to cliff.
A mountain goat is here, jumping from cliff to cliff.

A small but lively river winds along the northern flank of the ridge. The slope down to the water is so steep that only a slippery coating of dark green moss clings to life on the rocky face. The southern slope is less severe, but still quite steep, and peppered with so many loose rocks and boulders that a descent, though possible, should only be undertaken with great care. Both east and west of here, the land climbs up out of this rocky saddle.
118270:
A mountain goat is here, jumping from cliff to cliff.
A sharp-eyed hawk is here stalking some prey.
A mountain goat is here, jumping from cliff to cliff.

The rocky ridge comes to an abrupt end here. Its northern and western flanks are sheer, falling away to a river that skirts along its feet, far below. A coating of slippery, dark green moss is all that clings to those rocky walls. To the south the slope is gentler, yet the innumerable rocks and small boulders that are scattered across its surface would make descent to the plain beyond at least a little risky.
118271: Tailing off to the west, the hills rise sharply eastward, and within a very short distance the ground ahead is almost bare of vegetation. To the south the slope stands steeper still, blocking travel in that direction, but to the north the land makes a more gentle descent towards the bottom of a narrow valley.
118272: The land rises gently to the east as it climbs along the length of the vale. To the south it slopes more steeply, as the valley floor gives way to the flanks of a tall range of hills. A lively river rushes through the narrowing glen, its waters leaving a fine mist behind them.
118277: The only way to climb these hills is to scramble from rock to rock. Massive boulders and loose scree are scattered everywhere, and very little vegetation has managed to take hold in the thin soil. The land rises sharply to the east and falls away more gradually to the west, as it descends toward the plains below. The terrain to the south rises sharply into some hills.
118278:
On the ground, there are two piles of pine nuts.
A grizzly cub is here, snarling loudly.
A grizzly cub is here, snarling loudly.
A huge grizzly bear is here, roaming the wild.

A line of pine trees along the western side of the glade rise next to the walls of an old structure. The structure is hard to discern from here between the pine trees and large boulders. The wood appears aged, as if the building has been there for quite a long time. To the south the medium-sized pines grow more thick toward the east, blocking any travel from here to the south directly. The pine trees curve around the north side of the glade and continue east. To the east there are weeds and patches of coarse grass.
118279:
You see two piles of pine nuts on the ground.
A diamond-back rattlesnake is coiled here, ready to strike.

The land here is bare in the centre and surrounded by a thick line of silvery pines, smaller trees, and thorny shrubs along the west, south and east. Some boulders are also scattered along the tree line, large and all differ in shape from one another, which also prevents any travel in either of those three directions. The sound of water can be heard somewhere to the west or south.
118280: A brook trout is here, swimming in the current.

As the river flows from the north back to a westerly path, its surging waters undercut the southerly bank, creating a small rocky prominence that looms above the channel. The banks stand sheer above the waterway, their faces covered in slippery moss, making ascent impossible, but here and there wide cracks can be seen in the rock face, as if parts of the wall were loose.
118281: A brook trout is here, swimming in the current.

The channel starts to widen here, and as it does so the waters of the river begin to lose momentum. To the south a tall hilly ridge looms above the river, and its sheer, stony face sternly blocks the water. To the north, the bank descends almost to the level of the water. It also begins to yield a little, allowing the river to occasionally forge a breach as if seeking a path back to the north.
118282:
The prominent fin of a silver-yellow fish breaks the surface of the water.
The prominent fin of a silver-yellow fish breaks the surface of the water.
A brook trout is here, swimming in the current.
The prominent fin of a silver-yellow fish breaks the surface of the water.

As the river flows from the east, it strives to cut a pathway forward through the rocky bank ahead, but the cold, wet stone stubbornly stands against the writhing waters, forcing them to turn aside. They burgeon to the north, where the bank seems softer, making the ground beyond quite swampy. But in the end the path of least resistance is to the south.
118283: A lively little river flows from the north, steadily losing momentum, as it enters an ever wider channel. To the south, where the foot of a craggy ridge of hills slopes down to meet the plains, a cold, unyielding, rocky shore forces the waters to turn westward, where they approach an old, decrepit roadway.
118287: A swallow flies high above the ground.

Travelling at the bottom of a rising plain to the north, and hemmed in to the south by the footings of an ancient roadway, the river is funnelled into a narrower, but deeper channel. As the waters tumble down from the raised river bed of the ford that lies just east of here, they swirl about, finding their way in this deeper course. Though not yet too much deeper than the ford, the river is nevertheless just a bit too deep and a little too lively to permit wading.
118288:
The prominent fin of a silver-yellow fish breaks the surface of the water.
A bass swims here.
A bass swims here.
A swallow flies high above the ground.

The bank to the north grows taller and steeper as the river travels westward along the foot of the plateau. An ancient roadway, by now in a very poor state of repair, journeys beside the river here, and its stony footings form a firm bank that will not permit the channel to grow wider. In this confined course, the waters continue to flow along at a lively pace, but further westward the channel begins to widen.
118289:
A brook trout is here, swimming in the current.
A bass swims here.
A brook trout is here, swimming in the current.

East and west, the river telescopes into the distance. Its northern bank here is tall, steep and rocky, climbing to the top of a large plateau. But to the south the bank is softer and lower, and the waters have taken advantage of this to cut a wider channel through which they can flow lazily along.
118290: River by the Foot of a Plateau

The prominent fin of a silver-yellow fish breaks the surface of the water.
A bass swims here.
The prominent fin of a silver-yellow fish breaks the surface of the water.

A tall cliff looms above the surface of the river as it journeys westward along the foot of a tall plateau. The rock wall is almost vertical, but pitted with numerous small fissures, suggesting that an ascent might be possible. To the south a lower bank borders the waters, and a faint trail can be seen travelling beside the watercourse.
118291: Deep and Lazy Stretch of Water

The prominent fin of a silver-yellow fish breaks the surface of the water.
A bass swims here.

Sheltered from northerly winds by a plateau which looms above it to the north, the river flows lazily westward. Its waters here are quite deep, and a pair of heavy wooden pilings disappear into its murky depths a short distance from the southern bank. A few broken and rotten shards of wood bob gently, tugged by the current, but held weakly to the pilings by rusty, square-headed nails.
118292: The prominent fin of a silver-yellow fish breaks the surface of the water.

Turning south, the water brims here against the western cliff wall and plateau to the north, before it spills over more cliffs that form a waterfall. Green vines scale the cliff and disappear beyond to the north, and the cliff wall appears to continue far to the east along the river. The water here is deep and clear, with tiny bubbles that keep bursting at the surface.
118294:
A nest is here.
An ibex is watching you from afar.
An ibex is watching you from afar.
A big, nasty vulture is sitting here, protecting its nest.
A swallow flies high above the ground.

The sheer rock wall has tapered outwards as it gained elevation, such that a narrow ledge perches here, about three quarters of the way to the cliff top. Buffeted by the elements, this slender shelf would seem a precarious and most inhospitable location. Yet even here where no visible soil remains a tiny thicket of stunted bushes clings to life.
118301: The roar of a waterfall to the north drowns out many sounds. Boulders and swift currents dominate this area. To the impassable north, water plummets down into the boulder-strewn riverbed. Looking east, a trail is visible. To the west lies a swampy region, while a look south reveals a grassy plain.
118302: A canoe has been left here.

The deep river flows by a small landing, where boats can be left. The landing is constructed from oaken poles that are connected to one another by strong ropes. The landing has several extra ropes that can be used to secure boats. A little hovel just next to the landing has an entrance on the south side. The river's westward flow continues as it passes the sloping fields on its north bank.
118303: The large river flows westward, this particular part of it being a home to a wide collection of water plants that grow within. Some tracks can be seen along the banks, showing that many animals come here to feed. The grass is fed by the river, and is lush and green, yet everything around it is barren and dry. A small landing can be spotted some distance to the east.
118304: A wide river flows here, lying in between the endless plains of brown, dry grass. Infested with water plants, it attracts many animals. The river gently streams from the mountains to the east. The riverbed is scattered with flat stones and small rocks, while the riverside is covered with lilies and patches of green grass. The chirps of nearby birds can sometimes be heard.
118305:
A bass swims here.
A bass swims here.

The river flows gently, and the current is not too strong here. The water is deep, making it impossible to wade through. It is inhabited by small water animals and fish, who feed either on each other or on the many plants in the water. The river, coming from the east, continues to the west. At the sides of the river some patches of lush green grass grow, although further away, the grass becomes brown and dry.
118306: The large river that streamed from the east gently approaches a small tributary in the west. Another river can be seen to the south, soon to join with this one. The current is not strong, yet it is too deep and wide to allow wading through the river. The plains surrounding the rivers, nourished by the water, are greener than elsewhere. The sounds of rapids can be heard from the west.
118307: A small creek flowing from the south joins a larger river flowing from the east, creating a wider waterway that continues westward. The rapidly streaming white water is strewn with large rocks. The force of the river has washed away a great deal of earth, undermining the riverbanks considerably. Sloping fields stretch out in all directions.
118308: The stream has become extremely fast and violent, due to the joining of the two rivers. The water hurls around the rocks sticking out of the riverbed, creating white coats of foam. The current is very strong and the noise of the water makes it impossible to hear anything else. The river flows to the west, and to the east lies a delta where the two smaller rivers joined.
118309: A little slower than the rapids to the east, this stream is still a force to be reckoned with. It is both deep and wide, making it impossible to wade. Endless plains of dry grass appear at the sides of the stream. Large rocks lie in the water, preventing safe passage with a vessel.
118310: The prominent fin of a silver-yellow fish breaks the surface of the water.

The river, flowing rapidly, makes a brusque turn here, continuing to the north. Swirled away by the violent stream, it is hard to avoid being smacked against the sharp rocks protruding from the surface. The violent waves smash against the cliff wall that looms to the south. Seemingly endless plains lie to the west, some of them nourished by the river.
118311:
A large brown snake with black patches is coiled here.
A fallow deer is grazing peacefully here.

Well-nourished by the stream which flows all around save to the south, these plains have become quite lush and fertile. Thousands of flowers can be seen all over, the buzzing of nearby insects never allowing this place to be completely quiet. The plains continue to the south, the influence of water diminishing in the increasing distance.
118312:
A orc patrol-leader of the Ohurk-uai is looking for enemies here.
An orc soldier of the Ohurk-uai is here, patrolling the area.
An orc soldier of the Ohurk-uai is here, patrolling the area.
An orc soldier of the Ohurk-uai is here, patrolling the area.
An orc soldier of the Ohurk-uai is here, patrolling the area.

Sloping grasslands stretch out as far as the eye can see, sparsely populated by small thickets of bushy vegetation. Some isolated trees grow here and there, but most of the land is covered only by small patches of brown, dry grass. Several piles of small rocks are scattered through the area, brought by a river that once flowed here. The hard ground, a mixture of clay and limestone, makes ploughing near impossible.
118313:
A huge stone stands upright atop the hill, jutting into the sky.
A sturdy billy goat stands here, proudly protecting his goats.
A young goat playfully charges and hops away.
A goat is here, grazing in the hills.

This hill stands tallest amongst its peers and is topped by an enormous stone. The stone stands near the edge of a cliff that plunges down nearly vertically into a river. Dry grass covers the gentle slope of the hill in other directions leading to plains to the west and more hills to the east.
118314:
A small oaken table has been set here.
On the table, there are two large pieces of smoked, cured meat and two potatoes.
A wiry smuggler is here, attempting to avoid being seen.
An experienced husky smuggler is here, conspiring with his cohorts.

The hovel is smaller inside than it looked from the outside. The majority of the tools that are strewn about the floor and walls were used for fieldwork and fishing. The western wall's modest window offers a clear glimpse of the big river as it rushes down its course. The remaining space is taken up by benches and shelving.
118315: An old rundown shack with no door stands on the river's bank to the north.

This small trail consists mostly of dry grasses and an occasional stone or weed. However to the north the grass becomes greener as it grows near the banks of a slow-moving river. An old, but useable landing provides a way for boats to cross the river just below a waterfall to the west. In the distance to the east an ancient, broken road makes its way north and south.
118316: Bowing planks of rotting wood create the decaying skeleton of a small shack. The shack's roof has all but integrated into the earth; the majority of it is sinking into the moist ground. A sharp slope connects the ground-laden roof with its counterpart, stubbornly clinging to the tips of the bowing planks of rotting wood.
118317: A slim chasm here is surrounded by slimy, muddy walls, and in spots, rivulets of brown water streak down into the depths below. The water droplets carry the brown sediment along with them, no doubt further eroding the sides of this unstable hole.
118318: Small pools of fetid, dark water have collected here on the soggy ground, fed by a constant stream of dripping water from above. Footprints of all sizes dot the squishy surface, and in the western corner of the cave, a wide hole delves deeper into the recesses of the ground.
118319: Large pools of dark, sediment-laden water have collected in the many wide depressions here. Thin streams of water constantly break free from the dirt ceiling high above, causing a constant sloshing in the roiling pools below. The cave opens to the north, and a hole in the ceiling on the western wall provides access to a dark continuation of this cave.
118320: Many rocks lie scattered on the floor here, and a few rotten shards of wood poke out of the sediment. Here and there odd fragments of metal glint amid the stones. To the north, an old iron gate is visible. The walls are made of smooth rock, and a wide crack snakes its way from the ceiling to the floor. Strong wooden beams have been set here to support the roof against collapse.
118321: This coffin-shaped tunnel leads steadily to the north and south, whilst a side passage leads to the west. Rusted remnants of two parallel iron rails travel along the tunnel, attesting to its former status as a part of a mine. The rails end in the south, where some time in the past, a door was manufactured to keep a mine tightly closed. A pool of water has accumulated on the floor, water dripping slowly into it from the ceiling.
118322:
A shiny gold ring has been abandoned here.
A skeleton of some humanoid lies in the dust.
An ancient fungus smothers the boulders.
A huge black fungus is here, exuding a foul stench.
An ancient fungus smothers the boulders.

Though this chamber is fairly small, it is nevertheless too large for its roof to stay aloft unsupported. For this reason the miners left eight large pillars of the native sandstone equally spaced through the cavern. Each wall is scarred by the marks of pick and hammer, but the natural beauty of the rock strata, each a slightly different shade than its neighbours, still stands out for those who care to look. The only way out of this cave appears to be through the flooded tunnel to the east; if anyone had been here when the tunnel flooded, they would have been forced to swim out, or remain here and perish.
118323: The hard rock walls here indicate the enourmous effort it must have taken to carve out this cave. The marks of picks and chisels are everywhere in the walls and the roof. The stone floor is smooth, providing an easy walking surface. The tunnel is high enough for a man with a horse to pass through. Short stairs have been made in the north, where the tunnel ascends quickly. The stairs end in a hole in the roof, which can be covered with a hatch.
118324: Bulky pillars of sandstone stand in a regular pattern throughout this large, square chamber, supporting the roof above. To the south a ramp way cuts into the level floor, descending into a passage beyond. A similar ramp climbs out of the cavern to the east. Rusty iron rails travel along both ramps, but to the south they quickly vanish beneath a pool of chilly, stagnant water that floods the tunnel beyond.
118325: This fairly wide tunnel descends to the east and climbs gently to the south, before levelling off once more. The walls to either side were pockmarked by the action of hammer and pick, and a deep recess in one wall houses a rickety wooden ladder that pokes its way through a large hole in the roof to grant access to a chamber above. Two heavy rails of rusted iron travel along the passageway, and must once have provided access for the mine cars that would have carried ore from the workings below.
118326: The tunnel opens out here into a massive, rectangular chamber. Vast amounts of ore must have been removed from this area during the years the mine was in use, but the roof is held firmly aloft by huge pillars of the native sandstone that have been left in place in a regular pattern throughout the chamber. Toward one corner a weighty block and tackle is suspended above a sizeable hole in the floor. A wooden ladder pokes up through the hole beside it.
118327: An almost coffin-shaped tunnel stretches to the east and south, branching into two just a short way ahead. The walls to either side are pitted and scored by the mark of pick and hammer, and sturdy old wooden posts shore up the roof in a few places. A pair of heavy, rusted iron tracks runs the length of the tunnel, resting on hefty wooden sleepers. Aged and decaying, all of wood in this tunnel creaks and groans as if it were struggling to maintain its burden.
118328:
A sturdy bandit bodyguard stands here, eager to hack you to pieces.
A sturdy bandit bodyguard stands here, eager to hack you to pieces.

Where to the north the passage slopes gently down into the earth, here it crests briefly, creating a level staging area for the mine carts, before making an almost imperceptible descent towards the end of the tunnel. A lone cart stands here, its wooden walls rotting away in the damp air. A soft breeze makes the vegetation at the tunnel mouth dance and shiver. And an occasional stronger gust of wind rattles by.
118330:
A mountain lioness pads quietly through the terrain.
A mountain lion eyes you closely and prepares to pounce for his next meal.

Standing some ten feet above even the highest part of the plateau, this place affords a breathtaking view of the lands all around. Over fifteen feet across, this monstrous slab of rock has been scoured flat by the elements. Tiny cracks and fissures, the scars of countless cycles of frost and thaws, pit the ruddy surface. But not a single plant, even to the smallest poppy or tiniest clump of stonecrop, can be seen anywhere. Not a single patch of phlox clings to life here.
118332: The trail extends to the east and west, bordered to the north by a lazy river. To the south, in the middle of this otherwise barren landscape, lies a small forest, probably gaining its strength from underground streams seeking their own paths away from the river. Past the water, a steep plateau can be seen in the distance. Green, healthy grass grows near the banks of the water.
118333: Markings of a seldom used trail start here and head off towards the west. Bare patches of earth interrupt the otherwise solid growth of dry grass, which grows in contrast to the greener grass on the banks of the river in the north. The dry grass and occasional stone of an ancient, broken road lie eastwards.
118334: The murky water bubbles and foams as it flows down the widening river at a steady pace from a narrow channel in the east. Some rapids that can be heard from further upstream that cause the surface of the water to be covered in white foam. Not much can be seen below the surface of the water.
118335: The rivulet flows from east to west only to be interrupted by a grey boulder in its centre. The boulder protrudes out from the murky water, itself heavily clouded with brown silt, and causes the current to foam and splash. A few sticks and remains of dead plants drift along in the water.
118336: Something cold and scaly slithers past your leg.

Run-off and rain water from the lakes and slopes of the Misty Mountains have trickled down and accumulated into a pool here, where the land has been eroded into a slight depression. To the west the ground juts out and forms a small hill and a bank for the pool. As the water streams in, it is released once again to the north, as a small stream. The water is dirty and soiled from the sediment that has washed down from the hills and mountains to the east.
118337: A slow-moving stream starts its way down the barren land here, a result of the overflow of water running down the slopes of the towering Misty Mountains to the east. The water forms a pool in the south where the land is higher, then slowly gains speed as gravity forces it down into the grassy plains to the west. Foothills have formed to the south, dotted here and there with sparse foliage.
118338:
Clusters of slender stems and tall leaves thrive in the mud and shallows.
The corpse of a Dunadan sentry lies here next to the river bank.

Though a few stumps and rare patches of dirt are visible, most of the land here is covered in a thick film of soft sod. Wind snakes along the tops of the blades of grass making them dance and bow. A river can be seen to the north alongside a muddy bank. The ground rises to some rocky hills to the south.
118339: Shallow Crossing in a Muddy Stream

A large pike is lurking in the mud by the bottom.
A large, yellow crab is crawling around here.

A large amount of sediment and debris have pooled here in a shallow area around the stream creating a sort of marshy swamp. To the east and west can be heard running water, while passage south is impossible because of piled branches and detritus. Travel north leads to more of the ever present plains that dominate the region.
118340: A finch flies low above the ground.

The languid current of the muddy waters of this small stream gathers momentum here as the incline of the land increases markedly to the southwest. The slope of the lands to the west continues its downward journey, bottoming out into a soggy plain. The amount of sediment and debris carried by this stream begins to decrease, as evidenced by the continuously increasing clarity of the water.
118341: A finch flies low above the ground.

The water follows the steep decline of the surrounding landscape, flowing southward into the lower part of the valley. A tall hill rises up to the east, blocking the wind which normally blows down from the Misty Mountains in the distance. The land on either side of the stream is rendered inaccessible due to steep cuts in the land.
118342: A finch flies low above the ground.

The water is shallow and clear as it turns toward the west and continues for several miles. The surrounding land is soggy and overgrown with reeds and rushes. The occasional fish can be seen darting through the water in search of insects to nip. A steep bank of earth to the east and south makes travel impossible in that direction.
118343:
Clusters of slender stems and tall leaves thrive in the mud and shallows.
A large sturgeon swims slowly along the bottom.
A finch flies low above the ground.

The stream continues its westward flow, bordered to the north by a vast stretch of soggy marshland and to the south by a wide flat grassland. Reeds and other plant life grows steadily, rising out of the water and creeping up the bank. The sound of buzzing insects can be heard along the banks.
118344:
A brook trout is here, swimming in the current.
A finch flies low above the ground.
A finch flies low above the ground.

The stream flows steadily westward, gathering momentum as it travels through the soggy valley. A slight wind can usually be felt blowing from the east, where one can see the snow-covered peaks of the Misty Mountains far off in the distance. The clear water of the stream is bordered on the north and south by mostly barren plains. Steep, debris-choked banks prevent any travel north.
118345: Clusters of slender stems and tall leaves thrive in the mud and shallows.

The water of a small stream turns its course southward here, following the lay of the surrounding valley. The banks of the stream are soggy and covered in reeds and mud making passage over them impossible. In the distance to the northwest, a small grouping of tall trees has grown, seemingly out of place in the otherwise featureless valley.
118346: A finch flies low above the ground.

The small stream from the northeast collides with the mountain stream to the southeast here, creating an even larger body of water which continues its journey westward. Where the water meets, small currents and eddies are formed, churning the surface and creating a soft, white foam on. A wooden bridge has been built nearby, allowing travellers to cross.
118348: The current of the westward flowing river is intensified here, where the waters of two smaller streams, having joined forces just a short distance to the east, are channelled along their common course. The swift water boils and bubbles at the surface, sending white eddies and ripples to and fro. Above you a wooden bridge spans the river, blocking any view of the skies.
118350: The water rushes by quickly, flowing west with a renewed strength from the combining of the two smaller streams in the east. Foamy white caps of tiny waves ripple along the top of the otherwise clear water, dancing to and fro. The river banks rise up steeply here, hindering movement south.
118351:
A brook trout is here, swimming in the current.
A trout swims here.
A large sturgeon swims slowly along the bottom.

The river follows the contours of the land, flowing here from east to north in a sweeping curve. The combining of the rivers to the east has increased the current, making it harder to swim upstream. The southern and western banks rise steeply and are covered with slick mud, making access to the shore in those directions quite impossible.
118352: Evidence of mudslides can be seen on the bank of the water to the east, due to its steep slope. The water flows by, gradually following the lay of the land from the south to the west. An small drop in the land west of here forces the water to tumble down some rocks, creating a tiny waterfall.
118353: The clear water of the river grows shallower here due to a build-up of rock and sediment. A sudden break in the grass and thicket choked plains creates a tiny waterfall, some four feet high. The south bank rises high enough to block any passage in that direction.
118354: The shallow river flows from the east to the west. The surrounding fields are covered with patches of dry, brown grass and some small thorn bushes grow on the riverbanks. Several birds hover above the water, which is the home for many small water animals and various fish, searching for easy prey.
118355:
A salmon swims here.
A large sturgeon swims slowly along the bottom.

The river, having come from the east, flows to the north through steeply sloping fields. The current sweeps away a few branches and small logs. The water is not very deep nor wide, but enough so to prevent wading. The plains surrounding the river are dank and barren. The western and southern riverbank are too high and steep to allow climbing. The numerous plants that grow in the river provide food for little fish and other aquatic creatures, who are occasionally seen swimming in it.
118356: Snaking around amongst the plains, the small river flows from south to west. East of the creek lies a small, patch of grass. The surroundings consist of sloping fields which are lush and green due to the abundance of water. The water is quite clear and appears to be filled with life.
118357:
A heron is stalking the area, looking for fish.
A swallow flies high above the ground.

Coming from the east, the river slowly flows westwards. The grass surrounding the river is lush and green, due to the access to water. In the water, numerous diverse plant species flourish, luring numerous little animals who come for food. The steep riverbank to the south is high and slippery, making it impossible to climb southwards.
118358: The small river flows from the east to the west. Various plants grow in the water, forming the diet for the herbivorous fauna of the river. A sea of lush, green grass lies to the north. A sandy and slightly muddy riverbank lies to the south.
118359: Just southeast of where the Ancient Broken Road bends again on its long journey between south and north, wide brushlands spread out before you. The lands lie quite untouched and dense brush grows in abundance. Faint traces of old campfires can be seen here and there, where patches of bare earth, edged by yellowish grass, dot the landscape.
118360: A finch flies low above the ground.

Wide brushlands spread out between the stream to the east and the ancient road in the west. The land slopes quite dramatically down to lower grounds in the south and west where land and waterway are almost level, leaving the brush thick by the rich supply of water. To the north a vertical wall, probably the result of an age-old landslide, effectively prevents passage.
118361: Here, the brush gives way to more of the largely featureless plains that dominate the region. Grass rises from the red soil, mixed with the odd patch of brush here and there. An ancient, broken, road runs just to the west, obediently conforming to the meandering of the waterway. To the north are great thickets of brush, and a steep, muddy bank to the south blocks passage to the river.
118362: Surrounded to the east and south by muddy waters, this area is constantly covered by mud from regular flooding. So much so, that the dense mud makes passage south impossible. To the north, the land slopes up towards the ancient road some distance away. A lone hill rises just beyond the water to the east.
118363: Sharp rocks and large boulders litter the red earth of this field, making passage somewhat difficult. Easier paths for the ancient road and to the nearby water exist, leaving this area desolate and largely forgotten save for by the odd creature looking to stay out of common areas of travel.
118364: A skull is here, spiked to the end of a pole.

A small forest of trees grows here, providing a place hidden away from the sun for such creatures who prefer the darkness over the light. A cooking pit filled with scorched bones and charred bits of wood and flesh dominate the area. Logs and boulders are placed around it for some sort of seating arrangement. The skulls of unfortunate humanoids are randomly spiked about as some sort of savage decoration.
118365:
A nasty troll female crouches here, with a feral look in her eyes.
A swift and agile forest cat moves silently through the vegetation.
A young troll stares wide-eyed at the forest.

Surrounded by densely packed trees, this glade is impenetrable from all sides except from the south. Although the close forest is very tight, the ground here is trampled smooth by the feet of large humanoids. Trash and forest debris are piled into crude nests for the use of some sort of large and apparently foul smelling creatures. An acrid scent of urine and faeces competes with the smell of rotting vegetation and flesh.
118366: A flat, almost featureless plain sprawls before the river. Vegetation is richer due to the presence of water, but the soil still is red, and dusty in places during the warmer months. The riverbank to the west drops sharply by several feet, but to the south the ground draws more level with the water.
118367:
A dense carpet of blue flowers dip their heads in the breeze.
A scrawny goblin frantically tries to hide from the trolls.

Multiple giant feet have trampled the forest floor into a hard, compact mass devoid of vegetation. This is one of the hunting areas of the murderous forest trolls which infest forests across Arda, bringing evil and destruction wherever they go. Broken trees and branches are strewn about, mingled with equally shattered bones of animals and humanoids alike.
118368:
The corpse of a scrawny goblin is lying here.
A tree-snake lies wrapped around one of the tree branches.
A tree-snake lies wrapped around one of the tree branches.
A furry, striped raccoon is here, nosing around for some berries or roots.
A disgusting forest troll is searching for fresh meat here.
A swift and agile forest cat moves silently through the vegetation.

What could have been a beautiful, peaceful forest has been defiled by giant and destructive creatures that seem to care only to satisfy their violent and destructive urges. Trees bear scars from claws and teeth - mute testimony to the violence that takes place here when trolls go hunting or let their rage and stupidity overwhelm them in a frenzied orgy of violence.
118369:
A fallow deer is grazing peacefully here.
A fallow deer is grazing peacefully here.

Red dust and rocks are scattered across the plains, making movement difficult. The eastern forest casts a shadow in the area and blocks the wind and rain that usually blows over this area. To the south, rushing water can be heard.
118370: Rough, green grass grows here in the rich soils alongside the river to the north of here. Signs of various wildlife can be seen leading to and from the forests east of the riverbank. The eastern trees rise high, blocking visibility in that direction. To the south the plains head to the far side of the eastern forest. A trail leads west into a field.
118371: A large rabbit looks peacefully at you, ready to dart away.

The ground is damp in most places and soggy in some and fertile here. The river to the south feeds the plain here with abundant hydration. To the north the fields continue. To the east, the plains next to the river continue. The air here teems with life from small animals, birds, and insects.
118372: A brown fox is here, looking for some rabbits to chew up.

Due to the encircling rivers, these lands are well nourished by the groundwater and have grown lush and green. A few minor bushes occupy the landscape as well, adding to the diet of the local fauna. The ground becomes moist to the south, while close to the river to the north, a landing can be spotted.
118373:
