A duck is here, quacking happily.
A brown fox is here, looking for some rabbits to chew up.

These fields are mostly covered with bright green grass, due to the irrigation of the rivers which flow on the north and south. This easy access to water allows the plant life on these fields to grow more lush than the brown grass and dried out thorn bushes that seem to be the predominant vegetation on the far side of the two rivers.
118374:
Yellow flowers, with grey-green foliage, grow in clusters here.
A large rabbit looks peacefully at you, ready to dart away.
A tall stag is here, grazing peacefully.
A swallow flies high above the ground.

The plains grow lush and green here. Grass predominates, interspersed with various kinds of flowers and weeds. A small river to the south and a larger one to the north, both flowing westwards, provide natural irrigation. The lush lands continue to the west and to the east, but beyond either river lie dry wastelands.
118375: The fields are surrounded by the water of two rivers on three sides. The easy access to water allows the vegetation, which mostly consists of grass, to grow lush and green. The green fields continue eastwards, where the rivers provide an excellent natural irrigation.
118376:
A heron is stalking the area, looking for fish.
A swarm of mosquitoes is here, humming around you.
A swarm of mosquitoes is here, humming around you.

The small, slowly flowing river finds its way from the east to the north. The waterway is wide but neither very deep nor very fast, making this an excellent spot to cross. The water is home to many water plants, feeding various fish, which in their turn provide a food source to the numerous animals found near the river. The fields close to the river are covered with small patches of lush, green grass. The further away from the water, the more dry and brown the area becomes.
118377: A black raven flies in the sky searching for flesh to prey upon.

The brush here is littered with small stones and several rocks as it continues to the west. Several small, misshapen trees grow here among the rocky brush trying to eke out an existence. In the north lies a swampy area, made soggy by a river flowing in the northeast. Rocky fields can be spotted to the east.
118378:
A large sturgeon swims slowly along the bottom.
A large sturgeon swims slowly along the bottom.

The small river flows from the south to the west. The water is not very wide, but it is too deep to wade through it completely. The vegetation around the waterway is a great deal greener than the rest, due to the access to water. Seas of lush, green grass lie to the east. A larger river flows in the north, joining up with this one further to the west.
118379: The small river that flowed here from the east is about to join up with a much larger river, which came from the northeast. The current slowly grows stronger and the fish seem much larger than in the small stream. The plains in the direct vicinity of the river are covered with lush green grass, but the further away from the water the grass grows, the drier and the browner it becomes. The sound of rushing water can be heard, coming from the north.
118380: Huge Boulder in the Dry Grass

A low shrub with bright green, oblong leaves is growing here.
Scattered in and on the shrub, there are three piles of blueberries.
A black raven flies in the sky searching for flesh to prey upon.

A huge, broken boulder lies in the middle of the plains. The ground around it is covered with smaller fragments of rock and broken stones, making it quite difficult to traverse. Thick weeds and dry grass grow amongst the rubble. Some huge piles of debris lie to the west, preventing passage in that direction. The sloping plains continue to the south and the west, while a small river flows by to the north.
118381:
Yellow flowers, with grey-green foliage, grow in clusters here.
A rock lizard is here, motionless as it observes you.
A buck runs swiftly from place to place, looking about warily as it grazes.

A multitude of rocks surround the scarce vegetation of dried out grass and the occasional thorny bush or isolated tree that has appeared. The rubble blocks the path in every direction, save for the west and the south. To the west the brambles and thorn bushes start to populate the land.
118382:
Some small rocks have been piled into a mound here.
A black raven flies in the sky searching for flesh to prey upon.
A colourful butterfly is fluttering around here.

Sloping fields, covered by dark patches of dry grass and thorny bushes grouped in small thickets, can be found here. The earth beneath seems to consist mostly of clay. Small rocks scatter the area, and scarce broken stones lie here and there, making the footing treacherous. A wall of rock along a ridge runs north to south along the west. There is a crack in the boulder that sits to the west.
118383: A black crow flies low to the ground here, looking for carrion to eat.

Low bushes grow expansively here among the rocky ground. The vegetation grows in a tangled mess among scattered patches of brown, dried-out grass. Broken stones and small boulders lie scattered across the land, probably brought here by a river that found a new course long ago.
118384:
A buck runs swiftly from place to place, looking about warily as it grazes.
A buck runs swiftly from place to place, looking about warily as it grazes.

The sloping plains, stretching out for miles in all directions, are covered by small patches of brown, dry grass, scarcely interrupted by thin thickets of thorny brush or a lone, misshapen tree. Small rocks and broken stones are scattered across the land. The bushes and thickets grow thicker to the west and the south.
118385: Sloping fields stretch out towards the horizon in all directions. The predominant form of vegetation found in this region is dark brown, dry grass that grows in small patches in an irregular pattern. The hard ground seems to be a mixture of clay and limestone, rendering profitable agriculture all but impossible.
118386: A small grasshopper clings to a blade of grass, ready to spring.

The majority of the vegetation in this desolate area is brown, dry grass, with a few scattered small thickets of prickly brush. The fields continue in all directions. Most of the land consists of clay and limestone, yet the shallow river to the north has brought nutritious silt and water, making the grass to the north, grow longer and greener. A road can be seen far to the south.
118387: A sly cat prepares to pounce from its grassy hiding place.

The grassy land slopes abruptly from the brushy plains in the west towards the water of the shallow river to the north and east. The river can be seen quite clearly from this vantage point, as well as a small waterfall further upstream to the east. The ground consists of dried grass and stony reddish brown soil.
118388: Some fields here are composed of a dry, rough grass with some scattered thickets of thorn bushes. A few chalk and limestone rocks are scattered throughout the red soil. To the south, the land plunges into an impossible to climb descent, which slowly turns into a valley. In the distant east, the peaks of the Misty Mountains rise over the horizon.
118389: Tangled brush blends in with the long brown-dry grass upon the red soil. On three sides this barren land ends in a precipice. An ancient road crosses the land south and east, while to the north you can hear a swift river on its way westward. Vast grasslands spread out to the west.
118390: The barren lands are covered with small patches of brown, dry grass and once every thousand feet vegetated by a thin thicket of thorny bushes. A large road lies to the south, steadily finding its way through the sloping landscape. The way south is impassable due to a steep cliff which juts downward. Small stones and boulders lie scattered on the ground, the only remnants of a river that once flowed here.
118391: A thick tree stands here, its trunk split by lightning.

An old tree stands in the middle of the brush, its trunk split halfway in two by lightning long ago. A few branches, some of them scorched, lie on the ground. The brush appears empty save for the tree and low, thick thorny bushes. The thorn bushes grow taller and thicker to the south, such that they block the passage in that direction.
118392: Some thick writhing vines whip all around you.

Little can grow in this infertile ground. The only vegetation to be seen is parched, brown grass and the odd thorny bush. To the south and the east these thorny bushes have prospered despite the arid conditions and have formed a natural, impenetrable barrier.
118393: A great deal of caution is needed when crossing these plains because they are covered in thousands of boulders of all different sizes and shapes, some of which are fractured and others intact. Small patches of brown, dried-out grass can be spotted between the rocks, the only visible form of vegetation.
118394:
There is a huge, pyramidal beehive here.
A bee flies around here, collecting nectar from the flowers.
A bee flies around here, collecting nectar from the flowers.
A bee flies around here, collecting nectar from the flowers.

The ground under the bushes here is covered with piles of both large and small stones. The vegetation here is composed of thick patches of brown thorn bushes and dry grass. The vegetation thins out to the north and east into fields. Further to the east and south, an ancient broken road can be seen.
118395:
On the ground, there are two sticky honeycombs.
An angry bee is working on a honeycomb here.
An angry bee is working on a honeycomb here.
A drone bee flies around here, angrily buzzing.
A drone bee flies around here, angrily buzzing.
A huge, bulky queen bee is here.
A bee flies around here, collecting nectar from the flowers.
A bee flies around here, collecting nectar from the flowers.
A bee flies around here, collecting nectar from the flowers.

A grid is formed by numerous large honeycombs arranged in meticulous order. They are large, perfectly hexagonal sheets of honey and wax that are extremely sticky and impede progress. On the other hand, the bees constantly come and go, flitting around and forming tight swarms. There are no obvious differences between the bee pastures outside and inside the hive, but everything gets louder, from the resonant drone to the absolutely penetrating.
118396:
A large thorny branched shrub is growing here.
On the shrub, there are two piles of blackberries.
Some small rocks have been piled into a mound here.

The sloping fields stretch out towards the horizon in all directions. The ground rises into hilltops to the east and south. The area is mostly vegetated by small, dark clumps of coarse grass. The course grass is interspersed by a number of dense thickets of dark green, thorny bushes. Small rocks and stones lie scattered all about, growing far greater in number, further to the north.
118397: This hilltop is vegetated by some tiny patches of dry, brown grass. The ground is a hard-packed mixture of red-brown clay and limestone, that leaves any form of agriculture, quite unprofitable. A road lies to the southeast, curving throughout the landscape. Several small stones and broken boulders lie scattered around the land. The barren wastelands stretch out in all directions.
118398: This hill rises toward the southeast, ending in a sudden cliff. The cliff cannot be climbed. The ground on this hilltop is filled with dry, brown grass and rarely some thorny bushes. Small rocks and broken boulders lie scattered on the hard ground, which is a mixture of clay and limestone. A road can be spotted to the southeast.
118399: This dry, brown hill juts from the southeast toward the northwest, lowering into flat fields north and west. Most of these barren wastelands are covered with patches of dark brown, dry, grass. The ground, consisting of what seems to be a mixture of clay and limestone, is too hard and dry to allow ploughing or any profitable agriculture.
118400: Reaching out to the horizon in all directions, these sloping plains are covered with small patches of dry, brown grass, interspersed with the occasional small, thorny bush. The soil below is clay-like and infertile. Small rocks and broken boulders are scattered around the plains. The eastward slope of the plains rises gradually to a hilltop. The occasional high-pitched cry of a bird can be heard in the distance.
118401:
An apple tree with bright green leaves grows here.
On the tree's branches are three apples.
A pigeon is strutting around here.

These barren plains, vegetated mostly with dark patches of dry, brown grass, lie directly to the north of a small trail, that runs from west to south. The fields are covered with broken stones and small boulders, whilst every here and there, a small thorny shrub or lone tree sprouts up.
118402:
A small boar with big yellow tusks looks eager to fight.
A fierce boar is here, making grunting noises.

The hard-packed clay has made these lands largely infertile. A few patches of grass grow here, although they are mostly brown, due to lack of hydration. A thick, tangled wall of thorn bushes blocks the way north. The steep cliff wall of the ridge looms to the west, blocking the way. The fields continue to the east and south.
118403:
A goblin raider shrieks as it searches for something to maim.
A goblin raider shrieks as it searches for something to maim.
A goblin raider shrieks as it searches for something to maim.
A boar cub is playing here, and exploring the wide world.

This dry, barren hill is covered with brown patches of grass, interspersed with some small thorn bushes and a few lone trees. The ground drops to level fields to the west and the hill continues to the north, coming to another hill. The way east and south is blocked by a cliff too steep to climb down. The cliff overlooks a wide road.
118404: A field lark stands here, focused on finding food.

The only thing that distinguishes this area from the lands that surround it is that the thorny bushes grow a little less far apart here than they do in the more barren parts of the plain. They stand in small thickets scattered amongst the patches of wasted brown grass. Dry and brittle, the bushes are horribly misshapen.
118405: A tiny, harmless centipede is here.

A vast plain of dry, brown grass and a few thorny bushes stretches in all directions. A massive, impassable ridge can be seen running from the north to the southwest. The trail here runs from the west and turns south.
118406:
A Dunadan sentry vigilantly watches the surrounding lands.
A Dunadan sentry vigilantly watches the surrounding lands.
A Dunadan sentry vigilantly watches the surrounding lands.
A pigeon is strutting around here.

A small, dusty path, paved with bricks and small stones, connects to a larger road a little way to the east. The trail leads to the north, into the fields. The surrounding area is barren, covered only with dry patches of grass and some lone thorny bushes. The high-pitched cry of a bird can be heard from time to time.
118407: Barren plains, covered with patches of dry grass, stretch out as far as the eye can see. The only other form of vegetation present is small, misshapen, thorny bushes. The clay and limestone ground is quite hard, rendering any form of agriculture near impossible. The ground is covered with debris. A small trail can be spotted to the north.
118408: The barren plains stretch out in all directions save the north and west, where a sharp ridge blocks the view. Small rocks cover the hard ground, which seems to be a mixture of clay and limestone. The plains are vegetated with small patches of brown, dry grass and every here and there is a scarce thicket of thorn bushes. A small trail lies to the north.
118409: The trail continues to the west towards an abandoned farm house whilst to the southeast, the trail makes its way towards a larger road. The plains are barren and scarcely vegetated, with only some small thorny bushes and a lone tree to be seen between the dry patches of grass.
118410: A powerful ram stands here, poised and alert.

A small trail, paved with small bricks and stones, continues to the north towards a distant cabin to the northwest. Eastwards, the trail leads towards larger road. On all sides the trail is surrounded by sloping hills, whose sole vegetation consists of a few lone, misshapen trees and a carpet of dry, brown grass. No flowers can be spotted anywhere, unable to survive in this barren landscape.
118411: A slobbering giant greedily lumbers towards you.

This small trail runs from the west to the south. The trail is paved with several stones which prevent it becoming a pool of mud during heavy rain. The trail winds through the sloping hills that run along a ridgeline. The grass that grows on the sides of the path is brown and dry.
118412: A mountain lion eyes you closely and prepares to pounce for his next meal.

The sloping fields are largely barren, vegetated only by scattered patches of dry, brown grass and a few small, thorny bushes. A small trail marches past to the east and north, leading travellers between a larger road that lies to the southeast, and the ruins of a farm house alongside a rickety cabin. Small rocks and broken stones are scattered throughout the area.
118413: The brown and barren grasses spread out across this rolling hill. They are vegetated by extremely thick, misshapen thorn bushes and small patches of dark brown, dried-out grass, whilst some lone trees grow in a few places. Mossy stones lie scattered here and there. The ridge line that runs from the northeast to the southwest is characterized by the steep cliff that runs along the southeast.
118414: Consisting mainly of dry grass, weeds and sparse bushes, these grasslands stretch out as far as the eye can see. A few violet flowers grow in a small circle, the only flora that managed to bloom here. There are hills to the south and east that are covered in brown, dried grass.
118415: A tall slender holly tree stands on top of a small hill.

These grassy hills continue to undulate to the east and south. The ground on this hilltop is characterized by small, brown patches of grass. Small clumps of bushes grow scattered amongst the hilltop grasses, whilst a lone holly-tree stands near the top of this small hill which rises above the sloping fields to the north and west.
118416:
A small and tough weed grows here.
A wild brown donkey is here, on the lookout for enemies.
A jenny is grazing here.

These desert-like plains are dry and barren. Patches of brown grass sparsely cover the hard ground, which appears to be composed of a clay and limestone mixture. The occasional lone tree or thorn shrub valiantly rises into the air, but no other flora is visible. Nothing suggests the fauna would be richer than the flora.
118417: The slopes are covered with brown patches of grass and dried-out vegetation, interspersed with the occasional, misshapen tree. A pool of mud can be seen to the north. The grasslands seem to stretch out to the horizon in all directions. Sometimes the cry of a bird of prey can be heard in the distance.
118418: Muddy Pool at the Start of a Stream

A pool of bubbling mud is here.
A long slender eel glides along the water, its body coiled to strike.

A small source of water starts here, slowly flowing to the north. A thick muddy pool has formed close by, some of the mud following the stream. Small patches of coarse grass grow near the pool, while the bones of small animals that once became stuck, stick out of the mud. The odour of rotten flesh fills the area. Endless, sloping plains lie to the south.
118419:
There are two piles of wheat cereals here.
A mass of dark green leaves clings to a wall.

Dry weeds grow amongst the ancient cobblestones that line this floor. A crumbling stone wall remains as a reminder of where the old walls stood where this ruined farm house once stood. A shabby looking cabin has been constructed to the east reusing a portion of the foundations of the old farmhouse.
118420:
A black crow flies low to the ground here, looking for carrion to eat.
A thin, crippled deer looks around timidly.

The green grasslands from the north meet the barren waste from the east. The change from dry grasslands to verdant plains can be seen very clearly here as the vegetation becomes less lush than it was to the north. A muddy stream lies to the west, slowly flowing from its source to the southwest.
118421: A thin, hairy plant, with small, oval leaves, grows here.

The plains here are green with vegetation, since the river is not far to the west. The foliage consists mainly of lush, green grass and several trees, interspersed with a few thickets of thorny bushes. The channels continue eastwards, irrigating the plains there as well, making them equally lush.
118422:
A blooming water-lily floats on the surface of the water.
A long slender eel glides along the water, its body coiled to strike.
A swarm of midges is here, humming around you.

The plains have become somewhat waterlogged, lying at the bank of the stream to the west. Most of the grass has sunk in the mud and small pools appear all around. The scarce vegetation is composed mostly of smaller, water-loving plants. Algae float in the small pools, making it hard to distinguish them from the grass.
118423: The fields here are a sea of grass that seem to be a grazing spot for animals. The green fields continue to the east, whilst the original barren plains stretch out to the south. The land becomes significantly more bushy and thorny as it leads towards the north.
118424: Green grass can be found here that has been grazed short by some ungulates judging from the scat. The sloping land is fairly barren but gets progressively bushier and hillier to the southeast. More fields can be seen stretching out across the horizon to the north.
118425: A slobbering giant greedily lumbers towards you.

The barren hills are covered in tangles of thorny plants and dried-out grass, occasionally highlighted by a single, lone tree. It is impossible to produce or engage in any type of agriculture because of how dry and hard the ground is. Small pebbles and broken stones are strewn over the slopes. To the east, a cliff formed by big rocks prevents further movement.
118426:
A small black bird with red markings on its beak is here.
A jenny is grazing here.

The field is abundant with sun-grown grass and clover. To the south and east are vast wastelands, and to the north are lusher pastures. A decrepit old cottage and some ruins can be seen immediately to the south, and a little trail can be seen heading away from them.
118427: The small trail stops to the east where an ancient, crumbling rock wall seems indicate the ruins of a farm house property. A rather shabby-looking cabin has been constructed more recently on the foundations of the ruins. Seemingly, empty plains lie to both the south and north, and continue into the horizon.
118428: A small, dense tangle of roots covers the ground.

A dense thicket of thorny bushes somehow clings to life here, in the middle of the endless, barren wastelands; its roots sticking out of the ground. A dense tangle of branches, all covered in small, sharp thorns, blocks the way east and south. Sloping fields lie both to the north and west, while a small trail can be spotted to the south through the thick foliage.
118429: Not even the smallest patch of grass grows on these dusty hills. The ground, a compact mixture of clay and limestone, is littered with broken rocks and small stones. The sloping hills continue in all directions, but the path westward is blocked by a dense thicket of thorny bushes.
118430: A large amount of thick bushes, most of them rather thorny, grow here in these arid conditions. Little other vegetation is to be seen save for dried patches of brown grass. The bushes obstruct the passage to the north, east and south. Large boulders form a rock wall to the east and south which only allows passage to the west from here.
118431: Dry, brown patches of grass cover almost the entire landscape. Where the grass is absent, the ground underfoot is composed of hard-packed, red-brown clay. Small stones and broken rocks lie scattered throughout the area. A small trail lies to the south and to the west, providing easy passage for travellers between an abandoned farm house to the west and a road that can be seen far to the east. A lone tree stands in the fields.
118432: A tiny, harmless centipede is here.

Only scant vegetation and brown patches of grass can be found on these hills. The hills gradually become much drier than they are here as they spread out for miles to the south. To the west, in the distance, is a little structure. Along the east side of a ridge, a rock wall stretches north to south. The boulder that is to the east has a crack in it.
118433:
A low shrub with bright green, oblong leaves is growing here.
Scattered in and on the shrub, there are three piles of blueberries.

Shrubs and thorn bushes cover the ground, engulfing many young saplings and strangling them. The overgrowth is disrupted by a winding path which leads north and south through the thorny foliage. The west and east are an impenetrable wall of nasty thorns preventing any movement through the area.
118434: A winding path through the large clumps of thorn bushes runs here from the west and bends southward, continuing to more brush to the south. The thick thorn bushes to the north and the east have entangled themselves into an impenetrable wall of vegetation with nasty, large thorn spikes.
118435: This area of fields is vegetated by a number of large thickets of thorny brush that surround a pool of brownish water. Any passage northwards and southwards is blocked by dense thickets of thorn brush. The only clear passage is to the west or east down a winding path that runs through the clumps of thorny foliage.
118436: A junebug buzzes slowly through the air.

Deep rich green leaves pervade the thick, healthy thorn bushes here. The thorns that grow on the thorn bushes are long and strong. The thick thorn bushes grow with enough space for a traveller to move through without getting pricked too much from the vegetation. A small field lies far to the east, vegetated with larger thickets of brush. A river lies to the south, curving its way from north to south. The river flows steadily, causing little noise. The plains surrounding these lands seem to stretch on for ages, forming endless seas of wasteland with clumps of brush throughout.
118437:
An arrow made from a grey wood lies here.
An apple tree with bright green leaves grows here.
On the tree's branches is an apple.

This area is mostly covered with small patches of dry, brown grass, save for the occasional tree or thorn bush. Several broken rocks scatter the land, covered with scarce pieces of moss. The faint glimmer of a flowing river can be seen to the west. The path to the east is blocked by a huge, broken boulder, surrounded by a thicket of thorny bushes. Every now and then the high-pitched call of a bird can be heard in the distance.
118438: A heron is stalking the area, looking for fish.

Neither very fast nor very slow, this small river comes from the south, becoming more and more wide as it flows westwards. It is well vegetated by different water plants, which feed various animals. The plains to the east drain the river and has therefore become quite swampy.
118439:
A long slender eel glides along the water, its body coiled to strike.
A swarm of midges is here, humming around you.
A swarm of midges is here, humming around you.

Flowing gently northwards, the narrow stream is still shallow enough to allow wading. Some of the water is being drained by the swampy plains that lie to the northeast and have turned the surrounding plains lush and green. The water is extremely muddy and is overgrown with water plants.
118440: A black catfish is here, lurking in the mud.

The stream, although still filled with mud, sluggishly flows from south to north. The stream flows to here from the south, where a small water source arises to form a large pool of mud. The vegetation here is dry and barren and only sloping wastelands cover the surroundings.
118441: A small plant grows here, with long, pointed leaves and flowers at its top.

The area is covered by seemingly endless brown and dry grass. The gentle hills slowly decline to the south. A patch of thorny bushes lies to the southwest. The grass becomes greener to the north. The hills loom to the north and finally meet a wall of rock which cannot be passed.
118442: The sloping hills come to a halt as two rivers block their path to the north and the east. The sudden cliff that drops to the river does not allow passage. The noise of streaming water fills the area. The plains stretch out as far as the eye can see to the south and west. Several piles of rocks lie scattered around the clay and limestone land.
118443: For miles in every direction, there are more sloping fields. The barren wastes occasionally grow a small clump of prickly shrubs or a lone, deformed tree. The high-pitched chirp of small birds can be heard. Agriculture would be challenging due to the ground's tough, wet clay and limestone.
118444: Dry, brown patches of grass cover most of this area. Only infrequently does the occasional thick shrub or thorny bush interrupt. The sloping fields continue in all directions save to the north, where a river flows. The shrubs grow denser and the patches of grass grow greener the closer they are to the river. A bird's piercing call can occasionally be heard in the distance.
118445: A porcupine is waddling around here, its tail full of sharp quills.

The wide, barren wastelands are covered with dark patches of dry, brown grass. Small, thorny bushes sprout up every few hundred feet, but no other form of vegetation can be seen. The fields to the southwest are greener than here, due to irrigation which was placed long ago.
118446:
A very strong orkish patrol-leader is looking for enemies here.
An orkish soldier is here, patrolling the area.
An orkish soldier is here, patrolling the area.
An orkish soldier is here, patrolling the area.
An orkish soldier is here, patrolling the area.

These plains are fairly well vegetated by small, thorny bushes, however they are not dense enough to make travelling too strenuous. The thorn bushes grow denser to the southwest, blocking passage in that direction. Some grassy hills can be seen to the north across the plain of dry bushes.
118447:
A large thorny branched shrub is growing here.
On the shrub, there are two piles of blackberries.

Large heaps of hard stone litter the plains, making mounted navigation impossible. The barren wastes occasionally grow a small clump of prickly shrubs or a lone, deformed tree. To the west, a thicket of thorn bushes forms an insurmountable barrier that blocks access.
118448: A tree trunk that has fallen to the ground is covered in moss.

It is challenging to navigate through the rocky fields since they are uneven and littered with boulders of various sizes. The desolate wastelands are covered in little patches of dried-out grass, occasionally broken up by a lone tree or a small thorn shrub. To the west, a thick wall of prickly vegetation has sprouted, blocking any further movement.
118449:
A rotten corpse is hanging here.
An iron-grey wolf stands here, grizzled from countless hunts.
An iron-grey wolf stands here, grizzled from countless hunts.

This tiny refuge, surrounded by enormous downed logs and covered in soft, fuzzy green moss, serves as the residence of several forest creatures. Half of the den is covered by a particularly large fallen tree, creating a shield from the weather.
118450:
A huge stone giant is here, glaring at you.
A young ill-tempered stone giant is here, muttering incoherently.

This tunnel's floor is built of clay and rocks. Crawling creatures move about in the shadows and between the rocks. At the northern end of the tunnel, the ceiling and floor are in contact, although they diverge in the direction of the huge cave to the south. The rocky ceiling has a large, deep fissure in it.
118451: Here, a sizable natural cavern with a high ceiling and substantial, pure granite columns, has developed. The cavern is completely dry and looks as though it has been free of moisture for many years, but the smooth stone implies that water once ran through it.
118452:
A huge stone giant is here, glaring at you.
A young ill-tempered stone giant is here, muttering incoherently.

A dry cavern formed inside the hard granite mountainside has been altered to serve as a modest abode. The cavern appears to have developed gradually over time and stretches north to a natural cavern. The exit to the east is obstructed by a lot of rubble.
118453:
A huge stone giant is here, glaring at you.
A young ill-tempered stone giant is here, muttering incoherently.

Despite the fact that these caverns were undoubtedly built by nature, the inhabitants who presently reside there have converted them into simple habitations. While the exit to the west is covered by debris, the exit to the south has a strong stench of blood and meat.
118454:
An albino salamander is here, perched on some rocks.
An albino salamander is here, perched on some rocks.

The walls of this wet cave are black on all sides. Green algae make the floor slippery. The ceiling of the cavern is formed by large stalactites, formed by the constant dripping of the chalky rocks that have merged over the eons into a solid wall of folded rock. The cave continues to the east and south.
118455: A fierce-looking eel lurks in the darkness.

Hidden from the outside world, this cave shows many signs of having served as a refuge for various animals. The walls, floor, and ceiling of the cave are drenched with green algae that thrive in the murky water. The northern and eastern sides of the cave are covered in knee-deep murky water with spots of algae floating on it. The actual water appears to be surface water that seeps through the clay bottom. A large boulder covers a part of the ceiling.
118457: This cave is dark and small. The walls are flat and damp with moisture and shimmer from the small amount of light that enters from above. The cave has no corners or edges, and is roughly spherical in shape. The cave opens into a tunnel to the west. The tunnel is round and cylindrical in shape.
118458: The walls of the tunnel are made of smooth pitch black stone. The shape of the tunnel is cylindrical, and the walls are damp from some unseen source of water. The tunnel continues to the west and the very little amount of light which emits from the cave to the east is gone to the west.
118459:
A skeleton of some humanoid lies in the dust.
A skull-clad shaman of the Ohurk-uai is here, chanting some evil incantations.
The orkish bodyguard keeps an eerie eye on everything.

Puddles of murky water cover the entire length of this underground natural tunnel. Cold, unyielding rock and a thick reddish-brown mud that appears to be so viscous as to be seeping into the chamber even now make up its walls. Tiny glimmers and sparkles suggest that the sticky, oozing wall may contain hidden treasures.
118460: An ancient black altar stands in the centre of the room.

Jagged black crystals line the walls in this domed cave. A corrupted shrine sits in the middle of the round room. The shrine appears to be an altar to a malevolent and corrupt force. The lower part of the walls has faint inscriptions of evil runes and depictions of hideous scenes and torture. The burning of numerous old sacrifices has left stains on the altar room's ceiling.
118461: A diamondback rattlesnake is coiled here, ready to strike.

A large amount of bushes, most of them quite thorny, have grown very close together. The light armoured or bootless traveller might encounter some problems to traverse through the sharp thorns unharmed. But a small opening has been formed here that might provide some shelter from the seemingly ever present prevailing winds.
118462: A black crow flies low to the ground here, looking for carrion to eat.

The ridge stretches in north-east direction many miles, and to the south-west. Standing at an edge, it's windy here. Visibility is clear here, no trees or many shrubs to break the skyline and the only sign of any vegetation is a thick blanket of grass that covers the ground. The steep ridge descends quickly to the east and south.
118463: Poor soil quality and the lack of a constant water source provide little growth opportunity for almost all vegetation in this region of the hills. The ground is cracked in several places and sparse patches of a short, brown grass crop up occasionally, clinging to life despite the adverse conditions. The hilly plains stretch out in all directions, as far as the eye can see.
118464: A black crow flies low to the ground here, looking for carrion to eat.

The hard dirt is only occasionally interrupted by a small tuft of bunch grass. The hills to the north are dry and dusty. To the east the ridge descends abruptly. To the south, bushes and shrubs can be seen sprouting out from the grassland. The only noticeable sound is the soft rustle of the grass as the wind blows across the hills.
118465: Various dips and short inclines in these hills make travel difficult and limit the view in all directions. The occasional straggly bush or shrub can be seen sprouting up, giving a marginal amount of cover for the small animals that inhabit the area, and the grass grows short and thin in the depleted soil.
118466: A sparrow is flapping around on the ground.

The land falls away to the east, creating a sandy ridge here, that levels out into a plateau to the south. A fairly easy descent to the east leads directly into a thicket of thorn bushes. To the north a vast expanse of hills is visible, stretching out as far as the eye can see. Small tufts of grass cling to the ridge with a stubborn resiliency, undaunted by the constant exposure to the wind and sun at this elevated level.
118467: Around the old ruins to the east, there has been set up several tents. Someone has apparently made the ruins a temporary home for themselves. The short grass is crushed and trampled by constant use. Around the tents, a sturdy fence has been built from wooden planks and stones. Some smoke rises up from the centre of the camp area. To the south, one can see beyond the plains to the ford that crosses a small tributary, and a jagged ridge juts out to the north.
118468:
An orc-guard of the Morgundul is on patrol here.
An orc-guard of the Morgundul is on patrol here.

The plains gradually begin to slope upwards towards a plateau visible in the distance to the north. The lay of the land has enough of a slant that one can imagine the plains towards the river to the south can become extremely soggy during the rainy season, as the water runs down the subtle incline. The short grass grows lush and thick in that section of the land but begins to thin out as the land climbs. The outline of a road is discernible to the east and south.
118469: A field lark stands here, focused on finding food.

The plains are even throughout, growing with a thick bed of grass approximately a foot in height. The grass is a thick green carpet, capable of hiding small animals. Various tracks and trails can be seen where deer and other creatures have waded through. To the north the grass fields continue while to the west the fields dip and become uneven.
118470: A field lark stands here, focused on finding food.

This is the end of the long ridge that stretches to the north. The slope to the west is consisting mostly of loose gravel and soft sand, and that makes climbing up the slope impossible. Some grass sticks out on the top of the ridge. As the wind ripples through the fields of grass, the effect that it leaves is one of an ocean's rolling waves.
118471: This is a strip of fields between the ridge to the west and a depression to the south and east. Nothing else marks this barren landscape in any way. The grass is slightly shorter in the west, enough perhaps to afford cover to small animals, but little else.
118472: The grass field stretches for miles to the east, while a steep ridge resides to the west. The scenery changes little to the south as grasses continue to thrive unabated by stone or tree. The plains dry out considerably to the north and east becoming little more than dirt and dried weeds. The ridge to the west and north is impossible to climb because of steepness and loose gravel.
118473: The grass continues to grow with little change. No large tree or stone exists here and the grass does not grow very high. Very little can be heard except for the passing winds through the grass, which gives a ripple effect to the fields. A sudden depression appears to have been formed to the south. Descend is very steep, creating unclimbable rampart.
118474:
A field lark stands here, focused on finding food.
A huge warg is here, moving in for the kill.

There is little to this area except the small grasses which subsist on the dry soil. Nothing stirs, except the grass when the wind blows through it. A sharp decline drops suddenly to the south, looking like the ground has caved in. The fields continue to the east and west.
118475: A field lark stands here, focused on finding food.

Small bunch grasses grow here with little to interrupt them. The winds blow across the field so that it resembles waves upon an ocean. The fields continue to the west with no interruption. There is a broken road that encircles this field to the east and south, and a small dusty trail leads away from the field to the north. However, thickets of thorny plants prevent travelling to the east and south.
118476:
A huge warg is here, moving in for the kill.
A black raven flies in the sky searching for flesh to prey upon.

This is bottom of a depression that goes on to the east and south. The slope is very steep to the north and west. On the ground, there grows only little grass and some thistles and brushes here and there. Otherwise the soil is dry and void of life. A whirl of wind sometimes rises some dust to the air.
118477: The ground elevates quickly to the north and east. Some kind of natural event has formed this deep depression in the middle of vast fields of grass. The soil in the bottom of the depression is quite dry, and have some cracks formed here and there. There are markings of dried up water puddles on the ground. Some yellowish grass seems to be sticking out of top of the brink.
118478:
A small centipede is here scurrying about.
A black raven flies in the sky searching for flesh to prey upon.
A black raven flies in the sky searching for flesh to prey upon.

In the middle of this depression, in the vast plains, there are not many interesting features. The wall of the depression rises steeply to the east giving no chance for climbing up to the plains. The ground here consists of cracked, dried up mud. Depression continues to the north, south and west.
118479:
A large thorny branched shrub is growing here.
On the shrub, there are two piles of blackberries.
A huge grizzly bear is here, roaming the wild.
A black snake, with red markings, is lying here.

Small, dying bushes hug the dried soil here in the bottom of a depression. Amid the shrubs, several small boulders can be seen, embedded in the dry soil, and even these are cracked, slowly disintegrating as a result of the wind and cold winter frosts. More bushes can be seen to the west in the slope of depression.
118480:
A half-decayed corpse of a goblin lies rotting on the ground.
Some thick writhing vines whip all around you.

This is the western end of the depression. The ground is cracked in many places from the dryness and it is mostly devoid of plants. Only a few thistle and weed grow here and there. The walls of the depression are too steep to climb and there is no handhold visible. Upper, near to the edge, a few root protrudes out of the dried up muddy wall.
118481: A mass of wriggling vines drops on you from the trees.

The brush that springs up thick and wild in this portion of the land obstructs but does not completely block travel through the plains. Several bird nests have been built within the mesh of the tangled bushes. The partially concealed thorns and twisted branches of the bushes provide some reliable source of protection from snakes and other predators. There is a large thicket to the west and ground drops quickly to the north. An overgrown road runs through the countryside south of here.
118482:
A sprawling green bush of stinging nettle grows here.
Some thick writhing vines whip all around you.

Sheltered from the wind by the sharp ridge that rises up to the west and loops round to the south, a tangled mass of wiry bushes has sprung up into a large thicket. Tiny, arrow-shaped leaves cover the thorny branches and serve as a filter from the harsh elements of the plains. The bushes grow thick and dense, effectively preventing any passage to the north, but they appear to thin out noticeably to the east.
118483: There grows short grass and a few bushes here and there in the field. A few, lonely surviving tree have found their foothold here, but they look like dwarven versions of their normal counterparts probably due to the arid soil. An old ruins reside somewhere to the west, but apparently some people have made it a home themselves. The ground is trampled from the heavy use, and forms a clear path to the west.
118484: At the Entrance to a Camp

The entrance of the camp has no gate, but there is a fence surrounding the area. The ground is heavily trampled and crushed by frequent use, it's likely that the inhabitants may have horses or some other animals. The ground has only a few turfs of grass, and is otherwise dry and without any plant life. Some stones and rocks have been piled at the root of the fence to make it sturdier. The camp resides to the west.
118485: This is the pathway to a camp that someone built next to the ancient broken road. Several tents has been set up in the camp, and a quickly created, but still sturdy fence surrounds the area. A tent has been placed to the south of here. In the north, it looks like there are some fields.
118486: A large bonfire is burning here.

This is about middle of a camp, a rectangular tent has been set up to the north, and a large, more circular tent to the west. Some smoke rises up from most of the tents, and a big bonfire has been built here. To the south, a quickly built stable resides amongst the rubble of a building.
118487: This is a muddy area on the yard, there is a depression that stretches to the east. The bottom of the depression is muddy, apparently some water accumulates there. There are lots of animal prints on the muddy ground, a sort of trail has formed there that stretches to the south.
118488: A large, circular tent has been set up to the west. The ground is trampled by a frequent use. A few more tents have been set up in the surroundings. Some old ruins reside in the south parts of the camp area. A fence has been built surrounding the camp.
118489: At a Well in a Camp

A wide stone well sinks deep into the ground here.
A wild dog bares his yellow fangs at you (hidden).
A wild dog bares his yellow fangs at you.
A wild dog bares his yellow fangs at you.

A well has been dug here, in a slight depression of a trampled field. A circle of mortared stones around the well is topped by a wooden bar. A wooden bar, long rope, and a worn wooden bucket can be used for drawing water from the well. Beyond a fence to the west, there are more fields that seem to continue endlessly. The ruins of a small building are visible to the south.
118490: A bale of hay is lying here.

This is old and collapsed part of a building, but it is serving now as a stable for animals. The roof has been fixed, there are pinewood logs stretched between the walls and the gaps have been sealed with tar. The old stone walls were partly also collapsed, but they have also been fixed with pinewood planks.
118491:
A warm blanket covers the ground.
A sturdy crate made of nailed wooden planks sits on the floor.
A scrawny goblin, holding a cudgel, is sleeping here in the tent.

This small tent was made of coarse canvas, and has a flap functioning as a door. Some stones surround the small fireplace that is in the middle of the tent. Furs and mattresses lie around the tent working as sleeping places. The tent was set up using poles, that support the tightly stretched canvas.
118492: This is a heavily trampled area, due to the pasture area to the north. Some of the grain grows here wildly, among the weeds and other plants. The fence is bordering the path, preventing animals and people travelling freely. Only a couple of stunted pine trees grow in the area.
118493:
A warm blanket covers the ground.
A sturdy crate made of nailed wooden planks sits on the floor.

This tent is long and rectangular. There are several wooden poles in the middle of the tent set up in a straight line. There are sleeping berths on the both sides of the poles. Two fireplaces are in this long tent, placed symmetrically on the both sides of the middle of the tent.
118494:
A long water trough made of wood stands here.
A sturdy trained horse is standing here.
A pig is here searching for food.

This pasture is still growing grain and long grass, and apparently somewhat taken care of. The ground has markings of animal hooves on the ground, probably from domestic animals. The fence is encircling the area, keeping the animals in and predators out. There are a few boulders on the side of the area, maybe cleaned away from the field.
118495:
An erect shrub with green pinnate leaves is growing here.
Inside the shrub, there are two piles of crimson raspberries.
A large thorny branched shrub is growing here.
On the shrub, there are two piles of blackberries.
An apple tree with bright green leaves grows here.
On the tree's branches are two apples.

This pasture is in relatively good shape, it has a couple of apple trees growing in the corner of the area. Some grain and long grass grow wildly in the pasture, providing some food for keeping animals fed. A few pine trees grow next to the fence, and a few wild bushes with some berries.
118496:
A small and well-kept fire lights and warms the room.
A sturdy bed made from solid oak lies here, covered in warm blankets.
A small oaken table has been set here.
On the table, there are two pieces of smoked, cured meat.
A strong, heavy-set goblin glares blankly ahead.

This is a large tent made of coarse canvas and hard leather. There is a small fireplace in the middle of the tent and in the roof there is a hole for the smoke to escape. Some wood have been piled up nearby the fireplace. A pungent odour of wood burning is apparent in the tent. On the floor, there are some rugs, mats, and straws of hay. A bed made of hay and leathers and furs stands against one wall of the tent.
118497: Lush green grass and brightly coloured wildflowers carpet this vast, level meadowland. The air is filled with the scent of warm grass and rich topsoil and the low buzzing of small bumblebees can be heard as they fly from one open flower to the next. A small stream can be seen running on its course through the plains the south and east, and a road is barely visible to the north and west.
118498: This field of grasses and shrubs lies near an old road which meets a stream to the south. There is a small hill to the east that is covered in rocks and various types of grasses. To the north a large field of boulders and shrubs can be seen.
118499: The field here is broken and roughened by the upheaving of the land. The lack of moisture in this part of the grassland has had a severe impact on what can grow and what can not. There is little of note other than broken clods of dirt and low tufts of grass. To the north and west an ancient road winds around this field, while an upright slope of a rocky hill rises to the east.
118500: These hills are broken and bare. The frost damage done here to the soil has caused it to heave and crack. The ground is barren, and it looks to have been this way for a long time. The hills continue to the north, while to the east large rocks can be seen below the hills.
118501:
A small bit of raw meat is lying on the ground.
A small bit of raw meat is lying on the ground.
A small bit of raw meat is lying on the ground.
A small bit of raw meat is lying on the ground.
A small bit of raw meat is lying on the ground.
A small bit of raw meat is lying on the ground.
A small bit of raw meat is lying on the ground.
A small bit of raw meat is lying on the ground.
A small bit of raw meat is lying on the ground.
A small bit of raw meat is lying on the ground.
A filthy straw pallet is lying here.
A clear spring babbles as cool water trickles out of the ground.

Morruhk enter Middle-earth at this point. Here, either new Morruhk or dead Morruhks are called. Only a few distant lamps provide light for the dimly lit space. This room appears to be deep underground, beyond the reach of all but the most powerful magic. The massive cavern is reached through a winding path.
118502: Eastern Edge of the Large Cavern

There are three corpses of Morruhk orcs here.
A powerful uruk of the Zaugurz tribe is standing here.

This enormous cavern stretches out to the west. The ceiling of the entire cavern vaults upward to a cleverly designed dome that appears to also pull smoke away from any fires that may be lit here. Strewn bones and mould remnants of food that litter the hall, which is clearly inhabited.
118503:
The corpse of *an Orc* is lying here.
On the ground, there are two corpses of Morruhk orcs.
A large copper cauldron stands here on three short, stout legs.
A powerful uruk of the Zaugurz tribe is standing here.

Large barrels marked with peculiar markings and stacks of flour are piled up against the cavern's natural wall. A large cauldron in the corner of the cave has a shaft right above it that draws the smoke away. The senses are assaulted by the aroma of some type of meat boiling in the cauldron. Near the cauldron, a sizable makeshift table is placed.
118504:
The corpse of *an Orc* is lying here.
There are two skeletons here.

The southeast portion of the cavern contains a sizable, deep hole that acts as both a testing ground for prospective warriors and a death pit for slaves and prisoners who have nothing more to give. It is more difficult to escape this pit because its edges slope up to the north and west and are surrounded by wooden barriers.
118505:
The corpse of *an Orc* is lying here.
The butchered corpse of a Morruhk orc is lying here.
A powerful uruk of the Zaugurz tribe is standing here.

On the far southern side of this cavern, wooden targets in the shape of elves and men have been arranged in a line. Weapons missing their targets or glancing off shields are most likely to blame for the cuts and scratches on the granite walls.
118506:
The corpse of a pitiful slave is lying inside a cage.
A powerful uruk of the Zaugurz tribe is standing here.

Several rusting cages with strong lock bars are fixed on the floor at the cavern's centre. Some of the cages' walls are welded with chains and shackles that contain nothing but bones. These are the slaves' living quarters, including both slaves and captured prisoners. Their labour is employed to mine the low-grade iron lodes and to excavate new caverns. Here, where they must watch the rats eat the corpses of their deceased comrades, not a single item of furniture makes their lives any easier. The majority of the small mounds of bones are either completely destroyed or broken into tiny fragments.
118507:
A dented pail has been carelessly left here.
The corpse of a Morruhk orc hangs over the wells edge.
A granite well is situated on top of a stone dais.

In the midst of this cavern's northern wall, a well has been constructed on a stone dais to provide access to water. A rough opening extending farther into the mountain has been blackened on the wall to the left of the well. This hole allows a steady stream of hot air to enter the chamber, warming the area. The cave gets bigger to the south.
118508:
There are two pieces of gristly meat here.
A rotten corpse is hanging here.
The corpse of a Morruhk orc is dangling on a meat hook.

There is a powerful odour in this section of the vast cavern. Some corpses are stored in large boxes, while others are partially butchered and hung from a row of pointed meat hooks. Each box's bottom features several holes that allow the blood to seep out onto the floor. The granite of the northern wall has an uneven dark brown colour, which seems to be the darkest where a table has been chiselled out of it.
118509:
You see two filthy straw pallets on the ground.
A powerful uruk of the Zaugurz tribe is standing here.

The cavern's walls are lined with sturdy beds, and the enormous stone rock in the middle serves as a table. Furs from various animals are scattered all over the floor, serving as basic bedding for the cavern's warriors. The quarters have never been cleaned, and the stench of squalor hangs heavily in the air.
118510: A large stone chest is here.

The floor is coated in a thick layer of muck, and the damp air is dense with the scent of decay and mould. The entire cavern has a vaulted ceiling that rises to a cleverly crafted dome that looks to also draw smoke away from any fires that might be lit here.
118511:
A pair of tongs lie on the ground.
A large round whetstone rests on the ground.
The charred corpse of an orc is lying in front of the forge.
A metal forge with a raging fire warms the cavern.

Simple tools and firewood are heaped next to the rough stone forge, which is located in a depression in the cavern's uneven floor. The forge's fire blazes, occasionally shooting flares that tint the walls blood-red before fading them back to black.
118512: Fireplace in the Corner of the Cavern

On the ground, there are two charred skeletons.
There are two corpses of Morruhk orcs here.

This dark cavern's ceiling is sporadically seared by roaring flames that occasionally erupt from the enormous fireplace placed against the southern wall. Anyone who enters the vicinity of the fireplace will feel a bodily blow from the sweltering heat. Heat and the stench of burning flesh combine to create a foul odour that hangs heavily in the air. A number of dead, their bodies shattered in combat, are stacked carelessly next to the fireplace and are ready to be incinerated by fire.
118513: The bloody torso of a Morruhk orc is lying here.

This area of a large cavern is its westernmost portion. A dim light, and occasionally more smoke than light, is provided by iron brackets that are fastened to the walls. The smoke may be observed sluggishly ascending to an oculus positioned in the dome's centre to the east. The cavern's only visible exit is to the west.
118514: The bloody lower body of a orc is lying here.

Every kind of abandoned garbage lines the walls of this caverns intersection. To create a reasonably clear passage, pieces of broken furniture, spoiled food, and dirty, muddy brown clothing have all been pushed away. The greatest pieces of debris have been removed, but the centre of the cavern is still full of thick mud and worse.
118515: The walls of this cavern are solid, unyielding earth. To the north, where a grate serves as a barrier, the corridor becomes more stony, while to the south, it becomes filthy. To the west, the air is thick with the rich smell of fresh loam and the foul stench of feces.
118516:
A skeleton of some humanoid lies in the dust.
A half-decayed corpse of a goblin lies rotting on the ground.
A powerful uruk of the Zaugurz tribe is standing here.

Most of the floor space of this cavern is taken up by a deep pit with a bowl-like shape. The pit, stained and slippery with ominous substances, smells of rot and death. The centre of the pit is lined with broken bones, tattered clothing, and shattering armour. A tunnel of inky blackness leads northward to a junction.
118517: A piece of bloody meat lies here.

This is a significant cavern's westernmost segment. The musty animal smell seems to be originating from this place. It is noticeably heavier than in the east and almost tangible. Possibly the ventilation is insufficient, or perhaps the smell is coming from a nearby source. In front of some cages positioned against the cavern walls, a dark red liquid that is still moist is visible on the stone floor.
118518:
An orkish officer of the Zaugurz tribe is standing here.
A Zaugurz orc soldier is standing here.
A Zaugurz orc soldier is standing here.
A Zaugurz orc soldier is standing here.
A Zaugurz orc soldier is standing here.

A tunnel that is nearly eight feet high and widest in the centre runs from north to south. Its unlevel, earthen walls appear to have been carved out with a chisel. Broken roots that had been clumsily removed from the tunnels passage emerge from the ceiling, walls, and even the floor in some spots. The dirt is severely disturbed along the passage's western edge. The southern entrance of the tunnel is totally blocked by a rough grate that stretches from one side to the other. A rusty gate is located in the middle of the grate.
118519:
An orkish officer of the Zaugurz tribe is standing here.
A Zaugurz orc soldier is standing here.
A Zaugurz orc soldier is standing here.
A Zaugurz orc soldier is standing here.
A Zaugurz orc soldier is standing here.

The tunnel has been significantly enlarged, and the cave walls have been severely scraped. The underground floor has been pushed down by the stomping of numerous feet and is heavily littered with chaotic piles of broken bones and other debris. After the area was mined out, nothing appears to be left here.
118520: A noticeable crack runs down one of the walls.

Numerous torches have been set up in this part of the mine, and their light casts eerie shadows on the rocks that are dispersed across the wet, roughed-up walls. The northern side of the mine, where work has increased, has a large hole dug into it. The additional mining is justified by the glint of the iron ore.
118521: The ground gives place to a broad, dark corridor with a few towering stones and a largely smooth rock floor. Although a big portion of this location may have been a naturally occurring geological feature, it appears that the rock to the south and east has been shattered and artificially molded into the shape of a sizable tunnel.
118522: Here, the great stone walls turn outward to create a truly enormous tunnel. The ceiling is hidden by a shroud of shadow in the pitch-blackness above. The ground is unexpectedly soft and appears to be composed of layers of gravel, sand, and mud in the tunnel's centre. The walls slenderize toward the east, as though most of the water had been absorbed into the bedrock.
118523: This tunnel is suitable for defence because it is large in the middle and gets narrower to the north and south. The chances of holding this tunnel from invaders have been improved by the installation of a sizable gate into the northern rockwall.
118524: Torches have been hammered into the sidewalls of the narrow tunnel, casting gyrating shadows on the surfaces. Several tiny bits of iron ore can be seen among the rubble that blankets the ground. Other than that, there is nothing down here but chilly and damp, sultry air.
118525: A rusty pickaxe with a broken handle lies discarded here.

The tunnel gradually ascends while going with the rock's grain. The dark reds that stain the moist walls cause them to shine and glisten. Although the air is musty and stale, it is chilly, odorless, and not particularly unpleasant. The tunnel gets smaller as it moves north.
118526: A huge, black wolf is here, ready to devour.

A lush valley, sprawling with low bushes and thin, scraggly trees, stretches to the east and south. To the north, a narrow pass leads through the mountains in that direction. To the south, the vegetation begins to thin as the ground becomes more bare.
118528: A narrow pass between tall mountains descends southerly here. The ground is loose and gravelly, making passage hazardous and slippery. The mountain walls funnel the cold wind here, creating strong gusts. The mountains on the east and west create deep, dark shadows in the mountain pass.
118529: Mountainous terrain can be spotted in each direction. They appear to eventually descend to flat land in the distance to the south and west, but continue to climb higher to the east and north. The air here is cold and windy, with occasional strong gusts. The terrain underfoot is gravelly, and pebbles and small rocks tumble downward after each step.
118530: Valley Trail South of a Ravine
A huge, black wolf is here, ready to devour.

The trail runs east and west here, stretching between a tall, steep, mountainous wall to the south, and a slow-moving creek to the north. The trail appears to be well-travelled, as it is dusty and cut significantly into the ground around it.
118531: The valley here is wide, opening to the east and west, with a trail following it in both directions. The trail is narrow, dusty, and gravelly, but it is worn and well-travelled. A slow-moving creek borders the trail to the north, running alongside it. Patches of short grasses and short, scraggly shrubs borders the trail on either side.
118532: High walls of stone and dirt surround this dead end. Small, craggy trees struggle to maintain life in this harsh environment. Tiny pebbles are scattered across the ground, making footing slippery. Bird nests sit high up on flat sections of rock. The mountain opens up to the west.
118533: The mountains are void of most plant life here; only some lichen grows on the rock. The wind seems to be blowing constantly here, chilling the bones. The mountains continue in all directions from here; to the south, they are noticeably descending. While not easy, it's still possible to travel on this stark mountain slope.
118534: It is clear from the few remaining tool marks that long ago there was a carved pass here. Since that time the pass has become full of debris from various rock and mud slides. It is no longer possible to even climb over the great mass of fractured rock.
118535: A wide, vast field rests at the feet of mountains surrounding it. The ground is covered in a thick, green grass, and other vegetation and wildlife thrives here as well. Tall, thin trees grow here and there, and the chirping of birds can be heard. The air is cold and windy.
118536: Western end of a Narrow Pass

The mountains gradually climb to the east, while suddenly descending to the south. The cold, blustery wind swirls here in the corner, as it gusts through the mountain pass and valleys. To the south, a vast, green field can be spotted north of a ravine and a creek.
118537: The Misty Mountains continue to stretch out across the land here. A large, flat opening can be spotted to the south, but the southern slope makes travel in that direction impossible. Caution should be taken when travelling through a mountain pass that stretches east and west.
118538:
A mountain lion is here, fighting Sumac.
Sumac the Tarkhnarb Orc, wielding a giant spear, is here, riding a hungry warg, fighting a mountain lion.

Tall mountains continue to stretch as far as the eye can see. A narrow mountain pass runs east and west. To the north is a tall mountain with a smooth slope that is impossible to traverse. To the south, a small cave opening can be seen in the side of the mountain along the pass.
118539:
A bedraggled orkish warrior of the Morruhk is here, looking miserable.
A bedraggled orkish warrior of the Morruhk is here, looking miserable.
A bedraggled orkish warrior of the Morruhk is here, looking miserable.

Cramped and damp, this cave has been naturally formed in the side of the mountain, over the passage of time. The cave provides some shelter from the harsh conditions outside, but the opening is just enough to allow the blustery wind to blow inside. The walls and ceiling are covered with thin mosses and lichen.
118540: A steep slope on the side of a tall mountain, covered in snow and ice, climbs upward into the sky toward the mountain summit. In the opposite direction, several rocks and boulders protrude out from the mountainside, providing footing along the treacherous traverse.
118541: Craggy Summit in the Misty Mountains

Here is the summit of one mountain in an endless sea among the Misty Mountains. Although it is lower than other summits, it still gives a great vantage of the surrounding terrain. Snow-covered caps surround it in every direction, with rocks and large boulders protruding here and there to create foot and hand holds for dauntless travellers.
118542: High above the ground, this mountain is rocky and snow-covered. Footing is made possible by jutting and jagged rocks that erupt from the sides of the mountain. The northern slope is smooth and covered in a thick bed of snow. The air is thin, cold, and damp.
118547: A mountain lion eyes you closely and prepares to pounce for his next meal.

Deep in the midst of the Misty Mountains, mountains of various sizes impede safe travel in most directions. A valley opens to the south, while the tall mountains continue to stretch west, north, and east. A narrow mountain pass is able to be used to travel among the mountains here.
118548: Rolling mountains stretch in every direction, and a small mountain pass can be utilized to travel east and west. The passage is extremely treacherous and cumbersome, hindering travel among the mountains and making it extremely slow. Large rocks and boulders jut out of the mountain sides.
118549: Travel among the mountains comes to an abrupt ending here, as the northern, eastern, and southern slopes of the mountain are extremely steep and hazardous. Travel in any of those directions is nearly impossible, as falling would lead to sure death. In the west, the mountains climb more gradual, providing much safer passage.
118550: A narrow mountain ridge stretches east to west, along the crest of a tall mountain. Passage here is dangerous, as the northern slope is almost a complete drop to the ground far below. The mountain descends more gradually to the south and east.
118551: A thin bear is here, hunting for food.

A narrow mountain ridge results in a dead-end as it rises, preventing further passage. A steep rise climbs to another ridge to the south that leads in a southeasterly fashion. The craggy slopes of the mountains are covered in moisture. Little vegetation grows between the boulders.
118552: The Misty Mountains, vast and sprawling across the landscape, climb skyward in every direction, as far as the eye can see. The slopes of the mountains are rocky and craggy, and there are narrow passes between a few of the mountains, allowing for travel among them.
118553: The wind carries an odd smell to your freezing nose. You can't quite decide if it's the smell of dead meat or trolls. Maybe it's both. You're deep in the mountains now, and your only choice is to continue onward. The mist is so heavy here that you won't see the trolls until you are on top of them if there are any at all in this barren and cold place.
118570: A welcome respite from the rocky, mountainous terrain, this valley floor is vast and sprawling, teeming with vegetation and wildlife. Patches of grass, short shrubs, and thin trees are spread throughout the area, and the rustling of animals and chirping of birds can be heard throughout the valley.
118571: East of here, the mountains rise up so steeply that you can't even get a good hold on the smooth rock. This part of the mountains seems somehow different and you feel safe for the moment. The cold wind has stopped and the distant noises that were probably screams have disappeared.
118572:
Some thick writhing vines whip all around you.
Massive roots shift uneasily all around you.

Mountains to the north and east, and a deep ravine to the south, create a natural dead-end. Vegetation and wildlife flourish here, and the grass grows thicker toward the west. Thorny bushes line the edges of the field around the base of the mountains.
118573: An obvious trail has been worn into the ground in the centre of the valley floor. The valley is wide, and opens up to the east and west, with the trail following it in those directions. There is a small creek here as well, which flows slowly, and runs parallel to the trail.
118574: Valley Trail South of a Ravine
A huge, black wolf is here, ready to devour.

The trail here stretches east and west, dusty, and gravelly underfoot. It is mostly flat, with small, thin patches of short grasses bordering it on the north and south. A calm, slowly-flowing stream runs parallel to the trail on its north side. Just on the other side of the creek is a deep, narrow ravine.
118575: A twisted and charred gate of iron lies in ruin.

A narrow trail runs east to west. The trail is rocky and dusty, worn in the centre due to being well-travelled, with long grasses growing alongside it. To the north of the trail, a slow-moving creek runs parallel to it. Shortly beyond the north bank of the creek is a deep but narrow ravine, making travel beyond impossible. To the south, steep mountains rise suddenly from the ground, and there is a dark cave opening in the mountainside.
118576: Rows of stone blocks are stacked neatly and uniformly in a large circle, an homage to a time long forgotten, the remnants of an ancient tower. In the centre of the circle of stones is a short staircase also made of stone, crumbling and broken. The first few steps of what appears to be a spiral staircase remain, but not much else. There is a deep, narrow ravine to the west and south of the ancient ruins, with no bottom to it in sight.
118577: The slope of the mountain is composed of loose rocks and treacherous drops that will lead to certain death if someone falls down. The Misty Mountains expand in almost all directions from here. The mountain descends to the west, where a valley floor is clearly visible from here. A trail that runs from the west to the east is discernible in the south.
118578: The trail continues east to west, sloping down steeply to the west as it descends into the mountainous terrain. The trail is dusty, and covered with loose gravel, which shifts and tumbles downward when disturbed with a footstep. Tall mountains stretch into the sky to the south, and traversing them does not seem possible.
118579: The trail here ascends steeply upward to the east, a wall of mountainous rock creating a natural border to its south. Small plants and grasses grow from the ground beside the dusty trail, which also slopes downward westerly. The mountainous surroundings open up to the north.
118580: A diamond-back rattlesnake is coiled here, ready to strike.

This is a bramble-filled valley floor near the Misty Mountains. The ground ascends to the north, where the mountains loom ominously. Travelling in this valley is not pleasant because of the thorny shrubs growing stubbornly in every place, between the random boulders here and there.
118581: The valley curves northward and eastward as the mountains open in each of those directions. The surrounding mountains cast deep shadows on the valley, and the air is damp and heavy. Mosses and lichen grow thick on the valley walls. A tall, steep mountain stretches skyward to the south and west.
118582: A valley runs in all directions but south, where a steep mountain wall blocks passage in that direction. The valley is dark and damp, and mosses and lichen cover the mountain walls on every side of the valley. The ground is bare and rocky.
118583: A low valley, surrounded by steep, mountainous walls, turns north and west. The ground is rocky, making travel cumbersome. Mosses and lichen cover the walls. Steep mountains rise in the east and south, making passage in those directions impossible. The mountains cast deep shadows on the valley, and there is a dampness in the air.
118584: This natural tunnel is wide in its centre and narrows to the north and south. A large gate, made of iron, had once been installed in the tunnel's northern rockwall, but it is now completely demolished. The tunnel to the south leads to a crossroads.
118585: The tunnel goes mostly north to south with a fork to the east and has a smooth rock floor. There's a chance that a sizable portion of this location was a naturally occurring geological formation. The areas to the south and east, however, appear to be former mine tunnels.
118586: At this juncture, the tunnel appears to be bigger. Although the earth below is solid, it is covered in highly decomposed sludge. The tunnel generally runs from north to south, with a branch that leads to an old mine tunnel to the east.
118587: Massive roots shift uneasily all around you.

An almost eight-foot-high tunnel, widest in the centre, travels north to south. Between the boulder-like walls and ceiling, roots progressively elongate. A grate that originally blocked the tunnel's southern entrance has been totally dismantled.
118588: Little mounds of broken weapons and bones line the solid, unyielding earthen walls of this cavern. A grate that originally acted as a barrier to the north has been completely demolished. The corridor grows more stony behind the destroyed grate, and the stench of scorched air is strong to the south.
118589: This cavern's westernmost section is a dead-end with the only apparent entrance to the east. Its walls are lined with cages that were once used to hold animals before being destroyed. Whatever animals were here have long since disappeared or perished.
118590: The walls of this cavern's intersection are lined with burned muck. This area still smells like death even though the fire that started the burning has long since died out. The exit from this intersection that stands out the most is to the east, where a larger cavern emerges.
118591:
A tiny spider is here, eating a tiny bug.
A tiny spider is here, eating a tiny bug.
A tiny spider is here, eating a tiny bug.
A huge, venomous spider is here.
A huge, venomous spider is here.

A deep pit occupies the majority of the cavern's floor space. The pit reeks of death and is coated with charcoal. Broken bones and decaying parts of weapons line the bottom of the pit. A tunnel of inky blackness leads north to an intersection.
118592: This is the westernmost part of a vast cavern. The ceiling of the cave collapsed toward the centre, making access to the deeper areas more difficult. The floor is littered with splintered bones. The only evident way out of the cavern is to the west.
118593: A large stone chest is here.

There is no way through the rocks and earth here because the cavern has fully collapsed; the only direction is to the west. Before it collapsed, the cavern must have had a tall ceiling akin to a vault or a dome. Everything that was once here has been buried beneath the debris.
118594: A skeleton of some humanoid lies in the dust.

The floor, the walls, and the ceiling of this portion of the cavern are all completely burned. The scent of the charred remains permeates the air even though the flames have long since died out. The cavern collapsed towards the northeast, leaving only passages to the north and east.
118595: The walls of the cavern are strewn with decaying wood. A massive stone rock is set with bones in the centre of this cave. It smells bad since the floor is covered in filth and decomposing animal fur. The large cavern collapsed toward the southeast, leaving a lot of dirt and rocks on the ground.
118596: A skeleton of some humanoid lies in the dust.
