There is no other way out than to the west because the cavern has collapsed here. Rotten wood and rusted meat hooks can be found among the debris on the floor. A sizable table was chiselled into the northern wall, which appears to be the cave's natural wall. Animal and humanoid bones are scattered all over the table.
118597: The massive stone walls bend outward to form a very massive tunnel here. In the pitch-blackness above, a curtain of shadow obscures the ceiling. In the tunnel's centre, the earth is very soft and looks to be made up of layers of gravel, sand, and mud. The walls thin out toward the east, as if the majority of the water had been absorbed by the bedrock.
118598: A Zaugurz orc soldier is standing here.

This tunnel, which runs from west to south, is small and confined. The walls rise to the ceiling above, and shelves stick out all along the way. Beds of dried vegetation have been constructed for critters to sleep in. Animal feces are strewn throughout the gravel that covers the stone floor.
118599: Smiles the Troll is standing here.

The tunnel gradually ascends while following the grain of the rock. The damp walls sparkle and glisten because of the intense reds that stain them. Despite being musty and stale, the air is cool, odourless, and not terribly unpleasant. The tunnel narrows as it travels north.
118600:
A noticeable crack runs down one of the walls.
Smiles the Troll is standing here.

On the wet walls of this mine shaft, old torch holders have been set up. A big hole has been excavated into the northern side of the mine. The mine runs roughly in an east-west direction, with an intersection visible to the west.
118601: Burnt-out Forge in a Collapsed Cavern

A skeleton of some humanoid lies in the dust.
A Zaugurz orc scout is standing here.

In a depression in the sloping floor of the cavern sits a burnt-out stone forge. A dense coating of black dust surrounds the forge, indicating that a massive fire completely destroyed this section of the cavern. The cavern's ceiling collapsed to the north, leaving only a few feet of space between the rubble to the north and the natural cavern's wall to the south.
118602: A skeleton of some humanoid lies in the dust.

The floor of this cavern's far southern side is littered with wood debris that has been partially burned into charcoal. The walls to the south are composed of granite and have old scratch marks. The cavern's floor is covered in thick layers of dust.
118603: The cavern has a large, deep hole in the southeast corner. The bones that are scattered throughout the hole suggest that it was formerly used for a grisly purpose. Rotten and splintered wood on the ground appears to be the remnants of some form of barricade, and the edges slope toward the north and west.
118604: This tunnel extends to the west until it becomes difficult to traverse due to a lot of debris. Large rocks and earthen detritus were plainly brought up from the collapsed ceiling. Only dust covers the floor, aside from occasional debris.
118605:
A skeleton of some humanoid lies in the dust.
*Wazgubul the Morruhk Orc*, wielding an engraved broadsword, is standing here.

Several decaying cages are fixed on the floor in the centre of the cavern. The last intact chains and shackles from the cages, which show that they were used to imprison humanoids, are left between little mounds of bones that are either completely crushed or broken into tiny fragments.
118606: Shaft in the Corner of a Cavern

The area next to the cavern's wall is littered with wooden debris and rusted metal rings that appear to have been used as barrel hoops in the past. The remains of an iron cauldron, now useless and filled with holes, are located below an intact shaft that provides the cavern with fresh air.
118607:
The remains of a smashed well lie here in pieces.
A skeleton of some humanoid lies in the dust.
A large bat is here, fighting Smiles.
A huge bat is here, fighting Smiles.
A large bat is lying here, mortally wounded.
A hungry warg stands here, sniffing around for flesh.
Smiles the Troll is here, fighting a large bat.

Because of dirt and stone rubble left over after a collapse that blocked the west and south entrances to the cave, the only visible exit is to the east. The ruins of a stone well that had been built on a stone dais can be found in the middle of this cavern's northern wall. The water that used to collect in the well now trickles toward the south and disappears beneath debris.
118608:
A slavering warg stands here, sniffing around for fresh meat.
Smiles the Troll is standing here.

This ruined kennel is in an awfully dilapidated state with rusty, twisted cages and broken beams covering the floor. Rubble has fallen from the cavern ceiling to the ground causing movement to be difficult. A few cages have been completely flattened and rusty metal protrudes dangerously, ready to impale.
118609:
A large crystal stands out between the rocks.
A bear cub is here, looking around for something to play with.

The walls of this cave are crystalline and are composed of many small fractals of colour. Judging by the bones and decomposing remains on the floor, some wild creatures have discovered it and decided to make their home here. The cave continues deeper below ground level.
118610:
A brown bear is sleeping here.
A brown bear is sleeping here.
A bear cub is here, looking around for something to play with.

This small cave is littered with rocks and boulders. The temperature in here, below ground level, is high and the air is humid. A faint breeze of fresh air can be felt coming from above where the cave walls are covered with crystals.
118611: At the top of a Roaring Waterfall

The river abruptly ends here, flowing off the top of a waterfall as it carries on its journey west. The rushing noise of the water fills the air, accompanying a majestic view of the river and plains to the west. To the south, the brushland stands as a thick border to the river, with thin branches grasping out over the flowing surface of the water. Following the river into open air is possible, but perilous.
118613: A brook trout is here, swimming in the current.

A thick mist of water spray permeates the air here making it impossible to distinguish anything more than a few feet away. The sound of falling water is so loud as to drown out any other noise. The turbulent waters of the river, which roar down from a cliff to the east, buffet anyone trying to maintain their position standing here.
118614:
A long water trough made of wood stands here.
A bale of hay is lying here.
A sturdy bandit bodyguard stands here, eager to hack you to pieces.
A sturdy bandit bodyguard stands here, eager to hack you to pieces.
A beautiful and docile horse is standing here.

The stable walls are in a state of decay and deteriorating, including the roof above. Although it is clear the building itself has not been maintained in many years, the natural earth and dust along the ground appear disturbed, with more dust, gravel and rocks along the north and south walls. An impression within the dirt leads from the stable door along the western wall to the eastern wall where it disppears beyond sight beneath the wooden planks.
118615: The shed appears aged and unsafe, with the roof caved in slightly in several places. Years of weather and being unmaintained caused the shed to be at a state of disrepair. The planks are rotten and damaged along the ground from the rain and snow that have entered over time, with a select few along the western wall that were poorly replaced. The door of the shed is uneven from the weight and years on the hinges that are loose upon on the eastern wall.
118617:
A large, dusty alcove sits in a wall, smelling of soot.
A small oaken table has been set here.
On the table, there is a musty loaf of bread.
A small black vicious rat squeaks at you for disturbing it.

Uneven wooden boards, warped by age and damp, compose the floor of this long, low-roofed room. A thick carpet of green mould covers much of the floor, as well as the shattered remains of four heavy oak tables. The last few pieces of kindling by the fireplace look suspiciously like the legs of a chair. At one end of the room a long, sturdy counter rests atop a heavy wooden base, but some of its boards have been pried loose and pressed into service to block the back door of the structure entirely. Each of the windows has also been boarded over, though not so thoroughly as to prevent the entry of all natural light.
118618:
A sturdy crate made of nailed wooden planks sits on the floor.
A beer barrel has been left here.
A huge, poisonous spider is here.
A huge, poisonous spider is here.

The air here seems heavy and unwholesome. A noisome aroma pervades every corner and the walls are black with mildew. The most noticeable feature of this place, however, are the thick strands of sticky silk that crisscross from one wall to the other, extending from the uneven boards of the roof above to the chilly flagstones of the floor underfoot. The tiny bones of countless small creatures lie strewn all about the room.
118619:
The corpse of a bandit bodyguard is lying here.
The corpse of a bandit bodyguard is lying here.
A sturdy crate made of nailed wooden planks sits on the floor.

Built amid the roof trusses, the loft offers little head room, except to those of short stature. Front to back it is as wide as the inn below, with no attempt having been made to wall off the near useless floor space where the roof slopes right down to meet the rough floorboards. All around the room, but concentrated at the angles of the roof, lie the scattered remains of discarded wooden crates and boxes. Oddly, the loft does not seem nearly so long as the room below.
118620: The tunnel begins here and leads to the east, with six large beams made from a thick and sturdy wood to support the ceiling, which was also made of thick wooden panels. A small table, old and dusty, stand in the north-west corner of the entrance, with some of the chairs broken and in pieces along the ground. The western wall is made of stone and the floor is lined with flagstones; they appear to continue beneath the wall as if they continue to something beyond.
118621: The tunnel travels from the west and bends sharply in the centre, leading north to another section of the tunnel. The ceiling was reinforced here with wooden beams and eight large timbers that were reinforced with metal to use as braces from the ground to the ceiling. Four beams, two on each side to the west of the bend, and another four beams stand to support the ceiling to the north. A thick dusting covers the ground and lingers within the air, and several spider webs are in the south-east corner at the sharp bend in the tunnel.
118622: A bloodthirsty bat is sleeping here, hanging from the ceiling.

The tunnel travels from a north and south direction, appearing to widen greatly to the north where a thick darkness consumes whatever lies beyond there. The ceiling was reinforced here with wooden beams and six large timbers that were reinforced with metal to use as braces from the ground to the ceiling. Although the wood does not appear aged, it is covered in a thick dust that would imply this underpass has not been used frequently.
118623:
A large bat is here, hanging in the darkness.
A large bat is here, hanging in the darkness.
A large bat is here, hanging in the darkness.
A huge bat is here, emitting piercing squeaks.

The profound cavity is dark and deep, with niches along the south portion to help with footing over the earthen basin that was naturally formed here. Over the basin to the south, from what is visible from here at least, the cavern or tunnel continues. A draft is felt somewhere from above, but the darkness is so thick there it would be impossible to guess from which direction. Small rocks and pebbles are scattered along the centre of the cavity, with dust lingering along the earth, debris and even in the air.
118624: This fairly narrow tunnel was apparently excavated by some form of wildlife, for its walls bear what can only be claw marks. Turning slightly, so as to protect what lies beyond from any onslaught by the elements, the tunnel slopes gently downwards to the west, exploiting the natural rock strata to make digging easier, and take advantage of the natural drainage they provide.
118625: Having turned slightly as it cut deeper into the ground, the tunnel here is quite protected from the elements, creating a small but cosy nook. But even so, someone has taken great trouble to insulate the area with rolled heaps of bedding, so thick that they could even smother the sound of a footfall. Dry bundles of grass are mixed with leaves, twigs, and soft, twisted roots to line the rocky floor of the tunnel.
118626:
A dirty bandit waits here looking for an easy mark.
A dirty bandit waits here looking for an easy mark.

The tunnel comes to an abrupt end here in a tangle of fallen rock and fractured wooden posts. The roof above is comprised of a single, massive slab of sandstone that now lies at a severe angle, making it quite low toward the back. Sturdy iron tracks vanish beneath the mound of boulders, indicating at one point this was a mine, although it seems it was abandoned for those purposes a long time ago.
118627:
A small oaken table has been set here.
On the table, there are a dark bottle, two musty loaves of bread, and a raccoon fur hat.
A filthy straw pallet is lying here.
A malicious thug is here, threatening you.
A very strong orkish patrol-leader is looking for enemies here.
An orkish soldier is here, patrolling the area.
An orkish soldier is here, patrolling the area.
An orkish soldier is here, patrolling the area.

The rickety old cabin is filled with dust and cobwebs. The interior is very shabby and it seems the cabin is soon to collapse. In the middle of the room, which seems to serve as both a living room and bedroom, stands a small table. The bed is nothing more than a pallet in the corner and a wooden structure on the wall serves as a closet.
118628: A great wolf with coal-black eyes stares intently at you, drooling saliva.

The claw marks on the ground indicate that a huge animal built this burrow through the dirt. The walls and floor are constructed of dark soil that is laced with varying-diameter tree roots and the occasional stones. The natural tunnel's exit is hidden by a thick foliage.
118629: A scattering of sunlight reaches partway into this cave, giving food to small patches of red and green moss. The dirt floor is covered in footprints of various sizes, both large and small. The larger footprints sink deep into the hard earth, as if a heavy beast created them. Tiny, pointed pebbles, and dead grass have collected in the large depressions, their meandering paths across the grassy plains outside the caves coming to an end here.
118630:
The ugly troll mother is roaming the cave, taking care of her loved ones.
An old, strong cave troll is standing here.
The garden snake slithers harmlessly here.
A powerful young troll stares at you.

Large, bulbous boulders form the base of this large cave, and their large, beady faces form a deeply uneven surface on which to walk. No natural light reaches this far into the cavern, and the only signs of plant life are the withering tree roots that poke through the walls of dirt. A jumbled mound of dirt, and rocks of various sizes sits at the base of the western wall, perhaps a sign of digging, or excavation.
118631:
A small, mean earth troll is standing here, thinking of something hideous.
A small, mean earth troll is standing here, thinking of something hideous.

Clumps of dead grass, and a scattering of dirt, pebbles, and feathers have collected in this shallow inlet that has formed within the hills. Serrated rocks poke through the dirt floor, creating a tripping hazard for unwary travellers, and a potential death trap for those who trip.
118632: A junebug buzzes slowly through the air.

A trickle of water seeps from a crack in the rocky cave wall, covering the brown floor in a layer of mud and slippery rocks. Large boulders embedded within the walls create permanent, deep shadows on the soupy floor, and provide excellent cover for small animals and insects.
118633:
An old, strong cave troll is standing here.
A powerful young troll stares at you.

The brown walls of this cave are speckled with small sections of white quartz, and the dying ends of furry tree roots. The ground is a slippery mix of mud and sheer rock, and a jumbled mix of large and small footprints are imprinted into its surface. A small hole near the western wall is filled with a dark liquid of unknown origin.
118634:
A brown toad is here, hunting flies.
A great bustard strides over the grass.
A colourful butterfly is fluttering around here.

This grass covered hill drops quickly to the north and east. The absence of any tall vegetation allows for excellent visibility in all directions for several miles. Running along the northern margin of the hill, a small stream cuts through the countryside. To the west, an old and decaying road makes its way from north to south.
118635: Low grass grows here between large boulders, and the plains are littered with small, thorny bushes of all types which seem to grow more dense to the south. To the north some hills dot the horizon and to the west an old road marches on.
118636: Sheltered against the tall hills to the east, some dense foliage has flourished here making a soft rustle with each movement. Bristly shrubs, cracked by lack of water, crunch and writhe at the slightest wind. Southwards seems impassable while thick arid undergrowth dominates the west.
118637: Dry grass and shrubs grow out of the countless cracks in the hard, dry clay here. With each puff, a wind causes a constant crackling in the foliage. To the east the foliage continues. North, west, and south, an ancient road can be spied through the bushes, meandering along.
118638:
A huge, black wolf is here, ready to devour.
A huge, black wolf is here, ready to devour.
A black wolf pads restlessly, looking for its next prey.
A large brown wolf stands here, its teeth partly bared.

A general lack of vegetation can be found leading down into this dark wolf lair hinting at its activity. The lair is fairly clean, but carcass parts including bones, antlers, and hair have been brought by the pack's members and have been strewn about. The only way out of the lair is to go up.
118640: To the east, brush-covered plains sprawl out, and on the horizon the outline of distant mountains kisses the sky. To the north, nature and the hand of man fight for dominance of the land, where the plains meet an old, ruined roadway. Thick brush, short tussocks of coarse grass, and scattered rocks litter the landscape here. A rocky shelf that stands above the plain to the west and south must be the origin for the many boulders that have come to rest here.
118641: The plains stretch out in all directions, overgrown in this area by an abundance of low, thorny bushes. Their almost-naked branches have become twisted and tangled by the cruel prevailing winds. The ground is rather parched here, and the only other vegetation to be seen in the thin, rocky soil are a few stunted weeds and patches of coarse, yellowing grasses. Small rocks and larger boulders lie all about.
118642: Thick brush nestles here, thriving in a quite sheltered area, at least compared to the more open plains hereabouts. A rocky shelf stands to the south and west, forcing the chill winds that assail these lands upward and away from the ground. The result is a thicker layer of topsoil that can better support the vegetation.
118643:
A warm blanket covers the ground.
A Dunadan sentry vigilantly watches the surrounding lands.
A Dunadan sentry vigilantly watches the surrounding lands.

The small trail takes a sharp turn here bordering a rocky promontory that boasts a commanding view of the plains stretching out below. Little vegetation is to be seen on this stony table, which is so exposed to the blustery winds howling throughout these lands, that no topsoil worth speaking of remains. Still, a few tiny flowers sprout from cracks in the rock. Many, however, have been crushed underfoot, just one sign that this area is used as a camp.
118644: Rising Trail at the Foot of a High Cliff

The trail bends to the east and to the north here, running for a short time along the foot of a high cliff, climbing steadily as it does so. The mountain range to the south is tall and imposing, and it is not possible to scale its heights from this location. The topsoil is thin, probably as a result of the punishing winds that torment these lands month after month. No vegetation thrives here except for a few small, flowers that peep up through cracks in the rock, and there is little to mark the trail from the stony ground alongside it.
118645: A rock lizard is here, motionless as it observes you.

Cutting across the edge of a rocky plateau, an old, and barely noticeable trail makes its way from east to west. Running westward for quite some distance, it comes to an abrupt end however, not far to the east of here, where it meets up with a large rock pile. The massive wall of fallen rocks and boulders extends far to the south with a narrow gap threading its way through.
118646: Box Canyon in the Hollin Ridge

A dense carpet of blue flowers dip their heads in the breeze.
A bright green holly bush is growing here.
Partly covered by the bush's green leaves, there are two piles of hollyberries.

The more exposed parts of the plateau that lie further north are bare and rocky, but this small box canyon is fertile. It has become a meadow, protected on three sides from the chill winds that whip across the rest of these lands, denuding them of vegetation and topsoil.
118647: Slope on the North Face of a Spur

Rising steeply towards the peaks to the west, this mountainous slope faces the plains that lie north of the spur. The descent to the north is sharp, ending in a treacherous field of scree that marches down to the top of a tall cliff. East the going becomes a little easier, as the slope lessens.
118648: Green grass grows here in abundance, cascading over the cliff to the east. Nestling in the protection of the mountains, and of a range of hills that stands to the north, the valley stretches out to the east, a veritable oasis of vegetation amid the poor plains that characterize this region.
118649:
A nightingale is here, chirping a sweet melody.
A mountain goat is here, jumping from cliff to cliff.

An occasional blast of cold air rushes up the side of this mountain, as the winds of the chasm to the north encounter the sloping ground. Aside from the sounds of a loosened stone or dried leaf rolling along the ground, the low rush of moving air is all that can be heard.
118650: A large marmot is here, scurrying in between the rocks.

A large chasm cuts across the land to the north; more of a valley between high peaks, it effectively parts this region from the areas across it. A quiet and chill wind carries through the valley, giving the whole place a somewhat cold and unwelcoming feel.
118651: Cold, lifeless, distant from settled lands, and at times hostile, these tall mountain peaks are poorly suited for travel or for rest. Sharp stones lie scattered around the soil. No trees grow to provide firewood, no water flows or even sits stagnant to soothe wounds or refresh the tired wanderer.
118653:
A large marmot is here, scurrying in between the rocks.
A large marmot is here, scurrying in between the rocks.

A stunning view of mountainous terrain, and little else, is offered here. In all directions, mountains extend to the horizon and block sight of anything beyond, if indeed anything lies there. Perhaps this place is all that now exists; no reminders of comfortable dwellings or sustaining food appear on the steep slopes of the mountains. This place is forgotten by the world, and indeed that world seems only a lingering memory.
118654: Great distances separate this place from any safe havens; no shelter exists to offer protection against the burning sun or freezing snows. The ground is soaked with each rainstorm, and gravel is thrown through the air when winds blow through the area; no feature of this place makes it suitable for meaningful rest.
118655:
A mountain goat is here, jumping from cliff to cliff.
A mountain goat is here, jumping from cliff to cliff.
A mountain goat is here, jumping from cliff to cliff.

To many, a place of total despair is often pictured as a firey pit of anguish in which the unfortunate are doomed to burn for all of time. However, what is not often perceived is that a cold, lifeless, distant, and compeletely lonely area such as these mountains can also take its toll on sanity, and might be just as torturing.
118656: Some small rocks have been piled into a mound here.

Oddly placed in the middle of the mountains, a small pile of stones has been piled up here, but in a place where such rocks would not gather on their own. Instead, this mound is in the midst of otherwise level and clear terrain. Perhaps, long ago, some unlucky traveller was laid to rest here, when the mountains proved too treacherous.
118657:
Klaees (thedon), wielding a great warsword, is standing here.
Bulg (pukespy), wielding a great warsword, is standing here.
Drazud (freshmeat), wielding a great warsword, is standing here.

An old stone staircase winds its way down from the mountains above. Clear, cold water has collected at the basin of this high valley, creating a small mountain lake. With steep slopes to all sides, a lush green alcove has flourished here.
118658: Though not coming close to the heights reached by the loftier Caradhras, Celebdil and Fanuidhol, these peaks nonetheless reach high into the sky. An old stone staircase seemingly carved into the mountain can be seen winding a narrow path down the slope.
118659: Tree-lined peaks soar high above, even from this lofty vantage point. This long ridge reaches out from the Misty Mountains, like mighty fingers that grasp at the lower-lying plains beyond. Dipping a little to the east, the slopes draw closer to a narrow pass.
118660: From both north and south mountainsides, an ancient road climbs up to a narrow pass through this spur. The vantage point here allows seeing any traveller along the way for a long distance. An eerie quietness pervades this mountain perch, waiting, watching.
118662: Magnificent peaks stand atop unscalable slopes to the east and north of here. The entrance to a cave opens up to the south, while to the west there seems to be a faint path where small stones and rocks have been kicked out of the way.
118663: Craggy slopes roll down to the east, allowing for a possible descent down the mountainside. To the south, jagged cliffs plummet downwards making it impossible to traverse. White flowers peek out from behind many of the grey rocks.
118664:
A sturdy crate made of nailed wooden planks sits on the floor.
A Dunadan sentry vigilantly watches the entrance to the cave.

A weather-beaten cave provides some form of shelter here. Dirt has been tracked in and out of this cave, and wooden beams shore up its walls. The trail of dirt lead outside seems to come the east and west. Although the cave seems naturally formed, traces of craftsmanship can be seen about the edges.
118665:
An old stone statue stands here, its timeworn features difficult to make out.
A disfigured elven trader looks about with watchful eyes.

A great slab of rock juts out from the wall to the east, making passage to the north almost impossible. Only a narrow gap between the west wall of the tunnel and this protrusion can be seen. At the centre of this passage an ancient statue stands proudly yet is quite worn. The form of the statue can just barely be distinguished as that of an elf.
118666:
A weapons rack stands against the wall.
In the rack are a longbow and a light crossbow.
A neat straw pallet is lying here.
A target sits in the corner of the room.
A Dunadan sentry is standing here, preparing to train.

A couple of rough, wooden practice targets have been set here with deep gashes in them indicating heavy use. Straw lines the floor, tossed here and there making for a soft footing. The granite walls of the cave have been skillfuly carved and are smooth and perfectly vertical.
118667:
A Dunadan soldier is on duty here, guarding the stronghold.
A Dunadan soldier is on duty here, guarding the stronghold.
A Dunadan archer is here busily performing his duties.

A stone causeway perfectly level and smooth has been laid here. Dust and rubble have been swept to the edges of the walkway. On the walls hang heavy iron torches, flooding the area in a small circle of light. Here an intersections of paths branch off leading east, north and south.
118668: The path travels north and west, while to the south an adjoining area is lit with a dull glow. Torches have been hung on the walls providing both light and warmth to the passage, and casting flickering shadows upon the walls. Rocks and rubble line the sides of the walkway.
118669: Dimly lit by torches, a staircase can be seen here leading down. No railings are attached to it, and it is made of solid rock. Masterfully they are carved yet very old. They wind downward in a spiral, while to the north the tunnel continues up a gentle slope. Thick dust lies here as if it is seldom disturbed.
118670: The steps disappear above and below in a spiral. The granite from which they have been cut, once coarse, are now worn smooth with the footsteps of those who have come before. A black vein of obsidian runs along the passage, winding around the staircase like a vine.
118671: A Dunadan sentry is here standing guard at the base of the stair.

The staircase winds its way up and down with little to be seen in either direction due to the spiralling nature of the steps. Small stones mixed with slivers of shale are strewn about the stair, making careful foot placement an absolute must. The air is dry and musty, with particles of dust floating in the stillness.
118672: Streaks of limestone slash their way horizontally across the cave walls, while a blank greyness envelops the rest of the rock. The tunnel floor has been cut quite smooth. Traces of decorative carvings are barely visible among the walls, almost entirely faded with the passage of time.
118673: A hungry-looking giant lizard is slithering towards you (hidden).

Clearly fallen into disrepair, this tunnel leads off into the east and west. Grey stone dominates this cavern, with hardly another colour to be seen; an ocean of granite laps its way up the walls and ceiling. Small shelves of rock seem to have been cut into the walls for some forgotten purpose.
118674: A patch of moss grows here on a wet, flat stone.

Buried deep beneath the Misty Mountains, no natural light has ever reached this tunnel. The rough walls bear no distinctive features, and getting lost within these caverns would be very easy. But from here the choice of route is rather limited: the tunnel stretches west and south.
118675: The walkway makes a sharp bend from south to west, visible through the light cast by a single lit torch. On the eastern walls a great white rock, pale and almost luminous, juts out from the wall like a sword. It seems as if chunks of it are missing as if someone has taken a pick to it at some point.
118676: The passage walls bear no mark of pick or chisel, yet are smooth and quite polished. The tunnel here continues east and west, paved with wooden planks. Torches light the hallway and the sound of their crackling echoes off the stone walls. A light breeze can sometimes be detected coming from somewhere to the east.
118677: Bridge over a Pool of Darkness

A wooden platform spans from the east to the south, offering footing over a gaping chasm that opens down below. Here and there the floorboards are missing, and the bridge-like structure creaks and groans as weight is placed upon it. Nothing can be seen when peering down into the blackness of the chasm.
118678: A large crack lies in the floor, dividing the area down the middle.

The tunnel narrows here as it traverses north and south, leaving little room to wriggle through. The air is hot and stuffy, drafting up from the depths of the mountain itself from a crack that runs perpendicular across the tunnel. Some mounds of rubble have been pushed aside to clear space through the tunnel.
118679: A long, black fissure can be seen in the southwest corner of this cave leading, to an unending void of darkness. Wooden planks are stacked in front of it helping to bar anything from falling through. Torches help light the area casting flickering shadows which dance mysteriously on the walls.
118680: A Dunadan sentry is here standing guard.

The stone walkway extends to the west and east but branching in other directions as well. To the north and south, dark metal doors contrast with the rock wall. The south opens up into a larger hall where some smoke can be seen flowing in. Pelts of various animals line the walls.
118681:
A filthy straw pallet is lying here.
A renegade uruk is chained here, looking around with anger.

The cold floor and walls of this prison cell are comprised of solid grey rock. Desperate dig marks can be seen pocked across the walls from previous prisoners. Some soiled straw covers the ground while many sets of iron chains and shackles can be seen fastened to the walls.
118682:
A rough wooden bunkbed is pushed against the back wall.
A large stone fireplace with a roaring fire warms the room.
A Dunadan sentry is sleeping here.
A Dunadan sentry is sleeping here.
An elven ranger is here, changing the dressing on one of his bandages.
An elven maid, tall and lithe, sings a song as she tends the fire.
A Dunadan soldier is here busily performing his duties.
A Dunadan soldier is here busily performing his duties.
A Dunadan archer is here busily performing his duties.

A thick plume of smoke billows upwards from a rough campfire, exiting from a small hole in the ceiling, which allows for some respite from the difficult to breathe air. A few bunkbeds made of wooden stand around the edges of the room, as if bolted to the walls. Heavy, warm bear hides have been strung up around the dormitory.
118683:
A roast haunch of boar sends up a fragrant aroma.
A water barrel has been left here.
A small oaken table has been set here.
On the table, there are two pieces of smoked, cured meat and a casserole.
A wooden bench stands on one side of the table.
A Dunadan sentry is here preparing some meals.
An experienced Dunadan officer is standing here, keeping things under control.
A Dunadan sentry is here preparing some meals.

A long wooden table with iron fittings on each corner stands in the centre of the room. Chairs are gathered around it. A single lantern hangs above, casting as much shadow as it does light. In the back corner, a roaring hearth spreads a warm glow throughout the room as spits of meat roast over the open flame.
118684:
A nest is here.
A big, nasty vulture is sitting here, protecting its nest.
A big, nasty vulture is sitting here, protecting its nest.

Rolling mountains slope downwards to the east and south. The slope comes to an abrupt end just to the north of here at the top of a high cliff. Though it offers an unparalleled vista of the lands below, this cliff stands at such a height above the plains that no real detail is visible from here.
118685: A roughly cut tunnel stands here. Deep in the dark the tunnel curves around eventually twisting a path to the north. While clearly hewn from the rock, this passage seems to have not been touched by the hand of a living thing in at least an age.
118686:
A hungry-looking giant lizard is slithering towards you.
A hungry-looking giant lizard is slithering towards you.

The large crack to the south acts as a shield, blocking this cave from view. To the north a hole in the stone leads into another another small cave. A smooth patch of ground seems to have been cleared along one of the walls of this cave, while rubble lies on the floor everywhere else.
118687: Pool of Water in the Rocks

An albino salamander is here, perched on some rocks.
An albino salamander is here, perched on some rocks.
An albino salamander is here, perched on some rocks.

The floor here is jagged, with hundreds of grey rocks creating an uneven surface. At the far end of the cave a pool of water has accumulated in a basin. The water seems to be trickle from holes in the rocky walls. It dribbles slowly down their surfaces until collecting in the clear puddle.
118688: The cave is tall and wide. In the centre, a great chunk of rock has fallen from above and rests like a stone table. Above, there is an opening from whence this boulder must have come from. The walls are studded with twinkling stones guarding any secret, dark crevice.
118689: A greenish slime mould is here, smelling badly.

The tunnel worms its way up and down, with walls that are exceedingly worn and smooth. Tufts of mould grow dotted here and there on the walls. A strange ooze runs down the tunnel like viscous drool from above. Something dug or eroded this tunnel long ago, but what it was can only be guessed.
118690:
A greenish slime mould is here, smelling badly.
A giant, strange looking green fungus is here, ready to devour you in seconds.

The cavern walls shine in the dark as if covered in some liquid. Underfoot, a sticky ooze covers the ground. A horrible smell pervades this cave though the source is unclear. The air is perfectly still, and silence echoes deafeningly through the cave.
118691:
A giant, strange looking green fungus is here, ready to devour you in seconds.
A huge black fungus is here, exuding a foul stench.

Blackness envelops this room like moonless night. The walls are impossible to make out, and the floor is buried under something soft and squishy. The unidentifiable substance underfoot periodically squelches and spurts something foul onto the ground accompanied by a fetid smell. The air reeks of death.
118692:
A huge, poisonous tarantula extends her legs to you.
A newborn spider is here, hungrily crawling about.
A newborn spider is here, hungrily crawling about.

The cavern extends to the east and north; cobwebs spring into view showering the cave with their white, silky strings. A dreadful skittering can be heard from somewhere nearby, and a smell which can only be described as insulting to the very stones lingers here in dreadful delight.
118693:
A skeleton of some humanoid lies in the dust.
A black spider crawls here, a shiny red spot visible on its belly.
A black spider crawls here, a shiny red spot visible on its belly.

Thick cobwebs span the cave stretching from wall to wall. From up above, individual glistening strands of webbing coated in a sticky goo drift about on any breath of air that will carry them. As for the ceiling above, only darkness can be seen beyond the hanging lines. Darkness... and something else.
118694:
A rotting corpse is hanging here, covered in thousands of eggs.
A newborn spider is here, hungrily crawling about.
A newborn spider is here, hungrily crawling about.

The floor is strewn with cobwebs and bones. In the south of the cave, a small platform of rock stands a few inches above the rest of the floor. The stone platform is heavily webbed and from it hang several bodies. Thousands of eggs have been laid across the platform, affixed to corpse and stone.
118695:
A small box clutched by dead hands is poking out from the heap.
A grey spider is here wading through the flesh.

Putrid and seeping, a pile of corpses dominates the centre of this grim den. Pus drips from the gashes inflicted upon the mangled bodies, yet they are completely devoid of blood. The sockets, where the eyes once rested, are now bare and cold. A ghostly chill runs through the room as if death itself was watching over it.
118696: The rocky tunnel swerves hither and thither snaking its way to the west and south. Sticky webs suddenly appear as the tunnel leads westward, a few large bones dangling within the strands. Some debris rubble can be seen to the south where a large cave-in occurred, making it difficult to pass through.
118697: The corpse of a large earth troll is lying here.

Debris has fallen from above, creating a mound in the centre of this tunnel and hindering the passage. The natural cavern boasts little in the form of living things, but the air is not completely foul. A trickle of dirt falling from the ceiling indicates that the surface lies not far above.
118698:
A small, mean earth troll is standing here, thinking of something hideous.
A large earth troll is digging here, looking for some tasty morsels.

Underfoot the floor is predominantly comprised of stone with streaks of dirt here and there. To the north the blackness only grows deeper in the air carries a foul scent. Southwards, while no trace of light can be seen, a hint of fresh air can be felt.
118699: A small, mean earth troll is standing here, thinking of something hideous.

A musty scent hangs in the air in much the same way arrows do not. The walls here are a textured amalgamation of stone and earth. Any sound produced in this tunnel is instantly muffled by the copious amounts of exposed dirt.
118700: A small, mean earth troll is standing here, thinking of something hideous.

Thin streams of dirt trickle from the soft earth above. Above a breath of air can be felt washing over the the area. To the north the darkness of the tunnel winds away. Underfoot the soil is soft and roots creep about eager to catch unwary step.
118701: Surrounded completely by tall mountain peaks that dominate the land in all directions, this place shows no little sign of supporting wildlife, and even less of civilisation. A flowing breeze which winds its way between the peaks is all that disturbs the otherwise complete calm.
118702: A demon wolf lurks here, its dark form twisting and hiding its shape.

Deathly quiet, when rocks are not tumbling down the steep slopes, and when the winds subside long enough to let the heavy air come to rest is all that envelops these mountains. No insects buzz through the air, no birds call from overhead. Only an unsettling peace and stillness remains.
118706: The ceiling dips slightly, making this cavern a bit shallow. The walls, now the texture of granite, slide into the floor making the available space to stand scarce. Nooks and crevices can be seen travelling deep into the rocky walls causing numerous black holes to peep out.
118707: The cavern opens up a little to give some standing room. To the east an extremely cramped passage can be seen disappearing into the rock while to the north and south two more caves connect with this one. The air is still and stale; nothing breathes here.
118708: The ceiling in this cave hangs rather low to the ground with sharp stalactites jutting down from it. The air feels close and anxious with and almost deafening silence. A black strip of sparkling black rock seems to run like a river along the ceiling.
118709: The ceiling of this little space hangs low, making it difficult to pass through comfortably while the floor slants upward. The limestone walls crumble and trickle shards of rock onto the ground at the slightest touch. Westwards the path seems to become quite difficult, while the path east is a bit more open.
118710: A pale stone troll walks around here, looking for a fight.

Inside this fissure of rock, shelves of limestone form a scaffolding that might be possible to scale. Up above it is difficult to see a path forward as stalactites hang down blocking vision in that direction, but perhaps a small hole is visible. To the west a very narrow opening can be spotted; maybe it is big enough to squeeze through.
118711:
The battered corpse of an orc ripped in half lies on the floor.
A stone troll peers out from behind a rock.

Glistening rivers of obsidian stone writhe their way up the walls, intertwining throughout the rocky strata. The cave, much like a horrible black mouth, has stalactites and stalagmites scattered haphazardly throughout the rounded walls, and extends off to the west and south. Naturally formed steps provide a path to what appears to be a cave above this one.
118712: The cavern walls here are composed of a white, speckled stone. One solid grey rock leans against the northern rockface, and a black slab covers part of the pavement. Both are in stark contrast to the smooth marble walls. A crack runs along the ceiling of the passage. Nothing can be seen behind the darkness that lives in the crack.
118713: Boulders dominate the floor of the tunnel, with large pockets of space clearly visible in the ceiling from whence they undoubtedly came. The majority of the fallen stones are piled up in the northeast part of the passage causing the entire area to be tilted. The stones composition is unclear, but it crumbles quite easily. The tunnel bends sharply north and east.
118714: A young and vicious olog-hai eagerly awaits intruders.

A natural cave has formed here. The grey walls are marred with streaks of brown and black, and the floor is uneven with rocks taking up almost every inch of space. To the north, east and west it appears there are adjoining caverns, but it is impossible to make out what is in them from here.
118715: Bruzhor the Olog-hai is here, looking grim and hostile.

A huge pit cuts through the floor of this cave. Stretching several yards in length, it would be impossible to cross if it wasn't for the crude, rope bridge stretched across it. Darkness rises up from the depths of the chasm, and at the bottom, a void devours all knowledge of what could be known of that place.
118716:
A large bat is here, hanging in the darkness.
A large bat is here, hanging in the darkness.
A large bat is here, hanging in the darkness.
A huge bat is here, emitting piercing squeaks.
A bloodthirsty bat is sleeping here, hanging from the ceiling.
A bloodthirsty bat is sleeping here, hanging from the ceiling.

A natural stair rises up into this rocky dome. The tunnel floor can still be seen below, dominated by boulders, as it bends to the north and east. The rock here is of a crumbly nature which makes climbing impossible. A tiny crack at the top of the dome can be seen leading outside to the west.
118717: An ancient fungus smothers the boulders.

Smaller than most, this cave is bone-chillingly cold and tight. Its ceiling is low and very uneven with large, jagged rocks jutting down in many places. The floor is similarly rugged with scattered boulders and large holes all around. A gaping fissure in the floor leads into some blackness below.
118718: The damp walls of this crooked tunnel have seemingly been carved by crude tools into a canvas of sorts, bearing primitive drawings formed of shallow scratches in the rock beneath. Most of them depict multiple robust humanoids fighting each other or feasting on animals and smaller humanoids alike.
118719:
A musty old chest is here.
A stone troll mother stands here, looking at a mural on the wall.

Complete darkness reigns supreme within these mountains. This great cavern seems have been roughly cut into the mountain. Crude, dark murals span the walls, depicting scenes of violence and debauchery. They appear to be painted with a strangely red, viscous liquid.
118720: The moist, mould-covered walls enclose a small, roughly square-shaped burrow. The nearly-decayed remainders of a few wooden barrels lie next to a pile of ripped cloth and bone fragments, all stained with a dark, reddish-brown crust of unknown origin.
118721:
A huge stone troll looms overhead, ready to crush your body.
A pale stone troll walks around here, looking for a fight.
A pale stone troll walks around here, looking for a fight.
A pale stone troll walks around here, looking for a fight.

The floor and walls are damp and slippery in this roughly rotund cavern section. Tiny streams of water trickle in from various fissures in the walls, forming brown, algae-filled puddles of various sizes all across the uneven floor. Even though most of this cavern seems to be of natural origin, a few larger fissures in the walls have definitely been widened after the fact.
118722: A pale stone troll walks around here, looking for a fight.

A pool of water, bubbling and rippling as if almost at a boil, dominates the centre of this cavern. The dark walls of the cave are stained an even darker hue than usual due to the moisture in the air. Along the south wall a low ledge seems to have been hewn into the surface like a crude shelf.
118723:
A giant, strange looking green fungus is here, ready to devour you in seconds.
A huge black fungus is here, exuding a foul stench.

An overpowering odour rifles through the air, stripping it of any semblance of nature. Great piles of gnawed bones litter the floor, with one particularly massive heap laying claim to the centre of the room. This place wears death like a heavy cloak. Occasionally, the bones seem to move, as if something was crawling under the surface.
118724:
A huge, smoking campfire is burning here.
A bulging sack, dripping blood, hangs from the ceiling.
A pale stone troll walks around here, looking for a fight.
A stone troll mother is standing here, prodding a blood-drenched sack.

Considerably warmer than the neighbouring cavern, this cave abruptly leads to a dead end. Piles of charred stones are scattered here and there bleeding a choking smoke from beneath. It is difficult to see through the haze and the scent of burning cracked rock fills the nostrils.
118725:
A filthy straw pallet is lying here.
A renegade uruk is here, dirty and ragged.
A renegade uruk is here, dirty and ragged.
A renegade uruk is here, dirty and ragged.
Bruzhor the Olog-hai is here, looking grim and hostile.

A stone arch, in defiance of nature and time, stands alone in the centre of the cave. The walls are made of a blackish stone with veins of some silvery rock branching up to the ceiling. Much of the dark stone that comprises the walls has fallen to the ground creating a black shroud along the outer edges of the cavern.
118726:
A troll bitch is here staring at her reflection in a piece of glass.
An infant troll, baring its teeth, snarls here.
An infant troll, baring its teeth, snarls here.

The hue of the rock here turns to a greyish yellow colour. Great spires of stone strike upwards and downwards from the ceiling and floor. Pools of water cover the ground allowing for little movement save on a path that leads west. The shallow water glows with a faint, iridescent green light.
118727:
A young cave troll is sleeping here.
A young cave troll is sleeping here.
A young cave troll is sleeping here.
The ugly troll mother is roaming the cave, taking care of her loved ones.

Great slabs of rock, protruding from the walls, stab their way into the centre of this cave. Like knives piercing a skull, the rock slabs make it impossible to simply walk straight through the cave, instead demanding a zigzag route. North, east and west the walls close in, and the only way out lies south.
118728: A cold wind scorches this steep ridge, and continuing the ascent south leads up to a high mountain peak covered in mist. Further south, lower slopes can be glimpsed beyond the peak. There is no level ground to be seen anywhere near as boulders dot the mountain side like barnacles on a stone.
118729: This is high on the slopes of one of the taller peaks of a mountain spur, and the only direction from here is down, whether by choice, or by a most untimely fall. The way down seems most unstable, and it is evident that anything that descends from here will take some of the mountain with it.
118731: Towering peaks loom high above to the south and east. The cracked and uneven ground is littered with loose rocks and large boulders half buried in dirt, many of which must have fallen here from the higher slopes. A chill wind constantly buffets the mountainside, suggesting that this may not be a wise place to linger.
118732:
A large pile of boulders is sitting here, probably debris from a rockslide.
A hungry warg stands here, sniffing around for flesh.

A narrow, rock ledge curves along the base of some high mountain cliffs here, offering a means of travel between the rocky crags that extend to the south, and a steep, but scalable ascent to the west. The snow-capped peaks that reach high into the sky to the north and east can barely be seen from this vantage point.
118733: To the north the chill winds seem to increase dramatically, rolling down a steep incline from the peaks above as if intent only on making travel that way even harder. The wind gusts down rhythmically, sounding almost like the flap of giant wings. Though a fairly gentle slope descends to the west of here, the eastern and southern rock walls are impassable.
118734: Like a massive finger of stone, this tall peak reaches high into the skies. All around the snowy slopes fall away, save far to the east where great peaks rage into the heavens. To the south a decline can be spotted worming its way down the mountain slopes. The air is heavy with the sound of strange voices chanting, whispering, cursing.
118735:
A burly giant is here, covered with thick fur and snow.
A burly giant is here, covered with thick fur and snow.
A massive snow giant is here, covered in white fur.

This mountain soars above the rest, only rising to greater heights to the east. A basin has formed here containing a frozen lake, and to the east an icy path can be discerned climbing its way further up the mountain. Winds carrying ice and snow flurry fiercely, while voices in the air mutter and scream endlessly.
118736: A huge stone giant is here, glaring at you.

Rocky cliffs and mountain slopes abound to the east, their lofty, snow-clad peaks reaching high into the cloudy skies. The southern cliffs are sheer and slippery. Gentler inclines to the east and west offer a choice of routes from here, though in all cases the journey would not be easy, the uneven, always sloping ground strewn with loose rocks and boulders.
118737: A huge stone giant is here, glaring at you.

A wide ravine opens up to the north, spanned by a decrepit bridge. East and west, the mountain peaks stretch out in a long chain that reaches far into the distance. To the southeast the still higher peaks of the Mountains of Moria reach far up into the skies, their heads shrouded in great, grey, billowing clouds. Imposing cliffs loom above to the south and west, an impenetrable barrier to travel. Lesser slopes, that are strewn with boulders, but otherwise passable, extend to the north and east.
118738: The bridge spans a deep, rocky ravine. Built long ago by an unknown hand, it is now so time-worn as to be dilapidated. Flat and without any form of hand rails, the bridge spans the chasm as the wind screams across it. The stonework has been sanded smooth by the incessant, torturing wind.
118739: The mountain slope descends toward a high cliff to the north, whilst a taller peak looms above to the west. To the south, the mountainside is interrupted by a chasm. There is little protection here from the biting wind that blows through the mountains from the east, and the stones around are worn smooth and featureless from the strong wind.
118740: The mountain slope is speckled with boulders, but for the most part the ground here is fairly even. The cliff to the north offers a view of the lands far below, though from this height nothing can be discerned in detail. East and west, this slope reaches along the spur, with a tall, towering mountain standing above the rest and barring passage to the south. Many large boulders lie upon the ground here, split open by the cruel weather, or shattered as they have fallen from the higher slopes.
118741:
A mountain ibex is jumping from rock to rock.
A mountain ibex is jumping from rock to rock.
A mountain ibex is jumping from rock to rock.

A channel originating to the southeast runs on down the mountain to the north. Perhaps it was once the course of a stream, but it has long since run dry. Tall peaks loom above to the east and south, their snowy heads reaching far up into the clouds. The land slopes upward at a more modest grade to the west, along the flanks of this mountain spur.
118742: No water flows now, but it appears that at some time in the past a stream ran here, carving this channel out of the living rock. Though the cliffs to the south appear to offer no viable route between the plains and the mountain slopes, this ancient water course cuts back into them, twisting and curving its way between the valley and the heights above. The rock is fairly smooth, but it should be possible to travel this way, albeit only with considerable effort.
118743: Lush Valley by the Foot of a Cliff
A sparrow is flapping around on the ground.

A lush valley stretches to the north and west, its floor an ocean of tall, dark green grasses that wave gently in the wind. Protected to the north by a range of hills, and to the south by the rising mountains, this vale enjoys much milder weather conditions than most of the nearby lands. A few scattered broadleaf trees, and numerous low bushes thrive here, especially nearing the feet of the cliffs to the south and east, where a dense hedge of thorny shrubs has come to dominate the landscape.
118744: Lush Valley by the Foot of a Cliff

A large beautiful rose bush is blooming here.
Deep inside the bush, there are two red roses with leaves and thorny stems.

A lush valley extends out in all directions save to the south, where it runs right to the foot of a massive cliff. The mountain spur is only a low footnote to the Misty Mountains that lie further east, but the cliffs nonetheless afford this vale a good deal of protection from the harsh weather that blights much of the rest of the land hereabouts. As a result, the topsoil is thicker and richer here, supporting not only a thick sea of dark green grass, but also scattered broadleaf trees, and any number of low shrubs. A dense hedge of thorny bushes dominates the land at the very foot of the cliffs.
118745:
You see two handfuls of clover on the ground.
A colourful butterfly is fluttering around here.

Extending for several miles to the north, east and west, this lush valley comes to an abrupt halt here, its grassy floor marching right to the feet of a long mountain spur. The cliffs loom high above, but the vegetation still thrives here, despite the diminished access to sunlight. A pool of clear water has collected here surrounded by flourishing greenery.
118746: Lush Valley by the Foot of a Cliff

The green valley continues to the east, marching along the foot of a towering mountain range. The landscape is a sea of lush, green grass, growing in places as tall as a man. The soil is deep, rich and loamy. With the hills that stand to the north, and the mountain spur to the south, this land is well protected, and in addition to the grasses, a number of scattered trees and many shrubs also flourish here.
118750: Riding is out of the question here. No discernible pathway can be seen along these rocky slopes, so the only option is to pick a way between the rocks and boulders, seeking out the most level ground as best is possible. Mighty peaks loom high above, their crests hidden from sight amid the billowing clouds.
118751: A hungry warg stands here, sniffing around for flesh.

A low mountain range cuts through the area. The air that rolls down from those heights is frigid, and chilling to the bone. And the elements have taken their toll on the landscape itself, with no noticeable vegetation growing here at all. Rocks and boulders are all that occupies these lonely slopes.
118752: A grey-skinned mountain troll stands here.

A narrow entrance leads down into a cave deep in the mountains. Moisture and darkness grip the rocky walls. The filthy floor is somehow sticky to the touch and reek of rot and decay fills the air. Large foot prints in the dirt suggest that this is a Trollhome alongside the remnants of previous meals.
118753:
A grey-skinned mountain troll stands here.
A grey-skinned mountain troll stands here.

Something has left giant claw marks across the walls and ceiling of this cave as it descends, clearly the result of some animal-like excavation. The rocky burrow continues further down where the stench gets more foul. A filthy and perilous crack leads out to the west, following a slight breeze.
118754:
A filthy straw pallet is lying here.
A grey-skinned mountain troll stands here.

Bones and filth covers the ground of this smelly cave that has been excavated out of the mountain. Giant claw marks can be seen running along the sides of the walls of the cavern, seemingly in an attempt to expand it. The air is absolutely foul here and its source seems to be some bedding in the corner.
118755: A black spider crawls here, a shiny red spot visible on its belly.

A dark crack leads down into a web-draped grotto. A slight draft can be felt, hinting that the outdoors are somewhere nearby to the north. Webs have been heavily spun across the grotto, rarely hampering movement, but giving a spooky ambience as they billow in the draft of the cave.
118756: Yellow flowers, with grey-green foliage, grow in clusters here.

The valley is covered with lush, green grasses and bushes. From here, the green hills to the north and purple mountains to the south seem far away, yet they both loom over the valley. The soil seems fertile and would make good farmland if it were settled.
118757:
A long trunk lies on the ground, rotting away.
A low and wide-spread tree grows here.
On the tree's branches, there are three juicy plums.
A large rabbit looks peacefully at you, ready to dart away.
A colourful butterfly is fluttering around here.
A large rabbit looks peacefully at you, ready to dart away.

The valley extends for some miles both to the east and west, and reaches to the foot of the mountains in the south. The deep, loamy soil evidently has an ample supply of water, for lush, green grass covers the ground all around. A few scattered trees and many bushes also dot the landscape. This secluded valley would make excellent farmland if anyone were to settle here. But as it lies so very far from civilisation this would seem an unlikely prospect.
118758: A large rabbit looks peacefully at you, ready to dart away.

A few groves of tall trees dot the landscape, utilizing the excellent ground and ample moisture. The tall grass may hide wildlife, and there are trails worn in the grass that indicate larger animals make their way around here. The hills to the north can be reached from here following a sharp ascent and the mountains to the south rise up some distance away.
118759:
A sparrow is flapping around on the ground.
A fallow deer is grazing peacefully here.

The valley is covered by tall grass here with some scattered green, broadleaf trees growing here and there. Nestling in the shelter of a range of hills that lies to the north, and a mountain spur to the south, these lands are quite well protected from the fiercest weather, with the result that vegetation flourishes throughout the vale.
118760: The valley lies to the west, sheltered by mountains to the south and hills to the north and east. Long blades of dark green grass dance in the gentle wind, creating waves that ripple across the vale. To the south, a tall cliff face marks the starting point of a mountain spur, an offshoot of the Misty Mountains that dominate the horizon far to the east.
118761: Scattered trees dot the landscape among these rolling hills, growing denser to the east, where they climb up the slopes of more hills. To the west and northwest, the hills continue, their grassy slopes receding far into the distance. As the slopes march down into the valley below, to the south, the grass becomes much longer, and the vegetation lusher.
118762:
A bright green holly bush is growing here.
A large hawk-like bird is here overlooking its territory.

These plains are slightly raised, with some of the run-off from the nearby hill and mountain ranges supplying much needed moisture. The vegetation is green and broad-leaf bushes grow in abundance here. The bushes are hardy, being themselves the only natural windbreak in a land where the prevailing winds are cruel.
118763:
A bright green holly bush is growing here.
Partly covered by the bush's green leaves, there are some hollyberries.

The rolling hills continue to the east, north and west of here, their grassy slopes stretching off into the distance. Grass grows in abundance in and among the many large boulders that have come to rest here. Down a gentle slope to the south a lush valley opens up, covered by tall green grass. And further in the distance, across the valley, a rocky spur of the Misty Mountains can be seen towering above everything.
118764: In the south the many peaks of the Misty Mountains are visible. Their tall peaks reaching to the clouds. A lush green valley lies before the mountains and these rolling hills mark the northern boundary of that lush land. Tumbling down toward the vale, the slope gradually becomes grassier, and the vegetation much greener.
118765:
A tree with bright green leaves grows here.
A goblin corpse hangs from a treelimb.

The hills empty into a lush valley to the south and west. A few scattered trees grow here on the descending slopes of the hills, but not in any abundance. Far across the valley, a tall mountainous spur cuts the land from east to west, and it is this, together with the hills, that have created the rich vale that opens out not far to the south.
118766: Bordered to the west by steep slopes, covered in thick, thorny brush, a lush valley opens out all around. It tumbles down from the hillside to the north, terminating only some miles at the feet of a mountain spur. Thick, dark green grass carpets the entire area, with a few scattered trees and a number of healthy shrubs also to be seen.
118767: The west slope of this valley ends with a combination of large boulders and thick thorny brush, blocking further travel in that direction. Stretching out to the east, and widening in the south, the vale is full of lush, green grass that grows in many places as tall as a man. A few trees and bushes stand off in the distance.
118768: A dense carpet of blue flowers dip their heads in the breeze.

From the west a steep, bushy slope quickly descends. The overgrown, thorny thicket that covers its flanks seems to extend for miles both to the north and to the south. Extending eastward is a lush vale where grasses of all types grow in great abundance. Tucked away between a range of hills to the north and a tall mountain spur to the south, this valley is provided with ample protection from the elements, making it richer in vegetation than any area for many miles.
118769: A large rabbit looks peacefully at you, ready to dart away.

The hills taper off to the east and south, revealing a wide valley between them and the mountainous spur that lies further to the south. The hills run parallel to this valley for a long distance east from here, their slopes covered with medium-length, lush, green grass that merges smoothly with the taller grasses of the vale below. The faintest scar of a road can be seen cutting across the land, several miles to the west, but access to that region is blocked from here by an extensive area of extremely thick brush.
118770: A black catfish is here, lurking in the mud.

Curling with the contours of the lands that lie to the southeast, a stream flows here from the distant mountains, bringing its cold, clear water to the plains. The banks to either side are alive with lush green grass and a proliferation of low bushes. Further off to the west and south, a range of hills can be seen on the horizon.
118771:
A large hawk-like bird is here overlooking its territory.
A large sturgeon swims slowly along the bottom.

Lush, green grass can be seen growing along either bank of the stream, whose waters flow from south to west here. The stream bed is rather more rocky here than either upstream or downstream, and so the waters run much more rapidly, dancing and bouncing off the rocks as they go. The water is very cold and crystal clear, fed from run-offs from the mountain range to the east.
118772: A black catfish is here, lurking in the mud.

The waters of a cold, clear stream cut across the plains, flowing here from east to north. The channel is rather wide at this point, and the water flows by so lazily that it almost appears not to move at all. The southern bank can be reached by means of some quick-footed action over some slippery looking boulders.
118773: A large hawk-like bird is here overlooking its territory.

The plains here are a collection of tall green grasses. It is obvious that the stream feeds into here, as the ground has a slightly marshy feel to it. Water collects in footprints left here. A stream flows past this field to the east and north. To the south the ground becomes harder as it meets the slope of a hill. To the west the plains continue until they meet hills.
118774: These hills descend rapidly to the north and east, while they rise steadily to the south and west. The land here is a sea of soft, green grass that stretches all the way down the hillside to meet what appear to be lush plains that lie to the north.
118775:
A brown bear is sleeping here.
A brown bear is sleeping here.
A brown bear is sleeping here.

A narrow tunnel, extending about fifteen feet from an opening in the ground, leads onto an enlarged burrow. Dug into the red-brown soil, the walls, floor and ceiling are earthen, and are reinforced naturally by a proliferation of tangled roots. Though this is obviously a den of some sort, there is no sign of bones, fur, or any kind of animal activity.
118776: A small field can be seen over a slight rise here, while the landscape descends to the north. The slopes continue to roll further in the other directions. This hillside is covered with a scattering of small trees and low brush, that are just enough to offer scant protection against the winds and rain, but not sufficient to afford any real shelter from the elements.
118777:
The mauled corpse of a wild boar is lying here.
A partridge attempts to hide in the undergrowth.

A few solitary pines stand amidst the medium sized grasses that cover the hillsides here. The hills continue in all directions, rolling off well into the distance. To the south and east, far beyond the hills, tall mountains rise into the sky.
118778: Tall, slender evergreens grow in abundance here, yet never drawing so close to one-another as to constitute a true forest. The ground alternates between a deep litter of old pine needles close by the trees, and thick, green grasses that bend in the wind howling between the trunks. An occasional stump stands amid the grasses, covered with moss, and attesting to the age of this grove. The hills continue far to the south while slowly descending in the west. To the north and east the descent is more marked, as the hills give way to the plains that stretch out below.
118779: The lands here are parched, despite their location between a lush stretch of fields lying near a waterway to the north and east, and a band of grassy hills crossing the land from southeast to northwest, which passes by not more than a couple of miles from here. In this area, only a few low, tussocks of dull, dry, yellow-brown grasses have managed to survive.
118780: The hills are covered with grasses, with the occasional fir or pine standing alone on the slopes. The high ground continues to the east and west, before descending to meet the plains below. To the north, the descent is sharp, but in other directions the hills tail lazily off towards the lower lands. Far to the south and to the east, mountain ranges stretch across the horizon.
118782:
A very large lion with a dark mane watches you lazily.
A powerful lioness is barely visible in the grass.
A powerful lioness is barely visible in the grass.

The hills offer a view of the plains to the south and west of here. Partially hidden by thick brush, further to the west a road that has seen better days runs north and south. Covered with grasses and not as dry as the plains below, more hills roll to the north and east and quickly become covered with scattered trees. A mountain range to the south looms over the dry prairies.
118783:
Some pine nuts lie scattered upon the ground.
A very large lion with a dark mane watches you lazily.
A powerful lioness is barely visible in the grass.
A powerful lioness is barely visible in the grass.

A few scattered pine trees grow upon the rising slope of the hills. They offer only the most sparse of shade, or shelter from the prevailing winds. Between and around the trees are many old stumps, which show distinct signs of rotting. The hills continue to the south and west, with grasslands stretching out to the east. To the north the ground seems to become less solid underfoot.
118784: Soft, green grass carpets the hills, and thick bushes grow all about, offering a wind break even at the very crests of the hills. An occasional boulder rests amid the vegetation. These have obviously been here for quite some time, as their northern faces have collected a thick coating of moss and lichen.
118785: A deep cave navigates its way into the mountain before ending in a cave-in. A strong musky smell permeates the area, as if some huge beast has marked its territory over the years. A large boulder juts out in the centre of the lair, providing cover for a massive hollow that is lined with bones and fur.
118786: Rolling playfully, the hills dance around this area and connect with the green hills that rise to the south. Here the land is characterised mostly by rock, with but a thin covering of moss and other greenery growing in the cracks, while a small creek can be heard gurgling to the north.
118787:
A grey wolf is here, salivating profusely.
A salmon swims here.

The stream makes a slow arc from the east and turns to head in a northerly direction. The current is mild and the flow of the water smooth as it makes its journey from the eastern mountains and on through the green plains. But though the waters are leisurely, they have still undercut the western bank somewhat, making it impossible to scale, despite its low height. Tall clusters of reeds and grass thrive on the never-ending source of fresh water and a few fish can be glimpsed darting below the surface of the stream.
118788: A black catfish is here, lurking in the mud.

This narrow stream weaves and snakes through the fertile fields and plains. The strength of the current is not powerful enough to cut a new path through the countryside but instead the stream turns to follow the lay of the land when necessary. A wide expanse of flat, green fields can be seen to the east.
118789: Following a wide curve, the slow-moving waters change direction towards the north where the stream meets up with a second tributary. The muddy banks of the water are steep and slick here, making them quite impossible to scale. A road follows the stream to the west and grass-covered plains lie to the south.
118790: Foliage snakes its way through down from hills to the west and explodes into full bloom in this marshy riverbank. Surrounded by the hills to the west and south and a brook to the north, the greenery here peacefully grows in the shallows, oblivious to the hardships of the world.
118791: A large brown snake with black patches is coiled here.

The plains are dry here, despite a stream that cuts across the land to the north. The thin topsoil that rests atop a rocky substrate is able to retain so little moisture that many large cracks have appeared all around. Small patches of brown grass barely hold onto life in this arid area, growing with difficulty between the cracks. Further away in all directions the land becomes more fertile.
118792: You see two tall, grey-green plants on the ground.

The grass is thick and slick underfoot but caked in mud. Water squelches out of the ground at each step. To the south and west green hills can be reached, rising at first with a barely perceptible ascent from the plains. A small stream can be seen at some distance to the northeast.
118793: A green frog is here, hopping around.

The soil here is more mud than anything else, and the grasses are slick with dew. From the north and east comes the distinct sound of a babbling brook. Far to the south the plains start to rise gently towards a range of green hills that climbs from the horizon.
118794: A large sturgeon swims slowly along the bottom.

The water of this stream runs clear and very cold, having originated high on the mountains. It is not too deep, and its stone bed can clearly be seen, its shape dancing with the refraction of the water. Both banks are covered with thick, green grass interrupted only occasionally by an isolated large rock. Small minnow schools can be seen flitting about.
118795: This part of the stream at first glance appears quite deep, but upon closer inspection the bottom silt can be made out quite clearly. The banks can be seen in the distance. The water is very cold and clear as it runs by swiftly. The occasional school of minnows flits by and larger darker shapes can be discerned which can only be larger fish. Plains can be seen to the east and west, and beyond them hills which eventually join a large mountain range to the south.
118796: The grasses turn a boggy carpet to the north and east where they draw closer to a stream, and diminish in health to the south. The landscape is remarkably flat in this region, though some miles to the south a range of hills rises up from the plains. To the east, the Misty Mountains dominate the horizon.
118797: The water is crystal clear here with several large boulders providing some deep, and almost still pools near to either bank. Flowing from the south, the waters turn westward here, but the current is too languid to undercut the bank too much. Far to the south, beyond the dry plains, hills join a rocky mountain range.
118798: The stream continues to flow slowly here, turning now from its northerly course to travel due west. The ripple of water against the few large stones does not make much sound and the surface of the stream remains, for the most part, as smooth as glass. A few small fish can briefly be spied, darting about below the surface of the water. Upstream, to the south, the water widens noticeably, but at the same time becomes more shallow. Vast fields roll on beyond the steep river banks, seemingly forever, to both the north and the east.
118799: A field mouse noses about hungrily, searching for food.

Green fields of knee-high grass spread out all around as far as the eye can see. A gentle stream that flows by to the south and west is the only visible feature anywhere at all close by in this flat country. There are little or no sounds, or visible evidence of wildlife. Rising up, far in the southeast, the faint, yet distinct shape of a mighty mountain range reaches towards the sky.
118800:
A shrub with maple-like leaves is growing here.
On the shrub, there are two handfuls of blackcurrant berries.
A small boar with big yellow tusks looks eager to fight.
A boar cub is playing here, and exploring the wide world.
A fierce boar is here, making grunting noises.

These green hills descend quickly to the north and south, making passage not viable in those directions. The stream to the south provides enough moisture to sustain the healthy mixture of tall grass and wild grains that flourishes across this meadowland. The brown heads of wild grains nod gently with each breath of wind, and small animals are barely glimpsed as they use the thick vegetation as cover from their predators.
