118801: The grasses and small brush merge together making this area very green. There is a slight elevation to the land which gives the appearance of several small hills. These gently rolling lands stop abruptly to the east at a crevice, and to the west some green hills loom in the distance. A taller variety of grass becomes dominant to the south, perhaps fed by the nearby stream.
118802: The ground cover in these fields is thick and green and the tall stalks of grass wave gently with the occasional breezes that gust across the lands. The thick vegetation and close proximity of fresh, running water must make this an ideal environment for all manner of small game. In the distance the outline of the Misty Mountains looms high on the horizon.
118803: Blanketed by an abundance of short grass that covers every inch of ground, and bordered to the south by a small stream, these hills would make an excellent grazing area for wild animals. The lack of tall vegetation or trees provides a clear view of the surrounding fields and plains that roll out to the east, west, and north.
118804:
On the ground, there are two handfuls of clover.
A shrub with maple-like leaves is growing here.
On the shrub, there are two handfuls of blackcurrant berries.

A healthy mix of grass and wildflowers blankets the hills. Clover, in particular, grows especially well, flourishing in the rich, fertile soil and filling the air with its heavy scent. The hills continue to the east, and to the north, lie some fertile fields in the lower ground. A stream flows through the fields in the south, but the steep bank does not allow a safe descend.
118805: A golden crop of wild wheat thrives in the rich soil, the brown heads of grain waving gently back and forth at the slightest breath of air. There are many suitable holes and hiding places for small animals in the tall stalks of grain to run. The fertile fields continue to the west and a small stream runs directly north of the fields. The bank is too steep, with rocky shore to descend safely.
118806:
A tall and majestic oak tree grows here, surveying the lands about it.
On the tree, there is a perfect oak branch.

Provided with sufficient moisture by the streams that border these lush fields, the vegetation grows thick and plentiful in the dark, rich soil. Tall grass and weeds flourish together in abundance, supplying excellent cover for the various small plains animals that make their home in this area. The green fields roll on to the east.
118807: Tough grasses grow low to the ground among these gently rolling plains that stretch out into the distance in all directions. To the west, however, the vegetation starts to change in character, as these wild grasses start to give way to patches of a more cultivated cereal that suggest that at one time those lands were perhaps cultivated.
118808: Tall, green grasses stand close together as these hills are fed by a nearby stream. The stalks are tall enough to provide cover to small game. Wind that flows through here can be heard as the grass rustles in response to it. The fields stretch to the south, and hills to the east, but they dry out considerably. A stream winds its way around the field to the north and west.
118809: A small boar with big yellow tusks looks eager to fight.

On the hills, bushes and small, dry-looking trees spring up between dry grasses here. There are small hills of sandy looking soil that are mounded up as well, giving the area a very dry appearance. To the east, the hills continue while there is fresh looking grass to the west.
118810: A small boar with big yellow tusks looks eager to fight.

The hills here grow some bushes and small trees that become increasingly greener the further east it extends. From a marshy area to the east a smell of stale water emerges. There are grasslands to the south, and to the north a small stream can be seen. The hills continue off to the west.
118811: The fields continue here with short, green grasses. The grass grows low to the ground and can hide only small animals. The wind blows through the grass and a rippling among the field can be seen as well as heard. The fields continue on to the east. In the south, an impassable thicket of brushes block the way.
118812: A boar cub is playing here, and exploring the wide world.

In the middle of a wide fields, there is a sharp crevice with steep walls to other directions than to the south. The soil is dry and mostly gravely, but there are some grasses and raspberries and other weed growing here and there. The ground ascends to the south, where are green fields with more suitable conditions for grain and other plants to survive.
118813:
A small boar with big yellow tusks looks eager to fight.
A boar cub is playing here, and exploring the wide world.

The ground here is quite alive with grasses and occasional trees. Some rocky ground is apparent to the north, and to the south the plant growth is noticeably higher than here, probably maintained by a stream that flows idly in the distance. To the west, the ground rises sharply at some grassy hills.
118814:
A bright green holly bush is growing here.
Partly covered by the bush's green leaves, there are two piles of hollyberries.
A mottled snake is sneaking here, ready to sink its fangs into flesh.
A mottled snake is sneaking here, ready to sink its fangs into flesh.

The stream that flows by to the west has lent its life-giving waters to this part of the plains, making the lands lush and green. Large, broad-leaf bushes compete with a sea of tall grass to define the landscape here. Far to the south a range of hills cuts across the horizon, while to the east the Misty Mountains dominate the vista.
118815: A fallow deer is grazing peacefully here.

The ground is uneven here, filled with stones and boulders. The soil seems quite fertile in the area, and there grows some grass and bushes here. Some of the taller plants and small trees look trampled, cut, or torn, perhaps by some animals. The fields continue to every direction.
118816:
A roe deer is standing here, watching the terrain while chewing the vegetation.
A wild bull seems ready to charge you.

The fields here are not on level ground. The grasses that cover this area are smaller in variety and completely cover the grounds. To the south there is a sound of water faintly trickling as the fields meet a creek. There is a crevice on the ground to the west, which prevent travelling in that direction. A field of taller grass lies to the north.
118817:
A wild bull seems ready to charge you.
A fallow deer is grazing peacefully here.
A fallow deer is grazing peacefully here.
A buck runs swiftly from place to place, looking about warily as it grazes.

The land is covered by short grasses which ripple when the wind blows through it. There are grassy fields to the west from here and the large bank of a stream can be seen to the north. The sound of water running along a stream can be heard in the distance.
118818:
A field mouse noses about hungrily, searching for food.
A fallow deer is grazing peacefully here.
A fallow deer is grazing peacefully here.
A fallow deer is grazing peacefully here.

The fields here are lush and green, fed by nearby streams. The moisture in the soil continues to the north where a smell of stale water pervades. Deep and muddy marsh ponds block the way to enter the marshes. To the east and west the grassy fields continue. There are some rolling small hills to the south.
118819:
A fierce-looking eel lurks in the darkness.
A fat carp swims here.
A trout swims here.

Small fish dart beneath the surface of the clear water of this stream, flashing silver as their thin bodies catch and reflect any available light. The bed of the stream is covered with small pebbles, made smooth by the continuous flow of water, and by a few larger rocks that provide a hiding place for the occasional crayfish.
118820: Travelling from east to west, the gentle stream flows on through the fields and plains. The banks of the stream are cut high and sharp, suggesting that the water level rises substantially during the more rainy seasons. The land to the south looks wet and swampy. Far to the south, the hazy purple outline of the Misty Mountains looms above the horizon.
118821: A water moccasin slithers out of sight just below the surface of the water.

With a loud splash of rushing water, the streams from the north and the south meet here to form one body of water which flows on to the west. Although the current is quick and the expanse of the water is wide, the stream is actually deceptively shallow. Grass covered plains stretch out to the east but the river bank is too steep to allow access in that direction.
118822: Arising to the east as two smaller streams, this minor tributary to the Bruinen is nevertheless wide at this point, as it runs fast and shallow through the plains. Full of dirt and silt picked up from its travels in the countryside, the muddy body of water continues toward its western destination. A little way to the west a ford is visible, spanning the distance between two parts of an old and decaying roadway that travels north and south.
118824:
A brook trout is here, swimming in the current.
A fat carp swims here.

The meandering stream shifts from its western course and begins gradually to turn south, heading towards what appears to be a merging point with another, smaller tributary. Dirt and silt collected by the stream during its journey through the plains have muddied the waters making it impossible to see the stream bed. The banks of the stream to the north and west are extremely low and it is likely that the surrounding land would be flooded during the rainy season, to spill waters over the road.
118825:
A brook trout is here, swimming in the current.
A crayfish is here, snapping its claws at you.

The shallow stream trips and falls over rocks and stones as it continues on its twisted course in the plains. Various water plants stretch their thirsty roots deep into the stream, and tall reeds flourish along the banks of the water, nodding and swaying gently with each soft gust of wind that sweeps out from over the plains. A large, green meadow lies directly to the north.
118826: Twisting lazily from the north and turning to the west, the stream meanders on its way through the land. The banks of the water are high, making the fields and hills to the east and south easily accessible. Hidden within the reeds bordering the very edge of the water are small nests that look as though they were built by waterfowl. The marshy ground appears to be a prime breeding ground for small insects.
118827: The elevated bank to the west forces the stream to change direction and turn from the east to the south. The water is thick with silt and topsoil from the plains, turning the once clear water a muddy brown, and the current sluggish. The bank to the north is too steep to ascend, but it's possible to go on with the stream to the south as it flows on its way toward the distant Bruinen, or to the east towards the mountains.
118828: The stream runs swiftly and quietly at this point, heading west through the prairie lands and eventually leading to the Bruinen itself. There is a distant roar to the east that suggests the water becomes turbulent in that direction but in this area the surface of the water remains unbroken by rocks or other obstructions. The current moves too quickly to sustain any permanent plant life other than to feed the roots of the odd tree which has managed to take hold on the banks of the stream. A steep basin can be seen to the north and on the south side of the river a hilly bank is apparent.
118829: The current of this small stream begins to quicken as it cascades over a series of low waterfalls on its journey from east to west. The rushing water churns and froths over the falls, sending up tiny clouds of mist at the bottom of each fall. A sudden incline rises to the north, and beyond the hills in the high southern bank nothing else is visible.
118830:
A black catfish is here, lurking in the mud.
A trout swims here.
A red-breasted mallard swims about, periodically upending to look for food.
A brook trout is here, swimming in the current.

There is little in the way of vegetation in this area but the occasional tree can be found having taken hold on the banks of the stream. The roots of the trees have dug down and across, reaching out from the walls of the banks to dip into the fresh running water below. Piles of debris and soil gathered by the flow of the water through the plains have become tightly packed against the tangled mess of the outstretched roots. The water itself has begun to grow muddy and dirty from its contact with the topsoil of the land. As it travels past this near blockage, the water gathers speed, as it heads towards a series of small falls to the west.
118831: The quiet stream makes its way westward through the hills and plains. Meltwater that originated as snow in the distant mountains, the water is still chilly and so clear that the rock-covered bottom of the streambed can be seen perfectly. An expansive grassland stretches out to the south and hills are visible directly to the north.
118832: The bridge above is covering some of the sky here, and occasionally sounds of someone walking there are audible. The stream is clear and chilly here, formed from meltwater that is carried from the distant mountains in the east, to meet with the Bruinen, far to the west. Flatlands border the stream to the south, where the bridge connects to the ground some feet above the stream.
118833:
A canoe has been left here.
A swarm of mosquitoes is here, humming around you.
A small leech is here, floating in the water.

The low bank of the stream to the north appears to flood these lowlands on a frequent basis as the ground is thick with mud, and water is standing in several places. The musty smell of stagnant water hangs heavily in the air and there is a faint hum as tiny insects swarm over the pools.
118834: On the Bank of a River
A small leech is here, floating in the water.

A bridge has been constructed to the north crossing the river in a narrow spot. The ground here is waterlogged, with several sizeable pools of standing water that have become quite stagnant. The air has a musty, unwholesome smell and the environment has become an ideal breeding ground for mosquitoes and other small insects.
118835: The bridge underfoot is composed of logs and bundles of branches lashed together. Dirt has been rubbed into the cracks to form a sort of clay helping insulate against the water. The hides of various animals have been strung together above the bridge. They form a tunnel of some sort. Although stretched as tight as possible, they sag at the midpoint between supporting poles which have been driven into the bridge.
118836: Planks of wood and all manner of other types of foliage have been tightly bound together to create this bridge. A canopy of animal pelts sewn together is stretched overhead supported only by stakes periodically set along the path.
118837: There is a substantial drop-off to the south where the bank of the stream has collapsed, perhaps adding risk to any attempt to travel in that direction. The surrounding lands to the north are low and contain little in the way of vegetation except for an abundance of coarse grass that covers the ground.
118838: Clusters of slender stems and tall leaves thrive in the mud and shallows.

East and west the hills continue, while to the south a wide stream cuts across the countryside. The river side of the hills appear to be flooded with some frequency, the floodwaters arising from the stream. Tall clumps of grass, interspersed with reeds, grow in the muddy earth. To the west the rear of a run-down cottage can be seen.
118839: There is a good view of the lands to the south of here. The river flows joyfully down below the hill, the descent to the river is very steep making the climb not possible. There are some rocks jutting out of the hills, and there grow only some small brushes and a few pine and ash trees.
118841: A robin is here, carrying small pieces of wood to its nest.

This small hill gives a view of the nearby lands. It is covered in boulders and grasses, and could perhaps have been used as a lookout post at some time in the past. There is a small cottage that stands close by the base of this hill, and to the south a small stream tumbles past. A road runs north and south a little way to the west of here.
118842: A huge warg is here, moving in for the kill.

This field is nearly covered by large boulders and gravel. Little of the once fertile grasses that have grown here can be seen now. The dust that is kicked up by the wind scatters the small pebbles that lie here, giving this field a barren appearance. Grasses have sprung up to the east and south, whilst to the west hills, similar in appearance to this field, can be seen. The field of rocks continues north.
118843:
A huge warg is here, moving in for the kill.
A robin is here, carrying small pieces of wood to its nest.

Short, green grasses grow in abundance here on the flat landscape. Some boulders and other rocks have come to rest here, and the grasses and moss have almost overtaken all but a few. The flat grassland continues to the east and south. More rocks, larger than those here, have come to a rest to the north and west.
118844:
The corpse of a ferocious warg is lying here.
The corpse of a ferocious warg is lying here.
A ferocious warg is here, snarling angrily.
A ferocious warg is here, snarling angrily.

The plains are covered with small patches of dried-out, brown grass. Some thickets of thorny bushes lie scattered around in the fields. The ground is hard, leaving any form of agriculture out of the question. An ancient, broken road lies to the north and west, slowly curving through the sloping plains.
118845:
A black raven flies in the sky searching for flesh to prey upon.
A black raven flies in the sky searching for flesh to prey upon.

The hills here are composed mainly of red dirt, broken stone, rough scrub brush and sparse grass. To the north lies an ancient road. Passage west seems to be impossible, adding to the somewhat dismal nature of the landscape. To the east once more lie plains, while to the south are yet more hills.
118846: On these arid plains nothing but the hardiest grass can survive. The bleak land stretches out far to the south and west as a broad shelf, hardly wavering in its depth or height. This same shelf prevents passage south. To the north an ancient road cuts its path east and west across the shelf, bordered on the north by a low ridge.
118847: Small thickets of tangling thorn bush are dotted across the dry brown grass in these billowing fields. The ground is hard and infertile, composed of clay and limestone. A road can be spotted in the north, crossing the wide plains that dominate the landscape. Far to the east the white peaks of a mountain range reach their jagged fingers towards the sky, creating a magnificent backdrop for the rugged looking camp located in the plains to the northeast.
118848: Dry brown grass sprouts out of the red-brown earth which composes the billowing fields rolling down from the southeast. Far apart small thickets of tangled thorn bush give little shelter from the elements or a prying eye. In the north more plains stretch towards the ancient, broken road, and far off on the eastern horizon the peaks of a mountain range reach toward the sky.
118849: A swallow flies high above the ground.

Dry and dusty in the summer months, this field turns to a muddy mess when wet, or a frozen wasteland in the winter. Thin grass and miserable brush rise from the red soil, seeking what opportunity for growth might exit. To the north some sort camp can be seen. The Ancient Broken road continues to the west. All other directions give way to more of the same bleak plains.
118850:
A sturdy bandit bodyguard stands here, eager to hack you to pieces.
A sturdy bandit bodyguard stands here, eager to hack you to pieces.
A swallow flies high above the ground.

A breach in the ancient stone wall that surrounds the camp has been hastily patched and filled in quite recently. Until it is made more secure it is likely that additional guards might be posted in this area. The stench of death fills the air, suggesting that whatever battle that broke the wall happened recently.
118851:
A sturdy bandit bodyguard stands here, eager to hack you to pieces.
A sturdy bandit bodyguard stands here, eager to hack you to pieces.

This path breaking south off the Ancient, Broken Road heads to a settlement of some sort. Further south the trail fades into a plain, and some buildings and tents might be seen suggesting that there may be a more permanent occupation of this area than might be expected.
118852: The grass clad slopes roll downwards in soft, green waves from the hills in the south and west. Between the hills and the mountains in the east, a narrow strip of flat land stretches out, fed in large part by water from a pool that has formed in a small depression just to the north. A couple of short trees and some bushes grow together in a small clump on a slight rise, near to the body of water.
118853: Waves of thick grass cascade over the land enveloping the area in an ocean of green. Small shrubs dot the landscape, while boulders add texture to the scenic but windy view. Some rocky hills can be seen blocking passage to the south.
118854: Except for the tall mountains rising up in the east, this small plateau is the highest spot for many miles. The plateau is clad in short, green grass and spotted by patches of bright flowers. To the west, the ground rolls downwards into the river, albeit at an angle preventing passage in that direction. The plateau becomes narrower to the north, eventually transforming into a ridge, overlooking the stream that bends westward far below.
118855: A statue of a troll mother is here, clutching her infant in a stony embrace.

The land is higher here compared to the muddy lowlands below to the north, east and west. A ridge has formed as a result of the erosion of the water sweeping down from the incline of the Misty Mountains to the east. Rock and stone has been embedded over the years into the ground here, forcing the incoming waters to go around. To the south-east lie the rolling foothills of the Misty Mountains. All around are scattered broken bones and the torn, smashed remains of humanoid and animal corpses.
118856: At the Foot of a Hill

Tall strong grass grows on the flat grassland that spreads out widely, flowing between the stream that cuts the land diagonally, and the mountains towering up in the east. To the north another river runs its westward journey down from the mountains and away through the vast wilderness. The grasslands rise quickly in the east, where hills roll beneath the foot of the mountains.
118857: Two streams meet just west of here, one coming from the northeast and the other from the southeast. Despite this, the land has avoided becoming marsh-like due to it's slight elevation above the water, although it is still somewhat damp. Further inland however, the ground grows somewhat more dry and the grass grows taller. In the east, towards the Misty Mountains, some foothills rise out of the grasslands.
118858:
An ibex is watching you from afar.
An ibex is watching you from afar.
A sharp-eyed hawk is here stalking some prey.

The land starts to rise here as it draws closer to the mountains. The stream that runs to the north is now far below and the loose, sandy hillside that leads down there is far too difficult to climb. Wide fields roll away to the south and another waterway can be seen, running northwest from the Misty Mountains. To the east, more hills rise up, taller and larger than this one.
118859: A goat is here, grazing in the hills.

From the top of this tall hill the view of the surrounding landscape is good. Rolling grasslands spread out far into the south, between the stream that cuts through the land and the natural barricade of the Misty Mountains in the east. In the northeast another stream comes bending down from the mountains, crashing into the southerly one not too far west of here. The ground rises slightly to the north and slopes downwards again in the northwest.
118860:
A large beaver is here, gnawing on a piece of wood.
A goat is here, grazing in the hills.
A sharp-eyed hawk is here stalking some prey.

As a prelude to the towering mountains, these hills stand below the vast slopes in the east, linking them together with the rolling grasslands in the west. The rocky ground does not allow for much growth, and the water trickling down along cracks and crevices continues down towards the fields, not being able to sink into the bedrock. A small stream begins its westward journey far below to the north, twisting and turning through the landscape.
118861: Deep tunnels can be reached by going down a long flight of stairs that have been cut into the unyielding rock. Any sharp or protruding stones from the walls have been removed, and the cavern floor has been cleansed of abnormalities. This cave could almost pass for a hallway with a little decor and lights.
118862: The corpse of a young ill-tempered stone giant is lying here.

This modest cave has been transformed into a basic dwelling, and the cavern system ends here. The occupants must be enormous based on the size of the long, wooden bunks against the back wall. Although the worst of the sharp edges have been removed, the walls are still rough.
118863:
The corpse of a large earth troll is lying here.
The corpse of a large earth troll is lying here.

With the exception of the narrow exit to the north this chamber contains no distinguishable markings. The walls are smooth, with small patches of moss and the distinct stains of water. A soft breeze can be felt through a number of small cracks in the roof.
118864:
The corpse of a large troll is lying here.
A skeleton of some humanoid lies in the dust.
A nasty troll female crouches here, with a feral look in her eyes.
A large troll growls as it stands guard, looking awfully mean.

The cavern ceiling and walls here have been blackened with fire. On these walls, hundreds of skeletons have been hung with ropes and chains. The white skeletons provide a stark contrast against the cavern. The floor is covered in a thick layer of dust and random bones that have fallen from the skeletons.
118865: The tunnel bends sharply here. Rough rocks underfoot cause the ground to be uneven and difficult to navigate in the dark. Faint echoes coming from somewhere seem to curl their way around the corners of the bend, or perhaps they are just imaginary.
118866: A black widow spins a web in the corner of the tunnel.

A thick layer of dust lies mostly undisturbed on the tunnel floor. Though somewhat cramped, there is a little standing room in this tunnel. Some old cobwebs hang down from the ceiling above and stretch over rocks. The molted carapace of a large spider can be seen dangling from the web.
118867: The tunnel here is a tight fit as it bends, but opens up into a small pocket cave allowing anyone to stand comfortably again. It is very dark in here with small insects creeping along underfoot. Some stale air floats in from around the bend of the tunnel from time to time.
118868:
A large troll growls as it stands guard, looking awfully mean.
A mottled snake is sneaking here, ready to sink its fangs into flesh (hidden).

A small terminating tunnel branch can be seen to the side of this larger tunnel, creating a tiny nook. The nook is extremely small and cramped, offering barely enough room for even a hobbit to stretch freely. The air within the darkness of the tunnel is very still, with no noise to be heard.
118869: The small fierce-looking bat is hanging from the ceiling, obviously sleeping.

The main tunnel bends and breaks off into tiny little side passages that lead into their own unreflective walls of darkness. The sound of bats can be heard echoing from the tiny passages alongside faint wafts of stale air. The walls of the tunnel are hard and grey in colour.
118870: A cockroach is scuttling across the floor carrying some debris.

The walls are composed of what appears to be grey stone. The passage continues on, hard grey rock in every direction. The layers of sediment from which the rock had formed show a history of the passage of time. The rocky walls echo even the smallest of sounds.
118871: The darkness inhabits this tunnel like a feral animal in a den. The black stone walls reflect little if any light and the rough, textured, rocky floor aids in that cause. The ceiling of the tunnel is not very high, making the black walls seem closer than they are.
118872: A large troll growls as it stands guard, looking awfully mean.

The stone which makes up the walls here is ancient but extremely solid. The walls smoothly curve up to the pinnacle of the cave, creating a domed ceiling. In contrast to the walls, the floor underfoot is quite rough, with jagged stones and uneven surfaces abounding.
118873: Here an intersection of tunnels offers several paths forward. The walls are quite smooth and composed of a grey stone. On the walls, near the entrance of each tunnel, symbols have been scrawled in black charcoal. They gleam in the darkness.
118874: A large cockroach is crawling up the wall.

The area here behind this crack is quite concealed from the area above from which a draft can be felt. A few insects creep along the ground and up the walls. To the south, the walls of the crack narrow in closely as they lead into a tunnel which prevents anyone from seeing past into the darkness beyond.
118875:
A cockroach is scuttling across the floor carrying some debris.
Some ugly blow-flies are buzzing around here.

Heaps upon heaps of bones litter the cave with only a clear path down the middle. The path seems to be set above the rest of the ground, as if the bones were in a pit of lower rock. Insects crawl over ribs, climb into eye sockets, and scuttle along spines.
118876: A cockroach is scuttling across the floor carrying some debris.

The cavern's rock is of a monotone grey colour. Stones have been cleared along the floor to create an easy path. Dust lies thickly outside the lines but the way forward is very clear. The cavern opens up to a hill towards the west.
118877: The hills give way slightly here opening up into a small cleft. Sheltered from the elements a few green patches of shrubbery have sprouted here, but the ground is still mostly composed of dirt and rock. The sound of the wind blowing through the hills can be heard from time to time.
118878:
A goat is here, grazing in the hills.
A goat is here, grazing in the hills.

The hills rise and fall like waves in an ocean that has been frozen in time. The topsoil being almost entirely dirt, the slopes of the hills are smooth and mostly featureless. A gash runs between two of the hills making for somewhat of a path between them.
118880: A pale stone troll walks around here, looking for a fight.

The tunnel travels through the surrounding rock in a straight manner. The smooth walls seem to be composed of a grey stone that is moist to the touch. Streaks of different coloured sediments can be seen in its layers. The rock is not particularly hard here and crumbles easily.
118881: The ceiling of this tunnel is quite low. There is one very large hole in the wall, as if chunks of the stone have been taken out and moved somewhere else. The ground is covered in mushrooms and moist, crumbly rocks. The tunnel becomes progressively wetter as it heads westward.
118882: A giant fungus smothers the tunnel walls.

The small tunnel bends here abruptly. Stones line the border of the floor, some with long slash marks along them as if they were used for sharpening something. The cracks are stuffed full of soft wet fungus, keeping the air moist. The tunnel gets more dry towards the east but wetter to the south.
118883:
A mushroom-covered basin is here, filled with clear water.
A small mushroom grows nearby.

The sound of dripping water can be heard echoing through the cave. A small pool of rather clear water has formed in a small basin in the rocks. A few mushrooms have grown up the walls and around the small water sink. A musty smell pervades the room.
118884:
A small mushroom grows nearby.
A giant, strange looking green fungus is here, ready to devour you in seconds.
A huge black fungus is here, exuding a foul stench.
A huge black fungus is here, exuding a foul stench.

A heavy stone grate stands half-submerged in a pool of dirty water. Behind the grate not much can be seen, but the bilge water that flows through it is rank and cloudy. Around the edges of the pool, the corpses of small rodent-like animals lie in the murk. Mushrooms grow everywhere on the walls.
118885: A long, grey slab of stone lies along one side of the area. Various insects crawl along the edges, occasionally disappearing underneath it. On the face of the slab, a roughly-drawn face appears to have been etched into the stone and filled in with shavings of a white rock.
118886: The small fierce-looking bat is hanging from the ceiling, obviously sleeping.

The stone walls expand giving birth to a wide, spacious cavern. Though the stone in the walls is of a dark grey colour mixed with speckles of black and red, white stones are strewn across the floor. A cold draft and the sound of water can be heard raining down from a large hole in the ceiling.
118887: Tunnels converge here, forking in different directions. At the centre of the intersection, a pile of stones has been placed with a log from a tree sticking up in the middle. On the log, arrows have been scratched pointing in all directions into the tunnels, making the path through the area no clearer.
118888:
A large bonfire is burning here.
A foul chest stands in the corner, stinking of rotten meat.
A rotten corpse is hanging here.

Several low boulders with flattened tops have been placed around this cave. In the centre of the cavern, a space has been cleared and a fire pit has been dug. Charred and blackened rocks line the edge of the pit and inside the pit, two iron posts have been stuck with a horizontal iron rod spanning across them.
118889: A huge stone troll looms overhead, ready to crush your body.

This massive cavern stretches into the darkness, its walls unable to be seen. The floor is quite smooth and level save for a single crack. The crack, if it can truly be called a crack, yawns open like a horrible mouth in which nothing can be seen except the void.
118890:
A small and well-kept fire lights and warms the room.
The burnt and blackened skeletal remains of a human are here.

The back wall of this cave has several heavy, iron shackles that have been wrapped around boulders. The shackles are bent and warped as if something has writhed and strained against them. A firepit, still warm to the touth, sits in the centre of the room. A primitive iron rod rests next to the firepit with some charred flesh seared onto it.
118891:
A pale stone troll walks around here, looking for a fight.
A pale stone troll walks around here, looking for a fight.
A stone troll mother is here, trying to keep her family safe.

Several tunnels converge in front of a huge arch that is blocked by a stone gate topped with skulls. A moat filled with dusty stones and bones lies in front of the gate. A cold draft can be felt from the eastern tunnel where a huge slab of rock has been placed.
118892:
The corpse of a pale stone troll is lying here.
A pale stone troll walks around here, looking for a fight.
A huge stone troll looms overhead, ready to crush your body.

What appears to be a stone house has been built in the corner of this cave out of a heaping pile of rock. A slab of splintered wood has been pulled across the door frame, and short pillars, somewhat sculpted into crude shapes, lie out front. The centre of the house has a charred fire pit that has been crudely constructed out of a circle of rocks.
118893: The air here is cold and dry and the walls are made of a slick stone. Claw marks have been raked down the sides of the walls as if something has tried to dig around. Skulls and other various bones litter the ground. A low mist hovers over the stone floor before disappearing into a deep pit.
118894:
A filthy straw pallet is lying here.
A battered warg fur has been left here.
A brown fur is here lying on the ground.
A pale stone troll walks around here, looking for a fight.
A pale stone troll walks around here, looking for a fight.
A pale stone troll walks around here, looking for a fight.
A stone troll mother is here, trying to keep her family safe.

A low ceiling covers the cave, the colour of the stone weaving in and out of blues, greys, and blacks. Huge stone slabs have been set side by side on the floor of the cavern, the slabs being a couple of feet high. Old raggedy furs and skins are heaped on each of the slabs, like sheets on hard beds.
118895:
A stone bed lies here next to a slab with carvings.
On the bed, there is a tattered blanket.
A stone troll mother is here, trying to keep her family safe.
An infant troll, baring its teeth, snarls here.
An infant troll, baring its teeth, snarls here.
An infant troll, baring its teeth, snarls here.
A stone troll is here, old and hunched over, grumbling loudly.

Ragged skins have been crudely stitched together forming a stinking awning for this abode. A stone bed lies in the back corner of the hovel with a pile of dirty, torn blankets at its foot. A stone slab has been placed here with several carvings depicting crude scenes on its flat surface.
118896:
A large boulder is here, it must be heavy.
A pale stone troll walks around here, looking for a fight.

The slick stone here bears claw marks that lead westward alongside huge piles of refuse, bones, and rubble. It seems like there was a cave-in to the west of this deep pit that was quickly dug out and enlargened. The rubble-strewn passage has now been cleared allowing easy access. Some foul mist clings to the walls before dispersing as the pit opens to the west into a tunnel.
118897: This very wide tunnel bears the marks of crude tools used to chisel out the passage. The tunnel descends downwards into the dark and rises on its opposite side to the east where it terminates rather abruptly in a rubble-covered cave-in. Some of the rubble has been removed allowing easy passage through.
118898: Movement here is tricky due to the piles of jagged and jumbled sheets of rock that look to have been haphazardly thrown down from above through a craggy opening in the ceiling. Enough rocks have piled up to form a sort of stairway leading up into a foul-smelling darkness.
118899:
An albino salamander is here, perched on some rocks.
An albino salamander is here, perched on some rocks.

This large cavern is dominated by a sizeable waterfall loudly dashing down the north wall. Black liquid courses along water-smoothed rock before vanishing into dark fissures while the spray makes the air cool and wet. A well-trodden pathway leads to a western glow while to the east it vanishes into a deep, darkness.
118900: Phosphorescent lichen clings to the walls and ceiling of this cavern causing a wash of dim glow all over. The hard stone path leading east and west has been scraped clean of any growth as evidenced by large and small clawmarks. A rushing, roaring sound can be heard to the east, and a cooler draft comes from there.
118901: Weak torchlight flickers along the northern and southern walls of this high east-west tunnel. Some large boulders block parts of the tunnel at intervals, casting dark shadows along the way and lending the tunnel a very ominous atmosphere. A very faint roaring noise comes from somewhere to the east.
118902:
A splintered piece of a broken shield is on the ground.
Little parts of a broken weapon are lying on the ground.

This cavern's ceiling is so high it cannot be seen in the darkness. Around the walls are dim torches striving to light this vast space. On the west end, a stairway has been carved into the rock, vanishing upwards. Dominating the southern wall is a massive stone door, carved with foul glyphs. The floor is strewn with old debris and broken weaponry; evidence of battles long ago or perhaps just abandoned junk.
118903: This low, vaulted tunnel snakes its way north and south. The chipped ceilings and walls show signs of crude toolwork. To the north, a heavy stonedoor rests, engraved with foul glyphs and a leering goblin with twisted eyes and lolling tongue. On the west wall, a smaller, dark stonedoor is outlined with skulls of various sizes. The handle looks like bone.
118904: The floor of this cavern is worn smooth and has probably seen much use to reach its current state. The long passage slopes between two openings; the one higher up is shrouded in darkness while the lower one seems lit by the same scattered torches on the walls that sets this cavern in a dim, flickering glow.
118905: A series of sharply sloping caves run from the surface down deeper into the roots of the Misty Mountains. The caves shown signs of being roughly hewn in places, apparently to widen them and ease travel for large bipeds of unknown origin.
118906: Glowing phosphorescent moss covers the cavern walls.

Softly glowing moss clings gingerly to glistening stalagmites along the weaving stone pathway. Above, luminescent lichen tattoos the various stalactites protruding from the damp cavern ceiling. Dripping water echoes throughout the chamber. A glowing path slopes down into darkness.
118907:
A pool with many big pieces of ice floating in it is here.
Glowing phosphorescent moss covers the cavern walls.
A cavebear is sleeping here.

This high vaulted cavern spans hundreds of yards in every direction. Stalagmites and stalactites spring from floor and ceiling, and a quiet, dark pool of still water lies in the centre of the cavern. The walls of this cave are blanketed with brightly glowing green mosses, and beds of the same moss cover the slick, wet ground.
118908: A small, scrawny goblin skulks about.

A dark tunnel with arched ceilings snakes its way to the north and south amongst rubble and debris. Some tiny stalactites can be see hanging from the ceiling on the right side of the tunnel where water is slowly seeping out of the surrounding rocks. The muddy walls of the tunnel show signs of the crude chisels that were used to expand it.
118909: A giant rat patters against you, squeaking maliciously.

This chamber is lined with bulbous rock walls worn smooth by countless years of dripping condensation. Small droplets cling to every available surface. To the east, a crude outline of a door is the only break in the otherwise solid stone. An awful stench wafts in from the south, indicating something vile lies that way.
118910:
The corpse of a massive snow giant is lying here.
The corpse of a massive snow giant is lying here.
A massive snow giant is standing here, chained to a wall.
A massive snow giant is standing here, chained to a wall.

The slick walls of this chamber are marred only by the massive iron rings set into the rock. Each is as wide as a horse, and likely almost as heavy. Their only use seems to be as an anchor to chain up some immense beasts. The iron is covered in thick scratches, apparently the result of the prisoners attempts to gnaw their way free.
118911: A pile of every sort of horror covers this corner of the cavern. Rotten food, old shoes, and every other sort of refuse are cemented together by noxious paste of excrement. An occasion foot or finger can be seen mixed in with the rest the filth. The air is thick with a ghastly stench that threatens to turn even the strongest of stomachs.
118912:
A huge black fungus is here, exuding a foul stench.
A huge black fungus is here, exuding a foul stench.
A huge black fungus is here, exuding a foul stench.

The floor of the cavern gradually descends into a watery pit in the southwest corner. The water covering that corner is black as pitch, covered in bubbles as large as a man's head. It is entirely opaque, providing ample covering for whatever vile creature might be lurking below.
118913: The eastern side of this low-roofed tunnel is covered in stalactites and stalagmites that were formed by water slowly seeping out of the surrounding rock. Natural mineral pigments, ranging in colour from ochre to yellow, can be seen on the tunnel's walls as it snakes its way to the north and south.
118914: A strong, heavy-set goblin glares blankly ahead.

An old mine was operating here, as evidenced by a large pile of rubble and some heavy pine timbers that have been set into the tunnel as braces. This low vaulted tunnel can be seen snaking its way north and south. The old mine leads upwards into a dark cavern accompanied by a slight draft.
118915: A small, scrawny goblin skulks about.

Ensconced torches line the walls of this cavern, casting dancing shadows along the ceiling. The wide floor slopes downward toward a tunnel from which the continuous rushing sound of water emanates. Tunnels lead to the north and west into darkness.
118916:
A rigorous goblin patrol-leader is here, looking for enemies.
A strong, heavy-set goblin glares blankly ahead.
A strong, heavy-set goblin glares blankly ahead.
A goblin grunt is here, searching the area for enemies.
A goblin grunt is here, searching the area for enemies.
A small, scrawny goblin skulks about.

A crudely made stairwell ascends at the western end of the tunnel accompanied by a foul draft. The tunnel has otherwise been shaped by crude tools into a corridor that would allow two men to pass side by side. The eastern end of the tunnel expands out into a cavern.
118917: A small black vicious rat squeaks at you for disturbing it.

The air smells thickly of soil in this smooth, round tunnel. The walls are cut sharp, but still made of natural strata, giving them a dubious sturdiness. The floor has been flattened to allow travel for two and crunches underfoot with fresh, sharply cut gravel. Half-way through, the tunnel makes a bend.
118918: A small black vicious rat squeaks at you for disturbing it.

Roughly hewn walls of stone line this deep, round tunnel. The dull grey, damp stone is scored with harsh slashing marks indicating the strength of the hewer and the hardness of the tool. The tunnel is straight and the floor of the tunnel is flat, giving proof of the workmanship.
118919: Deep underground this tunnel winds its way through the heart of the earth. No life is here, only clay besotten mire interworked with layers of hard packed gravel. The tunnel is truly that, rounded and cut straight through; obviously not a natural formation.
118920: Walls of rock and dirt form a deep tunnel underground, the sides hewn by hasty but experienced miners. A dark band of thick gravel cuts diagonally through the rest, smelling bitter and oily to the touch. The air is thick with cold, wet air and dampens any sound.
118921: A small black vicious rat squeaks at you for disturbing it.

Dampness hangs in the air of this chilly, round tunnel. The walls are dirt and rocks and although not completely smooth, the tunnel itself is true. The floor of the tunnel is composed of grey and black crushed rocks, and is rather fresh.
118922: A round tunnel burrows through the rock and earth, leading eastwards so straightly that it would make a fletcher proud. At its western end, the tunnel ends in a short slope leading upwards into darkness. Most of the rock is dark grey granite, with faint veins of worthless quartz glittering in places.
118923:
A giant, mean looking earth beetle is standing here.
A large earth troll is digging here, looking for some tasty morsels.
A small, mean earth troll is standing here, thinking of something hideous.
A large earth troll is digging here, looking for some tasty morsels.
A small, mean earth troll is standing here, thinking of something hideous.
A small black vicious rat squeaks at you for disturbing it.
A small, mean earth troll is standing here, thinking of something hideous.

Long wisps of hair-filled goo hang from the roof, swinging in frequency with any disturbance in the air. Some strands hang low enough to touch the ground, creating a gooey trap for any insects that venture into its path. This inlet continues to the west, and the ground grows red and black to the north, as gravel intermixes with clay.
118924:
A huge black fungus is here, exuding a foul stench.
A small, mean earth troll is standing here, thinking of something hideous.
A small, mean earth troll is standing here, thinking of something hideous.
A large earth troll is digging here, looking for some tasty morsels.
A snake slithers towards you.
A small, mean earth troll is standing here, thinking of something hideous.
A large earth troll is digging here, looking for some tasty morsels.
A large earth troll is digging here, looking for some tasty morsels.

Short, mucous-laden stalactites hang across the roof, slowly dripping their contents onto the sticky floor below. The skeletal remains of rats, lizards and insects lay imbedded in the thick goo, creating a jagged collection of white and green. This gummy cavern extends to the east, and south, while to the north, the ground becomes rocky.
118925:
A huge black fungus is here, exuding a foul stench.
An ancient fungus smothers the boulders.
An ancient fungus smothers the boulders.
Massive roots shift uneasily all around you.
A small, dense tangle of roots covers the ground.
A snake slithers towards you.
A large earth troll is digging here, looking for some tasty morsels.
A large earth troll is digging here, looking for some tasty morsels.
A large earth troll is digging here, looking for some tasty morsels.

Several small depressions in the rocky ground have collected the mucous surrounding them, creating green pools of slime, and death traps for any animals that venture into them. Several small bodies lay in the stagnant pools, creating a furry texture to the otherwise bland, green liquid. The slime-filled cave continues to the north.
118926: The sides of this sinkhole are naturally jagged, and protruding rocks provide easy footholds for travellers. Red and green mosses form a carpeted surface for many of the steps, and the undersides of some host a variety of mushrooms and insects. A warm, damp breeze can be felt occasionally from above, and the squeaking of rats, and chittering of insects, echoes throughout the hole.
118927: Below, a large, smooth sinkhole drops into the deep recesses of the earth. The rocky ceiling above is shaped like a dome, and at its apex, a few long stalactites grow from eons of accumulated moisture and sediment. The rocky cave extends westard, into the dark interior of the mountain.
118928: The slick rocky floor is framed to the north and west by smooth walls of granite and quartz. On the walls, small clumps of white mushrooms sprout in several cramped nooks, and large patches of green moss have taken root in some damp soil. The floor here is very smooth, and almost featureless, as if carved out by eons of natural waterflow.
118929: A small black vicious rat squeaks at you for disturbing it.

This cramped space, formed by dirt and grey rock, extends north into the black of the mountain. The walls are mostly smooth, with few nooks or imperfections. A few tiny beads of water have collected at the tip of a tiny stalactite, forming a constant, slow drip onto the slick rock below.
118930: A series of wide caverns runs east and west. The stone walls show evidence of toolwork, crudely carved where the caverns narrow, possibly to make passage through here possible at all. The cavern floors are dusty and dry, with footprints in the dirt.
118931:
A mossy pool of water has formed in a depression on the cavern's floor.
A weapons rack stands against the wall.
In the rack are two short spears.
A strong, heavy-set goblin glares blankly ahead.
A strong, heavy-set goblin glares blankly ahead.

This rather long cavern has a wide gap in the ceiling exposing it to the open sky. A mossy pool of water has collected in the middle of it. To one side is a crudely fashioned wooden rampart. Scattered in a loose u-shape around the fortification are large stones to form an extra obstacle, perhaps.
118932: This wide, grey cavern is rather undistinctive. The walls are reasonably smooth and loose rocks are scattered about here and there. A crudely carved stairway is chipped into one of the cavern walls, leading up to a large stone which may be rolled aside.
118934:
A large cabinet capable of storing goods is here.
In the cabinet, there are a pair of rigid leather boots, a rigid leather helmet, and a pair of rigid leather trousers.
A sturdy peg for hanging armour is on the wall.
On the peg, there is a mottled cloak.
A weapons rack stands against the wall.
In the rack are a shortsword, a longspear, and a warhammer.

This chamber looks like it was carved out of the rock, the walls are too even to be natural. An assortment of weaponry and armour has been put here, hanging from pegs, sitting in weapon racks, or squeezed into cabinets. It is, in short, an armoury. Judging from the quality of the equipment found here, it is not maintained by someone who is too keen on quality and keeping things in good condition.
118935:
A strong, heavy-set goblin glares blankly ahead.
A strong, heavy-set goblin glares blankly ahead.
A goblin grunt is here, searching the area for enemies.
A goblin grunt is here, searching the area for enemies.

The series of caverns running from the west comes to an end then splits off into a pair of tunnels branching north and south. The northern tunnel slopes downward, while the southern route terminates in a winding spiral stair. A simple guardpost seems to have been set up at this junction, with simple furniture and an empty rack attached to a wall.
118936: A long procession of roughly hewn stairs winds up and down; hundreds of steps lost in darkness. The stairs are crudely tooled but also made smooth by time and evident travel. These caverns have been inhabited by something or another for many long centuries.
118937:
A huge black fungus is here, exuding a foul stench.
A huge black fungus is here, exuding a foul stench.
A huge black fungus is here, exuding a foul stench.
A giant, strange looking green fungus is here, ready to devour you in seconds.
An ancient fungus smothers the boulders.
An ancient fungus smothers the boulders.

Wet slime slowly ooze down the walls, gathering in shallow pools on the cavern's floor. The small cave, little more than a recess in the rock, stinks of decaying plant life. The air is still, thick, and humid. The ceiling is high and the source of the watery muck is hidden in the gloom above.
118938: A spiralling staircase leads upwards into a round vertical tunnel, with no end in sight. The cavern around the staircase looks like it has been expanded, the walls show signs of being crudely hewn to widen them. Both the stairs and the floor of the cavern are worn smooth.
118939:
A goblin grunt is here, searching the area for enemies.
A goblin grunt is here, searching the area for enemies.
A goblin grunt is here, searching the area for enemies.
A goblin grunt is here, searching the area for enemies.

A wide tunnel slopes downward, winding back and forth as it descends to the south. The tunnel is easily broad enough for several goblins to walk side by side, and the floor and walls of the tunnel show signs of crude chiseling as if it has been widened on purpose.
118940: A foul odour fills the air here. The moist cavern walls are coated with a slimy grey-green fungus, clearly the source of the malodorous stench. Green slime drips from the cavern ceiling and walls; the muddy floor is wet and slick.
118941: A pillar of rock, as broad as three full-grown trolls, dominates the centre of this nearly circular chamber. Fungal growth covers the pillar entirely, lending it a brown-green hue. The air is motionless, chill, and oppressively damp.
118942: Three tunnels, each oddly distinct, intersect at a round chamber. To the east, the passage is lined with phosphorescent moss so that the apparently smooth rock beneath cannot be seen. In contrast, greenish-brown growth obscures a twisting tunnel to the north. Southward, however, the walls are dry and appear almost polished, as if delved by hand rather than natural in origin.
118943:
A greenish slime mould is here, smelling badly.
A huge black fungus is here, exuding a foul stench.

A thin layer of slimy mildew covers the walls and floor of this tunnel, which slopes downward from the east and narrows abruptly into an impassable crack to the west. Water oozes slowly from the ceiling and down the walls. The air is cold and damp, and the footing is slick and treacherous.
118944:
A giant, strange looking green fungus is here, ready to devour you in seconds.
A huge black fungus is here, exuding a foul stench.
A goblin grunt is here, searching the area for enemies.

This chamber hosts a thriving population of varied fungi. Bulbous toadstools crowd in patches on the floor and phosphorescent mosses shimmer along the smooth rock walls. Hidden beneath the proliferation of fungi are indistinct piles of rot in many forms of unclear vegetal or animal origin. A narrow, twisting passageway exits to the west.
118945: A strong, heavy-set goblin glares blankly ahead.

A smooth, polished tunnel leading in from the north suddenly changes directions as it meets a natural opening in the rock running westward. All signs of construction halt at this corner, as if the delvers' plans were ruined in likewise abrupt manner. Faint, steady warmth wafts from further down the tunnel to the west.
118946:
The corpse of a scrawny goblin lies here.
A sturdy target for arrows, made out of thatch, stands here.
In the target is an arrow.

This broad chamber along an east-west tunnel is apparently used by goblins for training in combat. A small arena surrounded by stakes strung with leather thongs lies north of the central passageway, whereas several archery targets are set up to the south. Bloodstains and scattered bones reveal that restraint is not always a part of goblin combat exercises.
118947:
A boiling pot of water bubbles and pops here on a bed of coals.
A bed of crimson coals provides heat to the pot above it.
A small oaken table has been set here.
On the table, there are a quiver and a butcher knife.

A large tunnel running east-to-west broadens as it branches into a barracks to the north and smithy to the south. Goblin fletchers have taken up residence in this part of the cave, evidenced by bone arrowheads and wooden shafts, and animal sinew lying along the southern wall. Loose bundles of arrows and crude bows rest at the entrance of the barracks, ready to be taken up at a moment's notice.
118948:
A roughly woven hammock hangs from the ceiling.
A battered warg fur has been left here.
A filthy straw pallet is lying here.

All available space in this low, broad chamber is devoted to bedding of various sorts. Furs, crude mats, and piles of moss lie strewn haphazardly, yet no spot of the rock floor beneath is visible. The floor space has apparently proven insufficient, as several hammocks hang from pegs in the walls and ceiling. Faint warmth and the scent of smoke wafts from the south, a possible reason for the overstuffed popularity of these sleeping quarters.
118949:
A weapons rack stands against the wall.
In the rack is an orkish shortbow.
A strong, heavy-set goblin glares blankly ahead.
A strong, heavy-set goblin glares blankly ahead.

A tunnel entering from the east slopes suddenly upward to pass through a narrow crack no more than a few feet wide. Crude stairs have been carved into the rock at irregular intervals, sufficiently shallow for goblin-sized legs. The natural bottleneck of this tunnel affords a strong defensive position. Arms and supplies, including many crude bows, line the walls.
118950:
A small oaken table has been set here.
On the table, there are a hammer and a pair of tongs.
A large stone fireplace with a roaring fire warms the room.
A weapons rack stands against the wall.
In the rack are a scimitar and a black waraxe.
A goblin grunt is here, heating metal in his fire.

Ash and soot blacken the walls of a low, broad chamber. Weapons and armour in various states of construction and repair are strewn about the room. Along the southern wall, a gentle depression holds hot coals for a smithy's work. A natural chimney extends upward through the rock, making for a convenient egress for the smithy's fumes, revealing uncharacteristic ingenuity on the part of the goblins that use this chamber.
118951: This rocky chamber resembles a funnel, with steeply sloping sides converging toward a crude staircase that descends eastward from its bottom. The ceiling dips downward following the shape of the floor below. An oppressively dark tunnel winds away from the southern entrance to the chamber.
118952: A tunnel with pitch-black walls bends around a protruding obsidian rock formation along its north-eastern wall. The obsidian is run through with grey streaks of some unknown impurity. Scratches along the otherwise smooth stone indicate where some creature attempted, but then gave up on liberating this stone from the rocky walls.
118953: A narrow tunnel bends as it runs beneath a ceiling of hard, smooth obsidian. A failed mine that would have run north cuts off suddenly beneath a cascade of rubble. Several other attempts to extract minerals from the walls are also evident along the tunnel, these more quickly abandoned.
118954:
A small, scrawny goblin skulks about.
A small, scrawny goblin skulks about.
A strong, heavy-set goblin glares blankly ahead.
A small, scrawny goblin skulks about.

This tunnel makes a sharp and sudden bend from east to north. The sheer blackness of the walls would make this abrupt turn a rather unpleasant surprise for any who would carelessly dash along this passageway. Sundry supplies spill out of a deep recess in the southern wall.
118955: A stone-walled tunnel passes through deep underground, the walls crushingly strong and imposing. The mining work was quick, but skilled, leaving the path straight through. The walls are a dreary grey, broken up by dull, rust-coloured rivulets, dripping slowly down.
118956:
A small, scrawny goblin skulks about.
A small, scrawny goblin skulks about.

Piled on either side of a central walkway are stacks and stacks of broken or old weapons, armour, goblin clothing as well as general refuse. Some of the items have spilled out onto the path, making fast travel here dangerous. The footpath leads from the west to a rough-hewn stairway leading down.
118957: The floor of this tunnel slopes slightly downward from east to west. The passage is increasingly covered in dust and small stones. The tunnel seems to be very old and to the east heavy timbers support the ceiling.
118958: A swiftly flowing torrent, dark and freezing, carries from the south to the north through a large, water-worn opening in a slate-grey wall before vanishing into unknowable depths. A crude path leading up has been hewn out of the bare stone on the western rockface.
118959:
Something cold and scaly slithers past your leg.
Something cold and scaly slithers past your leg.

A swiftly, sweeping icy stream courses from south to north here, filling half the chamber with a chilly, dark liquid. The strange thing is how silent the river is flowing. To the east, a black eddy swirls into a deep pool.
118960: At the Side of a Hill

An ibex is watching you from afar.
An ibex is watching you from afar.

The grass grows taller here, closer to the water, than in the eastern fields. Small trails, trodden frequently by animals, run seemingly irregularly across the land in intricate patterns, some suddenly stopping at holes in the ground. To the north, the ground slopes slightly upwards to a low hill, the beginning of the mountains in the east.
118961: A finch flies low above the ground.

Hills rise up against the river to the west, with steep cliffs making passage in that direction and the south impossible. To the north and east lie more rolling plains. Even further east, the Misty Mountains rise majestically over the region.
118962: The small river flowing southwest of here announces its presence with a soft roaring as it picks up speed. As it has hollowed out the ground over the ages, sinking deeper and deeper, the eastern bank has risen several feet above the water. Thick brush stretch out in the southeast, towards the mountains.
118963: Vast fields of green grass surround you. Quite close to the north, a steep hillside rises up from the otherwise flat lands around. A thin, lonely tree stands in the middle of the field, surrounded by some short bushes, and far in the east, the slopes of the Misty Mountains start their upward journey towards the sky.
118964: An ibex is watching you from afar.

As the hard, rocky ground in the east loses its dominance to more nourishing earth, grass and small plants are able to grow more freely. The fields start off hesitantly, but quickly gain confidence as they roll south and westwards. The land changes quite dramatically in the north, where tall hills stand, close to the mountains. The steep, naked side of one of the hills shoots into the air just north of here.
118965:
Some small rocks have been piled into a mound here.
A large brown snake with black patches is coiled here.

Plains covered in green sod dominate the view, the sharp blades of grass striking upwards like thousands upon thousands of tiny spears. Patches of shrubbery have made this place home. An almost perfect circle of small white stones lies neatly in the grass, though whether by chance or purpose it is difficult to say. Some hills can be seen to the north that prevent travel.
118968: A sprawling green bush of stinging nettle grows here.

From small trickling rivulets the grass absorbs enough water to flourish on these rolling fields. Up and down they roll in an apparently never-ending fashion. Small thickets of stinging nettle occurs from time to time, and a few flowers can be spotted. In the east the steep slopes of the Misty Mountains rise up forming an impassable wall of cold hard rock and snow.
118969: Nourished by the meltwater of the Misty Mountains towering up steeply to the east, green grass overtakes the hard rock of the slopes. The grassland rolls ever up and down, each decline giving a little shelter against the elements. All over the small tracks of wildlife run irregularly, suddenly ending or starting, sometimes with a tiny hole in the ground.
118970: Hill at the Edge of the Plains

The ground becomes harder and higher as it draws closer to the mountains in the east, making it hard for the grass to grow. Some tougher thorn bushes and shrubs are scattered among the fading grass, seemingly having little trouble surviving in this harsh hill environment. A small stream twists through the lands to the west.
118971: With a swamp just to the west, this field is flat, damp and a bit smelly at times. Low lying areas have wetland plants growing in it, and the grass rising from the red soil is thicker than in other parts of the region. Even the wiry brush seems healthier and more robust. Still, it is an area that offers little of interest or even value. To the north some hills rise breaking the view, while a river flows to the northwest.
118972: Vast rolling fields of green grass surround you. Low bushes cling close to the ground, shaped by the years of constant cold winds blowing down from the towering mountain range that rises up towards the sky off in the east. Far to the northeast a forerunner of the Misty Mountains can be seen, rising up from the grasslands. To the south a small mountain stream makes its way northwest, gaining width as it goes.
118973: An ibex is watching you from afar.

A hill covered in rough brush and grass rise overlooking the river and plains. Passage south and west is blocked by the steep river banks. To the north more bleak plains as are typical of the region can be seen, while heading south offers even more of the same kind of plains.
118974: A brook trout is here, swimming in the current.

Having reached the vast plains of this flat land, the stream flows at a more languid pace in its journey to the northwest. The stream bends westwards, where vast plains spread out as far as the eye can see. To the south, a swamp forms a border where water and plains meet.
118975: Slowly the stream wends its way through the wilderness making a lazy bend here to the north. On its banks grows a rough green grass, mixed with small thorn bushes. To the east rise the foothills of the Misty Mountains and to the north and west an expanse of rolling grasslands spreads out. Flowing water has eroded the banks to the south, blocking all travel in that direction.
118976: A water moccasin slithers out of sight just below the surface of the water.

At this southern end of the river, plains turn to swamp, offering a haven for all sorts of creatures who love marshy areas. To the east and west lie more plains, while the river flows north and west for some distance. Looking northeast, one can see several hills breaking the monotony of the landscape.
118977: The ground becomes harder and rougher as it draws closer to the mountains in the east, making it hard for the dry, brown grass to grow. But some tougher thorn bushes and shrubs are scattered among the fading grass, seemingly having little trouble surviving in the harsh environment. A small stream makes its way through the landscape to the north, cutting the river bank in such a way as to block passage. To the south lie hills, while swamps form to the east, and plains continue far to the west.
118978: Small patches of bare earth mix in with the occasional stone in these sparsely vegetated grasslands. The ground is hard and infertile, composed of red-brown clay and limestone. Far to the east a few foothills can be seen, the lower slopes of the Misty Mountains.
118979:
A field vole has frozen to the spot, sensitive to your presence.
A demon wolf lurks here, its dark form twisting and hiding its shape.

These bleak plains come rolling down from the south to the north. There is close to no vegetation at all here, save the dry, brown grass that grows in patches in the dusty, red-brown soil. The fields extend ever onwards, and far off to the east the ever-white peaks of the Misty Mountains reach up towards the sky.
118980:
A huge warg is here, moving in for the kill.
A huge warg is here, moving in for the kill.
A huge warg is here, moving in for the kill.
A huge warg is here, moving in for the kill.

The rugged crags rears above the plains below as they climb toward the mighty peaks of the Misty Mountains. The mountain's teeth rise above the sky, gnawing at the firmament. Brush and scrub paint the landscape in green and grey.
118982: These craggy hills are but the foothills of the high peaks looming above the land to the east and south. Dangerous cracks and nooks in the rock are hidden by shrubs clinging to every little crack and patch of earth. The land descends to the west and north; towards numerous lower hills to the west and a barren-looking grassland to the north.
118983: There are two stinging nettles here.

The rolling hills are strewn with large clumps of stinging nettle leaves. Some care must be taken while crossing the hills to avoid brushing up against the spiny bushes. To the north, fields of grass and brush cover the land between these hills and a distant river.
118984: Patches of gorse and brush dot the faded landscape, blots of colour amidst an otherwise colourless land. To the north are featureless plains, and to the south are hills dusted with brush and trees. Here and there is the scuttle of small creatures.
118985: A field vole has frozen to the spot, sensitive to your presence.

A few thickets of tangled thorn bushes are scattered amid the small patches of dry, brown grass that cover the plains. The landscape rolls up and down, with a few large boulders giving scant shelter from the elements. Far to the east a mountain range reaches up towards the sky.
118986: Dry, brown grass covers the plains in small patches, with a few thickets of tangled thorn bushes in between. The landscape rolls up and down, giving little shelter from the elements. Close to the east a thickets of wiring brush can be seen, while in all other directions, the vista is dominated by vast fields of scraggly grass.
118987: These bleak plains all but define featureless. Flat and without any redeeming qualities, they are an uninterrupted flat area of scrub brush, grass and brown dirt. To the east, marshes meet the plains, and a twisted combination of mud, logs washed from the river further east, and dense brush create an area that cannot be crossed by even the sturdiest dwarf or strongest troll.
118988: Small thickets of tangled thorn bushes dot the dry, brown grass in these billowing fields. The ground is hard and infertile, composed of clay and limestone. To the east lies a swamp, while all other directions show more of the same, tiresome plains that offer no relief from the elements.
118989:
A young filly is just learning to walk.
A wild mare is watching you warily.
A young colt is frolicking playfully.
A domesticated pony, beast of burden to many, stands here.
A snake slithers towards you.

Dry, brown grass and small thickets of thorn bushes are the only flora in these plains. The ground is hard and dry, composed of red brown limestone and clay. To the west lie plains and beyond them an ancient road. To the east is an impassable cliff to the water, and to the south yet more plains.
118990: Clusters of slender stems and tall leaves thrive in the mud and shallows.

A small clear stream runs its course from the southeast to the north. Green grass grows on the banks, as well as reeds and other vegetation. West of here an ancient road can be seen, while barren folded fields extend south. On the horizon to the east the white peaks of the Misty Mountains reach their jagged fingers towards the sky.
118991:
A swarm of mosquitoes is here, humming around you.
A swarm of mosquitoes is here, humming around you.

Here, the river meets the plains and turns them into a swampy mess. Grass and water loving brush rise above the waterlogged soil, making passage more difficult. To the west the swamp gives way to plains, while the swamp continues to the south, and the river continues to flow in a southeasterly direction.
118992:
Clusters of slender stems and tall leaves thrive in the mud and shallows.
A trout swims here.

Following the altitude of the grassland the stream takes on a mainly northwest direction, twisting in between small ridges. The vegetation on the banks is mainly composed of short grass, reed and a few flowers. South and west of here swamps form along the edge of the river.
118993: Clusters of slender stems and tall leaves thrive in the mud and shallows.

Cutting its path through the grassland, the stream now turns in a northwesterly direction, following the contours of the land. The impassable banks are overgrown with reeds, grass and small flowers. Looking east and north one can see foothills to the Misty Mountains forming, but in the southwest grassy fields continue, seemingly forever.
118994:
A blooming water-lily floats on the surface of the water.
A hairy black spider wraps up a silken package with her hind legs.
A swallow flies high above the ground.
A grey snake slides along the water.

Plains meet river and turn into swampy marshes here. To the north and east lie more river. To the west are more swamps, with plains and hills visible further west. Passage south is blocked by dense vegetation and breaks in the terrain.
118995:
A swarm of mosquitoes is here, humming around you.
A swarm of mosquitoes is here, humming around you.
A swarm of mosquitoes is here, humming around you.

The low plains have been turned into a marsh by the surrounding waterlogged lands to the north and east. Higher plains to the west and south remain dry, but cannot be reached through the muck and mire of this area. Here and there swarms of mosquitoes flit about looking for some unfortunate creature to feed from and harass.
118996:
A black catfish is here, lurking in the mud.
A brook trout is here, swimming in the current.
A swallow flies high above the ground.

The water follows the decline of the surrounding landscape twisting back and forth, flowing northward into the lower parts of the valley. To the west, the bank rises up against the barren plains, preventing passage in that direction. Looking south, the river gives way to a dense swamp.
118997: A swallow flies high above the ground.

The cold mountain water makes a sharp turn west along a steeply undermined bank that has been hollowed out over the course of many years. Any travel to the north is prevented by that undercutting. South and west wide, large wet swamplands spread out, and to the east the foothills of the Misty Mountains rise slowly.
118998: A brook trout is here, swimming in the current.

A small stream runs its course from the southeast to the northwest. The eastern bank has been hollowed out over time, making travel in that direction impossible. Near the stream green lush grass grows in abundance, while further south barren dry grassland stretches out as far as the eye can see. To the east a forerunner of the Misty Mountains rises up from the rolling fields.
118999: These bleak plains continue far to the north and south as well to the east and west. There is close to no vegetation at all here, save a few patches of dried brown grass. Small, dried-out rivulets tell of a time long ago when the land was less parched, but now dusty, red-brown soil dominates the landscape. Far to the north a road can be seen.
119000: Dry, brown grass covers the plains in small patches, with a few thickets of tangled thorn bushes scattered between them. The landscape rolls up and down, giving little shelter from the elements. Far to the east great white peaks jut upward into the sky, a spectacular backdrop to the otherwise repetitive fields that extend all around.
119001: The arid fields stretch out before you, undulating gently as they progress from north to south. A few tangled thorn bushes can be seen, a contrast to the never-ending dry brown grass and hard limestone that otherwise dominate the landscape. Small old dried-out rivulets tell of a time long before, but now the dusty red-brown soil dominates the area.
119002: The elongated shape of a stoat can be seen darting across the terrain.

All bold colour has departed from this land. Paints of grey and sallow yellow wash the scrub with faded dreams. Still, a few white blooms toss in the breeze, as the Misty Mountains loom above on the eastern horizon, stretching in an unbroken line from northeast to southeast, its mighty peaks shrouded in clouds.
119003: Grey and green dominate the landscape with patches of mottled brush. To the west the brush clears, and to the east the brush continues, albeit a different hue. The mighty mountain range known as the Misty Mountains rises to the east, dominating the view.
119004: The rolling grey wastelands begin to rise to the west, where a slender goat trail winds up onto a high ridge that dominates the western skyline. To the south are more wastes, and to the east, much the same, but spotted with grey brush and clumps of wiry grass.
119005: Rising high above the surroundings, this ridge wends its way from the northeast to the south, becoming a high saddleback. Off to the west can be glimpsed a winding, broken road, grey and forbidding. Barren wastelands lie to the east. Beyond, a shimmering blue-grey river cleaves the blasted lands.
