119006:
A tall plant with a perfectly smooth stem gracefully marks the landscape.
A clear spring babbles as cool water trickles out of the ground.

A ring of hemlocks springs from the brush, their thick green spines filling the sky like a crown. Amidst the break in the scrub, a strange mushroom fairy ring mimics the brush. West and east the hemlocks pop amidst the scrub, their small white flowers in contrast with the drab greens surrounding them.
119007: The elongated shape of a stoat can be seen darting across the terrain.

The low hills are lightly covered with hemlock plants and sparse brush. The small white flowers of the hemlock plants stand in contrast to the faded greens of the other plantlife. The great Misty Mountains rise high above to the south like crowns against the sky.
119008:
A huge, poisonous tarantula extends her legs to you.
A huge, poisonous spider is here.
A black spider crawls here, a shiny red spot visible on its belly.
A huge, poisonous spider is here.
A forest spider is here crawling around.
A forest spider is here crawling around.
A forest spider is here crawling around.

The brush here is coloured in blueish-green, thickly clumped, and studded with nettles. A small cul-de-sac has been created by the dense foliage and towering peaks to the south. Little shows from the sky, the brush forms a dense hedge that covers any light from entering.
119009: These bleak fields roll in a north and south direction, and are covered with dense, stunted brush that struggle to rise from the barely fertile soil. On top of a small elevation, a single gnarled tree fights to rise above the unforgiving ground. From time to time, cold and harsh winds blow down from the mountains rising far to the east. Badly broken ground prevents any travel south, limiting options for the weary traveller, while foothills break the landscape closer to the east.
119010:
A black raven flies in the sky searching for flesh to prey upon.
A black raven flies in the sky searching for flesh to prey upon.
A black raven flies in the sky searching for flesh to prey upon.

Dry brown grass covers the hill in small patches, protruding through the thin, red-brown soil. A few thickets of tangled thorn bushes can be spotted in this unsheltered land. The soil is unfruitful which explains the barren view. Close to the east lie flatter brush-covered plains. Passage west and south appear to be impossible.
119011: Scattered brush and thorny bushes litter the hardened red soil. Fragments of quartzite are the only things that can be seen jutting up from the rolling hill, and no shelter is to be seen for miles around. Further off to the east rolling fields stretches out. Passage to the west is blocked by harsh terrain that offers no exit. To the south, even more hills rise.
119012: Miles of featureless, flat terrain spread all around. Here and there grass and scrub brush manage to find life on the nearly waterless plains. To the far east, hills can be seen breaking the monotony of the landscape. Dense, interlocking thickets of brush prevent all travel to the north and east, making this a rather unpleasant place to be cornered in.
119013: Long stretches of empty, grey plains spread out to the north and south punctuated only by spurts of dark bushes and patches of hardy grass. In the west, the land rises to a faint trail that leads higher up.
119014:
A mountain goat is here, jumping from cliff to cliff.
A mountain goat is here, jumping from cliff to cliff.

A dusty trail rolls up and down this high ridgeline. Among the rocks and dust some sprigs of hardy grass maintain a precarious existence in defiance of the elements. Looking west, a steep incline rises along the horizon. To the east, a small trail snakes up from dull, grey wastelands below.
119015: A faint goat trail winds its way from the high ridge to the north down into a stony vale. Tough, grey-green vegetation clings to the hillsides in patches and clumps as steep rockfaces prevent movement except along the winding trail.
119016: Many smooth round stones are scattered about.

A small valley nestles below the northern craggy hills. Flat, round stones are scattered across the vale in a variety of shapes and sizes. Tufts of scrubgrass and nettles poke up between the stones determined to survive the hostile environment. To the west, a wide plain opens up while beyond, a broad ridge of hills rises in the distance.
119017: The grasses that grow here are shorter than usual, clinging to the ground in abundance. This keeps them from blowing away and traps their own moisture securely to the ground. The plains continue to the west and south, while a wilted and dried field can be found north.
119018: Dry, wilted grasses lie scattered about here. This once thriving field is no longer fed by water and, as a result, the grasses are desiccated, and dead or dying. The fallow fields continue onwards north and west. To the south, short stout grasses, hardier than those found here, grow in abundance.
119019: A giant earth beetle is crawling on the ground here.

This could have once been a thriving field, with healthy plant life and maybe even produced some crops for hardworking farmers. Now it is only slightly more than a dry desert. The long wide cracks in the ground harbour dust, dirt and dead weeds. Little else exists here since it is so dry. The desolate fields continue to the north, west, and south.
119020: A giant earth beetle is crawling on the ground here.

The ground is hard and infertile, mostly composed of clay and limestone. A thick layer of dust covers the ground of these arid fields. A ridge ascends to the south and east, but it allows passage to south. No other landmarks can be seen across the wide plains, except for the large mountain range that looms in the distance to the east.
119022: A small brown snake is slithering around here.

This field is covered in small stones and pebbles. A landslide probably moved the covering soil away and left the rocks here. Small bunches of brown grass spring up between the rocks, however the field is far too filed with stones to be of any agricultural use. The fields continue in all directions with little discernible change.
119023: A black raven flies in the sky searching for flesh to prey upon.

The soil is dry and cracked in this place. No moisture reaches here and the dust is evident. The few scraggly weeds that have grown up from the cracks are little more than yellowed, dead husks. A single, stunted tree once grew here, but that has fallen to the ground, cracked and dry as a bone.
119024: The hills here are covered with rocks of every size. The brush and grasses that squeeze between the stones give this area a sparse appearance. There are rocky fields to the east and south of here, while there is a bit more vegetation to the west and little growth to the north.
119025:
A large thorny branched shrub is growing here.
On the shrub, there are two piles of blackberries.
A large, venomous-looking green snake is coiled up here.

The hills are broken up as the soil has been dug up all around here and left uneven. Grasses and small bushes have continued to grow and cover the broken land. A road can be seen under the ridge, running from the north around to the west as it meanders its way through the fields. To the south and east the fields continue.
119026: A slobbering giant greedily lumbers towards you.

Someone or something has dug a huge pit in the hillside, it does not look like it was naturally formed. Roots of some plants are poking through the ceiling and the walls. On the ground, there are a lot of loose sand and stones, and some bones and sticks and dry hay. The smell is quite strong here in this dusty and stale pit.
119027:
A brown snake watches you.
A brown snake watches you.

It would be a tremendous feat of nature for any life form to survive prolonged exposure to the harsh elements in this area. The dusty hills are dry and the ground is cracked in several places. There are no trees or shrubs to provide shelter nor is there any water source visible. The hills descend slightly to the east and continue to the north and south.
119028: Dry and lifeless, the slightest breath of wind kicks up whirlwinds of dust across this gritty promontory. The soil lacks any nutrients and is filled with cracks. An overgrown road lies directly to the west while the fields continue to the south. Far off in the east the horizon is filled with high jagged peaks creating the image of a large jaw jutting up from the earth.
119029: Thin cracks spread out tenuously where the earth has split from the lack of moisture, and small rocks litter the ground across these desolate fields. The fields stretch out flat and lifeless to the east, while a steep ridge ascends to the west and south. An old road is visible to the north.
119033: Grey and grey and grey. Barren and blasted, these areas are not a place any wise man might tread. The ground is uneven and the dry earth is cracked in places and covered with rocky formations in other. To the east, the lands flatten out more except for a tall rocky formation.
119034:
A big, nasty vulture is sitting here, protecting its nest.
A big, nasty vulture is sitting here, protecting its nest.

This rocky formation is butting up against the rising Misty Mountains to the east, but further ascent is blocked by sheer walls of rough stone. The ground has numerous cracks and crevices, some of which looks to be used as nests by birds. Westwards, a more gentle slope descends to lower ground.
119035:
A huge, hungry-looking rat is here.
A huge, hungry-looking rat is here.
A huge, hungry-looking rat is here.

This small cottage has not seen any use in many years. The walls look close to collapse, all the mortar between the stones having crumbled away long ago. The roof is filled with large holes that allow rain and snow to fall inside. The floor boards are rough and mouldy, creaking and groaning when the least weight is applied on them. Old broken furniture litters the floor, and spider webs cling all over. In a corner stands an old open stove.
119036:
A huge, hungry-looking rat is here.
A huge, hungry-looking rat is here.

The cavern has been used as a storage room once upon a time. Now it is a mouldy place filled with garbage. The cavern extends north into a damp cave, and a small ladder leads up towards the ceiling. A few roots can be seen reaching through the walls for water, and the western wall is intertwined with spidery webs.
119037: A black spider crawls here, a shiny red spot visible on its belly.

Dug from the moist earth this damp cave has been deserted for ages. The walls, floor and ceiling are all very rough, evidence that the cave was constructed in haste. The sodden earth gathers enough water to create small rivulets that make their way slowly down the walls, trickling towards the floor to gather in small, murky, brown puddles.
119038:
A huge, hungry-looking rat is here.
A huge, hungry-looking rat is here.
A huge, hungry-looking rat is here.
A huge, hungry-looking rat is here.
A huge, hungry-looking rat is here.
A huge, hungry-looking rat is here.

The walls, ceiling and floor are all comprised of a thick sticky mud. Rough shoring seems to have been hastily put in but it doesn't look to be very trustworthy. The tunnel descends deeper into the mirk to the south, while upwards traces of limestone lead on into the dark. The incessant dripping of water can be faintly heard percolating through the tunnel.
119039: The ground has become more watery sludge than mud, squelching and sucking underfoot. Some boards of old wood seem to have been thrown down here to help give some stable footing but they are now rotten and almost entirely consumed by the mud. There is no hint of fresh air here, only stale dankess.
119040:
A huge, hungry-looking rat is here.
A huge, hungry-looking rat is here.
A huge, hungry-looking rat is here.

Worms and what appear to be fish bones can be seen sticking through the mud walls, the rotten wooden scaffold holding the tunnel in place seems entirely dilapidated and ready to give way at any moment. Water trickles down the walls and through the ceiling, dribbling into the pool of water covering the floor. Wading through the slosh causes considerable amounts of movement and noise, yet the air hangs heavy and motionless.
119041:
A huge, hungry-looking rat is here.
A huge, hungry-looking rat is here.
A huge, hungry-looking rat is here.
A huge, hungry-looking rat is here.
A huge, hungry-looking rat is here.

The ground here rises sloping upwards and descends sharply towards the north. An oozing stream of thick mud continuously seems to be sliding down the tunnel to the north like a mirky honey dripping down a tree. The dripping of water somewhere is defeaning in the dead silence of this slimy passage.
119042: Up above a breath of fresh air can be felt wafting in, mixing in with the stale air of this muddy tunnel. Down Below the tunnel dips steeply leading to darkness with nothing but the sound of dripping water ahead. Up above an incline made of mud, tufts of grass, and roots leads to an opening one might be able to crawl through.
119049: This outhouse has clearly seen better days -and better users. Now broken down and reeking of unspeakable filth, it is both the only shelter from the sun for possible miles around, but also the only place to get a little private relief if truly needed. There is no real way of telling who might be desperate enough, or perhaps foolhardy enough to use this building. A stinking pit opens down from the middle of the building, and a well-worn, creaky door appears to be latchable for a little privacy.
119050: A large mean-looking troll is here.

This foul, stinking pit is full of water, faeces, and other disgusting items perhaps half a yard deep. The reeking smell seems to rise to the heavens and there is no real relief from it. Streaks of greenish brown slime line the crudely dug earthen walls, and the only way back up seems to require getting covered in that same slime.
119051: A pitiful man, unwashed and dressed in rags, toils endlessly.

Piles of stone and building materials lie piled up here, ready to be used to repair the ancient buildings and walls that make up this camp, and even perhaps to build new structures and walls. Prisoners captured along the abandoned road might be seen toiling away for their captors until ransomed or no longer of use to the bandits.
119052: A skull is here, spiked to the end of a pole.

More than anything it seems the bandits hate the goblin hordes that at times must infest the areas around the abandoned road. Since the trolls of the area aren't eating enough of them, the cruel bandits must do their part to keep the goblin population in check. Whenever they capture goblins alive, they are brought here to be tortured for information and pleasure, and then killed without mercy. Rows of severed heads serve as proof of their prowess at this task.
119053: The path heads further south into what looks like a settlement. It is possible though this is an unsavoury place for unsavoury people, as it is unlikely that any honest sort would live in this area. Certainly whoever lives here is bound to be of a rather sturdy sort given the isolation and dangers surrounding them.
119054: Just south of the trail entering the camp, the ground gives way to somewhat bare and churned out ground. In rainy weather it can be quite muddy, or equally dusty and unpleasant in warmer months. To the east is the patched up stone wall of an ancient building, while a crude wooden wall blocks passage west.
119055:
A malicious thug is here, threatening you.
A dirty bandit waits here looking for an easy mark.
A dirty bandit waits here looking for an easy mark.

Firmly inside the bandit camp, there are more open spaces that perhaps in some ancient time were used for drilling or markets or livestock before this small patch of buildings was abandoned and fell into ruin. To the east is another repaired stone building with a crudely patched up door, while in all other directions are more open areas. Perhaps the better for fighting and chasing enemies...
119056: An open field with quickly repaired stone buildings to the west serves as a makeshift training area for the men who reside in this camp. Targets of various sorts are placed with the building walls serving as a backstop. The ground itself is kept mostly clean and level, and a couple of places look like they are used to practice wrestling or other hand-to-hand combat arts. A crude barricade to the south blocks travel, while open fields lie to the north and east.
119057:
The corpse of a husky smuggler is lying here.
The corpse of a husky smuggler is lying here.
An experienced husky smuggler is here, conspiring with his cohorts.
An experienced husky smuggler is here, conspiring with his cohorts.

This flat and open field is regularly used, and so the grass and brush are trampled by the feet of men and hooves of horses. It may serve as a marshalling yard, or simply a place to gather and do such things as these rough, evil men like to do in their spare time. The occasional scent of alcohol or pipe-weed wafts through the air. To the east, a wooden barricade blocks travel.
119058: To the east of this field lies a broken looking, yet durable stone wall that cannot be readily climbed over. The rest of the area seems taken up by the same wiry grass and coarse shrubs that dominate this part of Arda. Perhaps the occupants of this camp have no ready use for this area, or perhaps it will someday fill with tents and buildings if the camp grows.
119060:
An apple tree with bright green leaves grows here.
On the tree's branches are three apples.

To the west, come the smells associated with a camp kitchen. Here in this field lie the detritus of that kitchen- a pile of compost in one corner, a pit of trash and bones in another, with a garden area making up much of the rest of this location. It seems even violent, evil men know they have to eat and eat well. To the south is a repaired stone wall of another building complex, and a wooden barricade to the north. To the east is another open area with a grim purpose.
119061:
A stove stands against one wall here.
A cook stands here preparing meals for the bandits.

A large open fireplace heats the room and whatever happens to be in the kettle placed over it. Elsewhere, sacks of vegetables and grains, and various other provisions fill the room, evidence of good looting of passing travellers and caravans. To the east lies an open area, while to the north and south, doors offer passage to other rooms in the stone-walled complex.
119062:
A simple wooden chest is here.
A small barrel made of aged oak and strong iron hoops stands here.

Tucked away behind the kitchen, this room is filled with crate, sacks, chests, bales and barrels of likely looted and captured goods, along with supplies needed to run the camp. It may even be possible that more valuable goods are hidden away out of sight...
119063: A small loyal cat is here.

Windowless stone walls and thick thatch roofing make up this room which is filled with bedding and storage chests. Clearly a place for the lower status guards and occupants of the camp to sleep, it is a cheerless room rank with the smell of sweat, smoke and stale wine.
119064:
A weapons rack stands against the wall.
In the rack are a falchion and a metal shield.

The stone walls of this room are surprisingly clean, and the room itself is rather well lit. Racks of weapons line two walls, while another has strange alchemical bottles and scrolls. The faint smell of beasts, leather and oiled steel permeate the room, and the overall orderly appearance suggests this room is regularly used by a disciplined person or persons.
119065:
A large dog curls his lips back and snarls.
A mugger lurks here, looking for a stranger to rob.
A brigand, looking at your nice purse, is sneaking here.

This old stone building has been hastily repaired by semi-skilled hands. Gaps in old mortar have been filled, and breaks in the wall quickly, but strongly repaired. The dirt floor has been covered with fresh reeds from the nearby river, and the roof given a new thatching that looks like it probably will keep water out. To the north is a somewhat private room that might be sleeping quarters for an important person. A desk and a couple of chairs fill out this room, while an old wooden door patched up with hide is to the west. A simple fireplace burns with a bright light and offers heat for cooking and warmth in cold weather.
119066:
The corpse of a woman slave is lying here.
A large stone fireplace with a roaring fire warms the room.
An ornate elven chest, embellished with golden wood, has been left here.
A sturdy bed made from solid oak lies here, covered in warm blankets.
On the bed, there is a piece of paper.
A large dog curls his lips back and snarls.
Osbert the chief smuggler stands here lusting for violence.
A woman slave stands here looking ashamed and scared.

Inside this windowless room is a large bed, a nightstand with a pitcher, and a rack for armour or weapons. Somewhat barren, it still manages to suggest that whoever sleeps here is comfortable. A carpet made of stitched together hides covers much of the floor, while the stone walls and thatched roof are in a similar condition as that of the room directly to the south.
119067:
A short burly man stands here, looking around for something.
A large dog curls his lips back and snarls.
A large dog curls his lips back and snarls.
An experienced husky smuggler is here, conspiring with his cohorts.
An experienced husky smuggler is here, conspiring with his cohorts.

This ramshackle old hut has somehow barely stood the forces of time, time, war and weather. It serves as a place to mostly get out of the elements, and to access a strangely well secured cellar below. Now and then noises might be heard from below, as if someone or something was imprisoned below, although for who's safety is anyone's guess...
119068: The butchered corpse of a wild-eyed man is lying here.

One might be forgiven for at first thinking this hole was a place where foul trolls or nasty goblins made a home, for it is both completely dark, and disgusting with smells of filth and excrement. However, it is instead proof of man's darker nature, and serves as a prison for some unfortunate wretch cast down in here for reasons unknown.
119069:
A saddle lies here on the ground.
A sturdy bandit bodyguard stands here, eager to hack you to pieces.
A stocky mountain mule is here, waiting to serve.
A sturdy pack horse is standing here.

Picket pins and hitching posts dot the landscape, indicating this area is used by the camp's inhabitants to keep their mounts. A whiff of the ground and the large amounts of horse droppings suggest why this area is muddy even in summer.
119070:
A fallen tree lies on the ground, its clump of roots pointing upwards.
A mountain ibex is jumping from rock to rock.
A huge stone giant is here, glaring at you.

A dry streambed winds westward as it descends a rugged slope. To the west, steep ravines and jagged fissures cut into the coarse, darkened rock that comprises the surrounding mountainous landscape. Southward, sheer rockfaces thrust ever-upwards towards rugged crags and sharp, broken peaks of various heights.
119071: Fractured rockfaces, lined with ice and permafrost, rise obstinately towards the west, making travel in that direction impossible for even the most resolute mountaineer. In all other directions, the rocky crags and mountainous terrain become slightly less perilous at ground level, allowing for ingress and egress if enough effort is applied. Above ground level, several boulders and columns of rock hang precariously between gaps in the rock.
119072: Jagged fingers of rock thrust up from thick, white blankets of crystalline snow. Chunks of scree have fallen from high above, pocking the harsh landscape with ashen craters of various depths. Sheer rock faces, marbled with ice-filled cracks and chipping stone form these natural, towering edifices.
119073: Sharp fingers of snow-capped mountain peaks frame the western horizon like massive, gnarled claws reaching up to tear the sky asunder. In all directions these jagged peaks rise to unknown heights as they pierce the clouds that cling desperately to the cold, dark stone high above. The only path down from this isolated precipice is through a narrow cleft to the north.
119074: Hidden from view by the surrounding peaks, this trail can only be detected from within or above. Although this place seems to be unknown by its careful placement in the mountains, the path seems well worn, though the ground shows no obvious sign of foot or hoof or wheel rut.
119075: Passing through the barren mountains and continuing south, this nature of this road is a bit mysterious; perhaps it was created for easier travel between certain places, for roads in this area are rare and out of the way. However, the way in which it has been hidden from spying eyes may imply that its purpose is not so simple.
119076: Bending to the west and north along the banks of a wide river, this path seems to vanish from sight into the mountains to the north. Plains extend out of sight to the west, seen beyond a few shorter mountain peaks; this river flows freely from the east to the west.
119077: As this path winds its way from the mountains to the northeast down to the wide plains to the west, the width of the trail thins a bit, perhaps to prevent it from being seen from afar. The path carefully follows the river that flows to the south; never far from a source of water, and a place to hide one's tracks.
119078: Following a quiet stream to the southeast, this trail is hardly discernible, even while being travelled. Whoever first created this path was careful to pass around any obstructions, rather than moving them or going over; at most times, the trail goes to the north of any obstacles, so the path is shaded even when the sun is directly overhead.
119079: Following the bend in the stream to the south and east, this trail makes its way north and west alongside great distances of plains. A steady wind sweeps the ground at all times, polishing stones and exposing the cracked soil.
119080: Passing from east to west along the stream to the south, this faint trail is sometimes hidden from view beneath the heavy silt that blankets the area; at times it seems to simply vanish. Plains extend out of sight to the north.
119081: Constant winds drift over this area, rippling the surface of the water that passes to the south, and wiping this place clean of tracks, given time. The path itself is always at risk of becoming buried as bits of soil are blown into its path, but for now it remains faintly visible below.
119082: Making a gentle bend from the south to the east as it tries to follow a stream through the area, the nature of this trail is not very clear. It is faint enough to be an animal trail, yet deliberate and carefully placed.
119083:
A carrot is growing here.
A large potato is growing here.

A small ring of stones, with even smaller bits of coal and unburned wood, are all that suggest that this place may be a campsite. Located just west of a flowing stream, which should be suitable for drinking, this site seems to be the terminal end of a trail that leads north. No other signs of road or civilisation can be seen, making this place even more odd.
119084: This area of the mountains seems devoid of life. cold dead rock lies all around. A narrow path leading north and east has been stomped into the ground. High thornbushes to the sides of the trail keep the path hidden from outside view. Faint sounds of activity trails in from the south.
119085: This area of the mountains is barren and lifeless. Away to the north the mountains give way some low hills which are crossed by a small river. Running east and west, a partially secluded trail makes its way through these steep and rocky mountains.
119086: The ground is hard and barren as the path leads north and west. Higher ground rising steeply to the east and south serves as a detour for those wishing to head into the mountains. Sounds of splashes seem to indicate the presence of water nearby and the way to the west becomes more secluded and hidden by rising ground.
119087: Jagged and rocky hills stand all around, completely obstructing any passage to the west. The ground is scattered with loose sharp rocks which could do significant injury to the careless traveler. Many sharp crevices cast dark shadows among the hills. The faint echo of splashing water reverberates from the hills to the north and east while a quiet path leads southwards.
119088: The river winds its way around the hills as they rise up in its path. Pebbles lining the riverbed make the ground hard and loose. One must carefully plant each foot as the rushing frigid water makes it difficult to keep balanced. The river flows from the east and heads north. To the west there seems to be a path leading from the river.
119089: You are standing among a range of hills that lie partly along the Misty Mountains. A river flows from the high mountains to the east and heads towards the Glanduin in the western horizon. The mountains stand tall and proud, their snow-capped peaks defying the sky with their magnificence. Upstream to the east, a parade of water tumbles towards you while the way to the south seems much drier.
119090: A black catfish is here, lurking in the mud.

Among the high hills you wander, exploring further into the mountains. Compared to the Misties, however, these hills are like children among adults. Ice covered peaks dominate to the east, lending an awesome, if not daunting, view. A low river has dug its bed through the hills and the only workable path seems to be along the river.
119091:
A bright green holly bush is growing here.
Partly covered by the bush's green leaves, there are two piles of hollyberries.

A thin trail consisting of a few small patches of hard ground formed from passing feet heads west. The surroundings are bare and the ground is flat. To the southeast the great Misty Mountains rise up in horizon. Sounds of lapping water emanate from the south while thick green vegation sprouts up from that direction.
119094: At this point, you are moving close from the Hithaeglir proper, in a sea of low bushes. To the south the Misty Mountains stretch high above you, their snowy peaks pointing towards the heavens. The dangers, both natural and otherwise, cause you to slow your step and view the beauty in a more cautious manner.
119095: You are standing near the tall peaks of the Hithaeglir. All around you they stand proudly. The air coming from the high altitude is cold and chill winds that dart among the mountains like spirits of eternal winter. Tales of deeds both daring and dark churn in your mind leaving you humbled against the grandeur of the scene.
119096: The Hills between the Misty Mountains

The hills here are quite high and anywhere else they would be considered mountains. However, among these peaks, they are but smaller versions of the incomparable Misty Mountains. From this height though, it appears possible to move among the mountains themselves. Perhaps that would not be the wisest choice but at heart you are still an adventurer.
119097: The Hills between the Misty Mountains

Standing impossibly high, the Misty Mountains rise about you. Their defiance of the laws of nature is a mute but unending testimony to the grandeur here. The hills you stand on now are quite high, even enabling access to the mountains to the north and south.
119098: The ground here is semi-smooth albeit scattered with sharp rocks and fallen scree. Once an active wash-out, it now serves as a mountainous pathway which continues to the west and south; the latter of which is obscured with mist and shadow. Walls of a dark stony colour loom high above to the east and north, denying even the most skilled mountaineer passage.
119099: The floor of this mountain valley is rather smooth and easy to traverse, the product of long erosion by snow melt and runoff. The mountain slopes to the north and south are likewise smooth, in this case presenting a total denial to any attempts to traverse them.
119100: The ground within this mountainous valley is fairly smooth, with indications that it was once the path of least resistance for melting snow and water run-off. To the south, however, the mountainsides loom overhead to dizzying heights, and offer no purchase for hands or feet.
119101: Sheer precipices loom high overhead to the north and south, seemingly closing in towards each other high above where numerous boulders and crags can be seen. To the east and west, the mountainous terrain remains parted in a natural valley for a great distance. The ground, although rocky and uneven, allows a fairly unobstructed path to continue onward.
119102:
A fallen tree lies on the ground, its clump of roots pointing upwards.
A dirty uruk stands here, the leader of a small pack of renegades.
A renegade uruk is here, dirty and ragged.
A renegade uruk is here, dirty and ragged.
A renegade uruk is here, dirty and ragged.

Far above, towering snow-capped peaks loom ominously against the sky like hideously nailed claws raking at the unfettered heavens. Whether by water erosion or some other natural occurrence, a semi-smooth stretch of uneven rock extends towards the east and west.
119103: Dark rock in the shape of towering, jagged finger-like formations reaches upwards as if it were a clawed hand raking at the heavens. Although broken rock and scree litter the ground here, passage is not impossible in all directions save the south, where a fractured rock wall spreads far and wide.
119104:
A large pile of boulders is sitting here, probably debris from a rockslide.
A dirty uruk stands here, the leader of a small pack of renegades.
A renegade uruk is here, dirty and ragged.
A renegade uruk is here, dirty and ragged.
A renegade uruk is here, dirty and ragged.

Massive rock formations, fractured, cracked, and failing, enclose the terrain here save to the east, where between two great leaning pillars of stone passage back out may be had. High above, nestled between a multitude of mountain peaks, lie several boulders and large, broken pieces of rock. Occasionally, scree can be heard in the distance tumbling down the steep stone walls, crashing into the ground with blurred velocity.
119105: A small flower grows here, with a purple bloom and wide leaves.

The ground within this mountainous valley is fairly smooth, with indications that it was once the path of least resistance for melting snow and water run-off. To the north, the mountains loom overhead to dizzying heights, their tops shrouded in mist and cloud.
119106: Jagged rock walls tower ominously high above, threatening to drop scree and boulders down at any time. Perched precariously atop the stony shelves, several large rocks are on the precipice of tipping into a downward descent. To the west, as well as the south, the natural mountainous valley turns ever onward.
119107: Cradled between two steep, jagged mountainsides to the north and south, a natural depression runs east and west. High overhead, numerous boulders and misshapen fingers of broken rock lay precariously wedged between crags of stone. Far in the distance, this rocky ravine appears to curve northward to the west, and southward to the east.
119108: Jagged outcroppings of dark, cold-cracked stone line the towering walls of mountainous rock that thrust upwards to the northeast and southwest. To the northwest and southeast, somewhat-even ground sprawls outward, evenly distanced between the haphazard wall formations, as if each side of the path took great care to be as far from the dense serration of rock that looms to either side.
119109: Twisting from the south, an uneven yet traversable mountain pass disappears into the empty, dark depths of a cavernous void at the base of an enormous rockface. One is able to see this cave slowly tapers inward for a few feet before all view is swallowed up in darkness. Several enormous stalactites hang from the mouth of the cave, the iron traces from the rock staining the tips an almost blood-red. Beneath these, stalagmites have formed from the mineral deposits dripping from the teeth-like formations overhead, staining the sides the same reddish colour. From a distance, it resembles the blood-stained maw of a wereworm, rather than the mouth of a cave.
119110: Towards the south, the jagged outline of a natural, rocky maw blends into the lighter landscape beyond. Darkness progressively replaces light in the depths of the cave to the north, and only dim outlines of dark, glistening rock can be seen. The faint drip of liquid lightly echoes across the wide walls and ceiling of this place, the roof of which disappears into total darkness high above. The only suggestion of a ceiling existing at all is the tips of rocky teeth hanging down far enough to barely discern them against the darkness.
119111: A small, scrawny goblin skulks about.

Towards the south, the darkness appears to be slightly less dense, as the occasional small point of light can be seen, suggesting an opening in the passages far in that direction. The hard, rocky floor of this cave abruptly slopes downwards to the north, where darkness overtakes any last reflections of light off the jagged stone walls.
119113:
A small, scrawny goblin skulks about.
A small, scrawny goblin skulks about.
A small, scrawny goblin skulks about.
A small, scrawny goblin skulks about.
A small, scrawny goblin skulks about.

The rocky passage continues to the east and west, offering little to no visibility save where artificial light is offered. However, as if reluctant to challenge the engulfing darkness, illumination seems to fall short of where the distance would shine otherwise. Faint drops of water faintly echo across the uneven walls of rock, which seem to resonate slightly louder to the east.
119114: Curving northward as the tunnel continues from the west, the darkness seems to swell thickest in that direction. Downward, the jagged floor begins to descend rapidly into a veil of shadow, beyond which even the strongest light seems unable to touch.
119120: The jagged stone floor gradually becomes more level here, from where it sloped down unevenly from the passage above. Toward the east, the darkness swells thickest, indicating the tunnel advances in that direction. Faint sounds of dripping water can be heard echoing strange patterns across the walls, occasionally mixed with other strange, unfamiliar noises.
119121: A rusty pickaxe with a broken handle lies discarded here.

Here the cold stone tunnel, with jagged teeth of rock overhead and along the walls, meets a sudden dead-end. Strewn about the floor are pieces of broken bone mixed with half-finished and broken tools, crafted from the surrounding hard stone. The only way out is south, where the darkness seems to wait in welcome for any light to foolishly challenge it.
119122: The cold, jagged walls of rock that comprise the walls of this tunnel begin to narrow slightly towards the south, where the tunnel appears to continue on into the darkness. Towards the east, the tunnel continues its solemn, cold march into the blackness.
119123: A narrow tunnel opening lies to the north, where the cold, jagged walls of dark-coloured stone also comprise the surrounding cave-end here. Upon the ground lie fragments of shale-like rock, scattered throughout piles of discarded pieces of bone. What appears to have been a failed attempt at making crude weaponry out of bone and stone now serves as litter upon the ground.
119124: Here, the cold stone walls that largely make up these dark, damp tunnels turns northward, where the darkness seems to swell into an opening; no sounds or faint glistens of sharp rock can be seen in that direction, as is present to the east and south.
119125: Sloping upwards, the ground here becomes ever-scattered with broken sheets of rock, amongst which several small bones are mixed. As the hard, rocky floor rises, so the space between the jagged walls become smaller, making for uneasy travels as the elevation rises. The tunnel bends in from the south, where very little can be seen in the engulfing darkness that seems to thicken with distance in that direction.
119126: A hungry-looking giant lizard is slithering towards you (hidden).

Rising from below and to the south, the rocky floor, littered with stones and the random bones of small creatures, levels out and begins to swing eastward. While the tunnel walls are much more narrow as it follows the descent, they begin to widen out the further east one travels. Several rocky protrusions thrust out from the cave walls, threatening any whom pass close to them.
119127: Descending from above, the stone and bone-laden tunnel floor evens out momentarily before turning westward, where the view yields nothing but the awaiting darkness. Toward the west the tunnel expands outwards, jagged fingers of rock protruding from the stone walls await any unaware travellers.
119128: Ascending from below, the stone and bone-laden tunnel floor evens out momentarily, before splitting toward the north and south where the view yields nothing but the awaiting darkness. Small droplets of water drip from the damp ceiling above, forming a small puddle from which runs a tiny stream downwards, flanking the rocky descent to one side.
119129: The sound of dripping water is ever-present here, where moisture can be seen pooling upon the ceiling before dripping into the puddle-covered stone floor below. From these puddles, small streams constantly flow downward where the walls of rock disappear under a cold, dark waterline.
119130: A hungry-looking giant lizard is slithering towards you (hidden).

Dripping water and bat droppings merge here to coat a treacherous, slippery, sloping tunnel. The water has no apparent source besides the ceiling above, from which it slowly accumulates to fall noiselessly on the guano-softened ground. The tunnel opens up into a broader cavern to the north and steepens further to the south.
119131: Unbearably cold water entirely fills this passageway. The channel flows slowly southward, where it broadens into a larger chamber. The flow is fed by several narrow cracks up and to the north. One of the cracks broadens into an open air tunnel above.
119132:
A long slender eel glides along the water, its body coiled to strike.
A long slender eel glides along the water, its body coiled to strike.
A large pale fish with bulbous eyes is swimming here.
A large pale fish with bulbous eyes is swimming here.

Icy water fills a large chamber floor-to-ceiling. A slow current, entering from a channel to the north and exiting through several cracks to the south, gives the water an even chillier and more dangerous aspect, and no creature not born to the cold could abide here for very long. Bobbing slabs of ice at the surface of the water reveal that there is open air above.
119133:
A fierce bat is here, lusting for your blood.
A fierce bat is here, lusting for your blood.
A huge bat is here, emitting piercing squeaks.

The strong presence of bats is unmistakable as great mounds of guano and its accompanying odour fill this expansive cavern. Far above, a broad crack in the mountainside shows their path of ingress and egress. The floor of the cavern is fairly level, though mounded here and there with waste. The cave narrows to a tunnel to the south, and a narrow crack leads downward further into the mountain.
119134: The rock of this chamber is oddly smooth, rising upward like a bowl from a shallow depression in its centre. A remarkably straight and level tunnel cuts northward through a door bordered with weathered runes. Mounds of guano pile beneath a narrow crack in the otherwise polished ceiling, coating a pile of rubble that rises up to the crack to create an unintended exit from this room.
119135: A steep tunnel descends from the west to join a larger north-south passage. Regularly spaced steps lead upward, shallow enough to befit the strides of dwarves. The floor and walls are smooth and polished, yet dusty with disuse. However, a few footprints of varying apparent age indicate these tunnels have not been completely abandoned.
119136: A passageway leading in from the south meets a winding stone staircase that descends steeply northward. The rough, natural ceiling suggests the builders simply took advantage of a natural opening in the rock. In several places along the stairs, deep gouges indicate exploratory mines of ore veins that apparently proved to be a disappointment.
119137: While the tunnel runs almost perfectly straight from this point eastwards, its floor slopes with frequent changes, and even slight reversals of the grade to a general trend of a westward descent. The walls of this sloped tunnel are made of natural rock formations.
119138: There is a sense that this tunnel continues for an eternity in both the east and west directions. The walls are made of natural rock with some thin fractures separating the geologic formation now and then. The floor is covered with layers of dust, concealing shards of crushed rock.
119139:
A desiccated goblin corpse lies here.
A bronze lever sits on a raised dais of polished stone.

The tunnel extends to the west, nearly ten feet high and widest in the middle, before terminating at two massive bronze doors that have fallen. A gaping hole can be seen where the gates used to sit. The northern side of the tunnel ends in another two massive bronze gates that have been set into the wall of smooth polished white rock.
119140:
A bronze lever sits on a raised dais of polished stone.
A crazed dwarf is here, drooling down his beard.

A large hallway artificially created by master craftsmen extends to the south toward a wall. The northern side of the hallway is caved in and rubble now blocks it completely. To the eastern side of the hallway there is the entrance to what seems to be a larger hall.
119141: A rusty pickaxe with a broken handle lies discarded here.

A long, steep staircase zigzags downward along the floor of a natural opening in the rock, following the slanting cavern as it bends eastward at the bottom. The cadence of the steps appears best suited for dwarf legs, though the clearance above the staircase would admit a much larger creature. Broken picks and shovels rest inside shallow delvings along the northern wall, none of which seems to have been particularly fruitful.
119142: A long stone staircase zigzags its way along the natural contours of a vast cavern descending from southwest to the north. The stairs consequently both rise and fall with steep undulations in the cavern floor. While the top of the cavern is in most places no more than twenty feet above the floor, several great gaps extend to distances unfathomable high above.
119143:
A giant, strange looking green fungus is here, ready to devour you in seconds.
A huge black fungus is here, exuding a foul stench.

Many stone tables fill a large, square feasting hall delved into the rock. Though all is covered in dust, a great degree of care and art is evident in its construction, from intricate bas reliefs of dwarf feasts and battles along the walls to elaborate patterns carved into the tables themselves. To the north, a passageway descends through the ruins of a stone gate. A long, winding staircase ascends into a vast cavern to the south.
119144: A large, dusty alcove sits in a wall, smelling of soot.

The ruined remnants of a forge line the eastern wall of this large, square chamber. The bottom half of a massive broken cogwheel rests in a long, narrow sluice that vanishes beneath a pile of rubble to the north. The shattered pieces of the forge itself would be scarcely recognisable except for the surprisingly intact bellows nearby. The only anvils that remain are broken beyond repair. A vast arcade extends westward from this chamber, and an ornate stone stairway runs upward and to the south.
119145: Water drips through numerous cracks in the ceilings and walls of this chamber, forming runnels that merge to flow down a set of steps leading to an underground river below. Stalactites in plenty hang from the ceiling, dripping frequently to add their contributions to the stream. A squared passage rises upward to the south.
119146:
A small, scrawny goblin skulks about.
A strong, heavy-set goblin glares blankly ahead.
A strong, heavy-set goblin glares blankly ahead.

An arched hall of magnificently carved obsidian ends abruptly at a great collapse along the western wall. Fine debris spreads away from the rubble, covering the broad, meticulously smooth floor. Efforts to break through the rubble appear to have ended in failure, a story told by crushed remains of both dwarves and goblins.
119147: Emerging from a grey rockface to the south through a dark opening worn smooth by untold aeons of wear, a swift and icy river flows through the wide, open tunnel. The strong current carries from south to north in a silent race to unknown destinations. A rough stairway has been cut into the bare slate on the eastern rockwall.
119150: Dark, grey waters swirl and eddy here, fed by the current to the west. A gentle suction pulls the dark water downward in an unstable spiral to an underground chamber from which a faint glimmer can be seen. Along the edge of the eddy, a crude path has been chiselled, winding upward to a dark room.
119151: A small natural stair leads up into this noisy grotto. The source of the noise is a a swift subterranean river that can be seen below; its dark grey waters swirling, rushing, and clamouring. The grotto is incredibly wet with moisture dripping from the ceiling and misting up from the rushing river current.
119152: The bottom of the chamber is covered with mud and silt.

The chilly and murky water in this chamber makes it difficult to see more than a few feet in any direction. Coating the floor is a thick layer of soft, dark brown sediment. Occasionally, a glimmer shines through the murk.
119153: There is a lot of snow on the ground.

A narrow mountain trail is running along the slope of the Caradhras, winding between the chasms and rocks and taking sharp turns every now and then. To the east, the red rock of the Caradhras is rising steeply to the heights. The path is surely not often walked upon, covered with debris and loose rocks, obviously fallen from the higher mountains.
119154: There is a lot of snow on the ground.

The winding trail running from the east takes a sharp turn around the high rock and seems suddenly to stop just a short distance north of here. To the west you can descend the mountain side, which does not seem to offer much safety but you should still be climbable with caution.
119155: There is a lot of snow on the ground.

The snow-capped peaks of the Misty Mountains surround you from all sides. Far at the horizon to the west, the green lands of Hollin lie, barely visible at the distance. Immediately to the east, a narrow path is winding between the rocks.
119156: There is a lot of snow on the ground.

The path running from the south seems to stop here. The wind is howling over the deserted land and finding a safe foothold becomes increasingly difficult. Near to the east, a wide ravine opens between the mountain top. Some low grass seems to be growing there.
119157: There is a lot of snow on the ground.

Mountain peaks rise majestically on all sides of this secluded ravine. A cool breeze rustles the grasses on the ground. More mountains lie immediately to the north and west while a dark cave opening can be seen to the east.
119158: A huge white bear is here, glaring fiercely at you.

A narrow opening at your west extends to an ample natural cave. The air is slightly warmer here than outside and a strong smell of animals permeates the room. Now and then the howling wind lashes in from the cave mouth, but otherwise it is pretty quiet. A few bones are lying all around on the cave floor.
119159:
There is a lot of snow on the ground.
Some orange-red blossoms grow amid grey-green foliage.

The Misty Mountains stretch far and wide all around you. As you move up the slope, the air becomes increasingly thin, making your breathing a laborous task. To the west, the ground gets lower while a wide open ravine opens up in the south. The Redhorn rises to the sky in the east.
119160: The mountains are rising sharply towards east here and, in a short distance, seem too steep to climb. Cold and strong wind is making it hard to walk and you have to concentrate on every step you take. Both north and south of you, the mountains rise almost straight into the sky, to the east the Caradhras is towering above the peaks of lesser mountains.
119161: Mountains, more mountains as far as your eyes can see. The stone ground is bare, without any vegetation. Rocks are lying loosely all around, ready to scatter away as soon as your feet touch them. North of here, a deep chasm blocks the way while to the west the rising ground is too steep to pass.
119162: The mountains slope slightly downward to the west. In this direction a majestic view over the lower peaks of the Misties opens, and even away farther, the rolling ground of Hollin can be seen. It might be a good idea to proceed with caution to avoid the chasms hidden below the snow.
119163: A small, scrawny goblin skulks about.

A small, grubby room is pontooned to the side of the bridge. The floor is a bit unsteady as it rises and falls in accordance with the river's mood. Mud has been repeatedly tramped in here, and the wood planks in the walls are largely warped and discoloured.
119164: A distinct trail can be seen leading towards what appears to be a dilapidated old farm to the south. Despite the fact that the property appears to be quite large, the farm's inhabitants long ago abandoned it and allowed it to collapse gradually. The trail ends at a high wooden fence enclosing the farm, with a wooden gate blocking the entrance.
119165: A goblin raider shrieks as it searches for something to maim.

To the south is an old structure with a collapsed straw roof, and a chimney that protrudes into the sky. Grass and ivy are gradually engulfing its crumbling walls. A big, abandoned barn made of medium-sized timbers is visible to the west and a small crudely constructed stable is to the east.
119166: With just a hitching post and a wooden roof to shield the animals from the elements, the stable in this area is fairly spartanly built. The weight of the animals has caused the clay floor to become harder. The only exit is to the west, leading back toward the gates.
119167:
A large cockroach is crawling on the floor.
A starving cow stands here, looking for a patch of grass.

As a result of time and weather, the walls now clearly show the decaying processes. The barn gate swings back and forth with wind gusts. Although the barn door is securely closed by a sturdy chain wrapped around the gate's frame and an iron lock.
119168:
A small oaken table has been set here.
On the ground, there are two straw pallets.
A goblin raider shrieks as it searches for something to maim.
A goblin raider shrieks as it searches for something to maim.

The old farm ruin looks to have deteriorated gradually over time. The building's straw roof portion fell in a little corner, leaving that area exposed to the elements, but its stone walls are still standing. A section of the room with a few straw-pellets appear to be utilized as a sleeping place, and the furniture appears to have been used recently.
119169:
An old, strong cave troll is standing here.
A stone troll is standing here, scowling about.
A stone troll is standing here, scowling about.

A strong smell of decomposition fills this cavern. The origin of the smell is probably the large pile of garbage lying in one corner. It has been left unattended over time and none can tell of what it is comprised. Small patches of moss grow upon the walls, and lichen is suspended from the ceiling. The cavern opens up to the south.
119170:
A nasty troll female crouches here, with a feral look in her eyes.
A nasty troll female crouches here, with a feral look in her eyes.
A large mean-looking troll is here.

A small cavern has been dug out here by crude hands. The area seems mainly to be used as a sleeping room for the inhabitants of the cave system. Around the centre of the room can be seen a number of huge beds made of dried grass. The earthen walls are moist, and composed of a red limestone.
119171:
An old, strong cave troll is standing here.
A stone troll stands here scratching at something embedded in his head.

A moist cavern extends under the spurs of the Misty Mountains. It has been enlarged by crude hands not caring if the walls are rough or smooth. Small rivulets of water dripping down the walls gather in the shallows of the ground forming small bodies of water. The still air smells of decomposition. No natural light source can be found.
119172:
An infant troll, baring its teeth, snarls here.
An infant troll, baring its teeth, snarls here.
An infant troll, baring its teeth, snarls here.
An infant troll, baring its teeth, snarls here.
An infant troll, baring its teeth, snarls here.
An infant troll, baring its teeth, snarls here.

This ground in this part of the cave is churned up mud, both a mixture of water leaking out from under the heavy door to the north, and acrid troll urine from the nests that seem to have been made for the very youngest of the troll's young. Disgusting piles of uncured hides, bones and even humanoid scalps plus grass and leaves make up these nests.
119173:
A dwarven peasant stares in insane horror.
A large troll is ready to butcher another prisoner.
A weary woman stands here, looking miserable.

This damp room is where the trolls keep their prisoners, or future meals, for they are really one and the same. Cold water drips from the roof, and flows in tiny rivulets down the wall, offering the only liquid these unfortunate wretches get before their terrible demise. A dark, heavy door to the south serves to keep the prisoners contained within this dank, dismal place.
119174: Ancient boulders rest upon an area of cracked, rocky ground that has almost no visible topsoil to sustain life. And yet among the rocks grows a proliferation of low bushes, their naked branches tangled and contorted by the prevailing winds. Dry, yellow grasses also to sprout from many cracks in the ground. To the west, the last remains of an ancient roadway cut across the land.
119175: The plains rise gradually to the south as they start their long approach toward a distant mountain spur. The ground underfoot is parched and cracked. A scant covering of yellow-brown grasses pokes up here and there, clinging feebly to life. A thick hedge has growth to the south making travel in that direction difficult.
119176: A woody evergreen plant grows here, with many stems reaching upward.

This is an area of transition where broken ground, with only a thin covering of yellow-brown grasses, gives way to dense thickets of dry, twisted shrubs. Though plainly struggling to hang on to life in this harsh environment, the bushes nevertheless constitute a dense thicket that nestles in the shelter at the foot of the hills to the east, and blocks travel up their slopes.
119177: A big cavebear is padding around here.

This cramped den extends back five or so yards before terminating. Roots fall from the ceiling of the den and bits of fur can be seen strewn across the ground. Something large has made its home here and bits of bedding made up of leaves, grass, and bark have been carefully placed at the end of the den.
119178: Shadows draping from the enormous pillars in this room hint at the former grandeur before the northern and western side partly collapsed. Now this part of the room is covered with rubble and the walls are partly covered in mould. In the centre of the room, stairs vanish into the floor leading deeper underground.
119179:
The corpse of a stone statue is lying here.
The corpse of a stone statue is lying here.
The corpse of a guardian stone beast is lying here.

A narrow stairway made of simple stone descends deeper under the ground toward the east. The stairs and walls are covered with small cracks. Some chunks of rock and smaller pebbles make it hard to actually move on the stairs.
119180:
A splintered piece of a broken shield is on the ground. (blue aura).
A silver lever sits on a raised dais of polished stone.

The floor and walls of this chamber are made of polished stone. On the west side of the chamber there are quite some chunks of rocks and rubble before a narrow stairway that leads out of the chamber. The walls have some cracks which are also the source of some moisture making it possible for mould to grow and cover most of the room.
119181:
The corpse of a dwarven statue is lying here.
The corpse of a dwarven statue is lying here.
A stone sarcophagus lies on the floor.

The entire tomb is covered in slime and mould, growing especially thick on the wet walls. A sarcophagus stands on a small pedestal in the centre of the room. Beside the sarcophagus a mould covered statue of a female scholar rests in a thinking pose.
119182:
A stone sarcophagus lies on the floor.
A tall statue of a dwarf, dressed in metal armour, stands here.
A tall statue of a dwarf, dressed in metal armour, stands here.

A large sarcophagus made of stone is standing on the floor in the middle of the room. Behind the sarcophagus toward the wall stands a statue of a male dwarven priest. The walls and ceiling behind the statue are covered with smaller cracks and the floor is overcast with rock pebbles.
119183: A rusty pickaxe with a broken handle lies discarded here.

At the northern side of this alcove there is the bottom end of a large and steep chute which seems to be impossible to ascend. The alcove itself is unadorned and seems to have the practical purpose to storage materials that are transported with the chute. The western side of the alcove is covered with fungi.
119184:
The remains of a giant green fungus lie here in a heap of rotting compost.
The remains of a giant green fungus lie here in a heap of rotting compost.
A small fungi-covered basin is here, filled with clear water.

A large hallway artificially created by master craftsmen extends to the north. The southern side of the hallway is caved in from the western side and the hallway is now blocked by earth and rubble. Between the rubble some water seems to be flowing out of the western wall into a small natural basin. Everything around that basin is covered by mould including the eastern wall.
119185: A divergence in the masterfully crafted hallway ascends to a very large stone hall to the east. The hallway continues from south to north while the northern side features a simple mechanism to block off the hallway with a heavy slab.
119186: This astonishing stone hall features marble floors and stunning ornamentation. This room is at least a hundred feet high and the most distinct feature is a huge dwarven statue standing next to the eastern wall. Between the statue's legs sits an entrance to what might be a tomb. A wooden door is set within the stone wall to the north, and a chute descends rapidly to the south.
119187: Towering above is a huge dwarven statue, its legs to the south and to the north forming a gangway. The gangway is made of simple yet beautiful black stone leading from the stone hall to the west to a stairway east, which seems to lead deeper under the ground.
119188: A large hallway created by master craftsmen extends from south to north. The floor is laid out with ornate stone tiles, and the walls are made of smooth polished rock. Toward the southern side there is a mechanism to block off the hallway with a huge slab.
119189: A large hall with walls made out of stone blocks connects a purpose-built tunnel to the north with a masterfully crafted hallway to the south. To the east two dwarven statues crafted out of black stone stand tall crossing their hammers. Between them there is an entrance leading deeper in what appears to be an old tomb.
119190: The walls of this tunnel are formed of robust stone blocks. However, to the north a cave-in makes further passage impossible. It seems the tunnel was used to haul heavy materials toward the south. To the east the cave-in left a big hole in the wall leading into darkness. To the south the tunnel connects with a large hall. The sound of water can be heard from a large hole in the ground.
119191:
A huge bat is here, emitting piercing squeaks.
A huge bat is here, emitting piercing squeaks.
A huge bat is here, emitting piercing squeaks.

A huge natural cavern extends to the north while to the west there is a big hole leading to what seems to be an artificial tunnel which was exposed after a cave-in. Guano covers the floor suggesting bats living inside the cavern.
119192: Towering above are two dwarven statues, one to the south and the other to the north. To the east is a passage leading to a stairway what seems to be a tomb. The passage is mosaicked with small polished stones creating a beautiful pattern leading toward the stairway.
119193:
The corpse of a stone statue is lying here.
The corpse of a stone statue is lying here.
The corpse of a guardian stone beast is lying here.

The stairway made of white marble stone descends deeper under the ground toward the east. The walls are mosaicked with small polished stones creating a beautiful pattern. On the top of the stairs there is a passage leading into a larger hall.
119194:
A delicate pendant wrought of bronze lies on the ground.
A butcher knife is lying here.
A fine pair of greaves are lying here.
A ring with a translucent blue gem has been left here.
A stone tablet lies here, covered in dwarven runes.
A pair of metal boots are standing here.
A dagger lies on the ground.
A large, closed face helm lies on the ground.
A fine pair of chain mail leggings are lying here.
A sparkling golden necklace has been left here.
There are six skeletons here.
There are two fine chain mail coifs here.
A shortsword is on the ground.
There are two pairs of greaves here.
A fine chain mail hauberk is on the ground.
An exquisite golden cup lies here.
There are two bars of gold here.
A handaxe has been left on the ground.
A pair of metal vambraces lies here.
A shiny gold ring has been abandoned here.
A fine pair of chain mail gloves are lying here.
A hooded brass lantern has been left here.
A metal helmet is on the ground.
A finely carved comb, inlaid with gold, has been carelessly abandoned here.
A silver wedding ring lies here.
A fine pair of chain mail sleeves lies here.
A pair of metal gauntlets are lying here.
A golden lever sits on a raised dais of polished stone.

The white walls of this antechamber give it a simple yet beautiful look. The only way out of the chamber seems to be toward the west where a stairway ascends. The walls of the antechamber are not decorated in any way and only its architectural features give a feeling for the size of this chamber.
119195:
The corpse of a dwarven statue is lying here.
The corpse of a dwarven statue is lying here.
A stone sarcophagus lies on the floor.

A large stone sarcophagus is standing on the floor in the middle of the alcove. Behind the sarcophagus toward the wall of the alcove is a white statue of a male dwarven warden. The walls behind the statue are covered with decayed tapestries.
119196:
The corpse of a dwarven statue is lying here.
The corpse of a dwarven statue is lying here.
A stone sarcophagus lies on the floor.

A black stone statue of a female dwarven overseer with a hammer in hands stands infront of a sarcophagus. The stone walls are decorated with small mosaics made of different metals giving the alcove a very elegant design. The only visible exit out of this alcove is to the north.
119197: Behind a wooden door there is a small room which seems to be a storage. Although the room is mostly empty now, it was probably used to store materials and tools a very long time ago. Now the only thing left here is a lot of dust on the floor.
119199: A small alcove has been skilfully carved into the stone. A decorated fountain made of quartz stone stands at the southern side of the alcove. Above the fountain the face of a dwarf is chiselled into the stone. The mouth of the stone face has a little hole which seems to have been the source of water for the fountain which is now totally dry.
119200:
The corpse of a stone statue is lying here.
The corpse of a stone statue is lying here.
The corpse of a guardian stone beast is lying here.
The shadow of a guardian stone beast is floating here.

The staircase, made of polished marble stone, spirals deeper under the ground. The colour of the walls and stairs change between white and black while a single line of golden ornamentation helps with the general sense of direction.
119201: The floor and walls of this tomb are made of marble stone with thin golden ornaments. The most distinct feature of the room are the colours of the floor and walls which are black to the northern side and white to the south. In the centre of the walls there are entrances leading deeper into the tomb.
119202:
The corpse of a dwarven statue is lying here.
The corpse of a dwarven statue is lying here.
A stone sarcophagus lies on the floor.

A large sarcophagus made of black metal is standing on the floor in the middle of the room. Behind the sarcophagus toward the wall of the alcove stands a black statue of a male dwarven lord. The walls behind the statue are covered with thin golden ornaments giving the room a very elegant feeling.
119203:
The corpse of a dwarven statue is lying here.
The corpse of a dwarven statue is lying here.
A stone sarcophagus lies on the floor.

A sarcophagus made of silvery white metal is standing on the floor at the back of the room. The white marble statue of a fierce dwarven lady stands in the centre of the tomb, arms crossed. The walls behind the statue are neatly embellished with golden ornaments.
119205: A huge stone slab lies here, its surface etched with markings.

A small terrace stands out like an island in a sea of darkness that makes up this pit. Peering into the dark depths, a faint glow of red can be seen. A lengthy stone slab, scorched black from the heat and fumes that rise from below, gives passage from the terrace to a tunnel in the west. A cold draft can be felt to the east.
119207: The corpse of a giant lizard is lying here.

A dim red light creeps out from cracks in the floor far below; heat radiating like an oven. The hazy glow flows past the rocks, casting shadows that dance and shiver on the walls in a haze. A bubbling and popping sound joins the show, acting as music in the darkness.
119208: The walls of this area are made of what appears to be pure obsidian. They gleam in the smallest of light, capturing it in their smoky crystals. The rocks on the floor are also made of obsidian, their edges jagged and sharp as razors.
119209: A lake of darkness extends off to the side of this cave. A stone ledge borders the bottomless hole, winding its path into the next cavern. The darkness inside the abyss is thick and impossible to penetrate with any amount of light. A cold draft can be felt leading down from further up in the chamber.
119210:
Little parts of a broken weapon are lying on the ground.
A splintered piece of a broken shield is on the ground. (blue aura).
A giant rat patters against you, squeaking maliciously.

Heaps of useless junk are piled here and there, booty after a troll's heart. The cave is quite dirty with objects lying about seemingly without rhyme or reason. The only clear walkway is an aisle down the centre of the hoard.
119211:
A sturdy crate made of nailed wooden planks sits on the floor.
A young troll is here digging around for food.
A young troll is here digging around for food.
A stone troll mother is here, trying to keep her family safe.
A small black vicious rat squeaks at you for disturbing it.
A pale stone troll walks around here, looking for a fight.

Tall, rough walls of granite flank the centre of this cavern. The ceiling is high above with long, needle-like stalactites reaching down. One particularly large stalactite stretches all the way from the ceiling to the floor, acting like a great pillar in the centre of the cave.
119212: A small circular cavern is here, ringed with three large pillars. The pillars stand like trees that have grown from the stone ground itself. Each stone has some sort of painting drawn on it. The pillars are arranged equidistant from each other forming a large triangle. On the ceiling, a great, black, lidless eye stares down.
119213:
An ornate elven chest, embellished with golden wood, has been left here.
A natural throne sits atop a dais of black rock.
A huge stone troll looms overhead, ready to crush your body.
A huge stone troll looms overhead, ready to crush your body.
A stone troll mother, ancient and gnarled, rises from her throne.
A sturdy pack horse is standing here.

Huge, troll-shaped pillars the size of small towers support the cave ceiling upon their sloping shoulders. In the centre of the cavern stands a throne that seems to have been naturally-formed from the very stones themselves. The throne sits atop a dais of black rock that protrudes from the cavern floor.
119214: A long black rock cuts through the chamber, dividing most of it in two. The walls curve up to the ceiling and down the other side in an almost perfect half moon. The floor is composed of ground-up obsidian and the temperature here is very chilly. A cold draft can be felt coming in from somewhere above.
119216: A small cleft in the mountainside offers protection from the elements. High in the mountains, not much can be seen on the slopes other than ice and stone. A large protruding rock juts out of the back wall of the alcove. The back of the alcove is strangely devoid of snow and ice.
119217: A narrow gap snakes its way through the mountains. There seems to be a faint path which has been traced along the low slopes offering a way forward. Large boulders have come to rest here, fallen from untold heights. The wind howls through the gap.
119218: The natural stone walls of this low gorge are glazed in ice and locked in permafrost. What perhaps was once a stream is now a frozen road of ice swishing through the gorge. The snow on the ground is dotted with small holes.
119219: Two tall mountains stand like impossibly tall spires flanking the area. Underfoot a deep snowdrift covers the ground and no sort of living plant life can be seen. However, some sort of path, perhaps an animal track, seems to have been patted into the snow.
119220: A mixture of dirt and snow covers the hard ground. The slopes are not too steep here but higher up the mountains it's clear that the incline grows significantly. A few boulders and stones which line the mountains offer some hand-holds if necessary.
119221: High in the sky, the world stretches out in all directions. The snow-clad mountain tops, like white soldiers in formation, march on for leagues. Far in the distance, the even greater heights of Caradhras can be seen. The wind is cold and unforgiving.
119222: View of the surrounding area is somewhat blocked by the rest of the mountain ridge that is not scalable. This spot does offer some protection from the wind, but slanted footing is the cost. The wind here is less harsh as the brunt of it is shielded by the ridge.
119223: A pair of mountains loom into the sky. Their icy stone slopes appear smooth and featureless while at the crests, a circular cap of snow has come to rest. They stand tall and proud, impervious to the passage of time. The snow becomes increasingly deep to the west, having become caught between the two mountains.
119224: This deep ravine between the mountain slopes acts as a trough, catching the endless amount of snow that slides down the slopes. The walls of the ravine are steep and made of stone that is locked in permafrost. Any small sound creates a magnifying echo as it bounces between the cliff-like walls.
119225: The mountains tower on either side, but here a small gap between them lies. The lofty ridges up above make sharp outlines against the sky. Though lower in altitude than the peaks surrounding this location, the snow is still plentiful.
119226: A huge white bear is here snuffling about for food.

Like a giant half moon, the top of this mountain drops off into sheer cliffs on one side. Ice has formed along the ridge making things smooth and slippery. A lone tree stands near the top completely devoid of all greenery. The tree has become completely frozen still and is as hard as a rock.
119227: Snow, stone, and ice mingle together creating what appears to be a landslide frozen in time. Debris can be spotted hidden in the ice and boulders of considerable size seem to have been swept along as well. The air here is motionless, almost as if holding its breath.
119228: A large marmot is here, scurrying in between the rocks.

This small valley hiding in the Misty Mountains offers a welcome respite from the steep slopes all around. Bits of grass grow here and there on the valley floor, mixed with stones and other rubble that has tumbled down from above. The air here is calm, with almost no wind, and is shielded by the mountain wall.
119229: This valley is sandwiched between the ever climbing mountains. The valley floor is covered in a thick layer of white snow. Though the area is mostly quiet, when a sound occurs it is magnified and echoes throughout the landscape.
119230: The mountain is very steep and slanted here. Jagged rocks and heavy stones lose their grip and slide down the mountainside at the slightest disturbance. The clattering noise of their fall echoes in the mountains, caught and carried by the wind.
119231: Two massive boulders stand here, looming overhead like the great snow giants of tales. The boulders provide cover from the sun but the surrounding area is mostly composed of ice save for slick patches of stone that appear suddenly in the most unpredictable places. The air is still, but the frost in it lingers.
119232: The corpse of a female humanoid lies frozen on the ground.

Shimmering and beautiful, some crystals of ice hang precariously from the ceiling; poised at any moment to crash to the ground. Icy mists lie like a thick blanket over the ground. The occasional wailing of wind can just be heard tearing over some opening somewhere in the surrounding caverns echoing off the walls. A few large stones, which must have fallen from the walls long ago, now lie on the ground covered in razorlike crystal ice structures.
119233: Razor-sharp shards of ice shoot up from the floor and climb up the walls. A frosty mist hangs over the floor, seemingly coming from cracks in the frozen walls. The air is perfectly still, as if holding its breath in anticipation of something.
119234: Walls of chipped ice tower over the area. The ice is thick, with signs of haphazard nicks and chips dotting the bottom. Clouds of vapor puff out of the ground, covering the area in a thin mist. Failed attempts to scale the wall can be seen, with frozen remains littering the floor.
119235: The corpse of a burly snow giant is lying here.

The hard stone floor of this cavern is slick with ice. A long crack travels along the walls circling the chamber. The cave's ceiling is quite lofty with echoes getting lost in the darkness above. A layer of frost covers the stone surfaces.
119236:
The corpse of a burly snow giant is lying here.
The corpse of a massive snow giant is lying here.
The half-eaten corpse of a mountain ibex is lying here.
