Though this cave is amply proportioned, it was made to seem smaller by the two large stone platforms that occupy opposing walls. Each is over ten feet long, and stands some five feet above the cave floor. It is obvious that they were hewn from the chilly stone for some purpose, but what that might be would seem unclear without considering the large, ragged remnants and poorly tanned skins that cover each.
119237: Grey stones lie scattered all about the floor of this cavern. The centre of the room is dominated by a single great rock with chisseled carvings that have been cut into its face. The area surrouding the rock has been cleared of all rubble to allow the carvings to be easily viewed.
119238: A frozen altar stands in the centre of the room upon a dais of black obsidian. Above the altar, a tall arch made of curved ice, so smooth that it could be mistaken for glass, stands beautiful. Some bones and frozen furs have been placed here as offerings to whatever deity the snow giants observe.
119239:
The corpse of a burly snow giant is lying here.
The corpse of a massive snow giant is lying here.

The walls of the chamber are made of frosted ice, forming an almost perfect circle as they wrap around the chamber. Pillars of ice reach up from the ground supporting the ceiling like trees of glass. Inside the pillars stand enormous bodies of giants, their faces glaring out but frozen in an icy eternal sleep. This isn't a cave, it's a tomb.
119240:
Traces of rich red tones form the aura of this place.
The corpse of a massive snow giant is lying here.
The corpse of Gukk the snow giant is lying here.
The corpse of a burly snow giant is lying here.

Huge stalactites, made from pure ice, hang from the ceiling and stick out from the walls like long knives. Several of the stalactites are missing, leaving only their stumps behind, as if someone has ripped them from where they previously hung. The walls of this chamber are made of stone but have long since become encased within thick sheets of ice.
119241:
The corpse of a burly snow giant is lying here.
The corpse of a massive snow giant is lying here.

A glistening sheet of ice blankets what was at one point a pond in the cave. Now the ice is so thick and smooth it is like polished glass, reflecting any light it catches. There are cracks snaking their way all through the walls creating many shapes. A hole in the wall opens up to the sky.
119242: The corpse of a massive snow giant is lying here.

A thin, serpentine path snakes through the ice, with sharp icicles stabbing through the walls. A thin path can be seen where countless footsteps have worn the ice down to the shards of rock. The view of the ceiling is blocked by the arching ice formations, almost as if the ice was the hand of a frozen giant.
119243:
An ornate elven chest, embellished with golden wood, has been left here.
The immense half-eaten corpse of a huge stone troll is hanging here on a hook.

Two tall pillars of stone stand at the back of the hall with a bear skin stretched taut between them. A large wooden club lies propped up against one of the pillars. Several large boulders with flattened tops are arranged in a circle around the room.
119244: The chamber has been hewn from the mountain by living hands judging from the smooth walls covered in frost. The floor is hard and frigid to the feet. Above, pillars of ice descend from the ceiling making contact with the floor and taking root. The walls are more rock here and show their age with visible lines of sediment slashing across them.
119245: What appears to have been at first a planned extension of the tunnel is now blocked completely with collapsed snow. The walls of this snowy crawlspace have been almost completely buried by blocks of ice and snow which have fallen and been crushed down by the weight of the glacier above.
119246: A rope bridge spans the distance across a gap between two mountain ridges. The bridge dances in the wind, the ropes holding it together more like bars of solid ice. The distance between the two peaks is vast but nothing compared to the dizzying fall to the ground below.
119247: The sounds of nature echo about this stone-clad area, muffled only slightly by the copious amounts of snow. What appears to have once been a small pond lies in the centre of a flat part of the mountain slope but it has long frozen over.
119248: Far up above, tall mountain peaks pierce the sky, their silhouettes like white-tipped arrow heads. The slopes from the mountains slant sharply downwards. Large boulders are dotted here and there in the white snow like speckles on marble.
119249: A huge rock juts out of the side of the mountain extending into nothingness. The ground is a dizzying distance below and the view offered by this proud perch is unmatched. The wind howls and moans around the rock almost in protest of this scar drawn across the sky.
119250: A crude shaft has been dug here which seems to be a very old mining operation. Heavy timbers support the walls and ceiling at regular intervals, giving off a heavy smell of pine tar. The shaft generally runs from west to east, narrowing the deeper it gets. Fissures in the stone create intricate patterns of smaller cracks crisscrossing larger cracks of varying sizes.
119251: A narrow mining shaft winds its way through the stone here. Severe cave-ins show instability in the mining shaft. Several marble stone blocks indicate there was some artificial structure to the south, however rubble now completely blocks it and makes further passage impossible. The eastern wall looks quite unstable with lots of rubble and natural stone blocks in that direction.
119252:
A small, scrawny goblin skulks about.
A small, scrawny goblin skulks about.
A small, scrawny goblin skulks about.

This large cavern branches off to the north, south, and east. The stone floor shows the wear and tear of many goblin claws. On the western wall is inset the goblin equivalent of a bulletin board. Presumably, it is used to post edicts from the Chief, patrol duties, shift changes and the latest enemies killed - of which there are none at the moment.
119253: Harshly chopped slag forms a round tunnel through the deep. Grey stone is rough to the touch and shows scores from the wickedly tough tool that made the work. The air is thick with moisture, and covers all with a cold, damp sweat. Under foot, the stone has been made flat and allows for travel of two wide.
119254: Strong and proficient work has made a straight, rough tunnel through the hard granite. The ceiling here is low and drips rust-coloured water in echoing splashes. The walls are dark grey, interworked with shiny, white courses and small green spots.
119255: A dwarf high tunnel runs through here, straight and rough. The stone walls are damp, dripping slowly from the moisture in the air of the deep underground, and shine black. Nary a sound can be heard in the lifeless dark, the ground being smooth, flat shale.
119256: A small black vicious rat squeaks at you for disturbing it.

An adeptly mined tunnel has been carved through dirt and rocks deep underground. The air is loamy and wet, yet more clay smelling than dirt. The tunnel is straight and sturdy, and the ground is packed hard with crushed, yellow stone.
119261: A small black vicious rat squeaks at you for disturbing it.

A tunnel ends in a dark, cramped cavern, the walls natural and pitted. The floor and ceiling are crammed with small, shiny stalagmites and stalactites, some of which reach from top to bottom. The stone is black and ancient, covered in wet mire and slick to the touch.
119268: Crude chiselling and chipping have resulted in jagged and craggy walls framing this passageway. The only smooth thing here is the hard stone floor showing the wear of much traffic over many years. Passages lead north, south, and west.
119269: Several heads, most of them old and little more than bones, adorn the walls of this long, low-ceilinged tunnel. Several torches, long burnt out, are mounted alongside the skulls and must have given a ghastly atmosphere to the tunnel when lit. Most of the heads are human or display the nasty fangs of orc or goblin.
119270: The western wall of this cave is one of many goblin worksites scattered throughout the caverns. Recent excavations show where the goblins have dug for ore or gemstones. The walls are shored up by uneven, roughly hewn timber that looks anything but stable.
119271: The passageway bends from north to east with a ceiling low enough to make a cave troll stoop. Running through the dark, craggy stone of the walls are veins of glossy, black rock with corners and edges deadly sharp to the touch.
119272: In this well-lit and spacious cavern, a huge wooden desk dominates with authority. Functioning as a guardpost before a wide stairwell set in the eastern wall, no one gets by without the guards say so. On either side of the stairway are leering goblin heads of stone, carved to instil fear in the lowly. A couple of lanterns hang on hooks on the wall opposite the desk, their flames steady and bright.
119273: In the corner, a wide stairway leads down to a well-lit chamber below. Over the top of the stairwell is a grinning goblin head. Shields and faded wall hangings intersperse with glowing torches, denoting this area is of some importance. The hard stone floor shows scuffs and claw marks leading east.
119274: This chamber, connected through empty doorways to the west and south, is large but sparsely furnished. Some simple benches line one wall and an empty table stands in front of them. A trophy is mounted on the wall next to the southern doorway, the remains of a very large humanoid head, but barely recognisable as such.
119275: A strong, heavy-set goblin glares blankly ahead.

Large flaming torches brightly illuminate this large cavern. Along the walls hang shields and dusty tapestries in disrepair. A large rectangular table dominates the space, cluttered with dirty plates, spilled goblets, and other signs of recent use.
119276: Fading parchments show rough sketches detailing past plans for raids on a variety of regional targets. The chieftain of this goblin tribe is obviously very bold and arrogant. A large square table sits here, holding up a large pile of these papers.
119277:
A weapons rack stands against the wall.
In the rack are a scimitar and a jagged-edged scimitar.
A sturdy peg for hanging armour is on the wall.
On the peg, there are a chain mail hauberk and a fine chain mail coif.
A strong, heavy-set goblin glares blankly ahead.
A strong, heavy-set goblin glares blankly ahead.
A small, scrawny goblin skulks about.

The east wall is covered with several different sets of rusted, worn out body armour: chain mail, brigandines, and the like in massive sizes. On the south wall is a large display of weapons ranging from twin-bladed axes to jagged longswords to all sorts of crushing devices - all in disrepair.
119278:
An ornate elven chest, embellished with golden wood, has been left here.
A huge, bronze throne covered in dented armor and bloody skulls rests here.
The vehement goblin chieftain is here, with a sneering look upon his face.
A bulky goblin warrior, elite and imposing, is standing guard.
A bulky goblin warrior, elite and imposing, is standing guard.

Great braziers mounted on four basalt columns light up every part of this throne hall, bathing it in a deep, orange glow. Intricate designs carved into the domed ceiling dance in the flickering light, while dark statues look down upon a crimson rug that splits the entire cave in half from the doors to the throne. The attempt at grandeur in this chamber bespeaks an arrogance as large as its owner, the goblin chieftain.
119279:
A small, scrawny goblin skulks about.
A small, scrawny goblin skulks about.
A small, scrawny goblin skulks about.

Wide enough for six goblin troopers to march abreast, this long passage has fairly low ceiling. Dotting the rough, chipped walls on either side are flickering torches set in rough metal sconces. The well-trodden walkway curves from the south to the west.
119280: Many pairs of goblin feet have clawed their way to the east and west. The stone floor has been pounded by all the foot-traffic. No dust along the walkway indicates this tunnel has been recently used. Dimly flickering torches line the walls.
119281:
A small, scrawny goblin skulks about.
A small, scrawny goblin skulks about.
A goblin grunt is here, searching the area for enemies.
A goblin grunt is here, searching the area for enemies.

After resting, eating and enjoying some off-duty time in the caves to the west and south, this is where small troops form up before moving out on patrol. A large assortment of weapons and other necessary gear hang on the north wall, dimly lit by several torches along the walls.
119282: A blood-stained target hangs on a wall.

Various sorts of tables and contraptions are laid out here, designed to entertain and challenge the goblins in their down time. From throwing knives at a bloody wall target to claw-wrestling, goblins enjoy what little off-duty time they can get here. Torch-light spilling in from the east casts gloomy shadows throughout this cavern.
119283: There are four filthy straw pallets here.

Into the west, north, and east walls, dark recesses have been chipped until a full-size goblin could fit inside. It looks as if many hundreds of goblins could sleep in here at the same time. The dank musty odours of goblin breath and body stench fill the air.
119284:
A beer barrel has been left here.
A long table occupies the middle of the room.
On the table, there are four musty loaves of bread and two beer mugs.
A goblin grunt is here, searching the area for enemies.
A goblin grunt is here, searching the area for enemies.

A single long, wide table occupies the central area of this part of an expansive cavern. Various food items, mostly large wooden plates with meats occupy the table. Several large mugs stand on the table, or lie on their sides, spilled contents staining a table that's seen better days.
119285:
A stove stands against one wall here.
A large, sturdy table made from oak is sitting here.
A weary woman stands here, looking miserable.
A weary woman stands here, looking miserable.
A small, scrawny goblin skulks about.
A small, scrawny goblin skulks about.

Hot and musty, this kitchen is dominated by a large pile of rotting meat that has been stacked haphazardly in one corner. What seems to be a meal has been prepared over a large pot that absolutely reeks of rot. Various cooking vessels and tools hang from a low overhead ceiling. A couple of flickering torches lights the kitchen, if just barely.
119286:
You see three pieces of gristly meat on the ground.
A salted fish has been left here.
You see two onions on the ground.
You see two turnips on the ground.
There are two sacks of flour here.
A goblin grunt is here, searching the area for enemies.
A goblin grunt is here, searching the area for enemies.

Dingy and dim, this corner of the cavern is cluttered with a few cabinets and storage lockers lining the walls. Piles of unwashed wooden food bowls are haphazardly stacked, waiting to be cleaned. A large wooden tub full of nasty water sits nearby.
119287: A crudely chiselled tunnel winds back and forth while rising to the south. Broad enough for several goblins to march side by side, the chipped walls are adorned with flickering torches interspersed with skulls. To the north, it almost smells like food is being prepared.
119288:
Some ugly blow-flies are buzzing around here.
Some ugly blow-flies are buzzing around here.
A small, scrawny goblin skulks about.

Though not known for cleanliness, even goblins understand that fouling the caverns make them unlivable. In the walls and along the baselines, are a series of small openings and pits for relieving oneself. The stench emanating from these areas is overwhelming and intense.
119290:
A strong, heavy-set goblin glares blankly ahead.
A strong, heavy-set goblin glares blankly ahead.

Here the cold, jagged tunnels of mountainous rock branch east and west, with the exception of a nearby rocky ascent upwards. The hard stone walls glisten with a faint hint of moisture when artificial light is present, which the darkness readily swallows once removed. In all directions the visibility yields to the engulfing darkness after only a few feet, as if the light itself knows the futility of further effort.
119293:
A brown fur is here lying on the ground.
A short spear is lying on the ground.

A natural recess extends deep into the wall of a larger tunnel to the north. This seems to have been considered a convenient location for tossing supplies of all sorts. Shabby furs, short spears, and poorly maintained armour feature heavily, with neither rhyme nor reason apparent in their placement in many sordid piles.
119310:
A pool with many big pieces of ice floating in it is here.
A black crow flies low to the ground here, looking for carrion to eat.
A black crow flies low to the ground here, looking for carrion to eat.
A black crow flies low to the ground here, looking for carrion to eat.
A black crow flies low to the ground here, looking for carrion to eat.
A black crow flies low to the ground here, looking for carrion to eat.

A vast glacier stretches down from a mountain to the north to end at a chill, clear lake. Water trickles into the lake from the glacier snout, and several large chunks of ice float on the surface. Steep, narrow moraines to either side offer no purchase for any traveller who would wish to continue up the mountainside.
119311: A black crow flies low to the ground here, looking for carrion to eat.

Parallel ridges run across a broad, U-shaped valley, each evidence of a glacier's retreat. The ridges are shallow and easy to traverse, and are composed of soil, gravel, and small rocks. The glacier that abandoned this debris long ago stands to the north at the edge of an icy lake. The deep valley it carved bends westward as it descends.
119312: A black crow flies low to the ground here, looking for carrion to eat.

A gently rolling till plain covers the floor of a deep, curved valley with steeply sloped sides. The pebbles, rocks, and boulders that litter the plain were abandoned long ago in the rapid retreat of a glacier. A careful eye will note that a faint pattern of parallel curves can be discerned among the debris, each following the bend of this valley as it descends from east to south.
119313: Two glacial valleys originating higher up in the Misty Mountains merge to form a broad valley that descends to the east. The meeting of the glaciers that formed these valleys left a long ridge of debris, as if to attempt to keep apart the two competing siblings. To the west, the farthest march of the combined glacier is evident in a tall terminal moraine.
119314: Some orange-red blossoms grow amid grey-green foliage.

Peculiar, teardrop-shaped hills dot a broad glacial valley. The hills are divided neatly down the middle by a tall ridge of sundry debris marking the separate paths carved by two distinct glaciers to the south and east. The steepest slopes of the hills face the path of glacial retreat, whereas their tails descend gently to the west.
119315:
A black crow flies low to the ground here, looking for carrion to eat.
A bear cub is playing here, protected by soft white fur.
A black crow flies low to the ground here, looking for carrion to eat.
A black crow flies low to the ground here, looking for carrion to eat.
A black crow flies low to the ground here, looking for carrion to eat.

A tall glacier looms at the head of a U-shaped valley, sloping steeply to where its snout meets scattered, chill pools amid rocks and debris. Further down the valley, isolated patches of ice have been abandoned in the glacier's retreat, doomed eventually to melt. Tall ridges composed of the same glacial detritus make for impassable ascents to either north or south.
119316:
A black crow flies low to the ground here, looking for carrion to eat.
A mountain goat is here, jumping from cliff to cliff.

A vast glacier looms at the head of a broad valley, its terminus steep and impossible to climb. Fallen blocks of ice mingle with varied rocky debris beneath the ice wall. To the north, the glacier valley broadens as it merges with another. The only passage eastward would follow a shallow ascent up to the northern rocky ridge built up by the glacier.
119317: A black crow flies low to the ground here, looking for carrion to eat.

A flat, narrow ridge overlooks a massive glacier to its south which was responsible for its creation. This vantage point affords a striking view down the valley to the west and of the debris that marked the glacier's long-ago retreat. Narrow crevasses cut across the glacier, none large enough to admit any curious creature foolish enough to investigate.
119318:
A hungry warg (mine) is standing here.
Zud the Tarkhnarb Orc, wielding a barbed thorny spear, is standing here.
A hungry warg stands here, sniffing around for flesh.
An enslaved shadow (rawr) is standing here.

A tall ridge running along the northern edge of a glacier meets a crevasse cutting across the entire valley. The ridge dips where it has eroded to form a shallow slope that descends to meet the icy crack in the glacier. Rubble and blocks of ice clutter the swiftly narrowing entrance.
119319: A narrow crevasse cuts through icy walls that extend apparently beyond limit to heights far above. Numerous cracks run upward along the walls, and long, precarious-looking icicles extend from jagged points left by fallen ice. The ground is slick with refrozen meltwater.
119320: A wide cleft in glacial ice broadens as it runs southward. Here and there, gaps in the glacier hundreds of feet above reveal glimpses of a sky, and a world beyond this endless ice. Rubble intermingles with shattered ice blocks to form a rough but navigable passage.
119321: A massive snow giant is here, covered in white fur.

A crevasse splitting vast walls of ice to the north here broadens into a frozen cave with smooth, ridged walls and dangling icicles. The air is warm for such cold surroundings, and the floor is strikingly devoid of ice. Old gnawed bones and mounds of shed fur suggest this cave is frequently inhabited.
119322:
A bubbling pool of hot water is here, steam rising from its surface.
The thawing, half-eaten corpse of an elk hangs next to one of the pools.
A burly snow giant is sitting here, trying to fight an enslaved shadow (rawr).
A hungry warg (mine) is standing here.
Zud the Tarkhnarb Orc, wielding a barbed thorny spear, is here, fighting a burly snow giant.
A hungry warg stands here, sniffing around for flesh.
An enslaved shadow (rawr) is here, fighting a burly snow giant.

Warm vents in the rocky floor have carved out a large cave in the ice of a glacier. The ceiling is smooth and rolls in long ridges perpendicular to the walls of the cave. Steam rises from several pools of water, making the air oddly humid in these cold surroundings. A thawing, half-eaten corpse of an elk rests next to one of the pools. The cave climbs steeply upward to the east, where it narrows again into a mere crack in the ice.
119323:
A low shrub with bright green, oblong leaves is growing here.
Scattered in and on the shrub, there are three piles of blueberries.
A large marmot is here, scurrying in between the rocks.
A black crow flies low to the ground here, looking for carrion to eat.
A black crow flies low to the ground here, looking for carrion to eat.

A tall, rocky ridge cuts across the middle of a broad valley, marking the farthest conquest of a glacier originating higher up in the mountains to the east. The ground is covered in small pebbles and sand, making for poor footing. To the north, the ridge leads up to a narrow ledge that cuts across the steep mountain slopes, whereas a slide down the unstable far slope of the ridge would seem to be a one-way trip to a valley cutting southeastward.
119324:
A black crow flies low to the ground here, looking for carrion to eat.
A black crow flies low to the ground here, looking for carrion to eat.
A mountain goat is here, jumping from cliff to cliff.
A black crow flies low to the ground here, looking for carrion to eat.
A black crow flies low to the ground here, looking for carrion to eat.

A nearly vertical slope curves from the north to the east, sloping away from a pair of peaks high above. The cliff is broken only by a thin shelf no wider than the breadth of three men. A faint trail is barely visible in the shadowy depths of a valley below.
119325:
A black crow flies low to the ground here, looking for carrion to eat.
A black crow flies low to the ground here, looking for carrion to eat.

A narrow ledge zigs and zags back and forth along the face of a cliff. Its outer edge is crumbling, leaving great, jagged gaps that leave only a few feet of passable terrain between a steep slope and steeper drop-off. Debris from the ledge, boulders, and scree litters the mountainside below.
119326:
A huge white bear is here snuffling about for food.
A black crow flies low to the ground here, looking for carrion to eat.
A black crow flies low to the ground here, looking for carrion to eat.
A black crow flies low to the ground here, looking for carrion to eat.
A black crow flies low to the ground here, looking for carrion to eat.

Smooth, flat rock juts outward from a mountain peak to the north, coming to a jagged edge where large slabs of rock have broken off to crumble into boulders strewn along the slope below. Far below, a trail winds back and forth between this precipice and a similarly steep set of cliffs on the opposite side. A narrow, rocky ledge descends eastward along the slope of the mountain.
119328:
An iron pick has been dropped here.
An albino fish is swimming here, looking for some food.

In the pitch black water it is very difficult to see. It's quite impossible to guess how deep it goes downward; into some deep fissure where dark, ancient things lurk most likely. There is no space between the rock above the water for a breath of air. To the east, none would ever call light, but the darkness seems less absolute.
119329:
The half-eaten remains of an albino fish are lying here.
A powerful young troll stares at you.

Black waves lap against a stony beach making no sound whatsoever. To the west the cavern wall comes down to the water and dips below, disappearing from sight. The beach is quite small, only a few yards across, but a path of freshly wet rock winds its way out of sight upwards.
119333:
A pale stone troll walks around here, looking for a fight.
A stone troll mother is here, trying to keep her family safe.

This chamber is dark in all corners but beads of condensation scatter the dim light as it drips down the walls of this damp cavern. Small bones are decaying in scattered piles throughout the floor. Several large nests of fur and hay have been arranged around the chamber for something to bed down.
119334: A huge natural cavern extends to the south. Big stalactites hang from the ceiling and some broken pieces scattered over the cavern floor suggest some stalactites came down. The western side of the cavern is covered with rubble from several cave-ins.
119336:
A mailbox stands here stuffed full of messages.
A sauna gnome is lurking here.
A sauna gnome is lurking here.
A sauna gnome is lurking here.
A sauna gnome is lurking here.

A warm summer night embraces Antti's summer cottage, blanketing it into soft shades of dark, wrapping everything within its protective arms, providing peaceful and safe sleep. The beautiful lake around the cottage is totally still, only a vague sound of some night bird can be heard in the distance. A group of Sauna gnomes are dancing on the smooth rock before the cottage.
119337: Dwarfing many of the surrounding mountain tops, this high terrace stands tall. Rocks, large and small, are in abundance here and the wind howls as it passes over them. The slightest physical disturbance often sends the rocks tumbling down the mountainside, bouncing and crashing into anything in their path.
119338:
A nest is here.
A small, helpless eaglet screams for more food.
A small, helpless eaglet screams for more food.
A small, helpless eaglet screams for more food.
A small, helpless eaglet screams for more food.
A mother eagle flies high above, looking for prey.

A great nest stands at the top of a high peak. Sheltered by a perfect alcove of rock above and on one side, this is an excellent vantage point of the surrounding areas. Ice creeps along the edges of the alcove but inside there is no ice to be found.
119339: Slippery ice covers the slopes with scarce a foothold to be seen. Small stones and pebbles have been frozen in the swirling white canvas. The world is split asunder with one hemisphere a wall of ice, the other an endless sky. Far below, the snow filled basins between the mountains twinkle and glisten.
119340: Along this mountain top a flattened natural path lies in contrast to the sharp ridges that surround it. Narrow and with a cliff-like drop off on either side, the path navigates over the mountain's peak. The wind sputters and whispers as it races over the mountain.
119341:
A nest is here.
A small, helpless eaglet screams for more food.
A small, helpless eaglet screams for more food.
A small, helpless eaglet screams for more food.
A small, helpless eaglet screams for more food.
A mother eagle flies high above, looking for prey.

The mountain approaches its crest here but diverts into a small alcove that has become a great eagle's sanctuary. The world stretches away below as the vantage of this place is unparalleled. Large branches have been woven together tightly forming huge nests with one particularly grand nest on a raised stone slab.
119342: The crest of this mountain climbs high into the sky giving an expansive view of the surrounding areas. Snow has piled up layer upon layer and every so often chunks around the edges fall off, crashing down the mountainside. The wind bites the top of the mountain with no remorse.
119344: A large pile of boulders is sitting here, probably debris from a rockslide.

Loose stones and boulders lie everywhere, ready to be sent tumbling and sliding down the mountain at the slightest provocation. The ground rises up to a rocky outcropping to reveal a protected cave leading down. Long sticks and branches, the wreckage of some huge bird's nest, can be found lying in the cave.
119346: The entirety of this mountain top is encased in heavy snow. The summit of the mountain, approaching the clouds themselves, stands tall above the ground far below. Great blocks of ice, like massive nails, surround the peak. The wind is harsh and unforgivingly cold.
119347: Nestled in the high Misty Mountains, this little dale lies quite hidden. Thick grass lies underfoot with a small frost on top, giving the grass a bit of crunch. There seem to be animal tracks imprinted in the grass, leading various directions. Several moss-covered boulders lie close to the steep slopes that lead back into the lofty mountains.
119348: A clear spring babbles as cool water trickles out of the ground.

A small valley in the mountains lies here. Although the surrounding slopes are covered in snow, here it's not so cold. A small spring can be spotted in the corner of this little dale. Green grass and other plant life radiate out from the spring, offering a welcome resting place to weary travellers.
119350: In the Shadow of the Misty Mountains

A mountain ibex is jumping from rock to rock.
A mountain ibex is jumping from rock to rock.

Towering above, the mountains wrap around this little valley like huge sleeping bears. The almost permanent shadow that is cast on this land ensures the area is not very warm. A small pond, frozen over with a thin sheet of ice, lies motionless in the corner of the valley.
119357:
A protrusion of rock juts out from the wall.
On the rock, there is a large metal wall shield.
A powerful young troll stares at you.

A hovel has been roughly made with fish skins draped across some upright stones. Beneath the "shelter" the bones of dead fish litter the area, and near the back the ground appears very smooth, as if large fists have pounded it into something more akin to a bed than the cave floor. A rough picture has been scraped into a large flat stone in the northern part of the cave.
119358: The chilly waters within this subterranean river are swift and strong. They pull on everything, carrying it downwards while the rocky ceiling gets progressively lower until nothing but claustrophobic, murky water exists. The water swirls and descends through a series of fast bends, painfully striking everything against the tunnel's rocky walls.
119359:
A brown bear is sleeping here.
A brown bear is sleeping here.
A domesticated pony, beast of burden to many, stands here.
A sturdy pack horse is standing here.

Rocks and gravel blanket the floor of a wide, tall cavern. Piles of dry grasses lie strewn about, some hidden behind large rock formations or boulders. The ceiling is formed from bare earth, and small, loose parts occasionally fall.
119365:
A white-painted bench is here.
A humble man stands here, ready to help you with your things.
A tall and strong guard is here.
A tall and strong guard is here.

A large crystal chandelier brightly illuminates the main floor of the manor. Well furnished with a dark navy blue rug overtop the smooth red oak floor, this home provides sanctuary to fellow high standing compatriots of Robal. Etched into the southern wall are stories of victories and friendships formed in a multitude of languages. Bookshelves line the whole northern walls and are subsequently filled with tomes, scrolls and flasks. Centre of the room stands a large imperial staircase ascending to the second floor that leads to additional bedchambers. At the other end, one can see shrubbery and greenery beginning to form and coalesce with red oak almost in a natural way.
119366: A humble man stands here, ready to help you with your things.

Crushed pebbles form a path in the garden leading from the east, then curving to the south where it leads to a small hut. Flowers grow along the path in vibrant colours and various sizes. A few bushes grow on the northern side of the garden, behind a small rock garden. The rocks and stones all glisten with a shiny finish.
119367: A humble man stands here, ready to help you with your things.

The high vaulted ceiling here in this room is adorned with a heavy crystal chandelier which cast shadows of light upon the dark hardwood furniture. A long table, made of rich mahogany, rests in the middle of the room. Surrounding it are a set of matching chairs covered in lush red silk. Maps are strewn about the table. Upon the maps are various models ranging from trolls to dragons. Large tapestries hang gallantly from the walls, depicting scenes of battles of long ago. At the far end of the table, a grand marble throne sits, engraved with the past deeds of its owner.
119368: The hills here are surrounded by natural rock walls in all directions, formed from rock formations rising from the earth. Passage to the north seems impossible due to some loose rocks and boulders which have formed a large fissure, but appear to fill it. A large area of dense brush looms in the south.
119370:
The corpse of a scrawny goblin is lying here.
The corpse of a rigorous goblin leader is lying here.
The corpse of a scrawny goblin is lying here.
Cromdreath the Mountain Troll (CC) is standing here.

These are old ruins that have recently been rebuilt to have a new roof and fixed walls. While the walls collapsed long ago, the western wall appears to have been freshly built and a small plaque has been affixed to it. Pinewood logs were used to fix the wall, the other walls are still mostly in the original condition. However, nearest to the roof, there were some holes in the other walls that had to be filled with wood. The roof is completely new. It was made of wooden planks and sealed with tar.
119371:
A wooden chest stands in the corner.
A weapons rack stands against the wall.
In the rack are a battle axe, three war arrows, a shortbow, a mace, and a broad spear.
A beer barrel has been left here.

This old cellar is robustly made and have survived the test of time for what might be centuries. The floor is made of flat stones, evidently carefully picked to fit neatly together. The stone stairs lead upwards out of the cellar.
119373:
Traces of white tones form the aura of this place.
A blooming water-lily floats on the surface of the water.
A placid pond is here, inviting you to take a refreshing drink.
A fallow deer is grazing peacefully here.
A large elk is standing here, chewing grass and leaves.

Rivulets of clear water seep from small cracks in the western cliff, forming a large pool in the marshy ground below. Water-lilies provide cover for darting minnows, and blue irises grow along the perimeter of the water. The land here is soft and spongy, and travel easily deforms it.
119374: A huge, hungry-looking rat is here.

A tight hole is slick with mud and wet rocks, water coming in from a hole overhead. The hole slides down and north, with loose rocks stopping travellers from slipping haphazard to another, wetter drop. The air is rich with the smell of dirt and blows up cool and gentle from below.
119375: A slick, muddy sinkhole widens as it pitches sharply down, spotted with enough rocks to provide a meagre passage. Water trickles through the mud in never ending rivulets, giving the cavern a state of tumult. The air is cold, and sounds of squeaks and flutters can be heard in the distance.
119376: A path has been cleared through a muddy sinkhole and leads to a steep, walkable slope up and south. At the bottom of the hole is a large accumulation of stones, wet and packed thick. The ceiling cuts down low and muddy on the north end, opening up abruptly just past the stones. About, the air is cold and wet.
119377: A dirty ruffian draped in rags advances towards you.

Long stalactites hang down wet-orange in this immense cavern, and along the north side are large enough to reach waiting stalagmites. Damp, water beads on all surfaces, dripping and gliding down to the craggy floor. The air is cool and full of echoing squeaks. To the east, the cave narrows to a tunnel.
119378:
A black pond of water is here.
An ancient fungus smothers the boulders.

The back of this cave smells of human filth and rotting cloth, and is even wetter than the front. Crammed at the far wall are bones, rotten potatoes, fur scraps, offal, torn clothes and broken weapons. The floor tilts to the back, and a bit of foul water can be seen pooled below the garbage.
119379:
A dirty ruffian draped in rags advances towards you.
A dirty ruffian draped in rags advances towards you.

Slick, wet walls slope down to a narrow floor in this rough and pockmarked tunnel. The ceiling is high as the tunnel bends north, and becomes lower as it turns to the west, just above the height of a man. Sounds of water dripping from above into small pools echo quietly about, and the smell of clay is deep.
119380: A winding, narrow tunnel extends west, widening to a vast cave. South, the tunnel narrows and large blocks of stone cause the path to tighten in three spots. The ground is natural, uneven, rough and muddy, slowing traffic to all but the most natural of cave dweller. The walls on either side slant up and extend to a tall ceiling that has actively dripping stalactites.
119381:
The corpse of Scarred is lying here.
A horse of the Rohirrim (ulo) is standing here.

Sounds echo in this large, tall-ceilinged cavern. The floor is uneven, with two larger high spots of lumpy rock. A depression in the eastern part of the cave is covered in pelts, cookware and a recently used roasting spit. Most of the ground is bare rock, with only corners or low spots filled with mud. On the western wall, high up, is a ledge that leads treacherously over to a narrow, vertical crevice on the north wall.
119382: Behind some roots is a rocky ledge, hard and smooth, appearing well used. The ledge is set high upon the wall of a large cave, and provides a good view of the great distance that would be travelled if one fell from here. Close inspection of the walls reveal rocky knobs that stick out at opportune spaces. To the west an acrid smell emanates, evident from the brown, foul dirt that oozes out from under the tips of the roots.
119383: A noticeable crack runs down one of the walls.

This narrow crevice extends upwards to the top of a tall ceiling. The walls are rough rock and slick with moisture, extending up from the narrowest point at the floor. As the crevice widens, a larger space is evident some thirty feet up, and could fit two men hidden from the cave below.
119384: A humble man stands here, ready to help you with your things.

Though nestled within the walls of Bree, this hall shows a distinctly dwarven architecture. Perhaps the owner, who has chosen to live in this city mostly of men, was homesick for the comforts and customs of the dwarves. A large table in the centre of the hall is laden with remains of a great feast. On the walls hang rows of trophies taken from over which this home's owner was victorious. There are several cots in one corner where the residents and guests may sleep. A humble man stands here, ready to help you with your things.
119385: A humble man stands here, ready to help you with your things.

Hardly any sunlight can be admitted into this small and dank room. All of the windows on the western side have been draped with heavy curtains, disallowing any passer-by from Staddle Street even a glimpse from the interior. The wooden walls have been decorated with numerous paintings of coins, jewellery, weapons and artefacts.
119386:
A doorwarden stands here ready to obey his master's wishes.
A tall and strong guard is here.

You descend a set of stairs from the entrance into a great white tunnel. Its walls are covered in tapestries and paintings of ancient realms. The stairs are made of marble and onyx. At the base of the stairs there is a tall portal of polished metal with intricate designs inlaid with gems and runes. Beyond the passage is another even greater chamber that seems to have a strange aura emanating from it.
119390:
A shadowy and lithe orc stands here, half-hidden in the darkness.
A shadowy and lithe orc stands here, half-hidden in the darkness.
A powerful orc of the Morruhk stands here, armed with whip and blade.

The air here is filled with the heavy scent of warg. The ground is littered with chewed and cracked bones with not a scrap of raw meat still clinging to them. Several enormous cages line the back of the cave along with instruments to care for and train the wargs of the Uruk-Morruhk.
119391: Only about four feet in height and width near the entrance from above, growing larger towards the eastern end this stone crypt holds shelves on any available surface. They are filled with small vials, flasks and trinkets, most of these covered with a thick layer of dust.
119392: A hushed tone pervades this cramped hall under the eaves of southern Bree's foundation. The low room has stone-laid recesses set into the walls. In these lie the decayed remains of the ancient Edain of many millennia ago. Ancient writings in a dialect of Westron describe the occupants, but the precise meanings cannot be gleaned, so changed is the modern language from its forebear.
119393: This large room acts as a common area and a pathway that leads to additional bedchambers. Unlike the foyer, this room is accompanied by a hearthstone in the middle of the room that is burning providing a bit of warmth and serenity to those that rest here. The polished red oak flooring signifies the delicacy of the architect work to make sure that these halls remain for an eternity. Across the eastern and western walls are commissioned paintings given by Ryalnos of adventures from those that live within these walls.
119394: A humble man stands here, ready to help you with your things.

Torches in silver sconces are fastened in each corner of this chamber made of stone. The stones differ in light colours, forming a matching pattern on each wall, with a brilliant white mortar between each stone. A bed stands along the southern wall, with a small table on one side and two shelves fastened to the wall on the other for scrolls, books and other trinkets.
119395:
Massive roots shift uneasily all around you.
Some roots lie here waiting to ensnare weary travellers.

The old cellar has a musty, stale scent. The stone walls have experienced the ravages of time, and frost damage has caused numerous noticeable fractures, allowing gnarly roots and vines to take up residence in the cellar. A messy layer of muck, grime, and water puddles has been spread over the formerly spotless paved stone surface. Thick oaken beams support a ceiling constructed of half-rotten planks that have collapsed in some places and deposited muck on the floor.
119396:
A small termite is running around making strange sounds.
A small termite is running around making strange sounds.
A small termite is running around making strange sounds.
A giant termite is here, crushing skulls and bones.
A small termite is running around making strange sounds.
A giant termite is here, crushing skulls and bones.

This hidden pit lies deep underneath a fallen tree, the home of a termite colony. A multitude of tiny holes can be seen extending in all directions where the workers have dug to expand the nest. This huge pit is where larger workers reside that are unable to fit into the smaller tunnels.
119400:
A huge, poisonous spider is here.
A huge, poisonous tarantula extends her legs to you.
A tiny spider is here, eating a tiny bug.
A tiny spider is here, eating a tiny bug.
A tiny spider is here, eating a tiny bug.
A tiny spider is here, eating a tiny bug.

Darkness besieges this cave, making it hard to distinguish anything in here. The floor is littered with old hardened cocoons, and strands of large, sticky spider webs. In a corner lies a pile of dried out flesh and the bones of an unidentifiable humanoid. The air is still, filled with the scent of death and decay.
119401: A humble man stands here, ready to help you with your things.

This room is filled with a peaceful aura. Bright walls and the white ceiling, like almost everything in this room have been embellished with diamonds. Floor is covered with a smooth, sky-blue carpet, dampening the footsteps. On the right wall there is a nice window, with a view to a cosy garden filled with flowers. There is a round table with some chairs in the left corner, and close to it a big bed, welcoming to take a nap after hard day.
119405: Large jutting rocks line the floor, ceiling, and walls of this crude cave entrance. Several sets of animal bones lie in various piles, in differing states of decay. It is apparent that a large predator of some sort uses this cave as its home.
119406: This cave opens from the east in a wide fashion and begins to narrow as it continues to the west. The large, jutting rocks that line all surfaces of this cave make it somewhat difficult to traverse through the cave. Debris lines the cracks that run between the jutting rocks on the cave floor.
119407: The eastern side of this cave tunnel begins to open to a wider part of the cave. The jutting rocks that line all surfaces of the cave begin to smooth as it runs from the east to the west. Foul smells emanate from the cave below.
119408:
A skeleton of some humanoid lies in the dust.
A cavebear is sleeping here.

This foul cave seems to be the home of a predator. The walls are made of hard rock and extremely rough as if something was digging around. Several patches of black fur cover the ground, as well as piles of bones and half-eaten corpses in various states of decay which emanate a penetrating odour. A deep footprint can be seen near the entrance, making it obvious the inhabitant of this cave must be both large and heavy.
119412:
An iron railing runs through the cave.
A large leech is moving close to you, searching for blood.

A lattice of giant wood beams provides support to this damp underground dig. The rocky walls are cut to an expertly smooth sheen, and small rivulets of water trace their way along tiny imperfections, to the smooth floor below. On the western wall, the ground slopes sharply upward, where a pair of giant rocks provides a barrier against wind, and the elements.
119413:
An old, sturdy mine cart stands here on the end of a pair of iron rails.
An unfinished iron railing extends to the middle of the cave.
A hardened miner is here, covered in sweat and dust.

A wooden lattice extends from the west, providing protection from cave-ins, and a place to hang tools and dry clothes. The black, rocky walls here are cut to an expertly fine sheen. To the east an uneven wall blocks further travel, and a small pile of rubble lays at the base of the wall. The air is stagnant here, with notes of dirt and mildew.
119414:
A sturdy peg for hanging armour is on the wall.
A weapons rack stands against the wall.
A stout Dwarven steward stands here, ready to defend the home.

Decorative weapons and a great many torches fill up the rooms walls while padded mats cover the floor. There are blood stains along the walls and on the floors looking almost as if a battle has been waged here.
119415: This room barely fits the bed and wash basin that lie here. The covers of the bed are the roughest of wool and lie in a jumbled mess at the end of the bed. One torch burns softly above the doorway providing enough light to fill the small bed-chamber.
119416:
A large bookshelf sits against the wall.
A large stone fireplace with a roaring fire warms the room.
A heavy desk, made of solid oak, stands here.
A humble man stands here, ready to help you with your things.

This is a smaller room than the one north, filled with large bookshelves, which are cluttered with scrolls and books. Upon a table in the centre of this room lie several large tomes. At the table stands a very large comfortable chair. At one end of this room a stone bed where the master of this temple sleeps.
119419: A humble man stands here, ready to help you with your things.

This is a quiet, serene garden. Luscious plants, beautifuly flowers, and sculpted shrubbery grow abundantly in a welcoming landscape, providing a brief respite from the hustle of life. A few marked paths lead deeper into the flora, allowing a more intimate encounter with nature.
119420:
A large stone fireplace with a roaring fire warms the room.
An elven guard is standing here at his post.

This small building contains a table, chairs, and several bunks. A small fireplace is set into the western wall, but aside from that, the room has no decorations of interest. Although most of the guards quarters are further into town, several stay here close to the gate in case of trouble.
119421: A humble man stands here, ready to help you with your things.

This is a small cottage made of pine and cedar, giving it a woodsy smell. Each wall is lined with circular targets made for archery. Each target is crafted from tightly bound straw, with a bullseye painted in the centre. The rest of cottage is scantly furnished, giving the impression the owner spends little time on anything but archery.
119422: A humble man stands here, ready to help you with your things.

This small dwelling leans up against the surrounding buildings, apparently having little support of its own. It looks ramshackle and run down, giving the impression its tenant is rarely in residence. A few broken items are scattered around the floor. They seem of little worth, but may have once had some value.
119423: The natural earth forms a depression below, though the ground itself is steady and packed. A constant gust of air flows through the underground cavity here, presumably entering from high above. The cavern walls that curve around in all directions are made of large wedges of slabs and pieces of slate, and appear to be embeded into the earth on purpose to form massive walls. The wedges block any passage to three openings within the natural earth walls to the west, north and south, where another underground area must be. The slabs to the east were tilted to the side, where an opening to another underground area is discerned.
119424: The walls of earthen rock in the tunnel lead from the north and curve towards a pile of crushed stone, rocks and other debris to the west. Gusts of air are coming from that direction, leaving various scents throughout the tunnel of crisp pine and soil. A large slab leans against the tunnel wall to the east, used to cover a section of the tunnel wall for more support or protection, and a draft can be felt passing through to another section beyond.
119425: The tunnel curves in a west and south direction, with sharp edges of slate along the eastern wall. Rocks and pebbles are piled up along the corner to the north-east of the tunnel crook, leaving the air dusty and dry. Along the worn ground are more pebbles and small stones scattered randomly, but clearly from the impression in the earth it was trampled over many times by something. Whatever it may be, it must have been large or consistent!
119426: The tunnel continues to the west and east from here, which is apparent from the depressed earth along the ground. Barely discernible to the south is a small crosscut leading to another tunnel or cavern beyond, through a portion of the tunnel wall that has collapsed. A heavy slab leans against the tunnel wall to the north, protecting another portion of the wall that has sustained damage.
119428:
A pale stone troll walks around here, looking for a fight.
A pale stone troll walks around here, looking for a fight.

The cavern is dark and a fine dust lingers in the air. Portions of every wall appear to be crumbling and starting to collapse, other than to the west. To the west a slab of large and sharp slate was used to attempt to block the cave off from the tunnel beyond or to keep something or someone within.
119429: The tunnel curves in a east and south direction from here, with sharp edges of slate along the western wall. A large pile of rocks and pebbles consume the north-west corner of the tunnel crook, layered with dust. Along the worn ground in the centre are smaller pebbles and stones, and judging from the impressions upon the earth with the dusting only along the edges of the tunnel, it has been trampled over recently.
119430: The tunnel continues to the north and south from here, which is apparent from the depressed earth along the ground. Slightly visible to the east is a small crosscut leading to another tunnel or cavern beyond, through a portion of the tunnel wall that has collapsed. A heavy slab leans against the tunnel wall to the west, protecting another portion of the wall that has sustained damage.
119431: A tiny spider is here, eating a tiny bug.

The tunnel curves in a north and east direction from here, with sharp edges of slate along the western wall. Dust has settled along debris of pebbles, rocks, and jagged pieces of slate along the edges of the depressed and packed earth of the centre of the tunnel. Spider webs, old and new, suspend along the tunnel wall, and toward the south-eastern portion.
119432: The tunnel continues to the west and east from here, which is apparent from all of the depressed earth along the ground. A large portion of the tunnel wall to the north was damaged, leaving a large opening to a cavern beyond. The pieces of rock and slate that form the debris appear easy to get through, but the sharper slate shards are angled facing the north, preventing anything to enter this part of the tunnel coming back from that direction. A heavy slab leans against the southern wall, concealing another opening.
119433:
A powerful young troll stares at you.
A stone troll mother is here, trying to keep her family safe.

The cavern is dark and a fine dust lingers in the air. Portions of every wall appear to be crumbling and starting to collapse, other than to the south. To the south a slab of large and sharp slate was used to attempt to block the cave off from the tunnel beyond or to keep something or someone within.
119434:
A pale stone troll walks around here, looking for a fight.
A pale stone troll walks around here, looking for a fight.
A stone troll mother is here, trying to keep her family safe.

The cavern is dark and a fine dust lingers in the air. Portions of every wall appear to be crumbling and starting to collapse, other than to the east. To the east a slab of large and sharp slate was used to attempt to block the cave off from the tunnel beyond or to keep something or someone within.
119435:
A petite web glistens along the bottom corner of cavern rock.
A huge, poisonous tarantula extends her legs to you.
A huge, poisonous spider is here.

The cavern is dark and a fine dust lingers in the air. Portions of every wall appear to be crumbling and starting to collapse, other than to the north. To the north a slab of large and sharp slate was used to attempt to block the cave off from the tunnel beyond or to keep something or someone within. Suspended throughout the ceiling and in the corners are large webs.
119436: A tiny spider is here, eating a tiny bug.

The tunnel appears to end here in an unnatural and penetrating darkness that any light could barely penetrate besides possibly standing right next to the source of it. The wall to the north has been heavily damaged, leaving a pile of debris with wedged pieces of sharp slate and other portions of the tunnel wall in a pile. Although easy to enter the opening, there are large pieces of slab and slate with sharp edges blocking passage back here. Thick, heavy and smouldering to the east is the dark. A very intense dark. So dark in fact, that it simply cannot be discerned what makes up the dark or what it truly is.
119438: Cold, rough walls of stone stand close about you on three sides. On the fourth side there might as well be a wall, for the floor rises so sharpy that it will take a good deal of luck or skill to make your way out of this dead end.
119443: A doorwarden stands here ready to obey his master's wishes.

The terrace on this roof of the Guards' Office has no wall on the western side, not even a rail - seems the Elf who built it is deft enough to not care about falling off. Half of the terrace is protected with a wooden cover, and the western part is open. To the east a simple door leads into the house. A round, reliable hatch can be used to descend down.
119444: An Elven steward stands here, watching over the household.

The eastern wall of this small, quiet home is decorated as part of a tree's trunk, crooked and bark-like. The backrest of the cushiony sofa standing nearby matches well, replicating the crook of a tree's trunk. In the centre of the room stands a round three-legged table, covered with a green spread woven from sweet smelling leaves. On the table has been placed a crystal vase filled with fruit. On the southern wall there is a bookshelf filled with books. At first glance, some of the books look plain, but with a skilled eye one recognizes the fine work of a true master.
119445:
A dwarven miner is here, digging the hard rock with his pick.
A dwarven miner is here, digging the hard rock with his pick.

Here the miners have come upon a natural opening in the rock. The floors have been polished smooth recently, and the walls bedecked with paintings and some tapestries, in preparation of new Dwarven Homes.
119446:
A huge clock is standing here.
A doorwarden stands here ready to obey his master's wishes.

Lamps mounted on the smooth stone walls cast flickering shadows around this well-lit hall. Every surface is impeccably clean, and polished to a shine. The three columns along the north wall, and the three columns along the south wall each depict one of the nameless six Dwarven fathers. Above the eastern doorway the seventh Dwarven father, Durin the first, the deathless, king of Khazad-dum is shown wearing a crown of seven stars. In the centre of the room rests a massive stone table around which visitors to Fenuln's hall can gather and feast.
119447:
A sturdy bed made from solid oak lies here, covered in warm blankets.
A large stone fireplace with a roaring fire warms the room.
A black and white cat is playing here.
A humble man stands here, ready to help you with your things.

The walls of this bedroom are rough cut granite with patches of green malachite carefully exposed, but still embedded in the walls where the water dripping through the copper rich stone naturally deposited the mineral. Between the large black bear fur covering the floor and the roaring fireplace, the chamber is quite cosy. The room is exceptionally well ventilated as there is barely any scent of smoke from the fire, and a gentle breeze of fresh air can be felt. In the corner a stone staircase leads downwards.
119448: A large stone chest is here.

Stalactites hang from the roof of the natural portions of the cavern, and broken rocks show the obvious signs of excavation elsewhere. A faint dripping sound can be heard, as the water from the nearby lake filters through the mountain. Piles of discarded stone are stacked adjacent to where valuable ore has been hewn from the mine. Although the chunks of granite look haphazardly cracked, a closer inspection reveals that the fractures must have been masterfully placed to efficiently extract all of the ore with the least number of pickaxe strikes.
119449: A dwarf trains scouts in the arts of stealth.

Though Dwarves by their nature are not drawn to stealth, some skills have found their way into Dwarven usage. Here, within mighty Zirakzigil many Dwarves hone these skills, trained by formidable rogue-captains. Though the Dwarves refuse such skills as backstabbing, all manner of other rogue skills you see practiced here.
119450: A large bulletin board, entitled "Thieves' Guild", is mounted here.

Here, upon the second level of Zirak, all the accumulated Dwarven knowledge of the scouts' skills is stored. Dwarves flit in and out, reading scroll after scroll, book after book, detailing how to perform each act of stealth. You are never quite sure how many Dwarves are in this chamber with you, and you wonder how many are lurking hidden, unnoticed by your eyes.
119451: A humble man stands here, ready to help you with your things.

The natural walls here have been carved and chiseled with an extraordinary pattern that resembles a brick wall. A large forge stands along the western wall, ablaze and venting through the ceiling above. Tool racks along the eastern wall are neatly kept and well organized. A large mural was beautifully painted near the forge of seven well-formed dwarves that are sleeping peacefully, while a craftsmen guards them protectively. The glow from the forge compliments this mural to honour Aule and the Seven Fathers.
119452: A humble man stands here, ready to help you with your things.

This is a dimly lit cave of hard grey stone. What little light there is shines upon the Duergar Coat of Arms above the hearth. The room is sparsley furnished with a bed, bookshelf and a few chairs. The shelf contains fantastical books of mythical creatures. Weapons and mining picks lie astray on the floor.
119453: What once was a path is wholly covered with mud. It seems to be really thick and a few bubbles on it indicate that it should not be hard at all. The rest of a dead stag, mostly some bones carefully washed by ants, can be seen. The poor animal was obviously asphyxiated when its head was caught in the mud. All around is a thick forest, with sharp bushes, preventing almost every move, except towards the northern path.
119454:
A sturdy bed made from solid oak lies here, covered in warm blankets.
A humble man stands here, ready to help you with your things.

This bedchamber is richly decorated. The wooden walls have several paintings hanging on them, each depicting the same person. The ground is entirely covered with a thick, flossy carpet. In the ceiling a large round mirror can be spotted. A wooden bed has been set up in the centre of the room, filled with dried leaves.
119461: Leading up from the basement, this old, winding stair reaches for the second floor of the ancient tower. The steps are cracked and broken in places and every step sends vibrations through the rock, sometimes causing small pieces of the old stonework to tumble down the stairs.
119462:
A sturdy bed made from solid oak lies here, covered in warm blankets.
A humble man stands here, ready to help you with your things.

This great room, built into the bottom of the northern slope of Bree Hill, looks very organised and well decorated. In a corner, there is a great view of a wide variety of weapons and trophies of past battles. On the other side of the room, there is a beautiful fireplace, emitting a nice calm pale glow, as the wood inside crackles and burns, soothing the room with warmth.
119463:
A white-painted bench is here.
A well-crafted white fountain is here, water pouring forth from it.
A heavy desk, made of solid oak, stands here.
A large bookshelf sits against the wall.
A large stone fireplace with a roaring fire warms the room.
A humble man stands here, ready to help you with your things.
A tall and strong guard is here.
A tall and strong guard is here.

As you enter the hall you notice a dim light reflecting on the huge pillars made of mahogany, in between which stand tall burgundy-coloured walls. A majestic lush carpet covers the stone cold floor. An illustrious sword-shaped crest of Eriador adorns the wall across the hall adjacent to the oil painting portraying Esmer of Calenardhon, heroic ancestor of Dunlendings. A curved hallway to the south leads toward the inner bedchamber.
119464:
A heavy desk, made of solid oak, stands here.
An elegant marble chest sits against the wall.
A sturdy bed made from solid oak lies here, covered in warm blankets.

In the western part of the room a handful of scented, black candles are lit on a nightstand. At the centre of the chamber there is a bed suitable for a king, covered by a great cave-bear fur. It looks very soft, inviting for a nap. Across the nightstand is a jewel-encrusted wardrobe holding clothes, armour and other necessities for the lord of the manor.
119465:
The corpse of a young troll is lying here.
The corpse of a young troll is lying here.

A large amount of grey, broken rock has been strewn across the floor of this cavern and piled up along the walls. Footing is unstable and no attempts appear to have been made to keep this area inhabitable; the rubble has simply been dumped here. The large cavern continues to the north and west; any noise echoes in the large space, bouncing against walls at least a hundred yards distant.
119466:
A plain leather belt is lying here.
A fishing rod has been left here.
A green pair of pants are on the ground.
A brown shirt is on the ground.
A grimy hill troll stands in a corner snickering to himself.

This dirty little burrow is barely large enough to be called a proper cave. It's been dug into musky, dark brown earth, with a couple of large boulders or the bedrock itself jutting out from the walls. The floor is soft and slightly wet earth with a fair number of large barefoot prints in it.
119467:
A subterranean lizard is here trying to blend with the surroundings.
A subterranean lizard is here trying to blend with the surroundings.
A mottled snake is sneaking here, ready to sink its fangs into flesh.

Covered in mud and decaying vines, the walls of this cavern are dark and cold. A mix of mud and water covers the ground beneath, making it slimy and slippery. No light enters the cavern, only this terrible smell sneaks in from somewhere. Some drag marks can be seen on the ground leading east from here to an opening of some kind.
119468: Someone has recently built a covered lookout on the top of the building. The walls are made of decent quality planks, and look sturdy. There are window-like openings in the walls, but no glass. The wind breezes through and it's easy to observe anything that is happening in the nearby surroundings. The ancient broken road is visible to the east and south.
119469: This dark hole has mud and rocks on the ground and water dripping from the ceiling. The walls here are solid, moist and cold and many claw-like scratch marks can be seen. Some are deep enough to reach through the mud and moss to the rock surface, revealing white chalk stone underneath. This hole is absolutely pitch black, no light seeps in at all.
119470: The river broadens slightly here, and the water takes on a more relaxed pace. Far enough from the Hithaeglir mountains to feel safe, and close enough to joining with its brother-branch, the river has little to fear. Yet, for some reason, it soon picks up its pace as it passes this section of the cliffs.
119472:
A large bat is here, hanging in the darkness.
A large bat is here, hanging in the darkness.
A large bat is here, hanging in the darkness.

Loose stones cover the floor of this cave, which extends for dozens of yards in every direction. The rocky walls are flat, but covered with small cracks. The roof appears to be of an entirely different stone, brown and earthy. Although clearly well-built at one time, this cave is so ancient that the ages will soon reclaim it.
119473:
A skeleton of some humanoid lies in the dust.
A huge bat is here, emitting piercing squeaks.
A large bat is here, hanging in the darkness.

Hidden behind the cave to the west, this ancient room may well have lain here undisturbed by the winds of time for thousands of years, perhaps even since the days of Earendil. Shards of broken masonry litter dusty corners, and an ancient stone chair rests atop a slightly raised dais against the eastern wall. Faint carvings can be seen on each wall, although what they represent is impossible to determine.
119474:
A ferry in the shape of a great white swan is here.
A sturdy pack horse is standing here.
A sturdy pack horse is standing here.
A sturdy pack horse is standing here.

Here, on the southern bank of the great river Celebrant, the densely growing mellyrn give way slightly, opening up to allow a landing. A large rock lies immersed in water just off the shore, creating a small area of peace and tranquility in the otherwise steadily flowing water. The powerful roar of the water echoes among the trees, almost drowning out the soft whispers of the forest and the singing of birds. Crossing the river is a slender rope, to which a delicate ferry is attached.
119475: A ferry in the shape of a great white swan is here.

A small wooden construction rests firmly on the sloping bank here, reaching into the current just far enough to create a pocket of solemn and tranquil water next to the bank. It is not quite a pier, but can still serve as a landing for boatsmen ferrying goods or travellers across. Close by the water, a tall tree stands, almost as a sentinel, with a wooden ladder running up the trunk. A slender rope can be seen running across the water to a landing on the other side of the river. A ferry is attached to the rope.
119476: Chilly water rushes all about in a chaotic and roaring frenzy. From up above, the muffled sound of falling water vibrates down from the surface. Millions of air bubbles created by the falling water cloud any view of the surroundings. As the falling masses of water force you deeper below the surface, another strong current can be felt rushing at you from the east.
119477: The strong current can be felt rushing westward. The water is cold but smooth as there is little to disturb it along its course here. The diameter of the spring itself is no more than a few feet as the polished rock sides of the waterway can be felt all around. To the east the current becomes impossibly difficult. However, a break near the top of the smooth rock siding of the spring can be felt and bubbles linger around the edges of the opening.
119478: This opening is quite small and a closer inspection reveals that the walls are comprised of smooth rock. A few slimy rock extensions hanging down from the ceiling form primitive beginnings of stalagtites. In the centre of the floor is a round opening in which water can be seen flowing by. The air is very humid and cool, yet it becomes more sparse and warm with every breath. It would be impossible for this small pocket of air to sustain a person for more than a short period of time.
119479: A humble man stands here, ready to help you with your things.

Hardly any sunlight is being admitted into this small and dank room. The windows on the southern side have been draped with heavy curtains, disallowing the passer-by from Highbluff Plaza even a glimpse from the interior. The wooden walls have been decorated with numerous paintings of coins, jewellery, weapons and artefacts.
119480: Right to the east lies a small, round door which leads into the hobbit hole. The garden here seems to be well-tended. A small path leads around the grass and to beds where flowers, vegetables, and spices for the kitchen are grown. A cut hedge forms the dense barrier to all other directions but the east.
119481:
Traces of fierce white tones form the aura of this place.
A mailbox stands here stuffed full of messages.
A large encrusted cedar chest is standing here.
A finely crafted crystal lamp is here.
An elven caretaker is standing here, offering his guests a rest.
A beautiful and docile horse is standing here.

As a sign of their hospitality, the Galadhrim have built this small pavilion on the ground, well aware of the fact that many of their visitors are unable to find peace of mind sleeping up in the trees. The pavilion stands just east of a marvellous fountain close to the foot of the house of Celeborn in the centre of Caras Galadhon. Built of the finest wood covered with intricate carvings, with windows made of coloured glass, the pavilion is a work of art, worthy of any ruler.
119483: Solemnity dominates this chamber, the smooth walls reflecting wavering light from torches on the walls that strangely enough still burn after all these years that must have passed since this place was in use. A spiraling stair leads up through a slab to the natural crown above you.
119484: A pale light enters through a tiny hole in the roof and penetrates through the dust to light this huge hall. A grand table, plain and strong, stands almost as long as the room itself with a noble chair at one end. A quick count shows that over 50 dwarves could eat here simultanously.
119485: A little stone lies on the ground.

You enter what appears to have been the forge. You see three separate forges, with a metal pipe leading up from each of them, joining at the centre of the room, and vanishing up through the ceiling: smoke collectors. Some mining tools, now decayed beyond any use, litter the floor. A mine-shaft leads off to the north, gently sloping downwards.
119486: The mine-shaft is barely six feet at its highest. It is ten feet wide. The walls are buttressed by stout wooden logs that seem rather dry and rotten. Yet you judge passage to be safe. The shaft slopes downwards and twists slightly. Once, it must have followed an ore vein.
119497:
A large bulletin board, entitled "Board of the Free Peoples", is mounted here.
A sign hangs above the doorway.
A huge clock is standing here.
A small oaken table has been set here.
On the table, there are a hunting knife and a beer bottle.
The elven bartender is standing here, gossiping behind the bar.

This dimly lit room is full of fishermen and other townspeople having friendly conversations over a few drinks. Fishing nets are hung from the ceiling and contain items like stuffed fish. In several places, nets hold up the torches which light this bar. It is a wonder this place hasn't burned down. You casually listen to some of the conversations and hear a few extremely tall fish tales. The stairs lead up.
119514: You have travelled far south now. There is an old path here, covered by the grass and the bushes. The grass has not been matted down in any particular area. It appears that this area has few travelers.
119530:
A bright green holly bush is growing here.
Partly covered by the bush's green leaves, there are two piles of hollyberries.

High snow-capped peaks cover your view east. The air is cold, coming from the Celebdil, and you should probably keep moving. If you take the mountain trail you should meet bitter cold, if no worse, before you come down to the other side. It will not help you to keep so secret that you are frozen to death. When you leave here, where there are still a few trees and bushes, you should carry a faggot of wood, as large as you can bear.
119546: Soon your way becomes steep and difficult. The twisting and climbing road has in many places almost disappeared, and is blocked with many fallen stones. A bitter wind swirls among the rocks. Your mind starts to wander and you begin to hate the cruel wind that seems intent upon chilling your body. It seems the mountains themselves gaze upon you as you march, malevolent and cruel, wishing misfortune for any creature that roams upon two feet.
119562: Laboriously you climbed a sharp slope and halt for a moment at the top. Numerous peaks rise high in the east. The peaks you can see are completely covered in ice but the Celebdil, the highest one, is hidden in the clouds. The trail changes here, while it starts to climb into the mountains. It looks like you will have to return the way you came or try to cross the Redhorn Pass.
119578: You have reached the beginning of the RedHorn Pass. You hear eerie noises in the darkness round you. It may be only a trick of the wind in the cracks and gullies of the rocky wall, but the sounds are those of shrill cries, and wild howls of laughter. Stones begin to fall from the mountain-side, whistling over your heads, or crashing on the path beside you. Every now and again you hear a dull rumble, as a great boulder rolls down from hidden heights above.
119594: Your company now gather together as close to the cliff as you can. It faces southwards, and near the bottom it leans out a little, so that you hope it will give some protection from the northerly wind and from the falling stones. But eddying blasts swirl round you from every side, and the snow flows down in ever denser clouds.
119610: The trail here is protected by a cliff-wall, the only shelter in the RedHorn Pass. Below your refuge are white humps and domes and shapeless deeps beneath which the path that you had trodden is altogether lost; but the heights above are hidden in great clouds still heavy with the threat of snow.
119627:
A big cavebear is padding around here.
A big cavebear is padding around here.

This den feels warm and comfortable to live in assuming you can imagine yourself being a bear. The little opening to the south allows only a slight draft of the cold mountain air into the cozy cave. Many bears have been born and trampled the cave on frigid winter nights.
119632: The riverbank becomes quite shallow here, not like the areas of steep riverbank further upstream. The flat riverbanks seem to lead to some type of road or track, and this place must once have been a ford when the river was in full flow. The riverbed itself continues to the north or south.
119633: A brigand, looking at your nice purse, is sneaking here.

You step out of the old tavern and onto an open deck. Around you are the rotting remains of some small tables with old chairs and stools around them. Looking through the gaps in the floorboards you can see a small, muddy stream flowing underneath. The only exit is back to the south.
