119641: This tunnel haphazardly slants downward at an almost vertical angle. Uneven stairs are roughly hewn into the rocky floor. In places, a partial collapse of tunnel has covered the stairs in a layer of loose stones and dirt. The footing here is slippery and any movement will be treacherous.
119642: This shallow cave shows signs of recent animal habitation. A cracked humanoid skull lies in one corner and various bones are scattered about. From the south wall a narrow tunnel climbs steeply. To the east a jagged opening leads out to the windy slopes of the misty mountains.
119643: In Front of the Nasty Mewlip's Inn

The coach to Bree and Tharbad is here.
A timetable for the coach to Fornost and Tharbad has been nailed to a wall.

A quiet wood follows the road to the west. To the east, there is a building. Through the window, the charming prospect of a bar can be seen, with rows of green bottles and gold labels, together with jars of pickles and preserves, and cheeses and boiled hams, and rounds of beef. A sign above the door invites travellers in and tells its name: The Nasty Mewlip's Inn.
119647: A barman watches you calmly, while skilfully mixing a drink.

This dim room, only sparsely lit by candles on small wooden tables, is filled with the smell of fresh beer, bread, and the melting candles. The shelf behind the bar is stocked with a fine choice of liquors. A notice, painted on a wooden board, is hanging above the bar.
119653: Tall grass here hides glints of rotten food and discarded cups, presumably left by patrons from the inn far to the west. The smell of rot permeates the air here, and insects can be seen crawling through the grass, no doubt attracted by the smell of decomposition.
119654:
A tall warden stands here, tending to the room.
A Dunadan soldier is here busily performing his duties.
An old man is walking around, cleaning up.

The walls on both the west and east side of this medium-sized chamber are made of solid stone, except on the north end where the straight walls begin to curve. The curved section of the wall was made with a beautiful white marble, with black and silver specks throughout each block drawing attention. A fine silver has been placed along the top and bottom of the walls as trim, with a unique pattern that trails from the south end to the marble portion, where two argent pillars stand on each side. Between the pillars is a silver-framed painting of a royal figure, with a silver plaque of inscription fastened above it. An expansive mural was painted on each of the stone walls leading to the pillars; one of a shipwreck upon the frozen seas and the other appears to be an immense battle with the Witch-king from an age long passed. The floor is polished and white, with the ceiling above matching, causing any noise to echo through the chamber.
119656:
A wolf cub happily plays here.
A wolf cub happily plays here.
A wolf cub happily plays here.
The mother wolf stands here, protecting her young cubs.
A great black and silver wolf is standing here, at the head of the pack.

The cold, damp earth floor of this hole partially covered in dead leaves and small tufts of fur. The roof seems to be supported by a network of roots, but nevertheless, soil and small stones fall to the ground, from time to time, adding small flurries of dust to the foetid air.
119657: A timetable for the coach to Fornost and Tharbad has been posted here.

The road bends sharply to the south and west here, avoiding the wooden building to the east that blocks movement in that direction. A trail winds its way north alongside the building. Looking south into the distance, a gauntlet of trees borders the roadside. To the west the road opens out more as the trees begin to thin.
119658: A painted timetable stands above the door to the shed.
You are walking next to the western city wall. The alley continues north and south. To the east you see a small square, while to the west you see the coach shed.
119659: A sign is nailed to a pole here.

Wooden docks provide landing facilities for ships. Ropes pile up, some of them are tied to the docks and hang downwards, nearly reaching the water surface. Looking through the narrow space between the planks below, small waves of dirty and stinking water breaks against the riverbank.
119660: A slavering warg stands here, sniffing around for fresh meat.

Rubble has twisted and bent the crudely-built iron cages that line the walls of this filthy cavern. Fallen rock can be seen everywhere among dusty piles of droppings, gnawed bones, and litter. The entire cave stinks of excrement and urine but even that can't distract by how the roof looks suspiciously unsafe and ready to collapse at any given time.
119661: This path passes through the soggy land, alongside a tiny stream. To the south, the path acts almost as a border between the sweeping grasslands of the east and the western wilderness. North-west and south the trail follows the trickle of water through the southern lands of Enedwaith.
119686: Here the water that has collected in the deep pool to the north drains through a narrow gap in the debris pile that has collected under the causeway. The waters flow over a sill of tree trunks, then abruptly plunge down into a churning dark basin of broken stone before washing you out downstream from the causeway again.
119692: High above the surrounding mountains you can see much of the landscape. Unfortunately, you are unable to maintain your position on this peak and topple down the west side; either gravely injured or more likely dead.
119694: High upon the Misty Mountain you can see a narrow passage to the east and a deep impassable crevice to the west. Often covered with snow, the wind blows without mercy upon this peak making it difficult to remain here.
119695: With great effort you have managed to reach a narrow cleft high upon the northern side of the mountain. Unfortunately, the cleft is coated in ice, has no handholds and a strong stiff wind blows pushing you down the northern side some five meters.
119696: With great effort, you have managed to reach a narrow cleft high upon the northern side of the mountain. Unfortunately, the cleft is coated in ice, has no handholds and a strong stiff wind blows pushing you down the northern side some eight meters.
119698: You lose your footing and hurtle downwards into thundering blackness. You bounce off a loose rocky surface with an agonising crash, and hurtle out into a spume-filled void.. Beneath the spume, torrential currents of unimaginable force swirl and collide endlessly, moving stones as if they were dry leaves and grinding them to powder against each other. Over the centuries, thousands of tons of rubble and slag - the discarded bones of Celebdil - were dumped here by the dwarves, to be reduced to slurry by the dark underground waters and carried away to an unimaginable destination. The same now happens to you.
119699:
There are two black leather belts here.
On the ground, there are two pairs of rigid leather sleeves.
You see two sturdy pairs of rigid leather gloves on the ground.
There are two sturdy pairs of rigid leather boots here.
A sturdy, rigid leather helmet lies here.
You see two rings on the ground.
A rigid leather helmet lies here.

A few almost unnoticeable tracks tread across the moors, apparently leading in no particular direction. They are encumbered with roots and bushes, and surrounded by thick vegetation. A deep fall blocks your way southward, and a little east of here an imposing rocky spur thrusts out over a huge waterfall, half veiled in thin mist.
119700: As you enter the room your mistake begins to become apparent. The ground beneath your feet feels decidedly unstable, and it would appear that this is the reason that this particular grave vault remains unguarded in any way. The only thing left to wonder at is just how much of the floor remains to shore up the tomb itself.
119701: A huge black portal, forged from seven massive stone blocks tethered together by iron bars and rusted bolts, blocks the northern exit from the cave. A row of four thick, oxidized iron rings hangs from the gate. The cavern itself is both wide and tall, with sharp edges of black stone protruding from the ceiling and walls. Shards of shattered stone lie spread across the ground. Remnants of man-like bodies have been left here, rotting away in the lukewarmth. In the southeastern corner a tunnel accessway takes a sharp turn, leading further down into the depths of Ettenmoors.
119702: En route to the ground far below, your mind leaves your body, taking the time to admire the landscape in the few seconds before impact. Maybe the next opportunity, you will choose to respect the physical laws which govern Arda.
119703: En route to the ground far below, your mind leaves your body, taking the time to admire the landscape in the few seconds before impact. Maybe the next opportunity, you will choose to respect the physical laws which govern Arda.
119704: A squirrel scampers around here, looking for nuts from the trees.

Trees, of mixed height and sort, mix and tangle their branches struggling for space. A dense foliage of ever-green bushes take the remaining space at the feet of the trees. The trees and the undergrowth together form an obstacle not easily passed. Some feet above hovers the tree-crowns that are woven together by twisting branches and dark leave; no light seems capable of passing through. North the woodland seems to open up a little, a clearing or forest border must be in that direction.
119712:
There are two sacks of flour here.
A large sack is on the ground.
A huge, venomous spider is here.
A huge, venomous spider is here.
A huge, venomous spider is here.

Old dirt and dust is mixed with flour all over the place. Some big sacks stand in a corner, next to a small table and chair. At the southwest corner of the room, the broken and disused remains of an old pulley lifting system can be seen, no longer used to transport sacks of flour between the mill above, and this small storage room.
119718: Entering through the small door, you come to this impressive oval chamber, panelled with stout woods. A large circular table made of elm dominates the room. Five high-backed chairs face the table and at each, the wood of the table is marked with a rune. Directly opposite the only doors a large hearth burns. Windows in the chamber face to all the points of the compass and provide the only visible means of lighting during the day. A soft breeze blows through the room making the atmosphere more bearable. This wind catches the rising smoke from the fire, curling it around as it makes its way up into the centre oculus of the conical roof.
119720: A humble man stands here, ready to help you with your things.

Dark coloured carpeting serves the purpose of hiding the numerous stains which have resulted from many a party here in this master chamber. An unmade bed sits in the corner, tilted higher on one side than the other. Several small notches have been made into the side of the oaken headboard. A large closet takes up a lot of the space on the south side of the room, spilling its contents all over the floor.
119721: A humble man stands here, ready to help you with your things.

This particular room looks like a study, with a small desk and matching chair standing in one corner, covered with hundreds of pieces of paper with varying degrees of unintelligable scribbles. The faint odour of something burning lingers, although no flame or smoke are visible. The frame of a bed stands on the opposite side of the desk, relatively clear of debris, with a small feather mattress and blanket.
119723:
A sturdy bed made from solid oak lies here, covered in warm blankets.
A humble man stands here, ready to help you with your things.

The light in this grand room seems to fade in and out as if in response to those entering and exiting it. Several large paintings depicting great battles, long since forgotten adorn the walls. To the right there is a fireplace, above which hangs an extremely well-crafted painting of Galador the Lord of Dol Amroth fighting fearsome beasts. At the very end of the room is a large window. From its ledge one can look far out to the horizon and even see part of the Old East Road.
119725: An elegant marble chest sits against the wall.

As you pass the threshold into this chamber you notice the floor is laid out before you in dark green marble as if it was a field of grass, and the ceiling is a black onyx with softly glowing diamonds as if they were stars. Upon the northern wall is a great throne made of gold and laced with silver. An elegant marble chest sits against the wall.
119726: A humble man stands here, ready to help you with your things.

You pass behind the throne and enter this final room. Its walls are made of carved panels of grey wood and the floor is covered in soft green velvet. A large desk is against the western wall covered in papers and maps. There is a large painting of Brogan adorning the northern wall. His large bed rests against the eastern wall, a crown of silver lays on the pillow.
119727:
A large fountain, made from grey stone, pours water from its centre.
A large bookshelf sits against the wall.
A humble man stands here, ready to help you with your things.

The heat in this room is intense, as the fires appear to be constantly stoked. A large forge has been built into the west wall. By its appearance it looks to be well used. A large anvil, seemingly made of mithril, resides in the centre of this chamber. Shelves line the the remaining walls, items stacked upon them in chaos, as if they had been placed there in great haste. The ceiling is black with soot and the floor is covered in metal shavings.
119728: A stout Dwarven steward stands here, ready to defend the home.

Atop the roof you enter a small temple dedicated to the Seven Fathers of the dwarves. A reflecting pool fills the centre of the room and murals cover the walls depecting the creation of the Dwarves by Aule.
119729: A humble man stands here, ready to help you with your things.

The bedroom is small but cosy, with a single bed placed against the far wall. A wooden nightstand sits next to the bed, and a small dresser can be found against another wall. A simple desk sits near a window that overlooks the town of Bree. The room is decorated with the trappings of a half-elf cleric, with several holy symbols adorning the walls and a set of prayer beads hanging from the bedpost. A thick rug covers the floor, adding a touch of warmth and comfort to the space. Overall, the room is modest but well-kept, reflecting the orderly and disciplined lifestyle of Melchor.
119730: The Housekeeper looks fed up with her job. She scowls at you unhappily.

Concealed behind silky curtains is this cosy, chamber filled with soft pillows and furs. Various small scented candles and incense burn slowly giving the room an exotic combination of dancing shadows and elegant aromas. Clearly the intent here was to create an atmosphere that makes one yearn for physical satisfaction. Pictures of beautiful females, rather scantly dressed, can be seen on the walls. Xile, the master of this house, clearly has a taste for every race, from graceful elves and beautiful women to even a bearded but enticing-looking dwarf.
119731:
A large fountain, made from grey stone, pours water from its centre.
A doorwarden stands here ready to obey his master's wishes.

A stunning staircase leads into the chamber below, seemingly made of the purest of white marble. It apparently is of dwarven make. A crystal chandelier hangs from the ceiling, while several trophies and various gleaming weapons of war hang along the walls.
119732: A humble man stands here, ready to help you with your things.

This vast cavern stretches several feet in every direction. The only exit is the spiral stone stair case, rising up from the center of this circular underground room. the surface of the floor, walls, and ceiling are covered in a glossy smooth black marble. The craftsmanship is of such quality that the transitions of the surfaces are indiscernible, an obvious sign that the stonework was crafted by a master mason. Set in the floor at the bottom of the staircase is a large mithril mural depicting a hammer crowned by 3 stars. Behind the staircase is a four-poster bed composed of the bedrock itself, and topped by a thick feather mattress. The posts stretch all the way to the ceiling, and carved into them are many intricate designs of rose vines. These designs are likewise comprised of mithril, embedded into the stone of the posts. The stone of the bed is likewise covered with the same seamless black marble that covers the surfaces in the rest of the room. Several Bookcases line the walls, and a large fireplace is set into the wall at the foot of the bed.
119733: A humble man stands here, ready to help you with your things.

Passing through the gate a sheltered garden is hidden away from the world here. All around the scent of delicate flowers and herbs are noticed, with a peaceful sound of gently running water. At a glance the garden is lovingly cared for in an effort to create a quiet, peaceful place to rest.
119734: A perceptive Dunadan sentinel stands on duty here, watching over the stable.

The stable is neat and orderly, with a large gate leading into the city on the southern wall. The gate is made from thick cedar that was painted white besides for the black posts that were used as a cross-brace for support. Two stalls, both equally large stand side by side along the western wall of the stable. The stalls were simply made, with one black post set in front of them where they connect that rises to the ceiling; two small lanterns hang from the black post, one on each side to provide each stall in the stable a dim light. A simple door leading beyond the stable is in the north-east corner.
119735: The walls were formed from solid stone and painted dark grey with a white crown moulding that has a beautiful marquetry design along the ceiling. Silver stones in the corners of the moulding were embedded and shimmer softly, creating a very relaxing ambience to the home. A large mirror with a black, hand-crafted frame hangs on the eastern wall and two shiny and black sconces are on the wall with a door between them to the south. A soft black carpet covers the marbled white floor in the centre of the room and a bed in a black metal frame stands against the northern wall. Along the western wall is a tall table with two chairs; the chairs are silver and glossy, with black cushions covering them, contrasting from the sheer and silver fabric that covers the entranceway next to the dining area.
119736: A Dunadan bodyguard stands here with an impassive expression on his face.

Silver railings trace the terrace on three sides and are covered in slender strands of green ivy, with periwinkle blooms in the shape of tiny bells. Four diamond-shaped pillars rise in each corner of the terrace, black and made of stone, each with a silver basin at the top. A brilliant white flame rises from each basin, providing a light and some warmth throughout the terrace. A little hammock is suspended from the eve of the roof to the east where the terrace railings connect to a stone building. A beautiful mural of a large and daunting mountain range was painted on the wall behind the swaying hammock, with each star painted above shimmering from some type of magic. A silver fabric was used to cover the entranceway to the east.
119737: The rushing torrent rages westward, threatening to sweep away all in its path. The river is shallow and icy cold -- its source cannot be too much farther in the mountains. The sides of the river are lined with slick and treacherous rocks, precluded any hope of exiting it here.
119738: The river pounds westward, leaving a shallow gorge to the east. The shallow water is full of sharp rocks and dangerous rapids, so extreme caution is required in order to successfully manoeuvre.
119739: Just below the surface a large bed of pebbles threatens to ground your craft. Without any large rocks to create turbulance the river moves swiftly over the small rocks.
119740:
A large bulletin board, entitled "Numenorean Chronicles", is mounted here.
A fine marble chessboard with ivory and ebony pieces is set here.
A steward of lost Numenor stands here, ready to assist you into a room.

In this place you hear the echoes of things that have gone by. If you wish to again become an active part of the tales of MUME type 'leave', otherwise just sit and remember... A large sign is posted on the wall for you to read.
119741: A mailbox stands here stuffed full of messages.
This mailbox is located in a shady grove, shielded from direct sunlight. There are signs that people have camped here.
119742: At the end of the dark, damp and forgotten crypt with its old and cracked stones lies a shimmering, pure pool. The water is perfectly smooth, like the surface of a polished mirror and shines with a clean and clear light from within. Like nothing else this pool reflects all the things the people of Numenor has lost.
119743: A humble man stands here, ready to help you with your things.

The skylight lounge nestled in the top of the highest tree in the wood, and it is made entirely out of glass that allows the natural light to come in. The ceiling is very high and the furniture is very comfortable. There is a small fire pit in the middle of the room and plenty of places to sit and relax. A bar is also situated in one corner of the room, and a dance floor in another.
119744: A humble man stands here, ready to help you with your things.

The floor of this room is covered in course sand, mixed with dry mud. The southern end of the room is open to the sky, giving a clear path for the sun to beat down within. A pool of dark water lays beneath the window, emanating the foul stench of death. A few deep tracks lead through the sand into the depths.
119745:
A large warhorse is standing here, clad in mail.
A humble man stands here, ready to help you with your things.

The centre of the room is occupied by a big table full of books, bottles, and other items that clearly indicate that this is the house of someone playing with magic, definitely without a care about tidying up. In one corner lies a single unmade bed. In front of the bed, hung on the wall, there is painting of an elf in the middle of a thunderstorm.
119746: An ancient black altar stands in the centre of the room.

This seems to be the main hall of the temple, the place where the worshippers gathered to pray and to make sacrifice. A black altar rises in the centre of the room, and far above it in the domed roof of the hall there is a louver to let the smoke out. No fire is burning on the altar now, and yet the air seems to be heavy with its dark smoke. An arch in the southern wall leads into a dimly-lit hallway. In the back of the room there is a small door, half-hidden in the dark.
119747: A humble man stands here, ready to help you with your things.

Somewhat unusual for Hobbits, this dwelling is above ground. Framed with solid timber and built with tight stonework, this cottage is seemingly very well constructed. The air is thick with herbs and spices, giving the room a distinctly medicinal smell. A large cooking fireplace takes up one corner of the room with a massive copper cauldron slowly boiling some kind of chunky stew. Several tables and cupboards in the room contain a large collection of spices, liquids, and all manner of vegetables.The most striking feature of this tidy home is a large, iron-banded trapdoor set into the middle of the earthen floor.
119748: A set of beautiful wooden stairs leads down into a large, well-appointed smial. The earthen walls are rubbed completely smooth, appearing as if made from a rich, polished dark-brown wood. There are several round windows that overlook the Brandywine that light the room and fill it with the pleasant sound of rushing water. Well-appointed furniture, luxurious carpets, and plush pillows fill the room. A large wooden table dominates the center the space and is covered with all manner of pastries, cheeses, meats, and other mouthwatering delicacies. Innumerable mathoms, pictures, mementos, and other ephemera fill large shelves against the walls. A tastefully molded corridor continues west towards another room.
119749: The bedroom is spacious and inviting, constructed of rich wood paneling that creates a cozy and luxurious atmosphere. At the center of the room stands a large four-poster bed constructed from mahogany and draped in burgundy-colored silk curtains. Soft, plush pillows and a thick duvet cover the luxurious bed. A beautiful fireplace made of aged stone radiates welcoming warmth. Two plush armchairs and a small table are arranged around the fireplace, offering a comfortable seating area for reading or relaxing by the fire. Like the rest of the home, the bedroom is well-appointed and tastefully decorated. In one corner sits a large wooden wardrobe adorned with intricate carvings. Within the wardrobe are several leather pouches and wooden boxes, each filled with trinkets and tiny treasures from faraway lands.
119752:
A white-painted bench is here.
A squirrel scampers around here, looking for nuts from the trees.
A guard of Bree stands here.

A large black stone, jagged and sharp, dominates the centre of the grove. All around it, short grass spreads out as if from the stone itself. A faint dirt path approaches the stone. The whole area is enclosed by a circle of tall dark trees.
119753:
A heavy desk, made of solid oak, stands here.
A large stone fireplace with a roaring fire warms the room.
A humble man stands here, ready to help you with your things.

Golden lettering and pictures that sparkle in the light cover the dark walls of this circular council chamber. This must be the working place of someone very important. Dwarven runes, written in gold, cover most of the stonework in the room. In the centre of the room a majestic, octagonal table is placed, circled by mahogany chairs. A particularly large and shining gem is noticed within the centre of the table and was placed into a beautiful stand of gold.
119754:
A light carpet covers the floor.
A humble man stands here, ready to help you with your things.

The floors, ceiling, and walls of this room are made from solid wood. The floor is a warm golden-amber colour with a bright sheen from careful oiling. A few different types of wood make up the walls, interrupted occasionally by solid oak beams. The ceiling seems to be mainly spruce boards, carefully fit between the beams.
119755: A humble man stands here, ready to help you with your things.

The scent in this room suggests that the master of the house likes herbs - yet no plants are visible. Instead, only a few small metal bars and gems lie on top of a shining anvil which has obviously seen a lot of usage. Other than that the house is empty.
119756: A tall and proud elf is standing here.

Deep inside the mallorn crown and high up the trunk a wooden platform encircles this ancient tree. Hardly two hand-spans wide, the flet is placed precariously among the weaker tree-top branches, its only support. A truly breath-taking view opens to the south of here. Another smaller flet can be distinguished far down the tree from here.
119757: Deep inside the mallorn crown and high up the trunk a wooden platform encircles this ancient tree. Hardly two hand-spans wide, the flet is placed precariously among the weaker tree-top branches, its only support. The Misty Mountains raise threateningly to the west and north, barring the view of Eregion and other lands beyond.
119758: Deep inside the mallorn crown and high up the trunk a wooden platform encircles this ancient tree. Hardly two hand-spans wide, the flet is placed precariously among the weaker tree-top branches, its only support. A spectacular view opens south and east from here onto the empty lands beyond the rivers.
119759: Deep inside the mallorn crown and high up the trunk a wooden platform encircles this ancient tree. Hardly two hand-spans wide, the flet is placed precariously among the weaker tree-top branches, its only support. The golden forest stretches far and wide, and this perch provides one a view even beyond the northern and eastern borders of Lorien.
119764: A Noldorin elf is here, guarding the line of Feanor.

The walls of this chamber are rough hewn stone, chipped haphazardly out of the surrounding walls. A soft, green glow can be seen permeating the room, but the source cannot be determined. Daggers, crossbows, and bows are shoved in the corners, with a giant table stacked with scrolls taking up the majority of the space. A family lineage map is carved into the stone walls, showing the line of Feanor. The last entry on the map shows the name Fea, decorated with a sinuous snake.
119765:
An elderly druid is here, willing to share his knowledge (glowing).
A beautiful and docile horse is standing here.

Several small trees rise from the surrounding grasslands, conspicuous for their height in an area that is otherwise flat. The trees are spaced some distance from each other, their branches barely touching. Near the trunk of the largest tree the grass has been worn down to dirt and a simple fire pit, ringed with stones, has been built in the very centre of the clearing with a small tent erected alongside.
119766:
An old, retired warrior is waiting here, eager to share his knowledge.
An old man walks around slowly, deep in thought.
A rugged-looking man is standing here.

Unmistakably this is the home of a once-great warrior. A warg-fur rug is stretched out in front of the hearth and a selection of battered weapons hang on the walls. A particularly large flail stands out from the rest and can only have been made for a troll, presumably one killed by the home's owner. A plain desk sits against the far wall while a rocking chair is given pride of place in front of the fire.
119767:
A circular stone well has been built here.
A young apprentice is here hard at work.
A little boy is here, running around.

This is the backyard of the blacksmith's workshop and a wooden canopy extends from the side of the building to provide shelter over part of the yard. Beneath the canopy the raw materials required by the smith have been piled; coal for the furnace, bars of iron and pre-cut wooden poles to be used as handles for tools.
119768:
A small flask has been left here on the ground.
There are two notes here.
A large grocer is here, waiting to buy or sell some goods.

While the shop may be small it is packed from floor to ceiling with all manner of items, most of them stored in dusty boxes upon wooden shelves. It certainly seems as if few people have bought much of the shopkeeper's stock recently. Hooks screwed into the roof timbers have been used to hang leather goods which gives the shop its characteristic smell.
119770: The passageway leading down is covered by various sized pieces of gravel and tiny pebbles. It is extremely steep, leading further beneath the mound. Due to the passageway being slanted at such a great angle, without any bumps or grooves, the footing is dangerous because of all the loose pieces of gravel. It appears that further down there is a junction of some kind in the shape of a fork, with two dark holes leading in different directions. The ceiling is quite high at this point, and there seems to be another tunnel entrance on the eastern wall, too far above to be reached.
119771:
Some thick writhing vines whip all around you.
A mass of wriggling vines drops on you from the trees.

The forest has many kinds of trees, all varying in their sizes. The trunks of these trees are very large and the bark covering them is thick with different textures. The undergrowth is very dense under the trees that are growing on the eastern side. Large ferns stand out among all of the undergrowth, due to the soft green colour that they have. A lot of moss can be seen growing thickly along the ground here.
119772: Thick, wet, and nutrient-rich from river runoff, the mud in this part of the forest provides just enough anchorage to hold the roots of the oak trees that grow here. Decomposing leaves and branches add to the richness of the soil, providing a safe haven for swamp-dwelling grasses. To the north, the ground becomes more stable and drier, and the thickness of the forest increases in that direction as several trees block any further view.
119773:
A mass of dark green leaves clings to a wall.
An elven Marchwarden is here, vigilantly guarding Lothlorien's borders.
An elven Marchwarden is here, vigilantly guarding Lothlorien's borders.

Thick patches of moss grow on the ground, encircling the mighty trunks of the trees which are coloured in green with a few tones of brown. Vines travel up the trees, hiding themselves in the leafy branches above. The undergrowth is thick, causing travel through to be quite difficult when on foot. Debris is scattered all over the ground, most of it being dried-up leaves and broken branches. An aged looking tower is camouflaged by the forest to the north. There are no paths leading to this tower and the forest has almost engulfed it. Vines have scaled their path up the tower walls as well and small strands of ivy are draped over the top of the door frame.
119774:
The remains of a thick tangle of vines lie here in a heap of rotting compost.
A sturdy pack horse is standing here.
A sturdy pack horse is standing here.
Sinor the elven ranger is here, ready for duty.

Surrounded by large, dark trees, a nearly perfectly round place opens up here. Thick vines with strong twines grow up the trees and connect them to each other so that they appear like a green wall. Despite their form, there is no sign of the trees having been arranged by any other means than nature. However, there are signs of the opening being used as a stable. A wooden construction reaching high above the ground, consisting of four poles covered with wooden planks, serves as a roof to protect the mounts from rain. Three smaller but massive poles beside three wooden feeders mark the places for each mount to be bound to. Nearby the feeders, there is a large dunghill, consisting of both older and quite fresh dung.
119775:
Maheel the elven Captain is here, observing those he is responsible for.
An elven Marchwarden is here, vigilantly guarding Lothlorien's borders.
An elven Marchwarden is here, vigilantly guarding Lothlorien's borders.
Sinor the elven ranger is here, ready for duty.

The tower walls are made of black stone laid in a circular fashion. Each stone appears to have been carved almost flawlessly, while white mortar was used to seal them together tightly. The mortar is not very bright in contrast due to dirt and dust settled upon the walls along the years. The frame which embraces the entrance door into the tower is made of a white-speckled stone and is of an unrivalled design. Along the wall are several candleholders, and the eastern wall has a staircase which begins its climb upward in a spiralling manner. It was made of the same black stone, with the exception of white, flat stone overlays highlighting each step. White stone pillars scale up along the staircase in a few select places.
119778: The staircase ascends into the top of the watch tower from here, and descends back to the entrance below. Candleholders are hung on the wall aligned with the spiral staircase, each giving their own glint of light from a white candle that has been placed into the holder. Black stone was used to make the stairs, and overlaying each stair is a flat and thin white-coloured stone. There are a few white stone pillars climbing upwards against the staircase, helping to keep its place tightly against the tower walls. The pillars come to an end at the ceiling, adding support to the large sheet of black slate.
119779: Rehan the elven ranger is here, ready for duty.

The tower belvedere graces those on watch with visibility of the area which surrounds the tower. The walls are of black stone, and a large sheet of black-grooved slate lies as the flooring of the belvedere. An opening in the slate turns into a spiral staircase, leading down to the base of the tower. In the centre stands a low table made of a dark wood. There is a steel basin sitting on this table, oval in shape, with a handle on each side. The ceiling is made of another massive sheet of black slate, similar to the material used for the floor. Four circular openings were carved into the tower walls and lined with an iron frame to stabilise the surrounding stones.
119780: A water barrel has been left here.

The corridor is not well lit, and what light does exist, is very dim. A black stone was used in the making of this underground corridor, while the flooring is a solid, large piece of black slate. The floor is not entirely flat, and the slate has a glossy appearance to its finish. Tall stands of black steel line the corridor, with openings at the top for placing large torches to add some light into the gloom.
119781: The corridor stretches ahead, crafted from black stone. The floor, a single, imposing slab of black slate, adds an element of sleekness to the passage. Despite the unevenness of the floor. Towering stands made of black steel flank the corridor, each equipped with openings at the top to hold large torches.
119787:
An elven Marchwarden is here, vigilantly guarding Lothlorien's borders.
An elven Marchwarden is here, vigilantly guarding Lothlorien's borders.

Impeccably crafted, the walls of the checkpoint consist of black stone bricks, showcasing their sturdy construction. Similar in material yet distinct in shape, the floor is adorned with individual tiles. Towards the western end of the chamber, the checkpoint culminates in a massive black slate wall.
119788: An underwater river pulls its contents southward through a narrow tunnel, enveloping them in a claustrophobic embrace. The murky waters and relentless rush flow through the confined passage of black stone, emanating the strength and power of a mighty river. Resisting the current would guide one back to solid ground, away from the watery depths.
119800: A sturdy crate made of nailed wooden planks sits on the floor.

Silent and veiled in an aura of tranquility, the chamber unveils wooden crates adorned with delicate elven engravings. The walls breathe with tapestries depicting woodland scenes, while the floor, fashioned from smoothly hewn stone, carries the grace of Lothlorien craftsmanship. A huge piece of slate forms the ceiling. At the north end is a staircase leading upwards through the slate.
119801:
Some ugly blow-flies are buzzing around here.
A large rabbit looks peacefully at you, ready to dart away.

A low, yet dense forest grows towards the south, where the tops of various trees intermingle to form a palette of dark greens. The ground here is hilly, with a few large rocks protruding from the ground. Towards the west, a thick, natural wall of jagged rocks thrusts up from the ground.
119802: A crack in the heart of the mountain widens here for some unknown reason. Above, it quickly narrows and is impassable. Just below, an underground stream has broken through the wall, filling it with water that drains into the unknown depths below.
119803:
A timetable for the coach to Tharbad has been nailed on to a wall.
A large torch lies here among the dust.
There is an old street-lamp on the border of the street.
A wealthy merchant is slowly strolling around here.
A simple servant quietly walks around, performing his duties.

You stand under a big red sign which proclaims that you are at the entrance to the well-known inn called 'The Crown of Arnor', or as people say around these parts, just 'The Crown'. Some oxcarts have been parked here, and presumably their drivers are inside enjoying a nice, hot meal.
119804: The passage is running even deeper into the heart of the Redhorn northwards, where it appears to soon bend to the left. To the south, a flickering torch can be seen. Smoke eminates from the dark grotto to the east as well as the sound of trickling water. The passage floor is worn out of regular use, with few occasional sharper rocks still remaining here and there.
119805:
A pair of vambraces, reflecting the light brightly, lie here (glow blue).
A pair of brightly shining greaves are on the ground (glow blue).

White and pure the marble encases you, and eerily the shadows play on the floor and walls and ceiling. No columns adorn this chamber, no decoration of any kind was placed here, but the unearthly beauty of the stone walls surrouding you is entrancing. Fine veins of lighter and darker coloured marble play across the surface, like a web of an insane spider. No exits or breaches in the wall can be seen, save for the door made of steel and ilthinaur in the south wall.
119821:
A great helm, in the form of a dragon, sits on the ground (glows blue).
A massive axe of Dwarven make has been placed here (glows blue).

The walls and ceiling of this chamber are made of beaten gold. On each wall there is a depiction of a dwarf doing some noble event. A golden light fills the room, undoubtably a reflection from the walls. The floor is plain, dark grey stone. To the west is a gold door.
119822: The low hills are slowly turning into a flatter landscape. The uneven, dark soil appears nutritious, as the flora here is rich. Beech and oak grow rather densely, yet leave enough room for bushes and vines to claim their presence. The hills continue their expansion in the north, while the south leads deeper into the dark forest of Mirkwood.
119823: The birch and oak reach to staggering heights in the west and south, creating a fortified, natural wall. The barely discernible north-south trail makes a turn here, leading east along the forest barrier. A great spider web spans across two tree-tops. It is littered with dead insects and moths of various sizes. The remains of a small animal have fallen to the ground, the skeleton almost completely buried in the dirt. A stench of decay encompasses the whole forest. To the north the forest opens up into some dark hills.
119824: A Path along the Forest Wall

The massive beeches have grown into each other, separated only by a modest path at their bases. The grand crowns sway restlessly on the mossy trunks of the trees. The path makes its way through Mirkwood forest, slowly zigzagging from the east and extending its way to the west. Great trees stand tall to the south, blocking any passage in that direction. Mirkwood forest in all its dreariness opens up for yet another few leagues to the north.
119825:
The corpse of a watersnake is lying here.
A skeleton is lying here half-buried in the mud.

Brown, murky mud floats all around, making it difficult to tell where the water of this pond actually ends and the bottom starts. The dark water is dense, full of dirty sediment, rotten algae and other particles. The muddy bottom is engulfing, making it hard to move around - or to the surface!
119833:
An albino fish is swimming here, looking for some food.
An albino fish is swimming here, looking for some food.

The shaft is completely flooded with with glacial water; lumps of ice float lazily to the surface. You can climb your way up or down along the ladder, but you cannot survive this shivering cold for long. Below you the tunnel is filled in with great boulders.
119834: You are at the end of a wide road leading into a spacious cavern. The road is pocked by large craters and widening cracks, but still you can see the care and skill with which it was formed. To the west a stately cavern gracefully opens to receive the road. To the east the road ends abruptly at a sheer cliff, the work of some avalanche or giant's rage in ages long since passed.
119836: A humble man stands here, ready to help you with your things.

Glossy white trim with an intricate design carved into it runs along the top of this room where the walls meet the ceiling, with traces of silver embedded throughout the wood. The walls are painted a light colour grey and appearing swirled to add some texture. Several small and silver sconces decorate the walls, each sconce holding a slender white candle that was left burning. Bows of an experienced huntress are suspended on the western wall, with easy access if needed for battle or war, close to the door. Below the bows is a tall and slender vase that is black as night, filled with a variety of arrows. Along the east side of the room is a bed and small table next to it, with several daggers on display upon black pegs that are fastened to the wall.
119837:
A sturdy bed made from solid oak lies here, covered in warm blankets.
An Elven steward stands here, watching over the household.

This is magically invented abode. The enchanted ceiling changes its shape biased on running time from a lavender blue sky with the golden beam, giving the room a natural light during day, to a dark blue of night with inner silver moonshine and thousands of fine stars. The flooring looks simply - a lawn, but it is as nice as cozy. A semi-large mahagony bed, embellished with fine jewels of multi-colours, stands at the western wall. Among it, fixed to the wall, is a pine shelf with miscellaneous sort of herbs, scrolls and potions. Opposite it is a large window with enchanted glass, giving a clear view of the outside area. Right of it is an oak cabinet filled with fashioned clothes, magical artifacts, rings and necklaces. Left of the window is a tall bookcase carrying widely very old looking books. In the middle of the northern wall stands a grated fireplace, which gives a fine warm to the room. The southeastern corner gives a huge space for a weapon racks and armour made of shiny unknown metal. An oak doorway leads southwards to the balcony.
119838:
A humble man stands here, ready to help you with your things.
A tall and strong guard is here.
A tall and strong guard is here.

This room is the bedchamber of half-elven war hero Columbia. The room itself has precise quadrate dimensions, its walls are high and made out of mahogany from the forest of Fangorn. Burgundy-coloured bookshelves fill the western side of the room, facing two enormous portraits adjacent to the door. The enchanted glass floor emits a bright, glowing light, creating a warm and cosy atmosphere.
119839:
A fine marble chessboard with ivory and ebony pieces is set here.
A large encrusted cedar chest is standing here.
A heavy desk, made of solid oak, stands here.
A large stone fireplace with a roaring fire warms the room.
A sturdy bed made from solid oak lies here, covered in warm blankets.

An echoing and humming sound is heard upon entering this sacred place which is surrounded by a very faint glow. The bedroom of the High Priest Columbia is a peaceful sanctum for both meditation and wisdom. The space here is full of oak furniture containing ancient scrolls, crystals, and artifacts that emit a soft blue glow. The low walls, mahogany floor and mirror ceiling create an alluring warm atmosphere for study and resting.
119840:
A sturdy bed made from solid oak lies here, covered in warm blankets.
A humble man stands here, ready to help you with your things.

This chamber is made out of wood from some black pine tree. The dark colours of the room are contrasted by a marble altar standing in the middle of the room. There is a bed in one of the corners, a desk with a chair next to the window, and a large bookshelf standing against one of the walls. The window shows the beautiful scenery of Rivendell.
119841: A humble man stands here, ready to help you with your things.

In a silent corner of the winding building is a surprisingly spacious abode, perfect for a small bed. The room is decorated sparsely with a handful of maps, many of which are faded and hardly recognisable due to heavy usage. A bookshelf, worn at the edges as if itself had once been read from cover to cover, is the other singular piece of furniture. A tidy and clean atmosphere sets the surroundings. A selection of aged, yet clean rugs, slightly mismatched in colour have been placed carefully across the floor, small areas of pine appearing among the gaps, creating the impression of wooden slats between the fading colours. Cutting across the ceiling is a single bolt of lightning, carved into the granite roof, appearing to lack the deliberate care of the rest of the room.
119842: A humble man stands here, ready to help you with your things.

The timber-framed building has a thatched roof, with a detailed cornice along all of the walls that borders the ceiling. The ornamental cornice has several oak leaves carved upon it. The flooring materials that were used appear to be made of some type of wood that has a rare, chalky-white finish and slightly textured.
119843: The valiant statue of an Elf wielding a bow stands here.

The memorial shrine is lit with torches that lead down a short hall to a statue of the finest dark marble. The statue stands at the end of the hall under a dome that opens upwards. The marble dome has been masterfully covered in murals depicting the valiant life of Tahimik Pagtulog from childhood to fatherhood.
119844: Herbs have every variety seem to grow here, but they are hard to distinguish admist the mass of weeds sprouting up across the garden. Clearly no one has tended to the plot in some time. A small gravel path connects the gate to the east to a small wooden building to the west.
119845: A humble man stands here, ready to help you with your things.

Tools of every variety are scattered around this workshop. Most lie strewn across a great wooden bench that takes up half the room, but others are stacked in corners, or just dropped in the middle of the floor. A small layer of sawdust covers every available surface, include a thin cloth pallet that lies against one wall.
119846: Jaak's Treehouse among the Living Vines

A small loyal cat is here, covered in fluffy orange fur.
A humble man stands here, ready to help you with your things.

This comfortable room seems alive due to the walls being covered in a manner of all green, growing plants that thrive with the love and care of an Elf. Vines and ivy cover the walls, their slender tendrils dance into the air as one moves past them. The room is lit by crystal lamps in the corners, and a cosy bed that stands alongside one wall; promising the comfort for the owner of this home. Several thick vines have been intertwined to be used as a ladder that leads up into the room above.
119847: This relaxing lounge is dominated by lush vegetation and potted plants. An elf who loves nature and growing things clearly spends a lot of time here. In the middle of the room is an ornate table with a large jar made of the finest silver. Leaning closer, the smell of the best pipe-weed the shire can produce permeates the air here. A carved wooden rack filled with different pipes are on display and comfy chairs are placed about the room. Near the rack is a small opening in the floor leading into the room below, with intertwined vines that are being used as a ladder.
119848: Aurora's Brilliant Prism among the Clouds

A row of prismatic crystal lanterns beams a brilliant rainbow of light throughout the brightly coloured room. In one corner, a shrine to the Maia Dawnborn sits, covered in the dust of disuse. A low couch dominates one side of the room where esoteric magic tomes are piled. A faint scent of Old Toby fills the air around the couch. A cabinet for arms and armour occupies another part of the room, while artfully placed mirrors scatter brilliant light in a seemingly infinite display of rainbow brilliance.
119849: Ayl's Hall of Elven Treasures and Trinkets

A room full of heavy ironbound chests and piles of assorted valuables, scattered herbs, and detritus at first suggest the holdings of a somewhat organised troll, but this is the wealth of a compulsive elf. Almost every part of the room is filled with enough wealth and supplies to equip armies, yet it gathers dust to soothe the ego of the owner. In one corner, a bed covered in cloaks and armour sits, with just enough room cleared to barely sleep. A pile of lembas nearby with some half empty wine bottles completes the scene.
119850: The room is small and square, with a high ceiling. The walls are made of thick vines, covered in thorns. The air is damp and musty, and the air whistling between gaps in the vines sounds vaguely of screams. The walls move ever so slightly in and out, as if the breathing of a sleeping nightmare. In regular intervals are sets of smaller vines affixed to the walls. The floor is covered in a thick layer of moss. Here and there a large thorn pokes through the moss almost in an attempt to trip those unaware. The only light comes from a very small porthole high up on the wall with a criss-cross of vines preventing egress. In the centre of the room is a single chair made of vines and the seat is a mesh of soft moss. Blocking the only point of exit is a large, thick wooden door. Stretching across the door from each direction are large vines as slide locks, preventing passage.
119851: A humble man stands here, ready to help you with your things.

This round chamber at the bottom level of the tower is quite empty and ascetic, giving the feeling that the owner is someone who journeys a lot. The only furniture in the room are a bed, a table and a chair. There are some writings on the wall, appearing to list the orcs that this wizard has slain in the battle. A distant, magical aura lies in the room.
119852: A humble man stands here, ready to help you with your things.

The room is simple. One cannot see much furniture inside - merely a bed, a chair and a table. Further investigation reveals several drawings, maps, and an array of weapons, filling the walls of this dimly lit lodge. Nothing else can be seen, only an old carpet covering the floor.
119853: A humble man stands here, ready to help you with your things.

This is a small and yet simple abode, with a white marble altar placed at the northern corner of the room. A grey, indistinct carpet covers the stone floor, marking the walkway from the entrance of this chamber to the altar itself. A few lanterns have been set in small niches alongside the walls, providing a permanent light source, yet otherwise the walls are grey and bare.
119854: A rounded tunnel slopes steeply into the dark inside of the hill. A layer of smooth rubble covers the floor, making it impossible to stand up. The only way of getting out of here is to continue sliding downwards into the dark deeps.
119855:
A pallet covered in a variety of thick, soft furs sits against one wall.
A humble man stands here, ready to help you with your things.
Thick slabs of stone make up the walls of this chamber, obviously brought here at great expense from some western mountain. The stone is rough, covered in sharp protrusions and pocked depressions.
119883: A natural grotto opens up here, with protruding stalactites and stalagmites clustered in rows like a huge gaping maw of sharp, dripping fangs. Moisture dripping down the stalactites makes an eerie echo as it drips into clear puddles and pools. There is a tunnel slanting back up to the surface, but it is smooth as glass, and very steep; a climb fit only for the most skilled. Several narrow, twisting, tube-like tunnels have been somehow bored into the solid rock by some manner which you cannot divine.
119884:
The corpse of a hungry warg is lying here.
The corpse of a ferocious reptile is lying here.
A giant brown turtle is peeking from under its shell.

Shallow puddles of water lie in broad pools across most of the floor of this cavern. The air is moist and thick. The dripping of water from the ceiling creates a continual string of soft echoes that combine with each other to form an effect that is both soothing and oddly disconcerting.
119885:
The corpse of a ferocious reptile is lying here.
The corpse of a ferocious reptile is lying here.

A single huge stalagmite dominates the centre of this large, fairly circular cavern, flanked by a retinue of smaller stalagmites. The overall effect of this formation suggests some sort of intelligent design, but more likely it is merely a matter of randomness upon occasion falling into patterns that suggest a pattern to one's conscious mind.
119886: An albino salamander is here, perched on some rocks.

This irregularly shaped cavern is wide and has a low undulating roof, which rises only about ten feet above the floor. The surrounding rock is the same pale, sometimes greenish limestone that forms the rest of this cavern network.
119887: The rough limestone walls of the cavern have been smoothed somewhat by the steady action of water seeping from the ceiling and sides of the cave. There are fewer stalactites here, but some blunted spires and nodules have been formed from the depositing of dissolved sediments.
119888:
A giant, thickly scaled lizard is here.
A giant, thickly scaled lizard is here.
A giant, thickly scaled lizard is here.
A large beaver is here, gnawing on a piece of wood.
A large black bat flitters near you.

The tunnel opens up into startling sight: a grotto embellished with a plethora of glittering stalactites hung like fairy-tale icicles in pastoral shades. The whole scene seems out of place in this otherwise foreboding environ, but nonetheless the enchantment of the place is palpable.
119889: A skeleton of some humanoid lies in the dust.

This entire cavern is suffused with a powerful, dank odour emanating strongly from several piles of heaped debris in one corner. Untidy piles of broken bones line the damp, mould-infested limestone walls. The ceiling is low, with short, sharp stalactites viciously threatening to scrape any unprotected scalp.
119890:
A small campfire burns here, its low flames giving off only a little light.
The corpse of a hungry warg is lying here.

Far beneath the earth, this damp cave has smooth limestone walls glistening faintly with embedded flecks of mica. An icy-cold pool of black water dominates the centre of the cave. From an undetermined direction comes the faint sound of rapidly rushing water.
119891: A copper penny lies on the ground.

The intricacy of this entanglement of brush creates an almost mystifying network of snarled passages, which dart to and fro in the vegetation. The paths have probably been created by wildlife inhabitants of this greenery, although none can be seen and no other sounds than a low rustling of grass can be heard. Reaching far above the tall brush blocks the view to the surrounding areas.

A large bulletin board, entitled "Trawl Bored", is mounted here.
A fine marble chessboard with ivory and ebony pieces is set here.
An ancient she-troll awaits her next meal.

Long ago, in the endless dungeons of his Hell of Iron, Melkor spawned the troll race. Angband was destroyed in the War of Wrath, swallowed by the sea with the land of Beleriand. But this black and desolate pit somehow survived, far beneath the ocean, a last remnant of a once mighty fortress of evil. And in this dark and foul chasm you find yourself, for a time, confined, unable to participate in the ongoing wars of Middle-earth. A grubby and tattered sign is posted on the wall for you to read.
119957: A Cramped Corner of the Pit
A mailbox stands here stuffed full of messages.

Deep in forgotten places, far beneath the ruined halls of Angband, lies this ash and slag-filled pit. It is no longer a part of the tales of Middle-earth, and yet some news of those lands still manages somehow to reach you here.
119958: This part of the cave is small and even darker than anything else around. In the middle of the room lies a pool that is so dark it draws even your twisted life in. It seems to go right to the darkest, most evil places that lie deep down under Arda, rightly forgotten and full of terrible power.
119959:
A huge clock is standing here.
A doorwarden stands here ready to obey his master's wishes.
A tall and strong guard is here.
A tall and strong guard is here.

The chalky stones have cracked, opening up a sheltered area amongst the rocks. There is a light wind, but the rocks over the top of the natural walkway provide ample protection from the elements. Goosegrass covers the ground and various small insects can be seen flitting aroud.
119960:
A tall and strong guard is here.
A tall and strong guard is here.

There is a smell of mint in this well-kept corridor. Chalk rock cut from the hill protects this hallway even in the most windy nights. On the north wall are murals depicting various joyful scenes and many close friends.
119961:
A sturdy bed made from solid oak lies here, covered in warm blankets.
A large bookshelf sits against the wall.
A heavy desk, made of solid oak, stands here.
An Elven maiden is here, tidying up the room.

A smell of jasmine and other fresh flowers wafts here, quite a contrast to the bleakness of the surroundings. Great care was used to make this room exquisite. Hand-crafted floral arrangements thrive along the sides of the stonework that has been assembled. The open sky grants full access for the sun and rain to bear down on the colourful plant life all around you. There is a cherry-finished bed in the corner, covered on top by a rock wall with different coloured mosses growing on it.
119962:
A large fountain, made from grey stone, pours water from its centre.
A spoon is placed here.
A pan is here, ready for use.
A stove stands against one wall here.
A large stone fireplace with a roaring fire warms the room.
A delicious looking apple tart has been placed here.
A loaf of bread has been left here.
A large piece of cheese has been placed here.
A bowl of salad has been placed here.
A small oaken table has been set here.

This room is easily double the size of all the other rooms combined. Odors of prepared foodstuffs tickle the nose as they rise up and out into the open air above. Several giant stoves are always in use; Baking, stewing, frying and boiling local favorites as well as delicacies from far away lands.
119963: A malicious thug is here, threatening you.

A steep slope of crumbly shale descends downwards from a small, jagged opening that has been covered with uprooted bushes and briars. The slope connects to the bottom of a mossy cavern which branches into dry, water-worn tunnels that cut into the shale bedrock. Boot prints litter the dirt in all directions.
119965:
A small, underground pool sits here crowned by stalactites.
A powerful looking bandit, commanding and menacing, stands here.
A burly bodyguard stands here, a dour expression on his face.
A burly bodyguard stands here, a dour expression on his face.
A burly bodyguard stands here, a dour expression on his face.

A huge cavern that is connected by a network of tunnels has been eroded out of the shale bedrock here. The ceiling and floor of the cavern are covered in red coloured stalagmites and stalactites that surround an underground pool. Tracks lead to other dusty, water-worn tunnels that are large enough to explore.
119966: A patch of moss grows here on a wet, flat stone.

This tunnel is progressively wetter and muddier as it heads downwards into the earth. The mud is slippery and littered with deep tracks alongside evidence of previous travellers slipping. The tunnel opens up into a larger section covered in strange moss before narrowing.
119967:
A neat straw pallet is lying here.
A makeshift table stands here constructed out of several crates.
On the table, there are a piece of smoked, cured meat and a large biscuit.
A malicious thug is here, threatening you.
A malicious thug is here, threatening you.

There is substantial evidence of men camping here in this larger section of the tunnel. A makeshift table covered with cooking supplies surrounds a tiny fire pit. A canvas from a ship's sail has been spread across the ground at the end of the tunnel upon which several straw pallets have been placed for sleeping.
119968: This chamber hewn in the rock has many small alcoves carved in the walls. Dried herbs stashed in them produce a soft aromatic smell that permeates this place. A tall countertop, with three sets of scales in different sizes, lines the north wall. Oak barrels crowd the west corner of the room far from the doors. A set of smoothly polished wooden beams serves as the ceiling.
119969:
An orkish warrior of the Durghash is here, with a cruel glint in his eye.
An orkish warrior of the Durghash is here, with a cruel glint in his eye.
An orkish warrior of the Durghash is here, with a cruel glint in his eye.

An orkish warrior of the Durghash is here, with a cruel glint in his eye.
A commanding Durghash is here, cruelly eyeing the surroundings.
A stone-grey troll advances toward you, with fury in its eyes.

You have entered a medium-sized vaulted chamber in the depths of Khazad-dum. As you look around, you cannot help admiring the great architectural skills of the Dwarves who once built this place: the walls are smooth, the ceiling well balanced, and the two archways leading north and south very ornate. Yet much of the former beauty of this place has been spoiled by the orcs. The floor is covered with broken bones and other disgusting remains of the orcs' victims; the walls have been covered with foul inscriptions, among which you notice many large blood-red circles; even the finely crafted arches have been repeatedly hit with large stone clubs.
119971: A smooth, straight section of tunnel leads from an ornate arch just south of here to a curving upslope far in the north. This passage has obvious dwarven architectural features such as seamless stone joints and polished stone walls, but there have been no dwarves available to maintain it for many centuries. Instead, orcs have done their best to defile the good work done here, covering every available surface with scrawls, crude drawings and tribal symbols used to mark off territories.
119972: This tunnel forks into two smaller, erroded passages that abruptly end in deadends within the shale bedrock. Piles of dusty, sharp rubble hint that there was a cave-in at some point ages ago. Boot prints litter the ground heading down the opposite end of the tunnel.
120017: Tiny ripples move across the surface of the dark and putrid water that fills this hole in the mountain. Black curving stone structures leap smoothly across the ceiling above the lake. Darkness lurks in the corners as if hiding something. From the water rises a faint mist that sweeps across the surface filling every depression in the walls that surrounds the lake.
120018: An ancient fungus smothers the boulders.

The misty air in the cavern clings to the walls building a thin layer of dew that makes the blue rock glisten. A strong stale odour is in the air; combined with the moisture it leaves a strange taste when inhaled. In some spots the walls are covered by a layer of fungi and green moss. Care must be taken not to slip on the wet moss-covered stones that form the floor of the cavern.
120020: A vast stone ceiling looms above the lake. Deep unbroken darkness emerges from dark fissures and deep cracks in the ceiling. Out of the darkness come chilling sounds echoing between the rock and the surface of the water, making the presence of bats very apparent. From where the lake meets the rock can be heard a steady clucking sound as water enters and leaves through hidden cracks in the rock.
120025: The gloomy waters of this dreary lake have a treacherous look to them. The moist air is chilly and filled with wisps of fog rising from the surface of the dark water. High above looms a vast ceiling that catches every sound, casting it back as a dull echo. The putrid water seems to be moving slowly up and down as if it was breathing.
120026: Some cracked and splintered pieces of wood float here.

Above the dark lake rises a vast stone ceiling concealed in darkness. The edge of the water is barely discernible in the deep gloom where all details seem to be interfluent and without any definition. The cold water is slowly rising and falling, as if something below it was breathing. The surrounding cavern walls are torn with deep fissures and long cracks, and as the water folds around the rock in its repetitive movement, tiny ripples are sent across the lake.
120037:
A small, wooden warning sign has been firmly placed here.
A huge black fungus is here, exuding a foul stench (red aura).

Water drips from the ceiling all around you, falling into small puddles on the ground. At your feet, small rivulets of water flow gently across the cold stone floor. On the walls grow thick layers of moss wreathing around black moulds. The damp air is heavy and so hard to breathe that gasping for air seems mandatory.
120038: This passage is worn, but it does not appear to be used at all by the dwarves of the Blue Mountains. A coating of dust and thick cobwebs covers the floor, and behind cracks and fissures in the broken rock, eyes of tiny spiders seem to be staring in your direction.
120052: In the narrow tunnel black walls surround you in a deep darkness. The air is chokingly dense and fills your mouth with an acidic taste as you breathe. Grey and black cobwebs span across the tunnel sending loose ends out towards you. The air greeting you from the south feels even denser.
120053: The darkness seems to be alive, as if slowly creeping nearer and nearer, trying to exhaust hope, quench bravery and instil fear among all who venture into its dark embrace. There is a feeling in the air of years of suppressed anger ready to explode in dark rage. Inky shadows in the blackness flit around, peering coldly into your soul with a paralysing determination. An opening covered with thick dark threads of spider webs lies to the east, emanating an almost palpable feeling of misfortune.
120054: You are in a broad cavern deep in the underground beneath the Blue Mountains. Between cracked shards aimed at you, the broken floor is littered with bones and torn fabric in many colours. Across the cavern span sticky webs spun by the dark minds of the spiders lurking nearby, waiting only for their trap to close on you. An empowering darkness seems to emanate from the webs.
120055: In the dark lair the presence of spiders is apparent from the many cobwebs strung from the ceiling to the floor. The threads are black and if viewed at certain angles they are nearly invisible as if designed to lure the prey towards captivity. A fusty smell of rotten flesh and acidulous moisture greets the beholder. A deep darkness gradually closes in, making any sense of direction vague and the image of the broken stone walls blurry.
120056: The rocky cavern walls, covered by layers of spider webs, loom deceptively around you. The smell in the lair is horrible. A mixture of rotting flesh and mouldy fabrics torn to pieces litters the floor. Darkness surrounds you with a fierce determination, bringing fear and despair into every mind. The den seems to thrive in the darkness, as if the spiders and the darkness were one.
120057: A great, dark spider advances toward you from the shadows (red aura).

Sticky threads of cobwebs dominate the view. From every conceivable outcrop in the walls and ceiling they grab hold and span across the lair in a fine black mesh. Some of the threads are hanging loose from the ceiling and they look alive as they swing back and forth in an attempt to grab hold of anything trappable. An impenetrable darkness lurking in the cavern blurs the view of the cavern walls and any sense of direction.
120058:
A great, dark spider advances toward you from the shadows (red aura).
A great, dark spider advances toward you from the shadows (red aura).

An obnoxious stench of rotten flesh hurtles towards you. Obscured by dense cobwebs, the darkened walls of the lair fade out of sight in the intrusive darkness that fills every corner and crack in the cavern. Mighty webs span out across the lair with fine threads searching for a victim to ensnare. The floor is slippery, covered by many layers of dirt.
120065: The corpse of a great, dark spider is lying here.

There is no ceiling in this tunnel, instead the dark walls leap upward into a broad shaft looming above the tunnel. Thick ropes dangle in the darkness from the shaft above. Sturdy wooden ladders mounted on the walls by the use of iron hoops ascend into the shaft above. The worn floor is smooth to the touch, worn down by busy feet labouring in the mine.
120066: A small black vicious rat squeaks at you for disturbing it.

The old tunnel leads onward through the underground, connecting the various parts of the dwarven mine. The worn floor is made of hard mountain rock, and any sound made seems to echo through the tunnel bouncing between the walls. A faint draft sweeps through the tunnel, indicating that some sort of exit must be near.
120067: As a bearer of the gift of Aule the tunnel wanders onward heedless of the slowly increasing slope. The surrounding walls follow the descent without curving the least. The well-crafted tunnel is used mainly for transportation of ore and other goods about the mine. A few holes near a darker spot on one of the walls testify to the fruitless attempts to find iron in this tunnel.
120068: Beneath a broad ceiling the old tunnel continues through the core of the Blue Mountains. The carved halls and tunnels built by dwarven hands seems to go on forever. Deep inside the mountains the dwarves have dwelt for ages now, and with each change of season the mines expand and the glorious dwarven carving skill is preserved.
120069: This mine was apparently created during the first attempts to extract the ore from the mountain. The surrounding walls show the signs of these efforts. Precise and careful was the work of the dwarves here, as almost all of the ore was removed and the mine is near empty.
120070: The corpse of a vicious rat is lying here.

Layers of dust have settled in the old mine. Once the sound of splitting stone filled the tunnels as dwarves extracted the iron ore from the mountain. Now the mine is abandoned, left to spiders who spin their webs in every corner. In the distance can be heard the sound of metal tools thrust against the hard mountain rock.
120071: This unfinished tunnel seems to have been abandoned long ago. Bleak cobwebs form light bridges spanning across the unfinished stone walls for the marching army of dust that covers the tunnel. There are many old mining tools scattered about here, but all are cracked and pitted by the weight of many centuries of disuse. It would appear that the tunnel was abandoned in a hurry.
120072: The solemn decrepitude of the worn tunnel was born with the passing of the mine workers. In times long gone the tunnel was mined by dwarven craftsmen, but now that the ore has been extracted and only empty walls are left the tunnel has been abandoned. The walls and ceiling are held in place by thick beams of wood to prevent a cave-in in what seems a fairly unstable region of the mine.
120073: Your journey through the dwarven mines has taken you to a little used area. This part of the mine must have been one of the first excavations and has probably been abandoned for a long time. It would appear that the departing of the dwarves and the depletion of ore were closely related events. This tunnel is not used for transportation either, as dwarven interest has found new roots elsewhere.
120074: The tunnel reveals many signs of careless mining. Although great persistence drove the dwarves to seek wealth in the mountain, they must have been somewhat disappointed with the obvious lack of ore in this region. The surrounding walls look unstable and ready to cave in at any moment. The ceiling however looks quite strong.
120075: Straight walls of hard rock stand like solemn guardians supporting a broad ceiling that is full of scars from digging done long ago. The old tunnel appears to have been dug in the time when the dwarves first began mining the Blue Mountains. There are no signs of ore in the tunnel and it would seem that it has never been mined actively, but it still has its function in the mine. Apparently, it is used regularly for transportation as ore is brought out and supplies and tools return the other way.
120076: The corpse of a mottled snake is lying here.

A passage branches off from the main tunnel to the north, passing under a stone arch which leaps across the ceiling with a broad curve and then leans on sturdy stone pillars with many intricate carvings. The floor is perfectly smooth here, yet not entirely due to extensive labour, but apparently also to being worn down by busy feet. Except for the carved pillars under the arch the tunnel is quite ordinary.
120077: The tunnel digging its way through the depths of the mountain passes through dark walls of hard rock carved with the precision only the Dwarves possess. The tunnel is otherwise quite plain. No ornamentations or expensive decorations can be seen. Most likely, this tunnel was constructed a long time ago as a part of the first explorations into the mountain conducted by Thorin and Thrain.
120078: The old tunnel plunges through the underground as though it has inherited the obduracy of its dwarven creators. There is little ore in this part of the mine, yet the dwarves apparently continued digging through this region in hope of finding riches further on.
120079: A cockroach is scuttling across the floor carrying some debris.

In a dusty recess of the elaborate dwarven tunnel-systems beneath the vast bulk of the Blue Mountains lies a small corridor in the mountainside. Carved meticulously, with skills and determination given the Dwarves by Aule, the corridor is a proud display of dwarven history told by many murals on the stone walls. Between the murals are arrayed various types of axes securely mounted into the wall. A strong oaken door rests comfortably fitting into a stone-set door-frame to the north.
120080: A cockroach is scuttling across the floor carrying some debris.

A curving stone ceiling looms above the tunnel. The hard rock has been polished by skilful hands and appears perfectly smooth, yet on the northern wall fine lines carved into the stone depict some sort of mural. The cold stone floor is even and without any cracks or other damage. This tunnel was undoubtedly carved with the intention that it should last far beyond the lifespan of its creator.
120081: The craftsmanship of the Dwarves is fully revealed as the faint light from oil lanterns hanging from the ceiling is reflected in the smooth surface of the tunnel walls. The ceiling in the dry tunnel is supported only by the walls; the weight of the mountain alone holds everything in place. In ages long gone, this tunnel had probably been a part of the first dwarven explorations into the depths of the Blue Mountains.
120082:
A small black vicious rat squeaks at you for disturbing it.
A cockroach is scuttling across the floor carrying some debris.

Dark walls of hard mountain rock make a solid foundation for the broad ceiling that spans across the tunnel. The even floor is tinged with a blue colour that seems to originate in the depths of the mountain itself. The immaculate surroundings have been carved with the utmost precision that can only be found in the work of Dwarves. A niche is carved into the west wall.
120083:
A cockroach is scuttling across the floor carrying some debris.
A cockroach is scuttling across the floor carrying some debris.

The dwarves busy themselves in the labour of the mine as you can hear by the distant sounds of metal upon hard rock passing through the air. Under the Blue Mountains lie vast treasures which the dwarves mine with a determination beyond that of men and elves.
