This tunnel seems to have been mined dry without much gain, but it is skilfully crafted with strong beams of wood supporting the ceiling and the walls.
120084:
A small black vicious rat squeaks at you for disturbing it.
A cockroach is scuttling across the floor carrying some debris.

The ageing of this mine must have started a long time ago when the dwarves made their first explorations into the depths of the mountain. Judging by the marks along the sides of the tunnel, heavy mining took place here once, and at that time the mine probably played an active part in the consolidation of wealth among the dwarves. Now it appears to be more or less abandoned and it is only seldom that any dwarf might pass here when duties require that goods are brought to the outer parts of the mines.
120085: A cockroach is scuttling across the floor carrying some debris.

A curve in the stone stretches the scars of dwarven pickaxes across the ceiling of the tunnel. This area was hewed through the core of the Blue Mountains by the hands of busy dwarves searching for ore. Now the tunnel is abandoned and closer inspection reveals that it was actually never quite finished.
120086:
A rusty pickaxe with a broken handle lies discarded here.
A cockroach is scuttling across the floor carrying some debris.

The skill of dwarven pickaxes tells on the surrounding walls the story of the dwarven effort to mine the underground of the Blue Mountains. Yet the effort appears to have stopped here. On the floor of the almost completed tunnel lie several discarded pickaxes, and broken rocks produced by the mining are scattered along the walls.
120087: Between huge stones towering around you like giants runs a narrow fissure in the mountain. The walls are very close, and moving through the fissure would shift between crawling on all fours and climbing up steep rocks. This fissure is natural and there are no signs that dwarves were ever active in this area.
120088: A cockroach is scuttling across the floor carrying some debris.

A narrow fissure between towering boulders proceeds through the underground. Darkness reigns here, feeding on any source of light that may pass. Grumbling and bickering, the mountain narrows the fissure making passage hard and troublesome.
120089: In the inner depths of the Blue Mountains your most trusty follower is the rumbling echo carrying the sound of every footstep through the turning tunnels. The tunnels here are natural and worn with the passing of time. Steep walls of flint, cracked and torn with sharp spikes, rise on every side of you. The black passage reveals no apparent signs of life.
120090: Mouldering walls of flint rise high in the darkness that holds a rocky ceiling far above your head. The natural tunnel is filled with debris broken loose from the crumbling surroundings. A yawning silence lies over the tunnel, yet there is something, somewhere in the distance, making faint repetitive noises.
120091:
A large bat is here, hanging in the darkness.
A huge bat is here, emitting piercing squeaks (red aura).
A cockroach is scuttling across the floor carrying some debris.

As you glance at the torn stone walls from which deep darkness seems to emanate, tiny gleaming dots appear like stars slowly taking form behind passing clouds in the night. As your vision is adjusted, the shining eyes reveal themselves as reflections in the rock. A big lode of iron ore is located just beneath the surface of the rock awaiting only a swift stroke of a pickaxe to free it from the rock that has bound it for ages.
120092:
A cockroach is scuttling across the floor carrying some debris.
A cockroach is scuttling across the floor carrying some debris.

Passage through the tunnel becomes troublesome as the walls narrow in and the ceiling descends, bearing closer and closer to the rising floor. The rough walls gleam in the darkness with a metallic shine indicating rich deposits of iron ore. A whispering echo of dripping water pervades the silence in the tunnel; the sound appears to be louder to the east.
120093: A Supply Room within the Mines

A large cabinet capable of storing goods is here.
In the cabinet, there are two large pieces of smoked meat, a hooded brass lantern, and a pick.
A small black vicious rat squeaks at you for disturbing it.
A cockroach is scuttling across the floor carrying some debris.
A cockroach is scuttling across the floor carrying some debris.

Nestled within the dark curves of the Dwarven tunnel system, this storage room provides a little light. Old, rundown tools and supplies litter the shelves on the walls mixing with other goods. Hanging from the ceiling is a simple torch which sometimes flickers.
120094: The looming darkness makes it hard to see your surroundings. Black creeping rocks line the floor making any journey difficult. The natural passage lies deep beneath the Blue Mountains, where the secret of its presence eludes most regular visitors. A rough ceiling above can barely be seen in the enshrouding darkness.
120095: The wiry passage suddenly changes its route digging up through the mountain. The colour of the rocky walls slowly changes from black to blue as the passage climbs through different layers of stone. Fresh air comes from a narrow shaft leading up.
120096: The ground rises steeply under a low ceiling. The ceiling is only a few feet from the rubble-strewn rocky floor that twists upwards silently warning you to look out for a slide. It is worn with deep cracks, and seems to be only waiting for a chance to cause a cave-in. Crawling either up or down the tilting ground will require great effort.
120097: A cockroach is scuttling across the floor carrying some debris.

The slanting tunnel begins to narrow in, and gradually light fades as the dark rock of the tunnel walls seems to absorb every colour. Moving through the tunnel would be easy, yet many cobwebs hanging from the ceiling are a constant nuisance as they cling to your head. A faint repeating noise can occasionally be heard, but it always fades quickly.
120098: The tunnel slowly makes its way upwards, passing under a low ceiling of dark rock. In some places the incline is barely noticeable, so the tunnel can be easily traversed, yet constant dodging would be needed to avoid the old dust-covered cobwebs that hang from the ceiling. Far away a weak sound of metal against stone can be heard.
120099: A small black vicious rat squeaks at you for disturbing it.

The black rock walls close together, leaving barely enough room to allow passage. The ruined roof covers the tunnel, pointed ends of splinters directed at any intruder. Sharp rocks on the ground make movement even more difficult. A faint sound of mining taking place far off in the mountain can be heard.
120100: Bleak walls of smooth rock leap upwards in a curving motion bending inwards to conjoin with the cavern ceiling about sixteen feet above the floor. The cavern is fairly large and obviously carved with much determination and skill. The level floor is hard and rings out in alarm with every step you take, the echoes bouncing from wall to wall all around you.
120101: The walls of the tunnel bend inwards towards each other slowly transforming into a crumbling ceiling above. The floor is lined with loose rocks from a recent collapse. A wooden structure of planks and thick beams has been constructed to prevent the tunnel from caving in completely. There are no apparent signs of ore here.
120102: Scars and chips in the sides of the tunnel show obvious signs of heavy mining over the long years. Now the tunnel walls stand bare and cracked, and knowing the thoroughness of the dwarves, one should not expect too much from mining here.
120103: This tunnel was once part of the vast mines beneath the Blue Mountains, but a recent cave-in turned it into a very narrow crawlspace. Crawling on hands and knees one could just barely manoeuvre through the rubble blocking the way. While cramped in this tight space, the sounds of nearby mining seem amplified.
120104: A small black vicious rat squeaks at you for disturbing it.

Although the old mine is finely crafted, the utilitarian nature of this mining area is obvious in the unadorned tunnel walls and the heavy flags of the stone floor. Days in which the old mine saw the energetic horde of dwarven miners burrowing their way though the mountain are long gone. Only faint sounds of mining activity elsewhere break the quiet decrepitude of the old mine.
120105: The floor here is quite level and paved with huge stone flags. It would appear that it was crafted this way to support heavy loads passing through. The sound of dripping water fills the air; looking closer at the rocky walls one can see tiny streams of water trickle down from the ceiling and disappear through near invisible cracks in the floor. Though the mining of these caves has long ceased, signs of the work that once filled these mines are clearly visible in the rugged walls.
120106: Judging by the rifts and cracks in the barren stone walls, this old mine once played the part of a productive ore source in the Dwarven excavation of the Blue Mountains. Now the ore has been extracted and the old mine has been partially abandoned. Only occasionally a few dwarves might pass through the mine on their way to the more productive areas within.
120107: The rugged stone walls lean inwards to a crumbling ceiling. There is no precise definition to either walls or ceiling and where they conjoin there are only loose rocks just waiting to fall apart. Measures have been taken to support the loose rocks by a wooden skeleton. Presumably the tunnel was created with the intention of providing easy access between various parts of the dwarven mines.
120108: With the skill bestowed in the Dwarves, they picked a tunnel through this region of loose rock and rubble. The tunnel walls has been fortified with a wooden structure of strong oak beams that span across the ceiling to keep the tunnel from caving in. Now the tunnel must be merely a part of the route by which the Dwarves transport raw materials and various tools and supplies through the mine.
120109: The barren ceiling is supported by a wooden structure of strong beams that joins with planks along the walls. The need for support is highly justified by the loose rocks sprayed across the floor underneath a nearby cave-in in a less supported area of the ceiling. The rumbling sound of metal mining its way through hard rock echoes through the dark-walled tunnel.
120110: Relentless digging performed by the dwarves in the past seems to be the cause of the worn appearance of this tunnel. Torn with dwarven determination, the rough tunnel had been emptied of ore long ago, and now not even the most skilled miner would stand a chance of finding ore here. A faint blue colour in the stone is the last remnant of the richness once held by the mountain.
120111:
A tiny spider is here, eating a tiny bug.
A tiny spider is here, eating a tiny bug.

Deep cracks, rendered into the hard rock by the efficient mining of the dwarves, lie in the shadows in the surrounding walls. Proficient strikes of many pickaxes carved and mined this tunnel in the past. Now the mine is empty but for a few spiders scurrying in the corners and building their tiny webs in hope of trapping anything edible.
120112: The tunnel proceeds through a region where the predominant blue rock slowly turns grey and dull. The rock is fairly loose here, and oak planks have been placed as reinforcement where the need for support seems inevitable to keep the tunnel from caving in. In the distance is heard the wailing sound of the mountain giving way to the children of Aule.
120113: Carved out of bluish rock, this tunnel stands as proof of the magnificent skills that are commonly found among the dwarven mine-workers. Even though this part of the underground is clearly emptied of all valuable minerals, it is still used for transporting minerals from parts where mining is still taking place. From somewhere east the sound of dwarves talking, wheels turning and pickaxes digging their way through the earth can be heard.
120114: The tunnel bears marks of heavy mining. In the rough walls are deep holes dug by the dwarves as they went forward in their search for ore. In other places, where the success of finding ore seemed less apparent, hardly a single strike had been performed. This form of selective mining seems to be paying off, as the sound of dwarves cheering in the distance can be heard whenever a new lode of ore has been struck.
120115: A quick glance shows that this part of the tunnels has been long empty of ore and is now used only for transportation of ore from other regions within. From time to time a dwarf might pass by, singing a merry tune of wealth and fortune, but besides that and the faint sound of working miners coming from somewhere to the north, the tunnel is silent.
120116:
A rusty pickaxe with a broken handle lies discarded here.
A cockroach is scuttling across the floor carrying some debris.

This mine once employed a great host of dwarven mine-workers that dug through the mountain in search of ore. Now the empty walls stand as silent testimony to the intensive mining that once filled the tunnels with the sounds of metal hitting the stone.
120117: The solid rock in which these mines are excavated carries the echoes of every sound you make through the tunnels. But from the look of the tunnel it doesn't seem likely that anybody is here to hear them. This part has been emptied a long time ago and is now just a proof of the dwarves' eager search for wealth. The air here is fresh and clean, but some moisture can be detected.
120118: Surrounded by sharp teeth-shaped rocks, a twisting passage leads through the dark underground. Little space is available to move between the narrowing walls where any attempt to walk would soon end in crawling. A veil of dust fills every nook and cranny. The sound of nearby mining echoes through the passage.
120119: A multitude of different fungi thrive in the moist conditions on the walls of the passage. Condensed water runs off the walls and gathers in small pools on the floor. As the ceiling dives low over a larger pool, one would need to crawl to pass through and it would be hard to avoid getting ones feet wet.
120120: The fissure is filled with soaking wet fungi that seem to thrive in the moist conditions. Barely avoiding a pointy protrusion in the western wall one can avoid the fungi and proceed through the fissure with nearly dry feet. Examining the roof closer, you notice a series of very narrow cracks that disappear in the rock as deep as any light would go.
120121: Arching across the ceiling vast stone constructions run in parallel stretches down towards the floor where they conjoin with deep, torn crevices. The floor, broken by evanescent cracks, blurs lightly with a deep blue colour. The cavern is natural, and there are no visible signs of Dwarven presence.
120123: The crumbling fissure with grinding spikes of hard rock writhes in its tortuosity trying to elude the darkness that lurks in every corner. The decrepitude of the broken surroundings makes poor living conditions even for the minor life forms, yet the sensation of something lurking in the darkness is apparent. The scrutiny of unseen eyes is upon you.
120125: A dark cleft inside the mountain has been partially filled with cold water. Loose rocks and boulders have fallen into the water and are now only visible as skerries just below the water surface. Deeply cut scars in the cold stone walls provide adequate grip for climbing through the fissure without falling into the water.
120126: A pool of darkish water has formed in a depression of the stone.

Rocks, boulders, cracks and holes would make travelling through the twisting passage a hard work. The passage often widens, only to narrow again, or to contract into a narrow crawlspace behind the next corner. The air is moist and tiny beads of water gently trickle down the walls drawing lines in the dust. From the north can be heard the unmistakable sound of mining.
120127: The corpse of a great, dark spider is lying here.

Curving obediently with the ceiling, blue stone veins follow a twisting passage through the underground. Fierce spikes of rock, rooted in the ceiling, wield sharp edges in objection to any trespasser. At times the path passes by open fissures from which only calm darkness sends its greetings. Stale, dusty air makes breathing difficult.
120128:
A dwarven miner is here, digging the hard rock with his pick.
A dwarven miner is here, digging the hard rock with his pick.
A cockroach is scuttling across the floor carrying some debris.

Confined by cracked walls of hard rock, the passage winds onward. Every movement is a test of agility as the twisting passage curls around sharp protrusions of rocks. As the passage turns yet another sharp corner, it suddenly begins to descend a perilous slope. The sound of mining echoes through the passage.
120129: Each step forward in the narrow confinement of the hostile surroundings would be a test of dexterity. Sharp rocks point their edges towards anything passing through, aiming to scratch and tear clothes and gear. The sound of mining can be heard as a distant war of rock and metal.
120130: A narrow opening in the underground leads past a large chasm and a ledge under a low ceiling of spiked rocks allows safe access past it. Darkness prevails in the chasm; nothing seems to escape the deep except the unmistakable sounds of bats. The passage continues its twisting route beyond the ledge, winding smoothly around corners and outcrops in the rock.
120131: Filling the surroundings in the cavern is a deep darkness that lurks in cracks and fissures in the grim solitude of the barren walls. The floor is torn with deep crevices and there is little distinction between it and the walls; the floor is merely an incline that leads upwards heading for the ceiling. The cavern is natural, and no signs of dwarven work can be seen in it.
120132:
A large bat is here, hanging in the darkness.
A large bat is here, hanging in the darkness.
A cockroach is scuttling across the floor carrying some debris.

A large dome-shaped cavern wrapped in shadows extends its arching ceiling over a series of undisturbed pools in the floor. With some care, passage is made possible by slippery gangways leading between the fungi-filled shores of the pools. The dark water in the pools exudes a musty and uncomfortable smell.
120133: In the vaporous air breathing is troubled by a salty taste that combined with a fusty smell invokes a nauseating sensation. The rugged floor is slippery and treacherous, covered by slimy fungi and pale moss and soaked by a never-ending stream of water beads inching their way down the cold walls. Nowhere is to be seen even a slightest hint of dwarven activity.
120134: A cockroach is scuttling across the floor carrying some debris.

Water drips from every conceivable irregularity in the stone ceiling and forms shallow pools on the ground. The air is moist and leaves a slight acidic taste in your mouth. Various fungi thrive in the wet environment at the base of the cold stone walls. Some caution is needed to avoid slipping on the wet floor.
120135: A small campfire burns here, its low flames giving off only a little light.

Wedged between the splintered walls and the descending roof, the passage forces its way through the core of the Blue Mountains. Shards of rock protrude from the floor everywhere except for a small opening beneath a gaping hole in the ceiling caused by a recent cave-in. An enveloping darkness lurks here, as if waiting to quench any source of light.
120137: Tiny streams of water flow down the cracks in the moss-covered walls. The air smells damp and stale, mainly due to a foul stench emanating from the southern wall. Water is gathering in bleak pools on the rough floor which becomes very slippery to the south. Supporting the weight of the Blue Mountains, the ceiling rests heavily on the surrounding walls.
120138: Bleak puddles of stale-smelling water dominate the broken floor of the tunnel. The sound of water dripping slowly from the tips of rocks protruding from the ceiling can be heard. Veins of glistening ore run over the tunnel walls yet there are no signs indicating the tunnel was ever mined.
120139: Movement in the narrow tunnel is difficult, complicated by many rocks protruding from the ceiling. From the gaps in the cracked stone dim reflections of light sparkle in the richness of the underground. A pesky odour sweeps across the rugged stone walls with an intrusive determination.
120140: Condensed water streams down the tattered stone walls. Deep cracks and holes in the flint decorate the whole passage, yet no signs of any Dwarven activity are to be seen anywhere. In the misty air there is a strange smell, as of rotting flesh mixed with mouldy fabric; there is no telling where the smell comes from.
120141: A musty smell fills the moist air in the passage, and the black rock gleams with a thin layer of condensed water. The water slowly gathers in faint lines and travels down the walls creating tiny pools in the uneven floor. A crack in the wall reveals a high concentration of minerals as light is reflected from inside it with a metallic shine.
120142: Beneath a low ceiling of sharp rocks runs a low passage through the mountain. Travel here is treacherous, as the passage twists and turns beneath the ever impending rocks in the ceiling. A distant sound of metal against hard rock can be heard as it repeats over and over. The humidity suddenly increases from barely noticeable until it is quite evident and makes breathing stressful.
120143: The corpse of a mottled snake is lying here.

Shrouded in darkness, the crumbling passage makes its way through an area of flint. In every corner the darkness lurks as if hiding something. The passage seems natural, formed long ago when the mountain was still young.
120144: Cramped between the rough surfaces of the surrounding stone walls is a tight space that snakes its way up and down through endless formations of blue rock that shines with a crystalline glitter as light exposes its surface. Rocky edges in the stone make passage difficult as they seize anything trying to make its way through.
120145: A low passage hews its way through different layers of hard rock. The colour of the stone shifts from blue to black as the passage continues up and down through the underground. Cobwebs are plentiful in every corner and crack, and a stale smell is in the air.
120146: Stooping low beneath a ceiling of fierce rocks, movement becomes difficult as the tunnel gradually narrows in. The hard rocks shift in colour as the passage slowly advances, up and down, through the heart of the mountain. The air is dense and moist, making breathing tiresome.
120147: Beneath a curving ceiling a narrow passage snakes through stone formations deep under the Blue Mountains. Deep fissures cross the walls and the floor, and care must be taken as the narrowing passage winds past the deep chasms of darkness. A faint trace of moisture fills the air over one of the larger pits. Travel here is tiring and little rest can to be found on the rough stone.
120148: The passage twists through the underground of black rock with gaping fissures. Little space is available for manoeuvring through the tight space confined by the barren protrusions of curving stone walls. Great care must be taken to avoid bumping into the outmost of the rocks that obscure the passage.
120149: The tunnel shows no signs of ever being mined actively. But being known for their stubbornness, the dwarves dug their way through this area anyway in hope of finding iron minerals further on. The building, however, must have been difficult as the rock is fairly loose in some areas, and the ceiling in the tunnel is supported in several locations by wooden planks to prevent a cave-in.
120150: Beneath the Dwarven Homes lies the vast complex of the dwarven mines. As the mine gradually expanded towards the discovery of new ore deposits, empty and dusty tunnels were formed on the way. The dark walls of the tunnel tell the story of the extensive labour that has enabled the dwarves to extract ore from the deepest part of the mountain, as pickaxes swung with great strength and determination against the rock left deep scars in the stone.
120151: Apparently unhindered, the tunnel advances through the mountain. The tunnel looks as if it was excavated recently and is just beginning to take shape. A low ceiling, cracked and torn with deep marks, is making its way further and deeper into the dark underground. A distant sound of metal striking hard rock indicates that work is going on elsewhere in the mine.
120152: A dark, rocky chunk of ore lies on the ground.

The walls of the tunnel seem to have been crafted recently. The hard rock that was once the solid foundation of the mountain has been crushed into fragments by the busy workmen who formed the tunnel. Precise and efficient were the movements that swung the tools searching for ore. The cracked walls leave little doubt about the richness of the mountain, as any light reflected by the rock is cast back in a strange deep blue colour.
120153:
A dented pail has been carelessly left here.
A water barrel has been left here.
A dwarven miner is here, digging the hard rock with his pick.
A dwarven miner is here, digging the hard rock with his pick.

Here in the dwarven mines deep inside the Blue Mountains the tremendous work of the dwarves becomes apparent indeed. Through great labour the dwarves have dug through the deep roots of the mountain in search of ore. This mine is proof of rich deposits of iron. Trapped just beneath the surface of the rock a thick lode of iron emits an evanescent metallic blur. On the rubble-strewn floor rest several empty buckets used to transport ore.
120154: A rusty pickaxe with a broken handle lies discarded here.

The tunnel passes through the heart of the dwarven mine. A big lode of ore must be nearby, as the mountain echoes with the sounds of dwarves working, driven by the will to make new discoveries. Discarded mining tools can be seen on the ground; apparently, the tools gave up long before their owners.
120155: Scars and chips bulge out from the sides of the tunnel, showing obvious signs of heavy mining over the long years. Now the tunnel stands empty and barren, and judging by its abandoned look, one should not expect to find here much ore.
120156: Through cracks and scars in the walls the purpose of this mine becomes clear. There is ore here. Glinting in the dark with a pale metallic light, the precious metal awaits the tools that will set it free. The mine echoes with the repetitive sound of axes hitting at the stone and the wails of the mountain reluctant to give up its treasures.
120157: The presence of ore is very apparent here. Long lines in the walls gleam with the omnipresent metallic shine. An echoing sound of metal thrust against hard rock rolls through the mine as the ore is mined by skilful hands. Rock bound together for ages by the weight of the mountain is released with each clanging sound of tools working their way through. Busy are the dwarves and in their labour they thrive.
120158: You are in the eastern part of the dwarven mines bearing closer to the east side of the mountain. The rumbling sound of rock giving way to the dwarven pickaxes echoes through the mine. Into the eastern wall a tunnel passes under an arch of coal-black rock, widening slightly ahead.
120159: A narrow passage winds its way through the mountain here. Bending a little, one can just barely squeeze through it. The walls are cold and covered with a dew that makes the surface of the rock shine with a pale silvery glow. The sound of metal eating its way through the foundation of the Blue Mountains can be heard from the north.
120160: A water barrel has been left here.

A narrow ceiling soars upwards carried by strong beams of oak reaching from wall to wall. The wood seems more decorative than functional as the sturdy rock could easily support itself. The walls, straight and tall, mauled from the rock of the mountain, rise high reaching to conjoin with the ceiling, more than at the height of three men from the ground. In the northern wall there is a large niche.
120161:
A sturdy peg for hanging armour is on the wall.
On the peg, there are a rigid leather helmet, a sturdy pair of rigid leather sleeves, a pair of rigid leather boots, a pair of rigid leather gloves, a studded leather belt, and a soft leather jerkin.
A weapons rack stands against the wall.
In the rack are a longsword, a mace, a dagger, and a handaxe.
A wooden chest stands in the corner.

The chamber, cut into the hard mountain rock, shows signs of recent digging in an attempt to enlarge it. The work appears to have been finished recently and the chamber now acts as a storage space. Broad wooden shelves mounted on the surrounding walls serve as a holding area for food and other goods.
120162: The cavern winds its smoothly curving walls around a stairway leading upwards in the centre. A coal-black rock floor serves as a steadfast foundation for the ascending stairway. Near the roof of the cavern is a wooden platform stretched from wall to wall. The ringing sound of metal forcing its strength upon hard rock can be heard in the distance.
120163: Strong oak planks span across a cavern some fifteen feet below. The platform easily carries more than a dozen men in full armour, yet it seems that there is more to this construction than meets the eye. The roof of grey rock, chiselled with the utmost care, casts dull shadows on the platform. In the centre of the platform is a rectangular hole, large enough for three dwarves to descend at once.
120164:
A huge black fungus is here, exuding a foul stench (red aura).
An ancient fungus smothers the boulders.

Fissures and cracks in the walls lie shaded in a dense vapour. Faint lines of water trickle down from the ceiling bending around outcrops and disappearing into dark funnels. The amount of moisture in the air is greatest near the southern wall where a deep dark hole seems to spout dense clouds towards you. The floor is slippery and care must be taken not to trip.
120165: The corpse of a great, dark spider is lying here.

Dripping with moisture, the broken walls cringe up towards a dark ceiling that seems to envelop the damp air in the tunnel. Bulbous fungi thrive on the moist rock. A foul stench comes from the exposed surface of black moulds that battle for space with a variety of other fungi species. The dense and vaporous air causes shallow pools of water to form as it condenses on the cold stone floor.
120166:
There are three toadstools here.
A giant slug is here, oozing around (red aura).

The dark cavern ceiling curves slightly above, supported by strong pillars covered by a slimy green substance. A musty smell pervades the moist air, mixed with a strong odour of sulphur. The cavern floor has a gleaming aura of light reflected from myriad tiny water-beads. Numerous fungi and other slimy creatures thrive in the moist conditions. There are no apparent signs that dwarves ever visited this place.
120167:
A sturdy, wooden chest sits here amidst the dust.
A small black vicious rat squeaks at you for disturbing it.

A circular cavern of dwarven make extends its arching walls inwards forming a spherical ceiling around an anvil in the centre of the cavern. The afferent walls surround what appears to be a dwarven workshop. Broad shelves and large wooden cabinets precisely ordered on the walls and in clusters on the floor provide storage space for many strange tools that are used by the dwarven metal-workers. Despite the obvious completeness of the workshop it has not been used for a long time, as is apparent from the dust and cobwebs that span the room.
120168:
Some withered twisted roots writhe towards you.
A horse of the Rohirrim (ulo) is standing here.

An enormous, brooding, black oak looms overhead upon a great bole on knotted roots. Its gnarled bark appears charred, but on closer inspection is extremely leathery and tough. A huge twisted mass of roots creep and crawl in every direction from the base of the tree, snarling underfoot. The oak's thick, dark limbs reach out to grasp at you like the bony hands of death, as it deeply shadows the glade around its base.
120169:
The corpse of a thug is lying here.
The corpse of an assassin is lying here.
The corpse of an assassin is lying here.
The corpse of a thug is lying here.

Bat guano fills the sides of this tunnel in huge piles several feet deep. The middle of the tunnel is strewn with debris that comes in during floods from a narrow crack in the ceiling that leads to the outside. The bats seem to be missing and were most likely disturbed by men whose tracks litter the tunnel.
120170: An old gravel path worms its way around many well-kept zigzagging rows of vegetables. Wooden sign posts are embedded at the beginning of each new row, showing the various names of plants and herbs. At the very end of the enclosing a patch of grass can be seen with colourful flowers blooming in random patches. A clearly visible sign has been placed here stating: Please do not trample the flowers.
120171: A humble man stands here, ready to help you with your things.

The walls have been strewn with countless maps depicting various scenes from all around Arda. All of the furniture is sitting under a layer of random equipment only an adventurer would need. Only the bed remains untouched and ready for a weary traveller. A soft wooly carpet has been laid out on the floor, dyed into forming a map of Bree and a large X where this address is.
120172: A doorwarden stands here ready to obey his master's wishes.

This is a cosy and friendly-looking dwarven home. The walls are covered with artefacts of different origin: Dwarven, Elven and even some items of Orkish origin can be found. A low archway, beaming warm light, leads to a bigger room due west.
120173: This room is quite big compared to the others in this home. Not as richly decorated as the entrance hall, only two notable items are here. A huge fireplace giving warmth and light can be seen in the corner. And next to it, a big round table covered with Numenorean carvings. In the southwwest corner are some stairs leading up the bedroom.
120174:
A water barrel has been left here.
A weapons rack stands against the wall.

This room is rather large. The walls are upholstered with soft, padded leather plates. There are no windows here and several torches have been set on the walls to fight the prevailing darkness. Other than that, the room is empty except for a big weapons rack in the rear of the room.
120175: A stout Dwarven steward stands here, read to defend the home.

The most prominent thing in the room is a set of large shelves placed high against the back wall. On the top shelf there appears to be a million different pots of spices and herbs useful for seasoning a variety of different foods. On the lower shelves there are huge pots and pans, the type that would make any cook jealous. Near the window there is a table large enough for two.
120176: A humble man stands here, ready to help you with your things.

The bedroom is small, fitting a bed, a table and a big bookshelf. The bed is neatly done and hasn't been used for some time it seems. A pile of books and scrolls is on the table, and a lantern giving some light. On the walls you see items of orcs Chazan has slain over the years: weapons, shields, scalps and a crude orkish horn.
120177: The balcony is decorated with various kinds of flowers. You can see the tree tops of Bree's park, leaves shifting and moving in the wind. On the floor of the balcony you notice a soft, fuzzy rug and a rocking chair is set in one corner.
120180: A humble man stands here, ready to help you with your things.

Nestled at the pinnacle of the ancient tree, the dimly-lit chapel emanates an enchanting, mystical ambiance. Muted light filters through the foliage, casting haunting shadows upon the weathered timber walls. Flickering candles illuminate cryptic symbols, evoking a sense of ancient sorcery and drawing visitors into a realm where dark secrets intertwine with arcane wonders.
120181: A humble man stands here, ready to help you with your things.

Perched atop a colossal, ancient tree, a realm of magic unfolds for the esteemed ancient magic mistress. This celestial chamber, reminiscent of Elven sanctuaries, gazes upon a breathtaking vista-a meandering river flowing through a lush forest, evoking the very essence of Middle-earth. Ethereal light bathes the room, filtering through intricate stained glass windows, casting a delicate glow upon the room. Elven tapestries, adorned with intricate designs, depict the tales of old. Soft whispers of enchantments linger in the air, above a throne-like chair, carved with elvish motifs. It is a place for deep meditation that allows communing with the ancient magic of Valinor and harnessing the power that echoes through the land of elves.
120182: The burnt and blackened skeletal remains of a human are here.

A strange odour hangs in the hair, catching at the back of your throat as you breath. The ground is devoid of vegetation or animal tracks and is stained a deep black colour. Here and there, pieces of rusted metal stick up from the ground and the scattered sun-bleached bones of some long dead creatures lie forgotten on the ground.
120183:
A bright red mushroom is growing here.
A giant slug is here, oozing around.
A giant slug is here, oozing around.

The forest humus above has given way to some dark force which has created this slimy covered hole. The smell of rotting flesh pervades this hole and piles of bone mixed with pieces of flesh rest here in slimy ooze. Something large has existed here for a long time, making a meal of anything which comes in from above. It does not seem to be a wise place to tarry.
120201: A copper penny lies on the ground.

Eerie white-trunked birch trees stand in a solid wall about the eastern and northern boundaries. The trees are vigilant, though not hostile. They appear to pose no threat but watch every movement made in the darkness below them. The thin air is almost too scant to breathe, and the hissing rustle from above makes the atmosphere tense.
120202: Stark white tree trunks stand in marked contrast with the gloomy surrounds. Their formation in a massive impenetrable barrier to the north and east is a reminder that evil forces are affecting this once strong and noble forest. Dark patches, such as this one, are developing and growing. Even so, the thin musty air is still laden with the stale scent of noble trees in more beautiful times. Nothing seems to have disturbed the forest floor for quite some time, and insects scurry away amongst the leaves and roots. Fungi of various colours grow rampant on the numerous pieces of fallen wood and debris.
120203: There are two copper pennies here.

The dreary cheerless trees that grow here are like menacing disfigurements of their once noble forms. Oak, birch, ash, and other varieties spread their limbs in an enveloping canopy high above the forest floor. The lack of natural light reaching through the canopy inhibits the growth of any new plants or undergrowth. Instead, the forest floor is strewn with ageless piles of fallen leaves and debris. A lingering fragrance of each tree variety can be discerned above the musty trapped air. The ground slopes gently away to a small ditch to the south, and to the north-east a white wall appears through the tree trunks.
120204: Dark menacing trees stand still and quiet, like statues watching and guarding their stronghold. Their massive branches spread across the ceiling of the forest, shutting out all natural light and weighing the air down with a stuffy stagnancy. The waterlogged earth squelches underfoot as a stench of rotting vegetation permeates the air. The ground slopes almost imperceptibly upwards to the north and south.
120205: Stark white birch trees stand in marked contrast with the dark and eerie surrounds. They form a massive barrier to the north, south and east, hemming in the evil trees and shadows of this encroaching dark patch. This area must have been recently overcome by the formidable birch trees because the thin, musty air is still laden with the stale scent of noble trees in more beautiful times. Nothing seems to have disturbed the forest floor for quite some time. Insects scurry away amongst the fallen leaves and fungi of various colours grow rampant on fallen pieces of wood.
120206:
A small bat is standing here.
A small bat is standing here.
A small bat is standing here.
A small bat is standing here.

As you look around you, you immediately can tell that no one has been in this small barn for many years. Dust covers everything, and you leave traces behind you. To the west there is a small farm-yard. You cannot proceed in any other direction.
120208: A humble man stands here, ready to help you with your things.

Perched high on a towering, ancient tree in Rivendell, a meditation room exudes enchantment. Its panoramic view reveals a lush, verdant forest and meandering rivers that glisten under the sun's gentle caress. Soft rays of celestial light filter through intricate windows, suffusing the space with a magical glow. Whispers of ancient spells linger in the air, inviting tranquility and deep introspection. Here, amidst nature's embrace and mystical ambiance, one can find solace and embark on a profound journey of meditation and spiritual awakening.
120209: Rows of hewn shelves line the northern, southern, and western walls. Empty barrels stand in deep rows against the walls of the black stone chamber. Chests of various sizes have been placed here in haphazard manners: some are closed, others have been cracked open and emptied. Shelves of broken clay urns and jars have been overturned. Everything is in complete disarray, as if an earthquake had tossed everything up in the air not too long ago.
120212:
A diamondback rattlesnake is coiled here, ready to strike.
A huge black fungus is here, exuding a foul stench.
A huge black fungus is here, exuding a foul stench.

A few beams of light filter in through tiny cracks and holes in what was formerly the floor of an old cabin. Now nothing remains of the former inhabitants but some old refuse and debris scattered about. You detect some sinister movement in the shadows however...perhaps there are some new denizens of this abode?
120214: Outside the East Gate of Bree

A thick stone wall stretches far both north and south, framing a metal gate set within. The dirt-packed road transitions into stone slabs before the gate, just far enough to cover the area the gate moves when it opens. A tower looming above the gate is the first sight of Bree travellers from the east see.
120216: A large rabbit looks peacefully at you, ready to dart away.

The ridge of rocky heather covered hills that extends eastward and northward for miles comes to a sudden end: a great bay, enclosed by steep cliffs and paved with round pebbles, lies to the east many yards below. It was the ancient bed of the river, which later chose a straighter course. A huge rocky spur thrusts southward, wrapped in thin mist, and from that direction the faint rumble of a waterfall can be heard.
120218: The flat top of a high hillock here allows a good view of the surrounding land: the undulating ground stretches unchanged for miles and miles, covered only sparsely by heather and small withered bushes. A crumbling fall opens to the north, and a stream of white stones can be seen down there, descending westwards.
120219:
Traces of white tones form the aura of this place.
There are twenty-one vials of preserved blood here.
A sturdy leather backpack has been left here.
A wooden painted map of Bree is here, nailed to a post.
There is an old street-lamp on the border of the street.
A white-painted bench is here.
The gatekeeper of Bree stands here.
A Guard of Bree is here, watching the gate.
A Guard of Bree is here, watching the gate.
A squirrel scampers around here, looking for nuts from the trees.

Towards the east, a tall and thick stone wall stretches far both north and south and deeply rooted in the wall, a hinged gate is set. An equal note is shown on both sides of the gate. Linked with the wall, a tower rises to the north. A paper note is attached to the gate.
120223: Prickly, white-stemmed plants, with blue flower heads grow in abundance.

The land is steeply sloped here, descending from a line of hills on the west into a deep, sheltered valley to the east. Two species of grass vie with one another for dominance, one short and thick, the other taller and wispy. A few weeds and wildflowers manage to poke their way through the grass, and a handful of hawthorn trees rise over the land.
120226: A fierce boar is here, making grunting noises.

The knoll rises gently from the surrounding fields, covered in a thick carpet of green grass. Small wildflowers in the landscape add pops of colour to the greenery. The view from the top offers a panoramic view of the surrounding countryside. The knoll offers great views of the grasslands south and west.
120227: In the heart of the stretched-out grass-laden field, a solitary willow stands, its trailing branches creating a sanctuary for the creatures of the field.To the east, a grassy knoll gently rises, its modest elevation not competing with the surrounding hills. To the west, the hills are crowned with brushes. On the north and south, the steep slopes form a natural barrier.
120228: A grey bird with a bright orange-red belly sits here, singing a melodic tune.

Hilltops rise from the land, their forms cloaked in a verdant sea of brush that softens the harshness of the stone. Every exposed surface is hidden beneath this living tapestry. Amidst the verdant sea, patches of mosses and lichens cling to the exposed stone, their forms tracing the contours of the land. The hilltops are a treacherous passage, the undulating terrain and dense vegetation creating a challenge for the unwary traveller.
120229: Upon this rocky ridge, large oaks find their dominion. They grow at various angles, their forms twisted and gnarled. Their roots burrow deep into the cracks and crevices of the stone. The branches of the oaks sway slowly, their movements a silent dance with the unseen wind. The ground is a patchwork of stone and soil, the former peeking through the latter like bones through the skin.
120230: The hillocks swell like waves of earth and stone within the verdant expanse of the South Downs. Bushes, sparse yet tenacious, sprout from the soil at the junction, their forms twisted by the rugged landscape. Among them, the low forms of bearberry and crowberry trace the contours of the hillocks, their leaves a vibrant green against the earthy tones of the terrain.
120231: The rocky face of the rocky promontory rises steeply from the surrounding landscape. Its jagged peaks and craggy edges seem to scrape the sky. The huge plateau at the top of the promontory stretches out before them, a barren expanse of bleak rock that glints in the sun.
120232:
The mauled corpse of a boar.
A coloured game bird is visible in the vegetation, watching you warily.

The hills of the South Downs give way here to a low valley of wavy grass. To the north, the grass expands into a wide green field. While in all other directions, the hills rise in an imposing vista of rocky mounds. A few lines of dirt, interrupted by the occasional brown circle, indicate the presence of some subterranean mammals.
120239:
A nest is here.
A big, nasty vulture is sitting here, protecting its nest.
A big, nasty vulture is sitting here, protecting its nest.

The grassland stretches out as far as the eye can see, the grass rippling gently in the wind like waves on the sea. Here and there, a small grove of trees provides a welcome respite from the open expanse. Birds soar overhead, their cries echoing in the distance. The area is completely enclosed by steep hills, the only passage is to the north where a verdant knoll is visible.
120240: A black and white skunk is scuttling about here, searching for food.

These hills, garbed in green, are adorned with short, squat trees. A vivid green carpet of moss clings fiercely to the hillside. Scattered across the hilltops, large boulders stand, remnants of an age long past. To the east, a thin line of hilltops rises. Towards the north, brush-covered hilltops peer over the landscape. However, venturing west or south is a dream held at bay by the formidable steepness of the hills.
120241: A small and tough weed grows here.

The hilltops gaze out over a landscape etched in stone and draped in green. Tall firs and dark oaks tower over the hilltops, forming a stark contrast to the undulating terrain. The terrain beneath the trees is a blend of stone and soil. Step-like rock formations climb up to a rugged cliff shelf, their forms tracing the contours of the hills. The hills continue to the south and west.
120242: The surfaces of these hillocks are windswept, shaped, and caressed by the constant zephyrs. Small clusters of wild marjoram are clinging to the crevices in these hillocks. To the east, a rocky line of hills stretches towards the horizon. To the north, a thin line of hilltops peeks over the horizon. The steep hills to the west and south form an impassable barrier.
120243: These rocky hills offer a stark contrast to the lush hillocks common to the South Downs. A haphazard tapestry of granite and gneiss, they rise in imposing grandeur. White spruce and balsam fir saplings take root in the crevices of the rocky terrain. To the south, the rocky terrain gives way to a solitary ledge, a protruding platform of stone. To the west, the landscape transforms into windswept hillocks.
120244: A rock lizard is here, motionless as it observes you.

The ground of this rocky ledge is a mosaic of bare stone and moss-covered rock. From this vantage point, a verdant, hill-ringed valley stretches out in the distance. A small hill rises from the valley floor, its form covered in a carpet of grass. Mosses and lichens find purchase in the crevices of the rock, their forms tracing the contours of the stone.
120245: In the very heart of this verdant sea, a lofty, stony apex rises. It stands as a bastion amidst the rolling hillocks, its form a stark contrast to the soft curves of the land. It is a sentinel, watching over the hills and valleys, its presence a constant in this ever-changing landscape. The slopes of the apex have recesses carved into their sides which bear the scars of time. These hollows are cradles of life, nurturing pockets of boreal vegetation.
120246:
There are two handfuls of clover here.
A bear is here, covered with coarse black fur.
A field mouse noses about hungrily, searching for food.
A thin bear is here, hunting for food.

In the heart of the forest lies a peaceful meadow, surrounded by hills. The grass is soft and inviting, and wildflowers grow in abundance. The meadow serves as a basin that is fed by numerous streams, each flowing down from the peaks, merging into larger and deeper watercourses. The meadow rises into rocky hills to the north. To the south, a mouth of a narrow valley is visible.
120247:
The mauled corpse of a starving bear.
The mauled corpse of a black bear.
A field mouse noses about hungrily, searching for food.

Thin slices of sharp shale break the ground's monotony, their jagged edges protruding like the dorsal fins of ancient leviathans. The few oaks here stand tall and proud, their roots plunged deep into the fertile soil. Curled around the boulders, vibrant ferns unfurl their fronds. To the south, a verdant hillock rises gently. East and west, steep hill slopes stretch upward and make travel impossible. Northward, a meadow unfurls like a green carpet, dotted with the vibrant hues of wildflowers.
120248: The grasslands form a sea of green that sways in the wind like waves on the ocean, framed by hills to the west, south, and farther north. The grass is tall and lush, and wildflowers grow in clusters, creating a kaleidoscope of colours. The only sounds are the rustling of the grass and the distant cries of birds.
120249: A field mouse noses about hungrily, searching for food.

Blanketing the valley floor is a sprawling field, vibrant and alive. It's a wide, tranquil expanse that sits nestled within the bosom of the valley. The vale extends to the south and west, opening into rolling expanse of lush meadows. Sparse trees adorn the surrounding hills to the north and east. The ground underfoot is soft and wet, squishing slightly with each step.
120250:
The mauled corpse of a brown bear.
A brown bear is sleeping here.

The thick smell of large, wet, mammals permeates this dank cavern. Large scratches cover the walls and floor, perhaps from the same creatures sharpening their claws. A small pile of the remains of crushed nuts and berries cover one corner, long since devoured.
120251:
A quail stands motionless.
A sly cat prepares to pounce from its grassy hiding place.

Situated between steep hills on the west, south, and northeast, a lush valley unfolds. The field, rich with soft, wet soil, stretches out like an inviting carpet. On the slopes, solitary trees maintain a stately vigil. The serenity of the glen is further accentuated by the occasional ripple of a breeze causing soft waves across its verdant carpet.
120252: The pasture is a riot of colour, with wildflowers of every hue covering the ground like a multicoloured carpet. A gentle breeze blows through the area, causing the flowers to sway gently in the wind. The sweet fragrance of the flowers permeates the air, attracting bees and butterflies in droves.
120253: The meadow is shrouded in a fine mist that hangs low to the ground, lending the surroundings an ethereal quality. A wide variety of flowers grow here, with their petals dripping with dew. Butterflies, their wings shimmering in the soft light, flit from bloom to bloom, sipping nectar as they go.
120254: Despite the rugged terrain and sharp outcroppings of stone, the grasses here are tenacious, their roots clinging to the rocky soil. The grasses are a deep shade of green, with blades as sharp as razors, able to cut through flesh with ease. As the wind whips across the grassland, the grasses bend and sway like the waves of a tumultuous sea.
120255:
The mauled corpse of a large elk.
A great bustard strides over the grass.

The land here is a series of steep hills, their slopes dressed in a motley garb of bracken and heather. The slopes are bedecked in a rich tapestry of northern bedstraw and Labrador tea, their delicate blossoms a stark contrast against the sweeping emerald. Trees, proud and mighty, emerge from the undulating sea of grass, their roots delving deep into the rich, loamy soil of the slopes.
120256: The boulder-strewn hilltops' surface is pocked with moss-filled nooks and crannies. Within the cracks of the boulders, small colonies of lichens thrive. The boulders form what appears to be a crude circle, suggestive of an ancient meeting place. Stonecrop clings stubbornly to the rocky outcrops, their yellow blossoms adding a dash of colour to the otherwise grey tableau. The west is marked by a range of hills that roll across the horizon. To the north, a solitary hillock rises, emerald green and studded with grey stones.
120257: Along the path, the traveller's gaze is drawn to the fir trees, few but fair, their verdant spires standing tall against the pastel panorama. Limestone outcrops, ancient bones of the earth, jut forth from the hillsides. To the west and east, the hills rise sharply, their steep sides veiled with a mixture of moss and creeping ivy, a vibrant green tapestry. The trail narrows as it enters a meandering maze of rolling emerald hills to the north. To the south, the trail continues into a shallow valley.
120258:
A long-necked bird, with a fairly short spear-like bill stands here.
A grey wolf is here, thin from starvation.

A turning trail cuts through the verdant canvas, winding its way across the undulating South Downs landscape. Next to this trail, a huddle of wild marjoram makes its home, rooted in the heart of a limestone crevice. The trail pushes onward, its path set to the west and north, further into the heart of the hills. To the east and south, the hills rise sharply. Their slopes are steep and treacherous, a deterrent to all but the hardiest of adventurers.
120259:
The corpse of a sturdy billy goat is lying here.
A large elk is standing here, chewing grass and leaves.

This path, narrow yet steadfast, boasts a worn, weather-beaten surface. It lies upon a bed of solid rock, etched out from the stony bluff. To the west, the land rises with daunting, near-vertical sculptures of rock and scrub, far too steep for any wanderer to traverse. To the east, the trail continues, turning, twisting, and teetering across the hills. Southward, the trail beckons, extending its reach toward the open fields beyond the Downs.
120260: A sturdy billy goat stands here, proudly protecting his goats.

An overgrown ridge, a forgotten scar of earth and stone, carves its way through the grassland. Lichen and moss creep across its surface, a green and grey shroud that softens its starkness. Staghorn clubmoss and reindeer lichen, common in these boreal climes, claim dominion here, their forms creating a miniature forest upon the ridge.
120261: Centre of a Stretch of Hills
A large elk is standing here, chewing grass and leaves.

The ground is a patchwork of loose boulders and rocks. A brook babbles its way through, its clear waters rushing over pebbles and rocks. A solitary hawthorn tree stands guard near the brook. To the west, the land rises in rocky hilltops, their jagged edges etch the horizon, forming a rugged skyline. To the east, hilltops crouch under the weight of boulders. To the north, the land weaves a junction of hilltops, where the hilltops meet in a convocation of stone and earth.
120262: The precipice of converging hilltops is scattered with fragments of scree, shards of a once-solid edifice, now shattered and strewn about the hilltop junction. Amidst these fragments, strange fungi make their homes, their caps mottled in hues of sun-kissed yellow. To the south, the heart of the South Downs undulates in rhythmic harmony. To the north, a steep overlook provides an unobstructed view over the sprawling hills.
120263: A great bustard strides over the grass.

The overlook is an impressive precipice, an auditorium without a roof, with its audience being the splintered rocks and its actors being the whispering winds. In the crevices of boulders here, small, stiff bushes have found a home, their roots gripping tenaciously. To the west, a narrow ridge winds, serpent-like, across the landscape. It is a precarious pathway, where a single misstep might lead to a heart-stopping plunge into the depths. North leads to a vast expanse of grasslands.
120264: The ridge snakes through the verdant landscape of the South Downs. Gazing eastward, a steep overlook commands the view, a precipice of rugged majesty that dares the bravest hearts to approach its edge. To the north, the terrain is interrupted by a twisting line of foothills. Moss clings tenaciously to the rocks scattered about, imbuing them with an almost ethereal, soft verdancy.
120265:
Some small rocks have been piled into a mound here.
A dun-coloured grouse is sitting still in the heather.
A black raven flies in the sky searching for flesh to prey upon.

The ground beneath is an undulating sea, the earth rising and falling in a twisting rhythm. The hills morph from stony foothills into small hills westward. Hardy mosses and lichens cling to the stone, their forms creating a verdant carpet. Travel in these South Downs is fatiguing, the constantly shifting landscape proving a challenge even for the most seasoned wanderer.
120266: A black raven flies in the sky searching for flesh to prey upon.

The sides of the hills fall away steeply. Clumps of bearberry and crowberry cling to the rocky slope, their forms huddled against the stone. In the heart of the oak cluster, a lone, large boulder stands. Its surface is worn and weathered, yet it stands unyielding.
120267:
A hollow tree is growing upright here.
A large elk is standing here, chewing grass and leaves.

The South Downs unfold like a tapestry of rolling hillocks, a landscape draped in hues of green and brown. A firm line of tall fir trees crowns the rocky expanse, their needle-clad forms standing as silent sentinels over the land. Dark oaks, ancient and proud, accompany them, their gnarled branches reaching skyward in a silent proclamation of resilience. Among the hillocks, vegetation thrives, the flora a testament to the land's nurturing touch.
120268: A ridge of hills, its form softened by time and weather, winds its way through the South Downs, a natural pathway carved into the land. It is a living bridge, tree-covered and vibrant, with paper birch and trembling aspen standing as silent sentinels. Their roots delve deep into the ridge, anchoring them to the land.
120269: The hills are marked by a few solitary trees, creating an open landscape amid the undulations. The sparse trees pierce the skyline above the low-lying flora. Occasional black spruce and balsam fir can be seen standing tall, yet with ample space around them. Under their intermittent shadow, patches of feathermoss and twinflower are scattered about.
120270: Along the rocky hilltops, hidden crevices and caves are tucked away in the black rock. This rocky wasteland has hardly any soil, and the scant earth that is present supports minimal plant life. Its flat surface stretches out in all directions, broken only by the occasional boulder or pile of rocks.
120271: The sun-baked meadows seem to stretch on forever, their flat, featureless expanse broken only by the occasional rocky outcropping. Small tufts of brown grass dot the landscape, their wispy tendrils waving in the hot breeze. The meadows here are not uniform, for interspersed across the vast carpet of green are noble firs, standing tall and solitary.
120272: The ridge of rocky hills makes a sharp turn here as it passes through the plains. Below to the west, the long line of the Greenway continues its plodding course north and south. The hills here are quite steep, limiting passage to the north, while a gentle slope to the east leads down into a large basin.
120273:
A brown snake watches you.
A great bustard strides over the grass.

The ridge is very narrow here as it begins to turn. Steep slopes all around indicate that staying to the middle of the ridge is the safest option. Just down the slopes to the west, the long line of the Greenway is visible for miles to the north and south.
120274: This long ridge of the South Downs runs south to north here as it borders the Greenway to the west. The eastern slopes are rocky and steep, making travel that way impossible. To the south and north the ridge is narrow, but fairly easily traversable.
120275: Surrounded by thick, thorny hedges, this broad and dusty road is more or less overgrown by tough grasses and ferns. The tracks themselves are hard and bare after the passage of merchants' carriages. The road continues to the north and south, a long straight line going on for miles and miles.
120276: Shooting straight through a brush-covered plain, this more or less overgrown roadway never seems to pause for breath. Muddy tracks made by coaches and merchant carriages make it evident that the road is still being used, but brambles and briars still threaten to trip the unwary traveller.
120277: A grey wolf is here, thin from starvation.

The Greenway runs north and south here, straight as an arrow. On the eastern side of the road, a five-foot deep dike collects debris and serves as a runoff for the rain. To the west, a line of thick brush creates a sort of wall of undergrowth.
120278:
A waist-high evergreen shrub grows here, with thick, reaching branches.
On the shrub, there are two piles of grey-green leaves.
A brown furry gopher is here, ready to dive back underground.

Dwarf willows and juniper shrubs cling to the crevices and crannies of this rocky terrain, their roots delving into the stone, finding purchase in the most unlikely places. A cluster of hillside daisies emerges from a crevice, their delicate blooms creating a vibrant contrast amidst the monochromatic surroundings. Amidst the boulders, a solitary Scots pine stands, with a massive gnarled trunk and twisted branches.
120279:
The mauled corpse of a mother wolf.
A wolf cub happily plays here.
A wolf cub happily plays here.
The mother wolf stands here, protecting her young cubs.
A wolf cub happily plays here.

This plateau is an unattainable expanse, its surface a rugged tapestry of exposed rock and sporadic vegetation. Boulders, large and ominous, litter the surface, their surfaces are worn and weathered from countless years of exposure. Jutting crags of granite and basalt rise like jagged teeth from the plateau, their stark forms casting long shadows down the slopes.
120280: The corpse of a mean brigand is lying here.

Far removed from the Greenway, the trail here is hard to make out from the grass and short brush. The path moves in a long arc between the west and north. The area is a meadow sandwiched between two strands of hills of the South Downs.
120281: A small cluster of clover grows here.

The hills of the South Downs have broken away to the northeast and southwest to reveal a protected prairie. Only slight undulations disrupt an otherwise smooth area of land. Some burrows are tucked away against the sheltered edges of hills to the north. Imprints of larger animals indicate a favored route of wild creatures.
120282: A colourful butterfly is fluttering around here.

A large portion of the ground shows evidence of having been plowed in the past but never followed through on planting. A small, dilapidated shack nearby indicates that this was once meant to be farmland but has been abandoned. The shack only has one wall standing with a jumble of half-burnt wood making up the rest of the debris.
120283: This section of the South Downs are a mix of grass-covered hills with large patches of gravel and pebbles. The portions of the trail traversing the small rocks show deep hoof marks where previous travellers struggled. The hills continue to the southeast and northwest.
120284:
There is a huge, pyramidal beehive here.
A bee flies around here, collecting nectar from the flowers.
A bee flies around here, collecting nectar from the flowers.
An angry bee is working on a honeycomb here.
An angry bee is working on a honeycomb here.
A huge, bulky queen bee is here.

Within the hill, a burrow reveals itself, nestled amidst the boulders and earthen walls. The air in this cavern is oppressively humid, and every surface is dangerously slick. The rocks are covered in moss, a few bare patches reveal that the cave walls are made of granite. Roots protrude down through the cavern ceiling. The cave's exit to the west, concealed by natural formations, leads into the hills.
120285:
A tall stag is here, grazing peacefully.
A brigand, looking at your nice purse, is sneaking here.

The mounds of the South Downs are very close together here with little room for level ground. The trail winds through the smoothest sections possible but would be difficult for a wagon to follow closely. Short grass grows on the mounds with frequent instances of tough bunches of weeds.
120286: A black crow flies low to the ground here, looking for carrion to eat.

The ground here is a rugged tapestry, a mosaic of boulders and stones that cover the little topsoil that remains. Large flat slabs of rock, remnants of some ancient upheaval, lie strewn haphazardly about the slopes. A rocky outcrop, like a skeletal hand reaching out from the earth, interrupts the gentle incline to the west. To the east and north, the land rises sharply, forming steep, imposing barriers that preclude any passage. A solitary trail, a sinewy ribbon of earth, can be seen snaking its way in the south.
120287: Rocky Outcrop in a Sloping Ridge

A sloping ridge rises and stretches across the terrain. Amidst a rockface that marks the crest of the ridge, verdant grass finds purchase. Beyond the ridge, a line of the South Downs stretches towards the horizon. In the middle of the ridge, a rocky outcrop stands proud and resolute. Its craggy face is a tableau of shades of grey, from the lightest ash to the deepest slate.
120288:
A great bustard strides over the grass.
A swallow flies high above the ground.
A field lark stands here, focused on finding food.

The valley's verdant floor, carpeted with grass of an emerald hue, stretches northward. To the west of the valley, bald hills rise in stark contrast, their steep flanks bereft of the verdant cloak that adorns the ridge. To the south, a rocky outcrop claims attention, a majestic formation that stands proudly on the sloping ridge. The east, however, presents a formidable ascent forbidding passage.
120289: Ancient Tree in the Middle of a Wide Valley

A small black bird with red markings on its beak is here.
A field vole has frozen to the spot, sensitive to your presence.
A great bustard strides over the grass.

In the heart of the valley, there stands an ancient tree, gnarled and twisted. Its branches reach out as though trying to embrace the entirety of the valley. Its roots are burrowed deep into the ground. At night, the valley is bathed in a soft, ethereal glow, the moonlight casting long shadows, painting the landscape in shades of silver and blue. The valley continues in all directions but east, which is blocked by steep South Downs.
120290: This yawning stretch of lowland is embraced by the gentle arms of the hills. The hillsides are a tapestry woven of entangled shrubbery and sharp-edged boulders. Straggling thorn bushes grow in profusion, their branches tangled in a wild dance, their roots clutching the hardy soil, wrestling with the rocky terrain. Scattered among the shrubs, sharp-edged boulders loom large.
120291:
A small black bird with red markings on its beak is here.
A magpie is flying around looking for some food.

A serpentine narrow passage cleaves through the ancient eminence of the South Downs. The verdant hills, lush and solemn, rise on either side, their slopes thickly dressed in a quilt of moss and lichen. Thorny bushes, bristling with robust, sharp spikes, adorn the path, their toughened branches twisted into gnarled labyrinths. Leaves of deepest green, veined with a lattice of white, cluster densely and provide a sparse yet verdant canopy over the trail.
120292: The entrance to the cave in the west is partially concealed by a tangle of brambles and gnarled roots and extends into a narrow passageway that winds its way towards the South Down hills. A faint, eerie glow emanates from a cluster of bioluminescent fungi that clings to the walls. To the east, a stone wall riddled with crevices looms large.
120294: A wooden chest stands in the corner.

The chamber resembling a crack in the cave's rock serves a significant function as the smuggler's treasure storage, despite its diminutive size. This unassuming nook seems to be home to the smuggler's most valued treasures, yet the rough walls and uneven floor suggest that little work was put into its construction.
120295:
The corpse of a husky smuggler is lying here.
The corpse of a husky smuggler is lying here.
The corpse of a husky smuggler is lying here.
A rudimentary fireplace is built into the east wall.
A beautiful and docile horse is standing here.

The cave's naturally formed walls, displaying a smooth and straight appearance, evidently bear the marks of human craftsmanship. Dirty items of contraband litter the floor, while boxes and barrels stand empty, ready to be filled with ill-gotten gains. To the west, a narrow passage beckons the curious, a sinuous crack in the rock just wide enough for a slender frame to slip through. To the north, the wall is adorned with strange markings.
120296: The corpse of a rattlesnake is lying here.

At the edge of a great valley, a generous expanse of life nestles within the embrace of the South Downs. Unapproachable they stand, their steep sides a formidable wall to the north and east, a challenge to any who would venture here. The lichen that thrives here has been cropped close to the ground by the unceasing diligence of the valley's true artisans, the sheep. At the valley's edge, a grove of hazelnut trees thrives. On the other side, a rocky outcrop thrusts upwards, its surfaces adorned with lichen and moss.
120297:
A bright red mushroom is growing here.
A bubbling brook winds through the valley.

Amid this secluded valley, a clear, bubbling brook winds its way. Its melody, a harmonious symphony of gentle ripples, echoes off the rocky walls. It nourishes the land, bringing forth patches of bluebell and gorse, their colours a stark contrast against the green and grey. Clustered around this brook are several moss-laden boulders, their surfaces veined with lichen, creating an abstract tapestry of life on stone. They serve as resting spots for the weary, a haven for the small creatures of the valley.
120298: Green at the Base of a Hill

The land here is covered in a verdant carpet of lush green grass, stretching as far as the eye can see to the west and south, and up to the base of the hills to the north and east. A small stream babbles along the bottom of the hill, its gurgling provides soothing background noise. Resilient lichen that forms a verdant carpet is cropped close to the earth. Indicating unseen grazers who find sustenance here.
120299: A beautiful and docile horse is standing here.

This meadow, resting in a deep valley, is cloaked in a light veil of mist that rises off the slightly wet ground. The field spreads out, dotted with clusters of wildflowers and tall grass, which hold onto the moisture with a gentle grip. The atmosphere within the meadow is calm and soothing, with the quiet rustling of the moist grass underfoot and the distant call of valley birds.
120300:
A field vole has frozen to the spot, sensitive to your presence.
A sharp-eyed hawk is here stalking some prey.

The valley lies nestled amidst the hills, shrouded in a mystical mist that swirls and eddies around the bases of the trees, their trunks emerging from the ethereal cloudiness. The terrain beneath is a unique kind of soil, marsh-like and springy. It bounces back at each step, as if in playful jest.
120301: Wide Valley Passing through the Hills

A field lark stands here, focused on finding food.
A small black bird with red markings on its beak is here.

A low valley, several miles wide, passes through the hills of the South Downs like a river flowing through a canyon. Covered in tall, green, grass, these fields wave in the wind like the sail of some massive ship. A few flowers dot the landscape, providing a bit of colour to the green expanse.
120302: A field vole has frozen to the spot, sensitive to your presence.

Verdant waves of grass cover the landscape here in every shade imaginable. A few flaxen flowers are the only break in the otherwise viridescent vegetation. The grass is long, easily knee-high, but still smooth and silky like a finely woven cloak.
120303: Patch of Grass Nestled in the Hills

There are two handfuls of clover here.
A large brown snake with black patches is coiled here.
A large brown snake with black patches is coiled here.

This patch of grassy fields marks an odd end to the otherwise open plains between the hills. A deep dike east of the Greenway creates an impassable obstacle to the west, while the hills to the north and east are so steep as to make them equally unnavigable. Only the fields back to the south offer any way out.
120304:
A big, brown, angry-looking bear is here.
A big, brown, angry-looking bear is here.

This moist den is covered in wet leaves and mud. A few depressions have been made in one corner, perhaps caused by some large beast rolling over in its sleep there. A flap of packed mud on the western wall marks the only exit to this tight chamber.
120305: The hills border this green valley to the west and south, while the valley expands to the north and east. A few shrubs grow at the base of the hill, like stitches at a seam. To the southeast, the valley widens even more like a canyon through the plains.
120306: This hilltop marks the northern end of one of the tall ridges of the South Downs. A few lines of packed dirt, barely visible, mark where travellers have left the safety and predictability of the Greenway to venture into the valley between the hills.
120307: A hardened ranger is walking around, looking for tracks.

The road bends here, skirting the line of hills to the east. It is lined with shallow ditches that allow water to run off the packed dirt into a deep, narrow dike. An old fence sits just past the eastern edge of the road, slightly in disrepair but still whole. A short trail juts off the Greenway through an opening in the fence.
120308: The wildflower meadow is a riot of colour, with petals of every hue imaginable swaying in the breeze. The ground is covered in a soft carpet of green grass, punctuated by small patches of wildflowers. Tall stalks of lavender jostle for space with bright pink coneflowers, while delicate white daisies nod their heads in the wind.
120309:
The corpse of a wild dog is lying here.
A magpie is flying around looking for some food.

The sunflower field stretches as far as the eye can see, an ocean of yellow that bathes the landscape in a warm glow. The sunflowers themselves are tall and proud, their petals soft and velvety to the touch, and their bright yellow heads always facing the sun. Beneath the canopy of sunflowers, the soft rustle of sunflower stems swaying in the gentle breeze creates a unique melody.
120310: A field vole has frozen to the spot, sensitive to your presence.

The rocky boulders, formidable and ancient, stand like a bulwark at this secluded valley's boundaries. The valley, a verdant cradle, is adorned with a carpet of soft, lush grass. The slopes, meanwhile, are sharp and unyielding, an almost unscalable fortress of earthen and stone defences that nearly encircles the valley. Narrow paths that slice through the monolithic boulders.
120311: A few trees grow in a line, providing only sparse shade. Tall grass dominates the landscape, resembling an unkempt pasture. A dusty trail runs straight east to west, its surface cracked and dry from the sun. A stretch of the South Downs hills can be seen close to the east.
120312: The trail gets thinner the farther away from the Greenway it becomes. It climbs between some hills to the south and meanders fairly straight to the east. Grass encroaches on the trail as it appears rarely used. A cliff to the west descends slowly to a field in the north.
120313:
A tall flower with a large head and bright yellow petals sways gently in the breeze.
A tall stag is here, grazing peacefully.

The vibrant green fields sprawl between the hills situated to the west, north and east. The grass is soft and inviting, perfect for grazing sheep and cattle. The air is filled with the sweet smell of fresh grass and wildflowers, and the only sounds are the distant cries of birds and the gentle rustling of the leaves in the breeze.
120314: This elevated meadow stands a touch above the surrounding plains, offering a gentle rise to the landscape. The open area stretches endlessly in all directions, its continuity sporadically interrupted by a boulder or a cluster of stones.
