Situated at the heart of the meadow is a semi-circle of boulders, assembled into a rudimentary windbreak. To the west of this area, the landscape evolves dramatically, with steep, imposing cliffs.
120315: The vibrant green meadow is like a sea of emeralds, stretching out in every direction. The grass is soft and lush, perfect for grazing animals, and the air is filled with the sweet fragrance of fresh-cut hay. Small wildflowers dot the landscape, their bright colours providing a delightful contrast to the verdant green of the grass.
120316:
A large elk is standing here, chewing grass and leaves.
A large elk is standing here, chewing grass and leaves.
A black wolf pads restlessly, looking for its next prey.

Gentle, undulating hills rise in the heart of these verdant grasslands. A soft carpet of bright, green fescue graces their sinuous forms, each blade dancing in the whispering wind. The grass grows taller along the sloping sides, with its bladed heads weighed down by seeds, demonstrating the fertility of this land.
120317:
A large, flat-topped boulder is here.
A beautiful and docile horse is standing here.

A narrow passage snakes its way through the South Downs that rise in a spectacle of earth and stone. This path, squeezed between the hills, looks like a thin lifeline cleaved into the landscape. The terrain rises abruptly, with steep hills full of rocks. The path is a thin trail, made of hard ground and scattered stones, that turns and twists without warning.
120318:
There are two clusters of yellow flowers here.
A skeleton of some humanoid lies in the dust.
A sturdy billy goat stands here, proudly protecting his goats.

On these hilltops, paper birch and trembling aspen stand in sporadic clusters, their bark gleaming silver and white, their leaves a vibrant green. Beneath their dappled shade, a meadow of lowbush blueberries and bunchberries springs forth, their round forms huddled close to the earth.
120319: A swallow flies high above the ground.

The surface of the rock is rough and pitted. At the edge of the plateau, the adventurers can see a series of rock outcrops that seem to defy gravity. These formations jut out from the side of the promontory at impossible angles, as if daring the wind to knock them down. Twisted, scraggly birches cling to the rocky soil, their branches gnarled and twisted by the wind.
120320:
A mean looking robber is here, demanding money from you.
A mean looking robber is here, demanding money from you.

A skilled craftsman has meticulously transformed the grotto's walls, which were once jagged and rough, into smooth surfaces. Within the grotto, various crates and barrels are carefully arranged, indicating that this space has been used as a warehouse or a hideout. To the east, the grotto continues into a stone-lined passage. To the west, a large stone slab, perfectly fitted to the grotto's wall, conceals an exit leading to the South Downs.
120321: Nestled along the passage, wooden cupboards, crates, and barrels are neatly arranged, suggesting the space's previous use as a warehouse or hideout. The scent of damp earth and moss fills the nostrils. The sound of water dripping from stalactites and echoing off the walls create a rhythmic, almost melodic symphony. The passage continues toward the west and the east.
120322:
A small oaken table has been set here.
On the table, there are a shortsword, a rigid leather breastplate, a cup, and a bottle.
A malicious thug is here, threatening you.
A malicious thug is here, threatening you.
A swarthy, little bandit advances forward.
A wiry smuggler is here, attempting to avoid being seen.

The walls of the hollow are a mixture of raw, jagged stone and smooth, carved surfaces, evidence of both nature's hand and the skilled touch. Crates and barrels line the walls and tables and chairs are scattered throughout the space, worn by time and use. In the centre of the hollow, a stone table stands, its surface engraved with markings that look like some sort of a map. The only exit from the hollow is to the west, a subtle crack in the rocky facade, adorned with intricately woven vines that blend seamlessly with the surrounding environment.
120323: Swelling hillocks rise from the earth like the backs of great, slumbering beasts. As a symphony of green, they are adorned with hardy weeds and resilient grasses. Crabgrass stands in defiant clusters, its blades sharp and unyielding, reaching up towards the sky amidst these grassy ranks, bearberry and wintergreen creep, their low forms tracing the contours of the hillocks, their red berries a stark contrast to the surrounding green.
120324: The terrain is adorned with undulating hillocks, rolling gracefully throughout the landscape. Huge boulders are scattered across these hillocks, their shadows cast silhouettes over the ground. The paths that wind their way through the hillocks are not man-made but are etched into the land by the patient hand of water. To the north, a cliff obstructs the path standing as a barrier.
120325:
The corpse of a black wolf is lying here.
The corpse of a rabid, grey wolf is lying here.
The corpse of a pack leader is lying here.
A large elk is standing here, chewing grass and leaves.

Scattered around these hills, massive boulders cloaked in a shroud of vibrant green moss, squat heavily on the earth. Great black oaks, the ancient lords of the forest, loom ominously over the tall stones, their gnarled limbs stretch out with dark and deeply furrowed bark. To the south, a worn trail meanders, winding through the verdant hills of Arda. To the east, a rocky outcrop springs forth, a sentinel of stone upon the sloping ridge. The northern vista is a tapestry of rolling hillocks.
120326: The hills from the northwest climb higher here and stand on a precipice above grasslands to the west and south. The ground is a mix of grass and pebbly soil. A lone tree, long dead, stands on the edge of the cliff to the west. The bark has been stripped and weathered, a grey trunk with broken limbs is all that remains.
120327: These hills form the eastern part of a long section of the South Downs extending to the northwest and the southeast. The mounds rise to the west until they end in a cliff. The elevation slowly decreases into a field to the north but is blocked to the east by a jumble of rocks. The large stones appear to have been pushed upward out of the ground and tumbled back on top of themselves.
120328: The tall hills here follow a winding cliff to the east until smoothing out at a lower elevation into a large field to the south. Eastern movement is blocked by a natural wall made of large stones too difficult to climb over. The hills are covered with dense, short grass.
120329: A lone, dead tree stands solitary among the vegetation.

Hills to the north slowly lower down into this stretch of flat ground. Grass and weeds grow in varying heights creating a scraggly landscape. Thin stalks of brown vegetation sprout up between patches of grass and dip their heads in lazy arcs. The fields sprawl out to the west and south with some knolls farther in the distance.
120330: The elevation of the grassy plains here seems to be slightly lower than the surrounding fields causing water to slowly collect. The result is a lush meadow where each imprint in the ground sends mud squishing out of the roots of the grass.
120331: Thick grass grows tall and droops back toward the ground. The vegetation covers the area completely and appears more pale than the adjoining meadow. The lush green colour is replaced with something closer to white and appears almost sickly. A large growth of brush extends to the south.
120332: This hill is clearly part of the South Downs extending to the northwest and southeast, but is separated by steep edges to the west and east. Exposed rocks and dirt tumble precipitously from the top of the hill. A patch of brush extends to the north.
120333:
The remains of a thick tangle of vines lie here in a heap of rotting compost.
A large thorny branched shrub is growing here.
On the shrub, there are two piles of blackberries.
Some thick writhing vines whip all around you.

The area is covered in knee-high bushes. They are remarkably stiff and make movement difficult as the branches tug and resist shifting. The ground between bushes is sparse grass mixed with broken twigs and dirt. Some large boulders partially obscure a cave in the hill to the west.
120334: A great, dark wolf stands here, sniffing the air.

Some worn bones have been collected into a corner of this cave. It appears to have been used by a bear or other wild animals at some point but has since seen further excavation to expand the area shown by a stark contrast in wall textures as the cave moves deeper into the hill. Tin and iron cooking equipment is scattered around a fire pit with animal furs in a pile nearby.
120335: A mass of wriggling vines drops on you from the trees.

Through the dense, creeping plants covering the ground, there is faint evidence of a path that runs north to south. The path has not been maintained or used regularly, and as a result, plants have overgrown it, making it difficult to see and use. It is unclear where the path leads, but it is a reminder of a time when this area was more heavily travelled.
120336:
The remains of a mass of vines lie here in a heap of rotting compost.
The corpse of a striped snake is lying here.
The remains of a thick tangle of vines lie here in a heap of rotting compost.
Some thick writhing vines whip all around you.
A garden snake slithers harmlessly here.

The centre of the area was once a crossroads where paths trail off to the north and south. Fainter tracks split off to the west and east but it isn't clear if they were created by animals or human inhabitants. Bushes and creeping vines have enveloped the landscape.
120337: A long abandoned trail snakes between the north and south. Grass covering the hills to the south covers the trail as it climbs in that direction. Dense vines prevent grass from growing over the old path as it moves to the north. Leafy climbing plants resist any movement.
120338: A great wolf with coal-black eyes stares intently at you, drooling saliva.

A wide field of rough grass covers the area. Wildflowers dot the land adding shades of colour to the sea of green. A difficult incline begins to the west. Thick vines interlocking with each other in an impassable mess mark the beginning of rough brush to the east and south.
120339: The only gentle slope on the hill is towards the east. All other directions are precipitously steep. The top of the hill is craggy with rocks of many sizes strewn unevenly. A few small burrows emerge from the dusty ground near the base of larger boulders that give cover for small rodents.
120340: A large brown snake with black patches is coiled here.

The soft grass is interrupted by a variety of dirt trails intersecting in the middle of the area. Well-trod paths wind off in all directions except to the south as a tall hill blocks the way. Animals travelling from grass fields surrounding the South Downs seem to make regular use of this intersection.
120341:
A small cluster of clover grows here.
A large brown snake with black patches is coiled here.

This quiet meadow is cradled between hills of the South Downs. The mounds stand like sentinels, blocking passage to the north. But in other directions, they rise more gently, allowing travellers to pass unimpeded. The field continues to the east for a long distance. Patches of wildflowers speckle the otherwise completely green landscape.
120342: A lone hawk soars high above you.

The grassy hills of the South Downs begin to descend down to the east where they meet a long field. Hills continue in all other directions without any unique features. A few solitary trees break up the green landscape. Thick bark covers the trunks leading to sparse branches with wide, floppy leaves.
120343: The ground rises from the valley in the west to meet the rest of the hills of the South Downs. Small, coffin-shaped lumps push up in modest hillocks around the larger hills. Scrubby weeds mingle with wildflowers in an otherwise grassy landscape.
120344: A wild bull seems ready to charge you.

Rolling hills extend in all directions for several miles. Green waves of grass rise and fall gently, while occasional trees break up the sea of emerald. A rabbit hole is unusually obvious being the only speck of brown in the lush landscape.
120345: A black and white skunk is scuttling about here, searching for food.

The hills of the South Downs extend in all directions like the undulating sand dunes of a desert. The green hills of grass rise and fall gracefully without sharp edges. Animal droppings dot the landscape frequently on account of regular visits by grazing creatures.
120346: The trail winds around a large, low mound, connecting the western and northern trail sections. Small pebbles from a dry streambed zig-zag down the side of the wide mound, eventually cutting through the trail. The South Downs stretch out to the south and east.
120347: The ground tumbles with mounds and knolls rising from a low level in the north to sharp edges to the east and south. The drop-off is too precipitous to allow movement to the east and south. Tall hills continue to the west. Hardy grass covers the land with colourful flecks of wildflowers occasionally peeking between the foliage.
120348:
The corpse of a wild bull is lying here.
A rock lizard is here, motionless as it observes you.

Rolling hills progressively grow taller towards the west and south. Short grass covers the ground up to the western and southern edges where reddish-brown dirt is exposed on the steep cliff. The hill face to the south has natural landings that could be climbed with enough skill.
120349: Steep escarpments mark the edges of these hills to the north and west, making passage impossible in those directions. A narrow ridge passes onto the hills to the south, while a gentle slope leads into a low valley to the east. Scattered small rocks speckle the landscape, leaving occasional grey spots in the otherwise green expanse.
120350: The dark earth of the Greenway makes another winding turn through the hills to the east and the patch of forest to the west. Beyond the forest, more hills rise, leaving little else on the horizon. To the east, a low valley lies between the ridges.
120351: Packed mud tracks with a wide strip of grass between them mark this portion of the Greenway. To the east, the billowing mounds of the South Downs rise and fall in long ridges like trees fallen on the green plains. West of the road, a small patch of forest marks the most significant vegetation for miles.
120352: The road narrows here, as the hills rise to the east and the dike to the west widens. Small pebbles and rocks line the dirt road, apparently the last vestige of some attempts to hold back the mud. Deep tracks in two parallel lines evidence the failure of that effort. Scores of extremely thick, gnarly bushes, effectively obstruct all travel to the west and east of the road.
120353: The road makes a sharp turn here as it winds around the forest to the north and west and the hills to the east. Two brown ruts have been dug deep by the biting turn of heavy-laden wagons. A circle of rocks off one corner of the road indicates this is a popular spot to rest and build a fire.
120354: Patch of Forest beside the Greenway

The eastern end of this stand of trees butts up to the Greenway here. A few of the trees have been cut, evidently needed by some industrious traveller. To the west, the forest thickens as the trees grow taller and closer together. To the south, the Greenway slowly snakes its way around the hills to the southwest.
120393:
A large beautiful rose bush is blooming here.
Deep inside the bush, there is a red rose with leaves and thorny stem.
A snake slithers towards you.

The thick, thorny, and generally inflexible nature of the bushes around here makes it impossible to navigate the area properly. The bushes form an utterly impenetrable wall to the west, while travel in other directions is possible by cutting through gaps in the thorns. The straight line of the Greenway is just visible through the shrubbery to the east.
120394:
A grey wolf is here, thin from starvation.
A robin is here, carrying small pieces of wood to its nest.
A magpie is flying around looking for some food.

This is the site of an old, ruined farmstead. A long time ago, a house, a barn and an outhouse stood here, but now the remains are almost completely hidden by overgrowth, thick bushes, and briars. Brush so thick that not even the sun would shine through it blocks all passage westwards, while other directions can probably be negotiated with some care.
120395: A sturdy pack horse is standing here.

Scores of thick, gnarly bushes effectively obstruct all travel in every direction except to the south. The ground beneath the thorny brambles is almost completely covered in a web of roots, with the bulkiest specimens thick as the arm of a full-grown man.
120399:
A robin is here, carrying small pieces of wood to its nest.
A partridge attempts to hide in the undergrowth.
A partridge attempts to hide in the undergrowth.

A level plain is blanketed with dense thickets of thorny bushes. These plants vary in height, ranging from waist-high to towering over a mounted rider, creating a formidable challenge for navigation. The vegetation to the west is impenetrable, rendering travel in that direction impossible.
120400: Both visibility and travel are severely impaired by the dense shrubbery that grows here. Among the wild bushes, black, moss-covered boulders further the inaccessibility of the area. To the north and south, the shrub-infested lands continue, while to the east the Greenway is just visible through the growth.
120401: A multitude of greenery and shrubs populate the area. Different species of plants blend together into a wild undergrowth. Small rocks are mixed in with the dry bushes. The weeds become more scattered towards the south where undulating hills dominate the scenery.
120402:
A field mouse noses about hungrily, searching for food.
A large mother hawk is here looking for prey to feed her young.

The hills are dominated by thick, green grasses of several varieties. Taller grasses shoot up towards the sky before bending over lazily towards the earth, unable to hold their full weight erect. A few narrow animal trails can be seen winding paths through the grass.
120403: Grassy hills cover the area, increasing in height towards the west until they appear impassable. The taller hills are the only bits of land void of the lush meadow that covers the rest of the area. Small animals could easily hide among the waving blades of grass.
120404: The hills here are long and wide without jagged features. Long grasses cover the entirety of the ground. The grass is a lush green colour like well-watered moss with occasional notes of darker greens. More hills can be seen in every direction.
120405:
A fallow deer is grazing peacefully here.
A white wolf is here, prowling for something to eat.

This broad hill gently slopes down to the east with more severe slopes in other directions. A few solitary trees give each other companionship on the otherwise sparse land. Sparse grass and weeds are more visible at lower elevations. A slight height advantage compared to the surrounding hills allows for intermittent glimpses of the Greenway to the east.
120406: A tall rock wall stands to the south as a last connection to the canyon to the west. Hills sprawl to the north and east. Large rocks have broken off from the wall to the south and have tumbled down and rest, growing fungus and moss. Some animal tracks are visible as they converge into the canyon.
120407: Bulbous rocks hang off the sides of the canyon to the north and south. The boulders precariously rest appearing as if the slightest movement could unleash them down the sides of the canyon into the valley below. The valley is not smooth, with rough hills where the ground has piled around stones that fell from the cliffs long ago.
120408:
A beautiful and docile horse is standing here.
A fallow deer is grazing peacefully here.

Tall canyon walls slowly curve allowing paths to the east and south. Several animal tracks have cleared narrow paths through the tall grass. The canyon walls slope slowly as they meet the floor of the valley. The walls are too steep to hold any vegetation except an occasional tough bush.
120409: An imposing canyon forms to the north while the sides open up to the east and west. Lumpy hills covered in thick grasses cover the area. Taller bluffs block movement south and can be seen further east. Scattered boulders grow moss in a variety of colours.
120416: Once a broad and busy highway, this road has now fallen into a state of disrepair. Thick, thorny shrubberies lay to the west, while a deep dike bars the way to the east. Farther east, the sloping ridges of the South Downs continue, giving an undulating outline to the otherwise flat horizon.
120423: Once a great highway, this road has gradually grown into disrepair. Its surface is covered by moss and grass except for the twin tracks made by the coaches and wagons that still brave the journey. A wide trench, several feet deep, serves to keep water from washing away what is left of the road.
120426: Heavy and thick bushes form barrier-like obstacles here, making travel extremely difficult. To the east, the hills of the South Downs rise over the plains. To the south, the bushes and shrubbery turn to a circle of tall trees, providing a sharp peak to the otherwise flat skyline.
120429: The Greenway makes a sharp turn here as it winds around the hills to the east and the forest to the southwest. The road is hard, packed, dirt, with deep grooves carved in two lines by heavy wheels of wagons. The corner of the bend has begun to deteriorate into a muddy mess of a hole thanks to some careless drivers' attempts to shave a few inches off their journey.
120436:
A cluster of white star-shaped forget-me-nots flourish here in reminiscence.
A shallow pond is here, tinted green with algae.
A dense carpet of blue flowers dip their heads in the breeze.
A red-breasted mallard swims about, periodically upending to look for food.
A red-breasted mallard swims about, periodically upending to look for food.
A red-breasted mallard swims about, periodically upending to look for food.

A large stand of trees has sprouted here, nestled between the downs to the west and the Greenway to the east. Among the trees, a small pond has formed, covered in a blanket of moss and green lily pads. To the south, the forest thickens with broad, aged trees.
120437:
A field mouse noses about hungrily, searching for food.
A white wolf is here, prowling for something to eat.

Low bushy weeds share the ground with longer grasses. The area is dominated by green plants, but a few cracks can be seen where the dirt is visible. The grassy knolls are all similar in height, too high to see over from the ravines between.
120444: A beautiful and docile horse is standing here.

Stumps from long broken trees and low brush sporadically cover the landscape. The hills show long striations from top to bottom as if raked by a giant claw. Inside the long marks can be seen dirt of deep brown, red and tan. Patches of sand are exposed near the bottom of the hills.
120445: A large brown snake with black patches is coiled here.

Tall rock formations block all movement except back to the north. Trenches in the ground make traversing the terrain difficult. Shallow mud congeals in the bottom of the deep furrows. Grass and weeds sparsely habitate the ground outside the troughs.
120446: A cluster of dark green, feathery fronds flourishes in the shade.

The undergrowth thins here, giving way to a crunchy layer of grass, branches, and brown leaves. The trees grow high, with very few branches except at the top of the canopy. A few spots of sky are sprinkled across the treetops, giving a speckled look to the view up above.
120447:
A tall pine tree grows here.
A robin is here, carrying small pieces of wood to its nest.
A snake slithers towards you.

The forest is thin here, encroached by the rolling downs to the west and the Greenway to the east. A steep, rocky slope to the west makes travel that way impossible, but to the south, the slopes are much more forgiving. The Greenway bends around the forest to the east, giving a snake-like switchback to the otherwise straight road.
120449: The South Downs come to a point here, poking toward the Greenway to the east. Down the slopes to the north, a large stand of trees covers the horizon, the only significant amount of trees for many miles. A narrow ridge across the mounds leads west, deeper into the Downs.
120451:
A small and tough weed grows here.
A brown fox is here, looking for some rabbits to chew up.

Three long trenches run from west to east as if carved by the claws of an unimaginable beast . Each trench is higher than the last, eventually culminating in a ridge preventing passage to the north. The bottoms of the long cuts contain a permanent mud. Some tough weeds struggle to grow on the steep sides of the troughs.
120453: There are several huge boulders arranged in a large circle of flat ground. The great stones are covered in a thick moss and seem to have been stationary for a very long time. Inside the circle are very faint imprints in the dirt, partially covered in short grass. Outside the circle are rising hills.
120455: A chasm looms deep to the west. Some trees grow on the edge of the precipice curving west and then upwards as if they were almost pulled into the depths when the ground broke. The area outside the chasm is scarred with jagged holes and uneven terrain.
120457: This nook is located below steep slopes in all directions except the east. It is well protected from the wind and elements, allowing heavy brush and short, wide trees to grow with abandon. Along with the growth here, tracks of rabbits and foxes can be seen in the passages through the brush and grass.
120459:
A brown fox is here, looking for some rabbits to chew up.
A restless rabbit bounces around.

Towering hills rise and fall in every direction. They are rocky and steep-sided, with extensive areas of exposed rock and little clinging vegetation. A few claw marks and abandoned nests left in nooks and cracks attest to the presence of at least some wildlife here.
120461:
An elk cow gazes coldly at you, chewing on a small branch.
A restless rabbit bounces around.

Rugged hills rolls out in every direction, hindering visibility and travel. There is no flat path to walk on, and the soil along the sides of the hills is gravelly and loose in spots. An occasional breeze passes through the hills, carrying with it the scent of pine or sage.
120465:
A large, venomous-looking green snake is coiled up here.
A large, venomous-looking green snake is coiled up here.
A small grasshopper clings to a blade of grass, ready to spring.
A brown fox is here, looking for some rabbits to chew up.

The ground rises above the surrounding hills. The view from the highest point reveals expansive undulating knolls in all directions. The view is interrupted only by a few trees managing to survive on this exposed piece of land. A steep drop off from the high ground allows movement only to the south.
120466: This is a precipice on the eastern edge of a rugged, hilly region that rolls out west and north of here. A slope drops off to the east, steep but traversable to flat plains beyond. In the distance, further east, the flat Greenway winds its way through a valley.
120467: Some robust trees with bushy leaves populate the area. The trees are spread out, prefering isolation over the community of a grove. Short grass mixed with weeds prevents almost any glimpse of dirt or rocks. A long abandoned broken wagon wheel is growing moss, propped against one of the trees.
120468: A worm is here slithering around.

As the road curves it begins to be sheltered by a cliff wall to the west. Hills descending from the northwest allow the road to carve through this area maintaining an easy grade. A field is to the north and a trail branching off from the Greenway is to the east.
120469: The road enters a narrow gorge here. Tall cliffs to the east and west sandwich the road allowing short hours of daylight. The ground beside the road is void of plants and life except for some faint tracks of small lizards. The road continues north and south.
120470: A woody evergreen plant grows here, with many stems reaching upward.

The hills in this area are rugged and bare, with only the occasional grasses and shrubs growing on them. The soil is rocky, loose, and challenging to travel over. The only signs of wildlife are of small mammals and birds that can easily shelter in nooks in the rocks.
120471: A brown fox is here, looking for some rabbits to chew up.

The slopes of the hills in the area are covered by fallen trees. A very strong wind must have passed through here at one time, uprooting many trees while snapping others at the trunk. Even while lying on their side, many trees continue to bud and grow leaves through the seasons. Plains open up south and west of here, while to the north there is an expanse of more hills.
120472: This is the eastern end of a valley, surrounded by towering hills on all sides except where it stretches outward, leading towards the west. The ground is covered in tall, golden grass that rustles gently in the breeze. Gentle slopes lead up into the hills north of here.
120473:
A large elk is standing here, chewing grass and leaves.
A black snake, with red markings, is lying here.

Tall grass populates the heart of a valley. Hills rise up north and south of here, while the soft valley floor stretches east and west. Large, shady trees spot the landscape. The grass is matted down here and there, signs that large animals bed down here often.
120474:
A reddish-brown shrub with purplish-pink flowers grows here.
Inside the shrub, there are three clusters of purplish-pink flowers.
A large elk is standing here, chewing grass and leaves.

This is the western end of a sprawling valley that winds its way between rolling hills. The valley floor is covered in tall, golden grass that rustles gently in the breeze. In the distance, a dry streambed crosses the valley. To the west, the hills rise up gently, their peaks just visible above the grass. To the east, the valley continues as far as the eye can see.
120481: This is the crest of a steep, green hill. The rolling terrain is dotted with large rocks, jagged outcroppings, and twisted shrubs. The grass is tall and swaying, rustling with every breeze. The air is filled with a strong, fermented scent from bear scat. The area is alive with other signs of bear activity, such as footprints and scratch marks on tree trunks.
120482: A deep V-shaped trough is cut naturally into the eastern slope of a hill, and travels upwards and downwards. Below here, the trough is heavily shaded by trees and covered by brush. It appears to drop below the ground, but it is impossible to see where it leads.
120483:
A long-necked bird, with a fairly short spear-like bill stands here.
An elk cow gazes coldly at you, chewing on a small branch.

Plains travel westward through a narrow valley. In all other directions, hills rise up to block or hinder travel. In the nearly vertical face of a hill to the north, a wide fissure seems to lead deep into the hill. In front of it is a small stone circle with a charred interior, the remains of a long dormant campfire.
120484:
A wild bull seems ready to charge you.
A wild bull seems ready to charge you.
A junebug buzzes slowly through the air.

The grass on this plain grows wild and verdant, reaching well above four feet high. Patches of wheat sprout here and there, never cultivated, but rather, growing wildly. The soil is loose, and dozens of small holes and burrows are visible within, home of many mice and snakes.
120486: These grassy plains roll up and down in verdant waves. Flat boulders poke a few inches out above the soil, their grey surfaces dotted green and brown with lichen. Gentle slopes lead to the south and east, while tall and impassable hills block travel elsewhere.
120487:
A small cluster of clover grows here.
A long-necked bird, with a fairly short spear-like bill stands here.

Only thistles grow more than a few inches high here. Most of the grass is shorn close to the ground, looking to be frequently grazed on. The earth is lumpy and recently churned in parts, showing evidence of many hooved animals travelling through this area.
120488: Grasses grow lush and thick here, their broad blades a dark green. The ground is soft and spongy from an abundance of moisture. Water runs off the surrounding hills and saturates in the earth here in this valley. The valley floor can be followed west and south from here.
120489:
A brown pond between old branches and roots is here.
A swarm of midges is here, humming around you.

Rainfall running off the surrounding hills collects here, filling stangant pools of water. Swarms of midges thrive here, and their humming fills the air constantly. Grass and other groundcover grows only sporadically, leaving much of the terrain soft and muddy.
120490:
A long, flat boulder lies on its side, providing a place to rest.
A large bullfrog croaks loudly.
A swarm of midges is here, humming around you.
A swarm of midges is here, humming around you.

A narrow valley passes northward between the hills here. The ground is grassy and easily traversed, but becomes more wild and overgrown as one travels west. Tiny flowers can be seen peeking above the undergrowth here and there. Grey stones litter the valley floor beneath a smattering of oak trees.
120491:
A swarm of hornets is coming out of its nest.
A swarm of hornets is coming out of its nest.

Thistles and spiny bushes growing over four feet high fill this area. The air and vegetation are filled with all manner of stinging and biting insects. A constant buzzing drowns out all other sounds. The ground is soft and muddy in parts, with thousands of pock-marks where insects have gathered balls of mud for their nests.
120492:
A swarm of hornets is coming out of its nest.
A swarm of hornets is coming out of its nest.

An enormous tree with thick, interwoven branches towers over the thistles and bushes. The trunk rises only a few feet above the ground before splitting into several large branches and hundreds of smaller ones. Its centre is filled by a massive hornet nest made of wood pulp and mud, nearly the size of a small cottage. A loud buzzing fills the air.
120493:
A skeleton of some humanoid lies in the dust.
A huge grizzly bear is here, roaming the wild.
A huge grizzly bear is here, roaming the wild.

The fissure in the earth leading outside to the south opens to a small cave within the hill. Three natural pillars of stone and earth rise between the uneven floor and ceiling. Scattered about are bones and debris, evidence that this cave was inhabited by man or creature at one time.
120501: To either side of the road, the large hills of the South Downs rise like the walls of a canyon. The eastern hills are steep and rocky, making passage impossible, while the western slopes have a much more forgiving grade. Some of the road has begun to wash away, apparently caused by the rain running off the adjacent hills.
120502: The road here is hard, packed dirt. Only a few small pebbles can be seen pushed off to the sides of the road. Thin, knee-high weeds grow tenaciously where they can avoid wagon wheels and boots. The ground slopes down slightly to the west and into a field. Hills to the east block the way.
120503: The greenway curves here and can be followed west or north. A smaller path leads off to the east without any sign indicating what waits at the end. Hills can be seen far off in almost every direction. A narrow gorge can be seen to the south.
120504: A tall cliff of dirt and stones rises in the west. The gorge to the north pauses here and opens to the east into a field in front of some decrepit buildings. Some grass and clover creep in from the east encroaching on the dusty road.
120505: The Greenway moves in a large curve between the north and west. An imposing cliff maintains a tall presence to the northwest. The rolling hills of the South Downs can be glimpsed to the east through ruined buildings. A wide field sprawls to the south.
120506: A steep hill rises west and north of the road, which travels east to curve around it. A tree grows nearly in the centre of the road here, looking quite out of place and creating an unusual obstacle that travellers must navigate around.
120507:
A large rabbit looks peacefully at you, ready to dart away.
A squirrel scampers around here, looking for nuts from the trees.

Steep hills rise east and west of the grassy green road here, keeping it almost continuously in shade. The earthen barriers muffle sound, keeping the air here quiet. The ground must often stay wet, as deep wagon ruts can be seen following the road north and south.
120508:
A weather-worn statue lies near the road here, having toppled over decades ago.
A squirrel scampers around here, looking for nuts from the trees.
A ruffian is sneaking around here, looking for some mischief to do.

The road is completely covered with dense, bright grass as it travels north and south. Only the occasional footprint or cart track can be seen, showing this part of the Greenway to be rarely travelled. Large, flat stones mark the start of an old pathway branching off of the main road to the west.
120509: A ruffian is sneaking around here, looking for some mischief to do.

The road is hard to follow here as it curves from the west to the north. Some time ago, sandy soil from a steep embankment to the east washed down and covered the road, which was then overrun by sage and other brush.
120510: A mass of dark green leaves clings to a wall.

The remains of an ancient stone wall follow along the west and north sides of the road as it curves and travels south and east. Thick, woody vines have grown into the wall in such a way that they hold it in place. In places with no such reinforcement, only rubble exists.
120511: Game trails made by rabbits and deer criss-cross the grassy road here, leading between the impassable bush thicket to the west and the open bushy plains to the east. This part of the Greenway clearly sees more traffic from creatures with four legs than from those with two. The road stretches as far as can be seen north and south.
120512: A wain lies wrecked and in pieces on the side of the road.

Soft green grass hides most of the hoof and foot prints left by the scant few travellers of this ancient road that travels north and south. A dense thicket of thorny bushes encroaches on the road from the west. East of here, the bushy plains are more open.
120513: The Greenway bends to the north and west. The road is wide, impressive, and lined with heavy stones. It is bordered on its sides by lush, green grasses and low shrubs. A thick wall of brush runs parallel to the road on the eastern side. This road is the primary route of travel between Bree and Tharbad.
120514: The Greenway continues winding through the countryside, bending east and south. It is bordered to the west by the base of a steep cliff, which runs parallel with the road, and a line of dense brush to the east. The road itself is wide, impressive, and lined with stones.
120515: The Greenway narrows down here, as it passes between the base of a very steep cliff to the west, and a wall of dense brush to the east. The road is lined with heavy stones, which have been worn down in the centre due to heavy travel. The sides of the road, between the cliff and brush, are bordered by lush, green grasses.
120516: The Greenway continues its journey between Bree and Tharbad here. To the west, a vast, imposing thistle patch grows. The undergrowth is so thick in this direction that it is only possible to travel in this direction on foot. Even then, passage will be difficult and perilous.
120517: The Greenway bends to the north and west here, continuing to wind through the countryside between Bree and Tharbad. It is lined with heavy stones, and worn well in the centre, a sign of heavy use and travel. Dense, thick brush border it to the east.
120518: The Greenway curves sharply east and south, running parallel to the base of a steep cliff to the west. The walls of the cliff are densely covered in vines and roots. The road is lined with stones, well-worn in its centre due to travel. To the north, a dense thistle patch grows.
120519: The Greenway continues its journey here between Bree and Tharbad. It narrows as it passes between a steep, vine-covered cliff to the west, and a dense patch of brush to the east. The road is lined with stones, and immediately bordered by green grass.
120520: The road here is wide and open. There is a huge, imposing vine wall that blocks passage to the west. It rises about twenty feet into the air and is covered in long, sharp thorns. To the east, vast expansive fields stretch out and disappear into the horizon.
120521: The road is majestic, wide, and well-trodden. It is bordered on either side by verdant fields and rolling grasslands. The road itself is made of smooth, well-worn stone, and it is a favoured route for travellers, merchants, and soldiers alike.
120522: The Greenway is surrounded on either side by picturesque hills and fields of Middle-earth. It is wide and well-travelled. The road itself is composed of smooth, well-worn stones. It stretches north and south, and is the primary route for travel and commerce between Bree and Tharbad.
120523: The Greenway bends south and east here. It is wide and well-travelled, with a well-worn track cut in the centre of the road. It is bordered on either side by fields of waving grass and breathtaking views of the rolling hills and dense forests that make up the heart of Middle-earth.
120524: Spanning north and south, the Greenway is wide and majestic. It is a handsome road, lined on the bottom with heavy stones. The road makes travel through the countryside very easy, and is capable of handling a lot of traffic. It leads northward to the town of Bree, and southward to the shady town of Tharbad.
120525: The Greenway stretches north and south, flanked on its sides by lush, green grasslands with beautiful vistas. The road is made of heavy stones, and is well-worn in its centre, evidence of heavy travel. The road is the main thoroughfare between Tharbad and Bree, and is used by travellers of all types.
120526: A hardened ranger is walking around, looking for tracks.

The winding Greenway cuts through the rolling grasslands, dotted with patches of wildflowers and tall, waving grasses. Aside from deep wagon tracks, the road is covered in lush grass. A few stunted trees and occasional bushes line the side of the road.
120527: The Greenway is surrounded by rolling fields of tall grass to the east and west, with occasional clumps of bushes and small trees here and there. Aside from some old wagon tracks pressed into the hard earth, the road doesn't seem to be used very often.
120528: Cutting through the rolling grasslands to the east and west, the Greenway snakes its way across the green plains. Smaller bushes line the sides of the road, leading into what seems to be a lush forest to the southwest and thicker brush to the southeast.
120529: A brown fox is here, looking for some rabbits to chew up.

Between the grass-covered Greenway to the east and a small dip to the west, the vast grassland dominates the area around here. In the distance to the south, the tall grass meets a small forest hugging the side of the road.
120530: The Greenway makes its way closer to a forest of beech and birch to the west. To the east, the northern grasslands gradually turn into brush-covered plains that stretch out far to the southeast. A fallen, moss-covered signpost lies on the side of the road.
120531: A magpie is flying around looking for some food.

Thick brush to the east on one side, a sparse forest of beech and birch on the other side to the west, the Greenway cuts a path through the vegetation. Far to the north, rolling grasslands can be seen surrounding the road. A shallow, damp ditch lines the western side of the road.
120532: A magpie is flying around looking for some food.

The grass-covered Greenway skirts around the forested hill to the west, away from the thick brush to the east. A fallen tree trunk lies halfway on the road almost obstructing passage. A tall, jagged boulder stands on the opposite side of the road, its weather-worn surface covered in lichen.
120533: The Greenway skirts around a forested hill to the northwest that overlooks this section of the road and funnels the northern grasslands into a narrow pass leading towards the southern lands. A high ledge rises up to the south and separates the pass from the vast brushland to the southeast.
120534: To the north, a forested hill sits high above a narrow pass, with the Greenway coming in from the east and leading down towards the southern plains with high, grass-covered ledges on both sides. The ridge to the southeast rises up from the southeastern brushland like some sort of warning sign.
120535: A magpie is flying around looking for some food.

Below the ledges to either side, the Greenway winds through a narrow pass between a forested hill above to the north and the southern grasslands. Bushes and tufts of grass jut out from the walls of the pass, with a few boulders on the side of the road, no doubt fallen from above.
120536: The Greenway leads from the greener plains to the south into a small, upward- sloping pass that leads towards a forested hill far to the north. To the northeast, a sharp ledge rises out in front of the endless brushland to the southeast.
120537: Running between the tall grasses to the east and a thick brush to the west, the Greenway makes its way from the small pass to the north into an eastward turn to the southeast. Aside from some shallow wagon tracks, the road's surface is completely covered in thick grass.
120538: The grass-covered Greenway runs past a thick brush to the west and turns slightly east, farther away from the dark, foreboding thicket. To the north, the road runs into a narrow upward-sloping pass towards a forested hillside. A thick wall of tangled bushes lines the side of the road to the south.
120539: The grass-covered dirt road runs past a thick, dark brush to the southwest, turning north towards a narrow pass sloping upwards. Rolling grasslands stretch out to the northeast, leading towards more brushlands in the distance.
120540: A large, dusty road continues straight from the north to the south. Trees grow densely to the west, perhaps a remnant of the ancient forest that used to cover this land, but to the east it is predominantly dry grass with the occasional bush.
120541: The road is packed hard from the passing horses, leaving an easy way to travel. Trees grow on either side, but to the east of the road they rapidly thin out, giving way to a plain. The road itself cuts a bold north-to-south route across the countryside.
120542: The road is old and well-travelled, judging from the soil. Travelling on it is quick and easy, but also a good place to be ambushed, with bushes closing in on either side. The east side seems safe though, the bushes there being sparse enough to see the plain beyond.
120543: Passage on this flat and hard road is easy, but the shrubs grow bushier and denser on either side in the Tharbad direction. The road continues north and east, skirting bramble bushes to the south. It might have been curved in this direction by the builders due to a geographical feature. Whatever reason that is can't be seen through the bushes.
120544: Turning from the west to the south, the roadway continues its long journey between Bree and Tharbad. Though packed down to be as hard as rock, the dirt which comprises the surface of the road nevertheless bears the marks of the heavy use it has borne over the years since it was built. To the north, grassy plains extend as far as the eye can see, while to the east there are numerous bushes and shrubs.
120545:
The corpse of a thin highwayman is lying here.
The corpse of a thin highwayman is lying here.
There are two arrows here.
The corpse of Thena Shadowstalker is lying here.
The corpse of a thin highwayman is lying here.
The corpse of a thin highwayman is lying here.
The corpse of a thin highwayman is lying here.
The corpse of Morthan Blacksoul is lying here.
A domesticated pony, beast of burden to many, stands here.

The wide road passes into a dense part of the scrubland here, with tall trees, bushes and shrubs closing off the west side, and dense high bramble bushes closing off the east side. Some stout timbers lie on the ground to the north and south.
120546:
The corpse of a fat highwayman is lying here.
The corpse of a fat highwayman is lying here.
The corpse of a fat highwayman is lying here.
A huge, smoking campfire is burning here.
A domesticated pony, beast of burden to many, stands here.
A sturdy pack horse is standing here.
A sturdy pack horse is standing here.

In a small clearing in the scrub, crude shelters have been made to provide protection from the elements. Many bedrolls and a fireplace seem to indicate that this is more or less a permanent camp. A hole just outside the camp, obviously a latrine, lends more weight to this theory.
120547: The road narrows here as it passes through dense bushes. A large collection of bushes and small trees can be seen just east of the road and a bramble hedge has formed to the west making travel that way impossible. The road continues to the north and south. To the north, a pile of stout timbers can be seen on the ground.
120578: This wide road travels inexorably onward, from north to south, through the flat countryside. The ground is hard and marked by the evidence of the passage of innumerable wagons over the years. To the west, a faint trail can be seen, crossing a rough field. Another barren field lies to the east.
120579: Straight as an arrow, the roadway continues its long journey north-south between Bree and Tharbad. The ground underfoot is hard and gouged with the deep ruts caused by the passage of many heavily-laden wagons over the years. Vast dry plains extend on either side of the road.
120580: Ever onward, the wide road continues its north-south march between Bree and Tharbad. Here it crosses a vast area of open plains, characterised by a covering of insipid grasses. Though packed down to be almost as hard as rock, the dirt which comprises the surface of the road nevertheless bears the marks of the heavy use it has borne over the years since it was built.
120581: The Greenway stretches onward into the distance, both north and south, as it makes its way through an area of open plains. On either side of the road, a flat expanse of grassy, and otherwise quite featureless land is all that can be seen.
120582: A trail weaves through the field primarily east to west. The trail forks to the south towards a farm in the distance. To the north, is a steep cliff face that could be climbed with some effort. The dusty curve of the Greenway is visible nearby to the west.
120583: The trail snakes west to east around low hills and knolls. A cliff to the north prevents access. The hills continue far to the south and east as part of the South Downs. There aren't any trees nearby but the small, occasional bushes and patches of grass appear healthy and thriving.
120584: Low hills are spread out with wide tracks of level ground roaming between them. Dark soil is occasionally interrupted by sparse bushes and a few isolated trees. A wagon track can be made out angling on the flattest earth towards a gate in the east.
120585:
There are two bales of hay here.
A circular stone well has been built here.
A pig is here, covered in mud.
A cow stands here, chewing her cud.

Grass of varying length spreads over the area. Some areas are very short, having been nibbled down nearly to the dirt by the roving animals. Other sections are frequented less and allowed the vegetation to grow higher. Many hoof prints are stamped into the ground. A wagon track leads east to a barn.
120586: Yellow flowers, with grey-green foliage, grow in clusters here.

Wild flowers of blues, reds, and whites dot the grassland. Perhaps the cliff in the west provides the perfect amount of daily shade to spur the unusually large number of blooms. Grass fills in every space where the flowers are not growing. A valley curves between hills to the north and the field opens up substantially in the east and south.
120587: The fertile field bends west to south as it bumps against the South Downs to the north and east. While the valley continues to curve towards the northwest, a larger field opens up to the south. An unusually high hill for the South Downs is visible far off to the south, rising above the other mounds.
120588: Soft grass covers the ground from the bottom of cliffs to the southwest to the cliffs farther away to the northeast. Animals traversing the space between the hills of the South Downs have created a dirt path through the vegetation. The path remains in the middle of the field as it angles along the hillside.
120589: Knee-high grass flows from the west into this area and farther south. This meadow is sandwiched between parallel strands of the South Downs. Rocky outcroppings high above cut into the hills to the north and east. Some small boulders have fallen out of the cliff and sit in the grass.
120590: The area looks as if nothing has ever stepped foot on this large field of perfect green grass. Perhaps animal and other traffic prefers the trail winding to the north and east. The soft grass may spring back to erase any footprints, making it look like nothing has ever stepped foot on this large field of perfect green grass.
120591: It is clear this is the eastern edge of a section of the South Downs as numerous hills curve to the south and west. A large field expands to the north east before another range of hills takes shape. Some large boulders taller than a man collect in the east edge of the area.
120592:
The mauled corpse of a black bear.
A black and white skunk is scuttling about here, searching for food.

The lush green hills of the South Downs are a little more brown in this area on account of many scattered, small pebbles. The stones are sprinkled around like remnants of large boulders being smashed into tiny pieces. Hills surround the area in all directions.
120593: The hills here are dominated by one that is significantly taller than the others. Steep sides fall from the peak in all directions except a small path to the west. The height creates a spectacular view of the fields to the east and miles of the South Downs to the west.
120594: Rolling hills of grass tall enough to hide a rabbit cover the area. In the dips at the lowest place between hills there are some snaking bushes enjoying the darkest space available in the lush knolls. The vegetation in the shadows seems to be doing well, but it still gets some sunlight over the low hills.
120595: The highest point on the hills allows for a view over the farm to the west. To the north, glimpses of a trail curving around hills can be seen traversing west to east. The hills are covered with lush green grass with a handful of trees spaced far apart.
120596:
A huge grizzly bear is here, roaming the wild.
A grizzly cub is here, snarling loudly.

Fields to the west begin rising slowly here as a soft entry to the rolling hills of the South Downs. Almost treeless grassy knolls extend for miles to the east and south. The ground between the blades of grass is dark and fertile. A large farm can be seen to the north.
120597: Field in Front of the Ruins

This peaceful field has access to the Greenway to the west but is dominated by a view of crumbling and shady buildings to the south. Some square and chiselled stones obviously used in buildings are scattered around the area, becoming more numerous farther south. The South Downs gain height to the east.
120598: The hills of the South Downs come to an abrupt end here at the western boundary. A shadowy set of ruined buildings sit below the edge of the cliff. There is a narrow valley to the east between miles of flowing hills. The grass covering the ground is soft and short.
120599: The beginnings of a road or well-travelled path start here and head to the south. Smooth tree trunks stuck into the dirt side-by-side form a wall on both sides of the path that expand around shadowy buildings farther in the abandoned town. Several parts of the wall are missing and the pieces that remain are marred by strike marks.
120600: A long, deep ditch hugs the Greenway to the north and west. It is too deep to enter and exit safely. Exposed rocks bulge out of the sides of the ditch but are not visible anywhere else in the shaggy fields nearby. A farm is visible to the east, perched on a strand of the South Downs.
120601:
A small barrel made of aged oak and strong iron hoops stands here.
A domesticated pony, beast of burden to many, stands here.
A hen is trying to pick some grains here.
A hen is trying to pick some grains here.
A sturdy pack horse is standing here.
A stocky mountain mule is here, waiting to serve.

This is a very large barn with numerous stalls for animals, hay, and grain storage. One stall holds barrels of wine while others are reserved for livestock. Some equipment stands in the corner for processing grapes before being barrelled. The farm house stands to the east while vineyards and pasture flow to the south and west.
120602:
There are two piles of wheat cereals here.
A young farm-hand is here hard at work.

The sprawling fields of crops are dominated by wheat, with smaller areas of corn, hay, and oats. Fertile ground has contributed to impressive crop heights. A garden has been carved out of the field to serve the farm workers. An ageing, wooden fence encloses the area to the west and south.
120603:
There are three piles of juicy grapes here.
A young farm-hand is here hard at work.

Long rows of grapevines stretch out north to south. The vines are pruned and well-kept. Thick brown stalks snake horizontally above the ground with smaller green vines growing up and over a rope. Billowy green leaves mingle with heavy bunches of grapes. Soft, short grass covers the fertile soil between rows. A fence protects the space to the east and south.
120604:
A large cabinet capable of storing goods is here.
In the cabinet, there are a cup, a hunting knife, and a pan.
A small oaken table has been set here.
On the table, there are two loaves of bread, a bulb of garlic, and a cabbage.
Farmer Heathertoes stands here, daydreaming about his crops.

The inside of the farmhouse is spacious. The front door opens to a crackling fire warming the living room. To the left is a long hallway with several living quarters for farmhands. To the right is a bright kitchen filled with ripe vegetables from the garden and freshly-baked bread.
120605:
A large, venomous-looking green snake is coiled up here.
A large, venomous-looking green snake is coiled up here.

A valley stretches west to east, sandwiched between cliffs of the South Downs. The grass is long and falls lazily onto itself creating a pillowy sea of green. A faint, narrow trail can be made out, snaking through the valley where animals traverse between the hills rising at both ends.
120606: The numerous, grass-covered hills continue here but bump up against a steeply rising hill to the east. The slope is full of vegetation like the lower hills but is impossible to climb. The area to the north and south begins to flatten out while the South Downs continue in the west.
120607: A brown fox is here, looking for some rabbits to chew up.

Scraggly weeds patch the ground between round stones as large as a fist. The ground beneath the stones is flat and does not appear saturated with stones. The stones are strewn about the ground in a haphazard manner, as if they had been tossed there by a giant hand. The hills of the South Downs surround on all sides except the east.
120608: A garden snake slithers harmlessly here.

Knee-high grasses sprout from the fertile soil. Only a few solitary trees take advantage of the nutrient-dense ground, but they have grown tall and are full of leaves. A protected valley is to the east and all other directions continue with smooth hills.
120609: Ample fields of grass mixed with a dense, spongy moss blanket the area and seem to deaden the sounds of nature. The moss appears most dense around some small dark holes in the centre of the valley. Moist air occasionally wafts out of the darkness.
120610: The grassy hills are like frozen ocean waves with troughs and crests connected by long, smooth lines. A few old trees with sturdy, brown trunks root into the dirt. A cliff is not far off to the southwest. A low valley unusually absent of hills stretches to the east.
120611: A large boulder sits precariously at the edge of the cliff.

The cliff here curves slowly in a long arc along the west and south edges. The ground is mostly exposed rock with no clear seams. Grass begins to grow farther away from the edge of the cliff. The Greenway can be seen several miles to the east.
120612: Undulating fields of grass and scrubby bushes cover the area. The cliff following the edge of the South Downs is just to the southwest and a valley extends directly east. Peaceful, green hills continue in all other directions. Some bare rocks are visible closer to the cliff.
120613:
A blooming water-lily floats on the surface of the water.
A shallow pond is here, tinted green with algae.

A stream of water sprouts out of the side of one of the grassy knolls, flowing a short distance before collecting in a small pond. The water flowing down the hill would not cover even the first knuckle of a finger penetrating the surface. The pond is no more than a foot deep and is crystal clear, unadulterated by muddy disturbances.
120614: A rock lizard is here, motionless as it observes you.

Vines and tangly bushes curl up from the edge of the cliff like a man clutching for his life. While the ground below is covered in thick brush, it only covers a short distance from the precipice. The rest of the ground is mostly grass and loose stones.
120615: A small cluster of clover grows here.

Scattered short bushes and tall grasses thin out towards the cliff edge to the south and west. Large and small rocks cover the ground near the dropoff and prevent vegetation from taking hold. It would be perilous to attempt to climb down the cliff.
120616: The flowing hills of the South Downs narrow here between fields to the north and a cliff edge to the south. The hills continue to the east and west. A large expanse of fields stretches out beyond the cliff. Some broad-leafed bushes cluster together in the creases between the knolls.
120617:
A great black and silver wolf is standing here, at the head of the pack.
A grey wolf is here, thin from starvation.
A grey wolf is here, thin from starvation.
A grey wolf is here, snarling aggressively.
A grey wolf is here, snarling aggressively.
A grey wolf is here, salivating profusely.
A grey wolf is here, salivating profusely.
A bear is here, covered with coarse black fur.

This section of the South Downs becomes fairly narrow between a cliff to the southwest and thick brush to the east. Some brush from the east has encroached on ths hill with some thorny vines mingling in the thick grass. The hills continue along the cliff edge to the west and south.
120618: A brown fox is here, looking for some rabbits to chew up.

A grassy field stretches out, mostly flat but dotted with small holes. Travellers should be careful not to twist an ankle in one of these holes, as they are all exposed dirt and have not yet been filled with vegetation. To the north, a tall hill blocks passage, while impenetrable brush blocks the east.
120619:
A large thorny branched shrub is growing here.
On the shrub, there are two piles of blackberries.
A mass of wriggling vines drops on you from the trees.
Massive roots shift uneasily all around you.

The entire area is filled with bushes of varying heights and widths. Some bushes hug the ground with vines curling out like stiff fingers. Other plants are as large as a horse with thorny vines growing in tangled messes. While paths can be made through most of the area, the brush is too dense to the east, north and south.
120620:
A great black and silver wolf is standing here, at the head of the pack.
A grey wolf is here, thin from starvation.
A grey wolf is here, thin from starvation.
A grey wolf is here, snarling aggressively.
A grey wolf is here, snarling aggressively.
A grey wolf is here, salivating profusely.
A grey wolf is here, salivating profusely.

The hills of the South Downs reach a high point before the precipitous drop off of the long cliff. Fields stretch out for many miles below the cliff to the west. From this height, brush can be seen encroaching on the hills as they continue to the southeast.
120621: Soft, rolling hills of the South Downs continue here from the west into the south and east. A large patch of brush encroaches from the north and forms an impenetrable barrier, blocking movement in that direction. The grass here appears healthy from fertile soil and plentiful moisture.
120622: Tall, leafy plants from the north have begun invading the grassy hills in the area. The South Downs extend to the west and south. Some established animal paths coming from the north have beaten down the grass in narrow slits winding through the hills.
120623:
Some thick writhing vines whip all around you.
Massive roots shift uneasily all around you.

The area is lower than the surrounding land. A few tall trees have broken out of the multitude of bushes and vines tangling the ground. Back to the east is the only way out of the area as the other directions are too steep and overgrown with vegetation to traverse.
120624:
A nest is here.
A big, nasty vulture is sitting here, protecting its nest.
A big, nasty vulture is sitting here, protecting its nest.
A cute rabbit is here.

The South Downs hills are smooth and grassy, dominating the landscape. Scattered trees dot the area, but none grow close enough to form a grove. To the west, a deep trench prevents movement. The trench is filled with dirt and a few decaying sticks.
120625: The hills of the South Downs slope down to the south into an area full of wild plants and vegetation. A sharp cliff is to the west and a wide chasm prevents movement to the east. The sharp trough between hills is unusual in the soft, rolling hills of the South Downs. It is too wide to leap across and at least thirty feet deep.
120626: A large brown snake with black patches is coiled here.

The field is overrun by thick flowery brambles, towering overgrown grass, and patches of lichen that cling to every surface. Shrubs of blackberries grow around the thickets. The brambles intertwine with one another, creating a natural barrier that no man could penetrate without great effort.
120627:
Some roots lie here waiting to ensnare weary travellers.
Massive roots shift uneasily all around you.

The thickets seem to form an impenetrable wall, daring any who might venture to pass through their thorny barrier. Even the bravest of souls might find themselves lost within the maze of brush, their progress slowed to a crawl by the tangled web before them. The thorny thickets seem to come alive, writhing and reaching out, trying to grasp at any who passed by. Amidst the tangled maze, a small walkway emerges, crossing over a gushing stream. The pathway is narrow, and made of rough-hewn stones, barely visible among the lush growth.
120628:
A large thorny branched shrub is growing here.
On the shrub, there are three piles of blackberries.

The meadow seems to shy away from the towering slopes that guard the western and southern frontiers. The grass, long and rich, is woven with intricate patterns of wildflowers. Along the periphery, where the meadow surrenders to the valley, a row of willows stands guard. Amidst this natural tapestry, a network of deep animal tracks is etched into the soft black earth. The occasional burrow can be spotted, a small, hidden sanctuary for the valley's smallest inhabitants.
120629: The trail here is meandering and narrow. Dotting the landscape, enormous boulders from the hills lie scattered about, cracked and weather-beaten. The ground is strewn with sharp chips of rock. Amongst the rocks, bright flowers of every hue burst forth. To the east, the trail winds and curls, leading to a large wooden gate carved into steep hills which is the only way forward. To the west, the trail beckons the traveller to the Greenway.
120630:
A sturdy pack horse is standing here.
A half wolf is here, loyally protecting his master.

This barn lies in slumber, the roof is sagging and once-sturdy timbers on the walls are now weathered and worn. The wooden dividers of abandoned stalls are worn and splintered, and the hay that once cushioned the feet of horses is now reduced to dust. Cobwebs hang like delicate shrouds in the rafters above. The barn continues to the north. To the east, lies the front door to the farmhouse. To the west, a strong wooden gate stands.
120631: A weathered wooden trough rests against the shed wall.

The air within this abandoned cattle shed is still and heavy, laden with the scent of dust. The floor of the shed is covered in a layer of dust and the interior of the barn is shrouded in shadow. In the rafters above, the remnants of old lanterns hang, their glass panes cracked and clouded, their flames long extinguished. The door to the north, heavy and creaking, hangs askew from its hinges. The barn continues to the east and south.
120632:
An aged scarecrow is standing here, clinging to a wooden frame.
A sturdy pack horse is standing here.
A sturdy pack horse is standing here.
A sturdy trained horse is standing here.

The earth beneath the crops is rich and dark, teeming with life as worms and insects work tirelessly to enrich the soil. The ground itself, though fertile, is somewhat marshy, springing slightly beneath each step as the water that sustains the land mingles with the earth. To the west, the hills ascend so steeply that no traveller could hope to venture upwards. To the south lies a rustic barn, with its weathered wood and thatched roof.
120633:
There is a huge, pyramidal beehive here.
An angry bee is here, collecting nectar from all the flowers of the garden.
An angry bee is here, collecting nectar from all the flowers of the garden.
A drone bee flies around here, angrily buzzing.
A drone bee flies around here, angrily buzzing.
A three-foot-long queen bee is here, buzzing agitatedly.

The field stretches to the south, with a vast expanse of swaying stalks. Amid this field stands a single, ancient tree, the bark of this venerable sentinel is gnarled and weathered, bearing the scars of many years. The South Downs to the west, north, and east form a natural barrier. Venturing farther south, the ground beneath grows softer, more pliant. The once-firm soil gives way to a marshier terrain, with the earth taking on a darker hue.
120634: A wooden chest stands in the corner.

The walls of this quaint farmhouse are built from the stones gathered from the surrounding hills. In the centre of the room, an old, round table serves as the heart of the home, surrounded by chairs with hand-carved backs depicting the bountiful harvests that have fed the family for generations. A sturdy bed made of oak, adorned with intricately carved floral patterns. A set of rustic cupboards stands against the wall. To the west, a door of heavy oak opens to reveal the barn.
120635:
A long, heavy wooden bench stands centrally in the barn.
A brown donkey watches the surroundings, perhaps looking for a chance to graze.
A tall, agile figure stands attentively.
A lean figure looms, his piercing gaze scanning his surroundings.
A lean figure looms, his piercing gaze scanning his surroundings.
A lean figure looms, his piercing gaze scanning his surroundings.

This ramshackle structure, with its timbers worn, barely manages to hold itself together. The scent of rotten hay mingles with the stench of faeces. In the dim corners, the rotten corpses of cattle lay forgotten, their eyes wide and unseeing. The earth beneath the feet is uneven, trodden by countless hooves that have long since departed. A backdoor to the north with deep cracks reveals a grassy grazing field. The barn continues to the west.
120636: Grassy Grazing Field by a Pond

A sturdy pack horse is standing here.
A sturdy pack horse is standing here.
A sturdy trained horse is standing here.
A great horned owl looks cautiously around it.

This serene landscape, nestled between the steep, impassable hills of the South Downs to the north and east, offers a stark contrast to the decaying barn to the south, its timbers worn and weathered. A pond lies nestled in the heart of the field, its waters calm and still. At the edge of the pond, there is a grove of ancient willow trees, their branches bending low. To the west, a field of crops dances gracefully in the breeze. To the south of this field, is a backdoor into the barn.
120661: A partridge attempts to hide in the undergrowth.

This is a small patch of grass, bordered by the Greenway to the north and east and a small forest to the west and south. The waves of green blades are long, broken up by the occasional wildflower or scrub bush. The grass is so thick in some spots that it is difficult to see what lies beneath.
120662: A great wolf with coal-black eyes stares intently at you, drooling saliva.

This is a dark natural cavern inside the hill. Remains of people who must once have been trapped are lying all around. Dank and unhealthy smells rise from the ground, and rotting roots and vines line the dark, earthen walls. The only way out of here is up through a stone lid that serves as a door.
120663:
A malicious thug is here, threatening you.
A malicious thug is here, threatening you.
A field mouse noses about hungrily, searching for food.
A buck runs swiftly from place to place, looking about warily as it grazes.

Sharp rocks to the north give way to sloping hills gently lowering to the south. A deep gully obscures movement to the east. Small trees find their homes scattered among the long mounds. Thorny brush huddles around each tree making homes for small, snuffling creatures.
120664: A faint cart path travels over a grassy hill, fading away almost entirely to the north while becoming more prominent as it leads downhill towards a cluster of buildings to the south. Standing to the east is a broken windmill, easily accessible through a wide gap in its western wall. Another trail branches off downhill to the west, showing signs of recent use by horse and man.
120665: This windmill was once used to grind grain. A thin layer of grey dust covers the interior and creates a haze in the air. Circular stone wheels lie broken away from the wooden shaft that once drove them. The shaft travels from floor to ceiling in the centre of the room.
120666: Grasses and weeds grown between shallow ruts in the earth, clearly defining a once often used cart path. It travels up a hill to the north, and to the south terminates where it enters the large double doors of a sturdy barn. To the east, a weary shed stands upon a rise. To the west, a wooded hill hinders travel in that direction.
120667: A small black vicious rat squeaks at you for disturbing it.

This old but sturdy barn served many functions. Small pens are built against the western wall, in which chickens and goats once lived. The south wall holds wicker drying racks from the straw covered dirt floor upward through a gap in the plank ceiling. Between the racks a wooden ladder is attached to the wall, leading to a hatch above. To the east, an open wall leads to another part of the barn, while heavy doors in the northern wall lead outside.
120668:
A simple wooden wagon, missing its rear wheels, sits here.
A domesticated pony, beast of burden to many, stands here.

A lean-to is built off of the barn's main structure. It is wide enough to hold two wagons side by side. Heavy metal rings are attached to the sides of the open wall to the west, places to tie a horse as it waits to be hitched up. Dry pony droppings are mixed into the dirt floor, giving the air a dusty, herbal scent.
120669: A thin but well-worn trail traverses a narrow valley between the steep wooded hills. The trail shows signs of being recently travelled by shod horses. To the west is a large stable at the base of a hill. To the east, a windmill stands upon a grassy rise, its blades looking skeletal and unmoving.
120670: A water barrel has been left here.

A footpath passes through a neglected field, a fork of the path leading to a large canvas tent to the south. The tent stands tall and sturdy, its stuctural poles lashed tightly to nearby trees. A wooded hill east of you hinders travel in that direction, but to the west and north the footpath continues its journey through this valley between the hills.
120671: The upper part of the windwill is more intact than the lower. Shafts and gears come together to drive power from the wind to the grinding stones below. They have not turned in quite some time. Amongst the mechanisms are at least a dozen nests. A dirt-encrusted window with a broken pane creates a portal for birds to come and go as they please. Many of their treasures (acorns, twigs and the like) are strewn about the floor.
120672: A barn-owl is here, looking for easy prey.

Wicker drying racks adorn the walls of the loft, many of them still carrying aged sheaves of wheat. Towards the centre of the floor, planking can be moved aside to open a hole through which to drop sheaves of grain stalks into a wagon below. A hatch in the floor near the south wall provides a safe way to climb down.
120673: A sturdy crate made of nailed wooden planks sits on the floor.

This shed sits on a grassy rise at the base of a larger hill. Its western wall is completely open, giving the building's occupants a clear view of a cart path travelling through a valley. The walls and ceiling are built from roughly cut boards, many of which are warped and broken. Rusted tools and empty burlap sacks hang from the walls, signs that bags of grain and flour were once stored here.
120674:
A sturdy pack horse is standing here.
A beautiful and docile horse is standing here.

A wide alley travels between four horse stalls made from roughly cut lumber. Simply crafted gates are latched closed. Halters and bridles hang on hooks outside of each stall, appearing to be clean and recently used. A wide double door leads outside to the east, while the stable itself extends further west.
120675:
A wooden saddle rack is built into the wall.
On the rack, there are a leather saddle and a saddlecloth.
A mean looking robber is here, demanding money from you.

Wide wicker shelves have been built into the north and south walls of this room, upon which are stacked loosely bound bundles of hay and bags of grain. The dirt floor is swept clean of any debris. A wide doorway to the east gives the owner of this stable easy access to feed any horses in the stalls. A small and sturdy wooden door is set into the west wall.
120676:
A hammer lies on the ground.
A malicious thug is here, threatening you.
A malicious thug is here, threatening you.
