This workshop is filled with horseshoeing equipment such as hammers, nails, and a small anvil, as well as other tools for use in planting and harvesting grasses and grains. The dirt floor is slightly damp, and the air has a musty odour. A dirty window in the west wall looks out to a steep hillside. A door is set into the east wall, while to the south a path through the clutter leads to a separate part of the room.
120677: The ceiling is lower here than to the north. Burlap sacks cover windows and hang from the ceiling, placed as if to keep this room as dark as possible. A short chain has been staked into the centre of the earthen floor, with leather bindings tied to several of its rings.
120678: A thin trail travels over a rise in the grassy earth, granting a view of the surrounding area. East of here can be seen a long canvas structure nestled amongst hills and trees. To the west, the trail looks to curve through fields towards a wooden structure southwest of here. Standing directly to the south is a wooden hovel, leaning from age and misuse. Atop it has been built a crude tower of lashed timbers. To the north there is a stable, but there is no entrance to it from this direction.
120679: A thin path turns through long abandoned fields, travelling east and south. Scattered around not far from the path are occasional patches of disturbed earth that could easily be unmarked graves, some more fresh than others. Hills tower above to the north and west, providing no passage in those directions.
120680:
A circular stone well has been built here.
A furtive footpad is here waiting for his prey.

Nestled at the end of this valley with hills rising above it to the west, south and east is a farmhouse built of logs cut from local trees, standing upon a foundation of mortar and stone. The only entrance appears to be through an open porch to the west. A stone well sits roughly a hundred feet from the house.
120681: A narrow porch with a wooden floor offers a sheltered entrance to this house. The porch is bare, and every sound seems to echo off of its walls. The floorboards creak under any movement across them, as if complaining constantly about unwanted visitors. A simple door in the south wall offers entry to the house proper.
120682:
A sturdy bed made from solid oak lies here, covered in warm blankets.
A small oaken table has been set here.
An experienced husky smuggler is here, plotting his illicit ventures.
A wiry smuggler is here, attempting to avoid being seen.
An experienced husky smuggler is here, plotting his illicit ventures.
A wiry smuggler is here, attempting to avoid being seen.
The chief of smugglers is here, planning his next move.

This simple farmhouse looks like it was once inhabited by a small family working the surrounding land, but it has in recent times been ransacked. Furniture and belongings have been shoved aside except for a wooden table dominating the main room. One corner of the room is a sleeping area. It looks to be in order and frequently used by the house's current occupants.
120683:
A wooden chest stands in the corner.
A large dog curls his lips back and snarls.
A large dog curls his lips back and snarls.
A large dog curls his lips back and snarls.

A simple cellar has been dug out beneath the farmhouse, its once earthen walls reinforced by mortar and stone. Simple shelves adorn its walls, some of them covered with aged carrots, turnips, acorns, and the like. The air holds a faint odour of rot. The dirt floor is riddled with claw marks.
120684:
There are four roughly cut tree trunk stools here.
A small and well-kept fire lights and warms the room.
A sturdy bandit bodyguard stands here, eager to hack you to pieces.

This canvas structure looks to be made of multiple peaked tents sewn together to create a long hall of sorts. The peak of this section is open to allow smoke from a fire pit in the centre of the room to escape. The northern wall of the tent opens to the hills outside, while the southern wall opens to another room deeper in the structure.
120685:
A large, sturdy table made from oak is sitting here.
A swarthy, little bandit advances forward.
A sturdy bandit bodyguard stands here, eager to hack you to pieces.
A swarthy, little bandit advances forward.

This peaked canvas tent creates a large room that is part of a longer structure. In the middle, looking quite out of place, is an oaken table and eight chairs, filled with dinnerware as well as an array of papers containing maps and lists. The northern wall is open, leading towards the front of the long canvas hall. A tent flap in the southern wall separates the rest of the structure.
120686:
There are six filthy straw pallets here.
A thief is sleeping here on a filthy straw pallet.

Cots made of wooden poles and canvas and covered by blankets are arranged tidily throughout this tent. This room easily provides space for a dozen men to sleep. A tent flap in a northern wall leads towards the front of the long canvas structure.
120687: Even when it was new, this simple log home was not much to behold. Since then, soft earth has slipped away beneath its western wall, causing it to lean noticeably. Its once sloped roof has been mostly ripped away, replaced with a crude tower of timbers lashed together with rope. As most of the chinking has worn away from the cabin walls, there are ample footholds to reach the tower above.
120688: Someone has turned the abandoned cabin below into a watchtower by replacing its roof with a wooden rampart roughly built from lashed timbers. It is covered by a simple roof made of poles and animal hides. From here its occupants can watch a cart path that enters this farmstead near a windmill at least half of a mile to the northeast.
120689:
A beautiful and docile horse is standing here.
A snake slithers towards you.

A large gully dominates the area. A cascade of bushes descend from the west over a sharp edge that is impossible to climb. Some hardy roots live in the shallow mud at the lowest part of the land. Sparse shrubs and patches of grass appear on several paths out of the gully to the east and south.
120690: A beautiful and docile horse is standing here.

From the gully to the north the land slopes up towards the south before meeting a set of large boulders. The large stones corral inhabitants away from the south and west. Smaller boulders spaced erratically make movement tedious and block longer views.
120691:
A cluster of dark green, feathery fronds flourishes in the shade.
A bear is here, covered with coarse black fur.

The ground undulates on a large scale like an ocean wave frozen in time. The dirt is unusually dark. Patches of stiff grass and weeds grow in small mounds on the black hills. To the east, a chasm reaches down to darkness. Its jagged edges snake around to the north and south allowing movement only to the west.
120692: A rolling, verdant landscape of steep hills stretches out in all directions. The ground is dotted with rocks and boulders, some as tall as trees, and the air is thick with the buzz of insects and the chirping of birds. Soft grasses cover the ground, providing an easy surface to travel over.
120693:
A huge black fungus is here, exuding a foul stench.
A huge black fungus is here, exuding a foul stench.

The floor of this small valley is dotted with blackened trees and singed undergrowth. A jagged scar runs down the hillside north and west of here, marking the path of a great forest fire. The scent of charred wood and vegetation hangs faintly in the air.
120694:
A single oak tree stands dead and broken, a long crack running down its centre.
A bee flies around here, collecting nectar from the flowers.
A bee flies around here, collecting nectar from the flowers.
A bee flies around here, collecting nectar from the flowers.

A tall, lonely hill, separated from the region of hills to the south, stands sentinel over the bleak plains. Branches and twigs litter the ground. Open plains surrounded by hills in the distance can be seen in all directions save south.
120695: A high plain stretches between the surrounding hills and peaks. Scrub and brush are all that grow here. The ground is rocky, dry and cracked, seeming to retain very little moisture. The terrain is much too harsh to travel any direction but east.
120696: A tall stag is here, grazing peacefully.

Tree covered hills rise and fall around this region. The forest is old and mature, with rough, wide trunks that stretch more than eighty feet in the air. The forest floor is covered with tracks of deer, foxes, and rabbits, and the branches above are filled with nests.
120697: A tree covered ridge travels along the top of a series of hills. Its slopes are too steep to traverse down to the north and south, leaving east and west the only directions of passage. A gentle decline to the west leads deeper into the forest.
120698:
A dense carpet of blue flowers dip their heads in the breeze.
A huge, black wolf is here, ready to devour.
A black wolf pads restlessly, looking for its next prey.
A black and white skunk is scuttling about here, searching for food.

A steep, rocky slope angles sharply out of the forest west and south of here, casting this area in shadows every day starting at mid afternoon. A more gentle slope rises in the opposite direction. Wildlife thrives here, both flora and fauna. There is no clear trail through the woods, but the forest floor is clear enough to offer meandering passage to the north and east.
120699: Small rock cairns occasionally mark the remains of a stone path travelling up and down through the hills. To the west, it descends a gentle slope to the valley floor below. The the south, it travels on a narrow knife edge atop a hill towards a wide, flat plateau. A cool, shaded trough can be traversed downward along the eastern slope.
120700: A swarm of hornets is coming out of its nest.

The terrain is difficult with large stones wrapped with prickly bushes and stiff vines. Any path is forced to wind around the green-wrapped boulders. The land slopes up at a tall angle towards the north leaving the only safe option for movement back to the south.
120701: Thick, thorny brush covers the floor of this deciduous forest, making it challenging to explore very far. High in the branches can be seen dozens of papery hornet nests. A soft, continual buzzing in the air makes it clear they are inhabited. To the east, the trees mostly fade away, but the brush continues.
120702: The eastern section of this area is covered with a multitude of tangled weeds and vines. The different plants appear to have grown together over time into an impenetrable wall of sinewy shrubs. The rest of the area is filled with tough roots curling in and out of the soil and leafy weeds.
120703: Snaking green vines flourish here with some stems as thick as small trees. The plants coil and twist among each other, preventing movement to the north and west. Some of the vines towards the east appear to have dried and become brittle.
120704:
Some thick writhing vines whip all around you.
A mass of vines reaches out from the surrounding brush.
A mass of vines reaches out from the surrounding brush.

Plants and bushes are impressively thick here. It is impossible to move without leaves and spindly branches impeding progress over the land. There are only a few small routes visible to traverse east and west. The ground slopes down dramatically to the east and it may be too challenging to return from that direction.
120705: A mixture of soft mosses and grasses cover the ground except for sporadic hoof and paw prints that sank through to dirt. The spongy ground is kept wet by the dense vegetation. Bushes as tall as a horse curl around each other in a wild tangle. The brush becomes impenetrable to the north.
120706: Thick brush carpets the area. Small, thorny vines growing low on the ground share space with willowy ferns. Limbs from woody bushes snarl into nearly impenetrable masses. The north and west become impassable due to the growth of thick vegetation.
120707: Many trees grow in this area, but their growth has been stunted, and none stand more than four feet tall. Their trunks are never more than a couple inches wide, and their thin branches droop to the ground. East of here, the trees stand taller and form a proper forest. To the south and west, rocky hills rise up.
120708: A badger is here, exploring for food.

Tall, steep hills rise and fall in this area. The tops of many are bald and lumpy, with great mounds of rock rising above the earth and grass. A narrow ridge can be traversed to the south, leading deeper and higher into the hills. A rocky slope to the east heads down towards a forest.
120709:
A short evergreen plant, with slightly bluish needles, grows here.
A bear is here, covered with coarse black fur.
A great black and silver wolf is standing here, at the head of the pack.

Large, grey rocks rise all around here, at the peak of a long hill. Narrow gaps between the boulders offer passage towards the north and east. Wind occasionally whistles between the rocks, but otherwise little can be heard.
120710: A grey bird with a bright orange-red belly sits here, singing a melodic tune.

Boulders and shards of rock have broken away from surrounding hills to create an uneven, rocky slope leading to the south. In that direction can be seen the flat summit of a tall hill. Steep slopes drop off to the north and east, offering a view of a forest hundreds of feet below.
120711: A flat plateau stretches out here, upon one of the tallest hills in the region. A steep slope drops off dramatically to the south, offering a commanding view of the lands below. They are mostly open plains, but far to the southwest can be seen a tall, stone structure built into a hillside. To the west, the plateau continues, while a rocky talus to the north offers passage down.
120712:
A nest is here.
A big, nasty vulture is sitting here, protecting its nest.

Mounds of rock rise steeply to the west and north, and a slope drops dramatically to the south, leaving only a narrow passage on which to stand. The rocky crags are filled with birds nests, some of them quite large, as if woven from tree branches instead of twigs. Over the cliff to the south can be seen open plains below, as well as a tall, stone structure built into a hillside far to the southwest. The plateau widens to the east.
120713:
A blooming water-lily floats on the surface of the water.
A clear spring gurgles and feeds small streams of water into a nearby pond.
A crayfish is here, snapping its claws at you.
A black catfish is here, lurking in the mud.

A glade opens up in the forest, surrounding a large pond of fresh, clear water. Cattails grow along its banks. Game trails lead in and out of the forest, creating several paths into the water. To the north and west the forest opens up to brushy plains, while to the south the trees grow taller.
120714: A steep escarpment west of here, along with tall, full trees, keeps the forest cool and shaded during most of the day. At night, the canopy hides the stars above. Animals seem to flourish here, both on the ground and in the trees. On the occasion when there is a breeze from the east, it brings with it a dank, musty odour.
120715:
A large toadstool grows nearby.
A tall stag is here, grazing peacefully.
A roe deer is standing here, watching the terrain while chewing the vegetation.

Deep in this forest, trees lean inward and the ground suddenly slopes downward in a conical fashion. At the bottom of this depression is a gaping sinkhole, about eight feet in diameter, that drops deep into the earth. Large, grey mushrooms with rounded caps grow around its perimeter. A musty odour fills the air, coming from within.
120716:
A white centipede is here.
A white centipede is here.

A deep hole in the ground rises above and below. Its walls are damp, hard packed earth. Large, shelf-life fungi grow from the walls, providing unusual foot and hand holds for anyone wishing to traverse this passage. The air is still and musty, smelling more dank below, but fresher above.
120717:
A giant, strange looking green fungus is here, ready to devour you in seconds.
A giant, strange looking green fungus is here, ready to devour you in seconds.
A giant, strange looking green fungus is here, ready to devour you in seconds.

The bottom of this deep sinkhole is littered with rotting leaves and branches, making the floor soft and uneven. Large, shelf-like fungi grow from the walls, while thin, white fungi with rounded caps grow from the floor like tall grasses. The air is damp and still, with an overbearing musty odour.
120718: Some small rocks have been piled into a mound here.

A valley winds its way west and south between some hills. In this area are several stone foundations, gravel paths, and a collapsed well. This was once a small village, but it has been abandoned for decades. To the east, a partially overgrown stone path climbs a hill.
120719: A large elk is standing here, chewing grass and leaves.

This valley winds its way east and west through grassy hills that rise up around here. A gentle incline offers easy passage up a lightly wooded hill to the south. The hills to the north are tall and densely wooded, giving wildlife ample refuge from the openness of the valley.
120720:
A black raven flies in the sky searching for flesh to prey upon.
A boar cub is playing here, and exploring the wide world.

Hills rise up east and west of here, terminating at plateus. Their banks are too eroded to climb. Occasionally, the remains of an old, rocky path or trail can be seen peeking through the grass, following the valley north and south.
120721:
A large elk is standing here, chewing grass and leaves.
A black raven flies in the sky searching for flesh to prey upon.

A valley bends through the surrounding hills, travelling north and east from here. There was a gravel road or trail here once, but now only pieces of it can be seen amongst the grass. Most of it washed away or disappeared into the earth decades ago.
120722:
A sly cat prepares to pounce from its grassy hiding place.
A black raven flies in the sky searching for flesh to prey upon.

A steep, grassy hill rises sharply out of the earth directly north of here. It is strewn with rocks and shrubs that look like they would provide ample handholds and footholds for someone wanting to venture upwards. Elsewise, the valley floor can be followed east or west.
120723: Tall hills rise up around this area. To the west, open plains travel between the hills, creating a valley that goes on for miles. Pieces of an overgrown path can be seen leading into the valley, but it looks to have been out of use for ages. South of here can be seen a field of tall grasses.
120724:
A large, venomous-looking green snake is coiled up here.
A large, venomous-looking green snake is coiled up here.
A sturdy pack horse is standing here.
A small grasshopper clings to a blade of grass, ready to spring.
A gaunt Barrow-wight is here, its glowing eyes gazing around intently.

Tall, dense grasses rise in all directions. Their tassels stretch ten feet or more into the air. The air is filled with the humming of insects. A faint trail makes its way northward, hard packed gravel that has barely kept from being overrun by vegetation over the decades.
120725: A wild sheep with a short, greyish coat grazes here.

Grassy hills of varying height roll up and down in every direction. Some cannot be climbed because they are too steep, or their soil is too loose, or there is not a path that is not too rocky. Those that can be climbed too often offer nothing more than a view of more hills.
120726: A powerful ram stands here, poised and alert.

This area is filled with several grassy hills. To the east and south, two hills rise imposingly, their steep slopes covered by jagged red rocks that seem to protrude in a threatening manner. It is as if the hills are great beasts with spikes growing from their skin, but they remain as unmoving as the land around them.
120727: Ruined Manor on a Flat Plateau

A small boar with big yellow tusks looks eager to fight.
A fierce boar is here, making grunting noises.
A boar cub is playing here, and exploring the wide world.
A boar cub is playing here, and exploring the wide world.
A small boar with big yellow tusks looks eager to fight.
A fierce boar is here, making grunting noises.
A boar cub is playing here, and exploring the wide world.
A boar cub is playing here, and exploring the wide world.

This is a wide, flat plateau high above the surrounding lands. It was once dominated by a sizeable manor, but it has largely collapsed, with only two walls remaining. A central room of the manor is exposed to the sky, within which a tall chair carved of stone but made to look like wood stands untouched by time.
120734:
A boar cub is playing here, and exploring the wide world.
A large elk is standing here, chewing grass and leaves.

A valley winds its way between hills that rise to the north and south of here. When not frozen, the moss-covered ground is soft and spongy from moisture that rolls down into the plains from the surrounding hills. Clusters of tall ferns rise from the earth in a few places.
120735:
A reddish-brown shrub with purplish-pink flowers grows here.
Inside the shrub, there are three clusters of purplish-pink flowers.

The open plains here are dotted with unusual shrubs, their twisting branches and vibrant leaves catching the eye. They have a distinctive shape, their branches spiralling upwards like the flames of a fire. The air here is fresh and crisp, smelling of pine and earth.
120736: The open plains here are dotted with clusters of trees and shrubs, providing pockets of shade in an otherwise sun-soaked landscape. To the north, towering hills rise abruptly from the earth, their rocky peaks scraping the sky. The plains are criss-crossed by a network of game trails, and occasionally the distant calls of predators and prey can be heard echoing across the landscape.
120737:
A large elk is standing here, chewing grass and leaves.
An elk cow gazes coldly at you, chewing on a small branch.

Open plains stretch out as far as the eye can see. They are filled with with tall blades of golden grass waving in the gentle breeze, dotted with jagged rocks and a patchwork of evergreen trees and shrubs. When wind whispers across the prairie, it carries the scent of pine and earth with it.
120738: In Front of an Ancient Temple

A small boar with big yellow tusks looks eager to fight.
A fierce boar is here, making grunting noises.
A boar cub is playing here, and exploring the wide world.

An ancient stone temple, the size of a small keep, stands directly west of here. A gaping hole with no doors offers easy entry. A rusted, iron fence connects to the temple and travels east. High above to the left of the entrance can be see a tower with glassless windows overlooking the fenced area.
120739:
Yellow flowers, with grey-green foliage, grow in clusters here.
A sturdy pack horse is standing here.

During the spring, the open plains here are dotted with wildflowers, creating a sea of colour as far as the eye can see. The hills to the east rise gently and roll gracefully towards the horizon. The sounds of birds and other wildlife fill the air.
120740:
An elk cow gazes coldly at you, chewing on a small branch.
A boar cub is playing here, and exploring the wide world.

A ten foot tall iron gate supported by stone pillars stands south of here. A rusting iron fence stretches out from it and travels far to the west and east. West of here, a stone structure the size of a small keep rises up from the surrounding prairie.
120741: Remains of a Tower on a Knoll
A black raven flies in the sky searching for flesh to prey upon.

This hill rises above the surrounding prairie, with eroded slopes impeding travel everywhere except to the north. At the very top of the hill are the remains of a simple stone tower. It has collapsed and only its bottom third still stands. In the distance, several miles to the west, can be seen a large stone structure. To the east can be seen a plateau on the other side of a valley, rocky ruins of some sort evident on its top.
120742:
A sly cat prepares to pounce from its grassy hiding place.
An elk cow gazes coldly at you, chewing on a small branch.

A rusting iron fence, at least eight feet tall and supported by stone pillars, stands south of here. It travels west as far as can be seen. To the east it turns south and out of view. Open plains stretch out around here, offering light and easy travel.
120743:
A small plant grows here, with long, pointed leaves and flowers at its top.
A large elk is standing here, chewing grass and leaves.
An elk cow gazes coldly at you, chewing on a small branch.

A dozen or so pine trees are clustered here, in the middle of an otherwise empty plain. The grass near the trees is matted down in several places where deer or elk have slept. Rocky hills rise all around this area, making travel difficult in any direction except the west.
120744: A valley filled with lush grass is nestled within rough, rocky hills. Boulders and a few small trees dot the landscape. During the spring and summer, this area is filled with blooming wildflowers. Near one of the hills is the burnt husk of what was once a small hunting cabin. Nothing but charred wood remains.
120745:
A large bat is here, hanging in the darkness.
A mouse sniffs around, searching for a morsel of food.

This ancient temple was built into the hillside eons ago. The floor, walls and ceiling are all crafted of rough-cut stone bricks. The structure looks strong in spite of its age. Chains hang from wooden rafters across the tall ceiling, from which hang two lit lanterns. A thick layer of dust covers the floor, though it has been disturbed as footprints can be seen leading to and from deeper into the temple to the south.
120746: A huge bat is here, emitting piercing squeaks.

This long, dusty hall built of rough-cut stone runs north and south. The stone walls are bare save for empty torch sconces covered by spider webs. Every sound echoes throughout the passage. The air is stale and musty, though it smells more fresh towards the north.
120747:
A large, sturdy table made from oak is sitting here.
On the table, there are a quill pen and a piece of paper.
There are two long, dusty benches made of wood here.

Six stone pillars rise up to meet heavy wooden rafters supporting a twenty foot high ceiling. Bare walls allow every sound to echo throughout the spacious room. The remains of broken wooden chairs are scattered across the floor. The end of one table has been cleared of dust and debris, and looks to have been recently used. A short staircase leads up to a dais south of here.
120748: This room is the base of a tower, about eight feet square and thirty feet high. A doorway leads to a larger room that is adjacent to the west. A sturdy staircase built of stone brackets and oak treads is built into the walls, spiralling upward.
120749: An old bell hangs from a decaying rope here.

The top of this tower is a room about eight foot square. The walls and ceiling are stone. A wooden platform offers a place to stand in most of the room, aside from the southern wall where a staircase begins its descent. Large, open windows in the east and west walls offer expansive views of the surrounding lands, as well as the rising and setting of the sun. A heavy wooden headstock, from which a bell can be hung, is attached near the ceiling.
120750: This room was once dedicated to the care of the deceased. A stone table and a copper tub sit near the centre of the chamber, a tattered ornate rug on the floor between them. Shelves on the walls still hold a few clay jars, but many of these vessels have been broken. Shards of pottery are scattered about.
120751:
An ancient altar carved of dark, grey stone rests in the centre of the room.
On the altar, there is a candlestick.

A dais of three steps rises a few feet above a large common room to the north. Its steps are adorned with a relief sculpture displaying the sun at different times of the day rising and lowering over a field of workers. Tattered tapestries hang on the walls, a thick layer of mould and dust hiding any colour or imagery they once contained.
120752:
A black wolf pads restlessly, looking for its next prey.
A rabid rabbit is here, frothing at the mouth.
A rabid rabbit is here, frothing at the mouth.

A ten foot tall iron gate supported by stone pillars stands north of here, marking the entrance of these burial grounds. In all other directions there are mounds of earth of varying sizes, many adorned by flat, grey stones. West of here, a stone structure the size of a small keep rises up behind the barrows.
120753:
A giant, strange looking green fungus is here, ready to devour you in seconds.
An ancient fungus smothers the boulders.

The walls of an ancient stone temple rise high above the ground, terminating at the top of a tower overlooking these burial grounds. A rusted, iron fence connects to the temple walls and travels east and south. Mounds of earth up to ten feet tall dot the land south and east of here.
120754:
A white-painted bench is here.
A roofless stone gazebo stands in the centre of the cobblestone circle.
A rabid raccoon stands here, frothing at the mouth.

This is the northeast corner of a large burial grounds, marked by a tall stone pillar and a rusting iron fence that travels west and south. A circular section of the ground here, about a hundred feet in diameter, is made of cobblestone. The once ornate surface has been overrun by grasses growing between its stones.
120755:
A grey wolf is here, salivating profusely.
A rabid raccoon stands here, frothing at the mouth.

There is evidence that many people were lain to rest in this area centuries ago. Barrows range in sizes from small enough to cover only a single man, to mounds of earth large enough to cover multiple generations of a family. No evidence exists of recent usage, as the barrows and the ground between are covered in thick, untamed grass and spotted with thorny bushes. No clear path exists, but travel between the barrows is possible in any direction.
120756: Flat, rocky terrain extends far into the distance to the north and east, dotted with the occasional jagged outcropping of stone. To the south is a field of tall briars that would be impossible to navigate. The ground is hard-packed and challenging to traverse, with loose rocks and boulders scattered throughout. The remains of a broken fence can be seen west of here.
120757: A low, many-branched shrub covers the ground here.

A group of boulders, averaging around ten feet in height, stands tall and proud here. The air is dry and crisp. Wind occassionally rushes past the boulders, breaking the stillness with whispers. To the south and east, thick briars block passage, forming an impenetrable barrier.
120758: A dented pail has been carelessly left here.

An old well whose interior has collapsed sits in the middle of four stone foundations. This is the remains of a small settlement that has been abandoned for decades. The remnants of a gravel trail can be seen leading eastward towards a tall, grey rise of stone in the distance.
120759:
A waist-high evergreen shrub grows here, with thick, reaching branches.
On the shrub, there are two piles of grey-green leaves.
A rock lizard is here, motionless as it observes you.

The ground here is a mix of sand and soil, covered with rocks and brush. A few trees dot the landscape in all directions. West of here, a tall fence of iron rises. It is hard to tell what is contained within. The rocky ground stretches out to the east and south.
120760:
Some small rocks have been piled into a mound here.
A large brown snake with black patches is coiled here.
A large brown snake with black patches is coiled here.

A wide channel has been carved into this eighty foot high hump of grey rock that protrudes from the plains. On all sides are nearly sheer walls, save for a few man-made shelves. The remains of simple but tall wooden ladders still lean against the walls in places. Scattered about are bricks of various sizes. Brush and weeds grow from cracks and crevices throughout.
120761: This area is filled with green barrows, grey name-stones, and black briars. The thorny brush becomes taller and thicker as one travels east. To the south, a tall fence of iron and stone pillars stands as if purpose built to keep the dead within their graves. The burial grounds continue to the west and north.
120762: A rabid rabbit is here, frothing at the mouth.

Thorny briars grow thick and tall in this area, save for a single passage around ten feet wide that winds its way through. The bushes thin out as one travels west, but become thicker still to the east. In spite of the wildness of this place, the air is eerily void of the sounds of animals.
120763: A grave-digger is here, preparing to mend his shovel.

A narrow passage west of here leads through dark briars and opens to this small glade. Tall trees from a dense copse of pines to the east look over this area. In the centre of the glade, six name-stones are arranged in a circle, facing outward.
120764: A huge black fungus is here, exuding a foul stench.

Several grassy, green mounds rise from the brushy field blocking travel to the north and west. Scattered about, both on and around the barrows, are name-stones. Most have toppled over and are weathered to illegibility. A break in a rusted iron fence to the south leads to open plains. To the east, the burial grounds continue.
120765:
A rabid rabbit is here, frothing at the mouth.
A colourful butterfly is fluttering around here.

This ridge overlooks a deep, wooded ravine to the south. North is a large brushy field filled with mounds, partially enclosed by a long fence. A large section of the fence has broken away from its stone pillars, offering easy passage. West and east of here a gentle slope leads down to grassy plains.
120766: A diamondback rattlesnake is coiled here, ready to strike.

Long, slender blades of grass lie atop one another in all directions, as the wind has never been able to figure out from which direction it should blow. A deep wooded ravine cuts across the plains to the south, terminating near a dense copse of pines to the east. To the north, just as the land slopes upward, a fence of rusted iron and stone pillars blocks passage.
120767:
A statue of a robed figure is here, its arms outstretched to the east and west.
A gaunt Barrow-wight is here, its glowing eyes gazing around intently.

Amongst the downs is an area of circular cobblestone that has been overrun by grass. It is surrounded by twisted, unkempt bushes that are the remains of what was once a manicured hedge. South of here is a small hill with a gaping entrance facing a statue, a stone stairway leading down and within.
120768:
Some ancient stone tombs, weather-stained and eroded, cover the landscape.
A grey wolf is here, salivating profusely.
A black wolf pads restlessly, looking for its next prey.

Barrows of varying heights dot the landscape north of here. Taller barrows hinder travel to the east. West of here stands the remains of an ancient iron fence. Near the fence, several stone tombs are built, recessed into the earth. Their entrances are blocked and sealed by piles of stone.
120769: A rabid raccoon stands here, frothing at the mouth.

This is the southwest corner of some large burial grounds, marked by a rusting iron fence that travels east and north from a stone pillar. Near the pillar are the remains of a tomb, recessed into the earth. Its roof has collapsed, creating a dark portal leading down.
120770: A gaunt Barrow-wight is here, its glowing eyes gazing around intently.

This tomb is recessed six feet into the ground. A short stairway in the eastern wall leads to a heavy, immovable stone slab. The floor of the tomb is littered by stone debris, as both the ceiling and the western wall have collapsed, leaving gaping holes. Two empty stone coffins adorn the walls, their lids leaning against them.
120771: This tomb is recessed six feet into the ground. A short stairway, partially covered by earth and grass, grants an unhindered exit. The tomb is built of fine stonework, with even the floor being crafted of bricks unmarked by any cracks or gaps. Six stone coffins adorn the walls.
120772: The floor of the passage is littered with stone debris, its source being a gaping hole in the brick wall to the east. The smell of fresh air comes from that direction, in contrast to the musty smell and thick clouds of dust that seem to fill the passages north and west of here.
120773: A mouse sniffs around, searching for a morsel of food.

The air is thick with dust that floats almost unmoving and obscures vision. This passage was cut roughly from the surrounding stone, possibly as a source of bricks for other structures. Set into the north wall is a simple wooden door.
120774: The western wall of this passage shows it was roughly cut from the surrounding stone. In stark contrast, an ornate archway lined with grey brick opens to a room to the east. The air is cold and unmoving, filled with thick dust that makes it hard to see. The main passage continues north and south.
120775: The air here is stale, dank, and unmoving. The walls of this passage are rough cut from the surrounding stone. The floor is littered with bones and debris. Thick dust hangs in the air, making it difficult to see very far. Some sort of chute can be made out in the ceiling leading upward, but there is no way to access it.
120776: A skeleton of some humanoid lies in the dust.

The air is thick with dust that floats almost unmoving and obscures vision. Several skeletons, mostly intact and clothed, litter the floor. This passage was cut roughly from the surrounding stone, possibly as a source of bricks for other structures. There are dark recesses in the walls that light does not easily penetrate, but all appear to be empty.
120777: Arches made of black brick curve ornately up the walls to the ceiling. Built into the walls between the arches are twelve stone sarcophagi, all of them looking untouched and sealed. Dust hangs densely in the air here. Arched doorways lead to the east and west.
120778: A wooden chest stands in the corner.

Brickwork arches support the walls and ceiling of this room. It looks like it was built as a continuation of the crypt to the west, but there are no sarcophagi here. Instead, there are several wooden shelves that once held linnens and supplies, but their contents have been ransacked, and little remains.
120779:
A faded map hangs on the wall.
A simple, worn cot sits close to the ground here.
On the cot, there is a tattered blanket.
A small oaken table has been set here.
On the table, there are a dark coloured flask and a lantern.
An evil priest is here chanting and praying to some foul entity (glowing).

This small chamber has only one entrance, a simple wooden door in the south wall. The walls and ceiling of this room are made of stone that has been blackened by a layer of soot, and footprints of dried mud criss cross the floor. Otherwise, the room is tidy, with sparse furnishings kept in order and showing signs of recent use.
120780:
A thin, hairy plant, with small, oval leaves, grows here.
A rabid rabbit is here, frothing at the mouth.

A deep, wooded ravine cuts across the plains south of here, travelling east as far as one can see. A rusted iron fence blocks passage to the north, beyond which can be seen prairie filled with green earthen mounds and large grey stones.
120781: A crumbling well filled with dusty water sprouts feebly from the ground.

This is a large courtyard between an old stable and a destroyed watchtower. A stone well stands in the middle of the area. Some of the rectangular stones are missing from the rim of the well. The water has a layer of dust covering the surface. A road continues to the south through the town.
120782: Wheel ruts are vaguely identifiable in the dirt but are obscured by caked mud and wooden debris scattered everywhere. The broken and splintered wood pieces appear to be from the nearby buildings to the west and east as they are only partially standing. Sharp shadows are created by the ruins of the buildings.
120783: The deeper into the old town the more debris and broken building materials are piled in the dirt. Ashes that cooled long ago have drifted into cracks and mix with the dirt creating a kind of grey mud paste. The road through town curves to the west surrounded by shadowy ruins.
120784:
The corpse of a robber is lying here.
The corpse of a robber is lying here.
Drazud (freshmeat), wielding a great warsword, is standing here.
Klaees (thedon), wielding a great warsword, is standing here.
Bulg (pukespy), wielding a great warsword, is standing here.

This was once a two-story house but the entire second floor has been destroyed. Enough wood of the second story floor remains to cover most of the first floor as a roof. The only remnants in the building are pieces of broken furniture and other debris that is difficult to identify. A small hatch in the floor is visible in one corner.
120785: Long, round wooden poles lie in the dirt with a small, square roof collapsed in a heap. This appears to be the remains of a watchtower for the small town. Burn marks on the ends of some pieces of wood indicate it may have suffered structural damage from a fire.
120786:
A wooden chest stands in the corner.
A wiry smuggler is here, attempting to avoid being seen.
An experienced husky smuggler is here, plotting his illicit ventures.
An experienced husky smuggler is here, plotting his illicit ventures.
A wiry smuggler is here, attempting to avoid being seen.

The long, wooden bar, where ale was once poured and stories were told, is now a silent reminder of a bygone era. Shattered glass from cups and bottles collects dust on the floor and a the bar. Stains from dried liquids run down the wood and leave vague circles on the floor. Some broken stools and tables are scattered around the edges of the room but it appears most of the furniture was removed.
120787:
A grim smuggler blends into his surroundings.
A thief is here looking for some stranger to rob.
A thief is here looking for some stranger to rob.
A grim smuggler blends into his surroundings.
A grim smuggler blends into his surroundings.

Collapsed tables and frayed canvas stretch out on the ground as evidence of a former market. Most of the stalls appeared open to the air. Some broken baskets contain a dark, putrid sludge that was must have once been fresh vegetables or fruit left to rot.
120788: A maze of trails from rabbits, deer, and their canine foes winds its way through the brush. These trails can be followed in any direction. The flat, curving Greenway wrap around to the north and west, while clearer plains open to the east. The brushy maze continues to the south.
120789:
A large thorny branched shrub is growing here.
On the shrub, there are three piles of blackberries.
A brown fox is here, looking for some rabbits to chew up.
A brown fox is here, looking for some rabbits to chew up.

The air holds the smell of sage and other herbs. Thick bushes stand tall here, providing shade during the day. To the south they become more dense and completely block passage. The brush opens up for easier travel to the east and west.
120790: A colourful butterfly is fluttering around here.

Thick bushes from the south and west invade the area but with much less density and height. Thorny vines tunnelling through the earth create frequent tripping hazards. This vegetation shares the space with sparse grass and many large patches of dirt.
120791: A single, long hill starts sloping up from west to east where it meets other knolls and crags that extend for several miles towards the southeast. Peaceful fields extend in all directions except to the east. Soft grass covers the ground completely.
120792: This rugged terrain has been overgrown by vegetation with rocky crags emerging from this field of grass. Occasional stands of trees are dotting the landscape, providing shelter for smaller creatures, their trunks sturdy and branches reaching high into the sky. They seem to stand as sentinels, guarding the peaceful fields below. The air is filled with the scent of dry earth and dusty stone, mingled with the sharp tang of the brush from the south.
120793: Boulders extend out of the earth and create a maze of outcroppings and craggy peaks, making the shadows of the large rocks loom over the area. The foothills can be quite steep in places, with sheer cliffs and rocky outcroppings that make climbing difficult. Deeper into the foothills, cliffs obstruct the path forward. The sound of trickling water can be heard echoing through the foothills, adding to the tranquil atmosphere of the region.
120794: While the land is covered in thick, shaggy grass, the bushes to the west have encroached. Seeds blown in the wind from the nearby brush have deposited in the area and taken hold with little challenge as they edge out the softer grass. Some large jagged rocks stand in the north.
120795: A grey wolf is here, salivating profusely.

A large jumble of jagged rocks slowly climbs to a height above nearby trees. It is much wider than it is tall, but a difficult slope to the west prevents movement down to the Greenway. Some of the jutting rocks have sharp corners and are as tall as a man. Small sharp stones chipped from their larger brethren are common on the ground.
120796: A brown fox is here, looking for some rabbits to chew up.

The hills here rise and fall like lazy waves, never reaching more than a man's height. The ground is primarily pebbles no larger than a thumb. Some of the stones have sharp edges that could almost slice skin while others are smooth as river rock. Some blades of grass have managed to split through the piles of stones and show signs of life.
120797:
A small cluster of clover grows here.
A lone hawk soars high above you.
A grey wolf is here, salivating profusely.

The land bows down slightly in a long arc between the hills in the north and south. Long fields continue to the east. The lush grass in the fields shows evidence of grazing, which suggests that animals may have been avoiding the more difficult terrain of the hills.
120798: A thin bear is here, hunting for food.

The peaceful slope to the west becomes a more rocky set of hills here. It is as if something punched up a fistful of rocks and boulders from under the surface of the earth. The jumble of jagged stones makes a wall to the east preventing movement.
120799: Deep Valley in the Woody Hills
A grey wolf is here, thin from starvation.

The slope of the land becomes steeper, leading down into a deep valley that lies at the centre of the woody hill range. Water has worn paths into the hills around this area, forming shallow streams and gullies that twist and turn throughout the terrain. Along the washed-out trails, a hardy brush grows, clinging tenaciously to the rocky soil. Its leaves are tough and leathery, and its branches twist and turn like the gnarled fingers of an old crone. To the east, the hills seem to be covered in patches of verdant grass, while to the west, a rocky outcrop dominates the landscape.
120800: A large mother hawk is here looking for prey to feed her young.

A vast expanse of grasslands stretches out as far as the eye can see. The grass, tall and golden, sways gently in the breeze, forming rippling waves. The air is thick with the sweet scent of blooming flowers, and the soft rustling of the reeds is calming background noise.
120801: Gentle Fields along a Steep Ridge

A colony of red ants is here. The ants seem to ignore you.
A furious, old bull is stamping with his hoof.

The fields begin to change, becoming more rocky and rugged as the ridge narrows. The land slopes downward abruptly towards the west, the gently rolling hills giving way to a steep drop-off that leads into a hollow in the landscape. The view from the edge of the grassland is breathtaking, as the horizon seems to stretch out forever, with only the foothills in the distance breaking the line of sight. The ground is littered with boulders and small rock formations, while steep ravines and gullies cut through the hillsides.
120802: Pass between the Ridge of Hills

A nest is here.
A big, nasty vulture is sitting here, protecting its nest.
A big, nasty vulture is sitting here, protecting its nest.

The stony paths become steeper and more treacherous, and the boulders loom ever larger in their path. These cliffs are made of rugged rock faces that have been weathered by centuries of wind and rain. Into the hills, more rocky outcroppings and cliffs can be seen. Some of these formations are so immense that they dwarf even the tallest trees in the region.
120803: Waterfalls cascade down the cliffsides, creating pools of crystal-clear water. A thick seam of peat runs through the centre of the hills. This peat seam gives the ground a soft and spongy texture, making it difficult to traverse on foot. The outcrop on the western side of the foothills rises abruptly from the ground, its bald, steep sides stretching towards the western side of the valley. The rock is rough and jagged, with sharp chips of stone littering the ground around it.
120804: Grass here is mixed with stiff weeds crawling over the dirt. Some taller patches of weeds sprout up much higher than the surrounding vegetation. Fields stretch out in all directions for miles. A cliff following the edge of the South Downs is visible far off to the north east.
120805: A black and white skunk is scuttling about here, searching for food.

Several large patches of ground are exposed with no plant life. Animal footprints have been stamped into the hard ground with no clear indication of how old they are. Sparse grass fills in the area between the spots of open ground.
120806: Numerous pebbles are scattered over the entire area allowing only solitary blades of grass to push up between the small stones. The rocks are jagged and almost sharp on some edges as if a cliff of the South Downs was shattered here into thousands of tiny pieces.
120807: A brown fox is here, looking for some rabbits to chew up.

The area is largely covered by soft grass. Small, willowy bushes spot the landscape providing ample area to move around them. A larger patch of bushes crowd next to the cliff of the South Downs to the east. Stiff bushes crowd in an impossible wall to the south.
120808:
A small campfire burns here, its low flames giving off only a little light.
A small plant grows here, with long, pointed leaves and flowers at its top.

Along the edges of the grassland, the hillsides are covered in entangled shrubbery and sharp-edged boulders that make for treacherous footing. The fields are lush with vibrant green grasses swaying gently in the breeze. In the distance to the west, a ridge of hills can be seen rising against the horizon. Flocks of birds soar overhead, their wings catching the wind as they ride the currents.
120809: Among the green grass of the field is a vague footpath to a long-abandoned building. The roof has caved in and the walls are only partially standing in sections. There are long, sturdy wooden benches strewn around the cobblestone floor. Fresh dirt has been tracked in from the faint path inside the old building and lead to one of the overturned benches.
120810: The cliffs to the north cast long shadows over the vegetation. A variety of rocks from the size of a fingernail up to the size of a head of cabbage mix in with the grasses and short bushes. The highest point in this area is where some dirt is sloped up against the cliff.
120811: The grass here mixes with large swathes of wild barley and wheat. The golden brown of the farm crops droop over in tall curls, like the hair of a sleeping giant. Perhaps a seed shipment on the Greenway was waylaid and some of the cargo ended up being scattered here. The wind whispers through the stalks, creating a gentle rustling sound.
120812:
A large thorny branched shrub is growing here.
On the shrub, there are two piles of blackberries.
A large, venomous-looking green snake is coiled up here.
A small, dense tangle of roots covers the ground.

Stones in the cliff the colour of dried algae indicate a stream once ran over the edge of the hills into the area. A trail of small, round pebbles traces the path of the water that once flowed here. It appears to have flowed west through the vegetation to lower ground.
120813: A blue dragonfly is circling around.

Species of tall shrubs and brambles seem to thrive here in the shade offered by the cliff to the north. The brush opens a little towards the south as the terrain opens up into huge fields. Some fallen trees are scattered around the area, mostly overgrown with the wild brush.
120814:
A huge, black wolf is here, ready to devour.
A black wolf pads restlessly, looking for its next prey.
A black wolf pads restlessly, looking for its next prey.

Thick brush to the north gives way to knee-high grass here and in the surrounding area. Small lumps can be felt in the dirt but the ground is mostly flat in all directions. A tall cliff of the South Downs can be seen off to the north east.
120815: The land here is almost completely flat and unremarkable. Hills are visible to south and northwest but this area is void of any notable change in altitude. Lush grass, ideal for grazing cattle, flows seamlessly on dirt that is almost black.
120816:
A lone hawk soars high above you.
A grey wolf is here, salivating profusely.
A colourful butterfly is fluttering around here.

This area is dominated by the remnants of a landslide from the cliff to the northeast. The cliff remains tall, as if a shelf of dirt sheared off and flowed down into the valley between the South Downs and the grouping of hills to the west. Some bushes and grass have started to push up through the dirt that was once part of the cliff, but the area is still mostly exposed soil.
120817:
A large thorny branched shrub is growing here.
On the shrub, there are two piles of blackberries.
A small, dense tangle of roots covers the ground.
A large, venomous-looking green snake is coiled up here.

The steep cliff against the South Downs to the north and east is covered with scraggly bushes and leafy vines. The most dense area is where the flat ground meets the bottom of the precipice. The vegetation opens up slightly farther towards the surrounding fields.
120818: A tall stag is here, grazing peacefully.

The ground dips very slightly but consistently into a large bowl shape between the collection of knolls to the southwest and the South Downs to the northeast. The centre and lowest part of the bowl contains a small area of dried, rotting vegetation indicating frequent standing water.
120819: A diamondback rattlesnake is coiled here, ready to strike.

The vegetation here grows thick and dense, undisturbed as it is naturally sheltered on almost all sides by natural and man-made obstacles. Some ruined buildings and crumbling walls stand to the north while a stone fence runs along the western edge of the area. The South Downs to the east end abruptly in a tall cliff. Some of the grass here has been flattened apparently by animals bedding down.
120820: The Greenway lies to the west, down a gentle slope. Rolling hills spread out to the south, while flatter ground is visible east. The tall grass covering the knolls is disturbed closer to the Greenway. Perhaps travellers have favored the area with matted vegetation as a place to relax while watching the road.
120821:
A large brown snake with black patches is coiled here.
A huge, black wolf is here, ready to devour.
A black wolf pads restlessly, looking for its next prey.
A black wolf pads restlessly, looking for its next prey.
A cute rabbit is here.

A long ridge of hills to the south and east bulge up in this area, sheltering a secluded meadow. Birds have made their home in some small natural caves high above the ground in the cliff wall. A handful of trees stand away from the steep terrain.
120822: A broken water trough lies surrounded by grass.

A peaceful field of knee-high grass is fenced in by piles of stones. This would be an ideal place for a flock of sheep or cows to graze. The only way out around the lengths of assembled stones is to the north. The ground is very flat. A small grove of trees give cover in the southeast corner.
120823: Large flat stones define a mostly overgrown path travelling west alongside an ancient stone wall. To the east, the path joins up with a wider and more defined road. Tall hills rise to the north, hindering travel in that direction. On occasion, a breeze from the south brings with it a noxious odour originating from some sort of flowering plant.
120824:
A magpie is flying around looking for some food.
A black wolf pads restlessly, looking for its next prey.
A colourful butterfly is fluttering around here.

A little-used path marked by flat stones rises up to greet steep banks to the north and west. The path leads down a gentle hill to the east and south, closely following a stone wall that cuts its way across the green landscape.
120825:
A mass of dark green leaves clings to a wall.
A brigand, looking at your nice purse, is sneaking here.

The remains of an ancient stone wall cut across the landscape, running southwest to northeast. Thick, woody vines have grown into the wall in such a way that they hold it in place. In places with no such reinforcement, only rubble exists. A path defined by wide flat stones follows the wall, leading north and west.
120826: Large flat stones define a mostly overgrown path travelling east and south alongside an ancient stone wall. A shallow ditch to the north is filled with tall, dense grasses whose tassels rise ten feet or more into the air.
120827:
There are three piles of wheat cereals here.
A magpie is flying around looking for some food.

Tall wheat grows in this once prosperous field, but it does not look like it has been harvested in many years. A shallow ditch curves around the field from the north to the west. Dense, tall grasses fill the ditch, blocking travel. South and east of here, a trail and a stone wall travel across the land.
120828: A colourful butterfly is fluttering around here.

Stone foundations are all that remain of several structures on either side of a stony path. This may have once been a large farmstead or a small village, but anything of value is long gone. Southeast of here can be seen a stone wall crossing the plains. The path loosely follows it to the east and south. A cluster of trees to the west provides shade, but blocks travel in that direction.
120829: A stony path narrows as it passes between a thick copse of pine trees to the northwest, and a moss-covered stone wall to the southeast. Not far west of here, the wall ends abruptly. Sound is dampened by the barriers, and the air holds the bright scent of pine and the musty smell of rotting plant matter.
120830: Stone cairns standing no more than two feet tall periodically mark a thin trail travelling through the plains. A pile of rotting wooden debris lies near the trail, the remains of a hovel that must have collapsed decades ago. The trail continues east and west from here. A dense thicket of pine trees blocks travel and visibility to the north, while to the south the scrubby plains open up for miles.
120831:
A mass of dark green leaves clings to a wall.
A colourful butterfly is fluttering around here.

A path marked by wide, flat stones set into the ground meanders its way north and west through the plains. A decrepit stone wall crosses the plains to the south, running southwest to northeast. The plains around here look like they may once have been cultivated farmland, but untended fields and the occasional building foundation are all that remain.
120832: Trail near a Short Log Structure
A gaunt Barrow-wight is here, its glowing eyes gazing around intently.

A dense thicket of pine trees stands to the north, wrapping around to the west. In front of the thicket west of here, a hundred yards from the trail, several of the trees were harvested and stacked into a simple log structure standing about four feet high. Round stones and crude masonry are pressed between the logs of the walls, providing structure and adornment. The roof is topped with gravel and earth, upon which grow many ferns.
120833: A dusty, stony trail bends and stretches westward and northward. It is surrounded by a lush, green grassland. Patches of tall, thick weeds and low, scraggly shrubs dot the landscape. Far to the south, a rising, thorny scrubland dominates the horizon.
120834:
A brown fox is here, looking for some rabbits to chew up.
A wild dog bares his yellow fangs at you.
A wild dog bares his yellow fangs at you.
A wild dog bares his yellow fangs at you.
A robin is here, carrying small pieces of wood to its nest.

A wide, stony trail spans east and west. Small stones and loose gravel surround a well-travelled and worn-down centre, which is smooth and bare. It is enveloped in every direction by a lush green grassland. Patches of tall weeds and low shrubs dot the landscape.
120835: A wide, stony trail bends south and west here. The centre of the trail is worn all the way to the bare dirt. Beneath it, the centre is surrounded by loose gravel on each side. Surrounding the trail is a rich, lush green field that stretches in all directions. Low bushes and shrubs grow waist-high on the borders of the trail.
120836:
A low shrub with bright green, oblong leaves is growing here.
Scattered in and on the shrub, there are three piles of blueberries.

A flat, expansive plain stretches out in all directions. The ground is covered in lush, green grass. Every now and then, small patches of thin shrubs and scraggly trees break up the monotony of the plain. Occasional patches of small stones and gravel appear sporadically as well.
120837: A sea of lush, green grass stretches in every direction. Spanning east and west, a well-worn, stony path has been cut into the ground. The path is composed of small, loose pebbles and gravel, with the ground worn bare in the centre.
120838: Edge of a Dense Thistle Patch

Brush, thorns, briars, and brambles dominate the landscape here. To the north, they are much thinner and eventually come to an end. To the south and east, the daunting vegetation thickens and becomes denser, making passage in those directions much more difficult. Thistle plants with blue flowers grow randomly among the vegetation.
120839: The grasslands to the north quickly transition into a landscape of thinning vegetation. Vines, thorns, and brush grow thicker southward. To the east, a dense, impassable wall of thorny vines and shrubbery has formed. Blue thistle flowers grow abundantly here throughout the brush.
120840:
A wild dog bares his yellow fangs at you.
A wild dog bares his yellow fangs at you.
A wild dog bares his yellow fangs at you.

A stony trail travels westward and northward here. It is worn in the centre, providing evidence that it is well-travelled. Loose gravel and pebbles line the sides. A lush, green grassland surrounds it, stretching out in every direction, with the occasional patch of thick weeds and shrubs sprouting up randomly.
120841: Northern Edge of a Large Thistle Patch

The northern portion of this large thistle patch is filled with low brush and dry vegetation. Some thorny vines hang down in some areas, but become much more prevalent to the south. Patches of grassy ground appear here and there, with no tall vegetation growing in these openings. Elsewhere, low shrubs and young, thin trees can be found all about the area.
120842: Northern End of a Large Thistle Patch

Creeping thistle weeds dominate the landscape, with blue flowers sprouting from the tops. Dry, thin brush and low shrubs grow all about, with the blue flower heads protruding through occasionally. The ground is mostly covered in grass, with bare patches popping up every now and then. Patches of dense, low, green shrubbery make rare appearances in the otherwise dry landscape.
120843: The terrain toward the east drops abruptly over a steep cliff, from which the Greenway can be spotted below. Dense, thin, and scraggly brush grows abundantly everywhere but to the east, where it thins before eventually opening before the cliff's edge. The occasional blue thistle flower sprouts up sporadically.
120844: Ancient Stone Wall Lining a Thistle Patch
Some small boulders have been stacked into a mound here.

An ancient stone wall northwest of here cuts across a gently rising hill. Tall grasses bend back and forth when there is a breeze, creating waves across the landscape. Several thistles with prickly leaves grow here, becoming more dense to the east and south.
120845: A sprawling green bush of stinging nettle grows here.

Thorny bushes interspersed with prickly thistles grow in abundance here, becoming impassibly thick to the east and south. The dense brush continues to the north, but thins out westward. The sounds of insects hum constantly, but there are no other signs of wildlife.
120846: Walls of Stone and Thorns Surrounding a Thistle Patch

Some thick writhing vines whip all around you.
A mass of vines reaches out from the surrounding brush.

An ancient stone wall cuts across the the brush covered landscape northwest of here. To the east, a tall, dense thicket of stems and thorns makes travel that direction impossible. It meets up with the stone wall directly to the north, creating an abrupt corner. Several thistles with sharp leaves and blue flowers grow in the open.
120847: Waist-high vegetation dominates the landscape, making normal movement through the area more difficult. Dense, thick, thorny vines hang down all around as well, adding to the difficulty of moving safely and easily about. Large areas of grassy ground, devoid of the dangerous vegetation, appear occasionally. Blue thistle flowers can be found scattered about, in no consistent manner of growth.
120848: Prickly, white-stemmed plants, with blue flower heads grow in abundance.

Dense vegetation can be seen in every direction, and almost everything seems to be covered in sharp thorns and spines. Thick roots carpet the ground, and rise up to form large walls blocking passage to the west and south. Blue thistle flowers grow abundantly here.
120849:
Prickly, white-stemmed plants, with blue flower heads grow in abundance.
A small, dense tangle of roots covers the ground.

Thin, dry brush and vegetation grow high here. Thorny vines hang down all around. The dry, cracked ground is covered in a blanket of thin, but densely-growing roots. Blue thistle flowers grow all over the landscape, and travel here is relatively easy.
120850: An ancient barrow, covered in thorns and thistles, swells from the earth.

Thin, dry, scraggly brush grows high and dense, with vines hanging down from above all throughout. Creeping thistle weeds grow all over, their blue heads adding dots of colour to the otherwise dull landscape. There is an occasional grassy area, devoid of brush, which provides some reprieve from tedious travel.
120851: Thin, dry, scraggly vegetation grows here at the edge of a thistle patch. It grows thicker into the thistle patch to the south, with blue thistle flowers scattered amongst it. To the north, the ground flattens out into a green grassland.
120852: A black snake hurries towards you with sly intentions.

The green, lush grassland to the north transitions into the outskirts of a thistle patch here. The vegetation is thin, but grows thicker to the south. The landscape here is dotted with blue thistle flowers, growing on long, thorny green stems.
120853: Blue thistle flowers grow abundantly all around in the dense, treacherous vegetation here. A tall wall of dense, thorny vines has formed to the west, blocking any hopes of passage in that direction. The ground is dry, cracked, and dusty. Overhead, a canopy of tangled, thick vines stretches in every direction.
120854:
Prickly, white-stemmed plants, with blue flower heads grow in abundance.
A black spider crawls here, a shiny red spot visible on its belly.

Dense, dry, scraggly, and treacherous vegetation grows here, deep inside a thistle patch. Everything seems to be covered in sharp thorns and long spines. The ground is dry and dusty, with no grass covering the bare dirt. Thistle flowers grow abundantly all around.
120855:
Prickly, white-stemmed plants, with blue flower heads grow in abundance.
A small barrow, covered in grass, rises slightly above the ground.
A small, naked humanoid creature glares at you.
A small, naked humanoid creature glares at you.

A blanket of thick, thorny vines has formed a cover overhead, allowing sunlight to still shine through during the daytime. The vegetation here is dangerous, thorny, dry, and tangled. The ground is dry, dusty, and worn to the bare dirt. Blue thistle flowers grow all around, spread throughout the dangerous surrounding vegetation.
120856: Prickly, white-stemmed plants, with blue flower heads grow in abundance.

A tangled canopy of dry, thorny vines stretches out overhead in all directions. The landscape is dominated by dense, thorny brush and travel is difficult to the west and south, and impossible to the north and east. The atmosphere is dry and dusty. Blue thistle flowers grow all throughout the dense brush.
120857:
Prickly, white-stemmed plants, with blue flower heads grow in abundance.
A crude shelter is here, built of woven vines and thatched with thistle stalks.

Overhead, the canopy of tangled, thorny vines continues to stretch out in all directions, ascending higher into the air toward the south and southwest. The vegetation is dry and thorny. Almost everything here is covered in thorns. The ground is dry, cracked, and dusty.
120858: Prickly, white-stemmed plants, with blue flower heads grow in abundance.

Dense, dangerous vegetation make travel here perilous. Adding to the peril, the terrain rises to the south and ends at a steep drop-off over a cliff edge. A blanket of vines encroaches in from the south, forming a carpet of vines and roots that are covered in thorns and spines.
120859:
Prickly, white-stemmed plants, with blue flower heads grow in abundance.
A massive barrow rises ominously out of the earth.

The terrain rises here, forming a steep drop-off over a cliff to the south and east. Entangled vines creep in from the south, forming a layer of dense vines and roots on the ground, which are covered in sharp thorns and spines. The vegetation is dense and dangerous.
120860: Prickly, white-stemmed plants, with blue flower heads grow in abundance.

A steep drop-off over a cliff edge impedes travel to the east, below which the Greenway can be spotted. The ground here is covered in thick roots and vines, making travel very tedious and perilous. An impassable wall of vines has formed to the west, and blue thistle flowers grow all about.
120861:
Prickly, white-stemmed plants, with blue flower heads grow in abundance.
Some thick writhing vines whip all around you.
Some thick writhing vines whip all around you.

The heart of the thistle patch is filled with dense, dry vegetation, making movement here extremely difficult in any direction. Thorny, spiny vines hang from above, and seem to sway and shift on their own accord. Blue thistle flowers grow abundantly here, and the ground is covered in a very thick, dense carpet of roots, which seem to cover an opening below.
120862: Corner of a Wall of Vines

A mass of wriggling vines drops on you from the trees.
A mass of wriggling vines drops on you from the trees.

A huge, towering wall of thick, thorny vines bends to the north and east. The wall towers at least twenty feet into the air, blocking passage in either direction. From the top of the massive wall, a thick canopy of thorny vines extends out to the north and east.
120863: A natural corridor has been formed here between a steep cliff wall to the north and a blockade of thorns to the south. The wall is formed from thick, green vines, covered in thorns, and woven tightly together. The wall rises approximately twenty feet high, and a canopy stretches from the top of it toward the top of the cliff to the north. The vegetation here is dense and treacherous.
120864: Massive roots shift uneasily all around you.

There is a steep cliff wall to the north and a wall of thorns to the south and east. A canopy forms from the top of the wall and stretches northward to the cliff and climbs to its crest. The vegetation is dense and makes manoeuvring difficult. The thorny vegetation here shifts restlessly, seemingly of its own accord, and the ground is covered in a carpet of tangled roots.
120865: Along a Huge Wall of Vines
Prickly, white-stemmed plants, with blue flower heads grow in abundance.

A towering wall of green vines, thickly-covered in long, sharp thorns, dominates the south here. Passage and sight beyond the wall to the south is impossible. At the base of the wall, thick roots grow and tangle together in the ground, where they disappear into the dry, cracked dirt. Blue thistle flowers grow all throughout the wall and the surrounding brush.
120866: Along a Wall of Vines and Thorns
Prickly, white-stemmed plants, with blue flower heads grow in abundance.

A huge, towering wall of green, thorny, entangling vines has grown here, blocking passage to the south. It stands approximately twenty feet tall, and a dense canopy grows from it, stretching northerly. Other dry, thorny vegetation grows abundantly and treacherously, and blue thistle flowers dominate the surroundings.
120867: Prickly, white-stemmed plants, with blue flower heads grow in abundance.

The treacherous vegetation grows thick in all directions and becomes almost impassable. Navigating and manoeuvring here are extremely difficult. Blue-flowered thistle plants grow sporadically throughout the briars and brambles. The atmosphere is dry and dusty.
120868:
Prickly, white-stemmed plants, with blue flower heads grow in abundance.
Some roots lie here waiting to ensnare weary travellers.

A thick, impassable wall of thorny vines rises suddenly to the south and east, standing approximately fifteen feet tall. The thorns covering the green vines are long and sharp. The area immediately surrounding the wall is filled with dense, treacherous vegetation. A narrow hole can be seen in the wall to the east, where the vines are thinner and can possibly be opened to allow passage.
120869:
Prickly, white-stemmed plants, with blue flower heads grow in abundance.
Massive roots shift uneasily all around you.

Dense brush and thorny, spiny bushes dominate the landscape, and a canopy of entangled vines grows overhead. The vegetation grows thinner below. The ground is dry and cracked, with not much grass covering the bare dirt. Blue thistles grow plentifully.
120870: Prickly, white-stemmed plants, with blue flower heads grow in abundance.

Brush, thorns, briars, and brambles grow thick and dense here, rising up about eight feet from the ground. The ground beneath the thick vegetation is bare, with small patches of thin grasses here and there. The air is dry and dusty. All about, thistle plants with blue flowers grow randomly.
120871: A large brown snake with black patches is coiled here.

A scrubby grassland stretches south, a vast sea of waving green grass. Despite its seemingly endless expanse, there is a sense of unease in the air. A huge wall of thorns blocks passage to the north, the sharp spines and twisted vines a warning to those who would venture too close. Thorny vines and roots creep in from the north, snaking their way through the grass and tangling around anything in their path. The air is thick with the smell of dust and the sound of the wind whistling through the grass.
120872: A skeleton of some humanoid lies in the dust.

A huge wall of thorns curves to the north and east, and the ground immediately bordering it is bare, the earth baked hard by the sun and devoid of any vegetation. Yet beyond that, the grassland stretches out to the south, an endless sea of green waves. Despite its harsh appearance, the thorny grassland is home to a variety of hardy creatures that have adapted to the unforgiving environment. These include snakes, lizards, and rodents, as well as the occasional wandering traveller seeking a passage through this treacherous region.
120873: This is a quiet field, with the exception of the sounds of birds and a gentle breeze rustling through the grass. Yellow and orange wildflowers cover the landscape, growing wherever they can with no prejudice. Animal tracks and paths crisscross across the terrain.
120874: A tall flower with a large head and bright yellow petals sways gently in the breeze.

A quiet, tranquil sea of green grass spreads out in every direction, disappearing into the horizons. Yellow and orange wildflowers dot the landscape with bees and other insects buzzing about them. Small paths have been worn into the ground by animals that traverse them.
120875: A wall of thick, green vines, covered in long, sharp thorns, blocks passage to the north. It rises suddenly from the otherwise flat grassland bordering it to the south, and the view beyond it is dark and ominous. In the south and east, the ground is covered in a lush, green blanket of grass.
120876: A brown fox is here, looking for some rabbits to chew up.

The terrain is flat, and covered in a thick, green carpet of grass stretching out what appears to be indefinitely to the south. A small farm can be seen in the distance to the east, and the low bellows of cows mooing can be heard on occasion.
120877: A flat, calm sea of thick green grasses stretches out to the north and south. Small animals and critters appear to have taken up residence here and there, with small mounds and dens dotting the landscape. Small patches of rocks and gravel line the ground here and there.
120878: A large farm can be seen a ways off in the distance to the west. Everywhere else, a lush, green field spawls out in all directions. The occasional sound of farm animals can be heard in the distance. Hills, mounds, and small holes have been made by small rodents or other animals, with small game trails worn into the grass.
120879: A colourful butterfly is fluttering around here.

Crumbling ruins stand in the centre of the field here dominating the immediate landscape. Large stone blocks lie stacked in rows, covered in lichen and moss, forming the perimeter of what must have once been a very large structure. Tall grass and weeds grow all around the blocks, almost reclaiming them back for the land.
120880:
A wild brown donkey is here, on the lookout for enemies.
A donkey foal is playing around.
A donkey foal is playing around.
A jenny is grazing here.
A snake slithers towards you.

Though the terrain is relatively flat, an occasional low hill rises from the ground and rolls back down. Green grass stretches out as far as the eye can see in every direction. Small footpaths can be seem worn into the ground, probably from some small game. A gentle breeze blow through the air.
120881:
A colourful butterfly is fluttering around here.
A wild bull seems ready to charge you.
A wild bull seems ready to charge you.

The ground is dry and covered in short grass with patches of bare dirt spread throughout. There are some rocks and stones scattered about the landscape, adding to the bare ground. Thorny, scrubby bushes make an appearance every now and then.
120882: Lush green grass covers the terrain in all directions. To the southwest, the ground slopes downwards like a huge, green stairway. Small bushes and an occasional little hill give a slight sense of depth in the encompassing greenery.
