120883: The lush green grasslands continue in all directions, with only a slight upward slope leading east towards the Greenway. A few bushes and smaller trees dot the landscape, with an occasional boulder or two jutting out from the grass-covered ground.
120884: There are two piles of wild strawberries here.

The terrain here is flat and green, teeming with wildlife. The buzzing of insects, chirping of birds, and the occasional distant sound of farm animals fill the air. There are sporadic stands of small, thinning trees, as well as small patches of high weeds and grasses.
120885: The flat, green terrain stretches as far as the eye can see in every direction. Small patches of thin shrubs and trees appear occasionally, breaking up the otherwise monotonous landscape. The ground is firm and densely packed, allowing easy passage in any direction here.
120886: The lush grassland stretches out in all directions, sloping slightly upwards to the east. An old, nigh-invisible footpath leads to the south, snaking between a few boulders and some groups of bushes. What might have once been a scarecrow now lies in a rotting pile of wood and rope on the ground, almost completely covered in grass.
120887: A faded footpath snakes through the grassy fields. A few ancient wooden fenceposts jut out from the grass-covered earth, indicating that this area might have once been farmland. A bigger group of trees and bushes can be seen in the distance to the south.
120888: A sprawling green bush of stinging nettle grows here.

A group of larger bushes and small trees stands out from among the vast grasslands, hiding the burnt and dilapidated remains of a larger building. A broken stone wall still stands to the south, almost completely covered in vines and grass. Among the stone rubble, a partly burnt section of a wooden floor still remains, grass growing from between the floorboards.
120889: The rolling grasslands undulate eastward like huge natural steps, with bushes and a few smaller trees jutting out from the higher points. A small footpath runs parallel to the nearest ledge, disappearing into the tall grass to the north.
120890: Grassy Field along a Forested Ledge

Up above to the east, a forest grows tall on a high ledge, overlooking the surrounding grassy plains. To the south, a large pile of boulders seems to have spilt into the grassy fields from above. A larger clump of trees and bushes stands out from the otherwise grassy plains to the northwest.
120891: The rolling grasslands stop abruptly at an overgrown stone wall to the north, the only standing remnants of some sort of building. Thick bushes and a few trees almost completely hide it from sight. To the south, a few small hills stand out from among the grassy fields.
120892: A bear is here, covered with coarse black fur.

The rolling plains of grass stretch out in all directions, with a few bushes and trees standing out from the overwhelmingly green sea. To the southeast, a few small hills can be seen jutting out from the grassland, sprinkled with piles of boulders and scraggly bushes.
120893:
A large, venomous-looking green snake is coiled up here.
A large, venomous-looking green snake is coiled up here.

This pocket of lush grassland is surrounded by a forested ledge to the northeast and some small boulder-covered hills to the southwest. Aside from a large pile of fallen boulders to the north, the flat grasslands stretch out far to the north.
120894: A bear is here, covered with coarse black fur.

The dome-shaped hills are almost completely covered with grass and bushes, with a few smaller boulders mixed in as well. Near the ground level, however, pieces of ancient stonework can be glimpsed from beneath the grass, revealing that the hills haven't formed naturally but have rather been built.
120895:
A sturdy billy goat stands here, proudly protecting his goats.
A young goat playfully charges and hops away.
A young goat playfully charges and hops away.

Springing out of the ground, these small hills look like oversized mushroom caps, round and jolly. Beneath the grass-covered exterior, the hills hide some ancient stonework, however. Instead of natural formations, the hills are in actuality outer domes of some ancient underground structures.
120896: The thick and dark brushland to the south comes to an end as the ground here slopes upward a bit. Dome-shaped hills rise out from the ground, covered in green grass and bushes. To the east, a high, grass-covered ledge angles upward to look over the hills like an oversized sundial.
120897: The grassy hills to the north are engulfed by the thick brush here, tangled branches almost completely obscuring the sky. Damp, moss-covered undergrowth consists of thorny vines and hanging moss, making traversing almost like navigating a natural maze.
120898:
A small pool of red-stained water lies here.
A water moccasin slithers out of sight just below the surface of the water.
A water moccasin slithers out of sight just below the surface of the water.
A water moccasin slithers out of sight just below the surface of the water.
A blue dragonfly is circling around.
A mass of wriggling vines drops on you from the trees.

The ground slopes down into a damp depression here, with scraggly branches and hanging vines surrounding a small pool of stagnant water below a steep rocky rise to the south. The stones scattered around the edge of the pool are covered with a slick green substance.
120899: Branches and vines are covered with thick strands of hanging moss around here, obscuring vision. To the east, the vines seem to be less restricting, the Greenway barely visible beyond. The uneven, moss-covered ground slightly slopes upwards to the southwest, leading farther into the brush.
120900: The tangled branches and vines give way to smaller, stunted bushes and less dense undergrowth to the east. The ground slopes downward towards the barely visible Greenway in the distance, branches and roots jutting out from the ground and making the descent quite precarious.
120901: Under a Canopy of Tall Shrubs

A tree-snake lies wrapped around one of the tree branches.
A tree-snake lies wrapped around one of the tree branches.
A fallow deer is grazing peacefully here.
A fallow deer is grazing peacefully here.

This place is shrouded from any view of the sky above by the dense, dark foliage of tall evergreen shrubs of various kinds. The scrubland probably continues in all directions, though not much can be seen to the east over high and thickly growing brambles, and densely growing blackthorn trees block travel southwards too.
120902: A bear is here, covered with coarse black fur.

Dense bushes and tangled undergrowth cover the uneven ground here and climb up a steep and dangerous-looking slope to the west, into even thicker brush. The thicket follows the Greenway like a shadow looming over the snaking, grass-covered road.
120903: Under a Canopy of Tall Shrubs

A tree-snake lies wrapped around one of the tree branches.
A tree-snake lies wrapped around one of the tree branches.

A canopy of tall evergreen shrubs creates an obscuring veil, hiding any view of the sky above. The scrubland likely extends in all directions; however, vision is limited due to all the shrubs and brambles, the latter of which also block the way west.
120904: Dense bushes have overtaken the grasslands completely around here, growing denser and denser farther west. To the east, the Greenway comes out of a pass to the north and makes its way past the brush, slightly turning east towards the grassy plains there.
120905:
A squirrel scampers around here, looking for nuts from the trees.
A tall stag is here, grazing peacefully.

The tall trees of this light forest are spread well apart, making passage across the firm, loamy soil quite easy, and lending an open, airy feeling to the place. To the east, a wide road can be seen, skirting the woodland, whilst westward, the shrubby trees close in somewhat, shading the ground from the sky above.
120906: A mass of wriggling vines drops on you from the trees.

Young trees and saplings have grown up in this area, probably spreading from the north where a remnant of the ancient forest remains. Bushes compete for space with the young trees and in some cases, it looks like the saplings grew up through the bushes and will eventually shade them. The scrubland continues to the west and south, but to the east a road is visible.
120907: A large, venomous-looking green snake is coiled up here.

Tall, leafy and mostly thorny, shrubs stand all around in this scrubland. Looking to the south and west, more of the same, as far as it is possible to see through the bushes and under the canopy of branches, but to the north dense and spiny blackthorn creates an effective barrier: it could almost be a planted hedge. There is a sense of the tall shrubs perhaps dying out towards the east, but this may be an illusion.
120908:
Spiny, densely-branched trees create a thick canopy here.
Inside the shrub, there are a cluster of purplish-pink flowers.
A sprawling, twisted tree grows here.
On the tree, there are two piles of hawthorn berries.
A mass of wriggling vines drops on you from the trees.

The landscape here is dominated by mature shrubs, mainly blackthorn and hawthorn, tall and leafy enough and closely packed enough to create effective shade from any sun that may beat down upon the ground from the sky. These thorny shrubs also make travel tiresome as it is impossible to move in a straight line for long, or indeed to see very far.
120909: A mass of wriggling vines drops on you from the trees.

Various types of shrubs populate this area: blackthorn dominates the northern landscape, hindering passage in that direction; sea buckthorn prevails in the southern expanse; hawthorn is more abundant towards the west, alongside other smaller shrubs scattered throughout. An unobstructed view to the east reveals the presence of a visible road.
120910:
A nightingale is here, chirping a sweet melody.
A fallow deer is grazing peacefully here.

This land has been colonized by sea buckthorn and it seems to be doing particularly well here, growing everywhere, swaying in the wind like waves in the sea. These shrubs vary in height between three and sixteen feet tall depending on maturity, with multiple tree-like branches. The bark is mostly dark brown to black, though on younger shoots they have silvery hairs. The leaves are shaped like lances with silvery hairs concealing their basic green colour. The density of the shrubs means it is not possible to see very far in any direction.
120911:
A large, venomous-looking green snake is coiled up here.
A mass of wriggling vines drops on you from the trees.

The almost continuous shade of the tall shrubs here does not seem to be preventing smaller evergreen bushes from growing. There is a particularly dense tangle of these to the south. To the north and west, the dark scrubland apparently continues, but the east seems brighter.
120912:
A nightingale is here, chirping a sweet melody.
A fallow deer is grazing peacefully here.

Shrubs, tall and bushy, shield the ground from the sun's penetrating rays. Brambles grow thick and tall to the south as they try and reach the light. The dark scrubland continues to the east and north, but to the west it looks lighter.
120913: Thorny shrubs prevail in this area of scrubland, their thorns designed to provide some protection for their leaves from browsing animals. This does not appear to have been particularly effective, as few leaves near the ground are visible. The scrubland seems to continue to the east, south and presumably to the north, although visibility in any direction is poor.
120914:
A cluster of dark green, feathery fronds flourishes in the shade.
A mass of vines whips all around you.
Some thick writhing vines whip all around you.
A tall stag is here, grazing peacefully.
A large hawk-like bird is here overlooking its territory.
A large hawk-like bird is here overlooking its territory.
A fierce boar is here, making grunting noises.

This deep dell is secluded, with short grass growing along much of the bottom and various shrubs growing upwards towards the open sky. A line of mostly smooth stones hints at where a seasonal stream may live out its dying days. The dell continues to the east and west, while the sides of the dell to the north and south are covered with slippery green moss.
120915:
A sprawling, twisted tree grows here.
On the tree, there are a few hawthorn berries.

Tall hawthorn trees stand all around, blocking almost any view of the sky above, and making passage through this scrubland tiresome. Dense and spiny blackthorn blocks any passage or sight to the east, while the scrubland continues in the other directions.
120916:
Spiny, densely-branched trees create a thick canopy here.
Inside the shrub, there are a cluster of purplish-pink flowers.
A huge, venomous tarantula extends her legs to you.
Massive roots shift uneasily all around you.
A great, dark wolf stands here, sniffing the air.

Here tall blackthorn trees, spiny and densely branched, create a canopy of foliage blocking out the sky above and making travel in any direction difficult. The dense scrubland also seems to continue in every direction, though it's impossible to see very far.
120917: The shade of elder trees and the mossy ground help to keep the soil damp, but this area may also be liable to occasional floods as it looks like there may be a stream to the south in a deep dell. To the north tall shrubs are visible at the skyline, while to the east the scrubland also continues.
120918: Tall shrubs overshadow this location. Not much grows at ground level, though whether this is the impact of the foliage canopy or whether browsers keep new growth at bay is hard to tell. The scrubland continues in all directions, but it feels like there is something of a change to the south.
120919: Some thick writhing vines whip all around you.

Strands of hanging moss and climbing vines make this part of the brush extremely hard to navigate. A jagged boulder juts out from the ground to the north, standing above a little stagnant pool. To the east, a once dried-out brook is now a completely overgrown ditch leading towards the road far to the east.
120920:
Spiny, densely-branched trees create a thick canopy here.
Inside the shrub, there are a cluster of purplish-pink flowers.
A mass of wriggling vines drops on you from the trees.

Blackthorn trees and other tall shrubs grow closely enough together here to create a thick enough canopy to obscure the sky. The blackthorn has also formed hedge-like barriers to the east, south and west, the dense spiny branches preventing travel in those directions.
120921: The cave is small and dark, with only a few rays of light filtering through the narrow entrance. The walls are rough and jagged, covered with moss and lichen. The floor is littered with bones, fur, and other signs of the cave's inhabitant. A faint smell of musk and blood lingers in the air. The cave is silent, except for the occasional drip of water from the ceiling.
120922: Endless green grass stretches out in all directions, with only some steeper ledges above to the east and below to the west, dividing the lush greenery into narrow sections. Aside from the occasional bush or small tree, only a small clump of trees can be seen far below in the distance to the southwest.
120923:
A small sign leans slightly at the end of one of the rows.
There are four potatoes here.

This is a small garden, with lots of flowers and green plants. The plants are placed in lines, as if someone put them there on purpose. The soil smells like manure, but this seems to be a great place to grow plants. A farmhouse and a barn stand nearby.
120924:
A reddish-brown shrub with purplish-pink flowers grows here.
Inside the shrub, there are a cluster of purplish-pink flowers.

The grassy field is a serene and peaceful place, a haven of tranquility and calm. The tall blades of grass wave gently in the breeze. Wildflowers add a touch of colour to the landscape, their delicate petals unfurling to soak up the sun's rays. The field is alive with the sound of rustling grass and the soft buzz of insects, and it seems to go on forever.
120925: The overgrown ruins of an old stone structure dot the landscape.

This stretch of woods is not nearly as ancient as the stand of ancient oaks farther south. Sticking out of the ground are the remnants of the foundation of an old stone building. The light undergrowth almost obscures the stones, but this area was definitely inhabited by man at some point in the past.
120926:
A tall flower with a large head and bright yellow petals sways gently in the breeze.
A wild sheep with a short, greyish coat grazes here.

A grassy field stretches out in all directions, the tall blades of green waving gently in the breeze. Wildflowers dot the landscape, adding splashes of colour to the verdant expanse. The air is filled with the scent of growth and life, and the sounds of birds and insects can be heard.
120927: Field South of a Thistle Patch

A reddish-brown shrub with purplish-pink flowers grows here.
Inside the shrub, there are a cluster of purplish-pink flowers.

To the north of the field stands a massive wall of vines, blocking access to the thistle patch beyond. The vines are thick and woven together, covered in sharp thorns that deter would-be intruders. The earth at the base of the wall is barren and lifeless, stripped of grass and vegetation. Despite this, the field itself is a rolling expanse of green, the grass tall and lush.
120928: Field South of a Thistle Patch

A reddish-brown shrub with purplish-pink flowers grows here.
Inside the shrub, there are a cluster of purplish-pink flowers.
A snake slithers towards you.

The field lies to the south of a huge patch of thistle, the spiky plants standing tall and proud. There is a huge wall separating the field from the thistle patch, and it is covered in sharp thorns. The field itself is a rolling expanse of green, the grass tall and lush.
120929:
A reddish-brown shrub with purplish-pink flowers grows here.

Small holes in the ground punctuate the grass here, but it is the wall or mound of brambles to the north that are most striking. It would be impossible to get through those mature and overgrown brambles, but the leaves, flowers and blackberries probably keep a lot of animals happy. To the west, the brambles die out, while the grass continues, also to the south.
121023: A dry plain is all that can be seen in the west, whilst to the north the horizon is dominated by an apparent line of vegetation of some kind. The ground here seems parched and quite unable to sustain life, as indicated by the thin wisps of unhealthy grass that seem barely able to cling to life. To the south, a gully cuts a deep scar across the countryside.
121024: A little thin and unhealthy grass clings to life here, on this parched plain. To the south, a rather deep gully runs from east to west, perhaps the bed of some ancient river, now long ago dried up and forgotten. The plain stretches onward north, east and west from here, with perhaps some scrubland beyond to the west.
121025: The grass is almost non-existent on this desolate plain. The soil is parched and thin. A river must once have passed just south of here, for a wide and deep gully cuts into the earth, making a scar that runs from east to west across the land. Whilst travel to the south would be made difficult by this feature, it seems that progress in that direction might still be possible. The plain continues to the north and east, but to the west bushes and shrubs are growing.
121026:
A large thorny branched shrub is growing here.
On the shrub, there are five piles of blackberries.
A bee flies around here, collecting nectar from the flowers.
A nightingale is here, chirping a sweet melody.

Dense bramble bushes have taken hold in this area, particularly to the west where their density and height mean nothing is visible on the other side of them. To the north, the brambles become increasingly sparse, and some other bushes and shrubs are making a living. To the east, the land seems to noticeably open up, while to the south there is a very deep gully.
121027: A river must once have cut this mighty scar in the countryside, but now it stands quite dry. Though shallow here, it deepens markedly to the west, and the way eastward is blocked by a huge pile of fallen boulders. The dry plain continues to the north and south.
121028: This is quite a deep gully here, but it gets shallower to the east and continues to deepen to the west. It is impossible to see out beyond the slopes, where some hardy bushes cling to life amongst the stones and dry, cracked mud. A river must have made this deep gully centuries ago and any torrential rainfall surely comes this way.
121029: A skeleton of some humanoid lies in the dust.

The river, which once cut this mighty channel through the land, may have gone south from here through a dark gulch. Here the gully is deep, becoming shallower to the west and east, and narrower and steeper also to the west. Dry, cracked mud hints at occasional water on the surface and some bushes growing here must have found it beneath.
121030:
The remains of a thick tangle of vines lie here in a heap of rotting compost.
A cluster of dark green, feathery fronds flourishes in the shade.

The gully becomes narrower and steeper here, and shallower to the west, where it seems to reach a dead end in a mass of vegetation. To the east, it becomes quite deep and wide as it cuts across the countryside. To the north and south, the smooth rock walls are not suitable for climbing up out of the gully.
121031: The gulch cleaves a north-to-south gash through the landscape, its towering walls curving towards each other, creating a tunnel-like passage that conceals the sky from below. The ground underfoot is cracked, and some plants have taken root, struggling to thrive in the dim light. The walls of the gulch are of cold, smooth stone.
121032: The gulch cuts a deep, twisting pathway through the plain, where once a seasonal stream meandered. The waterway has long ago dried up, to leave only some shrubs and a deep chasm, with steep high walls of stones, many of them precariously left behind during previous floods due to the bend here. Some of the shrubs have taken root down here, while the roots of one of the others above hang down into the gulch.
121033: Cleaving a deep gouge through the wilderness, the gulch turns here from a westerly to a southerly course. The stone walls are cold and smooth, rising vertically for many feet. A few hardy shrubs reach upwards, striving for the light of the sun.
121034: Smooth stone walls trace the path of this deep gulch through the wilderness. Rising tall, they seem to offer no hand or footholds, and like the ground underfoot, they are made predominantly of cold, hard rock. High on the south wall, a thin covering of earth can be seen, through which a few coarse roots poke.
121035: A shrub with maple-like leaves is growing here.

The gulch cleaves a mighty cleft, from east to west, through the land. The smooth stone walls rise high above the bottom, with no visible handholds to make an ascent easier. This place is deeply shaded, with nothing much growing in this dried river bed, though a tree branch, bearing brown, dried-out leaves, dangles down from above out of reach.
121036: The tunnel splits here, with a small passage leading to the south while the main tunnel continues to the east and west. Mud lies in all directions, damp and brown. A few roots poke through the ceiling, but fauna is otherwise lacking.
121037: Muddy Tunnel by an Underground River

The dark river creeps out over the tunnel floor here like blood oozing from a deep wound. Large grooves line the walls, indicating the river is far from its high water mark. To the east and west, the tunnel continues its way through the mud.
121038: The muddy walls close in here, giving room for only three to walk abreast. The floor is squishy, with water seeping in from all over the walls and trickling down to the floor in a constant, dripping flow. The passage widens to the east and west.
121039:
A large toadstool grows nearby.
A huge black fungus is here, exuding a foul stench.
A huge black fungus is here, exuding a foul stench.
An ancient fungus smothers the boulders.
An ancient fungus smothers the boulders.
An ancient fungus smothers the boulders.

Slick mud covers the walls, floor, and ceiling of this dank tunnel. Deep grooves have been carved through the mud by the passage of water over time. A few burrows can be seen in the walls, apparently home to some creatures who prefer the damp and dark.
121040:
A grizzly cub is sleeping here.
A grizzly cub is sleeping here.
A grizzly bear is sleeping here.
A grizzly bear is sleeping here.

A round, muddy cave has hollowed out here, perhaps the result of some occasional flooding. The mud-covered walls are still slick and wet, and dank air penetrates the senses. A small bit of water has pooled on the floor, but barely a handful in any particular spot.
121041: The underground river narrows here as the walls close in on both sides. To the north, the river opens up to a wider passage. To the south, the shore of a dark tunnel marks the edge of the river. The walls are smooth, apparently polished that way by significantly more water than flows today.
121042:
A water moccasin slithers out of sight just below the surface of the water.
A water moccasin slithers out of sight just below the surface of the water.
A water moccasin slithers out of sight just below the surface of the water.

The river flows on and on here, with slick brown walls guiding it on either side. A few holes can be seen in various spots in the wall. Perhaps the homes of some small creatures. The river is deep, and no light can penetrate to the bottom.
121043: An underground river flows through the dank tunnel here. The source is hidden, apparently stemming from beneath the rocks. The river continues to the east, while the shoreline of the tunnel can be found to the north. Brown, mud-slick walls prevent passage in any other direction.
121044:
An albino salamander is here, perched on some rocks.
An albino salamander is here, perched on some rocks.
An albino salamander is here, perched on some rocks.
A black snake hurries towards you with sly intentions.
A snake slithers towards you.

The air is heavy here with the smell of wet dirt and cave fungus. To the south, the tunnel floor gives way to the shoreline of an underground river. The water is moving, though only a small ripple can be heard. To the west, the tunnel continues on.
121051: The river twists and turns here, with the tunnel walls bulging in a hazardous fashion. A few stalactites hang from the ceiling, almost dipping into the water and providing further obstacles to safe passage. The current of murky water is steady.
121052: The walls close in on the river here, leaving little room for air in the damp passage. The current is steady, but only the occasional splash against the wall can be heard. The river continues to the south, but to the north it runs below a rocky outcropping.
121053:
A large leech is moving close to you, searching for blood.
A large leech is moving close to you, searching for blood.

A jagged slab of rock juts out from the wall here to form a rocky outcropping above the water. The floor is slick, making sure footing tough to come by. The river flows by to the south, while a pool of water sits to the west. A dank smell permeates the air.
121054:
A long slender eel glides along the water, its body coiled to strike.
A long slender eel glides along the water, its body coiled to strike.

The water here forms a large pool, surrounded by rock on all sides. Although no source is visible, a barely perceptible movement in the water indicates this pool is not stagnant. No bottom is visible, and the only ways out appear to be some rocky ledges to the north and east.
121055: A giant slug is here, oozing around.

Thick mud covers the floor of this ledge, making each step squish and squick. A few large boulders line the walls, but there is little else here. A large pool sits to the south, while the ledge continues to the west. The faint sound of moving water fills the air.
121056: This ledge is narrow and sloped, with its floor wet with the overflow of the underground river. Short burrows line the walls, apparently the home of some reptilian beasts. The ledge continues to the east, while it descends into the river to the west.
121057:
A hairy black spider wraps up a silken package with her hind legs.
A hairy black spider wraps up a silken package with her hind legs.
A hairy black spider wraps up a silken package with her hind legs.
A large sturgeon swims slowly along the bottom.
A large sturgeon swims slowly along the bottom.

This river is deep, with the bottom far out of reach. The walls curve into the ceiling, and are covered with a thick layer of grime. A steady current flows, though neither its source nor destination are apparent. To the east, the shore rises up out of the water.
121058: The ceiling hangs low over this underground river, leaving little space to breathe. The current is not very strong, but it is steady, and it seems to pull down below the walls. The babble of the river is a faint noise in the background of cave.
121059: The water stops abruptly here as it reaches the tunnel shore to the north. The undercurrent seems to continue beyond, though exactly where is unclear. A few notches in the wall demonstrate that something, or someone, has disturbed the mud.
121060: The muddy passageway leads into the black depths of the underground river here, leaving a only a wet route to the south. To the west, the mud continues into the darkness. It is unclear where the water leads, as the current seems to flow below the surface and into the walls.
121061: At the western end of the passage, the ground drops abruptly into a slick, muddy ramp. A few trickles of water flow doing the ramp, though not nearly enough to have formed the passage. The tunnel continues to the east, while a dark hollow has been carved in the northern wall.
121062:
A brown bear is sleeping here.
A brown bear is sleeping here.
A brown bear is sleeping here.

This hollow in the side of the tunnel is relatively dry, setting it apart from dankness around. A depression at one end of the the tunnel has been covered in leaves and small branches, evidently the home of some cave-dwelling creature. A few deep marks have been gouged into the walls, apparently made by some sharp claws.
121063: The tunnel slopes steeply here as the muddy passage winds upward. Deep grooves are carved into the curved walls, apparently caused by some massive rush of water. At the base of the slope, the burrow turns to the south as it stretches into the darkness.
121064: Brown, muddy water streams from the ceiling in a constant pitter patter of tiny droplets. Stalactites have been begun to form overhead, while small pools have rest below the flows, dotting the floor like shiny speckles. The dank tunnel continues its muddy path to the north and south.
121065:
A large bat is here, hanging in the darkness.
A large bat is here, hanging in the darkness.

The air here is thick with moisture with the faint scent of earth and mildew hanging heavily. Water droplets cling to the muddy walls, dripping rhythmically down to the wet floor. The dark passage continues its muddy way to the north and south.
121066: A small black vicious rat squeaks at you for disturbing it.

The tunnel twists at a sharp angle, the walls growing wetter and more uneven as it bends out of sight. A low, steady drip echoes through the air, mingling with the trickles of water that cross the uneven floor. The passage seems to have been carved from some great rush of water, though that seems to have been some time ago.
121067:
A large toadstool grows nearby.
A large bat is here, hanging in the darkness.
A large bat is here, hanging in the darkness.
A small black vicious rat squeaks at you for disturbing it.

The tunnel curves sharply and the winding floor is caked in thick, sucking mud. The walls, slick with moisture, are streaked with dark, wet marks where they have been disturbed by some unknown creature. 121068:
A small reptile with large eyes scurries along the walls.
A small black vicious rat squeaks at you for disturbing it.

The tunnel turns here, leading off to the north and east. The ground is moist and soft with small trickles of water pushing up through the mud. The walls and ceiling are pockmarked with deep indentations, apparently made by some burrowing creature.
121069: The muddy tunnel slopes upward here in a banked, twisting ramp. To the west, the passage widens as it spits off to the north and south. The walls are smooth, as if carved from the very waters of the earth. A faint trickle of water flows down here, heading to the west.
121071: A small leech is here, floating in the water.

This water of this murky pool churns in a spiral of brown and red muck. It seems to be deep, with no bottom visible from the surface. The shoreline of the muddy tunnel lies to the east, while wet walls of dirt and clay surround the rest of the pool.
121072: Umber-coloured water is all that can be seen in every direction. A soft current traverses this passage way, though neither the source nor the destination can be discerned. Even the exit is difficult to make out, though the water seems to come to a surface far above.

A large leech is moving close to you, searching for blood.

This muddy passage is narrow, with the muck-covered walls closing in from all sides save the south. Dark circles dot the floor of this underground river, apparently the nesting ground for some fish or amphibian. The water has a current to it, though the source is difficult to pinpoint.
121095: The muddy tunnel bends sharply here, with the walls banked at an angle that makes footing precarious. A rough path has been trod into the bank, though only a single handspan wide. A faint trickle of water runs along the inside edge, with a low, constant burble.
121112: The tunnel slopes sharply here as it curves down into the depths. The banked walls seem to have been formed by a massive flow of water. A few pockets line the muddy walls, appparently the home to some subterranean creatures. The sound of flowing water can be heard from below.
121123: The floor here is wet and squishy, with a coating of slick mud covering every visible surface. The faint burble of rushing water can be heard to the north, washing out most other sounds. The tunnel continues to the west, with a few boreholes marring the walls, evidently the homes of some small creatures. A dirt ramp leads down into the darkness.
121124: The damp tunnel turns here, and the ceiling drops abruptly with the bend. A few pools of water dot the floor, each with a faint gurgle indicating they are not stagnant. But the source of the water is not immediately visible. The tunnel continues to the east and south.
121125:
A huge black fungus is here, exuding a foul stench.
A giant, strange looking green fungus is here, ready to devour you in seconds.
A black snake hurries towards you with sly intentions.

The dank tunnel comes to a wet end here, with mud and grime the main distinguishing feature. A few bulbous stalactites hang from the ceiling, but they look less than stable as evidenced by the broken pile of white rock covering the floor.
121126: A dirt ramp spirals around the walls of this vertical tunnel. Off the ramp, the bottom of the tunnel can be seen far below. A few groves are carved into the centre of the ramp, indicating where something has been dragged up and down. A couple of brass lanterns hang from hooks in the wall.
121127: A ramp of smooth dirt and mud curves up around the tunnel walls here. A few lines of dirt mark the centre of the ramp, perhaps caused by dragging some sledge through the damp floor. A few torches line the walls, bathing the room in shadows.
121128: This curving passage has been hacked through the clay and earth, with pick marks scarring every wall. A trodden path leads from north to east, forming a slight trench through the muddy ground. Crude iron sconces line the walls, each flickering with a small flame.
121129: The walls of this tunnel are covered in bulges and pits that show the excavators cared little for making clearn lines. A small lantern in a hollow of the eastern wall casts a wan light over the chamber. The tunnel continues to the east, while a thick door blocks passage to the south.
121130: A brigand, looking at your nice purse, is sneaking here (hidden).

This circular chamber of dirt and rock has been hollowed out from the surrounding earth. A latern hangs from a hook in the eastern wall, giving a pale, dancing light. A thick door is framed in the northern wall of the chamber.
121131:
A malicious thug is here, threatening you.
A malicious thug is here, threatening you.
A ruffian is sneaking around here, looking for some mischief to do.
A ruffian is sneaking around here, looking for some mischief to do.

The excavated tunnels form a junction here, with passages leading out to the west, east, and south. A large lantern hangs from the ceiling, almost like a chandelier. Wooden supports keep the keep the ceiling from caving in, though by the look of them that may not be for long.
121132: A thick layer of packed mud coats the walls of this chamber. A path through the mud, beaten down by the tread of countless boots, leads to the west and the north. A few torches are tied to wooden posts and stuck into the floor, casting warm glow over the wet earth.
121133: A large passage has been cut through the earth and rock here. Rubble lines the edges of the cavern, leftovers from the mining. A few wooden braces are all that keep the walls from collapsing. A few torches sit in iron sconces, giving flickering light to the bending cavern.
121134: A wiry smuggler is here, attempting to avoid being seen.

A roughly fashioned stairwell of earth and packed rock has been built here. The steps curve in a spiral up the wall, supported by thin beams of timber. This cavern is wide, and appears a mix of natural cavities and excavated earth. A pair of lanterns hang along one wall, lighting the chamber.
121135:
A sturdy crate made of nailed wooden planks sits on the floor.
A beer barrel has been left here.
A small barrel made of aged oak and strong iron hoops stands here.
A heavy desk, made of solid oak, stands here.
The chief of smugglers is here, planning his next move.

This cavern has been made into an office of sorts, complete with desk, cabinets and a chair. Stacks of ledgers, maps, and other papers lie on crates and barrels around the chamber. A couple lanterns are set in brass holders in the wall, providing plenty of light by which to work.
121136:
There are three beer bottles here.
There are two stout barrels here.
There are three sacks of flour here.
A water barrel has been left here.
A sturdy crate made of nailed wooden planks sits on the floor.

Water drips from the ceiling of this dingy storage room. Crates and shelves line the walls, though most appear to be filled with rubbish. The storage room continues to the south, and a door fashioned from planks provides egress to the east.
121137:
A large sack is on the ground.
A small oaken table has been set here.
On the table, there is a sturdy rope.
A wooden chest stands in the corner.

Crates, jars, barrels, and sacks cover almost every inch of this cavern. A few shelves have been set into the dirt walls, though they are covered in a thick layer of grime. A small brass lantern hangs from the ceiling, provide a dim light to illuminate the mess.
121138: The earthen stairwell winds its way around this dark excavation. Wooden rafters support the structure from below, though they seem barely sufficient to withstand the load. Torches have been stuff into pockets in the walls, casting flickering shadows throughout the chamber.
121139:
An experienced husky smuggler is here, plotting his illicit ventures.
An experienced husky smuggler is here, plotting his illicit ventures.

A narrow staircase of packed earth has been carved into the wall of this vertical tunnel. There is no railing, and the steep drop-off at the inside edge of the steps seems dangerous. At the top, the stairs lead right into a wooden hatch set in the earthen ceiling. A lantern hangs near the hatch, lightning the tunnel below.
121167: The plain here is rather dry and dead. A few patches of grass are all the life to be found. This plain could once have been flourishing with life but must have died away when the river to the north-west dried out. The dry plain continues to the north, south and west.
121168: A diamondback rattlesnake is coiled here, ready to strike.

This spur of land stands between two deep scars in the dry plains, all that now appears to remain of an old river. Long ago this formed a gully to the north and a narrower and even deeper gulch to the west and south. The dry plain continues to the east.
121169: The plain here is rather dry and dead, with a few sickly patches of grass the only life to be seen. This land might once have flourished with life, but all has become barren with the passing of the days since a significant river cut its way down into a gulch, taking the water further and further away. The deep gulch passes to the southwest of here. To the west, it is possible to climb down into the chasm, but to the south it has become so deep that it would be necessary to search out handholds with great care.
121196: The dry plain stretches out to the west and south as far as the eye can see, with sparse vegetation and short, coarse grass underfoot. A steep-sided gulch cuts through the terrain to the north, north-east and east. Scrubby vegetation lines its banks, with one particularly tall shrub to the north.
121197: A colony of red ants is here. The ants seem to ignore you.

The plain is rather dry and desolate. There is little vegetation, with the exception of some short grass. Some small anthills further add to the arid appearance. To the west, there is a road running north and south. To the north, east and south, the dry plain continues.
121218: A rock lizard is here, motionless as it observes you.

The plain is dry and desolate. There is little vegetation to be seen. The ground seems inhospitable to any plant life. Stones and rocks are abundant. A similar landscape extends in every direction. There is a hushed soundscape, with the occasional soft skittering of a lizard's footsteps, the gentle sighs of the wind as it weaves its way through the barren expanse, and the occasional distant rattle of loose stones tumbling in the stillness.
121219: A sturdy pack horse is standing here.

The arid plain is devoid of vegetation. Rocks of various shapes and sizes are scattered across the landscape. A deep gulch runs along its northern boundary, making northward journeys hazardous. Some bushes grow at the edges of the gulch.
121220: The land all around seems dry and desolate, with little vegetation maintaining a foothold in the parched soil. Rocks and stones of various sizes lie all about, scattered among the thin and sickly tufts of grass, but there is little else to be seen. To the north, a deep cleft cuts across the landscape, where once a rapid river flowed.
121231: A rock lizard is here, motionless as it observes you.

The plain is arid and barren. Little vegetation is seen, except some short grass. Rocks of various sizes decorate the plain. A road runs north-south in the distance to the west. The dry plain continues in all other directions.
121271: An arid plain stretches both north and south, sandwiched between a north-south road to the west and a north-south gulch to the east. Seemingly, this was once the course of a notable waterway, which has long ago dried up. Scattered hardy shrubs can be seen at the lip of the gulch.
121292: This dry and barren field comes to an abrupt end to the east where it meets the rim of a gulch cutting a scar across the landscape. The walls of this chasm are almost vertical, and comprised of smooth, dark rock, impossible to climb safely. Apparently, this was once the course of a substantial waterway, which has long ago dried up and been forgotten. The steep, narrow gully that leads to the gulch is to the north. To the west, a wide road makes its way south through the plain, which continues to the south.
121293: A few straggly patches of thin, dry yellow grass grow here and there in the parched soil. To the north, the ground looks more fertile, the grass greener and there is some light vegetation, but here the overall impression is one of an unnatural pallor. The grass seems to almost die out to the west, while to the east it seems there is a road.
121294: Though this plain is dry, it is covered with grass and light vegetation. To the east, a road cleaves the parched plain, which appears to be even more desolate on the far side of the thoroughfare. The plain continues to the north, and also the south and west where the dry grass looks yellow and sickly.
121295: Tall grass, rather dry looking, occupies this area and as far east and south as the horizon, not terribly far away. Some small, hardy bushes cling to life. To the north, abandoned fields are visible, while to the west this plain looks unhealthily yellow.

The field here is grass, fairly healthy looking, in contrast with the grass to the east. Similar grassland lies to the south.
